The argument here retains the particular source marking and shared coefficient targets; it does not assume an identification with those constructions. ## Complete signed augmented links at arbitrary width An augmented link retains the auxiliary crossing circles rather than filling them. The [signed augmented-source theorem](../../notes/general_signed_augmented_source_volume.md) applies to every fixed connected augmented plat with a labeled convex ideal right-angled polyhedron $Q_D$ realizing its actual cut and face pairings. It allows any fixed retained half-twist pattern $\epsilon_i\in\{0,1,-1\}$ and proves $$\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N}\log|A_{D,N}^{\boldsymbol\epsilon}| =2\operatorname{Vol}(Q_D)=\operatorname{Vol}(Y_D^{\boldsymbol\epsilon}).$$ Here $A_{D,N}^{\boldsymbol\epsilon}$ is the marked complete-circle source and $Y_D^{\boldsymbol\epsilon}$ the augmented exterior. “Complete-circle” means that every auxiliary representation color equals the level \(N\); the auxiliary circles are still components of the link. The manifold in this formula therefore differs from the knot exterior obtained after filling them. The proof uses one shared radius per face, a nonzero coefficient saddle, and an explicit summation of the half-twist phases. The [untwisted proof](../../notes/general_untwisted_augmented_source_volume.md) is a shorter introduction to the positive part of this argument. The theorem requires its geometric certificate; it does not supply one for every plat. The [coverage comparison](../../notes/general_untwisted_augmented_source_literature_coverage.md) explains earlier overlaps and the parallel-belt parity obstruction. ## Other retained examples The current strict Conway theorem and its hypotheses are stated above. Earlier restricted grammars are not separate proof prerequisites. The source snapshot preserves their development. The [pretzel calculation](../../notes/actual_long_pretzel_casson_rivin_equality.md) and [filled belt-stack argument](../../notes/actual_long_filled_octahedral_belt_stack_volume.md) remain examples of other source and geometric comparisons. Each has its own component, parity, marking and filling assumptions. Their conclusions should be read from those statements rather than inferred from a shared scalar formula or attributed to the standalone Conway paper. ## General identities with a smaller conclusion Several approaches begin with the local algebra at a crossing-circle edge. The [generating-action theorem](../../notes/actual_matching_edge_polynomial_geometric_action.md), [continuant period](../../notes/actual_matching_edge_continuant_operator_period.md), and [rectangle bound](../../notes/actual_matching_circle_rectangle_bound.md) identify a finite operator, its local character relation and the range of certified geometric targets. A local character relation still needs a contributing global period before it gives the volume of a knot. For arbitrary fixed plat width, the [complete compiler](../../notes/actual_augmented_plat_phase_compiler.md), [mixed-color compiler](../../notes/actual_mixed_augmented_plat_compiler.md), and [entire Fourier core](../../notes/actual_augmented_plat_entire_core_color_packet.md) retain the finite phases and derivative terms. The [matching geometry](../../docs/papers/marked-fillings.pdf) supplies the complete complement under a positive labeled realization. The [general plat target](../../notes/general_augmented_plat_long_twist_target.md) states the further source estimate needed for unrestricted coverage. Recoupling means changing the order in which local representation factors are paired. The [positive scalar formula](../../notes/actual_matching_edge_racah_positive_scalar.md), [marked block identity](../../notes/actual_matching_edge_marked_four_port_block.md), and [completed-projector formula](../../notes/actual_matching_edge_completed_projector_block.md) fix the normalization of those changes and preserve their first normal derivatives. The [native-energy bound](../../notes/actual_matching_edge_native_projector_energy.md) controls the resulting projectors by explicit magnetic energies, which can themselves grow exponentially. The [Fourier energy profile](../../notes/actual_matching_edge_magnetic_energy_profile.md) gives boundary rate $5v_3/\pi$, with $v_3$ the regular ideal tetrahedron volume; the [shrinking-fold theorem](../../notes/actual_matching_edge_shrinking_fold_native_energy.md) extends it to every sequence approaching the fold. These are local costs, not a volume estimate for their full contraction. The [shared-cycle formula](../../notes/actual_matching_graph_shared_cycle_fourier_compiler.md) preserves bounded integer flows and the marked Fourier charge. Its [positive local coefficient theorem](../../notes/actual_q_hahn_fourier_coefficient_variational.md) gives an interior variational rate. The [positive Fourier partition](../../notes/actual_matching_graph_positive_fourier_partition.md) yields a Cauchy upper bound with shared constraints, but a sharp geometric rate and matching lower bound for that approach remain open. The [radial-frame obstruction](../../notes/actual_positive_fourier_radial_geometric_obstruction.md) explains one failed geometric interpretation. The [single-Racah recoupling formula](../../notes/actual_general_four_port_single_racah_kernel.md) is an exact local identity. For its supported folded colors, the [hyperideal-volume theorem](../../notes/actual_four_port_hyperideal_angle_volume.md) identifies the metric-normalized scalar rate as the extended tetrahedron volume divided by $\pi$, uniformly through the stated boundary limits. The normalization matters: the bare factorial sum has a different action. This local volume relation is not asserted to be new. Finally, the [positive Conway variational theorem](../../docs/papers/newton-calculus.pdf) evaluates the whole positive source as twice the maximum of a concave ideal-tetrahedron volume functional on its exact support polytope. Its cylindrical factors have the geometric interpretation described above. Cap products instead have their exhibited connected-sum decomposition and additive limits; they are not assigned one complete hyperbolic metric. ## Cube sectors are kept separate The cube calculation tests how local geometric contributions behave under sewing. The central odd-level sector and the four-rung sum have the stated geometric rate. In the latter, four rung labels are summed while eight cycle labels remain fixed. The [four-rung theorem](../../notes/actual_cube_four_rung_positive_source.md) and [projected-chain theorem](../../notes/actual_three_port_cauchy_transport_and_cube_kernel.md) retain these restrictions. ![Four blue rung labels are summed; the eight orange cycle labels remain fixed in the proved calculation.](../figures/cube-channels.png) Removing the cycle restrictions, controlling the full cube invariant and treating its even-level growth remain open in this route. Numerical cube calculations do not establish dominance or cancellation control. The [frontier chapter](frontier.md) explains how these alternatives relate to the current general questions without treating them as missing steps in the strict-tree theorem. ## The full expansion for the directed criterion The [directed all-orders theorem](../../docs/papers/meridian-expansions.pdf) extends the meridian expansion to every directed circle-tree certificate, including the alternative \(|n_v|\ge2^{27}\) or \(d_v\ge2^{28}\) at each vertex. It proves every finite order uniformly on fixed compact subsets of the nonreal translated charts needed by a fixed recurrence. With \(q_N=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(M=q_N^s\), and \(H_N(s)=\sin(\pi s)/(N\sin(\pi s/N))\), its first correction is \[ \frac{F_N(q_N^s)}{F_N(1)H_N(s)} =1+\frac{\pi i\,\tau_K s^2}{2N}+O(N^{-2}). \] Here \(F_N\) is the actual zero-framed reduced state and \(\tau_K\) is the preferred cusp shape of the same knot complement. The proof keeps the exact crossing and framing scalars. Normalization removes a constant term, and evenness removes a possible linear term. The complete expansion, rather than this first correction alone, supplies the operator consequence described next. It does not give a fixed-\(M\) asymptotic away from completeness or a uniform continuation through ordinary-color resonances. ## A classical characteristic selected by the full expansion The [filtered characteristic theorem](../../docs/papers/meridian-expansions.pdf) applies to the proved strict long-filling sources and the circle-tree sources under the summed condition, the local bound \(2^{-120}\), or any directed certificate by the extension above. An annihilator is a fixed, nonzero finite difference operator that kills the actual reduced sequence at all sufficiently large levels. Its multiplication and shift operators do not commute. After classical specialization, the first nonzero coefficient gives a commutative polynomial in meridian and longitude variables: its classical symbol. Given such an annihilator, the theorem proves that the full microscopic expansion selects an analytic curve in this polynomial's zero set. The selected factor is reciprocal and has an explicit rational peripheral expression. Its tangent is the preferred cusp shape. The [strict-tree geometric longitude theorem](../../docs/papers/meridian-expansions.pdf) identifies the entire selected curve for every covered strict long-filling presentation, with no restriction on the valence or adjacency of bare product junctions. The earlier summed circle-tree theorem and the local theorem with bound \(2^{-120}\) supply the required geometric theorem and full expansion; the directed all-orders extension establishes the same conclusion for every directed certificate. If \(n_v\) are the original crossing powers and \(w(D)\) is their oriented writhe, the preferred longitude is \[ L(M)=-M^{-w(D)-\sum_v n_v} \prod_{e\in\mathcal E_T} \frac{M^2-X_e(M)}{1-M^2X_e(M)}. \] Here \(\mathcal E_T\) is the original set of physical quarter-turn edges, and \(X_e=e^{2\pi ix_e}\) comes from the corresponding stationary index \(x_e\). The branch is selected by the original marked filling path. This condition matters: algebraic elimination alone retains other representations. To pass from circle trees to a bare product junction, the proof inserts a literal zero-crossing box and a circle around it. Meridian filling removes that circle and restores the original framed collar, including its ordered based puncture loops. Eliminating the added angular variable gives exactly the old product action. The full stationary system stays regular even at the possible half-edge fold. This identifies the actual representation germ of the original knot, rather than inferring geometry from an equality of scalar traces. The proof first constructs the nonparabolic representations of the pieces and joins them along their labeled twice-punctured disks. It retains the changes of puncture eigenlines caused by a half twist. Compare the squared preferred-longitude eigenvalue with the square of the displayed edge product. The boundary pairing shows that their ratio has zero derivative when the auxiliary variables vary at fixed \(M\). The edge equations have no additional algebraic constants over \(\mathbb C(M)\), so this ratio is a rational function of \(M\). For every \(M\ne0\), auxiliary parameters can be chosen so that the representation and all edge factors are finite and nonzero. The ratio therefore has no zeros or poles on \(\mathbb C^*\), leaving only a constant times an integer power of \(M\). The marked complete cusp fixes that constant and exponent, and the Seifert-surface calculation fixes the remaining sign. Combining this result with the full quantum expansion proves that the selected complex geometric irreducible factor divides the first nonzero classical symbol of every genuine all-level annihilator of the reduced invariant in these covered classes. The full and reduced normalizations have different gauge factors, which the proof keeps before removing common factors. The intrinsic conclusion also transfers to net-twist and arbitrary closure inputs that are carried by the stated marked ambient isotopies to a covered strict knot. The entire zero-framed family and preferred peripheral curves agree under that isotopy. The presentation-dependent edge factors are computed on the strict output; they are not asserted to match term by term in the input. No equality with the full A-polynomial, no factor multiplicity, and no identification of the entire recurrence ideal is claimed. Ordinary resonances and knots outside the covered classes remain separate questions. ## Comparing the result with other volume statements The phrase “volume conjecture” is used for several different sequences of quantum invariants. A comparison must specify the invariant, the manifold, the allowed levels, and whether the diagram has been changed. The following papers provide relevant coverage. They are not additional proof assumptions for the theorems in this manuscript. **Whitehead chains.** In [van der Veen's paper, §1 and the main theorem](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0611181), the link \(W_{a,b,c,d}\) is obtained by composing signed twist tangles, \(b\ge1\) belt tangles, \(c\ge0\) clasps and \(d\ge0\) mirror clasps. The theorem concerns the normalized colored Jones evaluation at \(e^{2\pi i/N}\). Its distinction between levels is essential: the stated asymptotic holds through all levels when \(b=1\); for \(b\ge2\), it holds on odd levels and the even-level evaluations vanish. Thus a claim for all integer levels cannot be inferred merely from membership in a broadly named family of chain links. **Turaev–Viro invariants.** Write \(TV_r(X,q)\) for the Turaev–Viro state-sum invariant of a compact three-manifold \(X\), at integer level \(r\) and the specified root \(q\). Its definition sums representation labels on a triangulation. It is a different quantity from the single reduced knot evaluation \(K_N(K)\). In the convention stated in [Ibarra, McQuire and Purcell, Conjecture 1.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.09296), the proposed limit is \[ \lim_{\substack{r\to\infty\\r\ \mathrm{odd}}} \frac{2\pi}{r}\log \left|TV_r\bigl(X,e^{2\pi i/r}\bigr)\right| =\operatorname{Vol}(X). \] For a link exterior, the volume on the right means the volume of its complete hyperbolic interior. Identifying two such interiors geometrically does not identify a Turaev–Viro state sum with a particular Kashaev evaluation. Three nearby statements illustrate the distinction: | Reference | Object and stated scope | | --- | --- | | [Kumar, *Fundamental shadow links realized as links in \(S^3\)*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.11447v3) | Constructs infinite families of links in the three-sphere whose complements satisfy the Turaev–Viro volume statement, using homeomorphisms with fundamental shadow-link exteriors. | | [Ibarra–McQuire–Purcell, *Augmented links, shadow links, and the TV volume conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.09296v1) | Gives a geometric comparison of octahedral fully augmented exteriors with shadow-link exteriors and a Turaev–Viro verification in the no-half-twist case. “Octahedral” is a restriction on the decomposition, not a synonym for every fully augmented link. | | [Shen, *The Chen–Yang volume conjecture for long integral fillings of fundamental shadow links*, version 3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11839v3) | States a volume theorem for the \(SO(3)\) Turaev–Viro invariants of sufficiently long fixed integral fillings, through odd levels, with independent signs and magnitudes. | The last paper is a September 2026 preprint; this comparison records its stated scope, without importing its proof. The knot theorems in this repository instead retain the original reduced Kashaev scalar, its marked closure, and both level parities. Any proposed deduction from one of these neighboring results must supply the exact relation between those quantities and preserve the same peripheral filling. The comparison makes no claim that the listed papers exhaust the literature or that the constructions here are disjoint from theirs. ## Inserting a piece at an ordinary triangular face Appendix R proves a second way to assemble diagrams whose full source estimates are already known. The attaching face may now be away from the two protected vertices. Its three circle curvatures are positive. The result allows any fixed finite list of certified pieces: an explicit construction supplies a suitable core and sufficiently small boundary ratios for each piece. As in the other planar theorems, the final strand connections must give one knot, and all final crossing powers must be independently sufficiently long. Everything is fixed before the quantum level tends to infinity. Here a *certified piece* means a matched triangulated sphere together with a strict bound for every locally allowed noncentral choice in its finite source. Each crossing region has three choices: the central term, a left one-sided term, or a right one-sided term. A choice of one term at every region is called a *string*. The certificate must cover every such noncentral string, even if its coefficient vanishes before insertion. Different strings may use different positive coefficient weights, but each shared face has one weight throughout a given string. This is the same input requirement as in the preceding protected sum. ### The geometric operation and the boundary condition Remove one triangle from the core and one triangle incident to the piece's protected edge. Identify their boundary vertices in opposite cyclic orders. The two triangles formerly matched to the removed faces become one matched pair. All other pairs retain their original order. The new interiors are disjoint, so this again gives a simple triangulated sphere with a matching. Reversing the original projection cut then specifies its augmented link and the primitive crossing disks. ![The core and the inserted piece share boundary vertices u, v and b. Two oppositely oriented triangles are removed and their retained partners are matched along ub. The core retains the only coefficient demands at u and v.](../../manuscript/build/figures/triangular-boundary-insertion.png) Write \(u,v,b\) for the three positive boundary curvatures, meaning reciprocals of circle radii. The inserted piece was originally estimated with \(u=v=0\); those zero curvatures represented its two protected lines. After insertion they become ordinary core circles. The theorem requires \(u/b\) and \(v/b\) to be sufficiently small. This condition must hold at the core's complete packing and at every weight vector selected for its noncentral strings. There are only finitely many such vectors for a fixed core. No condition on the quantum level is involved. Let \(B\) denote the inserted piece and \(I\) its interior vertices after its boundary face is removed. For a positive weight \(w_i\), put \(q_i=\log w_i\). The triangle potential is \[ Q(w_1,w_2,w_3)= \max_{\alpha_i\ge0,\;\sum_i\alpha_i=1/2} \left(\sum_i f(\alpha_i)+\sum_{w_i>0}\alpha_i\log w_i\right), \qquad f(t)=\frac{\Lambda(\pi t)+\Lambda(\pi/2-\pi t)}{\pi}, \] where \(\Lambda(x)=-\int_0^x\log(2\sin s)\,ds\). At a zero weight its load \(\alpha_i\) is required to be zero. The number \(\Phi_B\) is the minimum of the complete action for the original protected piece; \(2\pi\Phi_B\) is its augmented exterior's volume. The fixed-boundary identity is \[ \min_{q_I}\left(\sum_{t\text{ in the disk}}Q_t-\sum_{i\in I}q_i\right) =Q(u,v,b)+\Phi_B. \] Thus replacing the old triangle by the optimized disk changes the complete action by a constant. The identity includes the boundary normalization, which is essential for using it in a coefficient bound. The proof supplies existence as well as uniqueness. A finite transport argument gives strictly positive corner loads satisfying the interior demands. These loads prove that the action tends to infinity when the interior logarithmic weights escape to infinity with the boundary fixed. The Hessian is positive definite on those interior variables. At the resulting minimizer, the tangent-circle center triangles have angle sum \(2\pi\) at every interior vertex. Developing them gives the original boundary triangle once, so its three boundary angles are unchanged. The derivatives of the minimized disk action and of \(Q\) therefore agree. Taking \(u,v\) to zero determines the remaining constant as \(\Phi_B\). Appendix R proves the coercivity, development and zero-boundary limit separately. This is part of the established variational setting for circle packings and patterns; see [Rivin's paper](https://annals.math.princeton.edu/1994/139-3/p02) and [Bobenko–Springborn](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0203250). The normalized identity and its application to the present coefficient demands are proved in the appendix. Those references do not supply the quantum remainder estimate. ### Why the strict estimate survives insertion Put \(T=Q(u,v,b)\) and \(\Delta=2T-\log b\ge0\). In comparing the two old sources, the \(b\)-target is counted twice. The targets at \(u,v\) are supplied only by the core. After correcting that duplication, the assembled rate is bounded by the sum of the two old rates minus \(\Delta\), with a possible additional error of at most \(\Delta/2\). For a wholly central inserted piece, the conditional minimum is \(\Phi_B+\Delta\). Its circle at the attaching region is smaller than any boundary circle; the tangent-circle curvature formula proves this assertion. That comparison makes the attaching error zero, so \(+\Delta\) cancels \(-\Delta\) exactly. If the piece contains any noncentral label, its finite certificate extends by continuity to sufficiently small positive \(u,v\). Previously forbidden terms, overloaded at one of those two variables, have rates tending to minus infinity and are bounded separately. There is then a constant \(\gamma_B>0\) such that the piece's rate is at most \(\Phi_B-\gamma_B/2\). The remaining correction is at most \(-\Delta+\Delta/2\le0\), so the strict margin survives. A central attaching label with a noncentral term elsewhere belongs to this second case. Classifying only the attaching label would leave a gap in the proof. For any fixed finite number of insertions, the same argument applies piece by piece. Distinct insertions use distinct matching pairs, but may share boundary vertices. The shared weights are the actual core weights, and the target accounting still gives one demand per ordinary vertex. The new complete action is \(\Phi_D+\sum_j\Phi_{B_j}\), where \(D\) is the core. This is an identity for the augmented action; it does not say that volumes after filling add. ### Explicit cores and a checked example Begin with an octahedral sphere. Inside one ordinary face, repeatedly insert the circle tangent to its three boundary circles and alternate the matching as shown. For every positive even length \(n\), the construction has \(n+4\) matched regions. Its complete packing satisfies strict balance, so that one weight vector controls every noncentral string. ![Two successive subdivisions of an ordinary triangle, with the matching alternating between adjacent triangles. The terminal face has curvatures 2, 1 and b2.](../../manuscript/build/figures/ordinary-triangular-zigzag.png) The terminal face has curvatures \(2,1,b_n\), with the exact formula \[ b_n=3n^2+4\sqrt2\,n+2. \] Its boundary ratios \(2/b_n,1/b_n\) tend to zero. For several pieces, join finitely many octahedral cores by the earlier protected operation, and build a separate even chain at each selected ordinary face. Choose each length to meet the threshold for its assigned piece. This gives an explicit construction for any fixed finite list; it does not assume that an arbitrary supplied core already has sufficiently small ratios. For the seventeen-region piece used above, the finite certificate extends at \(n=2^{20}\). Its forty original branches and five newly allowed protected-overload bounds have margins exceeding \(0.02\). Every larger even \(n\) works with the same witnesses, by monotonicity in the two boundary weights. The bound is deliberately conservative; it is not a proposed optimal chain length or a twist threshold. Attaching this piece gives \(n+20\) final crossing regions. Its old rational lower certificate also proves that weak balance still fails at the complete packing. Moreover, in the one-core construction no separating three-cycle contains both global protected vertices. It therefore is not a nontrivial protected triangular sum at that recorded mark. This distinguishes the marked constructions; it does not rule out other presentations of their knots. The full invariant conclusion uses three earlier results on the final diagram: the exact filling-functional norm, the nonzero central asymptotic, and smooth completion along the original primitive slopes. The action comparison is with that same completed metric. Hence, after independently sufficiently long fixed signed fillings, \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N}\log|K_N(K)| =\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K) \] through all integer levels. The main knot cusp remains complete. The finite source certificate is the extra premise supplying the full remainder bound; no unresolved general remainder theorem is used.

title: How the full quantum invariant acquires the knot volume
text: # How the full quantum invariant acquires the knot volume This chapter follows the current strict Conway proof and then explains local tools used in other presentations. Its main written account is [Holomorphic source asymptotics and volume limits for strict Conway compositions](../../docs/papers/conway-asymptotics.pdf). The [dependency graph](../../docs/papers/dependencies.html) locates its finite, analytic and geometric inputs. The [methods chapter](methods.md) gives definitions, examples and literature references; the [notation chapter](notation.md) records the conventions. The main result concerns a particular, already defined knot invariant. For a knot \(K\) and an integer level \(N\), write \(K_N(K)\) for its reduced Kashaev invariant, normalized to be \(1\) on the unknot. The quantum parameter is \(q_N=e^{\pi i/N}\). A diagram computes \(K_N\) by multiplying crossing matrices, joining their indices along strands, and summing the remaining indices. Cups, caps and the marked cut specify how the strands close. In the technical notes, this entire prescribed expression is called the **source**. It includes its scalar factors and derivatives, not just the part that seems largest. The [strict Conway tree theorem](../../docs/papers/conway-asymptotics.pdf) proves \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N}\log|K_N(K)| =\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K) \] for every fixed literal expression satisfying its finite compatibility test, once all independent signed twist weights are sufficiently long and the endpoint pairing gives a knot. A literal expression records the actual order of tangle products and quarter-turns; algebraically equal scalar formulas are not silently treated as isotopic diagrams. The tree and its integer weights stay fixed as \(N\) grows. This is a theorem for the stated class, not a claim that every arborescent knot has such a presentation. ## Why retaining the full expression matters A color is a representation label on a strand or an auxiliary crossing circle. At a root of unity, two spectral labels can have the same eigenvalue. The value at that eigenvalue then fails to determine the operator: its first derivative in the transverse spectral direction can also contribute. The notes call these derivative terms **normals**. Derivatives in the generic quantum parameter are another kind of normal, so the variable of differentiation must always be specified. Let \(\zeta\) denote the generic quantum parameter before specialization. For example, a factor \([2N]_\zeta\) vanishes when \(\zeta=q_N\) but can have a nonzero derivative there. Deleting it before differentiating changes the prescribed expression. The full invariant is a signed, generally complex sum. A large term or a large positive upper comparison does not prove that the sum has that size. Two requirements must be met together: the geometric contribution has a nonzero coefficient, and everything omitted from its neighborhood is uniformly smaller. A **packet** in this guide means a local asymptotic formula with its action, nonzero prefactor and controlled error. A **whole-source bound** means a bound on the entire original quantum sum, including all colors and derivative terms. These requirements have now been proved for the strict-tree class. The older local methods later in this chapter remain useful for other presentations. Their unresolved steps are not unresolved steps in the strict-tree theorem. ## The completed proof for strict trees The exact tangle recursion supplies the starting point. A physical leaf is a quarter-turned twist operator. Multiplication stacks two tangles in their recorded order, while a turn changes which two boundary strands are regarded as inputs. Expanding these operations in a fixed finite basis gives exact formulas and exact inequalities on the integer indices. After the forced closing index is removed, the remaining indices form a primitive integer lattice: there is no hidden multiplicity from using only a sublattice. This is what permits a local lattice sum to be compared with an integral without losing its normalization. At complete colors, the factorial weights have a real limiting action: the logarithm of a weight, divided by \(N\), has that limit. The action is a function of the scaled leaf and product indices, subject to the original compatibility equations. It must be maximized with those equations still imposed. Strictness ensures that the maximum occurs where the relevant cell angles are positive. The geometry chapter explains why the resulting cells reconstruct the actual augmented exterior, rather than merely a collection of tetrahedra of the correct total volume. For the current volume proof, each full integer crossing power is first expanded exactly in ordinary colored circles. This allows the local analysis to use the source with no retained half twists. Its actual factorials have a holomorphic interpolation near every strict stationary state, including a leaf index equal to \(1/4\). Summing over the original integer lattice gives a nonzero local contribution with the required normalization at both level parities. The [quarter-index recurrence theorem](../../docs/papers/quarter-index-asymptotics.pdf) remains a separate local result. It controls two transfer roots of equal modulus without assuming that distinct roots imply dominance. That signed recurrence analysis is not needed for the pure-source argument used by the current strict volume theorem. The remaining difficulty is global: a pointwise estimate on each factor can be too large after the factors are joined. The [source-bound paper](../../docs/papers/conway-source-bounds.pdf) retains the shared indices, exact Fourier identities and first derivatives at repeated spectral roots. Positive comparison sums and boundary profiles control the expression outside its central region. Its Theorem 1.1 treats at least three leaves; Corollary 9.1 proves the two-leaf case separately. A local saddle estimate is not substituted for either bound. This yields two global facts. Every physical color tuple obeys the required upper bound, and any tuple with at least one color a fixed fraction away from complete has a strict exponential loss. The difference between a full leaf and its chosen local expression is an explicit complementary-color term, called an **alias**. Expanding these differences turns every unwanted term into an actual full quantum evaluation with at least one small color. The global color bound suppresses them. This is why the argument controls all aliases at once; it does not assume that individual absolute-value estimates preserve the cancellations. Finally, the finite Fourier formula expresses the filling evaluation as an oscillatory sum. The [whole-period theorem](../../docs/papers/oscillatory-fillings.pdf) estimates all charges, including the infinite tail and endpoint terms, once its local asymptotic and global gap hypotheses have been supplied. The resulting nonzero contribution dominates the entire remainder. The [strict marked geometry](../../docs/papers/strict-conway-geometry.pdf) and the asymptotics paper's shear calculation identify its action, including its additive constant, with the volume of the actual knot complement. Odd crossing powers keep their original retained half twist and integer filling slope in this geometric comparison. Only auxiliary crossing-circle cusps are filled; the main knot cusp remains complete. ## Subtree estimates with a uniform twist threshold For the ordered tree construction with at least one edge and an integer braid at every junction, the [directed subtree theorem](../../notes/actual_all_circle_directed_volume.md) uses an exact finite recursion with one attaching angle left free. Its outgoing polynomial always has degree at most \(N-1\), even for a large subtree. The proof establishes nonvanishing at angle zero, then divides by that exact value, retaining its phases and framing factors. The ratio has a real decay estimate and a complex estimate on a fixed rectangle. These bounds control the next finite crossing trace, including its Fourier endpoint terms. Its first contribution has coefficient one at both level parities, and the other contributions are strictly smaller. Different subtrees may use different decay constants. The last vertex needs no outgoing estimate because its value is the final scalar. This gives a finite numerical criterion and, in particular, the sufficient condition \[ |n_v|\ge2^{27}\quad\text{or}\quad d_v\ge2^{28} \] at each vertex independently. Here \(n_v\) is the signed crossing power and \(d_v\) the number of incident tree edges. The original strand pairing must form a knot. The theorem controls its actual invariant and identifies the limit with its complement volume. The tree and all powers are fixed before \(N\) grows. This numerical result complements the strict-tree long-filling proof; it does not narrow that proof to circle trees. ## The same limit written through a quantum \(A\)-operator This is a separate route through recurrence data. The current [meridian-expansion theorem](../../docs/papers/meridian-expansions.pdf) assumes a specified fixed annihilator of the actual state; it does not construct that operator. The earlier finite-state constructions below have their own hypotheses. They are not extra premises of the volume proof just described. A quantum \(A\)-operator is a finite difference operator in a meridian variable. It is more data than a classical algebraic curve, but an equation alone can still have several solutions. The actual solution is selected here by its original quantum-group definition and finitely many fixed small-color values. Write \(x=q_N^\alpha\) for the raw representation coordinate and \(M=-q_Nx\) for the marked meridian coordinate. If \(F_N(M)\) is the reduced ADO family in this coordinate, then \[ F_N(1)=K_N(K),\qquad F_N(-q_N^j)=C_j(q_N). \] The complete point is \(M=1\); \(C_j(q)\) is the ordinary reduced \(j\)-color period. These identities include the original framing and quotient-color conventions. Let $R$ be the number of matching circles, $C$ the number of restored physical cycles, and $A_{D,N}$ the original scalar for the fixed diagram $D$. The partition $Z_F(N)$, defined by the exact positive weights of that construction, satisfies $$|A_{D,N}|^2\leq N^{4R+2C-2}Z_F(N).$$ Every Kirchhoff equation, Fourier congruence and the original marked charge remains in $Z_F$. Its summands are products of positive coefficients and explicit sine-factorial weights. The equality before Cauchy retains all phases; this upper bound does not establish their survival. The [radial reconstruction obstruction](../../notes/actual_positive_fourier_radial_geometric_obstruction.md) explains a remaining difficulty. At a strict positive radial saddle, all ordinary source factors would lie in the central selected domain. They therefore cannot all assemble into the complete geometric representation of the certified right-angled cut in one frame. This is a conditional geometric obstruction, with no asserted numerical rate gap. The exact phases and the exceptional matching-block route remain essential to investigate. A useful inequality has the form $$|K_N|^2\leq e^{o(N)}Z_N.$$ Weighted Cauchy can prove such an estimate once the inner product, original source cost, and dual cost are explicit. Choosing a positive form alone does not make those costs small. The repository contains exact counterexamples to proposed unmarked norms and to replacing a full magnetic tensor by its scalar rate. The whole-support boundary Gram theorem gives polynomial costs on each supported local cell. To obtain a theorem by this particular method, one must also control how those norms behave when cells are joined. Correlated seam labels must remain shared; maximizing local factors independently can change the answer. For the specified planar reflection doubles with three boundary representation labels, there is now a stronger [exact full-source identity](../../notes/actual_planar_three_port_reflection_double.md): $$Z_N^{\mathrm{double}}=\sum_{\mathbf a\in\mathcal D_N}\frac{|Z_N^{\mathrm{half}}(\mathbf a)|^2}{\theta_N(\mathbf a)}\geq0.$$ Here $\mathcal D_N$ is the allowed set of boundary triples, and $\theta_N$ is the original positive boundary measure. Every interior color is already summed, with its phases retained, inside the half-packet. This includes the actual normals at both level parities. Since there are at most $N^3$ boundary triples, the doubled source differs from its largest squared weighted packet by at most that polynomial factor. Its asymptotic is therefore reduced to estimating the half-packets, whose internal cancellations have not disappeared. Positivity here allows zeros and is not a nonvanishing theorem for arbitrary plats. The retained Fourier phase now has an [exact integer quadratic form](../../notes/actual_matching_graph_centered_fourier_phase.md). The [holomorphic Legendre transport](../../notes/actual_q_hahn_holomorphic_fourier_legendre_transport.md) restores that phase and the original winding characters in the selected ordinary action. Its [global chart](../../notes/actual_q_hahn_global_fourier_legendre_chart.md) is one-to-one on the full physical tube. These are action and coordinate theorems; they do not analytically continue individual finite Fourier coefficients or select the global source cycle. ## What the local estimates can and cannot conclude For sources with phases, a matching lower bound requires survival of the geometric contribution. A large positive comparison partition does not exclude cancellation in the original invariant. The [local energy geometry](../../notes/actual_native_magnetic_energy_local_geometry.md) makes this distinction explicit. The highest-weight block at the fold has the volume action of a variable ideal octahedron. Away from the fold, its actual measure forces a signed boundary term. Even at the real energy maximum, the marked complex phase need not be stationary. A global argument must use the original incidence and peripheral conditions to address those phases. Positive-source calculations explain why angle maximization appears, but the current strict Conway volume proof uses the pure auxiliary source and the whole filling argument described above. Its exact full-power expansion retains signed and odd twists. The supporting source paper supplies the physical and Fourier complements, and the marked geometry identifies the filled action. A character identity or positive comparison alone is not used as a replacement for those estimates. The next boundary pieces now use the same original geometry: [literal prefix signs](../../notes/actual_right_angled_resonant_prefix_signs.md), [generic complemented heads and the outgoing determinant](../../notes/actual_q_hahn_complementary_hard_edge.md), and the [finite negative-clock boundary rate](../../notes/actual_q_hahn_negative_clock_boundary.md). The finite-current theorem also supplies an exact family of band weights that extracts the original root scalar after explicit bounded normalization. At the complete root this functional reduces to the existing coherent cut after a parameter change, so the residual framing freedom remains. This boundary-current route still lacks its unrestricted global internal-period comparison; the strict-tree theorem uses the different global argument explained above.

title: Methods and research approaches
text:
# Methods and research approaches The manuscript develops completed arguments under their stated hypotheses. This chapter also explains approaches whose general applications remain unresolved. Its purpose is to make the calculation behind each approach intelligible before sending the reader to a technical note. The [current papers](../../papers/README.md) give the detailed proofs used by the retained theorems. The library contains supporting arguments and current research; superseded versions remain in Git history. Use the [dependency graph](../../docs/papers/dependencies.html) to distinguish a method that is part of a particular proof from a related proposal that has not supplied its required estimate. There are three different conclusions to distinguish. An **identity** rewrites the same finite quantity exactly. An **estimate** bounds its size, perhaps only from above. A **volume theorem** proves a limit for the original invariant and identifies the number in that limit with the volume of the specified knot complement. A useful identity or a sharp upper bound can be a completed result without being a volume theorem. Throughout, \(K\) is a fixed knot, \(N\ge2\) is the quantum level, and \(K_N(K)\) is the reduced Kashaev invariant; the unknot has value one. We use \[ q_N=e^{\pi i/N},\qquad \zeta_N=q_N^2=e^{2\pi i/N}. \] Both roots occur in the literature. A formula written with \(q_N\) must not be compared with a formula written with \(\zeta_N\) without translating that convention. All diagrams and twist numbers are fixed before \(N\) tends to infinity. The [notation chapter](notation.md) gives the conventions used in the detailed calculations. The starting references are Kashaev's [triangulated construction](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9411147), its [R-matrix formulation](https://arxiv.org/abs/q-alg/9504020), and the [volume proposal](https://arxiv.org/abs/q-alg/9601025). The [Murakami–Murakami paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9905075) relates it to the colored Jones formulation. The finite invariant used here is specified directly; that relation is not a replacement for the source calculations. ## The estimate and the geometric identification Suppose an exact calculation splits the invariant into \[ K_N(K)=G_N+R_N. \] Here \(G_N\) is a specified contribution, including its original scalar factors, and \(R_N\) is everything else. Neither term is automatically a topological invariant on its own. A typical completed argument proves \[ G_N=a_N e^{NS},\qquad  rac{\log|a_N|}{N}\longrightarrow0,\qquad |R_N|\le e^{N(\operatorname{Re}S-\eta)+o(N)} \] for a fixed \(\eta>0\), with \(a_N
e0\) for sufficiently large \(N\). The complex number \(S\) is the critical value of the action in that calculation. Dividing by \(G_N\) shows that \(R_N/G_N	o0\), and hence \[ \lim_{N	o\infty} rac{2\pi}{N}\log|K_N(K)| =2\pi\operatorname{Re}S. \] There is still a geometric assertion to prove: \[ 2\pi\operatorname{Re}S =\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K). \] A formal critical point alone proves none of these three estimates. A positive comparison sum alone does not prove that \(a_N\) is nonzero. A representation of the knot group alone need not be the complete hyperbolic representation. ![The proof requires an exact decomposition, a nonzero geometric contribution, a bound on the remainder, and a geometric identification of the critical value.](../figures/methods-proof-map.svg) For the covered Conway constructions and decorated planar diagrams, the manuscript supplies all these steps. For an unchanged matched simple sphere with the stated Morse presentation and markings, the [geometric contribution theorem](../../docs/papers/casimir-source-asymptotics.pdf) supplies the contribution and its actual filled volume; the general signed remainder estimate remains open. This is why that partial theorem is included without being advertised as a full volume theorem. ## Exact polynomials and shared face variables A **crossing circle** is an auxiliary component bounding a disk pierced by two strands. Removing twists and inserting these circles gives an augmented diagram. After cutting its finite tensor calculation along the projection regions, assign one commuting variable \(L_f\) to each face \(f\). The same face has the same variable at every incident crossing region. Put \(d=N-1\). For the complete-color source identities in this section take \(N\ge3\). A local operator \(p(\Omega)\), where \(\Omega\) is the specified pair Casimir matrix and \(p\) is a polynomial, gives a homogeneous polynomial \[ H_p(x,b,c,y) =\sum_{i+k+\ell+t=d}a_p(i,k,\ell,t)b^ix^ky^\ell c^t . \] The four variables label the four ordered faces adjoining that region. The coefficient \(a_p\) is the corresponding finite matrix coefficient after the stated change to face coordinates. A box carrying a linear map is sometimes called a *coupon* in tensor-diagram notation; here it means precisely this local operator. For the marked spherical construction with \(r\) crossing regions, there are \(r\) ordinary faces and two protected faces \(u,v\). Its shared polynomial is \[ S_N( oldsymbol\sigma) =\left[\prod_{f
e u,v}L_f^dight] \left.\prod_{e=1}^{r}H_e( oldsymbol L;\sigma_e) ight|_{L_u=L_v=0}. \] The brackets mean coefficient extraction. The parameter \(\sigma_e\) is the spectral variable of crossing region \(e\). The two zero substitutions encode the original marked cut; they are not optional boundary conditions. The [finite source proof](../../docs/papers/filling-bounds.pdf) and its [general Morse version](../../notes/research_matched_sphere_morse_source.md) establish this identity with the scalar and endpoint conventions. The terms **central**, **left**, and **right** describe supports of this local polynomial. With \(h=\lfloor d/2floor\), central retains monomials for which both middle-face exponents \(i,t\) are at most \(h\). The left piece has \(t>h\), overloading face \(c\); the right piece has \(i>h\), overloading face \(b\). Since \(i+t\le d\), both exponents cannot exceed \(h\). Expanding the product of these local choices splits \(S_N\) into its all-central part and its complement. These are sectors of one prescribed calculation, not new knot invariants. The [geometric contribution theorem](../../docs/papers/casimir-source-asymptotics.pdf) estimates the original filling functional applied to the all-central sector; a full-invariant theorem must also control the complementary sectors. For a simple illustration of why the variables must remain shared, \[ [z^2](a+bz)(c+dz)=bd. \] Replacing the two factors by separate maxima over their \(z\)-degrees would ignore the common target degree. In a knot diagram there are many such simultaneous constraints. The shared coefficient retains them before any asymptotic estimate. ![A local operator becomes a polynomial in its four adjacent faces. Multiplication and one common coefficient extraction retain the face-degree constraints. The general Morse proof also retains intervening cups and caps.](../figures/homogeneous-face-source.png) Repeated spectral roots require derivatives as well as values. If \(J=cI+U\) with \(U^2=0\), then \[ p(J)=p(c)I+p'(c)U. \] Thus knowing only \(p(c)\) does not determine the operator. This elementary example explains **Hermite data**: values and the derivatives prescribed by the multiplicities of the spectral roots. Derivatives in a spectral variable and derivatives in the generic quantum parameter are different data. Every use of a “normal term” in the notes must specify which derivative it means. The [finite filling estimate](../../docs/papers/filling-bounds.pdf) bounds the next operation, inserting a fixed signed crossing power \(n\). For the original linear functional \(\mathcal L_N^n\) and a polynomial \(H\) of degree at most \(N-1\), \[ |\mathcal L_N^n H| \le (1+|n|/2)\sup_{\sigma\in[-2,2]}|H(\sigma)|. \] Its proof uses the exact values and derivatives at the spectral nodes. Applying it after the shared coefficient extraction adds no exponential cost at fixed twists. It does not estimate the supremum on its right. There is a useful distinction between vanishing values and a vanishing functional. Write \(\chi_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2\), where \(T_N(\cos	heta)=\cos(N	heta)\). If \(H\) vanishes at every root of \(\chi_N\), including the odd-level simple root \(-2\), the same theorem gives \[ |\mathcal L_N^n H|\le rac{N-1}{N}\|H\|_{[-2,2]}. \] The crossing-power factor disappears from this bound, but the derivatives of \(H\) at double roots can still contribute. For the shared difference \(\mathcal D_N=S_{N,\mathrm{full}}-S_{N,\mathrm{central}}\), the degree is at most \(N-1\) in each spectral variable and values vanish on the product of the spectral node sets. This is weaker than vanishing whenever any single variable is a node. Expanding the full functional in all variables cancels exactly its term with no derivatives and yields \[ \left|\left( igotimes_{e=1}^{r}\mathcal L_N^{n_e}ight)\mathcal D_Night| \le \left\{\prod_e(1+|n_e|/2) -\prod_e(1/N+|n_e|/2)ight\} \|\mathcal D_N\|_{[-2,2]^r}. \] The tensor product means that the functionals act successively on their respective spectral variables. This exact saving preserves the shared targets and both level parities. It leaves the size of the between-node polynomial as the remaining problem. These supremum-norm bounds are different from bounds in a positive coefficient norm. Passing between them requires the actual Gram matrix and its cost; the norms cannot be identified without a proof. ## Positive sums, factorial asymptotics, and angle optimization The simplest variational argument applies to a positive sum. Suppose \(\mathcal X_N\) is a finite index set with \(|\mathcal X_N|\le N^c\), and the weights \(w_N(x)>0\) satisfy a uniform logarithmic estimate \[ \log w_N(x)=N F(x/N)+o(N). \] Here \(c\) is fixed and \(F\) is a continuous action on the limiting admissible set. The elementary inequalities \[ \max_x w_N(x)\le\sum_xw_N(x) \le|\mathcal X_N|\max_xw_N(x) \] give the exponential rate once admissible integer points approach a maximizer at every sufficiently large level. That last condition is an actual support question. A sequence of numerically favorable levels does not establish it. Quantum factorials lead to integrals of logarithms of sine functions. The basic example is \[  rac1N\log\prod_{j=1}^{\lfloor Ntfloor} 2\sin rac{\pi j}{N} \longrightarrow \int_0^t\log(2\sin\pi x)\,dx =- rac{\Lambda(\pi t)}{\pi}, \qquad 0<t<1, \] where \[ \Lambda(	heta)=-\int_0^	heta \log|2\sin s|\,ds \] is the Lobachevsky function. Near \(t=0,1\), the logarithmic singularities require endpoint estimates; uniformity there is not a consequence of a smooth Riemann-sum rule. This positive-sum argument is a discrete Laplace principle. It is distinct from both majorization and a Tauberian theorem, even though all three exploit positivity or convexity. The [positive Conway variational proof](../../docs/papers/newton-calculus.pdf) establishes the support and factorial estimates for its stated expressions. The [geometric realization](../../docs/papers/strict-conway-geometry.pdf) is a further argument. Positivity by itself neither constructs a knot complement nor proves invariance under changes of triangulation. A proposed positive tetrahedral model must also satisfy the appropriate local move identities with its full peripheral factors retained. An **angle structure** on an ideal triangulation assigns positive dihedral angles to its tetrahedra. In each tetrahedron the three angles at a vertex sum to \(\pi\); around each manifold edge the incident angles sum to \(2\pi\). Opposite tetrahedron edges have equal angles. These are linear conditions, so the allowed assignments form a relatively open convex polytope, when it is nonempty. For one positively oriented ideal tetrahedron with angle triple \((\alpha, eta,\gamma)\), its volume is \[ V(\alpha, eta,\gamma) =\Lambda(\alpha)+\Lambda( eta)+\Lambda(\gamma), \qquad \alpha+ eta+\gamma=\pi. \] The total volume is strictly concave on the positive angle domain. This is the concavity used in the Casson–Rivin variational approach; the volume is not described as a convex function to be minimized. Stationarity in all allowed directions supplies the remaining length and gluing conditions. The peripheral equations and the actual face identifications still have to be retained. The [marked positive gluing proof](../../docs/papers/marked-fillings.pdf) carries out these steps for its stated triangulation certificate. For one tetrahedron this concavity can be checked directly. Use \(\alpha, eta\) as coordinates and put \(\gamma=\pi-\alpha- eta\). The negative Hessian of its volume is \[ -
abla^2V=  egin{pmatrix} \cot\alpha+\cot\gamma&\cot\gamma\ \cot\gamma&\cot eta+\cot\gamma \end{pmatrix}. \] Its first diagonal entry is \(\sin eta/(\sin\alpha\sin\gamma)>0\), and its determinant is one, using \(\cot\alpha\cot eta+\cot eta\cot\gamma+\cot\gamma\cot\alpha=1\). It is therefore positive definite. This calculation also explains why one cannot assume that every individual cotangent is positive: one angle may exceed \(\pi/2\), while the constrained Hessian still has the required sign. Summing these quadratic forms and restricting to the allowed linear variations gives strict concavity for the entire positive angle structure. One can see how the equations enter by differentiating: \[ dV(\dot{ oldsymbol\alpha}) =-\sum_{	ext{tetrahedron angle slots }a} \log(2\sin\alpha_a)\,\dot\alpha_a . \] An allowed variation \(\dot{ oldsymbol\alpha}\) satisfies the homogeneous versions of the tetrahedron and edge equations. Requiring this derivative to vanish for every such variation is a coupled condition. Maximizing each tetrahedron separately would instead assign it three angles \(\pi/3\); those independent choices need not satisfy the edge equations of the given triangulation. This explains why adding local maximum volumes is not the variational problem used in the proof. There are two logically different tasks here. One must find an interior critical point, and one must show that the cells and face pairings describe the intended manifold. Strict concavity proves uniqueness once those tasks have been met. It does not prove that every chosen triangulation has a positive solution. The [geometry chapter](geometry.md) explains the actual cells, cusp markings, and smooth fillings used in this project. For the precise standard criterion on an orientable manifold with torus boundary, see [Futer and Guéritaud, *From angled triangulations to hyperbolic structures*, Definition 3.1 and Theorem 1.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1004.0440). [Rivin's 1994 paper](https://annals.math.princeton.edu/1994/139-3/p02) gives the earlier variational setting. The marked gluing proof linked above establishes the version used by this source rather than inferring it from the appearance of a dilogarithm. ## Weighted Cauchy and the cost of joining pieces Let \(\mathcal I_N\) be the original finite index set, and write a scalar evaluation as \(Z_N=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal I_N}a_\alpha\). For any specified positive weights \(w_\alpha\), \[ |Z_N|^2 \le \left(\sum_\alpha w_\alphaight) \left(\sum_\alpha rac{|a_\alpha|^2}{w_\alpha}ight). \] This is Cauchy–Schwarz applied to the vectors \((\sqrt{w_\alpha})_\alpha\) and \((a_\alpha/\sqrt{w_\alpha})_\alpha\). A useful choice of weights must make both factors estimable for the original contraction. Weights can redistribute a cost, but cannot recover a phase discarded by the inequality. Indeed the infimum of the displayed right-hand side over positive weights is \((\sum_\alpha|a_\alpha|)^2\), attained by \(w_\alpha=|a_\alpha|\) when no entry vanishes and approached otherwise. For \(a_1=1,a_2=-1\), the exact sum is zero while even this optimized bound is four. The application therefore needs structural information about the joined source, not just an optimized positive weight for every separate term. The matrix form allows a further possibility: its off-diagonal entries can retain interference between different coefficients. If \(G\) is a positive definite Hermitian matrix, \(v\) is the source vector, and \(b\) is the row implementing the original closure, then \[ |bv|^2 \le (bG^{-1}b^*)(v^*Gv). \] The star denotes conjugate transpose. The first factor is the cost of the marked closure in the dual norm; the second is the source energy. Calling \(G\) a convenient inner product does not bound either cost. For a chain \(v_{j+1}=A_jv_j\), a concrete sufficient estimate is \[ A_j^*G_{j+1}A_j\le e^{2\varepsilon_j}G_j,\qquad G_j>0 . \] The matrix inequality means that its right-hand side minus its left-hand side is positive semidefinite. Iteration and the closure estimate give \[ |b\,v_m|^2\le (bG_m^{-1}b^*)\,e^{2\sum_j\varepsilon_j}\,(v_0^*G_0v_0). \] Thus a useful varying norm must control the actual transport between successive norms and both endpoints. Making an intermediate matrix small by a change of basis can enlarge these endpoint factors. For a network, the analogous check must keep every shared boundary index and its measure. When two pieces share a boundary label \(j\), the contraction still has one common sum over \(j\). If its original measure is a positive number \(	heta_N(j)\), a useful exact form is \[ Z_{\mathrm{joined}} =\sum_j rac{Z_A(j)Z_B(j)}{	heta_N(j)}. \] Set \(F_A(j)=Z_A(j)/\sqrt{	heta_N(j)}\), and define \(F_B\) likewise. Cauchy bounds the square of the joined value by \((\sum_j|F_A(j)|^2)(\sum_j|F_B(j)|^2)\). It gives no lower bound on their overlap: the two vectors can be orthogonal. The [whole-support boundary estimate](../../notes/actual_whole_support_boundary_gram_envelope.md) and [exact joining identity](../../notes/actual_nc_three_port_source_sewing.md) establish useful local inputs. For a reflected double, the two halves can be genuine complex conjugates in the specified pairing, giving a positive sum of squares. The [reflection-double theorem](../../notes/actual_planar_three_port_reflection_double.md) proves precisely that identity. Its internal half-evaluations still contain their original phases. The general problem is to transport the estimates through the whole diagram and prove that the required contribution survives. ### Moment matrices: positivity with interference retained A **moment** of a positive probability measure \(\mu\) on the real line is \(m_j=\int t^j\,d\mu(t)\), when that integral is finite. For a nonnegative integer \(r\), if the moments through degree \(2r\) exist, the matrix \[ H=(m_{i+j})_{0\le i,j\le r} \] is positive semidefinite. Indeed, for \(p(t)=\sum_{j=0}^r a_jt^j\), \[ a^*Ha=\int|p(t)|^2\,d\mu(t)\ge0. \] This is a *Gram matrix*: its entries are the inner products of the monomials \(1,t,\ldots,t^r\). Its entries with \(i
e j\) are the cross terms in the squared polynomial. They need not be discarded when applying Cauchy. For example, take the uniform probability measure on \([0,1]\) and \(p(t)=1-2t\). Then \[ H= egin{pmatrix}1&1/2\1/2&1/3\end{pmatrix}, \qquad \int_0^1p(t)\,dt=0,\qquad \int_0^1|p(t)|^2\,dt= rac13. \] Keeping only the diagonal of \(H\) would instead give \(1+4/3=7/3\). The full positive form retains some cancellation, but Cauchy's bound \(0\le1/3\) still does not compute the zero expectation. This distinction matters at exponential scale. The source has an exact example. For \(N\ge3\), put \(d=N-1\), \(M=\lfloor N/2floor-1\), and \(	heta=\pi/N\). The notes call the following one-sided polynomial a *protected cap*: two of its four face variables are the protected zeros, and \(A,C\) are the remaining ordinary variables. At spectral value \(2\), it is \[ H_{\mathrm{cap}}(A,C;2)= \sum_{j=0}^{M}(-1)^jU_jA^{d-j}C^j,\qquad U_j=\csc^2(	heta/2) \prod_{r=1}^{j}  rac{\sin^2(r	heta)}{\sin^2((r+1/2)	heta)}. \] The product formula defines \(U_j\) for \(0\le j\le d\), with the empty product equal to one. The polynomial uses only \(0\le j\le M\), its original one-sided support. The [positive cap-moment theorem](../../notes/research_flat_cap_positive_moment_form.md) constructs a probability measure \(\mu_N\) satisfying \[ \int t^j\,d\mu_N(t)= rac{U_j}{U_0}\quad(0\le j\le d). \] Thus, for arbitrary coefficients \(a_j\) and \(p(t)=\sum_{j=0}^{M}a_jt^j\), \[ \sum_{j=0}^{M}(-1)^jU_ja_j =U_0\int p(-t)\,d\mu_N(t),\qquad \left|\sum_{j=0}^{M}(-1)^jU_ja_jight|^2 \le U_0^2\int|p(-t)|^2\,d\mu_N(t). \] The degree check is \(2M\le d\). The measure has unbounded support, so a bound for \(p\) on \([0,1]\) cannot replace the integral. The [cap-moment norm obstruction](../../notes/research_cap_moment_cauchy_norm_obstruction.md) shows that the resulting Cauchy upper bound can exceed the original positive endpoint comparison exponentially, even with the original two-piece degree constraint imposed. It does not show that the signed expectation exceeds that comparison. A positive norm exists; the required source estimate can still fail for that norm. At even level \(N=2m\), the same moment theorem also gives an exact \(m\)-point **Gaussian quadrature**: an integral of any polynomial of degree at most \(2m-1=d\) is a positive weighted sum of its values at \(m\) positive nodes. Its symmetric tridiagonal matrix has entries \(\int t\,p_i(t)p_j(t)\,d\mu_N(t)\), where \(0\le i,j<m\) and \(p_i\) is the orthonormal polynomial of degree \(i\). The nodes are its eigenvalues. “Orthonormal” means that the integrals of products of distinct basis polynomials are zero and the integral of each squared polynomial is one. This finite evaluation is useful computationally; it is not an estimate of its summands. The standard matrix construction is explained by [Golub and Welsch, *Calculation of Gauss Quadrature Rules*, §§1–2](https://www.ams.org/journals/mcom/1969-23-106/S0025-5718-69-99647-1/S0025-5718-69-99647-1.pdf). The source note separately proves that its particular moments and degree cutoff permit that construction. ### Summing the exterior before estimating the cap There is a stronger use of the same idea. Remove the selected cap and extract the prescribed coefficient in **every** ordinary face variable except \(A,C\). At each of the other crossing regions keep the central polynomial at spectral value \(-2\). The result is a homogeneous binary polynomial \[ P_N(A,C)=\sum_{j=0}^{d}p_{N,j}A^jC^{d-j},\qquad d=N-1. \] Here \(p_{N,j}\) already includes all the other face sums. It is not the coefficient of one neighboring crossing. This order of operations preserves the interactions between neighbors that share a face. At odd levels, the exact central factors are determinants of positive Hermitian matrix pencils. They are *real stable*: a real polynomial is called real stable if it is nonzero whenever every argument has positive imaginary part. The determinant proof and coefficient extraction show that a nonzero \(P_N\) has the factorization \[ P_N(A,C)=P_N(1,1)\prod_{r=1}^{d}  igl((1-p_r)C+p_rA igr),\qquad 0\le p_r\le1. \] This is an identity for the original extracted polynomial. The [proof for this source](../../notes/research_cap_common_axis_bound.md) gives the matrix and extraction steps. For the general theory of stability preservers, see Borcea and Brändén's [*Multivariate Pólya–Schur classification problems in the Weyl algebra*](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0606360). The new inequalities below are proved directly from the displayed factorization. Define \[ 
u_d= rac1d\sum_r p_r,\qquad \kappa_d= rac1d\sum_r p_r(1-p_r). \] Equivalently these are the first and second derivatives at \(z=0\) of \(d^{-1}\log P_N(e^z,1)\). The second is the average variance of Bernoulli variables with parameters \(p_r\); it is not the variance of the list of parameters. Applying arithmetic–geometric mean to the squared linear factors, and then maximizing their common argument, gives \[ \max_{0\le t\le1} igl\{|P_N(-t,1)|,|P_N(-1,t)| igr\} \le P_N(1,1) \left(\max\{1-
u_d-\kappa_d,
u_d-\kappa_d,1-4\kappa_d\}ight)^{d/2}. \] The word “common” matters: every factor is evaluated at the same \(t\). Maximizing each factor separately would discard the cancellation being estimated. The original cap uses only the first \(M+1\) coefficients, with \(M=\lfloor N/2floor-1\). It therefore requires control of the alternating partial sum \[ Q_M(t)=\sum_{j=0}^{M}(-1)^jp_{N,j}t^j, \] not just the full polynomial. The coefficients of the factorization are log-concave: \(p_{N,j}^2\ge p_{N,j-1}p_{N,j+1}\), and their nonzero indices form an interval. Consequently successive term ratios decrease. This gives one estimate while the omitted alternating tail decreases and another while the retained terms increase. The [finite truncation theorem](../../notes/research_cap_uniform_spectral_gap.md) proves both estimates, including zero coefficients and both parity cutoffs. It integrates them against the positive density \[  rac{N\sin(\pi/N)}{\pi(1+t^N)}\,dt,\qquad t>0. \] Its moment matrix is the sine-Cauchy matrix \(C_{ij}=\sin(\pi/N)/\sin((i+j+1)\pi/N)\), for \(0\le i,j\le M\). The exact cap recurrence is self-adjoint in the inverse matrix, which bounds the cap functional uniformly for every real spectral value in \([-2,2]\). Only moments through degree \(2M\le N-2\) occur. The [companion norm theorem](../../notes/research_protected_cap_coupled_norm.md) also compares this matrix with the original cap moment matrix at polynomial cost. That comparison holds at both parities. Its application to a stable exterior still requires the odd-level factorization above.
