Here is a proof covering all degrees simultaneously. Choose \(c_v=k_0/2\) at every nonroot vertex and write \(\delta\) for their common value in (3). The elementary cosine estimate gives \[ \chi\ge\frac{r_0^2}{2}-\frac{r_0^4}{24} =2^{-9}\frac{3071}{3072}>2^{-10},\qquad \delta>2^{-30}. \tag{48} \] At any vertex, including the root, put \(\mathcal R_v=\sqrt{d_v^2+n_v^2}\). Then \[ A_v\ge\frac{k_0d_v}{2\pi^2},\qquad B_v\le16d_v, \qquad C_v\le\frac{\mathcal R_v^2}{8k_0d_v}. \tag{49} \] For the last inequality use \(16\le1/(8k_0)\). Each of the four branches of the minimum in (6) consequently has the following lower bound, respectively: \[ \frac\delta2,\qquad \frac{t_0k_0d_v}{\pi\mathcal R_v},\qquad \frac{k_0d_v}{16\mathcal R_v},\qquad 2^{-12}. \tag{50} \] The second displayed quantity is smaller than the third and fourth. For the third bound, use \(\pi|b_v|+t_0|D_v|\le\mathcal R_v(1+t_0/\pi)/2\). Thus every branch of (7), not just its tail branch, is bounded below by \[ \eta_v\ge\min\left\{ \frac{t_0\mathcal R_v\delta}{8\pi}, \frac{t_0^2 k_0d_v}{4\pi^2}\right\}. \tag{51} \] Indeed the second entry here is smaller than each of the other three entries in (7), by their explicit values and \(t_0\ll r_0\). On the other hand \[ \beta_v=\frac{420\pi}{361}\frac{d_v}{\mathcal R_v^2} <\frac{4d_v}{\mathcal R_v^2}. \tag{52} \] For comparison with half the first entry of (51), it suffices that \(\mathcal R_v^2>64\pi/(t_0\delta)\), since \(d_v\le\mathcal R_v\). The right side is less than \(2^{52}\), using \(\pi<4\) and (48). For comparison with half the second entry it suffices that \(\mathcal R_v^2>32\pi^2/(t_0^2k_0)\), whose right side is less than \(2^{53}\), since \(\pi^2<10\). Both inequalities follow strictly from \(\mathcal R_v^2\ge n_v^2\ge2^{54}\). The charge-cut condition in (8) follows as well. For the outgoing patch, the sharper elementary estimate is \[ \beta_v\le\frac{210\pi}{361|n_v|} \le\frac{330}{361}\,2^{-26} <\frac{3071}{3072}\,2^{-26} \le\frac{k_0}2\chi. \tag{53} \] Here \(\pi<22/7\), \(d_v/(d_v^2+n_v^2)\le1/(2|n_v|)\), and the displayed rational comparison prove (9) for every degree. This completes the corollary without a numerical scan or a threshold depending on the tree. The same proof gives a mixed condition, chosen independently at each vertex: \[ \boxed{\qquad d_v\ge2^{28}\quad\text{or}\quad |n_v|\ge2^{27} \qquad\text{for every }v.\qquad} \tag{53a} \] Under the degree alternative, \(\mathcal R_v^2\ge d_v^2\ge2^{56}\) proves the same two tail comparisons, while \[ \beta_v\le\frac{420\pi}{361d_v} \le\frac{330}{361}\,2^{-26} <\frac{k_0}2\chi \tag{53b} \] is the same outgoing patch bound. Neither alternative needs to hold uniformly over all vertices. In particular, the high-degree vertices may retain any fixed signed powers, including zero and small nonzero powers. No sum over the number of such vertices occurs. Here is a precise extension construction illustrating that freedom. Start with any fixed ordered circle-tree core whose original endpoint pairing closes to a knot and has no internal closed component. Retain all its fixed signed powers. At every core vertex choose one of its actual product slots next to its crossing box and insert a consecutive stack of an even number \(B\ge2^{28}\) of new terminal pieces. Every new leaf has a fixed odd power satisfying \[ |n_{\mathrm{leaf}}|\ge2^{27}+1. \tag{53c} \] The physical quarter-turn of an odd two-strand braid has diagonal pairing \(X=\{02,13\}\); this pairing is invariant under the quarter-turn. An even ordered stack of these leaves has the through pairing \(I=\{03,12\}\) and creates no internal circle. Inserting it in the specified slot therefore preserves the original local endpoint pairing in that actual frame. This is a pairing calculation, not an isotopy removing the new tangles. At the original closing box the same insertion takes place inside its local ball. An added terminal leaf may then be chosen as the recursive root using the original closed-collar move with its induced frame reversal and factor order retained. Thus the resulting diagram is again a knot, while its knot type may change. Each old vertex now satisfies the degree alternative and each new leaf satisfies the twist alternative in (53a). The resulting actual knot complement is hyperbolic and satisfies (10)–(12). The number and arrangement of prescribed short-power vertices are arbitrary but fixed; the number \(B\) does not depend on their total count. ![An even stack of added odd terminal tangles preserves the core's endpoint pairing.](../book/figures/directed-tree-volume.svg) The upper drawing is a tree of tangle operations, not a knot projection. Only one added pair is drawn at each original vertex. The construction inserts \(B/2\) consecutive pairs in one specified product slot, retaining the original cyclic order; \(B\ge2^{28}\) is even. Each added leaf has odd \(|m|\ge2^{27}+1\), and every tree edge applies the physical quarter-turn \(T\). The lower drawing forgets crossings and shows the literal endpoint pairings: two diagonal pairings compose to the through pairing. It does not claim that the new braids can be removed by an isotopy. ## 9. A star beyond both previous quantitative tests Consider an ordered star rooted at its central vertex, of odd degree \(d=30{,}000{,}001\). Set its power to 2 and every terminal power to the fixed odd integer \(2^{60}+1\). Choose \(c_v=k_0/2\) on every leaf. The knot pairing can be checked in the original terminal-root syntax, even though the finite contraction is evaluated from the center. Label the boundary points lower left, lower right, upper right, upper left by \(0,1,2,3\). The even and odd braid pairings are respectively \[ I=\{03,12\},\qquad X=\{02,13\};\qquad T(I)=H=\{01,23\},\quad T(X)=X. \tag{54a} \] At a terminal root there are \(d-1\) other leaves. Their turned odd braids have pairing \(X\); their ordered product has pairing \(I\) because \(d-1\) is even. The central power \(2\) preserves it. Its actual quarter-turn has pairing \(H\), and stacking the root's odd braid against \(H\) still gives \(H\), with no internal closed arc. Cylindrical closure joins \(03\) and \(12\), so it closes \(H\) into one component. All intermediate products before that last stack are two through-strand braids. There is no hidden internal component. The criterion can be verified by rational enclosures without expanding this large tree. All leaves have the same data. The center has approximately \[ \beta_o=1.219\,10^{-7},\qquad \eta_o=2.713\,10^{-7},\qquad \frac{\beta_o}{\eta_o/2}<0.9. \tag{54} \] Every leaf has a much smaller ratio. The root does not satisfy the nonroot patch inequality for any \(c>0\), because \(\beta_o>k_0\chi\). Nevertheless its exact final trace satisfies (8). Thus that outgoing patch must not be charged to a root that sends no message. Moreover \[ \sum_v\frac{d_v}{d_v^2+n_v^2} >\frac{30,000,001}{30,000,001^2+4}>2^{-25}, \tag{55} \] and its maximum is far above \(2^{-120}\). The example therefore lies beyond both published quantitative alternatives. Its size and all its powers are fixed; it is not an N-growing family. The constant sizes are coarse, and no optimality assertion is intended. Here are rational enclosures proving the inequalities rather than inferring them from those decimal values. Put \[ \pi_- =3,\quad \pi_+=22/7,\quad c=k_0/2,\quad \chi_-=r_0^2/2-r_0^4/24,\quad \delta_- =\frac{c\chi_-}{4(1+c)}. \tag{56} \] At the central vertex use the conservative height \(y_* =\delta_-/2\). It is at most each branch of (6). For example, with \[ D_- =\frac d{2\pi_+},\quad D_+=\frac{d+1}{2\pi_-},\quad A_- =\frac{dc}{\pi_+^2},\quad C_+=d+\frac{\pi_-^{-2}}{4A_-}, \tag{57} \] the three non-strip comparisons are \[ y_*<\frac{t_0D_-}{4C_+},\qquad y_*<\frac{dc}{8(1+t_0D_+)},\qquad y_*^2<\frac c8. \tag{58} \] The strip comparison follows from \(\delta\ge\delta_-\). Every quantity in (56)–(58) is rational. Direct cross-multiplication also gives \[ \frac{2[420\pi_+d/(361(d^2+4))]} {t_0D_-y_*/2}<\frac9{10}, \qquad 2\frac{420\pi_+d}{361(d^2+4)} <\min\left\{\frac{dc}{2},\ A_-r_0^2, \frac{D_-r_0^2}{8}\right\}. \tag{59} \] These compare the upper bound for twice the first-charge drop with all four lower bounds for \(\eta_o\). The charge cutoff is greater than two. For a leaf with \(n=2^{60}+1\), take \(y_*=t_0k_0/(2n)\). The same direct rational comparisons, using \(D_-=n/(2\pi_+)\), \(D_+=(n+1)/(2\pi_-)\), \(A_-=2k_0/\pi_+^2\), and \(C_+=16+[n/(2\pi_-)]^2/(4A_-)\), put this height below each branch of (6). They give a lower bound greater than \(2^{-49}\) for every entry of (7), while \(\beta_v<2^{-117}\). The outgoing patch follows from \(\beta_v<(k_0/2)\chi_-\). This proves the leaf inequalities. ## 10. Reproducing the finite arithmetic and pairings From the repository root run: python3 experiments/audit_actual_all_circle_directed_volume.py The [script](../experiments/audit_actual_all_circle_directed_volume.py) writes [its results](../experiments/actual_all_circle_directed_volume_results.json). An optional --output selects a different JSON file. It uses exact rational arithmetic for the constant inequalities, the all-degree corollaries and the star enclosures. It also constructs the literal four-endpoint pairings and checks the composition and closure identities used above. Those are finite checks, not numerical evidence for the asymptotic theorem. The proof of the full invariant estimates is the conditional kernel and trace induction in sections 2–7. The earlier [exact tree-message reproduction](../experiments/audit_all_circle_local_message_recursion.py) independently compares canonical quotient contractions with root-grid and complete first-normal traces; the present argument retains those same finite identities.

title: Full first-normal bounds for all supported Racah partners
text: # Full first-normal bounds for all supported Racah partners 29 October 2026. This proves a uniform polynomial relative bound for the ACTUAL first generic-q normal at every one of the 64 reflected branches of a supported folded sextuple. The new step is a positive finite presentation of the full generic source on face-supported branches, including branches whose seven-factorial formula has a live `[2N]` current. The already proved Fourier partner involution and exact first- normal Ward equation then cover the remaining branches. Every fixed generic normal order is controlled on the face-supported branches. The general 64-branch conclusion is FIRST ORDER ONLY. No completed physical recoupling norm or global volume equality follows merely from this local scalar theorem. ## 1. Statement and source convention Fix `N>=3`, `D=N-1`, `q=exp(pi i/N)`, and integer folded labels `j=(a,b,c,d,e,f)` in `[0,D/2]`, with all four face sums at least `D`. Use the SAME actual generic seven-factorial sum and normalization as in [the reciprocal source theorem](actual_racah_partner_reflection_identity.md): K_B(zeta)=[N]^2 S_B(zeta)^2 product_faces Delta_B^2, k(B)=D_log(zeta) K_B(q). Here B records any subset of the six changes `j -> D-j`. The original actual source prefactors, peripheral factors and marking are not changed. The proved root-value identity gives `K_B(q)=W_N^2>0` for all branches. There is an absolute constant C such that max_B |k(B)| <= C N^2(1+log N) W_N^2. (1) The local analytic square root positive at q, and the first inverse jets of K and its square root, have corresponding relative bounds. Every implicit constant below is independent of the supported labels, level parity and compositeness. A set of high bits is called face-supported if it is contained in one of the four faces (a,b,e), (c,d,e), (a,d,f), (b,c,f). For every such branch, and every fixed r, the stronger conclusion is |D_log(zeta)^r K_B(q)| <= C_r N^(c_r) W_N^2, (2) with the analogous local square-root and inverse bounds. An opposite pair of high bits is not face-supported; that two-bit case is tail- free and is already covered by the positive-core theorem. ## 2. A root-unit presentation of the FULL generic source A tail-free branch already has all fixed-jet bounds. Consider a live face-supported branch, so all three opposite sums exceed `2D`. Choose an opposite pair with maximal label sum, and use tetrahedral relabeling to call it `(e,f)`, with f its high-bit edge and e its low-bit edge. This is possible: the largest opposite sum exceeds D, whereas an opposite pair with both bits low has sum at most D. A face contains at most one edge of each opposite pair. In this labeling, e<=D/2<=f, e+f>=max(a+c,b+d), min(a,b)<=D/2, min(c,d)<=D/2. (3) For the last assertion, the two remaining possible high edges are in the face containing f. Each of the two faces containing e therefore has at most one high external edge. The same assertion is immediate when there are fewer than three high bits. Set p=min(a+d,b+c), s=a+b+c+d, h=max(|a-b|,|c-d|), t0=s-2p, rA=a+b-h, rC=c+d-h, n=p-f, t=p+f-D. (4) The exact elementary identity p+h=max(a+c,b+d) (5) follows by expanding the difference of the maximum and minimum: its four possibilities are `a-b,b-a,c-d,d-c`. The true triangle conditions give `n>=0` and `h<=e`. Equations (3),(5) imply n<=e-h, h+e+n<=2e<=D, n<=t. (6) Furthermore 0<=n<=rA,rC<=D, 0<=t<=D, 0<=t0, t0+n<=D. (7) Indeed `rA,rC<=D` follows from (3), and `n<=e-h` together with `e<=a+b,c+d` proves their lower bounds. The upper bound on t follows from `p+f<=2D`, since both relevant face sums are at most `2D`. Finally `t0+n=max(a+d,b+c)-f` is a face deficit and belongs to `[0,D]`. All these are literal integer inequalities, including walls. Write `Q=zeta^2`, `alpha=zeta^(2h+1)`, `z=zeta^(2e+1)`. The already proved [actual generic source conversion](actual_general_four_port_single_racah_kernel.md#6-exact-conversion-to-the-seven-factorial-sum-including-its-phase) is the exact identity S=S0 (V_n/C_n) G_n, G_n=sum_(k=0)^n (Q^-n,Q^(-p-f-1),alpha z,alpha/z;Q)_k Q^k /(Q,Q^(t0+1),Q^-rA,Q^-rC;Q)_k. (8) This is the actual finite generic series BEFORE specializing q. By (6),(7), every numerator and denominator factor of every term in (8) is a root unit. For the second upper parameter use `p+f+1=N+t`; its root exponents are those of `Q^-t`, and `k<=n<=t`. For the two spectral factors, their exponent ranges are h+e+1,...,h+e+k in [1,D], h-e,...,h-e+k-1 in [-D,-1]. (9) Thus there is no disappearing generic summand and no singular Pochhammer denominator in this presentation. ## 3. Every summand has positive root value Let `s_r=product_(u=1)^r 2sin(pi u/N)` and `c_j=2cos((2j+1)pi/N)`. Direct conversion of each finite Pochhammer in (8) to sine factors gives its kth root summand as A_k product_(i=0)^(k-1)(c_(h+i)-c_e), A_k= s_n/s_(n-k) * s_t/s_(t-k) * s_(rA-k)/s_rA * s_(rC-k)/s_rC * s_t0/[s_k s_(t0+k)] >0. (10) For clarity this is the same finite phase calculation as in the proved folded spectral formula; it only requires the inequalities (6),(7), not that every external label is folded. The residual monomial phase is `q^(Nk)` and the residual sign is `(-1)^k`, so both cancel. The spectral factorization uses (alpha z,alpha/z;Q)_k = product_(i<k) alpha Q^i (c_(h+i)-c_e) at the root. Since `h+i<e<=D/2` whenever `i<k<=n`, every displayed cosine difference is strictly positive. The term at k=0 is one. Hence the ENTIRE true generic series has a positive common phase at q and a nonzero value `G_n(q)>0`. Each term in (8) is a product of a bounded number of finite unit Pochhammers of lengths O(N), with integer exponents O(N). On the uniform disk |log(zeta/q)| <= c/[N^2(1+log N)], (11) every such term divided by its positive root value remains in a small sector about one. This is the elementary unit-factor harmonic estimate proved in the positive-core note: sum the logarithmic changes using `|sin(pi u/N)|>=2 dist(u,N Z)/N`. The bounded number of products, including negative exponents and exponents up to `2N`, only changes the absolute constant. Their positive sum obeys the same estimate. Cauchy inequalities therefore bound every fixed jet of G_n and its inverse relative to their root values. ## 4. Actual prefactor cancellation retains the generic normal It remains essential to check the prefactor in (8). Positivity of a substituted polynomial alone would not prove the source theorem. Choose `(a',b',c',d')=(a,b,c,d)` if `a+d<=b+c`, and `(b,a,d,c)` otherwise. The actual source formula gives R=(c+d-e, a+b-e, t0, a'-b'+e, d'-c'+e), S0=(-1)^s [s+1]!/product_(u in R)[u]!, V_n=zeta^n (Q^(-p-f-1);Q)_n /[(Q;Q)_n(Q^(t0+1);Q)_n(Q^(-s-1);Q)_n], C_n=alpha^n (Q^(-p-f-1);Q)_n /[(Q^(t0+1);Q)_n(Q^-rA;Q)_n(Q^-rC;Q)_n]. (12) Every entry of R is in `[0,D]`: these are face deficits, together with t0, bounded by (7). Because the branch is live, 2N<=s+1<3N, 0<=s+1-2N<n. (13) The second inequality follows from `max(a+d,b+c)+f<=2D`. Consequently `[s+1]!` contains exactly `[N]` and `[2N]`, while `(Q^(-s-1);Q)_n` contains exactly one zero factor, namely `1-zeta^(-4N)`. All other factors in (12) are root units by (6),(7). Cancel the common Pochhammers in V_n/C_n GENERICALLY. Then cancel the indicated zero factor using the exact identity [2N]/(1-zeta^(-4N))=zeta^(2N)/(zeta-zeta^-1). (14) If a superscript circle means omitting exactly the indicated factor, the result is the explicit analytic unit identity (-1)^D S/[N]=A(zeta) G_n(zeta), A(zeta)=(-1)^(D+s) zeta^(2N-2hn)/(zeta-zeta^-1) * [s+1]!^(omit N,2N)/product_(u in R)[u]! * (Q^-rA,Q^-rC;Q)_n /[(Q;Q)_n (Q^(-s-1);Q)_n^(omit -2N)]. (15) Every denominator in (15) is now a root unit. No term proportional to `[2N]` in the original seven-factorial sum has been dropped: (15) is an equality of the original generic germs, obtained from the exact finite source transformation and exact cancellation (14). The same unit-factor estimate applies to A and its inverse; the additional monomial has exponent O(N^2), and the extra quantum integer denominator is a root unit. Combining it with the positive G_n gives fixed relative jet bounds for the entire original regular source `(-1)^D S/[N]`. Its root value is the positive original core C, so A(q)>0 as well. The four regularized face factors are analytic units with the already proved uniform relative jet bounds. Therefore (2), its inverse version and its local square-root version follow on the SAME polynomial disk (11). ## 5. Cover all first normals using exact source relations The [first-normal Ward theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_partner_first_normal_ward_reduction.md) proves, for each opposite pair and every choice of the other bits, k(00)-k(01)-k(10)+k(11)=0. (16) Apply it independently to the three opposite pairs. Every branch is a signed sum of at most 27 branches having at most one high bit in each opposite pair. Thus it remains to handle high sets of size at most three, with no opposite pair. Sets of size zero, one or two are face-supported. A three-edge set with one edge of each opposite pair is either a face or the complement of a face, namely a three-edge star. Face sets satisfy (2). Consider a star set. If the branch is tail-free, use the positive-core theorem. If its maximal face sum is repeated, use the proved coherent Fourier bound. Otherwise use the exact controlled first-normal difference from the [Fourier source involution](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_coherent_racah_tail_fourier_residues.md#6-the-residual-is-an-exact-partner-involution): |k(B)-k(B*)| <= C N^2(1+log N) W_N^2, (17) where B* flips the three edges outside its unique largest face. The unique maximal face cannot be the all-low face complementary to the high star. Every other face shares one of its low edges and replaces its two remaining low edges by their high partners; its sum is at least that of the all-low face. Equality everywhere would also contradict uniqueness. Therefore the maximal face contains two high edges and one low edge. Its complementary flip turns the third high edge low and turns its other two low edges high. In terms of opposite pairs, B* has one pair in state `00` and two pairs in state `11`: a tetrahedral face contains exactly one edge from each opposite pair. Apply (16) to those two `11` pairs. This expresses k(B*) as a signed sum of at most nine branches with at most TWO high bits, all already controlled by (2). Equation (17) controls the star branch. Finally the initial 27-term interpolation proves (1) for every original partner, with constants independent of N, labels and parity. The estimates are on the actual full generic first normals. The proof has not replaced a normal by the root core, differentiated a root-value identity, or imposed the first-order Ward equation on higher orders. The original coherent tail itself now has a uniform bound on EVERY partner branch: |T_B(q)| <= C(1+log N) C_B(q). (18) For a tail-free branch T is zero. Otherwise write the exact germ as `K_B=U_B(C_B+[2N]T_B)^2`, where U_B is the product of the four regularized face factors. The logarithmic derivatives of U_B and the positive core C_B are `O(N^2(1+log N))`. Divide the first normal by `K_B(q)=U_B(q)C_B(q)^2` and use (1). This bounds `[2N]'(q) T_B(q)/C_B(q)` by the same order. Finally |[2N]'(q)|=2N/sin(pi/N)>=2N^2/pi, which proves (18). Thus the contribution of the actual retained tail to the first normal is controlled through an exact positive source presentation; no absolute estimate of its alternating summands was substituted. ## 6. Precise remaining scope This closes the local ALL-PARTNER FIRST-NORMAL scalar gap. Fixed higher normals are proved here for face-supported and tail-free branches. The exact first-normal Ward equation does not extend homogeneously to second order: its cluster trace contributes there. Thus arbitrary higher partner normals, the positive completed physical change-of-frame metric, shared global source constraints, and geometric overlap remain separate problems. Audit: [literal generic source transformation and support checks](../experiments/audit_actual_all_partner_first_normal_bound.py) and [recorded results](../experiments/actual_all_partner_first_normal_bound_results.json). The analytic bounds follow from the proof; the finite checks supplement the source and incidence identities.

text: # The retained Newton sign and the actual local peripheral branch 30 October 2026. The actual alternating low-color Newton sum has a localized critical scheme whose eliminated quadratic is exactly the polynomial closure of the original untwisted primitive-collar trace relation. Its selected complete germ is fixed by the already proved collar flags and meridian convention. For positive face variables, however, every real critical Newton index lies OUTSIDE the physical terminating range. The identity does not make that branch a contribution to the original finite sum. This is a local marked algebraic comparison, valid at an actual original port with positive outer and middle face variables. It is independent of bridge width. It does not cover a marked zero-face degeneration, a retained half twist at this port, the discrete endpoint analysis, or a global low-color representation/period. The nearby actual geometric family is already constructed separately; no new global gluing theorem is inferred from this scalar relation. ## 1. Keep the literal Newton coefficient and its sign The [exact Newton source formula](actual_positive_newton_capacity_obstruction.md), section0, gives T_h=sum_(r=0)^(h-1) (-1)^(h-1+r) b_(h,r) Bhat_r(-T), b_(h,r)=S_r^2 S_(h+r)/[S_(2r+1)S_(h-r-1)], S_j=product_(k=1)^j 2sin(pi k/N). Use the original Newton variables alpha=h/N, rho=r/N, mu=m/N, xi=i/N, eta=j/N. The strict nonzero Newton polytope means rho<mu<1, 0<xi,eta<rho, xi+eta<mu, mu+rho-xi-eta<1. Its shared-face critical action contains K+B_alpha+pi i rho+mu Log(b/c) +xi Log(x/b)+eta Log(y/b), with the fixed pi i alpha character and the rest of the original source still retained. Differentiating in mu,xi,eta gives the first three equations of section2; differentiating in rho gives (2). The finite +1 shifts affect this rate by o(1) on fixed strict compacts. They are not removed from the finite source. Differentiating gives exp(partial_rho B_alpha) =sin(pi(alpha+rho)) sin(pi(alpha-rho))/cos(pi rho)^2 =[sin(pi alpha)^2-sin(pi rho)^2]/cos(pi rho)^2. (1) The exact sign (-1)^(h-1+r) contributes pi i rho to the leading rho action. Its pi i alpha part must ALSO remain in the complete marked action; it is simply independent of rho. With K the actual four-tetrahedron Newton entropy, its retained rho critical equation is sin(pi(mu+rho-xi-eta)) sin(pi(mu-rho)) ------------------------------------------------- * sin(pi(rho-xi)) sin(pi(rho-eta)) [sin(pi alpha)^2-sin(pi rho)^2]/cos(pi rho)^2 = -1. (2) All logarithms use a specified continuation from the positive physical domain before adding the retained pi i character. There is no real interior solution in that domain, since every factor there is positive. This is precisely why its positive capacity maximum cannot be used as an actual saddle. Put Z=exp(2pi i mu), A=exp(2pi i xi), B=exp(2pi i eta), W=exp(2pi i rho), and kappa=4cos(pi alpha)^2. The two rational factors in (2) become (ZW-AB)(Z-W)/[Z(W-A)(W-B)], (W-exp(2pi i alpha))(W-exp(-2pi i alpha))/(W+1)^2. After multiplying their RECORDED denominators and bringing the -1 across, the constant and degree-four terms cancel. Divide only by the exponential unit W. The result is the quadratic (Z-A)(Z-B)(W+1)^2 +kappa (W-Z)(ZW-AB)=0. (3) This identity follows by expansion and contains no asymptotic approximation. The physical source fixes which component, logarithm and contour could be relevant; (3) does not choose them. The parameter kappa has the form of a meridian trace square under the established color marking, but this calculation alone does not identify the remaining variables with actual holonomy coordinates. Equation (3) is valid only off the denominators cleared from (2), including W=A,B,-1 and the original sine factors. At alpha=1/2 the second factor in (1) is identically 1 after cancellation. Then the uncleared equation reduces to W (Z-A)(Z-B)=0. Since W is an exponential unit, it has no generic finite solution. Any treatment at that color must use the literal discrete endpoint/pole structure or an independently justified continuation. The coefficient's exact finite offsets and all other original phases remain essential. ## 2. The localized shared-face critical scheme Write the four positive face variables as x,b,c,y, retaining the source input b/output c convention from the Newton coefficient extraction. Let U=exp(2pi i alpha), kappa=(U+1)^2/U. Over the Laurent ring in U,Z,A,B,W and the four face variables, the UNSATURATED equations are b(Z-1)(ZW-AB)-c(Z-W)(Z-AB)=0, x(Z-AB)(W-A)-b(ZW-AB)(A-1)=0, y(Z-AB)(W-B)-b(ZW-AB)(B-1)=0, (Z-A)(Z-B)(W+1)^2+kappa(W-Z)(ZW-AB)=0. (4) The actual regular critical scheme is their localization by the following product of recorded nonzero factors. The saturation ideal defines its closure and has the same restriction on D_reg != 0: D_reg=xybc UZABW (Z-1)(Z-W)(Z-AB)(ZW-AB) (A-1)(B-1)(W-A)(W-B)(W-1)(W+1) (W-U)(W-U^-1). (5) These factors come from the strict sine-product arguments of the literal coefficient and its weight. Some cancel in particular formulas, but are not silently removed from the original regular chart. The choice of the continued logarithms is additional marked data, not encoded by this algebraic saturation alone. At endpoint arguments the unsaturated equations are merely a closure; they are not the actual critical scheme without a separate boundary analysis. The discriminant of the quadratic in W is exactly kappa {kappa(Z^2-AB)^2 -4(Z-A)(Z-B)(Z+1)(Z+AB)}. (6) At leading-coefficient or discriminant zeros it need not have two distinct finite branches. No branch or integration cycle follows from this discriminant. ## 3. Exact elimination using the three shared-face equations The first three equations admit the following direct reduction. Set t=b(ZW-AB)/(Z-AB), L=b+c+x+y, D=xy-bc, E=bc(x+y)+(b+c)xy, A0=x+y. On the regular chart (4) implies A=(xW+t)/(x+t), B=(yW+t)/(y+t), Z=(t-cW)/(t-c), Lt^2+(1+W)Dt-WE=0. These are units on the positive locus; they are not consequences of (5) on every complex component. Retain the full pullback of (5) under these substitutions. In particular t, W, t-c and t-cW stay nonzero; Z=0 is not an allowed solution. The first Newton sine ratio has the exact expression exp(K_rho)=-1+W(c+x)(c+y)/[(t-c)(t-cW)]. Its correctly signed remaining equation is kappa(t-c)(t-cW) +(c+x)(c+y)[(W+1)^2-kappa W]=0. (8) After substituting W, the resultant is the unit (c+x)(c+y) times (Lt^2+E)^2-kappa t(t+x)(t+y)(E-Dt)=0. (9) This is another compact polynomial closure. It is used only with the same pulled-back exclusions, not as an unconditional off-grid identity. Eliminating t instead and putting zeta=(W+1)^2/W gives the factor (c+x)^2(c+y)^2 W^2 times (L^2+kappa D)zeta^2 -kappa(2L A0+kappa xy)zeta+kappa^2 A0^2=0. For kappa nonzero, z=zeta/kappa satisfies (L^2+kappa D)z^2-(2L A0+kappa xy)z+A0^2=0, (10) with discriminant kappa[4A0 E+kappa x^2y^2]. Extra roots on excluded divisors are not restored by the calculation. There is an explicit reverse reconstruction on the recorded open chart. If Q1,Q2 denote the left sides of (7)'s last equation and (8), then L Q2-kappa Q1 =(c+x)(c+y)[-kappa(1+W)t+L(W+1)^2-kappa A0 W]. Consequently t=L(W+1)/kappa-A0 W/(W+1) =W(Lz-A0)/(W+1). This proves equivalence on that open chart, not on its polynomial closure. The extra L unit is explicit; it cannot be inferred from (5) on an arbitrary complex component. ## 4. The real critical indices lie outside the terminating sum Assume x,b,c,y>0 and 0<alpha<1/2, so 0<kappa<4. The leading coefficient L^2+kappa D is positive, the middle coefficient has positive magnitude, and the discriminant in (10) is positive. Hence its two roots are real, distinct and positive. For each of the two z roots, the two W roots are distinct, nonreal and on the unit circle. Also P(A0/L)=-kappa A0 E/L^2<0, so Lz-A0 is nonzero. Formula(10a) makes both t and t/W nonreal. It follows that x+t,y+t,t-c,t-cW and E-Dt are nonzero, as are A,B,Z from (7). Their differences A-1,B-1,W-A,W-B,Z-1,Z-W are nonzero multiples of W-1 or t(W-1). Every factor in (5) is therefore a unit. No extra positive-base branch is created by (10); all four are reconstructed by (10a). This does not choose the actual source logarithms or cycle. title: The endpoint channel Hessian is the inverse primitive cusp shape
text: # The endpoint channel Hessian is the inverse primitive cusp shape 30 October 2026. The actual normalized augmented-plat phase has a nondegenerate channel block at every regular complete geometric point. After eliminating its two local q-Hahn variables on their recorded critical sheets, ALL channel/magnetic mixed second derivatives vanish at the complete channel endpoint. The diagonal entries are exactly H_(xi_i,xi_i)=-4pi i/tau_i, (0) where tau_i is the ACTUAL oriented primitive crossing-circle cusp shape, longitude translation divided by meridian translation. Hence each entry has strictly negative real part. This is a source theorem for every original augmented plat admitting the stated regular complete geometric chart, at any fixed width, with any retained half-twist pattern. The proof identifies the cusp shape directly from the actual meridian and longitude MATRICES. It does not infer that marking by matching a Hessian. It also does not assert that the remaining magnetic Hessian is nondegenerate after removing framing directions, or that a finite source cycle contributes a nonzero Gaussian amplitude. ## 1. A local critical reduction must keep its integer characters Use the fully normalized local phase Theta_epsilon and its rational critical map from [the actual character calculation](actual_augmented_plat_local_critical_character_map.md). Write y for the magnetic variables (tau,u,v), xi for the folded channel, and alpha,beta for the two internal q-Hahn variables. The high physical degree chart uses its proved affine adapter; its phase remains the same function of these LOW coordinates, not the same function with the physical pair product substituted for T. At a regular complete point J=exp(2pi i xi)=-1, both internal critical quadratics have simple roots. The holomorphic implicit-function theorem gives their chosen continuations alpha(y,xi), beta(y,xi) in a small logarithmic neighborhood. The exponentiated equations alone give Theta_alpha=2pi i n_alpha, Theta_beta=2pi i n_beta, with locally constant integers on these roots. Retain these characters and put Theta_tilde=Theta-2pi i(n_alpha alpha+n_beta beta). Then its two internal derivatives are EXACTLY zero. Define the root-reduced phase Theta_bar(y,xi) by substituting these roots into Theta_tilde. Envelope differentiation now gives exp(partial_xi Theta_bar)=R_epsilon =R0(-J)^epsilon. (1) Reducing an unadjusted phase whose internal derivatives are nonzero integer characters would add spurious alpha_xi and beta_xi terms. No choice of these local characters is, by itself, a proof that the corresponding Poisson sector contributes to the original finite sum. ## 2. Endpoint tangential derivatives vanish identically The actual source identities hold on the ENTIRE endpoint root chart: R0|_(J=-1)=1, C=I+bH, H=P+I, H^2=0, (dR0/dJ)|_(J=-1)=2b. (2) The derivative in (2) follows the implicit internal roots, holding the magnetic variables fixed. In particular it is not a derivative taken with their exponential coordinates Z,W incorrectly frozen. The scalar b is recovered from the actual ordered input/output meridians by b=Tr([H,A_in] A_out)/32. The endpoint regulator note's [rational chart](actual_augmented_plat_endpoint_regulator.md), with Z=(a-1)/(a+1), W=(b0-1)/(b0+1), gives explicitly b=(2Ta b0-Ta-Tb0+a+b0-2) /[2(T+1)(a-1)(b0-1)]. (3) Here b0 is a chart parameter, not the transport coefficient b. Formula (3) holds in both physical degree charts. The audit differentiates the original general-J rational expression for R0 using Z_J=-P_J/P_Z and W_J=-P_J/P_W, and checks (2) exactly over Q(T,a,b0). Because (-J)^epsilon=1 at J=-1, equation (1) implies partial_xi Theta_bar(y,1/2)=2pi i n_xi (4) for one LOCALLY CONSTANT integer n_xi on each connected marked endpoint chart. It does not automatically imply that this derivative is zero. Nevertheless differentiating (4) in ANY magnetic tangent direction gives partial_y partial_xi Theta_bar=0. (5) This is an identity along the whole endpoint chart, not a numerical vanishing at the geometric point alone. Finally dJ/dxi=-2pi i there, so (1),(2) give partial_xi^2 Theta_bar =-2pi i(2b-epsilon) =-4pi i(b-epsilon/2). (6) The high-degree adapter is independent of xi. Therefore (5),(6) remain valid in the actual high physical coordinates. ## 3. The primitive cusp translations fix the factor and sign The collar is the original threading word [2,1,1,2], followed by the retained main half twist R^epsilon. The [proved endpoint reconstruction](actual_augmented_plat_endpoint_regulator.md), section 3, supplies its raw trace -2 auxiliary meridian C_aux,raw=-[I+(epsilon/2-b)H]. (7) Thus the actual trace +2 meridian is mu=I+(epsilon/2-b)H. The actual disk-framed preferred longitude is P=BA, with no meridian power inserted. Since P=-I+H, its centered trace +2 representative is lambda_centered=-P=I-H. (8) Changing a matrix by its central minus sign changes no projective translation. Conjugate their common parabolic fixed point to infinity. The nonzero nilpotent H then has form [[0,h],[0,0]], h!=0. Equations (7),(8) say that the actual translations are translation(mu)=(epsilon/2-b)h, translation(lambda)=-h. Both primitive paths retain their original collar orientations. Therefore tau_geom=translation(lambda)/translation(mu) =1/(b-epsilon/2). (9) This proves the inverse cusp relation DIRECTLY at the complete point; no nearby deformation theorem or guessed cusp potential is used. With the positive orientation I(mu,lambda)=1, Im tau_geom>0. Substituting (9) into (6) proves (0), including Re(-4pi i/tau_geom) =-4pi Im(tau_geom)/|tau_geom|^2<0. Subtract the recorded constants 2pi i n_i xi_i from F, and add the actual positive cosine-branch color coupling -2pi i sum_i (xi_i-1/2) chi_i. By (12) and continuity, the holomorphic implicit-function theorem solves all CHANNEL equations uniquely for xi=xi(y,chi), near the geometric point. This eliminates only those variables. It does not solve the remaining y equations. At the complete geometric point, partial xi_i/partial chi_j=-delta_ij tau_i/2. (14) The resulting channel-eliminated phase f(y,chi) obeys f_(chi_i,chi_j)=delta_ij pi i tau_i, f_(chi,y)=0, (15) at chi=0. The transfer convention writing f''=2pi i tau_packet therefore has tau_packet=tau_geom/2, as already required in the explicitly solved Conway sources. text: # The actual Casimir plat phase and its marked representation germ 30 October 2026. On a regular chart at a complete geometric point, the constrained critical scheme of the original augmented-plat phase is isomorphic to the actual marked representation germ modulo one diagonal framing scale. This includes local Artin test rings, rather than only complex points or tangent dimensions. The proof reconstructs shared wire momenta from the event-incidence equations and supplies an inverse which is regular at the parabolic channel endpoint. The phase is the actual normalized Casimir/q-Hahn phase. This is not an application of the older braid-cut scheme claim with its different boundary state. Every original cup, ordinary cap, the unrestricted marked cap after its permitted whole-source degree restriction, and both physical degree adapters occur below. No quantum source quotient or asymptotic selection is asserted. ## 1. Objects and the precise local statement Fix a literal augmented plat, its retained half twists epsilon_v, and its actual outside wires. Its event graph has a vertex for each cup, cap or two-input/two-output circle coupon, and one directed edge for each physical wire between successive events. Identity segments are included in that wire. Let B be its oriented incidence matrix, with +1 at an incoming half-edge and -1 at an outgoing half-edge. The leading degree constraints are B x=b, b_cup=-1, b_cap=1, b_coupon=0. (1) Each connected component has equally many cups and caps, by counting its incoming and outgoing half-edges, so its entries of b sum to zero. The graph can have arbitrary cycles and width. We state the representation quotient for a CONNECTED event graph. The incidence construction below works componentwise without that assumption. A disconnected projection is a split diagram; contracting the connected local crossing-circle boxes does not change that connectivity. Thus the connected case includes an essential nonsplit augmented-plat diagram. Choose one of the actual low/high degree adapters at each coupon and a regular complete geometric point as in [the generic magnetic chart](actual_augmented_plat_regular_geometric_phase_chart.md). Fix its affine logarithmic lift of (1), its simple internal q-Hahn roots, and all logarithmic characters. All displayed local-map denominators, prefix diagonals, main K+1, and the chosen total F charts are units. We work in the corresponding formal neighborhood over C. The internal roots are eliminated by the exact marked critical reduction in [the channel-Hessian theorem](actual_augmented_plat_channel_hessian.md), not by substituting roots into an unadjusted phase. For each auxiliary circle retain its longitude eigenvalue J_v near -1 and prescribe its physical meridian eigenvalue m_v near 1. The channel equation is the original one R_(epsilon_v)=m_v^(-2). (2) The complete fiber has m_v=1. Equivalently the positive cosine branch uses m_v=exp(-pi i chi_v) and adds 2 Log(m_v)(xi_v-1/2) to the phase, with J_v=exp(2pi i xi_v). Let Crit be the formal scheme given by magnetic criticality on ker B and (2), with the retained integer characters. Let Rep be the actual Morse/ crossing-disk representation germ with the same peripheral marking: main meridians have their exact unipotent eigenvalue +1, auxiliary meridians have selected eigenvalue m_v, and the raw ordered disk product has selected eigenvalue J_v. All the same regular chart conditions hold. The main flag means the kernel of mu-I, NOT an arbitrary invariant line of a trace-two Artin matrix. The auxiliary flag is the selected J_v eigenline of its noncentral disk product. Then there is an isomorphism of formal functors Crit = Rep / T_diag, (3) where T_diag acts by simultaneous projective diagonal conjugation. The quotient has a concrete local slice: set the momentum S on one chosen physical wire to 1. Every such S is a unit. No reductive-quotient existence theorem or reduction of a nonreduced ring is needed for (3). Sections 2--6 give mutually inverse constructions over every local Artin C-algebra with the specified residue point. ## 2. Incidence criticality reconstructs all wire momenta Use physical half-edge variables before imposing (1). At a low coupon take the following ambient extension of its root-reduced phase: s=x_in,1+x_in,2, u=x_out,1, v=x_in,1, f_v=Theta_bar(s,u,v,xi). The second output is recovered by degree conservation. Write D, Y_in, Y_out for the ACTUAL derivatives in the local character note. The four exponentiated half-edge derivatives of this extension are incoming: (D Y_in,D), outgoing: (Y_out,1). (4) For a high coupon use the actual affine function Theta_bar(2-s,u-s+1,v-s+1,xi). Formula (4) remains true with D_high=1/(D Y_out Y_in) and the physical high head coordinates. Thus there is no separate high-degree gauge assumption. Let p_(v,e) be the local derivative of the chosen ambient extension and c_e=exp(sum_(v incident e) p_(v,e)). Magnetic criticality means product_e c_e^(l_e)=1 for every l in ker_Z B. (5) The integer cycle lattice is the full kernel: an oriented graph incidence matrix is saturated. A direct construction is enough here. Choose a spanning tree and one vertex value t_v0=1. Solve along its edges c_e=t_tail(e)/t_head(e). (6) Every non-tree edge satisfies (6) precisely because its fundamental cycle satisfies (5). This constructs unit vertex values over ANY commutative test ring. They are unique up to one common unit per connected component; no extraction of roots is involved. Now define the momentum at each incident half-edge by S_(v,e)=t_v exp(B_(v,e) p_(v,e)). (7) Equation (6) says exactly that the two definitions of S on a wire agree. At a coupon (4),(7) give S_in=(t_v D Y_in,t_v D), S_out=(t_v/Y_out,t_v). (8) This is the original local kernel formula with g=t_v D. Conversely shared momenta satisfying that formula give (7), hence (6),(5). Choosing another ambient extension changes its derivatives by a local multiple of the degree row and merely changes t_v, leaving S unchanged. In additive logarithmic language, (5) is grad F=B^t lambda after keeping the fixed integral character, and t_v=exp(-lambda_v). On a formal Artin neighborhood the exponential is injective on nilpotents. Thus the exponentiated equations and the exactly marked critical equations have the same infinitesimal scheme, not just the same complex zero set. The spanning-tree construction also proves the asserted saturation and the absence of hidden finite scale choices. ## 3. The actual boundary maps have precisely the inverse-pair relation On their actual forced degree fibers, the leading cup, ordinary cap and marked cap phases are respectively pi i(x_1-1), pi i x_1, pi i x_2. (9) The marked restriction x_1+x_2=1 follows only after all other actual caps and degree-preserving coupons act; it is not a local replacement of an unrestricted mark in a degree-changing source. Apply (7) with B=-1 at a cup and B=+1 at a cap. The two momenta are (-t,t) for the cup and ordinary cap, and (t,-t) for the marked cap. All three therefore give X_1 X_2=1, S_1/S_2=-1. (10) For an actual physical head use K=-1/X, F=S(1-X), E=(X^(-1)-1)/S, Lminus=[[1,0],[-KF,K]], G=[[K,E],[FK,FE+K^(-1)]]. (11) It has determinant one and trace -2. Its exact -1 eigenline is spanned by (1,S). Since K+1 is a unit, this kernel line is unique over the Artin ring; no nilpotent invariant-flag freedom is silently added. Equation (10) is equivalent to the actual based pair product P=I. For the converse, K_total=1 gives X_2=X_1^(-1), while F_total=(1-X_1)(S_1+S_2)=0 forces S_1=-S_2 because 1-X_1 is a unit. These are identities over the test ring. The ordinary and marked phases differ on the degree fiber by pi i-2pi i x_1; this retained integral character has the same exponentiated relation (10), but must not be deleted from the action. ## 4. A regular parabolic inverse for each actual coupon The local critical map reconstructs actual ordered pair matrices from (X,S), preserves their ENTIRE product P, and fixes Tr P=J+J^(-1). Conversely, given regular incoming and outgoing heads with that product, their ratios S_in,1/S_in,2 and S_out,2/S_out,1 determine their internal q-Hahn roots by the rational inverse (5) of the local map. The Jacobi equation is the actual trace equation, so these roots satisfy the two internal critical equations. Total-F preservation gives the exact D and therefore (8); the regular high adapter gives the same conclusion in the other physical chamber. The chosen simple roots eliminate any additional local root choice in this formal neighborhood. At J=-1 one MUST NOT divide by J-J^(-1) in an Artin ring. Here is an explicit replacement for the local conjugator formula. Put Q=P-J^(-1)I, A=A_in, A'=A_out, c=Tr([Q,A](A'-A)) / Tr([Q,A](Q A-A' Q)), C=I+cQ. (12) At the complete point Q=H=P+I and A'=A+b[H,A]-4b^2H. The denominator in (12) is Tr([H,A]([H,A]-4bH))=32, (13) using Tr([H,A]^2)=32 and Tr([H,A]H)=0. It is a unit throughout the formal neighborhood. The original generic conjugator identity now extends in this regular expression and gives C A C^(-1)=A', [C,P]=0, det C=R0=1+c(J-J^(-1)). (14) For precision, these rational identities hold on the smooth localized internal-root chart before imposing the global critical equations; their specialization therefore holds on nonreduced Artin test rings as well. This is not cancellation by a nonunit in such a test ring. Specify the selected auxiliary eigenvalue m and let h_J=J^(-1)-1, which is a unit near J=-1. The actual physical auxiliary meridian is C_aux=m R0 h_J^(-epsilon) C^(-1)(P^(-1)-I)^epsilon. (15) It has selected J-flag eigenvalue exactly m and det C_aux=m^2 R0(-J)^epsilon=1 (16) by (2). All inverses in (12),(15) are units. At completeness (15) is I+(epsilon/2-b)(P+I), exactly the original primitive collar matrix. Its inverse followed by the retained Hurwitz half twist induces C on the main pair. Thus the auxiliary is the literal disk-framed meridian, not a centralizer chosen only from its eigenvalue ratio. Conversely an actual auxiliary meridian with that eigenvalue commutes with P. Its inverse, composed with the retained half twist, transports the pair. Normalize this projective conjugator to have eigenvalue one on the J^(-1) flag. This divides by a unit even at the endpoint, because the commutant of the noncentral P is the free span of I,P. The normalized matrix is (12), and its eigenratio gives (2). The normalization and the conjugator are unique: at the complete pair a matrix commuting with P=-I+H has form aI+bH; commuting also with A forces b=0 since [H,A] has a unit entry. The same unit linear minor proves this assertion in the whole formal neighborhood. ## 5. Assemble the actual marked representation, and invert it From a critical point, section 2 supplies shared physical heads (11). At every horizontal slice prefix-transport them by their actual lower triangular matrices. The local coupon preserves P, and each cup/cap has P=I, so prefixes outside the event remain unchanged. Physical wires therefore carry the same based meridian at both ends. At each circle, (15) satisfies exactly the original threading relation [2,1,1,2] and the retained main Hurwitz move. These are the literal van Kampen relations of the drilled box; inverse-pair caps close the outside plat. They construct a representation of the actual marked augmented link. For the reverse construction start with that representation and its recorded Morse basepaths. If H_1,...,H_m are the raw trace -2 main meridians at a slice, let P_i=H_i ... H_1, P_0=I and use Bminus(P)=[[1,0],[-P_21,P_11]], G_i=Bminus(P_(i-1)) H_i Bminus(P_(i-1))^(-1), K_i=(P_i)_11/(P_(i-1))_11, X_i=-1/K_i, S_i=(G_i)_21/(K_i+1). (17) All denominators are units by the same regular chart. This is the explicit inverse of the actual prefix factorization. It remains valid over the Artin ring. The selected channel eigenvalue fixes the actual trace equation and its unique regular eigenline; the rational inverse from section 4 recovers the internal roots. The local maps then recover (8),(10), and section 2 gives magnetic criticality. No root is chosen by an order, norm, or independent semiclassical convention. Both constructions are inverse before quotienting, except for the one common scale in (6). Multiplying all momenta by t conjugates every matrix by diag(1,t) projectively: upper entries divide by t and lower entries multiply by t. The prefix construction respects that same conjugation. Setting one wire momentum to 1 removes exactly this freedom and proves (3) over all local Artin test rings. ## 6. Consequences and limits of the statement On the complete fiber m=1, (2) fixes J=-1 locally, scheme-theoretically. Indeed R_epsilon-1 vanishes identically on J=-1 and its J derivative there is 2b-epsilon=2/tau_geom, a unit at the actual complete cusp. The formal implicit-function theorem therefore gives J+1=0. This uses the primitive cusp normalization of the channel-Hessian theorem, not a semisimple endpoint quotient. At an irreducible geometric representation, changing the common projective frame supplies the PGL2 orbit; the diagonal scale above has already been quotiented. With the convention rho_g=g rho g^(-1), that scale acts on g by LEFT multiplication. Its two-dimensional local T_diag\PGL2 framing directions therefore remain in the critical scheme. Equation (3) identifies all its additional infinitesimal directions with actual marked representation deformations. This source equivalence alone does not exclude those additional deformations. The following corollary uses a separately checked geometric input. ## 7. With an actual positive certificate, the magnetic radical is exactly framing Assume additionally an ACTUAL marked positive complete ideal gluing certificate for this augmented exterior. The [multi-cusp marked rigidity theorem](../papers/marked-fillings/README.md) identifies its decorated representation germ modulo PGL2 with a smooth germ whose coordinates are the primitive peripheral eigenvalue logs. It proves this identification on Artin rings, with the exact main eigenvalue conditions used above. Fix all main eigenvalues to +1 and fix the auxiliary eigenvalues m. The unframed germ is then a point. The complete geometric representation is irreducible, so its framed germ is a smooth PGL2 orbit. Equation (3) and its explicit one-scale slice therefore prove Crit at fixed m is smooth of dimension two. (18) This assertion holds formally over nearby auxiliary eigenvalue parameters as well. The dimension comes from the actual T_diag\PGL2 framing quotient, not from deleting two presumed redundant equations or counting variables and equations. At completeness write F for the root-reduced phase after its affine degree restriction, in free magnetic coordinates y and channels xi. The scheme Crit is the zero scheme of its EXACTLY marked derivatives. Consequently its Zariski tangent space is the kernel of Hess F, even before any reducedness assertion. Equation (18) now proves that this kernel is precisely the two-dimensional framing tangent space. The independently proved channel calculation gives Hess F = [[F_yy,0],[0,diag(-4pi i/tau_geom,i)]]. (19) The channel diagonal is invertible. Hence the two framing directions are purely magnetic, and ker F_yy = tangent(T_diag\PGL2), dim ker F_yy=2. (20) There are no further magnetic infinitesimal null directions on this regular positive geometric germ. A local slice transverse to these actual frame directions has a nondegenerate holomorphic quadratic form. This supplies a classical normal form; it is not a computation of an actual source density, a finite quantum gauge factor, or a Gaussian coefficient on the physical summation cycle. ### A nearby classical stationary branch and its absolute action There is now also a holomorphic CLASSICAL stationary branch. Choose a local slice transverse to the two framing directions and keep the geometric sheet's integer Poisson characters fixed. The marked geometric implicit-function theorem solves the representation uniquely on that slice for m_i=exp(-pi i chi_i) near 1. The inverse in (17), the regular internal-root maps, and the fixed local logarithms reconstruct all the actual principal-phase variables holomorphically. Equation (3) proves that these variables satisfy every exactly marked stationary equation. This proves existence; it is no longer an assumption about an unspecified classical critical branch. Its critical value phi(chi) is independent of the transverse framing slice. Along the connected local framing orbit all internal derivatives vanish, so the value of the same marked phase is constant. This statement does not reset any additive period or change an integer mark. The auxiliary-color normalization can be checked directly in the [exact entire core](actual_augmented_plat_entire_core_color_packet.md). Its full-algebra identity centers (-1)^h T_h into cos[pi(N-2j-1)chi]. On the positive cosine branch the order-N coupling is EXACTLY pi i(1-2xi)chi. The finite -1 contributes exp(-pi i chi) to the amplitude, not a new term in the principal phase. The actual main cups/caps, kappa^epsilon factors and original exterior line have no auxiliary chi dependence in this packet. Their known leading constant phases are retained. In particular there is no additional order-N exterior color character to discard or calibrate by the volume. Envelope differentiation and the proved literal peripheral marking give partial_i phi=pi i(1-2xi_i), U_i=-2pi i chi_i, V_i=4pi i(xi_i-1/2), d(2pi i phi)=(1/2) sum_i V_i dU_i. (21) Here U,V are the centered projective meridian and preferred-longitude logs. The negative cosine sign requires the simultaneous reciprocal eigenflag convention stated in the local character note; it gives the same primitive differential with those consistently marked logs. An independently changed exterior color character would change the corresponding linear action/log mark and is not covered by silently reusing (21). The [absolute endpoint regulator comparison](actual_augmented_plat_endpoint_regulator.md) now applies to the complete point of this FULL stationary branch and fixes its value: 2pi Re phi(0)=Vol(Y_D). (22) Finally (21) and dV_i=tau_geom,i dU_i at completeness, or equivalently the channel elimination calculation, give phi_(chi_i,chi_j)(0)=delta_ij pi i tau_geom,i. (23) Thus the general transfer's parameter is tau_packet=tau_geom/2. These are statements about the actual marked PRINCIPAL action on its geometric sheet. They do not prove continuation from the locally lattice-selected q-Hahn roots, a nonzero finite-source cycle coefficient, or a uniform quantum packet with this action. The branch is called geometric here, not source-selected. ## 8. Scope This is a formal classical equivalence. It neither quotients the finite quantum coupon algebra nor replaces its co-source. It does not locate the point in a physical support chamber, continue the source-selected local branches to it, choose its Poisson coefficient, compute a nonzero amplitude, or bound any competing source. title: The actual augmented-plat endpoint action has its diagram regulator
text: # The actual augmented-plat endpoint action has its diagram regulator 30 October 2026. At the complete channel endpoint, the fully normalized q-Hahn coupon phase has the SAME Bloch–Wigner regulator as its original crossing-circle diagram, for every retained half twist. This is an absolute comparison: an exact rational wedge calculation gives a constant regulator difference, and a connected real chart proves that constant is zero. It is not an inference from matching peripheral derivatives. Consequently any regular, correctly marked geometric critical point of the assembled endpoint phase has critical rate equal to the volume of the actual augmented link. Existence of such a point on the source's required logarithmic sheet, a contributing cycle, and a nonzero controlled amplitude are separate questions. This note does not prove a source asymptotic. ## 1. The complete normalized endpoint symbol Use the original phase Theta_epsilon from [the local character calculation](actual_augmented_plat_local_critical_character_map.md), equation (1), with its inverse-measure factor H, both q-Hahn columns, and the retained half twist epsilon in {0,+1,-1}. Write T=exp(2pi i tau), U=exp(2pi i u), V=exp(2pi i v), Z=exp(2pi i alpha), W=exp(2pi i beta). At xi=1/2, J=exp(2pi i xi)=-1 and J0(1/2)=0. Adding H to the two column factorial actions cancels the terms J0(tau-1/2). The remaining factorial part is J0(u)+J0(tau-u)+J0(v)+J0(tau-v) -2[J0(alpha)+J0(1/2-alpha)+J0(beta)+J0(1/2-beta)] -J0(u-alpha)-J0(tau-u-1/2+alpha) -J0(v-beta)-J0(tau-v-1/2+beta). (1) The retained polynomial phase is pi i [(u+v)/2+(tau-1/2)(alpha+beta) +tau+3(epsilon-1)/4]. (2) On the original factorial branch, 2pi i J0(s)=-Li2(exp(2pi i s)) +pi^2(s^2-s)+Li2(1). (3) One verifies (3) by differentiation from 0<s<1 and the common value at s=0, then analytically continues with the recorded logarithmic marks. Thus the Bloch symbol of 2pi i Theta_epsilon is B_H=B(U,Z)+B(V,W), B(X,z)=-[X]-[T/X]+2[z]+2[-1/z]+[X/z]+[-Tz/X]. (4) The half-twist term in (2) contributes a REAL constant to 2pi i Theta, so it contributes no regulator. It does still change the actual auxiliary meridian needed to realize the same main-input/main-output relation. Neither that change nor the coefficient 2 in (4) may be discarded. ## 2. A rational chart for the endpoint critical correspondence Both actual internal q-Hahn equations at J=-1 are rationally parameterized by Z=(a-1)/(a+1), U=T(a-1)^2/(Ta^2+1), W=(b-1)/(b+1), V=T(b-1)^2/(Tb^2+1). (5) Indeed a=(1+Z)/(1-Z), and direct substitution gives the quadratic P(U,Z)=0 of the local character calculation; the same holds for V,W. Every regular endpoint root is represented by this chart away from the listed denominators. The chart has coordinates (T,a,b) in a nonempty Zariski-open subset of C^3. A common nonzero magnetic scale can be fixed at one: it simultaneously conjugates the head matrices and does not change any crossing symbol below. For clarity all reconstructions use the actual physical head matrices K=-1/X, F=S(1-X), E=(X^-1-1)/S, Lminus=[[1,0],[-KF,K]], G=[[K,E],[FK,FE+K^-1]]. (6) Put Y(X,z)=-(1-X)(Tz+X)/[(X-z)(T-X)], D=ZW(T-U)(T-V)/[(TZ+U)(TW+V)]. (7) In the low physical degree chart the input heads (X,S) are (V,Y(V,W)), (T/V,1), and the output heads are (U,1/[D Y(U,Z)]), (T/U,1/D). (8) Let A=G1, B=Lminus1^-1 G2 Lminus1, P=BA, H=P+I. Then H is nonzero nilpotent and the endpoint transport is C=I+cH, c=(2Tab-Ta-Tb+a+b-2) /[2(T+1)(a-1)(b-1)]. (9) This follows either by multiplying the explicit matrices or by c=Tr([H,A]A_out)/32. In particular C A C^-1=A_out. The full ordered product P, including its Borel frame, is preserved. For the HIGH physical degree chart one must use the actual affine index adapter, rather than substitute the physical pair product into (4). Its input and output heads are respectively (V/T,Y(V,W)), (1/V,1), (U/T,D Y(V,W)), (1/U,D Y(U,Z)Y(V,W)). (10) The low variables in (4),(5),(7) remain unchanged. The exact finite high-block identification has no extra phase or scalar. Formula (6) with (10), followed by c=Tr([H,A]A_out)/32, gives exactly the same coefficient (9) in the high physical chart. The executable certificate checks it independently with the same original crossing rule below. ## 3. Reconstruct the actual auxiliary meridian and every crossing The positive Hurwitz half twist on a trace -2 pair is simultaneous conjugation by P^-1-I. At P=-I+H its projective normalization is I+H/2. Therefore the raw, trace -2 auxiliary meridian for the original coupon R^epsilon L_N is C_aux,raw=-[I+(epsilon/2-c)H]. (11) This sign is its actual complete raw lift; the corresponding physical meridian has trace +2. The literal threading word [2,1,1,2] transports the main pair by C_aux^-1 and closes the auxiliary because it commutes with P. Composing its main half twist gives total conjugator I+cH. This uses the [proved original peripheral word](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_mixed_crossing_circle_preferred_longitude.md), not an assigned auxiliary longitude. To recover the actual THIRD Gauss head from (11), let L=Lminus2 Lminus1 and set G3=L C_aux,raw L^-1. Its coordinates are K3=(G3)11, E3=(G3)12, F3=(G3)21/K3. (12) Now execute chronological adjacent crossings [2,1,1,2], and then the signed main crossing R^epsilon if epsilon is nonzero. All maps here are rational. For two input heads (k,e,f),(l,g,h), the original positive crossing, with d=1-eh, is (ld, [dg+e(dl-l^-1)]/k, kh/d), (k/d, e/(ld), l[df+h(d/k-k)]). (13) With physical clocks A0=-1/k, B0=-1/l its five-dilog symbol is [B0]+[1/d]+[1/A0]-[B0/d]-[1/(dA0)]. (14) The original negative crossing has c0=1-(B0/A0)gf and outputs (lc0, kg, f+h/k-f/(l^2c0)), (k/c0, le+g-k^2g/c0, f/l), (15) with symbol [A0]+[c0]+[1/B0]-[A0c0]-[c0/B0]. (16) Call the sum of these FOUR or FIVE actual symbols B_disk,epsilon. Direct rational substitution checks all nine final Gauss coordinates: the first two heads are exactly (8) or (10), and the auxiliary head is exactly (12) again. Thus this is the actual original closed circle, not an abstract centralizer with a missing closing/pivot convention. The closing pivot is a monomial; its complete leading contribution and the main marked cup/cap phases are included in (2) and the global source characters. They contribute no extra dilogarithm symbol. A monomial can still change an action value off stationarity; section 5 treats that point explicitly. ## 4. Exact wedge identity and absolute real normalization With delta[z]=z wedge (1-z), the following identity holds over the rational function field Q(T,a,b), for BOTH physical degree charts and all epsilon in {0,+1,-1}: delta(B_H-B_disk,epsilon)=0. (17) Here is a finite algebraic certificate for (17), including its procedure so no fitted regulator or floating point identity is involved. Use (5) in (4); construct B_disk by (6)--(16); factor every argument and its complement into irreducible polynomials over Q. For an argument z write v_z for its integer exponent vector, retaining positive rational prime factors as well as polynomial factors. Then expand sum_(coefficient n, argument z) n (v_z v_(1-z)^t-v_(1-z) v_z^t). (18) The matrices from (4) and (14),(16) are identical. Then BOTH sides expand to 2 T wedge (T+1) +sum_(r=a,b) [ A_r wedge T - A_r wedge F_r +2 A_r wedge (r-1) + B_r wedge F_r -2 B_r wedge (r-1) + F_r wedge r +2 r wedge (r-1) ]. (18a) There are exactly fifteen nonzero coefficients in this polynomial-factor basis. In particular the mixed factors involving both a and b from the actual four-crossing diagram cancel; this is a global identity for the whole coupon, not equality of independent crossing maxima. For any Bloch symbol B the differential of its Bloch–Wigner regulator factors through delta B: dD(z)=log|z| dArg(1-z)-log|1-z| dArg z. Therefore (17) makes D(B_H-B_disk,epsilon) constant on its regular complex parameter chart. This chart is connected: it is obtained from C^3 by deleting finitely many proper polynomial hypersurfaces, and two generic points can be joined by complex lines avoiding their finitely many excluded intersection points. title: An exact analytic function of the auxiliary colors
text: # An exact analytic function of the auxiliary colors Fix an augmented plat diagram: a braid closed by specified cups and caps, with an auxiliary crossing circle around each retained twist region. At quantum level \(N\), the color \(n_i\in\{1,\ldots,N\}\) labels the representation on the \(i\)th auxiliary circle. The complete color is \(N\), and its deficit is \(h_i=N-n_i\). This note constructs a particular entire function of the scaled deficits. It is a finite cosine sum whose coefficients are contractions of the original quantum operators. At physical high colors it gives exactly the complete-circle part of the invariant. The remaining terms are also specified by an exact identity. This construction is needed before complex stationary phase: an arbitrary interpolation of the integer color values would not preserve the quantum expression being estimated. The finite formula works for every fixed augmented plat and both parities of \(N\). It gives exact Fourier reconstruction and a positive squared-norm identity. Those identities alone do not prove cancellation bounds or a nonzero geometric contribution. Such additional estimates are now established for the [strict Conway class](../papers/conway-asymptotics/README.md) and other stated families; this note does not assert them for every plat. ## 1. Splitting one circle operator without losing derivatives Let \(\Omega\) be the original Casimir operator on the pair of physical strands. Write \(T_n,U_n\) for the Chebyshev polynomials of the first and second kinds, normalized by \(T_0=1\), \(T_1(t)=t\), \(U_0=1\), and \(U_1(t)=2t\). The color-\(n\) circle operator is \[ L_n=(-1)^{n-1}U_{n-1}(\Omega/2),\qquad L_0=0. \] At level \(N\), the full pair algebra satisfies \[ P_N(\Omega)=2T_N(\Omega/2)+2=0. \] This polynomial relation includes repeated spectral nodes. Working in its quotient retains the first derivatives at those nodes, which the source notes call first normals. Merely recording the distinct eigenvalues would discard that information. For every integer \(0\le h<N\), the exact circle identity is \[ L_{N-h}=(-1)^hT_h(\Omega/2)L_N+(-1)^NL_h. \tag{1} \] Indeed, the Chebyshev identity \(U_{N-h-1}=T_hU_{N-1}-T_NU_{h-1}\), together with \(T_N=-1\) in the full quotient, gives (1). The first summand is called the core term and the second the alias term. These are names for the two terms of an operator identity; neither name implies an asymptotic estimate. Put \(M=\lfloor(N-1)/2\rfloor\). The distinct spectral nodes are \(c_j=2\cos((2j+1)\pi/N)\), for \(0\le j\le M\). Let \(L_{N,j}\) be the actual component of \(L_N\) at node \(c_j\), in every physical degree. The [complete compiler](actual_augmented_plat_phase_compiler.md) specifies these rank-one matrices and their derivative-derived coefficients. On the image of each component, multiplication by \(T_h(\Omega/2)\) acts by its value at \(c_j\): its derivative multiplies the complete-circle square-zero term and vanishes. Therefore \[ \begin{aligned} (-1)^hT_h(\Omega/2)L_N &=\sum_{j=0}^{M}\cos(\pi h m_j/N)L_{N,j},\\ m_j&=N-2j-1. \end{aligned} \tag{2} \] The centering in (2) uses that \(h\) is an integer. The frequencies \(m_j\) are distinct, nonnegative, and all have parity \(N-1\). At an odd level, \(m_M=0\), so the last cosine equals one. No division by a vanishing endpoint sine is involved. ## 2. Defining the whole finite function Fix the original augmented \(2k\)-plat skeleton and its \(b\) retained auxiliary circles. The number \(k\) records the plat width; \(b\) counts the color variables. At circle \(i\), retain the prescribed half twist \(R_i^{\epsilon_i}\), where \(\epsilon_i\in\{0,\pm1\}\), followed by the circle operator \(L_{N-h_i}\). For a tuple \(\mathbf j=(j_1,\ldots,j_b)\), define \(A_N(\mathbf j)\) as follows: replace the \(i\)th circle operator by \(L_{N,j_i}\), retain \(R_i^{\epsilon_i}\), and perform the original marked contraction. Thus \(A_N\) includes the original cups, ordinary caps, unrestricted marked cap, pivotal factors and external scalar. It is a definite finite coefficient, not an unspecified boundary vector or normalization. For \(\chi=(\chi_1,\ldots,\chi_b)\in\mathbb C^b\), set \[ C_N(\chi)= \sum_{j_1=0}^{M}\cdots\sum_{j_b=0}^{M} A_N(j_1,\ldots,j_b) \prod_{i=1}^{b}\cos(\pi m_{j_i}\chi_i). \tag{3} \] This is entire and even in each variable because the sum is finite. For a physical high-color tuple, \(0\le h_i\le M\), equation (2) shows that \(C_N(h/N)\) is exactly the contraction in which every circle uses its core term. At \(h=0\), every alias is \(L_0=0\), so \(C_N(0)\) is the full original complete-color scalar. Let \(Z_N(h)\) denote the full marked scalar at those physical colors. Expanding (1) at all circles gives \[ Z_N(h)=C_N(h/N) +\sum_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,b\}} (-1)^{N|S|}Z_{N,S}(h). \tag{4} \] Here \(Z_{N,S}\) uses \(R_i^{\epsilon_i}L_{h_i}\) at every circle in \(S\), and the complete-image cosine factor of (2) at every other circle. The [all-color Hermite compiler](actual_mixed_augmented_plat_compiler.md) specifies each contraction, including the normal terms. Equation (4) retains all nonempty alias subsets; it does not say that they are smaller. For a physical low color \(n\le\lfloor N/2\rfloor\), the usual physical decomposition instead sets its core to zero and takes the full ordinary coupon as its alias. Formula (3) still has values at the corresponding grid points, but they belong to its finite Fourier extension. They are not a redefinition of the physical low-color core. This distinction becomes important when estimating the color complement. ## 3. Recovering the coefficients and their squared norm Define a frequency weight by \(w_j=1/2\) when \(m_j>0\), and \(w_j=1\) when \(m_j=0\). Direct summation gives the exact orthogonality relation \[ \frac1N\sum_{h=0}^{N-1} \cos(\pi h m_j/N)\cos(\pi h m_l/N)=w_j\delta_{jl}. \tag{5} \] To check it, expand the product into exponentials. The differences \(m_j-m_l\) are even integers of absolute value less than \(2N\). The sums \(m_j+m_l\) are also even; their only multiple of \(2N\) in this range is zero, occurring at the odd zero-frequency node. These observations give exactly the two weights above. No assumption that \(N\) is prime is used. Applying (5) in each variable recovers the original contraction coefficients: \[ A_N(\mathbf j)= \frac{1}{N^b\prod_{i=1}^{b}w_{j_i}} \sum_{h_1=0}^{N-1}\cdots\sum_{h_b=0}^{N-1} C_N(h/N)\prod_{i=1}^{b}\cos(\pi h_i m_{j_i}/N). \tag{6} \] The corresponding Parseval identity is \[ \frac1{N^b}\sum_{h_1=0}^{N-1}\cdots\sum_{h_b=0}^{N-1}|C_N(h/N)|^2 =\sum_{j_1=0}^{M}\cdots\sum_{j_b=0}^{M} \left(\prod_{i=1}^{b}w_{j_i}\right)|A_N(\mathbf j)|^2. \tag{7} \] For fixed \(b\), the transform costs only a power of \(N\). However, (7) measures squared magnitudes. It does not make the signed sum \(C_N(0)=\sum_{\mathbf j}A_N(\mathbf j)\) positive or prove that its geometric contribution is nonzero. ### The opposite endpoint and the limits of periodicity Let \(e_i\) be the \(i\)th coordinate vector. Since all frequencies have the same parity, the finite function obeys \[ \begin{aligned} C_N(\chi+e_i)&=(-1)^{N-1}C_N(\chi),\\ C_N(\chi_1,\ldots,-\chi_i,\ldots,\chi_b) &=C_N(\chi_1,\ldots,\chi_i,\ldots,\chi_b). \end{aligned} \tag{8} \] Thus it is periodic at odd levels and antiperiodic at even levels. Values near the grid endpoint \(h_i=N\) reflect values near \(h_i=0\). There is a conditional consequence for a proposed global estimate of this extension. Suppose a fixed-neighborhood analytic asymptotic has complete rate \(F_0\) and an amplitude that is not identically zero near the origin. Choose arbitrarily small fixed positive real arguments where the amplitude is nonzero. Nearby grid values have rates arbitrarily close to \(F_0\), and (8) reflects them outside the near-zero neighborhood. Hence this Fourier extension cannot have a fixed exponential gap on the whole complementary cube. If the amplitude is nonzero at zero itself, the sample \(h=1\) already has the complete rate and reflects to \(h=N-1\). That particular moving-sample argument needs nonvanishing at zero, not merely a nonzero analytic function nearby. Periodicity by itself does not give this obstruction. In one variable, the exact reproducing kernel is \[ \sum_{j=0}^{M}w_j^{-1}\cos(\pi m_j\chi) =\sum_{r=0}^{N-1}e^{\pi i(N-1-2r)\chi} =\frac{\sin(N\pi\chi)}{\sin(\pi\chi)}. \tag{8a} \] At \(\chi=h/N\), for \(0\le h<N\), its value is \(N\delta_{h,0}\) at both parities. Multiplying by \(e^{NF_0}/N\) gives complete rate \(F_0\) and zero at every other sample. This example has no fixed-scale analytic neighborhood of the required asymptotic form. It explains why the additional hypothesis, and the physical distinction after (4), must be retained. Finally, the elementary inequality \(|\cos z|\le e^{|\operatorname{Im}z|}\) gives \[ |C_N(\chi)|\le e^{\pi(N-1)\sum_i|\operatorname{Im}\chi_i|} \sum_{\mathbf j}|A_N(\mathbf j)|. \tag{9} \] This exact estimate has a linear cost in complex height. The quadratic height control needed for a filling saddle is a stronger analytical statement. ## 4. What this finite construction supplies Formula (3) specifies a regular continuation even at the odd zero-frequency endpoint. Within its stated cosine span it is uniquely determined by the grid values. It does not replace a generic-quantum-parameter germ of the whole pointed invariant. For a general fixed plat, using this function in a filling proof still requires a uniform asymptotic on a fixed complex neighborhood, a selected contribution on the original integration cycle, bounds for all physical alias terms and far colors, and the actual marked geometric regulator. The complete and mixed compilers expose those quantities but do not themselves estimate them. The twist threshold is attached to the fixed diagram; the frequency scale \(N\) remains the quantum level. The [finite check](../experiments/audit_actual_augmented_plat_entire_core_color_packet.py) tests the full-algebra split, the centered characters, the tensor Fourier identities and the reproducing-kernel example. Its recorded cases include 162 signed split identities, 204 centered characters and 27 tensor Fourier packets. The proofs above, rather than the number of cases, establish the general identities and their stated limitations.

text: # The actual marked framing density from Casimir-source Ward currents 30 October 2026. local source theorem. This concerns the leading LOCAL density of the actual complete-color augmented-plat source after transverse Gaussian elimination. It retains the original mark, all finite offsets and the actual magnetic top-form. The invariant ordered-flag form alone is not its density: the marked cut supplies a meromorphic factor. No coefficient of this local density in the original global period is asserted. ## 1. Exact white Ward identities on the specified complex-head source Write Q=zeta^2, d=N-1, m=d-a, B=Q^(-N), and use the actual LARGE polynomial H=H_m^B(U,V) of the [generic white-source theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_generic_boundary_gauge_and_source.md). With A0=Q^d=1/(BQ), it satisfies the two exact identities (1-U)H(U/Q,V)+U(1-V)H(U,V/Q) =(1-UV Q^(-m))H(U,V), (1) A0(U-A0)H(QU,V)+U(V-A0)H(U,QV) =(Q^m UV-A0^2)H(U,V). (2) They are polynomial identities in independent complex U,V and generic Q,B, before root specialization. Put P_j(X)=product_(r=0)^(j-1)(X-Q^r), N_b=V^b P_b(U)P_(m-b)(V), H=sum_(b=0)^m c_b N_b. Each N_b individually satisfies (1), by canceling the endpoint factors in P_j(X/Q). With M_b=V^b P_b(U)P_(m-1-b)(V), direct factor cancellation gives L N_b=-UV { Q^b(A0-Q^(m-b-1))(Q^(m-b)-1) M_b +A0(A0-Q^(b-1))(Q^b-1) M_(b-1) }. (3) The out-of-range endpoint terms have their displayed zero coefficient. The ACTUAL finite coefficients obey c_(b+1)/c_b =-B Q^(b+1)(1-Q^(m-b))(1-BQ^(m-b)) /[(1-Q^(b+1))(1-BQ^(b+1))]. (4) Substituting A0=1/(BQ) into (3) makes the coefficient of each M_b zero by (4). This proves (2) and its endpoints, with every generic coefficient retained. To check the source convention, the actual white is W_a(i,j;r)=(-1)^m zeta^[-dr+di-m(m-1)] H(Q^i,Q^j)/F_m, i+j=m+r. The original coproduct F equation is (1-Q^i)W(i-1,j;r-1) +zeta^(-d)Q^i(1-Q^j)W(i,j-1;r-1) =(1-Q^r)W(i,j;r), which is (1). The original Ecal equation gives (2) after multiplying by UV and its fixed monomial. No small/large root collision is used. The K equation is the literal affine degree constraint. The specified cups and inverse caps obey their exact unit-step Ward equations by the moving-factorial recurrence, with the highest weight fixed. For example p_L(x)/p_L(x-1) is -zeta^(L-2x)(1-Q^x)/(1-Q^(L-x+1)). (5) This makes the two terms in Delta(F)p_L cancel identically. Reversing the literal cap and using the same recurrence proves its dual equation. These identities are meromorphic; neither an endpoint pole nor its normal is deleted. The actual signed circle factors, fixed label weights and generic scalar adapters are independent of magnetic heads. ## 2. The actual half-index symbols, and their first transport This section uses the PHYSICAL semiclassical parameter h=Log Q=2pi i/N, not the distinct generic epsilon derivative at one fixed root. Set A=Q^(u+1/2), q=Log A, and for a fixed highest-weight-L head put M_L=zeta^(L+1). The row action of its original balanced generators is K=M_L/A, F=(1-A/zeta)T_-, Ecal=(M_L^(-1)-M_L zeta^(-1)/A)T_+, T_+ f(q)=f(q+h), T_- f(q)=f(q-h). (6) In the Weyl convention Op_W[a(q) exp(sp)]f(q)=a(q+sh/2)f(q+sh), their EXACT symbols are K=M_L/A, F=(1-A)exp(-p), Ecal=(M_L^(-1)-M_L/A)exp(p). (7) Thus there is no order-h subprincipal term in these symbols. At a complete physical head M_L=-1. Different-head products in the original coproduct have the same property. A right matrix action uses the transposed shift; direct substitution gives the same symbol with p reversed. This retains the input/output operator ordering. All half-index shifts and the exact parameters M_L=exp[h(L+1)/2] are kept in the action and amplitude. In particular L/(2N) and (L+1)/(2N) are not identified near the fold. At each finite N, change the already proved selected packet to the half-index variables exactly. Reexpanding it retains the order-one exponential from the shift of its action, as well as the amplitude and coordinate Jacobian. The fixed-derivative estimates for that packet justify this operation; one does not replace it by its limiting phase before making the change. The finite affine offsets and their characters are exactly those already retained in the [complete local marked-density theorem](actual_augmented_plat_local_marked_density.md). The total K equation is an affine head constraint, so a trivalent tensor is initially supported on that constraint rather than an ordinary function of three unconstrained positions. Before the next calculation, take a primitive linear Fourier transform in one constrained head. Equivalently eliminate the same primitive affine equation with its full coarea half-density. The retained mixed position/momentum coordinates then give an ordinary local generating family. The Fourier normalization is kept as a base scalar and its Jacobian is kept in the density. This step does not apply an ordinary WKB formula to a delta-supported tensor or discard the K constraint. The first transport implication can be proved directly. Suppose P_h=sum_v a_v(q,h)T^v has Weyl symbol H(q,p)+O(h^2), and P_h[exp(S/h)(b+O(h))]=0 on a regular local Lagrangian chart.
