Expanding the actual shifted amplitude to first order gives, on H(q,S_q)=0, V dot partial_q b+(1/2)div_q(V)b=0, V=partial_p H(q,S_q). (8) Indeed each term contributes a_v exp(v dot S_q) v dot partial b; its remaining first correction is half the derivative of that same coefficient along v, including v^t S_qq v. Their sum is precisely half the displayed divergence. This is transport of the genuine Lagrangian half-density, rather than invariance of S alone. Primitive linear Fourier/constraint coordinates carry the same formula, by the ordinary Gaussian change of variables with its Jacobian retained. There is a useful normalization check. On the Hom correspondence P_out=P_in=P=[k,e;kf,*], the three principal constraint fields are X_K=(k/2)A_h, X_E=k A_f, X_F=A_e-(f/2)A_h, (9) where A_xi is actual simultaneous conjugation. In invariant group volume their divergences are 0,-e,f. Since X_E Log k=-e and X_F Log k=f, (8) gives k^(-1/2) times invariant half-density, not bare invariant half-density. Turning the input into an outgoing leg by the ACTUAL channel cup removes this adapter. For completeness, in the half-index coordinate u=(r+1/2)/N and lambda=(L+1)/N, the root cup is exp(pi i r) q0^(-r) G_N(r)G_N(L-r)/G_N(L). The uniform interior sine-factorial expansion makes each numerator G_N(Nu-1/2)=sqrt(N)exp[N J(u)](1+O(N^-1)). Therefore its variable amplitude is exp(-pi i u), namely sqrt(K) times a fixed-color scalar. The exact denominator G_N(L), also near the folded endpoint, stays in that scalar. This checks the required modular half-density factor without dropping an endpoint normalization. Equivalently the all-output vertex (W tensor I)p_(2a) is annihilated by its original total K-1,Ecal,F. On P_total=I, their fields are A_h/2,A_f,A_e, so its leading half-density is invariant. Ordinary caps have the dual property. This supplies a local check of the assembly below; it is not an assumption that every scalar kernel is a graph with nonzero mixed input/output Hessian. The latter would be false for the rank-one complete-circle kernel. ## 3. Actual scalar currents for an arbitrary fixed plat Keep the original Morse word, all complete-circle sectors, its cups, caps and the original exposed physical cut. Expand each sector as the literal W/pi network, or use its proved scalar-one exceptional packet with its restoring character. Equations (1)--(5) give its actual intertwiner identities in the independent complex heads. The retained cyclic turns and categorical duals use their original order. The exceptional numerator and its restored integer characters obey the same unit-step identities: an integer-affine exp(2pi i head) character is unchanged by every such shift. Compose the original Hopf-adjoint insertions through this network. There is an explicit finite scalar-current construction. Move each inserted K,Ecal,F through the next vertex using the displayed local identity; pair the two insertions on each contracted wire with its actual cup or cap. Keep every resulting multiplication coefficient. For a shifted factor c and an insertion j the reindexing is exactly j T^v c-(T^(-v)j)c =(T^v-I)[(T^(-v)j)c]. (10) Thus each unmatched internal term is a specified integral difference current, with its insertion shifted in the OPPOSITE direction. Use the original saturated affine head lattice to express these translations in a primitive free basis. The local degree equations ensure that the matched current has zero remaining constraint defect. No independent edge maximization or cyclic wrapping is involved. Ordinary pivotal contractions cancel the matched Hopf insertions. The only cut terms are the literal dual rows of the original mark, computed in the next section. This is the same finite Green-product construction as in the [ordered Gaussian-current calculation](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/residual_gaussian_ward_currents.md), but here its local inputs are the independent-head Casimir identities (1),(2), not a braid mixed-Hessian model. The construction is an algorithm on the actual word and works at every fixed width and both level parities. It retains finite endpoint currents on an original finite domain. In the local regular meromorphic chart it is the corresponding interior current identity; no claim identifying that completion with the whole cyclotomic source is needed below. The principal vector of a local insertion is obtained by differentiating its ACTUAL symbol with respect to p: expansion of a shifted amplitude gives sum_v h_v exp(v dot p)v. Equations (7)--(9) therefore identify the local variations as the actual conjugation fields on its trivalent correspondence. Their propagation through the original shared heads agrees with the explicit incidence/momentum inverse of the [critical-scheme theorem](actual_augmented_plat_critical_scheme.md). On the regular complete geometric germ they are tangent to that exact critical scheme. The two cut-compensated combinations below are its two actual framing fields. This uses the source critical-scheme inverse, not merely constancy of the critical action. ## 4. The actual marked co-source, including its sign Use the original balanced cut e_ab=1/N. The one-cut array is diagonal term by term after the other actual caps, by total-degree conservation. For Phi(C)=Tr(eC), the exact dual Hopf rows are e_K=K^(-1)eK-e, e_E=K^(-1)e Ecal-Ecal K^(-1)e, e_F=eF-KF e K^(-1). (11) At complete color, with A=Q^a in the original integer-index convention, their diagonals are (e_K)_aa=0, (e_E)_aa=q0(1-Q)A/N, (e_F)_aa=(1-Q)A/N. (12) These follow by two neighboring matrix entries, with the actual zero end arrows retained. The original scalar summand already contains 1/N. Consequently the boundary coefficients for W1=2(ad_K-I)+2ad_Ecal, W2=ad_F+ad_Ecal are b1=2q0(1-Q)A and b2=(1+q0)(1-Q)A. Both satisfy b_i/h -> -2 A. (13) The half-index replacement changes A only by 1+O(h), so not this leading co-source. This is a ROOT physical semiclassical statement; it does not identify any generic epsilon-normal of a bare marked row. Normalize the cut momentum to one as in the actual critical-scheme slice, and use F(r,s)=[[r,1-r],[s,-s]], mu=F^(-1)[[1,1],[0,1]]F, A_cut=(1+s)^(-1). The two actual fields, with the same conjugation convention, are xi1=-2(1-r)partial_r+2s partial_s, xi2=(2r-1)partial_r+2s partial_s. (14) Their determinant is -2s, a unit on this chart. Their difference is partial_r. The exact residual difference current has boundary row (1-q0)(1-Q)A/N, so its divided leading co-source is zero. The ordinary-cap comparison also exposes the marked insertion directly. At the exposed pair, with SECOND physical index x, its exact mark/cap ratio is N^(-1)q0^(-d^2)Q^(d x). Since d=N-1, Q^(d x)=exp(2pi i x) exp(-2pi i x/N). (15) The first factor is the retained integer character. On complementary integer indices a+x=d, the second is Q times the first integer clock Q^a (or its corresponding fixed half-index scalar). Up to that retained fixed-color scalar its leading factor is A_cut. Thus the marked source has a genuine A_cut insertion, not a constant Haar normalization. Equation (12) computes its differential covariance from the actual source. ## 5. Gaussian elimination transports the divergence and its Jacobian Use the selected ordinary packets and the joint deficient packet at the proved regular geometric frame. The complete marked-density theorem gives their nonzero relative product amplitude with its original magnetic top-form. The positive-certificate critical scheme gives exactly two magnetic null directions; all transverse magnetic Hessians are units. Keep two actual free magnetic coordinates chi which are etale on this framing orbit, and call the remaining coordinates u. One chi can be chosen to include the actual cut head. Keep every original finite offset, Poisson character and constant phase in this same branch. Contract only u by its local geometric Gaussian. This defines the leading two-form Omega_src: its coefficient is the actual product amplitude divided by the marked square root of det(-F_uu), with the full chi/u Jacobian and original magnetic top-form retained. The new local packet theorem makes this form NONZERO. This construction does not choose a component of the original global integration cycle. For clarity, the effect on a current can be checked without an invariance guess. A term j(chi,u,h)T_chi^gamma T_u^beta in the exact current has Gaussian image obtained by replacing its insertion by E_(chi+h gamma)[T_u^(-beta)j] and then shifting the external Gaussian block by h gamma. The insertion is translated oppositely, exactly as in (10). This is the substitution u_new=u+h beta with the local critical point recentered. Equivalently one proves the required leading identity by Gaussian integration by parts. Normal total currents have zero formal Gaussian integral; an external current has leading coefficient xi_i^chi times the Gaussian density. Its external divergence differentiates that WHOLE density, including the inverse Hessian determinant and coordinate Jacobian. No separately averaged product of insertions is substituted. The source packets are holomorphic on a common smaller chart with relative O(h) errors and fixed-derivative bounds. These justify the first transport expansion of the actual continued factors; unknown higher amplitude coefficients cancel from the leading current because its principal characteristic vanishes. A local descending normal Gaussian cycle gives the same leading computation. Its small outer boundary is exponentially below the critical value. None of these local operations moves the original finite-head cycle across a source divisor. Combining this calculation, the actual principal fields (14) and the explicit boundary rows (13) gives Lie_(xi_i) Omega_src-2 A_cut Omega_src=0, i=1,2. (16) This is the missing subprincipal transport statement. It was obtained from (1)--(13) and the original product amplitude, not inferred from invariance of the stationary action or from the old braid determinant. ## 6. The resulting orbit form and its scope Put Omega_cut=-dr wedge ds/[s(1+s)]. (17) Direct differentiation gives Lie_(xi_i)Omega_cut=2 A_cut Omega_cut. Divide (16) by this nonzero form. Both independent vector fields kill the ratio, so on a connected geometric framing chart Omega_src=c_D Omega_cut, c_D!=0, (18) where c_D is independent of the framing point. It retains the original source's base-only normalization, phases, parity convention and chosen Gaussian square roots. The theorem does not choose or erase these data. The local channel Gaussian multiplies c_D by its nonzero cusp-shape factor, since the cusp shapes and its marked Hessian are frame-invariant. Thus the actual local folded sum at either parity has the same orbit form, with its own retained nonzero constant. In the ordered-flag convention Pi=g^(-1)E11 g, with image v and kernel w, let Omega=dv wedge dw/(v-w)^2. For g=F^(-1), Pi=[[r,r(1-r)/s],[s,1-r]], w=(r-1)/s, 1/(v-w)=s, Omega=dr wedge ds/s. Consequently the ACTUAL marked answer is Omega_src=-c_D A_cut Omega. (19) The insertion at 1+s=0, the omitted s=0 chart, and all source-chart divisors remain. No nonconstant additional local factor survives the two proved Ward equations, but this says nothing about residues at the excluded boundaries or contributions from other WKB sectors. In particular, formal Gaussian current transport is not an invertible map on all fixed-root carry sectors: at h=2pi i/N the Bernoulli adapter for exp(hD)-1 vanishes on a literal A^N character. These source sectors, normal directions and original cotangent weights are not removed by (18). The selected global framing period, its boundary/current map, and its coefficient in the original finite cycle remain separate. There is a concrete residual-fiber consequence. Since A_cut=(1+s)^(-1), the same proved density is Omega_src=(c_D/s) dr wedge dLog A_cut. (20) Relative to the displayed base form dLog A_cut, its differential on a fixed affine framing fiber is c_D dr/s=c_D d(r/s). It is exact. Thus a specified first-cut localization in A_cut, with its actual base coefficient retained, does not by itself produce a nonzero closed period of this residual leading form. Its contribution requires the original relative boundary/current coefficient or other retained source weight. Equation (20) neither chooses a centralizer section nor discards the original cotangent, character or divisor terms. ## 7. Finite source checks The [focused exact audit](../experiments/audit_actual_augmented_plat_framing_density_source_ward.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_augmented_plat_framing_density_source_ward_results.json) check 14 termwise F identities, 14 E telescopes and 10 adjacent coefficient cancellations; 300 original H four-jet identities with 1,200 retained coefficients; 570 actual cup four-jet ratios; and 308 truncated complete cut-row diagonals. Symbolic checks also retain the exact Weyl half-steps, root cup phase, three modular divergences, two cut-field covariances, flag Jacobian and marked finite clock offset. A variable Gaussian and a coordinate change separately check the transverse determinant derivative and full top-form Jacobian. The general finite-current construction and its Gaussian transport are proved analytically in §§3--5, not inferred from these checks. The conclusion is the local framing form (18)–(19). Its global cycle coefficient and boundary currents remain unproved; no global period statement follows.

title: The actual local source phase generates ordered character transport
text: # The actual local source phase generates ordered character transport 30 October 2026. The explicit augmented-plat phase has a direct algebraic map to the original ordered pair character. This note proves that map, including the full factorial normalization, its centralizer transport, and its regular parabolic limit on the longitude cover. It is a local critical-phase theorem, not a claimed full-source asymptotic or a new choice of quantum invariant. The remaining global issues are stated in section 6. In particular the local calculation does not assign the source action an absolute manifold regulator merely because its critical equations have the right character. Subsequent comparison: the [regular geometric chart](actual_augmented_plat_regular_geometric_phase_chart.md) supplies an unfolded complete geometric candidate, and the [endpoint regulator theorem](actual_augmented_plat_endpoint_regulator.md) fixes its absolute volume anchor under full marked stationarity. Those additional results do not supply the physical cycle or global source estimate left open in this local note. ## 1. Retain the complete normalized coupon phase Use the low physical degree chamber of the [actual compiler](actual_augmented_plat_phase_compiler.md). Let tau be the scaled pair degree, u and v its output and input first magnetic indices, xi the folded Casimir index, and alpha,beta the two internal q-Hahn variables. Set J0(s)=integral_0^s Log(2 sin(pi w)) dw, B(s,r)=J0(s)-J0(r)-J0(s-r), E(tau,xi,u,alpha)=B(xi,alpha)+B(u,alpha) +B(tau-u,xi-alpha)-B(tau,xi), Phi(tau,xi,u,alpha)=E(tau,xi,u,alpha) +pi i [u-xi u+(tau+xi-1)alpha], H(tau,xi)=2J0(tau)-J0(tau-xi)-J0(tau+xi-1). All logarithms have the compiler's actual factorial marks. The complete coupon, with retained half twist epsilon in {0,+1,-1}, has leading phase Theta_epsilon=H+Phi(tau,xi,u,alpha)+Phi(tau,xi,v,beta) +pi i[tau+(epsilon-1)(xi+xi^2)]. (1) Its already recorded external kappa^epsilon is not removed or replaced; its leading constant is a unit phase and has no derivative in these variables. The finite offsets and normal-derived coefficients remain those of the exact compiler. Equation (1) is their leading phase, not an equality of finite quantum germs. Write T=e^(2pi i tau), U=e^(2pi i u), V=e^(2pi i v), J=e^(2pi i xi), Z=e^(2pi i alpha), W=e^(2pi i beta). On a regular logarithmic chart the two internal equations are exactly P(U,Z)=0, P(V,W)=0, P(X,Y)=T(J-Y)^2(X-Y)+(Y-1)^2(TY-XJ). (2) Every formula below is localized only where its displayed denominators are nonzero. In particular these equations have not licensed deleting boundary strata. Their leading quadratic coefficients may be assumed nonzero for the symbolic certificate; the rational identities themselves hold wherever their displayed denominators are defined. ## 2. The actual Casimir equation, with its magnetic momentum Direct differentiation of Phi gives Y(X,Z)=e^(Phi_u)=(1-X)(TZ-XJ)/[J(X-Z)(T-X)]. (3) The principal symbol of the original symmetric Jacobi block is a(X)= (X-T)(1-X)/T, d(X)=2X(1+T-X)/T, Omega_cl=a(X)(y+y^-1)+d(X). These follow directly from the physical tridiagonal entries, with q->1 and q^(N-1)->-1. Equation (2) implies a(X)[Y(X,Z)+Y(X,Z)^-1]+d(X)=J+J^-1. (4) This is an exact rational identity modulo P. For example its difference from the right side equals -X(J-T)P(X,Z)/[JT(X-Z)(JX-TZ)]. Thus the critical phase yields the actual ordered pair trace, not just an independently chosen quadratic with the same number of roots. The inverse change is explicit: Z=XJ[y(T-X)+(1-X)]/[yJ(T-X)+T(1-X)]. (5) On its regular chart, the Jacobi equation (4) conversely implies (2). The local root is therefore selected by the actual magnetic momentum y; one does not choose a root by its numerical size. ## 3. Full normalization preserves the ordered product Differentiating ALL terms of (1), including H and pi i tau, gives D=e^(Theta_tau) =JZW(T-J)(T-U)(T-V)/[(TJ-1)(TZ-UJ)(TW-VJ)]. (6) Omitting the inverse-measure factorials or their phase would change (6). Introduce an arbitrary nonzero common magnetic scale g. The actual incoming and outgoing raising-shift symbols are (S1_in,S2_in)=(g Y(V,W),g), (S1_out,S2_out)=(g/[D Y(U,Z)],g/D). (7) The signs in (7) follow from a kernel: right multiplication by a raising shift differentiates its input positively, and left multiplication differentiates its output negatively. Total-degree conservation supplies the common scale g. No Hermitian conjugation has been inserted. For a physical head define its original classical flag matrices by K=-1/X, F=S(1-X), E=(X^-1-1)/S, Lplus=[[K,E],[0,1]], Lminus=[[1,0],[-KF,K]], G=Lminus^-1 Lplus=[[K,E],[FK,FE+K^-1]]. (8) They have determinant one and trace -2. Prefix conjugation gives the ordered meridians A=G1 and B=Lminus1^-1 G2 Lminus1, exactly as in the proved quantum character identity. Their product is P=B A=[[T^-1,E_tot],[F_tot/T,F_tot E_tot+T]], F_tot=F1+K1^-1 F2, E_tot=E1 K2+E2. (9) Equations (2),(3),(6),(7) give F_tot,out=F_tot,in, K_tot,out=K_tot,in=T^-1, Tr P_in=Tr P_out=J+J^-1. (10) For F_tot nonzero, (9) then gives E_tot,out=E_tot,in as well. Hence the ENTIRE ordered matrix P is preserved. This is stronger than trace matching. The identity continues wherever the full rational expressions are defined; the present proof uses the stated regular F_tot chart. For reproducibility set g=1 and write f=(1-V)Y(V,W)+T-V. The first equality in (10) is the following explicit certificate: [(1-U)/Y(U,Z)+T-U]-D f = VZ(J-T)(T-U)P(V,W) /[(V-W)(JT-1)(JU-TZ)(JV-TW)]. (11) The scale g merely conjugates the common matrices and costs no source normalization. The HIGH-degree chamber has an equally literal adapter. If s is the physical pair degree divided by N, put tau=2-s, u=a-s+1, v=c-s+1, where a,c are its physical output/input first indices. These are the leading versions of the exact compiler's d=N-1 index translation; the finite offsets remain in its amplitude. The physical exponentials are (U/T,U^-1) at the output and (V/T,V^-1) at the input. Chain-rule differentiation of the SAME phase gives Y_out,high=Y(U,Z), Y_in,high=Y(V,W), D_high=1/[D Y(U,Z)Y(V,W)]. (11a) Use (7) with D_high and these PHYSICAL head exponentials. This is the actual Chevalley-and-flip map (X,S)->(X^-1,-S^-1) on both low heads, with the common scale consistently transported. It exchanges the total F and E and inverts total K. Therefore the whole high ordered product is preserved as well. There is no independent high frame gauge or differentiation of a root-only identity involved. The high coupon has the SAME channel derivative (12), and the four centralizer identities (14) are also checked symbolically in these physical high coordinates. Thus the local principal map covers BOTH original degree chambers, while retaining their separate integer lifts. ## 4. The channel derivative is a centralizer eigenratio Let R0=e^(partial_xi Theta_0). Direct differentiation yields R0=ZW(J-1)^4(TZ-UJ)(TW-VJ) /[JUV(J-Z)^2(J-W)^2(T-J)(TJ-1)]. (12) For J!=+/-1 define the matrix C=I+(R0-1)/(J-J^-1) (P-J^-1 I). (13) Its eigenvalues on the P-eigenlines J and J^-1 are R0 and 1, respectively, so det C=R0 and C commutes with P. Moreover A_out=C A_in C^-1, B_out=C B_in C^-1. (14) These are exact rational identities on (2). An entirely polynomial certificate is obtained by putting Ctilde=(J-R0/J)I+(R0-1)P. Clear only its displayed denominators in Ctilde A_in-A_out Ctilde. Every one of the four resulting entries has zero remainder modulo the two explicit quadratics P(U,Z),P(V,W). The accompanying executable certificate performs this calculation over Q(T,U,V,J), not at sampled roots or numerical shapes. Equations (8),(9) supply all matrices used. The second identity of (14) follows from the first and preservation of P. Thus R0 is the eigenratio of a genuine ordered-pair conjugator. It is not merely a scalar Casimir value. To compare with determinant-one peripheral lifts one must retain the selected square root of R0. For the retained half twist, the FULL derivative is e^(partial_xi Theta_epsilon)=R0(-J)^epsilon. (15) The physical conjugator in (14) is independent of epsilon at fixed magnetic/channel variables. Equation (15) removes the explicit half twist from its peripheral marking. Indeed positive original Hurwitz transport is (A,B)->(A^-1 B A,A); with P=BA it is simultaneous conjugation by P^-1-I, whose eigenratio is -J^-1. Therefore internal stationarity in the pure spectral phase, R0(-J)^epsilon=1, gives exactly that recorded signed Hurwitz factor. It would be incorrect to call R0 itself the unchanged auxiliary meridian for every epsilon. For the entire core's cosine branch exp[+pi i N(1-2xi)chi], the additional xi derivative is -2pi i chi. Hence its channel equation is R0(-J)^epsilon=e^(2pi i chi). (16) The opposite Fourier branch inverts the right side. The external color deficit chi is distinct from the internal channel xi. The primitive collar is fixed by the original threading word, not by centralization alone. Apply the positive Hurwitz rule chronologically at [2,1,1,2] to the three meridians (A,B,C_aux), and put K=P^-1 C_aux P. The exact three outputs are (K^-1 A K, K^-1 B K, K). Closing the auxiliary sets K=C_aux. Thus the pure physical transport is conjugation by C_aux^-1. The actual zero-self-linking disk longitude is P=BA, with no meridian factor, as proved in the [literal mixed-loop marking](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_mixed_crossing_circle_preferred_longitude.md), sections 4--5. Its argument uses the two underpasses and the absence of an auxiliary self-crossing; it is independent of plat width. On the chosen P eigenflag J=-ell, the primitive auxiliary meridian has eigenvalue M_aux. Hence the pure transport eigenratio is M_aux^-2. The retained main half twist adds the already computed factor (-J)^(-epsilon) to the physical transport and adds no auxiliary longitude detour. Consequently the exact marked relation is R0(-J)^epsilon=M_aux^-2=e^(-U_aux), M_aux=-q^(N-h) -> e^(-pi i chi), U_aux=-2pi i chi. (16a) This calibrates (16) and the primitive collar in the original source convention. Opposite eigenflag choices are retained by the Fourier sign, rather than replacing the projective multiplier by an unmarked square root. ## 5. The endpoint retains additive transport, rather than losing it At the geometric endpoint J=-1, both quadratics (2) have simple roots on any chart where their discriminants are nonzero. Equation (12) obeys R0=1 (17) identically modulo those two endpoint quadratics. Thus complete internal channel stationarity is automatic EXPONENTIALLY; a Poisson/logarithmic sheet is still to be recorded. It does not force C to be identity. Continue the two chosen roots analytically with J. The quotient in (13) has a removable singularity and C=I+b(P+I), b=(1/2) dR0/dJ at J=-1. (18) The derivative in (18) is along the chosen roots of (2), not a derivative with Z,W incorrectly frozen. The matrix H=P+I is nonzero and H^2=0 at an essential complete crossing disk. For common-trace parabolic A,B, Tr(H A)=4. Consequently the same coefficient is recoverable without any limit by b=Tr([H,A_in] A_out)/32. (19) To verify (19), C A C^-1=A+b[H,A]-4b^2 H, while Tr([H,A]^2)=32 and Tr([H,A]H)=0. The positive-certificate disk has distinct puncture flags, so this is its regular additive centralizer, not the central matrix P=-I. On the selected longitude cover set J=-ell=-exp(V_long/2). Then d_(V_long) log R0 at completeness=-b, log[R0(-J)^epsilon]=log R0+epsilon V_long/2. (20) With the calibrated auxiliary source convention R=e^(-U_aux), (20) is precisely the centered shear U_epsilon=U_0-epsilon V_long/2. The factor of two and inverse eigenratio convention are both retained. ## 6. The peripheral differential on a selected stationary branch There is a useful conditional consequence for the FULL assembled core phase, rather than just one local coupon. Choose one of the two original cosine signs sigma_i in {+1,-1} at each auxiliary region. Its added leading phase is exactly sum_i sigma_i pi i (1-2xi_i) chi_i. (22) The finite -1 in m_j=N-2j-1 changes the amplitude, not (22). Assume there is a holomorphic stationary branch of the assembled phase in all its internal variables on a specified logarithmic/Poisson sheet. This is a hypothesis here, not inferred from the local character equations. Call its critical action phi(chi), retaining the original source phases and fixed internal Poisson characters. Envelope differentiation gives partial_i phi=sigma_i pi i(1-2xi_i). (23) On the marked longitude branch centered at xi_i=1/2 put V_i=sigma_i 2 Log(-J_i) =sigma_i 4pi i(xi_i-1/2), U_i=-2pi i chi_i. These are equalities on the specified CENTERED logarithmic sheet. An integer change of a xi lift, or an additional recorded exterior color character, changes the corresponding linear term of phi and the marked peripheral logs together. Such terms must be kept; (24) is not a rule for resetting them to zero. Then (23) proves, without an unidentified proportionality constant, V_i=-2 partial_i phi, d(2pi i phi)=(1/2) sum_i V_i dU_i. (24) The local channel equations are R_epsilon,i=e^(sigma_i 2pi i chi_i). The actual collar comparison above identifies its selected multiplier with R_epsilon,i^(-sigma_i)=e^(U_i), while the selected longitude multiplier is J_i^(2sigma_i)=e^(V_i). An inverse choice of collar orientation or eigenflag must be changed explicitly on BOTH sides. Consequently the primitive differential is forced by the original Fourier-color coupling ON ANY such correctly marked stationary branch. It is not evidence that the branch exists globally, contributes to the finite source, or has the required complex estimate. Moreover (24) does not determine the additive value phi(0). Even after the marked representation comparison, its complete-volume anchor still needs an actual fundamental-chain or absolute period proof. ## 7. What can be sewn, and what is still missing The original cup has exact affine degree a+b=N-1 and phase x^(a-d); the ordinary cap has phase x^a, and the original marked cap has phase x^b after the allowed WHOLE-SOURCE degree restriction. Their principal equations all give X1 X2=1, S1/S2=-1, P=I. (25) This is the actual inverse-meridian cap relation. It does not identify the ordinary and marked amplitudes or discard their different normals. Their leading phases pi i u and pi i(1-u) have derivatives differing by an integral 2pi i character. Exponentiation hides precisely that original marked Poisson/logarithmic datum; it must remain in the global action and cannot be recovered from P=I alone. Shared physical wires identify the same X and S symbols, so (10),(14), and (25) are source-compatible local character equations at every width. Conversely, on a regular magnetic Borel chart an ordered parabolic pair with its actual P determines X,S, hence Y; equation (5) reconstructs its internal q-Hahn root. The full normalization (6) then reconstructs the outgoing scale. In this sense the local map covers the regular ordered-pair centralizer relation, including its parabolic limit. A global marked representation must still be compared with its source degree-chamber choices and integer carries, and the original logarithmic/ Poisson sheets. The local primitive collar is fixed above; the rational map alone does not prove that every positive complete gluing certificate lands in one physical source chart or has the required global lift. Nor does it supply existence of a nearby marked deformation merely from a complete point. Most importantly, the local generating phase and its correct character relation do NOT fix its absolute Bloch/regulator class. Section 6 proves the primitive differential on a correctly marked stationary branch; its existence and its actual degree-one complete-volume anchor remain necessary. Matching a character variety cannot fix an additive action constant or a different period class. No absolute comparison, cycle selection, nonzero amplitude, or global source gap is asserted here. The advance is the explicit local source-to-character generating map, with its full normalization and additive parabolic transport preserved. It is a reusable algebraic input to those remaining comparisons. Audit: [exact rational identities and parabolic normal checks](../experiments/audit_actual_augmented_plat_local_critical_character_map.py). The local character map retains the stated global-branch, logarithmic-mark, absolute-period and source-estimate limitations.

title: The complete source has a nonzero local marked density and folded Gaussian
status: Nonzero complete local marked density and folded Gaussian
text: # The complete source has a nonzero local marked density and folded Gaussian 30 October 2026. Fix a certified augmented plat, its original exposed mark, and the complete geometric chart with one exceptional matching edge. The proved ordinary and joint deficient packets give a nonzero LOCAL density of the actual complete root source. The paired-circle normal is already in this statement. Its folded channel sum has a nonzero local Gaussian coefficient at BOTH level parities. This is separate from the coefficient of a geometric saddle in the original global period. The two framing directions, the physical support cycles, crossed divisors and competing sectors remain. It is also a complete-color statement, not a mixed auxiliary-color or filling packet. ## 1. Start with the actual mark, rather than differentiating one coupon Write d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), x=q^d, M=floor(d/2), and let R be the fixed number of original complete-circle coupons. In a low physical degree t, the EXACT fixed-channel coefficient of the circle is C_(N,a)^epsilon(t;u,v) =kappa^epsilon x^(-t) nu_a^(epsilon-1) h_(t,a) f_a(t,u) f_a(t,v), h_(t,a)=k_a s_t^2/[s_(t-a)s_(t+a-d)], nu_a=(-1)^a q^[a(a+1)], k_a=1 if 2a=d, and k_a=2 otherwise. (1) Use the literal translated high block when needed. Equation (1) is the [complete root compiler](actual_augmented_plat_phase_compiler.md), including the full first-normal circle coefficient; it is not a value-only spectral projector. In particular the original scalar and its endpoint values are h0_a=k_a N s_(2a)/s_a^2, h0_M=N (N odd), h0_M=2N/sin(pi/N) (N even). (2) The latter formula follows from s_(N-2)=N/[2sin(pi/N)] and s_(N/2-1)^2=N/2. The vanishing paired retraction pi_a W_a=0 does NOT make (1) zero. The original nilpotent circle is h0_a W_a pi_a, whose displayed scalar already contains that circle's normal. In a 2k-head plat, keep all k original bottom cups, k-1 ordinary top caps, and the unrestricted original marked top row. Degree conservation forces the last pair to have degree d only AFTER the other caps act. Their product then has scale N^k N^(-(k-1)) N^-2=N^-1, (3) and an explicitly retained nonzero monomial in x. Thus the marked ROOT compiler is a finite sum of products of (1) and this monomial. It contains no further local q derivative. This direct use of the original mark is essential: nonzero E_a at one block would not by itself evaluate F_Delta'(0)/nu_N, the alternative whole-network ordinary-trace normal. That identity is proved only after the complete original closure. We do not differentiate one factor, assign a normal to each vertex, or move the bare mark. ## 2. The full normalization gives N^-1 per circle at the fold Put tau=t/N, alpha=a/N, eta=tau+alpha-1, zeta=tau-alpha. First work on a fixed ordinary physical compact, with alpha in a fixed real interval ending at 1/2. The finite source keeps its actual alpha. The original sine-factorial continuation G_N, on its marked strip, gives hhat_(t,a)=k_a G_N(N tau)^2/ [G_N(N zeta) G_N(N eta+1)]. (4) This is (1) on its supported physical grid. The endpoint +1 comes from d=N-1. The elementary uniform expansion G_N(Nw)=sqrt(2N sin(pi w)) exp[N J(w)](1+O(N^-1)) and the exact sine recurrence at N eta+1 give hhat_(t,a)=k_a b_h(tau,alpha) exp[N H(tau,alpha)] (1+O(N^-1)), H=2J(tau)-J(zeta)-J(eta), b_h=sin(pi tau)/[2sin(pi eta) sqrt(sin(pi zeta)sin(pi eta))]. (5) All sine factors here are units on the compact; their branches are the actual continued ones. In particular b_h remains nonzero and smooth at alpha=1/2. The large even value in (2) has canceled against the actual CD/column normalization. It is not an extra N in the coupon density. The [full ordinary packet](actual_q_hahn_full_physical_complex_packet.md) satisfies fhat_a=N^-1/2 B_alpha exp(N Phi_alpha)(1+O(N^-1)), where B_alpha is nowhere zero, uniformly through alpha=1/2. Hence (1) has the actual relative packet C_(N,a)^epsilon =kappa^epsilon k_a N^-1 b_epsilon exp[N Theta_epsilon^lit](1+O(N^-1)), Theta_epsilon^lit=H+Phi_alpha(tau,u/N)+Phi_alpha(tau,v/N) +pi i[-tau+(epsilon-1)(alpha+alpha^2)], b_epsilon=b_h B_alpha(tau,u/N) B_alpha(tau,v/N) exp[pi i(tau+(epsilon-1)alpha)]. (6) The exact kappa and retained outside framing line remain outside this formula. The -tau in (6) uses literal x^-t=q^-dt; the alternative +tau differs by the recorded degree character exp(-2pi i t). No character is discarded when comparing (6) to the marked stationary action. Every factor of b_epsilon is nonzero. Errors and fixed derivatives are uniform on smaller compacts, with smooth dependence on real alpha. The exceptional circle has the SAME assertion. Indeed its correctly restored [entire coefficient](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_matching_edge_deficient_packet_regulator.md) is exactly C_a(t;r,s)=k_a beta_a^2 V_a(d-t) q^[d(r+s-t)] R_a(q^(t-2r);c_t) R_a(q^(t-2s);c_t). Its scalar-one reflection sends (t,r,s) to (N-t-2,r+N-t-1,s+N-t-1). At negative determinant arguments the reflected values lie in the ordinary physical packet (6). The [joint deficient theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_q_hahn_joint_deficient_degree_packet.md) then supplies a nowhere-zero relative packet for each ratio R_a(z)/R_a(z_*), uniformly for the actual real alpha through the fold. The remaining ratio is the EXACT nonzero monomial q^[d(r+s-r_*-s_*)]. Multiplying these ratios propagates (6)'s absolute N^-1 scale and nonzero amplitude to the actual exceptional geometric compact. Different bounded marked logarithmic lifts retain their exact monomials; no root of a squared character is chosen afresh. This argument includes both beta factors, the residual sine product, the finite reflection offset -2, and the original fold weight k_a. There is no assertion that the individually large beta factors have a smooth nonzero endpoint asymptotic before that cancellation. The [literal generic lift](actual_matching_edge_generic_deficient_operator_lift.md) has the additional root character exp(-2pi i v); restoring the actual physical turn cancels it, giving precisely C_a above. Thus it does not introduce an additional zero or unknown scalar in the restored density. ## 3. A nonzero fixed-channel marked density Use the proved actual geometric frame, slightly deformed if needed to make the exceptional degree nonreal. All ordinary factors are on their selected physical sheets, and the exceptional pair is in the joint deficient corridor on its reflected selected sheet. These conditions are strict and hold on a common neighborhood. The internal q-Hahn roots have already been summed by their actual finite relative packets. Choose the original free magnetic coordinates y after the affine wire constraints. Retain every finite d=N-1 offset and every original cup, cap, degree and Poisson character. For a fixed vector of actual channels alpha=(a_1/N,...,a_R/N) near (1/2,...,1/2), the continued marked ROOT summand therefore has D_N(y,alpha)=U_N N^(-R-1) product_i k_(a_i) b_N(y,alpha) exp[N F(y,alpha)](1+O(N^-1)). (7) Here U_N is only the explicitly recorded head-independent unit phase. The original external line, if any, is kept separately. The functions b_N are holomorphic in y, smooth in the real alpha, nowhere zero, and bounded above and away from zero with fixed derivatives on smaller compacts. They include the nonzero order-one exponentials from the finite affine offsets. Such offsets may be kept literally instead; expanding them changes only b_N and its relative O(N^-1) error. The proof is multiplication of the FIXED number R of packets (6), their exceptional continuation, and the exact marked factor (3). This proves nonzero local density for the complete fixed-channel source, not merely nonzero separate polynomial values. It uses a direct root marked compiler, rather than an unjustified inference about the derivative of an ordinary closed density. The specified meromorphic extension agrees with the original source on its supported grid; its local use does not move any support-dependent residue cycle. ## 4. The actual endpoint lattice has a nonzero local folded Gaussian Fix a point y0 of the complete geometric framing orbit in this chart. Use the FULL marked channel stationarity: the channel derivatives of the unadjusted phase are 2pi i n_i with fixed integers n_i. Subtract these exact characters. This changes no actual channel summand because exp(2pi i n_i a_i)=1. In these marked conventions, F_alpha(y0,1/2)=0, F_(alpha_i,alpha_j)(y0,1/2)=delta_ij H_i, H_i=-4pi i/tau_i, Re H_i<0, (8) where tau_i are the actual oriented primitive cusp shapes. Half twists are included: H_i=-2pi/c_i+2pi i epsilon_i in the rectangular convention. The [channel Hessian theorem](actual_augmented_plat_channel_hessian.md) also proves F_(alpha,y)=0 at the endpoint. Negative real part alone would not substitute for the first equality in (8). The selected branch here is fixed as a neighborhood germ by the full ordinary anchor and the scalar-one deficient reflection, not merely by matching endpoint magnetic momenta. Thus its channel derivatives are the derivatives of the same actual marked principal phase. Explicitly, F=F_raw-2pi i sum_i n_i alpha_i is unchanged in the exponential at every actual grid point; at alpha=1/2 its exponential includes the known unit exp(-pi i N sum_i n_i). Alternatively use the centered F_c=F_raw-2pi i sum_i n_i(alpha_i-1/2), and place that compensating unit in U_N. These conventions give the same (9); the unit is not erased. Let 0<delta<1/6, and sum (7) only over the actual folded labels with 0<N/2-a_i<=N^(1/2+delta). This is a sum of SPECIFIED local continued density values at y0, not the original magnetic period. It has sum_local D_N(y0,a/N) =U_N N^(-R/2-1) b_N(y0,1/2) exp[N F(y0,1/2)] *(2pi)^(R/2)/product_i sqrt(-H_i) *(1+O(N^-1/2)). (9) Each square root is selected by continuation from H_i<0 real; Re H_i<0 makes it nonzero. This coefficient is nonzero at both parities. Here is an elementary lattice proof retaining the endpoint weights. For odd N, the numbers w=N/2-a are 1/2,3/2,5/2,...; their weights are 1 at w=1/2 and 2 thereafter. For even N they are 1,2,3,..., all with weight 2. In either case, for Re H<0, N^-1/2 sum_w k_a exp[H w^2/(2N)] =2 integral_0^infinity exp(H z^2/2) dz+O(N^-1/2) =sqrt(2pi)/sqrt(-H)+O(N^-1/2). (10) The half-step shift and the one exceptional odd weight affect only the O(N^-1/2) error. A direct interval Riemann estimate, using the integrable derivative of the Gaussian, proves this uniformly on compact subsets of Re H<0. The omitted tail is exponentially small in N^(2delta). Taylor's formula gives the quadratic diagonal in (8); the error in N F is O(|w|^3/N^2). On the stated window it tends uniformly to zero. Its Gaussian-weighted absolute sum, and the corresponding variation of b_N, are O(N^-1/2) relative to N^(R/2). This proves (9), including complex H_i; no positivity of the complex terms is assumed. The actual half-twist phase has an independent exact lattice check. Set s=d-2a, s_min=0 at odd N and 1 at even N, and a_max=M. Then nu_a/nu_(a_max) =exp[pi i(s^2-s_min^2)/(4N)]. (11) Indeed the integer character in (-1)^a cancels the linear term in a(a+1) along this parity-restricted lattice. Thus a retained signed half twist contributes its specified quadratic phase, with no alternating nearest-channel factor. Formula (9) does not require an exact even extension of the finite density across the folded endpoint; its one-sided Riemann proof uses the actual two parity lattices directly. No finite noninteger-channel interpolation has been used. Only the proved uniform packet at ACTUAL discrete a_i, its smooth coefficient functions, and the original channel spacing enter. The window has s_i=d-2a_i=O(N^(1/2+delta)), so it is also inside the already proved s_i log N=o(N) generic-normal upper-bound window. That latter bound is not needed to obtain the root local coefficient (9). ## 5. What the magnetic quotient Hessian does and does not add At the certified geometric point the [actual critical scheme](actual_augmented_plat_critical_scheme.md), section 7, identifies the magnetic Hessian radical with exactly the two-dimensional T_diag\PGL2 framing tangent space. On a holomorphic slice transverse to this orbit the magnetic Hessian is nondegenerate. Together with (7) and a nonsingular coordinate Jacobian, this gives a nonzero transverse Gaussian density PER UNIT local framing volume: its coefficient divides the nonzero numerator by the chosen square root of the transverse Hessian determinant. A small local descending Morse cycle for those transverse variables has that nonzero coefficient. This does not integrate the framing orbit or assign its measure to the finite source. Nor does a local Morse cycle establish its coefficient in the original physical cycle. In particular every real forbidden integer degree slice of the exceptional source has zero original period, despite the nonzero continued density away from its real lattice. The degree/cotangent transport and its residue terms cannot be omitted. Thus the unresolved question is not an unspecified zero of a local complete-circle amplitude: fixed-channel density (7) and the marked local folded sum (9) are nonzero. The remaining global work includes the actual degree/magnetic cycle and framing integral, its boundary terms and competing contributions, and any mixed-color extension. No nonzero individual genuine q-normal density is claimed or required by this direct root marked-density theorem. Focused audit: [source normalizations and actual folded lattices](../experiments/audit_actual_augmented_plat_local_marked_density.py), [saved results](../experiments/actual_augmented_plat_local_marked_density_results.json). It checks 49 original h0 endpoint values, 674 exact fold half-twist ratios, five literal unrestricted marked plat contractions, eighteen signed full-coupon relative packets at both parities, and eighteen complex-Gaussian parity calibrations. The source comparisons use the literal terminating columns independently of their determinant formulas. The Gaussian calibrations test the elementary lattice lemma, not a global source period. Uniformity and the exceptional continuation follow from the proofs above and their already audited source dependencies. The conclusion is a nonzero complete local density. It does not supply a global period, framing integral, mixed-color packet, or an individual nonzero generic-normal amplitude. The magnetic transverse statement is per unit local framing volume. No original cycle coefficient or mixed-color theorem is inferred.

title: An exact phase compiler for arbitrary fixed augmented plats
text: # An exact phase compiler for arbitrary fixed augmented plats 30 October 2026. Every fixed 2k-head plat made from the original complete crossing-circle coupons R^epsilon L_N, epsilon in {0,+1,-1}, has an explicit finite factorial sum with its entire original phase. There is no restriction on k>=2 or on the graph formed by its twist regions. The physical q-Hahn sums simplify: their internal quadratic phases cancel exactly, leaving a single linear Fourier phase. The resulting internal critical equation is a quadratic polynomial. This is a source-exact complete-color statement. It supplies an explicit global phase and finite algebraic candidate equations. It does not select their geometric branch, prove a global contour/gap, or supply a mixed-color filling corridor. Thus it is an advance toward a theorem for arbitrary fixed sufficiently twisted plats, not that volume theorem itself. A proposed twist threshold T(D) depends on the fixed skeleton D; it is distinct from quantum level N. ## 1. The phase of the actual physical Casimir column Put d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, x=q^d=-q^-1, kappa=q^(d^2/2), and s_n=product_(r=1)^n 2sin(pi r/N). For 0<=b<=a<=d write the POSITIVE sine binomial beta(a,b)=s_a/(s_b s_(a-b)). Let t<=d be an actual low physical pair degree, j a Casimir index, and 0<=u<=t. The actual canonical eigenvector of the physical pair Casimir has first entry one and components f_u(c_j), with c_j=q^(2j+1)+q^(-2j-1). Its already proved finite q-Hahn formula is f_u(c_j)=x^(t-j)/[t choose j]_Q sum_a (-1)^a x^[-(t-j-u+2a)] Q^[a(a-1)/2+a(t-j-u+a)] [j choose a]_Q [u choose a]_Q [t-u choose j-a]_Q, max(0,u-t+j)<=a<=min(j,u). (1) All factorial indices are below N. In particular (1) describes the original physical column, not an arbitrarily normalized eigenbasis. The elementary marked identity [v choose w]_Q=q^[w(v-w)] beta(v,w) turns (1) into the simpler exact formula f_u(c_j)=(-1)^u q^[-(j+1)u] sum_a (-1)^a q^[a(t+j+1)] E(t,j,u,a), E(t,j,u,a)=beta(j,a) beta(u,a) beta(t-u,j-a)/beta(t,j)>0. (2) Indeed the complete exponent of q inside (1) is -u+2a+a(a-1)+2a(t-j-u+a) +a(j-a)+a(u-a)+(j-a)(t-u-j+a)-j(t-j) =a(t+j+1)-(j+1)u. (3) The a^2 terms cancel. No factorial envelope or asymptotic estimate is used in this cancellation. On every channel that survives the COMPLETE circle, d-j<=t and j<=floor(d/2). Put delta=t+j-d. Since (-1)^a=q^(-Na), (2) is f_u(c_j)=(-1)^u q^[-(j+1)u] sum_a q^(delta a) E(t,j,u,a), 0<=delta<=floor(d/2). (4) Thus the summation variable carries a positive-coefficient polynomial at one specified Fourier argument q^delta. Its entire phase is retained; positivity of its coefficients does not imply positivity or a lower bound for that value. ## 2. Complete signed coupons in every original degree Take an arbitrary physical pair degree S in 0,...,2d. Set t=min(S,2d-S), shift=max(0,S-d). Use physical basis |shift+u,S-shift-u>, 0<=u<=t. The high block is literally the low block under this index translation, for both the Casimir and original signed crossing. For every j with j<d-j<=t the full reflected-circle resolution has positive coefficient h_(t,j)=2s_t^2/[s_(t-j)s_(t+j-d)]. If N is odd and j=d/2<=t, use the same formula WITHOUT the factor 2. No other channel contributes. Let nu_j=(-1)^j q^[j(j+1)]. Then the EXACT all-input kernel of B_epsilon=R^epsilon L_N is B_epsilon[u,v]=kappa^epsilon x^(-t) sum_j h_(t,j) nu_j^(epsilon-1) f_u(c_j) f_v(c_j). (5) This is bilinear in the two physical columns, not Hermitian. To prove it, start with the actual positive reflected tensor H=L_N P=sum_j h v_j v_j^*. Its normalized last component is (v_j)_t=x^t nu_j, and literal reversal gives P conjugate(v_j)=conjugate(x^t nu_j) v_j. Hence L_N=H P has coefficient h x^-t nu_j^-1 times v_j v_j^T. On this actual complete-circle image, R acts by kappa nu_j. At a double root its normal correction annihilates L_N: the latter is its derivative times the square-zero Jordan operator. At the odd simple root the value calculation is immediate. This proves (5) for both signs, all parities and all physical degree blocks. Thus the normal directions responsible for L_N have been evaluated exactly BEFORE the rank-one image is used. Formula (5) is not an initial semisimple quotient, and it does not identify an arbitrary generic-q germ with its root values. Substitution of (4) makes each (j,a,b) contribution to (5) the positive factorial weight h_(t,j) E(t,j,u,a) E(t,j,v,b) times kappa^epsilon (-1)^[t+(epsilon-1)j+u+v] q^[t+(epsilon-1)j(j+1)-(j+1)(u+v)+delta(a+b)]. (6) Equation (6) is the complete physical coupon phase. In particular the two internal summation variables have no individual square term. ## 3. Compile any fixed augmented 2k-plat Fix the positions and order of the twist regions in a literal 2k-head plat. Augment every chosen region by its original auxiliary circle and retain its prescribed parity epsilon. Use the original bottom cups, ordinary top caps and ONE unrestricted marked top cap: p_ab=N x^-b delta_(a+b,d), ell_ab=x^a delta_(a+b,d)/N, m_ab=x^b/N^2. (7) The original exterior line chi_N, including framing, stays explicit. All crossing-circle coupons and any remaining original crossings preserve integer degree. Only after the k-1 ordinary top caps have acted does total degree kd force the marked pair degree to d. This is the permitted whole-source restriction; m is not replaced locally in a separated degree-changing sector. Expand every augmented coupon by (5), or further by (6). Sum every actual physical wire index, channel j and internal q-Hahn index. Unchanged identity wires identify their labels. The resulting finite sum is EXACTLY chi_N times the original marked plat contraction. There is no inverse Clebsch matrix, recoupling determinant, fitted boundary vector, or division by a knot value in this construction. The powers in (7) multiply to N^-1; all other powers, phases and factorials are those in (5)--(6). Each kappa^epsilon is retained as its explicit external unit phase, not reset to one. For a fixed skeleton this is a finite union of rational affine state polytopes. The low/high choices t=S or t=2d-S give finitely many chambers. Every surviving channel and internal summation range is an explicit linear inequality, such as d-j<=t, 2j<=d, max(0,u-t+j)<=a<=min(j,u). All lattice offsets from d=N-1 and both parity endpoint weights are kept in the exact formulas. The number of states is bounded by a power of N depending on the fixed diagram. Augmentation removes the large full-twist powers from the number of blocks; those fixed filling parameters are not extra copies of a quantum-level dependent packet. This also computes the physical coefficient tensor entering the [marked multiport Chebyshev packet](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_marked_multiport_chebyshev_source_packet.md). That packet's correct C,...,C,H conjugation and final half-bandwidth fold may be applied afterward. Neither its polynomial DCT cost nor this exact compiler proves a sharp coherent energy bound. ## 4. An explicit global action and a local quadratic critical equation Let J(z)=integral_0^z Log(2sin(pi w))dw with the marks continued from positive factorial arguments. Put B(v,w)=J(v)-J(w)-J(v-w). For scaled labels (tau,xi,upsilon,alpha)=(t,j,u,a)/N the real factorial action of E is Ecal=B(xi,alpha)+B(upsilon,alpha) +B(tau-upsilon,xi-alpha)-B(tau,xi). (8) Its exact leading complex phase after (4) is Ecal+pi i[upsilon-xi*upsilon +(tau+xi-1)alpha]. (9) The finite +1 terms and d=N-1 differences give specified order-one amplitude/phase corrections; they are recovered from (4), not discarded. For a whole coupon add two copies of (8), the h action 2J(tau)-J(tau-xi)-J(tau+xi-1), (10) and the exact polynomial phase read from (6). Include the source characters from (7). Summing these functions over the original network gives its explicit global candidate phase. Uniform factorial errors are O_D(log N) even at endpoints; this alone bounds the absolute term envelope, not the coherent sum from below. There is a particularly simple algebraic equation for an INTERNAL q-Hahn stationary variable. The derivative of (8) exponentiates to sin(pi(xi-alpha))^2 sin(pi(upsilon-alpha)) / [sin(pi alpha)^2 sin(pi(tau-upsilon-xi+alpha))]. (11) The phase in (9) supplies exp(pi i(tau+xi-1)). Set T=exp(2pi i tau), Jc=exp(2pi i xi), U=exp(2pi i upsilon), Z=exp(2pi i alpha). With the original logarithmic marks and away from the displayed pole divisors, exp(partial_alpha Phi)=1 is exactly T(Jc-Z)^2(U-Z)+(Z-1)^2(TZ-U Jc)=0. (12) Its cubic terms cancel. The remaining quadratic coefficients are A=T(2Jc+U-2)-U Jc, B=T(1-Jc^2-2Jc U)+2U Jc, C=U Jc(T Jc-1), A Z^2+B Z+C=0. (13) The degree is at most two on special parameter loci; no division by A is made. Such degenerations and the specified pole divisors must remain in any branch analysis. The complete global stationarity equations likewise become explicit rational Laurent equations after exponentiating the original wire variables and clearing ONLY specified nonzero denominators. Thus finite algebraic candidate-branch and Jacobian tests are available at arbitrary fixed bridge width. Pole exclusions, logarithmic marks, boundary sectors and the original finite cycle remain part of the problem. A solution of (12) has not thereby been identified with a geometric tetrahedron or an A-polynomial branch. ## 5. Why the real positive saddle criterion does not automatically apply This exact phase also locates an obstruction. At a real strict complete-image channel, 0<tau+xi-1<1/2. The factorial logarithmic derivative (11) is positive real, while the derivative phase has argument strictly between 0 and pi/2. Consequently an interior real alpha cannot solve the stationary equation even after subtracting an integer Poisson frequency. Equivalently, the representation before (4) has imaginary derivative between 2pi and 5pi/2; its retained integer mark removes 2pi and leaves exactly the phase in (9). On the boundary delta=0 the finite q-Hahn sum in (4) IS positive, but this is one channel boundary, not a theorem that the whole augmented source concentrates there. The odd simple channel and even endpoint pairs must also remain in any endpoint analysis. Thus the real-concave version of the [analytic sewing criterion](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_six_port_analytic_sewing_criterion.md) cannot be applied to this raw expanded phase by ignoring its Fourier factor. One needs a source-preserving complex deformation, a selected local resummation, or another exact period representation, followed by a global boundary/gap and nonzero-period argument. The quadratic (12) makes the local candidate branches explicit; it does not choose their original-cycle coefficients. The mixed ordinary-circle colors required by long Dehn filling need a separate extension as well. Audit: [physical Casimir columns, full signed coupons and marked plats](../experiments/audit_actual_augmented_plat_phase_compiler.py). The fresh audit passes N=2,...,10: 99 original degree blocks, 704 canonical-column entries, all three signed complete coupon identities in every block, and eight literal marked plat contractions at k=2,3,4. Its matrices are built independently from the original coproduct and signed crossings, not from the q-Hahn formula being checked. The symbolic phase cancellation and quadratic degree are also checked exactly. These are source-identity checks, not numerical evidence for an unproved all-plat volume limit. The finite compiler does not supply a mixed-color packet or select a geometric cycle.

title: A finite criterion for a physical magnetic framing
status: Finite framing tests; right-angled obstruction follows
text: # A finite criterion for a physical magnetic framing **Subsequent scope result (30 October):** the [right-angled obstruction and localization](actual_right_angled_selected_framing_obstruction.md) proves that no common all-central selected frame exists for the actual certified right-angled plat cut. Generic geometric strip flags have exactly two strict physical-support failures, at arbitrary bridge width. The local conditional statements below remain valid; their simultaneous realization in that right-angled class cannot supply the general proof. 30 October 2026. This note reduces the simultaneous framing question for the actual complete augmented-plat character to a strict semialgebraic feasibility problem in one rank-one projector. It also treats the smaller central domain used by the joint accretive determinant. The criterion keeps every original prefix word and both actual degree adapters. There is no assertion that this feasibility problem always has a solution. The positive gluing certificate and the regular critical-scheme theorem do not by themselves prove that assertion. In particular, a nonempty real-open set of perfectly regular frames fails physical support at any one essential crossing disk. The obstruction below explains why merely avoiding algebraic divisors cannot settle the issue. ## 1. The common frame is a rank-one projector Fix the actual marked geometric representation and its finite original Morse word. For its prefix matrices Q use the same trace -2 main lifts as in the [regular magnetic chart](actual_augmented_plat_regular_geometric_phase_chart.md). A simultaneous projective frame g, modulo LEFT diagonal changes, is equivalently Pi=g^(-1) E_11 g, Pi^2=Pi, tr Pi=1, det Pi=0. (1) Indeed the two eigenspaces of Pi have distinct eigenvalues 1 and 0, so every such projector is obtained this way; its stabilizer is precisely the projective diagonal torus. This is the same two-dimensional complex framing quotient as in the [actual critical scheme](actual_augmented_plat_critical_scheme.md). Every needed prefix diagonal is the LINEAR function a_Q=tr(Q Pi)=(g Q g^(-1))_11. (2) At an input of a crossing-circle coupon put Q_0=W, Q_1=A W, Q_2=P W, P=B A, a_i=tr(Q_i Pi). For the output, replace A by the actual outgoing first meridian A'; Q_0 and Q_2 are unchanged. The original two physical wire phases are X_1=-a_0/a_1, X_2=-a_1/a_2, T=X_1 X_2=a_0/a_2. (3) We always impose the other finitely many regular-chart nonvanishings from the cited chart theorem. No independent local change of frame is permitted in (2). ## 2. Exact strict-support criterion For a nonzero X off the positive real axis choose its wire logarithm by x=Log_(0,2pi)(X)/(2pi i), 0<Re x<1. (4) Write s=x_1+x_2. The actual low adapter is tau=s, u=x_1; the high adapter is tau=2-s, u=1-x_2. At the complete channel the strict local physical domain is 1/2<Re tau<1, 0<Re u<Re tau. (5) For three nonzero prefix diagonals, (4)--(5) hold if and only if Im(a_0 conjugate(a_2)) != 0, 0 is not in the real convex hull of {a_0,a_1,a_2}. (6) Here the low or high adapter is determined, rather than freely chosen. The second condition is equivalent to the existence of one open half-plane through the origin containing all three numbers. Proof. Rotate a_0 to the positive axis. Under the convex-hull condition the three arguments have lifts arg a_0=0, arg a_2=delta in (-pi,pi), arg a_1=beta, max(0,beta,delta)-min(0,beta,delta)<pi. The first condition in (6) says delta is neither 0 nor an endpoint. The canonical physical arguments are consequently 2pi Re x_1=pi-beta, 2pi Re x_2=pi+beta-delta. (7) Their sum is 2pi-delta. Thus delta>0 gives the low adapter, delta<0 gives the high adapter, and Re tau=1-|delta|/(2pi) in (1/2,1). Both inequalities for u follow from 0<Re x_i<1: in the low case tau-u=x_2, and in the high case tau-u=1-x_1. Conversely (5) puts the sum of the two wire arguments strictly between pi and 3pi and away from 2pi. The inverse formulas (7) put the three prefix arguments in an interval of width less than pi. This proves (6). The input and output have the same a_0,a_2. Their prescribed adapter therefore agrees. Their canonical sums agree in real part by (7) and in imaginary part by X_1 X_2=T. Thus degree conservation holds as an EXACT complex equality, not only after exponentiation. At a cup or cap the first and last prefix words agree. The corresponding condition is simply that a_1/a_0 is not a nonpositive real number; all diagonals are nonzero. Then X_2=X_1^(-1) and their canonical logarithms sum exactly to 1. Applying these tests at every event makes the chosen wire logarithms solve the original affine incidence equations Bx=b without any additional integer adjustment. Ordinary and marked cap characters are still the distinct characters recorded in the source. ## 3. The central joint domain has an even simpler test The central domain adds |2 Re u-Re tau|<1/2 (8) to (5). This is the leading open domain Re c>0, Re z>0 for c=-cos(pi tau), z=exp[pi i(tau-2u)]. The exact finite c has tau+1/N in place of tau; any compact subset of (5),(8) satisfies its corresponding inequality for large N. For BOTH actual adapters, tau-2u=x_2-x_1. (9) Consequently the central condition is adapter-independent. In physical wire real parts it is the diamond |Re x_1-1/2|+|Re x_2-1/2|<1/2, Re(x_1+x_2) != 1. (10) An exact test using only the prefix diagonals is Im(a_0 conjugate(a_2)) != 0, |a_2| Re(a_1 conjugate(a_0)) +|a_0| Re(a_1 conjugate(a_2)) > 0. (11) Proof. In the argument lifts above, (8) is |2 beta-delta|<pi. This says precisely that a_1 lies in the open half-plane centered at the bisector of the MINOR angular interval from a_0 to a_2. The vector a_0/|a_0|+a_2/|a_2| points along that bisector. Taking the scalar product with a_1 gives (11). Conversely the resulting interval delta/2-pi/2<beta<delta/2+pi/2, with |delta|<pi, puts all three arguments in an interval of width less than pi. Thus (11) itself implies (6), as well as (8). This extra inequality is substantial: same-side disk flags, or merely being in the larger physical strip (5), does not imply (11). ## 4. A finite semialgebraic feasibility problem Equations (1),(2),(6) give a finite strict semialgebraic test for a simultaneous physical magnetic frame. One can encode the convex-hull test with one complex separator n_f per input/output triple: |n_f|^2=1, Re(n_f a_(f,i))>0 for i=0,1,2. For the central domain there are no separator choices. Introduce positive real r_(f,0),r_(f,2) with r_(f,i)^2=|a_(f,i)|^2 and require r_(f,2) Re(a_(f,1) conjugate(a_(f,0))) +r_(f,0) Re(a_(f,1) conjugate(a_(f,2))) > 0. (12) Also require the square of Im(a_(f,0) conjugate(a_(f,2))) to be positive, impose the cup/cap tests, and retain every regular-chart nonvanishing. All coefficients are algebraic when the actual marked representation is algebraic. Only one projector Pi is shared by the whole diagram. This formulation is suitable for an exact feasibility or infeasibility certificate; it is not a collection of independent local frame choices. A strict feasible frame persists under sufficiently small changes of the marked representation. The strict inequalities give a common positive margin on the finite set of triples, and all denominators remain nonzero. In particular it would persist for sufficiently long fillings once obtained at completeness. This persistence does not obtain the initial frame. Nor does (12) make the pair totals real: their imaginary parts come from the moduli of the prefix ratios. A theorem continuing only u at fixed real t,j cannot be applied to these generally complex totals. Even a joint domain requires comparing its selected internal roots with the actual geometric roots, and subsequently controlling the contributing global finite-source cycle. ### A finite family sharing one disk product is always feasible There is a constructive positive result: all input/output triples from any fixed finite family of transports sharing the SAME product P and prefix W can be made central simultaneously. This does not couple different disk products or different prefixes. Normalize A,P as in (13), put H=P+I, and write its transported splits as A_b=(I+bH)A(I-bH), with b in the given finite complex set. This includes every complete centralizer transport and any retained finite half-twist shifts. For a>0 put h=sqrt(2a+1) and take the projector L_a=[[1+a/2+i h/2, (a-1)/4+i h/2], [-a-1, -a/2-i h/2]]. (12a) Direct multiplication gives L_a^2=L_a, tr L_a=1, tr(P L_a)=1, tr(A L_a)=a, tr([H,A] L_a)=-4i h, tr(A_b L_a)=a-4i b sqrt(2a+1)-8b^2. (12b) For the finite b-set the last expression is a+O(sqrt(a)), uniformly as a tends to positive infinity. It therefore has positive real part for every b once a is large enough. The central scalar inequality in (11), with endpoints 1,1, is then strictly positive for every triple. Only its T=1 seam remains. These finitely many scalar inequalities hold on an open neighborhood of L_a in the complex projector surface. The nonconstant function tr(P L) cannot be real on any such open neighborhood. A sufficiently small perturbation therefore removes the seam, and gives all the strict central tests. For an arbitrary shared prefix W, recover the actual common projector by Pi=W^(-1)L/tr(W^(-1)L). (12c) It is rank-one of trace one, and its actual prefix diagonals are one common nonzero scalar times tr(L),tr(A_b L),tr(P L). Thus the central inequalities are unchanged. The additional trace in (12c) does not vanish identically on the projector surface: otherwise ell(W^(-1)v)=0 for every ell(v)=1, forcing W^(-1)=0. Hence its zero set cannot contain the feasible open neighborhood. The perturbation can simultaneously avoid this trace, the seam, and the finitely many proper regular-chart divisors. This proves the assertion for W as well, rather than assuming the W=I projector survives unchanged. The construction is a precise favorable near-coincident-frame mechanism at ONE auxiliary flag. It proves that each coupon's incoming and outgoing central inequalities are locally compatible. It leaves the genuinely simultaneous problem (12), with the actual different products and prefixes of the full plat, unresolved. ## 5. A geometric necessary condition and an open obstruction There is a useful uniform restriction on possible solutions. At one essential complete disk normalize its distinct puncture flags so that A=-[[1,1],[0,1]], B=-[[1,0],[-4,1]], P=B A=[[1,1],[-4,-3]]. (13) This normalization follows directly from Tr A=Tr B=Tr P=-2. The circle through the three parabolic flags is then the real circle. Write Pi=v ell with ell(v)=1, put w=ker ell, and put z=Wv. These are projective points; z is the right framing point transported by the ACTUAL prefix W. If (6) holds, then z and w lie in the same open side of this circle. (14) In particular replacing z by v in this test would be incorrect. Here is a direct proof. For real r=(r_0,r_1,r_2) set M(r)=r_0 I+r_1 A+r_2 P. The matrices in this pencil are real-linearly independent and det M=2(r_0^2+r_1^2+r_2^2)-(r_0+r_1+r_2)^2. (15) Suppose z,w are in opposite open half-planes. The condition M(r)z=w is two homogeneous real linear equations in three r's, so it has a nonzero solution. M(r) cannot annihilate a nonreal z: its real and imaginary vector parts are linearly independent, which would force M=0. The real Möbius transformation identity Im M(z)=det(M) Im(z)/|M_21 z+M_22|^2 therefore gives det M<0. Normalize the sign so that sum r_i>0. Equation (15) forces every r_i>0: if, for example, r_0<=0, then det M=(r_1-r_2)^2+r_0^2-2r_0(r_1+r_2)>=0, because r_1+r_2>0. This is a contradiction. Now 0=ell(M(r)Wv)=r_0 a_0+r_1 a_1+r_2 a_2. This is a strictly positive convex relation after division by sum r_i, contradicting (6). If z is nonreal and w is on the real circle, the same argument gives det M=0 and r_i>=0, still a nontrivial convex relation. If z is on the real circle, solve instead M(r)z=0, again two real equations in three unknowns. The same det=0 argument gives r_i>=0 and the same relation for every w. The point at infinity is handled in homogeneous coordinates, or by a real change of disk coordinates. Thus a good triple must satisfy (14). This is a necessary condition, not a converse. The opposite-side choice is a nonempty REAL-OPEN condition on the common framing quotient. It also allows v and w to be distinct, as required for a projector. The common regular-frame locus is a complex Zariski open dense subset by the cited chart theorem. It intersects this real-open bad set: a nonzero holomorphic polynomial cannot vanish on a real-open subset of this complex manifold. Hence EVERY such complete character has common regular frames that fail physical support already at this disk. This conclusion holds independently of whether the representation has a positive gluing certificate. For a small exact illustration use W=I, v=(i,1), ell=(1,i)/(2i), so w=-i. Equations (13) give (a_0,a_1,a_2)=(1,-1+i/2,-1-5i/2), (1/2)a_0+(5/12)a_1+(1/12)a_2=0. (16) The endpoint discriminant numerator is a_0 a_1+a_1 a_2+a_0 a_2=1/4, and the leading-coefficient numerator a_0+a_2+4a_1=-4-i/2; both are nonzero. Thus this support failure is not just the local root-discriminant failure. Formula (16) is only a local illustration; the preceding open-density argument deals with all the other regular divisors of the actual finite diagram. Near-coincident framing points do not evade (14). In the limit w=v, each condition concerns v and Wv on its own developed disk circle. The different prefixes W are fixed words of the representation, not small perturbations of the identity. No simultaneous same-side or central-domain conclusion follows just by taking w close to v. ## 6. What an ordinary fixed-total fiber estimate does and does not say At fixed real discrete t,j, the proved magnetic corridor can be multiplied over a fixed finite number of ORDINARY q-Hahn column factors. Pull their magnetic u variables back by affine wire maps preserving every such total. On a compact subset of the common corridors, the relative errors multiply to 1+O(1/N), the leading actions add, and the nonzero amplitudes multiply. An already evaluated normal-derived coefficient depending only on these fixed t,j may remain an EXACT scalar outside this product. This elementary product statement estimates neither generic q/normal derivatives of the columns nor the rank-two derivative terms of mixed source kernels. It supplies no bound for fiber summation and does not release t,j. It therefore does not establish an asymptotic for an arbitrary full original-source summand containing those normal terms. Audit: [exact projector, determinant, convexity and adapter checks](../experiments/audit_actual_augmented_plat_physical_framing_criterion.py). The audit includes numerical argument comparisons only as regressions of the explicit equivalences; it is not an existence search or a proof of a favorable simultaneous frame for arbitrary augmented plats. The expanded audit includes 100 exact central-feasibility checks for the constructive lemma. No global existence or cycle claim follows.

title: A regular magnetic chart for the complete geometric plat character
text: # A regular magnetic chart for the complete geometric plat character 30 October 2026. A complete geometric augmented-plat representation can be put simultaneously into the regular magnetic charts of the actual local critical-character map. This is a finite generic-framing theorem, not an assumption that the geometric flags are already in a convenient chart. At the leading exponentiated level its original Morse degree constraints also have an integral logarithmic lift. The statement constructs a regular candidate for the UNFOLDED principal equations. It does not prove that its logarithms lie in a nonempty physical support chamber, choose its Poisson sector in the original finite cycle, establish a nondegenerate reduced critical branch, or supply a quantum asymptotic. Those distinctions matter at the folded channel endpoint. ## 1. The actual prefix factorization Fix the finite ordered Morse word of the augmented plat and its actual complete geometric representation. Use common trace -2 lifts of the main meridians. At each circle box its two puncture flags are distinct and their ordered product P is noncentral parabolic with trace -2, as in the [geometric endpoint theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_augmented_plat_geometric_channel_endpoint.md). The same statements hold after its retained Hurwitz half twists. These hypotheses do not require a right-angled cell decomposition. In any actual complete geometric augmented exterior, the disk boundary is a nontrivial peripheral longitude of its auxiliary cusp. If its two main puncture parabolics had the same fixed point, their nontrivial parabolic product would have that point too. This would identify a main cusp lift with an auxiliary cusp lift. Distinct cusp lifts have disjoint sufficiently small horoballs; two horoballs with the same ideal center intersect. This is impossible for different components. The elementary common-trace calculation then forces Tr P=-2. At any horizontal cut let H_1,...,H_m be its ordered based meridians and Q_i=H_i ... H_1, Q_0=I. For a determinant-one matrix Q with Q_11!=0 put Bminus(Q)=[[1,0],[-Q_21,Q_11]], Bplus(Q)=[[Q_11,Q_12],[0,1]]. Then Q=Bminus(Q)^-1 Bplus(Q). Consequently the original physical head at slot i is G_i=Bminus(Q_(i-1)) H_i Bminus(Q_(i-1))^-1, K_i=(Q_i)_11/(Q_(i-1))_11, X_i=-1/K_i, S_i=(G_i)_21/(K_i+1). (1) For K_i!=0,-1 these are finite nonzero magnetic coordinates. The determinant-one and trace -2 equations give exactly the original head matrix (8) of the [local critical map](actual_augmented_plat_local_critical_character_map.md). Thus (1) does not introduce an independent flag realization. Change the ONE common frame by g in SL2(C), so every word Q changes to gQg^-1. There are finitely many heads and boxes. The following sections show that each excluded condition is a proper algebraic subset of this same frame group. Their finite union cannot cover it. ## 2. Every required endpoint chart divisor is avoidable A nonzero 2-by-2 matrix R has a nonzero (gRg^-1)_11 for some g. Indeed otherwise every vector/covector pair v,l with l(v)=1 would have l(Rv)=0, forcing R=0. Thus a forbidden diagonal of any NONZERO fixed word combination is a proper condition. This handles all prefix diagonals. It also handles K_i=-1, since Q_i+Q_(i-1)=(H_i+I)Q_(i-1) is nonzero for a nontrivial trace -2 parabolic. At a local input pair put R=Q_(i-1), A=H_i, B=H_(i+1), P=BA and Q_0=R,Q_1=AR,Q_2=PR. Write a_r=(gQ_r g^-1)_11. Its low physical coordinates obey U=-a_0/a_1, T=a_0/a_2. (2) The exclusions T=+/-1 and U=T are diagonal conditions for (I-/+P)R and (I+B)AR. These matrices are nonzero. The endpoint q-Hahn quadratic leading coefficient is U(T+1)-4T. Its vanishing, away from the nonzero a_r, is exactly a_0+a_2+4a_1=0. The corresponding fixed matrix is (I+P+4A)R. It is nonzero because Tr(I+P+4A)=-8. The discriminant is proportional to T+1-U. Here its vanishing is the quadratic expression a_0a_1+a_1a_2+a_0a_2=0. (3) To prove this is PROPER for every prefix R, conjugate just for this nonvanishing proof to the canonical pair A=-[[1,1],[0,1]], B=-[[1,0],[-4,1]], R=[[a,b],[c,d]], ad-bc=1. The normalization follows from the two distinct flags and Tr(BA)=-2. For the test frames g_r=[[1,r],[0,1]], direct multiplication gives a_0a_1+a_1a_2+a_0a_2=-( -a+c r-c )^2. (4) This polynomial is not identically zero, since the first column (a,c) of R is not zero. Therefore (3) is avoidable by a generic common frame. A different test frame can prove propriety for each box; the final choice avoids ALL of their finitely many bad loci. Both total F and total E may also be required nonzero. In the local Borel frame E_tot=P_12/a_0, so its zero is proper because P is noncentral. For F_tot the numerator, up to nonzero diagonal factors, is det(Rv,PRv), where v=g^-1 e_1. This quadratic in v is not identically zero for a noncentral P. Thus this exclusion is proper too. These conditions exclude every pole in the endpoint local formulas. For example P(U,Z) at J=-1 cannot have Z=0,1,-1,U or TZ+U=0: substitution gives a nonzero product of T,U,T+1,U-1,U-T. Its leading coefficient is nonzero and its discriminant is nonzero, so both roots are finite and simple. The actual magnetic momentum selects its root by the rational inverse (5) of the local map. For the HIGH chamber use T_low=T_phys^-1 and U_low=U_phys/T_phys. The discriminant divisor transforms by T_low+1-U_low=(T_phys+1-U_phys)/T_phys, and the leading coefficient by U_low(T_low+1)-4T_low =[U_phys(T_phys+1)-4T_phys]/T_phys^2. All other excluded head and total-coefficient divisors are the same ones above, with F and E exchanged. Thus the single generic frame works for either actual degree adapter at every box. If the marked geometric representation is algebraic, the good frame may be chosen algebraic (in fact rational after fixing its matrix coordinates). To see this use a rational big-cell parametrization of SL2 and clear the finitely many nonzero denominators. A nonzero polynomial over a number field cannot vanish on all rational tuples, by the elementary one-variable root count and induction. Equations (1) and the local inverse then give algebraic magnetic and internal phases. This does not make their logarithms algebraic. ## 3. The unconstrained integral degree lift The leading Morse degree equations are sum_out-sum_in=0 at a coupon, sum_out=1 at a cup, and sum_in=1 at a cap. Regard every physical wire as an oriented edge between successive events. Their coefficient matrix is the oriented incidence matrix of this finite graph: each wire occurs once positively and once negatively. Choose any logarithms of the magnetic X_e. Since the exponentiated degree equations hold, each defect from the desired affine equation is an integer. On each connected component the sum of these defects is zero. The wire terms cancel, and that component has equally many cups and caps, by counting incoming and outgoing half-edges. Every integral vertex vector of total zero is the incidence image of an integral edge vector: choose a spanning tree, remove its leaves one by one, and put the leaf defect on its unique remaining edge. The last defect is zero by the total-sum condition. Adding these integer corrections to the wire logarithms solves all affine degree equations exactly. This does NOT enforce 0<=Re u_e<=1, select the finite low/high support chambers, or erase a recorded phase. The original ordinary and marked cap characters differ by an integral Poisson character and must still be kept. The result is an unrestricted logarithmic lift, not a claim about the support of the physical finite sum. ## 4. Consequence and precise remaining gap In the good common frame reconstruct the local roots from the actual geometric momenta. Both q-Hahn internal equations hold.
