The local map preserves the whole ordered product and recovers the actual inverse auxiliary transport; at completeness its channel equation is R_epsilon=1. Shared wires carry the SAME X,S, and original cups/caps give the inverse-meridian relation P=I. Thus the local derivatives match on the tangent lattice of the Morse degree constraints, and their exponentials are one. Section 3 supplies an affine degree lift. This is a regular geometric solution of the UNFOLDED exponentiated principal equations, with the original marked representation. It is a genuine candidate input to the regulator comparison. The result does not identify a physical support chamber with a nonempty selected cycle, or show that the required logarithmic/Poisson sector contributes. It makes no claim of a reduced nondegenerate Hessian, nearby holomorphic critical family, nonzero source amplitude, or volume asymptotic. The frame construction is not an argument that one may change the original quantum source by choosing a favorable co-source. It is a coordinate choice on its classical marked character, retaining the original cup/cap equations. The dimension of its framing orbit after the phase-coordinate reductions is not asserted here. ## 5. The remaining bridge to the source-selected local branch The [actual q-Hahn logarithm theorem](actual_q_hahn_selected_complex_action.md) now selects the local internal branch for REAL strict physical parameters, including the folded endpoint. At that endpoint, if 1/2<tau<1, 0<u<tau, w=exp[pi i(tau-1/2)], its selected logarithmic root satisfies max(0,u-tau+1/2)<Re alpha<min(u,1/2), Im alpha>0. Consequently Z=exp(2pi i alpha) lies in the upper half of the unit disk. The strict inequality tau>1/2 matters: at w=1 the selected alpha is real instead. The implicit function theorem also gives joint complex parameter germs near these regular physical points. These are source-selected local data, not yet a global continuation to the geometric candidate constructed above. The exact endpoint quadratic is [U(T+1)-4T] Z^2+2U(T-1) Z+U(T+1)=0, discriminant=16TU(T+1-U). A small loop about U=T+1 at a generic fixed T exchanges its two roots. Thus unspecified algebraic or holomorphic continuation can change the branch. What is still needed is a common admissible continuation domain, or an explicitly controlled path, which carries the ACTUAL selected local kernels and their original logarithmic marks from a nonempty physical support chamber to the geometric point at every coupon simultaneously. Generic avoidance of the discriminant and the integral affine lift in section 3 do not supply that statement. Even after such a branch comparison, the remaining whole-source cycle and noncancellation estimate would be separate work. Long fillings perturb the auxiliary color parameters chi by O(1/p) near the complete source, with p the filling slope. They do not by themselves resolve this base magnetic branch-selection problem. The source-divisor extension permits a finite-order zero of an already constructed analytic amplitude; it does not construct the missing selected branch or prove that its amplitude germ is nonzero. Audit: [exact generic-chart identities](../experiments/audit_actual_augmented_plat_regular_geometric_phase_chart.py).

text: # Selected physical factors outside one exact matching-edge block 30 October 2026. This note assembles two separate inputs: the actual source's full physical packet and the proved right-angled geometric localization. It does not identify a contributing global finite cycle. ## 1. Inputs and statement Fix an actual augmented plat of arbitrary fixed width, with its retained half twists, literal Morse word, original exposed physical mark, and a positive convex ideal right-angled matching-polyhedron certificate as in [the actual matching geometry](../papers/marked-fillings/README.md). The actual source is the full marked matching-graph source; its folded labels, partner normals and generic lifts are not replaced by a root-only semisimple network. Choose any one crossing-circle matching edge e. Use the following two established inputs, with their distinct scopes: * The [prescribed-pair geometric theorem](actual_right_angled_selected_framing_obstruction.md) supplies a common regular frame with strip flags in the common shaded exterior K. Its only two strict physical-support failures are the two shaded facets at the ends of e. All other ordinary input/output factors have their actual canonical low or high physical coordinates. * The [full physical complex packet](actual_q_hahn_full_physical_complex_packet.md) concerns the original finite q-Hahn column. Its limiting domain is P={ (tau,nu) in C^2 : 1/2<Re tau<1, 0<Re nu<Re tau }. (1) On each compact of P, for sufficiently large N and actual integer folded channels j with j/N near 1/2, it gives the selected ordinary packet with nonzero amplitude. Its selected characteristic extends from the previously proved central domain. No complex continuation of the finite index j is inferred from this statement. Then the common frame can be chosen so that EVERY ordinary factor outside the two ends of e belongs to the source-selected branch on P. The two exceptions comprise ONE original matching-edge operator, whose four exterior objects all have highest weight d=N-1. That operator has the exact generic recoupling and retained first-normal formula of [the marked four-port block](actual_matching_edge_marked_four_port_block.md). The original physical mark remains where it was. The finite collection of good factors lies in a common compact subset of P. Consequently their ordinary finite-column packets can be multiplied there, with the product of their nonzero amplitudes and relative error 1+O(1/N). This is a local product statement at the framed geometric germ, not an estimate of the complementary tensor contraction, its summation, or the completed marked source. ## 2. The selected flag branches continue throughout P Here is the additional proof needed beyond the old central-domain statement. Write T=exp(2pi i tau), U=exp(2pi i nu), zeta=T^(1/2)/U, W=1-(T+1)/U, V=W+zeta^2, (2) where T^(1/2)=exp(pi i tau) retains its marked argument. The full packet proves W and V nonzero on P at the endpoint channel xi=1/2. Its square root of W is the analytic continuation from the positive real center. It need not be the pointwise principal square root outside the central domain. Since P is convex and W is nonzero, that continued square root is single valued. Normalize the actual incoming puncture matrices as A=-[[1,1],[0,1]], B=-[[1,0],[-4,1]], P_disk=B A. The exact original head formulas in the [selected local certificate](actual_augmented_plat_selected_local_certificate.md) give, for image flag z and kernel flag w, U_phys=(z-w)/(z-w+1), T_phys=(z-w)/(4wz+3w+z+1), Y_in=-w/(z+1), Y_out=Y_in^(-1). (3) First use the low adapter U_phys=U,T_phys=T. Directly solving (3), with delta=U/(1-U), gives the two pairs Delta=U(T+1-U)/T=-U^2 W/T, w=(-1 +/- sqrt(Delta))/(2(1-U)), z=w+delta. (4) The marked exponential arguments in (1) imply U!=1 and U!=T. Equation (2) gives Delta!=0. Thus (4) defines two distinct global analytic pairs of finite flags on P. Their actual normalized prefix triple is (a_0,a_1,a_2)=(1,-1/U,1/T). (5) The strict physical criterion applies to this triple throughout (1): the canonical physical wire coordinates are nu and tau-nu. The proved real determinant-pencil argument therefore puts z,w on the same OPEN side of the real disk circle. Neither flag can reach that circle along either analytic branch. In particular no unrecorded passage through infinity changes its side; infinity itself belongs to the forbidden circle. For the actual high adapter one instead has T_phys=1/T, U_phys=U/T. Its physical wires are 1+nu-tau and 1-nu. Both are in the canonical strip, and the total has the required high degree. Crucially, U_phys(T_phys+1-U_phys)/T_phys=Delta. (6) The same discriminant gives the two analytic flag pairs, now using 1-U/T in the denominator. This denominator is nonzero. Their physical triple (1,-T/U,T) is, up to a common nonzero factor and exchange of the outer terms, the triple (5). Hence the same open-side conclusion holds. The full tube P is connected. At any central base point, the original source calibration already proves selected input means both flags below the incoming real circle, and selected output means both flags above its own real circle, in BOTH adapters. The source characteristic has no collision on P, and the flag branches have no collision or circle crossing. Continuing that calibration proves throughout P selected input iff Im z<0 and Im w<0, selected output iff Im z>0 and Im w>0. (7) Each line uses that factor's own actual disk normalization. This proof continues the selected root, not the old pointwise test Re sqrt(W)>0. ## 3. From actual strips to all good factors At a complete coupon, the primitive collar gives C=I+b(P_disk+I), with Im b<0 and b-epsilon/2=1/tau_cusp. In eta(s)=1/(2s+1), eta(C s)=eta(s)-2b. Consequently (7) is equivalent, at any STRICTLY PHYSICAL input/output pair, to the same two actual strip tests as before: 0<Im eta(w)<-2 Im b, 0<Im eta(W_prefix v)<-2 Im b. (8) The exact based-prefix dictionary of the right-angled localization identifies these with its common shaded-exterior flags. Choose its prescribed failed facets to be the two ends of e. Every other factor then has strict physical support AND the required oriented strip side. Equations (7),(8), proved on the larger tube, make each of those factors source-selected. This is the extra conclusion that the earlier central-domain theorem could not provide. There are finitely many factors, so their strict margins have a common positive lower bound after fixing this frame. Small neighborhoods of their actual low/high coordinates have compact closure in P. Apply the full packet on those neighborhoods, uniformly for its allowed actual integer channels, and multiply a fixed finite number of estimates. For an algebraic geometric certificate the frame may be chosen algebraic, as in the prescribed-pair theorem. This does not turn the selected logarithmic action into a root-only polynomial evaluation: its original logarithmic characters and finite-source normalization remain specified. ## 4. Exact exceptional block and limits of the conclusion Both exceptional factors are kept together on e. The marked block theorem bends its actual operator K_a by the original physical cups, recouples through EVERY target g=0,...,d, and writes its whole-source first normal as Taylor coefficients of order at most two after clearing the possible simple poles. It retains the original circle weight and half-twist phase. The native row weight and physical cup scale introduce no exponential loss. Its explicit target and complement costs J_g,J_C are still part of that theorem's bound; they are not removed by the present geometric localization. The full packet also supplies the actual small-channel fixed generic jet bounds and the near-fold partner-normal upper bound on these SAME complex compacts. In its notation, for fixed r and s=l-j, |D^r C_j/C_j| <= C_r N^(8r), |w_(j,l)/C_j| <= C N^8(C N^16)^s, s<=eta N. (9) Here D=q d/dq, and the derivatives in the numerator are generic-q derivatives evaluated at the root; the denominator is the ordinary root column. Constants depend on the chosen compact, and every channel is still an actual integer. For a fixed number of good factors, the additional partner-normal loss is exp(O(sum s_i log N)). It is subexponential when each s_i log N=o(N). A fixed nonzero scaled separation is not covered by that inference. These are upper bounds, not a nonzero confluent amplitude. The separate all-physical lattice jet theorem is not by itself a theorem for complex geometric totals. No global cycle, lower bound, nonzero completed saddle coefficient, or sharp estimate of the complementary contraction has been proved here. Nor have we made the entire factorization physical: its two necessary support defects remain, now in one exact block. The useful reduction is that all other ORDINARY factors have an actual selected physical packet, at arbitrary fixed plat width, while the exceptional block has an exact source-preserving expression with its boundary costs displayed. Focused audit: [exact new low/high flag identities](../experiments/audit_actual_augmented_plat_selected_factor_localization.py). It checks both adapters and all four flag branches: eight original-head identities, twelve actual prefix traces, three discriminant identities and four sheet-involution identities. These are new exact algebraic checks only; the outside-central finite-source comparisons belong to the separate full-physical packet audit. The square root is continued from the prescribed matching-edge pair, rather than chosen pointwise as a principal root. The local product theorem does not control the complementary contraction. The proof uses the prescribed-pair identity and the full physical packet; a numerical fixture alone cannot select the global frame or branch.

title: A finite certificate for the selected geometric principal phase
status: Finite selected-phase certificate; global contribution open
text: # A finite certificate for the selected geometric principal phase **Subsequent scope result (30 October):** the [right-angled obstruction and localization](actual_right_angled_selected_framing_obstruction.md) proves that no common all-central selected frame exists for the actual certified right-angled plat cut. Generic geometric strip flags have exactly two strict physical-support failures, at arbitrary bridge width. The local conditional statements below remain valid; their simultaneous realization in that right-angled class cannot supply the general proof. 30 October 2026. For any fixed augmented plat, of arbitrary width, this note gives explicit tests which identify the geometric stationary branch with the source-selected LOCAL q-Hahn principal action. It also expresses the endpoint sheet test as a condition on the two common framing flags. No intersection with the original finite summation cycle is inferred. The certificate has not been shown to exist for every positive geometric augmented plat. Its point is to replace an unspecified local branch-identification assumption by finite tests on the actual marked representation, with all input/output signs retained. ## 1. Data and the selected-critical certificate Fix the actual augmented-plat Morse word, retained half twists, and primitive peripheral marks. Supply: 1. An actual marked positive complete gluing certificate, as in [the geometric certificate theorem](../papers/marked-fillings/README.md). It gives the geometric representation, not an unrelated component of the character equations. 2. ONE rank-one projector Pi satisfying all the regular-chart, central-support and cup/cap tests of [the physical framing criterion](actual_augmented_plat_physical_framing_criterion.md). These include the original affine degree equations with the canonical wire logarithms and the actual low/high adapters. 3. The actual magnetic multiplier at each ordinary column factor. At an input it is Y_geo=S_1/S_2; at an output it is Y_geo=S_2/S_1. The momenta S are reconstructed from the original prefix matrices, not chosen separately to make a test pass. 4. The selected-root test in section 2 at every input and output, and the original logarithmic/Poisson characters of the full marked phase. The latter are retained as part of the certificate, rather than erased after exponentiation. These conditions imply the following LOCAL conclusion. The actual geometric critical germ is a germ of the source-selected principal phase. Modulo its two framing directions its magnetic Hessian is nondegenerate. Its fully marked critical action phi has d(2pi i phi)=1/2 sum V_i dU_i, 2pi Re phi(0)=Vol(Y_D), phi_(chi_i chi_j)(0)=pi i tau_i delta_(ij), (1) with U_i=-2pi i chi_i and the original primitive cusp shapes tau_i. Its ordinary q-Hahn column amplitude factors are nonzero. The conclusion concerns the actual marked phase and its ordinary column factors. It is NOT a full-source amplitude theorem, a bound for generic normal currents, a continuation of the finite discrete channel, or a claim that the original cycle contributes at this germ. ## 2. The local sheet test is algebraic on the marked cover Use the actual low coordinates tau,nu of each column, after applying the high adapter when required. Put xi=1/2, zeta=exp[pi i(tau-2nu)], c=-cos(pi tau), W=1+2c zeta, V=1+2c zeta+zeta^2. (2) Here W is a scalar, not a prefix matrix. In the central domain Re c>0, Re zeta>0. Both W/zeta and V/zeta have positive real part; hence W and V avoid the nonpositive real axis. In particular the principal square root of W has strictly positive real part. The [joint original-kernel theorem](actual_q_hahn_joint_complex_amplitude.md), section 7, gives the source-selected multiplier Y_sel=(zeta+i sqrt(W))^2/V. (3) For the actual geometric multiplier define r_geo=[V Y_geo-zeta^2+W]/(2i zeta). (4) The actual Casimir characteristic equation says r_geo^2=W. Therefore Y_geo=Y_sel if and only if Re r_geo>0. (5) This is an equality test for the selected root, not just a test that both values solve the characteristic polynomial. The source theorem fixes the square root by its actual center phase and finite-source continuation. All expressions in (2)--(5) are algebraic after retaining the marked square root of T=exp(2pi i tau). Its argument is pi Re tau in (pi/2,pi), which fixes the square-root sign; zeta=T^(1/2)/U with U=exp(2pi i nu). Thus for an algebraic marked representation and projector the endpoint root test is a finite real-algebraic test. The logarithmic characters of the action remain additional marked data, not a consequence of squaring (4). ## 3. Exact flag formulas, including the output sign and high adapter Normalize one actual incoming pair to A=-[[1,1],[0,1]], B=-[[1,0],[-4,1]], P=B A, H=P+I. Write Pi=v ell, ell(v)=1. In these disk coordinates let w be the kernel flag of ell and let z be the image flag W_prefix v. This use of the actual prefix is essential. Normalize the local rank-one matrix W_prefix Pi by its trace; it has image z and kernel w. In affine coordinates a representative of the local common frame is g=[[1,-w],[1,-z]]. Direct substitution into the original head and prefix formulas gives U_phys=(z-w)/(z-w+1), T_phys=(z-w)/(4wz+3w+z+1), S_1/S_2=-w/(z+1). (6) The source internal root in a low column is obtained from the actual inverse, at J=-1, Z=-U[y(T-U)+(1-U)]/[-y(T-U)+T(1-U)]. (7) For the input use y=S_1/S_2; for the output use its RECIPROCAL. Equations (6),(7) give Z_in,low=(2w+1)/(2w-1), Z_out,low=(2z+1)/(2z+3). (8) For the high adapter one must first replace T_low=T_phys^(-1), U_low=U_phys/T_phys. Keeping the same actual input/output momentum convention in (7) then gives Z_in,high=-(2z+1)/(2z+3), Z_out,high=-(2w+1)/(2w-1). (9) These are rational identities, not deductions from a root-only symmetry. They retain the output sign of a kernel and the actual high-degree translation. ## 4. The endpoint selected sheets are oriented disk sides For any strict central triple, its two local framing flags z,w are on the SAME open side of the real disk circle, by section 5 of the physical framing criterion. The two roots of the local characteristic give the two opposite choices of that side. One can see the latter directly from (6). Fix U_phys,T_phys and put d=U_phys/(1-U_phys)=z-w. The equation for w is quadratic; its roots have sum -(d+1). Consequently its two flag pairs are related by (z,w) -> (-w-1,-z-1). (10) They therefore lie on opposite sides of the real circle. There is no collision or boundary crossing in the central domain. For example T+1-U cannot vanish there: arg T is in (pi,2pi), arg(1+T) is strictly between arg T and 2pi, while the strict physical U argument lies between 0 and arg T. The other regular root denominators are excluded by the regular-chart assumptions. The simple characteristic and the connected central domain preserve the two sheet labels. At a strict physical real point, the actual selected internal root Z is in the upper half of the unit disk, as proved by the original q-Hahn selection theorem. Equation (8) then gives w below the real circle for an input, and z above it for an output. Equation (9) gives the SAME respective side choices in the high adapter. Together with the same-side necessity, continuation through the central domain therefore proves the equivalent tests selected input <=> Im z<0 and Im w<0, selected output <=> Im z>0 and Im w>0, (11) where each line uses that factor's OWN actual disk normalization. The inequalities in (11), rather than an upper-half-disk assertion for Z at arbitrary complex parameters, are what continue globally. They agree with (5); either supplies the same endpoint sheet test. ## 5. A global strip-intersection question remains For one actual complete coupon its transport is C=I+bH. The primitive mark fixes b-epsilon/2=1/tau_cusp, so Im b<0 for the positive geometric orientation. In the incoming disk coordinate set eta(s)=1/(2s+1). Direct substitution gives eta(C s)=eta(s)-2b. The incoming condition in (11) becomes Im eta>0; the outgoing condition, in the disk frame C^(-1), becomes Im(eta+2b)<0. Thus, CONDITIONAL ON the strict central inequalities, both input and output are selected exactly when 0<Im eta(w)<-2 Im b, 0<Im eta(W_prefix v)<-2 Im b. (12) This is the actual oriented region between the two developed disk circles. Positivity of the primitive cusp orientation gives its positive height. It does not prove that all such regions meet. Let Omega_f denote this region in the one global flag sphere, using the actual input disk normalization at coupon f. Formula (12) gives the necessary separated global conditions w in intersection_f Omega_f, v in intersection_f W_f^(-1) Omega_f. (13) Once the coupled central tests also hold, (13) is sufficient for ALL endpoint local sheet tests. This is a finite geometric version of the certificate. It identifies the precise role of the actual prefix pullbacks; independent local flags do not establish (13). No general identification of these intersections with exteriors of polyhedral face disks is asserted here. Such an identification would need the actual based words and both disk copies, as well as the coupled central inequalities. The common-product feasibility lemma in the preceding framing note concerns support only; it does not by itself supply these selected input/output sheets. ## 6. Proof of the certificate and precise persistence The sheet test identifies each actual geometric magnetic multiplier with the selected local multiplier. The regular inverse (7) then identifies its internal root with the source-selected root, including the high adapter. The original full coupon phase, its factorial measure, external phases and marked cap characters are retained. Fixing the stipulated logarithmic/Poisson characters gives the actual marked principal phase, rather than merely its exponentiated equations. The [critical-scheme inverse](actual_augmented_plat_critical_scheme.md) now identifies this germ with the actual marked geometric representation germ modulo the diagonal scale. The positive multi-cusp gluing rigidity theorem makes its only magnetic null directions the two framing directions. A transverse framing slice therefore has nondegenerate magnetic Hessian. The same theorem's classical action corollary, using the primitive collar differential and the absolute endpoint regulator, gives exactly (1). No new period normalization is introduced by the test. The joint column theorem gives, for actual integer channels with real xi_N=j/N near 1/2, the nonzero ordinary amplitude fhat=N^(-1/2) B_(xi_N)(tau,nu) exp[N Phi_(xi_N)(tau,nu)](1+O(1/N)). A fixed finite product of such ordinary factors has the product estimate on a compact common domain. This supplies nonzero ordinary column amplitude germs at the certified branch; it supplies neither generic normal-factor estimates nor a full-source saddle coefficient. All strict central inequalities and (5) persist under small marked peripheral deformation. The unramified geometric germ and transverse critical slice then continue the certified CLASSICAL selected branch. The selected coefficient functions also continue holomorphically in xi near 1/2. This applies to sufficiently long geometric fillings, with their original primitive marks. It does not continue the finite discrete index j to a complex value or justify a channel contour. The remaining global tasks are substantive: produce the certificate for a broad geometric class, control all required normal currents, and prove that the original finite cycle has the required contribution and global exponential bound. This note resolves none of those tasks merely by having a stationary point with the correct volume. Audit: [exact original-head, adapter and strip identities](../experiments/audit_actual_augmented_plat_selected_local_certificate.py). The certificate distinguishes classical continuation from a finite-channel or whole-source asymptotic. Its general existence and the existence of a contributing cycle are not established here.

title: The actual braided residual-framing current
status: Actual finite framing current and source-preserving boundary weights
text: # The actual braided residual-framing current 30 October 2026. After a legitimate coherent functional fixes the first cut, the actual Hopf adjoint gives an exact current in the second cut. Its coefficients are two routed OFF-DIAGONAL bands of the original tensor. They are not reconstructed from the diagonal two-cut array. The identity holds at arbitrary width, with actual finite endpoints and every genuine quantum jet. This is a finite-source integration-by-parts identity. Its closed flux is zero; no nonzero relative framing residue or selected global cycle coefficient is inferred from that fact. ## 1. The source, coherent first cut, and actual generic generators Use the [braided source adapter](actual_braided_two_cut_source_adapter.md). Fix d=N-1 and zeta=q0 exp(epsilon). At the two actual Morse cuts let V=V_d^tensor b, W=V_d^tensor c, with b,c>=1, and let A:W->V and B:V->W be the original covariant maps. Original cups, caps and all scalar/peripheral factors remain in A,B. The partial closure P_V uses the actual generic pivot g=(-1)^d K on the closed heads. Let U be the recorded braid carrying the chosen W head to its first position. Thus in the parallel convention U=R_1...R_j, with R_j acting first. Define the WHOLE band operator C_(p,q)=P_V[A U^-1(E_pq tensor I)U B], J_(a,l)=(C_(l,l))_(a,a). (1) Indices outside 0,...,d are zero ACTUAL matrix entries. No Fourier wrap or continued endpoint is substituted for that zero. By actual integer degree conservation C_(l,l) is diagonal, although the nearby band operators in (1) need not be. Closing the identity cut gives sum_l C_(l,l)=z(epsilon)I. For t distinct from 0,1 put beta_a(t)=binom(d,a)t^a(1-t)^(d-a), e_t=beta(t) 1^T, Tr e_t=sum_a beta_a=1. (2) This is the existing coherent boundary functional with w=1 and z_coh=t/(1-t). It is source-preserving on the WHOLE exposed scalar: Tr(e_t zI)=z, exactly, including the fixed d=N-1. It is not an additional normalized state on the second identity edge. All formulas below also hold for any specified quantum-independent vector beta of sum one; (2) is the legitimate coherent localization used here. Write the actual generic generator entries as k_a=zeta^(d-2a), f_a=1-Q^(a+1), 0<=a<d, e_a=zeta^(-N)(1-Q^(N-a)), 1<=a<=d, Q=zeta^2. (3) Their missing endpoint arrows are ZERO. In particular f_d=e_0=0 as matrices, even though the untruncated expressions in (3) need not vanish there at generic zeta. The Hopf adjoints are ad_K C=K C K^-1, ad_E C=[E,C]K^-1, ad_F C=[F,C]+K^-1[K,C]F. The residual combination is D_c=ad_F-ad_E-2(ad_K-I). (4) Its proved principal framing field is partial_r in the actual F(r,s) chart, with the first cut clock A_cut=(1+s)^-1 fixed; see [the actual Ward fields](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_borel_ward_cut_contraction.md). Multiplication by s gives s partial_r. We do not identify a finite translation with this infinitesimal field merely from its symbol. ## 2. A source-defined flux using the two neighboring bands For 0<=a<d define L_a=f_a beta_a+(e_(a+1)/k_(a+1)) beta_(a+1), L_-1=L_d=0. (5) Define the actual band pairing and its second-head flux by T_t(p,q)=Tr(e_t C_(p,q)), M_l=f_l T_t(l+1,l) +(e_(l+1)/k_(l+1)) T_t(l,l+1), 0<=l<d, M_-1=M_d=0. (6) Every C_(p,q) contains the full U and U^-1 and all original contractions. In particular (6) is not a choice of interpolation for J. The source identity is M_l-M_(l-1) =sum_(a=0)^d (L_a-L_(a-1)) J_(a,l) =sum_(a=0)^(d-1) L_a[J_(a,l)-J_(a+1,l)], 0<=l<=d. (7) Here is a direct proof. Generic pivotal partial closure is an exact Hopf-adjoint map, and A,B,U intertwine the actual coproduct. Therefore applying D_c to C_(l,l) is the same as replacing its inserted E_ll by the corresponding adjoint in W. Since E_ll commutes with K, the spectator terms cancel, and the inserted matrix is exactly f_l E_(l+1,l)+(e_(l+1)/k_(l+1))E_(l,l+1) -f_(l-1)E_(l,l-1)-(e_l/k_l)E_(l-1,l), (8) tensored with the spectator identity and conjugated by U. Its pairing is the left side of (7), with all four bands and their actual order. On the first cut the dual rows are, literally, e_(t,K)=K^-1 e_t K-e_t, e_(t,E)=K^-1 e_t E-E K^-1 e_t, e_(t,F)=e_t F-K F e_t K^-1. The K row has zero diagonal. Direct multiplication gives (e_(t,F)-e_(t,E)-2e_(t,K))_(a,a) =f_a beta_a-f_(a-1) beta_(a-1) -(e_a/k_a) beta_a+(e_(a+1)/k_(a+1)) beta_(a+1) =L_a-L_(a-1). (9) Only these diagonals pair with C_(l,l). This proves the first equality in (7); finite summation by parts gives the second. The proof applies to rectangular A,B and arbitrary fixed width. It uses the actual routed bands, not a scalar Ward operator assigned to an unrelated residual index. For clarity, the generic interior coefficient in (5) is e_(a+1)/k_(a+1)=zeta[Q^(a+1-N)-1]. At the root (5) becomes L_a=(1-Q^(a+1))[beta_a-q0 beta_(a+1)]. This shorter root formula must NOT be differentiated as the generic current: the omitted term is zeta Q^(a+1)(Q^-N-1) beta_(a+1), whose first derivative at zero is -2N q0 Q^(a+1) beta_(a+1). Equation (5) retains it and all higher genuine derivatives. ## 3. Finite-head integration by parts, with the interval ends Let R_l denote either expression on the right of (7), and let h_l be any specified finite-head weight. On EVERY actual subinterval 0<=L<=R<=d, sum_(l=L)^R h_l R_l =h_R M_R-h_L M_(L-1) +sum_(l=L)^(R-1)(h_l-h_(l+1)) M_l. (10) In particular a window's two current ends are retained. On the whole head interval the actual endpoint arrows make M_-1=M_d=0. For h=1 this says sum_l R_l=0. It also follows from sum_l J_(a,l)=z and sum_a(L_a-L_(a-1))=0. Neither proof says that the current has zero period on an arbitrarily selected relative subchain, or that one of its two ends contributes nontrivially. The identity is generic before any specialization. It may be differentiated to any fixed quantum order, with the derivatives of the actual U, inverse route, generator entries, pivots, coupons and any moving h retained. The same holds for a specified finite sum of channel assignments with its original coefficients. The original closed normalization remains F=D_N z and z(0)=F'(0)/nu_N, with D_N=(-1)^d[N]_zeta. No extra derivative per band or per vertex is introduced by (7). ### The complete Fourier endpoint of the same actual channel At completeness let S be the cyclic physical-head shift and X_j its original Fourier projectors, (X_j)_(r,s)=Q^[j(s-r)]/N, eta_j=Q^j, j mod N. For the ROUTED first-slot channel C(X)=P_V[A U^-1(X tensor I)U B], the [complete Fourier source theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/universal_resonant_fourier_source_completion.md) applies: A U^-1 and U B are still actual covariant maps. Thus C(X_j)=z X_j. Its proof uses the actual root adjoint equations and C(I)=zI and also applies to the rectangular maps above. Since 1^T X_j=delta_(j,0)1^T, the legitimate first coherent functional still gives Tr(e_t C(X_j))=z delta_(j,0), exactly for every t. The actual cyclic generator formulas give D_c X_j=(eta_j-q0 eta_j^-1+2)X_j +(q0^-1 eta_j^-1-2)X_(j+1)-Q^-1 eta_j X_(j-1). (10a) Consequently this SAME sourced residual current has the exact three-node Fourier endpoint distribution Tr[e_t C(D_c X_j)] =z[(3-q0)delta_(j,0)+(q0-2)delta_(j,N-1) -delta_(j,1)]. (10b) Overlapping labels are added when N=2. The total of (10b) is zero. It is a statement about the original complete root source, not its generic normal, and no off-root cyclic endpoint is added. It locates the current at the complete resonance rather than at regular-node principal samples. Its coefficient remains the UNKNOWN whole scalar z; homogeneous Ward equations alone cannot determine it or show that the selected geometric component survives there. ## 4. The specified moving-period realization and its boundary chain There is a source-preserving residue realization of the coefficients in (6), not a new interpolation of those finite values. Expand their original generic tensors, including the routed crossings, in the specified finite white/cup/cap presentation. For U and U^-1 this is the FULL generic spectral expansion of each original crossing, with both small and large partner channels and their actual spectral denominators. It is not the restricted regular complete-circle sector sum. Use the actual large white polynomials and moving-period factorial with P=pi i/Log zeta. Keep every fixed generic spectral scalar and every integral character; clear a known intermediate scalar pole before taking the required higher jet. This is the source class of the [actual tensor connection](actual_tensor_source_finite_jet_connection.md). For each admissible assignment and each off-diagonal band retain its own primitive affine head lattice and original finite support. The band source has a fixed integral charge offset. At every allowed integer point its moving-period coefficient is the actual generic matrix entry. Its small product-cotangent torus therefore gives that same entry. Summing those tori reproduces T_t(p,q), and the displayed combinations reproduce M_l and (7), with no omitted normal. An original constant forbidden stratum remains zero rather than being assigned a 0/0 continuation. The first head may be left as the exact finite coherent sum (2). There is no need to invent a meromorphic interpolation of beta_a. For the remaining free coordinates x of an individual band let S(epsilon,x) be its specified meromorphic summand, Gamma its actual ordered residue cycle, and c(x)=product_j pi cot(pi x_j). For an integral translation v and an analytic retained weight w, change of variables gives the EXACT chain identity integral_Gamma c w (S_v-I)S =integral_Gamma c (S_-v w-w)S +integral_(Gamma+v-Gamma) c (S_-v w)S. (11) All periods use (2pi i)^(-n_free). The only fact used about c is its integer periodicity. When the last cycle difference is filled by an allowed annular chain, its value is the sum of the actual crossed source residues, with their orientations. All other crossed divisors, and any remaining relative ends, stay in that formula. At a coincident source/cotangent pole one must use the full finite part and complement derivative, as in the [actual degree-wall theorem](actual_matching_edge_degree_cycle_boundary.md). It is not enough to multiply a cup's simple residue by an assigned geometric scalar. Equation (7) is proved AFTER the original finite internal period contraction. The subsequent [common-band theorem](actual_matching_graph_common_band_ward_current.md) supplies its meromorphic interior Ward assembly on one primitive free-head lattice, with the actual charged insertions and full routed source. Its different original support cycles are still retained. Equation (10) keeps the exact finite-head ends of this contracted current, and (11) transports EACH specified band summand with those cycle differences. These formulas do not replace Gamma+v by Gamma merely because the source has a moving-P quasiperiod. The latter has its nontrivial rational gauge, characters and divisors even at finite normal order. ## 5. The literal source between Fourier nodes The actual routed channel has more information than its cyclic samples. Its genuine integral source preserves UNWRAPPED integer charge: if an inserted matrix is supported on row minus column equal to n, its output has that same charge. This follows before root specialization from the original crossings, cups, caps and typed degree equations. The fixed weight differences of rectangular A and B cancel. A bare root K-eigenvalue, which would identify n and n+N, is not used here. Put T_n=sum_(r-s=n)E_rs, with -d<=n<=d. Then X_j=N^-1 sum_n eta_j^(-n)T_n. Separating the DISTINCT output matrix diagonals in C(X_j)=zX_j proves C(T_n)=zT_n, -d<=n<=d, X(p)_(r,s)=p^(r-s)/N, C(X(p))=zX(p), p in C*. (12) In fact the j=0 identity suffices. X(p) is a specified finite rank-one matrix, not an interpolation assigned to contracted source values. Every physical position and every unwrapped band remains. Pairing with the same first coherent functional (2) gives exactly Tr[e_t C(X(p))]=z b_N(t,p), b_N(t,p)=(1-p^N)/[N(1-p)] (1-t+t/p)^(N-1). (13) The factor at p=1 is its removable value one. This formula follows by separately summing p^r and beta_s p^(-s), so it keeps the actual coherent degree d=N-1 and the original p=eta^-1 orientation. Whenever b_N(t,p)!=0, dividing THIS specified functional by b_N returns exactly the original root scalar z. This licenses that finite band-momentum boundary family; it does not license a general second diagonal functional or simultaneous evaluation of two heads. There is an exact whole-source absorption of this insertion. Let H=C(I)=P_V[AB]=zI, with the original pivots and all other source factors. Equation (12) gives Tr[e_t C(X(p))]/b_N(t,p)=Tr[e_eff H], e_eff=e_t X(p)/b_N(t,p), (e_eff)_(a,c)=beta_a(t)p^(-c)/(1-t+t/p)^d. (13a) Thus the right side is evaluated on the original white-cut network, without the extra U and U^-1 insertions. This is an identity AFTER the whole root contraction, not a local rule for moving X(p) through one crossing or moving a bare mark. No pivot has been added or removed. Moreover e_eff is exactly the existing normalized coherent kernel with z_coh=t/(1-t) and w=p^-1. Put D_p=diag(p^a). Directly, D_p^-1 e_eff D_p=e_(t_eff), t_eff=t/[p(1-t)+t]. (13b) The [original common diagonal gauge](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/compact_framing_gauge_and_boundary_residue.md) preserves t_eff and removes this common momentum p. Its one-cut physical map forgets the residual centralizer coordinate. Therefore the absorption supplies no additional pin of that coordinate: the two apparent parameters are one coherent position and the already present common diagonal gauge. The canceled formula for e_eff may extend across a Fourier zero of b_N, but this is not a generic-q removal of that zero or a contour transport statement. The source therefore has an exact boundary-scale test. In the first-slot chart r=1/(1-p)-b0 s, retain c0=b0 s and set p_N=1-1/(N rho+c0). For rho in a fixed compact subset of C*, and t,c0 in fixed compacts, direct expansion of the FINITE factor in (13) gives b_N(t,p_N)=rho(1-exp(-1/rho))exp(t/rho)+O(N^-1). (14) The error is uniform and absolute, including its limiting zeros. On a compact avoiding those zeros it is relative, and b_N and its inverse have bounded size for large N. At the exact Fourier nodes p=Q^-j, j!=0, (13) instead vanishes exactly. Their limiting positions rho=1/(2pi i j) are precisely the zeros in (14). At rho=infinity the displayed limiting factor tends to one. No pointwise substitution of p into the whole internal source is used to prove these facts. In the absorbed one-cut expression, t_eff=t+t(1-t)/(N rho)+O(N^-2). Thus this scaling gives a small coherent-position tilt, not an independent centralizer condition. All of (12)--(14) is ROOT-ONLY. For the original moving-q channel write Delta(epsilon,p)=C_epsilon(X(p))-z(epsilon)X(p). Although Delta(0,p)=0, its genuine first quantum derivative need not vanish. The focused original-matrix checks below exhibit nonzero derivatives, including after the coherent pairing. They retain the actual route, endpoint arrows and generic pivot. Thus differentiating (13) would discard a source term. If a quantum-dependent p is used, the additional p derivative of Delta(0,p) is zero; it does not remove the genuine defect. All required normals still use the original generic channel and the source currents (5)--(11). More explicitly, for the SAME actual generic A,B,U and pivot, the identity retaining every quantum correction is Tr[e_t C_epsilon(X(p))]/b_N =Tr[e_eff H_epsilon]+Tr[e_t Delta(epsilon,p)]/b_N. (14a) Every genuine jet differentiates the full right side. The second term cannot be discarded by the root absorption (13a). Equation (14) is a matching condition for any proposed contracted hard-edge calculation. Its coefficient is the UNKNOWN whole z. Local nonzero white packets do not determine how their transverse periods and charged support cycles reproduce that coefficient. ## 6. What covariance fixes in the genuine normal There is an exact freedom at every N. Write tau_e(X)=Tr(g_e X), D_e=tau_e(I), with the original generic pivot, and put B_e(X)=D_e X-tau_e(X)I. (15) Cyclicity of trace gives tau_e(ad_E X)=tau_e(ad_F X)=0 and tau_e(ad_K X)=tau_e(X) for the actual adjoints above; I is invariant. Thus B_e is a regular covariant channel, made from the straight channel and pivotal evaluation and coevaluation. It has B_e(I)=0. At the root tau_0(T_n)=0 for every unwrapped band, including T_0=I since D_0=0. Adding c(e)B_e therefore preserves C_e(I)=z(e)I and every root identity (12), for any holomorphic c. Nevertheless the constant diagonal of X(p) gives EXACTLY B_e(X(p))=D_e[X(p)-I/N], B'_0(X(p))=nu_N[X(p)-I/N], Tr[e_t B'_0(X(p))]=nu_N[b_N(t,p)-1/N]. (16) Except at the displayed zeros, this changes the retained coherent normal without changing z. This is freedom in the linear span of actual covariant tensor channels; it does not assert that every such linear combination is a single connected augmented plat. For the original routed channel, charge conservation also implies that Delta(e,p) has zero diagonal at every e: its charge-zero input is I/N and C_e(I)=z(e)I. A diagonal first functional consequently kills this defect, but also kills every nonzero off-node band. That is a zero constraint, not a determination of a boundary coefficient. The freedom is visible in an exact family of connected source words. At N=2 retain q as the generic quantum parameter, eta=q^(1/2) with eta_0=exp(pi i/4), and the original positive crossing and pivot R=eta Rhat, Rhat=[[1,0,0,0],[0,0,q^-1,0], [0,q^-1,1-q^-2,0],[0,0,0,1]], g=diag(-q,-q^-1), D=-q-q^-1. (17) These are the d=1 specialization of the original highest-weight R and pivotal closure. For any odd k>=3 choose A=R^(k-1), B=U=R. The actual routed channel is C_k(X)=ptr_g[R^(k-2)(X tensor I)R^2], C_k=eta^k Chat_k, z_k=eta^k zhat_k. Set lambda=-q^-2, u_j=sum_(r<j)lambda^r and v_j=1-u_j. The middle block of Rhat has roots 1,lambda, so its kth power is u_k times that block plus v_k I. The two literal pivotal terms of Chat_k(E10) are -q u_(k-1) and -q^-3. It follows that zhat_k=-q-q^-1 v_k, psihat_k=Chat_k(E10)_(1,0)-zhat_k =(q^-1-q^-5)u_(k-2), Chat_k(X)=(zhat_k+psihat_k)X-psihat_k tau_q(X)I/D. (18) For the last formula, the actual generic adjoint module End(V_1) splits as C I plus ker tau_q; the latter is generated by E10 and its E-adjoint ladder and has dimension three. Equivalently (18) follows by multiplying the displayed middle-block powers. Its apparently singular quotient denotes the regular literal source. Since tau_q(X(p))=D/2, the actual defect is exactly eta^k psihat_k[X(p)-I/2]. At q=i, zhat_k=-ki, psihat_k=0, partial_e psihat_k=-4i(k-2), [partial_e Delta_k(E10)]_(1,0)/z_k(0)=4(k-2)/k. (19) Here Delta_k(E10) means C_k(E10)-z_k E10. The Cartan factor eta_0^k is restored in both numerator and denominator; its derivative multiplies psihat_k(i)=0. Any retained nonzero regular exterior framing scalar has the same cancellation in this ratio. The ratios are 4/3 for k=3 and 12/5 for k=5. In particular C_5-(5/3)eta_0^2 C_3 has root scalar zero but nonzero extreme-band normal (-16i/3)eta_0^5. Both individual words are original connected odd two-braid closures with the same cut, pivot and route. For t=2/3,p=2, b_2=1 and the paired defect is HALF the extreme-band coefficient, giving ratios 2/3 and 6/5 instead. Covariance does identify the extra datum. For ANY regular covariant N=2 channel with C(I)=zI and the root identities (12), the same generic adjoint decomposition gives (18) with a scalar psi vanishing at the root. Since D'_0=-2i and g_0[0,0]=-i, C_0(E00)-z_0 E00=-psi'_0 I/2, Delta'_0(X(p))=psi'_0[X(p)-I/2]. (20) Thus this normal is determined by an additional ROOT open-diagonal source period, not by the whole-source scalar z. More generally the defect is independent of the regular covariant lift when the FULL root channel is fixed. Suppose C_e and Ctilde_e use the SAME actual generator family and fixed highest weights, are regular covariant, preserve unwrapped charge, and C_0=Ctilde_0 as maps on End(V_d). The quotient L_e=(C_e-Ctilde_e)/e is then regular, covariant and scalar on I. The proof in Sections 3--4 of the [universal root theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/universal_resonant_fourier_source_completion.md) applies to this quotient: it uses only linearity, root adjoint covariance and L(I)=zI. Our actual root generators are precisely its M=1 generators, with BOTH missing endpoint arrows zero. Its K row, highest-input E recurrence and physical F induction therefore give L_0(X_j)=(z'_0-ztilde'_0)X_j; its Fourier-row basis gives the full matrix identity. No realization of L_e as one closed word is needed. Unwrapped charge separates the T_n as in (12), so Delta'_0(p)=Deltatilde'_0(p). (21) This requires equality of the whole open root map, not merely its scalar closure, nor equality of individual small/large root columns. Equations (15)--(21) rule out determining it from covariance and root absorption alone. They neither refute the hyperbolic conjecture nor show that the additional period cannot be controlled on the selected geometry. ## 7. The remaining equation at the framing diagonal The new ingredient relative to the old formal Ward ideal is the source-defined M_l in (6), including the off-diagonal routed bands and its finite endpoint chain. Its principal D_c field is the residual centralizer direction. A stationary pushforward would have to send THIS current and THIS chain, with the coherent first head and original complement, to the residual framing current. In particular neither the finite values J_(a,l) nor the nonzero local stationary density determine the residue at the framing diagonal. No continuous second-head current has been defined by interpolating (7). To obtain the desired framing coefficient one must identify the pushforward of the prescribed band periods (6) and the endpoint/divisor chain (10),(11) with that diagonal current, and compute its actual relative coefficient. A global cycle or nonzero endpoint intersection is not proved here. The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_braided_residual_framing_current.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_braided_residual_framing_current_results.json) check 19 actual braid/complete-circle sources, including rectangular one-to-three-head birth/death cuts: 326 original routed band value/first jet coefficients, 134 flux coefficients, 334 weighted interval/jet identities, and 48 nonzero retained generic-normal corrections. Separate original-matrix checks verify 1177 full Fourier-projector channel entries and 67 three-node complete current values. The off-node extension checks 2087 unwrapped Toeplitz entries, 801 literal rank-one source entries and 57 coherent pairings. It retains 588 nonzero genuine first-normal entries and 54 nonzero coherent normal defects. Twelve boundary-scale checks include a limiting Fourier zero. The whole-source absorption has 114 actual root/first-jet checks and 801 effective coherent-gauge entries; 139 symbolic kernel identities, 139 gauge identities, six trace normalizations and the first position tilt are checked independently. The genuine-normal extension additionally checks the literal N=2 crossing and pivot jets, the factorized arbitrary-k channel identity, and the full generic channels, restored normal ratios and open-diagonal adapter for five odd braid powers. These finite checks accompany the all-k block-power proof (18), rather than replacing it. Symbolic checks verify the universal integer-shift chain rule and its resonant cotangent finite part. They do not audit an off-grid Ward identity or a stationary framing pushforward. Finite currents, off-grid Ward identities and a geometric period are distinct levels of the argument. The off-node result concerns the finite rank-one source, unwrapped charge and root boundary profile. It does not determine z, differentiate its root factor, or select a transverse period. The absorption identities (13a),(13b),(14a) reduce the whole source to the existing one-cut coherent family; they do not independently localize the residual framing direction. Freedom in the normal tensor span is distinct from freedom among two actual connected words. Independence of a lift is not determination by a scalar root coordinate, and no geometric-period obstruction follows.

title: A braided second-cut co-source with its actual pivotal weights
status: Exact braided change of cut with genuine pivotal derivatives
text: # A braided second-cut co-source with its actual pivotal weights 30 October 2026. finite-source theorem. The literal second identity cut cannot be replaced by another normalized boundary state, or even by an untransported pivotal marginal. There is an exact repair: retain the actual braid carrying the selected wire to the exposed position. Its conjugated matrix-unit insertion gives a second co-source for the SAME whole marked scalar. The original pivot, all exchange bands, and all genuine quantum derivatives remain explicit. This is a global finite-source identity. It does not prove that this co-source has a nonzero coefficient on the selected geometric framing fiber, or replace the two-cut tensor by simultaneous point evaluation. ## 1. The genuine generic source and its original first cut Fix N, d=N-1, q0=exp(pi i/N), and zeta=q0 exp(epsilon). Use the original ordinary highest-weight-d module and the ACTUAL generic physical cup. Its pivotal matrix is g(epsilon)=(-1)^d K(epsilon), g_a(epsilon)=(-1)^d zeta^(d-2a), D_N(epsilon)=Tr g=(-1)^d[N]_zeta. (1) At the root this is the original K^(1-N), on every physical index. Away from the root the latter frozen power is a different germ. In particular the derivative in (1) is (d-2a)g_a, not (1-N)(d-2a)g_a. All assertions below use (1). Take an actual parallel physical level with b ordered heads and write the cut word as A B, with matrices composing right to left. Cups and caps elsewhere are their original maps. On the complete source use the regular Hopf lifts of its root complete-circle sectors, or the proved exactly equivalent literal polynomial presentation WITH all its moving scalar adapters. A bare root-value substitution is not a generic lift. Let G=g tensor ... tensor g, P(C)=Tr_(heads 2,...,b)[(I tensor g tensor ... tensor g)C]. The exposed endomorphism is H=P(A B)=z(epsilon)I. This follows from the actual generic Hopf covariance and the distinct K weights and nonzero interior F arrows. Its root marked value is z(0), while the ordinary closed source is F=Tr(G A B)=D_N z, z(0)=F'(0)/nu_N, nu_N=2N(-1)^N/(q0-q0^-1). (2) This is the same original exposed mark and trace normal as in the [full source theorem](general_matching_graph_full_normal_source.md). The retained exterior normalization and peripheral factors multiply both sides; they are not changed here. The formulas also apply at an actual Morse level after transporting its oriented objects with their literal duality maps. A braid route between different ordered boundary objects then includes those maps. The following displayed parallel-head formulas specify the simplest case; one must not replace a typed route by an unclocked permutation. ## 2. What the literal second identity cut does not satisfy Insert E_bb on a chosen intermediate wire and keep the original first cut open. With the second index renamed j to avoid confusion with the number of heads, set J_(a,j)=[P(A E_jj^(slot) B)]_(a,a). (3) Summing the actual identity edge gives sum_j J_(a,j)=z, (1/N)sum_(a,j)J_(a,j)=z. (4) It follows that the first head can be fixed at ANY actual physical a0, giving z=sum_j J_(a0,j), with no new scalar. But the column sums need not be constant, and multiplying the first index by g_a does not fix that defect. The old exposed marked row is not a Hopf cap on an arbitrary partially summed tensor. For a concrete exact example, use the original three-positive-crossing two-strand word at N=3, cut after its first crossing and select its second wire. In the audit's cyclotomic field F_1009, with every original pivotal factor retained and the common exterior scalar omitted on both sides, its row sums are (227,227,227), while its column sums are (758,555,377). With g=(374,1,634), its pivotal column sums are (903,221,894). Thus neither proposed second marginal is a source identity. These examples only distinguish the formulas; the correct identity is proved next at every generic parameter and every level. ## 3. The actual braided projector and its two exact marginals Number the selected wire by j=0,...,b-1. Let R_i be the actual generic crossing between slots i-1 and i. Choose the recorded route U=R_1 R_2 ... R_j, U^-1=R_j^-1 ... R_2^-1 R_1^-1. (5) Thus R_j acts first and the selected wire moves left one position at a time. A different specified signed braid route is allowed with its literal inverse; the route is data. Every crossing and its full scalar is retained. Put X_l=U^-1(E_ll tensor I)U, J^U_(a,l)=[P(A X_l B)]_(a,a). (6) The X_l are actual mutually orthogonal idempotents with sum I. They are GENERALLY NOT local matrix units on the selected wire. Their full exchange and prefix bands are indispensable. The universal identities are J^U 1=z 1, g^T J^U=z g^T. (7) For the first, sum X_l=I and use H=zI. For the second define C_new=U B A U^-1. It is an actual Hopf intertwiner, so P(C_new)=z_new I. Every factor commutes with the total pivot G. Cyclicity of the FULL ordinary trace therefore gives D_N z_new=Tr(G U B A U^-1)=Tr(G B A)=D_N z. Cancel the nonzero generic function D_N before root specialization. Both open endomorphisms are regular, so z_new=z through epsilon=0. For each l, the same trace calculation now gives sum_a g_a J^U_(a,l) =Tr(G A X_l B) =Tr[G U B A U^-1(E_ll tensor I)] =g_l z. (8) This proves (7) with the actual order of U and its inverse. It uses the whole closed trace, not movement of a bare root mark. Since g_l is always a unit, it supplies the exact second co-source z=g_l^-1 sum_a g_a J^U_(a,l) (9) at any physical l. The original first-cut source remains z=(1/N)sum_(a,l)J^U_(a,l). The formula is valid for arbitrary fixed complete-channel assignments and their finite sum, with their original signs and scalar weights. Differentiating it retains the actual U, U^-1, g and coupon derivatives; no unproved generic normal is suppressed. The two cuts need not have the same Morse width. More generally let V=V_d^tensor b and W=V_d^tensor c, with b,c>=1, and use the actual rectangular covariant maps A:W->V and B:V->W. The selected route U and X_l act on W; use P_V in (6). Covariance gives G_V A=A G_W and G_W B=B G_V. The entire trace step is then Tr_V(G_V A X_l B)=Tr_W(G_W B A X_l). The ordinary partial closures P_V(A B) and P_W(U B A U^-1) are scalar on the same exposed simple object. Cancelling the SAME generic D_N proves (7)-(9) unchanged. This includes actual intervening births and deaths, with their original cups, caps and typed duality transport; it introduces no new pivot on the second identity edge. At the root g^T1=D_N(0)=0. Thus (9) is an essentially canceling pivotal co-source, not another positive normalized row. Equations (7) do not determine the individual entries of J^U: perturbations Z satisfying Z1=0 and g^T Z=0 remain. This kernel has dimension (N-1)^2: it is precisely Hom(C^N/span(1),ker(g^T)). It cannot be removed by two independent point evaluations. ## 4. Root characters and the change of cut-density line There are two distinct continuations to complex magnetic indices. The finite generic matrix pivot in (1) is defined on physical integer a. The specified actual CUP continuation instead gives, by its literal ratio p_d(a,d-a)/p_d(d-a,a), ghat(epsilon;a)=(-1)^d exp(2pi i a) zeta^(d-2a). (10) It agrees with (1) at every physical integer a and every epsilon. At the root, for complex a, it is exactly the marked literal power q0^[(1-N)(d-2a)]. Consequently ghat(0;a)/ghat(0;l) =exp[2pi i(a-l)] A_l/A_a, A_a=exp(2pi i a/N), A_l=exp(2pi i l/N). (11) A_l is the clock of the new FIRST head after the recorded braid U; it is not automatically the clock of the old bare selected wire. The integer-linear character is one on the physical grid, but not on a continued complex magnetic chart. Nor may the root power in (11) be differentiated as if it were the generic cup germ (10). This distinction is independent of the matrix identity (8). The actual geometric cut forms have the corresponding algebraic line transition: writing the conjugation-invariant form on the ordered-flag surface as Omega=-Tr(Pi dPi wedge dPi), their fixed-cut forms are Omega_cut,i=-A_i Omega. Their ratio is A_l/A_a. Thus the algebraic factor in (11) is exactly the expected change of cut-density line, WITH its source character still present. This does not identify the whole continued tensor, its integration cycle, or its boundary residues merely from equality of that ratio. ## 5. Remaining fiber and source problem The braided correction (6) is a concrete finite source operation; it neither normalizes away the kernel in (7) nor supplies an asymptotic bound for that kernel. Its added routes are actual matrices and may carry substantial magnetic growth before contraction. A geometric framing reduction must still transport this entire co-source, including the exchange bands, into the residual centralizer fiber and its original relative ends. The nonzero unit g_l^-1 in (9) is an exact normalization of the whole scalar, not a proof that a particular local geometric block survives this functional. Existing two-cut current identities retain the relevant band and endpoint data; no replacement by a trace-one state on the second identity edge is made. The focused [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_braided_two_cut_source_adapter.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_braided_two_cut_source_adapter_results.json) check 16 original braid/complete-circle sources at parallel widths two and three, 476 actual adapted entry value/first-jet coefficients, and 116 weighted column value/first-jet coefficients. They also retain the failed literal second marginals, check the original generic crossing intertwiners and their inverses, and verify the whole-source trace normal. These finite checks supplement the generic proof; they do not test a geometric fiber integral. These identities do not assert that the selected geometric fiber survives contraction with the retained co-source.

title: Complete ordinary-cap trees have one positive angle-simplex energy
text: # Complete ordinary-cap trees have one positive angle-simplex energy 29 October 2026. An arbitrary binary tree of the original ordinary-cap reassociation packets contracts exactly. Its internal factorials telescope, its actual phases remain explicit, and its full squared kernel is ONE positive angle-simplex weight. After its known row normalization the complete boundary packet is a coisometry; overlaps between any two such normalized cap trees are contractive. This holds at arbitrary fixed width, including all endpoint indices and arbitrary adjoining tensors. This is a constructive boundary contraction theorem. It does not say that a knot's interior operator preserves these source packets, that complete-channel Racah matrices are contractive, or that the remaining marked cap is an ordinary cap. No new whole-knot volume estimate follows from this theorem alone. ## 1. The literal node and its source type Use N>=2, d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, x=-q^-1, F_a=(Q;Q)_a, s_a=|F_a|, and the physical gauge B_a=N^(1/4)/sqrt(s_a). Let A=(C'_23)^(-1)C'_12, with the original finite Euler maps. The [proved original pivotal-cap identity](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_pivotal_cap_reassociation_angle_packet.md) uses ellhat=sqrt(N)ell, where ell is the LITERAL original ordinary cap including its pivot. Its gauged map Khat=(ellhat_12 tensor I)A is Khat_(n;(a,b,c)) =delta_(b,d)delta_(n,a+c<=d) q^[a(n-N-1)] sqrt(w_d(a,c,d-n)), w_d(i,j,k)=1/(s_i s_j s_k). (1) The b=d selection is the result of the COMPLETE pivotal q-Pascal sum, not a discarded input channel. In the ungauged physical coordinates and with the literal ell the same node is Kraw_(n;(a,b,c)) =delta_(b,d)delta_(n,a+c<=d) N^(-1) p(a) F_n/(F_a F_c), p(a)=(-1)^a Q^[a(a-1)/2]. (2) The original Cartan/framing/peripheral lines on any exterior are unchanged. Equation (2) uses x=-q^-1; the full unreduced meridian factors in the local theorem must instead be retained off completeness. ## 2. A source-exact complete tree, with every phase retained Choose any planar binary tree T with l>=1 ordered leaves. Its original physical input has 2l-1 heads: l active leaves, and one separator head between each two successive leaves. At an internal node, first contract its left and right subtrees, then apply the three-head node (1) to their two outputs and the original separator between them. Each separator is used once. These are ordinary compositions of the specified actual maps. Every nonzero input has ALL l-1 separator indices d. If the active indices are a_1,...,a_l, its root index is n=sum_i a_i<=d. Conversely every such input is allowed: all intermediate subtree sums are at most n. There is exactly one intermediate root index at every node. Therefore no unperformed internal summation or cyclic alias remains. For an internal vertex v write n_v for its subtree sum and n_L(v) for its left-subtree sum. The complete normalized-cap, quarter-gauged kernel is Khat_T(n;a_1,...,a_l; separators) =delta_(separators,d)delta_(n=sum a_i<=d) N^(-(l-1)/2) sqrt(s_n/product_i s_(a_i)) q^(Theta_T), Theta_T=sum_(v internal) n_L(v)(n_v-N-1). (3) Proof. Replace each square root in (1) by N^(-1/2)sqrt(s_(n_v)/(s_(n_L)s_(n_R))), using s_j s_(d-j)=N. Every internal s cancels between its output and its parent's input. The phases multiply to exactly the displayed sum. They have NOT been replaced by one, nor asserted to cancel on a cycle. There is an independent exact polynomial form for the LITERAL original cap tree before physical gauging: Kraw_T=N^(-(l-1)) F_n/(product_i F_(a_i)) product_(v internal) p(n_L(v)). (4) This follows by the same cancellation using (2), and specifies every original root phase. In particular it is not a norm-only construction. The literal gauged cap tree equals N^(-(l-1)/2)Khat_T: each use of ellhat in (3) restores its stated ell=ellhat/sqrt(N) factor. All input and output B gauges are explicit, and their internal inverse factors cancel under composition. No separator-state norm is silently substituted for its actual physical coordinate. ## 3. Exact positive simplex incidence and all-width energy By reflection, the squared surviving entry (3) is |Khat_T|^2=N^(2-l)/[s_(d-n) product_i s_(a_i)]. (5) Thus its true nonnegative integer charges are (a_0,a_1,...,a_l), a_0=d-n, sum_(i=0)^l a_i=d. (6) This is a bijection, not a relaxation: every composition in (6) is one allowed input/root combination of the complete tree. The internal subtree charges are its specified partial sums. All zero angles and zero-length slots are retained by s_0=1. Let E_(l,n)=N^(-(l-1))s_n sum_(a_1+...+a_l=n) product_i s_(a_i)^(-1). Different root rows have disjoint input-degree support, hence EXACTLY Khat_T Khat_T^*=diag(E_(l,0),...,E_(l,d)), ||Khat_T||_op^2=max_n E_(l,n), ||Khat_T||_HS^2=N^(2-l) Z_(l+1,N), Z_(m,N)=sum_(a_0+...+a_(m-1)=d) product_i s_(a_i)^(-1). (7) These quantities are independent of the binary tree. Equations (3)--(7) are an exact controlled contraction for the entire ordinary-cap tree, not independent Cauchy bounds at its nodes. For fixed l>=2 put Lambda(theta)=-integral_0^theta log(2sin t)dt. The uniform factorial estimate at ALL 0<=a<N gives log||Khat_T||_op^2=log||Khat_T||_HS^2+O(log N) =N (l+1)Lambda(pi/(l+1))/pi+O_l(log N). (8) Here the first equality follows directly from the N rows in (7). To prove the second, the continuum objective on (6) is sum_i Lambda(pi a_i/N). On the simplex of nonnegative angles summing to pi its unique maximum, for m=l+1>=3, is m Lambda(pi/m). For completeness its Hessian on the interior is -diag(cot theta_i). If all angles are below pi/2 it is negative on sum-zero vectors. If one angle exceeds pi/2, put S=sum of the other angles<pi/2. Weighted Cauchy and sum tan(theta_i)<tan S=-tan(theta_big) show the same strict negativity on the sum-zero tangent. Equality at pi/2 follows directly from the positive remaining cotangents. Thus the function is strictly concave; symmetry fixes its maximum at equal angles. Continuity includes the boundary. Rounding an equal composition to the integer sum d gives the lower bound at every sufficiently large level; there are only polynomially many compositions and all factorial errors are O_l(log N), giving the upper bound. No lattice progression is needed. For l=1 the map is identity, E_(1,n)=1, and its energy exponent is zero. There is a stronger UNIFORM root-conditioned formula. For every 0<=n<=d, including both endpoints, put t=n/N. Then log E_(l,n)=(N/pi)Phi_l(t)+O_l(log N), Phi_l(t)=l Lambda(pi*t/l)-Lambda(pi*t). (9) The constant is independent of n. For fixed sum of the l leaf angles, at most pi, the concavity argument just given places their maximum at equal values. The case l=2 at total pi may have additional maximizers, without affecting this value. For the lower estimate, distribute the integer n among l parts differing by at most one. Each angle changes by O_l(1/N), whose Lambda error is O_l(log N/N) uniformly even at zero or pi. There are at most (N+1)^(l-1) compositions. Applying the uniform factorial estimate to every term in E_(l,n), and to s_n, therefore proves BOTH sides of (9), with the stated uniform error. For l>=2 and 0<t<1 the explicit boundary action satisfies Phi_l'(t)=pi log[sin(pi*t)/sin(pi*t/l)], Phi_l''(t)=pi^2[cot(pi*t)-(1/l)cot(pi*t/l)]<0. (9a) Indeed x cot x is strictly decreasing on (0,pi), since its derivative has numerator sin(x)cos(x)-x<0. Its unique maximum is t=l/(l+1). Using Lambda(pi-theta)=-Lambda(theta), the maximum is exactly (l+1)Lambda(pi/(l+1)), giving (8). Formula (9) also includes a prescribed root tending to t=1, with rate l Lambda(pi/l)/pi. For l=1, E_(1,n)=1 and Phi_1=0 identically. ## 4. Exact coherent packet overlaps are contractive Every E_(l,n) is positive and known without a knot value. Define R_T=diag(E_(l,n)^(-1/2)) Khat_T. Then R_T R_T^*=I_N. Consequently P_T=R_T^*R_T is a specified orthogonal projection on the full physical input space, including its literal separator-d selection. For ANY two planar binary trees on the same ordered heads, R_T R_U^* is diagonal and ||R_T R_U^*||<=1. (10) The diagonal entry is the ACTUAL mixed phase sum of the two root rows, divided by E_(l,n); Cauchy proves its modulus at most one. This retains the off-diagonal leaf copies inside P_T and the full phases Theta_T. An arbitrary finite sequence of these packet overlaps is contractive. No artificial dephasing, ordinary positive pivotal trace or favorable choice of unknown source has been introduced. For a specified remaining row z on the root, its complete original boundary-functional norm remains exactly ||z Khat_T||^2=sum_n |z_n|^2 E_(l,n). (11) One may not drop these root weights, replace a marked row by an ordinary cap, or normalize z using an unknown period. For literal caps multiply the energies by N^(-(l-1)) as stated after (4). ## 5. What this gives for global gluing This proves a genuine positive angle incidence for a complete tree source: (6), including all its internal actual partial sums. It is a single angle simplex. It is NOT yet the edge/peripheral incidence of a knot ideal triangulation. The identity applies to arbitrary fixed width and to any polynomial or matrix exterior because it is an actual boundary-operator identity. The complete-channel Racah transition on an interior port has additional channels beyond these ordinary-cap packets. It is not the compression R_T R_U^*. Nor is an arbitrary interior R word proved to preserve P_T. The full marked packet in the local theorem must also remain. Thus (10) is a constructive boundary-tree overlap estimate; using it as a unitary or complete projection on an arbitrary knot interior would be an extra unproved step. The original full-source goal still needs the corresponding complete-channel or source-specific interior control. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_cap_tree_angle_energy.py): original coproduct-derived reassociation with the literal ordinary cap, all middle-index cancellations, exact complete tree q-factorial/phase formula, angle-simplex bijection, row energies, and coherent overlaps. The finite audit checks five levels of literal original cap/reassociation matrices and complete tree phases, and twenty all-tree-shape families checking metric kernels, positive simplex incidence, full mixed overlaps and retained arbitrary root co-sources.
