title: Complete augmented-link source normalization: no hidden exponential factor
text: # Complete augmented-link source normalization: no hidden exponential factor 29 October 2026. At the original boundary-parabolic complete color, the marked raw augmented-link period differs from its reduced zero-framed quantum/Kashaev evaluation only by a unit phase. The full one-cut ADO modified evaluation has the additional EXACT factor i^(N+3)/N. This is not an assertion about a generic meridian germ's size. It follows by retaining and then specializing that whole normalization germ and all actual turns. ## 1. Which scalar is raw, reduced, or modified Fix N>=2, d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, x=q^d and kappa=q^(d^2/2). The raw source here is the one in the [literal augmented pretzel diagram](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_odd_pretzel_augmented_transfer_source.md): every full physical crossing has its original common Cartan, the crossing circles are the exact auxiliary pivotal traces L_N, and the main component has k genuine cups, k-1 ordinary caps and ONE original marked cap. Their balanced entries are p_ab=Nx^(-b)delta_(a+b,d), ell_ab=x^a delta_(a+b,d)/N, m_ab=x^b/N^2. The [direct turn/source calculation](quantum_bridge_cap_source.md) proves that these are precisely the original left/right duality and the selected cut projector. Specifically, with g=K^(1-N), e=psi phi, psi_a=1,phi_a=1/N and D=g^(-1)e, \[ \operatorname{Tr}(gDC)=\operatorname{Tr}(eC),\qquad m p=1. \tag{1} \] Each cup contributes its actual N, each ordinary cap 1/N, and the single marked cap 1/N^2. Their net scalar is EXACTLY 1/N, the original cut average. There is no other cut normalization waiting outside this raw tensor contraction. Balanced factorial changes cancel by exact basis covariance on every internal wire; their potentially exponential condition numbers are never estimated as an external scalar. At completeness the original twist is \[ \theta_d=q^{(d^2+2(1-N)d)/2}=q^{-d^2/2}=\kappa^{-1}. \tag{2} \] Therefore any recorded change from the actual diagram's framing to the chosen component framings is a product of integer powers of theta_d, and has modulus one. For a braid normalization using total writhe w it is theta_d^(-w)=kappa^w. If individual component self-framings are prescribed instead, their difference from this convention is a linking/framing character, again a unit phase. Mutual crossings are not silently called self-writhe; only the modulus statement is independent of that convention. Let A_raw be the actual tensor scalar and F_red the reduced zero-framed evaluation with the same chosen marked component. With its explicitly recorded framing character zeta_(N,L), \[ F_{\mathrm{red}}(L)=\zeta_{N,L}A_{\mathrm{raw}}(L), \qquad |\zeta_{N,L}|=1. \tag{3} \] This applies to the original auxiliary-circle diagram before or after its exact finite L_N contraction. Each closed auxiliary circle uses an ORDINARY pivotal trace already in L_N, with no added1/N, no division by its zero quantum dimension, and no extra modified dimension attached to it. Modifying every component independently would define a different normalization from the original one-cut source. ## 2. The modified dimension is specialized as a WHOLE germ At fixed root q, use the original meridian M=-q q^alpha=e^u, so alpha=d+u/Log q. The given modified dimension is \[ d_N(\alpha)=-q^{N(1-N)/2} \frac{q^{\alpha+1}-q^{-\alpha-1}} {q^{N\alpha}-q^{-N\alpha}}. \] Substitution, retaining both numerator and denominator, gives the whole specified local meridian germ \[ d_N(e^u)=i^{N+3}\frac{\sinh u}{\sinh(Nu)},\qquad \boxed{d_N(1)=\frac{i^{N+3}}N.} \tag{4} \] This is a removable value, not a cancellation of two separately evaluated zeros. The full one-cut modified invariant, by its original definition, is d_N(M) times the reduced selected tangle scalar. Consequently \[ \mathcal N_N(L;M=1)=\frac{i^{N+3}}N F_{\mathrm{red}}(L), \qquad |\mathcal N_N|=\frac1N|A_{\mathrm{raw}}|. \tag{5} \] There is ONE such factor, on the marked component. The other components were closed by the ordinary trace in section 1. No claim about q-transverse derivatives is made: (4) is the actual meridian germ at a fixed root, not a substitution of a generic-q ordinary pivot for the full modified source. Equations (3)--(5) prove, in the respective two normalizations, |chi_red|=1, |chi_full|=N^(-1), (1/N)log|chi_red|=(1/N)log|chi_full|+log(N)/N=0. In particular the previously unspecified common external chi_N has zero exponential rate at THIS complete pointing. It need not have polynomial size on an arbitrary moving peripheral germ. ## 3. The enhanced Kashaev comparison extends to a link The original comparison note states its conclusion for knots. The local matrix identities used there also suffice for the present multicomponent source; no quotient-color argument is needed. Here is the missing connectivity check. Let a b-strand braid be colored by the full original V_N and close every head but the chosen first one with the actual pivot. The resulting cut matrix C commutes with E,F,K. This follows by partial trace of the explicit Hopf coproduct identities. For the K-pivot convention, tracing [A,E_prefix K_last+E_last] ordinarily over the last head yields commutation with E_prefix. For F, use K conservation and cyclicity to obtain Tr_last K_last[A,K_prefix^(-1)F_last]=0. Multiplying the original pivot by its complete scalar sign leaves this intertwining assertion intact. Repeating the argument closes all other heads, regardless of how many link components their permutation has. On the remaining V_N, K has N distinct weights and all internal F coefficients are nonzero. Thus C is a SCALAR matrix, at all even and composite N as well. Connectivity of the closed link was not used. The selected Tr(eC) is that scalar. The exact original Fourier/diagonal comparison in [the crossing calculation](kashaev_crossing_and_period_lattice.md) therefore works unchanged on this link cut. The large factorial similarities on traced factors cancel by cyclicity; the one on the open factor cancels because C is scalar. The local equality gamma alpha_q=alpha_K cancels all writhe factors. This compares the enhanced Kashaev period with the ordinary quantum-group enhancement with unknot value1, without any exponential gauge. To fix the dual/primal convention explicitly, the crossing note uses the dual pivot K^(-1). The original matrix B v_j=(-1)^j q^(j(j-N)) v_(d-j) in [the complete pointing comparison, section 2](kashaev_ado_pointing.md#2-exact-specialization-to-the-original-kashaev-period) intertwines that dual module with the primal one, conjugates its pivot to K, and satisfies R^T=(B tensor B)R(B^(-1) tensor B^(-1)). Those are direct generator and finite-crossing identities. The same full cut scalarity cancels this open-factor conjugation as well. Thus the primal K in the next display and the dual K^(-1) in the enhanced crossing comparison refer to identical scalar evaluations, with no additional normalization character. There is one useful sign when the latter is instead expressed with the ADO pivot/twist. At completeness g_ADO=(-1)^d K, theta_ADO=(-1)^d alpha_q. For a b-strand closure of total writhe w, the trace and framing ratios multiply to (-1)^(d(b-1-w)). If that closure has c components, its permutation gives w congruent to b-c modulo2. Hence \[ F_{\mathrm{red}}^{\mathrm{ADO}}(L) =(-1)^{d(c-1)}\langle L\rangle_{N} \tag{6} \] in those two explicitly specified enhanced-framing conventions. Other recorded choices of individual zero framings add only their already described unit twist character. In particular \[ \boxed{|\langle L\rangle_N|=|F_{\mathrm{red}}(L)| =|A_{\mathrm{raw}}(L)|.} \tag{7} \] For the odd-pretzel complete augmented diagram there is one main component and s genuine auxiliary circles, so c=s+1. The sign in (6) is (-1)^(ds); it is immaterial to the exponential rate but is not asserted to be one. The local full Cartan and the exact half-twist phases remain IN A_raw and in its proved leading constant. They are not counted a second time in chi. ## 4. What this closes, and its precise limit For the original one-cut enhanced Kashaev link evaluation, the full raw-period asymptotic has EXACTLY the same absolute value and exponential rate. For the full modified ADO evaluation it has the factor1/N and the phase in (4); its leading N-power must be adjusted accordingly. This closes the external normalization gate at the complete augmented source. It does not identify its action with a manifold volume without the geometric face-gluing calibration, and it proves no Dehn-filling or fixed-knot statement. The [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_complete_augmented_source_normalization.py) compares original enhanced Kashaev matrices, ordinary quantum matrices, and the actual ADO pivot/twist through full cuts of both knots AND multicomponent links. It checks scalarity, the component-dependent sign, and the entire modified-dimension germ. It does not replace a link by a knot on the basis of an invariant.

title: The actual complete circle as a positive face polynomial
text: # The actual complete circle as a positive face polynomial 30 October 2026. The complete ROOT circle, with its original weight and literal W/pi cup normalization, has an exact homogeneous polynomial factorization in its four face diagonals. For EVERY original folded channel that polynomial has nonnegative coefficients. Its local zeros enforce the original unwrapped channel support on a modular physical-head grid. Both level parities are included. This is local source algebra. The global face-grid measure, marked coefficient, stationary angle balance and original relative period are separate statements. ## 1. Exact local variables, lifts and scalar Put N>=3, d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, and keep an actual integer 0<=a<=floor(d/2). Write m=d-a, s=d-2a and beta_a=S_(2a)/S_a^2, S_j=product_(r=1)^j 2sin(pi r/N), k_a=1 if s=0, otherwise k_a=2. Let x,b,c,y be the outer, incoming-middle, outgoing-middle and final face diagonals, respectively. Choose their logarithms and use the literal centered physical heads S=d/2+N(Log x-Log b)/(2pi i), R=d/2+N(Log x-Log c)/(2pi i), sigma=d+N(Log x-Log y)/(2pi i). (1) The other physical heads are sigma-S and sigma-R. The auxiliary row is r=sigma-m, with its actual complement 2a-r. Thus Q^S=-q^-1 x/b, Q^(sigma-S)=-q^-1 b/y, Q^R=-q^-1 x/c, Q^(sigma-R)=-q^-1 c/y. The physical half-index and the auxiliary finite color are not confused. Define, using the original Hermitian matrices H_-,H_+, D_a(x,z,y)=det[z I+(x/2)H_-+(y/2)H_+], Ptilde_s(x,y)=product_(j=a+1)^(d-a)(x-Q^j y). (2) The empty determinants and products are one. Then the full coefficient of the specified regular root complete-circle source is EXACTLY h0_a W_a pi_a =k_a beta_a^2 D_a(x,b,y) D_a(x,c,y) Ptilde_s(x,y)/(bc)^(d/2). (3) This is the fixed-root Hopf lift from the [original source envelope](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_original_network_resonant_source_envelope.md), not a newly chosen off-grid continuation of a canceled exceptional kernel. A retained half twist multiplies (3) by its original fixed scalar omega_a^epsilon. Every power in (3) uses the logarithms in (1). If one adds literal N-lifts to R,S,sigma, the multiplier is (-1)^[d(n_R+n_S)]. The degree lift n_sigma cancels. It is identically one at odd N; at even N it must be retained or canceled by a proved global source-character calculation. Formula (3) makes no independent wrapping of an out-of-basis head. ## 2. Proof from the literal large white and cups At the root the actual white and dual are W_a(i,j;r)=(-1)^m q^[-dr+di-m(m-1)] H_m^1(Q^i,Q^j)/F_m, i+j=m+r, F_m=(Q;Q)_m, pi_a(r;i,j)=gamma_a^-1 p_(2a)(2a-r) W_a(d-j,d-i;2a-r)/[pV(d-j)pV(d-i)]. Here gamma_a=q^(2-a^2)/N^2 is FIXED, h0_a=k_a N beta_a, pV(z)=N q^(-d^2+dz), and no paired norm pi_a W_a is inverted. The exact Chevalley factor is W_a(d-j,d-i;2a-r)=q^[s(a-r)]W_a(i,j;r). Let T=Q^sigma and P_s(T)=product_(j=a)^(m-1)(T-Q^j). The exact root reflection of the SPECIFIED factorial section gives p_(2a)(d+a-sigma) =F_s q^[2m(d+a)] T^-a/P_s(T). (4) Indeed p_(d-s)(z)=F_s exp(pi i z)q^[(s-1)z] /product_(j=1)^s(1-Q^(z+j)); substitute z=d+a-sigma and retain exp(pi i z)=q^(Nz) literally. This proves (4) before canceling its possible poles. The root identities H_m=H_a P_s and H_a(U,V)=V^a K_a det[I-(qU/2)H_--(q^-1/(2V))H_+], K_a=q^(a^2) beta_a, are source-exact finite polynomial identities. For comparison with the previously normalized entire circle C_a, substitution in the preceding literal W/pi expression gives the same head factor q^[d(R+S-2sigma)]/P_s(T) as in C_a. Its remaining scalar ratio is one: use F_j=(-i)^j q^[j(j+1)/2] S_j, S_(d-j)=N/S_j. The ratio reduces to q^[-2N(-2N+a+3)]=1. This proves h0_a W_a pi_a=C_a as the specified meromorphic root functions, not just at physical nodes. It does not identify their moving-q germs with a different generic lift. Now use the exact original normalized coefficient C_a=k_a V_a(d-sigma) q^[d(R+S-sigma)-2a^2] H_a(U_o,V_o)H_a(U_i,V_i)/T^a, V_a(h)=product_(j=a+1)^m 2sin(pi(h+j)/N). On the logarithms (1), direct factorization gives V_a(d-sigma)=Ptilde_s(x,y)/(xy)^(s/2), H_a(-q^-1 x/z,-q^-1 z/y)=(-q^-1)^a K_a y^-a D_a(x,z,y), q^[d(R+S-sigma)]=(xy/(bc))^(d/2). (5) For the first identity, the scalar in the sine product is i^s q^[-sum_(j=a+1)^m j]=i^s q^(-sN/2)=1. The remaining powers of xy cancel because d=2a+s, and K_a^2 q^(-2a^2)=beta_a^2. This proves (3) with its exact scalar. The same formulas show that additional N-lifts contribute (-1)^[d(n_R+n_S)+(s-d)n_sigma]=(-1)^[d(n_R+n_S)], since s-d=-2a. ## 3. Coefficient positivity and homogeneity D_a is homogeneous of degree a in x,z,y and has NONNEGATIVE REAL coefficients. This follows directly from the actual positive matrices, without assuming their entries are real. Factor H_-=B_-B_-* and H_+=B_+B_+*, and apply Cauchy--Binet to the rectangular matrix [sqrt(z) I, sqrt(x/2) B_-, sqrt(y/2) B_+]. Its determinant expansion is a sum of squared absolute minors times the indicated monomials, hence has the claimed coefficients. Since all three source matrices I,H_-,H_+ are positive definite, every homogeneous monomial of degree a in the three variables in fact has positive coefficient: subtract a sufficiently small positive multiple of I from each matrix, then select the three identity parts in the same Cauchy--Binet expansion. This is a coefficient statement for each fixed N,a; no uniform lower coefficient bound is claimed. More strongly, the retained forced product has the exact positive expansion for EVERY original folded label: Ptilde_s(x,y)=sum_(j=0)^s [S_s/(S_j S_(s-j))] x^(s-j)y^j. (7) To prove it, multiply its finite linear factors, or induct on their number, to obtain the coefficient (-1)^j Q^[(a+1)j+j(j-1)/2] [s choose j]_Q. The exact finite Gaussian coefficient is [s choose j]_Q=q^[j(s-j)] S_s/(S_j S_(s-j)). The remaining q exponent is j[2a+2+j-1+s-j]=j(2a+1+s)=jN. Its factor q^(jN)=(-1)^j cancels the displayed sign. This proves (7), whose coefficients are strictly positive because s<N. It also retains both maximal-fold parities: Ptilde=1 at odd simple fold and Ptilde=x+y at even maximal fold. No quarter-channel restriction is needed. The numerator in (3) is consequently a homogeneous polynomial of degree 2a+s=d with nonnegative coefficients in the four face variables. The monomial denominator and all finite logarithmic carries are still part of the source. Evaluating some face variables at complex values does not preserve positivity of the resulting specialized coefficients. ## 4. Local modular support retains one forced zero Take physical heads i,j in {0,...,d}, sigma=i+j. In the original white the unwrapped auxiliary row is r=sigma-m, so its actual allowed range is 0<=r<=2a, equivalently m<=sigma<=d+a. (6) At U=Q^i,V=Q^j, every Newton summand of H_a has factors forcing k<=i and a-k<=j. Therefore H_a(Q^i,Q^j)=0 if sigma<a. Exact root complementation sends the pair to (d-j,d-i), proving the same vanishing if sigma>2d-a. The complete circle retains ONE factor P_s(Q^sigma) after (4) cancels one of the two factors from its large numerators. Hence: * If sigma<m, either sigma<a and the small numerator vanishes, or a<=sigma<m and the retained P_s vanishes. * If sigma>d+a, either sigma>2d-a and the complementary small numerator vanishes, or sigma-N belongs to [a,m-1] and P_s vanishes. These are zeros of the canceled entire root coefficient, not an assignment of a value to an unexplained 0 times infinity. Thus a modular auxiliary residue outside its original support is killed locally even though its individual continued channel cup may have a pole. If both physical pairs of a circle survive and their totals agree modulo N, both totals lie in the SAME interval (6), containing only 2a+1<=N integers. They therefore agree exactly. The auxiliary row is then the original unwrapped row. The complementary physical cup also adds no modular states: i+j congruent to d modulo N with 0<=i,j<=d forces i+j=d, since d-N<0 and d+N>2d. This local check supplies the missing support input for a possible global face-grid transformation. The global primitive measure, even-level coset and carry phases, original marked-cap monomial and coefficient-extraction identity still require their own proof. Focused audit: [literal circle, coefficients and support](../experiments/audit_actual_complete_circle_positive_face_polynomial.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_complete_circle_positive_face_polynomial_results.json). At 85 digits it checks 94 literal LARGE-white/dual/cup circle identities and 22 retained N-lift characters, with maximum source error below 4.6e-83. Independent continuant expansions check 79 original D polynomials and their 823 strictly positive coefficients; 522 forced-product coefficients check the all-label sine-binomial formula. Exact finite-field checks retain 6910 forbidden physical-pair zeros, 28211 circle zeros for unequal totals congruent modulo N, 5274 supported unwrapped pairs and 150 original physical-cup modular support identities. Three symbolic calculations check the phase, outer degree and centered mark exponents. No numerical global source transformation is asserted by this audit. The local modular support uses the one forced factor that remains after the cup cancellation. The global face grid, marked coefficient and exponential rate are separate from this local source statement.

title: The complete Fourier core and the actual marked geometric deformation
status: Selected core action on the actual marked geometric germ
text: # The complete Fourier core and the actual marked geometric deformation 30 October 2026. The exact complete-image Fourier core has the volume rate of the actual nearby marked geometric representation when its small external deficits are real. For complex deficits the explicit peripheral boundary correction is retained. The proof uses the established complex-core packet, common marked circle reconstruction and literal primitive-collar theorem. This note does not estimate the ordinary-color subset terms of the full mixed source or prove the long-filled knot limit. ## 1. The selected source critical point and its local peripheral data Fix any connected original certified augmented plat, with its actual main mark, all matching circles and retained half twists epsilon_i. No one-main-component restriction is imposed. Use the exact entire complete-image core and its [complex packet](../papers/casimir-source-asymptotics/README.md). Let chi_i=h_i/N denote its external deficit coordinates, and let S(chi) be the limiting selected critical action, with the explicit chi-independent exterior and maximal-channel phases still outside this normalized action. Set delta_i=1/2-mu_i for its internal channel coordinates. Its phase is sum_i[Q_bi(delta_i)+Q_ci(delta_i)] -sum_(finite faces) log l_f +pi i sum_i epsilon_i delta_i^2 +2pi i sum_i chi_i delta_i. (1) All Q terms retain their actual sine and forced-factor normalization. The [marked circle reconstruction](../papers/marked-fillings/README.md) proves that its face-stationary radii are the curvatures of one common analytic line-circle pattern, with the original two marked lines and all actual triangle incidences. Thus this is not a collection of independently framed local solutions. For each circle use its actual ordered input/output pairs and product P_i. The selected disk eigenvalue is J_i=-exp(-2pi i delta_i). (2) It is exactly the continuation of the actual internal node and selected line supplied by the marked-pattern theorem, including the two-line triangles. Let C_i transport the incoming pair to the outgoing pair, with C_i A_in C_i^-1=A_out and [C_i,P_i]=0. Normalize its eigenvalue on the J_i^-1 line to one, and denote its eigenratio by R0_i. The [primitive-collar theorem](../papers/marked-fillings/README.md) proves the ACTUAL primitive, corner-preserving identity R0_i=E_bi E_ci/D_i, Log R0_i(0)=0, (3) with the source-selected roots and the literal line-face limit. A doubled reflection between the two middle faces or the reciprocal flag is not a substitute for (3). The theorem identifies this C_i with the recorded even collar, including its common marked-line limit. Since partial_delta(Q_b+Q_c)=-Log(E_b E_c/D), channel stationarity of (1) is precisely Log R0_i-2pi i epsilon_i delta_i=2pi i chi_i. (4) With m_i=exp(-pi i chi_i), this says m_i^2 R0_i(-J_i)^epsilon_i=1. Every logarithm is its germ at the complete point, with the existing primitive marking; no integer shear or new linear action character is chosen. ## 2. All actual group relations, not only the local eigenvalues For the global assembly, for each actual white face f use its reflection R_f in the common circle pattern. For complex parameters this means the holomorphic complexification of the two reflection matrices R_f^+,R_f^-, with R_f^-R_f^+=I. It agrees with ordinary reflection at real parameters; one does not conjugate the complex deformation variables. At every original Morse slice let F_0,...,F_(2k) be its ACTUAL region sequence. Define the original prefix and raw physical heads by Q_j=R_(F_j)^+ R_(F_0)^-, H_j=R_(F_j)^+ R_(F_(j-1))^-. (5) These telescope: H_j...H_1=Q_j. Every main incidence remains tangent, so H_j has determinant one and trace -2; the physical main meridian is its recorded trace +2 lift. The same region labels on an unchanged physical wire give the same based head at its two ends. At an actual cup or cap the first and last regions agree, so the ordered pair product is I. This is the inverse-pair relation of the literal ordinary and marked closures, without replacing the unrestricted quantum mark. The two closure phases can differ by their retained integer character; that character has not been deleted from the action. Across a box the outer regions agree on its two sides. Thus the input and output products are the same P_i. The collar C_i in (3) gives their actual simultaneous conjugacy. For a retained half twist put h_J=J_i^-1-1, a unit near completeness. The original physical auxiliary meridian is the regular matrix M_i=m_i R0_i h_J^(-epsilon_i) C_i^-1(P_i^-1-I)^epsilon_i. (6) This is exactly the original collar/Hurwitz expression from [the literal Morse presentation](actual_augmented_plat_critical_scheme.md), section 4. Its selected J_i-line eigenvalue is m_i, while det M_i=m_i^2 R0_i(-J_i)^epsilon_i=1. It commutes with P_i. Its inverse followed by the recorded Hurwitz half twist induces C_i on the main pair. At the complete point it is the original primitive crossing-circle meridian, with its recorded SL lift; it is not a separately chosen centralizer eigenvalue. The relations just verified are ALL the original Morse/van Kampen relations: shared physical wires, inverse-pair cups/caps, the drilled box threading word [2,1,1,2], and the retained signed Hurwitz move. Their presentation was proved in section 5 of the same critical-scheme note from the actual diagram. It applies at arbitrary fixed width and with every actual matching-graph cycle. Thus (5),(6) construct a representation of the ACTUAL augmented link group, with every main meridian parabolic and all auxiliary meridians prescribed by m_i. No additional global cycle or generic frame is needed for this group identity. A regular common conjugate may be used to compare with the old critical chart, but no independently chosen local conjugates are introduced. At chi=0 this is the complete geometric representation by the original certificate and primitive collar calibration. The complete geometric representation is irreducible. The already proved positive marked gluing rigidity says that its nearby decorated representation germ, modulo one common conjugation, is uniquely parameterized by the actual cusp meridian logs. Fixing every main cusp log to zero leaves precisely the auxiliary coordinates in (4). Hence the constructed family is the selected marked geometric deformation, not another character component. ## 3. The exact peripheral action differential The primitive projective logs, centered at completeness, are U_i=2Log m_i=-2pi i chi_i, V_i=2Log(-J_i)=-4pi i delta_i. (7) Here P_i is the original ordered disk longitude, with the preferred peripheral convention already proved for the threading word. A half-longitude or an independently inverted flag would change (7) and is not permitted. The actual half-twist shear has already entered (4),(6). Envelope differentiation of the selected critical value in (1) gives partial_i S=2pi i delta_i, d(2pi i S)=(1/2)sum_i V_i dU_i. (8) There is no new order-N exterior color character in the original core: the exact color dependence is its prescribed finite cosine transform. The retained exterior framing unit and maximal-channel half-twist phases are chi-independent and stay in the analytic packet. Their constant phase must not be mistaken for a change of (8). At completeness the actual positive face coefficient and facet coning already prove 2pi Re S(0)=Vol(Y_D). The old correctly marked geometric action has the same differential (8) and the same absolute regulator anchor. Their holomorphic difference is therefore a chi-independent constant whose real part is zero. This fixes the exponential rate without assigning an unproved Chern-- Simons constant. All actual constant source phases remain explicit. For genuinely complex meridian logs, the boundary correction is retained. The [marked regulator identity](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/complex_peripheral_action_and_conversion_bound.md) with U=2Log M,V=2Log ell gives 2pi Re S(chi)=Vol(rho_chi) +(1/2)sum_i Re U_i Im V_i. (9) Main-cusp terms vanish because their U logs are identically zero. Equation (9) uses the continuously selected longitude arguments and the complete anchor; it does not say that the bare real action equals the incomplete representation volume at arbitrary complex chi. ## 4. An exact finite-polynomial volume limit Equations (1)--(9) identify the action of the ACTUAL fixed-complex-neighborhood core packet with the actual marked geometric deformation. The finite face torus and finite channel residue rectangle already specify that core period and its nonzero amplitude. No unknown geometric intersection coefficient remains for this complete-image term. In particular, for each fixed labeled certified diagram and retained half-twist vector there is a rho>0 such that, locally uniformly for REAL |chi_i|<rho, lim_(N->infinity) (2pi/N)log|F_N(N chi)| =Vol(rho_chi). (10) Here F_N is the EXACT finite cosine polynomial of the original complete-image source, not an interpolation chosen from its values. The limit includes both parities and all sufficiently large quantum levels. The right side is the volume of the selected actual geometric representation of the original marked exterior. No cone-manifold completion is asserted. Indeed U_i=-2pi i chi_i is purely imaginary on this real slice, so the correction in (9) vanishes. On the fixed complex polydisc the same limit is the right side of (9), including its correction. This follows directly from the locally uniform rate of the complex-core theorem; its nonzero relative packet supplies the needed absence of nearby zeros. ## 5. The selected algebraic peripheral germ There is also a finite algebraic description of the representation germ, distinct from its analytic action. Normalize the actual marked strip by H=1 and the fixed finite center by X_ref=0. For each finite circle retain its coordinates (X_f,Y_f,r_f). The marked reconstruction equations are polynomial in these variables and in I_i=-(J_i+J_i^-1)/2. (11) For example, a finite/finite edge has equation (X_f-X_g)^2+(Y_f-Y_g)^2-r_f^2-r_g^2-2I_e r_f r_g=0; the line equations are Y_f-r_f I_e=0 or 1-Y_f-r_f I_e=0. Main edges have I_e=1. These are equations over the rational Laurent field Q(J_1,...,J_R), with 3R-1 normalized circle variables and 3R-1 equations. The proved circle-variable Jacobian is invertible at the actual complete point. Hence its selected local algebraic component is smooth of dimension R, projects analytically locally isomorphically to the J coordinates, and is dominant and generically finite over them. Equivalently its function field is a finite extension of Q(J_1,...,J_R). This assertion is about the selected component; it does not assert that every fiber of the global polynomial system is finite. The source-selected E roots are algebraic as well. With x,y,b the actual curvatures, write z=sin^2(pi delta)=(2+J+J^-1)/4. Then E_b^2-2(x+y+2bz)E_b+[(x+y)^2-4xy z]=0. (12) Adjoin the selected square roots on their recorded germ and the roots M_i^2=[R0_i(-J_i)^epsilon_i]^-1, M_i(0)=1. (13) The nonvanishing denominators are localized at the units already proved for the actual collar. The displayed expression for C also contains the physical divisor J-J^-1, which is NOT inverted here: its divided difference is the regular germ proved by the literal three-point collar map. In particular R0-1 vanishes when J=-1 with the other parameters free, and the selected quotient extends through that divisor. Thus (5),(6) give an algebraic family of actual marked representations on a finite algebraic extension of the selected circle component. Its peripheral image is the selected algebraic germ with all main meridians M=1. The internal parameters are auxiliary longitude coordinates; they are not external finite channel labels. At completeness the eliminated circle solution is even in each delta, and the actual meridian-log Jacobian is partial U_i/partial delta_j =-2(c_i-pi i epsilon_i) delta_ij, c_i=pi(T_bi(0)+T_ci(0))/(x_i+y_i)>0. (14) Here c_i is a scalar radial coefficient, distinct from the collar matrix C_i. The Jacobian is invertible, so the auxiliary meridian logs are local coordinates on this same actual marked peripheral germ. This is a local A-variety statement with a specified branch and marking. It does not compute a global eliminated A-polynomial, give a scalar quantum A-operator, or assert that S is an algebraic number. The function S is the regulator primitive with differential (8). ## 6. The remaining full-source and filling distinction The exact finite packet still uses its N-dependent selected critical phase S_N and unit Hessian factor. Holomorphic convergence S_N->S does not by itself justify replacing N S_N by N S in a relative formula. The geometric identification here concerns the limiting action and its actual peripheral marking. The full external-color source also contains ordinary-color subsets. Their source-exact transport, possible degeneracies, exponential gaps and far-end cancellation have not been supplied by this identification. Consequently the arbitrary independently long signed-filling theorem remains separate. No knot family or allowed slope set is narrowed in order to replace those remaining requirements. ## 7. Focused verification The [source audit](../experiments/audit_actual_complete_core_geometric_deformation.py) has [saved results](../experiments/actual_complete_core_geometric_deformation_results.json). It checks literal global Morse region words at widths2,3,4: nine charts,436 prefix products,304 unchanged wire incidences and54 actual cup/cap words. These exact finite-field word checks assert the source algebra, not a new geometric certificate for those arbitrary diagrams. Separately, it solves the actual tetrahedral and octahedral white-sphere marked fixtures jointly with the source channel stationarity equations for12 real/complex external parameter vectors and retained half twists. The collar is then reconstructed from its two contact-point images and selected fixed flag, independently of the source formula for R0. The audit compares36 such collars,108 literal threading/Hurwitz relations, 36 primitive auxiliary eigenlogs,60 main parabolic edges and144 actual box/cup prefix products at60 digits. The largest relative residual is below1.7e-58. Two symbolic differential checks retain the primitive factor2 and the regulator boundary sign. The companion collar audit already checks the genuinely flipped finite compactifications and their marked-line limit; those checks are not replaced here. The algebraic-germ corollary follows from the proved Jacobian and finite-type equations, rather than from these numerical fixtures. The theorem concerns the exact complete-image core. title: When one shared positive Cauchy torus loses exponential accuracy
status: Analytical exponential loss of the optimal undivided bound
text: # When one shared positive Cauchy torus loses exponential accuracy 31 October 2026. The theorem concerns the full positive endpoint source on its shared face variables. It does not assert growth of the oscillatory invariant beyond volume. ## 1. The two different capacities Fix an actual certified simple-white marked plat with $R$ ports and $R$ ordinary faces. Keep its adjacent protected faces exactly zero. Set $h_f=\log L_f$ at ordinary faces and fix the common-scale gauge $\sum_fh_f=0$. Write $$ \begin{aligned} F(h)&=\sum_e X_e(e^h)-\sum_f h_f,\\ J(h)&=\sum_e H_e(e^h)-\sum_f h_f,\\ X_e&=Q(x_e,b_e,y_e)+Q(x_e,c_e,y_e),\\ H_e&=\max\bigl(\{X_e\}\cup\{\log b_e:b_e>0\} \cup\{\log c_e:c_e>0\}\bigr). \end{aligned}\tag{1} $$ The complete triangle theorem gives a unique minimizing gauge class $h^*$ for $F$, with $$ F(h^*)=\Phi_D=\frac{\operatorname{Vol}(Y_D)}{2\pi}.\tag{2} $$ In contrast, $H_e$ is the weighted rate of the **full** positive endpoint polynomial, as proved in the [closed half-block theorem](actual_fejer_half_block_entropy.md), Section 2. All variables in each expression are shared across the original ports. Zero protected variables are removed from the supported corner sets. **Theorem.** Both infima in (1) are attained on the scale quotient, and $$ \min_hJ(h)=\Phi_D \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad X_e(e^{h^*})\geq\log b_e,\ \log c_e \text{ for every positive middle}.\tag{3} $$ In particular, a strict failure of this nonstrict packing condition at one port implies $$ \min_hJ(h)>\Phi_D.\tag{4} $$ This concerns nonstrict balance in (3). Equality at a local target does not imply the strict condition used by the full filling theorem. ## 2. Coercivity from the actual triangle incidences Let $a^*_{tf}$ be the normalized complete triangle angles. Each row has sum $1/2$, every ordinary face has sum one, and every allowed ordinary corner is positive. A row with just one ordinary corner has its fixed value $1/2$. For a real ordinary-face vector $v$, define $$ B_\triangle(v)=\frac12\sum_t\max_{f\in t\text{ ordinary}}v_f -\sum_fv_f.\tag{5} $$ Using the face balances of $a^*$, (5) is the sum of nonnegative row differences between a maximum and a strictly positive weighted mean. Equality forces $v$ to be constant on the allowed corners of every row. The ordinary-face adjacency graph is connected: removing the two marked vertices from a simple triangulated sphere leaves a connected graph. Every remaining white edge occurs in an actual triangle row. Hence equality forces all ordinary values to be equal. On the unit sphere of the zero-sum gauge, $B_\triangle$ is continuous and strictly positive. Thus, for some $\kappa>0$, $$ B_\triangle(h)\geq\kappa\lVert h\rVert_2.\tag{6} $$ The triangle Legendre identity, evaluated at a vertex with zero entropy, gives $Q(e^{h_f}:f\in t)\geq\tfrac12\max_{f\in t}h_f$. Consequently $F(h)\geq B_\triangle(h)$, and $J\geq F$ is also coercive. Both are continuous, so both minima are attained. If the gauge has dimension zero, the same attainment assertion is immediate, and the argument below does not require (6). Uniqueness of the minimizer of $F$ can also be seen directly. On each supported row, the strictly concave triangle entropy has an interior maximizer at finite positive weights. Its Legendre potential is strictly convex in directions that are not constant on that row. Connectedness of the ordinary-face graph therefore makes the sum strictly convex modulo common scale. The actual complete angles give its critical point $h^*$. ## 3. Equality and strict loss Since $J\geq F\geq\Phi_D$, the nonstrict condition in (3) makes $J(h^*)=F(h^*)=\Phi_D$ and proves one direction. Conversely, suppose $\min J=\Phi_D$ and let $h_0$ attain that minimum. Then $F(h_0)\leq J(h_0)=\Phi_D$, so uniqueness forces $h_0=h^*$. Every term $H_e-X_e$ is nonnegative. Their sum can vanish at $h^*$ only if every positive middle logarithm is at most $X_e$. This proves (3), and (4) follows immediately. No local optimizers have been chosen independently and no minimax interchange is used. ## 4. Even level-dependent positive radii cannot remove this loss For even $N$, let $d=N-1$ and let $P_{e,N}$ be the original full positive Fejer endpoint polynomial. Define its exact positive Cauchy bound $$ \operatorname{Cap}_N= \inf_{L_f>0} \frac{\left.\prod_eP_{e,N}\right|_{L_u=L_v=0}} {\prod_{f\text{ ordinary}}L_f^d}.\tag{7} $$ The infimum permits arbitrary $N$-dependent radii. The uniform closed coefficient entropy theorem gives, uniformly on every compact set of ordinary logarithmic weights, $$ G_N(h):=\frac1N\log \frac{\prod_eP_{e,N}(e^h)}{\prod_f e^{dh_f}} \longrightarrow J(h).\tag{8} $$ This follows by finite positive Laplace summation: every local coefficient has its uniform closed entropy, the number of monomials is polynomial in $N$, and the supported rational grids approximate the compact simplex. The difference between $d/N$ and one is uniform on compact logarithmic sets. The exact weighted maximum is $H_e$, with its original normalization. There is no escaping-minimizer loophole in (8). Each allowed pure-face monomial has degree $d$ and logarithmic coefficient $o(N)$ uniformly over the finitely many vertices. Its coefficient entropy is zero. Keeping one such monomial at each port gives $$ G_N(h)\geq\frac dN B_{\mathrm{port}}(h)-\varepsilon_N, \qquad\varepsilon_N\longrightarrow0,\tag{9} $$ where $B_{\mathrm{port}}(h)=\sum_e\max_{f\in e\text{ ordinary}}h_f-\sum_fh_f$. The two triangle rows at each port show $B_{\mathrm{port}}\geq B_\triangle$. Thus (6) and (9), together with the bounded value $G_N(h^*)$, put all finite-level minimizers in one fixed compact set for sufficiently large $N$. At each fixed level coercivity also gives attainment. Compact uniform convergence now proves $$ \lim_{\substack{N\to\infty\\N\text{ even}}} \frac1N\log\operatorname{Cap}_N=\min_hJ(h).\tag{10} $$ Let $Z_N$ denote the actual original marked coefficient of this same positive product. The [complete endpoint theorem](general_fejer_endpoint_source_volume.md) gives $N^{-1}\log Z_N\to\Phi_D$. Combining with (10) yields $$ \lim_{\substack{N\to\infty\\N\text{ even}}} \frac1N\log\frac{\operatorname{Cap}_N}{Z_N} =\min J-\Phi_D.\tag{11} $$ At a strictly unbalanced complete packing this is a positive exponential loss in the best undivided positive Cauchy bound. It is not a claim of excess growth in the coefficient, which still has the actual volume rate. The statement is already decisive along even levels; no odd regularization is needed for this obstruction. ## 5. Consequence for the general strategy One cannot repair a strict packing imbalance merely by optimizing a single positive torus for the full endpoint product, even with radii depending on the level. The proved [anchored shared-radius theorem](general_anchored_shared_radius_filling_volume.md) avoids this particular loss by separating genuine source sectors first. It is not contradicted by (4) or (11). The [finite actual-sector cover theorem](../papers/planar-certificates/README.md) retains those common face constraints while permitting finer decompositions. A [certified original source](../papers/planar-certificates/README.md) shows that the anchored test itself is not universal, although a finer cover succeeds. The argument uses finite convex geometry, the original uniform local coefficient theorem and its actual endpoint volume calibration; it does not use a numerical optimizer as a proof.

title: Full-twist fillings of the positive Conway class remain links
text: # Full-twist fillings of the positive Conway class remain links 29 October 2026. The robust positive Conway grammar cannot produce knots by filling all its auxiliary circles with the existing integral FULL-TWIST kernel. If a compiled expression contains S occurrences of its seed A=h^3, every such filled diagram has at least 2S+1 main components. In particular the smallest seed still has at least three. This is a literal connectivity obstruction, independent of any asymptotic estimate or geometric deformation. It does not contradict the complete retained-circle volume theorem. It prevents presenting a future filling theorem for this unchanged class as a knot theorem. ## 1. The two internal circles in every seed The original unrotated complete circle L_N threads two through main arcs, with identity endpoint pairing. The genuine quarter-turn h=Rturn L_N has the planar U pairing: its two bottom main ports are joined to one another, as are its two top main ports. Stacking two U boxes creates one closed internal main component between the upper cap of the lower box and the lower cup of the upper box. It leaves U pairing on the four external ports. Therefore A=h^3 has exactly TWO closed internal main components and U external pairing. This is an actual tangle calculation, not a decomposition into quantum channels. A quarter-turn rotates a tangle and preserves all its already closed components. Stacking two tangles also preserves every closed component in each: identity wires are attached only to their exposed ports, so they cannot connect an existing closed component to another one. A stack can create additional closed components, but cannot destroy those present before it. Induction on E ::= A | Rturn E | E E consequently gives internal main components of E >= 2S(E), where S(A)=1, S(Rturn E)=S(E), and S(EF)=S(E)+S(F). Closing the four exposed ports adds at least one further main component. Hence every actual closed expression has c_main(E) >= 2S(E)+1. (1) Both cylindrical and cap closures satisfy this lower bound. All 3S(E) auxiliary components are counted separately. ## 2. The exact filling kernel preserves that connectivity The original auxiliary-color filling identity replaces a retained complete circle by the literal full twist R^(-2p), with p an integer, and its separately recorded scalar. A full twist has the IDENTITY permutation of its two main endpoints for every sign and magnitude of p, including p=0. Thus the replacement has the same main pairing as the original unrotated L_N. After the same physical quarter-turn, each replaced leaf has the same U pairing as h. All subsequent identity stacks, rotations and closures therefore have exactly the SAME main-component connectivity as the unfilled expression. In particular every one of the seed's two internal main circles persists after these fillings. If I is any subset of the auxiliary circles, the filled link has c_total(E,I)=c_main(E)+3S(E)-|I|, c_total(E,I) >= 5S(E)+1-|I|. (2) Filling every auxiliary component gives c_total=c_main>=2S+1>1. The threshold "sufficiently long" does not change this conclusion. Neither a sign choice nor arbitrarily large full-twist powers can change an even braid permutation into an odd one. ## 3. What a knot extension actually requires To reach knots one must change the original source topology, for example by retaining an ODD half-twist coupon at selected auxiliary ports before performing the full-twist fillings, or by using another seed whose exposed main connections can join these components. Such a change has its own exact quantum source. The present positive Newton coefficients and whole-source theorem cannot silently be reused after changing those coupons. The existing odd-pretzel knot construction does retain the required odd half twists, which is why its connectivity differs from the pure h grammar here. Volume invariance of an unmarked complete half-twist partner does not identify its finite quantum source or prove its long-filled asymptotic. The general complete Conway construction and any verified full-twist extension of it therefore provide a broad LINK theorem. A broad KNOT theorem remains a separate critical-path task. Audit: [literal pairings and full-twist permutation checks](../experiments/audit_actual_conway_full_filling_component_obstruction.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_conway_full_filling_component_obstruction_results.json). The proof of (1)--(2) is the all-expression component-preservation induction, not an extrapolation from the finite samples. Every seed has two permanent internal main circles. Turns and stacks preserve them, and full-twist filling has the identity endpoint permutation. Thus the resulting link-only scope is a topological fact, independent of source asymptotics.

title: Original crossing layers: a punctured Casimir norm torus and its parabolic limit
status: Exact local characteristic and norm-torus transport
text: # Original crossing layers: a punctured Casimir norm torus and its parabolic limit 30 October 2026. This is derived from the ACTUAL homogeneous root crossing kernel and its coefficient composition. It solves the local classical transport for every integer power. It does not prove a selected finite-cycle contribution, a kernel norm bound, a knot A-polynomial identification or a filled-volume limit. Throughout N>=3,d=N-1,q=exp(pi i/N), hbar=2pi i/N. Fix the original outer face variables x,y and put A=x+y,P=xy,f(z)=(z+x)(z+y). The letters P and sigma below are not new quantum parameters. The generic algebra is over characteristic zero with xyA nonzero; all source divisors explicitly recorded below remain excluded. ## 1. The exact original kernels and their composition The [frozen homogeneous theorem](../papers/filling-bounds/README.md) gives the original coupon polynomial H_F(x,b,c,y), homogeneous of degree d. For literal polynomials F,G in the SAME pair Casimir, including their full repeated-node data, H_FG(x,b,c,y)=[z^d] H_F(x,b,z,y) H_G(x,z,c,y). (1) Indeed H_G is the matrix of G on input monomials c^j, and H_F is the matrix of F on their output powers z^j. The coefficient condition t_left+i_right=d is exactly matrix multiplication. There is no extra N or mark factor in (1). If F,G are at different original ports, (1) does NOT assert that they commute or share one Casimir. For epsilon=+/-1 the full original crossing is R^epsilon=lambda0^epsilon r_N^epsilon(Omega), lambda0=q^(d^2/2), with the original square-root lift. The normalized homogeneous coefficient at x^k b^i y^l c^t, i+k+l+t=d, is exactly (-1)^(k+l+1) q^[epsilon(kl-(i+1)(t+1))] N/(S_i S_k S_l S_t). (2) No Hermite derivative has been replaced by nodal values. Formula(1) therefore gives R^n with its EXACT lambda0^n for every integer n, including negative n. All original cups, caps, physical endpoint zeros and marked face targets remain those of the homogeneous theorem. Write normalized simplex variables I,K,L,T with sum1 in the leading limit. The principal phase of (2), INCLUDING lambda0, is E_simplex + I Log b+K Log x+L Log y+T Log c +pi i(K+L)+epsilon pi i(KL-IT)+epsilon pi i/2. (3) Here E_simplex=(Lambda(pi I)+Lambda(pi K)+Lambda(pi L) +Lambda(pi T))/pi on its recorded continuation. The finite source is still (2), with i+k+l+t=N-1; its order-one phases and finite offsets are not discarded by using (3) for a principal characteristic. ## 2. Both signs and the actual input/output convention At a regular critical point of (3) put E_I=exp(2pi i epsilon I), and similarly E_K,E_L,E_T. Taking the three constrained differences of derivatives gives E_I^-1=1-b v, E_K=1+x v, E_L=1+y v, E_T^-1=1-c v. For either sign, exp(pi i epsilon)=-1 and the actual linear sign in (3) is exp(pi i)=-1. Thus the same equations hold; no epsilon-dependent integer character has been silently changed. Product E_I E_K E_L E_T=1 implies v[(x+y+b+c)+(xy-bc)v]=0. The v=0 branch has all sine factors zero and is excluded from the regular critical chart. Consequently, with D=P-bc and L0=A+b+c, E_I=D/f(b), E_T=D/f(c), E_K=-(x+b)(x+c)/D, E_L=-(y+b)(y+c)/D. (4) The recorded regular open set is xybc D f(b)f(c)L0 !=0. (5) In particular every E_j-1 remains nonzero. These are exponentiated critical equations, not a claim selecting logarithms or an integration chain. The linear signs and lambda0 are still present in (2),(3). The homogeneous kernel has LEFT output b, RIGHT input c. The actual coefficient target in (1) is degree d, hence the principal gluing law is T_left+I_right=1, NOT zero. Use the momentum r=exp(2pi i I) at the left face; the matching right momentum is r'=exp(-2pi i T). Then the coefficient/pullback advance from left to right is F_+(b,r)=(c,r'), c=[P-r f(b)]/b, r'=f(c)/(P-bc), F_-(b,r)=(c,r'), c=[P-f(b)/r]/b, r'=(P-bc)/f(c). (6) Direct substitution proves F_-=F_+^-1. Thus inverse crossings have opposite canonical transport. If the kernel is viewed instead as a map FROM its input phase point TO its output, the displayed advance is reversed. This is an orientation convention, not a new inverse crossing. The exact R R^-1 coefficient contraction is H_1. For equal signs in two successive layers, (4) and the target give (P-bz)(P-zc)=f(z)^2. (7) For opposite signs they give b=c on the regular chart, as required by (6). A cancelled pair can have a nonisolated middle critical variable; the finite identity is (1), not a claim about a Gaussian saddle of that identity kernel. ## 3. The invariant is the principal original Casimir The original face operator T has principal symbol T(b,r)=-(r+r^-1)+(2-r-r^-1)(A/b+P/b^2). Since the actual Casimir is Omega=-T, its symbol is sigma=2+[(r-1)^2/r] f(b)/b^2. Insert r=(P-bz)/f(b) (or its reciprocal for the inverse sign): sigma=2+(b+z+A)^2/(P-bz). (8) This is the actual conserved pair Casimir, not a chosen first integral of an unrelated recurrence. On (7), putting d1=P-bz,d2=P-zc and f=f(z), the relation d1d2=f^2 gives (b+z+A)^2/d1=(f-d1)^2/(z^2d1) =(d1+d2-2f)/z^2 =(z+c+A)^2/d2. Hence sigma is preserved, and (7) becomes EXACTLY c=-sigma z-b-2A. (9) Conversely (8),(9) imply (7) wherever the recorded units hold. Thus the full local layer sequence obeys b_(j+1)+sigma b_j+b_(j-1)+2A=0. Here and in (10), (b,z) denotes the POSITIVE companion chart on the common phase space: z=[P-r f(b)]/b. A negative crossing acts by the inverse of this map, rather than silently reusing its actual negative-layer right neighbor as that positive companion coordinate. All integer powers are powers of the one affine matrix M_sigma=[[0,1,0],[-1,-sigma,-2A],[0,0,1]], (b_j,b_(j+1),1)^t=M_sigma^j(b_0,b_1,1)^t. (10) Its determinant is1, so this includes negative powers. It is one formula for arbitrary fixed signed twist lengths, not a recurrence established by checking finitely many powers. ## 4. Explicit norm-one coordinate and the source punctures The fixed-Casimir conic is b^2+z^2+sigma bz+2A(b+z)+A^2-(sigma-2)P=0. (11) Assume sigma^2!=4 and C0=(sigma-2)[P-A^2/(sigma+2)] !=0. Put u=b+2A/(sigma+2), v=z+2A/(sigma+2), lambda^2+sigma lambda+1=0. Then (u-lambda v)(u-lambda^-1 v)=C0. (12) The involution is lambda<->lambda^-1. The conic is a torsor for the norm-one group of this quadratic spectral algebra, and the actual map (9) multiplies the first factor by lambda and the second by lambda^-1. In particular it is diagonal after this spectral cover. There is even an explicit norm trivialization: w=((lambda+1)/(lambda-1))*(x+lambda y), Norm(w)=C0, a=(u-lambda v)/w, Norm(a)=1, a ->lambda a. (13) To verify the norm, use Norm((lambda+1)/(lambda-1))=-(sigma-2)/(sigma+2) and Norm(x+lambda y)=x^2-sigma xy+y^2. Both factors are units under the stated generic hypotheses. The inverse crossing gives a->lambda^-1 a in the same phase-space convention (6). Thus arbitrary signed powers are explicit multiplication by lambda^n. The reference point a=1 is b=-x,z=-y. It lies on EVERY conic, but is an EXCLUDED SOURCE POINT: P-bz=0, f(b)=f(z)=0. Thus (13) is an algebraic norm trivialization; it does not make the actual source regular at its reference point. On the spectral cover, u=[lambda bar(w)/a-lambda^-1 w a]/(lambda-lambda^-1), v=[bar(w)/a-w a]/(lambda-lambda^-1). The regular SOURCE STATIONARY chart is the complement of (5) after this substitution. These are divisors of that classical critical chart, not new poles of the finite homogeneous polynomial H_R. In particular the possibly coincident basepoints b,z=(-x,-y),(-y,-x) have norm coordinates 1 and (y+lambda x)/(x+lambda y). Their adjacent lambda and lambda^-1 translates give the f(b) and f(z) zeros. The b=0,z=0 divisors are retained too. A word analyzed in this regular critical chart must retain the preimages of these divisors under ALL its intermediate powers. Transport of the completed algebraic conic is not permission to move the original source contour through them. ## 5. Exact Darboux factor and existing quantum Gaussian For this coordinate calculation always use the POSITIVE companion z=[P-r f(b)]/b as a rational coordinate on the common phase space, regardless of the sign of the next actual crossing. Then, for fixed x,y, the actual cotangent two-form is omega=dLog r wedge dLog b=db wedge dz/(P-bz). Let F be the left side of (11) and eta=u-lambda v. Then d sigma=(F_b db+F_z dz)/(P-bz), lambda F_b+F_z=(lambda-lambda^-1)eta, d sigma=-(lambda-lambda^-1)dLog lambda. These imply, with NO factor2 or sign ambiguity, omega=dLog lambda wedge dLog eta =dLog lambda wedge dLog a. (14) The scalar w depends only on lambda at fixed x,y and thus contributes zero to the wedge. With the explicit convention i_X omega=-dH, H=(Log lambda)^2/2 generates the displayed pullback advance a->lambda a. This agrees with (6); the opposite input-to-output interpretation reverses that map. This recovers an explicit classical coordinate for the EXISTING full-Hermite Gaussian functional calculus, rather than replacing it. The [existing Gaussian theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_coherent_filling_gaussian_chirp.md), section1, proves R^(2P)=q^(P d^2/2) exp[P K(Omega)/hbar], where K(sigma)=arccosh(-sigma/2)^2 is analytic off[2,infinity) with its removable value at sigma=-2. The same node and derivative check gives for every integer n R^n=q^(n d^2/4) exp[n K(Omega)/(2hbar)]. (15) Indeed at c_j=q^(2j+1)+q^(-2j-1), with x_j=pi i(2j+1)/N, K(c_j)=(x_j-pi i)^2, and the actual normalized crossing value is nu_j=exp[pi i(j^2-dj)/N]. This uses (-1)^j=exp(-pi i j), the unwrapped sign required by the original derivative. The derivative of the exponential at the node is the literal multiplier -n(d-2j)/[2(q^(2j+1)-q^(-2j-1))]; paired nodes retain this derivative, and the odd simple node needs no quotient0/0. Values and derivatives therefore agree in the full Casimir quotient. Negative n are allowed because all crossing eigenvalues are units. On the classical spectral cover K=(Log lambda)^2, so (14),(15) give the same Hamiltonian, with the recorded scalar factors unchanged. The finite ratio nu_(j+1)/nu_j=-q^(2j+2) has principal limit lambda=-exp(2pi i j/N), a root of lambda^2+sigma lambda+1=0. Its extra finite q shift is not dropped from (15) or from the kernels. Neither the unit-modulus node values nor the torus action bounds the full quantum operator or its shared-face coefficient. ## 6. The two endpoint fibers are different At sigma=-2, with A!=0, the original conic is the reduced parabola (b-z)^2+2A(b+z)+A^2+4P=0. Put t=b-z. Then the actual affine map gives t->t+2A, and b=-[(t-A)^2+4P]/(4A), z=-[(t+A)^2+4P]/(4A). The affine matrix M_-2 satisfies (M_-2-I)^3=0, and its square is nonzero when A!=0. Thus M_-2^n=I+n(M_-2-I)+n(n-1)(M_-2-I)^2/2 (16) for EVERY integer n. This is concrete nilpotent/unipotent classical transport at the parabolic Casimir, with quadratic face dependence. It does not imply polynomial growth of an original quantum period. At sigma=+2 the SCHEME (11) is the nonreduced double line (b+z+A)^2=0. Its reduced line has z=-b-A and the map is the involution (b,z)->(z,b). The full affine matrix retains its Jordan data: (M_2+I)^2(M_2-I)=0. Explicitly, if e=b+z+A with e^2=0, then M_2^2(b,z)=(b-2e,z+2e). Thus the reduction loses a real normal transport even though it is an involution on ordinary points. Do not call this fiber the same additive torsor as sigma=-2, and do not replace the double-line scheme by its reduction when retaining normal data. The regular one-layer critical chart excludes the reduced line because L0=0. This is a degeneration of the closure. For sigma^2!=4 but C0=0, (12) is a pair of lines rather than a norm-one torsor. Formula(10) still gives exact algebraic transport. The generic torus theorem does not assert that this reducible fiber is nonsingular. ## 7. Existing repository scope and the remaining source question The repository already has exact full-Hermite Gaussian powers in [the Gaussian source note](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_coherent_filling_gaussian_chirp.md) and its Fourier-Hermite source dependencies. It also has [the uniform group-relator note](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/uniform_twist_relator_source.md), sections1--2: a quadratic norm group for the TWIST-KNOT GROUP RELATOR w^k, explicitly not the original quantum crossing-source torsor. The [intrinsic quantum-A norm-torsor](intrinsic_quantum_a_norm_torsor.md) construction is a different cyclic quantum-A norm group. None of those statements is being reproved or relabeled as this local theorem. A focused search of the current notes found no displayed source-face conic (11) or the coefficient-layer recurrence (9). The additional interface here is the explicit original R-layer critical relation, its preserved ACTUAL pair Casimir, signed inverse conventions, norm coordinate, source punctures, and two distinct parabolic endpoint schemes. It holds at a local port independently of bridge width. Whole networks still require their original shared face targets, exterior phases and mark. No eliminated knot variety, period contribution, or volume estimate follows just from this algebraic linearization. No literature novelty claim is made. Coverage only: [Goldman, The complex-symplectic geometry of SL(2,C)-characters over surfaces](https://math.umd.edu/~wmg/csymp.pdf), PDF dated2 September2003, Proposition2.6.1 and sections2.6.1--2.6.2, already relates Dehn twists to Hamiltonian trace flows and distinguishes generic multiplicative from noncentral parabolic additive orbits. The [arXiv record](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0304307v2) is version2, 3 October2003. Those statements are coverage context, not inputs to this proof. The present conic has not thereby been identified with that surface character variety; multiplicative/additive twist dynamics is not being claimed as new in itself. ## 8. Verification scope The [focused exact audit](../experiments/audit_actual_crossing_casimir_torus.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_crossing_casimir_torus_results.json), checks 14 symbolic identities, 450 signed-integer torus steps, 866 inverse-chart checks, 20 excluded reference points and 180 parabolic or reduced-endpoint steps. It independently compares 28 original integer crossing powers, including identity cases, on 3,024 physical entries and 966 wrong-unwrapped-total zeros. Twelve mixed inverse compositions, 70 exact Gaussian node VALUES and 14 adjacent spectral ratios retain all displayed scalar phases. The full-Hermite Gaussian DERIVATIVE assertion is the analytical node-and-derivative proof in section5 and its existing source theorem; these 70 value checks are not advertised as an independent numerical derivative audit. The crossing-Casimir torsor does not determine a quantum norm, a selected finite-cycle contribution or a long-filled volume estimate.

title: The original crossing torus transports the actual meridians
status: Actual Hurwitz transport; regular forward representation morphism
text: # The original crossing torus transports the actual meridians 31 October 2026. The full physical phase of the [original crossing torus](actual_crossing_casimir_torus.md) induces the actual signed Hurwitz transport, including its common magnetic scale. Full regular critical points of the layered direct-power source therefore map to representations of the actual filled diagram. This is a forward morphism on the recorded localized chart, not an isomorphism or a selected-cycle theorem. No global coefficient bound is asserted. Use N>=3, d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N) and the original scalar lambda0=q^(d^2/2), with its recorded exponential lift. Put A0=x+y, P0=xy, f(b)=(b+x)(b+y). Distinguish the frozen crossing note's COEFFICIENT momentum r_H=exp(2pi i I) from the PHYSICAL momentum p=r_H^-1. This inverse must be proved from the full physical adapter, not chosen using the symmetric Casimir. We first do that calculation. ## Full physical phase, all derivatives and the original half powers Write the physical input heads as (v,t-v) and output heads as (u,t-u), all divided by N at principal order. The exact finite homogeneous identity is R^epsilon_entry=N^-1 H_(R^epsilon)/(bc)^(d/2), with its recorded log lifts; this is (7a) of the [homogeneous-source theorem](../papers/filling-bounds/README.md). There is no new cap or pivot in this identity. Let Psi_H be the ACTUAL homogeneous kernel phase (including lambda0^epsilon). At a regular local critical point of its three simplex variables, the envelope derivatives with respect to (Log x,Log b,Log c,Log y) are (K,I,T,L), where K+I+T+L=1. All integer characters from its original signs remain in the critical equations. The physical principal phase is therefore Theta=Psi_H-(Log b+Log c)/2. (0a) Take a common face-scale gamma=Log y and the literal head clocks Log x=gamma+2pi i t, Log b=gamma+2pi i(t-v)+pi i, Log c=gamma+2pi i(t-u)+pi i, Log y=gamma. (0b) These are precisely X_in,1=-x/b, X_in,2=-b/y and the corresponding output clocks -x/c,-c/y. Here b/c are PHYSICAL input/output middle clocks after the exact Fourier adapter. The frozen crossing note's LEFT output b / RIGHT input c instead describes its polynomial monomial operator; these are dual uses of the kernel, not competing physical orientations. The finite half-index and d/N offsets in the exact identity are retained in the original amplitude; (0a,b) are the explicitly stated PRINCIPAL symbol. Homogeneity cancels the common gamma derivative exactly at this order. Differentiation gives Theta_v=-2pi i(I-1/2), Theta_u=-2pi i(T-1/2), Theta_t=2pi i(K+I+T-1)=-2pi i L, Theta_gamma=K+I+T+L-1=0. (0c) For the original kernel convention, input raising-shift symbols differentiate positively and output symbols negatively. Restoring a nonzero common input scale g gives S_in=(g exp Theta_v,g), S_out=(g exp[-Theta_t-Theta_u],g exp[-Theta_t]). (0d) Indeed its generating one-form is Log(S1_in)dv+Log(S2_in)d(t-v)-Log(S1_out)du-Log(S2_out)d(t-u); comparison of dv,du,dt yields exactly (0d). Thus, independently of the crossing sign, p=exp(-2pi i I), p_out=exp(2pi i T), S_in=(-g p,g), S_out=(-g exp(2pi i L)p_out,g exp(2pi i L)). (0e) The outer derivative is ESSENTIAL: it fixes the common scale transport and not just the first/second-head ratio. No arbitrary scale is assigned after examining a trace. For epsilon=+/-1 set E_j=exp(2pi i epsilon j) as in the [crossing-torus theorem](actual_crossing_casimir_torus.md), section2. Equations (0e) read p=E_I^(-epsilon), p_out=E_T^epsilon, g_out/g=E_L^epsilon. (0f) Now (4) of that note supplies E_I=(P0-bc)/f(b), E_T=(P0-bc)/f(c), E_L=-(b+y)(c+y)/(P0-bc). Therefore positive physical chronology has (c,p_out)=F_-(b,p), and negative chronology has F_+(b,p). Equivalently it is the coefficient graph F_epsilon conjugated by p=1/r_H. This explicitly explains the inverse and its full normalization; it is not inferred from (2) below. ## The actual meridian matrices The resulting ACTUAL physical Gauss data are X1=-x/b, X2=-b/y, S1=-g p, S2=g. (1) The sign in S1/S2=-p is compulsory by (0c--f). As a separate check, the original Jacobi symbol at X=X1,T=X1X2=x/y has a(X)=-f(b)/b^2, d(X)=-2A0/b-2P0/b^2. Thus a(X)(Y+Y^-1)+d(X), with the original magnetic Y=S1/S2=-p, is exactly the source-torus invariant sigma=2+((p-1)^2/p)f(b)/b^2. (2) For each leg define the original matrices K=-1/X, F=S(1-X), E=(X^-1-1)/S, G=[[K,E],[FK,FE+K^-1]], Lminus=[[1,0],[-KF,K]]. Then the ordered physical meridians are A=G1, B=Lminus1^-1 G2 Lminus1, P=B A. (3) They have determinant one and trace minus two. Direct multiplication gives P11=y/x and Tr(P)=sigma; this is the original ordered pair Casimir, not just an abstract first integral. These formulas are on the same Gauss units as the original compiler; any additional scale or total-F denominator needed below is explicitly localized. ## Actual signed Hurwitz moves Positive physical chronology is (A,B) -> (A^-1 B A,A), and negative chronology is its inverse (A,B)->(B,B A B^-1). The first new physical clock is recovered from the new first meridian by b_new=x*(A_new)11. After setting g=1 for display, multiplication gives positive: c=(P0-f(b)/p)/b, S1_new=b p/(-b+p x-x), S2_new=-(-b+p y-y)/b, p_new=-S1_new/S2_new=(P0-bc)/f(c); negative: c=(P0-p f(b))/b, S1_new=-(b p+p x-x)/b, S2_new=b p/(b p+p y-y), p_new=-S1_new/S2_new=f(c)/(P0-bc). (4) For general g multiply both new S values by g. Rebuilding the second leg from X2_new=-c/y and these S values gives exactly the SECOND Hurwitz meridian as well, so the WHOLE ordered matrix P is preserved. This is stronger than trace matching. The displayed extra denominators are already factors of the regular source chart after the corresponding F_+ or F_- substitution; they must remain excluded. Substitution of (0f) gives exactly the S values in (4), including S2_new/g=E_L for positive chronology and E_L^-1 for negative chronology. Consequently the matrices checked here come from ALL physical phase derivatives, not only the Casimir. No crossing sign or original scalar is changed by the coefficient-to-physical inversion. ## Fixed product, centralizer and the spectral sign The full product has the actual form P=[[T^-1,E_tot],[F_tot/T,F_tot E_tot+T]], T=x/y. On F_tot!=0, fixing sigma and T fixes E_tot once F_tot is fixed. As (b,p) varies on one conic, choose the scale g so that F_tot has that fixed value. The common magnetic scale is thereby restored, and the conic is a rational chart of ACTUAL ordered trace-minus-two pairs with that fixed P. Conversely the original regular Gauss inverse recovers (b,p,g) from such a pair. This is a local birational statement, with the same recorded open units; not every completed-conic point is an allowed source point. If J is the selected eigenvalue of P, then J+J^-1=sigma, lambda=-J or -J^-1. On the chosen source spectral sheet lambda=-J. Hence physical positive crossings multiply the norm coordinate by lambda^-1, while negative crossings multiply by lambda. The central minus sign cannot be removed for an odd power. In particular the square of positive Hurwitz is simultaneous conjugation by P^-1: H_+^2(A,B)=(P^-1 A P,P^-1 B P), and the torus multiplication is lambda^-2=J^-2, as required. The opposite spectral sheet interchanges the reciprocal coordinate. At sigma=2 and f(b)!=0, equation(2) is the double equation (p-1)^2=0. Its reduced locus p=1 has the two meridians sharing their fixed line; positive Hurwitz swaps this commuting pair. This explains why the completed double line is not an additional regular source saddle. At sigma=-2 the already derived additive coordinate advances by -2A0 under positive physical chronology, the inverse of the pullback advance. All of this is rational matrix algebra on the source-defined classical chart. The exact finite kernels still retain their original Hermite data, scalar lambda0^n, punctures and original marked target. A global representation follows only after the actual wire/cup constraints are imposed; none of these identities assigns a coefficient to that branch. ## Full regular direct-power critical points and the filled group Fix the original flat-plat index word and integer exponents n_e=epsilon_e-2p_e. Expand each nonzero power into |n_e| literal signed crossings, preserving the original cups, caps and unrestricted marked cap. This is the same finite source by the [exact direct-power composition](actual_direct_long_power_source.md), and the same actual filled diagram by the specified crossing-disk marking. The fixed half-twist permutation and cap pairings are required to give one main component when calling this diagram a knot; otherwise the statements refer to its actual filled link. No asymptotic interchange in a growing power is involved: the exponents and expanded diagram are fixed before N. Consider the following PRECISE class of principal critical points. Each layer has the three simplex critical equations of its actual homogeneous coefficient phase, on the recorded open chart (all E_j and E_j-1, physical Gauss clocks, prefix diagonals and used denominators are units). The point is also critical in EVERY independent physical-head direction of the expanded diagram, with original degree constraints, cup/cap phases and the marked-cap character retained. Local branches and integer logarithmic characters are fixed throughout. No boundary endpoint, escaping flag, protected-zero limit or merely constrained tangential stationarity is included in this statement. Every such FULL regular critical point defines a representation of the ACTUAL filled knot group, with noncentral boundary-parabolic main meridians and the original Morse basepaths. Scheme-theoretically, let D_reg be the product of all of the displayed layer units, all physical clock and raising-symbol units, all original prefix diagonals, and the K+1 factors used for the unique noncentral main flags. Use the LOCALIZED critical scheme (O/I)[D_reg^-1], with the original fixed logarithmic characters on each formal neighborhood. If polynomial equations were cleared first, I:D_reg^infinity has the same restriction to this open scheme but denotes its closure, not an equivalent assertion on D_reg=0. The construction below is a regular morphism from this localized critical scheme to the actual marked representation scheme modulo simultaneous diagonal conjugation. It is valid over local Artin C-algebras as well: the spanning-tree recursion and all matrix formulas divide only by the recorded units. NO isomorphism, surjectivity or converse branch selection is claimed here. Here is the entire forward construction. 1. Use the oriented event incidence matrix B of the expanded source. Centered physical variations lie in ker_Z B. Its integral cycle lattice is saturated. Magnetic criticality says that the product of local derivative multipliers around every cycle is one. On a spanning tree solve for vertex multipliers; each non-tree edge then satisfies the same equation by its fundamental cycle. This is the elementary construction of sections2--3 of the [actual critical-scheme theorem](actual_augmented_plat_critical_scheme.md), and uses no extra geometric assumption on the width or cycles. It supplies a SHARED raising symbol S on every actual physical wire. The one free common multiplier rescales all S and hence conjugates every meridian by the same projective diagonal matrix. Fixing one actual unit S=1 gives a concrete gauge slice; this is not a new cap or a second boundary functional. 2. At each crossing, (0a--f) and (3)--(4) make those shared symbols the full actual signed Hurwitz map, including the common scale. This is why trace conservation alone would not suffice. At a cup the actual principal phase is pi i(x1-1), at an ordinary cap pi i x1, and at the marked cap pi i x2. The complementary constraint x1+x2=1 at the marked cap is the permitted WHOLE-SOURCE consequence of exact degree conservation through all other tensors, not a local replacement of the unrestricted mark. All three phases yield X1 X2=1 and S1/S2=-1, hence the literal based inverse-pair relation P=I. Their different integral characters remain in the action. 3. At each horizontal slice use the same lower-triangular prefix factors Lminus as the original Morse presentation. Whole-product preservation at crossings and P=I at cups/caps leave the prefixes outside the event unchanged. Therefore each wire has the same based meridian at both ends. The local Hurwitz relations and inverse-pair closure relations are exactly the original diagram's Wirtinger/Morse relations. They give its group representation, with the recorded central signs converted to the actual meridian lift as in the same critical-scheme compiler, section5. For n_e=epsilon_e-2p_e that diagram is the stated crossing-circle filling, so no new peripheral filling equation must be guessed from the scalar Casimir. The same proof works for a connected marked link diagram componentwise on its peripheral subgroups; the intended fixed-parity plat gives one main component. Its noncentral unipotent meridian has unipotent PSL2 centralizer, so its commuting longitude is boundary parabolic. Neither faithfulness nor discreteness of this representation is inferred. This conclusion does NOT identify every point of a CLEARED whole-box characteristic with a representation. Such a point must lift to the regular layered chart just specified. A critical point of a reduced phase with some variables already set to protected zero need not satisfy the full equations. Nor has an asymptotic for H_(R^n) on this entire chart been proved by this algebraic statement. The original finite coefficient may receive endpoint, singular or escaping contributions; the regular representation correspondence does not bound or select them. Identifying the actual original cycle and obtaining the required global phase-preserving estimate remain the substantive missing steps. ## Verification and scope [The focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_crossing_torus_meridian_transport.py) checks the four full physical-phase derivatives, both signed input/output momenta and common-scale transports, all entries of both actual Hurwitz meridians and the preserved whole product, the double-crossing conjugation, and the commuting endpoint. It also rejects the incorrect magnetic sign. [Results](../experiments/actual_crossing_torus_meridian_transport_results.json) record exact symbolic identities, not numerical evidence for cycle selection or an asymptotic. The global assembly uses the separately proved primitive incidence and literal Morse presentation, rather than a finite collection of diagrams. The morphism is forward and localized to the full-critical locus. No converse, boundary extension or contributing period is inferred.

title: A positive original cube packet with all four rung colors retained
text: # A positive original cube packet with all four rung colors retained 29 October 2026. Fix the EIGHT cycle channels of the original ordered cube to the odd Steinberg channel, while retaining EVERY physical complete-circle channel on its FOUR rungs. The original exposed marked source has an explicit positive Newton contraction. This includes all paired nilpotents, gives its exact global support, controls the entire four-color sum by the central term at polynomial cost, and proves a strict gap for macroscopic rung-color deficits. This is a specified sector of the original cube source, with its eight cycle projections still present. The remaining eight color sums and even levels are not evaluated. No conclusion about the full cube invariant or arbitrary cubic graphs is inferred. ## 1. The exact marked packet Keep N=2m+1>=3, d=2m, q=exp(pi i/N), the literal ordered cube and its EXPOSED marked white vertex from the [central cube theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_odd_central_cube_reflection_packet.md). Its two cycles have edge orders top (0,11,3,2), bottom (9,5,6,8), rungs (1,10,4,7). Every cycle edge has label m. The four rung labels j_0,...,j_3 vary independently over 0,...,m. For j<=m put k_j=2 if j<m, k_m=1, z_j(v)=s_(j+v)/[s_(j-v)s_v^2], 0<=v<=j, h_j=sum_(v=0)^j z_j(v) Bhat_v, P_(N,j)=sum_(v=0)^j z_j(v) beta(m,v)^2, S_N=P_(N,m), omega_j=kappa(-1)^j q^[j(j+1)], kappa=q^(d^2/2). Here the Newton basis and functional are the FULL root algebra, not the distinct-node quotient. In particular h_m is the genuine turned isolated projector from the central cube theorem. The actual complete circle sector L_j, paired or simple, obeys Rturn L_j=N k_j h_j. (1) Let Z_jvec denote the RAW original marked cube source with these twelve specified labels and no edge twists. Then Z_jvec=N^12 product_(r=0)^3[k_(j_r)P_(N,j_r)^2] phi(h_(j_0)h_(j_1)h_(j_2)h_(j_3)). (2) All factors and the functional in (2) are the actual ones. For any fixed signed edge exponents multiply (2) by exactly omega_m^(sum_cycle e_l) product_r omega_(j_r)^(e_(rung r)). (3) Thus a twisted individual label sector has a specified unit phase; a sum of differently phased rung sectors is not declared positive. The finite support of the untwisted source is particularly simple: Z_jvec>0 iff j_0+j_1+j_2+j_3>=d; Z_jvec=0 otherwise. (4) Every LOCAL vertex already has total label 2m+j>=d. The additional constraint (4) is a genuine global contraction constraint; it cannot be deduced by keeping only the local black scalar supports. ## 2. The full normal sector turns to a positive polynomial Let E_j be the FULL Hermite projector of the pair Casimir cluster c_j; L_j=L_N E_j. At a double node it retains the actual nilpotent circle normal. The complete Frobenius trace identity gives phi(L_j f)=N Tr(E_j m_f)=N k_j f(c_j). (5) It follows from the complete polynomial identity for L_N and the trace of multiplication; the trace in the j cluster has its actual algebraic multiplicity k_j. No spectral derivative has been removed from L_j before this identity is used. The Newton turn and pairing then give the v-th coefficient of Rturn L_j as phi(L_j Bhat_v)=N k_j Bhat_v(c_j). Direct paired-sine factorization gives Bhat_v(c_j)=z_j(v) for v<=j, and zero for v>j. This proves (1) as a FULL algebra identity. Its polynomial degree is j, and hence it also specifies its first normal at every other double node. The paired nilpotent has become an ordinary low-degree turned polynomial by the actual nonmultiplicative turn, not by treating it as a positive projector. ## 3. Use the actual physical source's cyclicity For the finite generic derivation retain the physical cup pV(u,d-u)=cV P_d(u), cV=N zeta^(-d^2), P_L(u)=(-1)^u zeta^[u(L-u-1)]F_uF_(L-u)/F_L.
