All factorials in this generic cup are retained. The root monomial formula is not substituted off the root. At the root gamma_j=q^(2-j^2)/N^2, h0_j=k_j N s_(2j)/s_j^2, pi_j=gamma_j^(-1)D_phys(W_j), L_j=h0_j W_j pi_j. Choose the regular generic W_j and pi_j lift of the original [first-normal theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_nc_morse_graph_first_normal_source_reduction.md). The latter identity is asserted at the root; its chosen lift is h0_j W_j(t)pi_j(t). Every denominator in W_j and pi_j is a unit at this odd root. Paired generic projectors are NOT used. There is an important simplification for unequal labels: rotate the actual black source U_abc, rather than assuming that every differently normalized canonical Theta has the same cyclic scalar. The physical nested-cup source has entries J_((a,b),(c,e),(f,g))=pV(a,g)pV(b,c)pV(e,f). The ratio to its pair-cyclic permutation is exactly K(a)K(b), because P_d(d-u)=K(u)^(-1)P_d(u), with d even. Covariance of each pi therefore proves the generic all-entry identity U_abc(alpha,beta,gamma) =K_a(alpha) U_bca(beta,gamma,alpha). (6) This is valid before specialization and therefore for its first normal as well. White source tensors have the corresponding genuinely dual identity. The scalar product of the three fixed gamma factors is symmetric and does not change (6). No plain leg permutation or same-order Hermitian dual is introduced. Use (6) to put each rung in the last black and first white slot, as in the explicit four-rung table of the central cube theorem. The two outer cycle objects are both Q_m=V_d, and the rung object is Q_j. Let W_j:Q_j->V_d tensor V_d be its ordinary Clebsch map and let D_can use the canonical cups on these two V_d objects. Set a_j=(-1)^(d-j) zeta^[-j(j+1)-d], Theta_mmj=(W_j tensor I)p_(2j)/a_j, s_j=the actual black corner s_(m,m,j), U_mmj=(s_j/a_j)(W_j tensor I)p_(2j). (7) To verify the anchor a_j, the proved lowest-column identity gives W_j[2j](d,j) =zeta^[j(d-2j)] h_(d-j), h_(d-j)=(-1)^(d-j)zeta^[-(d-j)(j+1)], P_(2j)(2j)=zeta^(-2j). Multiplication gives exactly (7), with no endpoint division by a zero factorial. Every a_j is a nonzero monomial. Contracting one rung is now the ALL-SIDE-LEGS-OPEN identity (s_j/a_j)^2 W_j D_can(W_j). (8) The two Q_j cup/cap matrices cancel in their actual order. Since the cycle object's physical cup is cV times its canonical cup, D_can(W_j)=cV^2 D_phys(W_j)=cV^2 gamma_j pi_j, W_j D_can(W_j) =cV^2 gamma_j L_j/h0_j at the root. (9) Equations (8),(9) retain the entire paired root operator. In fact for j<m this rung map is nonzero and nilpotent, with square zero. Splitting it into a vanishing generic norm times a singular generic projector would obscure this regular map; no such split is made. The four rung maps all act on V_d tensor V_d. Their genuine full-cup turn, cyclic four-box trace and mark are consequently exactly the entrywise identities (9a),(9b),(10) of the central cube theorem, now with four different self-dual regular maps. Projector idempotence was never needed in that index substitution. The exposed physical mark remains on a cycle V_d strand. It is not transported through any paired Q_j image. Generic ordinary closure is [N] times the root-open scalar; taking its first normal and dividing by nu_N is therefore the original marked value phi of the product of turns. ## 4. All source phases cancel, with paired factors retained Before simplifying, the preceding contraction gives at the root Z_jvec=(N gamma_m)^8 product_r[ h0_j gamma_j (s_j/a_j)^2] phi(product_r Rturn[W_j D_can(W_j)]). This follows from the original one-gamma-per-edge identity. Its eight cycle edge factors are N gamma_m; each of the four rung factors is h0_j gamma_j. The eight actual black/white source scalars are those in (8), not inferred from a closed theta norm. The mark's single quantum-dimension normal is treated only after this full contraction. Insert (9) and then (1). The remaining scalar is (N gamma_m cV)^8 N^4 product_r[k_j gamma_j^2 s_j^2/a_j^2]. (10) There is no missing h0_j: its occurrence in the edge factor cancels its explicit reciprocal in the regular map (9). The proved actual ordered scalar formula gives s_j=N^3 A_N(m,m,j), A_N(m,m,j)=(-1)^(j+1) q^[m^2-2m-j-3] P_(N,j). Its positive magnitude P_(N,j) is the finite one-leg source, and its displayed ordered phase is from the full source theorem, not a permutation guess. Squaring and using (7) yields exactly gamma_j^2 s_j^2/a_j^2 =N^2 q^[2m^2-2]P_(N,j)^2, (11) INDEPENDENT of j apart from P_(N,j). Also N gamma_m cV=q^[2-5m^2]. The complete phase in (10),(11) is q^[8-32m^2]=q^[8N(2-N)]=1. The powers of N are N^4 times N^8, and this proves (2). Full Cartan and all fixed signed crossing powers give precisely (3), as follows from the all-normal eigenvalue equality R^e L_j=omega_j^e L_j. ## 5. Exact global support and a whole four-color bound The positive Newton multiplication theorem applies to every h_j in (1). Its coefficients are strictly positive at all indices 0,...,j. If sum j_r<d, the product has degree below d, so phi=0. If sum j_r>=d, choose integers 0<=v_r<=j_r with sum v_r=d. Their product has positive coefficient at output d: at each multiplication choose its upper index, the current partial sum. These partial sums stay <=d<N, so none of the allowed products vanishes. All other coefficients are nonnegative. Thus phi(product h_j)>0, proving (4) without a norm or stationary-phase approximation. For v<=j<m the exact sine quotient is z_(j+1)(v)/z_j(v) =sin[pi(j+v+1)/N]/sin[pi(j-v+1)/N]>=1. The difference of these sines is 2cos[pi(j+1)/N]sin(pi v/N)>=0. The new coefficient at v=j+1 is positive. In the actual Newton cone this proves 0<=h_j<=h_m, 0<P_(N,j)<=S_N. (12) Multiplication and phi preserve the cone. Equations (2),(12), and k_j<=2 consequently give 0<=Z_jvec<=16 Z_(m,m,m,m). (13) Let Z_four-rung be the actual source obtained by replacing the four rung sectors by their FULL complete circles, while retaining the eight central cycle sectors and taking zero rung twists. Linearity of the original source makes it the sum of (2) over all four labels. It follows that Z_St<=Z_four-rung<=16(m+1)^4 Z_St. (14) The same statement holds after removing the common unit phase of arbitrary fixed cycle twists. It is not a triangle-inequality bound on an oscillating rung sum: the summed source itself is positive. There is also a strict full-source color gap. For every fixed delta>0, the proved one-leg factorial estimate supplies gamma_delta>0 with max_(m-j>=delta N) P_(N,j)/S_N <=poly_delta(N)exp(-gamma_delta N). Using (12) in (2) gives the entire four-color complement bound sum_(max_r(m-j_r)>=delta N) Z_jvec <=poly_delta(N)exp(-2gamma_delta N) Z_St. (15) All finite source values, not only a selected term or a value-only Casimir symbol, occur in (14),(15). The bounds are uniform over the whole four-rung physical color cube and include j=0 and paired axes. The empty range for an oversized delta is understood literally. The [proved positive central period rate](actual_positive_newton_cuboctahedral_period.md) and (14) therefore give lim_(N odd) (2pi/N)log Z_four-rung =16v8+2Vol(Q_cube)=Vol(actual augmented cube link). The eight fixed central cycle projections are still a substantive restriction; (14) does not allow their removal or control interference from the remaining cycle colors. This partial-source statement is not a full cube volume-conjecture theorem. Audit: [all-rung actual marked contractions and full local normals](../experiments/audit_actual_cube_four_rung_positive_source.py), with [recorded results](../experiments/actual_cube_four_rung_positive_source_results.json). It compares every rung tuple at N=3,5,7, further physical tuples at N=9,11, and a signed original edge word at each level. Every actual U cyclic identity is checked including its first normal; paired rung nilpotents and the full half-degree turn are checked as operators. The complex positivity and global support follow from the analytical proof above, not a sign or nonvanishing interpretation in a finite field. The four-rung source result is not an equality for the full cube invariant.

title: Direct crossing powers and a limitation of phase-blind spectral bounds
status: Exact powers; phase-blind spectral bound obstruction
text: # Direct crossing powers and a limitation of phase-blind spectral bounds , 30 October 2026. This is an exact root-source statement for the original connected fixed flat-plat compiler. It retains every cap, mark, level coset and crossing scalar. It gives a direct formulation for fixed integer twist powers and rules out one particular positive spectral upper bound as a route to a strict filled-volume rate. It does not bound the phase-preserving source or prove a filling asymptotic. Write N>=3, d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), S_j=prod_(v=1)^j 2sin(pi v/N), and lambda0=q^(d^2/2), with the original exponential lift. All Casimir derivatives below are taken at this fixed root, not in a generic-q germ. ## 1. Direct powers in the original coefficient source The [homogeneous source theorem](../papers/filling-bounds/README.md) assigns a degree-d polynomial H_F(x,b,c,y) to a polynomial F in the actual pair Casimir Omega. For two coupons on the SAME pair, H_(FG)(x,b,c,y)=[z^d] H_F(x,b,z,y) H_G(x,z,c,y). (1) A left term has intermediate exponent d-j, while a right term has output exponent i. Extraction imposes i=j, exactly matrix composition. The outer x,y powers add; there is no extra N or pivot factor. The identity is H_1=sum_(j=0)^d b^j c^(d-j). For every nonzero integer n, therefore, H_(R^n)(x,b,c,y) =[prod_(r=1)^(|n|-1) z_r^d] prod_(r=1)^|n| H_(R^sign(n))(x,z_(r-1),z_r,y), z_0=b, z_|n|=c. (2) Each layer retains its original scalar lambda0^sign(n). Thus the right side contains lambda0^n and the full repeated-node data. A filled box with exponent n_e=epsilon_e-2p_e may be compiled directly by (2), with all other physical tensors and marked face targets unchanged. This exact identity needs no external-color or alias split. The exponents p_e are fixed before N; no uniform asymptotic in growing word length is asserted. Casimirs at different ports need not commute. For reference, the normalized one-layer coefficient is [x^k b^i y^l c^t] H_(r_N^epsilon) =(-1)^(k+l+1) q^[epsilon(kl-(i+1)(t+1))] N/(S_i S_k S_l S_t), i+k+l+t=d, epsilon=+/-1. (3) The full layer is lambda0^epsilon times (3). For scaled simplex coordinates I,K,L,T its principal phase includes E_simplex + I Log b+K Log x+L Log y+T Log c +pi i(K+L)+epsilon pi i(KL-IT)+epsilon pi i/2. (4) Here E_simplex=sum Lambda(pi I_j)/pi. The finite d=N-1 offsets and order-one signs stay in (3). Each intermediate extraction subtracts Log z_r in (4). The [crossing Casimir transport theorem](actual_crossing_casimir_torus.md) derives the signed local characteristic, its punctured norm torus and its distinct endpoint schemes. None of these local statements selects the original global coefficient contour. ## 2. A general obstruction for the Hermite triangle bound The paired nodes are c_a=q^h+q^(-h), h=2a+1<N. Let P_a,Q_a denote the canonical confluent Hermite polynomials modulo chi(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2: P_a has value1 at c_a and all other node data0; Q_a has derivative1 there and all other node data0. At odd N retain the single c_*=-2 node with its value projector P_*. The ACTUAL normalized crossing data are r_N(c_a)=nu_a=(-1)^a q^[a(a+1)], gamma_a=r_N'(c_a)/r_N(c_a) =-(N-h)/[2(q^h-q^(-h))]. (5) Thus r_N^n has data nu_a^n and n gamma_a nu_a^n for every integer n; negative powers are legitimate because the values are units. These are full Hermite data, not an eigenvalue-only interpolation. For a polynomial H let |H|_coef replace each coefficient by its absolute value. Define the positive polynomial E_n=sum_a (|H_(P_a)|_coef+|n gamma_a| |H_(Q_a)|_coef) +[odd N: |H_(P_*)|_coef]. (6) For n!=0, |H_(R^n)|_coef<=E_n. The unit lambda0^n does not affect this inequality. The complete coupon is L_N=(-1)^(N-1)U_(N-1)(Omega/2). Its paired values vanish, while |L_N'(c_a)|=N/[2sin^2(pi h/N)], |L_N'(c_a)|/|gamma_a| =2N/[(N-h)sin(pi h/N)] <= N^2. (7) Indeed sin(pi h/N)>=2min(h,N-h)/N. If h<=N/2 the ratio is at most N^2/[h(N-h)]<=N^2; if h>=N/2 it is at most N^2/(N-h)^2<=N^2. At the odd simple node L_N(-2)=N. The triangle inequality, |n|>=1, and the independently proved nonnegative coefficients of H_(L_N) give the EXACT coefficientwise comparison H_(L_N) <= N^2 E_n. (8) This comparison is local, but its consequence retains the full shared source constraint. On any certified original connected fixed flat plat with R boxes and nonzero integers n_e, multiply (8) and extract the original marked target: [target] prod_e E_(n_e) >=N^(-2R) [target] prod_e H_(L_N). (9) The common original prefactor is polynomial in N and every crossing scalar has modulus1. The right side has the augmented complete-volume rate, by the [complete augmented-source theorem](general_signed_augmented_source_volume.md) with zero half twists. Every positive-radius Cauchy bound for the left side is at least that coefficient, so optimizing the radii cannot remove this obstruction. In particular this specific phase-blind Hermite strategy cannot yield any upper exponential rate strictly below the augmented volume, even for arbitrarily large fixed powers. When a hyperbolic nontrivial filling with smaller volume is under consideration, the [representation-volume strictness theorem](../papers/casimir-source-asymptotics/README.md) identifies the needed strict geometric decrease. Inequality (9) shows why a successful direct spectral proof must retain cancellation beyond (6). It does not contradict a phase-preserving bound, the volume conjecture, or a source estimate using different structure. The case n=0 is excluded: its nilpotent derivative weight vanishes. ## 3. The exact Gaussian retains the missing phases The existing [Gaussian filling theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_coherent_filling_gaussian_chirp.md), section1, proves even powers using full Hermite functional calculus. The same value-and-derivative argument gives every integer n: hbar=2pi i/N, K(z)=arccosh(-z/2)^2, R^n=q^(n d^2/4) exp[n K(Omega)/(2hbar)]. (10) K is analytic on C minus[2,infinity), with its removable value at -2. The fractional q power uses the literal original Log q. At a paired node set phi=pi(2a+1)/N and s=d-2a. Then K(c_a)=-pi^2s^2/N^2, q^[(d^2+s^2)/4]=lambda0(-1)^a q^[a(a+1)], K'(c_a)=-pi s/[Nsin(phi)], [n/(2hbar)]K'(c_a)=-ns/[4i sin(phi)]=n gamma_a. Thus (10) matches every derivative as well as every value. The odd simple node needs only its value. The unwrapped sign in the value formula is (-1)^a=exp(-pi i a); resetting it to the opposite analytic character would change the derivative. Full Hermite uniqueness proves (10), including n<0. This is not a generic-q identity or a unitary diagonalization. The cut at2, the nodes approaching it, all source punctures and the noncommuting neighboring Casimirs remain relevant to a global estimate. ## Validation and remaining scope The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_direct_long_power_source.py) compares homogeneous compositions with independently built original R matrices, including wrong-unwrapped totals and both signs. It also constructs the canonical Hermite basis and checks the coefficientwise comparison and Gaussian value/derivative data at both parities. [Results](../experiments/actual_direct_long_power_source_results.json) record the finite checks; they do not serve as a proof of an asymptotic. The finite audit checks the original powers, physical entries, wrong-total zeros, Hermite data, Gaussian values and derivatives. The phase-blind envelope does not imply a phase-preserving global rate or a selected-cycle contribution.

title: The even Fejér source: complete crossing paths and a forest remainder
status: Exact complete cross comparison and one-sided forest support
text: # The even Fejér source: complete crossing paths and a forest remainder Status update, 31 October 2026: the [full endpoint theorem](general_fejer_endpoint_source_volume.md) now controls the entire positive source, and the [unique-maximizer theorem](actual_fejer_unique_geometric_maximizer.md) gives a strict exponential gap for the one-sided remainder under the same labeled certificate. The exact decomposition and the warnings about inferring bounds from forest topology alone remain valid. , 31 October 2026. This is an exact coefficient reduction at every even level N>=4 for the original connected fixed flat plat. No estimate of the remaining forest contribution is asserted. The shared original marked targets are unchanged. The geometric rate corollary assumes the same labeled right-angled certificate as the complete-source theorem. Let N=2m>=4,d=N-1, c_j=2cos((2j+1)pi/N), s_j=2sin(jpi/N). In the actual face monomial basis, Omega z^j=c_j z^j-s_j^2(x+y)z^(j-1)-s_js_(j-1)xy z^(j-2). Use the [original homogeneous compiler](../papers/filling-bounds/README.md). Let chi_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2 and V_N(z)=chi_N(z)(z-Omega)^(-1), its polynomial resolvent numerator. Let P=-H_(V_N(-2)) be the positive Fejer homogeneous polynomial. The exact fixed-root resolvent convention is that of the [spectral derivative theorem](actual_spectral_total_derivative_source.md). Every path goes from its input j to its output i using steps1 or2; its middle exponents are b^i c^(d-j). A k-step path contributes its positive edge product times product_(unvisited r)(2+c_r), with the usual binomial expansion of its one-step factors (x+y). Split P=P_cross+P_left+P_right by cross: i<=m-1 and j>=m; left: j<=m-1; right: i>=m. These three classes partition the actual path set. Equivalently the cross part consists of monomials whose b and c exponents are both<=m-1. The two other classes have respectively c exponent>=m or b exponent>=m. Thus the decomposition is also by disjoint monomial supports, without any cancellation or selection of a new physical state. The three polynomials are parts of the original homogeneous coupon; they are not asserted separately to be covariant Casimir coupons or physical-head projections. The identity between the original source and the coefficient of their SUM is the frozen compiler identity. ## 1. Exact coefficientwise comparison for the entire cross part Put c_*=-2cos(pi/N), delta=2+c_*=4sin^2(pi/(2N)). The two minimum diagonal entries are c_(m-1)=c_m=c_*. At spectral value c_* the polynomial numerator has a nonzero path exactly when it visits BOTH indices m-1,m: otherwise its unused-factor product contains a zero. Call the resulting positive polynomial B=|H_(V_N(c_*))|_coef. For a path visiting both central indices, its coefficient at -2 divided by its coefficient in B is a subproduct of (2+c_r)/(c_r-c_*), r notin{m-1,m}. Every ratio is>=1, and the product of ALL such ratios is exactly C_N=[4/delta^2]/[chi''(c_*)/2] =4(4-delta)/(delta N^2)<2. (1) Here chi(-2)=4 and chi''(c_*)/2=N^2/[delta(4-delta)]. The bound delta N^2>=8 follows from the chord bound for sin on[0,pi/4]. Consequently B<=P_both<=C_N B coefficientwise. Every cross path that misses one of the central indices has exactly one crossing two-step: either m->m-2 or m+1->m-1. Split that step into two consecutive one-steps. This produces a path visiting both central indices, with the SAME input/output and total face degree. Its other edges and unused factors are unchanged; only the missed central factor delta is removed. If the original two-step starts at j0, its edge is s_(j0)s_(j0-1)xy and the repaired pair is s_(j0)^2s_(j0-1)^2(x+y)^2. Since xy<= (x+y)^2/2 coefficientwise, original path <= delta/[2s_(j0)s_(j0-1)] * repaired path =delta/[8cos(pi/N)] * repaired path. (2) A repaired path has at most TWO original preimages (merging either of those two pairs). Hence B <= P_cross <= C_N[1+delta/(4cos(pi/N))] B <3B. (3) The last bound uses N>=4, delta<=2-sqrt2 and cos(pi/N)>=sqrt2/2. All statements are coefficientwise, so they remain true at zero protected faces and after every original shared coefficient extraction. Let H_M be the actual maximal complete-channel contribution to H_(L_N), including N k_M beta_M^2 D_M(x,b,y)D_M(x,c,y)Ptilde_1(x,y), M=m-1. The exact paired derivative formula gives H_M=2B/N. Thus (N/2)H_M <= P_cross <= (3N/2)H_M. (4) Here beta and D are the literal factors of the [complete-circle polynomial theorem](actual_complete_circle_positive_face_polynomial.md). This includes the forced factor x+y and the actual multiplicity k_M=2. It is a comparison within the original source coefficient, not after choosing independent local radii. For a diagram with the stated geometric certificate, the all-cross term of the entire marked Fejer source has exactly the [known complete-volume exponential rate](general_signed_augmented_source_volume.md), with only fixed-diagram polynomial factors between its two bounds. At odd N the full positive endpoint numerator is already N times the simple maximal complete coupon, so its whole coefficient has that rate directly. The forest remainder treated here is specific to even levels. ## 2. Exact shared degree restriction on the remainder Expand the whole positive product by choosing cross,left,right at each original port. A noncross port puts at least m units into exactly one of its two middle faces: c for left, b for right. Draw its middle-graph edge pointing to that overloaded face. Each ordinary face has target d=2m-1, so it cannot receive TWO such arrows. Each protected face has target0, so it receives none. The original flat-plat middle graph has the [frozen gap description](../papers/triangular-insertion/README.md): each odd gap is a path of distinct bounded faces; each internal even gap is a cycle based at the SAME exterior face u, with its other faces unique to that gap. Therefore every selected-edge cycle contains u. An orientation with indegree<=1 at each vertex and indegree(u)=0 cannot exist on such a cycle: its equal numbers of edges and vertices would force indegree1 everywhere. This includes the length-two multicycles. Thus every nonzero remainder term is a ROOTED FOREST of noncross middle edges. Each component has exactly one indegree-zero root; any protected face in that component must be that root. Geometry independently checked this use of the frozen gap lemma. No free re-marking, smoothing order, or graph-to-plat adapter is used. This is the precise remaining positive source problem: bound the shared marked coefficient for these one-sided forest components, with the cross coupons on their complement. The cross comparison(4) does not estimate their weights. Local positive-radius estimates can be too large and are not substituted for this shared problem. ## 3. Exact half-size factorization, without an asymptotic conclusion For a left path all visited rows are in0,...,m-1, so every upper-half diagonal factor is unused. Their product is exactly2, since the two halves have equal products and chi(-2)=4. Moreover c^(d-j)=c^m c^(m-1-j). Consequently P_left=2c^m times the degree-(m-1) positive polynomial resolvent numerator of the literal lower m-row triangular block, at spectral value -2. The analogous upper block gives P_right with the factor b^m. All original sine coefficients are still evaluated at level N, not at level m. Replacing them by a level-m source would be a new, unproved step. The factorization explains the overloaded-face condition but does not yet identify an entropy or an actual smoothed representation for the forest. In particular the already proved L_1 smoothing gap cannot be applied merely because the selected middle graph is a forest. ## Validation and remaining scope The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_fejer_cross_half_source_reduction.py) checks the complete positive path sum, the central coefficient comparison, the repair and half-block identities, and actual original gap charts. [Results](../experiments/actual_fejer_cross_half_source_reduction_results.json) include nonzero marked-target support terms with noncross ports: the forest contribution does not vanish merely by this graph argument. The source interface of the path representation is separately audited against the original coproduct matrices; these new checks do not relabel that earlier test as a new independent physical-matrix construction. The positive path partition is not a covariant complete-colored image or a half-colored tensor. The scalar identity does not justify an $L^1$ smoothing argument for the half-block forest.

title: Diagonal Fejer ports reduce to a true identity smoothing
status: Literal identity forests and smoothed incidence constraints
text: # Diagonal Fejer ports reduce to a true identity smoothing 31 October 2026. diagonal and identity-forest reduction. This keeps the original protected targets and all remaining cross/left/right data. It does not factor arbitrary Green ports across matching/matching digon cuts. ## 1. Polynomial cost and the fixed-label distinction At N=2m,d=N-1 the FULL diagonal part of the positive endpoint numerator is exactly P_diag(b,c)=sum_(i=0)^d (4/a_i)b^i c^(d-i), a_i=4cos^2(pi(i+1/2)/N). Thus coefficientwise H_1<=P_diag<=C N^2 H_1, H_1=sum_(i=0)^d b^i c^(d-i). (1) Here C is absolute. The root at the half-integer sample closest to N/2 gives min a_i=4sin^2(pi/(2N)), so (1) is immediate. A fixed LEFT or RIGHT diagonal label includes only its corresponding half of the i range. For such a label retain ONLY the upper bound by C N^2 H_1. Equality of exponential rates with the full identity kernel is asserted only after summing BOTH actual diagonal types. At fixed diagram size the product cost remains polynomial. At the limiting entropy level a diagonal port has exactly q=(0,mu,1-mu,0), E=0, or its actual reflection. Enlarging its two possible half ranges to all identity loads sigma_b,sigma_c>=0, sigma_b+sigma_c=1 is therefore valid for an upper-bound reduction, without any phase or entropy cost. No remaining one-sided port is changed. ## 2. Feasibility forces the diagonal middle graph to be a forest Take any selected set D of diagonal ports in a feasible limiting source flow. Its middle b-c edges lie in the original gap graph. The only possible cycles are the entire internal even-gap cycles, each containing the protected exterior vertex u. If a component has n vertices and at least n edges, its identity edge loads already sum to at least n. Its vertices have total target at most n-1, since it contains u; all remaining local loads are nonnegative. This is impossible. Hence the diagonal middle graph is a forest, and its literal identity smoothing is connected. A tree cannot contain two protected vertices either: its n-1 edge loads would exceed the at most n-2 available targets. Thus each tree has at most ONE protected vertex directly from the load count. For a tree with n vertices the sum of its internal edge loads is n-1. The total remaining load is therefore1 when all its vertices are ordinary, and0 when it contains a protected vertex. Collapse that actual tree to one face of the same ordinary/protected type. Push all remaining local incidences to their resulting face label. Every remaining port retains its own local exponent vector and E. Conversely, for any nonnegative remaining loads with the collapsed face target, the lift of the identity loads is UNIQUE. Root a tree at its protected vertex if present, otherwise anywhere. At an edge parent->child let L be the total remaining load in the child subtree. Then assign sigma_child=1-L, sigma_parent=L. (2) Since a subtree load lies in[0,1] (or is zero in a protected tree), these are valid identity loads. Summing the subtree balances proves (2), and subtracting them proves every original face equation. No local E or entropy changes in this transport. The same is an EXACT finite coefficient identity. For an arbitrary remaining polynomial with nonnegative exponents, a surviving monomial has total degree d on each ordinary merged tree and0 on a protected tree. At an internal edge its endpoint identity degrees are j_child=d-L_degree(subtree), j_parent=L_degree(subtree). Both lie in[0,d]. Each H_1 coefficient is one, so there is no counting multiplicity. Consequently extracting the original target after inserting all H_1 factors equals extracting the ordinary d targets of the polynomial obtained by IDENTIFYING the face variables in each tree. This is the actual source-preserving identity smoothing, not a formal zero-radius substitution. Combined with (1), it bounds any fixed diagonal sector by the true smoothed remaining positive source with polynomial cost. ## 3. Two useful exclusions after deleting ALL diagonal ports Suppose D contains every diagonal port of the particular limiting flow. The resulting white triangular cellulation has NO loop edge. To prove this, choose the mark-free side of a proposed loop at a. If it contains v interior white vertices, Euler counting gives 2v-1 shaded triangles inside. The dual bridge must be MATCHING: the odd number of dual vertices and one matching incidence per vertex force its single crossing edge to be matching. There are v-1 whole retained ports inside and one inside triangle of that bridge port. Its middle is inside; both outer incidences are at a. The v ordinary interior targets sum to v. The whole ports supply at most v-1 there, so the bridge middle must carry the FULL unit, and every other incidence of that port must be zero. It is therefore a diagonal endpoint, contrary to its retention. Likewise no remaining MATCHING edge joins the two protected merged faces. Both outer loads of that port would be zero. For a one-sided port this forces nu-mu=0, hence diagonal; for a cross port the two middle loads would have to be1/2 each, but its actual finite cross support needs one outer unit. At the limiting functional this is the same full-diagonal load (1/2,1/2), with zero entropy. It can be included in D ONLY for the LIMITING entropy/load reduction: its zero entropy and identity load are the same. This does NOT apply the finite comparison (1) to that cross sector, which still needs its one outer unit. The separate [full-kernel entropy theorem](actual_fejer_full_kernel_entropy_identity_reduction.md) supplies the source RATE comparison for these limiting endpoints. The finite inequality in section1 is still not applied to a cross sector. The combinatorial no-protected-matching conclusion therefore concerns the enlarged LIMITING identity reduction when those cross endpoints are included. The remaining cellulation may have parallel edges and degree-two faces. Those are not excluded by this count and must not be replaced by a simple graph without retaining the actual topology. ## 4. What decomposes and what still does not A MAIN/MAIN two-edge cut leaves complete ports on each side. On its mark-free side, the number of internal ordinary targets equals the number of contained ports. Total-degree conservation then forces ALL incidences on its two boundary faces to have zero load. Thus this cut has the same zero-boundary separation as the complete-source angle proof; absolute local entropy constants are unchanged. A MATCHING/MATCHING cut is different. Two retained Green ports can cross it. Let ell>=0 be the total load that the v-1 whole inside ports send to the two boundary faces. The exact balance is q_inside,1+q_inside,2=1+ell. A cross middle is at most1/2, so in the old complete proof this forced ell=0 and both inside middles to equal1/2. General Green ports may have asymmetric middle loads and may also have ell>0. Therefore the old independent block capacity factorization does NOT extend by the same argument. This is an explicit remaining coupling, not a scalar normalization issue or a reason to alter the original support. A possible way around it is a DIRECT signed developing disk on the loopless triangular cellulation with parallel edges. Its vertex links are still topological circles/intervals, so the signed center holonomy argument should not require simpliciality. Repeated edges then develop to the same circle contact, which the global oriented chain permits. This still requires proving the correct treatment of structurally forced zero degrees and any escaping ordinary multipliers. The original representation must be restored by actual identity meridians at the deleted ports. If their outer product becomes nonparabolic, its recorded flag and the proved zero-volume filling cap must be used; an artificial x/y tangency must NOT be inserted. The exact reductions above do not yet show that the reduced mixed-E maximum is attained on the regular signed-development stratum, nor bound the remaining coupled matching cuts. No general diagonal-boundary volume inequality is asserted. The full-kernel companion gives the rate-level CROSS-seam reduction. No independent Green-block factorization across matching cuts is asserted.

title: Continuous full-kernel entropy and exact identity reduction of maxima
status: Full-simplex entropy and exact identity reduction
text: # Continuous full-kernel entropy and exact identity reduction of maxima Completion: the [general endpoint theorem](general_fejer_endpoint_source_volume.md) assembles this local result into the actual augmented-volume equality. Its [unique geometric maximum](actual_fejer_unique_geometric_maximizer.md) gives concentration; the original filling conjecture remains open. 31 October 2026. full-kernel entropy and identity-reduction theorem. This uses the [proved uniform closed local coefficient limits](actual_fejer_half_block_entropy.md). It does not assume that an infeasible fixed half-label pattern becomes feasible. It sums the full positive local kernel before forgetting its type. ## 1. The full local coefficient entropy is continuous For q=(X,B,C,Y)>=0, X+B+C+Y=1, define h(q) as follows. If C>=1/2, put h=E(B,1-C,X). If B>=1/2, put h=E(C,1-B,X). If B,C<=1/2, put h(q)=max_s { Ctri(s,B,1/2-B-s) +Ctri(X-s,C,1/2-C-X+s) }, (1) where max(0,X+C-1/2)<=s<=min(X,1/2-B), and Ctri(alpha)=V(2pi alpha)/(2pi) is the proved triangle entropy. The conventions agree on every overlap. At C=1/2 the second triangle is pure-middle, of entropy zero, and (1) is Ctri(X,B,Y), which is EXACTLY E(B,1/2,X). The B=1/2 boundary is reflected. At B=C=1/2 all entropies are zero. The interval in (1) has continuous endpoints, so compact maximization and continuity of Ctri prove h is continuous on the whole simplex. The closed half-block theorem proves the same for its two one-sided pieces. In particular h(0,B,1-B,0)=0 for every 0<=B<=1. (2) Let p_N(n) be the coefficient of the FULL positive polynomial P in a nonnegative local exponent vector n of total degree d=N-1. Every such coefficient is positive. The exact supports partition all these vectors into cross (both middle<=m-1), left (c>=m), and right (b>=m). The uniform half-block limits, positive cross convolution and B_cross<=P_cross<=3B_cross give sup_(n>=0, sum n=d) |N^-1 log p_N(n)-h(n/d)| ->0. (3) For the cross convolution the allowed outer-split interval has integer endpoints. Every limiting split has an O(1/N) integer approximation; there are O(N) summands. Uniform continuity of Ctri therefore makes its log-sum rate uniformly the maximum (1), including the terminal faces. The finite forced outer unit is retained in this argument. The changes from i/N,j/N to n/d are O(1/N) in the closed parameters, so continuity justifies that normalization. This is NOT a bound on an individual cross term by H1 at zero outer degree. ## 2. A shared variational theorem without fixed half labels Take any fixed finite incidence graph of these homogeneous degree-d polynomials, allowing repeated global labels among a port's four separate incidences. Give every ordinary face target d and each protected face target zero. Let P be the nonnegative real flow polytope with port supplies1, ordinary face demands1 and protected demands0. If its total supplies/demands disagree, or the polytope is empty, the coefficient is zero. Otherwise lim_(even N) N^-1 log [original target] product_e P_e =max_(q in P) sum_e h(q_e). (4) The upper bound follows by (3) and the polynomial number of arrays. For the lower bound, take a maximizing q and multiply by d. This gives EXACT integer node balances with real edge values. Fractional-cycle rounding inside each floor/ceiling interval gives an integral flow, with error at most one per incidence. The local polynomial contains EVERY degree-d monomial, so this rounded array is an actual positive term, regardless of which half label it receives at that level. Continuity of h and (3) give its desired rate. Repeated incidences remain parallel arcs in the rounding graph. Thus (4) agrees with the previously proved W_D on the original diagram, since both are limits of the SAME source. It does not deny the original eventual-feasibility test for FIXED patterns; it avoids assigning a fixed pattern at the seams, where h has the same continuous value. The formulation also applies to actual identity-smoothed incidence maps even when they are not simplicial right-angled certificates. No arbitrary graph-to-original-plat adapter is asserted. The same argument permits some local H1 factors. At such an identity port remove its two outer incidence arcs; the remaining middle loads sum to one and its coefficient entropy is identically zero. All its allowed coefficients are one, and fractional-cycle rounding respects this reduced incidence graph. Thus the corresponding mixed flow maximum is the ACTUAL mixed positive coefficient rate as well. ## 3. A maximum with pure-middle ports is an exact lower-port problem Let q attain (4), and let D be ANY collection of its pure-middle ports, including ordinary one-sided diagonals and a pure-middle cross endpoint (0,1/2,1/2,0). Replace those full local P factors by H1. The SAME q is feasible in the mixed identity flow polytope and has the same entropy by (2). Therefore the mixed maximum is at least W_D. Conversely, coefficientwise H1<=P_diag<=P, so its actual mixed coefficient rate is at most W_D. Hence W_D = rate of the actual mixed source with H1 on D. (5) This equality is about the FULL summed local kernel and its rate. It makes no false finite comparison between a cross boundary monomial and H1. In particular it repairs the pure-middle cross seam only after (3)--(4), without relabeling an infeasible fixed source pattern. Feasibility forces the diagonal middle graph to be a forest: every possible original even-gap cycle contains the protected exterior, and its unit edge supplies exceed that component's ordinary demands. A tree cannot contain two protected vertices either. The [exact subtree coefficient identity](actual_fejer_diagonal_identity_forest_reduction.md) therefore identifies the mixed H1 coefficient with the true connected identity smoothing, with all face targets and no multiplicity. Thus (5) is a genuine reduction to fewer remaining positive P ports. What it does NOT yet prove is that the resulting non-simple smoothed incidence graph has a regular entropy maximizer or that its W is bounded by the original complete volume. Matching/matching cuts can still carry asymmetric Green loads; their complete-source block factorization is not assumed. The remaining geometry must retain the actual smoothing and, when restoring deleted cusps, its literal identity meridians. The rate-level identity reduction does not give a volume bound for every nonsimple smoothed source or a quantum filling asymptotic.

title: The actual Fejér half block: uniform coefficient entropy
text: # The actual Fejér half block: uniform coefficient entropy , 31 October 2026. This gives the exact level-N half-block recurrence, its weighted rate, and the uniform exponential rate of EVERY coefficient, including the boundary degrees. It also fixes the complete-triangle normalization and disproves one proposed endpoint-convexity shortcut. These are local source theorems; no shared forest bound, representation, or filling-cycle conclusion is asserted. All limits below run through every even N tending to infinity. ## 1. The original finite polynomial and its exact recurrence Let N=2m>=4, d=N-1, M=m-1, theta=pi/N, and c_j=2cos((2j+1)theta), s_j=2sin(j theta), a_j=2+c_j=4cos^2((j+1/2)theta), product_(j=0)^M a_j=2. Use the [original homogeneous source](../papers/filling-bounds/README.md) and its [positive cross/half decomposition](actual_fejer_cross_half_source_reduction.md). Thus P=-H_(V_N(-2)), where V_N is the actual polynomial resolvent numerator, and P_left contains exactly the physical paths j to i with 0<=i<=j<=M. Their middle monomial is b^i c^(d-j). These pieces are not separately asserted to be covariant coupons. For an interval i+1,...,j let K_(i,j) be its positive tiling continuant. A monomer at r has weight s_r^2(x+y); a dimer ending at r has weight s_r s_(r-1) a_(r-1)xy. The latter includes the UNUSED intermediate diagonal. Set K_(i,i)=1 and Q_(i,j)=K_(i,j)/product_(r=i+1)^j a_r. The actual path expansion is exactly P_left=2 sum_(i<=j) b^i c^(d-j) product_(r<i)a_r product_(r>j)^M a_r K_(i,j) =4 sum_(i<=j) b^i c^(d-j) Q_(i,j)/a_i, (1) Q_(i,i)=1, Q_(i,i+1)=alpha_(i+1), Q_(i,j)=alpha_j Q_(i,j-1)+beta_j Q_(i,j-2), alpha_j=(s_j^2/a_j)(x+y), beta_j=(s_j s_(j-1)/a_j)xy. (2) All absent negative-index terms are zero. The original level remains N, not m. Define the strictly positive coefficients A_N(i,j,k)=[x^k y^(j-i-k)]Q_(i,j), 0<=k<=j-i. The corresponding coefficient of P_left is (4/a_i)A_N. The multiplier 4/a_i is between a positive constant and CN^2, uniformly in every row. Right paths are obtained by the literal row reflection j -> d-j and b <-> c, with the same x,y polynomial. ## 2. Uniform weighted rate, retaining both physical endpoints Fix positive x,y, uniformly on compact positive sets. The limiting Perron root at t=j/N is L(t;x,y)=[(x+y)sin^2(pi t)+sin(pi t) sqrt((x+y)^2 sin^2(pi t)+4xy cos^2(pi t))] /[2cos^2(pi t)], L^2-(x+y)tan^2(pi t)L-xy tan^2(pi t)=0, L>0. (3) It increases strictly from zero to infinity. Uniformly over ALL rows, sup_(0<=i<=j<=M) |N^-1 log Q_(i,j)(x,y) -integral_(i/N)^(j/N) log L(t;x,y)dt| ->0. (4) Here is a proof with no endpoint gap. Fix eta>0. On eta N<=j<=(1/2-eta)N the coefficients of (2) stay in a compact positive set, converge uniformly to their limits, and vary by O_eta(1/N) per step. For a constant recurrence q_l=alpha q_(l-1)+beta q_(l-2), q_0=1,q_1=alpha, one has q_l=(lambda_+^(l+1)-lambda_-^(l+1))/(lambda_+-lambda_-), lambda_-<0<lambda_+, |lambda_-|/lambda_+<=r_eta<1. Hence c_eta lambda_+^l<=q_l<=C_eta lambda_+^l, and the corresponding transfer-matrix powers obey the same upper exponential bound. Partition an arbitrary interior interval into blocks of length floor(sqrt N), with shorter end blocks. Positivity compares each block with its minimum and maximum constant coefficients. Retaining only tilings which do not cross a block boundary gives the lower bound; transfer matrices give the upper bound. The logarithmic block overhead is O_eta(sqrt N+1), and the accumulated variation cost is O_eta(sqrt N). Thus (4) holds uniformly for all interior intervals, including short ones. The omitted endpoint intervals cost at most C eta N log(2/eta)+C log N (5) in absolute logarithmic size. For the upper bound use transfer norm at most product_j(1+alpha_j+beta_j). Near zero these coefficients are bounded; near M the denominator a_j is comparable to ((M-j+1/2)/N)^2, giving the sum of logarithms C eta N+2 sum_(r<=eta N)log(N/r). For the lower bound concatenate only monomers on the omitted sites. Near zero alpha_j>=c(j/N)^2, and near M it is bounded below by a positive constant; their negative logarithms satisfy (5). These arguments also apply to intervals entirely inside an endpoint portion. Finally log L=log t+O(1) near zero and log L=-2log(1/2-t)+O(1) near one half, so the omitted limiting integrals are O(eta log(2/eta)). Let N tend to infinity and then eta to zero. This proves (4), locally uniformly in the positive weights. Write F(x,b,y) for the ABSOLUTELY normalized source triangle potential in [the original action theorem](actual_original_boundary_stationary_character.md), section6. Equation (1), (4), and polynomially many summands imply lim N^-1 log P_left =max_(0<=mu<=nu<=1/2) [mu log b+(1-nu)log c+integral_mu^nu log L(t)dt]. (6) For fixed mu the expression is convex in nu, so its maximum is at nu=mu or nu=1/2. The latter is (log c)/2+H(x,b,y), where H=max_(0<=mu<=1/2) [mu log b+integral_mu^(1/2)log L(t)dt]. The unique maximizer obeys L(mu)=b, or tan(pi mu)=b/sqrt(b(x+y)+xy). Its envelope derivative with respect to log b is mu, exactly the source triangle middle angle divided by 2pi. Both H-(log b)/2 and F-(log b)/2 tend to zero as b tends to infinity: for H use the logarithmic endpoint tail, and for F use its original positive logdet integral and integrable cos^(-2) endpoint bound. Therefore H=F with NO missing additive constant. Also F>=(log b)/2, from the actual determinant's b^M term. Consequently lim N^-1 log P_left =max(log c,F(x,b,y)+(log c)/2), lim N^-1 log P_right=max(log b,F(x,c,y)+(log b)/2), lim N^-1 log P=max(F(x,b,y)+F(x,c,y),log b,log c). (7) The last formula uses the exact cross comparison. All weights in (7) are positive and fixed before N. It is NOT a coefficientwise bound by a complete coupon plus an identity coupon, and it licenses no exchange of infimum over shared radii with a maximum over local branches. ## 3. Actual coefficients in strict interiors Put D={0<=mu<=nu<=1/2, 0<=xi<=nu-mu}, g(t,l)=log L(t;exp(l),1) =l/2+log tan(pi t)+asinh(tan(pi t)cosh(l/2)), Phi(mu,nu,l)=integral_mu^nu g(t,l)dt, E(mu,nu,xi)=inf_(l real)[Phi(mu,nu,l)-xi l]. (8) First consider compact subsets of 0<mu<nu<1/2, 0<xi<nu-mu. Normalize Q_(i,j) by product_(v=i+1)^j a'_v, where a'_v=s_v^2/a_v. The resulting monic degree-r polynomial, r=j-i, satisfies p_0=1, p_1=x+y, p_r=(x+y)p_(r-1)+gamma_r xy p_(r-2), gamma_r=a_(i+r-1)/(s_(i+r)s_(i+r-1))>0. (9) Substituting x/y=-z^2 and dividing by z^r gives the Jacobi recurrence q_r(t)=t q_(r-1)(t)-gamma_r q_(r-2)(t), t=z^-1-z. Its symmetric tridiagonal matrix has positive off-diagonal entries, so its roots are real and simple. The map z>0 ->z^-1-z is bijective onto the real line. Thus p_r(x,1) has exactly r negative real roots. The compact-interval bounds on gamma give a uniform Jacobi norm bound, placing all these roots in a compact negative interval away from zero and infinity. The polynomial is reciprocal as well. After a bounded tilt x=exp(l), y=1, its coefficient distribution is therefore a sum of r independent Bernoulli variables with probabilities uniformly away from zero and one. For k/r in a compact subset of (0,1), the unique exact-mean tilt stays bounded. Its probability at that mean is comparable to r^(-1/2): Fourier inversion has a Gaussian expansion on |theta|<=r^(-2/5), variance comparable to r, and modulus bounded by exp[-c r sin^2(theta/2)] elsewhere. Bounded third moments give the relative Gaussian error o(1). The logarithm of this probability is therefore O(log N). The weighted theorem (4) and this exact coefficient identity give N^-1 log A_N(i,j,k) -> E(mu,nu,xi) (10) for every sequence i/N->mu,j/N->nu,k/N->xi in a strict interior, locally uniformly there. To justify convergence of the exact tilts, the normalized log polynomials are convex and converge locally uniformly to differentiable strictly convex Phi. The two secant inequalities imply convergence of their first derivatives on compact intervals; the unique limiting tilt satisfies Phi_l=xi. The same root/variance bounds imply Phi_ll>0. No derivative of an unsupported weighted asymptotic has been taken. ## 4. The closed-domain theorem The function E is continuous on ALL of D, and sup_(0<=i<=j<=M,0<=k<=j-i) |N^-1 log A_N(i,j,k)-E(i/N,j/N,k/N)| ->0. (11) This also holds for the actual half-block coefficient (4/a_i)A_N, since its additional logarithm is uniformly O(log N). For continuity set q=nu-mu, B=2 integral_mu^nu log tan(pi t)dt, and delta_r(t)=asinh(tan(pi t)cosh(r/2))-r/2-log tan(pi t), r>=0. This is positive, decreases to zero, and is dominated by the integrable delta_0: it is -log t+O(1) at zero and tends to log2 at one half. Its full-interval integral tends to zero as r tends to infinity. Exactly, with a=min(xi,q-xi), E=B+inf_(r>=0)[a r+integral_mu^nu delta_r(t)dt]. (12) Hence B<=E<=B+integral_mu^nu delta_0, which proves E->0 uniformly as q->0. As a->0 choose a large fixed r first; (12) gives E-B->0 uniformly. Where a>=a0>0 the minimizer is restricted to a common compact r interval, so continuity follows by compact minimization. In particular E(mu,nu,0)=E(mu,nu,nu-mu)=B. For the uniform upper bound, every finite real l gives N^-1 log A_N<=N^-1 log Q_(i,j)(exp(l),1)-(k/N)l. At each point of D select a finite l within epsilon of its infimum, even when the infimum is reached only at infinity. Continuity gives a neighborhood where the same l works within 2epsilon. A finite cover of D and (4) for this finite set of tilts give the uniform upper bound. For the lower bound consider any sequence tending to a point with 0<xi<q. Trim to i'=max(i,ceil(eta N)), j'=min(j,floor((1/2-eta)N)), and set r'=j'-i', r=j-i, k'=floor(k r'/r). For small fixed eta, r'>0 and 0<=k-k'<=r-r'. Retain an arbitrary interior tiling and specified x- and y-monomers on the omitted sites. This is an actual subset of the original tilings, with no crossing dimer, and gives A_N(i,j,k)>=A_N(i',j',k') product_(omitted v)a'_v. (13) The omitted logarithmic cost is at most (5). Apply (10) to the strict retained interval, let N tend to infinity, and then eta to zero. Continuity gives the required lower rate. If xi=0 or q, including sequences whose integer k is not exactly extreme, the all-monomer term gives A_N>=binom(r,k) product a'_v>=product a'_v. Uniform log-sine/cosine Riemann estimates, including the upper half-step, give N^-1 log product_(v=i+1)^j a'_v =B(i/N,j/N)+O(log N/N). (14) This also handles q=0. Compactness turns these sequential lower bounds into the uniform statement (11). It is an exponential-rate theorem, not a relative amplitude or derivative asymptotic. ## 5. Exact endpoint normalization and a finite entropy formula Let R_M(b) be the original lower-block path numerator starting at M, with every ending b^i retained. Replace each unused spectral factor a_r, r<M, by a_r^*=c_r-c_*, where c_*=-2cos(pi/N), to obtain D_b=R_M^*(b). These definitions keep every original sine coefficient. The exact path comparisons give D_b<=R_M<=sqrt(C_N)D_b, C_N=4(4-delta)/(delta N^2)<2, delta=2-2cos(pi/N), [b^i x^k y^(M-i-k)]R_M=(2/a_i)A_N(i,M,k), B_cross=4(x+y)D_bD_c, B_cross<=P_cross<3B_cross. (15) For completeness, the comparison factor is the product over the lower unused rows of a_r/a_r^*, bounded by sqrt(C_N). Splitting the paired root path at its compulsory central one-step gives the last exact factorization. The recorded complete-channel identity implies D_b=C_front D_M(x,b,y), where D_M is the original determinant and C_front=product_(r<M)a_r^*=N/[2sin(pi/N)]. Thus this normalization differs from that determinant by only a polynomial scalar, not an unknown exponential constant. It follows uniformly on the ENTIRE triangle simplex that its actual coefficient entropy is C(alpha_x,alpha_b,alpha_y)=E(alpha_b,1/2,alpha_x), alpha_x+alpha_b+alpha_y=1/2, alpha_j>=0, C(alpha)=V(2pi alpha)/(2pi), V(theta)=2sum_j[Lambda(theta_j/2)+Lambda((pi-theta_j)/2)], Lambda(t)=-integral_0^t log|2sin w|dw. (16) The finite third degree is M-i-k, not N/2-i-k. Its bounded offset disappears only after (11) and uniform continuity. To prove the absolute last equality, for strict positive alpha choose x=tan(pi alpha_x), b=tan(pi alpha_b), y=tan(pi alpha_y). Their pairwise product sum is one. The unique maximizer in (6) with nu=1/2 is alpha_b, and the original triangle derivatives of F are exactly alpha_x,alpha_b,alpha_y. Differentiating this already proved smooth formula shows that log(x/y) is the correct minimizing tilt. Therefore E=F-sum alpha_j log L_j. The absolute source identity 2pi F=sum theta_j log L_j+V(theta) proves (16); continuity includes every boundary face. At a cross port the two triangular allocations and the ONE forced x-or-y unit in (15) must remain explicit before shared coefficient extraction. There is also a finite formula for the general E. For mu<nu put q=nu-mu, Dangle=2pi(xi-q/2), a=cos(pi mu), b0=cos(pi nu), kappa=sin Dangle/sqrt(a^2+b0^2-2a b0 cos Dangle), alpha_x(t)=1/4-t/2+asin(kappa cos(pi t))/(2pi), alpha_b(t)=t, alpha_y(t)=1/2-t-alpha_x(t). (17) Use the real principal arcsine. The domain |Dangle|<=pi q implies |kappa|<=1: the difference between the squared denominator and sin^2 Dangle is (cos Dangle-a b0)^2-(1-a^2)(1-b0^2)>=0. For strict outer degrees kappa=tanh(l/2) for the unique tilt, because direct integration gives alpha_x(t)=partial_l Phi(t,1/2,l) and Dangle=asin(kappa a)-asin(kappa b0). The right side is strictly increasing with the required range; this fixes the original branch after squaring. At xi=0,q take kappa=-1,+1. Subtracting the two correct endpoint Legendre identities gives E(mu,nu,xi)=C(alpha(mu))-C(alpha(nu)). (18) Set E=0 when mu=nu. This is a finite Lobachevsky evaluation on the whole closed domain. Its corresponding left degree vector is alpha(mu) on (x,b,y), minus alpha(nu) on (x,c,y), plus e_c. The output triangle can be written with generalized angles (-theta_x,2pi-theta_c,-theta_y); the Lobachevsky reflection identities give its negative V. This is a signed-angle identity, not a developing map, an independent geometric volume bound, or a cycle-selection rule. ## 6. The fixed-outer-degree endpoint convexity claim is false At l=0 one has g_l=1/2 and g_ll=sin(pi t)/4. At the balanced xi=(nu-mu)/2, the tilt is therefore zero. Hold mu and xi FIXED while varying nu. The exact Legendre Schur complement is E_(nu,nu)=pi cos(pi nu)/[sin(pi nu)(1-sin(pi nu))] -pi/[cos(pi mu)-cos(pi nu)]. (19) Indeed Phi_(nu,l)=1/2 and Phi_(l,l)=[cos(pi mu)-cos(pi nu)]/(4pi). At nu=1/4 the first term is pi/(1-1/sqrt2); for every 0<mu<1/4 the second term is larger. In particular mu=1/8,nu=1/4,xi=1/16 is a strict regular negative-curvature point. Choose a sufficiently small fixed rational epsilon>0. For all large even N use rounded i=N/8,k=N/16,j0=N/4 and jplus/minus=N(1/4+/-epsilon). The uniform coefficient theorem and (19) give, for the ACTUAL coefficients mathcal A_N(j)=(4/a_i)A_N(i,j,k), log mathcal A_N(j0) -[log mathcal A_N(jminus)+log mathcal A_N(jplus)]/2 >=c_epsilon N>0. (20) Thus coefficient log-convexity in this exact direction fails exponentially. The common source factor 4/a_i is retained. This does not disprove a shared forest bound: an exchange that changes other face degrees could behave differently. Holding the proportion xi/(nu-mu) fixed is a DIFFERENT direction and is not addressed by (19). Fixed-positive-radius endpoint convexity in (6) cannot be used after fixing xi without this Schur correction. ## 7. Validation and scope The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_fejer_half_block_entropy.py) and [saved results](../experiments/actual_fejer_half_block_entropy_results.json) retain independent original numerator comparisons, positive paths, and the absolute triangle anchor. Finite closed-boundary rate and coefficient-curvature profiles are diagnostics for the displayed proofs, not substitutes for uniform estimates. The exact source interface is also covered by the frozen numerator and cross-half audits linked above. The author run passes at 75 digits: 329 left and 329 right original numerator coefficients, 96 direct positive paths, 5 independent triangle anchors, 11 recurrence identities and 11 Jacobi/log-root identities, 52 actual negative roots, 12 closed-entropy integral reconstructions, and 64 extreme coefficient checks. It records 25 weighted-rate and 88 closed-coefficient profiles, and four increasing-level failures of the proposed coefficient log-convexity. The largest anchor or entropy reconstruction error is below 7e-76. These finite checks do not prove the uniform limits; those are proved above. No shared entropy maximum is evaluated here; in particular no local max/min exchange, general forest-volume inequality, or signed long-filled knot asymptotic is claimed.

title: Actual representation and signed volume from hybrid tight-cut pieces
status: Original group and relative volume from hybrid pieces
text: # Actual representation and signed volume from hybrid tight-cut pieces 31 October 2026. conditional representation and relative-volume theorem. The [hybrid tight-cut theorem](actual_fejer_hybrid_tight_cut_reduction.md) supplies the finite-flow input. This note proves the geometric and original-source topology step for its exact output, without an independent Green-block capacity factorization. It concerns the positive endpoint source, not the original phase-sensitive filled-knot period. ## 1. Precisely the decomposition data required Start with the actual connected identity smoothing of the original certified flat plat. Its full positive-kernel maximum is the same W_D by the [full-kernel identity reduction, §3](actual_fejer_full_kernel_entropy_identity_reduction.md) and its [literal forest contraction](actual_fejer_diagonal_identity_forest_reduction.md). At a chosen maximum, remove every pure-middle port by that reduction and represent terminal one-sided seams as CROSS at the same full-kernel entropy value. Use the following output of the hybrid tight-cut construction: * The remaining loopless white triangular cellulation is cut along actual digon disks into a finite tree of triangular spheres. * Each child is marked at the two adjacent vertices of its cut boundary; the root retains the original protected pair. Boundary loads on each mark-free side are zero, so the exact entropy is the SUM of the piece entropies, with the original triangle constants and multiplicities. * No GREEN (strict one-sided) port is cut. Every port crossing a matching cut is CROSS. Its entropy is the additive C(alpha)+C(beta), and its two original triangles are retained separately on their actual sides. No new physical auxiliary circle is inferred from closing a piece. * A strict relative hybrid witness on each piece, with the existing strict Green row margins, excludes every ordinary zero corner by the proved epsilon-log entropy gains. Finite row-space multipliers then give positive finite ordinary curvatures, protected curvatures zero, and the actual local tangent-circle angles. Each ordinary signed star has total0 or2pi; only the two forced marked lines degenerate. These are explicit inputs here. The [hybrid flow proof, §§4–5](actual_fejer_hybrid_tight_cut_reduction.md) and the [corner expansions and multiplier argument, §§2–4](actual_fejer_nondiagonal_maximizer_regularity.md) supply their finite support and regularity content. In particular an arbitrary digon decomposition with GREEN ports cut in half would NOT satisfy them. ## 2. Each piece has one actual signed circle development Apply the [cooriented developing-disk argument, §2](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_fejer_marked_signed_development.md) to each piece, with the following explicit multigraph and boundary adaptations. Its new protected edge need not be MAIN. If it is MAIN, the two adjacent triangles have protected middles, so they cannot be negative. If the edge was a MATCHING cut, its two incident triangles are the retained CROSS halves and are again positive. Their new protected outer loads are zero, so each is the fixed two-line triangle (0,0,pi). Thus in both cases the two marked triangles supply the genuine common strip. At a matching cut, formally pair the two boundary CROSS half-triangles along the new matching edge. This retains the cubic perfect-matching incidence needed for parity; it creates NO physical coupon. A GREEN matching edge between the new protected vertices would have both outer loads zero, hence be a pure-middle port already removed. Every other parallel marked edge gives an allowed MAIN/MAIN or CROSS MATCHING/MATCHING cut. Exhaustive splitting therefore makes the remaining marked line/line edge unique. Remove one positive marked triangle. The remaining abstract complex is a triangulated disk. A finite/finite edge fixes an orientation-preserving Euclidean gluing by its two distinct ordered centers; a line/finite edge fixes it by its COORIENTED line and center. The unique line/line edge is on the boundary and is never used for an underdetermined gluing. Around each interior finite vertex the holonomy fixes its center and rotates by its signed star angle, either zero or 2pi, so it is the identity. These vertex loops generate the dual disk's cycles. Boundary fans propagate the SAME two cooriented lines. The final finite circle touches both inward sides, forcing its radius to be half their shared distance and closing the omitted triangle. This argument uses disk topology and nondegenerate edge data, not simplicity of the remaining finite-edge graph. Double-triangle pieces have zero entropy and zero volume and are represented by two lines and one tangent circle. Every piece therefore gives its ONE family of oriented white planes, with each adjacent pair distinct and tangent. Its developed image may fold. Its signed two-ball chain volume is exactly the sum of sigma V for its original triangles, by the [signed cyclic-polygon and contact-triangle identities, §§1–2](actual_fejer_signed_cut_ball_regulator.md). ## 3. Glue the pieces, retaining every original port pairing Root the actual cut tree. A child's marked ordered tangent pair is mapped to its already assigned parent pair by an orientation-preserving Mobius map. Explicitly send their common contacts to infinity; both ordered pairs become opposite cooriented parallel planes. Positive scale and translation match their width and position. The remaining horizontal translation is free. Each interior white label belongs to one piece; shared boundary label occurrences form connected subtrees. Recursion therefore gives ONE reflection for every actual smoothed white face. No independent reflection is chosen at different occurrences of a face. The free translations can be chosen generically to avoid accidental coincidences of distinct nonadjacent white circles. This is not an embedding requirement; all adjacent tangent pairs already remain nondegenerate. The original main prefixes telescope and cups/caps give their literal inverse pairs, exactly as before the cuts. For a GREEN port both triangles lie in the same piece, so its actual source collar C is already supplied by the [literal signed Green formula, §3](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_fejer_marked_signed_development.md) and is conjugated by that piece's ONE gluing map. For an original CROSS port whose two triangles lie in different pieces, its outer white pair x,y is common. Let P=r_y r_x=-I+H. It is noncentral parabolic. Each ordered triangle gives an actual raw first meridian A with trace-2 and with Tr((P+I)A)=4. After H=[[0,h],[0,0]], h!=0, this says A_21=4/h. Trace and determinant determine the other entries from A_11. The centralizer I+tH acts simply transitively on these pairs. Hence there is a UNIQUE actual C mapping its recorded input first meridian to its recorded output first meridian; it maps the second as well because the whole ordered product P is common. Equivalently C sends ALL THREE original contact flags: O=x/y is fixed, C1=x/b goes to C0=x/c, and C2=b/y goes to C3=c/y. It is precisely the original untwisted shaded pairing within the first ball. The second ball uses r_u C r_u with ONE global r_u, and the inverse is used on the reverse pairing. This does NOT pair the two artificial halves used to close a child piece into a new physical coupon. The original port may continue to connect different pieces after the geometric cut. Its raw auxiliary meridian is -C^-1, with the original physical lift C^-1. The actual four-crossing threading word returns it and transports both ordered main ports. Thus every original smoothed Morse relation holds. The two halves' independent local radii are not asserted to form a regular source-gradient chart at that boundary port; the boundary representation is constructed by its ACTUAL three-point relation and its globally computed entropy, not by selecting an unproved finite-sum or local re-framing branch. All actual main meridians are noncentral parabolic. At any retained auxiliary cusp, C^-1 and its actual preferred longitude P are in the same parabolic translation centralizer. This remains true if C=I, because P remains noncentral. Thus the entire peripheral subgroup preserves the contact and its canonical horosphere. ## 4. The original relative fundamental chain has the summed volume Use the TWO original cut balls of the actual smoothed projection and their literal proper digon-cut disks. Under the common reflection assignment the two ends of each disk are the SAME tangent-pair contact. Their canonical pair horosphere is common. The [finite incidence and short-edge construction, §4](actual_smoothed_block_representation_volume.md) places all disk replacements at height T with bounded horizontal coordinates, preserving the actual shaded/white pairings. Added tetrahedra have an edge of length O(1/T), so |Vol tetra|<=2pi ell cosh^2 ell makes their total volume vanish. Cut-disk collapse has relative degree one in the abstract domain. It leaves every original shaded triangle uncut and retains its actual C map even when its partner lies in a different block. These are geometric chain operations, not source factorizations. Each resulting abstract piece is developed by its assigned signed circle family. Cone its white/shaded faces to its own marked boundary contact; the signed cyclic fan identity gives its first-ball volume (1/2)sum sigma V, including winding-zero white polygons. The ONE global reflection r_u develops the second original ball, reversing target and abstract orientations together, so its contribution is the same. Mobius alignment of a piece preserves this geometric volume; no open Gauss regulator is reset or declared invariant. The collapsed disks add zero, and all original boundary faces pair. Therefore Vol(rho_sm)=sum_pieces sum_(triangles in piece) sigma V =2pi sum_pieces (actual entropy). (1) There is no missing constant: the input entropy splitting uses the already proved C=V/(2pi) and E=C_input-C_output. Artificial closing triangles are the forced two-line V=0 configurations. The original mark and target degrees were retained in the identity and tight-cut steps; no new quantum mark or 1/N normalization is introduced. ## 5. Return to the original drilled group Restore each actual deleted UNTWISTED port. Its middle faces were identified, so its ordered input and output pairs agree. Assign the original auxiliary meridian to identity. The literal threading word is then the identity. Its original outer product may be axial (loxodromic or elliptic), parabolic or central, because the removed matching edge imposed no remaining tangency. Choose its recorded peripheral flag and use the [proved zero-volume axis/parabolic filling-cap construction, §4](../papers/casimir-source-asymptotics/README.md). This gives a representation rho of the original drilled group, factoring through the actual meridional identity smoothing, with Vol(rho)=Vol(rho_sm)=2pi W_D (2) IF the exact hybrid decomposition/regularity hypotheses in section1 have been established for that maximum. The [representation-volume bound and strict-kernel theorem, §§1–3](../papers/casimir-source-asymptotics/README.md) then give W_D<=Vol(Y_D)/(2pi). If at least one original meridian was killed, the already proved strict-kernel bound is strict; comparison with the known all-cross lower bound would exclude such a maximizing identity-deletion case. This assembly does not itself prove the hybrid tight-cut classification or the exclusion of every further free KKT stratum. It records exactly what geometry follows from those finite-flow outputs, and preserves all original group, peripheral and chain data needed for the comparison. ## Scope Root, coherent and cluster the complete conditional proof: the matching-mark CROSS boundary rows, cooriented piece development, original three-contact collar maps across pieces, one global reflected copy, actual digon-disk chain collapse and restored identity meridians. The axial restoration explicitly includes elliptic as well as loxodromic outer products.
