title: Hybrid Fejer flow: all proper tight sets come from permitted digon cuts
status: Exact hybrid Hall cuts, forced zeros and feasible perturbations
text: # Hybrid Fejer flow: all proper tight sets come from permitted digon cuts 31 October 2026. This is a finite incidence theorem for the ACTUAL loopless white triangular cellulation obtained after source-preserving identity smoothing. The [closed local entropy](actual_fejer_half_block_entropy.md) and [original shared source](actual_fejer_shared_entropy_variational.md) provide its local functions and literal incidence conventions. It does not replace a matching/matching Green cut by two independent entropy maxima. ## 1. Literal hybrid network Let T be a loopless triangular cellulation of the sphere, with R+2 white vertices and 2R triangular cells. Multiple edges remain distinct. The dual cubic graph has its original perfect matching: each port is the pair of triangles adjacent to its matching white edge. Keep two distinct protected white vertices u,v joined by an actual edge. Every other white vertex has target1; both protected targets are0. Some ports are tagged CROSS, others GREEN. A CROSS port retains its TWO triangle nodes, each of supply1/2, incident to that triangle's ordinary vertices. A GREEN port has ONE node of supply1 and its FOUR original incidences x,b,c,y: shared outer triangle corners x,y are aggregated once. Distinct incidences among these four remain parallel arcs if their global face labels coincide. This is the hybrid limiting flow used to perturb a fixed cross/strict-one-sided entropy point. The full supply is R, equal to the ordinary targets. For a set S of ordinary vertices let C_0(S) be the total supply of the complete triangle network touching S, and C_H(S) that of the hybrid network. Directly from the original pair of half-supplies, C_H(S)=C_0(S)+(1/2)g(S), (1) where g(S) counts the GREEN ports for which EXACTLY ONE of the two triangles touches S. In particular merging a pair never lowers a Hall capacity. The finite flow criterion is C_H(S)>=|S| for every S. ## 2. Complete Hall inequality and the equality case Take a nonempty proper S among the R ordinary vertices, and put U=V(T)\S, n=|U|. The induced embedded graph G=T[U] is loopless and contains the retained protected edge uv. Let p be the number of original triangular cells wholly supported on U. Each is still an actual face of G; a triangular face of G enclosing removed vertices does NOT count in p. Every other original triangle touches S, so C_0(S)=(2R-p)/2, C_0(S)=|S| iff p=2n-4. (2) Here is a face count which also handles disconnected induced graphs and isolated vertices. Move one point of S to infinity. Every original triangle supported on U is bounded in this planar drawing. For a connected component G_i with n_i>=2 vertices, write f_i for its bounded faces, e_i for its edges and p_i for its bounded original triangles. All face boundary walks have length at least2. Euler and edge counting give e_i=n_i+f_i-1, 2e_i>=3p_i+2(f_i-p_i)+2, p_i<=2n_i-4. (3) The final2 is the outer boundary walk. An isolated vertex contributes no triangle. If there are c>=1 nontrivial components and a isolated vertices, summing gives p<=2(n-a)-4c<=2n-4. (4) Thus the complete and hybrid Hall inequalities hold. For S empty or all ordinary vertices they are the trivial zero or total balance; every triangle has an ordinary corner because it has three distinct vertices and only u,v are protected. If S is proper and tight, p=2n-4. Equations (3)--(4) force a=0,c=1: G is connected. Every face not one of the p original triangles has boundary walk EXACTLY two edges, including the outer face. Since proper S implies n>=3, such a two-edge face cannot be one bridge traversed twice: its next boundary step would continue around the nontrivial remainder at one of its endpoints. Equivalently a bridge bounding a complete two-step face walk would make the entire connected graph a single edge. Consequently these faces are genuine digons bounded by two DISTINCT parallel original edges. Every removed S vertex belongs to the interior of one of these digon faces. Conversely each such non-original face contains removed vertices; the original cellulation is triangular. Therefore S is precisely the union of the interior vertex sets of these pairwise interior-disjoint actual digon disks. Each disk is mark-free in its interior. This classification uses the induced graph at S, not an assumed preselected digon decomposition tree. ## 3. Hybrid tightness merges only neighboring holes with the same endpoints Suppose C_H(S)=|S|. Then (1) and (4) force both C_0(S)=|S| and g(S)=0. Consider the digon disks from section2. Across an edge on one such disk's boundary, the inside triangle touches S. If this edge is MATCHING and its port is GREEN, the other triangle must touch S too, or that port would contribute to g(S). That other triangle belongs to a second digon disk on the other side of the SAME boundary edge. The two digons therefore have the same ordered pair of boundary vertices. Merge them across that green edge. Their union is again a digon disk bounded by the two remaining parallel edges. For clarity, all these mergers can be done at once. The adjacency graph of the S-digon disks across green matching boundary edges has degree at most2. Every connected component has a fixed endpoint pair. It cannot be a cycle for a proper S: a full cyclic family of parallel edge sectors fills the sphere except those two vertices, so the connected induced graph G would have only those vertices, contrary to n>=3. Its components are paths; each merges to one actual digon. This also proves that an intervening matching edge is removed only from the description of the separating boundary, not from the source or from its Green pair. After merging, every surviving matching boundary edge belongs to a CROSS port. A MAIN boundary edge never splits a paired triangle node. The two boundary edges of each resulting digon have the same type: the disk contains 2v triangular cells for v interior vertices, and the parity count of their one matching incidence per dual vertex forces an even number of matching edges to cross its two-edge boundary. Thus the permitted cuts are exactly MAIN / MAIN; or MATCHING / MATCHING with BOTH ports CROSS. (5) Each resulting disk is individually hybrid-tight. Its 2v triangles exhaust the demand v of its interior vertices; no green node crosses its boundary. The original tight set is a union of their interiors. In particular a general GREEN matching/matching cut has NOT been declared tight, split, or assigned additive entropy. The full set S of ordinary vertices is only the redundant total balance. Its possible U={u,v} one-edge or full-cycle exception does not force any additional ordinary incidence to vanish. ## 4. Forced zeros and a positive relative-interior witness For any feasible hybrid flow, a tight S forces every node touching S to send its entire supply into S. Thus each of its arcs to an ordinary vertex outside S is zero. Conversely an ordinary incidence arc is forced zero ONLY this way. One direct proof avoids a nondegeneracy assumption on the balance matrix. To force a small positive amount epsilon on an arc n->f, reduce that row supply and the target at f by epsilon. For any vertex set S containing f, both capacity and demand decrease equally. For S not containing f but touched by n, only capacity decreases. Such a constraint obstructs every positive epsilon exactly when S was tight. The finitely many other inequalities have positive slack, so a sufficiently small epsilon preserves them. The ordinary Hall criterion then supplies the remaining flow. Hence every non-forced ordinary arc is positive in some feasible flow. Averaging finitely many such flows gives one witness positive on ALL non-forced ordinary arcs and zero on the forced ones. Redundant face balances cause no difficulty. Equations (2)--(5) show that all forced zeros have the precise source-permitted digon origin above. Inside a MAIN/MAIN tight disk, whole ports remain inside and all incidences at its boundary white faces are zero. At a permitted MATCHING/MATCHING cut, its two inside CROSS triangles each have their two boundary corners zero and their interior middle corner1/2. These are constant, zero-entropy triangles. Only CROSS pairs are cut, so their additive C+C data may be retained/repaired across the boundary; no difference E=C_input-C_output is separated into independent pieces. The original outside and inside middle degrees are not reset by this network statement. Geometry and actual face-pairing assembly remain separate obligations. These cuts may be iterated as an exact HYBRID flow decomposition. Close the two sides by identifying their two boundary edges. The inside has new protected pair a,b and the outside retains its old pair. A MAIN cut leaves whole port nodes on their original sides. At a permitted matching cut, retain each of the four original CROSS triangle nodes on its own side and pair the two nodes on a closed side only as the formal C+C description. This creates no new physical coupon. The inside boundary loads are zero by tightness, while every outside boundary demand is unchanged. Thus the original hybrid feasible polytope is exactly the Cartesian product of those two piece polytopes, and its entropy is their sum: every GREEN E factor stays whole and every cut factor was additive C+C. The closure remains loopless, both marked vertices are adjacent, and every proper cut strictly reduces the number of triangles on each side. Iteration terminates. On each resulting piece there is no proper tight set, so section4 gives positivity on every ordinary allowed arc; the marked zero-dimensional triangle rows retain their fixed values. ## 5. Consequence for the boundary-regularity argument At a full-kernel maximum, tag terminal seams CROSS and keep the remaining strict non-diagonal half ports GREEN. The full continuous-h theorem permits this limiting description without claiming eventual feasibility of a newly fixed finite label pattern. The cross variables are their actual two triangle allocations. A small mixture with the relative-interior witness of section4 remains cross-admissible; each green point stays in its own strict half chamber because its original interval length and upper-endpoint margin are positive. The proved corner expansions then give a nonnegative epsilon log(1/epsilon) coefficient at every factor. Any zero ordinary degree or cross-triangle corner that is NOT structurally forced by (5) is activated and yields a strict positive gain. Thus such a maximum has no free zeros beyond those tight digon cuts. This assertion keeps diagonal ports excluded; their negative epsilon log(1/epsilon) term is not an allowed remainder. To turn this into a volume bound one must use the actual permitted cut pieces and their inherited marked flags when constructing finite positive multipliers and the global relative chain. The present proof is the complete finite support/witness classification, not an assertion that independent Green capacities factor across arbitrary digons. ## Scope The induced-face Euler argument includes disconnected induced graphs, digon faces and the proper-subset exception. The iterative cut uses variational C+C bookkeeping; it is not a finite-coupon replacement. Geometry additionally target-read the final iterative paragraph and confirmed its Cartesian flow product, unchanged outside targets, formal matching parity and termination. This record is scoped to the finite hybrid theorem and its regularity perturbation. This finite combinatorial proof has no separate numerical audit. It does not itself identify a group representation or a relative fundamental class, and it does not infer a phase-sensitive original filling asymptotic. The geometric piece assembly and whole-source comparison require their separate proofs.

title: Non-diagonal maximizers have no free zero degrees
status: Boundary regularity and finite shared multipliers
text: # Non-diagonal maximizers have no free zero degrees 31 October 2026. This uses the actual shared entropy theorem and the labeled complete geometric all-cross flow. It does not assume a global entropy redistribution or exchange inf and max. It supplies ordinary finite positive Lagrange multipliers on a precise stratum. The remaining diagonal strata are expressly excluded. ## 1. Source setting and the admissible perturbation Use the [shared entropy theorem](actual_fejer_shared_entropy_variational.md), with the actual two protected faces and fixed incidence map. A maximizer includes the two triangular allocations at each cross port. First perform the proved [batch terminal reduction](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_fejer_batch_terminal_reduction.md): every one-sided port with nu=1/2 is retagged cross at the SAME degree vector and entropy. Eventual feasibility of the new pattern follows by mixing with the geometric all-cross flow, scaling by d and rounding with strict middle slack. Assume now that no remaining one-sided port is diagonal. Thus at each one-sided port 0<=mu<nu<1/2, xi>=0, eta=nu-mu-xi>=0. (1) The positive interval length and upper endpoint margin are fixed at this particular finite-dimensional maximizer. No uniform margin over all possible maximizers is being asserted. Let qG be the actual geometric all-cross flow, with its literal triangular allocations. Every ordinary triangular corner of qG is positive; protected corners are zero. Every ordinary middle is strictly less than1/2, because its two outer faces form a matching edge and cannot both be the marked MAIN pair. Protected middle loads are zero. For a fixed sufficiently small epsilon>0 put q(epsilon)=(1-epsilon)q+epsilon qG. (2) At cross ports mix the triangular allocations themselves. At a one-sided port interpret its four mixed incidences by the SAME affine (mu,nu,xi) parameterization, or its actual reflection. It is immaterial that qG alone lies outside this one-sided domain: the strict margins in (1) keep (2) inside it for all small epsilon. Shared ordinary targets remain one and BOTH protected targets remain zero. The original label pattern is unchanged. Its eventual feasibility was already proved, so (2) is a legitimate limiting source flow in that same pattern. This perturbation activates every zero ordinary local incidence and every zero ordinary cross-triangle corner, while it leaves all protected zeros exactly zero. ## 2. All corner expansions for the actual E Write C(alpha)=sum_j f(alpha_j), f(t)=[Lambda(pi t)+Lambda(pi/2-pi t)]/pi, f(t)=-t log t+O(t) as t->0, f(1/2-t)=f(t). (3) For a cross triangle along an affine admissible path, the coefficient of epsilon log(1/epsilon) in its entropy change is sum_(alpha_j=0) dot_alpha_j -sum_(alpha_j=1/2) dot_alpha_j. (4) All these terms are nonnegative. At a vertex it is twice the sum of the activated zero corners; on an open edge it is the activation of its single zero corner. The remainder is O(epsilon), uniformly when the fixed direction ranges over a compact admissible set. This follows from t log t and boundedness of a log a for bounded nonnegative slopes. For a one-sided port set eta=nu-mu-xi. Along an affine path satisfying (1) for small epsilon, the coefficient h in E(epsilon)-E(0)=h epsilon log(1/epsilon)+O(epsilon) (5) is as follows. Slopes of coordinates that vanish at epsilon=0 are nonnegative. * If mu,xi,eta are all positive, h=0. * If mu=0 and xi,eta>0, h=dot_mu. * If mu>0 and xi=0, h=dot_xi; if eta=0, h=dot_eta. * If mu=xi=0, h=2(dot_mu+dot_xi). * If mu=eta=0, h=2(dot_mu+dot_eta). These cases exhaust (1). Here is a proof from the ACTUAL closed coefficient entropy, including the simultaneous corner. Use its exact formula from the [closed coefficient theorem](actual_fejer_half_block_entropy.md), E=C(alpha)-C(beta), alpha_b=mu, beta_c=nu, alpha_x-beta_x=xi, alpha_y-beta_y=eta, (6) where the input/output triangles have the common outer tilt. Their explicit arcsine reconstruction is the one in the half-block theorem; no independent optimization of alpha and beta is made. In the first case all corners are strict, so E is smooth. In the second, the tilt stays finite and the only vanishing corner is alpha_b=mu; the arcsine formulas are smooth for the other corners. Equation (3) therefore gives h=dot_mu. If mu>0 and xi=0, both alpha_x and beta_x vanish, but all their other corners stay strict. The arcsine formulas are smooth at kappa=-1 because mu,nu are strictly between0 and1/2. Both small corners are O(epsilon), and their difference is EXACTLY xi. Their singular coefficients subtract to dot_xi. The y-reflected case is identical. For mu=xi=0, the input triangle is the vertex (0,0,1/2), while the output triangle has its x corner zero and its other two corners strict. The common outer tilt gives tan(pi alpha_x)/tan(pi alpha_y) =tan(pi beta_x)/tan(pi beta_y). Since alpha_y=1/2-mu-alpha_x and beta_c remains near the fixed nu in (0,1/2), this equality and alpha_x=xi+beta_x imply beta_x=O(xi(mu+xi)), alpha_x=xi+O(xi(mu+xi)). (7) Indeed the left ratio is comparable to alpha_x(mu+alpha_x), while the right is comparable to beta_x. After continuity makes all these quantities small, absorb the beta_x terms. The constants are uniform over compact direction sets at the fixed positive nu. Thus beta_x=O(epsilon^2), alpha_x=epsilon dot_xi+O(epsilon^2), and alpha_y=1/2-epsilon(dot_mu+dot_xi)+O(epsilon^2). Equation (3) gives the coefficient 2(dot_mu+dot_xi) for C(alpha). The change in C(beta) is only O(epsilon), including its O(epsilon^2 log epsilon) zero-corner term. This proves the joint case, even if either or both activation slopes vanish. Reflection proves the remaining case. Every displayed O(epsilon) is for a fixed source point, uniformly over a compact set of admissible directions. ## 3. General exclusion of free zeros at a non-diagonal maximum Apply (4)--(5) to (2). Every entropy singular coefficient is nonnegative. If any ordinary local degree or ordinary cross-triangle corner is zero, the geometric witness activates it and at least one coefficient is strictly positive. All other changes are O(epsilon). The sum therefore increases by h_total epsilon log(1/epsilon)+O(epsilon)>0, h_total>0, contradicting maximality. Consequently a maximizer with all terminals removed and with no diagonal one-sided port has ONLY the zeros forced by the two original protected faces. Every ordinary cross-triangle corner and every ordinary incidence in a one-sided port is positive. For cross ports it is enough to retain the particular mixed triangular split: the optimized cross entropy at the mixed total degrees is at least that value. Thus the proof does not assume the new split is an optimizer, nor differentiate a maximum at a nonsmooth split. ## 4. Finite positive shared multipliers and the actual local equations Remove the protected variables, which are fixed to zero. On the stratum just obtained, all remaining local inequalities are strict except those that are identities of a zero-dimensional triangle. The objective is smooth in the resulting affine local coordinates. At a constrained maximum its differential annihilates the kernel of the actual face- balance matrix. Elementary finite-dimensional linear algebra gives FINITE REAL face multipliers lambda_f satisfying d(sum local entropy)+sum_(ordinary f) lambda_f dq_f=0. (8) Redundant balances cause no issue: a linear functional annihilating the kernel belongs to the row space. No constraint independence or unproved multiplier compactness across different maximizers is assumed. Put l_f=exp(lambda_f)>0 for ordinary f, and retain l_u=l_v=0. The common-scale freedom is harmless because every port has total degree one and every protected incidence is zero. At a cross triangle with at least two ordinary corners, f'(alpha)=log cot(pi alpha), so (8) implies tan(pi alpha_f)=l_f/T, T^2=sum_(pairs f,g in that triangle) l_f l_g. This is the actual center-angle formula; its one-ordinary-corner case is the forced angle vector (0,0,1/2). At a one-sided port with both outer variables ordinary, its outer stationarity gives the actual tilt log(l_x/l_y). If the parent middle is ordinary, row stationarity gives L(mu;l_x,l_y)=l_b; if it is protected, mu=0 and the same equation holds by the endpoint limit. The overloaded middle is ordinary, and its strict terminal equation is L(nu;l_x,l_y)=l_c. When one outer face is protected, the corresponding outer degree is fixed zero and the actual entropy is its extreme value B; the same equations hold with L(t;0,y)=y tan^2(pi t), or its reflection. Both outer faces cannot be protected, since their matching edge is not the protected MAIN edge. These formulas also include the forced joint corner x=b=0: the input is the two-line angle vector and the remaining terminal equation is unchanged. The local argument supplies finite positive multipliers, not a volume comparison by itself. The following conclusion also uses a conditional marked development and the global sewn-chain calculation cited below. The marked development retains its stated stationary-stratum hypotheses. Thus these maxima supply the FINITE positive ordinary multipliers and strict remaining equations required by the [marked signed-circle development](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_fejer_marked_signed_development.md). The [global signed cut-ball regulator](actual_fejer_signed_cut_ball_regulator.md) uses the original labeled degree-one fundamental chain, actual face pairings, one reflection of the second ball, and the retained peripheral horospheres. It proves that this stationary entropy is Vol(rho)/(2pi), and therefore at most Phi_D=Vol(Y_D)/(2pi). This invokes that GLOBAL chain proof, not the disproved invariance of a re-framed open crossing word. Consequently every global maximizer satisfying the no-diagonal hypothesis after batch terminal reduction has value at most Phi_D. If such a maximizer exists, the all-cross lower bound gives W_D=Phi_D. Equivalently, any strict inequality W_D>Phi_D would force a diagonal one-sided port in every maximizer with the minimal number of one-sided labels. This is a general reduction at arbitrary fixed width under the original labeled certificate, not an assertion that diagonals are absent. ## 5. The diagonal exception is essential This proof excludes every mu=nu port. In particular a diagonal at mu=nu=0 can LOSE entropy of order epsilon log(1/epsilon) under the same mixing, and can cancel the gains above. If the mixing has parent activation B and outer activations X,Y, then E(epsilon B,epsilon(B+X+Y),epsilon X) =2 max(X,Y) epsilon log epsilon+O(epsilon). (9) For X>Y, the exact arcsine reconstruction has kappa=1-O(epsilon^2). Both endpoint triangles approach the x vertex; their other-outer and middle loads are O(epsilon). The middle loads differ by -epsilon(X+Y), while their y loads differ by epsilon Y. The vertex singular terms in (3) therefore subtract to 2X epsilon log epsilon. For X<Y use the reflected calculation. For X=Y the tilt is exactly zero; the two outer corners stay near1/4 and only the middle corners are small. Their middle difference is -2epsilon X, giving the same formula. The parent B changes only the O(epsilon) term. The zero-width case X=Y=0 gives E=0 exactly. No such term was concealed in (5). Diagonal ports require an actual identity-deletion/block argument or another global entropy exchange. The lemma does not settle those strata or the phase-sensitive filling asymptotic. The underlying exact entropy and finite coefficient checks are in the linked half-block theorem. This finite-dimensional proof does not require a new numerical asymptotic audit. The global signed-chain argument retains its original pairings and marked apex.

title: Odd spectral regularization has the same full shared entropy
status: Odd full entropy; exact all-parity spectral derivatives
text: # Odd spectral regularization has the same full shared entropy 31 October 2026. All derivatives here are SPECTRAL derivatives at the fixed original root. No genuine-q normal is obtained by differentiating a root-only identity. The actual positive coupon below includes the semisimple derivative data of the full V. ## 1. Exact odd normalization and one comparison block Let N=2m+1>=3, d=2m, theta=pi/N. On the literal polynomial source block z^j, 0<=j<=d, write A=2+Omega, with diagonal and lowering coefficients a_j=2+c_j=4cos^2((j+1/2)theta), s_j=2sin(j theta), A z^j=a_j z^j-s_j^2(x+y)z^(j-1) -s_j s_(j-1)xy z^(j-2). The sole zero diagonal is a_m=0. All other diagonals and all allowed lowering weights are positive. The original endpoint zeros are retained. Let P_N(u)=H_(V_N(-2-u)), P0=P_N(0), Q=P_N'(0), F_N=V_N(-2)-N^(-2) V_N'(-2), H_(F_N)=P0+N^(-2)Q. (1) V_N is the [full original polynomial numerator](actual_gaussian_resolvent_numerator_and_cap.md) chi_N(sigma)/(sigma-Omega), chi_N=2T_N(sigma/2)+2. The second prime in (1) differentiates sigma; the Q prime differentiates u. Thus the minus sign in F_N is literal. The unused-row product expansion gives nonnegative coefficients of P_N(u) in u,x,b,c,y. At odd N its full diagonal product is product_j(a_j+u)= -chi_N(-2-u) =2cosh(N theta_u)-2, theta_u=arccosh(1+u/2). Its first two Taylor coefficients give exactly product_(j!=m)a_j=N^2, sum_(j!=m) a_j^(-1)=(N^2-1)/12. (2) Replace ONLY the zero central diagonal of A by a_m^*=N^(-2), keeping all lowering coefficients and other diagonals unchanged. Call this positive triangular block Atilde, and let Ktilde be the homogeneous polynomial of Atilde^(-1). It is a comparison kernel, NOT asserted to be a covariant physical coupon. Its full diagonal product equals1. Split the coefficient Q according to whether its underlying path visits m. Write Q_skip for the paths not visiting m. The unused-row formula and (2) give EXACTLY Ktilde=P0+N^(-2)Q_skip, 0<=Q-Q_skip<=((N^2-1)/12)P0. The second inequality is coefficientwise: on each path visiting m, the derivative adds the sum of reciprocal UNUSED noncentral diagonals. Consequently the ACTUAL polynomial coupon has the finite comparison Ktilde <= H_(F_N) <= (13/12)Ktilde. (3) In particular both have every degree-d monomial, with positive coefficient. One may also see this by the path consisting entirely of one-steps. No spectral projector has been substituted for V'. ## 2. Exact half and cross pieces of Ktilde As usual an input j and output i contribute b^i c^(d-j), with total outer degree j-i. Partition its full monomial support into left: c>=m+1; right: b>=m+1; cross: b,c<=m. (4) For a left coefficient i<=j<=m-1 no path visits m. Define Q_ij by the ACTUAL lower-block recurrence Q_ii=1, Q_ij=(s_j^2/a_j)(x+y)Q_(i,j-1) +(s_j s_(j-1)/a_j)xyQ_(i,j-2), with the missing second term zero. Then the coefficient at x^k b^i c^(d-j)y^(j-i-k) is EXACTLY a_i^(-1)[x^k y^(j-i-k)]Q_ij. (5) The right piece is its literal row-reflection b<->c; the steps and diagonals have this exact symmetry. Every cross path either visits m or skips it by the unique two-step m+1->m-1. Replace that skipped step by the two one-steps through m. Since xy <= (x+y)^2/2 coefficientwise, its weight is at most [1/(2N^2 s_m s_(m+1))] times the repaired path. (6) The repair is injective and its endpoints are unchanged. The paths visiting m have EXACTLY the P0 weights because the new reciprocal central diagonal is N^2. Therefore P0 <= Ktilde_cross <=[1+1/(2N^2 s_m s_(m+1))] P0. (7) The same visited-central path split gives an exact factorization P0=N^2 D_m(x,b,y)D_m(x,c,y), (8) with D_m monic of degree m in its middle variable. This is also the actual odd simple-fold factorization (the sine beta_m equals1). It can be proved without a value-only interpolation: split each original path at m and reflect its upper part. If D_m(x,b,y)=sum_i b^i G_i(x,y), then G_m=1 and, for i<m, G_i=[s_m^2(x+y)Q_(i,m-1) +s_m s_(m-1)xyQ_(i,m-2)]/a_i, (9) where a nonexistent Q term is zero. Equations (5)--(9) retain every physical endpoint and every finite outer unit. ## 3. Uniform CLOSED coefficient entropy on the shifted odd mesh The [closed half-block proof](actual_fejer_half_block_entropy.md) applies to (5), with the following explicit checks rather than an inference from a weighted limit. For j<=m-1, a_j=4sin^2((m-j)theta), s_j=2sin(j theta). On any fixed interior interval j/N in [eta,1/2-eta], the recurrence coefficients converge uniformly to the SAME positive monomer/dimer coefficients, with Perron root L^2-(x+y)tan^2(pi t)L-xy tan^2(pi t)=0. The corresponding normalized Jacobi recurrence has positive, uniformly bounded interior coefficients and hence the same bounded negative-root and Bernoulli local coefficient estimate. The boundary estimates also remain unchanged in order: for j near0, s_j is comparable to j/N; for r=m-j near0, a_j is comparable to (r/N)^2, with r>=1. Thus removing eta N endpoint indices costs at most O(eta N log(1/eta)+log N) in the monomer products and upper bounds. There is no zero coefficient inside either lower half. The all-monomer x/y choices realize every outer degree, including the extreme coefficients. These are precisely the ingredients of the closed proof: finite-tilt compact-cover upper bounds, trim/fill lower bounds at endpoints, the interior coefficient estimate on the trimmed interval, and the collapsing-interval bound. They prove uniformly for ALL 0<=i<=j<=m-1 and 0<=k<=j-i N^(-1)log([x^k y^(j-i-k)]Q_ij) =E(i/N,j/N,k/N)+o(1). (10) The factor a_i^(-1) has logarithm O(log N), uniformly. Formula (9) then gives the same uniform TRIANGLE coefficient entropy for D_m. For i<m its first term supplies every permitted k by choosing x or y; one of k or k-1 lies in [0,m-1-i]. All arguments in (10) differ by O(1/N) from the desired endpoint E(i/N,1/2,k/N). The second term only adds another argument with the same O(1/N) displacement. Their finite positive weights have polynomial upper/lower bounds. Closed continuity therefore proves the upper and lower limits uniformly. The corner i=m is the exact coefficient1 and entropy zero. Normalize all local exponents by d=2m. For D_m each triple divided by d has sum1/2; changing i/N,k/N to i/d,k/d changes them by O(1/N). Thus its absolute limit is the ALREADY normalized C(alpha)=E(alpha_b,1/2,alpha_x)=V(2pi alpha)/(2pi). The positive convolution (8), with O(N) summands and integer split endpoints, has the same uniform cross entropy max(C+C). Equations (5) and (7), closed continuity at both seams and the constant comparison (3) now prove, for every degree-d local exponent n, N^(-1)log [L^n]H_(F_N)=h(n/d)+o(1) (11) UNIFORMLY on the full closed simplex. This is the same h as the even full Fejer theorem, not only its positive-radius weighted maximum. ## 4. Actual shared coefficient and full complex spectral disks For a fixed original certified flat plat retain its original ordinary targets d and protected targets0. The actual polynomial coupon F_N in (1) is admissible in the original homogeneous compiler. By positivity, (11), and unrestricted integral flow rounding, its whole shared source satisfies N^(-1)log Z_(D,N;F_N at every port) -> W_D. (12) Here W_D is EXACTLY the same finite-dimensional full h maximum as at even levels. The separate [even endpoint volume theorem](general_fejer_endpoint_source_volume.md) therefore identifies W_D=Vol(Y_D)/(2pi). No odd identity-deletion or geometric reconstruction has been inferred by differentiating an even statement. For u>=0 define C_N(0)=1 and C_N(u)=product_(j!=m)(1+u/a_j) =[sinh(N theta_u/2)/(N sinh(theta_u/2))]^2 <=exp((N-1)theta_u). (13) The product of UNUSED noncentral ratios on any path is at most C_N(u). Visiting-central paths start from P0; skipping paths have their one central factor u. Consequently the exact positive path comparison is P_N(u)<=C_N(u)[P0+u Q_skip] <=C_N(u)max(1,N^2u) H_(F_N). (14) For arbitrary complex sigma the source-proved factorwise majorant is |H_(V_N(sigma))|_coef<=P_N(|sigma+2|). Multiplying (14) at all original ports and taking the UNCHANGED shared marked coefficient bounds the absolute full numerator contraction by Z_(D,N;F_N) product_e {exp((N-1)theta_(u_e)) max(1,N^2u_e)}, u_e=|sigma_e+2|. (15) In particular it has upper rate at most W_D+sum_e arccosh(1+u_e/2) on fixed bounded spectral disks, and upper rate at most W_D uniformly on ANY shrinking polydisks |sigma_e+2|<=r_N->0. This includes all actual semisimple numerator data. Cauchy estimates may be applied to spectral derivatives with their stated disk-radius cost; they are not genuine-q normal estimates. No Gaussian contour selection, complement estimate, or nonzero filling-cycle contribution is concluded here. ## 5. Exact whole-source spectral jets, both parities Let S_N(sigma_1,...,sigma_R) be the ENTIRE shared contraction of the original V_N numerators, with the original homogeneous face targets and protected zero specialization. Use F_N from (1) at odd levels and F_N=-V_N(-2)=P_N at even levels. For each variable choose the actual Cauchy radius r=N^(-2). The elementary inequality cosh t>=1+t^2/2 gives arccosh(1+1/(2N^2))<=1/N, max(1,N^2r)=1. At odd levels (14)--(15) therefore bound |S_N| on the whole polydisk by e^R Z_(D,N;F_N). At even levels the exact unused-factor comparison instead has factor product_j(1+r/a_j)=cosh^2(N theta_r/2)<=exp(N theta_r)<=e, at every port, and gives the SAME bound. Cauchy's formula yields for every multiindex alpha the finite all-parity estimate |partial_sigma^alpha S_N(-2,...,-2)| <= e^R alpha! N^(2|alpha|) Z_(D,N;F_N). (16) There is no unspecified exponential constant in (16): its right side is the actual positive shared source whose rate is W_D. This includes the full spectral semisimple derivatives at the parabolic endpoint. It does not identify these spectral jets with genuine-q normal jets, and it does not select any Gaussian or filling cycle. ## Validation and scope The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_fejer_odd_regularized_full_numerator.py) and its [results](../experiments/actual_fejer_odd_regularized_full_numerator_results.json) independently construct V and its SPECTRAL derivative on the original coproduct matrices. They compare 3,672 physical-grid entries, including 1,200 wrong-unwrapped-total zeros, and six whole original marked F_N sources. Four literal simple-fold factorizations retain the root scalar. The 75-digit positive checks cover 2,510 derivative paths, 1,035 full- support coefficient comparisons, 783 central-cross repairs and 3,105 spectral-radius coefficient bounds. The maximum identity error is below 3.90e-73. These are exact-source/formula checks, not numerical proofs of the uniform entropy limit or of the volume theorem. Root the full analytical proof through section4 and supplied/checked the exact whole spectral-jet corollary. Geometry the full proof, including every closed-coefficient and seam argument, then the complete audit code and freshly replayed it with redirected output. Geometry also separately checked section5's all-parity Cauchy constant. Public promotion changes only links, formatting and file-relative audit paths; its author replay reproduced the same counts and errors. No genuine-q normal, Gaussian contour selection or nonzero filling-cycle claim is part of this result.

title: Exact serial Fejer coupons have only a polynomial composition cost
status: Exact same-pair serial comparison; polynomial cost
text: # Exact serial Fejer coupons have only a polynomial composition cost 31 October 2026. This concerns the literal SAME ordered pair Casimir and its actual homogeneous composition. A diagrammatic digon may be replaced using this lemma only after its cups, dual turns and port order have been identified with that serial composition. No assertion about an arbitrary matching/matching separating cut is made. ## 1. Exact finite source and positive paths Let N be even, d=N-1, theta=pi/N. On the actual polynomial source block with basis z^j, 0<=j<=d, write Omega z^j=c_j z^j-s_j^2(x+y)z^(j-1) -s_j s_(j-1)xy z^(j-2), c_j=2cos((2j+1)theta), s_j=2sin(j theta), a_j=2+c_j=4cos^2((j+1/2)theta)>0. The endpoint factors s_0=0 make every illegal physical step zero. The even root characteristic polynomial is chi_N(sigma)=2T_N(sigma/2)+2, with chi_N(-2)=4. Hence the FULL positive endpoint coupon is exactly P_N=-V_N(-2)=4(2+Omega)^(-1). (1) This includes all repeated-node/Hermite data, with the [original full numerator convention](actual_gaussian_resolvent_numerator_and_cap.md). Its homogeneous polynomial H_P is the already proved original marked-source coupon; it has no new trace normalization or independently reset half-power. Put K=(2+Omega)^(-1). For any downward path pi from j to i, with steps one or two, let Vert(pi) be its distinct visited row indices and w(pi) the product of the literal nonnegative lowering weights. Expanding the triangular inverse gives its contribution to K as w(pi) product_(v in Vert(pi)) a_v^(-1). (2) One-steps retain (x+y) and two-steps retain xy. Thus all comparisons below are coefficientwise in the original four homogeneous faces, not only positive-weight evaluations. ## 2. Composition and the repeated-vertex multiplier Fix an integer ell>=1. Composing ell copies of K decomposes a complete downward path into ell consecutive subpaths, allowing zero-step subpaths. Each of the ell-1 break vertices is then counted an extra time in the inverse diagonal product. Breaks may repeat; their order along the path is fixed. Therefore the multiplier of (2) is EXACTLY h_(ell-1)({a_v^(-1):v in Vert(pi)}), (3) where h_r is the complete homogeneous symmetric polynomial of degree r. There is one decomposition for every multiset of break vertices. This also proves the formula for a zero-step path and arbitrary ell. All variables are nonnegative, and h_r(t)<= (sum t)^r. The full inverse diagonal sum has the exact value sum_(j=0)^d a_j^(-1)=N^2/4. (4) Indeed chi_N'(sigma)/chi_N(sigma)=sum_j(sigma-c_j)^(-1), while chi_N'(-2)=T_N'(-1)=-N^2 at even N and chi_N(-2)=4. This uses every row with its multiplicity, including repeated Casimir eigenvalues. The P_N^ell-to-P_N path multiplier is 4^(ell-1) times (3). Retaining the term with every break at the initial row j gives the lower bound (4/a_j)^(ell-1)>=1, since a_j<=4. Equations (3)--(4) therefore give the finite, uniform coefficientwise comparison H_(P_N) <= H_(P_N^ell) <= N^(2ell-2) H_(P_N). (5) No exponential asymptotic or fixed-radius comparison enters this bound. For fixed ell the two sides have the SAME exponential rate. It also holds when x=y, or after any original nonnegative variable identification or zero specialization. For reference the zero-step part satisfies the two-sided comparison H_1 <= (H_P)_diag=sum_j (4/a_j)b^j c^(d-j) <=N^2 H_1, (6) H_1=sum_j b^j c^(d-j). The lower bound uses a_j<=4; the upper bound follows from (4) or from min_j a_j=4sin^2(pi/(2N)). It concerns the FULL diagonal range, not one fixed left or right half label. ## 3. Literal homogeneous and whole-source use The [original homogeneous composition](actual_crossing_casimir_torus.md) gives, for the SAME pair Casimir, H_FG(x,b,c,y)=[z^d]H_F(x,b,z,y)H_G(x,z,c,y). (7) Thus a literal serial chain with the same ordered outer faces x,y and successive middle faces z_1,...,z_(ell-1) contracts to H_(P_N^ell) by extracting each ordinary internal target d. There is NO additional N, pivot, mark or common crossing phase in (7). Its source normalization has already been included in H, as established by the original physical grid/cup/cap/mark compiler. If the other remaining factors have nonnegative coefficients, substitute (5) into their product and then extract the unchanged original targets. The resulting whole positive source lies between the source with one P_N coupon and N^(2ell-2) times that source, with its internal middle targets removed by (7). Their exponential rates are identical, including the possibility that both coefficients are zero. All other ordinary and protected targets stay literal. Any actual cup/dual orientation needed to realize (7) is a separate diagrammatic premise, not inferred from the existence of two parallel edges alone. The exact identity smoothing in (6) and the serial bound (5) do not establish a full block factorization across arbitrary separating digons, nor a bound for the original phase-sensitive long-twist period. ## Validation and scope The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_fejer_serial_coupon_bound.py) and its [results](../experiments/actual_fejer_serial_coupon_bound_results.json) check 30 exact characteristic endpoint identities, 3 original full resolvent identities, and 15 original serial powers through 3,960 physical grid entries, including 1,290 wrong-unwrapped-total zeros. At 75 digits they also check 6,116 path break multipliers and 3,120 independently composed coefficients against BOTH bounds, with maximum relative error below 6.20e-74. Five full inverse-diagonal sums and 40 diagonal bounds retain the actual finite endpoint constants. Root the complete proof and audit code. Cluster the complete proof/code and freshly replayed all checks with redirected output, including the lower comparison and the absence of an extra N in homogeneous composition. Public promotion only changed links and file-relative audit paths; the portable author replay reproduced the same results. These checks concern the literal same ordered pair and its physical endpoints. They do not certify an arbitrary diagrammatic digon adapter, global volume comparison or filling cycle.

title: The actual Fejér source: a general shared entropy theorem
status: Fixed-pattern entropy, support test and central corridor
text: # The actual Fejér source: a general shared entropy theorem Status update, 31 October 2026: the separate [full endpoint theorem](general_fejer_endpoint_source_volume.md) now proves the geometric upper bound (14), and the [unique-maximizer theorem](actual_fejer_unique_geometric_maximizer.md) proves concentration at the complete configuration. The pattern-specific support theorem below is preserved; full-kernel support no longer requires pattern selection. The filled-knot quantum limit remains open. 31 October 2026. This concerns the positive endpoint numerator in the original homogeneous compiler, at even levels. It does not assert a quantum filling asymptotic or identify the new maximum with hyperbolic volume. All faces, incidences and marked targets are the actual ones. No independently optimized local norm is substituted. Let N=2m, d=N-1, M=m-1. Fix a connected original flat plat D with R ports, R ordinary faces and the two original protected faces u,v. Write the ordered local faces at port e as (x_e,b_e,c_e,y_e), allowing repeated global labels through the literal incidence map. Let P_e=-H_(V_N(-2)), V_N(sigma)=chi_N(sigma)(sigma-Omega)^(-1), Z_(D,N)=[prod_(f ordinary)L_f^d] prod_e P_e |_(L_u=L_v=0). The sign has made each local polynomial positive. The [original homogeneous theorem](../papers/filling-bounds/README.md) makes this the same marked endpoint-numerator source, up to its recorded common sign, with no new powers of N. All statements below are about this source; it is not being renamed Kashaev's invariant. ## 1. The local entropies, including boundary degrees Define on 0<=mu<=nu<=1/2, 0<=xi<=nu-mu E(mu,nu,xi)=inf_(l in R){integral_mu^nu g(t,l)dt-xi*l}, g(t,l)=l/2+log(tan(pi*t)) +asinh(tan(pi*t)*cosh(l/2)). (1) The integral is improper at 0 and 1/2, with integrable logarithmic singularities. If mu=nu then xi=0 and E=0. The [closed-coefficient theorem](actual_fejer_half_block_entropy.md) proves continuity of E on this compact domain and uniform convergence of the logarithms of ALL actual half-block coefficients divided by N to E, including zero outer degrees and endpoint rows. Its proof uses the original continuant, negative-root coefficient factorization in strict interiors, and explicit monomer bounds at the endpoints. It does not infer coefficient asymptotics by differentiating a weighted limit. The multiplier 4/a_i has logarithm O(log N) uniformly. The left type has normalized exponent vector and entropy q_left=(xi,mu,1-nu,nu-mu-xi), E_left=E(mu,nu,xi), (2) in the order (x,b,c,y). Right paths are the actual row reflection, so q_right=(xi,1-nu,mu,nu-mu-xi), E_right=E(mu,nu,xi). (3) For a triangular maximal complete block, put C(alpha_x,alpha_b,alpha_y)=E(alpha_b,1/2,alpha_x), alpha_x+alpha_b+alpha_y=1/2, alpha_j>=0. (4) This is the ACTUAL triangular coefficient entropy. Indeed its path polynomial D_b=R_M^* is coefficientwise between R_M/sqrt(C_N) and R_M, with 1<=C_N<2, while the j=M term of P_left is exactly 2c^m R_M. The leading-coefficient normalization C_front is only polynomial in N. Thus (4) follows from the same closed half-block lemma, with its absolute normalization. Equivalently, using the already fixed triangle potential, C(alpha)=V(2pi*alpha)/(2pi), V(theta)=2sum_j[Lambda(theta_j/2)+Lambda((pi-theta_j)/2)], sum_j theta_j=pi. (5) One can verify (5) by the source triangle gradient formula and its already normalized positive-radius Legendre duality. Formula (4) alone suffices for the theorem below. A cross type uses two triangular vectors alpha,beta, each of sum1/2: q_cross=(alpha_x+beta_x,alpha_b,beta_c,alpha_y+beta_y), E_cross=C(alpha)+C(beta). (6) When a local exponent vector q is fixed, maximize the right side of (6) over its allowed outer split. The exact identity B=4(x+y)D_b D_c and the coefficientwise comparison (N/2)H_M<=P_cross<=(3N/2)H_M prove this local coefficient limit. The forced x+y has degree1 and must be retained at finite N; its contribution to the limiting degree vector is zero. There are only O(N) outer splits. Boundary splits are included by the continuous closed lemma, not omitted. ## 2. Retain eventual feasibility before taking the scaled limit At a finite even level the local supports are EXACTLY: cross: nonnegative (k,i,t,l), sum=d, i,t<=m-1; left: nonnegative (k,i,t,l), sum=d, t>=m; right: nonnegative (k,i,t,l), sum=d, i>=m. (7) Every allowed coefficient is positive. For left/right a path consisting entirely of one-steps supplies every outer monomial. For cross the two positive triangular polynomials and their forced x+y supply every vector in (7); their coefficientwise comparison transfers positivity to P_cross. Fix one assignment s in {cross,left,right}^R. Its shared exponent arrays are bounded bipartite flows: a port supplies d, an ordinary face demands d, a protected face demands0, and each literal incidence is an arc. Impose the middle-arc bounds in (7), with all other bounds0<=q<=d. Multiple incidences remain separate arcs. All supplies, demands and bounds are integers affine in m. Subtract lower bounds and apply the elementary augmenting-path max-flow argument. Feasibility is equivalent to a finite set of cut inequalities, each of the form a*m+b>=0, together with the nonnegative residual supplies/demands. Therefore each assignment is either feasible at EVERY sufficiently large integer m, or infeasible at every sufficiently large m. There is no unproved arithmetic subsequence. There is also a uniform explicit test level. Each residual port supply has constant term -1; each residual ordinary-face demand has constant term -1 and each protected demand has constant term0. Every residual incidence capacity has constant term -1. In a cut inequality sum_(f in B) demand_f + sum_(e in A,f notin B) capacity_(e,f) -sum_(e in A) supply_e >=0, the constant term therefore lies between -5R and R, since there are R ordinary faces and 4R incidence arcs. The other nonnegativity conditions have constant terms -1 or0. Every slope is an integer. Hence at m_*=5R+1 all positive-slope inequalities hold and all negative-slope inequalities fail; the zero-slope conditions are unchanged. Consequently an assignment is eventually feasible IF AND ONLY IF its bounded integer flow is feasible at this ONE level m_*. The same verdict then holds at every m>=m_*. This is a finite source-incidence test, not a numerical asymptotic heuristic; no entropy convexity is used. Let A_D consist of the eventually feasible assignments. This is a finite, level-independent combinatorial test. It is essential to make this test before replacing m/N by1/2: a limiting inequality can be an equality while its original finite inequality is violated by1. In particular two overloads on one ordinary face are impossible because 2m>d, even though their limiting loads would sum to1. No protected face can be overloaded. The [original gap-graph theorem](actual_fejer_cross_half_source_reduction.md) then makes every noncross assignment in A_D a rooted forest, with its prescribed orientation. No arbitrary graph or re-marking is introduced. An exact example shows why a terminal equality does not permit deleting one forest label. For the certified width-three word [1,3,0,2,4,1,3], the protected faces are 0,8 and the ordered port quartets are (1,0,4,2), (2,0,5,3), (0,1,6,4), (4,2,7,5), (5,3,8,0), (6,4,0,7), (7,5,0,8). Take right types at ports4,6 (zero-based) and cross types elsewhere. For every m>=2, the following rows give an actual feasible integer flow: (m,0,1,m-2), (m,0,0,m-1), (0,m-1,m-1,1), (2m-3,1,1,0), (m-1,m,0,0), (m,0,0,m-1), (m-1,m,0,0). All ordinary targets equal 2m-1. Its scaled terminal point has nu_4=1/2, where the local right entropy and degree vector admit a cross description. Nevertheless changing ONLY port4 to cross is infeasible at every m: its protected c8,y0 force x5>=m since b3<=m-1, while the retained right port6 forces b5>=m. Face5 would receive at least 2m>2m-1. This is an obstruction to that relabeling step, not to the volume bound. For s in A_D, let P_s be the closed limiting flow polytope: port supply1, ordinary demand1, protected demand0, cross middle upper bounds1/2, and one-sided middle lower bound1/2. On cross ports retain the triangular split in (6), or equivalently maximize over that split after fixing q. ## 3. Every limiting flow is approximated by actual integer source degrees Here is an elementary argument avoiding any convexity hypothesis on E. Fix q in P_s. Clamp its entries to the finite-N bounds after division by N. This changes each entry by O(1/N), so the node-balance defects are O(1/N). Choose ANY feasible real finite-N flow, which exists by eventual feasibility. Its signed difference from the clamped flow is a directed residual flow. Decompose it into simple defect-to-defect paths and cycles. Discard cycles. Each retained edge adjustment is in the direction of the chosen feasible flow and has no larger magnitude, so it respects the finite bounds. The path part has the required divergences. Its total mass is O(1/N), and each simple path has length bounded by the FIXED incidence graph. Thus it repairs q by O(1/N) to a feasible finite-N flow. The estimate is uniform in q. Multiply by N. Supplies, demands and bounds are integers. Round inside the floor/ceiling interval of each entry by cancelling fractional cycles in the bipartite graph. A node incident to a fractional edge cannot have fractional degree1 because its balance is integer. Hence a fractional cycle exists until all entries are integral. Alternating increments on that cycle preserve every balance; move until some entry is integral. Each step respects the original integer bounds. The final rounding error is at most1 in each entry. This constructs an actual source degree vector whose scaled value tends to q. For cross ports choose the two triangular outer allocations and the one forced x/y factor after the incidence rounding. All local allocations are intervals with integer endpoints. Their rescaled endpoints converge to the endpoints of the limiting allocation interval, so any prescribed limiting split has an integer approximation, still respecting the SAME total q. This retains the finite forced factor even at zero outer degrees; the finite support has at least one outer unit. Conversely every sequence of scaled feasible integer flows has a subsequence converging to P_s. These two statements supply precisely the lattice approximation needed below. ## 4. General shared variational theorem Define the finite classical optimization problem W_D=max_(s in A_D) max_(q in P_s) sum_e E_(s_e)(q_e), (8) with the triangular splitting variables of (6) retained. All domains are compact and all local entropies are continuous. Then, provided A_D is nonempty, lim_(even N->infinity) N^(-1) log Z_(D,N)=W_D. (9) Proof. Expand the original positive product by the three disjoint local supports in (7), then by its incidence degrees. At cross ports the exact coefficientwise bounds B<=P_cross<=3B permit replacing P_cross by B=4(x+y)D_b D_c for this rate calculation: after the other positive factors and the SAME target extraction, the whole assignment is trapped between the replaced coefficient and 3^(number of cross ports) times it. Only this replaced coefficient is expanded into triangular splits; an exact factorization of P_cross itself is not asserted. The number of terms is polynomial in N because D is fixed. Every nonzero term has its logarithmic rate given by the uniform closed local coefficient theorems in section1. Compactness therefore bounds the limsup by (8). For the liminf choose a maximizer, use section3 to realize its actual integer degrees and splits at every sufficiently large even N, and retain that single positive term. Its rate tends to (8). There is no cancellation and no independent optimization of repeated faces. If A_D is empty, the original positive coefficient is eventually zero; one can use W_D=-infinity. The theorem does NOT prove the reverse inequality. ## 5. The central forest corridor already has the geometric rate Under the same labeled right-angled certificate, there is a genuine shared coefficient estimate near the central row. For a left path put k=M-j, so its overloaded exponent is m+k; for a right path use the reflected k=i-m. If all such k are at most delta*N, then the source formed by these terms together with the all-cross term obeys Phi_D <= liminf_(even N) N^-1 log Z_(D,N,delta) <=limsup_(even N) N^-1 log Z_(D,N,delta) <=Phi_D+C_D*delta*(1+log(1/delta)). (10) In particular if every noncross excess is restricted to K_N=o(N), the restricted source INCLUDING all-cross has limit Phi_D. The bound is valid at arbitrary fixed width and keeps both protected targets. Here is the exact transfer estimate behind this assertion. Put A_j=2+c_j, delta_N=A_M, and let R_j be the lower-block path numerator starting at j with all b powers retained. A positive path injection gives R_(j+1)>=A_j*b*R_j, 0<=j<M. (11) To prove it, raise every visited row by1. Both allowed sine step weights increase on this half interval. If U is the old unused set, the new unused set is {0} union(U+1), and its spectral-factor ratio is A_0*product_(r in U)(A_(r+1)/A_r)>=A_j, since all omitted ratios are at most1 and the full product telescopes. The outer exponents are unchanged and the b power increases by1. Iterating in the positive LAURENT coefficient order and using the literal half-block expansion gives P_left<=2c^m R_M sum_(j=0)^M (delta_N/A_j)(c/b)^(M-j). The paired-root comparison supplies R_M<=sqrt(C_N)D_b and D_c>=C_front*c^M, where C_N=4(4-delta_N)/(delta_N*N^2), C_front=N/sqrt(delta_N*(4-delta_N)), H_M=8(x+y)D_bD_c/N. Consequently the individual excess-k piece is bounded coefficientwise by P_(left,k)<=a_(N,k)*[H_M/(x+y)]*c^(k+1)*b^(-k), a_(N,k)=(4-delta_N)/(2N)*delta_N/A_(M-k)<=2/N. (12) The reflected formula interchanges b,c. This is an inequality for the original polynomials inside a finite Laurent ring; it does not replace a one-sided port by an identity coupon. In particular the remaining coefficient target changes by gamma_e=(k_e+1)e_overloaded-k_e e_parent. (13) A protected parent may therefore acquire a POSITIVE remaining target. It must not be set to zero before extracting that shifted coefficient. To obtain (10), take the original complete geometric curvature vector and replace its two zero marked entries by one epsilon>0, leaving all ordinary entries unchanged. This is ONE shared radius vector, fixed before N. At a certified port the outer matching pair cannot be the marked MAIN pair, so x+y stays bounded below; a fixed power of epsilon would also suffice here. The Laurent factors in (12) cost at most exp[C_D*delta*N*(1+log(1/epsilon))], with fixed extra constants. There are polynomially many k choices and finitely many assignments. Positive Cauchy applied to the original target thus bounds the entire restricted coefficient by the complete product at that shared vector times this exponential cost and a polynomial in N. No shifted marked target is discarded. The complete capacity at these regularized radii is at most Phi_D+C_D*sqrt(epsilon). Indeed its log-radius derivative is the actual center angle divided by2pi. A single regularized zero corner has angle O(epsilon); two simultaneously regularized zero corners in a triangle have angles O(sqrt(epsilon)). Integrating from0 to epsilon and summing the finitely many triangles gives this modulus. The original target logs involve only the unchanged ordinary faces. All beta, forced-factor and other retained scalar logarithms are o(N). Choose epsilon=delta^2, FIXED before N. This proves the upper estimate in (10); all-cross gives its lower estimate. For K_N=o(N), first let N tend to infinity at each fixed delta, then delta tend to zero. This argument does not use a downhill-radius condition. It shows that the unresolved positive-source maximum requires a genuinely macroscopic one-sided excess, rather than an omitted central endpoint window. ## 6. The geometric comparison and the remaining quantum assertion The geometric problem isolated by this variational theorem was the inequality W_D<=Vol(Y_D)/(2pi). (14) This is a problem about the actual compact constrained entropy maximum, including every admissible forest and boundary stratum. It is not the unjustified interchange of inf over shared radii and max over local weighted branches. Indeed the fixed-degree coefficient entropy can be nonconvex in a terminal row, so that shortcut is unavailable. At full interior critical points, the half-block equations have the parabolic Casimir energy sigma=-2 and the actual local action F(x,b,y)-F(x,c,y)+log c (or its reflected version). Developing these critical points and their boundary strata into actual augmented-group representations with the correct regulator proves (14) in the separate [endpoint theorem](general_fejer_endpoint_source_volume.md); it is not assumed in (9). title: The global signed cut-ball regulator, with the original marked apex

text: # The global signed cut-ball regulator, with the original marked apex 31 October 2026. conditional stationary-stratum lemma. Hypotheses are exactly the finite-positive-ordinary-radius stationary stratum and signed/cooriented circle development of [the marked signed-development lemma](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_fejer_marked_signed_development.md). This proof does NOT use invariance of an open crossing regulator under resetting a Gauss frame: that assertion failed the recorded direct test. The original graph, marking and untwisted shaded pairings stay fixed. ## 1. An elementary cyclic polygon chain identity Let z_0,...,z_(n-1) lie on one Euclidean circle, in their RECORDED polygon order, not necessarily its circular order. Choose real arguments phi_j for the points. Consecutive increments d_j=phi_(j+1)-phi_j may be signed and may differ by multiples of2pi; close with phi_n=phi_0+2pi w. Cone an oriented fan triangulation of this polygon to the common ideal point infinity in upper half-space. Its oriented volume is sum_(j=0)^(n-1) Lambda(d_j/2). (1) For an oriented triangle of distinct points on a circle, the usual ideal-tetrahedron angle formula gives (1): its three oriented half-arcs are its three angles modulo pi, with the common orientation sign. Lambda(-a)=-Lambda(a), Lambda(a+pi)=Lambda(a), and Lambda(pi-a)=-Lambda(a), so the formula is independent of the chosen argument lifts and holds for either triangle orientation. Sum it over the fan. Each internal diagonal appears with opposite orientations; its two Lambda terms cancel EXACTLY. Only the original boundary edges remain. No convexity or winding-one assumption has been used. The identity also includes repeated nonadjacent polygon vertices. First apply the finite fan identity with distinct generic points on that SAME circle. An edge with coincident endpoints contributes Lambda(0)=0. Any degenerate fan tetrahedron has zero limiting volume: its coalescing base points stay on this one circle, so its cross-ratio with infinity tends to the real axis. Equivalently use the normalized alternating ideal chain with repeated vertices set to zero. This is not an arbitrary four-ideal-point collision assertion. For a polygon on a line, every cone tetrahedron is coplanar with infinity and (1) has value zero in the limiting line interpretation. ## 2. Apply it to the ONE signed developed circle family At a finite white vertex f, its actual face polygon consists of the contact points with its neighboring white circles, in the original cyclic source order. At a triangle t its two successive contact rays turn by sigma_t theta_(t,f), modulo2pi. Hence (1) gives its oriented white-pyramid volume as sum_(t at f) sigma_t Lambda(theta_(t,f)/2). (2) This works at an overloaded vertex with winding zero just as at a winding-one vertex. If its generalized middle corner is written 2pi-theta rather than -theta, its Lambda contribution is identical by pi-periodicity. Thus no integer winding/branch constant is lost. Both marked white faces are lines through the cone apex and have zero contribution, matching their zero center angles. The shaded face of t is the ideal triangle of the three pairwise contacts of its tangent white circles. For a finite or one-line triangle its Euclidean angles are (pi-theta_(t,f))/2. Its orientation in the common plane is sigma_t times the original positive convention. Consequently coning this original ordered shaded triangle to infinity gives sigma_t sum_(f in t) Lambda((pi-theta_(t,f))/2). (3) This elementary contact-angle relation is unchanged by reflection of a center triangle. A two-line uv triangle contains the apex itself; its cone has zero volume, and (3) is zero because theta=(0,0,pi). These are precisely the forced degeneracies allowed here. Summing (2),(3) for one abstract cut ball gives V_ball = (1/2) sum_t sigma_t V(theta_t). (4) The developed boundary can overlap or fold. Equation (4) is the volume of its oriented chain, not the volume of an embedded region. ## 3. Why this is the original representation fundamental chain Use the TWO literal topological cut balls of the original augmented projection, with their original white/shaded cellulation and face permutations. On the first ball map every ideal contact vertex to its contact point in the ONE developed family. Map white polygon edges and shaded edges to their geodesics, and triangulate each white face by a fixed original combinatorial fan. These finite oriented face chains form a closed boundary cycle: every original edge occurs twice with opposite orientations, even if developed contacts coincide. Use the EXISTING labeled convex right-angled certificate to select the actual abstract triangulation once and for all: fan each incident white face from the original marked vertex p; triangulate every nonincident white face compatibly; then cone p to the nonincident triangles. The certified convex ball proves that this is a degree-one triangulation of the original ball. Keep that exact labeled abstract chain and merely change its developed ideal vertices to the signed circle contacts. Its volume is the cone of the boundary cycle to p=infinity; triangles already incident to p contribute zero cone terms. No new interior ideal vertex or new cusp is introduced. Degree one concerns the abstract original domain only, not its possibly folded developed image. Use ONE global reflection r_u to map the second ball. Reverse its abstract orientation together with this orientation-reversing target reflection, so its volume contribution is the same as (4). Do not choose independent block, port or face reflections for that ball. The face pairings agree with the original representation as follows. On a white face f, the prescribed orientation-preserving map is r_f r_u; reflection r_f fixes the entire white plane. It therefore identifies the complete second-ball white polygon chain with the first-ball chain, including every vertex and the original edge order. Here are the shaded maps with the actual copy labels and permutation. All ports in this endpoint source are UNTWISTED. In each original ball write its two shaded triangles as S_0=(O,C_1,C_2), S_1=(O,C_3,C_0). They pair WITHIN that same ball by O->O, C_1->C_0, C_2->C_3; this is exactly (3) of [the original matching geometry](../papers/marked-fillings/README.md), not the across-copy half-twist permutation (4). In the first ball, input A_b has its fixed flag C_1=x/b contact, input B_b its fixed flag C_2=b/y contact, and P=B_b A_b its flag O=x/y contact. Equation (5) of the line adapter gives C A_b C^-1=A_c, C B_b C^-1=B_c, and CP=PC. Therefore C sends these THREE flags respectively to C_0=x/c contact, C_3=c/y contact, and O. They are distinct at every permitted finite, one-line and two-line triangle. The ordered ideal-triangle isometry is thus exactly C, including its original pointwise permutation. On the reflected second ball the map is r_u C r_u (composition of anti-Mobius maps on either side), from r_u S_0 to r_u S_1 with the SAME three labels. The reverse pairing is its inverse. Thus no shaded face is silently moved across copies and no independent reflection is selected for the second map. Its whole ideal face is paired, not only the common auxiliary fixed point. These are precisely the untwisted Morse/threading pairings already used to construct the representation. Hence the two abstract ball chains descend, with THEIR original multiplicities and orientations, to an equivariant relative fundamental chain of the original exterior. In particular an immersed white polygon is not replaced by its image counted once, and an overloaded winding- zero face is not deleted from the abstract source cellulation. For completeness this ideal-chain construction has the usual genuine cusp realization. Each main meridian is NONCENTRAL parabolic: its two adjacent white circles are distinct and tangent. Its actual longitude commutes with it, hence belongs in PSL2 to its translation centralizer and preserves every horosphere at the same contact. At an auxiliary cusp the ACTUAL two generators are C^-1 and its preferred longitude P=B_b A_b (with the already recorded harmless central lift). Both are in the same parabolic translation group at the outer contact. This remains true if C=I: P is still noncentral because the matching outer pair is distinct and tangent. Commuting with identity ALONE is not used to infer any peripheral property. Thus the WHOLE peripheral subgroup preserves the chosen contact horosphere in every case. Decorate each contact by the horosphere of its ordered tangent white pair (normalize the pair to opposite parallel planes at width1, then take height1). The actual shaded map carries this decoration: it carries both adjacent white planes, because each is the unique plane orthogonal to the shaded plane along the corresponding edge. White reflections carry it as well. Use finite INCIDENCE corner points on these paired horospheres, truncate, and attach the original conical cusp tails. The established O(T^-2) horospherical boundary flux compares this with the ideal chain. No parabolic cusp vertex is falsely assigned a single fixed finite point. Only finitely many paired incidence points are used. Thus representation volume, defined by the original equivariant relative fundamental class, is Vol(rho)=2 V_ball=sum_t sigma_t V(theta_t). (5) All boundary/pairing data have been checked at the global chain level. An individual re-framed open crossing word need not have its former regulator. Its boundary correction is not discarded or assumed zero locally; instead (5) computes the sewn fundamental class directly. ## 4. The conditional actual-entropy consequence At the stationary stratum under discussion, the [proved exact coefficient identity](actual_fejer_half_block_entropy.md) is C(alpha)=V(2pi alpha)/(2pi). A cross port contributes the sum of its two C's; a strict left/right Green port contributes their signed difference, including the forced marked zero limits. These are the actual local E values, with their absolute normalization. Therefore sum_e E_e = (1/(2pi)) sum_t sigma_t V(theta_t) = Vol(rho)/(2pi) <= Vol(Y_D)/(2pi). (6) The last inequality is the [proved representation-volume bound](../papers/casimir-source-asymptotics/README.md) for the actual original hyperbolic exterior. No action constant, reference-flag normalization or separately chosen regulator has been introduced. This handles a FULL stationary configuration with finite positive ordinary radius multipliers and only the forced marked-line nonregularities. It is not yet the inequality for every maximum W_D. Additional ordinary zero/infinite multipliers, flat triangles, diagonal mu=nu, terminal nu=1/2 and other free KKT strata still require their own limiting or block construction. In particular one cannot silently change an eventually feasible forest type into a cross type: the exact finite support can prevent that even when their limiting local entropy and degree vector coincide. The cut-ball comparison is on the stated stationary stratum. It does not cover every boundary maximum or select a quantum cycle.

title: The one-sided full-numerator remainder on actual spectral polydisks
status: Absolute spectral-polydisk remainder gap; all parities
text: # The one-sided full-numerator remainder on actual spectral polydisks 31 October 2026. spectral remainder theorem. This is an absolute bound for the original shared polynomial numerator at the fixed root. It uses the unique geometric maximizer and the actual odd/even positive majorants. It is not a relative estimate against an oscillatory value, a Gaussian cycle theorem, or a genuine-q normal estimate. ## 1. The positive reference source and its fixed entropy gap Fix the original certified flat plat D, with R ports, unchanged ordinary face targets d=N-1 and its two protected targets zero. Write Phi=Vol(Y_D)/(2pi), V_N(sigma)=chi_N(sigma)(sigma-Omega_N)^(-1), F_N=-V_N(-2) (N even), F_N=V_N(-2)-N^(-2)partial_sigma V_N(-2) (N odd). These are the actual covariant coupons in the [homogeneous source theorem](../papers/filling-bounds/README.md), with the [exact odd/even majorants](actual_fejer_odd_regularized_full_numerator.md). The coefficient of H_(F_N) at every local degree-d exponent is positive, and its logarithmic rate is uniformly the same continuous h(q), q=n/d, at both parities. Let Z_F be their original whole shared coefficient. Then log Z_F/N -> Phi. The [unique-maximizer theorem](actual_fejer_unique_geometric_maximizer.md) gives a single q_geom in the compact incidence polytope Q_D, with every middle load strictly less than1/2. On the closed set B_D={q in Q_D: some q_(e,b)>=1/2 or q_(e,c)>=1/2} the continuous full entropy has maximum at most Phi-gamma, gamma>0, provided B_D is nonempty. Fix that gamma throughout. The empty case has no feasible one-sided source summands and the conclusions below hold with identically zero remainder. The path endpoints i<=j determine the original middle exponents b^i c^(d-j). At N=2m, CROSS means i<=m-1 and j>=m; LEFT means j<=m-1, and RIGHT means i>=m. At N=2m+1, CROSS means i<=m and j>=m; LEFT means j<=m-1, and RIGHT means i>=m+1. Thus any noncross term has a normalized middle load strictly greater than1/2, in B_D, at BOTH parities. Let Z_F,nc be the original coefficient obtained by retaining all path assignments with at least one noncross port in the positive product of H_(F_N). Positivity, the uniform local coefficient theorem and the polynomial number of integer arrays imply Z_F,nc <= exp[N(Phi-gamma+o(1))]. (1) The o(1) is independent of any spectral parameter used below. It is an all-level statement with the indicated parity-dependent F_N, not a subsequence assertion. No fixed-label eventual-feasibility test is needed: the upper bound uses the FULL local coefficients at the same actual integer exponents and the compact set B_D. ## 2. Exact support-preserving local spectral comparisons Put a_j=2+2cos((2j+1)pi/N), theta(r)=arcosh(1+r/2), r>=0. Let P_N(u)=(-1)^d H_(V_N(-2-u)); its unused-row path products are nonnegative polynomials in u and the four original face variables. For a complex u and |u|<=r, the triangle inequality on EACH original path gives its positive value at r as a coefficientwise majorant. All physical missing steps and endpoint zeros stay literal. At EVEN N every a_j is positive. The ratio of an unused-row product at r to its value at0 is bounded by the product over ALL rows. Hence |P_N(u)|_coef <= C_N(r) H_(F_N), C_N(r)=prod_j(1+r/a_j) =cosh^2(N theta(r)/2) <= exp(N theta(r)). (2) At ODD N=2m+1 only a_m is zero. The exact positive decomposition is H_(F_N)=P_N(0)+N^(-2)Q, Q=partial_u P_N(0). Write Q_skip for those derivative paths that skip row m. Visiting paths have nonzero value at0; skipping paths have precisely one factor u. Therefore |P_N(u)|_coef <= C_N(r)[P_N(0)+r Q_skip] <= C_N(r)max(1,N^2 r) H_(F_N), (3) C_N(r)=prod_(j!=m)(1+r/a_j) =[sinh(N theta(r)/2)/(N sinh(theta(r)/2))]^2 <= exp((N-1)theta(r)), with C_N(0)=1. These statements retain the independent spectral semisimple data in Q, not only the complete values at the root nodes. Equations (2)--(3) apply SEPARATELY to every specified endpoint-support class CROSS, LEFT or RIGHT. The comparison does not change i or j, nor any local face exponent. At odd levels all noncross paths skip m; there (3) may be sharpened to C_N(r)N^2r times the corresponding F_N piece, but the displayed common max suffices. Visited-central derivative paths belong to the cross support; they are never relabeled noncross. ## 3. The original shared numerator and its absolute remainder Let S_N(sigma_1,...,sigma_R) be the entire original shared coefficient of the product of H_(V_N(sigma_e)), with its original mark, cup/cap normalization and target degrees. Let S_N,cross be the same coefficient with every port restricted to the CROSS path class above. This is a literal finite path partition of the polynomial numerator. It does not replace a physical coupon by a freely interpolated off-node model. Set Delta_N=S_N-S_N,cross. Expanding this difference retains exactly the assignments having at least one noncross port. The common sign (-1)^(dR) has modulus one. Apply (2)--(3) before taking the ONE original shared target coefficient. For |sigma_e+2|<=r_e this proves the finite inequality |Delta_N(sigma)| <= Z_F,nc prod_e M_N(r_e), (4) where M_N(r)=cosh^2(N theta(r)/2) for even N, and M_N(r)=C_N(r)max(1,N^2r) for odd N. No extra N^R, independent face norm, changed protected degree, or discarded Fourier alias occurs. For fixed bounded radii, the odd additional factors cost only O(log N) per port. Combining (1) and (4) gives uniformly on the full polydisk |Delta_N(sigma)| <= exp{N[Phi-gamma+sum_e theta(r_e)+o(1)]}. (5) In particular for a common fixed radius r the exponent is Phi-gamma+R theta(r)+o(1). Since theta(r)->0, choose ANY sufficiently small fixed r with R theta(r)<gamma/4. For all sufficiently large N, the whole remainder on that polydisk is bounded by exp[N(Phi-gamma/2)]. (6) The radius can be made arbitrarily smaller. It depends on the fixed diagram's gap, and no uniformity in growing diagrams or bridge width is asserted. For ANY shrinking radii r_(e,N)->0, (4) instead gives limsup N^(-1)log sup_(|sigma_e+2|<=r_(e,N))|Delta_N| <= Phi-gamma. (7) This remains true for polynomially or exponentially small radii; the odd factor max(1,N^2r) causes no adverse small-radius cost. These are ABSOLUTE errors relative to the geometric exponential scale. They are not relative errors divided by S_N or S_N,cross, which may vanish on a complex spectral locus. A nonzero relative cross packet still requires an independent asymptotic theorem. ## 4. Spectral derivatives and the retained contour limitation On the exact Cauchy polydisk r_e=N^(-2), theta(r_e)<=1/N and M_N(r_e)<=e at both parities. Consequently for every multiindex alpha, |partial_sigma^alpha Delta_N(-2,...,-2)| <= e^R alpha! N^(2|alpha|) Z_F,nc. (8) For fixed alpha this has rate at most Phi-gamma. Fixed smaller polydisks inside (6) also retain its exponential bound under fixed spectral derivatives, by ordinary Cauchy margins. These are derivatives of the original numerator's spectral variables, not genuine-q normals. The actual direct-power period still contains the Gaussian factors, the full chi_N denominators, and contours enclosing ALL physical poles. The estimates above isolate its numerator on a specified small spectral polydisk only. They do not justify discarding a growing Gaussian arc, choosing a nonzero charge, moving the original cycle into that polydisk, or asserting a contribution to the filled-knot invariant. Those phase-sensitive operations remain separate. The spectral estimates use support-preserving path comparisons at both parities, with fixed or shrinking radii and the stated derivatives. Finite numerical experiments do not establish the asymptotic cancellation bounds.

title: Maximal volume fixes the actual marked endpoint configuration
status: Unique marked endpoint maximum; strict complement gap
text: # Maximal volume fixes the actual marked endpoint configuration 31 October 2026. general concentration theorem. This strengthens the already proved positive endpoint rate. It does not identify a phase-sensitive filling cycle, a genuine-q normal, or a Gaussian contour. All group conjugacies below are in PSL2(C); central SL2 lift signs are not inferred from volume. ## 1. Equality in the natural-map bound gives actual conjugacy Let Gamma be the marked complete finite-volume hyperbolic exterior group, with its original inclusion iota into PSL2(C). Let rho be ONE fixed representation with Vol(rho)=Vol(Gamma\H3)>0, in the normalization of [the representation-volume proof](../papers/casimir-source-asymptotics/README.md). Its proved section3 constructs orientation-preserving target isometries g_j and natural maps F_j such that G_j=g_j F_j -> J locally in C1 on H3, (1) where J is a global orientation-preserving hyperbolic isometry. This convergence is obtained on every compact subset with the SAME g_j. The equivariance is exact: rho_j(gamma)G_j(x)=G_j(iota(gamma)x), rho_j(gamma)=g_j rho(gamma)g_j^(-1). (2) For each fixed gamma the right and left input points converge. In particular rho_j(gamma) sends one point converging to J(x) into a bounded set, so these isometries are precompact: the stabilizer of a point of H3 is compact. A limiting isometry sends J(x) to J(iota(gamma)x) for every x, by (1)--(2). Hence it is uniquely J iota(gamma) J^(-1), and rho_j(gamma) -> J iota(gamma) J^(-1) (3) for every gamma. Equivalently one may first use four noncoplanar points and a finite generating set. This is exactly the equivariance upgrade in the proved peripheral-gap note; it uses no compactness of g_j yet. We now prove that for this FIXED rho the g_j themselves have a bounded subsequence. Suppose instead that a subsequence escapes every compact subset of PSL2(C). Choose its elementary singular-value decomposition g_j=k_j diag(exp(t_j/2),exp(-t_j/2)) l_j, k_j,l_j in PSU(2), t_j -> infinity. Pass to convergent k_j,l_j, with limits k,l.
