For each fixed gamma the matrix entries of rho_j(gamma) stay bounded by (3), in either SL2 lift. The upper-right entry of the middle conjugated matrix is exp(t_j) [l_j rho(gamma) l_j^(-1)]_12. It follows that [l rho(gamma) l^(-1)]_12=0 for every generator and hence for every gamma. Thus rho has a common fixed point p on CP1. Each rho_j then has the common fixed point p_j=g_j p. Compactness of CP1 gives a further subsequence p_j->p_infinity. Passing to the action in (3) shows that the complete holonomy J iota J^(-1) fixes p_infinity, a contradiction. Here non-elementarity of the complete exterior is elementary in this setting, not an imported volume-rigidity theorem. For the actual certified exterior, the noncentral based cusp words at distinct vertices of one convex white face already have distinct fixed points. More generally, if a complete cusped finite-volume lattice fixed one point, normalize it to infinity and take a precisely invariant embedded cusp horoball. All its translates are concentric and intersect, so every group element stabilizes the horoball and its horospheres. The positive finite-area Euclidean cusp quotient then extends through all heights; its hyperbolic volume below the horoball is infinite. This contradicts finite volume. Therefore g_j has a convergent subsequence g. Equation (3) yields g rho(gamma) g^(-1)=J iota(gamma) J^(-1) for all gamma. (4) In particular rho ITSELF, not just a limit of its characters, is conjugate to the actual marked complete holonomy. This proof does not deduce conjugacy merely from faithfulness and does not assume a closed orbit from outside results. ## 2. Every endpoint maximizer has the original labeled white circles Use the original fixed certified flat plat D and the full compact incidence-flow entropy H_D(q)=sum_e h(q_e), q in Q_D, W_D=max H_D=Phi_D=Vol(Y_D)/(2pi). (5) The last equality and all boundary reductions are the [full endpoint theorem](general_fejer_endpoint_source_volume.md). Let q be ANY maximizer, choosing maximizing triangle allocations at CROSS ports. No port of q is pure-middle. Otherwise the exact identity reduction and hybrid-piece representation construct a representation of the original pi_1(Y_D) with volume 2pi H_D(q)=Vol(Y_D), killing an essential original crossing-circle meridian. The strict-kernel theorem forbids this. Thus there is no identity contraction at a maximum. Consequently the source white triangulation is still the original simplicial sphere. Its induced graphs have no parallel-edge digons, so the hybrid tight-set classification gives no proper tight set. The positive hybrid witness and the proved corner expansions then give finite positive ordinary multipliers and only the two original marked zero curvatures. Terminal seams may be tagged CROSS, without changing q or entropy. The resulting signed circle development and original cut-ball representation rho are the regular marked ones, with volume Vol(Y_D). There are no independent pieces or arbitrary closing cusps in this equality case. Apply (4). It remains to show that conjugacy of the original marked representation actually determines its labeled face geometry. At every original MAIN contact, the based meridian supplied by the literal prefix/turn dictionary is noncentral parabolic and fixes exactly that contact. At every original MATCHING contact, the recorded full ordered product P=BA is the noncentral parabolic preferred longitude, and its unique fixed point is that contact. These are the actual based words of the original cut balls, not just unbased cusp conjugacy classes. There are no deleted ports with free peripheral flags here. A conjugacy to the actual complete holonomy therefore takes every labeled developed contact to the corresponding original complete contact. Each original white face of the nondegenerate convex certificate has at least THREE DISTINCT such contacts. Three distinct points of CP1 determine a unique generalized circle. Thus every labeled developed white circle/line is carried to its original complete white circle/line. This uses the source dictionary as well as the representation; an unlabeled character alone would not suffice. Normalize both configurations at their original marked MAIN contact p=infinity. The conjugacy sends p to p because it carries that based noncentral meridian. It is therefore affine, z->a z+b, a!=0. Affine maps preserve bounded disks and oriented center triangles. The two ordered marked lines also determine the strip sides; the ordinary bounded circles lie on the prescribed inward sides. Thus the possible choice of a complementary disk is not an additional freedom. The complete circle packing has the positive center-triangle signs in the original cyclic order. The reconstructed signed development must have those same signs. A GREEN port would have a negative triangle with an ordinary overloaded middle. Such a triangle cannot be a sign-invisible two-line triangle: on the original marked MAIN edge one of its middles is protected, and an outer matching pair cannot be the two protected vertices. It has either three finite circles or one line and two finite circles. In the latter case the cooriented line and horizontal contact order still distinguish its sign. Both cases contradict the recovered complete configuration. Hence EVERY port of a maximum is CROSS, and every local triangle angle is its actual complete geometric angle. The common affine scale cancels from all angle formulas. Let q_geom,e=(alpha_x,in+alpha_x,out, alpha_b, alpha_c, alpha_y,in+alpha_y,out), where each alpha is the corresponding complete angle divided by2pi. Then the preceding argument proves q=q_geom, and the maximizing CROSS allocations are geometric. (6) Thus q_geom is the UNIQUE full incidence-flow maximizer. No unspecified choice of square root, resetting of Gauss flags, or local open-word regulator invariance was used. ## 3. Compact gaps and the entire one-sided remainder For every epsilon>0 with a nonempty set in the maximum below, compactness of Q_D and continuity of the full h give gamma_D(epsilon) =Phi_D-max_{q in Q_D, ||q-q_geom||>=epsilon} H_D(q)>0. (7) This is a fixed-D gap; no effective uniformity in diagrams or increasing bridge width is asserted. There is also a single gap for all one-sided branches. At every original port its two outer vertices form a MATCHING edge. They cannot both be the original protected pair, whose edge is MAIN in the simple labeled certificate. Hence each complete triangle has middle angle strictly less than pi, even when one outer face is marked. Therefore eta_D=min_e {1/2-q_geom,e,b, 1/2-q_geom,e,c}>0. The closed set B_D={q in Q_D: some q_e,b>=1/2 or q_e,c>=1/2} is separated from q_geom by eta_D in the sup norm. If nonempty, its maximum entropy is Phi_D-gamma_D^one with gamma_D^one>0. At even N=2m,d=2m-1 every literal LEFT coefficient has c exponent at least m, and every RIGHT coefficient has b exponent at least m. After normalizing by d, any summand with at least one such port lies in B_D. The actual finite one-sided coefficient is bounded by the full positive coefficient at the same exponent. The uniform full coefficient theorem, polynomially many source summands and positivity consequently imply limsup_(even N) N^(-1)log Z_(D,N;at least one one-sided port) <=Phi_D-gamma_D^one. (8) When no such feasible source terms exist the left side is -infinity. The same argument bounds every fixed neighborhood complement by (7). In particular the whole positive source outside its CROSS contribution is exponentially smaller, uniformly over all its finitely many one-sided forest patterns. No subtraction or cancellation estimate is needed for this positive-source statement. The odd regularized source has the same uniform h and a positive path split with LEFT c>=m+1 or RIGHT b>=m+1, d=2m. Thus the same fixed-D gap applies to its one-sided remainder as well, by the separate exact [odd comparison theorem](actual_fejer_odd_regularized_full_numerator.md). Its extra visited-central spectral derivative paths stay in the cross support and are not called a one-sided remainder. These gaps do not themselves give a relative Gaussian asymptotic, a bound on an oscillatory filling transform away from the controlled spectral region, or a nonzero contribution of the original filling cycle. Those remain separate quantum statements. ## 4. scope The structural conclusion uses the linked analytic and geometric proofs. Numerical tests do not establish maximal-volume rigidity or uniqueness, and this note does not settle the fixed long-filled Kashaev limit.

title: Complete figure-eight clock sectors and diagonal Gram metrics
text: # Complete figure-eight clock sectors and diagonal Gram metrics 29 October 2026. The exact factorial length frame has a polynomial original clock co-source. Nevertheless one fully anchor-contracted clock sector of the original figure-eight knot has twice the desired volume rate. Consequently every positive DIAGONAL clock metric has an exponentially excessive Cauchy budget on this actual source. This concerns a COMPLETE clock sector, after its anchor sums and original closure contractions. It is not an expanded crossing state or an arbitrary inserted coupon. It does not disprove Cauchy--Schwarz, the volume conjecture, or a coherent non-diagonal special inner product. ## 1. The original source and its exact reduced table Use `q=exp(pi*i/N)`, `Q=q^2`, `d=N-1`, `x=-q^-1`, `F_a=(Q;Q)_a`, `s_a=|F_a|`. The actual word is `[1,-2,1,-2]`. Its clocks are the original overclocks `(h_0,h_1,h_2,h_3)`. The [whole charged source](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_global_charged_bridge_flow.md) and [actual closure contractions](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_general_flow_fusion.md) give K_N=sum_h K_(N;h), K_(N;h)=(chi_N/N) zeta_(N;h) C_(N;h), |zeta|=1. (1) `chi_N` is the unchanged original external dimension/framing line; at completeness its modulus and inverse have polynomial size. Every common Cartan, pivot and source factor stays in (1). `zeta` consists only of the explicitly retained powers of `x,Q`, the crossing Cartan phases and the closure-rescaling monomials. No unknown knot scalar has been divided out. The full source support gives `h_0=0`, before any separate-sector Schur argument. In the rescaled anchors of [the actual alternating-source table](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_alternating_balanced_source.md#3-a-second-support-inequality-in-the-actual-reduced-polynomial), write `B_L(U,V;Q^p)=product_(r<L)(U-Q^(p+r)V)`. Then C_(N;h)=[A^d B^d C^d D^d] product of these EIGHT blocks: | tail -> head | length | p | | --- | --- | --- | | B -> C | d-h_0 | 0 | | C -> A | h_0 | 1 | | D -> A | d-h_1 | h_1+1 | | A -> B | h_1 | -h_1+h_2+1 | | C -> B | d-h_2 | h_0+h_2+2 | | B -> D | h_2 | -h_2-h_3-1 | | A -> D | d-h_3 | -h_1 | | D -> C | h_3 | 0 | This table includes the original pivotal closure substitutions. For auditability, `zeta` in (1) is obtained without any scalar choice by: the `charged_data` weight; the `normalized_graph` tail monomials; the `contract_edge` closure factors; and the substitutions of anchors `B,D` by `x^-1 B,x^-1 D`. Each factor is an original root of unity. Those exact operations are implemented in the audit linked below. The normalized blocks b_L=B_L/D_L, D_L=s_L^(1/2)/N^(1/4) have `D_(d-h_i)D_(h_i)=1` at each crossing. Thus the product of all EIGHT table normalizers is exactly one. The coefficient `C_(N;h)` is also the completely contracted normalized-b clock STATE in this closure-contracted presentation. The co-source remains polynomial, as in [the exact clock-source theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_length_gauge_clock_source.md). ## 2. A uniform family with no internal cancellation Let N=3k+1, d=3k, h=(0,2k,k,2k), k>=1, beta_(L,r)=|[L choose r]_Q|=s_L/(s_r s_(L-r)), S_k=sum_(r=0)^k beta_(2k,r) beta_(2k,k-r)>0. (2) Then the COMPLETE table coefficient is exactly C_(N;(0,2k,k,2k))=N q^(3k^2-2k) S_k/F_k. (3) In particular the original sector modulus is |K_(N;(0,2k,k,2k))|=|chi_N| S_k/s_k. (4) Here is a direct coefficient proof. The full `B_d(B,C;1)` contracts `B=Q^-1 C`. Its `C -> B` loop is `C^(2k)N/F_k`. Reversing the `D -> A` interval and concatenating it with the `A -> D` interval produces `B_(2k)(A,D;Q)` with reversal factor xi_1=(-Q^(2k+1))^k Q^[k(k-1)/2]. The replacement in `B -> D` contributes `Q^-k`. For the two remaining C/D intervals use B_k(C,D;Q^(-3k)) B_(2k)(D,C;1) =xi_J (C^N-D^N)/(C-Q^(-2k)D), xi_J=(-1)^(2k)Q^[(2k)(2k-1)/2]. (5) For `0<=r<=k` its coefficient of `C^(k-r)D^(2k+r)` is `xi_J Q^[-2k(2k+r)]`. The remaining A/D extraction is therefore the `D^k` coefficient of `B_(2k)(A,D;Q)^2`, times the displayed common root factors. Indeed the second interval has effective start `Q^(k-2k-2k)=Q^(-3k)=Q`. The coefficient of `A^(2k-r)D^r` in `B_(2k)(A,D;Q)` is (-q^(2k+1))^r beta_(2k,r). Consequently every summand of its `D^k` coefficient has the SAME phase. Combining this phase, (5), `xi_1` and `Q^-k` gives precisely `q^(3k^2-2k)`, proving (3). All finite sums, including the loop factor, have been evaluated; no uncontracted anchor is left. ## 3. Its exact exponential rate Put `Lambda(theta)=-integral_0^theta log(2sin u)du` and `v_3=3 Lambda(pi/3)`. The successive ratios of `beta_(2k,r)` are beta_(2k,r+1)/beta_(2k,r) =sin((2k-r)pi/N)/sin((r+1)pi/N), which decrease with `r` because `(2k+1)pi/N<pi`. Hence the symmetric summands in `S_k` are maximal at the integer(s) nearest `k/2`. The sum lies between that maximum and `(k+1)` times it. The uniform factorial estimate, including its endpoints, is log s_a=-(N/pi)Lambda(pi*a/N)+O(log N). It follows directly that lim_(k->infinity) (1/N)log(S_k/s_k) =[3Lambda(pi/3)+2Lambda(pi/6)]/pi =2v_3/pi=Vol(4_1)/pi. (6) The elementary Lobachevsky duplication identity gives `2Lambda(pi/6)=3Lambda(pi/3)=v_3`. The identification `Vol(4_1)=2v_3` uses its two regular ideal tetrahedra, rather than an asymptotic volume formula for the invariant. Thus the actual complete sector has lim (2pi/N)log|K_(N;h)|=2 Vol(4_1). (7) This is larger than the desired full-knot rate `Vol(4_1)`. The full original figure-eight scalar does have that latter rate by its separately proved positive finite sum. There must therefore be cancellation between COMPLETE clock sectors in this exact frame. ## 4. What this forces on a special inner product For the flat clock energy `G_N=sum_h |K_(N;h)|^2`, (7) gives liminf_(N=1 mod3) (pi/N)log G_N >=2 Vol(4_1). (8) The same exponent holds for the normalized-b state energy, because the original co-source coefficient in (1) has only polynomial norm. This rules out identifying that flat energy, up to subexponential factors, with a positive geometric angle partition of rate `Vol/pi`. More generally let `K=sum_h a_h f_h`. For EVERY positive diagonal metric `G=diag(g_h)` the exact Cauchy budget is B(G)=(sum_h g_h|f_h|^2)(sum_h |a_h|^2/g_h) >=(sum_h |a_h f_h|)^2. (9) The infimum over all positive `g_h` is the right side, obtained by `g_h` proportional to `|a_h|/|f_h|`; zero entries follow by limits. In particular (7) makes ALL diagonal-clock Cauchy budgets too large for the desired geometric upper exponent, even when the metric depends arbitrarily on `N` and on the entire diagram. For a general positive definite, possibly non-diagonal `G`, the Riesz vector of the linear co-source `sum_h a_h f_h` is `conj(a)`. Consequently its budget is B(G)=(f^*Gf)(a^T G^(-1)conj(a)) >=||f||^2 ||a||^2/kappa(G). (10) In the original singleton source `||a||` has polynomial upper and lower bounds, while this fixture gives `||f||^2>=exp[2N Vol(4_1)/pi-o(N)]`. Therefore a sharp budget `B(G)<=exp[N Vol(4_1)/pi+o(N)]` requires log kappa(G)>=N Vol(4_1)/pi-o(N) (11) along this subsequence. Exponential conditioning is allowed: the factorial metrics already exhibit it. Equation (11) is not a nonexistence theorem. It says that a successful coherent Gram has to retain genuine phase cancellation; a diagonal reweighting cannot replace it. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_figure_eight_clock_gram.py): the literal original reduced table and its exact root-field coefficient, the common-phase formula (3), positive-sum maximum bounds and the large-level rate. The proof above is uniform in all `k`.

title: A source-specific Fourier gap for the exact filling endpoints
text: # A source-specific Fourier gap for the exact filling endpoints 29 October 2026. The full finite filling kernel, including its linear normal weight, has exponentially small endpoint-frequency strips when paired with an analytic source having a strict complete-color maximum. This is an estimate on a truncated original color corridor. It does not bound colors outside that corridor or prove survival of the remaining filled saddle. No Fresnel endpoint remainder is replaced by a polynomial error. ## 1. An exact finite Fourier lemma with its source hypotheses Let H=floor(delta N), d_N=(H+1/2)/N. Suppose a physical packet c_h, -H<=h<=H, has a holomorphic interpolation f_N(z), for |Re z|<=2delta and |Im z|<=sigma_0, satisfying \[ \|f_N(x+iy)\|\le C N^B \exp\{N(F-a x^2+C_0 y^2)\},\qquad a>0, \tag{1} \] \[ \|c_h-f_N(h/N)\|\le C N^B e^{N(F-\gamma)},\qquad\gamma>0. \tag{2} \] These are hypotheses on the specified source, not on arbitrary holomorphic test functions. Scalar or finite-dimensional vector/operator packets with the displayed norm bounds are allowed. All constants are independent of N. For any fixed phi_0>0 and fixed nonnegative integer r, there are g>0 and C',B' such that \[ \boxed{\left\|\sum_{h=-H}^Hh^r c_h e^{i\phi h}\right\| \le C'N^{B'}e^{N(F-g)},\quad \operatorname{dist}(\phi,2\pi\mathbb Z)\ge\phi_0.} \tag{3} \] The distance is at most pi; the assertion is empty if phi_0>pi. In particular no number-theoretic restriction on N is involved. Here is an exact contour proof retaining the finite endpoints. Reduce phi modulo2pi into [phi_0,2pi-phi_0], which changes no physical value. For a fixed small sigma>0 use the rectangle in the UNWRAPPED variable z whose vertical sides have Re z=+/-(H+1/2) and whose horizontal sides have Im z=+/-sigma N. Then \[ \sum_{h=-H}^H h^r f_N(h/N)e^{i\phi h} =\frac1{2\pi i}\oint z^r f_N(z/N)e^{i\phi z} (\pi\cot\pi z-i\pi)\,dz. \tag{4} \] Every enclosed integer has residue one. The subtracted entire term -i pi changes no residue and is essential for simultaneous upper and lower decay. Indeed pi cot(pi z)-i pi=2pi i/(exp(2pi i z)-1). On the upper horizontal side its product with exp(i phi z) is at most 4pi exp(-phi sigma N); on the lower side it is at most 4pi exp(-(2pi-phi)sigma N), for all sufficiently large N. On either vertical half-integer line the sharper exact bound is |exp(i phi z)(pi cot(pi z)-i pi)| <=2pi exp[-phi_0 |Im z|]<=2pi. Choose sigma<=sigma_0 so that C_0 sigma^2<=min(a delta^2/8,phi_0 sigma/2). For large N, d_N>=delta/2. The horizontal exponent in (4) is at most F-phi_0 sigma/2, and the vertical exponent is at most F-a delta^2/8. Its contour length and z^r cost only powers of N. Equation (2) contributes at most C N^(B+r+1)exp[N(F-gamma)] on the physical grid. Thus one may take g=min(gamma,a delta^2/8,phi_0 sigma/2)>0. (5) This proof neither discards a vertical current nor assumes that a universal residue rewrite lowers the maximum of arbitrary source values. Its input is precisely the state-specific analytic bound (1). ## 2. Apply the lemma BEFORE any Gaussian approximation to the filling Use the original q,Q,kappa and the exact full-jet kernel from [the coherent filling theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_coherent_filling_gaussian_chirp.md). For t_k=(k+1/2)/N and y_k=2pi i(t_k-1/2), write \[ K_P(h)=\frac{2(-1)^{N-1}}{N^2} \sum_{k=0}^{N-1}h_k e^{hy_k} \left[(h+2Py_k/\hbar)\sinh y_k+\cosh y_k\right]. \tag{6} \] Here |h_k|=1 for every integer P and real physical data. The original normal derivative has not been dropped: 2Py_k/hbar is its unwrapped linear weight, and the h term comes from the same exact circle difference. Every factor outside exp(hy_k) is at most polynomial in N for fixed P, uniformly over k. Here beta and K_P are the coefficients of the NORMALIZED power f_P=r_N^(2P), exactly as in the filling theorem. The actual box R^(-1)R^(2P) multiplies every color pairing below by the known unit phase kappa^(2P). In particular the actual prefactor corresponding to kappa^(-P) in (10)--(11) is kappa^P. This original phase is kept; it does not change any norm estimate. Let K_P^end retain any subset of the original k values with |t_k-1/2|>=eta_0>0. For a physical EVEN core c_h=c_(-h), the original half-color convention gives the exact truncated pairing sum_(h=0)^H beta_(N-h-1)c_h =(1/2)sum_(h=-H)^H K_P(h)c_h. (7) In (6), phi_k=2pi(t_k-1/2) belongs to [-pi,pi], and dist(phi_k,2pi Z)>=2pi eta_0 on the retained endpoint strips. Apply (3) for r=0,1 and sum the N original k values. It follows that \[ \boxed{\left\|\frac12\sum_{h=-H}^H K_P^{\mathrm{end}}(h)c_h\right\| \le C_P N^{B_P}e^{N(F-g)}.} \tag{8} \] This is a bound on the EXACT finite endpoint part, with both parities, all gcd cases and the normal source retained. There is no infinite charge tail to estimate, and no O(1/N) Fresnel error against an exponential target. The bounded current of section8 in the coherent filling note is consistent with (8), but (8) does not assume that every endpoint remainder equals that one Ward forcing. ## 3. The actual mixed-source input and its precise remaining scope The EXACT finite packet in [the analytic original-source theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_pretzel_exact_analytic_color_packet.md) provides (1)--(2) for a mixed pretzel period at fixed odd s>=5, on a sufficiently small complete-color corridor. Here the other physical cusp colors may be fixed in a sufficiently small corridor. To specify the interpolation, retain a fixed regular high Newton-index window in each box, use its canonical paired factorial continuation Fhat(v-h)Fhat(v+h) and q^(h^2), and apply the UNCHANGED Hermite functional Phi_2. The lower index windows and the full nonempty alias sets are their proved exponentially smaller physical source errors. Its separate exact-interpolation bridge must be retained; a pointwise relative O(1/N) approximation on the color lattice alone does NOT imply (2) with an exponentially small Fourier error. This construction is even in the continued color, rather than an arbitrary exp(pi i h) extension. The resulting nonzero analytic leading phase, composed with chi=pi z, is even in the color variable z=h/N. Its real second derivative at zero is strictly negative, uniformly for the other sufficiently small physical colors. Taylor's formula and the elementary inequality 2|xy|<=epsilon x^2+y^2/epsilon give Re Phi(x+iy)<=Re Phi(0)-a x^2+C_0 y^2. The analytic amplitude is uniformly bounded by a polynomial in N. The exact high-window finite-source interpolation error and the alias bound supply (2), after shrinking the corridor so that its height stays within gamma/2 of the complete height. Thus (8) removes a genuine class of endpoints of this original mixed-source corridor. Aliases need not be even and are estimated before folding. Directly from the original finite H,D data, |a_n|<=1+|P| for 0<=n<N and |beta_j|<=2(1+|P|). Their entire corridor pairing therefore costs only another factor 2N(1+|P|) times the proved alias error. The exact normal forcing and the vertical color sides in (4) are both retained. This does not estimate physical colors h>H. It does not discard the central k strip, establish a nonzero filled critical pairing, or identify its action with a preferred topological longitude. A fixed-large-filling proof still requires those three steps, including the peripheral sign convention. The present source-conditioned estimate is not an all-input operator norm bound for a free exterior. ## 4. The combined source is a total derivative, with exact paired charges There is a useful exact representation for the remaining coherent packet, avoiding the separate interpolation of any a_n. For ANY physical even core in (7), set \[ \mathcal F_N(z)=\sum_{h=-H}^Hc_h e^{2\pi i h z},\qquad U_N(z)=e^{2\pi iPNz^2}\sinh(2\pi i z)\mathcal F_N(z), \qquad z_k=(k+1/2)/N-1/2. \tag{9} \] The literal entire-normal filling kernel (6) gives EXACTLY \[ \boxed{\sum_{h=0}^H\beta_{N-h-1}c_h =\frac{(-1)^{N-1}\kappa^{-P}}{2\pi iN^2} \sum_{k=0}^{N-1}U_N'(z_k).} \tag{10} \] Indeed differentiating U multiplies its sinh term by 2pi i(2PNz+h) and differentiating sinh supplies 2pi i cosh. These are precisely BOTH linear normal contributions in (6). This holds with operator-valued c_h in their unchanged exterior order. In particular U_N(1/2)=U_N(-1/2)=0, and U_N'(1/2)=U_N'(-1/2) =-2pi i exp(pi iPN/2)sum_h(-1)^h c_h. The periodic extension of U_N' is continuous, with piecewise smooth derivative. Its Fourier series is absolutely convergent (two integrations by parts bound its nonzero coefficients by a constant times frequency^(-2)). Exact midpoint Fourier selection and one integration by parts therefore prove \[ \boxed{\sum_{h=0}^H\beta_{N-h-1}c_h =(-1)^{N-1}\kappa^{-P} \sum_{m\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}} (-1)^{m(N-1)}m\int_{-1/2}^{1/2} e^{2\pi iN(Pz^2-mz)}\sinh(2\pi i z) \mathcal F_N(z)\,dz.} \tag{11} \] The series is absolutely convergent for each N. Its constants can depend on the actual source; no uniform asymptotic tail estimate is silently inferred. The zero charge vanishes EXACTLY from the two original endpoint zeros of U_N, not by discarding a Fresnel current. Because the core is even, mathcalF_N is even and U_N is odd. The integrals at -m and m are opposites, so their weighted contributions in (11) are equal. Thus the +/-m channels ADD exactly, at every parity and level, before any saddle approximation. For the source obeying (1)--(2), mathcalF_N and its fixed derivatives are exponentially small on any fixed real strip eta_0<=|z|<=1/2, by (3). Equations (10)--(11) therefore provide a source-faithful central phase problem with exact normal charge m. The finite-k endpoint bound (8) is already quantitative. Passing between a restricted central integral and (11) must still retain the new side currents at its artificial cutoff; absolute convergence at fixed N alone is not a uniform exponential bound on all charges. The uniform infinite-tail bound is proved separately below; a central-saddle conclusion is not inferred from fixed-N convergence. ## 5. A uniform exponential high-charge tail, with its paired current Under (1)--(2), the large-|m| part of (11) is exponentially smaller than exp(NF). This is a UNIFORM estimate; absolute convergence at each fixed N alone would not suffice. For fixed integer P there are M_P>0 and finite B_P,C_P, independent of N, such that \[ \boxed{\sum_{|m|>M_P} \left\|m\int_{-1/2}^{1/2}U_N(z)e^{-2\pi imNz}\,dz\right\| \le C_P N^{B_P}e^{N(F-g_*)}.} \tag{12} \] The positive gap g_* and the contour width below depend ONLY on the source hypotheses, not on P. This matters for independently large fillings with no comparability between their lengths. First, (3), for a small real neighborhood of +/-1/2 in z, extends to a FIXED small complex strip. In its exact rectangle proof, an extra Im z=v in the Fourier variable costs at most exp(2pi delta |v|N) on the physical source support. The same argument applies to fixed derivatives of mathcalF_N, by taking r larger in (3). Thus for some fixed sigma_1,g_1>0, ||mathcalF_N^(j)(+/-1/2+iv)|| <=poly(N)exp[N(F-g_1)], |v|<=sigma_1, j=0,1,2. Fix a smaller sigma>0 using ONLY this source strip. On either endpoint line, at height -v, the chirp costs at most exp(2pi|P|Nv), and its first two derivatives cost powers of N and P. Keep that v-dependent cost; do not bound it by exp(2pi|P|sigma N) and then shrink sigma as the filling length grows. For m>0 shift its Fourier integral DOWN by sigma. On the lower horizontal side the elementary physical-grid estimate ||mathcalF_N(x-i sigma)|| <=poly(N)exp[N(F+2pi delta sigma)] gives an upper bound poly(N)exp{N[F-2pi sigma(m-|P|-delta)]}. (13) Crucially the two vertical currents must be paired. Their common Fourier endpoint phase is (-1)^(mN), and their difference is V_N(v)=U_N(1/2-iv)-U_N(-1/2-iv), 0<=v<=sigma. The original integer Fourier polynomial mathcalF_N is periodic. Together with the sinh zeros this gives V_N(0)=V_N'(0)=0 exactly, as already checked before (11). The source derivative bound on the two vertical strips, with the chirp cost explicitly retained, gives ||V_N(v)||<=poly(N,P)v^2 exp[N(F-g_1)+2pi|P|Nv]. Consequently the paired vertical contribution obeys \[ \left\|m\int_0^\sigma e^{-2\pi mNv}V_N(v)\,dv\right\| \le\frac{\operatorname{poly}(N,P)m}{(m-|P|)^3N^3} e^{N(F-g_1)},\quad m>|P|. \tag{14} \] For m>M_P>=2|P|+2delta+2 this is at most a fixed multiple of poly(N,P)m^(-2)N^(-3)exp[N(F-g_1)], which is summable. The horizontal bounds (13) have an exponentially convergent geometric sum with gap at least 2pi sigma, independent of P. Take g_*=min(g_1,2pi sigma)>0. The upper shift for negative m is identical; for an even core it also follows from the exact +/-m identity. This proves (12). Neither individual vertical current is set to zero. Here is the precise multiport justification. Leave all remaining z_j variables REAL until their tails have been removed. On the entire source U=exp(2pi iN sum P_i z_i^2) product_i sinh(2pi i z_i) mathcalF_N(z), define the commuting COLOR-register functionals D_i U=(2pi iN^2)^(-1)sum_k partial_i U(z_(i,k)), I_(i,m)U=(-1)^(m(N-1))m integral_[-1/2,1/2] U dz_i, D_i^lo=sum_(0<|m|<=M_i) I_(i,m), D_i^tail=D_i-D_i^lo. Midpoint Poisson and the matched endpoint values prove D_i=sum_m I_(i,m) exactly. These operations act linearly on scalar color registers; they do NOT commute or reorder physical Hopf boxes or matrix-valued exterior coefficients. Exact telescoping gives \[ \prod_iD_i-\prod_iD_i^{\mathrm{lo}} =\sum_i\left(\prod_{j<i}D_j^{\mathrm{lo}}\right) D_i^{\mathrm{tail}}\left(\prod_{j>i}D_j\right). \tag{14a} \] For fixed M_j, the real-integral functional D_j^lo has supremum norm at most sum_(0<|m|<=M_j)|m|=M_j(M_j+1). The original D_j uses N samples and one derivative. Its mixed derivatives on U cost powers of N and P_j: all remaining chirps have modulus ONE at real z_j, while differentiating them supplies only P_j N. Differentiating mathcalF_N supplies integer powers of h_j, bounded by powers of N. The endpoint Fourier bound and (14) are uniform in these remaining real spectators AND in every mixed derivative just described. To see this directly, sum the other physical h_j in absolute value using the original source bound exp[N(F_0-a sum x_j^2+C sum y_j^2)]. Their sums and fixed powers of h_j cost only powers of N; no positive exponential is introduced. The contour shift and paired vertical current occur ONLY in the tail coordinate i. Thus each term of (14a) is bounded by poly_(s,p)(N)exp[N(F_0-g_*)], with g_* fixed by the source and independent of the largest slope. There is no uncontrolled infinite charge sum in a spectator coordinate. Later central saddle-contour motions are made only AFTER (14a) has removed the tails. Equations (8),(11),(12) leave a FINITE set of nonzero coherent central charges for every fixed collection of integer fillings. Their source Fourier saddle is made explicit next. Comparing the remaining charge actions and bounding colors outside the chosen corridor are separate tasks. ## 6. A nonzero central Fourier packet from the EXACT analytic source This step uses the stronger, proved input from the exact color packet: on a fixed complex polydisk, with r color ports, C_N(pi x)=N^(3/2)e^(-i s pi d/4) A(pi x) exp[N phi(x)](1+O(1/N)), phi(x)=Phi_s(pi x), phi(0)=F_0, phi''(0)=2pi i tau_s I, tau_s=(1+exp(2iu_s))/2, Im tau_s>0. (15) The exact function C_N, not just this leading expression, has the complex Gaussian bound (1) in all continued coordinates. The case needed for filling all boxes is r=s. Define the ENTIRE finite packet mathcalF_N(z)=sum_(|h_i|<=H) C_N(pi h/N) exp(2pi i h dot z). (16) It is exactly even in every z_i. For a fixed sufficiently small complex z-polydisk, the holomorphic implicit-function theorem defines grad phi(xi(z))+2pi i z=0, Psi(z)=phi(xi(z))+2pi i xi(z) dot z. Then, UNIFORMLY on a smaller fixed complex polydisk, \[ \boxed{\mathcal F_N(z)=N^{(r+3)/2}e^{-i s\pi d/4} B(z)e^{N\Psi(z)}(1+O(1/N)),\quad B(z)=\frac{(2\pi)^{r/2}A(\pi\xi(z))} {\sqrt{\det[-\phi''(\xi(z))]}}.} \tag{17} \] The Gaussian square root is fixed at zero by the positive real part of -phi''(0). In particular B(0)=A(0)(-i tau_s)^(-r/2) !=0, xi(z)=-z/tau_s+O(||z||^3), Psi(z)=F_0-i pi sum_i z_i^2/tau_s+O(||z||^4). (18) Both Psi and B are even in each z_i and B is nonzero on a smaller polydisk. All phases in (15) remain in (17). Here is the finite-source proof of (17). Apply exact half-integer cotangent rectangles in the h coordinates to (16). The two constant cotangent parts give the ordinary integral with density N^r. The nonconstant parts cost exp(-2pi sigma N) on its horizontal sides; the extra factor exp(2pi iN x dot z), the quadratic complex-source growth and the small complex z displacement cost strictly less after choosing sigma first and then the z-polydisk. The vertical h sides keep their strict endpoint gap from (1). This proves mathcalF_N(z)=N^r integral_[-d_N,d_N]^r C_N(pi x)exp(2pi iN x dot z)dx +poly(N)exp[N(F_0-g)], g>0. (19) Slightly changing the half-integer endpoints of the integral is exponentially harmless, and all corresponding side currents are in the displayed error. This is a statement about the EXACT holomorphic source; a pointwise real-grid O(1/N) error would not imply (19). Deform the ordinary integral locally to the parallel real contour through xi(z). Its end connectors retain their strict gap for small z. The real part of phi'' remains negative definite, uniformly near zero. The elementary multivariate Gaussian integral and the uniform analytic amplitude in (15) therefore give (17); its exponentially small cotangent remainder stays below the saddle after shrinking the z-polydisk. This also proves the required uniformity BEFORE any later z-contour motion. No original-cycle coefficient has been assigned. For completeness, apply (11) successively in all r filled ports. The actual R powers restore their phases as explained above. The exact corridor source is \[ (-1)^{r(N-1)}\kappa^{\sum_iP_i} \sum_{m_i\ne0}(-1)^{(N-1)\sum_i m_i}\prod_i m_i \int_{[-1/2,1/2]^r} e^{2\pi iN\sum_i(P_i z_i^2-m_i z_i)} \prod_i\sinh(2\pi i z_i)\mathcal F_N(z)\,dz. \tag{20} \] All original normal charges and the full original source are kept. Every coordinate reflection (m_i,z_i)->(-m_i,-z_i) preserves its term, so the 2^r all-unit charges have exactly equal contributions, including the even-level signs. There is no charge with m_i=0. The large-charge remainder is controlled by (12) before any Gaussian approximation; the real endpoint-frequency strips are controlled by (8). Equations (17),(20) therefore give an actual nonzero analytic source amplitude for the remaining finite central phase problem Psi(z)+2pi i sum_i(P_i z_i^2-m_i z_i). (21) The comparison of its finite charges, its legitimate local saddle contours, and the physical color complement are not replaced by formal stationarity. In particular (20) alone is not a theorem for an entire filled knot. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_filling_source_fourier_endpoint_gap.py) checks the exact finite-k normal-weighted decomposition, its retained half-color source and endpoint split, the contour equality (4), and the quantitative estimates on explicitly controlled analytic packets, and the combined-source total derivative and exact paired-charge Fourier selection in (10)--(11). The actual mixed-source hypotheses are proved in the linked source notes; finite tests alone do not establish them.

title: Quantitative loss on a fixed boundary face of the complete angle flow
text: # Quantitative loss on a fixed boundary face of the complete angle flow 31 October 2026. analytical lemma. This concerns the original complete triangle capacity and its actual shared face equations. It does not turn the weighted LEFT envelope into a coefficientwise comparison. ## 1. Strong concavity with the source normalization For every actual triangle corner use the normalized load \(a=\theta/(2\pi)\in[0,1/2]\), with each triangle row summing to \(1/2\). Protected-face corners are zero, and every ordinary face has total load one. Let \(\mathcal P\) be this compact feasible polytope, retaining all actual corner incidences. Its complete source entropy is \[ E(a)=\sum_{t,f}f(a_{tf}),\qquad f(s)=\frac{\Lambda(\pi s)+\Lambda(\pi/2-\pi s)}{\pi}. \] This is the normalization in the [triangle Legendre identity](../papers/planar-certificates/README.md). For \(0<s<1/2\), direct differentiation gives \[ f''(s)=-\frac{2\pi}{\sin(2\pi s)}\leq-2\pi. \] Consequently \(f(s)+\pi s^2\) is concave, including both endpoints by continuity. Summing this fact proves, for \(a,b\in\mathcal P\) and \(0\leq t\leq1\), \[ E((1-t)a+tb)\geq(1-t)E(a)+tE(b) +\pi t(1-t)\lVert a-b\rVert_2^2. \tag{1} \] Let \(a^*\) maximize \(E\) on \(\mathcal P\), and set \(\Phi=E(a^*)\). In the actual geometric case, \(\Phi=\operatorname{Vol}(Y_D)/(2\pi)\). Since the left side of (1), with \(a=a^*\), is at most \(\Phi\), dividing by \(t>0\) and letting \(t\downarrow0\) gives \[ \boxed{\quad E(b)\leq\Phi-\pi\lVert b-a^*\rVert_2^2.\quad} \tag{2} \] No derivative at a forced zero or at a singleton row is used. In particular the maximizing assignment is unique even on a proper supported face. ## 2. Fixing selected triangles to their corner vertices Choose a set \(J\) of distinct original triangles and an allowed ordinary corner \(c(t)\) in each. Impose the additional constraints \[ a_t=v_t:=\tfrac12 e_{c(t)},\qquad t\in J. \] Write \(\mathcal P_J\) for the resulting face of \(\mathcal P\). If it is nonempty, (2) proves the explicit bound \[ \max_{\mathcal P_J}E \leq\Phi-\pi\sum_{t\in J}\lVert v_t-a_t^*\rVert_2^2. \tag{3} \] If it is empty, its entropy maximum is \(-\infty\). The loss in (3) is strict as soon as one chosen row was not already that singleton row at the complete solution. Distinct rows make the displayed squared losses additive; their shared face constraints remain in force. There is an exact shared-radius dual formulation. Write \(h_f=\log l_f\) for ordinary faces and retain protected zeros by deleting their allowed corners. With the same half-degree triangle function \(Q\), put \[ B_J(h)=\sum_{t\notin J}Q((e^{h_f})_{f\in t}) +\tfrac12\sum_{t\in J}h_{c(t)}-\sum_f h_f. \tag{4} \] Then \[ \inf_{h\in\mathbb R^{F_{\mathrm{ord}}}} B_J(h) =\max_{\mathcal P_J}E. \tag{5} \] Here the right side has value \(-\infty\) when infeasible; positive minimizing radii need not exist. To verify (5), take the product of all remaining compact triangle simplexes and the selected singleton rows, let \(A\) be its original face-incidence map, and define \(H(d)=\max_{Aa=d}E(a)\). Its hypograph is closed and convex, because the domain is compact and \(E\) is continuous and concave. Weak duality follows directly from the local Legendre formula. Strict separation of \((\mathbf1,H(\mathbf1)+\varepsilon)\) from that hypograph gives an affine majorant of height at most \(H(\mathbf1)+\varepsilon\) at \(\mathbf1\). The separating coefficient of the vertical coordinate is positive: it is nonnegative by downward closure, and if it were zero the feasible point with the same face coordinate would contradict strict separation. Normalizing that coefficient to one produces (4). Let \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\). When \(\mathbf1\) is outside the compact incidence image, separation in face coordinates and scaling the separator sends (4) to \(-\infty\). ## 3. What this resolves in the one-sided envelope For a LEFT port \((x,b,c,y)\), its term \[ Q(x,b,y)+\tfrac12\log c \] is exactly (4)'s local expression when the original \((x,c,y)\) triangle is fixed to its \(c\)-corner vertex. At the actual complete packing with \(c>0\) and \(x+y>0\), this triangle has at least two positive weights, so its maximizing row is not that vertex. Thus (3) gives a strict, explicit capacity loss for any fixed nonempty collection of these triangle restrictions, with the original common face constraints. The reflected statement applies to RIGHT ports. This proves a statement about the specified comparison capacities. It does not bound the full LEFT polynomial by that one comparison: the [proved weighted envelope](actual_global_left_weighted_spectral_envelope.md) also has the branch \(\log c\). A pointwise maximum of the two branches does not permit each branch to choose its own Cauchy radii before the original coefficient is extracted. An additional finite comparison, or a bound for their convex mixtures with the same face constraints, is still necessary for a general full-invariant theorem. ## Validation The proof is analytic: scalar differentiation, strong concavity on the closed simplex, and finite convex separation. No finite-width experiment is used to infer (2), (3), or (5). No comparison with the complete one-sided envelope is supplied.

title: The saturated four-port factorial action is a hyperideal tetrahedron volume
text: # The saturated four-port factorial action is a hyperideal tetrahedron volume 29 October 2026. The positive FACE-NORMALIZED Racah partition has an explicit local geometric action. Six folded Casimir labels determine the six dihedral angles of a truncated hyperideal tetrahedron; the four supported face sums are precisely its four vertex-angle conditions. The optimized action equals its actual hyperbolic volume divided by pi. This is proved here from a Lorentz Gram construction, finite rational identities and a direct first-variation calculation. No asymptotic 6j volume theorem is an input. The face normalization is essential. This note does not identify an arbitrary physical recoupling energy with that normalization, discard high partners/normals, or infer a global knot triangulation from one local tetrahedron. The actual four-port source kernel and its weighting must be matched separately. ## 1. The exact local angle dictionary and positive scalar action Order the six colors as (a,b,c,d,e,f). The four vertex triples and three opposite quadrilateral sums are F=(a+b+e, c+d+e, a+d+f, b+c+f), Q=(a+b+c+d, a+c+e+f, b+d+e+f). (1) For the geometric theorem first take real scaled colors in 0<a,b,c,d,e,f<1/2, every F_i>1. (2) Put alpha_a=pi-2pi a, and similarly for the other five. These angles are in (0,pi), and at each of the four indicated vertices sum_incident alpha=3pi-2pi F_i<pi. (3) Thus each vertex will be hyperideal, with a geodesic polar truncation triangle of area pi-sum alpha=2pi(F_i-1). All triangle deficits F_i-2(color in that face) are strictly between 0 and 1. The source-compatible quantum scaling is EXACTLY a=(j_a+1/2)/N, alpha_a=pi-(2j_a+1)pi/N, c_(j_a)=q^(2j_a+1)+q^(-2j_a-1)=-2cos alpha_a. (4) If the six folded integer labels are <=floor((N-1)/2) and every face sum is >=N-1, then (3) is at most pi-pi/N. Its truncation triangle area is (2pi/N)(faceSum-(N-1)+1/2). The only zero edge angles are the odd simple Steinberg labels. They are treated by continuous limiting geometry, not as strictly positive interior tetrahedral angles. These are internal Casimir angle coordinates; (4) is not an auxiliary-meridian identification. Let L(t)=integral_0^t log|2sin pi u|du, with period 1. On the interval max F_i<Z<min Q_k define A(Z)=L(Z-1)-sum_(i=1)^4 L(Z-F_i) -sum_(k=1)^3 L(Q_k-Z), M=(1/2)sum_faces [sum_(edges in face)L(F_i-2edge)-L(F_i-1)], Psi=max_Z A(Z)+M. (5) The interval is nonempty: every Q_k-F_i is a positive triangle deficit from one of the other faces. It lies in (1,2). For reference the finite positive scalar producing (5) is R_N=N sum_(max faceSum<=z<=min quadSum) s_(z-(N-1)) / {product_faces s_(z-faceSum) product_quads s_(quadSum-z)}, D_face=product_(edges in face)s_(faceSum-2edge) /[N s_(faceSum-(N-1))], W_N=R_N sqrt(product_faces D_face). (6) All factors in (6) are positive. It is the root of the explicitly normalized squared generic factorial expression, not the bare Racah sum. The phase-coherent root sum follows because its numerator has exactly one [N] zero and its seven denominator indices are <N. The finite phase/metric statements are proved in [the supported Racah theorem](actual_supported_racah_common_phase_and_normal_metric.md). For the shifted scaled variables (4), use Z=(z+7/4)/N: Z-F_i=(z-faceSum+1/4)/N, Q_k-Z=(quadSum-z+1/4)/N. Uniform all-index factorial estimates then give (5) as the limiting logarithmic action, with O(log N) endpoint errors. The geometric identification of this action is independent of a proposed source normalization. At six colors 1/3 the bare optimized A is 3v3/pi, whereas Psi=v3/pi; omitting M would already give the wrong volume. In these conventions log W_N/N has action Psi; the SQUARED weight W_N^2 has action 2Psi. That factor must be retained in a later energy or doubled-source comparison. ## 2. An own existence/uniqueness construction of the tetrahedron Number the vertices by the four triples in (1). The edge endpoints are a:13, b:14, c:24, d:23, e:12, f:34. Let n_i be its four outward face normals, face i opposite vertex i. Their prescribed Lorentz Gram matrix is G_ii=1, G_12=-cos alpha_f, G_13=-cos alpha_c, G_14=-cos alpha_d, G_23=-cos alpha_b, G_24=-cos alpha_a, G_34=-cos alpha_e. (7) We prove that G has signature (3,1), rather than assuming an angle realization theorem. Every three-by-three principal minor corresponds to three angles A,B,C at a vertex, A+B+C<pi. Its determinant is -4 cos((A+B+C)/2)cos((A+B-C)/2) cos((A-B+C)/2)cos((-A+B+C)/2)<0. (8) Its two-by-two minors are sin^2(alpha)>0, so that block has signature (2,1) and can be realized in Lorentz three-space. Its inverse has all entries negative: its off-diagonal cofactors have numerator cos C+cos A cos B>sin A sin B>0 and its determinant is negative. If the three inner products of the fourth normal with this block are nonpositive, its projection to the block has nonpositive square. Adding a new spacelike coordinate makes its square one, with a nonzero fourth component. This constructs G with signature (3,1). Otherwise choose a nonacute dihedral A>=pi/2 among these products and call its two normals n_0,n_1. At most two dihedrals can be nonacute, and two such edges must be opposite, because any two meeting at a vertex have sum <pi. The other products of n_0 are -cos B,-cos C, and those of n_1 are -cos D,-cos E. The three old normals have last mutual angle F, with D+E+F<pi. The vertex conditions imply B+D<pi-A, C+E<pi-A. In n_1-perpendicular Lorentz space define m_2=(n_2+cos D n_1)/sin D, m_3=(n_3+cos E n_1)/sin E, <m_2,m_3>=-(cos F+cos D cos E)/(sin D sin E)<-1. Write n_0=(-cos A)n_1+sin A u. The two required products of u with m_2,m_3 are both <-1: for example <u,m_2>=(-cos B-cos A cos D)/(sin A sin D)<-1. The inverse Gram matrix of m_2,m_3 has every entry negative. Thus their prescribed negative-product projection of u has negative square. An additional spacelike coordinate again makes u^2=1 and constructs the fourth normal independently. This proves det G<0 throughout (2), including the possible two opposite obtuse edges. Let C=adj(G). Its diagonal entries are negative by (8), so the dual vectors v_i=-sum_j(G^-1)_ij n_j have positive squares. Their off-diagonal products are strictly negative. Indeed Jacobi's minor identity gives (G^-1)_ii(G^-1)_jj-(G^-1)_ij^2 =sin^2(alpha_complement)/det G<0. No off-diagonal inverse entry can therefore vanish. The angle domain is convex and connected, and at a small regular angle all those entries are negative; continuity fixes their sign everywhere. Normalize the v_i to square one. Every pair has product <-1, so their projective edge crosses the Klein ball. Their sum is timelike, and has negative product with every v_i. It supplies an interior point of the four face halfspaces AND the four vertex-polar halfspaces. Cutting the six projective edges by those polar planes gives twelve finite hyperbolic vertices. Each lies strictly on the proper side of the other two polar planes, by the negative products. The result is a compact convex truncated tetrahedron, with four triangular polar faces and four right-angled hexagonal original faces. Its six original dihedrals are (7); every new truncation edge is right-angled. There are no assumed end or completeness conditions in this compact local construction. Its ordered face-normal Gram fixes it up to isometry. For an explicit compactness check, suppose a remaining point were ideal and write it in the vertex cone as x=sum_i t_i v_i, t_i>=0. The polar inequalities <x,v_i><=0 and x^2=0 force <x,v_i>=0 on every active coefficient. This would put the nonzero active vector t in the kernel of its principal vertex Gram block. All such blocks are nonsingular: their determinants are complementary principal minors of G divided by det G (size one and two were checked above; size three uses G_ii=1). Thus no ideal point remains after truncation. The length along original edge a, between its polar truncations, is ell_a=arccosh[ C_13/sqrt(C_11 C_33) ]>0. (9) The cofactor in (9) is positive since det G<0 and (G^-1)_13<0. The formula follows by restricting to the Lorentz plane spanned by its two normalized hyperideal endpoints. Other edges are obtained by vertex relabeling. ## 3. The optimized derivative is EXACTLY that truncated edge length Here is a finite rational certificate for the derivative, with all branches fixed by the positive interval. Set u_a=exp(2pi i a), etc., P=product_edges u. Let U_i be the four products of u on the faces in (1), and V_k the three products on the quads. Then product U_i=product V_k=P^2. Write n=exp(2pi i Z). The stationarity equation A'(Z)=0 is exactly (n-1)product_k(n-V_k)-product_i(n-U_i) =n(A2 n^2+A1 n+A0)=0, A2=sum U_i-1-sum V_k, A1=sum_(k<l)V_kV_l+sum V_k-sum_(i<j)U_iU_j, A0=sum_(i<j<l)U_iU_jU_l-P^2-sum_(k<l)V_kV_l. (10) Expansion gives the independent identity A1^2-4A2A0=16P^2 det G. (11) In (11), G has off-diagonals cos(2pi color), which is exactly (7). Also A0=P^2 conjugate(A2) and A1/P is real. Thus the two roots of (10) are distinct and on the unit circle. A2 cannot vanish, since that would make (11)/P^2 a nonnegative real square instead of 16det G<0. The function A' tends to +infinity at the lower positive interval endpoint and to -infinity at the upper one. It is continuous inside, and (10) permits at most two simple critical points there. The number is odd, so there is EXACTLY one, Z_*. It is a strict global maximum, with nonzero negative second derivative. This also fixes a smooth selected branch on the entire connected domain (2). For edge a let B(n)=u_c (n-U_1)(n-U_3)/[(n-V_1)(n-V_2)], R_a= sin pi(a+e-b)sin pi(a+b-e) /[sin pi(b+e-a)sin pi(F_1-1)] *sin pi(a+f-d)sin pi(a+d-f) /[sin pi(d+f-a)sin pi(F_3-1)]. All displayed sines in R_a are positive. Differentiating (5) at its selected stationary Z_* gives E_a:=exp(partial_a Psi)=B(n_*)sqrt(R_a)>0. (12) To verify (12), the bare derivative is the ratio of the two sin(Z-F) factors to the two sin(Q-Z) factors incident to a. Their canceled phase is u_c. The four face derivatives give R_a. Let n_+,n_- be the two roots of (10). Direct rational products give B(n_+)B(n_-)=1/R_a, B(n_+)+B(n_-)=C_13/(2K_a), K_a=sin pi(a+e-b)sin pi(a+b-e) sin pi(a+f-d)sin pi(a+d-f), sqrt(C_11 C_33) sqrt(R_a)=4K_a. (13) These are uniform algebraic identities, not tests at selected colors. For an explicit cleared-polynomial verification, put A=-A1-A2(U_1+U_3), B=A2 U_1U_3-A0, C=-A1-A2(V_1+V_2), D=A2 V_1V_2-A0, Den=C^2 A0-CD A1+D^2 A2. The sum/product of the two B(n) are respectively u_c[2AC A0-(AD+BC)A1+2BD A2]/Den, u_c^2[A^2 A0-AB A1+B^2 A2]/Den. With edge variables written a,...,f temporarily for u_a,...,u_f, the claimed product is (be-a)(abe-1)(df-a)(adf-1) /[(ae-b)(ab-e)(af-d)(ad-f)], and the claimed sum is 8a^2bdef C_13 /[(ae-b)(ab-e)(af-d)(ad-f)]. Substitute (10), multiply these explicit denominators, and expand: both polynomial differences are identically zero in six independent variables. The final identity in (13) is the elementary three-face Gram determinant (8), with its sine factors. The accompanying audit performs these symbolic zero checks; no interpolation is involved. Consequently the two possible E_a values are reciprocal and have sum 2C_13/sqrt(C_11C_33). They are exp(+ell_a), exp(-ell_a). Near the regular ideal limit all colors approach 1/3 from above; the metric factor in (12) diverges while its bare ratio remains finite and positive. Thus the selected E_a is the positive-length branch there. It cannot change branch on (2), since ell_a never vanishes. By connectedness and tetrahedral relabeling, partial_edge Psi=ell_edge for all six edges. (14) ## 4. An elementary volume-variation proof and its constant For completeness the needed first variation can be derived directly. On the hyperboloid the coordinate vector restricted to a totally geodesic face satisfies Delta_face x=2x. It follows by differentiating the usual cosh/sinh coordinates on H^2. A face with moving outward unit normal n has normal speed -<dot n,x>. The divergence theorem within that face therefore gives dot V=-(1/2)sum_faces sum_edges integral_edge <dot n,nu_edge> ds. For an edge between face normals n_i,n_j and angle alpha, the outward conormal within face i is (n_j+cos alpha n_i)/sin alpha. Adding its two face contributions uses d<n_i,n_j>=sin alpha d alpha, and gives dV=-(1/2)sum_edges ell_edge d alpha_edge. (15) The new truncation edges have fixed angle pi/2, hence contribute zero. Using alpha=pi-2pi color, (15) becomes dV=pi sum ell_edge d(color). Equations (14),(15) show that V-pi Psi is constant on the connected domain (2). Calibrate at the regular ideal boundary a=...=f=1/3. Then F_i=1, Q_k=4/3, Z_*=7/6, and A(Z_*)=-6L(1/6)=3v3/pi, M=6L(1/3)=-2v3/pi, Psi=v3/pi. (16) The Lobachevsky duplication identity gives Lambda(pi/6)=(3/2)Lambda(pi/3), so (16) has no numerical calibration. The Gram construction converges to the regular ideal tetrahedron, whose volume is v3=3Lambda(pi/3). One can justify volume convergence here without a realization or rigidity theorem. For the regular family take fixed Euclidean regular tetrahedral unit vectors t_i with mutual products -1/3 and use n_i=(T,S t_i), T^2=(3cos alpha-1)/4, S^2=1+T^2. At alpha=pi/3 their Klein faces have distance 1/3 from the center, giving the four ideal vertices -t_i. The finite polar truncation vertices converge to those same vertices. Here are exact uniform end inequalities. Set c=cos alpha, t=T/S and rho=3t=sqrt((9c-3)/(c+1))>1. The projective hyperideal vertex at -t_i is rho(-t_i). In a fixed upper-half-space frame sending w=-t_i to infinity, its polar cut is |z|^2+y^2<=(rho+1)/(rho-1). For every incident j!=i, t_j dot w=1/3. Its original face inequality therefore gives exactly 2(t_j)_perp dot z <=(t+1/3)+(t-1/3)(|z|^2+y^2) <=2(rho+1)/3. The three fixed perpendicular normals surround the origin at angles 120 degrees. Hence |z|<=C uniformly as rho decreases to 1. The cross-sectional area is bounded, and its volume above y=Y is <=C/Y^2. Do this in the four disjoint ideal-end frames; the remaining compact regions converge. This proves volume convergence to the ideal tetrahedron and fixes the constant in (15), with no O(epsilon) end estimate left as an assumption. We have therefore proved the LOCAL GEOMETRIC IDENTITY pi Psi(a,b,c,d,e,f)=Vol(truncated hyperideal tetrahedron). (17) Both sides extend continuously to the closed angle chamber. For Psi this follows directly from continuity of L and maximization on a continuously varying compact interval. The corresponding geometric extension is the limit from the interior; no assertion that every boundary point retains a nondegenerate truncated-tetrahedron cell is needed. In particular at six colors 1/2, Z_*=7/4 and Psi=v8/pi; the six original edge lengths tend to zero at the escaping ideal corners. The limiting cell is the regular ideal octahedron, not a tetrahedron with positive edges. One can check its geometry directly: G=2I-J and its four normalized polar normals are m_i=-n_i+(1/2)sum_j n_j. Then distinct n_i,n_j and distinct m_i,m_j have product -1, while <n_i,m_j> is -2 for i=j and zero otherwise. These are exactly the eight regular-octahedron face normals (1,sigma_1,sigma_2,sigma_3)/sqrt(2), partitioned by the product of the three signs. Thus the octahedral constant is attached to an explicit geometric cell, not only a limiting dilogarithm number. ## 5. Exact stationarity data, and what a global source still needs The local action supplies more than a constant fit. The colors give the actual face-normal Gram (7), its polar triangle areas are (3), and the optimized derivatives are the six metric edge lengths (14). For a specified gluing of such cells, (15) gives its first variation on EVERY allowed dihedral-angle tangent, not merely on a chosen one-parameter source family. In particular variations exchanging two angles around one fixed total-angle edge force equality of their corresponding truncated lengths. More generally a linear constraint matrix C gives the exact stationarity condition length vector in image(C^T). (18) If the ONLY angle constraints are sums around actual common edges, (18) forces one common length per glued edge. Three such matched alternating lengths determine a right-angled hexagon by elementary hyperbolic cosine laws, so the prescribed original hexagonal faces then match isometrically. Actual angle sums, link degree/winding, boundary markings and end completeness must still be checked. Additional source constraints can reduce the tangent space, and then stationarity in that smaller space does not imply this full metric gluing. No global strict-concavity or complete-manifold maximum theorem is asserted solely from the local derivative identity. There is a concrete obstruction to using just the four support inequalities as a complete volume-maximization certificate. Equation (14) gives partial_edge Psi>0 at every strict point. Increasing any color preserves those four inequalities. Along the line toward six colors 1/2, Psi therefore increases to v8/pi. By continuity that is the maximum over the CLOSED support chamber, and there is NO interior stationary point under only these inequalities. A geometric interior critical point for a larger graph needs the actual additional edge constraints, boundary potentials or their full source counterparts; the local face supports alone do not supply them. The [generic actual four-port theorem](actual_general_four_port_single_racah_kernel.md) now gives an explicit separable row/column gauge relating its literal inverse kernel L_(G,E) to the seven-factorial sum S. Its four Delta face factors give exactly the normalization in (6) after root-zero removal. Thus this finite scalar/generic normalization is explicit; it is not being taken from a named 6j evaluation. But identifying the resulting weight with a useful FULL marked-source Cauchy energy still requires controlled gauge transport, complete colliding partners and root normals, and the graph's actual port/edge incidence in (18). No individual partner value or semisimple normalization may replace that comparison. The bare Racah term is already wrong at the regular ideal tetrahedron by the factor in (16). ## 6. Uniform local quantum-volume theorem, including moving boundary colors The geometry identity has the following UNIFORM finite-level consequence. There is an absolute constant C such that, for EVERY N and every six folded integer labels satisfying all four face sums >=N-1, the positive normalized scalar W_N in (6) obeys |log W_N-(N/pi)Vol_ext(T(a_N))|<=C log(N+1), a_(N,edge)=(j_edge+1/2)/N. (19) The domain is empty at any level with no supported sextuple. The symbol Vol_ext is the continuous geometric extension of (17); at strict angles it is the ordinary compact truncated-tetrahedron volume, while zero-angle boundary cells are interpreted by their geometric limits. Constants in (19) do not depend on a distance from any face, edge, corner or the octahedral endpoint. Both level parities and composite N are included. Here is the full uniform estimate. Write F_i^int,Q_k^int for the integer forms (1), z_-=max F_i^int and z_+=min Q_k^int. All true factorial indices are in [0,N-1]. The elementary uniform estimate log s_n=N L(n/N)+O(log(N+1)), 0<=n<=N-1, has an absolute constant. Applying it to the fixed eight factorials in each positive R_N term changes its logarithm by O(log N). At its actual point Z_z=(z+7/4)/N, the action arguments differ from those true indices divided by N by exactly numerator: 3/(4N), each of seven denominators: 1/(4N). For a face metric the three deficits and its excess differ by exactly 1/(2N). The shifted and original arguments are all in [0,1]. The uniform modulus |L(t+epsilon)-L(t)| <=C0 |epsilon|(1+|log|epsilon||) therefore changes N times these actions by O(log N), including when an original factorial index is zero. The explicit N factors in R_N and D_face add only O(log N). The geometric maximization interval is I=[(z_-+3/2)/N,(z_++2)/N], whereas the true grid runs from (z_-+7/4)/N to (z_++7/4)/N in steps 1/N. Its first and last points are inset by exactly 1/(4N) from the two respective endpoints. Every point of I is within 1/N of a true grid point, even when z_-=z_+. The same modulus of L, now for its eight action terms, shows that the continuous maximum and the true-grid maximum differ by O(log N/N), uniformly. There are at most N positive terms: z_+-z_-<=N-1 by the complementary triangle-deficit bounds. The largest term bounds their sum from below, and N times it bounds the sum from above. Thus log W_N=N Psi(a_N)+O(log N) with one universal error constant. Equation (17) proves (19). No nonzero Hessian, separation from a boundary, selected complex cycle or asymptotic interpolation of an unobserved normal was used in this argument. In particular ANY convergent supported color sequence a_N->a in the closed chamber satisfies lim (pi/N)log W_N=Vol_ext(T(a)). (20) This is a genuine broad LOCAL quantum-volume theorem for the explicitly gauged scalar/residue. Its squared weight has twice the logarithmic action. It does not turn (19) into a full marked recoupling norm or authorize replacing a partner germ by its positive value core; those source requirements in section 5 remain. Audit: [universal rational certificates and local geometry](../experiments/audit_actual_four_port_hyperideal_angle_volume.py), with [recorded results](../experiments/actual_four_port_hyperideal_angle_volume_results.json). It verifies four symbolic identities in six independent edge variables, all six derivative/Gram lengths in regular, unequal and opposite-obtuse chambers, three independent direct regular geometric volume integrals, and the exact half-step angle ranges at eight full physical levels. Finite profiles check normalization; the uniform proof is the Gram construction, symbolic identities and first variation above. The range audit also verifies all shifted factorial arguments, exact quarter-grid endpoint insets and the <=N positive-term count in (19). The four-port theorem has the stated selected positive-length sheet and source scope; it is not a general graph-energy estimate. The scalar consequence (19) uses the supported Racah theorem with its half-step shifts and boundary-uniform constants. It does not extend the low-fold jet estimate to the retained partner current.

title: What a Tauberian argument would need from the original positive Fourier energy
text: # What a Tauberian argument would need from the original positive Fourier energy 28 October 2026. The positive Fourier energy is the right actual object for testing an Abelian/Tauberian approach. It permits elementary, self-contained statements about its Laplace transform and its exponential rate. Positivity alone identifies a limsup, however; it does not force the volume limit or suppress exceptional low levels. The results below give a precise additional cross-level condition that WOULD turn a critical Laplace singularity into the full original volume limit. No such cross-level condition or sharp singularity has yet been derived from the actual A-source. This is a criterion and a source-scope audit, not a proof of the conjecture. ## 1. The exact original energy and its existing bound Use the original unitary color Fourier transform and original reduced normalization from [the independently audited Plancherel identity](ordinary_color_plancherel_bound_audit.md). For every fixed knot presentation, E_N=sum_k |chat_(N,k)|²=|K_N|²+R_N, 1<=R_N<=N^B, N>=2, (1) with a fixed constant/power allowed in the upper bound. Every pivot, Cartan and framing factor is retained. The ordinary-color remainder is the original remainder, not a positive replacement model. Thus log E_N=log(1+|K_N|²)+O(log N). (2) For any fixed lambda>0, log E_N/N ->lambda iff (2pi/N)log|K_N| ->pi*lambda. (3) In particular the desired energy exponent is lambda=Vol/pi. The [direct ordinary-color coefficient bound](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_regular_fast_color_elimination.md) gives, for an ell-crossing b-braid, ||C_j||_1<=j^(ell+b-1)4^(ell*j). Taking j=N and using (1) proves E_N<=exp(CN) for a fixed C. This provides an actual nonempty convergence half-plane for the positive Laplace series Z(s)=sum_(N>=2) E_N exp(-sN). (4) It does not identify its sharp convergence boundary geometrically. ## 2. The abscissa gives exactly the exponential limsup Put lambda*=limsup_N log(E_N)/N, finite and nonnegative. Then (4) converges for real s>lambda* and diverges for s<lambda*. Indeed, for s>lambda*, choose epsilon<(s-lambda*). Eventually E_N<=exp((lambda*+epsilon)N), so comparison with a geometric series proves convergence. For s<lambda*, infinitely many terms satisfy E_N>=exp((s+epsilon)N), so the terms of (4) do not even tend to zero. The convergence boundary itself can be convergent or divergent. Consequently a source-derived proof that Z(s) is finite for every s>Vol/pi would give the sharp original exponential UPPER bound. Locating its abscissa at Vol/pi would identify the corresponding limsup. Positivity makes these implications exact, but does not compute the abscissa. Merely naming the abscissa is not an estimate. ## 3. A power singularity gives a genuine cumulative Tauberian conclusion Here is a special case sufficient to explain the Karamata-type idea, proved independently rather than assumed. Suppose, for lambda>0, alpha>0 and C>0, an actual calculation establishes Z(lambda+t) ~ C t^(-alpha), t down to0. (5) Then A(x):=sum_(2<=N<=x) exp(-lambda N)E_N ~ C x^alpha/Gamma(alpha+1). (6) Proof. Write a_N=exp(-lambda N)E_N>=0 and define finite positive measures on x>=0 by nu_t=(t^alpha/C) sum_N a_N exp(-tN) delta_(tN). For each integer k>=0 their Laplace moments satisfy integral exp(-kx)dnu_t =(t^alpha/C)Z(lambda+(k+1)t)->(k+1)^(-alpha). (7) Under y=exp(-x), these are ordinary polynomial moments on [0,1]. The candidate limit has x-density exp(-x)x^(alpha-1)/Gamma(alpha); its moments are exactly (7), by the defining Gamma integral. Polynomial moment convergence implies convergence against every continuous function on [0,1]: Bernstein polynomials approximate such a function uniformly, since uniform continuity and the binomial variance bound force the approximation error to zero. The measures' total masses tend to one, so the uniform approximation error is uniform in t. This proves the claimed weak convergence without a separate Tauberian theorem. The bounded function y^-1 times the indicator y>=exp(-1) has just one jump, at a point with zero limit mass. Approximate it from above and below by continuous functions. Hence (t^alpha/C)A(1/t) ->integral_0^1 x^(alpha-1)/Gamma(alpha)dx =1/Gamma(alpha+1), which proves (6). An immediate useful consequence is that HIGH-ENERGY LEVELS OCCUR IN EVERY FIXED MULTIPLICATIVE WINDOW: for each delta in(0,1), A(n)-A((1-delta)n) ~ C[1-(1-delta)^alpha] n^alpha/Gamma(alpha+1)>0. (8) Thus no fixed proportional interval can avoid all near-rate levels. Also the UNTILTED cumulative energy S(n)=sum_(N<=n)E_N obeys log S(n)/n ->lambda. (9) For the upper bound S(n)<=exp(lambda n)A(n). For the lower bound, use (8) and exp(lambda(1-delta)n), then let delta decrease to zero. Equations (6),(8),(9) are stronger than a bare limsup. They still do not prove log E_N/N->lambda for every individual N. ## 4. An operative cross-level condition completing the implication The following one-sided source-transport condition suffices. Suppose there are fixed delta0>0, L>=0 and A0>=0 such that, for every large n, E_(n-r)<=n^A0 exp(Lr) E_n, 0<=r<=delta0*n. (10) It prevents an exponentially deep drop from preceding nearby levels; it does not assert positivity of the original unsquared period. An exact source-preserving map between the relevant positive Fourier spaces, with norm at most n^(A0/2)exp(Lr/2), would prove (10). Then the cumulative exponential law (9) implies log E_n/n ->lambda. (11) To prove it, fix 0<delta<delta0. Since lambda>0, (9) gives S(n)-S((1-delta)n)=exp(lambda n+o(n)). By (10) this difference is at most n^(A0+1)exp(L delta n)E_n. Hence liminf log E_n/n>=lambda-Ldelta. Let delta decrease to zero; the upper bound E_n<=S(n) proves (11). Combining (3),(5),(10) therefore proves the original volume limit with V=pi*lambda. An O(1) bound on each negative neighboring log-increment implies (10). In contrast, a polynomial comparison at ONE neighboring step, E_(n-1)<=n^A E_n, accumulates to exp(O(r log n)); it does not imply (10). Such a weak comparison allows narrow exponentially deep dips. It cannot be substituted into this proof without further control. The power singularity (5) is itself a substantial averaged asymptotic. It is stronger information than the convergence abscissa. Neither (5) nor (10) is being inferred from positivity or from an algebraic classical characteristic. ## 5. What the current actual source does and does not supply The available exact A-equation transports COLOR j at a fixed q: sum_i a_i(q,-q^j) C_(j+i)(q)=0. The energy E_N changes the color range, the Hilbert-space dimension, AND the parameter q_N when N changes. The fixed-q recurrence does not provide an operator from the level n-r Fourier space to the level n Fourier space. The quantum-group coproduct is also at fixed q. Connected-sum multiplication changes the KNOT at a fixed level; it is not a submultiplicative relation in the LEVEL N. The verified cross-level polynomial rigidity of the color family identifies that family, but gives no norm estimate of the form (10). There is a concrete actual-source reason not to replace this missing level map by uniform continuity of a fixed-color polynomial in q. For 4_1, its exact Newton formula gives C_N(q_(N+1))=1 for EVERY N: at that root the evaluation node Q^N+Q^-N equals the first node Q+Q^-1, so all positive Newton indices vanish. The same fixed color at q_N is K_N. Thus a q-displacement of order N^-2 can cross the entire high-color boundary response. This does not disprove (10) for the COMPLETE level energies E_N,E_(N+1); it shows why fixed-q pointing and low-color derivative estimates do not supply it. Likewise each exact pointed Gram ratio is positive at its own level. It has not been rewritten as the moments of one fixed positive transfer operator across levels, nor as a positive renewal equation with a specified spectral edge. Either construction, with the original source and nonzero edge weight verified, could supply Tauberian input. The existing level-dependent Gram identity does not. There is even a small exact original hyperbolic-source warning against assuming cross-level moment/log-convex structure for raw E_N. For 4_1, the independently proved whole-source formula gives K_2=5, K_3=13, K_4=27, R_2=1, R_3=2, R_4=3, E_2=26, E_3=171, E_4=732. Thus E_2 E_4-E_3²=-10209<0. (12) So positivity within each Fourier space does not imply positivity of the cross-level Hankel matrix, or a raw positive moment representation of E_(n+2). This does not exclude an eventual inequality, a known polynomial normalization, or a different source-derived transfer. It simply prevents assuming that structure from Plancherel alone. ## 6. A minimal counterexample to positivity-only inference For any lambda>0, let E_N=exp(lambda N) at even N and E_N=1 at odd N. This is NOT a knot counterexample. Its purpose is to check the exact logical strength of the proposed Tauberian inference. It satisfies Z(lambda+t)~1/(2t), A(x)~x/2, log S(n)/n->lambda, but log E_N/N alternates between lambda and0. It violates (10). Thus even the pure-pole singularity and positivity leave an individual-level survival condition to establish. The useful next target is consequently a SOURCE-DERIVED positive Laplace/renewal description or a cross-level comparison such as (10). Neither is currently available. A Tauberian argument can use those inputs efficiently; it cannot create them or resolve the geometric branch coupling by itself. Reproduce the exact source warning and the positive-sequence checks: ```sh python3 experiments/audit_actual_fourier_energy_tauberian.py ``` Coverage only: this is the classical positive-measure Tauberian setting; see [Michael Taylor, Karamata's Tauberian Theorem](https://mtaylor.web.unc.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/16915/2020/07/karamata.pdf). Section 3 supplies its own moment proof for the precise power-law case used here; no quoted theorem supplies the missing knot-source inputs.

title: An exact bridge-number certificate for odd-prime-divisible plat boxes
status: Exact minimal bridge number from original plat Fox colors
text: # An exact bridge-number certificate for odd-prime-divisible plat boxes elementary certificate, 31 October 2026. This result is independent of the source asymptotics and circle-packing balance condition. It identifies exact-bridge congruence subfamilies when the prescribed plat parity gives a knot. Geometric balance must be established separately. ## 1. Fox colors and the signed crossing map Fix an odd prime $p$ and work over $\mathbb F_p$. A Fox coloring assigns a field element to each diagram arc between undercrossings. At a crossing, if $a$ is the overstrand color and $b,c$ are the two understrand colors, the condition is $$ b+c=2a.\tag{1} $$ All colorings, including the $p$ constant colorings of a knot, are counted. The rule is unoriented and unchanged on reversing a strand orientation. Follow a braid in its actual geometric slot order. Choose the positive crossing convention in which an incoming ordered pair $(a,b)$ becomes $(2a-b,a)$. Its matrix and inverse are $$ \begin{aligned} T&=\begin{pmatrix}2&-1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}=I+A, &A&=\begin{pmatrix}1&-1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad A^2=0,\\ T^{-1}&=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&2\end{pmatrix}=I-A. \end{aligned}\tag{2} $$ The opposite naming convention interchanges $T$ and $T^{-1}$ and has the same consequence. For every signed integer $e$, $$ T^e=I+eA.\tag{3} $$ This follows by the binomial formula for $e\geq0$ and the exact inverse $I-A$ for negative $e$. Thus $p\mid e$ implies $T^e=I$ over $\mathbb F_p$. At a crossing on slot $j$, embed this two-by-two block in the identity on the other slots; the same identity holds there. This is an identity on the ordered color register, not on strand labels. The underlying endpoint permutation remains the transposition of the two slots when $e$ is odd. In particular, $T^p=I$ for odd $p$ does not make the tangle an identity tangle or a permutation identity. ## 2. Coloring invariance, including constant colorings The local rules give bijections of coloring sets under all three Reidemeister moves, keeping exterior colors fixed. For type I, (1) forces the new short arc to have the old arc's color, so the extension is unique. For type II, write $s_a(b)=2a-b$. The strand passing under the other twice undergoes $s_a$ twice, and $s_a^2=I$; its intermediate color is uniquely determined. For type III, the exact identity $$ s_a\circ s_b=s_{s_a(b)}\circ s_a.\tag{4} $$ follows by evaluating both sides on $c$: both give $2a-2b+c$. This is the crossing-rule relation for the two three-crossing arrangements, and every intermediate color is uniquely determined from the exterior data. It proves the local bijection, with all orientation versions covered because (1) is unoriented and $s_a$ is its own inverse. Thus the number $\operatorname{Col}_p(K)$ is invariant under diagram moves for the same unframed knot. The bijections preserve constant colorings, so counting all colors introduces no diagram-dependent convention. The usual Reidemeister characterization of diagrams of the same knot is the underlying diagram-equivalence fact used here. ## 3. Exact count for the supplied standard plat Consider a standard $2k$-plat whose genuine crossings all lie in specified adjacent-strand boxes $\sigma_{j_i+1}^{e_i}$. Here the physical slots are numbered from $0$, so slot $j$ is the conventional generator $\sigma_{j+1}$. Use the standard adjacent cup and cap pairs $$ (0,1),(2,3),\ldots,(2k-2,2k-1) $$ in the same geometric slot order. Assume every $e_i$ is divisible by $p$. There are no extra uncontrolled crossings outside these boxes; any such crossings would have to be included in the color propagation separately. At one end each cup forces its two colors equal. The initial register is exactly $$ (a_0,a_0,a_1,a_1,\ldots,a_{k-1},a_{k-1}), \qquad(a_0,\ldots,a_{k-1})\in\mathbb F_p^k.\tag{5} $$ Every full box acts as the identity by (3), even though its physical endpoint permutation can be nontrivial. The opposite register is again (5), so all standard cap constraints hold automatically. These are topological arc constraints; the quantum marked-cap matrix does not modify the underlying diagram or its Fox coloring rule. Propagation through the actual braid is invertible and uniquely fixes every intermediate arc color. Conversely, every coloring restricts to one register (5). Hence the count is exactly $$ \operatorname{Col}_p(\text{plat})=p^k.\tag{6} $$ No strand permutation is dropped: the register uses geometric slot positions at each horizontal section. One must not propagate colors by the bare permutation after already applying the crossing matrices. The link component count is separate. If $\tau$ maps lower slot labels to upper labels, pull the upper adjacent matching back by $\tau$. The union of the lower matching $M$ and $\tau^{-1}M\tau$ is a two-colored $2$-regular multigraph on the $2k$ lower endpoints. Its cycles are precisely the plat components. Thus the prescribed parity yields a knot exactly when this graph is connected. Only $e_i$ modulo $2$ enters $\tau$. ## 4. Any knot with bridge number $b$ has at most $p^b$ colorings Take a diagram with $b$ overpassing bridges. Its overpasses have no undercrossings and carry $b$ individual colors. Every underpass starts at an endpoint of an overpass. Starting with that known endpoint color, follow the underpass: at each crossing the overpass color $a$ is already known, and (1) updates the traveling color by $c\mapsto2a-c$. All underpass arc colors are therefore determined by the $b$ chosen overpass colors. At their opposite endpoints the remaining matching conditions may impose restrictions, but never create an additional choice. Restriction to the overpasses is injective, so $$ \operatorname{Col}_p(K)\leq p^b.\tag{7} $$ This also covers the one-bridge unknot with no crossings.
