A geometric $b$-bridge presentation has its usual diagram with $b$ overpasses, so (7) applies to the minimal bridge number. Conversely, the supplied $2k$-plat is a $k$-bridge presentation: keep its braid monotone and use its $k$ caps as the only maxima. Its knot therefore has bridge number at most $k$. If the component test in Section 3 gives a knot $K$, invariance, (6), and (7) imply $$ p^k=\operatorname{Col}_p(K)\leq p^{\operatorname{br}(K)}, \qquad\operatorname{br}(K)\geq k, \qquad\boxed{\operatorname{br}(K)=k}.\tag{8} $$ The conclusion is minimal bridge number, not only a supplied plat width. ## 5. Compatibility with the actual signed filling parameters In the original source convention the full box exponent is $$ e_i=n_i=\epsilon_i-2P_i, $$ where $\epsilon_i$ is the fixed half-twist parity and $P_i$ is the signed integer full-twist parameter. Since $p$ is odd, $2$ is invertible modulo $p$. The condition $p\mid n_i$ is precisely $$ P_i\equiv\epsilon_i/2\pmod p.\tag{9} $$ It does not change $n_i\bmod2$ or the prescribed component permutation. Each congruence class contains arbitrarily large positive and negative $P_i$, independently at every box. It is therefore compatible with any fixed parity pattern already proved to give a knot and any independently sufficiently long signed-twist threshold. The prime $p=3$ already suffices. For example, the [simple-white family's component-parity construction](general_simple_white_plat_class.md), Section 3, can be combined with (9): the first $O$ layer has odd exponents and the other boxes even; its width-two example uses the stated first-slot odd exponent. The [balanced reduced-layer family](general_reduced_layer_long_filling_volume.md) establishes the separate geometry for $k\geq4$. In its congruence subfamilies, this coloring argument certifies minimal bridge number exactly $k$. The analytic volume theorem itself has no extra congruence restriction. ## Validation and scope The Fox certificate does not imply circle-packing balance.

title: The original Gaussian resolvent has a positive numerator and a controlled closing cap
status: Exact full numerator; controlled root Gaussian closing cap
text: # The original Gaussian resolvent has a positive numerator and a controlled closing cap 31 October 2026. The exact original numerator has a positive path expansion and a Fejer all-color formula, while the Gaussian resolvent has a subexponential closing cap at +2. No global contour selection, source asymptotic or generic-q continuation of the Gaussian is asserted. ## 1. Inputs already proved in the repository [actual matching edge continuant operator period](actual_matching_edge_continuant_operator_period.md) gives the actual generic tridiagonal blocks, both continuants, all Jordan poles and the true physical high-total adapter. [actual casimir off spectrum prefix action](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_casimir_off_spectrum_prefix_action.md) and [actual matching edge cross central green action](actual_matching_edge_cross_central_green_action.md) give selected logarithmic actions only on strict physical prefix/row compacts. They do not cover arbitrary complex magnetic heads, midpoint prefixes or a global contracted exterior. The latter theorem is explicitly an integrand theorem. [actual casimir endpoint resolvent bound](../papers/filling-bounds/README.md) bounds EVERY original block by CN^17 at +2 and on |sigma-2|<=cN^-18, including genuine resolvent normals. The stronger [actual casimir closing region bound](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_casimir_closing_region_bound.md) gives, for fixed gamma>0, throughout the angular cone sigma=2+r exp(i phi), |phi|<=pi-gamma, ||(sigma-Omega)^-1|| <= CN^3 exp[CN f(r)+C log^2 N], f(r)=sqrt(r) log(2+1/r). It includes every physical degree and all fixed genuine RESOLVENT jets. Thus the +2 joining region was already controlled; it must not be reported as an unresolved endpoint estimate. The new exact all-integer Gaussian uses the full Hermite data: R^n=q^(n d^2/4) f_n(Omega), f_n(sigma)=exp[n N K(sigma)/(4pi i)], K(sigma)=arccosh(-sigma/2)^2, chi_N(sigma)=2T_N(sigma/2)+2, V_N(sigma)=chi_N(sigma)(sigma-Omega)^-1. K is analytic on C minus [2,infinity), removable at -2. This equality is at the original root; it does not identify an arbitrary off-root R germ. The homogeneous source applies coefficient extraction to the ordered product of these local functions, retaining all original targets and the unit q^(n d^2/4). No additional N or marked scalar is introduced by this functional calculus. ## 2. A direct Gaussian consequence for the entire closing cap On either side of the K slit near +2, K(sigma)=-pi^2+O(sqrt(|sigma-2|)), |f_n(sigma)|<=exp[C |n| N sqrt(|sigma-2|)]. The estimate is uniform on either slit side, including its boundary values. Therefore the old whole-cone resolvent bound gives ||f_n(sigma)(sigma-Omega)^-1|| <=CN^3 exp[CN(f(r)+|n|sqrt(r))+C log^2 N]. (1) For every FIXED integer n this has vanishing exponential rate as r->0. It also holds with fixed genuine q derivatives on the resolvent ALONE, using the old resolvent product rule. Those are not advertised as genuine derivatives of R^n. There is an actual joining path in the Gaussian slit. Run inward on the two rays sigma=2-r exp(+/-i gamma), down to radius rho_N=min(cN^-18,r_N/2) when the outer radius is r_N, and join them by the short LEFT arc of that circle. The rays are covered by (1). The left arc is in the old polynomial endpoint disk and lies to the RIGHT of the largest spectral node, whose distance from 2 is comparable to N^-2. It never crosses the K cut. On that arc |f_n|=exp[O(|n|N sqrt(rho_N))] and the full resolvent is polynomial. The cap therefore has rate at most C[f(r)+|n|sqrt(r)], and any r_N->0 yields exp[o(N)] for fixed n. This establishes only the closing portion of a contour, with no estimate for its surrounding source contraction. ## 3. Exact positivity of the FULL homogeneous resolvent numerator Use distinct names B,C for the two middle face weights. In the proved source polynomial representation, Omega=-T acts on z^j, 0<=j<N, by Omega z^j=c_j z^j-b_j(x+y)z^(j-1)-e_j xy z^(j-2), c_j=2cos((2j+1)pi/N), b_j=4sin^2(j pi/N), e_j=4sin(j pi/N)sin((j-1)pi/N). Here b_0=e_0=e_1=0 and all allowed lowering weights are nonnegative. These are the original endpoint factors, not cyclic replacements. Expand the resolvent by ALL finite downward paths from j to i, using steps one or two. A path with k steps visits k+1 distinct row indices. Multiplication by chi_N removes precisely those k+1 factors, with their multiplicities even when eigenvalues coincide. Its numerator is (-1)^k (positive step weight) product_(unvisited r)(sigma-c_r). At sigma=-2-u, u>=0, the product has sign (-1)^(d-k). Consequently P_N(u;x,B,C,y):=(-1)^d H_(V_N(-2-u))(x,B,C,y) is a polynomial with NONNEGATIVE coefficients in all FIVE variables u,x,B,C,y. Its face degree remains d. The same original homogeneous adapter is used, including C^(d-j) for the initial degree j. For every complex sigma, |H_(V_N(sigma))|_coef <= P_N(|sigma+2|;x,B,C,y). (2) The inequality is termwise in face coefficients, since |sigma-c_r|<=|sigma+2|+2+c_r. It controls the entire polynomial numerator, including its independent semisimple data; no interpolation from only the complete-channel values was used. Cauchy on a fixed spectral disk also controls spectral derivatives by the same positive regularization with an enlarged radius. The spectral total-derivative identity supplied independently by cluster is compatible with this statement. Its paired data involve BOTH V(c) and V'(c); the latter cannot be recovered by differentiating a root-only complete-channel simplification. There is an exact Fejer normalization of the endpoint coupon. With T=-Omega, define F_N(X)=(T_N(X)-1)/(X-1), using the polynomial quotient. Then (-1)^d V_N(-2)=F_N(T/2) =N+2 sum_(j=1)^(N-1)(N-j) T_j(T/2) =L_N+2 sum_(h=1)^(N-1)L_h. (2a) The first equality follows by dividing chi_N(sigma)-chi_N(-2) by sigma+2 and using T_N(-X)=(-1)^N T_N(X). The other two follow from the finite cosine telescope. This is a coherent identity in the actual Casimir quotient, not positivity of the separate L_h coupons. It makes the extra semisimple endpoint data completely explicit. No existing Fejer-named note was found in the repository search. More generally the divided Chebyshev identity gives EXACTLY (-1)^d V_N(-2cosh w) =L_N+2 sum_(h=1)^(N-1) cosh((N-h)w)L_h. (2b) For example, subtract 2T_N(t/2) from 2T_N(s/2), divide by s-t, and expand in U_(h-1)(t/2); then set s=-2cosh w and t=Omega=-T. This is a polynomial identity in s,t, so it includes coincident nodes and all Hermite derivatives. The homogeneous coupon map and the whole original marked contraction preserve it linearly. For a set E of spectral ports, the contracted product of these signed numerators is consequently the exact finite sum over 1<=h_e<=N of the original external-color source, with weights 1 at h_e=N and 2cosh((N-h_e)w_e) at h_e<N. Every retained crossing on a complementary port remains in its actual order. There is no free interpolation or new mark. At a V-only selected port the coupon is literally L_h, with no newly inserted half crossing. If an original R^epsilon is retained separately at that same port, it multiplies BOTH sides of (2b) in its original order. Thus the shared numerator-capacity problem is concretely an exponential generating transform of ALL original colors. The existing small-deficit corridor controls only h_e close to N; neither (2b) nor path positivity supplies the missing phase-sensitive far-color bound. ## 4. Parity and an explicit limitation of a numerator norm argument For odd N, -2 is a simple node and V_N(-2)=N^2 P_simple=N L_(N,simple). For even N=2m, the exact scalar polynomial identity is -V_N(-2)=(2-Omega) U_(m-1)(Omega/2)^2. (3) Indeed chi_N(sigma)-4=(sigma^2-4)U_(m-1)(sigma/2)^2 and V_N(-2)=(chi_N(Omega)-chi_N(-2))/(Omega+2), interpreted as its polynomial quotient. Formula (3) retains semisimple contributions. The unrestricted positive-weight norm in (2) does NOT always have the complete folded rate. The B^d coefficient is a length-zero path, hence [B^d]P_N(u)=|chi_N(-2-u)|/(2+u+c_d). (4) At even N and u=0 this tends to one. Thus at x=y=C=1, B=exp(8), liminf N^-1 log P_N(0)>=8. In contrast, positivity and degree a of the original folded determinant give F(1,B,1)+F(1,1,1) <= (1/2)log B+2F(1,1,1) <=4+pi<8. The last elementary bound uses F(1,1,1)=3[Lambda(pi/6)+Lambda(pi/3)]/pi<=pi/2, obtained by the absolute Fourier bound |Lambda(theta)|<=pi^2/12. This is a strictly positive quartet, not a zero-face pathology. At odd N, the coefficient (4) vanishes exactly at u=0. But for any fixed k>0 and u_N=N^-k its exponential rate is zero: writing eta_N=arccosh(1+u_N/2), its numerator is 4sinh^2(N eta_N/2), while eta_N~sqrt(u_N). Therefore the same lower rate 8 reappears under polynomially small regularization. The relevant limits do not commute. No coefficientwise domination by bare P_N(0) is asserted. This is only a LOCAL arbitrary-positive-radius norm limitation. It is not a counterexample to the original shared marked coefficient, nor to a rate statement on a specially certified packing radius. The large diagonal term has a source-specific face degree and can be constrained by the remaining original graph. The phase-blind Hermite obstruction in [actual direct long power source](actual_direct_long_power_source.md) is a separate, graph-wide result. ## 5. The Gaussian does not automatically damp a whole enclosing contour On the spectral cover put sigma=-2cosh w, w=s+it, s>0, |t|<pi. Then K=squared w, |f_n|=exp[n N s t/(2pi)], chi_N(-2cosh w)=2[(-1)^N cosh(Nw)+1]. On a fixed compact with s>0, N^-1 log |f_n/chi_N| -> n s t/(2pi)-s. (5) Thus one side is damped and the other grows. On the growing side, a fixed spectral ellipse with |t|>2pi/|n| gives positive scalar quotient rate, increasing with |n|. The exact matrix numerator can change that rate, but the mere largeness of a fixed twist cannot justify a global decrease. A complete ellipse also meets the K cut near +2; deleting that point and using the proved cap does not change this bulk sign issue. In the half-plane Re w>0 the exact denominator has the convergent expansion epsilon=(-1)^N, 1/chi_N=epsilon exp(-Nw)/(1+epsilon exp(-Nw))^2 =sum_(m>=1) (-1)^(m-1) epsilon^m m exp(-mNw). (6) The individual Gaussian-charge phase is n w^2/(4pi i)-m w, before adding the actual V numerator phase and all face coefficient actions. Its stationary point without that numerator is w=2pi i m/n. There is no justification for discarding every m except the smallest. This agrees with the independently derived nonzero midpoint charges in the exact full-Hermite Fourier formula. ## 6. A precise remaining input A sufficient next theorem would control the original marked, shared-face resolvent numerator after sewing, uniformly on a specified spectral cycle and on the needed complex face torus. It must include the full V (or V and V'), not just positive complete samples, and prove: 1. a local analytic relative packet at the selected near-parabolic stationary point, including its original coefficient contour; 2. a strict global real-action bound for the complement of that packet on a homologous product cycle, preserving every spectral pole and the endpoint/Fourier currents; 3. control of every surviving nonzero charge in (6), or its equivalent unsplit resolvent period, with the actual neighboring Casimirs kept in their original order. The torsor theorem solves the classical local transport and normalizes the Gaussian Hamiltonian. The existing Green estimates supply selected integrand phases on strict physical charts, and (1) completes the +2 cap for this root Gaussian. Neither supplies the missing global source-specific amplitude, cycle comparison or complementary gap. The exact positive path theorem (2) is a concrete input, but (4) explains why replacing its shared coefficient by an unrestricted local norm would not complete the argument. ## Validation and scope The [focused original-source audit](../experiments/audit_actual_gaussian_resolvent_numerator_and_cap.py) and its [results](../experiments/actual_gaussian_resolvent_numerator_and_cap_results.json) record 77 symbolic identities, 3,100 independently built original coproduct/physical-grid entries (including 1,000 wrong-unwrapped-total zeros), and 4,039 nonnegative path/complex majorant checks. They do not numerically establish any asymptotic or contour claim. The joining radius must remain inside both the endpoint disk and an arbitrarily shrinking outer cap. The remaining bulk/shared-source requirements in Section 6 are not proved.

title: A generic all-port single Racah kernel with actual Clebsch normalization
text: # A generic all-port single Racah kernel with actual Clebsch normalization 29 October 2026. This proves a SINGLE terminating balanced 4phi3 formula for every entry of the genuine inverse four-port recoupling matrix. All external nonnegative INTEGER highest weights are allowed, including half-integral spins and their actual cyclic-turn sign. The normalizer comes from a true boundary entry and a leading coefficient, not a quoted 6j evaluation or polynomial norm formula. The independent source is the actual two-sum/all-entry construction in [the ordinary four-port theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_ordinary_four_port_recoupling_kernel.md). All high channels and generic normal tails are retained. Root sign coherence, positive recoupling and sharp graph energy are not inferred. ## 1. Highest-weight notation and actual bases Use generic zeta, Q=zeta^2 and F_n=(Q;Q)_n. On the ordinary module V_A of INTEGER highest weight A>=0 use the original balanced generators and canonical cup: P_A(u)=(-1)^u zeta^[u(A-u-1)] F_u F_(A-u)/F_A, p_A(u,A-u)=P_A(u), ell_A=p_A^(-1), F|u>=(1-Q^(u+1))|u+1>, Ecal|u>=zeta^(-A-1)(1-Q^(A+1-u))|u-1>, K|u>=zeta^A Q^(-u). Take external highest weights A,B,C,D with even total. The allowed intermediate highest weights are E=max(|A-B|,|C-D|),...,min(A+B,C+D), step2, G=max(|B-C|,|D-A|),...,min(B+C,D+A), step2. (1) Assume these equal-cardinality ranges nonempty. Every W_AB^E has its first highest component one. Put m=(A+B-E)/2. Its actual highest coefficients are h_AB^E(s)=(-1)^s zeta^[s(A-2B+2m-s-1)] F_(B-m+s)F_(A-s)/(F_(B-m)F_A), (2) and W_AB^E[r]=Delta(F)^r h/F_r, with the canceled physical coproduct entries proved in the independent source theorem. Define FULL invariant columns in the SAME external A,B,C,D order: S_E=(W_AB^E tensor W_CD^E)p_E, T_G(u,v,w,z)=(-1)^A zeta^(A-2u) [(W_BC^G tensor W_DA^G)p_G](v,w,z,u). (3) The factor (-1)^A K_A is the ACTUAL last-to-first pivotal turn: ell_A^T p_A=(-1)^A K_A^(-1). It reduces to the older K_A for integer spins but its sign matters when A is odd. Scaled physical cups have reciprocal evaluations and retain this same snake. We prove S_E=sum_G L_(G,E)T_G on EVERY external color. These are inverse coefficients, not the specialized six-head source column. ## 2. Explicit product normalizers from actual boundary entries Set H=(A+B+C-D)/2, L=min(A,H), Gmax=min(A+D,B+C), n=(Gmax-G)/2, U=(C+E-D)/2, V=(D-C+E)/2, m=(A+B-E)/2, chi_E=(-1)^U zeta^[U(E-U-1)-CV] F_U F_D/(F_((C+D-E)/2) F_E). (4) The unique outer-color contribution in the true S column gives S_E(i,H-i,0,D)=chi_E W_AB^E[U](i,H-i). (5) Its LAST physical Clebsch entry X_E has a product evaluation: if L=H: X_E=F_H h_AB^E(m)/(F_m F_U); otherwise L=A, put k=E-U: X_E=(-1)^m zeta^[-AB+2Am-m^2-m+k(E-B)] F_(m+k)/(F_m F_k). (6) The first is the unique coproduct term with second color zero. For the second the proved lowest endpoint is W_AB^E[E](A,B-m)=(-1)^m zeta^[-AB+2Am-m^2-m]. Apply Ecal^(E-U). To finish with first color A every lowering must act on the second object. Its coefficient divided by the target coefficient zeta^[-(E-U)(E+1)]F_(E-U) gives (6). Thus no magnetic sum is hidden in X_E. For G put i0=(A+G-D)/2, m_bc=(B+C-G)/2, m_da=(D+A-G)/2. The first nonzero T-chart entry is b_G=(-1)^A zeta^(A-2i0) h_BC^G(m_bc) *(-1)^m_da zeta^[-AD+2D m_da-m_da(m_da+1)]. (7) Indeed T_G(i,H-i,0,D)=0 for i>i0, and its value at i0 is (7). It retains the canonical cup, the W_DA lowest endpoint and the odd-A cyclic sign. Every b_G is a nonzero generic product. Define also J_n=zeta^[-n(B+1)] F_L F_(B-H+L) /[F_(L-n)F_(B-H+L-n)], J_0=1. (8) This is the product of n lower off-diagonals of the ACTUAL first pair Casimir on physical prefix degree H: Omega_AB(i,i-1)=zeta^(-B-1) (1-Q^i)(1-Q^(B-H+i)). (9) All factorial indices in (4),(6),(7),(8) are nonnegative on their physical ranges. The formulas are source entries, not fitted gauges. ## 3. The single terminating balanced Racah formula If A+D<=B+C choose differences C-D,B-A; otherwise choose D-C,A-B. Their maximum is E_min=max(|A-B|,|C-D|). Call the larger s1=E_min and the other s2. Define alpha=zeta^(1+s1), beta=zeta^(1+s2), gamma=zeta^(-1-C-D), delta=zeta^(-1-A-B), P=alpha beta gamma delta=Q^(-Gmax), z_E=zeta^(E+1), K=zeta^(Gmax+1). (10) At equality this gives the same unordered parameter set. The first parameter alpha is fixed to specify the polynomial normalization. Put C_n=alpha^n(PQ^(n-1);Q)_n /(alpha beta,alpha gamma,alpha delta;Q)_n, G_n(E)=sum_(k=0)^n (Q^-n,PQ^(n-1),alpha z_E,alpha/z_E;Q)_k Q^k /(Q,alpha beta,alpha gamma,alpha delta;Q)_k. (11) Listed Pochhammers are multiplied. This is ONE finite sum, possibly terminated earlier by another numerator. All generic denominators are units in the physical length: alpha beta has positive exponent of Q, while alpha gamma and alpha delta first reach zero AFTER n. The leading coefficient C_n is nonzero generic. Then the exact all-entry source coefficient is L_(G,E)=chi_E X_E/(b_G J_n C_n) *G_n(E), S_E=sum_(G in (1)) L_(G,E)T_G. (12) No 6j formula, norm or orthogonality measure is an input. ## 4. The uniquely fixed actual Jacobi operator The actual fourth-leg bend identifies an invariant column with a highest-weight-D three-object column. Its third-color-zero chart w(i)=Psi(i,H-i,0,D), max(0,H-B)<=i<=L, is injective by the original highest equation and ordinary F descendants. The actual middle Casimir Bmid in that chart is the upper-bidiagonal matrix (Bmid)_ii=zeta^(D-A+1)Q^i+zeta^(-D+A-1)Q^(-i), (Bmid)_(i-1,i)=-zeta^(B+C-A-1)Q^(i-H) *(1-Q^(A+1-i))(1-Q^(H-i+1)). (13) This is the independently derived physical color0/color1 extraction. Let Amid=Omega_AB. The S_E and T_G have respective eigenvalues lambda_E=zeta^(E+1)+zeta^(-E-1), lambda_G. Put lambda(W)=zeta^(W+1)+zeta^(-W-1), Delta=zeta+zeta^(-1), rho=zeta-zeta^(-1), and central values a0=lambda(A)lambda(B)+lambda(C)lambda(D), b0=lambda(B)lambda(C)+lambda(A)lambda(D), c0=lambda(A)lambda(C)+lambda(B)lambda(D). The original generic cleared Fricke identities force Bmid to be three-diagonal in the S basis. Write its action as Bmid S_E=p_E S_(E+2)+d_E S_E+m_E S_(E-2). The first relation gives d_E=(Delta b0-c0 lambda_E)/(Delta^2-lambda_E^2). (14) The E=0 exception means A=B,C=D and is fixed by the ACTUAL cup projection rather than cancellation of 0/0. With S1=sum_(i=0)^A Q^-i and S2=sum_(i=0)^A Q^(-2i), (13) gives ell_A p_A=(-1)^A zeta^A S1, ell_A Bmid p_A=(-1)^A{ zeta^(C+1)(1+Q^(A+1))S1 +[zeta^(2A-C-1)-zeta^(C+1)Q^(A+1)]S2}. The finite ratio S2/S1=(1+Q^(-A-1))/(1+Q^-1) gives d_0=lambda(A)lambda(C)/Delta, the value of (14) after imposing A=B,C=D and canceling. A=0 is immediate in one dimension. The diagonal of the second Fricke relation fixes the products P_E=p_E m_(E+2), with P_(E_min-2)=0, by [2lambda_E-(Q+Q^-1)lambda_(E+2)]P_E +[2lambda_E-(Q+Q^-1)lambda_(E-2)]P_(E-2) =rho^2[Delta a0-c0 d_E-Delta^2 lambda_E +lambda_E d_E^2]. (15) The forward coefficient is nonzero generic. There is a known ACTUAL LEFT eigenrow fixing the remaining gauge. At G=Gmax one has i0=L, so this physical eigenrow is simply the last chart coordinate. Hence ell_0(E)=L_(Gmax,E)=chi_E X_E/b_(Gmax)!=0. (16) This is a genuine source row, not a prescribed spectral weight. Set u_E=p_E ell_0(E+2)/ell_0(E) and v_E=m_E ell_0(E-2)/ell_0(E). Their sum is lambda_Gmax-d_E, and their successive products are still P_E. Starting from v_Emin=0, the sum and (15) determine them uniquely whenever the proposed interior u is nonzero. The exact result is u_E=K U(z_E), v_E=K U(z_E^-1), U(z)=product_(t=alpha,beta,gamma,delta)(1-tz) /[(1-z^2)(1-Qz^2)], d_E=K+K^-1-K[U(z_E)+U(z_E^-1)]. (17) To prove this uniformly, use independent formal variables zeta,Q^a,Q^b,Q^c,Q^d,Q^e, with A=2a,...,E=2e. For the first branch K=zeta Q^(a+d), both (14),(17) and the product recurrence (15) have IDENTICALLY ZERO cleared rational numerators. The attached audit supplies these two exact six-variable symbolic certificates. The second branch follows by a<->b,c<->d, which preserves a0,b0,c0. Parameter permutation preserves U. After canceled endpoint factors are evaluated, U(z_E) is nonzero on every interior channel and vanishes at the upper endpoint; U(z_E^-1) vanishes at the lower endpoint. The uniqueness therefore proves (17) for the ACTUAL operator, with no unfixed sign. ## 5. Leading coefficients supply the true source normalization Let ell_G(i0)=1 be the physical LEFT eigenrow of (13), zero below i0 and satisfying the elementary one-step equation above i0. The independent two-sum source identity is L_(G,E)=ell_G(w_E)/b_G, w_E(i)=S_E(i,H-i,0,D). (18) Divide by (16). Equation (17) gives the actual finite problem U(z_E)[g(E+2)-g(E)]+U(z_E^-1)[g(E-2)-g(E)] =(Q^-n-1)(1-PQ^(n-1))g(E). (19) Indeed lambda_G=lambda_Gmax+K(Q^-n-1)(1-PQ^(n-1)). This is the exact affine eigenvalue conversion, not a replacement of the physical Casimir. Our OWN [finite symmetric polynomial calculation](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/finite_balanced_sears_operator_proof.md) proves that G_n solves (19), with leading coefficient C_n in lambda_E=z_E+z_E^-1. Its degree is n and its generic leading coefficient is nonzero. The finite grid has distinct Casimir nodes, and its forward coefficient is nonzero until the last slot, so the actual source row is proportional to G_n. Its multiplier still needs determining. For that multiplier, the physical Amid is irreducible tridiagonal. Starting from its last row yields w_E(i)/w_E(L)=a polynomial in lambda_E of degree L-i with leading coefficient 1/product_(t=i+1)^L Amid(t,t-1). (20) Formula (9) evaluates its denominator. In (18) only i>=i0=L-n occurs and ell_G(i0)=1. Thus L_(G,E)/ell_0(E) has degree n and leading coefficient b_(Gmax)/(b_G J_n). (21) Since n is less than the number of channel nodes, this polynomial leading coefficient fixes the proportionality even on the finite grid. Comparing (21) with C_n proves EXACTLY (12), on every color. ## 6. Exact conversion to the seven-factorial sum, including its phase Put [r]!=zeta^[-r(r-1)/2]F_r/(1-Q)^r and s=(A+B+C+D)/2. The tetrahedral incidence is the FOUR faces and THREE opposite sums t=( (A+B+E)/2, (C+D+E)/2, (B+C+G)/2, (D+A+G)/2 ), u=( s, (A+C+E+G)/2, (B+D+E+G)/2 ). Define the literal seven-factorial finite sum S=sum_(z=max t)^(min u) (-1)^z [z+1]! /(product_i[z-t_i]! product_j[u_j-z]!). (22) All its true factorial indices are nonnegative. Choose the effective quadruple (A',B',C',D')=(A,B,C,D) when A+D<=B+C, and (B,A,D,C) otherwise. This latter permutation leaves (22) exactly unchanged: it exchanges its last two faces and its last two opposite sums. Set t0=s-Gmax, R1=(C+D-E)/2, R2=(A+B-E)/2, R3=(A'-B'+E)/2, R4=(D'-C'+E)/2, S0=(-1)^s [s+1]!/([R1]![R2]![t0]![R3]![R4]!), Mstar=(Gmax+G)/2+1, V_n=zeta^n (Q^-Mstar;Q)_n /[F_n(Q^(t0+1);Q)_n(Q^(-s-1);Q)_n]. (23) Every factor in S0 and V_n is nonzero generic. The EXACT source normalization of the seven-factorial convention is S=S0 (V_n/C_n)G_n(E), L_(G,E)=chi_E X_E/(b_G J_n S0 V_n) *S. (24) This includes all signs and powers of zeta. In particular the coefficient is not merely equated to a positive square or to an unnormalized named 6j symbol. Here is an own finite proof of (24). Write a=A'/2,b=B'/2,c=C'/2, d=D'/2, e=E/2, f=G/2. Then fmax=a+d, n=fmax-f and t0=b+c-a-d. At f=fmax the z range in (22) is the SINGLE z=s, which is precisely S0. For general n write z=s-k. Dividing by S0 gives the finite falling-product identity S/S0=sum_(k=0)^n (-1)^k [R1]_k^down [R2]_k^down [R3]_(n-k)^down [R4]_(n-k)^down /([s+1]_k^down [t0+1]_(n-k)^up [k]![n-k]!). (25) The products have their evident consecutive quantum integers. If a formal term lies outside the true range of (22), one falling product contains [0], and that term is EXACTLY zero. No nonzero factorial is assigned to a negative index. For generic formal z_E, factor the k=0 term of (25). Its residual balanced series is 4phi3(Q^-n,Q^-R1,Q^-R2,Q^(-t0-n); Q^(-s-1),Q^(R3-n+1),Q^(R4-n+1);Q,Q). (26) Apply the OWN finite Sears identity, retaining Q^-R1 and taking d_S=Q^(-s-1), e_S=Q^(R3-n+1). The resulting series is exactly the same finite symmetric eigenpolynomial as (11), but with FIRST parameter gamma=zeta^(-1-C-D). In particular its numerator pair is Q^-R1 and Q^(-c-d-e-1), and its denominator parameters are Q^-D', Q^(-(s-B')), Q^(-s-1). After multiplying the k=0 term and canceling the two E-dependent Sears denominator products, its scalar is D_n=(-1)^n zeta^[n(B'-A'+n+1)] (Q^(s-B'-n+1),Q^-D';Q)_n /[F_n(Q^(t0+1);Q)_n]. (27) These cancellations are performed as rational identities in formal z_E BEFORE specializing a channel. Thus the identity still holds when a k=0 factorial representation would have a negative index: the falling-product polynomial (25) has no such division. The OWN symmetric-polynomial proof makes the normalized degree-n eigenpolynomial independent of its first parameter. Its leading coefficient when gamma is first is C_n^gamma=gamma^n(PQ^(n-1);Q)_n /(gamma alpha,gamma beta,gamma delta;Q)_n. Reverse the finite product (Q^(s-B'-n+1);Q)_n in (27). The factors Q^-D' and Q^(-(s-B')) cancel those of C_n^gamma. All signs cancel, the remaining zeta monomial is zeta^n, and D_n C_n^gamma=V_n. (28) Consequently D_n times the gamma-first polynomial equals (V_n/C_n)G_n(E), proving (24). This is a finite product/Sears proof; no generic factorial interpolation or quoted tetrahedral theorem is required. The rational identity for formal z_E specializes to every physical E using (25). ## 7. Exact source relation to a face-normalized scalar metric The actual prefactor in (24) SEPARATES the two intermediate labels: a_E^src=chi_E X_E/S0(E), b_G^src=1/(b_G J_n V_n), L_(G,E)=b_G^src a_E^src S. (29) Thus source columns rescaled as S_E/a_E^src and b_G^src T_G have coefficient EXACTLY the seven-factorial sum (22). No phase has been omitted in this row/column gauge. For an admissible highest-weight triple define its usual finite factorial expression, without assuming any 6j interpretation, D(U,V,W)=[(U+V-W)/2]![(U+W-V)/2]![(V+W-U)/2]! /[((U+V+W)/2)+1]!, D_E=D(A,B,E)D(C,D,E), D_G=D(B,C,G)D(D,A,G). The coefficient sqrt(D_E D_G)S is therefore an explicit diagonal gauge of the actual source: use sqrt(D_E)S_E/a_E^src and b_G^src T_G/sqrt(D_G) as its two generic bases. Square-root branches can be fixed positive at real 0<zeta<1, where every factorial is positive. The squared identity is branch-independent. For ANY separately fixed level N it says exactly [N]^2 D_E D_G L_(G,E)^2/(a_E^src b_G^src)^2 =[N]^2 D_E D_G S^2. (30) In particular (30) identifies the source with this convention of the normalized scalar metric BEFORE a root normal is taken. If the four face sums are in the saturated low-fold chamber, the familiar root-zero factors in (30) are the actual generic ones. High partners and [2N] tails remain in the same equality. Principal-root positivity of the scalar convention must keep its spin phase. For INTEGER spins (all six highest weights even), the supported theorem gives the positive once-power factorial square. For admissible half-integral spins the branch-free generic identity (30) still holds, but the positive sine-factorial square differs by the sign (-1)^(A+B+C+D+E+G). This is the parity of the four face zero-removal signs. No positive-square assertion for arbitrary half-spin data is silently included in (30). These are diagonal gauges of a SCALAR recoupling matrix. They may have zeros or poles at the root; paired confluence and original boundary costs still require their own estimates. They neither make the physical root operator positive nor identify this scalar metric with the full marked magnetic/tensor energy. Also a_E^src depends on its four external objects; it has not been asserted to be a single universal per-edge metric throughout a graph. ## 8. Generic normals and scope The theorem and (24) are rational BEFORE root specialization. High intermediate channels, high partners and every normal of the original maps remain present. Individual source factors may have zeros or poles at a root, and extra terminations can have derivative tails. The GENERIC finite sum and original source maps must be combined before taking a fixed marked normal. In particular second-orbit zeros such as [2N] in (22) are retained in (24); they cannot be deleted when comparing first normals. There is a useful explicit finite normal budget. If the EXTERNAL highest weights A,B,C,D are all <N, while intermediate E,G retain their ENTIRE ranges (1), then every denominator of G_n in (11) is a root unit. Indeed alpha beta=Q^(t0+1), and the last exponent t0+n is one of the ordinary physical coupling deficits, hence <N. The other two exponents start at -m_cd or -m_ab for the minimal E, with n<=m_cd,m_ab<N; their products end before exponent zero. The factor F_n is a unit too. The numerator of C_n has at most one simple root zero: its negative exponents have magnitude <2N and length <N. The actual chi_E has at most one pole, from F_E on a high channel E>=N, whereas X_E, b_G and J_n are physical products with indices <N. Consequently pole_order L_(G,E)<=2. (31) The full invariant T_G has at most one pole from its canonical p_G, so each term L_(G,E)T_G has pole order at most THREE. To check this complete physical identity through its first normal, retain Taylor orders zero through FOUR after multiplying by the cube of a local root parameter. This is a uniform finite normal budget, not a bound on coefficient magnitudes. For unfolded high EXTERNAL partners with highest weights >=N use the generic formula itself and retain its explicit zero factors; (31) is not asserted for that different range. The identity supplies finite actual all-port coefficients for graph contractions and meromorphic jets. It does not make a recoupling positive, unitary, polynomially conditioned or sharply controlled under cycle sewing. Audit: [uniform certificates and independent literal source tensors](../experiments/audit_actual_general_four_port_single_racah_kernel.py). The finite audit checks two universal Fricke/AW identities, 381 generic all-port external families and 1125 single-sum source entries, including half-integral spins with the true (-1)^A cyclic sign. Eight root zero-order families check all 40,820 channel entries, including 14,332 retained high-channel entries, with the certified inverse pole bound two and full-term first-normal budget four. Finite tests supplement the displayed uniform proof; they are not a polynomial-fitting argument. The single-Racah identity does not imply an energy bound or positivity at every root.

title: A global spectral bound for an actual diagonal source sector
text: # A global spectral bound for an actual diagonal source sector analytical theorem, 31 October 2026. This concerns the original homogeneous face polynomial and its original shared marked coefficient. The triangular-basis diagonal sector is not identified with the identity operator. A coefficientwise inequality reduces its absolute bound to an actual identity-inserted positive source. ## 1. The exact diagonal polynomial and a uniform real bound Let $N\geq3$, $d=N-1$, and $$ \chi_N(\sigma)=2T_N(\sigma/2)+2, \qquad c_j=2\cos\frac{(2j+1)\pi}{N},\quad 0\leq j<N. $$ In the original triangular face representation, $\Omega$ has diagonal $c_j$ and lowers the face degree by one or two. The zero-step part of its actual resolvent numerator is $$ \begin{aligned} V_N(\sigma)&=\chi_N(\sigma)(\sigma-\Omega)^{-1},\\ D_N(\sigma;b,c)&=\sum_{j=0}^{d}d_j(\sigma)b^jc^{d-j}, &d_j(\sigma)&=\frac{\chi_N(\sigma)}{\sigma-c_j}. \end{aligned}\tag{1} $$ Every quotient is a polynomial, including all repeated and simple spectral nodes. This is exactly the part of $H_{V_N}$ with zero outer exponents. The middle names $b,c$ and their original orientation are unchanged. It is a restriction of the homogeneous coefficient polynomial, not an assertion that the physical kernel has been diagonalized or made into an identity. For every real $\sigma\in[-2,2]$, $$ |d_j(\sigma)|\leq N^2.\tag{2} $$ Indeed, $\chi_N(c_j)=0$ and the real mean-value integral gives $$ d_j(\sigma)=\int_0^1\chi_N'\bigl(c_j+t(\sigma-c_j)\bigr)\,dt. $$ For $z=2\cos\theta$, $$ \chi_N'(z)=N U_{N-1}(\cos\theta),\qquad U_{N-1}(\cos\theta)=\sum_{r=0}^{N-1}e^{i(N-1-2r)\theta}. $$ Its modulus is at most $N$, including the endpoint limits. Thus the removable values are handled automatically, and $$ |D_N(\sigma)|_{\mathrm{coef}}\leq N^2 H_1(b,c), \qquad H_1(b,c)=\sum_{j=0}^{d}b^jc^{d-j}.\tag{3} $$ This is an upper bound, not an equality or a phase-preserving replacement of $d_j$ by $1$. The weight in (1) depends on both $j$ and $\sigma$. Since $d_j$ has degree $d$, there is also a uniform complex-cover bound: $$ \bigl|d_j(-2\cos(2\pi\delta))\bigr| \leq N^2 e^{2\pi d|\operatorname{Im}\delta|}.\tag{4} $$ For completeness, if a polynomial $p$ of degree $d$ is bounded by $M$ on $[-1,1]$, then $w^{-d}p((w+w^{-1})/2)$ is holomorphic outside the unit disk and at infinity, with boundary modulus at most $M$. The exterior maximum principle gives $|p((w+w^{-1})/2)|\leq M|w|^d$. Apply this with $p(z)=d_j(-2z)$ and $|w|=e^{2\pi|\operatorname{Im}\delta|}$. No division by distance to a spectral node occurs. ## 2. The positive identity-inserted reference at both parities For the original fixed certified diagram $D$, let $F_N$ denote its actual positive Fejér reference coupon: $$ F_N= \begin{cases} (-1)^dV_N(-2),&N\text{ even},\\ V_N(-2)-N^{-2}V_N'(-2),&N\text{ odd}. \end{cases} $$ Fix a nonempty set $I$ of ports carrying the literal identity coupon. Let $Z_{I,N}$ be the original shared marked coefficient with $H_1$ at $I$ and $H_{F_N}$ elsewhere. Every original ordinary target is $d$; the two original protected targets are zero. The [strict identity-insertion theorem](general_fejer_endpoint_source_volume.md), Section 6, gives at even levels a compact full-flow maximum $W_I<\Phi_D$, where $\Phi_D=\operatorname{Vol}(Y_D)/(2\pi)$, or a zero source when the flow is infeasible. Its proof uses an actual representation of the original drilled group killing an essential deleted auxiliary meridian, together with the canonical general-peripheral volume bound. It does not bound independent pieces with unrelated marks. The same rate applies at odd levels. This does not differentiate an even identity: the odd regularized coefficient theorem gives the same uniform local full-simplex entropy $h$ for $H_{F_N}$, while $H_1$ has exact coefficient $1$ on its middle edge and zero elsewhere. Removing the two outer arcs at identity ports leaves the same integral bipartite-flow rounding with literal degree $d$. Compact Laplace therefore gives, at both parities, $$ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log Z_{I,N}=W_I<\Phi_D.\tag{5} $$ If the flow is infeasible, every finite coefficient is zero. This includes an identity edge joining the two protected roots: it cannot supply positive degree $d$ to either zero target. No protected radius is replaced by a positive surrogate. ## 3. Two strict-gap consequences for the actual spectral sectors First take one port $i$ in the pure-middle diagonal sector (1), with arbitrary $\sigma_i\in[-2,2]$. Allow every other port to retain its full numerator, provided $|\sigma_j+2|\leq r$. The [original unused-row majorant](actual_fejer_spectral_polydisk_complement.md), Section 3, gives $$ |H_{V_N(\sigma_j)}|_{\mathrm{coef}}\leq M_N(r)H_{F_N}, \qquad M_N(r)\leq\operatorname{poly}(N)e^{N\theta(r)}, \qquad\theta(r)=\operatorname{arcosh}(1+r/2).\tag{6} $$ At odd levels the factor $\max(1,N^2r)$ in $M_N$ is essential. Bare $H_{V_N(-2)}$ is not an odd majorant. Taking absolute coefficients before multiplying and extracting the one original marked target proves the finite inequality $$ |Z_{\mathrm{diag}\ i;\,\mathrm{full\ elsewhere}}(\boldsymbol\sigma)| \leq N^2M_N(r)^{R-1}Z_{\{i\},N}.\tag{7} $$ Choose fixed $r>0$ so $(R-1)\theta(r)$ is smaller than half the positive gap $\Phi_D-W_{\{i\}}$. Equation (5) gives $\gamma>0$ and $N_0$ such that, uniformly in this region and at both parities, $$ |Z_{\mathrm{diag}\ i;\,\mathrm{full\ elsewhere}}(\boldsymbol\sigma)| \leq e^{N(\Phi_D-\gamma)},\qquad N\geq N_0.\tag{8} $$ If the identity reference is zero, the sector is identically zero. Constants depend on the original fixed diagram. No independently framed norm or unproved physical smoothing has been used. Second, if all other ports are restricted to their actual CROSS sectors, those ports may range over the entire real spectral interval. The [exact cofactor interpolation theorem](../papers/filling-bounds/README.md), Section 8, gives $$ |P_{N,\mathrm{cross}}(\sigma)|_{\mathrm{coef}} \leq C\log^2(N+1)P_{N,\mathrm{cross}}(-2) \leq C\log^2(N+1)H_{F_N},\qquad \sigma\in[-2,2].\tag{9} $$ Combining (3) and (9) with the same marked extraction gives (8) uniformly over the full real spectral cube. The proof applies to any fixed nonempty collection $I$ of diagonal ports, using $Z_{I,N}$, with CROSS elsewhere. This is an inequality for every original coefficient; it neither identifies the restricted quantum sector with a smoothed representation nor asserts absence of cancellation. Both conclusions persist on a sufficiently small fixed complex strip in each globally varying $\delta$ coordinate. Equation (4) and the strip version of (9) add at most $2\pi N\sum_j|\operatorname{Im}\delta_j|$ to the exponent. Shrink the strip so this and the cost in (6) fit within the strict gap in (5). Polynomial factors contribute $o(N)$. ## 4. The entire original Fourier period of the diagonal/CROSS sector Use the global case of Section 3: a fixed nonempty set $I$ is pure diagonal and every other port is CROSS. For a disjoint path partition, remove the odd central zero-step monomial from CROSS and assign it to the diagonal class. This is only a coefficient projection onto positive outer degree, so (9) remains an upper bound. The exact sectors are then disjoint at both parities. Let $Z_N(\boldsymbol\sigma)$ be this shared sector polynomial. It has degree at most $d$ in each spectral variable. The preceding proof supplies fixed $\tau,\gamma>0$ such that $$ \left|Z_N\bigl(-2\cos(2\pi\delta_1),\ldots,-2\cos(2\pi\delta_R)\bigr)\right| \leq e^{N(\Phi_D-\gamma)}\tag{10} $$ for all large $N$, uniformly when $|\operatorname{Im}\delta_i|\leq\tau$ and for all real parts. Real periodicity follows from the polynomial cosines. Shrink $\tau$ once for Cauchy estimates; it is independent of the crossing powers. Insert this sector into the exact original Fourier formula, retaining its scalar, charge factors, sine factors and parity. Write $$ \begin{aligned} B_N(\boldsymbol\delta) &=\left(\prod_i\sin(2\pi\delta_i)\right) Z_N(-2\cos(2\pi\boldsymbol\delta)) e^{\pi iN\sum_i n_i\delta_i^2},\\ J_{N,\boldsymbol\ell} &=\int_{[-1/2,1/2]^R}B_N(\boldsymbol\delta) e^{2\pi iN\sum_i\ell_i\delta_i}\,d\boldsymbol\delta. \end{aligned} $$ Every $n_i$ is a fixed integer, with independent signs allowed. At either endpoint of coordinate $i$, $$ B_N|_{\delta_i=\pm1/2}=0, \qquad \partial_iB_N|_{\delta_i=1/2} =\partial_iB_N|_{\delta_i=-1/2}.\tag{11} $$ The sine vanishes, its derivative is $-2\pi$ at both endpoints, the source sees $\sigma_i=2$ at both, and the Gaussian is $e^{\pi iNn_i/4}$ at both. Only the sine-derivative term survives. These identities persist after derivatives in other coordinates. The Fourier endpoint factor is the same $(-1)^{N\ell_i}$ at both ends. Three integrations by parts therefore give $$ \begin{aligned} J_i=(2\pi iN\ell_i)^{-3}\bigg\{& \left[\partial_i^2 B_N e^{2\pi iN\ell_i\delta_i}\right]_{-1/2}^{1/2}\\ &-\int_{-1/2}^{1/2}\partial_i^3 B_N e^{2\pi iN\ell_i\delta_i}\,d\delta_i\bigg\}. \end{aligned}\tag{12} $$ The first two endpoint terms vanish by (11); the second-derivative endpoint difference in (12) is retained. Repeat in every coordinate. The boundary operations commute with the other derivatives and preserve their endpoint identities. There are at most $3^R$ terms, each with at most three derivatives per coordinate and evaluations or integrals over intervals of length one. Cauchy applied to the source alone in (10) bounds all such fixed-order derivatives by $C_\tau e^{N(\Phi_D-\gamma)}$. On the real cube the Gaussian has modulus one, and its $k$th derivative in coordinate $i$ is bounded by $C_k(1+N|n_i|)^k$. Thus $$ |J_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}| \leq C_{D,\tau,R}\left(\prod_i(1+|n_i|)^3\right) e^{N(\Phi_D-\gamma)}\prod_i|\ell_i|^{-3}.\tag{13} $$ The derivative cost $N^{3R}$ has canceled the integration-by-parts denominator. No Gaussian growth on the complex strip is used. The entire sector stays on the original whole real cube. The original charge weights have modulus $\prod_i|\ell_i|$; the parity and original framing scalar have modulus one. Since $\sum_{\ell\ne0}|\ell|^{-2}=\pi^2/3$, the complete charge sum is absolutely bounded by $$ |I_{N,\mathbf n;\,\mathrm{diag}\ I,\,\mathrm{CROSS\ elsewhere}}| \leq C_D\left(\prod_i(1+|n_i|)^3\right)e^{N(\Phi_D-\gamma)}.\tag{14} $$ This includes all charges and the actual second-derivative currents. It is not a sharp-cube localization or separately divergent inside/outside charge sum. Multilinearity of the finite source and fixed-level absolute Fourier convergence justify taking this polynomial sector; (13) additionally proves its uniform summability. There are finitely many diagonal/CROSS sectors for fixed $D$, so the same conclusion with a smaller gap holds for their union. For sufficiently long fixed independent signed twists, the proved local unit-charge filling rate exceeds $\Phi_D-\gamma/2$. Equation (14) is exponentially smaller than that nonzero local contribution. Constants may grow polynomially with the fixed powers; no joint growing-power/level asymptotic is claimed. The first case of Section 3, where other full ports are controlled only near $-2$, does not automatically have this whole-period conclusion. Equation (14) explicitly uses the global CROSS bound at every other port. ## 5. Remaining scope and verification The result is compatible with failure of a global coefficientwise endpoint bound for the full numerator. That failure already occurs at $\sigma=\sqrt3$ for a genuinely one-sided path with positive outer exponent, not for (1). Such a remote moving port is not covered by (9) or a small spectral neighborhood in (6). The [short-moving extension](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_global_short_moving_spectral_sector_gap.md) treats a separate small outer-degree corridor; it does not exhaust macroscopic one-sided paths. The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_global_diagonal_spectral_sector_gap.py) and [recorded results](../experiments/actual_global_diagonal_spectral_sector_gap_results.json) retain the exact finite source. The finite audit checks zero-step and divided-Chebyshev formulas, removable node values, parity sectors and marked sector polynomials. Its four nonzero fixtures include whole-interval three-integration-by-parts identities with nonzero second-derivative endpoint currents. These checks supplement the entropy and infinite-charge proofs.

Put $$ T_c^-=\sqrt{c^2z-cA+P},\qquad H_c=2cz-A+2\sqrt z\,T_c^-. $$ On the strict branch $c>L_{\mathrm{end}}$, the exact derivative is $$ J_c'(\delta)=-\log rac{H_c}{\sqrt D}.	ag{9} $$ A direct normalization proof avoids guessing a complex sheet. The diagonal and terminal candidates were already bounded in Section 2. At $\delta=0$, their known maximization attains (3), proving the envelope identity. The proof extends to $b=0$ by its sole-start limit and to $xy=0$ by the exact first-order recurrence and displayed formulas; $A$ stays positive. All face phases and the final spectral cap The [exact continuous-real positivity lemma](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_continuous_real_tail_coefficient_positivity.md) supplies a finite strengthening. The identity $$ \alpha_{j-1}+s_js_{j-1} =4\cos^2(\pi\delta)-4\sin^2\!\left( rac\pi{2N}ight)	ag{12} $$ is independent of $j$. Thus $ eta_j\geq-1$ for $|\delta|\leq1/2-1/(2N)$, equivalently $\sigma\in[-2,2\cos(\pi/N)]$. Induction using $$ Q_r-xQ_{r-1} =y[Q_{r-1}-xQ_{r-2}]+(1+ eta_j)xyQ_{r-2} $$ proves coefficientwise nonnegativity on this entire interval. The initial values are $Q_0=1$, $Q_1=x+y$. Arbitrary phases of $x,y$ therefore have modulus bounded by the same $K$ at their positive moduli. In (1), taking absolute values of $b,c$ and of the retained scalar prefix and suffix factors reduces all face phases to the same envelope (2). No one-sided angular gap or absolute-value replacement inside the signed recurrence is used. The remaining real spectral cap $[2\cos(\pi/N),2]$ has width $O(N^{-2})$. For a polynomial $p$ of degree at most $d$ bounded by $M$ on $[-2,b_N]$, $b_N=2\cos(\pi/N)$, the exterior-circle maximum principle gives $$ |p(2)|\leq M\exp\!\left[d\,\operatorname{arcosh} rac{6-b_N}{b_N+2}ight] \leq CM. $$ The same bound holds throughout the cap; its exponent is $O(1)$ uniformly in $N\geq3$. Apply it to the actual LEFT polynomial at each fixed face-phase tuple. Thus (3) bounds the global real-spectral weighted absolute value at arbitrary face phases. The RIGHT version follows by reversing the original row and middle orientation. Applying the same polynomial argument on the full real interval extends the bound to a fixed complex $\delta$ strip, at additional cost $e^{2\pi d|\operatorname{Im}\delta|}$, uniformly in those face phases. This is still not coefficientwise domination: the known $\sigma=\sqrt3$ individual-coefficient counterexample is compatible with summing at fixed moduli. Nor may the actual shared coefficient be replaced by an unproved infimum of sums of local maxima. At fixed moduli the weighted full upper rate is bounded by $$ \max\{Q_b(0)+Q_c(0),\log b,\log c\}, $$ because $Q_b(0)\geq	frac12\log b$, $Q_c(0)\geq	frac12\log c$, and a geometric mean never exceeds the larger endpoint. Zero-middle terms are interpreted by the exact vanishing statements above. A [strict complete-radius balance condition](../papers/planar-certificates/README.md) permits a shared-source application; no general capacity equality follows here. ## Validation and scope The recurrence is used only from its second step. This is a weighted local theorem, not a coefficientwise comparison or a shared capacity equality.

title: The actual primitive Hilbert-90 gauge has a dilogarithm action and exponential norm
text: # The actual primitive Hilbert-90 gauge has a dilogarithm action and exponential norm 27 October 2026. The explicit cyclic source gauge in [the actual Fourier twisted-trace theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_source_fourier_twisted_traces.md) has a rigorously computable exponential scale, even in the flat right-regular metric. This is an ACTUAL gauge from the original source construction, not an arbitrary central rescaling of a state. It proves why solving its norm-one transport equation does not by itself give a subexponential comparison to a geometric period. The result also identifies a concrete dilogarithm action of this source gauge on a regular chart. It does not identify that chart with the marked geometric A-component or its Bloch regulator. ## 1. The specified actual gauge Let q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, h=2pi*i/N and z^N=0. The primitive k=1 source sector has the unique scalar-polynomial gauge with constant term one g_N(z)=v_N(z)v_N(Qz) =[u_N(z)u_N(Qz)]^-1, (1) u_N(z)=sum_(a=0)^(N-1) z^a/(Q;Q)_a, v_N=u_N^-1 in the nilpotent algebra. It solves g_N(Qz)/g_N(z)=1/[(1-z)(1-Qz)], eliminating the corresponding inner twist of the source automorphism. The constant-term and transport equation make it unique: a quotient of two gauges would be Q-invariant, hence constant in degree<N. The full matrix comparison can have other choices; no uniqueness claim for all matrix gauges is made. The CANONICAL polynomial representative of (1), of degree<N, is exactly the Taylor polynomial through degree N-1 of exp(L_N(z)), where L_N(z)=sum_(a=1)^(N-1) (1+Q^a) z^a/[a(Q^a-1)] =-i sum_(a=1)^(N-1) cot(pi*a/N) z^a/a. (2) Indeed the logarithm of v_N in the nilpotent algebra is sum z^a/[a(Q^a-1)]. Adding its shifted logarithm gives (2). This establishes the relation to the ACTUAL finite gauge before using analytic estimates. It is not an unproved resummation of quantum jets. ## 2. Uniform asymptotics of the actual polynomial on a fixed disk For |z|<=1/4 one has, uniformly as N grows, g_N(z)=exp[(2/h) Li_2(z)+O(1/N)]. (3) The same statement with the opposite sign holds for the canonical degree-<N representative of g_N^-1. In particular these finite polynomials have no zero on that disk for all sufficiently large N. Here is a proof that retains the truncation error. First, on every fixed disk |z|<=rho<1, L_N(z)=(2/h)Li_2(z)+O(1/N). (4) For a<=N/2 use the uniform elementary estimate cot(t)=1/t+O(t) on 0<t<=pi/2. Dividing its error by a gives O(1/N) per coefficient, whose sum against rho^a remains O(1/N). For a>N/2, the inequality |cot(pi*a/N)| <= N/[2 min(a,N-a)] gives a tail O(rho^(N/2) log N), and the omitted tail of Li_2 is smaller. This proves (4) with both root endpoints accounted for. Put G_N=exp(L_N) as an ordinary analytic function. On |z|=1/2, the coarser |cot(pi*a/N)|<=N/2 gives |L_N(z)| <= (N/2)log 2, |G_N(z)| <= exp[(N/2)log 2]. Cauchy's coefficient bound and the degree-N Taylor tail therefore give, throughout |z|<=1/4, |G_N(z)-g_N(z)| <= 2 exp[-(N/2)log 2]. (5) Meanwhile (4) gives |G_N(z)| >= exp[-N Li_2(1/4)/pi-O(1/N)]. For example Li_2(1/4)<=13/48, so Li_2(1/4)/pi is strictly smaller than log(2)/2. Thus (5) is exponentially small RELATIVE to G_N on the entire disk. Combining it with (4) proves (3) for the actual canonical polynomial. Replacing L_N by -L_N proves the inverse statement by the identical estimate. The Taylor-tail estimate is essential. Nilpotent equality alone would not justify evaluating its analytic exponential away from zero, as the nonzero endpoint carry in [the meridian half-step theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_euler_meridian_half_step.md) explicitly demonstrates. ## 3. A positive exponential lower bound for this comparison gauge Take w=i/4 and set c=Im Li_2(i/4)/pi > 0. The alternating power series proves Im Li_2(i/4) >= 1/4-(1/4)^3/9=143/576. Equation (3) gives the precise scalar-gauge rate log|g_N(i/4)|=c N+O(1/N). (6) To pass from this polynomial value to an ACTUAL finite operator, use the flat right-regular basis f^a e_j. The operator R_f is a truncated shift with unit coefficients. For |x|=1, its argument xR_f has norm one, and the powers applied to a degree-zero basis vector are orthogonal. If g_N(z)=sum c_a z^a, this gives ||g_N(xR_f)|| >= (sum |c_a|^2)^(1/2) >= sqrt(15/16)|g_N(i/4)|. (7) The second inequality is just Cauchy--Schwarz for evaluation at |w|=1/4. Multiplication by x^a changes no coefficient norm. Thus this specified comparison gauge has exponential operator growth, with liminf N^-1 log||g_N(xR_f)||>=c. Applying the inverse version of (3) at -i/4 proves the same lower bound for its inverse. Its condition number therefore has liminf logarithmic rate at least 2c. All these operators are unipotent: their diagonal entries and determinants are one. The source transport is cyclic and obeys its exact norm-one equation. Those algebraic facts coexist with the exponential norm in (7). This result concerns the flat coefficient metric. A nonunitary physical fusion change requires its own metric comparison. ## 4. Implication for the intended torsor proof The primitive source transport is explicitly SOLVED at each level, and its gauge action is the specified dilogarithm in (3). Its comparison is not tempered. A proof may carry this action into the marked regulator rather than try to discard the gauge as a normalization. Which combination of actions and source sectors is selected by the original knot word remains to be proved. This establishes neither a counterexample to the volume conjecture nor an exponential estimate for the knot invariant. The number c above is a gauge-chart value, not a knot's hyperbolic volume. It does not rule out a different whole comparison with controlled norm. It does rule out inferring such control for this actual primitive gauge solely from Hilbert 90, finite cyclicity, unipotence or determinant one. The rigorous uniform normal-form estimate (3) is the new local period/action comparison here. The nonzero selected geometric image and global sector/cancellation estimates remain open. Subsequent direct source calculations now distinguish that operator norm from selected local periods. The [canonical resonant endpoint](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_primitive_gauge_resonant_endpoint.md) is an explicit Gauss period of size N^-1/2. The [normalized top-coefficient period](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_gauge_period_selects_algebraic_point.md) selects the algebraic point 2 on fixed polynomial observables and intertwines fixed ordered gauge meridian steps. Thus this specified source has an evaluated local leading period, not just an exponential operator estimate. Its full knot-word coupling and selected hyperbolic action remain unproved. [The high-precision diagnostic](../experiments/audit_actual_hilbert90_gauge_action.py) and [saved output](../experiments/actual_hilbert90_gauge_action_results.json) compare the literal finite v_N(z)v_N(Qz) polynomial with exp(L_N) and its dilogarithm action. The theorem rests on the uniform proof above; numerical rate samples are not used as a proof.

title: Analytic transport through a regular modulus crossing
text: # Analytic transport through a regular modulus crossing 28 October 2026. This gives a local marked-action upper bound for a holomorphic recurrence at a modulus crossing where its eigenvalues are DISTINCT and nonzero. The proof constructs an exponentially accurate diagonal form by elementary matrix identities and Cauchy estimates. It needs no exact solution, source overlap, formal WKB summation theorem or pointwise dominance assumption. The sufficient condition compares a COMPUTABLE analytic remainder barrier with the width of the marked classical actions. It always holds on a sufficiently short regular crossing window. Extending it over a whole knot orbit still requires a global action-barrier comparison; mere single-valued calibration of an action does not prove that. Actual real ramification and singular leading coefficients are outside this local theorem. ## 1. Explicit analytic data Write epsilon=1/N and x_(j+1)=x_j+epsilon on a fixed real interval I. Let U_R denote its complex stadium of radius R. Suppose T_N and T_0 are holomorphic on U_(2R), uniformly bounded, and ||T_N-T_0||_(U_(2R))<=C_0 epsilon. (1) Assume T_0 has a supplied holomorphic eigenbasis V_0 there: V_0^(-1)T_0V_0=D_0=diag(lambda_1,...,lambda_d), ||V_0||,||V_0^(-1)||<=K, |lambda_i|>=m>0, |lambda_i-lambda_k|>=delta>0. (2) These are bounds on specified coefficient functions. For a classical companion, V_0 has columns (1,lambda_i,...,lambda_i^(d-1))^t, so all data are directly checkable on its normalized spectral branches. An actual recurrence as in [the whole-source spectral theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_macroscopic_a_spectral_upper_bound.md) satisfies (1) on any such regular fixed domain, uniformly on its small complex-q source circle. An unverified classical polynomial alone does not supply that actual quantum premise. After the exact change by V_0, put B_N(z)=V_0(z+epsilon)^(-1)T_N(z)V_0(z). Cauchy's estimate gives B_N=D_0+O(epsilon) on U_R. Initially set D=diag B_N, R_N=B_N-D. The diagonal gap is at least 3delta/4 for large N and ||R_N||<=C epsilon. All constants below are uniform. ## 2. Exponentially accurate diagonalization, with its proof There are explicitly bounded constants sigma>0,C and holomorphic V_N,D_N,R_N on U_(R/2), with D_N diagonal, such that EXACTLY V_N(z+epsilon)^(-1)T_N(z)V_N(z)=D_N(z)+R_N(z), ||V_N-V_0||+||V_N^(-1)-V_0^(-1)||<=C epsilon, ||D_N-D_0||<=C epsilon, ||R_N||<=C exp(-sigma N). (3) The shifted identity is asserted where both z and z+epsilon belong to that neighborhood; this includes every real step across I. The one-dimensional case has no off-diagonal part and is immediate. Here is a constructive proof with quantitative constants. Maintain ||D||<=M and diagonal gap g=delta/2; take M larger than twice the initial diagonal bound. If R is off diagonal with norm eta, solve [D,X]=-R, diag X=0, X_(ik)=-R_(ik)/(D_(ii)-D_(kk)), ||X||<=a eta, a=d/g. On a stadium narrowed by Delta>=2epsilon, Cauchy gives ||X(z+epsilon)-X(z)||<=2a eta epsilon/Delta. With X^+=X(z+epsilon), (I+X^+)^(-1)(D+R)(I+X)=D+F, F=(I+X^+)^(-1)[(X-X^+)D+R X]. (4) This is an exact identity. If a eta<=1/2, its new off-diagonal norm is bounded by eta_new <=[8Ma epsilon/Delta+4a eta] eta. (5) Its diagonal change is O(eta^2). To see the latter without losing a derivative, (X-X^+)D is off diagonal. Its contribution to diag F therefore requires the extra factor (I+X^+)^(-1)-I=O(eta). The other term RX already has size O(eta^2). Choose a fixed c<=min(R/8,R/(128Ma)), p=floor(cN), Delta=R/(2p). For sufficiently large N the starting eta is at most 1/(32a). Equation (5) then decreases eta at least by a factor 1/2 at EVERY step. The accumulated diagonal change is O(sum eta^2)=O(epsilon^2), so the stated bound M and gap g persist. The p domain losses total R/2 and Delta>=4epsilon, so all exact shifts are legitimate. The basis is the product of I+X at each step. Since sum ||X||<=2a eta_0=O(epsilon), it and its inverse are I+O(epsilon). The final off-diagonal is O(epsilon*2^(-p)). For example one may use sigma=(c log 2)/2. (6) All bounds are derived from (1)--(2), not an unknown solution. They are conservative, not optimal conversion exponents. The same construction is holomorphic in additional parameters wherever those uniform premises hold, including the actual tiny complex-q circle. ## 3. A checkable action-width criterion Normalize the real marked actions at the left endpoint a of I: A_i(x)=integral_a^x log|lambda_i(t)| dt, W=max_(x in I)[max_i A_i(x)-min_i A_i(x)]. (7) Suppose W<sigma. Then the EXACT product P_N of T_N across I satisfies limsup (1/N)log||P_N||<=max_i A_i(b), (8) where b is its right endpoint. Every specified input and output with subexponential norms has the same upper bound. This is a product bound, not merely a prediction from formal critical points. Proof. Let d_(i,j) be the diagonal entries of the actual D_N(x_j), and put G_0=I, G_(j+1)=D_N(x_j)G_j, all diagonal. Uniformly in j, log |(G_j)_(ii)|=N A_i(x_j)+O(1), (9) by (3), nonvanishing in (2), and the ordinary uniform Riemann estimate. The remaining EXACT recurrence after G_j has factors I+E_j, E_j=G_(j+1)^(-1)R_N(x_j)G_j. Equations (3), (7), and (9) give ||E_j||<=C exp[-N(sigma-W)]. There are O(N) steps, so their product is I+O(N exp[-N(sigma-W)]). Consequently P_N=V_N(b) G_n [I+O(N exp[-N(sigma-W)])] V_N(a)^(-1). This proves (8) and gives an exponentially small relative matrix remainder after the explicitly marked diagonal propagation. The exponential anisotropy of G_j is RETAINED and estimated by W; it is not asserted to be a tame positive full-space metric. In fact the same proof pins down the WHOLE singular-value vector. Let A_(1)(b)>=...>=A_(d)(b) be the sorted endpoint actions. Under the stated barrier, bounded invertible endpoint frames and the I+o(1) middle factor give, for every k, log sigma_k(P_N)=N A_(k)(b)+O(1). (9a) Use the elementary singular-value inequalities for multiplication by a bounded invertible matrix on both sides of the diagonal G_n. Thus all partial sums satisfy the corresponding asymptotic log-majorization, and every fixed continuous convex function of the normalized log singular values has the endpoint-action limit. This conditional pinching is stronger than a convexity estimate. It does not make the barrier follow from Karamata, and does not prove a nonzero overlap for the selected scalar source. For finite N there is a more flexible certificate: construct (3) and the diagonal G_j, compute bounds e_j>=||G_(j+1)^(-1)R_NG_j||, and use ||P_N||<=||V_N(b)|| ||V_N(a)^(-1)|| max_i |(G_n)_(ii)| product_j(1+e_j). (10) Proving sum_j e_j=o(N) suffices. These quantities use only the explicitly constructed local diagonalizers and scalar diagonal products, not the unknown exact vector solution or its final scalar. ## 4. A distinct-root modulus crossing is locally harmless For two branches suppose |lambda_1(x_*)|=|lambda_2(x_*)|, while the eigenvalues themselves stay separated as in (2). On I=[x_*-ell,x_*+ell], let |d/dx log|lambda_1/lambda_2||<=L. Then |A_1(x)-A_2(x)|<=L ell^2 throughout I. Thus L ell^2<sigma is a sufficient condition for (8), even if the larger modulus switches at x_*. The bound applies also to distinct REAL roots of opposite sign. No positive real weights are introduced. The analytic data may be fixed on a neighborhood of x_* first; sigma is then independent of the shortened ell. Hence a sufficiently short crossing window always meets this condition. For more than two regular branches use W<=2ell max_(i,k) sup_I|log|lambda_i/lambda_k||. All quantities are checkable from a specified classical curve and actual analytic recurrence. For a simple root of F(x,L), partial_x Log lambda=-F_x/(lambda F_L), which bounds L. A calibrated Bloch/peripheral action may supply the A_i, but (7) still requires the explicit quantitative width comparison. This does not contradict the [Gaussian conversion example](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/analytic_two_channel_conversion_counterexample.md). On its whole interval the conversion has positive gain even though the complete branch actions vanish. Its global width cannot satisfy the sufficient barrier comparison. On a sufficiently short regular window the theorem gives precisely the local estimate (8). An exponentially small local conversion can still grow after a long external propagation; it cannot be discarded in later gluing. ### A verified action-coordinate radius can replace the Euclidean one The proof also works in a supplied univalent holomorphic coordinate w=zeta(z). Assume the transformed matrices and basis obey (1)--(2) on an action-plane neighborhood of radius R_w, and the EXACT shifted coordinate map f_epsilon(w)=zeta(zeta^(-1)(w)+epsilon) is holomorphic there with |f_epsilon(w)-w|<=V epsilon. In (4) set X^+=X(f_epsilon(w)). Cauchy's estimate changes (5) only by replacing epsilon/Delta with V epsilon/Delta. Hence one may use c<=min(R_w/(8V),R_w/(128MaV)), sigma=c log2/2. (11) The actual sampled recurrence and the real actions (7) are unchanged; no continuum substitution for a discrete step is made. This follows from a verified analytic coordinate and shift map, not a formal replacement of the independent variable. At a distinct-root crossing, an appropriately marked zeta(z)=integral Log(lambda_i/lambda_k) dz has nonzero derivative unless that MARKED logarithm vanishes. It is therefore a valid local coordinate on a sufficiently small domain. Its analytic inverse may be bounded by excluding its actual action-plane critical values and singularities. This gives a CHECKABLE action-domain version of the remainder barrier. It does not identify the optimal barrier with the nearest calibrated collision action, or show that a zero regulator jump implies the global width inequality. Those stronger connection statements are still unproved. ## 5. What finite gluing additionally requires On overlapping regular domains with the SAME marked V_0 and the same iteration (4), two truncation depths give compatible frames: their ratio is I+O(exp[-min(sigma_1,sigma_2)N]) on a smaller overlap. Indeed their factors are literally the same up to the smaller depth; every additional X is already exponentially small there. This proves an actual overlap statement without choosing an unspecified exact WKB solution. It does NOT justify resetting every local action to zero and then freely splicing its best endpoint. In global action coordinates, each off-diagonal error and overlap correction acquires its FULL factor exp[N(A_k-A_i)]. A sufficient finite-gluing condition is a strict positive margin between each domain's exponential remainder barrier and those globally calibrated action differences, including the overlap locations. More flexibly, one may verify the weighted finite-N certificate (10) on the full assembled blocks. Across genuine spectral ramification V_0 and its inverse need not be bounded, so (1)--(6) no longer apply. Equality of absolutely calibrated regulator values at a ramification point is useful geometric information, but does not itself prove a quantum connection estimate. An action-coordinate refinement controlling that connection, rather than the conservative Euclidean sigma, remains necessary for the proposed general endpoint theorem. Thus the proved local result is (3)--(8), including regular modulus crossings and an explicit analytic barrier. No general two-bridge or whole-knot geometric bound is claimed until the actual operator, boundary source and global conversion margins are verified. The original-source Cauchy recovery remains exactly that of the macroscopic spectral theorem. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_local_analytic_transport.py) checks the exact iterative identity, separated-root contraction, bounded frame and weighted product reconstruction on analytic model matrices. These are supplementary checks, not an actual quantum-operator or global ramification calculation.

title: Independently long fillings of signed octahedral belt stacks
text: # Independently long fillings of signed octahedral belt stacks 29 October 2026. This note assembles the quantum, peripheral, regulator and geometric inputs for the stated theorem. ## 1. The actual family and statement Fix n>=1, a word epsilon of length n in {+,-}, and an integer a. Use the two literal mirror/reversed pieces D_+,D_- of the [octahedral stack construction](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_balanced_octahedral_belt_stack_volume.md), with ONE retained outer complete circle and the actual outer R^a. Denote this ACTUAL augmented link by B_(epsilon,a). It has n inner crossing circles and one outer belt. Its complement is complete hyperbolic of volume2n v8, by its exact regular-cell/collar proof. Choose ANY subset I of those n+1 auxiliary circles. For each i in I use its preferred meridian and crossing-disk longitude to fill the primitive slope mu_i+p_i lambda_i, for fixed nonzero integers p_i. Equivalently perform the literal1/p_i surgery/full-twist substitution in the original oriented diagram. Circles outside I remain components with their literal color N/L_N; this is NOT p_j=0, which would meridionally fill and remove them. Denote the resulting link in S^3 by J_(epsilon,a,I)(p). There is a source-dependent finite P such that, whenever min_(i in I) |p_i|>P, the actual filled complement is hyperbolic and its original single-cut reduced Kashaev evaluation satisfies lim_(N->infinity) (2pi/N)log|K_N(J_(epsilon,a,I)(p))| =Vol(S^3 minus J_(epsilon,a,I)(p)). (1) For I empty this is the already proved COMPLETE stack theorem, with no filling threshold. For nonempty I the threshold may depend on I; for a fixed stack take the maximum over its finitely many subsets if desired. The limits include every parity and composite level. The slopes may have independent signs and arbitrarily unequal lengths. They are fixed before N tends to infinity. No numerical value of P, uniformity as n or a grows with N, or arbitrary branched-graph theorem is claimed. Full twists preserve the main permutation. When ALL n+1 circles are filled, J is a KNOT for odd a and has TWO components for even a. For a proper subset its unfilled auxiliary circles remain: the total is n+2-|I| for odd a and n+3-|I| for even a. ## 2. Whole original quantum source, not a formal critical value The exact color expansion inserts every R^(-2p_i) using the original ordinary mixed circles L_j and the complete Hermite filling coefficients. It retains the marked cut, original pivot, full half-Cartan and all dimension endpoints. Coefficient mass is polynomial for each fixed slope. No closed auxiliary component is assigned an extra modified dimension. The [inner auxiliary-color theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_belt_stack_auxiliary_color_inner_packet.md) proves source-fixed nonzero analytic packets through the quarter- index transition, for the ACTUAL colors j_i=N-h_i. Its exact finite factorial completion agrees with the actual physical low core on the grid, with a quantitatively retained exponential replacement error in a faithful norm containing every first Casimir normal. The nonzero RP band and the ENTIRE physical inner-color complement have strict gaps, for every fixed n>=1. The [outer squared-kernel theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_outer_color_squared_kernel.md) retains the actual full-Hermite outer ordinary color. Its exact double-pole kernel kills the dangerous false h≈N Fourier alias; it proves the remaining outer-color complement gap, together with a fixed-complex-neighborhood, separately even packet for ALL n+1 circle colors. This is not a spectral eta=meridian guess. Write p and q for the numbers of plus and minus pieces and m=q-p+a. In x_i=h_i/N its local source action has phi(x)=n v8/pi - pi x_0^2/[n-im] +(pi/2)sum_(i=1)^n(-1+i sigma_i)x_i^2+O_4, sigma_i=+1 for z, -1 for z^sharp. The real quadratic part is strictly negative in every color. The ENTIRE source cube complement is gapped, not just the individual box coefficients. Thus the hypotheses of the [general original-source long-filling transfer](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/general_original_source_long_filling_transfer.md) hold. Restrict every unfilled color literally to h_j=0/L_N and apply only the original filling functionals indexed by I. The exact complex packet, nonzero amplitude, negative real Hessian and entire-cube complement gap restrict to these coordinates. It proves a NONZERO full-source asymptotic, and the selected point tends to the complete source point as min_(i in I)|p_i|->infinity. The empty subset instead uses the already proved nonzero complete-stack asymptotic directly. Fixed normal jets, endpoint currents and all nonleading charge sectors are controlled by that proof before its conclusion. ## 3. The selected point is an actual marked representation The [typed character composition](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_belt_stack_typed_character_composition.md) supplies the group/flag lift which is essential after the source estimate. Its input is the source-selected internal critical root, not an arbitrary branch of a trace polynomial. The local pair matrices a,b,A=ba remain bounded and irreducible through A's parabolic trace -2. The selected inner box, its sharp type and every actual bare R interface satisfy their literal threaded Hurwitz equations and ordinary-pivot flag conditions. At the outer seam, TWO original nested main-head snakes reverse dual tensor order and invert the main meridian paths. Every incident mixed crossing is transported through the SAME original Hopf duality, including its full Cartan and nilpotent factors. The auxiliary cut/pivot and unrestricted marked co-source stay on their original side. This proves the actual outer disk word P_0=A^(-1), not a word selected from a matching cusp derivative. Irreducibility uniquely gives C_0=K_tot at closure. All complete white and BOTH inner shaded face maps match the regular octahedron certificate, as full three-vertex maps. The actual signed pants collars and outer R^a match too. The outer generator is then uniquely forced by closure to be the geometric one. Consequently the ENTIRE complete representation is the positively oriented holonomy of the ACTUAL B_(epsilon,a), not only a representation with matching flags, trace coordinates or Hessian. Let z_i=Log H_i and G be the actual logarithmic source primitive, with its real Cartan/spin constant retained. The preferred flagged peripheral data at ALL n+1 auxiliary circles are exactly M_i=exp(-z_i/2), lambda_i=-exp(-ell_i), ell_i=partial_(z_i)G. (2) For the outer circle ell_0=eta=Log(-w). The preferred minus sign is fixed by the original ordinary pivot and the disk framing. Simultaneously inverting both generators and swapping their common flag is equivalent; inverting only one is not. All surviving main meridians are noncentral parabolic, so BOTH small logs at each unfilled main cusp are zero, including the merged odd-a cusp. ## 4. The source action is the absolute regulator Keep the spin term in Gbar=G-pi i sum z_i. The actual source and preferred peripheral data give u_i=-z_i/2, v_i=pi i-ell_i, dGbar=2 sum_i v_i du_i, D_src=Im G-sum_i Re z_i Im ell_i. (3) The developed fundamental chain for the SAME marked representation has Bloch boundary -2 sum M_i wedge lambda_i. Its elementary Bloch--Wigner differential equals dD_src, including its factor2. Both sides have complete value2n v8 by the full geometric anchor. They therefore agree on the connected selected germ. No equality of an unproved transformed dilogarithm list is assumed. The exact source filling equations are z_i+2p_i ell_i=2pi i m_i, m_i=+1 or -1, i in I, z_j=0, j not in I. (4) Separate exact evenness gives ell_j=0 for every unfilled auxiliary coordinate, even as all the other colors vary. Its actual peripheral group remains noncentral parabolic near completeness. Its kept quadratic chirp is sum_(i in I)(z_i-2pi i m_i)^2/(4p_i). On(4) its imaginary part equals -sum_i Re z_i Im ell_i. Hence the imaginary FULL filled source action is exactly the marked representation volume D_src. This establishes the volume normalization, not just a numerical quadratic/cusp comparison. ## 5. Primitive completion supplies equality with hyperbolic volume The small geometric squared-eigenvalue logs are U_i=-z_i, V_i=-2ell_i, U_i+p_i V_i=-2pi i m_i, i in I, U_j=V_j=0, j not in I. (5) Thus the filled slope has its actual primitive2pi angular period. The preferred SL longitude sign in(2) is kept before passing to these small geometric logs. A mere exponentiated PSL identity would not establish this unit winding. The actual selected representations and peripheral flags tend to the now identified complete geometric ones as the chosen slopes become independently long. For each filled coordinate separate evenness implies ell_i divisible by z_i, so z_i=0 would contradict (4). The full geometric completion theorem therefore applies to these source-selected representations. Its explicit logarithmic torus/tube construction adds a smooth core at each primitive slope, with no missing axis sheet. The compact core and every unfilled main AND auxiliary cusp remain positive and complete. This constructs the COMPLETE hyperbolic metric on the actual filled topology; it is not merely a nearby incomplete metric. The oriented fundamental class and the two-way Gromov-volume comparison identify its regulator with the actual hyperbolic volume. Combining this with the NONZERO whole-source asymptotic and (3)--(4) proves(1). ## 6. Scope ledger The theorem expands a cyclic one-belt source family. It does not assert an arbitrary six-port tensor estimate, arbitrary branched augmentation, or the volume conjecture for every fixed bridge number. For partial filling, every unfilled color remains the literal L_N. Its two geometric logarithms vanish by exact separate evenness, and primitive completion leaves that cusp complete.
