The original generic identity remains `D_a^-1 p_a(Omega)` before every normal extraction; at root `D_a=1`, and its fixed scalar generic jets have the already proved polynomial relative bound on compact real targets below -2. No generic normal is replaced by a root derivative. Equation (11) is a comparison at the actual classical critical point. The algebraic ordinary-column character map is valid on its regular complex channel chart, but the existing ordinary-column ASYMPTOTIC theorem keeps that channel real and discrete. This note does not extend that theorem to (4). Nor does scalar convergence in (7) establish the action of the degree-O(N) polynomial p_a(Omega) on the complementary selected boundary state. Establishing that action, its actual phase, and its contribution to the original finite source remains necessary. In particular (9) is a scalar anchor, not a new proof that an assembled marked critical action equals the complement volume. Any such assembly must also retain the pivotal clock, original row and half-twist factors, native measures, shared wires, and the full physical normal already specified by the exact source identities. Audit: [actual inverse turn, ordered transport and scalar generating action](../experiments/audit_actual_matching_edge_polynomial_geometric_action.py). It proves four symbolic ordered-matrix identities, all four cyclic prefix identities, the exact eigenratio and parabolic normalization, and the rational Cayley identity fixing the sign. Five further symbolic identities check the generic target pair and its original-input trace relation. At 90 digits it checks three independent action integrals, twelve actual source-polynomial actions and first derivatives, four endpoint second derivatives, and twelve general-input scalar derivatives and character equations, at both level parities. No operator or network asymptotic is tested. The action uses the stated analytic c>1 continuation without claiming that it is realized by a complete geometric rectangle. No polynomial-operator substitution or source-cycle contribution follows.

title: A positive tail-free Racah scalar at one actual matching edge
status: All-target positive scalar; fixed generic jets
text: # A positive tail-free Racah scalar at one actual matching edge 30 October 2026. This is a specialization of the actual generic four-port coefficient theorem to the two halves of ONE crossing-circle matching edge. Its four outside objects are all the original physical V_(N-1). The scalar is positive after the retained single root zero is removed, including every new high recoupling channel and both level parities. All fixed generic scalar jets have polynomial relative cost. Each full recoupled tensor term has at most one pole, so its first normal needs Taylor order two after clearing that pole. This theorem controls the explicitly stated scalar and Laurent budget. It does not estimate the native boundary change-of-frame costs, the completed Hermite operator, or the surrounding coherent contraction. ## 1. The full actual channel range is uniformly saturated Put d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), and fix 0<=a<=floor(d/2), (A,B,C,D)=(d,d,d,d), E=2a, G=2g, 0<=g<=d. (1) The G range in (1) is the ENTIRE generic four-port recoupling range. No high partner is discarded. These are the four-port highest-weight conventions of [the actual coefficient theorem](actual_general_four_port_single_racah_kernel.md). The corresponding six spins are (d/2,d/2,d/2,d/2,a,g). Its faces and opposite sums are F=(d+a,d+a,d+g,d+g), Q=(2d,d+a+g,d+a+g). (2) Every face is at least d, and all its triangle deficits are among k,k,d-k for k=a or g. They lie in [0,d]. All four faces and three opposite sums are INTEGERS, also when N is even and the four physical spins d/2 are half-integral. Consequently the true Racah range is d+max(a,g)<=z<=min(2d,d+a+g), (3) and all seven denominator factorial indices are in [0,d]. Every numerator [z+1]! contains exactly one [N] and contains NO [2N]. Thus this special physical block is tail-free even when g>d/2. This is not a claim that arbitrary high recoupling partners are tail-free. For the genuine generic symmetric factorial at zeta define S_ag(zeta)=sum_(z in (3)) (-1)^z [z+1]! / ([z-d-a]!^2 [z-d-g]!^2 [2d-z]! [d+a+g-z]!^2), G_ag(zeta)=(-1)^d S_ag(zeta)/[N]_zeta. (4) The division in (4) is performed in every original summand before root specialization. It is an analytic germ at q, not a derivative of a root-only replacement. ## 2. An exact positive squared-trinomial formula Set s_k=product_(v=1)^k 2sin(pi v/N), s_0=1. The elementary identity s_(d-k)=N/s_k gives the explicit root scalar R_N(a,g)=G_ag(q) =sum_(r=max(0,a-g))^(min(a,d-g)) [s_(g+r)/(s_(g+r-a)s_r s_(a-r))]^2 >0. (5) To verify every factor, put k=z-d. The removed-numerator formula is N sum_k s_k / [s_(k-a)^2 s_(k-g)^2 s_(d-k) s_(a+g-k)^2]. Replace s_(d-k) by N/s_k and then set r=k-g. All indices in (5) are between 0 and d. The signs of the factors [N+1],...,[z+1] combine with (-1)^(d+z) to give +1. No half-spin phase was omitted: A+B+C+D+E+G=4d+2a+2g is even. The full high partner has the SAME root scalar: R_N(a,g)=R_N(a,d-g). (6) This is termwise: replace g by d-g and r by a-r, and use s_(d-k)=N/s_k in the numerator/first-denominator ratio. The actual ranges in (5) are carried onto one another. Equation (6) is proved at both parities and does not discard any generic normal. The face metric is especially simple. For a face (d/2,d/2,k), put Delta_k^2=[k]!^2[d-k]!/[d+k+1]!, D_k(zeta)=(-1)^k [N]_zeta Delta_k^2. (7) All D_k are analytic and nonzero at q, and D_k(q)=s_k s_(d-k)/N=1. (8) There are two faces of each kind k=a,g. The generic normalized scalar therefore has the single-valued form H_ag(zeta)=G_ag(zeta)D_a(zeta)D_g(zeta), H_ag(q)=R_N(a,g). (9) Its branch-independent identity is the exact actual scalar convention H_ag^2=[N]^2 S_ag^2 product_(four faces) Delta^2. (10) All powers and signs in (10) are the original ones. A scalar diagonal gauge relating (10) to the physical recoupling matrix is still required; root value 1 of the face factors alone does not make that matrix unitary. ## 3. Every fixed generic scalar jet has polynomial relative cost There are universal c,C>0 such that, for ALL labels in (1), on zeta=q exp(t), |t|<=c/[N^2(1+log N)], (11) G_ag/G_ag(q), D_a, D_g and H_ag/H_ag(q) are holomorphic and remain in a fixed small disk about 1. In particular they are nonzero. For every fixed m>=0 this implies |partial_t^m G_ag(0)|+|partial_t^m H_ag(0)| <=C_m [N^2(1+log N)]^m R_N(a,g). (12) The same relative estimate holds for their inverses. For clarity, the proof applies to the COMPLETE generic germ in (4). After the one [N] factor is canceled, each summand and each face metric is a quotient of factors zeta^u-zeta^(-u), 1<=u<2N, u!=N, with fixed factorial multiplicities. Its logarithmic change on (11) is bounded by C N^2(1+log N)|t|, using |sin(pi u/N)| bounded below by a constant times dist(u,NZ)/N and the finite harmonic sum. At the root every summand of G_ag is positive by (5). On a sufficiently small common disk these summands remain in one narrow sector, so their sum has the same uniform relative bound. Equations (7),(8) give it for D_a,D_g. Cauchy's estimate proves (12). This is the direct supported-scalar argument, with (2),(3) proving its hypotheses for the entire present range, including half-integral physical spins and high g. In particular no missing [2N]T normal survives here: such a numerator factor is absent from every term before differentiation. The result does not say that a normal equals the derivative of the positive root expression (5); (4) remains the differentiated source. ## 4. The actual physical coefficient has only a simple pole Let L_(2g,2a) be the actual inverse Racah coefficient, with its original pivotal turn and first-highest-entry-one Clebsch bases. The exact source formula is L_(2g,2a)=chi_E X_E/(b_G J_n S0 V_n) S_ag, n=d-g, S0=[2d+1]!/([d-a]!^2[a]!^2), V_n=zeta^n (Q^(-d-g-1);Q)_n / [(Q;Q)_n^2 (Q^(-2d-1);Q)_n], Q=zeta^2. (13) The four prefactors chi_E,X_E,b_G,J_n are root units. This follows from their actual boundary product formulas: E=2a<N; their physical endpoint factorial indices are all in [0,d]. No first-normal channel norm is divided out. S0 has exactly one root zero. The numerator of V_n has a single root zero exactly when 2g<d. (14) Indeed its negative exponents run from -(d+g+1) to -(2g+2), and the only possible root multiple is -N. Its denominator factors are all units: the negative product starts at -(2N-1) and has length d-g, ending strictly before -N. The two (Q;Q)_n factors have n<N. By the strict positivity in (5), S_ag has exactly one root zero. Thus the ACTUAL coefficient orders are ord_q L_(2g,2a)=-1 for 2g<d, ord_q L_(2g,2a)= 0 for 2g>=d. (15) This includes a=0 and all endpoints. It does not assert positivity or regularity of the uncompleted physical coefficient matrix. Let T_(2g) be the actual generic target invariant tensor. Its Clebsch entries have the regular canceled physical coproduct formulas; the only possible pole is the canonical intermediate cup, with denominator (Q;Q)_(2g). Hence T_(2g) is regular for 2g<N and has at most a simple pole for 2g>=N. These two ranges never overlap the pole range in (15). Consequently pole_order [L_(2g,2a) T_(2g)] <=1 (16) for EVERY channel and level parity. The fixed source tensor S_(2a) is regular, so the simple poles on the right of its exact recoupling identity cancel in their full sum. After multiplication by a local parameter t, each recoupled term is holomorphic. Its contribution to the first normal of the regular whole contraction is extracted from Taylor coefficient t^2. Thus this special block has a uniform first-normal budget TWO, improving the general all-port budget four. If a regular surrounding contraction is present, it must be included when extracting that coefficient; its derivatives are not discarded. ## 5. Relation to the geometric pair localization The [prescribed-facet corollary](actual_right_angled_selected_framing_obstruction.md) allows the two physical-support exceptions to be placed at the two halves of any chosen crossing-circle matching edge. Their four outside objects are then all V_d, so the present specialization applies regardless of the ribbon order of the other matching edges. A physical MAIN edge does not have that automatic property: its two channel legs can be adjacent instead of opposite in the actual cyclic order. The exact typed bend from the original W_a pi_a block to S_(2a), its fixed gamma factor, and the unchanged physical mark belong to the separate source interface. The normal must be extracted from the complete generic contraction, with all channels in (1) retained. Even after that interface, this is not a sharp completed block norm or a bound on the full source. Its scalar gauge factors can carry nontrivial boundary cost; the other local columns are not automatically in the central domain; and a global selected cycle and coherent bound remain necessary. The theorem makes the exceptional matching block an explicit tail-free scalar/finite-jet problem, without declaring those remaining tasks solved. Audit: [exact matching-edge scalar, original recoupling and normal budget](../experiments/audit_actual_matching_edge_racah_positive_scalar.py). It passes 21,772 support/phase/pole cases, ten independently reconstructed generic source tensor families with all 47 recoupling coefficients, 529 retained root germs, 1,257 termwise partner checks, and 1,058 exact face-unit jets. In 406 comparisons the partners have the same root value but DIFFERENT generic first derivatives. The audit retains that distinction; its finite cases test conventions, while the written harmonic-product argument proves the uniform jet bound. The positive scalar Racah model does not supply a norm for the native matrix source or control a whole source from root-face values.

title: The source-normalized Racah polynomial has all its zeros above two
status: Roots above two; selected scalar action
text: # The source-normalized Racah polynomial has all its zeros above two 30 October 2026. For EVERY folded original channel, the exact matching-edge Casimir polynomial has simple real zeros strictly greater than 2. A positive matrix factorization proves this, including maximal channels at both level parities. Its canonical logarithm and leading action consequently continue to the whole slit plane C minus [2,infinity), including every real geometric target below 2. No continuation of a finite target color g is required. This theorem concerns the actual scalar polynomial. It does not prove a relative amplitude, control moving-q normal derivatives, estimate the complementary tensor contraction, or select a global source cycle. ## 1. The exact original polynomial at the root Use the generic source identity proved in [the geometric target polynomial theorem](actual_matching_edge_geometric_target_polynomial.md). Its normalization is D_a G_ag D_g=p_a(lambda_g), lambda_g=zeta^(2g+1)+zeta^(-2g-1), with all generic source factors retained. Put q=exp(pi i/N), theta=pi/N, d=N-1, 0<=a<=M=floor(d/2), and specialize to q. Let s_k=product_(r=1)^k 2sin(r theta), and set lambda_r=2cos((2r+1)theta), phi_k(x)=product_(r=0)^(k-1)(lambda_r-x). The generic terminating formula becomes EXACTLY p_a(x)=sum_(k=0)^a c_(a,k) phi_k(x), c_(a,k)=s_(a+k)/(s_(a-k)s_k^4). (1) Indeed [d-r]=[r+1] and [d+r+2]=-[r+1] at q, so the generic alternating signs cancel. Also [g-r][g+r+1]=(lambda_r-lambda_g)/(4sin^2 theta), product_(r<k)(lambda_r-lambda_a)=s_(a+k)/s_(a-k). These identities yield (1) without changing the original spectral variable. In particular p_a(lambda_0)=1 and its leading coefficient is kappa_a=(-1)^a s_(2a)/s_a^4. (2) All displayed denominators are nonzero for 2a<N. For a=0 the polynomial is identically one. ## 2. An own three-term recurrence For 0<=n<M define A_n=-4sin^4((n+1)theta) /[sin((2n+1)theta)sin((2n+2)theta)], B_n=2/[cos(n theta)cos((n+1)theta)], C_n=-4sin^4(n theta)/[sin(2n theta)sin((2n+1)theta)], C_0=0. Then the finite polynomials (1) satisfy x p_n(x)=A_n p_(n+1)(x)+B_n p_n(x)+C_n p_(n-1)(x). (3) Here is a direct coefficient proof. Since x phi_k=lambda_k phi_k-phi_(k+1), the coefficient of phi_k on the left is lambda_k c_(n,k)-c_(n,k-1). The required ratios are c_(n+1,k)/c_(n,k)=sin((n+k+1)theta)/sin((n-k+1)theta), c_(n-1,k)/c_(n,k)=sin((n-k)theta)/sin((n+k)theta), c_(n,k-1)/c_(n,k) =4sin^4(k theta)/[sin((n+k)theta)sin((n-k+1)theta)]. (4) Substitution in (3), followed by the sine addition identities, gives equality. More explicitly the identity after division by c_(n,k) is lambda_k-4sin^4(k theta)/[sin((n+k)theta)sin((n-k+1)theta)] =A_n sin((n+k+1)theta)/sin((n-k+1)theta) +B_n+C_n sin((n-k)theta)/sin((n+k)theta). It is a rational identity in exp(i theta), exp(i n theta) and exp(i k theta); clearing its displayed denominators gives zero. The top coefficient k=n+1 is A_n=kappa_n/kappa_(n+1). The case n=0 follows directly from p_0 and p_1. Thus no presumed orthogonality or external q-Racah recurrence enters the proof. Set P_n=p_n/kappa_n, the monic polynomials. Equation (3) becomes P_(n+1)=(x-B_n)P_n-e_n^2 P_(n-1), e_n^2=A_(n-1)C_n =4sin^6(n theta) /[cos^2(n theta)sin((2n-1)theta)sin((2n+1)theta)]>0. (5) Consequently P_a(x)=det(xI-J_a), where J_a is the real symmetric Jacobi matrix with diagonal B_0,...,B_(a-1) and adjacent entries e_1,...,e_(a-1)>0. ## 3. The positive shift by two Let Dpos_a be the previously proved positive q-Hahn matrix; the distinct scalar face factor retains its original name D_a: (Dpos_a)_(n,n)=1/[cos(n theta)cos((n+1)theta)], (Dpos_a)_(n-1,n)=sqrt(beta_n), beta_n=sin^2(n theta) /[cos^2(n theta)sin((2n-1)theta)sin((2n+1)theta)]. For completeness, its leading principal minors are det Dpos_m=2^m product_(r=1)^m sin(r theta) /product_(r=m+1)^(2m)sin(r theta)>0. This finite formula was proved by the determinant recurrence in [the original q-Hahn determinant theorem](actual_q_hahn_joint_accretive_determinant.md#4-a-positive-definite-real-part). Every factor is positive because 2m<N, so Dpos_a is positive definite also at a=M. Put H=diag(sin((n+1/2)theta))_(n=0)^(a-1), s0=sin(theta/2). There is the exact matrix factorization J_a-2I=2 H Dpos_a H+2s0^2 Dpos_a. (6) The diagonal identity is sin^2((n+1/2)theta)+sin^2(theta/2) =1-cos(n theta)cos((n+1)theta). The adjacent identity is sin((n-1/2)theta)sin((n+1/2)theta)+sin^2(theta/2) =sin^2(n theta). These are precisely the entries in (5),(6). The right side of (6) is positive definite. Therefore EVERY eigenvalue of J_a is strictly greater than 2. The nonzero adjacent entries also imply simple spectrum: an eigenvector is determined by its first coordinate through the tridiagonal recurrence, and that coordinate cannot vanish. Hence ALL zeros of p_a are simple, real, and strictly greater than 2. (7) This is uniform in the folded channel, with no restriction to odd levels or to channels bounded away from the fold. ## 4. The canonical logarithm and its uniform derivative bounds Write the zeros as r_1,...,r_a>2. Since p_a(lambda_0)=1, p_a(x)=product_(h=1)^a (r_h-x)/(r_h-lambda_0). On Omega=C minus [2,infinity), define Log p_a(x)=sum_h Log((r_h-x)/(r_h-lambda_0)), (8) where each logarithm is continued from its positive real value at any x<2. Equivalently its argument has the principal logarithm in each individual factor. This is a single holomorphic branch on Omega, real on the whole interval x<2. For m>=1, |partial_x^m Log p_a(x)| <=(m-1)! a/dist(x,[2,infinity))^m. (9) Thus the original scalar itself, rather than a complexly continued finite color g, supplies a canonical selected branch at every geometric real target x<2. ## 5. Leading source action continues through the physical endpoint Here the scalar leading limit can also be proved directly. Let a_N/N tend to alpha in (0,1/2]. For a real x<-2, every term in (1) is positive. Uniform sine-factorial estimates and Riemann sums give N^-1 log p_(a_N)(x) -> max_(0<=t<=alpha) E_alpha(t;x), E_alpha(t;x)=J(alpha+t)-J(alpha-t)-4J(t) +integral_0^t log(2cos(2pi u)-x) du, J(v)=integral_0^v log(2sin(pi u)) du. (10) The endpoint logarithmic singularities in the sine factorials cost O(log N), uniformly in their integer indices. The final integrand in (10) is smooth and positive-argument for x<-2. The number of summands is at most N, so maximum-term comparison proves (10), including sequences approaching the folded channel. The maximum is unique and interior. Put A=sin^2(pi alpha), v=2-x and z=sin^2(pi t). Its derivative is partial_t E=log[(A-z)(v-4z)/(4z^2)]. For x<-2 this strictly decreases from +infinity to -infinity. The critical equation is linear after cancellation of its z^2 terms, and gives z_*=A v/(v+4A), t_*=pi^-1 arcsin(sqrt(A v/(v+4A))). (11) Now fix an anchor x0<-2. The bounds (9), divided by N, make N^-1 Log p_(a_N) a locally bounded normal family on the connected slit domain Omega: its value at x0 is bounded by (10), and its derivative is uniformly bounded along any fixed compact path. Every subsequential holomorphic limit agrees with (10) on the real interval x<-2. The identity theorem therefore makes the limit unique. Consequently N^-1 Log p_(a_N)(x) -> Psi_alpha(x) (12) locally uniformly on ALL of Omega, with every fixed x derivative. This is the actual source logarithm (8), not a formally chosen solution of a characteristic equation. On the entire real interval x<2 the continuation is explicitly Psi_alpha(x)=E_alpha(t_*(x);x), (13) with (11). Indeed 0<z_*<min(A,v/4), so all logarithms in the integral up to t_* have positive arguments. Formula (13) is real analytic on x<2 and agrees with (10) on x<-2, proving the claimed continuation. In particular the passage through x=-2 is regular. There is no claimed uniformity at the removed boundary x=2. The result proves a leading selected SCALAR action. It does not turn the original tensor contraction into a scalar evaluation, or justify discarding its generic first normals. Those distinctions remain essential to the global volume problem. Audit: [original root values, the own recurrence and positive matrix shift](../experiments/audit_actual_matching_edge_racah_root_location.py). The result concerns the scalar polynomial and its leading action. It does not replace the contracted operator by that scalar.

title: The full real native cost throughout every shrinking fold window
status: Full real norm rate in shrinking fold windows
text: # The full real native cost throughout every shrinking fold window 30 October 2026. Let j_N/N tend to 1/2, with 0<=j_N<=floor((N-1)/2). The FULL physical completed projector and, when paired, its actual nilpotent have exponential norm rate 5v3/pi. No restriction such as (N-1-2j_N)log N=o(N) is needed here. This concerns real integer physical degrees and magnetic indices, their Euclidean operator norms, and fixed generic-q jets. It does not extend the complex-normal corridor, supply a confluent complex amplitude, or estimate a marked whole-network contraction. ## 1. Statement and the exact source interfaces Put d=N-1, j=j_N, l=d-j and s=l-j. If j<l, let Q_j and M_j be the ACTUAL completed target pair in the [native projector theorem](actual_matching_edge_native_projector_energy.md). If j=l, retain the ordinary isolated midpoint projector Pi_j. Then, for every sequence j/N->1/2, N^-1 log ||Q_j||op ->5v3/pi, N^-1 log ||M_j||op ->5v3/pi (1) on its paired subsequence, and the same limit holds for Pi_j on its simple subsequence. All statements remain true for the Hilbert--Schmidt norm. Every FIXED generic-q jet of these operators has upper exponential rate at most 5v3/pi; equality is not asserted for a derivative that can vanish. We prove the paired claim; the isolated midpoint is already covered by the [full folded profile](actual_matching_edge_magnetic_energy_profile.md). Here s/N->0, while s itself can tend to infinity at any sublinear rate. All original physical degrees are retained. For complete degrees l<=t<=d, the exact Parseval comparison is N/(j+1) Z_(t,j) <= E_(t,j) <=N Z_(t,j), Z_(t,j)=|fhat_j(t/2)|^2/|sigma_(t,j)|. (2) The exact center source and double CD measure give Z_(t,j)=A_(N,t,j) R_j(1;c_t)^2, A_(N,t,j)=a_j^2/N *s_(2j)^2/s_j^4 *s_(t-j)/s_(t-l), c_t=-cos(pi(t+1)/N), a_j=|1-q^(4j+2)|. (3) All factorial indices lie in 0,...,d. The monic determinant R_j is the original source determinant, not an auxiliary positive replacement. It is increasing at z=1 for real c>=0. In (3), c_t ranges from cos(pi j/N) to 1, so this monotonicity applies. Let J(x)=integral_0^x log(2sin(pi y))dy on [0,1]. Its continuity, J(0)=J(1/2)=J(1)=0, and the uniform factorial estimate give sup_(l<=t<=d) |N^-1 log A_(N,t,j)| ->0. (4) Indeed the factorial part divided by N is 2J(2j/N)-4J(j/N) +J((t-j)/N)-J((t-l)/N)+O(log N/N). The first two terms tend to zero. The last two arguments differ by s/N->0, uniformly over t, so their difference tends to zero by uniform continuity. The remaining a_j and N factors have logarithms O(log N), since a_j>=4/N at a nonself-paired node. Thus (2)--(4), at the endpoint and throughout the complete range, prove max_(l<=t<=d) E_(t,j)=R_j(1;1)^2 exp(o(N)). (5) This is a maximum over one genuine physical degree. It does not maximize independently over degrees of adjacent network coupons. ## 2. The actual endpoint selects the same cubic limit Put u=floor(d/2), v=d-u and w_N=q^j. At t=d the positive coefficient polynomial appearing in the original physical column is P_N(w)=sum_(a=0)^j beta(j,a)beta(u,a)beta(v,j-a) w^a, C_j(d,u)=q^((d-j)u) P_N(w_N). (6) The denominator beta(d,j) is exactly one. The finite negative-root theorem applies to this original polynomial. Uniform factorial estimates and j/N,u/N,v/N->1/2 give uniformly over the whole support N^-1 log[beta(j,a)beta(u,a)beta(v,j-a)] =-3[J(a/N)+J(1/2-a/N)]+o(1). (7) Replacing j/N by 1/2 uses only uniform continuity of J, including both endpoints. There is no assumed bound on s log N here. For every positive real w, (7) gives the same strict real Laplace action as in the full folded theorem. Its selected saddle is alpha(w)=pi^-1 arctan(w^(1/3)). The actual negative-root product bound makes N^-1 Log(P_N(w)/P_N(1)) a normal family on the slit plane. Uniqueness from the positive real axis therefore gives the same holomorphic action for this whole sequence of actual polynomials. In particular at w_N->i, N^-1 log |C_j(d,u)| ->5v3/(2pi). (8) This is the selected complex rate, not a conclusion from comparing positive coefficients at w=i. The exact constant was computed from alpha(i)=1/4+i log(3)/(4pi) and D(i/sqrt(3))=5v3/6 in the preceding theorem. At degree d the magnetic polynomial has all j roots negative real. If u differs from d/2 by one half, its root-product formula gives cos(pi/(2N))^j <= |C_j(d,u)|/|fhat_j(d/2)| <=1; (9) if d is even the ratio is one. Finally the exact center scalar is |fhat_j(d/2)|=R_j(1;1) s_(2j)/s_j^3. (10) Its normalized logarithm tends to zero, since J(2j/N)-3J(j/N)->0. Equations (8)--(10) prove N^-1 log R_j(1;1)^2 ->5v3/pi. (11) ## 3. The incomplete band is smaller, using its own actual formula It remains to control j<=t<l, where the completed pair contains only its simple physical branch. The complete-range Fourier factorization is NOT assumed in this band. Instead start with the original generic finite column. Its highest-vector factor at the root is exactly F_(N-j+a-1) F_(N-a-1)/(F_(N-j-1)F_(N-1)) =Q^(a(a-j)) [j choose a]_Q. (12) This follows by complementing each factor 1-Q^(N-r)=-Q^(-r)(1-Q^r). Every denominator index is below N; (12) is valid for ALL 0<=j<=t< N, not just complete channels. Since [n choose k]_Q=q^(k(n-k)) beta(n,k), substitution into the original divided-descendant sum gives the exact identity C_j(t,u)=q^((d-j)u) sum_a E(t,j,u,a) q^(a(t+j-d)), E=beta(j,a)beta(u,a)beta(t-u,j-a)/beta(t,j), max(0,u-t+j)<=a<=min(j,u). (13) To check its phase directly, the Gaussian-binomial phases, divided-descendant powers and root highest ratio leave a(t+j-1)-ju before the factor (-1)^a x^(-2a). Combining that factor with x^u and q^N=-1 gives precisely (13). Thus its real positive envelope is an authorized bound for this ACTUAL root source outside the complete chamber. Set r=t-j<s=o(N). Every allowed a satisfies 0<=u-a<=r. Uniform factorial estimates, j/N,t/N->1/2, and that inequality imply N^-1 log E(t,j,u,a) =-J(x)-J(1/2-x)+o(1), (14) uniformly throughout the incomplete band and its full support. Here x can be chosen as min(u/N,1/2). The possible excess of u/N above 1/2 is o(1), so this harmless clipping and all arguments of J are justified by its uniform continuity. In detail the beta(j,a) term supplies the displayed profile, while beta(u,a), beta(t-u,j-a), and the denominator beta(t,j) each have normalized logarithm tending uniformly to zero because their complementary indices are at most r. There are at most N summands in (13). A triangle bound therefore gives the uniform upper estimate from (14). This step is used only in the collapsing boundary band and claims no selected oscillatory rate for an interior column. The simple CD measure there is |sigma_(t,j)|=s_(t-j)s_(t+j+1)/(s_t^2 a_j). Its normalized logarithm tends uniformly to zero: its three factorial arguments tend respectively to 0,1,1/2. Summing the squared column bound over at most N magnetic indices yields max_(j<=t<l) E_(t,j) <=exp[N(v8/(2pi)+o(1))]. (15) The smaller constant comes from the strict maximum at x=1/4 of -2J(x)-2J(1/2-x). This estimate retains endpoints and all source phases until the explicitly stated upper-bound step. ## 4. Assemble the real operator and retain the scope The exact generic high adapter duplicates the same physical low blocks. On each complete block M_j has norm E_(t,j); it is zero on the incomplete band. Hence (5),(11) give its full operator and Hilbert--Schmidt rate in (1). On a complete block M_j=(J_t-c_j)Q_j, with uniformly bounded J_t-c_j, providing the matching lower bound for Q_j. The native projector theorem gives its upper bound by a polynomial times the maximum or square sum of ALL energies. Equations (11),(15), and v8/(2pi)<5v3/pi prove the other claim in (1). Fixed generic-q derivatives add only the uniform polynomial factors already proved there. Thus every shrinking SCALED fold window has the same explicit real boundary cost, even when s log N is not o(N). The stronger width here comes from positivity and real physical norms, not from a larger joint complex domain for paired normal currents. No fixed nonzero scaled-width assertion or whole-source volume conjecture follows from this corollary. Audit: [original incomplete-band formula and shrinking-fold source](../experiments/audit_actual_matching_edge_shrinking_fold_native_energy.py). The indices remain real and physical. This result does not enlarge the complex-normal corridor or assert a whole-source limit. The continuity, root-product and operator arguments prove the shrinking real-window bounds. Finite samples check their conventions, not their uniformity.

title: The original shared Fourier source has an explicit centered quadratic phase
text: # The original shared Fourier source has an explicit centered quadratic phase 30 October 2026. In the exact positive Fourier partition, every Clebsch endpoint phase and every ordinary cup/cap constant cancels explicitly. The remaining original phase is a quadratic form in the shared integer labels, with the original half-twist phases and marked Fourier charge retained. This is an exact source identity, not a claim that its stationary point contributes to the finite sum. ## 1. Exact paired endpoint phase Use the original definitions in [the positive Fourier partition](actual_matching_graph_positive_fourier_partition.md). Put q=exp(pi i/N), d=N-1, r=a+w, t=d-|w|, and B_N(a,w)=k_a N s_(a+|w|) /(s_a^2 s_|w|^2 s_(a-|w|)). The actual first endpoint scalars c_W,c_pi and the actual finite polynomial scalar c_(t,a) satisfy the stronger COMPLEX identity h0_a c_W c_pi c_(t,a)^2 = B_N(a,w) q^[(2a-d)t]. (1) Indeed, the original reversed-conjugate white map gives c_W c_pi=|c_W|^2 conjugate(f_(t,a)(t))/G_(a,r). The original generic physical endpoint specializes to f_(t,a)(t)=(-1)^a q^[dt+a^2+a]. (2) This retains the actual endpoint convention; the term -2Na in its generic exponent has become the root unit q^(-2Na)=1. Meanwhile F_a=(Q;Q)_a=(-i)^a q^[a(a+1)/2]s_a gives c_(t,a)^2 =(-1)^a q^[2a(t-d)+a(a-1)]/s_a^2. (3) Multiplying (2),(3), the signs cancel and the exponent is (2a-d)t-2a(d+1). Its final term is -2aN and hence contributes one. The remaining modulus is exactly the already-proved B_N. This proves (1), including high-degree columns and both level parities; no choice of a Chevalley square root remains in the phase. ## 2. Center every actual physical port Work on the same shared state space S_N as in the positive partition: exact bounded Kirchhoff flows w, coefficient indices k_v, and ALL physical-cycle congruences, including charge one on the original marked cycle. On a restored physical cycle, let x be its integer base coordinate and write the actual FIRST coordinate at each node n as u_n=epsilon_n x+B_n, epsilon_n in {+1,-1}. Here B_n is the literal integer affine offset. At a Clebsch node v incident to edge i the actual total is T_n=d+w_i. At a cup or cap it is T_n=d. Define delta_n=B_n-T_n/2, gamma_v=d-2a_i+2k_v, gamma_b=d at cups/caps. (4) In particular delta_n can be a half-integer. Its definition is independent of the low/high adapter: the compiler offset b_v satisfies b_v+t_i/2=T_n/2 exactly. The residual exponent of a vertex in the original finite expansion can therefore be written as gamma_v(B_v-b_v)-t_i k_v =gamma_v delta_v+(d-2a_i)t_i/2. (5) Each matching edge has TWO such vertices. Their last terms in (5) cancel exactly against the paired endpoint phase (1). This uses their shared a_i,w_i,t_i; independent vertex normalization would hide the cancellation. For a cup or cap, its coordinate monomial contributes d B_b=d delta_b+d^2/2. There are H original cups and H restored ordinary caps. Their 2H constant terms add to H d^2, exactly canceling the H original cup constants q^(-d^2). Their powers of N have already canceled in the positive partition. The original marked cap is still represented by its specified charged-cap ratio; that ratio's global q^(-d^2) remains outside the sum. Consequently the COMPLETE residual phase is Theta_N(a,w,k) = product_i omega_(a_i)^epsilon_i * q^Lambda_N(a,w,k), Lambda_N=sum_(all ordinary vertices v) gamma_v delta_v +d sum_(all cups/caps b) delta_b. (6) The epsilon_i in the first line is the recorded half-twist sign, whereas epsilon_n in (4) is a physical-coordinate slope. Their roles are distinct. Although individual terms in Lambda_N may be half-integral, Lambda_N itself is an INTEGER. Modulo two, every gamma_n is d, and every physical matching total occurs at two vertices. There are an even number of cup/cap totals. Hence sum_n gamma_n T_n =0 modulo 2, Lambda_N=sum_n gamma_n B_n-(1/2)sum_n gamma_n T_n in Z. (7) Thus (6) uses the original q itself, unambiguously at both level parities. No new half-character choice has been introduced. The original omega factors retain their already-specified root convention. ## 3. The resulting exact shared quadratic sum The original complete-circle source is exactly A_(D,N)=q^(-d^2) N^(C-1) sum_(S_N) product_i[omega_(a_i)^epsilon_i B_N(a_i,w_i)] *q^Lambda_N(a,w,k) *product_(v incident to i) p_(t_i,a_i,k_v). (8) For a fixed recorded Morse graph, every B_n is affine in the matching variables w_i and d, obtained by the literal propagation u_next=T_n-u. Equation (6) is therefore an explicit quadratic polynomial in (a,w,k,d), restricted to the actual shared lattice. In particular the absolute values |w_i| in the positive amplitudes do not appear in this residual polynomial. The retained omega factors add their original quadratic channel phases. For an unmarked cycle, writing its new integer base coordinate as x'=x+h changes Lambda_N by -h m_c, where m_c is its total Fourier frequency. On the retained congruence m_c=0 modulo 2N this leaves q^Lambda_N unchanged. On the marked cycle the base coordinate is fixed as the SECOND original marked coordinate; its one-unit charge must not be discarded in making a similar reparametrization. This exact simplification preserves the positive upper comparison. It also isolates what that comparison removes: the bilinear interaction between the Fourier labels gamma_v and the actual centered affine offsets delta_v. In an interior coefficient chart the normalized logarithmic phase is N^-1 log(q^Lambda_N)=i pi Lambda_N/N^2. Its derivative with respect to lambda_v=k_v/N is 2pi i delta_v/N, precisely the real-center data in [the radial reconstruction obstruction](actual_positive_fourier_radial_geometric_obstruction.md). No equality of exponential rates, geometric maximum, holomorphic coefficient-index continuation, or contributing cycle follows from the quadratic form alone. Audit: [original paired phases and full centered cycle convolutions](../experiments/audit_actual_matching_graph_centered_fourier_phase.py). The result is an exact phase identity, not an assertion of a contributing saddle or equality of exponential rates.

title: A common head chart for the original charged Ward currents
status: Common charged head lattice and actual meromorphic Ward currents
text: # A common head chart for the original charged Ward currents 30 October 2026. This makes the off-diagonal Ward construction on a specified tensor source explicit before its finite head sums. The charge-zero and neighboring charge-one bands use one primitive head lattice. Cutting a spanning tree reduces the proof to the independent-head identities of the actual tensors. Reclosing the auxiliary cuts gives explicit difference currents. The original support cycles and their endpoint differences remain part of the result; a common affine chart does not make those cycles equal. ## 1. Typed incidence equations and their component obstruction Fix one channel assignment in the original generic source, including the full generic channel expansion of every routed R and R inverse. Keep all small and large partners, scalar denominators, physical turns and ordinary caps. Intermediate scalar poles are treated meromorphically before root specialization; to take a finite normal one first clears their known finite pole order and retains the required higher Taylor coefficients. No root projector replaces this generic expansion. Each wire e carries its fixed integral highest weight L_e and an actual head h_e. At a typed vertex the K equation is sum_out h_e-sum_in h_e =(sum_out L_e-sum_in L_e)/2. (1) These are ordinary signed INCIDENCE equations. A contracted wire is an output at one end and an input at the other. Cups and caps are vertices, not an unrecorded change of orientation. Their constants are respectively L and -L. At W:V_(2a)->V_d tensor V_d the constant is d-a; the dual has the opposite constant. Thus every constant in (1) is an integer in the actual source. Delete the original exposed cut and the routed first-head cut. For their band delta put the first input/output heads a,a+delta and the second input/output heads l,l+delta. Let B be the incidence matrix of the remaining INTERNAL graph. Its equation is B h=b(a,l)+delta q. (2) The signs of q come from the literal four port orientations. They are opposite unit charges at the two shifted boundary ends; they are not an assigned independent color. Integer degree conservation is retained, without reduction modulo N. Check connectedness after THESE cuts on the actual typed graph. For a connected graph the only incidence relation is the sum of its rows, and the source makes the right side of (2) have sum zero. A spanning tree therefore gives an integer-affine solution for arbitrary complex a,l,delta. With x the heads on the non-tree edges, h=h_*(a,l)+delta w+A x, (3) where h_* and w have zero non-tree coordinates, w is the signed unit tree path for q, and A is the integral fundamental-cycle basis. The non-tree rows of A are the identity. All three bands delta=0,1,-1 therefore have the SAME primitive free coordinates x. No division by a quantum number or passage to an index-N cover occurs. The internal CURRENT terms also have a specified chart: place the compensating charge on the auxiliary edge carrying the generator, instead of on the second actual cut, and use its signed unit tree path w_e in place of w. Its non-tree coordinates are again zero. Thus all possible placements have the same h_* and A and differ only by their recorded integral charge-path offsets. We do not mistake a charged intermediate tensor for a zero-band density. For a disconnected graph the exact criterion is zero total charge in EACH component. Components containing neither cut are retained as their original scalar factors. If a charged right side fails the component criterion, its affine band has no original states; one must not invent a path joining those components. If the component conditions constrain a,l, keep those original affine strata rather than asserting a two-dimensional chart. On a geometric two-position chart the required connected deleted graph is the explicit criterion in the [two-cut construction](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_two_cut_framing_port_reconstruction.md). For a chosen route U the graph is checked after its actual expansion; connectedness of a different uncut diagram is not a substitute. The physical inequalities 0<=h_e<=L_e remain separate from (3). In particular a dimension-one channel can give a thin or empty physical support even though the incidence graph is connected. ## 2. The specified meromorphic bands and local identities Use the actual large finite white polynomial and the specified moving-period factorial, with d and every L_e fixed as zeta varies. The independent-head W identities, proved in [the source Ward calculation](actual_augmented_plat_framing_density_source_ward.md), are polynomial identities, not equalities only on root samples. Its cup/cap equations follow from the same exact unit-step factorial recurrence. They apply meromorphically also to fixed L_e>=N: the finite scalar factorial can then have a root zero and its pole is retained as just specified. Integer-affine source characters are kept; their unit-step multipliers are the actual recorded ones. One may instead keep an original R as a four-port vertex only when using its specified literal factorial continuation. Its exact independent-variable Ward ratios are those of the [original crossing currents](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/local_r_ward_transfer_currents.md). This is a second permitted primitive presentation, not an assertion that two different off-grid presentations coincide merely because their physical matrices agree. The full spectral W/cup presentation above already suffices for the routed source. In (3), let s_delta(a,l,x) be the product of these actual factors with the indicated band charge, BEFORE applying the exposed coherent or root functional. It includes the fixed scalar, turn and peripheral characters of that convention; any extra generic boundary row must be separately specified and transported covariantly. No bare root mark is moved through this generic calculation. On the allowed physical lattice its original finite period is the actual coefficient of C(E_(l+delta,l)) from first input a to output a+delta. The zero band gives J_(a,l). For the next displayed interior identity use UNTRUNCATED analytic coefficients f(y)=1-Q^(y+1), k(y)=zeta^(d-2y), gamma(y)=zeta[Q^(y-N)-1]=e(y)/k(y). (4) For example f(d)=1-Q^N here, whereas the finite matrix arrow f_d is zero. The distinction is indispensable at a genuine quantum normal. The physical endpoint will be restored by its source cycle, not by substituting a root simplification in (4). ## 3. The tree construction of the common difference currents In addition to the two actual cuts, cut each non-tree edge of the internal graph. What remains is a typed TREE with auxiliary pairs of boundary heads. Its internal heads are uniquely determined by its boundary heads and (1). Its tensor entry is consequently a literal product of the specified factors, with no internal head sum. Propagating the original Hopf generator through this tree using the local identities proves its meromorphic Ward identity. Every coproduct prefix K factor and every ordered dual map stays in that propagation. Now identify the two auxiliary heads of edge e with its common coordinate x_e, using the original identity contraction. The two insertions on this cut give a discrete product rule. With their ACTUAL coefficient and tensor factors denoted j,c, it is j T_e c-(T_e^-1 j)c =(T_e-I)[(T_e^-1 j)c], (5) where T_e shifts x_e by one. The shift acts on the WHOLE indicated product, including its insertion and all prefix characters. A reverse shift is put in this form by (T_e^-1-I)u=-(T_e-I)T_e^-1 u. These are actual array translations, not new single-port matrix actions. This specifies the current algorithm: cut the stated tree, propagate the original generator in its original tensor order, and for each auxiliary cut collect the literal product on the right of (5), with its sign. Tree edges cancel pointwise. Each non-tree edge gives its own current j_(F,e) or j_(E,e). Equivalently the charge paths for the two placements of its insertion differ by exactly its fundamental cycle, which is x_e->x_e+1 in (3). This proves that the construction uses the same head chart, rather than silently comparing different charge lattices. The currents are finite sums of specified source products and shifts, not solutions chosen by interpolation. At the two remaining cuts the result is the explicit interior band identity f(l)s_+(a,l,x)-f(l-1)s_+(a,l-1,x) -f(a)[s_0(a,l,x)-s_0(a+1,l,x)] =sum_e (T_e-I)j_(F,e), (6) gamma(l)s_-(a,l,x)-gamma(l+1)s_-(a,l+1,x) -gamma(a)[s_0(a,l,x)-s_0(a-1,l,x)] =sum_e (T_e-I)j_(E,e). (7) The boundary head changes do not shift x: the latter are the literal heads of the fixed internal non-tree edges. All tree heads do change by their exact affine formulas in (3). Equations (6),(7) are meromorphic identities in independent complex a,l,x and generic zeta on every regular source chart, and hence after clearing their denominators. All genuine quantum derivatives are retained. Their signs can also be checked directly at the finite matrix boundary. For a diagonal C(E_ll), ad_F has its (a+1,a) entry f_a[J_(a,l)-J_(a+1,l)]; C(ad_F E_ll) has the other two terms in (6). For ad_E the (a-1,a) entry is gamma_a[J_(a,l)-J_(a-1,l)], and C(ad_E E_ll) has the other two terms in (7). The interior construction proves these same equations modulo the displayed actual internal currents BEFORE finite contraction. ## 4. An explicit two-crossing interior current Here is a source-level calculation with an internal cycle. Let r(a,b,k) be the literal positive crossing coefficient, sending (a,b) to (b+k,a-k), and write K(y)=x Q^-y, f(y)=1-Q^(y+1). Retain its common full Cartan scalar. For two consecutive crossings take external target c+d=a+b+1 and internal transfer k. Put T1=f(a) r(a+1,b,k) r(b+k,a+1-k,c-a-1+k), T2=K(a)^-1 f(b) r(a,b+1,k) r(b+1+k,a-k,c-a+k), T3=f(c-1) r(a,b,k) r(b+k,a-k,c-a-1+k), T4=K(c)^-1 f(d-1) r(a,b,k) r(b+k,a-k,c-a+k). Then for S_k:k->k+1 the exact independent-head equation is T1+T2-T3-T4=(S_k-I)J_F, J_F=r(b+k,a-k+1,c-a+k-1) *[K(a)^-1 f(b)r(a,b+1,k-1) -f(b+k-1)r(a,b,k-1)]. (8) Apply the first crossing's literal F identity at k and the second one at k, keeping the middle insertion. Their shared middle terms cancel except that the first-head middle insertion is evaluated at k and k+1. This gives (8) with its displayed sign. It is not an identity obtained by summing a finite row. The source's proper ratios verify it rationally in independent Q,x,Q^a,Q^b,Q^c,Q^k. For the E calculation use c+d=a+b-1 and the actual analytic e(y)=q^-1[x^-1-Q x Q^-y]. The four boundary terms are U1=K(b)e(a)r(a-1,b,k)r(b+k,a-1-k,c-a+k+1), U2=e(b)r(a,b-1,k)r(b-1+k,a-k,c-a+k), U3=K(d)e(c+1)r(a,b,k)r(b+k,a-k,c-a+k+1), U4=e(d+1)r(a,b,k)r(b+k,a-k,c-a+k). Its exact current is U1+U2-U3-U4=(S_k-I)J_E, J_E=r(b+k-1,a-k,c-a+k) *[K(a-k)e(b+k)r(a,b,k)-e(b)r(a,b-1,k)]. (8a) The middle first-input insertion now appears at k+1 in the first local equation and at k in the second. This proves (8a), including the displayed K prefix and its sign. Both identities keep the same two original crossing scalars on their two sides. The coefficients in (8) are interior functions. Its physical finite support and truncated endpoint arrows must still be retained when it is summed. In particular a generic f(d) is not set to zero as a meromorphic function merely because the physical matrix has no arrow there. ## 5. Original period chains, endpoints and the remaining global step For every charged band keep its original support polytope in (3) and its ordered product-cotangent tori Gamma_delta. These supports are different at neighboring bands and at adjacent a,l. A constant forbidden polar stratum remains its original zero state. When a separately proved source-null torus is added, its proof and ordered residue convention are retained. Equations (6),(7) may be integrated against any common regular test cycle. To replace the resulting band periods by the original ones, keep the differences between each Gamma_delta and that test cycle. For every internal current its translated-cycle correction is exactly integral_Gamma c w(T_e-I)j =integral_Gamma c(T_e^-1 w-w)j +integral_(Gamma+e-Gamma)c(T_e^-1 w)j, c=product_i pi cot(pi x_i). (9) The source normalization is (2pi i)^(-dim x). A chain filling the last cycle difference contributes ALL its crossed source residues and its remaining ends. Coincident cotangent/source poles require their actual finite parts and complement derivatives. The specified moving-P factorial and fixed highest weights remain in this process. No periodicity of the summand identifies the support cycles. On the original finite arrays the actual endpoint arrows and support rules recover the already proved [braided coherent flux](actual_braided_residual_framing_current.md). Pairing the first head with beta_a requires only its exact finite sum; no new meromorphic interpolation of beta is used. The first-head and second-head ends of a selected finite window remain the interval terms in that theorem. The individual meromorphic continuations of an outside-head term are not set to zero; its original source cycle is empty, and transport out of that source domain is accounted for by these chain differences. Thus the local meromorphic Ward equation and its actual charged source lattice are now specified together. This still does not identify the original cycle with a geometric descending cycle or compute the coefficient of the framing-diagonal residue. The stationary pushforward must carry the currents (6),(7) and the explicit chain differences (9), including all resonant characters and generic normals. A zero closed finite flux alone cannot make that relative coefficient nonzero. The focused [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_matching_graph_common_band_ward_current.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_matching_graph_common_band_ward_current_results.json) check the actual expanded two- through five-bridge plat graphs, including routed inverse pairs and all fixed channel weight types: 92 primitive cycles, 196 integral charge paths, and the disconnected component test. The two composed currents (8),(8a) are verified rationally in independent head exponentials. A separate comparison with the original generic crossing matrices checks 539 value/first-jet entries, including their full Cartan scalar, and seven nonzero untruncated endpoint-normal defects. These checks do not establish equality of the different charged support cycles or a geometric-cycle coefficient. The reduction requires the routed graph to be connected, the primitive chart to be fixed, and the endpoint divisors to be retained. It does not identify the charged cycles or a geometric period.

title: A positive Fourier partition with the original shared constraints
status: Exact shared positive partition; upper bound
text: # A positive Fourier partition with the original shared constraints 30 October 2026. The exact shared-cycle compiler admits a fully positive coefficient comparison whose scalar weight is explicit in the original source normalization. Every matching label, integral Kirchhoff equation and physical-cycle Fourier congruence is retained. This is an upper bound for the original complete-circle source, not a volume equality or a noncancellation theorem. ## 1. Original endpoint scalars, including the high-degree adapter Use the notation and recorded physical-port orders of [the exact shared-cycle compiler](actual_matching_graph_shared_cycle_fourier_compiler.md). Thus q=exp(pi i/N), d=N-1, s_j=product_(h=1)^j 2sin(pi h/N), 0<=a<=floor(d/2), r=a+w, |w|<=a. The physical total and its low adapter are T=d+w, t=d-|w|. Write c_W=W_a(b,T-b;r), b=max(0,T-d), for the actual first endpoint of the original Clebsch column. Then |c_W|=s_a/(s_|w| s_(a-|w|)). (1) Here is a proof retaining the normalization. If r<=a, the endpoint has first physical index zero. In the original coproduct Delta F=F tensor 1+K^-1 tensor F, only its second summand can reach that endpoint from the highest column. Dividing by the original ordinary-channel descendant factors gives, with F_j=(Q;Q)_j, c_W=q^(-dr) F_(d-a+r)/(F_(d-a)F_r). (2) The highest endpoint is one. Taking absolute values and using s_(d-j)=N/s_j proves (1) when w<=0. For the other half use the ACTUAL Chevalley maps J_L |u> = q^(-(L+1)u) |L-u>, S=P(J_d tensor J_d). For the balanced source generators, J_L exchanges F and Ecal and exchanges K and K^-1. The flip in S consequently gives S Delta F=Delta Ecal S and S Delta Ecal=Delta F S. In the original generic Clebsch image, uniqueness of its highest vector gives S W_a=kappa W_a J_(2a). This is a rational generic identity, then specialized; it does not assume semisimplicity at the root. Squaring it yields kappa^2=q^(-2Nd+2a(2a+1)). (3) The original W column and its Chevalley image have nonzero finite highest endpoints at the root, so the identity specializes there; alternatively (3) already makes any scalar singularity removable. All coefficients of the two J maps and kappa have modulus one at the root. The low endpoint (0,t) maps to the HIGH endpoint (d-t,d), exactly the endpoint used in the compiler. Thus its modulus is unchanged under r->2a-r. This proves (1) for both halves and both level parities. The original white map is pi_a(r;u,v)=G_(a,r)^-1 conjugate(W_a(v,u;r)), G_(a,r)=s_(2a)/(s_r s_(2a-r))>0. The normalized physical column has unit-modulus final endpoint, so its first-endpoint scalar satisfies |c_pi|=|c_W|/G_(a,r). (4) Both physical vertices have the same t and a. Their positive Fourier polynomials are normalized by c_(t,a) from the compiler, with |c_(t,a)|=1/s_a. Finally retain the actual complete-circle weight h0_a=k_a N s_(2a)/s_a^2, k_a=1 if 2a=d, and k_a=2 otherwise. Equations (1)--(4) give the exact positive scalar B_N(a,w) :=h0_a |c_W c_pi c_(t,a)^2| =k_a N s_(a+|w|) /(s_a^2 s_|w|^2 s_(a-|w|)). (5) There is no omitted exponential row, face or ordinary-channel metric in (5). The original physical cups have modulus N and ordinary caps modulus 1/N. Their numbers agree in the closed Morse diagram, so those moduli cancel globally. The original marked cap is handled by the exact charged-cap ratio in the compiler, rather than included in this cancellation. ## 2. The shared state space and all Fourier congruences Let R be the number of original matching circles and C the number of restored physical cycles. Collapse those cycles to the graph Gamma, orienting each matching edge from its pi cycle to its W cycle. A shared state consists of a_i in {0,...,floor(d/2)}, w_i in {-a_i,...,a_i}, div_Gamma w=0, k_v in {0,...,a_i} at EACH of the two ends v of i. Set t_i=d-|w_i|. On a fixed physical cycle, propagate its actual indices as literal affine functions of one starting coordinate x. Let epsilon_v in {+1,-1} be the slope of the recorded FIRST physical coordinate at vertex v, and epsilon_b the same slope at a physical cup or restored cap b. The total character is m_c(a,k)=sum_(v on c) epsilon_v(d-2a_i+2k_v) +d sum_(b on c) epsilon_b. (6) The actual bipartite cycle proof shows m_c is always even. All affine offsets, high-degree shifts and the terms -t_i k_v are retained in the remaining coefficient phase. They do not affect (6). Put b_c=0 except b_(c_*)=1 on the marked cycle, whose variable is the SECOND marked coordinate. Retain EVERY equation m_c(a,k)=2b_c modulo 2N. (7) Write S_N for this finite state space: the capacities, exact Kirchhoff equations, and all congruences (7), jointly. There are at most N^(4R) states: N choices for each a_i and each w_i, and N choices for each of the 2R coefficient indices. Constraints can only decrease this bound. No variables on separate vertices or cycles have been optimized independently. ## 3. Exact phase-bearing sum and one Cauchy inequality For a state in S_N, let Theta_N(a,w,k) be the phase left by the EXACT compiler after removing the positive factors (5) and the positive coefficients p_(t_i,a_i,k_v). Its modulus is one. This definition is explicit: multiply the original endpoint phases, c_(t_i,a_i), cup/cap monomials, recorded half-twist omega phases, and the affine-offset terms in compiler equation (7), then divide by their moduli. The global q^(-d^2) marked phase is written separately below. All these factors are nonzero; no arbitrary phase or framing normalization is introduced. The original complete-circle source is therefore EXACTLY A_(D,N)=q^(-d^2) N^(C-1) sum_(S_N) Theta_N(a,w,k) product_i B_N(a_i,w_i) product_(v incident to i) p_(t_i,a_i,k_v). (8) Define the fully positive shared coefficient partition Z_F(N)=sum_(S_N) product_i B_N(a_i,w_i)^2 product_(v incident to i) p_(t_i,a_i,k_v)^2. (9) ONE finite Cauchy inequality applied to the full sum (8) gives |A_(D,N)|^2 <= N^(4R+2C-2) Z_F(N). (10) The sharper factor |S_N| N^(2C-2) is equally valid. If S_N is empty, both sides of (8) vanish and (10) is immediate. The half-twist phases disappear only in (9),(10); they remain in the exact source (8). In particular, (9) retains the marked charge, all other cycle charges and the same matching magnetic label at both ends of every edge. Dropping these restrictions would give a different, generally weaker comparison problem. ## 4. Its local variational interface and its limit For a fixed diagram, the loss in (10) is polynomial in N. The local positive coefficients in (9) are precisely those in [the proved coefficient variational theorem](actual_q_hahn_fourier_coefficient_variational.md), with complete-channel parameters tau=t_i/N and xi=a_i/N. Its interior coefficient action may therefore be used in this JOINT constrained partition, with the original scalar (5). Its theorem does not supply uniform boundary asymptotics where these parameters or k_v/N approach the boundary. For clarity, the exact finite cycle charge also controls the limiting local momentum. Set lambda_v=k_v/N, xi_i=a_i/N and Y_v^*=exp[2pi i(lambda_v+1/2-xi_i)]. This is the selected radial coefficient saddle momentum on the interior parameter domain of that theorem. Since q^(d-2a_i+2k_v)=q^-1 Y_v^*, equations (6),(7) give EXACTLY product_(v on c) (Y_v^*)^epsilon_v (-1)^(sum_(b on c) epsilon_b) =Q^(E_c/2+b_c), E_c=sum_(v on c)epsilon_v+sum_(b on c)epsilon_b in 2Z. (11) The finite pivotal correction and original marked charge have not been dropped. Equation (11) is a phase constraint supplied by the Fourier extraction; it is not yet a proof of all marked complex gluing equations. In particular, the positive partition can lose cancellation between its states, and a constrained maximum alone need not supply a contributing original cycle. Neither equality in exponential rate in (10) nor identification of the constrained maximum with hyperbolic volume is asserted. Audit: [original endpoint norms and shared coefficient partition](../experiments/audit_actual_matching_graph_positive_fourier_partition.py). The exact constrained coefficient partition does not establish noncancellation or a volume statement.

title: The actual matching source as shared cycle Fourier periods
status: Exact shared flows and marked Fourier charge
text: # The actual matching source as shared cycle Fourier periods 30 October 2026. Fixing the matching magnetic labels reduces every physical component of the original complete-circle source to a one-variable cycle or marked path. The matching magnetic labels are bounded integral Kirchhoff flows. The exact unused-node zeros permit a full N-node Fourier sum, with literal affine lifts and no wrapping of the physical indices. The actual cups and caps cancel the half-character parity at BOTH level parities. The original mark selects a specified Fourier charge. This supplies a joint positive comparison energy of coherent cycle periods. It does not identify that energy's maximum with hyperbolic volume or prove survival of the original summed contribution. ## 1. Freeze the actual matching labels, not the physical wires Use the original complete-circle source of [the full matching-graph theorem](general_matching_graph_full_normal_source.md). Put q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, d=N-1, M=floor(d/2). At circle i retain its folded label a_i and its ordinary matching magnetic index r_i: 0<=a_i<=M, 0<=r_i<=2a_i, W_(a_i) pi_(a_i)=sum_(r_i) W_(a_i)[r_i] pi_(a_i)[r_i]. All original white maps, including their reversal and positive ordinary channel metric, are the actual pi maps. No paired norm pi_a W_a is inverted. The original circle multiplier is still h0_a omega_a^epsilon, as in the full source theorem. After these indices are fixed, every W or pi vertex has two physical ports. Its only support condition is the EXACT integer equation u+v=T_i=d-a_i+r_i. (1) Every physical cup or ordinary cap has support u+v=d. Straight segments identify their endpoint indices. Thus the physical graph is a disjoint union of cycles. The one original unrestricted mark cuts its cycle into a path with a dense endpoint functional. The matching labels are still shared by their two incident vertices; they have not been maximized or summed independently. At the root the original physical cup, cap, and mark are pV(u,d-u)=N q^(-d^2) q^(du), ellV(u,d-u)=N^-1 q^(du), mark(u,v)=N^-2 q^(dv). (2) These are the given source tensors, in their recorded order. The last row is unrestricted; it is not an invariant cap substituted for the physical mark. Any exterior framing line remains the one already recorded for the original invariant. Let F_c(a,r) denote the coherent physical contraction of component c, with every actual local scalar in it. The source is EXACTLY A_(D,N)=sum_(a,r) product_i[h0_(a_i)omega_(a_i)^epsilon_i] product_c F_c(a,r). (3) This is the root source identity itself. Its circle normals are already retained in h0_a pi_a, and its physical mark remains (2). It is not obtained by differentiating a truncated root formula. ## 2. Every fixed physical vertex has the same finite continuation For a vertex with (a,r), define T=d-a+r, t=min(T,2d-T), b=max(0,T-d). Then d-a<=t<=d. In its actual first physical coordinate u its nonzero entries have the form V(u,T-u)=c_V f_(t,a)(u-b), (4) where c_V is the ACTUAL endpoint entry V(b,T-b), and f_(t,a)(0)=1. For W, this follows by normalizing its physical column and using the original root partner identity. The high-degree block is the actual translated low block, not a freely changed framing. For pi, the exact relation pi_a(r;u,v)=G_(a,r)^-1 conjugate(W_a(v,u;r)) and the root column reflection f_(t,a)(t-y)=f_(t,a)(t) conjugate(f_(t,a)(y)) give (4), with its own actual endpoint c_V. The endpoint has modulus one before the W/metric scalar. Both local maps therefore use the same normalized finite f; their different constants are retained. The [literal magnetic polynomial](actual_q_hahn_magnetic_complex_corridor.md) gives a degree-a polynomial G_(t,a) satisfying f_(t,a)(y)=q^[(d-2a)y] G_(t,a)(Q^y), G_(t,a)(q^t z)=c_(t,a) P_(t,a)(z), P_(t,a)(z)=sum_(k=0)^a p_(t,a,k) z^k, p_(t,a,k)>0, c_(t,a)=q^[a(t+a-d)]/(Q;Q)_a. (5) For a=0 the polynomial is one. Every power in (5) has its literal specified exponent. In particular this is a finite continuation at ALL integer y, including values outside the physical range. Its unused-node zeros are G_(t,a)(Q^y)=0, t+1<=y<=d. (6) The positivity and zeros in (5),(6) were proved from the original coproduct. They are not inferred from a Fourier fit to samples. Equivalently, each physical vertex in (4) has the finite expansion V(u,T-u)=c_V c_(t,a) sum_(k=0)^a p_(t,a,k) q^[(d-2a+2k)(u-b)-tk]. (7) The scalar and the t-dependent phase in (7) must both be retained. Only the p coefficients are declared positive. ## 3. The first-failure zero lemma permits a full grid Choose a starting physical leg with value x in {0,...,d}. Along an ordinary vertex the other leg is T-x; at a cup or cap it is d-x. Straight intervals preserve the value. Hence all succeeding leg indices are literal affine functions u_e=epsilon_e x+b_e, epsilon_e in {1,-1}, b_e integer. (8) No modulo-N reduction is made in (8). The admissible x originally form an integer interval, with the final cycle closure imposed. Nevertheless the product of the continued factors (7) is zero at every x outside that interval. To prove this, take the FIRST vertex where a legal incoming index u in [0,d] would produce an illegal outgoing index. Cups and caps cannot cause that failure. If T=t<=d, it means u>t. If the incoming port is the first port, the polynomial argument is u in the unused range of (6). If it is the second port, the argument is t-u<0; its residue modulo N lies in {t+1,...,d}, again a zero of G. If T=2d-t>d, failure means u<T-d. On the first port the normalized argument is u-(T-d)<0, whose residue modulo N is in {t+1,...,d}. On the second port it is d-u, directly in that unused range. The same zeros hold for the actual white dual by (4), or directly by conjugating its reversed column. Thus that first illegal vertex has zero continued coefficient. Later affine indices need not be repaired; all later finite exponential polynomials remain defined. Therefore the cycle or path variable may be summed over ALL x=0,...,d. This lemma does not make f periodic: at even levels it is antiperiodic under y->y+N. Literal exponents in (7),(8) avoid losing precisely those signs. For an unmarked cycle the final value is epsilon x+B. Its exact closure may be replaced by delta_N((epsilon-1)x+B). (9) Indeed, whenever the product is nonzero all propagated leg values are in [0,d], so congruence of the final and initial values implies their equality. There is no surviving false winding state. At the marked component the final and initial values are instead inserted in the original dense row in (2); no closure delta is imposed. ## 4. Integral Kirchhoff flow and the actual mark Restore the ordinary cap only for the purpose of recording the physical graph. Its nodes have a canonical bipartition: W and cup nodes have two outgoing ports; pi and cap nodes have two incoming ports. Every original straight physical interval joins opposite types. Each physical cycle therefore has an EVEN number of nodes, including its cups and caps. Contracting these bivalent cup/cap nodes prematurely would hide this parity statement. Collapse every physical cycle to a vertex of a graph Gamma, and orient matching edge i from its pi cycle to its W cycle. Set w_i=r_i-a_i, -a_i<=w_i<=a_i. (10) An ordinary physical cycle closes if and only if its signed alternating sum of total degrees is zero. With the bipartition just specified, that defect is B_c=sum_(W on c)(d-a_i+r_i)-sum_(pi on c)(d-a_i+r_i) +d(#cups on c-#caps on c) =sum_(W on c) w_i-sum_(pi on c) w_i =(div_Gamma w)_c. (11) All d terms cancel because the two bipartite classes on a cycle have equal size. Each matching edge contributes with opposite signs to its two ends, so sum_c B_c=0 identically. Nonzero unmarked cycle contractions force their EXACT defects B_c=0, not just congruence modulo N. The omitted equation on the marked cycle then follows from the others. Thus (3) can be restricted EXACTLY to the bounded integral flow space w in ker(div_Gamma:Z^R->Z^C), |w_i|<=a_i. (12) There may be further quantum cancellations inside this support. The assertion is not that every flow gives a nonzero source term. On such a flow the marked endpoints are complementary. Let x be the SECOND coordinate of the original mark, so its first coordinate is d-x. Only now compare it with the ordinary cap in (2): mark(d-x,x)/ellV(d-x,x) =N^-1 q^(-d^2) Q^(dx). (13) This is the original specified mark, not a redefinition of it. Since d=-1 modulo N, it supplies a one-unit Fourier character. If instead the first marked coordinate were called x, its charge and constant phase would have the opposite displayed convention. ## 5. The exact shared-cycle Fourier compiler Insert (7) at every W or pi vertex of a physical component, and insert the monomials (2) at its cups/caps or marked endpoint. By (8), the dependence on x in each term is a SINGLE character q^[m_c(k)x], where m_c(k) is an explicitly determined integer affine function of the LOCAL Fourier indices k_v. All remaining factors consist of the positive product product_v p_(t_v,a_v,k_v), the original scalar endpoint/cup factors, and explicit q phases depending on the SAME matching labels and Fourier indices. For an arbitrary formal cycle one could expand its closure as delta_N((epsilon-1)x+B) =N^-1 sum_(h=0)^d q^[2hB+2h(epsilon-1)x]. (14) Thus its x sum is evaluated exactly by S_N(m)=sum_(x=0)^d q^(mx) = N if m=0 mod 2N, = 0 if m even but not 0 mod 2N, = 2/(1-q^m) if m odd. (15) For the ACTUAL source the odd case in (15) disappears for a proved reason. Every W/pi node has carrier parity d-2a=d modulo 2; every cup/cap and the dense mark has carrier parity d as well. The sign of the affine coordinate does not change that parity. Since the restored component has an even number of nodes, its total frequency m_c(k) is even for every Fourier tuple, at both level parities. The marked path has one fewer ordinary node and the mark supplies the last carrier. Thus the same conclusion holds before replacing the mark by its charged cap. The terms 2k and the closure terms in (14) do not alter the parity. Omitting a pivotal cup/cap carrier would destroy this argument. On a flow (12), let L_c(X) be the finite Laurent polynomial obtained by multiplying the ACTUAL continued ordinary vertex and cup/cap factors on c, with X=Q^x. It exists by this even-frequency result. Use the second marked coordinate for the variable on the marked cycle c_*. Let [X^b]_N denote cyclic coefficient extraction modulo X^N-1, summing every Laurent coefficient of exponent b modulo N. The full-grid lemma and (13)--(15) give A_(D,N)=q^(-d^2) N^(C-1) sum_(a,w:div w=0, |w_i|<=a_i) product_i[h0_(a_i)omega_(a_i)^epsilon_i] *[X_(c_*)^1]_N L_(c_*)(X_(c_*)) *product_(c!=c_*) [X_c^0]_N L_c(X_c). (16) Here C is the number of restored physical cycles. Every constant endpoint, cup, cap and source phase is included in L_c. For the marked cycle the Fourier sum contributes N and the original ratio (13) contributes 1/N; this explains the exact N^(C-1), including its phase q^(-d^2). Formula (16) is valid at BOTH level parities. It can be evaluated by cyclic convolution of coefficient arrays of length N, without enumerating all Fourier tuples. In an expanded form it is a finite sum with positive local p coefficients, the original scalar factors, explicit t_v-dependent phases, integral Kirchhoff constraints (12), and coupled Fourier congruences from (16). Those phases are not removed by positivity of the p's. ## 6. A joint energy, with every shared state retained Define the explicit positive comparison Z_cycle(N)=sum_(a,r) product_i h0_(a_i)^2 product_c |F_c(a,r)|^2. (17) Each cycle period in (17) is evaluated coherently BEFORE its absolute square. The matching labels and their magnetic indices remain common to both incident vertices and to all components they connect. If there are R original circles, the number of matching states is at most N^(2R), so finite Cauchy gives |A_(D,N)|^2 <= N^(2R) Z_cycle(N). (18) The circle half-twist phases have modulus one, but are removed only in this stated upper bound, not from the exact identity (3). This is one joint comparison energy for arbitrary fixed bridge width. It neither maximizes each vertex independently nor replaces each F_c by a product of column norms. To turn (17) into the desired geometric theorem, one must still control the coherent cycle periods with their shared labels and identify the resulting constrained action, including its phases, with the actual marked gluing equations. The real Legendre action of positive Fourier coefficients alone is not such an identification. A lower bound or contributing-cycle argument for (3) is still required; (18) allows complete cancellation in the original source. Audit: [original fixed-label cycles and full Fourier kernels](../experiments/audit_actual_matching_graph_shared_cycle_fourier_compiler.py). The exact Fourier compiler does not assert a global energy asymptotic or noncancellation of the source.

title: A finite angle-flow certificate for matching-edge smoothing
status: Sufficient angle-flow criterion for a smoothing rate gap
text: # A finite angle-flow certificate for matching-edge smoothing 30 October 2026. This note gives a sufficient, source-compatible strict capacity comparison after replacing ONE untwisted crossing-circle operator by L_1=I. It is not a theorem that every proper small-color subset has an exponential gap. In particular the finite test below has not been proved to follow from the labeled right-angled certificate for every matching edge. ## 1. Literal smoothing and the capacity being compared Start with the connected original marked source and labeled geometric certificate of the [complete-source theorem](general_signed_augmented_source_volume.md). Let one matching edge have its two actual ordered triangles (x,b,y), (x,c,y). Replacing its untwisted operator by L_1=I deletes these two triangles and identifies the two middle faces b,c. This is the literal identity on the two physical strands, with their original order. It is not an evaluation of the old source at unrelated b,c. Require for this lemma: * the resulting projection is connected; * the original two marked faces remain distinct; * b,c,x are distinct unmarked faces, and y is distinct from them (y may be a marked face); * all remaining incidences are the actual ones after this smoothing. No positive polyhedron for the smoothed graph is assumed. The [exact marked face coefficient](../papers/filling-bounds/README.md) still defines its complete source, including repeated incidences or bigons. A disconnected source, a merged pair of marked faces, and a retained half twist at the deleted port require separate treatment. They are not discarded or renormalized here. Write F(l_0,l_1,l_2) for the exact maximal-fold determinant rate from [the absolute source normalization](actual_original_boundary_stationary_character.md), section 6. It has logarithmic homogeneity one half. Set the two marked face variables to zero, and use one positive variable for every other face, with one common scale fixed. The smoothed capacity is Phi_sm = inf_l [sum_(remaining triangles t) F(l_t) -sum_(smoothed finite faces f) log l_f]. (1) Assume this infimum is attained at finite positive shared radii l. In particular the split labels b,c both have the SAME radius z>0. This is an explicit regularity hypothesis on the smoothed capacity; it is not supplied by the old circle packing. Let Phi_old denote the original packing evaluation, already proved to equal Vol(Y_original)/(2pi). ## 2. Angle duality with its absolute normalization For theta_j>=0 and sum_j theta_j=pi, put V(theta)=2 sum_j [Lambda(theta_j/2) +Lambda((pi-theta_j)/2)], Lambda(t)=-integral_0^t log|2sin u| du. The source-normalized local identity is 2pi F(l)=max_theta [sum_j theta_j log l_j+V(theta)]. (2) A zero l_j forces theta_j=0; its product theta_j log l_j is then interpreted by continuity. To prove (2), differentiate V on the open angle simplex: partial_j V=-log tan(theta_j/2), Hess V=diag(-1/sin theta_j). Thus the objective is strictly concave, and its critical point is exactly the source angle formula theta_j=2atan(l_j/sqrt(l_0 l_1+l_1 l_2+l_2 l_0)). The absolute constant is zero by F(l,0,0)=(1/2)log l and V(pi,0,0)=0. Continuity gives the one- and two-positive-face cases. Apply (2) at the positive minimizer in (1). The radius stationarity conditions say that the corners at every smoothed finite face have sum 2pi. Hence its actual local angles theta maximize total V subject to these face sums and the triangle sums pi, and sum_t V(theta_t)=2pi Phi_sm. (3) This also proves the required dual equality without an external duality theorem: (2) bounds any feasible total entropy above by the right side of (3), and the displayed local angles attain it. Split the merged face's corners into their OLD b-side and c-side sets. Write their sums as pi+Delta and pi-Delta, respectively. This split is part of the original incidence, not an arbitrary partition. The single merged-face constraint gives their sum, not their individual values. ## 3. A finite source-incidence feasibility test A corner transfer moves angle between two allowed corners of ONE remaining triangle. It preserves its triangle sum. Fixed zero corners and fixed pi corners are excluded. The graph of allowed face transfers joins two face labels when their allowed corners occur in one such triangle, retaining the original incidences. The possible face-divergence vectors are exactly those having zero sum on each connected component of this graph. One direction follows by summing the triangle transfers. For the other, route the required balances along a spanning forest. The path construction uses only actual remaining triangles; it is not a new quantum routing of a cut. There is also an exact finite test with prescribed corner slack. Give each allowed corner a lower bound e_tf>=0. For proposed face demands d_f, put r_t=pi-(fixed row sum)-sum_f e_tf, q_f=d_f-(fixed column sum)-sum_t e_tf. Nonnegative angles with these lower bounds, triangle sums and face demands exist if and only if r_t,q_f>=0, their total sums agree, and for EVERY subset S of the split face labels, sum_(f in S) q_f <= sum_(t incident to S) r_t. (4) Here fixed corner values are first subtracted from both their row and column demands. A triangle with repeated labels is still one row. To prove (4), use a finite network with capacities r_t from the source to triangle nodes, unlimited edges to their allowed face nodes, and capacities q_f from the face nodes to the sink. A finite cut is precisely one of (4), after minimizing over its triangle nodes. Augmenting along residual paths until none remains proves the converse and constructs the angles. Real capacities follow by the usual limiting argument from rational capacities on this finite network. In particular d_b=d_c=pi and d_f=2pi elsewhere tests a balanced DEGENERATE insertion. It is stronger than the merged 2pi condition. Feasibility alone gives no volume inequality: redistribution can lose entropy. The following test includes that loss. ## 4. Quantitative strict comparison Suppose every allowed movable corner of theta lies in [sigma,pi-sigma], sigma>0. Choose two actual corner directions D_bc,D_x with zero sum in each remaining triangle and face divergences div D_bc = e_c-e_b, div D_x = e_b+e_c-2e_x. (5) They are zero at the excluded corners. Such directions exist, for example, whenever b,c,x belong to the same allowed transfer component; they can be constructed by the preceding spanning-forest rule. Their finite norms, not just their existence, enter the test. Choose 0<eta<pi and set v=Delta D_bc+eta D_x. Require ||v||_infinity <= sigma/2, G := 2V(eta,pi-eta,0)+2eta log(l_x/z) -||v||_2^2/[2sin(sigma/2)] > 0. (6) Then the exact capacity comparison is Phi_sm <= Phi_old-G/(2pi) < Phi_old. (7) Proof. The adjusted old angles theta+v have sums pi+eta at b,c, 2pi-2eta at x, and the required unchanged sums elsewhere. Insert the deleted triangles with angles (eta,pi-eta,0) in their literal orders (x,b,y),(x,c,y). This is a feasible angle assignment for the original source. The new triangles are permitted boundary points; no positive geometric realization of this assignment is presumed. At the smoothed maximizer the entropy gradient at a movable corner is -log l_f plus a constant depending only on its triangle. The two old middle-face multipliers agree. The first variation on v is therefore EXACTLY 2eta log(l_x/z): the Delta term cancels. Taylor's integral remainder and the first inequality in (6) give sum_t[V(theta_t+v_t)-V(theta_t)] >=2eta log(l_x/z)-||v||_2^2/[2sin(sigma/2)]. (8) Add the two new entropies. Formula (2), evaluated at the original packing radii, bounds the entropy of every feasible original angle assignment by 2pi Phi_old. Equations (3), (6), (8) imply (7). This comparison retains the shared variables and the actual target face sums throughout. The test is not confined to zero imbalance. Indeed 2V(eta,pi-eta,0)=4eta log(1/eta)+O(eta). At Delta=0 the left positive term dominates the linear and quadratic costs for sufficiently small eta. Once a strict test succeeds, it continues to succeed under small changes of its regular input data.
