This is an openness statement about the explicit finite data subject to the hypotheses; it does not assert an open family of knot diagrams, or that every certified diagram satisfies the test. ## 5. Consequence and remaining source requirement The zero patterns created by smoothing need an explicit extension of the old local upper bound. At fixed nonnegative shared radii set A=x+y and retain the exact circle B_(N,a)=beta_a^2 D_a(x,b,y)D_a(x,c,y)P_s(x,y). There are precisely the following cases. * If A>0, the determinant-rate proof remains valid for every b,c>=0. A single positive matrix summand uses the exact LDL product, already treated separately in that proof. Its circle derivative is log(E_b E_c/D_xy)>=0, since E_b,E_c>=A and D_xy<=A^2. Thus the fold is still an upper bound, though strictness may be lost. The newly possible case b=c=0, xy=0 has EXACTLY B_(N,a)=A^d for every label: beta_a D_a=A^a and P_s=A^s. * If A=0 and b,c>0, P_s(0,0)=0 unless s=0. Even N therefore gives zero for every channel. At odd N only a=d/2 survives, beta_a=1, and B_(N,a)=(bc)^(d/2). Its rate is (1/2)log(bc), exactly the sum of the two fold rates F(0,b,0)+F(0,c,0). * If A=0 and b=0 or c=0, every channel contribution is zero. These statements include empty determinants at a=0; when A=0 the positive-degree forced factor still kills that channel. They do not apply the old strict geometric zero-pattern theorem to a new bigon. For a literal untwisted L_1 deletion satisfying the certificate, evaluate the EXACT smoothed positive face coefficients at the shared minimizer l in (1). The preceding cases bound every remaining local circle, including its beta factor, by its fold rate. There are only polynomially many channel choices, and the multiplicities, measure and mark have polynomial cost. Hence the whole smoothed complete source has upper rate at most Phi_sm and the strict gap (7). An identically zero local case is already stronger. Half-twist phases on retained ports may be bounded in modulus for this upper bound; they are not removed from the finite identity. This does not yet prove the proper-small-subset estimate needed for external colors N-h. A genuine L_h insertion has actual tridiagonal paths of displacement at most h-1. With the original outgoing/incoming first-head convention, displacement p imposes c=Q^p b, and its clock monomials shift face targets. At marked zero faces they can be Laurent; one must extract the shifted coefficient before setting those faces to zero. Their unwrapped intervals and possible Fourier aliases must still be controlled. A signed removed port also retains its actual braid. Neither those finite-source requirements nor arbitrary degenerate or JSJ smoothing limits follow from (7). Focused audit: [finite flow and source checks](../experiments/audit_actual_matching_smoothing_angle_capacity.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_matching_smoothing_angle_capacity_results.json). It checks 79 literal Morse box-deletion/face-identification maps; 74 exact rational Hall systems against an independent linear program (175,680 cut inequalities, including 26 infeasible systems); seven finite entropy-flow comparisons, four with nonzero imbalance; and 270 original degenerate channel factors through both parities. The entropy examples use stated combinatorial bipyramid/split incidences, not newly asserted labeled right-angled knot certificates. They audit the sufficient inequality, not its universal applicability. The attained shared-capacity and explicit finite-flow inequality hypotheses remain essential; no universal contraction or h>1 source estimate was inferred.

title: The boundary term and repeated monodromy sector of the Mellin equation
text:
# The boundary term and repeated monodromy sector of the Mellin equation 31 October 2026. The Fourier--Mellin construction packages the ordinary color invariants of a knot into a generating function. Its equation has a nonzero inhomogeneous term, determined by finitely many starting colors. That term is essential: after converting the equation to a homogeneous companion system, it provides a linear functional that detects the selected solution. For a knot with positive exponential growth of its Kashaev invariant, this homogeneous companion necessarily has at least two independent rational directions fixed by root monodromy. Thus a simple monodromy eigenvalue is not the reason its actual solution is selected. The selection also uses the prescribed source and the allowed expansion at the origin. The proof below keeps those data and explains why the Mellin and main-meridian realizations cannot be identified by merely renaming their variables. ## 1. The meridian equation and its ordinary colors Work over $\mathbb C(q)$ and set $Q=q^2$. The meridian multiplication operator $Y$ and shift $T$ satisfy \[ TY=QYT. 	ag{1} \] At level $N\ge2$, put $q_N=e^{\pi i/N}$ and $Q_N=q_N^2$. The marked meridian eigenvalue is $M=-q_Nx$, where $x$ is the exponential unrolled color parameter, and $Y=M^2$. Write $f_N(Y)$ for the actual reduced, zero-framed ADO state. Its fixed normalization is \[ f_N(1)=K_N,\qquad f_N(Q_N^r)=C_r(q_N)\quad(1\le r\le N), \qquad C_1(q)=1. 	ag{2} \] Here $K_N$ is the reduced Kashaev invariant, and $C_r(q)$ is the reduced ordinary invariant in dimension $r$. The equality at $r=N$ means $C_N(q_N)=K_N$. These are the [actual color specializations](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/root_orbit_pointing.md), with the [squared-meridian convention](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/even_meridian_norm_descent.md) retained. Choose a specified all-level annihilator, whose existence follows from the [finite cut-state construction](finite_sum_annihilator.md). After clearing its coefficient denominators and shifting its order once, write it as \[ P=\sum_{j=0}^{d}a_j(q,Y)T^j,\qquad a_j\in\mathbb C[q^{\pm1},Y^{\pm1}],\qquad d\ge1,\quad a_0a_d
e0. 	ag{3} \] Its root equation holds at all sufficiently large levels. Keeping $\mathbb C(q)$ as the coefficient field avoids assuming that a chosen operator descends in its coefficients to $\mathbb C(Q)$. For every fixed positive integer $n$, apply its root equation at $Y=Q_N^n$, taking $N>n+d$. Equation (2) gives a relation among fixed ordinary colors at infinitely many distinct $q_N$. Since those colors are Laurent polynomials, rational-function rigidity proves \[ \sum_{j=0}^{d}a_j(q,Q^n)C_{n+j}(q)=0 \qquad(n\ge1). 	ag{4} \] This is the color recurrence used below. Its coefficients, ordering, and initial colors are those of the specified knot equation. ## 2. Starting the generating series creates a nonzero source Let $A_q$ be the difference between the largest and smallest $q$ exponents in the collected Laurent monomials of $a_d(q,Y)$. Choose a fixed starting color \[ n_0\ge d+A_q+1, \qquad Z(q,X)=\sum_{n\ge n_0}C_n(q)X^n. 	ag{5} \] The series is initially formal at $X=0$. No convergence for generic $q$ is assumed. The choice of $n_0$ makes every substitution $a_d(q,Q^r)$ with $r\ge n_0-d$ nonzero. Indeed, distinct monomials $q^uY^v$ become $q^{u+2rv}$; a collision with different $v$ would require $2r\le A_q$. Monomials with the same $v$ were already collected. Let $S_Xg(X)=g(QX)$. The exact quantum-torus Fourier map is \[ \Phi(Y)=S_X,\qquad \Phi(T)=X^{-1},\qquad X^{-1}S_X=QS_XX^{-1}. 	ag{6} \] Write $a_j(q,Y)=\sum_m a_{jm}(q)Y^m$. Its ordered action on (5) is \[ A:=\Phi(P)=\sum_{j,m}a_{jm}(q)Q^{-mj}X^{-j}S_X^m, \qquad AZ=\mathcal B, 	ag{7} \] where \[ \mathcal B(q,X)= \sum_{j,m}a_{jm}(q)Q^{-mj}X^{-j} \sum_{r=n_0}^{n_0+j-1}C_r(q)Q^{mr}X^r. 	ag{8} \] To obtain (8), multiply (4) by $X^n$ and sum over $n\ge n_0$. For a term with shift $j$, the substitution $r=n+j$ leaves out exactly the colors $n_0,\ldots,n_0+j-1$. Those omitted terms are the inner sum in (8); it is empty for $j=0$. The factor $Q^{-mj}$ comes from the operator ordering in (6). The source is a Laurent polynomial in $X$, supported between $n_0-d$ and $n_0-1$. Its least coefficient is \[ [X^{n_0-d}]\mathcal B =C_{n_0}(q)a_d(q,Q^{n_0-d})
e0. 	ag{9} \] Only $j=d$ contributes to this coefficient. The second factor is nonzero by the monomial argument above, and $C_{n_0}(1)=1$ makes the first nonzero as well. Thus this finite-start construction has a nonzero source. Its least coefficient is a fixed nonzero rational function of $q$, so its specialization is nonzero at all but finitely many $q_N$. The source equation also determines the actual series uniquely in the prescribed space $X^{n_0}\mathbb C(q)[[X]]$. If a nonzero homogeneous difference had least exponent $r\ge n_0$, its image under $A$ would have a nonzero coefficient at $X^{r-d}$, namely $a_d(q,Q^{r-d})$ times that least coefficient. This is impossible. This is the [finite-start source construction](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/fourier_mellin_actual_source.md); it is stronger than choosing any rational solution of its root specialization. ## 3. Root rationality and the finite Fourier comparison The [actual root color-periodicity theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/cyclotomic_mellin_residue.md) gives $C_{n+N}(q_N)=C_n(q_N)$ for all $n\ge1$, including the multiples of $N$. Consequently, for $N\ge n_0$, \[ Z_N(X):=Z(q_N,X) = rac{\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^{N-1}C_r(q_N)X^r+K_NX^N} {1-X^N} -p_N^{\mathrm{pre}}(X),\qquad p_N^{\mathrm{pre}}(X)=\sum_{r=1}^{n_0-1}C_r(q_N)X^r. 	ag{10} \] This is the rational function with the same formal expansion at zero. Where the fixed operator specializes regularly, it satisfies $A_NZ_N=\mathcal B_N$ as a rational identity. It has at most simple poles at the $N$th roots of unity, and its residue retains the original scalar: \[ \operatorname{Res}_{X=\infty}Z_N(X) rac{dX}{X}=K_N. 	ag{11} \] Indeed the fraction in (10) tends to $-K_N$ at infinity, while $p_N^{\mathrm{pre}}$ has no constant term. The full modified ADO value remains $i^{N+3}K_N/N$ at completeness; (11) does not replace its whole meridian normalization by a different one. The central coordinates explain the limit of this Fourier comparison. At a primitive level-$N$ root, write \[ U=Y^N,\quad V=T^N,\qquad U_X=X^N,\quad V_X=S_X^N. 	ag{12} \] The algebra map (6) sends them to \[ \Phi(U)=V_X,\qquad \Phi(V)=U_X^{-1}. 	ag{13} \] In the rational main-meridian realization, $T$ acts by the root shift of $Y$, so $V=1$ and $U$ varies. Its Fourier image is therefore supported on $U_X=1$, with $V_X$ variable. In the rational Mellin realization, $S_X$ acts by the root shift of $X$, so instead $V_X=1$ and $U_X$ varies. In the original coordinates this is $U=1$, with $V=X^{-N}$ variable. These are two different central divisors, meeting at $(1,1)$. An isomorphism over a fixed center cannot equate their distinct annihilator ideals. At their intersection there is a genuine finite Fourier map. Its domain is the orbit ring $\mathbb C[Y^{\pm1}]/(Y^N-1)$, equivalently the functions on the $N$ meridian root points. A rational function may be used only when it is regular at those points; the actual $f_N$ is Laurent polynomial and meets this condition. Put \[ \mathscr F_N(h)=\sum_{r=0}^{N-1}h(Q_N^r)X^r \quad	ext{in }\mathbb C[X]/(X^N-1). 	ag{14} \] Termwise multiplication and cyclic reindexing prove $\mathscr F_N(Yh)=S_X\mathscr F_N(h)$ and $\mathscr F_N(Th)=X^{-1}\mathscr F_N(h)$. For $h=f_N$, this produces $K_N+\sum_{r=1}^{N-1}C_r(q_N)X^r$. It is precisely the class of the numerator \[ (1-X^N)(Z_N+p_N^{\mathrm{pre}}) =\sum_{r=1}^{N-1}C_r(q_N)X^r+K_NX^N. 	ag{15} \] modulo $X^N-1$. Thus the finite map compares the meridian orbit with the Mellin pole numerator. It does not evaluate $Z_N$ at a pole or identify their meridian neighborhoods. In particular it does not replace the retained normal coordinate of the [ramified Weyl fibre](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/ramified_weyl_fibre.md) by an ordinary orbit value. ## 4. Why the root clock cannot be lifted as a finite matrix gauge The distinction persists in the first quantum-normal direction. Vary the parameter through dual numbers by $Q=Q_N(1+\epsilon)$, $\epsilon^2=0$; the compatible half-root is $q=q_N(1+\epsilon/2)$. In the whole quantum torus, (1) implies \[ VU=Q^{N^2}UV=(1+N^2\epsilon)UV, \qquad [V,U]=N^2\epsilon UV. 	ag{16} \] Suppose a nonzero finite free matrix realization of the intersection fibre lifted through this parameter change, with both central actions reducing to identity. It would have $U=I+\epsilon E$ and $V=I+\epsilon F$, whose commutator is zero modulo $\epsilon^2$. Equation (16) instead gives $N^2\epsilon I$, a contradiction in characteristic zero. For the usual $N$-dimensional clock matrices the same obstruction follows by taking determinants in $TY=QYT$, which would require $Q^N=1$ rather than $1+N\epsilon$. This rules out lifting (14) as an ordinary finite matrix gauge through the quantum-normal direction. It does not rule out a comparison with differential normal operators or retained relative sources. The [first quantum-normal construction](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/first_quantum_normal_connection.md) includes a derivation because an off-root shift no longer has finite order. That derivation and its source cannot be inferred from the root Fourier matrix alone. ## 5. Positive growth forces two rational companion directions Assume now that the knot has positive exponential complete growth: \[ \liminf_{N	o\infty} rac1N\log|K_N|>0. 	ag{17} \] This is supplied, for example, by the established [strict-tree](../papers/conway-asymptotics/README.md) and [net-twist](../papers/conway-reductions/README.md) volume theorems for their stated knot classes. The next argument only uses (17). For every coefficient in (3), form the fixed Laurent polynomial $r_i(q)=a_i(q,q^{-2i})$. If it were nonzero, it would have a finite vanishing order $
u_i$ at $q=1$, and hence $|r_i(q_N)|\ge cN^{-
u_i}$ for all large $N$. Evaluate the actual root equation at $Y=Q_N^{-i}$. When $N>d$, its $i$th term is $r_i(q_N)K_N$ and all other terms are ordinary-color values. Those values are polynomially bounded in $N$ by the [positive ordinary-color trace](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/regularized_kashaev_period.md). The fixed Laurent coefficients are bounded on the root torus, so this equation would bound $K_N$ polynomially as well, contradicting (17). Therefore every $r_i$ is identically zero. Laurent-polynomial division now gives the exact right factor \[ P=B(Y-1),\qquad A=\Phi(B)(S_X-1). 	ag{18} \] Indeed the $i$th coefficient of $B(Y-1)$ is $b_i(q,Y)(Q^iY-1)$. This is the [boundary-column argument](peripheral_normal_period.md), applied here to the positive growth already known. In particular $A(1)=0$. Any fixed left shift used to give $A$ nonnegative $S_X$ order is applied to its source as well and preserves this identity. In that normalization $A$ has positive $S_X$ order. Otherwise it would be multiplication by a nonzero rational function, which cannot annihilate $1$. Retain the canonical homogeneous equation of the sourced Mellin system: \[ \widehat A=(S_X-\sigma(\mathcal B)/\mathcal B)A, \qquad \sigma g(X)=g(QX). 	ag{19} \] For every sufficiently large $N$, both $1$ and $Z_N$ are rational solutions of (19). They are independent over $\mathbb C(X^N)$: if $Z_N$ were central, then $A_NZ_N=Z_NA_N(1)=0$, contradicting $\mathcal B_N
e0$. This gives two independent vectors in the monodromy eigenspace, not merely two scalar formulas. Let $\mathsf C_N$ be the forward solution companion of (19), let $Jf=(f,S_Xf,\ldots)^t$ be its finite jet vector, and set $\mathsf T_0=\mathsf C_N^{-1}S_X$, $H_0=\mathsf T_0^N$. The positive order of $A$ makes (19) have at least two companion coordinates. Both $J1$ and $JZ_N$ are fixed by $\mathsf T_0$. If these vectors were dependent over $\mathbb C(X)$, their first coordinates would force $JZ_N=Z_NJ1$. Their second coordinates would then give $S_XZ_N=Z_N$, again making $Z_N$ central. Thus \[ \dim_{\mathbb C(X)}\ker(H_0-I)\ge2, \qquad \left. rac{d}{dt}\det(tI-H_0)ight|_{t=1}=0. 	ag{20} \] The source and the companion endpoints exclude only finitely many specialization levels. Equation (20) concerns this canonical homogenization of a denominator-cleared reduced-state operator. It does not assert a Jordan block, specify the full dimension of the eigenspace, or apply to every alternative minimal operator. Nor does it contradict selection of the actual series. The extra constant solution is outside $X^{n_0}\mathbb C[[X]]$. The source equation and that starting condition still distinguish $Z$ from the larger rational solution space. At roots, the [cyclotomic quantum-jet theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/mellin_cyclotomic_jet_uniqueness.md) retains further source and pole-lattice data when selecting the entire rational function. ## 6. The source row still detects the selected solution Write the normalized Mellin operator as $A=\sum_{j=0}^{r}c_j(q,X)S_X^j$. Its canonical homogenization (19) has order $r+1$. On its companion vectors there is the explicit row \[ \ell= rac1{\mathcal B}(c_0,\ldots,c_r),\qquad \ell Jf=Af/\mathcal B. 	ag{21} \] Equation (19) says that this quotient is shift-invariant. In companion form, $\sigma(\ell)\mathsf C=\ell$, so at a root \[ \ell H_0=\ell,\qquad \ell J1=0,\qquad \ell JZ_N=1. 	ag{22} \] The row kills the image of $H_0-I$ but does not kill the selected vector. Therefore the natural map from the kernel to the cokernel of $H_0-I$ is nonzero on $JZ_N$. This is the [observable-source criterion](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_mellin_normal_source_rigidity.md), which remains valid even though the simple-root test in (20) fails. It detects a specified direction rather than asserting semisimplicity of the entire monodromy. The algebraic boundary module explains the distinction. Before localization it is $\Delta_Y=\mathcal R_Q/\mathcal R_Q(Y-1)$, where $\mathcal R_Q$ is the quantum torus (1). Passing to rational meridian coefficients kills it because $Y-1$ becomes invertible. Its Fourier image is $\mathcal R_X/\mathcal R_X(S_X-1)$, which survives over $\mathbb C(q,X)$ as a rank-one trivial difference module. The two rational localizations thus retain different boundary data. The row (21) is an observable of the sourced Mellin presentation; it is not automatically a row for a localized main-meridian companion. The [source-symbol comparison](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/source_symbol_duality_and_presentation.md) also gives explicit examples where an extra homogeneous factor changes that test. What remains is a source-and-lattice comparison, not a choice of a preferred eigenvalue by its size or multiplicity. A proposed geometric realization must retain the finite-start source, the cyclotomic pole numerator, the normal derivatives, and the marked period functional through the change of polarization. The root Fourier identity proves the finite numerator comparison, while (16) explains why it does not supply the quantum-normal lift. Neither (20) nor (22) identifies a geometric factor of the classical main-meridian operator.

title: Every actual auxiliary color in the arbitrary-plat source compiler
text: # Every actual auxiliary color in the arbitrary-plat source compiler 30 October 2026. The original augmented-plat compiler extends to ALL ordinary auxiliary colors 1<=n<=N and signed local coupons R^epsilon L_n, epsilon in {0,+1,-1}. Its value and first-normal columns, inverse measures, color phases and source are explicit. No unknown recoupling inverse remains. The additional normal and color factors have uniform polynomial bounds; all exponential factorial profiles are displayed rather than absorbed in that claim. This is a finite ROOT-LEVEL source theorem at arbitrary fixed bridge width. It does not assert a coherent global gap or a uniform complex color interpolation, and is not yet an arbitrary-plat filling theorem. In particular the exact root normal below must not be confused with the generic-q normal of the whole original pointed invariant. ## 1. The circle polynomial is fixed by the original typed source Use d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, x=q^d, kappa=q^(d^2/2). The ordinary n-dimensional auxiliary module has its ACTUAL pivot K_n^(1-N), with no new factor 1/n. The typed threading [2,1,1,2] followed by that pivot trace gives, as a full physical matrix, L_n=l_n(Omega), l_n(z)=(-1)^(n-1) P_(n-1)(z), P_r(z)=U_r(z/2), P_0=1, P_1=z, P_(r+1)=z P_r-P_(r-1). (1) Thus L_1=I and L_2=-Omega. This normalization, including the sign, is the proved [original mixed-circle identity](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_crossing_circle_source_and_filling.md). It is not a replacement of an ordinary module by an N-dimensional ADO component at a putative meridian value. For an actual physical pair degree S set t=min(S,2d-S) and translate the first index by max(0,S-d), exactly as in the complete compiler. Use the canonical physical columns v_j=f(c_j), w_j=f'(c_j), c_j=q^(2j+1)+q^(-2j-1), nu_j=(-1)^j q^[j(j+1)]. All j=0,...,t are retained, grouped by equal nodes. The only double pair is j,l=d-j. The self-paired odd-level node is SIMPLE. Ordinary colors also retain the unpaired simple nodes killed by L_N. ## 2. An exact generic finite formula for the normal column The root formula for v_j is the q-Hahn sum in the [complete phase compiler](actual_augmented_plat_phase_compiler.md). To compute its first NORMAL, one must first use the actual generic highest-weight-d family, not differentiate a root-only simplification. Let zeta vary near q, Q=zeta^2, x=zeta^d and F_b=(Q;Q)_b. Define R_(j,a)=F_(N-j+a-1) F_(N-a-1) / [F_(N-j-1) F_(N-1)], C_(j,u,a)(zeta)=(-1)^a x^(u-2a) Q^[a(t-u)+a(a-1)/2] R_(j,a) [u choose a]_Q [t-u choose j-a]_Q/[t choose j]_Q, C_(j,u)(zeta)=sum_(max(0,u-t+j)<=a<=min(j,u)) C_(j,u,a). (2) Every factorial index lies in 0,...,d, so these are regular finite functions at the actual root. They are the normalized actual generic Clebsch columns. One direct derivation starts with the highest vector of degree j, whose a-th coefficient is (-1)^a x^-a Q^[a(j-1)-a(a-1)/2] R_(j,a). Apply F_tot^(t-j)/F_(t-j), with F_tot=F tensor I+K^-1 tensor F. The q-binomial expansion contributes x^[-(t-j-u+a)]Q^[a(t-j-u+a)] [u choose a][t-u choose j-a]. Its first component is x^[-(t-j)] [t choose j], which is a unit. Dividing by it gives precisely (2). Thus its eigenvalue is lambda_j(zeta)=zeta^(2N-1-2j)+zeta^(-2N+1+2j). (3) At the root, R_(j,a)=Q^[a(a-j)] [j choose a]_Q, recovering the previous physical column and its exact Fourier phase. This equality is used for the VALUES, not for their zeta derivatives. For a double pair j<l=d-j, put D=zeta d/dzeta. Then exactly w_(j,u)=[D C_(j,u)(q)-D C_(l,u)(q)] / [-2N(q^(2j+1)-q^(-2j-1))]. (4) Indeed C_(j,u)=f_u(zeta,lambda_j(zeta)); subtracting derivatives cancels the common derivative of f with respect to zeta. The remaining eigenvalue gap derivative from (3) is the displayed denominator. This retains the actual generic confluence. The differentiated sum in (4) is fully explicit. Write H_b=D log F_b=-2 sum_(r=1)^b r Q^r/(1-Q^r), H_0=0, Hbin(v,w)=H_v-H_w-H_(v-w). At the root each summand derivative is its original root value times Gamma_(j,u,a)=d(u-2a)+2a(t-u)+a(a-1) +H_(N-j+a-1)-H_(N-j-1)+H_(N-a-1)-H_(N-1) +Hbin(u,a)+Hbin(t-u,j-a)-Hbin(t,j). (5) Thus (4) is a difference of two finite factorial/Fourier sums with known q-harmonic coefficients. No chosen solution of a homogeneous recurrence or unidentified normal amplitude has been inserted. ## 3. Explicit bilinear measures and every signed mixed kernel Put CalP_t(z)=product_(r=0)^t(z-c_r) and B_t=(-1)^t s_t^2. At a simple node define sigma_j=x^t nu_j CalP_t'(c_j)/B_t. At a double node c=c_j=c_l put Q_j=CalP_t/(z-c)^2 and sigma_j=x^t nu_j Q_j(c)/B_t, rho_j=-(d-2j)/[2(q^(2j+1)-q^(-2j-1))], eta_j=rho_j+Q_j'(c)/Q_j(c). (6) These are the actual Christoffel--Darboux measures. In particular sigma_j never vanishes. The bilinear Gram block of (v_j,w_j) is sigma_j [[0,1],[1,eta_j]], with inverse sigma_j^-1 [[-eta_j,1],[1,0]]. The value rho_j is the spectral logarithmic derivative of the original normalized crossing R/kappa. For EVERY auxiliary color n and either sign, the entire contribution of a double node to R^epsilon L_n is therefore kappa^epsilon nu_j^epsilon /sigma_j * { [l_n'(c)+(epsilon rho_j-eta_j)l_n(c)] v_j v_j^T +l_n(c)(v_j w_j^T+w_j v_j^T) }. (7) A simple node contributes kappa^epsilon nu_j^epsilon l_n(c_j) v_j v_j^T/sigma_j. (8) Proof: in the actual Jordan chain, a function A(Omega) has matrix [[A(c),A'(c)],[0,A(c)]]. Multiplying by the displayed bilinear inverse gives sigma^-1[(A'-eta A)vv^T+A(vw^T+wv^T)]. Here A(c)=kappa^epsilon nu_j^epsilon l_n(c) and A'(c)=kappa^epsilon nu_j^epsilon[l_n'(c)+epsilon rho_j l_n(c)]. This proves (7), including epsilon=-1. It is a bilinear physical identity; conjugating a column would give the wrong coupon. Summing (7),(8) over ALL distinct nodes gives the original full matrix. In particular n=N collapses to the complete-circle formula: at a double node l_N(c)=0, leaving its specified first normal, and at an unpaired simple node l_N(c)=0. The self-paired simple value is treated separately. This reduction checks, rather than assumes, the complete-image formula. ## 4. Color dependence and uniform polynomial factors The color dependence is explicit and coherent. With theta_j=(2j+1)pi/N, l_n(c_j)=(-1)^(n-1) sum_(b=0)^(n-1) q^[(2j+1)(n-1-2b)]. (9) All its n-dependent phases remain. The derivative is the derivative of the SAME polynomial in z; it is not a derivative of a chosen eigenvalue lift. Away from sin theta=0 it can also be written l_n'(2cos theta)=(-1)^(n-1) [sin(n theta)cos theta-n cos(n theta)sin theta] / [2sin(theta)^3]. (10) At the odd self-node c=-2 use its polynomial limit, with l_n(-2)=n. There is no 0/0 cancellation left to a numerical prescription. Uniformly for every 1<=n<=N and every real node in [-2,2], |l_n(c)|<=n, |l_n'(c)|<=n(n^2-1)/6. (11) For the second bound group the finite Laurent expression for U into pairs 2cos(m theta). Its z derivative is m sin(m theta)/sin theta, whose absolute value is at most m^2 by the finite geometric sum. The sum of these positive-frequency squares is n(n^2-1)/6. This also proves the endpoint bound by continuity, without dividing by an endpoint sine. Every H_b in (5) has magnitude O(N^2(1+log N)), since sin(pi r/N)>=2min(r,N-r)/N. The remaining exponents in (5) are O(N^2). The denominator of (4) has modulus at least eight. Consequently, with Ebar_(t,j,u) the sum of the two positive q-Hahn envelopes at j,l, |v_(j,u)|<=E_(t,j,u), |w_(j,u)|<=C N^2(1+log N) Ebar_(t,j,u). (12) The known node gap bound also gives |rho_j|<=N^2/8 and |eta_j|<=C N^3. Thus every color and every extra normal factor in (7) is polynomially controlled, uniformly over the ENTIRE physical color interval, with normal order at most one on each local column. The inverse measure is NOT hidden in this statement. If a_j=|1-Q^(2j+1)|, its exact magnitudes are unpaired simple: |sigma_j|=s_(t-j)s_(t+j+1)/(s_t^2 a_j), double: |sigma_j|=N s_(t-j)s_(t+j-d)/(s_t^2 a_j^2), odd self-paired: |sigma_j|=N s_(t-j)^2/s_t^2. (13) Its phase is explicitly fixed by (6) or the simple product. All factorial indices are below N. Therefore an all-input bound for (7),(8) is a fixed polynomial times the sum of the products of the stated column envelopes divided by |sigma_j|. The exponential growth of those factorial profiles has not been proved to disappear. ## 5. Arbitrary fixed plats and the remaining filling problem Insert (7),(8) at every original augmented region of any fixed 2k-head plat and perform the literal wire contractions. Retain the original cup, ordinary caps, unrestricted marked cap, pivots and external line. The whole-source integer-degree argument permitting the final marked-pair restriction is the same as in the complete compiler. This yields an exact finite formula for EVERY physical auxiliary-color tuple (n_1,...,n_b), not merely a coefficientwise upper envelope or a complete-color value. Expanding (4),(5),(9) makes all color/normal couplings explicit: they are the original finite Fourier factors, factorial weights and bounded-order q-harmonic prefactors. For a fixed diagram the number of discrete variables and the total number of normal factors are fixed. Contracting does not increase that normal order with N. One may also use the finite polynomial values (1) directly; the two expressions are identities of the original matrices. This supplies a concrete all-color input to the existing exact full-twist resolution for any fixed signed slopes p_i. A prospective geometric threshold T(D) concerns the fixed skeleton and the sizes of those integer twists, not the quantum level N. The compiler alone gives no such threshold or nonzero geometric period. In particular an explicit finite formula is NOT automatically the uniform holomorphic packet required by analytic filling transfer. The naive expression sin(n theta)/sin theta is singular at the odd self-node theta=pi for nonintegral n; its cancellation at integer n does not authorize that continuation. A valid complex-color packet must specify its whole finite continuation and prove its uniform estimates, preserving all these endpoint and normal contributions. Likewise the polynomial bounds in (11),(12) leave the column and inverse-measure factorial rates present. A geometric global gap, source-preserving complex deformation, selected nonzero amplitude germ and actual marked regulator identification are separate tasks. The new result removes the UNKNOWN mixed local kernel and normal formula; it does not replace those analytic and geometric proofs. Audit: [generic normals and all original mixed signed operators](../experiments/audit_actual_mixed_augmented_plat_compiler.py). Fresh exact finite-field checks pass N=2,...,12: 143 physical blocks, 2,904 canonical value entries, 1,177 generic-confluence normal entries, and 231 full signed mixed-color operator identities. The normal columns from (2)--(5) are compared with independent continuant derivatives. Every compiled matrix is compared with the original coproduct Casimir polynomial and original signed crossing matrices. The generic matrix identities do not supply a uniform complex-color estimate or coherent gap.

title: Moving-period factorial normals along logarithmically escaping heads
status: Actual factorial normals for logarithmically escaping heads
text: # Moving-period factorial normals along logarithmically escaping heads 30 October 2026. source estimate. The marked Gamma factorial remains controlled when a head has imaginary part of order N log N. This is a bound for the actual factorial factors and fixed quantum jets. It does not provide a packet for a polynomial whose critical points merge, or cross an original zero or pole divisor. ## 1. The precise source factors and growing charts Use EXACTLY the interpolant Fhat_P and its logarithmic mark in [the moving-period factorial theorem](actual_moving_period_factorial_normals.md), with P=pi i/(pi i/N+epsilon), d=N-1 fixed. Put L_N=1+log N. Fix positive constants delta,C. The new interior arguments satisfy delta <= Re(z/N) <= 1-delta, |Im(z/N)| <= C L_N. (1) An exterior argument may instead have |Re(z/N)|<=C and delta<=|Im(z/N)|<=C L_N. Choose a fixed integer shift k_N=O(N) which puts its real part in a smaller interior strip, and use the original unit recurrence for that SAME function. The shift stays fixed when epsilon moves. Fixed physical integer arguments 0,...,d are also allowed, by their exact finite factorials. For a fixed finite number of these arguments, there are constants c,C_1, independent of N and the arguments, such that on |epsilon| <= rho_N=c/[N^2 L_N^2] (2) every factor is holomorphic and nonzero, and its relative value and inverse are bounded by C_1. In particular, for every fixed j, |partial_epsilon^j Fhat_(P(epsilon))(z)|_(epsilon=0) <= j! C_1 (C_1 N^2 L_N^2)^j |Fhat_N(z)|. (3) The same assertion holds for products and inverses of a fixed number of those factors, their normalized local square-root gauges, and retained powers zeta^E with |E|<=C N^2 L_N^2. All exponential root values and integer-linear characters remain part of the source. ## 2. A direct differentiated Gamma-product bound The convergent product defining G_P gives, at FIXED z, partial_P Log G_P(z)=-z/P +sum_(k>=1) { k psi(Pk+z+1)-k psi(Pk-z) -(2z+1)/P }. (4) It suffices first to work on |P-N|<=c/L_N. All Gamma arguments have positive real part there. Their real parts are at least c_delta N for k=1 and comparable to Nk for k>=2. Take K=ceiling(C_2(1+|z|/N)), C_2 sufficiently large. For k<=K, the uniform right-half-plane digamma expansion psi(w)=Log w+O(1/|w|) applies. Both arguments have size at least c_delta N. Their modulus ratio and the difference of their marked arguments are bounded uniformly: the large imaginary parts enter with opposite signs, and the real-part distance to the strip endpoints is fixed. Hence |psi(Pk+z+1)-psi(Pk-z)|<=C_delta, and the first K terms of (4) have total size O(K^2+K L_N)=O(L_N^2). This includes the case that z stays bounded in scaled coordinates. For k>K, |z+1|/|Pk|<1/4. Expanding the two digammas about Pk shows that their 1/(Pk) term is (2z+1)/(Pk), while their 1/(Pk)^2 terms are EQUAL and cancel. More explicitly the latter coefficient of psi(w+a) is -a^2/2+a/2-1/12, which has the same value at a=z+1 and a=-z. The uniform next remainder gives |k[psi(Pk+z+1)-psi(Pk-z)]-(2z+1)/P| <=C(1+|z|)^3/(N^3 k^2). (5) One may obtain (5) directly by differentiating the convergent Gamma-ratio expansion on a fixed larger relative P disk; the same 1/k cancellation and uniform |z/(Pk)|<1/4 give its bound. Summing (5) costs O((1+|z|/N)^3/K)=O(L_N^2). The initial -z/P term is smaller. Therefore |partial_P Log G_P(z)|<=C L_N^2. (6) The marked elementary exponential converting G_P to Fhat_P has P derivative -pi i z(z+1)/(2P^2), also O(L_N^2). Since |P'(epsilon)|=O(N^2), |partial_epsilon Log Fhat_P(z)|<=C N^2 L_N^2. (7) Disk (2) lies inside the P neighborhood just used. Integrating the actual logarithmic derivative along that disk proves the two-sided relative bound, and Cauchy's formula gives (3). No principal logarithm is reset, and no root-only reflection is differentiated. For completeness, the digamma estimates used here follow from the same uniform complex-sector Stirling expansion used to construct the original product. The Gamma arguments lie in the right half-plane, so its fixed sector can include angles up to pi/2. The finite sum and tail bounds above make explicit their dependence on the growing imaginary argument; a compact-set estimate is not silently reused. ## 3. Exterior rows, fixed endpoints and original gauges For an exterior row the O(N) fixed unit shifts introduce factors 1-exp[2(z+j)Log zeta]. Their scaled imaginary parts remain at least delta/2 on (2). Thus |exp[2(z+j)Log zeta]/(1-exp[2(z+j)Log zeta])|<=C_delta. Each logarithmic epsilon derivative has size O(N L_N), so the whole shift product costs O(N^2 L_N), within (7). Large or small absolute magnitudes of individual factors are NOT bounded away: only their relative variation is being estimated. These magnitudes and all phases remain in the root value. For a fixed physical integer n<=d, the original finite product has logarithmic derivative O(N^2 L_N), including n=d. Its known relative disk contains (2). This keeps the endpoint N-1 fixed rather than replacing it by P-1. Combining the bounds proves the statement for any fixed product, ratio and locally normalized square root. A marked monomial zeta^E has logarithmic derivative E, so it has precisely the additional cost claimed after (3). Consequently the actual moving-factorial cup and cap factors at heads of size O(N log N) have polynomial fixed-jet cost whenever their arguments obey these hypotheses. The same is true of their specified boundary gauges. This does not give a relative estimate for a SUM of white-polynomial terms, and does not replace the actual large generic white by its root-colliding small partner. ## 4. What this resolves at the resonant framing boundary For an actual clock X(r) asymptotic to c r^(2e), e=+1 or -1, on a marked ray r=N R with R in a compact set avoiding zero, its head z=Log X/(2Log q0) has |Im(z/N)|=O(log N). On a fixed logarithmic sheet with bounded real part it falls into the nonreal exterior class above for all sufficiently large N. Thus its large imaginary lift by itself is tame for the actual factorial normals. No bounded-lift hypothesis is falsely invoked. In contrast, a clock tending to one can give a factorial argument approaching an integer zero or pole. Nor does this theorem control a white numerator's endpoint saddle or its resonant coefficient sum. Those need their own exact small-argument products or turning analysis. The original finite support, generic normal, cotangent measure and selected global period remain unchanged and unproved by this estimate. The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_moving_period_factorial_logarithmic_escape.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_moving_period_factorial_logarithmic_escape_results.json) retain 12 independent Gamma-tail comparisons, 48 two-sided relative disk checks, 12 genuine fixed-index normals, 12 exact marked unit recurrences and 12 actual opposite-head cup gauges, at 85 digits. The maximum identity error was 2.18e-75. These are diagnostics of the specified function; the uniform estimate is proved above. The estimate concerns relative factorial/cup quantities and their genuine fixed jets. It does not bound an absolute magnitude, establish a turning packet or give a global period.

title: The exact factorial interpolant with a moving quantum period
status: Exact two-period section and finite unipotent jet transport
text: # The exact factorial interpolant with a moving quantum period 30 October 2026. The existing convergent Gamma product extends to the ACTUAL moving quantum parameter. It matches every original finite integer factorial, including the fixed endpoint d=N-1, before taking derivatives. On specified complex index charts it has uniform relative bounds and polynomial cost for every fixed genuine q derivative. The index d stays N-1 when the analytic period moves; no root reflection is differentiated as though d were the moving period minus one. ## 1. The same convergent product at a complex period Fix N>=3, q0=exp(pi i/N), and let zeta=q0 exp(epsilon), P=pi i/Log zeta=N/[1+N epsilon/(pi i)], Q_P=exp(2pi i/P)=zeta^2. (1) The logarithm of zeta is the local one pi i/N+epsilon. Use the analytic Log P near the positive number N and Log(Pk)=Log P+log k. Define, initially where all Gamma arguments have positive real part, G_P(z)=(2pi/P)^z Gamma(z+1) *product_(k>=1) Gamma(Pk+z+1) /[Gamma(Pk-z)(Pk)^(2z+1)], Fhat_P(z)=exp[pi i z(z+1)/(2P)-pi i z/2]G_P(z). (2) This uses the infinite Gamma product from the [exact interpolation theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/exact_factorial_interpolation_and_complex_contours.md), not its finite Barnes product whose number of factors was an integer. The log of the kth factor is locally uniformly O(k^-2), with leading term -z(z+1)(2z+1)/(6P^2 k^2). Its 1/k coefficient vanishes. The Gamma-ratio expansion therefore proves local uniform convergence, including P and z derivatives. The function is holomorphic and nonzero on the initial domain and G_P(0)=1. The Gamma functional equation and the convergent sine product give EXACTLY G_P(z+1)/G_P(z)=2sin(pi(z+1)/P), Fhat_P(z+1)=[1-Q_P^(z+1)]Fhat_P(z), Fhat_P(0)=1. (3) They also define its meromorphic continuation in z. Consequently, with n a fixed nonnegative integer, Fhat_P(n)=(zeta^2;zeta^2)_n. (4) In particular (4) holds for EVERY 0<=n<=d=N-1 on a neighborhood of the original root. This is equality of generic analytic germs, not merely of their root values. The marked power Q_P^z is always exp(2z Log zeta). There is also an exact SECOND difference equation, G_P(z+P)=-2sin(pi z)G_P(z), Fhat_P(z+P)=[1-exp(2pi i z)]Fhat_P(z). (4a) To prove its constant, first take -1<Re z<0, so both z and z+P are in the defining Gamma domain. The quotient of the products truncated at k=K is (2pi/P)^P/[Gamma(z+1)Gamma(-z)] *Gamma(P(K+1)+z+1)Gamma(PK-z) /[P^(2PK)Gamma(K+1)^(2P)]. The last ratio tends to (2pi)^(1-P)P^P by the same uniform complex-sector Stirling formula, with all powers marked by Log P. The Gamma reflection identity then gives -2sin(pi z); equivalently that elementary Gamma identity follows from its convergent product and the sine product already used in (3). Meromorphic continuation proves the first equation globally. The exponential in (2) has P-shift quotient i exp(pi i z), proving the second equation with the displayed scalar ONE. The complex-P reflection is consequently exact as well: G_P(z)G_P(P-1-z)=P, Fhat_P(z)Fhat_P(P-1-z) =P exp[pi i z(z-P+1)/P]. (4b) Indeed the z derivative of the first logarithm, truncated at K, telescopes to psi(PK+z+1)-psi(P(K+1)-z), which tends to zero. Its constant is G_P(P-1). Differentiating (4a) at z=0 gives G_P'(P)=-2pi. Differentiating (3) at z=P-1 gives G_P'(P)=-(2pi/P)G_P(P-1), hence the constant is P. The marked exponentials in (2) then give the second equation of (4b). ## 2. The complex-period asymptotic is uniform Let K be a compact subset of 0<Re x<1. Uniformly for z=Nx, x in K, and P in a sufficiently small relative complex disk about N, put y=z/P. On a slightly smaller disk y stays in a fixed compact of the same strip. The DIRECT Stirling proof in the interpolation theorem then gives Log G_P(z)=P J(y)+(1/2)Log(2P sin(pi y)) +pi cot(pi y)/(12P)+O_K(|P|^-3), (5) where J'=Log(2sin(pi y)) has its original mark, continued from 0<y<1. Formula (5) is proved for complex P term by term: the Gamma arguments z,Pk+z,Pk-z remain in fixed right-half-plane sectors; the kth Stirling remainder is O_K(|P|^-3 k^-3). Summing it is uniform. The sine product sums the leading terms and the cotangent identity sums the 1/P terms just as before. This argument does not interpolate an identity known only at integer periods. The remainder is holomorphic on a larger relative P disk, so its P derivative at FIXED z is O_K(N^-4) by Cauchy's formula. The derivative of the leading term is partial_P[P J(z/P)]=J(y)-y J'(y). The two elementary exponential factors in (2) also have bounded P derivatives on this chart. Thus |partial_P Log Fhat_P(z)|<=C_K. (6) Since |P'(epsilon)|=|P|^2/pi=O(N^2), (6) implies |partial_epsilon Log Fhat_(P(epsilon))(z)|<=C_K N^2 (7) for fixed marked z=Nx in this interior chart. The logarithm here is the relative one at epsilon=0. There is no principal-root or dilogarithm reset when epsilon varies. ## 3. Fixed integer shifts cover the nonreal exterior rows Let K be any compact scaled-index set with |x|<=M, |Im x|>=delta>0, z=Nx. (8) Choose on each of finitely many smaller charts an integer k_N, FIXED as epsilon moves, with |k_N|<=C_K N and (z+k_N)/N in a compact subset of 0<Re x<1. Such charts cover K by shifting the real part into the middle of the strip. For k_N>=0, use the exact formula Fhat_P(z)=Fhat_P(z+k_N) /product_(j=1)^(k_N)(1-Q_P^(z+j)); (9) for k_N<0 use the reciprocal-direction finite product. These are evaluations of the SAME meromorphic function by (3), not new independent factorial choices. For epsilon on the disk used below, all intermediate (z+j)/P have imaginary part bounded away from zero. Their real and imaginary parts remain bounded. Therefore each finite sine or Pochhammer factor in (9) and its inverse is bounded by constants depending only on K. Its logarithmic epsilon derivative is -2(z+j) zeta^[2(z+j)]/[1-zeta^[2(z+j)]]=O_K(N). There are O_K(N) factors. Combining this with (7) proves the same O_K(N^2) logarithmic derivative for these exterior rows. In particular negative rows and rows above N are controlled when their scaled imaginary parts stay away from zero. The statement does NOT give a bound across their real integer zeros or poles. Those are retained by the exact interpolation. ## 4. The fixed endpoint and all physical factorials For every original fixed integer 0<=n<=d, use (4) itself. On a sufficiently small disk about epsilon=0, partial_epsilon Log Fhat_P(n) =sum_(j=1)^n -2j zeta^(2j)/(1-zeta^(2j)). (10) At the root |1-q0^(2j)|>=c min(j,N-j)/N. Perturbing epsilon by at most c/[N^2(1+log N)] keeps every denominator comparable to its root value. Summing the displayed elementary bounds gives |partial_epsilon Log Fhat_P(n)| <=C N^2(1+log N), (11) UNIFORMLY in n, including n=d=N-1. No asymptotic estimate at the endpoint x=1 is being inferred from an interior compact. The finite index n, and specifically d, is fixed throughout. At the root one may use the already proved exact identity with N-1-z for evaluating root values. It is NOT an identity with that same fixed endpoint after P moves. For example its generic integer factorial factors have the nonzero logarithmic derivatives (10). Replacing the fixed d by P-1 during differentiation would change the source and is not part of this construction. The second period also supplies an exact normal-transport equation. Put H_N(z)=partial_epsilon Fhat_(P(epsilon))(z)|_0, with z FIXED. Since P'(0)=iN^2/pi, differentiating (4a) gives H_N(z+N)=[1-exp(2pi i z)]H_N(z) -(iN^2/pi)partial_z Fhat_N(z+N). (11a) The undivided identity remains meaningful at the physical zeros. The last term is essential: the left argument in (4a) moves with P. Thus actual generic normals do not obey a root-only N-shift rule obtained by omitting that index derivative. More generally put Delta=N-P and c(z)=1-exp(2pi i z). There is the exact local analytic identity Fhat_P(z+N)=exp(Delta partial_z)[c(z)Fhat_P(z)]. (11b) Indeed z+N=(z+Delta)+P, so this is just (4a) at z+Delta. Modulo epsilon^(J+1), Delta belongs to the ideal (epsilon), and the exponential in (11b) is the FINITE differential operator sum_(j=0)^J Delta^j partial_z^j/j!. On a chart where c is a unit, divide by the root multiplier and write U=c^-1 exp(Delta partial_z)c =exp[Delta(partial_z+c'/c)]. The conjugation identity follows by applying partial_z to c times a test function. Its logarithmic connection has explicit simple poles at the integers. On the order-J jet module, U-I raises the epsilon filtration and therefore (U-I)^(J+1)=0. Its inverse is the finite geometric series in -(U-I). This is an actual unipotent transport of finite quantum jets, with the differential correction (11a) at order one. The localization excludes the original c-divisors; the statement does not remove physical support zeros, prove convergence of an infinite jet expansion, or select a global degree cycle. The two exact shifts themselves form a flat rank-one difference connection. With a_P(z)=1-exp[2pi i(z+1)/P], one has a_P(z+P)=a_P(z) and c(z+1)=c(z), so applying the unit shift and the P shift in either order gives the same multiplier. At P=N, their compatibility includes the literal cyclotomic norm product_(j=1)^N(1-exp[2pi i(z+j)/N]) =1-exp(2pi i z). The Gamma product (2) chooses a section of this connection. These equations alone do not establish global uniqueness of a section: a factor periodic under both shifts preserves them. Nor do they determine the original source period or its cycle. ## 5. Uniform relative disks and genuine normal bounds Consider a fixed finite list of factorial arguments, each either * a fixed original integer between 0 and N-1; * z=Nx in a fixed compact of the interior strip; or * z=Nx in a fixed compact satisfying (8), continued by (9). All indices are held fixed when the generic parameter varies. Affine O(1) offsets are allowed by enlarging the compacts slightly. For sufficiently small c_K>0, on |epsilon|<=rho_N=c_K/[N^2(1+log N)] (12) every listed factorial is nonzero and holomorphic, and C_K^-1 <= |Fhat_(P(epsilon))(z)/Fhat_N(z)| <= C_K. (13) The same holds for any fixed finite product or quotient of the listed factors. Equations (7),(9),(11), integrated along the epsilon segment, prove (13), with a consistent relative logarithm. Cauchy's formula on (12) proves for every fixed j |partial_epsilon^j Fhat_(P(epsilon))(z)|_0 <=C_(K,j)[N^2(1+log N)]^j |Fhat_N(z)|. (14) Inverse factorials have the corresponding relative bound. In particular the entire assertion holds on the smaller actual normal disk |epsilon|<=c N^-10, at cost at most C_(K,j)N^(10j). The marked factors exp(pi i z), zeta^[z(L-z-1)] and the original physical cup scalar N zeta^(-d^2) cause no further difficulty: L and all indices are O(N), so the epsilon derivative of their logarithms is O_K(N^2), and higher derivatives follow on (12). Thus the original continued cups and inverse cups formed from these factors also satisfy (13),(14). No unit phase is discarded. One can specify the formerly ambiguous off-grid symmetric gauge as well. For a fixed integer L<N, set b_L(epsilon,z)=zeta^[z(L-z)] Fhat_P(z)Fhat_P(L-z)/Fhat_P(L), g_L(epsilon,z)=[b_L(epsilon,z)/b_L(0,z)]^(1/2). (15) Use the analytic square root equal to 1 at epsilon=0. Whenever the two index arguments satisfy the preceding hypotheses, (13) on a smaller disk makes this a specified holomorphic unit with the same relative jet bounds. It is symmetric under z->L-z and agrees with the original physical gauge at every admissible integer index. Its continuation is now fixed by (2), rather than inferred from bounded values on a finite integer set. At epsilon=0 the displayed phases cancel exactly, giving b_L(0,z)=G_N(z)G_N(L-z)/G_N(L). The already proved FIXED-root reflection therefore gives b_d(0,z)=1 meromorphically, also at noninteger z. This is useful for evaluating the root cup. It does not say that b_d(epsilon,z) is constant when P moves. In fact (4b) gives the exact fixed-endpoint correction b_d(epsilon,z)=P/Fhat_P(d) *exp[pi i z(N-P)/P] *Fhat_P(d-z)/Fhat_P(P-1-z). (16) The final quotient retains the difference between the original fixed d=N-1 and the moving endpoint P-1. Formula (16), or its derivative, may be used for boundary transport; replacing that quotient by one away from the root changes the genuine normal. ## 6. Application scope at the slightly nonreal geometric degree For the actual channel cup, the needed arguments are r=a-h and 2a-r, while the physical cups use v,d-v,l,d-l. In the joint deficient geometric corridor take a small but fixed NONZERO imaginary part of the degree. Then r/N and (2a-r)/N lie in nonreal exterior compacts, with opposite imaginary signs; the physical cup arguments have real parts strictly inside (0,1). The remaining factorials F_a,F_m,F_(2a),F_d have fixed integer indices below N. The lemma therefore controls all these explicit boundary factors and their genuine generic derivatives together. It does not justify crossing their real degree poles, deform the original support cycle, or prove a nonzero geometric contribution. Source assembly must still use the actual large-partner white columns and all original tensor marks. The present result is the moving-period analytic input for that assembly, not a replacement for its finite tensor identity or its global period argument. ## 7. Finite checks and scope The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_moving_period_factorial_normals.py) and its [results](../experiments/actual_moving_period_factorial_normals_results.json) check the actual generic integer factorials, independent Gamma/Barnes evaluations, relative disks, fixed-endpoint derivatives, exterior gauges, second-period and complex-period reflection identities, and fixed-N first and second normal transport. Its largest relative identity error at 85 digits was below 5.3e-82. These finite checks support, and do not replace, the proofs above. The moving-period theorem does not transport degree globally across retained divisors or identify a contributing quantum cycle.

title: The native highest-weight energy has a geometric action
status: Local energy cells; global phase gap retained
text: # The native highest-weight energy has a geometric action 30 October 2026. The exponential native projector cost is already geometric in a simple physical block. Its exact normalization also shows why a general comparison cannot assign a positive volume to every normalized magnetic summand or discard the phases at a maximum. ## 1. Exact highest-weight energy, both parities Put q=exp(pi i/N), d=N-1, s_r=product_(h=1)^r 2sin(pi h/N), and choose 0<=j<=floor(d/2). In the physical degree t=j the original normalized column is a highest vector. Its exact entries are f_u=C_j(q;j,u)=q^(ju) s_j/(s_u s_(j-u)), 0<=u<=j. (1) This follows directly from the original generic highest-vector ratio: at the root its negative-index Pochhammer factors give q^(u^2) [j choose u]_(q^2), and the Gaussian binomial has phase q^[u(j-u)] and positive magnitude s_j/(s_u s_(j-u)). The generic source is specialized only after this calculation. The actual Christoffel--Darboux measure of this simple degree block is |sigma_(j,j)|=s_(2j)/s_j^2. (2) For 2j<d, cancel the last factor in the original formula s_(2j+1)/(s_j^2 |1-q^(4j+2)|). For the odd simple midpoint 2j=d, the separately retained measure N/s_j^2 is the same expression, since s_d=N. No zero denominator is evaluated in this cancellation. Therefore its native rank-one projector norm is exactly E_(j,j)=sum_(u=0)^j W_N(j,u), W_N(j,u)=s_j^4/[s_(2j)s_u^2 s_(j-u)^2]. (3) For j<d-j this is the degree-t=j block of the completed cluster projector, not the singular individual projector on larger degrees. For 2j=d it is the degree-t=j block of the isolated midpoint projector. Formula (3) does not maximize over the other physical degrees of either operator. ## 2. Its complete local variational profile Let J(x)=integral_0^x log(2sin(pi y))dy. The endpoint-controlled factorial estimate log s_r=N J(r/N)+O(log N), uniform for 0<=r<N, gives, with xi=j/N and x=u/N, N^(-1)log W_N(j,u)=e(xi,x)+O(log N/N), e(xi,x)=4J(xi)-J(2xi)-2J(x)-2J(xi-x). (4) This is uniform on 0<=x<=xi<=1/2, with continuous endpoint values. For fixed 0<xi<=1/2 the action is strictly concave in 0<x<xi: e_x=2 log[sin(pi(xi-x))/sin(pi x)], e_xx=-2pi sin(pi xi)/[sin(pi x)sin(pi(xi-x))]<0. (5) Its unique maximum is x=xi/2. The actual discrete support contains a point within 1/N of this maximum, and has at most N points. Bounding (3) between its largest summand and N times that summand therefore proves, whenever j/N tends to xi in [0,1/2], lim N^(-1)log E_(j,j)=m(xi), m(xi)=4J(xi)-J(2xi)-4J(xi/2). (6) This statement includes both level parities. Moreover m'(xi)=2 log[cos(pi xi/2)/cos(pi xi)]>0 (0<xi<1/2), m(0)=0, m(1/2)=-4J(1/4)=v8/(2pi). (7) For even N=2h and j=h-1, the actual measure in (2) is 1/sin(pi/N); for odd N=2h+1,j=h it is one. This polynomial difference does not change the common folded limit (7). Thus the native exponential obstruction is not restricted to odd levels. ## 3. Four actual ideal tetrahedra at the folded color Write Lambda(a)=-integral_0^a log|2sin b|db, so J(x)=-Lambda(pi x)/pi. At xi=1/2, (4) becomes 2pi e(1/2,x) =4[Lambda(pi x)+Lambda(pi(1/2-x))] =4 Vol T(pi x,pi(1/2-x),pi/2), 0<x<1/2. (8) The tetrahedra in (8) have positive angles summing to pi. They also glue to an explicit convex ideal octahedron O_x. In the upper half-space boundary take its six ideal vertices to be 0, infinity, 1, -1, zeta, -zeta, zeta=exp(2pi i x). (9) The four unit-circle vertices form a Euclidean rectangle. Their unit-hemisphere plane separates the other two vertices. The upper half is the ideal quadrangular pyramid with apex infinity; reflection in that hemisphere gives the lower half with apex zero. Split the base along the diameter from 1 to -1. The two upper tetrahedra have the Euclidean triangle (1,zeta,-1), or (1,-zeta,-1), as a horospherical triangle at infinity. Each has angles pi x,pi(1/2-x),pi/2, up to permutation. Reflection gives two more tetrahedra of the same volume. These four tetrahedra fill the convex hull in (9). One can check the supporting planes directly: the vertical halfspace over each rectangle edge contains the origin, because the rectangle contains its center. It therefore contains ALL six vertices. Reflecting that halfspace in the unit hemisphere fixes the four rectangle vertices and exchanges zero and infinity, so the four lower face halfspaces contain all six vertices as well. Their eight triangular faces form the octahedral boundary. Along a shared rectangle edge, the two interior dihedral angles sum to either 2pi x or pi-2pi x, both strictly less than pi. The remaining pyramid edges have angle pi/2. Thus the joined boundary is locally convex; equivalently its eight triangular face planes support all six vertices. There is no hidden negative-volume piece. It follows that 2pi e(1/2,x)=Vol(O_x). At x=1/4 its eight faces form the regular ideal octahedron and its volume is v8. Equation (5) gives this as the unique maximum in this family. This is a geometric interpretation of ONE native degree-block energy, not a claim that this octahedron is already a cell in the supplied link complement. ## 4. The compulsory face subtraction away from the fold The same interpretation is signed for other colors. The elementary duplication identity Lambda(2a)=2Lambda(a)-2Lambda(pi/2-a) converts (4), for 0<x<xi<1/2, to 2pi e(xi,x) =4 Vol T(pi x,pi(xi-x),pi(1-xi)) -4Lambda(pi(1/2-xi)). (10) The second term is forced by the original measure (2). It is positive before its subtraction, since Lambda is positive on (0,pi/2). At x=0 the tetrahedron flattens and e(xi,0)=-(2/pi)Lambda(pi(1/2-xi))<0. (11) Consequently no representation of EVERY CD-normalized magnetic summand's action as a sum of nonnegative ideal-cell volumes can be correct without additional boundary terms or cancellations. This does not prevent the completed energy from having a positive geometric maximum: (6),(7) prove that its maximum is strictly positive. It identifies a necessary normalization in any such argument. ## 5. What a shared-variable action must retain For general physical degree and channel, the exact local energy is sum_u |C_j(t,u)|^2/|sigma_(t,j)|. On strict compacts where the selected ordinary packet applies, its summand has the action 2 Re Phi_xi(tau,nu)-kappa(tau,xi), (12) where kappa is the leading logarithm of the ACTUAL measure. Here tau, nu and xi are real admissible scaled physical indices; the complex packet supplies their selected action, not a different complex-degree operator norm. In the two chambers supplied by its factorial formulas, kappa=J(tau-xi)+J(tau+xi)-2J(tau), tau+xi<1, kappa=J(tau-xi)+J(tau+xi-1)-2J(tau), tau+xi>1. (13) The odd self-paired endpoint has the corresponding limit 2J(tau-1/2)-2J(tau). Polynomial factors in the finite measures do not contribute to (13). Formula (12) describes a normalized summand; the sum over u and the sum over physical degree are still to be taken. If a positive comparison energy is constructed by sewing these actual columns, its candidate action is the SUM of (12), together with the remaining original boundary weights, restricted to the SAME magnetic wire variables and exact affine degree constraints used in that sewing. Taking separate maxima in tau or nu before sewing changes that variational problem. Neither the existence of such a useful global comparison nor its equality with the manifold's angle-volume problem is proved here. The selected geometric framing generally gives COMPLEX magnetic coordinates. The localization theorem puts them in the selected physical tube, but does not put them on the real grid defining this positive energy. An identification with a real angle polytope, or a justified deformation of the original sum, is therefore an additional step; the local complex packet alone supplies neither. There is a further exact local warning about stationarity. Equation (1) has the marked highest-weight action Phi_high(xi,x)=J(xi)-J(x)-J(xi-x)+pi i xi x. At the energy maximum x=xi/2, partial_x Phi_high=pi i xi, exp(partial_x Phi_high)=exp(pi i xi). (14) At the folded value this multiplier is i, although the real energy derivative vanishes. Real-energy stationarity constrains the modulus of a transport multiplier; it does not by itself impose its marked phase or a full complex gluing equation. In a real link network those phases may cancel through the actual shared incidence and boundary characters, but that requires a separate proof. This example does not assert that an open column ought to have trivial boundary momentum. Thus the missing global bridge is precise: construct the actual sewn energy with its signed face terms and shared variables, and prove that its stationarity, INCLUDING the retained phase and peripheral conditions, gives the degree-one geometric gluing. The local octahedral volume and the correctly normalized summands alone do not establish that bridge or a nonzero original quantum period. ## 6. The larger full folded cost is twice an ideal cube volume The separate [full magnetic-energy theorem](actual_matching_edge_magnetic_energy_profile.md) now computes the full folded operator rate as 5v3/pi, with effective volume 10v3, for the odd simple projector and the actual even completed pair. This maximizes over physical degree and is strictly larger than the highest-weight block cost in (8). Here is an explicit local polyhedron with that larger two-copy volume. In Minkowski coordinates with form (-+++), let V_epsilon=(sqrt(3),epsilon_1,epsilon_2,epsilon_3), epsilon_i in {+1,-1}. These null vectors project to the eight Klein vertices of the cube [-1/sqrt(3),1/sqrt(3)]^3. The four vertices with product epsilon_i=+1 form a regular ideal tetrahedron: every distinct pair has the same Lorentz product, and the signed coordinate symmetries permute its vertices. Its face opposite V_epsilon has normal n_epsilon=(1,-sqrt(3)epsilon_1, -sqrt(3)epsilon_2,-sqrt(3)epsilon_3), <n_epsilon,n_epsilon>=8, <V_epsilon,n_epsilon>=-4sqrt(3). Reflection in that face sends the opposite vertex to V_epsilon-2<V_epsilon,n_epsilon>n_epsilon/8 =2V_(-epsilon). (15) Thus the four adjacent corner tetrahedra are also regular ideal tetrahedra, congruent to the central one. They fill the cube without overlap. Indeed the central tetrahedron has the four Klein inequalities epsilon dot x>=-1/sqrt(3), for sign triples of product +1. Inside the cube, two such inequalities cannot fail simultaneously: adding them would violate one coordinate bound of the cube. The part failing one inequality is precisely the tetrahedron with its opposite cube corner and the three neighboring central vertices. This gives the usual central tetrahedron and four corner tetrahedra as an actual geometric partition. Each original cube edge lies in one regular tetrahedron and has dihedral angle pi/3. Along each triangulated square-face diagonal, three tetrahedral angles add to pi. This is the regular ideal six-square-faced cube, with its stated angle data. Consequently this regular ideal cube has volume 5v3, and TWO copies have volume 10v3. This is an exact geometric interpretation of the local full folded COST. It supplies no face pairing, cusp marking, degree-one chain, or volume upper inequality for the original link complement. Attaching the local cube to a source diagram remains a separate shared-incidence problem. Focused audit: [original highest vectors, CD measures and ideal shapes](../experiments/audit_actual_native_magnetic_energy_local_geometry.py). It verifies 817 original finite highest-vector entries with their phases, 167 bilinear measures, 23 even/odd folded measure formulas, and all four actual tetrahedron cross ratios. The global sewing and phase-matching problem is not a conclusion of these checks. The cube addition also checks all four Lorentz reflections (15) exactly. The theorem concerns a degree block. It does not identify cells in the actual source complement, a real-grid geometric saddle, or a global volume equality. The cube volume is a local boundary-cost interpretation. It is not identified with the right-angled matching polyhedron; the topology of those constructions remains distinct.

title: The actual graph complement from one rectified core and octahedra
text: # The actual graph complement from one rectified core and octahedra 29 October 2026. This is a general GEOMETRIC theorem for the literal ordered noncrossing (NC) cubic sources. It gives the actual complete hyperbolic volume, rather than a scalar-vertex volume surrogate. Its input is a finite positive right-angled ideal core certificate. It does not prove the growing-color quantum asymptotic. Let Gamma be a connected plane cubic graph in the original NC source class, with b black and b white vertices and E=3b edges. Keep a crossing circle on each physical edge box. Suppose Q is a convex right-angled ideal polyhedron with the following labeled medial incidence: * Its ideal vertices x_e are the edges e of Gamma. * At every vertex v of Gamma there is a triangular face T_v with the three incident edge labels. * At every face f of Gamma there is a polygon F_f following its edge boundary. Every polyhedral edge separates a T_v from an F_f. The certificate includes the labeled oriented face cycles and positive supporting-plane inequalities. In particular a matching unlabeled polyhedron or cusp count is not sufficient. Such a Q will be called the ideal rectified core; this term means the ideal medial polyhedron, not the untruncated projective polyhedron used in some literature. Then the ACTUAL retained-circle source link L_Gamma(e), with any fixed signed edge twist integers e, has a complete hyperbolic metric and Vol(S^3 minus L_Gamma(e)) = 4b v8 + 2 Vol(Q). (1) The topology and peripheral crossings in this assertion are those of the original cups, caps and edge boxes. No quantum twist has been removed. Equation (1) is the target for an eventual full-source limit, not a proof of that limit. ## 1. A finite explicit octahedron on an ideal triangle Use the Lorentz product of signature (-,+,+,+). Normalize the three future null lifts a,b,c of a triangular face so that their pairwise products are -1. This is possible uniquely by positive rescaling: the three scale products are prescribed positive numbers. Let n be its outward unit spacelike normal. The regular ideal octahedron on the OTHER side of this face has three further vertices a' = b+c+sqrt(2)n, b' = c+a+sqrt(2)n, c' = a+b+sqrt(2)n. (2) These are future null vectors. Opposite pairs (a,a'), (b,b'), (c,c') have product -2 and every other pair has product -1. Thus the six vectors are Lorentz isometric to the standard regular ideal octahedron: four independent vectors determine an isometry by their Gram matrix, and the remaining two satisfy the same linear equations. The choice of +n places its interior outside Q. The three octahedral faces adjacent to the attaching face merge with the corresponding F_f faces. Indeed their third vertices have the form a+b+sqrt(2)n. If m is the normal of F_f along the edge ab, then <m,a>=<m,b>=<m,n>=0, the last equality being the right-angle condition. Thus all three vertices lie in that same supporting plane. The remaining boundary faces are an opposite WHITE triangle (a',b',c') and three SHADED triangles S_(v,e_a)=(a,b',c'), and cyclically. (3) Their outward unit normals are respectively n_white=2n+(a+b+c)/sqrt(2), n_a=n+sqrt(2)a, and cyclically. (4) Their incident products vanish. Equations (2)--(4) prove directly that all the surviving boundary dihedral angles are right angles. Attach an octahedron along EVERY T_v. This is an abstract gluing of convex cells along full ideal faces. The union is topologically a ball: the attaching triangles have disjoint interiors, and the same statement holds after small cusp truncation. We do not need to assume that all developed octahedra in a chosen global drawing have disjoint interiors. The intrinsic cell metric and the actual face identifications below are enough to construct the complete manifold. Flat boundary seams are merged only as intrinsic coplanar faces. Each original F_f is an ideal polygon. An attached coplanar triangle lies outside one of its sides, with its third ideal vertex on the empty ideal-boundary interval between that side's endpoints. Different sides have disjoint such intervals. These attachments therefore form an embedded ideal polygon with twice as many vertices. This also justifies the merged white-face isometries used below. ## 2. The complete labeled bowtie cell Call the resulting ball P. It contains Q and exactly 2b octahedra, with disjoint interiors in its intrinsic cell decomposition. Hence Vol(P)=Vol(Q)+2b v8. (5) It has 3E ideal vertices: E original x_e and three new vertices for each of the 2b original graph vertices. Its shaded faces are the 2E triangles S_(v,e). Its white faces are the 2b opposite octahedral triangles and the b+2 expanded old face polygons, hence E+2 in total. Every boundary edge separates a white and a shaded face. The boundary has 6E edges and Euler characteristic 2. For each edge e=vw, the two shaded triangles S_(v,e),S_(w,e) meet at x_e. They are precisely the two sides of its retained crossing disk. Their other vertices correspond to the two physical strand arcs at that end of the box. At each trivalent graph vertex the three original nested cup/cap arcs connect the three incident disks in a triangle. Consequently the white-face and cusp incidence is exactly the Fisher expansion T(Gamma), as independently traced in [the actual boundary construction](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_six_pants_boundary_torsor_and_sewing.md). This is a reversible topological cut: shrink each opposite white triangle toward the original vertex cup/cap matching; trace each expanded F_f along the original planar region; restore each pair of shaded triangles as its crossing disk. It recovers the literal NC diagram. In particular it does not use an arbitrary incidence permutation in place of the original ordered ports. Take two copies P^0,P^1 with opposite orientations. Glue each WHITE face across the copies by its labels. At e=vw an even box twist glues S_(v,e) to S_(w,e) within each copy, fixing x_e and matching the actual two strand positions. An odd twist uses the opposite copy and exchanges these two outer strand positions. These are exactly the disk maps from the original two-strand box; the same orientation rule is written explicitly for theta in [the marked-theta geometry](actual_marked_theta_link_and_angle_geometry.md). Because every shaded face is an ideal triangle, each prescribed vertex bijection is an isometry. Around every actual boundary edge the alternating white and disk maps give four right angles. At an old flat seam the two copies supply two angles pi. Internal attaching faces already have smooth neighborhoods. Thus all finite edge and face neighborhoods in the glued cell metric are hyperbolic. ## 3. Simultaneous horospheres and completeness Completeness requires more than the angle sums. At an original ideal vertex x_e the Q link is a Euclidean rectangle. Its two opposite sides belong to T_v and T_w, and have equal length on EVERY horosphere. Normalize its horosphere so that this length is 1. Do this independently at each original ideal vertex. On each triangular T_v, all three corner horocycle segments now have length 1: they are its canonical mutually tangent decoration. Equality of opposite rectangle sides shows there is no incompatibility between the two triangles at x_e. Equip each attached regular octahedron with its canonical decoration having side length 1 at every cusp square. Its three old vertex horospheres then agree with those just chosen on Q. Its new vertices use that same canonical decoration. Every S_(v,e) consequently has the canonical decoration at ALL THREE corners. Every shaded face pairing, including an outer-vertex exchange, preserves it. White pairings preserve decorations because they join identical copies. After uniformly shrinking these horospheres, they are disjoint and the complement of their ends is compact. The ideal links glue as compact nonsingular Euclidean surfaces. They are orientable, and the reversible link cut identifies them as the link's cusp tori. There is no dilation holonomy. Their ends are complete standard hyperbolic cusps. This proves completeness and finite volume of the literal link complement, with volume twice (5), establishing (1). Further full twists are crossing-disk collar homeomorphisms while the circle remains drilled. They change the preferred peripheral marking by the actual integral shear. They do not change the unmarked complete volume. The quantum twist phases and any later filling slopes must still retain that shear. ## 4. Algebraic input and an explicit nondegenerate example The input is finite real-algebraic data: future null vertex lifts, spacelike outward face normals, incidence equalities, strict supporting inequalities, the labeled convex face cycles, and vanishing Lorentz products at adjacent faces. A finite convex-hull/incidence check certifies the stated Q. Formulae (2)--(4) use only arithmetic and positive square roots. No limiting geometric realization or a choice of formal peripheral series is needed for this complete anchor. For the cube graph, the core is explicitly the convex hull in the Klein ball of (±1,±1,0)/sqrt(2) and their coordinate permutations. (6) Its six square planes are ±X_i=1/sqrt(2). Its eight triangular planes are ±X_1±X_2±X_3=sqrt(2). The corresponding Lorentz normals have norms squared 1/2 and 1, respectively; each incident square/triangle pair has product zero. Every vertex is ideal, and the strict nonincident supporting inequalities check directly. Thus it is a positive ideal right-angled cuboctahedron with the required cube labels. Here b=4 and Vol(actual augmented cube link)=16v8+2Vol(Q_cube). (7) The [exact audit](../experiments/audit_actual_nc_graph_rectified_core_geometry.py) checks this certificate and all eight octahedral attachments, their merged supporting planes, right angles and the actual resulting 36-vertex/72-edge/38-face bowtie incidence. The general proof is the cell construction above, not extrapolation from this example. The theta graph has a degenerate triangular core rather than a positive three-dimensional Q. Its separately proved four-octahedron construction has volume 4v8; it is not being passed through the strict hypothesis here. ### The input class is closed under actual vertex grafts Two such positive cores can be glued along triangular faces by the specified three-port bijection, putting their interiors on opposite sides of the common plane. The adjacent white polygons merge because their dihedral angles add to pi. The resulting union is convex. For an explicit proof, the two convex cores lie in opposite closed halfspaces and intersect exactly in the common triangle T. If x,y are in different cores, minimize d(x,z)+d(z,y) over z in T. This function tends to infinity when z escapes to an ideal end, so a minimum is attained at a finite point. Every finite seam point is locally convex because the right angles add to pi; T has no finite vertices. The minimizing broken path therefore straightens locally across the seam to the ambient geodesic. It is a single geodesic, contained in the union. Points in the same core are already joined there by a geodesic. This proves convexity. Its ideal end vertices and the remaining right-angled boundary faces have exactly the medial incidence of the planar three-edge vertex sum of the two graphs. The canonical unit decorations agree at the seam. Volumes add, and the finite certificate is transported by the explicit face isometry. This gives a constructive closure operation on the geometric input class, not an existence assumption for every planar graph. When the operation uses the ordered interval/outer-face graft of [the NC cube insertion](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_nc_spin_one_flow_order_certificate.md), it also retains the actual original source topology. In particular, start with the literal cube and repeatedly insert an ordered cube at any allowed interval vertex. Equivalently take the theta source followed by k>=1 such cube insertions. The resulting genuinely branching family has b=1+3k and a core formed from k copies of Q_cube. Its actual hyperbolic volume is Vol(S^3 minus L_Gamma(e)) =(4+12k)v8+2k Vol(Q_cube). (7a) The choices include arbitrary finite ordered binary branching trees. This establishes positive core existence and actual geometry throughout that family. The fixed-level spin-one theorem does not yet provide its all-N quantum limit. ## 5. The precise remaining quantum target For every graph satisfying the input certificate, the desired equality now has a geometrically specified right side: lim_N (2pi/N)log |K_N(L_Gamma(e))| =4b v8+2Vol(Q). (8) The exposed-mark first-normal source formula is exact, but it does not yet prove (8). The shared Q contribution is a global graph term; independent theta scalars cannot supply it. Growing-label control of the full magnetic first normal, coherent noncancellation, and the outer-color packet needed for fillings remain to be proved. For coverage only, the ideal medial polyhedron appears as the truncated rectification in [Belletti's paper](https://msp.org/agt/2025/25-2/agt-v25-n2-p01-p.pdf). Fully augmented right-angled cell decompositions and octahedral subclasses are discussed in [Purcell's exposition](https://users.monash.edu.au/~jpurcell/papers/expos-auglinks.pdf). No proof or quantum-invariant identification from those sources is used in the construction above, and no novelty of the geometric operation is asserted. The cube audit determines the six square faces from the source’s opposite black/white ribbon orders. In the vertex-graft argument, minimizing paths use the exact common triangle and cannot escape to an ideal end.

title: Exact three-port source sewing before and after the root normal
text: # Exact three-port source sewing before and after the root normal 29 October 2026. An actual NC/Morse vertex substitution has a generic three-port elimination, with an explicitly normalized theta denominator. At a supported boundary it preserves the original FIXED first normal: the new raw marked scalar is the product of the two old raw scalars divided by the positive actual marked theta scalar. This is not root multiplication of circle coupons. Unsupported boundaries retain their explicit open-column/source jets before an actual six-head support identity proves their complete-circle contribution zero. The theorem is channelwise at arbitrary N, with all three correlated boundary labels and original normal factors retained. It supplies a survival transfer when the two actual input sources are known. It does not prove a new all-N asymptotic for an unsolved primitive cube block, identify arbitrary six-pants boundary maps, or complete the graph-volume problem. ## 1. A literal NC vertex substitution, including the pointing Let A,B be ordered NC/Morse graphs of the [corrected exposed-source theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_nc_morse_graph_first_normal_source_reduction.md).
