text: # The original boundary source has exactly two flat face directions 30 October 2026. On the labeled original right-angled matching graph, the finite boundary models detect every homogeneous magnetic direction except two explicit face potentials. Two neighboring original physical heads give a primitive slice for those directions. This statement includes the closed source and the common fixed-charge two-cut lattice; arbitrary routed extra factors are excluded. Together with the separate local curvature estimates, the result gives a uniformly invertible transverse Hessian for the actual nonzero ROOT source product at the resonant boundary sample, in a shrinking folded-channel window. It does NOT say that this sample is stationary, perform a Gaussian contraction, or assign a coefficient in the original relative period. ## 1. The literal graph and its homogeneous lattice Use the labeled certificate and original reference meridian of the [common boundary chart](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_original_network_resonant_boundary_chart.md). Let Delta be its plane cubic graph, with R matching edges D and 2R vertices. The [full original source](general_matching_graph_full_normal_source.md), section 2, identifies this SAME graph with the actual W/pi contraction: matching edges carry V_(2a_i), and all other edges carry V_d, d=N-1. Cups, caps, reversals, and the cyclic order at every vertex are retained. No new routing braid is inserted. For an oriented typed edge of highest weight L_e center its head by z_e=h_e-L_e/2. The actual degree equation at each vertex is exactly sum_out z_e-sum_in z_e=0. (1) Changing an edge orientation replaces z_e by -z_e. A literal cup or cap replaces h by L_e-h, which makes precisely this sign change in centered variations. Thus degree-two bends can be contracted without changing the integral HOMOGENEOUS lattice. Half-integral centered basepoints when L_e is odd do not change that lattice: its variations remain integral. For fixed channel labels, the retained half twist multiplies the original circle term by its exact scalar omega_a^epsilon. The full-source identity already includes the physical reversal in pi. Consequently half twists do not add a magnetic constraint, remove a graph edge, or add a free magnetic variable to (1). Their scalar phases remain in the source. Write B for the oriented incidence matrix of Delta. Its homogeneous lattice is V_Z=ker_Z B, dim_C V=|E|-|V|+1=R+1. (2) The certificate makes Delta connected. Its white faces are the actual projection regions, not freely identified copies of developed faces. There are R+2 of them. Let P_f be one additive potential per white face, modulo a common additive constant. Assign to an oriented edge the difference of its left and right face potentials, with the sign chosen to agree with (1). This gives an integral isomorphism Z^(white faces)/Z(1,...,1) = V_Z. (3) Here is an elementary proof of surjectivity, including primitivity. Given an integral divergence-free edge assignment, integrate it along paths in the dual graph from a fixed face. Around a dual face, the sum is the original vertex divergence, hence zero. Every closed dual walk on the sphere is a sum of these oriented face boundaries; cutting it at repetitions and filling its simple components proves this directly. The potential is therefore well defined and integral. Its only ambiguity is the initial constant. Conversely differences have zero divergence because the consecutive faces around a vertex telescope. This proves (3) over the integers, not only by a dimension count. At an ordered shaded triangle with white regions (f0,f1,f2), the physical variations are, up to the fixed orientation, P_f0-P_f1, P_f1-P_f2, and the auxiliary variation is their sum P_f0-P_f2. This is also the differential of the actual prefix clocks X=-L_f0/L_f1, Y=-L_f1/L_f2. For a literal dual white, its heads are (d-j,d-i), so the two physical variations are reversed and negated and the auxiliary variation is negated. No dual row is incorrectly identified with the physical row. ## 2. The exact finite-clock rank In the common reference normalization, precisely two white faces contain the marked ideal vertex p: call them u,v. Their prefixes have zero lower-left entry. Every other white face has strictly positive normal coefficient and a quadratic prefix diagonal. This follows from the strict supporting inequalities of the labeled certificate. A right-angled ideal vertex has exactly two incident white and two incident shaded faces. The [white-normal polyhedron](actual_right_angled_selected_framing_obstruction.md), sections 2--3, is a convex three-dimensional polyhedron C whose vertices are these white faces and whose facets are the original shaded triangles. Its boundary is a triangulated sphere. An edge of C corresponds to an edge of Delta; u,v are joined by the original marked MAIN edge e0. Define L on (3) from each literal numerator by the following head rows: | Numerator type | Rows of L | | --- | --- | | 200, 002 | none | | 220 | first physical variation | | 022 | second physical variation | | 202 | sum of the two physical variations | | 222 | both physical variations | Pull these rows back through the actual dual reversal when the numerator is in pi. Row signs or invertible local changes of these rows do not change their common kernel. All six types, including 202/202 pairs, are allowed. No exclusion at rectangle parameter c=1 is made. The equations L P=0 say exactly that every pair of QUADRATIC white-face potentials belonging to one shaded triangle is equal. The induced graph on all vertices of C other than u,v is connected. To prove this without an external connectivity theorem, start with any path in the connected 1-skeleton. Remove occurrences of u by rerouting through its cyclic vertex link. In the resulting graph, occurrences of v can be rerouted through its link with u removed. This link is a cycle or a path and is connected. The replacement never returns to u. Thus any two surviving vertices remain joined. Every surviving edge is in a shaded triangle and its endpoints are both quadratic, so its equality is among the equations of L. Consequently all quadratic-face potentials coincide. After subtracting that common value, ker L={P_u,P_v arbitrary; P_f=0 for f!=u,v}, dim ker L=2, rank L=R-1. (4) This is a theorem about independent original source variables. It does not extend the critical-scheme/representation inverse off criticality. The two directions are precisely the LIMITING geometric framing tangents. At r=N rho the quadratic prefix logarithms have common varying part 2 Log rho-Log s. Write the two constant prefixes as e_u(1+z_u s), e_v(1+z_v s). The original marked primitive meridian makes z_u-z_v=+1 or -1: in the reference convention these are I and -J or its recorded reciprocal. After subtracting one quadratic face potential, the two remaining variable parts are P_u=-2 Log rho+Log s+Log(1+z_u s), P_v=-2 Log rho+Log s+Log(1+z_v s). (4a) The exact constant signs, face coefficients, and common 2 Log N are retained additive constants and disappear only on differentiation. The Jacobian of (4a) in (Log rho,s) has determinant 2(z_u-z_v)/[(1+z_u s)(1+z_v s)] != 0. (4b) It and its inverse are uniformly bounded on the specified compact chart. Thus these two complete-geometry tangent directions span (4). This is not a stationarity claim for the actual finite auxiliary labels. ## 3. A neighboring physical-head slice is primitive The marked main edge e0 separates u,v, so its homogeneous head is P_u-P_v up to sign. Choose either shaded triangle adjacent to e0 and let w be its third white vertex. It is different from u,v and hence quadratic. Each shaded triangle has exactly one matching edge and two main edges. Since e0 is main, exactly one of its other two edges is also MAIN. Call that edge e1. It joins w to u or to v. On ker L, the two actual head functionals at e0,e1 therefore have matrix, up to the recorded row and column signs, [[1,-1],[1,0]] or [[1,-1],[0,1]]. (5) Their determinant is +1 or -1. Thus fixing these two actual physical heads removes exactly the two flat directions, with a primitive, diagram-independent integer minor. This chooses source integration coordinates; it does NOT authorize a new single-port co-source, move an observable through a braid, or claim that e1 is first in an existing Morse slice. The slice W={head_e0=head_e1=0} in homogeneous variations has dimension R-1, and L|_W is injective. Because the diagram is fixed, choose an integral basis of W once. In that basis its smallest singular value is a positive diagram-dependent constant, independent of N and the frame. Alternatively fixing the two constant-face potentials directly is a primitive complementary slice with the same conclusion. An arbitrary second physical head need not work. If both its adjacent white faces are quadratic, its restriction to ker L is zero. In general the exact test is the rank of the two cut-head rows restricted to (4). The corresponding kernel dimension after fixing the heads is 2 minus that rank. No generic-cut transversality is silently assumed. ## 4. Closed, marked-open, and fixed-charge two-cut sources For the original marked source, equality of the two exposed heads is the permitted WHOLE-SOURCE consequence of integer degree conservation. It is not a local replacement of the unrestricted mark by an invariant cap. After that equality, restoring the exposed edge gives exactly (2), with its actual marked scalar weight still attached. The marked-open chart including the one free exposed head therefore has the same homogeneous space V. Fixing that head imposes its one displayed linear functional. For two cuts on DISTINCT original edges use the actual port orientations of the [common charged chart](actual_matching_graph_common_band_ward_current.md): the heads are (a,a+delta) and (l,l+delta). At a FIXED charge delta, subtract one recorded affine particular solution. Variations then have equal heads across each cut and restore exactly a cycle flow on Delta. Thus, when a,l are included as coordinates, the homogeneous space is again V and (4) applies unchanged. Fixing a,l gives the slice obtained by setting their two cut-head functionals to zero, so (5) is the promised sufficient condition for a full transverse slice. The deleted graph is connected for two distinct edges of this certified Delta. Indeed it is the dual of the triangulated sphere boundary of C. If deleting at most two dual edges disconnected its triangles, the boundary between a nonempty proper set of triangles and its complement would be a nonempty edge cycle with at most two edges. A simplicial sphere has no such cycle. This also proves that a single original edge is not a bridge. If two cut positions lie on the SAME edge, or a routed source uses a different graph, retain the component conditions of the common charged-chart theorem instead; the preceding conclusion need not apply. Varying delta itself adds an affine relative-boundary direction. It is not a closed cycle flow and is NOT counted as a third flat framing variable by (4). The neighboring-band quotient fixes delta to +1 or -1 after its single analytic interpolation. The two physical support cycles still differ; (3)--(5) do not identify them or erase an endpoint current. ## 5. Assembly of the finite transverse curvature bounds This section uses the separately proved local estimates in [the finite boundary curvature theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_q_hahn_boundary_model_curvature.md). Retain the exact models of the [correlated-band theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_correlated_boundary_band_ratio.md), their scalar phases, the literal pi reversal, and every cup and mark. The statement concerns the original uncontracted root product. It does not include the nonlinear binomial co-source or replace its actual weight. Use logarithmic face coordinates, so a physical clock is multiplied by exp(P_f-P_g). Equivalently the finite head changes by N(P_f-P_g)/(2pi i); the integral lattice in sections 1--4 is the same after this fixed scalar normalization. At the real limiting boundary clocks, the local 220/022 scalar curvature, 202 positive-total curvature, and 222 two-variable curvature are bounded below by cN and above by CN on their displayed rows of L. Their non-affine phases have already been retained in the local source formulas; the positive reference Hessians are taken in the corresponding real logarithmic clock coordinates. Thus their sum is a real symmetric matrix H0_N with cN ||L P||^2 <= P^T H0_N P <= CN ||L P||^2 (6) for real P, with a fixed finite number of local rows. Sign changes from 022 or the literal dual are included in L. In a fixed basis of the primitive slice W of section 3, (6) gives c_D N I <= H0_N|_W <= C_D N I. (7) Now retain the exact finite-r clocks at r=N rho. Their relative errors from the finite nonzero limiting clocks are O(1/N). The uniform complex logarithmic derivative bounds through order three in the local curvature theorem make their Hessian correction O(1). The 200/002 zero-free Bessel factors have O(1) Hessian on the common compact neighborhood; their endpoint-product corrections have Hessian O(1/N). Linear head monomials and all fixed channel scalars contribute zero Hessian. Let S=sum_i(d-2a_i). The retained 202/222 partner products and auxiliary root cups have Hessian O(S), since their factors are uniformly separated from zero. Mixed-type cup/partner residuals are smaller after their linear monomials are removed. These are estimates of the actual root identities; no root reflection or partner collision is differentiated as a generic-q identity. Physical cup/cap characters are linear. The nonzero actual product and finite model satisfy a relative O(1/N) estimate on a fixed source polydisc. Cauchy's formula gives an O(1/N) Hessian error for their local logarithms. Consequently the actual root source Hessian H_N at the boundary sample satisfies, on W, ||H_N-H0_N|| <= C_D(1+S). (8) For S=o(N), (7),(8) imply invertibility and ||(H_N|_W)^-1|| <= C_D/N. (9) This is a complex Hessian statement; positivity is asserted for the reference matrix H0_N, not for an arbitrarily perturbed complex point. All constants are uniform in the stated alpha/rho compacts and through both maximal-fold parities. The shrinking s-window is an INTERNAL channel window, not the external auxiliary-color h-window needed for the eventual filling theorem. Genuine q normals are not estimated by (8),(9). ## 6. What this does not yet prove The complete geometric framing sample is not automatically stationary for the finite labels a_i. Even at the folded limit the actual linear source characters and retained Poisson sector must be checked against the boundary action before invoking a stationary reduction. A Hessian bound alone does not bound the gradient or the displacement of a nearby critical point. The binomial base localization, transverse amplitude, Jacobian, square-root branch and common descending cycle would all have to be retained in a Gaussian theorem. The exact critical-scheme inverse remains a statement on the critical representation germ. No off-critical flat representations were used to obtain (4) or (9). In particular a generic unframed perturbation of a zero lower-left prefix is not assigned the same scale as a primitive source-head perturbation. Finally, selecting the primitive neighboring-head slice does not expose those heads as two first slots without additional source algebra. The original relative cotangent periods, their support/carry boundaries, the global nonzero coefficient and the mixed-color/alias estimates remain separate. No hyperbolic-volume equality follows here. ## 7. Focused audit and scope The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_original_boundary_transverse_rank.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_original_boundary_transverse_rank_results.json) pass 56 exact rank cases, 1136 ordered triangle/dual checks, 224 oriented chain maps, 112 primitive neighboring slices, 336 fixed-charge affine restorations, 56 deliberately nontransverse cut witnesses, and 56 cup/cap subdivisions. Original finite tensors at both parities separately check 5732 degree entries, 42 retained half-twist sectors and 540 cup/cap entries. Five exact prefix/frame identities include (4b). The actual cube and octahedral combinatorics are distinguished from supplemental combinatorial sphere regressions; the latter certify no additional geometric realization. The local curvature theorem has its own source-matrix audit. No numerical knot list replaces the class-wide proof. The transverse-rank theorem does not identify a stationary point, first-slot routing, Gaussian contraction or relative-period coefficient. The rank calculation does not establish a stationary sector, a descending cycle or a nonzero original period.

title: An exact positive full-source formula for planar three-port doubles
text: # An exact positive full-source formula for planar three-port doubles 30 October 2026. A literal planar three-port double has an exact nonnegative complete-circle source at EVERY quantum level. All interior and seam colors are summed; there are no fixed Steinberg cycle projections. The formula is a sum of squared COHERENT boundary packets, with the positive original marked theta scalar as its prescribed weight. It retains the single physical mark and every paired circle normal. The primitive half can have arbitrary fixed size and branching. Its boundary packet is still a genuine coherent contraction, not a product of local black scalar magnitudes. Thus this theorem removes cancellation between the double's boundary sectors; it does not yet compute their exponential size or prove the volume limit for arbitrary plats. ## 1. A reflection operation on the whole original Morse word Let J_n reverse ALL n physical V_N tensor factors. For a matrix F:V_N^tensor a -> V_N^tensor b put F^sharp = J_a F^dagger J_b. (1) This reverses composition and tensor order. It is a whole-word operation, not a partial transpose of one leg. Set d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), x=q^d. For the original physical cup and cap, p_(u,v)=N x^-v delta_(u+v,d), ell_(u,v)=x^u delta_(u+v,d)/N, one has exactly p^sharp=N^2 ell, ell^sharp=N^-2 p. (2) Indeed p^dagger P=N^2 ell, with P=J_2. The original unrestricted marked row is m_(u,v)=x^v/N^2; it is NOT replaced by its local adjoint in this argument. Let L_j be a FULL complete-circle Hermite sector. Its actual all-degree factorization, including a paired root normal, is L_j=F_j F_j^dagger P. Consequently L_j^sharp=L_j, (R^e L_j)^sharp=R^-e L_j. (3) For the second identity use the proved all-input equality R^e L_j=omega_j^e L_j with |omega_j|=1. If a structural crossing is present elsewhere in the original word, it obeys the independently proved identity P R^dagger P=R^-1 as well. These are actual matrix identities, including both parities; a paired nilpotent is not being replaced by a projector. In a Morse word from a physical one-head cut back to that head, the numbers of cups and caps are equal. Therefore every scale N^2 in (2) cancels globally. The word obtained by reversing its composition and tensor order, exchanging its cups/caps, and reversing its signed crossings is exactly T^sharp=T^dagger. It is the literal reflected Morse diagram. Boundary labels are transported by that same geometric reflection, including its reversal of the cyclic three-port order. The cut word T is a Hopf endomorphism of the original V_N. This module is irreducible: its interior E and F coefficients are all nonzero and its K weights are distinct. Hence T=z I. The original marked closure extracts precisely z, since m p=1. Its reflected one-head cut is z-bar I, so Z_reflected(reflected boundary labels) =conjugate(Z_original(boundary labels)). (4) This proves the marked identity without reflecting a bare local m, without moving a bare mark through a nested cap, and without first specializing an ordinary quantum trace to zero. A correct generic first-normal trace quotient gives the same scalar, but is not needed to establish (4). Any original exterior framing line is reflected and conjugated separately. Legitimate one-head cuts on another physical main arc give the same raw scalar when needed in the seam construction. To verify this, choose the regular generic lift of the WHOLE labeled diagram. Its closed scalar F(zeta) equals D_N(zeta) times the open scalar at either cut, where D_N is the same physical V_N quantum dimension. Away from its isolated zeros those open scalars agree; they are regular and therefore agree at the root. This transports the complete cut tangle, not a bare local marked row. The chosen lift is used only to establish this equality of the actual root coupons. ## 2. The double is a specified physical source Start with an actual planar complete-circle graph source Gamma and a specified three-port vertex disk for which its punctured source has an actual Morse realization. For example take the exposed outer white vertex of an original NC/Morse graph. Remove that vertex disk, reflect its remaining planar piece as in section1, and glue the two disk boundaries in their reversed cyclic order. The seam has three edges, not six consecutive edge coupons. Install ONE original complete-circle coupon on each merged edge. Equivalently remove the old boundary circle coupons before joining the two pieces and reinstall one on each seam. Signed seam exponents add; reflected partners cancel there. Reflect every remaining signed crossing in the second half as required by (3). Expand the surviving vertices to their actual nested main-strand arcs. A generic planar height produces the corresponding cups, caps and turned-circle Morse word. Choose its single physical one-head mark on an outer-face seam main arc FROM THE START. This construction is the planar vertex sum Gamma #_3 reflected(Gamma), with its actual source orientations. It does not assert that the result has the previous one-row NC edge order, nor insert unrecorded edge permutations or structural crossings to force such an order. The [geometric source certificate](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_planar_three_port_double_topology.md) records this disk construction, including its six-terminal reversal. The algebra below uses only its specified physical port joining and one-circle-per-seam convention. Applying two old root circle coupons in succession instead would give a different source and is NOT the double studied here. ## 3. Exact theta division before taking the fixed root normal Let D_N be the supported folded triples 0<=a,b,c<=floor((N-1)/2), a+b+c>=N-1. Write theta_N(a,b,c)>0 for the RAW original marked theta source with these three full-circle sectors and no twists. Its positivity and normalization are proved in the all-channel marked-theta theorem. Let Z_Gamma(a,b,c) be the original coherent source with these three boundary sectors fixed and EVERY other complete-circle color summed. The mark is a legitimate physical cut of the original closed source. The [three-port source sewing theorem](actual_nc_three_port_source_sewing.md) has an all-entry local proof. Removing the ordinary boundary invariant row from the regular generic lift leaves a genuine invariant column Y_Gamma(zeta)=alpha_Gamma(zeta) Theta_abc(zeta). The canonical Theta corner is one, so alpha is the finite open-corner contraction and is regular BEFORE dividing by a closed theta. The same argument applies to the literal disk joining in section2: the punctured source is an actual composition of Hopf morphisms, not a bare permutation of a six-head array. For a supported triple the ordinary theta has exactly one root zero. Its local source scalar is nonzero. The generic cross-multiplied sewing identity can therefore be divided by its single common quantum dimension factor BEFORE specializing. The one-circle-per-seam edge constants and the two removed source scalars give exactly Z_sewn(a,b,c)=Z_A(a,b,c) Z_B(a,b,c)/theta_N(a,b,c). (5) No paired projector norm or root L_j inverse is used. The retained first normal is the originally specified one; higher nonzero coefficients are not selected if it vanishes. Nontriangles vanish. For unsupported triples the actual product of three complete circles kills the regular saturated six-head boundary source before the exterior or the mark acts, by the exposed six-port pruning theorem. Thus there is no missing marked-white boundary current in the COMPLETE-circle sum. This is a whole-source statement; it is not an assertion that an arbitrary open local current vanishes. At the reflected boundary identify its labels by the actual reversed cyclic port map. Equation (4) makes its coherent packet the conjugate of Z_Gamma, while theta is symmetric and positive. Therefore the RAW original source of the double is exactly Z_double = sum_(a,b,c in D_N) |Z_Gamma(a,b,c)|^2/theta_N(a,b,c) >= 0. (6) All interior color sums in each factor of (6) are performed coherently. The sum includes every physical seam triple. Both parity cases and all paired first normals occur. If D_N is empty the sum and source are zero. If D_N is nonempty, strict positivity holds exactly when at least one coherent boundary packet is nonzero. No universal nonvanishing premise for an unknown primitive piece is added. ## 4. What the positive formula controls quantitatively Define the actual weighted boundary maximum B_N=max_(j in D_N) |Z_Gamma(j)|/sqrt(theta_N(j)). When the supported set is nonempty, B_N^2 <= Z_double <= |D_N| B_N^2, |D_N| <= N^3. (7) Hence whenever the source is nonzero its complete exponential rate is controlled, with an O(log N/N) error, by the largest COHERENT weighted boundary packet. This is a full-source estimate, not a norm of one fixed central channel or an absolute magnetic-state envelope. Equation (6) does not make the inside of each Z_Gamma a positive factorial sum. Estimating that coherent packet is still required to identify (7) with the actual doubled hyperbolic volume. In particular known projected cube or ladder packets cannot be substituted for the full Z_Gamma in (6). The double class has arbitrary fixed primitive size; it is a specified subclass of physical planar sources, not a proof for every fixed k-bridge skeleton. ## 5. A literal full-color NC cube double There is an especially direct certificate using the original ordered cube, with interval black vertex (0,1,2) and outer white vertex (0,10,11). Its ribbon reflection swaps the color classes and has edge permutation (1 10)(2 11)(4 7)(5 8), with 0,3,6,9 fixed. (8) It maps the interval black boundary to the outer white boundary IN THE DISPLAYED ORDER. The induced rotations at the other vertices are the genuine pivotal cyclic moves, not plain magnetic-leg swaps. Insert the reflected cube at that interval by the existing literal NC graft. The result has fourteen trivalent vertices and twenty-one complete circles. Its original mark stays exposed in that construction. Reflecting the signed interior edge exponents by (8) gives exactly (6). The focused audit computes this TWENTY-ONE-CIRCLE source directly by full physical magnetic tensors, with all colors already assembled in each complete L_N coupon. It independently compares the result to the supported three-color sum in (6), and checks each reflected boundary packet against the conjugate-root calculation. In particular none of its cycle colors is frozen to the central channel. Audit: [whole-word reflection and full physical doubles](../experiments/audit_actual_planar_three_port_reflection_double.py). The reflection-double identities do not give a full-source volume estimate. The size estimate for the remaining coherent half-packet is separate from these identities.

title: A common positive face radius gives the global channel maximum
status: Uniform all-channel rate and strict maximum
text: # A common positive face radius gives the global channel maximum 30 October 2026. This is a finite determinant/rate theorem for the original positive face polynomials. The exact marked coefficient interface is proved separately. No external filling-color packet or filled-knot equality is claimed here. ## 1. The original finite factors and one common radius Use the matrices and scalar normalization in [the exact positive circle](actual_complete_circle_positive_face_polynomial.md). Put d=N-1, a in {0,...,floor(d/2)}, s=d-2a, and mu=a/N. Write D_a(x,b,y)=det[bI+(x/2)H_-+(y/2)H_+], P_s(x,y)=product_(j=a+1)^(d-a)(x-Q^j y), B_(N,a)(x,b,c,y)=beta_a^2 D_a(x,b,y)D_a(x,c,y)P_s(x,y). The fixed multiplicity k_a is between1 and2 and does not change a normalized logarithmic rate. The retained half-twist omega_a^epsilon has modulus1 for an integer channel; it must still be kept in a channel SUM. Each circle uses the SAME face radius for every shared face. Set the two original marked face variables u,v to zero, and put all other face radii in a fixed positive compact set. The actual simple white-face sphere has no matching edge between u,v, because their edge is the original MAIN cut. Consequently x,y are not both zero. Each triangle has at least one positive radius. If one outer radius vanishes, at least one of b,c is positive: otherwise three distinct faces would be u or v. These are exactly the nondegenerate patterns used below. The result also holds when all four radii are positive. ## 2. Uniform logarithmic determinant rate, including both endpoints Let c(t)=cos(pi t), E_b(t)=x+y+2b c(t)^2 +2c(t)sqrt[b^2 c(t)^2+b(x+y)+xy], lambda_b(t)=E_b(t)/(4c(t)^2). Then, uniformly over ALL integer a and the stated positive compact sets with their fixed zero pattern, (1/N)log D_a(x,b,y) = integral_0^mu log lambda_b(t) dt + o(1). (1) All logarithms in (1) are real. Here is a direct finite-matrix proof. Away from t=0,1/2, the actual diagonal and squared adjacent modulus converge uniformly, with error O(N^-1), to A_b(t)=b+(x+y)/(2c(t)^2), B_b(t)=[(x+y)^2-4xy c(t)^2]/(16c(t)^4). Thus lambda_b=(A_b+sqrt(A_b^2-4B_b))/2. No matrix of virtual size beyond the maximal folded channel is introduced. If b>0, every principal matrix is bounded below by bI. If x,y>0, the exact [sum gap](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_q_hahn_positive_total_boundary_normals.md) H_-+H_+>=cos(pi/N)I gives the same uniform positive lower bound. On an interior index interval the matrices also have a uniform upper bound. Partition that interval into blocks of length ell tending to infinity with ell/N tending to zero. Removing each connecting adjacent entry is a rank-two perturbation. Both the original matrix and its block diagonal pinching lie between the same positive lower bound and a fixed upper bound. Eigenvalue interlacing, or integration of log det along this positive interpolation, bounds the log-determinant change by a constant times the number of removed edges. Within a block, freezing the coefficients changes operator norm by O(ell/N); the positive lower bound makes its log-determinant change O(ell^2/N). After a diagonal unitary gauge the frozen block is the real constant Jacobi matrix. Its eigenvalues are A_b+2sqrt(B_b)cos(j*pi/(ell+1)). Their logarithmic Riemann sum is (1/pi)integral_0^pi log(A_b+2sqrt(B_b)cos theta)dtheta =log[(A_b+sqrt(A_b^2-4B_b))/2]. For the last identity, factor the expression as lambda_b |1+sqrt(B_b)/lambda_b * exp(i theta)|^2; the second logarithm has mean zero by its convergent Fourier expansion. The positive spectral gap keeps the ratio below1 uniformly on this interior interval. The total block error is O(N/ell+ell), hence o(N). The same estimates allow a last shorter block, uniformly in a. For completeness the endpoint truncations are uniform, not a fixed-a argument. At either cut index a removed connecting edge has bounded size depending only on the chosen endpoint cutoff epsilon, and its rank-two cost is O_epsilon(1). A terminal block has a positive constant lower spectral bound and the Hadamard upper bound from the ACTUAL diagonal. Its log determinant is bounded in absolute value by C epsilon N(1+|log epsilon|)+O(log N) at the fold, and C epsilon N+O(1) at zero. Indeed the diagonal is at most C/[cos(n*pi/N)cos((n+1)*pi/N)]; summing its logarithm gives the displayed integrable endpoint bound through both parities. The limiting log lambda has the same integrable majorant. First let N increase, then let epsilon decrease. This proves uniform (1). The only remaining allowed case is b=0 and exactly one of x,y positive. Here D_a is a scalar multiple of det H_+ or det H_-, and the ACTUAL Cholesky pivots are p_(n-1)=sin(n*pi/N)/[cos(n*pi/N)sin((2n-1)*pi/N)]. Their exact product proves (1) directly by the same endpoint-truncated Riemann sums; its bulk ratio is x/(4cos(pi t)^2) or its y counterpart. This avoids using a positive spectral gap in this single-summand case. The empty determinant at a=0 is included. ## 3. The circle rate increases strictly to the fold Define I(v)=integral_0^v log(2sin(pi t))dt, J_mu(x,y)=integral_mu^(1-mu) log|x-exp(2pi i t)y|dt. The exact sine products, with their integrable endpoint logarithms, give uniformly in a (1/N)log beta_a = I(2mu)-2I(mu)+o(1), (1/N)log P_s(x,y) = J_mu(x,y)+o(1). (2) When x=y the second integrand has endpoint logarithmic singularities; the elementary sine-product comparison gives the same uniform o(1). If one outer radius is zero, the assertion is immediate from the single monomial. The positive coefficient identity fixes P_s>0. Combine (1),(2) to obtain the continuous uniform circle rate F_mu=2I(2mu)-4I(mu) +integral_0^mu [log lambda_b(t)+log lambda_c(t)]dt +J_mu(x,y). (3) For 0<mu<1/2, put D_xy(mu)=(x-y)^2+4xy sin(pi mu)^2. Direct differentiation, retaining the scalar beta and forced product, gives the cancellation partial_mu F_mu = log[E_b(mu)E_c(mu)/D_xy(mu)] >0. (4) Indeed the scalar derivative is4log(2cos(pi mu)), while the two determinant denominators multiply to16cos(pi mu)^4. The derivative of J is minus log D_xy. If xy>0, then E_b,E_c>=x+y and D_xy<(x+y)^2. If exactly one outer radius vanishes, at least one of b,c is positive, making at least one E strictly larger than x+y. Thus strictness holds in every actual pattern. Formula (3) is continuous at both endpoints even when the derivative at zero diverges. There is therefore a strict diagram-dependent gap on every region mu<=1/2-epsilon. For a fixed graph, multiplying the original factors at their shared radii and summing any polynomial number of channel choices preserves that exponential gap whenever at least one channel stays epsilon away from the fold. This upper estimate is at one common radius; it does not sum incompatible independent local optimizers. Near the fold (4) also gives the explicit classical quadratic gap. Write A=x+y>0 and T_b=sqrt[bA+xy], T_c=sqrt[cA+xy]. At mu=1/2-delta, partial_mu F_mu = 2pi delta(T_b+T_c)/A+O(delta^2), F_(1/2)-F_(1/2-delta) = pi(T_b+T_c)delta^2/A+O(delta^3). (5) The coefficient is strictly positive in the actual patterns. This is a statement about the limiting action. Uniform finite relative asymptotics on delta of order N^-1/2, and cancellation of the retained half-twist phases in the whole channel sum, require a further proof; the o(1) in (1)--(3) is NOT used as such a relative estimate. ## 4. Scope of the whole-source upper bound The [exact marked coefficient theorem](../papers/filling-bounds/README.md) makes every coefficient nonnegative before the explicit half-twist scalar. Evaluating its polynomial at the SAME positive radius bounds the selected coefficient by that value divided by its prescribed radius monomial. Equations (1)--(4) then control the entire finite channel sum from above, with all original scalar factors and only polynomial counting cost. The absolute endpoint value is computed separately from the actual facet coning and marked source normalization. A positive central coefficient with that value supplies a lower bound for an UNTWISTED channel sum, as assembled in the [complete untwisted theorem](general_untwisted_augmented_source_volume.md). Signed half twists require a noncancellation theorem. External crossing-circle colors needed for long Dehn fillings are not the internal a labels in this note and are not estimated here. Focused audit: [original finite channel factors](../experiments/audit_actual_positive_face_channel_rate.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_positive_face_channel_rate_results.json). It checks six symbolic identities, 704 all-label circles, 1408 original determinants, 528 independent Newton comparisons, 176 exact LDL products and 576 adjacent-channel ratios, including 64 maximal folds of each parity. The 72 rate samples are diagnostics only. No finite-window signed Gaussian or external-color theorem follows from the channel-rate estimate.

title: The positive face coefficient has one global saddle
text: # The positive face coefficient has one global saddle 30 October 2026. The coefficient below has an exact compact torus integral and a uniform finite Gaussian asymptotic through both folded parities. The determinant contraction proves the global angular gap. This is a coefficient theorem; its identification with the original source uses the separately checked marked face-grid identity. It does not estimate external filling colors. Setting the two marked face variables to zero uses only a connected geometric certificate; it needs neither the finite-r Bessel chart nor a one-main-component hypothesis. ## 1. The polynomial and its prescribed coefficient Fix the labeled original right-angled matching graph with R crossing circles and R+2 white faces. Let u,v be the two marked faces. Set their variables to zero. Give the other R faces positive variables l_f. For each actual label vector a=(a_i), let P_N(l)=product_i [D_ai(x_i,b_i,y_i)D_ai(x_i,c_i,y_i) P_si(x_i,y_i)], s_i=N-1-2a_i, d=N-1. Every argument here is its original shared face variable, including its specified zero when the face is u or v. The [local source factorization](actual_complete_circle_positive_face_polynomial.md) proves that P_N is homogeneous of degree dR with nonnegative coefficients. The coefficient of interest is A_N=[product_(f!=u,v) l_f^d] P_N(l). (1) All scalar factors k_ai beta_ai^2, original half twists, and the exact finite-grid measure are outside P_N and must be restored by the source identity. They are not absorbed in A_N. Assume S=sum_i s_i=o(N), with the graph fixed. Both maximal-fold parities and arbitrary integer near-fold label sequences are included. Let l^geom be the positive finite white-circle normal coefficients from the certified packing with u,v represented by parallel lines. Fix one finite face variable to1 by homogeneity, leaving n=R-1 logarithmic variables. ## 2. An exact global determinant contraction For any positive semidefinite matrices X_1,...,X_t with M=sum X_j>0, put A_j=M^-1/2 X_j M^-1/2. Then sum A_j=I. For real theta_j put B(theta)=sum_j exp(i theta_j) A_j. This is a contraction: Vz=(A_j^1/2 z)_j is an isometry and B=V* diag(exp(i theta_j))V. Cyclicity of trace gives exactly Tr(I-B*B)=sum_(j<k)|exp(i theta_j)-exp(i theta_k)|^2 Tr(A_j A_k). (2) Every pair trace is nonnegative. Since the squared singular values lambda_l of B are at most1, log lambda_l<=lambda_l-1 proves |det B|<=exp[-(1/2)sum_(j<k)|exp(i theta_j) -exp(i theta_k)|^2 Tr(A_j A_k)]. (3) A zero determinant satisfies the same bound by continuity. No limiting matrix, independent-entry positivity, or commutativity is required. Apply (3) to each original D_a, with its nonzero summands bI, xH_-/2,yH_+/2. When all three are present, the two pair traces involving the identity summand have lower bounds cN from the exact bulk-square argument in the [curvature theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_q_hahn_boundary_model_curvature.md). For a two-variable220/022 determinant its single pair trace has the same bound. For202, with b=0, the pair trace is precisely its log-radius variance; the exact positive-polynomial variance proof gives cN. A one-variable200/002 determinant is a monomial and has no angular gap. All constants are uniform on positive compact radius sets near l^geom. The resulting active pair graph connects all R finite faces. Indeed each shaded triangle equates its finite-face potentials, and the [exact rank proof](actual_original_boundary_transverse_rank.md) shows that deleting u,v leaves a connected graph. The forced polynomials P_s also have nonnegative coefficients, so their modulus ratio on the torus is at most1 and cannot weaken (3). Consequently, after fixing one phase, |P_N(l exp(i theta))/P_N(l)| <=exp[-c_D N dist(theta,0)^2] (4) on the entire n-dimensional torus, with its usual periodic distance. To see the uniform comparison, use a fixed spanning tree: the complex unit phase difference of any vertex from the fixed vertex is at most the sum of the edge differences along its path. Compactness then compares their squared sum with squared torus distance. The only common zero is the constant phase. Every edge row has literal coefficients +1,-1, so there are no other angular aliases. ## 3. The finite positive critical radius In logarithmic finite-face coordinates define Phi_N(z)=log P_N(l^geom exp z)-d sum_f z_f. (5) The actual circle-center angle force at the fold gives N^-1 partial Phi_N(0) ->0. (6) For each shaded triangle the determinant derivative tends to sum_j theta_j dlog l_j/(2pi). The consecutive center triangles give angle sum2pi at each finite white circle, so the total is1 per finite face; d/N tends to1. The retained P_s derivatives are O(S), and hence vanish after division by N. This uses the uniform original finite angle-force theorem, not independent local maximization. The finite Hessian is real positive on the fixed gauge slice, and its bounds are c_D N I<=H_N<=C_D N I on a fixed small real neighborhood. Its fixed higher derivatives are O(N) on a uniform complex neighborhood: preconditioning a D determinant gives a small perturbation of I, while near-fold forced roots stay separated from the positive radius compact. These are the same finite curvature and holomorphic bounds already proved. The quantitative implicit-function argument now gives a real critical radius l_N=l^geom exp z_N with z_N=o(1). Use the Hessian at zero as preconditioner: the normalized gradient error tends to zero, and the Newton remainder is O(|z|^2) with uniform constant, so contraction on a ball of radius C|partial Phi_N(0)|/N gives existence and uniqueness there. Strict convexity of log P_N on the gauge slice implies that no other real critical radius exists. Strictness follows directly from the positive determinant monomial support and the connected active pair graph. Let H_N be the Hessian at this actual finite critical radius. ## 4. The exact coefficient integral and its nonzero asymptotic The Cauchy coefficient formula, with one variable fixed by homogeneity, is exactly A_N=P_N(l_N)/product_f l_N,f^d *(2pi)^(-n) integral_[−pi,pi]^n [P_N(l_N exp(i theta))/P_N(l_N)] exp[-i d sum_f theta_f] dtheta. (7) There is no unknown source-cycle coefficient in this integral for A_N. Equation (4) makes the part outside any fixed small neighborhood exponentially small relative to its prefactor. At the origin the exact critical equation removes the linear term and the exponent equals -(1/2)theta^T H_N theta + O(N|theta|^3). Uniform fourth and higher derivative bounds, rescaling by N^-1/2, and symmetry of the Gaussian give A_N= P_N(l_N)/product_f l_N,f^d /[(2pi)^(n/2) sqrt(det H_N)] *[1+O(N^-1)]. (8) The cubic term is odd, so its first Gaussian integral is zero; its square and the quartic term cost O(N^-1). Gaussian domination from (4) controls the remaining expansion and tails. The square root is positive. Thus the coefficient is strictly positive for all sufficiently large N in this near-fold window, and has the displayed global relative asymptotic. This proves more than a constructed local contour statement. ## 5. Absolute value and remaining source tasks The [absolute facet-coning computation](actual_original_boundary_stationary_character.md) of the endpoint determinant action is 2pi lim (1/N)log[P_N(l^geom)/product_f(l_f^geom)^d] =2 Vol(Q)=Vol(Y_D). (9) For clarity its geometric input is explicit: each white cyclic-face pyramid contributes the sum of Lambda(theta_j/2), and each shaded contact triangle coned to the marked ideal vertex contributes the sum of Lambda((pi-theta_j)/2). These actual coned facets tile Q. The source Legendre potential is twice this sum, with additive constant fixed by the exact single-positive-variable Cholesky product. This uses the absolute marked action proof, not a volume chosen to normalize P_N. The shift z_N=o(1) changes the normalized saddle value by o(1), and the Hessian prefactor is subexponential. All exact circle scalars beta_ai also have normalized log tending to zero when S=o(N). Therefore the original fixed near-fold sector, ONCE the exact marked coefficient identity is restored, has absolute rate Vol(Y_D)/(2pi). Its retained half-twist scalar has modulus1 but may affect sums of different sectors. Combining this coefficient theorem with a common-radius all-channel upper bound gives a whole-source equality for the untwisted complete source, since all its sectors are nonnegative in the specified common normalization. The [complete untwisted source theorem](general_untwisted_augmented_source_volume.md) performs this combination with the exact measure and scalar. Signed sums and mixed external filling colors remain distinct tasks. No filled-knot volume equality is asserted. Focused audit: [finite determinant contraction and original coefficients](../experiments/audit_actual_positive_face_coefficient_saddle.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_positive_face_coefficient_saddle_results.json). It checks 256 original matrix torus cases, 96 pair traces, and 16 literal tetrahedral-graph coefficients against exact finite Cauchy quadrature. Gaussian profile errors are diagnostics; the global graph-wide estimate is proved above. The coefficient theorem does not settle the whole signed channel sum or external colors.

title: An exponentially accurate analytic interpolation of the actual fold factors
status: Exponential actual-grid interpolation; fixed complex faces
text: # An exponentially accurate analytic interpolation of the actual fold factors 30 October 2026. The construction below uses analytic contractions on shrinking disks, then the actual positive finite recurrence. It produces an even holomorphic fold interpolation whose error on the original channel grid is exponentially small, uniformly on a fixed complex face-radius neighborhood. Formal WKB existence alone is not used. This is a local complete-circle factor theorem; the shared coefficient period and the ordinary-color alias subsets remain separate. ## 1. Statement with the original finite anchor Fix a compact set of positive face radii in any one of the actual zero patterns of the [signed source theorem](general_signed_augmented_source_volume.md). Zero faces stay zero. Set B_(N,a)=beta_a^2 D_a(x,b,y)D_a(x,c,y)P_(d-2a)(x,y), d=N-1, M=floor(d/2), s0=d-2M, delta_a=(d-2a)/(2N), delta_min=s0/(2N), h=1/N. Use the explicit analytic functions E_b,J_b,a_b,V of [the fixed-fold theorem](actual_positive_face_fixed_fold_packet.md), equations(1),(2). In particular V is even, V(0)=0 and V''(0)=2pi(T_b+T_c)/(x+y)>0. The T_b=0 triangle is treated as the exact constant-pivot case, with J_b=1. There are fixed positive delta_*,rho,c,C, a complex logarithmic radius neighborhood O_rho of the given real compact, and even holomorphic functions H_N(delta;l) on |delta|<2delta_*, l in O_rho, such that H_N(0;l)=0 and H_N(delta;l)=-N V(delta;l) -(1/2)Log[J_b(delta;l)J_c(delta;l)]+O(N^-1). (1) The bound is uniform on smaller closed disks and neighborhoods, with all fixed derivatives by Cauchy estimates. Define the specified finite-N interpolation mathcal B_N(delta;l)=B_(N,M)(l) exp[H_N(delta;l)-H_N(delta_min;l)]. (2) The original B_(N,M) is retained exactly; it is a holomorphic unit on O_rho by positive-matrix preconditioning and the original forced factor. Then for EVERY original integer a with delta_min<=delta_a<=delta_*, B_(N,a)(l)/mathcal B_N(delta_a;l)=1+O(e^(-cN)), uniformly l in O_rho. (3) The right side of (2) is even in delta. No noninteger-dimensional matrix is introduced. For an actual retained half twist, the factor omega_M^epsilon exp[pi i epsilon N(delta^2-delta_min^2)] (4) agrees exactly with omega_a^epsilon on this grid, including its common q^(d^2/2) phase. Thus (2)--(4) preserve the entire local root complete-circle factor. They do not interpolate a different generic-q germ or ordinary small-color coupon. ## 2. A regular analytic equation in the squared fold variable First consider one triangle with T_b>0. Let z denote the pivot coordinate (N/2-a)/N. On a fixed small complex disk the functions E(z)=E_b(z), D(z)=(x+y)^2-4xy sin^2(pi z) obey E(z)E(-z)=D(z). Write B0(w)=[E(z)+E(-z)]/2, C0(w)=[E(z)-E(-z)]/(2z), t(w)=tan(pi z)/z, w=z^2. All are holomorphic in w near zero; t and C0 are units. Seek a reflection-preserving approximate pivot in the form e_v(z)=E(z) exp[z v(z^2)], (5) where v is holomorphic in w. Thus e_v(z)e_v(-z)=D(z) EXACTLY. Clear the actual recurrence residual as in the fixed-fold proof: Rcal_v(z,h)=tan(pi(z+h))e_v(z)+tan(pi z)e_v(-z-h) -[tan(pi(z+h))+tan(pi z)] [A+2b sin(pi z)sin(pi(z+h))]. (6) It vanishes at z=0,-h and is odd under z -> -z-h. Set z=zeta-h/2. Division therefore defines a holomorphic function of w=zeta^2: G_h(v)(w)= Rcal_v(zeta-h/2,h) /[zeta(zeta^2-h^2/4)]. (7) The values at the apparent three divisors in (7) are their removable limits. Holomorphic divisibility follows successively by the two zeros and centered oddness, including h=0 where the zeros coalesce. It does not require estimating separate singular quotients. At h=0 and v=0, G_0(0)=0. Its linearization is multiplication by the nonzero analytic function L(w)=2t(w)C0(w), L(0)=4pi^2 T_b. (8) This normalization resolves the formal fold pole in the analytic equation; it does not cancel the peripheral factors of the finite four-component operator. ## 3. The single-loss analytic estimate Here is the estimate that controls arbitrarily many corrections. Use sup norms on w disks, with radii in a fixed compact interval 0<R_1<=R<=R_0. For small v and 0<Delta<R-R_1, with h small enough that Ch<Delta, analytic differentiation gives ||D G_h(v)-L||_(R to R-Delta) <=C(||v||_R+h/Delta). (9) All constants are uniform on a fixed complex radius neighborhood. There is only ONE loss of analytic radius, not two independent derivatives in z. We give the cancellation explicitly. Write the even and odd parts of (5) as e_v(z)=B0(w)+w F_v(w)+z[C0(w)+G_v(w)]. Both F_v,G_v are pointwise analytic functions of (w,v(w)), and F_v=C0 v+O(v^2), G_v=B0 v+O(v^2). For example they follow directly from cosh(zv) and sinh(zv)/z, which are analytic in (w,v). For zeta^2=w put a=zeta-h/2, b'=zeta+h/2 and w_-=a^2,w_+=b'^2. The v-dependent part of (7) is exactly t_+ F_-+t_- F_+ +(h/(2zeta))(t_- F_+-t_+ F_-) +(1/zeta)(t_+ G_--t_- G_+), (10) where subscripts indicate evaluation at w_+ or w_-. The same formula with pointwise derivatives of F,G holds for D G_h. Every apparent divided difference is controlled by [K(w_+)-K(w_-)]/zeta =2h integral_0^1 K'(w_-+t(w_+-w_-))dt. (11) The segment stays in the outer disk when Ch<Delta. Cauchy's bound for K' costs Delta^-1. Comparing the first line of (10) with its h=0 value uses the same first-derivative estimate, since |w_+-w|+|w_--w|<=Ch. The nonlinear h=0 difference from (8) costs O(||v||). These facts prove (9), including w=0 by holomorphy. ## 4. Exponentially accurate analytic pivots The explicit first correction already proved in the fixed-fold note provides the starting function v^(0)(w)=h a_b(z)/z, w=z^2. It is holomorphic and O(h); the joint residual divisibility there gives G_h(v^(0))=O(h^2) on one fixed disk. Iterate v^(m+1)=v^(m)-L^-1 G_h(v^(m)) (12) on nested w disks, losing Delta=Kh at each step. Choose fixed K sufficiently large, then h sufficiently small. Equation (9) makes the map in (12) a contraction with Lipschitz factor at most1/2 between consecutive disks, as long as ||v||<=C_1 h. The first change is O(h^2), and subsequent changes decrease geometrically. Their sum is O(h^2), so that norm condition closes by induction. More explicitly put R_m=R_0-m Delta and T(v)=v-L^-1 G_h(v). Then v^(m) is defined on the disk of radius R_m. On the next disk, v^(m+1)-v^(m)=T(v^(m))-T(v^(m-1)), with the previous iterate restricted to R_m. Estimate (9) therefore gives ||v^(m+1)-v^(m)||_(R_(m+1))<= (1/2)||v^(m)-v^(m-1)||_(R_m). This is a contraction between nested analytic domains, not an assertion that translation is bounded on one unchanged disk. Perform m=floor(c_0/h) steps, with c_0 small enough that all disks still contain one fixed smaller disk. Keep one more radius margin to evaluate the final residual. The resulting analytic v_N obeys v_N=v^(0)+O(h^2), ||G_h(v_N)||<=C e^(-c_1/h). (13) Each operation is analytic in the face parameters, and all estimates are uniform there. The finite iteration count may depend on N; no analyticity in a varying quantum level is claimed. All functions are real on positive real radii and real w. Put e_N^*(z)=E(z)exp[z v_N(z^2)]. (14) It preserves reflection exactly, has the original first correction, and its ACTUAL Riccati residual is exponentially small on a fixed complex z disk. The removable divisions in (7) only multiply it by bounded analytic factors. For T_b=0 take e_N^*=A exactly. ## 5. Match the actual finite pivots, including complex face radii Choose a fixed real cutoff 2delta_0 within the disk of (14). Start the ACTUAL physical recurrence at the nearest k0 to 2delta_0 N, and estimate only k<=delta_0 N. At real positive radii the original pivots have A<=e_a<=2A+4b. Also e_N^*(k/N)/A>=exp(c k/N) for sufficiently large N in a nonconstant triangle. Consequently the exact error multiplier is bounded by [tan(k theta)/tan((k+1)theta)] exp[-c(k+1)/N]. (15) This is the same source-derived positive contraction as before. The initial error is bounded, and its propagation to k<=delta_0 N is O(e^(-c_2 N)). The sum of exponentially small local residuals remains exponentially small, with at most a polynomial loss. The matching extends to a FIXED complex face neighborhood, not just to a shrinking neighborhood. At each original principal matrix, positive-summand preconditioning gives M_j(l)=M_j(l_real)^(1/2)(I+E)M_j(l_real)^(1/2), ||E||<=C rho, uniformly j,N. The last inverse-entry formula then gives the original Schur-pivot ratio e_a(l)/e_a(l_real)=1+O(rho) uniformly, with no lower eigenvalue assumption beyond the stated positive matrices. The same bound holds for (14) by its uniform analytic unit bounds. Thus each complex error multiplier is at most exp(C rho) times (15). Over the entire finite interval the extra cost is at most exp(C rho N). Choose rho FIRST below both the initial-damping and analytic-residual exponential rates. It follows that e_a(l)/e_N^*((N/2-a)/N;l)=1+O(e^(-c_3 N)) (16) uniformly in the smaller complex face neighborhood and at EVERY physical pivot in the chosen real window, including the two parity endpoints. This step identifies the constructed analytic function with the actual polynomial source. No choice among homogeneous recurrence solutions has been assumed. ## 6. An analytic discrete primitive with the exact folded anchor Apply the construction to the two actual triangles. Their exact reflection makes the marked logarithm ell_N(z)=Log[e_(b,N)^*(z)e_(c,N)^*(z)/D(z)] odd and holomorphic on a fixed disk. Moreover ell_N=V'+h(a_b+a_c)+O(h^2), (17) uniformly and holomorphically. We now construct the logarithm of the channel product itself with exponential precision, instead of summing a finite-order Euler--Maclaurin error. Let A_h f(z)=h^-1 integral_(-h/2)^(h/2) f(z+t)dt. It preserves odd analytic functions. On nested z disks its difference from the identity has norm at most Ch/Delta. Start f^(0)=ell_N and iterate f^(m+1)=f^(m)+ell_N-A_h f^(m), losing Delta=Kh at every step. The first change is O(h^2), by the centered integral and bounded second derivatives. The same geometric contraction argument as in (12), now linear, gives an odd analytic f_N with f_N=ell_N+O(h^2), A_h f_N=ell_N+O(e^(-c_4 N)). (18) Define H_N(z)=-h^-1 integral_0^z f_N(t)dt. It is even, has value zero at zero, and obeys H_N(z+h/2)-H_N(z-h/2) =-ell_N(z)+O(e^(-c_4 N)). (19) Equations (17),(18) give exactly (1), since integral_0^z(a_b+a_c)=(1/2)Log[J_b(z)J_c(z)]. For adjacent ACTUAL channel indices the forced product contributes exactly D at the midpoint, and the two original pivots contribute their reciprocals. By (16) their ratio is exp[-ell_N(midpoint)] with exponentially small relative error. Compare this with (19) and sum at most O(N) steps from the physical maximal channel. The resulting error is still O(e^(-cN)). At the starting index (2) uses B_(N,M) EXACTLY and delta_min=s0/(2N). This proves (3). ## 7. What the theorem supplies and what it does not The comparison (3) is exponentially accurate on the actual channel grid, uniformly for fixed complex face radii, while (2) is even and holomorphic in a fixed fold disk. It therefore supplies the local interpolation input that a fixed-frequency Fourier contour argument requires. It is substantially stronger than a real-grid relative O(N^-1) approximation. Its phase and amplitude are those of the actual finite source, with all beta, forced factors, parity offsets and half twists retained. The full shared-face coefficient must still be assembled with its original Cauchy period, angular tails and finite channel endpoints. The entire complete-image core must then be distinguished from the nonempty ordinary-color subsets in the exact external reflection identity. No global alias gap, filled-knot conclusion, or generic-q normal theorem is inferred here. The focused [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_positive_face_exponential_fold_interpolation.py) and its [recorded results](../experiments/actual_positive_face_exponential_fold_interpolation_results.json) check 20 symbolic identities and 24 complex-face residual identities. Numerical analytic-iteration prototypes are compared with the original beta/D/P factors: four pivot cases through N=1024 and eight complete-circle comparisons at both parities, including fixed complex face parameters. These finite projections are diagnostics of the construction; they are not premises for the uniform exponential estimate proved above. No full mixed-color packet, ordinary-subset gap, or generic-q normal claim follows from this interpolation theorem.

title: The actual face factor on a fixed real fold interval
status: Exact finite difference period; fixed real fold packet
text: # The actual face factor on a fixed real fold interval 30 October 2026. An analytic first continuant correction improves the folded relative estimate to O(N^-1) on a FIXED real interval. The action and displayed amplitude extend holomorphically across the fold. This does not by itself continue the actual finite-degree source, or control its Fourier transform with an exponentially accurate error. An exact reflected finite sequence is proved separately below using the original large q-Hahn numerator. ## 1. Actual finite factors and analytic functions Use the original D_a, beta_a, P_s and B_(N,a)=beta_a^2 D_a(x,b,y)D_a(x,c,y)P_(d-2a)(x,y) of the [signed source theorem](general_signed_augmented_source_volume.md). The radii are in one of its fixed actual nonnegative patterns, with positive entries in a compact set. In particular A=x+y>0 and T_b+T_c>0, where T_b^2=bA+xy and T_c^2=cA+xy. Put d=N-1, M=floor(d/2), s0=d-2M and h=1/N. On a fixed sufficiently small complex z disk choose the square roots at their positive value at zero and define D(z)=A^2-4xy sin^2(pi z), E_b(z)=A+2b sin^2(pi z) +2sin(pi z)sqrt[T_b^2+b^2 sin^2(pi z)], J_b(z)=cos(pi z)sqrt[T_b^2+b^2 sin^2(pi z)]/T_b, a_b(z)=(1/2) partial_z log J_b(z). (1) If T_b=0, define instead E_b=A, J_b=1 and a_b=0; this is the exact single-summand case. Define the c functions in the same way. All these are holomorphic on a disk uniform over the radius compact. The E functions and J functions are nonzero there. Direct algebra gives E_b(z)E_b(-z)=D(z), J_b(-z)=J_b(z), a_b(-z)=-a_b(z). Consequently the following action is holomorphic and even, with V(0)=0: V'(z)=Log[E_b(z)E_c(z)/D(z)], V''(0)=2pi(T_b+T_c)/A>0. (2) The logarithm in (2) is zero at zero. This fixes the branch and the additive constant from the actual source, not from an interpolated color index. ## 2. Analytic cancellation of the first correction For the actual scaled Schur pivot e_a=(beta_a D_a)/(beta_(a-1)D_(a-1)) write z=(N/2-a)/N. Its exact recurrence is e(z)=(1+tau)[A+2b sin(pi z)sin(pi(z+h))] -tau D(z+h)/e(z+h), tau=tan(pi z)/tan(pi(z+h)). (3) Equation (3) denotes the original sequence only at its specified physical lattice. Define a holomorphic approximation on the disk by e_b^*(z,h)=E_b(z) exp[h a_b(z)]. (4) It obeys the exact reflection e_b^*(z,h)e_b^*(-z,h)=D(z). Clear the denominator in its recurrence residual, using this reflection: Rcal(z,h)=tan(pi(z+h)) e_b^*(z,h) +tan(pi z)e_b^*(-z-h,h) -[tan(pi(z+h))+tan(pi z)] [A+2b sin(pi z)sin(pi(z+h))]. (5) This is holomorphic jointly in z,h near zero. Its values at z=0 and z=-h are zero, because e_b^*(0,h)=A. Therefore Rcal=z(z+h)F(z,h) with F holomorphic. title: The radial positive Fourier comparison does not supply a common geometric frame
status: Conditional radial-frame obstruction; no rate gap
text: # The radial positive Fourier comparison does not supply a common geometric frame 30 October 2026. The positive coefficient partition retains the original shared Kirchhoff and Fourier constraints. Nevertheless its ordinary radial coefficient saddles cannot all assemble into the complete geometric representation of a certified right-angled augmented plat. The obstruction is conditional on that proposed assembly; it is not an exponential gap theorem for the positive partition. ## 1. Actual source and geometric hypotheses Use the original marked matching source and the positive partition of [the shared Fourier comparison](actual_matching_graph_positive_fourier_partition.md). Retain its actual port orders, cup/cap monomials, half-twist phases, folded channels and exact ordinary channel metric. For the geometric conclusion assume the literal Morse-prefix and positive right-angled matching-polyhedron certificate of [the selected-frame obstruction](actual_right_angled_selected_framing_obstruction.md). Hyperbolicity alone is not substituted for that certificate. At matching edge i write xi_i=a_i/N, omega_i=w_i/N, rho_i=|omega_i|, t_i=d-|w_i|, tau_i=t_i/N, lambda_v=k_v/N. We discuss strict radial saddles: in the limiting coordinates 1/2<tau_i<1, 0<lambda_v<xi_i, and xi_i>0. The complete support condition is rho_i<=xi_i. Any assertion about the COMPLETE geometric representation further requires its endpoint channel xi_i=1/2 at every crossing disk. A saddle at other channels is not identified with that complete representation. The coefficient variational theorem supplies the actual selected ordinary kernel at y_v=log w_v^*, nu_v=tau_i/2-i y_v/(2pi), Y_v^*=exp[2pi i(lambda_v+1/2-xi_i)]. (1) Here w_v^*>0 is the coefficient's radial tilt; it is unrelated to the signed integral matching variable w_i. These are local ordinary kernel statements, not a claim about completed partner amplitudes. ## 2. Why every radial local factor is central The central domain of the proved joint packet is 1/2<Re tau<1, |2Re nu-Re tau|<1/2. (2) Every point (1) lies strictly in this domain, since its last expression is zero. The local source selects its continued characteristic there. This assertion respects BOTH actual degree adapters. In the low block the original physical wires are nu and tau-nu, with real parts tau/2. In the high block they are 1+nu-tau and 1-nu, with real parts 1-tau/2. Thus the high adapter has the same normalized central point; it is not obtained by applying a low formula to the wrong physical total degree. Reversing the two physical ports replaces nu by tau-nu and leaves the central property intact. It also respects BOTH ends of a matching edge. The actual white map is the reversed conjugate Clebsch column with its ordinary positive channel metric. The exact shared-cycle compiler proves that, after its own endpoint scalar, it uses the SAME normalized finite f as the black map. The distinct physical input/output momentum conventions are those of the selected-local certificate; they are not changed by declaring a new reciprocal branch. Consequently, if these factors assemble into an actual framed critical representation, every input and every output has the source-selected central coordinate (2). It follows immediately from the selected-frame obstruction that: No all-ordinary strict radial Fourier reconstruction can assemble into the complete positively oriented geometric representation in one common actual source frame. (3) The geometric theorem covers the retained half twists and actual projection prefixes. The contradiction does not use a freely chosen circle packing or unrelated face labels. In particular adding the real constrained stationarity equations of the positive partition cannot make such an assembly possible: (3) already holds before those extra equations are imposed. ## 3. The exact coefficient phase contains missing coordinate data This failure is also visible directly in the original finite source. On physical cycle c write the actual FIRST port at vertex v as u_v=epsilon_v x_c+B_v, epsilon_v in {+1,-1}, b_v=max(0,T_i-d), T_i=d+w_i. The scalar B_v is the literal propagated affine offset. It is not reduced modulo N. The exact vertex expansion is c_v c_(t_i,a_i) sum_k p_(t_i,a_i,k) q^[(d-2a_i+2k)(epsilon_v x_c+B_v-b_v)-t_i k]. (4) After extracting the x_c character, the k-dependent residual phase in (4) has the exact successive ratio exp{2pi i[(B_v-b_v)/N-t_i/(2N)]}. (5) No endpoint scalar, cup monomial or half-twist factor changes (5), because those factors are independent of this coefficient index k. Other vertices retain their own coefficient indices. Thus on a fixed affine sign chamber, the leading logarithmic phase has derivative with respect to lambda_v equal to 2pi i delta_v, delta_v=(B_v-b_v)/N-tau_i/2. (6) Taking positive moduli deletes exactly this derivative. In contrast, the positive coefficient action L has derivative L_lambda=-y_v. The positive constrained lambda equations therefore match the real radial tilts through cycle multipliers, but do not by themselves match the real magnetic coordinates. More explicitly, suppose one tries to reconstruct the same radial local saddle on the original physical cycle. Write X_c=x_c/N. Its actual normalized first coordinate must satisfy nu_v=epsilon_v X_c+(B_v-b_v)/N. (7) Combining (7) with (1) requires BOTH equations epsilon_v Im X_c=-y_v/(2pi), epsilon_v Re X_c+delta_v=0. (8) The first is the radial magnitude matching. The second is the real center matching whose term is retained by (5),(6) and omitted in the positive envelope. It is not a consequence of Kirchhoff closure. Equivalently, on the original displayed logarithmic character, if one introduces a complex multiplier Lambda_c for the cycle's linear coefficient constraint, the local equation is -y_v+2pi i delta_v+epsilon_v Lambda_c=0. (9) With Lambda_c=2pi i X_c, (9) gives exactly (8). A real multiplier for the positive action retains only its real part. All of these statements concern the original affine lift. Introducing additional logarithmic characters or changing that lift would be extra data, not a justification for deleting (5). ## 4. What the retained Fourier constraints do prove The positive comparison still preserves a genuine phase equation. Let epsilon_b be the slope of the recorded first coordinate at each actual cup or restored cap of c. The exact source character is m_c=sum_v epsilon_v(d-2a_i+2k_v) +d sum_b epsilon_b. The actual even-cycle proof makes E_c=sum_v epsilon_v+sum_b epsilon_b even. Fourier extraction requires m_c=2b_c modulo 2N, where b_c is one at the original marked cycle and zero elsewhere. Substitution of (1), using d=N-1, gives EXACTLY product_v (Y_v^*)^epsilon_v (-1)^(sum_b epsilon_b) =Q^(E_c/2+b_c). (10) Thus the cup signs, finite pivotal correction and original one-unit charge remain specified. Their limiting product is one. Equation (10) closes these particular phase characters on the actual physical cycles; it does not supply (8), a common geometric frame, all complex edge equations, or a contributing source integration cycle. For reference, the interior positive action with its original scalar is S=sum_i [ b(xi_i,rho_i) +L(1-rho_i,xi_i,lambda_(i,W)) +L(1-rho_i,xi_i,lambda_(i,pi)) ], b(xi,rho)=J(xi+rho)-2J(xi)-2J(rho)-J(xi-rho). (11) Here S is the rate of the UNSQUARED coefficient weight; each summand of Z_F has rate 2S. This follows directly from the exact B_N in the positive partition and the uniform sine-factorial estimate. Its variables still satisfy the shared Kirchhoff equations and one fixed Fourier winding branch. Equation (11) is a local interior rate, not a global Laplace theorem covering its boundary. In particular no Casson--Rivin identification of (11) is obtained by differentiating it and ignoring (6). ## 5. Scope and the retained route This obstruction does NOT prove a strict numerical rate gap between the positive partition and the original source. Boundary maximizing sequences, different coherent regroupings, nonradial saddles and cancellations remain separate questions. It does not rule out a volume identity whose numerical value is obtained in another way. The existing [selected-factor localization](actual_augmented_plat_selected_factor_localization.md) instead puts every ordinary factor outside ONE prescribed matching edge on its actual selected FULL physical packet. Those coordinates need not be central or radial. The two exceptional factors are kept in their exact marked four-port block, with every target and required generic normal retained. The present calculation preserves that route; it does not replace its remaining contraction and period estimates. Focused audit: [finite phase derivatives and adapter identities](../experiments/audit_actual_positive_fourier_radial_geometric_obstruction.py). The radial obstruction does not give a rate gap or a boundary conclusion. The common-frame hypothesis and exceptional-block route remain essential.

text: # The positive Newton capacity can exceed the complete rate 30 October 2026. This concerns the proposed absolute Newton majorant, not the original alternating low-color source. The exact original Newton coefficient Put q=exp(pi i/N), d=N-1, s_j=2sin(pi j/N), S_j=product_(k=1)^j s_k, and B_r(z)=product_(k=0)^(r-1)(q^(2k+1)+q^(-2k-1)-z), Bhat_r=B_r/S_r^2. Its source scalar is N^(R-1) product_remaining(k_a beta_a^2), since every remaining epsilon is0. The source theorem retains its ordinary caps, mark, physical support and finite-grid measure.
