This one-port original-source identity assumes connected identity smoothing and distinct unmarked middle faces, exactly as in its linked source theorem. It does not extend the graph family through an absent flat-plat adapter. For 1<=h<=floor(N/2), the exact original Chebyshev--Newton identity is T_h=sum_(r=0)^(h-1) (-1)^(h-1+r) b_(h,r) Bhat_r(-T), b_(h,r)=S_r^2 S_(h+r)/[S_(2r+1)S_(h-r-1)]>0, b_(h,r)<=N/2. The last uniform bound follows from the actual sine product: its log-concavity in h puts the maximum at h=N/2; double-angle cancellation gives 2 product_(k=1)^r s_(2k)/product_(k=0)^r s_(2k+1). Its successive ratio changes once from <=1 to >=1, so the two endpoints suffice. They are csc(pi/N) and either N/2 or csc(pi/N), all <=N/2. This is also proved in [the pure-leaf calculation](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_pure_conway_auxiliary_color_leaf.md). The majorant studied here is the TRUE sum sum_r b_(h,r)Z_r, retaining these magnitudes rather than replacing all of them by N/2. ## 1. The complete shared-face angle problem Use one actual untwisted port with distinct unmarked middle faces b,c and distinct unmarked outer faces x,y. Its two removed triangles are (x,b,y),(x,c,y). Retain ALL other original triangle incidences and the original marked faces u,v. Let R be the number of original circles. For every remaining triangle t and incident face f introduce a_tf>=0, with sum_f a_tf=1/2. Its center angle is theta_tf=2pi a_tf. Corners at u,v are fixed zero. The exact fold local entropy is S_t(a_t)=V(2pi a_t)/(2pi), V(theta)=2 sum_j[Lambda(theta_j/2)+Lambda((pi-theta_j)/2)]. These are the source-normalized triangle entropies; no local constant or exterior phase is reset. Put rho=r/N, mu=m/N, xi=i/N, eta=j/N for the exact positive Newton coefficient (0). Its limiting domain is 0<=rho<=1/2, rho<=mu<=1, 0<=xi,eta<=rho, xi+eta<=mu, mu+rho-xi-eta<=1. (1) The true physical cap is rho<h/N; it approaches1/2 when h=floor(N/2). The actual root-zero wall at the last boundary is interpreted by approach from its nonzero side, not as replacing a vanished coefficient. Let K(mu,rho,xi,eta) be J(mu)+J(mu+rho-xi-eta)-J(mu-rho)-J(mu-xi-eta) -J(xi)-J(rho-xi)-J(eta)-J(rho-eta), (2) where J(t)=integral_0^t log(2sin(pi z))dz. This is the sum of four ideal-tetrahedron volumes/pi, with normalized angle triples (rho,mu-rho,1-mu), (rho,mu-xi-eta,1-mu-rho+xi+eta), (xi,rho-xi,1-rho), (eta,rho-eta,1-rho). The FULL shared-face constraints are sum_(t incident f) a_tf =1 for f outside{x,y,b,c,u,v}, sum_t a_tx=1-xi, sum_t a_ty=1-eta, sum_t a_tb=1-mu+xi+eta, sum_t a_tc=mu. (3) They follow directly from the exact finite monomial: c^m -> x^i y^j c^(m-i-j), followed by c=b and target exponent d. The input b exponent is d-m+i+j. Thus these are not factorwise maxima or independently chosen local degrees. Their sum is R-1, exactly the total remaining triangle degree. Define C_Newt=max_(1),(3) [sum_remaining S_t+K]. (4) The polytope is compact and the objective continuous and concave. It is the natural shared capacity for the positive one-port Newton coefficient with every other channel at maximal fold. The ordinary source polynomial and its normalized Newton kernel are nonnegative. The source measure N^(R-1), k factors and odd maximal-fold beta=1 are subexponential; no exponential normalization is omitted. ## 2. Euler--Lagrange equations and the lost phase At a strict constrained maximum let l_f>0 be the shared face multipliers. Use the Lagrangian sum S_t+K+sum_f log(l_f)(sum_t a_tf-demand_f). The triangle equations are exactly the original source circle-angle equations, tan(theta_tf/2) proportional to l_f. Write s(t)=sin(pi t). The remaining interior equations are s(mu)s(mu+rho-xi-eta) / [s(mu-rho)s(mu-xi-eta)] = l_c/l_b, s(mu-xi-eta)s(rho-xi) / [s(mu+rho-xi-eta)s(xi)] = l_b/l_x, s(mu-xi-eta)s(rho-eta) / [s(mu+rho-xi-eta)s(eta)] = l_b/l_y, s(mu+rho-xi-eta)s(mu-rho) / [s(rho-xi)s(rho-eta)] =1. (5) At an active rho boundary the last equality is replaced by its KKT inequality. These equations do not retain the original factor (-1)^(h-1+r) in the low-color Newton sum. In the actual complex stationarity equation that factor contributes the linear character pi i rho (with its fixed lattice mark); its exponential rho equation would have the opposite sign. Dropping it is therefore a change of critical scheme, not a harmless choice of a logarithm. ## 3. A certified two-sided Apollonian matched-graph family Start from the actual octahedral-white source used in the frozen smoothing-fixed-radius note: white faces0,1,2,3 form the equator, 4,5 are the two poles, matching edges are01,12,34,35, and marked MAIN23 is unchanged. In the marked chart, faces2,3 are the parallel lines y=0,2; circles0,1 have curvatures2 and centers(0,1/2),(0,3/2), and circles4,5 have curvature1 and centers(-sqrt2,1),(sqrt2,1). Make n literal Apollonian insertions into triangle(0,1,4), and n into triangle(0,1,5), each successive insertion inside the triangle adjacent to the retained matched edge01. On each side the new matching edge is the previous-middle/new-middle edge, exactly as in the frozen one-sided construction. Both constructions have disjoint interiors. The old matching01 remains; marked MAIN23 is untouched. The explicit small disks have curvatures B_n=4n^2+4sqrt2 n+1 and centers (+/- (2n+sqrt2)/B_n,1). The already proved tangent-disk and supporting-halfspace induction applies separately on the two sides. Thus this is an actual connected certified augmented matched graph, not an arbitrary angle graph. Identity smoothing at01 merges its two opposite final middle faces b_n,c_n; its two chains keep the smoothed projection connected and the marked faces distinct. There is an essential presentation qualification. The embedded dual and chosen matching give a literal general Morse augmented diagram, with its original cyclic ports. The currently proved marked coefficient compiler, however, assumes a fixed FLAT PLAT with k bottom cups, k top caps and its specified gap sweep. No adapter has yet been proved that carries the successive local subdivisions into that compiler while preserving this positive coefficient formula. Nor is a common bridge width over all n asserted. Choosing a fixed depth gives a finite graph, but a general link-to-plat isotopy by itself is not the missing adapter. Consequently the unconditional obstruction below concerns its specified positive determinant polynomial and capacity. Its conclusion for the original flat-plat quantum source requires that actual adapter; the exact one-port kernel formula alone does not supply it. The two original triangles at01 now have the SAME curvatures (l_x,l_b,l_y)=(2,B_n,2), (l_x,l_c,l_y)=(2,B_n,2). Put a_n=(2/pi)atan(1/sqrt(B_n+1)). Their normalized angles (theta_x,theta_b,theta_y)/pi are (a_n,1-2a_n,a_n), and a_n->0. KEEP EVERY remaining original packing angle exactly as it was. Its demands in (3) are met by rho=1/4, mu=1/2+a_n, xi=eta=a_n. (6) For sufficiently large fixed n these lie strictly in (1), and the four kernel tetrahedron triples are (1/4,1/4+a_n,1/2-a_n), (1/4,1/2-a_n,1/4+a_n), (a_n,1/4-a_n,3/4), (a_n,1/4-a_n,3/4). Let F0=Vol(Y_n)/(2pi) be the geometric complete capacity of this certified matched graph. Its identification with the original flat-plat complete rate requires the stated compiler adapter. The value of the FULL shared objective at this feasible state exceeds F0 by E(a_n)=K(1/2+a_n,1/4,a_n,a_n) -V(pi a_n,pi(1-2a_n),pi a_n)/pi. (7) The subtraction is the TWO deleted source triangle entropies, each V/(2pi), not one. By continuity of the actual Lobachevsky functions, E(a_n) -> 2 Catalan/pi = v_oct/(2pi)>0. (8) Indeed the last two kernel tetrahedra flatten, the first two tend to the right ideal tetrahedron with angles(pi/4,pi/4,pi/2), of volume Catalan, while the old two source triangle entropies tend to0. Hence for every sufficiently large FIXED n, C_Newt >= F0+E(a_n)>F0. (9) This refutes the proposed universal strict comparison even AFTER allowing all shared radii/angles to readjust: (6) is already a feasible full angle state. It does not refute the original volume conjecture. ## 4. A lower bound for the specified positive coefficient The following lower-bound step uses only the supplied positive determinant saddle estimates. At odd N, M=d/2, each normalized remaining white polynomial D_M has degree M and nonnegative coefficients. For a fixed strict source-angle triple, its prescribed coefficient with exponents M theta_j/pi+O(1) has exponential rate V(theta)/(2pi). This follows from the SAME PSD contraction proof as the frozen face-coefficient saddle, applied to that single two/three-variable pencil and its prescribed interior logarithmic-gradient target: pair traces give the global torus gap, the Hessian is cN on its homogeneity quotient, and the finite saddle moves o(1). One-variable forced faces are literal monomials. Fixed zero marked corners are deleted before this argument; all other corners in this fixed certified packing are strictly positive. There are compatible integer exponents with all these triple fractions and all original ordinary face targets. Scale the remaining packing flows by d rather than N: every row then has the integer sum M=d/2, and all face columns outside x,y,b,c already have target d. Round within the bipartite row/face incidence network, allowing the four displayed face columns to vary by O(1). Impose the integer floor and ceiling of each given entry as lower and upper bounds. The row equations and fixed face-column equations form a totally unimodular network matrix. Its bounded feasible polytope has an integral vertex, preserving every fixed integer margin and changing each entry by at most1. Marked zeros stay zero. Strict positive entries stay positive for large N. The resulting actual remaining input monomial has c exponent m=d(1/2+a_n)+O(1)<N, and its deficits determine i=d a_n+O(1), j=d a_n+O(1), with the merged b target exactly d. Choose r=N/4+O(1) integer. Every finite kernel sine product is then in its strict nonzero domain. The exact Newton coefficient formula and the uniform sine-product estimates show that this ONE product of positive coefficients contributes rate F0+E(a_n). Thus for the specified positive Newton polynomial coefficient at maximal remaining labels, liminf_(N odd) N^-1 log Z_(r_N) >= F0+E(a_n). (10) The specified original-compiler scalar, if its adapter is established, is polynomial and does not change this inequality. For h_N=floor(N/2), r_N=N/4+O(1), the exact coefficient b_(h_N,r_N) has exponential rate zero directly from the exact finite sine products: lim N^-1 log b_(h_N,r_N) =2J(1/4)+J(3/4)-J(1/2)-J(1/4)=0, using J(3/4)=-J(1/4), J(1/2)=0 and the uniform O(log N) factorial errors. No off-grid color interpolation is needed for this step. Consequently the TRUE absolute Newton expansion sum_(r<h_N) b_(h_N,r) Z_r also has lower rate at least F0+E(a_n). This is not an artifact of replacing b by its upper bound N/2. To obtain a volume-rate upper bound for the alternating polynomial, one would therefore need exponential cancellation in the retained signs (-1)^(h_N-1+r), possibly together with remaining source sums. No such upper bound or cancellation theorem has been proved here. The positive-polynomial majorant cannot supply a capacity comparison on all certified matched graphs. Without the presentation adapter this is not a claimed flat-plat source counterexample. Finally, (9) prevents an interpretation of the maximizing positive capacity as Vol(rho)/(2pi) for a representation of the SAME original group with the actual source normalization. Such an interpretation would contradict the independently proved universal representation- volume bound. The missing Newton phase in (5) identifies a concrete reason that the positive critical scheme is not the original one. ## Appendix: proof of the finite positive Newton identity One may first work at generic q, writing s_j=(q^j-q^-j)/i and c_j=q^(2j+1)+q^(-2j-1). The original operator acts by T c^m=-c_m c^m+s_m^2(x+y)c^(m-1) +s_m s_(m-1)xy c^(m-2). (A1) The literal coefficients at the bottom two rows are zero, so there are no negative powers. Define D(c^m)=s_m c^(m-1), R_j(c^k)=s_(k+2j+2)c^(k+1) +s_(k+j+1)(x+y)c^k+s_k xy c^(k-1). Direct computation gives R_0 D=T+c_0, D R_j=R_(j+1)D+s_1 s_(2j+2)I, sum_(j=0)^(r-1) s_1 s_(2j+2)=c_0-c_r. It follows inductively that B_r(-T)=R_0 R_1...R_(r-1)D^r. (A4) This already proves the exact zero for r>m. For r<=m, the coefficient of x^i y^j c^(m-i-j) asserted by (0), after multiplication by S_r^2, is C_r(m;i,j)= S_m S_(m+r-i-j) S_r^2 / [S_(m-r)S_(m-i-j)S_i S_(r-i)S_j S_(r-j)]. (A5) The recurrence B_(r+1)(-T)=(T+c_r)B_r(-T), using (A1), proves (A5). For completeness, set k=m-i-j. After dividing on the generic open set and clearing the factors, the only identity needed is s_(k-r)s_(r+1-i)s_(r+1-j) +s_(k+1)[s_i s_(r+1-j)+s_j s_(r+1-i)] +s_(k+r+2)s_i s_j =s_(k+i+j-r)s_(r+1)^2. (A6) This follows by substituting s_a=(q^a-q^-a)/i. The zero-index boundary terms of the recurrence are recovered after clearing denominators, or directly from (A4). Thus the generic polynomial identity holds. Specialize it through the finite products in (0): all denominators S_r,S_i,S_j,S_(r-i),S_(r-j) are nonzero for r<N. If m+r-i-j<N, all surviving sine factors are positive; otherwise its interval of r consecutive numerator factors contains s_N, since m-i-j<N. This proves the claimed root positivity. At the top endpoint r=d, only m=d and i+j=d survive, and every binomial [d choose i]_s equals1. Hence a useful exact endpoint is Bhat_d(-T)c^d=sum_(i=0)^d x^i y^(d-i), Bhat_d(-T)c^m=0 for m<d. (A7) ## Validation and remaining source interface The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_positive_newton_capacity_obstruction.py) and [saved results](../experiments/actual_positive_newton_capacity_obstruction_results.json) check the exact local identity against the original coproduct Casimir: 2,436 monomial paths, including812 high totals and756 preserved whole-N blocks, 55,562 low-color matrix entries and15,316 complete-color entries. Two cleared symbolic identities and1,286 exact numerator-zero cases check the finite formula; finite-field arithmetic verifies equality, while nonnegativity is supplied by the sine-product proof. Four explicit two-sided matched graphs check76 matching incidences, 1,416 white and2,376 shaded support inequalities,228 right angles and 62 shared-face equations. Six integral-flow roundings check132 integer row margins,60 fixed face columns and all strict Newton domains. Eighteen literal determinant coefficients include three-, two- and one-variable cases. The finite coefficient/entropy profiles are diagnostics; the limit and positive gap follow from the written analytic arguments. The audit does not label the graph family as a flat-plat source fixture. The two-sided supporting-halfspace, matching, mark and load calculations do not supply the missing flat-plat compiler adapter. The classical capacity identity is geometric. Its use for the source remains conditional on the stated source interface.

title: An exact positive Newton period with cuboctahedral hyperbolic volume
text: # An exact positive Newton period with cuboctahedral hyperbolic volume 29 October 2026. For every odd N=2m+1 define the ACTUAL root polynomial h=Rturn(E_St) in H_N and the original Frobenius period W_N=phi(h^4). The [positive multiplication theorem](../papers/newton-calculus/README.md) retains the full source and proves W_N>0. This note proves lim_(N odd ->infty) (pi/N)log W_N=Vol(Q_cube), (1) where Q_cube is the explicit ideal right-angled cuboctahedron in the [actual core geometry](actual_nc_graph_rectified_core_geometry.md). The proof is a real, strictly concave volume maximization. No stationary-phase noncancellation or contour-selection assumption occurs. The [literal cube source reduction](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_odd_central_cube_reflection_packet.md) then gives the corresponding actual hyperbolic-volume rate for its ODD CENTRAL JOINT SECTOR. The full color sum and even levels are not asserted here. A sector is not substituted for the whole invariant. ## 1. Exact positive partition with every root normal Use d=2m, s_r=product_(u=1)^r 2sin(pi u/N), and Bhat_r from the Newton theorem. That theorem gives h=sum_(i=0)^m b_i Bhat_i, b_i=s_m^2/(s_i^2s_(m-i)^2)>0, h^2=sum_(k=0)^d a_k Bhat_k, a_k=sum_(0<=i,j<=m, max(i,j)<=k<=i+j) b_i b_j mu_(i,j,k), W_N=sum_(k=0)^d a_k a_(d-k). (2) The last equation is the original full Frobenius pairing, not a value-only trace. Every a_k is strictly positive. Its summation labels can be written (i,j,u,v,k), with the first pair producing k and the second producing d-k. There are only polynomially many such labels. Put L(x)=integral_0^x log(2sin(pi t))dt, continuously on [0,1]. The uniform sine-factorial estimate is log s_r=N L(r/N)+O(log N), for every 0<=r<=d, including endpoints. Define g(x)=-2L(x)-2L(1/2-x), 0<=x<=1/2, mu(x,y,z)=L(x+y)+L(z)-L(x)-L(y) -L(z-x)-L(z-y)-L(x+y-z). (3) The mu-domain is max(x,y)<=z<=x+y<=1. The exact summands in (2) have logarithm N times A(i,j,u,v,k)=g(i)+g(j)+g(u)+g(v) +mu(i,j,k)+mu(u,v,1-k) (4) up to O(log N), when the letters now denote their scaled real labels. Replacing d/N by 1 or m/N by 1/2 changes these estimates by O(log N), uniformly. This follows from the modulus of continuity of L at 0,1, not from an invalid bounded derivative at those endpoints. Let P be the compact convex polytope defined by 0<=i,j,u,v<=1/2 and the two mu-domain constraints in (4). Positivity and polynomial state count give the upper bound by max_P A. Any strictly interior feasible point can be rounded to actual odd-level integers with O(1/N) changes; a single positive term supplies the matching lower bound at an interior maximizer. Thus it suffices to find that maximum. ## 2. Each multiplication action is a positive tetrahedral volume For a mu-triple put p=z-x, q=z-y, r=x+y-z, w=1-x-y. They are nonnegative and p+q+2r+w=1. Write V(alpha,beta,gamma) for the volume of the ideal tetrahedron with dihedral angles pi alpha, pi beta, pi gamma, where their sum is 1. Thus V=-pi[L(alpha)+L(beta)+L(gamma)]. The identity L(1-t)=-L(t) gives EXACTLY pi mu = V(p+r,q+r,w) +V(p,q,2r+w)+V(p+q,r,r+w). (5) All three are positive ideal angle triples when p,q,r,w>0. Also pi g(x)=2V(x,1/2-x,1/2). (6) The ideal tetrahedron volume is strictly concave on its angle simplex. For an elementary Hessian check, eliminate its third angle; the diagonal coefficients involve cot(alpha)+cot(gamma)>0 and the determinant uses cot(alpha)cot(beta)+cot(beta)cot(gamma) +cot(gamma)cot(alpha)=1. Hence the negative Hessian is positive definite. The linear angle map in (5) is injective: its second triangle supplies p,q and its third supplies r. Therefore mu is strictly concave on its open domain. Continuity extends concavity to the closed domain. The same conclusion holds for g. This is a positive volume functional for the FULL period partition. Off its maximum the tetrahedra in (5) are not yet asserted to be the metric tetrahedra of a glued cuboctahedron. The exact value at the maximum is compared with the actual polyhedron in section 4. ## 3. Unique global maximum and its algebraic equation The polytope and A are invariant under i<->j, u<->v, and exchange of the two pairs with k->1-k. Averaging over these symmetries cannot decrease a concave function. The strict concavity of the four g terms forces i=j=u=v=t at a maximizing point unless those values already agree. With these fixed, strict concavity of the two mu terms forces k=1/2. It is therefore enough to maximize on 1/4<=t<=1/2 the function A_sym(t)=6g(t)+2[L(2t)-L(2t-1/2)]. (7) In its interior, A_sym'(t)=-12log tan(pi t)+4log[-tan(2pi t)]. (8) The derivative tends to +infinity at 1/4 and to -infinity at 1/2. The original strict concavity, or direct differentiation of (8), gives a unique maximum. Setting y=tan(pi t)>1 in (8) yields 2y/(y^2-1)=y^3, hence y^2=2. Thus t*=atan(sqrt(2))/pi. All inequalities in P that can be strict are strict at (t*,t*,t*,t*,1/2). In particular rounding i,j,u,v to the nearest t*N and taking k=m gives actual summands at every large odd level. This completes the positive Laplace proof of the limit N^(-1)log W_N=A_sym(t*), without choosing a subsequence inside odd N. ## 4. Direct volume of the ACTUAL ideal cuboctahedron Let theta=atan(sqrt(2)) and delta=pi/2-theta. The Klein vertices of Q_cube are the permutations of (±1,±1,0)/sqrt(2). Its supporting planes and all right angles were certified in the core geometry. For a completely explicit volume calculation order its twelve vertices by choosing the zero coordinate in order 0,1,2, then the other two signs in order (--),(-+),(+-),(++). Cone its faces to vertex 0, which is (0,-1/sqrt(2),-1/sqrt(2)). The nonincident face fans give the following fourteen geometric tetrahedra, specified by the unordered sets of their three other vertices; each tetrahedron is positively reoriented when computing its shape: (4,8,5), (4,5,9), (6,10,7), (6,7,11), (2,9,3), (2,3,11), (1,5,3), (1,3,7), (1,5,8), (2,4,9), (3,5,9), (1,7,10), (2,6,11), (3,7,11). (9) These are disjoint face cones in a convex polyhedron. The first eight triangulate its four nonincident square faces; the last six are its nonincident triangular faces. There is no tetrahedron recognition based only on a numerical volume. Stereographic coordinates z=(X+iY)/(1-Z) and the cross-ratio formula give ten tetrahedra of angle type A, two of B, and two of E: A=(theta,delta,pi/2), B=(theta,theta,pi-2theta), E=(2theta-pi/2,delta,pi-theta). (10) Representative positive cross ratios are respectively 2/3+i sqrt(2)/3, 1/3+2i sqrt(2)/3, and 2/3+i sqrt(2)/6. Their three cyclic shape arguments give (10) directly. For example the E angles follow from the shapes 2+i sqrt(2) and -1/3+i sqrt(2)/3, together with tan(2theta-pi/2)=1/(2sqrt(2)). The audit verifies every cross ratio in (9) algebraically in Q(sqrt(2),i), using its positive shape representative rather than treating the displayed vertex order as an orientation. With Lambda(x)=-integral_0^x log|2sin t|dt, (9),(10) give Vol(Q_cube)=12Lambda(theta)+12Lambda(delta) -2Lambda(2theta)+2Lambda(2theta-pi/2). (11) On the other hand L(t)=-Lambda(pi t)/pi, so substituting t* into (7) gives precisely pi A_sym(t*)=(11). This proves the claimed equality with the ACTUAL complete core volume in (1). ## 5. The original cube sector and the remaining whole-source problem The separately proved literal exposed-source identity is Z_(cube,central)=N^12 S_N^8 W_N omega_m^(sum e), where S_N is the original positive central trivalent scalar after its recorded unit phase, lim N^(-1)log S_N=v8/pi, and the retained twists are unit characters in this fixed sector. Therefore lim_(N odd) (2pi/N)log|Z_(cube,central)| =16v8+2Vol(Q_cube) =Vol(S^3 minus the ACTUAL augmented cube link). (12) The last equality is the independent complete-core construction with b=4. Thus the geometric growth is present in an actual source sector and its complete positive partition, including every root normal. This does NOT establish that other color sectors cannot cancel or exceed it, nor the corresponding even-level assertion. Those are still required before claiming the full cube volume conjecture, and general graphs need their own full-source control. Audit: [positive partition and exact cuboctahedral shapes](../experiments/audit_actual_positive_newton_cuboctahedral_period.py). Finite values check the implementation; the limiting equality follows from the uniform factorial envelope, strict concavity, lattice rounding and the explicit geometric tetrahedra above.

title: A rational Bloch regulator for every positive-source volume maximum
text: # A rational Bloch regulator for every positive-source volume maximum **Later geometric result, 29 October 2026:** for every retained cylindrical robust Conway factor, the [actual cell realization](../papers/strict-conway-geometry/README.md) now identifies the source class with the geometric rational Bloch class over a common number field, and its regulator with the actual complete complement volume. The abstract rational-angle theorem below continues to apply more broadly and does not itself supply a manifold. 29 October 2026. The algebraic volume period of every robust positive Conway source is the regulator of an actual rational Bloch cycle. The cycle is obtained by subtracting the complex-conjugate shape symbols. Its boundary vanishes by the source's full constrained stationarity equations. This is stronger than a formal sum of algebraic dilogarithms, but does not identify the cycle with the marked fundamental class of a link complement. The argument applies to EVERY rational affine ideal-angle volume problem in the [algebraic maximum theorem](../papers/newton-calculus/README.md), including boundary maxima and nonunique optimizers. It uses that theorem's quotient by the exact flat Hessian kernel; it does not assume that an optimizer is isolated in the original wire coordinates. ## 1. The rational Bloch group and regulator convention Let K be a number field with its specified complex embedding, stable under complex conjugation. Write U_K=K^times tensor_Z Q, additively, and write ell(a) for the image of a nonzero field element in U_K. Thus ell(ab)=ell(a)+ell(b); roots of unity have image zero. Let P(K)_Q be the Q-vector space on symbols [z], z in K minus {0,1}, modulo the five-term relations [x]-[y]+[y/x] -[(1-x^-1)/(1-y^-1)]+[(1-x)/(1-y)]=0, (1) where the displayed arguments are defined and different from 0 and 1. Use the boundary convention delta[z]=ell(z) wedge ell(1-z), B(K)_Q=ker(delta:P(K)_Q -> exterior^2 U_K). (2) This is the rational Bloch group, not an assertion of an integral lift or of a particular K_3 lattice. The five-term relation has zero boundary by direct expansion. In fact put X=ell(x), Y=ell(y), A=ell(1-x), B=ell(1-y), C=ell(x-y). The five pairs ell(z),ell(1-z) in (1) are (X,A), (Y,B), (Y-X,C-X), (Y+A-X-B,C-X-B), (A-B,C-B). Their signed wedge sum is identically zero in the free exterior algebra on X,Y,A,B,C. Thus (2) is well defined without requiring algebraic independence of the displayed field elements. Let D(z) be the Bloch-Wigner dilogarithm, normalized so that a positive ideal tetrahedron of shape z has hyperbolic volume D(z). Then D(bar z)=-D(z). The same five-term relation holds for D, so R_K:P(K)_Q -> R, R_K([z])=D(z) (3) is a well-defined regulator component for the specified embedding. For completeness, the five-term identity follows from dD(z)=log|z| d arg(1-z)-log|1-z| d arg(z). Applying this alternating bilinear differential to the preceding zero wedge sum shows that the five-term D expression is locally constant in x,y. The complex domain with x,y different from 0,1 and from each other is connected. Letting y tend to x, all three ratio arguments tend to 1, where D has continuous value zero; the first two terms cancel. The constant is therefore zero. This also fixes the sign convention and normalization in (3). ## 2. The algebraic data selected by the source maximum Use the notation of the algebraic maximum theorem. The compact rational polytope carries positive rational weights w_j and rational affine ideal-angle triples alpha_j. Let F be its smallest face containing all maxima. On F discard the atoms which are identically flat, and call the remaining set I. Those positive atoms have the SAME angle triples at every maximum. After removing their common rational flat kernel, choose rational coordinates y_l in which the positive angles read alpha_jr=a_jr+sum_l b_jrl y_l, a_jr,b_jrl in Q. The proved algebraicity theorem supplies an optimum y_* for which the phases, sine values and positive shapes are algebraic. More explicitly choose a positive integer B clearing the b denominators, and put u_l=exp(pi i y_*l/B), t_jr=exp(pi i alpha_jr), s_jr=2sin(pi alpha_jr)>0. Then t_jr=eta_jr product_l u_l^(B b_jrl), eta_jr=exp(pi i a_jr), (4) where eta_jr is a root of unity. Choose K to contain these finitely many algebraic numbers and their conjugates. It is a finite number field stable under the given complex conjugation. No assertion that K is the trace field of a manifold is being made. All positive angles are interior in their simplices at a relative- interior maximizer of F. Constrained stationarity in EVERY quotient tangent y_l gives sum_(j in I,r) w_j b_jrl log s_jr=0. (5) For an integer C clearing the rational exponents, (5) gives the exact algebraic relation product_(j,r) s_jr^(C w_j b_jrl)=1. (6) There is no winding ambiguity here: the s_jr are positive real numbers, and (6) is derived from the selected real maximum. Its image in U_K, divided by the nonzero rational C, is sum_(j,r) w_j b_jrl ell(s_jr)=0. (7) Equations (4) and (7), not merely the algebraicity of the shapes, are the reason the regulator has a Bloch-cycle lift. ## 3. The antisymmetric shape boundary For a positive angle triple (a,b,c), a+b+c=1, set t_a=exp(pi i a), s_a=2sin(pi a), and cyclically, z=t_a s_b/s_c. The Euclidean angle sine rule, or an elementary sine identity, gives 1-z=t_b^-1 s_a/s_c. (8) For the elementary check multiply (8) by sin(pi c): it says sin(pi c)=exp(pi i a)sin(pi b)+exp(-pi i b)sin(pi a). The imaginary parts cancel and the real part is sin(pi(a+b)), which equals sin(pi c). In particular Im z>0 and z has the prescribed ordered ideal angles. Write T_r=ell(t_r), S_r=ell(s_r). Since s_r is positive real, conjugation fixes S_r and sends T_r to -T_r. Also T_a+T_b+T_c=ell(-1)=0 in U_K. Using (8) to expand both shape boundaries therefore gives the exact identity delta([z]-[bar z]) =2(T_a wedge S_a+T_b wedge S_b+T_c wedge S_c). (9) For clarity, the individual unsymmetrized expansion is delta[z]=-T_a wedge T_b +T_a wedge(S_a-S_c)+T_b wedge(S_b-S_c) +S_b wedge S_a-S_b wedge S_c-S_c wedge S_a. The phase-phase and sine-sine terms are unchanged by conjugation; only the two middle phase-sine terms change sign. Their difference is (9). Thus the proof does not assume that the unsymmetrized sum of positive shape symbols already has zero boundary. ## 4. Stationarity kills the complete rational boundary Define the source class beta=(1/2) sum_(j in I) w_j([z_j]-[bar z_j]) in P(K)_Q. (10) By (4), after torsion has been removed, T_jr=B sum_l b_jrl U_l, U_l=ell(u_l). Equations (9) and (7) now give delta beta =sum_(j,r) w_j T_jr wedge S_jr =B sum_l U_l wedge (sum_(j,r) w_j b_jrl S_jr) =0. (11) Hence beta is in B(K)_Q. It is anti-invariant under complex conjugation and its regulator is EXACTLY R_K(beta)=sum_(j in I) w_j D(z_j)=max_P V. (12) There is no undetermined additive multiple of a volume constant in (12): the symbols use their actual positive shapes and the regulator uses actual ideal-tetrahedron volume. If there are no positive atoms, beta=0 and the maximum is zero. If there are no quotient tangent variables, (4) makes every T_jr zero and the same proof works directly. This construction includes rational weights and affine constants of arbitrary denominators. Passing to Q coefficients removes the roots of unity in (4), the factor ell(-1) in (9), and the cleared exponent in (6). The argument does NOT remove that torsion integrally. No integral K-theory, integral Bloch boundary, or integral peripheral normalization is asserted. The ordered positive triples are uniquely selected by the maximum, even when some original wire coordinates are free. Thus (10) does not depend on choosing values for those flat coordinates. It is unchanged as a displayed symbol expression by a rational change of quotient coordinates; the coordinates are used to prove (11), not to define its shapes. There is also an elementary descent which removes the auxiliary phase field. Put F_shape=Q(z_j,bar z_j : j in I) subset K. The displayed expression beta already belongs to P(F_shape)_Q. The inclusion F_shape^times -> K^times is injective; tensoring with Q preserves that injection. Exterior squares of vector spaces preserve injections as well (extend a basis of the smaller space to a basis of the larger one). Thus exterior^2 U_(F_shape) -> exterior^2 U_K is injective. The image of delta beta is zero by (11), so its boundary was zero over F_shape itself. Consequently beta belongs to B(F_shape)_Q. This descent uses neither a presumed injection of Bloch groups nor a Galois or Hilbert-90 theorem. The phase coordinates merely provide a finite algebraic field in which the boundary calculation is transparent. For an empty atom list the class is zero over Q. ## 5. The full original quantum limit is a Bloch regulator For EVERY fixed robust actual positive Conway expression E, the [whole-source variational theorem](../papers/newton-calculus/README.md) and the algebraic maximum theorem yield, along all levels and both parities, lim_(N -> infinity) (2pi/N)log Z_(E,N) =2 max_(P_E) V_E =R_(F_shape)(B_E), B_E=sum_(j in I_E)([z_j]-[bar z_j]) in B(F_shape)_Q. (13) The weights here are all one and B_E=2 beta. Although its displayed symbol expression has integer coefficients, its proved zero-boundary statement is rational; possible integral torsion has not been checked. Z_(E,N) is the entire original source, with all colors and repeated-root normal directions retained. The class is selected by that exact source's positive variational problem, not by choosing an arbitrary branch of an A-polynomial. The [cap-sum reduction](../papers/newton-calculus/README.md) is compatible with this construction. At a cap-closed product, the maximizing polytope is a Cartesian product, its final gate is flat, and the positive atom list is the union of the two lists. Thus, in a common number field, B_(cap FG)=B_(cap F)+B_(cap G). This agrees with the literal componentwise connected sum and exact source multiplication. It also shows why a nonzero Bloch regulator alone cannot certify a single complete hyperbolic complement. ## 6. The remaining geometric question is now more precise We have an actual source-selected RATIONAL BLOCH CLASS, and its regulator is the full quantum limit in (13). What is still missing for a broad hyperbolic-knot theorem is a proof that this regulator is the volume of the actual complement, for example by identifying the class with its marked geometric Bloch class or by supplying a source-compatible complete gluing certificate with the same volume. The vanishing in (11) is algebraic and global, but it is not a face pairing, an edge winding count, a cusp completeness equation, or a fundamental-class degree computation. It also does not identify K with a trace field, construct a generic-meridian A-torsor, or show that a formal source cycle is the preferred geometric representation. Those statements must not be inferred from the word "Bloch". Audit: [formal wedge and stationarity certificates](../experiments/audit_actual_positive_source_bloch_regulator.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_positive_source_bloch_regulator_results.json). The identities are uniform symbolic exterior-algebra calculations; finite numerical volumes are not used in their proof. Descent to the conjugation-stable shape field uses exterior-square injectivity. It does not assume that Bloch groups inject under field extension. The marked manifold-class comparison remains open.

title: A varying-radius alias estimate lowers the proved width threshold to nine
text: # A varying-radius alias estimate lowers the proved width threshold to nine 29 October 2026. The original short RP band admits a stronger global bound when its TRUE sine-binomial coefficients and its varying monic spectral radius are kept together. The uniform rate is B_*=(1/pi) integral_0^(pi/2) log rho(u) du < 81/100, instead of the previous (1/2)log(4+sqrt(15)). This proves the ENTIRE original-color source gap for every fixed odd width s>=9. All color endpoints, the even middle color, and the original Hermite normal jets remain. The previously proved corridor/filling and geometric-completion arguments therefore apply unchanged at those widths. This does not remove every width restriction: s=3,5,7 remain outside the present global alias argument. No assertion for them is obtained by naming this positive envelope a sharp source asymptotic. ## 1. Keep the exact original short-band coefficients Use q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, d=N-1, s_a=|(Q;Q)_a| and the monic physical middle continuants p_l. The exact identity in [the original global alias theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_pretzel_global_alias_and_colored_source_gap.md) is (-1)^(N+h-1) P_(N,h)(z) =sum_(l=0)^(h-1) (-1)^l q^(3l^2+4l+1-2hl-h) [h+l choose 2l+1]_Q bar p_l(z). (1) It holds for EVERY 1<=h<=floor(N/2), including h=N/2 at even N. All Gaussian factorial indices are below N. The actual alias is R P_(N,h), not P alone and not a semisimple truncation. The monic recurrence has p_(l+1)=(z-D_l)p_l-a_(l-1)^2 p_(l-1), D_l=4qQ^l-q(1+Q)Q^(2l), a_(l-1)=-(1-Q^l)^2, (p_0,p_(-1))=(1,0). (2) The finite root phases in (1) are retained. Only after this exact identity will absolute values be taken. In particular no conjectural Laurent positivity or ordinary-color unitarity is needed. ## 2. Exact pointwise maximal frozen radius Freeze u=pi l/N in [0,pi/2]. After a unit phase change the two frozen roots obey lambda^2-d_z lambda+a^2=0, d_z=z exp(-2iu)-4+2exp(2iu), a=4sin(u)^2. (3) For z=-2 define t=sqrt(1+8sin(u)^2), rho(u)=(t+1)/2 * [2+sqrt((t+1)(3-t))]. (4) This is EXACTLY the larger root modulus in (3), not a numerical fit. For a derivation put y=1-cos(2u), so a=2y, d_(-2)=-4+4i sin(2u). Then |d_(-2)|^2=16(1+2y-y^2), |d_(-2)^2-4a^2|=16sqrt(1+4y). If the root moduli are rho and a^2/rho, their squared sum is (|d|^2+|d^2-4a^2|)/2. Solving this quadratic and taking its positive square root gives (4). Equivalently set t-1=2sin theta; then rho(u)=(1+sin theta+cos theta)^2, 0<=theta<=pi/2. In particular rho is continuous, positive, rho>=a, and 4<=rho<=3+2sqrt(2). It is the POINTWISE maximum over all real z in [-2,2]. Indeed at z=2 the roots both equal -a. For fixed a, a root of modulus r>=a makes d_z lie on the ellipse d=r exp(i theta)+(a^2/r) exp(-i theta). Its closed interior is exactly the region where both roots have modulus at most r. For r=rho(u), the z=-2 endpoint lies on the ellipse and the z=2 endpoint lies inside. Convexity covers their entire affine z-segment. The two endpoints u=0,pi/2 follow directly from (3); no inverse eigenframe is used there. ## 3. A uniform varying-product estimate for the actual polynomials Put I(v)=integral_0^v log rho(pi t) dt, 0<=v<=1/2. The exact companions of (2), divided at their l-th step by rho(pi l/N), converge uniformly to a bounded continuous family whose root moduli are at most one, uniformly for z in [-2,2]. Their coefficients have no singular root endpoint. The frozen-block Cayley--Hamilton argument therefore gives max_(z in[-2,2]) |p_l(z)| <=exp[N I(l/N)+epsilon_N N], max_(0<=l<=floor(N/2)) epsilon_N ->0. (5) For clarity this is an actual product bound, not an adiabatic claim. For a fixed block length L, the exact normalized block differs uniformly by o(1) from its frozen power. A bounded 2x2 matrix with root moduli at most one has ||B^L||<=CL by Cayley--Hamilton, also at a double root. First choose L to make log(CL)/L small, then N large, and concatenate blocks. Uniform continuity of log rho turns the scalar product of radii into N I(l/N)+o(N), uniformly in l. The initial vector is exactly (1,0). This proves (5) through BOTH index endpoints without a conditioned eigenvector factor. ## 4. The entire sine-binomial envelope has an exact global maximum Let J(x)=integral_0^x log(2sin(pi t)) dt, 0<=x<=1. The already proved UNIFORM factorial estimate gives, with alpha=h/N and beta=l/N, log |[h+l choose 2l+1]_Q| =N[J(alpha+beta)-J(2beta)-J(alpha-beta)]+O(log N). (6) The index shifts by one cost O(log N), uniformly even at zero and N-1. This estimate is applied only to actual indices below N. Combining (5),(6), the possible term rate in (1) is at most F(alpha,beta)=J(alpha+beta)-J(2beta)-J(alpha-beta)+I(beta), 0<=beta<=alpha<=1/2. (7) Its maximum is EXACTLY B_*=I(1/2). Here is an elementary proof. For 0<beta<alpha<1/2, partial_alpha F=log[sin pi(alpha+beta)/sin pi(alpha-beta)]>=0, because their difference is 2cos(pi alpha)sin(pi beta)>=0. Thus maximize first at alpha=1/2. At that boundary, d/d beta F(1/2,beta) =log[rho(pi beta)/(4sin(pi beta)^2)]>=0, using rho>=a in section2. Therefore the maximum occurs at (alpha,beta)=(1/2,1/2). Since J(0)=J(1)=0, its value is B_*. All boundary cases follow by continuity of J and I. No unsupported interior saddle or numerical optimization is being used. Sum the at most N terms in (1). The polynomial degree is h-1<=N/2; complex Markov on [-2,2] controls N^(-2) times its first derivative at every actual node with only the same fixed factor as before. The actual crossing R has faithful Hermite norm at most9/8. Hence limsup_N (1/N) log max_(1<=h<=floor(N/2)) ||R P_(N,h)||_H <= B_*. (8) Thus (8) retains ALL original source normal jets and the actual crossing. It is not a bound for an unrelated positive comparison model. ## 5. A finite rigorous upper certificate and the width-nine margin The bound B_*<81/100 has a direct finite interval-arithmetic certificate, described explicitly here so it is reproducible as a proof rather than as sampled evidence. In variable t in[1,3], put u(t)=asin sqrt((t^2-1)/8). For a rational interval [a,b] in[1,3], (t+1) is increasing and sqrt((t+1)(3-t)) is decreasing. Therefore rho(u(t)) <= K(a,b) =(b+1)/2 * [2+sqrt((a+1)(3-a))]. Divide [1,3] into512 equal rational intervals. This gives the EXACT analytical upper sum B_* <= (1/pi) sum_[a,b] [u(b)-u(a)] log K(a,b). (9) Outward-rounded Arb evaluation at100-bit precision encloses the right side in [0.80908894192172909372913834 +/- 5e-26] <81/100. Only a fixed finite sum of square roots, asin, log and pi is evaluated; no large-N experiment enters this certificate. The [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_pretzel_all_width_extension.py) reconstructs the upper sum and proves the strict comparison by its enclosing interval. For the complete augmented rate A_s=V_s/(2pi), put j_0=v_8/pi. Its exact alias margin is g_s=A_s-(s-1)j_0 =j_0-(2s/pi) integral_0^(pi/s) (pi/s-v)sec(v)dv. (10) For alpha=pi/s<1, cos v>=1-v^2/2 gives g_s >= j_0-pi/s -pi^3/[12s^3(1-pi^2/(2s^2))]. (11) Use pi<22/7 and the first32 alternating terms of G=sum_(k>=0)(-1)^k/(2k+1)^2 as a rational LOWER bound for Catalan's constant; j_0=4G/pi. At s=9 the resulting rational lower bound is greater than0.812633708, hence greater than13/16 and81/100. The loss in (11) decreases with s>=9. Consequently g_s>B_* for EVERY odd s>=9. (12) This strictly improves the previous threshold25. The same constants do not prove the condition at s=3,5,7. ## 6. Transfer to the ENTIRE actual source and the remaining widths Every original auxiliary color is already covered by the exact two-band identities: high colors are c_(N,h)+RP_(N,h), low colors are pure (-1)^N RP_(N,j), including even j=N/2. The global coherent core bound remains j_0, with a strict macroscopic-color contraction. Every term containing m>=1 aliases therefore has upper rate (s-m)j_0+mB_* <=(s-1)j_0+B_* < A_s for odd s>=9. The full value-plus-normal functional costs only a polynomial, and the fixed subset count2^s is harmless. The all-core term outside a fixed cusp corridor has its separately proved strict gap. This proves the SAME entire-color-cube source gap as the old global theorem at EVERY odd s>=9. All subsequent analytic inputs were already proved for every fixed odd s>=5: the exact even complex high-window packet, whole filling Fourier endpoint/current bounds, nonzero unit-charge sum, original normalization, and the actual geometric filling construction. Thus they transfer unchanged once their long-slope threshold is increased as necessary. The original full volume equality consequently extends to every fixed odd s>=9 with all independently sufficiently long fixed signed slopes. No width or slope is allowed to grow with N. For s=5 and7 the present phase-free per-alias margin test remains insufficient; at s=3 the old limiting margin is exactly zero and its local corridor alias estimate was also only proved for s>=5. Those are TWO distinct remaining gates. Extending the theorem there needs a stronger coherent alias/source estimate, not a changed declaration of the existing condition. No fabricated all-width conclusion is inferred from (8). ## 7. Why another constant improvement in this termwise route is insufficient The monic bound used above is exponentially sharp at the actual endpoint z=-2. This identifies exactly which ABSOLUTE-TERM step must be replaced to reach the remaining widths; it is not a claim that the full coherent alias P_h has this rate or that the whole source fails to cancel. For l=floor(N/2)-1 one has log|p_l(-2)|=N B_*+O(1). (13) Here is a direct uniform proof. Use tau=l/N and epsilon=1/N in the literal companion (2), and write it as T_epsilon(tau). Its leading eigenvalues lambda(tau),sigma(tau) can be chosen smoothly on the WHOLE closed interval[0,1/2], with lambda(0)=-4, sigma(0)=0, |lambda(tau)|=rho(pi tau)>=4, |sigma(tau)|<=|lambda(tau)|, |lambda(tau)-sigma(tau)|>=4. (14) The last inequality follows from the explicit discriminant in section2. There is no equality of the two eigenvalue moduli in the open interval: for u>0 and u<pi/2 the normalized d_(-2) has nonzero imaginary part, whereas two roots of equal modulus and positive real product would have real sum. Their moduli meet only at the terminal endpoint, where their eigenvalues remain distinct. Thus the branch starting at -4 is the dominant branch throughout; no hidden exchange of expanding channels is used. Take the uniformly invertible eigenframe S(tau)=[[lambda,sigma],[1,1]]. Taylor expansion of the explicit smooth companion gives S(tau+epsilon)^(-1)T_epsilon(tau)S(tau) =diag(lambda,sigma)+epsilon A(tau)+O(epsilon^2), with all coefficients and two derivatives uniformly bounded. An explicit bounded off-diagonal matrix X, determined by X_ij=-A_ij/(D_i-D_j), makes the near-identity change I+epsilon X diagonal through first order. The resulting matrix is diag(lambda+epsilon A_11,sigma+epsilon A_22)+O(epsilon^2). Divide each step by d_1=lambda+epsilon A_11. Its normalized form is diag(1,r_tau)+O(epsilon^2), with |r_tau|<=1+Cepsilon. All normalized products therefore have uniformly bounded norm. The original initial vector (p_0,p_(-1))=(1,0) has first eigen-coordinate -1/4+O(epsilon). At the first step the second coordinate is O(epsilon), because sigma(0)=0. Over at most N/2 steps the O(epsilon^2) residual changes the first coordinate by O(epsilon), and keeps the second O(epsilon). The first physical coordinate consequently has a uniformly nonzero bounded prefactor times product d_1. Finally log|product d_1|=sum_j log rho(pi j/N)+O(1) =N I(l/N)+O(1). This proves (13), including the endpoint of equal moduli without an inverse eigenvalue-modulus gap. The proof applies equally to bar p_l. Now choose the ACTUAL h=floor(N/2) and the top term l=h-1 in (1). Its Gaussian coefficient is EXACTLY [2h-1 choose 2h-1]_Q=1, and its other displayed coefficient is a unit phase. Therefore any termwise-absolute estimate of the expansion (1) has rate at least B_* already from this single EXACT monic term. Since g_7 and g_5 are both smaller than B_*, this specific route cannot remove those widths by a sharper frozen-radius constant or a better estimate of that term. That comparison can also be certified without a numerical limiting fit: rho>=4 everywhere and rho>=5 on[pi/6,pi/3]. The latter follows from its displayed unimodal (1+sin theta+cos theta)^2 expression and the two explicit endpoint values, both greater than5. Hence B_* >= (log5)/6+(log4)/3 > .73. On the other hand sec v>=1 in (10) gives g_s<=j_0-pi/s. The elementary bounds G<11/12 and pi>157/50 give j_0<1.17, so g_5,g_7<1.17-157/350<.73. The finite interval audit checks the two endpoint and logarithmic comparisons with outward rounding. This is an obstruction to the STATED ABSOLUTE-TERM METHOD, not to the actual source. A further improvement must combine the P_h terms coherently, or pair the complete alias with the other boxes and the original Phi_2 functional before estimating. The exact Frobenius/ circle-source pairing under investigation is eligible for that task; deleting the alias or a normal jet is not. ## 8. Parity of the number of boxes: the even-width link statement The same proof applies to every fixed INTEGER s>=9, if even widths are stated as LINKS rather than knots. This is a source/parity audit, not an inference that a link is a knot. The exact unwrapped-degree and Phi_2 product identities use the original cups, ordinary caps and ONE marked cap and hold for any integer box count. The only use of oddness in their topological conclusion is the component count: following the main strand advances its box label by2 modulo s. Thus there are gcd(s,2) main components. With all crossing circles present the augmented diagram has s+gcd(s,2) components; after their prescribed fillings it has gcd(s,2) main components. In particular an even s gives a two-component pretzel link. The analytic checks are likewise independent of oddness of s: * The complete polynomial is the SAME z_N and the source is the SAME full-Hermite Phi_2(z_N^s). The coherent inner bounds have no s in them. The enclosing-circle saddle has s j'(eta_s)=1 and alpha=pi/s in(0,pi/2) for every integer s>2. Its two Gaussian constants are nonzero and the higher winding bound is unchanged. * The mixed packet remains exactly even in EACH color. The complex saddle Hessian and the real color curvature are nonzero for s>2. Local source replacement uses a strictly positive alias margin; (12) supplies it for all integer s>=9. * The exact filling formula is applied once per port. Under every unit charge reflection both m_i and its sinh factor change sign. Its level character is (-1)^((s+sum_i m_i)(N-1))=1, because sum_i m_i is congruent to s modulo2. This conclusion does not require s odd. All endpoint/tail estimates depend on the fixed number of ports and continue verbatim. The original LINK normalization is already proved in [the complete source-normalization theorem](actual_complete_augmented_source_normalization.md), section3: a cut partial trace is a scalar Hopf endomorphism of the remaining simple V_N regardless of connectivity. Thus the same single-cut reduced Kashaev link value has the modulus of the raw source. Its enhancement sign is (-1)^((N-1)(c-1)) with the ACTUAL component count c. There is still only one modified dimension if that optional convention is used, not one per main component. The literal port matrices, reversed-cap ordering, shaded/white face geometry, and primitive auxiliary filling equations also do not use oddness. For even width the two main-component meridians remain noncentral parabolic. The general geometric completion theorem keeps BOTH unfilled cusps complete; it does not collapse them to one. Consequently, with the same sufficiently long independently signed fixed twists, the source and volume equality extend to the original single-cut reduced two-component pretzel LINK for every fixed even s>=10. The knot conclusion is the odd s>=9 part. No assertion for a normalization that modifies every component independently is made. The even widths4,6,8, like the odd widths3,5,7, are not supplied by the present full-color gap. The audit includes literal even-width full marked sources against the unwrapped transfer and exact rotated Phi_2 product; numerical checks supplement the parity-independent derivations above.

Their integral is \(O(\log N/N)\), while a sample exceptionally close to the zero can only improve the upper bound. On the other cells, \(\lvert f'(t)vert\le C/\operatorname{dist}(t,a+\mathbb Z)\) gives an accumulated harmonic-sum error \(O(\log N)\). No sampled vanishing factor has been divided out. For the lower bound in (7), choose a point within \(O(1/N)\) of a maximizing \(\delta\) on the lattice $$ \delta_N\in  egin{cases} N^{-1}\mathbb Z,&N\ 	ext{even},\ N^{-1}(\mathbb Z+	frac12),&N\ 	ext{odd}, \end{cases} \qquad0\le\delta_N\le	frac12.	ag{8} $$ At these points \(\chi_N(\sigma)=4\), and every sampled cosine stays at least half a mesh step from its zero. Thus the two-sided estimate applies to all unused intervals. The modulus of continuity of each logarithmic integral under an \(O(1/N)\) shift is \(O(\log N/N)\), uniformly in the interval. This proves (7), including its endpoint cases. Nonempty monomer products start at \(r\ge1\), so their lower endpoint uses the same elementary sine estimate. At even levels (2) is the product (1) at \(\delta=0\). At odd levels LEFT skips the unique central zero row. The derivative in (2) removes exactly that factor; its \(N^{-2}\) scalar and the single removed mesh factor have only \(O(\log N)\) logarithmic cost. Hence, uniformly, $$  rac1N\log p_N(v) =2\int_\mu^

u<1/2\), differentiation of (6), or of its explicit logarithmic primitive, gives $$ \partial_\delta K =\log\left|  rac{\cos(\pi(\mu+\delta))\cos(\pi(
u-\delta))} {\cos(\pi(

u\), \(w=

The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_protected_outer_spectral_energy.py), with [results](../experiments/actual_protected_outer_spectral_energy_results.json), builds the physical coproduct Casimir and extracts coefficients by the original three-clock inverse DFT. title: Actual complementary heads and the outgoing large-clock packet
status: Exact generic complemented heads and the outgoing boundary determinant
text: # Actual complementary heads and the outgoing large-clock packet 30 October 2026. Two exact source identities extend the proved boundary packets. Generic Chevalley complementation transports the retained 0F1 normals to the small second-clock regime. A separate positive-matrix comparison controls the outgoing large-second-clock numerator at the root, through the fold. The original scalar factors and large partner remain explicit. This does not yet assemble every cup factor or select a global period. ## 1. An exact generic reciprocity, before any root collision Let H=H_m^B(U,V) be the actual generic white polynomial, and put A0=Q^d=(BQ)^(-1), d=N-1 fixed. Then H(A0/V,A0/U)=A0^m(UV)^(-m)H(U,V). (1) Here U=Q^x,V=Q^y use their marked logarithms, and the complementary heads are EXACTLY d-y,d-x. In particular d does not move with the quantum period, and (1) may be genuinely differentiated. There is a direct independent-variable proof from the actual [white Ward equations](actual_augmented_plat_framing_density_source_ward.md). Set Htilde=(UV/A0)^m H(A0/V,A0/U). It is polynomial of degree at most m in each variable. Substituting X=A0/V,Y=A0/U shows that the E equation for H becomes the F equation for Htilde, and the F equation becomes its E equation, with the original coefficients. For example multiply the E equation at X,Y by UV/A0^2; it reads U(1-V)H(QX,Y)+(1-U)H(X,QY)=(Q^m-UV)H(X,Y), which is precisely the transformed F equation. These two equations determine the polynomial up to one scalar. To see this without a finite-grid continuation assumption, expand in the Newton basis P_b(U)=product_(r<b)(U-Q^r). After removing the first b basis terms, evaluate the F equation at U=Q^b. The coefficient h_b(V) must satisfy Q^b(1-V)h_b(V/Q)=(1-VQ^(b-m))h_b(V). Among polynomials of degree at most m its solutions are exactly the multiples of V^b P_(m-b)(V), as follows by coefficient comparison, starting at its lowest power. Induction gives the actual Newton basis used in the source. The E equation then fixes its adjacent coefficients by the original generic ratio. This is a rational-function proof for generic Q,B; specialization follows after clearing denominators. Finally H(0,0)=(-1)^m Q^[m(m-1)/2]. The coefficient of U^mV^m in Htilde is A0^(-m)H(0,0)=(-B)^m Q^[m(m+1)/2], exactly the top coefficient of H. This proves (1) with scalar ONE, and in particular retains the actual Chevalley normalization. ## 2. The genuine small-second-clock packet Suppose at the root U_N is in a fixed compact subset of C*, V_N=N^(-2)v_N with v_N in such a compact, and the fixed marked heads have size O(N log N). Retain t=N^2 epsilon and all moving quantities from the [generic resonant hard-edge theorem](actual_q_hahn_generic_resonant_hard_edge.md). The transformed clocks U'=A0/V,V'=A0/U satisfy its hypotheses. At t=0 define kappa'_N=A0(0)/v_N, V'_N=A0(0)/U_N, K'_N=sin^2(pi m/N)(V'_N-1)/(pi^2 kappa'_N V'_N). Equation (1) transports the exact normalization as well: Z_low(t)=c_m(t)A0(t)^m product_(r<m)(1-Q(t)^r V(t)/A0(t)) =(-1)^m Q(t)^[m(m-1)/2] product_(r<m)(1-B(t)Q(t)^(r+1)V(t)). (2) Thus, uniformly on each fixed |t|<=rho<pi, H_m^B(U,V)/Z_low(t) =0F1(;1-t/(pi i);-K'_N)+O((1+log N)/N). (3) All fixed scaled genuine quantum jets have the same convergence. The transformed heads d-y,d-x are fixed as epsilon varies; neither the A0 derivative nor the marked character is suppressed. Equation (2) notably cancels the B powers in c_m A0^m exactly. The estimate remains absolute across zeros of the limiting function. ## 3. A uniform comparison of the two actual positive matrices At the ROOT let a<=floor((N-1)/2), theta=pi/N, and use the actual Hermitian matrices H_+,H_- from the [full physical determinant theorem](actual_q_hahn_full_physical_complex_packet.md). Their diagonal is d_n=1/[cos(n theta)cos((n+1)theta)], and their adjacent upper entries are sqrt(B_n)[sin(n theta)+/-i cos(n theta)], B_n=sin^2(n theta)/[cos^2(n theta) sin((2n-1)theta)sin((2n+1)theta)]. They satisfy, uniformly in N,a including the maximal folded a, H_+ <= 2H_-+8I, H_- <= 2H_++8I. (4) Here the inequalities are Hermitian quadratic-form inequalities. The proof retains their exact endpoint coefficients. Both matrices have the same Cholesky pivots as the positive D matrix, namely p_(n-1)=sin(n theta)/[cos(n theta)sin((2n-1)theta)]. Write their quadratic forms as sums of squared adjacent Cholesky terms and the final positive pivot. Flipping an offdiagonal phase changes its term by 2i sqrt(B_n)cos(n theta)/p_(n-1) times the next coordinate. The inequality |x+y|^2<=2|x|^2+2|y|^2 gives an additional diagonal cost 8 B_n cos^2(n theta)/p_(n-1) =4sin(2n theta)/sin((2n+1)theta)<=8. Indeed sin(2n theta)=2cos(theta)sin((2n+1)theta) -sin((2n+2)theta), and the last sine is nonnegative for every actual offdiagonal n<=a-1. This proves the first inequality in (4), and complex conjugation proves the second. No lower eigenvalue estimate or inverse channel norm is introduced. ## 4. The actual root numerator when the second clock is large Put K_a=[2a choose a]_Q. The exact source determinant, with its retained scalar, gives H_a^1(U,V)/V^a =K_a det[I-(qU/2)H_--(q^-1/(2V))H_+]. (5) For example derive this from R_a(z;-cos gamma) =det[zI-(e^(i gamma)H_-+e^(-i gamma)H_+)/2], with z=q^t/U, e^(i gamma)=q q^t and (q^t)^2=UV, before canceling the displayed powers. This proves (5) as a polynomial identity and does not make a square-root choice in its final formula. Let qU range in a fixed compact subset of Re z<0, and let V=N^2 kappa_N with kappa_N in a fixed compact subset of C*. Set M0=I-(qU/2)H_-. Then H_a^1(U,V)=V^a K_a det(M0)[1+O(N^-1)]. (6) This is a UNIFORM RELATIVE estimate, including folded a. To prove it put D0=I+(eta/2)H_-, where -Re(qU)>=eta>0. The conjugated M0 has inverse norm at most one, while (4) bounds D0^(-1/2)H_+D0^(-1/2) uniformly. Thus the relative perturbation from the last term in (5) has norm O(N^-2). Expanding Log det costs at most a O(N^-2)=O(N^-1). This also proves nonvanishing and a marked relative logarithm on the stated domain. At qU negative real, det M0 is strictly positive. K_a and V^a retain their original phases. For the actual LARGE root channel m=d-a, the exact root partner identity supplies H_m^1(U,V)=H_a^1(U,V) product_(r=a)^(m-1)(UV-Q^r). Consequently its corresponding packet is H_m^1(U,V)=V^m U^(m-a) K_a det(M0)[1+O(N^-1)]. (7) The added product differs from (UV)^(m-a) by 1+O(N^-1). This is explicitly a ROOT identity: it is not differentiated as a generic large/small collision. Generic normals in this second large-clock regime remain separate from (6),(7). ## 5. The genuine paired 200/220 circle There is an exact geometric use of the negative ray in (6). Take the root theorem's 200 box with B=-J, J=[[1,1],[0,1]], and write A=[[a,-(a+1)^2/4],[4,-2-a]], P=BA, C=I+b(P+I), Aout=C^-1 A C, Q1=e[[1,z],[0,1]], W=A^-1Q1, e=+/-1. Direct multiplication, with the ACTUAL inverse collar transport, gives W_21=-4e, (Aout W)_21=16e b^2, U_geom,out=-W_21/(Aout W)_21=1/(4b^2). (8) Here C names the auxiliary collar, so its inverse gives the displayed transport. Conventions naming the transport itself C write C A C^-1 instead. The lower-left entry and ratio in (8) are unchanged under b->-b, so this squared-ray certificate is identical in those two notations; it does not change any primitive peripheral mark. The [marked complete rectangle collar](actual_matching_edge_geometric_target_polynomial.md) has b=-i/(2c), c>0, including its retained half-twist convention. Thus U_geom,out=-c^2. The physical half-index argument is U=q^-1 U_geom,out up to the retained finite-r correction, so qU approaches precisely this negative ray. Formula (7) therefore gives the nonzero outgoing 220 numerator paired with the incoming 200 Bessel packet. No independent phase of U has been chosen. The actual white monomial, F_m denominator, categorical dual, channel cup, physical caps and exterior source scalar still have to be retained when assembling the full box. Their exact lifts and logarithmic-escape estimates remain available; they are not set equal to one by (8). Other prefix patterns, original boundary currents and the global relative-cycle coefficient are not resolved by this local paired-numerator statement. Focused audit: [original generic reciprocity and complementary packets](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_complementary_hard_edge.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_q_hahn_complementary_hard_edge_results.json). It checks 126 original generic reciprocity four-jets, retaining 504 coefficients; three exact paired-circle matrix identities; 17 folded positive-matrix comparisons and 173 pivot evaluations; 21 small and 21 large original-source determinant identities; and eight each of root220 relative-rate, generic002 packet and genuine002 first/second normal diagnostics. These finite checks supplement the proofs and do not prove their uniform asymptotic estimates. The result gives exact reciprocity, genuine 002 normals and a root 220 numerator packet. It supplies neither generic 220 normals, a completed boundary-circle packet nor a global period coefficient.

title: Exact coefficient duality for the original complete-channel polynomial
text: # Exact coefficient duality for the original complete-channel polynomial 30 October 2026. The positive coefficients of the actual magnetic polynomial are log-concave. Consequently a positive-radius evaluation recovers each coefficient within a factor at most j+1. The selected ordinary source action then gives a uniform coefficient rate, with an explicit optimal radius, throughout the interior coefficient-slope domain. This theorem keeps the source's physical total and integer channel. It neither deletes the Fourier phases when coefficients are sewn nor proves cancellation control for the original graph contraction. ## 1. The original polynomial and its positive coefficients Put d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, and retain the ACTUAL complete range 0<=j<=floor(d/2), d-j<=t<=d. The proved magnetic factorization is fhat(u)=q^(du) Q^(-ju) G_t(Q^u), G_t(q^t z)=c_t P_(N,t,j)(z), c_t=q^[j(t+j-d)]/(Q;Q)_j, P(z)=B_h(z) A_n(z)=sum_(k=0)^j p_k z^k, h=d-t, n=t+j-d, h+n=j. (1) Here B_h has the positive coefficients beta(h,k)=s_h/(s_k s_(h-k)), where s_r=product_(a=1)^r 2sin(pi a/N). The actual residual A_n has positive leading coefficient and n negative real roots. These are properties of the original coproduct polynomial, proved in [the magnetic corridor theorem](actual_q_hahn_magnetic_complex_corridor.md), not a replacement of its values by an interpolating polynomial. In particular p_k>0 for every 0<=k<=j. The source condition t+j>=d is essential here. Although its ordinary analytic continuation has a larger domain, positivity of this factorization is not asserted for arbitrary nonphysical t or for limiting tau+xi<1. ## 2. Log-concavity and an exact polynomial-loss duality The coefficient sequence p_0,...,p_j is log-concave: p_k^2>=p_(k-1)p_(k+1), 1<=k<j. (2) An elementary proof is enough. The consecutive ratio of B_h is beta(h,k)/beta(h,k-1) =sin((h-k+1)pi/N)/sin(k pi/N). Its decrease follows by cross multiplication: the difference of the two adjacent numerators is sin(pi/N)sin((h+1)pi/N)>0. The h=0 sequence consists of one coefficient and is included. Now let a_k be any nonnegative log-concave sequence with interval support, extended by zero elsewhere. Multiplication of its polynomial by z+rho, rho>0, gives b_k=rho a_k+a_(k-1), and b_k^2-b_(k-1)b_(k+1) =rho^2(a_k^2-a_(k-1)a_(k+1)) +rho(a_k a_(k-1)-a_(k-2)a_(k+1)) +(a_(k-1)^2-a_(k-2)a_k)>=0. (3) The middle term is nonnegative by the decreasing consecutive ratios; zero endpoints cause no problem. Factoring A_n into its positive linear factors and iterating (3) proves (2). For EVERY k=0,...,j the exact finite statement is p_k <= inf_(w>0) P(w) w^(-k) <= (j+1)p_k. (4) The first inequality holds because p_k w^k is one positive summand. For an interior k choose p_(k-1)/p_k <= w <= p_k/p_(k+1). This interval is nonempty by (2). At such a tilt, the kth term is a mode of the entire sequence p_l w^l, again by decreasing ratios. Its sum is at most j+1 times that term, proving the upper inequality. For k=0 and k=j, take w to zero and infinity respectively; the infimum equals the endpoint coefficient. For j=0 all statements are identities. Thus (4) is a two-sided estimate for actual coefficients, with no unknown exponentially small cancellation or probability prefactor. It is not an asymptotic Gaussian coefficient formula. ## 3. The correct radial free energy and its explicit derivative Set tau=t/N, xi=j/N and w=exp(y), y real. Because the polynomial coordinate in (1) is z=Q^u/q^t, the corresponding magnetic variable is nu=u/N=tau/2-i y/(2pi). (5) The reciprocal determinant coordinate is 1/w, not w. Taking absolute values in the EXACT source normalization (1) gives log P(exp y)=log s_j-(d-2j)y/2+log|fhat(N nu)|. (6) Use the actual selected action Phi_xi from [the full physical packet](actual_q_hahn_full_physical_complex_packet.md). For complete physical indices with tau in a fixed compact subinterval of (1/2,1), xi bounded away from zero, and y in a fixed finite interval, N^(-1)log P(exp y)=F(tau,xi;y)+O(log N/N), F=J(xi)-(1/2-xi)y +Re Phi_xi(tau,tau/2-i y/(2pi)). (7) The scaled parameters in (7) are their ACTUAL values at level N. The possible complete boundary displacement tau+xi=1-1/N is retained; its limiting parameters satisfy tau+xi>=1. The packet and the factorial estimate are uniform for these indices. The derivative in y of the error in (7) is O(1/N) on smaller compact intervals. The log s_j term is independent of y and has not been dropped. There is an explicit derivative requiring no new saddle selection. Put c=-cos(pi tau)>0, C=cos(pi xi), s=sin(pi xi)>0, B=w^2+2cw+C^2. On (5) the selected multiplier is Y=exp(Phi_nu)=(s+i sqrt(B))^2/(1+2cw+w^2), Arg Y=2 arctan(sqrt(B)/s) in (0,pi). (8) It has modulus one, and the square root is positive real. This is the already calibrated ordinary branch on this central vertical line. Differentiating (7), with its MINUS sign in (5), yields F_y=xi-1/2+pi^(-1) arctan(sqrt(B)/s), F_yy=s w(w+c)/[pi sqrt(B)(1+2cw+w^2)]>0. (9) As y tends to minus or plus infinity, F_y tends respectively to 0 and xi, including the folded endpoint C=0. Every interior slope 0<lambda<xi therefore has a unique finite optimal tilt. It is explicitly a=pi(1/2-xi+lambda), w_*=sqrt(c^2-C^2+s^2 tan(a)^2)-c>0, y_*=log w_*. (10) The quantity s tan(a) is strictly greater than C for lambda>0, which proves positivity of this root. Formula (10) also gives uniform finite tilt bounds on compact interior slope families. Equivalently, the selected magnetic momentum at that coefficient is Y_*=exp[2pi i(lambda+1/2-xi)], Log Y_*=2pi i(lambda+1/2-xi) in i(0,pi). (10a) Thus the Fourier index prescribes the FULL local phase on this selected radial saddle, not only the modulus of a multiplier. Its radial boundary variable is the positive root (10), equivalently w_*^2+2cw_*+C^2=s^2 tan^2(pi(1/2-xi+lambda)). Actual network orientation and incidence are still needed to combine these local characters into global equations. ## 4. Uniform actual coefficient rates Take any compact family of limiting complete parameters with 1/2<tau<1, 0<xi<=1/2 and tau+xi>=1. Keep the coefficient slope lambda strictly inside (0,xi), uniformly on that family. For all legal integer sequences N,t,j,k approaching this family, use the actual scaled values tau_N=t/N, xi_N=j/N, lambda_N=k/N. Define L(tau,xi,lambda) =F(tau,xi;y_*)-lambda y_*, (11) where (10) fixes the unique positive tilt. Then log p_k=N L(tau_N,xi_N,lambda_N)+O(log N), (12) uniformly over that family and both level parities. The value in (11) is also the infimum over all real y of F-lambda y. Its slope derivatives obey L_lambda=-y_*, L_(lambda lambda)=-1/F_yy(y_*)<0. (13) For completeness, no unbounded minimizer is hidden in (12). The finite function F_N(y)=N^(-1)log P(exp y) is convex, and its derivative is the tilted mean of k/N. Choose fixed endpoints y_-<y_+ beyond the compact set of optimal tilts (10). By (9) there is a uniform strict gap between F_y(y_-) and the target slopes, and between those slopes and F_y(y_+). The derivative convergence in (7) puts every finite minimizer of F_N-lambda_N y in [y_-,y_+] for large N. The uniform value estimate (7), followed by (4), proves (12). Boundary slopes k/N approaching zero or xi, unbounded tilts, and physical degree endpoints tau=1/2 or tau=1 are outside this uniform statement. Their exact finite inequality (4) remains valid; a rate or relative amplitude at those boundaries needs its own estimates. No relative coefficient amplitude is claimed even in the interior. ## 5. What this supplies for a sewn source Each original coefficient has now an actual positive radial variational description, retaining its normalizer and its Fourier index. This permits the index k to remain a shared variable in an exact affine wire/cycle compiler. If a positive comparison partition is assembled from these coefficients, their actions must first be summed on that shared incidence set before taking any maximum. The original magnetic source is reconstructed with its displayed Fourier factors and scalar c_t. A positive coefficient theorem does not erase those phases, identify a graph contraction with the product of coefficient envelopes, or prove a nonzero geometric overlap. Those are separate requirements for the full volume conjecture. Focused audit: [original positive coefficients and radial duality](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_fourier_coefficient_variational.py). Three formal identities check the log-concavity step, curvature and inverse tilt. At 90 digits, 794 actual positive polynomials satisfy 3,938 log-concavity and tilted-mode checks; nine literal off-lattice source values check the radial sign and normalization. Eighteen interior coefficient sequences check the stated rate and tilt gradient. The uniform theorem is proved above, not inferred from those sequences. The variational theorem concerns discrete channels and interior slopes. Positive coefficients are distinct from a coherently sewn graph source.

title: The actual ordinary packet on the full strict physical tube
status: Selected full physical complex amplitude; finite correction
text: # The actual ordinary packet on the full strict physical tube 30 October 2026. A second exact Hermitian realization of the original q-Hahn determinant puts its zeros in a sharp angular cone. It extends the ordinary joint action and nonzero relative amplitude from the central wedge to the FULL strict physical tube. Both magnetic coordinates vary complexly; the channel remains an actual integer. The finite source has a small upper-boundary correction, which is necessary: an explicit one-channel counterexample is given below. Every fixed compact in the full physical tube is covered for all sufficiently large N. No contributing global cycle or coherent whole-source estimate is asserted. ## 1. Exact source and a second determinant Put theta=pi/N, q=exp(i theta), Q=q^2, d=N-1 and 1<=j<=floor(d/2). Write t=N tau, u=N nu, xi=j/N, z=exp[pi i(tau-2nu)], gamma=pi(tau+1/N). The original joint source is exactly fhat_j(u,t-u)=x^u q^(jt) [2j choose j]_Q R_j(z;-cos gamma)/Delta_j(Q^t), x=q^d, Delta_j(T)=product_(r=0)^(j-1)(T-Q^r). (1) All powers and scalar factors are those of [the original joint amplitude theorem](actual_q_hahn_joint_complex_amplitude.md). Let b_n=sin^2(n theta)/[cos^2(n theta) sin((2n-1)theta)sin((2n+1)theta)]. The exact monic recurrence is R_0=1, R_1=z+c/cos(theta), R_(n+1)=[z+c/(cos(n theta)cos((n+1)theta))]R_n +b_n[cos^2(n theta)-c^2]R_(n-1). (2) Define j-by-j real matrices A and K, indexed by 0,...,j-1: A_(n,n)=1/[cos(n theta)cos((n+1)theta)], A_(n-1,n)=A_(n,n-1)=sqrt(b_n)sin(n theta), K_(n-1,n)=sqrt(b_n)cos(n theta), K_(n,n-1)=-sqrt(b_n)cos(n theta), K_(n,n)=0. Then the SAME polynomial has the second exact determinant R_j(z;-cos gamma)=det[zI-cos(gamma)A-sin(gamma)K]. (3) Indeed the upper and lower adjacent entries of J_gamma=cos(gamma)A+sin(gamma)K are sqrt(b_n)sin(n theta+gamma) and sqrt(b_n)sin(n theta-gamma). Their product is b_n[cos^2(gamma)-cos^2(n theta)], so the continuant of zI-J_gamma is exactly (2). The two Hermitian matrices H_+=A+iK, H_-=A-iK (4) are POSITIVE DEFINITE. Their adjacent entries have modulus sqrt(b_n) and their diagonal equals that of the proved positive matrix D in [the first determinant theorem](actual_q_hahn_joint_accretive_determinant.md). A diagonal unitary phase gauge makes each of these tridiagonal offdiagonals positive real. Thus each H_+ and H_- is unitarily equivalent to D, including the maximal channel. Consequently J_gamma=(e^(i gamma)H_-+e^(-i gamma)H_+)/2. (5) This is a source-exact matrix identity, not an asymptotic model. ## 2. A sharp finite angular exclusion, and its necessary correction For any eigenvector v of J_gamma with norm one, its eigenvalue is zeta=(h_-/2)e^(i gamma)+(h_+/2)e^(-i gamma), h_-=v*H_-v>0, h_+=v*H_+v>0. (6) If pi/2<Re gamma<3pi/2, these two rays bound a left angular cone. Put a_gamma=min(Re gamma,2pi-Re gamma). Every nonzero eigenvalue satisfies |Arg zeta|>=a_gamma; the inequality is strict when the two boundary rays are distinct. When Re gamma=pi all eigenvalues are strictly negative real. Positive coefficients in (6) also exclude a zero eigenvalue in this range. Define the full physical tube P={ (tau,nu) in C^2: 1/2<Re tau<1, 0<Re nu<Re tau }, and its finite-level subdomain P_N={ (tau,nu) in P: Re tau<1-1/(2N) }. (7) For a physical point the principal argument of z in (1) is exactly pi(Re tau-2Re nu), with absolute value <pi Re tau. On P_N, a_gamma>pi Re tau. Therefore (3) is nonzero there. The factors Delta_j(Q^t) are also nonzero: their zeros require tau=r/N modulo an integer, 0<=r<j<N/2. All remaining factors in (1) are nonzero. Thus the original finite source is holomorphic and nowhere zero on P_N. The case j=0 is its explicit nonzero exponential. The correction in (7) cannot simply be deleted for every finite N. Already j=1 has its zero at z_N=cos[pi(tau+1/N)]/cos(pi/N). Take tau_N=1-1/(4N)+i and delta=3pi/(4N). Then z_N=[-cos(delta)cosh(pi)+i sin(delta)sinh(pi)]/cos(pi/N), Arg z_N=pi-arctan[tan(delta)tanh(pi)] <pi Re tau_N. (8) For the strict inequality, set a=pi/(4N): tan(a)/tan(3a)<1/3<tanh(pi), valid for N>=3. Define nu_N=[tau_N-Log(z_N)/(pi i)]/2 with the principal logarithm. It satisfies 0<Re nu_N<Re tau_N, but (1) vanishes. The denominator is nonzero. This is an exact finite-source counterexample on P. These points approach the boundary of P as N grows and therefore do not obstruct the fixed-compact theorem below. ## 3. Uniform inverse and logarithmic bounds on full physical compacts Fix a compact K0 contained in P. For all large N, K0 lies in P_N and gamma has real part between pi/2 and pi. Put M=zI-(e^(i gamma)H_-+e^(-i gamma)H_+)/2. The three coefficients z, -e^(i gamma), -e^(-i gamma) lie in one open half-plane through zero. To see this, write a=Re gamma and psi=Arg z. The latter satisfies |psi|<a. The other two arguments are pi-a and -(pi-a). Their angular span together with psi is strictly less than pi. On a fixed physical compact the span stays uniformly below pi, because Re nu and Re(tau-nu) are bounded below and Re tau stays away from 1/2 and 1. Their moduli also have positive lower and finite upper bounds on K0. Rotate the half-plane by a phase beta. Locally, and uniformly on a finite cover of K0, this gives Re(e^(-i beta)M)>=delta I+eta_- H_-+eta_+ H_+, delta,eta_-,eta_+>=c_(K0)>0. (9) Hence ||M^(-1)||<=C_(K0). Conjugating M by H_+^(-1/2), or by H_-^(-1/2), also gives |tr(M^(-1)H_+)|+|tr(M^(-1)H_-)|<=C_(K0)j. Since partial_z M=I and partial_gamma M=-(i/2)e^(i gamma)H_-+(i/2)e^(-i gamma)H_+, both logarithmic derivatives of R_j with respect to z and gamma are O_(K0)(j). No lower eigenvalue bound for D, H_+ or H_- is used. The result is uniform through the folded channel. The scalar factors in (1) have the same explicit O(N) logarithmic derivative bounds as before. Thus the first derivatives of N^(-1)Log fhat_j are uniformly bounded on full physical compacts. Choose its scalar holomorphic logarithm on the convex P_N by continuation from its already fixed central value. The exact real center phase remains Im Log fhat_j(t/2,t/2)=pi[d(t-j)+j^2]/(2N). (10) The principal matrix logarithm of the old central realization is not being asserted outside its domain. A central anchor bounds the continued normalized scalar logarithm, and Cauchy estimates give all its fixed derivatives on smaller physical compacts. The normal-family argument now extends the ACTUAL selected leading action throughout P. Any subsequential limit agrees on the central open subset with the already proved Phi_xi, and hence everywhere by the holomorphic identity theorem. This gives local uniform convergence with all derivatives, uniformly for xi=j/N in compact real subintervals of (0,1/2], always using its actual value. ## 4. The characteristic is simple on the entire tube Set gamma0=pi tau, s=sin(pi xi), C=cos(pi xi), and W=1-2cos(gamma0)z+C^2 z^2, V=1-2cos(gamma0)z+z^2. (11) Both are nonzero on P. This has a two-dimensional positive-cone proof which includes C=0. Let u=(1,0)^T, v=(s,C)^T and B_gamma0=e^(i gamma0)u u*+e^(-i gamma0)v v*. Its trace is 2cos(gamma0), its determinant is C^2, and det(I-z B_gamma0)=W. Every nonzero eigenvalue is a NONNEGATIVE combination of the same two left-cone rays, with at least one positive coefficient. It therefore lies in the closed cone |Arg lambda|>=pi Re tau. Reciprocation preserves that cone, so its reciprocal cannot be the physical z, whose argument has smaller absolute value. This proves the assertion for W. Taking s=0,C=1 proves it for V. The full source characteristic from the exact Casimir shift is H=A(Y+Y^(-1))+D-(J+J^(-1))=0, A=(U-T)(1-U)/T, D=2U(1+T-U)/T, U=e^(2pi i nu), T=e^(2pi i tau), J=e^(2pi i xi). Here A!=0 on P, and xi is bounded away from zero. Its two solutions are Y_+=(s z+i sqrt(W))^2/V, Y_-=(s z-i sqrt(W))^2/V.
