The proof uses the finite determinant, matrix traces and elementary sums, not a saddle selection assumption. These are numerator results. Scalar phases, partner products and all source normalization remain explicit. No genuine generic quantum derivative, full source cycle, or volume equality follows. ## 1. The literal source and its negative raw clocks Put N>=2, d=N-1, theta=pi/N, q=exp(i theta), Q=q^2 and 0<=a<=floor(d/2). Let H_a^1(U,V) be the root white polynomial in the [resonant boundary theorem](actual_q_hahn_resonant_hard_edge.md). Its exact determinant, proved in the [complementary boundary theorem](actual_q_hahn_complementary_hard_edge.md), is H_a^1(U,V)=V^a K_a det[I-(qU/2)H_--(q^-1/(2V))H_+], K_a=[2a choose a]_Q. (1) The empty determinant for a=0 is one. The Hermitian positive definite matrices H_-,H_+ have common diagonal d_n=1/[cos(n theta)cos((n+1)theta)], 0<=n<a, and upper adjacent entries sqrt(B_n)[sin(n theta) -/+ i cos(n theta)], 1<=n<a, B_n=sin^2(n theta)/[cos^2(n theta) sin((2n-1)theta)sin((2n+1)theta)]. (2) Their positivity follows from the original exact Cholesky pivots; it holds at both level parities and through the folded endpoint. Use the ACTUAL half-index arguments U=q^-1 X, V=q^-1 Y, X<0, Y<0, alpha=-X/2>0, beta=-1/(2Y)>0. Then the matrix in (1) is EXACTLY M=I+alpha H_-+beta H_+ > I. (3) In particular its determinant is positive, while V^a and K_a retain their original phases. This statement concerns the raw clocks X,Y, not an independently rotated pair of physical heads. The original 222 geometry supplies precisely these limiting signs. The exact finite-r arguments differ from their limits, and are handled next; they are not silently set equal to their limits. ## 2. Uniform relative transport, with its first correction retained Change the coefficients in (3) to alpha(1+e_-), beta(1+e_+), allowing complex e_-,e_+. Set eta=|e_-|+|e_+|<1 and E=M^(-1/2)[alpha e_- H_-+beta e_+ H_+]M^(-1/2). Both alpha M^(-1/2)H_- M^(-1/2) and beta M^(-1/2)H_+ M^(-1/2) are positive semidefinite, and their sum is I-M^-1<I. Hence ||E||<=eta, with no dependence on N,a, or a small eigenvalue of an individual H matrix. The marked logarithm, zero when e_-=e_+=0, therefore satisfies Log(det(M+Delta M)/det M)=tr E+R, |R|<=a eta^2/[2(1-eta)], |Log(det(M+Delta M)/det M)|<=-a log(1-eta). (4) Indeed expand tr Log(I+E) in its absolutely convergent matrix power series, use |tr E^j|<=a eta^j, and sum the terms j>=2. This also proves nonvanishing and specifies the relative branch. If X is changed to X(1+u) and Y to Y(1+v), the exact choices are e_-=u, e_+=(1+v)^(-1)-1. (5) Thus O(N^-1) relative clock corrections give det(M+Delta M)/det M=exp(tr E)[1+O(N^-1)]. (6) The trace need not tend to zero: it is an order-one source transport term and must stay. Corrections O(log N/N) have at most O(log N) logarithmic cost, with a nonzero relative factor. The estimates are uniform through the fold. The factors V^a, K_a and all other source factors remain outside this comparison and are kept EXACTLY. These are clock perturbations at one root, not the moving-Q or moving-B generic quantum derivatives. ## 3. The determinant's leading rate Suppose a/N tends to xi in [0,1/2] and alpha,beta tend to positive limits. The convergence below is uniform when alpha,beta stay in compact subsets of the positive reals. For 0<=t<1/2 write c(t)=cos(pi t), D(t)=1+(alpha+beta)/c(t)^2, b(t)^2=[(alpha+beta)^2-4alpha beta c(t)^2]/[4c(t)^4], lambda_+(t)=[D(t) +sqrt(1+[2(alpha+beta)+4alpha beta]/c(t)^2)]/2. The square root here is positive real. Then (1/N)log det M -> I(xi;alpha,beta), I(xi;alpha,beta)=integral_0^xi log lambda_+(t) dt. (7) The endpoint xi=1/2 is included. The improper integral converges because log lambda_+(t)=O(1+|log(1/2-t)|). An a=0 subsequence has empty determinant and rate zero. Here is a proof from the actual finite matrices. The diagonal of M is 1+(alpha+beta)d_n; the squared modulus of its upper entry is B_n[(alpha+beta)^2 sin^2(n theta) +(alpha-beta)^2 cos^2(n theta)]. (8) Away from t=1/2 these converge to D(t), b(t)^2. On each fixed closed interval below 1/2, entries are uniformly bounded. The few initial n, for which the B_n continuum approximation is not uniform, do not affect the Riemann limit: after removing an arbitrarily short initial interval convergence is uniform, while all the removed entries have a common bound. Their contribution to each fixed matrix trace moment is bounded by that interval's length times a constant depending only on the moment. For a fixed integer j, expand tr M^j into closed nearest-neighbor walks of length j. Away from the two ends, each walk sees entries whose variation over j indices tends uniformly to zero. The constant-coefficient walk sum is the zeroth Fourier coefficient of [D(t)+2b(t)cos(phi)]^j; complex offdiagonal phases cancel because a closed walk traverses each edge equally in both directions. Endpoint walks contribute O(j/N) to the normalized trace. Consequently, for every polynomial P and xi<1/2, (1/N)tr P(M) -> integral_0^xi (1/(2pi)) integral_0^(2pi) P(D+2b cos phi) dphi dt. (9) All eigenvalues of M lie in [1,C_xi] by (3) and the bounded row sums. The limiting symbol lies in the same type of interval: D-2b>=1. Approximate log on this interval by truncating log z=log R-sum_(j>=1)(1-z/R)^j/j, R>C_xi. The tail converges uniformly geometrically since z>=1. Its trace error divided by N is bounded by (a/N) times the uniform error. Thus (9) holds for log as well. Finally D+2b cos phi=lambda_+ |1+(b/lambda_+)exp(i phi)|^2, where b/lambda_+<1. Expanding the scalar logarithm in powers of exp(i phi) shows that its second factor has mean logarithm zero. This proves (7) below the fold, without invoking a limiting matrix theorem. To include the fold, cut off the last h<=delta N+O(1) indices. Write M in these two principal blocks. Its Schur complement S on the last block satisfies I<=S<=M_tail: the lower bound follows by minimizing the quadratic form of M>=I over the first block. The upper bound is the explicit positive Schur subtraction. Hence 0<=log det M-log det M_bulk <=log det M_tail<=sum_tail log[1+(alpha+beta)d_n]. (10) The last inequality follows, for example, from its Cholesky pivots being no larger than its diagonal entries. With j_n=N-2n-2>=1 at every allowed diagonal entry, d_n<=C N^2/j_n^2. The j_n have step two. Integral comparison for the sum of log j therefore bounds (10) by C h[1+log(N/max(1,h))]+O(log N). After division by N this tends to zero as delta tends to zero. The same integrable bound handles the tail of (7). This proves the endpoint, including every sequence of actual folded colors. For varying positive parameters, (4) bounds the normalized logarithmic change by C(|Delta log alpha|+|Delta log beta|), uniformly in the channel and N on positive compact sets. Thus the fixed-parameter argument extends uniformly to compactly varying alpha,beta; the integral in (7) has the same continuity by its integrable fold bound. ## 4. The original scalar and large partner Let Lambda(x)=-integral_0^x log|2sin v| dv. The exact magnitude of K_a is s_(2a)/s_a^2, where s_j=product_(r=1)^j 2sin(pi r/N). Elementary Riemann sums, splitting off the integrable endpoint logarithms, give (1/N)log|H_a^1(q^-1X,q^-1Y)| -> xi log|Y|+[2Lambda(pi xi)-Lambda(2pi xi)]/pi +I(xi;alpha,beta). (11) Equation (1), not just (11), retains its complex scalar phase. For the actual large channel m=d-a, keep the exact root identity H_m^1(U,V)=H_a^1(U,V) product_(r=a)^(m-1)(UV-Q^r). (12) For xi bounded away from zero and XY in a positive compact, the product in (12) is uniformly away from its factors' zeros. Its additional logarithmic rate is integral_xi^(1-xi) log|XY-exp(2pi i t)| dt. (13) The finite q^-2 in UV=Q^-1 XY and the exact endpoints stay in (12). At small colors, or under complex perturbations near any forced divisor, use that exact product, not a claimed uniform relative replacement of it. No derivative of (12) is used to assert a generic quantum normal. This is a boundary extension of the earlier strict physical-tube theorem: the canonical raw negative clocks have limiting real total degree one, which lies on that tube's boundary. Unlike the whole rational column, the numerator determinant has no omitted Delta_a(UV) denominator. This note estimates the numerator only. The action in (7) has the original selected normalization. To check this directly, rotate both raw clocks to X_delta=e^(-i delta)X and Y_delta=e^(-i delta)Y, with fixed small delta>0. Their actual heads lie in the earlier strict physical tube for all sufficiently large N. The two determinant coefficients become alpha e^(-i delta) and beta e^(i delta), so (4) bounds the difference of their normalized marked logarithms from the negative-clock value by C delta, uniformly in N and through the fold. The strict-tube theorem gives the original selected action at each fixed delta. Taking N to infinity and then delta to zero identifies its boundary value with (7). The branch is transported by (4) from the positive determinant; at X=Y=-1 this is the old real center, where the determinant is positive, so the two branches agree there. Continuation through the connected negative-clock quadrant retains that equality. The exact factors V^a and K_a are still those of (1). No unrelated solution of the characteristic equation or new additive constant is being selected by the trace-walk calculation. This comparison uses the strict-tube theorem for xi>0. At xi=0, the present small-a/N trace bounds and scalar sums give rate zero; the selected boundary value there follows by continuity, without invoking the earlier fixed-positive-color packet at zero color. It supplies one piece of the original boundary source, not its global cycle coefficient or the full complementary-color gap. Focused audit: [original numerator and determinant checks](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_negative_clock_boundary.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_q_hahn_negative_clock_boundary_results.json). At 90-digit precision it compares 48 literal source numerators, 30 independent dense determinants and 48 large-partner identities. It checks 36 retained trace corrections against the proved remainder bound, six independent dense trace calculations and 42 positive Schur-tail inequalities. The 36 leading-rate diagnostics supplement the written proof; they are not its justification. The conclusion concerns the root numerator. It does not establish generic-$q$ normal data or a global period. The selected boundary calculation retains the original half offsets and the positive branch specified above.

title: Negative roots of the actual complete-channel source polynomial
text: # Negative roots of the actual complete-channel source polynomial 30 October 2026. The finite polynomial inside EVERY physical complete-channel q-Hahn column has only negative nonzero roots. They are simple; its sole possible zero at the origin is the forced support power. This is an all-level theorem for the ACTUAL finite coefficients, not an inference from the stationary quadratic or a sampled real-root plot. In particular the physical Fourier evaluation of that polynomial never vanishes. The proof uses an exact two-binomial recurrence and an elementary sine coefficient multiplier. An independent sine-operator peeling proof of the two-binomial step is retained in section5. ## 1. The exact source polynomial and its support Put N>=2, d=N-1, theta=pi/N, q=exp(i theta), and s_r=product_(k=1)^r 2sin(k theta), s_0=1, beta(n,a)=s_n/[s_a s_(n-a)] for 0<=a<=n, beta(n,a)=0 outside that integer range. For physical 0<=t<=d, 0<=u<=t and 0<=j<=t set v=t-u and P_(t,j,u)(z)=sum_a E_a z^a, E_a=beta(j,a) beta(u,a) beta(v,j-a)/beta(t,j). (1) Its nonzero support is exactly a0=max(0,j-v), a1=min(j,u), n=a1-a0. (2) All coefficients in this interval are strictly positive. The actual [complete augmented-plat compiler](actual_augmented_plat_phase_compiler.md) uses the further restrictions j<=floor(d/2), t+j>=d and the exact physical evaluation f_u(c_j)=(-1)^u q^[-(j+1)u] P_(t,j,u)(q^delta), delta=t+j-d>=0. (3) Equation (1) is precisely that finite compiler coefficient, with no q-factorial normalizer omitted. The theorem holds even without those further complete-image restrictions: P(z)=C z^a0 product_(h=1)^n(z+rho_h), C>0, rho_h>0, and all rho_h distinct. (4) If n=0 this is a positive monomial, with no nonzero roots to list. ## 2. A two-binomial polynomial has simple negative nonzero roots For u,v>=0 with t=u+v<N define Q_j^(u,v)(z)=sum_a beta(u,a) beta(v,j-a) z^a, 0<=j<=t. (5) The symmetric quantum-binomial product is the finite identity B_k(w)=sum_a beta(k,a)w^a =product_(r=0)^(k-1)(1+q^(k-1-2r)w). (6) For an elementary proof, use B_k(w)=(1+q^(k-1)w)B_(k-1)(q^-1 w). The two coefficient terms combine to beta(k,a) by the sine addition identity; B_0=1 starts the induction. No root-location assertion for B_k is made: its roots usually lie on a unit-circle arc. Let F(w,z)=B_u(zw)B_v(w)=sum_j Q_j(z)w^j. Its q-shifts obey (1+q^-u zw)(1+q^-v w)F(qw,z) =(1+q^u zw)(1+q^v w)F(q^-1 w,z). Comparing the coefficient of w^j and dividing by 2i gives the EXACT three-term recurrence sin(j theta) Q_j =[z sin((u-j+1)theta)+sin((v-j+1)theta)] Q_(j-1) +z sin((t-j+2)theta) Q_(j-2), (7) with Q_0=1 and Q_1=[sin(u theta)z+sin(v theta)]/sin theta. First suppose j<=min(u,v). For 2<=j<=min(u,v), every sine coefficient shown in (7) is strictly positive, since t<N. At any negative zero r of Q_(j-1), the sign of Q_j(r) is opposite to that of Q_(j-2)(r). Starting with Q_0,Q_1, a direct induction therefore gives j SIMPLE negative roots of Q_j strictly interlacing those of Q_(j-1). For completeness, adjacent roots of Q_(j-1) give j-2 alternating sign intervals; its rightmost root has Q_j<0 while Q_j(0)>0; and its leftmost root has sign opposite to the sign of Q_j at negative infinity. These provide all j roots. The leading and constant coefficients are positive by (5). All other j are reduced to this case by the following EXACT identities: Q_j^(u,t-u)(z)/beta(t,j) =Q_u^(j,t-j)(z)/beta(t,u), (8) Q_j^(u,v)(z)=z^u Q_(t-j)^(u,v)(1/z), (9) Q_j^(u,v)(z)=z^j Q_j^(v,u)(1/z). (10) Identity (8) follows coefficientwise by canceling six sine factorials; (9),(10) follow from beta(k,a)=beta(k,k-a). Their Laurent expressions are exactly polynomials because the same forced support zeros are present on both sides. Choose the smallest of j,t-j,u,v. If it is j, use (7). If it is t-j, use (9). If it is u, use (8). If it is v, use (10) and then (8). The new degree parameter is at most both new group sizes, so the previous Sturm induction applies. Reversal replaces each nonzero negative root by its reciprocal and multiplication by a positive constant or a forced power of z does not change its sign or simplicity. Thus (5) has exactly its forced zero of order a0, followed by n simple negative roots, for EVERY 0<=j<=t<N. ## 3. The sine multiplier preserves negative roots Let D=z d/dz and define the REAL coefficient operator S_r=sin[theta(D+r)], S_r A(z)=[e^(ir theta)A(e^(i theta)z) -e^(-ir theta)A(e^(-i theta)z)]/(2i). (11) Suppose A has degree n and only negative roots, with positive leading coefficient, and 0<r, r+n<N. Then S_r A has n SIMPLE negative roots. Here is a direct proof. Write A(z)=C product(z+rho_h), rho_h>0. For x>0 follow the continuous argument arg[e^(ir theta)A(-e^(i theta)x)]. Each factor rho_h-x e^(i theta) has strictly decreasing argument, with derivative -rho_h sin(theta)/|rho_h-x e^(i theta)|^2. The total argument decreases from r theta to (r+n)theta-n pi. It crosses exactly 0,-pi,...,-(n-1)pi, once each. Those crossings are exactly the n negative roots of (11); the factors being measured never vanish on x>0. Its leading and constant coefficients are positive. Repeated roots of the input do not spoil the strict argument monotonicity. A forced power z^a is retained: S_r[z^a A]=z^a S_(r+a)A. Thus the same assertion applies if 0<r+a and r+a+n<N. The elementary root reflection s_a s_(d-a)=N gives beta(j,a)=s_j/N product_(r=1)^(d-j) 2sin[(a+r)theta], 0<=a<=j. (12) Consequently multiplication of the a-th coefficient by beta(j,a), on a polynomial of degree at most j, is the exact operator M_j=(s_j/N) 2^(d-j) product_(r=1)^(d-j) S_r. (13) Every factor in (13) satisfies r+degree<=d<N. On a polynomial with its forced zero at the origin the shifted inequality in section3 is the same one. It therefore preserves that zero and all remaining negative roots. Applying M_j to Q_j and dividing by the positive beta(t,j) gives precisely (1). Equations (5)--(13) prove (4). The empty product j=d causes no exception: then j=t=d and n=0. ## 4. The actual Fourier value and its logarithmic branch In the complete-image chamber, 0<=delta<=j<=floor(d/2). Thus q^delta has argument between 0 and pi/2, strictly below pi/2 at finite N. It lies away from every zero in (4), so the ACTUAL canonical column (3) is nonzero, including all magnetic endpoints. More generally P(z)/P(1) has a canonical holomorphic logarithm on C minus the nonpositive real axis, fixed to be zero at z=1. Its exact factorization is Log[P(z)/P(1)]=a0 Log z +sum_h Log[(z+rho_h)/(1+rho_h)]. (14) For real |phi|<pi this also gives the elementary bound cos(phi/2)^n <= |P(e^(i phi))|/P(1) <= 1. (15) This follows from |e^(i phi)+rho|^2=(1+rho)^2-4rho sin^2(phi/2). The loss in (15) can be exponential in N. It is not a subexponential whole-source bound, a Gaussian amplitude estimate, or a proof of noncancellation after summing different physical magnetic variables. The zero-free logarithm is the rigorous input for a separate local complex asymptotic argument. ## 5. Independent sine-operator peeling proof of section2 There is a second own proof that does not use the recurrence or the intersection duality. Begin with the finite Laurent polynomial A_initial(z)=z^j B_v(1/z)=z^(j-v) B_v(z). Apply the coefficient multiplier beta(u,a). By (12) with j replaced by u, it is proportional to product_(r=1)^(d-u) S_r. The same product is zero on every unwanted Laurent power: for a<0 the factor r=-a occurs, and for a>u the factor r=N-a occurs. This uses v<=d-u and j<=u+v<=d. On the wanted powers it equals beta(u,a) exactly, so its output is the polynomial (5). The factors commute. If j>u, apply first r=N-j,...,d-u in increasing order. The identity S_(N-k) B_k=sin(k theta) B_(k-1) removes each forced high power, with the fixed prefactor z^(j-v) accounted for in the shift. If j<v, next apply r=v-j,...,1 in decreasing order. The identity S_0 B_k=sin(k theta) z B_(k-1) removes each forced negative Laurent power. All extracted constants are positive. The remaining polynomial is a positive multiple of z^a0 B_n(z), with a0,n as in (2). The unused factors have r from max(0,v-j)+1 to d-max(u,j). After extracting z^a0 their parameters are s=r+a0. They satisfy 0<s and s+n<N, and their number is n+(d-t) >= n. (16) Use at least n of these factors to strip B_n. More generally, S_s[B_k(z) A(z)]=B_(k-1)(z) T_(s,k)A(z), T_(s,k)A=Im{e^(is theta)(1+q^k z)A(qz)} (17) for real z; equivalently take the two conjugate polynomial terms as in (11). If A has m negative roots, positive leading coefficient, and k+m=n, the argument at z=-x decreases strictly from s theta to (s+k+m)theta-(m+1)pi. Here 0<k<N and 0<s+n<N. It therefore crosses exactly m+1 multiples of pi, giving T_(s,k)A exactly m+1 SIMPLE negative roots and positive leading/constant coefficients. Starting with A=1, each step reduces k by one and increases m by one. After n steps no B factor remains and all roots are negative. The remaining d-t ordinary S_s factors preserve them by section3. This independently proves the complete support and root assertion for Q. It also explains why a reciprocal sine factorial by itself need not be a multiplier: the proof uses the whole paired coefficient structure. Audit: [exact recurrence, dualities, finite source coefficients and root counts](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_negative_root_source_polynomial.py). Numerical root counts remain regression checks, not the all-level proof.

title: The actual partner normal is transverse to a generic collision
text: # The actual partner normal is transverse to a generic collision Subsequent complex estimate: the [near-fold theorem](actual_q_hahn_near_fold_complex_partner_bound.md) controls the full paired normal on a fixed complex compact when (l-j) log N=o(N). It is a relative upper bound in a shrinking scaled channel window; fixed nonzero scaled shifts and a leading normal amplitude remain open. The theorem below retains its original scope. 30 October 2026. The large partner in the original mixed-circle column can be compared with the small column BEFORE specializing q. Their equality holds on a generic spectral-collision hypersurface. This gives an exact transverse derivative formula for the original first normal, and an explicit finite tail. The tail has genuine additional poles; there is no individual-normal holomorphic theorem on the entire joint central wedge. No polynomial relative bound for that normal on a smaller corridor is proved here. Nor does a pole of an individual continued column imply a pole of the full physical coupon after all measures and terms are combined. ## 1. The original generic column in a symmetric finite form Use Q=zeta^2, d=N-1, B=Q^(-N), x=zeta^d, U=Q^u, T=Q^t and X=U^(-1). Write (a;Q)_k=product_(r=0)^(k-1)(1-a Q^r). The actual generic Clebsch column from [the mixed compiler](actual_mixed_augmented_plat_compiler.md), section 2, has the finite expression C_m=x^u F_m, F_m(Q,B;X,T)=sum_(k=0)^m (Q^(-m);Q)_k (B^2 Q^(m+1);Q)_k (X;Q)_k Q^k /[(BQ;Q)_k (T^(-1);Q)_k (Q;Q)_k]. (1) In (1), B is temporarily an independent variable. Its specialization B=Q^(-N) is the original generic source; B is not a replacement quantization. All displayed denominator factors are units near a primitive N-th root with B=1, except the indicated T divisors. For clarity, the finite transformation in (1) has a direct proof. The original bivariate numerator is H_m^B(U,V)=sum_(a=0)^m (-1)^a B^a Q^[a(a+1)/2] [m choose a]_Q (BQ^(m-a+1);Q)_a/(BQ;Q)_a V^a product_(r<a)(U-Q^r) product_(r<m-a)(V-Q^r), F_m=H_m^B(U,T/U)/product_(r<m)(T-Q^r). (2) The normalized generic Casimir operator, after removing x^u, has eigenvalues Lambda_m=B^(-1)Q^(-m)+B Q^(m+1). On the Newton basis P_k(X)=(X;Q)_k its action is triangular: L P_k=Lambda_k P_k+eta_k P_(k-1), eta_k=(B^(-1)-Q^k)(1-Q^(k-1)/T)(1-Q^(-k)). (3) One can check the lower term without a summation transformation. At X=1,Q^(-1),...,Q^(2-k), the shifted polynomial vanishes, so the lower term is divisible by P_(k-1). At X=Q^(1-k), only the X/Q shift remains; its coefficient is (B^(-1)-Q^k)(1-Q^(k-1)/T), and P_k(X/Q)/P_(k-1)(X)=1-Q^(-k). The leading coefficient gives Lambda_k. Consequently the coefficients of a degree-m eigenfunction normalized to F_m(1)=1 satisfy a_(k+1)/a_k=Q(1-Q^(k-m))(1-B^2 Q^(m+k+1)) /[(1-BQ^(k+1))(1-Q^k/T)(1-Q^(k+1))]. (4) For generic parameters these eigenvalues are distinct. The degree-m normalized eigenfunction is unique, and (4), with a_0=1, gives (1). Rational continuation then proves the identity wherever defined. There is no small-channel restriction hidden in this argument. To justify the generic operator identity for a fixed arbitrary m, first take every integer source size N>=2m+1. The original generic Clebsch calculation and its sufficiently many complete physical t slices give the identity at B=Q^(-N), after clearing denominators. The cleared residual is a FIXED finite Laurent polynomial in B,Q,U,T. Write it as sum B^a p_a(Q,U,T). For N larger than its finite Q-exponent widths, the supports of Q^(-Na)p_a are disjoint. Its vanishing at all such N forces every p_a=0. Thus (3) and the actual numerator identity are formal in B,Q, and apply equally to a large m<N. The physical slice count at one fixed N is not being applied to a large partner. ## 2. The collision identity is generic Fix 0<=j<l and j+l=N-1. The eigenvalue difference factors as Lambda_l-Lambda_j =B^(-1)Q^(-l)(1-Q^(l-j))(1-B^2 Q^N). (5) On the generic hypersurface B^2 Q^N=1, the two numerator parameters of (1) for m=j are the two numerator parameters for m=l in the opposite order. In the large series the second parameter is Q^(-j), so its terms k>j vanish. Therefore, IDENTICALLY in X,T, F_l=F_j on B^2 Q^N=1. (6) Work locally near the actual primitive root Q_0, B=1, with the denominators in (1) inverted. The collision is smooth there because its B derivative is nonzero. Equation (6) gives a regular rational function R_(j,l) such that F_l-F_j=(1-B^2 Q^N) R_(j,l). (7) At even N another algebraic component of the collision can meet denominator divisors. This does not affect the stated local germ: every factor 1-BQ^r, 1<=r<N, is a unit at Q_0,B=1. The assertion does not cancel a denominator identically zero on an irrelevant component. At the actual root, (6) also proves the useful bivariate factorization H_l^1(U,V)=H_j^1(U,V) product_(r=j)^(l-1)(UV-Q_0^r). (8) This is an identity of the continued source numerator, not just an equality on the physical integer magnetic grid. ## 3. The actual generic-q normal becomes a transverse B derivative Return to B=Q^(-N), q=exp(pi i/N), Q_0=q^2, x=q^(N-1), and put Delta=q^(2j+1)-q^(-2j-1), D=zeta d/dzeta. The actual tensor Casimir eigenvalue is lambda_m(zeta)=zeta^(2N-2m-1)+zeta^(-2N+2m+1), D(lambda_j-lambda_l)(q)=-2N Delta. The root-only expression q^(2m+1)+q^(-2m-1) has the same value but would give the WRONG derivative sign. The actual mixed compiler uses w_j=[D C_j(q)-D C_l(q)]/[-2N Delta]. (9) Along this ACTUAL generic family, D(1-B^2 Q^N)=2N at the root. Since F_l-F_j vanishes identically in X,T on the collision, the derivatives of x^u, X=zeta^(-2u), and T=zeta^(2t) do not contribute to the derivative of the difference. Equations (7),(9) give exactly w_j=x^u R_(j,l)(Q_0,1;X,T)/Delta =x^u [B partial_B(F_j-F_l)]_(Q_0,1)/(2 Delta). (10) The partial derivative in the second line holds Q,X,T fixed. This is an exact consequence of generic collision divisibility. It is NOT differentiation of the root-only identity F_l=F_j. In particular the large partner's generic normal has not been dropped. ## 4. The explicit surviving derivative tail All expressions in this section are at Q=Q_0. Put a=Q^(-j), b=Q^(-l), c_k=(a;Q)_k(b;Q)_k(X;Q)_k Q^k /[(Q;Q)_k^2(T^(-1);Q)_k], L_k(y)=-sum_(r=0)^(k-1) y Q^r/(1-y Q^r). For k<=j, every factor in L_k(a),L_k(b) is a unit. Differentiating (1) in B and subtracting cancels the common denominator derivative. For k>j the single vanishing numerator factor has derivative [y partial_y(y;Q)_k]_(y=Q^(-j)) =-(a;Q)_j(Q;Q)_(k-j-1). Thus the original normal is w_j=x^u/Delta * { sum_(k=0)^j c_k [L_k(b)-L_k(a)] +(a;Q)_j sum_(k=j+1)^l (b;Q)_k(Q;Q)_(k-j-1)(X;Q)_k Q^k /[(Q;Q)_k^2(T^(-1);Q)_k] }. (11) The second line is a nonempty tail whenever j<l. Bounded harmonic coefficients in the first line do not bound this coherent sum relative to F_j; nor do they remove the tail. Equation (11) records all of it with the original normalizer. ## 5. Genuine extra poles obstruct a whole-wedge normal theorem As a polynomial in X, w_j/x^u has EXACT degree l. Only the k=l tail term contributes its highest coefficient, which is (-1)^l Q^[l(l+1)/2] (Q^(-l);Q)_l(Q^(-j);Q)_j(Q;Q)_(l-j-1) /[Delta (Q;Q)_l^2(T^(-1);Q)_l]. (12) Its numerator is nonzero: all nonzero factorial indices are less than N, and 2j+1<N gives Delta!=0. Therefore each divisor T=Q^r, j<=r<l, (13) is a genuine SIMPLE pole of the normalized normal for generic X. The highest-coefficient residue is nonzero and cannot be canceled by lower powers of X. Its residue polynomial has degree l, so it does not vanish on an open set of magnetic coordinates. The ordinary small column F_j has no pole at any of (13). Its denominator only uses r<j. If N/2<r<l, the scaled pair degree tau=r/N lies strictly inside the joint central wedge. An open set of its central magnetic coordinates avoids the finitely many roots of the residue polynomial. Thus the actual terminating continuation of this INDIVIDUAL first normal cannot be holomorphic on that whole wedge, let alone admit a uniform relative polynomial estimate there. These additional divisors lie below the physical high-partner range t>=l. On a fixed compact tau>1/2 they disappear when j/N is sufficiently close to 1/2. Consequently (13) does not disprove a smaller corridor near the folded endpoint. It also does not prove such a corridor estimate: the tail in (11) still requires control. Finally, (13) is not a theorem about poles of the entire mixed coupon. The original inverse measure and the other terms may cancel individual-column poles. Nor does it exclude a separately specified whole-source continuation. It rules out silently extending the ordinary-column joint theorem to this canonical generic normal. Audit: [generic collision, original normal and pole certificates](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_partner_normal_collision.py). The collision calculation does not imply a smaller-corridor estimate or a pole of the full coupon.

title: Every fixed generic jet of an actual physical q-Hahn column
status: All physical generic column and divided-pair jets
text: # Every fixed generic jet of an actual physical q-Hahn column 30 October 2026. This note extends the physical prefix estimate to the original generic deformation. Every fixed generic-q derivative of every admissible physical column has polynomial cost relative to its nonzero root value, including large channels. The actual divided pair also has polynomial fixed generic jets. The upper half of the column is treated by its backward generic recurrence, not by differentiating a root-only reflection identity. The statement is on integer physical degrees and magnetic indices. It supplies no fixed complex magnetic neighborhood, no nonzero confluent amplitude, and no completed four-port or network norm. ## 1. The actual generic column and its endpoints Fix N>=3, d=N-1, q0=exp(pi i/N), and integers 0<=m<=t<=d, 0<=u<=t. Write q=q0 exp(epsilon), Q=q^2, x=q^d, v=t-u, and F_r=(Q;Q)_r. The original finite source is C_m(q;t,u)=sum_(a=max(0,m-v))^(min(m,u)) (-1)^a x^(u-2a) Q^[av+a(a-1)/2] F_(N-m+a-1)F_(N-a-1)/(F_(N-m-1)F_(N-1)) [u choose a]_Q [v choose m-a]_Q/[t choose m]_Q. (1) These are precisely the genuine generic highest-vector ratios of the [mixed compiler](actual_mixed_augmented_plat_compiler.md), not the squared-binomial formula obtained after root specialization. All factorial indices in (1) are below N. The function is regular near q0. Its endpoints are exact monomials: C_m(q;t,0)=1, C_m(q;t,t)=(-1)^m q^[dt-2Nm+m^2+m]. (2) For the second equality only a=m survives; the original ratio of F-factorials is then one. These formulas hold before differentiating. There are universal c,C>0 such that, simultaneously for all the integer indices above, C_m(q0;t,u)!=0, |C_m(q0 exp(epsilon);t,u)/C_m(q0;t,u)|<=C for |epsilon|<=cN^(-8). (3) The functions in (3) are holomorphic on that disk. In particular, for every fixed r>=0, |D^r C_m(q0;t,u)|<=C_r N^(8r)|C_m(q0;t,u)|, D=q d/dq. (4) There is no small-channel restriction on m in (3),(4). ## 2. The original generic physical Casimir block The degree-t balanced tensor basis has entries indexed by u=0,...,t. Let J_t(q) have diagonal D_u, upper entries A_u^+ and lower entries A_u^- (the superscripts refer to the matrix positions). A direct application of the original generic coproduct gives D_u=q^-1 Q^(u-t)(1-Q^(N-u))(1-Q^u) +q^(-2d-1)Q^u(1-Q^(N-t+u))(1-Q^(t-u)) +q^(2d+1)Q^-t+q^(-2d-1)Q^t, (J_t)_(u,u+1)=A_u^+ =q^-N Q^(2u+1-t)(1-Q^(N-u-1))(1-Q^(t-u)), (J_t)_(u+1,u)=A_u^- =q^-N(1-Q^(N-t+u))(1-Q^(u+1)), 0<=u<t. (5) For example the lower offdiagonal is the contribution of F on the first head after E on the second; the upper offdiagonal retains both Cartan factors of the opposite path. Their generic values differ. Replacing them by their equal root values before differentiating would change the source. The vector (1) satisfies J_t(q) C_m(q;t,.)=lambda_m(q) C_m(q;t,.), lambda_m=q^(2N-2m-1)+q^(-2N+2m+1). (6) This follows from its highest degree m, highest weight 2d-2m, and the original coproduct Casimir. Alternatively, substitution of the finite highest-vector and its divided descendants yields (5),(6) entry by entry. Thus the normalization C_m(0)=1 in the magnetic index fixes the SAME source vector, not an auxiliary eigenvector. At q0 the two offdiagonals in (5) coincide, and (5) simplifies to D_u=U/T [2(q0^-1+q0 T)-(q0+q0^-1)U], A_u=(U-T)(1-Q0 U)/T, U=Q0^u, T=Q0^t, Q0=q0^2. (7) For the reversal matrix P_t, (7) also gives P_t J_t(q0) P_t=conjugate(J_t(q0)). (8) Only this ROOT identity is needed below. No generic version of (8), or a flat high-degree adapter, is assumed. ## 3. A polynomial generic neighborhood from prefix coercivity The [physical prefix theorem](actual_q_hahn_physical_partner_normal_bound.md) proves, for every 1<=h<=floor(t/2), Im J_[h](q0) >= 4 sin^3(pi/N)/h^2 * I. (9) Although that note applies the estimate to complete double channels, its weighted-row identity and positive Dirichlet proof use only 1<=t<=d and h<=floor(t/2). In this entire range the weights 1/sin((t-r)pi/N) are positive, its row residual is 4 sin(r pi/N) sin^2(pi/N) sin(t pi/N) /sin((t-r-1)pi/N)>=0, and every retained conductance is at least 4sin(pi/N). The same Poincare step therefore proves (9) for all t used here. It requires no sign assumption on -cos((t+1)pi/N) and no channel condition t>=l. The bound is independent of the real spectral parameter. Since lambda_m(q0) is real, it implies ||(lambda_m(q0)I-J_[h](q0))^-1||<=C N^5. (10) The reversed prefix has the conjugate root matrix by (8), hence has the same inverse bound. This holds for every m<=t, not merely for the two members of a double node. Every elementary exponent in (5),(6) is O(N). On a fixed disk |epsilon|<=c/N the entries and eigenvalues are O(1) and their epsilon derivatives are O(N), uniformly over all indices. The bandwidth is fixed. For either the forward or reversed prefix, ||M(epsilon)-M(0)||<=C N|epsilon|, M(epsilon)=lambda_m(q)I-J_prefix(q). (11) Combining (10),(11), on rho_N=cN^(-8) the relative perturbation has norm at most Cc/N^2. Decrease c so that it is below 1/2. For prefix size h<=N, |det M(epsilon)/det M(0)| <=(1+Cc/N^2)^h<=C, (12) and the determinant is nonzero throughout the disk. The offdiagonal products introduce only polynomial local costs. At the root |A_u^+|=|A_u^-| =4 sin((t-u)pi/N) sin((u+1)pi/N) >=4 sin^2(pi/N)>=16/N^2. (13) Equation (5) gives derivative O(N), so these entries remain nonzero on the same disk. Their relative logarithmic changes are bounded by C N^3|epsilon|. A product of at most N such entries therefore has a uniformly bounded ratio to its root value, and so does its inverse. In fact its logarithmic change is O(N^4|epsilon|). For u<=floor(t/2), the exact forward recurrence gives C_m(q;t,u)=det(lambda_m(q)I-J_[u](q)) / product_(r=0)^(u-1) A_r^+(q). (14) The empty determinant and product at u=0 are one. Equations (10)--(14) prove root nonvanishing and (3) on this half. For u>=ceil(t/2), put h=t-u and reverse the ACTUAL generic recurrence. Normalize its endpoint by the exact nonzero C_m(q;t,t) in (2). The normalized reversed column has initial entry one and is again a leading-prefix determinant divided by its own upper offdiagonal product. Its prefix has size h<=floor(t/2). Equations (8)--(13) apply to this reversed generic matrix because its ROOT is conjugate to the forward one and its generic entries satisfy the SAME bounds. The endpoint exponent in (2) is O(N^2), so its ratio on the small disk is also uniformly bounded. This proves (3) on the upper half, including t=0,1 by the endpoint formulas alone. Cauchy's formula now gives (4) for the genuine generic source. The derivative holds N,t,u fixed, as the original compiler does. ## 4. The completed divided pair also has fixed generic jets Suppose j<l, j+l=d and l<=t. Put s=l-j and define the original generic divided pair W_(j,l)(q;t,u)= (C_j(q;t,u)-C_l(q;t,u))/(lambda_j(q)-lambda_l(q)). (15) The [exact collision identity](actual_q_hahn_partner_normal_collision.md) gives C_j(q0;t,u)=C_l(q0;t,u), and its actual gap is lambda_j-lambda_l=(q^s-q^-s)(q^N-q^-N). (16) The second factor has a simple zero at q0; the first does not. Thus (15) has a removable singularity, with root value exactly the retained physical paired normal W_(j,l)(q0;t,u) =[D C_j-D C_l]/[-2N Delta_j], Delta_j=q0^(2j+1)-q0^(-2j-1)=q0^s-q0^-s. (17) On |epsilon|=rho_N, the first factor in (16) has modulus at least c/N and the second at least cN rho_N. There are no other zeros inside this disk. The two bounds (3), using their equal root values, therefore give |W_(j,l)(q;t,u)|<=C rho_N^-1 |C_j(q0;t,u)| on |epsilon|=rho_N. Cauchy's formula applied AFTER the removable singularity is filled proves, for every fixed r>=0, |D^r W_(j,l)(q0;t,u)| <=C_r N^[8(r+1)] |C_j(q0;t,u)|. (18) For r=0 the earlier N^6 physical paired-normal estimate is sharper. The additional content here is the higher genuine generic-q jets, including the variation of the matrix, both original columns, and the gap. Equation (18) is not obtained by treating a q derivative as a spectral derivative. For example D W at the root contains second q derivatives of the original columns, as it must. ## 5. Interface and limits The [matching-edge rewrite](actual_matching_edge_marked_four_port_block.md) needs Taylor order two after clearing its simple poles. Equations (4),(18) remove a possible physical-column obstruction to controlling such jets. To apply them to a completed target pair one must STILL prove its exact expression in these normalized columns, their divided pair, and its actual scalar measures. The native boundary cost of that four-port tensor has not been replaced by a polynomial in this note. Nor is a surrounding contraction estimated here. The estimates concern integer t,u. They do not prove a fixed complex magnetic corridor or control the extra poles of the large partner's unrestricted continuation. The separate shrinking-channel complex theorem and the present physical generic theorem address different domains. No lower bound for W or a nonzero selected global contribution follows from either upper estimate. Audit: [original generic physical matrix and retained divided-pair jets](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_physical_generic_jet_bound.py). The focused exact audit passed 1,204 original physical column four-jets, 1,204 generic eigenvector equations, 2,408 forward/backward comparisons, 432 generic endpoint jets, and 378 divided-pair jets through order two. It retains 4,816 column and 1,134 pair coefficients; 323 tested second pair jets are nonzero. Those checks verify source and normal conventions, while the prefix perturbation proof supplies the uniform bounds. The theorem retains the integer physical domain. It gives neither a completed four-port norm nor a fixed complex magnetic neighborhood.

title: A polynomial bound for the actual partner normal on the physical grid
status: All physical paired first normals; complex corridor open
text: # A polynomial bound for the actual partner normal on the physical grid Subsequent complex estimate: the [near-fold theorem](actual_q_hahn_near_fold_complex_partner_bound.md) controls the full paired normal on a fixed complex compact when (l-j) log N=o(N). It is a relative upper bound in a shrinking scaled channel window; fixed nonzero scaled shifts and a leading normal amplitude remain open. The theorem below retains its original scope. 30 October 2026. Every original physical magnetic entry of a complete double Casimir channel has a polynomially bounded confluent normal relative to its nonzero ordinary value. This includes both halves of every physical degree block, both parities, and every complete double channel. The estimate is for the ACTUAL generic divided difference. It is not an estimate obtained by differentiating a root-only formula. The argument is a positive-imaginary-part estimate for a half-prefix of the original complex symmetric Casimir matrix, followed by its exact reflection symmetry through first order at a double spectral node. No complex magnetic continuation, global magnetic contour, or whole marked-source estimate follows from this physical-grid statement. ## 1. The source and the quantitative statement Put theta=pi/N, q=exp(i theta), Q=q^2, d=N-1, x=q^d. Let 0<=j<l, j+l=d, l<=t<=d, 0<=u<=t, c_j=q^(2j+1)+q^(-2j-1), Delta_j=q^(2j+1)-q^(-2j-1). All these indices are integers. Let C_(j,u) be the original root column normalized by C_(j,0)=1. Let w_(j,u) be its actual confluent normal as specified by [the mixed compiler](actual_mixed_augmented_plat_compiler.md): w_(j,u)=[D C_(j,u)-D C_(l,u)]/[-2N Delta_j], D=zeta d/dzeta, evaluated at zeta=q. (1) Both generic columns in (1) use the original highest weight d and its full factorial ratio. Then EVERY C_(j,u) is nonzero and |w_(j,u)/C_(j,u)|<=N^6/256+N^2/8. (2) If t/N stays in a fixed compact subset of (0,1), the right side can be replaced by C_K N^4. In the present complete range t>=l this only requires a fixed upper separation from t/N=1. No separation from the folded channel is required. ## 2. The actual prefix has positive imaginary part The original degree-t Casimir block J_t is complex symmetric tridiagonal, as proved directly from the balanced tensor operators in [the complete Hermite packet](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_complete_casimir_hermite_packet.md). For r=0,...,t put U_r=Q^r, T=Q^t. Its entries simplify exactly to D_r=U_r/T [2(q^(-1)+qT)-(q+q^(-1))U_r], A_r=(U_r-T)(1-QU_r)/T, 0<=r<t. (3) Every A_r is nonzero. For 1<=m<=floor(t/2), let J_[m] be its leading m-by-m principal submatrix. Because the matrix is symmetric, its Hermitian imaginary part is the entrywise imaginary-part matrix. Set h_r=(t-2r)theta and c=-cos((t+1)theta). Its diagonal and upper offdiagonal imaginary parts, including the next boundary coefficient, are d_r=4 sin(h_r)[c+cos(theta)cos(h_r)], o_r=4 sin(h_r-theta)sin((t-r)theta)sin((r+1)theta). (4) For 0<=r<m these o_r are positive. Introduce positive weights a_r=1/sin((t-r)theta), 0<=r<=m. A direct sine expansion gives the EXACT weighted row identity d_r-o_(r-1)a_(r-1)/a_r-o_r a_(r+1)/a_r =4 sin(r theta)sin^2(theta)sin(t theta) /sin((t-r-1)theta) >=0, (5) where the r=0 term involving o_(-1) is absent. The right side is zero at r=0. All denominators in (5) are positive in the stated range. One elementary verification expands sin(b-a) and cos(a+b+theta), with a=r theta and b=(t-r)theta. After multiplying by sin(b-theta)/4, the residual is precisely sin(a)sin^2(theta)sin(a+b). Conjugate Im J_[m] by diag(1,-1,1,...), so its offdiagonals are -o_r. For a vector v write v_r=a_r y_r, and set y_m=0. Equation (5) expresses its quadratic form as sum_(r=0)^(m-1) k_r |y_r-y_(r+1)|^2 +sum_(r=0)^(m-1) V_r a_r^2 |y_r|^2, k_r=o_r a_r a_(r+1) =4 sin((t-2r-1)theta)sin((r+1)theta) /sin((t-r-1)theta), V_r=the nonnegative right side of (5). (6) There is a genuine Dirichlet term at the right endpoint; it is not discarded when the prefix is taken. The conductances obey k_r>=4 sin(theta). (7) Indeed the two numerator sine arguments alpha,beta are at least theta, with alpha+beta=(t-r)theta<pi. On the interval theta<=alpha<=alpha+beta-theta, their product is minimized at an endpoint, so sin(alpha)sin(beta)>=sin(theta) sin(alpha+beta-theta), which is (7). Since a_r<=1/sin(theta) and sum|y_r|^2<=m^2 sum|y_r-y_(r+1)|^2, equations (6),(7) prove Im J_[m] >= [4 sin^3(theta)/m^2] I. (8) The sign-conjugation is unitary and does not change this lower bound. For t/N in a fixed compact inside (0,1), all a_r in this half-prefix are uniformly bounded; the stronger lower bound is c_K/N^3. ## 3. Lower-half spectral derivatives Let f_r(z) be the original normalized forward column, f_0=1, f_r(z)=det(zI-J_[r])/(A_0 ... A_(r-1)). (9) The real point c_j is a double eigenvalue of J_t. The actual source and normal are exactly C_(j,r)=f_r(c_j), w_(j,r)=f_r'(c_j). (10) This is the generic-confluence identity in the complete Hermite packet and the mixed compiler: differentiating the two normalized generic columns cancels the common q derivative and retains the original eigenvalue-gap derivative -2N Delta_j. For ANY real z, (8) gives ||(zI-J_[m])^(-1)||<=m^2/[4 sin^3(theta)]. In particular the determinant in (9) is nonzero there. Taking its logarithmic derivative gives |f_m'(z)/f_m(z)| =|tr((zI-J_[m])^(-1))| <=m^3/[4 sin^3(theta)]. (11) Since m<=N/2 and sin(theta)>=2/N, (11) is at most N^6/256. The compact-degree improvement of (8) gives C_K N^4 instead. For m=0 the normal is zero and the value is 1. ## 4. Reflection extends the bound through the full physical block Let P reverse the indices 0,...,t. Formula (3) gives exactly P J_t P=conjugate(J_t). (12) The characteristic polynomial is p_(t+1)(z)=product_(m=0)^t(z-c_m), and the forward column satisfies (J_t-zI)f(z)=-p_(t+1)(z)e_t/(A_0 ... A_(t-1)). (13) At a double node c_j, both the residual and its first derivative vanish. Reflecting and conjugating (13), and using uniqueness of the forward recurrence with its first component fixed, therefore gives, at that node, f_(t-r)=f_t conjugate(f_r), f'_(t-r)=f'_t conjugate(f_r)+f_t conjugate(f'_r). (14) This is a first-order identity at a DOUBLE node. It is not inferred by differentiating a value identity known only at isolated points. One may justify (14) as an identity modulo (z-c_j)^2: the reflected column has first entry conjugate(f_t(conjugate z)); its first-row error is a multiple of p_(t+1)(z), so its forward recurrence agrees to this order. Setting r=t in the value identity gives |f_t|=1. The endpoint normal has a particularly simple original generic calculation. At u=t only a=m survives in the generic Clebsch sum, and its highest-vector ratio R_(m,m) is identically 1. Thus C_(m,t)(zeta)=(-1)^m zeta^[d(t-2m)+m(m-1)]. (15) The two exponents for j,l differ by N(l-j). Combining (15) with the actual gap in (1) gives f'_t(c_j)/f_t(c_j)=-(l-j)/(2 Delta_j), |f'_t/f_t|<N/[4 sin(theta)]<=N^2/8. (16) For r>t/2 apply (14) with t-r in the lower half. Its value is nonzero and f'_r/f_r=f'_t/f_t+conjugate(f'_(t-r)/f_(t-r)). (17) Equations (11),(16),(17) prove (2) for every physical entry. ## 5. Scope of the estimate The paired normal, including its formerly hidden large-channel contribution, is controlled on the entire physical grid. Its exponential rate there cannot exceed that of its ordinary column by more than O(log N)/N. This is a relative entrywise statement; it does not control cancellations after a whole graph is sewn. The high-total-degree blocks are transported by the constant Chevalley-plus-flip adapter in the complete Hermite packet. Thus the same root spectral-column estimate applies after the stated physical index translation. It is the root confluent column being transported here, not a new generic-q adapter assumed to be flat. The estimate does NOT extend by continuity to a fixed complex magnetic neighborhood. The canonical large-partner continuation has the additional degree poles proved in [the generic collision note](actual_q_hahn_partner_normal_collision.md), and its finite tail requires a separate complex estimate. A bound on integer magnetic samples, even at all levels, supplies no such analytic continuation theorem. Focused audit: [original normal, positive prefix and reflection](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_physical_partner_normal_bound.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_q_hahn_physical_partner_normal_bound_results.json). The symbolic weighted-row identity passed. Exact arithmetic checked 131 original Casimir blocks, 726 weighted-row identities, 8,578 actual generic paired normals and their first-order reflections, and 571 original endpoint normals. At 90 digits, 10,164 actual relative-normal bounds passed; the audit also checked 288 positive prefix matrices and 2,384 conductance inequalities. These finite checks supplement the uniform proof above. The high-degree adapter transports the root spectral column without assuming that an individual generic derivative is flat. The theorem is restricted to the physical grid. No complex magnetic continuation or whole-source bound is inferred.

title: The original q-Hahn source at a resonant framing boundary
status: Original resonant boundary packets and retained source zeros
text: # The original q-Hahn source at a resonant framing boundary 30 October 2026. The actual prefix words give an explicit degeneration of the original white arguments when the residual framing parameter tends to infinity. One of its large-clock regimes has a uniform, source-normalized Bessel limit. The numerator is the actual LARGE generic-channel numerator specialized at the root; neither a scalar symbol nor an off-lattice channel is substituted. This is a local root-value boundary model. Genuine quantum normals are separate. It neither puts every box in this regime nor computes the coefficient of the geometric component in the original global period. ## 1. Actual prefix words determine the escaping heads Normalize the reference positive meridian to J=[[1,1],[0,1]], and keep the original common framing F(r,s)=[[r,1-r],[s,-s]], with s nonzero. For every actual based prefix Q=[[a,b],[c,d]] put L_Q(r)=Tr(Q F E11 F^-1) =-c r^2/s+(a-d+c/s)r+d+b s. (1) These are the actual prefix diagonals. On a fixed horizontal cut the physical clock of its i-th wire is X_i=-L_(Q_(i-1))/L_(Q_i). No independent local frame is chosen. For the complete discrete faithful holonomy, each prefix is either genuinely quadratic in (1), or constant. Indeed c=0 implies a=d=+/-1. To see this directly, conjugating J by Q supplies translations a^(2n). If |a^2| differs from one these accumulate at the identity. If |a^2|=1, the discrete additive group generated by these translations has rank at most two; rotations preserving it form a finite group. Thus a^2 is a root of unity. If a^2 is not one, the upper triangular Q has finite projective order, contrary to the free deck action. Consequently Q=+/-[[1,b0],[0,1]], whose L_Q is constant. This argument uses actual holonomy words, not arbitrary matrices assigned to ports. Fix s so all the finitely many constant L_Q are nonzero. Let e(Q)=0 in this constant case and e(Q)=1 in the quadratic case. At r=N rho, with rho in a fixed compact subset of C*, X_i=C_i(s) r^k_i (1+O(1/r)), k_i=2(e(Q_(i-1))-e(Q_i)) in {-2,0,2}. (2) For two quadratic prefixes the limiting ratio is the ratio of their lower-left entries, with the displayed minus sign. These are actual geometric limiting data. They are not independently optimized. The k_i obey the homogeneous original cup/cap/coupon incidence equations, since the exact products of the corresponding clocks do. Thus the logarithmic escape is one coupled integral flow. On a cut, each run of quadratic prefixes has paired -2/+2 boundary transitions. The exact finite affine offsets have a uniform convenient realization. If X_i=exp(2pi i x_i) with the recorded logarithmic lift, set i_i=N x_i-1/2, Q_N^(i_i)=q_N^-1 X_i. (3) This prescription applies to the PHYSICAL V_d heads. It gives every physical cup/cap i_1+i_2=N-1 and q_N^(d-2i_i)=-1/X_i. At a white vertex define the channel row by its original equation r0=i_1+i_2-(d-a), with the actual discrete a retained. An auxiliary V_(2a) head is not assigned the same universal -1/2 offset. Its finite color is equivalently (a+1/2)/N. Thus degree constraints remain exact, but this is not evaluation of every finite channel at the complete parabolic stationary point. It samples the principal geometric germ without asserting finite-N stationary equations. For k_i!=0, the imaginary index has size N log N. For X_i=1+zeta/r+O(r^-2), instead, i_i=zeta/(2pi i rho)-1/2+O(N^-1), (4) up to its retained integer logarithmic lift. The -1/2 is essential. A point near a negative half-integer is not an original integer support zero. An O(1/N) perturbation of a clock near one must not be discarded. The same caution applies to characters: exp(2pi i i_i)=-X_i^N. (5) Its magnitude need not be one, and can be N^(2N) in (2). ## 2. The literal white, dual and exceptional arguments At a circle write a0=L_W, a1=L_(AW), a1'=L_(Aout W), a2=L_(PW), where P=BA=Bout Aout and W is its original prefix. Its incoming geometric clocks are U=-a0/a1, V=-a1/a2, T=UV=a0/a2, (6) and the output replaces a1 by a1'. By the actual generic white formula, the numerator is H_m^B(q_N^-1 U,q_N^-1 V), with m=d-a, B=Q^-N. The channel a remains the actual discrete integer. For prefix degrees (deg a0,deg a1,deg a2), the root arguments have the following orders; the factors q_N^-1 in (3) remain in each entry. | Degrees | U | V | T | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 000 | finite | finite | finite | | 002 | finite | r^-2 | r^-2 | | 020 | r^-2 | r^2 | finite | | 022 | r^-2 | finite | r^-2 | | 200 | r^2 | finite | r^2 | | 202 | r^2 | r^-2 | finite | | 220 | finite | r^2 | r^2 | | 222 | finite | finite | finite | Here "finite" means a nonzero limit, which can still meet a further chart divisor, including one. For the original complete-circle boxes, 000 and 020 are impossible: a0 and a2 constant would make P preserve the reference main cusp, although P is a nontrivial longitude of a different, auxiliary cusp. Distinct cusp lifts have disjoint small horoballs and cannot have the same center. For routed crossing bands one must retain all eight rows unless that extra hypothesis is proved. There is no implicit Hermitian adjoint. The literal pi dual uses the reversed complementary indices (d-j,d-i). The exact Chevalley identity W_a(d-j,d-i;2a-r0) =zeta^[(d-2a)(a-r0)] W_a(i,j;r0) (7) reduces it to the incoming white with its actual scalar retained. Alternatively its two raw H arguments are the reversed reciprocals Q^d/Q^j,Q^d/Q^i. All routing spectra and their paired partners remain. For the exceptional inverse turn retain its actual coordinates h=v-u, ell=t-v, sigma=d-h, r0=a-h. Its two numerator pairs are exactly (Q^(sigma-u),Q^u), (Q^ell,Q^(sigma-ell)). (8) With physical half-index sampling these are the original outgoing and incoming pairs in (6), respectively. The moving factorial arguments are r0,2a-r0 in the channel cup and v,d-v,ell,d-ell in the inverse physical cups; ordinary pi has the analogous original complemented indices. This specifies their whole marked logarithmic lifts. The specified generic exceptional lift has root character exp(-2pi i v). Restoring the original physical turn contributes the inverse exp(2pi i v), exactly as in the [source lift](actual_matching_edge_generic_deficient_operator_lift.md), equation (13). They cancel BEFORE an estimate. Bounding them separately at (2) could introduce artificial N log N growth. None of this proves uniform asymptotics for the listed moving factorials or numerators. ## 3. A uniform original-root packet when the first clock is large Put Q=exp(2pi i/N), and keep an actual integer m with delta <= mu=m/N <= 1-delta, delta>0. At the root the exact polynomial is H_m^1(U,V)=sum_(k=0)^m c_k V^k product_(j<k)(U-Q^j) product_(j<m-k)(V-Q^j), c_k=(-1)^k Q^[k(k+1)/2] [m choose k]_Q^2. (9) This includes the actual large m=d-a. Suppose U=N^2 kappa_N, V=V_N, where kappa_N and V_N range in fixed compact subsets of C*. Keep the EXACT last Newton term E_N=c_m (UV)^m product_(j<m)(1-Q^j/U), c_m=(-1)^m Q^[m(m+1)/2]. (10) It is nonzero for large N. Define the entire function Bessel(K)=sum_(l>=0) (-K)^l/(l!)^2 =J_0(2sqrt(K)), K_N=sin^2(pi mu)(V_N-1)/(pi^2 kappa_N V_N). (11) The series, not a square-root branch, defines the notation. Uniformly on those compacts, H_m^1(U,V)/E_N=Bessel(K_N)+O(N^-1). (12) In particular U=N^2 kappa(1+O(N^-1)), V=V0+O(N^-1) gives the same formula with K=sin^2(pi mu)(V0-1)/(pi^2 kappa V0). The finite m/N, the phase c_m, and the product in (10) have not been discarded. Equation (12) is an absolute normalized estimate. A relative packet is asserted only on a compact set where Bessel(K) is nonzero. Here is a proof retaining the WHOLE finite polynomial. Set k=m-l. The exact ratio of that summand to (10) is (-1)^l Q^[-ml+l(l-1)/2] [m choose l]_Q^2 * (UV)^(-l) product_(j<l)(V-Q^j) /product_(j=m-l)^(m-1)(1-Q^j/U). (13) For j<=m<=(1-delta)N, |1-Q^j|>=c_delta j/N. Consequently |[m choose l]_Q|<=(C_delta N)^l/l! for EVERY l<=m. The denominator in (13) has inverse bounded independently of N,l, since |U|>=cN^2. Thus every term is bounded by C^l/(l!)^2. This proves uniform summable tail domination, not just convergence of the fixed-l terms. For fixed l, expand the exact Gaussian products. The identity exp(-2pi i mu)(1-exp(2pi i mu))^2/(-2pi i)^2 =sin^2(pi mu)/pi^2 gives precisely (-K_N)^l/(l!)^2. Uniformly for l<=N^(1/4), the product expansion has absolute error at most C^l(1+l)^C/[N(l!)^2]. This follows by expanding each of the l numerator and denominator factors; their relative errors are O(l/N), while product_(j<l)(V-Q^j) is compared in absolute value if V=1. The factorial bound makes the remaining tail smaller than every power of N. Summing proves (12). ## 4. A geometric transition with an explicit nonzero model Consider a 200 box whose second raw puncture is the reference B=-J. Then Q1=AW=epsilon[[1,b],[0,1]], Q2=BQ1, epsilon=+/-1. Write A21=c_A. The actual complete disk relation Tr(BA)=-2 and Tr A=-2 give c_A=4. Since W=A^-1Q1, its lower-left entry is -epsilon c_A. Substituting (1),(6), at r=N rho gives kappa=Q0_21 rho^2/[s L_Q1], V0=-L_Q1/L_Q2, K=sin^2(pi mu) s^2/(4pi^2 rho^2). (14) The q_N^-1 argument corrections are included in the O(N^-1) allowed in (12). They were not dropped in (4), where their size is decisive. The inverse orientation B=-J^-1 gives the same squared expression. In the actual first-slot Fourier convention eta_j=Q^j and p=eta_j^-1, the resonant scale for each fixed nonzero integer j is r=1/(1-exp(-2pi i j/N))-beta s, rho -> 1/(2pi i j). Hence this local boundary factor tends Bessel(-j^2 s^2 sin^2(pi mu)) =I_0(2j s sin(pi mu)). (15) For Re s!=0 it is nonzero. An elementary proof avoids a zero theorem: if I_0(z)=0, f(t)=I_0(zt) obeys (t f')'=z^2 t f, f(0)=1, f'(0)=0,f(1)=0. Integration against conjugate f gives z^2 integral_0^1 t|f|^2=-integral_0^1 t|f'|^2<0. Thus z is purely imaginary. The ordinary regular framing exclusions remove finitely many s values; Re s!=0 can also be imposed wherever that first-cut frame is legitimately varied. In particular on the legitimate real interior first-cut slice A_cut=exp(2pi i alpha), 0<alpha<1, one has s=exp(-2pi i alpha)-1 and Re s=cos(2pi alpha)-1<0. The local nonvanishing condition is therefore automatic on that slice, after its other regular exclusions. This is not a proof that an arbitrary selected global frame path reaches every required box in the 200 regime. The j=0 node is the exact resonance r=infinity, not an additional finite rho value. No uniform result in growing j or across all eight regimes is claimed. In particular 202 leaves a nontrivial whole boundary polynomial in T; it does not reduce to the last term in (10). ## 5. The paired small-second-clock endpoint The 002 regime has an equally direct original-source proof; it does not use an unrecorded interchange of the two physical legs. Let V=kappa_N/N^2, U=U_N, E_N^0=product_(j<m)(V-Q^j), K_N^0=kappa_N sin^2(pi mu)(1-U_N)/pi^2, (16) where kappa_N,U_N lie in fixed compact subsets of C*. Then H_m^1(U,V)/E_N^0=Bessel(K_N^0)+O(N^-1). (17) The EXACT ratio of its kth Newton term to E_N^0 is c_k V^k product_(j<k)(U-Q^j) /product_(j=m-k)^(m-1)(V-Q^j). (18) The denominator product differs from (-1)^k Q^[mk-k(k+1)/2] by a relative O(k/N^2), uniformly for k<=m. Together with the same Gaussian bound as before, this gives C^k/(k!)^2 domination for EVERY k. Its fixed-k limit is [kappa_N sin^2(pi mu)(U_N-1)/pi^2]^k/(k!)^2. The product-error argument in section 3, including absolute comparison when U_N=1, proves the uniform O(N^-1) remainder. Both the exact phase and the full endpoint product are retained in (16),(18). For a genuine 002 disk with first puncture A=-J write Q0=epsilon[[1,b],[0,1]], Q1=AQ0 and Q2=BQ1. The complete trace relation gives B21=4. Substitution into (1),(6) now gives U0=(1+b s)/(1+(b+1)s), kappa=s(1+(b+1)s)/(4rho^2), K^0=sin^2(pi mu)s^2/(4pi^2rho^2). (19) Thus the same fixed-Fourier I0 factor and its legitimate real first-cut nonvanishing apply. The exact physical argument shifts q_N^-1 change U0,kappa by the permitted O(N^-1); the actual endpoint product is still kept. This proves paired 200/002 models, not the unproved reduction of 022/220 or 202 to either one. ## 6. The mixed 202 boundary retains a whole positive polynomial Put V=T/U and define the exact boundary polynomial A_b(T)=(-1)^b Q^[b(b-1)/2] P_b(QT), P_b(w)=sum_(k=0)^b beta(b,k)^2 w^k, beta(b,k)=s_b/[s_k s_(b-k)]. (20) Termwise in (9), A_b is the limit as U tends to infinity with T fixed. For the actual small channel a<=floor((N-1)/2), P_a is precisely the two-binomial polynomial Q_a^(a,a) in the [proved negative-root theorem](actual_q_hahn_negative_root_source_polynomial.md). Its roots are negative real and simple. Retain this whole polynomial; it is not a replacement by its largest coefficient. If U=N^2 kappa with kappa in a fixed compact subset of C*, and T in a fixed compact subset of C minus (-infinity,0], then H_a^1(U,T/U)=A_a(T)(1+O(N^-1)), (21) uniformly in the actual discrete a. There is no lower bound on the distance of a/N from zero needed for this statement. For the ACTUAL large channel m=d-a, the exact root partner identity gives H_m^1(U,T/U)=A_a(T) product_(r=a)^(m-1)(T-Q^r)(1+O(N^-1)). (22) The forced unit-arc factors in (22) are displayed, including their zeros. At such a zero both sides are zero exactly. No generic normal is inferred by differentiating this root collision identity. Here is a uniform relative proof, including complex cancellation. After taking out its exact phase, H_a is sum_(k=0)^a beta(a,k)^2(QT)^k product_(r<k)(1-Q^r/U) product_(r<a-k)(1-(T/U)Q^-r). (23) Expand BOTH correction products by the finite quantum binomial identity, proved by multiplying their linear factors. The term of degree i in the first is a polynomial in Q^k proportional to U^-i product_(r<i)(1-Q^(k-r))/(Q;Q)_i; the degree-j term in the second is proportional to (T/U)^j product_(r<j)(1-Q^(-a+k+r)) /(Q^-1;Q^-1)_j. (24) The omitted factors in (24) have modulus one. These identities hold also when i>k or j>a-k: the corresponding numerator contains zero. Therefore expanding (24) gives an EXACT finite linear combination of A_a(Q^hT), with 0<=h<=i+j. Since i,j<=a<N/2, the sum of absolute coefficients of this combination is at most (C/N)^(i+j)/(i!j!). (25) Indeed |(Q;Q)_i|>=(c/N)^i i!, and each numerator polynomial in Q^k has coefficient sum at most 2^i; the second factor is identical. The i=j=0 term is exactly A_a(T). Write P_a(w)=C_a product_l(w+rho_l), rho_l>0. On the indicated compact T domain, w=QT remains a fixed distance in angle from the negative ray for large N. For 0<=h<=cN, choose c small enough so the rotation from QT to Q^(h+1)T remains in this domain. The bound |w P_a'(w)/P_a(w)|<=C a then gives |A_a(Q^hT)/A_a(T)|<=exp(C h). For EVERY other h one still has the crude bound exp(CN), by applying (|w|+rho)/|w+rho|<=C to each root. Sum (25) first over 1<=i+j<=cN; the exp(C h) factor leaves O(N^-1). For i+j>cN, the factorial tail in (25), even multiplied by exp(CN), is smaller than every inverse power of N. This proves (21) without replacing a complex sum by its positive envelope. The original root identity H_m=H_a product_(r=a)^(m-1)(T-Q^r) proves (22). For the ACTUAL right-angled matching-polyhedron source, the 202 condition gives a useful geometric certificate: T_infinity is POSITIVE. Use precisely the literal white-reflection prefixes proved in [the original cut dictionary](actual_right_angled_selected_framing_obstruction.md), section 3: Q_i=r_(F_i)r_(F_ref). The exterior first-slot reference white face F_ref contains the fixed point p of the original marked main meridian. The 202 middle prefix is upper triangular and fixes p. Thus r_(F_1)r_(F_ref)(p)=p and r_(F_ref)(p)=p force r_(F_1)(p)=p. In other words p lies on the MIDDLE white circle. This is a consequence of the actual common prefix, not a new local framing choice. In the recorded disk coordinate eta that circle has diameter [0,1]. Its puncture lifts and product are A=-[[1,0],[2,1]], B=-[[3,-2],[2,-1]], P=BA=-[[1,2],[0,1]]. (26) Writing eta0 for p and conjugating by [[0,-1],[1,-eta0]] sends p to infinity. Direct multiplication gives A21=-2 eta0^2 and B21=-2(eta0-1)^2. Since Q1 is upper triangular, Q0=A^-1 Q1 and Q2=B Q1 have leading lower-left ratio T_infinity=-A21/B21=-eta0^2/(eta0-1)^2>0. (27) Indeed eta0/(eta0-1) is purely imaginary on that circle. The two outer prefixes are genuinely quadratic, so eta0 is neither 0 nor 1; the positive value is finite and nonzero. Therefore the actual T=T_infinity+O(1/N) at r=N rho lies in a fixed compact subset of the domain of (21). This applies with every retained half twist, since the proved outside white-reflection prefixes are unchanged. The certificate requires this actual right-angled cut and its marked first-slot reference. It is not asserted for arbitrary routed 202 crossings lacking that dictionary. No basing or reference meridian is changed. The 022/220 boundary polynomials still require their separate source treatment, and no global contributing cycle follows from (27). The full matched source still needs its original boundary current, remaining factors, normal extraction and selected relative cycle. The local nonzero Bessel factor proves none of their noncancellation. Focused audit: [original coefficients, marked prefix signs and boundary packets](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_resonant_hard_edge.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_q_hahn_resonant_hard_edge_results.json). It checks 9 exact geometric identities, all 8 incidence patterns, 72 literal-source comparisons, 72 endpoint packets, 24 mixed-boundary identities and 24 complex relative 202 packets. These are focused checks of the proof, not a global-period experiment. The root-value results do not imply a generic-normal or global-cycle statement.

title: The actual q-Hahn column selects a complex leading action
text: # The actual q-Hahn column selects a complex leading action 30 October 2026. The negative-root theorem gives an asymptotic for the ACTUAL local Fourier sum, including its cancellation. The normalized logarithm converges on the entire slit plane to the analytic continuation of its positive real variational action. In the right half-plane this selects a nondegenerate internal saddle with its original logarithms. This is a local leading-order theorem at both level parities. It does not give a complete amplitude expansion, a uniform generic-q normal, or a noncancellation theorem for the assembled plat source. ## 1. The exact finite polynomial and its logarithm Use the original coefficients of the [phase compiler](actual_augmented_plat_phase_compiler.md): P_N(w)=sum_a E(t_N,j_N,u_N,a) w^a, E(t,j,u,a)=beta(j,a) beta(u,a) beta(t-u,j-a)/beta(t,j), a0_N=max(0,u_N-t_N+j_N), a1_N=min(j_N,u_N). Here 0<=j_N<=t_N<N and 0<=u_N<=t_N. Every beta is the positive sine binomial at theta=pi/N. No fitted scalar or knot value enters this definition. The [negative-root theorem](actual_q_hahn_negative_root_source_polynomial.md) proves the exact factorization P_N(w)/P_N(1)=w^a0_N product_(r=1)^(a1_N-a0_N) (w+rho_(N,r))/(1+rho_(N,r)), rho_(N,r)>0. (1) Consequently on Omega=C minus (-infinity,0] the actual polynomial has a unique holomorphic logarithm that is real at w=1. Define L_N(w)=Log(P_N(w))/N. (2) This is a specified logarithm, not the principal argument of a possibly many-times-wound numerical value. Its real part is always log|P_N(w)|/N, independent of that qualification. ## 2. The real variational problem is strict Suppose (t_N,j_N,u_N)/N -> (tau,xi,upsilon), 0<xi<tau<1, 0<upsilon<tau. (3) Set a0=max(0,upsilon-tau+xi), a1=min(xi,upsilon), and use J(s)=integral_0^s log(2 sin(pi y))dy, B(v,a)=J(v)-J(a)-J(v-a), Ecal(alpha)=B(xi,alpha)+B(upsilon,alpha) +B(tau-upsilon,xi-alpha)-B(tau,xi). The interval (a0,a1) is nonempty. For every real w>0 the function Ecal(alpha)+alpha log w has a unique interior maximum, denoted alpha(w), and write its value as psi(w). Its derivative is Ecal'(alpha)=log[sin^2(pi(xi-alpha)) sin(pi(upsilon-alpha)) / (sin^2(pi alpha) sin(pi(tau-upsilon-xi+alpha)))]. The derivative tends to +infinity at a0 and -infinity at a1. Its second derivative is strictly negative: Ecal''=-pi{2[cot(pi(xi-alpha))+cot(pi alpha)] +cot(pi(upsilon-alpha)) +cot(pi(tau-upsilon-xi+alpha))}<0. (4) For the sign, the first paired arguments sum to pi xi in (0,pi); the second pair sums to pi(tau-xi) in (0,pi). Apply cot A+cot B=sin(A+B)/(sin A sin B). All displayed individual arguments lie in (0,pi) on the support interior. Uniform sine-factorial estimates give log E(t_N,j_N,u_N,a)=N Ecal_N(a/N)+O(log N), over the ENTIRE finite support; Ecal_N uses the actual scaled parameters. The support is an interval of the full integer lattice. An upper bound by its largest term and a lower bound by a nearest lattice point to the unique maximizer therefore prove L_N(w) -> psi(w), w>0. (5) The argument is uniform when (3) ranges over a compact subset of its strict domain and w ranges over a compact positive interval. Factorial endpoints are included in the upper bound; none is silently removed before taking the maximum. ## 3. Negative roots prove the complex limit For each compact K in Omega, sup_(w in K,rho>=0) |Log((w+rho)/(1+rho))| < infinity. (6) Indeed (w+rho)/(1+rho) is on the segment between w and 1. Its modulus stays bounded above and away from zero uniformly on K, and its argument stays on the single branch between Arg w and zero. Equivalently compactify rho by rho/(1+rho) in [0,1]. The same bound applies to Log w. Since a1_N<N, (1) implies that L_N(w)-L_N(1) is locally uniformly bounded on Omega. Equation (5) bounds L_N(1). Cauchy estimates and subsequence compactness now give holomorphic subsequential limits, uniformly on compact subsets. All such limits agree on the positive real axis by (5); the identity theorem makes them identical on the connected slit plane. Thus the WHOLE sequence converges: L_N(w) -> psi_hol(w), locally uniformly on Omega. (7) All complex derivatives converge locally uniformly as well. This proves existence and uniqueness of the analytic continuation in (7), instead of assuming that an arbitrary algebraic saddle has that role. The same subsequence argument proves uniformity for compact strict parameter families in (3): any proposed failure has a convergent parameter subsequence, to which the preceding proof applies. Continuity of psi_hol in those parameters follows by the same compactness and positive-axis uniqueness argument. Only elementary compactness for holomorphic functions is used here: Cauchy estimates give equicontinuity on a compact exhaustion; successive subsequences converge there, and the real-axis values determine their unique holomorphic limit. No contour replacement of the finite source or unproved saddle coefficient is inserted. ## 4. A positive root measure fixes the branch Put alpha_hol(w)=w psi_hol'(w). Differentiating (1) yields w L_N'(w)=a0_N/N+(1/N)sum_r w/(w+rho_(N,r)). (8) The measures (1/N)sum_r delta_rho have total mass tending to a1-a0. Compactify their domain by adjoining zero and infinity. Any weak limit mu obeys alpha_hol(w)=a0+integral w/(w+rho) dmu(rho). (9) For real w, the envelope derivative of the strict maximum gives alpha_hol(w)=alpha(w). The barrier equation shows alpha(w)->a0 as w decreases to zero and alpha(w)->a1 as w increases to infinity. Thus mu has no mass at zero or infinity and has total mass a1-a0 on (0,infinity). Formula (9), rather than a chosen ordering of quadratic roots, specifies the actual selected branch. For Im w>0 its imaginary part is strictly positive. If additionally Re w>=0 and w!=0, then a0<Re alpha_hol(w)<a1. (10) For (10), each integrand w/(w+rho) has real part strictly between zero and one. At positive real w, alpha_hol is the original real interior maximum. Along the physical first-quadrant arc all four sine arguments in (4) stay nonzero: their imaginary parts are nonzero away from the positive real axis, and their real-axis initial values lie in the support interior. More explicitly, (10) keeps each argument in the vertical strip 0<Re s<1. There Re(sin(pi s))>0, so its logarithm has one analytic branch agreeing with the positive real logarithm. The saddle equation therefore continues there without an arbitrary logarithm reset: Ecal'(alpha_hol(w))+Log w=0. (11) It is nondegenerate throughout that quadrant. In fact alpha_hol'(w)=integral rho/(w+rho)^2 dmu(rho) never vanishes there. For 0<=Arg w<pi/2 the integrands lie in an open angular sector of width less than pi; at Arg w=pi/2 each has strictly negative imaginary part. Their positive integral is nonzero. Differentiating (11) gives Ecal''(alpha_hol(w))=-1/[w alpha_hol'(w)] !=0. (12) Thus on the physical arc psi_hol is exactly the continued critical value Ecal(alpha_hol)+alpha_hol Log w, with its positive-axis normalization. This conclusion concerns the leading logarithm. It does not by itself compute a Gaussian prefactor or an error O(1/N). ## 5. Consequence for every actual complete-circle column On a complete-circle channel, the exact column is f_(u_N)(c_(j_N))=(-1)^u_N q^[-(j_N+1)u_N] P_N(q^delta_N), delta_N=t_N+j_N-(N-1). If (3) holds and xi<=1/2, tau+xi>=1, then q^delta_N -> w_star=exp[pi i(tau+xi-1)], 0<=Arg w_star<=pi/2. Equation (7) supplies the actual, cancellation-sensitive limit lim_N (1/N)log|f_(u_N)(c_(j_N))| =Re psi_hol(w_star). (13) Both level parities and all composite levels are included. The explicit unit prefactor gives the unwrapped leading complex phase psi_hol(w_star)+pi i(upsilon-xi upsilon) in the compiler's convention. At the folded endpoint xi=1/2 this selects the actual local branch of its previously derived quadratic. The high physical degree block uses its already proved exact index translation, so (13) applies there in those translated variables too. For comparison, negative roots give the finite bound cos(phi/2)^(a1_N-a0_N) P_N(1) <= |P_N(exp(i phi))| <= P_N(1), |phi|<pi. (14) The lower factor can be EXPONENTIAL in N. It is not a polynomial normalization loss. Formula (13) determines that cancellation rate through the selected analytic action instead of dropping it. This does not yet control cancellations among different magnetic or channel states in a whole plat, the mixed-color aliases, the original generic first normals, or the selected global geometric period. Those remain necessary for the general long-filling volume equality. Audit: [actual Fourier columns and selected complex action](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_selected_complex_action.py). The analytic proof above is uniform; finite numerical checks only verify the formula conventions and the selected continuation. The selected-complex-action theorem retains its actual logarithmic sheets and the stated global and amplitude limitations. The real magnetic-parameter theorem does not imply a complex global-source packet.

title: Polynomial cost of the actual small-channel generic normals
status: Polynomial fixed generic derivatives; small channels
text: # Polynomial cost of the actual small-channel generic normals 30 October 2026. This note concerns the original generic highest-weight N-1 columns, including the factors that simplify only at the root of unity. On compact subsets of the joint central wedge, every fixed generic-q derivative of a small-channel column has at most polynomial cost relative to that column's root value. The estimate includes the folded small channel and both parities. It does not bound the paired large-channel derivative, the confluent spectral normal formed from both channels, or the whole marked source. ## 1. The exact generic deformation Fix N>=3, d=N-1 and q0=exp(pi i/N). Let q vary near q0; put Q=q^2, B=Q^(-N), A=B^(-1), x=q^d, t=u+v, U=Q^u, V=Q^v, T=UV, s=q^t, D_j(T)=product_(r=0)^(j-1)(T-Q^r). All complex powers use log(q)=pi i/N+epsilon. Gaussian binomials and Pochhammer products below have base Q. Define H_j^B(U,V)=sum_(a=0)^j (-1)^a B^a Q^[a(a+1)/2] [j choose a]_Q (B Q^(j-a+1);Q)_a/(BQ;Q)_a V^a product_(r<a)(U-Q^r) product_(r<j-a)(V-Q^r), C_j(q;t,u)=x^u H_j^B(U,V)/D_j(T), S_j^B(U,T)=U^j H_j^B(U,T/U). (1) This is the actual generic column in [the mixed compiler](actual_mixed_augmented_plat_compiler.md), section 2, at physical t,u. It also specifies a finite rational continuation for complex t,u. To check the source before differentiating, its highest-vector ratio is exactly R_(j,a)=(Q^(N-j);Q)_a/(Q^(N-a);Q)_a =Q^[a(a-j)] (B Q^(j-a+1);Q)_a/(BQ;Q)_a. (2) Converting the three Gaussian binomials in that compiler into finite Newton products gives (1). In particular the additional factor is B^a times the displayed Pochhammer ratio. Merely inserting a power of -q^(-N) into the root-only squared-binomial formula would give the wrong generic source and the wrong first derivative. The exact leading scalar is S_j^B(0,T)=T^j K_j, K_j=(B^2 Q^(j+1);Q)_j/(BQ;Q)_j. (3) Here is an elementary proof of the finite identity used in (3). For generic a,c,Q and integer n>=0, sum_(k=0)^n (Q^(-n);Q)_k (a;Q)_k / [(Q;Q)_k(c;Q)_k] (c Q^n/a)^k =(c/a;Q)_n/(c;Q)_n. (4) Multiply both sides by a^n(c;Q)_n. Each side is a polynomial of degree at most n in a. At a=c Q^m, 0<=m<n, the quotient (a;Q)_k/(c;Q)_k=(c Q^k;Q)_m/(c;Q)_m is a polynomial in Q^k of degree m. For each of its powers Q^(rk), r<=m, the finite binomial sum on the left is (Q^(r-m);Q)_n=0. Thus the left polynomial has all the n roots of product_(r<n)(a-cQ^r). Its constant term, from k=n alone, is (-1)^n c^n Q^[n(n-1)/2], fixing the multiplier to 1. This proves (4) as a rational identity. Taking n=j, a=B^(-1)Q^(-j), c=BQ gives (3), after converting (Q^(-j);Q)_a to the Gaussian binomial. No asymptotic identity is used here. ## 2. The generic Casimir polynomial and its three-term recurrence The exact equation for S=S_j^B is Q^(-j)(QU-A)(U-T) S(QU,T) +Q^j(BQT-U)(1-U) S(U/Q,T) +[(1+A)U+QT(1+B)U-(1+Q)U^2 -T(AQ^(-j)+BQ^(j+1))]S(U,T)=0. (5) It follows from the actual generic coproduct Casimir, whose column eigenvalue is q^(2N-1-2j)+q^(-2N+1+2j). Alternatively, one can verify its extension from physical columns by exactly the finite degree argument used for the root equation in [the joint determinant note](actual_q_hahn_joint_accretive_determinant.md). The residual has degree at most j+1 in U: the top degree cancels; its constant coefficient also vanishes. At each original complete slice t=d-j,...,d, its original t+1 column values and U=0 force the whole U polynomial to vanish. The residual has degree at most j+1 in T. These j+1 slices, together with T=0, force its vanishing identically. At T=0 use S(U,0)=(-1)^j Q^[j(j-1)/2]U^j; the residual cancels directly. This proves (5) in a neighborhood of the actual root, where all these finite source columns and distinct slice values are defined. Let R_n(z) be the monic reverse polynomial obtained from (1): R_n(z)=z^n S_n^B(s/z,s^2)/(s^(2n)K_n). Equation (5) says L R_n=Lambda_n R_n for the triangular operator L z^n=Lambda_n z^n+b_n z^(n-1)+d_n z^(n-2), Lambda_n=AQ^(-n)+BQ^(n+1), b_n=[(1+A)+Qs^2(1+B)-Q^(-n)(Qs^2+A) -Q^n(BQs^2+1)]/s, d_n=Q^(1-n)+Q^n-1-Q. (6) Terms with negative powers are absent, since b_0=d_0=d_1=0. Write the two coefficients below the leading one as u_n,v_n. Their exact expressions are u_0=0, u_n=b_n/(Lambda_n-Lambda_(n-1)), n>=1, v_0=v_1=0, v_n=(b_(n-1)u_n+d_n)/(Lambda_n-Lambda_(n-2)), n>=2.
