For 0<=n<j, put alpha_n=u_(n+1)-u_n, beta_n=v_(n+1)-v_n-alpha_n u_n (n>=1). Then exactly R_0=1, R_1=z+alpha_0, R_(n+1)=(z+alpha_n)R_n+beta_n R_(n-1). (7) For completeness, a finite moment argument rules out extra lower terms in (7). Set mu_0=1, mu_(-1)=0 and impose (BQ^(r+1)-A)mu_r +[(Qs^2+A)-(BQs^2+1)Q^r]mu_(r-1)/s +(Q^r-Q)mu_(r-2)=0, 1<=r<=2j-1. (8) The difference of the two monomial pairings for L factors as (Q^n-Q^m)Q^(-n-m) times (8) at r=m+n. Thus L is symmetric for this finite moment functional. Its eigenvalues of degrees 0,...,j are distinct near the root. The usual finite orthogonality argument now kills the terms below R_(n-1) in zR_n-R_(n+1); the top two coefficients give (7). This argument can first be made at generic s, where the preceding norms do not vanish: the norm recursion is h_n=-beta_n h_(n-1). At B=1 the beta_n are the nonzero polynomials in c displayed below, so generic nonvanishing follows inductively. Rational continuation then proves (7) also when a particular beta_n vanishes. No positive generic moment functional is assumed. Combining (1),(3) gives the exact normalized source C_j=x^u q^(jt) K_j R_j(q^t/U)/D_j(Q^t). (9) All the generic coefficients in this section retain B=Q^(-N). Equation (7) is not a deformation chosen after specialization. ## 3. A uniformly controlled generic neighborhood Let W be the joint wedge 1/2<Re(t/N)<1, |2Re(u/N)-Re(t/N)|<1/2. For every compact K contained in W there are constants c_K,C_K>0, independent of N and 0<=j<=floor((N-1)/2), such that |C_j(q0 exp(epsilon);t,u)/C_j(q0;t,u)|<=C_K whenever |epsilon|<=c_K N^(-8), (t/N,u/N) in K. (10) In particular the denominator on the left is nonzero. The power 8 is a convenient conservative bound; no optimal power is claimed. Here are explicit estimates proving the assertion. At epsilon=0, put theta=pi/N, c=-cos((t+1)theta), z=q0^(t-2u). On a fixed K, Re c and Re z have positive lower bounds for all sufficiently large N. The root recurrence (7) is alpha_n=c/[cos(n theta)cos((n+1)theta)], beta_n=Bcal_n[cos^2(n theta)-c^2], Bcal_n=sin^2(n theta)/[cos^2(n theta) sin((2n-1)theta)sin((2n+1)theta)]. Thus its determinant is M_0=zI+cD+Kskew, with the actual positive D and real skew matrix Kskew in the joint determinant note. Accretivity gives ||M_0^(-1)||<=1/Re z, uniformly in the channel, including the fold. Construct the generic tridiagonal matrix M_epsilon with diagonal z(q)+alpha_n(q). Freeze its upper entries to their ROOT values r_n=sqrt(Bcal_n)[c+cos(n theta)], 1<=n<j, and use lower entries -beta_n(q)/r_n. Its determinant is R_j by (7), and at epsilon=0 it is exactly M_0. There is no square-root choice for the generic beta_n. Since sqrt(Bcal_n)>=1/2 and Re c is uniformly positive, |r_n| is bounded below independently of N. The only spectral differences in (6),(7) factor as Lambda_n-Lambda_(n-1) =(1-Q)A Q^(-n)(1-B^2 Q^(2n)), Lambda_n-Lambda_(n-2) =(1-Q^2)A Q^(-n)(1-B^2 Q^(2n-1)). (11) At the root their nonzero factors give lower bounds c/N^2 for all required n<=j. All elementary exponents have size O(N), so these bounds persist in a disk |epsilon|<=c N^(-3). On a smaller such disk, direct differentiation of (6),(7) gives uniformly |u_n|=O(N^2), |u_n'|=O(N^5), |v_n|=O(N^4), |v_n'|=O(N^7), |alpha_n'|=O(N^5), |beta_n'|=O(N^7). (12) Here primes mean d/d epsilon. The coefficients b_n,d_n,Lambda_n are O(1), with derivatives O(N); (12) follows by the quotient rule and (11). Consequently the tridiagonal operator norm satisfies ||M_epsilon-M_0||<=C_K N^7 |epsilon|. On the disk in (10), ||M_0^(-1)(M_epsilon-M_0)||<=C_K c_K/N. Choose c_K small. The determinant ratio is bounded by (1+C_K c_K/N)^j, and hence uniformly bounded; it is also nonzero. The remaining scalar factors in (9) have controlled ratios on the same disk. The exponents of x^u q^(jt) have size O(N^2). Each root factor of K_j has size at least c/N, its derivative is O(N), and there are O(N) factors; thus |(log K_j)'|=O(N^3). The factors of D_j(Q^t) are separated uniformly from zero on K, so its logarithmic derivative is O(N^2). Integration over the N^(-8) disk bounds all these scalar ratios. This proves (10). Finitely many remaining N can be absorbed by changing constants; j=0 follows immediately from C_0=x^u. ## 4. Consequence for actual generic derivatives, and its limit Cauchy's estimate applied to the exact source in (10) gives, for every fixed integer m>=0, |(q d/dq)^m C_j(q0;t,u)| <=C_(K,m) N^(8m) |C_j(q0;t,u)|. (13) The derivative holds t,u,N fixed, exactly as the original generic compiler does. At physical integer t,u it is its actual generic normal; at complex t,u it is the derivative of the finite source continuation (1). Combining (13) with the proved joint root-value amplitude preserves its leading exponential action, as an upper bound, for these fixed-order small-channel derivatives. The mixed compiler's confluent column is proportional to D C_j-D C_(N-1-j). Except at the simple folded endpoint, its second term is a LARGE channel. In that channel K_l vanishes at the root and the monic recurrence crosses resonant eigenvalue differences. The argument above does not apply. In particular (13) is not a bound for that difference, its spectral derivative, a complete mixed kernel, or a generic normal of the whole pointed invariant. Focused audit: [actual generic values and normals](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_small_channel_generic_normals.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_q_hahn_small_channel_generic_normals_results.json). It passed 1,304 original generic value-and-derivative comparisons, 216 generic determinant identities, 216 generic Casimir identities, 216 Vandermonde value-and-derivative identities, and 1,041 original root-normal comparisons in exact finite-field dual arithmetic. At 100 digits, 48 nonphysical generic comparisons and 24 original root-normal comparisons passed; 96 points on the stated polynomial disk were also sampled. The disk samples are regressions, not the proof of uniform control. The result is restricted to the stated small-channel domain and fixed-t,u Cauchy derivative convention. The paired large channel is excluded.

title: A uniform nonzero complex amplitude for the actual q-Hahn column
text: # A uniform nonzero complex amplitude for the actual q-Hahn column Subsequent extension: [joint pair-degree and magnetic amplitudes](actual_q_hahn_joint_complex_amplitude.md) are now proved on a central complex domain, using the original finite kernel and an exact accretive determinant. The present theorem and its proof retain the real-parameter hypothesis stated below. 30 October 2026. The original finite q-Hahn polynomial has a full leading asymptotic, with a specified nonzero amplitude and relative error O(1/N), uniformly on compact subsets of the right half-plane. Its magnetic parameters are the ACTUAL scaled integers, varying in a compact strict REAL parameter set. No rate of convergence of those parameters is assumed. The proof starts with the previously proved actual logarithmic limit, then uses the exact finite difference equation to improve its error. A positive real Gaussian sum fixes the actual multiplicative constant. Thus the transport equation below describes the original polynomial, not merely a formal solution with an unspecified connection coefficient. This theorem does not interpolate the discrete magnetic parameters holomorphically, take a generic-q first normal, or control the assembled global magnetic/channel sum. ## 1. Original finite source and theorem Let 0<=j<=t<N, 0<=u<=t, v=t-u, theta=pi/N, and s_n=product_(r=1)^n 2 sin(r theta), beta(n,a)=s_n/(s_a s_(n-a)), E_a=beta(j,a) beta(u,a) beta(v,j-a)/beta(t,j), P_N(w)=sum_(a=a0)^a1 E_a w^a, a0=max(0,j-v), a1=min(j,u). (1) These are exactly the coefficients of the [original complete-circle phase compiler](actual_augmented_plat_phase_compiler.md). Put lambda_N=(tau,xi,upsilon)=(t/N,j/N,u/N), D={0<xi<tau<1, 0<upsilon<tau}. All uniform statements below take lambda_N in a fixed compact subset K of D. In particular all saddles at w=1 stay a uniform distance from the factorial boundaries, even when the two descriptions of a support endpoint exchange at upsilon=xi or upsilon+xi=tau. Use the original energy J(s)=integral_0^s log(2 sin(pi y))dy, Bcal(b,a)=J(b)-J(a)-J(b-a), Ecal_lambda(alpha)=Bcal(xi,alpha)+Bcal(upsilon,alpha) +Bcal(tau-upsilon,xi-alpha)-Bcal(tau,xi). For positive real w, let alpha_lambda(w) be the unique interior maximum of Ecal_lambda(alpha)+alpha log w. The [selected complex action theorem](actual_q_hahn_selected_complex_action.md) continues both alpha and its critical value psi_lambda holomorphically to Re w>0, with psi_lambda(w)=Ecal_lambda(alpha_lambda(w)) +alpha_lambda(w) Log w, w psi_lambda'(w)=alpha_lambda(w). (2) All logarithms continue from their real values at w=1. Define, with derivatives in the variable s, A_lambda(s)=sin^2(pi s) sin(pi(tau-upsilon-xi+s)), B_lambda(s)=sin^2(pi(xi-s)) sin(pi(upsilon-s)), F_lambda(s,w)=A_lambda(s)-w B_lambda(s), C_lambda=(sin(pi xi)/2) sqrt[sin(pi upsilon) sin(pi(tau-upsilon)) sin(pi(tau-xi))/sin(pi tau)]. The root selected in (2) satisfies F_lambda(alpha,w)=0. Define Acal_lambda(w)=sqrt(2 pi) C_lambda /sqrt[B_lambda(alpha_lambda(w)) F_(lambda,s)(alpha_lambda(w),w)]. (3) The square root is the holomorphic continuation of its positive real value at w=1. It is well-defined and never zero on Re w>0. **Theorem.** Uniformly for lambda_N in K and w in any compact subset of Re w>0, P_N(w)=N^(-1/2) Acal_(lambda_N)(w) exp[N psi_(lambda_N)(w)] (1+O(N^(-1))). (4) The relative error is holomorphic in w. On smaller compact subsets each fixed number of its w derivatives is O(N^(-1)) as well. Formula (4) uses the actual lambda_N, not an arbitrarily chosen limiting triple. Replacing lambda_N by its limit without controlling the displacement would in general change the leading exponential and the amplitude. ## 2. Exact finite difference equation, including endpoints Let D_w=w d/dw and h=1/N. The coefficient ratio in (1) gives the exact identity sin^2(pi h D_w) sin(pi h(D_w+v-j)) P_N(w) =w sin^2(pi h(j-D_w)) sin(pi h(u-D_w)) P_N(w). (5) For every supported a, its coefficient equation is sin^2(a theta) sin((v-j+a)theta) E_a =sin^2((j-a+1)theta) sin((u-a+1)theta) E_(a-1). At the lower endpoint either a=0 or v-j+a=0. At the first integer above the upper endpoint either j-a+1=0 or u-a+1=0. Thus the zero coefficients outside the support satisfy the SAME equation; there is no endpoint source term in (5). In functional calculus notation, [A_lambda(h D_w)-w B_lambda(h D_w)]P_N=0. (6) Every sine product in (6) is a finite linear combination of the four shifts w -> exp(i pi k h)w, k=-3,-1,1,3. In particular (6) is an exact finite-shift identity, not an infinite differential expansion. ## 3. Uniform simplicity and the actual derivative bootstrap The [negative-root theorem](actual_q_hahn_negative_root_source_polynomial.md) gives positive rho_r and P_N(w)/P_N(1)=w^a0 product_r (w+rho_r)/(1+rho_r). It fixes a holomorphic Log P_N real at w=1. Put G_N(w)=Log P_N(w)/N, a_N(w)=D_w G_N(w). The actual leading-limit theorem proves a_N-alpha_(lambda_N) -> 0 (7) uniformly on larger compact subsets of the right half-plane, also when the real parameters vary in K. Fixed w derivatives converge there too. Alternatively the explicit expression a_N=a0/N+(1/N)sum_r w/(w+rho_r) directly bounds every fixed derivative on those compact subsets. These bounds are independent of the positions of the negative roots. For completeness, the selected branch is uniformly simple here. Its positive limiting root measure gives alpha_lambda'(w)=integral rho/(w+rho)^2 dmu_lambda(rho). For Re w>0 the integrands lie in an angular sector of width less than pi, so their positive integral cannot vanish. Its measure has positive mass strictly between zero and infinity. The support-strip property of alpha makes A and B nonzero. Differentiating its saddle equation gives F_s(alpha,w) D_w alpha=w B(alpha)=A(alpha), Ecal''(alpha)=-F_s(alpha,w)/A(alpha). (8) Consequently F_s is nonzero. Continuity in the real parameters and compactness make its modulus bounded away from zero on each of the sets used below. Complex conjugation supplies the same statement in the lower right quadrant. Fix nested compact neighborhoods within Re w>0. For each fixed c=i pi k, k in {-3,-1,1,3}, all small shifts stay in the larger one. Taylor's theorem along the short logarithmic segment, using the uniform derivative bounds, yields P_N(exp(c h)w)/P_N(w) =exp(c a_N(w)) [1+(h c^2/2)D_w a_N(w)+O(h^2)]. (9) Indeed the exponent before exponentiating is N[G_N(exp(c h)w)-G_N(w)] =c a_N+(h c^2/2)D_w a_N+O(h^2). This is an estimate for the actual polynomial ratios. Inserting all four shifts into (6), with their exact sine coefficients, proves 0=F(a_N,w)+(h/2)(D_w a_N) F_ss(a_N,w)+O(h^2). (10) Equation (7) and the uniformly simple zero first imply a_N-alpha=O(h). To justify this improvement, use the uniform expansion F(a_N,w)=F_s(alpha,w)(a_N-alpha)+O(|a_N-alpha|^2), absorb the quadratic term using (7), and use boundedness of D_w a_N in (10). Cauchy's estimate on a slightly larger compact set then gives D_w a_N-D_w alpha=O(h) and the analogous estimate for every fixed further derivative. Substitution back into (10) now proves the sharper actual estimate a_N=alpha-(h/2)(D_w alpha)F_ss(alpha,w)/F_s(alpha,w) +O(h^2). (11) The order h^2 remainder is justified by the first improvement and Cauchy, not assumed as a WKB ansatz. Differentiating (3) and using (8) gives the exact transport identity D_w log Acal_lambda =-(1/2)(D_w alpha)F_ss(alpha,w)/F_s(alpha,w). (12) For example, differentiate log(B(alpha)F_s(alpha,w)). Its two extra terms cancel: (B'/B)D_w alpha+w F_sw/F_s =(B'/B)(wB/F_s)-wB'/F_s=0. Thus (11) identifies the logarithmic derivative of the ACTUAL source with the explicit amplitude to error O(h^2). ## 4. The real sum fixes the constant, with arbitrary lattice offset On a compact interior subinterval the sine-factorial estimate is s_n=sqrt[2N sin(pi n/N)] exp[N J(n/N)](1+O(N^(-1))). One elementary derivation subtracts log x from log(2 sin pi x), applies the trapezoidal estimate to the resulting smooth function, and applies the usual integral remainder estimate for log(n!). The errors and their required finite derivatives are uniform away from 0 and 1. Applied to every factor of (1), this gives E_a=N^(-1) C_lambda /sqrt[A_lambda(a/N)B_lambda(a/N)] exp[N Ecal_lambda(a/N)](1+O(N^(-1))). (13) The positive real saddle alpha=alpha_lambda(1) stays uniformly inside the support. Strict concavity and the global factorial O(log N) bound give an exponential loss outside a fixed saddle neighborhood. Inside that neighborhood put z=(a-N alpha)/sqrt N. Taylor expansion of the phase and the smooth prefactor in (13) gives a Gaussian times H(alpha)+N^(-1/2)[H'(alpha)z +H(alpha)Ecal'''(alpha)z^3/6] +O(N^(-1)(1+|z|^8)), with a uniformly integrable Gaussian majorant; one may first restrict |z|<=N^(1/20), whose complementary tails are exponentially small. Here H=C_lambda/sqrt(AB). The term of order N^(-1/2) is ODD. No arithmetic assumption about N alpha is needed. For any shifted grid h_Z(Z+eta), h_Z=N^(-1/2), and a smooth Gaussian times a fixed polynomial f, the centered-cell Taylor formula gives |h_Z sum_(n in Z) f(h_Z(n+eta))-integral_R f| <= (h_Z^2/8) integral_R |f''|. (14) The bound is independent of eta: integrate the Taylor remainder over each cell centered at its grid point, then sum the disjoint cells. The same estimate applies to the odd term, whose integral is zero. Hence the arbitrary fractional saddle offset introduces an error O(N^(-1)), not an uncontrolled O(N^(-1/2)) correction. Gaussian tails allow the finite interval to be replaced by that whole translated grid. The resulting ACTUAL positive sum is P_N(1)=N^(-1/2) [sqrt(2 pi) C_lambda /sqrt(A(alpha)B(alpha)(-Ecal''(alpha)))] exp[N psi_lambda(1)](1+O(N^(-1))). By (8), A(-Ecal'')=F_s, so the bracket is precisely Acal_lambda(1). This proves the real normalization in (4), uniformly in lambda_N. ## 5. Integrating the proved derivative error The function H_N=Log P_N-N psi_(lambda_N)+(1/2)log N-log Acal_(lambda_N) uses the branches fixed at w=1. Sections 3 and 4 prove D_w H_N=O(N^(-1)), H_N(1)=O(N^(-1)). Join 1 to each w in a chosen compact subset of Re w>0 by its straight segment. The union of these segments is a compact set bounded away from zero and the imaginary axis. A slightly larger compact set supplies all the preceding derivative estimates. Integrating H_N' on those bounded-length segments proves H_N=O(N^(-1)) uniformly. Exponentiation proves (4). Cauchy's estimate on nested compact sets then proves the asserted relative derivative bounds. This is where both inputs are essential: negative roots gave the actual leading selection and bounded holomorphic derivatives, while the positive real sum fixed the multiplicative constant left open by the finite difference equation. ## 6. The original physical column and both integer offsets In the complete-circle chamber the exact compiler uses f_u(c_j)=(-1)^u q^[-(j+1)u] P_N(q^delta), q=exp(pi i/N), delta=t+j-(N-1). Let w_star=exp[pi i(tau+xi-1)]. Then q^delta=w_star exp(pi i/N). Keeping both occurrences of +1, formula (4) gives f_u(c_j)=N^(-1/2) Acal_(lambda_N)(w_star) exp[pi i(alpha_(lambda_N)(w_star)-upsilon)] exp{N[psi_(lambda_N)(w_star) +pi i upsilon(1-xi)]} (1+O(N^(-1))). (15) In detail, moving w_star to w_star exp(pi i/N) contributes exp(pi i alpha)(1+O(N^(-1))), while q^[-(j+1)u] contributes the otherwise easily lost factor exp(-pi i upsilon). For actual complete-circle channels xi<=1/2 and tau+xi>=1-1/N. On a fixed strict compact parameter set tau<1, these w_star and their exact shifted values stay in a compact right-half-plane set. Thus (15) holds at both level parities, at the folded endpoint, and at composite levels. The high physical degree block inherits the formula by its already proved exact index translation, with the same transported column convention. The scope is a single ACTUAL local column, with real magnetic indices. Nothing here selects a global magnetic integration cycle, proves cancellation bounds for the assembled plat, or differentiates the root formula in the generic-q normal direction. title: Exact partner reflection of the normalized Racah root value
text: # Exact partner reflection of the normalized Racah root value 29 October 2026. For every supported folded sextuple, the normalized squared Racah VALUE is unchanged under ANY of the sixty-four independent reflections j -> N-1-j. The proof uses the actual generic source normalization, a genuine cyclic turn, a uniform factorial certificate, and residues of channel projectors on a saturated analytic invariant lattice. It does not assume a semisimple root quotient or a named 6j symmetry. All higher normal currents remain present; they are NOT invariant, as an exact first-normal counterexample below shows. ## 1. Statement and the precise metric convention Fix N>=2, D=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N). Start with six folded spins a,b,c,d,e,f in [0,D/2], with all four admissible face sums F=(a+b+e,c+d+e,a+d+f,b+c+f) >= D. (1) Admissible means the ordinary triangle conditions and integer face sums. The original graph channels are INTEGER spins; the same proof allows admissible half-integral spins with the phase stated below. Let Q=(a+b+c+d,a+c+e+f,b+d+e+f). At generic zeta define S=sum_(z=max F)^(min Q) (-1)^z[z+1]! /(product_i[z-F_i]! product_k[Q_k-z]!), Delta_F^2=[F-2x]![F-2y]![F-2z]!/[F+1]!, mathcal W(zeta)^2=[N]^2 S^2 product_faces Delta_F^2. (2) The factorials are symmetric quantum factorials, retained GENERICALLY. For a partner branch replace any subset of the six spins by D-j in these SAME formulas. Every branch of (2) has a finite root limit. For INTEGER spins it is the positive quantity W_N^2=R_N^2 product_faces d_F, R_N=N sum_(max F<=z<=min(Q,2D)) s_(z-D)/(product_i s_(z-F_i) product_k s_(Q_k-z)), d_F=product_(j in face)s_(F-2j)/(N s_(F-D)), s_r=product_(u=1)^r 2sin(pi u/N). (3) Then EXACTLY W_N^2(j_1,...,j_6) =W_N^2(D-j_1,j_2,...,j_6)=... (4) under all sixty-four independent partner choices, at both parities and every composite level. No asymptotic assertion is used. For admissible half-integral spins the generic squared expression has mathcal W(q)^2=(-1)^[2sum_six j] W_N^2. That sign is unchanged by every partner reflection, since its exponent changes by 2D-4j, an even integer. Thus both the signed generic metric value and the positive sine-factorial convention satisfy (4). No positive-square convention is silently extended to half spins. ## 2. The full actual source fixes a reciprocal trace normalization Let A=2a,B=2b,C=2c,D0=2d,E=2e,G=2f be INTEGER highest weights. Use the ACTUAL invariant columns S_E,T_G and inverse source matrix L_(G,E) from [the generic all-port source theorem](actual_general_four_port_single_racah_kernel.md). Write its explicitly proved seven-factorial prefactor as p: L_(G,E)^ABCD=p_abcd(e,f) S. This p includes every actual cup, cyclic sign, monomial and factorial. The reciprocal coefficient is not obtained by squaring p and guessing an ordered norm ratio. Indeed let C_A move the last V_A to the front by its actual snakes, so it multiplies by (-1)^A K_A. It gives C_A S_G^BCDA=T_G^ABCD, C_A T_E^BCDA=S_E^ABCD. (5) For the second equality, the two cyclic moves interchange the two coupled pairs in S_E. Their clock is K_A K_B=K_E, while the internal cup reversal has ratio P_E(E-r)/P_E(r)=(-1)^E zeta^(-E+2r). The monomial cancels K_E, and the total sign is (-1)^(A+B+E)=1 by channel parity. This proves (5) on ALL external colors, not just on a highest corner. It follows that the actual reciprocal matrix is R_(E,G)^ABCD=L_(E,G)^BCDA. (6) The exact source prefactors consequently satisfy p_abcd(e,f) p_bcda(f,e) =[2e+1][2f+1] product_faces Delta_F^2. (7) Here is a uniform own algebraic certificate for (7). In the all-port theorem, put s=(A+B+C+D0)/2, Gmax=min(A+D0,B+C), n=(Gmax-G)/2, t0=s-Gmax and M=(Gmax+G)/2+1. Its finite product V_n can be written V_n=zeta^[n+2n(t0+n)] F_M F_(s+1-n)F_t0 / [F_(G+1)F_(s+1)F_n F_(t0+n)]. (8) Replace every symmetric factorial by zeta^[-r(r-1)/2]F_r/(1-Q)^r in the explicit source prefactor p=chi_E X_E/(b_G J_n S0 V_n). There are FOUR algebraic cases: the two choices of Gmax and the two choices of the cyclic Emax. For all four, literal cancellation gives the following ratio to the right side of (7): nonzero F_r exponents: none, residual zeta exponent:0, residual (1-Q) exponent:0, residual sign exponent: E+G-3A-2B-C-2D0. (9) This last integer is even because E=A+B mod2 and G=B+C mod2. The accompanying certificate represents each F_r by its INDEPENDENT symbolic linear argument in A,B,C,D0,E,G and verifies all four factor-exponent dictionaries identically. Quadratic zeta exponents are expanded as polynomial identities. Thus (9) is a finite uniform factorial proof, not a numerical fit or an assumed orthogonality norm. Let M_abcd=Inv_K(V_A tensor V_B tensor V_C tensor V_D0), over generic meromorphic germs K. On this ACTUAL space let Pi_e^S and Pi_f^T be the generic rank-one channel projectors for the two pairings. By ordinary matrix trace in the source basis, (6),(7) give tr(Pi_e^S Pi_f^T)=R_(E,G)L_(G,E) =[2e+1][2f+1] product_faces Delta_F^2 S^2, mathcal W^2=[N]^2 tr(Pi_e^S Pi_f^T)/ ([2e+1][2f+1]). (10) This is the proper source-normalized, gauge-free trace identity. It uses an ordinary trace on the multiplicity space, not an illicit replacement of the original marked physical row by a quantum trace. The all-port source identities already keep that row and any exterior outside the local recoupling. No original framing or crossing scalar has been canceled in (10). There is a corresponding exact GENERIC diagonal bilinear transport, which fixes the distinction from an incorrectly ordered Clebsch norm. Write L_(G,E)=a_E b_G S with the actual separable source gauges in the all-port theorem, and D_E=Delta_abe^2 Delta_cde^2, D_G=Delta_bcf^2 Delta_daf^2. Equations (6),(7) give M_S(E)=a_E^2/([2e+1]D_E), M_T(G)=[2f+1]D_G/b_G^2, R=M_S^(-1) L^T M_T, L^T M_T L=M_S. (10a) The transpose is bilinear, not a Hermitian adjoint. These generic weights can have zeros, poles and phases at the root, so (10a) does not supply a positive full confluent metric or a bound on its source conditioning. It retains the actual source gauges rather than replacing the reciprocal prefactor by its square. ## 3. Every partner has exactly the needed physical channel collision For one folded face (x,y,z) with x,y,z<=D/2 and x+y+z>=D, any subset of partner flips gives D<=x'+y'+z'<=2D, 0<=y'+z'-x'<=D, and its two cyclic versions. (11) The minimum of the first expression is the folded sum and its maximum is three D minus that sum. The minimum of the second over flips is foldedSum-D, and its maximum is 2D-foldedSum. This proves (11) before any root calculation, including boundary faces. Fix ANY partner branch of all six labels. The ACTUAL generic left channel range is I_S=[|a-b|,a+b] intersect [|c-d|,c+d], step1. (12) Both e and e*=D-e lie in this range by (11). Applying its deficit bound to BOTH values gives max I_S <= D+min(e,e*) < N+min(e,e*). (13) All indices in I_S are nonnegative. The root Casimir eigenvalues are lambda_j(q)=q^(2j+1)+q^(-2j-1). Equality to lambda_e means j=e mod N or j=D-e mod N. Equation (13) excludes EVERY upward alias e+N and e*+N, and there are no downward aliases because 0<=e,e*<=D<N. Thus the complete collision class in the FULL actual range (12) is EXACTLY {e,e*}. The same proof applies to the right range and {f,f*}. The argument retains all generic high channels in (12); it does not truncate a channel range to its folded half. Other eigenvalue clusters can collide too, but none collides with this selected one. ## 4. Saturation makes the residue comparison legitimate Let O be the analytic-germ ring at zeta=q, K its fraction field, and V_A(O),... the ordinary highest-weight modules with the original balanced matrices. Those matrices are holomorphic even for high partners: their entries contain no divided-factorial denominators. The actual generic invariant lattice is Lambda=Inv_K(V_A(K) tensor V_B(K) tensor V_C(K) tensor V_D0(K)) intersect V_A(O) tensor V_B(O) tensor V_C(O) tensor V_D0(O). (14) It is a finite free O module. Indeed it is a saturated submodule of a finite free module over the one-dimensional local analytic DVR; torsion-free finite modules there have an O basis. The generic rank is the already proved channel dimension |I_S|=|I_T|. Each interval Casimir preserves (14): it is an actual holomorphic Hopf intertwiner and preserves generic invariants, so it preserves their intersection with the ambient lattice. Consequently its matrix on Lambda is holomorphic. This is the point that prevents singular generic source frames from being mistaken for a regular root basis. If e!=e*, the eigenvalue gap is a SIMPLE zero: D_logzeta(lambda_e-lambda_e*)|q =2N(q^(2e+1)-q^(-2e-1))!=0. (15) If this factor vanished the node would be -2 and e=e*=D/2. The unique-collision statement of section3 shows that the pair's minimal factor is coprime at q to the factors for all other channels. Finite polynomial Bezout therefore constructs an analytic cluster projector E_e onto the two selected generic eigenlines. Hence Pi_e=E_e (A-lambda_e* I)/(lambda_e-lambda_e*), Pi_e+Pi_e*=E_e, (16) where A is the interval Casimir. Each projector has at most a simple pole on the ACTUAL saturated lattice, and their residues are opposite. No semisimplicity assumption at the root was used. If e=e*=D/2, the same Bezout argument constructs its analytic single-channel projector. The corresponding generic quantum dimension is exactly [2e+1]=[N], which has one simple zero. For a paired e the dimension is a root unit and [2e*+1]|q=-[2e+1]|q. (17) Identical conclusions hold for f and the other interval Casimir. ## 5. Laurent orders prove the full sixty-four value identity Let r be the number of PAIRED selected internal channels among e,f. The preceding saturated-lattice construction gives tr(Pi_e Pi_f)=O(t^-r), t=log(zeta/q). The scalar [N] has a simple zero, and each simple internal channel contributes exactly one [N] to the denominator of (10). Therefore the scalar prefactor in (10) has zero order r. The product has a finite limit, without any deletion of a normal direction. For a paired e, replace Pi_e by Pi_e*=E_e-Pi_e. The coefficient of t^-r in the trace changes sign: E_e is analytic and its product with Pi_f has pole order at most r-1. At the same time the nonzero leading quantum-dimension factor [2e+1] changes sign by (17). The signs cancel in (10). The simple case e=e* is tautological. This proves one internal-edge partner reflection for ANY choice of the other five partner values, including an odd simple f. The f proof is identical. Finally the face/opposite incidence in (2) is invariant under every tetrahedral vertex relabeling, and this group acts transitively on the six edges. Any chosen edge can thus be put in the internal e position of (10). After any previous reflections, (11)--(17) still hold. Iterating proves ALL sixty-four choices in (4), with no parity or prime-level exception. For clarity the root positivity and retained tail can also be read directly from (2). All seven denominator factorial indices are in [0,D] by (11) and the opposite-face difference identities. The root value core z<=2D has common phase and is nonempty since max F<=2D. The tail z>2D contains the additional factor [2N] and vanishes ONLY at the value. Thus (3) has strictly positive terms. This is compatible with, and does not replace, the source/projector proof of its symmetry. ## 6. The full generic normal is retained and is not symmetric There is an EXACT generic relation in place of an incorrect jet symmetry. For a paired e write d_j=[2j+1] and let E_e=Pi_e+Pi_e* be its analytic cluster on the SAME actual source space. Equation (10) gives, before specialization, d_e* mathcal W(e*,f)^2+d_e mathcal W(e,f)^2 =[N]^2/d_f tr(E_e Pi_f). (17a) The right side is O(t), with t=log(zeta/q), whether f is paired or simple. If f is also paired, its complete double sum obeys sum_(i,j=0,1) d_(e_i)d_(f_j) mathcal W(e_i,f_j)^2 =[N]^2 tr(E_e E_f)=O(t^2). (17b) Here e_0=e,e_1=e*,f_0=f,f_1=f*. The four terms retain their full generic gauges and normal currents. Analyticity of the clusters proves the stated orders. In particular the weighted sum in (17b) has zero first normal, although its individual summands need not. These are source/projector conservation identities, not bounds on the individual cluster trace or an instruction to dephase copies. Set G(zeta)=(-1)^D S(zeta)/[N]. Termwise removal of the actual zeros gives the exact local analytic decomposition G=C+[2N]T. (18) Here C contains z<=2D and T contains z>2D, with BOTH [N] and [2N] removed in its numerator. All true denominator indices are <N, and z+1<3N on these partner branches, so C,T are analytic. For the latter bound, every folded opposite sum is >=D; replacing its four labels gives at most 4D minus that sum, hence <=3D. This accounts for every numerator zero and loses no tail. For the logarithmic generic derivative, dot G(q)=dot C(q)+4N/(q-q^-1) T(q). (19) There are actual partner branches where this additional normal is nonzero. At N=4, labels (2,2,2,2,2,1) give T(q)=-1 and the missing current is exactly 8sqrt(2)i. It is not valid to differentiate the positive value core alone. Even the COMPLETE normalized squared metric in (2) is not generically jet-symmetric. An exact cyclotomic certificate at N=4 maps q->762 modulo the prime 1009 (q^4=-1), with all remaining denominators units. In the coordinate t=log(zeta/q), the root values for folded (1,1,1,1,1,1) and single partner (2,1,1,1,1,1) are both 2. Their first Taylor coefficients reduce respectively to 994 and 426, a difference 441!=0 modulo 1009. Thus the actual algebraic first derivatives differ over C; the certificate is a nonvanishing proof, not a numerical trend. The audit retains the full C+[2N]T and every face-normalization jet in this comparison. The theorem is therefore an EXACT ROOT VALUE symmetry, not a generic-q symmetry or a bound on all partner normal jets. Controlling those currents in a coherent metric remains a separate analytic step. Raw source coefficients transform with their explicit source prefactors; they are not declared invariant. Original exterior, marking and crossing/peripheral factors remain where the actual all-port theorem places them. This reflection of internal Casimir branches is not an auxiliary-meridian deformation or a graph identification. Audit: [uniform generic source cancellation and exact partner checks](../experiments/audit_actual_racah_partner_reflection_identity.py). The proof is the genuine cyclic source identity, four uniform factorial certificates, full source-lattice collision argument and Laurent-order comparison above. Exact finite checks supplement it; they do not infer sixty-four symmetry from sampled knots. The reflection tests do not establish equality of generic jets or a full-graph estimate. No positive Hermitian transport or generic-jet invariance follows from the reflection identity.

text: # Actual prefix signs at the right-angled framing boundary 30 October 2026. For the original right-angled matching-polyhedron cut, the limiting clock signs are determined by the OUTWARD face normals with their actual source lifts. In particular every 222 pair has two negative limiting clocks, every 022/220 finite clock is negative, and every 202 total is positive. There is no independent choice of signs or local framing. The input is the labeled geometric certificate and the actual white-reflection prefix dictionary. The statement is not asserted for an arbitrary routed crossing that lacks that dictionary. It does not compute the coefficient of a global selected period. ## 1. Keep the actual reflection lifts Fix the original exposed first physical head, with positive marked meridian J=[[1,1],[0,1]]. Its ideal fixed point p is infinity. The exterior reference white face F_ref contains p. Indeed the first head is the product of the two adjacent white reflections, and p is their common ideal vertex. The exterior spine is the recorded one in [the actual cut proof](actual_right_angled_selected_framing_obstruction.md), section 3, not a newly chosen basing path. For an outward UNIT spacelike face normal n write M(n)=[[n0+n3,n1-i n2],[n1+i n2,n0-n3]], H_f=adj M(n_f)=[[a_f,b_f],[bar b_f,d_f]], J_f=[[0,-1],[1,0]] bar H_f =[[-b_f,-d_f],[a_f,bar b_f]]. (1) The anti-linear map J_f followed by conjugation is its plane reflection. The ACTUAL trace-minus-two prefix lift is Q_f=J_f bar J_ref. (2) Consecutive products telescope with these signs; this is precisely the lift fixed by the original source dictionary. Multiplying individual Q_f by arbitrary minus signs would change the clock signs below and is not allowed. The marked ideal vertex lies in the inward halfspace of every face. For its null lift p=(1/2,0,0,1/2), this inequality is <n_f,p>=-(n0-n3)/2=-a_f/2<=0. Consequently a_f>=0; a_f=0 iff p is on F_f, a_f>0 for every nonincident white face. (3) Strictness is exactly the nonincident supporting inequality in the positive labeled certificate. Since a_ref=0 and det H_ref=-1, |b_ref|=1. Multiplying the recorded matrices now gives (Q_f)21=-a_f bar b_ref. (4) Thus all NONZERO lower-left prefix entries have the SAME phase and a strictly positive real coefficient. This is an equality of the actual SL2 lifts, not a projective sign convention inferred after computing a ratio. ## 2. The boundary table with its real signs In the common frame F(r,s)=[[r,1-r],[s,-s]], let L_f=Tr(Q_f Pi), Pi=F E11 F^-1. For a nonincident face the leading term is L_f=(a_f bar b_ref/s)r^2(1+O(1/r)). (5) For incident faces it is constant, by the actual cusp-stabilizer calculation in the [source boundary theorem](actual_q_hahn_resonant_hard_edge.md). Fix s away from these finitely many constant-prefix zeros. At an original circle, label the consecutive incoming white faces F_0,F_1,F_2 as in that source theorem; the output has its own middle face and the SAME outer faces. Put X=-L_0/L_1, Y=-L_1/L_2, T=XY=L_0/L_2. (6) With 0 denoting an incident/constant face and 2 a nonincident/ quadratic face, (4)--(6) prove the following limits: | Pattern | Forced finite boundary data | | --- | --- | | 222 | X_infinity=-a_0/a_1<0, Y_infinity=-a_1/a_2<0 | | 022 | Y_infinity=-a_1/a_2<0 | | 220 | X_infinity=-a_0/a_1<0 | | 202 | T_infinity=a_0/a_2>0 | The a_i in this table are the positive coefficients in H_f, NOT the complex prefix diagonals L_i. In 002 and 200 the finite ratios of constant prefixes retain their actual dependence on s; the paired Bessel packets already keep that dependence. The two outer faces cannot both contain this marked MAIN cusp: their common ideal vertex is the distinct auxiliary cusp of the disk. Thus 000/020 do not occur in these original complete-circle boxes. The same proof holds with every retained half twist. Its shaded pairings and primitive auxiliary marking change, but the exact outside white-reflection prefix loops (2) do not. It also proves the signs for every original white interval and cup/cap adjacency to which the same dictionary applies. It does not authorize an arbitrary routed band to be assigned these original face labels. ### One main component gives every 200/002 Bessel calibration Suppose the fixed retained-half-twist diagram has ONE main component; the auxiliary crossing circles are still present. This is the relevant connectivity hypothesis when subsequent independent full twists produce a knot. Full twists do not change that connectivity. Every original based physical puncture is then a conjugate of the marked primitive main meridian or its inverse. In the recorded trace-minus-two lift it has the form -g J^epsilon g^-1, epsilon=+1 or -1, with g an ACTUAL element of the complete holonomy group. In a 200 box both Q_1 and Q_2 fix infinity, so the actual second puncture B=Q_2 Q_1^-1 does also. Its unique parabolic fixed point implies g(infinity)=infinity. The complete torus-cusp stabilizer acts by translations on its horospheres; hence g commutes with J. One can also see the absence of another multiplier directly: a dilation would make conjugates of J accumulate at the identity, while a nontrivial unit-modulus rotation would give a fixed axis in hyperbolic space. Discreteness and the free complete deck action exclude both. Therefore B=-J^epsilon in every original 200 box. Likewise Q_0,Q_1 fix infinity in a 002 box, so its actual first puncture is A=-J^epsilon. This is primitive meridian conjugacy, with no added longitude, cusp translation or independent local basing. It can fail when there is more than one main component. The orientation does not change the Bessel parameter. For 200 write Q_1=e[[1,z0],[0,1]], e=+1 or -1. Since Tr A=Tr B=Tr(BA)=-2, B=-J^epsilon forces A_21=4epsilon. At r=N rho the actual raw clocks give U_raw/N^2 -> -4epsilon rho^2/[s(1+z0 s)], V_raw -> (1+z0 s)/(1+(z0+epsilon)s). Their actual white arguments remain q^-1 times these clocks. Substituting these limits in the proved 200 Bessel parameter cancels epsilon and gives K=s^2 sin^2(pi mu)/(4pi^2 rho^2), mu=m/N. For 002 write Q_0=e[[1,z0],[0,1]]. Now A=-J^epsilon forces B_21=4epsilon, and U_raw -> (1+z0 s)/(1+(z0+epsilon)s), N^2 V_raw -> s(1+(z0+epsilon)s)/(4epsilon rho^2). The proved 002 parameter gives the SAME K. All constant-prefix zeros remain excluded as above. Thus the original 200/002 Bessel theorems cover every such original box in this one-main-component class, including either orientation and every fixed retained-half-twist pattern. At the literal Fourier scaling rho=1/(2pi i j), fixed j!=0, the limit is I_0(2j s sin(pi mu)); it is nonzero when Re s!=0. This is a local root-numerator conclusion, with exact normalizations retained in the source theorem. It does not add a generic normal or a global period claim. There is also a nonzero local choice compatible with the actual [off-node source family](actual_braided_residual_framing_current.md), section 5. Take rho in a positive real compact and s=exp(-2pi i alpha)-1 with alpha in a compact subset of (0,1/2), still avoiding the finitely many excluded constant-prefix zeros. The packet is J_0(s sin(pi mu)/(pi rho)), with a nonreal argument, and is therefore nonzero. For completeness, if J_0(z)=0, its radial equation (t f')'=-z^2 t f for f(t)=J_0(zt), integrated against bar f, gives z^2 integral_0^1 t|f|^2=integral_0^1 t|f'|^2>0; hence z is real. On the same positive-rho compact the exact source family's limiting factor rho(1-exp(-1/rho))exp(t_coh/rho) is nonzero as well. This is compatibility of local parameter choices: the coherent variable t_coh is not identified with alpha, and the unknown whole-source coefficient or a selected cycle is not determined. ## 3. Actual half-index and factorial consequences Retain physical head i=N x-1/2, with X=exp(2pi i x), exactly as in the source boundary theorem. The actual white argument is q^-1 X, not X. A negative finite limiting clock has a logarithmic lift with Re x=1/2; a pair of them has canonical total Re(x+y)=1. This is a boundary of the earlier strict physical packet, not a point claimed to lie in one of its fixed compact subsets. In particular the 222 finite head clocks stay away from X=0,1 and infinity. The finite clocks of 022/220 do also. The remaining head in 022/220 has imaginary part of order N log N; its actual factorial normals have the separately proved [logarithmic-escape control](actual_moving_period_factorial_logarithmic_escape.md) when their stated argument hypotheses hold. Auxiliary rows still come from i+j=(d-a)+r0 with the ACTUAL discrete a. They are not assigned the universal physical-head -1/2 offset. For 202 the total is on a positive compact ray for a fixed diagram and boundary chart, so the whole-polynomial relative packet in the source boundary theorem applies without changing the reference cusp. For 220 the actual qU approaches a strictly negative ray, exactly the domain of the complementary determinant packet; 022 is transported by the ACTUAL generic reciprocity with its scalar and marks retained. There is also a useful exact finite matrix consequence for the 222 LIMITING clocks, separate from an asymptotic statement. The original small-channel determinant identity in the [complementary source theorem](actual_q_hahn_complementary_hard_edge.md) is H_a^1(U,V)/V^a=[2a choose a]_Q det[I-(qU/2)H_--(q^-1/(2V))H_+]. (7) The Hermitian matrices H_-,H_+ are positive definite for every actual a<=floor((N-1)/2), including the fold. At the physical half-index arguments U=q^-1 X_infinity, V=q^-1 Y_infinity, (7) contains I+|X_infinity|H_-/2+H_+/(2|Y_infinity|)>=I. (8) Thus this exact limiting-argument determinant is strictly positive. For the large m=d-a the original forced partner product remains. No generic derivative is obtained by differentiating that root collision identity. Nor does (8) by itself replace the actual r=N rho arguments by their limits: their O(1/N) perturbation can change a determinant of size O(N) by an order-one factor. The boundary dictionary supplies honest geometric domains for the actual numerators and factors. It does not prove a full 222 packet, erase finite offsets or characters, or supply the original relative framing-cycle coefficient. Focused audit: [actual signed cuboctahedral prefixes](../experiments/audit_actual_right_angled_resonant_prefix_signs.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_right_angled_resonant_prefix_signs_results.json). The labeled ideal right-angled cuboctahedron, cube matching in one coordinate and marked main edge in another supply all six permissible patterns. The audit retains the actual SL2 lifts and their trace-minus-two heads; it checks 168 support inequalities, 24 right angles, six prefix matrices, 16 ordered disk triples and two half-index identities. Eight additional exact symbolic cases retain both primitive orientations, both prefix lifts and both 200/002 endpoint formulas. No generic partner differentiation, boundary asymptotic or global period is inferred. The resonant-prefix calculation gives local nonzero packets and off-node information, not a whole-period estimate.

title: The right-angled cut obstructs an all-central selected frame
status: No all-central selected frame; exactly two physical failures
text: # The right-angled cut obstructs an all-central selected frame Subsequent full-domain result: the [full strict physical packet](actual_q_hahn_full_physical_complex_packet.md) extends the actual ordinary amplitude and the stated small/near-fold complex bounds to fixed physical compacts, with the necessary finite-level boundary correction. The [selected-factor corollary](actual_augmented_plat_selected_factor_localization.md) then selects every ordinary factor outside one prescribed matching-edge block. Global contraction and period estimates remain open. The argument below keeps its original domain and proof scope. 30 October 2026. The shaded-face circle packing does give common exteriors. It does not supply a frame in which every original ordinary column is both in the proved central domain and on its selected endpoint sheet. For the literal projection Morse prefixes of a positively certified right-angled augmented plat, the following argument instead gives an obstruction to that simultaneous choice. The unfolded geometric critical germ, the actual quantum source, and the volume conjecture are not contradicted. The obstruction concerns this particular all-column physical-support/selected-sheet route. The decisive dictionary is section 3. It retains the actual projection basepaths and the positive normalizations of the reflection lifts; an abstract circle packing without this dictionary would not prove the statement. ## 1. Geometric input and statement Let Q be the labeled convex ideal right-angled polyhedron supplied by [the actual matching-graph certificate](../papers/marked-fillings/README.md). Its shaded faces are triangles; its white faces are the actual projection regions. Every edge separates the two colors, and every vertex has four alternating incident faces. The shaded triangles are paired by the actual crossing disks. Half twists retain the face quotient and primitive marks recorded in that construction. At the horizontal cuts outside the crossing boxes use the original ordered Morse meridians H_1,...,H_m and prefixes Q_i=H_i...H_1. The exterior projection region is F_0. The two conditions in question are: * Every input and output triple has canonical wire logarithms in the CENTRAL domain of the framing criterion and the joint kernel theorem. * Every input and output lies on the source-selected endpoint sheet in the selected-local certificate, with the positive geometric orientation. Subject to the literal prefix identification proved in section 3, NO common rank-one frame has both properties. The argument uses the weaker necessary strict-support test, not a failure peculiar to the central wedge boundary. ## 2. Disks of nonadjacent facets and the white-normal polyhedron Use Lorentz signature (-,+,+,+). Choose an interior point of Q as the Klein origin, and write every outward unit facet normal as n=(n_0,n_vec). Then n_0>0. Adjacent normals have Lorentz product zero. Distinct facets which do not share an edge have disjoint supporting planes in hyperbolic space. Here is a direct proof for this ideal right-angled setting. If two such facets share an ideal vertex, their planes are the opposite vertical planes of its rectangular horosphere link, hence are parallel. Otherwise their closed ideal boundaries are disjoint. A bounded- distance minimizing sequence between the two facets cannot escape: two bounded-distance sequences escaping to infinity have the same ideal limit, which would be a common ideal boundary point. Thus the distance is achieved at finite points. A minimizing point in a facet interior has a perpendicular joining geodesic. If it is on an edge, the neighboring facet plane is orthogonal. The tangential direction toward the other closest point lies in the outward normal cone of that edge, by minimality; but its scalar product with the same edge normal is nonpositive because the other point belongs to Q. Orthogonality makes these two statements force the tangential component to vanish. There are no finite vertices. The minimizing segment is therefore perpendicular to both supporting planes. Intersecting planes have no positive-length common perpendicular. The planes are disjoint. The orientations face the common interior of Q, so their outward halfspaces are disjoint. Indeed, for disjoint planes the alternative orientations would put one plane strictly in the outward halfspace of the other, making its supporting inequality redundant or removing that facet of Q. Their unit normals consequently have product at most -1. In particular same-colored outward ideal disks have disjoint interiors, with tangencies only at shared ideal vertices. A finite set of these disks has a nonempty open common exterior: take a point on one boundary away from all finitely many tangencies and then move a little to its exterior. For each WHITE face f put v_f=n_f,vec/n_f,0, C=conv{v_f}. (1) For each SHADED face b with outward normal m_b, exactly its three neighboring white normals satisfy m_b,vec . v_f=m_b,0. (2) Every other white normal satisfies the strict inequality < in (2), by the preceding disjoint-plane argument. Those three v_f are not collinear: their three unit normals have Gram matrix with diagonal 1 and off-diagonal -1, of determinant -4. They are linearly independent, and their positive affine normalizations are therefore not collinear. Thus they give an exposed triangular facet of C. These triangles have exactly the dual incidence of the original checkerboard sphere: two white vertices are joined at each ideal vertex of Q, and the two shaded triangles there are its two incident facets. The cyclic links at a white vertex are the original white-face boundary cycles. Consequently the known triangles form an embedded closed connected two-manifold in the boundary of the three-dimensional convex hull C. Along every known edge both convex-hull sides are already present; at every vertex the known cyclic link is the whole link. There is no room for an extra facet. Equivalently this closed triangulated sphere is both open and closed in the boundary of C. Hence C={ y in R^3 : m_b,vec . y <= m_b,0 for EVERY shaded b }. (3) This is an equality of finite Euclidean convex polyhedra. It is stronger than merely saying that C meets the unit ball. It identifies C with the intersection of the shaded inward halfspaces, extended in Klein coordinates. Its vertices are generally outside the unit ball and its edges are tangent to that ball. Let K be the open common exterior of all shaded ideal disks. A flag in K, viewed as a unit vector on the Klein sphere, is a STRICT interior point of C. The distinction matters: an arbitrary hyperbolic geodesic need not meet C. Only the selected flags will supply its required endpoints in C. ## 3. The literal white-reflection prefixes Let r_f be reflection in the white face plane f. At a horizontal Morse cut outside all crossing boxes, label the white intervals encountered from the exterior left spine by F_0,F_1,...,F_m. The original prefix loop surrounding the first i punctures is the two-white-face bigon: it crosses the projection cut in F_0 and F_i, with its upper and lower paths lying in the two opened projection balls. The horizontal cut misses every crossing-disk half sheet; the exterior spine misses them as well. Thus these paths need no unrecorded shaded-face deck transformation. Reversing the literal cut identifies its projective holonomy as Q_i=r_(F_i) r_(F_0), H_i=r_(F_i) r_(F_(i-1)). (4) The order is the original convention Q_i=H_i...H_1, not its inverse. It can be checked in the canonical incoming disk coordinate eta, in which its punctures are 0 and 1 and its auxiliary flag is infinity. The consecutive white reflections are r_0(eta)=-conjugate(eta), r_mid(eta)=conjugate(eta)/(2conjugate(eta)-1), r_1(eta)=2-conjugate(eta). They give A=r_mid r_0, B=r_1 r_mid and P=r_1 r_0, exactly the original canonical puncture pair after eta=1/(2s+1). A cup or cap has equal first and last white regions, so (4) gives the required inverse pair. A retained half twist changes the shaded pairing and the auxiliary primitive meridian; it does not change these outside two-white-face loops. The input and output before/after a box have the same two outer white faces. Both are adjacent to BOTH shaded faces meeting at that box's auxiliary ideal vertex. The lift signs are also fixed. In the Hermitian Lorentz model use M(n)=[[n_0+n_3,n_1-i n_2],[n_1+i n_2,n_0-n_3]], H(n)=adj M(n), E=[[0,-1],[1,0]], J(n)=E conjugate(H(n)). For an outward UNIT spacelike normal, J(n) conjugate(J(n))=I, and J(n) followed by conjugation is its plane reflection. Direct multiplication gives tr[J(n_g) conjugate(J(n_f))]=2<n_g,n_f>. (5) The consecutive white planes at a main segment are tangent and face the common interior, so their product is the required trace -2 lift. The actual negative-parabolic heads therefore telescope without independent signs: Q_i=J(n_(F_i)) conjugate(J(n_(F_0))). (6) Changing from a unit normal to the normalized vertex (1,v_f) rescales by n_f,0>0. Thus the linear coefficients used below have only POSITIVE relative normal factors. Arbitrary sign choices for reflections would lose this fact. ## 4. Selected sheets put both global flags in K Write the common projector as Pi=v ell, ell(v)=1, and let w=ker ell. Put w_0=r_(F_0)(v). For a coupon whose left prefix interval is F, equation (4) gives W_prefix v=r_F(w_0). (7) Its two shaded disk circles bound the region Omega of the selected-local certificate. This is precisely the common exterior of those two outward shaded disks: at their common auxiliary vertex they become the parallel sides of the original cusp rectangle. The primitive orientation gives the positive strip between them, not either exterior complementary half-plane. Both planes are orthogonal to the adjacent white plane F. Thus r_F preserves EACH shaded halfspace and preserves Omega. On the CENTRAL domain the proved selected input/output tests require w and W_prefix v in Omega. By (7) this is equivalent to w,w_0 in Omega. Every shaded face occurs in exactly one original disk pair, so all the tests together imply w in K, w_0 in K. (8) This proves the separated strip intersections are nonempty in this geometry; it does NOT yet give the coupled physical-support inequalities. The latter are what fail below. ## 5. Polarization forces a failed strict-support triangle For every original prefix, its diagonal is a_f=ell[ J(n_f) conjugate(J(n_(F_0))) v ] =ell[ J(n_f) conjugate(w_0) ]. Since ell has kernel w, all a_f are one common nonzero scalar times the polarized circle forms L_n(w,w_0)=det(w,J(n)conjugate(w_0)). (9) These are real-linear in the Lorentz normal n. Up to complex conjugation, (9) is the Hermitian polarization w^* H(n) w_0. For a null normal with M(n)=y y^*, direct factorization gives w^* H(n) w_0=conjugate(det(y,w)) det(y,w_0). (10) If w!=w_0, the simultaneous real and imaginary kernel of (9) is therefore the Lorentz two-plane spanned by the two null lifts of w and w_0. To verify that it has exactly dimension two, send these two distinct flags to the coordinate axes: the condition is the vanishing of one off-diagonal Hermitian entry. If w=w_0, the kernel is a real hyperplane containing its null lift; the following argument still applies. By (8) and (3), those null lifts, normalized to time coordinate 1, give points of the STRICT interior of C. Thus the affine kernel of (9) meets int C. A real line in that kernel, through such a point, meets the boundary of the bounded polyhedron C. Let a boundary point lie in a shaded facet with neighboring white vertices v_0,v_1,v_2. It has barycentric coordinates lambda_i>=0, sum lambda_i=1. Linearity gives sum_i lambda_i L_((1,v_i))(w,w_0)=0. (11) The unit normal n_i is n_i,0(1,v_i), with n_i,0>0. By (9), equation (11) is a nontrivial NONNEGATIVE relation among that facet's three actual prefix diagonals a_i, after dividing each weight by n_i,0 and renormalizing their sum. Therefore 0 in conv_R{a_0,a_1,a_2}. (12) But this shaded facet is one original input or output factor. Its strict physical-support criterion requires exactly the opposite of (12). If the boundary point lies on an edge or vertex, zero weights are allowed in (11), and the same contradiction follows. A vanishing diagonal would additionally violate the regular chart rather than evade the argument. Thus the geometric oriented-strip conditions and simultaneous strict physical support cannot both hold for this literal right-angled factorization. In particular the proved CENTRAL-domain source-sheet certificate has no common frame here. ## 6. A generic pair has exactly two failed physical triples The obstruction has bounded combinatorial size. For a generic pair of DISTINCT flags w,w_0 in K, its affine polarization kernel is a line through int C which meets the boundary in the interiors of exactly TWO facets. A facet's diagonal triangle contains zero if and only if this line meets that facet: both directions follow from (9), the positive normal scalings, and barycentric coordinates. Therefore exactly two original input/output triples fail the convex-hull test, independently of the number of bridges, boxes, or white faces. Such generic pairs exist, and one may also avoid every total-degree seam and regular-chart divisor. Indeed distinct endpoint pairs in the open set K times K parameterize an open set of hyperbolic geodesics, equivalently Klein affine lines meeting the open ball with these endpoints. Meeting any one fixed edge line of C imposes a nonzero real algebraic coplanarity condition on this four-real-dimensional line space. It cannot contain an open subset. Avoiding the finitely many such conditions makes the two boundary intersections interior to facets. A bounded convex polyhedron and an interior-crossing line have exactly two boundary points. For a disk, put its two outer white circles at Re eta=0 and Re eta=1. If eta(w)=a+ib and eta(w_0)=c+id, its actual right flag has coordinate -c+id under the left white reflection. Up to a common scalar the two outer prefix coefficients are a_0=-(a+c)+i(d-b), a_2=(a+c-2)-i(d-b). Thus Im(a_0 conjugate(a_2))=-2(d-b). The seam condition is exactly Im eta(w_0)=Im eta(w), a proper real analytic condition on ANY open subset of K times K. The strip coordinate is finite there and its imaginary part is nonconstant. A finite union of these seam loci also has empty interior. At cups and caps the two outer faces coincide, but one may additionally avoid a real ratio for the two DISTINCT adjacent white coefficients. This too is a proper algebraic condition: for any two distinct white normals, real dependence of their complex polarizations means that the kernel Lorentz plane meets their real span. In the affine chart it is the coplanarity condition for the kernel line and the line through those two white vertices, including parallel intersection at infinity. A fixed such condition has empty interior in the open space of secants. Avoiding it is stronger than, and implies, the required cup/cap canonical-log test. Finally (w,w_0) maps to the common frame by v=r_(F_0)(w_0), ell(v)=1, ker ell=w. Away from v=w this is a real analytic diffeomorphism onto an open part of the frame quotient. The finitely many proper algebraic regular-chart divisors cannot contain that open part. All the exclusions can be made simultaneously. At every remaining facet the framing criterion therefore gives STRICT PHYSICAL support, with its canonical low or high adapter. Exactly two facets still fail that criterion. The next corollary shows that their identities can in fact be prescribed. This is a geometric localization statement. It does not show that the other factors lie in the smaller central domain, extend the proved source-sheet equivalence to the whole physical strip, or estimate the two exceptional factors. Those distinctions prevent this corollary from being mistaken for a global amplitude theorem. ### The two exceptional facets can be prescribed Choose ANY two distinct shaded facets b_1,b_2 of C. Each supporting hyperbolic plane lies in the inward halfspace of every other shaded plane. Its whole unit-sphere circle therefore belongs to its C facet; away from the finitely many tangency points it lies in that facet's relative interior. Equivalently, the triangular facet circumscribes this circle and its edges touch at the original ideal vertices. Choose distinct non-tangency points r_i on the two circles. Their open chord is in int C, since its endpoints are relative-interior points of different facets, and it lies in the open unit ball. Perturb each r_i a little within its own facet, away from the circle's center, to a point p_i OUTSIDE the closed unit ball and still in the relative facet interior. A fixed midpoint of the chord remains in the open ball by continuity. Thus the line through p_1,p_2 has two distinct sphere intersections, both strictly between the p_i and hence in int C. These sphere flags w,w_0 belong to K. The full intersection of their line with C is precisely [p_1,p_2], so its two failed facets are exactly b_1,b_2. All these properties persist on an open set of endpoint pairs. The finite edge, seam, cup/cap, projector and regular-chart exclusions from the preceding argument can therefore be imposed as well. For an algebraic positive certificate the flags may also be chosen algebraic: the strict feasible set is open in a rational chart of the sphere-pair space, and algebraic points are dense there. In particular take the two shaded triangles incident to the original marked physical main edge of the matching graph. They are distinct and meet at that edge's ideal vertex in Q. The two exceptional ordinary column factors can be localized at those two vertices, without moving the mark or changing the source. One can instead choose the two halves of any designated crossing-circle matching edge. This is a geometric choice of frame; it neither deletes those factors nor proves an estimate for their exact contraction. The other factors are strictly physical, not automatically in the smaller central domain. ## 7. Scope and consequence The obstruction is to a proposed sufficient condition for applying the ordinary local theorem everywhere at a geometric critical point. It does not contradict the joint kernel theorem, whose domain remains correct; the selected-local certificate remains a conditional theorem. Nor does it contradict the unfolded geometric critical scheme or its volume regulator. A geometric critical point can lie outside the strict physical chamber of some factors, and its relevant contour can require additional continuations, branch changes, normal terms, or a coherent resummation before local estimates are applied. The generic-frame theorem avoids algebraic poles. It never supplied strict physical support or selected sheets. The present obstruction explains why those additional real inequalities cannot be obtained from the right-angled circle packing by choosing a sufficiently generic common frame. Audit: [exact outward lifts and convex polarization](../experiments/audit_actual_right_angled_selected_framing_obstruction.py). The formal reflection and null-factorization identities pass. The regular ideal octahedron checks 72 exact prefix products, 78 selected endpoint pairs with exact failed-facet convex relations, 67 transverse two-facet exit checks, and 936 reflected selected halfspace checks. This finite fixture does not replace section 3's actual Morse-basepath proof or section 2's general facet-incidence argument. The source conclusion is restricted to an ALL-CENTRAL selected frame; the larger physical-domain statement is geometric with the oriented strip sides imposed. No volume conjecture, unfolded critical germ, or contour outside that central route is refuted by this result. The original marked main edge is selectable without transporting its mark. The exact fixture checks all six distinct facet pairs of the regular ideal octahedron. Central support and source estimates for the other factors and the exceptional block remain additional restrictions.

title: Connected untwisted smoothing has a strict source-capacity gap
text: # Connected untwisted smoothing has a strict source-capacity gap 30 October 2026. Let D be a fixed connected augmented flat plat with the original labeled nondegenerate convex ideal right-angled certificate. Its original two marked white faces and literal physical/matching port orders are retained. Delete a nonempty subset S of UNTWISTED circle ports by the actual L_1 identity smoothing. Assume the resulting source is connected. The surviving ports may retain their original signed half twists. The [exact capacity decomposition](actual_smoothed_source_capacity_blocks.md) supplies simple white blocks and zero-capacity double triangles. If a loop occurs, its capacity is -infinity. Otherwise the construction below gives a representation of the original drilled group, killing every deleted meridian, with volume 2 sum_blocks Vol(Q_block)=2pi Phi_sm < Vol(Y_D)=2pi Phi_D. (1) The two original marked faces remain distinct and adjacent: in the literal flat-plat merge forest they have opposite gap parity. No one-main-component assumption is needed. The proof uses the actual white/shaded cut balls and their original pairings. It neither asserts a three-manifold JSJ identification nor factors the finite quantum source into block sources. ## 1. The common circle data can be assembled along the digon tree Choose a root block. Each simple block has its proved positive circle packing; a double-triangle block is represented by three mutually tangent circles, with its two shaded triangles having the SAME three contact points and zero three-dimensional volume. Normalize the latter, for example, as two opposite lines and one disk tangent to both. At a digon attachment its boundary vertices a,b are adjacent in each closed block. There is an orientation-preserving Mobius map carrying the child's ORDERED oriented tangent disks a,b to the already assigned parent disks. To see this explicitly, send their common contact to infinity. Both pairs become ordered opposite parallel halfplanes; positive scaling and a translation match their width and position. The remaining freedom is horizontal translation inside the strip. Thus every shared white face receives exactly the same reflection on both sides. Recursing along the actual cut tree assigns circles to all original smoothed white faces. The free translations can avoid any additional finite accidental equalities of distinct circles. A globally embedded packing is NOT required here; only every block's packing and the shared ordered circles are retained. ## 2. The two types of digon cuts have different actual pairings The digon encloses 2v source vertices. Since each vertex has one matching incidence, its number of crossing matching edges is even. Thus the two crossed source edges are both MAIN or both MATCHING. MAIN/MAIN: the matching pairs stay within the pieces. The same raw physical head r_b r_a (or its literal inverse when the port is reversed) appears at the two cut ports. Topologically the cut is the actual two-main-arc sphere, or the corresponding meridional annulus after deleting cusp neighborhoods. This is the familiar componentwise connected-sum situation, with the actual meridian identified. MATCHING/MATCHING: the two original shaded pairings cross the cut pieces. They must not be replaced by gluing entire artificial cusp tori. In particular no equality of the two blocks' cusp shapes is required. The local algebra gives the needed actual collar directly. The oriented boundary of the proper cut disk traverses its two cut edges in opposite directions. Closing either side therefore records one input and one output side. The original cross-piece pairing keeps these opposite sides and its prescribed vertex permutation; it is not an arbitrary input-to-input identification of two block triangles. Let the common outer white pair be a,b and put P=r_b r_a=-I+H. It is a noncentral parabolic: H^2=0. For either side write its ordered raw main pair as (A,B), with BA=P and Tr A=Tr B=-2. Then Tr(H A)=4. After H=[[0,h],[0,0]], this means A_21=4/h. Its trace and determinant give A_22=-2-A_11 and A_12=-(A_11+1)^2/A_21. Hence the normalized centralizer I+tH acts SIMPLY TRANSITIVELY on these ordered pairs. For any original input/output triangles across a cut matching edge, there is a unique C=I+tH with C A_in C^-1=A_out; it also transports B. This C fixes the common a/b contact and sends the a/middle and middle/b contacts to their recorded output contacts, because those are the unique main parabolic eigenpoints. It is therefore exactly the ordered three-point map of the two actual ideal shaded triangles. This proves the contact/peripheral adapter; it does not infer one from a scalar eigenratio. For a retained half twist epsilon, use the literal primitive matrix M=C^-1 (I+H/2)^epsilon. It has determinant1 and commutes with P. The original threading word [2,1,1,2] followed by the recorded signed Hurwitz move transports the input pair to the output pair, exactly as in the proved critical-scheme and primitive-collar identities. The signs are the actual parabolic specialization of (P^-1-I)/(-2), not a freely chosen peripheral shear. Both P and M fix the same cusp point. MAIN cuts match their meridian; MATCHING cuts instead retain BOTH original M matrices separately. ## 3. The actual group representation, including each deleted meridian Use the same white reflections at every occurrence of an original smoothed face. At a Morse slice the raw physical heads are H_j=r_(F_j) r_(F_(j-1)). Their prefixes telescope; literal cups/caps have product I, and unchanged wires have unchanged based heads. Every surviving box has the contact map of section2 and its original half twist. These are all the [literal Morse/van Kampen relations](actual_augmented_plat_critical_scheme.md), so the construction gives an actual SL2 representation (with the existing raw trace-minus-two / physical trace-plus-two lift convention). Restore each deleted UNTWISTED box in the original drilled diagram. Its middle faces satisfy b=c by the literal smoothing. Thus its input and output ordered main pairs are equal. Set its actual auxiliary meridian to I. The original threading word is then the identity and the four physical ports are unchanged, including the case where the outer product happens to be central. This explicitly factors the representation through the actual meridional filling quotient. It does not wrap a source head or alter the original mark. ## 4. The ideal bigon collapse and the fundamental chain The connected augmented projection has the usual TWO literal cut balls obtained by cutting along the projection sphere and the recorded crossing disks. This is a topological cut before any convexity claim. Its white/shaded boundary cellulation is the rectified white graph; the surviving half twists specify the same recorded shaded face maps. For a loopless triangular sphere, the source cubic dual is bridgeless, so these white faces have disk boundaries; degree-two faces are allowed. In either cut ball, a digon CUT between white faces a,b bounds a proper disk D whose boundary has one arc in white face a, one in white face b, and whose two ideal endpoints are the crossed source edges. Cutting the ball along D gives two balls. Collapsing D in either boundary to a point gives exactly the two closed block balls of the combinatorial digon decomposition. All shaded triangles are unchanged; only the two cut ideal vertices coalesce. Iterating constructs the actual block tree separately in both cut balls. This does not claim that the doubled disk separates the full exterior when its shaded pairings cross the cut. Under the circle assignments of section1, BOTH cut ideal vertices develop to the SAME contact p=a intersect b. Thus D is assigned a constant ideal image p. Each remaining block ball, after collapsing its cut disks, maps with degree ONE to its actual convex Q_block. The double-triangle block maps into its single ideal triangle and has volume zero. Here is a finite-chain way to retain the multiplicity. First decorate each tangency of an ordered white pair by its CANONICAL horosphere. Send the contact to infinity and normalize the strip between the two white planes to width1. The horosphere at height1 is independent of the remaining horizontal translation, and pulling it back gives the decoration. Swapping the ordered pair preserves the same horosphere. Reflection in a boundary white plane preserves heights in this model. An actual shaded face map carries each of its three adjacent white planes: such a plane is the unique plane orthogonal to the shaded plane along the specified ideal triangle edge. Therefore the actual three-point shaded map, including its retained vertex permutation, carries these pair decorations. All finite replacements can consequently be chosen face-compatibly before passing to the quotient. These are the finitely many INCIDENCE points and truncated corners of a fundamental chain. They are not a single finite point assigned equivariantly to an ideal cusp vertex: a nontrivial parabolic stabilizer would forbid the latter. Translated corners on the same horosphere are retained, with their actual pairing maps. The TWO cut endpoints have the same white pair a,b, not merely the same ideal image. In their common normalized strip choose every replacement vertex of the collapsed disk at height T, with bounded horizontal coordinates. Reflected white maps and the actual shaded maps preserve the preceding decoration. Since the triangulation and its face maps are finite, all coordinates stay bounded in their respective normalized strips. In particular any two replacement vertices on one cut disk have distance 2 asinh(|z_1-z_2|/(2T))=O(1/T). Complete the truncated chain with the original conical cusp tails. Their boundary comparison is the previously proved horospherical O(T^-2) flux estimate; no artificial finite cusp fixed point is used. This specific common-height construction is essential: arbitrary sequences of ideal vertices converging to the same p need not have vanishing tetrahedral volume. We use the following uniform elementary bound. If a possibly partly ideal tetrahedron has two FINITE vertices at distance ell, then |Vol(tetrahedron)| <= 2pi integral_0^ell cosh(t)^2 dt <= 2pi ell cosh(ell)^2. (4a) Indeed take the plane through one of these vertices and the other two vertices. The tetrahedron lies in the one-sided distance-ell slab over this plane. In Klein coordinates adapted to the plane, orthogonal projection is the linear coordinate projection; its image is the convex hull of at most four points in the plane and has area at most 2pi. Fermi coordinates have volume element cosh(t)^2 dA dt, proving the bound. Degenerate plane choices follow by a finite approximation. The estimate is uniform when either of the last two vertices is ideal. Triangulate the proper disks and both adjacent balls compatibly. Collapsing a boundary disk of a ball to a point again gives a ball, with relative degree1. Refine against a vertex-fan triangulation of Q_block. One can perform the refinement by coning triangulated disk faces and their mapping cylinders; every additional tetrahedron in the collapse region then has at least TWO disk replacement vertices. By (4a) their total volume is O(1/T). The remaining block chain has relative degree1 and tends to an ordinary ideal triangulation of its actual Q_block. Thus its developed volume tends to Vol(Q_block). This is the degree of an explicit ball quotient, not an assumed global covering degree, and the vanishing of the correction is supplied by (4a), not by a continuity claim at coincident ideal flags. All original face boundaries cancel. White face maps use the SAME reflection on every piece of that face, including the collapsed arcs. For a MAIN cut the original matching/shaded pairs remain in their pieces. For a MATCHING cut the original shaded triangles are not cut internally at all, and the contact maps of section2 identify their three actual ideal vertices across pieces. Their retained Hurwitz versions are precisely the original signed face maps. Consequently the straightened chain is the actual marked exterior's relative fundamental chain, not a sum obtained by changing the face pairings. Choose ONE reflection r_u to develop the whole second cut ball from the first. Use this same choice on every block; the remaining white gluing transformations are r_f r_u in the original convention. Thus the second ball is not assembled from independently reflected blocks. Its original opposite topological orientation and this one reflected geometric development give the SAME positive volume. Therefore Vol(rho_sm)=2 sum_(simple blocks) Vol(Q_block) =2pi Phi_sm. There is no additional contribution from the cut annuli or from the double-triangle blocks. No JSJ identification or finite tensor-product identity is used. All remaining cusp images are parabolic (possibly rank deficient) with their actual commuting peripheral words. Finally restore the original deleted solid-torus cusps. Their meridians are trivial. The [proved axis/parabolic flattening](../papers/casimir-source-asymptotics/README.md) gives a zero-volume filling cap, so the representation of the original drilled exterior has exactly the same volume. The complete original meridian was nontrivial; the strict-kernel theorem therefore gives Phi_sm<Phi_old for every such nonempty connected untwisted smoothing with finite capacity. ## 5. A uniform corridor for the actual untwisted external colors Fix any set E of original UNTWISTED external circle ports. Let A_N(N-h_E,N_else) denote the literal original mixed contraction, with external color N-h_i at i in E and color N at every other port. The other ports may carry their original signed half twists. Let F_N^E(h) be its EXACT empty-subset cosine term from the [external reflection identity](../papers/marked-fillings/README.md), with deficit zero at ports outside E. Put Phi_D=Vol(Y_D)/(2pi). There exist delta(D)>0, gamma(D)>0 and a fixed power K(D) such that, for every sufficiently large N of EITHER parity and every integer 0<=h_i<=delta(D)N, |A_N(N-h_E,N_else)-F_N^E(h)| <= N^K(D) exp[N(Phi_D-gamma(D))]. (5) All constants are allowed to depend on the fixed labeled diagram; there is no width-independent or twist-independent uniformity claim. One can choose them simultaneously for all subsets E of its untwisted ports. This is a near-complete REAL INTEGER color corridor, not an off-grid identity or a genuine-q normal theorem. Proof. Expand by the exact full-matrix reflection identity. A nonempty subset S contains literal L_(h_i) at its ports; a term with h_i=0 is zero. If its identity smoothing is connected, the [simultaneous polynomial correspondence](../papers/triangular-insertion/README.md) bounds its full finite source by C(l)^sum h_i times the smoothed positive-coefficient bound at ANY fixed positive shared radii l. This retains the original mark, all carries and the actual tensor endpoints. Equation (1), or the loop capacity -infinity, gives Phi_sm<Phi_D. Choose fixed positive finite-face radii with marked radii zero making the fold capacity strictly below Phi_D. Then choose both marked radii small and POSITIVE, still below that value with a fixed margin.
