This is permitted by continuity of the local fold entropy, with the limit -infinity allowed when every local argument vanishes. The resulting C(l) is finite; it need not be uniformly bounded as marked radii tend to zero. The [all-channel determinant upper bound](actual_positive_face_channel_rate.md) at these now strictly positive radii bounds every remaining folded label by the same fold value, up to a uniform o(N) logarithmic error. There are only polynomially many such labels. Multiplicities and measures are polynomial, the remaining cosine factors have modulus at most one, and the retained integer-label half-twist phases are units. There are finitely many S. Fix one such radius choice for each connected S and take the minimum positive capacity margin and maximum log C(l). Choose delta small enough that C(l)^sum h_i consumes less than half that margin. Absorb the uniform o(N) and polynomial factors by decreasing gamma. For disconnected smoothing the exact correspondence instead vanishes whenever 2 sum_(i in S)(h_i-1)<N-1. Choosing also delta<1/(4 max(1,|E|)) guarantees this for all large N. Summing the finitely many subsets proves (5), with the original subset signs intact. This proves the missing proper-subset suppression in this corridor. It does not bound colors outside the corridor or vary a signed circle port: an odd half twist retained at a small port is not an identity smoothing. Full filling-source transfer still requires those separate inputs. No finite tensor product over the capacity blocks was used. ## 6. Verification and precise scope The finite-chain construction uses common horospheres and the specified fixed second-ball reflection. Section 5 requires fixed positive-radius regularization and finite subset margins, retaining signed complete ports and exact disconnected vanishing. The representation may be nondiscrete and the global circle configuration may overlap. The argument uses convexity of each individual block, not global packing embeddedness.

title: Smoothed source capacity, simple blocks and their actual polyhedra
text: # Smoothed source capacity, simple blocks and their actual polyhedra 30 October 2026. This concerns the L_1 opposite smoothing, not deletion of the old white edge xy or an asserted three-manifold JSJ decomposition. The new source is assumed connected and its two original marked white vertices u,v are distinct and still joined by their actual marked MAIN edge. The source white cellulation is a spherical triangular cellulation, allowing repeated incidences, loops and parallel edges. ## 1. Remove the attainment hypothesis by finite convex duality Use the [already normalized local entropy](actual_matching_smoothing_angle_capacity.md) V(theta)=2 sum_j[Lambda(theta_j/2)+Lambda((pi-theta_j)/2)], 2pi F(l)=max_(theta>=0,sum theta=pi)(theta.log l+V(theta)). Marked corners are fixed to zero. Let Theta be the product of the remaining compact row simplexes (possibly empty), A its finite-face incidence, and d_f=2pi for each finite face. Define H(d)=max{sum_t V(theta_t):theta in Theta,A theta=d}, with H=-infinity when infeasible. Then the literal log-radius capacity is EXACTLY H(d)/(2pi), even if its positive-radius infimum is not attained. There is no additive constant. Proof. H is concave and upper semicontinuous on its compact domain, by compactness and concavity of V. Weak duality is the local displayed identity. Conversely separate (d,H(d)+epsilon) strictly from the closed hypograph of H. The coefficient of the vertical coordinate is positive: it is nonnegative since the hypograph extends downward; if it were zero, strict separation would contradict d belonging to the projection. Normalize that coefficient to one. The resulting finite affine majorant gives logarithmic radii with capacity at most (H(d)+epsilon)/(2pi). Let epsilon decrease. If d is outside the projection, separation in the finite face coordinates and scaling that separator make the log-radius infimum -infinity instead. ## 2. A loop is infeasible; a two-edge cycle splits exactly For a triangular disk with a simple m-edge boundary and v interior vertices, Euler and 3t=2e_internal+m give t=2v+m-2. This uses incidences with multiplicity and remains true for a one-edge loop or a two-edge parallel cycle, whose boundary has respectively one or two vertices. Because u,v are joined by an actual embedded edge, any simple separating loop or two-edge cycle has a side with NO marked vertex in its interior. An edge joining strictly opposite sides would cross the cycle. Marked vertices on the boundary cause no problem. For a one-edge loop choose that side. It has 2v-1 triangles, with total available angle (2v-1)pi. Its v interior vertices alone demand 2v pi. Thus the angle polytope is empty and the capacity is -infinity. This statement is only about this source capacity; a source vanishing theorem would additionally retain the finite label/forced-factor support. For a two-edge cycle with distinct boundary vertices a,b, the chosen side has 2v triangles. Its interior demands exhaust their entire angle 2v pi. Consequently every a- and b-corner on that side has angle zero. Identify its two boundary edges to obtain a triangular sphere D_in, marked at a,b. Identify the same two edges on the other side to obtain D_out with the original marked pair u,v. The original feasible angle polytope is EXACTLY the Cartesian product of the two resulting angle polytopes. The boundary contributions of D_in are zero, so the full demands on D_out are unchanged, including when a or b was originally marked. Conversely any pair of such assignments glues to a feasible original assignment. Entropy is a sum over the unchanged triangles. Therefore Phi(D)=Phi(D_in;a,b)+Phi(D_out;u,v). The identity includes nonattainment and infeasibility by section1. The new marks a,b are adjacent along the glued boundary edge, so the argument iterates. It does not reset an actual quantum mark or assert factorization of the finite source: it is an exact statement about the already normalized classical source capacity. ## 3. Terminal blocks and finite positive multipliers Repeatedly split parallel-edge two-cycles. Each split has a positive number of triangles on both sides, so the process terminates. If a loop occurs its block is infeasible. Otherwise the terminal blocks have simple underlying graphs. A three-vertex sphere consists of two copies of the same triangle. With its adjacent marked pair a,b the remaining vertex c receives angle pi in each triangle. Its entropy is zero and 2F(0,0,l_c)-log l_c=0. Every other terminal block is a genuine simple triangulated sphere with at least four vertices. Its graph is 3-connected: deleting one or two vertices preserves connectivity by rerouting through their cyclic links (equivalently use the elementary triangulated-sphere argument in the frozen transverse-rank theorem). Such a block has a strictly feasible relative angle assignment. Here is a finite Hall proof rather than a circle-packing existence assumption. Let there be R finite vertices and 2R triangles. Every triangle has at least one finite vertex. For a nonempty proper subset S of finite vertices, put T=finite\S. In the sphere punctured at any vertex of S, the original triangles supported on T union{u,v} are bounded faces of a simple planar graph on |T|+2 vertices. There are at most 2|T|-1 such faces. Hence at least 2|S|+1 original triangles touch S. The required angle of S is only 2|S|pi. The full finite set gives equality of total supply and demand. These strict finite Hall inequalities allow a common small lower bound epsilon>0 on every allowed corner. Singleton rows (the two uv triangles) are fixed at pi and are understood relatively. Maximize total V on this compact feasible polytope. An allowed zero angle cannot occur at a maximizer: moving toward the strictly feasible assignment gives a positive epsilon log(1/epsilon) contribution at every new zero corner, also nonnegative at an old pi corner, while all other contributions have finite first derivative. Thus all nonfixed allowed angles lie strictly between zero and pi. Finite-dimensional Lagrange multipliers now give tan(theta_tf/2)=k_t l_f, l_f>0. The row sum pi forces k_t=(sum_(f<g in t)l_f l_g)^(-1/2), including the two-positive-face rows. These are exactly the local source angles. They attain the radius capacity. Strict concavity makes the angle maximizer unique; connectedness of the finite-face adjacency graph makes its multipliers unique up to common scale. Thus no global attainment hypothesis is needed for these simple terminal blocks. ## 4. Constructing the simple block's actual circle packing Here is an elementary construction, including the development step. It supplies the simple block with its labeled convex polyhedron rather than inferring geometry from the existence of radius multipliers alone. Remove one triangular face abc of the simple sphere. Fix three positive boundary radii r_a,r_b,r_c, hence three mutually externally tangent boundary disks. The remaining triangulated disk has v interior vertices and 2v+1 triangles. Give each interior vertex demand2pi and leave the three boundary demands free, with total pi. Maximize sum_t V(theta_t)+sum_(boundary corners tf)theta_tf log(1/r_f). A strictly positive angle assignment exists by the same finite Hall argument. Treat the three boundary vertices as one supply destination of demand pi, retaining their separate corners. An interior subset S touches at least2|S|+1 disk triangles. Indeed puncture the sphere at a vertex of S and put T=interior\S. The complementary simple planar graph has |T|+3 vertices and at most2|T|+1 bounded triangular faces. The removed boundary face abc is one of them, so at most2|T| are disk triangles; subtracting from2v+1 gives the asserted strict bound. A proper subset consisting of the boundary destination and some interior vertices also has strict Hall slack: its complement T contains only interior vertices, and triangles wholly supported on T are bounded faces of a simple planar graph, at most2|T|-5 when |T|>=3 and none when |T|<=2. The full set has equal total supply and demand. Thus a common positive lower bound on all corners is feasible. The entropy boundary derivative argument of section3 places the maximizer in the open angle simplexes. The fixed boundary log terms have bounded derivatives and do not alter that argument. In particular each boundary angle sum is positive; their sum is pi, so each is strictly less than pi. Lagrange multipliers now give the same tangent-circle angle formula with the prescribed boundary radii and positive finite interior radii. Glue Euclidean triangles with side lengths r_f+r_g. Their angles are exactly those just obtained. Every interior vertex has total angle2pi. The disk therefore has a global orientation-preserving Euclidean development: continuation around each interior vertex has rotation 2pi and zero translation, and such loops generate the punctured disk's holonomy. Its boundary consists of three straight sides, with positive angle sums less than pi and the prescribed strict triangle lengths. It maps once around a convex triangle. This development is an embedding. Indeed it is locally an orientation-preserving isometry at every interior point, including interior vertices. For a point off the developed finite edges, the number of its preimages is its boundary winding number. That number is1 inside the boundary triangle and0 outside. Continuity and local injectivity extend the conclusion across the finite edges and vertices. Place a disk of radius r_f at every developed vertex. The three disks in each triangle are mutually externally tangent. The sector of a vertex disk between that triangle's two incident edges lies inside the triangle: its opposite center segment is covered by the other two tangent disks, which are disjoint from the vertex disk. The separation from that segment is strict: its two pieces lie in the other disks, their unique mutual contact is strictly outside the third positive disk, and the third disk's contacts with those disks lie on the two different incident center edges. Thus it cannot meet a nonincident triangle or acquire an accidental nonedge contact. These sectors assemble to the full disk at an interior vertex because its angle sum is2pi. At a boundary vertex they assemble to the part of the fixed boundary disk inside the carrier triangle. Thus different disks have disjoint interiors, and the only contacts are the actual triangulation edges. Restoring the omitted outer face gives the exact labeled sphere packing. Arbitrary separating triangles cause no problem: the development uses every triangle, not an assumed three-connected drawing of only part of the graph. For completeness, its right-angled polyhedron has a direct support certificate. For each bounded triangle the circle through its three contact points is its Euclidean incircle: on a center edge fg the incircle contact is at distance r_f from f. It is orthogonal to the three vertex disks. Its disk lies in that center triangle and contains no other packing contact. For the omitted outer triangle take the opposite side of its contact circle; all interior disks and contacts lie in its bounded curvilinear gap and hence inside that circle. Consequently every packing contact lies in all the prescribed inward white and shaded halfspaces, strictly unless incident to that face. The convex hull of the contacts has precisely the white cyclic facets and these shaded triangles: they form the closed labeled sphere of supporting faces, with no missing face or extra ideal vertex. At each contact, its two white and two shaded planes have the prescribed cyclic order and successive right angles. This is the actual convex ideal right-angled polyhedron Q_block of this labeled block. ## 5. Absolute capacity and independence of the adjacent marked pair Choose ANY adjacent pair of white vertices in this simple block, and send their contact to infinity by one orientation-preserving Mobius map. The two corresponding disks become the opposite marked halfplanes; all other disks stay bounded and disjoint in their common strip. Their positive curvatures satisfy the source angle equations, and therefore attain the capacity with that marked pair. The already proved actual facet-coning normalization gives Phi(block;any adjacent marked pair)=Vol(Q_block)/pi. It is independent of that pair. There is no source scalar or additive volume constant: the local normalization V(pi,0,0)=0 and section1's exact duality fix it. The double-triangle block has capacity0 instead and is not declared a nondegenerate ideal polyhedron. Combining this construction with section2 expresses every finite smoothed capacity in the stated class as a sum of these actual block polyhedron volumes divided by pi, with zero from double-triangle blocks. The new pair on a cut block is a geometric/capacity choice; no original quantum mark has been moved. ## 6. The remaining topology and strict-comparison questions This does not by itself identify the blocks as the hyperbolic JSJ pieces of the smoothed marked exterior. That assertion requires the actual cut gluing, peripheral maps and possible Seifert pieces. Nor does the decomposition compare their summed capacity strictly with the original unsmoothed capacity: the L_1 operation merges the opposite b,c faces, and is not the old white-edge xy contraction. These two remaining questions are not consequences of circle-packing existence. Finite-N care: a two-cycle can cut two MAIN edges or two MATCHING edges. In the latter case retained forced polynomials couple the two sides away from the odd maximal fold. Thus this capacity product is not a claimed all-level source product. Degree-two blocks can have zero capacity while still enforcing exact even-level zeros, as the parallel Belt examples already demonstrate. ## 7. Focused verification [The focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_smoothed_source_capacity_blocks.py) and its saved results check eight digon LP systems and their separate factors, five genuine loop cellulations with infeasible demands,474 exact marked planar Hall cuts with21 independent positive LP assignments, and158 fixed-boundary Hall cuts with seven positive disk assignments. Fourteen actual disk developments include tetrahedral, bipyramidal and separating-triangle stacked spheres, with equal and unequal boundary radii. The audit checks232 disk pairs,1572 shaded supporting inequalities,348 white/shaded right angles and42 independent adjacent mark capacity evaluations. The geometric solve uses floating-point arithmetic, with maximum residual below3.2e-13; the subsequent entropy evaluation uses40 digits. Its marked-capacity spread is below2.6e-26. These are independent numerical diagnostics of the finite construction, not a numerical substitute for the all-block proof. A glued two-block example also checks the genuinely nonattained primal capacity against its exact dual block sum at four diverging radius scales. The positive primal excess decreases toward zero; the double-triangle capacity is checked separately. No finite quantum factorization or strict smoothing loss is tested or inferred. Capacity decomposition, finite quantum factorization and an actual JSJ decomposition are different claims. The universal strict smoothing comparison remains unproved.

title: A fixed-radius smoothing bound and its explicit limitation
status: Sufficient source bound; matched-graph capacity obstruction
text: # A fixed-radius smoothing bound and its explicit limitation 30 October 2026. ; source-coverage correction below. A one-variable test at the original positive face variables gives a strict source upper bound after a literal untwisted L_1 insertion. It needs neither a balanced split nor an attained smoothed capacity. The test is not universal: an explicit certified family below makes its best possible gap tend to minus infinity. This is a failure of fixed old radii, not a counterexample to a fully optimized smoothing gap or a volume conjecture. The family is proved as a labeled right-angled MATCHED-GRAPH capacity example. Its identification with the fixed flat-plat source coefficient is conditional on an additional source-preserving presentation adapter; section3 does not supply that adapter. ## 1. An exact sufficient source test Use the original connected certified source, actual marked faces u,v, and the normalization of [the smoothing capacity theorem](actual_matching_smoothing_angle_capacity.md). Let a specified UNTWISTED port have triangles (x,b,y),(x,c,y). Its replacement L_1=I deletes those two triangles and identifies b,c. Assume the resulting projection is connected, the marked faces remain distinct, and b,c are distinct unmarked faces. All repeated incidences after the identification are retained. The deleted port's original half twist must be zero; a remaining R^epsilon is not an identity. Let l^0 be the original positive finite face curvatures (reciprocals of Euclidean circle radii), with the two marked line variables zero. The established term "fixed-radius bound" refers to these face variables; it does not identify them with Euclidean radii. Write F for the source-normalized local fold rate, with F(t l_0,t l_1,t l_2)=F(l_0,l_1,l_2)+(1/2)log t, partial_(log l_j) F=theta_j/(2pi), theta_j=2atan(l_j/sqrt(l_0 l_1+l_1 l_2+l_2 l_0)). (1) At a one-positive-variable triple the nonzero angle is pi. These are the continuous boundary values, not a different local model. The exact original action is Phi_old=sum_(all triangles) F(l_t^0) -sum_(old finite faces) log l_f^0. For s real, replace BOTH b,c by z=exp(s), leaving every other finite face variable at l^0. Sum over the actual remaining triangles, and count the merged face only once in the target monomial. Define P_sm(s)=sum_(remaining triangles) F(l_t(s)) -sum_(smoothed finite faces) log l_f(s), G(s)=Phi_old-P_sm(s). (2) If G(s_*)=g>0 for one finite s_*, then the original marked contraction with that L_1 insertion and all other circles complete satisfies limsup_(N->infinity) N^-1 log|A_N^(L1)| <=Phi_old-g. (3) Every retained half twist on another port stays in its exact source sum. Its channel phase has modulus one, so the upper bound is valid with those phases. The original mark, N-power measure, multiplicities, beta factors, and full range of every remaining channel are retained. Proof: the exact marked face-coefficient theorem applies to the literal shorter diagram. For each label assignment its positive coefficient is bounded by evaluation at the shared radii in (2), divided by its actual target monomial. The degenerate local cases in the smoothing theorem bound every original beta^2 D D P factor by its fold rate at these same radii. Finite labels and original scalar factors contribute only a polynomial in N. Taking the sum in absolute value proves (3). No minimizer of the smoothed capacity is used. If a remaining source factor is identically zero, the bound is already stronger. The statement does not move the mark or substitute a second boundary trace. Log-radius convexity of F makes P_sm convex, hence G concave. Its derivative is the explicit actual incidence sum G'(s)=1-(1/(2pi))sum_(remaining b/c corners) theta_corner(s). (4) If a triangle acquires the merged label twice, both corners occur in this sum. Thus the best test in (2) is a one-dimensional convex minimization, with no split-side imbalance hypothesis. It may hold when the full smoothed minimizer escapes to a boundary. It is only a sufficient test; section3 proves that it need not hold at all. ## 2. Boundary regularization and the precise charged extension The strict bound has a useful continuity margin. Set the two marked face variables to small FIXED positive values eta_u,eta_v before coefficient extraction. Keep their target exponents zero, and keep all other target exponents d=N-1. Each nonzero local triple in (2) has a continuous F limit as eta_u,eta_v tend to zero. Hence these values can be fixed sufficiently small that the new evaluation rate is at most Phi_old-g/2. This does not assign target degree d to a marked face and does not take a quantum-level-dependent limit. More precisely, let P_N be one of the actual nonnegative-coefficient polynomial products after smoothing, including beta factors, and let n* be the actual target vector. At the fixed positive evaluation l*, any integer shift nu obeys |[L^(n*+nu)]P_N| <= P_N(l*)/(l*)^(n*) exp(C_l ||nu||_1). (5) A negative target exponent gives zero. Phased identifications such as c=Q^p b cost nothing in this bound: take absolute values of the polynomial coefficients before evaluation. A finite sum of such specified coefficients with total scalar norm at most N^C C_0^H and ||nu||_1<=C_1 H therefore costs only N^C exp(C_2 H) in addition to the regularized capacity. If H<=delta N with delta sufficiently small, it still has a strict exponential gap. Equation(5) is a coefficient bound, NOT an already proved L_h source expansion. Actual L_h paths retain their unwrapped physical endpoints, their c=Q^p b identifications and all clock charges. In particular, after a charged modular face average a target congruence can cross N and admit a new exponent shifted by an ENTIRE N, not merely O(h). Those aliases are not controlled by (5) with H=O(h). They must either be excluded by the actual support or be estimated separately. The fixed positive marked radii resolve the elementary Laurent-coefficient bound; they do not silently remove these finite-source questions. No signed deleted-port R^epsilon norm is discarded. ## 3. A certified matched-graph family where the capacity test fails The initial white triangulation is the octahedral sphere with equator 0,1,2,3 and poles4,5: its triangles are (p,j,j+1 modulo4), p=4,5, j=0,1,2,3. Mark the actual MAIN edge23. Choose the matching edges of the dual cubic source by the white edges {01,12,34,35}. (6) They cover each triangle exactly once, and do not contain the marked edge. Starting with b_0=5, insert b_n into the triangular interstice (0,1,b_(n-1)), replacing that triangle by its three subdivisions. Add the matching white edge b_(n-1)b_n at each step; the matching edge01 stays. This is again a perfect matching: the new triangle (0,1,b_n) inherits01, while the other two new triangles are paired by b_(n-1)b_n. The complement is the actual union of main cycles. To specify the marked diagram, use this EMBEDDED dual cubic graph, not just its abstract isomorphism class. Replace a small neighborhood of every selected matching edge by the standard untwisted complete crossing-circle box, with its four main half-edges in their inherited cyclic order. Join these half-edges along the complementary embedded edges, and put the original mark on edge23. This is an explicit augmented-link diagram. Each subdivision above replaces one trivalent source vertex in a small disk by a three-vertex triangle, retaining its three external ports and adding the specified matching edge. It therefore preserves this literal construction and its marking; no assertion that an arbitrary abstract cubic graph is an admissible source is needed. A Morse presentation gives its actual cups, caps, and complete-circle tensors. This construction does NOT prove that the diagram has the fixed flat-plat presentation required by the [marked face-coefficient theorem](../papers/filling-bounds/README.md), sections1--3, with the same designated circle ports and mark. That theorem's gap sweep and marked conservation argument cannot simply be imported into an arbitrary Morse presentation. Neither a uniform bridge width over this family nor a source-preserving flat-plat adapter at a fixed depth is established here. Here is the labeled geometric certificate, not just a combinatorial example. In the boundary plane use the two marked parallel lines y=0 and y=2 for faces3 and2. The four finite initial circles have face0: center(0,1/2), radius1/2; face1: center(0,3/2), radius1/2; face4: center(-sqrt2,1), radius1; face5: center(+sqrt2,1), radius1. The inserted circles have center and radius center(b_n)=((2n+sqrt2)/B_n,1), radius(b_n)=1/B_n, B_n=4n^2+4sqrt2 n+1. (7) They are tangent to circles0,1 and b_(n-1), and lie strictly inside that triangle's old interstice. These statements follow directly by squaring the center distances; equivalently their curvatures satisfy the positive Descartes recurrence with the two fixed curvatures2,2. All other old circles and contacts are unchanged. Thus this is a labeled packing with precisely the stated triangulation at every n. Its halfspace certificate can also be read directly. Take the geodesic planes of these white circles and the circles through the three contact points of each complementary triangle. The latter are orthogonal to its three white circles. Their inward halfspaces give the initial ideal right-angled cuboctahedron. Each insertion attaches the ideal right-angled octahedron with the three old and three new contact points along the old shaded triangle. Its adjacent white planes are the same planes, so the seams are flat and all remaining dihedral angles are pi/2. The three new outward shaded disks are contained in the old outward shaded disk and tangent to its boundary at the old contacts. Every new ideal vertex satisfies all the other old supporting inequalities, strictly when it is not incident to that facet. Thus the coplanar seams disappear and the union is the intersection of precisely the retained and new inward halfspaces; it is convex, rather than merely locally right-angled. Induction gives a convex ideal right-angled polyhedron with the exact new labeled facets. No unlabeled volume match is used as a certificate. Consequently the labeled packing face curvatures are exactly l_0=l_1=2, l_4=l_5=1, l_2=l_3=0, l_(b_j)=B_j. The dual cubic graph is 3-connected: the initial cube is 3-connected, and replacing a vertex by its three-edge triangle preserves this property. Remove the matching port01 and its two triangles (0,1,b_n),(0,1,4), and merge b_n with4. The remaining projection is connected (already deleting the two old cubic vertices leaves a connected graph), and the marked faces2,3 remain distinct. Thus this is the literal opposite matching-edge smoothing of this marked graph. Applying section1 to its actual quantum source would additionally require the presentation adapter just specified. The geometric and capacity calculations do not require the main cycles to have one component. Only five remaining triangle terms depend on the new common radius z: two are (2,B_(n-1),z), two are (2,z,0), and one is (z,0,0). The graph capacity functional (2) is therefore exactly G_n(z)=C_n-2F(2,B_(n-1),z)-2F(2,z,0)+(1/2)log z, C_n=F(2,B_n,2)+2F(2,B_(n-1),B_n) +F(2,1,2)+2F(2,1,0)-log B_n. (8) This includes both deleted triangles and the changed face-target monomial. In particular it is not just a comparison of local volumes. We prove the obstruction uniformly over ALL z>0. Monotonicity and homogeneity of F give 2F(2,B_(n-1),z)>=log B_(n-1), 2F(2,z,0)>=log max(2,z). Thus the z-dependent expression in (8) is bounded above by its n-dependent constant minus (1/2)|log(z/2)|. Evaluation at z=2 and the following limits show that its maximizers stay in one fixed compact subset of (0,infinity). On that compact, continuity and homogeneity give uniformly F(2,B_n,2)=(1/2)log B_n+o(1), F(2,B_(n-1),B_n)=(1/2)log B_n+F(0,1,1)+o(1), 2F(2,B_(n-1),z)=log B_(n-1)+o(1). The limiting z-dependent function is -2F(2,z,0)+(1/2)log z. Its derivative vanishes only when the angle at z is pi/2, namely at z=2; strict log-radius convexity makes this its unique maximum. Substituting in (8) proves sup_(z>0) G_n(z)=-log n+K+o(1), K=F(2,1,2)+2F(2,1,0)-(3/2)log2. (9) In particular the best fixed-old-radius test is NEGATIVE for every sufficiently large n. Full radius readjustment is essential here. This does not say that the fully optimized smoothed capacity exceeds the original capacity: the former is an infimum over ALL remaining radii, whereas (8) varies only the merged radius. ## 4. Remaining general comparison Literal smoothing identifies opposite middle faces. It is not ordinary deletion of the shared white edge01, and a generic graph-minor volume inequality is not automatically its capacity inequality. Section3 also rules out promoting the one-variable test to a theorem forced by every positive labeled certificate. The general connected untwisted smoothing gap and its near-complete small-color corridor are now [proved separately](actual_smoothed_block_representation_volume.md) in the original fixed flat-plat scope. That theorem does not provide the missing presentation adapter for the family in section3. The present note retains its exact sufficient source bound in section1 and its independent matched-graph functional limitation. Signed varied ports and far-color source bounds remain separate. Focused audit: [original source and labeled certificate checks](../experiments/audit_actual_smoothing_fixed_radius_gap.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_smoothing_fixed_radius_gap_results.json). At 80 digits it checks ten literal original marked L_1 contractions against the shorter face-coefficient source, retaining every remaining half twist and the original cups, mark, and measure. These original matrix fixtures test section1; they are NOT the Apollonian graphs of section3 and do not establish the missing adapter. The audit also checks two symbolic tangency identities; nine perfect matchings, three-connected graphs, and connected literal smoothings; 2,340 white and 3,816 shaded support values; and 432 original right-angle incidences. Seven finite optimized one-variable profiles and one positive-marked regularization check diagnose the exact normalization. The analytic argument, not those finite profiles, proves the all-n limitation in (9). No full optimized smoothing gap or L_h alias bound is inferred. Condition (3) is sufficient. The charge and alias qualifications after (5), and the fixed-old-face scope of the counterfamily, remain essential. ### Source-coverage correction, 30 October 2026 The family in Section 3 proves the geometric matched-graph capacity obstruction (9). It is not a source counterexample to the fixed-radius strategy: the exact face identity proves a fixed flat-plat formula, whereas that inference would require a general Morse formula. A link-to-plat isotopy alone does not preserve the designated complete-circle tensors, mark or face-coefficient normalization.

title: An exact spectral total derivative for the original root source
status: Exact full-Hermite spectral derivative; global estimate open
text: # An exact spectral total derivative for the original root source , 31 October 2026. This is an exact fixed-root identity for the original pair Casimir, retaining its simple and repeated spectral nodes. No contour deformation or uniform exponential estimate is asserted. Put N>=3,d=N-1,q=exp(pi i/N). Let chi(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2, and let Omega be the ACTUAL pair Casimir from the [original source theorem](../papers/filling-bounds/README.md). Define its polynomial resolvent numerator V(z)=chi(z)(z-Omega)^(-1). This is the unique degree-(N-1) matrix polynomial supplied by polynomial division and chi(Omega)=0. It is not the determinant adjugate of the full N^2-dimensional matrix. At a paired c=2cos(phi), its resolvent is (z-Omega)^(-1)=P/(z-c)+Q/(z-c)^2+regular. Write h(z)=chi(z)/(z-c)^2 locally. The Chebyshev ODE gives h(c)=N^2/(4-c^2), h'(c)/h(c)=c/(4-c^2). Consequently Q=V(c)/h(c) and P=V'(c)/h(c)-h'(c)V(c)/h(c)^2. With Qhat(z)=(4-z^2)V(z)/N^2 this is Q=Qhat(c), P=Qhat'(c)+c Qhat(c)/(4-c^2). For any function f holomorphic at the spectral nodes, therefore, f(c)P+f'(c)Q =[(4-c^2)(fV)'(c)-c f(c)V(c)]/N^2 =-d_phi[2sin(phi) f(2cos(phi))V(2cos(phi))/N^2]. (1) When N is odd, the simple node is c=-2, chi'(-2)=N^2, and the right side of (1) at phi=pi is 2f(-2)P_*. Thus the original simple term has exactly one half of that derivative. Each paired node occurs twice in the full odd-angle grid and the derivatives are equal there. The exact original operator is accordingly f(Omega)=-1/2 sum_(k=0)^(N-1) B_f'(phi_k), B_f(phi)=2sin(phi) f(2cos(phi))V(2cos(phi))/N^2, phi_k=(2k+1)pi/N. (2) No cyclic physical head is introduced: the cyclic variable in (2) is the spectral parameter, with the original projector multiplicities. For R^n use its [exact full-Hermite Gaussian](actual_direct_long_power_source.md) f(2cos(phi))=q^(n d^2/4) exp[-n(phi-pi)^2/(2hbar)], hbar=2pi i/N, 0<=phi<=2pi. On this interval B_f has equal zero endpoint values and equal first derivatives. Its second derivatives can differ at the endpoints, reflecting the K-cut at z=2. Thus its periodic extension is C^1, but endpoint currents must be retained in further integration by parts. In particular the zero Fourier integral of -B_f' is exactly zero. With Fourier convention hat B(j)=(2pi)^(-1)int_0^(2pi) B(phi)e^(-ijphi)dphi, the finite midpoint formula gives the convergent fixed-N identity f(Omega)=-(iN^2/2)sum_(ell in Z) ell (-1)^ell hat B(Nell). (3) The ell=0 term is zero. For each fixed N,n the sum is absolutely convergent: periodic B is C^1 with piecewise smooth higher derivatives, so hat B(j)=O(j^-3). Constants here may depend exponentially on N; this observation gives no uniform global bound. Formula (3) is an alternative exact source period, closely related to the existing [Fourier-Hermite Gaussian formulas](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_coherent_filling_gaussian_chirp.md). It does not erase their endpoint currents or determine which nonzero charge contributes after sewing. ## Why complete-channel samples do not control the derivative At a paired node, L_N(c)=0 and L_N'(c)=(-1)^(N-1)N/(2sin^2(phi)). Hence its complete sector equals L_N'(c)Q=(-1)^(N-1)2V(c)/N. The complete positive packet therefore controls V(c), whereas V'(c) also carries the independent semisimple projector P. The simplest illustration is a diagonal coefficient on the face boundary x=y=0: Omega is diagonal there, so at a paired eigenvalue c its entry V(z)=chi(z)/(z-c) vanishes at z=c, but V'(c)=chi''(c)/2 is nonzero. At even N every spectral node is paired, so all corresponding complete diagonal samples vanish while the semisimple derivatives reconstruct the identity. This example concerns the ACTUAL local polynomial specialization, not a freely chosen off-grid interpolation. Thus the proved exponential interpolation of complete packet values cannot simply be differentiated to estimate (2) or (3). A bound on the original polynomial resolvent numerator between nodes, including its semisimple derivative and the retained endpoint charges, is an additional input. No claim that such a bound is impossible is made. ## Exact link to the retained physical colors Polynomial division of the Chebyshev identity gives, in the SAME original Casimir quotient, V(z)=U_(N-1)(Omega/2) +2sum_(h=1)^(N-1)T_(N-h)(z/2)U_(h-1)(Omega/2) =(-1)^d L_N +2sum_(h=1)^(N-1)(-1)^(h-1)T_(N-h)(z/2)L_h. (4) One proof starts from [T_N(x)-T_N(y)]/(x-y)=U_(N-1)(y) +2sum_(h=1)^(N-1)T_(N-h)(x)U_(h-1)(y), then substitutes x=z/2,y=Omega/2 and T_N(Omega/2)=-1. The scalar polynomial identity also follows immediately by induction in N using the two Chebyshev recurrences. It was checked exactly for N=2,...,14 before recording it here. The homogeneous source and every actual exterior functional preserve (4) by linearity. Thus controlling the original off-node numerator means controlling a SPECIFIED coherent combination of all physical colors, with their signs. It is not determined by the complete packet alone. On the other hand a bound on this coherent combination could be sharper than bounds on its separate colors, so (4) is not a no-go statement for a phase-preserving resolvent method. ## Validation and scope The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_spectral_total_derivative_source.py) uses the original coproduct Casimir and independently built signed R matrices. It checks all monomials through degree N-1 and powers n=+/-1,...,+/-5 at N=3,...,8, including both parity conventions. The divided-Chebyshev identity is also checked symbolically at N=2,...,14. [Results](../experiments/actual_spectral_total_derivative_source_results.json) record finite identities; they assert no uniform Fourier constants. The theorem is at a fixed root of unity. It does not establish a uniform Fourier estimate or select a contributing cycle.

title: A positive supported Racah factorial, its metric and retained partner current
text: # A positive supported Racah factorial, its metric and retained partner current 29 October 2026. This is an independent finite FACTORIAL theorem. It does not assume that a proposed four-port source coefficient is a Racah sum. On the full folded supported chamber it proves a common phase, a positive root normalization, a uniform positive Laplace principle, and polynomial relative bounds for every fixed generic-q normal jet. Complementary high partners have the same positive value core but an additional explicitly retained normal current. Connecting these formulas to the actual source requires its separate typed coefficient identity. A positive root value is not by itself a bound on a complete Hermite recoupling operator. ## 1. Seven factorials, with a root unit at every denominator Fix N>=3, D=N-1, M=floor(D/2), q=exp(pi i/N), and six INTEGER folded spins 0<=a,b,c,d,e,f<=M. Define four faces and three quads F=(a+b+e, c+d+e, a+d+f, b+c+f), Q=(a+b+c+d, a+c+e+f, b+d+e+f). (1) Assume every F_i>=D. Every face is an ordinary triangle: its two smaller entries sum to at least D minus its largest, which is at least its largest because D>=2M. Moreover EVERY face deficit F_i-2ell lies in [0,D]. Every difference Q_k-F_i is one such deficit of a complementary face. Therefore z_-=max F_i <= z_+=min Q_k, D<=z_-<=z_+<=4M<=2D, 0<=z-F_i<=D, 0<=Q_k-z<=D. (2) Use the GENUINE generic symmetric factorial [n]!_zeta, with [u]_zeta=(zeta^u-zeta^-u)/(zeta-zeta^-1). Set S(zeta)=sum_(z=z_-)^(z_+) (-1)^z [z+1]! /[product_i [z-F_i]! product_k[Q_k-z]!]. (3) No negative factorial is assigned a value: the displayed interval is the true finite range. By (2), every denominator is a unit at q. The numerator contains EXACTLY ONE factor [N]. Factoring it BEFORE specialization defines the analytic function G(zeta)=(-1)^D S(zeta)/[N]_zeta. (4) Let s_r=product_(u=1)^r 2sin(pi u/N), s_0=1. The exact positive root value is R_N:=G(q)=N sum_z s_(z-D) /[product_i s_(z-F_i) product_k s_(Q_k-z)]>0. (5) Indeed the signs of [N+1],...,[z+1] multiply to (-1)^(z+1-N). Together with (-1)^(D+z) this is +1. Also s_D=N. The powers of 2sin(pi/N) cancel, since sum_i(z-F_i)+sum_k(Q_k-z)=z, sum_i F_i=sum_k Q_k=2(a+b+c+d+e+f). Thus (5) is a finite exact identity, including boundary faces F_i=D, collapsed z intervals, both level parities and composite levels. ## 2. The exact positive face metric For a face (x,y,z) of sum F, define the generic squared triangle factor and its regular normalization by Delta_F^2=[F-2x]![F-2y]![F-2z]!/[F+1]!, D_F(zeta)=(-1)^(F-D)[N]_zeta Delta_F^2. It is analytic and nonzero at q, with positive root value d_F=D_F(q) =s_(F-2x)s_(F-2y)s_(F-2z)/(N s_(F-D))>0. (6) The natural positive normalized scalar is W_N=R_N sqrt(product_faces d_F). (7) This metric is not optional in a geometric interpretation. The branch-independent generic squared identity is EXACTLY [N]^2 S(zeta)^2 product_faces Delta_F^2 =G(zeta)^2 product_faces D_F(zeta). (8) The root of its right side is W_N^2>0. There is no residual sign, because sum_faces(F-D)=2(a+b+c+d+e+f)-4D is even. Equation(8) defines a finite factorial normalization; it is not a claim that an as-yet-unproved physical recoupling matrix is unitary in this metric. The ordered physical Clebsch norms, source gamma factors and any intermediate quantum dimensions must still be matched by an actual coefficient theorem. A quantum dimension can vanish at the odd simple endpoint. It is not canceled by evaluating (7) alone; its generic source limit must be retained before interpreting this as a physical Gram. ## 3. A uniform positive action on the ENTIRE folded chamber Put L(t)=integral_0^t log(2sin(pi u))du on [0,1], continuously at both endpoints. Write x=(a,b,c,d,e,f)/N, D_N=D/N, and use the same linear forms F_i(x),Q_k(x). On I_N=[max_i F_i(x),min_k Q_k(x)] define A_N(x,Z)=L(Z-D_N)-sum_i L(Z-F_i(x)) -sum_k L(Q_k(x)-Z), V_N(x,Z)=A_N(x,Z) +(1/2)sum_faces[sum_(ell in face)L(F(x)-2x_ell) -L(F(x)-D_N)]. (9) Uniformly over ALL allowed integral labels, log R_N=N max_(Z in I_N) A_N(x,Z)+O(log N), log W_N=N max_(Z in I_N) V_N(x,Z)+O(log N). (10) Proof. Every factorial index is in [0,D], so the uniform elementary sine-factorial estimate log s_r=N L(r/N)+O(log N) applies to every term, including endpoints. There are at most 2N positive terms. Their maximum gives the upper bound and one term gives the lower. The modulus of continuity of L is O(epsilon log(1/epsilon)); rounding Z to a feasible integral index changes N times the action by at most O(log N). All constants are independent of the labels. The same estimate applied to the four explicit factors (6) proves the second line. Thus no cancellation or selected complex saddle is required. For any convergent scaled-label sequence, (10) yields the corresponding max-action limit, with D_N replaced by 1. This is an action theorem; identification with an actual geometric tetrahedron is a separate task. Two calibrations expose the metric's role. At all six scaled labels 1/3, the bare action maximum is 3v3/pi, whereas the face metric adds -2v3/pi and the normalized maximum is v3/pi. At all six labels 1/2, the metric action is zero and the normalized maximum is v8/pi. Here v3=3Lambda(pi/3), v8=8Lambda(pi/4). The maxima occur respectively at Z=7/6 and Z=7/4, by direct differentiation of (9). The independently proved [local hyperideal geometry theorem](actual_four_port_hyperideal_angle_volume.md) now identifies this normalized maximum with actual truncated-tetrahedron volume. Its exact Casimir angle coordinates are a_ell=(ell+1/2)/N. Using Z=(z+7/4)/N shifts the numerator factorial argument by 3/(4N), each denominator argument by 1/(4N), and every face-metric argument by 1/(2N). The same uniform endpoint modulus gives the SHARP scalar bound log W_N=(N/pi)Vol_ext(T(a_ell))+O(log N) (10a) on the entire supported chamber, with a universal error constant. Vol_ext denotes the continuous boundary-volume extension when an odd simple channel has zero dihedral angle. This is a local scalar energy calibration, not a proof that a source graph supplies the corresponding cell gluing or a completed Hermite metric. ## 4. Polynomial relative generic normal jets, not just root values Take zeta=q exp(t), with ALL integer labels fixed, and cancel the single displayed [N] in each term of (3). This is the actual generic factorial germ, not a formal root recurrence continued off the root. There is a universal c>0 such that on |t|<=r_N=c/[N^2(1+log N)] (11) the functions G and each D_F are holomorphic and nonzero, and their ratios to their positive root values differ from one by less than 1/4. The canonical analytic square roots of D_F, positive at t=0, therefore define H(t)=G(t) product_F sqrt(D_F(t)), with H(0)=W_N. Shrinking the SAME universal c if necessary gives |H/H(0)-1|<1/4. Here is a uniform proof. After cancellation, all factors zeta-zeta^-1 cancel too, by the factorial degree equality used in section1. Every remaining factor is zeta^u-zeta^-u, 1<=u<2N, u!=N. At t=0 its absolute value is at least 4 dist(u,N Z)/N. For |t|<=N^-2, its derivative has absolute value at most 30N. Thus each unit factor's logarithmic change is bounded by 15N^2|t|/dist(u,N Z) when that relative change is small. Across a summand there are at most eighteen copies of the harmonic sum sum_(k=1)^N 1/k; the four face factors have the same fixed bound. Consequently each product ratio has logarithmic change at most C N^2(1+log N)|t|, with universal C. Choosing, for example, a sufficiently small c<=10^-6 makes every summand stay in a small common sector around its POSITIVE value in (5). A positive weighted sum stays in that sector as well. This proves (11), including the nonzero lower bound and analytic square roots. Cauchy's inequality now gives, for every fixed k>=0 and F=G or H, |F^(k)(0)|/k! <=2 r_N^-k F(0), |(1/F)^(k)(0)|/k! <=2 r_N^-k/F(0). (12) Thus finite normal jets and inverse scalar jets have polynomial relative cost UNIFORMLY throughout this folded supported chamber. This scalar assertion does not estimate a change of physical frame. Together with (10a), it bounds squared fixed normal jets by a polynomial times exp[(2N/pi)Vol_ext(T(a_ell))], with all joint labels still shared. ## 5. Complementary partners: positive value core and a real missing current Now replace ANY subset of the six folded labels ell by D-ell. At each face, its new deficits are old deficits, their complements D-old_deficit, the old excess F-D, or its complement D-(F-D). They all lie in [0,D]. Its new sum lies in [D,2D]. Therefore (2)'s denominator-unit assertion survives at EVERY one of the up to 64 partner assignments, and the new z range is nonempty with z_-<=2D. Also the sum of its six labels is at most 4D, because every new face has sum at most 2D. Hence z_+<=8D/3<3N-1. The generic sum still contains [N] in every term, but some terms now contain [2N] too. The EXACT decomposition is (-1)^D S(zeta)/[N]_zeta=C(zeta)+[2N]_zeta T(zeta), (13) where C sums the TRUE terms z<=2D after deleting the numerator [N], and T sums the terms z>=2N-1 after deleting BOTH [N] and [2N]. All their denominators are units. At q the nonempty core is exactly the positive expression (5), with z truncated at 2D. The positive metric (6) and squared identity (8) apply at every partner value too. The core C has the same polynomial scalar-jet bound as section4. The term [2N]T is NOT zero as a generic normal. In particular ((-1)^D S/[N])'(0)=C'(0)+(4N/(q-q^-1))T(0). (14) Writing z=2N-1+k, its retained root value is explicitly T(0)=-2sin(pi/N)N^2 sum_k (-1)^k s_k /[product_i s_(2N-1+k-F_i) product_j s_(Q_j-2N+1-k)]. (15) Every index in (15) is physical. The alternating sum must remain coherent. Its absolute-value envelope is not a substitute for it. For example N=4, partner labels (2,2,2,2,2,1) arise by five flips from the supported folded labels (1,1,1,1,1,1). Their faces are (6,6,5,5), quads (8,7,7). Core z=6 gives C(0)=sqrt(2), while the single tail term z=7 gives T(0)=-1. The EXTRA first normal in (14) is exactly 8sqrt(2)i. Deleting the tail loses actual data. Accordingly (12) is a theorem for the complete LOW-fold scalar germ and for partner value cores. It is NOT asserted for the full partner germ without a further coherent estimate for T. Nor are the partner columns deleted from a physical Hermite cluster. This is the remaining normal interface for using the positive factorial in a full recoupling energy argument. A research lead, originally unproved, is preserved by the [64-partner value diagnostic](../experiments/diagnose_supported_racah_partner_value_reflection.py) and its [recorded root images](../experiments/supported_racah_partner_value_reflection_diagnostic_results.json). For three specified folded tuples per level when distinct, every one of the 64 complement bit patterns was checked at N=3,...,10: 1408 comparisons showed no failure of W_squared invariance. These are exact finite cyclotomic-root images, not a uniform complex identity proof. No symmetry of generic germs, bound on the [2N] current, completed physical Gram or volume theorem is inferred from that observation. The subsequent [actual partner-reflection theorem](actual_racah_partner_reflection_identity.md) now proves the root-value symmetry uniformly from the actual reciprocal source and analytic projector residues. Its exact first-normal counterexample shows why this does not establish generic-jet symmetry. ## 6. An exact valuation interface to the separately proved physical kernel The preceding factorial theorem has not used a source identity. One can now APPLY the independently proved [actual inverse four-port theorem](actual_general_four_port_single_racah_kernel.md), equations (23),(24). Put its external highest weights (A,B,C,D_ext)=(2a,2b,2c,2d), E=2e and G=2f. It states L_(G,E)=chi_E X_E/(b_G J_n S0 V_n) *S, p=min(a+d,b+c), q=max(a+d,b+c), s=p+q, n=p-f, t0=q-p, V_n=zeta^n (Q^(-p-f-1);Q)_n /[F_n(Q^(t0+1);Q)_n(Q^(-s-1);Q)_n]. (16) Throughout the fully supported folded chamber, chi_E X_E, b_G and J_n are root units, while S0 has exactly one [N] zero. This follows directly from the source product formulas: all their physical factorial indices are <=D, whereas the numerator of S0 is [s+1]! with D<=s<=2D. For X_E at its endpoint, its numerator index is <=A when that endpoint is H, and <=B when it is A. Hence no endpoint root zero has been hidden in that assertion. Both f faces imply p+f>=D and q+f>=D. The sole possible numerator zero of V_n is at index k=p+f-D. It is INSIDE 0,...,n-1 exactly when 2f<D. Its denominator has no root zero: t0+n=q-f<=D, and the first potential zero in (Q^(-s-1);Q)_n has index s-D>=n. Consequently the actual inverse coefficient has exact order ord_q L_(G,E)=-1 if 2f<D, ord_q L_(G,E)= 0 if 2f=D. (17) Its leading coefficient is nonzero by the positive finite sum (5). Thus a positive root factorial does NOT turn the uncompleted physical coefficient matrix into a finite positive operator: paired output channels have genuine simple poles and must be combined with their partners in a regular Hermite frame. The same bookkeeping in the actual ordered invariant norm N_E=n_(ab)^e n_(cd)^e [2e+1] gives order two for paired e and order one for odd simple e. These are source-frame orders, not optional quantum-dimension factors. Equations (16),(17) supply an explicit local interface for matching the positive metric (6) to a completed physical recoupling energy; they do not complete that matching or bound the partner current (15). Audit: [true root factorials, partner ranges and retained Taylor coefficients](../experiments/audit_actual_supported_racah_common_phase_and_normal_metric.py). The common phase, metric, uniform action and jet arguments above are independent of the proposed actual four-port source identity. The result does not include a full partner-jet bound or a positive completed physical recoupling Gram.

title: A tame Hermite frame for the original source channel
text: # A tame Hermite frame for the original source channel 29 October 2026. The colliding c_0 Casimir channel containing the original cup has an explicit generalized vector with harmonic-sum coefficients. Its source-adapted Hermite frame has UNIFORMLY bounded physical condition number after a common N^(3/2) scale. In that frame the original marked and ordinary caps are exactly the two coordinate rows, and the full crossing is a unit scalar times a Jordan matrix with uniformly bounded off-diagonal coefficient. This proves an actual source-controlled Hermite Gram for the selected T=N-1 channel, including its derivative direction. It does not estimate recoupling from this channel into all other channels on overlapping pairs. No full-channel q-Racah norm or sharp knot bound follows yet. ## 1. The original physical source and Casimir Fix `q=exp(pi*i/N)`, `Q=q^2`, `d=N-1`, `rho=q-q^(-1)`, `x=q^d=-q^(-1)`, `N>=2`. On balanced heads use exactly mathsfF|a>=(1-Q^(a+1))|a+1>, Ecal|a>=(Q^(-a)-1)|a-1>, K|a>=xQ^(-a)|a>, F_tot=mathsfF_1+K_1^(-1)mathsfF_2, E_tot=Ecal_1 K_2+Ecal_2, Omega=F_tot E_tot+qK_tot+q^(-1)K_tot^(-1). Missing endpoint arrows are zero. Work on the physical integer-degree d subspace with basis `|u,d-u>`, `0<=u<=d`. Let `c_*=q+q^(-1)`. The original cup, ordinary pivotal cap and marked row restrict here to p_u=N x^(u-d), ell_u=x^(-u)Q^(-u)/N, m_u=x^(d-u)/N^2. (1) The unrestricted marked row is not replaced by this restricted row on other degrees; every vector constructed below has degree d. These are the fixed actual turns, with no invented scalar frame. Define finite harmonic sums H_0=0, H_u=sum_(j=1)^u 1/(1-Q^j), g_u=x^(u-d)=p_u/N, v_u=-g_u H_u/rho. (2) Then the exact Jordan equations are (Omega-c_*)g=0, (Omega-c_*)v=g. (3) In particular g,v are independent, and their span is the actual size-two c_* block inside integer degree d. This block, rather than the entire 2N-dimensional c_* generalized eigenspace across degrees, is the source channel treated in this note. ## 2. Derivation from generic q with actual cup duality retained Use a variable z near q and the ordinary highest-weight representation of highest weight d=N-1. Put `Q_z=z^2`, `x(z)=z^d`, `F_a(z)=product_(j=1)^a(1-z^(2j))`. Keep the standard highest-weight endpoint, including `mathsfF|d>=0`. All factorials with `a<N` are nonzero near q. The top-channel descendant and spin-zero invariant cup may be normalized as g_u(z)=x(z)^(u-d), h_u(z)=g_u(z) R_u(z), R_u(z)=(-1)^u z^[-u(u+1)] F_u(z)F_(d-u)(z)/F_d(z). (4) Indeed `g(z)=F_tot(z)^d|0,0>/F_d(z)`. The finite coproduct binomial proves its displayed components. The E equation for an invariant degree-d vector gives the successive ratio h_(u+1)/h_u=-z^[d-2u-2] (1-z^(2u+2))/(1-z^(2d-2u)), which is (4); direct F and K equations give `F_tot h=0`, `K_tot h=h`. Thus h is the ACTUAL self-duality cup up to the stated analytic unit normalization. Its paired evaluation is transported reciprocally. One does not extend the root-only expression `K^(1-N)` as a generic-q pivot or assume a root cyclic endpoint away from q. The exact Casimir eigenvalues are Omega(z)g(z)=c_top(z)g(z), Omega(z)h(z)=c_triv(z)h(z), c_top(z)=z^(2N-1)+z^(-2N+1), c_triv(z)=z+z^(-1). (5) These follow from the defining coproduct: the top highest vector has K-root `z^(2d)`, while h is invariant. They can also be checked directly from the entries above. Root complementation gives `R_u(q)=1`, so `h(q)=g(q)`. Meanwhile D_logz(c_triv-c_top)|q=2N rho, D_logz R_u|q=-2N H_u. (6) For the second equation, differentiate (4) and pair its last u factorial terms with indices `N-j`. Their sum reduces to `-2N sum_(j<=u)(1-Q^j)^(-1)`; the quadratic integer terms cancel. All derivatives are at fixed N and the actual root, at either parity. Consequently lim_(z->q) [h(z)-g(z)]/[c_triv(z)-c_top(z)]=v. (7) Applying (5) before the limit proves (3). This is a normalized divided difference of actual Clebsch channels, with the original cup kept. It does not use the fixed-q common-meridian splitting at a dual cap; that cap's exact dual-color product keeps its Casimir nodes collided. An analytic rescaling of h or g, equal to one at q, can add a multiple of g to v. The source-adapted vector in Section3 removes precisely that ambiguity. Thus the final Hermite frame does not depend on the unphysical first derivative of an eigenvector normalization. ## 3. Exact original co-sources and the canonical Hermite lift The finite sums in (1)--(2) give ell g=0, m g=1/N, gamma_N:=ell v=q x^(-d)/(N rho^2) =(-1)^N/(N rho^2), mu_N:=m v=-(sum_(u=0)^d H_u)/(N^2 rho). (8) In particular gamma_N is NONZERO at every level. To check its value, interchange the two finite sums: sum_(u=0)^d Q^(-u)H_u =sum_(j=1)^d [sum_(u=j)^d Q^(-u)]/(1-Q^j) =-1/(1-Q^(-1)). Also `q x^(-d)=(-1)^N`, by `x=q^d` and the actual half-period q. This accounts for the full parity sign. Define the SOURCE-ADAPTED generalized vector t_N=(v-mu_N p)/gamma_N. (9) Then all original source pairings are exactly m p=1, m t_N=0, ell p=0, ell t_N=1, (Omega-c_*)t_N=theta_N p, theta_N=1/(N gamma_N)=(-1)^N rho^2. (10) Thus the two original co-sources, not newly chosen dual rows, are the inverse frame on this actual Jordan channel. In particular `(Omega-c_*)|span(p,t_N)=theta_N p ell`, agreeing with the retained rank-one nilpotent source. No ordinary quantum dimension is divided out. The generalized direction and the marked co-source remain. The replacement `v->v+lambda g` changes `mu_N` by `lambda/N`, so the numerator in (9) is unchanged. This proves the normalization independence asserted after (7). ## 4. Fourier--Plancherel gives uniform physical conditioning For `1<=j<N`, |1-Q^j|>=4min(j,N-j)/N, |rho|>=4/N. Hence, with `Harm_N=1+log N`, max_u |H_u| <=(N/2)Harm_N, ||v||_2 <=(N^(5/2)/8)Harm_N, |mu_N| <=(N/8)Harm_N, |gamma_N|^(-1)=N|rho|^2<=4N. These estimates already give polynomial frame bounds without a spectral projector. A stronger exact Fourier calculation removes their condition growth. On degree d the original marked row is `m=p^*/N^3`, so (10) gives `p^*t_N=0`. If `Hbar=(1/N)sum_u H_u`, (9) becomes (t_N)_u=(-1)^(N+1)N rho g_u(H_u-Hbar). (11) Use the unnormalized cyclic Fourier transform `Hhat_k=sum_(u=0)^d H_u Q^(-ku)`. Pairing j with N-j gives `H_d=d/2`. The cyclic difference of H therefore has value `-d/2` at zero and `(1-Q^u)^(-1)` at `u=1,...,d`. Its Fourier transform is EXACTLY `-k`, for `1<=k<=d`: successive transforms differ by `sum_(j=1)^d Q^(-kj)=-1`, starting at zero for k=0. Consequently Hhat_k=-k/(1-Q^(-k)), 1<=k<=d, ||t_N||_2^2=N|rho|^2 sum_(k=1)^d k^2/|1-Q^k|^2. (12) This is ordinary finite Plancherel on the FULL physical N-window; no Fourier channel is omitted or independently dephased. The elementary root identity is sum_(k=1)^d |1-Q^k|^(-2)=(N^2-1)/12. For a direct proof differentiate `P(z)=(z^N-1)/(z-1)` twice at one. The first reciprocal sum is d/2 and the sum of squared reciprocals is `d(5-N)/12`; their difference is the displayed absolute sum. Pairing k and N-k then gives N^2(N^2-1)/48 <=sum_(k=1)^d k^2/|1-Q^k|^2 <=N^2(N^2-1)/24. Since `4/N<=|rho|<=2pi/N`, it follows that N^3/4<=||t_N||_2^2<=pi^2 N^3/6, p^*t_N=0, ||p||_2^2=N^3. (13) For the two physical columns `V=[p,t_N]` this proves sigma_min(V)>=N^(3/2)/2, sigma_max(V)<=pi N^(3/2)/sqrt(6), kappa(V)<=2, uniformly EVERY N>=2. (14) For the last bound use the known first column norm N^(3/2), not just the two extreme singular-value bounds: the other column's relative norm lies in `[1/2,pi/sqrt(6)]`, and `pi/sqrt(6)<2`. The condition number is therefore at most two; N=2 attains two. The exact inverse on its range is still the two original rows m,ell by (10). The ordinary row on the full physical degree-d space has a larger norm because it also sees other channel directions; its restriction here is precisely the coordinate dual of t_N. No inverse of a possibly ill-conditioned whole Casimir projector was used. ## 5. An actual positive Hermite Gram and crossing bound On `S_N=span(p,t_N)` define the positive inner product ||w||_(Herm)^2=|m w|^2+|ell w|^2. (15) It makes p,t_N orthonormal. It has rank two on S_N, not rank one, and retains BOTH the value and derivative channels. Both original co-sources have dual norm one. Equation (14) compares this Gram uniformly with N^(-3) times the physical metric. This is an explicit source-controlled Hermite Gram, not a metric defined from an unknown knot scalar or terminal word. Keep the original crossing's common Cartan scalar kappa. The independently derived Casimir polynomial has r(c_*)=1, r'(c_*)=-d/(2rho). Therefore in the p,t_N frame the EXACT original signed crossing is R_+=kappa [[1,tau_N],[0,1]], R_-=kappa^(-1) [[1,-tau_N],[0,1]], tau_N=(-1)^(N+1)d rho/2, |tau_N|<=pi. (16) Thus, for every signed integer l, ||R_+^l||_(Herm)<=1+pi|l| (17) at the original complete root, since `|kappa|=1`. The original full Cartan, pivot, framing and modified-dimension line have not been renormalized; (16) is a basis expression for that same operator. The PHYSICAL operator norm on this SAME invariant source channel is consequently at most `2(1+pi|l|)`, uniformly in N. The Gram (15) is asserted on the SELECTED TWO-DIMENSIONAL invariant channel only. Adjacent crossings may take it into other intermediate Casimir channels. Extending it through the full q-Racah transform, with the source, is the remaining problem. Declaring the rest of the physical tensor space orthogonal would not control that leakage, and no such full-channel estimate is claimed here. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_tame_c0_hermite_source_frame.py): literal original E/F Casimir and signed R, all original source rows, generic-q cup/descendant divided difference, parity and frame singular values at both odd and even levels.

title: Exact transport of quantum derivatives in a tensor contraction
status: Explicit rational source gauge and commuting finite-jet connection
text:
# Exact transport of quantum derivatives in a tensor contraction A quantum tensor contraction is a finite sum over representation indices. This note studies one summand before those indices are summed. Its indices satisfy affine conservation equations at vertices, cups and caps. After choosing independent coordinates for those equations, we ask what happens when one coordinate is shifted by the quantum period. The quantum parameter is allowed to vary near its root value. The period then moves, so a shift by the fixed integer \(N\) differs from a shift by the moving period. That difference produces derivatives in the independent index coordinates. The result is an explicit system of commuting differential operators on every fixed finite list of quantum derivatives. The term *finite jet* means this list of Taylor coefficients; *flat connection* means that the directional operators commute. All formulas concern the specified continuation of the original tensors, including cups, categorical duals, parity signs and the marked trace normalization. They do not turn the finite admissible sum into a periodic sum. Moving an integration or residue cycle would require its own boundary and divisor calculation, which is not supplied here. ## 1. The moving period and the original local factors Fix an integer \(N\ge3\), put \(d=N-1\), and write \(q_0=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(\zeta=q_0e^\epsilon\). Here \(\epsilon\) is the small generic-quantum-parameter displacement, not a half-twist sign. Choose the logarithm near \(q_0\) and define \[ P= rac{\pi i}{\operatorname{Log}\zeta},\qquad Q=\zeta^2, \qquad\eta=e^{2\pi iP},\qquad\Delta=N-P. 	ag{1} \] At \(\epsilon=0\), \(P=N\), \(\eta=1\), and \(\Delta=0\). The highest weights and polynomial degrees remain fixed integers as \(\epsilon\) varies. Only their specified coefficients and continued index arguments vary. At a white vertex, let \(W_a:V_{2a}	o V_d\otimes V_d\) be the actual generic intertwining tensor, with \(0\le a\le\lfloor d/2floor\). The variables \(i,j\) are its two ordered physical indices and \(r\) its channel index. Let \(F_m=(Q;Q)_m=\prod_{k=1}^{m}(1-Q^k)\), with \(F_0=1\). The fixed finite polynomial \(H_m^B(U,V)\) is the q-Hahn numerator specified in the [generic source formula](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_generic_boundary_gauge_and_source.md). Its polynomial arguments, rather than a newly chosen interpolation of matrix values, define the continuation: \[  egin{aligned} W_a(i,j;r)&=(-1)^m\zeta^{-dr+di-m(m-1)}  rac{H_m^{Q^{-N}}(Q^i,Q^j)}{F_m},\ m&=d-a,\qquad i+j=m+r. \end{aligned} 	ag{2} \] The degree is the actual large-channel degree \(m=d-a\). Replacing it by its colliding small partner \(a\) would preserve some root values but change their generic derivatives. For integers \(p,q\), shifting the indices in their conservation equation gives \[ W_a(i+Pp,j+Pq;r+P(p+q))=(-1)^{dq}W_a(i,j;r). 	ag{3} \] Indeed \(Q^P=1\) leaves both polynomial arguments unchanged, and the remaining exponent changes by \(-dPq\). In particular, shifting \(i\) by \(P\) and \(j\) by \(-P\) at fixed total multiplies the tensor by \((-1)^d\). The asymmetric sign records the order of the two physical legs. The cup has a different multiplier because it contains factorials. Use the specified continuation \(\widehat F_P\) from the [moving-factorial theorem](actual_moving_period_factorial_normals.md), which satisfies \[ \widehat F_P(z+P)=(1-e^{2\pi iz})\widehat F_P(z). \] For an actual fixed highest weight \(0\le L<N\), its ordered cup is \[ p_L(x,L-x)=e^{\pi ix}\zeta^{x(L-x-1)}  rac{\widehat F_P(x)\widehat F_P(L-x)}{F_L}. 	ag{4} \] The physical cup also has the head-independent scalar \(N\zeta^{-d^2}\), which remains in the tensor contraction. Set \(Y=e^{2\pi ix}\). Retaining both the quadratic monomial and \(e^{\pi ix}\) gives \[  egin{aligned} p_L(x+nP,L-x-nP)&=\mu_{L,n}(P,x)p_L(x,L-x),\ \mu_{L,n}(P,x)&=(-1)^{Ln} rac{1-Y}{\eta^{-n}-Y}, \qquad n\in\mathbb Z. \end{aligned} 	ag{5} \] For \(n=1\), the two factorials contribute \((1-Y)/(1-\eta^{-1}/Y)\); the monomials contribute \((-1)^{L-1}/Y\). Their product is (5). Repeated shifts telescope, and reversing the shift gives negative \(n\). These are meromorphic identities, interpreted after clearing denominators where necessary. The cap is the actual matrix inverse of the cup. Its ordered entry is therefore \[ \ell_L(x,L-x)= rac1{p_L(L-x,x)}. 	ag{6} \] Its multiplier is \(1/\mu_{L,-n}(P,L-x)\), not simply \(1/\mu_{L,n}(P,x)\). This reversal is needed for the cyclic and pivotal normalizations. The physical cup and cap scalars remain unchanged. The other elementary multipliers are explicit. The Chevalley monomial \(\zeta^{-(L+1)x}\) gains \((-1)^{(L+1)n}\), while the original pivotal clock \((-1)^L\zeta^{L-2x}\) gains one. An integer affine character \(e^{2\pi i\ell(\mathrm{heads})}\) gains \(\eta^{\ell(n)}\), where \(\ell(n)\) denotes its linear change under the integer shift. Categorical dual tensors are expanded into their original ordered white maps, cups, caps and reversal factors. Thus the same calculation applies without replacing a dual by a Hermitian adjoint or dividing by a vanishing root norm. Scalar channel weights, fixed generic normalizers and retained half-twist eigenvalues do not depend on these indices and do not change under their shifts. ## 2. Solving the index constraints before transporting Fix a typed tensor network and an admissible assignment of its finite channel labels. A *head* in the compiler means a basis index on a specified oriented end of an edge. Impose all its literal equations: for example, \[ i+j=m+r\quad	ext{at a white vertex},\qquad x+y=L\quad	ext{at a cup or cap}, \] together with equality of contracted indices. Write the resulting integer affine system as \(B\mathbf h=\mathbf b\). Choose one integer solution \(h_0\) and a matrix \(A\) whose columns form a \(\mathbb Z\)-basis of \(\ker_{\mathbb Z}B\). Then \[ \mathbf h=h_0+Ax,\qquad x\in\mathbb C^k. 	ag{7} \] The columns span the whole integer kernel, not a proper sublattice. This kernel is saturated because \(\mathbb Z^n/\ker_{\mathbb Z}B\) is isomorphic to the free subgroup \(\operatorname{im}_{\mathbb Z}B\). They also span the complex kernel. An inconsistent channel assignment contributes no summands. The original finite inequalities are retained separately: writing (7) neither removes nor wraps them. Let \(S(\epsilon,x)\) be the meromorphic summand obtained from (2), (4) and (6), with all original ordering, characters and scalars. It agrees with the generic quantum summand at every admissible integer assignment. Exposed boundary indices are either fixed or included with their explicitly specified factors and constraints. No continuation is silently assigned to an arbitrary external state. Constant arguments need particular care. On the chosen affine chart, a tensor factor whose head argument is constant remains its original constant source factor. An admissible fixed integer cup is evaluated by finite factorials. A forbidden constant polar assignment is not defined by substituting into a ratio \(0/0\): retain its original zero summand, or invoke a separately proved generic cancellation. The construction makes no assertion about an undefined constant interpolation. For a direction \(b\in\mathbb Z^k\), the shift \(x\mapsto x+Pb\) changes every local head by an integer multiple of \(P\). Multiplying the local identities gives \[ S(\epsilon,x+Pb)=C_b(P,x)S(\epsilon,x). 	ag{8} \] The multiplier \(C_b\) is computed directly: multiply the white signs, cup ratios, reversed inverse-cap ratios, clocks and characters. If \(z_l(x)\) is an integer affine head argument, set \[ Y_l=e^{2\pi iz_l(x)}. \] Then \(C_b\) is rational in \(\eta\) and these \(Y_l\). Since \(N\) is an integer, it is \(N\)-periodic in every free coordinate. Away from the divisors \(Y_l=1\), its root value is the explicit sign character \[ C_b(N,x)=\chi(b)\in\{1,-1\}. 	ag{9} \] The character includes the ordered white-leg signs and the actual highest-weight parities. It is not reset to one when \(N\) changes parity. Any additional boundary character must be transported as well before enlarging the class of networks. This construction also applies term by term in a finite channel sum. For the usual matching network, the homogeneous head equations are the same for all channel assignments, the channel weights \(2a\) are even, and \(h_0\) is integral. A common multiplier for the sum further requires that the integer linear coefficients of every separately recorded head character be unchanged across assignments. With a common primitive basis and this condition, \(e^{2\pi ih_0}=1\) and all local parities agree, so the same \(C_b\) applies. Otherwise retain a finite vector of summands with diagonal transport. Even in the common-multiplier case, the support-dependent summation cycles remain separate. ### An explicit rational gauge The multiplier is not merely known to exist: the cup formula gives a particular function that produces it. Define \[ g(z)= rac{e^{2\pi iz}}{1-e^{2\pi iz}}. \] A direct calculation yields \(g(z+nP)/g(z)=(1-Y)/(\eta^{-n}-Y)\). Thus dividing a cup by \(g\) leaves the constant shift character \((-1)^{Ln}\). For every nonconstant cup argument put one factor \(g\) into \(G\); for every inverse-cap argument put its inverse. Include all separately retained integer exponential characters: \[ G(x)=\left(\prod_{	ext{cup/cap arguments }l}g(z_l(x))^{e_l}ight) e^{2\pi i\ell(h_0+Ax)},\qquad e_l\in\{1,-1\}. 	ag{9a} \] Only nonconstant arguments enter this product. A constant argument has shift number zero and multiplier one, so adding its \(g\)-factor would be unnecessary and could introduce an undefined pole at a fixed integer. In particular, simplify \(\mu_{L,0}=1\) before evaluating a constant argument. For a cap whose first matrix index is \(x\), the cup argument used here is \(L-x\), as required by (6). White maps, Chevalley factors and clocks need no further rational gauge. The specified \(G\) is rational in the marked head exponentials and independent of \(P\), and the exact multiplier is \[ C_b(P,x)=\chi(b) rac{G(x+Pb)}{G(x)}. 	ag{9b} \] Equivalently, \(S/G\) is quasiperiodic with period \(P\) and character \(\chi\). This is an identity of meromorphic functions, including the zeros and poles of \(G\). It does not authorize deleting \(G\) from a period integral. Nor is the gauge automatically negligible in an asymptotic estimate. For \(z=N(x+iy)\) with fixed \(y>0\), \( |g(z)|=e^{-2\pi Ny}(1+o(1))\). Hence \(G\) can change the leading exponential action and contribute residues. A change of variables in the transport formula must retain both effects. ## 3. From the moving shift to finitely many quantum derivatives Choose a head chart on which the actual source is regular in \(\epsilon\) after its proved generic cancellations. Its order-\(J\) jet is its Taylor polynomial modulo \(\epsilon^{J+1}\). If an intermediate expression has a known scalar pole of order \(M\), first multiply by \(\epsilon^M\); recovering the desired Laurent coefficients then needs the corresponding higher Taylor order. No principal part is discarded. For a direction \(b\), let \(D_b\) denote directional differentiation in \(x\), and let \(M_f\) denote multiplication by a function \(f\). Since \(x+Nb=(x+\Delta b)+Pb\), equation (8) gives \[  egin{aligned} S(\epsilon,x+Nb)&=T_bS(\epsilon,x),\ T_b&=e^{\Delta D_b}M_{C_b}. \end{aligned} 	ag{10} \] Composition acts from right to left, so the translation differentiates both \(C_b\) and the summand. Because \(\Delta=O(\epsilon)\), only finitely many translation terms can affect an order-\(J\) jet: \[ T_b^{(J)}= \sum_{r=0}^{J} rac{\Delta^r}{r!}D_b^rM_{C_b} \pmod{\epsilon^{J+1}}. 	ag{11} \] The required Taylor coefficients of \(C_b\) are rational in the \(Y_l\), with their divisors retained. This is a finite calculation for any specified derivative order. The operators commute on local meromorphic functions, not only when applied to the particular summand. Since \(G(x+Nb)=G(x)\), equations (9b) and (10) give \[ T_b=\chi(b)M_Ge^{\Delta D_b}M_{G^{-1}}. 	ag{11a} \] They are simultaneous conjugates of ordinary translations. This proves their group law. One can also check it directly from the multiplier relation \[ C_{b+c}(P,x)=C_b(P,x+Pc)C_c(P,x). 	ag{12} \] Its \(N\)-periodicity gives \(C_b(x-\Delta c)=C_b(x+Pc)\), and consequently \[  egin{aligned} T_bT_c &=e^{\Delta D_{b+c}}M_{C_b(x-\Delta c)C_c(x)}\ &=T_{b+c}=T_cT_b. \end{aligned} 	ag{13} \] The same equality survives finite-jet truncation. Remove only the recorded root sign, setting \(U_b=\chi(b)^{-1}T_b^{(J)}\). Then \(\Delta\in(\epsilon)\) and \(C_b/\chi(b)=1 mod\epsilon\), so \[ (U_b-I)	ext{ raises the power of }\epsilon,\qquad \prod_{r=1}^{J+1}(U_{b_r}-I)=0. 	ag{14} \] Thus the normalized transport is unipotent on finite jets. Its inverse is a finite geometric series, or simply \(U_{-b}\). This is a local statement over a meromorphic coefficient field; it is not a norm bound near the poles or a nilpotence statement about the final sum. The commuting logarithmic derivatives are explicit: \[  egin{aligned} U_b&=e^{\Delta
abla_b}\pmod{\epsilon^{J+1}},\ 
abla_b&=D_b-D_b\operatorname{Log}G =M_GD_bM_{G^{-1}}. \end{aligned} 	ag{14a} \] Here \(D_b\operatorname{Log}G\) acts by multiplication. Its logarithmic poles occur on the recorded integral-head divisors. This is the flat finite-jet connection referred to in the title. ### The first derivative as a concrete example Write \(S=S_0+\epsilon S_1+O(\epsilon^2)\) and \(C_b=\chi(b)(1+\epsilon c_{b1}+O(\epsilon^2))\). Since \(P'(0)=iN^2/\pi\), equation (10) becomes \[  egin{aligned} S_0(x+Nb)&=\chi(b)S_0(x),\ S_1(x+Nb)&=\chi(b) igl(S_1-P'(0)D_bS_0+c_{b1}S_0 igr). \end{aligned} 	ag{15} \] The root value is quasiperiodic, but its first quantum derivative also contains the derivative caused by the moving period and the derivative of the multiplier. For a cup argument \(z_l\) shifted by \(n_lP\), the latter contribution is \[  rac{2\pi iP'(0)n_l}{1-e^{2\pi iz_l}}. 	ag{16} \] An inverse cup uses its literal reversed argument and the negative contribution. A character \(\eta^k\) contributes \(2\pi iP'(0)k\); white and clock signs have zero derivative. These poles are genuine normal terms, not an error that can be removed by setting \(\eta=1\) too early. ## 4. The three-coordinate exceptional kernel The [specified generic exceptional operator](actual_matching_edge_generic_deficient_operator_lift.md) provides a concrete network with free coordinates \((t,u,v)\). Retain its channel \(a\) and define \[  egin{gathered} r=a-v+u,\qquad \ell=t-v,\qquad s=d-2a,\ Y_r=e^{2\pi ir},\qquad Y_v=e^{2\pi iv},\qquad Y_\ell=e^{2\pi i\ell},\ A(Y)= rac{1-Y}{\eta^{-1}-Y},\qquad B(Y)= rac{1-Y}{\eta-Y}. \end{gathered} \] Here the local functions \(A(Y),B(Y)\) are unrelated to the integer constraint matrices of Section 2. Applying (3)–(6) to the two actual large white tensors, Chevalley scalar and three ordered cups gives \[ C_u=(-1)^sA(Y_r),\qquad C_v=(-1)^s rac{B(Y_r)}{A(Y_v)B(Y_\ell)},\qquad C_t= rac1{A(Y_\ell)}. 	ag{17} \] These multipliers apply to the full generic polynomial kernel and its completed version, because the moving face scalar is independent of \(t,u,v\). The retained character \(e^{-2\pi iv}\) is one under a fixed integer \(N\)-shift but not under a moving \(P\)-shift. Erasing it before forming (17) would lose part of the derivative. The rational gauge is short in these coordinates: \[ G_K= rac{g(r)}{g(v)g(\ell)} =e^{2\pi i(u-v-t)}  rac{(1-Y_v)(1-Y_\ell)}{1-Y_r}. 	ag{17a} \] Substitution into (9b) recovers all three multipliers, with \(\chi_u=\chi_v=(-1)^s\) and \(\chi_t=1\). This checks the abstract-looking construction on the actual kernel, retaining its integer exponential and its channel-row pole. It does not replace the kernel by its phase-cancelled root value before differentiation. ## 5. Closing the source with its original normalization For the marked invariant, use the same exposed physical index and its actual generic ordinary pivotal closure. Let \(F(\epsilon)\) be that finite closed source. With the symmetric quantum integer \([N]_\zeta=(\zeta^N-\zeta^{-N})/(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})\), its normalization is \[  egin{aligned} D_N(\epsilon)&=(-1)^d[N]_{q_0e^\epsilon},\ 
u_N=D_N'(0)&= rac{2N(-1)^N}{q_0-q_0^{-1}},\ Z&= rac{F'(0)}{
u_N}. \end{aligned} 	ag{18} \] The transport applies to the continued ordinary summand and its first jet before this normalization. It does not create a generic continuation of a bare dense root mark. If an off-root marked row is prescribed, that row must be transported covariantly with its original cup. Otherwise the available statement is the ordinary closure and (18). Likewise, a regular Hopf lift of a complete-circle coupon and the literal moving-quantum-parameter exceptional polynomial are different generic germs. The proof uses whichever germ has actually been specified. Agreement at the root is not enough to identify their derivatives. At the physical integer lattice, \(Y_l=1\). Individual rational transport factors can therefore have poles even when the complete source has a removable cancellation. Equations (8) and (10) hold meromorphically and can be cleared of denominators before specialization.
