They do not authorize applying a singular factor to a root value without its full germ, or discarding a residue. Finally, shifting a summand does not preserve its finite admissibility polytope. A residue representation has its own cotangent factors and boundary. A global period identity would have to carry that cycle, its crossed divisors and every affine marking character. No such cycle deformation or selected contribution is proved in this note. ## 6. Finite checks and their scope The [calculation script](../experiments/audit_actual_tensor_source_finite_jet_connection.py) and [saved results](../experiments/actual_tensor_source_finite_jet_connection_results.json) check the rational gauge, the three exceptional-kernel multipliers, their composition laws, the first-derivative connections and a shared integral head chart. Direct evaluations of the original large white polynomial, moving-factorial cups and full generic completed kernel check 24, 6 and 6 moving-period shifts, respectively. Three fixed-\(N\) transports include first and second normals; the largest recorded relative identity error at 85 digits was below \(1.2	imes10^{-82}\). Those finite checks test the formulas and their implementation. The arbitrary-network assertion follows from multiplying the local identities and the operator proof above. Neither the numerical checks nor the local connection claim a transported global period or a volume equality.

title: The adjoint finite-jet connection on the original source cycle
status: Adjoint connection on the original cotangent period
text: # The adjoint finite-jet connection on the original source cycle 30 October 2026. The exact tensor-source transport has a corresponding identity for the original cotangent period. Its adjoint acts on the cotangent density as well as on the explicit source gauge. The resulting double-pole and finite-part terms are retained. This does not make the finite head sum periodic or move its cycle to the geometric critical point. ## 1. The actual period and the specified source connection Use the [actual tensor-source connection](actual_tensor_source_finite_jet_connection.md). After the original integral affine head equations, write the primitive free lattice as h=h0+A x, x in C^k. Constant head factors remain their original source constants. Fix the finite channel labels, or retain the finite vector of label sectors when their characters differ. Every outside tensor, turn and peripheral character is part of the specified meromorphic source S(epsilon,x). At the original marked arc use its ordinary generic pivotal closure and subsequent exposed-trace normal, or an explicitly chosen covariant generic marked row. No generic continuation of the bare root mark is supplied by this theorem. Initially assume S is root-regular in epsilon on a common neighborhood of the cycle, after retaining its actual meromorphic cancellations. If a chosen representation has a finite Laurent pole of order M, apply the statements to epsilon^M S through order J+M to recover the original Laurent jet through order J. One must not use only J translation terms before multiplying a source with such a pole. Put P=pi i/Log(q0 exp(epsilon)), Delta=N-P, and P'=iN^2/pi. For b in Z^k, let D_b=sum b_j partial_(x_j). The source theorem proves S(epsilon,x+Nb)=chi(b) G(x) exp(Delta D_b)[G(x)^-1 S], (1) where chi(b) is the actual parity character and G is the explicit P-independent rational cup/character gauge. Its construction omits constant head factors; in particular it never inserts g(integer) for an identically constant cup argument. Formula (1) is meromorphic and its exponential is a FINITE differential operator modulo any fixed epsilon^(J+1). The original lattice density and normalized period are W(x)=product_(j=1)^k pi cot(pi x_j), I_Gamma[S]=(2pi i)^(-k) integral_Gamma W(x) S(x) dx, (2) with dx=dx1 wedge ... wedge dxk. Gamma is the original sum of compact local tori, or a specified closed cycle on the same source chart. It avoids the divisors of S, W, G and G^-1 on its surface on a common epsilon germ, or the genuinely canceled meromorphic integrands are used throughout. Its interior may contain the original cotangent and source poles. The [source-null extension theorem](actual_matching_edge_degree_cycle_boundary.md) allows its explicitly proved zero ordered tori to be included as well. Other polar strata are not implicitly added or removed. ## 2. Exact adjoint transport of every finite quantum jet For every fixed J, on the original CLOSED cycle one has I_Gamma[S(epsilon,x+Nb)] =chi(b)(2pi i)^(-k) integral_Gamma G^-1 exp(-Delta D_b)(W G) S dx mod epsilon^(J+1). (3) All derivatives in (3) act on the actual top-form density W G. This is not a replacement of the original period by a period of S/G. The final meromorphic integrand is used with every cancellation and divisor retained, rather than evaluated factor by factor at G=0 or G=infinity. Proof: for meromorphic f,g with no pole on the cycle, integral_Gamma f D_b g dx=-integral_Gamma (D_b f) g dx. Indeed D_b(fg) dx=d(fg contraction_b(dx)), whose integral on a closed cycle is zero. This argument needs no pole-free interior. Apply it r times to the r-th term of (1), with f=W G and g=G^-1 S. Since Delta is independent of x and belongs to (epsilon), only r<=J occurs for the root-regular source specified in section 1. For a Laurent source use the cleared source and the enlarged order stated there. This proves (3) without an infinite differential expansion or an analytic translation of Gamma by the small complex number Delta. For the literal translated cycle Gamma+Nb, a change of variables also gives I_(Gamma+Nb)[S]=I_Gamma[S(epsilon,x+Nb)], (4) because the original W is N-periodic. This is an identity of the specified continued source at that translated cycle. It does not say the shifted head values are admissible original states or vanish outside the physical basis. In particular the meromorphic continuation need not vanish at out-of-basis shifted indices. If a geometric deformation from one cycle to the other crosses source divisors, their tubes and residues remain in that deformation. Equations (3),(4) compute the translated period; they do not identify the two cycles in the complement of those divisors. ## 3. The first normal and the original exposed trace normalization Write S=S0+epsilon S1+O(epsilon^2). Formula (3) yields I_(Gamma+Nb)[S0]=chi(b) I_Gamma[S0], I_(Gamma+Nb)[S1]-chi(b) I_Gamma[S1] =chi(b) P' (2pi i)^(-k) integral_Gamma G^-1 D_b(W G) S0 dx. (5) The sign is positive: Delta'=-P' and the adjoint exponential is exp(-Delta D_b). The correction includes derivatives of BOTH W and G. Writing it as W D_b Log(WG) is permissible only as a meromorphic identity; the un-divided density in (5) specifies its actual periods. For the original ordinary exposed-head closure, retain nu_N=2N(-1)^N/(q0-q0^-1), P'/nu_N=(-1)^(N+1) N sin(pi/N)/pi. (6) When the original root closure I_Gamma[S0] is zero, its translated root closure is also zero by (5), so division of the first-normal identity by nu_N gives the exact corresponding marked-period difference. Its correction density has the nonzero order-one scalar in (6), rather than an arbitrarily assigned boundary coefficient. It is not yet a nonzero global geometric contribution. For a primitive direction with several nonzero b_j, D_b differentiates the corresponding original cotangent factors. A chosen degree h need not be a primitive free variable. For h=A0 x_j+B0 at fixed other coordinates, the weight is (pi/A0)cot(pi(h-B0)/A0) dh. The finite-part rules of the boundary theorem apply with that weight. Neither (3) nor (5) replaces it by pi cot(pi h) dh. ## 4. A literal cup exhibits a nonzero double-pole correction For one varying cup argument, its source gauge is g(x)=Y/(1-Y), Y=exp(2pi i x), pi cot(pi x)=-pi i(1+2g(x)). Let w=pi cot(pi x). The correction density in (5) is g^-1 (w g)'=w'+w * 2pi i/(1-Y). (7) At an integer n, with y=x-n, this equals -2/y^2+pi i/y+O(1). Consequently its residue against a root source regular there is pi i S0(n)-2 S0'(n). (8) Both copies of the derivative matter: one comes from the original cotangent and one from the actual cup gauge. For the ordered fixed-L cup with L=d=N-1, the exact fixed-root reflection gives p_d(0,x)=exp(pi i d x/N). On a physical n in [0,d], the difference of its translated and parity-weighted original first-normal cotangent periods is therefore exactly (-1)^d N(N-2) exp(pi i d n/N). (9) This is the ordered channel-cup normalization of the source theorem. For the physical cup, multiply by its original root scalar N q0^(-d^2); its generic scalar derivative cancels from the difference because the corresponding root difference is zero. The translated cup can have a generic pole at n+N. Its cotangent period is the actual Laurent finite part, not its value at that pole. Thus (9) is a concrete counterexample to silently declaring these continued periods periodic. ## 5. Scope of the cycle identity The source connection, the original primitive lattice and the original weight together determine every finite-order correction in (3). The isolated wall residues and source-null ordered periods are already given by the boundary theorem. Their combination supplies exact finite-head transport with its boundary terms retained. What remains separate is a deformation of the FULL original period through all its source divisors to a contributing geometric cycle, including its noncompact ends and the coherent outside contraction. No equality of the positive envelope with volume, no periodic extension of the physical basis, and no nonzero saddle coefficient follows from this adjoint identity. Focused verification: [adjoint and original cup audit](../experiments/audit_actual_tensor_source_translated_cycle_normals.py) and [saved results](../experiments/actual_tensor_source_translated_cycle_normals_results.json). The audit checks 60 exact meromorphic adjoint residues through derivative order three, the actual cotangent double-pole coefficient, and 12 genuine translated first-normal cup finite parts obtained independently from the original moving-Gamma Laurent coefficients. The latter agree with (9) to relative error below 5.3e-38 at 100 digits. These are checks of the retained local periods, not evidence for a global saddle coefficient. The result retains all source and gauge divisors and makes no contributing-cycle assertion. No wrapped physical state or geometric contribution is inferred from the translated normal identities.

title: Exponential metric motion is necessary for the current terminal Gram
text: # Exponential metric motion is necessary for the current terminal Gram 29 October 2026. This is an exact obstruction to a UNIFORM, all-port Lyapunov propagation of the presently constructed terminal Gram at subexponential extra cost. Its test vector is now proved to occur on a FIXED original source trajectory, by the cup slide below. It is not an obstruction to Cauchy, a substantially changing positive metric, or a source estimate which first retains the relevant coherent cancellations. Use the original principal root and complete source module W from [the closed kernel](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_terminal_packet_closed_kernel.md): q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, d=N-1, x=q^d, F_a=(Q;Q)_a, s_a=|F_a|, kappa=q^(d^2/2), e_j=|j,d-j>. Let R be the FULL original positive checked crossing on W, and let T be the actual terminal projector map. The verified identities are \[ T=N^{-1}X R P_{\mathrm{rev}}R,\qquad H:=TR^{-1}=N^{-1}X R P_{\mathrm{rev}},\qquad X=\operatorname{diag}(x^j),\quad P_{\mathrm{rev}}=\operatorname{diag}(P_{d-j}), \tag{1} \] where P0=1 and the ACTUAL endpoint satisfies \[ P_d=\sum_{j=0}^dF_j=-q\Phi_N(r_N^3),\qquad |P_d|\leq3N^2. \tag{2} \] The full original pivotal functional, odd simple node, even levels, Cartan and framing phases behind (2) are retained in [the quantitative Green proof](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_terminal_green_capacity_bound.md#2-the-actual-endpoint-closes-polynomially-at-every-parity). No estimate of a sum of absolute Green currents is used here. ## 1. A complete exact energy comparison Put \[ Z_N=\sum_{j=0}^d s_j^2,\qquad v_N=R^{-1}e_0. \] Three literal finite crossing identities give everything needed: \[ R e_0=\kappa x^{-d}e_d,\qquad (R^{-1}e_0)_j=\kappa^{-1}x^jF_{d-j},\qquad |(R e_d)_j|=s_j. \tag{3} \] The second uses the original NEGATIVE crossing formula, rather than assuming a unitary inverse. The third uses root factorial reflection. In particular ||v_N||^2=Z_N, while ||R v_N||=1. Applying (1), \[ \boxed{\displaystyle \|T v_N\|^2=|P_d|^2/N^2,\qquad \|T Rv_N\|^2=\|T e_0\|^2=Z_N/N^2.} \tag{4} \] Both equalities are of COMPLETE coherent packet energies, not of one expanded shear path. The denominator is an original polynomial source endpoint, and the numerator is the entire positive factorial sum. Let epsilon_N=exp(-N^2), and let the current positive terminal Gram be \[ G_N=T^\dagger T+\epsilon_N I. \] Every uniform Lyapunov inequality \[ R^\dagger G_N R\preceq C_N G_N \] must therefore satisfy the exact finite lower bound \[ \boxed{\displaystyle C_N\geq\frac{Z_N+N^2\epsilon_N} {|P_d|^2+N^2\epsilon_N Z_N}.} \tag{5} \] This includes levels at which T is singular; nothing is inverted except the genuine original crossing. It also holds after tensoring the physical ports with any spectator coefficient Hilbert space. The sine-factorial estimate, including its endpoint uniformity, gives \[ \log Z_N=\frac{v_3}{\pi}N+O(\log N), \tag{6} \] where v3 is the regular ideal tetrahedron volume. Indeed log s_j=N J(j/N)+O(log N), and J has its unique maximum v3/(2pi) at 5/6. Polynomially many terms and a nearest lattice point give (6). No volume-conjecture asymptotic is a premise. Combining (2), (5), (6), and epsilon_N=e^(-N^2) proves \[ \boxed{\displaystyle \log C_N\geq\frac{v_3}{\pi}N-O(\log N).} \tag{7} \] One may use the finite bound C_N>=Z_N/(9N^4+1) for every N>=2: Z_N<=N4^(N-1) implies N^2 exp(-N^2)Z_N<1 in this range. Thus this FIXED original terminal Gram does not have a subexponential-cost all-port Lyapunov inequality even for R12. The exponent is forced by a retained source endpoint, not by a generic nonnormal-matrix norm estimate. For the related source-slot Gram \(\widehat G_N=H^\dagger H+\epsilon_N I\), the flat unit vector e0 gives the even simpler exact quotient \[ \frac{\|HR e_0\|^2+\epsilon_N\|Re_0\|^2} {\|H e_0\|^2+\epsilon_N} =\frac{Z_N+N^2\epsilon_N}{|P_d|^2+N^2\epsilon_N}. \tag{8} \] So the conclusion is not caused only by the Euclidean size of v_N. ## 2. Any uniformly comparable moving metric must pay the same cost The statement also quantifies what an adaptive metric has to change. Suppose positive metrics G_before,G_after obey \[ G_{\mathrm{before}}\preceq A_N G_N,\qquad G_{\mathrm{after}}\succeq B_N^{-1}G_N, \] and a propagation inequality is asserted: \[ R^\dagger G_{\mathrm{after}}R\preceq C_N G_{\mathrm{before}}. \] Testing v_N proves, without additional assumptions, \[ C_N A_N B_N\geq \frac{Z_N+N^2\epsilon_N}{|P_d|^2+N^2\epsilon_N Z_N}. \tag{9} \] If A_N and B_N are exp(o(N)), C_N must carry the exponent in (7). Conversely a subexponential step cost requires exponential metric motion relative to this terminal metric, of at least the displayed amount. Exact pullback of a metric can of course make an individual step an isometry; (9) says that its change of scale cannot be ignored when comparing it with this fixed boundary-conditioned metric. This does not forbid an angle/gluing dependent metric with a genuine global certificate for its exponential variation. It specifies one necessary quantitative condition such a construction must meet. ## 3. Original-source scope The [literal all-input cup slide](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_terminal_source_normalization_packet.md) now strengthens the test to an ACTUAL fixed source trajectory: R23 p=N R12^(-1)e0, R12 R23 p=N e0. Thus the two prefixes [2] and [2,1] realize the exact quotient (5), with both test vectors multiplied by N. Their complete terminal packet energies are respectively |P_d|^2 and Z_N. Restricting the unchanged metric to vectors reached by original braid prefixes does not remove the obstruction. Their scalar closures retain cancellation: the second complete packet is x^(-d)(Q^(-j) conjugate(F_j))_j and sums to the unit phase x^(-d)Q. It is an explicit factorial divergence, with its endpoint and arbitrary spectator finite differences retained in the linked proof. The [shrinking-clock disk bound](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_normalization_clock_disk_bound.md) now proves a sharp zero-exponent energy estimate for this particular normalization packet in a different coherent metric. No general interior-source energy estimate follows from that repair. The identity Rp=kappa p still holds on the bare cup, but does not apply after the genuine adjacent prefix R23. Any successful source argument must retain this distinction and its coherent closure. At this chosen paired source cut, any diagonal product-head gauge A_a B_b that fixes the cup term by term has A_j B_(d-j)=1. It is therefore the IDENTITY on all of W. Such a paired-source factorial gauge cannot alter this test. Interior gauges not satisfying that condition, or coherent non-product metrics, have to retain their actual interfaces and are outside this restricted observation. All original co-source factors remain unchanged: K=chi 1^T T A p and its polynomial Cauchy boundary cost are the ones already proved. No arbitrary positive trace replaces the pivotal source. Equations (4)--(9) diagnose the cost of propagating its CURRENT complete Gram; they do not give an excess-volume lower bound for a knot scalar. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_terminal_gram_lyapunov_obstruction.py) uses the literal positive and negative crossing formulas and complete open terminal kernel. It checks the original cup, all coherent energies in (4),(8), and the regularized finite quotient rather than diagonalizing an unresolved near-singular Gram. The finite audit checks seven original complete terminal modules; nineteen literal signed-crossing/source/Gram families at N=2,...,20; five large-level exact energy quotients through N=384.

title: Exact three-port Cauchy transport and a nontrivial projected cube kernel
text: # Exact three-port Cauchy transport and a nontrivial projected cube kernel 29 October 2026. The whole-support correlated Gram bound removes a local marked normalization cost. It does not by itself prove sharp transport through a graph. Complete-circle three-port sewing observes only the socle of each regular cube and hence reduces to a scalar weighted Cauchy pairing. This note makes that limitation precise, then gives an ACTUAL nontrivial positive cross-color transfer for the cube packet already proved, with its sharp norm and iterated source rate. The eight cycle projections remain in one cube; there is no full-color cube or arbitrary-graph volume-conjecture assertion. ## 1. What the correlated Gram does under complete-circle observation On a supported source cell use the exact boundary frame R_r=C[eta_1,...,eta_r]/eta_i^2, lambda(fv)=tau[eta_all](q f), q(0)=1, w_I=q^(-1/2)eta_Iv, <w_I,w_J>=delta_IJ. The [whole-support theorem](actual_whole_support_boundary_gram_envelope.md) proves polynomial source cost K and exact dual cost tau^2 K in this frame. But the complete paired-circle product itself is simply eta_all w_empty=w_all, eta_all w_I=0 for I!=empty. (1) Thus it has operator norm EXACTLY ONE and rank one. The simple axes contribute their actual scalar N, so the full three-circle product has norm N^(3-r). On its image the original row is lambda(w_all)=tau, lambda(eta_all f v)=tau f(0). (2) Equations (1),(2) keep the original marked row; they do not replace it by an ordinary cap. They also show that the complete observation does not measure the lower nilpotent coordinates of f. After this observation, a Cauchy estimate on one cell is an estimate of its one surviving scalar. Polynomial K supplies no independent geometric upper bound for that scalar's exterior-dependent energy. ## 2. The exact weighted packet and its available transport Let D_N be the supported folded triples and put theta_l=Z_theta(l)>0, a_G(l)=Z_G(l)/theta_l, F_G(l)=sqrt(theta_l)a_G(l)=Z_G(l)/sqrt(theta_l). Here Z_G(l) is the COMPLETE coherent interior source with the three boundary labels fixed, not an individual black vertex. For the exact typed vertex substitution, including the exposed mark and one circle per merged edge, the [source sewing theorem](actual_nc_three_port_source_sewing.md) gives Z_new=sum_(l in D_N) theta_l a_A(l)a_B(l) =sum_l F_A(l)F_B(l), |Z_new|^2<=E_A E_B, E_G=sum_l |Z_G(l)|^2/theta_l. (3) The bilinear sewing map has norm one in this explicitly prescribed Hilbert space. Its Cauchy proof conjugates the first numerical vector; it does NOT assume that one physical graph is the mirror of the other. No extra K or generic inverse-frame factor occurs in (3). The theta weight can be exponential and must not be called a polynomial cost. Grafting a fixed piece B onto an unsummed boundary is multiplication by a_B. Its norm is EXACTLY max_l |a_B(l)|. Thus sharp control of (3) requires the actual boundary packet or this multiplier, not just an estimate of the closed scalar sum_l Z_B(l). For example, for two supported labels l_1,l_2 the numerical packet a(l_1)=T/theta_(l_1), a(l_2)=-T/theta_(l_2) has closure zero and unbounded energy as T grows. This is a finite-space obstruction to deducing energy from one closure; it is not asserted to be a realizable knot counterexample. The proved signed-theta boundary has a_theta,e(l)=product_i omega_(l_i)^e_i. It is consequently an exact unitary multiplier in (3). These are actual source-preserving twist operations; theta substitution itself leaves the graph skeleton unchanged. The one-variable complete-pretzel circle metric is a different actual cut and polarization. A bound on its one closed functional does not identify a three-variable F_G or bound E_G without an explicit port-opening identity. No such general identity is inferred here. ## 3. An actual two-boundary cube transfer beyond a scalar closure Now take N=2m+1 and the original ordered cube of the [four-rung packet](actual_cube_four_rung_positive_source.md). Fix its eight cycle edges to m. Keep the outer-white rung (edge 10) at j, the interval-black rung (edge 1) at l, and sum the other two rung labels (edges 4,7). Use zero rung twists. Set p_j=P_(N,j)>0, k_j=2 except k_m=1, h_j=Rturn L_j/(N k_j), f=sum_(l=0)^m k_l p_l^2 h_l, theta_j=Z_theta(m,j,m)=N^3 k_j p_j^2. (4) The last normalization is exact: in the actual theta formula s_j s_(d-j)=N and the one-leg source has R_N(m,j,m)=p_j. All paired rung nilpotents and the original unrestricted mark remain. By the proved four-rung SOURCE formula and linearity, the actual two-boundary cube contribution is B_(j,l)=N^12 k_j k_l p_j^2 p_l^2 phi(h_j h_l f^2). (5) This is a full coherent magnetic contraction, not a product of unsewn black coefficients. The exposed white boundary is (m,j,m) and the interval black boundary is (m,l,m), with their original orders. Both are supported at every j,l. For a typed graft, the three shared contacts are summed once using the exact denominator theta_l, so its relative-packet transport is a_new(j)=sum_l B_(j,l)/theta_j *a_old(l). Equivalently in F=sqrt(theta)a coordinates its matrix is A_(j,l)=B_(j,l)/sqrt(theta_j theta_l) =N^9 sqrt(k_j k_l)p_j p_l phi(h_j h_l f^2). (6) This is an actual cross-color kernel, not the product of two known closed scalar values. It is real symmetric and ENTRYWISE strictly positive. Indeed all h_j have positive Newton coefficients through their degree j, while f^2 has strictly positive coefficients at every degree 0,...,d. The constant coefficient of h_jh_l is positive, so the actual phi in (6) is strictly positive. The Newton theorem retains the full root algebra and its first normals in this argument. Entry positivity does not make A a positive semidefinite Gram. At N=3, h_0=1,h_1=1+Bhat_1, p_0=1,p_1=2 and f=6+4Bhat_1. The exact matrix of the phi factors in (6) is [phi(h_j h_l f^2)]_(j,l=0,1) = [[16,80],[80,244]], determinant=-2496. (7) Thus A itself has determinant -19968*3^18. This is a genuine correlated transfer with both eigenvalue signs; no Hilbert norm square or physical reflection identity is being smuggled into it. ## 4. Its operator norm has the sharp primitive-core increment Put h=h_m, S=p_m, W=phi(h^4)>0. Coefficientwise Newton monotonicity and the positive multiplication law give h_j<=h, p_j<=S, S^2 h<=f<=2(m+1)S^2 h. Consequently, with R_N=N^9 S^6 W, R_N<=A_(m,m)<=[2(m+1)]^2 R_N, 0<A_(j,l)<=2A_(m,m), A_(m,m)<=||A||_2<=2(m+1)A_(m,m). (8) The last lower bound is a diagonal Rayleigh quotient. The upper bound is the maximum row sum for the absolute-entry matrix, or sqrt(||A||_1||A||_infty); symmetry makes those norms equal. It does not require A to be positive semidefinite. Thus (8) is a direct source-preserving weighted Cauchy transport estimate whose exponent is computed independently from positive factorial periods. The proved actual central scalar and [cuboctahedral period theorem](actual_positive_newton_cuboctahedral_period.md) give, on all odd levels, lim (1/N)log||A||_2=6v8/pi+Vol(Q_cube)/pi. In hyperbolic-volume units this is lim (2pi/N)log||A||_2 =12v8+2Vol(Q_cube) =Vol(augmented cube)-Vol(augmented theta). (9) The equality with these ACTUAL complements is the independently proved labeled rectified-core geometry, not a volume-constant fit. It is the precise primitive-core increment in this projected packet. ## 5. Iteration is a genuine but still projected graph-source family Start with theta, keeping its two cycle contacts at m and its third label j summed. Repeatedly insert the ordered cube at the interval black vertex (0,1,2), with outer white boundary (0,10,11). Preserve the original exposed mark. At each stage the two cycle contacts remain m and the middle contact is summed as an actual full circle. The exact NC substitution supplies the new Morse word and one circle per merged edge. Equations (3),(5),(6) give, for fixed k>=0, Z_k^proj=u^T A^k u, u_j=sqrt(theta_j). (10) This is the raw original partial source of the resulting graph. It retains ALL 1+3k rung labels and fixes the 2+6k cycle labels to m. The graph has b=1+3k vertices of each color. The one exposed physical mark is never replicated; the formula comes from the already normalized fixed-first-normal quotient at each graft. Every matrix entry in (10) is positive. Choosing only the central index at each step supplies the lower bound, while (8) and u_j<=sqrt(2)u_m supply the upper bound N^(3+9k) S^(2+6k) W^k <= Z_k^proj <=[2(m+1)]^(3k+1) N^(3+9k) S^(2+6k) W^k. (11) For k=1 this is the exact four-rung packet bound; k=0 is the one-rung theta face. Therefore for every fixed k, lim_(N odd) (2pi/N)log Z_k^proj =(4+12k)v8+2k Vol(Q_cube). (12) The actual graph geometry is the same sequence of triangular core grafts: its core is k cuboctahedra glued along triangles, with additive volume k Vol(Q_cube). The [rectified-core theorem](actual_nc_graph_rectified_core_geometry.md) therefore identifies (12) with its ACTUAL augmented complement volume. All cycle twists can be kept as one common unit character; different rung-twist phases do not preserve this positivity argument. The proved one-leg boundary gap also transfers, without a new stationary-phase assertion. For fixed delta>0, p_j/S<=poly(N)exp(-gamma_delta N) whenever m-j>=delta N. Resolve each f in (5) into its actual complete-circle color sum and iterate the source quotient. Every one of the 1+3k rung labels occurs with its factor k_jp_j^2 ONCE, while every surviving phi factor is bounded above by W using h_j<=h. Therefore sum_(some rung m-j>=delta N) Z_(k,labels)^proj <=poly_(k,delta)(N)exp(-2gamma_delta N) N^(3+9k)S^(2+6k)W^k. (13) These are the whole-label one-leg estimates of the actual theta source transported through a specified branching kernel. They now control EVERY unfrozen rung channel in the projected chain, rather than just its scalar endpoints. The labels remain INTERNAL pair- Casimir channels. No auxiliary meridian interpretation, complex peripheral-color packet or Dehn-filling estimate follows from (13). This is an unbounded sequence of actual graph diagrams and correlated source transports. It remains a PARTIAL original source with many cycle projections and odd levels. Removing those projections and controlling even levels remain necessary before asserting a full graph invariant equality. The result does not rename the general scalar Cauchy inequality as a sharp energy theorem: its new energy bound is the independently positive two-boundary kernel (5)--(8). Audit: [literal boundary kernels and projected graph sources](../experiments/audit_actual_three_port_cauchy_transport_and_cube_kernel.py), with [recorded results](../experiments/actual_three_port_cauchy_transport_and_cube_kernel_results.json). The focused replay passes the exact N=3 non-PSD certificate, all three full boundary matrices at N=3,5,7 using 353 original marked rung contractions, and seven complete projected-chain sources, including the fourteen-vertex two-cube source with all seven rung labels summed. The source checks use the actual unrestricted mark and local regular generic first-normal identities. They supplement the all-N source/graft and positive-cone proofs, not an inference from measured matrix spectra or a whole-graph invariant claim. The exact scalar quotient pairing and the bounded projected cross-color kernel are different objects. The latter estimate does not establish equality with a full graph invariant.

title: A polynomial-cost Fourier kernel for every original twist block
text: # A polynomial-cost Fourier kernel for every original twist block 29 October 2026. Every signed power of the original equal-color crossing has an explicit Chebyshev expansion whose coefficient mass is O(N(1+|ell|)). It retains the full Casimir Hermite jets, including the odd simple node. For a full twist ell=2p this supplies the coefficient kernel for the entire ordinary circle-color packet, rather than an inversion of a single complete-color circle. The [literal mixed-color circle calculation](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_crossing_circle_source_and_filling.md) identifies the displayed operators with the original pivotal encircling sources. This is therefore an exact quantitative source transformation at arbitrary width, with the marked cut unchanged. Polynomial coefficient mass does not prevent cancellation in the resulting filling sum, and does not prove geometric survival. ## 1. The complete local spectral data Use N>=2, d=N-1, q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, kappa=q^(d^2/2). The original pair Casimir Omega has polynomial P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2, c_k=w_k+w_k^(-1), w_k=q^(2k+1), 0<=k<N. Its distinct nodes have multiplicity two, except c=-2 when N is odd. The original full checked crossing is R=kappa r_N(Omega), with the original, already derived values and jets nu_k=r_N(c_k)=(-1)^k q^[k(k+1)], r_N'(c_k)/nu_k=-(d-2k)/[2(w_k-w_k^(-1))] (1) at double nodes. The possible simple node has only the value condition. These are the complete physical spectral data; there is no semisimple projection. For a negative power use the actual inverse crossing, not its adjoint. For any integer ell let f_(N,ell) be the unique polynomial of degree less than N representing r_N^ell modulo P_N. Negative powers exist because every nu_k is nonzero. Define finite data h_k=nu_k^ell, d_k=-(ell/2)(d-2k) h_k. (2) At double nodes, d_k=(w_k-w_k^(-1))f'(c_k). At the odd simple node d-2k=0 and w_k-w_k^(-1)=0, so d_k=0 without prescribing an additional derivative. All |h_k|=1 and |d_k|<=|ell|N/2. ## 2. Exact Fourier-Hermite interpolation Take the marked finite Fourier transforms H_n=(1/N)sum_k h_k w_k^(-n), D_n=(1/N)sum_k d_k w_k^(-n), 0<=n<N. (3) Then the COMPLETE polynomial is f_(N,ell)(z)=a_0+sum_(n=1)^d a_n 2T_n(z/2), a_0=H_0, a_n=[D_n+(N-n)H_n]/N, 1<=n<N. (4) Here is a direct proof, avoiding a conditioned confluent Vandermonde inverse. Set g(w)=f(w+w^(-1)). Its Laurent coefficients are a_0 and the symmetric pair a_n at exponents n and -n. Since w_k^N=-1, the node values and logarithmic derivatives have Fourier aliases H_n=a_n-a_(N-n), D_n=n a_n+(N-n)a_(N-n), 1<=n<N, H_0=a_0, D_0=0. (5) Solving the two equations gives (4). The paired nodes k,d-k have the same h and opposite d, so the compatibility conditions for (5) are automatic. At n=N/2, when present, H_n=0 and the second equation still gives the correct coefficient. At the odd simple node the logarithmic derivative of every such g is zero. Thus (4) imposes exactly the N original Hermite conditions, with no extra endpoint constraint, at every even and composite level too. Equation (4) immediately gives the uniform coefficient bounds |a_0|<=1, |a_n|<=1+|ell|/2. (6) No separation bound for nearby Casimir nodes is needed. ## 3. Full circle-color coefficients and their norm Let U_j denote the second-kind Chebyshev polynomial, U_0=1, U_1=z when its argument is z/2. Put a_N=a_(N+1)=0 and define beta_j=(-1)^j(a_j-a_(j+2)), 0<=j<N. (7) The identities 2T_n=U_n-U_(n-2), n>=2, and 2T_1=U_1 give f_(N,ell)(Omega) =sum_(j=0)^d beta_j (-1)^j U_j(Omega/2), R^ell=kappa^ell sum_(j=0)^d beta_j L_(j+1), L_(j+1)=(-1)^j U_j(Omega/2). (8) All phases, including kappa^ell, are retained. Summing (6) gives sum_(j=0)^d |beta_j| <= 2N(1+|ell|/2). (9) For ell=2p, (8) is an exact full-twist filling kernel of mass at most 2N(1+|p|). The separate [physical circle proof](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_crossing_circle_source_and_filling.md) realizes L_j as the actual ordinary pivotal j-color encircling operator, including its original framing and trace. A single L_N is not inverted or declared sufficient; the whole degree-<N basis occurs in (8). This bound holds uniformly in N and p, including negative twists and all gcd/parity cases. There is no division by p or by a Gauss sum. For ell=0 the expansion reduces exactly to L_1=I. For full twists the data in (3) are particularly explicit: h_k=Q^[p k(k+1)], d_k=-p(d-2k)h_k, H_n=(1/N)sum_k Q^[p k(k+1)]q^[-n(2k+1)]. (10) The corresponding D_n is the SAME finite quadratic sum with its retained linear normal weight -p(d-2k). Dropping this weight would erase the derivative data of the original crossing and generally change the invariant. Formula (10) specifies the filling phases before any large-N or long-filling analysis. ## 4. Simultaneous filling and the actual remaining theorem Replace a fixed collection of disjoint twist blocks R^(2p_i) by (8) BEFORE any exterior contraction. Distributivity gives the exact sum of the same original tensor diagram with circle operators L_(j_i) in those slots. All spectator tensors, the original marked cut and peripheral/framing line retain their order and values. The total coefficient mass is at most product_i [2N(1+|p_i|)]. (11) For a fixed number of blocks this is polynomial when the p_i are fixed; more generally its logarithm is o(N) whenever sum_i log(1+|p_i|)=o(N). Thus no exponential coefficient cost is introduced by retaining the complete circle-color data. Together with the physical circle identification, this supplies an original-source input for simultaneous crossing-circle fillings. It does not identify a fixed complete-color augmented-link scalar with this packet, nor replace its trace by a different invariant. The next geometric survival question is substantive: obtain a nonzero selected geometric period for that actual MIXED-COLOR augmented source and control the coherent filling sum (10). Taking absolute values in (11) gives only a maximum over the base packet; it does not automatically yield the smaller filled-manifold volume. No broad original-knot volume theorem is claimed by this expansion. The [complete Fourier--Hermite Gram](../papers/filling-bounds/README.md) turns these coefficients into an explicit positive Cauchy metric. Its exact dual cost is 1+ell^2(N^2-1)/(12N^2), uniformly bounded in N for a fixed twist. A literal original normalization insertion also proves that this metric's energy can be excessive even when the final knot is hyperbolic. A sharp geometric energy estimate requires more than the controlled filling-source norm. The [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_twist_circle_fourier_kernel.py) compares 81 signed physical crossing powers at N=2,...,10 and 64 complex full-Hermite/coefficient-mass cases through N=48. The formulas retain both Fourier aliases, the even middle index and the odd simple node.

title: Whole-domain large Fourier charges: exact paired currents and a vanishing-rate operator tail
status: Whole-domain operator tail; mixed environment kept
text: # Whole-domain large Fourier charges: exact paired currents and a vanishing-rate operator tail , 31 October 2026. This concerns the actual fixed-root operator coupons and their original marked contraction. It does not split an infinite charge series at an artificial real cutoff. Twists are fixed before $N$. The resulting all-far-sector bound is proved; a partial-far mixed-source estimate is isolated explicitly in Section 5. ## 1. Original one-port Fourier coupons Put $d=N-1$, $q=e^{\pi i/N}$, $\Omega$ equal to the original pair Casimir, $\chi_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2$ and $V_N(z)=\chi_N(z)(z-\Omega)^{-1}$, interpreted as its degree-$d$ polynomial. Work in the original balanced physical basis used by the [full endpoint-resolvent theorem](../papers/filling-bounds/README.md), including its high-total adapter. All physical degrees form its orthogonal direct sum. For a fixed integer $n$ define $$ \begin{aligned} B_{N,n}(\delta)&=\sin(2\pi\delta)e^{\pi i nN\delta^2}V_N(-2\cos(2\pi\delta)),\\ J_{N,n,\ell}&=\int_{-1/2}^{1/2}B_{N,n}(\delta)e^{2\pi i\ell N\delta}\,d\delta,\\ F_{N,n,\ell}&=q^{nd^2/4}(-i)\ell(-1)^{(N+1)\ell}J_{N,n,\ell}. \end{aligned} $$ The [exact full-Hermite formula](actual_spectral_total_derivative_source.md) gives $$ R^n=\sum_{\ell\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}}F_{N,n,\ell}.\tag{1} $$ The series is absolutely convergent for each fixed $N,n$. Its endpoint regularity is that of the WHOLE interval. Since $B$ is odd, $J_{-\ell}=-J_\ell$; therefore $F_{-\ell}=F_\ell$, including the original parity character. There is no $\ell=0$ term. For integer $M\geq1$ put $$ T_{N,n;M}=\sum_{|\ell|>M}F_{N,n,\ell}.\tag{2} $$ This is a literal operator in the actual Casimir quotient, not an auxiliary scalar source or a truncated physical head sum. ## 2. Exact contour shift and the paired endpoint current For positive $\ell$ shift the WHOLE interval vertically UP to height $\tau>0$. The integrand is entire. If $H_{N,n,\ell;\tau}$ denotes the upper horizontal integral, the two actual side currents give $$ \begin{aligned} J_{N,n,\ell}={}&H_{N,n,\ell;\tau}\\ &-i(-1)^{N\ell}\int_0^\tau e^{-2\pi\ell Nv} \left[B_{N,n}\!\left(\tfrac12+iv\right)-B_{N,n}\!\left(-\tfrac12+iv\right)\right]dv. \end{aligned}\tag{3} $$ Both endpoints have the SAME spectral value $z(v)=2\cosh(2\pi v)$. Their sine values are $-i\sinh(2\pi v)$, whereas the two Gaussian values are $e^{\pi i nN(1/4-v^2)}e^{\mp\pi nNv}$. Consequently EXACTLY $$ B\!\left(\tfrac12+iv\right)-B\!\left(-\tfrac12+iv\right) =2i\sinh(2\pi v)\sinh(\pi nNv)e^{\pi i nN(1/4-v^2)}V_N(2\cosh(2\pi v)).\tag{4} $$ In particular the paired current vanishes to order TWO at $v=0$. The second factor is a hyperbolic sine, not a bounded oscillatory sine. Its growth $e^{\pi|n|Nv}$ is kept in every estimate. Substitution in (3) gives the plus-sign version $$ J=H+2(-1)^{N\ell}\int_0^\tau e^{-2\pi\ell Nv} \sinh(2\pi v)\sinh(\pi nNv)e^{\pi i nN(1/4-v^2)}V_N(2\cosh(2\pi v))\,dv.\tag{5} $$ Thus multiplication by the original Fourier character in $F$ leaves the vertical character $(-1)^\ell$, not a level-dependent endpoint sign. No individual vertical side is set to zero. Formula (3) is an equality before any summation or norm bound. ## 3. Uniform original operator bound for the tail There are absolute $\tau_0>0$ and constants $c,C,C_0$ such that the following holds for every fixed $n$, $0<\tau\leq\tau_0$ and integer $M$ with $$ D=M-\frac{|n|}{2}-1\geq1. $$ After increasing the constants when needed, $$ \begin{aligned} \|T_{N,n;M}\|\leq{}&C_{n,\tau}N^Ce^{C(\log N)^2} \Bigl\{(M+1)e^{-N(2\pi\tau D-C_0)}\\ &\qquad+\left[D^{-1}+(|n|+1)D^{-2}\right]e^{N\varepsilon(D)}\Bigr\},\\ \varepsilon(D)&=Ce^{-cD}\longrightarrow0\quad(D\longrightarrow\infty). \end{aligned}\tag{6} $$ Only fixed-$n$ uniformity in $N$ is asserted. In particular, for every $\eta>0$ there is $L_\eta$, independent of $n$, such that choosing $$ M\geq\frac{|n|}{2}+1+L_\eta, $$ (with an integer ceiling) makes $$ \limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\|T_{N,n;M}\|\leq\eta.\tag{7} $$ The constants multiplying (6) may depend on the fixed $n$. The cutoff in (7) has the natural Gaussian threshold $|n|/2$ and an additional fixed allowance. This is a bound for the original FULL-V Fourier coupon, including semisimple data. Proof of the horizontal part. In the original balanced root basis $\|F\|,\|\mathcal E\|\leq2$ and $K$ is unitary. The literal coproduct gives $\|F_{\mathrm{tot}}\|,\|\mathcal E_{\mathrm{tot}}\|\leq4$, hence $\|\Omega\|\leq18$ on the ENTIRE physical tensor product. This includes high totals without changing the norm by a basis adapter. Equivalently the actual blocks have fixed bandwidth and uniformly bounded entries. The exact divided-Chebyshev identity is $$ V_N(z)=U_{N-1}(\Omega/2)+2\sum_{h=1}^{N-1}T_{N-h}(z/2)U_{h-1}(\Omega/2). $$ The scalar recurrences imply $\|U_j(\Omega/2)\|\leq C_*^{j+1}$ for an absolute $C_*>1$. On $\delta=x+i\tau$, $|x|\leq1/2$, $$ |T_k(-\cos(2\pi\delta))|\leq e^{2\pi k\tau}. $$ Thus $\|V_N(-2\cos(2\pi\delta))\|\leq CN e^{N(C_0+2\pi\tau)}$ for a fixed $C_0$. The sine is bounded, the Gaussian modulus is at most $e^{\pi|n|N\tau}$, and the Fourier modulus is $e^{-2\pi\ell N\tau}$. The resulting geometric sum of $\ell$ times horizontal integrals is bounded by the first term of (6), after a harmless adjustment from $M+1$ to $M$. It introduces no false coefficientwise real-spectral bound. Proof of the vertical part. Use the already proved [original closing-region estimate](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_casimir_closing_region_bound.md) on the right real ray, with $r=2\cosh(2\pi v)-2$: $$ \|(2\cosh(2\pi v)-\Omega)^{-1}\| \leq CN^3e^{CNf(r)+C(\log N)^2},\qquad f(r)=\sqrt r\log(2+1/r). $$ It applies at $v=0$ by the polynomial endpoint bound as well. Since $\chi_N(2\cosh(2\pi v))=2\cosh(2\pi Nv)+2$, and $r$ is comparable to $v^2$, $$ \|V_N(2\cosh(2\pi v))\| \leq CN^3\exp\!\left\{N\left[2\pi v+Cv\log(C/v)\right]+C(\log N)^2\right\}.\tag{8} $$ All constants are uniform for $0\leq v\leq\tau_0$, and $v\log(C/v)=0$ at $v=0$. Also $$ |\sinh(2\pi v)\sinh(\pi nNv)|\leq C|n|Nv^2e^{\pi|n|Nv}. $$ For $D_\ell=\ell-|n|/2-1$, (5) therefore gives, up to polynomial factors, $$ |n|N^4\ell e^{C(\log N)^2}\int_0^\tau v^2 \exp\!\left\{N\left[-2\pi D_\ell v+Cv\log(C/v)\right]\right\}dv.\tag{9} $$ Reserve half the damping for the integral. Elementary one-variable optimization yields $$ \sup_{v\geq0}\left[Cv\log(C/v)-\pi Dv\right] \leq C'e^{-cD}=\varepsilon(D). $$ Since $D_\ell\geq D$, the remaining integral is at most $$ e^{N\varepsilon(D)}\int_0^\infty v^2e^{-\pi ND_\ell v}\,dv =\frac{2e^{N\varepsilon(D)}}{(\pi ND_\ell)^3}. $$ Finally $$ \sum_{\ell>M}\frac{\ell}{D_\ell^3} \leq C\left[D^{-1}+(|n|+1)D^{-2}\right].\tag{10} $$ This proves (6), with both charge signs included using their exact symmetry. The bound is an ABSOLUTE summation of paired whole-domain currents. It never uses convergence of an infinite sharp-cube series. Choose $D$ so $2\pi\tau D-C_0>0$ and $\varepsilon(D)<\eta$ to obtain (7). The $n=0$ case has zero vertical current; its finite-band Fourier formula in fact has no charges $|\ell|>1$, consistent with this proof. ## 4. A genuine source consequence when ALL ports are far Keep the original diagram order, the original physical cups/caps and its single mark. Replacing every $R_i^{n_i}$ by $T_{N,n_i;M_i}$ gives EXACTLY the subseries of the original whole-domain Fourier period with $|\ell_i|>M_i$ for EVERY port. Finite-$N$ absolute convergence and multilinearity justify this identity; physical coupons are never commuted. Call this marked contraction $Z_{\mathrm{allfar}}$. In the same balanced physical basis, the finitely many actual turns, closures and single marked cap have polynomial operator/Euclidean norms in $N$. Their entries are the original $N$ times unit-phase cup, $N^{-1}$ ordinary cap and $N^{-2}$ marked cap. More explicitly, cups and ordinary caps have $a+b=d$; the marked cap $m_{ab}=x^b/N^2$ is UNRESTRICTED. Their Euclidean norms are respectively $N^{3/2}$, $N^{-1/2}$ and $N^{-1}$, and the retained right-turn pivots are unit phases. The number of wires and contractions is fixed by the diagram. Hence $$ |Z_{\mathrm{allfar}}|\leq\operatorname{poly}_D(N)\prod_i\|T_{N,n_i;M_i}\|, \qquad\limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log|Z_{\mathrm{allfar}}|\leq\sum_i\varepsilon(D_i).\tag{11} $$ once each horizontal term has been made exponentially decreasing. This is an actual shared-source estimate, not a replacement of its coefficient by arbitrary face radii. All $n_i$ are fixed before $N$. The [geometric local unit theorem](general_localized_unit_charge_filling_period.md) gives $\Phi_{\mathrm{fill}}\geq\Phi_D/2$ for ALL independently sufficiently long fixed twists, after increasing a threshold depending only on the original diagram. Choose fixed $D_i$ so $\sum_i\varepsilon(D_i)<\Phi_D/4$ and all horizontal exponents in (6) are negative. These $D_i$ depend on the fixed diagram, not on ratios or magnitudes of the long slopes. The actual cutoffs can therefore be chosen as $M_i=\lceil|n_i|/2+1+D_i\rceil$. Then (11) gives a uniform strict RATE gap from the proved local contribution throughout that general long-filling class. Prefactor and relative-error constants may still depend on the fixed twists; no joint growing-twist/level limit follows. This does not cover the much larger UNION of sectors in which only one or some charges are far. ## 5. Partial far subsets: the exact missing mixed-source estimate Let $\mathcal E_{D,S,N}$ be the literal original marked exterior functional with $R_j^{n_j}$ retained, in their original order, on every $j$ outside a nonempty set $S$. Define its norm on the remaining tensor product of operator spaces by $$ \|\mathcal E_{D,S,N}\|= \sup_{\substack{\|A_i\|\leq1\\ i\in S}} \left|\mathcal E_{D,S,N}\!\left(\bigotimes_{i\in S}A_i\right)\right|. $$ Then the immediate correct bound for that subset is $$ \left|\mathcal E_{D,S,N}\!\left(\bigotimes_{i\in S}T_i\right)\right| \leq\|\mathcal E_{D,S,N}\|\prod_{i\in S}\|T_i\|.\tag{12} $$ There is no established reason for the first factor to have rate less than $\Phi_{\mathrm{fill}}$. The remaining signed $R$ powers are NOT uniformly unitary in this basis. Their individual exponential norm bounds only supply a crude upper rate depending on the retained twists. Equation (7) alone therefore cannot remove a partial-far sector. The exact finite inclusion-exclusion identity for the union is $$ Z_{\mathrm{full}}-Z_{\mathrm{all\,low}} =\sum_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq\mathrm{ports}}(-1)^{|S|+1} \mathcal E_{D,S,N}\!\left(\bigotimes_{i\in S}T_i\right).\tag{13} $$ It retains the original full $R$ powers on the complement of $S$, rather than replacing them by an uncontrolled collection of infinitely many spectator charge pieces. A direct sufficient new input would be a strict bound on these actual mixed exteriors, or a narrower estimate on the paired-current families $$ \mathcal E_{D,S,N}\!\left(\bigotimes_{i\in S}V_i(2\cosh(2\pi v_i))\right), \qquad0\leq v_i\leq\tau.\tag{14} $$ with a rate strictly below $\Phi_{\mathrm{fill}}$ as $v$ tends to zero, uniformly on a small fixed closing box, including simultaneous endpoint subsets. Every sine, Gaussian and charge character in (4)-(5) would then remain explicit and summably controlled. Horizontal pieces can be made as small as needed by increasing the fixed charge cutoffs, using a crude finite exponential norm for the fixed remaining coupons. The difficult input is thus the SHARED endpoint environment in (14), not a missing local +2 resolvent estimate. Neither the positive Fejer endpoint theorem at $\sigma=-2$ nor the noncross local gap proves (14) at $\sigma=+2$ with arbitrary remaining $R$ powers. Nor does a local norm estimate prove the needed shared rate. This distinction is preserved in (11)-(14). No full invariant or partial-far complement theorem is claimed here. ## Validation and scope The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_whole_domain_large_charge_tail.py) and its [results](../experiments/actual_whole_domain_large_charge_tail_results.json) check paired endpoint entries, whole-interval contour identities and charge-sign identities from the physical blocks. These are finite normalization checks, not proofs of an asymptotic rate or a mixed-source gap.

title: The original complete core has a finite coupled face-coefficient system
status: Exact polynomial system and fold selection; regular-chart momenta
text: # The original complete core has a finite coupled face-coefficient system 30 October 2026. The original four-component circle system admits a polynomial source gauge that preserves its first component. Tensoring it on the actual shared face variables gives an exact whole-source system coupling only finitely shifted face coefficients. The original finite support and a source-selected fold adapter determine its polynomial solution. Its reduced characteristic is identified algebraically with the existing ORDERED local character transport. This is a system for the complete-image external-color core. It does not erase its ordinary small-color subsets, eliminate the coefficient family to a scalar A-polynomial, or establish a complex asymptotic of its period. ## 1. A polynomial four-component source gauge Use N>=3, d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2 and the actual polynomial Z_j(x,b,y), 0<=j<=d, of the [fixed-fold source theorem](actual_positive_face_fixed_fold_packet.md), equation(10). Write Z_-1=0 and Delta_j=(x-Q^j y)(x-Q^(-j)y), Pcal_j=P_d(x,y)/product_(r=1)^j Delta_r, P_d(x,y)=product_(r=1)^d(x-Q^r y). The rational presentation of Pcal_j is used only to define the following source; its canceled polynomial expressions are proved below. Retain omega_j=q^(d^2/2)(-1)^j q^[j(j+1)], U_j=omega_j^epsilon Pcal_j (Z_j^b Z_j^c, Z_j^b Z_(j-1)^c, Z_(j-1)^b Z_j^c, Delta_j Z_(j-1)^b Z_(j-1)^c)^T. (1) Here the superscript b or c indicates the middle face, not a power. The first component is precisely the original reflected complete-circle polynomial omega_j^epsilon B_ext,j. In the notation of the fixed-fold note, U_j=G_j V_j with G_j=diag(1,1,1,Delta_j). ALL FOUR components of (1) are polynomials in x,b,c,y. Below the fold, Pcal_j is the ordinary forced polynomial, so the claim is immediate. Above the fold put r=d-j and s=d-2r. The actual large-H reflection gives Z_j=P_s Z_r, Pcal_j=P_s^-1. For s>=2, Z_(j-1)=P_(s-2) Z_(r+1), so the second and third components reduce respectively to P_(s-2) Z_r^b Z_(r+1)^c and P_(s-2) Z_(r+1)^b Z_r^c. At the even first bridge s=1, they instead reduce to Z_M^b Z_M^c, where M=floor(d/2). Finally (U_j)_4=omega_j^epsilon B_ext,(j-1), j>=1, because Delta_j Pcal_j=Pcal_(j-1). It is zero at j=0. This proves polynomiality, including zero-face evaluations, without choosing a Laurent expansion at a pole. The component degrees are d,d-1,d-1,d. The gauge G is not invertible on Delta_j=0; no such divisor is discarded. Put theta=pi/N and retain the actual finite coefficients u_j=cos((j-1)theta)sin(j theta), v_j^b=sin((2j-1)theta)[x+y+2b cos(j theta)cos((j-1)theta)], barw_j=sin((j-1)theta)cos(j theta), w_j=barw_j Delta_(j-1), L_j=u_j^2 Delta_j, r_j=(-Q^j)^epsilon. The exact polynomial-gauge recurrence is L_j U_j=r_j N_j U_(j-1), (2) N_j= [v_j^b v_j^c, -v_j^b w_j, -w_j v_j^c, barw_j^2 Delta_(j-1)] [u_j v_j^b, 0, -u_j w_j, 0] [u_j v_j^c, -u_j w_j, 0, 0] [Delta_j u_j^2,0, 0, 0]. Indeed N_j=G_j M_j G_(j-1)^-1 on the localized field. Its only apparent denominator is w_j^2/Delta_(j-1), and it cancels exactly as displayed. Thus (2) is polynomial and extends across that divisor. The original finite sequence is zero outside 0,...,d. The equations at j=0 and j=N remain true: the first uses u_0=0 and U_-1=0; the last uses the two actual terminal scalar relations and u_N=0. There is no periodic closing arrow or omitted endpoint current. Every coefficient of (2) is Laurent in Q^j. Its face degree is at most three. If mathcal U(z)=sum_(j=0)^d U_j z^j and Theta f(z)=f(Qz), then exactly [L(Theta)-z(-Q Theta)^epsilon N(Q Theta)]mathcal U(z)=0. (3) The Laurent Theta powers lie between -5 and5; the z-degree is at most1. These bounds are independent of N. The first component is unchanged from the original finite core. For its full Fourier gauge S(chi)=exp(pi i d chi)mathcal U(exp(-2pi i chi)), retain exactly exp(pi i d chi)Theta mathcal U=q^d S(chi-1/N). (4) ## 2. The original source selects the fold crossing This section concerns the finite source, not a choice of formal WKB solution. Work over the face coefficient field localized at the Delta_j that occur, and put M=floor(d/2), s0=d-2M and h=M+s0+1=d-M+1. The known initial vector is U_0=omega_0^epsilon P_d(x,y)(1,0,0,0)^T. Let R4 reverse the four components. The ACTUAL source has the exact polynomial fold adapter U_h=q^((s0+1)epsilon) R4 U_M. (5) A direct proof uses h=d-(M-1) and h-1=d-M in the large-H reflection. The first and fourth components exchange because B_ext,(d-j)=B_ext,j; the two cross products exchange with their forced factors. Finally Delta_h=Delta_M and omega_h/omega_M=q^(s0+1). These give every component of (5), including the even bridge s0=1. No new square root is required. The adapter is a unit phase times a permutation. Near the actual fold Delta_M=(x+y)^2-4xy sin^2((s0+1)pi/(2N)) is uniformly positive on the stated positive radius compact. The adapter advances one step at odd levels and TWO at even levels. To see why this matters, write N=2H, M=H-1. At j=H the leading coefficient is nonzero and the transfer has rank one: U_H=(1,A^-1,A^-1,1)^T (U_(H-1))_1, A=x+y. (6) At j=H+1 its leading coefficient is zero, while N_(H+1) has just one nonzero row, sin^2(theta)(A^2,-A^3,-A^3,A^2). It annihilates (6), so this row places no condition on U_(H+1). An invertible analytic gauge cannot change this rank loss. For generic face data and every even N>=4, the finite system (2), with zero support outside 0,...,d and prescribed U_0, therefore has a THREE-dimensional affine freedom whenever it has a solution. States through U_H are determined. The new U_(H+1) is an arbitrary four-vector; all later transfers through d are invertible. The terminal row at N imposes one nonzero condition. The determinant of N_j is [Delta_j/Delta_(j-1)](u_j w_j)^4, so these assertions retain the relevant factors. At odd N, u_j never vanishes inside 1,...,d, and the prescribed U_0 already determines every state. The source adapter (5) fixes the even free vector and restores uniqueness. Its compatibility with the terminal equation is provided by the literal Newton source and its reflection. This is not a claim of three different original sources: the unsupplemented operator has extra solutions, while its specified source data fixes one. ## 3. Exact whole-source coefficient equations Use the actual labeled planar source graph. Each circle i has its literal four incident faces (x_i,b_i,c_i,y_i), with all repeated or shared face names identified. Tensor the local polynomial vectors: W(z_1,...,z_R;L)=tensor_(i=1)^R mathcal U_i(z_i;L). It has 4^R components and is polynomial in EVERY face variable. For any nonnegative exponent vector n, define the finite coefficient family C_n(z)=[product_f L_f^(n_f)] W(z;L), (7) and set it to zero if some n_f<0. The component indexed by alpha has face degree dR-m(alpha), where m counts its local second/third indices. Thus the entire family is finite. It is not a choice of rational-series expansion or a coefficient integral through newly introduced divisors. Let S_i be the operator (3) acting on tensor factor i. Expand its actual face-polynomial coefficients as S_i=sum_nu L^nu S_(i,nu)(z_i,Theta_i). All nu are nonnegative and |nu|<=3. Exact coefficient extraction gives sum_nu S_(i,nu)(z_i,Theta_i) C_(n-nu)(z)=0, i=1,...,R, for every n. (8) These are the sought finite FACE SHIFTS. No scalar equation for only one selected coefficient is inferred. The operators commute before extraction: they act on separate external registers and separate tensor factors, while their shared face multiplications commute. The coupled coefficient equations inherit this compatibility. The local initial vectors and adapters (5) tensor to give the actual finite solution. Over the localized face field, uniqueness follows by advancing each register through its regular rows and its specified fold jump; the constructions in different registers commute. Polynomiality then follows from (1), not from an assertion about arbitrary operator solutions. The adapters can equally be recorded coefficientwise in (7). Let u,v be the two original marked faces and define n* by n*_u=n*_v=0, n*_f=d for every other face f. For the all-first tensor component, the exact original entire complete core is F_N(h)=chi_(D,N) N^R exp[pi i d sum_i h_i/N] (C_(n*))(exp(-2pi i h_1/N),...,exp(-2pi i h_R/N))_(1,...,1). (9) This follows from the source-exact reflected Fourier pairing and the original marked face-coefficient theorem. It retains the common twist phase, N^R measure, original mark and finite parity. The two marked faces are set to zero only AFTER polynomial extraction. Equation (9) is the empty subset in the external reflection formula; ordinary-color subsets are not represented by deleting them from this statement. ## 4. The principal characteristic is the actual ordered character map There is an exact algebraic identification with [the original local critical-character map](actual_augmented_plat_local_critical_character_map.md). Use its variables T,U,V,J and internal roots Z,W. On a regular chart, P(X,Y)=T(J-Y)^2(X-Y)+(Y-1)^2(TY-XJ)=0. (10) The source convention has b incoming and c outgoing. Thus the OLD ordered map has T=x/y, U=-x/c at the output and V=-x/b at the input. Put r=(J+1)^2/(4J), A=x+y, and D=A^2-4xy r, B_b=A+2br, B_c=A+2cr, e_out(Z)=-y Z(J-1)^2(TZ-UJ)/[J U(J-Z)^2], e_in(W)=-y W(J-1)^2(TW-VJ)/[J V(J-W)^2]. (11) Then (10) implies exactly e_out^2-2B_c e_out+D=0, e_in^2-2B_b e_in+D=0. (12) Here is a finite polynomial certificate. By homogeneity set y=1, x=T. For one generic triangle with middle face z=-T/X, write e=-Z(J-1)^2(TZ-XJ)/[J X(J-Z)^2] and B_z=T+1+2zr. Then e^2-2B_z e+D=-P(X,Z) K(X,Z)/[J X^2(J-Z)^4], K=J^3 X(J-T) +[JT(1-J^2)+2J^2X(T-1)]Z +[X(1-JT)+2T(J-1)]Z^2. Conversely the resultant of P(X,Z) and J X(J-Z)^2 e+Z(J-1)^2(TZ-XJ) is J^4 X^2(J-1)^4(T-X)^2 (e^2-2B_z e+D). Thus, away from the displayed degeneracies and the quadratic discriminant, the two local roots correspond to the two continuant roots. This is an elimination of the ACTUAL critical equation. The same character map's ordered centralizer eigenratio is R0=ZW(J-1)^4(TZ-UJ)(TW-VJ) /[JUV(J-Z)^2(J-W)^2(T-J)(TJ-1)]. Since D=y^2(T-J)(T-J^-1), its exact factorization is R0=e_out e_in/D. (13) It is therefore the lambda in the reduced continuant quartic D(lambda^4+1)-4B_bB_c(lambda^3+lambda) +(4B_b^2+4B_c^2-2D)lambda^2=0. (14) The polynomial gauge changes no full principal determinant: with u=(1/2)sin(2pi mu), J=exp(2pi i mu), the retained determinant is u^8 D^3 Pquartic(z(-J)^epsilon), (15) where Pquartic is the left side of (14). This polynomial identity follows by similarity where D!=0 and hence extends as a polynomial; it does not license canceling u or D on their zero strata. The finite Fourier equation has the stationary relation z(-J)^epsilon lambda=1. With z=exp(-2pi i chi), equations(13)--(15) give precisely R0(-J)^epsilon=exp(2pi i chi)=M_aux^-2. (16) This is the marked meridian relation of the original threading word, including its half-twist shear and inverse eigenratio, rather than a new normalization of the trace curve. The magnetic and total momenta agree as well. For one original H Newton summand, let its two raw heads be X,Y with XY=T and internal root Z. Differentiating the two literal Newton products, at their stationary root, gives the exponentiated logarithmic forces p1=Z(X-1)/(X-Z), p2=JZ(Y-1)/(YZ-J). For example the first product contributes integral_0^kappa Log(X-exp(2pi i t))dt; exponentiating 2pi i times its logarithmic X derivative gives p1. The second product and its literal Y^k factor give p2. The retained white monomial q^(d i) contributes the additional minus sign in the fixed-total first-head momentum. Thus -p1/p2=(1-X)(TZ-XJ)/[J(X-Z)(T-X)], (16a) which is exactly the old magnetic Y(X,Z), with no Hermitian reversal. For the full circle, the original residual sine product contributes -(T-J)/(TJ-1) to the total-degree force; the monomial q^[d(R+S-sigma)] T^-a contributes -J^-1. Consequently e^(Theta_tau)=J^-1 (T-J)/(TJ-1) p2(U,Z)p2(V,W) =JZW(T-J)(T-U)(T-V)/[(TJ-1)(TZ-UJ)(TW-VJ)]. (16b) Here each p2 uses its own second head T/U or T/V. These are the literal normalization factors from the source circle formula, not functions adjusted to fit the character equation. Equations(13), (16a),(16b) recover all three derivatives used by the original ordered-character theorem. Its typed incoming/output construction therefore preserves the entire ordered product P=BA and transports the two punctures by the same centralizer. The integer logarithmic marks are still required before turning these exponential equations into additive stationary equations. ## 5. Branch calibration and what has not been eliminated For positive regular face radii and mu=1/2-delta with small delta>0, the actual positive continuants select e_out=E_c(delta), e_in=E_b(delta), as in the fixed-real fold theorem. Equation(13) then selects the positive product branch. Put C=pi[sqrt(bA+xy)+sqrt(cA+xy)]/A. At delta=0, R0=1, J=-1, and (1/2) dR0/dJ=C/(2pi i). The derivative follows from dJ/ddelta=2pi i and d Log R0/ddelta=2C. In the original ordered map this is exactly the additive parabolic conjugator coefficient: the matrix transport is `I+[C/(2pi i)](P+I)`, not the identity merely because R0=1. With the retained half twist, its primitive cusp ratio is tau=1/[C/(2pi i)-epsilon/2]=2pi i/(C-pi i epsilon), agreeing with the independently marked rectangle calculation. Equations(10)--(16) hold first on the stated regular character chart. Their cleared polynomial relations have zero-face limits, but taking such limits can lose flag or branch information. The original source and the large-H adapters, rather than an arbitrary quartic root, specify those limits. In particular no new geometric branch is inferred merely from the quartic at u=0. In a prospective coefficient saddle, a face shift n->n-nu has multiplier L^nu, with L_f=exp(-partial_(n_f/N) action). The actual shared-face incidence in (8) is therefore retained. The Cauchy stationary equations for the original coefficient use its literal target n*, not independent triangle radii. Under the primitive face/head change of variables they are the original magnetic conservation/gluing equations wherever the full local character chart is regular. This last comparison is a stationary-equation identification, not a theorem that a solution is selected by the finite period. At the two marked zero faces one must retain the actual boundary limit and co-source. The equations do not eliminate the neighboring coefficient indices, prove a scalar A-polynomial for an arbitrary network, or identify every component of their characteristic variety with a geometric component. Nor do they prove a fixed complex external-color packet, its nonzero saddle coefficient, or the needed bounds for the nonempty small-color subsets. Their exact finite source solution, primitive normalization and local ordered-character interface are what is established here. Focused [exact source audit](../experiments/audit_actual_whole_source_coupled_face_difference_system.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_whole_source_coupled_face_difference_system_results.json): It constructs 50 literal homogenized Newton polynomials and checks 300 canceled source components, 360 polynomial recurrence rows, 15 exact core Fourier pairings, 192 coupled rows with 27,254 shared-face coefficient equalities, and 12 marked tetrahedral-graph coefficient extractions. Seven symbolic certificates check the polynomial gauge and original ordered magnetic/total/channel character maps. The independently developed fold block uses 336 original Newton values, 48 source jumps, 2,208 system rows and 48 full finite-system rank checks through N=18 and both parities. The rank counts concern the explicitly localized operator field; finite fixtures do not assert a geometric certificate or an asymptotic theorem. The incoming-b/output-c convention and magnetic, total and channel characters are part of the regular-chart identity. It does not reconstruct a marked zero-face representation. The geometric-boundary and period qualifications in Section 5 remain part of the finite difference-system result.

title: Polynomial actual boundary Gram costs on the entire supported color domain
text: # Polynomial actual boundary Gram costs on the entire supported color domain 29 October 2026. The correlated six-head marked boundary Gram has POLYNOMIAL source cost on EVERY supported folded color cell, at both level parities. No fixed central corridor is required. The second-root- zero Racah terms do not need a uniform strict exponential gap: a global elementary sine-product inequality bounds every such term by the same action as a positive main term. All low/high partner branches, the original marked normal and every lower moment are retained. This controls the pointed algebraic Gram from the [actual six-pants boundary](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_six_pants_boundary_torsor_and_sewing.md). It does not identify its constructed reflection with a physical mirror, bound the physical change of frame or general recouplings, or prove a graph's sharp geometric energy/noncancellation. ## 1. The whole-support theorem Let N>=2, d=N-1, M=floor(d/2), q=exp(pi i/N), and take ANY 0<=l_1,l_2,l_3<=M, l_1+l_2+l_3>=d. (1) There is one paired axis for each 2l_i<d; let their number be r<=3. The actual regular source cell, complete-circle coordinates eta_i, original marked co-source lambda and nested-cup vector v_l are those of the proved boundary theorem. In particular m_I=lambda(eta_I v_l), tau_l=m_all=Z_N(l)/N^(3-r)>0, q_l(eta)=sum_I (m_(I^c)/tau_l)eta_I, q_l(0)=1, K_l=sum_I |coeff_I(q_l^(1/2))|^2. (2) There are absolute constants C,C0, independent of N and of ALL labels satisfying (1), such that max_I |m_I/tau_l|<=C0 N^C, 1<=K_l<=C0 N^C. (3) The exponent may be increased between the two estimates. Thus the actual source and dual costs of this prescribed Gram are exactly K_l and tau_l^2 K_l, with log K_l=O(log N)=o(N) uniformly on the whole support. The estimates include saturation faces, edges, corners, nearest paired neighbors and odd simple axes. Unsupported open source cells are not deleted. They lack the positive top moment in (2), so (3) is asserted precisely on (1). The theorem does not assert a polynomial norm for the embedding of this finite coordinate cell into the physical tensor product. ## 2. The original generic trace and all its normal factors The [proved generic source identity](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_generic_trivalent_racah_source_identity.md) and the genuine ordered physical trace give, for each unfolded ordinary triangle j=(a,b,c), the EXACT rational function T_j=(-1)^d product_i[2j_i+1] *[r_1]![r_2]![r_3]!/[J+1]! *product_i([j_i]!^2[d-j_i]!/[N+j_i]!) S_j^2, J=a+b+c, r_i=J-2j_i, S_j=sum_t (-1)^(d+t)[N+t]! /{[d+t-J]! product_i[t-j_i]![J-j_i-t]!}, max(j_i,J-d)<=t<=J-max(j_i). (4) Here [n] and [n]! are symmetric quantum integers and factorials at zeta=q(1-Z)^(1/(2N)), with the branch through q. These are the actual source functions, not a separately normalized 6j model. The unfolded choices are j_i=l_i or d-l_i on a paired axis, and the single l_i on a simple axis. With the original paired-circle unit ell_j(Z)=L_N(c_j(zeta))/Z, the physical moment formula is m_I=(-1)^d(q-q^(-1)) [Z^(r+1-|I|)] sum_unfolded Z^r T_j product_(i in I)ell_(j_i)(Z). (5) There are at most eight summands and the coefficient order is <=4. The original marked physical trace is exactly the one in (5). No ordinary quantum dimension is specialized to zero before this coefficient is extracted. Two elementary integer facts now hold on the ENTIRE supported domain. For every unfolded branch, d<=J<=2d, 0<=r_i<=d. (6) To verify them, increase a coordinate from l_i to d-l_i. The maximum J is 3d-sum l_i<=2d and the minimum is sum l_i>=d. For r_i, its maximum over the flips is 2d-sum l_i<=d and its minimum is sum l_i-2l_i>=d-2l_i>=0. In particular every unfolded branch is an ordinary triangle. Moreover EVERY one of the seven denominator factorial indices in S_j is less than N, for every true term. Indeed 0<=d+t-J<=d-max j_i<=d, 0<=t-j_i<=some other label<=d, 0<=J-j_i-t<=some other label<=d. (7) For example t<=j_i+j_k bounds t-j_i, and t>=j_k bounds J-j_i-t. No root denominator appears in any Racah summand. Its numerator contains [N] once for t<N and both [N],[2N] for t>=N; t<=2d<2N excludes a third zero. This is the only termwise change at the second band. ## 3. A uniform global profile, including the second-zero band Let L(t)=integral_0^t log|2sin(pi u)|du, extended periodically to R. Its period is 1 and L(-t)=-L(t). Define the EXACT half-step scaled colors a_i=(j_i+1/2)/N, S=sum a_i, x_i=S/2-a_i (i=1,2,3), x_4=1-S/2. Equations (6) imply 0<x_i<1/2 for all four i, sum_i x_i=1. (8) The half-step is useful: a high-partner replacement j_i->d-j_i is exactly a_i->1-a_i. It permutes the four x coordinates while replacing each by its complement 1/2-x. There is no O(1/N) error in this assertion. For instance flipping the first color sends (x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4) ->(1/2-x_4,1/2-x_3,1/2-x_2,1/2-x_1). (9) For a summand put s=(t+3/4)/N and v=s-S/2=(t-J/2)/N. Its three child pairs obey x_i+v=(t-j_i+1/4)/N>0, x_i-v=(J-j_i-t+1/4)/N>0, i<=3. (10) Also x_4+v=1-(J-t+3/4)/N is in (0,1). The fourth minus argument is x_4-v=1-s=(N-t-3/4)/N: it is positive for t<N and negative for t>=N, precisely the second-zero band. After removing its one or two root zeros, the absolute factorial summand has, up to polynomial factors, the profile H_x(v)=-sum_(i=1)^4 [L(x_i+v)+L(x_i-v)]. (11) For t<N the numerator is s_t; for t>=N it is s_(t-N), apart from the complete root-orbit polynomial factors. Both have rate N L(s) up to O(log N), because L has period 1. The denominator d+t-J has rate L(1+s-S)=-L(S-s). Substitution of (10) then gives (11). This same argument covers endpoints: changing an argument by O(1/N) changes N L by O(log N), uniformly even at a zero of sine. One may prove this modulus of continuity by integrating |log u| over an interval of length O(1/N) near the nearest integer. The decisive inequality is H_x(v)<=H_x(0)=Phi(x):=-2sum_i L(x_i) (12) for EVERY actual term, including the second-zero band. Here is a direct elementary proof. The function is even in v, and (10) gives |v|<min(x_1,x_2,x_3). For v>0 away from its logarithmic corner, put alpha_i=pi x_i and theta=pi v. Then H_x'(v)=log |P_minus/P_plus|, P_plus=product_i sin(alpha_i+theta)>0, P_minus=product_i sin(alpha_i-theta). (13) If theta<alpha_4, every factor is positive and sin(alpha_i+theta)-sin(alpha_i-theta) =2cos(alpha_i)sin(theta)>0. Thus |P_minus|<P_plus. If theta>alpha_4, exactly the fourth minus factor is negative. Expand the sum of the two products: P_plus+P_minus =2 sum_(A subset {1,2,3,4}, |A| even) cos(theta)^(4-|A|)sin(theta)^|A| product_(i in A)cos(alpha_i) product_(i notin A)sin(alpha_i)>0. (14) Every factor is nonnegative, and an interior term is strictly positive by (8). Since P_minus<0, (14) again says |P_minus|<P_plus. Continuity across theta=alpha_4, where (13) tends to minus infinity, proves (12). Evenness treats negative v. No local concavity or uniform strict exponential tail gap was used. The integer nearest t=J/2 is a true term of the FIRST band: (6) gives max(j_i,J-d)<=floor(J/2) and ceil(J/2)<=min(J-max j_i,d). At that term |v|<=1/(2N), so the same uniform modulus of continuity gives H_x(v)=Phi(x)+O(log N/N). ## 4. Positive main value and polynomial normal envelopes For t<N, the exact root identity is ([N+t]!/[N])|_q=(-1)^t[d]![t]!. All denominators in (4) are positive symmetric factorials at q. Thus S_main/[N] has ONE common phase (-1)^d. Its positive absolute sum is Rcore_N(j)=N sum_(true t<N) s_t/{s_(d+t-J) product_i s_(t-j_i)s_(J-j_i-t)}. It has at most N terms and contains the midpoint term identified above. The uniform two-sided sine-factorial estimate and (12) therefore give, throughout the whole support and every branch, N^(-C)e^(N Phi(x))<=Rcore_N(j) <=N^C e^(N Phi(x)). (15) The estimate uses only ONE midpoint summand for its lower bound; no bulk Hessian, saddle width or distance from a saturation face is assumed. Second-band terms, after removing [N][2N], obey the same upper bound by (12). They may approach the leading action at boundary scales, which is why a uniform strict gap is unnecessary. Use the common disk |Z|<=c/N^2. A quantum-factorial ratio with a fixed number of factors and indices <=3N has, after explicitly removing its zeros, a polynomial envelope relative to its nonzero root product on this disk. This follows either from the proved [bounded normal factorial estimate](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/bounded_normal_quantum_factorial_envelope.md) or directly: a nonzero 1-q^(2k) has magnitude >=c0/N; its change is O(|Z|), and O(N) such factors accumulate only bounded relative growth here. Removed [N] and [2N] factors and the symmetric-int normalization cost fixed powers of N. Their count is uniformly bounded. Equations (7),(12),(15) hence bound the ENTIRE holomorphic S_j/Z by poly(N)e^(N Phi(x)). Cauchy estimates for four fixed normal orders add only another fixed power of N. No alternating-sum cancellation is needed for the second-zero terms. To include the complete prefactor of (4), note first that ([N] [j]!^2[d-j]!/[N+j]!)|_q=(-1)^j. (16) Its zero-removed envelope is polynomial, with no factorial action. All three r_i are <N, while N<=J+1<2N. The zero-removed triangle factor therefore has rate P(x)=sum_(i=1)^3 L(2x_i)-L(S-1), up to O(log N). Each simple axis contributes one dimension zero [2j+1]=[N]; the other dimensions and all ell_j in (5) have polynomial fixed jets, uniformly to the nearest paired neighbor. If s0=3-r is the number of simple axes, the prefactor without S^2 has zero order s0-4. Multiplication by Z^r and S^2, whose order is at least two, leaves order at least ONE. Consequently Z^r T_j product ell is holomorphic on the common disk; it is never estimated as a bare singular expression. The preceding bounds give for its fixed jets |[Z^k]{Z^r T_j product ell}|<=N^C exp(N E(x)), k<=4, E(x)=P(x)+2Phi(x) =sum_(i=1)^4[L(2x_i)-4L(x_i)] =-2sum_(i=1)^4[L(x_i)+L(1/2-x_i)]. (17) The second equality uses L(S-1)=-L(2x_4), and the third is the elementary duplication identity for L. This expression is unchanged by every permutation or individual complement x_i->1/2-x_i. Equation (9) therefore makes E EXACTLY the same function for all unfolded branches of a fixed folded triple, with these half-step coordinates. Finally the PROVED actual positive top moment has the exact weight Z_N(l)=N^2 product_i k_(l_i) s_(J_l-2l_1)s_(J_l-2l_2)s_(J_l-2l_3) /s_(J_l-d) *R_N(l)^2. The same midpoint argument (15), uniform factorial bounds and its positive prefactor give N^(-C)exp(N E_fold)<=tau_l<=N^C exp(N E_fold) (18) on the ENTIRE supported domain. Endpoint factors s_0=1 cause no problem, and replacing their scaled arguments by the half-step ones changes logarithms by only O(log N). Combine (5),(17),(18), sum at most eight branches, and absorb the polynomial |q-q^-1|: this proves the first estimate in (3). The finite square root of q_l=1+n_l is sum_(k=0)^r binom(1/2,k)n_l^k, with n_l^(r+1)=0. It is a polynomial of degree <=3 in at most seven normalized moments. Thus the first estimate implies the second, with constants independent of the labels and N. Its constant coefficient is one, so K_l>=1. This completes the whole-support actual Gram theorem. ## 5. Scope and verification The new ingredient beyond the central-corridor bound is the global sine-product inequality (12)--(14), together with the half-step folding coordinates. A second-zero action gap may vanish at boundary scales; uniform positive factorial comparison replaces it. The result controls the correlated marked Gram on its actual regular source cells. It supplies neither a physical mirror interpretation of that Gram nor a bound for genuine transitions between different pair decompositions. Those remain separate global source/geometry tasks; polynomial K alone has no hidden cuboctahedral volume term. The [multiprecision source diagnostic](../experiments/diagnose_actual_whole_support_boundary_conditioning.py) uses the proved generic trace (4), every partner and the original physical circle normal. It compares two precisions and two normal steps on saturation faces/corners and interior examples. These are diagnostics; the uniform theorem follows from the finite generic source identity, (12), common-disk factorial envelopes and the positive midpoint bound, not sampling. The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_whole_support_boundary_gram_envelope.py) and [recorded results](../experiments/actual_whole_support_boundary_gram_envelope_results.json) verify the universal even-product polynomial with an identically zero cleared numerator; 46,495 unfolded integer branches and 257,107 true Racah terms at N=2,...,32; 215 independent generic physical-double-sum versus Racah traces; and five all-moment original marked crosschecks. Floating-point action comparisons in that audit are labeled diagnostics; the proof of (12) is the exact sign argument (13),(14). The separate [paired-precision data](../experiments/actual_whole_support_boundary_conditioning_diagnostic_results.json) include ten boundary/interior cases through N=256, both parities, simple axes and saturation corners. The largest displayed K is below 2.78; this finite observation is not used to choose the polynomial exponent or prove its uniformity. The whole-support boundary envelope is not a global source-volume theorem.

title: An elementary balance certificate for one zero middle
status: Exact 9/4 curvature certificate for source balance
text: # An elementary balance certificate for one zero middle source-normalized lemma, 31 October 2026. This is a local analytic test on actual complete curvatures.
