It does not by itself construct a family of diagrams or assert that the test holds for one. Let a port have middle curvatures $0$ and $e>0$, outer curvatures $x,y\geq0$, and $A=x+y>0$. Retain the original complete triangle potential $Q$ from the [calibrated source](../papers/casimir-source-asymptotics/README.md). If $$ \frac eA\leq\frac94,\tag{1} $$ then its strict complete-radius balance gap satisfies $$ Q_e(0)+Q_0(0)-\log e>\frac1{2500}.\tag{2} $$ Here $Q_e(0)=Q(x,e,y)$ and $Q_0(0)=Q(x,0,y)$. Either outer curvature may vanish. If $e=0$ as well, both one-sided sectors vanish exactly and no positive-middle balance inequality is required. ## 1. The worst outer split has one zero outer curvature For fixed $A$ and $P=xy$, the zero-spectral lower-tail Perron factor is $$ \Lambda_P(t)=2\sin(\pi t) \left[A\sin(\pi t)+\sqrt{A^2\sin^2(\pi t)+4P\cos^2(\pi t)}\right]. $$ It increases with $P$ for every $t\in(0,1/2)$. The original weighted start action is $$ F_b(\mu;P)=\mu\log b+\int_0^\mu\log[4\cos^2(\pi t)]\,dt +\int_\mu^{1/2}\log\Lambda_P(t)\,dt. $$ Its maximum over $\mu$ is exactly $Q(x,b,y)$; for $b=0$ the sole start is $\mu=0$. Each $Q$ is therefore nondecreasing in $P$ at fixed $A,b$, by taking the maximum after the pointwise comparison of these actual actions. This is a local comparison, not a shared minimax exchange. Consequently $$ Q(x,e,y)+Q(x,0,y)\geq Q(A,e,0)+Q(A,0,0). $$ The exact half-degree homogeneity and monomial normalization give $$ \begin{aligned} Q(A,e,0)+Q(A,0,0)-\log e&=F(r)-\log r,\\ r&=e/A,\qquad F(r)=Q(1,r,0),\qquad Q(A,0,0)=\tfrac12\log A. \end{aligned}\tag{3} $$ No additive source constant has been removed. ## 2. Exact one-variable formula and monotonicity At outer weights $1,0$, the actual saddle is $$ \mu(r)=\frac1\pi\arctan\sqrt r,\qquad \frac{dF}{d\log r}=\mu(r),\qquad F(0)=Q(1,0,0)=0. $$ Define $T(z)=\int_0^z\arctan(t)\,dt/t$. Then $$ F(r)=\frac2\pi T(\sqrt r).\tag{4} $$ The derivative of $F(r)-\log r$ with respect to $\log r$ is $\mu(r)-1<0$, so it suffices to bound its value at $r=9/4$. Direct differentiation using $\arctan z+\arctan(1/z)=\pi/2$ for $z>0$ proves $$ T(z)-T(1/z)=\frac\pi2\log z. $$ At $z=3/2$, (4) therefore yields $$ F(9/4)-\log(9/4)=\frac2\pi T(2/3)-\log(3/2).\tag{5} $$ ## 3. A rational lower bound without numerical quadrature Integrating the alternating power series of $\arctan$ gives $$ T(t)=\sum_{j\geq0}\frac{(-1)^jt^{2j+1}}{(2j+1)^2},\qquad0<t<1. $$ Four terms, ending with the negative term $j=3$, give a strict lower bound at $t=2/3$. The inequality $\pi<22/7$ follows, for example, from the positive integral $$ \frac{22}7-\pi=\int_0^1\frac{x^4(1-x)^4}{1+x^2}\,dx>0. $$ Hence $$ \frac2\pi T(2/3)> \frac7{11}\sum_{j=0}^3\frac{(-1)^j(2/3)^{2j+1}}{(2j+1)^2} =\frac{155342}{382725}.\tag{6} $$ For the logarithm, use $\log(3/2)=2\operatorname{artanh}(1/5)$. Its positive series and a geometric tail bound give $$ \log(3/2)<2\sum_{j=0}^2\frac{(1/5)^{2j+1}}{2j+1} +\frac{2(1/5)^7}{7(1-1/25)} =\frac{177391}{437500}.\tag{7} $$ Subtracting (7) from (6), $$ F(9/4)-\log(9/4)> \frac{57269}{136687500}>\frac1{2500}.\tag{8} $$ Equations (1), (3), (5), and (8) prove (2), including the exact one-zero-outer limit. The estimate does not depend on normalization scale, because the balance gap is scale invariant. ## 4. Interface with an actual symmetric plat construction Suppose an actual certified source has only the following port types in its one complete marked packing: - Equal middle curvatures $b=c$, with $A>0$. - One zero middle and the other $e$ satisfying $e/(x+y)\leq9/4$. Every such port is balanced. For equal positive middles, this follows from $Q_b(0)>\tfrac12\log b$; if both are zero, the one-sided sectors vanish. For the second type, it follows from (2). The [conditional full-invariant balance theorem](../papers/planar-certificates/README.md) therefore applies to any literal source for which these actual geometric statements have been proved. The [reduced-layer family theorem](general_reduced_layer_long_filling_volume.md) establishes the required packing, reflection, original mark and uniform ratio bound for its literal words at every $k\geq4$. Those are separate geometric conclusions, not consequences of the local inequality alone. ## Validation and scope The bound follows from scalar comparison, monotonicity, exact rational inequalities and protected-zero limits. Numerical quadrature or a sample of diagrams cannot establish its uniformity.

title: The actual period from an all-level A-operator and finite pointing
text: # The actual period from an all-level A-operator and finite pointing Research note, 25 October 2026. Starting from any specified nonzero all-level annihilator of the actual reduced ADO state, the Kashaev value is recovered from that operator and finitely many fixed small colors, without a rank-one or regular-orbit assumption. Singular steps require a uniformly bounded quantum-parameter jet. Those initial jets are bounded because the colors are fixed. This gives an exact operator period; its volume growth remains unproved. The definitions and independently checked normalization are those of [the ADO note](kashaev_ado_pointing.md). In particular F_N(-q_N^j)=C_j(q_N), 1<=j<=N, F_N(1)=<K>_N, q_N=exp(pi*i/N), (0.1) where C_j(q) is the fixed finite-dimensional reduced period, with unknot normalization one. It is Laurent polynomial in the recorded quantum parameter, analytic at q=1, and C_j(1)=1. Only finitely many fixed colors will be input. No large-color Jones estimate or unverified holonomicity theorem is used. ## 1. Cross-level rigidity gives the generic trace recurrence Fix a specified nonzero all-level reduced ADO annihilator P=sum_(i=0)^d a_i(q,M)T^i, TM=qMT, d>=1, (1.1) with rational coefficients, annihilating F_N for all but finitely many N. Clear denominators once so that a_i are Laurent polynomials. This changes no state or peripheral normalization. A possible order-zero annihilator of this nonzero state is necessarily zero. For any fixed positive integer j form the Laurent polynomial H_j(q)=sum_(i=0)^d a_i(q,-q^j) C_(j+i)(q). (1.2) At every sufficiently large N with N>=j+d, (0.1) and the actual ADO equation give H_j(q_N)=0. Infinitely many distinct q_N occur. A nonzero Laurent polynomial has only finitely many nonzero roots, so sum_(i=0)^d a_i(q,-q^j) C_(j+i)(q)=0 (1.3) identically in q, for every j>=1. This is an elementary Zariski rigidity argument. It requires neither an equality of annihilator ideals nor an identification of the root central curve with A_K. The inclusion of the ADO recursion ideal in a suitably normalized colored-Jones recursion ideal is already stated in [Brown--Dimofte--Garoufalidis--Geer, 2005.08176](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.08176). Its proof is not a premise: (1.2)--(1.3) follow directly from the quotient-color identity already independently proved here. Reduced meridian convention M=-q^j includes the needed sign and shift; it must not be replaced silently by a different paper's x-variable. ## 2. A fixed initial window avoids identically singular steps Write the support of the leading coefficient as a_d(q,M)=sum_(a,b) c_(a,b) q^a M^b. Let A be its q-exponent span, D its M-exponent span, and s its number of monomials after collecting terms. Choose j_0=A+1. (2.1) For j>=j_0 the substituted Laurent polynomial a_d(q,-q^j) is nonzero identically. In fact its exponents are a+bj. A collision between distinct b's would imply |j|=|a-a'|/|b-b'|<=A, and terms with the same b do not collide. Thus (1.3) propagates the fixed initial vector c_0(q)=(C_(j_0)(q),...,C_(j_0+d-1)(q))^t (2.2) as rational functions in q to every later color. Let B_j(q) be the companion matrix, now evaluated at M=-q^j with q variable. For N>=j_0+d put r_N(q)=e_d^t B_(N-d)(q)...B_(j_0)(q). Then the exact period formula is <K>_N=[r_N(q)c_0(q)]_(q=q_N). (2.3) The right side is the value of the whole regular germ. Its product equals the Laurent polynomial C_N(q) identically, so all apparent poles cancel before evaluation. The operator and the fixed initial periods specify this value uniquely. There is no free levelwise central multiplier and no choice of a favorable root solution. The use of small colors here is finite pointing of the A-module. Equation (2.3) does not substitute a large-color Jones asymptotic for the requested A-operator analysis. ## 3. A uniform bound on the required q-jets For all sufficiently large N, a_d(q_N,M) is a nonzero Laurent polynomial of M-span at most D. The points -q_N^j appearing in the product are distinct. Therefore at most D steps satisfy a_d(q_N,-q_N^j)=0. Each such step has q-multiplicity at most s-1. To see this, any nonzero Laurent polynomial with t<=s monomials has the form h(q)=sum_(r=1)^t c_r q^e_r, e_r distinct. If h and its first t-1 logarithmic derivatives vanished at a nonzero q_0, then sum_r e_r^k c_r q_0^e_r=0, k=0,...,t-1. The Vandermonde determinant in the distinct integers e_r is nonzero in characteristic zero. All c_r would be zero, a contradiction. Ordinary and logarithmic vanishing multiplicities coincide at q_0!=0. Consequently the total pole budget of the companion product obeys B_N=sum_(j=j_0)^(N-d) ord_(q=q_N) a_d(q,-q^j) <=D(s-1). (3.1) This counts tangencies of the moving curve M=-q^j as well as ordinary root-orbit zeros. The simpler meridian bound D from [the preceding note](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/bounded_meridian_jets.md) cannot just be reused for q-jets, because M moves with q. Use t=q/q_N-1 and expand r_N(q_N(1+t))=sum_(k=-B_N)^infinity R_(N,k)t^k, J_k(N)=[t^k]c_0(q_N(1+t)). The whole-germ formula becomes <K>_N=sum_(k=0)^B_N R_(N,-k) J_k(N). (3.2) For every fixed k<=D(s-1), J_k(N) is bounded as N tends to infinity: its entries are q_N^k C_j^(k)(q_N)/k! for a fixed finite set of colors, and these functions are analytic near q=1. Thus initial pointing introduces no unknown exponential level normalization. Every growing part of (3.2) is in the specified operator's long companion product and its bounded-order germ. As in the meridian calculation, regular numerator matrices and the full denominator product compute (3.2) using a fixed truncation. No division by a zero coefficient at q_N is performed. ## 4. Why levelwise Hilbert 90 alone would miss this coherence There are fixed operators with extra root-level solutions that cannot be the coherent knot family. For example take Q=(1+q^2 M^2)T^2-(1+q^2)T+q^2(1-M^2) =(T-q^2)[(1+M^2)T-(1-M^2)]. (4.1) For even N put f_N(M)=product_(r=N/2)^(N-1)(1-q_N^(2r) M^2). Telescoping gives (1+M^2)f_N(q_N M)=(1-M^2)f_N(M), so Q annihilates both 1 and f_N. Moreover f_N(-q_N^j)=0 for 1<=j<=N/2, |f_N(1)|=sqrt(2N). (4.2) For the modulus, pair the conjugate factors in product_(r=1)^(N-1)(1-exp(2pi*i*r/N))=N and retain the middle factor 2. This gives the stated square root exactly. Hence h_N=1+a^N f_N, a>1, has value one at every fixed small color for all sufficiently large even N, yet its target has logarithmic rate log(a). Take h_N=1 at odd levels. The same fixed Q annihilates the whole manufactured root family. This family cannot satisfy (0.1) with fixed Laurent polynomials C_j at every permitted level. For fixed j its values are one at infinitely many levels, so polynomial rigidity forces C_j=1 identically. But at a single even level, j=N/2+1 has a nonzero f_N value and contradicts that identity. Equivalently the generic recurrence with initial C_1=C_2=1 forces C_j=1 for all j, since 1+q^(2j+2) is never identically zero. Thus the cross-level condition used in Sections 1--3 is essential. The example is not a counterexample to any knot invariant or to the volume conjecture. It distinguishes an arbitrary norm-torsor section at each root from the actual coherent pointed period. ## 5. Peripheral factors and the exact scope of the theorem If the specified literature operator is in full ADO normalization, first transport it by the fixed rational gauge already checked in [the pointing note](kashaev_ado_pointing.md). Retain the actual whole factor d_N in comparing states. Its exact evaluation is N_N(1)=eta_N <K>_N/N; its reference residue and target jet are those in [the preceding note](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/bounded_meridian_jets.md#5-the-full-ado-normalization-keeps-its-residue-and-first-jet). No generic factor such as 1+M^N is being replaced by one. The theorem has these inputs: a specified actual nonzero all-level annihilator, and the independently established fixed-color identities. It has no root rank, semisimplicity, primeness, regular-orbit, or alternatingness assumption. It removes the extra rank/regularity conditions of the earlier exact cofactor and value-propagation formulas. The subsequent [finite cut-state proof](finite_sum_annihilator.md) now independently supplies a nonzero actual all-level meridian annihilator for every knot, so this theorem's existence input is available. It does not prove the classical-symbol identification with the geometric A-curve. Most importantly it does not estimate the logarithmic growth of the actual matrix-period expression (3.2). Comparison with the marked regulator period remains the volume theorem. Bounded jet order and bounded initial jets alone do not rule out cancellation in a long matrix product or prove its geometric norm. The [exact diagnostics](../experiments/audit_all_level_a_period.py) test moving-q germs against known polynomial solutions, including singular steps of higher multiplicity and even/composite levels. They also check the coherence obstruction (4.1)--(4.2) algebraically. The [results](../experiments/all_level_a_period_results.json) are diagnostics, not evidence that an unaudited knot operator has the required symbol or volume growth. No novelty claim is made for the standard recurrence or sparse-polynomial arguments. The subsequent [affine source construction](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/affine_quantum_a_period.md) retains a specified inhomogeneous source as an extension class, with a cyclic resolvent when its homogeneous block is nonresonant. The [adequacy argument](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/adequacy_and_algebraic_periods.md) proves that fixed algebraic meridian sections cannot reproduce the actual adequate color periods. It supplies nonsplitting tests for this extension, without inferring the missing volume norm. The [cyclotomic Mellin uniqueness theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/mellin_cyclotomic_jet_uniqueness.md) extends the same bounded-jet argument to the whole rational root generating function. The actual source window through orders zero to D(s-1), together with the exact cyclotomic numerator lattice, determines every competing section and its Kashaev residue. This does not impose a rank or semisimplicity condition, and does not estimate that residue's growth.

title: Which custom definitions can agree with the literature construction?
text: # Which custom definitions can agree with the literature construction? Research note, 25 October 2026. The earlier custom candidates are preserved in `quantum_a_volume.md`. They have different answers to the equivalence question. The exact comparison below keeps q and the peripheral variable Q generic. **Subsequent target clarification.** Kashaev's original invariant is the target; the AK/Faddeev constructions discussed below are comparison objects. The [crossing proof](kashaev_crossing_and_period_lattice.md) and [ADO pointing proof](kashaev_ado_pointing.md) now fix the original enhanced state and its meridian normalization independently of published comparison proofs. The exact triangular Kashaev crossing has, with k=a-c and d=b+k, |A_(c,d;a,b)|=s_N(a)s_N(b+k) /(s_N(a-k)s_N(b)s_N(k)). Thus the positive sine factorials occur in the actual literature kernel. Its phase, pairing, and modified-dimension lattice are also specified in those notes. This is a direct local connection with the earlier positive candidate. Equality of the full positive sum and the complex Kashaev period has not been established. ## 0. Current comparison after reviewing the notes The custom constructions are not a single definition. Their status is: | Construction | Comparison with the specified literature object | Useful result | | --- | --- | --- | | Compact local product Psi_q | Exactly the numerator factor of Faddeev Phi; its modular-dual completion is exactly Phi | A local definition that can be retained with its full completion | | Positive sine-factorial sum | No exact generic-boundary state equivalence established | An independently proved volume rate and a positive comparison action | | Naive figure-eight cone-transfer recurrence | No rational two-component gauge, even after a finite power cover of the peripheral coordinate | A classical-action/volume model with a different quantum deformation | | Minimal annihilator of the fixed Faddeev state | Uses the literature annihilator convention; existence is proved independently in the b-shift algebra | A way to formulate the volume law for the same state and operator | | Inverse Fourier transform of the normalized charged tensor | Exactly recovers the preceding meridian state in ordinary charts and extends it to a moving longitude plane | A tensor-derived state and volume theorem for every globally branched complete positive geometric chart | For the last row, `general_annihilator_and_volume.md` supplies the existence and geometric-component arguments. The uniform twist geometry and the subsequent `twist_topology_and_peripherals.md` now supply the explicit twist-knot realizations and preferred peripheral certificates. The subsequent phase and tetrahedral-symmetry audits prove selected-state equivalence along certified proper positive paths, including the actual three-to-two-tetrahedron figure-eight move. A general connecting-path theorem remains an obligation. The further `six_three_and_two_bridge_audit.md` gives a complete independent geometric and peripheral certificate for the specified 6_3 literature state. The subsequent `singular_faces_and_six_two.md` evaluates singular face contractions of the original charged operators, rather than changing the tetrahedral function. It recovers an exact boundary fiber for 6_2 and proves its volume law and minimal-annihilator existence. Thus a direct reduction of the literature tensor is useful beyond the earlier invertible-face formulation. It does not establish equivalence of the positive factorial sum. The further boundary-state note proves the exact Gaussian change between a rationally sheared peripheral coordinate and the true meridian. This is an explicit equivalence for the stated tensor-derived states. It does not identify the earlier naive cone-transfer state or the positive factorial state with them. An operator by itself does not select the solution or its exponential normalization. The structural continuation in `pointed_steinberg_recoupling.md` now gives an algebraic role for finite q-factorial ratios: they are the kernel of a pointed cyclic-module factorization, with its generic normalization unit determined. The cyclic dilogarithm frames live on the explicit Heisenberg torsor of `heisenberg_period_torsor.md`. This supplies a uniform comparison target for the positive factorial candidate, retaining its phases. Equality of its full contracted period with that target remains unproved. The further `fourier_boundary_state.md` now removes the ordinary-fiber rank restriction. Its definition uses the existing charged tensor and real level, followed by a completely normalized inverse Fourier transform. The quadratic level term makes its coordinate the actual meridian. It agrees exactly with the preceding fiber/Gaussian state wherever that state is defined. Rational geometry and matrix certificates for a six-tetrahedron 5_2 realization verify the additional moving-plane case. This is a useful reformulation of the literature tensor; it is not an identification of either earlier positive state with it. Independence of arbitrary triangulations and equality with a canonical intrinsic knot state remain obligations. ## 1. The compact quantum product has an exact literature completion Our local function was Psi_q(x)=(x;q)_infinity=product_(k>=0)(1-q^k x), |q|<1. It satisfies Psi_q(qx)=Psi_q(x)/(1-x), and the formal pentagon in the earlier note. This function is directly related to the Faddeev function used in the literature state; it is one of its two compact product factors. More precisely, take Re b>0 and Im(b^2)>0, and put q=exp(2 pi i b^2), q_tilde=exp(-2 pi i b^(-2)), X=exp(2 pi b Z), X_tilde=exp(2 pi Z/b). Then both |q| and |q_tilde| are less than one, and the exact identity is Phi_b(Z) = Psi_q(-q^(1/2) X)/Psi_q_tilde(-q_tilde^(1/2) X_tilde). (1.1) This is equation (44) of Andersen–Kashaev, [arXiv:1109.6295v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1109.6295v2), with its compact product notation expanded and the square roots fixed by the displayed exponentials. The following argument checks the identity instead of assuming the source's proof. **Independent verification.** Let P_b(Z) be the product quotient on the right. The elementary shift equation for Psi gives P_b(Z-i b/2)=(1+exp(2 pi b Z)) P_b(Z+i b/2), P_b(Z-i/(2b))=(1+exp(2 pi Z/b)) P_b(Z+i/(2b)). The factors in the other product cancel in each equation. The same two equations were derived directly for Phi from its integral in Section 2.2 of `literature_state_volume.md`. Their continuation to the present complex-b domain follows by holomorphic dependence on b from a common initial strip. The quotient R(Z)=Phi_b(Z)/P_b(Z) is therefore meromorphic and has periods i b and i/b. They are linearly independent over the reals in the stated complex-b domain. Both Phi_b and P_b tend to 1 as Re Z tends to minus infinity on a fixed horizontal line in their initial strip. For Phi this follows by moving the defining w-contour a small positive distance; for P it follows from the absolutely convergent products. A meromorphic function with two independent periods and this left-end limit must be identically 1. To see this explicitly, the real translation flow on the compact period torus is recurrent. There are R_k tending to plus infinity whose classes tend to zero. At a regular point Z_0 of the initial strip, R(Z_0)=lim_k R(Z_0-R_k)=1. The meromorphic identity theorem extends the result to the plane. This fixes the normalization as well as the functional equations and proves (1.1). For real b>0, neither compact infinite product is defined by an absolutely convergent |q|<1 product. Their *completed quotient*, continued as the Faddeev integral, has a well-defined value. Dropping the dual factor at this boundary is not justified by (1.1). In particular, the compact pentagon by itself does not establish the required global unit-circle state-integral identities. **Usefulness.** The compact product was a useful local definition. Its precise connection to a standard literature building block is now explicit. To obtain the literature knot state one still needs its dual factor, Gaussian, measure, boundary variables, and integration cycle. Equation (1.1) does not identify our entire custom knot model with the standard one. ### 1.1 Exact local operator agreement does not determine the completion Write the numerator in (1.1) as N_b(Z) and the denominator as D_b(Z). The modular-dual variable is unchanged by Z->Z-i b, since exp(2pi(Z-i b)/b)=exp(2pi Z/b). Hence D_b(Z-i b)=D_b(Z), N_b(Z-i b)=(1+q^(-1/2)exp(2pi b Z))N_b(Z). The completed Phi_b=N_b/D_b satisfies exactly the same latter equation. Thus the custom compact factor and the literature tetrahedron function already agree at the level of this local quantum difference operator. This is an exact partial equivalence, stronger than a shared classical action. Their quotient is an i b-periodic function, generally nonrational in the peripheral exponential. The second, dual shift equation and the left-end normalization fix the completion in Section 1. The first operator alone does not. The period factor can depend on b and can affect a semiclassical limit on a prescribed ray. This is a concrete reason that a volume conjecture must specify the state and normalization together with its quantum A-operator. The formulas here initially hold in the convergent complex-b product domain of (1.1); the real-b state uses the completed continuation, not a bare divergent product on the unit circle. ## 2. The positive angle-factorial model retains magnitudes of q-factorials At q=exp(2 pi i/N), and 0<=k<N, the exact identity is (q;q)_k =(-i)^k exp(pi i k(k+1)/(2N)) s_N(k), s_N(k)=product_(j=1)^k 2 sin(pi j/N). (2.1) It follows term by term from 1-exp(2 pi i j/N)=-2 i exp(pi i j/N) sin(pi j/N). Consequently 1/s_N(k)=(-i)^k exp(pi i k(k+1)/(2N))/(q;q)_k. (2.2) The custom positive state can therefore be written with compact q-factorial weights and an explicit compensating quadratic phase. This gives a concrete starting point for a comparison with cyclic or root-of-unity quantum dilogarithms. It does not say that discarding or compensating those phases commutes with summation, elimination, or Pachner moves. Its proven Laplace volume limit remains useful. It supplies a positive comparison action whose maximum is the complete geometric volume. It does not yet control the interference and contour of the literature state. The specialized local ratio 8 is still only a comparison of bare amplitudes. Products of peripheral units can specialize to 8. To decide the correct move law one must lift the boundary variables, specify how they enter the state, compute the exact multiplier, and check compositions of moves. No particular generic multiplier is identified by the single numerical test. In particular the test proves neither equivalence nor an obstruction modulo permitted boundary factors. ### 2.1 The factor-eight test has a measure-scale asymptotic There is more information available without inventing a peripheral extension. For the same symmetric bipyramid, on the lattice progression 6|N, write L_N=s_N(N/3)^(-6), R_N=s_N(2N/3)^(-3) sum_(p=1)^(N/3-1) [s_N(p)s_N(N/3-p)]^(-3). Then L_N/R_N ~ N. (2.3) Thus the discrepancy has a natural scale associated with the extra summation variable. An explicit measure factor N would remove this leading discrepancy; it would not establish the exact finite-N identity, since L_6/R_6=8. Here is the calculation. Uniformly for x in compact subsets of (0,1) with Nx integral, Stirling and Euler–Maclaurin applied after extracting the factor 2 pi j/N at the origin give s_N(Nx)=sqrt(2N sin(pi x)) exp(-N Lambda(pi x)/pi)(1+O(1/N)). The two-tetrahedron expression therefore has leading form L_N ~ 3^(-3/2) N^(-3) exp(N V/pi), V=6 Lambda(pi/3). For the three-tetrahedron sum let x=p/N. Its classical volume is v(x)=3[Lambda(2pi/3)+Lambda(pi x)+Lambda(pi(1/3-x))]. Its unique maximum is at x=1/6, where v=V and v''=-6 sqrt(3) pi^2. At this point the product of the three tetrahedral prefactors is 3^(-3/4)N^(-9/2). Summing the Gaussian with spacing 1/N supplies 3^(-3/4)sqrt(N). The uniform logarithmic factorial bound in the earlier note controls the endpoints, which have a strict volume gap. Consequently R_N ~ 3^(-3/2) N^(-4) exp(N V/pi), proving (2.3). This identifies a missing leading measure scale, not a full boundary multiplier or a proof of equivalence. More generally a nonzero rational boundary factor regular near (q,M)=(1,1) has zero contribution to a semiclassical limit h log|Z|. A finite-order zero or pole also contributes zero when approached along a nonzero algebraic path, since h log h tends to zero. The exact specialized state can still be zero or undefined if the factors are canceled in the wrong order. Factors accumulated in a number growing like 1/h can change the exponential rate. Exact move invariance and invariance of the volume rate are separate statements. ### 2.2 How a generic boundary multiplier changes the operator Let A=sum_j a_j(q,Q)E^j annihilate Z and let Z'=U(q,Q)Z, where U is a nonzero rational peripheral factor and E Q=q Q E. Before any specialization, A'=U A U^(-1) =sum_j a_j(q,Q) U(q,Q)/U(q,q^j Q) E^j (2.4) annihilates Z'. Clearing denominators must be recorded, since it introduces explicit peripheral factors. This is the precise scalar gauge law; replacing U by its value at Q=1 before shifting would give the wrong equation. For example, for U=1+Q^n the coefficient multiplier is (1+Q^n)/(1+q^(jn)Q^n). Although U(q,1)=2, its generic shift ratios carry nonconstant information. A product of three such factors can specialize to 8. This illustrates the user's normalization point without claiming that these particular factors are the missing multiplier in the bare bipyramid calculation. For a fixed number of moves, a nonzero multiplier meromorphic of finite order in a semiclassical parameter h has h log|U|->0 along any path on which its leading nonzero term is c h^k. It preserves the volume rate on that path. This statement requires the nonzero leading term: an identically vanishing specialization cannot be assigned a logarithmic rate by it. Nor does it apply to an exponential normalization exp(C/h). Generic normalization, exact quantum equivalence and volume-rate equivalence therefore remain distinct questions. ## 3. The naive cone-transfer equation is a different rational q-system For the figure-eight knot put F(Q)=Q^4-Q^3-2Q^2-Q+1, t(Q)=F(Q)/Q^2, A_custom=E^2-t(Q)E+1, E Q=q Q E. This is the earlier left-ordered cone-transfer equation, expressed in Q=m^2 so that its commutation parameter agrees with the literature one. For the literature operator audited in Section 4 of `literature_state_volume.md`, divide by its leading coefficient and write A_lit=E^2-T(Q)E+d(Q), T(Q)=(q^2 Q^2-1) R(Q)/(q^2 Q^2(q Q^2-1)), R(Q)=q^4 Q^4-q^3 Q^3-q(q^2+1)Q^2-qQ+1, d(Q)=(q^3 Q^2-1)/(q Q^2-1). The earlier scalar-gauge invariant already distinguishes these operators. The following stronger statement also rules out a rational change of the two-component solution basis, in these fixed peripheral coordinates. **Proposition 3.1.** For generic q, the companion systems C_custom(Q)=[[t(Q),-1],[1,0]], C_lit(Q)=[[T(Q),-d(Q)],[1,0]] admit no invertible rational matrix D(Q) satisfying C_lit(Q) D(Q)=D(qQ) C_custom(Q). (3.1) This excludes equivalence over C(q,Q), including overall rational equation multipliers and rational scalar gauges. It does not address a change of polarization or a gauge with essential singularities. **Proof.** It suffices to work at a generic positive real q!=1: a matrix rational in q,Q could be specialized there, away from its finitely many bad parameters. The q-orbits of nonzero finite points are then infinite. First D has no finite nonzero poles. C_custom and its inverse are regular there. C_lit has poles only at alpha_+=q^(-1/2) and alpha_-=-q^(-1/2), and zeros of its determinant only at q^(-1)alpha_+ and q^(-1)alpha_-. Consider a q-orbit containing a pole of D. If beta is its lowest-index pole, evaluate (3.1) at beta/q. Its right side has a pole and D on its left side is regular. Hence C_lit must have a pole there: beta=q alpha_+ or beta=q alpha_-. Every pole of D on that orbit therefore has index at least 1 relative to alpha. At its highest-index pole C_lit is regular and invertible, so (3.1) forces another pole of D one step farther along the orbit, a contradiction. Orbits containing no alpha give an immediate contradiction at their lowest-index pole. Thus every entry of D is Laurent polynomial in Q. Taking determinants in (3.1), and using that a rational q-periodic function is constant, yields det D(Q)=c(q)(q Q^2-1), c(q)!=0. (3.2) Write the lower row of D as (a(Q),b(Q)). If v=(f(qQ),f(Q))^T is a custom solution vector, its image is (h(qQ),h(Q))^T with h(Q)=a(Q) f(qQ)+b(Q) f(Q). The upper row is forced by the second row of (3.1) to be (a(qQ)t(Q)+b(qQ), -a(qQ)). (3.3) It remains to bound the Laurent degrees of a,b. This can be done entirely formally at zero and infinity. For a scalar equation E^2 f-U(Q)E f+v(Q) f=0, the formal quotient r(Q)=f(qQ)/f(Q) obeys r(qQ)r(Q)-U(Q)r(Q)+v(Q)=0. Its two distinct slopes give the following unique formal branches. The leading constants follow by balancing this displayed equation; their formal series are obtained recursively because the slopes are distinct: | Location | Custom large branch | Literature large branch | Custom small branch | Literature small branch | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Q=infinity | q^(-2)Q^2 | q Q^2 | Q^(-2) | q^(-1)Q^(-2) | | Q=0 | q^2 Q^(-2) | Q^(-2) | Q^2 | q^2 Q^2 | For each branch set H_branch=a r_branch+b=h/f. It is nonzero: otherwise the invertible D would kill the corresponding entire solution vector via (3.3). Its leading integral Laurent power is fixed by r_lit/r_custom = H_branch(qQ)/H_branch(Q). At infinity the powers of H_large and H_small must therefore be 3 and -1; at zero their orders must be -2 and 2. Subtracting the two branch identities gives a=(H_large-H_small)/(r_large-r_small). Thus a has highest degree 1 at infinity and lowest order 0 at zero. From b=H_small-a r_small one gets highest degree at most -1 at infinity and lowest order at least 2 at zero. Since a,b are Laurent polynomials, a=A+BQ, b=0. Equations (3.2)–(3.3) now demand (A+BqQ)(A+BQ)=c(q)(qQ^2-1). The coefficient of Q is AB(1+q), so AB=0. But the right side has both a nonzero constant and a nonzero quadratic coefficient. This is impossible. QED. This result does not follow just from a different determinant: d(Q) is itself a q-coboundary. The pole argument and both endpoint degree constraints are needed. **Corollary 3.2 (finite power covers do not remove the obstruction).** The same non-equivalence holds over rational functions of q^(1/D) and Q^(1/D) for every fixed positive integer D. In particular it covers rational factors in the meridian eigenvalue m when Q=m^2, including (1+m^n). **Proof.** Write Q=M^D and let E act by M->q^(1/D)M. Specialize to a generic positive q!=1 and take its positive D-th root. The finite-pole propagation argument in Proposition 3.1 works separately on every lifted orbit, so a,b are Laurent polynomials in M. The formal endpoint constraints become degree_infinity a=D, order_zero a=0, degree_infinity b<=-D, order_zero b>=2D. Thus b=0 and a is a polynomial of degree D with nonzero constant term. The determinant identity becomes a(q^(1/D)M) a(M)=c(q)(q M^(2D)-1). (3.4) All roots on the right have modulus q^(-1/(2D)). If rho is a root of a, then rho and q^(-1/D)rho must both be roots on the right. They have different moduli, and rho cannot be zero. This is impossible. A rational gauge over the stated function field would specialize to a gauge at some such generic positive q, so none exists. QED. The exclusion is still for fixed peripheral coordinates (and their finite power covers). It does not exclude Fourier-type changes of polarization, nonrational gauges, or a different corrected quantization of the custom classical action. ### 3.1 What survives of the custom volume theorem Both systems have the same geometric classical characteristic equation after removing the explicitly recorded limiting prefactor. Their difference at generic q is a quantum correction. The positive transfer and dominant-root estimates in the earlier note remain valid for their specified states and may also apply to bounded perturbations of a literature transfer system when the contour selects its dominant solution. They do not, by themselves, identify that selected solution or its absolute exponential normalization. There is also an opposite exponential convention to track: the custom norm grows like exp(+V/h), while the literature Faddeev state here decays like exp(-V/(2 pi b^2)). This can be compatible with a change of semiclassical ray or polarization, but it is not an exact equality of states on the rays already specified. A transform proving such a relation would have to be written down with its measure and integration cycle. ## 4. Relation to the manuscript and next mathematical obligations The manuscript's Schläfli identity and Euclidean endpoint explain the custom cone-transfer normalization. Its warnings about measures, Jacobians and pole accumulation also explain why equality of a classical action is too weak to identify quantum states. The independent literature-state proof in `literature_state_volume.md` avoids the compact-fold limit by staying at a nondegenerate positive ideal saddle. It gives a useful broad analytic criterion using the same polyhedral volume functional. The original proof obligations now have the following status: 1. Uniform positive geometric and preferred peripheral certificates are supplied for both twist families in the two twist notes. Their extension to broader alternating families remains open. 2. A general annihilator-existence theorem for the same rescaled literature integrals is proved in `general_annihilator_and_volume.md`. Explicit useful minimal operators beyond 4_1, and stronger full-symbol equalities, remain separate algebraic work. 3. Global move identities with generic boundary factors, exact normalization and integration cycles remain to be audited before identifying arbitrary realizations as one knot state. `faddeev_pentagon_audit.md` now supplies the positive Faddeev charged pentagon, its exact phase, and its insertion into proper absolutely convergent full face contractions. It also gives the explicit constant equivalence J_coarea=J_printed/p_1^2 for the fiber-measure convention. The remaining work includes the precise meridian polarization and continuation between other move patterns. `peripheral_phase_and_state.md` subsequently reconstructs the exact charged-tensor phase and identifies the fiber integral with a specified published AK level. Its transform is injective, and move covariance reduces to an affine phase and possible meridian translation. This is an explicit equivalence for the fixed realizations; the coefficients and contours for general connecting sequences still require checks. `tetrahedral_symmetry_and_figure_eight.md` supplies one actual zero-slope certificate: the two published figure-eight realizations differ only by their explicit phase, and their selected minimal operators agree. This does not identify the different naive custom cone-transfer operator. The geometric-endpoint moment argument in the peripheral-phase note now forces zero slope along any certified proper positive path. It gives state equivalence up to the retained scalar within that component, rather than assuming arbitrary triangulations lie in one component. For 4_1, the state asymptotic and explicit minimal annihilator are treated in the companion note. For the certified geometric state-integral class, the analytic volume theorem and general annihilator-existence proof are now available. The two twist families also have uniform geometric and preferred peripheral certificates. Exact global move equivalence and the extension to all alternating knots remain unfinished; neither follows from the shared classical action of the custom and literature constructions.

title: What fixed algebraic rigidity can force for the actual selected period
text: # What fixed algebraic rigidity can force for the actual selected period 28 October 2026. Exact cyclotomic pointing already determines the actual quantum period. It does not automatically make its geometric coefficient nonzero. Two precise facts sharpen the torsor target: 1. The SAME original figure-eight family has exponential growth on its complete meridian arc and bounded values on every fixed-color meridian arc approaching the same complete classical point. A uniform dominant geometric comparison regular on the raw central fibre is therefore impossible. The divided normal source is essential, rather than an optional choice of coordinates. 2. The explicit whole-word Kummer period has a fixed number of variables, but growing cover genus and growing character homology. It has not yet supplied the fixed finite-rank algebraic object required by the existing whole-comparison rigidity theorem. These are proofs about the original anchored state and its actual cover. No rescaled invariant or adjustable levelwise source is used. ## 1. The source is already fixed; uniqueness is not the missing datum Use the actual family and conventions of [the all-level operator theorem](all_level_a_period.md) and [the normal-period theorem](peripheral_normal_period.md): q_N=exp(pi*i/N), Q_N=q_N^2, Y=M^2, F_N(1)=K_N, F_N(Q_N^j)=C_j(q_N), 1<=j<N. For each FIXED j, C_j(q) is the specified Laurent-polynomial ordinary-color period, C_j(1)=1. The exact all-level recurrence, its actual finite initial window and its bounded quantum jets determine K_N uniquely. The [Mellin theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/mellin_cyclotomic_jet_uniqueness.md) strengthens this to the entire rational root section with its pole lattice. There is consequently no freedom to alter the knot period while keeping those exact data. The unresolved assertion is that this unique anchored object has the required selected regulator character. Uniqueness cannot be converted into existence of a regulator comparison without producing a candidate satisfying the original source, lattice and quantum-normal equations. ## 2. Fixed algebraic coefficients have polynomial size on a fixed-color arc Put t=1/N and retain the root source coordinates (t,Q,Y) on the central slice U=Y^N=1. Let E be a fixed finite FIELD extension of k(t,Q,Y), k a fixed embedded characteristic-zero field. A specified finite residue-field mark and an etale selected place can be retained. Let a be a nonzero element of E, regular on the marked chart where the arc is tested. For all sufficiently large FIXED positive integers j, every specialized conjugate of a on gamma_j(t)=(t,exp(2pi*i*t),exp(2pi*i*j*t)) (1) has upper and lower polynomial bounds at t=1/N, for all large N. The required lower bound on j depends on the fixed presentation of a, not on N. In particular it cannot be exponentially small or zero at infinitely many large levels. Here is a direct proof, including the possible vanishing issue. Choose a polynomial relation for a with nonzero constant and leading coefficients, clear all denominators, and consider each nonzero coefficient P(t,Q,Y). Write P=sum_(r,s) p_(r,s)(t) Q^r Y^s. Let A be the span of its Q exponents. For j>A the integers r+js belonging to different collected pairs (r,s) are distinct. Thus P(gamma_j(t))=sum_(r,s) p_(r,s)(t) exp(2pi*i*(r+js)t) is not identically zero. Independence follows by successively applying the constant-coefficient operators partial_t-2pi*i*(r+js), with powers exceeding the polynomial degrees, to isolate one exponential. A nonzero resulting analytic germ has finite vanishing order at t=0. Apply this to the finitely many relation coefficients. Cauchy's root bound and the same bound for the reciprocal polynomial give c N^(-B)<=|a_(i,N)|<=C N^B. (2) The proof is uniform over all roots of the selected relation. It does not assume bounded absolute cyclotomic degree or heights. In particular, the complete figure-eight scalar itself cannot be a fixed algebraic function of (t,Q) on a finite cover: (2) would give zero exponential rate, contradicting (3) below. This does not exclude a fixed algebraic connection or torsor with a transcendental marked horizontal period. Its irregular regulator character must be retained before applying algebraic coefficient rigidity. For algebraic sections on a finite integral shape cover, apply the argument to a fixed nonzero norm or a polynomial relation on the selected irreducible component. Clearing actual poles must precede specialization. A statement about a fixed algebraic section is much stronger than algebraicity at each separate N. ## 3. An original-source obstruction to a regular central-fibre comparison Take the original figure-eight knot. The independently proved [whole-source identity](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/figure_eight_whole_source_identity.md) gives lim_(N->infinity) N^-1 Log|F_N(1)| =Vol(4_1)/(2pi)>0. (3) For every fixed j>=1, the SAME family and SAME original cap give F_N(Q_N^j)=C_j(q_N)->1. (4) No normalization, operator or source was changed between (3) and (4). Both arcs approach (Q,Y,U)=(1,1,1), and U=1 on both. More literally, the actual pivot has g_k(M)=M^(1-N)g_k(1). On these unit-meridian arcs its change is a specified common unit for every closed head. Moving that unchanged factor into its retained external line leaves the same numerical cut functional. Thus this growth contrast does not hide an independently chosen co-source. Suppose a proposed whole geometric comparison on the raw central fibre had the form F_N(Y)=a_N(Y) G_N(Y)+R_N(Y), (5) where a is a nonzero section of the fixed algebraic type in Section 2. Suppose on every fixed-color arc (1) its geometric period and remainder satisfied, for a common V>0, N^-1 Log|G_N(Q_N^j)|->V, |R_N(Q_N^j)|<=exp(N(V-delta_j)), delta_j>0. (6) Then (5) is impossible. Choose a fixed j larger than the presentation bound of Section 2. Its a_N(Q_N^j) is nonzero and polynomially bounded above and below. Equations (5)--(6), by the reverse triangle inequality, give positive exponential growth on that arc, contradicting (4). Equivalently, if bounded ordinary-color values force the coefficient to vanish on EVERY fixed-color arc, the exponential separation proof in Section 2 forces its algebraic restriction to the raw central fibre to vanish identically. It cannot then give the nonzero complete value by ordinary regular evaluation. This excludes a tempting shortcut: a uniform dominant geometric block with a regular algebraic scalar coefficient on that fibre. It does NOT exclude a source-preserving normal extension, a nonregular meridian lattice, or cancellation between blocks with the same exponential size. The latter possibilities are precisely data which raw algebraic point rigidity does not fix. ### The original divided source explains the necessary distinction The exact actual source is already known to use the normal extension. With U=Y^N and t_mu=U-1, set Y_r(t_mu)=Q_N^r(1+t_mu)^(1/N), v_N(t_mu)_r=(Y_r(t_mu)-1)F_N(Y_r(t_mu)). Then the unconditional original state identity is K_N=N e_0^*[t_mu^1]v_N, whereas the central state v_N(0) contains only the polynomially bounded ordinary-color row. The source has degree minus one; it is not ordinary evaluation of the lowest state degree. See [the source-adapted filtration](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/source_adapted_leading_filtration_and_actual_scale_test.md). The elementary expression (U-1)/(Y-1), U=Y^N, likewise vanishes at every proper root-orbit point and has complete whole-germ value N. It is not a regular function on the raw two-variable fibre U=1 at Y=1. This illustrates the required divided lattice; it does not define a replacement invariant or prove its regulator coefficient is nonzero. Thus the actual source-anchored example supports the user's normal-torsor viewpoint, while ruling out its regular scalar version on the unextended central fibre. ## 4. The explicit Kummer period has growing ambient rank For an odd prime p the actual one-variable cyclic cover is C_p: y^p=product_(j=1)^(p-1)(1-Q_p^j t)^j. It is connected. Its p-1 finite branch points have ramification index p, since each j is coprime to p. Infinity is unramified: the polynomial degree p(p-1)/2 is divisible by p. Counting the Euler characteristic of the punctured p-sheeted cover and filling its ramified points gives 2-2g=p*2-(p-1)*(p-1), g=(p-1)(p-3)/2. (7) The growth persists in the particular nontrivial deck character used by y^-1 dt. Remove the finite branch points from the base sphere. It retracts to a graph with one vertex and p-2 loops. In any nontrivial deck-character component the covering graph chain groups have dimensions 1 and p-2, and its boundary map has rank one: a branch generator acts by a nontrivial p-th root. Hence that character's H_1 has dimension p-3. Filling the ramification points changes only the trivial character, because each such point is deck-fixed. Therefore dim H_1(C_p)_chi=p-3 (8) for every nontrivial character chi, including the selected one. The small-circle source has an additional important feature. Removing the p preimages of t=0 adds one boundary-circle dimension to each nontrivial character. The original selected circle projects into that canonical one-dimensional boundary subspace. Thus growing ambient rank DOES NOT rule out a smaller selected period object. It does show that fixed variable count alone has not constructed such an object uniformly in p. In particular the compact C_p cannot all be the smooth proper fibres of one fixed finite-type algebraic curve family on finitely many strata: their genus is unbounded. A fixed selected torsor must be a genuinely constructed reduction or comparison, not an automatic consequence of the displayed Kummer equations. ## 5. What a successful rigidity certificate would now have to contain The existing [whole-comparison rigidity theorem](whole_period_cyclotomic_rigidity.md) can promote bounded algebraic quantum-jet identities to an exact whole comparison. The existing [critical-source theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/irreducible_critical_source_and_whole_norm.md) can then force every geometric coefficient nonzero from an irreducible descended critical line and a nonzero exact source moment, or from a faithful trace realization. Fixed algebraic coefficients automatically have polynomial norms on the root arc. Those theorems would remove a separately assumed nonzero geometric weight. Their inputs are substantive and finite: * a fixed algebraic comparison space or an explicitly bounded selected quotient of the actual Kummer/quantum object; * the source-normal pairing, its meridian pole lattice and its quantum-normal connection retained by that comparison; * an actual descended critical line/observable with its exact source moments, rather than only a classical shape field; * control of the TOTAL compact remainder after that projection. The first three have not been supplied for the selected knot period. The new exact cut construction supplies the original cycle, and its infinity bound removes a real global escape obstacle. It does not make their fixed algebraic reduction or critical source moment automatic. Equations (3)--(4) show why that reduction must retain the divided source before passing to a central or associated-graded fibre.

title: A nonzero all-level annihilator from the actual finite cut state
text: # A nonzero all-level annihilator from the actual finite cut state Research note, 26 October 2026. This gives an independent existence proof of a nonzero all-level meridian annihilator for the reduced literature ADO state of every knot. The proof keeps the finite-sum boundaries, handles an elimination operator vanishing under summation, and removes a central factor before root specialization. It does not identify the operator's classical symbol with the geometric A-curve or prove a volume estimate. Existence of level-independent ADO recursions is existing coverage: [Brown--Dimofte--Garoufalidis--Geer, 2005.08176](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.08176). Proper q-hypergeometric sums and q-holonomicity are standard, with scope surveyed in [Garoufalidis--Le, 1601.07487](https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.07487). Their closure, Hamiltonian-reduction, and holonomicity proofs are not premises here. The proof below is a filtered dimension count with explicit boundary strata and finite exponential moments. ## 1. An auxiliary off-root lift, with the root state unchanged Choose a braid presentation of a zero-framed knot. At a fixed positive integer N, keep q generic and use the N by N matrices E v_a=[a]_q*(x*q^(1-a)-x^(-1)*q^(a-1))/(q-q^(-1)) v_(a-1), F v_a=v_(a+1), K v_a=x*q^(-2a)v_a, 0<=a<N, with the endpoint vectors zero. These need not be a quantum-group representation away from the root. Only their finite matrix entries will be used off-root. On a crossing put D_(a,b)=x^(-a-b)q^(2ab), and Theta=sum_(k=0)^(N-1) c_k (E tensor F)^k, c_k=q^(k(k-1)/2)*(q-q^(-1))^k/[k]_q!, R_tilde=D*Theta. (1.1) This is the actual unrolled R with its common q^(alpha^2/2) factor removed, x=q^alpha. The inverse is R_tilde^(-1)=Theta_inv*D^(-1), Theta_inv=sum_(k=0)^(N-1) (-1)^k*q^(-k(k-1)/2)*(q-q^(-1))^k/[k]_q! *(E tensor F)^k. (1.2) For a proof, set Q=q^2 and rewrite the two coefficient series as the q-exponential and its inverse. Their coefficient convolution is the finite q-binomial identity product_(j=0)^(m-1)(1+Q^j*t) =sum_(r=0)^m Q^(r(r-1)/2) {m choose r}_Q t^r. Inserting the last factor and collecting coefficients proves this identity inductively. At t=-1 its right side is zero for m>0, which is exactly the inverse-series convolution after the factorial rewrite. Finally (E tensor F)^N=0 truncates it. Thus (1.2) holds for generic q, without a root-of-unity relation. Use the checked crossings obtained by permutation, pivotal K^(1-N), and the residual framing factor x^(w(N-1)), with w the braid writhe. Take the (0,0) entry of the cut partial trace and call it L_N(q,x). No scalarity or topological invariance is asserted for this off-root lift. At q_N=exp(pi*i/N), it is exactly the actual reduced period L_N(q_N,x)=F_N(x). (1.3) The cancellation of the removed factors against the twist, and the root normalization, are those already independently checked in [the ADO pointing note](kashaev_ado_pointing.md). All denominators [k]_q!, k<N, and q-q^(-1), are nonzero at q_N. Consequently L_N is regular there as a rational function of generic x. ## 2. The precise finite-sum class The lift is a finite sum over crossing powers and strand labels. All matching constraints are integral linear equations. Their integer solution lattice has a fixed integral basis; use its coordinates k=(k_1,...,k_s). All actual labels and crossing powers are fixed integral linear functions of k. Their bounds 0,...,N-1 define a finite support P_N by finitely many inequalities ell_nu(N,k)>=0. (2.1) Every nonzero summand on this support is a product of: * a monomial q^Q(N,k) x^L(N,k), with Q integer-valued quadratic and L integral linear; * finitely many q-factorials (q^v;q^v)_ell(N,k) and their inverses, with nonnegative integral linear lengths; * finitely many (x^u*q^ell(N,k);q^v)_m(N,k) and their inverses, with u!=0 and nonnegative integral linear lengths; * finitely many fixed nonzero Q(q)-scalars raised to integral linear exponents, including signs. Here v!=0 is fixed. Include all factorial and Pochhammer length conditions among (2.1). A term is defined as zero outside P_N. Its value is nonzero as a rational function of generic (q,x) on P_N. This is the only regularity of a summand used below. The x-dependent Pochhammer parameters also satisfy the proper alignment condition: v divides each coefficient of k_i in ell. This ensures that an internal unit shift moves an argument by an integral number of its q^v steps. For the actual R-weights both v and those coefficients are even, with v=+/-2. The proof does not assert this shift bound for unaligned Pochhammer products. To check this class for (1.1), use E^k v_a=([a]_q!/[a-k]_q!) *product_(r=0)^(k-1)[alpha-a+r+1]_q v_(a-k). The second product is an x-dependent Pochhammer of length k. Explicitly, writing rho=q-q^(-1), it is (-x^(-1))^k q^(k(a-1)-k(k-1)/2) rho^(-k) *(x^2*q^(2-2a);q^2)_k. Also [r]_q!=q^(-r(r-1)/2)*(q^2;q^2)_r/(1-q^2)^r. These formulas verify both the alignment and the allowed linear exponents of scalar factors, with no appeal to a closure theorem. The other coefficients in (1.1)--(1.2) are q-factorials and quadratic q-monomials. Pivotal and framing entries contribute x-powers linear in (N,k) and q-powers quadratic in (N,k). Thus their shift ratios belong to the class just described. Choose a fixed positive integer B so that shifting x by q^B shifts every x-dependent Pochhammer argument by an integral number of its q^v steps. B=1 works for these R-weights: u=+/-2, v=+/-2. Write T for this x-shift and S_i for k_i -> k_i+1. Set z=q^N and t_i=q^k_i. The variable z will be retained until the last specialization. ## 3. A global shift-span bound, including the boundaries Let I_N(q,x;k) be one summand, extended by zero. For R>=1 consider the actions x^a z^c T^b S_1^beta_1...S_s^beta_s I, 0<=a,c,b,beta_i<=R. (3.1) These are functions of (N,k,x), over the coefficient field Q(q). Their joint span has dimension O(R^(s+2)). The constant depends on the fixed summand data and support, not N or R. ### Interior rational-shift estimate Where a collection of shifted terms is supported, choose one supported shift beta_0 as reference. Ratios of the shifted products to I(k+beta_0) are rational in x,z,t_1,...,t_s. They have a common Laurent-polynomial denominator of degree O(R), and after clearing it all exponents are bounded in absolute value by C R. Indeed a shift changes every factorial length and Pochhammer endpoint by O(R). All possible endpoint factors belong to finitely many types 1-q^r x^u z^v t^a, with r in intervals of length O(R). Include their required denominator factors once, with the bounded multiplicities of the original products. Quadratic q-monomials change by linear functions of (N,k), hence by Laurent monomials of degree O(R) in z,t; x-shifts of x^L contribute the same kind of monomial. Powers q^O(R^2), and the shifted scalar factors, are scalars in Q(q). Without boundaries this proves the O(R^(s+2)) estimate immediately. Ignoring the zero extension at a boundary would be incorrect. ### Boundary stratification and its codimension Choose C so |ell_nu(0,beta)-ell_nu(0,0)|<=C R for all shifts in (3.1). Partition the integer pairs (N,k) by declaring each support form either greater than C R, less than -C R, or equal to one particular integer in [-C R,C R]. A stratum with a form less than -C R contributes zero to every shifted term. On any remaining stratum the supported shifts are a fixed subset: large forms remain positive, while near-boundary forms have fixed integer values. An empty subset contributes zero. Otherwise choose beta_0 from that subset. All q-factorial ratios between it and another supported shift have nonnegative endpoint indices. Their intervening factorial factors have strictly positive indices. A common denominator can therefore be chosen nonzero on the stratum. The x-dependent factors are nonzero for generic x. Thus the interior estimate still applies there. Suppose the fixed near-boundary forms have rank r as affine constraints on (N,k). Their consistent integer labels have only O(R^r) possibilities: choose r independent forms, after which all dependent labels are determined. There are finitely many choices of forms and large/small patterns. On each such stratum, the multiplicative variables z,t satisfy r independent binomial constraints z^b product_i t_i^a_i=q^d. (3.2) The Laurent monomials of degree O(R) in x,z,t modulo these constraints span a space of dimension O(R^(s+2-r)). To see this integrally, use Smith normal form of the fixed constraint lattice. The r constrained exponents can be reduced modulo fixed integers; the other s+2-r exponents range through O(R) integers. This also keeps the finitely many components if the lattice is not saturated. The varying right sides q^d are coefficient-field scalars. Restrict the family (3.1) to all these strata. A function is determined by its restrictions, and multiplication by the nonzero reference summand or common denominator does not increase dimension. Consequently its dimension is at most sum_(r=0)^(s+1) O(R^r)*O(R^(s+2-r)) =O(R^(s+2)). (3.3) This proves the global bound. It also treats small N, intersecting boundary faces, and redundant support inequalities. In particular it does not assume that the index polytope is a box. The same estimate holds for a finite sum on the same lattice by applying it to the direct sum of their spaces. One can retain separate term components in the elimination below, so cancellation between terms is not an assumption. ## 4. Elimination without internal multiplication variables The PBW monomials of the operators in (3.1) are linearly independent in the formal Ore algebra. There are (R+1)^(s+3) of them. For large R this exceeds the bound (3.3). Finite linear algebra yields a nonzero formal operator P(x,z,T,S_1,...,S_s) I=0 (4.1) with coefficients in Q(q), and no multiplication t_i in P. Identity (4.1) is global on the zero-extended integer array, not merely an equality of ratios at interior indices. The construction is effective in principle. List the boundary strata, clear the proper denominators, reduce their monomials by the binomial constraints, and solve the resulting finite linear system over Q(q). No efficiency or minimal-order claim is made. ## 5. Finite moments repair vanishing under summation For each N introduce independent formal units w_i and the finite Laurent polynomial F_N(q,x,w)=sum_(k in Z^s) w^k I_N(q,x;k). Since the support is finite, translation of the sum is exact: sum_k w^k S_i I(k)=w_i^(-1) F_N(q,x,w). Thus (4.1) becomes P(x,q^N,T,w_1^(-1),...,w_s^(-1)) F_N(q,x,w)=0. (5.1) Expand the nonzero polynomial P in its commuting internal shifts around S_i=1: P=sum_alpha A_alpha(x,z,T)(S-1)^alpha. Choose a nonzero A_alpha at least total degree h. Set w_i=exp(v_i) in (5.1). Its coefficient of v^alpha at that least degree is (-1)^h A_alpha(x,q^N,T) F_N(q,x,1)=0. (5.2) Every term in which a positive-degree moment of F_N occurs has a lower-degree coefficient of P, and therefore vanishes. Hence A_alpha is a genuine nonzero meridian operator for the summed state, even if P(x,z,T,1,...,1)=0. This is a formal finite-moment argument, with no convergence, contour shift, or boundary omission. ## 6. Specializing q^N=-1 without losing the operator Apply (5.2) to the actual off-root lift L_N. Clear denominators and write its nonzero operator as A(x,z,T)=(z+1)^h A_0(x,z,T), where at least one coefficient of A_0 has nonzero value at z=-1. The factor is central. For every fixed positive N, q^N+1 is a nonzero rational function of generic q, so the identity for L_N also implies A_0(x,q^N,T)L_N(q,x)=0 before specialization. At q=q_N the lift is regular, as proved in Section 1. Therefore P_K(q,x,T)=A_0(x,-1,T), P_K(q_N,x,T)F_N(x)=0 (6.1) for all but finitely many N. The excluded levels are poles of the fixed rational q-coefficients. P_K is nonzero by construction. This cancels a common operator factor before specialization of an auxiliary lift. It changes neither the state nor any peripheral factor in a state comparison. In particular the actual full ADO factor d_N is still the whole rational germ of the pointing note. At the trivial quotient color the actual reduced state has value one. Thus an order-zero multiplication operator cannot annihilate it at all large levels. After removing a common shift, (6.1) has positive order and nonzero leading and trailing coefficients in Q(q,x). Its existence proves that the actual localized all-level annihilator ideal is nonzero for every knot. The exact change x=-q^(-1)M and the fixed full/reduced shift gauge transport this operator to the meridian M and to the full literature ADO normalization. In the localized skew polynomial ring over Q(q,M), left Euclidean division gives the unique monic element of least order in the actual nonzero ideal. This is the literature minimal-operator convention; the construction above need not compute that minimal element efficiently. ## 7. What this settles and what the triangulation must still supply The [all-level exact period theorem](all_level_a_period.md) can now be applied to a nonzero actual annihilator for every knot, with its finite fixed-color pointing and bounded q-jets. Existence of such an operator is no longer an unaudited premise in that application. No proof of an equality with a Jones recursion ideal is needed for this implication. This proof does not show that the minimal operator has the geometric A-component in its classical symbol, that it has a rational inhomogeneous source factor, or that its period has the geometric regulator norm. A positive ideal triangulation supplies the geometric Bloch class and gluing branch. The exact comparison between its quantum gluing period and the actual cut-state module remains necessary, as detailed in [the triangulation bridge](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/triangulation_regulator_bridge.md). The subsequent [relative octahedral presentation](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/relative_octahedral_period.md) now rewrites these very cut-state coefficients into five tetrahedral atoms, proves their local ideal-octahedron geometry, and derives the finite factorial's source and exact cyclic boundary transition. This gives explicit local input for the remaining comparison; it does not identify this eliminated meridian operator's global geometric block or its selected regulator period. The [diagnostics](../experiments/audit_finite_sum_annihilator.py) check the generic off-root crossing lift and its inverse against the actual root matrices, explicit global boundary certificates, and the finite-moment and central-specialization repairs. Their [results](../experiments/finite_sum_annihilator_results.json) are checks of these ingredients, not a volume theorem or an efficient all-knot computation of minimal operators.

title: Which derivatives the current direct-power route actually requires
text: # Which derivatives the current direct-power route actually requires The [whole-source local packet](../papers/casimir-source-asymptotics/README.md) now assembles these results for the actual full numerator. The original global spectral filling period remains open. 31 October 2026. . Conclusion: the current route to the original root sequence does NOT require a genuine-q normal estimate. It does require the full spectral Hermite/Jordan data at the fixed root. Those are different derivatives. For each individual N, fix q_N=exp(pi i/N), d=N-1, and the literal original pair Casimir Omega_N. In notes/actual_direct_long_power_source.md, section3, the exact identity is R_N^n=q_N^(n d^2/4) exp[n K(Omega_N)/(2hbar)], hbar=2pi i/N, K(sigma)=arccosh(-sigma/2)^2. At each double Casimir node its value AND derivative with respect to sigma equal those of the actual original R_N^n. At the odd simple node only its value is required. Full Hermite uniqueness in the root Casimir quotient therefore proves the matrix equality, including negative powers and the original square-root scalar. No semisimple quotient is taken. An earlier generic argument used to establish these finite identities would not by itself introduce a uniform off-root asymptotic requirement. The source map in notes/actual_homogeneous_casimir_face_source.md, sections1--4, applies to these exact polynomials at the SAME fixed root. It retains the original physical endpoints, Cartan factors, changing strand positions, and unrestricted marked cap. The other caps and integer total-degree conservation force the marked complementary pair only AFTER the whole contraction. Its literal mark satisfies mp=1. The cup/cap constants and mark character are assembled explicitly in (7a,b); the inverse Fourier measure and original degree constraint give the exact coefficient (9), with no extra N factor and no root limit. In particular the ordinary quantum dimension is never divided out in this direct marked evaluation. The passage from that raw marked contraction to the original enhanced Kashaev normalization is the existing fixed-root crossing/pivot/dual comparison and retained framing character. The complete-color comparison in notes/actual_complete_augmented_source_normalization.md uses root cut scalarity, exact basis covariance and mp=1. It is local in the crossing word and applies when a box contains the actual power R_N^n. The enhanced reduced normalization differs by a recorded unit phase. If one instead asks for the full one-cut modified ADO normalization, its additional exact factor is i^(N+3)/N at the complete pointing; that is not an uncomputed q-normal correction and has zero exponential rate. No such extra modified factor is silently attached to Kashaev's unknot-one evaluation. The exact spectral Cauchy and total-derivative periods are therefore alternative formulas for the SAME root marked scalar for every N. Their V_N(sigma) and partial_sigma V_N contain the independent nilpotent and semisimple data. Differentiating a value-only complete interpolation would be invalid, but that issue is spectral, not a requirement to deform q away from q_N. The current cofactor proofs address precisely this fixed-root spectral issue. The generic trace identity F_D(t)=D_N(t) z_D(t), with z_D(0)=F_D'(0)/D_N'(0), is a valid ALTERNATIVE presentation of the marked scalar in the matching-graph notes. Using that presentation for asymptotics would require its specified moving-q lift and normal. The direct marked/Casimir route does not use this quotient and need not inherit its analytic hypotheses. Similarly, extending the result to a generic-q or moving meridian invariant is a separate problem. Although q_N varies with the integer level N, the desired theorem is a limit of exact fixed-root identities indexed by N. It needs uniform N estimates for those identities, not a derivative with respect to q. The shared coefficient packet is now proved by the linked whole-source theorem. The subsequent localized period theorem also supplies the nonzero unit-charge contribution with its original normalization. The outstanding gate is control of its exact global spectral/charge remainder. A genuine-q normal should not be listed as another necessary gate for this route. Audited sources: actual_direct_long_power_source §§1--3; actual_homogeneous_casimir_face_source §§1--4; actual_original_marked_face_coefficient §§2--4; actual_complete_augmented_source_normalization §§1--3; actual_spectral_total_derivative_source; actual_coherent_filling_gaussian_chirp §1; general_augmented_plat_long_twist_target equation(3a). This is an analytical dependency audit, not a new numerical test. Root independently checked the cited fixed-root Gaussian, Hermite data, original coefficient normalization and reduced/modified distinction. The [localized original period](general_localized_unit_charge_filling_period.md) now proves the nonzero unit-charge contribution and dominance in the finite local charge sector. The remaining gate is its exact global remainder, including the full integrals of remote charges. It does not require a generic-q continuation.

title: Full rank-one cyclotomic descent, including ramified zeros and poles
text: # Full rank-one cyclotomic descent, including ramified zeros and poles Research proof for independent audit, 27 October 2026. This extends [the unramified Q-parameter proof](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/q_parameter_curvature_extension.md). The new ingredient is a weighted sequence-uniqueness lemma allowing finite exponential--Puiseux amplitudes. It removes both ramification and finite-nonzero limiting-root hypotheses from that rank-one result. This remains a comparison-line theorem. The actual geometric comparison line, its full cyclic transport identities and its source/cut marking must still be supplied. The original volume conjecture is not proved here. ## 1. Statement and the coefficient-field requirement Let sigma_Q(Y)=QY and a(Q,Y) be a nonzero element of ℚ(Q,Y). Assume that for every sufficiently large positive integer n, product_(j=0)^(n-1) a(zeta_n,zeta_n^jY)=1, zeta_n=exp(2pi*i/n), (1.1) as a whole rational identity in Y. Then there exists f(Q,Y) in ℚ(Q,Y)^*, a(Q,Y)=f(Q,QY)/f(Q,Y). (1.2) No unramifiedness, limiting-root separation, or levelwise degree bound for Hilbert-90 gauges is assumed. The conclusion is generic rational descent. It does not assert that f is a unit at the ideal meridian or that it preserves an unspecified period pointing. The same conclusion over a subfield K of C holds if (1.1) is known at every primitive n-th root for the chosen coefficient embedding. For ℚ-coefficients this whole-root condition follows by cyclotomic Galois conjugation. For a number field a sufficient stronger marking is to know (1.1) for all coefficient conjugates. A single geometric embedding is not silently promoted to that condition. ## 2. Scaled roots supply all powers without a nonresonance assumption For a fixed positive integer k set xi_N=exp(2pi*i*k/N). Its order is m=N/gcd(k,N). Whole-root (1.1) gives the m-step transport identity at xi_N for all sufficiently large N. Its N-step transport consists of gcd(k,N) repetitions and is also one. Factor a over an algebraic splitting field as a(Q,Y)=r(Q)Y^s product_(i=1)^d(1-alpha_i(Q)Y) /product_(j=1)^e(1-beta_j(Q)Y). (2.1) Every alpha_i,beta_j is a nonzero algebraic function of Q. Its value may tend to zero or infinity at Q=1. For sufficiently large root orders the values themselves are finite and nonzero. The ordinary primitive-root product first gives s=0, r(zeta_n)^n=1 and d=e. It also gives equality of the multisets of n-th powers of the alpha and beta values. The fixed-rational scalar discreteness argument yields r(Q)=Q^(k_0), k_0 in Z. (2.2) Here is that argument in full. The identities |r(zeta_n)|=1 exclude a zero or pole of r at Q=1, so choose an analytic logarithm ell of r near one. Then L_n=n ell(exp(2pi*i/n)) belongs to 2pi*i Z. The expansion of this fixed analytic germ gives L_n=n ell(1)+2pi*i ell'(1)+O(1/n), with a convergent expansion in powers of 1/n after the linear term. Hence L_(n+1)-L_n=ell(1)+O(1/n^2). These differences lie in the discrete set 2pi*i Z, so ell(1) belongs to that set and r(1)=1. Choose the logarithm with ell(1)=0. The sequence L_n now converges in the same discrete set and is eventually 2pi*i k_0 for a fixed integer k_0. Thus r(zeta_n)=zeta_n^(k_0) at infinitely many roots. The rational function r(Q)-Q^(k_0) has infinitely many zeros and is therefore identically zero. This proves (2.2). At xi_N use its actual order m, not a primitive N-step product formula. Equality of the m-th power multisets, raised to the gcd(k,N)-th power, gives equality of their N-th power multisets. In particular sum_i alpha_i(xi_N)^N=sum_j beta_j(xi_N)^N (2.3) for every fixed k and all sufficiently large N. ## 3. Convergent Puiseux forms from a finite cover Put t=Log Q/(2pi*i), with the logarithm near Q=1. There is a positive integer e_0 such that, after t=s^(e_0), all branches in (2.1) are single-valued meromorphic functions of s near zero. Here is a direct justification of the needed analytic form. Choose a punctured t-disk avoiding other discriminant zeros and coefficient poles of the finite root polynomials. Local analytic roots give a finite covering there. Its monodromy is a permutation of finitely many roots. Taking e_0 divisible by the cycle lengths kills this monodromy, so the pulled-back roots are single-valued holomorphic functions on a punctured s-disk. Cauchy's elementary root bound, after division by the leading polynomial coefficient, bounds every root by a fixed power of |t|^(-1). Multiplying by a sufficient power of s then gives a bounded holomorphic function, which extends across zero. Hence each root is meromorphic there. Since no root is identically zero, it has a convergent form alpha_i(exp(2pi*i*t)) =a_i t^(nu_i) exp(lambda_i(t^(1/e_0))), (3.1) where a_i!=0, nu_i is rational and lambda_i is holomorphic with lambda_i(0)=0. Choose the branch t^(1/e_0)>0 on the positive t-axis, which contains all scaled roots used below. The beta branches have corresponding data b_j,mu_j,eta_j. Define A_i(t)=exp(lambda_i(t^(1/e_0))/t), B_j(t)=exp(eta_j(t^(1/e_0))/t). (3.2) These need not extend meromorphically across t=0. Each is of the specific form exp(P(s^(-1))) g(s), s=t^(1/e_0), (3.3) where P is a polynomial with no constant term and degree below e_0, and g is a holomorphic unit. Indeed separate the terms of lambda(s)/s^(e_0) with negative s exponents; the remainder is holomorphic. Multiplication by any algebraic/Puiseux weight changes g to a meromorphic function after a common further ramification. The next lemma permits these weights explicitly. ## 4. Weighted exponential--Puiseux sequence uniqueness Fix e>=1. Consider finitely many triples (nu,a,P), with nu rational, a!=0 complex and P a polynomial of degree below e with P(0)=0. Let g_(nu,a,P)(s) be meromorphic germs at zero. Merge identical triples by adding their g coefficients. If sum_(nu,a,P) N^(-nu N) a^N exp(P(N^(1/e))) g_(nu,a,P)(N^(-1/e))=0 (4.1) for every sufficiently large integer N, then every merged g is identically zero. **Oscillatory estimate.** If phi(x)=theta x+sum_(r=1)^(e-1)b_r x^(r/e), theta,b_r real, and either theta is nonzero modulo 2pi or some b_r is nonzero, then the Cesaro mean of exp(i phi(N)) is zero. If theta is nonzero modulo 2pi, partial sums of exp(i theta N) are bounded. Summation by parts bounds the sum through M by O(1+M^rho), where rho<1 is the highest fractional exponent; the total variation of exp(i sum b_r x^(r/e)) has that bound. If all b_r vanish the sum is bounded directly. If theta is zero modulo 2pi, let rho in (0,1) be the highest nonzero fractional exponent. Eventually |phi'(x)| is comparable to x^(rho-1), and |phi''(x)|=O(x^(rho-2)). The sum--integral error is O(M^rho), by integrating the derivative's absolute value over unit intervals. Integration by parts with 1/(i phi') bounds the integral by O(M^(1-rho)); its derivative term is bounded by the integral of |phi''|/|phi'|^2=O(x^(-rho)). Both bounds are o(M), proving the estimate. **Proof of (4.1).** If a merged coefficient is nonzero, choose successively among the finitely many such terms: 1. the smallest nu; 2. the largest modulus R=|a| at that nu; 3. the lexicographically largest vector of real coefficients of P, ordered from the highest power down; 4. the smallest Laurent order m of g among those remaining terms. Normalize by the common positive scale N^(-nu N) R^N exp(Re P(N^(1/e))) N^(-m/e). Every term outside these selected scales tends to zero: the successive comparisons are on the N log N, N, fractional-power and log N scales. The normalized equality becomes sum_l c_l exp(i phi_l(N))+o(1)=0, (4.2) with at least one nonzero leading Laurent coefficient c_l. The residual phases are distinct modulo constants: equal phases would have the same complex a and the same complex P, and would already have been merged. Their pairwise differences therefore satisfy the oscillatory estimate above. Multiply (4.2) by exp(-i phi_j(N)) and take Cesaro means. Every cross term has mean zero, and the error tends to zero, so c_j=0. This contradicts the selection of m. It proves the lemma. In particular, distinct pairs (nu,a) remain distinguishable when their amplitudes are finite sums of (3.3). This weighted conclusion is stronger than the earlier meromorphic-amplitude lemma and is the form usable for rational partial-fraction source coefficients. ## 5. Branch pairing from all scaled power sums At xi_N, equation (3.1) gives exactly alpha_i(xi_N)^N =N^(-nu_i N)(a_i k^(nu_i))^N A_i(k/N)^k.
