(5.1) For fixed k the amplitudes in this formula are finite sums of (3.3), with the same common ramification. Apply the lemma to (2.3). Distinct (nu,a) remain distinct after replacing a by a k^nu. Thus for every pair (nu,a), sum_(alpha_i in (nu,a)) A_i(kt)^k =sum_(beta_j in (nu,a)) B_j(kt)^k. Rescale the argument and take k=1,...,d. For each (nu,a) this gives equality of the first d power sums of its A and B functions. Newton identities, padding by zeros to length d, identify their multisets over the common field of meromorphic functions on the ramified punctured disk. Their entries are nonzero exponentials, so the group cardinalities agree. A fixed permutation pairs A_i=B_(pi(i)) as function germs. The paired branches have the same nu and a. Their quotient is therefore exp(lambda_i-eta_(pi(i))). The equality of A and B says that (lambda_i-eta_(pi(i)))/t has exponential one. It is holomorphic on a connected ramified punctured disk, even if initially it could have a pole at zero. A holomorphic function with values in the discrete set 2pi*i Z is constant. Hence lambda_i-eta_(pi(i))=2pi*i k_i t, alpha_i(Q)=Q^(k_i) beta_(pi(i))(Q), k_i in Z. (5.2) This proves the required integral Q-shift pairing without any assumption on ramification or limiting values. ## 6. Finite divisor flow and rational descent For k_i>0 use the finite gauge product_(u=0)^(k_i-1)(1-Q^u beta_(pi(i))(Q)Y). For k_i<0 use the inverse product over k_i<=u<0. Their product, times Y^(k_0), gives (1.2) over a finite splitting field. Its numerator and denominator Y-degrees are each at most |k_0|+sum_i |k_i|. (6.1) The finite divisor flow is unique on each infinite Q-shift orbit. Consequently it is invariant under the Galois group of the splitting field over ℚ(Q). The product part has value one at Y=0, fixing its remaining scalar. It therefore descends to ℚ(Q,Y). This also proves descent over K under the stated whole-root hypothesis. The remaining generic scalar ambiguity is a function of Q alone; a specified regular anchor can fix it. The theorem does not discard a zero or pole of the gauge at the ideal meridian or replace the required source/cut lattice by a generic isomorphism. ## 7. Scope for the actual A-period program The actual reduced knot state has a rational Q-operator. This places its rational coefficient constructions in the correct cyclotomic field. However, the theorem applies to a specified rank-one comparison coefficient with the full transport identity (1.1). The current root-state data do not automatically construct that comparison or prove its norm characters agree with a geometric regulator realization. Those remain substantive inputs. The proof concerns fixed rational comparison data. It neither trivializes the whole quantum A-module nor asserts algebraicity of the selected Mellin period, which is transcendental for the adequate class. Algebraic comparison maps and transcendental marked periods remain compatible. [Ramified and weighted audit](../experiments/audit_full_rank_one_cyclotomic_descent.py). [Results](../experiments/full_rank_one_cyclotomic_descent_results.json).

title: The entire original all-CROSS Fourier period from its local packet and global spectral gap
status: Entire CROSS period has actual filled-volume rate
text: # The entire original all-CROSS Fourier period from its local packet and global spectral gap analytical theorem, 31 October 2026. This concerns the actual all-CROSS shared numerator and its **whole original Fourier/Hermite period**. The two source estimates used below have separate proofs. All twists are independently signed, sufficiently long, and fixed before the level tends to infinity. The remaining moving one-sided sectors of the full numerator are not estimated here. ## 1. Exact source, hypotheses, and conclusion Fix the original certified marked flat plat $D$ with $R$ ports, $d=N-1$ and $q=e^{\pi i/N}$. In this note write $C_N(\boldsymbol\delta)$ for the raw shared all-CROSS coefficient $$ C_N=C_N^{\mathrm{raw}}= \left[\prod_{f\ \mathrm{ordinary}}L_f^d\right] \left.\prod_i H_{V_N,\mathrm{cross}}\right|_{L_u=L_v=0},\qquad C_N^{\mathrm{raw}}=(-1)^{dR}C_N^{\mathrm{positive}}. $$ where $C_N^{\mathrm{positive}}$ is the sign-adjusted coefficient formed from $P_{\mathrm{cross}}=(-1)^dH_{V_N,\mathrm{cross}}$ in the preceding cofactor/global-gap notes. The spectral arguments are $\sigma_i=-2\cos(2\pi\delta_i)$, with both parity definitions of CROSS retained. The absolute global gap is unchanged by this exact sign. The raw source is an entire, separately even, one-periodic function of each $\delta_i$, obtained from a polynomial of degree at most $d$ in each $\sigma_i$. It is not an independently optimized product of local norms. In particular the sign $(-1)^{dR}$ in (2) belongs to this raw convention, not to the preceding positive $C_N$. The original all-CROSS sector of the raw marked period is $$ \begin{aligned} I_{\mathrm{cross}}={}&q^{\frac{d^2}{4}\sum_i n_i}(-i)^R \sum_{\boldsymbol\ell\in(\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\})^R} \left(\prod_i\ell_i\right)(-1)^{(N+1)\sum_i\ell_i}\\ &\quad\times\int_{[-1/2,1/2]^R} \left(\prod_i\sin(2\pi\delta_i)\right)C_N(\boldsymbol\delta) \exp\!\left\{N\sum_i[\pi i n_i\delta_i^2+2\pi i\ell_i\delta_i]\right\} \,d\boldsymbol\delta. \end{aligned}\tag{1} $$ Every $n_i=\epsilon_i-2p_i$ is its actual nonzero fixed integer crossing power. A separately recorded final-diagram framing/component character multiplies (1) when converting the raw contraction to the final invariant convention. No additional mark or power of N is inserted. Formula (1) follows by linear projection of the [exact full numerator identity](../papers/filling-bounds/README.md) onto these path sectors; a separate covariance claim for an individual path sector is unnecessary. For every fixed $N$ and $\mathbf n$ the whole-domain charge series is absolutely convergent. Indeed $B_N=(\prod_i\sin(2\pi\delta_i))C_Ne^{\pi iN\sum_i n_i\delta_i^2}$ has zero endpoint values and matching first derivatives in each variable, including after differentiating other variables. Three integrations by parts in each coordinate give $O_{N,\mathbf n}(\prod_i|\ell_i|^{-3})$; after the charge factors this is summable. This observation alone is not a bound uniform in $N$. The two source inputs are: (H1) On a fixed complex cube around $\boldsymbol\delta=0$, the actual all-CROSS numerator has the relative packet $$ C_N(\boldsymbol\delta) =\frac{(-1)^{dR}N^{2R}e^{N A_N(\boldsymbol\delta)}} {(2\pi N)^{(R-1)/2}\sqrt{\det H_N(\boldsymbol\delta)}} \left[1+O(N^{-1})\right].\tag{2} $$ with its exact finite anchors and determinant branch. $A_N$ is real on the real chart, even in each coordinate, and tends with fixed derivatives to $A_0$, with $A_0(0)=\Phi_D$ and $A_0''(0)=-2\operatorname{diag}(C_i)$, $C_i>0$. On a smaller chart $\operatorname{Re}A_N''$ is uniformly negative definite. This is the CROSS packet proved before the full-numerator restoration in the [whole-source packet theorem](../papers/casimir-source-asymptotics/README.md), so it uses the same $A_N$ and $H_N$. Equivalently the full packet plus its independently controlled noncross error gives the same local asymptotic. (H2) For every fixed $\eta>0$, there are $\tau_\eta,\gamma_\eta>0$ such that $$ |C_N(\boldsymbol\delta)|\leq e^{N(\Phi_D-\gamma_\eta)}.\tag{3} $$ for all sufficiently large N, $\max_i|\operatorname{Re}\delta_i|\geq\eta$ on the centered real cube, and $|\operatorname{Im}\delta_i|\leq\tau_\eta$. Periodicity extends this to equivalent real representatives. Every fixed derivative has the same strict exponential bound on smaller strips. The [global CROSS spectral-gap theorem](../papers/casimir-source-asymptotics/README.md) retains the protected zero faces and all original start rows. **Theorem.** There is a diagram-dependent threshold $n_0$ such that for every fixed independently signed integer vector with $|n_i|\geq n_0$, the entire period (1) equals $$ \begin{aligned} I_{\mathrm{cross}}={}&q^{\frac{d^2}{4}\sum_i n_i}(-2i)^R\sqrt{2\pi}\,N^{R+1/2}\\ &\quad\times\frac{\prod_i\sin(2\pi\delta_{N,\mathbf1,i})} {\sqrt{\det H_N(\boldsymbol\delta_{N,\mathbf1})}\sqrt{\det Q_{N,\mathbf1}}} e^{N S_{N,\mathbf1}}\\ &\quad\times\left[1+O_{\mathbf n}(N^{-1})+O_{\mathbf n}(e^{-\eta_{\mathbf n}N})\right]. \end{aligned}\tag{4} $$ for some $\eta_{\mathbf n}>0$. Here $\boldsymbol\delta_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}$ is the actual finite saddle of $$ \begin{aligned} \Phi_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}(\boldsymbol\delta) &=A_N(\boldsymbol\delta)+\pi i\sum_i n_i\delta_i^2+2\pi i\sum_i\ell_i\delta_i,\\ S_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}&=\Phi_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}(\boldsymbol\delta_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}),\\ Q_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}&=-\Phi_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}''(\boldsymbol\delta_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}). \end{aligned} $$ and the $Q$ determinant root is the Gaussian branch $\operatorname{Re}Q>0$. The coefficient in (4) is nonzero for each fixed $\mathbf n$, at both level parities. Its normalized logarithmic modulus limit is the actual smooth filled hyperbolic volume, by the [marked action and boundary correction](../papers/casimir-source-asymptotics/README.md). The same exact half twist $\mathbf n=\boldsymbol\epsilon-2\mathbf p$ occurs only once. The proof uses no separately summed infinite sharp-cube series. Only a finite charge set is localized. The infinite tail is estimated on whole original intervals before any charge summation. ## 2. Basic bounds, endpoint identities, and parameter choices The local packet and real concavity bound near zero, together with (H2) outside a smaller fixed cube, imply $$ \sup_{\boldsymbol\delta\ \mathrm{real}}|C_N(\boldsymbol\delta)| \leq e^{N(\Phi_D+e_N)},\qquad e_N\longrightarrow0.\tag{5} $$ Polynomial Bernstein on each cosine variable yields, for any fixed $T$, $$ |C_N(\boldsymbol\delta)| \leq\exp\!\left[N(\Phi_D+e_N)+2\pi d\sum_i|\operatorname{Im}\delta_i|\right], \qquad |\operatorname{Im}\delta_i|\leq T.\tag{6} $$ This is a bound for the whole shared polynomial; no factorwise positive-radius majorant is used. For source derivatives, apply Cauchy to (6) in the required variables. Gaussian derivatives are evaluated separately on REAL spectator coordinates, avoiding any unwanted large-twist exponential cost. If a source factor $Z$ is an arbitrary entire polynomial in the $\sigma_i$, its product with $\prod_i\sin(2\pi\delta_i)$ and the fixed Gaussian satisfies $$ \left.B\right|_{\delta_j=\pm1/2}=0,\qquad \left.\partial_j B\right|_{\delta_j=1/2} =\left.\partial_j B\right|_{\delta_j=-1/2}.\tag{7} $$ The first derivative is solely the derivative of the sine: the two cosines are both $-1$, the spectral argument is $2$ at both ends, and the Gaussian endpoint value is $e^{\pi iNn_j/4}$. These facts remain true after arbitrary derivatives in other variables, including when one different coordinate is held complex. Thus three integrations by parts give exactly $$ \begin{aligned} \int_{-1/2}^{1/2}B e^{2\pi iN\ell_j\delta_j}\,d\delta_j =(2\pi iN\ell_j)^{-3}\biggl\{ &\left[\partial_j^2B e^{2\pi iN\ell_j\delta_j}\right]_{-1/2}^{1/2}\\ &-\int_{-1/2}^{1/2}\partial_j^3B e^{2\pi iN\ell_j\delta_j}\,d\delta_j \biggr\}. \end{aligned}\tag{8} $$ The second-derivative endpoint difference is retained. Repeating (8) over any spectator subset gives at most $3^{R-1}$ boundary/integral terms. Fixed source Cauchy bounds and real Gaussian derivatives cost at most $C_{\mathbf n}N^3$ per differentiated variable; these powers cancel the $N^3$ denominators. After the actual charge factors, every spectator coordinate supplies $|\ell_j|^{-2}$. Choose a small fixed outer cube $K_B=[-B,B]^R$ inside (H1). Choose $a>0$ much smaller than $B$ so the localized contribution theorem applies uniformly for all positive charges $\ell_i/|n_i|\leq a$. Next choose $0<b<a/4$, with $K_b$ inside the same chart. All these constants depend only on $D$. Below $n_0$ will be enlarged finitely many times, independently of ratios among the $|n_i|$. ## 3. The infinite far-charge union is exponentially small Use (H2) at $\eta=1/4$. Choose $\tau>0$ sufficiently small that the source and all required spectator derivatives have a strict bound $e^{N(\Phi_D-\gamma_e)}$ at $$ \delta_i=\pm\frac12+iv,\qquad 0\leq v\leq\tau. $$ with every other coordinate real or in a fixed Cauchy neighborhood of radius $\tau$. This uses the separated endpoint coordinate, regardless of the other real coordinates. Shrink $\tau$ and $\gamma_e$ once if needed. For a positive far charge $\ell_i$, shift its whole interval upwards by $i\tau$, keeping all other integrations on their whole real intervals. Write $$ B_i(z;\boldsymbol\delta_{\mathrm{other}}) =\sin(2\pi z)e^{\pi i n_iNz^2}C_N(z,\boldsymbol\delta_{\mathrm{other}}). $$ The exact pair of endpoint currents is $$ \begin{aligned} B_i(1/2+iv)-B_i(-1/2+iv) ={}&2i\sinh(2\pi v)\sinh(\pi n_iNv)\\ &\quad\times e^{\pi i n_iN(1/4-v^2)} C_N(1/2+iv,\boldsymbol\delta_{\mathrm{other}}). \end{aligned}\tag{9} $$ The other sine/Gaussian factors remain outside this equality. Multiplying the actual Fourier character leaves the endpoint parity $(-1)^{\ell_i}$. Its modulus is one. Both vertical sides were retained; the paired factor vanishes quadratically at $v=0$. For the paired vertical contribution, apply (8) in every spectator coordinate. The strict endpoint strip bound and source Cauchy estimates then give, after all original charge weights, an upper bound $$ C_{\mathbf n}|n_i|N\ell_i\,e^{N(\Phi_D-\gamma_e)} \left(\prod_{j\ne i}|\ell_j|^{-2}\right) \int_0^\tau v^2 e^{-2\pi N(\ell_i-|n_i|/2)v}\,dv.\tag{10} $$ Here $|\sinh(2\pi v)\sinh(\pi n_iNv)|\leq C|n_i|Nv^2e^{\pi|n_i|Nv}$. No oscillatory-sine substitution is made. For $\ell_i>|n_i|/2+D$, with $D\geq1$, the integral is at most $C/[N^3(\ell_i-|n_i|/2)^3]$. Consequently summing (10) over this far coordinate and all nonzero spectator charges is bounded by a polynomial factor times $e^{N(\Phi_D-\gamma_e)}$. The exact estimate $$ \sum_{\ell>M}\frac{\ell}{(\ell-|n|/2)^3} \leq C\left[D^{-1}+(|n|+1)D^{-2}\right].\tag{11} $$ makes the summability explicit. Constants may depend on the fixed $\mathbf n$. For the upper horizontal contribution, apply the same spectator integrations by parts. Source Cauchy from (6), in a fixed radius-$\tau$ neighborhood of the spectators, has exponential cost at most $2\pi R\tau N$. The shifted sine is bounded, while the bad-coordinate Gaussian and Fourier factors cost exactly at most $$ e^{\pi|n_i|N\tau-2\pi\ell_iN\tau}. $$ Thus the weighted horizontal contribution is bounded by $$ C_{\mathbf n}\ell_i\left(\prod_{j\ne i}|\ell_j|^{-2}\right) \exp\!\left\{N\left[\Phi_D+e_N+2\pi R\tau -2\pi\tau(\ell_i-|n_i|/2)\right]\right\}.\tag{12} $$ Choose a fixed $D$ large enough that $2\pi\tau D>2\pi R\tau+2\gamma_e$, and set $$ M_i=\left\lceil\frac{|n_i|}{2}+D\right\rceil.\tag{13} $$ The geometric tail of $\ell_i$ times (12) is exponentially bounded by $\Phi_D-\gamma_e$ after a harmless decrease of $\gamma_e$ and all large N. Both signs of the far charge obey the same estimate, either by downward shifts or the exact separate-evenness/reflection identity. Therefore, for some fixed $\gamma_\infty>0$, $$ \sum_{\substack{\boldsymbol\ell\in(\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\})^R\\ \exists i:\ |\ell_i|>M_i}} \left|\mathcal I_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}^{\mathrm{cross}}\right| \leq C_{\mathbf n}\operatorname{poly}(N)e^{N(\Phi_D-\gamma_\infty)}.\tag{14} $$ Here $\mathcal I_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}^{\mathrm{cross}}$ denotes the full weighted charge term in (1). Use the union bound over $i$; multiple far coordinates cause no issue. Every other coordinate was summed on its whole original domain after (8). Finite-N absolute convergence and the displayed dominating series justify all summations. No partial-far exterior with uncontrolled $R$ powers appears: the hypothesis used is the shared all-CROSS endpoint gap, valid for arbitrary real spectator spectra. This is the stronger input missing from the local operator-tail argument. ## 4. The finite charges outside the local scaled box The remaining set $0<|\ell_i|\leq M_i$ is finite after $\mathbf n$ is fixed. Suppose at least one coordinate $i$ has $|\ell_i|/|n_i|>a$. Reflect charge signs if necessary; the source is separately even, so absolute estimates are unchanged and assume $\ell_i>0$. On the original real domain outside $K_b$, (H2) gives rate $\Phi_D-\gamma_b$. The Gaussian and Fourier factors there have modulus one. No contour estimate is needed for this finite-charge portion. Inside $K_b$, shift only coordinate $i$ upward by $$ t_i=\frac{b}{|n_i|}.\tag{15} $$ All actual side currents of this small rectangle are retained. The packet and its real-action Taylor bound give, uniformly for $x$ in $K_b$ and $0\leq v\leq t_i$, $$ \operatorname{Re}A_N(x+iv e_i) \leq A_N(0)-c|x|^2+Cv^2.\tag{16} $$ Reality makes the first Taylor term purely imaginary. The Gaussian-plus-Fourier contribution in this coordinate is $$ -2\pi n_ix_iv-2\pi\ell_iv \leq-2\pi|n_i|(a-b)v\leq0.\tag{17} $$ On the horizontal translate, $v=t_i$, this costs at least $2\pi b(a-b)$, while the source error is at most $Cb^2/n_0^2$. On either vertical side $|x_i|=b$, (16) gives at least $cb^2$ loss, and (17) is nonpositive. Enlarge $n_0$ so $C/n_0^2$ is small. Then the horizontal and both sides have a fixed strict gap $\gamma_{\mathrm{bad}}>0$ below $\Phi_D$, independently of slope ratios. The packet's amplitudes contribute only polynomial factors. Together with the exterior $K_b$ bound, every such bounded bad charge is exponentially small. There are finitely many of them, so their whole sum obeys the same strict rate with a fixed-n prefactor. No infinite sharp-cube series has been split. ## 5. Finite local charges and the actual unit contribution It remains to consider the finite set with all $|\ell_i|/|n_i|\leq a$. On the real domain outside the larger $K_B$, (H2) gives a fixed loss $\gamma_B$. Inside $K_B$ apply the [localized original contour theorem](general_localized_unit_charge_filling_period.md) to the packet (2). It retains the exact side currents, the finite action, the Gaussian determinant branch and all sine/charge/parity factors. For positive charges the finite critical values satisfy $$ \operatorname{Re}S_{N,\mathbf1}-\operatorname{Re}S_{N,\boldsymbol\ell} \geq\sum_i\frac{C_i}{2n_i^2}(\ell_i^2-1).\tag{18} $$ All sign-unit choices contribute exactly equally. Every other charge in this finite local box has a positive fixed-n gap. The all-unit local contribution is precisely (4), with its $O_{\mathbf n}(N^{-1})$ relative error and nonzero limiting amplitude. The half twists are included once through $n_i=\epsilon_i-2p_i$. The limiting unit loss from $\Phi_D$ is $O_D(\sum_i|n_i|^{-2})$. Enlarge the diagram-dependent $n_0$ until this loss is less than one quarter of the minimum of $\gamma_\infty$, $\gamma_{\mathrm{bad}}$, $\gamma_b$ and $\gamma_B$. Also require $a n_0\geq1$ so the unit charge lies in the local box. Since $S_{N,\mathbf1}$ tends to its limiting value, all complementary bounds above are then exponentially smaller than $e^{N\operatorname{Re}S_{N,\mathbf1}}$ for large N. The smallest nonunit gap in (18) may depend on the fixed vector $\mathbf n$, but remains positive. Combining the finite local sector, bounded bad charges and the absolutely bounded infinite union proves (4). The exact critical volume identity identifies $$ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N}\log|I_{\mathrm{cross}}| =\operatorname{Vol}(\text{the actual smooth filled exterior}).\tag{19} $$ There is no uniform joint growing-twist/level error assertion: the twists are fixed first, while the threshold applies to arbitrary independent signs and magnitudes. ## 6. Scope of the transfer The argument proves a contribution theorem and all-charge control for the entire original all-CROSS spectral sector from the proved inputs (H1)-(H2). The original full numerator also contains moving one-sided sectors. The already established diagonal/CROSS and short-moving sector gaps can be retained separately, but they do not exhaust that remainder. Formula (19) is therefore not yet the general filled-knot invariant theorem. The crucial new analytic point is (14): a uniform shared endpoint gap makes partial far-charge tails summable without changing the actual source or creating infinite sharp-cut subseries. The old polynomial $+2$ operator bound alone would not control the spectator environment. No generic-$q$ normal theorem or unproved choice of a Lefschetz coefficient is used. ## Validation and scope The theorem evaluates the entire all-CROSS sector; the moving one-sided remainder of the original full numerator remains outside its conclusion.

title: Full original long filling from anchored shared-radius certificates
text: # Full original long filling from anchored shared-radius certificates theorem, 31 October 2026. At most $2R$ finite tests on shared face radii imply the full original independently long-filling volume theorem. These tests strictly extend balance at the complete packing for a fixed marked source. They are not asserted for every certified diagram. The proof makes no exchange of a maximum and an infimum and uses no coefficientwise LEFT comparison. ## 1. The original source and the finite certificate Fix an original marked flat plat $D$ with $R$ ordered ports $(x_e,b_e,c_e,y_e)$, the original adjacent protected MAIN faces $u,v$, and its labeled simple-white convex right-angled certificate for the complete augmented exterior $Y_D$. Write $\Phi_D=\operatorname{Vol}(Y_D)/(2\pi)$. Every ordinary face variable below is positive; the protected variables remain exactly zero. Each vector $L=(L_f)$ is shared across the entire original face incidence graph. These source variables are curvatures, not Euclidean disk radii. Let $Q(x,t,y)$ be the absolutely normalized [complete triangle action](../papers/casimir-source-asymptotics/README.md). Its homogeneity is $Q(\lambda x,\lambda t,\lambda y)=Q(x,t,y)+\tfrac12\log\lambda$. Define $$ \begin{aligned} X_e(L)&=Q(x_e,b_e,y_e)+Q(x_e,c_e,y_e),\\ H_e(L)&=\max\bigl(\{X_e(L)\}\cup\{\log b_e:b_e>0\}\cup\{\log c_e:c_e>0\}\bigr). \end{aligned}\tag{1} $$ The two possible anchored rates are $$ \begin{aligned} A_{e,\mathrm L}(L)&=\max\{\log c_e,Q(x_e,b_e,y_e)+\tfrac12\log c_e\},&&c_e>0,\\ A_{e,\mathrm R}(L)&=\max\{\log b_e,Q(x_e,c_e,y_e)+\tfrac12\log b_e\},&&b_e>0. \end{aligned}\tag{2} $$ The labels $\mathrm L,\mathrm R$ mean LEFT and RIGHT; $L_f$ is a shared face variable. If the overloaded middle is protected, that anchor is absent because the exact finite sector is zero. Set $$ \mathcal C_{e,s}(L)=A_{e,s}(L)+\sum_{f\ne e}H_f(L) -\sum_{j\ \mathrm{ordinary}}\log L_j.\tag{3} $$ Here $f\ne e$ in the first sum indexes ports. There are at most $2R$ surviving anchors. Suppose that for **each** surviving anchor there exists a fixed positive ordinary shared vector $L^{e,s}$, with the same protected zeros, satisfying $$ \mathcal C_{e,s}(L^{e,s})<\Phi_D.\tag{4} $$ Different anchors may use different whole vectors. Variables shared by several ports are never optimized independently inside one product. Equivalently, $\inf_L\mathcal C_{e,s}(L)<\Phi_D$; even if that infimum escapes, strict inequality supplies a finite positive witness. No minimizer is required. If no anchor survives, the full numerator is already all-CROSS and its existing theorem applies directly. Then every independently signed, fixed, sufficiently long filling vector in the original parity convention satisfies $$ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N}\log|K_N| =\operatorname{Vol}(\text{the actual filled exterior}).\tag{5} $$ For the prescribed knot parity, this is the actual knot invariant. The threshold depends on $D$ and the witnesses. There is no bound on ratios of the independent twist lengths, no joint growing-twist/level limit, and no uniformity in growing diagram size. ## 2. The source estimate at one shared vector The [global LEFT theorem](actual_global_left_weighted_spectral_envelope.md) proves (2) as a uniform weighted absolute upper rate at all face phases and all real spectral values. It retains both outside products, both parity partitions, and the shrinking final spectral cap. Reflection gives RIGHT. This is a value bound, not a coefficientwise inequality. The [exact cofactor interpolation theorem](../papers/filling-bounds/README.md), Section 8, bounds CROSS coefficientwise by $C\log^2(N+1)$ times its positive zero-spectral CROSS polynomial on the entire real spectral interval. That polynomial has weighted rate $X_e$, by the original determinant and half-block normalization. This includes a single protected outer face and protected middles. The outer faces cannot both be protected: their original edge is MATCHING, while the protected edge is MAIN. Thus $x_e+y_e>0$ at every witness. For $t>0$ and $x+y>0$, the actual triangle action satisfies $Q(x,t,y)>\tfrac12\log t$; its nonstrict version already follows from the endpoint monomial. Therefore $$ A_{e,\mathrm L}\le H_e,\qquad A_{e,\mathrm R}\le H_e.\tag{6} $$ For example, $Q_b+\tfrac12\log c\le Q_b+Q_c=X_e$. A protected overloaded middle gives an exactly zero sector, rather than an estimate involving $\log0$. Hence $H_f$ bounds CROSS, LEFT and RIGHT at every unanchored port on the same common face Cauchy torus. Take any exact path sector with a one-sided port, and choose one such port $(e,s)$ as anchor. Evaluate its entire original shared coefficient extraction at $L^{e,s}$, using $H_f$ at the other ports. The original ordinary target is $d=N-1$ at each ordinary face and zero at $u,v$. Replacing $d/N$ by $1$ changes the fixed-radius normalized logarithm by $O(N^{-1})$. If $\gamma$ is smaller than the minimum of the finitely many positive gaps in (4), all sufficiently large $N$ therefore satisfy $$ |Z_{\mathrm{sector}}(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_R)| \le e^{N(\Phi_D-\gamma)}\tag{7} $$ uniformly on the full real spectral cube. All original source scalars and normalization conventions remain those of the homogeneous theorem. Every phase stays inside the original local sector until the valid weighted absolute estimate is taken. The LEFT/CROSS/RIGHT partition is disjoint at both parities. At even $N=2m$, LEFT has $j\le m-1$, CROSS has $i\le m-1$ and $j\ge m$, and RIGHT has $i\ge m$. At odd $N=2m+1$, LEFT has $j\le m-1$, CROSS has $i\le m\le j$, and RIGHT has $i\ge m+1$; the central zero-step belongs to CROSS once. Their finite sum is the exact full numerator. There are at most $3^R-1$ sectors in full minus CROSS. Assigning an anchor to each proves (7) for that entire difference, with a smaller gap. Only $2R$ witness vectors are needed; no atomwise optimization is performed. The remainder has spectral degree at most $d$ in every variable. The cosine Bernstein bound for $\sigma_i=-2\cos(2\pi\delta_i)$ extends (7) to a fixed thin complex strip, at cost $\exp[2\pi d\sum_i|\operatorname{Im}\delta_i|]$. Choose its height below the fixed gap and shrink once more for source Cauchy derivatives. ## 3. The entire original Fourier period Apply the analytic argument in Section 4 of the [whole-domain sector theorem](actual_global_diagonal_spectral_sector_gap.md) to this remainder polynomial. That argument requires the whole-strip bound, polynomial cosine dependence, and the original sine and Gaussian factors; it does not require the polynomial itself to be diagonal. The original sine factor vanishes at each endpoint $\pm\tfrac12$, and its first derivative has equal endpoint values. The source cosine and Gaussian also have equal endpoint values. Three integrations by parts in each coordinate retain the second-derivative boundary current and give charge decay $\prod_i|\ell_i|^{-3}$. After the original weight $\prod_i|\ell_i|$, the whole-domain charge sum converges absolutely. Fixed-strip Cauchy bounds apply only to the source; Gaussian derivatives are taken on the real cube. Thus $$ |I_{\mathrm{full}}-I_{\mathrm{cross}}| \le C_D\prod_i(1+|n_i|)^3e^{N(\Phi_D-\gamma')}, \qquad\gamma'>0.\tag{8} $$ No infinite sharp-cube series has been split. Both endpoints and their actual currents, all nonzero charges, and the original framing phases are retained. The [whole all-CROSS theorem](general_all_cross_long_filling_volume.md) supplies a nonzero relative asymptotic for fixed independently signed sufficiently long $n_i=\epsilon_i-2p_i$. Its actual filled critical rate tends to $\Phi_D$, with deficit $O_D(\sum_i n_i^{-2})$. Choose every $|p_i|$ above the geometric and analytic thresholds and so that this deficit is less than $\gamma'/2$. Equation (8) is exponentially smaller than the original all-CROSS contribution, giving $$ \frac{I_{\mathrm{full}}}{I_{\mathrm{cross}}} =1+O_{\mathbf n}(e^{-c_{\mathbf n}N}).\tag{9} $$ The original normalizing characters and nonzero polynomial factors do not change the exponential limit. This proves (5). The argument uses spectral identities at the fixed root and imposes no extra generic-$q$ derivative hypothesis. [Complete-radius balance](../papers/planar-certificates/README.md) implies (4): use the geometric vector for every anchor. There $H_f=X_f$ at all ports and each surviving $A_{e,s}<X_e$. The following example shows that the converse fails for a fixed marked source. ## 4. An original flat plat failing complete-radius balance Use three standard adjacent cups and caps with the literal zero-based slot word $$ (1,3,2,1,3),\tag{10} $$ marking the first original top cap. Its actual ordered quartets are $$ (1,0,4,2),\ (2,0,5,3),\ (4,2,6,5),\ (1,4,0,6),\ (6,5,0,3).\tag{11} $$ The protected faces are $0,1$, and faces $2,\ldots,6$ each retain target $d$. The original compiler gives exactly these data. The ten triangles form a simple sphere with seven vertices and fifteen edges; the protected edge is MAIN. No general Morse-to-flat-plat adapter or isotopy is assumed. Let $z=\sqrt5$. An exact marked packing has lines $0:Y=0$, $1:Y=2$, and these disks, listed as horizontal center, vertical center, Euclidean radius: $$ \begin{aligned} 2&=(z-1,1,1),&6&=(1-z,1,1),\\ 3&=(0,(3-z)/2,(3-z)/2),\\ 4&=(0,(1+z)/2,(3-z)/2),\\ 5&=(0,1,z-2). \end{aligned}\tag{12} $$ Every graph edge other than the marked line-line contact is an exact tangency; every nonedge pair has strictly disjoint support. These are twenty finite pair checks. The marked lines touch at infinity. The [simple-sphere packing construction](actual_smoothed_source_capacity_blocks.md) supplies the actual labeled right-angled certificate, retaining the original matching and source pairings. The complete curvature vector is $$ L^{\mathrm{geom}}= \left(0,0,1,\frac{3+\sqrt5}{2},\frac{3+\sqrt5}{2},2+\sqrt5,1\right).\tag{13} $$ At the first and fourth ports, complete balance fails. The certified evaluation below gives $$ -0.10315<X_0(L^{\mathrm{geom}})-\log L^{\mathrm{geom}}_4<-0.10190.\tag{14} $$ The fourth port has the same value by reflection. Nevertheless, the following rational shared vectors satisfy (4). Each vector lists $(L_2,L_3,L_4,L_5,L_6)$; both protected values stay zero. | Anchor, with zero-based port index | Shared ordinary vector | Certified gap $\Phi_D-\mathcal C$ | |---|---|---| | 0 LEFT | $(3,4,3/2,5,1)$ | $>0.50$ | | 3 RIGHT | $(1,4,3/2,5,3)$ | $>0.50$ | | 1 LEFT | $(3/2,5,2,2,1)$ | $>0.71$ | | 4 RIGHT | $(1,5,2,2,3/2)$ | $>0.71$ | | 2 LEFT | $(2,6,2,18,1)$ | $>1.35$ | | 2 RIGHT | $(1,6,2,18,2)$ | $>1.35$ | These are all six surviving anchors. At the other four sides, the sector vanishes because its overloaded middle is protected. The conservative uniform gap $0.45$ certifies the full-source conclusion. In conventional braid indexing the word is $\sigma_2,\sigma_4,\sigma_3,\sigma_2,\sigma_4$. Choosing the first two exponents odd and the last three even makes one main component by the original cup/cap permutation. All five sufficiently long fixed parameters remain independent in magnitude and sign. Restricting every full exponent to a multiple of $3$ gives exact bridge number $3$ by the [Fox certificate](actual_fox_coloring_exact_plat_bridge.md); this congruence is not required for the volume statement. The example proves strict enlargement of the tests for a fixed marked source. It does not prove strict inclusion of the underlying unmarked knot families: another mark or presentation might satisfy the older balance test. ## 5. Rigorous interval evaluation No floating optimizer enters the certificate. For a nonnegative triangle $w$ with at least two positive entries, set $$ \begin{aligned} D&=\sqrt{w_1w_2+w_2w_3+w_3w_1},\qquad a_i=\arctan(w_i/D),\\ Q(w)&=\sum_{w_i>0}\left\{ \frac{\Lambda(a_i)+\Lambda(\pi/2-a_i)}\pi +\frac{a_i}\pi\log w_i\right\}. \end{aligned}\tag{15} $$ For a triangle with just one positive entry, use $Q(w)=\tfrac12\log w_i$ exactly. Formula (15) is the absolutely normalized original source identity, with $\sum_i a_i=\pi/2$. Hence $$ \Phi_D=\sum_eX_e(L^{\mathrm{geom}}) -\sum_{f=2}^6\log L_f^{\mathrm{geom}}.\tag{16} $$ The absolutely convergent Fourier series gives, for every real $a$, $$ \Lambda(a)=\frac12\sum_{n=1}^M\frac{\sin(2na)}{n^2}+r_M(a), \qquad |r_M(a)|\le\frac1{2M}.\tag{17} $$ The remainder bound follows from $\sum_{n>M}n^{-2}\le M^{-1}$. The [portable audit](../experiments/audit_general_anchored_shared_radius_filling_volume.py) evaluates the $M=1024$ sum with Arb at 192 bits, then adds this analytic tail ball. Square roots, $\pi$, arctangents, logarithms, maxima and all arithmetic retain enclosing balls. There is no unproved floating solve, rounded optimizer or numerical asymptotic limit. The [saved result](../experiments/general_anchored_shared_radius_filling_volume_results.json) encloses $\Phi_D$ in $(5.17452,5.18696)$, and every table entry has its asserted strictly positive lower bound. The packing checks use exact algebra in $\mathbb Q(\sqrt5)$. The checks cover five original ports, ten triangles, fifteen edges, twenty exact pair supports, two failed geometric balance tests, and six fixed rational whole-source witnesses. They certify this finite example and its quantitative inequalities; Sections 1–3 prove the general analytic transfer. ## 6. What remains open about general optimized capacities A fixed shared vector gives a valid Cauchy bound. In contrast, one cannot replace $\inf_L\max\{F_0(L),F_1(L)\}$ by $\max\{\inf_LF_0(L),\inf_LF_1(L)\}$. In particular, the LEFT value envelope is not an exact finite decomposition into an identity polynomial and a half-triangle polynomial. This distinction has a precise convex-dual form. Let $C(\alpha)$ be the original triangle coefficient entropy on $\alpha_x+\alpha_b+\alpha_y=\tfrac12$. The source identity is $$ Q(x,b,y)=\max_\alpha\bigl\{C(\alpha)+\alpha_x\log x+\alpha_b\log b+\alpha_y\log y\bigr\}. $$ Thus the concave entropy associated with the LEFT weighted envelope admits mixtures $$ q_c=1-\frac t2,\qquad(q_x,q_b,q_y)=t\alpha, \qquad\text{entropy}=tC(\alpha),\qquad0\le t\le1.\tag{18} $$ At $t=0$ this is pure $c$; at $t=1$ it is a triangle plus pure half-$c$. Protected input coordinates force their $\alpha$ entries to vanish. This is generally not the actual one-sided entropy $E$. Compact finite-dimensional convex duality converts the optimized envelope into this problem with concave local entropies, including limiting multipliers; it does not remove interior $t$. The unanchored $H$ additionally permits mixtures with complete CROSS and pure-$b$ atoms. The [identity forest reduction](actual_fejer_diagonal_identity_forest_reduction.md) controls the exact identity endpoint $t=0$. A [fixed-triangle capacity loss](actual_fixed_triangle_boundary_capacity_gap.md) controls $t=1$. At fractional $t$, the positive triangle has a changed row supply. Simply retaining its unscaled geometric angles changes the face stars by $(1-t)(\alpha-e_c/2)$, which need not vanish. The old hybrid representation therefore cannot be reused for an arbitrary mixture without further proof. The present theorem supplies a strictly broader sufficient certificate for marked sources; whether every original certified diagram passes an optimized sector or anchor test remains open. ## 7. Exact certificate checks The six rational certificates and twenty exact pair checks have smallest certified gap greater than $0.5023$. They use the specified quartets, first mark, exact packing, simple-sphere certificate and six surviving sides. Numerical optimization and finite asymptotic samples are not proof inputs.

title: Fixed-skeleton long fillings: the proved geometric quantifiers
status: Geometric long fillings; quantum threshold conditional
text: # Fixed-skeleton long fillings: the proved geometric quantifiers 30 October 2026. The new multi-cusp rigidity result and the existing geometric completion theorem have a useful joint corollary: an actual positive marked augmented-link certificate supplies ALL independently sufficiently long signed integral fillings, without requiring a quantum source branch to construct those geometric fillings. This is an assembly of the repo's established geometric arguments, not a claim of a new general hyperbolic Dehn filling theorem or of a volume-conjecture proof. ## 1. Fix the topology before either parameter limit Fix k>=2 and one ordered 2k-strand plat skeleton D. Its r designated crossing-circle disks, outside wires, upper/lower pairings, marked cut, and retained half twists epsilon_i in {0,+1,-1} are part of D. The corresponding filled word has exponents epsilon_i-2p_i. Combine adjacent powers of the same generator before calling the disks independent. Let Y_D be the actual drilled augmented exterior, with its primitive crossing-disk pairs (mu_i,lambda_i). Supply a positive complete ideal gluing certificate for this ACTUAL marked Y_D, as in [the general positive certificate](../papers/marked-fillings/README.md). A certified right-angled matching-graph realization is one existing way to supply it. The conclusion below applies at every fixed k and fixed r; neither k nor r is sent to infinity, and constants may depend on the entire fixed diagram D. A parity test decides whether filling all auxiliary circles gives knots: the fixed plat pairings composed with the permutation of the retained half-twist word must have one component. Full twists have trivial strand permutation. Consequently the number of surviving main components is independent of every p_i. Long twisting cannot repair a failed knot connectivity test. A 2k-plat gives a k-bridge presentation; minimal bridge number is not being asserted. ## 2. Geometric corollary with independent signed slopes There exists T_geom(D)<infinity with the following property. Choose ANY subset I of the r auxiliary cusps and ANY fixed signed integer slopes p_i, i in I, satisfying |p_i|>T_geom(D) for every i in I. Fill precisely those cusps along the original primitive curves mu_i+p_i lambda_i. Then the actual filled exterior has a positively oriented complete finite-volume hyperbolic metric. All main cusps and all auxiliary cusps outside I remain complete. There is no common-sign or slope-comparability condition. One threshold works for every subset. The empty subset recovers the supplied complete augmented geometry. Here is the direct proof, including the existence step that the older completion theorem did not assert on its own. By [multi-cusp marked rigidity](../papers/marked-fillings/README.md), with main meridian logs fixed to zero, the auxiliary PROJECTIVE meridian logs U=(U_1,...,U_r) are holomorphic coordinates on the decorated geometric germ. The actual preferred longitude logs obey V_i(U)=U_i t_i(U), t_i(0)=tau_i, Im tau_i>0. (1) This divisibility follows from the exact commuting-similarity identity, not a guessed source potential. Choose a sufficiently small geometric neighborhood where all t_i are nonzero and where the framed representations lie in the fixed neighborhood required by the existing [geometric completion theorem](general_source_regulator_hyperbolic_equality.md). Normalize a developed triple to obtain a bounded holomorphic representative of the framed family there. Introduce complex parameters e_i and solve V_i(U)+e_i U_i=-2pi i e_i, i=1,...,r. (2) At (U,e)=(0,0) the U-Jacobian is diag(tau_i), hence invertible. The holomorphic implicit-function theorem gives one solution U(e) in a fixed polydisk around zero. Shrink that polydisk so the framed family stays in the above completion neighborhood and |t_i(U(e))+e_i|>=c_D>0. Using (1), equation (2) becomes the exact coordinatewise identity U_i(e)=-2pi i e_i/[t_i(U(e))+e_i]. (3) In particular |U_i(e)|<=2pi|e_i|/c_D, even when the e_i have arbitrarily unequal magnitudes. If e_i=0, then U_i=V_i=0 EXACTLY. That cusp is unfilled and parabolic; it has not been assigned a filling coefficient p_i=0. Now put e_i=1/p_i for i in I and e_i=0 otherwise. For sufficiently large independently signed |p_i| this is in the same polydisk and (2) gives the ACTUAL small-log equations U_i+p_i V_i=-2pi i, i in I. (4) The curve mu_i+p_i lambda_i is primitive because its meridian coefficient is one. Equation (4) has unit charge, with its original orientation. All unfilled groups are parabolic and nontrivial nearby. These are precisely the inherited hypotheses of the geometric completion theorem: actual nearby framed representation, correct primitive marking, parabolic unfilled ends, and unit-charge filling logarithms. That theorem constructs the complete smooth metric on the correctly marked filled topology. This proves the corollary. The argument makes no rational-surgery quantum claim. Retained half twists belong to Y_D and its own primitive collar. A hidden half-integer slope on a different pure link is not substituted for (4). ## 3. The strongest honest general volume statement is still conditional For this SAME D, suppose the original mixed-color marked source satisfies all hypotheses of [the general original-source long-filling transfer](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/general_original_source_long_filling_transfer.md): an exact analytic color packet, uniform complex asymptotic with nonzero leading density, the full complementary-color/alias/normal-current gap, and selection of the actual marked geometric action and its complete regulator anchor. Then that transfer theorem gives a threshold T_vol(D)>=T_geom(D) such that, for every FIXED signed vector p with all |p_i|>T_vol(D), lim_(N -> infinity) (2pi/N) log |K_N(K_D(p))| =Vol(S^3 minus K_D(p)). (5) Here the parity test in section 1 is assumed, and all auxiliary circles are filled. Every quantum level is included, both parities and composite levels. The order of quantifiers is for each fixed k and admissible fixed D, there exists T_vol(D), for every fixed signed long vector p, take the full sequence N -> infinity. The general quantum hypotheses have NOT yet been proved for every D. Thus T_geom(D) is established under the positive marked certificate, whereas existence of T_vol(D) for arbitrary certified D remains the active volume-conjecture target. The exact compiler, classical geometric critical scheme and local column amplitudes do not by themselves supply that missing full-source estimate or period coefficient. If only a nonzero analytic density germ is proved, rather than a unit or a controlled peripheral monomial times a unit, the [source-divisor extension](general_long_filling_source_divisor.md) allows an exceptional analytic divisor of slopes. Its density-one conclusion must not be restated as the all-long-slopes assertion (5). There is no assertion of uniformity when p depends on N. The transfer errors and their constants are proved with p fixed. Likewise no threshold depending ONLY on k follows from these arguments: bridge width bounds the number of simultaneous heads, while the number/order of boxes and all geometric and source constants remain part of D. This is a limitation of the proved quantifiers, not a proof that a universal k-only threshold cannot exist within a more restrictive certified class. ## 4. What long twisting does and does not provide Given the positive marked base certificate, long integral twists provide the hyperbolic filled geometry by section 2. They preserve the already fixed knot/link connectivity. They do not imply the base certificate: Y_D is independent of p, as are its cusp labels, essential crossing disks and actual cut topology. Nor does hyperbolicity of a filled knot imply that every chosen augmented presentation has a hyperbolic base. There is an elementary obstruction to using raw crossing counts in place of essential marked disks. Two adjacent same-pair blocks can satisfy R^(2p) R^(-2p+2c)=R^(2c) with fixed c while both apparent twist counts grow. This identity holds in the original source, with its Cartan factor and marked closure. It motivates merging redundant regions and certifying the drilled topology; it does not disprove a uniform threshold inside the certified essential class. The present target is therefore broad but precise: every fixed certified essential augmented 2k-plat skeleton, for every k>=2, with the required parity and independently long signed full twists. It is not a claim that every k-bridge knot already lies in that long-twist class, nor that the full volume conjecture for that class has now been proved. The geometric threshold assumes the marked positive certificate. The quantum threshold also requires the stated source estimates.

title: The general long-twist target at arbitrary fixed plat width
text: # The general long-twist target at arbitrary fixed plat width 31 October 2026 update. The target remains arbitrary fixed k>=2 and independently sufficiently long FIXED signed twists, with the knots and slopes fixed before the quantum level tends to infinity. It remains a CONJECTURE for a general essential hyperbolic augmented skeleton. The latest [endpoint theorem](general_fejer_endpoint_source_volume.md) proves the actual augmented volume for the full positive numerator, with [odd regularization](actual_fejer_odd_regularized_full_numerator.md) and a [unique geometric maximum](actual_fejer_unique_geometric_maximizer.md). This settles the positive endpoint optimization at every certified fixed width. The whole-period and conditional full-invariant results below now extend this endpoint calculation. The [full spectral numerator theorem](../papers/casimir-source-asymptotics/README.md) now proves a nonzero relative asymptotic on a fixed complex neighborhood of the geometric endpoint, including every spectral Hermite datum. Its ordinary-face cycle is the original Cauchy torus. The [absolute marked action](../papers/casimir-source-asymptotics/README.md) identifies the unit-charge filling critical value with the actual filled volume. The [local charge comparison](../papers/casimir-source-asymptotics/README.md) proves strict dominance of the all-unit charge among nearby positive integer charges, uniformly for independent signed twists with no ratio condition. These results hold under the supplied simple-white geometric certificate at arbitrary fixed plat width. The [localized original-period theorem](general_localized_unit_charge_filling_period.md) now deforms the actual restricted spectral contour to that saddle, retains its boundary currents, and proves its coefficient is nonzero. The finite local charge sector therefore has the actual filled volume as its normalized logarithmic growth rate, at both level parities. The [entire CROSS period theorem](general_all_cross_long_filling_volume.md) now controls every original Fourier charge and the whole spectral contour for the CROSS sector, with its actual filled-volume rate. The [complete-radius balance theorem](../papers/planar-certificates/README.md) also proves the FULL original invariant limit whenever the actual marked complete packing satisfies its finite test at every port. A sufficient [algebraic criterion](../papers/planar-certificates/README.md) is $$ (x+y+b)(x+y+c)\geq\max\{b^2,c^2\}. $$ The theorem permits every independently long fixed signed twist vector, with no slope-ratio condition. What remains is broad geometric coverage of this condition, or a bound for the macroscopic one-sided sectors when it fails. In particular, arbitrary supplied plat width or a numerical packing experiment does not by itself prove the desired family coverage. A separate generic-q normal estimate is unnecessary for this exact fixed-root route; see the [scope audit](fixed_root_direct_power_scope.md). The older mixed-color route and its conditions are preserved below as alternative approaches. The [one-end layer theorem](general_one_end_layer_long_filling_volume.md) now proves actual balance for a family at EVERY fixed k>=2, with 3k-3 independently long signed twist regions. An exact packing recurrence and convex comparison prove its curvature bound uniformly. The [Fox certificate](actual_fox_coloring_exact_plat_bridge.md) gives subfamilies of minimal bridge number exactly k. This establishes genuinely unbounded bridge complexity at every k>=2, but not every k-bridge diagram. The earlier reduced-layer family remains separately recorded with its original k>=4 scope. There is now a whole-source intermediate theorem: the [original signed augmented source](general_signed_augmented_source_volume.md) has limit equal to the actual complete volume for every fixed connected plat with the stated labeled right-angled certificate and any retained half-twist pattern. Both parities and composite levels are included. This is an augmented-LINK theorem, including patterns whose main strands form one component; it is not yet the general long-filled knot theorem. The proof uses the [exact positive face coefficient](../papers/filling-bounds/README.md), its [global torus saddle](actual_positive_face_coefficient_saddle.md), the [uniform all-channel bound](actual_positive_face_channel_rate.md), and the [absolute facet-coning volume](actual_original_boundary_stationary_character.md). The signed extension derives a uniform relative folded Gaussian from the original continuants and sums the actual phases to a nonzero leading coefficient. All original factors and the primitive grid measure remain. The [fixed complex complete-core theorem](../papers/casimir-source-asymptotics/README.md) now supplies a nonzero asymptotic on a fixed neighborhood in EXTERNAL crossing-circle colors, for the exact complete-image term of reflection. The [marked geometric assembly](actual_complete_core_geometric_deformation.md) now identifies its limiting action, including at the zero faces, with the actual geometric regulator and its complex boundary correction. The [whole-source untwisted corridor](general_untwisted_mixed_source_volume_corridor.md) now transfers this volume identity to the original mixed source when any chosen set of untwisted ports varies near completeness. The [homogeneous source theorem](../papers/filling-bounds/README.md) now gives the exact original coefficient for all Casimir coupons and a JOINT signed/unsigned corridor under finite shared-radius certificates, including disconnected subsets. Existence of such signed certificates for a general class and the combined far-color bound remain open. The current dependency map is in the [frontier chapter](../book/chapters/frontier.md). The older source, operator, Fourier and torsor tools are preserved below with their own scopes. They are not an assertion that the general filling inputs have now been proved. ## 1. Quantifiers and the actual diagram Fix k>=2 and an ordered 2k-strand plat diagram with r designated two-strand twist boxes. Every crossing belongs to one of the boxes; all other wires, cups and caps are those of this fixed diagram. For example its braid word can be written beta(p)=sigma_(i_1)^(epsilon_1-2p_1) ... sigma_(i_r)^(epsilon_r-2p_r), epsilon_s in {0,+1,-1}, p_s in Z. The index word, box ordering, endpoint marking and epsilon are fixed. Adjacent powers of the same generator are combined before treating their twist parameters as independent. The fixed upper and lower pairings together with the permutation of the epsilon word must give one component. This is a finite permutation/matching test: adding a full twist does not change it. Thus every p gives a knot with a k-bridge presentation, so b(K_D(p))<=k; equality is not asserted. Drill one actual crossing circle around each box, remove the full twists, and retain its specified half twist. Denote the resulting marked augmented exterior by Y_D. Require Y_D to be hyperbolic, with the actual primitive crossing-disk markings retained. This is a geometric hypothesis on the supplied diagram, not an assertion that every presentation of a hyperbolic knot has hyperbolic augmentation. **General long-twist conjecture.** For every such fixed diagram D there is T(D)<infinity such that, for every fixed integer vector p with all |p_s|>T(D), lim_(N->infinity) (2pi/N) log|K_N(K_D(p))| =Vol(S^3 minus K_D(p)). (1) Here N is the quantum level. Twist numbers are fixed BEFORE this limit. The conjecture includes both level parities and composite levels, arbitrary signed twist vectors, and no comparability condition on their magnitudes. It asks for the volume of the FILLED knot, not the complete drilled volume or a limit in which p grows with N. For a partial filling the analogous statement is about the remaining link exterior with its original single marked normalization. The quantifier is every fixed k and every admissible fixed skeleton; there is no proposed universal threshold depending on k alone. We use T(D) for the required twist length so that it cannot be confused with the quantum level N. A twist region here is a designated two-strand box with its essential crossing disk, not an arbitrary tangle with a large crossing count. Under an actual positive marked gluing certificate, the [geometric long-filling corollary](general_augmented_plat_long_filling_quantifiers.md) now proves a threshold T_geom(D) for complete hyperbolic geometry of every independently long signed filling. Existence of the quantum threshold T(D) in (1) is the remaining conjectural assertion for a general skeleton. These two thresholds must not be conflated. A [finite sufficient geometric criterion](general_simple_white_plat_class.md) is now available: the ACTUAL white cellulation of the flat plat is a simple triangulated sphere. The existing angle optimization and labeled cut construction then supply its complete right-angled geometry, with all prescribed half-twist patterns and primitive markings. This class has explicit examples at every fixed supplied width. It is a sufficient class for the geometric and endpoint results. Assertion (1) is now proved in its complete-radius balanced subclass; without that additional test it remains open. ## 2. Why twist length needs a diagram hypothesis Raw box counts do not measure geometric twisting. For the actual crossing operator, including its Cartan factor, R^(2p) R^(-2p+2c)=R^(2c). (2) Both displayed blocks can have arbitrarily many crossings while the diagram remains the fixed bounded-twist diagram on the right. The identity holds inside ANY 2k-strand source and before its marked cap. It is an exact algebraic cancellation, not an asymptotic example. Likewise a nugatory twist can change a presentation without adding an essential drilled cusp. Thus independent long parameters must refer to actual essential crossing disks. Certifying Y_D directly is a uniform way to impose this requirement without restricting k or assuming that a visually complicated plat is geometrically essential. ## 3. The exact reduction already works for every fixed k The all-input circle identity gives the original full-twist expansion on each pair of strands. Let A_(D,N)(h_1,...,h_r) be the actual augmented source with circle color j_s=N-h_s, including all its specified half twists, cups, caps, pivots and the exposed first cut. Then the [general source transfer](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/general_original_source_long_filling_transfer.md) has the exact identity K_N(K_D(p))=chi_N kappa^(-2 sum_s p_s) sum_(j_1,...,j_r=1)^N product_s beta_(j_s-1)^(-p_s) A_(D,N)(N-j). (3) The source A is defined before the displayed recorded outer factor chi_N; it is not normalized using the unknown answer. All repeated Casimir-root normals are part of beta. Multilinearity applies each substitution in its original operator order. Physical crossings at different boxes need not commute. Only the independent color-register functionals commute. Consequently the long-twist problem does not require a new surgery formula for each bridge number. The same exact filling map is already available. What is missing generally is control of its input A_D. There is also a direct polynomial form, supplied by the homogeneous source theorem. For N>=3 put d=N-1 and let f_(e,N,p)(Omega) be the ACTUAL root Casimir polynomial for the whole operator R^(epsilon_e-2p_e) in the original box, including its repeated-node Hermite data. If Z_(D,p,N) denotes the original marked contraction before its recorded exterior framing factor, then exactly Z_(D,p,N)=[prod_(ordinary faces f) L_f^d] prod_e H_(f_(e,N,p)) |_(L_u=L_v=0). (3a) Every local polynomial has degree d; the number of shared face variables depends only on the fixed skeleton. Thus (3a) is an exact polynomial form of the full source at arbitrary fixed k, including negative twists. The known exterior normalization is retained when passing from Z to K_N. This gives a second route for studying long twists directly at each box. No sharp long-power estimate for these kernels is being assumed: their coefficients are complex, and larger p does not by itself make their shared-face contraction positive. Nor is (3a) being called the eliminated knot A-polynomial. These whole-box kernels also compose without introducing an external circle color. For two Casimir polynomials f,g, exactly H_(fg)(x,b,c,y)=[z^d] H_f(x,b,z,y) H_g(x,z,c,y). (3b) Indeed the input index j of the left kernel contributes z^(d-j), while the output index j' of the right kernel contributes z^j'. Extraction forces j'=j and gives the original matrix composition. Thus arbitrary positive or negative twist powers admit a layered coefficient formula using only the literal R or R^-1 kernels, with all their scalar phases retained. This is an alternative finite presentation of the same source, not a new asymptotic estimate. The [direct-power theorem](actual_direct_long_power_source.md) retains the original phases and proves a limitation of the absolute-value spectral bound. The [crossing Casimir theorem](actual_crossing_casimir_torus.md) now solves the local classical transport uniformly in the twist power: on the generic spectral cover it is multiplication by lambda^n on a punctured norm torus, with a separate additive parabolic fiber. Its canonical Hamiltonian agrees with the exact full-Hermite quantum Gaussian. These facts hold independently of bridge width; they do not supply the remaining global coefficient estimate or an eliminated knot A-polynomial. The [physical meridian transport](actual_crossing_torus_meridian_transport.md) now gives a further width-independent algebraic result. Differentiating the original physical kernel, including its half powers and the outer head derivative, fixes the physical momentum as the reciprocal of the coefficient momentum. The resulting matrices obey the full signed Hurwitz relations, not merely conservation of their Casimir trace. After the literal cup/cap/marked constraints are imposed, every FULL regular critical point of the layered source defines a representation of the actual filled diagram group. This is a forward morphism on its specified regular open scheme; it is not a classification of critical points after setting protected faces to zero, nor a proof that the original coefficient cycle selects the geometric representation. The [full spectral total derivative](actual_spectral_total_derivative_source.md) and [Gaussian resolvent numerator](actual_gaussian_resolvent_numerator_and_cap.md) retain both semisimple and nilpotent data of every original pair Casimir. The numerator is an exact coherent transform of ALL physical colors; its positive path expansion can be sewn with the same shared face targets. The closing cap near spectral +2 is controlled at fixed twist power. The fixed complex shared numerator and entire CROSS spectral period are now proved. Complete-radius balance also controls the full one-sided remainder. Without that condition, its macroscopic sectors remain to be estimated. Long twisting alone does not damp both sides of a spectral contour. The [full positive endpoint theorem](general_fejer_endpoint_source_volume.md) now proves W_D=Vol(Y_D)/(2pi) for the original even numerator under the labeled right-angled certificate, at every fixed plat width. Its full local support gives one unrestricted incidence-flow polytope; the older single-level support test remains useful only for fixed branch patterns. The [odd regularization](actual_fejer_odd_regularized_full_numerator.md) has the same rate and supplies explicit bounds for fixed spectral jets. The [unique-maximizer theorem](actual_fejer_unique_geometric_maximizer.md) identifies the only endpoint maximum with the original marked complete geometry and gives a strict gap for its complement, including the entire one-sided remainder. These are positive-source and spectral statements. The localized spectral Gaussian unit-charge contribution is now proved. The entire CROSS period and balanced full remainder are now controlled as well; unrestricted geometric coverage remains the gap. ## 4. Remaining inputs and preserved alternative routes For the current direct fixed-root route, the full local numerator packet, its contributing ordinary-face saddle and the marked filled critical value are proved by the results linked at the start. The whole-CROSS period and full balanced-class limit are also proved. The remaining input is broad coverage of balance or a more general full remainder estimate. The mixed-color requirements in this section concern the older alternative route and must not be added as prerequisites to the direct one. **Full mixed-color quantum source.** The complete-image term already has its exact holomorphic packet and a uniform complex asymptotic. The original mixed source agrees with it exponentially accurately on the physical integer corridor for all untwisted varied ports, and for joint signed/unsigned ports satisfying the finite certificates below. What remains generally is to establish those certificates (or stronger phase-preserving estimates), and to bound the combined original source on the ENTIRE physical color complement. This must include opposite-end aliases, their exact cancellations, and the normal currents used by the filling transform. The marked multiport Chebyshev/Parseval packet is exact at every fixed k, but its physical source-to-coefficient energy is still the quantity to estimate. For clarity, the new near-complete sufficient condition is finite and independent of the quantum level. For every nonempty reflected subset S of the varied ports, choose ONE shared positive weight per original face such that C_S(l)=sum_(e notin S) [F(x_e,b_e,y_e)+F(x_e,c_e,y_e)] +sum_(e in S,epsilon_e!=0) G(b_e,x_e,y_e,c_e) +sum_(e in S,epsilon_e=0) log max(b_e,c_e) -sum_(ordinary faces f) log l_f < Vol(Y_D)/(2pi). Here F is the complete triangle potential and G the exact crossing coefficient-magnitude potential defined in the [homogeneous source theorem](../papers/filling-bounds/README.md). Different subsets may use different weights. The finite strict margins give one fixed color corridor for ALL subsets, including disconnected ones, at arbitrary fixed bridge width. Establishing these inequalities for a structural class of diagrams is a general theorem problem; it does not require a separate quantum asymptotic for each knot. Their validity alone still does not control the far-color complement. **Actual geometry.** Supply the marked complete augmented exterior and its absolute volume anchor. A positive ideal gluing certificate on a triangulation of the actual exterior is one sufficient route. Another starts from its actual disk/projection cut: the cubic graph of shaded triangles and its distinguished crossing-circle matching describe the whole polyhedron, and a positive right-angled realization supplies the complete metric. A triangulation of an unrelated manifold or a numerically matching volume does not identify this labeled topology. The [general marked gluing certificate](../papers/marked-fillings/README.md) proves the geometric implication directly. It also proves the Casson--Rivin equivalence with an interior critical point of the actual angle-volume function, whose unique maximum is Vol(Y_D). Positive phases and positive multiplier variables give a finite algebraic certificate; the selected optimum has algebraic shapes. None of these geometric facts implies the quantum packet estimate. **Same selected action.** Prove that the critical source action is the calibrated primitive on the ACTUAL peripheral branch, retaining the selected square roots and logarithms. The required equations are G=2pi i phi, U_s=-2pi i x_s, V_s=-2 partial_s phi, Im G(0)=Vol(Y_D). (4) The filled source saddle then gives the primitive equation U_s+p_s V_s=-2pi i. The existing geometric completion theorem constructs the actual smooth filled metric and identifies its volume with the boundary-corrected source action. It is this last equality, not an unnamed source volume, that yields the right side of (1). The already proved long-filling transfer is independent of k once these inputs are available. It must not be cited as having supplied them for an arbitrary plat. The new [critical-scheme equivalence](actual_augmented_plat_critical_scheme.md) and [marked multi-cusp rigidity](../papers/marked-fillings/README.md) now supply a nearby geometric stationary branch under an actual positive gluing certificate. The only magnetic Hessian null directions are the two framing directions; a transverse slice removes them. The branch has the actual peripheral differential and absolute volume anchor. The quantum statement still requires that the original finite source select and contribute to this branch. The new [actual local character map](actual_augmented_plat_local_critical_character_map.md) proves the primitive differential on any correctly marked stationary branch. The [absolute endpoint regulator theorem](actual_augmented_plat_endpoint_regulator.md) proves the complete-volume anchor at a regular correctly marked geometric critical point. A [generic framing theorem](actual_augmented_plat_regular_geometric_phase_chart.md) supplies a regular unfolded geometric candidate, but does not select its physical logarithmic sheet or a contributing quantum cycle. Thus the identities in (4) have a general classical proof with these hypotheses. Under the stronger labeled right-angled certificate the complete-image source realization is now proved; its extension to the full mixed source outside the proved corridors remains part of the quantum problem. The [actual channel Hessian](actual_augmented_plat_channel_hessian.md) also has a general primitive normalization: H_(xi_i,xi_j) is -delta_ij 4pi i/tau_i, and the channel/magnetic mixed block vanishes. Its negative real part gives a local channel elimination at the geometric endpoint, while holding the magnetic variables as parameters. It supplies no nonzero cycle coefficient or magnetic asymptotic. ## 5. Preserved operator and Fourier routes The [complete source compiler](actual_augmented_plat_phase_compiler.md) and [all-color compiler](actual_mixed_augmented_plat_compiler.md) give explicit finite factorial sums, phases and generic confluence normals for every fixed plat. Their inverse measures retain their exponential profiles. No unknown local recoupling inverse remains. The [entire core function](actual_augmented_plat_entire_core_color_packet.md) also supplies an exact separately-even finite Fourier interpolation, including the odd endpoint. It does not supply a uniform complex asymptotic. If the required nonzero analytic corridor packet exists, its periodicity mirrors the same rate near the opposite cube face. The actual physical alias split therefore matters for the global gap. For each actual local q-Hahn column, the [negative-root theorem](actual_q_hahn_negative_root_source_polynomial.md) now proves a canonical slit-plane logarithm, and the [complex-action theorem](actual_q_hahn_selected_complex_action.md) proves its actual leading action on the physical Fourier arc. The [uniform amplitude theorem](actual_q_hahn_uniform_complex_amplitude.md) adds a nonzero prefactor with relative error O(1/N). The [magnetic corridor theorem](actual_q_hahn_magnetic_complex_corridor.md) continues the actual finite kernel in one magnetic variable while the pair degree and channel stay real and discrete. The subsequent [joint determinant](actual_q_hahn_joint_accretive_determinant.md) and [joint amplitude theorem](actual_q_hahn_joint_complex_amplitude.md) now continue pair degree and magnetic coordinate together on a fixed central domain, including folded channels, with an explicit selected local sheet. The channel remains an integer. The [common-framing criterion](actual_augmented_plat_physical_framing_criterion.md) states finite strict inequalities for simultaneous use on a plat; the [right-angled obstruction](actual_right_angled_selected_framing_obstruction.md) now proves that an all-central selected frame cannot exist for the actual certified right-angled cut. Generic geometric strip flags localize the weaker strict physical-support failures to exactly TWO factors, for arbitrary bridge width. Those facets can be prescribed, including the pair adjacent to the original marked physical edge. The [full physical packet](actual_q_hahn_full_physical_complex_packet.md) and [selected-factor corollary](actual_augmented_plat_selected_factor_localization.md) now put EVERY other ordinary factor in its actual selected physical packet, with no central-support hypothesis. The two exceptions can instead be placed together at one crossing-circle matching edge. The [selected local certificate](actual_augmented_plat_selected_local_certificate.md) remains a conditional local theorem; it does not establish a whole-source cycle or sum estimate. The [small-channel generic-normal estimate](actual_q_hahn_small_channel_generic_normals.md) and [exact partner collision](actual_q_hahn_partner_normal_collision.md) retain the original derivatives. The latter exposes additional individual normal poles, so a full-domain paired-normal estimate cannot be assumed. The [physical paired-normal theorem](actual_q_hahn_physical_partner_normal_bound.md) does prove polynomial relative cost on the whole complete physical grid, retaining the actual large partner and both parities. The [complex near-fold theorem](actual_q_hahn_near_fold_complex_partner_bound.md) now supplies subexponential relative cost on a fixed complex compact when (l-j) log N=o(N). A fixed nonzero scaled channel shift and a whole-source asymptotic remain open. Every fixed generic q jet of all physical columns and completed divided pairs is also controlled by the [physical generic-jet theorem](actual_q_hahn_physical_generic_jet_bound.md). Its forward/backward proof does not supply a completed boundary tensor norm. The full physical packet extends the complex near-fold bound to all fixed physical compacts, still with a shrinking scaled channel window. These local results are not a whole-source asymptotic. Outside the specified marked domain the endpoint quadratic has monodromy, so an unspecified analytic continuation alone cannot identify the selected geometric root. A controlled simultaneous continuation and a global cycle estimate remain necessary. Choosing the exceptional pair at a crossing-circle matching edge also gives the [exact marked four-port rewrite](actual_matching_edge_marked_four_port_block.md) of the COMPLETE-circle source. Its original row measure cancels the exponential factorial gauge, and the [positive scalar theorem](actual_matching_edge_racah_positive_scalar.md) controls every recoupling target and fixed generic jet. The [completed-projector formula](actual_matching_edge_completed_projector_block.md) also cancels the target scalar gauge and combines the collision pairs before taking the first normal, retaining their nilpotent part. The remaining native projector/complement costs are explicit but not yet sharply bounded by the geometric action. This is not the general mixed-color packet required for fixed long fillings. The [native-projector energy theorem](actual_matching_edge_native_projector_energy.md) now bounds every fixed generic operator derivative by a polynomial times its explicit magnetic energy, uniformly at both parities and all physical degrees. A simple midpoint channel proves that energy can itself be exponential. The remaining joint variational estimate must keep the actual shared wire variables and these energy terms; independent local maxima do not supply it. The [full folded boundary rate](actual_matching_edge_magnetic_energy_profile.md) is now computed by exact Plancherel and the actual selected endpoint polynomial. It remains valid in [all shrinking real fold windows](actual_matching_edge_shrinking_fold_native_energy.md). For arbitrary fixed skeletons, the [shared-cycle compiler](actual_matching_graph_shared_cycle_fourier_compiler.md) gives an exact bounded-flow source with coupled Fourier congruences and the original one-unit mark. Its [positive coefficients](actual_q_hahn_fourier_coefficient_variational.md) have a uniform interior variational rate. These source reductions retain every shared label and phase. They do not supply the general mixed-color packet, sharp joint geometric estimate or lower bound needed for the fixed-long-filling theorem. The [explicit positive partition](actual_matching_graph_positive_fourier_partition.md) now gives a polynomial-loss Cauchy upper bound retaining every shared flow and Fourier charge. Its sharp rate is not yet the hyperbolic volume: the [conditional radial-frame obstruction](actual_positive_fourier_radial_geometric_obstruction.md) prevents one proposed all-ordinary geometric reconstruction, without proving a numerical gap. The exact coherent source and the retained exceptional matching block remain the objects to estimate. The [full graph identity](general_matching_graph_full_normal_source.md) puts all folded labels and normals on the actual matching graph. The [reflection-double identity](actual_planar_three_port_reflection_double.md) removes the final gluing cancellation for specified three-port doubles, retaining the full source. Neither identity already bounds the internally coherent half-packets for arbitrary graphs. The [matching-graph geometry](../papers/marked-fillings/README.md) constructs the actual complete complement and primitive markings from a labeled positive right-angled certificate. It also constructs a positive ideal triangulation. The [geometric endpoint theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_augmented_plat_geometric_channel_endpoint.md) locates the complete disk character at c=-2, the folded-channel endpoint, and retains its marked peripheral square root. This is necessary geometric information, not a proof of quantum selection. The [endpoint phase calculation](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_central_endpoint_magnetic_phase_obstruction.md) also shows that a universal separate-leg positive normalization already fails at N=3. It leaves coherent resummation available. The [source-divisor extension](general_long_filling_source_divisor.md) allows a nonzero analytic source-density germ to vanish at the complete point. With the other packet, gap and geometric hypotheses proved, it yields the filling equality away from an analytic exceptional divisor, including density one of long slopes in each signed box. A peripheral monomial times a unit gives EVERY independently long signed slope. The general nonzero-germ version does not by itself prove the all-slopes conjecture (1). These results remove finite-source and geometric ambiguities. The principal remaining theorem is still a coherent asymptotic with the required global gap and the actual selected geometric period. The [arbitrary-width Conway extension](../papers/newton-calculus/README.md) is retained as an application and a calibration of these interfaces. It does not settle (1) for all k-bridge diagrams. The full cube source, which lies beyond that grammar, remains one useful branching test, not the definition of the general target. ## 6. Literature coverage only Purcell's [highly twisted volume paper](https://research.monash.edu/en/publications/volumes-of-highly-twisted-knots-and-links/) states hyperbolicity and geometric volume bounds under diagrammatic hypotheses; those are not an original Kashaev volume-limit theorem. Van der Veen's [augmented KTG paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/0805.0094) states a volume conjecture result for its augmented knotted trivalent graphs and a containing-link corollary. Its abstract does not assert (1) for all independently long fillings of arbitrary fixed plats. These are coverage observations, not imported proofs or an exhaustive novelty claim. The definitions and source normalizations must still be compared before identifying any covered family. A further primary-statement coverage check on 31 October 2026 distinguishes three nearby claims. [Giambrone](https://arxiv.org/abs/1310.8414v3) states coarse volume bounds for certain plat closures via stable Jones coefficients. [Lee](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.09903v2) takes the twist parameters to infinity to obtain a limiting skein element before studying its root-of-unity growth. [Shen](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11839v3) states long fixed signed filling results for SO(3) Turaev-Viro and WRT invariants of fundamental shadow-link fillings along odd levels. These abstract statements have different invariants or quantifiers from the full Kashaev knot limit here. This checks stated coverage only: no proof correctness, equivalence of invariants, or exhaustive novelty conclusion is inferred, and no proof technique from these papers is used above.

title: An endpoint-conditioned energy for the original shared source
status: Explicit joint shared-flow criterion; universal comparison open
text: # An endpoint-conditioned energy for the original shared source 31 October 2026. **Conditional general theorem.** The finite shared-coefficient identities and local coefficient bounds below are proved. Sections 5–6 give an explicit compact shared-flow criterion: keep the endpoint entropy and relative-energy bound on the **same** flow, optionally taking their minimum with the older one-sided envelope. A strict score gap proves the full long-filling limit. The universal geometric inequality for that score remains open; no independent local norm or endpoint concentration supplies it. The universal question here has the stated flat-plat scope. Its extension to all matched-sphere Morse diagrams is false. The [absolute-source obstruction](research_absolute_source_cancellation_obstruction.md) gives a feasible flow on the original fifty-four-region example for which the combined score in (23) exceeds the augmented-volume rate by more than \(1/5\). The same example obstructs the joint criterion (19). It does not disprove their conditional implications or establish that this diagram belongs to the narrower flat-plat class. At one fixed spectral tuple, the exact absolute sum already has the excess through both parities; arbitrary positive diagonal Cauchy weights cannot remove it. ## 1.
