Actual coefficients and both parity supports Fix the original certified flat plat \(D\), with \(R\) coupons, degree \(d=N-1\), ordinary face targets \(d\), and two protected targets zero. Keep the [actual homogeneous source](../papers/filling-bounds/README.md) and its full polynomial resolvent numerator $$ V_N(\sigma)=\chi_N(\sigma)(\sigma-\Omega_N)^{-1}, \qquad \chi_N(\sigma)=2T_N(\sigma/2)+2. $$ The [positive reference at both parities](actual_fejer_odd_regularized_full_numerator.md) is $$ F_N= \begin{cases} -V_N(-2),&N\ \text{even},\\ V_N(-2)-N^{-2}\partial_\sigma V_N(-2),&N\ \text{odd}. \end{cases}\tag{1} $$ For a four-incidence exponent \(v=(v_x,v_b,v_c,v_y)\ge0\) with \(|v|=d\), define $$ p_N(v)=[x^{v_x}b^{v_b}c^{v_c}y^{v_y}]H_{F_N}, \qquad a_N(v;\sigma)=[x^{v_x}b^{v_b}c^{v_c}y^{v_y}]H_{V_N(\sigma)}. \tag{2} $$ The reference satisfies \(p_N(v)>0\) for every such exponent, at both parities. In particular none of the inverses below divides by zero. Protected targets remove every array with positive degree at a protected incidence; they are never replaced by positive marked radii. Let \(\Gamma_N\) be the exact original shared array set: an element \(\boldsymbol v=(v_e)\) satisfies all original face targets. Separate incidences retain their original quartet labels. The path endpoints are \(i=v_b\) and \(j=d-v_c\), so the original classes are determined by each monomial: $$ \begin{array}{c|c|c|c} &\mathrm{CROSS}&\mathrm{LEFT}&\mathrm{RIGHT}\\ \hline N=2m&v_b,v_c\le m-1&v_c\ge m&v_b\ge m\\ N=2m+1&v_b,v_c\le m&v_c\ge m+1&v_b\ge m+1 \end{array}\tag{3} $$ They are disjoint and exhaustive. The odd central zero-step monomial is CROSS in this convention. The odd reference derivative retains the same endpoints, so the same partition applies to \(F_N\). For a subset \(A_N\subseteq\Gamma_N\) specified by these supports, put $$ \begin{aligned} W(\boldsymbol v)&=\prod_e p_N(v_e),& \mathcal R(\boldsymbol v;\boldsymbol\sigma) &=\prod_e\frac{a_N(v_e;\sigma_e)}{p_N(v_e)},\\ Z_A&=\sum_{\boldsymbol v\in A_N}W(\boldsymbol v),& S_A(\boldsymbol\sigma) &=\sum_{\boldsymbol v\in A_N}W(\boldsymbol v) \mathcal R(\boldsymbol v;\boldsymbol\sigma). \end{aligned}\tag{4} $$ \(S_A\) is exactly the raw original shared numerator with this support restriction. There is no additional \(N^R\), pivot, or independently normalized face contraction. The sign-adjusted convention differs by a common unit sign and gives the same inequalities. The original external character and Fourier-period factors remain outside the numerator. ## 2. The finite shared Cauchy inequality Define $$ E_A(\boldsymbol\sigma) =\sum_{\boldsymbol v\in A_N}W(\boldsymbol v) |\mathcal R(\boldsymbol v;\boldsymbol\sigma)|^2 =\sum_{\boldsymbol v\in A_N} \prod_e\frac{|a_N(v_e;\sigma_e)|^2}{p_N(v_e)}. \tag{5} $$ Cauchy on this one shared array set proves $$ |S_A(\boldsymbol\sigma)|^2 \le Z_AE_A(\boldsymbol\sigma) \le Z_AE_{\Gamma_N}(\boldsymbol\sigma).\tag{6} $$ The full energy is a concrete positive shared coefficient: $$ \begin{aligned} E_{\Gamma_N}(\boldsymbol\sigma) &=[\text{original targets}]\prod_e K_N(\sigma_e;x_e,b_e,c_e,y_e),\\ K_N(\sigma;l)&=\sum_{|v|=d}\frac{|a_N(v;\sigma)|^2}{p_N(v)}l^v. \end{aligned}\tag{7} $$ Equation (7) by itself supplies no domination by the endpoint source. It retains every original face demand and does not replace extraction by a product of independent local norms. Equivalently, for \(Z=Z_{\Gamma_N}\) and \(\mu_N(\boldsymbol v)=W(\boldsymbol v)/Z\), $$ \frac{S_A}{Z}=\mathbb E_{\mu_N}[\mathcal R\,1_A],\qquad \frac{E_{\Gamma_N}}Z=\mathbb E_{\mu_N}[|\mathcal R|^2],\qquad \frac{|S_A|}Z \le\sqrt{\mu_N(A)\,\mathbb E_{\mu_N}[|\mathcal R|^2]}.\tag{8} $$ Endpoint concentration does not control an exponentially large ratio on a rare array. The new input is a second-moment bound on this same distribution. Shared face rescaling does not improve (6). Multiplying each reference coefficient by the same face monomials multiplies \(W\), on every feasible array, by the fixed scalar \(\prod_f L_f^d\). It scales \(Z_A\) and \(E_A\) reciprocally, leaving their product unchanged. ## 3. The sufficient rate and its filling consequence Write \(\Phi_D=\operatorname{Vol}(Y_D)/(2\pi)\). The [endpoint source theorem](general_fejer_endpoint_source_volume.md) gives \(N^{-1}\log Z\to\Phi_D\). Let \(\mathrm{NC}_N\) contain every array with at least one noncross port. Its [unique-maximizer concentration](actual_fejer_spectral_polydisk_complement.md) gives $$ \limsup_N\frac1N\log Z_{\mathrm{NC}} \le\Phi_D-\gamma_D,\qquad\gamma_D>0.\tag{9} $$ If this support is empty, its original remainder is zero. Otherwise a sufficient new estimate is $$ \limsup_N\frac1N\log \sup_{\boldsymbol\sigma\in[-2,2]^R}E_{\mathrm{NC}}(\boldsymbol\sigma) \le\Phi_D+\gamma_D-\varepsilon \quad\text{for some }\varepsilon>0.\tag{10} $$ Using the full energy in (10) is stronger. Equations (6) and (9) then give $$ \limsup_N\frac1N\log \sup_{\boldsymbol\sigma\in[-2,2]^R}|S_{\mathrm{NC}}(\boldsymbol\sigma)| \le\Phi_D-\frac{\varepsilon}{2}.\tag{11} $$ Thus an energy rate at most \(\Phi_D\) would suffice, but is not necessary: the endpoint mass gap leaves the additional budget \(\gamma_D\) in (10). For individual sectors with endpoint rate \(z_s\) and energy rate \(e_s\), the sufficient condition is \(z_s+e_s<2\Phi_D\). The two optimizations must retain their own shared constraints; their maximizing flows need not agree. Each \(S_A\) has degree at most \(d\) in each spectral coordinate. Under \(\sigma_e=-2\cos(2\pi\delta_e)\), Bernstein's bound extends (11) to a sufficiently thin fixed complex strip, with cost at most \(\exp(2\pi d\sum_e|\operatorname{Im}\delta_e|)\). Shrink the strip to retain a positive gap and apply Cauchy for fixed derivatives. The [whole-domain current argument](actual_global_diagonal_spectral_sector_gap.md) then bounds the entire summable charge series, retaining second-derivative endpoint currents. It uses no infinite sharp-cube localization. Together with the [ALL-CROSS long-filling theorem](general_all_cross_long_filling_volume.md), (10) therefore implies the full invariant's volume limit for \(D\) and independently sufficiently long, fixed signed twists. The filled action approaches \(\Phi_D\), so its loss can be made smaller than the fixed remainder gap. This is a conditional implication, not an established universal energy estimate. ## 4. Exact reduction to spectral coefficient suprema Define $$ k_N^*(v)=\frac1N\log\max_{\sigma\in[-2,2]}|a_N(v;\sigma)|, \qquad h_N(v)=\frac1N\log p_N(v).\tag{12} $$ The coefficient polynomial is nonzero: (1) excludes simultaneous vanishing of its endpoint value and first derivative. For nonempty \(A_N\), put $$ J_{A,N}=\max_{\boldsymbol v\in A_N} \sum_e\bigl(2k_N^*(v_e)-h_N(v_e)\bigr). $$ Then, exactly, $$ e^{NJ_{A,N}} \le \sup_{\boldsymbol\sigma\in[-2,2]^R}E_A(\boldsymbol\sigma) \le |A_N|e^{NJ_{A,N}}.\tag{13} $$ The upper bound treats each positive summand. For the lower bound choose a maximizing **shared** array, then maximize each of its coefficient polynomials in its independent spectral coordinate. All these choices occur in the same source. No shared face radius is separately optimized. Since \(|A_N|\le\binom{d+3}{3}^R\), the logarithmic error in (13) is \(O_D(\log N/N)\). The [uniform reference entropy](actual_fejer_full_kernel_entropy_identity_reduction.md) replaces \(h_N(v)\) by \(h(v/d)\) with uniform \(o(1)\) error. Thus the energy question is exactly the finite shared-flow condition $$ \limsup_N\max_{\boldsymbol v\in\mathrm{NC}_N} \sum_e\bigl(2k_N^*(v_e)-h(v_e/d)\bigr) <\Phi_D+\gamma_D.\tag{14} $$ No continuous limit for \(k_N^*\) is assumed. A feasible array sequence exceeding this budget would disprove this sufficient route; a large local ratio without the remaining original targets would not. ## 5. A joint variational criterion on the original shared flow Let \(\mathcal P_D\) be the compact polytope of nonnegative original four-incidence loads \(q_e\), with \(\sum_vq_{e,v}=1\) at every port, ordinary face sums one, and protected face sums zero. Repeated incidences, when present in an allowed source, are counted with their actual labels. Write \(h(q)\) for the proved continuous full reference entropy. In the closed CROSS region \(q_b,q_c\le1/2\), it is the two-triangle entropy \(h_C(q)\), including the constrained split of the outer loads. The [one-sided relative-energy theorem](../papers/casimir-source-asymptotics/README.md) and the CROSS interpolation bound give, uniformly on the actual finite supports and on the whole real spectral interval, $$ \frac1N\log\frac{|a_N(v;\sigma)|^2}{p_N(v)} \le g(v/d)+o(1),\qquad g(q)= \begin{cases} h_C(q),&q_b,q_c\le\tfrac12,\\ C(q_x,q_y,\tfrac12-q_x-q_y),&q_c\ge\tfrac12 \text{ or }q_b\ge\tfrac12. \end{cases}\tag{15} $$ On either seam the retained triangle has middle load \(1/2-q_x-q_y\), so the formulas agree. At \((q_b,q_c)=(1/2,1/2)\) both are zero. Thus \(g\) is a well-defined continuous function on the full simplex. It does not reassign either middle load. A zero actual coefficient satisfies (15) with logarithm minus infinity. Define on the **same** original feasible flow $$ H(\boldsymbol q)=\sum_eh(q_e),\qquad G(\boldsymbol q)=\sum_eg(q_e),\qquad \mathcal P_D^{\mathrm{NC}} =\left\{\boldsymbol q\in\mathcal P_D: \max_e\max(q_{e,b},q_{e,c})\ge\tfrac12\right\}. \tag{16} $$ The exact finite noncross set is contained in this closed set after scaling by \(d\). The set may also contain limiting boundary flows of patterns that are eventually infeasible; keeping them enlarges the maximum and is safe for this upper criterion. Empty maxima are minus infinity. For **each** feasible finite array, uniform reference entropy and (15) give $$ \prod_e|a_N(v_e;\sigma_e)| \le\exp\left\{\frac N2 [H(\boldsymbol v/d)+G(\boldsymbol v/d)]+o(N)\right\}. \tag{17} $$ The error is uniform over all arrays and real spectral coordinates. Sum (17) over the original noncross arrays. Their number is polynomial in \(N\), and compactness and continuity then prove $$ \limsup_N\frac1N\log \sup_{\boldsymbol\sigma\in[-2,2]^R}|S_{\mathrm{NC}}| \le\frac12\max_{\boldsymbol q\in\mathcal P_D^{\mathrm{NC}}} [H(\boldsymbol q)+G(\boldsymbol q)].\tag{18} $$ This is an arraywise inequality. It is stronger than replacing the right side by \(\tfrac12(\max H+\max G)\), whose two maximizers may differ. It requires neither an unknown limiting spectral coefficient function \(k^*\) nor a minimax exchange. **Joint criterion.** For the fixed certified diagram, the explicit condition $$ \boxed{\displaystyle \max_{\boldsymbol q\in\mathcal P_D^{\mathrm{NC}}} [H(\boldsymbol q)+G(\boldsymbol q)]<2\Phi_D} \tag{19} $$ implies a fixed real spectral gap for the entire noncross numerator. The polynomial strip extension and whole-domain current argument of section 3 then prove the full invariant's filled-volume limit for independently sufficiently long fixed signed twists, with its original mark, characters, and normalization. The ALL-CROSS relative asymptotic remains the leading term. Condition (19) is a proved sufficient reduction; its validity for every certified diagram is open. ## 6. Combining the energy bound with the earlier envelope One can retain both available local estimates without comparing them. On the closed LEFT simplex let \(t=2(1-q_c)\) and define $$ h_{\mathrm{env},L}(q)= \begin{cases} t\,C(q_x/t,q_b/t,q_y/t),&t>0,\\ 0,&q=e_c. \end{cases}\tag{20} $$ RIGHT is the literal interchange of \(b,c\). This continuous perspective is the exact concave conjugate of the [proved weighted upper envelope](actual_global_left_weighted_spectral_envelope.md) \(\max\{\log c,Q(x,b,y)+\tfrac12\log c\}\): its two atoms have loads \(e_c\) and \(\alpha+e_c/2\), respectively. Finite positive outer and middle tilts, followed by a finite compact covering as in the local energy theorem, therefore give a uniform **coefficient upper bound** \(N^{-1}\log|a_N|\le h_{\mathrm{env},L}(q)+o(1)\). This does not decompose the finite source into the two atoms or exchange an infimum over shared radii with their maximum. Protected faces continue to impose exponent zero; a sector with protected overloaded middle is identically absent. Put \(\widetilde h=(h+g)/2\) and $$ h_{\mathrm{sharp}}(q)= \begin{cases} h_C(q),&q_b,q_c\le\tfrac12,\\ \min\{h_{\mathrm{env},L}(q),\widetilde h(q)\}, &q_c\ge\tfrac12,\\ \min\{h_{\mathrm{env},R}(q),\widetilde h(q)\}, &q_b\ge\tfrac12. \end{cases}\tag{21} $$ The formulas agree on their seams. Taking the minimum of two uniform bounds is valid; no assertion that \(\widetilde h\le h_{\mathrm{env}}\) is needed. Repeating the same finite-array sum proves $$ \limsup_N\frac1N\log \sup_{\boldsymbol\sigma\in[-2,2]^R}|S_{\mathrm{NC}}| \le\max_{\boldsymbol q\in\mathcal P_D^{\mathrm{NC}}} \sum_e h_{\mathrm{sharp}}(q_e).\tag{22} $$ **Combined criterion.** The compact, original-incidence condition $$ \boxed{\displaystyle \max_{\boldsymbol q\in\mathcal P_D^{\mathrm{NC}}} \sum_e h_{\mathrm{sharp}}(q_e)<\Phi_D} \tag{23} $$ has the same full signed long-filling consequence. It is sufficient whenever (19) holds. It also retains every previously established genuine sector or branch-cover certificate based on the one-sided perspective envelope: (21) only lowers that comparison on each covered original sector. To handle the closed-set convention, a flow with a strict overload is approximated by the proved full-support integer flow rounding while retaining that overload; a subsequence fixes its actual finite sector. Continuity then extends the corresponding certificate. At flows with only terminal seams, the score equals the endpoint entropy, whose strict gap on this closed noncross boundary is already proved. This is an implication between criteria, not a claim of a newly verified strict enlargement of the diagram classes. No concavity of (21) is asserted or required. Equations (18) and (22) use direct compact maximization of the original flows, not unproved convexity or an independent optimization at each face. Proving (23) universally, or finding a feasible original flow that obstructs it, is the remaining geometric entropy problem. ## 7. Proved inputs and remaining limits The [CROSS cofactor interpolation theorem](../papers/filling-bounds/README.md) already gives coefficientwise \(O(\log^2N)\) domination by the CROSS endpoint polynomial. That polynomial is at most \(H_{F_N}\) at both parities. CROSS factors therefore have polynomial energy cost. The [support-preserving endpoint estimates](actual_fejer_spectral_polydisk_complement.md) also bound (7) on small spectral polydisks. The general one-sided theorem now supplies the local triangle bound (15). The unresolved step is the global comparison (19) or (23) on the original shared-flow polytope. A new [protected-outer theorem](actual_protected_outer_spectral_energy.md) computes \(k_N^*\) and its relative-energy limit there, with uniform closed boundary control. It is a local input to (14), not a shared-flow estimate. Earlier metrics do not supply (10). The [complete-circle positive quotient](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_complete_circle_reflection_positive.md) bounds transmission on an already inserted \(L_N\), not replacement by \(V_N\) or overlapping coupons. The [full Fourier–Hermite Gram](../papers/filling-bounds/README.md) has an actual whole-source excess-energy example on a redundant normalization insertion, but is not the energy (7). The [Newton-turn Gram](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_newton_turn_positive_gram.md) keeps turns and coherent reflected circuits; it does not bound arbitrary source energies. The [length-normalized star](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_length_normalized_star_gram.md) retains both coefficient and dual weights, which cannot be dropped. The new joint and combined-score reductions use the proved uniform local theorem; their global strict inequalities remain hypotheses, not general volume comparison theorems. Sections 5–6 prove conditional reductions; their universal strict entropy hypotheses remain open.

title: Established volume results and the remaining research question
text: # Established volume results and the remaining research question 25 November 2026. The [paper collection](../papers/README.md) is the current source for the proved statements. The [dependency graph](../docs/papers/dependencies.html) records which statements their proofs use. The [reference manuscript](../manuscript/README.md) gives a unified account; it does not add hypotheses or conclusions to the individual papers. The strict Conway theorem proves the reduced Kashaev volume identity for each eligible fixed construction with independently sufficiently long auxiliary fillings. Ordered circle trees have separate summed and directed degree-and-twist criteria. The planar results require their specified balance or certificate hypotheses. A nonzero central contribution for a more general diagram is distinct from a bound on its entire complement. These distinctions are stated in the [illustrated results guide](../book/chapters/results.md). For each fixed strict template, long-filling assignments have density one in its integer lattice. The theorem leaves infinitely many short-coordinate assignments untreated. It does not establish finitely many exceptions, density one among distinct knots, or a theorem for every arborescent knot. The extension problem is to permit an arbitrary fixed short partial filling and prove the limit for all sufficiently long remaining fillings that give hyperbolic knots. The [research status](research_finite_exceptions_progress.md) explains the quantifiers, infinite-fiber difficulty, exact orthogonal elimination of linear packets and current finite-source reductions. The [route guide](research_routes_and_preserved_ideas.md) keeps the distinct methods and their limitations accessible. This page replaces an accumulated list of intermediate local results. The [earlier text](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/general_equality_frontier.md) is available in Git history. Its historical assertions are not a separate current proof inventory.

title: The full even Fejér endpoint source has the actual complete volume
status: Actual even endpoint volume; strict identity-insertion gap
text: # The full even Fejér endpoint source has the actual complete volume 31 October 2026. general endpoint-volume theorem. This is an endpoint theorem for the original positive polynomial numerator. It does not rename that numerator Kashaev's invariant, prove its Gaussian filling transform, or assert the fixed long-filled knot conjecture. ## 1. Statement and normalization Fix a connected original flat plat D, at any fixed bridge width, with R ports and its literal ordered face incidences (x_e,b_e,c_e,y_e). Retain the original two protected faces u,v and their MAIN edge. Assume the existing labeled convex ideal right-angled certificate for its actual untwisted augmented exterior Y_D. Thus Y_D is hyperbolic and its two original cut balls, white/shaded face pairings, crossing-circle matching and primitive markings are specified. No realization of an unrelated triangulation is sufficient for this hypothesis. For even N put d=N-1 and use the original pair Casimir Omega_N and its full characteristic polynomial chi_N(sigma)=2T_N(sigma/2)+2, V_N(sigma)=chi_N(sigma)(sigma-Omega_N)^(-1), P_N=-V_N(-2)=4(2+Omega_N)^(-1). The middle expression is the actual polynomial numerator, including its repeated-node data. H is the original homogeneous coupon compiler. Set Z_(D,N)=[prod_(f ordinary)L_f^d] prod_(e=1)^R H_(P_N)(x_e,b_e,c_e,y_e) |_(L_u=L_v=0). (1) All coefficients in (1) are nonnegative. All source scalars and the marked coefficient targets are retained; no additional N^R is inserted. Then lim_(even N->infinity) (2pi/N) log Z_(D,N) =Vol(Y_D). (2) The limit runs through all even levels, including composite levels. Its hypotheses impose no bound on the fixed bridge width or number of ports. The geometric certificate and original flat-plat incidence are essential stated assumptions. This theorem concerns the complete augmented exterior, not a metric obtained by long filling. ## 2. One continuous entropy on the full local simplex The [closed local coefficient theorem](actual_fejer_half_block_entropy.md) gives the one-sided entropy E(mu,nu,xi)=inf_l {integral_mu^nu g(t,l)dt-xi*l}, g(t,l)=l/2+log tan(pi*t) +asinh(tan(pi*t)cosh(l/2)), 0<=mu<=nu<=1/2, 0<=xi<=nu-mu. Its triangular endpoint is C(alpha)=E(alpha_b,1/2,alpha_x), for nonnegative alpha of sum1/2, and its ABSOLUTE normalization is C(alpha)=V(2pi alpha)/(2pi), V(theta)=2sum_j[Lambda(theta_j/2)+Lambda((pi-theta_j)/2)]. On q=(X,B,Cm,Y)>=0 of sum1 define h by the two E branches when Cm>=1/2 or B>=1/2, and by max[C(alpha)+C(beta)] over the actual cross split when B,Cm<=1/2. The branches agree at both terminal seams; h is continuous on the ENTIRE closed simplex and h(0,B,1-B,0)=0. Every degree-d monomial is present in the full positive H_P. Uniformly over those monomials, its coefficient p_N(n) satisfies N^-1 log p_N(n)=h(n/d)+o(1). (3) This is the [uniform full-kernel theorem](actual_fejer_full_kernel_entropy_identity_reduction.md), proved from the closed half-block estimates, positive cross convolution, the coefficientwise cross comparison and continuous seam values. It retains the finite forced outer factor. It does not require assigning a fixed half label to a limiting seam point. Let Q_D be the compact nonnegative incidence-flow polytope: each port supplies1, each ordinary face demands1, and protected demands are0. Repeated local incidences remain distinct arcs. Scaling a flow by d and fractional-cycle rounding preserves exact integer balances with at most one unit of error per incidence. Every rounded local vector is in the full support. The number of summands is polynomial in N. Thus (3), positivity and compactness prove lim_(even N) N^-1 log Z_(D,N) =W_D:=max_(q in Q_D) sum_e h(q_e). (4) The [all-cross comparison](actual_fejer_cross_half_source_reduction.md) and the [complete source volume theorem](general_signed_augmented_source_volume.md) give W_D>=Phi_D:=Vol(Y_D)/(2pi). It remains to prove the opposite inequality for a maximizer of (4). ## 3. Remove pure-middle maximizing ports by exact source identities Choose a maximizer q, including maximizing triangle allocations at its cross ports. Let J consist of ALL ports with both outer loads zero. This includes one-sided diagonals and the pure-middle cross seam. The literal identity coupon is H_1(b,c)=sum_(j=0)^d b^j c^(d-j). It has entropy zero on the whole pure-middle segment, and coefficientwise H_1<=H_P. The mixed source with H_1 on J therefore has rate at most W_D. The SAME maximizing q is feasible for its mixed flow problem and has the same entropy. The full-kernel flow theorem with identity nodes gives the reverse inequality, so these rates are EXACTLY equal. No finite cross monomial with zero outer degree is invented. The selected middle edges form a forest in the original gap graph. Every possible original middle cycle contains the protected exterior; its unit edge supplies would exceed its vertices' total demand. A tree cannot contain both protected vertices either, by the same load count. For each remaining monomial, its identity degrees along a tree are uniquely determined by subtree balances and lie between0 and d. Consequently exact coefficient extraction contracts each identity tree to its ordinary/protected merged face, with coefficient one and no multiplicity. This is the [actual connected identity smoothing](actual_fejer_diagonal_identity_forest_reduction.md). The inherited maximizing local vectors at the remaining ports still have positive total outer load. A loop in the smoothed white cellulation would enclose v ordinary vertices but only v-1 whole ports and one half port. Its demand forces that half port's middle load1, making it pure-middle, a contradiction. A retained matching edge between the two protected roots would also force a pure-middle port. Thus the remaining white triangular cellulation is loopless, with distinct adjacent protected roots. Multiple edges are retained. The empty source has rate zero and is handled separately; it cannot attain W_D>=Phi_D>0. ## 4. Hybrid Hall theory resolves all remaining forced boundary degrees At the inherited maximum tag each B,Cm<=1/2 port CROSS, retaining its two triangle allocations. Every other port is GREEN, in a strict one-sided chamber with 0<=mu<nu<1/2. A CROSS port supplies two triangle nodes of mass1/2. A GREEN port supplies one node of mass1 incident to its four original faces. Its entropy is E, not two independent triangle entropies. A shared outer incidence is aggregated once for this node. For an ordinary vertex set S, merging a triangle pair changes its Hall capacity by +1/2 exactly when one triangle touches S and the other does not. It never decreases capacity. The [hybrid Hall theorem](actual_fejer_hybrid_tight_cut_reduction.md) proves: * Every proper tight set is a union of actual digon interiors, after adjoining neighboring holes joined by a GREEN matching edge. * Their surviving cuts are MAIN/MAIN, or MATCHING/MATCHING with BOTH boundary ports CROSS. No GREEN pair is split. * These tight sets explain exactly the structurally forced zero arcs. Every other ordinary arc is positive in one common feasible witness. For completeness, the counting behind this classification is exact. On the induced graph of U=V\S, let p count original triangle faces and n=|U|. Euler and boundary-walk length at least2 give p<=2n-4; equality forces a connected induced graph whose other faces are genuine digons. Hybrid equality additionally forbids a GREEN edge from separating a triangle touching S from one not touching S. Adjacent such holes merge along the same parallel-edge pair. For proper S these mergers are paths, not cycles. Thus the surviving cuts have precisely the types above. The reserve-epsilon Hall test then proves the positive-witness assertion. Split along these actual permitted cuts, iterating on the inherited marked pieces. The child boundary loads are zero. At a matching cut, the separated CROSS triangles are the original additive C rows; their pure-middle closing caps have entropy zero. Formal re-pairing of two boundary C rows is only bookkeeping and creates no physical coupon. The resulting hybrid flow and entropy constraints are Cartesian across pieces. Every piece perturbation reassembles an original cross split, whose full h is at least the corresponding C+C value. Hence the inherited point is maximizing on each piece. Mix that point slightly with its strictly positive relative hybrid witness. CROSS allocations stay within their triangle simplexes, so no terminal seam is pushed into a losing one-sided chamber. The strict GREEN row margins persist. The [proved corner expansions](actual_fejer_nondiagonal_maximizer_regularity.md) give only nonnegative epsilon log(1/epsilon) terms and a strictly positive one at every activated ordinary zero. All other changes are O(epsilon). Maximality therefore excludes every ordinary zero except the two marked faces and the zero-dimensional closing rows. Diagonal losses are absent: all pure-middle ports were removed in section3. Finite-dimensional row-space Lagrange multipliers now exist on each piece, including when the balance equations are redundant. Exponentiating them gives finite positive ordinary curvatures. The local equations are the actual tangent-circle formula for each C row and the actual Green equations L(mu;x,y)=b, L(nu;x,y)=c for each E port, with their proved one-line/two-line limits. Every ordinary signed star sums to0 or2pi. ## 5. The entropy is the volume of a representation of the original group The [hybrid-piece representation theorem](actual_fejer_hybrid_piece_representation.md) applies to exactly these data. Its essentials are included here to specify the volume being bounded. Each piece develops ONE signed circle family by finite-center star holonomy. The marked edge may be MAIN or MATCHING. In the latter case its two incident rows are the positive zero-entropy CROSS closing halves, so the same two-line strip construction applies. All permitted parallel marked chords have been split. No unproved translation holonomy remains. Along the actual cut tree, map each child's ordered tangent boundary planes to the parent's pair by ONE Mobius map. This gives one reflection for each occurrence of an actual shared white face. A GREEN port remains within one piece and retains its entire local source collar. At an original CROSS port spanning pieces, the common outer product P is noncentral parabolic. Its two raw first meridians have trace-2 and Tr((P+I)A)=4. The parabolic centralizer acts simply transitively on them, so there is a unique C mapping the WHOLE ordered input pair to the output pair and all three recorded contact flags. This is the original shaded pairing, even when its two triangles lie in different pieces. Use the two original topological cut balls and the original face maps. One global reflection develops the second ball. Their proper digon-cut disks have both ends at the same tangent-pair contact. Compatible finite incidence horospheres and the short-edge tetrahedron bound make the added cut-disk volume tend to zero. Signed cyclic polygon coning, including winding-zero faces and repeated contact images, then computes the actual relative fundamental chain: Vol(rho_sm)=sum_pieces sum_triangles sigma V(theta) =2pi*(inherited maximizing entropy). (5) Each piece uses its own genuine marked contact in this chain calculation. Mobius invariance is used for geometric tetrahedron volumes, not for an open crossing expression with a reset Gauss flag. The failed local re-framing argument is neither needed nor reinstated. Finally restore the deleted original auxiliary meridians as identities. The ordered physical pairs coincide across each identity smoothing. Their outer product need not be parabolic; the established axial (loxodromic or elliptic), parabolic, or central zero-volume filling cap retains its actual peripheral flag. Thus rho_sm extends through the actual quotient to a representation rho of pi_1(Y_D), with the SAME relative volume. Equations (4)--(5) give 2pi W_D=Vol(rho)<=Vol(Y_D). The last inequality uses the [classical representation-volume bound](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/general_representation_volume_kernel_strictness.md) for the original hyperbolic exterior. Together with the all-cross lower bound this proves (2), including the absolute volume constant. ## 6. A strict identity-insertion consequence The same argument starts with any fixed nonempty set I of original identity coupons and P coupons elsewhere. If its mixed incidence polytope is empty, its coefficient is zero at every even level and its rate is -infinity. Otherwise its original identity graph is a forest with at most one protected vertex per tree, and its coefficient contracts exactly. The full-kernel theorem gives a compact maximum. Any further pure-middle maximum ports can be added to I: lifting the identity degrees gives a feasible pure-middle assignment in the original graph, so the union is again a permitted forest. The hybrid argument and actual representation assembly then apply unchanged. The classical kernel statement below is separate from the construction of that representation and its volume identification. It concerns the positive endpoint source, not the full signed knot invariant. The resulting representation kills each specified original auxiliary meridian. Those are essential in Y_D. The [strict-kernel volume bound](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/general_representation_volume_kernel_strictness.md) therefore gives lim_(even N) N^-1 log Z_(D,N;H_1 on I) <Vol(Y_D)/(2pi). (6) The empty remaining source has rate zero, also strictly below the positive complete hyperbolic volume. This is a strict statement about the actual positive identity-inserted source. It is not a phase-sensitive estimate for all small colors or a replacement for their normal data. ## 7. What is still required for the requested knot conjecture The theorem closes the COMPLETE even positive endpoint estimate, at arbitrary fixed bridge width under the labeled geometric certificate. It does not control the full Gaussian-resolvent contour away from this endpoint, its nonzero Fourier charges, the selected geometric cycle or its nonzero contribution. The [odd regularized numerator theorem](actual_fejer_odd_regularized_full_numerator.md) now supplies the same rate for its actual value-plus-spectral-derivative coupon, and fixed spectral jets have an explicit polynomial bound. These are spectral derivatives at the fixed root, not genuine-q normals. Independently long fixed signed fillings still require those quantum inputs, with the original peripheral normals and scalars, before the filled hyperbolic volume can be concluded. The general original Kashaev volume conjecture remains open. Its target has not been replaced by (2). ## 8. Finite verification The [focused structural audit](../experiments/audit_general_fejer_endpoint_source_volume.py) and [recorded results](../experiments/general_fejer_endpoint_source_volume_results.json) check 41 literal loopless identity smoothings at widths two, three and four; 918 hybrid patterns; 121004 exact Hall cuts; 716 tight-set covers by independently constructed actual dual digon disks; and 816 independent positive-arc max-flow tests. The original local coefficient, physical source and signed-volume audits remain linked in the dependencies. These finite tests supplement the general proof; they do not numerically prove the asymptotic or the relative fundamental-class identification.

title: The original localized spectral period has a nonzero unit-charge filling contribution
status: Localized original contribution; input to whole-period theorem
text: # The original localized spectral period has a nonzero unit-charge filling contribution analytical theorem, 31 October 2026. This proves a relative asymptotic on an **actual fixed real spectral cube**, with its original Fourier charges, sine factors, parity and marked coefficient. It does not estimate the integral outside that cube or the remote charge sum. The inputs are the [full spectral numerator packet](../papers/casimir-source-asymptotics/README.md), the [local charge comparison](../papers/casimir-source-asymptotics/README.md), and the exact period (13a) in the [cross-cofactor source interface](../papers/filling-bounds/README.md). The finite-root spectral identity is also recorded in the [spectral total-derivative theorem](actual_spectral_total_derivative_source.md). ## 1. Exact original normalization and the local quantity Fix the original certified marked flat plat with $R$ ports. Put $d=N-1$, $q=e^{\pi i/N}$, and let $n_i$ be its actual nonzero integer crossing powers. In the long-twist convention $n_i=\epsilon_i-2p_i$. Define the ENTIRE original shared spectral numerator $$ S_N(\boldsymbol\sigma)=\left[\prod_{f\ \mathrm{ordinary}}L_f^d\right] \left.\prod_i H_{V_N(\sigma_i)}\right|_{L_u=L_v=0}. $$ The original fixed-root Fourier/Hermite period is exactly $$ \begin{aligned} I_{D,\mathbf n} ={}&q^{\frac{d^2}{4}\sum_i n_i}(-i)^R \sum_{\boldsymbol\ell\in(\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\})^R} \left(\prod_i\ell_i\right)(-1)^{(N+1)\sum_i\ell_i}\\ &\quad\times\int_{[-1/2,1/2]^R} \left[\prod_i\sin(2\pi\delta_i)\right] S_N\!\left(-2\cos(2\pi\boldsymbol\delta)\right) \exp\!\left\{N\sum_i\left[\pi i n_i\delta_i^2+2\pi i\ell_i\delta_i\right]\right\} \,d\boldsymbol\delta . \end{aligned}\tag{1} $$ Here $I_{D,\mathbf n}$ is the RAW original marked contraction. If the final $K_N$ convention is $K_N=\chi_{D,N}I_{D,\mathbf n}$, its already recorded external character multiplies every localized formula below as well. The [complete-pointing normalization](actual_complete_augmented_source_normalization.md), especially sections 1 and 3, retains the reduced framing character (modulus one) and the enhanced component sign; a full one-cut modified ADO convention has the additional $i^{N+3}/N$ factor. None is silently absorbed into our raw amplitude. The actual final-diagram framing/component character must be used, rather than the augmented diagram's component count. Any such separately recorded scalar is still outside (1). In particular (1) has no additional $N^R$, mark, spectral square-root Jacobian or division by a quantum dimension. The displayed $q$ power is the literal unwrapped scalar $\exp[\pi i d^2(\sum_i n_i)/(4N)]$. Charge zero is absent by the exact total-derivative identity, not discarded by an asymptotic argument. The full finite-$N$ charge series in (1) is absolutely convergent; no uniform-in-$N$ summability is used below. Choose $b>0$ within the fixed complex neighborhood of the full packet. For a charge $\boldsymbol\ell$ let $J_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}$ be the integral in (1) restricted to the CLOSED real cube $K_b=[-b,b]^R$. All local charge contributions below include the factors preceding that integral in (1). This is a sharp restriction of the original real contour, with its actual boundary. There is no analytic compactly supported cutoff and no assigned Lefschetz-cycle coefficient. Only FINITELY many restricted charge terms are ever summed here. A sharp cube has boundary jumps and its individual $J_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}$ do not inherit the absolute charge summability of the original full-domain integral. The proved full packet is $$ S_N\!\left(-2\cos(2\pi\boldsymbol\delta)\right) =\frac{(-1)^{dR}N^{2R}e^{N A_N(\boldsymbol\delta)}} {(2\pi N)^{(R-1)/2}\sqrt{\det H_N(\boldsymbol\delta)}} \left[1+O(N^{-1})\right].\tag{2} $$ It is uniform and holomorphic on a fixed complex polydisc. Every finite scalar and logarithmic normalization stays in $A_N$; the explicit $N^{2R}$ alone is taken out. $H_N$ is the ordinary-face Hessian after fixing ONE common face scale. Its determinant root is continued from its positive value at $\boldsymbol\delta=0$. The dimension of that face quotient is $R-1$. The packet restores the full $V$ numerator, including its semisimple spectral data, by the proved noncross exponential gap. The finite interpolant used to define $A_N$ is real on the real local chart and even in each $\delta_i$. Uniqueness of the face IFT preserves both properties. On smaller fixed polydiscs, with all fixed derivatives, $$ A_N\longrightarrow A_0,\qquad A_0(0)=\Phi_D,\qquad A_0''(0)=-2\operatorname{diag}(C_1,\ldots,C_R),\qquad C_i>0.\tag{3} $$ These are finite-source properties, not a choice of a phase fitted to the answer. In particular $$ \partial_i A_N(\boldsymbol\delta) =-2\delta_i B_{i,N}(\delta_1^2,\ldots,\delta_R^2),\qquad B_{i,N}\longrightarrow B_i,\qquad B_i(0)=C_i.\tag{4} $$ The quotients at $\delta_i=0$ are removable. After shrinking the chart, $|B_{i,N}-C_i|\leq C_i/8$ for all large N. In particular $\operatorname{Re}B_{i,N}>C_i/2$, and the real symmetric matrix $\operatorname{Re}A_N''(z)$ is negative definite uniformly for ALL complex z in that chart and all large N. ## 2. Finite-N filling saddles for independent signed twists There are fixed $b,a,n_0>0$, with a much smaller than b, such that the following holds for every fixed integer vector $\mathbf n$ with $|n_i|\geq n_0$. There is no condition on ratios $|n_i|/|n_j|$. For positive real charges satisfying $\ell_i/|n_i|\leq a$ define $$ \Phi_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}(\boldsymbol\delta) =A_N(\boldsymbol\delta)+\pi i\sum_i n_i\delta_i^2 +2\pi i\sum_i\ell_i\delta_i.\tag{5} $$ It has a unique critical point $\boldsymbol\delta_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}$ in the chosen small polydisc. Indeed, writing $t_i=\ell_i/n_i$, its equations are precisely $$ \delta_i=-\frac{t_i}{1+i B_{i,N}(\boldsymbol\delta^2)/(\pi n_i)}.\tag{6} $$ Uniform contraction proves existence, uniqueness and holomorphic parameter dependence, exactly as in the limiting charge lemma. Bounds on $B_{i,N}$ and their derivatives are uniform in N. Consequently $$ |\delta_i|\leq 2|t_i|,\qquad \operatorname{Im}\delta_i =\frac{\ell_i}{\pi n_i^2} \frac{\operatorname{Re}B_{i,N}(\boldsymbol\delta^2)} {\left|1+i B_{i,N}(\boldsymbol\delta^2)/(\pi n_i)\right|^2}>0.\tag{7} $$ In particular $\operatorname{Im}\delta_i\leq C\ell_i/n_i^2$. This sign holds for BOTH signs of $n_i$. All coordinates of the saddle are nonzero when all $\ell_i>0$. Write $\boldsymbol\delta_*=x_*+iy_*$, with $y_*>0$ componentwise, and put $$ S_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}=\Phi_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}(\boldsymbol\delta_*),\qquad Q_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}=-\Phi_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}''(\boldsymbol\delta_*). $$ Since the Gaussian contributes a purely imaginary diagonal Hessian, $\operatorname{Re}Q_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}$ is positive definite. No real or complex eigenvalue of Q vanishes. The spectral determinant root used below is the unique Gaussian branch on the convex cone of complex symmetric matrices with positive real part, positive at a positive real matrix. Thus $$ \int_{\mathbb R^R}e^{-\frac12 t^TQt}\,dt =\frac{(2\pi)^{R/2}}{\sqrt{\det Q}}.\tag{8} $$ This fixes its phase even when the different $n_i$ have different signs. For fixed $\mathbf n$ and $\boldsymbol\ell$, $\boldsymbol\delta_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}$ and $S_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}$ converge to the corresponding limiting critical point and value. No convergence rate is needed and $A_N$ is NOT replaced by $A_0$ in a relative formula. ## 3. Deformation of the actual restricted real contour We prove the requisite contour coefficient, rather than postulate it. Translate $K_b$ coordinate by coordinate to $K_b+i y_*$. Cauchy's theorem on each rectangle gives equality with the translated integral plus its oriented side integrals. The exact integrand is entire in $\boldsymbol\delta$; the packet is only used to estimate it inside the common local chart. The side integrals are retained in this equality. Here is a uniform exponential bound for every side. Its points have $z=x+iv$ with x in $K_b$, at least one $|x_j|=b$, and $0\leq v_i\leq y_{*,i}$. Separate reality and the real Hessian bound give $$ \operatorname{Re}A_N(x+iv)\leq A_N(0)-c|x|^2+C|v|^2.\tag{9} $$ To see the quadratic, rather than linear, error in v, Taylor-expand at the REAL point x: the first term $i\nabla A_N(x)\cdot v$ is imaginary. The remaining derivatives are uniformly bounded. The real Gaussian and charge contribution is $$ -2\pi\sum_i n_i x_i v_i-2\pi\sum_i\ell_i v_i \leq Cb\sum_i\frac{\ell_i}{|n_i|}.\tag{10} $$ The second term is nonpositive. Equation (7) bounds the first term, without using a common sign or a bound on slope ratios. Thus every side has real phase at most $$ A_N(0)-cb^2+C|y_*|^2+Cb\sum_i|t_i|.\tag{11} $$ The critical value satisfies the complementary estimate $$ \operatorname{Re}S_{N,\boldsymbol\ell} \geq A_N(0)-C\sum_i|t_i|^2.\tag{12} $$ For completeness, $A_N(\boldsymbol\delta_*)-A_N(0)=O(\sum_i|t_i|^2)$. The critical equations imply $|n_i x_{*,i}+\ell_i|\leq C|\delta_{*,i}|$; hence the real quadratic-plus-linear phase $-2\pi\sum_i(n_i x_{*,i}+\ell_i)y_{*,i}$ has the same bound (and in fact a smaller additional factor $n_{\min}^{-1}$). This proves (12) without bounding the large purely imaginary quantity $n_i\delta_i^2$ by its absolute value. First fix b within the source chart, then choose a/b sufficiently small and $n_0$ sufficiently large. Equations (11)-(12) give a fixed $\kappa_b>0$ such that ALL sides satisfy $$ \operatorname{Re}\Phi_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}(z) \leq\operatorname{Re}S_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}-\kappa_b.\tag{13} $$ All polynomial prefactors in (2), bounded sine factors and finite side volumes preserve this exponential loss. Thus the actual local real contour has coefficient +1 on its translated horizontal saddle plane, with only exponentially small side currents. On that plane $\Phi'$ vanishes at $x_*+iy_*$, and for every real x in $K_b$ $$ \operatorname{Re}\Phi_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}(x+iy_*) \leq\operatorname{Re}S_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}-c|x-x_*|^2.\tag{14} $$ Indeed the real part of its real-coordinate Hessian is $\operatorname{Re}A_N''$, which is uniformly negative definite along the entire segment. The critical point stays a fixed distance from the cube boundary because $|x_*|\leq2a$ much less than b. This proves the requisite local and nonlocal estimates on the translated restricted contour. It does not say anything about the original contour outside $K_b$. ## 4. Relative asymptotic and its nonzero coefficient Define $$ a_N(\boldsymbol\delta) =\frac{\prod_i\sin(2\pi\delta_i)}{\sqrt{\det H_N(\boldsymbol\delta)}}. $$ The holomorphic Gaussian estimate on (14), using (8), yields $$ J_{N,\boldsymbol\ell} =(-1)^{dR}\sqrt{2\pi}\,N^{R+1/2} \frac{a_N(\boldsymbol\delta_{N,\boldsymbol\ell})}{\sqrt{\det Q_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}}} e^{N S_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}} \left[1+O_{\mathbf n,\boldsymbol\ell}(N^{-1})\right].\tag{15} $$ The error in the full packet is holomorphic and uniformly $O(N^{-1})$; Cauchy bounds, or direct Gaussian integration of that error, preserve (15). The ordinary Taylor Gaussian error is $O(N^{-1})$, since its odd first correction integrates to zero; replacing the cube by the full real Gaussian changes the answer exponentially. The exact side integrals in (13) are likewise exponentially small relative to (15). Constants may depend on the FIXED slopes and charges. No joint large-twist/large-level error estimate is asserted. The power and constant follow directly from the TWO actual integrals: $$ N^{2R}(2\pi N)^{-(R-1)/2}(2\pi/N)^{R/2} =\sqrt{2\pi}\,N^{R+1/2}.\tag{16} $$ There is no undetermined stationary multiplier. Every sine in (15) is nonzero: $\delta_{*,i}$ is nonzero by (6) and lies in a small disk with no other zero of $\sin(2\pi\delta_i)$. Both determinant roots are units. For each fixed $\mathbf n$ and $\boldsymbol\ell$ the coefficient in (15) converges to a nonzero number. Therefore the local integral is nonzero for all sufficiently large N. Let $U_{N,\mathbf n;b}$ denote the sum of the original contributions in (1) with $\ell_i\in\{+1,-1\}$, each restricted to $K_b$. Reflection of one coordinate $\delta_i\mapsto-\delta_i$ changes $J_{N,\boldsymbol\ell}$ by a minus sign and also changes $\prod_i\ell_i$ by a minus sign. $S_N$ and the quadratic phase are separately even, and the parity character is unchanged. Thus all $2^R$ sign choices contribute EXACTLY equally. With $S_{N,\mathbf1}$, $\boldsymbol\delta_{N,\mathbf1}$, $Q_{N,\mathbf1}$ defined above, $$ \begin{aligned} U_{N,\mathbf n;b} ={}&q^{\frac{d^2}{4}\sum_i n_i}(-2i)^R\sqrt{2\pi}\,N^{R+1/2}\\ &\quad\times\frac{\prod_i\sin(2\pi\delta_{N,\mathbf1,i})} {\sqrt{\det H_N(\boldsymbol\delta_{N,\mathbf1})}\sqrt{\det Q_{N,\mathbf1}}} e^{N S_{N,\mathbf1}}\left[1+O_{\mathbf n}(N^{-1})\right]. \end{aligned}\tag{17} $$ The parity cancellation is literal: $$ (-1)^{(N+1)R}(-1)^{dR}=(-1)^{2NR}=1. $$ Equation (17) holds through BOTH level parities and arbitrary independent signs of the sufficiently long fixed $n_i$. The remaining $q$ scalar has modulus one and is kept exactly. This proves a nonzero contributing localized original unit-charge period, not merely the existence of the corresponding critical point. ## 5. Optional enlargement to the finite LOCAL charge sector For fixed $\mathbf n$ let $L_i=\lfloor a|n_i|\rfloor$, with $n_0$ enlarged so $L_i\geq1$. Restrict (1) to $K_b$ and to $0<|\ell_i|\leq L_i$. This is a finite set after the twists are fixed. The exact finite version of the monotonicity calculation applies to $A_N$, because (4) and $\operatorname{Re}B_{i,N}>0$ hold: $$ \partial_{\ell_i}\operatorname{Re}S_{N,\boldsymbol\ell} =-\frac{2\ell_i}{n_i^2} \frac{\operatorname{Re}B_{i,N}} {\left|1+iB_{i,N}/(\pi n_i)\right|^2}. $$ After the same fixed shrink, for every positive charge in this box, $$ \operatorname{Re}S_{N,\mathbf1}-\operatorname{Re}S_{N,\boldsymbol\ell} \geq\sum_i\frac{C_i}{2n_i^2}(\ell_i^2-1).\tag{18} $$ The harmless constants can be decreased if needed to make this inequality uniform in all large N. If any nonunit positive charge exists, the right side has a strictly positive minimum $\eta_{\mathbf n}$ over that FINITE set. Formula (15), the exact charge factors $\prod_i\ell_i$, and the independent sign symmetry imply that the entire restricted local charge sector equals (17) with an additional relative $O_{\mathbf n}(e^{-\eta_{\mathbf n}N})$ error (or after a smaller $\eta_{\mathbf n}$). If all $L_i=1$, there are no extra local charges. There is no comparison of an infinite charge sum and no assertion about charges near an alias. ## 6. Geometric value and exact remaining limitation The limiting action in (5) is $$ \begin{aligned} A_0+\pi i\sum_i(\epsilon_i-2p_i)\delta_i^2 +2\pi i\sum_i\ell_i\delta_i &=A_{\boldsymbol\epsilon}-2\pi i\sum_i p_i\delta_i^2 +2\pi i\sum_i\ell_i\delta_i,\\ A_{\boldsymbol\epsilon}&=A_0+\pi i\sum_i\epsilon_i\delta_i^2. \end{aligned} $$ Thus the half twists occur ONCE. The [marked action and collar identity](../papers/casimir-source-asymptotics/README.md) gives the actual primitive saddle equation $$ U_{\boldsymbol\epsilon,i}+p_iV_i=-2\pi i\ell_i. $$ Here $S_{0,\mathbf1}$ denotes the limiting critical value. At the all-unit long-filling branch, its Gaussian peripheral correction cancels exactly and $2\pi\operatorname{Re}S_{0,\mathbf1}$ is the actual smooth filling volume. Consequently the localized quantity (17), and the finite local charge sector in Section 5, have that volume as their normalized logarithmic modulus limit. The original exterior unit framing phase does not change this conclusion. This is NOT yet the original invariant's volume limit. For the FINITE selected charge set $\mathcal L$ (the sign-unit set or the finite box of section 5), define the exact remainder as the original full period (1) MINUS that finite localized sector. It is the sum of: - the finitely many $\boldsymbol\ell\in\mathcal L$, each integrated over the original full cube minus $K_b$, with its original charge factor; and - ALL $\boldsymbol\ell\notin\mathcal L$, each kept on its WHOLE original domain $[-1/2,1/2]^R$, with the original absolutely convergent summation. Do not separately sum the remote inside-$K_b$ and outside-$K_b$ pieces. The sharp boundaries would generally destroy their separate charge summability; such a split would require a specified shared regularization and its boundary cancellation. The endpoint currents are already encoded in the exact identity (1), not additional terms to append to that identity. No endpoint cancellation was discarded in deriving the finite localized formula. This exact remainder still requires a phase-preserving global estimate excluding cancellation of the nonzero contribution (17). Generic-$q$ normal derivatives are not an additional requirement for this fixed-root route; the exact marked source and all $\sigma$-Hermite data are already retained in (1)-(2). ## Validation and scope The result proves a localized contribution and its finite local charge sector; it does not prove a bound for the remaining original period or the general filled-knot volume conjecture.

title: Long filling across a finite-order zero of the original source amplitude
text: # Long filling across a finite-order zero of the original source amplitude 30 October 2026. The general original-source filling theorem does not need its leading analytic amplitude to be a unit at the complete point. A NONZERO amplitude germ is sufficient away from its pulled-back analytic zero set. That exceptional set occupies density zero among large signed integer slope boxes. Suitable rational rays avoid it eventually; a coordinate monomial times a unit avoids it at EVERY independently sufficiently long slope tuple. This removes one source hypothesis. It does not construct the required whole-source gap or complex packet for an arbitrary plat, and it does not prove that an unknown original source has a nonzero amplitude germ. The source, its full normal terms and all peripheral factors remain the ones in the [general transfer](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/general_original_source_long_filling_transfer.md). ## 1. The precise weaker packet hypothesis Fix a diagram and a chosen nonempty set of b filled circle ports. Keep the exact all-input full-twist identity, known nonzero outer factor chi_N, entire physical color-complement gap, and exponentially accurate finite corridor interpolation of the general transfer theorem. The finite packet C_N is holomorphic and even separately in all b coordinates on the SAME fixed complex neighborhood required there. Replace only its relative unit-amplitude assumption by C_N(x)=N^mu exp[N phi(x)] [a(x)+r_N(x)], sup |r_N| <= C/N, (1) uniformly holomorphically on that neighborhood. Here a is a nonzero holomorphic GERM, allowed to satisfy a(0)=0; phi is separately even, phi(0)=F0 real, phi''(0)=2pi i diag(tau_1,...,tau_b), Im tau_i>0. (2) The explicit original unit phase eta_N stays outside C_N, as before. An absolute holomorphic remainder in (1) is essential. A pointwise estimate on physical colors, or an estimate obtained by division by an amplitude that vanishes, does not supply this hypothesis. Separate evenness of a follows even if not assumed: the holomorphic functions N^(-mu) exp[-N phi] C_N are separately even and converge uniformly to a. The same is then true of r_N. Their fixed derivatives are uniformly bounded on smaller domains by Cauchy's formula. The upper Gaussian corridor estimate uses boundedness of a+r_N, not a lower bound for a, so it remains valid. If some auxiliary cusps are UNFILLED, first set their color variables to zero in the actual packet and action. The amplitude required here is the resulting restricted germ a_I(x_I)=a(x_I,0). A nonzero full germ need not have a nonzero restriction: a(x_1,x_2)=x_2^2 vanishes identically when only port 1 is filled. Such a restriction needs its own first nonzero asymptotic coefficient; it is not covered by (1). ## 2. The actual filling map and its source divisor Put epsilon_i=1/p_i for the fixed nonzero integer slopes. The minimal charge source saddle xi(epsilon) solves phi_i(xi)+pi i epsilon_i(xi_i-1)=0, 1<=i<=b. (3) The analytic implicit-function theorem gives a unique small solution, xi(0)=0, and DIRECT differentiation gives D xi(0)=diag(1/(2 tau_1),...,1/(2 tau_b)). (4) In particular xi is a local biholomorphism. The factor 2 in (4) comes from the original full-twist convention and must be retained. There is a stronger coordinatewise statement. Separate evenness writes phi_i(x)=x_i psi_i(x), where psi_i is analytic and psi_i(0)=2pi i tau_i. Equation (3) becomes xi_i=epsilon_i u_i(epsilon), u_i(epsilon)=pi i/[psi_i(xi(epsilon))+pi i epsilon_i], u_i(0)=1/(2 tau_i). (5) Every u_i is a unit on a sufficiently small common polydisk. Thus xi_i is nonzero whenever epsilon_i is nonzero, independently of the relative sizes and signs of the other coordinates. Define the pulled-back source germ f(epsilon)=a(xi(epsilon)), Z={epsilon: f(epsilon)=0}. (6) It is nonzero because xi is locally invertible. Therefore Z is a proper complex analytic zero set, with its multiplicities supplied by f. Multiplying a by a nowhere-zero analytic change of source trivialization leaves Z unchanged. This is the source divisor used here; it is not inferred from the classical A-polynomial. The map (3) involves the marked analytic action and logarithmic coordinates. Even if the exponentiated shape branch is algebraic, Z is NOT asserted to be Zariski closed in epsilon or in the slopes. ## 3. Full-source transfer off the divisor For every independently sufficiently long fixed signed tuple p with f(1/p)!=0, the full original invariant has the SAME action and N-power as the general transfer: K_N(p)=chi_N eta_N kappa^(-sum p_i) N^mu D(p) exp[N S_p] [1+O_p(N^-1)], (7) where S_p=phi(xi)+(pi i/2) sum_i (xi_i-1)^2/p_i. (8) The coefficient D(p) is nonzero. Its source-amplitude factor is exactly a(xi); no value a(0) is inserted in its place. Here is the required modification of the proof, rather than an application of a theorem whose unit hypothesis has failed. Use the same local Fourier critical map xi_F(z), action Psi(z), and determinant branches as in the general transfer. Analytic finite-window stationary phase applied to (1) gives the ABSOLUTE expansion F_N(z)=N^(mu+b/2) exp[N Psi(z)] [B(z)+O(N^-1)], B(z)=(2pi)^(b/2) a(xi_F(z)) / sqrt(det[-phi''(xi_F(z))]). (9) Both the remainder and its fixed derivatives are uniform on a smaller fixed complex neighborhood. The proof expands the bounded analytic amplitude a+r_N on the translated Gaussian contour, so it never divides by a or B. Thus (9) is valid also on their zero sets. Every global-color, finite-color-endpoint, noncentral Fourier and large-charge estimate in the transfer uses an UPPER bound for C_N and its controlled derivatives. Those estimates are unchanged by (1). The strict ordering of nonminimal charges depends on phi, not on a lower amplitude bound. For fixed p their exponential losses dominate all the bounded amplitude factors. At the second saddle use (9) in its absolute form. Put z_i*=(xi_i-1)/(2p_i), T_1(z)=Psi(z)-2pi i sum_i(p_i z_i^2+z_i). Then T_1(z*)=S_p and the leading coefficient is D(p)=Gamma(p) a(xi), Gamma(p)=2^b (2pi)^b product_i sinh(2pi i z_i*) / [sqrt(det[-phi''(xi)]) sqrt(det[-T_1''(z*)])]. (10) The determinants are nonzero on the chosen translated contours. Equation (5) and smallness imply z_i* is nonzero for each finite p_i; also |z_i*|<1/4, so its sinh factor is nonzero. Hence Gamma(p)!=0. At fixed p with a(xi)!=0, division by this now NONZERO leading coefficient turns the absolute O_p(N^-1) into the relative error in (7). Its constant may increase as p approaches Z. The 2^b minimal signed-charge sectors still ADD. Under a sign change of one charge, its saddle coordinate changes sign; the exact packet and its leading amplitude are separately even. The charge times sinh factor, determinant branch and exact parity character have the same transformation as in the original proof. This argument uses the exact source symmetry, not positivity of a. Consequently lim_N (2pi/N) log|K_N(p)|=2pi Re S_p. (11) If the SAME source branch has the actual marked representation, primitive peripheral equations and complete regulator anchor required by the general geometric completion theorem, the right side is the actual filled hyperbolic volume. Nothing in this amplitude extension supplies those independent certificates. Points in Z are excluded from this particular leading-coefficient argument. They are NOT counterexamples to a volume limit: a later Gaussian or source coefficient may give the same exponential rate. The diagram and slopes remain fixed BEFORE N tends to infinity; no joint large-N/large-slope uniformity is asserted. ## 4. Coordinate zeros permit every independently long slope Suppose on the chosen filled-coordinate chart a(x)=product_i x_i^(2 nu_i) v(x), nu_i>=0, v(0)!=0. (12) The even powers are consistent with the actual separate evenness. Combining (5) and (12) gives the exact germ factorization f(epsilon)=product_i epsilon_i^(2 nu_i) V(epsilon), V(0)!=0. (13) Thus EVERY independently sufficiently large signed nonzero tuple p avoids Z, and uniformly over those tuples, c product_i |p_i|^(-2 nu_i) <= |a(xi(1/p))| <= C product_i |p_i|^(-2 nu_i). (14) No slope-comparability condition enters. The conclusion is therefore as strong in its slope quantifier as the old unit-amplitude transfer. For ONE filled cusp every nonzero separately-even analytic germ automatically has the form (12), so the complete-point unit assumption can always be dropped in that one-variable case. For completeness the known filling prefactor also has a uniform magnitude comparison. Here z_i*=(-epsilon_i/2)(1+O(||epsilon||)) and diag(epsilon_i) T_1''(z*)=-4pi i I+O(||epsilon||). The other Hessian remains bounded and invertible. Formula (10) gives |Gamma(p)| comparable to product_i |p_i|^(-3/2), on each signed orthant, and hence on their finite union. Under (12), |D(p)| is comparable to product_i |p_i|^(-2 nu_i-3/2). This is a statement about the slope-dependent leading coefficient, not a uniform error estimate when slopes grow with quantum level N. ## 5. Rational-ray survival for a general nonzero amplitude Let d be the vanishing order of f at zero, including d=0 for a unit, and let P_d be its first nonzero homogeneous Taylor polynomial. For fixed nonzero signed integers q_1,...,q_b with P_d(1/q_1,...,1/q_b)!=0, (15) the ray p_i=n q_i satisfies f(1/(nq))=n^(-d)[P_d(1/q)+O_q(n^-1)]. (16) Every sufficiently large n therefore avoids Z, with magnitude comparable to n^(-d). Applying (7) separately at each fixed ray point gives its full quantum volume limit whenever the geometric certificates hold. The ray parameter n is not the quantum level N. There is such a rational ray in EVERY prescribed sign orthant. Indeed multiply P_d(1/q) by product_i q_i^d. The result is a nonzero polynomial in the q_i. A nonzero polynomial cannot vanish on the entire product of infinite one-sided integer sets: fix all but one variable, use the finite root count, and induct on the number of variables. This proves existence without assuming rational or algebraic coefficients for P_d. Condition (15) is sufficient, not necessary. A ray on which P_d vanishes may have a nonzero higher-order coefficient in f. ## 6. Density one in every large signed integer box Fix signs sigma_i. Among tuples p_i=sigma_i n_i, T<=n_i<=2T, n_i integers, the number lying in Z is o(T^b) as the integer scale T tends to infinity. Thus the proportion for which (7) applies tends to one. This does not assert that ALL tuples avoid Z or that its exact integer points lie in a fixed algebraic hypersurface. Here is an elementary counting proof. Put t_i=n_i/T in [1,2]. Uniform analytic Taylor remainder estimates on this compact set give T^d f(sigma_1/(Tt_1),...,sigma_b/(Tt_b)) =P_d(sigma_1/t_1,...,sigma_b/t_b)+O(T^-1). Therefore a bad tuple satisfies |Q(t)|<=C/T, where the NONZERO polynomial Q(t)=product_i t_i^d P_d(sigma_1/t_1,...,sigma_b/t_b) has no negative powers. Choose a nonzero real polynomial R from the real or imaginary part of Q. On [1,3]^b its first derivatives are bounded. To each bad grid point t attach the disjoint half-open cube product_i[t_i,t_i+1/T). Every point of that cube then satisfies |R|<=C'/T, with one fixed constant C'. Hence #bad/T^b <= volume{x in [1,3]^b: |R(x)|<=C'/T}. (17) A nonzero real polynomial has zero set of Lebesgue measure zero. For a direct proof, write it as a polynomial in its last variable. Except on the common zero set of its coefficients, contained in the zero set of one nonzero lower-dimensional coefficient, every fiber has finitely many roots. Induction and Fubini prove the claim. The sublevel sets on the right of (17) decrease to that zero set, so continuity of finite measure makes their volumes tend to zero. This proves the stated density without a quantitative sublevel or Diophantine theorem. The unit case d=0 is immediate as well. ## 7. Finite level classes and exact scope The argument also covers finitely many level classes, for example even and odd N, with the SAME phi and separate uniform expansions (1) having nonzero germs a_r. All original class-dependent unit phases are retained. Use the finite union of their divisors. Outside it each class has (7), possibly with its own nonzero coefficient; the exponential limit (11) holds along the full sequence. The union still has density zero in each signed slope box. A rational ray avoiding the product of the finitely many first nonzero Taylor polynomials avoids every divisor eventually. If each amplitude is a coordinate monomial times a unit, every independently long tuple works at all the level classes. For partial fillings these nonzero-germ checks must again be made AFTER restricting the unfilled variables. The advance is removal of the complete-point UNIT requirement, including arithmetic survival of many long fillings. A proven nonzero finite-order marked source amplitude can now be used even when its complete value vanishes. The exact mixed source, its global gap, its uniform complex packet and its actual geometric marking remain necessary. No arbitrary-plat equality, whole knot A-polynomial identification, or nonzero-source theorem is inferred from this lemma. Audit: [implicit saddle, coordinate zeros and integer-slope examples](../experiments/audit_general_long_filling_source_divisor.py). The density-one statement is proved by the analytic rescaling and measure argument above, not by the finite counts in that audit. The source and geometric hypotheses remain conditional as stated. They are not established here for arbitrary plats.

title: Arbitrary-depth marked unit-chain extensions of balanced plats
text: # Arbitrary-depth marked unit-chain extensions of balanced plats structural theorem, 31 October 2026. A balanced original plat can admit arbitrarily many additional independently twisted regions at the **same fixed bridge width**. The construction below preserves its original marked cap and every old circle radius. It is a literal source operation, not a claim about arbitrary stacking of plats or abstract gluing of matched graphs. ## 1. Hypotheses and full-invariant conclusion Let $D$ be a fixed original flat $2k$-plat, $k\geq2$, with $R$ ordered crossing regions. Assume: - Its first zero-based box slot is $1$. - No box uses slot $0$. - The first original top cap, on slots $(0,1)$, is marked. - Its white sphere is simple, carries the actual labeled right-angled certificate, and its one complete marked packing satisfies the [complete-radius balance condition](../papers/planar-certificates/README.md) at every port. Retain every original half-twist sign and the original cup/cap conventions. For any integer $m\geq0$, form the literal bottom-to-top word $$ D^{(m)}=(1,2)^mD.\tag{1} $$ Each new box has half-twist $\epsilon=0$ and an independent signed integer full-twist parameter $p$, hence actual braid exponent $-2p$. Slot $j$ is conventional braid generator $\sigma_{j+1}$, so the added braid is $$ \prod_{j=1}^{m}\sigma_2^{-2p_{j,1}}\sigma_3^{-2p_{j,2}}. $$ No old box is combined, deleted, moved or reinterpreted. The new number of crossing regions is $R+2m$. **Theorem.** The original marked diagram $D^{(m)}$ is again certified and simple-white, and every port satisfies complete-radius balance. If the original parity gives a knot, the extended diagram still gives a knot. For each fixed $m$, there is a threshold $T(D,m)$ such that every independently signed fixed filling vector with all parameters above that threshold in absolute value satisfies $$ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N}\log\left|K_N\!\left(K_{D^{(m)},\mathbf p}\right)\right| =\operatorname{Vol}\!\left(S^3\setminus K_{D^{(m)},\mathbf p}\right).\tag{2} $$ This is the full original normalized invariant, both level parities and the entire original charge sum, through the general balance theorem. Every twist is fixed before $N\to\infty$; no comparison of their magnitudes is required. The threshold is not asserted to be uniform in $m$. In particular, the [one-end-layer cores](general_one_end_layer_long_filling_volume.md) $O_kE_k^{\mathrm{right}}O_k$ satisfy these hypotheses. Thus for every fixed $k\geq2$ and every $m\geq0$, (1) supplies $3k-3+2m$ independently long signed twist regions. This is arbitrary depth at fixed width. The added alternating tangle acts on the first four physical strands; the claim does not say that each added layer spans all $2k$ strands. The case $m=0$ is unchanged. Assume $m\geq1$ in the source patch and balance arguments of Sections 2–4. ## 2. Exact original gap dictionary The absence of slot $0$ means the bottom odd-gap face $v$ on slots $(0,1)$ remains the first top-cap face. It is the protected face paired with the exterior $u$. Before the first box, every internal even gap belongs to $u$. Hence the first port of $D$ is $$ (v,u,e,a),\tag{3} $$ where $a$ is the bottom odd-gap face on slots $(2,3)$. Simplicity makes $e$ an ordinary face distinct from $u,v,a$; $a$ is also ordinary. All other regions and cyclic port orders are those of $D$. For the prefix, let $a^{(0)}$ be the original bottom face in gap $3$, set $f_0=u$, and let $f_j,a^{(j)}$ be the new faces created by the $j$th pair $(1,2)$. The literal sweep gives $$ \begin{aligned} \text{slot }1_j &: (v,f_{j-1},f_j,a^{(j-1)}),\\ \text{slot }2_j &: (f_j,a^{(j-1)},a^{(j)},u), \qquad1\leq j\leq m. \end{aligned}\tag{4} $$ The right outer region at slot $2$ is still $u$: the prefix never crosses the next even gap, whether it is internal for $k>2$ or exterior for $k=2$. Identify the old core face $a$ with $a^{(m)}$. The first core port becomes $$ (v,f_m,e,a^{(m)}).\tag{5} $$ Every later core quartet is unchanged under that one face relabeling. The mark remains $u,v$. This is an exact instance of the [original Morse face dictionary](../papers/filling-bounds/README.md), without isotopy, stabilization or a change to the quantum marked cap. ## 3. The actual empty gap and complete packing Normalize the old marked disks as the outside halfplanes below $Y=0$ and above $Y=2$. The original triangle $(v,u,a)$ implies that $a$ is tangent to both lines and has radius $1$. Translate its center to $(0,1)$. This triangle is one of the two marked-edge triangular interstices. Choose the one global horizontal reflection so it is the empty right complementary component of the marked strip. The unit disk $a$ touches both strip boundaries and separates the strip into left and right components. Every other old finite disk lies in the left component: otherwise the actual triangular interstice would contain another disk or the embedded contact graph would cross its boundary. The right component is therefore empty. This uses the actual labeled embedded packing, not an assumed gap in an arbitrary developed configuration. Leave every old disk unchanged. For $0\leq j\leq m$, set $$ \operatorname{center}(a^{(j)})=(4(m-j),1),\qquad \operatorname{radius}(a^{(j)})=1, $$ where $a^{(m)}$ is the old disk $a$. For $1\leq j\leq m$, set $$ \operatorname{center}(f_j)=(4(m-j)+2,1),\qquad \operatorname{radius}(f_j)=1.\tag{6} $$ The $2m$ new disks form a chain in the actual empty right component. Consecutive disks are tangent, and nonconsecutive disks have disjoint interiors and no contact. Every new disk touches both marked lines. Only $f_m$ touches an old finite disk, namely $a^{(m)}$. Thus no unintended old/new contact occurs. More explicitly, if another old disk has center $(X,Y)$, then $X<0$. Its squared support slack against a new unit disk at $(s,1)$, $s\geq2$, equals its nonnegative slack against $a$ plus $s^2-2sX>0$. The triangles in (4)–(5) are exactly the gaps above and below this chain. At the far right, $(v,u,a^{(0)})$ replaces the old unbounded triangle $(v,u,a)$. The other triangle $(v,a,e)$ of the old first port is unchanged. Equivalently, one old triangular disk has been replaced by a triangulated disk with $2m$ additional vertices and the same original boundary. The new source sphere is simple, and the displayed packing realizes precisely its contact graph and cyclic order. The [proved simple-white packing construction](actual_smoothed_source_capacity_blocks.md), Sections 4–5, supplies its actual labeled right-angled cut balls. Marked uniqueness and contact-center development identify this packing with the normalized complete source packing. Every old ordinary curvature is unchanged; every new curvature equals $1$. No separate radii are chosen for different ports. ## 4. Exact balance at every port Use the original half-degree triangle action and put $$ C_0=Q(0,1,1)=\frac{2G}{\pi}>0,\qquad Q(0,0,1)=0,\tag{7} $$ where $G$ is Catalan's constant. These constants have the [original source normalization](actual_zero_middle_nine_quarter_balance.md). The first new slot-$1$ port has outer weights $(0,1)$ and middle weights $(0,1)$, hence balance gap $C_0$. Every later new slot-$1$ port has outer weights $(0,1)$ and middle weights $(1,1)$, hence gap $2C_0$. Every new slot-$2$ port has outer weights $(1,0)$ and middle weights $(1,1)$, again gap $2C_0$. For the modified first core port, the outer curvatures are $v=0$ and $a=1$. Its old middles were $0$ and $E=\operatorname{curvature}(e)>0$. Every finite disk inside the height-$2$ strip has radius at most $1$, so $E\geq1$. Before and after the modification, the largest positive middle logarithm is therefore $\log E$. The old action sum was $Q(0,E,1)$; the new sum is $$ Q(0,1,1)+Q(0,E,1),\tag{8} $$ larger by exactly $C_0$. The old strict balance is preserved. All other core ports retain their weights and balance gaps exactly. The minimum local balance margin of $D^{(m)}$ is at least the smaller of the old minimum margin and $C_0$, independently of $m$. This does not make the analytic filling threshold uniform in $m$: the number of ports, source constants and geometric filling data still depend on the extended diagram. ## 5. Retained phases, knots and bridge number Every new exponent $-2p$ is even, of either sign, so its endpoint permutation is the identity. The new boxes do not change the original component graph. Every original half twist remains in its original box, and the marked cap remains fixed. These even exponents are independent genuine crossing regions; their trivial endpoint permutation is not an identity on the finite quantum source. For each fixed extended diagram, its certificate and proved balance let the [full-source theorem](../papers/planar-certificates/README.md) control the entire one-sided remainder and apply the original all-charge filling theorem. This proves (2), including the original normalization and sufficiently long smooth hyperbolic filling. The conclusion is not inferred from the packing picture alone. If the original parity gives a knot and all old and new full exponents are additionally divisible by $3$, the [Fox-coloring certificate](actual_fox_coloring_exact_plat_bridge.md) gives exactly $3^k$ colorings. The supplied $2k$-plat then has minimal bridge number exactly $k$. For the new boxes, this condition is $p\equiv0\pmod3$. Every required congruence allows independent arbitrarily large positive and negative parameters. It is used only for the bridge lower bound, not for the volume theorem. ## Validation and scope The operation applies to every core satisfying the stated hypotheses, not only the one-end template. It does not prove balance for arbitrary multilayer plats or arbitrary marks. It preserves the original protected edge and all old disk coordinates; no generic re-framing invariance is used. The focused audit checks finite literal core/depth charts and exact width-two/width-three packing extensions. These checks supplement the general source patch and empty-gap proof; they do not infer the uniform or quantum theorem by sampling. The [focused exact audit](../experiments/audit_general_marked_unit_chain_filling_volume.py) and [recorded results](../experiments/general_marked_unit_chain_filling_volume_results.json) reproduce 56 original extended charts, 1176 quartets, 2352 triangles, 3528 edges and 56 knot-parity checks, together with 12 exact seed extensions, 1084 circle/line pair supports, 84 new unit-port tests and 12 changed core-port tests.

title: The full original augmented-plat source on its matching graph
text: # The full original augmented-plat source on its matching graph 30 October 2026. EVERY fixed original augmented plat has an exact state sum on the SAME marked cubic graph Delta as its geometric projection/disk cut. The nonmatching edges carry the physical V_N; a matching edge carries an ordinary Q_j=V_(2j), summed over ALL folded labels. Every term is the original first normal of its genuine generic pivotal closure. The statement holds at both parities and composite levels, with the actual paired nilpotent circle sectors retained. This is a full complete-circle source identity, not merely a selected central sector. It supplies the source-compatible graph to be resummed. It proves no positivity, dominant branch, mixed auxiliary-color packet, or volume asymptotic. ## 1. The actual complete-circle factorization Fix an original 2k-plat with r crossing boxes, all outside wires and cups/caps recorded, signed retained exponents epsilon_i, and ONE exposed original marked physical arc. Put d=N-1, M=floor(d/2), q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, s_u=product_(v=1)^u 2sin(pi v/N), s_0=1. The all-input complete circle is the sum of its full folded sectors. The proved physical factorization in [the original all-channel source](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_trivalent_all_channel_marked_contraction.md) is L_N=sum_(j=0)^M L_j, R^epsilon L_j=omega_j^epsilon h0_j W_j pi_j, pi_j=G_j^-1 W_j^dagger P, G_(j,a)=s_(2j)/(s_a s_(2j-a)), h0_j=k_j N s_(2j)/s_j^2, k_j=2 if 2j<d, k_j=1 if 2j=d, omega_j=q^(d^2/2) (-1)^j q^[j(j+1)]. (1) Here W_j:Q_j->V_N tensor V_N is the actual first-entry-one Clebsch map, and P is the original two-head reversal. Crucially, pi_j W_j=0 on a paired node, pi_j W_j=I on the odd simple node 2j=d. (2) Thus W_j pi_j is not generally a projector. Formula (1) includes the circle's original first-normal coefficient before introducing Q_j; no semisimple root quotient is made. All input physical degrees are included in (1). ## 2. Split the actual graph, preserving its typed vertices For a fixed label vector j=(j_1,...,j_r), split each coupon as W_j pi_j. Its intermediate edge Q_j is exactly the crossing-disk edge d_i in Delta. The remaining legs follow the actual outside main intervals and carry V_N. The vertex cyclic orders are the disk-side sectors of [the matching-graph construction](../papers/marked-fillings/README.md). Consequently the state graph has matching edges D: Q_(j_i), nonmatching edges: V_N, vertices: the actual ordered W_(j_i) or pi_(j_i). (3) Every vertex has two physical legs and one matching-channel leg. This requires no bipartite coloring, no Fisher structure, and no ordering of all black vertices below all white ones. Cups/caps and actual head reversals are retained at every bend. One does not replace a cyclic turn by an unclocked index permutation. Let Z_Delta(j) denote the contraction in (3) with the original exposed physical mark, after removing only the displayed scalar factors in (1). Multilinearity of the actual ordered coupon word gives A_(D,N)=sum_(j in {0,...,M}^r) product_i[h0_(j_i) omega_(j_i)^epsilon_i] Z_Delta(j). (4) This is the raw source before its independently recorded exterior framing line. Physical coupons in overlapping strand positions have not been commuted. Only the independent finite color sums distribute over their original order. ## 3. An explicit regular generic lift at EVERY folded label Keep N and the root constants h0_j,omega_j fixed. Let zeta=q exp(t) and use the generic balanced highest-weight-d object V_d(zeta), with Q=zeta^2 and F_u=(Q;Q)_u. Its actual physical cup is pV_(a,d-a)=N zeta^(-d^2) (-1)^a zeta^[a(d-a-1)] F_a F_(d-a)/F_d, ellV=pV^-1. (5) On Q_j choose the ordinary highest-weight-2j cup pQ_j with first coefficient one, given by the same formula with d replaced by 2j and the initial scale omitted. All its factorial indices are <N. The regular W_j(t) has highest degree l=d-j and coefficients h_u(t)=(-1)^u zeta^(-du) Q^[u(l-1)-u(u-1)/2] (Q^(j+1);Q)_u F_(d-u)/F_d, W_(j,a)(t)=F_pair(t)^a h(t)/F_a, 0<=a<=2j. (6) All denominator indices in (5),(6) are below N.
