The original highest recurrence and divided coproduct prove its generic Hopf covariance, including its last endpoint; this is the already checked finite construction in the cited all-channel note. Put gamma_j=q^(2-j^2)/N^2, a FIXED nonzero root constant, and define pi_j(t)=gamma_j^-1 D_t(W_j(t)), D_t(W_j)=pQ_j(t)^T W_j(t)^T [ellV(t)^T tensor ellV(t)^T] P. (7) At t=0 this is exactly pi_j of (1). Equation (7) retains the ordinary cup normalization, both physical inverse cups, reversed tensor order and gamma_j. It divides by NO vanishing paired norm pi_j W_j. Thus W_j(t)pi_j(t) is a regular generic Hopf coupon whose root is the actual normalized circle sector, at both parities. This is a chosen lift of a fixed-root map. It is not asserted to be the original circle's entire moving-q germ, nor a new off-root link invariant. That distinction causes no ambiguity in the marked root scalar below. ## 4. Every marked sector is ONE retained trace normal Let F_Delta(j;t) be the ordinary closed original diagram obtained by using the regular W_j(t)pi_j(t) coupons, the original outside cups/caps, and an ordinary cap also at the chosen marked arc. Splitting its coupons gives exactly the typed generic network (3), with (5)--(7). Leave that exposed physical arc open. Generic Hopf covariance makes the resulting endomorphism of V_d a scalar z_Delta(j;t) I: generic K has distinct weights and every interior F arrow is nonzero, so its commutant is scalar. All entries are regular, so z_Delta is holomorphic. The literal physical closure therefore gives F_Delta(j;t)=D_N(t) z_Delta(j;t), D_N(t)=(-1)^d [N]_(q exp(t)), D_N(0)=0, nu_N=D_N'(0)=2N(-1)^N/(q-q^-1) !=0. (8) The original unrestricted root marked row has m pV(0)=1. After the other actual caps act, the remaining column is z_Delta(j;0)pV(0), so that mark extracts precisely z_Delta(j;0). Hence Z_Delta(j)=F_Delta'(j;0)/nu_N. (9) Only the physical trace factor is divided out. The mark is not put on a channel Q_j, whose dimension or norm could vanish, and no bare mark is moved through an enclosing cap. The exposed one-head cut is part of the specified original diagram. If another regular generic Hopf lift has the same root coupons, it has the same root open endomorphism and marked scalar. Its ordinary closure differs by D_N(t) times a holomorphic scalar vanishing at zero, so its normalized first derivative is the same. This proves the required lift independence without identifying moving-q germs. Combining (4),(9) gives the full source theorem: A_(D,N)=(1/nu_N) sum_(j in {0,...,M}^r) product_i[h0_(j_i) omega_(j_i)^epsilon_i] F_Delta'(j;0). (10) Equivalently the first derivative is taken after summing the regular finite physical networks. For fixed N the sum is finite. Its regular physical presentation needs only first jets; a singular recoupling frame may require higher Laurent coefficients before its pole cancellations recover this same first normal. ## 5. The special odd endpoint and the exact geometric target For N=2m+1 and all j_i=m, Q_j=V_N, h0_m=N and pi_m W_m=I. Then all edges of Delta carry the same ordinary object, and (10)'s central contribution is N^r omega_m^(sum epsilon_i) F_Delta'(m,...,m;0)/nu_N. This recovers the earlier endpoint interface, without extending its projector argument to even levels. Equation (10) includes the paired sectors at every parity instead of discarding them. If Delta has the actual positive right-angled ideal polyhedron Q_Delta, its shaded triangles are the source vertices in (3), and its ideal vertices are the source edges. The literal quotient gives the actual complete augmented volume 2Vol(Q_Delta). Coning Q_Delta and using the identical subdivisions in its second copy gives a marked positive ideal triangulation T. Its GLOBAL angle polytope is sum_(three opposite pairs in t) alpha_(t,a)=pi, sum_(all tetrahedral incidences at global e) alpha_(t,e)=2pi, alpha>=0. (11) All incidence coefficients come from the actual complete face-pairing words, including the shaded half twists. The [proved positive gluing theorem](../papers/marked-fillings/README.md) gives its unique positive maximum and absolute value max_(11) sum_t V_ideal(alpha_t)=2Vol(Q_Delta). (12) A separately certified marked positive triangulation may replace Q_Delta. Thus (10) and (11) are now on the same actual topology. An exact coherent resummation must STILL show how its state variables map to these edge incidences and how its retained source action equals the single constrained functional (12). Ordinary spin triangle inequalities or independently maximized vertex factorials do not supply (11). The original phase obstruction excludes independent magnetic-leg positive gauges; it does not exclude a coherent positive resummation. The NC class is recovered when Delta is the Fisher expansion of its source graph Gamma. Its facial triangle contractions give the known local coefficients and the Gamma-network first normal. The odd cube's clocked rung resummation gives a positive global Newton period and its shared core action. Those are actual special reductions of (10), not a proof that every Delta has the same positive form. ## 6. What this settles and what remains Equation (10) is a full-source matching-graph state sum for every fixed plat width. It retains all internal folded labels, both level parities, all paired nilpotent circles, actual cup/dual constants and one original mark. No vanishing root norm is inverted. The external line is not renormalized using a hoped-for answer. It permits zero sectors and zero whole source values. It does not prove endpoint dominance or even complete-color nonvanishing. It is not yet the mixed auxiliary-circle-color packet required for long fillings. Those fillings still require the whole-color gap, selected geometric cycle, actual peripheral branch and unit logarithmic charge. A formal first-normal formula alone provides none of those estimates. ## 7. Coverage only and exact verification [Van der Veen, arXiv:0805.0094v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0805.0094), Definitions 1--2 and Theorem 2, starts with a specified KTG-move sequence and gives a sufficient augmentation multiplicity. Its stated formula holds at ODD N and is zero at EVEN N, with an explicitly so(3) conclusion. Its singly augmented outside is built from regular ideal octahedra. That is not an all-level theorem for every single- circle matching graph or for all independently long fillings. Only its definitions and theorem statements are used here for coverage. [Ibarra--McQuire--Purcell](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.09296) addresses OCTAHEDRAL fully augmented links, states its TV result without half twists, and sets Dehn fillings aside. The invariant and root differ from the original marked source here. [Belletti](https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.01904) states a Yokota upper-bound conjecture, results for a specified large family and TV consequences. Neither supplies the original coherent first-normal estimate for arbitrary Delta. No proof technique from those papers is used here. [The exact audit](../experiments/audit_general_matching_graph_full_normal_source.py) checks eight original plats at N=2,...,6 and widths k=2,3,4. It checks 204 fixed-label generic trace normals and five EXHAUSTIVE color sums, using independently constructed original Casimir/circle/R matrices. It explicitly verifies the paired zero pi_j W_j, the complete circle sum, actual signed twists, and the unrestricted marked contraction. The outside-interval compiler also checks every oriented matching-graph face. The regular generic jets retain (5)--(7) before specialization. [Recorded results](../experiments/general_matching_graph_full_normal_source_results.json). These are exact source-identity checks, not finite-level evidence for an unproved nonvanishing or asymptotic claim. The four-box width-two fixture has positions (1,0,2,1), zero based. Its two middle circles surround complementary pairs in a transverse four-punctured sphere and cobound the unpunctured annulus between those pairs. They are parallel augmentations, so this fixture is NOT an essential hyperbolic skeleton. The source also explains its even zeros: on the regular four-head invariant space the two complementary pair Casimirs agree, by the actual generic cup duality. Their circle product is therefore L_N^2, which is zero at even levels. The retained disjoint half twists commute with this product. These exact zeros are not being presented as hyperbolic counterexamples. The audit tests the finite source identity even on such degenerate diagrams. The even-zero fixture is the stated parallel-circle obstruction. Formula (10) does not imply nonvanishing, select a geometric branch, or give a general asymptotic.

title: Long-filling volume for one-end-layer plats at every bridge width
status: Full original invariant at every k ≥ 2; exact-bridge subfamilies
text: # Long-filling volume for one-end-layer plats at every bridge width theorem, 31 October 2026. This is a right-end extension of the [reduced-layer construction](general_reduced_layer_long_filling_volume.md). It retains the original flat-plat source, first-cap mark, all half twists and all independently signed full twists. The proof covers every $k\geq2$; it does not assert balance for every certified plat. ## 1. Exact word and conclusion Number physical adjacent slots from $0$ to $2k-2$, so slot $j$ is conventional braid generator $\sigma_{j+1}$. Define $$ \begin{gathered} O_k=(1,3,\ldots,2k-3),\qquad E_k^{\mathrm{right}}=(2,4,\ldots,2k-2),\\ D_k^{\mathrm{right}}=O_kE_k^{\mathrm{right}}O_k,\qquad R=3k-3. \end{gathered}\tag{1} $$ Keep the standard adjacent cup/cap pairs and mark the first original top cap on slots $(0,1)$. In conventional generator notation, the actual filled braid is $$ \begin{aligned} \beta_k(\mathbf p)={}& \left(\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}\sigma_{2j}^{\epsilon_j-2p_{1,j}}\right) \left(\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}\sigma_{2j+1}^{-2p_{2,j}}\right)\\ &\quad\times\left(\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}\sigma_{2j}^{-2p_{3,j}}\right). \end{aligned}\tag{2} $$ with each $\epsilon_j=+1$ or $-1$ fixed. All products retain bottom-to-top order and increasing $j$ within the layer. The first O layer is odd; the other two layers are even. Its plat is therefore a knot, as checked again below. Write $K_k(\mathbf p)$ for this plat. **Theorem.** For every fixed $k\geq2$ and fixed first-layer sign pattern there is a threshold $T(k,\boldsymbol\epsilon)$ such that for every integer vector $\mathbf p$ with all $|p_{r,j}|\geq T$, fixed before $N$ tends to infinity, the full original normalized root invariant obeys $$ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N}\log|K_N(K_k(\mathbf p))| =\operatorname{Vol}\bigl(S^3\setminus K_k(\mathbf p)\bigr).\tag{3} $$ All $3k-3$ twist parameters can have independent signs and magnitudes. The result holds at both level parities. No comparability of twist magnitudes or joint growing-twist/level limit is asserted. Moreover, in the congruence subfamily where every exponent in (2) is divisible by $3$, the minimal bridge number is exactly $k$. The congruence is used only for that lower bound, not for (3). Here $K_N$ denotes the original normalized root invariant, with the framing and component conventions of the [exact original period](general_localized_unit_charge_filling_period.md). The analytic implication is the [general complete-radius balance theorem](../papers/planar-certificates/README.md). It remains to prove its hypotheses for the actual source (1), uniformly in $k$, which occupies Sections 2–5 below. ## 2. Literal incidence, simple certificate and reflection Let $u$ be the exterior, $a_0,\ldots,a_{k-1}$ the bottom odd-gap faces, and $e_1,\ldots,e_{k-1}$ the first-layer bounded even-gap faces. The middle layer changes $a_j$ to $b_j$ for every $1\leq j\leq k-1$, while $a_0$ remains unchanged. Set $b_0=a_0$ and $e_k=u$. All other names are distinct. The literal gap sweep gives $$ \begin{array}{lll} \text{first }O:&(a_{j-1},u,e_j,a_j),&1\leq j\leq k-1,\\ \text{middle }E:&(e_j,a_j,b_j,e_{j+1}),&1\leq j\leq k-1,\\ \text{final }O:&(b_{j-1},e_j,u,b_j),&1\leq j\leq k-1. \end{array}\tag{4} $$ Each quartet has the original two triangles $(x,b,y),(x,y,c)$. The protected pair is $u,a_0$ on its original MAIN edge. There is no graph- to-plat adapter or isotopy in this description. The MAIN edges are $u-a_i$, $u-b_i$ (sharing only $u-a_0$ at the left end) and $e_j-a_{j-1},e_j-a_j,e_j-b_{j-1},e_j-b_j$ (sharing only $e_1-a_0$). The MATCHING edges are the two chains $a_{j-1}-a_j$ and $b_{j-1}-b_j$, and the chain $e_1-e_2-\cdots-e_{k-1}-u$. All these edges have distinct endpoints; none is repeated as a separate edge. This includes $k=2$: the three matching edges are $a_0-a_1,a_0-b_1,e_1-u$. Every listed edge is incident to exactly two of the actual triangles in (4), by the same gap incidence pairing as in the reduced family, with the right middle-E box now closing against the exterior. The inherited sphere has $$ V=3k-1,\qquad E=9k-9,\qquad F=6k-6,\qquad V-E+F=2.\tag{5} $$ Thus the white cellulation is a simple triangulated sphere for every $k\geq2$. The [existing simple-block construction](actual_smoothed_source_capacity_blocks.md) gives the actual labeled convex ideal right-angled packing and its original two cut balls. There is an orientation-reversing sphere automorphism $a_i\leftrightarrow b_i$, fixing $u,a_0,e_1,\ldots,e_{k-1}$, and interchanging the first/final layers. Normalize the original marked tangency $u-a_0$ to infinity, with $u$ the outside lower half-plane $Y\leq0$ and $a_0$ the outside upper half-plane $Y\geq2$. Uniqueness of the marked positive curvature solution up to scale, followed by unique contact-center development, realizes the automorphism by a vertical reflection. Translate its axis to $X=0$. This is precisely the uniqueness/reflection argument in the reduced-family proof, with the same connected ordinary-face Hessian. In particular the actual curvatures satisfy $A_i=B_i$. Put $L=k-1$. The fixed graph cycle is $$ u-a_0-e_1-e_2-\cdots-e_L-u. $$ It separates the original sphere into the a-side and b-side triangulated disks. The ordered axis chain now runs from the upper marked line through $e_1,\ldots,e_L$ to the lower marked line, with no extra endpoint a-circle on the axis. All $a_i$ lie on one side, all $b_i$ on the other: this follows from the consistently oriented a-side triangles along the fixed chain, including the last triangle $(a_L,e_L,u)$. Choose the a-side to be $X>0$. The fixed disks have disjoint axis intervals, ordered strictly from top to bottom. Write $$ \begin{gathered} y_0=2>y_1>\cdots>y_{L-1}>y_L=0,\\ \operatorname{radius}(e_j)=\frac{y_{j-1}-y_j}{2},\qquad E_j=\operatorname{curvature}(e_j)=\frac2{y_{j-1}-y_j}. \end{gathered}\tag{6} $$ For $L=1$ this means $e_1$ is the unit disk centered at $(0,1)$. ## 3. Height recurrence with the correct right boundary For $1\leq i\leq L-1$ the ordinary right-side circle $a_i$ is tangent to $u$ and both $e_i,e_{i+1}$. If its center is $(X_i,r_i)$, elementary tangency gives $$ 2r_i=\frac{y_i(y_{i-1}-y_{i+1})}{y_{i-1}-y_i},\qquad X_i^2=\frac{y_{i-1}y_i(y_i-y_{i+1})}{y_{i-1}-y_i}.\tag{7} $$ These are actual squared-distance identities, not a continuation past a zero height. The final circle $a_L$ is treated separately in Section 5. Set $$ z_j=\sqrt{1-\frac{y_j}{y_{j-1}}}\quad(1\leq j\leq L), \qquad z_0=0,\qquad z_L=1.\tag{8} $$ For $L\geq2$ the first pair $a_1,b_1$ touches both marked lines, so $r_1=1$. Using $y_0=2$ in (7) gives $$ (1-z_1^2)(1+z_2)=1.\tag{9} $$ At every other interior index $2\leq j\leq L-1$ use actual tangency of consecutive right-side circles $a_{j-1},a_j$. With $p=z_{j-1}$, $z=z_j$, $w=z_{j+1}$, and $q=1-z^2$, the same substitution as in the reduced proof gives $$ 1-2q(1+pw)+q^2(1-p^2)(1-w^2)=0.\tag{10} $$ For $w<1$, its second root $1/[(1-p)(1-w)]$ exceeds $1$ and is excluded by the actual height ratio $0<q<1$. At the last such index $w=z_L=1$, the quadratic becomes the exact linear equation $1-2q(1+p)=0$. Both cases, together with (9), yield $$ (1+z_{j-1})(1-z_j^2)(1+z_{j+1})=1, \qquad 1\leq j\leq L-1.\tag{11} $$ There is no equation at $j=L$ and no evaluation of $f$ at $\log2$ below. This is the new boundary condition; the old zero-endpoint equation must not be imposed on the added end box. ## 4. Uniform interior bound, including $k=2$ and $k=3$ For $L\geq3$ let $v_j=\log(1+z_j)$, with $v_0=0$, $v_L=\log2$ and $0<v_j<\log2$ at all interior indices. The same strictly convex function $$ f(v)=-v-\log(2-e^v),\qquad f (0)=0,\qquad f''(v)=\frac{2e^v}{(2-e^v)^2}>0. $$ satisfies $$ f(v_j)=v_{j-1}+v_{j+1},\qquad1\leq j\leq L-1.\tag{12} $$ Place the exact three-node seed $$ (\log(5/3),\log(9/5),\log(5/3)). $$ at any consecutive three positions among $1,\ldots,L$ and extend by zeros. Call the resulting vector $s$, with $s_0=0$. At every interior index, $f(s_j)\leq s_{j-1}+s_{j+1}$, while the right boundary automatically obeys $s_L\leq\log2=v_L$. Put $t=\max_{1\leq j\leq L}(s_j/v_j)$. If $t>1$, its attaining index must be interior. At that index strict convexity gives $f(s_j)>t f(v_j)$, while the neighbor comparison gives $f(s_j)\leq t f(v_j)$, a contradiction. Therefore $v\geq s$. Every interior index lies in a translated seed, so $$ z_j\geq\frac23,\qquad1\leq j\leq L-1.\tag{13} $$ The inclusion of position $L$ in a translated seed is legitimate because it is compared only as a boundary value; $f(\log2)$ is never evaluated. For $L=2$, equation (9) with $z_2=1$ gives $z_1=1/\sqrt2>2/3$ exactly. For $L=1$ there is no interior index. Thus (13) holds wherever needed for every $k\geq2$, with these exact small-width interpretations. ## 5. Curvature ratios and the last physical interstice For $j<L$, let $p=z_{j-1}$, $z=z_j$ and $D_0=p^2+z^2-p^2z^2>0$. The physical formulas (7) and recurrence (11) give exactly $$ \begin{aligned} \frac{A_{j-1}}{E_j}&=\frac{p^2z^2}{D_0},& \frac{A_j}{E_j}&=\frac{z^4(1+p)^2}{D_0},\\ \frac{A_{j-1}+A_j}{E_j} &=z^2\left[1+\frac{2p(1+p)z^2}{D_0}\right]\geq z^2. \end{aligned}\tag{14} $$ At $j=1$ this includes $A_0=0$ and $r_1=1$. At $j=L-1$ it uses $w=1$ only through the valid linear boundary recurrence, and all circles in (7) are still genuine finite disks. Therefore (13),(14) give $$ \frac{E_j}{A_{j-1}+A_j}\leq\frac94,\qquad1\leq j<L.\tag{15} $$ It remains to check the actual final O ports, involving $e_L$ and $a_L$. For $L\geq2$, the circle $a_L$ has exactly three white neighbors: the lower line $u$, $e_L$, and $a_{L-1}$. These three neighbors are pairwise tangent. The a-side disk decomposition places $a_L$ in their bounded curvilinear interstice next to the $u-e_L$ contact; its reflected partner lies in the opposite interstice. The positive Descartes branch is consequently $$ A_L=A_{L-1}+E_L+2\sqrt{A_{L-1}E_L}.\tag{16} $$ There is also a direct physical branch check requiring only the already proved same-side development. Put $H=y_{L-1}$ and $p=z_{L-1}$ in $(0,1)$. Formula (7) gives $X_{\mathrm{prev}}=H/p>H$ and $2r_{\mathrm{prev}}=H/p^2$, while $\operatorname{radius}(e_L)=H/2$. For $a_L$ centered at $(X,r)$, tangency to $u$ and $e_L$ gives $X^2=2Hr$. Tangency to $a_{\mathrm{prev}}$ then gives $|1/X-1/X_{\mathrm{prev}}|=1/H$. Since $X_{\mathrm{prev}}>H$ and $X>0$, the only positive solution is $$ X=\frac H{1+p}. $$ Consequently $A_L=2(1+p)^2/H=(\sqrt{A_{\mathrm{prev}}}+\sqrt{E_L})^2$, proving (16) without an arbitrary Descartes-root choice. It also agrees with the original bounded-gap contact order. In particular $A_L\geq E_L$, so $$ \frac{E_L}{A_{L-1}+A_L}\leq1.\tag{17} $$ For $L=1$, the actual marked strip contains $e_1$ of radius $1$ at $(0,1)$ and $a_1,b_1$ of radius $1$ at $(2,1),(-2,1)$. Thus $E_1=A_1=B_1=1$ and (17) holds directly with $A_0=0$. This is the literal word $(1,2,1)$, not a changed marking of the reduced width-two word. Equations (15),(17) establish the zero-middle bound $E/(x+y)\leq9/4$ at every first/final O port. The [source-normalized nine-quarter lemma](actual_zero_middle_nine_quarter_balance.md) gives strict balance there, with gap $>1/2500$. At every middle-E port, including the last port with outer $u=0$, the two positive middles have equal curvatures $A_j=B_j$. Since the outer sum $E_j+E_{j+1}>0$ (with $E_{L+1}=0$), the original strict inequality $Q(x,A_j,y)>\tfrac12\log A_j$ gives balance there as well. There is no exception at a protected outer line. Thus every port passes the actual complete-radius balance test for every $k\geq2$, in one shared original marked packing. ## 6. Full source, knot parity and exact bridge subfamilies The general complete-radius balance filling theorem now proves (3), including the full original one-sided remainder, the entire all-charge period, the original normalization and both parities. Its threshold can depend on the fixed diagram and prescribed parity, and no claim is made for arbitrary certified diagrams failing balance. The first O layer has odd exponent on the zero-based slots $1,3,\ldots,2k-3$. The resulting transpositions $(1\ 2),(3\ 4),\ldots,(2k-3\ 2k-2)$ join the initially $k$ cap components successively. All remaining boxes have even exponent. Therefore the original endpoint-pairing graph is one cycle and the plat in (2) is a knot. This argument includes $k=2$ and does not confuse zero-based slots with conventional generator indices. The [Fox-coloring certificate](actual_fox_coloring_exact_plat_bridge.md) applies without change: if every actual exponent in (2) is divisible by $3$, every full crossing box acts as the identity on ordered $\mathbb F_3$ colors, and the standard cup/cap register has exactly $3^k$ colorings. Any $b$-bridge knot has at most $3^b$ colorings. Together with the supplied $k$-bridge plat this gives minimal bridge number exactly $k$. Each required exponent congruence is compatible with its prescribed parity and independent arbitrarily large signed full twists. This identifies unbounded actual bridge complexity, without putting a congruence restriction on the volume theorem. No finite search over k or numerical packing values are used to prove this uniform statement. The reduced-family proof supplies the recurrence algebra, comparison principle and source Q normalization; this note proves the changed right boundary and the literal all-width incidence explicitly. ## Validation and scope The proof applies to every fixed width, but does not provide a single filling threshold independent of the diagram or width. It proves this explicit family, not a universal balance condition for every certified plat. The [focused exact audit](../experiments/audit_general_one_end_layer_long_filling_volume.py) and [recorded results](../experiments/general_one_end_layer_long_filling_volume_results.json) check the original right-end box incidences, first mark, reflection and knot parity at 39 widths, six changed-boundary identities, and all 36 exact circle-support pairs and nine port tests of the width-two and width-three seeds. This supplements the analytical proof; the old interior recurrence audit is not repeated, and finite tests are not used to infer the uniform or asymptotic conclusion.

title: Long-filling volume for reduced-layer plats of unbounded bridge number
status: Full invariant for every k ≥ 4; exact-bridge congruence subfamilies
text: # Long-filling volume for reduced-layer plats of unbounded bridge number theorem, 31 October 2026. Fix $k\geq4$ and signs $\epsilon_j\in\{1,-1\}$ for $1\leq j\leq k-1$. In conventional one-based braid-generator notation, form the standard $2k$-plat of $$ \beta_k(\mathbf p)= \left(\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}\sigma_{2j}^{\epsilon_j-2p_{1,j}}\right) \left(\prod_{j=1}^{k-2}\sigma_{2j+1}^{-2p_{2,j}}\right) \left(\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}\sigma_{2j}^{-2p_{3,j}}\right). $$ All products follow the original bottom-to-top order, with $j$ increasing within a layer. There are $3k-4$ independent integer full-twist parameters. Denote the resulting knot by $K_k(\mathbf p)$ and its original normalized root invariant by $\mathcal K_N(K_k(\mathbf p))$, retaining the framing and component conventions of the [original spectral period](general_localized_unit_charge_filling_period.md). **Theorem.** For every such fixed $k$ and sign pattern there is a threshold $T(k,\boldsymbol\epsilon)$ such that, for every fixed integer vector with all $|p_{r,j}|\geq T(k,\boldsymbol\epsilon)$, $$ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N} \log\left|\mathcal K_N(K_k(\mathbf p))\right| =\operatorname{Vol}\bigl(S^3\setminus K_k(\mathbf p)\bigr). $$ The twists can have independent signs and magnitudes; they are fixed before $N\to\infty$. The conclusion concerns the full original invariant. The proof below verifies the complete-radius balance hypothesis of the [general full-source filling theorem](../papers/planar-certificates/README.md) on one actual marked packing for every member of this source family. The comparison includes both level parities and the entire charge sum through that theorem. The supplied knots have bridge number at most $k$. The congruence subfamily in which every displayed braid exponent is divisible by $3$ has bridge number **exactly $k$**. This additional congruence is used only for the bridge lower bound, not for the volume theorem. Thus the family has unbounded minimal bridge complexity, rather than merely unbounded presentation width. This explicit construction does not assert balance for every simple-white plat or cover all $k$-bridge knots. Its uniform proof covers $k\geq4$; no balance claim is made here for the analogous reduced width-three word. ## 1. Literal source word, mark, and simple white sphere Use zero-based adjacent physical slots $0,\ldots,2k-2$. Slot $j$ is the braid generator usually denoted $\sigma_{j+1}$. The standard bottom and top cup pairs are $(0,1),(2,3),\ldots,(2k-2,2k-1)$. For $k\geq3$ put $$ \begin{gathered} O_k=(1,3,\ldots,2k-3),\qquad E_k^{\mathrm{int}}=(2,4,\ldots,2k-4),\\ D_k=O_kE_k^{\mathrm{int}}O_k,\qquad R=3k-4. \end{gathered}\tag{1} $$ These are the original bottom-to-top box slots, without an isotopy, Markov stabilization, or abstract graph-to-plat adapter. Mark the first original top cap, on slots $(0,1)$. Name the exterior $u$, bottom odd-gap regions $a_0,\ldots,a_{k-1}$, and bounded even-gap regions $e_1,\ldots,e_{k-1}$. The internal middle layer replaces $a_j$ by $b_j$ for $1\leq j\leq k-2$. Set $b_0=a_0$ and $b_{k-1}=a_{k-1}$, because there are no boxes in slots $0$ or $2k-2$. All other named regions are distinct. The original gap sweep gives exactly $$ \begin{array}{lll} \text{first }O:&(a_{j-1},u,e_j,a_j),&1\leq j\leq k-1,\\ \text{middle }E:&(e_j,a_j,b_j,e_{j+1}),&1\leq j\leq k-2,\\ \text{final }O:&(b_{j-1},e_j,u,b_j),&1\leq j\leq k-1. \end{array}\tag{2} $$ A quartet $(x,b,c,y)$ contributes the actual triangles $(x,b,y),(x,y,c)$. The protected regions are precisely $u$ and $a_0$. Their edge is MAIN. The white MAIN edges are $u-a_i$ and $u-b_i$, with the two named endpoint identifications retained; and $e_j-a_{j-1},e_j-a_j,e_j-b_{j-1},e_j-b_j$, again retaining the two endpoint identifications. The MATCHING edges are the two chains $a_{j-1}-a_j$ and $b_{j-1}-b_j$, together with the internal chain $e_j-e_{j+1}$. For $k\geq3$ no listed edge has equal endpoints, and there are no parallel edges: the two a/b chains have distinct interior vertices and share only their two endpoints. Each listed edge is incident to exactly two of the triangles in (2). At the left end, for example, $e_1-a_0$ is shared by the first-O output and final-O input triangles, while $u-a_0$ is shared by their other triangles. The right end is identical. The remaining $e_j$ MAIN incidences close against the appropriate middle-E triangle; the remaining $u$ incidences close between consecutive O boxes. Every matching edge pairs its own original box. Thus this is the actual simple triangulated sphere, with $$ V=3k-2,\qquad E=9k-12,\qquad F=6k-8,\qquad V-E+F=2.\tag{3} $$ The sphere topology and cyclic order are inherited from the original Morse construction, not inferred only from Euler characteristic. The [proved simple-block construction](actual_smoothed_source_capacity_blocks.md), §§4–5, therefore supplies the actual labeled convex ideal right-angled certificate and its two original cut balls. In particular (1) is a certified source diagram for every $k\geq3$. ## 2. The actual reflection packing and height coordinates The white sphere has the reflection automorphism $a_i\leftrightarrow b_i$ fixing $u,a_0,a_{k-1}$, and every $e_j$. It exchanges the first and last layers, with the original cyclic order reversed. Normalize the marked tangency $u-a_0$ to infinity, with the white disks $u$ and $a_0$ the outside half-planes below $Y=0$ and above $Y=2$. All ordinary disks lie inside this strip. This automorphism is realized by a reflection of the actual packing. One way to justify the needed uniqueness is the [proved strictly convex marked angle potential](actual_positive_face_coefficient_saddle.md): after fixing the common scale, its ordinary-face Hessian is a connected positive graph Laplacian. Equivalently, the maximum-ratio argument for two positive curvature solutions propagates strictness along every ordinary adjacency until it reaches a fixed normalization. The normalized radii then determine the contact-center development uniquely up to a horizontal Euclidean isometry. The orientation-reversing automorphism preserving both marked lines individually is therefore a vertical reflection; translate its axis to $X=0$. Write $a_i$ for both the named disk and its positive curvature when no confusion results. Then $a_i=b_i$. Put $L=k-1$. The fixed disks form the actual tangent chain $$ a_0\ (Y=2),\ e_1,e_2,\ldots,e_L,a_L,\ u\ (Y=0). $$ Their centers lie on $X=0$. Disjoint interiors, successive tangencies and the two endpoint lines force their intervals to be ordered strictly from top to bottom. Write $y_0=2$, and $y_j$ for the contact height between $e_j$ and the next fixed disk, $1\leq j\leq L$. Consequently $$ \begin{gathered} 2=y_0>y_1>\cdots>y_L>0,\\ \operatorname{radius}(e_j)=\frac{y_{j-1}-y_j}{2},\qquad \operatorname{radius}(a_L)=\frac{y_L}{2}. \end{gathered}\tag{4} $$ The fixed graph cycle $u-a_0-e_1-\cdots-e_L-a_L-u$ divides the original white sphere into two triangulated disks: all interior $a_i$ belong to one disk, all interior $b_i$ to the other. In the consistently oriented a-side development, the triangles $(a_i,e_i,e_{i+1})$ all lie on the same side of their downward-directed fixed-chain center edges. Their original cyclic orders therefore put every $a_i$ on the same side of $X=0$; one cannot choose these signs separately. The reflection puts all $b_i$ on the opposite side. Choose the a-side to be $X>0$. Thus for $1\leq i\leq L-1$ each reflected pair consists of two distinct disks, and the $a_i$ center is $(X_i,r_i)$ with $X_i>0$, where $r_i$ is its Euclidean radius. These disks are tangent to $u$ and to $e_i,e_{i+1}$. The first pair is also tangent to the upper line $a_0$, hence $r_1=1$. The last $a_L$ is the single axis disk. Elementary squared-distance tangency gives exactly $$ 2r_i=\frac{y_i(y_{i-1}-y_{i+1})}{y_{i-1}-y_i},\qquad X_i^2=\frac{y_{i-1}y_i(y_i-y_{i+1})}{y_{i-1}-y_i}.\tag{5} $$ For clarity, a circle of radius $r$ centered at $(X,r)$, tangent to the axis circle whose bottom/top heights are $U,V$, satisfies $X^2=V(2r-U)$. Applying this to the two neighboring fixed circles proves (5). No circle-packing approximation is used. ## 3. Exact scalar recurrence, with its branch fixed by geometry Define $$ z_j=\sqrt{1-\frac{y_j}{y_{j-1}}}\quad(1\leq j\leq L), \qquad z_0=z_{L+1}=0.\tag{6} $$ All actual $z_j$ lie strictly between $0$ and $1$. I claim $$ (1+z_{j-1})(1-z_j^2)(1+z_{j+1})=1, \qquad 1\leq j\leq L.\tag{7} $$ At $j=1$, $r_1=1$ and $y_0=2$ in (5) imply $z_2=z_1^2/(1-z_1^2)$, which is (7). At the other end, tangency of $a_{L-1}$ to $a_L$ at $X=0$ gives $X_{L-1}^2=2r_{L-1}y_L$. Equation (5) then gives $y_L=y_{L-2}-\sqrt{y_{L-2}(y_{L-2}-y_{L-1})}$, where the plus root is excluded by $y_L<y_{L-1}$. Hence $z_L^2=z_{L-1}/(1+z_{L-1})$, again (7). For an interior $j$ put $p=z_{j-1}$, $z=z_j$, $w=z_{j+1}$, and $q=1-z^2$. The positive horizontal coordinates and radii of the two consecutive right-side disks, normalized by $y_{j-1}$, are $$ \begin{aligned} \frac{X_{j-1}}{y_{j-1}}&=\frac zp,& \frac{X_j}{y_{j-1}}&=\frac{qw}{z},\\ \frac{2r_{j-1}}{y_{j-1}}&=\frac{p^2+(1-p^2)z^2}{p^2},& \frac{2r_j}{y_{j-1}}&=\frac{q[z^2+qw^2]}{z^2}. \end{aligned}\tag{8} $$ Their literal tangency is $(X_{j-1}-X_j)^2=4r_{j-1}r_j$. Substitution and cancellation of the positive factor $y_{j-1}^2/p^2$ gives $$ 1-2q(1+pw)+q^2(1-p^2)(1-w^2)=0.\tag{9} $$ The two possible roots are $$ q=\frac1{(1+p)(1+w)}\qquad\text{or}\qquad q=\frac1{(1-p)(1-w)}.\tag{10} $$ The second root is strictly greater than $1$ since $p,w>0$, whereas the actual height ratio $q$ lies in $(0,1)$. This excludes it before making any reconstruction or selecting a formal branch. The first root is precisely (7). The interior proof needs no order assumption on the two positive horizontal centers beyond the actual tangency. ## 4. A comparison principle gives the uniform 2/3 bound Set $v_j=\log(1+z_j)$, so $0<v_j<\log2$ and $v_0=v_{L+1}=0$. Define $$ f(v)=-v-\log(2-e^v). $$ Equation (7) becomes $$ f(v_j)=v_{j-1}+v_{j+1}.\tag{11} $$ On $[0,\log2)$, $f(0)=0$ and $$ f''(v)=\frac{2e^v}{(2-e^v)^2}>0. $$ In particular $f(tv)>t f(v)$ whenever $t>1$ and $0<v<tv<\log2$. For $L=3$ the explicit positive solution is $$ \begin{aligned} (z_1,z_2,z_3)&=(2/3,4/5,2/3),\\ (v_1,v_2,v_3)&=(\log(5/3),\log(9/5),\log(5/3)). \end{aligned}\tag{12} $$ Direct substitution verifies all three equations and both zero boundary values. For any $L\geq3$, place this three-node vector at any three consecutive positions and extend it by zeros elsewhere, calling the resulting vector $s$. It satisfies $$ f(s_j)\leq s_{j-1}+s_{j+1}.\tag{13} $$ including at every zero position next to its support. If some $s_j>v_j$, let $t=\max_j(s_j/v_j)>1$ and choose an attaining index. There $s_j=tv_j$, so strict convexity gives $f(s_j)>t f(v_j)$. On the other hand (13) and the maximal-ratio property give $$ f(s_j)\leq s_{j-1}+s_{j+1} \leq t[v_{j-1}+v_{j+1}]=t f(v_j), $$ a contradiction. Thus $v$ dominates every translated three-node vector. Every index $1,\ldots,L$ belongs to such a placement, and the smallest nonzero seed entry is $\log(5/3)$. Therefore for every $k\geq4$, $$ z_j\geq\frac23\qquad\text{for every }j.\tag{14} $$ This comparison uses the actual packing solution already constructed from the source certificate. It does not require a shooting guess or a new nonlinear existence theorem. It also establishes the bound for every interior index, not just for the two ends. ## 5. Exact curvature comparison and strict source balance Let $E_j$ denote the curvature of $e_j$ and $A_i$ the curvature of $a_i$, with $A_0=0$. From (4),(5), with $p=z_{j-1}$, $z=z_j$, and $D_0=p^2+z^2-p^2z^2>0$, equation (7) simplifies the two adjacent curvature ratios to $$ \frac{A_{j-1}}{E_j}=\frac{p^2z^2}{D_0},\qquad \frac{A_j}{E_j}=\frac{z^4(1+p)^2}{D_0}.\tag{15} $$ At $j=1$ the first ratio is $0$ and the second is $z_1^2$ because $r_1=1$; at $j=L$ the second formula uses the actual endpoint curvature $A_L=2/y_L$. Thus (15) includes both boundary cases with their original zero/axis interpretation, not a continued finite-circle formula imposed there. Adding gives $$ \frac{A_{j-1}+A_j}{E_j} =z_j^2\left[1+\frac{2p(1+p)z_j^2}{D_0}\right] \geq z_j^2\geq\frac49. $$ Consequently $$ \frac{E_j}{A_{j-1}+A_j}\leq\frac94.\tag{16} $$ at every first/final O port, uniformly for all $k\geq4$. The [zero-middle balance lemma](actual_zero_middle_nine_quarter_balance.md) uses the original absolutely normalized triangle action $Q$ and proves $$ Q(x,E,y)+Q(x,0,y)-\log E>\frac1{2500} \quad\text{if }x+y>0\text{ and }\frac E{x+y}\leq\frac94.\tag{17} $$ It retains either protected zero outer corner. Its proof is elementary: at fixed $A=x+y$ the cofactor Perron action increases with $P=xy$; the worst boundary value at $E/A=9/4$ is $(2/\pi)\operatorname{Ti}_2(2/3)-\log(3/2)$, which has an exact rational positive lower bound from four alternating $\operatorname{Ti}_2$ terms and the $\operatorname{atanh}$ series for the logarithm. Thus every O port passes the actual complete-radius balance condition. At each internal E port the two middle curvatures are equal, $A_j=B_j>0$, while both outer curvatures are positive. The original strict inequality $Q(x,A_j,y)>\tfrac12\log A_j$ gives $2Q(x,A_j,y)>\log A_j$. Thus every port in the literal diagram (1) satisfies the balance condition, using one common marked packing. No independent local radius optimization or entropy min/max exchange is involved. ## 6. General-theorem coverage, knot parity, and genuine width The general balanced-diagram long-filling theorem therefore applies to $D_k$ for every $k\geq4$ and every fixed half-twist pattern. For each fixed $k$ and source pattern there is a diagram-dependent threshold; all fixed filling powers beyond it may have independent signs and magnitudes. The family construction places no comparison constraint between these powers and no joint growing-twist/level limit. For knot parity put $\epsilon=+1$ or $-1$ on each box of the first $O$ layer, and zero on the other boxes. The first-layer zero-based transpositions $(1\ 2),(3\ 4),\ldots,(2k-3\ 2k-2)$ merge the $k$ initially separate cap cycles successively; each joins two previously different components. Every other box has even exponent and trivial endpoint permutation. Thus the filled main diagram is a knot for every integer full-twist vector. This is a direct computation on the original cups and slots. There are genuinely unbounded minimal bridge numbers inside this family, not merely arbitrarily wide presentations of two-bridge knots. Require additionally that every actual exponent $n_i=\epsilon_i-2p_i$ be divisible by $3$. This is one residue class of $p_i$ modulo $3$, compatible with all retained parities and arbitrary independent large signs. The Fox-coloring crossing operator on ordered strand colors is $T=\begin{pmatrix}2&-1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$ over $\mathbb F_3$; $(T-I)^2=0$ and $T^3=I$, for either signed crossing convention. Every whole box therefore acts identically on slot colors, though odd boxes still permute strand endpoints. The $k$ independent adjacent bottom-cup colors survive every top cap, so the knot has exactly $3^k$ Fox 3-colorings. Any $b$-bridge diagram has at most $3^b$ such colorings, because colors on its $b$ overpassing bridges determine every underpassing segment by the crossing rule. Reidemeister moves preserve colorings, so $b(K)\geq k$; the supplied plat gives $b(K)\leq k$. Hence $b(K)=k$ for this congruence subfamily. The independent full proof is the [Fox-coloring bridge certificate](actual_fox_coloring_exact_plat_bridge.md). The congruence condition is used only for this bridge lower bound. The analytic volume theorem still covers all independently long powers in the prescribed knot parity. Conversely, this explicit family is not claimed to exhaust balanced diagrams, all simple-white diagrams, or all $k$-bridge knots. The present uniform construction covers $k\geq4$; it makes no balance claim for the reduced $k=3$ word. ## Validation and scope The general statement follows analytically for every fixed $k\geq4$; finite packing samples are not used as its proof. The [focused exact audit](../experiments/audit_general_reduced_layer_long_filling_volume.py) and [recorded results](../experiments/general_reduced_layer_long_filling_volume_results.json) check the literal original Morse incidences, mark, reflection and knot parity at 38 widths, five symbolic tangency/root/curvature identities, the three rational seed equations, the rational balance bound, and all 44 circle-support pairs and eight port tests of the exact width-four seed. Root the audit code and replayed it with identical results. These finite checks support the source and algebra interfaces; the uniform comparison and the asymptotic invariant theorem are analytical conclusions, not extrapolations from sampled packings.

title: A uniform representation-volume gap for fixed peripheral words
text: # A uniform representation-volume gap for fixed peripheral words 30 October 2026. This extends the supplied [natural-map proof](../papers/casimir-source-asymptotics/README.md) to a varying sequence of representations. No quantum source estimate follows from this geometric statement alone. Let X=Gamma\H^3 be the fixed oriented finite-volume complete hyperbolic exterior, with its fixed marked complete PSL2 holonomy iota. For each n let rho_n:Gamma->SL2(C), followed by its PSL2 action, and let Vol(rho_n) have the same canonical peripheral-regulator normalization as in that note. Then Vol(rho_n) -> Vol(X) implies, after passing to a subsequence and conjugating by orientation-preserving target isometries g_n, that g_n rho_n(gamma) g_n^-1 -> iota(gamma) (1) for every fixed gamma in Gamma, with one common conjugation and the actual marking. A fixed final conjugation is absorbed into g_n. For absolute volumes tending to Vol(X), pass to a constant-sign subsequence; the limit is either iota or its orientation-reversed conjugate. ## Proof with nonuniform cusp data Choose any s_n>2 tending to2. For rho_n choose its own cusp-adapted map f_n and its natural map F_n=F_(s_n,f_n). The cusp estimates are used separately at the fixed pair (s_n,rho_n), and prove exactly integral_X Jac F_n = Vol(rho_n). No uniform cusp constants, uniform cusp truncation, or exchange of a cusp limit with n is needed. The radial construction, however, gives uniform INTERIOR estimates independent of f_n: |Jac F_n| <= (s_n/2)^3, AA^T <= H/3, (I-H) DF_n=s_n A, ||D_x nu_n||_TV <= s_n, ||D_x^2 nu_n||_TV <= 3s_n^2/2. The latter bounds differentiate only the domain radial kernel. Therefore integral_X [(s_n/2)^3-Jac F_n] ->0. (2) This is a nonnegative deficit. On any fixed compact lifted ball it tends to zero in L1 as well: the projection has bounded finite multiplicity on that ball. Choose points with Jacobians tending to1. The strict matrix inequality forces H->I/3 and all singular values of DF_n to1 there. Normalize their target images by orientation-preserving isometries g_n. The same fixed-radius Hessian bootstrap as in the frozen note now gives uniform C2 bounds near those points: positivity of I-H controls DF_n; its first variation is bounded by C(1+||DF_n||), and the uniform second measure derivative controls D2F_n. A C1 subsequential limit has Jacobian1 everywhere by (2). The strict matrix inequality forces its derivative to be an orientation-preserving isometry. This convergence propagates along finite chains of overlapping fixed-radius balls; target values in the new ball stay bounded by the known overlap and derivative bound. A diagonal exhaustion gives G_n=g_n F_n -> G_infinity locally in C1 on H^3, where G_infinity is a global orientation-preserving hyperbolic isometry. This construction does not assume compactness or irreducibility of the representations and does not claim that the normalizing g_n are bounded. It remains to use the equivariance, rather than only kernel invariance. Set rho'_n=g_n rho_n g_n^-1. For every fixed gamma and x, rho'_n(gamma) G_n(x)=G_n(gamma x). (3) Choose four fixed source points whose G_infinity-images are noncoplanar. Both sets of points in (3) converge. The isometries rho'_n(gamma) are precompact: their values at one fixed target point are bounded, because that point is o(1) from G_n(x), and the stabilizer of a point is compact. Every limiting isometry sends the four G_infinity(x)-points to their G_infinity(gamma x)-images. These determine an isometry uniquely, so rho'_n(gamma) -> G_infinity iota(gamma) G_infinity^-1. Absorb G_infinity^-1 in the common g_n. This proves (1) simultaneously for every fixed gamma; it also suffices to check a finite generating set. The SL2 central signs need not stabilize, and are immaterial for trace squared. No assertion about their lift is made. ## Uniform peripheral gap in the marked finite-dimensional problem Fix finitely many actual peripheral words m_1,...,m_b and delta>0. Suppose each iota(m_i) is parabolic or central, so tr^2 iota(m_i)=4. Then there is g=g(X,{m_i},delta)>0 such that EVERY actual SL2 representation satisfying max_i |tr^2 rho(m_i)-4| >= delta has |Vol(rho)| <= Vol(X)-g. (4) Otherwise a sequence violating every positive gap would have absolute volumes tending to Vol(X). Apply the proved compactness statement, passing to a constant-sign subsequence. Trace squared is continuous and conjugacy-invariant; its value at every selected word would tend to4 in either orientation, contradicting the fixed delta. This proof supplies a positive gap, not an effective numerical value. For a physical peripheral eigenvalue m=e^(pi i chi) with real chi, |tr^2 rho(m_i)-4|=4 sin^2(pi chi). Thus a selected real color parameter a fixed distance from the integer aliases meets (4), IF it is the eigenvalue of an actual representation whose volume controls the relevant source period. The latter implication is NOT proved here: it requires the source action, its cycle, its upper bound, and cancellation of all ordinary complementary terms to be established separately. This statement is not a bound on F_N or L_h. The fixed finite set is essential. One cannot take a supremum over ALL peripheral words whose exponents are allowed to grow with n: powers of a near-parabolic element may have trace far from ±2. The actual finite set of marked crossing-circle meridians is within the theorem's scope. ## Validation and scope The source action, period upper bound and cancellation of the complementary contribution remain separate requirements. The cusp normalization uses a fixed pair, whereas the interior estimates are representation-independent. The peripheral quantifier is over the specified finite set. The absolute-volume orientation alternative and source limitations remain as stated.

title: Volume equality for the original signed augmented source
text: # Volume equality for the original signed augmented source 30 October 2026. This note proves a uniform relative folded-channel estimate from the original finite continuants, then sums the actual half-twist phases. It concerns a fixed connected certified right-angled augmented diagram, at arbitrary fixed bridge width, through both parities and all sufficiently large levels. The external crossing-circle colors needed for long fillings are not the internal channels estimated here. ## 1. Exact source and statement Use the labeled geometric certificate and original marked normalization of the [untwisted theorem](general_untwisted_augmented_source_volume.md). Let R be the number of crossing circles, d=N-1, M=floor(d/2), and s0=d-2M in {0,1}. Retain any fixed vector of actual half twists epsilon_i in {0,1,-1}, and the separately specified exterior framing unit chi_(D,N). Write Y_D^epsilon for the certified complete augmented exterior with those recorded face pairings. Its volume is 2Vol(Q_D), unchanged by the half-twist pairings. The [exact marked coefficient identity](../papers/filling-bounds/README.md) is A_(D,N)^epsilon = chi_(D,N) N^R sum_(0<=a_i<=M) product_i[k_ai omega_ai^epsilon_i] F_N(a), F_N(a)=product_i beta_ai^2 * C_(N,a), (1) where C_(N,a) is the specified nonnegative face coefficient of product_i[D_ai,in D_ai,out P_(d-2ai)]. The two marked faces are set to zero; all the other face variables are shared. Here beta_a=S_(2a)/S_a^2, S_j=product_(r=1)^j 2sin(pi r/N), omega_a=q^(d^2/2)(-1)^a q^[a(a+1)], q=exp(pi i/N), k_a=1 if 2a=d, and k_a=2 otherwise. No trace normal is missing from (1): the original complete-circle coefficient is already included in these factors. This is the root complete source identity, not a differentiation of an off-grid root formula or a statement about individual generic-q normals. Let l_N be the unique positive critical radius of the all-maximal coefficient, with one finite face radius fixed by homogeneity. The [global coefficient theorem](actual_positive_face_coefficient_saddle.md) gives l_N -> l^geom. For circle i, let (x_i,b_i,c_i,y_i) be its actual four face radii at l_N, including the prescribed zeros, and put A_i=x_i+y_i, C_i(l_N)=pi[ sqrt(b_i A_i+x_i y_i) +sqrt(c_i A_i+x_i y_i)]/A_i, Z_i,N=C_i(l_N)-pi i epsilon_i. (2) The actual zero patterns have A_i>0 and C_i>0. All their positive coordinates stay in compact sets, so Re Z_i,N has a uniform positive lower bound. Each square root of Z_i,N below has positive real part. We prove the stronger asymptotic A_(D,N)^epsilon =chi_(D,N) N^R F_N(M,...,M) product_i omega_M^epsilon_i *(pi N)^(R/2) product_i Z_i,N^(-1/2) *[1+o(1)]. (3) In particular the original signed source is nonzero for all sufficiently large N, and lim_(N->infinity) (2pi/N) log|A_(D,N)^epsilon| =2Vol(Q_D)=Vol(Y_D^epsilon). (4) All quantifiers hold for each fixed connected diagram with its actual nondegenerate labeled certificate; the diagram does not grow with N. Neither one main component nor a restricted graph grammar is required. The statement includes signed complete augmented link exteriors, including those whose main strands form one component, that satisfy the certificate. It does not assert the volume limit after independently long Dehn fillings of the crossing circles. ## 2. An endpoint-safe recurrence for the normalized determinant For one actual triangle write D_a(x,b,y)=det[bI+(x/2)H_-+(y/2)H_+], Z_a^b=beta_a D_a(x,b,y), e_a=Z_a^b/Z_(a-1)^b, A=x+y>0, theta=pi/N. The original tridiagonal entries and sine products give EXACTLY e_1=A+2b cos(theta), e_a=(1+tau_a)[A+2b cos(a theta)cos((a-1)theta)] -tau_a[A^2-4xy cos^2((a-1)theta)]/e_(a-1), tau_a=tan((a-1)theta)/tan(a theta), 2<=a<=M. (5) For clarity, beta_a/beta_(a-1) equals sin((2a-1)theta)sin(2a theta)/sin^2(a theta). Multiplying the literal continuant recurrence by this ratio gives (5); its off-diagonal product becomes tau_a times the displayed quadratic. No matrix of virtual size beyond M is used. Since 0<=tau_a<1 and 0<=4xy<=A^2, induction in (5) proves A<=e_a<=2A+4b. (6) If T_b=sqrt(bA+xy)=0, necessarily b=0 and xy=0, and e_a=A identically. This single-variable case is retained separately. In every other fixed zero pattern T_b/A is bounded above and below by positive constants on the positive radius compact. Set k=N/2-a, so k_min=N/2-M=(s0+1)/2, and set E_k=e_a/A, lambda_b=2pi T_b/A, E_k^*=exp(lambda_b k/N). Then (5) becomes, with tau=tan(k theta)/tan((k+1)theta), E_k=(1+tau)[1+(2b/A)sin(k theta)sin((k+1)theta)] -tau[1-(4xy/A^2)sin^2((k+1)theta)]/E_(k+1). (7) Choose a sufficiently small fixed delta0>0. Substituting E^* in (7), its residual R_k satisfies uniformly for k_min<=k<=2delta0 N |R_k|<=C[k/N^2+k^3/N^3]. (8) Here is the cancellation behind this estimate. Uniform Taylor expansion gives tau=k/(k+1)+O(k/N^2). The two terms linear in k/N cancel. The quadratic k^2/N^2 terms cancel because lambda_b^2=4pi^2(b/A+xy/A^2). The finite k+1 offset leaves an O(k/N^2) term, which must not be dropped; the remaining Taylor terms are O(k^3/N^3). Taylor remainders are uniform when k theta is in the stated small compact interval, including k=1/2 and k=1. This approximate solution selects the actual positive solution without an asymptotic boundary condition. Start at k0 in [2delta0 N-2,2delta0 N] on the actual integer or half-integer lattice. By (6) both E_k0 and E_k0^* are bounded. Subtracting (7) for the two sequences gives an error recurrence with nonnegative multiplier K_k=tau[1-(4xy/A^2)sin^2((k+1)theta)] /(E_(k+1)E_(k+1)^*) <=tau exp[-lambda_b(k+1)/N]. The exact telescope of the tau factors therefore bounds propagation from j to k by P_kj<=C(k/j) exp[-c(j^2-k^2)/N]. (9) For k<=delta0 N the starting error is exponentially small, because the recurrence was started at twice this cutoff. Summing (8) with (9) gives |E_k-E_k^*|<=C[N^-1+k^2/N^2]+Ce^(-cN), |log(e_a/A)-lambda_b k/N| <=C[N^-1+k^2/N^2]+Ce^(-cN). (10) Indeed the residual sum is at most Ck sum_(j>=k) exp[-c(j^2-k^2)/N](N^-2+j^2/N^3). For k<=sqrt(N), comparison with Gaussian integrals bounds it by Ck/N^(3/2)<=C/N. For k>=sqrt(N), write j=k+l and use j^2-k^2>=2kl to obtain C[N^-1+k^2/N^2]. This proves (10) at both physical fold endpoints. The exact constant case T_b=0 satisfies it with zero error. ## 3. The original circle has a relative folded packet For t=M-a>=0, the t removed pivots have k=k_min,...,k_min+t-1, hence sum k=t(t+s0)/2. Summing (10), Z_(M-t)^b/Z_M^b =A^(-t) exp[-pi T_b t(t+s0)/(AN)] *exp[O(t/N+t^3/N^2)]. (11) The original forced product changes by the EXACT paired factors P_(s0+2t)(x,y)/P_s0(x,y) =product_(k=k_min)^(k_min+t-1) [A^2-4xy sin^2(k theta)] =A^(2t) exp[O(t^3/N^2)]. (12) Combining the two triangles, the powers of A cancel. With B_(N,a)=beta_a^2 D_a(x,b,y)D_a(x,c,y)P_(d-2a)(x,y), log[B_(N,M-t)/B_(N,M)] =-C(x,b,c,y)t(t+s0)/N+O(t/N+t^3/N^2), C=pi(T_b+T_c)/A>0. (13) This is uniform on the stated radius compacts for 0<=t<=delta0 N. For any fixed 0<delta<1/6, it is a relative 1+o(1) packet uniformly for t<=N^(1/2+delta). Choosing delta0 smaller if necessary also gives B_(N,M-t)/B_(N,M)<=C0 exp[-c0 t^2/N] (0<=t<=delta0 N). (14) The O(t/N) term in (13) is absorbed by a constant plus a small multiple of t^2/N; the cubic term is absorbed by choosing delta0. No limiting-rate error has been used as a relative estimate. We also need finite radius derivatives, but not derivatives of the sharp error (10). For any actual principal matrix M_j at real positive radii, a fixed sufficiently small complex logarithmic radius change gives M_j(z)=M_j(0)^(1/2)(I+E)M_j(0)^(1/2), ||E||<1/4 uniformly j,N. This follows from its sum of positive semidefinite radius summands; zero faces stay zero. If v=M_j(0)^(-1/2)e_last, the ratio of the last inverse entries is v^*(I+E)^(-1)v/(v^*v)=1+O(||E||), uniformly even when M_j is ill-conditioned. Its reciprocal is the ratio of the original Schur pivots. Thus the marked logarithm of each pivot ratio is uniformly bounded on this polydisc. Cauchy estimates give all fixed logarithmic radius derivatives O(1). The paired factors in (12) have the same property near the fold. Consequently partial_z^j log[B_(N,M-t)/B_(N,M)]=O_j(t), j>=1, (15) uniformly there. This is a finite matrix estimate, including the single-variable and both maximal-fold cases. ## 4. Transfer from shared-radius values to actual coefficients Use the fixed n=R-1 log-radius gauge of the coefficient theorem. Put f_t(z)=log[product_i B_(N,M-ti)(l^geom exp z)]-d sum_f log l_f; the beta factors are constant in z. Let z_t be its unique positive critical radius, and z_0 that of the all-maximal vector. For max t_i<=N^(1/2+delta), the global coefficient theorem supplies both critical points in the same fixed neighborhood, with Hessians between cN and CN, fixed higher derivatives O(N), and its relative O(N^-1) coefficient formula uniformly. Its hypotheses hold since sum s_i=o(N). Write A_t=sum_i t_i(t_i+s0)/N, eta_t=C sum_i(t_i/N+t_i^3/N^2). Equation (13), uniformly on a real neighborhood, says f_t(z)-f_0(z) =-sum_i C_i(z)t_i(t_i+s0)/N+error, |error|<=eta_t. (16) The C_i have bounded first derivatives. Comparing the minimum of f_t with its value at z_0 and using the strong convexity of f_0 gives |z_t-z_0|<=C[A_t/N+sqrt(eta_t/N)], f_t(z_t)-f_0(z_0) =-sum_i C_i(z_0)t_i(t_i+s0)/N +O(eta_t+A_t^2/N). (17) For example, the lower comparison is obtained by completing the square in cN|z-z_0|^2-C A_t|z-z_0|-eta_t, while the upper comparison uses z=z_0. This argument does not differentiate the remainder in (16). By (15) and the O(N) third derivatives of f_0, the Hessians at their respective minima differ by O(sum_i t_i)+O(N|z_t-z_0|). Their determinant ratio therefore tends to1 uniformly in this window. For delta<1/6, eta_t=o(1), A_t^2/N=o(1), and the displacement in (17) is o(1). Restoring the uniform relative coefficient formulas yields the actual finite-source sector ratio F_N(M-t_1,...,M-t_R)/F_N(M,...,M) =exp[-sum_i C_i(l_N)t_i(t_i+s0)/N] *[1+o(1)] (18) uniformly on the whole stated window. All beta/CD normalization, the two physical fold offsets and the shared radius constraints have been retained. There is no continuous-color interpolation assumption. ## 5. The full signed channel sum, including its tails The original finite half-twist has the exact ratio omega_(M-t)/omega_M=exp[pi i t(t+s0)/N]. (19) Its (-1)^a factor cancels the apparent nearest-node alternation; it cannot be discarded before expanding the quadratic exponent. Multiply (18) by (19) and retain k_a from (1). If N is odd, k_M=1 and all other k_a=2, giving the full integer Gaussian. If N is even all k_a=2 and t(t+1)=(t+1/2)^2-1/4, giving the full half-integer Gaussian. In either case, uniformly for Z in compact subsets of Re Z>0, sum_(t>=0) k_(M-t) exp[-Z t(t+s0)/N] =sqrt(pi N)/sqrt(Z) *[1+o(1)], (20) where the notation on the left extends the corresponding multiplicity pattern to the infinite Gaussian lattice. This follows directly by the real Riemann sum for exp(-Zx^2), with Gaussian tail domination; the integral is sqrt(pi)/sqrt(Z) by analytic continuation from Z>0. The even factor exp(Z/4N) tends to1. Truncation at the window of (18) has exponentially small Gaussian tails. The uniform o(1) in (18) causes o(N^(R/2)) absolute error in the normalized signed sum, since its absolute Gaussian majorant has that order. The product of the nonzero integrals in (20) has order N^(R/2) with a fixed positive lower bound on its modulus after normalization. This proves a nonzero signed leading coefficient on the window. It remains to justify deleting every other original channel. Evaluate each positive coefficient at the SAME all-maximal critical radius l_N. The central coefficient formula gives, with n=R-1, F_N(M-t)/F_N(M) <=C N^(n/2) product_i[B_(N,M-ti)(l_N)/B_(N,M)(l_N)]. (21) When all t_i<=delta0 N but some t_i>N^(1/2+delta), (14) makes the right side at most a polynomial times exp(-cN^(2delta)). The polynomial number of labels and their bounded k factors are harmless. The proof of (14) started at 2delta0 N, so no unresolved initial continuant error remains at this mesoscopic cutoff. If some t_i>delta0 N, the [uniform all-channel common-radius theorem](actual_positive_face_channel_rate.md) gives a strict macroscopic rate gap, uniformly at l_N -> l^geom. All other circle rates are bounded above by their fold values. Dividing by the central coefficient, whose rate is the same fold value, leaves exp(-cN+o(N)); again the number of labels is polynomial. All phases have modulus1. Thus neither tail affects the window's leading coefficient. Equations (18)--(21) establish (3). Finally the [absolute source coning anchor](actual_original_boundary_stationary_character.md) and the central coefficient theorem give N^-1 log F_N(M,...,M) -> Vol(Y_D^epsilon)/(2pi). Every additional factor in (3) is polynomial or a unit, and its displayed Gaussian product is nonzero. This proves (4). ## 6. Scope and verification This closes cancellation of the retained half-twist phases for the original complete augmented source under the stated general geometric certificate. It uses the exact marked compact-torus coefficient, not an assumed geometric intersection number or an independently normalized local thimble. The distinct external-color packet and its aliases needed to pass to independently long filled knots remain unproved by this theorem. No whole-source generic-q normal or growing-diagram uniformity is claimed. Focused audit: [original signed finite sources and folded factors](../experiments/audit_general_signed_augmented_source_volume.py), with [saved results](../experiments/general_signed_augmented_source_volume_results.json). At 90 digits it checks 1260 original normalized pivots, 280 direct original determinants, 180 exact single-summand pivots, 756 forced pairs and 756 circle ratios, 108 literal half-twist ratios and their fold multiplicities, and 476 complex-radius pivot comparisons. Ten whole original W/pi source sums at bridge widths two and three are compared with the independently summed face coefficients, retaining all phases, physical cups and the original marked cap. These finite source fixtures are normalization tests, not geometric certificates; their possible zeros do not assert a failure of the theorem's nondegenerate certificate hypothesis. Forty all-channel tetrahedral signed sums and 168 local folded packets are asymptotic diagnostics. The uniform estimates and noncancellation are proved above. The conclusion is the stated complete signed augmented-link equality; external filling colors remain separate.

title: A combinatorial geometric certificate for actual plats at every fixed width
status: Combinatorial certificate; actual examples at every fixed width
text: # A combinatorial geometric certificate for actual plats at every fixed width The subsequent [planar decoration theorem](../papers/terminal-decorations/README.md) constructs balanced diagrams from every simple triangulated sphere with a chosen dual matching. It includes the full general Morse source and independently long fillings. The theorem below retains its own original scope. 31 October 2026. Combinatorial sufficient class and arbitrary-width construction. The main class is ALL actual flat plats with a simple white triangulated sphere. The explicit words below prove nonvacuity at every supplied width; they do not replace the general long-twist target by one family. ## 1. The existing simple-sphere construction applies to the actual source Start with an original ordered 2k-strand flat plat, k>=2, whose boxes cover all crossings, retaining the original cups, caps, marked top cap, cyclic port order and crossing-disk matching. Build its actual plane cubic matching graph and dual white triangular cellulation by the literal construction in [the actual matching geometry](../papers/marked-fillings/README.md), sections1–2, or equivalently by the original middle-gap sweep. Require that this white cellulation is a SIMPLE triangulated sphere: its vertices and edge occurrences are the actual regions and incidences, there are no loops or parallel edges, and every triangular cell has three distinct vertices. This is a finite combinatorial test on the supplied diagram, not an abstract graph chosen to imitate it. The nondegenerate sphere has at least four white vertices. Each source triangle still has exactly one designated matching edge. The already proved construction in [the simple-block construction](actual_smoothed_source_capacity_blocks.md), sections4–5, applies with this WHOLE sphere as its single simple block. Its fixed-boundary Hall argument gives an interior angle maximizer; Euclidean disk development is an embedding of degree1; the strict sector argument excludes unintended contacts. The contact circles of the shaded triangles then give all supporting halfspaces. Therefore it constructs a convex three-dimensional ideal right-angled polyhedron with exactly these LABELED white faces, shaded triangles, ideal contacts and cyclic orders. Separating triangles are allowed by that proof. Sections3–6 of [the actual matching geometry](../papers/marked-fillings/README.md) identify this labeled medial sphere with the TWO actual projection/crossing-disk cut balls. They glue white faces across the copies and shaded triangles by the original retained half-twist permutations. The original meridians, primitive crossing-disk longitudes and source mark are retained. Their right-angle edge cycles and cusp decorations prove completeness for every fixed half-twist pattern. In particular the ACTUAL augmented exterior Y_(D,epsilon) is hyperbolic, with volume2Vol(Q). Its positive ideal triangulation supplies the general marked gluing certificate. Thus the simple-white test is a SUFFICIENT combinatorial geometric certificate for the exact class used by the right-angled source results. It is not a claim that every hyperbolic or prime twist-reduced plat satisfies this test. The older matching-geometry existence-gap paragraph can now be sharpened for this class using the later simple-block proof. No external alternating-link existence theorem is being imported. ## 2. Explicit literal words at all widths k>=3 Number adjacent strand slots from0 to2k-2. Put O_k=(1,3,...,2k-3), E_k=(0,2,...,2k-2), w_k=O_k E_k O_k, R=3k-2. (1) These are the original bottom-to-top box slots; no isotopy or abstract matching-to-plat adapter is needed. Denote the exterior by u, the k bottom odd-gap regions by a_0,...,a_(k-1), the k top odd-gap regions by b_0,...,b_(k-1), and the intermediate bounded even-gap regions by e_1,...,e_(k-1). Set e_0=e_k=u for formulas only. All the other named vertices are distinct. The literal gap sweep gives exactly these ordered four-face incidences: first O: (a_(j-1),u,e_j,a_j), 1<=j<=k-1; middle E: (e_j,a_j,b_j,e_(j+1)), 0<=j<=k-1; final O: (b_(j-1),e_j,u,b_j), 1<=j<=k-1. (2) The two cells of a quartet (x,b,c,y) are (x,b,y) and (x,y,c). The MAIN edges of its white sphere are exactly u-a_i, u-b_i (0<=i<=k-1), e_j-a_(j-1), e_j-a_j, e_j-b_(j-1), e_j-b_j (1<=j<=k-1), and its MATCHING edges are exactly a_(j-1)-a_j, b_(j-1)-b_j (1<=j<=k-1), u-e_1-e_2-...-e_(k-1)-u (the k cycle edges). (3) For k>=3 every listed edge has distinct endpoints and occurs only once in (3) and the MAIN list. In particular the matching cycle has length at least3. The triangles in (2) are distinct and every listed edge occurs in precisely two of them. These are the actual embedded sphere cells from the gap sweep, with vertices=3k, edges=9k-6, triangles=6k-4, vertices-edges+triangles=2. For example the MAIN edge e_j-a_(j-1) appears in the first-O output triangle and the preceding middle-E input triangle; the other three e_j MAIN incidences pair in the same way. The end u-a_0,u-a_(k-1) incidences close against the first and last middle-E cells, and the interior u-a_i incidences pair between consecutive first-O cells; the b incidences are reflected. The matching edges each pair the two triangles of their own original box. This checks the full labeled sphere, not just its Euler count. The protected mark can be the original first top cap: its two adjacent white faces are u,b_0, joined by MAIN. Consequently every w_k, k>=3, meets the simple-white certificate. ## 3. Width two and the knot parity For k=2 take the original slot word (1,0,1), with R=3. Its actual quartets are (1,0,3,2), (0,1,4,3), (4,3,0,2). The six triangles form the triangular bipyramid on vertices0,...,4, with equatorial triangle(0,2,3) and apices1,4. Thus its white sphere is simple and nondegenerate. The superficially similar word (1,0,2,1) must NOT be used for this argument: its two middle boxes produce parallel matching edges between the same white pair. For k>=3 put epsilon=+1 or -1 on EVERY box of the FIRST O layer, and zero on the other boxes. For k=2 use one nonzero epsilon on the first slot1 box and zero on the other two. Signs do not affect permutation. Starting with k disjoint cap components, the successive first-layer transpositions on slots1,3,...,2k-3 join component j to the already joined components0,...,j-1. At that step their two strands are in DIFFERENT components; cutting and cross-rejoining them merges those two cycles. Induction therefore gives ONE main component. Equivalently, the exact permutation is the product of the disjoint transpositions (1 2)(3 4)...(2k-3 2k-2), and the lower standard pairing together with the upper pairing transported by this permutation form a single alternating cycle. All full twists have trivial strand permutation. Thus for each such fixed parity pattern EVERY fixed integer vector p gives a knot with box exponents epsilon_i-2p_i. The [geometric long-filling theorem](general_augmented_plat_long_filling_quantifiers.md) gives a threshold T_geom(D,epsilon) for independently long signed p_i, with no comparability requirement. Each resulting knot has a k-bridge PRESENTATION, hence minimal bridge number at most k. This class construction alone does not prove b(K)=k. The later [Fox certificate](actual_fox_coloring_exact_plat_bridge.md) does prove it when every box exponent is divisible by3, independently of the quantum asymptotic problem. ## 4. Exact coverage and threshold dependence The main geometric assertion applies to EVERY actual simple-white flat plat, not just (1). Its width and number/order of boxes may be arbitrary but are fixed before the quantum limit. Each fixed retained half-twist pattern and original primitive marking is part of D. The geometric threshold can depend on that full D, including cusp moduli, the positive-shape and framed-completion neighborhoods, and the common inverse-slope IFT polydisk. It is not asserted to depend only on k. A maximum over the finitely many cusp subsets gives one threshold for partial fillings as well, with unfilled inverse slopes0. The endpoint/complete-source results apply with their separately stated source and parity scopes. The later [balance theorem](../papers/planar-certificates/README.md) proves the full fixed long-filling limit under its additional geometric condition. The [one-end layer family](general_one_end_layer_long_filling_volume.md) establishes that condition for its actual words at every k>=2. This class construction alone does not prove balance or the quantum limit for all its diagrams. The direct fixed-root route needs no separate genuine-q normals; the older mixed-color route has its own hypotheses. Neither result identifies all essential hyperbolic plats with this class or certifies an arbitrary abstract matched graph as an original source. ## 5. Focused verification The [literal-source audit](../experiments/audit_general_simple_white_plat_class.py) and [recorded output](../experiments/general_simple_white_plat_class_results.json) check the original gap-sweep incidences, distinct triangle and edge occurrences, sphere counts and one-component parity at widths 2 through 30. At width 30 the source has 88 ports and 90 white vertices. These finite checks support the source dictionary; the symbolic formulas and construction above prove the arbitrary-width statement. They do not prove minimal bridge number or the phase-sensitive quantum filling limit.

title: Independent tangle depth at every initial bridge gap
status: General bridge-gap closure; all widths and fixed depths
text: # Independent tangle depth at every initial bridge gap theorem, 31 October 2026. The [one-end plat family](general_one_end_layer_long_filling_volume.md) admits arbitrarily deep, independently chosen tangles at **every** first-layer bridge gap. The construction preserves its original marked cap and all core circle radii. It is checked on the literal source; it does not assert a theorem for arbitrary stacking or arbitrary plat diagrams. ## 1. The all-width, all-depth family Fix $k\geq2$, put $L=k-1$, and choose any fixed depth vector $\mathbf m=(m_1,\ldots,m_L)$ with $m_j\geq0$. Number adjacent box slots from zero and set $s_j=2j-1$. Replace the $j$th box of the first $O$ layer by $$ (s_j,s_j+1)^{m_j}s_j.\tag{1} $$ Process $j=1,\ldots,L$ in its original order, retaining the middle $E^{\mathrm{right}}$ and final $O$ layers. The resulting literal word is $$ \left[\prod_{j=1}^{L}(2j-1,2j)^{m_j}(2j-1)\right] (2,4,\ldots,2L)(1,3,\ldots,2L-1), \qquad R=3k-3+2\sum_{j=1}^{L}m_j.\tag{2} $$ Products in (2) mean concatenation of slot lists in bottom-to-top order. A slot $s$ is conventional braid generator $\sigma_{s+1}$. Each added pair therefore means two independently powered boxes $\sigma_{2j}^{-2p}\sigma_{2j+1}^{-2q}$. Retain the standard adjacent cups/caps and mark the first original top cap. The retained original first-$O$ boxes have fixed half twists $\epsilon_j\in\{1,-1\}$. All added boxes and the original middle/final layers have $\epsilon=0$. Every box has its own independent signed integer full-twist parameter. No region is merged, removed or assigned a dependent parameter. **Theorem.** Every word (2) is an original certified simple-white marked plat, and its actual complete packing satisfies $Q$-balance at every port. Its prescribed parity gives a knot. For every fixed $k$, depth vector and sign pattern, there is a threshold $T(k,\mathbf m,\boldsymbol\epsilon)$ such that every independently signed fixed full-twist vector with all $|p_i|\geq T$ satisfies $$ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N}\log\left|K_N\!\left(K_{k,\mathbf m}(\mathbf p)\right)\right| =\operatorname{Vol}\!\left(S^3\setminus K_{k,\mathbf m}(\mathbf p)\right).\tag{3} $$ This is the full original normalized invariant, both level parities and the entire charge sum, through the [full-source balance theorem](../papers/planar-certificates/README.md). Depths and twists are fixed before $N$ grows. No comparison between twist magnitudes, or threshold uniform in widths or depths, is asserted. Requiring every actual exponent to be divisible by $3$ gives a subfamily of minimal bridge number exactly $k$; that congruence is not required for (3). More generally, the same closure works for any balanced certified core with the initial $O$ layer, no slot $0$, the first-cap mark, and ordered actual initial curvatures $$ 0=A_0\leq A_1\leq\cdots\leq A_L. $$ The one-end cores satisfy strict inequalities, proved below. Neither this order nor balance is asserted for arbitrary initial-layer diagrams. ## 2. Exact simultaneous source dictionary The original first-$O$ port $j$ is $$ (a_{j-1},u,e_j,a_j),\tag{4} $$ where $u$ is exterior, $a_0$ is the protected first-cap face, and $a_j$ is ordinary for $j\geq1$. Set $A=a_{j-1}$ and identify the eventual last face of the local prefix with the old core face $B=a_j$. For $m_j=m>0$, let $f_0=u$ and let $b^{(0)}$ be the current bottom odd-gap face. Prefix pair $t$ has the exact original quartets $$ \begin{aligned} \text{slot }s_j &: (A,f_{t-1},f_t,b^{(t-1)}),\\ \text{slot }s_j+1 &: (f_t,b^{(t-1)},b^{(t)},u), \qquad1\leq t\leq m. \end{aligned}\tag{5} $$ The retained old box becomes $$ (A,f_m,e_j,b^{(m)}).\tag{6} $$ Identify old $B$ with $b^{(m)}$. If $m_j=0$, retain (4) unchanged. These formulas hold simultaneously. Before processing bridge $j$, earlier blocks have changed only gap positions up to $2j-1$. The face there is already the identified old $A$; the current bottom odd gap $2j+1$ has not changed. The even gaps $2j$ and $2j+2$ remain exterior $u$, the latter being exterior outright when $j=L$. The two local slots change only their own gaps. Thus (5) is the [original gap sweep](../papers/filling-bounds/README.md); after (6), the current middle gap contains old $e_j$. Induction on $j$ proves the entire first-layer dictionary. Every later core quartet is unchanged under these face identifications. The first marked face is never crossed because slot $0$ is absent. Introduce symbols $C_{j,n}$ with $C_{j,0}=a_j$. For depth $m$, $$ \begin{aligned} b^{(t)}&=C_{j,2(m-t)},& f_t&=C_{j,2(m-t)+1},\\ b^{(0)}&=C_{j,2m},& f_0&=u. \end{aligned}\tag{7} $$ Every positive-$n$ symbol is a distinct new source face. In particular the old core disk $a_j$ is preserved as $b^{(m)}$; the original bottom face is now the outermost new chain disk. The same indexing is used by the actual packing. ## 3. An exact chain inside a finite triangular gap Consider one original empty interstice $(A,u,B)$, with $u$ the baseline halfplane $Y\leq0$. First assume its actual curvatures satisfy $A,B>0$. Put the $A$-contact at $X=0$ and the $B$-contact on the positive side. The old radii are $1/A,1/B$, and the $B$ center is $(2/\sqrt{AB},1/B)$. Inside this actual bounded curvilinear interstice define, for $n\geq0$, $$ \begin{aligned} C_n&=(\sqrt B+n\sqrt A)^2,& r_n&=C_n^{-1},\\ X_n&=\frac{2}{\sqrt A(\sqrt B+n\sqrt A)},& Y_n&=r_n. \end{aligned}\tag{8} $$ The $n=0$ disk is old $B$. In the positive coordinate $\sqrt{C/A}$, this is the affine translation $\sqrt{C_n/A}=\sqrt{B/A}+n$. That identity describes the circle-chain construction; it is not an identification with a global quantum torsor or a theorem about its periods. Every disk is tangent to $u$ and old $A$. Consecutive disks obey $$ X_n-X_{n+1}=2\sqrt{r_nr_{n+1}}, $$ so their tangencies are exact. For nonconsecutive indices, the squared-distance support slack is $$ 4r_nr_\ell\bigl[(n-\ell)^2-1\bigr]>0.\tag{9} $$ Each next disk occupies the bounded gap toward the $A/u$ contact, with $0<X_{n+1}<X_n$. This actual contact order selects the sum of square roots in (8); the other algebraic branch is not used. The finite chain remains within the original empty interstice. Other old disks lie outside that face, and the new contact points avoid its three old vertices. Hence the only old finite contacts are with $A$, and with $B$ for $n=1$. These coordinates describe the existing original gap. They are not an independent conjugation of a local quantum word. In the common marked plane, if the $A$-contact is $X_A$ and $\sigma=\operatorname{sign}(X_B-X_A)$, the actual new horizontal centers are $X_A+\sigma X_n$. Every old disk stays fixed. For $j=1$, old $A=a_0$ is the upper protected line and its curvature is zero. Use the [exact parallel-line construction](general_marked_unit_chain_filling_volume.md): normalize the lines to $Y=0,2$, so old $B$ has radius $1$, and add $2m$ unit disks in the empty complementary component. Here $C_n=B=1$. No finite-circle expression is divided by $A=0$. Insert $2m_j$ circles in each original first-$O$ triangular gap using (7)–(8). The original gap interiors are disjoint, including when their boundaries share old edges. The finite new disks remain in those gaps and avoid their old vertices, so different patches cannot overlap or acquire extra contacts. Each old triangular disk is replaced by the literal triangulated disk in (5)–(6), with the same boundary. The new sphere is simple, with exactly the source contact graph and cyclic order. The [proved packing construction](actual_smoothed_source_capacity_blocks.md), Sections 4–5, supplies its actual labeled right-angled certificate. Marked uniqueness identifies this unchanged-core packing with the complete source packing. ## 4. Balance at all new and modified ports The only order needed is $B\geq A\geq0$. For $A>0$, put $s=\sqrt{B/A}\geq1$, so $C_n/A=(s+n)^2$. A new odd port has outer curvatures $A,C_n$ for even $n\geq2$. Its positive middles are $C_{n-1},C_{n+1}$, except that the first prefix port replaces the latter by zero. Thus $$ \frac{\max\{\text{middles}\}}{A+C_n} \leq\frac{(s+n+1)^2}{1+(s+n)^2}\leq2,\tag{10} $$ because $2(1+t^2)-(t+1)^2=(t-1)^2\geq0$. A new even port has outers $C_{n+1},0$ and middles $C_n,C_{n+2}$, for even $n\geq0$. Hence $$ \frac{\max\{\text{middles}\}}{\text{sum of outers}} =\left(\frac{s+n+2}{s+n+1}\right)^2\leq\frac94.\tag{11} $$ Here $s+n+1\geq2$. Equivalently, $$ \frac94-\left(\frac{t+1}{t}\right)^2 =\frac{(t-2)(5t+2)}{4t^2}\geq0\qquad(t\geq2). $$ Apply the [zero-middle $9/4$ lemma](actual_zero_middle_nine_quarter_balance.md) after replacing the smaller middle by zero. The original $Q$ is nondecreasing in that middle, so (10)–(11) give strict balance at every new port, with gap $>1/2500$. For $A=0$, the parallel-line chain has all positive curvatures equal to $1$ and the same conclusion follows directly. At the retained old port, only its input middle changes from zero to $$ C_1=(\sqrt A+\sqrt B)^2\leq2(A+B).\tag{12} $$ The output middle $E=e_j$ stays fixed. Its new action sum is $Q(A,C_1,B)+Q(A,E,B)$. Against the new target $\log C_1$, use the $9/4$ lemma with $C_1/(A+B)\leq2$ and then monotonicity in $E$. Against the old target $\log E$, use monotonicity in the changed input middle and the old strict balance. This controls both targets without assuming $E\geq1$. It also covers $A=0$, where $C_1=B$. The protected zeros remain exact. Every later core port retains its weights and gap. The new minimum local margin is at least the smaller of the old minimum and $1/2500$, independently of depths.
