This does not assert a filling threshold uniform in the number of ports. ## 5. The one-end core has the required curvature order Normalize its marked lines to $Y=0,2$. Its a-side circles have centers $(X_i,r_i)$ and curvatures $A_i=1/r_i$. The actual cyclic list of contacts on the lower white line is $$ (a_0,a_1,\ldots,a_L,e_L,b_L,\ldots,b_1), $$ with the marked contact at infinity and the fixed $e_L$ contact at $X=0$. The embedded complete packing therefore gives $X_1>\cdots>X_L>0$. For $i<L$, the proved height formulas, with $z=z_i$ and $w=z_{i+1}$, give $$ \frac{X_i}{r_i}=\frac{2zw}{z^2+w^2-z^2w^2}\leq2,\tag{13} $$ since the denominator minus $zw$ is $(z-w)^2+zw(1-zw)\geq0$. Tangency gives $X_i-X_{i+1}=2\sqrt{r_ir_{i+1}}$. Its left side is strictly below $X_i\leq2r_i$, so $r_{i+1}<r_i$. Therefore $0=A_0<A_1<\cdots<A_L$. For $k=2$, there is no interior comparison and $A_1>0$ is immediate. An independent proof uses the already established curvature ratios in the [one-end theorem](general_one_end_layer_long_filling_volume.md), equation (14). For $2\leq j<L$, $$ \frac{A_j}{A_{j-1}} =\frac{z_j^2(1+z_{j-1})^2}{z_{j-1}^2}>\frac{16}{9}, $$ using $z_j\geq2/3$ and $0<z_{j-1}<1$. Its last positive-root identity gives $A_L>A_{L-1}$, and the small cases are exact. Thus the order does not depend only on a new reading of the contact diagram. ## 6. Full source, independent twists and bridge number Every inserted even exponent $-2p$ has identity endpoint permutation. All original odd first-$O$ boxes and other core boxes remain in their original order with their original half twists. The first marked cap is unchanged. Thus the original knot parity persists for arbitrary neighboring depth choices. The total framing character is that of the extended original diagram. Its exact normalization is retained; it is not identified numerically with the core's character, and no equality of old and new invariants is claimed. For each fixed width and depth vector, the certificate and balance meet the existing full-source theorem. Its entire spectral and charge argument proves (3) for all independent sufficiently long fixed signed twists, including the $2\sum_jm_j$ new parameters. This is not an inference from local angle volume or a selected contribution alone. The same proof permits arbitrary fixed added half twists $\epsilon\in\{0,1,-1\}$ **provided the resulting actual endpoint permutation gives a knot**. Their extended framing and peripheral conventions are retained. The white source dictionary and complete packing do not change under these retained half twists. The concrete even additions in (1) are the convenient subfamily that automatically preserves the old knot parity. If every full exponent is also a multiple of $3$, the [Fox certificate](actual_fox_coloring_exact_plat_bridge.md) counts exactly $3^k$ colors on the standard cup/cap register. The supplied plat then has minimal bridge number exactly $k$. These congruences allow independent large parameters of either sign and preserve the prescribed parity. They are required only for the bridge lower bound. ## Validation and scope The construction gives arbitrary independent depth at every initial bridge gap; it does not cover arbitrary multilayer plat diagrams or prove a universal balance criterion. The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_general_simultaneous_bridge_gap_filling_volume.py) and [recorded results](../experiments/general_simultaneous_bridge_gap_filling_volume_results.json) compare the closed dictionary against the original Morse compiler on 413 nonuniform charts, checking 11880 ports, 23760 triangles, 35640 edges, all marks and core permutations. Seven symbolic identities check tangent chains, support and inequalities. Twenty-five exact simultaneous seed packings supply 2333 circle/line supports, 168 new-port bounds and 32 modified targets. These checks supplement the general proof; finite samples do not establish its uniform or quantum conclusion.

title: A general source-regulator equality theorem and its exact quantum scope
text: # A general source-regulator equality theorem and its exact quantum scope 29 October 2026. The geometric equality step extends to EVERY oriented complete finite-volume cusped hyperbolic three-manifold. No pretzel, alternating, bridge-width, polyhedral, or positive ideal-triangulation hypothesis is required. The proof below constructs the nearby local geometry explicitly by equivariant averages, rather than assuming a general deformation or Dehn filling theorem. This does NOT extend the proved original-source asymptotic to every knot. Section8 identifies the additional quantum hypotheses, their proved pretzel instance, and the currently missing broader source estimates. Neither a formal saddle nor a correct cusp Hessian supplies those inputs. ## 1. General geometric completion theorem Let M be an oriented complete finite-volume hyperbolic three-manifold with h torus cusps and geometric holonomy rho0. Fix primitive oriented bases (mu_i,lambda_i) of its actual peripheral groups. On each torus fix the complete Euclidean cusp coordinate, so its two holonomies are translations by a real-linearly independent pair of complex numbers. There is a neighborhood U of the complete FRAMED representation with the following property. A point of U consists of an actual representation rho: pi1(M) -> PSL(2,C) and, for each cusp, a common peripheral fixed flag close to its complete flag. Use a frame depending continuously on that flag to send it to infinity. The peripheral transformations are then complex similarities. Let U_i,V_i be the uniquely small logarithms of the complex similarity multipliers of mu_i,lambda_i, continued from zero at completeness. Select any subset F of cusps to fill. Suppose: 1. Every unfilled peripheral group is parabolic, so BOTH similarity multipliers are one. It remains nontrivial near rho0. 2. For each i in F, choose an arbitrary primitive integer pair (a_i,b_i) and a sign epsilon_i in {+1,-1}, and impose the ACTUAL log equation a_i U_i+b_i V_i=2pi i epsilon_i. (1) Then rho descends to the Dehn filling of M along the actual slopes sigma_i=a_i mu_i+b_i lambda_i. The descended representation is the holonomy of a positively oriented COMPLETE finite-volume hyperbolic metric on that filled topology. In particular it is discrete and faithful there. Any number of cusps may remain, including zero. The neighborhood U is fixed before the slopes: the conclusion applies to every slope tuple and framed representation satisfying these conditions inside U. It does NOT assert existence of such a representation for all slopes. Existence is supplied by the actual source branch in the proved application, and must be supplied in another application. For nearby representations, (1) itself forces the relevant slopes to be long. The proof is independent of a graph presentation and of any geometric triangulation existence theorem. Sections2--5 establish it directly. ## 2. A nearby equivariant developing map on every compact core Identify the universal cover of the complete M with H3, and write Gamma for pi1(M), acting by rho0. Choose a compact cusp-truncated core and a slightly larger compact collar. Cover that compact set by finitely many open balls which lift injectively to H3, and choose a smooth partition of unity subordinate to them. Write eta_(j,gamma) for the lifts using one chosen lift of the j-th ball. Thus sum_(j,gamma) eta_(j,gamma)(x)=1, eta_(j,gamma)(rho0(delta)x)=eta_(j,delta^-1 gamma)(x). The sum is locally finite. On a fixed compact fundamental part only finitely many gamma occur. No freeness of the deformed action is assumed. Use the future unit hyperboloid in Minkowski space for H3. Form Y_rho(x)=sum_(j,gamma) eta_(j,gamma)(x) rho(gamma) rho0(gamma)^-1 x, E_rho(x)=Y_rho(x)/sqrt(-<Y_rho(x),Y_rho(x)>). (2) Every summand is future timelike unit. A convex combination with nonnegative weights summing to one is future timelike, so normalization is defined. The Lorentz action of PSL(2,C) makes (2) unambiguous without choosing SL signs. Reindexing gamma gives exactly E_rho(rho0(delta)x)=rho(delta)E_rho(x). (3) At rho=rho0 every summand in (2) equals x, so E_rho0(x)=x. On the compact fundamental part, only finitely many matrices and derivatives of fixed smooth weights occur. Consequently E_rho tends to the identity in C1 as rho tends to rho0. For rho in one sufficiently small neighborhood, it is an orientation-preserving local diffeomorphism. Equivariance then gives this property over the whole lifted compact core and collar. This is the needed compact-core deformation proof. It uses neither an unproved compatible geodesic mesh nor a subdivision that could invert thin tetrahedra. It also does not assume local character-variety rigidity. ## 3. An explicit positive similarity link and an entire cusp tail In one complete cusp write its cover as (w,t) in C x [t0,infinity), (w,t) -> (w+lambda,t), lambda in Lambda, dev0(w,t)=(w,exp(t)), where Lambda is the complete translation lattice. In the moving selected flag frame, denote the deformed affine action by A_rho(lambda)(z)=a_lambda z+b_lambda. It is a homomorphism from Lambda to Aff(C), tends to the original translation action, and all a_lambda are nonzero. Choose a smooth compactly supported nonnegative function eta on C with sum_(lambda in Lambda) eta(w-lambda)=1. Such eta is obtained from any bump whose translates cover a fundamental parallelogram by dividing by its positive periodic translate sum. Define d_rho(w)=sum_lambda eta(w-lambda) A_rho(lambda)(w-lambda). (4) Affine maps commute with convex combinations of total weight one, so d_rho(w+nu)=A_rho(nu)d_rho(w). (5) At completeness every term is w. On a fixed compact fundamental domain, d_rho is C1-close to w; its real Jacobian is therefore positive and nonzero. Equivariance propagates this local-diffeomorphism property everywhere. Thus (4) gives a genuine nonsingular similarity structure on the COMPACT cusp torus, not just a formal list of peripheral matrices. The developed images and Euclidean lengths of fixed generator paths are uniformly bounded near completeness. Let chi_rho:C->R be the real-linear extension of the character lambda -> log|a_lambda|. The map F_rho(w,t)=(d_rho(w),exp(t+chi_rho(w))) (6) is exactly rho-equivariant in upper half-space: its horizontal and vertical coordinates transform by a_lambda z+b_lambda and |a_lambda|y. Its differential is triangular with positive determinant exp(t+chi_rho(w)) det_R Dd_rho(w). Hence it is an orientation-preserving local diffeomorphism for EVERY t>=t0. At completeness it is dev0. Restore the continuously varying flag frame when viewing (6) in the global target H3. Define it on one chosen lift of each disjoint cusp neighborhood and propagate by rho-equivariance to the other lifts. The exact peripheral equivariance makes the coset representative irrelevant, so this gives a well-defined map on the entire lifted end. On a fixed compact cusp collar it is C1-close to the original developing map. Interpolate E_rho and F_rho by the unique hyperbolic geodesic between their values, with a smooth Gamma-invariant cutoff in t. The interpolation is rho-equivariant and is C1-close to the identity on that compact collar. Thus it too is a positive local diffeomorphism after one further uniform shrink of U. Set it equal to E_rho on the compact part and F_rho on each deep tail. We have now constructed a global rho-equivariant developing LOCAL DIFFEOMORPHISM on the ideal-end-deleted original manifold. Pulling back the H3 metric yields an actual oriented curvature-minus-one metric. There are no polyhedral edge or vertex singularities to check: the map is a smooth local diffeomorphism everywhere at finite points. The construction is simultaneous at all finitely many cusps. It works on a single neighborhood of the complete framed representation, with no comparison between different deformation sizes or slopes. ## 4. The small multiplier logs are the actual log-link periods At a filled cusp (1) ensures at least one multiplier is nontrivial. Commutativity of affine peripheral maps implies that they have a common finite fixed point q in addition to infinity. For a generator with a!=1, this is q=b/(1-a). The two original generator translations are nonzero. As the representation approaches completeness, at least one such formula therefore gives |q|->infinity, uniformly over the small framed neighborhood with its parabolic locus removed. The image of an ENTIRE closed fundamental parallelogram under d_rho is uniformly bounded by the compact C1 estimate in section3. Fixed generator paths also have uniformly bounded developed images and Euclidean lengths. For U sufficiently small the whole parallelogram image misses q, including its interior, not only its boundary paths. Equivariance and the fact that every peripheral map fixes q then show that the ENTIRE development misses q. On the simply connected link cover choose f=Log(d_rho-q). The differential df is invariant under deck transformations and is invertible as a REAL two-dimensional differential: d_rho is a positive local diffeomorphism and the logarithm has nonzero complex derivative. Thus |df|^2 descends to a nonsingular Euclidean metric on the compact link torus. It is complete. Its lifted local isometry f is globally one-to-one onto C: lift every Euclidean line segment by completeness to get a covering of C, which is simply connected. Its periods therefore form an injective rank-two translation lattice. For each fixed generator path of length at most L and image in |d|<=R, |Delta f|<=L/(|q|-R) ->0. (7) The endpoint affine action gives exp(Delta_mu f)=exp(U) and similarly for V. Their differences are integer multiples of 2pi i. Both the actual increments in (7) and the prescribed small multiplier logs tend to zero, so these integers are EXACTLY zero in U: Delta_mu f=U, Delta_lambda f=V. (8) The neighborhood needed for (8) is independent of the slopes, because one first proves (8) for the FIXED basis before multiplying by a_i,b_i. No diagonalizing-frame singularity or hidden large winding is allowed. SL eigenvalue signs must first be centered to these projective geometric logs; an old longitude spin is not an extra geometric rotation. For completeness, q need not be bounded by the inverse of one chosen coordinate if that coordinate vanishes. Choose either generator with nonunit multiplier. Each numerator stays bounded away from zero, and max(|a_mu-1|,|a_lambda-1|) tends uniformly to zero. This proves the uniform |q|->infinity statement even when one generator is parabolic. ## 5. Primitive filling gives a complete smooth hyperbolic manifold Translate q to zero. Then d_rho=e^f. On the compact link quotient the positive function exp(t0+chi_rho(w))/|d_rho(w)-q| is bounded above: numerator and denominator transform by the same |a_lambda|. Thus the explicit end (6) contains the ENTIRE equivariant epigraph y>A|d-q| for some finite A. There is no unproved assumption that an abstract cusp link is realized by an actual full geometric end. About the axis 0--infinity put r=y/|d-q| and use R=asinh(1/r), theta=Im f, X=Re f+(1/2)log(1+r^2). Direct substitution into the upper-half-space metric gives ds^2=dR^2+cosh(R)^2 dX^2+sinh(R)^2 dtheta^2. (9) The epigraph contains the whole punctured tube 0<R<R0. A log period L acts by (X,theta)->(X+Re L,theta+Im L). By (1),(8), the actual primitive slope has period 2pi i epsilon. Choose integers c,d with ad-bc=1. Its complementary primitive period cU+dV has nonzero real part, since the log-link period lattice has real rank two. Adding R=0 in (9) is therefore an ordinary smooth hyperbolic solid torus, with meridian EXACTLY a mu+b lambda. The angular period is 2pi, not a multiple or a merely exponentiated relation. The affine holonomy of that meridian is the identity, since it has multiplier one and fixes both q and infinity. Thus rho descends to the actual filled fundamental group. Either epsilon sign changes the orientation of the meridian parameter, not the positive orientation of the metric. At an unfilled cusp all a_lambda=1. Formula (4) is an ordinary translation-equivariant local diffeomorphism. Its compact Euclidean link is complete, so its lifted development is the Euclidean plane. Here chi=0 and (6) contains a full horoball quotient: the cusp is complete and has finite volume. The remaining middle region is compact. The finitely many attached bounded-radius solid tori and the ordinary unfilled cusps prove that the whole filled metric is complete and finite-volume. Its complete universal developing cover is H3: lift geodesic segments under its complete local isometry to obtain a covering of simply connected H3. Consequently the descended holonomy is discrete and faithful. This proves the theorem in section1 without importing a deformation, Dehn filling, discrete-faithfulness, or character-uniqueness theorem. ## 6. Absolute regulator calibration for any such source branch Let rho_z now be an actual connected marked representation family near rho0, and use the small squared peripheral logs U_i,V_i above. The elementary marked Bloch boundary/fundamental-chain calculation used in [the general peripheral volume proof](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/general_peripheral_representation_volume_bound.md) and [the source regulator proof](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_pretzel_marked_regulator_and_filling_action.md) is independent of the diagram and number of cusps. In these coordinates it says d Vol(rho_z)=(1/2)sum_i [Re V_i dIm U_i -Re U_i dIm V_i]. (10) Here Vol(rho) is the absolute representation volume of the SAME oriented fundamental class and cusp eigenflags. One way to check the factor is to use eigenlogs u=U/2,v=V/2 (with their fixed central signs): the boundary is -2 sum M_i wedge lambda_i, so the Bloch--Wigner differential is 2 sum(Re v dIm u-Re u dIm v), exactly (10). Distinct boundary tori have zero mutual intersection pairing. No equal-color assumption enters. Suppose a holomorphic source potential F on this marked branch has dF=(1/2)sum_i V_i dU_i, Im F(0)=Vol(M). (11) These are hypotheses about the actual peripheral connection and its absolute COMPLETE anchor, not just about its Hessian. Define D_F=Im F-(1/2)sum_i Re U_i Im V_i. (12) Direct differentiation of (11) gives the right side of (10). Both functions equal Vol(M) at the complete point. Therefore throughout the connected marked branch D_F=Vol(rho_z). (13) This is an absolute identity. It does not reset logarithms on loops, splice different character lifts at a projected node, or infer a constant from a matching stationary polynomial. Nonzero spin terms must be retained when converting the literal source to the centered form (11); they cancel only in the paired expression (12). At an actual filled point from section1, the representation volume in (13) is the volume of its constructed complete geometric metric. If comparing with any other complete hyperbolic metric on the same marked oriented filled topology, apply the independently proved representation-volume inequality in BOTH directions. Their volumes are equal. No unproved equality case or imported rigidity theorem is needed to identify (13) with its usual hyperbolic volume. The finite filling-chain normalization is also diagram-independent: replace the old cusp map by its axis-valued comparison, whose shared conical boundary homotopy has volume O(Y^-2); then extend the SAME finite boundary triangulation through the solid torus with every vertex on that axis. All added tetrahedra have zero volume. This is the compatible construction in the cited peripheral/source proofs; putting only unrelated new vertices on the axis would not suffice. ## 7. Arbitrary primitive filling action, with the exact boundary term When a source branch has local U coordinates and (11), a primitive slope a_i mu_i+b_i lambda_i with b_i!=0 has filling potential F_sigma(U)=F(U)+sum_(i in F) [a_i U_i^2/(4b_i)-pi i epsilon_i U_i/b_i]. (14) Its U_i derivative is (a_i U_i+b_i V_i-2pi i epsilon_i)/(2b_i). At its stationary filling point and with unfilled cusps complete, Im F_sigma =Im F-(1/2)sum_(i in F) Re U_i Im V_i =Vol(rho)=Vol(M(sigma)). (15) Indeed Im V_i=(2pi epsilon_i-a_i Im U_i)/b_i, which proves (15) without deleting a complex endpoint term. Constants already known to be real do not affect (15), but remain in any exact period formula. If b=0, primitivity forces |a|=1 and (1) cannot occur with small U; there is therefore no omitted near-complete filling in this chart. Equivalently one may change the primitive basis and its potential. For the existing convention U=-z,V=-2ell,a=1,b=p, epsilon=-m, (14) is G(z)+(z-2pi i m)^2/(4p) up to a REAL constant. This recovers the exact chirp/source formula, including its factor two and its retained longitude spin. ## 8. The conditional QUANTUM bridge, and what is actually proved The geometric theorem is unconditional for every actual framed representation satisfying section1. To prove the volume conjecture for a new original knot/source family one must additionally prove: * An exact original-source construction or selected-cycle argument supplies the ACTUAL near-complete representation of the base group, with the literal caps, all port equations, chosen eigenflags and true primitive preferred peripheral markings. * The selected parameter point exists in the fixed neighborhood, with all unfilled cusps complete and the actual small log equations (1) with unit charges. An exponentiated equation alone is insufficient. * The source action has the calibrated derivative and complete constant (11), and its filling kernel has the boundary correction (14) in the same convention. * The COMPLETE original finite source has a nonzero asymptotic contribution with exponential action F_sigma/(2pi i), with all other terms controlled. In particular its scalar has the form K_N=exp[N F_sigma/(2pi i)] A_N, (1/N)log|A_N| ->0, (16) after the recorded original framing/normalization factors. This must be established from the source, not assumed from a formal saddle. It includes overflow and alias bands, all colors, normal derivative channels, boundary currents, Stokes accessibility and noncancellation, at the desired full sequence of levels. Then (15),(16) prove lim_(N->infinity) (2pi/N)log|K_N|=Vol(M(sigma)). (17) This bridge is transparent about which work remains quantum. It does not assert that a positive norm, formal gluing solution, local normal block or representation-volume upper bound implies (16). Nor does it assume every augmented diagram has a known positive original-source base period. Those conclusions need independent proofs. The [existing full original-source pretzel theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_long_pretzel_full_source_survival.md), its [literal global lift](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_pretzel_port_lift_and_geometric_anchor.md), and its [marked regulator certificate](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_pretzel_marked_regulator_and_filling_action.md) do supply all four inputs for fixed odd s>=25 and independently sufficiently long fixed signed slopes, subject to the unchanged quantifiers of those source theorems. The subsequently independently audited [varying-radius alias extension](actual_pretzel_all_width_extension.md) lowers that actual quantum width threshold to every fixed odd s>=9: its entire-color bound is B_*<.81, whereas the exact width-nine source margin is greater than .812633708. All other local analytic and geometric ingredients were already valid there. The remaining widths3,5,7 are not proved by this envelope. The [specific positive-core proof](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_long_pretzel_geometric_filling_completion.md) was already sufficient for that class. The present result removes ALL graph/polyhedron/width restrictions from the GEOMETRIC implication, but does not claim a new unproved original-invariant family. For other fully augmented bases, crossing-circle source/filling identities are exact, but a whole-source open-corridor survival estimate and complete global color/alias gap have not been proved just by those identities. For arbitrary knots, a classical A-curve or the general representation-volume inequality still does not provide the missing selected-source asymptotic. These are specific unproved quantum inputs, not residual uncertainty about which hyperbolic volume (15) denotes. There is now a stronger, independently checked way to supply the last quantum bullet for integral crossing-circle fillings: the [general original-source long-filling transfer](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/general_original_source_long_filling_transfer.md) proves the filled nonzero asymptotic from an EXACT even holomorphic BASE color packet, its uniform complex Gaussian expansion, and a strict gap over the entire complementary physical color cube. Its exact multilinear filling identity retains every confluent normal coefficient, and its Fourier proof keeps the endpoint currents and all charges. Thus one need not assume the desired filled asymptotic in each new application. What remains to prove for another augmented base is that specified original packet and global gap, together with its actual bounded geometric lift and calibration. The theorem does not infer those base certificates from the underlying hyperbolic geometry. ## 9. Adversarial scope audit of the current equality claim The existing long-pretzel equality proof passes the following geometric checks: its actual base holonomy is complete and positively oriented; its local port construction is a genuine representation, not trace data alone; its bounded cusp frames persist; the unfilled main cusp is genuinely parabolic; its geometric multiplier logs are centered before forming the slope; and the surviving source charges give primitive 2pi, rather than an accidentally killed PSL word. These are precisely the hypotheses used here. The following stronger statements are NOT justified by that proof: * Equality for every knot, every augmented diagram, short fillings, growing width, or slopes growing with N. * Inferring hyperbolicity from killing a slope without the local geometry and actual winding. A 4pi cone completion has the same killed PSL meridian and is excluded only by the unit period. * Replacing framed representation convergence by convergence of a few traces or cusp ratios. The finite C1 construction needs the actual finite generator matrices and selected flags in a bounded frame near the complete holonomy. A singular diagonalizing frame is not that input; the literal bounded port lift supplies it in the established application. * Calling the complete augmented volume Vol(M) the volume of a nontrivial finite filling. The latter is (15), evaluated at its actual selected parameter point. * Obtaining existence of a nearby representation for arbitrary long slopes from the conditional wording of section1. A source analytic family or an independently proved deformation theorem must supply that existence. * Treating Casson--Rivin strict concavity on the OLD complete-cusp angle slice as the filled equality proof. Its constraints differ. The direct construction above does not need an all-ideal angle chart or a universal positive triangulation existence claim. Thus the genuine extension here is a universal geometric completion and absolute calibration theorem for any ACTUAL selected near-complete source branch. It leaves the full-source estimates exactly where they belong, and does not replace the active broader equality goal by a generic conditional assertion. ## 10. Focused construction checks [The new focused audit](../experiments/audit_general_source_regulator_hyperbolic_equality.py) passes exact arbitrary-slope action algebra, eight Lorentz normalization/reindexing-equivariance families, and sixteen explicit affine-cusp/primitive-slope families with both winding signs. Its compactly supported cubic partition checks the positive real link Jacobian, exact affine and height equivariance, small log increments, and nonzero complementary core period. This tests the NEW construction, not only its inherited tube-coordinate formula. The universal argument is the analytical C1-continuity/compactness proof above; these finite checks make no additional knot-source or general existence claim. Before equivariance is used, the entire fundamental-parallelogram image must avoid q. Section 3’s compact C1 estimate gives this exclusion, which is used explicitly in Section 4. The positive-core and primitive log-link arguments are required in addition to the representation equations.

title: Coverage of the untwisted augmented-source volume theorem
status: Primary theorem statements and exact parity compatibility
text: # Coverage of the untwisted augmented-source volume theorem Checked 30 October 2026 against the primary versions linked below. This compares definitions and theorem statements with [the untwisted source theorem](general_untwisted_augmented_source_volume.md). It imports no external proof or proof technique and makes no priority claim. The present statement fixes one connected augmented plat, its actual labeled convex ideal right-angled cut polyhedron, and its complete link exterior. It concerns the original single-mark root invariant, no retained half twists, and the full integer sequence of levels. It does not concern arbitrary filled knots, all retained half-twist sums, or an invariant chosen only after fixing a geometric triangulation. ## 1. The invariant name is not a distinction Murakami--Murakami, *The colored Jones polynomials and the simplicial volume of a knot*, arXiv:math/9905075v2, 10 June 1999, Theorem 4.9, identifies their Kashaev invariant with the normalized colored Jones evaluation for every link and every integer N>=2. The introduction specifies N-dimensional colors, a primitive N-th Jones root, and unknot value one. Thus an overlapping colored-Jones theorem cannot be excluded merely by calling our source "original Kashaev." [Primary version, pp.1 and15](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/9905075v2). Our parameter dictionary is q=exp(pi i/N), Jones t=q^2, and skein A=exp(pi i/(2N)). The [literal source identity, section4](general_matching_graph_full_normal_source.md) divides exactly one ordinary physical trace factor D_N=(-1)^(N-1)[N] before root specialization, equivalently retains its specified first normal. It is not division by one quantum dimension for every component. Mark, framing and dual-order phases must still be matched in any concrete comparison; they cannot convert an exact zero into a nonzero value when they are units. ## 2. Direct overlapping link results and the parity test Van der Veen, *Proof of the volume conjecture for Whitehead chains*, arXiv:math/0611181v2, 30 July 2007, Main Theorem, covers W_(a,b,c,d). Its b=1 conclusion runs over all N; this includes the named Whitehead-link and Borromean-ring examples. For b>=2 the statement is odd-only and the even evaluations vanish. Definition1 makes b the number of Belt tangles. The generic normalization on printed p.4 is sum_n [2n+1]/[N] times the composed tangle eigenvalues, so the even zeros are not explained by a different number of component reductions. The text also records a Seifert piece when b>=2. [Primary version, pp.2--4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0611181v2). This possible contradiction was checked against the actual diagram, not dismissed by terminology. In Figure1 a Belt is one circle around two straight strands. The stated commuting composition permits two Belt copies to be adjacent. Their circles cobound an annulus disjoint from those strands; the literal cut graph has two parallel MAIN edges with an intervening white bigon. A nondegenerate face of the required convex ideal polyhedron cannot be that bigon. Independently, our exact face polynomial reproduces the even zero: the intervening middle-face degree is at most a_1+a_2<=N-2, whereas the marked coefficient requires N-1. This is a finite source compatibility check, not an asymptotic argument. The complete labeled geometric certificate is essential; connectedness or the word "augmented" alone is insufficient. Van der Veen, *The volume conjecture for augmented knotted trivalent graphs*, Algebraic & Geometric Topology9 (2009), 691--722, Definition2 and Theorem2, uses a KTG move sequence and a sequence-dependent minimum number of augmentation rings at every unzip. It states an odd-N SO(3) volume law and zero even-N evaluations. The singly augmented outside consists of regular ideal octahedra; additional rings introduce the stated Seifert pieces. The normalization divides by an unlink according to SPLIT components, not by every link component. This is substantial prior augmented-family coverage, but the theorem's multiplicity and parity hypotheses must be retained. [Published primary paper, pp.692,695--696](https://msp.org/agt/2009/9-2/agt-v9-n2-p02-s.pdf); [arXiv:0805.0094v2, 5 February 2009](https://arxiv.org/abs/0805.0094v2). ## 3. Octahedral results and nearby quantum regimes Ibarra--McQuire--Purcell, *Augmented links, shadow links, and the TV volume conjecture: A geometric perspective*, New York J. Math.32 (2026), 1--34, Definition2.8, restricts "octahedral" to the indicated regular-ideal-octahedron decomposition. Theorem2.12 identifies these complements with fundamental shadow-link complements. Theorem4.15 gives the untwisted Turaev--Viro volume limit at exp(2pi i/r), odd r. Theorem4.16 also gives a colored-Jones limit for equal colors m at t=exp(4pi i/(2m+1)), with m even; Remark4.17 presents the extension to all m as an expectation. This is not the ordinary N-dimensional/Jones-root exp(2pi i/N) specialization merely by renaming m. The introduction explicitly attributes earlier Kashaev coverage of octahedral augmented examples to van der Veen. [Published primary version, pp.4,8,30--31](https://nyjm.albany.edu/j/2026/32-1p.pdf). The earlier arXiv:2506.09296v1 has different theorem numbering; the numbers here are those of the journal version. Wong--Yang, *Relative Reshetikhin--Turaev invariants, hyperbolic cone metrics and discrete Fourier transforms I*, arXiv:2008.05045v4, 11 December 2022, Theorem6.3, states generalized colored-Jones asymptotics for twisted octahedral fully augmented links at exp(4pi i/r), odd r, with colors giving sufficiently small cone angles. Theorem6.1 includes the corresponding odd-r Turaev--Viro statement, including twists. These are important overlapping geometric families and quantum conclusions, not a theorem restricted to the untwisted case. Their root/color and relative-RT conventions still need to be retained when comparing the exact invariant above. [Primary version, sections1.1 and6](https://arxiv.org/html/2008.05045v4). ## 4. General polyhedra and triangulations are separate coverage Belletti, *An upper bound conjecture for the Yokota invariant*, arXiv:2002.01904v2, 20 June 2024; published AGT25 (2025), 645--675, Theorem4.9, proves its upper-bound conjecture for graphs obtained from the tetrahedron by the two specified vertex/face moves. The trivalent Yokota invariant is a unitary bracket absolute square, with odd root order and its own admissible colors. The right-angled rectification and TV consequences are relevant prior coverage, but do not identify the original single-mark all-level link source. [Primary version, Definition2.7 and Theorem4.9](https://arxiv.org/html/2002.01904v2). Ge's *Geometric ideal triangulations of hyperbolic 3-manifolds*, arXiv:2609.27635v1, submitted 23 September 2026, is an existing primary preprint. Theorem1.1 states geometric ideal triangulation existence for every complete finite-volume cusped hyperbolic 3-manifold. This is a geometric statement, not a Kashaev/colored-Jones asymptotic, an invariant-normalization identity, or a theorem selecting an original quantum period. No inference about the correctness of its proof is made in this coverage check. [Primary statement](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.27635v1). Jun Murakami's 13 October 2026 IPAM talk abstract explicitly describes fully augmented right-angled polyhedra and their complexified filling deformations. This is a closely related existing program, but that abstract does not state the present full-level untwisted theorem. [Primary event abstract](https://mathinstitutes.org/videos/25102). The search also found Casandra Monroe's 2018 Princeton senior thesis, *Knot Too Big: The Volume Conjecture for Augmented Links*. Its repository abstract concerns fully augmented links. The repository's PDF endpoint required authentication during this check, so its theorem statements were NOT verified; its title alone supports neither inclusion nor exclusion. [Primary repository record](https://theses-dissertations.princeton.edu/items/c0cd5846-e602-42cc-b935-b9e36c73fb7e). ## 5. Publication wording supported by this check The result should acknowledge existing Whitehead-chain, augmented-KTG and octahedral-link volume results. Its precise statement concerns the recorded original source for any fixed untwisted augmented plat with the specified complete labeled right-angled certificate, without assuming a regular octahedral decomposition. The consulted primary statements do not by themselves establish inclusion of that entire class with that exact all-level normalization. This bounded check is not an exhaustive novelty conclusion. For any claimed overlapping diagram, first match the literal topology, augmentation multiplicities, quantum root and color dimension, one-cut normalization, framing, and level subsequence. Existing covered cases remain covered; a different presentation is not a new case. Conversely, a TV or generalized-Jones theorem cannot silently be substituted for the ordinary root specialization. The known parallel-belt even-zero family shows why these checks are mathematical requirements rather than bibliographical qualifications. No external proof techniques were used. The theorem's own proof remains the exact source/coefficient identity, its global coefficient asymptotic, the uniform channel upper rate, and its absolute geometric normalization. The comparison in Section 2 concerns the literal parallel-belt annulus/bigon and the even-level middle-face degree obstruction. It is not a verification of the external volume proofs.

title: Volume equality for the original untwisted augmented source
text: # Volume equality for the original untwisted augmented source 30 October 2026. This theorem concerns the original complete-circle source of every fixed connected augmented plat carrying the stated labeled right-angled geometric certificate, with NO retained half twists. Its bridge width and matching graph are arbitrary. Both quantum parities and composite levels occur. The source is exactly the original marked root invariant with its recorded normalization; its value is not chosen using the geometric answer. This is a theorem about complete augmented LINK exteriors. It does not assert the volume conjecture for general long-filled k-bridge knots. In a standard adjacent-cap2k-plat the zero-half-twist skeleton has k main components. A full twist cannot change that component count. Thus the untwisted result must not be advertised as that knot theorem. ## 1. Precise statement Fix the literal connected2k-plat box diagram D, k>=2, with R designated crossing circles and its original physical mark. Require a labeled convex ideal right-angled polyhedron Q_D whose face identifications are the actual projection/crossing-disk cut of this diagram. The actual quotient is its complete hyperbolic augmented exterior Y_D and Vol(Y_D)=2Vol(Q_D). This is the [marked geometric certificate](../papers/marked-fillings/README.md), not merely the existence of an unlabeled polyhedron or a positive triangulation of unspecified topology. There is no restriction on R, bridge width, a Conway grammar, or an octahedral decomposition. Let A_(D,N) be the original marked complete-circle root source of [the full matching-graph identity](general_matching_graph_full_normal_source.md), with epsilon_i=0 at every box. Write chi_(D,N) for its separately specified exterior framing factor (one when absent); it has modulus1 in the recorded normalization and is retained below. Then lim_(N->infinity) (2pi/N) log|A_(D,N)| =Vol(Y_D). (1) In particular A_(D,N) is nonzero for all sufficiently large N. The limit runs over all positive integer levels, including even and composite levels. It is not an iterated limit in which the diagram grows with N. ## 2. The exact positive finite source Set d=N-1 and M=floor(d/2). The [marked face-coefficient theorem](../papers/filling-bounds/README.md) gives EXACTLY A_(D,N)=chi_(D,N) N^R sum_(a in {0,...,M}^R) product_i[k_ai beta_ai^2] C_(N,a), (2) C_(N,a)=[product_(f!=u,v)L_f^d] product_i[D_ai,in D_ai,out P_si] at L_u=L_v=0. All C_(N,a) are nonnegative, so positivity concerns the scalar after the displayed common unit phase is removed. The original mark removes exactly the two face exponents u,v, and total polynomial degree dR excludes every additional Fourier alias. The primitive face grid supplies precisely N^R after its original single1/N marked factor. The complete-circle normal is already in k_ai beta_ai^2. No root-only replacement for an uncomputed generic normal is made here. The finite identity also holds for several main components. It requires connected projection and the literal single marked cap. It does not replace that mark by independent reduced normalizations on each link component. ## 3. Lower bound from an actual positive coefficient Choose the single original label vector a_i=M at every circle. The [global coefficient saddle theorem](actual_positive_face_coefficient_saddle.md) applies through both folds. It proves a positive coefficient with an exact compact-torus integral, a unique positive critical radius near the actual circle packing, and a nonzero relative Gaussian asymptotic. Its absolute action is computed from the source determinant and the actual facet coning: lim (1/N)log C_(N,(M,...,M))=Vol(Y_D)/(2pi). (3) At the fold beta_M has zero normalized logarithmic rate, k_M is1 or2, and the factor N^R is polynomial. After removing the same unit phase, every other term of (2) is nonnegative. Keeping this ONE actual term therefore proves the required lower bound. No local-contour contribution or cancellation coefficient is left to assume in this step. ## 4. Upper bound for the whole original sum Evaluate all face polynomials at the SAME finite positive circle-packing radii l_f, with L_u=L_v=0. Positivity gives for each exact coefficient C_(N,a)<= product_i[D_ai,in(l)D_ai,out(l)P_si(l)] /product_f l_f^d. (4) The [uniform channel-rate theorem](actual_positive_face_channel_rate.md) keeps the original beta factors and proves a uniform logarithmic rate for every integer a_i, including0 and both folds. At these shared radii the local circle rate is strictly increasing in mu_i=a_i/N up to1/2. Its derivative is the explicit positive quantity log[E_b(mu_i)E_c(mu_i)/D_xy(mu_i)]. Thus (4), WITH the beta factors in (2), has normalized rate at most the all-fold value plus o(1), uniformly over all label vectors. The actual coning identity fixes that value absolutely as Vol(Y_D)/(2pi). There are only (M+1)^R channel vectors, the multiplicities are at most 2^R, and the outside N^R is polynomial. Summing the upper bounds does not change their exponential rate. This proves the matching upper bound and hence (1). The same argument gives a strict macroscopic channel gap: for each fixed eta>0, terms having some a_i/N<=1/2-eta have a smaller common-radius upper rate by a positive diagram-dependent amount. It does not by itself give a relative asymptotic in the sqrt(N) folded window. ## 5. What remains for the requested knot theorem Retained half twists preserve the exact positive coefficients but attach the original phases product_i omega_ai^epsilon_i to different channels. The upper bound above survives. Positivity no longer supplies the lower bound for that signed sum. A uniform relative folded-window estimate and a nonzero signed Gaussian coefficient are still required generally. Long fillings require a further source theorem in the EXTERNAL crossing-circle colors. These are different from the internal a_i in (2). The existing exact long-filling transform and marked geometric filling threshold do not supply that mixed-color packet or its alias gap. The target remains: every fixed essential hyperbolic2k-plat skeleton, with independently sufficiently long FIXED signed full twists, has the original knot volume limit. This note establishes the complete untwisted augmented-source theorem and a general signed-source upper bound; it does not mark that larger target as solved. ## 6. Dependencies and verification scope The proof combines exact source normalization/support/measure, a global positive coefficient saddle, a uniform all-channel upper rate, and an absolute geometric coning identity. Each dependency has a separate written proof and focused original-source audit. No finite set of knot examples, estimated limiting graph values, or unverified literature proof replaces any of these steps. No novelty or literature-coverage claim is made by this note. The result is the stated complete untwisted augmented-link theorem. It does not settle the general signed long-filled knot conjecture. The [primary-statement coverage comparison](general_untwisted_augmented_source_literature_coverage.md) records prior overlapping families and root conventions. In particular, the parallel-belt examples with even-level zeros fail the required nondegenerate cut certificate; the exact coefficient formula reproduces their zeros. No external proof or priority claim is used.

title: Whole original mixed-source volume in the untwisted corridor
text: # Whole original mixed-source volume in the untwisted corridor 30 October 2026. The whole original mixed source has the actual geometric volume limit throughout a fixed near-complete corridor at its untwisted external circle ports. This follows from the frozen source gap, complex core and marked geometric assembly; no additional numerical theorem is needed. Fix a certified connected augmented flat plat D and a set E of its UNTWISTED external circle ports. The other ports stay at external color N and may keep their original signed half twists. Use the original cups, ordinary caps, unrestricted mark and scalar normalization throughout. Write A_N(N-h_E,N_else) for this actual mixed source and F_N^E(h) for its exact empty-subset cosine core, with deficits zero off E. The [block-representation/corridor theorem](actual_smoothed_block_representation_volume.md), section5, supplies delta0,gamma>0 and K such that, for all large N of either parity and every integer 0<=h_i<=delta0*N, |A_N(N-h_E,N_else)-F_N^E(h)| <=N^K exp[N(Phi_D-gamma)], Phi_D=Vol(Y_D)/(2pi). The [global complex-core theorem](../papers/casimir-source-asymptotics/README.md), sections1 and6, supplies a zero-free relative unit asymptotic on one fixed complex neighborhood of completeness, with exact finite-N phase S_N tending uniformly to the selected S. In particular uniformly on a smaller real neighborhood, (1/N)log|F_N^E(N chi)|=Re S(chi)+o(1), S(0)=Phi_D. Choose 0<delta<=delta0 so the real cube [0,delta]^E lies in that neighborhood and Re S(chi)>=Phi_D-gamma/2 there. Its uniform lower bound gives, after decreasing a constant c>0 and increasing N0, A_N(N-h_E,N_else)/F_N^E(h)=1+O(exp(-cN)) (1) uniformly on the entire PHYSICAL integer corridor 0<=h_i<=delta*N. Polynomial factors and the uniform o(N) in the core lower bound are absorbed by, for example, any c<gamma/4 after increasing N0. No equality of off-grid continuations or of genuine-q normal families is used. The ratio is legitimate because the actual core is zero-free there for all sufficiently large N, of both parities. By the [marked geometric assembly](actual_complete_core_geometric_deformation.md), sections2--4, the selected representation rho_chi has main meridians complete and crossing-circle logs U_i=-2pi*i*chi_i. For real chi, Re U_i=0, so its regulator boundary correction vanishes. Thus for ANY integer sequence h_N with 0<=h_N<=delta*N and h_N/N tending to chi, lim_(N->infinity) (2pi/N)log|A_N(N-h_(N,E),N_else)| =Vol(rho_chi). (2) This is the WHOLE original mixed source, not merely its cosine core. The class and fixed width are arbitrary within the actual labeled certificate, and constants may depend on D. The representation is the actual near-complete marked geometric family; no cone-manifold completion, distant-color estimate, signed varied-port corridor, filled-knot invariant equality or uniformity over growing diagrams is asserted. Equations (1)--(2) use only already frozen uniform theorems and need no new numerical audit. The finite-N phase remains in the relative core asymptotic; only its uniform limiting action is used for the exponential comparison and the volume limit. No off-grid or genuine-q identity is inferred.

title: An intrinsic norm torsor from the quantum A-module
text: # An intrinsic norm torsor from the quantum A-module Research note, 25 October 2026. The target is Kashaev's original invariant. The noncommutative A-polynomial defined through recursions is a literature object: see Garoufalidis, [math/0306230](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0306230). The construction below starts with a specified operator, without choosing a new ordering of a classical polynomial. It applies to any finite-order q-difference module and uses no triangulation or FAMED condition. This is algebraic structure and an independently proved comparison criterion, not a proof of the volume conjecture. A prescribed Kashaev solution or period pairing is additional data. The current [A-polynomial torsor formulation](a_polynomial_torsor_status.md) puts these algebraic results alongside the regulator period, including its explicit rank-three algebraic connection, and distinguishes the norm-one torus from the scalar intertwiner torsor. It records the unproved classical-curve and selected-period comparison. For the actual knot state, the subsequent [squared-meridian descent](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/even_meridian_norm_descent.md) applies this construction with Y=M^2 and cyclic degree N at q=exp(pi*i/N), retaining the full state's even-level sign. The [regular-period theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/regularized_kashaev_period.md) then supplies the exact complete scalar Tr(Y F_N)/N at Y^N=1 and a positive trace norm. The ordinary-color contribution is polynomially bounded, so these give equivalent volume targets for hyperbolic knots. Their norm comparison with the marked regulator remains unproved. The later [peripheral normal-period theorem](peripheral_normal_period.md) also identifies an integral datum invisible in this localization. Positive volume growth requires every polynomial annihilator to annihilate the complete-color delta module R/R*(Y-1). That module vanishes over C(q,Y), while its selected normal extension records the full ADO value. The theorem gives an exact derivative and inverse-matrix presentation under its explicit rank or Weyl-sector hypotheses. No general hyperbolic-knot rank or norm theorem is inferred. When its stated quantum reciprocity holds, central reflection supplies a further quadratic Hilbert-90 frame: g=(1+gamma(U))/2 for gamma(U)gamma(U^(-1))=1 and gamma(1)=1. The frame preserves the marked normal period. The ambient signed dihedral relation retains kappa^N=(-1)^(N-1); it does not assert T-stability of the scalar solution line or establish the regulator norm. The [actual Weyl-descent theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_weyl_descent.md) now proves the reflection of the literature knot state and forces a unitary monomial reciprocity for its primitive minimal normal operator. Thus its equivariant structure is not inferred from the classical A-curve. Primitive generator units preserve the selected normal metric period. The relevant root-fiber injectivity and regulator norm remain to establish. ## 1. The central curve of an actual root-of-unity module Let q=zeta be a primitive n-th root of unity. Let E=C(x), sigma(x)=zeta*x, F=E^sigma=C(u), u=x^n. Assume that specializing the specified operator is defined and its leading and trailing coefficients are nonzero in E: Ahat=sum_(j=0)^r a_j(x) T^j, T f=sigma(f) T. Its cyclic module has E-basis e,T e,...,T^(r-1)e. The relation Ahat e=0 specifies an invertible companion matrix C(x), with T=C sigma, H=T^n=C sigma(C)...sigma^(n-1)(C). The state is a solution pairing with this module; it is not identified with an arbitrary choice of its column basis. **Central-curve lemma.** D_n(u,v)=det(v I-H(x)) belongs to F[v]. Indeed sigma(H)=C^(-1) H C, so all characteristic coefficients are sigma-invariant. This proof works at composite as well as prime n. It retains all coefficients before any specialization u=1. D_n is determined by the root-of-unity module. Equality of its relevant component with a component of the classical A-polynomial is an extra compatibility statement. Neither a classical symbol at q=1 nor the existence of a quantization establishes that equality. ## 2. A simple component carries a canonical cyclic norm equation Take a component of D_n=0 on which v is a simple eigenvalue, and let k be its function field. The algebra S=k[x]/(x^n-u) is a degree-n finite etale k-algebra. It may be a product of fields; the argument does not assume that this Kummer algebra is connected. Sigma acts on it, and S^sigma=k. The eigenmodule L=ker(H-v I) in S^r has rank one over S. T preserves it because T commutes with T^n. Choose a basis e_L and write T e_L=a e_L, a in S^*. Iteration gives the exact equation N_(S/k)(a)=product_(j=0)^(n-1) sigma^j(a)=v. (2.1) Changing the basis to f e_L changes a to a sigma(f)/f. Thus the generic scalar problem is a cyclic norm torsor on the central curve of the actual operator, rather than on a chosen shape chart. As a k-vector space L has dimension n. Multiplication by x and the semilinear operator T give T x=zeta x T, x^n=u, T^n=v. This is a splitting module of the corresponding central quantum torus. Its endomorphisms commuting with x are S-linear scalars; commuting also with T restricts them to k. Simplicity follows after a separable base change: x has n distinct eigenlines and T cyclically permutes them, so there is no proper nonzero invariant subspace. ## 3. Hilbert 90 gives the comparison torsor explicitly Two scalar realizations a,b with the same norm v have ratio r=a/b of norm one. Define r_0=1, r_j=product_(i=0)^(j-1) sigma^i(r), f(c)=sum_(j=0)^(n-1) r_j sigma^j(c). The norm-one equation implies r sigma(f(c))=f(c). Some c makes f(c) invertible. One elementary justification works also for an etale product: after a separable closure sigma cyclically permutes n coordinates; each coordinate of f(c) is a nonzero linear form. Their product is a nonzero polynomial. Since k is infinite, there is a k-rational c outside its zero set. Hence r=f/sigma(f). A scalar intertwiner between the two modules exists, and any two nonzero intertwiners differ by k^*. This identifies the generic intertwiner torsor as G_m. Globally, local intertwiners give a line bundle on the common regular locus; generic Hilbert 90 does not automatically trivialize that line bundle. Alternatively adjoin lambda with lambda^n=v. Then lambda^(-1)T has n-th power one, and the same calculation descends its invariant rank-one line. This is the peripheral-root realization of the torsor. Consequently, once two specified constructions have the same simple central component, their unpointed module comparison reduces to a scalar period line. Identifying their distinguished vectors, cycles and level-dependent scalar remains necessary. The [root-orbit pointing theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/root_orbit_pointing.md) now gives an exact way to fix that central scalar on the relevant fiber. The actual reduced state has value one at M=-q, in the same root orbit as M=1. A comparison within the same rational solution line that preserves this anchor has central factor one at M^(2N)=1. For the full state one uses the specified nonzero central residue. The theorem also reconstructs the fiber period by maximal minors of the root operator matrix when its rational kernel has rank one. This does not establish the required kernel rank or the geometric period comparison for the full knot class. The subsequent [all-level period theorem](all_level_a_period.md) uses polynomial coherence of the actual integer-color traces to give an exact period formula without that rank condition. It needs only a fixed initial color window and bounded-order q-jets, whose initial values stay bounded near q=1. Its [meridian counterpart](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/bounded_meridian_jets.md) bounds the integral kernel's Smith exponents by the fixed leading M-span. This supplies finite pointing, not the remaining geometric norm comparison. The [affine source extension](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/affine_quantum_a_period.md) retains additional information when the actual homogeneous operator has the stated inhomogeneous source factor. Its root period is a cyclic affine fixed point; in the nonresonant case it is an exact resolvent. The generic source class is not killed by finite stable algebraic covers, by normalized trace. The [adequacy proof](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/adequacy_and_algebraic_periods.md) excludes a fixed algebraic meridian trace for all nontrivial adequate knots. Under either stated source nonresonance test this forces the affine class to be nonsplit. Its identification with the marked regulator and its norm remains separate from multiplicative Hilbert 90 at any single root level. The [formal classical-curve construction](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/formal_a_curve_period_torsor.md) gives a different, complementary branch construction directly at q=1. Its Hensel lift and formal connection do not assume that D_n equals the classical A-polynomial. They still require the geometric component to occur in the actual operator's classical symbol and do not select the actual knot period from its formal branch alone. ### 3.1 Extending through coalescing eigenvalues and apparent poles Normalize the chosen central curve. Work where u and v are units, so the x-root cover Y remains finite etale. The generic rank-one eigenline can be extended as a fractional line lattice Lambda_0 on Y. Define Lambda_cyc=sum_(j=0)^(n-1) T^j Lambda_0. (3.1) **Extension lemma.** Lambda_cyc is an invertible fractional line sheaf, T Lambda_cyc=Lambda_cyc, and it is the smallest T-stable lattice containing Lambda_0. Proof: the sum is coherent and torsion-free of rank one; on a smooth curve this is invertible. The identity T^n=v and the fact that v is a unit give T Lambda_cyc=Lambda_cyc. Minimality follows by applying each T^j to the inclusion of Lambda_0. No regularity of the original companion matrix at the point is needed on this generic eigenline. After adjoining lambda^n=v, the invariant lattice for lambda^(-1)T descends to a line bundle on the peripheral-root base. This handles apparent poles or eigenvalue coalescence in the matrix presentation. It does not equate the limiting eigenline with the entire kernel of the specialized matrix, which can be larger. It also does not assign a value to a meromorphic period without its pointing. Different initial lattices can retain different divisor data. A useful exact model is T e=((x-1)/(zeta*x-1)) e, T^n=1. Its coefficient has a zero and pole above u=1. Put P_n(x)=(x^n-1)/(x-1)=1+x+...+x^(n-1). Starting from O_Y e, (3.1) gives O_Y e/P_n(x): at each root of unity other than x=1 some summand has a simple pole, while at x=1 the summand j=0 remains a unit. In the extended frame e'=e/P_n, T e'=e', e' at x=1 equals e/n. (3.2) Thus the pole is removed by an actual lattice change, and the exact specialization retains a factor n. Its exponential rate is zero. This is a uniform algebraic example of why peripheral multipliers and the integral period lattice must be tracked together. ### 3.2 Retain the full spectral algebra at a multiple root Extending one generic eigenline does not recover the whole generalized eigenspace or the operators acting on it. The [Casimir/recoupling calculation](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/casimir_braiding_and_recoupling_lattice.md) now gives an explicit instance relevant to the actual Kashaev crossing: its cyclic spectral algebra is C[z]/(T_N(z)+2), with double roots. The crossing and pivotal trace both use first derivatives at those roots. Its vacuum lies in the socle of a double point and does not by itself fix a module frame there. When a generalized spectral module is rank one over its finite spectral algebra A, its frame comparison is an A^*-torsor. Section 7 of that note extends Hilbert 90 to characteristic-zero Artin bases by a finite nilpotent logarithm and an explicit additive telescoping formula. This retains the jets. The rank-one-over-A hypothesis is proved there by cyclicity of the relative Casimir; it is not assumed for every specialized quantum A-module. The simple-component argument above remains valid on its stated locus. ## 4. A uniform exact check on the central-curve condition For the companion family C(x)=[[0,-1],[1,c-x]], put s_0(c)=2, s_1(c)=c, s_(j+1)=c s_j-s_(j-1). Then at every primitive level n, D_n(u,v)=v^2-(s_n(c)-u)v+1. (4.1) Here is a direct proof. The determinant of H is one. Its trace is sigma-invariant and is a polynomial in x of degree at most n, so only the constant and x^n terms survive. The constant is tr(C(0)^n)=s_n(c). The top coefficient is (-1)^n zeta^(n(n-1)/2)=-1. This proves (4.1) uniformly. For c=1, s_n(c)=2 cos(n*pi/3). Thus constants can retain a periodic level dependence even when the input coefficients are integral. This is an abstract module calculation, not a counterexample about a knot invariant. It shows what must actually be checked in any claimed quantum-Frobenius compatibility. The exact audit in `experiments/audit_intrinsic_norm_torsor.py` checks the central curve, eigenline norm, and Hilbert-90 formula at composite levels as well as prime levels. It does not assume equality with a classical knot A-polynomial. ## 5. Which normalization factors affect the volume rate Let c(q) be a fixed nonzero meromorphic germ at q=1. Along q_n=exp(2*pi*i/n), log|c(q_n)|=O(log n), provided the specialized factor is defined and nonzero. This follows by writing c(q)=(q-1)^j g(q), g(1)!=0. The same conclusion holds for a fixed algebraic Puiseux germ, with rational j. Multiplication by such a factor preserves the exponential volume rate. A regular nonzero factor 1+x^n=1+u at u=1 is harmless for that rate, although its exact value remains part of the state comparison. Finite-level Hilbert 90 by itself gives no uniform-in-n bound on its remaining k^* scalar. For instance, (u/2)^n is a central algebraic unit at each level, equals one at u=2, and equals 2^(-n) at u=1. This preserves an unpointed module while changing a chosen scalar period's exponential size. It demonstrates insufficient reconstruction data, not freedom to renormalize the already defined Kashaev invariant. Thus one needs level-compatible pointing and regulator normalization of this intrinsic period line. The all-level theorem linked above now specifies the quantum period by finite pointing once an actual operator is given; its regulator comparison remains missing. A fixed algebraic generic-q comparison could be sufficient for the rate; arbitrary unrelated finite-level gauges are not. The subsequent [central normalization theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/algebraic_central_normalization.md) allows a fixed finite algebraic comparison depending also on the central variable z=M^(kN), evaluated as a whole germ. Its value is between fixed powers of N. This covers the exact ADO normalization and retains factors such as 1+M^N. The levelwise unit (u/2)^n above has no such fixed finite algebraic presentation across levels. The subsequent [local normalization tower](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/cyclotomic_normalization_tower.md) proves distribution between arbitrary levels and its regulator estimate directly from finite products and an exact convergent series. The [regular cyclic/Steinberg family](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/cyclic_steinberg_lattice.md) extends the selected local vacuum and gives explicit recoupling lattices at degeneration. These supply local comparison data; neither establishes the global period identification required in Section 7. ## 6. The classical A-curve and finite-cover descent Fix the peripheral monomials m,l in the unhalved conventions of the Bloch-period note. Put omega=-(1/2)(log|m| dArg(l)-log|l| dArg(m)). The previously proved identity delta(beta)=-(1/2)m wedge l gives dD(beta)=omega on an augmented character chart. This is the general exactness property of the A-curve, with its peripheral conventions retained. Exact polynomials and their volume functions are existing literature definitions; see Guilloux--Marche, [1804.01395](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.01395). No novelty is claimed for exactness or for conjugation normalization. Here is a useful direct descent argument. Suppose p:Y->C is a connected finite cover of smooth curves, and a single-valued real function V on Y satisfies dV=p^*omega. Remove the finitely many branch values and set V_C(c)=(1/degree(p)) sum_(y over c) V(y). Then dV_C=omega. The function V-p^*V_C is locally constant on the connected punctured curve Y, so constant; its fiber average is zero, so it is zero. Thus V descends exactly. Continuous extensions at removed points agree wherever they exist. In particular, a finite peripheral cover does not prevent descent of the real regulator norm. If C is preserved by complex conjugation iota, then iota^*omega=-omega. Any primitive V_0 gives a unique conjugation-odd primitive V_odd=(V_0-V_0 composed with iota)/2. Uniqueness follows since two primitives differ by a constant, which cannot be odd. When the chosen representation component and its volume are conjugation-compatible, this fixes the real normalization. That compatibility is not assumed for every component; the marked Bloch lift retains the normalization in the general case. The subsequent [Regge/cover calculation](regge_period_covers_and_a_curves.md) distinguishes this parameter-cover descent from a manifold cover. The latter changes peripheral variables by an integer monomial map, sends the geometric A-factor by elimination and multiplies the marked regulator by the topological cover degree. Its quantum boundary inclusion changes the commutation parameter by the boundary degree. For the unordered ideal-shape parameter space, the finite Regge action also needs its orientation local system: an untwisted norm over its six orderings cancels the Bloch volume. That is a failure to descend the same differential form, rather than an exception to the descent argument above. ## 7. The general target after the geometric audit The audited geometric existence input supplies a positive fundamental- class representative for every hyperbolic knot. On the classical side the existing Bloch-period notes give the marked regulator line and log||P_hyp||=2 Vol(M)/pi. For the original Kashaev invariant, the required comparison is (4/n) log|<K>_n| - log||P_hyp|| -> 0. (7.1) The sign and scale differ from the later AK state comparison. Equation (7.1) is still unproved. Sections 1--3 identify the intrinsic algebraic comparison torsor. The subsequent [Kashaev/ADO pointing calculation](kashaev_ado_pointing.md) supplies the actual normalization line and its specialization at the Kashaev point. It also proves that rational root-level states lie in a central v=1 sector. That sector need not be the geometric component of the classical q->1 A-curve. The required comparison must retain the original quantum family and its selected period, rather than assume these two curves coincide. Compatibility with the marked geometric regulator and the norm statement (7.1) remain unproved. The subsequent [ramified Weyl-fibre theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/ramified_weyl_fibre.md) specifies the branch-point lattice for the actual normal ADO state. Its invariant lattice retains the first negative-sector coefficient as an ordinary fibre coordinate, and its full complete period is the exact functional (eta_N/2)e_0^*b_0. Under generic rank one the saturated kernel gives a pointed line even at a special rank jump. An equivariant change of frame may fix the ordinary root fibre and still change this coordinate, so a comparison must transport the marked ramified fibre and functional. No equality of central spectra or regulator norms is deduced from that construction. The subsequent [actual threaded-character theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/ado_threaded_shadow.md) proves an additional distinction: the selected ADO evaluation has abelian even-threaded interior data, whereas a null-homologous loop separates the fixed complete hyperbolic character. Hilbert-90 frame descent cannot identify eigenlines with those different scalar data. A source extension can instead select a horizontal source-one eigenvector of a separating observable. Its actual relative realization and norm comparison remain unproved.

title: A literature quantum A-family with the Kashaev evaluation fixed
text: # A literature quantum A-family with the Kashaev evaluation fixed Research note, 25 October 2026. The preceding [crossing calculation](kashaev_crossing_and_period_lattice.md) independently identifies the normalized enhanced Kashaev period with the reduced highest-weight quantum-group period. Here we give its meridian family, its exact normalization lattice, and its implications for the norm torsor. Definitions are the unrolled quantum-group R, pivotal and modified-dimension formulas in Brown--Dimofte--Garoufalidis--Geer, [2005.08176](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.08176), Section 2. Their holonomicity and recursion-ideal comparison theorems are not assumed. The calculations below use the displayed definitions directly. ## 1. The zero-framed reduced family is rational in its color Fix r>=2, q=exp(pi*i/r), and x=q^alpha. On V_alpha use H v_j=(alpha-2j)v_j, K v_j=x q^(-2j)v_j, E v_j=[j]_q[alpha-j+1]_q v_(j-1), F v_j=v_(j+1), 0<=j<r. Use the finite universal R from the preceding note with k<r, pivotal matrix K^(1-r), and twist theta_alpha=q^((alpha^2+2(1-r)alpha)/2). Let F_r(alpha) be the reduced (1,1)-tangle scalar for a zero-framed knot, with unknot value one. It is the usual modified-trace ADO invariant divided by the modified dimension, not a new local weight. **Rationality lemma.** F_r(alpha) is a Laurent polynomial in x with complex coefficients at fixed q. Proof: remove the common factor q^(alpha^2/2) from each positive R and its inverse from each negative R. The remaining entries are Laurent polynomials in x, since q^((alpha-2c)(alpha-2d)/2) =q^(alpha^2/2) x^(-c-d) q^(2cd), [alpha-j+1]_q =(x q^(-j+1)-x^(-1)q^(j-1))/(q-q^(-1)). All denominators [k]_q!, k<r, are nonzero constants. For a braid word of writhe w, the total removed factor is q^(w alpha^2/2). It cancels with theta_alpha^(-w); the remainder is x^(-w(1-r)). The pivotal entries are also Laurent monomials in x. Finite products, sums and partial traces prove the assertion. Scalarity on generic typical colors and the resulting identity extend through the finite exceptional set. In particular F_r(alpha+2r)=F_r(alpha). This has a direct algebraic proof from the defining matrices; it is not a consequence imported from a holonomicity theorem. ## 2. Exact specialization to the original Kashaev period At alpha=r-1 the matrices are the r-dimensional highest-weight matrices of the crossing note. The two pivotal conventions differ by K^(1-r)=(-1)^(r-1) K. The corresponding twists differ by the same sign. For a b-strand braid closing to a knot, w has parity b-1. Hence the resulting factor (-1)^((r-1)(b-1-w)) is one. The dual convention in the crossing note is equivalent to the original highest-weight color: an explicit intertwiner with its dual is B v_j=(-1)^j q^(j(j-r)) v_(r-1-j). For example, with Delta E=E tensor K+1 tensor E and Delta F=F tensor 1+K^(-1) tensor F, the antipodes are S(E)=-E K^(-1) and S(F)=-K F. Direct substitution verifies B on E,F,K. The same substitution in the finite R gives R^T=(B tensor B)R(B^(-1) tensor B^(-1)). Consequently the already specified enhanced period satisfies F_r(r-1)=<K>_r. (2.1) This is a uniform matrix and pairing comparison for knots, with the zero framing and unknot normalization fixed. The subsequent [root-orbit pointing proof](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/root_orbit_pointing.md) extends this calculation to every integer color 1<=j<=r: F_r(M=-q^j)=C_j(q), where C_j is the reduced j-dimensional period. Its proof uses the invariant quotient of the color and a filtered cut-trace argument for a one-component braid closure. In particular F_r(-q)=1 supplies a nonzero reference anchor on the same central fiber as M=1. For the full state this is a residue anchor, as the modified dimension has a pole at M=-q. The [all-level period theorem](all_level_a_period.md) now uses these identities and polynomial rigidity to recover the exact Kashaev value from any specified actual all-level annihilator and finitely many fixed small colors. Whole q-germs handle singular steps with a uniform jet bound. Root-level rank one is not required. ## 3. The generic peripheral factor is an actual cyclic lattice gauge Write N_r(alpha)=d_r(alpha)F_r(alpha) for the modified-trace ADO invariant. Its defining modified dimension is d_r(alpha)=-q^(r(1-r)/2) (q^(alpha+1)-q^(-alpha-1))/(q^(r alpha)-q^(-r alpha)). Introduce the marked meridian coordinate M=-q x, so that M=1 at alpha=r-1. Then, exactly, d_r(M)=eta_r (M-M^(-1))/(M^r-M^(-r)) =eta_r M^(r-1)/P_r(M^2), eta_r=(-1)^(r+1)q^(r(1-r)/2)=i^(r+3), P_r(t)=1+t+...+t^(r-1). (3.1) Thus the modified-dimension factor is the cyclic stable-lattice generator 1/P_r(t) from Section 3.1 of the intrinsic norm-torsor note, with t=M^2, together with its explicit monomial and phase. This is an instance in the literature state itself, not just a model. At M=1 the whole rational germ is regular and evaluates to d_r(1)=eta_r/r, <K>_r=r eta_r^(-1) N_r(r-1). (3.2) Setting numerator and denominator separately to zero would discard this value. The exact comparison keeps the peripheral polynomial P_r and its specialization P_r(1)=r. No topological or norm conclusion uses a bare numerical multiplier in its place. There is also a level-independent difference equation. Since the color shift sends M to q M and q^r=-1, d_r(qM)/d_r(M)=g(q,M), g(q,M)=-q^(-1)(q^2 M^2-1)/(M^2-1). (3.3) If f(M)=M-M^(-1), then g=-f(qM)/f(M). Thus this normalization line is a fixed rational gauge tensored with the sign character of the shift. Its root-level realization is the explicit peripheral divisor in (3.1). It is not a collection of arbitrary independent finite-level scalars. The subsequent [relative octahedral calculation](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/relative_octahedral_period.md) also derives 1/P_r(M^2) as the missing cyclic transition of the finite factorial actually appearing in these R entries. Its polynomial recurrence retains the source M^(2r)e_partial, and its cyclic system is nonsingular even on the completion's polar divisor. Thus this normalization has an explicit local relative origin as well as the meridian gauge calculation above. The global source/regulator comparison is not inferred from it. ## 4. The literature annihilator ideal and the pointed conjecture The all-level ADO annihilator ideal is defined in the literature by I_ADO={P(q,x,T): P(q_r,x,T)N_r(x)=0 for all but finitely many r}, T x=q x T, q_r=exp(pi*i/r). See equation (1.5) of the cited definition source. Under x=-q^(-1)M, the exact change from N_r to F_r induces the automorphism of the localized Ore algebra C(q,M)[T^(+/-1);sigma] M -> M, T -> g(q,M) T. (4.1) Indeed d_r^(-1) T d_r=g T. Therefore existence of a nonzero all-level annihilator is equivalent in the two normalizations, and their localized ideals correspond by (4.1). No unverified equality with the colored-Jones recursion ideal or AJ specialization is needed for this statement. The subsequent [finite cut-state proof](finite_sum_annihilator.md) now supplies a nonzero actual all-level meridian annihilator for every knot. The cited paper's holonomicity theorem remains outside the proof premises; the stronger multicomponent dimension statement is not needed for this conclusion. At M=1 the comparison uses the lattices and regular whole period germs in (3.1)--(3.2), since the localized coefficient g is meromorphic there. Localization alone does not specify this specialization. The subsequent [actual peripheral-fusion proof](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_peripheral_fusion.md) derives this gauge from the pivotal partial traces of the two adjacent-color projectors, without a modified-trace comparison theorem. The full state has elementary boundary actions M+M^(-1) and T+T^(-1). The fusion wall at M=1 has a nonzero square-zero Casimir residue with exactly normalized partial trace; its actual knot coefficient and the normal Kashaev functional are retained as distinct meridian derivatives. Peripheral skein relations thus yield actual annihilators, without identifying the entire ideals or their geometric components. For this literature family with its prescribed pointing, the desired quantum-A volume statement is lim_(r->infinity) (2*pi/r) log|F_r(M=1)|=Vol(S^3 minus K). (4.2) Equations (2.1) and (3.2) identify (4.2) with Kashaev's original conjecture. The same rate for N_r at the regular germ M=1 is equivalent, since log r/r tends to zero and |eta_r|=1. This is a precise formulation with a fixed literature state, not an arbitrary solution of an operator. Equation (4.2) is not proved here. ## 5. What a root-of-unity central torsor does and does not select There is a useful general constraint. Let a nonzero rational function h(x) solve a specialized finite-order q-difference equation with q a primitive n-th root. Let H=T^n be its companion monodromy as in the intrinsic norm-torsor note.
