Then det(I-H)=0. (5.1) Proof: evaluation at h is a nonzero module map from the cyclic operator module to (C(x),sigma). On the target sigma^n=1. Hence the map kills H-I, so H-I cannot be invertible. This proof uses the solution pairing, not an identification of column vectors with solutions. Both F_r and N_r are rational in x at zero framing. Thus any specified all-level operator annihilating them has a central v=1 sector at its regular root levels n=2r. This finite-level sector must not be identified automatically with the geometric component of the classical q->1 A-curve. The quantum family and its distinguished pointing remain essential. No assertion is made that the literal classical A-curve is the central spectral curve of each root-level state. The required torsor comparison is therefore a comparison of the all-level pointed period with the marked geometric regulator, retaining the normalization lattice. The cyclic norm torsor alone does not select the volume-dominant geometric sector.

title: The specified Kashaev crossing and its period pairing
text: # The specified Kashaev crossing and its period pairing Research note, 25 October 2026. This uses Kashaev's crossing weights, [q-alg/9504020](https://arxiv.org/abs/q-alg/9504020), equations (2.7)--(2.12), and the enhanced braid definition recorded in Murakami--Murakami, [math/9905075](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9905075), Sections 1 and 4. Their comparison proofs are not premises. We derive the Fourier identity and normalization comparison below directly from finite products. This is an independent verification of a known comparison, not a new volume theorem. It fixes the literature state to which a quantum A-module argument must apply. All integers N>=2, including even and composite levels, are allowed. The subsequent [Casimir/lattice comparison](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/casimir_braiding_and_recoupling_lattice.md) expresses this same crossing and its inverse by confluent Casimir polynomials, retaining the double-point derivatives and exact writhe phase. It also derives the actual pivotal closing trace on that spectral algebra and identifies the operators through the singular cyclic recoupling lattice. ## 1. The Fourier transform is triangular Put omega=exp(2*pi*i/N), p_j=product_(h=1)^j(1-omega^h), p_0=1, and bar_p_j=product_(h=1)^j(1-omega^(-h)). Let R^o be exactly the unbraided matrix in Kashaev's equation (2.12). Use F_ij=omega^(ij)/sqrt(N), A=(F^(-1) tensor F^(-1)) R^o(F tensor F). **Fourier identity.** With indices in {0,...,N-1}, the only nonzero entries are A_(a-k,b+k ; a,b) =omega^(1+(a-k)(b+1)) p_a p_(b+k)/(p_(a-k) p_b p_k), 0<=k<=min(a,N-1-b). (1.1) In particular, conservation here is equality of ordinary integer sums, not just equality modulo N. ### Direct proof For a nonzero original entry introduce residues u=[j-i-1], v=[i-l], t=[l-k], h=[k-j]. The two theta factors say u+t<N and v+h<N. Their total is congruent to -1 modulo N, so u+v+t+h=N-1. Conversely every such composition and one free j specify exactly one original entry. In these coordinates, i=j-1-u, k=j+h, l=j+h+t (mod N), R^o_(i,j ; k,l)=N omega^(1-(t+h)(u+h)) /(p_u bar_p_v p_t bar_p_h). (1.2) The free j-sum in the Fourier transform gives the conservation delta. Put z=t+h. The remaining sum factors into A_(c,d ; a,b)=delta_(a+b=c+d mod N) sum_(z=0)^(N-1) omega^(1+c-z^2+z(a+b)) S_(N-1-z)(omega^(c-z)) S_z(omega^(z-a)), (1.3) where the elementary finite binomial identity is S_m(X)=sum_(j=0)^m X^j/(p_j bar_p_(m-j)) =product_(j=1)^m(X-omega^j)/p_m. (1.4) For a direct induction, use bar_p_m=(-1)^m omega^(-m(m+1)/2)p_m and compare coefficients in (1-omega^m)S_m(X)=(X-omega^m)S_(m-1)(X). The first factor in (1.3) vanishes unless c<=z; the second vanishes unless z<=a. Using p_(N-1)=N and the same formula for bar_p_j, the surviving sum, with m=a-c, is omega^(1+c(b+1)) (p_a/p_c) sum_(j=0)^m (-1)^j omega^(j(j-1)/2) omega^((b+1)j)/(p_j p_(m-j)) =omega^(1+c(b+1)) (p_a/p_c) (omega^(b+1);omega)_m/p_m. (1.5) The last equality follows from the same finite binomial identity. If b+m>=N, this Pochhammer symbol contains 1-omega^N and vanishes. Otherwise d=b+m as an ordinary integer and the symbol is p_(b+m)/p_b. This proves (1.1), with no primality assumption. ## 2. A literal comparison with the root-of-unity quantum-group matrix Let s=exp(pi*i/N), H_j=N-1-2j, and use the N-dimensional highest-weight module with H v_j=H_j v_j, K v_j=s^(H_j)v_j, E v_j=[j]_s^2 v_(j-1), F_low v_j=v_(j+1). At the endpoints the missing vectors are zero. These are the specialized usual matrices E v_j=[j]_s[N-j]_s v_(j-1), since [N-j]_s=[j]_s. Let R^q=s^(H tensor H/2) sum_(k=0)^(N-1) s^(k(k-1)/2)(s-s^(-1))^k/[k]_s! E^k tensor F_low^k. (2.1) Every denominator in (2.1) is nonzero. Put G_j=p_j/(1-omega)^j=s^(j(j-1)/2)[j]_s!, D_j=(-s)^j, gamma=omega*s^(-(N-1)^2/2). Then (1.1) gives exactly A=gamma (D G tensor G) R^q (G^(-1) tensor G^(-1)D^(-1)). (2.2) Here G,D are diagonal. To verify (2.2), substitute the matrix elements of E^k and F_low^k in (2.1), replace each [j]_s! by s^(-j(j-1)/2)p_j/(1-omega)^j, and cancel. The remaining exponent and factorials are precisely those in (1.1). Thus exponentially large factorials in G have not been declared harmless; their positions in the exact conjugations remain specified. ## 3. The published enhancement and every braid word Let P swap tensor factors, and let S v_j=v_(j+1 mod N). In the enhanced Kashaev convention used here, B_K=P(R^o)^T, mu_K=-s S, alpha_K=-s, beta_K=1. (3.1) The transpose/order in (3.1) matters. Substituting (2.8) of Kashaev in P(R^o)^T gives exactly the four-index enhanced crossing definition. For the quantum-group dual convention put B_q=P(R^q)^T, mu_q=K^(-1), alpha_q=s^((N^2-1)/2), beta_q=1. (3.2) Equation (2.2), transposed and with the tensor factors exchanged, gives a similarity of B_K with gamma*B_q. For a braid on b strands, define U_b=F^(-tensor b) tensor_(j=1)^b (G^(-1)D^(j-1)). The meaning is the product of F^(-tensor b) with the displayed diagonal tensor product. Since B_q conserves the integer weight sum, it commutes with D tensor D. Thus the same U_b works simultaneously for every adjacent generator and its inverse: rho_K(word)=gamma^(w(word)) U_b rho_q(word) U_b^(-1). (3.3) The enhancement also matches exactly: U_b mu_q^(tensor b) U_b^(-1)=mu_K^(tensor b), gamma*alpha_q=-s=alpha_K. (3.4) For the first identity, diagonal G,D commute with mu_q and F^(-1)diag(omega^j)F=S; also s^(-(N-1))=-s. The quantum-group partial traces have values alpha_q and alpha_q^(-1). One way to verify the scalars is to use the coproduct intertwining equations for (2.1) and trace cyclicity: the weighted partial traces commute with the dual module's generators. These act irreducibly because their adjacent coefficients are nonzero and the K eigenvalues are distinct. The traces are therefore scalar. The positive trace at v_(N-1) and negative trace at v_0 each have a single contributing term, giving s^((N^2-1)/2) and its inverse. The coproduct equations themselves reduce to the coefficient recurrence c_(k+1)/c_k=s^k(s-s^(-1))/[k+1]_s of the finite sum (2.1). These checks are elementary algebra and do not invoke a global state-integral theorem. For a braid closure with one component, cut the first strand and take the weighted partial trace over the others. The unnormalized operator is scalar: it is a quantum-group endomorphism of the simple color. Conjugations on the traced factors cancel by cyclicity; conjugation on the open factor cancels because this operator is scalar. Finally the factors gamma^(w) cancel against alpha_K^(-w) by (3.4). **Consequence.** The normalized enhanced Kashaev period in (3.1) equals the reduced N-colored quantum-group period at s=exp(pi*i/N), with unknot value one. This holds for every braid presentation of a knot and every N>=2. It is a direct independent verification of the standard enhanced-state comparison, not an appeal to its published proof. The usual quantum-group parameter for the colored Jones polynomial is omega=s^2; the chosen dual and tensor-order convention is retained. ## 4. A printed phase needs attention The literal candidate inverse printed in Kashaev's (2.15), combined with the normalization (2.12), fails the identity (2.16) already at N=2: the product is -I. This is checked in characteristic zero with rational entries. The exact cyclotomic diagnostics at further levels give omega*I. We use the actual matrix inverse in (3.3), determined by (2.2), rather than silently deleting this phase. This observation concerns a printed normalization identity, not a counterexample to the knot volume conjecture. The enhanced definition (3.1) specifies its own actual inverse and scalar normalization. ## 5. Reproducible algebraic checks and scope `experiments/audit_kashaev_crossing.py` evaluates the original four-index weight independently of (1.1), checks its complete Fourier transform, the quantum-group matrix comparison, and the enhanced partial traces. It includes even and composite levels. Prime-field diagnostics are supplementary to the characteristic-zero identities proved above. The coefficient and enhancement identities fix a literature state uniformly, with no FAMED hypothesis or knot census. They do not prove the AJ conjecture or the Kashaev volume conjecture. In particular, they do not make the AK/Faddeev contour state equal to this finite period. That is a different comparison. A standard noncommutative A-polynomial can now be discussed together with this distinguished reduced quantum-group period, rather than an arbitrary solution of its recurrence. Root-of-unity periodicity and the geometric q->1 branch must still be distinguished in its period-torsor comparison.

title: Coverage check: normalized Racah factorials and hyperideal volume
text: # Coverage check: normalized Racah factorials and hyperideal volume 29 October 2026. Coverage only: primary-source definitions and theorem statements were checked. Their proofs are not inputs to our independent [factorial/normal theorem](actual_supported_racah_common_phase_and_normal_metric.md) or [local geometry theorem](actual_four_port_hyperideal_angle_volume.md). The local 6j–hyperideal-volume relationship is established literature; no novelty is claimed for recovering it here. Our convention is zeta=exp(pi i/N), [u]=(zeta^u-zeta^-u)/(zeta-zeta^-1), integer graph spins j<=floor((N-1)/2), and four face sums>=N-1. W_N is the positive magnitude of the regularized face-normalized scalar, with [N] removed before evaluation. Its exact Casimir angles are pi-(2j+1)pi/N. The uniform result includes closed-chamber sequences and O(log N) error for log W_N; its fixed normal jets are derivatives in zeta=q exp(t), not merely coefficients in a large-N expansion. ## Closest prior statements **Costantino (2007).** Definition3.2 gives the strict hyperbolic-type conditions 1<face sum<2 and triangle deficits between0 and1. Theorem3.9 gives a simple pole and the volume growth of the regularized [n]6j coefficient. His [u] uses q^(u/2), so q_paper=zeta^2 makes the quantum integers IDENTICAL to ours. The D-block volume is twice the tetrahedron volume, matching our pi/N normalization. This already covers the interior leading rate, without an odd-level restriction; parity/composite levels alone are not a new distinction. [Definitions3.1–3.2 and Theorem3.9](https://arxiv.org/html/math/0611399v4), [published article](https://doi.org/10.2140/gt.2007.11.1831). **Chen–Murakami (2023; preprint2017).** Theorems1–2 give the volume limit when a tetrahedron has an ideal or ultra-ideal vertex and a refined Gram-determinant prefactor for specified rational-angle sequences. They take odd r, xi_r=exp(2pi i/r), q=xi_r^2 and [u]=(q^(u/2)-q^(-u/2))/(q^(1/2)-q^(-1/2)). Their scaling is spin/r=(pi-angle)/(4pi). Substituting r=2N would match our quantum integer but violates their odd-r hypothesis. Their explicit halfshift is also prior art. [Theorems1–2 and definition in§2](https://arxiv.org/html/1706.04887v3), [journal DOI](https://doi.org/10.4310/JDG/1679503803). **Belletti–Detcherry–Kalfagianni–Yang.** Theorem1.2 gives the sharp, tuple-uniform v8+O(log r/r) upper capacity for r-admissible6j symbols; AppendixTheoremA.1 states the ideal/hyperideal volume limit under explicit face/deficit conditions. Their root is exp(2pi i/r), r odd, with doubled integer colors. This is substantial overlapping coverage, but a universal v8 bound is not the same statement as our label-dependent two-sided closed-chamber volume estimate. Setting r=2N introduces the [N] poles that their odd-root evaluation avoids. [Theorem1.2,§2 and AppendixA](https://arxiv.org/html/1807.03327v2). **Belletti–Yang (2025).** Theorem1.4 covers generalized hyperbolic volume growth under a negative diagonal-cofactor hypothesis. Theorem1.5 states a refined asymptotic along sequences with fixed sides of the color wall and a limiting tetrahedron without ideal vertices. The root remains exp(2pi i/r), r odd. Their§2 records the earlier ideal/hyperideal cases as well. These results preclude presenting the local volume mechanism as new. [Theorems1.4–1.5 and§2.2](https://londmathsoc.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1112/topo.70033), [arXiv version](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.13864). **Costantino–Murakami (2013).** Their graph face model and6j symbols use non-integral quantum-group representations and relate them to truncated-tetrahedron volume. This is relevant background, not an identified equality with our ordinary highest-weight Hermite source. [Publisher abstract and primary paper](https://ems.press/journals/qt/articles/4181). ## What this bounded check establishes The verified interior local volume claim is covered, most directly by Costantino after the explicit root substitution. Our exact all-chamber O(log N) estimate, scalar generic-normal/inverse-jet bounds and retained [2N] partner current have more specific technical statements; this bounded statement check neither proves they are absent elsewhere nor supports a novelty claim. A refined large-level asymptotic is not automatically a theorem about fixed-root generic-q jets, and a lowest-nonzero Laurent coefficient is not an arbitrary prescribed source normal. None of these local statements supplies our literal marked-source normalization, a positive completed recoupling Gram, or general graph sewing/peripheral constraints. Turaev–Viro conclusions are not silently substituted for original Kashaev invariants. The full-source problem remains separate.

title: Auditing the ordinary-color remainder in the original Fourier energy
text: # Auditing the ordinary-color remainder in the original Fourier energy 28 October 2026. The question is the precise inequality used when replacing the original complete-color value by a positive Fourier norm. The proof below uses the actual finite crossing matrices and a reconstructed positive path trace. No published asymptotic, unitarity, ADO/Jones comparison, or volume-conjecture theorem is a premise. The root convention is essential. Set q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, [j]=sin(pi j/N)/sin(pi/N). Let a fixed braid on b strands close to a ONE-component zero-framed knot, and let C_j(q) denote its original reduced ordinary j-color, with unknot value one. Then, for every 1<=j<N, |C_j(q)| <= [j]^(b-1) <= sin(pi/N)^(1-b). (1) There is no corresponding assertion at j=N. The statement is also not asserted at arbitrary Galois-conjugate roots. The immediate consequence needed in the Fourier argument is the all-level, all-ordinary-color estimate 0 <= E_N-|K_N|^2 <= (N-1)(N/2)^(2b-2). (1a) Here the braid presentation, and therefore b, is fixed as N varies. Neither hyperbolicity nor alternatingness is needed for this bound. The positive-energy identity is exact; only the replacement of its ordinary-color remainder by a polynomial uses the estimate. ## 1. The positive algebra and its trace can be checked directly Put delta=q+q^(-1)=2cos(pi/N), and mu_a=sin((a+1)pi/N)/sin(pi/N), 0<=a<=N-2. These numbers are positive; with zero boundary values they satisfy mu_(a-1)+mu_(a+1)=delta mu_a. On walks of length m in the chain 0,...,N-2 starting at zero, let U_i change only the middle height of a return (c,a,c), with coefficient sqrt(mu_a mu_a')/mu_c. Direct local multiplication gives U_i*=U_i, U_i^2=delta U_i, U_i U_(i+1) U_i=U_i, U_i U_j=U_j U_i for |i-j|>1. Consequently B_i=q^(1/2)I-q^(-1/2)U_i is unitary: its eigenvalues are q^(1/2) and -q^(-3/2). The same displayed relations prove the braid relation. Inverse crossings are the actual inverses. The weighted trace tau_m(A)=sum_walks mu_(last height) A_(walk,walk) is positive. Its weight is central in the path algebra because every generator preserves the last height, so it is tracial too. Directly, tau_(m+1)(A tensor I)=delta tau_m(A), tau_(m+1)((A tensor I)U_m)=tau_m(A). (2) In the first identity sum over the last step using the mu recurrence. In the second identity only the unchanged middle height contributes to the diagonal: mu_c from the last vertex cancels the denominator mu_c of U_m, leaving exactly the weight mu_a on the length-m walk. These recursions identify the trace with the original fundamental quantum trace. Indeed the latter has K=diag(q,q^(-1)) and U block [[q,-1],[-1,q^(-1)]] on (01,10), zero on (00,11); its partial K-trace is I and Tr K=delta. Both traces therefore satisfy (2), with value one on the empty diagram. Uniqueness does not require semisimplicity: the Temperley--Lieb relations inductively span the next algebra by the included algebra and elements A U_m B, and traciality plus (2) determine both types. The spanning claim follows by reducing each U_m A U_m with the preceding spanning statement and the two local quadratic/adjacent relations. ## 2. Ordinary colors are positive projections in this trace Write n=j-1. The recursively defined color projector is p_0=p_1=I, p_(m+1)=p_m tensor I -[m]/[m+1] (p_m tensor I)U_m(p_m tensor I). For n<=N-2 every denominator used is nonzero and every coefficient is real. The local algebra proves idempotence and annihilation by U_1,...,U_(n-1); hence its path realization is an orthogonal projector. The trace recursion gives tau_n(p_n)=[n+1]=[j]. This is the actual highest-weight color, not a color assigned to an unrelated positive model. In the ordinary fundamental tensor space, the common kernel of the U_i has one vector at each tensor weight: the local 01/10 relation fixes their coefficient ratio and adjacent exchanges connect all words of that weight. The vectors obtained by successive coproduct F-actions on the highest tensor span those lines. Their coefficients involve only nonzero [r]!, r<=n. Thus they give the original j-dimensional highest-weight module. The projector acts as identity on this common kernel and has image in it. Restricting the cabled finite universal R to these images gives the original j-color R, by its coproduct identities. A direct coefficient proof of both identities, including the Cartan factors, is given in the [independent color audit](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_ordinary_color_comparison_audit.md#4-the-fundamental-cable-is-the-literal-colored-r). The retained highest-vector Cartan scalar is q^(n^2/2); the ordinary framing twist is q^(n(n+2)/2). Both have modulus one. For b colored strands let P be the tensor product of these projectors. The trace of a disjoint colored closure, or (2) successively, gives tau(P)=[j]^b. The cabled braid is unitary in the path representation and preserves P. It also preserves each last-height block. In an orthonormal basis of Im P within each such block, its diagonal entries have modulus at most one and every trace weight is positive. Therefore |tau(P B P)| <= tau(P)=[j]^b. Dividing by the NONZERO original ordinary quantum dimension [j], and retaining the unit-modulus zero-framing factor, proves (1). At j=N the relevant quantum dimension is [N]=0. In the positive path trace the corresponding negligible projector has zero image. The division just used is unavailable. This is precisely why this proof places no polynomial bound on K_N. ## 3. The ADO orbit really has these ordinary-color values At the orbit color x=q^(j-1), the original N-dimensional module has the invariant subspace U=span(v_j,...,v_(N-1)); its quotient is the ordinary j-dimensional module. Every tensor factor of the finite R, its inverse, and the pivot preserves U. In a basis adapted to U, each matrix path along an underlying strand can enter U but cannot leave it. A one-component braid closure passes through the open cut. For its quotient block that cut starts and ends outside U, forcing every contributing path around the component to stay in the quotient. Thus the induced cut is exactly the all-j-colored cut, even though the other braid strands were traced first. No assertion of this form is made for a separate closed link component. The conventions agree after the explicit signs are kept: K^(1-N)=epsilon_j K, theta_ADO=epsilon_j theta_ordinary, epsilon_j=(-1)^(j-1). The braid permutation is a b-cycle, so its writhe w satisfies w=b-1 modulo 2. The resulting sign is epsilon_j^(b-1-w)=1. Consequently the original even meridian family satisfies F_N(Q^j)=C_j(q), with F_N(1)=K_N. This is the filtered matrix argument of `root_orbit_pointing.md`, with the precise one-component and framing hypotheses exposed. To distinguish the two coordinates used in the older notes, write this as F_N^M(-q^j)=F_N^Y(Q^j)=C_j(q), Y=M^2. The functions in this identity are REDUCED periods. The full ADO state also carries its original modified-dimension factor, which can have a pole at an ordinary orbit point. Neither its value nor a transverse derivative is bounded by (1). No such value or derivative is used in the Fourier remainder below. ## 4. An explicit positive Fourier remainder Set c_0=K_N and c_j=C_j(q) for 1<=j<N, and use the unitary transform chat_k=N^(-1/2) sum_(j=0)^(N-1) Q^(-kj)c_j. Finite character orthogonality proves exactly E_N:=sum_k |chat_k|^2 =|K_N|^2+R_N, 0<=R_N=sum_(j=1)^(N-1)|C_j(q)|^2 <=sum_(j=1)^(N-1)[j]^(2b-2). (3) In particular this remainder is polynomial uniformly over the entire ordinary-color range, including j=N-1, rather than just at fixed j. There is an explicit sharper constant. Put r=b-1>=1 and assume N>r. The Fourier expansion of sin^(2r)(pi j/N) has frequencies -r,...,r. Only its constant coefficient survives summation over all N roots; that coefficient is binom(2r,r)/4^r. The j=0 summand is zero. Hence 0<=R_N <= N binom(2r,r)/(4^r sin^(2r)(pi/N)) <= binom(2r,r) N^(2r+1)/16^r. (4) For b=1 the closure is the unknot and R_N=N-1 instead. For small N<=r the sum bound (3) remains valid without the simplified formula. Equivalently chat=K_N u+e, where u is the constant unit vector, e is orthogonal to u, and ||e||^2=R_N. This orthogonality is exact; there is no discarded cross term. There is also an unconditional logarithmic statement, which is safer than writing an equality of unsmoothed logarithms before a positive rate has been established. The trivial ordinary color satisfies C_1=1, so R_N>=1 for every N>=2. Set P_(N,b)=(N-1)(N/2)^(2b-2)>=1. Then the exact energy identity and (1a) give 1+|K_N|^2 <= E_N <= P_(N,b)(1+|K_N|^2), (4a) 0 <= log E_N-log(1+|K_N|^2) <= log P_(N,b). In particular, uniformly without any nonvanishing assumption, (pi/N)log E_N =(pi/N)log(1+|K_N|^2)+O_b(log N/N). (4b) With log 0=-infinity this is equivalently 0 <= (pi/N)log E_N-max(0,(2pi/N)log|K_N|) <= (pi/N)log(2P_(N,b)). (4c) For any fixed V>0, (4a)--(4c) prove (2pi/N)log|K_N| -> V if and only if (pi/N)log E_N -> V. (5) The implication from positive energy to the original invariant uses the fact that a polynomial remainder is smaller than any sequence with strictly positive exponential rate. It does not assume eventual nonvanishing of K_N; that nonvanishing follows from the positive energy rate and (3). An unrestricted equality of log E_N and 2 log|K_N| at exponential scale does NOT follow merely from the polynomial remainder: zeros or exponentially small values would invalidate that inference. ## 5. What is verified, and what remains The finite Plancherel checks do not establish a volume limit. The remaining analytical questions are stated below. * [Positive path algebra](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/ordinary_color_positive_trace_independent_audit.md): both Markov identities on noncommuting words, the full projection induction including the first zero-dimension projection, and 42 signed colored closures including j=N-1. * [Original color identification](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_ordinary_color_comparison_audit.md): the uniform one-component filtered trace proof and direct R coproduct calculation, supplemented by 228 exact whole-knot cut comparisons and 22 signed-cable families, with the original Cartan and twist phases. The explicit sine-energy identity in (4) was independently checked in 225 pairs (N,r), with 80-digit arithmetic; its proof is the finite character calculation above. No defect was found in either uniform proof. These checks establish the remainder estimate's stated scope, not the geometric size of the remaining Fourier energy. The polynomial remainder in (3) has an independent algebraic proof. The positive energy E_N still requires its geometric exponential estimate. In particular, the canonical cleared operator B(Y-1) becomes Bhat(S-I) in the dual cyclic coordinate and kills the constant mode u exactly. Retaining the original normal/pointed source is therefore essential when estimating that energy. Plancherel validates the positive target; it does not by itself supply its size.

title: The original source has no automatic positive reflection form
text: # The original source has no automatic positive reflection form 27 October 2026. A universal reflection/Gram argument for the original Kashaev source fails at every level: its identity value is zero while an actual normalized unknot word has nonzero value. A two-channel reflection square has source -2. The standard alternating three-strand weaving transfer also cannot be made a positive Hermitian operator, at any level N>=3, by a positive metric or a scalar phase. These are obstructions to AUTOMATIC positivity of the original word source or transfer. They do not rule out a separately proved positive formula for a particular knot family, a word-dependent source elimination, an explicitly projected positive channel, or the existing positive squared norm of the original invariant. They do not disprove the volume conjecture. ## 1. The original source is not a positive functional Fix q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, N>=2, complete color x=-q^-1=q^(N-1), and retain the original pivot K e_a=x Q^-a e_a, g=K^(1-N). For b>=2 the original reduced one-cut source on actual braid intertwiners is t_b(A)=Tr[(P_0 tensor g^(tensor(b-1)))A]. (1) The all-ones first output row gives the same value on these integer-weight-preserving words. The full source is its original nonzero dimension factor d_N(1)=i^(N+3)/N, with the original zero-framing line. No ordinary quantum dimension is divided out. Since Q has exact order N, Tr(g)=x^(1-N)sum_(a=0)^(N-1)Q^-a=0, t_b(I)=0. (2) Let B_i be the original checked crossing with its own common Cartan factor recorded, and theta its original twist factor. Use the actual zero-framing normalized generator Bhat_i=theta^-1 B_i. The ordinary positive Markov chain W_b=Bhat_(b-1)...Bhat_1 closes to the unknot and has t_b(W_b)=t_b(W_b^-1)=1. (3) This can be checked directly without a knot-polynomial formula. At each last-strand pivotal closure the actual positive crossing has partial trace theta I; its inverse has theta^-1 I. For the positive crossing evaluate on the first highest vector: the closure forces both local indices zero, leaving g_0. For the inverse evaluate on the first lowest vector: only its zero transfer survives, leaving theta^-1. The root scalar-closure identity makes those the whole partial traces. Repeating the closures proves (3), with every original factor retained. **No-go theorem.** There is no involution dagger on a unital complex algebra containing these actual words, and no nonzero scalar multiple of t_b, which makes it a positive linear functional on all A^dagger A. Indeed a positive functional obeys Cauchy--Schwarz. Its value on the identity is zero by (2), so its value on every element would be zero. Equation (3) contradicts this. Equivalently, if the reflection Gram matrix on the channels I,W_b were Hermitian, its upper-left entry would be zero and its off-diagonal entry nonzero. Its determinant is negative. For the usual anti-linear inverse-word reflection, W_b^dagger =W_b^-1. The explicit formal braid combination A=I-W_b gives A^dagger A=2I-W_b-W_b^-1, t_b(A^dagger A)=-2. (4) This is an actual source evaluation of a linear combination of original braid words. It is not an invented negative test functional. The full dimension/phase line multiplies both positive and negative directions by the same fixed nonzero scalar; no phase can turn their indefinite Gram form positive. ## 2. The original cups and caps have the same obstruction The actual nonzero cup and cap obey cap cup=Tr(g)=0. They therefore cannot be Hermitian adjoints in a positive-definite reflection structure: that identity would be the squared norm of the nonzero cup. This is the actual isotropic cup/cap channel already exhibited in [the sewn-source construction](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/sewn_source_and_meridian_charge.md). One marked cap changes its specified channel and gives the normalized unknot value, but it does not convert ALL ordinary cup/cap pairings in a multi-bridge plat into positive adjoint pairings. Thus drawing a braid or plat as two reflected halves is not by itself a proof that its original scalar is a sum of absolute squares. A valid restricted formula must prove how its actual co-source becomes the required adjoint on the particular image subspace, with the marked cap and all other turns retained. ## 3. Even the basic alternating weaving transfer is not positive Let T_N=B_12 B_23^-1 on three original same-color strands. Its two crossing scalars and zero-framing factors cancel, since the word has writhe zero. It is the block repeated in the alternating weaving words (sigma_1 sigma_2^-1)^m. Consider its invariant physical total-index-one subspace with basis |100>,|010>,|001>. Literal crossing coefficients give T_N|_1=[[1-Q,0,1], [-q,0,0], [0,-q^-1,1-Q^-1]]. (5) For example the local index-one crossing block is [[1-Q,-q],[-q,0]] in the ordered pair |10>,|01>. The two coefficients are rho/x=1-Q and x^-1=-q at x=-q^-1. Multiplying the two adjacent blocks gives (5). This is a computation in the original head, without a proposed positive replacement crossing. Its exact characteristic polynomial is (lambda-1) [lambda^2-(1-Q-Q^-1)lambda+1]. (6) At N=3 it is (lambda-1)^3 but the matrix in (5) is not identity. Thus it is nontrivially unipotent and cannot be self-adjoint in any positive-definite Hermitian metric. At every N>=4 the two other roots are exp(+/-i theta_N), where cos(theta_N)=[1-2cos(2pi/N)]/2, pi/3<=theta_N<2pi/3. They are nonreal. Every positive-metric self-adjoint operator has real spectrum. Consequently T_N cannot be a positive Gram operator C^dagger C after any similarity. Multiplying it by a scalar phase cannot help: its eigenvalue 1 forces that phase to be positive real, leaving the nonreal pair unchanged. Nor does a fixed power remove the obstruction. For any fixed m>=1, the positive eigenvalue condition for T_N^m would require m theta_N to be an integer multiple of 2pi. The angle theta_N is strictly increasing to 2pi/3, so this cannot hold for all sufficiently large N. Indeed each admissible multiple can occur at most once. A fixed alternating weave block therefore cannot be converted into a positive transfer at all levels by taking a fixed number of repetitions. This statement concerns the transfer as an operator. A positive scalar identity for a particular closure could still result from source cancellation and a nontrivial finite-sum identity, as the [actual figure-eight proof](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/figure_eight_whole_source_identity.md) demonstrates. Operator positivity is stronger than that scalar conclusion. ## 4. What remains possible for a positive high-weight channel The unit-circle eigenpair in (6) does not exclude a separately constructed positive spectral channel elsewhere in the tensor module. Such a route would require at least: 1. An explicit source-compatible projection or relative source reduction on the actual word, rather than deleting the nonpositive channels from the invariant by definition. 2. A proved positive representation of the retained scalar with its original marked cap, phases and peripheral line. 3. A bound showing that omitted channels cannot cancel the desired leading contribution, plus a nonzero coupling to the calibrated geometric critical class. The existing positive trace for ordinary colors does not automatically give these facts on the Kashaev projective color. Its quantum dimension is precisely zero, while the modified source detects its nonsemisimple data. Nor does Rivin uniqueness establish positivity of this quantum source. No new positive high-weight channel satisfying these conditions has been constructed here. There IS already a valid positive formulation for all knots: the [original cyclic norm](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/regularized_kashaev_period.md#6-a-positive-trace-norm-gives-another-exact-formulation) satisfies H_N=|K_N|^2/N+O(poly(N)), and the [pointed A-Gram theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/pointed_a_gram_period.md) expresses its equivalent pointed norm by positive polynomial coefficients. Those constructions retain the actual source and target. They are not an ordinary reflection-positive word trace, and their geometric exponential estimate and source overlap remain open. The present obstruction does not invalidate them. ## 5. Exact checks and scope [The audit](../experiments/audit_original_reflection_gram_obstruction.py) and [saved results](../experiments/original_reflection_gram_obstruction_results.json) check 17 literal original-source cases, braid indices two through four, including the normalized positive unknot chain, its actual inverse and (4). Seven exact root tests check the literal invariant block (5). Its characteristic polynomial is also checked symbolically. The complex positivity conclusion comes from the all-level proof, not from an inference about finite-field signs. This rules out the automatic Gram/reflection route and its basic alternating-transfer version. It neither rules out a separately proved positive family nor supplies a hyperbolic volume lower bound. A genuine selected geometric-cycle or source-compatible positive-channel theorem is still needed.

title: The peripheral delta module and the normal derivative of the knot period
text: # The peripheral delta module and the normal derivative of the knot period Research note, 26 October 2026. This identifies a boundary component which any positive-volume proof must retain. The ordinary principal-root colors force polynomial growth if a polynomial annihilator acts nontrivially on the complete-color delta vector. When that boundary component is retained, a simple rank condition expresses the actual complete period as the first normal derivative of a homogeneous kernel line. The derivative has a polynomially bounded source. Its size is therefore an inverse-operator and source-coupling problem, in the natural cyclic trace metric. The statements below separate a necessary boundary factor from a further rank condition. The positive volume limit is now proved for the knots of the [net-twist theorem](../papers/conway-reductions/README.md). For every such knot, Section 2 therefore proves the boundary-factor condition for every polynomial all-level annihilator. The special-fiber rank condition in Section 4 remains additional; the scalar volume theorem does not prove it or identify a full quantum module with the geometric regulator. The subsequent [actual Weyl-descent proof](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_weyl_descent.md) constructs P=B*(Y-1) from the primitive minimal normal operator for every knot and proves its unitary reciprocity. Thus those symmetry data in Section 6 are available for the canonical actual operator. Those symmetry statements do not prove special-fiber injectivity or give direct estimates for the inverse below. Section 2's necessity test still concerns every polynomial annihilator. The subsequent [peripheral-fusion proof](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_peripheral_fusion.md) derives the regular normal boundary lattice from the actual fundamental parallel, retaining its pole before changing lattice. Its odd normal state w_N=(M-M^(-1))F_N has K_N=(1/2)partial_(Log M)w_N at M=1. The adjacent-color splitting there has a nonzero square-zero Casimir residue whose pivotal partial trace is identity. These exact quantum extension data do not establish the root-fiber rank or the regulator norm. The subsequent [ramified Weyl-fibre theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/ramified_weyl_fibre.md) retains this derivative as an ordinary coordinate of a descended algebraic fibre over s=((U-1)/(U+1))^2. Its - sector generator is z e_- rather than a vector discarded by setting z=0 first. The source equation and complete functional then hold in that fibre, with their original rank qualifications. An explicit dimension formula gives signatures for which negative-sector injectivity cannot hold; saturated kernels and further lifting data remain available. No regulator norm is inferred from this descent. ## 1. Fixed state, ring, and principal-root bound Use the actual literature state in [the ADO audit](kashaev_ado_pointing.md), with q_N=exp(pi*i/N), Q_N=q_N^2, Y=M^2, F_N(Y) Laurent polynomial, K_N=F_N(1)=<K>_N, F_N(Q_N^r)=C_r(q_N), 1<=r<N. The [regular-period theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/regularized_kashaev_period.md) reconstructs the positive path trace directly from the actual fundamental crossing. For any fixed b-strand knot braid it proves |C_r(q_N)|<=D_N=sin(pi/N)^(1-b)<= (N/2)^(b-1). (1.1) Take a specified actual annihilator with denominators cleared and recorded, in the polynomial quantum torus R=C(q)[Y^(+/-1),T^(+/-1); T Y=q^2Y T], P=sum_(j=0)^d a_j(q,Y)T^j, a_j in C[q^(+/-1),Y^(+/-1)]. (1.2) An initial power of T permits the nonnegative shift convention. The [existence](finite_sum_annihilator.md) and [squared-meridian descent](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/even_meridian_norm_descent.md) theorems supply such an actual operator, but do not yet identify its classical geometric factors. ## 2. A nonzero complete column forces polynomial growth For 0<=i<=d put r_i(q)=a_i(q,q^(-2i)). (2.1) If r_i is not identically zero, it has finite vanishing order nu_i at q=1. For all large N, |r_i(q_N)|>=c_i N^(-nu_i). Evaluate the actual equation at Y=Q_N^(-i). Its i-th term is r_i(q_N)K_N. If N>d, every other term uses a noncomplete orbit color, and hence has modulus at most C_P D_N by (1.1). The fixed Laurent coefficients are bounded on the unit torus. Consequently |K_N|<=C N^(b-1+nu_i). (2.2) Thus a positive exponential volume rate requires a_i(q,q^(-2i))=0 for every i. (2.3) Equivalently every coefficient is divisible in the Laurent ring by q^(2i)Y-1. Polynomial division at its nonzero root proves this equivalence. Hence the required factorization is exactly P=B*(Y-1), B in R with Laurent coefficients. (2.4) This is right multiplication: its i-th coefficient is b_i(q,Y)*(q^(2i)Y-1). A monic operator over C(q,Y) can have poles on those divisors; an ordinary evaluation of that localized operator cannot replace the cleared equation used above. The result is a dichotomy for an arbitrary knot. For the knots covered by the strict-tree and net-twist volume theorems, their positive volume limit rules out (2.2), so every polynomial annihilator satisfies (2.3). For a hyperbolic knot outside the proved class, this remains a necessary condition for its conjectured positive-volume limit. Conversely, the boundary factor alone supplies no exponential lower bound. The [nearby-zero theorem](actual_ado_complete_meridian_zero_accumulation.md) gives another consequence of the same ordinary-color values: zeros of the actual reduced state approach the complete meridian at distance $O(1/N)$. Its final section also records the two-sign version of the boundary factor for operators in the unsquared coordinate $M$. ## 3. The missing component is a fixed boundary module At generic q define Delta=R/R*(Y-1), delta=class of 1. It has C(q)-basis T^j delta, j in Z, and Y T^j delta=q^(-2j)T^j delta. Therefore P delta=0 is exactly (2.3). The module is simple at indeterminate q: polynomial interpolation in Y isolates one term of any nonzero finite combination of these distinct eigenvectors, and powers of T then generate all of them. Every vector is killed by a nonzero polynomial in Y. Localizing the meridian to C(q,Y) therefore kills Delta completely. For a polynomial annihilator ideal I, positive exponential growth would imply I is contained in R*(Y-1). Its cyclic module would have Delta as a quotient. For one specified P satisfying (2.4), this quotient already follows without a volume assumption. The generic norm torsor over C(q,Y) needs a meridian lattice to retain this boundary datum. At the actual root, impose T^N=1 as well. The resulting Delta_N is the N-dimensional clock-and-shift module with Y^N=T^N=1, at every parity and composite level. It is irreducible because the N distinct Y-eigenvalues and their cyclic shift generate all matrix units. On functions of the root orbit the complete delta vector is e_0=(1,0,...,0), e_0(Y)=S_N(Y)/N modulo Y^N-1. Thus P annihilates this vector on the central fiber when (2.4) holds. If c_N=(0,C_1,...,C_(N-1)), the actual state there is F_bar_N=c_N+K_N e_0. (3.1) Every vector in this affine line satisfies the same special operator equation and has the same ordinary-color pointing. The complete coefficient is fixed by extension away from the central fiber. This affine ambiguity is not permission to change the actual state. At q=1, (2.4) also gives the vertical factor Y-1 in the classical polynomial symbol. Removing vertical factors to state an A-curve equation discards this specific boundary-module datum. The marked integral/meridian extension must therefore accompany that curve. ## 4. The actual full period is a normal derivative Assume (2.4) for the specified operator. Work near U=Y^N=1, with t=U-1 and the fixed root germs Y_r(t)=Q_N^r*(1+t)^(1/N), 0<=r<N. Represent B by the cyclic matrix B_N(t): its row r, column r+j modulo N receives b_j(q_N,Y_r(t)). Write B_N(t)=B_0+t B_1+O(t^2), (B_1)_(r,r+j)=(1/N)(Y*d/dY)b_j(q_N,Q_N^r). (4.1) Retain the full vector of the actual state and put v_N(t)_r=(Y_r(t)-1)F_N(Y_r(t)), v_N(t)=v_0+t v_1+O(t^2). Since P F_N=0, B_N(t)v_N(t)=0. At the special fiber, (v_0)_0=0, (v_0)_r=(Q_N^r-1)C_r(q_N), 1<=r<N, B_0 v_0=0, B_0 v_1=-B_1 v_0, (v_1)_0=K_N/N. (4.2) The last identity keeps the zero of Y-1 until differentiation: Y_0'(0)=1/N. In particular the complete full ADO value is exactly N_N(1)=eta_N (v_1)_0, eta_N=i^(N+3). (4.3) Indeed the full state, before specialization, is N_N(M)=eta_N M^(N-1)*(Y-1)F_N(Y)/(U-1). Its poles, its sign character, and its phase have all been retained. The normal derivative realizes their cancelled whole germ. Suppose now that rank B_0=N-1. (4.4) The known nonzero vector v_0 spans its kernel; the reference component is Q_N-1 because C_1=1. The solutions of the inhomogeneous normal equation in (4.2) form a genuine affine torsor under C*v_0. Since (v_0)_0=0, its complete-coordinate functional is constant. Thus (4.2) determines K_N exactly, without choosing the derivative of a central normalization unit. More explicitly replacing v_N(t) by c(1+t)v_N(t), c(1)=1, adds c'(1)v_0 to v_1. The complete value in (4.3) does not change. This is the anchored normal-period comparison, with its specified root germs. The rank condition is additional to the existence of the actual operator; it is not assumed for every knot. The regular complete scalar of the preceding note is R_N(1)=(v_1)_0-p_N(1), |p_N(1)|<=D_N. (4.5) So the normal derivative and that regularized field-trace period give the same positive-volume target. ## 5. The first obstruction selects a point of the delta torsor Let D(t)=diag(Y_r(t)-1), so P_N(t)=B_N(t)D(t). At zero, Im D(0) is the hyperplane of vectors with zero complete coordinate. Its kernel is C*e_0. Since ker B_0=C*v_0 is inside this hyperplane, rank P_0=N-2, ker P_0=span(e_0,c_N). (5.1) The first lifting obstruction is the linear map kappa:ker P_0 -> coker P_0, x -> [P_1 x]. (5.2) This is the usual first Bockstein: a lift x+t x_1 solves the equation through first order exactly when P_0 x_1+P_1 x=0. In particular P_1 e_0=(1/N)B_0 e_0. This is not in Im P_0. Otherwise e_0 would differ from a vector in Im D(0) by a member of ker B_0, also in Im D(0), a contradiction. The actual vector c_N+K_N e_0 lifts. Hence kappa has rank one on the two-dimensional kernel, and its kernel selects that exact line. Choose any left null vector ell of P_0 with ell P_1 e_0 nonzero. The period is the exact ratio K_N=-ell P_1 c_N/(ell P_1 e_0). (5.3) Changing ell subject to this condition gives the same answer, because the actual lift exists. This derivative pairing records the boundary extension that the ordinary special kernel omits. Under (4.4) the rank loss in P is exactly one simple Smith factor; no unverified higher-order lift is being used. More singular cases need the higher jets retained in the [bounded-jet construction](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/bounded_meridian_jets.md). ## 6. A bounded source and the exact inverse-matrix period Use the Hermitian norm on the orbit coming from the cyclic trace; the unnormalized Euclidean version differs only by the common factor N^(1/2). The fixed Laurent coefficients give ||B_1||<=C_B/N, ||v_0||<=2D_N*sqrt(N). (6.1) For the first inequality write B_1 as a finite sum of diagonal coefficient matrices times unitary cyclic shifts, and bound each Y-derivative on the unit torus. Thus the normal equation has a polynomially bounded, explicitly specified source. Let B_0^+ be the Moore--Penrose inverse. Since e_0 is perpendicular to ker B_0, every solution of (4.2) has the same complete coordinate, and exactly K_N=-N*e_0^* B_0^+ B_1 v_0. (6.2) If s_N is the smallest nonzero singular value of B_0, then |K_N|<=2 C_B D_N sqrt(N)/s_N. (6.3) Consequently positive volume growth would force an exponentially large inverse norm in this specified boundary problem. The source itself cannot supply that positive exponent. Small singular values alone are insufficient: (6.2) also retains the source and the complete-coordinate pairing. In a singular-vector decomposition it is the sum of their two overlaps divided by the corresponding singular values. No largest-eigenvalue prescription is being used. The geometric action already has imaginary value Vol at completeness, by the [actual action proof](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/quantum_longitude_and_regulator_action.md). For a knot covered by the net-twist theorem, whenever the stated rank condition holds, (6.2) is an exact expression for its invariant and therefore has the scalar volume growth proved there. Deriving this growth directly from the inverse and identifying the geometric regulator at the module level remain additional tasks. Neither (6.3) nor a geometric critical point by itself controls the two overlaps. Extra left operator factors can create small singular values with zero relevant overlap. ### A Weyl symmetry isolates the relevant inverse There is a stronger reduction when the *actual operator* has a checked reciprocity. Write R h(Y)=h(Y^(-1)), Q=q^2, and suppose J=-Y R, J'=c(q,Y)T^d R, B J=J' B, c(q,Y)c(q,Q^(-d)Y^(-1))=1, |c(q,Y)|=1 on the unit torus. (6.4) Both give unitary involutions on the root orbit; B_0 intertwines them. Their -1 eigenspaces are orthogonal to the +1 eigenspaces, and e_0 has J-eigenvalue -1. The factor Y-1 is the squared-meridian form of the Weyl denominator, up to the retained monomial M. If J v_0=v_0, differentiating the operator identity at U=1 proves J' B_1 v_0=-B_1 v_0. Explicitly inversion sends t to -t+O(t^2), and the domain involution has derivative J/N. Applying the differentiated identity to v_0 kills the terms containing B_0 v_0 and leaves exactly this source parity. Thus only the -1 symmetry sector enters the complete normal period. Under (4.4) this source parity is automatic whenever K_N is nonzero. Indeed the one-dimensional kernel makes J v_0=epsilon*v_0. If epsilon=-1, the same differentiation gives source parity +1. The -1 part of v_1 would then be a multiple of v_0 and have zero complete coordinate, forcing K_N=0. More generally (4.4) can be weakened in this symmetry setting: it suffices that J v_0=v_0 and B_0 is injective on the -1 domain. The actual derivative places the source in its image. Extra +1 kernel vectors do not affect the value. Writing the restricted Moore--Penrose inverse as B_-^+, the exact period is K_N=-N e_0^* B_-^+ B_1 v_0. (6.5) It is this inverse and its specified source that need a regulator norm theorem. Small singular values in the other symmetry sector make no contribution. Reciprocity is additional quantum data; it is not assumed merely from the classical A-curve's inversion symmetry. The subsequent [actual-state proof](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_weyl_descent.md) now derives this reciprocity for the primitive minimal normal operator of every knot, and also proves J v_0=v_0 directly. An arbitrary nonprimitive or left-multiplied operator still needs its own checked intertwiner and lattice. There is an explicit Hilbert-90 descent of the reflected kernel frame. If its generic rational kernel is a C(U)-line, reciprocity gives J v=gamma(U)v, gamma(U)gamma(U^(-1))=1. When J v_0=v_0, gamma is a unit at U=1 with gamma(1)=1. Set g(U)=(1+gamma(U))/2. Direct division gives g(U)/g(U^(-1))=gamma(U). Thus g*v is J-invariant and g(1)=1. This is an explicit frame change of the same pointed line, not a replacement knot state. Its derivative adds g'(1)v_0 and leaves the complete normal period unchanged. Zeros or poles of this frame elsewhere remain part of the lattice data. This is quadratic Hilbert 90 on the central involution, after the normal pointing has already fixed the value at the branch point. The ambient cyclic orbit also retains a precise signed dihedral relation. Direct multiplication gives J T J=Q*T^(-1). With the actual ADO character kappa=-q^(-1), put T_tilde=kappa*T. Then J T_tilde J=T_tilde^(-1), T_tilde^N=kappa^N=(-1)^(N-1). (6.6) Thus the uniform half-root lambda=-q, lambda^2=Q, is compatible with the Weyl action and with the full even-level sign. This is an action on the ambient orbit module. It does not assert that the scalar operator's rational solution line is stable under T; only its checked reflection intertwiner and central frame descent are used. Neither Hilbert-90 descent nor this finite symmetry supplies the missing regulator norm. ## 7. A fixed initial form bounds the rational root period rank There is a simple separate certificate for generic rational rank. For any Laurent polynomial operator L, let r be the least Y-exponent in its coefficients and define I_0(q,z)=sum_j [Y^r]a_j(q,Y)*z^j. (7.1) At q_N, suppose this initial form is nonzero. On E=C(Y) over C(U), U=Y^N, represent Y^(-r)L in the monomial basis 1,Y,...,Y^(N-1). Its matrix is integral over C[U]. Modulo U it is lower triangular: positive powers of Y either increase the basis exponent or wrap with a positive power of U. Its diagonal entries are I_0(q_N,Q_N^k). The principal submatrix on their nonzero indices has nonzero determinant. Therefore dim_(C(U)) ker L <=#{0<=k<N : I_0(q_N,Q_N^k)=0}. (7.2) This counts distinct lattice roots, not their multiplicities. If I_0=g(q)*z^a*(z-q^(2s))^m, with g(q_N) nonzero and m>=1, the bound is one at every such level. Any known nonzero rational period then proves generic rank one. The same applies at infinity. This is a condition on the actual quantum initial form, not on the commutative A-polynomial alone. Terms vanishing at q=1 can change the extremal Y-coefficient. The bound certifies the generic line used in Hilbert 90. It does not replace (4.4), which concerns its special fiber and the normal derivative. A rational kernel line may acquire extra special solutions; that possibility is exactly what the lattice retains. The subsequent [torsion initial-rank theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/torsion_initial_rank.md) extends the pure-binomial test: rational-coefficient initial forms have only finitely many isolated torsion-grid exceptions outside their contained binomial torsion curves. Their eventual root count is given by finite periodic congruences. A single occupied curve therefore gives generic rank one even in the presence of non-toric initial factors. The proof keeps the q half-root and provides an explicit exceptional-level bound. It does not establish the special negative-sector injectivity or regulator norm. ## 8. The rank hypothesis cannot be suppressed For a manufactured root family let F_N(Y)=1+a_N S_N(Y), B=(T-1)(T-Q), P=B*(Y-1). Then P F_N=0 because (Y-1)F_N=Y-1+a_N(U-1), and B kills 1,Y. All ordinary orbit values are one, while K_N=1+N*a_N is arbitrary. Here B_0 has a two-dimensional kernel. Its complete-coordinate functional does not vanish on that kernel, so the first normal equation leaves this freedom. The quantum initial form also has two distinct lattice roots, consistent with (7.2). These are not knot states. In particular choosing a_N to change the complete value violates the coherent all-level color data, whose recovery is proved in [the all-level theorem](all_level_a_period.md). The example only explains the rank requirement for the simpler normal equation (6.2), not a new ambiguity in the actual invariant. ## 9. Independent operator and actual-state calibration The audit derives a telescoping operator for the finite block H_N(Y)=sum_(k=0)^(N-1) t_k(Y), t_k=product_(r=1)^k(Y+Y^(-1)-Q^r-Q^(-r)). The subsequent [whole-source four-plat proof](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/figure_eight_whole_source_identity.md) identifies H_N with the actual figure-eight ADO state at every level, with all peripheral factors retained. The derivation here does not take that equality as a premise. Put Z=Q^k and C(Y,Z)=(Y-1)^2 Z/((Y-Z)(1-YZ)), D(Y)=Y(Y+1)(Q-Y^2)(QY^2-1), g=Q^2Y^2-QY^4+QY^3+QY-Q+Y^2, c_-=Y^2(Q-Y)(QY^2-1), c_0=-(Y-1)^2(Y+1)g, c_+=Y^2(QY-1)(Q-Y^2). The finite products give the two Y-shift ratios and the k-ratio directly. Substitution proves the exact rational certificate sum_(j=-1)^1 c_j(Y)*t_k(Q^jY)/t_k(Y) =D(Y)*(C(Y,QZ)*t_(k+1)/t_k-C(Y,Z)). (9.1) At a root Q^N=1, C(Y,1)=-1 and t_N=Y^N+Y^(-N)-2. Telescoping therefore gives (c_-T^(-1)+c_0+c_+T)H_N =D(Y)*(3-U-U^(-1)). (9.2) The central factor is retained. Applying D(Y)T-D(QY) kills the source. Left multiplication by T removes the negative shift. The common coefficient factor removed in the audit is exactly Q^3Y(Q^3Y^2-1)^2, recorded before any specialization. The resulting polynomial P has every boundary column factor, initial form z(Q-z), and classical symbol (Y-1)^2(Y+1)^2*(z-1)*Y^2*A_geo(Y,z), A_geo=z^2-(Y^2-Y-2-Y^(-1)+Y^(-2))*z+1. (9.3) This checks the familiar geometric peripheral polynomial and the additional boundary factors in fixed conventions. It does not prove an AJ theorem for arbitrary knot operators or identify root central curves with A_geo. For this calibrated operator the exact reciprocity in (6.4) is c(Q,Y)=-Q^12 Y^8 and d=3. Substituting its coefficients verifies -Q^j Y b_j(Y)=c(Q,Y)b_(3-j)(Q^(-3)/Y). The two involution and unit-norm identities follow by multiplication. The -1 domain has dimension ceil(N/2), including every parity. The audit verifies the source parity and recovers the same period using only that folded inverse. This removes an irrelevant symmetry sector before any asymptotic estimate; it is not such an estimate. [The audit](../experiments/audit_peripheral_normal_period.py) verifies the certificate symbolically. At levels 2,3,4,5,6,7,8,10 it proves coefficientwise equality of H_N with independently computed actual figure-eight cut Laurent polynomials over the stated finite fields, and verifies their annihilation. At eleven levels through 18 it checks both matrix ranks, the derivative product rule, and exact recovery of the complete block period by (4.2), (5.2), and the Weyl-folded inverse (6.5). It also checks 50 initial-root dimension examples and six explicit rank- ambiguity examples. All checks passed. The larger block tests do not extend the actual-state comparison beyond its stated levels. That all-level comparison is now supplied by the independent four-plat proof, which also proves the selected volume limit and leading coefficient for the actual figure-eight invariant. Results are in [the output](../experiments/peripheral_normal_period_results.json). python3 experiments/audit_peripheral_normal_period.py The boundary delta module, first lifting obstruction, Moore--Penrose inverse and initial-form argument use standard module and linear algebra. Their proofs above specify their role in the actual marked period; no novelty claim or imported analytic theorem is made. The quantum-torus Weyl involution already has explicit coverage in [Le's lectures, Section 5.9](https://letu.math.gatech.edu/Papers/Lectures_Luminy_2014_new.pdf). Only its scope is used for coverage; no AJ, state-comparison or analytic conclusion from that source is a premise. The weighted involutions and source parity above were obtained by direct operator identities, with all monomial phases retained. The [geometric triangulation bridge](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/triangulation_regulator_bridge.md) supplies the marked Bloch action for the comparison with this normal period. The scalar volume equality is established for the stated strict and net-twist knot classes. The survival and identification of the actual geometric factor, the additional rank conditions in this note, and the volume conjecture outside the established classes remain open.

title: A polynomial unfolding of the actual pointed cyclic source
text: # A polynomial unfolding of the actual pointed cyclic source Research theorem, 27 October 2026. There is an explicit whole algebraic unfolding of the original cyclic boundary. Allow its cyclic repair to acquire a characteristic polynomial, while keeping the actual highest vector, normalized output row and aligned rank-one multiplicative relation. The resulting sourced moduli chart is a principal open subset of affine (N-1)-space over the Q-line. Every matrix and the full co-source have polynomial formulas. A unipotent conjugation, requiring no quantum-gap division, trivializes the clock and retains the residual spectral polynomial in the transformed co-source. This is a source-specific chart of the existing framed multiplicative-commutator problem. It is not a new definition of the knot invariant, nor a proof that its residual polynomial is the knot's geometric A-polynomial. That requires the actual crossing-word and peripheral transport. ## 1. Keep the source and relax just the fixed cyclic polynomial Let R be any commutative coefficient ring and Q a unit. Let E be locally free of rank N, N at least two. Consider invertible X,Y, a vector v, and rows w,ell satisfying Q inverse X Y X inverse Y inverse=I+v w, (1) Xv=v, ell v=1, ell Y=ell. (2) Require the actual source-orbit chart: v,Yv,...,Y^(N-1)v is a basis. These hypotheses retain the normalized source v ell; in particular its image is aligned with the moment vector v. They relax the additional actual finite-head equation Y^N=I. The row w in (1) is the moment covector; ell is the original co-source and must not be replaced by w. In this canonical basis write Y e_j=e_(j+1), 0<=j<N-1, Y e_(N-1)=sum_(i=0)^(N-1) t_i e_i. (3) Then t_0 is a unit, ell=(1,...,1), and sum_i t_i=1. (4) Conversely choose arbitrary t_1,...,t_(N-1), set t_0=1-sum_(i>0)t_i and invert t_0. Define x_0=1 and x_m=(1-Q^m)t_(N-m) +sum_(l=1)^(m-1)t_(N-m+l)x_l, 1<=m<N. (5) The UNIQUE possible clock is X_(i,j)=Q^i x_(j-i) if i<=j, and zero if i>j. (6) It is invertible: det X=Q^(N(N-1)/2). The unique row w is the zeroth row of Q inverse X Y X inverse Y inverse minus I. All other rows of that matrix vanish. Consequently (3)-(6) are a complete construction and classification over R, including bases with nilpotents. They do not require Q^N-1 or any 1-Q^j to be invertible. Here is the entry proof. Equations (2) and cyclicity first fix the zeroth column of X and the row ell. Equation (1) is equivalent to saying that XY-QYX has image in Rv. In its nonzero-index rows, the first N-1 columns force (6) inductively: until the final column the additional companion term contains X_(N-1,j)=0. For i=N-m>0 the final-column equation, divided only by the unit Q^i, is x_m=sum_(l=0)^(m-1)t_(N-m+l)x_l-Q^m t_(N-m), which is exactly (5). Conversely that recurrence kills every nonzero-index row. Invertibility of X,Y then gives (1) and w. The final-column output equation ell Y=ell is precisely (4). Thus the sourced quotient in this cyclic chart is EXACTLY Spec R[t_1,...,t_(N-1), (1-sum_(i>0)t_i) inverse]. (7) If a free basis of E is included in the data, the representation chart is GL_N times (7). There are no residual stabilizers: an automorphism fixing Y and v fixes its full cyclic basis. In particular the sourced chart is smooth and flat over the whole Q-unit base, of relative dimension N-1. This follows from the displayed coordinate ring, not from a nonroot generic smoothness theorem. The surrounding [framed moment scheme](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_resonant_framed_moment_smoothness.md) also has a direct root Jacobian proof and a cyclic-vector quotient of relative dimension 2N. The present formulas describe its full sourced subchart globally, rather than merely near that root. ## 2. The pointed spectral factor and a polynomial Hilbert-90 gauge The companion characteristic polynomial and its reversed form are chi(z)=z^N-sum_i t_i z^i, h(z)=z^N chi(1/z) =1-sum_(m=1)^N t_(N-m)z^m. (8) Because chi(1)=0, there are monic and constant-one polynomials chi_red and h_red, respectively, with chi(z)=(z-1)chi_red(z), h(z)=(1-z)h_red(z), h_red(z)=z^(N-1)chi_red(1/z). (9) Let L be the actual finite lowering shift, L e_j=e_(j-1) for j>0 and L e_0=0. Thus L^N=0. Put B=diag(1,Q,...,Q^(N-1)), G=h(L). (10) G is upper unipotent, with polynomial inverse: its nonconstant part is nilpotent. Equations (5)-(6) imply the exact WHOLE identity X=G B G inverse. (11) To verify this without matrix inversion, let x(z)=sum_(m=0)^(N-1)x_m z^m. Recurrence (5) is equivalent to h(z)x(z)=h(Qz) modulo z^N. Thus X=B h(QL)h(L) inverse. Since B L B inverse=Q inverse L, B h(QL)=h(L)B, which proves (11). This is an explicit finite polynomial coboundary, rather than a comparison obtained after truncating a quantum jet or choosing a singular eigenbasis. In particular no factors 1-Q^j or 1-Q^N have been canceled. The source is transported exactly as well: G inverse v=v, ell G=e_0^t h_red(L). (12) Indeed Gv=v and ell(I-L)=e_0^t, while (9) holds at L. Therefore the coefficients of the residual spectral factor remain in the actual transformed co-source. For every whole operator C, ell C v=[e_0^t h_red(L)] [G inverse C G] v. (13) The new transport is G inverse Y G, and every crossing, cap and inserted current has to be conjugated with it. Trivializing X alone does not erase the co-source polynomial. If the original period carries an external peripheral/dimension line, retain that SAME line on both sides of (13), including its norm-zero ratios. ## 3. The actual finite head is a regular section, not a singular limit The actual data are recovered by EQUALITY at t_0=1, t_i=0 for i>0, chi(z)=z^N-1, h(z)=1-z^N, h_red(z)=1+z+...+z^(N-1). (14) Then G=I, X=B, Y=P is the original cyclic repair, and w=(Q^-N-1)e_0^t, ell=e_0^t sum_(j=0)^(N-1)L^j=(1,...,1). (15) This is exactly the original orbit co-source of [the moment/source theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_rank_one_multiplicative_moment_and_orbit_source.md). The finite head itself still uses its two explicit endpoint deletions; unfolding P has not changed those actual matrices. Conversely Y^N=I FORCES (14): applying it to v and using its cyclic basis gives t_0=1 and t_i=0 for i>0. This works over every commutative base, without a distinct-eigenvalue or characteristic zero hypothesis. The fixed cyclic source is cut out by the N-1 ordinary coordinate equations t_i=0 in the smooth chart (7). It is a flat section over Q. The earlier aligned rigidity theorem is precisely this section, with the defect projector retained. The determinant of (1) supplies another retained character: 1+w v=Q^-N. (16) At a primitive N-th root the matrix v w therefore has square zero, even when w is nonzero elsewhere on the unfolded fiber. The actual section has w=0 there, and its divided normal still recovers e_0 e_0^t. Square-zero boundary monodromy does not imply nilpotence of the full braid image; the previously proved semisimple braid sector is unaffected. ## 4. Finitely many mixed source moments recover the polynomial This chart has a concrete comparison test. The uninserted source moments ell Y^j v are all one, so they cannot distinguish ANY of the residual spectral polynomials. Keep the clock insertion and define instead m_j=ell X Y^j v, 0<=j<N, m_0=1. The canonical columns give m_j=sum_(l=0)^j Q^(j-l)x_l, x_j=m_j-Qm_(j-1), 1<=j<N. (17) If the usual finite-head units 1-Q^m, 1<=m<N, are inverted, equation (5) then gives the UNIQUE recursive reconstruction t_(N-m)=[x_m-sum_(l=1)^(m-1)t_(N-m+l)x_l]/(1-Q^m). (18) Finally t_0=1-sum_(i>0)t_i. The mixed moment map is therefore a polynomial coordinate change over this head localization, with polynomial inverse there; it is not just a pointwise injectivity assertion. The determinant of its Jacobian, in the ordered variables t_(N-1),...,t_1, is exactly product_(m=1)^(N-1)(1-Q^m), (19) because (5) is triangular in this order and (17) is unit triangular. At a primitive N-th root (19) is N. These formulas construct a finite algebraic test for a proposed source-transport comparison and retain its whole normal derivatives. They do not yield a uniform bound on the inverse matrix's condition number; its other entries depend on the retained polynomial. For the actual fixed finite repair P one simply has m_j=Q^j and recovers chi=z^N-1. A different polynomial cannot be assigned to that same transport by relabeling its spectral factor. An actual quantum meridian transport would have to supply its own mixed moments and satisfy the sourced equations before this test could be applied to it. ## 5. What this gives to the A-torsor program There is now a fully explicit algebraic sourced family, its spectral polynomial with a FORCED pointed factor z-1, and a whole comparison carrying the remaining polynomial into the co-source. This supplies functions and a flat scheme before quantum jets. It also makes precise why an unpointed spectral equation and a bare diagonal clock omit selected-period data. Nothing here identifies chi_red with A_K. The coefficients t_i are arbitrary source-transport coordinates until an ACTUAL crossing word or quantum meridian transport produces them. No such new transport is substituted for the original P. The identity (13) compares a given full operator exactly; it does not determine its scalar period or give a growing-N norm bound. An upper-unipotent gauge can have large condition number, so its determinant one is not a subexponential estimate. In particular [the actual Fourier cancellation theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_fourier_source_cancellation.md) continues to apply. A nonzero formal block with the regulator action can lie in the zero-source current sector. To prove the volume conjecture the actual word class, source polynomial and independent normal/norm divisors must be carried into the marked regulator period. The present theorem is an exact algebraic source unfolding and polynomial comparison; it does not prove that final selected norm. The underlying multiplicative-commutator terminology is covered by [Chalykh--Fairon's one-loop quiver presentation](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1704.05814). Only its defining equation is used; the classification and all gauge/source formulas above follow from the entry proof. [The exact audit](../experiments/audit_companion_source_shell.py) and [saved results](../experiments/companion_source_shell_results.json) check the universal formulas at six symbolic levels and twelve full generic/primitive-root moment fibers. The [independent proof audit](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/companion_source_shell_independent_audit.md) checks the chart, periodic section, polynomial gauge and retained co-source separately. The [actual meridian compatibility audit](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_meridian_companion_source_compatibility.md) now proves a universal mismatch if one tries to use the invariant's meridian orbit state directly as this normalized highest source. Its canonical highest residual has pairing K_N. This chart remains a comparison tool; a division by that unknown value cannot serve as the requested geometric-period proof.

title: Coverage check for the retained-circle Conway theorem
text: # Coverage check for the retained-circle Conway theorem Checked 29 October 2026. This is a comparison of definitions and stated coverage, not an audit of external proofs and not an import of their proof techniques. The current own results are the [actual local source cells](../papers/strict-conway-geometry/README.md) and [whole retained cylindrical Conway theorem](../papers/strict-conway-geometry/README.md). The exact grammar is A=h^3, E ::= A | R E | E E, followed by the specified cap-sum boundary reduction. It is not identified here with all arborescent or all fully augmented links. ## 1. Augmented knotted trivalent graphs Van der Veen's [2009 paper, Definition 2 and Theorem 2](https://arxiv.org/html/0805.0094v2) starts from a KTG move sequence. Its main theorem requires sufficiently many augmentation rings at each unzip, with the threshold depending on the sequence. The stated quantum formula uses odd N; its even-N values vanish. The geometric part is a regular-octahedral outside, with additional Seifert pieces for multiple-ring unzips, and gives volume (2t+2)v8 for t triangle moves. This is substantial prior coverage of augmented examples. Applying that theorem to a current diagram would require an explicit KTG move sequence, the required augmentation multiplicities, and an exact comparison of its invariant normalization with the original marked source used here. None is implied merely by retaining crossing circles. In particular an odd-level colored-Jones statement cannot silently replace the current positive all-level source identity. ## 2. Fundamental shadow links and octahedral fully augmented links Ibarra, McQuire and Purcell's [2026 paper, Definition 2.8 and Theorems 2.12 and 4.15](https://nyjm.albany.edu/j/2026/32-1v.pdf) restricts the relevant class to octahedral fully augmented links. It identifies their complements with fundamental-shadow-link complements and states a Turaev–Viro volume theorem without half twists, along odd levels. The displayed volume is 2(c-1)v8 for c crossing circles. The paper explicitly distinguishes this invariant and root from the colored-Jones/Kashaev setting. Our cell construction uses general ideal prisms and pyramids and does not assume a regular-octahedral decomposition. The words “fully augmented” therefore do not establish coverage by that theorem. Conversely, this observation alone is not a proof that our entire class is new or strictly larger: an exact inclusion or noninclusion requires a diagram or geometric certificate. No such general class equivalence is asserted in this coverage check. ## 3. Whitehead chains Van der Veen's [Whitehead-chain paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0611181) states a volume-conjecture result for a particular infinite link family containing the Whitehead link and Borromean rings. It does not state a theorem for arbitrary branching and turn depth in the current expression grammar. Overlapping examples should retain their earlier attribution; no claim of disjoint classes is made here. ## 4. The geometric program also has direct antecedents The primary abstract of Jun Murakami's [13 October 2026 IPAM talk](https://mathinstitutes.org/videos/25102) describes a route from doubled right-angled fully augmented polyhedra to deformed filled complements and spatial-graph invariants. This is an explicitly related program. The abstract presents an approach; it does not state the current all-level theorem for this exact source grammar. Its proofs have not been audited here. Thus the broad idea of relating augmented-link quantum expressions to geometric polyhedra should not be advertised as new. The concrete claims to assess in this repository are narrower and checkable: the original full Newton coefficient, its positive all-level limit, the exact prism face metric as an action derivative, its actual ordered stack map, and the complete geometric realization of the specified retained cylindrical factors. ## 5. What this check does and does not establish The consulted primary statements do not by themselves subsume the present exact grammar, normalization and all-level conclusion. This is a limited coverage finding, not an exhaustive priority claim. It supplies no reason to trust or reject any external proof. The own local and global arguments must stand on their explicit source, topological, geometric and completeness calculations. A future comparison should record, for each proposed inclusion, the actual diagram transformation and the complete invariant dictionary: color dimension versus highest weight, root convention, component normalization, marking and framing, and level subsequence. Those data are mathematical hypotheses, not optional bibliographical details. Until they are supplied, the safe statement is the explicit retained-circle theorem, not a claim to settle arbitrary augmented links, arbitrary hyperbolic knots, or all formulations of the volume conjecture. ## 6. Coverage check for the signed long-filling extension The stated coverage of Ce Shen's [September 2026 preprint, version 3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11839v3) is long integral fillings of marked fundamental-shadow-link exteriors for SO(3) Turaev--Viro invariants along odd levels, with a corresponding Witten--Reshetikhin--Turaev asymptotic. This is directly related prior coverage. Its statement alone does not give the full-level original Kashaev invariant for the present signed Conway knot diagrams. No proof from that preprint is used here, and its correctness was not audited in this coverage check. The Ibarra--McQuire--Purcell paper cited above likewise explicitly distinguishes its Turaev--Viro conclusion and its octahedral class. The current signed-coupon construction retains the general prism and pyramid geometry, the selected original period, actual primitive odd-link meridians, and both level parities. An identification of an overlapping subfamily still needs the explicit diagram and invariant dictionary. No exhaustive novelty claim or equality of the present grammar with all arborescent links follows from this limited check. ## 7. Ordered compositions with long net twists Checked 31 October 2026. The [net-twist theorem](../papers/conway-reductions/README.md) uses actual tangle isotopies to reduce an arbitrary fixed ordered cylindrical product closure to a strict template or an elementary two-strand braid closure. Its bound concerns the final disjoint sums of twist integers. The analytic input is the earlier strict-tree theorem in this repository. The comparison below concerns the main statements of primary papers; their proofs are not used or assessed here. | Primary statement | Coverage relevant to this comparison | | --- | --- | | [Jun Murakami, double-twist knots, Theorem 1](https://arxiv.org/html/2501.00225v3#Thmthm1) | The stated volume-conjecture theorem covers hyperbolic double-twist knots without a long-twist condition. This is direct prior coverage of an arborescent subfamily; the present theorem makes no priority claim for those knots. | | [Chen–Zhu, twist-knot asymptotics, Theorem 1.2 and Corollary 1.4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2307.13670v1#page=3) | The ordinary-root result concerns twist knots with parameter at least six. It does not state an arbitrary ordered-tree theorem. | | [Van der Veen, Whitehead chains, Main Theorem](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0611181v2#page=2) | The one-belt statement runs through all levels. With two or more belts the even-level invariant vanishes and the expansion uses odd levels. These are specified link constructions; passing to knots by filling every auxiliary circle requires an additional argument. | | [Van der Veen, augmented knotted trivalent graphs, Theorem 2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0805.0094v2#page=5) | For a fixed graph-move sequence, sufficiently many augmentation rings give the stated odd-level theorem. The rings remain present, and the displayed even-level invariant is zero. This does not by itself establish the present all-level filled-knot conclusion. | Two more recent statements concern different objects. [Ge's Theorem 1.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.27635v1#page=1) asserts existence of finite geometric ideal triangulations for complete finite-volume cusped hyperbolic manifolds. It is not a theorem about a quantum invariant. [Liu–Ming–Sun–Wu–Yang's Theorem 1.6](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.16560v1#S1.Thmtheorem6) states a volume asymptotic for their modular-double Turaev–Viro state integral on a geometric ideal triangulation. Identifying that integral with the finite-dimensional reduced Kashaev invariant would be a separate theorem; the triangulation assertion does not supply such an identification.
