Equations (19)–(21) retain every original target. ### Odd levels Let \(N=2m+1\), \(d=2m\), and put \[ j_N=\lfloor m\lambdafloor,\qquad e_N=m\lambda-j_N\in[0,1). \qquad	ext{(22)} \] Since \(\lambda<1\), \(j_N\le m-1\), so this remains a genuine left coefficient. There is no outer unit to choose. Each spectator row has degree \(m\), with required column totals \[ b_{f,N}=d-j_N\mathbf1_{f=x} -(d-j_N)\mathbf1_{f=z}. \qquad	ext{(23)} \] Scale the original table by \(d=2m\). Equation (5) shows that its column correction is just \[ \delta_f=e_N\mathbf1_{f=x} -e_N\mathbf1_{f=z}. \qquad	ext{(24)} \] It can be transported along one path from \(z\) to \(x\) in the spectator graph, using only original row supports. Rounding gives \[ k_{tf,N}=d\alpha_{tf}+O_D(1),\qquad \sum_f k_{tf,N}=m,\qquad \sum_t k_{tf,N}=b_{f,N}. \qquad	ext{(25)} \] Both spectator middle degrees are at most \(m\), as required for the odd central piece. The cap's overloaded degree is at least \(m+1\). Thus (25) is an actual array in the same original sector. In either case \(k_{tf,N}/N	o\alpha_{tf}\). Positivity and the factorizations (15)–(16) show that the contribution of the constructed array is at least \[  egin{cases} N\,4^{R-1}\displaystyle\prod_t [ oldsymbol L^{k_{t,N}}]R_{m-1,t}, &N=2m,\[2mm] N^{\,2R-1}\displaystyle\prod_t [ oldsymbol L^{k_{t,N}}]D_{m,t}, &N=2m+1. \end{cases} \qquad	ext{(26)} \] The factor \(N\) comes from (13). Applying (17) to the fixed finite set of rows proves (8) on each parity, hence on the full sequence. ## 6. The unchanged 54-region diagram Use the sphere, matching and original mark recorded in [the singleton-sector certificate](../papers/planar-certificates/README.md), §§2–5. It has \(56\) white vertices, \(162\) edges, \(108\) triangles and \(54\) matched crossing regions. Its protected faces are \(29,50\), and the selected ordered quartet is \[ e_*=32,\qquad (x,b,z,y)=(0,50,16,29),\qquad \lambda= rac{548219162717}{10^{12}}. \qquad	ext{(27)} \] The [exact certificate](../experiments/actual_singleton_sector_obstruction_certificate.json) records all \(106\) spectator rows with their original face labels. They satisfy (5) exactly, their ordinary support graph is connected, and their minimum supported corner load is \[  rac{29141577}{40000000000}>0. \qquad	ext{(28)} \] The same certificate verifies an original knot-producing parity pattern. No terminal tangles or replacement diagram are involved. Let \(Y_D\) be the actual complete augmented-link exterior supplied by these marked sphere data, and write \[ \Phi= rac{\operatorname{Vol}(Y_D)}{2\pi}. \qquad	ext{(29)} \] The complete action and this absolute volume normalization are identified by [the original Morse geometry](../papers/casimir-source-asymptotics/README.md). The rational interval certificate evaluates the entropy of the feasible table from below, and the complete positive action at one trial radius vector from above. It proves \[ E_{\mathrm{tab}}>67.8938190642,\qquad \Phi<67.6882466366,\qquad E_{\mathrm{tab}}-\Phi> rac15. \qquad	ext{(30)} \] The second number is an upper bound for \(\Phi\), obtained by testing its minimizing action; it is not an assertion that the trial radii are the complete critical point. The [rational verifier](../experiments/verify_actual_singleton_sector_obstruction.py) uses exact target equations and outward interval bounds, with no optimization in the verification. Combining (8) and (30), at the one fixed tuple (7), \[  oxed{\displaystyle \liminf_{N	o\infty} rac1N \log\mathcal A_{N, oldsymbol s}(+2,-2,\ldots,-2) \ge E_{\mathrm{tab}}>\Phi+ rac15 .} \qquad	ext{(31)} \] The \(+2\) entry in this notation is region \(32\). This is a lower bound for actual absolute local-coefficient products, not only for a convex envelope or its dual relaxation. ## 7. Every positive diagonal Cauchy reference has the same limitation For any finite complex array \((A_a)_{a\in I}\), \[ \inf_{w_a>0} \left(\sum_a w_aight)^{1/2} \left(\sum_a rac{|A_a|^2}{w_a}ight)^{1/2} =\sum_a|A_a|. \qquad	ext{(32)} \] Cauchy's inequality gives the lower bound. If no entry is zero, equality holds for \(w_a=|A_a|\). Assign a positive weight tending to zero to each zero entry to obtain the same infimum in general. If all entries vanish, both sides are zero. Apply (32) to the original array partition in (3). Even if the positive reference may depend on the level, every spectrum, the full diagram and the entire shared array, its best bound is exactly \(\mathcal A_{N, oldsymbol s}\). Equation (31) therefore rules out a universal upper rate \(\Phi\) by this method. A shared positive face gauge cannot change the conclusion: it multiplies every feasible array by the same original target monomial, canceled by the coefficient normalization. This also holds for level-dependent gauges. This limitation concerns diagonal positive references on the unchanged array partition. A non-diagonal Hermitian form or a regrouped sum can retain phase correlations before taking absolute values. Equation (32) does not rule out those estimates. ## 8. Exponential cancellation on the same odd levels Let \(B_{N,j}\ge0\) be the original shared coefficient of the product of positive central spectator polynomials, with targets \(d-j\) at \(x\), \(j\) at \(z\), and \(d\) at every other ordinary face. The protected variables remain zero. The finite identities are \[  egin{aligned} S_{N, oldsymbol s}(+2,-2,\ldots,-2) &=(-1)^{d(R-1)} \sum_{j=0}^{M}(-1)^jU_{N,j}B_{N,j},\ \mathcal A_{N, oldsymbol s}(+2,-2,\ldots,-2) &=\sum_{j=0}^{M}U_{N,j}B_{N,j}. \end{aligned} \qquad	ext{(33)} \] The two lines use the same exterior and the same targets. For the diagram in §6, the separate [uniform protected-interval theorem](research_cap_uniform_spectral_gap.md), §§3–4, proves \[ \limsup_{\substack{N	o\infty\N\ {\mathrm{odd}}}}  rac1N\log\sup_{\sigma\in[-2,2]} |S_{N, oldsymbol s}(\sigma,-2,\ldots,-2)| \le\Phi-\eta,\qquad \eta=\min\{3/1000,\gamma_D\}>0. \qquad	ext{(34)} \] Here \(\gamma_D\) is the strict omitted-tail capacity gap for the same original exterior. Its hypotheses retain the actual odd factors \(N^2D_mD_m\), their positive binary exterior after the other original targets are extracted, the original cutoff \(M=m-1\), and the certified untilted and tilted exterior pressures. In that theorem the binary variables are \(A=L_{16}\), \(C=L_0\); therefore its protected quartet \((C,0,A,0)\) and its coefficients \(p_j=B_{N,j}\) agree literally with (27) and (33). Take \(\sigma=+2\) in (34) and use the odd subsequence of (31). With \(\log0=-\infty\), \[  oxed{\displaystyle \limsup_{\substack{N	o\infty\N\ {\mathrm{odd}}}} rac1N \log rac{|S_{N, oldsymbol s}(+2,-2,\ldots,-2)|} {\mathcal A_{N, oldsymbol s}(+2,-2,\ldots,-2)} \le- igl(E_{\mathrm{tab}}-\Phi+\eta igr) <- rac15-\eta .} \qquad	ext{(35)} \] The denominator is positive for every sufficiently large level by the constructed arrays. Equation (35) is cancellation on the same odd levels and at the same fixed tuple, rather than a comparison of different parity subsequences. No even-level signed gap is asserted here. Nor does (35) estimate the other noncentral strings, simultaneous spectral variation at the spectators, or the filling functionals. The conclusion is a precise limitation of absolute summation and a precise instance of coherent cancellation in the original finite source; it is compatible with an eventual full knot-volume theorem. ## 9. Retaining the same flow does not repair the scalar energy score There is a related obstruction to the refined coefficient score in [the endpoint-conditioned energy criterion](general_endpoint_conditioned_source_energy.md), §§5–6. We recall its definitions to distinguish this statement from a bound for the signed sum. The positive local reference is \(-V_N(-2)\) at even levels and \(V_N(-2)-N^{-2}\partial_\sigma V_N(-2)\) at odd levels. For a normalized incidence load \(\zeta=v/d\), let \(h(\zeta)\) be the reference coefficient entropy. Let \(g(\zeta)\) be the proved upper rate for the squared absolute coefficient divided by its positive reference. The one-sided upper rate \(h_{\mathrm{env}}(\zeta)\) is the perspective of the retained triangle entropy. The combined score uses \[ h_{\mathrm{sharp}}(\zeta) =\min\{h_{\mathrm{env}}(\zeta),(h(\zeta)+g(\zeta))/2\} \quad	ext{on a one-sided load}, \qquad h_{\mathrm{sharp}}=h_C\quad	ext{on a central load}. \qquad	ext{(36)} \] Here \(h_C\) is the largest sum of the two triangle entropies over outer allocations giving that central four-incidence load. On the protected left ray, the exact local formulas are \[  egin{gathered} \zeta(u)=(u,0,1-u,0),\qquad 0\le u\le1/2,\ h(\zeta(u))=-2f(u),\qquad g(\zeta(u))=f(u)+f(1/2-u)=2f(u),\ h_{\mathrm{env}}(\zeta(u))=h_{\mathrm{sharp}}(\zeta(u))=0 . \end{gathered} \qquad	ext{(37)} \] The reference and relative-energy identities are the protected case of [the exact coefficient energy](actual_protected_outer_spectral_energy.md), §2, and [the one-sided triangle bound](../papers/casimir-source-asymptotics/README.md). The perspective has mass \(2u\) and a singleton normalized row \((1/2,0,0)\), whose entropy is zero. The value at \(u=0\) follows by continuity. In particular, the vanishing score is not merely the result of replacing a coefficient by a coarse, positive-radius bound. Keep the table (5) and set \(u=\lambda/2\). At a spectator, aggregate its rows \(\alpha=(\alpha_x,\alpha_b,\alpha_y)\) and \( eta=( eta_x, eta_c, eta_y)\) to \[ \zeta_e=(\alpha_x+ eta_x,\alpha_b, eta_c, \alpha_y+ eta_y). \qquad	ext{(38)} \] Both middles are at most \(1/2\). The two original rows are a permitted outer split, so \(h_C(\zeta_e)\) is at least their combined entropy. Equations (5) retain all ordinary and protected face totals after this aggregation. On central loads \(h=g=h_C\). Therefore the same single feasible flow in the 54-region example satisfies \[ \sum_e h_{\mathrm{sharp}}(\zeta_e)\ge E_{\mathrm{tab}}>\Phi+ rac15, \qquad \sum_e(h(\zeta_e)+g(\zeta_e)) \ge2E_{\mathrm{tab}}>2\Phi+ rac25 . \qquad	ext{(39)} \] Thus neither universal scalar score inequality holds on arbitrary matched simple-sphere Morse diagrams at their prescribed mark. This does not contradict the conditional implications of the energy criterion. That note asks its universal question on the narrower class of certified flat plats; the present construction does not identify this marked sphere with a member of that class. Strict concavity of complete triangle entropy does not compare these two different feasible sets. In the complete problem the missing input triangle of (4) puts load \(1/2\) on \(x\). If its output triangle puts load \(r\) on \(x\), the restored totals of the fixed spectator table would be \[ 1+(1/2-u+r)\quad	ext{at }x,\qquad 1-(1/2-u+r)\quad	ext{at }z . \qquad	ext{(40)} \] Since \(u<1/2\) and \(r\ge0\), these fail the complete face equations. The feasible noncentral table is consequently not a complete angle structure with the same faces. No nonhyperbolic representation or cone metric is inferred from it; the exact signed cancellation is instead the statement proved in (35). ## 10. Finite verification and proof scope The [source checker](../repro/check_absolute_source_obstruction.py) independently evaluates the original polynomial matrix \(V_N(\sigma)\) over finite fields, checks its protected coefficients and odd central factorization, and constructs exact rounded tables with the original targets. Those are finite checks of the identities and incidences. The all-level lower bound uses the written rounding argument and the uniform local coefficient theorem (17), not an extrapolation from the checked levels. The complete-volume comparison (30) uses the separate marked geometric construction and its rational action certificate. The signed upper bound (34) uses the separate stable-exterior theorem, its pressure certificates and omitted-tail gap. These inputs have different purposes; none follows merely from the finite-field checks or the absolute-array construction.

title: A nonzero initializer from the actual charge normal
text: # A nonzero initializer from the actual charge normal Research proof, 23 November 2026. The first charge normal of the original analytic Hermite coupon gives an explicit nonzero asymptotic at zero charge. This is a derivative of the actual finite source, obtained directly from its physical nodes. Its exponential rate is the complete-edge rate, independent of the fixed signed crossing powers. It is an inserted observation, not the original unit coupon or a lower bound for the original knot invariant. ## 1. The original finite source and the assertion Fix an integer \(N\ge2\), put \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), and \[ \eta=(-1)^d,\qquad P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2,\qquad \phi_N(f)=\eta N^2[z^d]\operatorname{rem}_{P_N}f. \tag{1} \] Here \(T_N\) is the Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind. Use the full algebra \(A_N=\mathbb C[z]/P_N\), including its repeated-root normals, and the original Newton polynomials and edge kernel of [S]: \[ S_a=\prod_{j=1}^a2\sin(\pi j/N),\quad S_0=1,\quad e_a(z)=S_a^{-2}\prod_{j<a}(2\cos((2j+1)\pi/N)-z), \] \[ K_N(t,u)=\sum_{a=0}^{d}e_a(-2\cos t)e_a(-2\cos u). \tag{2} \] Let \(\mathcal C_{N,\chi}\) be the actual entire Hermite family of [D, Section 9]. At a double root \(c_\tau=-2\cos\tau\), \(0<\tau<\pi\), its complete data are \[ \mathcal C_{N,\chi}(c_\tau)=\cos(N(1-\chi)\tau),\qquad \mathcal C_{N,\chi}'(c_\tau) =-\frac{N(1-\chi)\sin(N(1-\chi)\tau)}{2\sin\tau}. \tag{3} \] At the odd-level simple root \(-2\), its value is one. Define \[ \mathfrak d_N=\left.\partial_\chi \mathcal C_{N,\chi}\right|_0. \tag{4} \] This notation does not denote a modified quantum dimension. Let \(\Gamma=(V,E)\) be a fixed finite undirected graph carrying exactly the same-index kernels (2). Repeated edges and loops are allowed. Choose a nonempty set \(I\subseteq V\) of selected vertices, none isolated. Put \(m=|I|\), \(e=|E|\), and let \(d_v\ge1\) be the original degree of \(v\in I\), counting a loop twice. Every unselected boundary angle is fixed at zero. Fix integers \(n_v\), of either sign or zero, before taking \(N\to\infty\). Use the original crossing packet \(R_N=q^{d^2/2}\sum_{a=0}^d(-q)^a e_a\), with the displayed exponential meaning of its fractional power, and retain all its original phases. Its nodal value, in the normalization of [S, Sections 3 and 7], is \[ R_N(c_t)^{n}=C_{N,n}e^{inNt^2/(4\pi)},\qquad C_{N,n}=\exp\!\left(\frac{\pi i n(N-1)^2}{4N}\right). \tag{5} \] Products and negative powers are taken in the full original algebra. Define the actual normal source \[ Z_N^{\rm nor}= \left(\prod_{v\in I}\phi_N^{(v)}\right) \left[\prod_{v\in I}R_N(z_v)^{n_v}\mathfrak d_N(z_v) \prod_{vw\in E}K_N(t_v,t_w)\right], \qquad z_v=-2\cos t_v. \tag{6} \] For a loop the factor is \(K_N(t_v,t_v)\). No outside polynomial is reduced, and no semisimple replacement precedes (6). **Theorem.** Put \[ G_{\rm Cat}=\int_0^{\pi/4}\log(\cot s)\,ds,\qquad M_\infty=\frac{4G_{\rm Cat}}\pi,\qquad \varepsilon_N=\prod_{v\in I}C_{N,n_v}. \] Then, through both level parities, \[ \boxed{\quad Z_N^{\rm nor}=\varepsilon_N N^{3(m-e)/2} (2\pi)^m4^{-e}\prod_{v\in I}(d_v-in_v)^{-3/2} e^{NeM_\infty}\bigl(1+O(N^{-1})\bigr). \quad} \tag{7} \] The powers use the branch positive on the positive real axis, continued in the right half-plane. In particular the leading coefficient is nonzero. Constants may depend on the fixed graph and power vector. The exact identities below hold at every level; (7) is a large-level asymptotic and does not assert nonvanishing at every small level. ## 2. The charge derivative retains exactly the nodal values At each double root, \(\cos(N\tau)=\eta\) and \(\sin(N\tau)=0\). Differentiating the actual data (3), rather than a lattice asymptotic, gives \[ \mathfrak d_N(c_\tau)=0,\qquad \mathfrak d_N'(c_\tau)=\frac{\eta N^2\tau}{2\sin\tau},\qquad P_N''(c_\tau)=\frac{N^2}{2\sin^2\tau}. \tag{8} \] The normal's value at the odd simple root is zero. Since \(P_N\) is monic of degree \(N\), the top coefficient of a remainder equals the sum of the finite residues of \(f/P_N\). For any polynomial \(E\), put \(f=\mathfrak d_NE\). The residue at a double root is \(2\mathfrak d_N'(c)E(c)/P_N''(c)\). Consequently the exact full-algebra identity is \[ \phi_N(\mathfrak d_NE) =2N^2\sum_{\tau\in\mathcal T_N}\tau\sin\tau\,E(c_\tau), \quad \mathcal T_N=\left\{\frac{\pi(N-1-2l)}N: 0\le l<\lfloor N/2\rfloor\right\}. \tag{9} \] Thus \(\mathfrak d_N^2=0\) in \(A_N\), while \(\phi_N(\mathfrak d_N\overline f f)\ge0\); conjugation fixes the real variable \(z\). These are consequences of the original first normals. They do not discard those normals from (6). Enumerate the distinct double nodes as \(c_l=2\cos((2l+1)\pi/N)\), \(0\le l<r=\lfloor N/2\rfloor\). They are strictly decreasing. The literal factors in (2) show \[ e_a(c_l)>0\ (a\le l),\qquad e_a(c_l)=0\ (a>l),\qquad K_N(c_l,c_j)=\sum_{a\le\min(l,j)}e_a(c_l)e_a(c_j)>0. \tag{10} \] Here the notation \(K_N(c_l,c_j)\) means evaluation in its spectral arguments. In particular every row \(a\ge r\) vanishes at the retained nodes. At odd levels this also kills \(a=(N-1)/2\), whose only other nodal value lies at the simple root. This does not assert that its double-root normals vanish. Formula (9) now converts (6) exactly to a finite nodal sum with weights \(2N^2t\sin t\), kernels (10), and the phases (5). ## 3. A global nodal tail bound For a physical node \(c_t=-2\cos t\), a nonzero Newton value obeys \[ 0\le\frac{e_a(c_t)}{e_a(-2)} =\prod_{j<a}\left(1- \frac{1-\cos t}{1+\cos((2j+1)\pi/N)}\right) \le e^{-a(1-\cos t)/2}. \tag{11} \] If a numerator is zero the same inequality remains true. A zero denominator can occur only beyond the surviving rows at odd levels; those values already vanish. At a complete boundary \(t=0\), the ratio is one wherever defined. For completeness, the required complete-index estimates are elementary. Set \[ b(x)=2\int_0^x\log(\cot\pi s)\,ds. \tag{12} \] On compact subintervals of \(0<x<1/2\), midpoint summation in the cosine numerator and Stirling's formula in the sine denominator give \[ e_a(-2)=\frac{e^{Nb(a/N)}}{2N\sin(\pi a/N)}(1+O(N^{-1})). \tag{13} \] One obtains its uniform logarithmic version down to \(a=0\) by separating \(\log(2\sin\pi s)=\log s+\log(2\sin\pi s/s)\). The latter summand is smooth at zero and the former is handled by Stirling. The cosine summand is smooth on every such lower interval. The function \(b\) increases to its unique maximum at \(1/4\), then decreases; \(2b(1/4)=M_\infty\). Fix, for example, \(\epsilon=1/10\). Equations (12)--(13) imply \(\sum_{a<\epsilon N}e_a(-2)^2\le CN^A e^{N(M_\infty-\delta)}\) for some \(\delta>0\). Also [S, (18)] gives \(K_N(0,0)\le CN^A e^{NM_\infty}\). Applying (11) to the remaining indices, and using \((1-\cos t)+(1-\cos u)\le4\), proves for all physical or complete endpoints \[ 0\le K_N(t,u)\le CN^A e^{N\{M_\infty-c[(1-\cos t)+(1-\cos u)]\}} \tag{14} \] with some fixed \(c>0\). Thus the whole nodal sum outside any fixed small angle box is exponentially smaller than \(e^{NeM_\infty}\). Each selected angle receives its original degree \(d_v\ge1\). The weights in (9) are polynomial in \(N\), and the nodal crossing values have modulus one. This also controls every loop and repeated edge, without dropping a physical row or endpoint current. ## 4. The half-Gaussian coefficient in both parities The full local kernel theorem imported in [S, (18)] has its original separately even phase and amplitude. In particular, near zero, \[ K_N(t,u)=N^{-3/2}a(t,u)e^{N\psi(t,u)}(1+O(N^{-1})), \quad a(0,0)=\tfrac14,\quad \psi=M_\infty-\frac{t^2+u^2}{4\pi}+O((t^2+u^2)^2). \tag{15} \] The amplitude calibration can also be checked directly from (13). The phase \(2b\) has second derivative \(-8\pi\) at \(1/4\), so real Laplace summation of \(e_a(-2)^2\) gives \(K_N(0,0)\sim\tfrac14N^{-3/2}e^{NM_\infty}\). The exact consecutive-product ratio makes the low sequence unimodal, so its omitted shoulders have a strict gap. At odd levels the high values are zero. At even levels, putting \(b=d-a<N/2\), reflection gives \(e_a(-2)=[N^2e_b(-2)\cos^2(\pi(b+1/2)/N)]^{-1}\le1\) for \(a\ge N/2\). Thus no additional leading coefficient is hidden in that calibration. Put \(x_v=\sqrt N\,t_v\) in the exact nodal sum. The crossing phase and all incident quadratic terms give \(\exp[-(d_v-in_v)x_v^2/(4\pi)]\) at vertex \(v\). Furthermore \(t\sin t=t^2(1+O(t^2))\). The positive grid has spacing \(2\pi/N\). For even \(N\) it is the positive midpoint grid; for odd \(N\) it is the positive integer grid, with its zero point absent and of zero weight. Every factor is separately even. Reflection therefore converts either grid to half a full Gaussian lattice. The full-lattice rectangle or midpoint rule has error \(O(N^{-1})\) at spacing \(2\pi/\sqrt N\): apply the cellwise second-derivative remainder to a Gaussian times a fixed polynomial. Taylor's formula in (15), followed by Gaussian moment bounds and (14), gives the same relative error for the actual kernel product. For instance first restrict to \(|x_v|\le N^{1/12}\); the error is bounded by \(N^{-1}\) times a fixed polynomial in the \(x_v\), against a decaying Gaussian. The remaining scaled angles have exponentially small Gaussian tails by (14). These arguments apply to complex Gaussians because \(\Re(d_v-in_v)=d_v>0\). Each vertex's coefficient is consequently \[ 2N^2\frac{N}{2\pi}N^{-3/2} \int_0^\infty x^2e^{-(d_v-in_v)x^2/(4\pi)}\,dx =2\pi N^{3/2}(d_v-in_v)^{-3/2}. \tag{16} \] Multiplying (16), the edge factors \(4^{-e}N^{-3e/2}\), and the exact phase \(\varepsilon_N\) proves (7). ## 5. Original-source meaning and continuation limits If \(Z_N(\boldsymbol\chi)\) denotes (6) with each \(\mathfrak d_N\) replaced by its actual coupon, finite Hermite interpolation gives the exact identity \[ Z_N^{\rm nor}= \left.\left(\prod_{v\in I}\partial_{\chi_v}\right) Z_N(\boldsymbol\chi)\right|_{\boldsymbol0}. \tag{17} \] No lattice-only charge asymptotic was differentiated. The uniform zero-face theorem [Z] instead divides a specified principal Fourier interpolation; it expressly distinguishes that interpolation from the whole off-lattice coupon source. Formula (7) evaluates the actual normal observation (17), with arbitrary fixed signed powers. However \(\mathcal C_{N,0}=\eta\,1\) and \(\mathcal C_{N,1}=1\). Thus the full source is not divisible by the charges. Its all-zero value remains \(\eta^m\) times the uninserted source. Subtraction or antisymmetrization would change the observation; in particular \(\mathcal C_{N,1}-\mathcal C_{N,-1}=0\). The positive form in (9) also does not define a quotient preserved by Newton reversal \(Je_a=e_{d-a}\), the original turn: its null space contains \(e_d\), while \(Je_d=e_0\) is not null. For example, a reversed edge \(\sum_a e_a(c_l)e_{d-a}(c_j)\) vanishes at every pair of double nodes: nonzero factors would require both \(a<r\) and \(d-a<r\), which is impossible. Such a retained edge is outside theorem (7). Accordingly (7) supplies a nonzero inserted initializer at the complete edge rate \(eM_\infty\). For a general graph this has not been identified with a manifold volume. It gives no source-preserving continuation to the unit coupon, no control of transported cuts or relative-cycle coefficients, and no filled-volume or original-knot lower bound. ## Complete proof sources and coverage Both complete matching proof texts were read: - [D] [Actual analytic coupon family](research_dominant_saddle_transport.md), 685 lines, SHA-256 `413940497a23e884d726b91f9c0ebc01994fef8216811ed2c6fb0838fc80bb04`. - [S] [Original finite small-charge source](research_small_charge_path_source.md), 809 lines, SHA-256 `c6d0ce2a4ecf1412aa3752cb8a94c6933bb47acab5d96d879c6f1b17b2db2a90`. The complete [Z] [zero-charge low-source theorem](research_zero_charge_uniform_low_source.md), 496 lines, SHA-256 `d4412c67ca520894840b80e390058ce2438af906ea13f719abb5def5c252496d`, was read for coverage. It does not assert (17)'s actual normal asymptotic. Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used. Earlier finals, manuscripts and public documents were not edited.

title: Actual Clebsch generating legs and their binomial dual
text:
# Actual Clebsch generating legs and their binomial dual Private written proof, 18 November 2026. The ordinary generating function of an actual normalized Clebsch column admits an exact magnetic summation. A contracting finite recurrence then gives a holomorphic unit on a full small activity disk. Its literal ordinary-binomial dual has a selected coefficient-circle saddle with nonzero amplitude. A uniform-Casimir extension then estimates both literal confluent partner legs by Cauchy differentiation. The phases, finite support and full Hermite channel row are retained. No subsequent Casimir-channel contraction is estimated. Complete direct H fixes the physical column and its full Hermite inverse. Complete direct C supplies the finite Chu identity used below. The recurrence, analytic estimates, and dual contour proof are given here. Complete direct U supplies the stronger uniform-Casimir magnetic unit; Section 5 proves its actual binomial-dual and partner extension. ## 1. The actual column and its magnetic generating function Put \[ d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\quad x=-q^{-1}, \quad f_a=(Q;Q)_a,\quad s_a=\prod_{h=1}^a2\sin(\pi h/N). 	ag{1} \] Write \( eta(a,b)=s_a/(s_bs_{a-b})\). For indices below \(N\), \({a rack b}_Q=q^{b(a-b)} eta(a,b)\), with the displayed phase. On the physical degree \(0\le T\le d\), H defines the normalized Casimir column \(f_T(\lambda_j)\), whose first entry is one, at \(\lambda_j=q^{2j+1}+q^{-2j-1}\), \(0\le j\le T\). Set \(r=T-j\). Its literal highest vector and descendant are \[ h_j=\sum_{a=0}^j(-1)^ax^{-a}Q^{a(a-1)/2} {j rack a}_Q|a,j-aangle, \qquad f_T(\lambda_j)= rac{x^r}{{T rack j}_Q}  rac{F_\Sigma^r}{f_r}h_j. 	ag{2} \] The first formula follows from H's generic highest vector by root specialization. In polynomial coordinates it is \[ h_j(w_1,w_2)=\prod_{a=0}^{j-1}(w_2-x^{-1}Q^aw_1). 	ag{3} \] Let \(v(w)|a,bangle=w_1^aw_2^b\), and define \(L_{T,j}(w)=v(w)f_T(\lambda_j)\). We claim the exact formula \[  oxed{ L_{T,j}(w)= rac{x^r}{{T rack j}_Q}h_j(w) [t^r] rac1{(tw_1;Q)_{j+1}(x^{-1}tw_2;Q)_{j+1}}.} 	ag{4} \] Here is a finite proof including the cap. The literal actions are \(F_i=w_i(1-QT_{Q,i})\), \(K_1^{-1}=x^{-1}T_{Q,1}\), and \(F_\Sigma=F_1+K_1^{-1}F_2\). Its two summands obey \(AB=Q^{-1}BA\); in the order \(A^{r-b}B^b\), the divided coefficient is \(1/(f_{r-b}f_b)\). On one actual head, \[ \sum_{n=0}^{d-a} rac{t^nF^n}{f_n}w^a =w^a rac{1-(tw)^N}{(tw;Q)_{a+1}}. 	ag{5} \] This follows either from Gaussian Pascal or multiplication by the denominator. The numerator is retained; it first affects degree \(N\). Since \(r<T+1\le N\), extraction of \(t^r\) from the two-head product is therefore exactly extraction from \[ \sum_{a=0}^j  rac{(-1)^ax^{-a}Q^{a(a-1)/2}{j rack a}_Q w_1^aw_2^{j-a}} {(tw_1;Q)_{a+1}(x^{-1}tQ^aw_2;Q)_{j-a+1}}. 	ag{6} \] Put \(U=tw_1,V=x^{-1}tw_2\). After taking the common denominator in (4), its numerator divided by \(w_2^j\) is \[ (UQ;Q)_j\sum_{a=0}^j  rac{(Q^{-j};Q)_a(V;Q)_a}{f_a(UQ;Q)_a} (UQ^{j+1}/V)^a =(QU/V;Q)_j. 	ag{7} \] The equality is C's finite Chu identity. Since \(x^{-2}=Q\), the last polynomial is \(h_j/w_2^j\). Apparent denominators in this calculation are removed by polynomial continuation. This proves (4). It does not extend removal of the numerators in (5) to degrees at least \(N\). On \(w_2
e0\) put \(ho=xw_1/w_2\), and define \[ P_{n,j}(ho)=\sum_{a=0}^n  eta(j+a,a) eta(j+n-a,n-a)ho^a, \qquad p_{n,j}=P_{n,j}/ eta(j+n,n). 	ag{8} \] All indices used below satisfy \(j+n<N\). The two Gaussian coefficients in (4) have the common phase \(q^{jn}\). It cancels the phase of the normalizer in (2), giving \[  oxed{L_{T,j}(w)=w_2^T\mathcal L_{T,j}(ho),\qquad \mathcal L_{T,j}(ho)=(Qho;Q)_j p_{r,j}(ho).} 	ag{9} \] Thus \(\mathcal L_{T,j}(0)=1\). Neither the highest-vector phase nor an input/output gauge has been discarded. ## 2. A full disk, not only a positive-radius estimate Fix a compact set of real parameters \[ 0<\xi<	au<1, \qquad \xi=j/N,\quad	au=T/N,\quad\kappa=	au-\xi. 	ag{10} \] All asymptotics use these actual scaled integer parameters. There is an \(\epsilon>0\), depending only on that compact set, such that \(\mathcal L_{T,j}\) is zero-free on \(|ho|<\epsilon\) for all sufficiently large \(N\), and has the relative asymptotic proved below. No interpolation of \(j\) or \(T\) is intended. The exact recurrence which proves this is \[ p_{0,j}=1,\quad p_{1,j}=1+ho,\qquad p_{n,j}=(1+ho)p_{n-1,j}-ho b_n p_{n-2,j}, 	ag{11} \] where \[ b_n=  rac{\sin(\pi(2j+n)/N)\sin(\pi(n-1)/N)} {\sin(\pi(j+n)/N)\sin(\pi(j+n-1)/N)}. 	ag{12} \] To verify it without an orthogonal-polynomial assertion, let \(G(t)=[(t;Q)_{j+1}(ho t;Q)_{j+1}]^{-1}\). Then \[ (1-t)(1-ho t)G(t) =(1-Q^{j+1}t)(1-ho Q^{j+1}t)G(Qt). \] Its \(t^n\) coefficient, after removing the common phase \(q^{jn}\), is \[ \sin(\pi n/N)P_{n,j} =(1+ho)\sin(\pi(j+n)/N)P_{n-1,j} -ho\sin(\pi(2j+n)/N)P_{n-2,j}. \] Dividing by the specified \( eta\) gives (11). The \(b_n\), \(1\le n\le r\), are uniformly bounded on (10). Choose \(\epsilon\) so small that \[ z\longmapsto1+ho-ho b_n/z 	ag{13} \] maps \(|z-1|\le1/4\) into itself and has Lipschitz constant at most \(1/3\) there, uniformly in \(n,N\). Induction proves every ratio \(r_n=p_{n,j}/p_{n-1,j}\) exists, is in that disk, and is holomorphic in \(ho\). This proves the asserted zero-freeness, including the whole coefficient circle needed later. It does not use positivity at complex \(ho\). Here are the phase and amplitude, including the subprincipal term. Write \(h=1/N\), and use \(s\in[0,\kappa]\) as a real integration parameter. Uniformly there, (12) has the expansion \[ b_n=b(s)+h b_1(s)+O(h^2),\quad s=n/N, \] \[ b(s)=1- rac{\sin^2(\pi\xi)}{\sin^2(\pi(\xi+s))}, \qquad b_1(s)=- rac{\pi\sin(\pi\xi)\sin(\pi(2\xi+s))} {\sin^3(\pi(\xi+s))}. 	ag{14} \] There is no singularity at \(s=0\) in these formulas. Let \[ R(s)= rac{1+ho+ \sqrt{(1+ho)^2-4ho b(s)}}2, \qquad a(s)=- rac{ho b(s)R'(s)+ho b_1(s)R(s)} {R(s)^2-ho b(s)}. 	ag{15} \] The square root and logarithms below are their holomorphic branches at \(ho=0\); all denominators are units after shrinking \(\epsilon\). A prime in (15) means \(s\)-derivative, not a Casimir or meridian derivative. Substitution into (13) shows that \(\widetilde r_n=R(nh)+h a(nh)\) has a residual \(O(h^2)\). Indeed the coefficient of \(h\) is exactly \[ a(1-ho b/R^2)=-ho bR'/R^2-ho b_1/R. \] At the first step, \(b(0)=0\), \(b_1(0)=-b'(0)\), and \(a(0)=-R'(0)\). Hence \(\widetilde r_1=1+ho+O(h^2)\). The contraction (13) now gives \(r_n=\widetilde r_n+O(h^2)\) uniformly for every \(n\le r\). Taking the logarithms fixed at zero and summing yields, by the ordinary Euler--Maclaurin formula with bounded derivatives, \[ \log p_{r,j} =N\int_0^\kappa\log R(s)\,ds +	frac12\log rac{R(\kappa)}{R(0)} +\int_0^\kappa rac{a(s)}{R(s)}\,ds+O(N^{-1}). 	ag{16} \] Every error just used is holomorphic and uniformly bounded on a slightly larger disk, so fixed \(ho\)-derivatives follow by Cauchy. Put \(c_0=2\pi i\). Applying the same elementary sum formula to \(\log(Qho;Q)_j\) proves \[  oxed{\mathcal L_{T,j}(ho) =e^{N S_L(ho)}A_L(ho)(1+O(N^{-1})),} 	ag{17} \] where \[ S_L=\int_0^\xi\Log(1-ho e^{c_0s})\,ds +\int_0^\kappa\log R(s)\,ds, 	ag{18} \] \[ A_L= \sqrt{ rac{1-ho e^{c_0\xi}}{1-ho}} \sqrt{ rac{R(\kappa)}{R(0)}} \exp\int_0^\kappa rac{a(s)}{R(s)}\,ds. 	ag{19} \] Both square roots equal one at zero. In particular \(S_L(0)=0,A_L(0)=1\), and \(A_L\) is a holomorphic unit. Direct differentiation of the integrals gives the useful calibration \[ c:=S_L'(0) =- rac{\sin^2(\pi\xi)}{\pi} (\cot(\pi	au)+i) =- rac{\sin^2(\pi\xi)e^{i\pi	au}} {\pi\sin(\pi	au)}
e0. 	ag{20} \] The exact factor \(x\) remains in \(ho=xw_1/w_2\); replacing it by its limit would change a subprincipal term. ## 3. The literal ordinary-binomial dual The original coherent input on this degree block has components \[ c(z)_{a,T-a}= inom da inom d{T-a}z_1^az_2^{T-a}. \] Its right value leg is therefore exactly \[ R_{T,j}(z)=\operatorname{CT}_{u,v} L_{T,j}(u,v)(1+z_1/u)^d(1+z_2/v)^d. 	ag{21} \] The two coefficient circles are the original finite dual, with all indices between zero and \(d\). Homogeneity reduces (21) to \[  oxed{R_{T,j}(z)=z_2^T inom dT\operatorname{CT}_{ho} \mathcal L_{T,j}(ho)\mathcal B_T(\eta/ho), \quad \eta=xz_1/z_2,} 	ag{22} \] where \[ \mathcal B_T(t)= inom dT^{-1} \sum_{a=0}^T inom da inom d{T-a}t^a = inom dT^{-1}[v^T](1+tv)^d(1+v)^d. 	ag{23} \] In particular (22) is not a Hermitian pairing or a reciprocal-monomial replacement of the coherent input. For later use, (23) has a uniform holomorphic unit on a full small \(t\)-disk. Let \(v=v(t)\) be the root near \(v_0=	au/(1-	au)\) of \[  rac{tv}{1+tv}+ rac{v}{1+v}=	au, \qquad D(t)= rac{tv}{(1+tv)^2}+ rac{v}{(1+v)^2}. 	ag{24} \] Then \[ \mathcal B_T(t)=e^{N S_B(t)}A_B(t)(1+O(N^{-1})), 	ag{25} \] \[ S_B=\log(1+tv)+\log(1+v)-	au\log v +	au\log	au+(1-	au)\log(1-	au), \] \[ A_B= rac{\sqrt{	au/(1-	au)}}{(1+tv)(1+v)\sqrt{D(t)}}. 	ag{26} \] The branches continue their positive values at zero, and \(S_B(0)=0,A_B(0)=1,S_B'(0)=b:=	au/(1-	au)>0\). For completeness, this is an actual coefficient estimate. At \(t=0\) the circle \(v=v_0e^{i	heta}\) has a unique modulus maximum at \(	heta=0\), with quadratic coefficient \(D(0)=	au(1-	au)>0\). Outside a fixed small arc the binomial modulus has a uniform exponential gap. For small complex \(t\), use the circle \(v(t)e^{i	heta}\); its radius and argument change by a small amount and coefficient extraction is unchanged. The outside gap persists by continuity on the compact circle. Near zero the phase is holomorphic, stationary, and has positive real quadratic part. Taylor expansion, Gaussian integration and the vanishing of the odd cubic integral give relative \(O(N^{-1})\), uniformly on a fixed smaller disk. The amplitude \([(1+tv)(1+v)]^{-1}\) is the exact \(d=N-1\) correction. Dividing by \[  inom dT=\sqrt{ rac{1-	au}{2\pi N	au}} e^{N[-	au\log	au-(1-	au)\log(1-	au)]} (1+O(N^{-1})) \] gives (25)--(26). Zeros of the polynomial on the distant portion of a circle do not require a logarithm there: the complement bound uses its actual modulus. This proves the full-disk relative estimate and zero-freeness, not just a formal saddle equation. ## 4. A selected nonzero saddle for the whole right leg Fix \(0<\vartheta_0<\pi/2\). Parameterize the small input activity by \[ \eta= rac{a^2}{bc},\qquad 0<|a|<\epsilon_1,\quad|\arg a|<\vartheta_0. 	ag{27} \] Here \(b,c\) are exactly (20),(26). Choose \(\epsilon_1\) uniformly on the compact parameter set (10). There is a unique stationary point near \(a/c\), \[ ho_*=(a/c)(1+O(a)),\qquad D_ho\{S_L(ho)+S_B(\eta/ho)\}|_{ho_*}=0, \quad D_ho=ho\partial_ho. 	ag{28} \] It is holomorphic in \(a\) through its scaled coordinate \(cho_*/a\). Put \[ \Psi=S_L(ho_*)+S_B(\eta/ho_*),\qquad \mathcal H=D_ho^2\{S_L(ho)+S_B(\eta/ho)\}|_{ho_*}. 	ag{29} \] Then \(\Psi=2a+O(a^2)\) and \(\mathcal H=2a+O(a^2)\). On every compact subset of (27), the actual finite right leg obeys \[  oxed{ R_{T,j}(z)=z_2^T inom dT  rac{e^{N\Psi}A_L(ho_*)A_B(\eta/ho_*)} {\sqrt{2\pi N\mathcal H}} (1+O(N^{-1})).} 	ag{30} \] The square root is continued from positive real \(a\). The coefficient in front of this selected Gaussian is exactly \(+1\). To prove the contour assertion, write \(ho=(a/c)u\). Uniformly on a fixed annulus about \(|u|=1\), the phase in (22) is \(a(u+u^{-1})+O(a^2)\). Divide its stationary equation by \(a\) and apply the analytic inverse-function theorem near \(u=1\). Use the permitted original coefficient circle \(ho=ho_*e^{i	heta}\). Both its arguments \(ho\) and \(\eta/ho\) lie in the full disks of (17),(25). Exact stationarity and bounded second angular derivatives give \[ \Re\{S_L(ho_*e^{i	heta})+ S_B(\eta e^{-i	heta}/ho_*)-\Psi\} \le-[2\Re a-C|a|^2](1-\cos	heta). 	ag{31} \] Indeed the leading difference is \(2a(\cos	heta-1)\); the remainder has derivative zero at zero, hence is \(O(|a|^2	heta^2)\) there, and is \(O(|a|^2)\) on the rest of the circle. These bounds give the stated global factor \(1-\cos	heta\). For sufficiently small \(\epsilon_1\), (31) is a strict gap on every compact subset of (27). Insert the uniform relative units (17),(25) into the exact integral. The integral of the error is bounded by \(O(N^{-1})\) times the same Gaussian scale, using (31). The retained central arc has quadratic coefficient \(\mathcal H\) with positive real part. Its Gaussian integral, with measure \(d	heta/(2\pi)\), is \((2\pi N\mathcal H)^{-1/2}\); its odd cubic term integrates to zero and the remaining error is relative \(O(N^{-1})\). This proves (30), including the entire complementary circle. The amplitude is nonzero, so the actual right leg is nonzero for all sufficiently large \(N\) on smaller compact subsets. Fixed coherent-variable derivatives follow by Cauchy on nested complex neighborhoods. The theorem does not cover a sequence \(a	o0\) without a separate uniform scaling analysis, although the exact finite leg at \(\eta=0\) is (22). ## 5. Uniform Casimir dependence and both true partner legs The preceding proof is retained independently. A stronger input from U now removes its restriction to values at integer channels. Define the literal polynomial \[ \mathsf L_T(ho;\lambda)= \sum_{a=0}^T x^{-a}f_a(\lambda)ho^a, \qquad \sigma_N=(T+1)/N,\quad	au_N=T/N. 	ag{32} \] Here \(f_a\) is H's actual continuant column, with \(f_0=1\). Keep \(\sigma_N\) in a fixed compact subinterval of \((0,1)\). U proves, uniformly for \(\lambda\) in any fixed compact disk, \[ \mathsf L_T(ho;\lambda) =e^{N\phi(ho;\lambda,\sigma_N)} \mathcal A(ho;\lambda,\sigma_N)(1+O(N^{-1})) 	ag{33} \] on a full small \(ho\)-disk. Its relative error is holomorphic with fixed \(ho,\lambda\) derivatives of the same size on smaller sets. Its phase is calibrated by \[ \phi= rac1{c_0}\int_0^ho rac{\log Y(t)}t\,dt, \quad (1-ho)^2(1-Y)(1-e^{-c_0\sigma}Y) +(2-\lambda)ho=0,\quad Y(0)=1. 	ag{34} \] Its explicit transported amplitude \(\mathcal A\) is U's formula (5), normalized by \(\mathcal A(0)=1\), including all first-order quantum shifts. In particular put \[ c_\lambda:=\phi_ho(0;\lambda,\sigma_N) = rac{\lambda-2}{c_0(e^{-c_0\sigma_N}-1)},\qquad k_N=\partial_\lambda c_\lambda = rac1{c_0(e^{-c_0\sigma_N}-1)}. 	ag{35} \] The subscript on \(c_\lambda\) denotes its dependence, not a derivative. These quantities are nonzero on compact Casimir sets avoiding \(2\), except that no such exclusion is needed for \(k_N\). Let \(R_T(z;\lambda)=f_T(\lambda)^{\mathsf t}c(z)\). Equations (21)--(23) remain exact with \(\mathcal L_{T,j}\) replaced by \(\mathsf L_T\), since they were coefficient identities. Use the binomial phase and amplitude (24)--(26) with \(	au=	au_N\), and write \(b=	au_N/(1-	au_N)\). On compact Casimir sets avoiding \(2\), set \[ \eta= rac{a^2}{b c_\lambda},\qquad 0<|a|<\epsilon_2,\quad |\arg a|<\vartheta_0<\pi/2. 	ag{36} \] Replace \(S_L,A_L\) in (28)--(31) by \(\phi(\cdot;\lambda,\sigma_N),\mathcal A\). Denote the resulting stationary point, action, Hessian and amplitude by \[  egin{split} \widehatho_*&=(a/c_\lambda)(1+O(a)),\ \widehat\Psi&=\phi(\widehatho_*;\lambda,\sigma_N) +S_B(\eta/\widehatho_*;	au_N),\ \widehat{\mathcal H} &=D_ho^2\{\phi(ho;\lambda,\sigma_N) +S_B(\eta/ho;	au_N)\}|_{\widehatho_*},\ \widehat A &= rac{\mathcal A(\widehatho_*;\lambda,\sigma_N) A_B(\eta/\widehatho_*;	au_N)} {\sqrt{\widehat{\mathcal H}}}. \end{split}	ag{37} \] The same exact coefficient-circle proof gives \[  oxed{R_T(z;\lambda)=z_2^T inom dT  rac{e^{N\widehat\Psi}\widehat A}{\sqrt{2\pi N}} (1+O(N^{-1})).} 	ag{38} \] This is uniform and holomorphic on nested complex neighborhoods of compact subsets of (36), including the Casimir variable. In detail, U's full-disk estimate supplies (33) on the entire coefficient circle; \(c_\lambda\) is uniformly bounded away from zero there; the expansion is again \(a(u+u^{-1})+O(a^2)\) on a fixed annulus. The inverse-function construction and the global gap (31) are thus uniform in \(\lambda\). Their actual complementary integral and relative error estimates apply without any change to the finite caps. Consequently the actual partner rows have the controlled logarithmic derivatives \[  oxed{ egin{split}  rac{\partial_\lambda L_T(w;\lambda)}{L_T(w;\lambda)} &=N\phi_\lambda(ho;\lambda,\sigma_N) +\partial_\lambda\log\mathcal A+O(N^{-1}),\  rac{\partial_\lambda R_T(z;\lambda)}{R_T(z;\lambda)} &=N\partial_\lambda\widehat\Psi +\partial_\lambda\log\widehat A+O(N^{-1}). \end{split}}	ag{39} \] The first line has \(L_T(w;\lambda)=w_2^T\mathsf L_T(ho;\lambda)\). In both lines the physical coherent arguments are held fixed. In particular the second derivative holds \(\eta=xz_1/z_2\) fixed, not the auxiliary \(a\). Stationarity gives the exact envelope identity \(\partial_\lambda\widehat\Psi =\phi_\lambda(\widehatho_*;\lambda,\sigma_N)\). Locally the branch in (36) varies holomorphically as \(\lambda\) varies with \(\eta\) fixed. Cauchy differentiation of the relative error in (33),(38) proves (39); no derivative of a coarse absolute error or of an integer channel is used. For sufficiently small nonzero activity these are nontrivial partner estimates: \(\phi_\lambda=k_Nho+O(ho^2)\) and \(\widehat\Psi_\lambda=(k_N/c_\lambda)a+O(a^2)\) are nonzero. Thus each partner has a nonzero order-\(N\) leading factor relative to its value on compact subsets of those punctured charts. At zero activity the exact partners vanish, and no such assertion is made. Higher fixed Casimir derivatives follow from the same holomorphic error control. At an actual node use \(\lambda_j=2\cos(2\pi j/N+\pi/N)\) literally in (33)--(39). Their \(\sigma_N=(T+1)/N\) differs from the \(	au_N=T/N\) in the binomial dual. Neither shift is dropped. The older formulas (17)--(20) use their own exact-root, integer-channel calibration. Equality of the leading characteristic equations alone does not identify their subprincipal amplitudes with (33). At a double node H identifies the derivative in (39) with the actual generic-quantum confluent column. This is still a fixed-root Casimir derivative, not a meridian or quantum-parameter normal of the source. ## 6. The retained Hermite channel contour and source requirements The argument sums the physical magnetic coordinate, and (30) also pays its actual ordinary-binomial dual. It leaves the integer channel unsummed. On the complete paired chamber the exact reciprocal-monomial identity has phase \(
u_j=(-1)^jq^{j(j+1)}\); it is not a reason to replace (21) by a positive pairing. H's inverse measure itself contains \(
u_j\), and its derivative columns remain essential. More precisely, write \(f_T(\lambda)\) for H's actual continuant column, and define \(L(\lambda)=v(w)f_T(\lambda)\) and \(R(\lambda)=f_T(\lambda)^{\mathsf t}c(z)\). For a Casimir polynomial multiplier \(m\), the exact contribution of a double node is \[  rac{(mLR)'(\lambda_j)-\eta_jm(\lambda_j)L(\lambda_j)R(\lambda_j)} {\sigma_j}, 	ag{40} \] and that of a simple node is \(mLR/\sigma_j\). The prime here is the actual Casimir derivative. H proves its equality with the specified generic-quantum divided difference, including its source normalization. Equations (33)--(39) estimate both actual legs and partners on their stated charts. They do not estimate the sum of (40) over its physical channels. There is an exact way to combine all the partners before that remaining step. Keep H's continuants \(p_a\), characteristic polynomial \(P_T=p_{T+1}\), and \(B_T=A_0\cdots A_{T-1}\). Let \(\Gamma_T\) be a union of small positive circles around the distinct roots of \(P_T\), excluding the zeros of \(p_T\). Such circles exist: \(p_T\) is nonzero at every root of \(P_T\), either by H's nonzero inverse normalizers or by backwards use of the continuant recurrence. For every actual Casimir polynomial multiplier \(m\), \[  oxed{v(w)m(J_T)c(z)= rac{B_T^2}{2\pi i} \int_{\Gamma_T} rac{m(\lambda)L(\lambda)R(\lambda)} {P_T(\lambda)p_T(\lambda)}\,d\lambda.} 	ag{41} \] Indeed H gives \(\sigma_j=P_T'(\lambda_j)p_T(\lambda_j)/B_T^2\) at a simple node. At a double node put \(Q_j=P_T/(\lambda-\lambda_j)^2\); then \(\sigma_j=Q_jp_T/B_T^2\) and \(\eta_j=Q_j'/Q_j+p_T'/p_T\). The residue is exactly (40). This proves (41), with no lost derivative or additional coefficient. Equivalently let \(\mathfrak r_T\) denote the polynomial of the original \(\kappa\)-stripped checked crossing on this block. H's endpoint calibration, including its derivative, says \(p_T\equiv B_Tx^T\mathfrak r_T\pmod {P_T}\). The crossing is invertible, so its inverse in this same finite algebra gives the alternative exact row \[  rac{B_Tx^{-T}}{2\pi i}\int_{\Gamma_T}  rac{m(\lambda)\mathfrak r_T^{-1}(\lambda) L(\lambda)R(\lambda)}{P_T(\lambda)} \,d\lambda. 	ag{42} \] The inverse is the actual polynomial remainder, with its phase and Hermite jets. Equation (42) removes the extra \(p_T\) poles algebraically; it does not replace the inverse crossing by a positive weight. Enlarging (41) instead must retain any \(p_T\) poles it crosses. No channel-contour deformation or complementary-channel estimate is asserted by either exact representation. Every multiplier, inverse measure, original pivot, turnover, and peripheral line remains where the actual Hermite contraction puts it. The construction proves no nonzero value for that channel sum or for the closed opposite-source period. It supplies no uniform meridian or quantum-parameter normal. Nor is the small activity chart asserted to contain a specified geometric point. The generic-q and whole-meridian families must be transported before any such normal is taken. All asymptotic charts keep the physical total away from its top value: \(T=d\), where \(e^{-c_0\sigma_N}=1\), is excluded. The exact identities (4),(21),(40)--(42) still retain that finite block. ## Complete proof directs and coverage * H: notes/actual_complete_casimir_hermite_packet.md, SHA256 a4e96738a3a093d963fe13cc03585085951fa8699a506ade4e2e7a47c17b3f4c. * C: notes/research_balanced_gauss_cyclic_divisor_source.md, SHA256 c15668d7dff95346d72801b721bf95970b661e5b17d125aaadd7e0dc38905b00. * U: notes/research_actual_jacobi_generating_unit.md, SHA256 ab3760dd38817c2345c231d8ef67c8a7fa8bb03e3b26d4ef1de1b87182f6728d. The complete q-Hahn Fourier coefficient variational theorem, holomorphic Fourier--Legendre transport, and complete-core complex packet were read for coverage. Their Fourier polynomial, selected action chart, and certified complete-image period are different objects from the ordinary magnetic generating leg and the literal dual (21). No asymptotic from them is imported here. Only written mathematics and text/hash operations are used. Frozen and public files are unchanged.

title: An analytic Euler transition on actual endpoint head blocks
text: # An analytic Euler transition on actual endpoint head blocks Private written proof, 18 November 2026. After explicit factorial endpoint gauges, a compressed literal crossing has a uniformly bounded transfer generator. Its entire finite Euler polynomial converges in operator norm to the exponential of that generator, with error \(O(N^{-1})\). The inverse has the corresponding estimate. This is an actual finite-matrix transition, not substitution of commuting symbols into a formal Euler series. A single quadratic zero permits a head collar of width \(O(N^{1/2})\). Two quadratic zeros permit two collars of width \(O(N^{3/4})\). Every collar is a single interval. Monotonicity proves the exact compression identity even when a transfer can exit a collar. All complementary blocks remain source currents, with no smallness claim. The finite Fourier projector and the original quantum/meridian normal rows are retained. The complete directs are B, the literal balanced crossing; E, the actual endpoint factorial chart; and V, the common two-wall module. Their pins are below. The new analytic estimates and compression proof are given in full here. No neighboring-network packet hypothesis is inferred. ## 1. The actual finite Euler factors Fix \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), and use \[ h_N=\frac{2\pi i}{N},\qquad Q=e^h,\qquad q=e^{h/2}, \qquad x=-M/q. \tag{1} \] On the original balanced head, with basis \(w_0,\ldots,w_d\), let \[ \mathcal E w_a=\alpha_a w_{a-1},\quad \alpha_a=MQ^{-a}-M^{-1}\quad(a\ge1),\qquad \mathcal E w_0=0, \tag{2} \] \[ Fw_a=(1-Q^{a+1})w_{a+1}\quad(a<d),\qquad Fw_d=0. \tag{3} \] These are the actual compressed matrices before specialization. Away from the ordinary-color path they are auxiliary finite matrices, not a generic finite-dimensional Hopf representation. V retains their exact Hopf defect. Put \(A=\mathcal E_1\otimes F_2\), so \(A^N=0\), and \(F_n(Q)=\prod_{j=1}^n(1-Q^j)\), \(F_0=1\). B gives the literal positive uncheck Euler factor and its inverse: \[ \Theta_N(A)=\sum_{n=0}^{d} \frac{(-1)^n q^{n^2}}{F_n(Q)}A^n,\qquad \Theta_N(A)^{-1}=\sum_{n=0}^{d} \frac{q^n}{F_n(Q)}A^n. \tag{4} \] The positive crossing is \(\kappa\,\mathsf P D\Theta_N\); the negative is its literal inverse. Here \(\mathsf P\) is the flip, \(D_{a,b}=x^{-a-b}Q^{ab}\), and \(\kappa\) is the unchanged common Cartan line. All pivots and framing remain their original matrices. For completeness (4) is a finite algebraic identity whenever \(F_n\), \(n<N\), are units. The two displayed polynomials \(U,V\), with \(A\) replaced by \(z\), have coefficient recurrences giving, modulo \(z^N\), \[ U(Qz)=U(z)/(1-qz),\qquad V(Qz)=(1-qz)V(z). \tag{5} \] Hence \(U(z)V(z)=1\) modulo \(z^N\): its positive coefficients below \(N\) vanish since \(1-Q^j\ne0\). Substitute \(z=A\). This proof uses no infinite product convergence and applies on the normal disks below. ## 2. A global factorial majorant and the uniform exponential limit At \(h=h_N\), \[ |1-Q^j|=2\sin(\pi j/N)\ge\frac4N\min(j,N-j). \tag{6} \] For \(n\le N/2\), this directly gives \(|F_n|\ge(4/N)^n n!\). For \(n>N/2\), the ratio \(\prod_{j=1}^n\min(j,N-j)/n!\) decreases to \[ \binom{N-1}{\lfloor N/2\rfloor}^{-1} \ge2^{-(N-1)}\ge4^{-n}. \tag{7} \] Consequently, at every level and for every \(0\le n<N\), \[ |F_n(Q_N)|\ge N^{-n}n!. \tag{8} \] Choose a sufficiently small absolute \(\eta>0\). On the doubled normal bidisk \[ |h-h_N|\le2\eta N^{-2},\qquad |M-1|\le2\eta N^{-1}, \tag{9} \] every \(1-Q^j\) and \(\alpha_j\), \(1\le j<N\), remains a unit, with modulus at least half its root modulus. Indeed the change of either factor is at most \(C\eta/N\), whereas its root modulus is at least \(4\min(j,N-j)/N\). Decrease \(\eta\) once. Thus \[ |F_n(Q)|\ge (2N)^{-n}n! \tag{10} \] on (9). Uniformly there, the two normalized coefficients satisfy \[ \left|\frac{(-1)^n q^{n^2}h^n}{F_n(Q)}-\frac1{n!}\right| \le \frac{C^n n^2}{Nn!}, \qquad \left|\frac{q^nh^n}{F_n(Q)}-\frac{(-1)^n}{n!}\right| \le \frac{C^n n^2}{Nn!}. \tag{11} \] The right sides are zero at \(n=0\). To prove this, first take \(n\le N/2\). Each factor \[ \frac{-hj}{1-e^{hj}} \tag{12} \] is bounded by an absolute constant and differs from one by at most \(Cj/N\); the apparent value at \(hj=0\) is removable. Telescoping their product gives \(C^n n^2/N\). The additional phases \(e^{hn^2/2}\) and \(e^{hn/2}\) are uniformly bounded in modulus on (9) and differ from one by at most \(Cn^2/N\). This proves (11) in the first half. In the second half (10) and \(|h|\le C/N\) bound either normalized coefficient times \(n!\) by \(C^n\), while \(n^2/N\ge1/2\). Enlarging \(C\) proves (11) for that half too. It follows for every finite operator \(T\) with \(T^N=0\) and \(\|T\|\le R\) that \[ \|\Theta_N(hT)-e^T\|\le C_R/N,\qquad \|\Theta_N(hT)^{-1}-e^{-T}\|\le C_R/N. \tag{13} \] Both exponential series terminate. Sum (11) against \(R^n\); \(\sum n^2(CR)^n/n!\) is finite independently of \(N\). In particular both operators in (4) have uniformly bounded norms and inverses on such a family. Their least singular value is bounded below by \(1/(e^R+C_R/N)\). This is an operator statement; it does not bound an arbitrary prescribed scalar contraction below. ## 3. The two exact endpoint gauges Define diagonal matrices, all regular and invertible on (9), by \[ G_F w_a=F_a(Q)w_a,\qquad G_E w_a=H_a(Q,M)^{-1}w_a,\qquad H_a=\prod_{j=1}^a\alpha_j,\quad H_0=1. \tag{14} \] Direct coefficient calculation gives \[ G_F^{-1}FG_F=S,\qquad G_F^{-1}\mathcal E G_F\,w_a=\beta_a w_{a-1}, \quad \beta_a=(1-Q^a)\alpha_a, \tag{15} \] where \(S\) is the physical unilateral raising matrix, zero at \(d\). Similarly \[ G_E^{-1}\mathcal E G_E=S^*,\qquad G_E^{-1}FG_E\,w_a=\beta_{a+1}w_{a+1}\quad(a<d), \tag{16} \] and the last arrow is still zero. No factor at index \(N\) is inverted or used to replace that forced zero. At \(M=1,h=h_N\), \[ \beta_a=\frac{(1-Q^a)^2}{Q^a}=-4\sin^2(\pi a/N), \qquad H_a=Q^{-a(a+1)/2}F_a. \tag{17} \] Thus each gauge has E's endpoint condition-number bound, up to reversal: \[ \operatorname{cond}(G|_I) \le N\left(\frac{eN}{R}\right)^{2R} \tag{18} \] for an interval \(I=[0,R]\) or \([d-R,d]\), \(R\le d/2\); interpret the bracket as one for \(R=0\). In particular every collar \(R=o(N)\) has subexponential gauge cost. The same conclusion holds uniformly on (9), with an additional fixed power of \(N\). Each factor relative to its root value differs from one by at most \(C\eta/\min(j,N-j)\); it stays in a fixed disk away from zero. Summing its log-modulus over \(j<N\) costs at most \(C\log N\). This proves the extra polynomial bound for both the gauges and their inverses, including upper collars. Their fixed normal derivatives have the usual further polynomial cost by Cauchy's formula on smaller bidisks. One may use a globally tame change of head basis throughout the original network. For each chosen interval set \[ \widetilde G=G P_I+(I-P_I). \tag{18a} \] E's separate bounds for the gauge and its reciprocal, and the factor-ratio argument above, give \[ \|\widetilde G\|\,\|\widetilde G^{-1}\| \le N^{C}\left(\frac{eN}{R}\right)^{2R}. \tag{18b} \] This is subexponential for \(R=o(N)\). The internal interval arrows are exactly (15) or (16); interface arrows use their literal two endpoint gauge factors. The compressed operators below are therefore the same whether one uses \(G\) or \(\widetilde G\). No exponentially conditioned full-head change is needed to obtain them. All changes are exact source changes of basis: neighboring tensors carry the two inverse factors, exposed rows and columns transform, and diagonal pivots commute with the gauges. The transformation is not an equality of two independently reset boundary probes. ## 4. Monotone compression retains the exact cutoff Let \(I,J\) be single intervals of integer head indices and let \(P=P_I\otimes P_J\). In any of the diagonal gauges above, \(A\) moves \((a,b)\) to \((a-1,b+1)\), or is zero. If its initial and final indices lie in \(I\times J\), every intermediate index does. Therefore, exactly, \[ P A^n P=(PAP)^n\quad\hbox{on }\operatorname{im}P. \tag{19} \] This remains true when a transfer can exit the interval: it cannot return. Hence, writing \(T=PAP/h\) on that image, \[ P\Theta_N(A)P=\Theta_N(hT),\qquad P\Theta_N(A)^{-1}P=\Theta_N(hT)^{-1}. \tag{20} \] The two compressed factors are exact inverses, not merely asymptotic ones. The union of an upper and a lower collar is not a single interval and is not covered by (19); its cross-collar blocks remain. There are two useful bounded-generator regimes. Constants in the following bounds may depend on the fixed collar constants. Every collar width also satisfies \(0\le R_i\le\lfloor d/2\rfloor\): * **One quadratic zero.** Use \(G_F\) on the donor, leave the recipient balanced, and take the donor interval to be a lower or upper collar of width \(R_1\le C_1N^{1/2}\). The recipient interval may be any physical interval, including the whole head. On (9), \[ \|T\|\le C(R_1+1)^2/N\le C'. \tag{21} \] * **Two quadratic zeros.** Use \(G_F\) on the donor and \(G_E\) on the recipient. Let both intervals be lower or upper collars, of widths \(R_i\le C_iN^{3/4}\). Then \[ \|T\|\le C(R_1+1)^2(R_2+1)^2/N^3\le C'. \tag{22} \] For the proof, on either donor collar \(|\beta_a|\le C(R_1+1)^2/N^2\), and on either recipient collar \(|\beta_{b+1}|\le C(R_2+1)^2/N^2\). These estimates follow directly from (9) and (15)--(17), including the actual zero endpoint arrows. The unchanged balanced \(F\) has norm bounded by an absolute constant on (9). A weighted transfer is an injective partial shift of basis vectors, so its norm is the maximum coefficient. Finally \(|h|^{-1}\le CN\). This proves (21)--(22). Apply (13) to obtain the claimed uniform exponential transitions and uniform inverses on all these compressed blocks. For a checked positive crossing the output projector is \(\mathsf P P\mathsf P\). The exact remaining factor is \(\kappa\mathsf P D\). At the physical complete root it is unitary in the gauged coordinate norm, since its diagonal entries have modulus one. Thus the corresponding compressed actual checked block is uniformly invertible as a map between these two projected spaces. The negative block, with the input/output spaces exchanged, is exactly its inverse. Away from that fiber the entire \(D,\kappa\) factors are retained; no normal of them is omitted by the Euler estimate. ## 5. Finite projectors, outgoing blocks and normal rows The gauge is diagonal and does not change \(P_I\). Its exact root Fourier kernel is \[ (P_I)_{jk}^{\mathrm{Fourier}} =\frac1N\sum_{a=L}^{U}Q^{a(k-j)}. \tag{23} \] Keeping the same unwrapped ratio \(t\) gives the finite polynomial \[ \frac1N t^L K_{U-L}(t),\qquad K_R(t)=\sum_{a=0}^R t^a,\qquad K_R(1)=R+1. \tag{24} \] Both endpoints, and the upper-collar power \(t^{d-R}\), remain. No delta-function matching or independent cancellation of the two apparent \(1-t\) poles is part of (13). The full crossing is not replaced by its compressed block. Its four \(P,(I-P)\) blocks are kept exactly. In particular the unestimated outgoing/incoming currents can be written without changing a coefficient: \[ [\Theta_N(A),P] =\sum_{n=1}^{d}\frac{(-1)^nq^{n^2}}{F_n(Q)} \sum_{j=0}^{n-1}A^j[A,P]A^{n-1-j}. \tag{25} \] The elementary \([A,P]\) is supported on the interval-edge arrows; the surrounding powers can transport it far outside the collar. No small bound for (25) or for an unrestricted exterior follows. The actual head-normal rows also remain. In V's ambient module, put \[ \delta=1-Q^N,\qquad w=MQ^{-N}-M^{-1},\qquad \rho=q-q^{-1},\qquad K_Hw_a=xQ^{-a}w_a. \tag{26} \] Here \(U=|N\rangle\langle d|\), \(L=|d\rangle\langle N|\) are the two ambient head/tail arrows, and \(P_d=|d\rangle\langle d|\). The head projector \(P_H\) satisfies \[ [F,P_H]=\delta U,\qquad [\mathcal E,P_H]=-wL,\qquad [\mathcal E_H,F_H]-\rho(K_H-K_H^{-1}) =-\delta w\,P_d. \tag{27} \] Extend a head gauge by the identity on the tail, rather than attempting to invert a factorial at \(N\). The transformed rows are exactly \(\delta U G\) and \(-wG^{-1}L\); their product retains the same diagonal head projector. The original marked source and co-source transform with them. This gives a regular full normal-germ prescription, without erasing either wall or their mixed normal. There is also a quantitative fixed-jet statement for the compressed transition itself. On a smaller concentric bidisk, (13) and Cauchy's formula imply for fixed \(j,\ell\ge0\) \[ \left\|\partial_h^j\partial_M^\ell \bigl(\Theta_N(hT_N)-e^{T_N}\bigr)\right\| \le C_{j,\ell}N^{2j+\ell-1}, \tag{28} \] and the same assertion for the inverse. The matrices \(T_N\), including their gauges, are differentiated as whole analytic functions. Thus the error is \(O(N^{-1})\) for the corresponding scaled normals. The genuine ordinary-color path \(M=-e^{Nh/2}\) lies in (9) on a smaller \(h\)-disk of radius proportional to \(N^{-2}\). Restricting the exact identities first therefore retains its actual fixed-\(N\) quantum normals. A fixed-\(M\) auxiliary array is not declared a generic representation. ## 6. The scalar Poisson profile requires an explicit packet The paid unconditional conclusion is the operator \(e^{T_N}\) with the original finite projection. A scalar \(e^\xi\) requires more. For example suppose a normalized incoming packet \(v_N\) lies in \(\operatorname{im}P\), \(|\xi_N|\le R\), and satisfies \[ \|(T_N-\xi_N)v_N\|\le\varepsilon_N. \tag{29} \] Then the integral identity for the difference of two exponentials and the uniform bound for \(T_N\) give \[ \|\Theta_N(hT_N)v_N-e^{\xi_N}v_N\| \le C_R(\varepsilon_N+N^{-1}). \tag{30} \] This is a precise sufficient packet hypothesis. It is not assumed for the original neighboring tangle, and (30) does not control the discarded-output blocks in (25). The quadratic and quartic geometric contacts motivate the collar scales in (21)--(22); the proof itself uses only the literal matrix coefficients and the displayed width conditions. It does not choose which geometric endpoint, normal contour or relative framing interval occurs in the original global state. Uniform invertibility of this local compressed transition is not a lower bound for the knot scalar. ## Complete proof-source pins * B: notes/balanced_verma_coherent_braiding.md, SHA256 0203bdd7dbb36a4f8deb1c310b3445608e53d10922049447da8eecec4f87d1c4. * E: notes/actual_endpoint_head_factorial_chart.md, SHA256 5cea9fc9b738c68e77b8d86b0445d4110df14f614b333032ba87faa98bff1b0c. * V: notes/common_verma_two_wall_source.md, SHA256 b94f53c2f92840a3817af0619e1a7ec0c6e73403f0ea01463c7bc3d27878d1fd. All three complete directs were read nontruncated in the current author sequence and their used implications checked. The q-Hahn partner/fold statements were inspected for coverage only: their spectral-channel collision estimates do not give the operator transition proved here. Only written mathematics and text operations were used. Frozen and public files are unchanged.

title: An actual coherent chart for each capped Euler coproduct factor
The original crossing in the coupled flag Euler exchange
text: # The original crossing in the coupled flag Euler exchange Research note, 22 November 2026. This identifies the nilpotent factor of the original complete crossing in the physical flag coordinates of [D]. The factor moves the multiplicity clock, and participates in both the existing cyclic and marked full-dilogarithm exchanges. All identities hold on the complete two-head space and preserve arbitrary exteriors. Pascal/Gaussian factorizations of the original crossing already appear in [C, Section 6.1]. The additional identification here is the explicit operator \(X\) in the actual coupled flags, and its exchanges with the same cyclic and full functions used in [A,P]. This does not match every remaining nine-cell factor or give a geometric scalar lower bound. ## 1. The actual flags and the new nilpotent argument Use the complete balanced heads and conventions of [D]: \[ N\geq2,\quad d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\quad x=-q^{-1},\quad\lambda=x^{-1}=-q,\quad F_h=(Q;Q)_h . \tag{1} \] The auxiliary flag wraps are \(S_1^N=1\), \(S_2^N=(-1)^d\). Keep the original positive checked crossing as \(\kappa W\), where \(\kappa\) is its unchanged common Cartan/source scalar. Thus \(W\) is exactly the stripped matrix of [A, (11)], with \(W|0,0\rangle=|0,0\rangle\). Its full negative inverse is \(\kappa^{-1}W^{-1}\). The actual cup and averaged marked row remain \[ p=N\sum_{a=0}^d x^{a-d}|a,d-a\rangle,\qquad \ell|a,b\rangle=x^b/N^2,\qquad \ell p=1. \tag{2} \] Retain the original flag operators \[ \Delta=Z_1(\lambda S_2-S_1),\quad \gamma=-e_2K_1,\quad v=Z_2^{-1}+S_1e_2,\quad M=Z_1Z_2v,\quad S=S_1v^{-1}. \tag{3} \] Here \(M\) is the multiplicity clock, not a peripheral meridian eigenvalue. Here \(v^N=M^N=S^N=1\), \(\Delta^N=0\), \(\Delta v=Qv\Delta\), and \(M\) commutes with \(\Delta,v\). The original \(S_1\) commutes with \(v\), and \(\Delta S_1=QS_1\Delta\), so \([S,\Delta]=0\). Define the physical nilpotent operator \[ X=(1-Q^{-1}M^{-1})\Delta S^{-1}. \tag{4} \] For clarity, these formulas have a completely explicit coordinate meaning. In the rescaled frame \(\widetilde{\mathcal B}\) of [D, (27)], \[ \begin{gathered} v=Z_s,\quad M=Z_m,\quad S=S_m,\quad S_1=S_mv,\\ X|m,s\rangle=(1-Q^{-m})(1-Q^{1-s}) |m-1,s-1\rangle . \end{gathered} \tag{5} \] Indices in (5) are cyclic, and the displayed zero coefficients are retained. The identity for \(S_1\) follows by applying \(S_1\Delta^a=Q^{-a}\Delta^aS_1\) to the columns \(\Delta^a|m,0\rangle/F_a\). Formula (5) proves \(X^N=0\), \([X,\Delta]=0\), and \(Xv=QvX\). The physical space still has dimension \(N^2\). Let \(E_j(v)\) denote the \(v=Q^j\) projectors, with \(E_N=E_0\), and set \[ \mathcal G=\sum_{j=1}^N g_jE_j(v),\qquad g_j=(-1)^{j-1}Q^{j(j-1)/2},\qquad g_N=1. \tag{6} \] It is unitary in the fixed positive Gram of [D], and commutes with \(M,S_1,v\). Its consecutive ratios give \[ \mathcal G\Delta\mathcal G^{-1}=-Q\Delta v^{-1}. \tag{7} \] The sole exceptional marked transition has input \(v=Q\); its \(\Delta\)-arrow is zero in the original physical module. No cyclic arrow has been dropped to impose (7). ## 2. Exact crossing factorization on the full space For a nilpotent argument \(Y^N=0\), write \[ P_N(Y)=\sum_{h=0}^d\frac{(-1)^hQ^{h(h-1)/2}}{F_h}Y^h, \qquad \mathcal E_N(Y)=\sum_{h=0}^dY^h/F_h=P_N(Y)^{-1}. \tag{8} \] The inverse follows from the finite \(Q\)-binomial theorem in every degree below \(N\); higher degrees vanish. No \(F_N\) is divided out. The original crossing has the factorization \[ \boxed{\qquad W=\mathcal G\mathcal E_N(X),\qquad W^{-1}=P_N(X)\mathcal G^{-1}.\qquad} \tag{9} \] Here is a full-space proof from the actual Hurwitz identities. Directly from (5), \[ [X,S_1]=(1-Q^{-1})\Delta v,\qquad X(\Delta v)=Q(\Delta v)X . \tag{10} \] Thus \[ [X^h,S_1]=-Q^{-1}(1-Q^h)\Delta vX^{h-1}, \qquad 1\leq h\leq d. \tag{11} \] Summing (11) with the coefficients of (8), the only truncated top correction is \(\Delta vX^d/F_d=0\), because it contains \(\Delta^N\). Therefore \[ \mathcal E_N(X)S_1\mathcal E_N(X)^{-1} =S_1-Q^{-1}\Delta v,\qquad [\mathcal E_N(X),\Delta]=0. \tag{12} \] For \(A_*=\mathcal G\mathcal E_N(X)\), equations (7),(12) give \[ A_*S_1A_*^{-1}=S_1+\Delta,\qquad A_*\Delta A_*^{-1}=-Q\Delta v^{-1}. \tag{13} \] These are precisely the original identities for \(W\): the first is [A, (10)], and the second is obtained by subtracting \(t_2\) from \(t_3\) in [A, (15)]. Both \(A_*\) and \(W\) fix \(|0,0\rangle\): this is also the frame's \(|0,0\rangle\) column, so \(X\) kills it, and its clock value is \(v=1\), where \(g_N=1\). Their identical first conjugation implies equality on every \(S_1^m|0,0\rangle=|m,0\rangle\). Their identical second conjugation then implies equality on every \(\Delta^a|m,0\rangle/F_a\). These \(N^2\) vectors form the complete invertible frame of [D, (27)]. This proves (9), including every endpoint and both parities, without an unspecified intertwiner scalar or a semisimple quotient. The resulting clock updates are also explicit: \[ WvW^{-1}=v+X,\qquad WXW^{-1}=-QXv^{-1},\qquad WMW^{-1}=M+(Z_1Z_2)X . \tag{14} \] Indeed \(\mathcal E_N(X)v\mathcal E_N(X)^{-1}=v(1-X)\) by the finite Euler recurrence, and \(\mathcal GX\mathcal G^{-1}=-QXv^{-1}\) by (4),(7). The actual crossing preserves \(Z_1Z_2\). In particular the new factor is not confined to the commutant of \(M\). The completed flag shift also has a closed transport. Put \(B_0=(1-Q^{-1}M^{-1})S^{-1}\), so \(X=B_0\Delta\). It is a first-coordinate nilpotent, \(B_0^N=0\), and commutes with \(\gamma\). Indeed \(M\) does, while the opposite phase factors in \(S_1\gamma=Q\gamma S_1\) and \(v\gamma=Q\gamma v\) cancel in \(S\). Consequently \[ [X,\gamma]=\lambda(1-Q^{-1})B_0v,\qquad \mathcal E_N(X)\gamma\mathcal E_N(X)^{-1} =\gamma-\lambda Q^{-1}B_0v . \tag{14a} \] The same sum as in (11),(12) proves this, with top term \(B_0vX^d=0\) because it contains \(B_0^N\). The Gaussian ratios give \(\mathcal G\gamma\mathcal G^{-1}=-\gamma v\); the exceptional \(v=1\) arrow of \(\gamma\) is physically zero. For the original completion of [D, (9)], write \(c_*=[(-\lambda)^dF_d]^{-1}\). Then \[ \gamma':=W\gamma W^{-1}=-\gamma v-\lambda Q^{-1}B_0v,\qquad W\Gamma W^{-1}=\gamma'+c_*\Delta^d . \tag{14b} \] Its rank-\(N\) corner is unchanged: \(E_1(v)\Delta^d=\Delta^d\), and \(( -Q\Delta v^{-1})^d=\Delta^dv=\Delta^d\). The scalar is \((-1)^dQ^{d(d+1)/2}=1\), including even \(N\); the last equality uses \(\Delta^d(v-1)=\lambda^{-1}\Delta^N\gamma=0\). Thus all these updates retain the actual completion, not just the nilpotent arrows. In particular the retained commutator \(O_t\) of [D, (23)] transports explicitly. Using the primed operators in (14),(14b), put \[ \mathcal U'=\sum_{m=0}^dE_m(M')(\Gamma')^m,\qquad WO_tW^{-1}=\mathfrak d_N(tv')(\mathcal U')^{-1} \mathfrak d_N(tv')^{-1}\mathcal U'. \tag{14c} \] All root marks are transported with the same clock labels. The right side has no unspecified \(W\)-conjugate. An actual observation uses the inverse-dual row \(\eta W^{-1}\) and column \(WY\); no bound on that row or on a common Gram for overlapping pairs is asserted. ## 3. The cyclic and marked full exchanges with the actual crossing On the marked Fermat cover \(t\beta\ne0\), \(\beta^N=1-t^N\), let \(\mathcal C_t=\mathfrak d_N(tv)\) be exactly the cyclic matrix of [A, (22)] and [D, (14)]. Its functional equation and \(Xv=QvX\) give \[ \mathcal C_tX\mathcal C_t^{-1} =\beta^{-1}X(1-Q^{-1}tv). \tag{15} \] The two summands on the right \(Q\)-commute. Their finite Euler factorization is the mixed identity of [A], now on this explicit argument from the original crossing. Inverting it reverses the order. Since \(\mathcal C_t\) commutes with \(\mathcal G\), (9) gives \[ \boxed{\quad \mathcal C_tW= \mathcal G\,\mathcal E_N(-\beta^{-1}Q^{-1}tXv) \mathcal E_N(\beta^{-1}X)\,\mathcal C_t . \quad} \tag{16} \] Every argument has nilpotent degree \(N\); apparent higher degrees in the product vanish, rather than requiring a cyclic replacement. The same \(\mathcal C_t\), with its full scalar and root marks, occurs once on both sides. The full crossing is obtained by retaining the original multiplier \(\kappa\). There is also a nonsingular physical-root version. Use the marked matrix \(F_v\) of [P, (10)--(12)], not a separate specialization of the singular \(\beta^{-1}\) factors: \[ F_v=\phi_N\sum_{j=1}^N\frac{E_j(v)}{F_{j-1}},\qquad \phi_N=\sqrt N\exp\!\left\{i\pi\left[ \frac14-\frac{N+N^{-1}}{12}\right]\right\}. \tag{17} \] The exact relation \(F_v\Delta F_v^{-1}=\Delta(1-Q^{-1}v)\), and the commuting factors of (4), imply \(F_vXF_v^{-1}=X(1-Q^{-1}v)\). Hence \[ \boxed{\qquad F_vW=\mathcal G\,\mathcal E_N(-Q^{-1}Xv) \mathcal E_N(X)\,F_v . \qquad} \tag{18} \] This equality retains the marked \(j=N\) value of the full function. It is not obtained by identifying its top and bottom logarithmic marks. ## 4. Original source and exterior scope The source identities \(\Delta p=0\), \(vp=Qp\), and \(Mp=p\) imply \(Xp=0\), \(\mathcal Gp=p\). Consequently the literal original pairings are \[ \ell\mathcal C_tWp=\mathfrak d_N(tQ),\qquad \ell F_vWp=\phi_N . \tag{19} \] For the full crossing they are multiplied by the unchanged \(\kappa\). No scalar on either side of (16) or (18) has been reset to one. More generally, (9),(16),(18) preserve every actual two-head exterior row and input tensor, before any further sums or relative integrals. The exterior remains attached; (19) does not replace it by a special cap. Original turns, pivots, framing and peripheral factors remain unchanged outside these operator equalities. All \(N\) coordinates of each physical head are retained. This gives an actual crossing factor, not merely a pure-\(\Delta\) oscillator identity. It does not assert that distinct overlapping crossings use one common flag frame or one positive Gram with tame transition norms. Nor does it identify the remaining complete nine-cell tensor with the right side of (16), or authorize cancelling its exteriors. No global geometric period, sharp whole-source bound, or nonvanishing of the original general closing is proved here. ## Complete proof sources and coverage - [D] [The retained Pachner ratio in the original physical flag algebra](research_retained_pachner_ratio_physical_flags.md), 365 lines, SHA-256 650d25db94060e306464ae00ef92ceb1e51ba4bec53da2c15ee67a89113be21a. - [A] [Actual shared quantum flags and their charged exchange](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_shared_quantum_flags_and_charged_exchange.md), 459 lines, SHA-256 dcab795cc141e2e1db726998cf7b1141dd03c681eaae9076387f90581f53a7d9. - [P] [The full dilogarithm resolves the actual charged flag pentagon at the root](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_marked_full_phi_flag_pentagon.md), 328 lines, SHA-256 3052cef4a1d666253562c13ceaf6a9bc472baf7691f23d13e33bb3f8d6e9888f. [C] [An explicit coherent Gram for an actual split source](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_pascal_coherent_gram.md), 494 lines, SHA-256 b6e6d697b4e21d30ca683f265b9c41170a0bee424d783169b2e0c70233dc889e, is coverage only. It already proves an exact original crossing Pascal/Gaussian alphabet. No novelty is claimed for that factorization method; the proof above identifies its needed physical flag argument and the actual cyclic/full exchange, with literal source normalization.
