# The actual Gauss kernel's rational collective graph Private written proof, 18 November 2026. The fixed-width coherent estimate K has a specific canonical graph. After fixing total occupation and dividing the common diagonal frame, that graph is a rational collective conjugation of the actual dressed meridians. We identify it by its initialized coherent boundary and the proved analytic uniqueness in K. We do not infer it by substituting classical symbols into a high-degree matrix function. The rational map extends farther than the estimated kernel. In particular it has an algebraic continuation to the regular geometric opposite-frame problem. Its generating projection, its marked primitive, and the coefficient of an original relative cycle are separate issues. The complete directs K, R, L are pinned below. ## 1. Literal polarizations and the classical tensor variables Retain K's root conventions \[ c_0=2\pi i,\quad Q=e^{c_0/N},\quad q=Q^{1/2},\quad x=-q^{-1},\quad d=N-1. 	ag{1} \] There are \(r\) remaining heads. On fixed degree \(T\le d\), put \(\sigma=(T+1)/N\in I\Subset(1/2,1)\), \(C=e^{-c_0\sigma}\). All classical formulas below use the principal value \(x=-1\). Their total Cartan is \(K_{m tot}=(-1)^rC\). Write a head's occupation as \(p\) and \(a=e^{-c_0p}\). For a monomial output row, the actual principal symbols are \[ K=-a,\qquad E=w^{-1}(a-1),\qquad F=w(1-a^{-1}). 	ag{2} \] For the ordinary-binomial input \(c(z)=\sum_{b=0}^d inom db z^b w_b\), the literal right action gives \[  oxed{\quad K=-a,\qquad E=z rac{1-p}{p}(a-1),\qquad F=z^{-1} rac p{1-p}(1-a^{-1}). \quad} 	ag{3} \] These are continued in their resolved charts at removable endpoints. For example \[  rac{(Ec(z))_b}{c(z)_b} =z rac{d-b}{b+1}(Q^{-b-1}-1). \] This proves the \(E\) row in (3); the other row follows from \((Fc)_b=(1-Q^b)c_{b-1}\). K's weighted-row operators \(R_{Ev}\), \(R_{Fv}\) have the reciprocal expressions. They act on the transpose leg. Exactly at this root, \[ E^t=-qKF,\qquad F^t=-qK^{-1}E. 	ag{4} \] For example their raising coefficient is \(Q^{-b}(1-Q^b)=Q^{-b}-1\). Consequently K's weighted-row characteristic equations are unchanged; extracting the underlying input tuple requires (3), not replacing its physical input momentum by that of the transpose row. The actual suffix Casimir is symmetric in this root basis: for a transfer from head \(j\) to head \(i<j\), its coefficient and the reversed coefficient are both \[ K_{<i}^{-1}K_{>j} (1-Q^{a_i+1})(Q^{-a_j}-1). \] In the reversed calculation the intermediate Cartans cancel and leave \(Q^{a_i-a_j+1}Q^{-a_i-1}=Q^{-a_j}\). The diagonal is unchanged. Thus passing from K's transposed suffix rows to the actual input tuple (3) preserves their symbols in precisely the order used below. In R's factorial convention the momentum is \[ \pi_{m out}=1/w,\qquad \pi_{m in}=z(1-p)/p,\qquad E=(a-1)\pi,\quad F=(1-a^{-1})/\pi. 	ag{5} \] These formulas fix both coherent polarizations used here. For each physical head define \[ b_i^-= egin{pmatrix}1&0\-K_iF_i&K_i\end{pmatrix}, \quad b_i^+= egin{pmatrix}K_i&E_i\0&1\end{pmatrix}, \quad G_i=(b_i^-)^{-1}b_i^+. \] Put \(B_j^-=b_j^-\cdots b_1^-\) and \[ H_i=(B_{i-1}^-)^{-1}G_iB_{i-1}^-. \] Then the ordered product and its trace are \[ P=H_r\cdots H_1 = egin{pmatrix}K&E\KF&K^{-1}+EF\end{pmatrix}, \qquad \Omega=\operatorname{tr}P=K+K^{-1}+EF, 	ag{6} \] where \(E=\sum_iE_i\prod_{j>i}K_j\) and \(F=\sum_i(\prod_{j<i}K_j^{-1})F_i\). The physical meridians are \(-H_i\); their flags are the same. ## 2. A rational collective map and its marked flow On independent heads the brackets obtained from the literal root commutators are \[ \{\log K_i,E_i\}=E_i,\qquad \{\log K_i,F_i\}=-F_i,\qquad \{E_i,F_i\}=K_i-K_i^{-1}. 	ag{7} \] The individual \(E_iF_i+K_i+K_i^{-1}\) are Casimirs. Let \(D_0=\operatorname{diag}(1/2,-1/2)\). The following dressing identities hold for every based \(H_i\): \[  egin{split} \{\log K,H_i\}&=[D_0,H_i],\ \{E,H_i\}&=[K e_{21},H_i],\ \{F,H_i\}&=[e_{12}-F D_0,H_i]. \end{split} 	ag{8} \] Here all unindexed variables are the full ordered totals. For an explicit verification, start with one head and substitute (6) in (7). The first entries in the last two rows are respectively \(-K(H_i)_{12}\) and \((H_i)_{21}\); the remaining entries follow from the displayed \(E,F,K\) brackets. For old based heads the induction passes immediately through an additional independent head, denoted by lower-case \(k,e,f\): \[ K_{m new}=Kk,\qquad E_{m new}=Ek+e,\qquad F_{m new}=F+K^{-1}f. \] For the new based head write \(B=\left( egin{smallmatrix} 1&0\-KF&K\end{smallmatrix}ight)\) and \(H=B^{-1}G_{m head}B\). The product rule gives \(\{X,H\}=B^{-1}(\{X,G_{m head}\}+[G_{m head},V_X])B\), where \(V_X=\{X,B\}B^{-1}\). Direct use of (7) gives \[ V_{\log K_{m new}}= egin{pmatrix}0&0\KF&0\end{pmatrix}, \quad V_{E_{m new}}= k egin{pmatrix}0&0\1-K^2&-E\end{pmatrix}, \quad V_{F_{m new}}=  egin{pmatrix}0&0\-Ff&F\end{pmatrix}. \] The corresponding commutator matrices for \(\{X,G_{m head}\}\) are \(D_0,\ k(ED_0+e_{21}),\ K^{-1}(e_{12}-fD_0)\). Subtract \(V_X\) and conjugate by \(B\). The results, up to scalar matrices, are \(D_0,\ Kk e_{21},\ e_{12}-(F+K^{-1}f)D_0\). These are exactly (8) for the new totals. This completes the induction without a Poisson reduction premise. By differentiating \(\Omega=FE+K+K^{-1}\), (8) gives \[ \{\Omega,H_i\}=[P,H_i],\qquad \{\log K,\Omega\}=0. 	ag{9} \] Indeed its commutator matrix is \(FK e_{21}+E e_{12}+(K-K^{-1}-EF)D_0=P-\Omega I/2\). Thus the trace Hamiltonian is a collective centralizer motion, not a separate conjugation chosen independently at each head. For a local marked primitive introduce \[ \Omega=z+z^{-1},\qquad u=(Kz)^{-1},\quad v=z/K. \] Choose consistent logarithms and dilogarithms on a simply connected regular patch. The factorial Hamiltonian is \[ {\cal H}_A=c_0\Log K+ \operatorname{Li}_2(u)+\operatorname{Li}_2(v) -\operatorname{Li}_2(uv)-\operatorname{Li}_2(1). 	ag{10} \] It is the scalar factorial primitive of L, including the leading \(K^d\) character. Explicitly, with \(I(x)=[\operatorname{Li}_2(1)-\operatorname{Li}_2(e^{c_0x})]/c_0\), the ratio has phase \(I(x+y)-I(x)-I(y)\); multiplying by \(c_0\) and adding \(c_0\Log K\) gives (10). Equation (10) is not asserted to be the coherent kernel obtained by evaluating a high-degree operator at its symbol. Its derivatives are \[  egin{split} \partial_{\log z}{\cal H}_A &=\Log(1-u)-\Log(1-v),\ \partial_{\log K}{\cal H}_A &=c_0+\Log b,\qquad b= rac{(1-u)(1-v)}{(1-uv)^2} =- rac{EF}{K(1-K^{-2})^2}. \end{split} 	ag{11} \] For the kernel convention \(v(w)A c(z)\), the canonical map is the inverse Heisenberg flow. The actual inverse-free relation \[ A_N(K,\Omega)E=E A_N(QK,\Omega) \] follows from \(KE=QEK\). On a local nonzero scalar or amplitude branch with Hamiltonian (10), its ratio fixes \(E_{m out}=\exp(-\partial_{\log K}{\cal H}_A)E_{m in}\). No global inverse of \(A_N\) is used: L's upper primary root channels are zero. By (9), the centralizer part of that flow is \(\exp[-(\partial_\Omega{\cal H}_A)P]\). Its eigenvalue ratio is \[ \exp[-(z-z^{-1})\partial_\Omega{\cal H}_A] = rac{1-v}{1-u}. \] It is therefore projectively \(I-P/K\). The commuting Cartan part is \(\operatorname{diag}(b^{-1},1)\). Dividing their product by \(1-K^{-2}\) gives the entirely rational representative \[  oxed{\quad g_A= egin{pmatrix} 0&d_0/F\ -F/d_0&1-EF/(K d_0) \end{pmatrix},\qquad d_0=1-K^{-2},\qquad \det g_A=1. \quad} 	ag{12} \] In particular the map is \(H_i\mapsto g_AH_ig_A^{-1}\), and \[  oxed{\quad K'=K,\qquad E'=-K d_0^2/F,\qquad F'=-EF^2/(K d_0^2),\qquad \Omega'=\Omega. \quad} 	ag{13} \] Every prefix or suffix trace is preserved. Formula (12) extends to \(F(K^2-1)
e0\), even at \(E=0\) or \(\Omega=\pm2\). It maps this chart birationally to \(E'
e0,\ K^2
e1\). It is canonical on its regular logarithmic domain by (8)--(11); the identity of the rational symplectic forms extends wherever both rational charts are defined. Recovering individual head Gauss coordinates additionally requires their relevant prefix pivots. At fixed \(K\), the diagonal factor in (11) is the common frame being quotiented. The projective map is already represented by \(I-P/K\) on the smaller \(EF
e0\) chart. A function of \(K\) added to (10) changes the unquotiented common-moment seam and does not change this projective graph. ## 3. Matching the actual initialized coherent boundary We now identify (12) with K's estimated graph; the preceding Hamiltonian calculation alone would not identify an actual branch. Use K's ordinary-binomial boundary saddle, at output \(ho_1=\cdots=ho_{r-1}=0\). To avoid confusing it with (11), call the binomial saddle \(U\). Put \[ p_i= rac{U\xi_i}{t+U\xi_i},\quad P_s=\sum_{i<r}p_i=t\phi'(t;C),\quad p_r=\sigma-P_s,\quad U= rac{p_r}{1-p_r}. \] Set \[ A_i=e^{-c_0p_i},\quad R=A_r= rac{CY}{1-t},\quad C Y^2-(1+C-t)Y+1-Ct=0,\quad Y(0)=1. 	ag{14} \] These are the actual selected functions proved in K's complete initialized boundary, not a new spectral interpolation. Let \(\varepsilon=(-1)^r\), \(a=z_r/U\), and \(P_0=-\varepsilon t a\). Then (3) gives, for \(i<r\), \[ \pi_i=(-1)^{r-i}ta,\qquad \pi_r=a . 	ag{15} \] Write \(B_i=\prod_{k\le i}A_k\), \(B_0=1\). The first \(r-1\) dressed input meridians are exactly \[ H_i=-I+(B_i-B_{i-1}){\cal N}(P_0),\qquad {\cal N}(p)= egin{pmatrix}-1&p\-p^{-1}&1\end{pmatrix}. 	ag{16} \] For verification the partial lowering sum before head \(i\) is \[ F_{<i}= rac{(-1)^{r-1}}{ta}(1-B_{i-1}^{-1}). \] Consequently \((B_{i-1}^-)^{-1}[\pi_i:1]\) is \([P_0:1]\), and the upper-right entry of the conjugated nilpotent is \(P_0B_{i-1}\). This proves (16), including its signs. The full totals of this boundary tuple are \[  egin{split} K&=\varepsilon C,\ E&=a[(1-t)R+tC-1]=a[CY+tC-1],\ F&=- rac{\varepsilon}{aCt} [C-t-(1-t)R] =- rac{\varepsilon}{aCt}[C-t-CY]. \end{split} 	ag{17} \] Their trace is \(\Omega=\varepsilon\lambda_G(t)\), where \[ \lambda_G(t)=C(1+Y)+t . 	ag{18} \] Substitution of (14) checks this last equality directly. The condition \((I-P/K)[P_0,1]^t\in\mathbb C e_1\) is \[ (1-CY)(C-t-CY)=(C^2-1)t. \] After division by \(C\), it is precisely the quadratic (14). Thus the actual branch \(Y(0)=1\), rather than the other root, is mapped by (12) to the output vacuum flags. It is useful to verify the covectors as well. If \(g_A[P_0,1]^t\) lies on \(e_1\), direct rank-one conjugation gives \[ g_A{\cal N}(P_0)g_A^{-1} = rac{d_0^2}{P_0F^2}e_{12}. 	ag{19} \] At output vacuum the first \(r-1\) head Cartans are \(-1\), their lowerings vanish, and \[ F'=(-1)^{r-1}w_r(1-C^{-1}). \] Using (13) recovers its \(w_r\) in the same representative. Let \[ D_*=- rac{(1-t)^2R(R-1)}{t c_0(C-1)C}. \] Equations (14),(17) imply \[  rac{d_0^2 w_r}{P_0F^2} =-c_0(-1)^{r-1}D_*. 	ag{20} \] For example the only quadratic simplification needed is \(CY+tC-1=Y(CY-1+t)\), which is (14). In the monomial output polarization (2), a based head at this axis has upper-right entry \(-c_0(-1)^{r-1}S_{ho_i}/w_r\). Equations (16),(19),(20) therefore give exactly \[ S_{ho_i}(0,\xi)=D_*(B_i-B_{i-1}), 	ag{21} \] the initialized gradients K proves from the actual finite matrix. The input gradients are the same \(p_i\) as its boundary saddle. This matches both sides of the initialized canonical relation. For completeness this initial comparison determines a local graph, not merely a set of special points. The preimage of the output vacuum Lagrangian under the canonical map (12) is smooth. Equations (14)--(16) parametrize it on the chosen small branch. Its map to the input \(\xi_i\) is locally invertible: K proves \[ \xi_i=k(P_s) rac{p_i}{1-p_i},\qquad k(P_s)= rac{P_s}{(2/c_0)\sigma/(1-\sigma)}(1+O(P_s)), \] with Jacobian \(2(P_s/[(2/c_0)\sigma/(1-\sigma)])^{r-1}(1+O(P_s))
e0\). Thus the graph has an analytic mixed generating function near the axis. Set its boundary constant equal to K's actual \(\psi(\xi)\). Collective conjugation preserves all the suffix traces in K's principal reverse equations. Its generating function therefore satisfies those same principal rows. K's convergent coefficient recursion, with its nonzero low diagonal and prescribed boundary, proves analytic uniqueness. Hence this generating function is K's actual \(S\) on a sufficiently small connected subchart. Analytic identity extends the equality over the connected portion of that estimated chart on which these generating coordinates are regular. **Conclusion.** The canonical graph of the genuine nonzero-amplitude kernel in K, after the fixed-degree common-frame quotient, is (12). Its phase and coefficient are still K's initialized ones. This proof does not extend that coefficient estimate by rational continuation. ## 4. The geometric opposite-frame criterion Here is an explicit target for comparison with the original source. R's complete \(F_\Sigma=0\) section has first meridian and full product \[ H_1^0= egin{pmatrix}-1&0\-F&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad P_{m full}= egin{pmatrix}-K&E\0&-K^{-1}\end{pmatrix}. 	ag{22} \] The selected first-meridian flag is \(e_2\); the selected total flag is \(e_1\). If \(K^2
e1\), the other total eigenline is \([E/(K-K^{-1}):1]\). It differs from the meridian flag exactly when \(E
e0\). Keeping that meridian flag, the change to the opposite total eigenflag induces on the remaining tuple the common conjugation \[  oxed{\qquad \ell= egin{pmatrix}1&0\(K-K^{-1})/E&1\end{pmatrix}, \qquad (K,E,F)\longmapsto(K^{-1},E,F). \qquad} 	ag{23} \] To verify the actual framing, R gives \(H_{i+1}^{m full}=h_0H_i h_0^{-1}\), with \(h_0=\left( egin{smallmatrix}1&0\F&-1\end{smallmatrix}ight)\). The full-frame change is \(\left( egin{smallmatrix}1&0\-(K-K^{-1})/E&1\end{smallmatrix}ight)\). Conjugating it by \(h_0=h_0^{-1}\) gives (23). Direct multiplication verifies the new total entries. For complete discrete faithful holonomy with regular total product, R proves that this product is loxodromic and that neither of its eigenlines can equal a nontrivial parabolic meridian flag. Hence \(E
e0\); also \(F
e0\), since \(H_1^0\) is noncentral. Thus both (12) and (23) have algebraically regular representatives at the relevant geometric frame. The unit conditions persist in a sufficiently small holonomy neighborhood. This last observation is not a quantum meridian-normal estimate. These are different maps: \(A_N\) preserves the tail \(K\), whereas the opposite kernel reverses it. The original routing is exactly \[ T=\mathcal B_m(W_	au^{-1})\,A_N\,D_{m top}\,\mathscr C_r, \qquad J_{m op}=D_N(MK)^{-1}T . 	ag{24} \] All factors, order, scalars, source pivots and meridian currents in L remain. Comparing with (23) requires applying the turnover, degree factor and routed reduced braid in (24), with the same cut and presentation. One cannot identify the bare map (12) with (23), or delete these interfaces because both preserve ordered characters. ## 5. Marks and the distinct analytic continuation gate On regular patches (10),(11) give the collective flow time \[ \partial_\Omega{\cal H}_A = rac{\Log(1-u)-\Log(1-v)}{z-z^{-1}}. 	ag{25} \] The rational graph removes the displayed spectral square root. It does not remove the logarithms from the action. The actual coherent phase is obtained with the boundary calibration in Section 3; it is not simply (10) evaluated on an input point. At fixed degree, a remaining function of \(K\) is the common diagonal seam. A full occupation stationary equation must still impose its closing value. L gives a concrete finite warning against discarding marks. If the factorial logarithms \(u=e^{c_0x},v=e^{c_0y}\) are both shifted by one, the actual left factor of the sewn source is multiplied by \[ d_{{m deck},N}(M)=  rac{1-M^{-2mN}}{1-M^{-2N}}. 	ag{26} \] It has value \(m\), not one, at \(M=1\), and \(\left.\partial_\mu d_{{m deck},N}(e^\mu)ight|_0=-Nm(m-1)\). Individual ordered decks can have the actual radical poles recorded in L. Thus a rational equality of graphs cannot reset the marked factorial lift or its normal source. There are explicit independent tests for geometric reach. * K's estimate has physical real \(\sigma\), so \(|K|=1\). The regular complete geometric total eigenvalue is loxodromic. Its nonreal occupation moment is outside this estimated slice. * Given a chosen logarithmic tuple, recover \(p_i=-\Log(-K_i)/c_0\), the actual input \(z_i=\pi_i p_i/(1-p_i)\), and output \(w_i=1/\pi_i'\). Then test K's actual \(\xi_i=(-1)^{r-i}z_i/z_r\) and \(ho_i=(-1)^{r-i}w_i/w_r\), including its punctured sector, bounded shapes, and small output domain. These ratios are unchanged by residual common diagonal framing. That freedom cannot force membership in the estimated chart. * Even the initialized scalar projection has a genuine branch gate: \[ t= rac{(\lambda-2C)(\lambda-C-1)} {\lambda-1-2C+C^2},\qquad \Delta_B(t)=(1+C-t)^2-4C(1-Ct). 	ag{27} \] The selected branch begins at \(\lambda=2C,t=0,Y=1\). The other zero-activity branch is \(\lambda=C+1\). The projection can ramify at \(\Delta_B=0\) while (12) remains regular. Higher-dimensional generating projections have their corresponding mixed-Hessian gates. Equation (27) follows by eliminating \(Y\) from (14),(18). It is a test of this initialized projection, not a global parametrization of every tuple by its trace alone. Consequently a geometric point can belong to the algebraic continuation of this source graph without belonging to the domain where K selected and estimated its coefficient. The remaining analytic problem is transport of the original capped coherent and occupation contour, with its complementary chains and marked degree connectors, to the appropriate generating chart. A path avoiding the rational poles or a unique algebraic critical point does not supply that transport or its relative coefficient. title: The actual Gauss first column as a zero-free analytic boundary kernel
text: # The actual Gauss first column as a zero-free analytic boundary kernel 18 November 2026. Private written proof. This note estimates an initialized column of the actual operator \(A_N\) in [G], including its finite transfer sum, vacuum normalization and both factorial caps. The result is a full small-disk phase and nonzero amplitude. It supplies boundary data for a two-variable kernel problem; it does not estimate that entire kernel or its original closed source. The quantum parameter and meridian are fixed at completeness. All occupations remain integers. The chamber is \((T+1)/N\) in a compact subset of \((1/2,1)\). ## 1. Actual column, normalization and statement Put \[ c_0=2\pi i,\quad h=c_0/N,\quad Q=e^h,\quad q=e^{h/2}, \quad d=N-1,\quad x=-q^{-1},\quad f_n=(Q;Q)_n. \] Take two remaining heads in [G]'s actual \(A_N=q_FE_\Sigma^d i_d\). On their integer degree \(0\leq T\leq d\), use the physical basis \(|a,T-a\rangle\), \(0\leq a\leq T\), and put \[ H=d-T,\qquad \sigma_N=(T+1)/N,\qquad C=Q^H=Q^{-T-1}=e^{-c_0\sigma_N}. \tag{1} \] Thus the total tail Cartan on this degree is \(K_T=C\). Matrix indices in this note are physical indices in that basis. Let \[ G_T(\rho)=\sum_{a=0}^T x^{-a}\frac{(A_N)_{a0}}{(A_N)_{00}}\rho^a. \tag{2} \] For \(2T+1\geq N\), its normalization is exactly \[ (A_N)_{00}=(-1)^d C^d f_T^2\ne0. \tag{3} \] In particular \(G_T(0)=1\). If the output evaluation sends \(|a,T-a\rangle\) to \(w_1^a w_2^{T-a}\), then the actual column is \[ v_{\mathbf w}A_N|0,T\rangle =(A_N)_{00}w_2^T\,G_T(xw_1/w_2). \tag{4} \] Any original input binomial coefficient or dual extraction is still outside (4); it has not been absorbed into the normalization. Here are the phase and amplitude. For auxiliary \(\sigma\) near a compact interval \(I\Subset(1/2,1)\), put \(C=e^{-c_0\sigma}\). Let \(Y(0)=1\) solve \[ CY^2-(1+C-\rho)Y+1-C\rho=0. \tag{5} \] The derivative in \(Y\) at zero is \(C-1\), uniformly nonzero. With \(D=\rho\partial_\rho\), define \[ Z=-\frac{CY\,DY+\rho Y-C\rho}{2CY-(1+C-\rho)}. \tag{6} \] Use the logarithms zero at \(\rho=0\), and set \[ \begin{split} \phi_G(\rho;\sigma) &=\frac{\operatorname{Li}_2(\rho)}{c_0} +\frac1{c_0}\int_0^\rho\frac{\log Y(t)}t\,dt,\\ {\cal A}_G(\rho;\sigma) &=(1-\rho)^{-1/2} \exp\left\{\int_0^\rho\frac{Z(t)}{tY(t)}\,dt -\frac12\log Y(\rho)\right\}. \end{split} \tag{7} \] All integrands are regular at zero. These definitions fix \(\phi_G(0)=0\), \({\cal A}_G(0)=1\). The dilogarithm in (7) is its power-series germ at zero. **Theorem.** For each \(I\Subset(1/2,1)\) there is a fixed \(r>0\) such that, for \(\sigma_N\in I\) and all sufficiently large \(N\), the literal polynomial (2) is zero-free on \(|\rho|\leq r\) and \[ G_T(\rho)=e^{N\phi_G(\rho;\sigma_N)} {\cal A}_G(\rho;\sigma_N)(1+O(N^{-1})). \tag{8} \] The relative error is holomorphic, with all fixed \(\rho\)-derivatives \(O(N^{-1})\) on smaller disks. The amplitude is nonzero. In particular \[ \partial_\rho\phi_G(0;\sigma)=2/c_0. \tag{9} \] The accompanying normalization is \(\partial_\rho\log{\cal A}_G(0;\sigma)=1/(1-C)\). Indeed (5),(6) give \(Y'(0)=1\), \(Z'(0)=1/(1-C)\); the exact first coefficient from (16),(17) is \[ G_T'(0)=-\frac{Q}{1-Q} \left(1+\frac{1-C}{1-QC}\right) =\frac{2N}{c_0}+\frac1{1-C}+O(N^{-1}). \tag{9a} \] The phase retains \(\sigma_N=(T+1)/N\) exactly. The theorem neither interpolates \(T\) nor differentiates a root-reflection formula in the meridian or quantum parameter. ## 2. Complete finite first-column calculation For clarity we derive the column from the actual [G, (9)] formula, rather than selecting a scalar Casimir node. On one complete head, \[ Ew_a=(Q^{-a}-1)w_{a-1},\quad Fw_a=(1-Q^{a+1})w_{a+1},\quad Kw_a=xQ^{-a}w_a, \] with the literal missing bottom/top arrows. The two-head totals are \(E=E_1K_2+E_2\), \(F=F_1+K_1^{-1}F_2\). Only \(E_2^n\) survives on \(|0,T\rangle\). The coefficient of \(|a,T-a\rangle\) in \(F^nE^n|0,T\rangle\), for \(a\leq n\leq T\), is \[ {n\brack a}_Q x^{-(n-a)} \frac{f_a f_{T-a}}{f_{T-n}}\, Q^{-nT+n(n-1)/2}\frac{f_T}{f_{T-n}}. \tag{10} \] Indeed the ordered coproduct expansion is \(F_1^a(K_1^{-1}F_2)^{n-a}\) with coefficient \({n\brack a}_Q\); its right factor acts while the first occupation is zero. At \(M=1\), [G]'s lowering products are \(H_n=Q^{-n(n+1)/2}f_n\), \(H_d=(-1)^dN\). Insert (10) in [G, (9)] and keep the ordered \(K_T^{d-n}\). The powers \(x^{-2n}=Q^n\), \(K_T^{-n}=Q^{n(T+1)}\) give exactly \[ (A_N)_{a0}=(-1)^dNC^d x^a V_a,\qquad V_a=\sum_{n=a}^T Q^{n(n+1)} {T\brack n}_Q{T-a\brack n-a}_Q. \tag{11} \] This is an actual matrix entry with its full scalar. The finite binomial product, proved by its coefficient recursion, gives \[ V_a=Q^{-T(T-1)/2}[t^T]\, (-tQ^{T+1};Q)_T\,(-t;Q)_{T-a}. \tag{12} \] The exponent of the coefficient indexed by \(n\) is \(n(n+1)+T(T-1)/2\), which verifies every phase in (12). Since \(2T+1\geq N\), put \(L=T-H=2T+1-N\geq0\). The product in (12) is identically \[ (1-(-t)^N)\, \frac{(-t;Q)_L}{(-tQ^{T-a};Q)_{a+1}}. \tag{13} \] This is an identity of rational functions with polynomial left side. Only inside \([t^T]\), where \(T<N\), may the first factor in (13) be replaced by one. The remaining denominator has the distinct poles \(t_r=-Q^{-T+r}\), \(0\leq r\leq a\). If the partial fraction decomposition has a polynomial part, its degree is at most \(L-a-1<T\), so it has no effect on \([t^T]\). The numerator at \(t_r\) is \[ (Q^{H+1+r};Q)_L =\begin{cases} \displaystyle \frac{N(-1)^{H-r}Q^{(H-r)(H-r+1)/2}}{f_{H-r}f_{H+r}}, &0\leq r\leq H,\\ 0, &H<r\leq a. \end{cases} \tag{14} \] For the second case the product contains a full-root factor. For the first use the exact reflection \[ f_{d-b}=\frac{N(-1)^bQ^{b(b+1)/2}}{f_b}. \] The other denominator factors evaluated at \(t_r\) have product \[ (-1)^{a-r}Q^{-(a-r)(a-r+1)/2}f_r f_{a-r}. \] Taking \([t^T]\) of \(1/(1+tQ^{T-r})\), and simplifying these displayed powers, gives \[ \begin{split} V_0&=f_T^2/N,\\ \frac{V_a}{V_0} &=(-1)^aQ^{a(a+1)/2}f_H^2 \sum_{r=0}^{\min(a,H)} \frac{Q^{r(r-a)}}{f_r f_{a-r}f_{H-r}f_{H+r}}. \end{split} \tag{15} \] The first line also follows from (12) at \(a=0\); reflection identifies \((-1)^TQ^{T(T+1)/2}f_T/f_H\) with \(f_T^2/N\). Equations (11),(15) prove (3). Define the actual finite polynomials \[ \begin{split} {\cal E}_N(\rho) &=\sum_{k=0}^{d} \frac{(-1)^kQ^{k(k+1)/2}}{f_k}\rho^k,\\ B_H(\rho) &=\sum_{r=0}^H \frac{(Q^{-H};Q)_r(Q^{H+1}\rho)^r} {f_r(Q^{H+1};Q)_r}. \end{split} \tag{16} \] There are no zero denominators: \(2H\leq d\). The \(r\)-th coefficient of \(B_H\) is exactly \[ \frac{(-1)^rQ^{r(r+1)/2}f_H^2} {f_r f_{H-r}f_{H+r}}. \] Writing \(a=r+k\) in (15), the mixed \(rk\) phase cancels. Thus the exact initialized-column identity is \[ \boxed{\quad G_T= \operatorname{trunc}_{\leq T}({\cal E}_N B_H). \quad} \tag{17} \] Both finite caps and the final truncation are part of (17). No noninteger occupation or omitted full-root factor is implicit. ## 3. Exact rows and uniform low-degree logarithms With \(Sg(\rho)=g(Q\rho)\), coefficient ratios in (16) give \[ {\cal E}_N(\rho)-(1-Q\rho){\cal E}_N(Q\rho) =\rho^N/N, \tag{18} \] and \[ CB_H(Q^2\rho)-(1+C-Q\rho)B_H(Q\rho) +(1-CQ\rho)B_H(\rho)=0. \tag{19} \] The top term in (18) uses \((-1)^dQ^{d(d+1)/2}/f_d=1/N\). In (19) the degree \(H+1\) term vanishes because \(C=Q^H\); this is the literal terminating equation, not an infinite-series specialization. Choose \(k_N=\lfloor\delta N\rfloor\) with small fixed \(\delta>0\). Uniformly for \(\sigma_N\in I\), it can be chosen so that \(k_N<H\), \(k_N<T\), and, for \(1\leq n\leq k_N\), \[ |CQ^n-1|\geq b>0,\qquad |Q^n-1|\geq b n/N. \tag{20} \] This uses \(H/N=1-\sigma_N\) in a compact subset of \((0,1/2)\). Initially form \(R_N=B_H(Q\rho)/B_H(\rho)\) as a formal series. Its exact Riccati equation is \[ CR_N(\rho)R_N(Q\rho) -(1+C-Q\rho)R_N(\rho)+1-CQ\rho=0. \tag{21} \] For \(r_N=R_N-1\), this becomes \[ (CS-1)r_N=-Q\rho(1-C)-Q\rho r_N-Cr_NSr_N. \tag{22} \] In degrees at most \(k_N\), the inverse of \(CS-1\) has coefficient cost \(b^{-1}\). The quadratic positive majorant \[ b\bar r=C_1\rho(1+\bar r)+C_1\bar r^2, \qquad\bar r(0)=0 \] therefore bounds its low coefficients by a common geometric sequence. The analytic implicit function theorem proves convergence of the majorant on a fixed disk; on a smaller disk it is less than \(1/2\). Consequently the low coefficients of \(\log R_N\) also have a common analytic bound. This is the finite coefficient argument in [U, §3], with the exact multiplier (20). Set \[ \ell_{B,N}=\sum_{n=1}^{k_N} \frac{[\rho^n]\log R_N}{Q^n-1}\rho^n. \] Its exponential agrees with \(B_H\) through degree \(k_N\), and \(|\ell_{B,N}|\leq C_2N|\rho|\) on a fixed disk. Likewise (18), divided formally by its unit at zero, shows that \[ \ell_{E,N}=\sum_{n=1}^{k_N} \frac{Q^n}{n(Q^n-1)}\rho^n \tag{23} \] is the exact logarithm of \({\cal E}_N\) through that degree. It too satisfies \(|\ell_{E,N}|\leq C_2N|\rho|\). By (17), \(e^{\ell_{E,N}+\ell_{B,N}}\) agrees with the actual \(G_T\) through degree \(k_N\). ## 4. Transport and the full finite-tail comparison For \(C\) held exact, substitute \(Y+hZ\) into (21). The constant order in \(h\) is (5); the coefficient of \(h\) is \[ [2CY-(1+C-\rho)]Z+CY\,DY+\rho Y-C\rho. \] Equation (6) cancels it. On a fixed common disk the residual is \(O(h^2)\), with zero constant coefficient. Subtract its equation from (22). All error terms other than \((CS-1)e\) have zero-constant analytic coefficients; the quadratic difference is \(e\,Sr_N+r_{\rm app}Se\), times \(C\). The same positive coefficient majorant as in [U, §5], or directly \(b\bar e=C_3|h|^2\rho/(R-\rho)+K(\rho)\bar e\) with \(K(0)=0\), proves \[ [\rho^n]\log R_N=(\log Y)_n+h(Z/Y)_n +O(|h|^2R_1^{-n}),\quad n\leq k_N. \tag{24} \] Here one first shrinks the comparison disk so \(K<b/2\). Thus only finite coefficient inversion below the multiplier wall has been used. For \(n\leq k_N\), shrink \(\delta\) if needed and use \[ (Q^n-1)^{-1}=(hn)^{-1}-1/2+O(|h|n). \] Summation of (24), with the analytic tails above \(k_N\), gives \[ \ell_{B,N} =\frac{N}{c_0}\int_0^\rho\frac{\log Y(t)}t\,dt +\int_0^\rho\frac{Z(t)}{tY(t)}\,dt -\frac12\log Y(\rho)+O(N^{-1}). \tag{25} \] For the other factor, \(Q^n/(Q^n-1)=(hn)^{-1}+1/2+O(|h|n)\). Equation (23) therefore gives \[ \ell_{E,N} =\frac{N}{c_0}\operatorname{Li}_2(\rho) -\frac12\log(1-\rho)+O(N^{-1}). \tag{26} \] All errors are uniform and analytic on a fixed smaller disk. The \(Q\)-shift in the actual reciprocal Euler factor is essential for the sign of the one-half logarithm in (26). It remains to compare with the complete column, not just its low formal coefficients. The elementary global sine bound proved in [U, §4] is \[ e^{-C_4N}\leq |f_j|\leq e^{C_4N}, \qquad0\leq j<N. \] It applies to every index in (16). Hence every coefficient of \({\cal E}_N\), \(B_H\), their product and its truncation \(G_T\) is at most \(e^{C_5N}\), increasing \(C_5\) to absorb the finite convolution sum. On a fixed comparison circle of radius \(R_2<1\), both \(G_T\) and \(e^{\ell_{E,N}+\ell_{B,N}}\) are bounded by \(e^{C_6N}\). Their first \(k_N+1\) coefficients agree exactly, so \[ |G_T-e^{\ell_{E,N}+\ell_{B,N}}| \leq 2e^{C_6N} \frac{(|\rho|/R_2)^{k_N+1}}{1-|\rho|/R_2}. \tag{27} \] Choose the final fixed radius so that \(\delta\log(R_2/|\rho|)\) beats this exponential constant and the inverse-unit cost \(e^{C_2N|\rho|}\). Then (27) is exponentially small relative to the constructed unit. Combining (25),(26) proves (8), including zero-freeness and every fixed derivative by Cauchy on smaller disks. This estimates the full polynomial (17). In particular the three finite boundaries—the cap of \({\cal E}_N\), the termination of \(B_H\), and the truncation at \(T\)—were all retained before the tail estimate. No operator or scalar endpoint was dropped. ## 5. Actual characteristic boundary data and limits Equation (5) gives \(Y'(0)=1\). The selected logarithmic ratio of the first-column phase is \[ Y_G=\exp(c_0D\phi_G)=\frac{Y}{1-\rho}. \tag{28} \] For the actual Jacobi characteristic in [U, (3)], define its Casimir argument by \[ \lambda_G(\rho) =2+\frac{(1-\rho)^2(1-Y_G)(1-CY_G)}{\rho}. \] The expression has a removable singularity at zero. Substituting (5) gives the exact analytic identity \[ \lambda_G(\rho)=C(1+Y(\rho))+\rho,\qquad \lambda_G(0)=2C,\quad \lambda_G'(0)=1+C. \tag{29} \] Thus these boundary data are initialized by the actual contracted operator column. They are not an arbitrarily supplied spectral leg or a chosen eigenvalue on the physical real channel grid. For \(I\Subset(1/2,1)\), \(C\ne-1\), so the derivative in (29) is nonzero on each such compact interval. This is a local characteristic-projection statement, not a proof of the full two-variable kernel or a closed-source contour. Equations (3),(4) keep the actual normalization and the output monomial. All remaining factors of the opposite kernel in [G, (6)] remain to be applied. No bound for those factors, meridian normal, inverse frame, relative closing window or geometric contribution is inferred here. ## Complete directs and author protocol - **G:** [research_opposite_kernel_forced_cyclic_normalization.md](research_opposite_kernel_forced_cyclic_normalization.md), 489 lines, SHA256 42e6d6c3a5039859c241a2832de56301eff49d749db86d67868f3534c89aaaaa. - **U:** [research_actual_jacobi_generating_unit.md](research_actual_jacobi_generating_unit.md), 400 lines, SHA256 ab3760dd38817c2345c231d8ef67c8a7fa8bb03e3b26d4ef1de1b87182f6728d. title: The actual root head: a smooth matrix block and its retained cut
The actual Jacobi generating polynomial on a uniform Casimir disk
text: # The actual Jacobi generating polynomial on a uniform Casimir disk 18 November 2026. This is a fixed-root analytic estimate for the literal continuant columns of [H]. It proves a zero-free generating disk, an explicit phase and nonzero amplitude, and the actual Casimir-derivative partner on that disk. The finite last-row forcing is retained throughout. There is no interpolation of the integer occupation or of the channel. The parameter \((T+1)/N\) stays in a compact subset of \((0,1)\). In particular this proof does not apply to \(T=N-1\). It is not a meridian normal theorem, an estimate for the inverse Clebsch measure, or a claim about a closed-source coefficient. ## 1. Literal polynomial and the theorem Put \[ c_0=2\pi i,\quad h=c_0/N,\quad Q=e^h,\quad q=e^{h/2}, \quad d=N-1,\quad x=-q^{-1}. \] For \(0\leq T\leq d\), use exactly the Jacobi entries and continuants of [H, §§1–2]. In a form convenient for the generating row they are \[ \begin{split} A_a&=(Q^{a-T}-1)(1-Q^{a+1}),\qquad 0\leq a<T,\\ D_a&=2(q+q^{-1}Q^{-T})Q^a -(q+q^{-1})Q^{-T}Q^{2a},\\ p_0&=1,\quad p_1=\lambda-D_0,\quad p_{a+1}=(\lambda-D_a)p_a-A_{a-1}^2p_{a-1},\\ f_a(\lambda)&=\frac{p_a(\lambda)}{A_0\cdots A_{a-1}}, \qquad f_0=1. \end{split} \tag{1} \] The expression for \(D_a\) follows by expanding [H, (2)]; its two constant terms cancel against the two Cartan terms. Define \[ L_T(\rho;\lambda)=\sum_{a=0}^T x^{-a}f_a(\lambda)\rho^a,\qquad \sigma_N=\frac{T+1}{N},\qquad c=e^{-c_0\sigma_N}=Q^{-T-1}. \tag{2} \] Fix a real compact interval \(I\Subset(0,1)\) and a compact Casimir disk \(\Lambda\Subset\mathbb C\). All estimates below hold for \(\sigma_N\in I\), sufficiently large \(N\), and \(\lambda\in\Lambda\). They also hold on a slightly larger Casimir disk when needed for Cauchy estimates. Constants may depend on these compact sets. For an auxiliary \(\sigma\) near \(I\), put \(c=e^{-c_0\sigma}\). Let \(Y(\rho;\lambda,\sigma)\) be the analytic solution, \(Y(0)=1\), of \[ (1-\rho)^2(1-Y)(1-cY)+(2-\lambda)\rho=0. \tag{3} \] It exists on a common disk because the \(Y\)-derivative at \(\rho=0\) is \(c-1\), bounded away from zero. Write \(D=\rho\partial_\rho\), and set \[ \begin{array}{lll} a_0=c(1-\rho)^2,&b_0=-(1+c)(1-\rho)^2, &d_0=1-\lambda\rho+\rho^2,\\ a_1=-3c\rho(1-\rho),& b_1=2(1+c)\rho(1-\rho),& d_1=\rho^2-\lambda\rho/2. \end{array} \] Define the analytic function \(Z\), with \(Z(0)=0\), by \[ Z=-\frac{a_0Y\,DY+a_1Y^2+b_1Y+d_1}{2a_0Y+b_0}. \tag{4} \] Its denominator is again \(c-1\) at zero. Use the logarithm of \(Y\) equal to zero there, and define \[ \begin{split} \phi(\rho;\lambda,\sigma) &=\frac1{c_0}\int_0^\rho\frac{\log Y(t)}t\,dt,\\ {\cal A}(\rho;\lambda,\sigma) &=\exp\left\{\int_0^\rho\frac{Z(t)}{tY(t)}\,dt -\frac12\log Y(\rho)\right\}. \end{split} \tag{5} \] Both apparent singularities at zero are removable. Thus \(\phi(0)=0\), \({\cal A}(0)=1\), and \({\cal A}\) is nonzero. **Theorem.** There is a radius \(r>0\), independent of \(N,T,\lambda\) in the stated ranges, such that the actual polynomial (2) is zero-free on \(|\rho|\leq r\), and \[ L_T(\rho;\lambda) =e^{N\phi(\rho;\lambda,\sigma_N)} {\cal A}(\rho;\lambda,\sigma_N)(1+\epsilon_{N,T}(\rho,\lambda)), \qquad |\epsilon_{N,T}|\leq C/N. \tag{6} \] The relative error is holomorphic on a larger disk than any final closed disk under consideration. Its fixed \(\rho,\lambda\) derivatives are \(O(N^{-1})\) on smaller compact sets. In particular \[ \partial_\rho\phi(0;\lambda,\sigma) =\frac{\lambda-2}{c_0(e^{-c_0\sigma}-1)}. \tag{7} \] The exact shift \(\sigma_N=(T+1)/N\) is part of (6), including its amplitude. Replacing it by \(T/N\) without expanding the resulting phase change would alter the displayed amplitude. ## 2. Exact row and its forced partner Let \[ s_b=|(Q;Q)_b|,\quad B_T=A_0\cdots A_{T-1}=(-1)^Ts_T^2,\quad P_T(\lambda)=\prod_{j=0}^T (\lambda-q^{2j+1}-q^{-2j-1}). \tag{8} \] The last-row residual in [H] is \((J_T-\lambda)f=-P_T(\lambda)e_T/B_T\). Summing it with the weights \(x^{-a}\rho^{a+1}\) and using (1) gives \[ \begin{split} &c(1-Q\rho)(1-Q^2\rho)L_T(Q^2\rho) -(1+c)(1-Q\rho)^2L_T(Q\rho)\\ &\hspace{35mm} +(1-q\lambda\rho+Q\rho^2)L_T(\rho) =-\frac{q^{T+1}P_T(\lambda)}{s_T^2}\rho^{T+1}. \end{split} \tag{9} \] For completeness, before multiplication by \(q\) the three coefficients on the left are respectively \[ Q^{-T}q^{-3}(1-Q\rho)(1-Q^2\rho),\quad -q^{-3}(Q+Q^{-T})(1-Q\rho)^2,\quad q^{-1}-\lambda\rho+q\rho^2. \] The right side is \(-P_Tx^{-T}\rho^{T+1}/B_T\). Since \(x^{-T}=(-1)^Tq^T\), this is exactly (9), with its sign and top coefficient. All endpoint terms are thus included. Denote the difference operator on the left of (9) by \({\cal D}_{T,\lambda}\). Differentiation gives, for \(k\geq1\), \[ {\cal D}_{T,\lambda}(\partial_\lambda^k L_T) =kq\rho\,\partial_\lambda^{k-1}L_T -\frac{q^{T+1}P_T^{(k)}(\lambda)}{s_T^2}\rho^{T+1}. \tag{10} \] At a double Casimir node \(P_T'=0\), the \(q\rho L_T\) term remains. The true partner is not a second homogeneous solution of (9). Indeed its coefficients are exactly \(x^{-a}f_a'(\lambda)\); [H, §2] proves that these are the literal confluent Clebsch columns. ## 3. Low-degree analytic control of the ratio Initially all ratios and logarithms in this section are formal series at \(\rho=0\); \(L_T(0)=1\) makes them unambiguous. Put \[ R_N(\rho)=\frac{L_T(Q\rho)}{L_T(\rho)},\qquad R_N(0)=1, \] and \[ a_h=c(1-Q\rho)(1-Q^2\rho),\quad b_h=-(1+c)(1-Q\rho)^2,\quad d_h=1-q\lambda\rho+Q\rho^2. \] Dividing (9) by \(L_T(\rho)\) yields \[ a_hR_N(\rho)R_N(Q\rho)+b_hR_N(\rho)+d_h =-\frac{q^{T+1}P_T(\lambda)}{s_T^2} \frac{\rho^{T+1}}{L_T(\rho)}. \tag{11} \] Choose a small fixed \(\delta>0\) and put \(k_N=\lfloor\delta N\rfloor\). It can be chosen so that \(k_N<T+1\) and, for all \(1\leq n\leq k_N\), \[ |cQ^n-1|\geq b>0,\qquad |Q^n-1|\geq b\,n/N. \tag{12} \] For example first choose \(\delta\) smaller than one fourth of the distance of \(I\) to the endpoints of \((0,1)\). The arguments \(n/N-\sigma_N\) then stay away from integers. Decrease \(\delta\) further below whenever required. The right side of (11) has no coefficient in these degrees; it has not been set equal to zero as a function. Here is a coefficient-majorant proof with a common analytic radius. Write \(R_N=1+r_N\), \(a_h=c+\alpha_h\), \(b_h=-(1+c)+\beta_h\). Both \(\alpha_h,\beta_h\) have zero constant term, with uniformly bounded degree-two coefficients. If \(S f=f(Q\rho)\), the homogeneous low-degree equation is \[ (cS-1)r_N=-(a_h+b_h+d_h) -\alpha_hSr_N-(\alpha_h+\beta_h)r_N -a_hr_NSr_N. \tag{13} \] The first term on the right also has zero constant term. Because \(|Q|=1\), replacing every coefficient by its absolute value does not change a shift majorant. Division in degree \(n\leq k_N\) costs at most \(b^{-1}\). A scalar series \(\bar r(0)=0\) solving \[ b\bar r=C\frac{\rho}{1-\rho}(1+2\bar r) +\frac{C}{1-\rho}\bar r^2 \tag{14} \] with \(C\) enlarged if necessary therefore dominates every coefficient of \(r_N\) through degree \(k_N\), by induction. The analytic implicit function theorem at \((\rho,\bar r)=(0,0)\) supplies a common radius. On a smaller radius \(\bar r<1/2\), so the same coefficient argument for \(\log(1+r_N)\) gives \[ |[\rho^n]\log R_N|\leq C R^{-n}, \qquad 1\leq n\leq k_N, \tag{15} \] with fixed \(R>0\). The statements are uniform on the enlarged Casimir disk. They make no assertion about the later coefficients of the formal ratio, which can detect the top row. Let \(g_{N,n}=[\rho^n]\log R_N\). The identity \(\log R_N=\log L_T(Q\rho)-\log L_T(\rho)\) gives the exact low-degree coefficients \[ \ell_N(\rho)=\sum_{n=1}^{k_N} \frac{g_{N,n}}{Q^n-1}\rho^n,\qquad [\rho^n]e^{\ell_N}=[\rho^n]L_T\quad(0\leq n\leq k_N). \tag{16} \] Equations (12),(15) imply \(|\ell_N(\rho)|\leq CN|\rho|\) on a fixed smaller disk. Thus \(e^{\ell_N}\) is a genuine analytic unit; it remains to compare it to the whole finite polynomial. ## 4. The entire finite cap is exponentially small relative to that unit The continuant recurrence in (1) gives \(|p_a(\lambda)|\leq C^a\), uniformly on the enlarged Casimir disk: \(|A_a|\leq4\) and \(|D_a|\leq8\) suffice. Its exact denominator satisfies \[ |A_0\cdots A_{a-1}|=\frac{s_a s_T}{s_{T-a}}. \tag{17} \] There is an elementary global constant \(C\) such that \[ e^{-CN}\leq s_j\leq e^{CN},\qquad 0\leq j<N. \tag{18} \] For the upper bound use \(2\sin(\pi k/N)\leq2\). For the lower bound use \(2\sin(\pi k/N)\geq4\min(k,N-k)/N\), discard factors at least one, and sum the remaining negative logarithms. There are at most two copies of \(\sum_{k\leq N/4}\log(N/(4k))=O(N)\); the latter bound follows by comparing \(\sum\log k\) with \(\int_1^n\log t\,dt\). This proves (18), including the endpoints. Consequently \[ |x^{-a}f_a(\lambda)|\leq e^{CN},\qquad0\leq a\leq T. \tag{19} \] No individual factorial lower bound of size \(N^{-O(N)}\) is used. Choose a fixed comparison radius \(R_1<\min(R,1)\). Both \(L_T\) and \(e^{\ell_N}\) have supremum at most \(e^{C_1N}\) there. They agree through degree \(k_N\), so the Cauchy coefficient bound and geometric summation give, for \(|\rho|<R_1\), \[ |L_T-e^{\ell_N}| \leq 2e^{C_1N} \frac{(|\rho|/R_1)^{k_N+1}}{1-|\rho|/R_1}. \tag{20} \] On a final disk of sufficiently small fixed radius \(r_1\), the factor \(\delta\log(R_1/r_1)\) exceeds \(C_1\) and the cost in \(|e^{-\ell_N}|\leq e^{CNr_1}\). Hence, for some \(\epsilon>0\), \[ L_T=e^{\ell_N}(1+O(e^{-\epsilon N})), \qquad |\rho|\leq r_1. \tag{21} \] The proof works first on a slightly larger disk than any chosen closed final disk. This proves actual zero-freeness for large \(N\). In particular the omitted high degrees, and thus the entire original top forcing, have been estimated as part of the original polynomial. There is no deletion or alteration of its physical support. ## 5. Actual phase and amplitude with a transported error Taylor expansion in \(h\), keeping \(c=e^{-c_0\sigma_N}\) exact, gives \(a_h=a_0+ha_1+O(h^2)\), and the corresponding expansions for \(b_h,d_h\) recorded above (4). On a fixed common disk the functions \(Y,Z\) of (3),(4) are analytic and uniformly bounded. Since \[ Y(Q\rho)=Y(\rho)+hDY(\rho)+O(h^2), \] the analytic approximant \(R_{\rm app}=Y+hZ\) satisfies \[ a_hR_{\rm app}(\rho)R_{\rm app}(Q\rho) +b_hR_{\rm app}(\rho)+d_h=O(h^2). \tag{22} \] The residual is analytic on a fixed larger disk, has zero constant term, and its degree-\(n\) coefficients are bounded by \(C|h|^2R_2^{-n}\). Equation (3) cancels its constant order in \(h\); (4) cancels the order-\(h\) term, including the shifted \(Y\,DY\). We spell out the stability step. Subtract (22) from the low-degree equation (13), and write \(e=R_N-R_{\rm app}\). The constant diagonal multiplier is still \(cQ^n-1\). Every other linear coefficient in \(e,Se\) has zero constant term and a common analytic majorant. The quadratic difference is linear in the error after writing, for the zero-constant parts, \[ r_NSr_N-r_{\rm app}Sr_{\rm app} = e\,Sr_N+r_{\rm app}Se. \] The known factors on the right have the common majorants from §3 and the analytic bound for \(R_{\rm app}\). Thus the coefficient induction is dominated by \[ b\,\bar e=C|h|^2\frac{\rho/R_2}{1-\rho/R_2} +K(\rho)\bar e,\qquad K(0)=0, \tag{23} \] where \(K\) is a fixed convergent series with nonnegative coefficients. Shrinking the radius makes \(K<b/2\). The convergent solution of (23) proves, through degree \(k_N\), \[ |[\rho^n](R_N-Y-hZ)|\leq C|h|^2R_3^{-n}. \tag{24} \] All of this is finite coefficient induction; it does not require an inverse of the full difference operator at its later resonant degrees. Taking the logarithm on a smaller disk yields \[ g_{N,n}=(\log Y)_n+h(Z/Y)_n+O(|h|^2R_4^{-n}), \qquad1\leq n\leq k_N. \tag{25} \] Decrease \(\delta\) if necessary so \(|hn|\) stays in a fixed small disk for \(n\leq k_N\). The analytic Bernoulli expansion then gives \[ \frac1{Q^n-1}=\frac1{hn}-\frac12+O(|h|n). \] Substitution in (16),(25) shows that the degree-\(n\) coefficient of \(\ell_N\) equals \[ \frac{(\log Y)_n}{hn}+\frac{(Z/Y)_n}{n} -\frac12(\log Y)_n +O\!\left(|h|(n+1)R_5^{-n}\right). \tag{26} \] The error is summable on a fixed smaller disk. The tails above \(k_N\) of the three analytic main series cost at most \(CN(r/R_5)^{k_N+1}\), hence are exponentially small after a further fixed decrease of \(r\). Equations (5),(26) give \[ \ell_N=N\phi(\rho;\lambda,\sigma_N) +\log{\cal A}(\rho;\lambda,\sigma_N)+O(N^{-1}). \tag{27} \] Together with the exponentially relative estimate (21), this proves (6). Formula (7) follows by differentiating (3) at zero. Every normalization in (5) is fixed at zero; no free scalar phase or amplitude was introduced. ## 6. Genuine Casimir partners and precise scope The proof was performed on larger complex \(\rho,\lambda\) domains. Cauchy estimates applied to the holomorphic relative error in (6) therefore prove its fixed derivative bounds. In particular \[ \frac{\partial_\lambda L_T}{L_T} =N\partial_\lambda\phi+ \partial_\lambda\log{\cal A}+O(N^{-1}), \tag{28} \] and the equivalent normalized transport statement is \[ e^{-N\phi} (\partial_\lambda L_T-N\phi_\lambda L_T) ={\cal A}_\lambda+O(N^{-1}). \tag{29} \] Here \(\sigma_N,\rho\) are held fixed. Higher fixed Casimir derivatives follow by the same argument. At any double node of [H], this estimates the actual partner \(\sum x^{-a}f_a'(\lambda)\rho^a\), including the inhomogeneous row (10). It does not assert that the partner is nonzero at every point; for example it vanishes at \(\rho=0\). There is no branch coalescence in this selected germ at a special finite value of \(\lambda\), including \(\lambda=-2\). The relevant nondegeneracy is \(c-1\ne0\), uniform only because \(\sigma_N\) stays away from \(0,1\). At \(T=d\), \(c=1\), the uniform lower bound for the degree-one multiplier fails. That case is outside the theorem. These are fixed-root Casimir derivatives, not \(q\)-derivatives, meridian derivatives, or derivatives of an interpolated integer channel. The theorem estimates the actual magnetic generating polynomial. Applying it to a binomial dual contour still requires that contour's normalization and saddle estimate. It supplies neither a bound for the full inverse Hermite frame nor a geometric closing-cycle coefficient. ## Complete direct and author protocol The sole complete proof direct is: - **H:** [actual_complete_casimir_hermite_packet.md](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_complete_casimir_hermite_packet.md), 321 lines, SHA256 a4e96738a3a093d963fe13cc03585085951fa8699a506ade4e2e7a47c17b3f4c. H supplies the literal finite Jacobi block, its complete continuants, last-row residual and actual confluent partners. All analytic majorants, high-degree estimates and transported errors used here are proved in this note. No numerical checks or mathematical programs are used. Author freeze protocol: the entire matching final and the sole complete H direct were read nontruncated in this author sequence, every used implication was checked, and both file hashes were renewed. Independent matching-final/direct review and parent adoption remain separate.

title: The actual long-transfer cross-collar kernel
text: # The actual long-transfer cross-collar kernel Private written proof, 18 November 2026. The opposite endpoint blocks excluded from the short Euler transition have an exact finite kernel with a genuine factor \(N\). This note gives both signed factors, their checked-crossing order, their endpoint gauges, and their finite Fourier kernels. The root reflection identity is used only after specialization. The full unreflected products are retained for every quantum/meridian normal. The sole complete direct E supplies the literal balanced matrices, crossing order, gauges and two-wall convention. All new reflection, phase and Fourier calculations are given below. No neighboring packet, contributing cycle or scalar noncancellation is assumed. ## 1. The full finite germ before reflection Fix \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), and write \[ Q=e^h,\qquad q=e^{h/2},\qquad x=-M/q,\qquad F_t=\prod_{j=1}^t(1-Q^j),\quad H_t=\prod_{j=1}^t(MQ^{-j}-M^{-1}). \tag{1} \] Empty products equal one. E's compressed arrows are \[ {\cal E}|a\rangle=(MQ^{-a}-M^{-1})|a-1\rangle,\qquad F|b\rangle=(1-Q^{b+1})|b+1\rangle \tag{2} \] away from their forced extremes; \({\cal E}|0\rangle=F|d\rangle=0\). Put \(A={\cal E}\otimes F\), and \[ \Theta^\pm =\sum_{n=0}^d\frac{\sigma_n^\pm}{F_n}A^n,\qquad \sigma_n^+=(-1)^nq^{n^2},\qquad \sigma_n^-=q^n. \tag{3} \] Here \(\Theta^-=(\Theta^+)^{-1}\). The actual crossings are \[ R^+=\kappa\,{\mathsf P}D\Theta^+,\qquad R^-=\kappa^{-1}\Theta^-D^{-1}{\mathsf P},\qquad D_{a,b}=x^{-a-b}Q^{ab}. \tag{4} \] The original scalar Cartan line \(\kappa\), all pivots, and every neighboring tensor are unchanged. Take nonnegative endpoint deficits \(u,v,w,z\) satisfying \[ s=u+w=v+z\le d,\qquad n=d-s. \tag{5} \] The uncheck block goes from \((a,b)=(d-u,v)\) to \((w,d-z)\). This is an actual transfer of length \(n\); it has not been replaced by a short transfer modulo \(N\). Direct multiplication of (2) gives \[ T^\pm_{u,v;w,z} :=(\Theta^\pm)_{(w,d-z),(d-u,v)} =\frac{\sigma_n^\pm}{F_n} \frac{H_{d-u}}{H_w}\frac{F_{d-z}}{F_v}. \tag{6} \] The head support and conservation condition (5) are part of this formula. Every index in a denominator lies below \(N\). For an exact form adapted to normals define \[ U_F(t)=\prod_{r=1}^t(1-Q^{N-r}),\qquad U_H(t)=\prod_{r=1}^t(MQ^{r-N}-M^{-1}). \tag{7} \] Thus \(F_{d-t}=F_d/U_F(t)\) and \(H_{d-t}=H_d/U_H(t)\) where these factors are units. In E's normal bidisk they are units. Canceling only the identical full factor \(F_d\) gives \[ \boxed{\quad T^\pm_{u,v;w,z} =\sigma_n^\pm H_d \frac{U_F(s)}{U_H(u)F_vH_wU_F(z)} . \quad} \tag{8} \] This is an identity of the unspecialized finite analytic germ, not a derivative of a root reflection. Let \(T=d-u+v=w+d-z\). The two checked blocks, in their different physical input orders, are exactly \[ R^+_{(d-z,w),(d-u,v)} =\kappa x^{-T}Q^{w(d-z)}T^+_{u,v;w,z}, \tag{9} \] \[ R^-_{(w,d-z),(v,d-u)} =\kappa^{-1}x^TQ^{-(d-u)v}T^-_{u,v;w,z}. \tag{10} \] The inverse Cartan factor acts on the input after the flip. It cannot be put on the positive crossing's output. ## 2. Reflection at the complete root and all signed phases For the root formulas below, specialize \[ h=2\pi i/N,\qquad M=1,\qquad Q^N=1,\qquad q^N=-1. \tag{11} \] For \(0\le t\le d\), factor \(X^N-1\) and then reverse the last \(t\) factors of \(F_d\). This proves \[ F_d=N,\qquad \frac{F_d}{F_{d-t}} =\prod_{r=1}^t(1-Q^{-r}) =(-1)^tQ^{-t(t+1)/2}F_t, \qquad F_{d-t}=\frac{N(-1)^tq^{t(t+1)}}{F_t}. \tag{12} \] Also \(H_j=Q^{-j(j+1)/2}F_j\). The unreflected coefficient can therefore first be written \[ T^+_{u,v;w,z} =(-1)^nq^{-n(2w+1)} \frac{F_{d-u}F_{d-z}}{F_{d-s}F_wF_v}, \tag{13} \] \[ T^-_{u,v;w,z} =q^{-n^2-2nw} \frac{F_{d-u}F_{d-z}}{F_{d-s}F_wF_v}. \tag{14} \] For example, the exponent in (13) comes from \(q^{n^2}Q^{-n(d-u)+n(n-1)/2}\) and \(d-u=n+w\). Substitution of (12) gives the common factorial core \[ {\cal C}_{u,v;w,z} =N\frac{F_s}{F_uF_vF_wF_z} \tag{15} \] and the phases \[ T^+_{u,v;w,z} =(-1)^{N+u+z}q^{(w+1)^2+u+z(z+1)} {\cal C}_{u,v;w,z}, \tag{16} \] \[ T^-_{u,v;w,z} =(-1)^{u+z-s} q^{-n^2-2nw+u(u+1)+z(z+1)-s(s+1)} {\cal C}_{u,v;w,z}. \tag{17} \] In (16), reducing \(q^{-2dw}\) uses \(Q^d=Q^{-1}\), and \(q^{-d}=-q\). These reductions are root identities. Keeping the full \(D,{\mathsf P}\) factors in (9)--(10) yields particularly simple balanced checked entries: \[ \boxed{\quad R^+_{(d-z,w),(d-u,v)} =\kappa(-1)^s q^{s+(u-v)^2}{\cal C}_{u,v;w,z}, \qquad R^-_{(w,d-z),(v,d-u)} =\kappa^{-1}q^{(u-z)^2}{\cal C}_{u,v;w,z}. \quad} \tag{18} \] These follow by multiplying (13) or (14) by the displayed Cartan factor before reducing powers. In particular, \[ T^+_{0,0;0,0}=Nq^{d^2}=(-1)^NNq,\qquad T^-_{0,0;0,0}=(-1)^dNq^d=(-1)^NNq^{-1}, \tag{19} \] \[ R^+_{(d,0),(d,0)}=N\kappa,\qquad R^-_{(0,d),(0,d)}=N\kappa^{-1}. \tag{20} \] For \(N\ge2\), \(R^-_{(d,0),(d,0)}=0\): the flip gives input \((0,d)\) to the inverse Euler factor, which can only have transfer zero. The large inverse corner in (20) is the opposite physical corner. The same observation gives \(R^+_{(0,d),(0,d)}=0\). ## 3. Exact endpoint gauges and the symmetric kernel Use E's \(G_F|a\rangle=F_a|a\rangle\). On both heads, the uncheck transformed entry is the original one multiplied by \(F_{d-u}F_v/(F_wF_{d-z})\). Before specialization it is \[ (T^\pm)_{FF} =\sigma_n^\pm\frac{H_{d-u}F_{d-u}}{H_wF_wF_{d-s}} =\sigma_n^\pm H_d \frac{U_F(s)}{U_H(u)U_F(u)H_wF_w}. \tag{21} \] At the root it depends on \(u,w\) alone, apart from conservation: \[ B_N^+(u,w)=(-1)^NNq^{u^2+w^2+2s+1} \frac{F_s}{F_u^2F_w^2}, \tag{22} \] \[ B_N^-(u,w)=(-1)^{N+s}Nq^{-1-s-2uw} \frac{F_s}{F_u^2F_w^2}. \tag{23} \] For instance the positive unreduced exponent is \(-n(2w+1)+2u(u+1)-s(s+1)\); (22) follows using \(n=d-s\). This also verifies the input/output gauge order. For the other physical endpoint chart, \(G_E|a\rangle=H_a^{-1}|a\rangle\), the exact expression is \[ (T^\pm)_{EE} =\sigma_n^\pm H_d \frac{U_F(s)}{U_H(z)U_F(z)H_vF_v}. \tag{24} \] Its root value is \(B_N^\pm(z,v)\). Thus both separated endpoint types have the same scalar kernel with their appropriate deficit pair. Write \(S_t=\prod_{j=1}^t2\sin(\pi j/N)\). Since \(F_t=(-i)^tq^{t(t+1)/2}S_t\), equations (22)--(23) become \[ B_N^\pm(u,w)=(-1)^NN\,(\pm i)^s q^{\pm(s+1)(s+2)/2} \frac{S_s}{S_u^2S_w^2}. \tag{25} \] Here the upper sign is positive Euler; the lower sign is its inverse. The two kernels are entrywise complex conjugates at the root and are symmetric in \(u,w\). This is not a positivity assertion about the full crossing or its contraction. One can also display a Gaussian-binomial core without discarding any source factor. Multiply an input upper-donor column with deficit \(u\) by \(F_u\), and an output lower-donor row with index \(w\) by \(F_w\). Equivalently apply an additional diagonal change with value \(F_u\) on the upper collar and \(F_w^{-1}\) on the lower collar. For disjoint collars this is one well-defined head gauge. The resulting block is exactly \[ \widetilde B_N^\pm(u,w)=F_uF_w B_N^\pm(u,w), \tag{26} \] with core \(N F_{u+w}/(F_uF_w)\) and the phases (22)--(23). All neighboring rows and columns carry the inverse changes. On the donor, combining this change with \(G_F\) gives lower value one and upper value \(F_{d-u}F_u=N(-1)^uq^{u(u+1)}\) at the root. For \(EE\), multiply the lower-recipient input column by \(F_v\) and the upper-recipient output row by \(F_z\). For widths \(R=o(N)\), these are source changes with subexponential condition numbers. Indeed for \(t\le R<N/2\), \[ (4/N)^t t!\le |F_t|\le (2\pi/N)^t t!. \tag{27} \] The lower factorials and their reciprocals have maximum \(\exp(O(R\log(eN/R)))\); (12) gives the same upper-collar bound with an additional factor \(N\). Set the diagonal change to one outside the selected collars. Every entry of the selected block is still transformed by its exact input/output values. This does not compress away the path through the bulk or invoke the short-interval identity \(PA^nP=(PAP)^n\) on a union of collars. There is a uniform Pascal-core limit on the \(\sqrt N\) deficit scale. Replacing \(F_u,F_w\) in the compensated root rescaling by their positive moduli \(S_u,S_w\) gives the exact kernel \[ S_uS_w B_N^\pm(u,w) =(-1)^NN(\pm i)^s q^{\pm(s+1)(s+2)/2} \frac{S_s}{S_uS_w}. \tag{27a} \] For \(s=u+w\le C\sqrt N\), \[ \frac{S_s}{S_uS_w} =\binom{s}{u}\bigl(1+O_C(N^{-1/2})\bigr). \tag{27b} \] Indeed \(S_t=(2\pi/N)^t t!\exp E_t\), where \[ |E_t| =\left|\sum_{j=1}^t\log\frac{\sin(\pi j/N)}{\pi j/N}\right| \le C_1t^3/N^2 \] on this range. Apply this to \(t=s,u,w\); the powers of \(2\pi/N\) cancel. The phase in (27a), including its quadratic part, is retained. The elementary moment identity \(\binom{u+w}{u}=(u!w!)^{-1}\int_0^\infty t^{u+w}e^{-t}\,dt\) describes this factorial core only. The original crossing phases, neighboring factors and closing functional are not positive by this identity. The \(S\)-rescaling is a root statement. If its analytic normal extension is desired, use \(i^tq^{-t(t+1)/2}F_t\), which equals \(S_t\) at the root, together with the unreflected formulas; do not differentiate absolute values or the root reflection identity. ## 4. The finite Fourier kernel retains both ends Take nonempty deficit intervals \(I_u,I_v,I_w,I_z\subset[0,R]\), with their endpoints retained and \(s=u+w\le d\). For each \(s\), set \[ L(s)=\max(\min I_v,s-\max I_z),\qquad U(s)=\min(\max I_v,s-\min I_z),\qquad K_j(t)=\sum_{a=0}^j t^a . \tag{28} \] If \(L(s)>U(s)\), the corresponding term is zero. Otherwise \[ \sum_{\substack{v\in I_v\\s-v\in I_z}}t^v =t^{L(s)}K_{U(s)-L(s)}(t). \tag{29} \] There is no denominator \(1-t\); at \(t=1\) the factor is \(U(s)-L(s)+1\). Use the root Fourier basis \(|k\rangle_{\!F}=N^{-1/2}\sum_{a=0}^dQ^{ak}|a\rangle\). Let \(j_1,j_2\) label the output Fourier heads and \(k_1,k_2\) the input. The projected uncheck \(FF\) block is exactly \[ \frac{Q^{d(k_1-j_2)}}{N^2} \sum_{\substack{u\in I_u,\ w\in I_w\\u+w\le d}} B_N^\pm(u,w) Q^{(j_2-k_1)u+(j_2-j_1)w} t^{L(s)}K_{U(s)-L(s)}(t),\qquad t=Q^{k_2-j_2}. \tag{30} \] To check all Fourier signs before summing \(v\), its exponent is \[ k_1(d-u)+k_2v-j_1w-j_2(d-z) =d(k_1-j_2)+(j_2-k_1)u+(j_2-j_1)w+(k_2-j_2)v. \tag{31} \] This proves (30) with the exact upper-collar monomial. For the balanced or \(EE\) block one may always use the same four-index sum with its entry (16)--(17) or (24); this retains the same conservation and interval masks without cancellation. The checked \(FF\) kernels also have a finite geometric inner sum. At the root, the positive one is \[ \frac{\kappa Q^{d(k_1-j_1)}}{N^2} \sum_{u,w} B_N^+(u,w)Q^{(j_1-k_1)u+(j_1-j_2)w} x^{u-d}Q^{w(d-s)} t_+^{L(s)}K_{U(s)-L(s)}(t_+), \quad t_+=x^{-1}Q^{w+k_2-j_1}. \tag{32} \] The inverse, with its physical input order from (10), is \[ \frac{\kappa^{-1}Q^{d(k_2-j_2)}}{N^2} \sum_{u,w} B_N^-(u,w)Q^{(j_2-k_2)u+(j_2-j_1)w} x^{d-u} t_-^{L(s)}K_{U(s)-L(s)}(t_-), \quad t_-=xQ^{u-d+k_1-j_2}. \tag{33} \] Both sums have exactly the ranges in (30). For (32), write \(D_{w,d-z}=x^{u-d}Q^{w(d-s)}(x^{-1}Q^w)^v\). For (33), write \(D_{d-u,v}^{-1}=x^{d-u}(xQ^{u-d})^v\). These identities prove the Cartan ordering in the Fourier formulas. A prescribed mark depending on \(v\) stays inside the inner finite sum; it is not replaced by the unmarked \(K\) in (29). Likewise every further intermediate projector remains its actual path mask or finite Fourier kernel. Equations (30)--(33) describe the local bare crossing block, to be paired with the unchanged, inversely transformed neighboring source. They are not a delta approximation or an independent replacement of that source. ## 5. Full normal rows and the scope of the \(N\) corner For the extreme corner, (8)--(10) give before specialization \[ R^+_{(d,0),(d,0)} =\kappa M^{-d}q^{Nd}H_d,\qquad R^-_{(0,d),(0,d)} =\kappa^{-1}(-1)^dM^dH_d . \tag{34} \] At root \(q\), with \(M\) still unspecialized, the whole polynomial identity is \[ H_d=(-1)^dM^{-d}\sum_{r=0}^dM^{2r},\qquad {\cal D}_N(M)=M^{-d}\sum_{r=0}^dM^{2r}. \tag{35} \] Thus the two corners are \(\kappa M^{-d}{\cal D}_N(M)\) and \(\kappa^{-1}M^d{\cal D}_N(M)\). The removable expression \({\cal D}_N(M)=(M^N-M^{-N})/(M-M^{-1})\) is shorthand for the whole sum, including at \(M=1\). It is not replaced by \(N\) before taking meridian derivatives. For genuine \(h\)-normals use (8)--(10), (21), and (24), not (12), (16)--(18), or (25). In E's bidisk \(|h-2\pi i/N|\le\eta N^{-2}\), \(|M-1|\le\eta N^{-1}\), all displayed factors of indices below \(N\) are units. The actual top rows \[ \delta=1-Q^N,\qquad w_{\rm top}=MQ^{-N}-M^{-1},\qquad [F,P_H]=\delta U,\quad[{\cal E},P_H]=-w_{\rm top}L \tag{36} \] and their mixed defect remain exactly as in E, with all gauge factors conjugated before differentiation. Fixed root Fourier bases may be kept for these germs; a varying Fourier transform, if used instead, must itself be differentiated. On the ordinary head path \(M=-q^N\), exactly \[ H_d=(-1)^d M^{-d}F_d. \tag{37} \] This follows from \(MQ^{-j}-M^{-1}=-M^{-1}(1-Q^{N-j})\). It does not identify an auxiliary ADO-pivot closed normal with an ordinary colored-Jones normal: the full original pivot/twist adapter remains necessary. No new uniform normal asymptotic is asserted here. The displayed \(N\) is therefore a literal local degree factor in the original signed crossing, with its common scalar line retained. It is distinct from a closing-current prefactor and is not counted twice. The endpoint windows and neighboring contractions may still annihilate a contribution. Nothing here proves a nonempty global support sector, its occurrence in the original relative cycle, or a lower bound for the knot scalar. ## Complete proof-source pin * E: notes/research_actual_compressed_endpoint_euler_transition.md, SHA256 9c735f005fa94afe56931af5fc0cb77ee95849a9c4c89067290711135ad1ed16. The complete direct was freshly read nontruncated in the active author sequence and every used implication checked. The earlier endpoint-current note was searched for coverage: it retains the opposite-collar blocks but does not evaluate this kernel. Only written mathematics and source/text operations were used. Frozen and public files are unchanged.

title: Actual meridian jets on fixed cyclic-dilogarithm Hankel banks
text: # Actual meridian jets on fixed cyclic-dilogarithm Hankel banks Private written proof, 19 November 2026. The exact moving diagonal frames of F extend the root estimates of W and H to a complex scaled meridian collar. The result concerns the literal highest-cut pivotal source, with its external scalar displayed. The new conclusion is uniform radial-tail control for that family and every fixed true meridian jet. The root banks do not move. W already supplies an exact meridian period; no whole-meridian Euler/Gaussian factorization is used below. ## 1. Source, scalar, and exact moving frames Fix \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\), and a signed braid word \(\beta\) on \(m\) heads with \(c\) crossings and writhe \(w\). Put \(r=m-1\), \(M=e^\mu\), \(x=-M/q\), and \[ \mathcal P_N(M)=\Xi_N(M)\operatorname{Tr} [(P_0\otimes K_{\rm r}(M)^{1-N})W_\beta(M)]. \tag{1} \] Here \(P_0=|0\rangle\langle0|\), both the first input and output are zero, and \(\Xi_N\) is the prescribed external dimension, framing, and peripheral line. Every crossing in \(W_\beta\) includes its actual scalar \(\kappa(M)^{\pm1}\). We remove precisely that scalar and write \(\mathcal E_N(M)=\Xi_N(M)\kappa(M)^w\), \(\mathcal P_N=\mathcal E_N\widehat{\mathcal P}_N\). This defines the hatted source directly from stripped matrices, even at a zero or pole of the external line. Let \(J_iw_a=aw_a\), \(f_a=(Q;Q)_a\), and \[ h_a(M)=M^{-a}\frac{f_a}{(M^{-2}Q;Q)_a},\qquad D_h(M)=\operatorname{diag}(h_a(M)). \tag{2} \] Put \(\widehat R_{i,0}^{\pm}=\kappa(1)^{\mp1}R_i^{\pm}(1)\). F(32), with the actual checked flip and inverse order, gives \[ \begin{split} \kappa(M)^{-1}R_i^+(M) &=M^{-J_i-J_{i+1}}D_{h,i+1}(M) \widehat R_{i,0}^+D_{h,i}(M)^{-1},\\ \kappa(M)R_i^-(M) &=M^{J_i+J_{i+1}}D_{h,i}(M) \widehat R_{i,0}^-D_{h,i+1}(M)^{-1}. \end{split} \tag{3} \] We insert these factors at their original stages, without cancelling or commuting adjacent frames. All crossing scalars are counted once in \(\mathcal E_N\); in particular no extra \(\kappa(1)^w\) remains. For \(0<\eta'<\pi\), \(M=e^{u/N}\), \(|u|\le\eta'\), F(24)--(25) prove, uniformly over the complete occupation range, \[ \|D_h^{\pm1}\|\le(N+1)^{C_{\eta'}},\qquad \|M^{\pm(J_i+J_{i+1})}\|\le e^{2\eta'}. \tag{4} \] These diagonal bounds hold in the ordinary Euclidean head norm as well as F's binomial norm: both norms are the maximum of the diagonal entries. The proof uses the zero-free sine factors \(1-e^{-2u/N}Q^j\), \(1\le j<N\), and integration of \(|\partial_u\log h_a|\le C_{\eta'}\log(N+1)\). Thus both frames and inverses are holomorphic on this collar. The actual coupon has trace norm exactly \[ \|P_0\otimes K_{\rm r}(M)^{1-N}\|_1 =N^r|M|^{-rd}\le e^{r\eta'}N^r. \tag{5} \] This is not W's summed-output first-input-zero coupon. No equality between those coupons after resolvent insertion is asserted. ## 2. Only the root factors are replaced by contour kernels Write \(u_N(t)=\sum_{a<N}t^a/f_a\) and \(v_N(t)=\sum_{a<N}(-1)^aQ^{a(a-1)/2}t^a/f_a\). Use W's strict root factorization with \(x_0=-q^{-1}\): \[ C=F_2u_N(T_-)F_1F_2^{-1},\quad C^{-1}=F_2F_1^{-1}v_N(T_-)F_2^{-1},\quad \widehat R_0^+=CDu_N(T_+)C^{-1},\quad \widehat R_0^-=Cv_N(T_+)D^{-1}C^{-1}. \tag{6} \] Here \(F_i=\operatorname{diag}(f_a)\), \(T_\pm=x_0^{-1}S_1^\pm S_2^\mp\) are the literal truncated unit shifts, and \(D_{a,k}=(-1)^kQ^{k(k-1)/2}x_0^{-2k}\). In particular \(T_\pm^N=0\), \(\|T_\pm\|\le1\), and \(D\) is unitary. The conventions in (6) match F(31): the same head has \(Fw_a=(1-Q^{a+1})w_{a+1}\), \(Kw_a=x_0Q^{-a}w_a\), and \(R^+(1)w_{0,b}=\kappa(1)x_0^{-b}w_{b,0}\). For example the fusion coefficient of (6) from \((a,k)\) to \((a-h,k+h)\) is \(x_0^{-h}f_af_{k+h}/(f_hf_k)\), exactly its physical fusion coefficient; both negatives are the matrix inverse. Thus (6) replaces the root matrices in (3), including their scalar convention, and makes no assertion about (6) at \(M\ne1\). For \(\epsilon=\pm1\) let \[ A_\epsilon(t)=\prod_{j=1}^{N-1}(1-Q^{\epsilon j}t)^{-j/N}, \qquad A_\epsilon(0)=1. \tag{7} \] W's all-inverse realization uses three transfer slots and six factorial slots per crossing. A \(v_Q(T)\) slot uses \(A_+(t)(tI-T)^{-1}\); a \(u_Q(T)\) slot uses \(A_-(t)(tI-Q^{-1}T)^{-1}\). The inverse and direct factorial slots respectively use \[ A_-(t)\operatorname{diag}_a(Q^{-a}t^{-a-1}),\qquad A_+(t)\operatorname{diag}_a(NQ^{-a-1}t^{a-N}). \tag{8} \] Every slot is integrated with \(dt/(2\pi i)\) on its marked small circle. Its matrix Laurent orders are precisely among \(-1,\ldots,-N\). These identities are finite coefficient identities; all caps survive. There are \(s=9c\) slots. Keep the moving factors (3), the coupon (1), and their original order around these slots. For each slot orientation \(\epsilon\) and \(1\le j<N\), set \[ H_{\epsilon,j}(\rho)=(\rho-1)^{-j/N} \prod_{k\ne j}(1-\rho Q^{\epsilon(k-j)})^{-k/N}, \qquad 1<\rho<\infty. \tag{9} \] The nonendpoint logarithms continue radially from zero; the first power is positive real. H's oriented jump is \(2i\sin(\pi j/N)H_{\epsilon,j}\). A Laurent matrix kernel \(\sum_{a=0}^{d}B_at^{-a-1}\) becomes \(\sum_aB_aQ^{\epsilon ja}\rho^{-a-1}\). Let \(\mathcal R_N(\boldsymbol\rho,\boldsymbol j;u)\) be the literal pointed trace of that ordered cut network with (3). Then exactly \[ \widehat{\mathcal P}_N(e^{u/N}) =\sum_{\boldsymbol j\in\{1,\ldots,N-1\}^{s}} \int_{[1,\infty)^s}\mathcal R_N(\boldsymbol\rho,\boldsymbol j;u) \prod_{\ell=1}^{s} \frac{\sin(\pi j_\ell/N)}{\pi} H_{\epsilon_\ell,j_\ell}(\rho_\ell)\,d\rho_\ell. \tag{10} \] The identity follows at the matrix level before applying the chosen linear functional. Every bank, sheet mark, and curve is independent of \(u\). At finite endpoints the exponents \(-j/N>-1\) are integrable; at infinity \(A_\epsilon=O(|t|^{-(N-1)/2})\) and every matrix kernel is \(O(t^{-1})\). H's cut-arc proof therefore applies also at even and composite levels, without assuming a closed lift of a large base circle. Moving diagonals introduce no new \(t\)-poles. ## 3. Uniform absolute tails and true meridian derivatives On every bank, a transfer resolvent has norm at most \(N/\rho\), a direct factorial kernel at most \(N/\rho\), and an inverse factorial kernel at most \(1/\rho\). Equations (4)--(5) give constants \(C,B\), depending only on the fixed word and \(\eta'\), such that \[ |\mathcal R_N(\boldsymbol\rho,\boldsymbol j;u)| \le C(N+1)^B\prod_\ell\rho_\ell^{-1}. \tag{11} \] For instance \(B=r+6c+2cC_{\eta'}\) suffices after changing \(C\). No exponentially conditioned factorial remains in this rational source. No norm of a prefix quotient or a reduced axis trace is used. Put \(G_j=|f_j|/N^{j/N+1/2}\) and \(c_N=(N-1)(N-2)/(4N)\). H proves \[ |H_{\epsilon,j}(\rho)|\le G_j(\rho-1)^{-j/N}\rho^{-C_j},\quad C_j=(N-1)/4-j/(2N)\ge c_N, \quad\frac{\sin(\pi j/N)}\pi \int_1^\infty(\rho-1)^{-j/N}\frac{d\rho}{\rho}=1. \tag{12} \] Let \(\widehat{\mathcal P}_{N,\mathrm{tail}}(R,u)\) denote (10) restricted to \(\max\rho_\ell\ge R\), \(R\ge1\). Absolute integration and the union bound now prove, uniformly on \(|u|\le\eta'\), \[ |\widehat{\mathcal P}_{N,\mathrm{tail}}(R,u)| \le C(N+1)^B sR^{-c_N}\Big(\sum_{j=1}^{N-1}G_j\Big)^s. \tag{13} \] The same bound without \(sR^{-c_N}\) controls the full absolute integral. This integrable envelope also proves holomorphy under the integral. For \(0<\eta<\eta'\), Cauchy's formula in \(u=N\mu\) gives \[ \sup_{|u|\le\eta} |\partial_\mu^k\widehat{\mathcal P}_{N,\mathrm{tail}}(R,u)| \le\frac{k!N^k}{(\eta'-\eta)^k} C(N+1)^B sR^{-c_N}\Big(\sum_jG_j\Big)^s \tag{14} \] for every fixed \(k\ge0\), and the analogous full-integral bound. Here \(\partial_\mu=N\partial_u\) differentiates the actual fixed-\(q\) family, including its pivot and all moving frames. The derivative is not a derivative of a root-only symbol. H's uniform factorial estimate is \(\log G_j=N\int_0^{j/N}\log(2\sin\pi t)dt+O(\log N)\), whose maximal rate is \(v_3/(2\pi)\), with \(v_3\) the regular ideal tetrahedron volume. Thus for fixed \(R>1\) and fixed \(k\), (14) yields \[ \limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log \sup_{|u|\le\eta}|\partial_\mu^k \widehat{\mathcal P}_{N,\mathrm{tail}}(R,u)| \le\frac{9cv_3}{2\pi}-\frac14\log R. \tag{15} \] For \(c=0\) the integral is empty and the radial tail is zero. For \(N=2\), \(c_N=0\) in the exact bound; decay in (15) is a large-level conclusion. No restriction on parity or compositeness was used. ## 4. Restoring the original line and the scope of the estimate For the standard zero-framed raw source, R(23) supplies the exact compensation \(\Xi_N=\alpha^{-w}\), \(\alpha=\kappa x^{-d}\). Consequently its line is not an extra hypothesis: \[ \mathcal E_N=\alpha^{-w}\kappa^w=x^{dw},\qquad \sup_{|u|\le\eta'}|\mathcal E_N(e^{u/N})| \le e^{|w|\eta'}. \tag{16} \] Its \(\mu\)-derivative of order \(a\) is \((dw)^a x^{dw}\). Thus (15) holds unconditionally for every fixed meridian jet of this actual zero-framed pointed source. Explicit additional fixed powers of \(M^d\) and \(D_N(M)/N\), or their inverses, preserve the conclusion, including any retained polynomial \(N\)-prefactor: F(26) gives \(D_N(e^{u/N})/N=\sinh u/[N\sinh(u/N)]\), a uniformly bounded holomorphic unit with bounded inverse on the buffered collar. The full original tail is exactly \(\mathcal E_N(e^{u/N})\widehat{\mathcal P}_{N,\mathrm{tail}}\). Every true derivative retains the product rule \[ \partial_\mu^k\mathcal P_{N,\mathrm{tail}} =\sum_{a=0}^{k}\binom ka(\partial_\mu^a\mathcal E_N) (\partial_\mu^{k-a}\widehat{\mathcal P}_{N,\mathrm{tail}}). \tag{17} \] If the prescribed line is holomorphic on the buffered collar and \(\sup_{|u|\le\eta'}|\mathcal E_N(e^{u/N})|\le e^{o(N)}\), the same rate (15) holds for every full source jet by Cauchy. Otherwise (13)--(14),(17) retain its exact size and derivatives; no subexponential bound for an unspecified external line is assumed. A meromorphic line is retained as a Laurent germ, with its prescribed finite part taken only after multiplication; its additional pole and jet orders are not suppressed. The radial tail becomes exponentially small in absolute size for \(R>\exp(4\cdot9cv_3/(2\pi))\), after any retained subexponential line. This gives neither relative angular localization nor a nonzero closing contraction. The reduced axis trace has an additional prefix coupon and is not covered by (11) merely by renaming the source; an equality after the full axis contraction does not give separate sample bounds or identify geometrically localized densities. Arbitrary inserted marks likewise require their own bounds. The meridian normal is transported by the actual fixed banks; geometric cycle selection and an arbitrary-short-component lower bound remain open. ## Complete proof directs and author verification * F: `notes/research_actual_meridian_source_frames.md` (506 lines), SHA256 `6f58fba195ba5e8208e1d5180a1d684b933f9f5d50eb28efc56609580fe29976`. * W: `notes/actual_whole_word_cyclic_dilog_resolvent_period.md` (290 lines), SHA256 `9725d8955cb9bf4770566756eb00470d7e990c7e06b9513276509b01a037d59d`. * H: `notes/actual_cyclic_dilog_hankel_cycle.md` (316 lines), SHA256 `502ddfc4b13c7bd775bf27398592085f3951019ff959e1fe6e363a1a468993ea`. * R: `notes/research_actual_reduced_braid_source.md` (330 lines), SHA256 `9a472ef27b08305a519ff1f24b6d2b909e63a0acbdc49b3a29e001c52a2f2243`. All four complete directs were freshly whole-read nontruncated in this active author sequence. Only written proofs and text/hash operations were used. No mathematical program, test, or build was run; frozen and public files were not edited.

title: Exact meridian frames for the actual opposite source
text: # Exact meridian frames for the actual opposite source Private written proof, 18 November 2026. The actual lowering coproduct is diagonally conjugate to its complete root value. A different, purely Cartan frame conjugates the raising coproduct and the entire prefix quotient. Their combination cancels the factorial meridian dependence of the middle turnover and, apart from its retained scalar, puts the remaining non-Cartan dependence of the opposite kernel in one explicit diagonal insertion. The true first meridian jet follows by the product rule. Both frames have polynomial conditioning on a fixed scaled meridian disk. The complete direct J supplies the literal finite matrices, quotient, turnover, and source normalization; B supplies the ordered balanced crossings. Every new conjugation, normal formula, and bound is proved below. These are changes of presentation of the same finite source, not a simultaneous trivialization of its quantum-group representation or a relative estimate for a closed scalar. ## 1. The literal one-head lowering frame Fix \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\), and \(m\ge2\) heads. The quantum parameter stays fixed. Write \[ f_a=(Q;Q)_a,\qquad x=-M/q,\qquad J_iw_a=a w_a. \tag{1} \] The actual balanced arrows on each head are \[ E(M)w_a=(MQ^{-a}-M^{-1})w_{a-1}\ (a>0),\quad E(M)w_0=0, \qquad Fw_a=(1-Q^{a+1})w_{a+1},\quad Kw_a=xQ^{-a}w_a. \tag{2} \] The upper \(F\) arrow is zero. Define the meromorphic diagonal \[ h_a(M)=M^{-a}\frac{f_a}{(M^{-2}Q;Q)_a},\qquad h_0=1, \qquad D_h(M)w_a=h_a(M)w_a. \tag{3} \] It is an invertible holomorphic matrix near \(M=1\), and \(D_h(1)=I\). For \(a>0\), \[ \frac{h_{a-1}}{h_a} =M\frac{1-M^{-2}Q^a}{1-Q^a}. \] Multiplication by \(Q^{-a}-1\) therefore proves exactly \[ E(M)=D_h(M)E(1)D_h(M)^{-1},\qquad K(M)=M K(1). \tag{4} \] The forced bottom arrow is zero on both sides, including when \(M\ne1\). No cyclic bottom arrow has been added. J's balanced turnover is \[ C(M)w_b=c_b(M)w_{d-b},\qquad c_b(M)=\prod_{j=1}^b\frac{MQ^j-M^{-1}}{1-Q^j}, \qquad C_0w_b=(-1)^b w_{d-b}. \tag{5} \] Put \(D_N(z)=(z^N-z^{-N})/(z-z^{-1})\) with its Laurent polynomial continuation, and \(s_N(M)=D_N(M)/N\). Then \[ \boxed{\quad C(M)=s_N(M)D_h(M)C_0.\quad} \tag{6} \] Indeed \(c_b/[(-1)^b h_{d-b}]\) has consecutive ratio one: use \(Q^{d-b}=Q^{-b-1}\) in the ratio of (3). At \(b=0\) its value is \[ h_d^{-1}=M^d\frac{(M^{-2}Q;Q)_d}{N} =\frac{M^d}{N}\frac{1-M^{-2N}}{1-M^{-2}} =s_N(M). \] All removable values are interpreted by continuation. This is a whole-meridian identity at the fixed quantum root; no root reflection has been differentiated in \(q\). ## 2. Two exact tensor frames Let \(E_0=E_\Sigma(1)\), \(F_0=F_\Sigma(1)\), and define \[ A_E(M)=\bigotimes_{i=1}^m \bigl[D_h(M)M^{-(m-i)J_i}\bigr],\quad B_F(M)=M^{-\sum_{i=1}^m(i-1)J_i},\quad B_E(M)=M^{\sum_{i=1}^m(m-i)J_i}. \tag{7} \] All these matrices are diagonal. The ordered coproducts are \[ E_\Sigma(M)=\sum_{i=1}^m E_i(M)\prod_{j>i}K_j(M),\qquad F_\Sigma(M)=\sum_{i=1}^m\left(\prod_{j<i}K_j(M)^{-1}\right)F_i. \tag{8} \] A lowering arrow conjugated by \(M^{-aJ}\) gains \(M^a\); a raising arrow gains \(M^{-a}\). Equations (4),(8) consequently give \[ \boxed{\quad E_\Sigma(M)=A_E(M)E_0A_E(M)^{-1},\qquad F_\Sigma(M)=B_F(M)F_0B_F(M)^{-1}. \quad}\tag{9} \] The first formula supplies exactly the \(M^{m-i}\) of the right Cartan tail; the second supplies the \(M^{-(i-1)}\) of the left inverse Cartan prefix. In particular, for every polynomial \(p\) with meridian-independent coefficients, \[ p(E_\Sigma(M))=A_E(M)p(E_0)A_E(M)^{-1}. \tag{10} \] This includes the actual finite Euler polynomial \(\sum_{n<N}\lambda^nE_\Sigma(M)^n/f_n\) at fixed \(\lambda\). It does not replace a polynomial with shifted denominators \((M^{-2}Q;Q)_n\). Any meridian dependence in \(\lambda\) or the coefficients retains its own derivative. Let \(L_1w_a=w_{a-1}\), with bottom zero, and let \(F_{\rm r}(M)\) be the ordered raising coproduct on heads \(2,\ldots,m\). J's prefix and quotient are \[ S(M)=\sum_{n=0}^d\frac{(x^{-1}L_1F_{\rm r}(M))^n}{f_n}, \qquad q_F(M)=p_0S(M)^{-1},\qquad i_F(M)=i_0. \tag{11} \] Write \(S_0=S(1)\), \(q_0=p_0S_0^{-1}\), and \[ B_{\rm t}(M)=M^{-\sum_{i=2}^m(i-1)J_i} \] on the remaining-head space \(U\). The first exponent in \(B_F\) is zero, so \(L_1\) is unchanged. The term on head \(i\ge2\) in \(x^{-1}F_{\rm r}(M)\) has meridian power \(M^{-(i-1)}\). Hence, exactly, \[ S(M)=B_F(M)S_0B_F(M)^{-1},\qquad \boxed{\ q_F(M)=B_{\rm t}(M)q_0B_F(M)^{-1}.\ } \tag{12} \] Here \(p_0B_F=B_{\rm t}p_0\) and \(B_Fi_0=i_0B_{\rm t}\). The entire finite prefix sum and its inverse are retained, including every endpoint. The two frames are different. In particular \(K_\Sigma(M)\) still has its scalar factor \(M^m\); (9) does not assert a single simultaneous conjugation of \(E,F,K\) to their root values. ## 3. One diagonal insertion in the actual opposite kernel Let \(\mathsf J\) reverse the tensor factors, and put \(\mathscr C_0=C_0^{\otimes m}\mathsf J\). The actual turnover is \(\mathscr C(M)=C(M)^{\otimes m}\mathsf J\). From (6),(7), \[ A_E(M)^{-1}\mathscr C(M) =s_N(M)^m B_E(M)\mathscr C_0. \tag{13} \] Define the relative diagonal \[ D_{\rm rel}(M)=B_F(M)^{-1}A_E(M) =\bigotimes_{i=1}^m \bigl[D_h(M)M^{(2i-m-1)J_i}\bigr]. \tag{14} \] J's actual analytic opposite map, with its original normalization, is \[ T(M)=q_F(M)E_\Sigma(M)^d\mathscr C(M)i_0. \] Equations (9),(12),(13) give the exact presentation \[ \boxed{\quad T(M)=s_N(M)^m B_{\rm t}(M)q_0D_{\rm rel}(M) E_0^dB_E(M)\mathscr C_0i_0. \quad}\tag{15} \] Apart from the displayed scalar \(s_N(M)^m\), only the diagonal insertion has non-Cartan meridian dependence. No new prefix or Euler kernel has been substituted. There is a useful equivalent symmetric Cartan placement. Set \(\xi=d\,m(m-1)/2\). Complementing and reversing each occupation in \(\mathscr C_0\) gives \[ B_E(M)\mathscr C_0=M^\xi\mathscr C_0B_F(M). \] Thus \[ \boxed{\quad T(M)=s_N(M)^m M^\xi B_{\rm t}(M) [q_0D_{\rm rel}(M)E_0^d\mathscr C_0i_0] B_{\rm t}(M). \quad}\tag{16} \] The two tail factors in (16) have the same sign. The scalar \(M^\xi\) and the tensor reversal are part of the identity. ## 4. The true first normal and the source finite part All derivatives in this section are with respect to \(\mu=\log M\) at \(\mu=0\), with \(q\) fixed. Let \[ \Sigma_{a,N}=\sum_{j=1}^a\frac{Q^j}{1-Q^j},\quad \Sigma_{0,N}=0. \] Direct differentiation of (3) gives \[ (\log h_a)'=-a-2\Sigma_{a,N}. \tag{17} \] Consequently the lowering-frame generator and relative generator are \[ \mathcal H=A_E'(1)= \sum_i[-(m-i+1)J_i-2\Sigma_{J_i,N}],\qquad \mathcal L=D_{\rm rel}'(1)= \sum_i[(2i-m-2)J_i-2\Sigma_{J_i,N}]. \tag{18} \] The notation \(A_E'(1)\) means the stated \(\mu\)-derivative. Since \(A_E(1)=I\), (10) gives the exact commutator \[ \left.\partial_\mu p(E_\Sigma(e^\mu))\right|_0 =[\mathcal H,p(E_0)]. \tag{19} \] This formula retains the actual bottom-zero normal. It is not obtained by differentiating a meridian-independent root symbol. Put \(\mathcal B=-\sum_{i=2}^m(i-1)J_i\) on \(U\). The Laurent polynomial \(D_N(e^\mu)\) is even in \(\mu\), so \(s_N(1)=1\) and \(s_N'(1)=0\).
