With \[ T_0=q_0E_0^d\mathscr C_0i_0,\qquad \mathcal V=q_0\mathcal L E_0^d\mathscr C_0i_0, \] differentiation of (16) therefore yields the true ordered row \[ \boxed{\quad T_1:=\left.\partial_\mu T(e^\mu)\right|_0 =\xi T_0+\mathcal B T_0+T_0\mathcal B+\mathcal V. \quad}\tag{20} \] No derivative of \(q_F\) or turnover has been discarded: (12)--(16) have evaluated them before this product rule. To retain the original normalized source, let \(r=m-1\), \(K_{\rm r}(M)=M^rK_0\), and \(\varepsilon=K_0^N=(-1)^{(N+1)r}\). J's normalization is \[ J_{\rm op}(M)=H(M)^{-1}T(M),\qquad H(M)=D_N(M^mK_0). \tag{21} \] Its exact diagonal inverse has expansion \[ H(e^\mu)^{-1}=\frac{U_{-1}}{\mu}+U_0+O(\mu),\qquad U_{-1}=\frac{K_0-K_0^{-1}}{2\varepsilon mN},\quad U_0=\frac{K_0+K_0^{-1}}{2\varepsilon N}. \tag{22} \] This follows by expanding \((M^mK_0-M^{-m}K_0^{-1})/ [\varepsilon(M^{mN}-M^{-mN})]\); it includes the removable self weights. Therefore the actual residue and finite part are \[ \operatorname{Res}_{\mu=0}J_{\rm op}=U_{-1}T_0,\qquad \operatorname{FP}_{\mu=0}J_{\rm op}=U_0T_0+U_{-1}T_1, \tag{23} \] with \(T_1\) given by (20). The diagonal factors are on the left, as in the actual source. Individual windows and insertions still retain the normal rows in J; (23) does not remove their defects. ## 5. Polynomial conditioning on the whole scaled collar Use the original binomial head metric \(\|w_a\|^2=\binom da^{-1}\) and its tensor products. Fix \(0<\eta<\pi\) and put \(M=e^{u/N}\), \(|u|\le\eta\). There are no zeros of any factor in (3) on this disk. More quantitatively, for \(1\le j<N\), \[ 1-e^{-2u/N}Q^j =-2i e^{\pi i j/N-u/N} \sin((\pi j+i u)/N). \] The real part of the sine argument lies strictly between zero and \(\pi\). Since \(|\sin z|\ge|\sin\operatorname{Re}z|\), the elementary sine bound on this interval gives \[ |1-e^{-2u/N}Q^j| \ge \frac{4(\pi-\eta)}{\pi}e^{-\eta/2} \frac{\min(j,N-j)}N. \tag{24} \] Here \(\pi\min(j,N-j)-\eta\ge(\pi-\eta)\min(j,N-j)\), and \(N\ge2\) was used in the exponential factor. The analytic logarithm of each \(h_a(e^{u/N})\) is normalized to zero at \(u=0\). Differentiating it gives \[ \partial_u\log h_a(e^{u/N}) =-\frac aN-\frac2N\sum_{j=1}^a \frac{e^{-2u/N}Q^j}{1-e^{-2u/N}Q^j}. \] By (24) its absolute value is at most \(C_\eta\log(N+1)\), uniformly in every \(0\le a<N\). Integrating along the straight segment from zero proves \[ (N+1)^{-C_\eta}\le |h_a(e^{u/N})| \le(N+1)^{C_\eta}. \tag{25} \] The same bound holds for the inverse. All Cartan factors in (7),(14),(16) have uniformly bounded modulus and inverse on this collar, for fixed \(m\). Also \[ s_N(e^{u/N})=\frac{\sinh u}{N\sinh(u/N)} \tag{26} \] is a uniformly bounded holomorphic unit with bounded inverse on \(|u|\le\eta\); the values at zero are removable, and the nearest nonzero zeros of \(\sinh u\) are at \(\pm\pi i\). For example write (26) as the quotient of \(\sinh u/u\) and \(\sinh(u/N)/(u/N)\) on their indicated compact zero-free disks. Diagonal operator norms in the binomial metric are the maxima of their entries. Equations (25)--(26) thus give polynomial bounds, uniform over all head occupations, for \(A_E^{\pm1}\), \(D_{\rm rel}^{\pm1}\), and the bounded Cartan frames. Choose \(\eta<\eta'<\pi\) and apply Cauchy's estimates on the larger disk: every fixed \(u\)-derivative has polynomial cost as well. A fixed \(\mu\)-derivative costs a further \(N\) per derivative, since \(\partial_\mu=N\partial_u\). At the root, (17)--(18),(24) give directly \[ \|\mathcal H\|+\|\mathcal L\| \le C_m N\log(N+1). \tag{27} \] These are bounds for the specified frames and insertions. They are not relative bounds on \(T(M)/T_0\), on individual matrix entries, or on a closing scalar that may cancel. ## 6. Original marks, cut, and pivot The F frame has an exact adapter for an arbitrary actual matrix \(A(M)\), without an intertwining assumption: \[ q_F(M)A(M)i_0 =B_{\rm t}(M) [q_0\widetilde A(M)i_0]B_{\rm t}(M)^{-1}, \qquad \widetilde A(M)=B_F(M)^{-1}A(M)B_F(M). \tag{28} \] Every crossing or mark in a product is transported in that order; adjacent frame factors cancel exactly. At the first normal, \[ \widetilde A_1=A_1+[A_0,\mathcal B_F],\qquad \mathcal B_F=-\sum_i(i-1)J_i. \tag{29} \] Thus transported marks do not have unchanged normal matrices. The original pointed pivot is \(P_0\otimes K_{\rm r}(M)^{1-N}\). It commutes with \(B_F\). Writing \(g_0=K_0^{1-N}\), cyclicity gives the exact source identity for every \(A\), \[ \operatorname{Tr}[(P_0\otimes K_{\rm r}(M)^{1-N})A(M)] =M^{-rd}\operatorname{Tr}[(P_0\otimes g_0)\widetilde A(M)]. \tag{30} \] All original external scalars and framing factors remain in \(A\); the explicit pivot power in (30) is not suppressed. The source-normalized trace formula of J can additionally be used for its actual total intertwiners. It is not imposed on arbitrary marks merely because (28) exists. In coherent resolutions these diagonal transformations act on both sides of the finite kernels and on the retained source coupons. A partial resolution or relative window is transported as a matrix too. No claim that its original real chain is fixed, or that its boundary current vanishes, follows from (9),(12), or the polynomial conditioning. The exact finite frame and isolated insertion (14),(20),(23) therefore preserve the original source. The following local crossing calculation makes the same normal adapter explicit for every fixed original braid word. ## 7. Literal crossing and whole-braid first jets Use two adjacent heads \(i,i+1\) at the same meridian, and set \(\mathcal J_i=J_i+J_{i+1}\). Retain the original common Cartan scalar \(\kappa(M)\). B gives the actual positive checked crossing and its finite nilpotent factor in the order \[ R_i^+(M)=\kappa(M)P_iD_i(M)\Theta_i(M),\qquad \Theta_i(M)=\sum_{n=0}^d \frac{(-1)^nq^{n^2}E_i(M)^nF_{i+1}^n}{f_n}, \tag{31} \] where \[ D_i(M)w_{a,b}=x^{-a-b}Q^{ab}w_{a,b} =M^{-a-b}D_i(1)w_{a,b}. \] These are the original finite heads, with no semicyclic wrap. The actual negative crossing is its inverse: the order is \(\kappa^{-1}\Theta_i^{-1}D_i^{-1}P_i\), and B gives \(\Theta_i^{-1}=\sum_{n<N}q^nE_i^nF_{i+1}^n/f_n\). Since \(F_{i+1}\) is meridian independent, (4) gives \(\Theta_i(M)=D_{h,i}(M)\Theta_i(1)D_{h,i}(M)^{-1}\). The diagonal factors commute, while \(P_iD_{h,i}=D_{h,i+1}P_i\). Therefore, including the scalar, \[ \boxed{\begin{split} R_i^+(M) &=\frac{\kappa(M)}{\kappa(1)}M^{-\mathcal J_i} D_{h,i+1}(M)R_i^+(1)D_{h,i}(M)^{-1},\\ R_i^-(M) &=\frac{\kappa(1)}{\kappa(M)}M^{\mathcal J_i} D_{h,i}(M)R_i^-(1)D_{h,i+1}(M)^{-1}. \end{split}}\tag{32} \] The second formula follows by taking the actual inverse of the first. In moving \(M^{\mathcal J_i}\) to the left one uses exact conservation of the sum of the two occupations. In particular the checked flip has changed the location of the left \(D_h\); it cannot be omitted from this calculation. Put \[ \ell_i=-J_i-2\Sigma_{J_i,N},\qquad \gamma_\kappa=\left.\partial_\mu\log\kappa(e^\mu)\right|_0, \qquad R_{i,0}^\pm=R_i^\pm(1). \] Differentiating (32) in the actual fixed-\(q\) family yields \[ \boxed{\begin{split} R_{i,1}^+ &=(\gamma_\kappa I-\mathcal J_i+\ell_{i+1})R_{i,0}^+ -R_{i,0}^+\ell_i,\\ R_{i,1}^- &=(-\gamma_\kappa I+\mathcal J_i+\ell_i)R_{i,0}^- -R_{i,0}^-\ell_{i+1}. \end{split}}\tag{33} \] All new matrix insertions here are diagonal and have norm \(O(N\log(N+1))\) in the original binomial metric. The original scalar derivative \(\gamma_\kappa\) is displayed, not absorbed into that bound. More explicitly, let an actual fixed marked word be \[ W(M)=\zeta(M)A_L(M)\cdots A_1(M), \] where the \(A_j\) are literal signed crossings or prescribed marks, and \(\zeta\) retains any original external and zero-framing line. Its true first normal is exactly \[ W_1=\zeta_1 A_{L,0}\cdots A_{1,0} +\zeta_0\sum_{j=1}^L A_{L,0}\cdots A_{j+1,0}A_{j,1}A_{j-1,0}\cdots A_{1,0}. \tag{34} \] For crossing factors substitute (33); for a mark retain its prescribed derivative. Thus a fixed unmarked braid has a finite root-word expression for its first normal with the explicit diagonal insertions (33) and the original scalar derivatives. No cancellation of adjacent \(D_h\)'s is assumed. Bounds for additional marks are not supplied by their mere insertion. Higher fixed meridian derivatives can likewise use the exact factorization (32) and the polynomial collar bounds, with all scalar derivatives retained. In the original highest-cut pivotal functional this gives \[ \left.\partial_\mu\operatorname{Tr} [(P_0\otimes K_{\rm r}(e^\mu)^{1-N})W(e^\mu)]\right|_0 =\operatorname{Tr}[(P_0\otimes g_0)(W_1-rd\,W_0)]. \tag{35} \] The pivot derivative, \(\kappa\), zero-framing line, and every marked normal are therefore explicit. Equations (32)--(35) concern fixed-root meridian derivatives, not quantum-parameter derivatives or an ordinary-color path without its full adapter. They do not bound a relative closing scalar or establish noncancellation after contraction. Analytic composition and geometric source contributions remain separate. ## Complete proof direct * J: notes/research_opposite_polarization_source_kernel.md, SHA256 d52c6dd8e62f575a262fc7af460e258f7cb0e40b5a9c037ac46dd8d151002d44. * B: notes/balanced_verma_coherent_braiding.md, SHA256 0203bdd7dbb36a4f8deb1c310b3445608e53d10922049447da8eecec4f87d1c4. Both complete directs were freshly read nontruncated in this active author sequence. Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used. Frozen and public files were not edited.

title: Gaussian and endpoint kernels for the actual Newton crossing
text: # Gaussian and endpoint kernels for the actual Newton crossing 20 November 2026. The full original crossing has a positive Hermitian row covariance, even though its phases cannot all be removed by a diagonal change of coordinates. This note calculates that covariance in two regimes. In the interior of the Newton index interval its normalized kernel is Gaussian at scale \(\sqrt N\). At either endpoint, any fixed number of rows has the same explicit Pascal moment kernel after the stated polynomial row rescaling. These are asymptotics of the actual finite crossing, with its Cartan scalar and both closing indices retained. The results do not give a norm estimate for an arbitrary short tangle. They do not identify a reflected norm with the original scalar closure, or show that its geometric contribution survives arbitrary gluing. ## 1. The exact covariance and its phases Put \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\), and \[ s_0=1,\qquad s_a=\prod_{u=1}^a2\sin(\pi u/N),\qquad \beta_{ik}=\frac{s_i}{s_ks_{i-k}}\quad(0\leq k\leq i\leq d). \tag{1} \] Set \(\beta_{ik}=0\) outside this triangular support. The actual Newton crossing of [the source-exact crossing theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_newton_twist_canonical_graph.md), Section 1, is \[ T_{ik}=\kappa(-1)^iq^{i+k^2}{i\brack k}_Q, \qquad \kappa=q^{d^2/2}. \tag{2} \] All fractional powers of \(q\) in this note mean their displayed exponentials. The finite root factorial phase gives \[ {i\brack k}_Q=q^{k(i-k)}\beta_{ik},\qquad T_{ik}=\kappa D_iq^{ik}\beta_{ik},\qquad D_i=(-1)^iq^i. \tag{3} \] Thus no quadratic phase in \(k\) has been omitted from (2); it has combined with the actual factorial phase in (3). Write \(D=\operatorname{diag}(D_i)\). Define the covariance and a fixed diagonal unitary matrix by \[ \mathcal C=TT^*,\qquad U_i=D_iq^{i^2/4},\qquad K=U^*\mathcal C U. \] Here and below \(U_i\) denotes the \(i\)-th diagonal entry of \(U\). The exact kernel is \[ K_{ij}=q^{-(i^2-j^2)/4} \sum_{k=0}^{\min(i,j)}\beta_{ik}\beta_{jk}q^{(i-j)k}. \tag{4} \] The scalar \(\kappa\) cancels in this covariance because \(|\kappa|=1\); it remains in the actual rows \(T\). The unitary matrix \(U\) is explicit and independent of any tangle value. Formula (4) does not assert that \(K\) is entrywise real at finite \(N\). Both original closures remain those of the complete Newton algebra: the cup-mark closure is coefficient row \(e_0^*\), and the cylindrical closure with its original ordinary trace and mark is row \(e_d^*\). The exact physical-source intertwiner and all external framing factors are those of the cited crossing theorem, Section 4. In particular, \(i=0,d\) below refer to these same Newton boundary indices. ## 2. The uniform interior theorem Let \[ J(x)=\int_0^x\log(2\sin\pi t)\,dt,\qquad B(x)=J(x)-2J(x/2),\qquad c(x)=\pi\cot(\pi x/2). \] For a compact interval \(I\subset(0,1)\), the row energies satisfy, uniformly for \(x=i/N\in I\), \[ \boxed{\quad \mathcal C_{ii} =\sqrt{\frac{c(x)}{2\pi N}}\, e^{2NB(x)}(1+o(1)). \quad} \tag{5} \] For each fixed \(H<\infty\), put \[ a=\frac{i+j}{2N},\qquad h=\frac{i-j}{\sqrt N}. \] Then, uniformly over \(a\in I\), \(|h|\leq H\), \[ \boxed{\quad \frac{K_{ij}}{\sqrt{\mathcal C_{ii}\mathcal C_{jj}}} =\exp\!\left[-\frac{\pi h^2}{4\sin(\pi a)}\right]+o(1). \quad} \tag{6} \] Uniformity includes arbitrary integer choices of \(i,j\) in this range. No parity subsequence or rounding convention is required. ### 2.1 Factorial estimates with their prefactors For every compact subinterval of \((0,1)\), uniformly for \(x=n/N\) in that subinterval, \[ s_n=\sqrt{2N\sin\pi x}\,e^{NJ(x)}(1+O(N^{-1})). \tag{7} \] To prove (7), write \(h_0(t)=\log(\sin\pi t/(\pi t))\). It extends smoothly at zero and has bounded derivatives on \([0,1-\delta]\). Stirling's formula and the trapezoidal sum estimate give \[ \begin{split} \log s_n &=n\log(2\pi/N)+\log(n!)+\sum_{u=1}^nh_0(u/N)\\ &=NJ(x)+\tfrac12\log(2\pi Nx)+\tfrac12h_0(x)+O(N^{-1})\\ &=NJ(x)+\tfrac12\log(2N\sin\pi x)+O(N^{-1}). \end{split} \] The errors are uniform because \(n\) is a fixed positive fraction of \(N\). We will also use the weaker endpoint-uniform estimate \[ \log s_n=NJ(n/N)+O(\log N),\qquad 0\leq n<N. \tag{8} \] Subtracting \(\log t+\log(1-t)\) from \(\log(2\sin\pi t)\) leaves a continuously differentiable function on \([0,1]\). Its Riemann-sum error is bounded uniformly in the upper endpoint. Integral comparison for the two logarithms gives the \(O(\log N)\) error. This proves (8), including \(n=0,N-1\). Put \[ b(x,z)=J(x)-J(z)-J(x-z),\qquad 0\leq z\leq x<1. \] Where \(x,z,x-z\) stay in fixed interior intervals, (7) implies \[ \beta_{ik} =\frac1{\sqrt{2N}} \sqrt{\frac{\sin\pi x}{\sin\pi z\sin\pi(x-z)}} e^{Nb(x,z)}(1+O(N^{-1})), \quad x=i/N,\ z=k/N. \tag{9} \] Its maximum in \(z\) is at \(x/2\), because it is symmetric and \[ b_{zz}(x,z) =-\pi\frac{\sin\pi x}{\sin\pi z\sin\pi(x-z)}<0. \tag{10} \] For \(x\in I\), the negative quadratic bound from (10) can be chosen uniformly on the whole open interval \(0<z<x\). Estimate (8) then controls the same tails with at most a polynomial factor. ### 2.2 The row energy Set \(x=i/N\) and \(t=(k-Nx/2)/\sqrt N\). On each fixed bounded \(t\)-interval, (9) and Taylor expansion give \[ \beta_{ik}^2 =\frac{c(x)}{\pi N}e^{2NB(x)} e^{-2c(x)t^2}(1+o(1)), \tag{11} \] uniformly for \(x\in I\). The lattice spacing in \(t\) is \(N^{-1/2}\). Hence summing (11) gives (5), since \(\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-2ct^2}dt=\sqrt{\pi/(2c)}\). Here is a common tail justification for this step and the next. Choose \(0<\varepsilon<1/6\). On \(|t|\leq N^\varepsilon\), third derivatives on a fixed interior neighborhood bound the exponent remainder by \(O(N^{-1/2+3\varepsilon})=o(1)\); (9)'s prefactors are uniformly smooth there. Outside this range, (10) and (8) bound the normalized sum by a polynomial times \(e^{-c_0N^{2\varepsilon}}\), uniformly in \(x\in I\), for some \(c_0>0\). In the interior range, a uniform Gaussian bound gives the usual Riemann-sum convergence. This proves the displayed estimates uniformly, rather than only at one selected central lattice point. For the mixed sum, apply the same quadratic bound separately at \(x=i/N\) and \(x=j/N\). Their maximizing indices differ by \(O(\sqrt N)\); the sum of the two quadratic bounds is centered at \((i+j)/4\). This gives the same tail estimate about that center. ### 2.3 The mixed kernel Write \(i/N=a+\epsilon\), \(j/N=a-\epsilon\), where \(\epsilon=h/(2\sqrt N)\), and set \(t=(k-Na/2)/\sqrt N\). Let \(c=c(a)\). The sum of the two real exponents in (9) is \[ \begin{split} N\{b(a+\epsilon,k/N)+b(a-\epsilon,k/N)\} =2NB(a)+\frac{h^2}{4}\{J''(a)-c\}-2ct^2+o(1). \end{split} \tag{12} \] Indeed \(b_z(a,a/2)=0\), \(b_{zz}(a,a/2)=-2c\), and \(b_{xx}(a,a/2)=J''(a)-c\). The mixed \(\epsilon t\) terms cancel between the two copies. The prefactor product in (9) is \(c/(\pi N)(1+o(1))\) in this range. The phase in (4) is exactly \[ q^{(i-j)k}=q^{(i^2-j^2)/4}e^{i\pi ht}. \tag{13} \] The chirp already included in \(K\) removes the first factor. Using the uniform tail argument above, the remaining mixed sum is therefore its real Gaussian integral with Fourier multiplier \(e^{i\pi ht}\). Its ratio to the zero-frequency integral is \[ \frac{\int e^{-2ct^2+i\pi ht}dt} {\int e^{-2ct^2}dt} =e^{-\pi^2h^2/(8c)}. \tag{14} \] Finally \(B''(a)=J''(a)-c/2\). Comparing (12) with the two diagonal exponents in (5) contributes the further factor \(e^{-ch^2/8}\). Since \[ c+\pi^2/c=\frac{2\pi}{\sin\pi a}, \] their product is (6). This completes the uniform proof of the interior theorem. ## 3. Both endpoint limits Fix a nonnegative integer \(R\). In this section \(0\leq r,s\leq R\) are fixed while \(N\) tends to infinity. They count Newton rows from an endpoint; they are not reinterpreted as Casimir derivative orders. Define the positive matrix \[ A_{rs}=\binom{r+s}{r}\qquad(0\leq r,s\leq R). \tag{15} \] At the lower endpoint, \[ K_{rs}\longrightarrow A_{rs}. \tag{16} \] At the upper endpoint put \[ W_{N,r}=\sqrt N\,\frac{(N/(2\pi))^r}{r!}. \] Then \[ \boxed{\quad \frac{K_{d-r,d-s}}{W_{N,r}W_{N,s}} \longrightarrow A_{rs}. \quad} \tag{17} \] The convergence is simultaneous on each fixed finite block. Consequently either endpoint has normalized correlation limit \[ \frac{A_{rs}}{\sqrt{A_{rr}A_{ss}}} =\frac{(r+s)!}{\sqrt{(2r)!(2s)!}}. \tag{18} \] For (16), fixed factorial indices in (1) give \(\beta_{rk}\to\binom rk\). All phase factors in (4) tend to one, so its limit is \(\sum_k\binom rk\binom sk=\binom{r+s}{r}\), by Vandermonde. For (17), the exact reflection identity \(s_as_{d-a}=N\) gives \[ \beta_{d-r,k}=\frac{s_{k+r}}{s_rs_k} =\frac{\prod_{u=1}^r2\sin(\pi(k+u)/N)}{s_r}, \qquad 0\leq k\leq d-r. \tag{19} \] Since \(s_r=(2\pi/N)^rr!(1+O_R(N^{-2}))\), zero extension past this support gives the uniform limit \[ N^{-r}\beta_{d-r,k} =\frac{\sin^r(\pi k/N)}{\pi^rr!}+O_R(N^{-1}) \qquad(0\leq k<N). \tag{20} \] For \(r>0\), the omitted last \(r\) terms obey the same error bound because their \(\sin^r(\pi k/N)=O_R(N^{-r})\). For \(r=0\), the formula is exact and all indices occur. Before the chirp in (4), the scaled covariance is thus a Riemann sum: \[ \begin{split} &N^{-(r+s+1)}(D^*\mathcal CD)_{d-r,d-s}\\ &\hspace{8mm}\longrightarrow \frac1{\pi^{r+s}r!s!} \int_0^1\sin^{r+s}(\pi t)e^{i\pi(s-r)t}\,dt. \end{split} \tag{21} \] Expanding the sine power into exponentials gives exactly \[ \int_0^1\sin^{r+s}(\pi t)e^{i\pi(s-r)t}dt =\mathrm i^{s-r}2^{-(r+s)}\binom{r+s}{r}. \tag{22} \] Indeed every exponential has integer even frequency on \([0,\pi]\); only its constant term survives. Here \(\mathrm i\) is the imaginary unit. The chirp factor in (4), at \(i=d-r,j=d-s\), tends to \(\mathrm i^{r-s}\). Equations (21)--(22) therefore give (17), with its precise positive row factors. In particular \[ \mathcal C_{d-r,d-r} \sim\frac{N^{2r+1}}{(2\pi)^{2r}(r!)^2}\binom{2r}{r}. \tag{23} \] The case \(r=0\) is the exact identity \(\mathcal C_{dd}=N\); the original last closing row is included. ## 4. An explicit orthogonal frame on each fixed endpoint block Let \(P\) be the \((R+1)\)-dimensional lower triangular Pascal matrix, \[ P_{rk}=\binom rk\ (k\leq r),\qquad (P^{-1})_{rk}=(-1)^{r-k}\binom rk. \] Vandermonde gives the exact factorization \[ A=PP^{\mathsf T}. \tag{24} \] Alternatively, (18) is the Gram of the normalized monomials \(t^r/\sqrt{(2r)!}\) in \(L^2(\mathbb R_+,e^{-t}dt)\). Both descriptions prove strict positive definiteness of every fixed block. Take the actual row vectors of \(U^*T\). On its lower endpoint block, apply \(P^{-1}\). On its upper endpoint block, in the order \(d,d-1,\ldots,d-R\), first divide row \(r\) by \(W_{N,r}\), then apply \(P^{-1}\). Equations (16)--(17) and (24) say that the resulting row Grams converge to the identity. Their condition numbers are therefore uniformly bounded for all sufficiently large \(N\), with \(R\) fixed. The only \(N\)-dependent magnitudes in this orthogonalization are the displayed polynomial factors \(W_{N,r}\). The two endpoint blocks can also be used together. For fixed \(r,s\leq R\), the sum for the mixed entry has only \(k\leq r\). Formula (19) at fixed \(k\) gives \(\beta_{d-s,k}\to\binom{s+k}{s}\), while \(q^{(r-d+s)k}\to(-1)^k\). Consequently \[ (D^*\mathcal CD)_{r,d-s} \longrightarrow\sum_{k=0}^r(-1)^k\binom rk\binom{s+k}{s} =(-1)^r\binom sr. \tag{25} \] The last binomial is zero when \(r>s\). One proof extracts the coefficient of \(z^s\) from \((1+z)^s[1-(1+z)]^r=(-1)^rz^r(1+z)^s\). The extra chirp has modulus one, so the corresponding mixed \(K\)-entries are \(O_R(1)\). Dividing the upper rows by \(W_{N,s}\) makes the whole mixed block tend to zero. For \(N>2R+1\), the lower and upper row sets are disjoint. Stack their two explicitly rescaled and Pascal-transformed row families. Its full Gram, including the mixed block, therefore obeys \[ \operatorname{Gram}(\text{combined endpoint rows}) \longrightarrow I_{2R+2}. \tag{26} \] This is simultaneous asymptotic orthogonality of the two finite boundary windows, with their actual mixed phases retained. The first row of \(P^{-1}\) is \(e_0^*\). Thus the original endpoint row is kept: at the upper endpoint it is exactly \(\overline{U_d}\,e_d^*T/\sqrt N\), and at the lower endpoint it is \(e_0^*T\). These known phases and powers of \(N\) are retained when pairing with an actual source. No unknown period defines the frame or its normalization. This is a fixed-\(R\) result. It supplies no uniform conditioning when \(R\) grows proportionally to \(N\), and no completeness claim for a truncated endpoint packet. The whole crossing still contains every repeated-root channel of the original algebra. ## 5. Geometric meaning and the remaining gluing step The positive row amplitude in (1) is already an exact angle weight: \[ \beta_{ik}=N\,w_d(k,i-k,d-i),\qquad w_d(a,b,c)=\frac1{s_as_bs_c},\qquad a+b+c=d. \] The symmetric interior maximum is the ideal angle triple \((x/2,x/2,1-x)\), at the continuum scale. With \(\Lambda(\theta)=-\int_0^\theta\log(2\sin u)du\), \[ \pi B(x)=2\Lambda(\pi x/2)+\Lambda(\pi(1-x)) \] is its ideal tetrahedron volume. Formula (6) quantifies the actual overlap of neighboring row packets, including the Fourier phase. It is a nonzero Gaussian kernel after one explicit diagonal chirp; it is not obtained by replacing those phases with their magnitudes. The coefficient \(\sin(\pi a)\) in (6) is unchanged at leading order by the genuine turn's reflection \(a\mapsto1-a\). The two fixed endpoint limits likewise have the same moment matrix after their stated row weights. These facts describe local compatibility of the kernel. They do not give a global operator inequality for arbitrarily many rows or an arbitrary sequence of crossings and turns. In particular no statement here identifies this row covariance with the full main-color Plancherel energy, the quotient covariance \(C_E\) of a whole Conway expression, or the original scalar closing after an unspecified short component. Such an identity or a controlled composition theorem is still needed before these local orthogonal frames can prove the finite-exception volume statement. ## Direct sources and written proof check The author read both complete direct sources and checked the written finite identities and every asymptotic argument above. The source hashes used are: | Source | SHA-256 | |---|---| | [Actual crossing and original source](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_newton_twist_canonical_graph.md) | `387681510416839fd3407f730ab701c7c1c8855b73da66497756721234d4f6d9` | | [Earlier exact Gaussian frame](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_gaussian_frame_newton_transport.md) | `b6ed7fa19097323f76b0b22fb4fc7361b9d4e52c3f19d17c12d94c6fff623af9` | The earlier frame note provides exact reconstruction and explicit crossing kernels, but does not prove the bulk covariance limit or the two endpoint limits established here. No mathematical program, test, build or numerical calculation was used in this proof.

title: An exact oblique contour decomposition through the geometric point
text:
# An exact oblique contour decomposition through the geometric point Private written proof, 18 November 2026. For any fixed finite braid of a hyperbolic knot, the literal root state has an exact contour decomposition with a distinguished translated real sheet passing through the regular geometric point. Its local coefficient is \(+1\). The construction retains an exact physical boundary band, every initial mixed rectangle current, every translated side current and all other horizontal sheets. No factorial divisor occurs in the constructed bulk prisms. This supplies a whole-source domain and a relative-current decomposition, not a thimble coefficient or a scalar lower bound. The geometric centralizer remains a null direction. The retained boundary terms and other sheets have not been bounded by smaller actions. Their number or their geometric mass alone cannot provide that estimate. The complete proof directs are A, the literal factorial amplitude, and L, the local geometric period for any braid. All new coordinate, cell, translation and orientation calculations are given below. ## 1. Primitive cut-and-transfer coordinates and a strict interior Let the fixed braid have \(c\) crossings, let \(m=c+1\), and put \[ d=N-1,\qquad h=2\pi i/N,\qquad c_0=2\pi i. 	ag{1} \] Use as independent integer coordinates the cut occupation \(a\) and every signed-crossing transfer \(n_1,\ldots,n_c\). At a positive crossing the two oriented strand visits change occupation by \(-n_i,+n_i\); at a negative crossing they change it by \(+n_i,-n_i\). Traverse the single oriented knot from the cut. Every wire occupation is thereby an integer linear form \[ \ell_e(k)=a+\sum_i\epsilon_{ei}n_i, \qquad \epsilon_{ei}\in\{-1,0,1\}. 	ag{2} \] Each transfer is encountered with both signs before returning to the cut, so the final occupation is exactly \(a\). Conversely the cut and transfers of a matching state recover all its wires by this traversal. Thus these coordinates identify the whole matching lattice with \(\mathbb Z^m\), with no index factor. Equivalently, split each crossing into its two strand visits and join the donor to the receiver by a transfer edge. The wire edges form one directed knot cycle. That wire cycle with the cut edge removed is a spanning tree; the cut and \(c\) transfer edges are its chords. The traversal above is the direct integer reconstruction on this expanded graph. The actual support is exactly \[ S_N=\{k\in\mathbb Z^m:0\le \ell_e(k)\le d 	ext{ for every wire},\quad n_i\ge0\}. 	ag{3} \] The positive inequalities \(n_i\le a_{m in}\) and \(n_i\le d-b_{m in}\), and the analogous negative inequalities, are the nonnegativity and upper bounds of the output wires. In particular \(0\le n_i\le d\) follows from (3). All five factorial arguments of each literal crossing in A are wire occupations or transfers. No support value is extended cyclically or assigned an artificial negative factorial. Let \(\mathscr L\) be the finite list consisting of every wire form (2) and the coordinate forms \(n_i\). It has nonzero integer rows, and the support is equivalently \(0\le\ell(k)\le d\) for all \(\ell\in\mathscr L\). This list may contain repetitions. Set \[ L_0=\max_{\ell\in\mathscr L}\sum_j|\ell_j|, \qquad B\in\mathbb Z,\qquad B>L_0/2+2. 	ag{4} \] There is a strict real normalized interior independent of \(N\). Take \[ x^0_{m cut}=	frac12,\qquad x^0_{n_i}=\varepsilon_0= rac1{8(c+1)}. 	ag{5} \] During the knot traversal each transfer has coefficient \(0\) or \(\pm1\), so every wire lies strictly between \(3/8\) and \(5/8\). Every transfer equals \(\varepsilon_0>0\). Consequently all \(\ell(x^0)\) lie in a fixed compact subinterval of \((0,1)\). This also tracks the upper endpoint \(d=N-1\): for all sufficiently large \(N\), a fixed real neighborhood of \(Nx^0\) of radius proportional to \(N\) has every form in \([B,d-B]\). The required threshold may depend on the fixed braid. ## 2. The geometric chart and the literal holomorphic domains Use L's complex-binomial cut with parameter \(	heta\), and its original scalar normalization. Its actual interpolated summand will be denoted \(I_N(z)\), now in the coordinates of Section 1. It includes the exact binomial Gamma factor, signed crossing monomials, Cartan line, tail pivots and framing. The change from L's primitive chord coordinates to these coordinates is integral and unimodular. The cut clock and every transfer clock at its chosen geometric point are off the unit circle. Hence in the new coordinates the same point \(x^*\) satisfies \[ \Im x^*_j
e0\quad(1\le j\le m),\qquad \Im\ell(x^*)
e0\quad(\ell\in\mathscr L). 	ag{6} \] The wire assertions follow from the same common frame. All logarithmic flow relations remain exact under the coordinate change. The corrected integer character is correspondingly an integer vector \(q\in\mathbb Z^m\). Fix it once and put \[ J_N(z)=e^{-c_0q\cdot z}I_N(z). 	ag{7} \] At every original integer state the new character is one. Near \(x^*\), L gives the actual nonzero local amplitude, additive principal stationarity, and geometric action rate. No character is changed during the contour construction. We use two elementary consequences of A's exact marked product. The root factorial \(\widehat F_N(\zeta)\) is holomorphic and nonzero for \[ -1<\Re\zeta<N, 	ag{8} \] and also at every nonreal \(\zeta\). For (8), every Gamma argument in A's product has positive real part, and its normally convergent logarithm is finite. For nonreal \(\zeta\), \(\zeta/N\) lies in A's slit domain; its product there is holomorphic and nonzero. These are the same marked function. The binomial interpolant \[  rac{\Gamma(N)} {\Gamma(z_{m cut}+1)\Gamma(N-z_{m cut})} 	heta^{z_{m cut}}(1-	heta)^{d-z_{m cut}} 	ag{9} \] is entire in \(z_{m cut}\), with its fixed logarithms; it introduces zeros but no poles. All remaining exact monomials in \(I_N\) are entire nonzero exponentials. Therefore \(J_N\) is holomorphic on any region where every factorial form is either in (8) or nonreal. This conclusion concerns the actual full summand, not only its principal action. ## 3. Retain the whole boundary band Define the bulk states and their indicator by \[ R_N=\{k\in\mathbb Z^m:B\le\ell(k)\le d-B 	ext{ for every }\ell\in\mathscr L\}, \qquad \chi_N={ f1}_{R_N}. 	ag{10} \] They are a subset of \(S_N\). Keep the complementary states \(S_N\setminus R_N\) exactly as their original positively oriented small product tori. Denote their sum by \(\Gamma_N^{m band}\). Their radii can be chosen small and fixed in unscaled coordinates so that every factorial form has real part in \((-1,N)\) and no other integer pole is enclosed. Equation (8) verifies this at every supported state. The band is not discarded or estimated. There are \(O(N^{m-1})\) band states. Indeed every such state has some fixed nonzero integer form within a fixed distance of one of its two physical supporting hyperplanes. All independent coordinates lie in \([0,d]\). Fix the other \(m-1\) coordinates and one nonzero coefficient of that form; only \(O(1)\) choices of the remaining coordinate lie in the band. Sum over the finite list of forms. This count gives no bound on their weighted sum. For \(k\in R_N\), the closed unit cube \[ C_k=\prod_j[k_j-	frac12,k_j+	frac12],\qquad \Omega_N= igcup_{k\in R_N}C_k 	ag{11} \] has every factorial form in \([2,d-2]\) on its real points, by (4). The union is an oriented real polyhedral \(m\)-chain, with the standard \(dx_1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx_m\) orientation. It contains a real neighborhood of \(Nx^0\) of radius proportional to \(N\), for all sufficiently large \(N\). This holds even if \(Nx^0\) lies on a unit-cell boundary: all cells meeting a sufficiently small proportional neighborhood are bulk cells by the strict margin in (5). ## 4. Polarized residue kernels and initial rectangle currents Put \[ \epsilon_j=\operatorname{sgn}(\Im x^*_j),\qquad K_{\epsilon_j}(z_j)=\pi\cot(\pi z_j)-i\pi\epsilon_j, \] \[ \omega_N= rac1{(2\pi i)^m}J_N(z) \prod_jK_{\epsilon_j}(z_j)\,dz_1\cdots dz_m. 	ag{12} \] Every kernel has residue one at every integer. Thus the original small-torus residue identity is still exactly \[ \int_{\Gamma_N}\omega_N=K_N. 	ag{13} \] The subtraction in (12) is recorded off the lattice, not treated as equality of meromorphic integrands. Replacing one cotangent by its subtracted constant removes that coordinate's lattice-pole family and integrates to zero on each original supported torus. Choose a positive vector \(a=(a_1,\ldots,a_m)\) sufficiently close to \((|\Im x^*_1|,\ldots,|\Im x^*_m|)\) that \[ \operatorname{sgn}\ell(\epsilon a) =\operatorname{sgn}\Im\ell(x^*) \quad(\ell\in\mathscr L). 	ag{14} \] Here signs act coordinatewise, and the quantities are real. Require in addition \[ \ell(\sigma a)
e0 \quad(\ell\in\mathscr L,\ \sigma\in\{\pm1\}^m). 	ag{15} \] This is possible: (14) is an open condition at the original positive vector, while (15) excludes only finitely many proper real hyperplanes. Every row of \(\mathscr L\) is nonzero. Fix a small positive number \(\eta\). For each coordinate and integer \(l\), let \(H_{j,\sigma}^{\,l}\) be the interval \([l-	frac12,l+	frac12]+i\eta\sigma a_j\), oriented in increasing real direction. Let \(V_j^{\,l}\) be the interval \(l+	frac12+i[-\eta a_j,\eta a_j]\), oriented upward. The positively oriented rectangle boundary about \(l\) is \[ B_j^{\,l}=\sum_{\sigma=\pm1}(-\sigma)H_{j,\sigma}^{\,l} +V_j^{\,l}-V_j^{\,l-1}. 	ag{16} \] Every product rectangle over a bulk cell is a valid residue cycle: on its whole product box every factorial real part stays in \([2,d-2]\), and each coordinate rectangle encloses only its original integer. Its period is the corresponding literal summand. Expand \(\sum_k\chi_N(k)\prod_jB_j^{\,k_j}\) in the coordinate order \(1,\ldots,m\). For \(J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\), define \[ \Delta_J\chi_N(l)= \sum_{\delta\in\{0,1\}^{J}}(-1)^{|\delta|} \chi_N(l+\delta). 	ag{17} \] Finite index shifts in (16), with no integration by parts in the source, give the exact chain identity \[ \sum_k\chi_N(k)\prod_j B_j^{\,k_j} =\sum_{\sigma\in\{\pm1\}^m}c_\sigma (\Omega_N+i\eta\sigma a) +\mathcal M_N,\qquad c_\sigma=\prod_j(-\sigma_j), 	ag{18} \] where the complete mixed current is \[ \mathcal M_N= \sum_{\varnothing
e J\subseteq[m]}\ \sum_l \Delta_J\chi_N(l) \sum_{\sigma\in\{\pm1\}^{J^c}} \left(\prod_{j
otin J}(-\sigma_j)ight) \prod_{j=1}^m  egin{cases} V_j^{\,l_j},&j\in J,\ H_{j,\sigma_j}^{\,l_j},&j
otin J . \end{cases} 	ag{19} \] Products in (19) always have the stated coordinate orientation. These are explicit integer coefficients, including all intersections and cancellations; no mixed face is suppressed. Whenever \(\Delta_J\chi_N(l)
e0\), at least one adjacent cube is a bulk cube, and the displayed face lies in its boundary. Its factorial real parts therefore remain in the physical strip. Each vertical coordinate is half-integral in real part; each horizontal coordinate has nonzero imaginary part. Thus every cotangent factor is regular on the whole mixed current. Furthermore such a coefficient occurs only within a bounded unscaled distance of a facet of (10). If all defining indicators were constant on the cube \(l+\{0,1\}^{J}\), the alternating sum would vanish. A changing indicator has its defining form within \(\sum_{j\in J}|\ell_j|\) of its threshold. These currents are consequently in fixed-width physical facet bands, with all their exact multiplicities retained. They have \(O(N^{m-1})\) cells; several difference directions may lie on a single slanted facet, so higher codimension is not asserted. ## 5. Simultaneous oblique translation of each horizontal sheet Let \(v_\sigma=\sigma a\) and \(\delta=x^*-x^0\). For the preferred sign vector \(\epsilon\), choose the path \[ b_\epsilon(t)=(1-t)i\eta v_\epsilon+tN\delta, \qquad 0\le t\le1. 	ag{20} \] For every other sign vector choose \[ b_\sigma(t)=i igl((1-t)\eta+tN igr)v_\sigma. 	ag{21} \] All coordinates of \(x+b_\sigma(t)\), with \(x\in\Omega_N\), have fixed nonzero imaginary signs \(\sigma_j\). In (20) this uses \(\operatorname{sgn}\Im\delta_j=\epsilon_j\). Hence no coordinate lattice pole occurs in any prism. Every factorial form on these prisms has a fixed nonzero imaginary sign as well. For (21) this is (15). For (20), \[ \Im\ell(x+b_\epsilon(t)) =(1-t)\eta\ell(v_\epsilon) +tN\Im\ell(x^*), 	ag{22} \] whose two terms have the same nonzero sign by (14). For all sufficiently large \(N\) its absolute value is bounded below by a positive constant independent of \(N\). The same holds for (21). Section 2 proves that the entire literal summand is holomorphic on a neighborhood of every closed prism. Thus no additional factorial/source-divisor current is hidden in these translations. Give \([0,1]	imes\Omega_N\) the orientation \(dt\wedge dx\), and map it by \((t,x)\mapsto x+b_\sigma(t)\). Define \(\mathcal S_{\sigma,N}\) as the image of \([0,1]	imes\partial\Omega_N\), with the \(dt\)-then-boundary orientation. Since \[ \partial([0,1]	imes\Omega_N) =\{1\}	imes\Omega_N-\{0\}	imes\Omega_N -[0,1]	imes\partial\Omega_N, \] holomorphic Stokes gives exactly \[ \int_{\Omega_N+i\eta v_\sigma}\omega_N =\int_{\Omega_N+b_\sigma(1)}\omega_N -\int_{\mathcal S_{\sigma,N}}\omega_N. 	ag{23} \] This is a finite sum of ordinary polyhedral Stokes identities; internal cell sides cancel with opposite orientations. There is no appeal to a contour at infinity. Combining (13), (18), and (23) gives the full original scalar: \[  oxed{\displaystyle K_N= c_\epsilon\int_{\Omega_N+N\delta}\omega_N +\sum_{\sigma
e\epsilon} c_\sigma\int_{\Omega_N+iNv_\sigma}\omega_N +\int_{\Gamma_N^{m band}}\omega_N +\int_{\mathcal M_N}\omega_N -\sum_\sigma c_\sigma\int_{\mathcal S_{\sigma,N}}\omega_N .} 	ag{24} \] Every term and every sign in (24) has been specified. The band tori use the same polarized form (12); their residues remain the original boundary-state summands. No complementary real band has been set to zero. All constructed bulk currents have polynomial geometric mass in \(N\) for the fixed braid and chosen frame. The top sheets have \(O(N^m)\) volume; their boundary prisms have \(O(N^{m-1})\) unit facets and translation length \(O(N)\). The initial mixed currents have \(O(N^{m-1})\) fixed-size cells and bounded integer multiplicities. Every kernel factor on the latter and on the translated prisms is bounded independently of \(N\). These are geometric and kernel bounds, not bounds for \(J_N\) or the full weighted periods. ## 6. The distinguished sheet and what its coefficient means The preferred sheet contains \(Nx^*\), since \[ Nx^*=Nx^0+N\delta, 	ag{25} \] and \(\Omega_N\) contains a proportional neighborhood of \(Nx^0\). After scaling by \(N\), it therefore contains a fixed real neighborhood of the geometric point. All chord and factorial imaginary parts there are nonzero. L's actual local expansion and corrected geometric action apply to this same form. For \(z=Nx\) on this neighborhood, the polarized kernel satisfies \[ K_{\epsilon_j}(Nx_j) =-2\pi i\,\epsilon_j+O(e^{-\gamma N}). 	ag{26} \] Consequently its coefficient, including the rectangle orientation and residue normalization, is \[ c_\epsilon(2\pi i)^{-m} \prod_j(-2\pi i\epsilon_j)=1. 	ag{27} \] Thus the preferred top has the literal nonzero local amplitude of \(J_N(Nx)N^m\,dx\), multiplied by \(1+O(e^{-\gamma N})\). Its coefficient in this explicit current decomposition is exactly the recorded \(+1\), not an unknown local contour weight. For a nonpreferred top the kernel bound is instead \[ \left|\prod_j K_{\epsilon_j}(x_j+iNv_{\sigma,j})ight| \le C\exp\!\left\{-2\pi N \sum_{\sigma_j
e\epsilon_j}a_jight\}, \qquad x\in\Omega_N. 	ag{28} \] This follows from the elementary exponential formula for cotangent. The character in (7) and the entire factorial action remain outside this kernel estimate. Their growth can outweigh (28). No source gap or alias suppression is deduced from this penalty alone. The principal critical family on the preferred top retains the geometric \(r\)-centralizer null direction. A real sheet through one of its points is not thereby a specified transverse Gaussian cycle or a centralizer period. Other critical points, equal-holonomy aliases, all facets and the band may compensate its contribution. Formula (24) gives no noncancellation estimate and no lower bound for \(K_N\). ## 7. Exact character differences and the remaining reduction For the unpolarized cotangent form of L, an integer-character step has the exact identity \[ (e^{-2\pi iz_j}-1)\pi\cot(\pi z_j) =-i\pi(1+e^{-2\pi iz_j}). 	ag{29} \] Iterating independent character differences cancels precisely the selected coordinate lattice-pole families. This does not cancel factorial divisors or source endpoints. Each difference has zero period on each original supported torus, not merely on their sum. It therefore supplies no finite Fourier lower bound for the original scalar: all those integer-character periods are the same \(K_N\). The polarized replacements used in (12) are the corresponding one-coordinate pole-free changes with fixed constants. The substantive additional control in (24) is its verified whole-source domain and its complete finite relative boundary: the original boundary band, initial mixed facet currents, translated staircase side prisms and the other top sheets. There is no unidentified interpolation-divisor crossing in their bulk construction, and no discarded infinity end. What remains is to estimate these actual terms and resolve the residual critical family; their existence and coefficients are no longer hypothetical. The older factorial-core contour compiler already has exact cell telescoping and finite-facet rules on retained holomorphic tubes. Those calculations are coverage, not a proof premise here. The new ingredient is that the common nonreal framing gives the required oblique holomorphic prisms for the full literal braid bulk in arbitrary fixed diagrams, while the entire complementary physical band remains in (24). This does not evade the individual-evaluation homology obstruction by claiming a low norm for the undecomposed source. Its potentially large boundary terms are explicit. ## Complete proof-source pins * A: notes/research_literal_crossing_slit_chart_amplitude.md, SHA256 c3682b0f84000aad4c2f53235b9c93bbd86283905a75d6f07ac03b1a3c00bc4a. * L: notes/research_local_geometric_period_for_any_braid.md, SHA256 3ebc94ac5c71dfb38d627704c8a3e3227ff07a6293d39eb79d662b272124578e. Both complete texts were freshly read nontruncated in this author sequence. Their used implications are checked separately from the explicit graph, source-domain, current and orientation calculations above. Only written mathematics and text/hash operations are used. Frozen and public files are unchanged.

title: The actual one-head finite Euler kernel through a small coherent activity
text: # The actual one-head finite Euler kernel through a small coherent activity Private written proof, 18 November 2026. The finite Euler polynomial of the actual root lowering operator has a nonzero coherent-kernel asymptotic on every compact chart away from incidence, for sufficiently small complex Euler parameter. This follows from its exact finite recurrence. A coefficient majorant proves that the actual logarithm converges uniformly; a second majorant proves the relative error. Thus the analytic characteristic calculation below is not being used as a substitute for an asymptotic theorem. The donor and recipient coordinates remain the original binomial coherent coordinates. All finite endpoint terms remain. This result estimates one actual matrix factor; it does not evaluate its contraction with the opposite-source quotient or identify a geometric contribution to a closed period. The sole complete direct S is pinned below. It supplies the literal root matrices and their coherent convention. All finite identities and analytic estimates needed here are proved inline. ## 1. The exact finite polynomial and a homogeneous recurrence Put \[ c=2\pi i,\quad N\ge2,\quad d=N-1,\quad h=N^{-1},\quad Q=e^{ch},\quad q_-=Q^{-1},\quad f_n=(Q;Q)_n. \tag{1} \] The actual lowering matrix at the complete meridian is \[ E w_a=(Q^{-a}-1)w_{a-1}\quad(a\ge1),\qquad Ew_0=0, \qquad E^N=0. \] Define the actual finite operator \[ U_N(\lambda)=\sum_{n=0}^d\frac{\lambda^n E^n}{f_n}. \tag{2} \] With evaluation row \(v(w)w_a=w^a\) and binomial column \(c(z)=\sum_a\binom da z^aw_a\), its exact kernel is \[ \boxed{\quad v(w)U_N(\lambda)c(z) =\sum_{a=0}^d\binom da z^a \prod_{k=1}^a(w+Q^{-k}\lambda). \quad}\tag{3} \] Indeed, for \(n\le a\), the coefficient of \(w_{a-n}\) in \(E^nw_a/f_n\) is \[ {a\brack n}_Q Q^{-na+n(n-1)/2}. \] It is exactly the coefficient of \(w^{a-n}\lambda^n\) in the product in (3), by the finite binomial product. For \(n>a\) both sides vanish. No occupation has been continued to a complex index. Use homogeneous coordinates \(w=(w_0,w_1)\), \(z=(z_0,z_1)\). On the complement of incidence put \[ I=w_0z_0+w_1z_1\ne0,\qquad \theta=\frac{w_1z_1}{I},\qquad t=\lambda\frac{w_0z_1}{I}. \tag{4} \] These ratios are regular functions on \(X=(\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1)\setminus\{I=0\}\). The homogeneous version of (3), divided by \(I^d\), is \[ G_d(\theta,t)=\sum_{a=0}^d\binom da(1-\theta)^{d-a} \prod_{k=1}^a(\theta+q_-^kt). \tag{5} \] For every integer \(j\ge0\), define the same expression with \(d\) replaced by \(j\), while keeping the fixed \(Q\) in (1). Pascal's identity and removal of the first product factor give \[ \boxed{\quad G_{j+1}(\theta,t) =(1-\theta)G_j(\theta,t) +(\theta+q_-t)G_j(\theta,q_-t),\qquad G_0=1. \quad}\tag{6} \] In particular \(G_j(\theta,0)=1\). Equation (6), including its last step \(j=d-1\), is exact for the physical kernel. ## 2. A uniform analytic logarithm of the actual recurrence Fix an arbitrary compact set of \(\theta\)-values, enlarged slightly to an open neighborhood with compact closure. Constants below are uniform there. Let \(D=t\partial_t\). Initially interpret \[ V_j=h\log G_j \] as a formal power series with constant coefficient zero. Define \[ \delta_h V(t)=\frac{V(q_-t)-V(t)}h, \qquad \mathcal F_h(V)= \log\{1-\theta+(\theta+q_-t)e^{\delta_hV}\}. \tag{7} \] The logarithm in (7) is its formal series at constant coefficient one. The exact recurrence is \[ V_{j+1}=V_j+h\mathcal F_h(V_j). \tag{8} \] We prove convergence uniformly for \(0\le j\le N\), rather than assuming that the finite \(G_j\) has no zeros. The coefficient of \(t^n\) in \(\delta_hV\) is \((q_-^n-1)v_n/h\), whose absolute value is at most \(|c|n|v_n|\). The part of \(\mathcal F_h\) linear in \(V\) is \(\theta\delta_hV\). Consequently the coefficient of \(v_n\) in (8) is exactly \[ r_n=1-\theta+\theta q_-^n, \qquad |r_n|\le e^{Cnh}. \tag{9} \] Every other term of coefficient \(n\) uses only \(v_1,\ldots,v_{n-1}\). The Taylor series in two variables of \(\log(1-\theta+(\theta+q_-t)e^w)-\theta w\) has an absolute coefficient majorant, uniform in \(N,\theta\), of the form \[ F(t,p)=C t+\frac{C(t+p)^2}{1-C(t+p)},\qquad p=D U, \tag{10} \] after increasing \(C\) to absorb \(|c|\). This follows directly by expanding the exponential and logarithm on a fixed small bidisk in \((t,w)\); there is no term linear in \(w\) left after the subtraction. Here and below inequalities of formal series with nonnegative coefficients are coefficientwise. Consider the positive majorant flow \[ \partial_\tau U=C D U+F(t,D U),\qquad U(0,t)=0. \tag{11} \] It has an analytic solution on a fixed small \(t\)-disk for \(0\le\tau\le2\). The following elementary characteristic argument also supplies the required uniform radius. Put \(p=D U\). The characteristic equations are \[ \dot t=-t(C+F_p(t,p)),\qquad \dot p=t F_t(t,p),\qquad \dot U=F(t,p)-pF_p(t,p). \tag{12} \] At \((t,p)=(0,0)\) all right sides vanish except for the harmless linear coefficient \(-Ct\). On a sufficiently small bidisk, \(F_p=O(t+p)\) and \(tF_t=O(t)\). Integration and the elementary Gronwall inequality therefore keep \(|t|+|p|\le C_1|t(0)|\) for time two. Picard iteration on a slightly larger bidisk gives holomorphic dependence on the initial value. Moreover \(\partial t(\tau)/\partial t(0)=e^{-C\tau}+O(|t(0)|)\). The inverse-function theorem, uniformly on the compact time interval, then gives an analytic solution \(U(\tau,t)\) on a fixed disk. Differentiating (12) verifies \(p=D U\) and (11). Alternatively this identity follows from its zero initial value and its homogeneous linear evolution. The coefficient equations of (11) show inductively that all coefficients of \(U\) are nonnegative. For clarity, this flow really dominates the discrete recurrence. If the absolute coefficients of \(V_j\) are bounded by a nonnegative series \(A\), (9)--(10) bound the next series by \[ e^{ChD}\{A+hF(t,D A)\}. \tag{13} \] The time-\(h\) flow of (11), starting at \(A\), dominates \(A+hF(t,D A)\): every coefficient is increasing and the vector field has nonnegative coefficients. A further time \(h\) dominates the linear flow \(e^{ChD}\). These statements hold coefficient by coefficient; the already established analytic solution bounds their series. Induction gives \[ |V_j|_{\rm coeff}\le U(2jh,t),\qquad j\le N. \tag{14} \] Thus all formal logarithms converge on a fixed disk, uniformly in \(j,N,\theta\). Their exponentials equal the polynomials \(G_j\) by equality of Taylor coefficients. In particular \[ \boxed{\quad G_j(\theta,t)\ne0\quad(j\le N,\ |t|<\epsilon),\quad} \tag{15} \] for a fixed \(\epsilon>0\), with the analytic logarithm fixed by \(G_j(\theta,0)=1\). This is an actual zero-free statement. ## 3. The calibrated analytic flow and its subprincipal transport The limiting equation suggested by (8) will now be solved analytically and then compared with the actual recurrence. Put \[ \mathcal F(V)=\log Z,\qquad Z=1-\theta+(\theta+t)e^{-cDV},\qquad \partial_\tau V=\mathcal F(V),\quad V(0,t)=0. \tag{16} \] Let \(b\) be a small initial activity and define \[ \omega(b)=\frac{c(\theta+b)}{1+b},\qquad t_\tau=b e^{\tau\omega(b)},\qquad \Delta_\tau=1+\frac{c\tau(1-\theta)b}{(1+b)^2}. \tag{17} \] The map \(b\mapsto t_\tau\) has derivative \(e^{\tau\omega(b)}\Delta_\tau\), nonzero on a fixed small disk, uniformly for \(0\le\tau\le1\) and the stated \(\theta\)-set. It has a unique small analytic inverse. Define \[ R_\tau=1+\frac{c\tau b}{1+b} \operatorname{exprel}\!\left(\frac{c\tau(\theta+b)}{1+b}\right), \qquad p_\tau=\frac1c\Log R_\tau, \tag{18} \] where \(\operatorname{exprel}(z)=(e^z-1)/z\) with value one at zero. Equivalently \(R_\tau=(\theta+t_\tau)/(\theta+b)\), but (18) is the required removable expression when \(\theta+b=0\). All logarithms are continued from \(b=0\). Finally set \[ V(\tau,t_\tau) =\tau\log(1+b)+\omega(b)\int_0^\tau p_\sigma\,d\sigma. \tag{19} \] These are analytic functions on the same small disk. Here is a direct verification of (16). With \(W=e^{-cp}\), its characteristic equations are \[ \dot t=\frac{c t(\theta+t)W}{Z},\qquad \dot p=\frac{tW}{Z},\qquad \dot V=\log Z+\frac{c p(\theta+t)W}{Z}. \tag{20} \] Equations (17)--(18) give \((\theta+t_\tau)e^{-cp_\tau}=\theta+b\) and \(Z=1+b\). They satisfy the first two equations in (20), and (19) satisfies the third. Differentiation with respect to the initial activity shows \(p=DV\); the possible difference has zero initial value and the homogeneous linear characteristic equation. This proves (16), with its integration constant fixed. In particular \(V(\tau,0)=0\). The first correction in the exact map (7) is \[ \mathcal F_h(V)=\mathcal F(V)+h\mathcal F_1(V)+O(h^2),\qquad \mathcal F_1(V)=\frac WZ \left[-ct+\frac{c^2}{2}(\theta+t)D^2V\right]. \tag{21} \] This is an analytic expansion on smaller disks, with fixed derivatives: expand \(V(e^{-ch}t)\) and \(e^{-ch}t\) directly. The transport equation for a subprincipal function \(A\) is \[ \partial_\tau A =-\frac{c(\theta+t)W}{Z}D A +\mathcal F_1(V)-\tfrac12\partial_\tau^2V, \qquad A(0,t)=0. \tag{22} \] It has the explicit solution \[ \boxed{\quad A(\tau,t_\tau)=-\frac c2p_\tau-\frac12\Log\Delta_\tau.\quad} \tag{23} \] To check this without a transport assumption, differentiate (16): \[ V_{\tau\tau} =-\frac{c(\theta+t)W^2}{Z^2} \{t-c(\theta+t)Dp\}. \] Along (17), \[ Dp=\frac1c\left\{\frac{t}{\theta+t} -\frac{b}{\Delta_\tau(\theta+b)}\right\}. \] The displayed fractions have their removable meaning from (18). Substituting into the right side of (22) along the characteristic cancels the two mixed terms and leaves \[ -\frac12\omega(b)\frac{t_\tau}{\theta+t_\tau} -\frac12\frac{b\omega'(b)}{\Delta_\tau} =-\frac c2\dot p_\tau-\frac12\partial_\tau\Log\Delta_\tau. \] Analytic continuation across the removable denominators proves (23) everywhere on the small chart, including \(\theta=0\). ## 4. Comparison with the actual finite kernel We supply an analytic error argument for the discrete evolution. Let \(W_j=V(jh,\cdot)+hA(jh,\cdot)\). Equations (16),(21),(22) and Taylor's formula give \[ W_{j+1}-W_j-h\mathcal F_h(W_j)=\mathcal R_j, \qquad \mathcal R_j=O(h^3),\quad \mathcal R_j(0)=0, \tag{24} \] uniformly on a fixed small disk, for \(j<N\). Uniform analyticity on a larger disk gives a coefficient majorant \(|\mathcal R_j|_{\rm coeff}\le C h^3t/(r-t)\). All constants can be chosen uniformly in \(\theta\) on the original compact set. Here is the stability estimate needed for summing (24). The bounds (14) and the analytic functions (19),(23), on slightly larger disks, majorize the coefficients of \(V_j,W_j,\delta_hV_j,\delta_hW_j\) by fixed convergent series with zero constant term. In the difference \(\mathcal F_h(V_j)-\mathcal F_h(W_j)\), the term linear in their difference is \(\theta\delta_h(V_j-W_j)\). Expanding the remaining analytic difference, or integrating its derivative on the formal line segment, gives a majorant \[ B(t)D e_j,\qquad B(t)=\frac{C t}{r-t},\qquad e_j=|V_j-W_j|_{\rm coeff}. \tag{25} \] The factor \(t\) occurs because the derivative of the nonlinear remainder in (10) vanishes at \((t,p)=(0,0)\). The estimate for \(\delta_h\) again uses \(|q_-^n-1|/h\le|c|n\). Thus (9),(24) give \[ e_{j+1}\le e^{ChD} \left\{e_j+hB(t)D e_j+C h^3\frac{t}{r-t}\right\}, \qquad e_0=0. \tag{26} \] For completeness, a fixed analytic majorant for this recurrence is obtained from the linear positive flow \[ \partial_\tau Z=C D Z+B(t)D Z+C\frac{t}{r-t},\qquad Z(0,t)=0. \tag{27} \] Its characteristic equation is \(\dot t=-t(C+B(t))\). For a sufficiently small initial disk it and the integral of the displayed analytic forcing are regular through time two; the inverse characteristic map is regular as in (12). Hence \(Z\) is analytic on a fixed smaller disk. Its coefficients are nonnegative. The same two-step flow comparison used in (13) now gives \[ e_j\le h^2 Z(2jh,t),\qquad j\le N. \tag{28} \] This proves the actual, uniform estimate \[ V_j=V(jh,t)+hA(jh,t)+O(h^2). \tag{29} \] Every fixed derivative follows on smaller disks by Cauchy estimates. In particular no high-order formal expansion has been substituted for an uncontrolled finite polynomial. Use \(j=d=N-1\) in (29). Since \(V_\tau(1,t)=\log(1+b)\) along (17), where now \(t=b e^{\omega(b)}\), the endpoint shift \(d/N=1-h\) gives \[ \boxed{\quad G_d(\theta,t)=e^{N V(1,t)} \frac{e^{-cp/2}}{(1+b)\sqrt{\Delta}} (1+O(N^{-1})), \quad}\tag{30} \] where \[ t=b\exp\!\left[\frac{c(\theta+b)}{1+b}\right],\qquad p=\frac1c\Log\!\left[\frac{\theta+t}{\theta+b}\right],\qquad \Delta=1+\frac{c(1-\theta)b}{(1+b)^2}. \tag{31} \] The ratio for \(p\) always means (18). The square root and all logarithms are one or zero, respectively, at \(b=0\). Every factor in the leading coefficient is nonzero on the small chart. The relative error and its fixed derivatives are uniform. As a check that the upper cap has not been erased, at \(\theta=1\) the exact recurrence gives \[ G_d(1,t)=\prod_{k=1}^d(1+Q^{-k}t) =\frac{1-(-t)^N}{1+t}. \tag{32} \] Here (31) gives \(b=t,p=0,\Delta=1\), and \(V(1,t)=0\) since \(DV=p=0\) and \(V(1,0)=0\). Formula (30) therefore gives the correct unit \((1+t)^{-1}\); the exact Fermat numerator in (32) is exponentially close to one on the proved small disk. ## 5. The actual coherent chart and its limits For any compact \(\mathcal K\Subset X\), the two functions \(\theta\) and \(w_0z_1/I\) in (4) are bounded. Thus a fixed small disk \(|\lambda|<\epsilon_{\mathcal K}\) puts the actual kernel in (30). In homogeneous notation the theorem is \[ \boxed{\quad K_{U_N}(w,z)=I^d e^{N V(1,\theta,t)} \frac{e^{-cp/2}}{(1+b)\sqrt{\Delta}} (1+O(N^{-1})). \quad}\tag{33} \] It is valid through projective coordinate infinities: all normalized parameters used in the proof are regular on \(X\). The actual normalized kernel is zero-free on this neighborhood for every \(N\) by (15), and its displayed asymptotic coefficient is a unit. At \(\lambda=0\) it is exactly the original identity kernel. In a local trivialization its phase is \(\log I+V\), with the additional amplitude factor \(I^{-1}\) from \(d=N-1\). At \(\lambda=0\), the mixed phase derivative in affine coordinates is \(\partial_w\partial_z\log(1+wz)=(1+wz)^{-2}\), nonzero. Continuity and the proved derivative bounds keep this mixed derivative nonzero on smaller compact charts for sufficiently small \(\lambda\). Thus (33) is a regular local generating kernel near the identity, including its computed nonzero amplitude. The finite canonical rows are also explicit. With the original \(K\), one has \(KE=QEK\), so \[ EU_N=U_NE,\qquad KU_N=(1-\lambda E)U_NK. \tag{34} \] For the second identity use the exact polynomial recurrence \(E_N(QX)=(1-X)E_N(X)+X^N/N\) at \(X=\lambda E\); the last term is zero as a matrix. Therefore the actual phase in (33), when read in the original coherent canonical coordinates, has \(e_{\rm out}=e_{\rm in}\) and \(k_{\rm out}=(1-\lambda e_{\rm out})k_{\rm in}\). These rows check the graph of an already proved analytic kernel. They were not used to infer its amplitude or its zero-freeness. The theorem is at fixed quantum root and complete meridian. It does not differentiate the meridian-dependent lowering matrix, its vacuum row, or a shifted denominator \((M^{-2}Q;Q)_n\). Those are additional actual normal insertions. Likewise no quantum-parameter derivative is obtained by differentiating \(E^N=0\) or the root products. All occupations, including the original finite upper and lower arrows, have been retained in (2)--(6). The theorem controls one actual Euler factor on a small coherent neighborhood; it does not replace a coproduct factorization, an inverse-factorial donor contraction, the quotient \(q_F\), or the original pivotal first-jet closing row. No assertion is made that a prescribed geometric source frame lies in this neighborhood, or that a closed source period is nonzero. ## Complete proof direct * S: notes/research_finite_trace_separator_and_opposite_characteristic.md, SHA256 1d5abd4e14df7aa32f17405e27543a35d815c130903ed379ab9c60bec2eef0f6. title: A character metric for the actual whole-meridian peripheral action
text: # A character metric for the actual whole-meridian peripheral action Written proof, 23 November 2026. The actual reduced knot family has a positive whole-meridian metric in which both fundamental peripheral actions have norm at most two. Evaluation at the complete color has an explicit polynomial dual norm on every finite Laurent-degree space. These bounds retain the whole family and its meridian normals. They do not give a lower bound for its original marked scalar. ## 1. The actual source and its boundary action Fix \(N\ge2\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), and the marked meridian \(M=-qx\). Let \(F_N(M)\) be the original reduced, zero-framed ADO knot source, with unknot value one and complete value \(K_N=F_N(1)\). The complete sources [P] and [W] prove, in these conventions, \[ F_N(M^{-1})=F_N(M),\qquad \Lambda F=-\frac{f(qM)F(qM)+f(q^{-1}M)F(q^{-1}M)}{f(M)}, \qquad \mathsf U F=(M+M^{-1})F,\quad f=M-M^{-1}. \tag{1} \] Here \(\Lambda\) adds the specified zero-framed fundamental longitude, and \(\mathsf U\) adds the specified fundamental meridian. Equation (1) holds for every intermediate link insertion, with word order retained. It is a whole-meridian identity at the fixed root \(q\). By [J], \(F_N\) is a Laurent polynomial; (1) supplies its Weyl symmetry. We work on the full ladder \[ \mathscr P=\mathbb C[M,M^{-1}]^{M\mapsto M^{-1}},\qquad \mathscr P_D=\{F\in\mathscr P:\operatorname{supp}_M F\subset[-D,D]\}. \tag{2} \] The original knot family is also even in \(M\). Fundamental meridian insertions can change that parity, so the ladder (2) includes both parities. No exponents are identified modulo \(N\) or \(2N\). The actual full modified period is still \[ \mathcal N_N(M)=d_N(M)F_N(M),\qquad d_N(M)=i^{N+3}\frac{M-M^{-1}}{M^N-M^{-N}},\qquad \mathcal N_N(1)=\frac{i^{N+3}}N K_N. \tag{3} \] The metric below is placed on the reduced Laurent family. It does not replace the meromorphic multiplier in (3). ## 2. A simultaneous bounded metric For \(n\ge0\), put \[ \chi_n(M)=\frac{M^{n+1}-M^{-n-1}}{M-M^{-1}} =\sum_{r=0}^n M^{n-2r}. \tag{4} \] These Laurent polynomials form a basis of \(\mathscr P\), since the leading coefficient in degree \(n\) is one. Define \[ \|F\|_{\mathrm H}^2 =\frac2\pi\int_0^\pi |F(e^{i\theta})|^2\sin^2\theta\,d\theta. \tag{5} \] This is the usual character Haar metric. The proof needed here is elementary: \(\chi_n(e^{i\theta})\sin\theta=\sin((n+1)\theta)\), and integration of products of sines gives \[ \left\|\sum_{n=0}^D a_n\chi_n\right\|_{\mathrm H}^2 =\sum_{n=0}^D|a_n|^2. \tag{6} \] In particular the zeros of the density at the endpoints do not make this a degenerate norm on Laurent polynomials. Multiplying (4) by \(f\), applying the shifts in (1), and collecting the two antisymmetric monomials gives exactly \[ \Lambda\chi_n=-(q^{n+1}+q^{-n-1})\chi_n, \qquad \mathsf U\chi_n=\chi_{n+1}+\chi_{n-1},\quad \chi_{-1}=0. \tag{7} \] Thus the apparent quotients at \(M=\pm1\) in (1) cancel in the Laurent-polynomial ring, before any endpoint evaluation. Since \(|q^{n+1}+q^{-n-1}|\le2\), (6) proves \[ \|\Lambda F\|_{\mathrm H}\le2\|F\|_{\mathrm H},\qquad \|\mathsf U F\|_{\mathrm H}\le2\|F\|_{\mathrm H}. \tag{8} \] For the second inequality one can also use the multiplication formula \(\mathsf U=2\cos\theta\) directly in (5). Both operators extend to bounded self-adjoint operators on the Hilbert completion. The finite degree maps are \(\Lambda:\mathscr P_D\to\mathscr P_D\) and \(\mathsf U:\mathscr P_D\to\mathscr P_{D+1}\); no upper-degree compression is part of this statement. Let \(\mathcal W\) be an ordered word of length \(s\) in these two actual peripheral operations, with \(m\) meridian letters. Repeated application of (1) identifies its result with the actual descendant source, and (8) gives \[ F_N^{\mathcal W}=\mathcal W F_N\in\mathscr P_{D+m},\qquad \|F_N^{\mathcal W}\|_{\mathrm H}\le2^s\|F_N\|_{\mathrm H} \quad(F_N\in\mathscr P_D). \tag{9} \] For a finite linear combination \(\sum_w c_w\mathcal W_w\), the corresponding cost is \(\sum_w|c_w|2^{|w|}\). It is independent of the level for a fixed peripheral expression. There is no claim of such independence for expressions whose length grows with \(N\). ## 3. The original complete-color functional On \(\mathscr P_D\), complete evaluation is \[ \operatorname{ev}_1 F=\sum_{n=0}^D(n+1)a_n,\qquad C_D^2:=\|\operatorname{ev}_1\|^2 =\sum_{n=0}^D(n+1)^2 =\frac{(D+1)(D+2)(2D+3)}6. \tag{10} \] Cauchy--Schwarz proves the upper bound, and the vector \(\sum_{n=0}^D(n+1)\chi_n\) proves equality. Consequently the actual marked descendants obey \[ |F_N^{\mathcal W}(1)| \le 2^s C_{D+m}\|F_N\|_{\mathrm H}. \tag{11} \] In particular this uses the original \(K_N=F_N(1)\), without changing the closing to a discrete positive-color average. For completeness, fixed-root meridian normals have polynomial dual bounds too. Let \(\partial_u=M\partial_M\). Each monomial in (4) has exponent of absolute value at most \(n\), whence, for \(j\ge0\), \[ \sup_{|M|=1}|\partial_u^j F(M)| \le D^j C_D\|F\|_{\mathrm H},\qquad F\in\mathscr P_D, \tag{12} \] where \(D^0=1\), including \(D=0\). For \(D=0,j>0\) the derivative is zero. Thus whole-meridian data are retained rather than being replaced by root-orbit values. In the odd normal lattice of [P], \[ w_N=fF_N,\qquad w_N(1)=0,\qquad K_N=\tfrac12\partial_u w_N(1). \tag{13} \] Indeed \(\partial_u f(1)=2\). This is the same original normal functional, now evaluated on its full Laurent representative. There is also a direct comparison with the full-circle Fourier norm \(\|F\|_{\mathrm c}^2=(2\pi)^{-1}\int_0^{2\pi}|F(e^{i\theta})|^2d\theta\). Weyl symmetry and (5) give \(\|fF\|_{\mathrm c}^2=2\|F\|_{\mathrm H}^2\). Since \(\|\chi_n\|_{\mathrm c}^2=n+1\), the triangle inequality and Cauchy--Schwarz, together with \(|f|\le2\), give \[ \frac1{\sqrt2}\|F\|_{\mathrm H} \le\|F\|_{\mathrm c} \le\sqrt{\frac{(D+1)(D+2)}2}\,\|F\|_{\mathrm H}. \tag{14} \] Thus the new metric differs from the whole Fourier coefficient norm by at most a polynomial in the actual degree. This comparison is with the full Fourier ladder, not with aliased samples on one orbit. ## 4. The quantitative source consequence and its limit Fix a \(b\)-strand braid presentation of length \(\ell\), writhe \(\mathfrak w\), and one closed component. The complete proof [J, Section 1] derives from the literal canceled crossing entries \[ F_N(M)=f_N(M^2),\qquad \operatorname{supp} f_N\subset[-AN,AN],\qquad A=\max\!\left(1,\left\lceil\frac{3\ell+|b-1-\mathfrak w|}{2} \right\rceil\right). \tag{15} \] Hence \(D\le2AN\) is valid for the original source at every level. For every fixed peripheral word and fixed meridian derivative order, (11)--(12) have only polynomial level cost: \[ |F_N^{\mathcal W}(1)|\le C_{A,\mathcal W}N^{3/2}\|F_N\|_{\mathrm H}, \qquad |\partial_u^jF_N^{\mathcal W}(1)| \le C_{A,\mathcal W,j}N^{j+3/2}\|F_N\|_{\mathrm H}. \tag{16} \] All original peripheral framing and pivotal factors are those already fixed in (1). For the full modified period, its complete value has the additional explicit multiplier \(i^{N+3}/N\) from (3). The polynomial and its finite jets have not been quotiented by a root-of-unity vanishing ideal. Such a quotient can forget alias and wall data even though it retains all root values. Likewise no orthogonal compression of the character ladder has been inserted into the actual peripheral composition. The character basis and Haar metric are classical. The quantitative conclusion here is their simultaneous application to the actual normalization-matched whole-meridian source, its peripheral words, and its specified complete-color functional. The bounded actions and polynomial dual cost are upper estimates. They give neither a lower bound for \(K_N\), nor a comparison of this whole-meridian norm with the norm of the original finite all-color value orbit. Such a comparison would require control of the retained alias and normal channels. No geometric contribution or volume limit is inferred. Everything here holds at fixed \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\). Meridian derivatives in (12)--(13) are not off-root quantum-normal derivatives. The different normal paths, pivotal derivatives, and endpoint corrections in the complete-color divided Ward source remain separate data. ## 5. Complete proof sources and coverage The three complete proof inputs are: | Label | Source | SHA256 | |---|---|---| | P | [Actual peripheral fusion](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_peripheral_fusion.md) | cee06548a794b0adfe56a289be7d5972c80be17dc41d854075a135473bd8959a | | W | [Actual Weyl descent](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_weyl_descent.md) | cf3add0dd88bcf413e04a595bfa52198b3d1a96c123ae6e356c994510f7093c4 | | J | [Ordinary-orbit quantum jets](research_ordinary_orbit_jet_reconstruction.md) | 6c9c3089b93204ae6b7045265ece6deac1552563de806dae3810392c239c028d | P supplies the actual operators and the original normal functional; W supplies Weyl symmetry; J supplies only the literal Laurent width. All metric, evaluation, word, and derivative bounds are proved above. The closest complete comparisons are [whole clock endpoint extension](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/whole_clock_function_algebra_and_endpoint_extension.md), SHA256 `63c540e62024d1c753f41b677d00557e075936eeebc8774161e7d29d88be5780`, and [complete-color divided Ward fusion](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/complete_color_divided_ward_and_fusion.md), SHA256 `8add5faf754a4ab5eef78829e0e85b83a0d50c38ed197d20f47a7d84ebfa05cc`.
