title: The actual reciprocal wall on the nine-cell boundary
text: # The actual reciprocal wall on the nine-cell boundary Private written proof, 17 November 2026. The finite wall in the original middle five-point chart has an explicit local transport to the paired boundary faces of the proved nine-cell source. Its factorial gauge sees the exact endpoint factor \(N^2\). After the remaining crossing factor and the actual Fourier adapter, the original wall has rank \(N\) and norm \(N\). Its lowering-current defect is retained, with norm \(N|Q^{-1}-1|\), and changes the total boundary character by one. This is not an identification with the entire negative-ray current of a full-function period. ## 1. Original operators and insertion Fix odd \(N>2\), \(Q=e^{2\pi i/N}\), \(s=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(d=N-1\), \[ x=-s^{-1},\qquad \lambda=x^{-1}=Qx,\qquad x^N=\lambda^N=1. \tag{1} \] Bracketed indices are reduced to \(0,\ldots,d\). First use the original unit wrap \(S_1^N=S_2^N=1\). The complete balanced matrices [S] are \[ Z|a\rangle=Q^a|a\rangle,\quad K=xZ^{-1},\quad f=(1-Z)S,\quad e|a\rangle=\lambda(1-Q^{-a})|a-1\rangle , \tag{2} \] with the last arrow zero at \(a=0\). Put \[ p_a=(Q;Q)_a,\quad P(T)=\sum_{h=0}^d\frac{(-1)^hQ^{h(h-1)/2}}{p_h}T^h,\quad n=e_1S_2,\quad B=-e_1Z_2S_2. \tag{3} \] The original uncheck crossing [M], with its common scalar Cartan line retained externally, is \[ R_0=DP(B)P(n),\qquad D|a,b\rangle=x^{-a-b}Q^{ab}|a,b\rangle . \tag{4} \] The diagonal also follows from the zero-transfer coefficient [S,(11)]. The actual reciprocal coordinate and wall are \[ X=xS_2S_1^{-1},\quad W=E_dX=x|d\rangle\langle0|\otimes S_2,\quad U=\Gamma n\Gamma^{-1},\qquad (1-QZ_1)U=X-W, \tag{5} \] \[ \Gamma|a\rangle=g_a|a\rangle,\quad g_a=(-1)^aQ^{-a(a-1)/2}p_a^2,\quad g_0=1,\quad g_d=Q^dN^2 . \tag{6} \] These are [M,(8)--(10)], with the finite endpoint retained. The particular original-head insertion transported here is \[ R_W=DP(B)\,W\,P(n) =DP(B)\Gamma^{-1}(g_dW)P(U)\Gamma . \tag{7} \] Inserting bare \(W\) between \(\Gamma^{-1}\) and \(P(U)\) would instead give \(g_d^{-1}R_W\). These two coupons are distinct. For the original total lowering matrix \(H=f_1+K_1^{-1}f_2\), \[ J=[H,W]=(Q^{-1}-1)|d\rangle\langle0|\otimes S_2^2,\qquad [K_1K_2,W]=0. \tag{8} \] Indeed \(f_1W=Wf_1=0\), \(K^{-1}|d\rangle=x|d\rangle\), and \(fS-QSf=(1-Q)S^2\); use \(x^2=Q^{-1}\). The current insertion is \(R_J=DP(B)JP(n)\). ## 2. Remaining-factor transport, including every endpoint Let \(L=DP(B)\) and \(W_r=x|d\rangle\langle0|\otimes S_2^r\). Then \(W=W_1\) and \(J=(Q^{-1}-1)W_2/x\). Nilpotence and the finite binomial identity give \(P(B)^{-1}=\sum_{h=0}^d B^h/p_h\). Direct multiplication of (2) yields, for \(0\le h\le a\), \[ (B^h)_{a-h,[b+h];a,b} =\lambda^hQ^{h(b-a)+h^2}\frac{p_a}{p_{a-h}} . \tag{9} \] The entire column and row needed for the wall are consequently \[ \begin{split} P(B)|d,b\rangle &=\sum_{h=0}^d\lambda^hQ^{h(b+h)}|d-h,[b+h]\rangle,\\ (P(B)^{-1})_{0,[a+b];a,b}&=\lambda^aQ^{ab}. \end{split} \tag{10} \] For the first use \(p_d/(p_{d-h}p_h)=(-1)^hQ^{-h(h+1)/2}\); the second is the term \(h=a\) in the inverse. Both include all endpoints. After \(W_r\), put \(h=d-u\) in the first line and apply the Cartan ratio. The complete result is \[ \boxed{(LW_rL^{-1})_{u,v;a,b} =Q^{-b-1}x^{a-u+r-1}\delta_{v,[a+b+r-1-u]}.} \tag{11} \] For a phase check, before the Cartan ratio the \(Q\)-exponent is \(ab+h([a+b+r]+h)\); that ratio adds \(uv-ab\), giving \(dv\). The remaining \(\lambda\)-powers give (11). At \(r=1\), each total-clock block is rank one, with \(N\) by \(N\) entries of modulus one. Distinct blocks have orthogonal source and target spaces. The same argument applies to \(r=2\), so \[ \|LWL^{-1}\|_2=N,\qquad \|LJL^{-1}\|_2=N|Q^{-1}-1|. \tag{12} \] The bare reciprocal coupon in (7) has exterior norm \(1/N\). Separate exponential bounds on \(\Gamma^{\pm1}\) would lose this exact polynomial endpoint calculation. For the original common wrap \(S_1^N=S_2^N=\mu\ne0\), use \(W_r=x\mu^{-1}|d\rangle\langle0|\otimes S_2^r\). Then (11) has the additional factor \[ \mu^{\lfloor(a+b+r-1-u)/N\rfloor}. \tag{13} \] Choose a local \(\zeta^N=\mu\) and \(T_\zeta|a\rangle=\zeta^a|a\rangle\). Conjugating by \(T_\zeta\otimes T_\zeta\) removes (13) and leaves \(\zeta^{r-1}\) times (11). The total degree changes by \(r-1-N\lfloor(a+b+r-1-u)/N\rfloor\), proving this also at the seam. The original \(R_0\) conserves ordinary integer degree and commutes with this gauge. At unit marks it is unitary; on compact nonzero \(\mu\)-domains it and its inverse have uniform bounds and fixed-order parameter derivatives. Below \(\mu=1\); under this optional gauge the current acquires the specified \(\zeta\). ## 3. The actual planar Fourier adapter Let \(F_{ia}=N^{-1/2}Q^{ia}\), \(\mathcal F=F\otimes F\), and \(D_x|a\rangle=x^a|a\rangle\). The original coefficient [S,(11)] before the flip is \[ (R_0)_{a-h,b+h;a,b} =x^{-a-b-h}Q^{ab-(b+1)h} \frac{p_ap_{b+h}}{p_{a-h}p_bp_h}. \tag{14} \] The literal Fourier matrix \(A=\mathcal F^{-1}R^o\mathcal F\) in [P,(1.1)] has the same support and factorial ratio, with phase \(Q^{1+(a-h)(b+1)}\). Their ratio is \(Qx^{b-(a-h)}\), giving \[ A=Q(D_x^{-1}\otimes I)R_0(I\otimes D_x). \tag{15} \] All displayed matrices besides \(R_0,A\) are unitary. An exterior left coupon \(C\) becomes \(\mathcal F(D_x^{-1}\otimes I)C(D_x\otimes I)\mathcal F^{-1}\). No factorial similarity is omitted. Applying this to (11) gives \[ (C_r)_{\rm pl} =NQ^{-1}\sum_{i=0}^d(\lambda Q^i)^{r-1} |i,i+1\rangle\langle i,i|. \tag{16} \] For clarity, the pre-Fourier \(r=1\) matrix is \(Q^{-v-1}\delta_{u+v,a+b}\). In \(\mathcal F C\mathcal F^{-1}\) its exponent is \((i-j+1)u+(j-1-k)a+(j-1-l)b-1\), so the output is \((i,j)=(i,i+1)\) and the input is \((k,l)=(i,i)\). This fixes the Fourier sign. Thus \[ \boxed{C_{\rm pl}=NQ^{-1}\sum_i|i,i+1\rangle\langle i,i|, \quad J_{\rm pl}=N(Q^{-1}-1)\sum_iQ^i|i,i+1\rangle\langle i,i|.} \tag{17} \] The specified unbraided matrix obeys \(R^o_{i,j;k,l}=R_{\rm can}(i,j,k,l)Q^{k+l}\). Its input factors are untouched by a left coupon. Therefore \[ (R_W)_{\rm can}(i,j,k,l) =NQ^{-1}\delta_{j,i+1}R_{\rm can}(i,i,k,l). \tag{18} \] In [P]'s actual composition support, equal first two indices give \(u=[j-i-1]=d\), forcing the other three composition indices to zero. Using \(p_d=N\) proves \[ R_{\rm can}(i,i,k,l)=Q^{1-2i}\delta_{k,i}\delta_{l,i}, \] \[ \boxed{\begin{split} (R_W)_{\rm can}&=NQ^{-2i}\delta_{j,i+1}\delta_{k,i}\delta_{l,i},\\ (R_J)_{\rm can}&=N(Q^{-1}-1)Q^{1-i} \delta_{j,i+1}\delta_{k,i}\delta_{l,i}. \end{split}} \tag{19} \] Their matrix norms are exactly \(N\) and \(N|Q^{-1}-1|\le2\pi\). These are local inserted-crossing bounds, not bounds for an arbitrary exterior contraction. ## 4. Literal paired-face operators and cyclic seams Use [A] unchanged. On the first two output ports set \[ k_m=\alpha_{m,-}-\alpha_{m,+}+h_m,\quad l_m=\beta_{m,-}-\beta_{m,+}+h_m,\quad f_m(k)=a_m^{[k-1]}b_m^{[-k]} . \tag{20} \] Here \(a_m=s_{0m}\), \(b_m=s_{m5}\). The actual adapter and inverse dual have entries \[ \mathcal A_m(\alpha;j)=f_m(k_m)Q^{jk_m},\qquad \mathcal L_m(j;\beta)=\frac{Q^{-jl_m}}{N^2f_m(l_m)}. \tag{21} \] Summing the single index in (17) gives the full face kernels \[ \boxed{\mathcal W_{\alpha;\beta} =\frac{Q^{k_2-1}}{N^2} \frac{f_1(k_1)f_2(k_2)}{f_1(l_1)f_2(l_2)} \delta_{k_1+k_2,l_1+l_2},} \tag{22} \] \[ \boxed{\mathcal J_{\alpha;\beta} =\frac{(Q^{-1}-1)Q^{k_2}}{N^2} \frac{f_1(k_1)f_2(k_2)}{f_1(l_1)f_2(l_2)} \delta_{k_1+k_2-l_1-l_2,-1}.} \tag{23} \] They act on the simultaneous-translation invariant paired images and kill their specified complementary kernel. The other two ports retain the identity on their paired images. The current is nonzero and lowers the total boundary character by one. Every seam is retained. In particular, \[ \frac{f_m(k+1)}{f_m(k)} =\frac{a_m}{b_m} \left[1+\left(\frac{b_m^N}{a_m^N}-1\right)\delta_{k0}\right]. \tag{24} \] Neither the seam nor the inverse dual \(f_m(l)^{-1}\) is replaced by an unwrapped progression or a Hermitian adjoint. When the decoration differences \(a_m^N,b_m^N\) range over compact nonzero sets, [A]'s normalized adapters and inverse on the image are uniformly bounded. Hence \[ c_KN\le\|\mathcal W\|_2\le C_KN,\qquad c_KN|Q^{-1}-1|\le\|\mathcal J\|_2\le C_KN|Q^{-1}-1|. \tag{25} \] Fixed-order decoration derivatives have the corresponding upper bounds. No genuine-\(Q\) or meridian-normal derivative is used. ## 5. Actual nine-cell insertion and sector transport The proved canonical identity [C] is \[ \mathcal B=C_N(\mathbf s)Q^{3(h_1-1)/2}s_{05}^{d} \sum_{\mathbf i}R_{\rm can}(\mathbf i) \prod_{m=1}^4 f_m(k_m)Q^{i_mk_m}. \tag{26} \] Applying (22)--(23) to its first two ports, equivalently substituting (19), gives the all-boundary identities \[ \boxed{\begin{split} \mathcal B_W&= N^2C_NQ^{3(h_1-1)/2+k_2}s_{05}^{d} \prod_m f_m(k_m)\,\delta_{\sum k_m,2},\\ \mathcal B_J&= N^2(Q^{-1}-1)C_NQ^{3(h_1-1)/2+1+k_2}s_{05}^{d} \prod_m f_m(k_m)\,\delta_{\sum k_m,1}. \end{split}} \tag{27} \] The arbitrary physical exterior and its inverse dual are unchanged. In particular the actual \(C_N\), its phase and all lifted roots remain in the identity. No whole-cut scalarity is used. For distinct real decorations and real odd roots, [C] proves \(|C_N|=N^{-2}\). On fixed compact noncollision decoration sets, every other absolute factor in (27) is bounded above and below. Each support has \(N^7\) literal eight-face assignments. Thus these unnormalized Euclidean array norms are respectively \(\Theta_K(N^{7/2})\) and \(\Theta_K(N^{5/2})\). This is a local source bound with its actual scalar retained. For clarity, canonical support is not imposed after an untransported sector change. Let \(\chi=(\chi_0,\chi_1,\chi_2,\chi_3)\), \(\sum\chi_i=1\), and set \(\beta=1-\chi_0,\gamma=\chi_2+\chi_3,\delta=\chi_3\). The literal covariance of [C] is \[ R_\chi(i,j,k,l) =Q^\gamma R_{\rm can}(i,j+\beta,k+\gamma,l+\delta). \tag{28} \] Transporting the wall with these same port shifts yields \[ (R_W)_\chi=NQ^{\gamma-2i} \delta_{j,i+1-\beta}\delta_{k,i-\gamma}\delta_{l,i-\delta}; \tag{29} \] the current has the same support and phase \(N(Q^{-1}-1)Q^{\gamma+1-i}\). The first-two-port kernels (22)--(23) acquire \(Q^{-\beta(k_2-l_2)}\). The full nine-cell sector scalar is the one in [C] and stays external. An unchanged canonical coupon in the shifted coordinates would be a different insertion. ## 6. Current and analytic scope Writing \(H_L=LHL^{-1}\), the actual current equation is \[ [H_L,LWL^{-1}]=LJL^{-1}. \tag{30} \] The right side has been evaluated explicitly in (17),(23),(27), not discarded. All dual rows use the literal inverse adapters. The partial-factor generator \(H_L\) is not asserted to be the unchanged external coproduct. The weight commutator remains zero, since \(L\) commutes with \(K_1K_2\). This is a local realization of the specified finite reciprocal wall and lowering defect on the actual nine-cell boundary. It neither makes the wall Hopf-natural nor relocates it to the marked cut. It does not identify it with the full negative-ray atomic current, its intersections, or its continuous cycle: those functions and chains still require their own source-preserving transport. All formulas are at the complete fixed odd root. Decoration derivatives do not supply a generic-meridian or off-root quantum identity. No selected geometric coefficient or whole scalar lower is inferred. ## Direct sources and readback The complete target and all five complete direct texts are read before freezing, with matching hashes renewed. Only written mathematics, file reads and hashes are used. * [M](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_middle_five_point_wall_factorization.md), SHA256 a3c9d055fd2acc763f746113379987bfefddb46431a14577067dabb1a46dbcd7: exact two-factor crossing, reciprocal wall and factorial gauge. * [S](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_shared_quantum_flags_and_charged_exchange.md), SHA256 dcab795cc141e2e1db726998cf7b1141dd03c681eaae9076387f90581f53a7d9: original balanced matrices, crossing coefficients and currents. * [P](kashaev_crossing_and_period_lattice.md), SHA256 71e67223742fe905af47d0475435f3a13acc877695bd0cdc321798cf2e608037: literal Fourier crossing and canonical composition support. * [A](research_kashaev_paired_face_boundary_adapter.md), SHA256 c430fd2714acdc7588003e1c18c60453e1ebe123bd7c0155d20a0eef639ec8ed: paired image, inverse dual, cyclic seam and uniform bounds. * [C](research_nine_cell_canonical_crossing_evaluation.md), SHA256 332062e67d64ab4a0767637c0fdd96f186d62c430ad38042aef35ad857d8d7c9: actual all-boundary identity and retained scalar modulus.

title: The actual reduced braid network and its resolved critical scheme
text: # The actual reduced braid network and its resolved critical scheme Private written proof, 18 November 2026. The exact constant-prefix quotient has a finite Euler network. Its regular exponentiated generating correspondence is the Hamiltonian reduction of the original braid correspondence at total lowering coordinate zero. The central first head on that level retains its eigenflag. Discarding that flag would give a different reduction. For a regular semisimple total product, a fixed point of the reduced correspondence lifts to an actual braid fixed point: there is no additional upper-unipotent closing seam. Under the positive complete gluing certificate specified below, the geometric fixed germ, after the common momentum quotient, is a reduced point. For complete discrete faithful holonomy, the needed resolved charts exist after the source-preserving presentation changes in R. These are statements about the actual finite coefficients and their principal rational correspondence. A uniform Fourier integral description on the first-head vacuum, a nonvanishing local amplitude there, and an original-cycle coefficient are not asserted. The three complete proof directs are R, M and H, pinned at the end. ## 1. The finite reduced source and the Euler factors Fix \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\), and \(x=-M/q\). The quantum parameter is fixed at this root while the common meridian \(M\) varies. Put \[ f_a=\prod_{\ell=1}^a(1-Q^\ell),\qquad f_0=1,\qquad Lw_a=w_{a-1}\ (a>0),\quad Lw_0=0. \tag{1} \] The actual \(F\) raises occupation with coefficient \(1-Q^{a+1}\), except that its top arrow is zero. For \(m\) original heads, R proves the exact algebra map \[ \mathcal B_m(W)=p_0S_m^{-1}Wi_0,\qquad S_m=\sum_{n=0}^{d}\frac{(x^{-1}L_1F_{\rm r})^n}{f_n}. \tag{2} \] It retains the original pointed and pivotal source through R's explicit meromorphic Cartan kernel and its removable meridian limit. On braid generators its values are \[ \mathcal B_m(R_i)=R_{i-1}\quad(i\ge2),\qquad \mathcal B_m(R_1)=\kappa S_{m-1}D, \quad Dw_a=(-1)^aQ^{a(a-1)/2}x^{-2a}w_a . \tag{3} \] The negative generators are the exact inverses. The \(R_i\) and \(\kappa\) in this equation have their original Cartan, flip and scalar conventions. Every external framing line and the first-meridian-jet source functional remain those of R. Here is a finite local factorization of the new operator. On \(r\) heads, write \[ F_{\rm tail}=\sum_{j=2}^rK_2^{-1}\cdots K_{j-1}^{-1}F_j, \qquad Z_j=x^{-1}L_1K_2^{-1}\cdots K_{j-1}^{-1}F_j . \tag{4} \] For \(i<j\), the literal weight relations give \(Z_iZ_j=Q^{-1}Z_jZ_i\). The finite product identity is \[ S_r=\prod_{j=2}^r e_Q(Z_j),\qquad e_Q(Z)=\sum_{n=0}^{d}\frac{Z^n}{f_n}, \tag{5} \] with increasing \(j\) from left to right. To prove (5), expand the power of the sum in (4), moving the \(Z_i\)'s into this order. The recursion for the resulting coefficients is the finite Gaussian-binomial recursion; its coefficient of \(Z_2^{n_2}\cdots Z_r^{n_r}\) is \(f_{\sum n_j}/\prod f_{n_j}\). All terms of total degree \(\ge N\) vanish because of the common \(L_1\). Thus only the nonzero denominators \(f_n\), \(n<N\), occur. This also proves the identity at even or composite levels. More explicitly, the entry from \((a,b_2,\ldots,b_r)\) to \((a-n,b_2+n_2,\ldots,b_r+n_r)\), \(n=\sum n_j\), is \[ \prod_{j=2}^r x^{-(j-1)n_j}Q^{\,n_j\sum_{2\le i<j}b_i} \frac{f_{b_j+n_j}}{f_{b_j}f_{n_j}}, \quad n_j\ge0,\quad n\le a,\quad b_j+n_j\le d . \tag{6} \] The rightmost factor in (5) acts first, which explains the unshifted earlier \(b_i\)'s in its phase. The entry of \(S_r^{-1}\) has the same expression multiplied by \((-1)^nQ^{n(n-1)/2}\). Indeed this is the inverse coefficient in degree \(n\) of the finite series in the sum (4). Outside the displayed support both entries are zero. In particular \(S_ri_0=i_0\). None of these identities replaces the physical finite projectors by a cyclic or infinite series. ## 2. The generating correspondence derived from (6) In this and subsequent classical equations write \(x=-M\) for the principal value. Use the factorial coordinates \[ K_j=x/A_j,\qquad e_j=(M/A_j-M^{-1})p_j,\qquad f_j=(1-A_j)/p_j . \tag{7} \] They are precisely M's coordinates, including the selected inverse-meridian eigenflag. On a unit logarithmic chart put \(b_j=\Log A_j\), \(c_j=\Log C_j\). The principal expression read from (6) is \[ \mathcal S_S=\sum_{j=2}^r\left[ -(j-1)\Log x\,c_j+c_j\sum_{2\le i<j}b_i +\operatorname{Li}_2(A_j)+\operatorname{Li}_2(C_j) -\operatorname{Li}_2(A_jC_j)-\operatorname{Li}_2(1) \right]. \tag{8} \] Its input positions are \(A_1,A_2,\ldots,A_r\) and its output positions are \(A_1/\prod C_j,A_2C_2,\ldots,A_rC_r\). For the inverse entry add \(\pi i\sum c_j+\tfrac12(\sum c_j)^2\), on the sheet of the actual sign. The exact half powers, \(\kappa\), and the quantum-to-principal \(x\) shift remain in (3) and (6). No marked primitive constant is discarded by these statements. The convention is \(d\mathcal S=\sum_{\rm out}\log p'\,d\log A' -\sum_{\rm in}\log p\,d\log A\). Differentiating (8), including all monomials, gives \[ p_1'=p_1,\qquad \frac{p_j'}{p_j} =\left(\prod_{\ell>j}C_\ell\right) \frac{1-A_jC_j}{1-A_j}, \qquad \frac{p_j'}{p_1} =x^{-(j-1)}\left(\prod_{2\le i<j}A_i\right) \frac{1-A_jC_j}{1-C_j}. \tag{9} \] Thus these are equations of the literal coefficient graph, not an assumed symbol of the whole triangular matrix. Put \[ u=p_1/x,\quad z_j=uK_2^{-1}\cdots K_{j-1}^{-1}f_j,\quad T_j=1-\sum_{\ell\ge j}z_\ell,\quad T_{r+1}=1,\quad C=T_2 . \tag{10} \] Eliminating the momenta in (9) gives, successively from the last recipient, \[ C_j=T_j/T_{j+1},\quad A_1'=A_1/C,\quad p_1'=p_1,\qquad K_j'=K_jT_{j+1}/T_j,\quad f_j'=f_j/T_{j+1}. \tag{11} \] Equivalently, \(p_j'=p_j(T_{j+1}-A_jT_j)/(1-A_j)\). All identities first hold where the factors used in (9) are units; their rational forms (10)--(11) specify their extension. The total recipient \(F\) and \(p_1\) are unchanged. The inverse entry's additional derivative therefore gives the inverse recipient conjugator \(g^{-1}\) in (13), with the donor \(A_1\) multiplied by \(C\); substitution checks the inverse of (11). For \(D\) in (3) the map is \[ A_1'=A_1,\qquad p_1'=-A_1p_1/x^2 . \tag{12} \] This includes the actual sign in \(D\). For later use there is a matrix form of (11). Form the dressed meridians of the recipient tuple by M's lower Gauss prefixes, and let \(P_j\) be its product through recipient \(j\). Then \[ P_j'=gP_jg^{-1},\qquad g=\begin{pmatrix}C&u\\0&1\end{pmatrix}. \tag{13} \] Here is a direct verification, without a whole-matrix semiclassical assertion. For a recipient prefix write its ordered totals as \(K,F,E\), so \[ P=\begin{pmatrix}K&E\\KF&K^{-1}+EF\end{pmatrix}. \tag{14} \] The sum of its terms in (10) is \(uF\), hence \(T=C+uF\). Equation (11) telescopes to \[ K'=KT/C,\quad F'=F/T,\quad E'=TE+u/K-uKT/C . \tag{15} \] The last equality follows by substitution in (7) for one recipient and induction using \(E_{\le j}=K_jE_{\le j-1}+e_j\) and \(F_{\le j}=F_{\le j-1}+K_{\le j-1}^{-1}f_j\). These are the entries of \(gPg^{-1}\), proving (13). The ratios of consecutive prefixes give the same conjugation for each dressed meridian. ## 3. The first-head flag at total lowering zero At completeness \(M=1,x=-1\), use the resolved first-head chart \[ A_1=1+p_1t,\qquad K_1=-(1+p_1t)^{-1},\quad f_1=-t,\quad e_1=-p_1^2t/(1+p_1t). \tag{16} \] The selected eigenline is \([p_1:1]\). This chart remains regular at \(p_1=0\), and \[ d\log A_1\wedge d\log p_1 =\frac{dt\wedge dp_1}{1+p_1t}. \tag{17} \] At \(t=0\) its meridian matrix is central, but its selected flag is still present. In particular the equation \(A_1-1=0\), by itself, would add the component \(p_1=0\); the resolved lowering-zero equation is \(t=0\). The actual first-head vacuum selects the zero logarithm of \(A_1=1\). Other integer logarithmic sheets are not identified with that physical endpoint by this equation. Write \(F_{\rm r},K_{\rm r},E_{\rm r}\) for the new remaining totals and \(C=1-p_1F_{\rm r}/x\). Applying the map (11) from new to original variables gives \[ K_{1,\rm old}=\frac{xC}{1+p_1t},\qquad f_{1,\rm old}=-\frac{t+F_{\rm r}/x}{C}. \tag{18} \] Its original total lowering coordinate is exactly \(-t\): substitute (11) in \(F_\Sigma=f_{1,\rm old}+K_{1,\rm old}^{-1}F_{\rm r,old}\). Thus the chart implements \(F_\Sigma=0\) as \(t=0\). All \(K\)'s, \(C\) and the recipient \(T_j\)'s are required to be units. A recipient with \(A_j=1,p_j=0\) is represented by its own version of (16); when \(f_j\) is a unit, (11) extends in its regular \((K_j,f_j)\) chart. The entire framing motion on this level can be checked explicitly. At the section \(p_1=0,t=0\), set \[ H_1^0=\begin{pmatrix}x&0\\-F_{\rm r}&x^{-1}\end{pmatrix}, \qquad h_0=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\-F_{\rm r}/x&1/x\end{pmatrix}. \tag{19} \] If \(H_j^{\rm r}\) are the dressed remaining meridians, then the original ones are \(H_{j+1}^0=h_0H_j^{\rm r}h_0^{-1}\). For arbitrary \(p_1\) on the level, all original meridians are \[ H_i(p_1)=U(p_1)H_i^0U(p_1)^{-1},\qquad U(p)=\begin{pmatrix}1&p\\0&1\end{pmatrix}. \tag{20} \] Indeed the product of the original first lower-Gauss inverse and (13) is \[ b_{-,1}^{-1}g =\begin{pmatrix}C&p_1/x\\-F_{\rm r}/x&1/x\end{pmatrix} =U(p_1)h_0 , \tag{21} \] and direct conjugation verifies the first meridian as well. Consequently, on \(F_\Sigma=0\), \[ K_\Sigma=xK_{\rm r},\qquad E_\Sigma=E_{\rm r}+p_1(K_\Sigma^{-1}-K_\Sigma). \tag{22} \] The Hamiltonian lowering flow is this upper-unipotent motion, up to the choice of Poisson sign in (17). Its quotient is therefore the remaining tuple. This statement retains the flag coordinate; it is not a coadjoint-orbit calculation at a central point with the flag forgotten. ## 4. The reduced boundary generator is the actual quotient map We verify the nontrivial generator with arbitrary tails. Use the section in (19), and let the first remaining physical head have \(K_2,e_2,f_2,p_2\). Write \(F_T\) for the total lowering coordinate on all later heads. Thus \(F_{\rm r}=f_2+K_2^{-1}F_T\). The original first head has \(K_1=x,e_1=0,f_1=-F_{\rm r}/x\). M's positive crossing equations have \(1-e_1f_2=1\) and give \[ \begin{split} &K_{1,R}=K_2,\quad K_{2,R}=x,\quad e_{1,R}=e_2/x,\quad e_{2,R}=0,\\ &f_{1,R}=xf_2,\qquad f_{2,R}=f_R=-xK_2f_2-F_T/x . \end{split} \tag{23} \] Undoing the first-head map (11) uses \[ p_{1,\rm new}=p_2/x,\qquad g_m=\begin{pmatrix}K_2/x&p_2/x^2\\0&1\end{pmatrix}. \tag{24} \] The resulting first remaining coordinates are \[ K_{2,\rm new}=K_2+p_2F_T/x^2,\qquad p_{2,\rm new}=-p_2/(xK_2). \tag{25} \] They are exactly (12), followed by \(S_{m-1}\): after \(D\) the donor momentum is \(p_D=-p_2/(xK_2)\), and its new \(C_T=1-p_DF_T/x\) is \(K_{2,\rm new}/K_2\). This also checks every later meridian, not just the first remaining head. Define \[ g_T=\begin{pmatrix}C_T&-p_2/(x^2K_2)\\0&1\end{pmatrix}, \quad b_{-,2,\rm new}= \begin{pmatrix}1&0\\-K_2f_R&K_{2,\rm new}\end{pmatrix}, \quad b_{-,2,R}=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\-xf_R&x\end{pmatrix}. \tag{26} \] The exact identity \[ g_T^{-1}b_{-,2,\rm new} =b_{-,2,R}g_m =\begin{pmatrix}K_2/x&p_2/x^2\\-K_2f_R&K_{2,\rm new}\end{pmatrix} \tag{27} \] identifies their lower-Gauss conjugations. It proves equality of the full quotient maps for arbitrary later heads. For \(i\ge2\), the physical crossing preserves the ordered remaining \(K,F,E\), so its map commutes with the first-head construction; its quotient is the physical \(R_{i-1}\). Inverse generators follow by inversion. Equations (23)--(27) initially use units and then extend on the resolved charts of Section 3 as rational identities with unit denominators. We have thus proved the correspondence directly from the finite reduced coefficients (3), (6): their regular canonical graph is the quotient of \(R_\beta\) on the original \(F_\Sigma=0\) by (20), equivalently the quotient of \(S_m^{-1}R_\beta S_m\) on the new level \(t=0\). No asymptotic action of the whole matrix \(S_m\) on its physical vacuum was used. ## 5. Fixed schemes and the single common momentum Assume \(K_\Sigma^2\ne1\) on this level. A reduced fixed point lifts to an equation \[ R_\beta(z)=U(s)\cdot z . \tag{28} \] The original braid preserves the exact ordered total \(E\) and \(K\). Equations (20)--(22) consequently imply \[ s(K_\Sigma^{-1}-K_\Sigma)=0. \tag{29} \] The second factor is a unit, so \(s=0\). Conversely any original fixed point on this level gives a reduced fixed point. The same calculation works over every local Artin algebra. Thus the reduced fixed scheme is precisely the original fixed scheme on \(F_\Sigma=0\), divided by the upper-unipotent action. It has no additional closing seam. For clarity, passing to independent occupation variables removes one further, specified common momentum. Regard an \(S_r\) factor as a vertex with \(r\) inputs and \(r\) outputs. Its positions have the sole linear conservation equation; inputs and \(r-1\) transfers give its \(2r-1\) coordinates. Equations (9) recover all its momentum ratios. The physical crossings have the same property by M; a \(D\) vertex has one incoming and one outgoing wire and (12). The resulting closed network is connected for a braid whose closure is a knot. For \(m>2\), the word must use \(R_1\) or its inverse, since otherwise its first strand closes as a separate component. Its \(S_{m-1}\) vertex joins all remaining heads. For \(m=2\) there is one remaining wire. Identity pieces may be omitted. The conservation matrix \(L\) of this network therefore has rank one less than the number of vertices. On the vector space of conserved wire positions, the same linear argument as H gives \[ 0\longrightarrow\mathbb C\longrightarrow\mathbb C^{V} \mathop{\longrightarrow}^{L^t}\mathbb C^{E} \longrightarrow(\ker L)^*\longrightarrow0. \tag{30} \] The differential of the sum of the actual local primitives is the list of momentum mismatches restricted to \(\ker L\). Vertex constants can remove that list exactly when the derivative vanishes; their only ambiguity is one global constant. A spanning tree supplies a fixed right inverse, so this is an equality of local schemes, not just tangents. The Fourier integer covector is extended from chord edges and assigned to incident local primitives, as in H. This retains its additive derivative while changing no exponentiated graph. Original pivotal turns are treated in the same fashion. Thus, on a regular logarithmic coefficient chart, the actual occupation gradient scheme is the reduced fixed scheme divided by the single common momentum \(p_j\mapsto\lambda p_j\). On a resolved boundary chart the preceding rational fixed-scheme assertion still makes sense; (30) does not assert that a singular logarithmic primitive has become holomorphic or that a hard projector has disappeared. ## 6. The geometric resolved chart and its local rigidity R permits at most three source-preserving positive stabilizations and an actual braid conjugation so that the complete total product \(P\) is regular semisimple. Suppose first the holonomy is complete, discrete and faithful. In a torsion-free discrete group a nonparabolic noncentral semisimple element is loxodromic: a finite-order elliptic would be torsion, and the powers of an infinite-order elliptic accumulate at the identity. A loxodromic element cannot share a fixed point with a nontrivial parabolic element. In coordinates putting that point at infinity, conjugating the nontrivial translation by appropriate powers of the loxodromic multiplier produces distinct elements converging to the identity. This contradicts discreteness. Choose an eigenline \(v\) of \(P\) and the selected eigenline \(w\) of the first meridian. They are distinct. In the basis \((v,w)\), the total \(P\) is upper triangular and the first meridian has the form (19), with \(F_{\rm r}\ne0\). Every stage prefix \(P_j\) has nonzero upper-left entry. Otherwise \(P_jv\) would be proportional to \(w\), making \(v\) the fixed point of a conjugate of the first parabolic meridian, which was just excluded. Likewise a physical \(f_j=0\) would make \(v\) an eigenline of \(P_{j-1}^{-1}H_jP_{j-1}\), again a conjugate meridian. This proof applies to every prefix in the finite braid and to each reselected first-meridian flag used in (19). At the section (19), the full prefixes satisfy \[ P_j^{\rm full} =h_0P_{j-1}^{\rm r}\operatorname{diag}(x,1). \tag{31} \] In particular their \((1,1)\) entries are \(x\) times those of the remaining prefixes. The new remaining physical heads are exactly the old heads numbered \(2,\ldots,m\) on this section. All their \(K\)'s and \(f\)'s are therefore units at every quotient stage. For an \(S_{m-1}\) generator the input and output \(K\)'s in (11) are units. Starting at \(T_{r+1}=1\) shows successively that all its \(T_j\)'s are units. Its recipients have unit \(f_j\). The donor may have \(p_j=0,A_j=1\); its chart is then (16), with \(t_j=-f_j\) retained. This proves existence of a regular resolved correspondence chart at the geometric point. It does not prove that every new three-factorial shape in (8) avoids one. In particular repeated parabolic flags can force zero transfers. Such points remain resolved correspondence points, not automatically ordinary nonzero-factorial amplitude charts. Now additionally supply the actual exterior's positive complete gluing certificate in H. Its exact selected meridian-eigenvalue theorem makes the unframed geometric representation germ a reduced point. Before quotienting frames, the germ is therefore a smooth conjugation orbit of dimension three. Its projective stabilizer is trivial: a lift of a projective centralizer must conjugate each lifted meridian to itself or its negative; the nonzero parabolic trace excludes the negative. It then centralizes all generators and is scalar by irreducibility, as in H. The exact eigenflag is retained, as in (16), including over Artin rings. The equation \(P_{21}=0\), equivalently \(F_\Sigma=0\), is transverse to that orbit when \(P\) is regular semisimple: infinitesimal lower-unipotent conjugation changes \(P_{21}\) by a nonzero multiple of \(K_\Sigma-K_\Sigma^{-1}\). It leaves a smooth two-dimensional germ. Quotienting the free upper unipotent action (20) leaves the diagonal framing direction, and the common momentum in (30) is exactly that diagonal conjugation. This action is free locally: if every remaining \(p_j\) were zero, their unit \(f_j\) would give every \(A_j=1\) and hence \(K_\Sigma^2=1\), contrary to the stated unit condition. Consequently the geometric resolved reduced fixed germ modulo the common momentum is a reduced point, on each choice of the eigenline \(v\). There are two discrete eigenline choices, not an additional continuous gauge. Whenever an actual regular logarithmic generating chart represents this point, (30) identifies its gradient scheme with that reduced point. Its Hessian is therefore invertible: the kernel is the Zariski tangent of the gradient scheme. This last holomorphic-phase statement requires that chart; the resolved rational result does not manufacture it at singular factorial/projector faces. ## 7. Source and action scope All finite support inequalities in (6), the actual negative coefficients, the prescribed pivots, framing scalars and meridian derivatives remain in (2)--(3). The proof does not differentiate the root reduction as an off-root quantum-normal identity. Such normals retain the prefix carry from R's complete sources. The original scalar source is still the specified Cartan-weighted first-meridian-jet functional of the finite reduced network. The geometric correspondence does not estimate that matrix or its spectral radii. In particular a physical-basis reduced matrix norm is not identified with representation volume. Equation (8) records the literal principal primitive, its three-factorial part, and the inverse's marked quadratic term. Equality of the rational canonical maps proves no equality of marked primitive constants. No reduced regulator/volume calibration is claimed here. Nor does a reduced isolated geometric germ determine a nonzero local amplitude, a thimble coefficient, or the original relative period. ## Complete proof-source pins * R: notes/research_actual_reduced_braid_source.md, SHA256 9a472ef27b08305a519ff1f24b6d2b909e63a0acbdc49b3a29e001c52a2f2243. * M: notes/marked_braid_holonomy.md, SHA256 eff47c757d0e44bda0c396c094315b8e1fce11f1fc2d6445d636c6d2d3a46c4f. * H: notes/research_positive_certificate_braid_morse_bott.md, SHA256 6ef5423e542170ffe3b5464753613ae042341d9c2ee20a2fa94fd0d828738410. All three complete sources were freshly read nontruncated in this author sequence, and every used implication was checked. The finite Euler, resolved-flag, generator and quotient calculations above are written proofs. No mathematical programs were run. Frozen and public files were not edited.

title: The actual reduced braid operators and their pointed trace
text: # The actual reduced braid operators and their pointed trace Private written proof, 18 November 2026. The first-meridian-jet source formula can be used with an explicit finite braid representation. The reduced operator is not an unspecified quotient: its generators are the original crossings on the remaining factors and one triangular Euler operator. The same source formula proves cyclicity on the actual intertwiner algebra. No modified-trace theorem is imported. The complete directs are C for the prefix quotient, H for its scalar source kernel, E for the original crossing matrices, and M for the marked Hurwitz convention. All additional generator, cyclicity, stabilization and norm arguments are below. ## 1. The actual quotient and its algebra map Fix \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\). Keep \(q\) fixed and vary the common meridian \(M\) near one. Write \(x=-M/q\) and \(f_a=\prod_{j=1}^a(1-Q^j)\), \(f_0=1\). The original balanced factors have \[ K w_a=xQ^{-a}w_a,\qquad Fw_a=(1-Q^{a+1})w_{a+1}\quad(a<d),\qquad Fw_d=0. \tag{1} \] The lowering matrix has coefficient \(MQ^{-a}-M^{-1}\) for \(a>0\), and its vacuum arrow is zero. For \(m\) factors let \(F_{\rm r},K_{\rm r}\) be the ordered coproducts on factors \(2,\ldots,m\). With the literal shift \(L_1w_a=w_{a-1}\), \(L_1w_0=0\), C gives \[ S_m=\sum_{j=0}^{d} \frac{(x^{-1}L_1F_{\rm r})^j}{f_j},\qquad S_m^{-1}F_\Sigma S_m=F_1,\qquad [S_m,K_\Sigma]=0. \tag{2} \] Its inverse has coefficient \((-1)^jQ^{j(j-1)/2}/f_j\) in degree \(j\). For one factor use \(S_1=I\). Let \(i_0v=w_0\otimes v\) and let \(p_0\) extract first occupation zero. For an actual total intertwiner \(W\), C proves \[ S_m^{-1}WS_m=\sum_{n=0}^{d}F_1^n\otimes B_n(W). \tag{3} \] The constant coefficient is the exact finite matrix \[ \mathcal B_m(W):=B_0(W)=p_0S_m^{-1}Wi_0. \tag{4} \] Here \(S_mi_0=i_0\). Since positive powers of \(F_1\) cannot contribute a constant term, (3) proves \[ \mathcal B_m(XY)=\mathcal B_m(X)\mathcal B_m(Y),\qquad \mathcal B_m(I)=I,\qquad [\mathcal B_m(W),K_{\rm r}]=0. \tag{5} \] An invertible total intertwiner has invertible image, with inverse \(\mathcal B_m(W^{-1})\). All statements concern the actual common-meridian family at the fixed quantum root. ## 2. Explicit braid generators Assume \(m\ge2\). Let \(R_i\) be the original positive checked crossing on factors \(i,i+1\), including its common Cartan scalar \(\kappa\). E fixes the literal formula \[ R_i=\kappa\,\mathsf P_iD_i\Theta_i,\qquad (D_i)_{a,b}=x^{-a-b}Q^{ab}, \tag{6} \] where the Euler transfer lowers the first input occupation. The negative crossing is the actual inverse. These crossings are total intertwiners at the fixed root throughout the common-meridian family. For \(i\ge2\), the crossing is internal to the remaining tensor. It commutes with its ordered total \(F_{\rm r}\) and \(K_{\rm r}\), hence with \(S_m\). It also commutes with the exposed first-factor maps. Thus, with the remaining positions relabelled \(1,\ldots,m-1\), \[ \mathcal B_m(R_i)=R_{i-1}. \tag{7} \] The right side is precisely the original physical crossing on those two remaining factors. The crossing \(R_1\) has a different explicit image. On input \(w_0\otimes w_b\otimes v\), its positive transfer is forced to be zero, so \[ R_1(w_0\otimes w_b\otimes v) =\kappa x^{-b}w_b\otimes w_0\otimes v. \tag{8} \] In \(p_0S_m^{-1}\), only the degree-\(b\) term can then reach the first row. Equation (4) gives \[ \mathcal B_m(R_1)(w_b\otimes v) =\kappa\frac{(-1)^bQ^{b(b-1)/2}x^{-2b}}{f_b} F_{\rm r}^{\,b}(w_0\otimes v). \tag{9} \] C's finite prefix identity on the remaining \(m-1\) factors is \[ S_{m-1}(w_b\otimes v) =f_b^{-1}F_{\rm r}^{\,b}(w_0\otimes v). \tag{10} \] Consequently define the diagonal matrix on the first remaining factor by \[ D_{\rm red}w_b=(-1)^bQ^{b(b-1)/2}x^{-2b}w_b =(-1)^bq^{b(b+1)}M^{-2b}w_b . \tag{11} \] The exact reduced generator is \[ \boxed{\quad \mathcal B_m(R_1)=\kappa S_{m-1}D_{\rm red},\qquad \mathcal B_m(R_1^{-1}) =\kappa^{-1}D_{\rm red}^{-1}S_{m-1}^{-1}. \quad} \tag{12} \] For \(m=2\), \(S_{m-1}=I\). Every endpoint in (8)--(12) is the actual finite endpoint. No cyclic wrap or infinite series replaces it. Equations (5), (7), and (12) give the original braid relations on the remaining space: they are images of the actual braid relations under an algebra map. They also give \(\mathcal B_m(W_\beta)\) by a literal finite product. All common crossing scalars and any separately prescribed zero-framing line remain. First meridian derivatives follow by the ordinary product rule for this finite product, including derivatives of \(S_{m-1},D_{\rm red},\kappa\). No condition-number bound for the triangular factor is asserted. ## 3. Cyclicity with the original pointed and pivotal source The original highest-cut source is \[ \Phi_0(W)=\operatorname{Tr} ((P_0\otimes K_{\rm r}^{1-N})W). \tag{13} \] H proves the exact meromorphic identity \[ \Phi_0(W)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\rm r} \left(\frac{D_N(M)}{D_N(MK_{\rm r})}\mathcal B_m(W)\right), \qquad D_N(z)=\frac{z^N-z^{-N}}{z-z^{-1}}, \tag{14} \] with its prescribed removable continuation for an actual analytic intertwiner. The fraction is a function of the actual remaining Cartan, not a scalar Casimir choice. For two such intertwiners \(X,Y\), their constant coefficients commute with that function of \(K_{\rm r}\). On the generic meridian set where its denominator is invertible, (5) and the ordinary matrix trace therefore give \[ \Phi_0(XY)=\Phi_0(YX). \tag{15} \] The two original finite source functions are analytic. Thus (15) extends through completeness, as an equality of their common-meridian germs. In particular \[ \Phi_0(GWG^{-1})=\Phi_0(W) \tag{16} \] for an invertible actual total intertwiner \(G\). This permits unmarked braid conjugation with the original highest cut and tail pivot. Braid conjugation also preserves the writhe, so its prescribed external zero-framing scalar is unchanged. This conclusion does not apply to arbitrary marked matrices failing the total intertwining equations. ## 4. A source bound on an actual meridian collar Write \(B(M)=\mathcal B_m(W(M))\). H proves, in the original remaining occupation norm, \[ |\Phi_0(W(1))| \le N^{m-1}\big(\|B(1)\|+m^{-1}\|B'(1)\|\big). \tag{17} \] Suppose the actual finite matrix \(B\) is analytic on a neighborhood of \(|M-1|\le\eta/N\). Matrix Cauchy estimates and the maximum principle give \[ |\Phi_0(W(1))| \le N^{m-1}\left(1+\frac{N}{m\eta}\right) \sup_{|M-1|=\eta/N}\|B(M)\|. \tag{18} \] This is a polynomial cost at fixed \(m,\eta\). Every external scalar line must still be included if the source convention places it outside \(W\). Neither (17) nor (18) bounds the actual reduced word. A large norm does not imply that its specified trace functional is nonzero. ## 5. A regular semisimple total product after at most three stabilizations There is a useful presentation choice for an irreducible complete representation of the knot group. The tuple of its ordered noncentral parabolic meridians is denoted \(H_1,\ldots,H_m\) in M's sign convention, and \(P=H_m\cdots H_1\). Positive Hurwitz motion sends an adjacent pair to \[ (H_i,H_{i+1})\longmapsto (H_i^{-1}H_{i+1}H_i,H_i). \tag{19} \] It preserves \(P\). Applying positions \(j,j+1,\ldots,m-1\) therefore moves a chosen \(H_j\) to the last position unchanged. Conjugate the braid by that explicit Hurwitz word. Append a new last meridian equal to the old last one, and positively stabilize the braid. Its last crossing fixes this equal pair, so the new tuple still satisfies every braid fixed-point relation. Its total product is \(H_jP\). Repeated stabilization on this last meridian gives \(H_j^tP\). Topologically these are Markov stabilizations of the same knot. If \(\operatorname{tr}(P)^2\ne4\), no change is needed. If \(P\) is noncentral parabolic, write \[ P=\epsilon(I+A),\qquad H_j=\delta(I+B),\qquad A^2=B^2=0,\qquad \epsilon,\delta\in\{1,-1\}. \tag{20} \] Irreducibility supplies a meridian whose eigenline differs from the unique eigenline of \(P\). For this choice \(\operatorname{tr}(BA)\ne0\): in a basis making \(A\) strictly upper triangular, the lower-left entry of \(B\) is nonzero and computes this trace. Thus \[ \operatorname{tr}(H_j^tP)^2 =(2+t\,\operatorname{tr}(BA))^2 . \tag{21} \] For a nonzero number \(c\), the two numbers \(2+c\) and \(2+2c\) cannot both belong to \(\{2,-2\}\). One or two positive stabilizations therefore make this product regular semisimple. If \(P\) was central, a first stabilization makes it noncentral parabolic; the preceding argument then uses at most two more. The enlarged tuple is still irreducible because it generates the same group. This proves the bound of three. For completeness the exact quantum scalar of each such stabilization follows directly from (6), with no generic modified-trace assumption. Put \(g=K^{1-N}\). Integer-degree conservation makes \(\operatorname{Tr}_2((I\otimes g)R_+)\) diagonal. For its input occupation \(a\), set \(t=Q^{1-a}x^2\). The literal finite crossing coefficients give \[ \begin{split} T_a={}&\kappa x^{1-N}x^{-2a}Q^{a(a-1)} \sum_{n=0}^a(-1)^nQ^{n(n-1)/2+(1-a)n} {a\brack n}_Q(t;Q)_n . \end{split} \tag{22} \] The finite sum is \(t^a\). To check it, its coefficient of \(t^k\), \(k<a\), is a nonzero scalar factor times \((Q^{k+1-a};Q)_{a-k}\), which contains \(1-Q^0\). This follows by expanding the products and using the finite product expansion for the Gaussian coefficients. Its leading coefficient is one. All products have length at most \(a<N\), so no root denominator was inverted. It follows that \[ \operatorname{Tr}_2((I\otimes g)R_+) =\alpha I,\qquad \alpha=\kappa x^{1-N}. \tag{23} \] The actual zero-framing compensation multiplies by \(\alpha^{-1}\) when the positive writhe increases by one. It consequently cancels exactly the scalar in (23). Equivalently, define the normalized zero-framed raw braid source by its prescribed factor \(\alpha^{-\mathrm{wr}(\beta)}\); (23) verifies its positive Markov invariance directly. Any separately retained modified-dimension line is unchanged. Together with (16), these operations preserve the original normalized root-meridian source, with its actual meridian germ. This is not an off-root quantum-normal argument. For the resulting regular semisimple \(P\), there is always an eigenline different from the selected meridian flag. It supplies a finite classical frame with \(P_{21}=0\). This statement does not place every other shape in a common regular slit chart or put the geometric point on the original integration cycle. The stabilization lemma establishes presentation regularity only. ## 6. Scope and complete proof-source pins The reduction is exact on the root-quantum common-meridian family. Quantum normals retain C's additional prefix row \(J_N\); the root generator reduction is not differentiated as an ordinary-color quantum-normal identity. No assertion about a geometric integration cycle, source positivity, or a surviving geometric contribution is made. * C: notes/research_prefix_commutant_and_pointed_normal_functional.md, SHA256 b4fb801a1482316aebb4799f1d0b80d5b43ced39138d903c04cfde811ca166b0. * H: notes/research_scalar_prefix_kernel_and_first_meridian_jet.md, SHA256 d7d82848a1b3f50709352905bafcc7ddfee36f41e434bf5de4663b4b6181dc9e. * E: notes/research_actual_compressed_endpoint_euler_transition.md, SHA256 9c735f005fa94afe56931af5fc0cb77ee95849a9c4c89067290711135ad1ed16. * M: notes/marked_braid_holonomy.md, SHA256 eff47c757d0e44bda0c396c094315b8e1fce11f1fc2d6445d636c6d2d3a46c4f. All four complete directs were read nontruncated in this active sequence and are retained unchanged. Every used implication was checked. Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used. Frozen and public files were not changed.

title: Physical conditioning of the complete upper Gauss normal
text:
# Physical conditioning of the complete upper Gauss normal Private written proof, 18 November 2026. The upper Fourier coefficient sector of the actual balanced Gauss source has polynomial bounds, including its first meridian normal. Those bounds do not survive evaluation on the original physical Cartan--Casimir matrices. This note proves an exponential norm lower bound for the **complete prescribed upper first-normal sum**, not merely for one interpolation coupon or for an arbitrary nonnormal matrix. The lower bound survives every positive diagonal physical metric, including the binomial coherent metric. The proof uses an actual two-tail-head block at every even level. An exact finite harmonic cancellation computes its whole radical multiplier. The product of its nonzero singular values then prevents cancellation from making the full matrix polynomially bounded. The original tail pivot on this block is one. A marked pivotal matrix-entry test is therefore explicit, but it is not an unmarked knot contraction or a claim about a fixed short-tangle exterior. The only complete proof directs are C and H, pinned at the end. No numerical tests, mathematical programs, or imported asymptotic theorems are used. ## 1. The actual upper first-normal operator Set \[ N=2p\ge2,\quad d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\quad 	heta=\pi/N, \qquad f_n=(Q;Q)_n,\quad s_n=|f_n|. 	ag{1} \] The quantum root is fixed. Meridian derivatives below are \(\partial_\mu\), where \(M=e^\mu\), at \(\mu=0\). Use C's exact Fourier polynomials and symmetric coupons: \[ L_l(u)= rac1N\sum_{a=0}^{d}(uQ^{-l})^a,\qquad \mathcal D_{lk}(u,v) =	frac12\{L_l(u)L_k(v)+L_k(u)L_l(v)\}. 	ag{2} \] Their physical evaluation is the symmetric-polynomial substitution \[ u+v= rac{\Omega}{qK},\qquad uv= rac1{QK^2}. 	ag{3} \] There is no choice of a scalar root of the Casimir in (3). For \(l+k\ge N\), C proves \[ C_{lk}(1)=0,\qquad \dot C_{lk}=2N rac{f_{l+k-N}}{f_lf_k}. 	ag{4} \] Here \(C_{lk}(M)=g_{l+k}/(g_lg_k)\), with \(g_n=(M^{-2}Q;Q)_n\). Define the **whole prescribed upper normal** \[ U_N(K,\Omega)= \sum_{\substack{0\le l,k<N\l+k\ge N}} \dot C_{lk}\mathcal D_{lk}(K,\Omega). 	ag{5} \] It is not the derivative of a root-reflected factorial formula. Since every upper coefficient vanishes at the root, derivatives of the moving coupons do not occur in this particular normal: \[ \left.\partial_\mu \sum_{l+k\ge N}C_{lk}(M) \mathcal D_{lk}(K(M),\Omega(M))ight|_0 =U_N(K(1),\Omega(1)). 	ag{6} \] Moving-coupon derivatives remain essential in C's complete lower plus upper source; (6) does not remove them there. Take two literal remaining heads and their physical integer-degree \(d\) block \[ \mathcal V_d =\operatorname{span}\{|a,d-aangle:0\le a<N\}. 	ag{7} \] Their actual root total Cartan is \(K=1\). Hence their original total pivotal operator \(K^{1-N}\) is also one on this block. We write \(U_N\) for the actual matrix \(U_N(1,\Omega)|_{\mathcal V_d}\). The basis in (7) initially has its balanced flat Euclidean norm. Section 4 treats every positive diagonal change of that norm. The physical upper factor in C is \[ \mathcal A_{m up}(M)=H_d(M)K(M)^d \sum_{l+k\ge N}C_{lk}(M)\mathcal D_{lk}(M). 	ag{8} \] Here \(H_d(M)=\prod_{a=1}^d(MQ^{-a}-M^{-1})\). Because \(H_d(1)=(-1)^dN=-N\), (6) gives \[ \mathcal A_{m up}(1)=0,\qquad \mathcal A_{m up}'|_{\mathcal V_d}=-N U_N. 	ag{9} \] Thus the estimate below concerns an actual meridian-normal part of the literal Gauss source. ## 2. Exact evaluation of the full radical multiplier Let \(C_n(z)\) be the monic polynomial defined by \[ C_n(w+w^{-1})=w^n+w^{-n}. 	ag{10} \] On (7), H proves that the actual Casimir \(\mathcal J=\Omega\) is complex symmetric tridiagonal. Its offdiagonals are \[ \mathcal J_{a+1,a}=\mathcal J_{a,a+1} =-(1-Q^{a+1})^2,\qquad 0\le a<d. 	ag{11} \] Its characteristic polynomial is \[ C_N(z)+2=C_p(z)^2. 	ag{12} \] The distinct nodes, all double, are \[ \lambda_j=qQ^j+q^{-1}Q^{-j} =2\cos((2j+1)	heta),\qquad 0\le j<p. 	ag{13} \] Write \(k=d-j\), \(\Delta_j=qQ^j-q^{-1}Q^{-j}=2i\sin((2j+1)	heta)\), and \(
u_j=(-1)^jq^{j(j+1)}\). The symmetric polynomial (5), at \(K=1\), has degree at most \(d\) in \(z=\Omega\). At \(z=\lambda_j\) one can evaluate it using \(u=Q^j,v=Q^k\). The interpolation polynomials in (2) then select only the pair \((j,k)\), whose sum is \(d<N\). Consequently \[ U_N(\lambda_j)=0. 	ag{14} \] To compute its derivative, vary \(u=Q^je^t,v=Q^ke^{-t}\). The product \(uv=Q^{-1}\) is fixed and \(\Omega_t|_0=\Delta_j\). For \(l
e j\), the exact finite fraction for \(L_l\) gives \[ Q^jL_l'(Q^j)=- rac1{1-Q^{j-l}}. 	ag{15} \] The coefficient array is symmetric, so its sum against \(\mathcal D_{lk}\) equals its sum against \(L_l(u)L_k(v)\). Only \(l>j\) or \(k'>k\) survives in its \(t\)-derivative. Put \[ T_r(l)= rac{f_{r-1}f_l} {f_{l+r}(1-Q^{-r})},\qquad l+r<N. 	ag{16} \] Using \(f_d/(f_jf_k)=
u_j^{-1}\), equations (4),(15) give the exact finite sum \[ (U_N)_t(\lambda_j) =2
u_j^{-1}\left\{ \sum_{s=1}^{j}T_s(k)-\sum_{r=1}^{k}T_r(j)ight\}. 	ag{17} \] No phases in this sum have been discarded. Here is its finite harmonic cancellation. Direct subtraction yields \[ T_r(l)-T_r(l-1) = rac{Q^{l+r}f_{l-1}f_{r-1}}{f_{l+r}} =:G(l,r)=G(r,l). 	ag{18} \] Indeed the quotient of the two \(T\)'s is \((1-Q^l)/(1-Q^{l+r})\), and \((Q^r-1)/(1-Q^{-r})=Q^r\). Expanding \(T_r(j)\) from \(j=0\) makes the two double sums in (17) equal rectangular sums of \(G\). They cancel. Finally \[ T_r(0)= rac1{(1-Q^r)(1-Q^{-r})} = rac1{4\sin^2(r	heta)}. 	ag{19} \] Since \(j<k\), we obtain \[  oxed{\quad U_N'(\lambda_j)= - rac{
u_j^{-1}}{2\Delta_j} \sum_{r=j+1}^{d-j}\csc^2(r	heta). \quad} 	ag{20} \] This is the derivative with respect to the Casimir argument, of the already specified meridian normal (5). Every coefficient in (20) is nonzero. ## 3. The original Hermite frame and its determinant For clarity we recall exactly the part of H used here. Let \(\phi_a(z)\) be the normalized continuant column of the tridiagonal matrix (11): \[ \phi_0(z)=1,\qquad \phi_a(z)=  rac{\det(zI-\mathcal J_{[0,a-1]})} {\mathcal J_{1,0}\mathcal J_{2,1}\cdots \mathcal J_{a,a-1}}. 	ag{21} \] It has degree \(a\) and the displayed reciprocal leading coefficient. Write \[ v_j=(\phi_0(\lambda_j),\ldots,\phi_d(\lambda_j))^{\mathsf t}, \qquad v'_j=(\phi_0'(\lambda_j),\ldots,\phi_d'(\lambda_j))^{\mathsf t}. 	ag{22} \] These are the actual value and Jordan-partner columns, \((\mathcal J-\lambda_j)v'_j=v_j\). The bilinear pairings of distinct nodes vanish, and the pairing on each two-column block is \[  egin{pmatrix}0&\sigma_j\ \sigma_j&\sigma_j\eta_j\end{pmatrix}, \qquad |\sigma_j|= rac1{4\sin^2((2j+1)	heta)}. 	ag{23} \] No estimate or value of \(\eta_j\) is needed. The inverse of this two-by-two block shows that a polynomial whose values vanish at all nodes acts by \(\sum_j P'(\lambda_j)v_jv_j^{\mathsf t}/\sigma_j\). Applying (14),(20), and setting \[ F=(v_0,\ldots,v_{p-1}),\qquad b_j=U_N'(\lambda_j)/\sigma_j, 	ag{24} \] therefore proves the actual matrix identity \[ U_N=F\operatorname{diag}(b_j)F^{\mathsf t}. 	ag{25} \] It has rank \(p\). In particular, this expression retains all Jordan directions and is not a diagonal spectral evaluation. Equations (20),(23) give \[ |b_j|=\sin((2j+1)	heta) \sum_{r=j+1}^{d-j}\csc^2(r	heta) \ \ge\ \sin((2j+1)	heta). 	ag{26} \] The first \(p\) physical rows of \(F\), denoted \(F_0\), have a Vandermonde determinant. By (11),(21), \[ |\det F_0|^2 = rac{\prod_{j<k}|\lambda_k-\lambda_j|^2} {\prod_{a=0}^{p-1}s_a^4}. 	ag{27} \] The roots in (13) are precisely those of monic \(C_p\). Differentiating \(C_p(2\cos t)=2\cos(pt)\) gives \[ |C_p'(\lambda_j)|= rac p{\sin((2j+1)	heta)}. 	ag{28} \] The elementary root product \(\prod_{j=0}^{p-1}\sin((2j+1)	heta)=2^{1-p}\) follows by taking absolute values in \(z^p+1\) at \(z=1\). Hence \[ \prod_{j<k}|\lambda_k-\lambda_j|^2 =2^{p-1}p^p,\qquad \det(F^*F)\ge|\det F_0|^2 = rac{2^{p-1}p^p}{\prod_{a=0}^{p-1}s_a^4}. 	ag{29} \] The Gram inequality is Cauchy--Binet and uses an actual physical-row minor, not a chosen eigenframe norm. ## 4. An exact lower bound in every diagonal physical metric For any positive diagonal \(D\) in the basis (7), let \(\|\cdot\|_D\) mean \(\|D(\cdot)D^{-1}\|_{m op}\). This includes the balanced flat norm and the tensor binomial coherent metric restricted to this block. For a full-column-rank matrix \(X\), thin QR shows that the product of the \(p\) nonzero singular values of \(X B X^{\mathsf t}\) is \(\det(X^*X)|\det B|\). More generally, for (25) after diagonal conjugation, that product is \[ \left(\prod_j|b_j|ight) \sqrt{\det(F^*D^2F)\det(F^*D^{-2}F)}. 	ag{30} \] To verify it, write \(DU_ND^{-1}=(DF)\operatorname{diag}(b_j) (D^{-1}\overline F)^*\) and take thin QR on both rectangular factors. Their determinant moduli are the square roots of their Gram determinants. Complex conjugation on the second Gram does not change its positive real determinant. Determinant Cauchy--Schwarz applied to \(DF,D^{-1}F\) gives \[ \det(F^*D^2F)\det(F^*D^{-2}F) \ge\det(F^*F)^2. 	ag{31} \] One proof takes their exterior products of degree \(p\) and applies ordinary Cauchy--Schwarz; their mutual determinant is \(\det(F^*F)\). Combining (26),(29)--(31), the product of the nonzero singular values is at least \[  rac{2^{p-1}p^p}{\prod_{a=0}^{p-1}s_a^4} \prod_{j=0}^{p-1}\sin((2j+1)	heta) = rac{p^p}{\prod_{a=0}^{p-1}s_a^4}. 	ag{32} \] At least one singular value is at least their geometric mean. We have proved the finite, uniform statement \[  oxed{\qquad \|U_N\|_D\ \ge\ p\left(\prod_{a=0}^{p-1}s_aight)^{-4/p} \quad	ext{for every positive diagonal }D. \qquad} 	ag{33} \] This argument concerns the **entire** upper normal. Its scalar phases cannot invalidate (33), since they cancel from the product of singular values. ## 5. The positive exponential rate Define \[ J(t)=\int_0^t\log(2\sin(\pi x))\,dx,\qquad \gamma=-8\int_0^{1/2}J(t)\,dt. 	ag{34} \] Here \(\gamma>0\). Indeed the logarithm is negative up to \(t=1/6\) and positive thereafter up to \(1/2\), and \(J(1/2)=0\). The latter identity follows by putting \(I=\int_0^{\pi/2}\log\sin x\,dx =\int_0^{\pi/2}\log\cos x\,dx\), adding, and using \(\sin x\cos x=	frac12\sin2x\); it gives \(I=-(\pi/2)\log2\). Thus \(J(t)<0\) for every \(0<t<1/2\). For completeness a monotone integral comparison on \([1/N,1/2]\) gives, uniformly for \(0\le a\le p\), \[ \log s_a=NJ(a/N)+O(\log N). 	ag{35} \] The function \(\log(2\sin\pi x)\) is increasing on this interval. Comparing its left and right rectangle sums costs at most its endpoint difference \(O(\log N)\); the omitted interval \([0,1/N]\) has integral \(O((\log N)/N)\). This proves (35), including \(a=0\). Since \(J\) has bounded variation on \([0,1/2]\), a second rectangle comparison gives \[ \sum_{a=0}^{p-1}\log s_a =N^2\int_0^{1/2}J(t)\,dt+O(N\log N). 	ag{36} \] Equations (33),(36), with \(p=N/2\), imply \[  oxed{\quad \log\|U_N\|_D\ge\gamma N-O(\log N), \qquad N\ 	ext{even}. \quad} 	ag{37} \] The constants are independent of \(D\). By (9), the same exponential rate holds for the actual upper normal \(\mathcal A_{m up}'\), with its extra factor \(N\). Consequently a polynomial estimate on a whole scaled meridian collar for this evaluated upper sector is impossible: Cauchy's estimate would give a polynomial first \(\mu\)-normal, contradicting (37). ## 6. Source meaning and limits C bounds the complete upper coefficient array, its fixed scalar Fourier jets on thin annuli, and its fixed meridian jets by polynomials. Equations (33),(37) show that evaluation on the specified original physical representation can nevertheless cost an exponential. This holds after every positive diagonal factorial or coherent change of metric. There is an exact marked pivotal test. In any such orthonormal physical coordinates, one entry of \(U_N\) has modulus at least \(\|U_N\|_D/N\). The corresponding reversed matrix-unit mark has norm one. Since the actual total tail pivot is one on (7), its pivotal trace with \(U_N\) is exactly that entry. Applying (9) retains the actual \(H_dK^d\) first-normal factor as well. The mark can depend on the level and the entry attaining this bound. It is not asserted to be the image of a fixed braid or a fixed short filling. The complete opposite source remains C's identity \[ T=\mathcal B_m(W_	au^{-1})\,\mathcal A_N\, D_{m top}\mathscr C_r(M),\qquad J=D_N(MK)^{-1}T. 	ag{38} \] None of these factors, the original cut, its framing scalar, or an exterior contraction is removed. Even though the upper factor vanishes at the root, its normal (9) must be transported through all factors in (38). The present lower bound for that factor does not give a lower bound after those compositions. Their coherent cancellations remain possible. Thus the proposed general polynomial-cost evaluation of the upper Fourier carry is false already on this actual fixed-width physical block. A proof that its contribution is small in a particular original closed source would require additional source-specific cancellation or a weighted non-diagonal estimate with its boundary costs retained. No knot noncancellation, geometric occurrence, or volume conclusion is inferred. ## Complete proof directs * C: notes/research_balanced_gauss_cyclic_divisor_source.md, SHA256 c15668d7dff95346d72801b721bf95970b661e5b17d125aaadd7e0dc38905b00. * H: notes/actual_complete_casimir_hermite_packet.md, SHA256 a4e96738a3a093d963fe13cc03585085951fa8699a506ade4e2e7a47c17b3f4c. Both complete directs were read nontruncated in this active author sequence. Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used. Frozen and public files were not changed.
