# Carry-projector Ward decay through an actual fixed braid word Private written proof, 19 November 2026. The normalized coherent estimate for a carry-projector current can be propagated through a literal finite braid word on an explicit open domain. The proof sums the actual crossing transfers before estimating the current. It does not multiply normalized coherent symbols or assume a crossing amplitude is a unit. The propagation cost is a positive linear map on output moduli. Its finite composition gives a computable exponential base for the complete word. On the domain where that base is less than one, all fixed coherent derivatives and genuine meridian jets of the composed current decay exponentially. The physical caps, crossing scalars, and original zero-framing line remain explicit. No assertion places an arbitrary geometric critical point or closing cycle in this domain. ## 1. Actual matrices and a finite column majorant Fix \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\), \(M=e^\mu\), and \(x=-M/q\). The quantum root is fixed. There are \(m\ge2\) physical heads with occupations \(0,\ldots,d\). F supplies the literal arrows \[ E(M)e_a=(MQ^{-a}-M^{-1})e_{a-1}\quad(a>0),\quad E(M)e_0=0, \qquad Fe_a=(1-Q^{a+1})e_{a+1},\quad Ke_a=xQ^{-a}e_a. 	ag{1} \] The upper \(F\) arrow is zero. Write \(f_a=(Q;Q)_a\), and remove only the actual common crossing scalar by setting \(\widehat R^\sigma(M)=\kappa(M)^{-\sigma}R^\sigma(M)\), \(\sigma=\pm1\). The finite matrices of F(31) are \[ \widehat R^+=PD\sum_{n=0}^{d}  rac{(-1)^nq^{n^2}}{f_n}E_1^nF_2^n, \qquad \widehat R^-=\sum_{n=0}^{d} rac{q^n}{f_n}E_1^nF_2^nD^{-1}P, 	ag{2} \] where \(P\) flips the heads and \(De_{a,b}=x^{-a-b}Q^{ab}e_{a,b}\). These are physical finite matrices, not cyclic completions. At \(M=1\), every nonzero positive entry has output \((b+n,a-n)\), \(0\le n\le\min(a,d-b)\). The negative entry has output \((b-n,a+n)\), \(0\le n\le\min(b,d-a)\). The donor product in (2) satisfies \[ \prod_{j=a-n+1}^{a}(Q^{-j}-1) =Q^{-n(2a-n+1)/2} rac{f_a}{f_{a-n}}. 	ag{3} \] Thus the positive coefficient, up to a modulus-one phase, is \({a rack n}_Q\prod_{j=b+1}^{b+n}(1-Q^j)\). For the negative coefficient it is \({b rack n}_Q\prod_{j=a+1}^{a+n}(1-Q^j)\). All the displayed factorial indices are below \(N\). The finite Gaussian polynomial has nonnegative coefficients with sum \( inom an\): induction in \({a rack n}_Q={a-1 rack n}_Q+ Q^{a-n}{a-1 rack n-1}_Q\) proves both statements, including the endpoint polynomials one. Consequently, at every level, \[ |(\widehat R^+_0)_{b+n,a-n;\,a,b}|\le inom an2^n, \qquad |(\widehat R^-_0)_{b-n,a+n;\,a,b}|\le inom bn2^n. 	ag{4} \] Here the subscript zero means \(M=1\). Extending the nonnegative majorant sum beyond an actual recipient cap only enlarges a bound; no forbidden matrix entry is introduced into (2). For nonnegative output weights \(s_1,s_2\), summing every actual transfer in (4) gives \[  egin{split} \sum_{c,e}|(\widehat R^+_0)_{c,e;\,a,b}|s_1^cs_2^e &\le(s_2+2s_1)^a s_1^b,\ \sum_{c,e}|(\widehat R^-_0)_{c,e;\,a,b}|s_1^cs_2^e &\le s_2^a(s_1+2s_2)^b. \end{split} 	ag{5} \] The binomial theorem proves these inequalities also at zero weights, with \(0^0=1\). No division by \(s_1\) or \(s_2\) is used. For a pair at positions \(i,i+1\), define the nonnegative linear maps \(\mathsf U_{i,\sigma}\) by leaving every other coordinate fixed and replacing that pair by \[ \mathsf U_+(s_1,s_2)=(s_2+2s_1,s_1),\qquad \mathsf U_-(s_1,s_2)=(s_2,s_1+2s_2). 	ag{6} \] They are majorants for the signed matrices, not inverse maps or classical braid maps. ## 2. Word composition and the true meridian collar Let the fixed word act as \[ W_ eta(M)=R_{i_c}^{\sigma_c}(M)\cdots R_{i_1}^{\sigma_1}(M), \qquad \omega=\sum_{\ell=1}^c\sigma_\ell,\qquad \widehat W_ eta=\kappa(M)^{-\omega}W_ eta. 	ag{7} \] Given an output weight vector \(s\ge0\), define recursively \[ s^{(c)}=s,\qquad s^{(\ell-1)}=\mathsf U_{i_\ell,\sigma_\ell}(s^{(\ell)}), \qquad U_ eta(s)=s^{(0)}. 	ag{8} \] The order in (8) is backwards through the actual ordered product. Taking absolute values of the finite matrix product, summing its last output first, and applying (5) inductively proves \[ \sum_{\mathbf b}|(\widehat W_ eta(1))_{\mathbf b,\mathbf a}| s^{\mathbf b} \le \prod_{j=1}^m U_{ eta,j}(s)^{a_j}. 	ag{9} \] Every intermediate sum still uses \(0\le a_j\le d\). This estimate extends to the actual complex meridian family. For \(0<\eta'<\pi\), F(25),(32) supply the diagonal matrices \[ D_h(M)e_a=h_a(M)e_a,\qquad h_a(M)=M^{-a} rac{f_a}{(M^{-2}Q;Q)_a},\qquad \|D_h^{\pm1}\|\le(N+1)^{C_{\eta'}} 	ag{10} \] on \(|N\mu|\le\eta'\), and the exact identities \[  egin{split} \widehat R_i^+(M) &=M^{-J_i-J_{i+1}}D_{h,i+1}(M) \widehat R_{i,0}^+D_{h,i}(M)^{-1},\ \widehat R_i^-(M) &=M^{J_i+J_{i+1}}D_{h,i}(M) \widehat R_{i,0}^-D_{h,i+1}(M)^{-1}. \end{split} 	ag{11} \] All frames and their inverses are holomorphic on that collar. For each entry, their absolute cost is at most a power of \(N\), and \(|M|^{\pm(J_i+J_{i+1})}\le e^{2\eta'}\). Applying (5) with these bounds at every original stage proves \[  oxed{\quad \sum_{\mathbf b}|(\widehat W_ eta(e^\mu))_{\mathbf b,\mathbf a}| s^{\mathbf b} \le C(N+1)^B\prod_j U_{ eta,j}(s)^{a_j}, \qquad |N\mu|\le\eta'. \quad} 	ag{12} \] The constants depend on the fixed word and collar, not on its occupations, the output weights, or the level. No adjacent frames were cancelled and no off-root factorial reflection was used. ## 3. The complete composed threshold kernels For any actual matrix on the \(m\) heads, use the input-binomial kernel \[ K_A(z,w)=\sum_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b} A_{\mathbf b,\mathbf a} \prod_j inom d{a_j}z_j^{b_j}w_j^{a_j},\qquad I_N(z,w)=\prod_j(1+z_jw_j)^d. 	ag{13} \] All its sums are finite. Fix an adjacent pair \(p,r=p+1\), and put \[ E_{pr}=E_pK_r+E_r,\quad F_{pr}=F_p+K_p^{-1}F_r, \quad J_{pr}=J_p+J_r,\quad \Pi_0=\mathbf1_{J_{pr}\le d},\quad\Pi_1=I-\Pi_0. 	ag{14} \] Define the normalized composed currents \[ \mathcal E_{ eta,p}=  rac{K_{\widehat W_ eta E_{pr}\mathbf1_{J_{pr}=N}}}{I_N}, \qquad \mathcal F_{ eta,p}=  rac{K_{\widehat W_ eta F_{pr}\mathbf1_{J_{pr}=d}}}{I_N}. 	ag{15} \] The current acts first, immediately before the displayed word. Assume only \(1+z_jw_j
e0\). Write \[ U=U_ eta(|z|),\quad X_j=U_j|w_j|,\quad \mathcal B_{ eta,p}(z,w)=  rac{(\sqrt{X_p}+\sqrt{X_r})^2 \prod_{j
e p,r}(1+X_j)} {\prod_j|1+z_jw_j|}. 	ag{16} \] Then for the same buffered collar as in (12), \[  oxed{ egin{split} |\mathcal E_{ eta,p}| &\le C(N+1)^B d(|w_p|+|w_r|)\mathcal B_{ eta,p}^{d},\ |\mathcal F_{ eta,p}| &\le C(N+1)^B(U_p+U_r)\mathcal B_{ eta,p}^{d}. \end{split}} 	ag{17} \] In particular the estimate includes zero output coordinates. Here is the complete contraction proof. On input pair occupations \((a,b)\), \(E_{pr}\) has coefficients \(xQ^{-b}(MQ^{-a}-M^{-1})\) and \(MQ^{-b}-M^{-1}\), and lowers the first or second occupation. On the threshold \(a+b=N\) both occupations are positive, so neither bottom arrow is added. The coefficients are bounded on the collar. Equation (12) thus weights the two terms by \(U_p^{a-1}U_r^b\) and \(U_p^aU_r^{b-1}\), respectively. For \(F_{pr}\), on \(a+b=d\), the analogous weights are \(U_p^{a+1}U_r^b\) and \(U_p^aU_r^{b+1}\), with bounded coefficients \(1-Q^{a+1}\) and \(x^{-1}Q^a(1-Q^{b+1})\). Their actual upper zeros remain in the finite sum. For clarity let \(S_\ell(X,Y)=\sum_{a+b=\ell} inom da inom dbX^aY^b\). The positive-coefficient estimate \[ S_\ell(X,Y)\le R^{-\ell}(1+RX)^d(1+RY)^d 	ag{18} \] with \(R=(XY)^{-1/2}\) gives \(S_d\le(\sqrt X+\sqrt Y)^{2d}\). Moreover \(S_N\) is divisible by \(XY\), and reindexing \(a-1\) with \( inom da\le d inom{d-1}{a-1}\) gives \[ S_N(X,Y)/X\le d(\sqrt X+\sqrt Y)^{2d},\qquad S_N(X,Y)/Y\le d(\sqrt X+\sqrt Y)^{2d}. 	ag{19} \] These are precisely C's divided-shell estimates, with their proof unchanged when the denominator is the original \(I_N\). Continuity of the polynomial quotients gives (19) also at zero. In the first lowering term, \(|w_p|\) times \(S_N/X_p\) is the weighted pair sum; the other term uses \(|w_r|S_N/X_r\). For the raising terms the factors are \(U_pS_d,U_rS_d\). Every spectator sum is exactly \((1+X_j)^d\). Multiplication of these bounds and division by \(|I_N|\) proves (17). The argument estimates the full finite composition, including all its transfers, before any normalized kernel is formed. ## 4. An explicit open domain, jets, and original scalar lines Let \(\mathcal K\) be a compact subset of \[ \mathcal V_{ eta,p}= \{(z,w):1+z_jw_j
e0	ext{ for all }j, \mathcal B_{ eta,p}(z,w)<1\}. 	ag{20} \] This is a nonempty open set for every fixed word. Indeed take \(z_j=w_j=t>0\). By homogeneity of (6),(8), write \(U_ eta(t\mathbf1)=t\,a\), where every \(a_j>0\) is fixed. Then \[ \mathcal B_{ eta,p}(t\mathbf1,t\mathbf1) =t^2(\sqrt{a_p}+\sqrt{a_r})^2  rac{\prod_{j
e p,r}(1+a_jt^2)}{(1+t^2)^m} \longrightarrow0. 	ag{21} \] Choose one sufficiently small positive \(t\), independent of \(N\), and a complex neighborhood of it. Its binomial input mean on every head is \(dt^2/(1+t^2)\), an extensive positive occupation; the domain is not restricted to the vacuum point. Choose \(0<\eta<\eta'<\pi\). Compactness supplies a fixed complex neighborhood of \(\mathcal K\) with bounded coordinates, nonzero incidence denominators, and \(\mathcal B_{ eta,p}\le\gamma<1\). The kernels (15) are holomorphic there and on the buffered meridian collar. Apply (17) on that neighborhood, then Cauchy's formula in the coordinates and in \(u=N\mu\). For every fixed multi-index \(\alpha\) and integer \(k\ge0\), \[ \sup_{\substack{(z,w)\in\mathcal K\|N\mu|\le\eta}} \left(|\partial_{z,w}^{\alpha}\partial_\mu^k\mathcal E_{ eta,p}| +|\partial_{z,w}^{\alpha}\partial_\mu^k\mathcal F_{ eta,p}|ight) \le C_{\alpha,k,\mathcal K,\eta,\eta'} (N+1)^{B+k+1}\gamma^d. 	ag{22} \] Thus these actual composed currents and all the stated jets are exponentially small. The \(N^k\) cost is the true meridian cost \(\partial_\mu=N\partial_u\); all moving crossing frames are differentiated. No derivative of a root-only expression is substituted. The raw word in (7) retains the scalar \(\kappa(M)^\omega\). For it the exact current is \(\kappa^\omega\) times (15), and every derivative retains the full product rule. For the standard zero-framed word, H(16) gives \[ \alpha=\kappa x^{-d},\qquad \overline W_ eta=\alpha^{-\omega}W_ eta =x^{d\omega}\widehat W_ eta. 	ag{23} \] The last scalar is bounded by \(e^{|\omega|\eta'}\) on the collar; its derivative of order \(j\) is \((d\omega)^j x^{d\omega}\). Hence (22) holds for the actual zero-framed composed current as well. Prescribed further scalar lines remain multiplied in their original positions; the same exponential conclusion for them needs their stated buffered subexponential bounds, not a scalar reset. Fixed integer Cartan powers inserted beside the current also obey (17),(22). They multiply its finitely many arrow coefficients by unit \(Q\)-phases and fixed Laurent powers of \(M\). This includes the spectator Cartans in the total coproduct currents below. ## 5. Two-sided transport of every internal threshold A coarser estimate covers a current at an arbitrary internal seam, with actual finite word factors on both sides. Let \(A(M),B(M)\) be fixed products of stripped crossings and the degree projectors (14), and let \(c\) be their total number of crossings. Put \[ C_E=[E_\Sigma,\Pi_0],\qquad C_F=[F_\Sigma,\Pi_0], \qquad \mathcal J_E= rac{K_{A C_E B}}{I_N},\quad \mathcal J_F= rac{K_{A C_F B}}{I_N}. 	ag{24} \] The threshold pair may be any adjacent pair. Let \[ s=\max_j|z_j|,\quad t=\max_j|w_j|,\quad 	au=st, \qquad C_m= rac{m^m}{(m-1)^{m-1}},\qquad \Omega_{m,c}(	au)= rac{3^c C_m	au}{(1-	au)^m}. 	ag{25} \] For \(0\le	au<1/(m-1)\), the following actual kernel bounds hold on the buffered meridian collar: \[ |\mathcal J_E|\le C(N+1)^{B_0}(m-1)t\,\Omega_{m,c}(	au)^d, \qquad |\mathcal J_F|\le C(N+1)^{B_0}s\,\Omega_{m,c}(	au)^d. 	ag{26} \] Fixed compact sets of phase marks \(\Pi_0+\zeta\Pi_1\) may also replace any of the inserted projectors; only the constant changes. These marks need not intertwine the total arrows. To prove (26), first set both weights in (5) equal to one. Each root crossing has maximum input-column sum at most \(3^d\). Equation (11) preserves this up to a collar-uniform polynomial factor. Every inserted degree projector has column norm at most one. The total-current matrices \(C_E,C_F\) have bounded column norm on the collar, since (1) and the fixed coproduct have bounded arrow coefficients. Therefore \[ \|A C_E B\|_1+\|A C_F B\|_1 \le C(N+1)^{B_0}3^{cd}. 	ag{27} \] Here \(\|\cdot\|_1\) is the maximum absolute input-column sum, not a coherent-kernel norm. Each crossing and each projector preserves the global integer degree \(J_{m all}=\sum_jJ_j\). A nonzero \(C_E\) input has pair degree \(N=d+1\), hence global degree at least \(d+1\), and its output degree is one lower. A nonzero \(C_F\) input has pair degree \(d\), and its output degree is one higher. These support statements remain true with \(B\) before the current and \(A\) after it. For \(s,t>0\), (27) consequently bounds the absolute coherent numerators by \[  egin{split} C(N+1)^{B_0}3^{cd}s^{-1} \sum_{J\ge d+1} inom{md}{J}	au^J, \qquad C(N+1)^{B_0}3^{cd}s \sum_{J\ge d} inom{md}{J}	au^J, \end{split} 	ag{28} \] respectively. The coefficient \( inom{md}{J}\) is the exact Vandermonde sum of all input binomial weights at total degree \(J\). No independence of the intervening occupations is assumed. For \(R>1\), the degree tail beginning at \(l\) is at most \(R^{-l}(1+R	au)^{md}\). Choose \(R=((m-1)	au)^{-1}\). The two tails in (28) are at most \((m-1)	au(C_m	au)^d\) and \((C_m	au)^d\). Finally \(|I_N|\ge(1-	au)^{md}\). Substitution proves (26), including the factor \(s^{-1}	au=t\) in its first bound. At \(	au=0\), both actual kernels vanish by the stated total degree support, and (26) follows by continuity. The domain \(\Omega_{m,c}(	au)<1\), within the preceding \(	au\)-range, contains a nonempty polydisc about the origin and fixed positive points in it. On every compact subset, a fixed complex buffer gives \(\Omega_{m,c}\le\gamma<1\). The same holomorphy and Cauchy argument as in (22) proves exponential decay of all fixed mixed coherent and true meridian jets of (24), with only polynomial \(N\)-cost. The scalar restoration (23) applies unchanged. This result estimates literal two-sided compositions; it makes no assertion about arbitrary matrices of uncontrolled degree support or column norm. ## 6. The exact Ward row and the remaining source scope For \(Z_{pr}=\Pi_0+\zeta\Pi_1\), C's literal degree identities are \[ [E_{pr},Z_{pr}]=(\zeta-1)E_{pr}\mathbf1_{J_{pr}=N},\qquad [F_{pr},Z_{pr}]=(1-\zeta)F_{pr}\mathbf1_{J_{pr}=d}. 	ag{29} \] Thus (17),(22) estimate the corresponding actual rows \(\widehat W_ eta[E_{pr},Z_{pr}]\) and \(\widehat W_ eta[F_{pr},Z_{pr}]\), uniformly for \(\zeta\) in a fixed compact set. With the ordered total coproducts of F(8), \[ [E_\Sigma,Z_{pr}]=[E_{pr},Z_{pr}]\prod_{j>r}K_j, \qquad [F_\Sigma,Z_{pr}]=\left(\prod_{j<p}K_j^{-1}ight) [F_{pr},Z_{pr}]. 	ag{30} \] Terms outside the pair commute with its degree projector; within the pair, the indicated Cartan factors give (30) directly. For the actual braid intertwiners these are also the full rows \([E_\Sigma,W_ eta Z_{pr}]=W_ eta[E_\Sigma,Z_{pr}]\) and the analogous \(F_\Sigma\) row, with their original scalar. For completeness, this intertwining can be checked in the finite sum (2). Let \(\Theta=\sum_n c_nE_1^nF_2^n\) denote its positive Euler factor. The arrows (1) give \[ [E,F^{n+1}]=-q^{-1}Q^{-n}(1-Q^{n+1})F^n(K-Q^nK^{-1}). 	ag{31} \] Together with \(c_{n+1}/c_n=-q^{2n+1}/(1-Q^{n+1})\), this cancels consecutive coefficients of \(E_1^{n+1}F_2^n\) and proves \[ \Theta(E_1K_2+E_2)=(E_1K_2^{-1}+E_2)\Theta, \qquad \Theta(F_1+K_1^{-1}F_2)=(F_1+K_1F_2)\Theta. 	ag{32} \] The second identity follows by the same adjacent-transfer comparison. Conjugating the right-hand expressions by \(D\) and then flipping the heads gives the original coproduct. At the top of the finite comparison the residual has \(E_1^N\) or \(F_2^N\), which is zero; the lower comparison uses the actual bottom-zero arrow. This proves the positive intertwining, and its actual inverse proves the negative one. No cyclic endpoint is used in this Ward interpretation. In particular a carry-sector word \(W_{ eta,\mathbf b}=(R_{i_c}^{\sigma_c}\Pi_{i_c,b_c}) \cdots(R_{i_1}^{\sigma_1}\Pi_{i_1,b_1})\) has a total Ward commutator equal to the finite Leibniz sum over its projector slots. Each summand has the form in (24), with exactly \(c\) crossings between its two sides and with the other projectors retained. After stripping the common scalar, (26) and its jet bounds estimate every such internal current and their sum, uniformly over the finite sector set. The same holds after zero-framing restoration (23); the raw scalar retains its displayed product rule. This does not use sectorwise scalar-cut identities. The usual donor-Gaussian column estimate already appears in ordinary-color coefficient bounds. The conclusion here is its specific finite composition with a threshold current in the actual balanced meridian family, giving (16)--(22) and the two-sided bounds (24)--(28) on explicit nonempty complex coherent domains. The original Newton/Fourier identities for one or two negative crossings and the q-Hahn local amplitudes concern different kernels; none is used as a proof premise here. The bound is on the original composed kernel divided by its stated identity kernel. It is not relative to a possibly vanishing kernel of \(W_ eta\), and it is not an exponentially small operator norm. The two-sided theorem covers actual fixed word/projector products, including every internal sector current. A separate contracted boundary state cannot be renamed as a free binomial column without estimating its actual adapter. Applying these bounds to the closing source still requires a contour and bounds on its remaining density and boundary currents. No geometric membership of these domains, cycle coefficient, or noncancellation of the original closed scalar is inferred. ## Complete proof directs * C: `notes/research_carry_projector_ward_decay.md` (236 lines), SHA256 `6aec272af36618cb3f13ab40b2fa539a6c5d8f5ad40d8688206f7a3f3a806829`. * F: `notes/research_actual_meridian_source_frames.md` (506 lines), SHA256 `6f58fba195ba5e8208e1d5180a1d684b933f9f5d50eb28efc56609580fe29976`. * H: `notes/research_actual_meridian_hankel_transport.md` (271 lines), SHA256 `e50f4257e3464863167d8a04c060753d937921d27c551d8ee18f882add1111e9`. All complete directs were whole-read nontruncated in this active sequence. The proof uses only written finite calculations and text/hash operations. Frozen and public files were not edited.

title: Actual braid words, the normal cocycle, and the original source
text:
# Actual braid words, the normal cocycle, and the original source Private written proof, 19 November 2026. Author-final for independent review. The first normal layer of the actual root braid algebra has an explicit generator transport. In a common frame that makes the remaining lowering operator constant, every internal crossing has zero quotient-normal class. The boundary crossing has a finite formula from its actual capped prefix coefficients. The original closing of any word is then a sum of Levi traces, diagonal normal terms, and specified quadratic couplings of off-diagonal blocks. This is a finite source theorem. It does not replace the closing by a positive norm or prove a geometric coefficient is nonzero. The complete directs are F, the reciprocal flag classification; C, the actual prefix Ward equations; and R, the actual reduced braid representation and its source. All additional normal, frame, generator, and word calculations are proved below. ## 1. The actual root algebra and its normal derivation Fix \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\), and \(m=r+1\ge2\). Keep the quantum root fixed and put \(M=e^\mu\), \(x=-M/q\). Write \(f_n=\prod_{j=1}^n(1-Q^j)\), \(f_0=1\), and \({t rack n}_Q=f_t/(f_nf_{t-n})\) for \(0\le n\le t<N\). On the remaining tensor \(U\), write \[ K(M)=M^rK_0,\quad K_0^N=\varepsilon I,\quad \varepsilon=(-1)^{(N+1)r},\qquad \mathcal A=\operatorname{End}_{K_0}(U). 	ag{1} \] For a literal braid word \( eta\), including its crossing scalars, let \[ ho_\mu( eta)=p_0S_m(M)^{-1}W_ eta(M)i_0. 	ag{2} \] R proves that this is an actual holomorphic group representation into \(\mathcal A^	imes\). All indices stay in \(0,\ldots,d\). F identifies the entire actual root intertwiner algebra with \[ \mathcal T=V\oplus(\mathcal A/V),\qquad (b,[c])(b',[c'])=(bb',[bc'+cb']), 	ag{3} \] where \(V\) is the root prefix image. The coordinates of a root intertwiner lifted analytically to \(W(\mu)\) are the constant coefficient and the first coefficient modulo \(V\) of its actual reduced family. They do not depend on the lift: the difference of two lifts is \(\mu T(\mu)\), whose reduced first coefficient lies in \(V\). Write these coordinates as \(\pi(W)\) and \(
u(W)\). Thus the exact normal map satisfies \[ 
u(WZ)=\pi(W)
u(Z)+
u(W)\pi(Z). 	ag{4} \] This is a derivation relative to the root reduction, not a derivation determined by its value \(\pi(W)\) alone. For actual braid words put \(b_ eta=ho_0( eta)\) and \[ c_ eta=[ho'_0( eta)b_ eta^{-1}]\in\mathcal A/V. 	ag{5} \] Since \(b_ eta^{\pm1}\in V\), conjugation acts on this quotient. The ordinary product rule gives \[  oxed{\quad c_{ eta\gamma}=c_ eta+\operatorname{Ad}(b_ eta)c_\gamma, \qquad c_{ eta^{-1}}=-\operatorname{Ad}(b_ eta^{-1})c_ eta. \quad}	ag{6} \] It is a cocycle on the actual root braid operators, or equivalently on braid words through their full root operators. It need not descend to the reduced root matrix \(b_ eta\) alone. The lost square-zero layer in (3) is precisely the datum that would be discarded by that stronger assertion. ## 2. A common moving frame, with every connection term There is an analytic \(K_0\)-preserving matrix \(G(\mu)\), with \(G(0)=I\), such that \[ G(\mu)^{-1}E_r(M)G(\mu)=E_r(1)=:E. 	ag{7} \] Here is a finite construction. Split the first remaining head from the rest. The columns \(E_r(M)^a(w_d\otimes v)\), \(0\le a\le d\), in a fixed remaining occupation basis \(v\), form a matrix \(T(M)\). Its least first-head row is \(d-a\), with invertible coefficient \((e_d\cdots e_{d-a+1})K_{m rest}^a\), where \(e_j=MQ^{-j}-M^{-1}\). This gives an analytic triangular basis near \(M=1\). For one remaining head use the same construction with empty rest. Finite root quantum-binomial expansion and the forced head endpoints give \(E_r(M)^N=0\). Thus \(T(M)\) makes \(E_r(M)\) the same length-\(N\) Jordan shift for every \(M\). Take \(G(M)=T(M)T(1)^{-1}\). Every column has a fixed \(K_0\) weight, so \([G,K_0]=0\), proving (7) with the stated normalization. Set \[ \widehatho_\mu( eta)=G^{-1}ho_\mu( eta)G, \qquad \Gamma=G'(0),\qquad h_ eta=\widehatho'_0( eta) =ho'_0( eta)+[b_ eta,\Gamma]. 	ag{8} \] The quotient-normal class is therefore changed by the explicit inner derivation \([b_ eta,\Gamma] mod V\). Its logarithmic version changes by the coboundary \[ \widehat c_ eta=c_ eta+ [\operatorname{Ad}(b_ eta)\Gamma-\Gamma]. 	ag{9} \] No meridian derivative of the frame has been suppressed. The flattened quotient-normal class is independent of the choice of frame satisfying (7) and \(G(0)=I\). Indeed two such frames differ by a matrix commuting with \(E\) and \(K_0\); its derivative at zero commutes with both arrows in F's reciprocal complexes. F's classification puts that derivative in \(V\), so the change in (9) is zero in \(\mathcal A/V\). The source is invariant under this moving frame for the entire meridian germ. R's exact source matrix is central in \(\mathcal A\): with \(D_N(z)=(z^N-z^{-N})/(z-z^{-1})\), \[ D_\mu= rac{D_N(M)}{D_N(MK(M))},\qquad \Phi_0(W_ eta(M))=\operatorname{Tr}(D_\muho_\mu( eta)) =\operatorname{Tr}(D_\mu\widehatho_\mu( eta)). 	ag{10} \] This equality is made before taking a finite part. In particular the polar-source trace of the commutator in (8) is exactly zero, not an estimate of a pointwise coherent kernel. For an internal original generator \(\sigma_i^{\pm1}\), \(i\ge2\), R identifies its reduced matrix with the physical crossing on the remaining heads. It commutes with \(E_r(M)\) for all \(M\). Consequently its flattened matrix commutes with \(E\) and \(K_0\) for all \(\mu\). F then puts it in the fixed algebra \(V\) throughout the germ, so \[ [h_{\sigma_i^{\pm1}}]=0\quad\hbox{in }\mathcal A/V, \qquad i\ge2. 	ag{11} \] This statement concerns internal generators only. The initialized boundary generator has an explicit normal adapter below. ## 3. The whole-meridian boundary coefficients Write C's full prefix expansion of an actual word as \[ S_m^{-1}W_ eta S_m=\sum_{n=0}^dF_1^n\otimes B_n^ eta, \qquad B_0^ eta=ho_\mu( eta). 	ag{12} \] Let \(L_2\) be the literal lowering shift on the first remaining head, with its zero bottom arrow. The positive first crossing has the exact whole-meridian identity \[  oxed{\qquad B_n^{\sigma_1}(M)= rac{x^{-n}}{f_n} ho_\mu(\sigma_1)L_2^n, \qquad 0\le n\le d. \qquad}	ag{13} \] To verify it, R's zero-transfer input row is \(R_1(w_0\otimes w_b\otimes v)=\kappa(M)x^{-b} w_b\otimes w_0\otimes v\). Put \(c_j=(-1)^jQ^{j(j-1)/2}\). The term of \(S_m^{-1}\) returning this first-head occupation to \(n\) has \(j=b-n\). Therefore, for \(b\ge n\), \[ B_n^{\sigma_1}(w_b\otimes v) = rac{\kappa c_{b-n}x^{-2b+n}}{f_nf_{b-n}} F_r^{b-n}(w_0\otimes v). 	ag{14} \] It is zero for \(b<n\). R's formula for \(ho(\sigma_1)\) applied to \(L_2^n(w_b\otimes v)\) is precisely (14), proving (13), including \(\kappa\), every physical cap, and every fixed- quantum meridian derivative. In particular no upper transfer sum or root-only identity has been differentiated. ## 4. Division-free normal arrow defects Fix a nonself pair \(\{\chi,\chi^{-1}\}\), and choose the unique \(1\le s<N\) with \(Q^s=\chi^2\). Set \[ A=E^s:U_{\chi^{-1}}	o U_\chi, B=E^{N-s}:U_\chi	o U_{\chi^{-1}}. 	ag{15} \] These are F's actual exact-complex arrows. In the common frame (7) they remain constant throughout the meridian germ. The actual weights are \(M^r\chi\) and \(M^r\chi^{-1}\); they need not be reciprocal away from zero. For a fixed root weight \(\lambda_0\), the total prefix weight \(x(M)M^r\lambda_0\) has tail weight \(M^rQ^n\lambda_0\) in first-head row \(n\). Put \(\widehat E'=(I\otimes G^{-1})S_m^{-1}E_\Sigma S_m(I\otimes G)\). C's transformed lowering row gives, for \(0\le n\le t<N\), \[ p_0(\widehat E')^t i_n =c_{t,n}(\lambda_0;\mu)E^{t-n},\quad c_{t,n}=Q^{n(n-1)/2}{t rack n}_Q \prod_{j=t}^{t+n-1} (M^m\lambda_0-M^{-m}Q^{-j}\lambda_0^{-1}). 	ag{16} \] It is zero for \(n>t\), and \(c_{t,0}=1\). The same first-step recurrence as in F proves (16): a tail step replaces \(\lambda_0\) by \(Q\lambda_0\), while a first-head lowering step contributes \(M^m\lambda_0-M^{-m}Q^{-n}\lambda_0^{-1}\). The two finite Gaussian Pascal identities complete the induction. Only indices below \(N\) occur. If \(\lambda_0^2=Q^{-t}\), the first factor of every nonempty product in (16) vanishes at zero. Its derivative is \(2m\lambda_0\). The remaining factors are \(\lambda_0(1-Q^{-j})\), \(1\le j<n\), so exactly \[  oxed{\qquad \partial_\mu c_{t,n}|_0 =2m(-1)^{n-1}\lambda_0^n{t rack n}_Q f_{n-1} =:\omega_{t,n}(\lambda_0),\qquad 1\le n\le t. \qquad}	ag{17} \] The phase \(Q^{n(n-1)/2}\) cancels the negative-power product; there is no missing Cartan or factorial scalar. Put \(\widehat B_n^ eta=G^{-1}B_n^ eta G\). Commuting the whole word with \(\widehat E'\), and retaining all columns in (16), gives \[ \widehatho_{\mu,Q^t\lambda_0}( eta)E^t -E^t\widehatho_{\mu,\lambda_0}( eta) =\sum_{n=1}^t f_nc_{t,n}E^{t-n} \widehat B_n^ eta|_{U_{\lambda_0}}. 	ag{18} \] At resonance, differentiating has no derivative of the right-hand matrix factors: each scalar \(c_{t,n}(0)\) is zero. Also \(G(0)=I\). Thus the actual normal defect is \[  oxed{\qquad \mathfrak D_t^ eta :=h_{ eta,Q^t\lambda_0}E^t-E^th_{ eta,\lambda_0} =\sum_{n=1}^t f_n\omega_{t,n}(\lambda_0) E^{t-n}B_n^ eta(0). \qquad}	ag{19} \] Use \((\lambda_0,t)=(\chi^{-1},s)\) for \(\mathfrak D_A\), and \((\chi,N-s)\) for \(\mathfrak D_B\). For the positive boundary generator (13) makes (19) completely explicit: \[ \mathfrak D_t^{\sigma_1} =\sum_{n=1}^t\omega_{t,n}(\lambda_0)x_0^{-n} E^{t-n}b_{\sigma_1}L_2^n, \qquad x_0=-q^{-1}. 	ag{20} \] All operators in (20) are the original root matrices. Displaying them in flag bases conjugates every factor by those same fixed bases; it does not replace \(L_2\) by a newly normalized shift. Let \(X_ eta=b_ eta|_{U_\chi}\), \(Y_ eta=b_ eta|_{U_{\chi^{-1}}}\). The product rule and the root arrow intertwinings give \[ \mathfrak D_A^{ eta\gamma} =X_ eta\mathfrak D_A^\gamma+ \mathfrak D_A^ eta Y_\gamma, \qquad \mathfrak D_A^{ eta^{-1}} =-X_ eta^{-1}\mathfrak D_A^ eta Y_ eta^{-1}. 	ag{21} \] The reverse arrow has the same formulas with \(X,Y\) interchanged. This supplies the negative boundary generator with the actual inverse and its scalar; no inverse-crossing approximation is used. ## 5. The normal class in the physical flag blocks Choose F's fixed complements, so the pair spaces have dimensions \((k,l)\) and \((l,k)\), and the root word has the form \[ X_ eta= egin{pmatrix}a_ eta&b_ eta^{m off}\0&d_ eta\end{pmatrix}, \qquad Y_ eta= egin{pmatrix}d_ eta&f_ eta\0&a_ eta\end{pmatrix}. 	ag{22} \] The complements identify \(A\) and \(B\) with their identity arrows as in F. Write the flattened first normal on the pair as \((C_ eta,D_ eta)\), and define \[ \alpha_ eta=C_{11}-D_{22},\quad \delta_ eta=C_{22}-D_{11},\quad p_ eta=C_{21},\quad q_ eta=D_{21}. 	ag{23} \] These are exactly its quotient class in \(\mathcal A/V\). Direct multiplication by the two arrows gives \[ \mathfrak D_A^ eta=  egin{pmatrix}-q_ eta&\alpha_ eta\0&p_ eta\end{pmatrix}, \qquad \mathfrak D_B^ eta=  egin{pmatrix}-p_ eta&-\delta_ eta\0&q_ eta\end{pmatrix}. 	ag{24} \] Consequently (19)--(21) determine the entire actual quotient-normal class, not just its closing trace. Internal generators have all four blocks in (23) equal to zero, by (11). The common crossing scalar is still included in every root matrix in (20),(22). A logarithmic derivative of a scalar multiple of a generator adds a scalar multiple of \(b_ eta\), which lies in \(V\), so it has zero quotient-normal class. This observation does not remove the scalar's root value. Nor does it remove its derivative when differentiating the whole closed source rather than computing its root value. ## 6. The exact closing of an arbitrary signed word Write the literal word as \( eta=g_L\cdots g_1\), with each letter an actual signed generator. Use (22),(23) for each letter, and write its diagonal blocks as \(a_i,d_i\) and off-diagonal blocks as \(b_i^{m off},f_i\). For each \(i\), let \[ \gamma_i=g_{i-1}\cdots g_1g_L\cdots g_{i+1}. 	ag{25} \] Its two root blocks are denoted by \[ X_{\gamma_i}= egin{pmatrix}A_i&B_i\0&D_i^{m c}\end{pmatrix}, \qquad Y_{\gamma_i}= egin{pmatrix}D_i^{m c}&F_i\0&A_i\end{pmatrix}. 	ag{26} \] An empty product is the identity. Put \(a_\chi=(\chi-\chi^{-1})/(2\varepsilon m)\). Then the original source contribution of this whole physical pair is \[  oxed{ egin{aligned} \Phi_{\mathfrak o}(W_ eta(1))={}&  rac{\chi+\chi^{-1}}{\varepsilon} \left[\operatorname{Tr}(a_L\cdots a_1) +\operatorname{Tr}(d_L\cdots d_1)ight]\ &+a_\chi\sum_{i=1}^L \left[\operatorname{Tr}(\alpha_iA_i) +\operatorname{Tr}(\delta_iD_i^{m c}) +\operatorname{Tr}(p_iB_i)-\operatorname{Tr}(q_iF_i)ight]. \end{aligned}}	ag{27} \] Every trace is on its indicated rectangular product's square space. To prove (27), the actual first derivative of the matrix product is a sum with one \((C_i,D_i)\) insertion. Cyclicity of each ordinary block trace changes its complementary factors to (25). Expanding \(\operatorname{Tr}(C_iX_{\gamma_i}-D_iY_{\gamma_i})\) gives exactly its four displayed terms. F's original source formula then gives (27), including \(a_\chi\) and the Levi coefficient. Each \(B_i,F_i\) in (26) is a sum with exactly one root off-diagonal letter. For an ordered upper-triangular product this follows by choosing the unique step from its lower block to its upper block. Thus the last two terms in (27) are the actual quadratic couplings between a root off-diagonal and a normal off-diagonal. Trace removes either one in isolation; it does not remove their products. No adjoint, complex conjugation, or norm has replaced these bilinear contractions. For a self weight \(\chi=\pm1\), the source contribution is \(\chi\operatorname{Tr}(b_ eta|_{U_\chi})/\varepsilon\), counted once. Summing these and (27) over all inversion orbits gives the entire original pointed source. Separately prescribed exterior scalar lines multiply that full result with their actual values. They retain their product-rule derivatives on the meridian germ. Equation (27) computes the original root value from the reduced first normal. For a fixed full root operator, the full reduced first derivative is lift-dependent, although its quotient class is not. A derivative of the original closed source generally also needs the reduced second coefficient against the simple pole in (10); no such extra jet is discarded or supplied by the root formula (27). ## 7. One boundary occurrence and the exact remaining duty Suppose a word has a single \(\sigma_1^{\epsilon}\), \(\epsilon=\pm1\), and all other letters are internal. R's cyclic source identity permits rotating it to \(\sigma_1^{\epsilon}\eta\), with \(\eta\) internal. The same cyclicity holds in each paired block since \(D_\mu\) is a scalar there on each weight. By (11), only the boundary letter remains in the normal sum of (27). If the internal root blocks are \(a_\eta,d_\eta,b_\eta^{m off},f_\eta\), that normal term is \[ a_\chi\left[ \operatorname{Tr}(\alpha_\epsilon a_\eta) +\operatorname{Tr}(\delta_\epsilon d_\eta) +\operatorname{Tr}(p_\epsilon b_\eta^{m off}) -\operatorname{Tr}(q_\epsilon f_\eta)ight]. 	ag{28} \] The boundary covector is specified by the finite positive formula (20),(24) or the exact inverse law (21). All extensive internal spectators remain in the actual root word in (28). For the positive left stabilization this is consistent with an independent whole-meridian source contraction. If \(W_\eta=I\otimes W_{m old}\), R's zero-transfer row and the highest cut force the new first and old first occupations both to zero. The retained pivotal factor there is \(x^{1-N}\). Hence \[ \Phi_0(R_1(I\otimes W_{m old})) =\kappa(M)x^{1-N}\Phi_0(W_{m old}). 	ag{29} \] The actual positive zero-framing compensation cancels this same scalar, as in R. Equation (29) retains its true meridian derivative; it is not a new nonzero-source theorem. The result completes the finite normal transport of actual signed words and their prescribed closing. It reduces a one-boundary presentation to an explicit boundary covector against an actual internal root representation, rather than an unspecified normal matrix. It supplies no analytic lower bound for that contraction, no positive Levi metric, and no selected geometric coefficient. The remaining coefficient and relative-cycle estimates cannot be deduced from radical nilpotence or invertibility of the word. ## Complete direct-source pins * F: notes/research_reciprocal_chain_flags_and_root_radical.md, 428 lines, SHA256 7589bb0f796a874608b9e558aac1f78699884f0003da4a73ba52778c1edba66e. * C: notes/research_prefix_commutant_and_pointed_normal_functional.md, 549 lines, SHA256 b4fb801a1482316aebb4799f1d0b80d5b43ced39138d903c04cfde811ca166b0. * R: notes/research_actual_reduced_braid_source.md, 330 lines, SHA256 9a472ef27b08305a519ff1f24b6d2b909e63a0acbdc49b3a29e001c52a2f2243.
