title: Exact reduction fibers and the remaining core theorem
text:
# Exact reduction fibers and the remaining core theorem Research note, 2 November 2026. The exceptions in this note are original integer filling assignments. Neither replacing those assignments by knot types nor discarding redundant coordinates is part of the argument. The frozen manuscripts are unchanged. The existing reductions give more than a warning about infinite fibers: on each fixed structural branch, linear algebra decides whether a nonempty fiber is a singleton or is infinite. In the latter case it contains a family on which every genuinely varying original coordinate tends to infinity. Thus the issue cannot be avoided by requiring all remaining original coefficients to be long. ## 1. The data of a reduction branch Let \(p=(p_1,\ldots,p_d)\in\mathbb Z^d\) be the original surgery coefficients. A retained half-twist pattern has already been fixed, so the crossing powers are \(n_i=\eta_i-2p_i\), with \(\eta_i\in\{-1,0,1\}\) fixed. There is no additional parity restriction on \(p\). Consider one branch of an exact tangle reduction. Suppose its parameter set has the form \[ \Omega=\{p\in\mathbb Z^d: Ap=a,\quad \ell_j(p)
e c_j\quad(1\le j\le q)\}, 	ag{1} \] where all matrices, vectors, and linear forms have rational coefficients. The reduced parameters are \[ f(p)=Bp+b. 	ag{2} \] The reduction must identify the actual closed knot, including the zero-framing convention for the invariant. An equality between finite quantum contractions alone is insufficient for this purpose. These hypotheses apply to the zero-aware all-root reduction in [the Conway reductions paper](../papers/conway-reductions/closures.tex). Its branch is chosen by the original parities and the zero or nonzero values of finitely many subset sums. Its surviving parameters are sums over disjoint original label blocks. Substituting \(n_i=\eta_i-2p_i\) gives precisely affine equations and inequalities of the form (1), and the surviving weights give (2). Fixed numerical values, including the values needed to make an elementary factor an unknot, can be added to \(Ap=a\). Finite alternatives such as a terminal exponent \(1\) or \(-1\) should first be split into separate branches. The same description applies to a prescribed finite sequence of the proved degree-two \(0,\pm1\) moves: a \(\pm1\) move gives affine shifts, and a zero move gives a sum. This statement does not assert a classification of all partially filled exteriors. ## 2. A nonempty fiber is either a singleton or infinite Fix a reduced assignment \(y\), and suppose \(\Omega_y=\{p\in\Omega:f(p)=y\}\) is nonempty. Put \[ H= egin{pmatrix}A\B\end{pmatrix}. 	ag{3} \] **Proposition 1.** If \(H\) has column rank \(d\), then \(\Omega_y\) consists of one point. If its rank is smaller than \(d\), then \(\Omega_y\) is infinite. More precisely, for any \(p_0\in\Omega_y\) there is a nonzero \(v\in\mathbb Z^d\) such that \[ p_0+kv\in\Omega_y \quad\hbox{for every integer \(k\) outside a finite set}. 	ag{4} \] **Proof.** The difference of two points of the fiber lies in \(\ker_{\mathbb Q}H\). Full column rank therefore gives uniqueness. Otherwise this rational kernel contains a nonzero integral vector \(v\). Every \(p_0+kv\) satisfies all equations defining the fiber. If \(\ell_j(v)=0\), its \(j\)-th nonvanishing test remains true because it was true at \(p_0\). If \(\ell_j(v)
e0\), the equality \(\ell_j(p_0+kv)=c_j\) holds for at most one integer \(k\). There are finitely many tests, so only finitely many integers are excluded. Since \(v
e0\), the other points are distinct. \(\square\) Thus the nonzero subset-sum tests do not cut an affine fiber down to a nonempty finite set. They remove finitely many points from any suitable line. This conclusion does not apply without further work to a different parameter domain that imposes one-sided sign conditions or arbitrary nonlinear inequalities. The present target allows signed coefficients of unrelated magnitudes. There is a useful stronger choice of direction. Let \[ I=\{i:v_i=0	ext{ for every }v\in\ker_{\mathbb Q}H\}, \qquad J=\{1,\ldots,d\}\setminus I. 	ag{5} \] Every coordinate in \(I\) is constant on the affine fiber. **Proposition 2.** If \(\Omega_y\) is infinite, the vector \(v\) in (4) can be chosen so that \(v_j
e0\) for every \(j\in J\). Consequently \(p_i=p_{0,i}\) for \(i\in I\), while \(\lvert p_jvert\longrightarrow\infty\) for every \(j\in J\), along the family (4) as \(\lvert kvert\longrightarrow\infty\). **Proof.** For each \(j\in J\), the equation \(v_j=0\) defines a proper linear subspace of \(\ker_{\mathbb Q}H\). A vector space over the infinite field \(\mathbb Q\) is not a finite union of proper linear subspaces. One direct verification is to choose a rational basis \(w_1,\ldots,w_r\) and evaluate \(w_1+t w_2+\cdots+t^{r-1}w_r\): each nonzero coordinate form is a nonzero polynomial, so it vanishes at only finitely many rational \(t\). Choose another \(t\), clear denominators, and use Proposition 1. \(\square\) The original coefficients need not tend to infinity with the same sign. For a zero merger, the familiar direction is \((1,-1)\). Allowing independent signed long fillings is exactly what makes these directions relevant. ## 3. What can be pulled back from a cofinite theorem Suppose an exact reduction identifies the knot at \(p\in\Omega\) with the knot at \(f(p)\). Let \(E\) be a finite collection of reduced assignments for which the volume identity remains unresolved. Outside \(f^{-1}(E)\) the reduced theorem transfers to the original family. For a fixed branch (1), Proposition 1 gives the complete fiber test: * If \(H\) has full column rank, at most \(\lvert Evert\) original assignments remain unresolved. * If \(H\) has deficient rank, every nonempty fiber over an element of \(E\) is infinite. To prove a cofinite conclusion on this branch, each hyperbolic knot represented by such an exceptional fiber must satisfy the volume identity. The second assertion is a requirement for the proof, not a claim that any of these knots fails the conjecture. If one did fail, every assignment in its fiber would be a counterexample. For a finite collection of structural branches, apply this test to each branch separately. All equations accumulated earlier in the reduction must remain in \(A\). Keeping only the final effective coordinates would lose exactly the information being tested. There is also a direct consequence for a proposed long-remainder theorem. Suppose that, for every fixed partial assignment of the original template, all sufficiently long remaining original coefficients giving hyperbolic knots satisfy the volume identity. If a hyperbolic reduced knot has an infinite fiber in (1), fix the coordinates in \(I\) from (5) and apply that theorem along (4). Eventually all coordinates in \(J\) satisfy its threshold, and the knot is the same reduced knot at every point. The long-remainder theorem therefore proves the volume identity for that particular core. It cannot merely leave the core among finitely many reduced exceptions. ## 4. The four-vertex example and the matrix test Use the original crossing \(R\), physical quarter-turn \(T\), and cylindrical closure \(C\). On the four-vertex path write \[ K_4(a,v,b,c)=C igl(R^aT(R^vT(R^bT(R^c))) igr). 	ag{6} \] The proved marked zero move gives \[ K_4(a,0,b,c)\simeq K_2(a+b,c). 	ag{7} \] For clarity, temporarily use the crossing powers as coordinates in one fixed parity class. Fixing the reduced pair \((s,c_0)\) imposes \[ v=0,\qquad a+b=s,\qquad c=c_0. 	ag{8} \] The matrix of these three equations in four variables has kernel spanned by \((1,0,-1,0)\). On the fixed parity lattice, take twice this vector. Hence every hyperbolic \(K_2(s,c_0)\) has infinitely many preimages of one fixed original parity pattern, with \(a,b\) both long and of opposite signs. The exact topology behind (7), including the reversal under \(T^2\), is proved in [the scope audit](research_finite_exception_scope_audit.md#2-an-infinite-fiber-on-a-four-vertex-path). The rank calculation adds no topological assumption. Thus a finite reduced exceptional list for two-circle knots is not enough to prove the cofinite statement for this four-circle template. Every hyperbolic knot on that list must be settled before its entire zero-merger fiber is covered. ## 5. A bounded-size form of the padding implication The preceding obstruction is not restricted to paths. The existing strict-padding argument has the following quantitative form. The grammar is the enlarged literal strict class of [the asymptotics manuscript](../papers/conway-asymptotics/main.tex), which permits an elementary closing child; the statement does not assert membership in its older completed-root subfamily. **Proposition 3.** Let \(K=C(Q)\) be a hyperbolic knot represented by a literal strict Conway expression with \(m\) labelled leaves, whose integer powers are all fixed. There is a literal strict template with \(m+2\) labelled leaves and one fixed parity pattern having infinitely many assignments representing \(K\). Consequently, a cofinite assignment theorem for every strict template with at most \(m+2\) leaves proves the volume identity for every such hyperbolic \(m\)-leaf core, without exceptions. **Proof.** Put \(h(b)=T(R^b)\) and form \[ E(a,b)=C igl(h(b)[R^aT(Q)] igr). 	ag{9} \] This uses the permitted operations because \(R^a=T^3h(a)\). Reopening \(Q\) turns its former closing product into a retained product. Each allowed closing pair \(AA,AL,AH,LH\), in either order, also has a nonempty open product, of type \(A,A,H,H\), respectively, by the [literal type table](../papers/newton-calculus/supports.tex). Its other products remain allowed. Hence \(Q\), now used as an open tangle, has type \(A\) or \(H\). A new strict state may be chosen; the old closed optimizer is not being reused at its former root. Thus \(T(Q)\) has type \(A\) or \(L\), while \(R^a\) has type \(H\). Their product has type \(H\), and the outer closing pair has types \(L,H\), which is allowed. Strictness is a property of this formal expression and does not require \(b
e0\). Let \(D\) denote cap closure and \(	au=T^2\) the physical half-turn. The proved cap isotopies give, at \(b=0\), \[  egin{aligned} E(a,0)&\simeq D(R^aT(Q))\ &\simeq D(R^a)\mathbin{\#}D(T(Q))\ &\simeq U\mathbin{\#}C(	au Q) \simeq K. \end{aligned} 	ag{10} \] Here \(U\) is the unknot. These are the actual marked cap isotopies of [the reductions paper](../papers/conway-reductions/closures.tex), not commutations of open tangles. They retain components and the transported framing; the final zero-framing correction gives the same reduced Kashaev invariant. The last step rotates the entire closed picture: the physical \(	au\) permutes the prescribed cylindrical closing pairs \(\{0,3\},\{1,2\}\) and their empty outside arcs. It is not an erasure of a half-turn on an open tangle. Fix either parity for \(a\), even parity for \(b\), and the original core parities. Vary \(a\) through that infinite parity class, keeping \(b=0\). Equation (10) identifies every resulting knot with \(K\). If \(K\) failed the identity, one fixed \((m+2)\)-leaf template would have infinitely many failing assignments. \(\square\) For an explicit family in original surgery coordinates, take \(\eta_a=\eta_b=0\) at the two new circles. Then \((p_a,p_b,\mathbf p_Q)=(r,0,\mathbf p_Q)\), \(r\in\mathbb Z\), gives \((a,b)=(-2r,0)\). These are distinct original assignments with the core parameters fixed. This one retained pattern passes the full knot test: even changes in a braid power preserve both endpoint pairings and any internal component, while (10) shows that the resulting link is exactly the knot \(K\). In particular, for the entire strict Conway class the following statements are equivalent: 1. Every fixed admissible template has finitely many exceptional hyperbolic assignments. 2. Every hyperbolic strict Conway core satisfies the volume identity at every integer assignment. The implication from 2 to 1 has no exceptions at all; the reverse implication is (9)--(10). The proposition makes the increase in template size explicit. It does not claim that all hyperbolic knots lie in this Conway class. ## 6. A reduction scheme that does not assume its conclusion For one fixed input template, a valid finite proof can have three kinds of terminal record: 1. A whole-boundary source theorem proves the volume identity for all sufficiently long remaining original assignments. Only the finitely many choices of a bounded remaining coordinate require successor records. 2. An exact reduction reaches a knot whose volume identity is already proved, or a branch with no hyperbolic final knot. 3. An unresolved final record has a finite fiber in the original assignment space. The reduction tree must have finite branching and a strictly decreasing nonnegative integer complexity, or a specified lexicographic combination of such complexities. Then it is finite. The union of the type-3 fibers is finite. This is the elementary finite-branching argument, now with an exact fiber test available for affine reduction branches. A type-2 reduction is allowed to pass through an intermediate exterior outside the current geometric source class. What it cannot do is declare its hyperbolic closed descendants solved merely because that intermediate exterior has simplified. The padded family (9) already proves this independently of any classification of those intermediate exteriors. Nor can an essential-tangle or JSJ decomposition alone bypass the issue. If it supplies an exact reduction of a padded family, every original assignment still represents the same core in (10). A decomposition theorem might locate that core and remove unnecessary parameters, but the required numerical volume identity for the core is unchanged. This observation asserts no unproved JSJ classification. For a *single* fixed template, a finite reduction tree may expose only finitely many collapsed hyperbolic cores. Proving their individual identities could finish that template. A theorem for *every* strict template cannot use a fixed list of solved cores as a substitute: Proposition 3 lets any hyperbolic strict core appear in this role. The present long-filling and short-component theorems therefore give genuine terminal records of type 1 and 2, but not a general reduction theorem of this form. The remaining general input must handle the connected short sources and their exact degenerations, including every collapsed hyperbolic core that has an infinite original fiber. This is the precise point at which a purely cofinite induction would otherwise become circular. ## 7. Why arbitrarily long presentations in finitely many parents do not bypass this A different proposed shortcut would be to represent a fixed core by arbitrarily long fillings of an already controlled strict parent, until the existing long-filling theorem applies. Within a fixed finite collection of such parents this cannot work in general. The following obstruction follows directly from the primitive volume differential already proved in [the strict geometry paper](../papers/strict-conway-geometry/fillings.tex); no assertion about cancellation in quantum sums is needed. **Proposition 4.** Fix one complete strict parent \(Y\), a nonempty set of its crossing-circle cusps to fill, and a hyperbolic knot exterior \(X\). There is a constant \(B(Y,X)\) such that no filling of those cusps with all \(\lvert p_ivert>B(Y,X)\) is isometric to \(X\). Here the other cusps, if any, stay complete, and an asserted homeomorphism to \(X\) can be substituted for isometry whenever its hyperbolic volume is known to be the same. The conclusion is that a fixed \(X\) cannot occur arbitrarily far out in the region where every slope is long; it is not a finiteness assertion about all possible presentations of \(X\). **Proof.** Write \(r_i=1/p_i\). The near-complete implicit solution also exists with the meridian equation \[ U_i+p_iV_i=-2\pi i\lambda,\qquad 0\le\lambda\le1, 	ag{11} \] for all sufficiently small real \(r_i\). To see the uniformity, solve \(V_i+r_iU_i=-2\pi i\lambda r_i\) near the complete point: the derivative with respect to the deformation variables at \(r=0\) is the same invertible diagonal matrix for every \(\lambda\in[0,1]\). The implicit neighborhoods can be chosen uniformly on that compact interval, and local uniqueness patches the solutions. The original positive chain and its bounded frames remain in their fixed near-complete neighborhood. In the conventions of that paper, \(U_i=-2\pi i\chi_i\) and \(V_i=\widetilde	au_i U_i\), where the removable holomorphic ratio satisfies \(\operatorname{Im}\widetilde	au_i>0\). Equation (11) gives \[ \chi_i= rac{\lambda r_i}{\widetilde	au_i+r_i}, \qquad \operatorname{Re}V_i=  rac{2\pi\lambda r_i^2\operatorname{Im}\widetilde	au_i} {\lvert\widetilde	au_i+r_ivert^2}>0 \quad(\lambda>0). 	ag{12} \] Let \(\mathcal V\) be the volume of the original ideal chain. Its proved differential is \[ d\mathcal V= rac12\sum_i  igl(\operatorname{Re}V_i\,d\operatorname{Im}U_i -\operatorname{Re}U_i\,d\operatorname{Im}V_i igr). 	ag{13} \] The real and imaginary parts of (11) imply \(\operatorname{Re}U_i=-p_i\operatorname{Re}V_i\) and \(d\operatorname{Im}U_i+p_i\,d\operatorname{Im}V_i =-2\pi\,d\lambda\). Hence \[  rac{d\mathcal V}{d\lambda} =-\pi\sum_i\operatorname{Re}V_i<0 \quad(\lambda>0). 	ag{14} \] At \(\lambda=0\), the absolute volume is \(\operatorname{Vol}(Y)\); at \(\lambda=1\), the calibrated chain is the smooth filled metric. Consequently every such long filling has volume strictly smaller than \(\operatorname{Vol}(Y)\). Its volume tends to \(\operatorname{Vol}(Y)\) as all \(r_i	o0\), by continuity of the same chain at the complete point. If no \(B(Y,X)\) existed, a sequence with \(\min_i\lvert p_ivert	o\infty\) would have every filled volume equal to \(\operatorname{Vol}(X)\). Convergence would force \(\operatorname{Vol}(X)=\operatorname{Vol}(Y)\), contrary to the strict inequality for each member of the sequence. \(\square\) The maximum of these constants works for a fixed finite set of parents. Thus an exact rewriting procedure cannot guarantee a proof for an arbitrary fixed core simply by making every coefficient arbitrarily long while keeping the parent in a finite controlled set. At least one short parameter, a degeneration outside those parents, or unbounded parent complexity must remain. This agrees with, but is independent of, the affine-fiber obstruction above. ## 8. A terminal splitting inside the original circle-tree class There is a padding construction that stays within the original ordered circle-tree syntax, including its subclass of paths. It does not use the enlarged strict closing grammar of Section 5. It also makes a stronger statement for one prescribed template: cofiniteness for a single enlargement forces the identity at every hyperbolic assignment of the smaller template. Fix a nontrivial original ordered circle-tree template \(Q\). Choose its terminal root as in [the circle-tree paper](../papers/circle-tree-volume/main.tex). Closed cyclicity puts the evaluated expression in the form \[ K_Q(s,\mathbf n)=C(R^sT(F_{\mathbf n})). 	ag{15} \] Here \(s\) is the terminal crossing power; \(\mathbf n\) contains the other original powers. The ordered expression \(F_{\mathbf n}\) and all its disk frames are retained. Write \(	au=T^2\) for the physical half-turn, and define one enlarged template \[ P_Q(a,v,b,\mathbf n)= C\!\left(R^aT\!\left(R^vT\!\left(R^b T(	au F_{\mathbf n})ight)ight)ight). 	ag{16} \] This replaces the terminal vertex by a three-vertex path. It adds two vertices and does not create a bare product junction. The half-turn \(	au\) propagates through the old expression by reversing its indicated stacks, commuting with \(T\), and preserving every signed integral power. Thus (16) is one fixed original ordered circle-tree template. If \(Q\) is a path, so is \(P_Q\). **Proposition 5.** At \(v=0\), for every integer assignment, \[ P_Q(a,0,b,\mathbf n) \simeq K_Q(a+b,\mathbf n). 	ag{17} \] The isotopy retains all components and transports ribbons. After the prescribed zero-framing correction, the reduced Kashaev invariant and knot-complement volume agree. **Proof.** The actual ordered rotation and closure identities of [the reductions paper](../papers/conway-reductions/moves.tex) give \[  egin{split} P_Q(a,0,b,\mathbf n) &=C\!\left(R^a	au(R^bT(	au F_{\mathbf n}))ight)\ &=C\!\left(R^aT(F_{\mathbf n})R^bight)\ &\simeq C\!\left(R^bR^aT(F_{\mathbf n})ight) =K_Q(a+b,\mathbf n). \end{split} 	ag{18} \] The second line uses the reversal \(	au(GH)=	au(H)	au(G)\), together with \(	au T=T	au\), \(	au^2=1\), and \(	au(R^b)=R^b\). The third line is closed cyclicity, not commutation of open tangles. All moves are ambient isotopies with the indicated marks and components carried. The knot complement and its preferred zero framing therefore agree. \(\square\) Fix the carriers of \(Q\), writing \(s=\eta_s-2p_s\). Give the three vertices in (16) carriers \[ (\eta_a,\eta_v,\eta_b)=(0,0,\eta_s) 	ag{19} \] and transport the remaining carriers with \(	au\). For every original assignment \((p_s,\mathbf p)\) and every integer \(r\), the enlarged assignment \[ (p_a,p_v,p_b,\mathbf p) =(r,0,p_s-r,\mathbf p) 	ag{20} \] has \(a+b=s\). The map \(((p_s,\mathbf p),r)\mapsto(r,0,p_s-r,\mathbf p)\) is a bijection onto the full slice \(p_v=0\) of this one enlarged integer parameter space. The knot-component test is unchanged on corresponding points by (17). Let \(\mathcal F_Q\) denote the set of hyperbolic assignments of \(Q\) at which the volume identity fails, and define \(\mathcal F_{P_Q}\) in the same way. This notation expresses a logical implication; no failing knot is asserted to exist. Under the bijection (20), \[ \mathcal F_{P_Q}\cap\{p_v=0\} =\mathcal F_Q	imes\mathbb Z. 	ag{21} \] Consequently, if \(P_Q\) has only finitely many exceptional hyperbolic assignments, then \(\mathcal F_Q\) is empty. The same enlarged template works simultaneously for all assignments of \(Q\); it is not chosen anew after fixing a core knot. There is an equally sharp consequence for the proposed partial-filling induction. Fix \((p_s,\mathbf p)\), fix \(p_v=0\) and all entries of \(\mathbf p\), and leave only \(p_a,p_b\) free. Along (20), both free absolute values tend to infinity as \(|r|	o\infty\), while the knot stays fixed. Thus a long-remainder theorem for these two-free-coordinate strata already proves the volume identity for every hyperbolic assignment of every \(Q\) to which it applies. A residual finite exceptional list of smaller cores is insufficient. This is a necessary implication of the original target, not a change to it. ## 9. What the rational normal form leaves unresolved The exact [rational corridor normal form](research_definite_rational_corridor_normal_form.md) reduces a fixed nondegenerate corridor to a chain of one sign with coefficient magnitudes at least two, with integral boundary shifts and a recorded proper rotation. Its shifts are injective translations of surviving original parameters. It therefore gives a valid reduction of the required source theorem to that family of chains. It does not provide their whole-boundary asymptotics. A simple exact family shows why the available reductions do not finish this step. Consider the normalized negative continued fraction with \(r\ge2\) entries, all equal to three. Put \[ k_0=1,\qquad k_1=3,\qquad k_j=3k_{j-1}-k_{j-2}. 	ag{22} \] Its normalized two-boundary matrix is \[  egin{pmatrix} k_{r-1}&k_{r-2}\ k_r&k_{r-1} \end{pmatrix}, \qquad  rac{k_r}{k_{r-1}}=[3,\ldots,3]_- . 	ag{23} \] The continuant identity \(k_{r-1}^2-k_rk_{r-2}=1\) follows by induction from (22). In particular this is the determinant-one normalized matrix, not only a slope calculation. Also \(1<k_{r-1}<k_r-1\). Hence neither diagonal entry is congruent to \(1\) or \(-1\) modulo \(k_r\). The exact [one-vertex compression criterion](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_rational_corridor_compression.md) therefore rules out compression of this whole corridor to one internal vertex, even allowing the prescribed integral boundary shifts and proper half-turn. The ceiling algorithm is unique, so normalization again gives the same string of threes. There is no zero or unit coefficient to eliminate and no string of twos to compress. Original path vertices have degree at most two, so re-rooting cannot meet the high-valence threshold in [the hybrid tree theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_hybrid_tree_filling_closure.md). For \(r\ge3\), the new internal \(3,3\) kernel also leaves an adjacent short filling: its [proved composition rule](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_internal_pair_three_kernel_compositions.md) requires a sufficiently long intervening power. These observations concern the stated reductions and source theorems; they do not exclude a different exact identity or a future uniform chain theorem. For a fixed original template, finite branching can produce only finitely many fixed short records at each stage. That does not make their original assignment fibers finite, nor does it prove the missing boundary theorem for such a record. Equations (20)--(21) show that even a record representing one fixed hyperbolic core can already carry the full obstruction. Accordingly, a complete reduction argument still has to do both things: establish the original source theorem for every short record it uses, and settle every unresolved hyperbolic core whose original fiber is infinite. The existing normal form, local eliminations and high-valence theorem do not jointly supply those two conclusions. ## 10. Which short corridors can be made long, and what conjugation preserves This section concerns exact presentations. It neither gives a counterexample to the volume conjecture nor asserts that an arbitrary fixed-level quantum representation is faithful. First apply the marked degree-two moves only where their valence and attachment hypotheses hold. A unit deletes one vertex and translates the two neighboring powers; a zero merges powers and retains the fiber test of Sections 1--3. The physical half-turns, branch ordering, primitive curves, and original component test are part of each record. At a branching vertex these degree-two moves are not automatic. For a fixed remaining rational corridor, the exact ceiling normal form then has internal magnitudes at least two. Its integral end twists are bijective translations of the still-free original parameters; its degenerate zero case is a merger, not such a translation. Thus the local elimination rules remove \(0,\pm1\) from an irreducible degree-two record, but they do not remove adjacent coefficients of magnitudes two through seven. The [new path source theorem](research_uniform_path_trace_assembly.md#7-the-source-theorem-at-powers-seven-and-eight) proves the original scalar and a local outside packet for the stated positive-seven and signed-eight classes. The [whole-boundary upgrade](research_network_whole_boundary_decay.md) now supplies the additional real-period and quadratic-strip estimates required by the long-turn reset theorem. Path endpoints already have canonical degree at most \(N-1\), so this is a proved admissible source. This does not give the same conclusion for an arbitrary adjacent short block. ### 10.1. An exact threshold criterion for the two uniform-sign forms Let \(\mathbf b=(b_1,\ldots,b_m)\), \(b_i\ge2\), be the normalized negative list of a nondegenerate fixed corridor, and let \[ [D(\mathbf b)]_-=  rac{[\mathbf b]_-}{[\mathbf b]_--1}. 	ag{24} \] The full matrix and affine marking results in [the definite normal form](research_definite_rational_corridor_normal_form.md) and [the complement classification](research_binary_negative_corridor_positive_reexpression.md#7-what-repeated-complementation-can-reach) show that, with the original two outside frames, the only uniform-sign lists with magnitudes at least two, allowing integral end twists and the retained proper rotations, are \(\mathbf b\) and \(D(\mathbf b)\). The pendant assertion uses the original cap and its established stabilizer, not an arbitrary attached tangle. **Proposition 6.** Fix an integer \(K\ge3\). Such a corridor has a uniform-sign presentation with all internal magnitudes at least \(K\) if and only if at least one of the following holds: 1. Every \(b_i\ge K\). 2. The list is all twos, of length \(m\ge K-1\). 3. For some \(k\ge1\), \(\mathbf b=(2^{r_0},3,2^{r_1},\ldots,3,2^{r_k})\), with \(r_0,r_k\ge K-2\) and \(r_i\ge K-3\) for \(0<i<k\). These are exact marked presentation criteria; applying a source theorem still requires that theorem's boundary hypotheses. *Proof.* Uniqueness leaves only the two lists just specified. The recursion for the complement is \[ D((a))=(2^{a-1}),\qquad D((a,\mathbf b'))=(2^{a-2},d_1+1,d_2,\ldots), \quad D(\mathbf b')=(d_1,d_2,\ldots). 	ag{25} \] For its output to have no two, the input must be binary with both ends two, apart from the excluded singleton two. For a binary input its complement is exactly \[ D(2^m)=(m+1),\qquad D(2^{r_0},3,\ldots,3,2^{r_k}) =(r_0+2,r_1+3,\ldots,r_{k-1}+3,r_k+2). 	ag{26} \] Comparing each entry with \(K\) proves necessity and sufficiency. The matrix equality, fixed end shifts, and proper rotation are those of the cited normal form, so no outside parameter is identified with another. \(\square\) For example \(K=7\), the positive path theorem with complete retained ends, and its whole-boundary upgrade give admissible two-boundary kernels for every fixed binary corridor with endpoint runs of twos of length at least five and internal runs of length at least four. The older threshold-64 proof gave the stronger run requirements 62 and 61. This is a family of arbitrarily long fixed short corridors, not a bounded list of knot checks. Their end twists are retained using the proved canonical boundary-multiplication theorem. All words remain fixed as the quantum level tends to infinity. ### 10.2. Arbitrarily long conjugators do not remove a cyclic short core Use the actual pillowcase linear generators \[ S= egin{pmatrix}0&-1\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad A_b= egin{pmatrix}1&b\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad U=SA_1. 	ag{27} \] The presentation proved in Section 4 of the definite-normal-form note is \(\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb Z)=\langle S,U\mid S^2=U^3=1angle=C_2*C_3\). A reduced word alternates nonidentity syllables from the two factors. For a cyclically reduced word of length greater than one, record the cyclic sequence of exponents \(1\) or \(2\) of its \(U\)-syllables; \(S\) occurs between consecutive recorded syllables. Conjugacy preserves this sequence up to cyclic rotation. Indeed, when a reduced conjugator meets a cyclically reduced word, cancellation either removes an outer conjugator syllable or moves one end syllable of the word to the other end. Iterating gives precisely the cyclic rotations. **Proposition 7.** Suppose \[ C(\mathbf b)=SA_{b_1}\cdots SA_{b_m},\qquad |b_i|\ge3. 	ag{28} \] In its cyclic \(U\)-exponent sequence, the block \(b_i\) leaves at least \( |b_i|-2\) consecutive equal exponents. In particular, for every \(r\ge1\), the element \((SA_3)^r\) is not conjugate to any word (28) all of whose powers have magnitude at least four. More strongly, if it is conjugate to a word (28), every one of that word's powers has magnitude exactly three. *Proof.* Since \(A_1=SU\), the original blocks are \[ SA_b=U(SU)^{b-1}\quad(b>0),\qquad SA_{-b}=S(U^2S)^b\quad(b>0). 	ag{29} \] At a positive-positive seam, the two adjacent \(U\)'s merge to \(U^2\). At a negative-negative seam, the adjacent \(S\)'s cancel and the adjacent \(U^2\)'s merge to \(U\). At opposite-sign seams there is no cancellation. This description also applies at the cyclic seam. Each block has at least three \(U\)-syllables before these operations, so its first and last syllables are distinct and at least one interior syllable remains. There is consequently no further cancellation. At most the first and last \(U\)-syllables of each block change; its remaining \(|b_i|-2\) interior syllables have the same exponent and remain consecutive in the recorded sequence. For a positive list, the entire cyclic exponent sequence is \(2,1^{b_1-2},2,1^{b_2-2},\ldots,2,1^{b_m-2}\), up to rotation. For \(b_i=3\) it alternates \(2,1\), with no constant run of length two. Conjugacy preserves that fact, so (29) forces every \(|b_i|-2\le1\). \(\square\) This rules out a genuine conjugation of the all-three cyclic core into the signed-eight path class, regardless of the length or size of the conjugating word. Proper marked rotations cannot evade it: their pillowcase linear part is the identity. It does not classify all isotopies of a particular capped tangle, and it does not forbid a different nonconjugate presentation or an analytic theorem for the original core. At the exact source level a similarity also transports both observations. If \(Q'_N=P_NQ_NP_N^{-1}\), then \[ (\ell_NP_N^{-1})Q'_N(P_Na_N)=\ell_NQ_Na_N. 	ag{30} \] Here \(P_N\) denotes the invertible conjugating operator, not the Casimir polynomial. Unitary carrier scalars and the actual physical rotation are retained separately by the marked quantum identities. Keeping the old cap or readout instead of the transported one changes the observed tangle. Thus (30) provides no new nonzero coefficient for the original observation. The long-turn reset theorem starts with an already admissible source; it cannot be invoked for an arbitrary short block solely because that block has been conjugated. There is a positive similarity for \(JM^3\), namely \(M(JM^3)M^{-1}=\kappa M^*M\), but the [positive-cycle theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_positive_three_crossing_cycle.md#1-exact-source-and-positive-conjugacy) retains two different transformed boundary vectors for the original open kernel. Its positivity controls matched adjoint caps and the cyclic trace. It is not a positivity theorem for all transported bilinear observations in (30). The resulting next source problem is therefore concrete: prove a whole-boundary theorem for the normalized chains with coefficients at least two, or a closure theorem for their genuinely adjacent short blocks, with the marked boundary chirps and full normal data. For branching components the corresponding multi-boundary source is still needed. The affine-fiber obligation of Sections 6--8 continues to apply even if this rational-source problem is solved. The exact finite checks of the complement criterion, signed seams, matrix normalization, and conjugacy signatures are reproduced by `python experiments/check_short_corridor_conjugation.py --output repro/results/research-short-corridor-conjugation.json`. They validate the algebra in this section, not an asymptotic estimate.

title: An all-level local lift of the faithful beta packet
text: # An all-level local lift of the faithful beta packet Written proof, 23 November 2026. This note defines an explicit marked local lift of the nine-cell kernels to every integer level and evaluates its two faithful boundary packets. After the same continuant completion, they are exactly the original positive and negative physical crossings. Every Casimir normal and every displayed scalar is retained. At odd levels the local kernels are precisely the earlier charged kernels. At even levels this is a specified local extension, with integer charge lifts and the physical square root of the quantum parameter. It is not attributed to an existing even-level charged invariant. No global charged Pachner theory, tetrahedral symmetry, positive geometric period or volume lower bound is asserted. The earlier odd-level final [V] and all frozen files remain unchanged. ## 1. The marked data at every level Fix \[ N\ge2,\quad d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2, \quad x=-q^{-1},\quad \gamma=-q. \tag{1} \] Thus \(\gamma^2=Q\). Define \[ g(j)=\gamma^{j^2}\qquad(j\in\mathbb Z). \] The two identities needed below hold at every level: \[ g(j+N)=g(j),\qquad g(j+k)=g(j)g(k)Q^{jk}. \tag{2} \] Indeed \(\gamma^{N^2}=(-1)^{N(N+1)}=1\), and \(\gamma^{2Nj}=Q^{Nj}=1\). The second assertion is the expansion of \((j+k)^2\). At odd \(N\), \(\gamma=Q^{(N+1)/2}\), so \(g(j)\) is exactly the original \(Q^{j^2/2}\), with its half taken modulo \(N\). Choose six distinct complex decorations \(z_0,\ldots,z_5\) and jointly marked nonzero roots \[ s_{ij}^{\,N}=z_i-z_j\qquad(i<j). \tag{3} \] Work on a lifted regular domain for these roots and all normalization square roots below. For a sorted cell \(T=abcd\), put \[ X_T=s_{ad}s_{bc},\quad Y_T=s_{ab}s_{cd},\quad Z_T=s_{ac}s_{bd},\quad \alpha_T=X_T/Z_T,\quad\beta_T=Y_T/Z_T. \tag{4} \] The Pluecker identity gives \(\alpha_T^N+\beta_T^N=1\). Both parameters are nonzero. Set \[ W_T(n)=\prod_{j=1}^{[n]}\frac{\beta_T}{1-\alpha_TQ^j},\qquad \overline W_T(n)=\prod_{j=0}^{[n]-1} \frac{\beta_T}{1-\alpha_TQ^j}. \tag{5} \] Here \([n]\in\{0,\ldots,d\}\), and empty products are one. Every denominator is nonzero. The product around a whole period is \(\beta_T^N/(1-\alpha_T^N)=1\), so both functions extend periodically to all integers. The bar is a label, not conjugation. The normalization is fixed before any boundary coefficient is evaluated. For a cell write \[ (P,Q_0,R,B,C,H)=(s_{ab},s_{bc},s_{cd},s_{ac},s_{bd},s_{ad}), \] and use the literal finite normalizations of [B]: \[ \langle U,V\rangle=\frac{U^N-V^N}{N(U-V)},\qquad k_*=\frac{\langle B,Q_0\rangle^{1/2}\langle H,R\rangle^{1/2} \langle C,R\rangle^{1/2}} {\langle H,C\rangle^{1/2}}, \] \[ v(u;r)=\prod_{j=1}^r(1-uQ^j)^{-1},\qquad f(u,v\mid z)=\sum_{r=0}^{d}\frac{v(u;r)}{v(v;r)}z^r, \qquad z^N=\frac{1-u^N}{1-v^N}, \] \[ u=R/H,\quad v=R/(QC),\quad z=BC/(HQ_0),\qquad \rho_T=k_*f(u,v\mid z),\quad \bar\rho_T=k_*f(Qv,u/Q\mid z^{-1}). \tag{6} \] The same marked root \(k_*\) is used twice. No normalization is chosen from a physical crossing or its source value. These factors are units at every level. The finite product proof in [B, Section 2] uses only cyclic sequences and Fourier sums, and gives \[ f(u,v\mid z)f(Qv,u/Q\mid z^{-1}) =\frac{N(1-Qv)(1-u)(1-z^N)(Qvz-u)} {(1-u^N)(1-z)(Qv-u)}, \] \[ \rho_T\bar\rho_T =\frac{(PR)^N}{N(BC-HQ_0)}\ne0. \tag{7} \] For clarity, no parity premise enters that proof: after regrouping its two finite sums by the index difference, every nonzero difference gives a polynomial in \(Q^r\) of degree \(N-2\), with constant term one; Fourier summation retains only that term. The zero difference is the elementary sum \(\sum_r(1-tQ^r)^{-1}=N/(1-t^N)\). Substitution of the displayed roots proves (7). Their central differences and partial sums are nonzero by (3), so the literal denominators are units. This is the same finite normalization calculation as [B], without its charged odd-level interpretation. ## 2. The local charge lift and the nine kernels Choose integer marks \(h_1,\ldots,h_4\) with \(\sum_mh_m=2\). Use either sector \((r_1,r_2,r_3,r_4)=(1,0,0,0)\) or \((0,0,0,1)\). The following is the complete lifted charge table; temporarily it also makes sense for any integer sector with \(\sum r_m=1\): \[ \begin{array}{c|ccc} T&a&b&c\\\hline 1234&0&1/2&0\\ 1245&0&1/2&0\\ 2345&1&-1/2&0\\ 0123&-r_2&r_1+r_2-1/2&1-r_1\\ 0134&1-r_3&1/2-r_4&-r_1-r_2\\ 0125&r_2+r_3-h_1&h_1+r_4-1/2&r_1\\ 0235&1+r_3-h_1-h_2&h_1+h_2-r_2-r_3-1/2&r_2\\ 0345&h_4-1&3/2-h_4-r_3&r_3\\ 0145&0&1/2-r_4&r_4 \end{array}. \tag{8} \] Thus \(a,c\) are integers and \(b=1/2-a-c\) is a marked half-integer. These are the same exact affine charge equations as [S], now read in \(\tfrac12\mathbb Z\), rather than using an inverse of two modulo an even integer. Every tetrahedral vertex sum is \(1/2\). The non-link interior edge totals are one and the two link totals are zero. For example the latter are \(1/2+(r_1+r_2-1/2)-r_1-r_2=0\) and \(1/2+0-1/2=0\). The boundary totals are \(h_m,1-h_m\), and the four distinct \(05\) totals are \(r_m\). Face indices \(\alpha,\beta,\eta,\delta\) lie in \(\mathbb Z/N\). Define the two local kernels explicitly by \[ T_T(a,c)_{\alpha,\beta}^{\eta,\delta} =\rho_T Q^{c(\eta-\alpha)+\alpha\delta} \gamma^{ac+\alpha^2}W_T(\eta-a-\alpha) \delta_{\beta,\eta+\delta}, \] \[ \bar T_T(a,c)_{\eta,\delta}^{\alpha,\beta} =\bar\rho_T Q^{c(\eta-\alpha)-\alpha\delta} \gamma^{-ac-\alpha^2}\overline W_T(\eta+a-\alpha)^{-1} \delta_{\beta,\eta+\delta}. \tag{9} \] These are well-defined cyclic face tensors by (2),(5). Their charge marks are not silently reduced modulo \(N\) at even levels: \(a\mapsto a+N\), for example, can change \(\gamma^{ac}\) by \((-1)^c\). Marks modulo \(2N\) suffice. At odd levels (9) coincides with [S, (3)] and its specified scalar normalization. At even levels (9) is the new local definition used in this note. Use the nine signs \[ \begin{array}{c|rrrrrrrrr} T&1234&1245&2345&0123&0134&0125&0235&0345&0145\\\hline \text{sign}&+&+&+&+&+&-&-&-&+ \end{array} \tag{10} \] and the original face slots \((\alpha,\beta,\eta,\delta)=(\alpha_3,\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\alpha_0)\). Here is the complete internal pairing, with omitted local vertices in parentheses: \[ \begin{array}{c|ll} 123&1234(3)&0123(0)\\ 124&1234(2)&1245(3)\\ 134&1234(1)&0134(0)\\ 234&1234(0)&2345(3)\\ 013&0123(2)&0134(3)\\ 245&1245(0)&2345(1)\\ 012&0123(3)&0125(3)\\ 125&1245(2)&0125(0)\\ 023&0123(1)&0235(3)\\ 235&2345(2)&0235(0)\\ 034&0134(1)&0345(3)\\ 345&2345(0)&0345(0)\\ 014&0134(2)&0145(3)\\ 145&1245(1)&0145(0) \end{array}. \tag{11} \] The boundary faces are, respectively, \((015,025)=(p_1,m_2)\) for \(0125\), \((025,035)=(p_2,m_3)\) for \(0235\), \((035,045)=(p_3,m_4)\) for \(0345\), and \((015,045)=(m_1,p_4)\) for \(0145\). Multiply the contraction by its original edge factor \[ \mathfrak e=(s_{12}s_{23}s_{34}s_{14})^{-d}. \tag{12} \] Call the resulting boundary arrays \(B_+^{\rm lift}\) and \(B_-^{\rm lift}\) in the two sectors. This defines them directly from local kernels, not from a desired crossing row. ## 3. The six sums and their phases at all levels Put \(k_m=[m_m-p_m+h_m]\). Name the fourteen internal indices as in [S]: \(A,B,C,D,E,F,G,H,I,J,K,L,M,V\) on the fourteen faces in the order displayed in (11). The deltas give \[ C=B+D,\quad V=H+F,\quad F=J+L,\quad I=E+A,\quad K=M+C, \] \[ H=m_2-p_1,\quad J=m_3-p_2,\quad L=m_4-p_3,\quad V=p_4-m_1. \tag{13} \] Their compatibility is precisely \(\sum k_m=2\) modulo \(N\). No eliminated sum contributes a factor \(N\). On this support use \[ u=B-A,\quad v=H-B,\quad \tau=J-1-D,\quad r=E-G,\quad s=M-1-E,\quad z=m_1-M. \tag{14} \] The inverse is \(B=H-v,A=H-v-u,D=J-1-\tau,M=m_1-z,\) \(E=m_1-1-z-s,G=m_1-1-z-s-r\). It is an affine bijection over every \(\mathbb Z/N\). For the canonical sector the signed sum of the constant \(ac\) terms is \(h_1-1\). The integer non-Gaussian exponent before (14) is \[ AD+BF+DL+GA+EC-IJ-KL+MV-GH-M+E+p_1-G. \] The Gaussian ratio is exactly \[ \frac{g(A)g(B)g(D)g(E)g(M)}{g(I)g(K)} =Q^{-EA-MB-MD-BD}. \tag{15} \] Indeed use (13), periodicity of \(g\), and its polarization in (2). Thus no representative-dependent quadratic carry is dropped. Substitution of (14) in the remaining integer exponent gives \(\Xi+h_1\), where \[ \Xi=u(1+\tau+r)+v(1+r+s)+(1+\tau)(1+s)+z+r-k_1. \] Writing \[ \mathfrak n=\mathfrak e\, \rho_{1234}\rho_{1245}\rho_{2345}\rho_{0123}\rho_{0134} \bar\rho_{0125}\bar\rho_{0235}\bar\rho_{0345}\rho_{0145}, \tag{16} \] the canonical array is therefore zero off its support, and on it equals \[ \begin{split} B_0^{\rm lift}(\mathbf k)=\mathfrak n\gamma^{3h_1-1} \sum_{u,v,\tau,r,s,z} Q^{\Xi} \frac{W_{1234}(u)W_{1245}(v)W_{2345}(\tau) W_{0123}(r)W_{0134}(s)W_{0145}(z)} {\overline W_{0125}(1-k_1+r+s+z) \overline W_{0235}(2-k_1-k_2+u+v+s+z) \overline W_{0345}(k_4+\tau+v+z)}. \end{split} \tag{17} \] All six indices are cyclic. Equation (17) is obtained from the nine defined kernels, not independently assigned. For the negative sector no change in the six arguments is needed. The changed linear charge phases contribute \(Q^{k_1-h_1}\); the changed \(ac\) terms contribute \(\gamma^{1-h_1}\). Consequently \[ B_+^{\rm lift}=B_0^{\rm lift},\qquad B_-^{\rm lift}(\mathbf k) =Q^{k_1}\gamma^{1-3h_1}B_0^{\rm lift}(\mathbf k). \tag{18} \] This also follows by putting the two integer sectors into (8),(9). The phase agrees with [S, (17b)] at odd levels and is fixed by the displayed lift at even levels. The calculation shows that each array depends on its eight boundary indices only through \(\mathbf k\). A prescribed \(\mathbf k\) has \(N^4\) paired-face lifts. Its paired average is therefore \(N^{-4}\) times their sum, and equals the displayed coefficient. ## 4. The scalar beta identity and the retained quotient For five increasing labels define, with the fixed finite \(f\) of (6), \[ \mathfrak f_{abcde} =f(\alpha_{abcd},\alpha_{abce}/Q \mid\beta_{abcd}/\beta_{abce}). \tag{19} \] At every level its exact scalar convolution is \[ \sum_r Q^{Kr}\frac{W_{abcd}(r)}{\overline W_{abce}(r+L)} =\mathfrak f_{abcde} \frac{\overline W_{acde}(K+L)} {\overline W_{bcde}(K)\overline W_{abde}(L)}. \tag{20} \] Here is a parity-independent verification. If \(a_r\) is the cyclic summand of \(f(x,y\mid z)\), its recurrence is \((1-xQ^{r+1})a_{r+1}=z(1-yQ^{r+1})a_r\). Summation gives \[ (1-z)f(x,y\mid z)=(x-Qyz)f(x,y\mid Qz), \] \[ f(x,Qy\mid z) =\frac{x-Qy}{(1-Qy)(x-Qyz)}f(x,y\mid z). \tag{21} \] Use \(x=\alpha_{abcd},y=\alpha_{abce}/Q\), \(z=\beta_{abcd}/\beta_{abce}=\alpha_{bcde}\). The two sides of (20) have the same \(K,L\) steps by (21) and the monomial identities \[ \alpha_{acde}=\alpha_{abce}z/x,\quad \alpha_{abde}=\alpha_{abce}/x,\quad \beta_{acde}/\beta_{bcde}=1/x,\quad \beta_{acde}/\beta_{abde}=1/\beta_{abce}. \] At \(K=L=0\) they agree by (19). Every step multiplier is a unit on the regular domain, so this proves (20) around the whole cyclic seam. If \(\mathfrak f\) vanished, all \(K\) values at \(L=0\) would vanish. Fourier inversion would then annihilate the nonzero summand vector. Thus these finite normalizers are units too. Apply (20) first to the \(r\)-sum in (17), with \(K=u+v+1,L=1-k_1+s+z\). The distinguished retained quotient is \[ \frac{\overline W_{0235}(K+L)} {\overline W_{0235}(K+L-k_2)}. \tag{22} \] It is identically one at \(k_2=0\), before any remaining sum. Deleting only (22) thus leaves both faithful slices below unchanged. All other factors and phases in (17),(20) remain. This is an exact local beta elimination for the defined lifted kernels, not a global even-level charged Pachner assertion. ## 5. Complete evaluation on the two faithful slices Stay on the support \(\sum_mk_m=2\) modulo \(N\), and impose \(k_2=0\). Set \[ a=[-k_1],\qquad C=[k_3-1]+1\in\{1,\ldots,N\}, \qquad b=[-C]. \tag{23} \] Write \((z;Q)_n=\prod_{j=0}^{n-1}(1-zQ^j)\) and \({n\brack r}_Q=(Q;Q)_n/[(Q;Q)_r(Q;Q)_{n-r}]\) for \(0\le r\le n<N\), and set the latter to zero otherwise. All factorial denominators here are nonzero. Use the following exact scalar, without changing any normalization: \[ \begin{split} J={}&\mathfrak n\, \mathfrak f_{01235}\mathfrak f_{01345}\mathfrak f_{12345}N^3 \frac{1-\alpha_{1245}}{\beta_{1245}} \frac{1-\alpha_{2345}}{\beta_{2345}} \frac{1-\alpha_{0145}}{\beta_{0145}} \frac{\beta_{1345}}{1-\alpha_{1345}^{N}} . \end{split} \tag{24} \] This is exactly [E, (4)]. In particular it retains all nine cell normalizers, all three beta sums, the three factors \(N\), and the displayed linear factors. It is a unit by (4),(7),(20). After the first beta sum, sum \(s\) using \(01345\), with \(K=v+\tau+1,L=z+1-k_1\), then \(u\) using \(12345\), with \(K=\tau+1,L=v+1\). Direct substitution of (20) and \(W(z)/\overline W(z+1)=(1-\alpha)/\beta\) leaves the following three sums. Put \(K_*=J(1-\alpha_{1345}^N)/N^3\); then \[ \begin{split} B_0^{\rm lift}(\mathbf k) ={}&K_*\gamma^{3h_1-1}Q^{1-k_1} \beta_{0145}^{-a}\beta_{0345}^{-b} \sum_{v,\tau,z}\frac{Q^{v+\tau+z}} {1-\alpha_{1345}Q^{v+\tau+1}}\\ &\quad\cdot\prod_{j=1}^{a}(1-\alpha_{0145}Q^{z+j}) \prod_{j=0}^{b-1} (1-\alpha_{0345}Q^{v+\tau+z+2-k_1+j}). \end{split} \tag{25} \] This records the precise remaining factors. In particular (25) does not estimate the beta kernels by their absolute values. For \(0\le h\le b\) expand the second product by the finite binomial theorem. Its coefficient is \((-\alpha_{0345})^hQ^{h(h-1)/2}{b\brack h}_Q\). The exact \(v\)-sum is \[ \sum_v\frac{Q^{(1+h)v}} {1-\alpha_{1345}Q^{v+\tau+1}} =\frac{N\alpha_{1345}^{d-h}}{1-\alpha_{1345}^N} Q^{-(1+h)(\tau+1)}. \tag{26} \] It follows by multiplying by \(1-\alpha_{1345}^N\), expanding the finite geometric numerator, and taking the one surviving Fourier coefficient. The remaining \(\tau\) exponent is zero, so its sum is \(N\). In the first product of (25), let the degree be \(e\). The \(z\)-sum selects \(1+h+e=N\), hence \(e=d-h\), and contributes the third \(N\). There is no other possible multiple: \(1\le1+h+e\le2N-1\). Use \(\alpha_{1345}\alpha_{0145}=\alpha_{0345}\). The two product signs have total \((-1)^d\); their quadratic exponent is \[ \frac{h(h-1)}2+\frac{(d-h)(d-h+1)}2 =\frac{Nd}{2}-Nh+h^2. \] All these are ordinary integers. Since \((-1)^dQ^{Nd/2}=1\) at every level, the result is \[ \begin{split} B_0^{\rm lift}(\mathbf k) ={}&J\gamma^{3h_1-1}Q^{-k_1} \beta_{0145}^{-a}\beta_{0345}^{-b}\alpha_{0345}^{d} S(a,b;k_1),\\ S(a,b;k_1) ={}&\sum_{h=0}^b {b\brack h}_Q{a\brack d-h}_Q Q^{h^2+h(1-k_1)}. \end{split} \tag{27} \] Invalid binomial coefficients are zero. Every factorial index is below \(N\). Equations (25)--(27) are a direct finite calculation with all endpoints and normalizations retained. For the positive faithful row take \[ \mathbf k_+(j)=(1,0,[j+1],[-j]),\qquad 0\le j\le d. \tag{28} \] Then \(a=d,C=j+1\). Reflection of the numerator factors gives \({d\brack h}_Q=(-1)^hQ^{-h(h+1)/2}\). Thus \[ S(d,b;1)=\sum_{h=0}^b{b\brack h}_Q (-1)^hQ^{h(h-1)/2}=(1;Q)_b. \] It is zero for \(j<d\), when \(b=N-j-1\ge1\), and one for \(j=d\), when \(b=0\). Therefore \[ B_+^{\rm lift}(\mathbf k_+(j)) =J\gamma^{3h_1-1}Q^{-1} (\alpha_{0345}/\beta_{0145})^d\delta_{j,d}. \tag{29} \] For the negative faithful column take \[ \mathbf k_-(i)=([-i],0,1,[i+1]),\qquad 0\le i\le d. \tag{30} \] Here \(a=i,C=1,b=d\), and \(1-k_1\equiv1+a\). Insert the same reflection formula for \({d\brack h}_Q\) in (27), then put \(e=d-h\). The result, including its constant, is \[ S(a,d;k_1)=Q^{-a}(Q^{1-a};Q)_a=\delta_{a,0}. \tag{31} \] For example the constant before the binomial sum is \((-1)^dQ^{d(d+1)/2+ad}=Q^{-a}\), and the remaining argument is \(Q^{1-a}\). If \(a\ge1\), its finite product contains \(1-Q^0\). If \(a=0\), it is the empty product. Multiplying by the original negative sector phase (18) gives \[ B_-^{\rm lift}(\mathbf k_-(i)) =J(\alpha_{0345}/\beta_{0345})^d\delta_{i,0}. \tag{32} \] There is a useful check against the rational-coefficient calculation in [E, (20)]. At the surviving endpoints its rational function is \((1-X)^{-1}\). Both coefficients \([X^d]\) and \([X^{2N-1}]\) equal one. Their displayed combination is \((1-\alpha_{0345}^N)^{-1}\), not one. At both endpoints the rational formula's prefactor satisfies \(\beta_{0345}^{C}=\beta_{0345}^{-b}\beta_{0345}^{N}\). Its factor \(\beta_{0345}^N=1-\alpha_{0345}^N\) cancels the displayed denominator and leaves \(\beta_{0345}^{-b}\). Thus the rational rewrite retains its high coefficient even in this slice. The direct calculation (25)--(27) avoids deleting or estimating that carry. No assertion of its vanishing is used. ## 6. The specified port pullback and original signed crossings Define, from the already fixed finite quantities, \[ C_N=\frac{J}{N^2} \left(\frac{s_{34}} {s_{01}s_{02}s_{03}s_{35}s_{45}^{\,2}}\right)^d, \qquad f_m(k)=s_{0m}^{[k-1]}s_{m5}^{[-k]}. \tag{33} \] This is the same explicit expression as [E, (4)]. It is a unit, with its phase and every marked root retained. No even-level real-decoration modulus assertion is needed. Use the following explicit selected port scalars: \[ e^+_j=C_N\gamma^{3(h_1-1)}s_{05}^dN^2Qx^{-j} \prod_{m=1}^4f_m(k_{+,m}(j)), \] \[ e^-_i=C_Ns_{05}^dN^2x^{i-d} \prod_{m=1}^4f_m(k_{-,m}(i)). \tag{34} \] They are defined nonzero local pullback factors at every level. At odd levels they are exactly the original selected port scalars of [R,V]. We do not assume the odd-level all-boundary port theorem as a theorem for even levels. Instead the selected comparisons follow directly from (29),(32). At the positive surviving tuple \((1,0,0,1)\), the products in (33) give \[ C_NN^2s_{05}^d\prod_m f_m(k_m) =J(\alpha_{0345}/\beta_{0145})^d. \] At the negative surviving tuple \((0,0,1,1)\), they give \[ C_NN^2s_{05}^d\prod_m f_m(k_m) =J(\alpha_{0345}/\beta_{0345})^d. \tag{35} \] For the first use \(\alpha_{0345}/\beta_{0145} =s_{05}s_{34}s_{15}/(s_{35}s_{01}s_{45})\); for the second use \(\alpha_{0345}/\beta_{0345}=s_{05}s_{34}/(s_{03}s_{45})\). Since \(\gamma^2=Q\), \(x^2=Q^{-1}\), and \(Qx^{-2d}=1\), equations (29),(32)--(35) prove \[ w_j:=(e^+_j)^{-1}B_+^{\rm lift}(\mathbf k_+(j)) =x^{-d}\delta_{j,d}, \] \[ v_i:=(e^-_i)^{-1}B_-^{\rm lift}(\mathbf k_-(i)) =x^d\delta_{i,0}. \tag{36} \] Explicitly the positive surviving phase ratio is \(\gamma^2Q^{-2}x^d=Q^{-1}x^d=x^{-d}\), and the negative one is \(x^d\). None is fixed afterward by comparison with a desired source value. By [H], at every \(N\ge2\) the actual full signed crossings satisfy \[ e_0^{\mathsf T}R_+|_{W_d} =\kappa x^{-d}e_d^{\mathsf T},\qquad R_-|_{W_d}e_d=\kappa^{-1}x^de_0, \qquad \kappa=q^{d^2/2}. \tag{37} \] The first is the literal sparse checked-crossing row in [H, Section 3]. The second follows by inversion and symmetry of complete pair boxes. Consequently (36) gives exactly the entire first row of the stripped positive crossing and the entire last column of the stripped negative crossing, including their zero entries. It does not assert that the other entries of a raw pulled-back array agree with a physical crossing. The same result holds after deleting (22), since both observed tuples have \(k_2=0\). If \(w^\flat,v^\flat\) denote the ratio-free selected data, then \(w^\flat=w,v^\flat=v\). One can take their paired averages before (34); the averaging factor is exactly \(N^{-4}\), as established after (18). ## 7. Full-normal completion and source scope For completeness the reconstruction is purely finite algebra. Let \(A=\Omega|_{W_d}\) be the actual complex symmetric irreducible tridiagonal Casimir, with diagonal \(a_j\) and nonzero offdiagonal \(b_j=-(1-Q^{j+1})^2\). Its full minimal polynomial is \(P_N=2T_N(z/2)+2\). Put \[ p_0=1,\quad p_1=z-a_0,\quad p_{j+1}=(z-a_j)p_j-b_{j-1}^2p_{j-1},\qquad B_j=\prod_{h<j}b_h,\quad u_j=p_j/B_j. \] Then \(u_j(A)e_0=e_j\), by induction, and symmetry gives \(e_0^{\mathsf T}u_j(A)=e_j^{\mathsf T}\). Thus \(I_+(w)=\sum_jw_ju_j\) is the unique polynomial class having first row \(w\). Reversing the diagonal and offdiagonal lists gives \(\widehat u_j(A)e_d=e_{d-j}\) and \(I_-(v)=\sum_iv_i\widehat u_{d-i}\). The full-pair commutant theorem identifies the resulting polynomial class with its original operator on all physical degrees. It follows from (36),(37), at every level, that \[ \boxed{\quad R_+=\kappa I_+(w^\flat)(\Omega),\qquad R_-=\kappa^{-1}I_-(v^\flat)(\Omega). \quad} \tag{38} \] Faithfulness uses the full minimal polynomial, including multiplicities. In particular every first Casimir normal at a double node is retained. These are fixed-root statements, not quantum-parameter or moving-meridian derivative assertions. Reconstruct before multiplying boxes, applying a genuine turn or using the original marked closing. Then every leaf is the same complete physical crossing by (38), and induction through any fixed literal Conway compiler gives the same open packets and original closed scalar. Fixed signed integer powers are included by finite multiplication. All Cartan, pivot, framing and peripheral lines keep their original positions. The reconstruction and inverse port factors move to an exterior by their full bilinear dual if that representation is used. They are not omitted on individual modified noncommutant tensors. Likewise, replacing a leaf by its completed expression (38) leaves the same compiler's leaf element, normalized local maps, original budgets and degree-four objective pointwise unchanged. No old budget is assigned to a new optimization over the uncompleted local variables. The actual signed data have Euclidean norm one and reconstruct packets of Newton norm \(\sqrt N\), as in [V]. This is only their particular norm ratio, not a bound for arbitrary inverse data or for the uniform physical Hilbert--Schmidt norm. This proves a local all-level extension of the faithful-slice adapter. At even levels its source is the explicitly defined marked lift (8)--(12), and its equality to the original source is proved after the faithful pullback and completion. It is not a claim that this raw lifted tensor already defines a literature charged state on arbitrary triangulations. No full even-level all-boundary crossing identification, global spin state sum, charged Pachner invariance, geometric cycle selection, positive closing or volume lower bound follows. ## Complete inputs and coverage The following complete matching texts were read. Their finite formulas fix the source data; the parity-independent lift and both selected calculations are written out above. | Text | Lines | SHA-256 | |---|---:|---| | [S: Literal nine-cell source](research_nine_tetrahedron_boundary_source_reduction.md) | 666 | 5aeecb0c174f33baa1264bc34c7419d4ccae007e84f4410b3dcb47c6c81c554c | | [B: Literal finite normalizers](research_literal_charged_tetrahedron_bubble.md) | 383 | 1dfe35f26137572235b1c3af66dcf410e0af758836baddaa8dd6d958c0f61d9b | | [E: Canonical beta evaluation](research_nine_cell_canonical_crossing_evaluation.md) | 424 | 332062e67d64ab4a0767637c0fdd96f186d62c430ad38042aef35ad857d8d7c9 | | [H: Actual full Casimir packets](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_complete_casimir_hermite_packet.md) | 321 | a4e96738a3a093d963fe13cc03585085951fa8699a506ade4e2e7a47c17b3f4c | | [P: Full pair commutant](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_pair_casimir_commutant_and_rotated_trace.md) | 331 | 00ab946b3eddb61256bdbd8ec487789a15991a80e1a28b4eee53bbb4a00f7666 | | [V: Adopted odd-level faithful adapter](research_faithful_boundary_beta_adapter_v2.md) | 510 | fd19f126280ca6a6e307c15fe167ea787821f8f8f8e00b33404fe503d7770188 | | [C: Original normalized compiler](research_convex_normalized_conway_source.md) | 329 | 6b89b4c6a67ef7a32cc41a5966c650f32de65d284ae7b70d94a71bddba21df3c | | [R: Odd-level full-Psi port source](research_full_psi_ray_crossings_and_nine_cell_boundary.md) | 588 | 495a2fde1ed1d7ca0707f060208121bddb2673be21ff3bcb9bac737420ac2d24 | The odd-level limitation of the cited charged sources is not erased. For primary coverage, [Baseilhac--Benedetti's matrix-dilogarithm definition](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0306283) is indexed by odd levels. [Ishibashi, Remark 2.2 and Appendix B](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00220-026-05604-6) discusses the physical square-root convention at arbitrary levels with additional signs; its [phase correction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23572) retains further root-lifting data. These are coverage statements only. No external pentagon proof, normalization theorem or even-level state identification is imported. General cyclic products, quadratic refinements, finite Fourier sums, binomial identities and continuant reconstruction are existing methods. The source-specific assertion here is their complete signed faithful-slice calibration for the displayed local lift. Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used.
