title: Rational quantum normals of the original graded Verma source
text: # Rational quantum normals of the original graded Verma source Private written proof, 17 November 2026. The same untruncated, ordinarily pivoted, graded cut source as [V] has rational coefficients at every quantum-normal order and every prescribed root q_N. At order j its only possible denominator is the (2j+1)-st power of the original deleted classical Burau determinant. The proof retains closed head-carry cycles, not just the root associated graded. On genuine integral-color curves this source is the original finite reduced, zero-framed period. Its order-j root jet at color NR is polynomial in R of degree at most j. The grading-one completion is uniquely fixed by those finite-color germs, is presentation independent, and satisfies every supplied actual generic color recurrence. All-root rational loops and recurrence compatibility have existing literature coverage, discussed at the end. No literature proof is a premise here. This is an independent proof for the specified original graded source, with an explicit determinant exponent and normal path. It proves no convergence of the whole quantum expansion, large-level estimate, geometric-cycle coefficient, or volume lower bound. ## 1. The exact source and theorem Fix N>=2, q0=exp(pi i/N), Q0=q0², and \[ \delta=1-Q^N,\qquad q=q_0(1-\delta)^{1/(2N)},\quad Q=q^2. \tag{1} \] Initially x is held fixed. Put \(\mathbb K=\mathbb Q(q_0)\). On the untruncated Verma basis \(v_a\), \(a\ge0\), retain [V]'s two canceled checked crossings: \[ \begin{split} R^+_{b+n,a-n;\,a,b} &=x^{-a-b+n}Q^{(a-n)b}{a\brack n}_Q (x^{-2}Q^{a-n};Q)_n,\quad 0\le n\le a,\\ R^-_{b-n,a+n;\,a,b} &=x^{a+b-n}Q^{-ab}{b\brack n}_Q (x^2Q^{1-b};Q)_n,\quad 0\le n\le b. \end{split} \tag{2} \] Their coefficients are Laurent polynomials in q,x. No vanishing factorial is divided after root restriction. Let beta have b strands, writhe w, and one-cycle permutation. Set c=b-1-w, an even integer. Its literal source is \[ V_\beta(q,x;\tau)=x^c \sum_{a_2,\ldots,a_b\ge0}\tau^{\sum a_i}Q^{-\sum a_i} \langle0,a_2,\ldots,a_b|B_\beta|0,a_2,\ldots,a_b\rangle. \tag{3} \] Every tau coefficient is a finite Laurent polynomial: crossings preserve total index, bounding every intermediate index. Thus \(V_{\beta,j}=[\delta^j]V_\beta\) is defined coefficientwise. Put k=x^N and retain \[ L_+(k)=\begin{pmatrix}1-k^{-2}&k^{-1}\\k^{-1}&0\end{pmatrix}, \qquad L_-(k)=\begin{pmatrix}0&k\\k&1-k^2\end{pmatrix}. \tag{4} \] Let L_beta be their embedded product in the original word order, and A_beta its first-row-and-column deletion. Write \[ D_\beta(x,\tau)=\det(I-\tau^N A_\beta(x^N)),\qquad D_\beta(x,0)=1. \tag{5} \] **Theorem.** For every j>=0, \[ V_{\beta,j}(x,\tau)= \frac{P_{\beta,j}(x,\tau)}{D_\beta(x,\tau)^{2j+1}}, \qquad P_{\beta,j}\in\mathbb K[x^{\pm1},\tau]. \tag{6} \] The equality is first in formal tau series and thereby specifies its rational continuation. Factors may cancel. No other meridian or grading poles occur. At j=0 this is the fully normalized identity [V, (3.2)]. ## 2. Factorial-block jets and the actual transfer zeros Let \(p_r=\prod_{s=1}^r(1-Q_0^s)\), \(0\le r<N\). Factoring every multiple-of-N zero gives, for A>=0, \[ (Q;Q)_{NA+r}=\delta^A A!N^A p_r U_{A,r}(\delta), \qquad U_{A,r}(0)=1. \tag{7} \] For h>=1 the coefficient of delta^h in log U is polynomial in A of degree at most h+1. Here is an elementary proof with the zero factors retained. Each normalized zero factor is \[ \frac{1-(1-\delta)^l}{l\delta}; \] its logarithmic order-h coefficient is polynomial in l of degree at most h. A normalized nonzero-residue factor is \[ \frac{1-Q_0^s(1-\delta)^{l+s/N}}{1-Q_0^s},\quad 1\le s<N, \] with the same degree bound. Sum over the finite residue intervals. Finite power sums raise degree by at most one, as follows by expanding in falling factorials and using \(\sum_{l=0}^{A-1}(l)_d=(A)_{d+1}/(d+1)\). The root nonzero factors have product \(N^A p_r\), proving (7). Exponentiating shows that the order-h coefficient of a product or quotient of these units has polynomial degree at most 2h: in a product with positive orders h_i, the degree is at most \(\sum(h_i+1)\le2\sum h_i\). Write a=NA+r, n=NC+t, and \[ e=\mathbf1_{t>r},\qquad r'=r-t+Ne. \tag{8} \] The actual factorial zero count in the Gaussian is e. Equation (7) therefore yields the exact series \[ {NA+r\brack NC+t}_Q =\delta^e\frac{N^e p_r}{p_t p_{r'}} {A\choose C}(A-C)^e \sum_{h\ge0}\delta^h G_h(A,C), \quad G_0=1,\quad \deg G_h\le2h. \tag{9} \] When e=1, C<=A-1. Extending to C=A adds only the displayed zero A-C; it does not create a continued endpoint. Temporarily work over \(\mathbb K(x)\) away from the root zeros of the color products. The positive color product has root value \[ (1-k^{-2})^C H_{r,t}(x),\qquad H_{r,t}(x)=(x^{-2}Q_0^{r-t};Q_0)_t. \tag{10} \] After dividing by (10), its order-h coefficient is polynomial in A,C of degree at most 2h, with rational x coefficients. Indeed, split its NC+t factors into C complete residue cycles and a partial cycle. The logarithmic order-h coefficient of each factor is polynomial of degree at most h in its block index. Its finite sum, whose endpoints are affine in A,C, has degree at most h+1. Exponentiation gives the asserted 2h bound. For the negative crossing the root color product is \((1-k^2)^C(x^2Q_0^{1-s};Q_0)_t\); the same proof gives degree at most 2h in B,C. Negative starting exponents cause no change in the finite power-sum calculation. All temporary color-product inverses will be removed in Section 5. Finally the varying parts of \(Q^{(a-n)b}\) and \(Q^{-ab}\) have order-h coefficients of degree at most 2h in A,B,C. Their exponents are quadratic and \(\log(Q/Q_0)=N^{-1}\log(1-\delta)\). This proves the full local polynomial budget, including Cartan. ## 3. Differential realization and the bounded closed carries Represent a block tuple by the polynomial monomial \(Z_1^{A_1}\cdots Z_b^{A_b}\), keeping each residue as a finite head. Let Gamma(L) send \(Z_j\) to \(\sum_iL_{ij}Z_i\); then Gamma(L)Gamma(L')=Gamma(LL'). For a positive crossing fix r,s,t and put \[ f=\mathbf1_{s+t\ge N}. \] Its actual output blocks and residue-sum change are \[ (B+C+f,A-C-e),\qquad \text{output head sum}-\text{input head sum}=N(e-f). \tag{11} \] Before these shifts, the root block coefficient \[ {A\choose C}(1-k^{-2})^C k^{-A-B+C} \tag{12} \] is exactly Gamma(L_+) on \(Z_1^A Z_2^B\). At total normal order j, after the factor \((A-C)^e\), the remaining multiplier in (12) is polynomial in A,B,C of degree at most \(2(j-e)\); there is no term unless j>=e. These polynomials are actual Euler operators. A,B are the input Euler eigenvalues, and C is the first output Euler eigenvalue minus B, before (11). Products of left and right Euler operators give the specified polynomial. Right operators may be moved left through Gamma(L_+): conjugation by an invertible linear substitution preserves polynomial differential order. L_+ and its inverse have Laurent entries in k. Thus each local head entry is a finite sum of terms \[ Z_1^f\partial_{Z_2}^{\,e}D\,\Gamma(L_+),\qquad \operatorname{ord}D\le2(j-e),\quad \deg_{\rm Fr}D=0. \tag{13} \] The derivative supplies A-C and the correct endpoint zero. The multiplication supplies the other carry. Total order is at most \(2j-e\), and the Frobenius degree shift is f-e. For a negative crossing, instead set \[ e=\mathbf1_{t>s},\quad f=\mathbf1_{r+t\ge N},\quad (A',B')=(B-C-e,A+C+f). \] Its base coefficient is \({B\choose C}k^{A+B-C}(1-k^2)^C\), from Gamma(L_-). The exact analogue of (13) is \(Z_2^f\partial_{Z_1}^{\,e}D\Gamma(L_-)\), with the same bound. This derives the inverse sign directly from its literal entry. Compose along the original word, moving linear substitutions to the right. Differential order is subadditive and is preserved by these conjugations. There are finitely many head paths for fixed N and word, although no block index is truncated. For a traced head path, including the head-zero cut, (11) implies \[ \sum f=\sum e\le j. \tag{14} \] Every e costs at least one normal order. Root downward carries therefore cannot occur without a compensating order-costly rise in a closed path. All such cycles are included. The resulting operator before Gamma(L_beta) has degree zero and order at most 2j. The pivot is still present. For a_i=NA_i+r_i, \[ Q^{-\sum a_i} =Q_0^{-\sum r_i}(1-\delta)^{-\sum A_i-\sum r_i/N}. \tag{15} \] Its order-h coefficient is a degree-h polynomial in block Euler operators. Allocating h of the normal budget to (15) preserves the bound 2j. The scalar x^c and the actual head phase and grading \(\tau^{\sum r_i}\) remain as specified in (3). ## 4. The cut trace and its unchanged determinant An elementary trace fact is needed. If D is a degree-zero polynomial differential operator of order at most d, then \[ \operatorname{Tr}_{\rm Sym}(D\Gamma(B)) \quad\text{has denominator at most}\quad \det(I-B)^{d+1}. \tag{16} \] This is a formal identity when B has positive formal degree and requires no inverse of B. The order-zero trace is \(\det(I-B)^{-1}\), proved coefficientwise in [V, (3.1)]. Each homogeneous Weyl monomial \(Z^\alpha\partial^\beta\), with \(|\alpha|=|\beta|\le d\), is a linear combination of products of at most d vector fields \(Z_i\partial_{Z_j}\). Normal ordering their product gives the desired leading monomial plus smaller-order terms; induction subtracts the latter. A vector field on Gamma(B) is the infinitesimal left substitution \(B\mapsto(I+sE_{ij})B\). Thus the trace is obtained by at most d polynomial directional derivatives of the determinant inverse. Each raises its denominator power by at most one. These identities hold on each finite homogeneous polynomial space, proving (16). Put \(T_0=\operatorname{diag}(0,1,\ldots,1)\), the ACTUAL first-block-zero projector, and z=tau^N. Giving z to every block variable gives the original grading on this projector. For each degree-zero D from Section 3, finite-degree cyclicity yields \[ \begin{split} \operatorname{Tr}\bigl(\Gamma(zI)\Gamma(T_0) D\Gamma(L_\beta)\bigr) &=\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(D\Gamma(zL_\beta T_0)\bigr),\\ \det(I-zL_\beta T_0)&=\det(I-zA_\beta)=D_\beta(x,\tau). \end{split} \tag{17} \] Neither T0 nor A_beta has been inverted. Equations (14)--(17) prove (6) over \(\mathbb K(x)\). Their numerator is polynomial in tau: head grading is nonnegative and the trace differentiations have polynomial matrix-entry numerators. No negative grading powers have been introduced. ## 5. Removal of every apparent meridian pole Clear the temporary x-only denominators: \[ V_{\beta,j}= \frac{A(x,\tau)}{g(x)D_\beta(x,\tau)^{2j+1}}, \quad A\in\mathbb K[x^{\pm1},\tau],\ 0\ne g\in\mathbb K[x^{\pm1}]. \tag{18} \] The original finite-sector definition says every tau coefficient of V_beta,j is Laurent in x. Multiplication by D_beta^(2j+1) therefore says A/g has Laurent-x coefficients. Since A/g is a polynomial in tau, each of its finitely many coefficients is Laurent; cancel g from each coefficient of A. This proves (6). In particular the inverses of 1-x^(±2N) and all temporary head factors disappear. Genuine determinant poles remain. At tau=1 the exact normalization in [V, (4.1)] is \[ D_\beta(x,1)=x^{Nc}\Delta_K(x^{2N}). \tag{19} \] Thus each completed coefficient has only Alexander poles, of order at most 2j+1, apart from Laurent meridian powers. At j=0 it is precisely \(F_N(M)/\Delta_K(M^{2N})\), \(M=-q_0x\), as in [V]. No zero and pole were evaluated separately. ## 6. Integral colors before any specialization For ANY positive integer L, put x=q^(L-1) before taking a root. The actual subspace W_L=span{v_a:a>=L} is a Verma submodule; the quotient is the ordinary L-dimensional color. This follows also directly from (2). If a>=L>a-n, the positive color product contains \(1-x^{-2}Q^{L-1}=0\); its other strand rises b to b+n. If b>=L>b-n, the negative product contains \(1-x^2Q^{1-L}=0\); its other strand rises a to a+n. Both signs therefore propagate any high flag along its physical strand, in the actual swapped order. A high flag in any contributing matrix path, even one first created internally, cannot disappear. Follow it around the ONE closed component: it must eventually reach the fixed cut index zero, which cannot carry it. Thus every surviving intermediate index is <L and has its literal quotient coefficient. Hence \[ V_\beta(q,q^{L-1};\tau) =\text{the finite graded quotient cut polynomial}. \tag{20} \] This identity precedes root specialization; no infinite tail survives along the curve. At tau=1 this is the original reduced zero-framed C_L(q). The ordinary closed pivots contribute x^(b-1). Restoring the common Cartan scalar of each crossing and dividing by the ordinary twist for zero framing contributes x^(-w). Their product is exactly x^c in (3). The highest cut introduces no additional dimension factor. This is the finite source convention in [A], and uses no frozen root pivot. ## 7. High-color jets have degree at most their normal order There is an exact generic parity identity. Set \[ G|a_1,\ldots,a_b\rangle=(-1)^{\sum_i i a_i} |a_1,\ldots,a_b\rangle . \] Replacing x by -x multiplies either crossing entry by \((-1)^{a+b+n}\). Degree conservation identifies this with the quotient of its output and input G signs. Thus B_beta(q,-x)=G B_beta(q,x)G^(-1). Diagonal closure cancels G, and c is even, so \[ V_\beta(q,-x;\tau)=V_\beta(q,x;\tau). \tag{21} \] Set x*=q0^(N-1). At color L=NR, R>=1, (21) removes the R-dependent root sign, and the integral curve is \[ x=x_*(1-\delta)^{s_R},\qquad s_R=R/2-1/(2N). \tag{22} \] At k=x*^N=±1, L_beta is diagonally conjugate to the one-cycle strand permutation. Its deleted compression is nilpotent: every remaining permutation path eventually hits the deleted strand. The same argument holds at q0^i x* for any integer i. Therefore \[ D_\beta(q_0^i x_*,\tau)=1\quad\text{for every }\tau. \tag{23} \] Every coefficient of (6) is regular at these meridians. Substitution of (22) into the rational normal coefficients is legitimate coefficientwise. At order j, the fixed-x coefficient of order l receives at most j-l Euler-x differentiations, with coefficients polynomial in s_R of that degree. Equation (20) identifies the result at tau=1 with the finite-color jet. Hence \[ [\delta^j]C_{NR}\!\left(q_0(1-\delta)^{1/(2N)}\right) \text{ is polynomial in R of degree at most j}. \tag{24} \] This holds for every R>=1 at each fixed N>=2, with no parity character. Its coefficient of R^j is \[ \frac{(-1/2)^j}{j!}(x\partial_x)^j \left.\frac{F_N(-q_0x)}{\Delta_K(x^{2N})}\right|_{x=x_*}. \tag{25} \] Only l=0 and the highest displacement power in (22) contribute. This coefficient may vanish; no bound in N is asserted. The original meridian gives a useful coordinate without an offset. Set \(Y=M^2=q^2x^2\). Evenness makes \[ \mathcal W_{N,K}(\delta,Y)= \widehat V_{N,K}\bigl(q(\delta),-\sqrt Y/q(\delta)\bigr) \tag{25a} \] independent of the square-root choice; here the completion is defined in (26) below. Each order-j coefficient is rational in Y with denominator dividing \(\Delta_K(Y^N)^{2j+1}\), apart from Laurent Y powers. Indeed an order-l fixed-x coefficient receives at most j-l Euler derivatives in this substitution; each raises the determinant pole order by at most one. Its bound is therefore \(2l+1+(j-l)\le2j+1\). At the root \(q_0^{2N}=1\). On the genuine color-NR curve one has EXACTLY \[ Y=(1-\delta)^R,\qquad \mathcal W_{N,K}(0,Y)= \frac{\mathfrak F_N(Y)}{\Delta_K(Y^N)}, \quad \mathfrak F_N(M^2)=F_N(M). \tag{25b} \] The last definition is legitimate by (21) and the root comparison. Thus the coefficient of R^j in (24) also equals \[ \frac{(-1)^j}{j!}(Y\partial_Y)^j \left.\frac{\mathfrak F_N(Y)}{\Delta_K(Y^N)} \right|_{Y=1}. \tag{25c} \] This retains the original meridian path; it does not freeze x while differentiating a fixed-M family. ## 8. Canonical completion, uniqueness, and actual recurrences Define \[ \widehat V_{N,K}(q,x)= \sum_{j\ge0}\delta^j V_{\beta,j}(x,1). \tag{26} \] It is a formal series with rational meridian coefficients. This does not assert generic convergence of (3) at tau=1. The following elementary rigidity suffices. In eta=log(1-delta), u=log(x/x*), a formal germ H(eta,u) vanishing on every line u=s_R eta is zero. Its homogeneous degree-n coefficient restricts to a polynomial of degree at most n in s_R. Infinitely many distinct slopes force every coefficient of that polynomial to vanish. Two presentations of the same zero-framed knot have the same C_NR(q) in (20), hence the same restrictions on all these lines after (21). Equation (23) makes their coefficients regular germs. Rigidity identifies the full germs; equality of a rational meridian germ identifies the rational function. Thus (26) is presentation independent. It is also unique among formal rational-meridian series regular at x*, even in x, and with the prescribed integral-color germs. Without evenness, use one parity of R, still infinitely many slopes, for the analogous local uniqueness at each root point. Take any SUPPLIED actual generic color recurrence, in the original meridian convention M=-q^L, \[ \sum_{i\in I}a_i(q,-q^L)\,C_{L+i}(q)=0, \tag{27} \] for all sufficiently large positive L and a fixed finite integer shift set I. Clear coefficient denominators first. Its action on the completion is \[ H(q,x)=\sum_{i\in I}a_i(q,-qx) \widehat V_{N,K}(q,q^i x). \tag{28} \] All terms are regular at x*, by (23). On the genuine curve x=q^(NR-1), the shifted colors NR+i are positive for large R. The ANY-L statement (20) makes (28) exactly (27). Restrict here to odd positive R: the genuine curve then has root x* itself, and its logarithmic slope is s_R, with no sign gauge applied to the possibly odd recurrence coefficients. These are still infinitely many distinct slopes. Rigidity gives H=0 as a germ and coefficientwise as rational functions. Thus every supplied actual generic color annihilator acts on this same selected all-root completion. No existence theorem for a recurrence, minimality, equality of annihilator ideals, or geometric-factor identification is inferred. ## 9. Coverage and scope The general all-root rational-loop and recurrence statements have existing literature coverage. Garoufalidis--Wheeler, [“A lift of the colored Jones polynomial of a knot” (2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.01619), Theorem 1.3 and Corollaries 1.5 and 1.9, state all-root loop expansions via an etale Habiro ring and recurrence compatibility. Their abstract and theorem/corollary statements were consulted for coverage only. Willetts's unified invariant already gives the root ADO/Alexander normalization recorded in [V]. These are statement-level coverage, not proof premises. No novelty is claimed for all-root rationality itself. The internal addition here is the independent, literal proof for (3): its bounded differential insertion, all closed carry cycles, exact projector and determinant power, cancellation of apparent poles, and original finite-color normal restrictions. The finite high-color PBW theorem cannot simply replace Section 3: at generic Verma meridian, unbounded block transfers survive already at order zero. Fixed-x, fixed-M=-qx, and integral-color normals are different. The latter paths require their original chain rule. No generic analytic completion, coefficient-size estimate, geometric cycle comparison, or selected scalar lower follows. The only complete proof directs are: | Label | Complete source | SHA256 | |---|---|---| | V | notes/frobenius_verma_period.md | b11489368e7ac1106c7a5e760154b0713dfbc7eaf9b76193438df57b48041a90 | | A | notes/adequacy_and_algebraic_periods.md | d471549b23c1dd982b7152ef0e90d6fb51d1be9a3c73c1b52ed0e41c9b2c0caa | V supplies (2)--(5), the polynomial root trace, and the exact Alexander/ADO normalization. A is used only for the original finite reduced-color, ordinary cut and zero-framing convention; its adequacy and degree theorems are not used. All factorial-jet, carry, differential, pole-removal and slope-rigidity steps are proved above without mathematical programs or tests.

title: Explicit boundary Casimirs in the marked observation coordinates
text: # Explicit boundary Casimirs in the marked observation coordinates 24 November 2026. Written research proof. The all-width marked observation has an explicit inverse on the actual source. This note replaces that full reconstruction, for each of the two outer pair Casimirs, by one shared linear Borel resolvent on the middle physical packet. All other pair Casimirs remain literal middle operators. The resolvent has an exact finite inverse with denominator two, at every level, and norm at most \(e^{C_bN}\) at fixed width. In a specified coherent Borel metric its normalized multiplier has norm at most three. The formulas transport the actual braid representation by its original Casimir polynomials, including every Jordan derivative. The braid polynomials themselves are not asserted to have bounded order. All source constraints remain, and the original marked closing has an explicit physical row with polynomial norm. These identities do not lower-bound the final coherent scalar. ## 1. Source, middle packet and statement Fix \(N\ge2\), and use the complete conventions of [O,M,P]: \[ d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\quad x=-q^{-1},\quad \xi=q^{-3},\quad \theta=\pi/(2N). \tag{1} \] On the original orthonormal physical head \(V=\mathbb C^N\), \[ E|a\rangle=(Q^{-a}-1)|a-1\rangle,\quad F|a\rangle=(1-Q^{a+1})|a+1\rangle,\quad K|a\rangle=xQ^{-a}|a\rangle . \tag{2} \] Missing arrows are zero. The coproducts are \[ E_{12}=E_1K_2+E_2,\qquad F_{12}=F_1+K_1^{-1}F_2,\qquad K_{12}=K_1K_2 . \tag{3} \] The unrolled weight \(H|a\rangle=(d-2a)|a\rangle\) is additive. The actual unscaled pair Casimir is \[ \Omega_{12}=F_{12}E_{12}+qK_{12}+q^{-1}K_{12}^{-1}. \tag{4} \] In particular the one-head scalar identity is \(FE+qK+q^{-1}K^{-1}=-2I\). Let \(b\ge4\) be even, \(n=b-2\), and \(W=V^{\otimes n}\). Write \(E,F,K\), without a subscript, for the total operators on \(W\). Write \(E_j,F_j,K_j\) for its individual physical heads. The original endpoint rows and observation are \[ \eta_a=\frac{1-q^3}{2}q^{3a},\qquad \zeta_a=\frac{1-q^{-3}}2x^a,\qquad \mathscr D=\eta\otimes I_W\otimes\zeta . \tag{5} \] As in [O], let \(\mathcal I_b\) be the full unrolled root invariant space and \(\mathcal S_b\) its saturated generic source subspace. Their images under \(\mathscr D\) retain [O]'s unrolled and divided-current equations. It is useful to state the larger working domain as well. Let \(\mathcal I_b^{\rm sm}=\ker E_{\rm tot}\cap\ker F_{\rm tot} \cap\ker(K_{\rm tot}-I)\), without the unrolled condition. The same literal currying and Borel reconstruction in [O] identify \[ \mathcal K_W:=\mathscr D(\mathcal I_b^{\rm sm}) =\ker(B_\sigma^W-\sigma I),\qquad B_\sigma=F-EK^{-1}+\sigma K^{-1},\quad \sigma=-q^{-1}-q^2 . \tag{6} \] The smaller actual source image is \(\mathcal Y_b=\mathscr D(\mathcal S_b)\subset\mathcal K_W\). Neither the unrolled nor the generic-source constraint follows just from membership in \(\mathcal K_W\). Define operators on the whole middle physical space: \[ \mathcal C=E-\xi K,\qquad \mathcal R=(\mathcal C+QI)^{-1},\qquad \mathcal V=(1-\xi)\mathcal R . \tag{7} \] The inverse in (7) always exists; it is proved below. Set \[ \begin{split} C_{L,0}&=-2K_1+q^3E_1-q^{-4}F_1K_1,\\ C_{L,+}&=(1+q^{-2})K_1-q^3E_1 +q^{-6}F_1K_1+2q^{-1}I,\\ C_{R,0}&=qF_n-K_n^{-1}E_n-2K_n^{-1},\\ C_{R,+}&=2qI+(1+q^2)K_n^{-1}-q^3F_n+K_n^{-1}E_n . \end{split} \tag{8} \] All products have the displayed order. In particular \(K_n^{-1}E_n\) has not been interchanged. **Theorem.** The transported pair Casimirs are the restrictions of the following explicit operators on \(W\): \[ \boxed{\quad T_1=C_{L,0}+C_{L,+}\,QK\mathcal V,\qquad T_{b-1}=C_{R,0}+C_{R,+}\mathcal V,\qquad T_i=\Omega^W_{i-1,i}\quad(2\le i\le b-2). \quad} \tag{9} \] For every \(\Phi\in\mathcal I_b^{\rm sm}\), \[ T_i\mathscr D\Phi =\mathscr D\Omega_{i,i+1}\Phi . \tag{10} \] They consequently preserve \(\mathcal K_W\), the unrolled image, and the actual saturated source image \(\mathcal Y_b\). For fixed \(b\), on the whole physical \(W\), \[ \|\mathcal R\|+\|\mathcal V\|+\|T_1\|+\|T_{b-1}\| \le e^{C_bN}. \tag{11} \] No polynomial bound on these physical norms is asserted. The shared auxiliary vector \(\mathcal V y\) need not belong to any of the constrained source images. ## 2. Literal currying and the two cup transposes Retain the original turns \[ p_{ab}=Nx^{-b}\delta_{a+b,d},\qquad \ell_{ab}=x^a\delta_{a+b,d}/N,\qquad m_{ab}=x^b/N^2 . \tag{12} \] There is no degree delta in \(m\). Let \(P=(p_{ab})\), and let \(A=V\otimes V\) be the two-input module for the literal currying \[ \Phi_f=(I\otimes f\otimes I)(p_{12}\otimes p_{34}),\qquad f:A\longrightarrow W . \tag{13} \] For small Hopf intertwiners, this is exactly the invariant tensor correspondence, with no unrolled equation imposed. Adding the unrolled equation gives [O]'s original \(\mathcal I_b\). Its entrywise normalization is \[ (\Phi_f)_{a,i,b} =N^2x^{a-b-d}f_{i,d-a,d-b},\qquad \|\Phi_f\|_{\rm ph}=N^2\|f\|_{\rm HS}. \tag{14} \] The observation is evaluation at the fixed pair vector \[ y=\mathscr D\Phi_f=f(\mathbf u),\qquad \mathbf u_{ab}=C_D\tau^a,\quad \tau=-Q^{-1},\quad C_D=N^2\sin^2(3\theta)q^{3d}. \tag{15} \] The constant \(C_D\) is the original nonzero endpoint contraction. It is not reset or suppressed in any linear identity below. For an operator \(A_0\) on the left outer head, contraction changes the first input seed by the anti-homomorphism \[ J_L(A_0)=P^{\mathsf T}A_0^{\mathsf T}(P^{\mathsf T})^{-1}, \qquad J_L(K)=K^{-1},\quad J_L(E)=-K^{-1}E,\quad J_L(F)=-FK . \tag{16} \] For an operator on the right outer head the corresponding map is \[ J_R(A_0)=PA_0^{\mathsf T}P^{-1},\qquad J_R(K)=K^{-1},\quad J_R(E)=-EK^{-1},\quad J_R(F)=-KF . \tag{17} \] These follow either from (2),(12) or from the two actual cup intertwining equations. The difference in order between (16) and (17) is essential. For example \[ J_L(FE)=EF,\qquad J_L(K^{-1}E)=-Q^{-1}E,\qquad J_R(FK)=-F . \tag{18} \] All operators here act on the indicated input factor of \(A\). They are finite matrix identities, including their top and bottom rows. ## 3. One universal Borel resolvent On the input pair write \[ X=Q^{-(a+b)},\qquad Y=Q^{-b},\qquad Z=Q^{-a}=X/Y,\qquad R=Q^{-1}. \tag{19} \] In particular \(Z\) is not \(X^{-1}Y\). The exact gauged \(E_A\) action from [O], divided by \(\mathbf u\), is \[ \mathcal L P =\xi R X P(RX,Y)-\xi YP(RX,Y)+(RY-1)P(RX,RY), \qquad K_A=RX . \tag{20} \] Substitute \(P=Y^{-1}\), as a function on the finite clock grid. The terms proportional to \(XY^{-1}\) cancel against \(-\xi K_A Y^{-1}\), leaving \[ (E_A-\xi K_A+QI)(Y^{-1}\mathbf u) =(1-\xi)\mathbf u . \tag{21} \] This calculation uses the root relation \(Y^N=1\), not an unrecorded continuation past an endpoint. On every even-head middle module, \(E^N=0\), \(K^N=I\), and \(KE=QEK\). The root Gaussian-binomial identity therefore gives \[ \mathcal C^N=(E-\xi K)^N =(-\xi)^NI=(-1)^{N+1}I , \tag{22} \] since \(\xi^N=-1\). Mixed Gaussian coefficients vanish because \(Q\) is primitive and their denominator indices are less than \(N\). This proof includes all even and composite levels. The elementary finite geometric identity now gives \[ \boxed{\quad \mathcal R=\frac12\sum_{j=0}^{N-1} (-\mathcal C)^jQ^{N-1-j}. \quad} \tag{23} \] Indeed multiplication by \(\mathcal C+Q\) gives \(Q^N-(-\mathcal C)^N=2I\). There is no division by a possibly vanishing channel value, and no level \(N\) is inverted in (23). Because \(f\) intertwines \(E,K\), it also intertwines the finite inverse (23). Equation (21) gives \[ v:=f(Y^{-1}\mathbf u)=\mathcal V y,\qquad f(Z\mathbf u)=QK\,v . \tag{24} \] For the second identity use \(X=QK_A\), with \(K_A\) on the left. Only the single vector \(v\) will be needed for both boundary gates. The inverse clock modification has a different, polynomial expression: \[ f(Z^{-1}\mathbf u) =\frac{q}{q-1}K^{-1}(E-\xi K+I)y . \tag{25} \] Equation (25) concerns \(Z^{-1}=X^{-1}Y\), not \(Z\). The latter is the clock that survives in the left Casimir below. For the quantitative bound, the actual physical totals satisfy \(\|E\|\le2n\), \(\|K\|=1\), hence \(\|\mathcal C\|\le2n+1\). Formula (23) proves \[ \|\mathcal R\|\le \frac N2(2n+1)^{N-1}\le e^{C_nN}. \tag{26} \] This estimates the finite sum directly. It does not multiply \(N\) unrelated inverse estimates or introduce an \(N\log N\) exponent. Since \(|1-\xi|\le2\), it also bounds \(\mathcal V\). ## 4. Orthogonal channels for this actual resolvent The finite Euler mechanism gives more information about the denominator. Put \(F_r=(Q;Q)_r\), \(F_0=1\), and, on a nilpotent argument \(t^N=0\), set \[ \mathsf e_N(t)=\sum_{r=0}^d\frac{t^r}{F_r},\qquad \mathsf X=EK^{-1},\qquad S=\mathsf e_N(\mathsf X/\xi)^{-1}. \tag{26a} \] The inverse polynomial is \(\sum_{r<N}(-1)^rQ^{r(r-1)/2}t^r/F_r\). Finite Gaussian convolution proves this inverse and \(\mathsf e_N(Qt)=(1-t)\mathsf e_N(t)\); no \(F_N\) is used. Also \(\mathsf X^N=0\) and \(K\mathsf XK^{-1}=Q\mathsf X\). Consequently \[ SKS^{-1}=(1-\mathsf X/\xi)K,\qquad \mathcal C=-\xi SKS^{-1},\qquad \mathcal V=S(1-\xi)(Q-\xi K)^{-1}S^{-1}. \tag{26b} \] For example \(S^{-1}=\mathsf e_N(\mathsf X/\xi)\) and \(K S^{-1}=\mathsf e_N(Q\mathsf X/\xi)K =(1-\mathsf X/\xi)S^{-1}K\), which proves the first identity with its displayed order. In the positive metric \[ G_C=S^{-\dagger}S^{-1}, \quad\text{the singular multipliers of }\mathcal V\text{ are }\quad \frac{\sin3\theta}{|\sin((2j-5)\theta)|},\qquad 0\le j<N, \tag{26c} \] with their actual physical multiplicities. Indeed \(K\) is already unitary diagonal on the physical middle packet, with eigenvalues \(Q^j\). The denominator \(Q-\xi Q^j\) has modulus \(2|\sin((2j-5)\theta)|\), while \(|1-\xi|=2\sin3\theta\). All the displayed angles are odd half-grid angles. Thus \[ \|\mathcal V\|_{G_C}\le3,\qquad \|\mathcal V^{-1}\|_{G_C}\le N . \tag{26d} \] For the first bound use \(\sin3\theta\le3\sin\theta\) and the minimum denominator sine \(\sin\theta\). For the second use \(\sin3\theta\ge\sin\theta\ge1/N\) and the maximum denominator sine at most one. These inequalities include \(N=2\). In this metric \(\mathcal C\) itself is unitary. Its channels are orthogonal physical \(K\)-weight channels in the \(S^{-1}\) coordinates, not a value-only reduction of a pair Casimir. This specified metric is in the controlled exponential window: \[ \|S^{\pm1}\|\le e^{C_nN},\qquad \|G_C^{\pm1}\|\le e^{C_nN},\qquad \|\log G_C\|=O_n(N). \tag{26e} \] To prove the bounds, use \(\|\mathsf X\|\le2n\) and \(|F_r|^{-1}\le2^{d-r}/N\), obtained from \(\prod_{a=1}^d(1-Q^a)=N\) by bounding the complementary factors by two. The finite forward and inverse Euler coefficients have the same absolute values. Summing their \(N\) terms gives (26e) directly. Every literal internal middle crossing, and every internal pair Casimir, commutes with the total \(E,K\), hence with \(S\). Those gates remain literal after this change of coordinates. All other data must be changed as well: \[ \bar y=S^{-1}y,\quad \overline{\mathcal Y}_b=S^{-1}\mathcal Y_b,\quad \bar T_i=S^{-1}T_iS,\quad \bar y_{\rm in}=S^{-1}y_{\rm in},\quad \bar\Lambda=\Lambda S . \tag{26f} \] In particular the entire outer coefficient \(C_{L,+}QK\) is conjugated; the total \(K\) in that factor is not silently left unchanged. The transformed input and closing are not asserted to have polynomial norm, and the outer coefficient costs remain. The constant bound (26d) concerns this shared resolvent in this exact metric. The Euler/Pascal coherent-Gram mechanism is already present in [A,B]; its application to the specified denominator is the assertion here. ## 5. The left boundary, with its original endpoint coefficients The direct expansion of the original unscaled Casimir is \[ \begin{split} \Omega_{12}={}& (FE)_1K_2+F_1E_2+(K^{-1}E)_1(FK)_2\\ &+K_1^{-1}(FE)_2+qK_1K_2+q^{-1}K_1^{-1}K_2^{-1}. \end{split} \tag{27} \] After (16), every left endpoint contraction is one of the following ratios on the first input coordinate of (15): \[ \begin{array}{c|c} \text{outer operator }A_0& J_L(A_0)\mathbf u\,/\,\mathbf u\\ \hline FE& RZ+QZ^{-1}-2\\ F& q^3(1-Z)\\ K^{-1}E& R^3Z-R^2\\ K^{-1}&xZ=-q^{-1}Z\\ K&x^{-1}Z^{-1}=-qZ^{-1}. \end{array} \tag{28} \] For instance \(J_L(F)=-FK\) gives the second row by applying the literal first-head \(F,K\) to \(\tau^a\). The first row is \(EF\), whose diagonal is \(Q^{-(a+1)}+Q^{a+1}-2\). Every missing arrow in deriving the table carries its exact factor \(1-Q^0\) or \(1-Q^N\). Put \(y_+=f(Z\mathbf u)\), \(y_-=f(Z^{-1}\mathbf u)\). The observation of (27) is exactly \[ \begin{split} K_1(Ry_++Qy_--2y) &+q^3E_1(y-y_+)\\ &+F_1K_1(R^3y_+-R^2y)+xF_1E_1y_+\\ &+qx^{-1}K_1y_-+q^{-1}xK_1^{-1}y_+ . \end{split} \tag{29} \] The \(y_-\) coefficient vanishes, since \(Q+qx^{-1}=0\). The remaining \(y\) coefficient is \(C_{L,0}\) of (8). Before simplification the \(y_+\) coefficient is \[ RK_1-q^3E_1+R^3F_1K_1+xF_1E_1+q^{-1}xK_1^{-1}. \tag{30} \] Use the one-head identity following (4), together with \(x=-q^{-1}\). This gives exactly \(C_{L,+}\) in (8). Finally \(y_+=QK\mathcal V y\) by (24), proving the left formula and the identity (10) at \(i=1\). No crossing scalar \(\kappa\) belongs to this Casimir calculation. ## 6. The right boundary and literal interior gates Using the one-head identity on both factors, the same original pair Casimir, with middle head \(n\) on the left, can be written \[ \begin{split} \Omega_{\rm right} ={}&F_n\otimes E+(K_n^{-1}E_n)\otimes FK\\ &-[2I+(q+q^{-1})K_n^{-1}]\otimes K -2K_n^{-1}\otimes I . \end{split} \tag{31} \] This is an identity of the original two-head matrices, with the last tensor factor the right outer head. The required right endpoint ratios, by (17), are \[ \begin{array}{c|c} \text{outer operator }A_0& J_R(A_0)\mathbf u\,/\,\mathbf u\\ \hline E&q-q^3Y^{-1}\\ FK&Y^{-1}-1\\ K&-qY^{-1}\\ I&1 . \end{array} \tag{32} \] For example \(J_R(E)=-EK^{-1}\) acts on the second input vector \(\mathbf1\), giving \(-(Q^{-(b+1)}-1)x^{-1}Q^{b+1}=q-q^3Q^b\). This fixes the order and phase of the first row. The exact contraction of (31) is therefore \[ F_n(qy-q^3v)+K_n^{-1}E_n(v-y) +q[2I+(q+q^{-1})K_n^{-1}]v-2K_n^{-1}y =C_{R,0}y+C_{R,+}v . \tag{33} \] Use \(v=\mathcal V y\) to obtain the right formula in (9). It uses the same auxiliary vector as the left boundary, without reflecting or moving the original marked row. For \(2\le i\le b-2\), the pair is entirely inside \(W\). It commutes with the endpoint contraction, so directly \[ \mathscr D\Omega_{i,i+1}\Phi =\Omega^W_{i-1,i}\mathscr D\Phi . \tag{34} \] Equations (29),(33),(34) prove the complete identity (10). The elementary head bounds \(\|E_j\|,\|F_j\|\le2\), \(\|K_j^{\pm1}\|=1\), together with (26), prove (11) on the whole unconstrained middle packet. For the degenerate even width \(b=2\), no middle head remains. Its invariant space is the original cup line, and \(\Omega_{12}p=(q+q^{-1})p\). Thus its transported Casimir is that scalar; the two boundary formulas with local middle heads are only used when \(b\ge4\). ## 7. The complete braid representation and its source Every physical pair Casimir commutes with the total small Hopf action and the unrolled weight. It also preserves the saturated generic source, since it is the specialization of the literal generic pair Casimir acting on generic invariant tensors. Thus (10), together with the faithful reconstruction of [O], shows that the operators (9) preserve all the stated images. In particular, on \(\mathcal K_W\), \[ P_N(T_i)=0,\qquad P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2,\qquad [T_i,T_j]=0\quad(|i-j|>1). \tag{35} \] Here \(T_N\) on the right is Chebyshev. These follow by transporting the full physical identities of [P]. They have not been asserted on the entire free \(W\), nor declared a characterization of the unrolled or saturated source. Let \(r_N\) be exactly [M]'s original degree-\(<N\) braid polynomial, with its prescribed values and first derivatives at every repeated root of \(P_N\). Let \(s_N\) be its literal inverse in \(\mathbb C[z]/P_N\). Then the complete signed braid generators on \(\mathcal K_W\) are \[ \widetilde R_i^+=\kappa r_N(T_i),\qquad \widetilde R_i^-=\kappa^{-1}s_N(T_i),\qquad \kappa=q^{d^2/2}. \tag{36} \] Their restriction to \(\mathcal Y_b\) is the actual source representation. They satisfy the braid relations and are inverse signed generators there because the original matrices do. Polynomial functional calculus retains all pair-Casimir Jordan derivatives. Replacing \(r_N\) by its nodal values would change the actual representation. The bounded-order rational formulas are those for the Casimirs and their shared resolvent, not a bounded-order assertion for the \(N\)-dependent polynomial \(r_N(T_i)\). No new coarse bound for the physical braid norm is needed: faithfulness gives, with the original physical norm retained, \[ \|\widetilde R_i^\pm|_{\mathcal Y_b}\| \le e^{C_bN}\|R_i^\pm|_{\mathcal S_b}\|_{\rm ph}. \tag{37} \] This does not estimate the actual remaining word or convert an exponential metric cost into a polynomial one. The input and readout also remain explicit. For \(b=2k\ge4\), the original cup packet has observation \[ y_{\rm in}=\mathscr D(p^{\otimes k}) =C_D\,(\tau^a)_a\otimes p^{\otimes(k-2)}\otimes\mathbf1 . \tag{38} \] Let \(\ell_0=\ell^{\otimes(k-1)}\otimes m\) be the literal last-mark row. Its transported row is \[ \Lambda(y)=\ell_0\Phi_{f_y}. \tag{39} \] For every original regular braid word, with all original framing and external factors denoted by \(\chi_N\), \[ K_N=\chi_N\,\Lambda\!\left( \widetilde R_{i_s}^{\epsilon_s}\cdots \widetilde R_{i_1}^{\epsilon_1}y_{\rm in}\right). \tag{40} \] Any splitting of the original factor \(\chi_N\) must use its original convention. It has not been bounded or divided out. Equation (39) retains the full marked cap; it is not a positive trace or a new favorable source row. ## 8. The original input has an explicit cost in the coherent metric The constant resolvent bound does not make the actual source inexpensive. Its cost can be evaluated for the original input itself. On the pair \(A=V\otimes V\), let \(S_A\) be (26a), with the literal vector \(\mathbf u\) of (15). Then, at every \(N\ge2\), \[ \boxed{\quad \|S_A^{-1}\mathbf u\|_{\rm ph}^2 =|C_D|^2\sum_{\substack{k,j\ge0\\k+j\le d}} |(q^{-1};Q)_k|^2 \left|{k+j\brack k}_Q\right|^2 . \quad} \tag{40a} \] This is a positive identity for one specified actual source, not an absolute-value replacement for a coherent contraction. Here is a finite derivation, with the root cutoff retained. Use the input clocks (19), put \(a_*=\xi RX\), and let \(f_r=\mathbf u^{-1}E_A^r\mathbf u\), as in [O]. The ordered identity \((EK^{-1})^r=Q^{r(r+1)/2}K^{-r}E^r\) and the factorial reflection \(F_r=(-1)^rQ^{r(r+1)/2}(R;R)_r\) give \[ \frac{S_A^{-1}\mathbf u}{\mathbf u} =\sum_{r=0}^d\frac{(-1)^ra_*^{-r}f_r}{(R;R)_r},\qquad f_r=\sum_{k\le r}{r\brack k}_R L_kY^k(-1)^{r-k}(a_*;R)_{r-k}. \tag{40b} \] The second identity is exactly [O]'s finite orbit formula, with \(L_k=\prod_{h=1}^k(R^h-\xi)\). For \(m<N\), subtracting consecutive right sides proves \[ \sum_{r=0}^m\frac{(a_*;R)_ra_*^{-r}}{(R;R)_r} =\frac{a_*^{-m}(a_*R;R)_m}{(R;R)_m}. \tag{40c} \] Its \(m=0\) case is one, so the subtraction proves it by induction. Apply (40c) after interchanging the finite sums in (40b). Use \(L_k=R^{k(k+1)/2}(\xi Q;Q)_k\), \({d\brack k}_R=(-1)^kR^{-k(k+1)/2}\), and \((R;R)_d=N\). All phases then give \[ \frac{S_A^{-1}\mathbf u}{\mathbf u} =\frac{a_*^{-d}}N \sum_{k=0}^d(q^{-1};Q)_k(a_*R;R)_{d-k}Y^k . \tag{40d} \] No factorization across terms with total index at least \(N\) was used. The clocks \(X,Y\) are independent uniform \(N\)-point clocks and \(|a_*|=1\). First apply Parseval in \(Y\), and then expand \((a_*R;R)_{d-k}\) by the finite Gaussian-binomial formula and apply Parseval in \(X\). Each sum contributes its factor \(N\), canceling the squared prefactor \(N^{-2}\) in (40d). The result is \(|C_D|^2\sum_{k+j\le d}|(q^{-1};Q)_k|^2 |{d-k\brack j}_R|^2\). Factorial reflection gives the exact magnitude identity \[ \left|{d-k\brack j}_R\right| =\frac{|F_{k+j}|}{|F_k|\,|F_j|} =\left|{k+j\brack k}_Q\right|, \tag{40e} \] which proves (40a), including its edges. The rate of this actual source cost is explicit. For \(1\le k<N\), put \(R_k=\prod_{h=1}^k\sin(h\delta)/\sin((h-\tfrac12)\delta)\), where \(\delta=\pi/N\). This product first increases and then decreases. Its endpoints are \(R_0=1\), \(R_d=N\sin\theta\ge1\), so \(R_k\ge1\). On the increasing half, monotonicity of \(\sin t/t\) gives \(R_k\le\prod_{h\le k}h/(h-\tfrac12)\le2k\le N\); for \(h\ge2\), bound the ratio by \(h/(h-1)\) to telescope. The decreasing half has the same upper bound. Consequently \[ N^{-2}\le \frac{|(q^{-1};Q)_k|}{|F_k|} =\frac{\sin\theta}{R_k\sin((k-\tfrac12)\delta)} \le1,\qquad N^{-4}\sum_{0\le j\le t\le d}\left|\frac{F_t}{F_j}\right|^2 \le\frac{\|S_A^{-1}\mathbf u\|^2}{|C_D|^2} \le\sum_{0\le j\le t\le d}\left|\frac{F_t}{F_j}\right|^2 . \tag{40f} \] At \(k=0\) the ratio is one, so the comparison includes that edge. Write \(I(t)=\int_0^t\log(2\sin\pi s)\,ds\). The uniform factorial estimate in [A] gives \(\log|F_r|=NI(r/N)+O(\log N)\). The maximum of \(I(t)-I(j)\), \(0\le j\le t\le1\), is achieved at \(j=1/6,t=5/6\), with value \(v_3/\pi\). Here \(v_3=2\Lambda(\pi/6)=3\Lambda(\pi/3)\), \(\Lambda(t)=-\int_0^t\log|2\sin s|\,ds\); the equality follows from the double-angle integral identity. The nearest grid pair gives a lower bound, while the at most \(N^2\) terms give the upper bound. Equations (40a)--(40f) prove \[ \log\|S_A^{-1}\mathbf u\| =\frac{v_3}{\pi}N+O(\log N). \tag{40g} \] Thus a genuine source exponential remains in this coherent frame. For the original width \(b=2k\), insert the interior invariant cups by \(J(v\otimes w)=v\otimes p^{\otimes(k-2)}\otimes w\). This is an actual \(E,K\)-intertwiner, so \[ S_W^{-1}y_{\rm in}=J(S_A^{-1}\mathbf u),\qquad \|S_W^{-1}y_{\rm in}\|^2 =N^{3(k-2)}\|S_A^{-1}\mathbf u\|^2,\qquad \log\|S_W^{-1}y_{\rm in}\| =\frac{v_3}{\pi}N+O_b(\log N). \tag{40h} \] Only the known polynomial cup norms were added. The closing remains \(\Lambda S_W\). The physical row computed next does not bound this conjugated row; no polynomial closing budget in this coherent metric, or closed-scalar lower bound, is inferred. ## 9. The original marked closing is an explicit physical row At four heads, the complete pair commutant [P] writes the actual curried intertwiner as \(f=f(\Omega)\), with a unique representative of degree at most \(d\) modulo \(P_N\). The literal cups and last marked cap in (12)--(14) give \[ \lambda_4(f):=(\ell_{12}\otimes m_{34})\Phi_f =\frac{x^d}{N}\operatorname{Tr}(Q^{a_1}f). \tag{40i} \] Indeed their entrywise contraction is \(x^dN^{-1}\sum_{a,c,e}Q^a f_{(a,c),(a,e)}\). The actual pair intertwiner preserves integer degree by [P], so only \(c=e\) remains. The indices \(a_1,a_2\) below mean the physical occupations in these traces. Let \(\mathsf J|a\rangle=|d-a\rangle\) and \(\mathsf W=\mathrm{flip}(\mathsf J\otimes\mathsf J)\). The identities \(\mathsf JE\mathsf J=-F\), \(\mathsf JF\mathsf J=-E\), \(\mathsf JK\mathsf J=K^{-1}\) show that \(\mathsf W\) sends the total \(E,F,K\) to \(-F,-E,K^{-1}\). Their commutator therefore gives \(\mathsf W\Omega\mathsf W=\Omega\). Consequently \(\operatorname{Tr}(Q^{a_1}f)=Q^{-1}\operatorname{Tr}(Q^{-a_2}f)\). Since \(x^dQ^{-1}=(-1)^dx\), (40i) equals exactly [P]'s original fixed-root functional \(\phi(f)\). In particular \[ \lambda_4(f)=(-1)^dN^2[f]_d . \tag{40j} \] Here \([f]_d\) is the top coefficient of that degree-\(<N\) representative, with every Hermite direction retained. We compute that coefficient directly from the observed vector \(y=f(\Omega)\mathbf u\). In the pair coideal kernel \(B_\sigma^{12}z=\sigma z\), write \(z=\sum_a|a\rangle\otimes z_a\). Its first row gives \[ z_1=\frac{B_\sigma+q^{-1}\sigma}{1-Q}z_0,\qquad \pi_0\Omega z= -q^{-1}(1-Q)FKz_1-qFEz_0-Kz_0-K^{-1}z_0 . \tag{40k} \] These identities follow from (2)--(4); the upper arrow \(q(1-Q)\) is nonzero even at \(N=2\). Substitution yields the actual radial operator on the remaining head, \[ A_\sigma=-K-K^{-1}-q^{-2}\sigma FK -q^{-1}\sigma F-q^{-1}FKF . \tag{40l} \] On \(Y^r=Q^{-rb}\) it is tridiagonal in the clock powers, with coefficients of \(Y^{r+1}\) and \(Y^{r-1}\), respectively, \[ a_r=(Q^r-q)(Q^r-Q^{-1}),\qquad c_r=Q^{-1}(Q^r-1)(Q^r-q^3),\qquad \prod_{r=0}^{d-1}a_r=\frac{2Nq^4}{1-q^3}=:\mathfrak h . \tag{40m} \] These follow by applying the displayed one-head matrices to \(Y^r\). In particular \(c_0=a_d=0\), while \(a_0,\ldots,a_{d-1}\ne0\). For the product, separate the excluded \(Q^{-1}\) factor from \(\prod_{r=0}^d(Q^r-q)=2(-1)^{N+1}\), and differentiate \(t^N-1\) at \(t=Q^{-1}\) for the other factor. Since \(\pi_0\mathbf u=C_D\mathbf1\), the top clock coefficient of \(\pi_0y=f(A_\sigma)C_D\mathbf1\) is \(C_D\mathfrak h[f]_d\). There is no wrap before degree \(d\). Finite Fourier extraction and (40j) therefore give the explicit row on the actual image: \[ \boxed{\quad \Lambda_4(y)=\alpha_4(y):= \frac{c_\Lambda}{N}\sum_{b=0}^d Q^{-b}y_{0,b},\qquad c_\Lambda=\frac{(-1)^dN(1-q^3)}{2C_Dq^4},\qquad \|\alpha_4\|_{\rm ph}=\frac1{N^{3/2}\sin3\theta}. \quad} \tag{40n} \] The norm is that of this explicit extension to the full physical pair. It follows from \(|c_\Lambda|=1/(N\sin3\theta)\) and its \(N\) unit-modulus coefficients. No source scalar is used to normalize it. For width \(b=2k\ge4\), let \(L_{\rm int}=I\otimes\ell^{\otimes(k-2)}\otimes I:W\to V\otimes V\). It contracts exactly the original interior ordinary pairs. Those literal caps commute with the two endpoint observations, so the original last-mark row, with no relocation, is \[ \boxed{\quad \Lambda(y)=\alpha_4(L_{\rm int}y)\quad(y\in\mathcal Y_b),\qquad \|\alpha_4L_{\rm int}\|_{\rm ph} =\frac{N^{-(k+1)/2}}{\sin3\theta}. \quad} \tag{40o} \] The extension norm uses \(\|\ell\|=N^{-1/2}\) on each disjoint pair. All phases in (40n), the original last mark, and the external \(\chi_N\) in (40) remain. After the coherent change of metric the closing is still \((\alpha_4L_{\rm int})S_W\); its norm or asymptotic has not been estimated here. ## 10. Linear auxiliary gate and remaining limits The shared vector can equivalently be retained as a linear auxiliary packet: \[ (E-\xi K+QI)v=(1-\xi)y,\qquad T_1y=C_{L,0}y+C_{L,+}QKv,\qquad T_{b-1}y=C_{R,0}y+C_{R,+}v . \tag{41} \] Its solution is unique on the whole \(W\), with the bound (26). Thus these particular boundary Casimir steps have explicit linear residual equations of bounded algebraic order. Their squared residual energies are quadratic in the retained vectors. The coefficients and their known exponential budgets must still be carried in any normalized compiler. No recompilation of a whole quartic objective is asserted here. Although \(y\) lies in the actual constrained image, \(v\) need not. Imposing its coideal, unrolled or divided-current equations on that auxiliary packet would be an extra projection. Only the final combinations in (9), on their stated domains, are known to preserve the source. This is why all intermediate physical coordinates are kept. [O] already proves faithfulness, explicit reconstruction and the exact image constraints of these observations. [M] already gives complete all-width source modules, actual braids and original closing rows; [P] already gives the full pair commutant and its repeated-root Casimir algebra. [A,B] already provide finite Euler/Pascal metrics, literal Borel fusion and source-preserving cap transport. No first coherent Gram, first Borel model or first quantum-group factorization is claimed. The addition here is the explicit general-width transport of both boundary Casimirs through these particular observations: the two literal cup-transpose tables, the cancellation of one endpoint clock, and the shared universal Borel inverse with denominator two and a controlled physical norm. The actual input cost in its coherent metric and the original physical closing row are also computed, with their separate scope retained. This supplies actual gate formulas, not a common positive pairing for arbitrary signed words. The original source constraints and coherent closing remain necessary. No geometric trial field, cap noncancellation estimate or finite-exception volume theorem is proved by (40)--(41). ## Complete inputs and closest coverage | Label | Complete text | Lines | SHA256 | | --- | --- | ---: | --- | | O | [All-width marked-mode observation](research_all_width_marked_mode_observation.md) | 591 | b2ec8912696338d23e67e2ceb3e69a3fd5a1e20dfcfbe49228cd514a7d40f3f7 | | M | [Complete original source multiplicities](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_complete_source_multiplicity_module.md) | 602 | 14cfb558f50c5b091cec9439692dfeb87129e31f38588cb1ebfd8e8547ac99a9 | | P | [Full physical pair commutant](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_pair_casimir_commutant_and_rotated_trace.md) | 331 | 00ab946b3eddb61256bdbd8ec487789a15991a80e1a28b4eee53bbb4a00f7666 | | A | [Earlier actual Pascal coherent Gram](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_pascal_coherent_gram.md) | 494 | b6e6d697b4e21d30ca683f265b9c41170a0bee424d783169b2e0c70233dc889e | | B | [Actual Borel fusion and divided cap period](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_borel_regular_fusion_and_divided_cap_period.md) | 361 | 1d6953e47a2aedd795982886064e03bd8ae1cbe97a3fc868c60cd4d82b9cd971 | Only written mathematics, source reads and text/hash operations were used. title: Marked-mode observations retain every actual plat source
text:
# Marked-mode observations retain every actual plat source 24 November 2026. Written research proof. The endpoint observations underlying the calibrated marked modes are faithful on the entire actual invariant source, at every fixed even width. They admit an explicit reconstruction with norm \(e^{C_bN}\). The proof uses a finite \(q\)-binomial inverse for the original \(E,K\) action. It needs neither a projective decomposition nor successive inversions of ill-conditioned weight maps. At four heads these observations are exactly the previously calibrated marked-mode coordinates, after one specified original crossing. Thus they retain the complete \(N\)-dimensional source, including all pair Casimir normal directions. At greater width their image has explicit source constraints; it is not a free array of coideal labels. The original closing functional is transported through the full inverse. Faithfulness does not give a lower bound for its scalar after an arbitrary fixed short partial filling. ## 1. Actual endpoint maps and the theorem Use the root and physical conventions of [M,P,N,H,K,D]: \[ N\ge2,\quad d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\quad x=-q^{-1}=q^d,\quad 	heta=\pi/(2N). 	ag{1} \] On \(V=\mathbb C^N\), in its original orthonormal basis, \[  egin{split} E|aangle&=(Q^{-a}-1)|a-1angle,& F|aangle&=(1-Q^{a+1})|a+1angle,\ K|aangle&=xQ^{-a}|aangle,& H|aangle&=(d-2a)|aangle . \end{split} 	ag{2} \] Missing endpoint arrows vanish. The actual coproducts are \[ E_{12}=E_1K_2+E_2,\quad F_{12}=F_1+K_1^{-1}F_2,\quad K_{12}=K_1K_2 . 	ag{3} \] The unrolled \(H\) is additive. All physical norms below are unnormalized Euclidean or Hilbert--Schmidt norms. The root \(q\)-binomial identity gives \(E_{m tot}^N=F_{m tot}^N=0\). On an even number of heads \(K_{m tot}^N=1\). These identities hold on the whole physical middle module used below. Put \(c=1+q\) and \(\sigma=-q^{-1}-q^2\). Define two explicit rows \[ \eta_a= rac{1-q^3}{2}q^{3a},\qquad \zeta_a= rac{1-q^{-3}}2x^a,\qquad 0\le a<N . 	ag{4} \] They retain the original root branches; \(q^3
e1\) at every level under consideration. For \(b\ge2\) even, let \(\mathcal I_b=\operatorname{Inv}_{E,F,K,H}(V^{\otimes b})\) be the complete root invariant space of [M], with total \(H=0\). The observation is \[ \mathscr D_b=(\eta\otimes I_{V^{\otimes(b-2)}}\otimes\zeta)  ig|_{\mathcal I_b}. 	ag{5} \] For \(b=2\) the middle tensor factor means \(\mathbb C\). **Theorem.** The map (5) is injective at every \(N\ge2\). Its inverse on its image is explicit, and for each fixed even \(b\) there is a constant \(C_b\), independent of \(N\), such that \[ \|\Phi\|_{m ph}\le e^{C_bN}\|\mathscr D_b\Phi\|_{m ph} \qquad(\Phi\in\mathcal I_b). 	ag{6} \] The same assertion holds on the actual saturated generic source \(\mathcal S_b\subset\mathcal I_b\). No generic source condition is removed in making this restriction. On the full physical tensor product, before restriction, the row norm is \[ \|\eta\otimes I\otimes\zeta\| =N\sin^2(3	heta)\le C/N . 	ag{7} \] Thus the pullback of the observed physical norm is a known positive metric on the actual source, with logarithmic condition \(O_b(N)\). No polynomial condition bound is asserted. ## 2. Literal currying and its rank-one input The actual cups and caps are \[ p_{ab}=Nx^{-b}\delta_{a+b,d},\quad \ell_{ab}=x^a\delta_{a+b,d}/N,\quad m_{ab}=x^b/N^2 . 	ag{8} \] In particular \(m\) has no degree delta. The two snake identities for \(p,\ell\) are the original ones; \(mp=1\) and \(\ell p=0\). No marked cap is replaced by an ordinary cap below. Let \(A=V\otimes V\), and let \(W=V^{\otimes(b-2)}\) with the actual total operators. Rigid duality with exactly (8) identifies \[ \operatorname{Hom}_{E,F,K,H}(A,W)\longrightarrow\mathcal I_b, \qquad f\longmapsto\Phi_f=(I\otimes f\otimes I)(p_{12}\otimes p_{34}). 	ag{9} \] Here the two middle inputs of the four-head expression are replaced by the complete output \(W\); the order of the two outer heads is fixed. The inverse is contraction with the corresponding literal caps. The Hopf and \(H\) equations pass through these snake identities, so both directions preserve the stated intertwiner conditions. There is also an entrywise verification fixing all scalars. Let \(P_{ab}=p_{ab}\), and regard the two input indices of \(f\) as a matrix for each output index \(i\). Then \[ (\Phi_f)_{a,i,b}=(Pf_iP)_{ab} =N^2x^{a-b-d}f_{i,d-a,d-b},\qquad \|\Phi_f\|_{m ph}=N^2\|f\|_{m HS}. 	ag{10} \] The inverse uses \(P^{-1}\) twice. These matrices have singular values \(N\) and \(1/N\), respectively. The observation is consequently evaluation at one specified pair vector: \[ \mathscr D_b\Phi_f=f(\mathbf u),\qquad \mathbf u=(\eta P)\otimes(P\zeta) =C_D\sum_{a,b=0}^d	au^a|a,bangle , 	ag{11} \] \[ 	au=-Q^{-1},\qquad C_D=N^2\sin^2(3	heta)\,q^{3d}. 	ag{12} \] Indeed \((\eta P)_a=N(1-q^3)q^{3d}	au^a/2\), while \((P\zeta)_b=N(1-q^{-3})/2\), independent of \(b\). The factor \(C_D\) is nonzero and bounded above and below in modulus by universal constants: \(2\le|C_D|\le9\pi^2/4\). This includes \(N=2\), when \(C_D=-2i\), and \(N=3\), when \(\sigma=0\) and \(C_D=9\). Also \(\|\eta\|=\|\zeta\|=\sqrt N\sin(3	heta)\), proving (7). We next prove that this exact \(\mathbf u\), rather than a favorable replacement, is cyclic already for the \(E_A,K_A\) action. ## 3. A finite \(q\)-binomial orbit basis Identify functions on the pair grid with \[ \mathscr R=\mathbb C[X,Y]/(X^N-1,Y^N-1),\qquad X=Q^{-(a+b)},\quad Y=Q^{-b}. 	ag{13} \] The change from \((a,b)\) to these two clocks is a permutation. The monomials \(X^sY^r\), \(0\le r,s<N\), are an orthogonal Fourier basis, each of norm \(N\). Set \[ R=Q^{-1},\qquad \mathfrak c=x	au=q^{-3},\qquad \alpha=\mathfrak cR . 	ag{14} \] Divide a pair vector by its nonzero entries \(C_D	au^a\). The original total \(E_A\) then acts by the exact operator \[  egin{split} (\mathcal L P)(X,Y) ={}&\alpha X P(RX,Y)-\mathfrak cY P(RX,Y)\ &+(RY-1)P(RX,RY). \end{split} 	ag{15} \] For the first term use \(E_1K_2\), with input \(a+1,b\); for the second-head term the input is \(a,b+1\). Their missing endpoint arrows are zero because their displayed coefficients vanish there. Thus (15) is a grid identity including all endpoints, not an extension past the physical boundary. Put \(f_r=\mathcal L^r1\). Then \[ E_A^r\mathbf u=\mathbf u\,f_r(X,Y),\qquad K_A=Q^{-1}X . 	ag{16} \] For \(n,k<N\) define the finite products \[ L_k=\prod_{j=1}^k(R^j-\mathfrak c),\qquad N_n(X)=\prod_{j=0}^{n-1}(\alpha R^jX-1),\qquad \widetilde N_n(X)=\prod_{j=0}^{n-1}(R^j-\alpha X). 	ag{17} \] Empty products are one. Each factor of \(L_k\) is nonzero: \(R^j\) is an even power of \(q\), whereas \(\mathfrak c=q^{-3}\) is an odd power. Let \({r rack k}_R\) be the Gaussian binomial polynomial. The exact forward and inverse identities are \[  oxed{\quad f_r(X,Y)=\sum_{k=0}^r {r rack k}_R L_kY^kN_{r-k}(X),\qquad 0\le r<N , \quad} 	ag{18} \] \[  oxed{\quad L_rY^r=\sum_{k=0}^r{r rack k}_R \widetilde N_{r-k}(X)f_k(X,Y). \quad} 	ag{19} \] In particular \(f_r\) has \(Y\)-degree \(r\), with constant leading coefficient \(L_r\). Hence \[ \{(QK_A)^sE_A^r\mathbf u:0\le r,s<N\} \quad\hbox{is a basis of }A . 	ag{20} \] Here are finite proofs of both identities. Applying (15) to \(P(X)Y^k\) gives \[ P(RX) igl[(\alpha X-R^k)Y^k+ (R^{k+1}-\mathfrak c)Y^{k+1} igr]. 	ag{21} \] Use \(L_k=(R^k-\mathfrak c)L_{k-1}\) and \(N_{n+1}(X)=(\alpha X-1)N_n(RX)\). The two Gaussian Pascal identities \[ {r+1 rack k}_R={r rack k}_R+R^{r+1-k}{r rack k-1}_R =R^k{r rack k}_R+{r rack k-1}_R 	ag{22} \] then prove (18) by induction, including its lower and upper terms. For the inverse, work with formal series only modulo \(z^N\). Every denominator \((R;R)_n\), \(n<N\), is nonzero. The product recurrences show that \[ D(z)=\sum_{n<N} rac{N_n(X)}{(R;R)_n}z^n,\quad \widetilde D(z)=\sum_{n<N}  rac{\widetilde N_n(X)}{(R;R)_n}z^n 	ag{23} \] satisfy \[ (1+z)D(z)=(1+\alpha Xz)D(Rz),\qquad (1+\alpha Xz)\widetilde D(z)=(1+z)\widetilde D(Rz) \pmod {z^N}. 	ag{24} \] Their product is \(R\)-invariant, with constant one. Since \(1-R^n
e0\) for \(0<n<N\), it equals one modulo \(z^N\). Thus the corresponding finite Gaussian convolution is the identity. Substitute (18), and use \({r rack k}_R{k rack j}_R={r rack j}_R{r-j rack k-j}_R\); this proves (19). No denominator \((R;R)_N\), infinite product or limiting root prescription is used. ## 4. Quantitative reconstruction without a product of losses The same finite formulas give an exponential, rather than \(e^{CN\log N}\), bound for the full inverse. The complete odd-grid product is exactly \[ \prod_{j=1}^N|R^j-\mathfrak c| =|1-\mathfrak c^N|=2 . 	ag{25} \] Every factor is at most two. Therefore, for \(k<N\), \[ 2^{\,k-N+1}\le|L_k|\le2^k . 	ag{26} \] On \(|X|=1\), both \(N_n,\widetilde N_n\) have coefficient absolute sum at most \(2^n\). Also \[ |{r rack k}_R|\le {r\choose k}. 	ag{27} \] The last inequality follows from the nonnegative integer coefficients of the Gaussian polynomial, obtained recursively from (22). Thus every conditional matrix in (18) and its inverse (19), evaluated at a clock value of \(X\), has norm \(e^{CN}\). Using normalized Fourier transforms first in \(X\) and then in \(Y\) proves the same condition bound for (20). The two unnormalized value transforms contribute \(N\) to the forward matrix and \(1/N\) to its inverse. They contribute no exponential loss. For subsequent source use it is helpful to give the reconstruction operators themselves. At a physical pair index \((a,b)\) put \(X_{ab}=Q^{-(a+b)}\), \(Y_b=Q^{-b}\), and define \[  egin{split} \mathscr R_{ab} = rac1{N^2}\sum_{s,r=0}^d X_{ab}^{-s}Y_b^{-r}(QK)^s L_r^{-1} \sum_{k=0}^r {r rack k}_R \widetilde N_{r-k}(QK)E^k . \end{split} 	ag{28} \] Operator factors are in the displayed order. Equations (16),(19) and the two Fourier inversions give \[ \mathscr R_{ab}^{A}\mathbf u =C_D	au^a|a,bangle . 	ag{29} \] The superscript indicates the actual module on which a word acts. These are weighted coordinate reconstructors on this cyclic input; they have not been asserted to be orthogonal matrix units. Each expression (28) is a linear combination of words in \(E,K\) of length \(O(N)\), with coefficient absolute sum \(e^{CN}\). For example the inner sum has coefficient bound \(3^r\); combine it with (26) and the two normalized finite Fourier sums. Only \(K^N=1\), \(E^N=0\), and \(KE=QEK\) are needed. On a fixed \(n\)-head physical middle module, \(\|E_W\|\le2n\), \(\|K_W\|=1\). Hence \[ \|\mathscr R_{ab}^{W}\|\le e^{C_nN}. 	ag{30} \] If \(f:A	o W\) intertwines \(E,K\), (29) implies \[ f|a,bangle =(C_D	au^a)^{-1}\mathscr R_{ab}^{W}f(\mathbf u). 	ag{31} \] There are only \(N^2\) such vectors. Combining (10),(30),(31) proves (6), with all polynomial powers of \(N\) absorbed into the stated \(e^{C_bN}\). In fact evaluation at \(\mathbf u\) is injective for every \(E,K\)-intertwiner, before imposing \(F\) or \(H\). ## 5. The exact image, including the unrolled constraint The image need not be guessed from a dimension comparison. The algebra generated by \(E,K\), with \(E^N=0,K^N=1,KE=QEK\), is spanned by its \(N^2\) ordered monomials. Their independent orbit (20) proves that the pair is its regular cyclic module with cyclic vector \(\mathbf u\). Consequently every \(y\in W\) specifies a unique \(E,K\)-intertwiner \(f_y:A	o W\), given explicitly by (31). Write the actual coideal operator as \[ B_\sigma=F-EK^{-1}+\sigma K^{-1}. 	ag{32} \] The exact seed relation is \[ B_\sigma^A\mathbf u=\sigma\mathbf u . 	ag{33} \] For a direct check, the one-head vector \(\mathbf1\) has \(B_\sigma\)-eigenvalue \(c\), while \((	au^a)_a\) has \(B_c\)-eigenvalue \(\sigma\). Substitute (2) and \(\sigma=-q^{-1}-q^2\); the coefficients of \(Q^a\) cancel. The coproduct identity \(B_\sigma^{12}=F_1-E_1K_1^{-1}+K_1^{-1}B_\sigma^2\) then proves (33), including both endpoints. An \(E,K\)-intertwiner \(f_y\) also intertwines \(F\) if and only if \[ (B_\sigma^W-\sigma I)y=0 . 	ag{34} \] Necessity follows from (33). For sufficiency let \(\Delta=f_yF_A-F_Wf_y\). The actual commutator \([E,F]=(q-q^{-1})(K-K^{-1})\) gives \(\Delta E_A=E_W\Delta\) and \(\Delta K_A=QK_W\Delta\). Condition (34) is exactly \(\Delta\mathbf u=0\), using (33). Thus \(\Delta\) vanishes on the whole basis (20). This proves (34) without a full quantum-group PBW or a projective decomposition assumption. The unrolled condition is also explicit. Put \[ \mathfrak a_H=\sum_{a,b=0}^d(2d-2a-2b)\mathscr R_{ab}. 	ag{35} \] The weighted normalization in (29) is important: \(\mathfrak a_H^A\mathbf u=H_A\mathbf u\). No extra factor \(C_D	au^a\) is inserted in (35). For an \(E,F,K\)-intertwiner, the defect \(H_Wf_y-f_yH_A\) is again an \(E,F,K\)-intertwiner, by the two commutators with \(H\). It therefore vanishes if and only if it vanishes at \(\mathbf u\). We obtain the exact image description \[  oxed{\quad \mathscr D_b(\mathcal I_b)= \{y\in W:(B_\sigma^W-\sigma I)y=0,\quad (H_W-\mathfrak a_H^W)y=0\}. \quad} 	ag{36} \] For such \(y\), the inverse is the literal \(\Phi_{f_y}\) of (9)--(10), not a freely prepared boundary vector. All coefficients in (35) are known and have word bounds \(e^{CN}\). For the actual saturated generic source, [D]'s value theorem adds the specified regular divided-current condition: \[ \mathscr D_b(\mathcal S_b)= \{y	ext{ satisfying (36)}: \mathcal J_E^{(b)}\Phi_{f_y}=0\}. 	ag{37} \] This keeps the entire original operator on the reconstructed invariant tensor; it does not presume a new divided-current identity on a free coideal clock. The corresponding \(\mathcal J_F\) condition is redundant on the actual source, as proved in [D]. When the whole parameter-dependent source is differentiated, its actual inhomogeneous normal Ward equations must still be retained. Equation (37) is not a homogeneous assertion for those jets. At \(b=4\), [M,D] give \(\mathcal S_4=\mathcal I_4\), of dimension \(N\). For \(b\ge6\), neither the unrolled condition in (36) nor the saturated-source condition in (37) is dropped. The coideal kernel by itself is generally larger. ## 6. Why these are the calibrated marked-mode observations We verify the endpoint interpretation without moving the marked cap. On an invariant tensor, the recursive coideal and the equations \(E_{m tot}=F_{m tot}=0,K_{m tot}=1\) give \[ B_c^{(2,\ldots,b)}\Phi=C_1\Phi,\qquad C=cK-KF+KEK^{-1}. 	ag{38} \] One may multiply the recursion by \(K_1\) to obtain this formula. The actual cup gives \(CP=PB_c^{\mathsf T}\), so \(C\) has the same simple coideal spectrum as \(B_c\). Direct substitution also gives \[ C\mathbf1=\sigma\mathbf1,\qquad \eta C=\sigma\eta,\quad\eta\mathbf1=1,\qquad B_c(	au^a)_a=\sigma(	au^a)_a,\quad \zeta B_c=\sigma\zeta,\quad\zeta(	au^a)_a=1 . 	ag{39} \] For instance the two normalizing sums are \(\sum q^{3a}=2/(1-q^3)\) and \(\sum q^{-3a}=2/(1-q^{-3})\). It follows that (5) selects the first and last coideal heights \(\sigma\) in the complete nested height expansion of an actual invariant tensor. The remaining middle vector lies in \(\ker(B_\sigma^W-\sigma I)\), in agreement with (36). The one-head graph eigenvectors \[ u_\lambda(ho)_a =q^{-a}D_a(\lambda;ho)/F_a 	ag{40} \] have first coordinate one. Thus no further scalar is hidden when the remaining observations are read in that height basis. For completeness these fixed-width physical-to-height frame changes and their inverses have norm \(e^{C_bN}\). The continuant recurrence bounds \(D_a(\lambda;ho)\) by \(C^a\) for \(|\lambda|,|ho|\le2\). Since \(\prod_{a=1}^d(1-Q^a)=N\), every partial product has inverse at most \(2^{d-a}/N\). This bounds (40). The inverse row is \((E_d(\lambda;ho)/p_N'(\lambda))(D_a/F_a)_a\); its extra factor has modulus \(\sin\alpha_\lambda\le1\), as in [N,K]. Iterating these finite frame changes a fixed number of times proves the claimed \(e^{C_bN}\) bound. This is a controlled exponential change, not an assumed polynomial equivalence with the physical metric. Now specialize to four heads. Expand an actual invariant \(\Phi\) with external height \(c\). At last height \(\sigma\), let \(v_l(
u)\) be its slice at the neighboring height \(ho=\mu_l\). Use exactly [N]'s calibrated row \(r_l\) and constant \[ C_0=r_ls_l= rac{2\kappa}{1-q^3},\qquad \kappa=q^{d^2/2},\qquad a_l= rac{r_lv_l}{C_0}. 	ag{41} \] The source identity \(r_lB^+_{c,ho}=C_0e_*^{\mathsf T}\) proves \[ a_l=e_*^{\mathsf T}B^-_{c,ho}v_l . 	ag{42} \] Hence \(a=(a_l)_l\) is precisely the remaining height coordinate vector of \[ \mathscr D_4 R_{12}^-\Phi . 	ag{43} \] The original crossing is invertible and preserves the complete root invariant and saturated source spaces. The target coideal kernel on the middle two heads has dimension \(N\), by its graph recurrence. Together with (6), (36), and the dimension in [M,D], this proves that (41) is an isomorphism on the entire four-head actual source, at every level. Its inverse, in the specified physical source and raw height coordinates, has norm \(e^{CN}\). In addition to (6), the only fixed crossing in (43) has the exact conditional matrices \(\kappa U_ho^{-1}\mathcal D\overline{U_c}\) of [N,H]; (40) and its inverse bound control these and their inverses by \(e^{CN}\). No inverse of an unknown word is used. Most importantly the original readout after the literal cap-straddling crossing is still \[ (\ell_{12}\otimes m_{34})R_{23}^+\Phi = eta_N C_0\sum_{l=0}^d a_l . 	ag{44} \] All factors in \( eta_N\) are the original ones in [N,H]. An original external \(\chi_N\) remains a further multiplier. To restore the original bare closing in (44), retain \(R_{23}^-\) in the word; \(R_{12}^-\) is already part of the observation coordinates. This is an exact transport, not a change in its framing or mark. ## 7. General words, source constraints, and remaining scope For any fixed even width, let \(\mathcal Y_b=\mathscr D_b(\mathcal S_b)\) be the constrained image (36)--(37). Every original regular signed braid gives the strict transported map \[ \widetilde R_i =\mathscr D_bR_i\mathscr D_b^{-1} \quad\hbox{on }\mathcal Y_b . 	ag{45} \] Products of these maps equal the transport of the whole product. The original cup source is \(\mathscr D_b(p^{\otimes b/2})\). The original last-mark row is its literal composition with the reconstructed \(\Phi_{f_y}\); no positive trace or favorable observation is substituted for it. The inverse and metric bounds are \(e^{C_bN}\), not small-error estimates for arbitrary transported states. In particular, replacing every raw slice by its independent marked-mode projection need not produce an invariant tensor. Faithful coordinates must be reconstructed by (31),(36),(37). At greater width the remaining labels are subject to those conditions, even though all of them appear in a height array. The result does not authorize projecting before a later crossing without this exact full-source reconstruction. [M] already constructs complete all-width source modules and original cap rows, and [P] proves the full pair commutant. [D] already distinguishes the saturated source from the larger root invariant space. Neither the existence of a full frame nor those source restrictions are claimed new here. The addition is faithfulness and a controlled reconstruction for these particular marked-mode observations, which are the ones carrying [N,H]'s calibrated source data. The finite Gaussian-binomial and Fourier tools themselves are standard; all root conventions and inverse factors are fixed above by the actual matrices. Every pair-Casimir derivative channel remains in the reconstructed physical tensor. No geometric trial field, common positive scalar pairing, or noncancellation under arbitrary coherent exteriors has been proved. The full finite-exception volume target after arbitrary fixed short partial fillings remains open. ## Complete inputs and closest coverage | Label | Complete text | Lines | SHA256 | | --- | --- | ---: | --- | | M | [Complete original source multiplicities](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_complete_source_multiplicity_module.md) | 602 | 14cfb558f50c5b091cec9439692dfeb87129e31f38588cb1ebfd8e8547ac99a9 | | P | [Full physical pair commutant](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_pair_casimir_commutant_and_rotated_trace.md) | 331 | 00ab946b3eddb61256bdbd8ec487789a15991a80e1a28b4eee53bbb4a00f7666 | | N | [Marked-boundary normal gap](research_coideal_marked_boundary_normal_gap.md) | 512 | bb9bd6d04480ae8733c0fd1c5901834bdf2ea3e8c7eb3617fb8eb58e66e57956 | | H | [Height pairing and original boundary](research_coideal_height_pairing_and_marked_boundary.md) | 543 | bed81fcb12b20d16d41c55b476b13d8d69b1fe79d0d0620c31230ba652b1d82f | | K | [Continuant source kernel](research_coideal_continuant_source_kernel.md) | 365 | 3ea997e5258c9413fd7c771a6a1475b90b39bf731ac55c0902fd136943b26f44 | | D | [All-width divided-current source restriction](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_all_width_divided_source_projection.md) | 204 | dc83b5e232a3d258f516a479d7257e85b9e5663a38e166f07c6ad9ae81004a68 | Only written mathematics, source reads and text/hash operations were used.
