title: Analytic Hermite coupons on the original positive coefficient circle
text:
# Analytic Hermite coupons on the original positive coefficient circle Private written proof, 17 November 2026. The fixed-degree restriction on inserted coupons can be removed for functions holomorphic on the entire coefficient disk. Their full Hermite interpolants have degree as large as \(N-1\), but their original trace is governed by the value of the analytic function at the actual coefficient saddle, with an explicit analytic-norm error. Slowly varying exponential coupons have a relative estimate and remain in this class under any fixed number of ordinary products. A function given only on a slit or near the saddle is different: its poles, cut banks, and endpoint currents remain in an exact formula below. In particular this theorem does not discard the original crossing's cut at \(C\ge2\), and does not prove closure under the physical turn. ## 1. Actual product, coefficient circle, and full Hermite interpolation Use the original conventions \[ N\ge3,\quad D=N-1,\quad J=\lfloor D/2floor,\quad \eta=(-1)^D,\quad c_a=2\cos((2a+1)\pi/N), \] \[ P_N(C)=2T_N(C/2)+2,\qquad \phi_N(f)=\eta N^2[C^D]\operatorname{rem}_{P_N}f,\qquad F_j(C)=K_N(c_j,C). 	ag{1} \] Fix \(m\ge3\) and \(\varepsilon>0\). Consider all physical tuples \(0\le j_i\le J\) with \[ s=\sum_i j_i,\qquad k=s-D\ge\varepsilon N,\qquad f_N(C)=\prod_{i=1}^mF_{j_i}(C),\qquad \Gamma_N=\phi_N(f_N)>0. 	ag{2} \] Every trace below includes canonical reduction and all repeated-root normals, even when the ordinary degree of \(f_N\) exceeds \(D\). The positive coefficient source supplies positive Jacobi eigenvalues \(r_{j,b}>0\), \(d_a=c_0-c_a\ge0\), and \[ \mathfrak a_N=\prod_{i,b}r_{j_i,b}^{-1},\qquad H_N(x)=  rac{\prod_{i,b}(1+r_{j_i,b}x)} {\prod_{a=0}^{N-1}(1-d_ax)},\qquad \Gamma_N=N^2\mathfrak a_N[x^k]H_N . 	ag{3} \] Let \(ho_N\) be its unique mean-\(k\) saddle. Uniformly in (2), for sufficiently large \(N\), \[ 0<a\leho_N\le b<1/4,\qquad cN\le V_N\le CN, 	ag{4} \] where \(V_N\) is the exact tilted variance. Define \[ \zeta_N=c_0-ho_N^{-1},\qquad C_N(	heta)=c_0-ho_N^{-1}e^{-i	heta}, \quad-\pi\le	heta\le\pi . 	ag{5} \] The circle in (5) contains every physical root strictly inside, since \(d_a<4<ho_N^{-1}\). All these circles and their interiors lie in one fixed disk centered at \(2\). Choose a closed disk \(\Omega_0=\{|C-2|\le R_0\}\) with \(R_0>1/a+2\), and a larger open disk \(\Omega_1\) with a fixed positive buffer around \(\Omega_0\). Every coefficient circle has a fixed positive distance from \(\partial\Omega_0\); the Cauchy estimates below use this interior margin and norms on \(\Omega_0\), not an uncontrolled norm on \(\Omega_1\). For a function \(a_N\) holomorphic on \(\Omega_1\), let \(q_N\) be its unique polynomial of degree at most \(D\) matching the following data: \[ q_N(c)=a_N(c),\quad q_N'(c)=a_N'(c) \quad(c	ext{ a double physical root}), 	ag{6} \] and only the value at the odd simple root. This is ordinary confluent interpolation with exactly \(N\) conditions. Equivalently, \((q_N-a_N)/P_N\) is holomorphic throughout \(\Omega_1\). The polynomial \(q_N\) is an actual coupon in the original algebra, with its original spectral normals. ## 2. Exact source integral and the degree-free estimate Let \(S_{ho_N}\) be the exact sum of independent Bernoulli and geometric variables in the coefficient source, and put \[ \chi_N(	heta)= e^{-ik	heta} rac{H_N(ho_Ne^{i	heta})}{H_N(ho_N)}, \qquad p_N=\mathbb P(S_{ho_N}=k). 	ag{7} \] The same source proves, uniformly, \[ |\chi_N(	heta)|\le e^{-cN\sin^2(	heta/2)},\qquad p_N=(2\pi V_N)^{-1/2}(1+O(N^{-1})), 	ag{8} \] \[ \mathbb P(S_{ho_N}=k+h)/p_N=1+O_h(N^{-1}) \quad(h	ext{ fixed}). 	ag{9} \] These are statements about this actual finite product, not a probability model replacing the original source. **Theorem 1.** For the full Hermite coupon (6), \[  oxed{\quad  rac{\phi_N(q_Nf_N)}{\Gamma_N} = rac1{2\pi p_N}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi} \chi_N(	heta)a_N(C_N(	heta))\,d	heta =a_N(\zeta_N)+O(N^{-1}M_N), \quad} 	ag{10} \] where \(M_N=\sup_{\Omega_0}|a_N|\). The constant is uniform in (2) and \(a_N\); no bound on the degree or on the polynomial coefficient norm of \(q_N\) is imposed. **Proof of the exact formula.** On the positively oriented spectral circle \(|C-c_0|=ho_N^{-1}\), the original trace is \[ \phi_N(q_Nf_N)= rac{\eta N^2}{2\pi i} \oint  rac{q_N(C)f_N(C)}{P_N(C)}\,dC. 	ag{11} \] The residues are precisely the full physical trace. Replacing \(q_N\) by \(a_N\) changes the integrand by a holomorphic function: the quotient in (6) times the ordinary polynomial \(f_N\). Its contour integral is exactly zero. Set \(z=c_0-C\), then \(x=1/z\). The spectral circle is positive in \(z\) and negative in \(x\); this reversal and the sign \(P_N(c_0-z)=(-1)^N\prod_a(z-d_a)\), together with \(\eta=(-1)^{N-1}\), give \[ \phi_N(q_Nf_N)=  rac{N^2\mathfrak a_N}{2\pi i} \oint_{|x|=ho_N}^{+} H_N(x)a_N(c_0-x^{-1})x^{-k-1}\,dx . 	ag{12} \] Only values on this circle are used; no analytic extension of \(a_N(c_0-x^{-1})\) to \(x=0\) is asserted. Divide by the exact uninserted coefficient (3) to obtain (10). **Proof of the error.** A useful consequence of (8)--(9) is \[  rac1{2\pi p_N}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}\chi_N(	heta) \sin	heta\,d	heta=O(N^{-1}), \qquad  rac1{p_N}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi} |\chi_N(	heta)|	heta^2\,d	heta=O(N^{-1}). 	ag{13} \] The first identity is the difference of the probabilities at \(k-1\) and \(k+1\), divided by \(2ip_N\). The second follows from the Gaussian bound (8) and \(p_N\asymp N^{-1/2}\). On a fixed small arc put \(A_N(	heta)=a_N(C_N(	heta))\). Cauchy's estimate on the circle's fixed buffer inside \(\Omega_0\) gives \(|A_N'|+|A_N''|\le CM_N\), so \[ A_N(	heta)=A_N(0)+A_N'(0)\sin	heta+O(M_N	heta^2). 	ag{14} \] Outside this arc, (8) is exponentially small, and \(|A_N|\le M_N\). Equations (13)--(14) prove (10). The polynomial quotient was canceled exactly before any absolute estimate. \(\square\) For later use, the same proof gives a local version which does not require a holomorphic function on the whole disk. Suppose \(A_N(	heta)\) is bounded and piecewise defined on the outer circle, has one \(C^2\) branch on \(|	heta|\le\delta\) for a fixed \(0<\delta<\pi\), and let \[ M_{m out}=\sup_{[-\pi,\pi]}|A_N|,\quad M_1=|A_N'(0)|,\quad M_2=\sup_{|	heta|\le\delta}|A_N''(	heta)|. \] Then \[ \left|  rac1{2\pi p_N}\int\chi_N A_N-A_N(0) ight| \le C_\delta\left\{  rac{M_1+M_2}{N} +\sqrt N\,e^{-c_\delta N}M_{m out}ight\}. 	ag{15} \] Subtract \(A_N(0)+A_N'(0)\sin	heta\) to prove this. The tail containing \(M_1\) is absorbed into \(CM_1/N\). Formula (15) estimates only the outer integral; the exact source currents for a slit function are retained in section 4. ## 3. Slowly varying actual coupons and ordinary composition **Theorem 2.** Suppose \(b_N\) is holomorphic on \(\Omega_1\) and \[ L_N=1+\sup_{\Omega_0}|b_N|=o(\sqrt N),\qquad a_N=e^{b_N}. 	ag{16} \] For its full Hermite coupon \(q_N\), uniformly in (2), \[  oxed{\quad  rac{\phi_N(q_Nf_N)} {e^{b_N(\zeta_N)}\Gamma_N} =1+O(L_N^2/N). \quad} 	ag{17} \] In particular the original observed trace is nonzero for large \(N\). It has the same exponential rate as \(\Gamma_N\), since \(|b_N(\zeta_N)|=o(N)\). **Proof.** Fixed-buffer Cauchy estimates give, on a small fixed angular arc, \[ B_N(	heta):=b_N(C_N(	heta))-b_N(\zeta_N),\quad |B_N(	heta)|\le CL_N|	heta|,\quad |B_N''(	heta)|\le CL_N . \] Taylor's formula for the exponential implies \[ \left|e^{B_N(	heta)}-1-B_N'(0)\sin	hetaight| \le C(L_N+L_N^2)	heta^2 e^{CL_N|	heta|}. 	ag{18} \] Its normalized integral against (8) is \(O(L_N^2/N)\). Indeed completing the square in \(-cN	heta^2+CL_N|	heta|\) gives the bound \[  rac1{p_N}\int	heta^2 e^{-cN	heta^2+CL_N|	heta|} \,d	heta \le  rac{C}{N}(1+L_N^2/N)e^{CL_N^2/N}=O(N^{-1}). 	ag{19} \] The linear term in (18) is \(O(L_N/N)\) by (13). On the complementary arc, the normalized integral is at most \(C\sqrt N e^{-cN+2L_N}\), which is negligible. Apply the exact formula (10) to obtain (17). \(\square\) The hypothesis is on an analytic representative, not on the coefficients of its degree-\(D\) interpolant. For example \(b_N=\lambda_N b\), with \(b\) fixed holomorphic and \(\lambda_N=o(\sqrt N)\), is allowed. This class has an exact ordinary composition law. If \(q_{N,1},\ldots,q_{N,r}\) interpolate \(e^{b_{N,1}},\ldots, e^{b_{N,r}}\), then their canonical product interpolates \(e^{\sum_
u b_{N,
u}}\), including every mixed product-rule term at the repeated roots. For fixed \(r\), condition (16) is preserved. Therefore (17) applies to this canonical product, with its actual leading coefficient \(\exp(\sum_
u b_{N,
u}(\zeta_N))\). No physical turn or additional unspecified closing map occurs in this composition assertion. For three rows on a strict macroscopic compact, the common characteristic theorem further identifies \[ \zeta_N=2-4/L(\mathbf j/N)+O(N^{-1}). 	ag{20} \] Apply its exact observed-\(C\) asymptotic and the coefficient source's observed-\(C\) formula to the same trace to prove (20). For bounded analytic coupons this replacement changes (10) by \(O(M_N/N)\); under (16) it changes the relative leading factor in (17) by \(1+O(L_N/N)\). It supplies no global continuation of the selected branch. ## 4. Poles, cuts, and the canonical remainder There is an exact version retaining every obstruction to the disk hypothesis. Let \(a_N\) be a selected holomorphic branch near all physical roots, with its full jets defining \(q_N\) as in (6). Suppose it continues to the interior of the coefficient circle after removing specified poles and cuts. Cut banks and endpoint arcs are oriented as inner boundaries of that punctured domain, so that the domain lies on their left. Assume these contours avoid the physical roots and their limiting integrals exist; otherwise keep the finite excision contours themselves. Write \(\mathscr B_N\) for the sum of the oriented inner cut-bank and endpoint integrals, and let the indicated residues be the isolated nonphysical poles. Then, exactly, \[  oxed{\quad \phi_N(q_Nf_N)=  rac{\eta N^2}{2\pi i}\oint_{m outer}  rac{a_N f_N}{P_N}\,dC+\mathscr C_N, \quad} 	ag{21} \] \[ \mathscr C_N=  rac{\eta N^2}{2\pi i}\mathscr B_N -\eta N^2 \sum_{m nonphysical\ poles} \operatorname{Res} rac{a_Nf_N}{P_N}. 	ag{22} \] This is the residue theorem on the punctured disk: its physical residues equal those of the full Hermite coupon. No external coefficient or first normal has been substituted. For a real slit \([u,v]\) directed toward the outer boundary, the two banks contribute \[ \int_u^v  rac{(a_{N,+}-a_{N,-})(C)f_N(C)}{P_N(C)}\,dC 	ag{23} \] with this orientation. Endpoint arcs remain unless their limits are proved to vanish. There is no branch reset on the outer circle; its successive arcs use the prescribed continued branch. On a cut-free saddle arc, (15) gives the exact insertion criterion \[  rac{\phi_N(q_Nf_N)}{\Gamma_N} =a_N(\zeta_N) +O_\delta\!\left( rac{M_1+M_2}{N} +\sqrt N e^{-c_\delta N}M_{m out}ight) + rac{\mathscr C_N}{\Gamma_N}. 	ag{24} \] In the disk-holomorphic case the last term is exactly zero, which is the substantive simplification in Theorems 1--2. For a general slit representative it is an original source term, not an interpolation error. A nonzero leading observation follows only if the displayed errors and the actual current are small relative to \(a_N(\zeta_N)\). The original Gaussian representative of a fixed crossing has a spectral cut at \(C\ge2\). Its canonical polynomial is entire, but replacing that polynomial on the circle by one selected Gaussian branch falls under (21)--(24), not the disk theorem. No bound on its cut current, outer-circle growth, or subsequent physical turn is supplied here. ## Complete direct sources Both complete direct texts were read at the following pins, with their used implications checked: * [Positive physical-product coefficient saddle](research_physical_products_positive_coefficient_saddle.md), SHA256 e82fea1f786383a1cfe4529573805adf5fc75a77e433e38ea609024bdeed7824: the exact coefficient source, uniform circle/variance, characteristic-function decay, and adjacent probabilities. * [Original common Jacobi characteristic](research_triple_row_common_characteristic.md), SHA256 8f1077d9d0db4797576fe039aff6621d5aa088a60fa309c661995703b23d280c: the actual observed-\(C\) asymptotic used in (20). Only written mathematics, source reads, and metadata hashes were used. No mathematical programs, tests, numerics, or builds were run. Frozen notes and public manuscripts were not edited.

text: # Exponential suppression of an analytic discrete switch 31 October 2026. This is a finite difference normal-form theorem with an explicit error. It does not identify one eigenbranch as the growth rate of a general slowly varying recurrence. Its application to the original middle-row sums requires their literal transfer and boundary data. ## 1. Analytic triangular transfer and an exact finite construction Let \(I=[a,b]\), \(U_R=\{z\in\mathbb C:\operatorname{dist}(z,I)<R\}\), and let the bounded analytic block matrix \[ T(t)=\begin{pmatrix}A(t)&B(t)\\0&C(t)\end{pmatrix} \tag{1} \] be given on \(U_R\). Rectangular off-diagonal blocks are allowed. Assume the Sylvester operator \[ \mathcal S_t(X)=XC(t)-A(t)X \] has a bounded analytic inverse on \(U_R\). Fix compatible matrix norms. Put \[ H_0(t)=\mathcal S_t^{-1}B(t),\qquad \mathcal L_t(X)=\mathcal S_t^{-1}(A(t)X), \quad K=\sup_{U_R}\|\mathcal L_t\|, \quad M_0=\sup_{U_R}\|H_0(t)\|. \] For a positive mesh \(h\), define the EXACT difference operator \[ (\mathcal F_h H)(t)=\mathcal L_t\,[H(t-h)-H(t)] \] and its finite sum \[ H^{[m]}=\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}\mathcal F_h^j H_0, \qquad P_h(t)=\begin{pmatrix}I&H^{[m]}(t)\\0&I\end{pmatrix}. \tag{2} \] All shifts in this expression are literal. No convergent infinite formal series, interpolated solution of a difference equation, or summability theorem is assumed. Direct multiplication gives \[ P_h(t)^{-1}T(t)P_h(t-h) =\begin{pmatrix}A(t)&R_h(t)\\0&C(t)\end{pmatrix}, \qquad R_h(t)=\mathcal S_t\bigl(\mathcal F_h^mH_0(t)\bigr). \tag{3} \] Indeed the off-diagonal block is \(B-\mathcal S_tH^{[m]}+A(H^{[m]}(t-h)-H^{[m]}(t))\), and the finite geometric identity \(H^{[m]}-\mathcal F_hH^{[m]}=H_0-\mathcal F_h^mH_0\) proves (3). ## 2. An exponentially small residual with a bounded gauge Choose \[ m=\left\lfloor\frac{R}{8(K+1)h}\right\rfloor\ge1, \qquad \sigma=\frac{R}{2m}. \tag{4} \] For a function analytic on \(U_r\), Cauchy's derivative bound on the segment from \(t-h\) to \(t\) gives, when \(h\le\sigma/2\), \[ \|H(t-h)-H(t)\|_{U_{r-\sigma}} \le \frac{2h}{\sigma}\|H\|_{U_r}. \] There are \(m\) nested domains between \(U_R\) and \(U_{R/2}\). Consequently each application of \(\mathcal F_h\) costs at most \[ q=\frac{4Khm}{R}\le\frac{K}{2(K+1)}<\frac12. \] The choice (4) also ensures \(h\le\sigma/2\). Thus on \(U_{R/2}\), \[ \|H^{[m]}\|\le2M_0,\qquad \|R_h\|\le M_0\sup_{U_R}\|\mathcal S_t\|\,2^{-m} \le C_0e^{-c/h}, \quad c=\frac{R\log2}{8(K+1)}. \tag{5} \] One may take \(C_0=2M_0\sup\|\mathcal S_t\|\). The matrices \(P_h,P_h^{-1}\) are uniformly bounded. If the coefficients also depend analytically on parameters on a compact complex neighborhood, the same construction and constants work uniformly after shrinking that neighborhood. Only the stated Sylvester separation is needed; eigenvalues within either diagonal block may coincide or vanish. ## 3. The full product retains both endpoint contributions Take \(t_j=t_0+jh\), \(j=1,\ldots,n\), all in \(I\), with \(nh\le L\) fixed. Write \(A_j=A(t_j)\), \(C_j=C(t_j)\), \(H_j=H^{[m]}(t_j)\), and use identity matrices for empty products. Let \(S_n\) be the off-diagonal block of \(T_n\cdots T_1\). The block triangular product has at most one off-diagonal transition, so (3) gives the exact identity \[ \boxed{\displaystyle S_n=H_n(C_n\cdots C_1)-(A_n\cdots A_1)H_0 +\sum_{j=1}^n A_n\cdots A_{j+1}\,R_h(t_j)\, C_{j-1}\cdots C_1.} \tag{6} \] In (6), \(H_0\) denotes the gauge at \(t_0\), not the zeroth term \(\mathcal S^{-1}B\) used in (2). Define the possible switch amplification \[ \Omega_n=\max_{1\le j\le n} \|A_n\cdots A_{j+1}\|\, \|C_{j-1}\cdots C_1\|. \] Then \[ \|S_n\|\le2M_0\bigl(\|A_n\cdots A_1\| +\|C_n\cdots C_1\|\bigr) +nC_0e^{-c/h}\Omega_n. \tag{7} \] In particular, if the two pure endpoint products satisfy \[ \|A_n\cdots A_1\|+\|C_n\cdots C_1\| \le C_1e^{-\gamma/h}\Omega_n, \qquad\gamma>0, \] then \(\|S_n\|\le C_2(1+n)e^{-\min(c,\gamma)/h}\Omega_n\). This is a strict exponential loss relative to the absolute interior-switch envelope. The residual term in (7) can still dominate both pure products. It would be false to infer from this theorem that the growth is always one diagonal branch's action. ## 4. Scalar phase separation For scalar blocks \(a,c\), the Sylvester hypothesis is just \(c-a\ne0\) on a fixed complex neighborhood. If on the real interval \[ a(t)=e^{i\theta_a}a_+(t),\qquad c(t)=e^{i\theta_c}c_+(t),\qquad m_*\le a_+,c_+\le M_*, \] and \(|\sin((\theta_a-\theta_c)/2)|\ge\varepsilon>0\), then \[ |a(t)-c(t)|\ge2m_*\varepsilon. \] Analyticity and uniform bounds extend this separation to a sufficiently small fixed complex neighborhood. Thus a nonzero relative phase gives the required analytic gap even when \(|a|=|c|\) on the real interval. With a scalar positive coupling \(b_+(t)\) bounded above and below, the corresponding positive switch sum has size between constant multiples of \(\Omega_n\) and \(n\Omega_n\). Hence (7) proves exponential cancellation relative to that positive sum whenever its maximizing switch has a fixed rate gap from both endpoints. Constant phases on the coupling do not affect this comparison. ## 5. Interface with the original source The [positive tail transfer](research_positive_eta_word_transfer.md) supplies an exact two-state active block for the original spectral continuant. Before and after that block, the source carries the actual middle powers, unused row factors, and the retained omitted-half scalar modes. The [literal four-state dictionary](research_original_one_sided_four_state_transfer.md) now applies (3) directly to a mismatched middle phase. The [regular-window theorem](research_regular_spectral_window_phase_exclusion.md) checks full block separation and both endpoint gaps, without a guessed analytic interpolation of discrete endpoints. In particular it excludes a collision with the secondary eigenvalue as well as the Perron eigenvalue. Those regular windows include exact sampled zeros in common retained factors. Protected degeneracies, spectral caps and boundary maxima still require separate estimates. An inconsistent shared phase system gives an exponential improvement relative to its specified window envelope; no general comparison of that envelope with hyperbolic volume is claimed.

title: A compact positive variational formula for Conway knot sources
text: # A compact positive variational formula for Conway knot sources 21 November 2026. Research note; previous finals and public manuscripts remain unchanged. A finite Conway construction has an explicit tensor compiler with output \((1,K_N)\), where \(K_N\) is its original reduced Kashaev invariant. The constant coordinate is kept orthogonal to the physical boundary space. It supplies an anchor even when \(K_N=0\), without introducing ordinary main colors. This note gives a compact quartic minimization whose value \(Q_N\) satisfies \[ 1+|K_N|^2\le Q_N\le(1+1/N)(1+|K_N|^2). \tag{1} \] For a fixed expression with \(m\) tensor vertices, the minimization has \(2N(m-1)\) real variables, and its degree is at most four, independently of \(m\) and \(N\). The objective is an explicit positive sum of squared local transport residuals. The theorem is quantitative weighted Cauchy--Schwarz; its proof does not require the reference-coordinate or matrix interpretations. Those interpretations give an exact boundary inner product and four positive local norm factors below. Joint convexity and a hyperbolic-volume limit are not proved for the quartic problem. ## 1. The original complete boundary packet Fix \(N\ge2\), and put \[ d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\quad \kappa=q^{d^2/2},\quad c_j=q^{2j+1}+q^{-2j-1}, \] \[ s_0=1,\qquad s_r=\prod_{u=1}^r2\sin(\pi u/N). \] All fractional powers mean these displayed exponentials. Use the full actual pair algebra and its normalized Newton basis \[ H_N=\mathbb C[z]/(2T_N(z/2)+2),\qquad b_r=\frac{\prod_{j=0}^{r-1}(c_j-z)}{s_r^2}, \quad 0\le r\le d. \tag{2} \] Here \(T_N\) is the Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind. We identify \(H_N\) with its \(N\)-dimensional coefficient space in (2), with the Euclidean Hermitian norm. The quotient retains the value and first derivative at every double root; no normal direction is discarded. The actual turn and multiplication are \[ Jb_r=b_{d-r},\qquad M(f,g)=fg\pmod{2T_N(z/2)+2}. \] In coefficient coordinates, \[ M(b_i,b_j)=\sum_r\mu_{ijr}b_r,\qquad \mu_{ijr}=\frac{s_{i+j}s_r} {s_i s_j s_{r-i}s_{r-j}s_{i+j-r}} \tag{3} \] when \(i+j\le d\) and \(\max(i,j)\le r\le i+j\). All other coefficients are zero, including products with \(i+j\ge N\). The physical signed crossing coupons are \[ R^{\pm1}=\kappa^{\pm1}\sum_{r=0}^d(-q)^{\pm r}b_r. \tag{4} \] These are the full repeated-root identities of the [Newton source theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_newton_turn_positive_gram.md) and [Conway compiler](research_conway_full_boundary_quotient_gram.md). Take a fixed literal tangle expression made from these signed crossings, identity coupons, products and quarter-turns. Its ordered, oriented closure is assumed to be one knot, with the original reduced marking and zero-framing convention. Let \(f_E\in H_N\) be its actual open boundary packet. Write its exact original closing row as \(\ell_N\), so that \[ K_N=\ell_N f_E. \tag{5} \] For the two normalized Newton closures, this is the appropriate row \(e_0^{\mathsf T}\) or \(e_d^{\mathsf T}\), with the known framing and normalization line retained in it. Framing contributes a root phase. Any recorded fixed power of \(N\) is also kept in \(\ell_N\). In particular \(\log^+\|\ell_N\|=O(\log N)\) for a fixed diagram, where \(\log^+x=\max(0,\log x)\). ## 2. An orthogonal constant reference Give every internal edge the space \[ \widehat H_N=\mathbb C e_\star\oplus H_N, \] with its orthogonal direct-sum inner product. The symbol \(e_\star\) denotes a separate reference coordinate. It is not the physical algebraic unit \(b_0\): indeed \(Jb_0=b_d\). Compile the expression using the following actual linear or multilinear maps: \[ \widehat f=(1,f)\quad\hbox{at a leaf},\qquad \widehat J(a,u)=(a,Ju), \tag{6} \] \[ \widehat M((a,u),(b,v))=(ab,M(u,v)),\qquad \widehat\ell_N(a,u)=(a,\ell_Nu)\in\mathbb C^2. \tag{7} \] The mixed reference/physical input sectors of \(\widehat M\) are zero. Thus induction through the tree gives open packet \((1,f_E)\) and final output \[ Y_N=(1,K_N),\qquad \|Y_N\|^2=1+|K_N|^2. \tag{8} \] Every coefficient of these gates is prescribed before the closed invariant is evaluated. The quantum invariant in the second coordinate has not been changed. Let the compiler tree have \(m\ge2\) vertices, including its closing map. Its root has depth zero. For an edge \(e\), let \(r_e\) be the depth of its child vertex. Let \(T_{v,N}\) be the coefficient tensor at vertex \(v\). Its squared Hilbert--Schmidt norm is the sum of the squared absolute values of all its coefficients. Put \[ B_N=\prod_v\|T_{v,N}\|_{\rm HS},\qquad t_N=B_N^2\sqrt{3mN/2}. \tag{9} \] Each tensor has a reference coefficient equal to one, so \(B_N\ge1\). Both numbers in (9) are explicit functions of the original local data. ## 3. Boundary translations and the corresponding inner product For \(w\in H_N\), define \[ S(-w)(a,u)=(a,u-aw),\qquad D_r(t)(a,u)=(a,t^ru),\qquad g_e=D_{r_e}(t_N)S(-w_e). \tag{10} \] These are invertible for every \(w_e\); the inverse translation is \(S(w_e)\). In fact \((S(-w)-I)^2=0\). At each edge apply \(g_e\) to the child output and its inverse to the parent's argument. The bilinear edge pairing and the output (8) are preserved exactly. The positive inner product on that edge is particularly simple: \[ \boxed{\quad \|(a,u)\|_{e,w}^2 =|a|^2+t_N^{2r_e}\|u-aw_e\|^2. \quad} \tag{11} \] Its Gram matrix is \[ \begin{pmatrix} 1+t_N^{2r_e}\|w_e\|^2&-t_N^{2r_e}w_e^*\\ -t_N^{2r_e}w_e&t_N^{2r_e}I_N \end{pmatrix}>0. \] The anchored line through \((1,w_e)\) is orthogonal to every physical variation \((0,h)\). The physical space remains full dimensional. When \(w_e\) is the true proper boundary packet, this is an exact orthogonality adapted to that packet, with no normalization by \(K_N\). ## 4. Explicit positive local factors For \(w\in H_N\), let \(M_w:H_N\to H_N\) be multiplication by \(w\). Keep \(t=t_N\) in the following formulas. They give the exact squared Hilbert--Schmidt norms of the gauged tensors. At a leaf of depth \(r\), with its original packet \(f\) and outgoing translation \(w\), the factor is \[ 1+t^{2r}\|f-w\|^2. \tag{12} \] At a turn vertex of depth \(r\), write \(w_c\) for its child translation and \(w_p\) for its outgoing translation. The factor is \[ 1+t^{2r}\|Jw_c-w_p\|^2+t^{-2}\|J\|_{\rm HS}^2. \tag{13} \] At a multiplication vertex of depth \(r\), the factor is \[ \begin{split} 1&+t^{2r}\|M(w_L,w_R)-w_p\|^2\\ &+t^{-2}\bigl(\|M_{w_L}\|_{\rm HS}^2+ \|M_{w_R}\|_{\rm HS}^2\bigr) +t^{-2r-4}\|M\|_{\rm HS}^2. \tag{14} \end{split} \] Here \(w_L,w_R\) are its two child translations. Finally the original closing vertex contributes \[ 1+|\ell_Nw_c|^2+t^{-2}\|\ell_N\|^2. \tag{15} \] To check these identities, the incoming inverse at a child edge of depth \(r+1\) is \(S(w_c)D_{r+1}(t)^{-1}\). It sends \((a,u)\) to \((a,aw_c+t^{-r-1}u)\). Substitute this expression into (6)--(7), then apply the outgoing map in (10). For a product, the physical output is \[ ab\,t^r\{M(w_L,w_R)-w_p\} +t^{-1}\{aM(w_L,v)+bM(u,w_R)\} +t^{-r-2}M(u,v). \] The input sectors reference/reference, reference/physical, physical/reference and physical/physical are orthogonal. Summing their squared coefficient norms gives (14), with no discarded cross term. The other formulas follow from the same substitution. ## 5. A compact quartic minimum Write \(s=m-1\), the number of proper vertices, or equivalently edges. Attach a variable \(w_v\in H_N\) to each proper vertex's outgoing edge. Let \(v_0\) denote the root's unique child. The residual at a proper vertex is \[ \mathcal R_v(\boldsymbol w)= \begin{cases} f_v-w_v,&v\text{ is a leaf with prescribed packet }f_v,\\ Jw_c-w_v,&v\text{ is a turn with child }c,\\ M(w_L,w_R)-w_v,&v\text{ is a product with children }L,R. \end{cases} \tag{16} \] Every residual is known explicitly from the original operations. Put \[ c_v=B_N^{2r_v-1},\qquad \mathcal A_N(\boldsymbol w)=\sum_{v\ne\mathrm{root}} c_v^2\|\mathcal R_v(\boldsymbol w)\|^2, \tag{17} \] \[ \mathcal J_N(\boldsymbol w) =1+|\ell_Nw_{v_0}|^2+Ns\mathcal A_N(\boldsymbol w), \qquad \boxed{\quad Q_N=(1+1/N) \min_{\|w_v\|^2\le B_N^2}\mathcal J_N(\boldsymbol w).\quad} \tag{18} \] This is a positive real polynomial problem on \(2N(m-1)\) real variables. Its degree is at most four: a product residual is bilinear in its two child variables before its squared norm is taken. Its coefficients and ball radii are algebraic at each level. The nonempty compact domain makes the minimum exist. The factor \(t_N\) from the inner-product construction is not used in (16)--(18). **Theorem.** The quartic minimum (18) satisfies (1) for every \(N\ge2\). **Proof.** Let \(f_v\) be the true open packet of the proper subtree rooted at \(v\). Repeated Cauchy--Schwarz in its anchored compiler gives \(\|(1,f_v)\|\le B_N\); every omitted vertex norm is at least one. In particular \(\|f_v\|\le B_N\). At every product vertex present, \(\|M\|_{\rm op}\le B_N\); also \(\|\ell_N\|\le B_N\) and \(\|J\|_{\rm op}=1\). These bounds are all that the proof uses from the compiler. They can instead be checked directly for any chosen larger bound \(B_N\ge1\). For every allowed collection \(\boldsymbol w\), define \(d_v=\|f_v-w_v\|\). At a leaf, \(d_v=\|\mathcal R_v\|\). At a turn or product, \[ d_v\le\|\mathcal R_v\|+B_N^2\sum_{c\text{ child of }v}d_c. \] For a product, this follows from the exact bilinear identity \[ M(f_L,f_R)-M(w_L,w_R) =M(f_L-w_L,f_R)+M(w_L,f_R-w_R) \] and the bounds \(\|f_R\|,\|w_L\|\le B_N\). Following the unique path from each vertex to the root and using \(\|\ell_N\|\le B_N\) therefore gives \[ |K_N-\ell_Nw_{v_0}| \le\sum_{v\ne\mathrm{root}}B_N^{2r_v-1}\|\mathcal R_v\| \le\sqrt{s\mathcal A_N}. \tag{19} \] The weighted Cauchy inequality \((a+b)^2\le(1+1/N)(a^2+Nb^2)\) for nonnegative \(a,b\) now proves \(1+|K_N|^2\le(1+1/N)\mathcal J_N(\boldsymbol w)\). For the reverse bound choose \(w_v=f_v\). This is allowed, every residual vanishes, and \(\mathcal J_N=1+|K_N|^2\). This proves (1). No step divides by a closed invariant. \(\square\) If two such compilers give the same original \(K_N\), then \[ |\log Q_N-\log Q_N'|\le\log(1+1/N)\le1/N. \tag{20} \] Both logarithms lie in the same interval of that length. This includes replacing a fixed proper subtree by its full open boundary packet and retaining its original normalization. The raw polynomial objectives need not agree pointwise. A different valid packet bound \(B_N\) also changes the logarithmic minimum by at most the same amount. ## 6. The product of local norm factors The four factors (12)--(15) give a second, less economical minimum. Let \(\Phi_N(\boldsymbol w)\) be their product and define \[ P_N=\min_{\|w_e\|^2\le B_N^2}\Phi_N(\boldsymbol w). \] It has the same number of variables as (18), but degree at most \(4m\). It satisfies the exact bounds \[ 1+|K_N|^2\le P_N\le e^{2/N}(1+|K_N|^2). \tag{21} \] For the lower bound, gauges preserve the original output \(Y_N\), and leaf-by-leaf Cauchy--Schwarz bounds its squared norm by \(\Phi_N\). For the upper bound, use \(w_e=f_e\). All transport residuals vanish. Every original local norm is at most \(B_N\), and \(\|M_{f_e}\|_{\rm HS}\le\|M\|_{\rm HS}\|f_e\|\le B_N^2\). A leaf factor is one, a turn factor is at most \(1+B_N^2/t_N^2\), and a product factor is at most \(1+3B_N^4/t_N^2\), because \(r\ge1\) and \(t_N\ge1\). The root factor is at most \(\|Y_N\|^2(1+B_N^2/t_N^2)\). Consequently \[ \Phi_N((f_e)_e)\le\|Y_N\|^2 \exp(3mB_N^4/t_N^2)=e^{2/N}\|Y_N\|^2. \] Two exact presentations therefore have \(|\log P_N-\log P_N'|\le2/N\). The product lower bound has a polynomial sum-of-squares certificate. For a leaf vector \(a\) and neighboring tensor \(T_{iI}\), \[ \|a\|^2\|T\|_{\rm HS}^2-\|a^{\mathsf T}T\|^2 =\sum_{I,\,i<j}|\overline a_iT_{jI} -\overline a_jT_{iI}|^2. \tag{22} \] Apply (22) successively and multiply each defect by the squared norms of the other vertices, themselves sums of squares. Telescoping gives a real polynomial sum-of-squares expression for \(\Phi_N(\boldsymbol w)-1-|K_N|^2\). The entries are polynomials in \(w_e,\overline w_e\) with \(t_N\) fixed. This certifies the finite lower inequality (21); it supplies no geometric lower bound. ## 7. Growth of the source constants The elementary identities \(s_d=N\) and \(s_as_{d-a}=N\) imply \(N2^{-d}\le s_a\le2^d\). Formula (3) consequently gives the coarse bound \(\mu_{ijr}\le2^{7d}\), and hence \(\|M\|_{\rm HS}\le N^{3/2}2^{7d}\). The crossing leaves in (4) have norm \(\sqrt N\); the turn is unitary. Together with the known closing row this proves, for each fixed literal construction, \[ \log B_N=O(N),\qquad\log t_N=O(N). \tag{23} \] Fixed signed powers can first be expanded into signed crossing leaves. The constants may depend on those fixed powers and on the construction. ## 8. The remaining geometric statement For any \(V>0\), (1) gives \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac\pi N\log Q_N=V \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}N\log|K_N|=V. \tag{24} \] Indeed \(\log(1+|K_N|^2)\) differs from \(\max(0,2\log|K_N|)\) by at most \(\log2\), including zeros with \(\log0=-\infty\). A strictly positive limiting rate removes that maximum and implies eventual nonvanishing. This construction uses the complete physical packet and an orthogonal constant reference. It requires no estimate for ordinary colors, and no identification of an auxiliary-circle Fourier norm with a main-color norm. All physical normal directions and the original closing row remain. The translations form the additive group of \(H_N\), since \(S(u)S(v)=S(u+v)\); their square-zero off-diagonal block supplies the elementary boundary centering used in the proof. To prove the proposed volume theorem one must still compare the leading value of this actual positive polynomial problem with hyperbolic volume. For the finite-exception program, that comparison is needed after every required fixed short partial assignment and sufficiently long remaining fillings which give hyperbolic knots. Fixed short subtrees can be contracted exactly before applying the construction. No geometric comparison, regulator identification, or new volume-equality class is inferred from (24) alone. ## Complete direct sources The complete matching texts were read. The first two give the actual physical operations and source conventions; the third records the earlier full-matrix filtering construction for comparison. The quartic theorem, orthogonal reference, division-free translations and explicit polynomial factors are proved above; the full-matrix argument is not a prerequisite. * [Complete Conway compiler](research_conway_full_boundary_quotient_gram.md): `debe56dbad8151b90d44d0fccbf0dcf33dafb780370e01c8acdadbd2939dc077`. * [Actual Newton turn, crossing and source](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_newton_turn_positive_gram.md): `d8b21fa8db909120035e86e997a0e02cb84f8dce2dcf6fb244bb5c85c17e28a3`. * [Earlier quantitative metric bound](research_regularized_source_metric_compactness.md): `fd8dae7561eff37089e8481b4eb8c8344acb56da86b502350292f6d2be9c8818`. Only written mathematics and text operations were used. No mathematical program, test, build, git operation or public-document edit was performed.

title: Every original MAIN edge gives the same full marked coefficient
text: # Every original MAIN edge gives the same full marked coefficient 31 October 2026. , unpublished finite source theorem. This extends the existing top-cap statement by an actual spherical rerouting and a general Morse compiler. It does not insert a newly reset mark into an internal head of the old presentation. No source sector or absolute envelope is transported. ## 1. Statement and exact scope Fix a connected complete-colored flat-plat source with R recorded boxes, N>=3, d=N-1, q_N=exp(pi i/N). Each original box carries its full matrix f_e(Omega) R_e^(epsilon_e), epsilon_e in {0,+1,-1}, in the original order, with the full Cartan/crossing scalar. The f_e are arbitrary finite polynomials; their coefficients may depend on N and on additional spectral parameters. Let H_e be their original homogeneous face polynomials, of degree d. Treat the crossing as its actual root polynomial only when forming H_e; its auxiliary generic lift below uses the actual finite universal crossing. Keep the actual labeled plane matching graph and its ordered quartet (x_e,b_e,c_e,y_e) at each box. Set P(L)=product_e H_e(L_xe,L_be,L_ce,L_ye), deg P=dR. For an original MAIN edge separating distinct faces a,b, put Z_(a,b)=[product_(f!=a,b)L_f^d] P |_(L_a=L_b=0). (1) Then Z_(a,b) equals the original top-cap-marked scalar, with the same full finite normalization. In particular it is independent of the MAIN edge, including edges on different complete-colored components. A fixed recorded exterior framing or component character multiplies both sides equally. No component-dependent normalization is introduced. The graph connectedness here is the projection connectedness already needed by the face compiler. MAIN edges have distinct adjacent faces in the intended certified simple-white class. More generally that property also follows by contracting each matching edge: the resulting connected 4-valent graph has no bridge, since every vertex degree is even. The theorem includes the full cleared numerator V_N(sigma), all its root Hermite data, both level parities and composite levels. It is not an equality for individual LEFT/CROSS/RIGHT projections, which are not the intertwiners used in the proof. Equation (1) does not claim that every choice of edge passes a geometric or absolute-source certificate. ## 2. A regular generic pivotal lift which matches the root exactly Hold N fixed and use a variable q on a neighborhood of q_N, with the same local square-root choice for Cartan factors. Work in the category generated by finite-dimensional integral highest-weight U_q(sl2) modules, tensor products, duals and direct sums. Write H for the integral weight operator and K=q^H. Define z=(-1)^H, g_tilde=zK. (2) E and F shift H by two, so z is central. It is group-like because the tensor-product weight is the sum, and z^2=1. Since the actual antipodes give S^2=Ad K, g_tilde implements the same S^2 and is a valid pivotal structure. On V_L and its dual, z=(-1)^L. At q=q_N, on EVERY integral weight, including tensor-product weights, q_N^(-NH)=(-1)^H, g_tilde=q_N^((1-N)H)=K^(1-N)=g. (3) Thus this auxiliary pivot specializes literally to the original pivot. It is not the generic ADO expression K^(1-N), which would not implement S^2 at generic q. No identity of their transverse derivatives is used. The regular complete-color lift is the ordinary highest-weight module V_d with K v_i=q^(d-2i)v_i, Fv_i=v_(i+1), Ev_i=[i]_q[N-i]_q v_(i-1), and endpoint arrows zero. Its self-duality is J(q)v_i=(-1)^i q^(i(i-N)) v_(d-i)^*. (4) Directly, the F equation is c_(i+1)=-q^(-d+2i)c_i, and the E,K equations agree. At the root c_i=q_N^(i^2), the specified actual duality. The balanced basis v_i/(q^2;q^2)_i is regular at q_N, since i<N. So are J, its inverse and all four g_tilde-pivotal turns. In the unbalanced self-dual frame one also checks directly J(q)^(-t)J(q)=(-1)^d K=g_tilde on V_d: its i-th diagonal entry is c_i/c_(d-i)=(-1)^d q^(d-2i). Thus the chosen generic double-dual frame already has the displayed pivot, not a missing sign. Extend each f_e by holding its coefficients fixed and using Omega(q). The actual R and R^(-1) have finite sums with factorial denominators [h]_q!, h<N, all units at q_N. Hence the original full box matrices are regular Hopf intertwiners in these exact local frames. For V_N one may use the polynomial [chi_N(sigma)-chi_N(z)]/(sigma-z), chi_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2, and only at the root use chi_N(Omega)=0. No generic resolvent or simple-node interpolation replaces the numerator. ## 3. Sphericality for every generic endomorphism used here The two pivotal traces for any endomorphism A in this tensor-generated category are Tr(g_tilde A), Tr(g_tilde^(-1) A). (5) They agree, not only on one complete simple module. Here is an elementary proof that also specifies what is not specialized at the root. For real q>0, q!=1, use the involution K*=K, E*=KF, F*=EK^(-1). It is compatible with the actual coproducts Delta E=E tensor K+1 tensor E and Delta F=F tensor 1+K^(-1) tensor F. On V_L give consecutive basis vectors positive squared norms n_0=1, n_i=[i]_q[L-i+1]_q q^(-L+2i)n_(i-1). These make precisely E*=KF; the remaining adjoint identities follow. Tensor-product norms give finite-dimensional unitary representations. Duals are unitarizable as well: the regular generic J identifies the dual of V_L with the corresponding V_L, and the transported positive norm gives the same adjoint relations. Reversed tensor products of these duals therefore remain in the same finite unitary category. Every invariant subspace has invariant orthogonal complement, since the adjoints of the generators remain in the represented algebra. For completeness, every irreducible summand is V_L with L a nonnegative integer. Choose a highest-weight vector of weight L; the commutation relations give E F^i v=[i]_q[L-i+1]_q F^(i-1)v. If r is the first zero F^r v, then [r]_q[L-r+1]_q=0. For real q>0 this forces r=L+1. The preceding ladder has distinct weights and spans the irreducible summand. Thus an arbitrary intertwiner on a tensor-generated object has blocks A=direct_sum_L (I_(V_L) tensor A_L). On such a block, both traces in (5) equal (-1)^L [L+1]_q Tr(A_L), because the weights L,L-2,...,-L are symmetric. Summing proves (5) for every endomorphism, including non-scalar multiplicity blocks. The original matrix entries and any specified generic endomorphism are rational in q^(1/2), with fixed complex coefficients. Identity on an interval of positive real q therefore proves the generic rational identity. This is sphericality for the category and maps actually used. Only the original regular finite matrices are later specialized at q_N. Neither the irreducible decomposition nor its projections are specialized; they may be singular there. In particular this proof discards no root nilpotent or Jordan datum. ## 4. Rerouting with all coupon disks and frames fixed Regard the original source as a ribbon graph on the oriented sphere, with each actual box contained in a small parametrized closed disk. These disks include every retained crossing, its local ordered inputs and outputs and its blackboard ribbon framing. They are kept fixed pointwise throughout the following construction. Choose a point p in face a outside the disks. A path from p to the old point at infinity can be chosen outside all coupon disks and transverse to finitely many MAIN arcs, missing their endpoints. A smooth vector field in a thin neighborhood of this path moves p to the old point at infinity, while fixing every coupon disk. Its time maps are orientation-preserving sphere diffeomorphisms. The image graph misses the new infinity because p was not on the graph. Thus it gives a plane presentation with a as its exterior face and the SAME ordered local coupon frames. No crossing is created; the ribbon framing is transported inside the sphere, with no normal twist. Only MAIN arcs are crossed: the disjoint coupon disks contain the matching edges, and their complement in the sphere is connected. The selected edge is incident to this unbounded face. Take a short subarc of it and a simple path through that face to a region above all coupon disks and the rest of the compact drawing. A thin rectangular neighborhood of the path is disjoint from the graph except at the chosen subarc. Push that subarc along the rectangle, leaving two parallel sides joined by a semicircular tip. This is an ordinary planar finger isotopy of an arc, not a new cup/cap component or a crossing. Its tip is an exposed top cap. Outside it is a; inside it is the same face b, extended along the thin strip. The coupon disks stay fixed. A small perturbation of the remaining arcs makes the presentation Morse. It need not be a flat plat. These operations have a finite tensor description. Away from passages of the outside point across a MAIN arc, ordinary planar isotopy is generated by tensor interchange and the four actual snake identities; their J and g_tilde factors cancel exactly. When the outside point passes a MAIN arc, the two plane readings close the same correctly bent endomorphism by its two pivotal traces. Equation (5) makes them equal. The cut boundary is transported by these turns, not assigned a new matrix in its old internal basis. This proves that the rerouted generic CLOSED scalar is the original one. All R/Cartan factors remain inside the fixed coupon disks. Leave the exposed cap open. The remaining network is a Hopf map to V_d tensor V_d^* or its reversed order. Under the actual cup/duality it is an endomorphism of V_d (or its dual). Generically it is a scalar a_(a,b)(q)I: distinct K weights force a commuting endomorphism to be diagonal, and the nonzero F arrows force equal diagonal entries. This scalar is regular at q_N, being one entry of a regular open network after the regular cup identification. Closing it with the corresponding ordinary cap gives Z_closed(q)=(-1)^d[N]_q a_(a,b)(q). (6) The same generic closed scalar is obtained with any original top cap left open, and its dimension factor is the same. Since [N]_q!=0 generically, their regular open scalars agree. They agree at q_N by specialization. No root quantum dimension is divided by zero. For a right cap use the original reduced defect g_tilde^(-1)e; for a left cap use g_tilde e, where Tr(e)=1 in the actual boundary basis. Their marked evaluations of the scalar open map are both a_(a,b)(q). At q_N these are the actual root turns/marks by (3). Therefore the rerouted marked scalar equals the old top-cap-marked scalar exactly. There is no further root sign to insert: the auxiliary pivot already matches g. In the original flat presentation it reproduces the old standard-K conversion factor (-1)^(d(k-1)) automatically. ## 5. Exact ordered root turns in the new Morse presentation The whole face compiler can now be repeated; it is not inferred from the old flat-gap sweep. Put x0=q_N^d and Q=q_N^2. The original balanced left/right matrices are ev_L(a,b)=x0^a/N delta_(a+b,d), coev_L(b,a)=N x0^(-a) delta_(a+b,d), ev_R(b,a)=x0^a g_b/N delta_(a+b,d), coev_R(a,b)=N x0^(-a)g_b^(-1) delta_(a+b,d), g_b=q_N^(-d^2-2b). In their literal left-to-right ordered physical pair (i,j), ALL four are exactly cup(i,j)=N q_N^(-d^2+di) delta_(i+j,d), cap(i,j)=N^(-1) q_N^(di) delta_(i+j,d). (7) For the right cap the ratio to (7) is q_N^(-2Ni)=1; for the right cup it is q_N^(2N(d-i))=1. No local logarithmic lift is reset. The two marked arrays are genuinely different off support: mark_R(i,j)=x0^j/N^2, mark_L(i,j)=x0^i g_(d-i)/N^2. (8) Each contracts to one with its corresponding original cup. With one cap exposed, global unwrapped degree conservation forces i+j=d: all boxes preserve total head degree, each cup supplies d and every other cap consumes d. On this forced support the two arrays (8) both equal N^(-2)q_N^(dj). This is not an early restriction of the mark. ## 6. Winding gives the unchanged P and exactly the two missing targets At each fixed box the existing full homogeneous matrix adapter remains matrix_e=N^(-1) H_e(x,b,c,y)/(bc)^(d/2). (9) Its local ordered frame was never changed. In the centered face lift, a physical head along a vertical segment is i=d/2+N(Log L_left-Log L_right)/(2pi i). At a cup or cap the first head sees the outside face o and inside z, so q_N^(di)=q_N^(d^2/2)(L_o/L_z)^(d/2). Let M_f count the original input/output middle incidences in face f. Let T_f count +1 for the outside of every ordinary physical turn and -1 for its inside, including the cap to be marked at this stage. In this GENERAL Morse presentation one has M_f-T_f=2 for f!=a, M_a-T_a=-2. (10) Here is the turning proof. Traverse each face boundary with the face on its left, rounding repeated boundary passages by a thin regular neighborhood when necessary. Inside a fixed box, take the same local planar resolution as the original input/output matching pair. Its net boundary turn is +pi at each middle face and zero at each outer face: the two middle passages reverse the vertical tangent, while each outer passage continues it. Along a Morse arc, an inside U-turn contributes +pi and its outside passage -pi. All remaining arc segments have zero net turn after a vertical-tangent deformation; this can equally be read as the signed crossing count of the horizontal tangent direction. Thus total boundary turn is pi(M_f-T_f). The bounded-face boundary has winding +1, and the exterior boundary winding -1. This proves (10), including repeated face labels by counting each occurrence. It does not require every turn to lie above or below every coupon. Multiplying (7),(9), the ordinary face character is therefore product_f L_f^((d/2)(T_f-M_f)) =L_a^d product_(f!=a)L_f^(-d). (11) At the exposed marked cap the original second head gives mark/cap=N^(-1)(L_b/L_a)^d. (12) Both a,b characters cancel; every other face has exponent -d. If the new Morse presentation has k' cups, it also has k' caps. The turn constants are N^(k')N^(-(k'-1))N^(-2)=N^(-1). Their q_N^(d^2/2) head constants cancel the k' cup constants q_N^(-d^2), exactly. The whole literal marked summand is consequently N^(-R-1) P(L)/product_(f!=a,b)L_f^d. (13) All half powers have assembled into integer face exponents. This establishes the coefficient CHARACTER with the same polynomial P, not a rotated, smoothed or independently renormalized local coupon. ## 7. Primitive grids, actual support and the unique alias Adding degree-two bends changes neither the closed graph's cycle lattice nor its dimension. Centering a head by d/2 turns the support i+j=d at a bend into a sign reversal. At a fixed box, unwrapped total conservation gives the actual divergence equation. Hence the integral homogeneous source lattice is still the divergence-free lattice of the same connected graph. On a sphere it is integrally isomorphic to face-potential differences modulo one common constant: integrate an integer flow along dual paths; its sum around a dual face is precisely the original vertex divergence, and every closed dual walk is generated by these face boundaries. No finite-index Jacobian is introduced. There are R+2 white faces, so fixing L_a=1 leaves R+1 independent N-point grids. At odd N the centered heads have integral offsets and the grids are L_f=Q^(p_f). At even N use the original cocycle whose value is one on MAIN edges and zero on MATCHING edges. Each shaded triangle has two MAIN edges, so it integrates to face parities t_f; set t_a=0 and take L_f=q_N^(t_f)Q^(p_f), p_f in Z/N. (14) In particular t_b=1. These are the same actual half-index offsets in the rerouted frame, not new independent choices of local carries. Every grid point gives canonical physical heads in {0,...,d}. First apply the established canonical physical support of the full-polynomial adapter (9), including its original endpoint zeros; it kills any failure of unwrapped conservation. At a turn the congruence i+j=d modulo N already implies i+j=d in this physical range. Conversely a supported physical state determines one grid point by the primitive face-potential construction. Thus summing (13) over the N^(R+1) grid points is exactly the original finite source. For supported states, changing integrated face-log lifts coherently by 2pi i leaves the entire summand unchanged, since its final face exponents are integral. These coherent face changes induce the actual closed integral head-flow changes. Arbitrary independent single-head resets are not justified: recorded local carries cancel globally only after physical support and coherent face integration are established. Let a monomial of P have nonnegative degrees n_f and total dR. Its grid average can survive only if n_b=0 modulo N, n_f=d modulo N for f!=a,b. The latter degrees are at least d. There are R of them, so their minimum already exhausts dR. Consequently the only alias is n_a=n_b=0, n_f=d for f!=a,b. (15) The even coset phase is one at (15). The normalized grid average in (13) is therefore exactly (1), with no additional N factor. Together with section 4's equality of actual reduced scalars, this proves the statement. ## 8. What this changes, and what it does not The permitted marking is an actual cut exposed after the described rerouting. It carries the original cup/dual boundary transport and the auxiliary pivot specializes exactly to the original root pivot. It is not an identity obtained by moving the old nonintertwining D through the interior coupons or by replacing it with the same matrix on another old head. That incorrect operation already fails in a direct finite internal-head test; that separate operation is not used anywhere in this proof. The equality is for the full polynomial source and hence for any common linear spectral/Fourier functional applied to it, with the same retained twists and exterior framing scalar. A successful full-source certificate at any such MAIN edge would therefore suffice for the original marked scalar, provided all hypotheses of that certificate have independently been checked in that marked geometry. No universally successful mark, sectorwise transport, equality of envelope capacities, or general strictly-overloaded source bound is inferred. In particular the existing flat-plat certificate theorems may use their original top-cap position, gap forest, or specific Morse sweep. Those hypotheses have not been rechecked for every rerouted presentation here. The finite equality does not itself extend those certificate theorems to arbitrary MAIN marks. No generic-q ADO derivative, root semisimplicity, scalar orthogonality, or low-demand cap/CROSS inequality is part of this proof. Only the auxiliary generic finite tensor identities are continued to the root. ## 9. Source dependencies and internal verification The exact inputs are the [original top-cap transport proof](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_arbitrary_casimir_top_mark_transport.md), [literal duality and snakes](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/relative_pivotal_duality.md), [all four balanced turns and the original mark](quantum_bridge_cap_source.md), [full homogeneous polynomial adapter](../papers/filling-bounds/README.md), [original face-character and grid theorem](../papers/filling-bounds/README.md), and [primitive integral face-potential lattice](actual_original_boundary_transverse_rank.md). The full fixed-coupon sphere rerouting is written in section 4; it does not require an unrecorded planar-frame transformation. The [focused audit](../experiments/research_audit_arbitrary_main_edge_mark_transport.py) and its [results](../experiments/research_arbitrary_main_edge_mark_transport_results.json) construct the original physical coproduct matrices, full divided-polynomial numerators and actual positive/negative crossings, including their Cartan scalars. They contract the old physical top mark independently of the homogeneous calculation, then compare every actual MAIN-pair two-zero coefficient. The exact fixtures comprise 20 sources, 160 MAIN-pair coefficients, 19 nonzero sources, and 10 cases at each level parity. They use widths two and three, with both full numerators and arbitrary polynomial coupons. Field agreement and conservative integer-overflow bounds are explicit. No optimization, projected-sector identity, numerical asymptotic, or geometric certificate is inferred from these finite checks. The general identity is proved in sections 2--7.

title: The actual balanced Gauss source as a cyclic divisor contraction
text: # The actual balanced Gauss source as a cyclic divisor contraction Private written proof, 18 November 2026. The finite balanced Gauss polynomial in the actual opposite source is an exact Fourier interpolation of a full square of shifted factorial ratios. Those ratios are the multiplication coefficients of one finite cyclic algebra. Its closed residue contour retains all poles, becomes nilpotent at completeness, and has an explicit first-normal carry with coefficient \(2N\). The construction descends polynomially to the actual commuting Cartan and Casimir, including their Jordan data. This is an exact source adapter. It does not assert an asymptotic for the reconstructed coherent kernel, remove its exterior coupons, or select a geometric contribution. Complete direct G supplies the actual Gauss factor and F supplies the proved meridian frame bounds. All Fourier, algebra, residue, and normal calculations for the adapter are proved here. Finite-flat Fermat/socle residue constructions already occur in [the earlier charged-source note](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_charged_socle_and_fermat_source.md). That is coverage, not a proof premise here. The present identification is for the literal balanced Gauss factor, its calibrated functional, and its quantitative upper-carry sector. ## 1. The actual operator to be transported Fix \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), and \(Q=q^2\). The quantum root is fixed. Put \[ c=M^{-2}Q,\qquad f_n=(Q;Q)_n,\qquad g_n(c)=(c;Q)_n,\qquad \delta=1-c^N=1-M^{-2N}. \tag{1} \] The definition of \(g_n\) applies also to \(n\ge N\). Every \(g_l\), \(0\le l<N\), is a holomorphic unit near \(M=1\), for each fixed \(N\). Use G's actual remaining-head operators \(K,E,F\), with \(\Omega=FE+qK+q^{-1}K^{-1}\). In particular \(K\) and \(\Omega\) commute. G proves that the literal finite operator \(\mathcal A_N=q_FE_\Sigma^d i_d\) is \[ \mathcal A_N=H_d(M)K^d\, \mathcal F_N(a,b;c;c/(ab)),\quad H_d(M)=\prod_{j=1}^d(MQ^{-j}-M^{-1}), \tag{2} \] where, initially for scalar algebra, \[ \Omega=z+z^{-1},\quad a=qKz,\quad b=qK/z,\qquad \mathcal F_N(a,b;c;t)= \sum_{n=0}^d\frac{(a;Q)_n(b;Q)_n}{f_ng_n(c)}t^n. \tag{3} \] The scalar notation in (2) is shorthand for its polynomial evaluation in \(K,\Omega\); it is not a spectral assumption. The original opposite map is retained in G's exact order \[ T=\mathcal B_m(W_\tau^{-1})\,\mathcal A_N\, D_{\rm top}\,\mathscr C_r(M),\qquad J=D_N(MK)^{-1}T, \tag{4} \] where \(D_N(z)=(z^N-z^{-N})/(z-z^{-1})\) has its Laurent-polynomial continuation, \(r=m-1\), \(\tau=R_1\cdots R_r\), and \[ D_{\rm top}=\kappa^r x^{-rd}(x^{-1}Q^{-1})^{\mathsf n}, \qquad x=-M/q. \] Here \(\mathsf n\) is remaining total occupation. The original \(\kappa\), quotient, turnover, and normalization stay attached to (4). Every replacement below concerns precisely \(\mathcal A_N\). ## 2. A full-square Fourier interpolation Set \(u=a^{-1}\), \(v=b^{-1}\), and define the polynomial \[ \begin{split} \mathcal S_N(u,v;c) &:=\mathcal F_N(a,b;c;c/(ab))\\ &=\sum_{n=0}^d \frac{Q^{n(n-1)}c^n(u;Q^{-1})_n(v;Q^{-1})_n} {f_ng_n(c)}. \end{split}\tag{5} \] It has degree at most \(d\) in each variable. The second equality follows by factoring \((-a)^nQ^{n(n-1)/2}\) from \((a;Q)_n\), and likewise for \(b\). Define the finite interpolation polynomials \[ L_l(u)=\frac1N\sum_{j=0}^d(uQ^{-l})^j, \qquad 0\le l<N. \tag{6} \] They satisfy \(L_l(Q^k)=\mathbf1_{l=k}\). We claim the exact whole-meridian identity \[ \boxed{\quad \mathcal S_N(u,v;c)= \sum_{l,k=0}^d C_{lk}(c)L_l(u)L_k(v),\qquad C_{lk}(c)=\frac{g_{l+k}(c)}{g_l(c)g_k(c)}. \quad}\tag{7} \] In particular the square in (7) is not truncated before taking meridian derivatives. To prove it, evaluate (5) at \(u=Q^l,v=Q^k\). The finite Chu identity proved in G gives \[ \mathcal S_N(Q^l,Q^k;c) =\frac{(cQ^k;Q)_l}{(c;Q)_l} =\frac{g_{l+k}(c)}{g_l(c)g_k(c)}. \tag{8} \] For clarity, its required finite identity is \[ \sum_{n=0}^l \frac{(Q^{-l};Q)_n(b;Q)_n}{f_n(c;Q)_n} (cQ^l/b)^n=\frac{(c/b;Q)_l}{(c;Q)_l}. \] After multiplication by \((c;Q)_l\), denote the left side by \(\mathcal T_l(b,y)\), where \(y=c/b\). Gaussian Pascal gives \(\mathcal T_{l+1}(b,y)=(1-byQ^l)\mathcal T_l(b,y) -yQ^l(1-b)\mathcal T_l(bQ,y)\). Starting with \(\mathcal T_0=1\), induction gives \(\mathcal T_l=(y;Q)_l\). Thus only products shorter than \(N\) are divided. Equality on all \(N^2\) grid points proves (7) by the degree bound, first generically and then holomorphically. Away from removable denominators, (6) can also be written \[ L_l(u)=\frac{1-u^N}{N(1-uQ^{-l})}. \tag{9} \] Consequently (7) is a double cyclic Cauchy projection. Both Fermat numerators in (9) remain. Formula (6), not an independently inverted denominator in (9), defines its matrix values. More explicitly let \(\mathsf F_{jl}=N^{-1/2}Q^{-jl}\) and \(\mathbf v(u)=(1,u,\ldots,u^d)\). Then \[ \mathcal S_N(u,v;c)=N^{-1}\mathbf v(u)\mathsf F C(c)\mathsf F^{\mathsf t}\mathbf v(v)^{\mathsf t}. \tag{10} \] This fixes the Fourier normalization and the transpose on the second leg. Moving these finite transforms in a sewn contraction requires their corresponding inverse transforms on the exterior. ## 3. Polynomial descent to the actual source The symmetry \(C_{lk}=C_{kl}\) permits replacement of the summand in (7) by \[ \mathcal D_{lk}(u,v)= \tfrac12\{L_l(u)L_k(v)+L_k(u)L_l(v)\}. \tag{11} \] Every \(\mathcal D_{lk}\) is a symmetric polynomial, hence a polynomial in \(u+v\) and \(uv\). In the actual variables, \[ u+v=\frac{\Omega}{qK},\qquad uv=\frac1{QK^2}. \tag{12} \] Thus (11) defines a literal Laurent polynomial \(\mathcal D_{lk}(K,\Omega)\), without choosing either root of \(z+z^{-1}=\Omega\). In particular, \[ \boxed{\quad \mathcal A_N(M)=H_d(M)K^d \sum_{l,k=0}^d C_{lk}(c)\mathcal D_{lk}(K,\Omega). \quad}\tag{13} \] This is an identity of the original finite matrices. It holds on all Casimir Jordan blocks and does not require \(u^N=v^N=1\), a semisimple spectral grid, or an auxiliary scalar geometric substitution. It can be inserted inside any original marked contraction by linearity, with all the other factors of (4) and the closing functional retained. The auxiliary Fourier legs in (10) are not thereby identified with an orthogonal eigenbasis of the physical heads. ## 4. The cyclic algebra and its original closed contour The root product identity gives \[ g_{n+N}(c)=\delta g_n(c). \tag{14} \] Consider the free rank-\(N\) algebra \[ \mathcal B_\delta=\mathbb C[y]/(y^N-\delta),\qquad e_l=\frac{y^l}{g_l(c)},\quad 0\le l<N. \tag{15} \] Coefficients may be holomorphic in the meridian germ. Equation (14) shows that its multiplication is exactly \[ e_l e_k=C_{lk}(c)e_{(l+k)\bmod N}. \tag{16} \] Let \(\ell_c(e_j)=1\). Define \[ U_u(y)=\sum_{l=0}^d L_l(u)\frac{y^l}{g_l(c)},\qquad W_c(y)=\sum_{j=0}^d g_j(c)y^{d-j}. \tag{17} \] Then (7) says \(\mathcal S_N=\ell_c(U_uU_v)\). This functional has an exact divisor contour. If a positively oriented circle encloses all zeros of \(y^N-\delta\), then \[ \boxed{\quad \mathcal S_N(u,v;c)=\frac1{2\pi i} \oint\frac{U_u(y)U_v(y)W_c(y)}{y^N-\delta}\,dy. \quad}\tag{18} \] Indeed on each monomial \(y^j\), \(0\le j<N\), the integral equals \(g_j(c)\): expand at infinity and select the coefficient of \(y^{-1}\). The integral annihilates multiples of \(y^N-\delta\), since the resulting integrand is a polynomial. It therefore equals \(\ell_c\) on every polynomial modulo that relation. This proves (18), including products of arbitrary degree. For \(\delta\ne0\), choose any \(\rho^N=\delta\). The same cycle is the complete root sum \[ \frac1N\sum_{j=0}^d \frac{U_u(\rho Q^j)U_v(\rho Q^j)W_c(\rho Q^j)} {(\rho Q^j)^d}. \tag{19} \] Changing the Kummer root \(\rho\) permutes the terms. At \(\delta=0\), the algebra is nilpotent and (18) is the original single coefficient residue at zero. No one pole of (19) has been selected or discarded. A fixed contour may be used on any parameter set where it encloses the entire divisor and crosses none of it. For example a radius less than one at \(\delta=0\) does not automatically work on an \(N\)-uniform scaled meridian collar: it must still satisfy \(|\delta|<R^N\). The product law is associative with a useful normal filtration. For any number of factors, write \(\sum_i l_i=wN+j\), \(0\le j<N\). Then \[ \boxed{\quad \prod_i e_{l_i} =\delta^w\frac{g_j(c)}{\prod_i g_{l_i}(c)}e_j. \quad}\tag{20} \] This follows directly from powers of \(y\), so it is independent of parenthesization. Since \(\delta\) has a simple zero at \(M=1\), a meridian jet of order \(k\) sees only windings \(w\le k\). The first normal has the derivative of the zero-winding coefficient and the one-winding coefficient multiplied by \(2N\); all higher windings vanish. This statement is for products in this one coupon algebra with holomorphic coefficients. It does not identify an arbitrary braid assembly with that algebra, or bound derivatives of an exterior source. ## 5. The two triangles and the actual first normal Differentiate in \(\mu=\Log M\), at \(\mu=0\). For \(j<N\), put \[ \Sigma_j=\sum_{h=1}^j\frac{Q^h}{1-Q^h},\qquad \Sigma_0=0. \] Then \(\partial_\mu g_j/g_j=2\Sigma_j\) at the root, and \(\delta'=2N\). To distinguish the parameter \(c\) from \(M\), put \(C^0_{lk}=C_{lk}(Q)\) and \(\dot C_{lk}=\partial_\mu C_{lk}(Qe^{-2\mu})|_0\). The exact coupon values and derivatives are \[ \begin{array}{ll} l+k<N:& C^0_{lk}=\dfrac{f_{l+k}}{f_lf_k},\qquad \dot C_{lk}=2C^0_{lk}(\Sigma_{l+k}-\Sigma_l-\Sigma_k),\\[2mm] l+k=N+j:& C^0_{lk}=0,\qquad \boxed{\ \dot C_{lk}=2N\dfrac{f_j}{f_lf_k}\ }, \quad 0\le j\le N-2. \end{array}\tag{21} \] The second row follows from \(g_{N+j}=\delta g_j\), before specialization. Thus it is a genuine whole-meridian normal, not the derivative of a reflected root factorial identity. The phases can be fixed without choosing an asymptotic branch. Write \(s_j=\prod_{h=1}^j2\sin(\pi h/N)>0\), with \(s_0=1\). Since \(f_j=(-i)^jq^{j(j+1)/2}s_j\), (21) becomes \[ \begin{split} C^0_{lk}&=q^{lk}\frac{s_{l+k}}{s_ls_k}, &&l+k<N,\\ \dot C_{lk}&=2Ni(-1)^{j+1}q^{lk}\frac{s_j}{s_ls_k}, &&l+k=N+j. \end{split}\tag{22} \] In particular the positive sine ratios have an explicit chirp. One may split \(q^{lk}=q^{(l+k)^2/2}q^{-l^2/2}q^{-k^2/2}\) by introducing the integer total-output leg. On the upper triangle that integer is \(N+j\), not silently its residue \(j\). The phases and the transported exterior remain in the source. For the actual operator write \(\mathcal D_{lk}(M)\) for (11)--(12) evaluated on its physical family. The complete product rule is \[ \begin{split} \mathcal A_N'={}&(H_dK^d)'\sum_{l,k}C_{lk}\mathcal D_{lk}\\ &+H_dK^d\sum_{l,k} (C'_{lk}\mathcal D_{lk}+C_{lk}\mathcal D'_{lk}). \end{split}\tag{23} \] Each \(\mathcal D'\) is the derivative of its actual ordered matrix polynomial; no commutation of matrices at different meridians is assumed. The other factors in (4), including \(D_N(MK)^{-1}\), the original pivot and any marks, retain their own product-rule terms. Differentiating the fixed contour (18) retains both numerator derivatives and \[ \frac{\delta' U_uU_vW_c}{(y^N-\delta)^2}. \tag{24} \] At completeness this is the \(2N/y^{2N}\) denominator contribution. It is not erased by replacing the entire divisor by its value at zero. All these derivatives keep \(q=q_N\) fixed; quantum-parameter normals are outside the statement. ## 6. A uniform bound for the entire upper carry sector This sector has a quantitative property stronger than a root first-normal identity. For \(l+k=N+j\), put \[ l'=d-l,\qquad k'=d-k,\qquad n'=l'+k'=N-j-2, \qquad r_{ab}=\frac{s_{a+b}}{s_as_b}\quad(a+b<N). \tag{24a} \] The exact reflection \(s_a s_{d-a}=N\) gives \[ \frac{s_j}{s_ls_k} =\frac1{2N\sin(\pi(j+1)/N)\,r_{l'k'}}. \tag{24b} \] For fixed \(n<N\), consecutive positive ratios satisfy \[ \frac{r_{a+1,n-a-1}}{r_{a,n-a}} =\frac{\sin(\pi(n-a)/N)}{\sin(\pi(a+1)/N)}\ge1 \quad\text{before the midpoint}. \] Indeed the difference of these sines is \(2\cos(\pi(n+1)/(2N))\sin(\pi(n-2a-1)/(2N))\ge0\). The sequence is symmetric and its two endpoint values are one. Thus \(r_{ab}\ge1\). Since \(\sin(\pi(j+1)/N)\ge\sin(\pi/N)\ge2/N\), (21),(24b) imply \[ |\dot C_{lk}|\le N/2\qquad(l+k\ge N). \tag{24c} \] The same sector is polynomially bounded on a whole scaled meridian collar. F proves, for every fixed \(0<\eta<\pi\), uniform polynomial bounds on the holomorphic units and their inverses \[ h_a(M)=M^{-a}\frac{f_a}{g_a(c)},\qquad M=e^{\xi/N},\quad |\xi|\le\eta,\quad 0\le a<N. \] The precise identities here are \[ \begin{array}{ll} l+k<N:& C_{lk}(c)=\dfrac{f_{l+k}}{f_lf_k}\dfrac{h_lh_k}{h_{l+k}},\\[2mm] l+k=N+j:& \boxed{\ C_{lk}(c)=(M^N-M^{-N}) \dfrac{f_j}{f_lf_k}\dfrac{h_lh_k}{h_j}.\ } \end{array}\tag{24d} \] They follow directly from (14) and the definition of \(h\). By (24b), \(|f_j/(f_lf_k)|\le1/4\). Since \(M^N-M^{-N}=2\sinh\xi\) is bounded on this disk, the entire upper triangle in (24d) is bounded by \(C_\eta(N+1)^{p_\eta}\). Cauchy on a slightly larger scaled disk proves polynomial bounds for every fixed \(\xi\)-derivative. A \(\mu\)-derivative introduces one further \(N\) per order. No denominator with a zero on the collar has been divided. There is also uniform exponential decay in every compact reflected interior triangle. Suppose \(l',k'\ge\epsilon N\) and \(l'+k'\le(1-\epsilon)N\), with fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/3\). Choose \(0<\gamma\le\min(\epsilon/4,\sin(\pi\epsilon)/(4\pi))\). For sufficiently large \(N\), the first \(\lfloor\gamma N\rfloor\) ratios in the preceding unimodal sequence are at least two: their numerator is at least \(\sin(\pi\epsilon)\), and their denominator is at most \(2\pi\gamma\). All subsequent ratios up to the smaller of \(l',k'\) are at least one. Hence \(r_{l'k'}\ge2^{\lfloor\gamma N\rfloor}\). Equations (24b),(24d) give exponential decay there, up to a polynomial, uniformly on the collar and for every fixed meridian derivative. These array bounds also control their scalar Fourier interpolants on the unit torus. Parseval in (6) gives \(\sum_l|L_l(u)|^2=1\) when \(|u|=1\). Therefore \[ \left|\sum_{l+k\ge N} \dot C_{lk}L_l(u)L_k(v)\right| \le\|\dot C_{\rm upper}\|_{\rm F}\le N^2/2, \qquad |u|=|v|=1. \tag{24e} \] The same argument gives a polynomial bound on the full scaled collar, and exponential decay for the reflected-interior subarray. More generally, on \(e^{-R/N}\le |u|,|v|\le e^{R/N}\), Parseval gives \[ \|L(u)\|_2^2=N^{-1}\sum_{j<N}|u|^{2j}\le e^{2R}, \qquad \|\partial_u^pL(u)\|_2\le C_{p,R}N^p. \] The derivative estimate follows from the same sum with the falling factorial \(j(j-1)\cdots(j-p+1)\). Thus every fixed scalar Fourier jet of the upper interpolant is polynomial on this thin annulus, jointly with the stated meridian derivatives; the reflected-interior subarray retains its exponential decay. Fourier variables are held fixed when differentiating coefficients in \(M\). These are scalar coefficient-array and scalar-jet estimates. They do not bound arbitrary evaluated matrix/Jordan norms or conditioned projectors in (13), an unbounded moving Fourier path, the lower triangle, or the closed source. On arbitrary scalar arguments the same Parseval sum gives \(\|L(u)\|_2\le\max(1,|u|)^d\). Thus the entire upper interpolant, and each fixed meridian derivative, is bounded on the stated collar by \[ C(N+1)^p\max(1,|u|)^d\max(1,|v|)^d. \tag{24f} \] Its possible exponential cost in this scalar bound is entirely in the two displayed boundary factors; (24f) is not an evaluated operator bound. ## 7. The root arc and affine source rows At \(c=Q\), define \[ \Phi_a(z)=\sum_{n=0}^d\frac{(a;Q)_n}{f_n}z^n. \] Coefficient comparison including the last degree proves \[ (1-z)\Phi_a(z)-(1-az)\Phi_a(Qz) =-\frac{1-a^N}{N}z^N. \tag{25} \] Iterate this row around the finite clock. The transport product is \((1-a^Nz^N)/(1-z^N)\). Dividing on a generic set and cancelling the full orbit factors gives the all-polynomial formula \[ \Phi_a(z)=\frac1N\sum_{k=0}^d \prod_{j=0}^{k-1}(1-aQ^jz)\prod_{j=k+1}^{d}(1-Q^jz). \tag{26} \] Polynomial continuation proves it at every omitted divisor. In (3) with \(c=Q\), the exact original Hadamard contour is \[ \mathcal F_N(a,b;Q;t) =\operatorname{CT}_z\Phi_a(z)\Phi_b(t/z), \qquad abt=Q. \tag{27} \] The two numerator activities satisfy \((az)(bt/z)=Q\) exactly. They cannot both belong to disks of radius less than one. Changing the coefficient-circle radius does not delete this reciprocal interface. Equivalently, the root coefficient array in (7) has generating polynomial \[ P_N(X,Y)=\sum_{l+k<N}\frac{f_{l+k}}{f_lf_k}X^lY^k. \] Gaussian Pascal, including the total-degree-\(N\) boundary, gives \[ \boxed{\ (1-X)P_N(X,Y)-YP_N(QX,Y)=1-X^N-Y^N.\ } \tag{28} \] The internal degree-\(N\) coefficients vanish because \({N\brack l}_Q=0\) for \(0<l<N\); the two corner terms remain. With \(T_Qf(X)=f(QX)\), this also follows from \(P_N=\sum_{n<N}(X+YT_Q)^n1\) and \((X+YT_Q)^N=X^N+Y^N\). This affine Fermat row describes the root coupon value. Its whole-meridian normal is (21), not a homogeneous continuation of (28). ## 8. A literal one-head calibration and the remaining scope The moving coupons in (23) matter even on one actual tail head. On its occupation \(j\), the displayed balanced arrows give \(\Omega(M)=-M-M^{-1}\) and \(K_j(M)=-Mq^{-1}Q^{-j}\). Choosing \(z=-M\) in the scalar calculation gives \(u=M^{-2}Q^j,v=Q^j\). The terminating Chu identity therefore gives the exact value of the normalized factor \[ \mathcal S_N(M^{-2}Q^j,Q^j;M^{-2}Q) =\frac{(M^{-4}Q^{j+1};Q)_j}{(M^{-2}Q;Q)_j}. \tag{29} \] If \(2j\ge N\), its root value is zero. The numerator contains exactly one factor \(1-M^{-4}\); all other factors and the denominator are units at the root. Its true \(\mu\)-derivative is \[ 4N\frac{f_{2j-N}}{f_j^2}. \tag{30} \] This is twice the fixed-grid coefficient normal in (21); the moving polynomial coupon supplies the rest. At \(j=d\), the complete root sum is zero although its \(n=d\) summand in (3) is exactly \(Q\), and (30) equals \(4/(1-Q^{-1})\). These follow by \(f_d=N\) and \(f_{d-1}=N/(1-Q^{-1})\). This is an all-level actual-head calibration, not a claim about a knot contribution. Equations (7),(13),(18),(20) give an associative, finite Fourier and closed-divisor presentation of the same actual Gauss factor, with its source normalization and all first-normal carries. Section 6 also bounds the entire upper coefficient sector on a scaled meridian collar. These conclusions do not supply a relative estimate after contraction with \(\mathcal D_{lk}(K,\Omega)\), the factors of (4), or an exterior. The known concavity of the positive triangle weight is not a new conclusion here and does not remove its chirp. Nor does (19) choose one Kummer root as a contributing geometric period. The actual reconstructed kernel asymptotic and its source pairing remain open. ## Complete proof directs * G: notes/research_opposite_kernel_forced_cyclic_normalization.md, SHA256 42e6d6c3a5039859c241a2832de56301eff49d749db86d67868f3534c89aaaaa. * F: notes/research_actual_meridian_source_frames.md, SHA256 6f58fba195ba5e8208e1d5180a1d684b933f9f5d50eb28efc56609580fe29976. Both complete directs and the entire final were read nontruncated in this author sequence; used implications and pins were checked. Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used. Frozen and public files were not edited.

title: Exact strip reconstruction on every compact positive angle triangle
text: # Exact strip reconstruction on every compact positive angle triangle Private written proof, 18 November 2026. The actual balanced Gauss polynomial has a single cardinal projection of an exact factorial ratio. Pairing the two sides of a width-one strip gives an explicit boundary current with both Fermat numerators. The current is polynomially bounded on the real scalar torus, uniformly on a scaled meridian disk. Consequently the exact ratio is the selected, nonzero asymptotic throughout every compact positive angle triangle, including a fixed complex neighborhood and fixed normal derivatives. This is a scalar reconstruction theorem for the polynomial in complete direct C. Its Laurent-polynomial evaluation on the actual Cartan and Casimir, its Jordan data, exterior coupons, and source functional are still the ones in C. No operator norm, coherent-kernel estimate, or geometric source coefficient is inferred from this scalar theorem. ## 1. Exact functions and the theorem Put \[ c_0=2\pi i,\quad Q=e^{c_0/N},\quad d=N-1,\qquad c=e^{c_0(1+\beta)/N},\quad \rho=e^{c_0\beta}=c^N. \tag{1} \] The root is fixed. The physical scaled meridian is \(M=e^{\xi/N}\), with \(\beta=-2\xi/c_0\). Fix a sufficiently small disk \(|\beta|\le\beta_0<1/4\), and enlarge it slightly whenever Cauchy estimates are used. Use F's exactly normalized factorial \(\widehat F_N\), denoted by \(F_N\) in this note. Its proved identities are \[ \begin{split} F_N(z+1)&=(1-Q^{z+1})F_N(z),&F_N(0)&=1,\\ F_N(z+N)&=(1-e^{c_0z})F_N(z),\\ F_N(z)F_N(d-z)&=N e^{i\pi z(z-d)/N}. \end{split}\tag{2} \] The second identity follows by multiplying the first \(N\) times. The function is holomorphic and nonzero on \(-1<\Re z<N\), and continues holomorphically to \(\Re z>-1\) by the first identity. Its further zeros cause no numerator poles below. For \(A=e^{c_0x}\), \(B=e^{c_0y}\), define the exact ratio \[ \mathcal B_{N,\beta}(x,y)= \frac{F_N(N(x+y)+\beta)F_N(\beta)} {F_N(Nx+\beta)F_N(Ny+\beta)}. \tag{3} \] Let \(\mathcal S_N(A,B;c)\) be C's literal degree-at-most-\(d\) polynomial in each scalar argument. The precise conclusion is: **Theorem.** For every compact set \[ K\Subset\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:x>0, y>0, x+y<1\}, \tag{4} \] there is a fixed complex neighborhood \(U\) of \(K\), and \(\epsilon>0\), such that \[ \boxed{\quad \mathcal S_N(e^{c_0x},e^{c_0y};c) =\mathcal B_{N,\beta}(x,y) \bigl(1+O(e^{-\epsilon N})\bigr). \quad}\tag{5} \] The estimate is uniform on \(U\times\{|\beta|\le\beta_0\}\), after shrinking the disk if necessary. Every fixed derivative of the normalized error has the same exponential bound on smaller domains. In particular the reconstructed scalar is nonzero there for large \(N\). Here is its calibrated leading term. On the logarithmic strip set \[ I(z)=\frac{\operatorname{Li}_2(1)- \operatorname{Li}_2(e^{c_0z})}{c_0}, \qquad \Phi(x,y)=I(x+y)-I(x)-I(y), \tag{6} \] with continuation from the real interval \(0<z<1\). Also put \[ \Lambda(x,y)=\frac{\pi\sin\pi(x+y)} {\sin\pi x\sin\pi y}. \tag{7} \] The powers and square root are continued from their positive real values on the triangle. Uniformly on a smaller \(U\), \[ \boxed{\quad \mathcal S_N= \frac{\Gamma(1+\beta)N^{-\beta}\Lambda(x,y)^\beta} {\sqrt{2N}} \sqrt{\frac{\sin\pi(x+y)}{\sin\pi x\sin\pi y}} e^{N\Phi(x,y)}\bigl(1+O(N^{-1})\bigr). \quad}\tag{8} \] This proves reconstruction for arbitrary compact strict triangles, not only for a neighborhood of the entropy maximum. ## 2. One cardinal projection, with the original coefficients Write \(g_j=(c;Q)_j\) and \(L_k(B)=N^{-1}\sum_{j=0}^d(BQ^{-k})^j\). C proves \[ \mathcal S_N(A,B;c)= \sum_{l,k=0}^d\frac{g_{l+k}}{g_lg_k}L_l(A)L_k(B). \tag{9} \] For each integer \(0\le k<N\), (2) gives exactly \[ \mathcal B_{N,\beta}(x,k/N) =\frac{(cA;Q)_k}{(c;Q)_k}. \tag{10} \] This is a polynomial of degree at most \(k\) in \(A\), whose values at \(A=Q^l\) are the coefficients in (9). Therefore \[ \boxed{\quad \mathcal S_N(A,B;c)= \sum_{k=0}^d L_k(B)\mathcal B_{N,\beta}(x,k/N). \quad}\tag{11} \] This identity is whole-meridian. In particular it does not delete the upper triangle before differentiation. No approximate sampling or interpolation in an occupation index has occurred. Use the cardinal kernel \[ \mathcal K_N(y,w)= \frac{c_0(B^N-1)} {(e^{c_0Nw}-1)(e^{c_0(y-w)}-1)}. \tag{12} \] Its residue at \(w=k/N\) is \(L_k(B)\); its residue at the source pole \(w=y\) is \(-1\). It is one-periodic in \(w\). Source values coinciding with a grid point will always be obtained by holomorphic continuation of the final identities. Fix \(a=1/2\). For sufficiently large \(N\), the strip \[ -a/N<\Re w<1-a/N \tag{13} \] contains exactly the grid \(0,1/N,\ldots,d/N\) and one source pole for \(y\) in any fixed compact substrip of \(0<\Re y<1\). The denominator arguments \(Nw+\beta\) remain in the zero-free strip of \(F_N\), since \(|\Re\beta|<1/4\). The numerator argument has positive real part if \(x\) is in a compact substrip and \(N\) is large. It can cross \(N\), where it can have zeros, but it has no poles. Thus the only poles of the integrand in (13) are the stated cardinal and source poles. Integrate \(\mathcal K_N(y,w)\mathcal B_{N,\beta}(x,w)\) on the positively oriented rectangle obtained by cutting (13) at imaginary heights \(\pm T\). The two horizontal ends tend to zero as \(T\to\infty\), for each fixed \(N\). A proof of this assertion, including the lower end, is given in Section 3. Pair the remaining vertical sides by \(w\mapsto w+1\).
