No physical Cartan weight is replaced by an off-circle geometric eigenvalue, and no fixed-root meridian normal or complementary current is erased. ## Complete sources and prior coverage * W, complete proof direct: notes/research_actual_word_normal_cocycle_and_source.md, 458 lines, SHA256 db453e02bc349e7740b2718b25819e9aa8ad1a71b86044fb7128524bea292106. * C, complete proof direct: notes/research_root_capped_euler_coproduct_factorization.md, 360 lines, SHA256 e11f5f827f226ee93505e00aed3885a33abdbfc15ee71e023a67c048c9c17720. * Earlier collar proof, complete coverage only: notes/research_boundary_ward_logarithmic_collar.md, 434 lines, SHA256 43e71e44044d14895cacc02eeed99bd742f47964bbd2317bd22663e93bca08bd. The complete matching source and coverage texts were read untruncated in the author sequence. The earlier collar proof is not used as a premise for the positive Toeplitz argument. The exact integral, cycle Gram, inverse estimate, endpoint comparison and physical extraction are proved above. This text is submitted for independent whole-text and whole-source review. Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used; earlier frozen files were unchanged.

title: The actual degree-selected boundary Ward packet has a nonzero entry
text: # The actual degree-selected boundary Ward packet has a nonzero entry Written research proof, 23 November 2026. For the literal reduced boundary crossing, the entire resonant Ward sum is one donor-diagonal commutator. Its component with donor loss one has no triangular-transfer cancellation. An explicit physical input and output give a lower bound after both the required total degree selection and the physical weight restriction. This holds at every level, including even and composite levels, whenever the indicated physical weight exists. The result is a lower bound for a full first-normal matrix packet. Its exhibited component can lie on an occupation boundary; it is not identified with a growing geometric mode. The original marked closing, arbitrary exterior and its possible scalar cancellation remain. No knot-volume or general short-component lower bound is claimed. ## 1. Original operators and the selected physical arrow Fix \[ N\ge2,\quad d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2, \quad m=r+1,\quad r\ge2,\quad x(M)=-M/q, \quad x_0=x(1),\quad F_j=(Q;Q)_j. \tag{1} \] The quantum parameter remains fixed. All physical occupation bases are orthonormal in the Euclidean norms used below. Split the remaining \(r\) heads into a first donor and its ordered tail. Write \(L|j\rangle=|j-1\rangle\) for \(j>0\), with bottom zero, and \(Z|j\rangle=Q^j|j\rangle\). Let \(K_{\rm T}(M),E_{\rm T}(M),F_{\rm T}(M)\) be the actual tail coproducts. The complete remaining lowering and Cartan operators are \[ \begin{split} E(M)&=E_{\rm T}(M)+L(MZ^{-1}-M^{-1})K_{\rm T}(M),\\ K_r(M)&=x(M)Z^{-1}K_{\rm T}(M)=M^rK_0. \end{split} \tag{2} \] In particular \(K_0L=QLK_0\). The root values are denoted by omitting \(M\); thus \(E=E(1)\). Retain the actual scalar \(\kappa(M)\). Source [R, (12)] gives the literal positive reduced boundary crossing \[ \begin{split} b(M)&=\kappa(M)S_r(M)D(M),\\ S_r(M)&=\sum_{j=0}^{d} \frac{(x(M)^{-1}LF_{\rm T}(M))^j}{F_j},\\ D(M)|j\rangle&=(-1)^jQ^{j(j+1)/2}M^{-2j}|j\rangle. \end{split} \tag{3} \] All missing physical arrows are zero. Set \(b=b(1)\), \(\kappa=\kappa(1)\ne0\), and \(D=D(1)\). The matrix \(D\) is unitary and the zero donor-loss part of \(S_r\) is exactly the identity. Choose an actual eigenvalue \(\lambda\in\operatorname{spec}K_0\) and its nonself reciprocal Ward order \(1\le t<N\), so \[ \lambda^2=Q^{-t},\qquad P_\lambda\ne0, \qquad a_0=\lambda/x_0,\qquad a_0^2=Q^{1-t},\quad |a_0|=1. \tag{4} \] Here \(P_\lambda\) is the original frozen Cartan projector. At even \(N\), only orders occurring among these actual weights are being asserted. No absent weight is supplied by interpolation. The original flattened boundary Ward arrow of [W, (19)--(20)] is \[ \mathfrak D_tP_\lambda =2m\sum_{n=1}^t(-1)^{n-1}a_0^n \frac{F_t}{F_{t-n}(1-Q^n)}E^{t-n}bL^nP_\lambda. \tag{5} \] The total degree loss is already \(t\). Every transfer and scalar in (5) is retained. ## 2. Whole-meridian conjugation and resonant cancellation The transformed lowering row [C, (5)], applied to the remaining prefix, is \[ S_r(M)^{-1}E(M)S_r(M) =E_{\rm T}(M)+L\bigl(MK_{\rm T}(M)Z^{-1} -M^{-1}K_{\rm T}(M)^{-1}\bigr). \tag{6} \] The diagonal in (3) satisfies the exact finite relation \(D(M)^{-1}LD(M)=-M^{-2}LZ\), including the bottom zero. Define \[ \begin{split} C_M&=E_{\rm T}(M)-M^{-1}LK_{\rm T}(M),\\ X_M&=MLZ^{-1}K_{\rm T}(M),\qquad Y_M=M^{-3}LZK_{\rm T}(M)^{-1}. \end{split} \tag{7} \] Equations (2),(3),(6) give the whole-meridian identities \[ E(M)=C_M+X_M,\qquad b(M)^{-1}E(M)b(M)=C_M+Y_M. \tag{8} \] Within (7), only the invertible Cartan matrices are inverted; \(b(M)^{-1}\) in (8) is the actual inverse crossing. The scalar \(\kappa(M)\) cancels in conjugation and will reappear in \(b\). The physical relations \(ZL=Q^{-1}LZ\) and \(K_{\rm T}E_{\rm T}=QE_{\rm T}K_{\rm T}\) imply \[ X_MC_M=QC_MX_M,\qquad Y_MC_M=Q^{-1}C_MY_M. \tag{9} \] For example both summands of \(C_M\) have the indicated relation with \(X_M\), by these two relations separately. The inverse relations prove the statement for \(Y_M\). All are finite-matrix identities with their actual endpoints. On the frozen input weight in (4), powers of these operators obey \[ \begin{split} X_M^nP_\lambda &=M^{rn}a_0^nQ^{n(n-1)/2}L^nP_\lambda,\\ Y_M^nP_\lambda &=M^{-(r+2)n}a_0^{-n}Q^{-n(n-1)/2}L^nP_\lambda. \end{split} \tag{10} \] Indeed \(X_M=M^rL(x_0^{-1}K_0)\) and \(Y_M=M^{-(r+2)}L(x_0^{-1}K_0)^{-1}\). Commuting their frozen Cartans through \(L\) proves (10). Apply the finite binomial formula in the order \(C_M^{t-n}X_M^n\) and \(C_M^{t-n}Y_M^n\). Since \({t\brack n}_{Q^{-1}}=Q^{-n(t-n)}{t\brack n}_Q\), the ratio of the two input-weight coefficients is \(M^{-2mn}(a_0^{-2}Q^{1-t})^n=M^{-2mn}\). Thus exactly \[ \begin{split} \Delta(M)P_\lambda &:=(b(M)^{-1}E(M)^tb(M)-E(M)^t)P_\lambda\\ &=\sum_{n=1}^t {t\brack n}_Q M^{rn}a_0^nQ^{n(n-1)/2} (M^{-2mn}-1)C_M^{t-n}L^nP_\lambda. \end{split} \tag{11} \] Every index is below \(N\). In particular \(\Delta(1)P_\lambda=0\) and the root arrow intertwines. Writing \(C=C_1\), \(X=X_1\) and differentiating in \(\mu=\log M\) gives \[ \left.\partial_\mu\Delta(e^\mu)P_\lambda\right|_0 =-2m\left.\partial_s(C+sX)^tP_\lambda\right|_{s=1}. \tag{12} \] The derivatives of the other factors in (11) are multiplied by \(M^{-2mn}-1=0\), so no normal has been omitted in (12). ## 3. The true flattened normal is one donor commutator Source [W, (7)--(8)] supplies an analytic Cartan-preserving frame \(G(M)\), with \(G(1)=I\), such that \(G(M)^{-1}E(M)G(M)=E\). Its reduced normal is the derivative of \(\widehat b(M)=G(M)^{-1}b(M)G(M)\), and its Ward arrow is \([\widehat b'(1),E^t]P_\lambda\), with the derivative taken in \(\mu\). More explicitly, \[ [\widehat b(M),E^t]=G(M)^{-1}[b(M),E(M)^t]G(M). \tag{13} \] At \(M=1\) the commutator on the right vanishes on \(P_\lambda\) by (11). Since \(G\) preserves the input weight, its connection terms vanish after that restriction when (13) is differentiated. Also \([b(M),E(M)^t]=-b(M)\Delta(M)\). Therefore the actual flattened normal, not an independently chosen lift, is \[ \mathfrak D_tP_\lambda =-b\left.\partial_\mu\Delta(e^\mu)P_\lambda\right|_0 =2mb\left.\partial_s(C+sX)^tP_\lambda\right|_{s=1}. \tag{14} \] The scalar derivative of \(\kappa\) also multiplies the vanishing root commutator, rather than being silently discarded. The last derivative is explicitly diagonal. On the donor define \[ g_j(s)=\prod_{h=1}^j\frac{Q^{-h}-1}{sQ^{-h}-1} =\frac{F_j}{\prod_{h=1}^j(s-Q^h)},\qquad G_s|j\rangle=g_j(s)|j\rangle,\quad g_0=1. \tag{15} \] For each fixed level these are holomorphic and invertible near \(s=1\), with \(G_1=I\). Their consecutive ratio proves \[ C+sX=G_sEG_s^{-1},\qquad \Gamma|j\rangle=\gamma_j|j\rangle, \quad \gamma_j=-\sum_{h=1}^j\frac1{1-Q^h},\quad\gamma_0=0, \qquad \Gamma=\left.\partial_sG_s\right|_1. \tag{16} \] The tail terms commute with this one-donor frame. The forced zero arrow remains zero; no uniform \(s\)-collar is assumed. Equations (14)--(16) prove the fixed-degree collapse \[ \boxed{\quad \mathfrak D_tP_\lambda=2mb[\Gamma,E^t]P_\lambda. \quad} \tag{17} \] It is also the ordered polynomial derivative \(2mb\sum_{j=0}^{t-1}E^jXE^{t-1-j}P_\lambda\). The diagonal \(\Gamma\) is the same for every physical order and weight. No coefficient projection remains to be estimated in (17). For input donor occupation \(j\) and output \(j-n\), the entry of this commutator is the corresponding entry of \(E^t\) times \[ \gamma_{j-n}-\gamma_j=\sum_{h=j-n+1}^j\frac1{1-Q^h}, \qquad \operatorname{Re}(\gamma_{j-n}-\gamma_j)=n/2. \tag{18} \] All terms of \(E^t\) have donor loss \(n\ge0\). The loss-zero entries in (17) vanish, and none of its positive-loss multipliers is zero. These are exact root identities, not a replacement of the co-source by a Hermitian norm. ## 4. The protected donor-loss-one component Let \(J|j\rangle=j|j\rangle\) on the donor. Define the actual matrix-entry projection \[ \mathsf R_1(T)=\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi} e^{-i\phi}e^{-i\phi J}T e^{i\phi J}\,d\phi. \tag{19} \] It retains precisely donor occupation loss one. It is contractive in physical operator norm and orthogonal in Hilbert--Schmidt norm. The diagonal projector \(P_\lambda\) commutes with this degree action, so input weights are not mixed by (19). Put \([t]_Q=(1-Q^t)/(1-Q)\). In the coproduct \(E=E_{\rm donor}K_{\rm T}+E_{\rm T}\), its two terms \(Q\)-commute. The donor-loss-one part of \(E^t\) is consequently \([t]_Q E_{\rm T}^{t-1}E_{\rm donor}K_{\rm T}\). The loss-one multiplier in (18) cancels its donor coefficient: \[ \frac{Q^{-j}-1}{1-Q^j}=Q^{-j},\qquad \mathsf R_1([\Gamma,E^t]) =[t]_Q E_{\rm T}^{t-1}X. \tag{20} \] Every term of \([\Gamma,E^t]\) has donor loss at least one. Every term of \(S_r\) has nonnegative donor loss, and its zero-loss term is the identity. Therefore in (17) the only contribution to loss one is this zero-transfer term of the literal crossing. Since \(XP_\lambda=a_0LP_\lambda\), the exact observed packet is \[ \boxed{\quad \mathsf R_1(\mathfrak D_tP_\lambda) =2m\kappa[t]_Q D E_{\rm T}^{t-1}XP_\lambda =2m\kappa a_0[t]_Q D E_{\rm T}^{t-1}LP_\lambda. \quad} \tag{21} \] There is also a short direct verification from the original sum (5). Its terms with \(n\ge2\) have donor loss at least two. In its \(n=1\) term, loss one forces the identity term of \(S_r\) and the tail-only term of \(E^{t-1}\). Its scalar coefficient is \(2ma_0F_t/[F_{t-1}(1-Q)]=2ma_0[t]_Q\), giving exactly (21). Thus the selected-entry argument below does not depend on choosing a flattening frame or estimating a diagonal meridian gauge. All the higher transfers remain in the full matrix; they cannot enter this particular entry projection. Because \(D\) is unitary, (19)--(21) give in both of the stated physical norms \[ \|\mathfrak D_tP_\lambda\| \ge2m|\kappa|\,|[t]_Q|\, \|E_{\rm T}^{t-1}LP_\lambda\|. \tag{22} \] There is no inverse or condition number of \(b\) in this inequality. ## 5. An explicit nonzero physical matrix entry Write the actual weight as \(\lambda=x_0^rQ^{-h}\), with \(0\le h<N\). Choose an input with donor occupation \(j\), the next \(r-2\) occupations equal to \(d\), and last-tail occupation \(A\). First set \(A=d\) and solve \[ j+(r-2)d+A\equiv h\pmod N, \qquad 0\le j<N. \tag{23} \] If this gives \(j=0\), replace \(A\) by \(d-1\); the new solution is \(j=1\). Thus in either case \(j>0\), the input is in \(U_\lambda\), and \(A\ge t-1\). In the output lower the donor to \(j-1\), the last tail head to \(A-(t-1)\), and leave all other occupations unchanged. Exactly one term of \(E_{\rm T}^{t-1}\) reaches that output: every lowering is on the last head, so there is no later Cartan factor. Its coefficient is \((-1)^{t-1}F_{t-1}\) for \(A=d\), and \((-1)^{t-1}F_t/F_1\) for \(A=d-1\). Put \(\delta_{j-1}=(-1)^{j-1}Q^{(j-1)j/2}\). The corresponding entry of the full original \(\mathfrak D_tP_\lambda\) is exactly \[ 2m\kappa a_0[t]_Q\delta_{j-1}(-1)^{t-1} \begin{cases} F_{t-1},&A=d,\\ F_t/F_1,&A=d-1. \end{cases} \tag{24} \] Both phases \(a_0\) and \(\delta_{j-1}\) have modulus one. All products have length below \(N\), including at \(t=N-1\). For \(N=2,t=1\), the tail power and its product are empty, and the same argument gives the specified nonzero entry. Since \(|[t]_Q|\ge1\) for \(1\le t<N\) and \([t]_QF_{t-1}=F_t/F_1\), either case of (24) proves \[ \boxed{\quad \|\mathfrak D_tP_\lambda\|_{\rm op},\quad \|\mathfrak D_tP_\lambda\|_{\rm HS} \ \ge\ \frac{2m|\kappa|\,|F_t|}{|1-Q|}, \qquad r\ge2,\quad N\ge2, \quad} \tag{25} \] for every actual physical weight and order in (4). Equivalently the normalized packet \(\mathfrak D_tP_\lambda/(2mF_t)\) has both norms at least \(|\kappa|/|1-Q|\ge |\kappa|N/(2\pi)\). No physical order, endpoint or meridian-normal direction was removed to get this lower bound. This estimates the actual degree-selected boundary normal packet, not merely the matrix before its required coefficient observation. The witnessing input is near occupation endpoints and has not been identified with a geometric growing packet. The remaining source functional in [W, (27)], its off-diagonal normal couplings, both reciprocal arrows and any arbitrary short exterior stay in place. They can annihilate or cancel matrix components even though (25) holds. Exact negative-letter and word cocycles retain their actual inverse and exterior factors. No general marked-scalar or geometric volume lower bound follows from (25) alone. More specifically, the Ward arrow has total integer degree loss \(t>0\). For any degree-preserving exterior \(B_{\rm ext}\), its direct ordinary trace \(\operatorname{Tr}(B_{\rm ext}\mathfrak D_tP_\lambda)\) is zero. The original source is not that trace: [W, (24),(27)] first reconstructs the normal blocks from both reciprocal arrows and retains their diagonal and off-diagonal bilinear contractions. The donor projection is not an invariant-preserving replacement of that procedure. For a presentation with one boundary crossing, the complete Markov contraction [W, (29)] still leaves the arbitrary internal core and its unknown scalar; it is not a new nonvanishing argument. ## Complete proof sources and coverage * C: notes/research_prefix_commutant_and_pointed_normal_functional.md, 549 lines, SHA256 b4fb801a1482316aebb4799f1d0b80d5b43ced39138d903c04cfde811ca166b0. * R: notes/research_actual_reduced_braid_source.md, 330 lines, SHA256 9a472ef27b08305a519ff1f24b6d2b909e63a0acbdc49b3a29e001c52a2f2243. * W: notes/research_actual_word_normal_cocycle_and_source.md, 458 lines, SHA256 db453e02bc349e7740b2718b25819e9aa8ad1a71b86044fb7128524bea292106. * Complete coverage: notes/research_boundary_ward_positive_toeplitz.md, 338 lines, SHA256 2df4811faadc585018011ef86e18d81cf0f8dc3745d05ac0f689d84f076979d9. All four complete matching texts were read untruncated in the author sequence. The Toeplitz proof controls the unprojected logarithmic factor; it is not a premise for this selected-entry lower bound. The whole-meridian conjugation, resonant derivative, one-donor commutator and explicit physical observation are proved above. This text is submitted for independent whole-text and whole-source review. Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used; earlier frozen files were unchanged.

title: The braid cut, the literal empty cap, and global nine-cell sewing
text: # The braid cut, the literal empty cap, and global nine-cell sewing Private written proof, 17 November 2026. Starting with a supplied braid presentation of a knot, we assemble the literal charged tetrahedral sources into a closed triangulated pair. Its normalized source is the original fixed-zero planar source times a specified scalar of modulus one on injective real decorations. All vertex measures, wire clocks, sector phases, and the actual empty closing ball remain in the formula. No state-invariance theorem or printed nine-cell comparison is used. ## 1. The planar source and its open diagonal Fix odd \(N>2\), \(q=\exp(2\pi i/N)\), \(d=N-1\), and \(\epsilon=1/2\in\mathbb Z/N\). Let a braid on \(b\ge2\) strands have one-component closure and \(c>0\) crossings. Draw its strands upward in a rectangle, and its disjoint nested closing arcs on the right. Cut the outermost closing arc, on strand 1. The two free ends are on the unbounded face. A crossing has four distinct *corner occurrences*, even when some of its regions coincide. For an admissible sector assignment \(\chi\), let \[ O_\chi(i,j)=\sum_{\text{internal colors}} \prod_v R_v(\,\cdot\mid\chi_v) \prod_{e\text{ internal}}q^{j_e}. \tag{1} \] Here \(R\) is exactly [K,(2.7),(2.8)]. The two end-edge factors are omitted in (1). Admissibility means that every crossing and bounded face has charge sum 1, and every unbounded-face corner has charge 0. At \(i=j=0\), (1) is the original fixed-cut source [K,(3.6)]. The array \(F_\chi(i,j)\) of [G] includes both end factors, so \(F_\chi(i,j)=q^{i+j}O_\chi(i,j)\); the two conventions will not be interchanged in the cap contraction. **Open diagonal identity.** For every such assignment, \[ O_\chi(i,j)=q^{-i}\delta_{ij}O_\chi(0,0). \tag{2} \] This does not assert that the last scalar is nonzero. We give the complete passage from the enhanced braid to (2). Write \(R^o\) for [K,(2.12)] and \(B_+=P(R^o)^t\). By [P], \[ B_-=B_+^{-1},\qquad \mu=q^\epsilon S,\qquad S|j\rangle=|j+1\rangle, \] and the weighted partial trace of a one-component braid over strands 2 through \(b\) is a scalar operator. This follows there from the explicit Fourier and diagonal comparison with the simple highest-weight module, including all conjugations and the writhe phase; it is not an invariance assertion imported from [K]. For precision the negative planar convention can also be checked without assuming the printed inverse. Put \(p_r=\prod_{t=1}^r(1-q^t)\). The Fourier matrix \(A\) in [P,(1.1)] has inverse \[ (A^{-1})_{a-k,b+k;a,b} =(-1)^kq^{-1-a(b+1)-ak+k(k+1)/2} \frac{p_a p_{b+k}}{p_{a-k}p_b p_k}, \tag{3} \] with the same ordinary triangular index range. In the product \(AA^{-1}\), the entry of total displacement \(r>0\), after its common nonzero factor, is \[ \sum_{k=0}^r \frac{(-1)^kq^{k(k-1)/2+(1-r)k}}{p_kp_{r-k}} =\frac{(q^{1-r};q)_r}{p_r}=0. \] The diagonal is 1. Reflection \(j\mapsto d-j\) and \(\overline p_k=(-1)^kq^{-k(k+1)/2}p_k\) give \(A^{-1}=J_dP\overline A PJ_d\), with tensor factors understood. Since \(B_+=\mathcal F^{-1}PA^t\mathcal F\), \(\mathcal F=F\otimes F\), and \(F^{-1}J_dF^{-1}=Z\), this is \[ B_-=(Z\otimes Z)\overline{B_+}(Z^{-1}\otimes Z^{-1}), \qquad Z|j\rangle=q^j|j\rangle. \tag{4} \] Substitution in [K,(2.8),(2.15)] shows that the printed negative matrix is \(qB_-\). Thus no signed inverse phase is discarded. At either signed braid crossing, put charge 1 in the south sector (between its two inputs) and 0 in the other sectors. The matrix \(B_+\) is that raw \(R\) times \(q^{\text{sum of output colors}}\). For \(B_-\) there is additionally \(q^{-1}\). For example, positive input/output labels \((a,b)\to(c,d')\) give cyclic planar labels \((a,b,d',c)\); the negative crossing uses \((b,d',c,a)\). These substitutions fix the overpassing pair and the south sector, rather than reversing a corner by convention. In each traced closing arc, \(\mu\) makes the next input color equal to the previous output color plus 1 and contributes \(q^\epsilon\). Use the output color as the color of the whole corresponding planar edge. At each local port let \(x=1\) if it is the first crossing input after one of the closing arcs \(2,\ldots,b\), and \(x=0\) otherwise. The first cut has no shift. At a crossing replace its south-sector assignment \(a^0\) by \[ a^*_{(e,e')}=a^0_{(e,e')}-(x_{e'}-x_e). \tag{5} \] All four \(W\) arguments agree. The change in its explicit prefactor is \(q^{-x_{\rm under,1}-x_{\rm under,2}}\). Let \(U\) denote the sum of these local under-port shifts, and let \(n_-\) count negative crossings. The unnormalized enhanced open operator \(T\) therefore satisfies \[ T_{ij}=q^{\epsilon(b-1)-n_- -U}\,q^i O_{a^*}(i,j). \tag{6} \] Every internal wire has exactly one output factor. The remaining output factor is precisely \(q^i\) at the free output; neither end has been given a new mark. Here is the face check in (5). In the braid rectangle a crossing terminates the gap below it and starts the gap above it. Every finite gap region receives its one south-sector charge. Each of the \(b-1\) initial gap regions also terminates once, while the terminal gap regions have no south charge. Every adjacent braid generator must occur: otherwise the closure permutation preserves a proper initial set of strands and the closure is not one component. The nested outside band \(R_j\), \(1\le j<b\), joins the initial and terminal gap \(j\); initially its charge is 1. The innermost band \(R_b\), touching the right exterior gap, initially has charge 0. The cut merges \(R_1\) with the outside region \(R_0\). The input shift from closing arc \(j\ge2\) transfers one charge from the region on the left of that initial strand, \(R_{j-1}\), to the one on its right, \(R_j\). This holds whether its first crossing uses that strand as the left or right input: substitution in (5) subtracts 1 from its left corner and adds 1 to its right corner. Consequently every bounded region has total 1 and the outer region has total 0. These statements count occurrences, so repeated boundary walks cause no change. Individual outer corners of \(a^*\) need not vanish. We compare it directly with any admissible \(\chi\), whose existence is proved in Section 2. The corner difference \(\delta=\chi-a^*\) has zero sum at every crossing and around every bounded face. The expanded-circle proof in [G, Section 2] therefore integrates it to edge potentials \(z_e\): existence uses these bounded-face sums, not the individual outer-corner condition. Explicitly, give the old edges increment zero and the circle corners increment \(\delta\); the bounded-face boundaries generate the integral cycle group, so path integration is single-valued, including repeated edges and bridges. On the old \(R_0\) side of the outermost cut, all corners of \(a^*\) are individually zero. Indeed this is the outside of the outermost closing arc, meeting only the left exterior gap and no shifted closing input. The corners of \(\chi\) there are also zero. This one boundary path from one free end to the other has increment zero, so the two end potentials agree. Subtract their common value to make both zero. Thus \(\delta=z_{e'}-z_e\) with the original end colors fixed; no consistency of separately assigned repeated-edge values is assumed. The literal color substitution gives \(O_\chi=q^{\Omega(z)}O_{a^*}\), where \[ \Omega(z)=\sum_{e\text{ internal}}z_e- \sum_v(z_{\rm under,1}+z_{\rm under,2}). \tag{7} \] The scalarity of \(T\) in (6) proves (2), by evaluating the same formula at \(i=j=0\). All phases are retained, even if this value is zero. Explicitly, if \(w\) is the braid writhe and \(J_N\) is the normalized enhanced period of [P], then \[ O_\chi(0,0)=q^\Gamma J_N,\qquad \Gamma=\Omega(z)-\epsilon(b-1)+n_-+U+\epsilon w. \tag{8} \] No assertion of independence from a new off-root lift is made. ## 2. A global integral sector assignment There is an explicit level-independent 0/1 admissible assignment. Checkerboard-color the regions of the closed shadow. Its black and white Tait graphs are dual, have \(c\) edges, and their vertex counts sum to \(c+2\). The cut edge is adjacent to one black and one white root region. Choose a spanning tree \(T\) of the black graph. Its complementary dual edges form a spanning tree \(T^*\) of the white graph: a dual cycle would separate the primal tree, and the edge count is exactly the number of dual vertices minus one. For a crossing whose black edge is in \(T\), give charge 1 to the black corner farther from the black root along \(T\). Otherwise give charge 1 to the white corner farther from the white root in \(T^*\). Give all other corners zero. Each crossing has exactly one 1. Each nonroot region receives exactly one, at its parent tree edge, and both roots receive zero. After cutting, those roots form the outer region. A loop is never chosen as a tree edge; the dual of a primal bridge is not in the complementary dual tree. Thus the construction also covers repeated regions and multiple edges. The selected child endpoint of a tree edge is a particular corner occurrence, not a possibly repeated region name. This proves the hypotheses used in Section 1 without solving a level-dependent linear system. We use this \(\chi\) below. ## 3. The actual three-ball and one global vertex order The closed shadow has a dual quadrilateral cellulation of \(S^2\), with \(c\) cells, \(2c\) sides, and \(c+2\) region vertices. Cut its side dual to the chosen knot edge. The result is a disk \(Q\) with \(2c-1\) paired interior sides and two free boundary sides. It has \(c\) interior region vertices and the two root vertices on its boundary. This remains an incidence description when cell boundaries repeat. The knot edge separates two distinct checkerboard regions, so the cut is along an embedded side, not a loop in the dual surface. Suspend \(Q\) between poles \(\mathsf P,\mathsf S\). Each region vertex sweeps an arc from \(\mathsf P\) to \(\mathsf S\), designated as one edge; its midpoint is not an additional vertex of the chosen cell structure. The suspension of a side is a bigon disk between two such pole edges. Subdivide it by its material midpoint \(m\) into the two triangles \(\mathsf Pm\mathsf S\). The boundary of each suspended quadrilateral is consequently the four paired port disks of the nine-cell ball [S]. Replace that ball by its literal nine tetrahedra, preserving all eight individual boundary triangles and their orders. This is a replacement of a ball by a ball relative to its boundary. The assembled space is the suspension of a disk, hence a three-ball. The description of a region arc as one edge is only a choice of PL cell structure; subdividing that arc recovers the usual suspension coordinates. The nine-ball link edges \(13,24\) give exactly the two original crossing strands with their overpassing data. For an explicit local model place its central tetrahedral vertices at \(1=(1,0,-t),2=(0,1,t),3=(-1,0,-t),4=(0,-1,t)\), \(t>0\). Their oriented determinant is \(8t>0\); edge \(24\) is above edge \(13\) in the planar projection. The other cells attach around this central tetrahedron as in [S] and retain these two arcs and the four cyclic boundary ports. Use the indicated individual boundary triangles when identifying its ball with the suspended quadrilateral, without adding a boundary twist. Side gluing gives the original cut knot. Its remaining boundary is the four-triangle sphere \[ \mathsf Pa\mathsf S^\pm,\qquad \mathsf Pb\mathsf S^\pm, \tag{9} \] with two distinct \(\mathsf P\mathsf S\) edges and no boundary edge \(ab\). Its four vertices are \(\mathsf P,\mathsf S,a,b\). To meet the primary's actual total vertex order and injective decoration requirement, insert the two-cell collar [I] on **every** internal wire. Topologically, inflate the corresponding side of \(Q\) to a bigon between parallel copies with the same two region endpoints. This refines the same disk. Suspending that bigon is the collar ball: its side midpoints are the two material vertices, and its core edge subdivides the original strand. Thus no new region vertex or extra pole detour is introduced. Every crossing port is a distinct global material vertex. Order the poles first and last, and order the blocks in any sequence, with the four material vertices inside each block in its required cyclic order \(1<2<3<4\). This is one total order on all vertices, not an arbitrary collection of local branchings. Each collar uses the appropriate one of the two recipes [I,(2)], so its order is also the restriction of this same global order. Self-adjacent wires are handled in exactly this way: the two ports of the same crossing remain distinct vertices connected by a collar. Give \(h=1\) to incoming crossing ports and \(h=0\) to outgoing ports. Each crossing has two of each, so \(\sum h_m=2\). On a wire the charges are complementary; [I] supplies \(h=1\to0\) in either order relative to its two material vertices. Its port ordering is literal: at one end the positive/negative face labels are \((\alpha,\alpha')\), and at the other they are \((B',B)\). Thus its difference coordinates are \(\alpha'-\alpha+h_L\) and \(B-B'+h_R\), as in [I,(14)]. They glue to the opposite ordered port of [S], not to an independently chosen Fourier transform. All old side and region occurrences remain. Choose distinct real numbers on all these global vertices, and choose each odd root \(s_{uv}\) real, with \(s_{vu}=-s_{uv}\). Use positive square roots of the real divided-difference brackets. Every local tetrahedron has distinct vertices; all of its Fermat factors and normalizations are regular. The real decoration need not be increasing in the global vertex order. This is the common branch on which [C] gives its exact modulus for every block. For the closing calculation name the two free material vertices \(a<b\) in this global order. If \(a\) is the input rather than the output, the array in (13) is the transpose of (1). Identity (2) is unchanged by this transpose, and its \(00\) value is unchanged. Thus the cap below uses the same global total order, with no unproved endpoint permutation. ## 4. The entire open tetrahedral source Let \(C_v=C_N(\mathbf s_v)\) be exactly [C,(4)]. For the local sector \(\chi_v=(x,y,\zeta,w)\), put \[ \phi_v=3(h_1-1)/2+d_{\chi_v}+\zeta+w, \] \[ d_\chi=\zeta-2y+w/2-\tfrac32(\zeta+w)h_1 +\tfrac32y h_2-\tfrac32\zeta h_4. \tag{10} \] The complete local identity [C,(38)] is \[ B_v=C_v q^{\phi_v}s_{\mathsf P\mathsf S}^{d} \sum_{i_1,\ldots,i_4}R_v(\mathbf i\mid\chi_v) \prod_{m=1}^4\mathcal A_{v,m}(i_m). \tag{11} \] It includes the original six internal sums and all ordinary local edge weights. The adapter is \[ \mathcal A_h(i)=q^{ik}f(k),\qquad k=\alpha_- -\alpha_+ +h,\qquad f(k)=s_{\mathsf Pm}^{[k-1]}s_{m\mathsf S}^{[-k]}. \tag{12} \] The bar on an opposite tetrahedron denotes its literal dual tensor, never a Hermitian adjoint. One oppositely ordered port identification has raw pairing \(N^2(s_{\mathsf Pm}s_{m\mathsf S})^d Z\). Its two new ordinary edges contribute the inverse decoration power, and its one newly interior material vertex contributes \(N^{-1}\). The normalized joining tensor is therefore \(S=NZ\). The collar has tensor \(K=Z^{-1}/N\), and \(SKS=S\), with no phase [I,(16)--(20)]. It commutes with the literal \(E_{00}\) cut. Thus inserting the collars changes neither the physical wire nor its original pointing. There are \(2c-1\) effective internal wires. There are exactly \(c\) interior region edges \(\mathsf P\mathsf S\), each ordinary because its sector charges sum to 1. Their weights cancel the \(c\) factors \(s_{\mathsf P\mathsf S}^d\) in (11), even though the edges have the same endpoints. Hence the actual open source is \[ \boxed{\quad B_Q=K_{\rm open}\sum_{i,j}O_\chi(i,j)\, \mathcal A_a(i)\mathcal A_b(j),\qquad K_{\rm open}=N^{2c-1}\prod_v C_v q^{\phi_v}. \quad} \tag{13} \] On the common real branch, \[ |K_{\rm open}|=N^{-1}. \tag{14} \] This is a boundary tensor identity, not a count substituted for a contraction. With collars expanded there are \(4c-2\) actual joins and \(2c-1\) collar tensors; their product is exactly the same \(N^{2c-1}\) and the same original wire clocks. Every tetrahedron, edge, vertex and face sum has been included. ## 5. The literal empty cap and its Hamiltonian route Fill (9) with two oppositely oriented tetrahedra \((0,a,b,5)=(\mathsf P,a,b,\mathsf S)\), glued across \(0ab\) and \(ab5\), namely faces 3 and 0. Their sole interior edge is \(ab\); the remaining faces are the two copies of \(0a5\) and \(0b5\). Declare \(ab\) ordinary. Close the material knot along the boundary path \[ a-0-5-b, \tag{15} \] using one of the two distinct \(05\) edges. This simple boundary path is pushed into the cap ball and is boundary-parallel there. The cap and open source have the same four boundary triangles, four pole-to-material edges and two \(05\) edges. Their individual face matching is a homeomorphism of the boundary spheres. Its radial extension identifies the two-ball union with \(S^3\). The remaining tangle meets that sphere only at \(a,b\); the simple arc (15), pushed into a collar, is the usual boundary-parallel closing arc up to isotopy relative to that tangle. Thus the pair is the original knot in \(S^3\). It visits both poles once, and every material vertex now has exactly two incident link edges. Let \(h_a+h_b=1\) be the two incoming open port charges. In the opposite-pair convention \(0a|b5,0b|a5,05|ab\), choose cap triples \[ (\lambda,\epsilon-\lambda,0),\qquad (-h_b-\lambda,h_b-\epsilon+\lambda,1). \tag{16} \] Each sums to \(\epsilon\). Together with the old port charges, the totals on \(0a,b5\) are 0, and those on \(0b,a5\) are 1. The selected \(05\) edge has total 0, the other total 1, and the interior \(ab\) has total 1. Thus (15) is the actual admissible Hamiltonian route. We henceforth take \(\lambda=-h_b\). We compute the cap instead of replacing it by \(E_{00}\). Write \(X=s_{05}s_{ab}\), \(Y=s_{0a}s_{b5}\), \(Z=s_{0b}s_{a5}\), so \(X^N+Y^N=Z^N\). The literal kernels [S,(3)] give \[ \sum_{x,y}T(\lambda,0)_{xB}^{Ay} \bar T(-h_b-\lambda,1)_{A'y}^{xB'} =X^d q^{3(h_b+\lambda)/2} \delta_{A'-A,h_b}\delta_{B'-B,h_b}. \tag{17} \] Here is an endpoint-inclusive proof. The two conservation deltas give \(\Delta=A'-A=B'-B\). Put \(n=A-\lambda-x\) and \(L=\Delta-h_b\). The remaining phase is \(q^{n+\Delta+\lambda+(h_b+\lambda)/2}\), and its ratio is \(W(n)/\bar W(n+L)\), with Fermat triple \((X,Y,Z)\). For \(1\le L<N\), \[ \frac{W(n)}{\bar W(n+L)} =(Z-X)Y^{-L}\prod_{j=1}^{L-1}(Z-Xq^{n+j}). \] After multiplication by \(q^n\), all its frequencies are between 1 and \(N-1\), so its cyclic sum is zero. For \(L=0\), \[ \sum_n q^n\frac{W(n)}{\bar W(n)} =\frac{N X^d(Z-X)}{Y^N}. \] This follows by completing \(1/(Z-Xq^n)\) to the full cyclic product. Multiplication by the independently proved \(\rho\bar\rho=Y^N/[N(Z-X)]\) gives (17), including the case \(L=0\) and every cyclic carry. The face orders in this gluing are also fixed. On the source side they give \(k_a=A'-A+h_a=1\), and \(k_b=B-B'+h_b=0\). Hence its physical row is proportional to \(q^i f_a(1)f_b(0)\), where \[ f_a(1)=s_{a5}^d,\qquad f_b(0)=s_{0b}^d. \] The two unconstrained common indices \(A,B\) supply \(N^2\). The cap's new ordinary edge weights are precisely those of \(ab,a5,0b\) and the ordinary \(05\) copy; they cancel \(X^d f_a(1)f_b(0)\). All **four** vertices \(0,5,a,b\) of the open boundary now become interior, contributing \(N^{-4}\). Thus the normalized cap row, for the source convention [K,(4.19)], is \[ N^{-2}q^{3(h_b+\lambda)/2}q^i =N^{-2}q^i. \tag{18} \] It is not a local \(E_{00}\) tensor and is not asserted equal to one on arbitrary exterior states. Its action on this whole open source is determined by (2). ## 6. Exact closed comparison and its scope Let \(Z_{\rm lit}\) be the literal closed source with its factor \(N^{-\#\mathrm{vertices}}\), as in [K,(4.19)]. Equations (2),(13),(18) give \[ Z_{\rm lit} =N^{-2}K_{\rm open}\sum_{i,j}q^iO_\chi(i,j) =N^{-1}K_{\rm open}O_\chi(0,0). \tag{19} \] The primary's closed normalization is \(N^2Z_{\rm lit}\). Consequently the full exact formula is \[ \boxed{\quad N^2 Z_{\rm lit} =\left(\prod_{v=1}^c N^2 C_N(\mathbf s_v)q^{\phi_v}\right) O_\chi(0,0). \quad} \tag{20} \] Every phase in (20) is specified by (4) of [C] and (10) above. For distinct real decorations the multiplier has modulus exactly 1. Together with (8), this also gives the normalized enhanced period with its recorded root phase, rather than an unidentified scalar. The equality holds even at a level where that period vanishes. The construction uses a supplied one-component braid presentation; it makes no separate claim about transporting the sector adapter through every arbitrary Morse presentation. Repeated face occurrences are retained explicitly. If the primary notation identifies sectors merely by the pair \((v,f)\), its literal applicability is restricted to diagrams without such repetitions; our finite source specifies the corner extension throughout, with the same proved local tensors. The proof assigns the actual link, charges, total vertex order, injective decorations, and fixed cut. It is not an invariance theorem for all triangulations, a positive geometric development, an off-root meridian family, or a transport of a selected integration cycle. In particular it supplies no nonvanishing or volume lower bound. ## Complete direct sources - [K] Kashaev, *A Link Invariant from Quantum Dilogarithm*, q-alg/9504020v1, complete primary definitions. title: A braid-compatible retraction onto the original saturated source
text:
# A braid-compatible retraction onto the original saturated source 24 November 2026. Written research proof. The divided-current source equation has a retraction that commutes with every original regular braid. In the coherent corner coordinates this retraction is an explicit finite polynomial in the actual middle divided currents. Its source and complementary spaces therefore remain separate through overlapping crossings and through regular linear cup/cap maps. A positive metric makes this separation orthogonal, agrees with the physical metric on the source, and retains the original polynomial input/closing budget. A second specified metric gives a uniform divided-current repair gap for the entire source equation. These metrics have different budget statements, made explicit below. Neither estimates the scalar carried by the restricted word nor identifies a geometric contributing saddle. ## 1. The physical root source and its full divided currents Use the actual conventions of [D,K,M,C]. Put \[ N\ge2,\quad d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2, \quad x=q^d=-q^{-1},\quad \varrho=q-q^{-1}. 	ag{1} \] On the original orthonormal head \(V=\mathbb C^N\), \[ E|aangle=(Q^{-a}-1)|a-1angle,\quad F|aangle=(1-Q^{a+1})|a+1angle,\quad K|aangle=xQ^{-a}|aangle, \quad H|aangle=(d-2a)|aangle . 	ag{2} \] Missing endpoint arrows vanish. Ordered totals use \(E_{12}=E_1K_2+E_2\), \(F_{12}=F_1+K_1^{-1}F_2\), \(K_{12}=K_1K_2\), and additive unrolled \(H\). All norms and adjoints below use physical Euclidean coordinates unless a metric is specified. For \(b=2k\) heads let \(T_b=V^{\otimes b}\) and define \[ \mathcal Z_b=\ker E_b\cap\ker F_b\cap\ker(K_b-I),\qquad \mathcal I_b=\mathcal Z_b\cap\ker H_b. 	ag{3} \] The unrolled weight is retained: \(\mathcal Z_b\) includes all its weights \(H_b=2Nj\), whereas \(\mathcal I_b\) is its weight-zero part. Let \(\mathcal S_b\subset\mathcal I_b\) be the saturated specialization of the regular generic invariant tensors, in the actual balanced lattice. It is the original deformable source, not the whole root invariant space. Define the full first-normal currents by generic division before specialization: \[ J_{E,b}=\left[ rac{E_b(\zeta)^N}{1-\zeta^{2N}}ight]_q, \qquad J_{F,b}=\left[ rac{F_b(\zeta)^N}{1-\zeta^{2N}}ight]_q. 	ag{4} \] Their ordered divided coproduct is regular by [K]. Every nonzero local factorial index is less than \(N\). The scalar relating either current to its divided power is the same: \[ \alpha_N=  rac{Nq^{-N(N-1)/2}}{(1-Q)^N}. 	ag{5} \] Thus these are specified physical matrices at every level, including even and composite levels; (4) does not divide a zero root matrix. Both currents preserve \(\mathcal Z_b\). Here is the mixed-commutator check needed for this assertion. For the standard generator \(e_\zeta=E/(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})^2\), the elementary finite identity is \[ [e_\zeta^{[n]},F] =e_\zeta^{[n-1]}  rac{\zeta^{n-1}K-\zeta^{1-n}K^{-1}} {\zeta-\zeta^{-1}}. 	ag{6} \] It follows by summing the \(n\) ordinary commutators before dividing by \([n]_\zeta!\). There is an analogous identity for \([e_\zeta,F^{[n]}]\), with a Cartan coefficient multiplying \(F^{[n-1]}\). At \(n=N\), specialization and (5) show that \([J_{E,b},F_b]\) factors through \(E_b^{N-1}\) and that \([E_b,J_{F,b}]\) factors through \(F_b^{N-1}\). Those factors kill \(\mathcal Z_b\), since \(N\ge2\); the intervening Cartan operators preserve the ordinary kernels. Each current commutes with its own ordinary generator, and its Cartan character is \(Q^{\pm N}=1\). This proves preservation of all three kernels in (3), including \(N=2\). The unrolled weights change by \(+2N,-2N\). The actual divided commutation calculation [D] on the full physical \(K_b=1\) sector gives \[ [J_{E,b},J_{F,b}]=-NH_b. 	ag{7} \] Consequently on \(\mathcal Z_b\) the operators \[ e=J_{E,b}/N,\qquad f=-J_{F,b}/N,\qquad h=H_b/N 	ag{8} \] satisfy exactly \([e,f]=h\), \([h,e]=2e\), \([h,f]=-2f\). No physical Hermitian relation between these operators is assumed. ## 2. A full-current retraction commuting with the braid word On the weight-two part of \(\mathcal Z_b\), put \[ R=\sum_{j=0}^{k-2}  rac{(-1)^j f^{j+1}e^j}{(j+1)!(j+2)!}. 	ag{9} \] For \(k=1\) that weight space is zero and the sum is empty. Indeed \(|H_b|\le2k(N-1)<2kN\), so the possible weights of \(h\) lie between \(-2(k-1)\) and \(2(k-1)\). For a weight-two vector \(v\), the ordinary relations give \[ ef^{j+1}e^jv=f^{j+1}e^{j+1}v +(j+1)(j+2)f^je^jv. 	ag{10} \] The successive terms telescope to \(eR=I\). The final term vanishes by the displayed weight bound. Therefore on \(\mathcal I_b\) \[  oxed{\quad \Pi_b=I-Re =I+\sum_{m=1}^{k-1}  rac{J_{F,b}^{m}J_{E,b}^{m}} {N^{2m}m!(m+1)!}. \quad} 	ag{11} \] It satisfies \(e\Pi_b=0\), is the identity on \(\ker e\), and hence \(\Pi_b^2=\Pi_b\). The complete source theorem [D], on the full invariant tensor rather than only its extraction, says \[  oxed{\quad \operatorname{ran}\Pi_b =\mathcal I_b\cap\ker J_{E,b}=\mathcal S_b. \quad} 	ag{12} \] Its redundant \(J_F\) equation is retained. For \(b=2\), the invariant space is the original cup line and (11) is the identity. The unit space at \(b=0\) also has identity retraction. Every original regular generic signed braid intertwines the total generic \(E,F,K,H\). Taking a power, dividing by the common scalar in (4), and specializing gives commutation with both full currents. It follows term by term in (11) that \[ R_i^{\pm1}\Pi_b=\Pi_bR_i^{\pm1} \quad\hbox{on }\mathcal I_b. 	ag{13} \] The same conclusion holds for any specified regular generic linear Hopf, unrolled-weight intertwiner, including the original interval Casimir polynomials and regular circle coupons. It retains their actual confluent Casimir data; no repeated-root derivative has been deleted. This is stronger than knowing only that a braid preserves \(\mathcal S_b\): its complementary space \(\ker\Pi_b\) is preserved as well. For any braid word, a complementary component cannot return to the source under a later overlapping crossing. ## 3. The explicit projector in the coherent corner coordinates Let \(b=2k\ge4\), \(W=V^{\otimes(2k-2)}\), \(D=(k-1)d\), and let \(W_D\) be its physical central-degree space. The coherent corner isomorphism [C] is \[ \mathscr F_b:\mathcal I_b\longrightarrow W_D, \qquad \mathscr F_b\Phi=c_{m edge}\,q_0\Phi, \qquad q_0\Phi= rac{x^{2d}}{N^2}\Phi_{0,W,d}. 	ag{14} \] Here \(c_{m edge}
e0\) is the exact original constant of [C]. Formula (14) also defines the coefficient extraction on every weight of \(\mathcal Z_b\). In fact it extends to an isomorphism \(q_0:\mathcal Z_b	o\ker(K_W-I)\), with all unrolled weights retained. Here is an elementary proof of this larger assertion. Let \(A=V\otimes V\) and \(v=|d,0angle\). For \(0\le a,b<N\), the actual coproduct gives \[ F_A^bv=x^b(Q;Q)_b|d,bangle. 	ag{14a} \] In \(E_A^aF_A^bv\), the unique term using only first-head lowerings is a nonzero multiple of \(|d-a,bangle\). Every other term has second occupation less than \(b\). Ordering by that occupation proves that the \(N^2\) vectors \(E_A^aF_A^bv\) are a triangular basis of \(A\). The ordinary root quantum algebra acting on even blocks has \(E^N=F^N=0\), \(K^N=1\). Reordering its elementary commutator shows that its induced left module \(U/U(K-I)\) is spanned by the same \(N^2\) monomials. The map sending its cyclic vector to \(v\) is therefore an isomorphism. For every even middle block this gives \[ \operatorname{Hom}_{U}(A,W)\longrightarrow\ker(K_W-I), \qquad f\longmapsto f(v) \quad\hbox{bijectively}. 	ag{14b} \] The ordinary cup/cap snake identities in [M] identify the left-hand space with \(\mathcal Z_b\), without imposing an unrolled-weight-zero condition. Literal currying gives \(f(v)=q_0\Phi_f\) just as in [C]. Since the two extracted end weights cancel, \(q_0H_b=H_Wq_0\). This proves the full graded isomorphism and includes all endpoint arrows; it assumes no semisimple quantum decomposition. Both full currents have a definite parity under this extraction: \[  oxed{\quad q_0J_{E,b}=(-1)^dJ_{E,W}q_0, \qquad q_0J_{F,b}=(-1)^dJ_{F,W}q_0 \quad\hbox{on }\mathcal Z_b. \quad} 	ag{15} \] We give a direct ordered-coproduct proof, without differentiating the root extraction. Put \(v=\Phi_{0,W,d}\). The ordinary invariant equations at the two ends imply \[ \Phi_{a,W,d}= rac{(-1)^aE_W^a}{(Q;Q)_a}v, \qquad \Phi_{0,W,d-a}= rac{F_W^a}{(Q;Q)_a}v, \quad 0\le a<N. 	ag{16} \] For example the first recursion is \((1-Q^{a+1})\Phi_{a+1,W,d}+E_W\Phi_{a,W,d}=0\). The second is \((1-Q^{a+1})\Phi_{0,W,d-a-1}=F_W\Phi_{0,W,d-a}\). They use \(K_b\Phi=\Phi\), not the additional condition \(H_b=0\). In a term of the divided \(E_b^{[N]}\) coproduct contributing to output end colors \((0,d)\), the last local exponent is zero. If the first exponent is \(a\), then \(0\le a<N\), and the middle exponent is \(N-a\). For \(a>0\), move the middle Cartan power past the first string in (16). The remaining middle operator contains \(E_W^{N-a}E_W^a=E_W^N=0\) at the root; all the local factorials in this mixed term are nonzero. Thus every mixed term vanishes. The \(a=0\) term is the full middle divided current times \(K_{m last}^N=(x^{-1})^N=(-1)^d\). The common normal factor is (5), proving the first identity (15). For \(F_b^{[N]}\), output first color zero forces its first exponent zero. If the last exponent is positive the second string in (16) gives \(F_W^N=0\); the surviving term retains \(K_{m first}^{-N}=x^{-N}=(-1)^d\). This proves the second identity, with the same sign at even as at odd levels. The signs in (15) cancel in every paired current product. Hence the transported retraction is the explicit middle polynomial \[  oxed{\quad P_b:=\mathscr F_b\Pi_b\mathscr F_b^{-1} =I_{W_D}+\sum_{m=1}^{k-2}  rac{J_{F,W}^{m}J_{E,W}^{m}} {N^{2m}m!(m+1)!}. \quad} 	ag{17} \] The missing \(m=k-1\) term is zero: it would lower middle degree \(D=(k-1)(N-1)\) by \((k-1)N>D\). In particular (17) is empty at four heads. Its range is precisely \[ \mathscr F_b\mathcal S_b =\ker(J_{E,W}:W_D\longrightarrow W_{D-N}), 	ag{18} \] with zero target when appropriate, as already identified in [C,D]. If \(B_i=\mathscr F_b R_i\mathscr F_b^{-1}\), then \[ [P_b,B_i^{\pm1}]=0. 	ag{19} \] This includes the two actual boundary Casimir braid polynomials in [C], as well as every interior crossing. Formula (17) has the same finite-current shape as the earlier prefix projector [D]. The proof here establishes its braid commutation in this specified corner chart; it does not identify two different extraction charts without their actual coordinate change. ## 4. Linear gluing and its tensor-product limit Let \(T_\zeta:T_b(\zeta)	o T_{b'}(\zeta)\) be any specified regular generic linear Hopf intertwiner preserving unrolled weight. Then its root map intertwines both full divided currents. The finite sums (11) can be padded with zero terms to a common length, because powers beyond each physical weight range vanish. Consequently \[ T\Pi_b=\Pi_{b'}T \quad\hbox{on }\mathcal I_b. 	ag{20} \] Thus an ordinary cup insertion, ordinary cap contraction, regular linear sewing, or composition of these with actual braids carries source to source and complement to complement. On nontrivial corner packets the transported map \(\widetilde T=\mathscr F_{b'}T\mathscr F_b^{-1}\) obeys \(\widetilde T P_b=P_{b'}\widetilde T\). The marked row is not a Hopf map and is handled by the original closing in the next section, rather than by (20). This is naturality for a linear map on the complete incoming packet. It is not a monoidal identity \(\Pi_{b+b'}=\Pi_b\otimes\Pi_{b'}\). Nontrivial ordinary divided- \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) factors can couple to a trivial factor. Therefore one cannot independently project two arbitrary inputs before a binary tensor operation and infer that their full coupled source is retained. One first forms the complete incoming tensor and uses its full projector. ## 5. A compatible positive metric with the original closing On each corner packet define \(Q_b=I-P_b\) and \[ G_b=P_b^\dagger P_b+Q_b^\dagger Q_b, \qquad \|v\|_{G_b}^2=\|P_bv\|^2+\|Q_bv\|^2. 	ag{21} \] This is an explicit metric of the level and fixed source representation, independent of the word or its unknown scalar. The elementary triangle inequality gives \[ G_b\succeq	frac12 I,\qquad G_bP_b=P_b^\dagger P_b=P_b^\dagger G_b. 	ag{22} \] Thus source and complement are orthogonal, and \(P_b\) is their orthogonal projection in this metric. On either subspace separately the metric equals the original physical metric. No upper polynomial bound for \(G_b\), its condition number, or \(\|P_b\|\) is asserted. For every intertwiner \(A\) with \(AP_b=P_{b'}A\), one has \[ \|Av\|_{G_{b'}}^2 =\|AP_bv\|^2+\|AQ_bv\|^2 \le\|A\|_{m physical}^2\|v\|_{G_b}^2. 	ag{23} \] In particular all actual reduced braid matrices satisfy \(\|B_i^{\pm1}\|_{G_b}\le\|B_i^{\pm1}\|_{m physical}\). This statement does not make the physical crossing norm small. Keep the exact corner input and literal original row [C]: \[ z_{m in}=c_{m edge}|dangle\otimes p^{\otimes(k-2)}\otimes|0angle, \qquad \lambda_D=c_{m edge}^{-1}\langle0,d| (I\otimes\ell^{\otimes(k-2)}\otimes I). 	ag{24} \] All turn powers, pivots, framing and any original external scalar \(\chi_N\) remain as prescribed. This literal row already annihilates the full divided currents: \[  oxed{\quad \lambda_DJ_{E,W}=\lambda_DJ_{F,W}=\lambda_DH_W=0, \qquad \lambda_DP_b=\lambda_D. \quad} 	ag{24a} \] To prove the current identities on the full physical middle tensor, put \(A=V\otimes V\). The map \(L_{m int}=I\otimes\ell^{\otimes(k-2)}\otimes I:W	o A\) is a regular generic Hopf map. Generic division by the same normal factor therefore gives \(L_{m int}J_{E,W}=J_{E,A}L_{m int}\), and likewise for \(F\). The pair row \(\langle0,d|J_{E,A}\) would require input degree \(d+N=2N-1>2d\), and \(\langle0,d|J_{F,A}\) would require degree \(d-N=-1\). Both rows are zero at every \(N\ge2\). The unrolled equation follows because that pair row has weight zero and the ordinary caps preserve \(H\). Formula (17) now proves the last identity in (24a) on all of \(W_D\). This argument concerns the row after the proved whole invariant-tensor reduction [C]; it does not assert that the raw marked cap \(m\) is a Hopf map. The actual cup source satisfies \(P_bz_{m in}=z_{m in}\). Commutation (19) and (24a) show, for every original word \(B\), \[ \lambda_D BQ_b=0,\qquad \chi_N\lambda_D Bv=\chi_N\lambda_D BP_bv \quad\hbox{for every }v\in W_D. 	ag{25} \] Thus the unchanged original closing sees no complementary component, even for an arbitrary root packet input. This is a global invariant source quotient, rather than a local cap-null quotient through an untransported neighboring crossing. For any physical row \(\lambda\), orthogonality in (21) gives the exact dual identity \[ \|\lambda P_b\|_{G_b^*} =\|\lambda|_{\operatorname{ran}P_b}\|_{m physical,*} \le\|\lambda\|_{m physical}. 	ag{26} \] Indeed its value depends only on the source component, and its supremum is already attained by allowing only that component. Applying [C]'s exact physical boundary product yields \[  oxed{\quad \|z_{m in}\|_{G_b}\, \|\lambda_D\|_{G_b^*} \le\|z_{m in}\|\,\|\lambda_D\|=N^{k-2}. \quad} 	ag{27} \] If \(\chi_N\) is included in the row, the bound is multiplied by \(|\chi_N|\); no estimate for that separate original factor is implied. The compatible source restriction therefore introduces no exponential boundary cost and no source-to-complement-to-source excursions under the linear word. It retains every coherent contribution inside the source. ## 6. A quantitative gap for the complete source equation Put \(r=k-1\) and work on the full middle physical sector \[ \mathcal L_W= igoplus_{j\in\mathbb Z}W_{H_W=2Nj} =\ker(K_W-I). 	ag{28} \] Its weight-zero part is \(W_D\). On this whole sector the actual operators \(e=J_{E,W}/N\), \(f=-J_{F,W}/N\), \(h=H_W/N\) satisfy the ordinary relations (8), by [D]. Their possible \(h\) weights are even integers with \(|h|\le2r-2\); in particular \(e^{2r-1}=f^{2r-1}=0\). This is a statement about the actual divided currents, not a new replacement module. These matrices integrate to a specified representation \(ho:SU(2)	o GL(\mathcal L_W)\). One construction avoids a complete-reducibility assumption. Send the standard complex \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) generators to \(e,f,h\). On \(SL_2(\mathbb C)\) the right Maurer--Cartan form gives the matrix path equation \(U'=dho(g'g^{-1})U\), with \(U(0)=I\). The bracket identities make its curvature zero. Polar decomposition retracts this group onto \(SU(2)\cong S^3\), so it is simply connected; flat transport is independent of the path and respects multiplication. This constructs \(ho\), whose restriction to the displayed compact group is used below. Equivalently its Gauss-cell matrices are the finite exponentials in (32); their identities follow by differentiating the elementary \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) commutators. No root semisimplicity is used. With Haar measure of total mass one, define \[ \mathfrak G=\int_{SU(2)}ho(g)^\daggerho(g)\,dg. 	ag{29} \] It is positive and invariant. Differentiating the compact generators \(ih\), \(e-f\), \(i(e+f)\) gives \[ h^{\dagger_{\mathfrak G}}=h, \qquad e^{\dagger_{\mathfrak G}}=f. 	ag{30} \] Thus different \(h\) weights are orthogonal for this metric. The norm of a divided-current residual below is its norm in its actual output weight, not a norm on an incorrectly identified copy of \(W_D\). The metric has controlled exponential size in the physical frame. To check this using only the actual matrices, the ordered formula [K,(3),(5)] gives, up to phases, a nonzero \(J_E\) entry as \(N\prod_i{a_i rack b_i}_Q\), where each upper index is less than \(N\). For \(J_F\) the corresponding upper indices are the final occupations, also less than \(N\). A Gaussian polynomial has nonnegative integer coefficients, so its absolute value on the unit circle is bounded by the ordinary binomial coefficient. On \(n=2r\) physical heads this proves \[ \|J_{E,W}\|,\|J_{F,W}\| \le N^{n+1}2^{nd},\qquad \|e\|,\|f\|\le e^{C_rN}. 	ag{31} \] This bound involves no division by a small total root factorial. Use the exact finite positive rule (38), proved below without any metric-size estimate. Its fixed-width nodes have \(g_
u=\left( egin{smallmatrix}a&b\- ar b& ar a\end{smallmatrix}ight)\) with \(|a|\ge a_{\min}(r)>0\), since every Gaussian node has \(-1<t<1\). At each such node Gauss factorization gives \[ ho(g)=\exp(- ar b f/a)\,a^h\,\exp(be/a). 	ag{32} \] Both unipotent parameters and \(\|a^{\pm h}\|\) are bounded by width-only constants. The exponentials truncate at degree \(2r-2\). Equations (31),(32) and the finite rule therefore imply \[ \max_
u\|ho(g_
u)^{\pm1}\|\le e^{C_rN},\qquad e^{-C_rN}I\preceq\mathfrak G\preceq e^{C_rN}I. 	ag{33} \] For the lower bound keep any one positive-weight node and use its inverse bound. Thus the construction has linear logarithmic metric radius; exponentiating the possibly large number \(\|e\|\) was not used. For completeness the resulting weight-zero gap can be derived directly from (30). A highest vector \(v\), with \(ev=0\), \(hv=mv\), has \[ \|f^av\|_{\mathfrak G}^2 =a!\,m(m-1)\cdots(m-a+1)\|v\|_{\mathfrak G}^2. 	ag{34} \] The commutator proves this recurrence, and positivity and termination force \(m\) to be a nonnegative integer. All weights here are even, so \(m=2J\), \(J\in\{0,\ldots,r-1\}\). Each such chain and its \(\mathfrak G\)-orthogonal complement are invariant under \(e,f,h\). Removing a highest chain and repeating yields an orthogonal sum of these explicitly normalized chains. Matching their successive \(e,f,h\) coefficients with the monomials of \(\operatorname{Sym}^{2J}\mathbb C^2\) identifies each chain with that explicit polynomial representation: in its monomial basis \(f\) successively replaces a first coordinate by a second, and \(e\) reverses this with the coefficients from (34). Uniqueness along the chain fixes the group action as well. In particular its matrix coefficients are polynomials of degree \(2J\) in the fundamental group entries. On its weight-zero vector the normalized raising coefficient is \(\sqrt{J(J+1)}\). The \(J=0\) chains in \(W_D\) are exactly the actual saturated source (18). The projector (17) is their \(\mathfrak G\)-orthogonal projector: its range is \(\ker e\), and \(v-P_bv\) is in \(\operatorname{im}f\), perpendicular to that kernel by (30). Consequently, for every \(z\in W_D\), \[  oxed{\quad \|z-P_bz\|_{\mathfrak G} \le rac{1}{\sqrt2\,N}\|J_{E,W}z\|_{\mathfrak G}. \quad} 	ag{35} \] At widths or levels with no nontrivial chain this is the identity \(0\le0\). The formula therefore includes \(r=1\) and \(N=2\). It is a global normal estimate for the whole divided-current source equation, not a single marked-mode path estimate. Every source vector is fixed by \(ho\). Hence its \(\mathfrak G\) norm is exactly its physical norm, and, just as in (26), \[ \|\lambda_D\|_{\mathfrak G^*} =\|\lambda_D|_{\operatorname{ran}P_b}\|_{m physical,*}, \qquad \|z_{m in}\|_{\mathfrak G} \|\lambda_D\|_{\mathfrak G^*}\le N^{k-2}. 	ag{36} \] An original \(\chi_N\) multiplies the second factor by \(|\chi_N|\). Thus source repair uses a specified metric and the original boundary without an exponential boundary budget. The residual in (35) is measured in that metric; (33) does not imply a polynomial physical singular gap. The literal row itself is also group invariant: \(\lambda_Dho(g)=\lambda_D\) on \(\mathcal L_W\), by (24a). If an operator \(A\) on the full \(\mathcal L_W\) commutes with \(e,f,h\), it commutes with \(ho\), and integration gives \[ \|A\|_{\mathfrak G} \le\|A\|_{m physical,\mathcal L_W}. 	ag{37} \] Here the right-hand norm is explicitly the full-sector norm. A bound known only for a central-degree matrix is not substituted for it. The full isomorphism (14b), together with (15), supplies actual extensions \(\widetilde B_i=q_0R_iq_0^{-1}\) on \(\mathcal L_W\). They commute with \(e,f,h\), and restrict to the matrices \(B_i\) on \(W_D\). The same holds for regular linear maps between widths, since the sign in (15) is independent of the number of heads. For the two boundary Casimirs their extended formulas are exactly the \(L,R\) of [C,(29)] on \(K_W=1\): that endpoint derivation used only \(K_W=1\), not \(H_W=0\). Their signed braid polynomials retain all original Hermite data. Thus (37) applies to these actual extended gates, with their full-sector physical norm on its right. The separate metric \(G_b\) in (21) already gives (23) for all the actual central packet gates from the proved commutation with \(P_b\). No comparison losing that distinction is needed for (35),(36). The Haar formula can also be made an exact finite positive Gram of width-only size. After the orthogonal chain construction, every spin is an integer \(J\le r-1\). Use Euler angles \(\phi,\psi\) on the two diagonal circles and \(t=\cos\vartheta\) for the middle rotation. Take \(L=2r-1\) equally spaced nodes on each circle and the \(r\) Gauss--Legendre nodes for normalized measure \(dt/2\). Explicitly use \(\phi_a=2\pi a/L\), \(\psi_b=2\pi b/L\), and \[ g(\phi,t,\psi)=  egin{pmatrix}e^{i\phi/2}&0\0&e^{-i\phi/2}\end{pmatrix}  egin{pmatrix}\sqrt{(1+t)/2}&\sqrt{(1-t)/2}\ -\sqrt{(1-t)/2}&\sqrt{(1+t)/2}\end{pmatrix}  egin{pmatrix}e^{i\psi/2}&0\0&e^{-i\psi/2}\end{pmatrix}. 	ag{38a} \] The product weight is the normalized Gaussian weight divided by \(L^2\). Normalized Haar measure in these Euler coordinates is the product of the two uniform circle measures and \(dt/2\): the middle rotation Jacobian is \(\sin\vartheta\,d\vartheta=-dt\). Circle products of matrix coefficients have frequencies at most \(2r-2<L\), so the two circle sums perform their integrals exactly. The remaining terms have matching magnetic indices. Products of their middle-rotation coefficients are polynomials in \(t\) of degree at most \(J+J'\le2r-2\): each coefficient is a sum of monomials in \(\cos(\vartheta/2),\sin(\vartheta/2)\), and matching indices make both exponents even in the product. The \(r\)-node Gaussian rule is therefore exact. Thus for explicit positive, width-only weights, \[ \mathfrak G=\sum_{
u=1}^{r(2r-1)^2} w_
uho(g_
u)^\daggerho(g_
u), \qquad w_
u>0,\qquad\sum_
u w_
u=1. 	ag{38} \] The Gaussian rule itself can be obtained from the monic degree-\(r\) polynomial orthogonal to lower degrees for \(dt/2\). Its coefficients are rational moments. Orthogonality forces its \(r\) roots to be simple and inside \((-1,1)\): otherwise the product of its interior sign-change factors has degree less than \(r\) and gives a nonzero integral of fixed sign. Divide a polynomial of degree at most \(2r-1\) by this orthogonal polynomial and interpolate the remainder at its roots. This proves the Gaussian rule; its cardinals \(l_i\) have weights \(\int l_i=\int l_i^2>0\). The weights sum to one. Thus all group nodes and weights in (38) are algebraic and independent of \(N\). The represented node matrices are algebraic too: use (32), whose two exponentials are finite, and whose \(a^h\) has integer physical exponents. This does not require finding an unknown unitarizing change of basis. The center acts trivially because the spins are integers, so the ordinary normalized Euler rule on \(SO(3)\) equals the Haar average here. This finite formula evaluates the same actual Gram; it introduces no new state or positivity assumption about the marked scalar. ## 7. Exact source restriction in a linear residual compiler There is a direct minimization consequence for a specified linear word compiler. Allow packet spaces of different widths, actual linear maps \(A_iP_{i-1}=P_iA_i\), and fixed input \(v_0=z_{m in}\) in the source. For positive weights \(a_i,a_*\), a target \(c\in\mathbb C\), and the unchanged original closing row \(\lambda=\lambda P_m\), consider \[ \mathcal E(v_1,\ldots,v_m) =\sum_{i=1}^m a_i\|v_i-A_iv_{i-1}\|_{G_i}^2 +a_*|\lambda v_m-c|^2. 	ag{39} \] Every vector residual splits into its orthogonal source and complement parts. The closing term sees only the source part. Since \(Q_0v_0=0\), \[ \mathcal E(v)=\mathcal E(Pv) +\sum_{i=1}^m a_i \|Q_iv_i-A_iQ_{i-1}v_{i-1}\|^2. 	ag{40} \] Consequently projecting every trial packet cannot increase the energy or any upper ball constraint \(\|v_i\|_{G_i}\le R_i\). The infimum, with or without such balls, is exactly its restriction to source packets; the complementary minimum is zero. By (23), the original physical gate norm budgets also suffice in these metrics. This is exact deletion of nonsource variables in this legitimate linear compiler. It neither identifies its minimum with an unweighted scalar energy nor changes the distinct nonlinear Conway quartic problem. For a binary tensor operation the full coupled projector must be used; its metric need not be the tensor product of the two input metrics. ## 8. What the retraction settles [D,K] already identify the saturated source as an actual divided-current kernel and provide its finite polynomial projector. [M] already gives complete source coordinates and exact original boundaries. [C] already identifies the coherent corner projection and its polynomial boundary product. The additional points are the full-small-invariant construction (11), braid and linear-gluing naturality, its signed current transport (15), explicit commuting form (17), compatible metric budget (27), and the full-source repair estimate (35) in the specified finite Gram (38). The original corner row is itself divided-current invariant (24a), so the complementary part is invisible to every word closing (25). These statements concern fixed-root values. Differentiated generic families retain their full inhomogeneous Ward equations and the derivatives of any transported projector; the root formula does not silently make those equations homogeneous. Arbitrary root-only coupons without the specified regular generic lift are not covered by (20). The construction imposes the complete value source restriction before estimating a coherent word. Its repair gap is in \(\mathfrak G\), not a claimed polynomial physical singular gap for \(J_E\). It gives no sharp word energy or positive lower bound for the original marked scalar. The remaining estimate concerns the source-projected word recursion or gradient and its original closing. Formula (35) quantifies distance when comparing with an unprojected trial; exact source projection itself requires no small-current-residual premise. The finite-exception volume statement after arbitrary short partial fillings is unchanged by this compatibility result alone. ## Complete inputs | Label | Complete text | Lines | SHA256 | | --- | --- | ---: | --- | | D | [All-width divided-current source projection](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_all_width_divided_source_projection.md) | 204 | dc83b5e232a3d258f516a479d7257e85b9e5663a38e166f07c6ad9ae81004a68 | | K | [Actual six-port divided-power source kernel](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_six_port_divided_power_source_kernel.md) | 288 | e62a2612f0610f46278347db48024979c4f525ecca34c98c87048c4162c97fb0 | | M | [Complete original source multiplicities](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_complete_source_multiplicity_module.md) | 602 | 14cfb558f50c5b091cec9439692dfeb87129e31f38588cb1ebfd8e8547ac99a9 | | C | [Coherent marked-cap corner reduction](research_coherent_marked_cap_corner_reduction.md) | 466 | 6cf47746a43975723780aec77dc125846515b9c0115359fb1d5ce160f9858ca9 | Only written mathematics, source reads and text/hash operations were used. title: A logarithmic strip bound for every canonical crossing power

# A logarithmic strip bound for every canonical crossing power Private written proof, 23 November 2026. Every signed integer power of the original crossing has a canonical polynomial whose real-boundary norm is logarithmic in the level, with only linear dependence on the absolute power. The same estimate controls its whole periodic microscopic strip and every fixed parameter derivative. Both level parities and all first physical normals are retained. This improves a polynomial evaluation bound for the actual finite polynomial. It does not estimate a genuine turn or an original closing from below, and supplies no new volume-identity case. ## 1. The complete original data Fix \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), and the recorded phases \[ q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\quad \kappa=e^{\pi i d^2/(2N)},\quad P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2. \] For every \(n\in\mathbb Z\), let \(r_{n,N}\) be the canonical degree-below-\(N\) representative of \(\kappa^{-n}R^n\) in the original full algebra \(\mathbb C[z]/P_N\). Negative powers mean the actual inverse. Put \[ t_j=(2j+1)\pi/N,\quad c_j=2\cos t_j,\quad 
u_j=(-1)^jq^{j(j+1)},\quad g(t)=r_{n,N}(2\cos t). \] The complete source [F] gives exactly \[ h_j:=g(t_j)=
u_j^n,\qquad \gamma_j:=g'(t_j)=- rac{in}{2}(d-2j)h_j \quad(0\le j<N). 	ag{1} \] Thus \(|h_j|=1\), \(|\gamma_j|\le |n|N/2\), and \(\sum_j\gamma_j=0\). For the last assertion pair \(j,d-j\): their values agree and their derivatives are opposite. At odd \(N\) the self-paired node is \(-2\) and its angular derivative is zero. This imposes no additional spectral normal at that simple node. Define \[ M_{N,n}=1+|n|\left\{ rac\pi2+  rac4\pi(1+\log N)ight\}. 	ag{2} \] **Theorem.** Uniformly for all \(N\ge2\) and all integers \(n\), \[  oxed{\quad\max_{-2\le z\le2}|r_{n,N}(z)|\le M_{N,n}.\quad} 	ag{3} \] For \(w_N(\alpha)=2\cosh(\alpha/N)\), every \(r\ge0\) and integer \(k\ge0\) also satisfy \[ \sup_{|\Re\alpha|\le r} |r_{n,N}(w_N(\alpha))|\le e^rM_{N,n}, \] \[  oxed{\quad \sup_{|\Re\alpha|\le r} |\partial_\alpha^k r_{n,N}(w_N(\alpha))| \le k!e^{r+1}M_{N,n}. \quad} 	ag{4} \] There is no restriction on the imaginary height in these suprema. The unnormalized crossing has the retained scalar \(\kappa^n\), of modulus one, so its absolute bounds are identical. ## 2. Exact trigonometric Hermite interpolation For \(\delta=t-t_j\), define the removable trigonometric polynomials \[ K_j(t)= rac1{N^2} \left\{ rac{\sin(N\delta/2)}{\sin(\delta/2)}ight\}^2, \qquad L_j(t)= rac2{N^2}\sin^2(N\delta/2)\cot(\delta/2). 	ag{5} \] The finite geometric series gives \[ K_j(t)= rac1{N^2}\sum_{\ell=-(N-1)}^{N-1} (N-|\ell|)e^{i\ell(t-t_j)}, \] \[ L_j(t)= rac1{N^2}\left\{\sin(N\delta) +2\sum_{\ell=1}^{N-1}\sin(\ell\delta)ight\}. 	ag{6} \] At the grid, \(K_j(t_k)=\delta_{jk}\), \(K_j'(t_k)=0\), \(L_j(t_k)=0\), and \(L_j'(t_k)=\delta_{jk}\). The apparent singularity at \(\delta=0\) gives these same limits. For real \(t\), \(K_j(t)\ge0\), and finite character summation in (6) gives \(\sum_jK_j(t)=1\). The exact original polynomial is \[ g(t)=\sum_j h_jK_j(t)+\sum_j\gamma_jL_j(t). 	ag{7} \] Indeed its right side matches all values and angular derivatives. Its possible frequency-\(N\) term vanishes: since \(\sin(N(t-t_j))=-\sin Nt\), its coefficient is a multiple of \(\sum_j\gamma_j=0\). It therefore has trigonometric degree at most \(N-1\), like \(g\). Their difference, multiplied by \(e^{i(N-1)t}\), is a polynomial in \(e^{it}\) of degree at most \(2N-2\), with double zeros at the \(N\) distinct grid points. It vanishes identically. This argument includes even middle aliases and the odd simple spectral node through precisely the data (1). ## 3. The logarithmic norm and the whole strip Fix real \(t\), choose a closest grid point, and let its circular distance be \(a\le\pi/N\). All numerators \(\sin^2(N(t-t_j)/2)\) in (5) agree. The closest contribution obeys \[ |L_j(t)|\le rac2{N^2} rac{N^2a^2}{4} rac2a=a \le rac\pi N. \] At \(a=0\) use the removable limit. The other points at circular distance \(k\) grid steps have distance at least \((2k-1)\pi/N\), with at most two points at each step. Using \(|\cot(\delta/2)|\le2/|\delta|\) for \(0<|\delta|\le\pi\), and bounding the odd harmonic sum by \(H_N\le1+\log N\), gives \[ \sum_j|L_j(t)|\le rac1N \left\{\pi+ rac8\pi(1+\log N)ight\}. 	ag{8} \] The value part of (7) has modulus at most one by positivity and partition of unity. Combine (1) and (8) to prove (3). For completeness, if a polynomial \(p\) has degree at most \(d\) and real-interval norm \(M\), then \(H(\zeta)=\zeta^dp(\zeta+\zeta^{-1})\) is a polynomial bounded by \(M\) on the unit circle. The maximum principle in its disk, and replacement of \(\zeta\) by \(\zeta^{-1}\), give \[ |p(\zeta+\zeta^{-1})|\le M\max(|\zeta|,|\zeta|^{-1})^d. \] Take \(\zeta=e^{\alpha/N}\) and \(d=N-1\) to obtain the first bound in (4). Cauchy's formula on a unit disk about each \(\alpha\), using the strip of width \(r+1\), proves the derivative bound. These are fixed-root parameter derivatives, not moving-\(q\) normals. ## 4. The logarithmic factor is needed uniformly over all powers Take the actual level-dependent integer power \(n=2N\). Its data are \(h_j=1\) and \(b_j=\gamma_j/i=-N(d-2j)\). For \(1\le\ell<N\), the exact Fourier--Hermite formula [F] says \[ r_{2N,N}(z)=1+\sum_{\ell=1}^{N-1}2a_\ell T_\ell(z/2),\qquad a_\ell= rac1{N^2}\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}b_j e^{-i\ell t_j} = rac{i}{\sin(\ell\pi/N)}. 	ag{9} \] To check the last equality, put \(s=Q^{-\ell}
e1\). The finite geometric series and its derivative give \(\sum_js^j=0\), \(\sum_jjs^j=-N/(1-s)\); substitution in (9) gives \(-2q^{-\ell}/(1-Q^{-\ell})=i/\sin(\ell\pi/N)\). Consequently, at the endpoint itself, \[ r_{2N,N}(2)=1+2i\sum_{\ell=1}^{N-1}\csc(\ell\pi/N),\qquad |r_{2N,N}(2)|= rac4\pi N\log N+O(N). 	ag{10} \] For the asymptotic, subtract \(1/(\pi t)+1/(\pi(1-t))\) from \(\csc\pi t\). The difference is bounded on \([0,1]\). Its finite sum is \(O(N)\), whereas the two subtracted sums total \(2NH_{N-1}/\pi\). This proves (10). Thus a bound \((1+|n|)o(\log N)\) cannot hold uniformly over all integer powers. This sharpness uses \(n=2N\); it is not a growth claim for a fixed short filling. ## 5. Full-algebra multiplication in the same norm For a canonical polynomial \(f\), write \(M(f)=\max_{[-2,2]}|f|\), and put \(A_N=\pi+(8/\pi)(1+\log N)\). Let \(\operatorname{can}\) mean the remainder modulo the full \(P_N\), including every first normal. Then \[ M(\operatorname{can}(fg))\le(1+2eA_N)M(f)M(g), 	ag{11} \] and for every signed integer \(n\), \[ M(\operatorname{can}(r_{n,N}f)) \le\{1+(e+|n|/2)A_N\}M(f). 	ag{12} \] Indeed the strip proof applies to every canonical \(f\). Cauchy's formula on a unit disk gives \(|\partial_\alpha f(w_N(\alpha))|\le eM(f)\) on the imaginary axis. With \(\alpha=iNt\), this implies \(|\partial_t f(2\cos t)|\le eNM(f)\). The full product has nodal values bounded by \(M(f)M(g)\) and angular derivatives bounded by \(2eNM(f)M(g)\). Insert those data in (7) and use (8) to obtain (11). For (12), use the unit nodal values and the exact normal (1) instead. The angular derivatives sum to zero by reflection in both cases, including the self-paired odd simple node, so (7) is valid for the canonical full product. Quotient carries have already been retained; no semisimple projection is used. Thus the canonical multiplication constants in this norm grow only logarithmically with \(N\), with linear dependence on \(|n|\) for an actual crossing power. This is a Banach norm estimate; it supplies no comparison with a physical Hilbert metric. ## 6. Gain, limits and complete source versions The earlier circle estimate [K] gives coefficient mass \(2N(1+|n|/2)\); [F] already gives a polynomial real-boundary bound from its first-kind coefficients. The addition here is the logarithmic evaluation estimate for the canonical polynomial, its full periodic strip and derivatives, the full-product estimates (11)--(12), and the actual sharpness sequence (10). The more general free-boundary interpolation estimate [H] deliberately uses unoptimized polynomial cardinal bounds and concerns different data. Canonical reduction and the full physical normals remain essential. The estimates do not bound the Newton norm of a multiplication operator by \(M_{N,n}\), make a genuine turn harmless, compare its contour with an analytic representative without currents, or give a lower bound for the original cap. Arbitrary fixed short components still require their whole source and geometric comparison. No volume theorem is proved. All three complete matching texts were read; the proofs above use only written mathematics. title: A canonical finite splitting of the full Hermite filling kernel
text: # A canonical finite splitting of the full Hermite filling kernel Private written proof, 18 November 2026. The physical circle basis gives an explicit endomorphism whose image is exactly the kernel of the original filling functional. Its one-dimensional complement has a specified period normalizer. The endomorphism and its inverse on that kernel have polynomial norm bounds, for every fixed signed crossing power. This is finite algebra on the original full Hermite space. It neither replaces the closing functional nor supplies a lower bound for its value on an exterior source. In particular the conjugated endomorphism below is not identified with off-grid Gaussian averaging. The sole complete proof directs are **N**, the physical finite Newton calculus, and **F**, the actual Fourier--Hermite crossing-circle kernel. Their exact paths and pins are recorded at the end. ## 1. The physical space, row and circle basis Fix \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), and the original lifts \[ q=e^{\pi i/N},\qquad \kappa=q^{d^2/2},\qquad \mathcal H_N=\mathbb C[z]/(\chi_N),\qquad \chi_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2. \tag{1} \] The quotient includes all first normals at double roots and the single value at the odd-level simple root. Let \(R\) be the actual physical crossing of N, with its Cartan phase. Its values at every root are nonzero, so it is a unit of the full quotient. Negative powers below mean its actual inverse. The original pivotal circle operators are the basis \[ L_j=(-1)^{j-1}U_{j-1}(z/2),\qquad 1\le j\le N. \tag{2} \] They are a basis because their degrees are \(j-1\), with nonzero leading coefficients. Use their coefficient norm \[ \left\|\sum_{j=1}^N c_jL_j\right\|_\circ=\sum_{j=1}^N|c_j|. \tag{3} \] This is a specified finite norm, not an energy defined using an unknown knot value. Write \(\phi\) for the actual cylindrical closing functional of N. Its normalization and that of an integral filling are \[ \phi(f)=(-1)^dN^2[z^d](f\bmod\chi_N),\qquad \phi_n(f)=\phi(R^nf),\qquad n\in\mathbb Z. \tag{4} \] Thus \[ \phi(L_j)=0\quad(j<N),\qquad \phi(L_N)=N^2. \tag{5} \] All peripheral or framing factors already outside this physical pair row remain outside it. Nothing is divided by a quantum dimension or by the possibly nilpotent operator \(L_N\). ## 2. The zero-twist average and its exact inverse off one line On \(z=-2\cos t\), the actual circle basis has the identity \[ L_j(-2\cos t)=\frac{\sin(jt)}{\sin t}. \tag{6} \] For the unique polynomial representative of degree \(<N\), average its sine-weighted value over one grid cell: \[ \frac1{\sin t}\int_{-1/2}^{1/2} \sin(t+2\pi\rho/N)\, f(-2\cos(t+2\pi\rho/N))\,d\rho . \tag{7} \] Equation (6) shows directly that (7) is again a polynomial of degree \(<N\), and its action on the basis is \[ K_0L_j=\lambda_jL_j,\qquad \lambda_j=\frac{\sin(j\pi/N)}{j\pi/N}. \tag{8} \] At sine zeros (7) is interpreted by this polynomial identity. Equivalently (8) defines \(K_0\) intrinsically in the specified physical basis; it does not require choosing another representative. For \(1\le j<N\), \(\lambda_j>0\), whereas \(\lambda_N=0\). Consequently \[ \ker K_0=\mathbb C L_N,\qquad \operatorname{im}K_0=\ker\phi. \tag{9} \] Define \[ G_0L_j= \begin{cases}\lambda_j^{-1}L_j,&j<N,\\0,&j=N,\end{cases} \qquad P_0f=\frac{\phi(f)}{N^2}L_N . \tag{10} \] Then the complete exact identities are \[ K_0G_0=G_0K_0=I-P_0,\qquad G_0P_0=P_0G_0=K_0P_0=P_0K_0=0. \tag{11} \] The function \(\sin x/x\) decreases on \(0<x<\pi\): the numerator of its derivative is \(x\cos x-\sin x\), whose derivative is \(-x\sin x<0\) and whose value at zero is zero. Since \(\sin(\pi/N)\ge2/N\), this proves \[ \|K_0\|_\circ\le1,\qquad \|P_0\|_\circ=1,\qquad \|G_0\|_\circ\le\frac{\pi N}{2}. \tag{12} \] These are induced operator norms. The estimate includes \(N=2\). ## 3. Conjugation by the actual signed crossing Let \(M_f\) denote multiplication by \(f\) in the full quotient. For every signed integer \(n\), set \[ \widetilde K_n=M_{R^{-n}}K_0M_{R^n},\qquad G_n=M_{R^{-n}}G_0M_{R^n},\qquad u_n=\frac{R^{-n}L_N}{N^2},\qquad P_nf=u_n\phi_n(f). \tag{13} \] All operations in (13) are on quotient classes, with every Hermite normal retained.
