Equations (5), (9)--(11) give \[ \phi_n(u_n)=1,\qquad \ker\widetilde K_n=\mathbb C u_n,\qquad \operatorname{im}\widetilde K_n=\ker\phi_n, \tag{14} \] \[ \widetilde K_nG_n=G_n\widetilde K_n=I-P_n,\qquad G_nP_n=P_nG_n=\widetilde K_nP_n=P_n\widetilde K_n=0. \tag{15} \] In particular \(\widetilde K_n\) has rank \(N-1\), and \(G_n\) is its genuine two-sided inverse on \(\ker\phi_n\). Every original boundary class has the exact decomposition \[ f=\widetilde K_nG_nf+u_n\phi_n(f). \tag{16} \] Thus the sequence \[ 0\longrightarrow\mathbb C \mathop{\longrightarrow}^{c\mapsto cu_n}\mathcal H_N \mathop{\longrightarrow}^{\widetilde K_n}\mathcal H_N \mathop{\longrightarrow}^{\phi_n}\mathbb C \longrightarrow0 \tag{17} \] is exact, with the displayed splitting. The last coordinate is the original period itself, not a substitute for it. This is a sequence of complex vector spaces: \(\ker\phi_n\) is not asserted to be an ideal, and (17) is not a quotient-algebra or \(\mathcal H_N\)-module construction. ## 4. Polynomial conditioning with no deleted normal directions Here is an elementary multiplication estimate in (3). Put \(C_r(z)=U_r(z/2)\), \(r\ge0\). Laurent expansion after \(z=w+w^{-1}\) proves the polynomial fusion identity \[ C_rC_s=\sum_{j=0}^{\min(r,s)}C_{r+s-2j}. \tag{18} \] For the basis products, \(r,s\le N-1\), so every index on the right is at most \(2N-2\). For \(0\le v\le N-2\), another Laurent identity gives \[ 2T_N(z/2)C_v=C_{N+v}-C_{N-v-2}. \] Using the full relation \(2T_N(z/2)=-2\), including multiplicities, one obtains \[ C_{N+v}=-2C_v+C_{N-v-2} \quad\hbox{in }\mathcal H_N. \tag{19} \] Each unreduced term of (18) therefore has circle coefficient mass at most three, and there are at most \(N\) such terms. The signs in (2) do not affect this bound. It follows that \[ \|L_iL_j\|_\circ\le3N,\qquad \|fg\|_\circ\le3N\|f\|_\circ\|g\|_\circ,\qquad \|M_f\|_\circ\le3N\|f\|_\circ . \tag{20} \] F gives the original signed-power expansion, with its full Hermite data and retained unit phase, \[ R^n=\kappa^n\sum_{j=1}^N\beta_{j-1}^{(n)}L_j,\qquad \sum_j|\beta_{j-1}^{(n)}| \le2N(1+|n|/2). \tag{21} \] This bound is for every integer \(n\), positive, negative or zero; it is not obtained from a semisimple evaluation of the crossing. For clarity its finite Fourier input is the paired value/normal data \(|h_k|=1\) and \(|d_k|\le |n|N/2\). Their exact alias inverse gives first-kind coefficients \(|a_0|\le1\), \(|a_j|\le1+|n|/2\). Taking the actual second-kind differences \((-1)^j(a_j-a_{j+2})\), with \(a_N=a_{N+1}=0\), gives (21). Let \(b_n=1+|n|/2\). Since \(|\kappa|=1\), (20)--(21) imply \[ \|M_{R^{\pm n}}\|_\circ\le6N^2b_n. \tag{22} \] Combining this with (12)--(15) yields explicit uniform bounds \[ \boxed{\quad \|\widetilde K_n\|_\circ,\ \|P_n\|_\circ\le36N^4b_n^2,\qquad \|G_n\|_\circ\le18\pi N^5b_n^2,\qquad \|u_n\|_\circ\le6b_n . \quad} \tag{23} \] For fixed signed \(n\), the splitting is therefore polynomially conditioned in this recorded physical circle norm. No inverse of a confluent Vandermonde matrix or small Casimir-node separation was estimated. Formula (19), rather than distinct-root reduction, keeps the full normal directions. ## 5. A positive metric and coupled filling slots Declare the basis (2) orthonormal and denote its Hilbert norm by \(\|\cdot\|_2\). Pull this metric back by the actual multiplier: \[ \langle f,g\rangle_n =\langle R^nf,R^ng\rangle_2 . \tag{24} \] Then \(\widetilde K_n\) is self-adjoint and nonnegative, with the same eigenvalues (8). The projection \(P_n\) is orthogonal. Its normalized vector is \(R^{-n}L_N\), and \[ |\phi_n(f)|=N^2\|P_nf\|_n,\qquad \|f-P_nf\|_n \le\frac{\pi N}{2}\|\widetilde K_nf\|_n . \tag{25} \] Both assertions follow by writing \(R^nf\) in the orthonormal circle basis; no Cauchy equality for the exterior source is assumed. Since \(\|v\|_2\le\|v\|_\circ\le\sqrt N\|v\|_2\), (22) gives \[ (6N^{5/2}b_n)^{-1}\|f\|_2 \le\|f\|_n\le6N^{5/2}b_n\|f\|_2 . \tag{26} \] This is polynomial equivalence to the specified circle coefficient metric, not to every physical tensor-space norm. For \(r\) filling slots retain an arbitrary coupled class \(H\in\mathcal H_N^{\otimes r}\) and signed powers \(n_1,\ldots,n_r\). Use the tensor metric pulled back by \(\bigotimes_i M_{R^{n_i}}\). Let \(P_i,K_i\) act as \(P_{n_i},\widetilde K_{n_i}\) in their own slot, and put \[ P=\prod_iP_i,\qquad \phi_{\boldsymbol n}=\bigotimes_i\phi_{n_i}. \] The \(P_i\) are commuting orthogonal projections. Expanding in the tensor circle basis gives the pointwise indicator inequality \(1-\prod_i p_i\le\sum_i(1-p_i)\), \(p_i\in\{0,1\}\), and hence \[ \boxed{\quad \|H-PH\|_{\boldsymbol n}^2 \le\sum_i\|(I-P_i)H\|_{\boldsymbol n}^2 \le\left(\frac{\pi N}{2}\right)^2 \sum_i\|K_iH\|_{\boldsymbol n}^2,\qquad |\phi_{\boldsymbol n}(H)|=N^{2r}\|PH\|_{\boldsymbol n}. \quad} \tag{27} \] No factorization of \(H\) was used. Thus, if the actual source satisfies the additional estimate \[ \left(\frac{\pi N}{2}\right)^2 \sum_i\|K_iH\|_{\boldsymbol n}^2 \le\delta^2\|H\|_{\boldsymbol n}^2, \qquad 0\le\delta<1, \] orthogonality gives the exact consequence \[ |\phi_{\boldsymbol n}(H)| \ge N^{2r}\sqrt{1-\delta^2}\,\|H\|_{\boldsymbol n}. \tag{28} \] The source estimate in this implication is not proved here. Polynomial conditioning and a one-dimensional period space do not make it automatic. The metric in (24) is explicit and uses only the chosen filling powers; an exterior source can have a large component in the kernel of its original closing row. ## 6. Scope and coverage The earlier Fourier--Hermite kernel and positive Gram already give polynomial coordinate bounds for the original circle packet. The additional statement here is the explicit singular endomorphism (8), its crossing conjugate, and the exact kernel/period splitting (14)--(17). For \(n\ne0\), \(\widetilde K_n\) is not claimed equal to \[ \frac1{\sin t\,f_{N,n}(t)} \int_{-1/2}^{1/2} \sin(t+2\pi\rho/N)f_{N,n}(t+2\pi\rho/N) H(-2\cos(t+2\pi\rho/N))\,d\rho . \tag{29} \] Here \(f_{N,n}(t)=q^{nd^2/4}\exp(-nt^2/(2h))\), \(h=2\pi i/N\), is the actual centered Gaussian lift of the crossing values and normals. Formula (29) uses that lift between nodes. In (13), \(R^nH\) is first its full quotient class, whose canonical polynomial agrees with that lift only in the required nodal jets. Averaging intermediate values need not preserve that agreement. No equality of their principal symbols or microlocal interpolation estimate is asserted. Likewise a polynomial bound for \(G_n\) does not estimate \(\phi_n(f)\) from below. Equation (16) records that unknown coordinate exactly and allows it to vanish. The result applies to the original class supplied by any exterior contraction, but does not prove its overlap with the period line, select a geometric component, or remove relative boundary currents. ## Complete proof-source pins * N: papers/newton-calculus/finite.tex, SHA256 2db2d7e15df0210c32bace4c761bdabadbb5d67140473a61425dac4d1e382f8e. * F: notes/actual_twist_circle_fourier_kernel.md, SHA256 1d93f6f13d271c56eee6e7ea8ddf5b9ea0eea92a2076ede7068df552bab94292. N supplies the full physical algebra, circle basis, trace and crossing normalization. F supplies the complete signed-power coefficient bound. The average, fusion reduction, exact splitting and induced norm estimates are proved here. Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used. Frozen notes and public manuscripts are unchanged.

title: Bounding a signed cap contribution by two derivatives of its pressure
text:
# Bounding a signed cap contribution by two derivatives of its pressure The polynomial remaining after every other face has been summed contains information about cancellations that is lost in an estimate of each local factor. At odd levels it factors into linear forms with nonnegative coefficients. Two derivatives of its logarithm then suffice for a useful bound on its negative real axis. The finite inequality is proved first; sections 2–5 show exactly how it applies to the prescribed coefficient of the original source. The application fixes the selected cap spectrum at \(+2\) and all other spectra at \(-2\). The [uniform spectral extension](research_cap_uniform_spectral_gap.md) allows the selected parameter to vary over \([-2,2]\). Both applications retain the odd-level restriction. Neither bounds the entire filled-knot remainder. ## 1. Finite polynomial theorem Let \(d\ge1\), and suppose a nonzero homogeneous binary polynomial has the factorization \[ P(A,C)=P(1,1)\prod_{r=1}^{d} igl[(1-p_r)C+p_rA igr], \qquad P(1,1)>0,\quad 0\le p_r\le1. 	ag{1} \] Factors with \(p_r=0\) or \(p_r=1\) are allowed. Define \[ 
u_d= rac1d\sum_r p_r,\qquad \kappa_d= rac1d\sum_r p_r(1-p_r),\qquad R_d=\max\{1-
u_d-\kappa_d,\ 
u_d-\kappa_d,\ 1-4\kappa_d\}. 	ag{2} \] Here \(\kappa_d\) is the average Bernoulli variance. It is not the variance of the root parameters \(p_r\). The latter is \(
u_d-\kappa_d-
u_d^2\). In particular \[ 0\le\kappa_d\le
u_d(1-
u_d),\qquad  rac14\le R_d\le1. 	ag{3} \] The lower bound on \(R_d\) follows because its first two entries sum to \(1-2\kappa_d\ge1/2\). **Finite theorem.** Put \[ B^- =\sup_{0\le t\le1}|P(-t,1)|,\qquad B^+ =\sup_{0\le t\le1}|P(-1,t)|. 	ag{4} \] Then \[  oxed{\ \max(B^-,B^+)\le P(1,1)R_d^{d/2}.\ } 	ag{5} \] For the proof, the arithmetic-geometric mean inequality on the nonnegative squared factors gives, for each fixed \(t\), \[  egin{aligned}  rac{|P(-t,1)|^2}{P(1,1)^2} &\le \left( rac1d\sum_r[1-(1+t)p_r]^2ight)^d,\  rac{|P(-1,t)|^2}{P(1,1)^2} &\le \left( rac1d\sum_r[t-(1+t)p_r]^2ight)^d. \end{aligned} 	ag{6} \] No factor is divided out, so zeros cause no exception. Using \(d^{-1}\sum p_r^2=
u_d-\kappa_d\), the two averages are \[  egin{aligned} Q_-(t)&=1-2(1+t)
u_d+(1+t)^2(
u_d-\kappa_d),\ Q_+(t)&=t^2-2t(1+t)
u_d+(1+t)^2(
u_d-\kappa_d). \end{aligned} 	ag{7} \] They are convex quadratics: their quadratic coefficients are respectively \(d^{-1}\sum p_r^2\) and \(d^{-1}\sum(1-p_r)^2\). A convex function on \([0,1]\) is bounded above by the larger endpoint value. The endpoint values here are \[ Q_-(0)=1-
u_d-\kappa_d,\quad Q_+(0)=
u_d-\kappa_d,\quad Q_-(1)=Q_+(1)=1-4\kappa_d. 	ag{8} \] Equations (6)--(8) prove (5). The essential order is to average the squared factors at one common value of \(t\), and only then maximize. Maximizing every root factor separately loses this information. The numbers in (2) can be read from the polynomial itself without finding its roots: \[ 
u_d= rac1d\left.\partial_z\log P(e^z,1)ight|_{z=0},\qquad \kappa_d= rac1d\left.\partial_z^2\log P(e^z,1)ight|_{z=0}. 	ag{9} \] The theorem is invariant under exchanging \(A,C\), which replaces \(
u_d\) by \(1-
u_d\) and leaves \(\kappa_d\) unchanged. ## 2. The exact original cap pairing Fix a connected matched simple-sphere Morse source with \(R\) original crossing regions, its original cups, caps, and main mark. The two protected face variables are set to zero; all \(R\) ordinary targets remain \(d=N-1\). Fix one protected left coupon with the literal quartet \[ (C,0,A,0). 	ag{10} \] Use its actual spectrum \(+2\), and use the actual central polynomial at spectrum \(-2\) at every other original region. This is one fixed genuine sector, not an arbitrary mixture of local comparison branches. Remove only the common raw unit sign from each central coupon. Let \(P_{e,\mathrm C}(-2;L)\) denote the resulting positive polynomial, including its original scalar normalization. Extract every other ordinary variable first: \[ P_N(A,C)= \left[\prod_{f
e A,C	ext{ ordinary}}L_f^dight] \prod_{e
e e_*}P_{e,\mathrm C}(-2;L) =\sum_{j=0}^{d}p_{N,j}A^jC^{d-j}. 	ag{11} \] Every shared variable is still the original face variable. The total degree is exactly \(d\), since \((R-1)d-(R-2)d=d\). Positivity of the endpoint path coefficients gives \(p_{N,j}\ge0\). Put \(	heta=\pi/N\), \(M=\lfloor N/2floor-1\), and \[ s_r=2\sin(r	heta),\quad c_r=2\cos((2r+1)	heta),\quad U_{N,j}=\left(\prod_{r=1}^{j}s_r^2ight) \prod_{r=j+1}^{d}(2-c_r). 	ag{12} \] The literal protected left numerator is \[ H_{\mathrm L}(C,0,A,0;+2) =\sum_{j=0}^{M}(-1)^jU_{N,j}C^jA^{d-j}. 	ag{13} \] Thus imposing the two remaining original targets gives exactly \[ S_N=[A^dC^d]\,H_{\mathrm L}(C,0,A,0;+2)P_N(A,C) =\sum_{j=0}^{M}(-1)^jU_{N,j}p_{N,j}. 	ag{14} \] The corresponding unadjusted raw sector differs by the product of the original central unit signs. There is no alteration of its magnitude. At odd levels \(d\) is even and these particular signs are already positive. Equation (14) is a source coefficient; no filling functional or physical framing normalization has yet been applied. The exact all-index positive cap moment law provides a positive random variable \(X_N\) with \[ \mathbb E X_N^j= rac{U_{N,j}}{U_{N,0}}\quad(0\le j\le d),\qquad U_{N,0}=\csc^2 rac\pi{2N}\le N^2,\qquad \mathbb E X_N^d=N^2\sin^2 rac\pi{2N}\le rac{\pi^2}{4}. 	ag{15} \] Its support is not assumed bounded. Define the actual omitted finite tail \[ T_N=\sum_{j=M+1}^{d}(-1)^jU_{N,j}p_{N,j}. 	ag{16} \] Then, with no moment above degree \(d\), \[ S_N+T_N=U_{N,0}\mathbb E P_N(-X_N,1). 	ag{17} \] For \(X_N\le1\) use the first supremum in (4). For \(X_N\ge1\), homogeneity gives \(P_N(-X_N,1)=X_N^dP_N(-1,X_N^{-1})\). Consequently \[ |S_N|\le U_{N,0}\left(B_N^-+\mathbb E X_N^d B_N^+ight)+|T_N|. 	ag{18} \] This is the existing full-exterior negative-axis reduction, stated here with the exact left-cap coordinate order. It uses coherent extraction of the entire exterior, not an independent norm of each incident coupon. ## 3. Why the actual odd polynomial meets the finite hypothesis At \(N=2m+1\), the actual central endpoint numerator is exactly \[ P_{e,\mathrm C}(-2;x,b,c,y) =N^2D_m(x,b,y)D_m(x,c,y),\qquad D_m(x,b,y)=\det\left(bI+ rac x2H_-+ rac y2H_+ight), 	ag{19} \] where the two physical Hermitian matrices \(H_-,H_+\) are positive definite. All normalizations in (19) are those of the original endpoint source. In particular the factor \(N^2\) is retained. If all surviving arguments have positive imaginary parts, the matrix in (19) has positive-definite imaginary part and is invertible. Each determinant is therefore real stable. Products, identification of shared variables, coefficient extraction by differentiation followed by evaluation at zero, and specialization of the protected variables to zero preserve real stability or yield the zero polynomial. These are applied to the actual full exterior in (11). When \(P_N
e0\), binary homogeneity and nonnegative coefficients give exactly (1), with \(d=N-1\). Nonvanishing for all sufficiently large odd levels follows from the same original positive coefficient packet used below. For a level where \(P_N=0\), the sector itself is zero and every upper bound is automatic. Nothing here substitutes a positive comparator for an even-level numerator: that substitution would not preserve signed negative-axis values. Combining (5), (15), and (18) gives the finite original-target estimate \[ |S_N|\le N^2\left(1+ rac{\pi^2}{4}ight) P_N(1,1)R_{N-1}^{(N-1)/2}+|T_N|, \qquad N	ext{ odd}. 	ag{20} \] ## 4. The pressure and the omitted tail use the same original demands Assume the original exterior admits a strictly positive feasible half-load table with every other ordinary face load equal to one, and its supported ordinary pair graph is connected. Keep \(A=C=1\). Let \(I\) consist of the other ordinary faces, write \(L_i=e^{w_i}\), and define \[ \mathcal F(z,w)=\sum_{t	ext{ exterior}}Q_t(L)-\sum_{i\in I}w_i, \qquad A=e^z, C=1. 	ag{21} \] The triangles are precisely the original triangles outside the selected cap. For supported corner loads \(\alpha_f\ge0\), summing to \(1/2\), the triangle potential is \[ Q_t(L)=\max_{\sum\alpha_f=1/2} \sum_{f\in t} igl[f(\alpha_f)+\alpha_f\log L_f igr],\qquad f(a)= rac{\Lambda(\pi a)+\Lambda(\pi/2-\pi a)}{\pi},\qquad \Lambda(t)=-\int_0^t\log|2\sin u|\,du. 	ag{22} \] Protected zero corners have forced load zero and are omitted from the supported maximization. The strict table makes the recession function positive in every nonzero direction of the \(I\) coordinates: equality between a triangle maximum and its strictly positive weighted average would force the log-direction constant on that triangle. Connectedness, together with the fixed boundary values at \(A,C\), then forces the whole direction to be zero. Compactness of the unit sphere gives coercivity. The positive triangle Laplacians give a positive-definite Hessian after grounding \(C\). Thus the stationary \(w_*\) exists, is finite, and is unique; the implicit solution \(w(z)\) exists near zero. Define \[ F(z)=\mathcal F(z,w(z)),\qquad M_{\mathrm{cap}}=F(0),\quad 
u=F'(0),\quad \kappa=F''(0)>0. 	ag{23} \] The second derivative is the Schur complement of the original triangle Hessian, not the curvature of an independently reweighted star. The actual positive determinant packet gives locally uniform convergence of the holomorphic logarithms \[  rac1N\log P_N(e^z,1)\longrightarrow F(z) \quad	ext{on a fixed complex disk around }0,\qquad N	ext{ odd}. 	ag{24} \] Here the finite coefficient integral extracts exactly the \(I\) targets \(d\). Its real radius is the actual finite stationary radius. The determinant contraction has a strict global angular gap because the supported pair graph is connected and each edge character is the primitive difference of two face phases. The finite Hessian is uniformly positive after division by \(N\); the positive determinant pencils have all fixed logarithmic derivatives \(O(N)\) on a uniform complex neighborhood. The local Gaussian and the complementary angular gap therefore give a relative, locally uniform packet. Its analytic logarithm and Cauchy differentiation yield \[  rac1N\log P_N(1,1)	o M_{\mathrm{cap}},\qquad 
u_{N-1}	o
u,\qquad \kappa_{N-1}	o\kappa. 	ag{25} \] The factors \(N^2\) in (19) remain present and contribute only \(O(\log N/N)\) to the normalized logarithm. No differentiation of a merely pointwise rate is used. This local proof is the effective-response theorem; its input is the exact Morse source and connected determinant graph, not a flat-plat layout. Let \(\Phi\) be the original complete augmented source action, normalized so that \(2\pi\Phi\) is the actual augmented complement volume. Let \(R(s)\) be the residual complete triangle capacity with exterior loads \(A:s,C:1-s\), all other ordinary loads one, and the same protected zeros. The original complete positive action gives \[ \Phi=\max_{1/2\le s\le1}\{R(s)+2f(s-1/2)\},\qquad \max_{1/2\le s\le1}R(s)\le\Phi-\gamma 	ag{26} \] for some \(\gamma>0\). The second statement uses the unique strict complete optimizer: interior splits have a strictly positive restored cap entropy, while the two endpoint splits make its half-triangle a pure vertex and cannot be the strict optimizer. Compactness supplies a uniform loss. The uniform closed coefficient upper for the actual endpoint central polynomials gives \(\limsup N^{-1}\log p_{N,j_N}\le R(s)\) whenever \(j_N/d	o s\). Also \(U_{N,j}\le N^2\) for every \(0\le j\le d\). The omitted tail in (16) consequently satisfies, for all sufficiently large levels, \[ |T_N|\le e^{N(\Phi-\gamma/2)}. 	ag{27} \] At odd levels the first omitted index is exactly \(j=m=d/2\); this endpoint is included in (26). No endpoint current or low-degree cutoff has been dropped. ## 5. A two-derivative sufficient criterion Define \[ \mathscr L(
u,\kappa) =- rac12\log\max\{1-
u-\kappa,\ 
u-\kappa,\ 1-4\kappa\}. 	ag{28} \] Equations (20), (25), and (27) prove \[  oxed{\quad \limsup_{\substack{N	o\infty\N	ext{ odd}}} rac1N\log|S_N| \le\max\left\{M_{\mathrm{cap}}-\mathscr L(
u,\kappa),\ \Phi- rac\gamma2ight\}.\quad} 	ag{29} \] Thus \(\mathscr L(
u,\kappa)>M_{\mathrm{cap}}-\Phi\) proves a strict absolute rate gap for this original sector, at the fixed spectra under consideration. If the difference is \(\delta>0\), the limiting gap is at least \(\min(\delta,\gamma/2)\). A bound with any smaller positive gap holds for all sufficiently large odd levels. A nonstrict inequality gives the weak absolute rate bound. This criterion can be combined with the existing Mahler or higher-derivative criteria by taking their maximum. It is not claimed to dominate each of them for every root distribution. It instead controls the common negative-axis parameter directly. In the limiting root-measure notation of the existing pressure theorem, the conclusion is the additional explicit lower bound \(\chi_D\ge\mathscr L(
u,\kappa)\). ## 6. Scope and limitations The existing negative-axis note proves the exact exterior extraction, finite moment reduction, omitted-tail estimate, odd real stability, and factorwise Mahler loss. The effective-response note proves the local complex pressure packet and its Schur-complement response. The root-pressure note proves that this germ determines the full root measure and the exact common-variable negative-axis loss; its explicit low-order bounds use the Mahler loss, including the conductance and fourth-derivative improvements. The finite squared-factor estimate (5) adds a direct two-derivative lower bound on that common-variable loss. It does not require continuing a classical saddle through the negative axis or reconstructing the limiting density. The full original-source coefficient has been grouped before taking modulus in (17). Thus this estimate is compatible with the separate exponential lower bound for the sum of absolute original-array terms: cancellation is retained here, whereas that termwise sum discards it. That particular array lower bound was established on even levels; the present signed estimate is on odd levels. No same-level conclusion is inferred by comparing those two parity-restricted statements. The conclusion concerns one genuine singleton sector and one mixed spectral tuple. It gives no bound for multiple noncentral coupons, all real spectra, a complex filling contour, odd endpoint derivatives, or the even source. In particular the actual even central cofactor is not generally real stable. Its coefficientwise positive comparison with a stable reference does not control signed negative-axis values. The strict fixed-spectrum odd result therefore is not a full remainder theorem and does not prove a new knot-volume equality. ## Sources used in the proof - [The original one-cap coefficient reduces to two negative-axis suprema](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_global_cap_negative_axis_and_mahler_bound.md), sections 1--4 and 6: the exact original extraction, finite cap completion, odd factorization, and strict omitted tail. - [Effective boundary response and the original global cap variance](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_global_cap_effective_response_criterion.md), sections 1--3: strict exterior pressure, connected determinant packet, and the actual Schur response. - [The classical boundary-pressure germ determines the cap root loss](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_cap_root_measure_from_classical_pressure.md), sections 2--7: prior root-measure, Mahler, and common-variable criteria; the present bound does not require its logarithmic-potential convergence theorem. - [An exact positive moment form for the original flat-cap coefficients](research_flat_cap_positive_moment_form.md): the original finite moments through degree \(d\), with unbounded support retained. - [The full numerator after localization: exact cross cofactors and the packet interface](../papers/filling-bounds/README.md), section 3, and [Finite local curvature of the original boundary models](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_q_hahn_boundary_model_curvature.md): actual odd endpoint determinants and their finite curvature/holomorphic estimates. - [The positive face coefficient has one global saddle](actual_positive_face_coefficient_saddle.md), sections 2--4: determinant angular contraction and the primitive finite coefficient Gaussian. - [The geometric contribution and all Fourier charges](../papers/casimir-source-asymptotics/README.md) and [The original complement and its geometric contribution](../papers/casimir-source-asymptotics/README.md): original Morse source marking and complete action normalization; only the exact source and complete geometric action are used here. - [The exact even CROSS endpoint is not real stable, and the remaining parity adapter](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_even_cross_stability_obstruction.md): the even-parity limitation.

title: A full spectral-strip gap for an original cap and its whole CROSS star
text:
# A full spectral-strip gap for an original cap and its whole CROSS star 31 October 2026. The cap varies in a small complex disk about +2; every neighboring CROSS spectrum may range over the entire real fold with a sufficiently thin fixed complex strip. This is a relative weighted-star theorem, not an absolute Phi_D bound. The face targets and both parity cutoffs are unchanged. ## 1. Original source and theorem Let F=(u,A,v,C) be an original marked cap, with u=v=0 and A,C ordinary. Include EVERY other original A-incident port in a product of k genuine CROSS coupons. The valence k is fixed with the original diagram but otherwise arbitrary. Remove the fixed common raw signs and write \[  egin{aligned} P_N^{ oldsymbol\delta}(A,Y)&=\prod_eP_{e,\mathrm{CROSS}}(A,Y;\sigma(\delta_e)),\ \sigma(\delta)&=-2\cos(2\pi\delta),\ P_N^0(A,Y)&=P_N^{ oldsymbol\delta}(A,Y) ig|_{ oldsymbol\delta=0}. \end{aligned}	ag{1} \] The endpoint product has nonnegative coefficients at both parities. All shared variables remain identified. The actual finite CROSS degree projections are unchanged as the spectra vary. Fix positive ordinary radii, protected variables exactly zero, with L_A=L_C. Write P_N^+(a)=P_N^0(a,L_Y). The actual endpoint weighted action has the locally uniform real limit \[  rac1N\log P_N^+(L_Ce^t)\longrightarrow F(t),\qquad F	ext{ differentiable at }0,\qquad0<
u:=F'(0)< rac12.	ag{2} \] The derivative condition is the substantive scalar hypothesis. At a classified stationary cap with only CROSS neighbors it follows from the SAME original demand: L_A=L_C and F'(0)=sum_(e!=F) q_(e,A)=1-q_(F,A)=nu in (0,1/2). Put d=N-1 and M=floor(N/2)-1. For cap spectrum sigma the original projected polynomial and the extracted star are \[  egin{aligned} H_{F,\mathrm{cap}}(A,C;\sigma)&=\sum_{j=0}^M(-1)^jb_j(\sigma)A^{d-j}C^j,\ B_N(Y;\sigma, oldsymbol\delta)&=[A^d]H_{F,\mathrm{cap}}P_N^{ oldsymbol\delta}. \end{aligned}	ag{3} \] **Theorem.** There are fixed epsilon_*>0, h_*>0, eta>0 and N_0 such that \[ \sup_{\substack{|\sigma-2|\le\varepsilon_*\,,\ |\operatorname{Im}\delta_e|\le h_*\ \operatorname{Re}\delta_e\in\mathbb R\,,\ |Y_f|=L_f}} |B_N(Y;\sigma, oldsymbol\delta)| \le e^{-\eta N}P_N^+(L_C),\qquad N\ge N_0.	ag{4} \] Both parities and every remaining face phase are included. This extracts exactly the original A^d against the WHOLE neighboring product; it is not a shifted demand or an independent allocation at each neighbor. ## 2. Root-safe cap factors and the exact global CROSS majorant Set theta=pi/N and \[  egin{aligned} c_j&=2\cos((2j+1)	heta),&s_j&=2\sin(j	heta),\ B_j&=\prod_{r=1}^js_r^2,&b_j(\sigma)&=B_j\prod_{r=j+1}^d(\sigma-c_r),\ U_j&=b_j(2),&\gamma_j&=2-c_j>0. \end{aligned} \] These are the full original unused-row products, also at repeated spectral roots. They satisfy the polynomial relation \[ (\sigma-c_{j+1})b_{j+1}(\sigma)=s_{j+1}^2b_j(\sigma).	ag{5} \] For j<=M, the explicit increasing-sine ratios give U_j<=U_0=csc^2(theta/2)<=C N^2. Since product gamma_j=4 and chi_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2, for |sigma-2|<=epsilon_s, \[ |b_j(\sigma)|\le U_j\prod_{r>j}\left(1+ rac{\varepsilon_s}{\gamma_r}ight) \le CN^2e^{N\kappa_s},\qquad \kappa_s=\operatorname{arcosh}(1+\varepsilon_s/2).	ag{6} \] There is no division by b_j, chi_N, or a varying spectral factor. This polynomial estimate is used near every endpoint or sampled zero outside the strict row interval below. The original cofactor interpolation theorem supplies the stronger, GLOBAL coefficientwise CROSS bound, on any fixed strip |Im delta|<=T, \[ |P_{e,\mathrm{CROSS}}(\sigma(\delta))|_{\mathrm{coeff}} \le C_T\log^2(N+1)e^{2\pi d|\operatorname{Im}\delta|} P_{e,\mathrm{CROSS}}(-2).	ag{7} \] This is equation (27) of [the original cofactor factorization](../papers/filling-bounds/README.md), section 8, not an inferred coefficient lower asymptotic. Its nodal positivity covers ALL j,a<=J: for j<=a it is the direct positive original recurrence; for j>a it is the retained physical tail adapter. Thus the plain coefficient majorant includes j=J-1 at all nodes. Its central coefficientwise comparisons use (x+y)^2>=2xy, with the original forced outer units retained. Taking products in (7), even when face variables are shared, yields \[ |P_N^{ oldsymbol\delta}|_{\mathrm{coeff}} \le Q_N\exp\!\left(2\pi d\sum_e|\operatorname{Im}\delta_e|ight)P_N^0.	ag{8} \] where Q_N is a fixed polynomial upper bound in N on a fixed strip. For later rate estimates put \[ \omega=\kappa_s+2\pi\sum_e|\operatorname{Im}\delta_e|.	ag{9} \] ## 3. Actual MAIN-edge angular loss on the whole neighbor fold The triangle on the opposite side of original MAIN edge AC from (u,A,C) belongs to a different port in P_N^delta. It contains the two supported positive variables A,C. Fix phi_0 in (0,pi/8) and a small radial interval |t|<=T_0. The cofactor angular theorem gives gamma>0 and a FIXED strip height h_0>0 such that \[  egin{aligned} |P_N^{ oldsymbol\delta}(Ce^{t+i\phi},Y)| &\le CN^K\exp\!\left(2\pi d\sum_e|\operatorname{Im}\delta_e|-\gamma Night)P_N^+(L_Ce^t),\ \phi_0\le|\phi|\le\pi,\quad |t|&\le T_0,\quad |\operatorname{Im}\delta_e|\le h_0, \quad\operatorname{Re}\delta_e\in\mathbb R,\quad |Y_f|=L_f. \end{aligned}	ag{10} \] Here C on the left is the actual complex face value. Thus A and C have precisely the stated phase difference regardless of other face phases. No phase is assigned to a protected zero. To verify (10) against the actual source, put u=-4sin^2(pi delta). At even N=2m the central formula is \[  egin{gathered} s_m^2(x+y)D_bD_c+s_ms_{m-1}xy(D_bE_c+E_bD_c),\ D_b=R_{m-1}(b;u),\qquad E_b=(a_{m-1}+u)R_{m-2}(b;u). \end{gathered} \] At odd N=2m+1 it is \[ G_bG_c+u s_ms_{m+1}xyD_bD_c,\qquad G_b=R_m(b;u),\quad D_b=R_{m-1}(b;u).	ag{11} \] The skipped-central odd term is retained. Every central summand has a cofactor on the actual AC side, at index J or J-1. On that side the actual angular theorem gives C N^K exp(-gamma N)R_j(positive;0), uniformly on the entire real fold and its fixed thin strip. The J-1 case includes the theorem's omitted-node extra-factor/division argument and its polynomial cost; no logarithmic angular prefactor is being claimed. On the other side apply the exact coefficient interpolation/Bernstein bound. The remaining central factors are bounded on that strip. At positive radii use, at even levels, D_b(0)>=s_(m-1)^2(x+y)R_(m-2)(b;0) and (x+y)^2>=2xy; at odd levels use G_b(0)>=s_m^2(x+y)D_b(0) and G_b(0)G_c(0)>=2s_m^4 xyD_b(0)D_c(0). These compare every central term to the actual positive endpoint kernel without division by a small diagonal or central zero. This proves (10); the other star ports use (7). Shrinking the strip later preserves all these fixed constants. ## 4. Total-degree tails and fixed choices of radii Choose delta_j>0 such that \[ 0<
u-2\delta_j<
u+2\delta_j< rac12,\qquad l=\lceil N(
u-\delta_j)ceil,\quad r=\lfloor N(
u+\delta_j)floor. \] For sufficiently large N, 0<l<=r<r+1<=M. Differentiability in (2) gives fixed t_-<0<t_+, as small as desired, and beta>0 with \[  egin{aligned} F(t_-)-(
u-\delta_j)t_-&\le F(0)- eta,\ F(t_+)-(
u+\delta_j)t_+&\le F(0)- eta. \end{aligned}	ag{12} \] Choose them also within (-T_0,T_0), and so small that \[ F(t)-vt\le F(0)+\gamma/4, \] for t between 0 and either chosen radius, and v in {nu-delta_j,nu+delta_j}. Continuity gives this extra condition. The integer rounding of l/N and (r+1)/N costs only O(1) in logarithms. Write P_N^delta=sum_j p_j^delta(Y)A^j. Formula (3) gives the exact total-degree split j<l, l<=j<=r, and j>r, all with j<=M. Positivity of P_N^0, (6),(8), and the two Chernoff radii show that the exterior parts have bound \[ \left|\sum_{\substack{0\le j\le M\j<l\ \mathrm{or}\ j>r}} (-1)^jb_j(\sigma)C^jp_j^{ oldsymbol\delta}(Y)ight| \le\operatorname{poly}(N)e^{N(F(0)- eta+\omega+o(1))}.	ag{13} \] For example, the lower positive tail is bounded by exp(-(l-1)t_-)P_N^+(L_C exp(t_-)); the upper one by exp(-(r+1)t_+)P_N^+(L_C exp(t_+)). No individual neighbor A allocation is restricted. Endpoint or zero spectral rows are controlled by (6), not by solving a divided recurrence there. ## 5. An exact finite analytic antidifference on the interior rows Put h=1/N. For a complex log-radius zeta set \[  egin{aligned} w_j(\zeta)&=(-1)^jb_j(\sigma)e^{-j\zeta},\ a_N(t,\zeta,\sigma)&=-e^{-\zeta}  rac{4\sin^2(\pi(t+h))}{\sigma-2\cos(2\pi(t+3h/2))}. \end{aligned}	ag{14} \] Then w_(j+1)=a_N(j/N)w_j EXACTLY by (5). On a fixed complex tube about the strict row interval and a fixed rectangle |Re zeta|<T_1, |Im zeta|<2phi_0 with T_1>T_0, the denominator stays away from zero for sigma in a sufficiently small complex disk about 2. At sigma=2, a_N converges uniformly there to -exp(-zeta). After shrinking these fixed neighborhoods if necessary, a_N-1 has a uniformly bounded analytic inverse. The original b_j can still be zero; it is never divided out. All divisions in this construction are confined to the stated bulk interval, where both the denominator in (14) and a_N-1 are uniformly nonzero. Here is the finite construction, including its error. Put \[  egin{aligned} K_N&=(a_N-1)^{-1},\ (\mathcal F_hH)(t)&=- rac{a_N(t)}{a_N(t)-1}\,[H(t+h)-H(t)],\ H_N&=\sum_{q=0}^{m_N-1}\mathcal F_h^qK_N. \end{aligned}	ag{15} \] Let rho be the row-tube radius, K a uniform bound on |a_N/(a_N-1)|, and K_0 a uniform bound on |K_N| on the larger tube and fixed parameter rectangle. Choose \[ m_N=\left\lfloor rac{ho N}{8(K+1)}ightfloor\ge1. \] Use m_N nested tubes from radius rho to rho/2. Cauchy's derivative bound makes each forward difference cost at most 2h/s, with s=rho/(2m_N), so each F_h costs at most 4Khm_N/rho<=1/2. All literal shifts stay in the preceding tube. The finite geometric identity now gives \[  egin{aligned} a_N(t)H_N(t+h)-H_N(t)&=1-e_N(t),\ e_N(t)&=(a_N(t)-1)\mathcal F_h^{m_N}K_N(t),\ |H_N|&\le2K_0,\qquad |e_N|\le Ce^{-cN}. \end{aligned}	ag{16} \] All functions are analytic in zeta and sigma on the fixed parameter rectangle; the bounds are uniform. This constructs an exact finite antidifference, not an asymptotic solution for a discrete coefficient. Consequently the original window kernel satisfies EXACTLY \[ \sum_{j=l}^rw_j =w_{r+1}H_N((r+1)/N)-w_lH_N(l/N) +\sum_{j=l}^re_N(j/N)w_j.	ag{17} \] BOTH endpoint terms remain. Each w_j retains the full b_j unused-row product, including every common sampled zero. ## 6. Exact A contour and both radial side currents The actual window coefficient is \[  rac1{2\pi}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi} P_N^{ oldsymbol\delta}(Ce^{i\phi},Y) \sum_{j=l}^rw_j(i\phi)\,d\phi.	ag{18} \] This is a literal coefficient contour, not a finite grid. No alias or bound on the total degree of P_N relative to N is needed. For |phi|>=phi_0, (10) and (6) give rate at most F(0)+omega-gamma. For |phi|<=phi_0, insert (17). The residual contributes at most \[ \operatorname{poly}(N)e^{N(F(0)+\omega-c+o(1))}.	ag{19} \] by (6),(8). No analytic interpolation of p_j has been used. Consider separately the boundary terms j=l and j=r+1. Apart from the actual scalar (-1)^j b_j(sigma), their integrand is \[ W_j(\zeta)=P_N^{ oldsymbol\delta}(Ce^\zeta,Y) e^{-j\zeta}H_N(j/N;\zeta,\sigma). \] It is holomorphic on the small rectangle of (14)-(16). Deform the segment zeta=i[-phi_0,phi_0] to Re zeta=t_- for j=l, and to Re zeta=t_+ for j=r+1. The exact contour identity retains BOTH joining segments, at Im zeta=+phi_0 and Im zeta=-phi_0. On the shifted vertical segment, bounded H_N, (6),(8),(12) give rate at most F(0)+omega-beta. On either joining segment, the actual A/C phase difference is exactly +/-phi_0, so (10) applies. The small-radius choice after (12) bounds the rate there by \[ F(0)+\omega-3\gamma/4.	ag{20} \] Thus BOTH endpoint terms have a strict rate improvement, and both original radial currents have been controlled, not discarded. All bounds are uniform in the other face phases. ## 7. Closing the fixed spectral neighborhoods The row interval, angular threshold, radii and positive losses beta,gamma,c were fixed using the endpoint profile before the final spectral neighborhoods were chosen. Take epsilon_* within the initial cap disk, and h_* within the initial CROSS strip, such that \[ \operatorname{arcosh}(1+\varepsilon_*/2)+2\pi k h_* < rac14\min\{ eta,\gamma/2,c\}.	ag{21} \] All these numbers are fixed before N tends to infinity. Equations (13),(18)-(20) give a uniform upper rate strictly below F(0). Since log P_N^+(L_C)=NF(0)+o(N), reducing the gap once more proves the actual finite comparison (4) at all sufficiently large levels. This includes arbitrary real parts of every CROSS fold parameter. No cap moment sequence at a varied spectrum, unknown degree interpolation, or finite-order adiabatic extrapolation has entered. The finite high-order construction (15)-(17) supplies the stated exponential residual, and all source cutoff endpoints remain. ## 8. Exterior attachment and precise remaining scope As the whole A-star was included, the unchanged exterior G_N has no A incidence. For the remaining original target monomial Y^t, (4) and Cauchy give \[  ig|[Y^{\mathbf t}]B_N(Y;\sigma, oldsymbol\delta)G_N(Y) ig| \le e^{-\eta N}P_N^+(L_C)  rac{\sup_{|Y_f|=L_f}|G_N(Y)|}{\prod_fL_f^{t_f}}.	ag{22} \] Here ordinary t_f=d and protected exponents zero are unchanged. Boundary variables may be shared arbitrarily. All raw source scalar signs are fixed unit factors; there is no new N normalization. This is a genuine spectral-neighborhood RELATIVE star improvement. Its displayed weighted star/exterior envelope is not generally known to be at most exp(N Phi_D). The hypothesis that every other A-incident port is CROSS also remains explicit. Consequently no universal cap elimination, full source gap, or volume theorem is inferred. ## 9. A shorter fixed-spectrum proof using only finite positive moments At the fixed spectra cap +2 and all neighbors -2, there is a separate proof of the relative star gap that avoids analytic antidifferencing. It uses the [exact positive cap-moment law](research_flat_cap_positive_moment_form.md), not its disproved squared-norm strengthening. Put \[ P_N^0(A,Y)=\sum_{j\ge0}p_{N,j}(Y)A^j,\qquad R_N(x;Y)=\sum_{j=0}^Mp_{N,j}(Y)(-Cx)^j. \] There is a positive random variable \(X_N\) with \[ \mathbb E X_N^j=U_j/U_0\quad(0\le j\le d),\qquad B_N(Y;2,0)=U_0\mathbb E R_N(X_N;Y).	ag{23} \] Its support is unbounded. Only the displayed finite moments are used. The original full sine products give \(B_d=N^2\) and \(\prod_{r=0}^d\gamma_r=4\), hence \(U_d=N^2\) at both parities. Thus \[ m_d:=\mathbb E X_N^d=N^2\sin^2\! rac{\pi}{2N} \le rac{\pi^2}{4},\qquad U_0\le CN^2.	ag{24} \] Fix a small \(\delta_0>0\). The actual AC-cofactor angular theorem at phase difference \(\pi\) gives constants \(C_0,K,\gamma>0\) with \[ |P_N^0(-Cx,Y)|\le C_0N^Ke^{-\gamma N}P_N^+(L_Cx), \quad 1-\delta_0\le x\le1+\delta_0,\quad |Y_f|=L_f. \] The central formulas (11) retain every term at both parities; the ordinary AC variables are supported in one actual triangle. This bound is therefore uniform in every other face phase. Choose \(0<\delta<\delta_0\) and \(R>1+\delta\). Split the expectation in (23) into the lower, middle and upper ranges separated by \(1-\delta\) and \(1+\delta\). In the lower range, positivity of the endpoint product gives \( |R_N(x;Y)|\le P_N^+(L_C(1-\delta))\). In the upper range the TRUE total cap cutoff gives \[ |R_N(x;Y)|\le x^M P_N^+(L_C),\qquad \mathbb E\!\left[X_N^M\mathbf1_{X_N\ge1+\delta}ight] \le(1+\delta)^{-(d-M)}m_d. \] On the bounded middle range, use the finite identity \(R_N(x;Y)=P_N^0(-Cx,Y)-\sum_{j>M}p_{N,j}(Y)(-Cx)^j\). Its first term has the angular gap. The second has the finite Chernoff bound \((x/R)^{M+1}P_N^+(L_CR)\). The full product is evaluated only on this bounded interval: neither its higher powers nor its square is integrated against the moment law. Combining the three ranges gives \[  egin{aligned} \sup_{|Y_f|=L_f}|B_N(Y;2,0)|\le U_0 igg[&P_N^+(L_C(1-\delta))\ &+m_d(1+\delta)^{-(d-M)}P_N^+(L_C)\ &+C_0N^Ke^{-\gamma N}P_N^+(L_C(1+\delta))\ &+\left( rac{1+\delta}{R}ight)^{M+1}P_N^+(L_CR) igg]. \end{aligned}	ag{25} \] This is an explicit finite inequality for the actual positive star values; no individual neighbor A allocation is made. Let \(F_0=F(0)\). Choose \(t>0\) with \(F(t)-F_0<t/2\), set \(R=e^t\), and then take \(\delta>0\) small enough that all four deficits are positive: \[  egin{aligned} \eta_1&=F_0-F(\log(1-\delta)),\ \eta_2&=	frac12\log(1+\delta),\ \eta_3&=\gamma-F(\log(1+\delta))+F_0,\ \eta_4&=	frac12(t-\log(1+\delta))-F(t)+F_0. \end{aligned}	ag{26} \] The first uses \(F'(0)>0\); the fourth uses \(F'(0)<1/2\) with the radius \(t\) fixed first. Continuity gives the third. At even levels \(d-M=M+1=N/2\); at odd levels these quantities are \((N+1)/2\) and \((N-1)/2\). The bounded offsets, (24), and the endpoint weighted limit therefore turn (25) into a strict exponential gap relative to the actual \(P_N^+(L_C)\). This proof does not extend the positive moment sequence to a varying cap spectrum. Sections 2–7 provide that separate analytic extension. The fixed-spectrum argument also does not supply a coefficientwise comparison with the paired endpoint reference: it is the same weighted, phase-uniform star estimate as the main theorem. ## Inputs The original cap factors follow from the exact polynomial tail formula in the [all-demand source proof](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_cap_cross_all_demand_subexponential_contraction.md) and its [original-demand dictionary](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_two_port_main_cap_original_demand_convolution.md). The all-strip coefficientwise bound is the [original cofactor factorization](../papers/filling-bounds/README.md), section 8, equations (22)–(27). The [global cofactor angular theorem](../papers/casimir-source-asymptotics/README.md), sections 1–4, supplies the fixed strip and the polynomial omitted-node cost. The [mixed CROSS/window note](research_mixed_cross_window_cycle_packing.md), sections 1–2, also records the exact central comparisons and support. The finite normal form is the [analytic switching theorem](research_analytic_switching_suppression.md), sections 1–3; its forward version is proved explicitly in (15)–(17). The endpoint action comes from the [even closed half-block theorem](actual_fejer_half_block_entropy.md), section 5, and the [odd raw factorization and coefficient theorem](actual_fejer_odd_regularized_full_numerator.md), sections 1–3. The stationary interpretation uses the [full-fiber common-weight classification](research_full_fiber_sharp_stationary_classification.md). The [incidence and assembly note](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_cap_cross_incidence_and_disjoint_assembly.md) explains why the present whole-star operation is different from attaching a two-port estimate to an exterior carrying A. All divisions in the antidifference argument are confined to the bulk, where both g_(j+1) and a_N-1 are nonzero. The proof retains both window endpoints and both contour-joining currents. The endpoint moment argument in Section 9 uses only the finite d-th moment. The full product is evaluated on the bounded central interval, not integrated beyond the available moment range.

title: A boundary-response criterion for a protected source term
text:
# A boundary-response criterion for a protected source term Removing one crossing-region factor from the marked source leaves a polynomial in two face variables. Its positive logarithmic growth records how the remaining triangles distribute their loads between those faces. The first derivative is the load at one boundary face; the second is an effective conductance obtained from the triangle Hessians. This note shows how those two quantities can pay for restoring the two removed triangles. More precisely, let \(F(z)\) be the exterior pressure when the boundary weights are \(A=e^z,C=1\), and put \(
u=F'(0)\), \(\kappa=F''(0)\). Under the strict feasibility and connectivity hypotheses below, the condition \(0<
u\le1/2\), \(
u+\kappa\ge1/2\) gives a strict exponential bound for the original signed left contribution, uniformly over its real spectral variable \(\sigma\in[-2,2]\), at odd levels. Every other crossing region keeps its central numerator at spectrum \(-2\). The comparison is with the unchanged diagram's complete action \(\Phi=\operatorname{Vol}(Y)/(2\pi)\), where \(Y\) is its augmented link exterior. The precise bound and proof appear in section 9. The argument allows arbitrary fixed matched simple spheres satisfying these hypotheses, with no restriction on their number of vertices or cycles. It estimates one source contribution. It does not estimate several noncentral regions, varying neighboring spectra, even levels, or the full filling period. No strict enlargement of a known knot-volume class is asserted here. ## 1. Original coordinates and the exact restoration problem Start with a finite simple triangulation of the sphere, with its triangular faces paired across shared edges. This pairing is the matching. A distinguished nonmatching edge carries the original main mark. Use the ordered source of its [matched-sphere Morse diagram](research_matched_sphere_morse_source.md): the matching pairs specify crossing regions, and the two endpoints of the marked edge specify the protected face variables. All these incidences and the mark remain fixed. Use the source argument order \((x,b,c,y)\), for which the two central triangle factors are \((x,b,y)\) and \((x,c,y)\). The selected protected left contribution, also called the cap, has arguments \[ (x,b,c,y)=(C,0,A,0). 	ag{1} \] Here \(A\) is the ordinary overloaded middle; \(C\) is the other ordinary face. Thus the two omitted complete triangles have supports \(\{C\}\) and \(\{A,C\}\). They are not two copies of a two-supported triangle. At level \(N\), write \(d=N-1\). A protected face variable is set to zero by the original main mark; every ordinary face retains the coefficient target \(d\). Let \(I\) be the ordinary faces other than \(A,C\). After extracting precisely those targets from the other central factors, the remaining polynomial is \[ P_N(A,C)= \left[\prod_{i\in I}L_i^dight] \prod_{e
e e_*}P_{e,\mathrm C}(-2; oldsymbol L) =\sum_{j=0}^{d}p_{N,j}A^jC^{d-j}. \] Here \(e_*\) is the selected crossing region. The notation \(P_{e,\mathrm C}\) means its actual central source numerator, with only its common unit sign removed. In particular its original \(N^2\) normalization is retained. At odd levels the coefficients are nonnegative and the nonzero binary polynomial is real stable, meaning that it does not vanish when both variables have positive imaginary part. These facts follow from the original determinant factors, as explained in [the common-axis estimate](research_cap_common_axis_bound.md), sections 2–3. The degree is \(d\), since removing one degree-\(d\) factor and extracting all but the two remaining ordinary targets leaves that homogeneous degree. We write \(S_N(\sigma)\) for the exact shared coefficient when the selected region uses its left numerator at spectrum \(\sigma\) and every other region uses this central numerator at \(-2\). Restoring the removed unit signs multiplies this coefficient by a unit scalar, leaving its absolute value unchanged. No filling functional has been applied. The complete triangle potential used below is \[ Q(w_1,w_2,w_3)= \max_{\substack{a_j\ge0,\ \sum_j a_j=1/2\a_j=0	ext{ if }w_j=0}} \sum_{j:w_j>0} igl[f(a_j)+a_j\log w_j igr], \qquad f(a)= rac{\Lambda(\pi a)+\Lambda(\pi/2-\pi a)}\pi, \] where \(\Lambda(t)=-\int_0^t\log|2\sin u|\,du\). The nonzero weights are positive, and at least one weight is positive in each triangle under consideration. Thus a supported triangle carries total load \(1/2\), and a singleton of weight \(w\) has potential \( rac12\log w\). These are the absolute source conventions of [the triangle entropy formula](../papers/planar-certificates/README.md). Retain every other original triangle, every other ordinary target one, and both protected zeros. Fix \(C=1\), put \(A=e^z\), and minimize over the remaining ordinary log weights: \[ F(z)=\min_{w_I}\left\{ \sum_{t	ext{ exterior}}Q_t(e^z,1,e^{w_I}) -\sum_{i\in I}w_iight\}. 	ag{2} \] Assume a strictly positive feasible exterior half-load table and a connected supported ordinary pair graph. The row masses are \(1/2\), and the extracted demands are precisely one at every \(i\in I\). Strict positivity means that every unprotected corner of a retained triangle has positive load. The graph has one vertex for each ordinary face and joins two faces whenever they occur in the same retained triangle. These are the hypotheses of [the effective-response theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_global_cap_effective_response_criterion.md). It identifies the pressure below with the odd-level limit of \(N^{-1}\log P_N(e^z,1)\), with locally uniform holomorphic derivatives. Define \[ M=F(0),\qquad 
u(z)=F'(z),\qquad \kappa(z)=F''(z),\qquad 
u=
u(0),\quad\kappa=\kappa(0). 	ag{3} \] The interesting interior-cap case has \(0<
u<1/2\). The proofs below also allow \(
u=1/2\). The two omitted complete triangles contribute \( rac12\log C+Q(C,A,0)\). With \(C=1\), set \[ q(z)=Q(1,e^z,0) = rac2\pi\operatorname{Ti}_2(e^{z/2}),\qquad \operatorname{Ti}_2(r)=\int_0^r rac{\arctan t}{t}\,dt. 	ag{4} \] The original remaining target at \(A\) contributes \(-z\). Therefore the complete action of the unchanged diagram is exactly \[  oxed{\quad \Phi=\min_{z\in\mathbb R} \{F(z)+q(z)-z\}.\quad} 	ag{5} \] This is the complete-capacity duality with the original targets. It is not a filling equation or a geometric interpretation of a tilted exterior. [The complete matched-sphere construction](../papers/casimir-source-asymptotics/README.md) identifies \(2\pi\Phi\) with the volume of the original augmented exterior. The useful identities for the restored triangle are \[ q'(z)= rac1\pi\arctan(e^{z/2}),\qquad q''(z)= rac1{4\pi\cosh(z/2)},\qquad q(z)- rac z2=q(-z)>0. 	ag{6} \] The last identity follows by differentiating both sides and evaluating at zero. In particular \(q(0)=2G/\pi\), where \(G=\operatorname{Ti}_2(1)\) is Catalan's constant. ## 2. The positive exterior exists for every finite real tilt The strictly feasible table in (2) proves coercivity in the extracted variables for every fixed finite \(z\). Indeed the recession function is the sum of the triangle maxima minus the prescribed target pairing. Equality with the strictly positive table forces a recession direction to be constant on every supported triangle. Connectedness and the two fixed boundary coordinates then make that direction zero. Compactness of the unit sphere gives a positive recession margin. Changing finite boundary values changes only bounded terms in this argument. The triangle Hessians are graph Laplacians. After grounding \(C\), their sum is positive definite. Thus the minimum exists uniquely for every real \(z\), and the implicit function theorem gives a real analytic interior solution \(w_I(z)\). This argument does not assume that the tilted weights give a complete circle packing or a hyperbolic link exterior. For supported triangle weights \(a,b,c\), its conductance between two distinct supported corners is \[ g_{ab}= rac{ab}{2\pi(a+b)\sqrt{ab+ac+bc}}. 	ag{7} \] The formula includes a protected third corner by setting \(c=0\). A singleton triangle has zero Hessian. Parallel contributions from distinct original triangles are all retained. Differentiate the stationary interior equations with respect to \(z\). The derivative vector has boundary values one at \(A\), zero at \(C\), and is harmonic at every extracted face. The finite connected network maximum principle gives \[ 0\le w_i'(z)\le1\qquad(i\in I). 	ag{8} \] Consequently, between \(z\) and \(z+s\), \(s\ge0\), every positive weight is multiplied by a factor in \([1,e^s]\). The two positive degree-one expressions \(ab/(a+b)\) and \(\sqrt{ab+ac+bc}\) are coordinatewise increasing and homogeneous. Each therefore increases by a factor in that same interval. Their quotient in (7) yields \[ e^{-s}g_{ab}(z)\le g_{ab}(z+s)\le e^s g_{ab}(z). 	ag{9} \] Minimizing the Dirichlet energy over the same boundary potentials preserves both inequalities. Thus the actual Schur response satisfies \[  oxed{\quad e^{-s}\kappa(z)\le\kappa(z+s) \le e^s\kappa(z),\quad s\ge0.\quad} 	ag{10} \] In particular, \[  egin{aligned} 
u(z+s)&\ge
u(z)+\kappa(z)(1-e^{-s}),\ F(z+s)-F(z)&\ge
u(z)s+\kappa(z)(s-1+e^{-s}),\ 
u(z+s)+\kappa(z+s)&\ge
u(z)+\kappa(z). \end{aligned} 	ag{11} \] These are geometric-network inequalities for the original triangle pressure. The root factorization of the odd polynomial gives the same lower bound in the second line, but is not needed for its derivation. ## 3. A sufficient response region without a volume enclosure Suppose \[ 0<
u\le rac12,\qquad 
u+\kappa\ge rac12. 	ag{12} \] The complete minimizer in (5) lies at positive \(z\): at zero the derivative is \(
u-3/4<0\), and the complete capacity has its strict finite minimizer. For \(z\ge0\), (6) and (11) give \[  egin{aligned} F(z)+q(z)-z &\ge M-\kappa+ (
u+\kappa-1/2)z+\kappa e^{-z}+q(-z)\ &\ge M-\kappa. \end{aligned} 	ag{13} \] Hence \[ M-\Phi\le\kappa. 	ag{14} \] The finite odd stable exterior supplies \(0<\kappa\le
u(1-
u)\le1/4\). Its common-axis loss is \[ \mathscr L(
u,\kappa)= - rac12\log\max\{1-
u-\kappa, 
u-\kappa,1-4\kappa\}. 	ag{15} \] Under (12), the first two entries in the maximum are at most \(1/2\). Since \(\kappa\le1/4\), they are strictly smaller than \(e^{-2\kappa}\). The third entry is also strictly smaller than \(e^{-2\kappa}\) for \(\kappa>0\). Therefore \[  oxed{\quad M-\Phi\le\kappa <\mathscr L(
u,\kappa).\quad} 	ag{16} \] Applying the existing common-axis theorem, including its original omitted-tail estimate, proves a strict rate gap for the original odd-level singleton at \((+2,-2,\ldots,-2)\). A limiting gap is at least \[ \min\{\mathscr L(
u,\kappa)-\kappa,\ \gamma/2\}, 	ag{17} \] where \(\gamma\) is the original complete omitted-tail gap. This criterion uses only the exterior load and effective response; it does not rephrase the desired inequality using an unknown \(\Phi\). It is independent of the number of triangles and of graph cycles. ## 4. The weighted rate throughout the half-load interval Put \(H(z)=F(z)-z/2\). Strict complete feasibility supplies an exterior feasible load strictly greater than \(1/2\) at \(A\), so the positive pressure derivative eventually exceeds \(1/2\). There is a unique finite \(z_{1/2}\ge0\) with \[ 
u(z_{1/2})= rac12,\qquad \min_{z\in\mathbb R}H(z)=H(z_{1/2}). 	ag{18} \] Let \(z_*\) be the finite attained complete minimizer in (5). Equation (6) gives the strict comparison \[ \Phi=H(z_*)+q(-z_*)>H(z_{1/2}). 	ag{19} \] At any \(0\le z\le z_{1/2}\), write \(a=1/2-
u(z)\ge0\) and \(k=\kappa(z)>0\). By (11) and (12), \(a\le k\). For \(0\le s\le z_{1/2}-z\), \[ 0\le rac12-
u(z+s)\le a-k(1-e^{-s}). 	ag{20} \] If \(a<k\), the right side vanishes at \(T=-\log(1-a/k)\); the half-load point occurs no later than this value. Integrating (20), and using its limiting value when \(a=k\), gives the sharper action bound \[  egin{aligned} H(z)-H(z_{1/2}) &\le J(a,k),\ J(a,k)&=a+(k-a)\log(1-a/k)\le k,\qquad 0\le a\le k. \end{aligned} 	ag{21} \] Here \(0\log0=0\). It follows that the weighted rate proposed for the coupled spectral estimate satisfies \[  oxed{\quad F(z)- rac z2+ rac12\log(1-4\kappa(z))<\Phi, \qquad 0\le z\le z_{1/2}.\quad} 	ag{22} \] Indeed \(- rac12\log(1-4k)>2k\ge J(a,k)\) for \(0<k<1/4\). At \(k=1/4\), the left side has value \(-\infty\). Compactness of the interval gives a uniform strict margin. If \[ b=
u+\kappa-1/2>0, 	ag{23} \] then (20) at zero gives \(z_{1/2}\le-\log(b/\kappa)\); hence (10) implies \(\kappa(z)\ge b\) throughout the interval. In particular the margin in (22) is greater than \(b\). The sharper expression in (21) may be used instead. This is a geometric comparison for the displayed rate. Section 9 applies the separate odd stable-section estimate to the actual cap contraction. There is no asserted even-level analogue. ## 5. Comparison with complete-packing weak balance Let \(z_*\) be the original complete minimizer in (5). At this cap the complete-packing weak-balance test is exactly \[ q(z_*)\ge z_*. 	ag{24} \] The other middle is protected and carries no surviving one-sided condition. This is a test at the restored complete packing, whereas (12) uses the exterior stationary point with \(A=C\). For the present interior-cap problem, (24) implies (12). Here is a quantitative proof. The function \(q(z)-z\) is strictly decreasing. At \(z=\log(5/2)\), \[ q(-z)< rac2\pi\sqrt{ rac25}< rac49< rac z2. 	ag{25} \] For the last inequality, \(\log(5/2)=2\operatorname{artanh}(3/7) >6/7+18/343>8/9\). Thus (24) implies \(1<t=e^{z_*}<5/2\). At the complete stationary point, \[ 
u(z_*)=1-q'(z_*)> rac58, 	ag{26} \] because \(\sqrt{5/2}<	an(3\pi/8)=1+\sqrt2\). For each root parameter \(p\in[0,1]\) of the original odd stable polynomial, its positive-tilt value is \(p_t=tp/(1-p+tp)\). Direct algebra gives \[ p(2-p)\ge\min\{1,2/t\}\,p_t> rac45p_t \quad	ext{when }p_t>0. 	ag{27} \] To see the nonstrict inequality, divide by \(p_t\) when it is nonzero. The ratio \((2-p)(1+(t-1)p)/t\) is a concave quadratic in \(p\), so its minimum occurs at an endpoint. Average, pass to the same positive pressure, and use (26): \[ 
u+\kappa=\int p(2-p)\,d\mu(p) > rac45
u(z_*)> rac12. 	ag{28} \] Consequently, within the stated range \(0<
u\le1/2\), every cap satisfying complete weak balance belongs to the response region. The ordinary coordinates are not exchanged: \(A\) remains the overloaded middle in (1), as required by the restoration formula. This proof does not require weak balance at the other regions, whose source terms are central in this singleton. However, this note does not prove that (12) gives a strict enlargement within the realizable interior-cap matched-sphere class. A stable binary polynomial by itself would not establish such a geometric classification. In particular no new full knot-volume class is claimed. ## 6. Exact positive tilt of the original common-axis inequality There is a separate, exact way to optimize the positive boundary ratio without changing the cap moments. At a finite odd level let \(d=N-1\), and set \(ho=e^z>0\). Normalize the actual binary exterior by \[  rac{P_N(ho A,C)}{P_N(ho,1)} =\prod_{r=1}^d[(1-p_r(z))C+p_r(z)A]. 	ag{29} \] Let \(
u_d(z),\kappa_d(z)\) be its mean and mean Bernoulli variance, and write \(a=e^{-z}\). Applying the squared-factor arithmetic-geometric mean inequality before maximizing the common negative-axis parameter gives \[  egin{aligned} \max\{B_N^-,B_N^+\} &\le P_N(e^z,1)\,\mathcal R_d(z)^{d/2},\ \mathcal R_d(z)=\max igl\{&1-
u_d-\kappa_d, a^2(
u_d-\kappa_d),\ &1-2(1+a)
u_d+(1+a)^2(
u_d-\kappa_d) igr\}. \end{aligned} 	ag{30} \] Indeed the normalized factors on the two original intervals are \((1-p)-atp\) and \(t(1-p)-ap\), \(0\le t\le1\). Their averaged squares are convex quadratics in the same \(t\). Their three endpoint values are exactly those in (30). The original cap moment pairing and omitted finite tail are unchanged. Thus, after the established pressure limit, \[ \limsup_{N	ext{ odd}} rac1N\log|S_N| \le\max\left\{ \inf_{z\in\mathbb R}\left[F(z)+ rac12\log\mathcal R(z)ight], \Phi- rac\gamma2ight\}, 	ag{31} \] where \(\mathcal R\) uses the actual \(
u(z),\kappa(z)\). It is enough to use any certified finite collection or interval of real tilts. The cap weights have not been rescaled independently, and the polynomial value \(P_N(e^z,1)\) is retained. Dropping that factor would give an incorrect free gain from changing radii. Equation (30) is distinct from the weighted expression in (22). This note does not identify the two bounds or attribute (22) to (30). ## 7. Why stability and two moments alone cannot settle every geometry There is an elementary obstruction to deducing a universal result from only an abstract stable binary exterior and the formal restoration formula. For \(0<\varepsilon<1\), take the root measure with mass \(2/5\) at \(7/10\) and mass \(3/5\) at \(\varepsilon\). Its normalized pressure is \[ F_\varepsilon(z)-M = rac25\log\left( rac3{10}+ rac7{10}e^zight) + rac35\log(1-\varepsilon+\varepsilon e^z). 	ag{32} \] It is realized by genuine stable binary polynomials of degrees divisible by five, has full coefficient support, and has positive response. As \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), its initial mean and response tend to \(7/25\) and \(21/250\). Nevertheless, evaluating the formal restoration at \(z=\log(1/\varepsilon)\) gives \[ M-\inf_z[F_\varepsilon(z)+q(z)-z] \ge rac1{10}\log rac1\varepsilon - rac35\log2- rac{2\sqrt\varepsilon}{\pi} \longrightarrow+\infty. 	ag{33} \] The actual negative-axis supremum has a finite lower rate from its endpoint \(P_N(0,1)\): \[ M+ rac25\log rac3{10} + rac35\log(1-\varepsilon). 	ag{34} \] Hence no correct positive-tilt upper bound for that entire supremum can pay the restoration excess for all these abstract polynomials. This does not construct a matched-sphere counterexample. In fact the unbounded excess is incompatible with the existing positive one-cap geometric pyramid budget in its stated strict range. The example isolates the additional geometric restriction needed by any universal argument; real stability, complete support and positive response do not supply it alone. ## 8. Proof inputs and limits The [common-axis theorem](research_cap_common_axis_bound.md) supplies the original extraction, moment weights, odd stable factorization, squared-factor estimate and omitted-tail bound. The exact restoration of the two complete triangles is recorded in [the cap-capacity comparison](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_cap_constrained_capacity_budget.md) and [the algebraic boundary pressure](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_cap_algebraic_boundary_curve_and_volume_period.md). The [effective-response theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_global_cap_effective_response_criterion.md) gives the original triangle conductance and positive coefficient packet. The limitation discussed in section 7 is compared with [the original one-cap geometric volume budget](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_one_cap_original_chain_volume_budget.md). Sections 2–6 keep these original loads and the same complete action. The Dirichlet estimate controls how the exterior changes with its positive boundary ratio; the restoration formula compares that change with the complete packing. The signed source is retained until the whole exterior has been extracted. The tilted weights are not asserted to describe another hyperbolic manifold. ## 9. Odd singleton consequence on the entire real cap interval Use the finite sine-Cauchy metric and stable alternating-section lemma from [the stable-section proof](research_cap_uniform_spectral_gap.md), sections 1–2. Those are additional finite-source inputs, separate from the geometric comparison above. Their hypotheses hold for the original odd central exterior, with its actual determinant factors and all extracted targets. For clarity, put \[ d=N-1,\qquad M_N=\lfloor N/2floor-1,\qquad Q_{N,M_N}(t)=\sum_{j=0}^{M_N}(-1)^jp_{N,j}t^j . 	ag{35} \] Here \(M_N\) is a cutoff degree, distinct from the pressure \(M=F(0)\). The finite metric theorem bounds the full real cap spectrum by a polynomial multiple of \(\|Q_{N,M_N}\|_C\), where \[ \|Q_{N,M_N}\|_C^2 =\alpha_N\int_0^\infty  rac{|Q_{N,M_N}(t)|^2}{1+t^N}\,dt, \qquad 0<\alpha_N\le1,\qquad \|t^{M_N}\|_C\le1. 	ag{36} \] Take \(T=e^{z_{1/2}}\). The finite stable-section proof gives a pointwise bound on \(0\le t\le T\) by \(|P_N(-t,1)|+p_{N,M_N}t^{M_N}\). On \(t\ge T\), its log-concavity and log-convex pressure argument gives the bound \[ \left(\max\{P_N(T,1)/T^{M_N},(d+1)p_{N,M_N}\} +p_{N,M_N}ight)t^{M_N}. 	ag{37} \] The proof covers support ending at or before \(M_N\), support starting after it, and zero endpoint coefficients; no coefficient-ratio bound is required. This is an estimate for the actual truncated alternating polynomial, not for the full square integrated past its moment range. For \(0\le t\le1\), the original common-axis bound gives rate at most \(M-\mathscr L(
u,\kappa)<\Phi\). For \(1\le t\le T\), put \(z=\log t\). The same actual polynomial, normalized at this positive tilt, satisfies \[ |P_N(-e^z,1)| \le P_N(e^z,1)(1-4\kappa_d(z))^{d/2} \le P_N(e^z,1)e^{-2d\kappa_d(z)}. 	ag{38} \] The pressure and its first two normalized derivatives converge uniformly on the compact interval \([0,z_{1/2}]\). To justify this use of the derivative, apply the original positive coefficient packet at each real tilt. Section 2 supplies the unique strict stationary interior point at every tilt. These points form a compact set; the grounded Hessians stay positive and the same connected, primitive ordinary phase graph gives a strict complementary angular gap. The determinant derivatives are uniformly bounded on small complex neighborhoods. A finite subcover therefore gives relative holomorphic packets with uniform error on the interval. Analytic logarithms and Cauchy differentiation give the asserted convergence. This is not differentiation of a pointwise rate or a continuation to the negative axis. After the factor \(t^{d/2}\) is removed in the integral (36), (38) has limiting rate \(H(z)-2\kappa(z)\). Equation (21) shows this is at most \(H(z_{1/2})-\kappa(z)\). The minimum of \(\kappa(z)\) on the compact interval is positive. Thus the bounded part of the integral is strictly below \(\Phi\), uniformly; the estimate also avoids a logarithmic continuity issue if \(\kappa(z)=1/4\). The first term of (37) has rate \[ \lim_N rac1N\log rac{P_N(T,1)}{T^{M_N}} =F(z_{1/2})- rac{z_{1/2}}2 =H(z_{1/2})<\Phi . 	ag{39} \] The bounded difference between \(M_N\) and \(d/2\) changes no rate. The original closed coefficient-capacity theorem bounds \(p_{N,M_N}\) by rate at most \(\Phi-\gamma_D\), for some \(\gamma_D>0\), because \(M_N/d	o1/2\). The finite norm \(\|t^{M_N}\|_C\le1\) completes the unbounded-tail estimate. Consequently, under (12), the original signed singleton satisfies \[  oxed{\quad \limsup_{\substack{N	o\infty\N\ \mathrm{odd}}}  rac1N\log\sup_{\sigma\in[-2,2]}|S_N(\sigma)| \le \Phi-\delta,\qquad \delta=\min\{\mathscr L(
u,\kappa)-\kappa,\, \Phi-H(z_{1/2}),\,\gamma_D\}>0 . \quad} 	ag{40} \] Every other original region retains its central numerator at spectrum \(-2\). The result concerns one original sector and one free spectral variable. It supplies no estimate for varying neighboring spectra, several noncentral regions, the even central exterior or the entire filled invariant. In particular this corollary is not a new knot-volume theorem.

title: An exponential obstruction to the bare cap-moment Cauchy estimate
text: # An exponential obstruction to the bare cap-moment Cauchy estimate This obstruction keeps the original even-level demand. It disproves the proposed strengthening by a positive Cauchy norm, not the signed convolution, a shared source estimate, or a volume-conjecture limit. ## 1. The original coefficient and the particular proposed norm bound Use the exact source in [original-demand cap/CROSS convolution](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_two_port_main_cap_original_demand_convolution.md): the adjacent ordered quartets are \[ E=(A,0,C,Z),\qquad F=(0,A,0,C), \] with the two original protected faces specialized to zero. The ordinary face \(A\) occurs only at these two ports, so its degree \(d=N-1\) is extracted first. The CROSS coupon at \(E\) is evaluated at \(-2\) and the RIGHT coupon at \(F\) at \(+2\). Keep \[ N=2m,\quad M=m-1,\quad \theta=\pi/N,\quad s_r=2\sin(r\theta),\quad a_r=4\cos^2((r+\tfrac12)\theta). \] The original positive endpoint continuant and its unused factors are \[ \begin{split} K_0&=1,\qquad K_1=s_1^2(A+Z),\\ K_r&=s_r^2(A+Z)K_{r-1} +s_rs_{r-1}a_{r-1}AZK_{r-2},\\ C_{j,h}&=[A^jZ^{d-h-j}]K_{d-h} \prod_{r=d-h+1}^{d}a_r. \end{split} \tag{1} \] For \(0\le n\le d-1\), the actual remaining coefficient is, up to the common raw sign \((-1)^d\), \[ S_{N,n}=\sum_{j\in J_n}(-1)^jU_jC_{j,n-j},\qquad D_{N,n}=\sum_{j\in J_n}V_jC_{j,n-j}>0, \quad J_n=[\max(0,n-M),\min(M,n)]\cap\mathbb Z, \tag{2} \] where the endpoint comparator is \(D_{N,n}\), and \[ \begin{split} U_j&=\csc^2(\theta/2) \prod_{r=1}^{j}\frac{\sin^2(r\theta)} {\sin^2((r+\tfrac12)\theta)},\\ V_j&=\sec^2(\theta/2) \prod_{r=1}^{j}\frac{\sin^2(r\theta)} {\cos^2((r+\tfrac12)\theta)}. \end{split} \tag{3} \] The degree \(A^d\), both remaining degrees \(C^nZ^{d-n}\), every unused row in (1), and the genuine RIGHT/CROSS cutoffs are unchanged. The positive moment theorem [positive cap-moment theorem](research_flat_cap_positive_moment_form.md) constructs a positive random variable \(X_N\) with \(U_0\mathbb E X_N^j=U_j\) through degree \(d\). Set \[ F_{N,n}(t)=\sum_{j\in J_n}C_{j,n-j}t^j,\qquad \mathcal L_N(p)=U_0\mathbb E p(X_N). \] Thus \(S_{N,n}=\mathcal L_N(F_{N,n}(-t))\). The bare moment-Cauchy upper bound is \[ |S_{N,n}|\le \mathcal N_{N,n},\qquad \mathcal N_{N,n} :=\sqrt{U_0\mathcal L_N(F_{N,n}(-t)^2)} =U_0\sqrt{\mathbb E F_{N,n}(-X_N)^2}. \tag{4} \] Its square is finite because \(\deg F_{N,n}\le M\) and \(2M=d-1\). The proposed strengthening \(\mathcal N_{N,n}\le C N^kD_{N,n}\), uniformly in \(N,n\), is false. More precisely, with \[ f(t)=-\int_0^t\log\tan(\pi s)\,ds =\frac{\Lambda(\pi t)+\Lambda(\pi/2-\pi t)}{\pi}, \quad 0\le t\le\tfrac12, \] for every fixed \(u\in(0,1/4]\) and every sequence of even levels and original degrees satisfying \(N\to\infty\) and \(n/N\to u\), we prove \[ \boxed{ \liminf_{N\to\infty} \frac1N\log\frac{\mathcal N_{N,n}}{D_{N,n}} \ \ge\ \chi(u):=4f(u/2)-2f(u)-k(u)>0,\qquad k(u)=2\int_0^u\log(2\cos(\pi t))\,dt.} \tag{5} \] This is an obstruction with the original face demand already imposed. The open comparison \(|S_{N,n}|\le C N^kD_{N,n}\) is not contradicted: the signed expectation in (4) can be much smaller than its norm. ## 2. A single exact orthogonal projection The beta-product construction can be split into two independent copies: \(X_N=Y_NY_N'\), where \[ w_j=\mathbb E Y_N^j=\sqrt{U_j/U_0},\qquad \frac{w_j}{w_{j-1}} =\frac{\sin(j\theta)}{\sin((j+\tfrac12)\theta)}. \tag{6} \] All moments used below have degree at most \(d\). Let \(\ell_N(p)=\mathbb E p(Y_N)\). For completeness, the exact orthogonal polynomials used here follow directly from these moments. On polynomials of degree at most \(M\), with \(D=t\partial_t\), set \[ T=t^{-1}(\cos(2\theta D)-1) -\cos(\theta(2D+\tfrac12)). \] The first numerator annihilates constants. Writing \(A_j=\cos(2j\theta)-1\), \(B_j=-\cos((2j+\tfrac12)\theta)\), its monomial action is \(Tt^j=A_jt^{j-1}+B_jt^j\). The exact sine ratio (6) gives \[ (A_i-A_j)w_{i+j-1}+(B_i-B_j)w_{i+j}=0. \] Thus \(T\) is symmetric for \(\ell_N\). The eigenvalues \(B_0,\ldots,B_M\) are distinct, and its eigenpolynomials \(P_r\), normalized by \(P_r(0)=1\), are orthogonal. Coefficient comparison gives \[ \frac{[t^{j+1}]P_r}{[t^j]P_r} =-\frac{\sin((r+j+\tfrac12)\theta)\sin((r-j)\theta)} {\sin^2((j+1)\theta)}. \] Consequently their leading coefficients and squared norms are \[ \kappa_r=[t^r]P_r =(-1)^r\frac{\prod_{a=r}^{2r-1}\sin((a+\tfrac12)\theta)} {\prod_{a=1}^{r}\sin(a\theta)},\qquad g_r=\ell_N(P_r^2) =\frac{\sin(\theta/2)}{\sin((2r+\tfrac12)\theta)}. \tag{7} \] Here empty products give \(\kappa_0=g_0=1\). One direct verification of the norm formula is the multiplication recurrence \(tP_r=\mathcal A_rP_{r+1}+\mathcal B_rP_r+ \mathcal C_rP_{r-1}\), whose leading coefficients and value at zero give \[ \mathcal A_r=-\frac{\sin((r+1)\theta)\sin((r+\tfrac12)\theta)} {\sin((2r+\tfrac12)\theta) \sin((2r+\tfrac32)\theta)},\qquad \mathcal C_r=-\frac{\sin(r\theta)\sin((r-\tfrac12)\theta)} {\sin((2r-\tfrac12)\theta) \sin((2r+\tfrac12)\theta)}. \] Symmetry then gives \(g_r/g_{r-1}=\mathcal C_r/\mathcal A_{r-1} =\sin((2r-\tfrac32)\theta)/\sin((2r+\tfrac12)\theta)\), which telescopes to (7). For the indices needed below, eventually \(r\le n<M\), since \(n/N\to u\le1/4\). Thus no polynomial beyond the finite Hilbert degree is needed. These are the single-factor polynomials, not the different Jacobi polynomials of the source continuant. Now take any sequence specified in (5), at sufficiently large \(N\). Then \(n<M\), so the original range is exactly \(J_n=\{0,\ldots,n\}\), not a replacement cutoff. In the positive tensor metric \(\ell_N\otimes\ell_N\), project \(F_{N,n}(-tu)\) onto \(P_n(t)\otimes1\). Orthogonality removes every \(j<n\), while \(\ell_N(t^nP_n)=g_n/\kappa_n\). Therefore \[ \langle F_{N,n}(-tu),P_n(t)\otimes1\rangle =(-1)^n C_{n,0}w_n\frac{g_n}{\kappa_n}, \] and a single orthogonal projection gives the exact bound \[ \boxed{\mathcal N_{N,n} \ge U_0 C_{n,0}\frac{w_n\sqrt{g_n}}{|\kappa_n|}.} \tag{8} \] This projection is unaffected by any cancellation among the other tensor components. It uses no condition-number estimate for the monomial-to-orthogonal basis change. The remaining factors in (8), apart from \(C_{n,0}\) and \(\kappa_n\), have zero exponential rate. The literal sine product gives, for \(j\le M\), \[ 4\cos^2(\theta/2)\le U_j\le\csc^2(\theta/2)\le N^2, \qquad N^{-1}\le g_j\le1. \tag{9} \] For the lower bound on \(U_j\), compare each denominator sine to \(\sin((r+1)\theta)\) and telescope; all the angles are at most \(\pi/2\). In particular \(w_n\ge\sqrt3/N\), and none of these factors can hide an exponential loss. ## 3. The exact endpoint comparator rate The uniform closed endpoint coefficient theorem in [uniform half-block and triangle coefficient theorem](actual_fejer_half_block_entropy.md) and [continuous full-kernel coefficient theorem](actual_fejer_full_kernel_entropy_identity_reduction.md) applies to the actual coefficients (1). On a triangle of total load \(1/2\), its entropy is the sum of \(f\) at the three corner loads. The CROSS rate is the maximum of the sum over its two genuine triangles, with one shared outer split. Finite forced degree shifts and polynomial scalar factors are already covered by that uniform closed theorem. For \(n/N\to\rho\le1/4\), \(j/N\to v\), the endpoint cap has \(N^{-1}\log V_j\to-2f(v)\). The CROSS coefficient in (1) has limiting loads \((v,0,\rho-v,1-\rho)\). Write the first outer split as \(a\). The two triangle entropies give the combined rate \[ E_\rho(a,v)=2f(a)+f(v-a)+f(\rho-v)+f(\rho-a)-2f(v), \qquad 0\le a\le v\le\rho. \tag{10} \] The uniform closed coefficient theorem and the polynomial number of terms in (2) imply that the rate of \(D_{N,n}\) is the maximum in (10), along any such sequence. The \(d=N-1\) versus \(N\) normalization changes the arguments by \(O(1/N)\); continuity handles it. At limiting \(\rho=1/4\), one does not need the finite ratio \(n/d\) to be at most \(1/4\). We prove the elementary maximum identity \[ \max_{0\le a\le v\le\rho}E_\rho(a,v)=2f(\rho), \qquad 0<\rho\le\tfrac14. \tag{11} \] On this interval \(f\) is nonnegative, increasing and concave. The three boundary edges satisfy \[ \begin{array}{ll} a=0:&E=f(\rho-v)+f(\rho)-f(v)\le2f(\rho),\\ a=v:&E=2f(\rho-v)\le2f(\rho),\\ v=\rho:&E=2[f(a)+f(\rho-a)-f(\rho)] \le4f(\rho/2)-2f(\rho)\le2f(\rho). \end{array} \] Equality occurs at \(a=v=0\). There is no critical point in the open triangle. Indeed put \(z=\tan(\pi v)\), \(p=\tan(\pi\rho)\), \(u=\tan(\pi a)\). The two critical equations are \[ u^2=\frac{(z-u)(p-u)}{(1+zu)(1+pu)},\qquad \frac{z-u}{1+zu}=z^2\frac{p-z}{1+pz}. \] Let \(r=p-z\), so \(0<r<1\). The second equation forces \(u=z/(1+rz)\). Substituting into the first forces \[ 1+2rz+z^2=r^2(1+rz)^2. \] But the left side minus the right side is \[ (1-r^2)\bigl[1+2rz+(1+r^2)z^2\bigr]>0. \] This contradiction proves (11), since every interior maximum of the smooth function would be critical. Compactness and the displayed boundary checks include all corners. It follows, along the sequences in (5), that \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log D_{N,n}=2f(u). \tag{12} \] The lower bound can also be seen without a coefficient limit: the original \(j=0\) term has \[ C_{0,n}=N^2\prod_{h=0}^{n-1} \frac{\cos^2((h+\tfrac12)\theta)}{\sin^2((h+1)\theta)}, \] whose logarithmic rate is \(2f(\rho)\), while \(V_0\) has zero rate. Thus the maximizing boundary term is genuinely present in the original finite sum. For the numerator projection, \(C_{n,0}\) has both middle loads zero and total outer load \(n/d\to u\). Its two endpoint triangles maximize \(2f(a)+2f(u-a)\) at \(a=u/2\). Hence \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log C_{n,0}=4f(u/2). \tag{13} \] The lower bound here is specifically the positive endpoint coefficient lower theorem, not the later sharp spectral limsup majorant. To see its application directly, the original coefficientwise comparison (15) of [uniform half-block and triangle coefficient theorem](actual_fejer_half_block_entropy.md) specializes at both middle variables zero to \[ 4(A+Z)D_0(A,Z)^2\ \le\ K_d(A,Z) \ <\ 12(A+Z)D_0(A,Z)^2. \] The actual \(D_0\) coefficients have the uniform closed triangle rate \(2f(a)\), including this protected-middle face. Choose a genuine integer split of the desired outer degree within a bounded distance of \(n/2\), and retain either forced outer term \(A\) or \(Z\). The positive convolution supplies the lower rate in (13); concavity and its polynomial number of terms supply the matching upper rate. The forced outer unit and each degree \(M=N/2-1\) cause only bounded degree offsets, covered by the closed coefficient theorem. Thus (13) uses the original continuant coefficient, not an auxiliary unconditioned face polynomial or an unproved spectral lower estimate. ## 4. A strictly positive excess and its precise limitation The explicit product (7) yields \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log|\kappa_n| =\int_u^{2u}\log\sin(\pi t)\,dt -\int_0^u\log\sin(\pi t)\,dt =k(u). \tag{14} \] For the last equality, rewrite the difference as \(\int_0^{2u}\log\sin(\pi t)\,dt -2\int_0^u\log\sin(\pi t)\,dt\), then use sine doubling. The endpoint logarithm is integrable; upper and lower sums on the two monotonicity intervals, with its first cell integrated directly, justify these shifted Riemann sums. The error from the finite products to the same integrals with endpoint \(n/N\) is \(O(\log N/N)\); continuity then handles arbitrary \(n/N\to u\), including integer floors.
