The phases cannot all be removed There is a structural limit to simultaneous diagonal gluing and real multiplication. **Proposition 2.** For \(N\ge2\), in any basis \(g_a\) satisfying \(\phi(g_ag_b)=\delta_{ab}\), the full triple tensor \(\phi(g_ag_bg_c)\) cannot have all its entries in \(e^{i\vartheta}\mathbb R\) for one common phase \(\vartheta\). In particular it cannot be entirely real or nonnegative. **Proof.** Write \(1=\sum_a\ell_ag_a\), so \(\ell_a=\phi(g_a)\). Then \[ \sum_a\ell_a^2=\phi(1)=0 . \tag{30} \] Suppose the triple tensor were \(e^{i\vartheta}R_{abc}\) with all \(R_{abc}\) real. The unit equations become \[ \sum_av_aR_{abc}=\delta_{bc},\qquad v_a=e^{i\vartheta}\ell_a . \tag{31} \] Their solution is unique: the difference of two solutions would give an element whose multiplication operator is zero, and applying it to \(1\) would show that element is zero. Real coefficients therefore force \(v=\bar v\). It is nonzero because the unit is nonzero. But then \(\sum_a\ell_a^2=e^{-2i\vartheta}\sum_av_a^2\ne0\), contrary to (30). \(\square\) This statement concerns bases orthonormal for the original **bilinear Frobenius form**. It does not concern every Hermitian orthonormal basis. The original Newton basis already has real nonnegative multiplication, but its Frobenius pairing is anti-diagonal. The two facts are compatible. Here the signed leaves and gluing simplify, while necessary phases remain in \(C\) and in the two explicit closing rows. ## 7. Scope and complete sources The construction is at the fixed original root and complete main color. It transports the entire Casimir algebra, including its Hermite directions. It does not claim a generic-\(q\) or moving peripheral extension without the corresponding original families. No positive geometric contour, nonzero global saddle coefficient, or additional volume-identity class follows from this basis change. Both complete proof texts were read at the matching pins: | Source | SHA-256 | |---|---| | [Original Newton turn, closures and signed crossings](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_newton_turn_positive_gram.md) | d8b21fa8db909120035e86e997a0e02cb84f8dce2dcf6fb244bb5c85c17e28a3 | | [Full positive Newton multiplication](../papers/newton-calculus/README.md) | 543b5be6035ecec349ce8e78ee47085345ceefe4fc51e5f2005b802d999805bb | The complete [arbitrary-power compiler](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_arbitrary_power_source_compilation.md) and [finite Fourier-band theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_newton_interpolation_finite_fourier_band.md) were also read for coverage, at pins 55e2de84870cfd20dac5922791dbc2bed54909439dfbf4663f17c70a1089445f and 2e2d95184081ba6440b56268cb597624d97a5f1931e8c0df886fa754e6684304. They already supply exact source compilation and finite Fourier representations. No novelty is claimed for the Fourier transform or for unitary changes of tensor coordinates. The useful combination here is diagonal original bilinear gluing, both signed leaves as exact modes, one symmetric multiplication tensor, and the obstruction to removing all of that tensor's phases. Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used. No mathematical program, numerical experiment, test, build, git operation or earlier-final edit was performed.

title: Closed products and Gaussian weights for the full Conway tensor
text: # Closed products and Gaussian weights for the full Conway tensor Written research proof, 22 November 2026. The generating polynomial of the entire centered Conway tensor has a single finite sum over the physical Casimir nodes. Every summand uses explicit finite products and a quadratic Gaussian crossing weight. The first-normal contribution is explicit as well. In particular this does not replace the repeated-root algebra by its ordinary values. The result generates all three-index coefficients algebraically and gives a uniform complex upper bound for their generating polynomial on fixed discs. It does not estimate their coherent contraction with a short component or prove an action-relative geometric bound. ## 1. The polynomial generating the centered modes Fix the original level and phases \[ N\ge2,\quad d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\quad h=Q^{-1},\quad \eta=(-1)^d,\quad \kappa=q^{d^2/2}, \] \[ P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2,\qquad \mathcal H_N=\mathbb C[z]/(P_N). \tag{1} \] Here \(T_N\) is the Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind. Every fractional power of \(q\) means its displayed exponential. Use the original Frobenius trace \(\phi_N\) and centered basis \(f_a\) of the Fourier compiler. Its signed crossing class \(R=R^+\) obeys \[ f_a=N^{-1/2}R\,p_a(z),\qquad p_0=1,\qquad C_{abc}=\phi_N(f_af_bf_c). \tag{2} \] Each \(p_a\) is its unique ordinary polynomial of degree \(a\). The entire quotient, including its spectral first normals, is used. Define an ordinary polynomial in independent variables \(t,z\): \[ A_N(t,z)=\sum_{a=0}^d p_a(z)t^a. \tag{3} \] It satisfies the exact forced equation \[ \boxed{\quad (1+zt+t^2)A_N(t,z) -(1+q^{-1}t)^2A_N(ht,z) =\frac{\eta}{N}P_N(z)t^N. \quad} \tag{4} \] This is an ordinary polynomial identity, not just an identity at distinct spectral values. Here is its derivation. The compiler gives \[ zp_a=(h^{a+1}-1)p_{a+1} +2q^{-1}h^ap_a+(h^a-1)p_{a-1}, \qquad p_{-1}=0,\quad 0\le a<d. \tag{5} \] The final equation at \(a=d\) holds in \(\mathcal H_N\), with its first term absent since \(h^N=1\). Sum these equations after multiplication by \(t^{a+1}\). All coefficients of the difference in (4) vanish except possibly that of \(t^N\); the \(t^{N+1}\) coefficient cancels because \(h^N=1\). The remaining coefficient vanishes in the full quotient and has degree at most \(N\) in \(z\), hence is a scalar multiple of \(P_N\). By (5), \[ [z^a]p_a=\frac{(-1)^a}{(h;h)_a},\qquad (h;h)_d=N. \tag{6} \] Its leading coefficient is therefore \(\eta/N\), proving (4). We will repeatedly use coefficientwise uniqueness in \(t\). For a polynomial \(X(t)\) of degree at most \(d\), its constant term and the right side of (4) determine every other coefficient: in degree \(t^a\), \(1\le a<N\), the coefficient of the new unknown is \(1-h^a\ne0\). The remaining terms involve only lower degrees. This argument also applies to the differentiated inhomogeneous equations below. ## 2. Closed products at every physical node Index the distinct physical nodes by \[ 0\le j\le\lfloor d/2\rfloor,\qquad \theta_j=(2j+1)\pi/N,\quad v_j=qQ^j=e^{i\theta_j},\quad c_j=v_j+v_j^{-1},\quad m_j=N-2j-1. \tag{7} \] The double nodes have \(m_j>0\), equivalently \(0\le j\le\lfloor(N-2)/2\rfloor\). When \(N\) is odd, the last node \(j_*=(N-1)/2\) is simple: \(c_{j_*}=-2\) and \(m_{j_*}=0\). Use empty products when an interval has length zero, and define \[ D_j(t)=\prod_{r=-j+1}^{0}(1+q^{-1}Q^rt),\qquad B_j(t)=\prod_{r=j+2}^{N-j}(1+q^{-1}Q^rt). \tag{8} \] Their degrees are \(j\) and \(m_j\), respectively. The exponent \(r=N\) in a product means \(Q^N=1\); no endpoint factor is omitted. Then the exact physical value of the whole generating polynomial is \[ \boxed{\qquad A_N(t,c_j)=D_j(t)^2B_j(t).\qquad} \tag{9} \] Thus all values \(p_a(c_j)\) are coefficients of one finite product. To prove (9), call its proposed right side \(V_j(t)\). Cancellation of its consecutive factors gives \[ \frac{D_j(ht)}{D_j(t)} =\frac{1+q^{-1}Q^{-j}t}{1+q^{-1}t},\qquad \frac{B_j(ht)}{B_j(t)} =\frac{1+q^{-1}Q^{j+1}t}{1+q^{-1}Q^{-j}t}. \tag{10} \] For the empty last product at an odd simple node, the numerator and denominator in its displayed ratio coincide. Since \(q^{-1}Q^{j+1}=v_j\) and \(q^{-1}Q^{-j}=v_j^{-1}\), (10) gives \[ (1+c_jt+t^2)V_j(t)=(1+q^{-1}t)^2V_j(ht). \tag{11} \] Ratios here may first be read off their zero sets; after clearing denominators they are polynomial identities everywhere. The degree of \(V_j\) is \(2j+m_j=d\), and \(V_j(0)=1\). Equation (4) is homogeneous at \(z=c_j\), so the uniqueness just proved gives (9). No infinite-product specialization is involved. ## 3. The full first normal At every double node the required normal is \[ \boxed{\qquad \partial_z A_N(t,c_j) =\frac{D_j(t)^2\,tB_j'(t)}{v_j-v_j^{-1}}. \qquad} \tag{12} \] Here the prime on \(B_j\) means differentiation in \(t\). The formula is a spectral derivative in \(z\), not the result of differentiating (9) in a continuously varied index \(j\). No derivative condition is imposed at the odd simple node. Differentiate (4) in \(z\). At a double node \(P_N'(c_j)=0\), giving \[ (1+c_jt+t^2)\partial_zA_N(t,c_j) -(1+q^{-1}t)^2\partial_zA_N(ht,c_j) =-tA_N(t,c_j). \tag{13} \] The proposed right side of (12) is polynomial of degree at most \(d\) and has constant term zero. To verify (13), put \[ L_j(t)=\frac{tB_j'(t)}{B_j(t)} =\sum_{r=j+2}^{N-j} \frac{q^{-1}Q^rt}{1+q^{-1}Q^rt}. \] The two ends of this finite sum give \[ L_j(t)-L_j(ht) =\frac1{1+v_jt}-\frac1{1+v_j^{-1}t} =-\frac{(v_j-v_j^{-1})t}{1+c_jt+t^2}. \tag{14} \] Multiply (14) by the product identity (11). The result is precisely (13) for (12), first where the rational expressions are defined, then everywhere as a polynomial identity. Coefficientwise uniqueness with constant term zero proves the full normal formula. The denominator \(v_j-v_j^{-1}=2i\sin\theta_j\) is nonzero at every double node, including the last even-level double node. For example \(N=2\) gives \[ A_2(t,z)=1+(-z/2-i)t,\quad D_0=1,\quad B_0=1-it,\quad \partial_zA_2(t,0)=-t/2 . \tag{15} \] At \(N=3\), the simple node has \(A_3(t,-2)=(1+q^{-1}t)^2\); its derivative is not needed. ## 4. The literal trace and Gaussian crossing data For a germ \(F\) at the physical nodes the original full trace is \[ \phi_N(F)=\eta\sum_{j\ {\rm double}} \{(4-c_j^2)F'(c_j)-c_jF(c_j)\} +\mathbf1_{N\ {\rm odd}}F(-2). \tag{16} \] We recall its normalization. The top Newton polynomial has leading coefficient \(\eta/N^2\) and trace one. Therefore \(\phi_N\) is \(\eta N^2\) times the leading coefficient of the full Hermite remainder. That coefficient is the sum of the finite residues of \(F/P_N\). At a double root the Chebyshev equation gives \[ \frac{P_N''(c_j)}2=\frac{N^2}{4-c_j^2},\qquad \frac{P_N'''(c_j)}{3P_N''(c_j)}=\frac{c_j}{4-c_j^2}. \tag{17} \] The residue is thus \(\{(4-c_j^2)F'(c_j)-c_jF(c_j)\}/N^2\). At the odd simple node \(P_N'(-2)=N^2\) and \(\eta=1\). This proves (16), retaining all required first normals. Use the original signed positive crossing, not a fitted Gaussian. Its value and its independent full normal are \[ \rho_j:=R(c_j)=\kappa(-1)^jq^{j(j+1)},\qquad \frac{R'(c_j)}{R(c_j)} =\frac{i\,m_j}{4\sin\theta_j} \quad(j\ {\rm double}). \tag{18} \] These are the literal full-jet crossing formulas in the phase-transport source. They follow there by checking the holomorphic representative \[ q^{d^2/4}\exp\!\left(\frac{iN}{4\pi} \arccos(-z/2)^2\right) \tag{19} \] at the physical angular lifts and differentiating it in \(z\). Its square-angle branch is regular at \(-2\) and slit at \([2,\infty)\). The first normal is part of the source identity, not inferred from the values in (18). At the odd simple node use only the value \(\rho_{j_*}\) in (18)'s first formula. Every \(\rho_j\) has modulus one. ## 5. One finite Gaussian sum for all coefficients Let \(\mathbf t=(t_1,t_2,t_3)\), and put \[ \mathscr C_N(\mathbf t)=\sum_{a,b,c=0}^d C_{abc}t_1^at_2^bt_3^c. \tag{20} \] Equations (2)--(3) give the exact full-algebra identity \[ \mathscr C_N(\mathbf t) =N^{-3/2}\phi_N\!\left(R^3 \prod_{\ell=1}^3 A_N(t_\ell,z)\right). \tag{21} \] Substitute (9), (12), and (18) into the literal trace (16). The result is \[ \boxed{\begin{aligned} \mathscr C_N(\mathbf t) ={}&\frac{\eta}{N^{3/2}}\sum_{j\ {\rm double}} \rho_j^3\prod_{\ell=1}^3D_j(t_\ell)^2\\ &\ \cdot\left[ (3im_j\sin\theta_j-c_j)\prod_{\ell=1}^3B_j(t_\ell) -2i\sin\theta_j\sum_{\ell=1}^3 t_\ell B_j'(t_\ell)\prod_{r\ne\ell}B_j(t_r) \right]\\ &+\frac{\mathbf1_{N\ {\rm odd}}}{N^{3/2}}\, \rho_{j_*}^3\prod_{\ell=1}^3D_{j_*}(t_\ell)^2 . \end{aligned}} \tag{22} \] The sum has one term per distinct physical node. All factors in its products are explicit in (8). The crossing weight \(\rho_j^3=\kappa^3(-1)^jq^{3j(j+1)}\) is a specified quadratic Gaussian phase. Its normal contributes the term \(3im_j\sin\theta_j\); omitting it would change the tensor. The normal of \(A_N\) differentiates the \(B_j\) factor as in (12), and is exactly the other term in the bracket. The odd simple node has its own coefficient one in (16), rather than being inserted into a double-node formula with a singular denominator or an extra factor two. In particular the constant terms of (22) at \(N=2,3\) are respectively \[ C_{000}=\frac{3\kappa}{2\sqrt2},\qquad C_{000}=\frac{-2+3i\sqrt3}{3\sqrt3}. \tag{23} \] These also follow directly from \(C_{000}=N^{-3/2}\phi_N(R^3)\). Equation (22) is an identity of trivariate ordinary polynomials. Coefficient extraction gives every \(C_{abc}\), with all phase carriers and both level parities. It is not an evaluation restricted to distinct spectral roots: the separately proved normal formula is essential to that statement. ## 6. An explicit cyclic rank-one equation The finite forcing also determines the exact cyclic compatibility condition. Put \(a=q^{-1}\) and \[ g(t,z)=\frac{1+zt+t^2}{(1+at)^2}. \] In the rational function ring with polynomial \(z\), one has \[ \boxed{\quad \prod_{r=0}^{N-1}g(h^rt,z) =1-\frac{(-1)^NP_N(z)t^N} {[1+(-1)^Nt^N]^2}. \quad} \tag{24} \] For an elementary proof introduce \(v\) with \(v+v^{-1}=z\). The numerator product is \[ (1-(-vt)^N)(1-(-v^{-1}t)^N) =1-(-1)^N(P_N(z)-2)t^N+t^{2N}, \] using \(v^N+v^{-N}=2T_N(z/2)=P_N(z)-2\). The denominator is \((1-(-at)^N)^2=[1+(-1)^Nt^N]^2\), since \(a^N=-1\). Subtracting these two expressions proves (24); their symmetric dependence on \(v,v^{-1}\) makes it a polynomial identity in \(z\). This gives a precise cyclic statement on the nonreduced algebra. Let \[ \mathcal B=\mathcal H_N\otimes_{\mathbb C}\mathbb C(t),\qquad \sigma(t)=ht,\quad \sigma(z)=z. \] Then \(\mathcal B^\sigma=\mathcal H_N\otimes\mathbb C(t^N)\): expand in a fixed complex basis of \(\mathcal H_N\), and then use the basis \(1,t,\ldots,t^{N-1}\) of \(\mathbb C(t)\) over \(\mathbb C(t^N)\), on which \(\sigma\) acts diagonally with distinct eigenvalues \(1,h,\ldots,h^{N-1}\). By (24) the cyclic product of \(g\) is one in \(\mathcal B\), and (4) reads \[ \sigma A_N=gA_N\quad\hbox{in }\mathcal B. \tag{25} \] The element \(A_N\) is invertible there. Indeed (9) is a nonzero rational function at every residue field of \(\mathcal H_N\); an element of each dual-number component is a unit exactly when its value is nonzero. Thus the set of invertible solutions of (25) is nonempty, and every such solution is uniquely \(A_N b\) with \(b\in(\mathcal B^\sigma)^\times\). This follows just by taking the ratio of two solutions. It requires no general Hilbert 90 theorem over a nonreduced ring. Among polynomial solutions of degree less than \(N\) in \(t\), the normalization \(A_N(0,z)=1\) selects this one by the coefficientwise uniqueness following (6). In particular the cyclic description retains the nilpotent components rather than taking the norm only at distinct spectral values. ## 7. A uniform complex bound for the full generating tensor Fix \(0<r<1\). Define the dilogarithm only on its convergent disc, \(\operatorname{Li}_2(w)=\sum_{k\ge1}w^k/k^2\), and set \[ \mathcal S(v,t)= \frac{\operatorname{Li}_2(-vt)+\operatorname{Li}_2(-v^{-1}t) -2\operatorname{Li}_2(-t)}{2\pi i}, \qquad |v|=1,\quad |t|\le r. \tag{26} \] Every factor in (9) is zero-free on this disc. With logarithms normalized to zero at \(t=0\), one has the uniform estimate \[ \log A_N(t,c_j)=N\mathcal S(v_j,t)+O_r(1), \qquad |t|\le r, \tag{27} \] simultaneously for every physical node, every \(N\ge2\), and both parities. Here the complex logarithm, not just its real part, is controlled. Write \(f_t(u)=\log(1+te^{iu})\). Its size and first derivative are uniformly bounded for \(|t|\le r\). The consecutive factors in (8), whose phase spacing is \(2\pi/N\), give Riemann sums with a uniformly bounded total error. Their endpoints differ by at most a fixed number of mesh cells from the arcs \([-\theta_j,0]\) and \([\theta_j,2\pi-\theta_j]\). Hence \[ \frac1N\log(D_j(t)^2B_j(t)) =\frac1{2\pi} \left(2\int_{-\theta_j}^0 f_t(u)\,du +\int_{\theta_j}^{2\pi-\theta_j} f_t(u)\,du\right) +O_r(N^{-1}). \] The full circle integral is zero, by the absolutely convergent logarithm series. The displayed integral therefore equals \((2\pi)^{-1}(\int_{-\theta_j}^0-\int_0^{\theta_j})f_t\). Integrating the same series identifies it with (26). This proves (27), including shrinking arcs at the end nodes. The normal is controlled uniformly as well: \[ \left|\frac{\partial_zA_N(t,c_j)}{A_N(t,c_j)}\right| \le C_rN\quad(j\ {\rm double}). \tag{28} \] For completeness, the logarithmic derivative \(L_j=tB_j'/B_j\) is bounded by \(C_r m_j\). Taking instead the complementary factors in the full length-\(N\) product gives the second bound \[ |L_j|\le C_r(N-m_j)+C_rNr^N. \] The last term comes from the logarithmic derivative of \(\prod_{s=1}^N(1+q^{-1}Q^st)=1+(-1)^Nt^N\). Now \(\min(m_j,N-m_j)=N\min(\theta_j,\pi-\theta_j)/\pi\) and \(\min(\theta_j,\pi-\theta_j)/\sin\theta_j\le\pi/2\). Also \(\sin\theta_j\ge2/N\) at double nodes, while \(Nr^N\) is uniformly bounded. Divide these estimates by \(|v_j-v_j^{-1}|=2\sin\theta_j\) and use (12) to get (28). Combining the original trace with (27)--(28) gives an actual upper bound for the whole tensor-generating polynomial: \[ \boxed{\quad |\mathscr C_N(t_1,t_2,t_3)| \le C_rN^{1/2} \exp\!\left\{N\max_{0\le j\le\lfloor d/2\rfloor} \operatorname{Re}\sum_{\ell=1}^3 \mathcal S(v_j,t_\ell)\right\}, \qquad |t_\ell|\le r. \quad} \tag{29} \] Indeed each double-node summand of (21) has modulus at most \(C_rN\prod_\ell|A_N(t_\ell,c_j)|\): in (16), the crossing normal contributes \((4-c_j^2)3|R'/R|=3m_j\sin\theta_j\le3N\), the other three normals are bounded by (28), and \(|c_j|\le2\). The simple-node term obeys the same safe bound. There are at most \(N\) nodes and the prefactor is \(N^{-3/2}\), proving (29). All constants depend only on the fixed disc radius. The estimate is uniform on fixed complex discs inside the unit disc. It does not assert a bound as \(r\) tends to one, a lower bound on an individual coefficient, or an identification of its variational exponent with a geometric filling action. ## 8. Scope and complete sources The three-index Fourier calculation has been replaced by one physical node sum of closed products and their specified polynomial derivatives. There is no unknown source coefficient in (22). This is not a low-rank replacement of the \(N\)-dimensional boundary algebra; the generating polynomial still contains all \(N^3\) tensor coefficients. The original turns, bilinear gluing and marked closure remain those of the centered compiler. No positive measure is assigned to the Gaussian-weighted node sum. No individual-entry asymptotic, geometric norm, source-cycle estimate, or new volume-conjecture class is inferred. The valid complex bound (29) takes absolute values of the node terms and is not claimed to retain their cancellations or be sharp. All derivatives here are the original spectral Hermite normals; no moving-\(q\) or peripheral-normal extension is asserted. The two complete matching proof sources are: | Source | SHA-256 | |---|---| | [Centered Fourier compiler, 405 lines](research_centered_fourier_conway_compiler.md) | 0edbabe42280d70e4d5dcbcb55b188a3e773c14b99fbd212eb0fe8c5b176a413 | | [Original Hermite phase transport and trace, 293 lines](research_bergman_jet_quotient_phase_transport.md) | 0985159d134d82a404bd07973cf5ee55eb78c115e154465cbeac1b201c1c2686 | The finite forcing, cyclic equation, value product, spectral normal, generating formula and fixed-disc bound are proved above. No generic-parameter orthogonality measure, infinite product, or hypergeometric summation theorem is imported. For coverage, the generic Al-Salam--Chihara generating function is standard: see Dennis Stanton, [Generating functions and orthogonality (2022), equation (2.1)](https://www-users.cse.umn.edu/~stant001/PAPERS/Dick-gf2022.pdf). The compiler's normalization is \(p_a(z)=(-1)^a Q_a(z/2;q^{-1},q^{-1}\mid h)/(h;h)_a\), so the usual generic series uses the variable \(-t\). This reference is coverage of that generic generating function only. No infinite product at a root of unity or external orthogonality argument is used for the finite forced equation or its full-normal source formulas. Earlier finals and public manuscripts remain unchanged.

title: A uniform representation-volume gap along centered long cone paths
text:
# A uniform representation-volume gap along centered long cone paths Research note, 18 November 2026. For a fixed complete hyperbolic core, sufficiently long primitive filling equations remain in one complete-holonomy chart throughout the cone-angle cube. Near-maximal representation rigidity then gives a uniform volume gap to every other representation satisfying the same centered equations. The comparison is along the whole path, rather than only at its endpoints. The conclusion concerns marked representations and their volumes. It neither compares different logarithmic lifts of the same representation nor transports the original quantum cycle. ## 1. Complete proof sources and the comparison data The only proof sources are: * **N**, [A uniform volume gap away from geometric holonomy]( https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_near_maximal_representation_volume.md), complete text. Its Theorem 1 and Corollary 2 give a fixed positive volume deficit outside any conjugacy-invariant neighborhood of the oriented complete holonomy. Its Sections 5--6 explain why every nearby peripheral decoration lies in the supplied positive gluing chart. * **F**, [A finite positive certificate supplies every sufficiently long filling branch](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/finite_geometric_certificate_uniform_filling_existence.md), complete text. It supplies the actual centered peripheral germ, the uniform contraction for all primitive slope directions, and the absolutely normalized local volume expansion. Let \(M\) be one fixed oriented complete finite-volume hyperbolic three-manifold, with \(c\) torus cusps and volume \(V>0\). Supply the actual positive complete marked triangulation required by these sources. In an application, \(M\) may already be a fixed hyperbolic short partial filling. Its primitive cusp paths and every earlier filling are fixed. On cusp \(i\), choose the positively oriented primitive basis \((\mu_i,\lambda_i)\). In the decorated complete-holonomy chart write \(U_i,V_i\) for the centered logarithms of the projective similarity multipliers. Thus these are twice eigenvalue logarithms; no central \(\mathrm{SL}_2\) sign is inserted in them. Source F proves \[ V_i(U)=U_i	au_i(U),\qquad \Im	au_i(0)>0. 	ag{1} \] All these are the actual peripheral words of \(M\). Choose a subset \(I\) of cusps and primitive slopes \((a_i,b_i)\in\mathbb Z^2\), \(i\in I\). Set \[ \ell_i=(a_i^2+b_i^2)^{1/2},\qquad \ell_{\min}=\min_{i\in I}\ell_i. \] For the empty subset take \(\ell_{\min}=+\infty\); its branch is the complete representation and the same proof below gives the gap in N. Choose signs \(\epsilon_i\in\{1,-1\}\) and real charges \(\lambda=(\lambda_i)_{i\in I}\in[0,1]^I\). The prescribed equations are \[ U_j=0\quad(j
otin I),\qquad a_iU_i+b_iV_i=2\pi i\epsilon_i\lambda_i\quad(i\in I). 	ag{2} \] On the constructed branch the first condition keeps every unfilled physical main cusp complete. At a coordinate \(\lambda_i=0\), equation (1) will also make that selected cusp parabolic on the constructed branch. Here is a precise convention for competitors. Each peripheral group has a retained common fixed flag, and is parabolic, trivial, or fixes both endpoints of an axis individually, as in N. On the selected cusps its multipliers lie in a fixed sufficiently small neighborhood of one; take their single-valued centered logarithms there and impose (2). On all other cusps impose the stated boundary-parabolic condition. These conditions describe actual decorated representations, modulo simultaneous conjugation. They do not allow an arbitrary deck translate of a centered logarithm to be substituted into (2). Only competitors near complete holonomy need these small-multiplier conditions in the proof: all representations outside the fixed neighborhood already satisfy the stronger volume deficit supplied by N. ## 2. The uniform centered branch and its volume There are constants \(L_0,C>0\), depending on the fixed marked certificate, such that, whenever \(\ell_{\min}>L_0\), equation (2) has one solution in a fixed centered chart for every \(\lambda\in[0,1]^I\). Denote its representation by \(ho_{\mathrm g}(\lambda)\). To see the uniformity directly, take the polydisk from F on which \[ \Im	au_i\ge m>0,\qquad |	au_i|\le T,\qquad \sum_j|\partial_j	au_i|\le L. \] With \(c_0=m/\sqrt{1+T^2}\), the real two-column estimate in F gives \[ |a_i+b_i	au_i(U)|\ge c_0\ell_i. 	ag{3} \] Keep unfilled coordinates zero and use the fixed-point map \[ \mathcal T_{\lambda,i}(U)=  rac{2\pi i\epsilon_i\lambda_i}{a_i+b_i	au_i(U)}. 	ag{4} \] Since \(0\le\lambda_i\le1\), exactly the estimates of F give \[ \|\mathcal T_\lambda(U)\|_\infty \le rac{2\pi}{c_0\ell_{\min}},\qquad \|D\mathcal T_\lambda(U)\| \le rac{2\pi L}{c_0^2\ell_{\min}}. 	ag{5} \] One fixed long-slope threshold makes the image lie in the interior half-polydisk and the second bound smaller than \(1/2\). This proves existence and uniqueness throughout the closed charge cube. It also gives invertibility of the normalized filling Jacobian \(I-D\mathcal T_\lambda\), with inverse norm at most two. The branch is holomorphic in a neighborhood of each charge value; uniqueness patches these neighborhoods along the whole cube. Coordinatewise, \[ |U_i|\le rac{2\pi\lambda_i}{c_0\ell_i},\qquad U_i=  rac{2\pi i\epsilon_i\lambda_i}{a_i+b_i	au_i(0)} +O\!\left( rac{\lambda_i}{\ell_i\ell_{\min}}ight). 	ag{6} \] The constants do not depend on signs, directions, relative slope lengths, or charges. If \(\lambda_i=0\), (4) gives \(U_i=V_i=0\) exactly. Such a cusp remains nontrivial parabolic in the fixed chart. The absolutely normalized volume expansion proved in F is \[ \operatorname{Vol}(ho_U) =V- rac14\sum_i\Im	au_i(0)|U_i|^2 +O\!\left(\|U\|_\infty\sum_i|U_i|^2ight). 	ag{7} \] Substitution of (6) gives, uniformly on the entire charge cube, \[ \operatorname{Vol}(ho_{\mathrm g}(\lambda)) =V-\pi^2\sum_{i\in I}  rac{\Im	au_i(0)\lambda_i^2} {|a_i+b_i	au_i(0)|^2} +O\!\left(\ell_{\min}^{-1} \sum_{i\in I} rac{\lambda_i^2}{\ell_i^2}ight). 	ag{8} \] In particular its volume loss is at most \(C\sum_i\ell_i^{-2}\). At unit charges, F identifies this branch with the actual smooth hyperbolic filling. At intermediate charges the argument here constructs the actual representation path. If an actual cone deformation with these centered periods is supplied in the chart, uniqueness identifies its holonomy with this path. No separate metric-existence assertion at every intermediate angle is needed for the volume comparison. ## 3. Uniform dominance over centered competitors **Theorem.** There are \(L_*\) and \(g>0\), depending only on the fixed marked core and certificate, such that for every subset \(I\), every independently signed primitive slope tuple with \(\ell_{\min}>L_*\), and every \(\lambda\in[0,1]^I\), each competitor specified in Section 1 obeys \[ ho
ot\simho_{\mathrm g}(\lambda) \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \operatorname{Vol}(ho) \le\operatorname{Vol}(ho_{\mathrm g}(\lambda))-g . 	ag{9} \] The relation \(\sim\) is conjugacy of the underlying projective representation. The assertion is signed, with the chosen orientation. It does not separate central lifts or source decorations of one underlying representation. **Proof.** First choose a sufficiently small representation neighborhood of the oriented complete holonomy, before choosing the slopes. At each cusp retain a primitive element with nonidentity parabolic complete image. Its nearby images remain nonidentity. Every fixed flag of these nearby matrices lies near the unique complete flag: otherwise a convergent subsequence of flags in \(\mathbb{CP}^1\) would produce a second fixed flag of the nonidentity parabolic. As explained in N, Sections 5--6, developing the supplied triangulation from any such peripheral flags therefore gives positive shapes in its fixed gluing chart. The normalized decorated representation and gluing constructions are inverse there. Shrink this representation neighborhood so every centered peripheral vector lies in the contraction polydisk of Section 2. Its conjugacy saturation \(\mathcal U\) is open. Consequently any competitor in \(\mathcal U\), with any retained flags, satisfying the centered equations (2), is the unique fixed point (4). It is conjugate to \(ho_{\mathrm g}(\lambda)\). This uses centered similarity logs of all the actual selected primitive words, rather than traces or exponential filling equations alone. N, Corollary 2, now gives a fixed \(\delta>0\) such that every admitted representation outside \(\mathcal U\) satisfies \[ \operatorname{Vol}(ho)\le V-\delta. 	ag{10} \] This estimate requires no bound on shape coordinates, chosen conjugations, or peripheral translation lengths. Increase the slope threshold until (8) gives \[ \operatorname{Vol}(ho_{\mathrm g}(\lambda))>V-\delta/2 	ag{11} \] for all charges, subsets and directions under consideration. There are only finitely many cusps and subsets, so the same threshold works for all of them. Every nonconjugate competitor lies outside \(\mathcal U\); (10)--(11) prove (9) with \(g=\delta/2\). \(\square\) In particular (9) holds along every path in the charge cube, including the straight cone path \(\lambda_i=t\), \(0\le t\le1\). For a fixed hyperbolic short partial filling, the constants depend on that entire short-filled core. There is no uniformity assertion over varying short cores. ## 4. Exact volume ordering on the larger centered charge box There is also an exact comparison of different nearby real charges. It does not require that their magnitudes be at most one. Choose a sufficiently small fixed \(ho_*>0\). The same fixed-point map, with numerator \(2\pi iq_i\), is a contraction for every \[ q\in\mathbb R^I,\qquad |q_i|\leho_*\ell_i. 	ag{12} \] Indeed its image norm is at most \(2\piho_*/c_0\), and its derivative norm is at most \(2\pi Lho_*/c_0^2\). Choose \(ho_*\) so these are within the fixed chart and below the contraction threshold. Write \(\mathcal V(q)\) for the volume of the resulting representation. Choose an integral complementary primitive curve on each selected cusp: \[ a_i d_i-b_i c_i=1,\qquad s_i=a_iU_i+b_iV_i=2\pi iq_i,\qquad W_i=c_iU_i+d_iV_i. 	ag{13} \] The exact volume differential F(10) is invariant under this determinant-one change of peripheral basis. Along the real charge box it therefore gives \[ d\mathcal V = rac12\sum_i [\Re W_i\,d\Im s_i-\Re s_i\,d\Im W_i] =\pi\sum_i\Re W_i\,dq_i. 	ag{14} \] Unfilled terms vanish since their \(U_i,V_i\) are identically zero. By (1), (3) and (13), \[ W_i=2\pi iq_i  rac{c_i+d_i	au_i(U)}{a_i+b_i	au_i(U)},\qquad \Re W_i= - rac{2\pi q_i\Im	au_i(U)} {|a_i+b_i	au_i(U)|^2}. 	ag{15} \] Here the last identity uses \(\Im[(c+d	au)/(a+b	au)]=\Im	au/|a+b	au|^2\); the determinant in (13) fixes its sign. Consequently \[  rac{\partial\mathcal V}{\partial q_i} =- rac{2\pi^2q_i\Im	au_i(U(q))} {|a_i+b_i	au_i(U(q))|^2}. 	ag{16} \] This is exact, including all coupling between cusps. There is no uncontrolled derivative of the remainder in (8). The volume is unchanged by independently reversing the sign of any \(q_i\). For \(q_i
e0\), change only that cusp's retained common eigenflag to the other fixed flag of the same representation. This negates \(U_i,V_i\) and keeps all other cusp logs unchanged. The nearby-flags argument in Section 3 puts this decoration in the same positive chart. Its centered charge is the sign-reversed tuple, so uniqueness identifies it with that tuple's constructed representation. The underlying representation has not changed. At \(q_i=0\) the assertion follows directly, or by continuity. Thus \(\mathcal V(q)\) is a function of the coordinatewise absolute charges and is strictly decreasing in each \(q_i^2\) on (12). More quantitatively, if \(q,\widetilde q\) lie in that box and \(|q_i|\ge|\widetilde q_i|\) for every \(i\), integration of (16) one coordinate at a time gives \[ \mathcal V(\widetilde q)-\mathcal V(q) \ge c_1\sum_i rac{q_i^2-\widetilde q_i^2}{\ell_i^2}, \qquad c_1= rac{\pi^2m}{1+T^2}>0. 	ag{17} \] We used \(|a_i+b_i	au_i|^2\le(1+T^2)\ell_i^2\). Equality of all absolute charges gives the same underlying representation by the flag argument. This box includes every sufficiently near-complete representation whose centered primitive slope logs are purely imaginary. In fact \[  rac{|q_i|}{\ell_i} \le rac{\sqrt{1+T^2}}{2\pi}|U_i|. 	ag{18} \] Shrink the representation neighborhood in Section 3 so the right side is below \(ho_*\). This shrink is independent of the slopes. Representations outside it still have the fixed gap from N. At unit charge, (17) compares every nonzero centered integer-charge tuple \(q\in(\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\})^I\) in the neighborhood with the tuple of unit absolute charges. If some \(|q_i|\ge2\), its volume deficit is at least \(3c_1/\ell_{\max}^2\), where \(\ell_{\max}=\max_{i\in I}\ell_i\). All tuples with \(|q_i|=1\) give the same underlying representation. Outside the neighborhood, combine N with (11). Thus the geometric comparison over all such nonzero integer charges has a positive gap for each fixed long slope tuple: \[ g_\sigma=\min\{\delta/2,\,3c_1/\ell_{\max}^2\}. 	ag{19} \] This statement assumes that the centered primitive charges are those integers; it does not infer this from an exponentiated filling equation. More generally, if \(q_i=\lambda_i n_i\) with nonzero integers \(n_i\) and \(\lambda_i\in[\lambda_0,1]\), \(\lambda_0>0\), the same argument gives a gap \(\min\{\delta/2,3c_1\lambda_0^2/\ell_{\max}^2\}\) to every different underlying representation. This is a geometric statement for that specified charge family, not an assertion that a deformation of the original quantum kernel has been constructed. For other charge families, the comparison across different classes need not give a fixed positive gap up to every endpoint. For example, \((\lambda-2)^2-\lambda^2=4(1-\lambda)\) tends to zero as \(\lambda\uparrow1\); the two minimal signs then represent the same underlying representation. Their source coefficients still need to be combined with their actual signs and peripheral factors. ## 5. Why exponentiated projective data alone are insufficient The same actual gluing germ shows why exponentiated slope equations would be insufficient. Fill just one cusp, and fix \(1/2<\lambda<1\). Formula (4) also defines the nearby actual representation for the bounded signed charge \(\lambda-1\). The two branches have the same exponentiated projective slope multiplier: \[ e^{2\pi i\lambda}=e^{2\pi i(\lambda-1)}. 	ag{20} \] Nevertheless their volumes, by the same uniform expansion (8), satisfy \[ \operatorname{Vol}(ho_{\lambda-1}) -\operatorname{Vol}(ho_\lambda) = rac{\pi^2\Im	au(0)(2\lambda-1)} {|a+b	au(0)|^2}+O(\ell^{-3})>0 	ag{21} \] for all sufficiently long slopes. The last inequality follows from \(|a+b	au(0)|\le C\ell\) and \(\Im	au(0)>0\). These are actual representations of the same fixed core, constructed by its supplied positive germ. Equation (21) makes no assertion that the second branch occurs in the original quantum cycle. The two charges in (20) differ by an odd integer: the unsquared \(\mathrm{SL}_2\) slope multiplier changes sign. Thus this comparison does not apply to a source that separately fixes that sign. In the latter case the possible charge shifts are even, and the geometric comparison in Section 4 is the relevant one. Determining the actual congruence class, including integer-spin channels and Weyl factors, is a literal source calculation, not a consequence of projective volume rigidity. Thus near-maximal rigidity does not select a logarithmic sheet. Even within the complete neighborhood, the full source equations must be matched to the centered primitive equations before (9) applies. Representations outside that neighborhood already satisfy (10). ## 6. The remaining source question This assembly replaces an arbitrary-cone maximality premise by a proved geometric comparison for sufficiently long centered fillings of a fixed core. It supplies a gap throughout the deformation and local isolation of the marked representation branch. It does not identify every original critical action with that volume, eliminate equal-action decorations, or prove a quantum Hessian nondegenerate from the representation Jacobian. In particular, an initially nonzero thimble coefficient is not transported by this note. Applying (9) to that question still requires the actual centered source marking and action normalization, the original relative cycle with both endpoint currents, and control or exact cancellation of source divisors and ends. Compactness of near-maximal representations does not imply compactness of their highest-cut source coordinates. ## Frozen proof-source pins * N: `research_near_maximal_representation_volume.md`, SHA256 `9ff00d61704e2fc7a13e8abb5cbd37d61d3413220bcc4e6f763609a48177f997`. * F: `finite_geometric_certificate_uniform_filling_existence.md`, SHA256 `f3f78212e1f42f501593412a71c21590f24f8838f4add8abeb2f12534ad2b39b`.

title: Two contributions to the original source near the real cube
text:
# Two contributions to the original source near the real cube 21 November 2026. Research note. Earlier finals and public manuscripts remain unchanged. The real three-boundary source has two different continuations in its asymptotic expansion. The initialized interior saddle contributes the known dilogarithmic exponential. The ends of the full Fourier contour, after all Fourier charges have been summed, contribute a nonzero term of order \(N^{-3/2}\). Its exponential phase is constant. Both contributions can be estimated on a fixed complex neighborhood of each compact real cube. This proves a nonzero saddle coefficient on one side of the real cube and identifies the endpoint contribution that prevents a single saddle formula on a whole neighborhood. No assertion places an arbitrary short-filled component in this neighborhood. ## 1. The original source and the connection estimate Fix \[ N\ge2,\quad d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad \eta=(-1)^d,\quad \kappa=q^{d^2/2},\quad D_N(t)=1-\eta t^N . 	ag{1} \] As in the complete generating-section and initialized-source theorems, \[ \mathcal C_N(\mathbf t)= N^{-3/2}\phi\!\left(R^3 \prod_{
u=1}^3G_N(t_
u;z)ight). 	ag{2} \] Here \(\phi\) is the original Frobenius closing on \(\mathbb C[z]/(2T_N(z/2)+2)\). All double-root derivatives are retained; \(T_N(\cos	heta)=\cos(N	heta)\). The polynomial \(G_N\) and the positive crossing \(R\) are the actual finite packets, with the original normalization. Use the holomorphic functions on the unit polydisk \[  egin{aligned} \Psi(\mathbf t)&=- rac{\pi}{12} + rac1{2\pi}\left[ \sum_
u\operatorname{Li}_2(-t_
u) +\operatorname{Li}_2(-t_1t_2t_3) -\sum_{\mu<
u}\operatorname{Li}_2(t_\mu t_
u)ight],\ B(\mathbf t)&=\prod_{\mu<
u}(1-t_\mu t_
u)^{-1/2}, \qquad A_0(\mathbf t)=\prod_
u(1+t_
u)^{-1}. \end{aligned} 	ag{3} \] The power-series branches at zero specify all these functions; the square roots are positive on the real cube. Set \[ \Delta_N(\mathbf t)=\prod_
u D_N(t_
u),\qquad L_N=(-1)^N\kappa^3e^{-3\pi i/(4N)} . 	ag{4} \] **Theorem.** For every \(0<ho<1\), there is a fixed open complex neighborhood \(V_ho\) of \([-ho,ho]^3\), with closure in the unit polydisk, such that \[  oxed{\quad  rac{\mathcal C_N(\mathbf t)}{L_N\Delta_N(\mathbf t)} =e^{i\pi/4}B(\mathbf t)e^{iN\Psi(\mathbf t)} +N^{-3/2}A_0(\mathbf t)+\mathcal R_N(\mathbf t), \quad} 	ag{5} \] where, uniformly on \(V_ho\), \[ |\mathcal R_N(\mathbf t)| \le C_ho\left[ N^{-1}e^{-N\operatorname{Im}\Psi(\mathbf t)} +N^{-5/2}ight]. 	ag{6} \] The neighborhood and constant are independent of \(N\). The estimate holds along the full sequence, including both parities. In particular, uniformly where \(\operatorname{Im}\Psi\le0\) in this neighborhood, \[ \mathcal C_N= L_N\Delta_Ne^{i\pi/4}B e^{iN\Psi}(1+O_ho(N^{-1})). 	ag{7} \] This source is nonzero there for all sufficiently large \(N\). For each fixed \(\epsilon>0\), uniformly where \(\operatorname{Im}\Psi\ge\epsilon\), \[ \mathcal C_N= L_N\Delta_NN^{-3/2}A_0(1+O_{ho,\epsilon}(N^{-1})). 	ag{8} \] These are statements about the complete original source, rather than an absolute-value envelope. ## 2. Analytic interpolation on a complex angular strip The real-source proof used the explicit analytic section \[ U_N(t,z)=\exp\left\{\sum_{n=1}^{N-1}  rac{(-1)^{n+1}(2T_n(z/2)-2q^{-n})} {n(e^{-2\pi in/N}-1)}\,t^night\}. 	ag{9} \] It agrees with the actual \(G_N\), with exponentially small relative error, at every physical value and first Casimir normal. Write \[  egin{aligned} \Phi(t,2\cos	heta)&=  rac{\operatorname{Li}_2(-te^{i	heta}) +\operatorname{Li}_2(-te^{-i	heta}) -2\operatorname{Li}_2(-t)}{2\pi i},\ A(t,	heta)&=(1+2t\cos	heta+t^2)^{-1/2}. \end{aligned} 	ag{10} \] Choose \(ho<ho_1<1\) and a small \(b>0\) with \(ho_1e^{2b}<1\). On \(|t|\leho_1\) and \(|\operatorname{Im}	heta|\le2b\), the power-series logarithms in (9)--(10) give \[ \log U_N(t,2\cos	heta) =N\Phi(t,2\cos	heta)+\log A(t,	heta)+O(N^{-1}), 	ag{11} \] uniformly with every fixed number of angular derivatives. Here and below one may reduce the strip slightly before taking derivatives. For completeness, expand \[ (e^{-2\pi in/N}-1)^{-1} =- rac{N}{2\pi in}- rac12+O(n/N) \qquad(n\le N/2). 	ag{12} \] After substituting \(q^{-n}=e^{-\pi in/N}\), the two main series in (9) are precisely \(N\Phi\) and \(\log A\). A fixed angular derivative introduces at most a power of \(n\) and the factor \(e^{2bn}\). Thus the low-frequency errors sum to \(O(N^{-1})\). For \(N/2<n<N\), use \[ |e^{-2\pi in/N}-1|\ge c(N-n)/N . 	ag{13} \] The remaining tails are bounded by a polynomial in \(N\) times \((ho_1e^{2b})^{N/2}\). This proves (11) on the stated complex strip, without assuming continuation of a real asymptotic. Define the phase and amplitude \[  egin{aligned} \sigma(	heta,\mathbf t)&=  rac{3(	heta-\pi)^2}{4\pi} + rac1i\sum_
u\Phi(t_
u,2\cos	heta),\ A_N(	heta,\mathbf t)&= \prod_
u U_N(t_
u,2\cos	heta) e^{-N\sum_
u\Phi(t_
u,2\cos	heta)},\ a_N(	heta,\mathbf t)&=\sin	heta\,A_N(	heta,\mathbf t). \end{aligned} 	ag{14} \] They are holomorphic on a common strip and parameter neighborhood. Equation (11) gives \[ A_N=A_*+O(N^{-1}),\qquad A_*=\prod_
u(1+2t_
u\cos	heta+t_
u^2)^{-1/2}, 	ag{15} \] in every fixed angular \(C^k\) norm there. In particular these analytic amplitudes and their required derivatives are uniformly bounded. Several endpoint identities are exact for complex \(\mathbf t\): \[  egin{gathered} \sigma(0)=\sigma(2\pi)=3\pi/4,\qquad \sigma'(0)=-3/2,\quad \sigma'(2\pi)=3/2,\ a_N(0)=a_N(2\pi)=0,\qquad a_N'(0)=a_N'(2\pi)=A_N(0),\ A_N(0)=A_0(\mathbf t)+O(N^{-1}). \end{gathered} 	ag{16} \] They follow from \(\Phi(t,2)=0\), its dependence on \(\cos	heta\), and (15). Reflection about \(\pi\) fixes \(\sigma,A_N\) and negates \(a_N\). ## 3. The exact source-weighted Fourier formula Put \(	heta_j=(2j+1)\pi/N\), \(c_j=2\cos	heta_j\), and \(\chi_N=q^{d^2/4}\). The calibrated physical interpolation in the real-source theorem is \[ R(c_j)=\chi_Ne^{iN(	heta_j-\pi)^2/(4\pi)},\qquad \phi(f)=(-1)^N\sum_{j=0}^{N-1} \left.\partial_	heta \{\sin	heta\,f(2\cos	heta)\}ight|_{	heta_j}. 	ag{17} \] Its crossing derivative matches at every double node. The odd simple node uses its value alone. These statements do not replace the canonical crossing polynomial between the nodes. The physical Hermite estimate for (9) remains exponentially accurate on a sufficiently small complex neighborhood of the real cube. Indeed at the real cube \(\Phi\) is purely imaginary; at complex distance \(\delta\), its real part at physical angles is \(O_ho(\delta)\). Values of \(U_N\) are consequently bounded by \(C_ho e^{C_ho\delta N}\), with first normals bounded by the same factor times a fixed power of \(N\). The full physical relative error is \(O_ho(N^2ho_1^N)\). Choose \(\delta\) so small that \(e^{C_ho\delta}ho_1<1\). The paired source formula (17) then bounds the total replacement error by \(O(e^{-cN})\), after absorbing its polynomial factors. The same argument applies to \(G_N/D_N\), since \(D_N=1+O(ho_1^N)\). Thus, on a fixed smaller neighborhood, \[  rac{\mathcal C_N}{\Delta_N} =(-1)^N\chi_N^3N^{-3/2} \sum_j\left.\partial_	heta \{a_N(	heta)e^{iN\sigma(	heta)}\}ight|_{	heta_j} +O(e^{-cN}). 	ag{18} \] This error is absolute. In particular it is not measured relative to a possibly decaying saddle. The periodic extension of \(\partial_	heta(a_Ne^{iN\sigma})\) is continuous at the seam and piecewise smooth, by (16). Its Fourier coefficients are absolutely summable for each fixed \(N\). Midpoint sampling and one integration by parts therefore give the exact identity \[ \sum_j\left.\partial_	heta \{a_Ne^{iN\sigma}\}ight|_{	heta_j} = rac{iN^2}{2\pi} \sum_{\ell
e0}(-1)^\ell\ell I_{\ell,N},\qquad I_{\ell,N}=\int_0^{2\pi} a_N(	heta)e^{iN(\sigma(	heta)-\ell	heta)}\,d	heta. 	ag{19} \] The zero charge vanishes exactly. No endpoint or physical normal has been removed. Reflection also gives \[ I_{-\ell,N}=-I_{\ell,N} 	ag{20} \] for complex parameters, with no complex conjugation. ## 4. Nonstationary charges with their endpoint coefficient For real parameters the phase derivative \(\sigma'\) increases from \(-3/2\) to \(3/2\), and its derivative is bounded above and below by positive constants on the compact cube. All its fixed derivatives are uniformly bounded. For \(|\ell|\ge2\) write \[ \varphi_\ell=\sigma-\ell	heta,\qquad v_\ell=\varphi_\ell' . 	ag{21} \] The derivative has no zero on the real interval. This persists on a sufficiently thin complex strip and parameter neighborhood. There is a uniform contour on which \(\varphi_\ell\) is real. Fix a real base parameter in the compact cube and solve \[ \varphi_{\ell,\mathbf t}(	heta) =\varphi_{\ell,\mathrm{base}}(r), \qquad 0\le r\le2\pi . 	ag{22} \] At the base this is \(	heta=r\). The analytic implicit function theorem continues the solution uniformly, with displacement \(O(\delta/(|\ell|-3/2))\). One can see uniform uniqueness by integrating the bound \(|\sigma'|\le3/2+o(1)<2\) on a convex thin rectangle: the linear term \(-\ell	heta\) dominates its difference. The endpoint phase values are fixed by (16), so the contour's endpoints are still exactly \(0,2\pi\). This contour is homotopic to the original interval in the analytic strip. Local parameter neighborhoods obtained this way cover the compact real cube; finitely many suffice, giving uniform constants. On (22) the exponential has modulus one. Integrating by parts three times, using \(\partial_	heta e^{iN\varphi_\ell} =iNv_\ell e^{iN\varphi_\ell}\), proves \[ I_{\ell,N}=  rac{A_N(0)e^{3\pi iN/4}}{N^2} \left\{(3/2-\ell)^{-2}-(-3/2-\ell)^{-2}ight\} +O(N^{-3}|\ell|^{-3}) \quad(|\ell|\ge2). 	ag{23} \] For the sign, the first boundary term vanishes since \(a_N=0\); the second is \(N^{-2}[a_N'e^{iN\varphi_\ell}/v_\ell^2]_0^{2\pi}\). Both endpoint exponentials equal \(e^{3\pi iN/4}\). The next boundary term and remaining integral have the bound in (23). Every inverse phase derivative costs at least \(O(|\ell|^{-1})\); the uniform strip bounds control its derivatives and the contour lengths. Thus \[ \sum_{|\ell|\ge2}|\ell|\, \left|I_{\ell,N}-  rac{A_N(0)e^{3\pi iN/4}}{N^2} \{(3/2-\ell)^{-2}-(-3/2-\ell)^{-2}\}ight| \le CN^{-3}. 	ag{24} \] This is an absolute complex estimate. It does not bound a complex oscillatory integral by its real-parameter modulus. ## 5. The unit charges: a saddle and two endpoint rays It suffices to treat \(\ell=1\), by (20). At real parameters, \(\varphi_1\) is strictly convex and has one nondegenerate critical point in \((0,2\pi)\), uniformly separated from the endpoints. Let \(	heta_c(\mathbf t)\) be its analytic continuation and \(\alpha(\mathbf t)=\varphi_1(	heta_c,\mathbf t)\). It exists on a fixed complex neighborhood. Its imaginary part can be made uniformly small there. Here is the contour construction that separates its saddle from its endpoints. At a real base define \[ y(	heta)=\operatorname{sgn}(	heta-	heta_c) \sqrt{2(\varphi_1(	heta)-\alpha)} . 	ag{25} \] The quotient \(2(\varphi_1-\alpha)/(	heta-	heta_c)^2\) is positive on the whole real interval, including its removable value at the critical point. Its analytic square root therefore extends to a thin common neighborhood of that interval. Moreover \(y'\) is positive there on the real interval. It follows that \(y\) has a univalent holomorphic extension on a smaller neighborhood: local invertibility is uniform by compactness, while injectivity away from the diagonal persists from strict real monotonicity. These properties persist for nearby complex parameters. In this coordinate the phase is exactly \[ \varphi_1=\alpha+y^2/2. 	ag{26} \] The endpoint phases are the fixed real numbers \( eta_-=3\pi/4\), \( eta_+=-5\pi/4\). Their differences from the real critical value are uniformly positive. Choose a small fixed \(h>0\) and then make the parameter neighborhood small enough that \(|\operatorname{Im}\alpha|<h/4\). On each inverse branch of (26), replace the original path in the phase plane by \[ \alpha\longrightarrow\alpha+ih \longrightarrow eta_\pm+ih \longrightarrow eta_\pm , 	ag{27} \] with the orientation reversed on the left branch. The inverse is the positive or negative square root in (26). For \(h\) small these paths lie in the analytic \(y\)-domain: near the critical point their distance is \(O(\sqrt h)\); away from it the inverse is uniformly regular. Their connectors have imaginary phase at least \(3h/4\), and hence exponentially small absolute integrals. This explicitly justifies the deformation, including when the critical phase has either sign. To evaluate the critical rays, write \(b_N(y)=a_N(	heta(y))\,d	heta/dy\). On \(y=\pm e^{i\pi/4}\sqrt{2s}\), the two rays combine to \[  rac{e^{iN\alpha+i\pi/4}}{\sqrt2} \int_0^h \{b_N(e^{i\pi/4}\sqrt{2s}) +b_N(-e^{i\pi/4}\sqrt{2s})\} s^{-1/2}e^{-Ns}\,ds . 	ag{28} \] The brace is \(2b_N(0)+O(s)\), with uniform analytic bounds. The elementary gamma integral consequently gives \[ e^{iN\alpha+i\pi/4} \sqrt{2\pi/N}\,  rac{a_N(	heta_c)}{\sqrt{\sigma''(	heta_c)}} +O(N^{-3/2}e^{-N\operatorname{Im}\alpha}) +O(e^{-cN}). 	ag{29} \] The square root is fixed by its positive real value. The truncated gamma tail is exponentially small because of the choice \(|\operatorname{Im}\alpha|<h/4\). On an endpoint ray use the local phase coordinate \(v=\varphi_1\). Its amplitude is \(a_N(	heta(v))/v_1(	heta(v))\), which vanishes at the endpoint. Its first derivative there is \(a_N'/v_1^2\). Expanding this analytic amplitude on the vertical ray and using \(\int_0^h se^{-Ns}\,ds=N^{-2}+O(e^{-cN})\) gives precisely the endpoint term in (23) with \(\ell=1\), now with error \(O(N^{-3})\). We have therefore proved the uniform complex expansion \[  egin{aligned} I_{1,N}={}& e^{iN\alpha+i\pi/4}\sqrt{2\pi/N}\,  rac{a_N(	heta_c)}{\sqrt{\sigma''(	heta_c)}}\ &+ rac{A_N(0)e^{3\pi iN/4}}{N^2} \{(3/2-1)^{-2}-(-3/2-1)^{-2}\}\ &+O\!\left(N^{-3/2}e^{-N\operatorname{Im}\alpha} +N^{-3}+e^{-cN}ight). \end{aligned} 	ag{30} \] The reflected charge has the opposite integral, so the source weights in (19) make the saddle contributions add. ## 6. Summing the endpoints and restoring the original phases Unlike a bound on the nonunit charges alone, (23) and (30) identify the same endpoint coefficient for every charge. Their source-weighted sum is absolutely convergent: \[ S(a)=\sum_{\ell\in\mathbb Z}(-1)^\ell\ell \{(a-\ell)^{-2}-(-a-\ell)^{-2}\},\qquad a=3/2. 	ag{31} \] The combined summand is \(O(|\ell|^{-2})\). The elementary partial-fraction identity \[ \sum_{\ell\in\mathbb Z} rac{(-1)^\ell}{\ell-a} =-\pi\csc(\pi a) 	ag{32} \] uses symmetric limits. It follows, for example, by integrating \(\pi\csc(\pi z)/(z-a)\) on rectangles with vertical sides at half-integers and horizontal sides tending to imaginary infinity; the boundary integral tends to zero, and the displayed residues give (32). Differentiation is absolutely convergent. Changing \(\ell\) to \(-\ell\) in one half of (31) yields \[ S(a)=-2\pi\csc(\pi a) +2a\pi^2\csc(\pi a)\cot(\pi a),\qquad S(3/2)=2\pi. 	ag{33} \] Thus the endpoint term does not vanish after the actual source has summed all Fourier charges. Inserting it into (18)--(19) gives \[ (-1)^N i\chi_N^3e^{3\pi iN/4} \Delta_N N^{-3/2}A_N(0). 	ag{34} \] The exact identity \[ i\chi_N^3e^{3\pi iN/4} =\kappa^3e^{-3\pi i/(4N)} 	ag{35} \] turns (34) into \(L_N\Delta_NN^{-3/2}A_N(0)\), with a positive coefficient \(+1\). Equation (16) replaces \(A_N(0)\) by \(A_0\) with error \(O(N^{-5/2})\) after normalization. The remainders in (24) and (30) have the same order after multiplication by the source factor \(N^{1/2}\). For the saddle, the identities established on the real cube continue holomorphically to this neighborhood: \[  egin{gathered} 	heta_c=2\pi-	heta_*,\qquad 2\cos	heta_*=1- rac{t_1+t_2+t_3+ t_1t_2+t_1t_3+t_2t_3}{1+t_1t_2t_3},\ \alpha=\Psi+3\pi/4-2\pi,\qquad  rac{2\sin	heta_*\,A_*(	heta_*)} {\sqrt{\,2\pi\sigma''(	heta_*)\,}}=B . \end{gathered} 	ag{36} \] The analytic critical branch and square roots are fixed at the real cube; its critical points remain distinct from the endpoints. The real action and amplitude identities imply (36) in the complex neighborhood by the identity theorem in each variable. Replacing \(A_N\) by \(A_*\) in (29) costs \(O(N^{-1}|e^{iN\Psi}|)\) after source normalization. Equations (19)--(20), (29), and (35)--(36) then give the first term of (5), with its displayed coefficient. The remaining absolute exponential errors can be absorbed in \(O(N^{-5/2})\). This proves (5)--(6). Because \(A_0\) and \(B\) are uniformly bounded above and away from zero after shrinking the neighborhood, (7)--(8) follow. ## 7. Why a whole-neighborhood single saddle formula fails The endpoint branch is visible immediately on one side of every real point. To verify that the two sides really occur, at a real point write \[ z_*=2\cos	heta_*\in(-2,2),\qquad b_i=1+t_i z_*+t_i^2 . 	ag{37} \] The envelope derivative of the initialized action is \[ \partial_{t_i}\Psi=  rac{\log b_i-2\log(1+t_i)}{2\pi t_i}<0. 	ag{38} \] For \(t_i
e0\), its sign follows from \(b_i/(1+t_i)^2=1+t_i(z_*-2)/(1+t_i)^2\). At \(t_i=0\), its continuous value is \((z_*-2)/(2\pi)<0\). Moving a small fixed distance in a negative imaginary coordinate direction therefore gives \(\operatorname{Im}\Psi>0\). At each such fixed point the first term of (5) decays exponentially, whereas the actual source has the nonzero endpoint asymptotic (8). Consequently no fixed complex neighborhood of any real point supports the single-saddle relative formula (7) throughout. On the opposite side, (7) proves that the initialized saddle coefficient is nonzero without assigning it by hand. The connection estimate does not decide cancellation in the shrinking transition region where the two terms have comparable size. It neither asserts zero-freeness on all \(V_ho\) nor extends the result to the whole unit polydisk. No derivative estimate for the relative one-saddle remainder is inferred. ## 8. Scope and complete proof sources This is a fixed-root statement with the actual first Casimir normals, both parities, the odd simple node, and every displayed normalizing factor retained. The endpoint is a contribution to the same initialized source, not a change of closing or a discarded alias. The uniform complex estimate is obtained by explicit contour deformation; it is not inferred from holomorphy of a real asymptotic. The result supplies a source-sensitive complex packet on \(\operatorname{Im}\Psi\le0\) near the real cube and the connection to its endpoint contribution. Establishing the required geometric parameter domain, the assembled coefficient cycle, and a nonzero original coefficient after arbitrary fixed short fillings remains separate. No volume identity is proved here. The additional source-specific statements are the uniform two-contribution estimate, the nonzero fully summed endpoint coefficient, and the resulting complex-side distinction. Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used. No mathematical program, numerical experiment, test, build, git operation or earlier-final edit was performed.

title: One finite hypergeometric sum for the original multiplication tensor
text:
# One finite hypergeometric sum for the original multiplication tensor 21 November 2026. Research note. Earlier finals and public manuscripts remain unchanged. The generating polynomial of the centered Conway multiplication tensor can be recovered from one finite, very-well-poised \({}_6\phi_5\) partial sum. The original Frobenius source is a specified first derivative of that sum at the root. The sum itself vanishes there, so its value cannot replace the derivative. The proof calibrates a generic-node interpolation at both values and first derivatives before taking the limit. It does not use Rogers' infinite summation formula on the unit circle. No geometric noncancellation or volume bound is claimed. ## 1. The original generating polynomial Fix \(N\ge2\), and put \[ d=N-1,\qquad \eta=(-1)^d,\qquad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\quad \kappa=q^{d^2/2},\quad c_j=qQ^j+q^{-1}Q^{-j}. 	ag{1} \] Use the full original algebra \(\mathcal H_N=\mathbb C[z]/P_N(z)\), \(P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2\), its original Frobenius row \(\phi\), and its positive crossing \(R\). Here \(T_N(\cos	heta)=\cos(N	heta)\). The centered compiler supplies the basis \(f_a=N^{-1/2}R\,p_a(z)\), where \(p_0=1\), and \[ \phi(f_af_b)=\delta_{ab},\qquad C_{abc}=\phi(f_af_bf_c),\qquad G_N(t;z)=\sum_{a=0}^dp_a(z)t^a . 	ag{2} \] The three-boundary polynomial of interest is exactly \[ \mathcal C_N(t_1,t_2,t_3) =\sum_{a,b,c=0}^dC_{abc}t_1^at_2^bt_3^c =N^{-3/2}\phi\!\left(R^3\prod_{
u=1}^3G_N(t_
u;z)ight). 	ag{3} \] In particular this uses the original closing, not the bilinear functional \(\phi(R^2\,\cdot)/N\) with its extra \(R\) omitted. Here are the complete physical data used from the generating-section theorem. For \(|t|<1\), set \(D_N(t)=1-\eta t^N\). Then \[ G_N(t;c_j)=D_N(t)  rac{\displaystyle\prod_{\ell=-j+1}^{0} (1+q^{-1}Q^\ell t)} {\displaystyle\prod_{\ell=1}^{j+1} (1+q^{-1}Q^\ell t)} . 	ag{4} \] Empty products equal one. At a double node choose \(0\le j<d/2\), and write \[ s_j=qQ^j-q^{-1}Q^{-j},\qquad F_\ell(t)= rac{q^{-1}Q^\ell t}{1+q^{-1}Q^\ell t}. 	ag{5} \] All \(s_j\) in this range are nonzero. The actual first derivative has the equivalent finite form \[  rac{\partial_zG_N(t;c_j)}{G_N(t;c_j)} = rac1{s_j}\sum_{\ell=j+2}^{N-j}F_\ell(t). 	ag{6} \] For clarity, (6) includes the central correction in the initialized root equation. Indeed its weighted-primitive form is \[  rac1N\sum_{k=0}^d  rac{kQ^{-k}t}{1+c_jQ^{-k}t+Q^{-2k}t^2} - rac{\eta(d-2j)}{s_j} rac{t^N}{D_N(t)} . 	ag{7} \] Partial fractions turn the first term into \[  rac1{Ns_j}\sum_{k=0}^dk \{F_{j+1-k}(t)-F_{-j-k}(t)\}. 	ag{8} \] All indices here are cyclic modulo \(N\). Reindexing gives \[  rac1{s_j}\left\{ \sum_{\ell=j+2}^{N-j}F_\ell - rac{d-2j}{N}\sum_{\ell=1}^{N}F_\ellight\}. 	ag{9} \] The full cyclic sum is \(\sum_{\ell=1}^{N}F_\ell=-\eta Nt^N/D_N(t)\). Thus the last term of (9) cancels the second term of (7), proving (6). Dropping that central term would give the wrong Hermite data. At odd \(N\), the simple node \(-2\) needs only the value in (4). ## 2. Generic finite products recover the whole Hermite class Keep \(N\) fixed and let \(\xi\) vary near \(q\). Write \[ Q_\xi=\xi^2,\quad c_j(\xi)=\xi Q_\xi^j+\xi^{-1}Q_\xi^{-j},\quad \kappa_\xi=\xi^{d^2/2},\quad \omega_j(\xi)=\kappa_\xi(-1)^j\xi^{j(j+1)} . 	ag{10} \] A fixed holomorphic branch of the power defines \(\kappa_\xi\). Introduce the finite products \[ H_j(\xi;t)=  igl[1-(-\xi t)^N igr]\,  rac{\displaystyle\prod_{\ell=-j+1}^{0} (1+\xi^{-1}Q_\xi^\ell t)} {\displaystyle\prod_{\ell=1}^{j+1} (1+\xi^{-1}Q_\xi^\ell t)} . 	ag{11} \] For fixed \(N\), these are holomorphic for \(\xi\) sufficiently near \(q\) and \(t\) in any fixed closed disk inside the unit disk. For generic \(\xi\), interpolate the \(N\) values \(H_j(\xi;t)\) at the distinct nodes \(c_j(\xi)\) by a polynomial \(\widetilde G_\xi(t;z)\) of degree below \(N\). Likewise interpolate \(\omega_j(\xi)\) by \(\widetilde R_\xi(z)\). **Lemma 1.** Both polynomial families extend holomorphically to \(\xi=q\), and \[ \widetilde G_q(t;z)=G_N(t;z),\qquad \widetilde R_q(z)=R(z) \quad\hbox{in }\mathcal H_N . 	ag{12} \] **Proof.** The only coincident nodes at \(q\) are the pairs \(j,k=d-j\). Their differences have nonzero first derivative: with a dot denoting \(\xi\partial_\xi\), \[ \dot c_j(q)-\dot c_k(q)=2Ns_j . 	ag{13} \] The two values in each pair agree at the root. For \(H_j\) this follows from (4); for \(\omega_j\) it follows directly from (10). Thus all corresponding divided differences have removable singularities. Grouping each pair in Lagrange interpolation proves regularity of the coefficients. Equivalently, one may use Newton interpolation with each coalescing pair adjacent: the only vanishing denominator is its simple difference (13). It remains to check which Hermite polynomial these limits give. The common scalar in (11) cancels from a difference of logarithmic derivatives. For \(k=d-j\), the extra numerator indices of \(H_k\) are \(-k+1,\ldots,-j\); adding \(N\) identifies them with the extra denominator indices \(j+2,\ldots,N-j\). Their powers have logarithmic derivatives differing by \(2N\). Consequently \[  rac{\dot H_j(q;t)-\dot H_k(q;t)}{H_j(q;t)} =2N\sum_{\ell=j+2}^{N-j}F_\ell(t). 	ag{14} \] Dividing by (13) gives exactly (6). Together with (4), this proves the first equality in (12), including every double-node derivative. The original crossing has the nodal values \[ R(c_j)=\omega_j(q),\qquad  rac{R'(c_j)}{R(c_j)} = rac{2j-d}{2s_j} 	ag{15} \] at the paired nodes. From (10), \[  rac{\dot\omega_j(q)-\dot\omega_k(q)}{\omega_j(q)} =j(j+1)-k(k+1)=N(2j-d). 	ag{16} \] Equations (13) and (16) reproduce (15). Simple nodes require only their value. Full Hermite uniqueness proves the second equality in (12). \(\square\) These interpolating families are auxiliary. No claim is made that their off-root values equal an independently chosen moving-meridian or generic quantum-group source. Their entire root Hermite limits have been checked, which is what (3) needs. ## 3. A weighted node limit is the original Frobenius source Write \[ [m]_\xi= rac{\xi^m-\xi^{-m}}{\xi-\xi^{-1}},\qquad \mathcal L_\xi(f)=  rac{\eta}{[N]_\xi} \sum_{j=0}^d[2j+1]_\xi f(c_j(\xi)). 	ag{17} \] **Lemma 2.** If the coefficients of a polynomial family \(f_\xi\) are holomorphic near \(q\), then \[ \lim_{\xi	o q}\mathcal L_\xi(f_\xi) =\phi(f_q). 	ag{18} \] Its degree may exceed \(N-1\); the right side uses the original class modulo \(P_N\). **Proof.** In each pair \(j,k=d-j\), the root weights have opposite signs and the root nodes agree. The numerator in (17) therefore vanishes at \(q\). At a possible odd simple node its weight is \([N]_\xi\). Moreover \[ (\xi\partial_\xi)[N]_\xi ig|_{\xi=q} =- rac{2N}{q-q^{-1}} . 	ag{19} \] For a pair with common root \(c\), direct differentiation of the numerator and division by (19) gives \[ (-1)^N\{c f_q(c)+(c^2-4)f_q'(c)\}. 	ag{20} \] Terms differentiating the coefficients of \(f_\xi\) cancel between the opposite root weights. At odd \(N\), the simple node contributes \(f_q(-2)\). Here is an independent check that this is exactly \(\phi\). The leading coefficient of \(e_d\) is \(\eta/N^2\), so (3) of the centered compiler gives \[ \phi(f)= rac{\eta N^2}{2\pi i} \oint_\Gamma rac{f(z)}{P_N(z)}\,dz , 	ag{21} \] where \(\Gamma\) is positively oriented and encircles every root once and no other pole. Polynomial division justifies (21) at every degree. The Chebyshev equation is \[ (4-z^2)P_N''-zP_N'+N^2(P_N-2)=0. 	ag{22} \] At a double root \(c\), it and its derivative give \[ P_N''(c)= rac{2N^2}{4-c^2},\qquad P_N'''(c)= rac{3cP_N''(c)}{4-c^2}. 	ag{23} \] The residue in (21) is therefore (20). At the odd simple root \(P_N'(-2)=N^2\), giving \(f(-2)\). This proves (18). \(\square\) The derivative in this lemma is a calibrated way of taking the confluent source. It is not inferred from the nodal values alone. ## 4. The initialized finite \({}_6\phi_5\) sum For a nonnegative integer \(j\), write \((a;B)_j=\prod_{h=0}^{j-1}(1-aB^h)\). Define the following finite sum, with \(Q_\xi=\xi^2\): \[  egin{aligned} S_N(\xi;\mathbf t)= \sum_{j=0}^d&  rac{1-Q_\xi^{2j+1}}{1-Q_\xi}\,  rac{\prod_{
u=1}^3(-\xi/t_
u;Q_\xi)_j} {\prod_{
u=1}^3(-\xi^3t_
u;Q_\xi)_j} (-\xi t_1t_2t_3)^j . \end{aligned} 	ag{24} \] At zero boundary parameters, use its equivalent regular definition \[ S_N(\xi;\mathbf t)= \sum_{j=0}^d  rac{1-\xi^{4j+2}}{1-\xi^2}\, (-\xi)^j  rac{\displaystyle\prod_{
u=1}^3\prod_{h=0}^{j-1} (t_
u+\xi^{2h+1})} {\displaystyle\prod_{
u=1}^3\prod_{h=0}^{j-1} (1+\xi^{2h+3}t_
u)} . 	ag{25} \] Thus the sum is holomorphic near \(\xi=q\) on every fixed closed unit subdisk in its three boundary variables. It is the first \(N\) terms of the canceled very-well-poised \({}_6\phi_5\) with base \(Q_\xi\), leading parameter \(a=Q_\xi\), square root \(\sqrt a=\xi\), three other parameters \(b_
u=-\xi/t_
u\), and argument \(aQ_\xi/(b_1b_2b_3)=-\xi t_1t_2t_3\). The factors \((a;Q_\xi)_j/(Q_\xi;Q_\xi)_j\) cancel, and the square-root factors give \((1-Q_\xi^{2j+1})/(1-Q_\xi)\). Formula (25), rather than an uncanceled quotient, specifies every endpoint and both parities. For the terminology and standard nonterminating series see [Schlosser (2000), equation (5.2)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0007046). That infinite summation theorem is not used here. Our finite window \(0\le j<N\) is prescribed by the original source, not by an assertion that an infinite series terminates at the root. **Theorem.** For \(|t_
u|<1\), \[  oxed{\quad \mathcal C_N(\mathbf t)=  rac{(-1)^N(q-q^{-1})\kappa^3}{2N^{5/2}} \prod_{
u=1}^3 rac{1-\eta t_
u^N}{1+qt_
u} \left.(\xi\partial_\xi)S_N(\xi;\mathbf t)ight|_{\xi=q}. \quad} 	ag{26} \] In particular all \(C_{abc}\) are recovered by coefficient extraction from one finite sum and this specified derivative. **Proof.** Apply Lemmas 1 and 2 to \(f_\xi=\widetilde R_\xi^3\prod_
u\widetilde G_\xi(t_
u;z)\). This gives \[ \mathcal C_N(\mathbf t) = rac{\eta}{N^{3/2}}\lim_{\xi	o q}  rac1{[N]_\xi}\sum_{j=0}^d [2j+1]_\xi\,\omega_j(\xi)^3 \prod_
u H_j(\xi;t_
u). 	ag{27} \] Every first derivative in this equation has already been calibrated. For generic \(\xi\) the sum in (27) is exactly \[ \kappa_\xi^3 \prod_{
u=1}^3 rac{1-(-\xi t_
u)^N}{1+\xi t_
u} S_N(\xi;\mathbf t). 	ag{28} \] To check it, divide its \(j\)-th term by the common \(j=0\) factor. Use \[ [2j+1]_\xi=Q_\xi^{-j}  rac{1-Q_\xi^{2j+1}}{1-Q_\xi}, \qquad  rac{H_j}{H_0} =(\xi^{-1}t)^jQ_\xi^{-j(j-1)/2}  rac{(-\xi/t;Q_\xi)_j} {(-\xi^3t;Q_\xi)_j}. 	ag{29} \] The remaining crossing factor is \((-1)^jQ_\xi^{3j(j+1)/2}\). Its product with the three factors in (29) and the dimension factor is precisely (24). At \(\xi=q\), the \(j\) and \(d-j\) terms of the original sum in (27) cancel. At odd \(N\), the middle term has weight \([N]_q=0\). The common factor in (28) is nonzero in the unit polydisk, so \[ S_N(q;\mathbf t)=0 . 	ag{30} \] Taking the derivative using (19) proves (26). Derivatives of the common factor in (28) multiply (30) and vanish. Its root value, including every \(1-\eta t_
u^N\) and the actual \(\kappa^3\), remains in (26). \(\square\) ## 5. A reduced vertex on the original coefficient cycle The scalar factors \(D_N(t_
u)\) in (26) must remain in the polynomial identity. There is a separate exact simplification for the closed-tree coefficient period. Reverse finite vertex indices, with the corresponding swaps of the signed inputs and original caps, as in the generating-section assembly theorem. Every edge then has anti-diagonal contraction. If \(V_v\) is the generating polynomial of its actual finite vertex array, the original scalar is \[ [\,\prod_e t_e^d\,]\prod_v V_v((t_e)_{e
i v}). 	ag{31} \] All powers in these vertex polynomials are nonnegative. On such a trivalent vertex define the analytic Taylor section \[ \widehat{\mathcal C}_N(\mathbf t)=  rac{(-1)^N(q-q^{-1})\kappa^3}{2N^{5/2}} \prod_{
u=1}^3(1+qt_
u)^{-1} \left.(\xi\partial_\xi)S_N(\xi;\mathbf t)ight|_{\xi=q}. 	ag{32} \] It is regular near the origin by (25), and (26) says exactly \[ \mathcal C_N(\mathbf t) =\prod_{
u=1}^3D_N(t_
u)\, \widehat{\mathcal C}_N(\mathbf t). 	ag{33} \] Since \(D_N(t)=1+O(t^N)\), these two sections agree modulo the ideal generated by \(t_1^N,t_2^N,t_3^N\). They therefore give the same original coefficient in (31): after expanding the difference one vertex at a time, each extra term has degree at least \(N>d\) on some edge, and no other factor has negative powers to bring it back to degree \(d\). The coefficient-conjugate vertex has the conjugate Taylor section. Equivalently, (31) has its prescribed small-circle representation \[  rac1{(2\pi i)^{|E|}} \oint\cdots\oint \prod_v V_v((t_e)_{e
i v})\, \prod_e rac{dt_e}{t_e^N}, 	ag{34} \] with all circles sufficiently small and positively oriented. The replacements (32) preserve this entire period, including its actual input and closing arrays. Thus every multiplication vertex can be written using the one finite sum in (25), its specified normal and the simple factors \((1+qt_
u)^{-1}\), on the original Taylor cycle. This is a statement about these nonnegative auxiliary generating powers. It is not a rule for deleting a peripheral \(M^N\) factor, setting a parameter equal to one, reversing an untruncated Taylor series, or moving the cycle through a singularity. ## 6. What has been simplified The three-boundary tensor is now a prescribed confluent finite hypergeometric source. No unknown interpolation coefficient or choice of cycle has been added. Both the simple node and all double-node derivatives survive. The identity is initially proved on the unit polydisk, where every factor is regular. Since its left side is a polynomial, the full right side has the corresponding removable extension wherever an individual displayed denominator vanishes. This does not allow individual terms, or their derivatives, to be discarded. Evaluating the sum only at the root would give zero by (30); it would lose the original source. Replacing it by an infinite Rogers product would require a separate argument and is not done. No nonzero leading coefficient, geometric saddle or lower bound for an arbitrary short component follows from (26) alone. ## Complete proof sources and coverage All three complete proof texts were read at the matching pins. The first fixes \(C\), both closures and all phase conventions; the second supplies the full physical generating section and its actual first normals; the third supplies the original crossing's nodal values and derivatives used in (15). | Source | SHA-256 | |---|---| | [Centered original compiler](research_centered_fourier_conway_compiler.md) | 0edbabe42280d70e4d5dcbcb55b188a3e773c14b99fbd212eb0fe8c5b176a413 | | [Full-degree generating section](research_full_degree_centered_generating_section.md) | 6fbef2085aca79503518745a08d3466ec84cd337ec8131944e2aebb9c95c2f6b | | [Arbitrary-power original source](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_arbitrary_power_source_compilation.md) | 55e2de84870cfd20dac5922791dbc2bed54909439dfbf4663f17c70a1089445f | The existing arbitrary-power representation already retains the original angle trace, and the centered compiler already gives the full three-dimensional Fourier tensor. The identity here is the particular initialized one-sum representation (26), with its full Hermite calibration and its unchanged coefficient cycle.
