The original highest-cut pivotal functional is an explicit central resolvent inside an ordinary full trace. This gives a compact coherent period with no cut coupon to reset under Weyl turnover. The actual turnover and half-twist return yield a specified rational exact-form current, including every meridian pole and finite-part term. A symmetric representative has a literal orientation-preserving involution on the original product of compact spheres. These are exact finite-source identities. They do not identify the two geometric eigenline contributions of the reduced trace. The opposite polarization and local relative boundary currents remain. The complete directs H, P, C and G are listed at the end. H fixes the pointed functional, P the whole-meridian turnover, C the compact kernel calculus, and G the resolved reduced geometric chart. All new Chebyshev, inverse-Jacobian, and compact-current calculations are below. ## 1. Exact central full-trace reconstruction Fix \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\), and \(m\ge2\) heads with common meridian \(M\) near one. The quantum parameter stays fixed at \(q_N\). Write \(x=-M/q\), and let \(W(M)\) be an analytic actual total intertwiner. It may be the original zero-framed braid word, with every prescribed scalar retained. The original source is \[ \Phi_0(W)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\rm full} ((P_0\otimes K_{\rm r}^{1-N})W). \tag{1} \] Let \(D_N(z)=(z^N-z^{-N})/(z-z^{-1})\), with its Laurent-polynomial continuation at \(z=\pm1\). Define two polynomial families by \[ \begin{split} &T_0(t)=2,\quad T_1(t)=t,\quad T_{j+1}(t)=tT_j(t)-T_{j-1}(t),\\ &U_0(t)=1,\quad U_1(t)=t,\quad U_{j+1}(t)=tU_j(t)-U_{j-1}(t). \end{split} \tag{2} \] They are monic in positive degree, and substitution proves \[ T_N(z+z^{-1})=z^N+z^{-N},\qquad U_{N-1}(z+z^{-1})=D_N(z). \tag{3} \] Use the full ordered Casimir \(\Omega_\Sigma=F_\Sigma E_\Sigma+qK_\Sigma+q^{-1}K_\Sigma^{-1}\), with the scaled lowering operator of H and P. Set \[ Z_N(M)=U_{N-1}(-\Omega_\Sigma(M))^{-1}. \tag{4} \] The inverse is taken generically and then as a meromorphic matrix; it is not evaluated separately at a singular root color. Exactly, \[ \boxed{\displaystyle \Phi_0(W(M))=\frac{D_N(M)}{N} \operatorname{Tr}_{\rm full}(Z_N(M)W(M)). } \tag{5} \] No semisimplicity is needed. In the actual triangular coordinates, H and P give \[ S_m^{-1}\Omega_\Sigma S_m =F_1E_{\rm r}-(MK_{\rm r}+M^{-1}K_{\rm r}^{-1}),\qquad S_m^{-1}WS_m=\sum_{n=0}^{d}F_1^n\otimes B_n . \tag{6} \] Both are lower triangular in the first occupation. Every diagonal block of the second is \(B_0\); every diagonal block of \(U_{N-1}(-S_m^{-1}\Omega_\Sigma S_m)\) is \(D_N(MK_{\rm r})\). The diagonal of its inverse is the inverse diagonal. Hence \[ \operatorname{Tr}_{\rm full}(Z_NW) =N\operatorname{Tr}_{\rm r}(D_N(MK_{\rm r})^{-1}B_0). \tag{7} \] H's exact scalar-kernel identity proves (5). Its meromorphic continuation is prescribed by the analytic original left side. All Jordan entries and polar coefficients remain. The coupon (4) commutes with every total generator and actual total intertwiner. A mark failing total intertwining retains its Ward defect and is not covered by (5). These fixed-root meridian identities are not off-root quantum-normal identities. ## 2. The exact inverse-Jacobian source Put \(r=m-1\), \(K_{\rm r}(M)=M^rK_0\), and \(\varepsilon=(-1)^{(N+1)r}\), so \(K_0^N=\varepsilon I\). Let \(\mathcal X\) be the \(N\) eigenvalues \(\chi\) of \(K_0\), with occupation projectors \(P_\chi\). Define \[ z_\chi=M^m\chi,\qquad \lambda_\chi=-z_\chi-z_\chi^{-1},\qquad t_\chi(M)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\rm r}(P_\chi B_0(M)). \tag{8} \] The monic degree-\(N\) polynomial with these generic distinct roots is \[ p_M(\lambda)=(-1)^N \bigl[T_N(-\lambda) -\varepsilon(M^{mN}+M^{-mN})\bigr]. \tag{9} \] Indeed \(z_\chi^N=\varepsilon M^{mN}\), and (3) proves each root equation. Differentiating (3) gives \(T_N'=NU_{N-1}\), hence \[ p_M'(\lambda_\chi)=(-1)^{N+1}N D_N(z_\chi). \tag{10} \] Let \(t_M(\lambda)\) be the degree-\(<N\) polynomial interpolating \(t_M(\lambda_\chi)=t_\chi(M)\). Its coefficients are meromorphic; colliding values are not evaluated before cancellation. Then \[ \boxed{\displaystyle \Phi_0(W(M)) =(-1)^{N+1}N D_N(M) \sum_\chi\frac{t_\chi(M)}{p_M'(\lambda_\chi)} =(-1)^{N+1}N D_N(M)[\lambda^{N-1}]t_M(\lambda). } \tag{11} \] The first equality is H's weightwise source formula and (10). The second follows by taking the leading coefficient in \[ t_M(\lambda)=\sum_\chi t_\chi(M)\frac{p_M(\lambda)} {(\lambda-\lambda_\chi)p_M'(\lambda_\chi)}. \] Equivalently the sum is the sum of finite residues of \(t_M(\lambda)d\lambda/p_M(\lambda)\). This fixes the inverse Jacobian and its sign for the actual source; it is not a choice of a scalar on a torsor. Retain the whole meromorphic expression and the removable continuation of (5). ### Polynomial central coupon and a uniform pole-order bound The full matrix, not only its spectrum, satisfies \[ p_M(\Omega_\Sigma)=0. \tag{11a} \] Here is a direct proof through the possible root Jordan blocks. In (6) the off-diagonal letter \(F_1E_{\rm r}\) raises first occupation by one and changes a remaining weight \(\chi\) to \(Q\chi\), since \(K_{\rm r}E_{\rm r}=QE_{\rm r}K_{\rm r}\). An entry rising by \(k<N\) therefore visits only the scalar diagonal values \(\lambda_\chi,\lambda_{Q\chi},\ldots,\lambda_{Q^k\chi}\). For a polynomial \(f\), its entry on this path is \(F_1^kE_{\rm r}^k\) times the divided difference of \(f\) at those nodes, restricted to the starting weight space. For \(f(t)=t^j\), expansion of all diagonal steps proves this: their sum is the complete homogeneous polynomial of degree \(j-k\) in the visited nodes, which is exactly that divided difference. Linearity proves the assertion for every \(f\). Multiplicity of a weight does not alter its scalar diagonal; paths beyond the first-head endpoint vanish. For generic \(M\), these \(k+1\le N\) nodes are distinct. The polynomial \(p_M\) vanishes at every one, so its divided difference is zero. All entries therefore vanish. Both sides of (11a) are analytic matrix functions of \(M\); continuation proves (11a) also at collisions, without deleting any Jordan direction. Substituting \(t=z+z^{-1}\) proves the polynomial identity \((t^2-4)U_{N-1}(t)^2=T_N(t)^2-4\). With (9),(11a) it gives \[ \boxed{\displaystyle Z_N(M)= \frac{(\Omega_\Sigma^2-4I)U_{N-1}(-\Omega_\Sigma)} {(M^{mN}-M^{-mN})^2}. } \tag{11b} \] The equality holds generically and hence meromorphically. Thus the coupon is a polynomial in the actual Casimir with a scalar meridian denominator; its pole order at \(M=1\) is at most two for every \(N,m\). For later finite parts put \[ B_\beta(u)= (\Omega_\Sigma(e^u)^2-4I) U_{N-1}(-\Omega_\Sigma(e^u))W_\beta(e^u). \tag{11c} \] It is analytic. Original-source analyticity in (5) forces \(\operatorname{Tr}B_\beta(u)=O(u^2)\). Consequently \[ \Phi_0(W_\beta(1)) =\frac{\operatorname{Tr}B_\beta''(0)}{8m^2N^2}. \tag{11d} \] This is an exact alternative source formula, not a norm bound. At the matrix level the finite part remains \[ \operatorname{FP}_{u=0} \frac{D_N(e^u)B_\beta(u)} {N(e^{mNu}-e^{-mNu})^2} = \frac{B_\beta''(0)}{8m^2N^2} +\frac{N^2-1-2m^2N^2}{24m^2N^2}B_\beta(0). \tag{11e} \] Indeed expand \(\sinh(Nu)/(N\sinh u)\) and \(4\sinh^2(mNu)\) to their quadratic terms. The second summand has zero full trace but is not discarded as an operator or a compact relative current. ## 3. The original compact full-trace period Use C's head metric \(\langle e_a,e_a\rangle=\binom da^{-1}\), and \[ X=(\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1)\setminus\{1+wz=0\},\qquad \Gamma=\{w=v,\ z=\bar v\}\simeq S^2 . \] For an operator \(A\) on \(m\) heads put \[ K_A(\mathbf w,\mathbf z)= \sum_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b} \mathbf w^{\mathbf a}A_{\mathbf a\mathbf b} \prod_{i=1}^m\binom d{b_i}z_i^{b_i},\qquad \omega_A=K_A\bigwedge_{i=1}^m \left(-\frac{dw_i\wedge dz_i} {2\pi i(1+w_i z_i)^{N+1}}\right). \tag{12} \] All indices lie in \(0,\ldots,d\). C's exact beta pairing gives \[ \int_{\Gamma^m}\omega_A=N^{-m}\operatorname{Tr}_{\rm full}A. \tag{13} \] Define the actual source matrix and form by \[ A_\beta(M)=\frac{D_N(M)}{N}Z_N(M)W_\beta(M),\qquad \mathcal O_\beta(M)=N^m\omega_{A_\beta(M)}. \tag{14} \] Then \[ \Phi_0(W_\beta(M))=\int_{\Gamma^m}\mathcal O_\beta(M). \tag{15} \] Composition uses C's exact kernel formula with one factor \(N\) per integrated head. Thus (15) also has an expanded finite-word period with the explicit resolvent coupon, every original crossing, and every prescribed scalar. No full exponential or infinite occupation sum replaces the finite coherent identity kernel. There is no cut reset or additional \(N\) normalization. Write \(u=\Log M\), with \(u=0\) at completeness. The matrix and form (14) have finite meromorphic pole order at fixed \(N,m\). Their coefficients are smooth on the compact cycle, which avoids the incidence divisor. Laurent expansion and integration commute: \[ \Phi_0(W_\beta(1)) =\int_{\Gamma^m}\operatorname{FP}_{u=0}\mathcal O_\beta(e^u). \tag{16} \] Negative coefficients have zero total integral but are retained as forms. Higher meridian jets are obtained from the whole product in (14) in the same way. Substituting \(D_N(1)=N\) before taking that product's finite part can lose polar cross terms. ## 4. Literal compact Weyl turnover and its normal current At completeness P's balanced turnover is \[ C_0e_a=(-1)^a e_{d-a},\qquad C_0^2=(-1)^dI. \tag{17} \] It is unitary for the binomial metric. Direct substitution gives \[ K_{C_0AC_0^{-1}}(w,z)=(wz)^dK_A(-1/w,-1/z). \tag{18} \] Thus conjugation pulls back \(\omega_A\) by \(\iota(w,z)=(-1/w,-1/z)\). Its powers cancel the transformed denominator and Jacobian exactly, including at zero and infinity. Let \(\mathsf J\) reverse tensor factors and \(\mathscr C_0=C_0^{\otimes m}\mathsf J\). It corresponds to \[ \mathcal I(\mathbf w,\mathbf z)_i =(-1/w_{m+1-i},-1/z_{m+1-i}). \tag{19} \] This preserves \(\Gamma^m\) with orientation \(+1\): each sphere map is holomorphic of degree one, and interchanging real two-dimensional factors adds no sign. The paired forms have the same sign. For the meridian germ retain the entire matrix \[ C(M)e_a=c_a(M)e_{d-a},\qquad c_a(M)=\prod_{j=1}^a\frac{MQ^j-M^{-1}}{1-Q^j}. \tag{20} \] Set \[ D(M)=\mathscr C_0^{-1} (C(M)^{\otimes m}\mathsf J). \tag{21} \] This is the tensor product of diagonal \(C_0^{-1}C(M)\), whose entries are \((-1)^a c_a(M)\). It is invertible near one and \(D(1)=I\); it is not replaced by \(I\) in a normal derivative. Let \(\beta^{\rm rev}\) replace \(\sigma_i^{\pm1}\) by \(\sigma_{m-i}^{\pm1}\) without reversing word order. P's exact conjugations of the word and Casimir, and \(D_N(M^{-1})=D_N(M)\), give \[ A_\beta(M)=\mathscr C_0D(M)A_{\beta^{\rm rev}}(M^{-1}) D(M)^{-1}\mathscr C_0^{-1}. \tag{22} \] The original zero-framing line is reciprocal and included. An additional nonreciprocal external scalar must keep its explicit ratio in this formula. The difference from the fixed compact pullback is the specified trace-zero matrix \[ X_1(M)=[D(M),A_{\beta^{\rm rev}}(M^{-1})D(M)^{-1}]. \tag{23} \] It need not vanish in the finite part: \(D(M)-I\) can multiply poles of the central coupon. ## 5. The rational current and half-twist return We require a tensor version of C's explicit primitive. For every matrix \(A\) there is a finite linear rational construction with \[ \omega_A-\frac{\operatorname{Tr}A}{N^m}\omega_I=d\eta_A, \tag{24} \] where \(\omega_I\) is the product normalized volume form. To prove it, let \(\mathcal E_i\) replace head \(i\) by its normalized partial trace times \(I_i\). The commuting maps give \[ A-\mathcal E_1\cdots\mathcal E_m A =\sum_{i=1}^m\mathcal E_1\cdots\mathcal E_{i-1} (A-\mathcal E_i A). \tag{25} \] Each summand has zero \(i\)-th partial trace. Treat its other heads as matrix coefficients. C's construction expresses it as \([J_{0,i},B_i]+[J_{-,i},C_i]\): divide off-diagonal entries by row-minus-column, and put the trace-zero diagonal prefix sum divided by \(j+1\) in the raising entry. All denominators are nonzero integers. The vector fields \[ V_{0,i}=w_i\partial_{w_i}-z_i\partial_{z_i},\qquad V_{-,i}=\partial_{w_i}+z_i^2\partial_{z_i} \] preserve \(\omega_I\) and give those commutators on symbols. Cartan's formula proves (24), with the sum of \(\sigma_{B_i}\iota_{V_{0,i}}\omega_I+ \sigma_{C_i}\iota_{V_{-,i}}\omega_I\) as \(\eta_A\). It is global and linear in matrix entries, hence preserves every Laurent coefficient. Apply this construction to (23). Exactly, \[ \mathcal O_\beta(M)- \mathcal I^*\mathcal O_{\beta^{\rm rev}}(M^{-1}) =N^m d\mathcal I^*\eta_{X_1(M)}. \tag{26} \] For the remaining reversal let \(V(M)=W_{\Delta_m}(M)\) be the actual half-twist operator. P proves \(\beta^{\rm rev}=\Delta_m\beta\Delta_m^{-1}\). Centrality of \(Z_N\) gives \[ A_{\beta^{\rm rev}}(M)=V(M)A_\beta(M)V(M)^{-1}. \tag{27} \] No cut coupon is moved and replaced here. Put \[ X_2(M)=[V(M^{-1}),A_\beta(M^{-1})V(M^{-1})^{-1}]. \tag{28} \] Then (24)--(28) give the same-word identity \[ \boxed{\displaystyle \mathcal O_\beta(e^u)-\mathcal I^*\mathcal O_\beta(e^{-u}) =d\mathcal T_\beta(u),\qquad \mathcal T_\beta=N^m\mathcal I^* (\eta_{X_1(e^u)}+\eta_{X_2(e^u)}). } \tag{29} \] All entries of this current are specified finite original operators. Compact Stokes proves its zero period, without discarding its pairing on relative boundaries. In particular \[ \mathcal O_\beta^{\rm sym}(u)= \tfrac12(\mathcal O_\beta(e^u)+ \mathcal I^*\mathcal O_\beta(e^{-u})) \tag{30} \] obeys \(\mathcal O_\beta(e^u)-\mathcal O_\beta^{\rm sym}(u) =\tfrac12d\mathcal T_\beta(u)\). It has the same original period and obeys \(\mathcal O_\beta^{\rm sym}(u)= \mathcal I^*\mathcal O_\beta^{\rm sym}(-u)\) exactly. Finite parts and all coefficient identities hold before integration. Its constant Laurent coefficient is invariant; its coefficient of \(u\) is anti-invariant. The latter concerns the derivative of the **whole pointed source**, not the separate \(B_0'\) in H's closing row. All polar and current coefficients remain specified. ## 6. Geometric scope and the scalar loxodromic character On C's controlled physical head-symbol domain, (19) has \[ (A,p)\longmapsto(A^{-1},-p^{-1}),\qquad (K,E,F)\longmapsto(K^{-1},F,E)\quad(M=1). \tag{31} \] Indeed \(T=wz/(1+wz)\) changes to \(1-T\), while \(A=e^{2\pi iT}\) and \(p=1/w\). This is not a uniform symbol theorem for an arbitrary growing full-word kernel. The total-product slice in G requires a further distinction. For ordered totals put \[ b_+=\begin{pmatrix}K&E\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\quad b_-=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\-KF&K\end{pmatrix},\quad P=b_-^{-1}b_+,\quad J=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}. \] Total Chevalley/reversal gives directly \[ b_+'=Jb_-^{-1}J,\qquad b_-'=Jb_+^{-1}J,\qquad P'=Jb_-Pb_-^{-1}J. \tag{32} \] Thus \(F_\Sigma=0\) is sent to \(E_\Sigma=0\); the actual \(B_0\) quotient of G uses the former. Conjugation in (32) transports a labeled holonomy eigenline with its eigenvalue. It does not reselect the reciprocal eigenline on the original \(F_\Sigma=0\) slice. Equations (29)--(30) therefore pay a compact source symmetry with its boundary current, but do not identify the two geometric eigenline sectors of a reduced local decomposition. That needs the opposite-polarization source map and its relative chains. Where (29) can be integrated over a chain \(\mathcal C\), its difference remains exactly \(\int_{\partial\mathcal C}\mathcal T_\beta\). Compact Stokes does not set these local endpoints to zero. The central coupon is also not a unit amplitude at a loxodromic scalar argument. On a compact set \(|z|\ge1+\delta>1\), \[ U_{N-1}(z+z^{-1})^{-1} =(z-z^{-1})z^{-N}(1-z^{-2N})^{-1}. \tag{33} \] The last factor is \(1+O((1+\delta)^{-2N})\). Its fixed \(j\)-th derivative has error \(O_j(N^j(1+\delta)^{-2N})\), on a fixed smaller holomorphic neighborhood. This follows by differentiating its convergent geometric series. On a chosen branch its scalar logarithm is \[ -N\Log z+\Log(z-z^{-1})-\Log(1-z^{-2N}). \tag{34} \] For \(|z|<1\), use the reciprocal; (3) is invariant under that replacement. The order-\(N\) character is retained. These scalar identities are not an operator asymptotic, a coherent-kernel phase, or an original-cycle contribution. No positivity, geometric thimble coefficient, cancellation of two geometric residues, or addition of their first-jet terms is inferred. The new exact source object is (5),(11),(15), with the concrete involution and full relative current (29). ## Complete proof directs * H: notes/research_scalar_prefix_kernel_and_first_meridian_jet.md, SHA256 d7d82848a1b3f50709352905bafcc7ddfee36f41e434bf5de4663b4b6181dc9e. * P: notes/research_reduced_casimir_pair_localizer.md, SHA256 e5307ed7e424ba181db9b73f8473342a094ed85caf0b521b4aa965bb78e3c4ea. * C: notes/compact_coherent_source_period.md, SHA256 8c6c3277367a4aa6c69269da635139d5f881f3d3d0d894e04dd97028d76537e4. * G: notes/research_actual_reduced_braid_critical_scheme.md, SHA256 ddddcd9bf75f35afdf3e5de0c03323acee2c66e624db36142c2344ef729a977a. All four complete sources were read nontruncated in this active sequence. The assertions concern the actual fixed-root meridian germ. No mathematical programs, numerical cases, or imported modified-trace proof are used.

title: A full boundary frame from charge-normal values and genuine turns
text: # A full boundary frame from charge-normal values and genuine turns Written proof, 23 November 2026. Values of an actual boundary packet and its genuine turn recover every Newton coefficient with polynomial inverse cost. The observation weights come from the actual charge-normal trace. An explicit odd-level completion retains the simple-node direction. The resulting positive metric preserves the turn and both original closing rows. This is a reconstruction and error estimate, not a lower bound for the original knot scalar. ## 1. The full source and the completed observations Fix \(N\ge2\), put \(d=N-1\), \(\gamma=\pi/N\), \(q=e^{i\gamma}\), and use the complete original algebra and coefficient norm of [G]: \[ H_N=\mathbb C[z]/P_N,\qquad P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2,\qquad e_k(z)=s_k^{-2}\prod_{h<k}(c_h-z), \] \[ c_h=2\cos((2h+1)\gamma),\qquad s_k=\prod_{h=1}^k2\sin(h\gamma),\quad s_0=1,\qquad \left\|\sum_{k=0}^d\alpha_ke_k\right\|_{\rm N}^2 =\sum_{k=0}^d|\alpha_k|^2. \tag{1} \] Here \(T_N\) is the first Chebyshev polynomial. All repeated-root first normals belong to \(H_N\). The actual quarter-turn and original closings satisfy \[ Je_k=e_{d-k},\qquad \lambda_0(f)=f(c_0)=\alpha_0,\qquad \phi_N(f)=(-1)^dN^2[z^d]\operatorname{rem}_{P_N}f=\alpha_d, \] \[ \phi_N(fg)=\alpha^{\mathsf T}J\beta,\qquad \phi_N(f)=\lambda_0(Jf). \tag{2} \] Here \(g=\sum\beta_ke_k\), and the transpose has no conjugation. These are the original normalized source identities, including the actual turn cups and caps. Put \(r=\lfloor N/2\rfloor\). The distinct double nodes are \(c_j\), \(0\le j<r\), with positive angles and weights \[ \tau_j=\pi-(2j+1)\gamma,\qquad w_j=2N^2\tau_j\sin\tau_j. \tag{3} \] The actual entire charge family of [D] has normal \(\mathfrak d_N=\partial_\chi\mathcal C_{N,\chi}|_0\), and its exact full-algebra trace is \[ \phi_N(\mathfrak d_NE)=\sum_{j<r}w_jE(c_j). \tag{4} \] Thus, with \(f^\sharp(z)=\overline{f(\bar z)}\), \[ G_D(f):=\phi_N(\mathfrak d_N f^\sharp f) =\sum_{j<r}w_j|f(c_j)|^2. \tag{5} \] This positive form alone is degenerate. Define its full completion by \[ \|f\|_{\rm D}^2=G_D(f)+G_D(Jf) +\mathbf1_{N\ {\rm odd}}\bigl(|f(-2)|^2+|(Jf)(-2)|^2\bigr). \tag{6} \] The odd simple-node terms in (6) are specified additional metric rows. They are not contributions of the charge-normal coupon itself. **Theorem.** Equation (6) is positive definite on the full \(H_N\), and \[ \boxed{\qquad \|f\|_{\rm N}\le N^2\|f\|_{\rm D},\qquad \|Jf\|_{\rm D}=\|f\|_{\rm D}. \qquad} \tag{7} \] Moreover both original closing rows and their bilinear contraction obey \[ |\lambda_0(f)|,\ |\phi_N(f)|\le w_0^{-1/2}\|f\|_{\rm D} \le(2\pi N)^{-1/2}\|f\|_{\rm D}, \] \[ \boxed{\qquad |\phi_N(fg)|\le N^4\|f\|_{\rm D}\|g\|_{\rm D}. \qquad} \tag{8} \] These estimates use the original normalization of \(\phi_N\). Any separately recorded closing scalar multiplies the corresponding bound by its absolute value. ## 2. An explicit polynomial inverse for half of the values The double nodes are strictly decreasing. Direct factorization gives \[ A_{jk}:=e_k(c_j)= \begin{cases} s_{j+k}/(s_{j-k}s_k^2),&0\le k\le j<r,\\ 0,&k>j. \end{cases} \tag{9} \] Indeed \(c_h-c_j=4\sin((h+j+1)\gamma)\sin((j-h)\gamma)\). All indices in (9) are less than \(N\). The square matrix \(A\) is triangular with nonzero diagonal. Write \(a_u=2\sin(u\gamma)\). Its inverse is exactly \[ (A^{-1})_{kj} =(-1)^{k-j} \frac{a_{2j+1}s_k^2}{s_{k+j+1}s_{k-j}}, \qquad 0\le j\le k<r. \tag{10} \] To prove (10), interpolate a polynomial of degree at most \(k\) at \(c_0,\ldots,c_k\). Its \(e_k\)-coefficient is \((-1)^ks_k^2\) times the leading interpolation coefficient. The node products have sign \((-1)^j\) and magnitude \[ \left|\prod_{\substack{0\le h\le k\\h\ne j}}(c_j-c_h)\right| =\frac{s_{k+j+1}s_{k-j}}{a_{2j+1}}. \tag{11} \] This follows by multiplying the two sine factors of every node gap. It proves every entry in (10), including the boundary \(k=j=0\). The inverse is polynomially bounded despite the size of some forward entries. Factoring its magnitude gives \[ |(A^{-1})_{kj}|= \frac{a_{2j+1}}{a_{k+j+1}} \prod_{h=0}^{j-1}\frac{a_{k-h}}{a_{k+h+1}} \le\frac N2. \tag{12} \] For each factor in the product, the two sine indices have sum \(2k+1<N\), so the numerator is at most the denominator. The remaining numerator is at most two, and its denominator is at least \(4/N\). Empty products are one. Consequently \[ \|A^{-1}\|_2\le rN/2\le N^2/4. \tag{13} \] The weights satisfy \[ \min_{j<r}w_j\ge4\pi,\qquad w_0\ge2\pi N. \tag{14} \] For the first bound use \(\pi/N\le\tau_j\le\pi-\pi/N\). If \(\tau_j\le\pi/2\), then \(\sin\tau_j\ge2\tau_j/\pi\); otherwise \(\sin\tau_j\ge2(\pi-\tau_j)/\pi\). The second bound uses \(\tau_0\ge\pi/2\) and \(\sin(\pi/N)\ge2/N\). ## 3. Reconstruction at both parities Let \(f=\sum\alpha_ke_k\). Values at the double nodes only see \(\alpha_0,\ldots,\alpha_{r-1}\), because all later \(e_k(c_j)\) vanish. Their vector is \(A(\alpha_0,\ldots,\alpha_{r-1})^{\mathsf T}\). Values of \(Jf\) similarly recover \(\alpha_d,\ldots,\alpha_{d-r+1}\). Equations (13)--(14) give \[ \sum_{k<r}|\alpha_k|^2+ \sum_{k>d-r}|\alpha_k|^2 \le\frac{N^4}{64\pi}\{G_D(f)+G_D(Jf)\}. \tag{15} \] At even \(N=2r\), these are all the coefficients. This proves (7) in that case. Suppose \(N=2r+1\). Only the middle coefficient \(\alpha_r\) is missing. Its recovery from the simple value must retain cancellations. Put \[ Q(z)=\prod_{j<r}(z-c_j) =U_r(z/2)-U_{r-1}(z/2), \tag{16} \] where \(U_k(\cos t)=\sin((k+1)t)/\sin t\). The second polynomial is monic and has the stated roots, since its value at \(z=2\cos t\) is \(\cos(Nt/2)/\cos(t/2)\). Also \(Q(-2)=(-1)^rN\). Let \(\ell_j\) be its Lagrange cardinal polynomial at \(c_j\). Direct differentiation of the last trigonometric expression yields \[ \ell_j(-2)=(-1)^{r-j+1}2\sin((2j+1)\gamma/2), \qquad |\ell_j(-2)|\le2. \tag{17} \] In particular this endpoint extrapolation has no exponential cost. The root identity \(\prod_{h=1}^{N-1}(1-e^{2\pi ih/N})=N\), paired into conjugates at odd \(N\), gives \(s_r^2=N\). Since \(\prod_{j<r}(c_j+2)=N\), one has \(e_r(-2)=1\), while \(e_k(-2)=0\) for \(k>r\). The polynomial \(p=\sum_{k<r}\alpha_ke_k\) has the same double-node values as \(f\). Thus the middle coefficient is explicitly \[ \alpha_r=f(-2)-p(-2) =f(-2)-\sum_{j<r}\ell_j(-2)f(c_j). \tag{18} \] Weighted Cauchy--Schwarz and (14),(17) show \[ |\alpha_r|^2 \le\left(1+\sum_{j<r}\frac{|\ell_j(-2)|^2}{w_j}\right) \bigl(|f(-2)|^2+G_D(f)\bigr) \le(1+r/\pi)\|f\|_{\rm D}^2. \tag{19} \] Combining (15),(19), and \(N^4/(64\pi)+1+r/\pi\le N^4\) for odd \(N\ge3\), proves (7). The isometry in (7) follows directly from (6) and \(J^2=I\). Both parities retain every independent coefficient, hence every physical first normal at the repeated nodes. ## 4. Positive resolution and original-source error bounds Let \(S_Nf\) be the observation vector in (6), including its square-root weights and both odd simple rows. Then \[ H_N^{\rm obs}=S_N^*S_N\succeq N^{-4}I,\qquad \mathcal R_N=(S_N^*S_N)^{-1}S_N^*,\qquad \mathcal R_NS_N=I,\qquad \|\mathcal R_N\|_{2\to{\rm N}}\le N^2. \tag{20} \] The last assertion follows because \(S_N\mathcal R_N\) is the ordinary orthogonal projection onto the observation range, and (7) bounds its inverse there. Thus redundant observation data cause no ambiguity. Equivalently, if \(s_\ell\) are the observation rows and \(\psi_\ell=(H_N^{\rm obs})^{-1}s_\ell^*\), then \[ f=\sum_\ell\psi_\ell(s_\ell f),\qquad \|f\|_{\rm D}^2=\sum_\ell|s_\ell f|^2. \tag{21} \] This is an exact positive frame in the completed metric. Indeed \(\langle\psi_\ell,f\rangle_{\rm D}=s_\ell f\), so its rank-one resolution operators are positive for that inner product. Equation (6) contains \(w_0|f(c_0)|^2\) and \(w_0|(Jf)(c_0)|^2\). Identities (2) and (14) therefore prove the closing bounds in (8). Its bilinear bound follows from \(|\alpha^{\mathsf T}J\beta|\le\|\alpha\|_2\|\beta\|_2\) and (7). It concerns two separate inputs; no unit bound on a full tensor-product row is asserted. In particular the entire boundary error is controlled by \[ \|f-\widetilde f\|_{\rm N} \le N^2\|f-\widetilde f\|_{\rm D}. \tag{22} \] The right side requires both actual value observations and those of the genuine turned error. It is not supplied by one coherent input, one physical row, or a positive scalar sum alone. No upper polynomial bound for \(S_N\), its Gram condition number, or the full multiplication operator in this metric is claimed. Every original gate and closing must use the same chosen metric when its budget is estimated. The theorem does not transfer an earlier budget or source lower bound from a different metric. These are auxiliary pair-Casimir samples. They have not been identified with ordinary main-meridian colors of an assembled knot. Nor does the charge-normal initializer of [D] provide both sets of observations or a lower bound for their particular original closing coordinate. Reversed edges and the simple completion remain explicit. No unit-coupon continuation, geometric rate, or finite-exception theorem follows. ## Complete proof sources and coverage Both complete proof inputs were read at matching pins: - [D] [Actual charge-normal source](research_actual_charge_normal_initializer.md), SHA256 a36b691f41231aee6440a198196d72708b4ce02e6a1f1c248c6aaf40ec032e85. - [G] [Original endpoint and turn identities](research_conway_global_closing_curvature.md), SHA256 863f170da9a9017aa8b83b1ace44ee3e2c851f57c806c77678b3699e3f2f305f. D supplies the actual trace (4) and Newton source; G supplies the genuine turn, both original closings and the Frobenius pairing. The inverse, odd extrapolation and quantitative completed-frame bounds are proved above. No off-root quantum-normal differentiation is used. The complete closest comparisons are [the uniform physical metric](research_conway_uniform_physical_quartic.md), SHA256 39895b430535f565d30133b46ef57f67589207bc83f40597ffe96e2ce79bbda8, and [complete Casimir--Hermite frames](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_complete_casimir_hermite_packet.md), SHA256 a4e96738a3a093d963fe13cc03585085951fa8699a506ade4e2e7a47c17b3f4c. They control different physical or spectral coordinate systems. Neither supplies the joint value-and-genuine-turn reconstruction bound (7). The interpolation method is elementary; the quantitative conclusion concerns this specified full source and its original closing.

title: A quantitative phase loss for the original charged block source
text: # A quantitative phase loss for the original charged block source Private written proof, 14 November 2026. No computation, import, test or manuscript change is used. The exact bridge reduction of the original signed braid gives root intervals with positive sine-binomial magnitudes and a specified phase on each block. Here their phase loss is bounded explicitly, at every block length and every positive radius. The resulting coefficient estimate retains the original shared charges, all clock factors and the closing pivots. It improves the positive radial upper bound by a weighted graph phase energy. The positive radial bound has a precise constrained tetrahedral-volume dual. Neither that dual nor the phase loss is identified here with the hyperbolic volume of the original partially filled tangle. No lower bound for its coherent clock sum is asserted. ## 1. The exact block and a uniform angular estimate Put \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\), \(N\ge2\). For \(0\le L<N\), set \[ c_{L,j}=\left|{L\brack j}_Q\right|,\qquad B_{L,N}(t)=\sum_{j=0}^L c_{L,j}t^j =\prod_{r=0}^{L-1}(1+q^{2r-L+1}t). \tag{1} \] All the coefficients are positive, and \(c_{L,j}=c_{L,L-j}\). The last equality is the finite Gaussian binomial identity: the phase \(q^{j(L-j)}\) of \({L\brack j}_Q\) cancels the phase \(q^{j(j-L)}\) from expanding the product. Empty products are one. For \(0\le\lambda\le1\), \(\rho>0\), define \[ \begin{split} I_{\lambda,\rho}(\theta) &=\frac1{2\pi}\int_{-\pi\lambda}^{\pi\lambda} \log|1+\rho e^{i(\theta+x)}|\,dx,\\ k(\lambda,\rho)&=\frac{\rho\sin(\pi\lambda)} {\pi(1+\rho)^2}. \end{split} \tag{2} \] The logarithmic singularities in this ordinary integral are integrable. **Theorem 1.** There is an absolute constant \(C\ge1\) such that, for every \(N,L,\rho,\theta\) as above, \[ |B_{L,N}(\rho e^{i\theta})| \le C N^C B_{L,N}(\rho) \exp\{-N k(L/N,\rho)(1-\cos\theta)\}. \tag{3} \] The elementary bound \(|B_{L,N}(\rho e^{i\theta})|\le B_{L,N}(\rho)\) also holds. No interval of lengths, positive-radius compactum, or avoidance of the zeros on the left of (3) is required. We first prove the exact integral inequality \[ I_{\lambda,\rho}(0)-I_{\lambda,\rho}(\theta) \ge k(\lambda,\rho)(1-\cos\theta). \tag{4} \] By evenness and periodicity it suffices to take \(0\le\theta\le\pi\). Put \(a=\pi\lambda\) and \(f_\rho(x)=\log|1+\rho e^{ix}|\). The arc integral is absolutely continuous in its center. Almost everywhere, \[ -I'_{\lambda,\rho}(\theta) =\frac1{4\pi}\log\frac{1+\rho^2+2\rho\cos(\theta-a)} {1+\rho^2+2\rho\cos(\theta+a)}. \tag{5} \] The numerator \(A\) is at least the denominator \(B\), because \(A-B=4\rho\sin a\sin\theta\). Using \(\log(A/B)\ge(A-B)/A\) and \(A\le(1+\rho)^2\) proves \(-I'(\theta)\ge k(\lambda,\rho)\sin\theta\). Integration gives (4). Isolated zeros are handled by the integrable limit. The endpoint lengths have \(k=0\) and obey the same assertion. Here is a uniform sum-to-integral estimate which retains those zeros: \[ \begin{split} \log|B_{L,N}(\rho e^{i\theta})| &\le N I_{L/N,\rho}(\theta)+C_1\log(N+1),\\ \left|\log B_{L,N}(\rho)-N I_{L/N,\rho}(0)\right| &\le C_1\log(N+1). \end{split} \tag{6} \] The first line is automatic if the polynomial vanishes. Palindromicity reduces both assertions to \(0<\rho\le1\), since replacing \(\rho\) by \(\rho^{-1}\) adds \(L\log\rho\) to both the discrete and integral expressions. For \(0<\rho\le1/2\), \(f_\rho\) is uniformly bounded and has uniformly bounded variation. For \(1/2\le\rho\le1\), put \(t=|x-\pi|_{\mathbb T}\in[0,\pi]\). Then \[ |1+\rho e^{ix}|^2 =(1-\rho)^2+4\rho\sin^2(t/2) \ge 2t^2/\pi^2. \tag{7} \] Clip \(f_\rho\) below at \(-M\), where \(M=\log N+2\). The clipped periodic function has total variation \(O(M+1)\), uniformly in \(\rho\): on each half-period it is monotone before clipping, and its maximum is at most \(\log2\). Equation (7) gives \[ \int_0^{2\pi}(\max(f_\rho,-M)-f_\rho)\,dx \le C_2 e^{-M}. \tag{8} \] Indeed clipping occurs only where \(t\le C_3e^{-M}\), and there its excess is bounded by \(\log(C_3e^{-M}/t)\), whose integral on \([0,C_3e^{-M}]\) is \(C_3e^{-M}\). The points \((2r-L+1)\pi/N\) in (1) are the midpoints of \(L\) intervals of length \(2\pi/N\) filling \([-\pi L/N,\pi L/N]\). For a function of bounded variation, the error between this midpoint sum and \(N/(2\pi)\) times its integral is bounded by its total variation on the arc. Apply this to the clipped function, then use (8). This proves the first line of (6) with \(O(\log N)+O(Ne^{-M})=O(\log(N+1))\). For the centered arc in the second line, every point is at circular distance at least \(\pi/N\) from \(\pi\), since \(L\le N-1\). Equation (7) makes clipping inactive throughout that arc; the case \(\rho\le1/2\) is already bounded. The same variation estimate proves the second line of (6). The empty arc is immediate. Combining (4) and (6) proves (3). ## 2. The actual shared coefficient and its graph phase energy Consider a fixed finite directed multigraph, including parallel edges and loops, and the ordinary polynomial \[ P_N(X)=\Gamma_N\prod_{e:u\to v} X_u^{L_e}B_{L_e,N}(w_eX_v/X_u), \qquad |w_e|=1,\quad 0\le L_e<N. \tag{9} \] The Laurent notation represents an ordinary polynomial. Let \(a_i\) be prescribed nonnegative integral coefficient charges, with \(\sum_i a_i=\sum_e L_e\). Retain \(\Gamma_N\) exactly. Its vanishing makes all subsequent bounds trivial. Write \(w_e=e^{i\omega_e}\). With one positive radius \(r_i\) at each original vertex, put \[ \begin{split} {\cal C}_N(r) &=|\Gamma_N|\frac{\prod_e r_u^{L_e} B_{L_e,N}(r_v/r_u)} {\prod_i r_i^{a_i}},\\ {\cal E}_N(r,w) &=\min_{\vartheta\in\mathbb T^{V}} \sum_{e:u\to v}k(L_e/N,r_v/r_u) \{1-\cos(\omega_e+\vartheta_v-\vartheta_u)\}. \end{split} \tag{10} \] The minimum exists. There is one radius per shared vertex, not separate radii for its different incidences. The full arc loss gives the stronger energy \[ \begin{split} D_{\lambda,\rho}(\theta) &=I_{\lambda,\rho}(0)-I_{\lambda,\rho}(\theta),\\ {\cal E}^{\rm arc}_N(r,w) &=\min_{\vartheta\in\mathbb T^V} \sum_{e:u\to v} D_{L_e/N,r_v/r_u}(\omega_e+\vartheta_v-\vartheta_u) \ \ge {\cal E}_N(r,w). \end{split} \tag{10a} \] The inequality is (4). The integral profiles are continuous in their center, including across their integrable logarithmic zeros, so this minimum also exists. **Theorem 2.** If there are \(b\) blocks in (9), then \[ \boxed{\displaystyle |[X^a]P_N| \le C^bN^{Cb}\inf_{r_i>0} \{{\cal C}_N(r)e^{-N{\cal E}^{\rm arc}_N(r,w)}\}.} \tag{11} \] This bounds the specified coefficient itself. Take its original Cauchy integral on \(X_i=r_ie^{i\vartheta_i}\). Subtract the two estimates in (6) to bound each block by its positive value times \(\exp(-ND_{\lambda,\rho}(\theta))\), at polynomial cost, with the literal relative angle \(\theta=\omega_e+\vartheta_v-\vartheta_u\). Multiplication and the minimum in (10a) give the bound at that radius. Normalized Haar integration adds no factor. The constant is independent of every radius, so infimizing proves (11). No block value is divided out. Replacing \({\cal E}^{\rm arc}_N\) by \({\cal E}_N\) gives the explicit weaker bound using only (3). For a simple cycle \(C\) with no repeated edges, orient its traversal and let \[ \delta_C=\left|\arg\prod_{e\in C}w_e^{\epsilon_e} \right|_{\mathbb T}\in[0,\pi]. \tag{12} \] If \(k_e=k(L_e/N,r_v/r_u)>0\) on this cycle, then \[ {\cal E}_N(r,w)\ge \frac{2\delta_C^2}{\pi^2\sum_{e\in C}k_e^{-1}}. \tag{13} \] Vertex angles telescope, so the sum of the circular distances of its edge angles is at least \(\delta_C\). Now use \(1-\cos t\ge2|t|_{\mathbb T}^2/\pi^2\) and weighted Cauchy. A loop is included as a one-edge cycle. Collections of cycles may be combined by the existing fractional cycle-packing argument. The energy is zero exactly when the connection is flat on the subgraph with positive \(k_e\), by spanning-tree propagation of vertex phases and the nonnegative summands in (10). This characterization is not needed for (11). If lengths approach zero or one, or radius ratios escape, the bound still holds; its explicit \(k_e\)'s may tend to zero, so a uniform exponential loss is not inferred. ## 3. Source normalization and the coherent clock sum The original-source identity in [the charged bridge-flow theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_global_charged_bridge_flow.md), equations (12), (17)--(19), is \[ K_N=\frac{\chi_N}{N} \sum_{h\ {\rm over\text{-}monotone}} W_h[X_1^{N-1}\cdots X_s^{N-1}]P_h(X). \tag{14} \] It retains integer-weight conservation, all original closure adapters and pivots, and the homogeneous alias cancellation. Each fixed-clock block is exactly \[ \prod_{\ell=0}^{L-1}(\alpha X_u-Q^\ell\beta X_v) =\alpha^L X_u^L B_{L,N}\bigl(-(\beta/\alpha)q^{L-1}X_v/X_u\bigr). \tag{15} \] The actual propagated root phases have modulus one. Thus (9) is literally the fixed-clock polynomial in (14), with the extracted \(\alpha^L\)'s retained in \(\Gamma_h\). Its \(w_e\)'s are the source theorem's equation (18), including the unpivoted cut and every pivotal closing block. They are not selected by optimizing (10). Every \(W_h\), including its sine-factorial magnitudes and Gaussian phases, remains. If \(b\) bounds the number of blocks of the fixed word, (11) yields \[ |K_N|\le\frac{|\chi_N|}{N}C^bN^{Cb} \sum_h |W_h|\inf_r \{{\cal C}_{h,N}(r)e^{-N{\cal E}^{\rm arc}_{h,N}(r,w_h)}\}. \tag{16} \] The number of clocks is polynomial in \(N\) for a fixed word. No zero-feedback fiber, omitted closing character, or arbitrary observation replaces (14). Formula (11) applies also to another prescribed coefficient of an actual charged polynomial. Its use for an open matrix element requires that element's actual boundary coefficient adapter; (14) alone is not such an adapter. ## 4. The constrained tetrahedral entropy of the positive bound This identifies the positive optimization, not the knot geometry. Put \[ J(x)=\int_0^x\log(2\sin\pi t)\,dt,\qquad v_\lambda(x)=J(\lambda)-J(x)-J(\lambda-x). \tag{17} \] For \(0\le x\le\lambda\le1\), reflection gives \[ v_\lambda(x)=\frac1\pi \{\Lambda(\pi x)+\Lambda(\pi(\lambda-x)) +\Lambda(\pi(1-\lambda))\}, \tag{18} \] where \(\Lambda(a)=-\int_0^a\log|2\sin t|\,dt\). The three arguments are the angles of a possibly degenerate ideal tetrahedron. The endpoint-aware sine-product estimate gives \[ \log c_{L,j}=N v_{L/N}(j/N)+O(\log(N+1)) \quad(0\le j\le L<N). \tag{19} \] For clarity, the uniform sine-product estimate used here follows by subtracting the endpoint logarithms from \(\log(2\sin\pi t)\). The remainder is smooth on the closed interval; ordinary integral comparison for the increasing sequence \(\log j\), at either endpoint, gives error \(O(\log(N+1))\). Applying it to the three factorials in \(c_{L,j}\) proves (19). For \(0<\lambda<1\), \[ v_\lambda''(x)= -\frac{\pi\sin(\pi\lambda)} {\sin(\pi x)\sin(\pi(\lambda-x))}<0, \qquad 0<x<\lambda. \tag{20} \] Its endpoint derivatives are \(+\infty\) and \(-\infty\). For real \(y\), the unique maximum of \(v_\lambda(x)+yx\) is therefore interior and satisfies \[ e^y\sin(\pi(\lambda-x))=\sin(\pi x). \tag{21} \] The largest-term estimate in (1), its at most \(N\) positive terms, and (19), together with (6) at phase zero, prove \[ I_{\lambda,e^y}(0) =\max_{0\le x\le\lambda}\{v_\lambda(x)+yx\}. \tag{22} \] The endpoint lengths follow by continuity. Fix limiting lengths \(\lambda_e\) and limiting charges \(a_i^0\). Their literal coefficient-flow equations are \[ \sum_{e:v\to i}x_e-\sum_{e:i\to v}x_e =a_i^0-\sum_{e:i\to v}\lambda_e,\qquad 0\le x_e\le\lambda_e. \tag{23} \] Suppose this polytope has a point strict in every coordinate and all \(0<\lambda_e<1\). Then \(\sum_e v_{\lambda_e}(x_e)\) has a unique interior maximizer. Strict concavity gives uniqueness. Moving a boundary point toward the strict feasible point has positive infinite derivative from every opened endpoint, so a boundary point cannot maximize. Lagrange multipliers for the affine equations supply vertex log-radii \(\rho_i\) with (21) and \(y_e=\rho_v-\rho_u\). Substitution into (22) gives \[ \begin{split} \max_{\text{(23)}}\sum_e v_{\lambda_e}(x_e) =\inf_{\rho\in\mathbb R^V} \left\{\sum_{e:u\to v} [\lambda_e\rho_u+I_{\lambda_e,e^{\rho_v-\rho_u}}(0)] -\sum_i a_i^0\rho_i\right\}. \end{split} \tag{24} \] Conversely, (22) bounds any feasible flow by the expression in braces, since (23) cancels its radius terms. This proves both directions without assuming an interchange of extrema. At finite \(N\), write \(P_N^+\) for (9) with \(\Gamma_N\) replaced by its modulus and all \(w_e\) replaced by one. The existing [flat-block coefficient theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_flat_block_sublevel_transport.md) gives, under its strict-Hall hypotheses, \[ \frac{\operatorname{Cap}(P_N^+)}{\prod_e(L_e+1)} \le [X^a]P_N^+\le\operatorname{Cap}(P_N^+). \tag{25} \] The scalar magnitude is included on both sides. At a minimizing radius \(r_*\), (11) and (25) imply \[ |[X^a]P_N|\le C^bN^{Cb}\prod_e(L_e+1)\,[X^a]P_N^+ e^{-N{\cal E}^{\rm arc}_N(r_*,w)}. \tag{26} \] This is an upper comparison, not a positive lower bound for the original coefficient. ## 5. Contribution and remaining geometric comparison The earlier [cycle-packing theorem](research_regular_window_cycle_packing.md) already turns supplied local losses into a shared coefficient bound. The additions here are the explicit loss for the actual sine-binomial blocks, uniformity through all allowed lengths and all positive radii with polynomial cost, and (11) for the original charged bridge source. No asymptotic replacement of a crossing or deletion of an endpoint is used to obtain the phase loss. Equations (18), (23), (24) connect the bound to a concave tetrahedral entropy problem. In (14), however, the lengths and block phases depend on the remaining clocks. Their Gaussian feedback and \(W_h\) remain part of the source. The coefficient flow equations have not been proved to give all marked geometric gluing and peripheral equations for arbitrary short Conway pieces. The maximum in (24) must not be called their hyperbolic volume. At specified geometric radii, (11) supplies the positive radial envelope minus the full arc-loss energy, bounded below by the explicit graph cosine energy. Proving a strict gap below the geometric action on a whole complementary family still requires that numerical-free analytic comparison. Nontrivial holonomy alone, or positive energy alone, does not supply it. Compatible sectors and cancellation among original clock phases remain. No general partial-filling volume theorem is claimed. ## Direct source versions The written proof was checked against these source versions: | Source | SHA-256 | | --- | --- | | actual_global_charged_bridge_flow.md | b444e487eab3ec0a56c40b22584837cefcbe374a137b0beeaa185116c2a81d8c | | anchor_phase_cycles_and_exact_fusion.md | 37cdfb5125a27671069581e631b73f98c67e7ca944f38e37fe151a37f729a571 | | actual_flat_block_sublevel_transport.md | 182d1f125cb927b709556095c8cc888f0b459713b2943013c08eb99033c70a5b | | research_regular_window_cycle_packing.md | b0e36ecff57053bb660d542387ad903d36a6c39a52c142555d2e5dfc1b05d3ea |

title: Angle optimization for the complete charged bridge source
text: # Angle optimization for the complete charged bridge source Private written deduction, 14 November 2026. The object throughout is the original closed, marked braid scalar. No numerical calculation, test, or change to a frozen manuscript is used. The exact bridge formula has a useful consequence before any saddle is chosen. Including its clock prefactors turns the absolute weight of every term into reciprocal sine factorials on a transportation polytope. Its limiting exponent is a concave sum of ideal-tetrahedron volumes. The phase-sensitive block estimate then gives a finite-dimensional variational upper bound for the original scalar, with every clock and closing factor retained. This upper bound is not yet identified with the volume of the knot complement, and it supplies no lower bound for the coherent clock sum. ## 1. The original events and their endpoint charges Use the complete signed braid and the exact conventions of [the charged bridge formula](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_global_charged_bridge_flow.md). There are \(B\) overbridge events and \(b\) closing events. Put \(k=B+b\), the number of anchor segments, and \(d=N-1\). Every event has total polynomial degree \(d\), and the original coefficient requires degree \(d\) at every anchor. Distinct incidences at the same anchor remain distinct. An overbridge with \(m\ge1\) encounters has \(m+1\) ordered binary blocks, with lengths \[ L_0=d-h_1,\qquad L_j=h_j-h_{j+1}\ (1\le j<m),\qquad L_m=h_m. \tag{1} \] Their sum is \(d\). A closing event has one block of length \(d\). Let a block \(e:u\to v\) give exponent \(n_{e,0}\) to its tail anchor and exponent \(n_{e,1}\) to its head anchor. Thus \[ n_{e,0},n_{e,1}\ge0,\qquad L_e=n_{e,0}+n_{e,1}. \tag{2} \] The two incidences are kept separately even when \(u=v\). Define \(\mathcal P\) by nonnegative real incidence coordinates \(x_{e,\epsilon}\) satisfying \[ \sum_{e\text{ in event }v}\sum_{\epsilon=0}^1x_{e,\epsilon}=1, \qquad \sum_{(e,\epsilon)\text{ assigned to anchor }a} x_{e,\epsilon}=1. \tag{3} \] This is a compact bipartite transportation polytope, with event vertices on one side and anchor vertices on the other. Its underlying incidence graph is fixed by the original word and the chosen exact overbridge grouping. **Proposition 1.** The original clock assignments together with one chosen monomial from each block, whose product has the prescribed anchor degrees, are in bijection with \(d\mathcal P\cap\mathbb Z^{\mathrm{incidences}}\). Indeed (2) recovers every block length. For an overbridge the inverse of (1) is \[ h_j=\sum_{\ell=j}^{m}L_\ell . \tag{4} \] Nonnegative lengths summing to \(d\) give precisely the original monotone clocks. The second equations in (3) are the original anchor coefficient conditions. Conversely a chosen block monomial gives these incidences and clocks uniquely. The exact block coefficients have already summed their internal choices; there is no missing binomial multiplicity in this bijection. ## 2. The exact magnitude, including the clock factors Put \[ S_j=\prod_{r=1}^{j}2\sin(\pi r/N),\qquad S_0=1. \] All \(S_j\), \(0\le j\le d\), are positive, and \[ S_jS_{d-j}=N. \tag{5} \] The magnitude of a block coefficient is \(S_{L_e}/(S_{n_{e,0}}S_{n_{e,1}})\). The original overbridge factor, with its phase still retained, has magnitude \[ |\Gamma_v|=\frac{S_{h_1}}{S_{h_m}\prod_{j<m}S_{h_j-h_{j+1}}} =\frac{N}{\prod_{e\text{ in }v}S_{L_e}}. \tag{6} \] This is the root-reflection calculation in [the original length-frame source](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_length_gauge_clock_source.md), Section 3. Consequently each overbridge contributes exactly \[ \frac{N}{\prod_{e\text{ in }v} S_{n_{e,0}}S_{n_{e,1}}}. \tag{7} \] A closing block has the same expression with its single pair of incidences; by (5) that expression is exactly one. Its pivotal phase has not been removed. For an allowed incidence assignment \(n\), let \[ \Omega_N(n)=\frac{W_{h(n)}}{|W_{h(n)}|} \prod_e\alpha_e(h(n))^{L_e} w_e(h(n))^{n_{e,1}}. \tag{8} \] Here \(W_h,\alpha_e,w_e\) are exactly the original factors in the charged bridge formula, including its closing pivots and propagated frames. Every factor in (8) has modulus one. In particular no phase is chosen from an optimizer or from the value of the knot invariant. The original scalar is exactly \[ \boxed{\displaystyle K_N=\chi_N N^{k-1} \sum_{n\in d\mathcal P\cap\mathbb Z^{\mathrm{incidences}}} \Omega_N(n)\prod_{e,\epsilon}S_{n_{e,\epsilon}}^{-1}.} \tag{9} \] This follows from (7) for all events and the original factor \(\chi_N/N\). Closure incidences can instead be eliminated using (5), giving the equivalent factor \(\chi_N N^{B-1}\). Equation (9) keeps them to make both sets of conservation equations explicit. The exact bridge theorem has already proved that the anchor sampling introduces no cyclic aliases. None is discarded in (9). ## 3. Concavity of the actual absolute exponent Define \[ J(t)=\int_0^t\log(2\sin\pi s)\,ds,\qquad \mathcal V(x)=-\sum_{e,\epsilon}J(x_{e,\epsilon}). \tag{10} \] The continuous values at zero and one are included. A closing row has two entries summing to one, so its contribution to (10) is zero. For nonnegative \(y_1,\ldots,y_s\) with sum one, set \(A_j=\sum_{i\le j}y_i\). Reflection \(J(1-t)=-J(t)\) gives the exact identity \[ -\sum_{i=1}^sJ(y_i) =\sum_{j=2}^{s-1} \{-J(A_{j-1})-J(y_j)-J(1-A_j)\}. \tag{11} \] Each summand is the volume divided by \(\pi\) of an ideal tetrahedron with angles \(\pi A_{j-1},\pi y_j,\pi(1-A_j)\). The sum telescopes, so there is no added volume constant. This identity extends to the closed simplex by continuity. The tetrahedral angle-volume function is strictly concave on its open angle simplex. For the normalized tetrahedral volume \(-J(a)-J(b)-J(c)\), the negative Hessian in the first two normalized angles is \(\pi\) times \[ \begin{pmatrix} \cot(\pi a)+\cot(\pi c)&\cot(\pi c)\\ \cot(\pi c)&\cot(\pi b)+\cot(\pi c) \end{pmatrix},\qquad a+b+c=1. \tag{12} \] The diagonal entries of the displayed cotangent matrix are positive by the sine addition formula, and that matrix has determinant one. The fan maps in (11) jointly detect every nonzero tangent variation of a row with \(s\ge3\). Thus its row entropy is strictly concave in the open simplex. A two-entry row has identically zero entropy. Summing proves concavity of \(\mathcal V\) on \(\mathcal P\), with strict concavity wherever every nonzero allowed variation changes a positive row with at least three entries. Forced zero faces and directions supported only on two-entry rows must be retained; no general interior-maximizer assertion is needed. Define the positive sum without its external scalar by \[ Z_N^+=\sum_{n\in d\mathcal P\cap\mathbb Z^{\mathrm{incidences}}} \prod_{e,\epsilon}S_{n_{e,\epsilon}}^{-1}. \] Then \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log Z_N^+ =\max_{x\in\mathcal P}\mathcal V(x). \tag{13} \] If the polytope is empty the sum is zero; otherwise the following proof also establishes that its required integer points exist. Uniformly for \(0\le j<N\), \(\log S_j=NJ(j/N)+O(\log(N+1))\). This follows by subtracting the two endpoint logarithms from \(\log(2\sin\pi t)\) and applying elementary integral comparison to the remaining smooth function and to each endpoint logarithm. There are polynomially many incidence assignments. This proves the upper bound in (13). To prove the lower bound, round \(dx\) for a maximizing real flow while retaining its row and column sums. Confine each coordinate to its floor/ceiling interval. A nonintegral supported subgraph has no vertex of degree one, since all required sums are integral. It therefore has an even cycle. Alternately increase and decrease its entries until one becomes integral, keeping every sum and every floor/ceiling interval. Repeat. The resulting integer flow differs coordinatewise from \(dx\) by at most one. Continuity of (10), or its endpoint modulus \(O(\delta|\log\delta|)\), proves the matching exponential lower bound for this positive sum. This is a lower bound for \(Z_N^+\), not for the coherent scalar (9). ## 4. Fixed-clock capacity equals constrained angle optimization Let \(\lambda_e=x_{e,0}+x_{e,1}\), and let \(\mathcal L\) be the projection of \(\mathcal P\) onto these block lengths. Each overbridge row has length sum one; every closing length is one. For fixed \(\lambda\in\mathcal L\), put \[ v_\lambda(t)=J(\lambda)-J(t)-J(\lambda-t),\qquad 0\le t\le\lambda. \] The original anchor constraints are \[ \sum_{e:v\to a}t_e-\sum_{e:a\to v}t_e =1-\sum_{e:a\to v}\lambda_e. \tag{14} \] The endpoint cases \(\lambda=0,1\) remain included. For positive radius ratios \(r\), define \[ I_{\lambda,r}(\theta)=\frac1{2\pi} \int_{-\pi\lambda}^{\pi\lambda} \log|1+r e^{i(\theta+s)}|\,ds. \tag{15} \] The block theorem proves \[ I_{\lambda,e^y}(0) =\max_{0\le t\le\lambda}\{v_\lambda(t)+yt\}. \tag{16} \] Write \(s_a=\log r_a\) for anchor log-radii. The exact dual identity for the closed feasible polytope is \[ \begin{split} \max_{x\in\mathcal P,\,x_{e,0}+x_{e,1}=\lambda_e}\mathcal V(x) ={}&-\sum_eJ(\lambda_e)\\ &+\inf_s\left\{\sum_{e:u\to v} [\lambda_es_u+I_{\lambda_e,e^{s_v-s_u}}(0)] -\sum_a s_a\right\}. \end{split} \tag{17} \] Closing lengths contribute \(J(1)=0\). In particular the prefactor in the first line of (17) is exactly the limiting magnitude of the original clock factors; it is not omitted. The inequality from left to right follows immediately from (16) and (14). Equality holds also on tight faces, without claiming a finite minimizing radius there. To see it, let \(D t\) be the incidence imbalance in (14), and let \(F(t)=\sum_ev_{\lambda_e}(t_e)\). The set \(\{(Dt,z):0\le t\le\lambda,\ z\le F(t)\}\) is closed and convex. Separate it from \((b,z_0)\), where \(b\) is the feasible target in (14) and \(z_0>\max_{Dt=b}F(t)\). The coefficient of \(z\) in a strict separating functional must be positive: it cannot be negative because the set extends downward, and cannot be zero because it contains a point with first coordinate \(b\). Normalize that coefficient to one. The remaining coefficients give an affine multiplier whose unconstrained maximum is less than \(z_0\). Letting \(z_0\) decrease to the constrained maximum proves the reverse inequality. Formula (16) evaluates that maximum as the radial expression in (17). This argument handles loops, forced endpoints, and degenerate lengths. Thus the positive radial capacity, including the original clock prefactor, has precisely the same limiting variational problem as the incidence angles. These are two representations of the same positive comparison, not independent optimizations whose values may be combined arbitrarily. ## 5. A phase-sensitive upper bound for the complete original scalar The original block gains have limits \(w_e(\lambda)=\exp(i\omega_e(\lambda))\) as the normalized clocks approach \(\lambda\). These follow from the explicit integer-linear exponents in the charged bridge formula, including the signs from \(x=-q^{-1}\). One may use their circle values; no globally selected argument is required. Finite pivot shifts and the \(-1\) in \(d=N-1\) remain in (9). Their limiting shifts are obtained from those exact formulas, not reset independently. For any fixed positive anchor radii define \[ \begin{split} \mathcal A(\lambda,r)={}&-\sum_eJ(\lambda_e) +\sum_{e:u\to v}\lambda_e\log r_u-\sum_a\log r_a\\ &+\max_{\vartheta\in\mathbb T^k} \sum_{e:u\to v}I_{\lambda_e,r_v/r_u} (\omega_e(\lambda)+\vartheta_v-\vartheta_u). \end{split} \tag{18} \] The expression is invariant under a common scaling of all radii. If \(c_\chi=\limsup_NN^{-1}\log|\chi_N|\) is finite, then \[ \boxed{\displaystyle \limsup_N\frac1N\log|K_N| \le c_\chi+\sup_{\lambda\in\mathcal L} \inf_{r_a>0}\mathcal A(\lambda,r).} \tag{19} \] In the original framing conventions the external factor is retained explicitly; its known subexponential size makes \(c_\chi=0\). To prove (19), apply the original Cauchy coefficient integral at any fixed radii in each clock sector. The uniform midpoint estimate in [the block phase-loss theorem](research_charged_block_holonomy_rate_loss.md) gives \(\log|B_{L,N}(r e^{i\theta})|\le NI_{L/N,r}(\theta)+O(\log(N+1))\), including every zero. The factorial estimate and (6) supply the first term of (18). There are only polynomially many clocks for the fixed word. Along a subsequence giving the largest nonzero sector rate, its feasible normalized lengths have a convergent subsequence \(\lambda_N\to\lambda\in\mathcal L\). For every fixed choice of radii, the arc integrals are jointly continuous in their length and center, uniformly on the center circle. This also holds at a logarithmic zero, by integrability and translation continuity of the logarithmic kernel. The sector rate is consequently at most \(\mathcal A(\lambda,r)\) for every fixed \(r\). Taking the infimum now proves (19). Neither a radius chosen uniformly for all clock sectors nor an interchange of supremum and infimum is used. If all sectors vanish the bound is immediate. The maximum in (18) equals the centered positive arc sum minus the exact graph arc-loss energy. Consequently the infimum of (18) over radii is bounded by the positive capacity rate in (17), and can be strictly smaller. The quantitative cycle estimate in the block theorem gives an explicit loss when the actual gains have incompatible phases on a regular cycle. Boundary lengths and diverging optimal radii are included in (19); they do not automatically give a uniform positive loss. ## 6. Which geometric equations have been obtained There is a direct local volume interpretation on a smaller real chamber. Order one overbridge row by its original blocks, taking the tail incidence and then the head incidence of each block. If every angle in that row satisfies \(0<x_i<1/2\), put equatorial vertices on the unit circle with successive arguments differing by \(2\pi x_i\), and use apices \(0,\infty\) in the upper-half-space boundary. The convex ideal bipyramid is subdivided by its axial edge into tetrahedra of shapes \(e^{2\pi i x_i}\). Its volume is \[ \sum_i D(e^{2\pi i x_i}) =-2\pi\sum_iJ(x_i). \tag{20} \] The gaps less than \(\pi\) put the origin inside the equatorial polygon, so these tetrahedra have disjoint interiors and positive orientations. The row equation gives angle \(2\pi\) around the internal axial edge. The outer equatorial edge in position \(i\) has dihedral angle \(2\pi x_i\); the polar edge at the intervening equatorial vertex has dihedral angle \[ \pi(1-x_{i-1}-x_i). \tag{21} \] This follows by adding the two neighboring tetrahedral angles \(\pi/2-\pi x_{i-1}\) and \(\pi/2-\pi x_i\). The anchor equations in (3) are therefore the correct numerical equatorial angle sums if those incidences are realized by face pairings. The charged coefficient metadata alone do not specify or verify all such face pairings for the original knot exterior. In particular a class \(C\) of glued polar edges must satisfy \[ \sum_{(v,i)\in C}(1-x_{v,i-1}-x_{v,i})=2, \tag{22} \] and the remaining shape and peripheral equations must be retained. No assertion that (22) follows from (3) is made here. At a block's internal pair of incidences the angle (21) depends only on its length. Between blocks it depends on their separate endpoint charges. Consequently the full clock-dependent phase (8), not only fixed-clock graph holonomy, must enter a proposed gluing comparison. Outside the chamber of (20), the algebraic entropy identity (11) and all variational results remain valid. The axial subdivision need no longer be a positive geometric subdivision. None of these positive comparisons changes the phase or declares the original cycle to pass through the absolute optimizer. The two-crossing positive-chart obstruction is avoided in the exact bridge identity, but is not resolved by assigning independent positive shapes to the original crossings. A geometric identification of (18), and a nonzero contribution to (9), remain separate tasks. ## Direct source versions The direct source formulas used in this proof were read in these versions: | Source | SHA-256 | | --- | --- | | actual_global_charged_bridge_flow.md | b444e487eab3ec0a56c40b22584837cefcbe374a137b0beeaa185116c2a81d8c | | actual_length_gauge_clock_source.md | ccc3139960cf113f97e0454a902a11dfabca15ceb0b1e12f8175dc56a2be5315 | | research_charged_block_holonomy_rate_loss.md | dfd2cae48cd534a12602670145ee09c3c959cf663e304e62896d4b47e1184b6e |

title: Local propagation of an actual charged source by a signed heat step
text: # Local propagation of an actual charged source by a signed heat step Private written analysis, 16 November 2026. The entire charged-source heat identity gives a local asymptotic transport theorem with an estimated exterior integral. A sufficiently small real power step preserves a known nonzero geometric expansion on a smaller complex charge domain. This uses the whole initial source, including its physical first normals and its global exponential growth, rather than an assumed coefficient of a formal saddle. The domain loss is essential. The output is the characteristic image of an eroded initial domain. Iteration transports the same initial set of classical angle labels; it does not supply a fresh complex neighborhood at every step. No continuation to arbitrary short fillings or to charge one is claimed. ## 1. Exact source and a global envelope For \(N\ge2\), use the full algebra and original trace \[ \mathcal A_N=\mathbb C[z]/(2T_N(z/2)+2),\qquad \phi_N=\eta N^2[z^{N-1}]\operatorname{rem},\qquad \eta=(-1)^{N-1}. \tag{1} \] The entire charged source, canonical real powers and carriers are those of the exact heat reduction: \[ C_{N,b}=\exp\!\left(\frac{\pi i b(N-1)^2}{4N}\right),\qquad \widetilde Z_N=\left(\prod_v C_{N,b_v}^{-1}\right)Z_N . \tag{2} \] At each double physical node \(c=-2\cos\tau\), its charge coupon has value \(\cos(N(1-\chi)\tau)\) and spectral first derivative \[ -\frac{N(1-\chi)\sin(N(1-\chi)\tau)}{2\sin\tau}. \tag{3} \] The odd simple node has value one. Thus all normal directions are retained. No free boundary polynomial is reduced. In one power coordinate the exact evolution is \[ \partial_b\widetilde Z_N=-\frac{i}{4\pi N}\partial_\chi^2 \widetilde Z_N . \tag{4} \] For a nonzero real step \(\delta\), put \[ v_\delta=e^{-i\,\operatorname{sgn}(\delta)\pi/4},\qquad \mathcal H_\delta f(\chi)= \sqrt{\frac N{|\delta|}}\int_{\mathbb R} e^{-\pi Nr^2/|\delta|}f(\chi+v_\delta r)\,dr . \tag{5} \] This equals the actual carrier-removed source at power \(b+\delta\) when \(f\) is that source at power \(b\). Its line may be translated by any finite complex amount. The exact identity applies coefficientwise to ordinary free boundaries and to mixed normal observations. At zero step \(\mathcal H_0\) is the identity. For the fixed finite same-index graph sources of the small-charge theorem, there are constants \(C,p,A\), uniform for powers in a fixed bounded real box, such that \[ |\widetilde Z_N(\mathbf b,\mathbf y;\mathbf u)| \le A N^p\prod_v(1+|y_v|) \exp N\!\left(C+\pi\sum_v|\Im y_v|\right). \tag{6} \] Here ordinary free spectral variables range over a fixed compact set. A fixed number of their derivatives obeys the same kind of bound. Constants depend on the fixed graph and compact set; (6) is not a filled-action estimate. Here is an elementary verification of the finite exponential constant in (6). Put \(c_a=2\cos((2a+1)\pi/N)\), with the repeated nodes retained, and write \[ S_j=\prod_{r=1}^j2\sin(\pi r/N),\qquad e_j(z)=S_j^{-2}\prod_{a<j}(c_a-z). \tag{7} \] For \(j\le N/2\), the sine chord inequality and \(j!\ge(j/e)^j\) give \[ S_j\ge(4/N)^j j!\ge e^{-N/4}. \tag{8} \] The last bound follows by minimizing \(x\log(4x/e)\) for \(0\le x\le1/2\). For \(j>N/2\), the full sine product and reflection give \(S_jS_{N-1-j}=N\), hence \(S_j\ge N2^{-N/2}\). In particular \(S_j\ge e^{-N}\) for every \(0\le j<N\). On \(|z|\le M_0\), with \(M_0\ge2\), every fixed derivative of \(e_j\) is bounded by a polynomial in \(N\) times \[ \exp N[\,2+\log(2+M_0)\,]. \tag{9} \] The same conclusion holds for a kernel \(K_N(z,w)=\sum_{j<N}e_j(z)e_j(w)\), its diagonal restriction at a loop, and fixed products of kernels. For bounded real powers the crossing values have modulus one and their first normals are \(O(N^2)\). Formula (3) contributes at most a polynomial times \((1+|\chi|)e^{\pi N|\Im\chi|}\); nonzero physical sines have polynomial reciprocals. Expanding the finitely many mixed first-normal terms in the original traces and summing their polynomially many physical labels proves (6). The odd simple node requires no derivative and satisfies the same bound. This argument also retains fixed additional polynomial coupons with comparable finite exponential bounds. For a more general compiled exterior, the local theorem below requires its actual bound (6), rather than assuming one from a geometric phase. ## 2. A quantitative one-coordinate theorem Let \(D_R=\{z:|z-z_0|<R\}\). Other charge coordinates or ordinary boundary parameters may range over a fixed compact holomorphic parameter set; all assumptions and estimates below are uniform there. Suppose the actual initial functions \(f_N\) are entire in the charge variable and satisfy \[ |f_N(z)|\le A_N(1+|z|)^p e^{N(C+\pi|\Im z|)},\qquad \log A_N=o(N), \tag{10} \] and, on a neighborhood of \(\overline D_R\), \[ f_N(z)=N^\alpha e^{NS(z)} \{a_0(z)+O_{\rm hol}(N^{-1})\},\qquad |a_0(z)|\ge a_*>0 . \tag{11} \] In (11) the error is a uniformly bounded holomorphic function times \(N^{-1}\). Suppose \(S,a_0\) are holomorphic there. Put \[ M=\sup_{\overline D_R}|S'|,\qquad L=\sup_{\overline D_R}|S''|,\qquad B=\frac{M^2+(M+\pi)^2}{2\pi}, \tag{12} \] \[ E_{\max}=\sup_{\overline D_R} \{C+\pi|\Im z|-\Re S(z)\},\qquad E_*=1+\max(0,E_{\max})+B. \tag{13} \] The positive part makes the estimates valid without a sign convention for a nonoptimal chosen envelope. **Theorem 1.** Fix \(0<\rho<R\). If \[ 0<|\delta|\le \min\left\{1,\frac{\pi}{L+1}, \frac{\pi\rho^2}{4E_*}\right\}, \tag{14} \] then \[ \Phi_\delta(z)=z+\frac{i\delta}{2\pi}S'(z) \tag{15} \] is injective on \(D_R\). On the output domain \(\Phi_\delta(D_{R-\rho})\), set \[ z=\Phi_\delta^{-1}(\chi),\qquad S_\delta(\chi)=S(z)+\frac{i\delta}{4\pi}S'(z)^2 . \tag{16} \] The actual heat evolution obeys \[ \boxed{\quad \mathcal H_\delta f_N(\chi)= N^\alpha e^{NS_\delta(\chi)} \left\{\frac{a_0(z)} {\sqrt{\,1+i\delta S''(z)/(2\pi)\,}} +O_{\rm hol}(N^{-1})\right\}. \quad} \tag{17} \] The square root is the holomorphic branch tending to one at \(\delta=0\). Its argument lies in \(|w-1|\le1/2\). The leading coefficient is nonzero. Uniformity holds for the displayed steps, and ordinary derivatives are uniform on smaller output domains. If (11) has an expansion to every fixed order, so does (17). This theorem estimates the discarded part of the actual integral. It does not assume its relative cycle already has a geometric coefficient. Applied to (4), the original crossing carrier is restored by the exact ratio \(C_{N,b+\delta}/C_{N,b}=C_{N,\delta}\). ### Exact contour, local phase and exterior estimate The bound on \(S''\) and convexity of \(D_R\) give \[ |(\Phi_\delta(z)-\Phi_\delta(w))-(z-w)| \le\frac{|\delta|L}{2\pi}|z-w| \le\frac12|z-w|. \tag{18} \] Thus (15) is injective with a regular inverse. Write \(b=z-\chi=-i\delta S'(z)/(2\pi)\). Translate the exact line in (5) to \(y=z+v_\delta r\). The translated formula is \[ \mathcal H_\delta f_N(\chi)= e^{i\,\operatorname{sgn}(\delta)\pi/4} \sqrt{\frac N{|\delta|}} \int_{z+v_\delta\mathbb R} e^{-i\pi N(y-\chi)^2/\delta}f_N(y)\,dy . \tag{19} \] For fixed \(N,\delta\), the connectors at \(r=\pm R_1\) have a negative quadratic Gaussian exponent and only linear exponential growth from (10); they tend to zero as \(R_1\to\infty\). This proves the equality before any asymptotic estimate. There are no hidden factorial or physical-grid poles. The phase on the local segment is \[ T(y)=S(y)-\frac{i\pi}{\delta}(y-\chi)^2,\qquad T'(z)=0 . \tag{20} \] For \(|r|\le\rho\), its whole segment stays in \(D_R\), and \[ \Re\{T(z+v_\delta r)-T(z)\} \le-\frac{\pi}{|\delta|}r^2+\frac L2r^2 \le-\frac{\pi}{2|\delta|}r^2 . \tag{21} \] Also \(T(z)=S_\delta(\chi)\). For \(|r|\ge\rho\), use the global initial bound (10). The quadratic kernel, its shifted linear term, and the source type give the following exponential upper bound, before polynomial factors: \[ C+\pi|\Im z|+\frac{|\delta|M^2}{4\pi} +(M+\pi)|r|-\frac{\pi r^2}{|\delta|}. \tag{22} \] In particular the growth of the source on the Fresnel ray has not been dropped: \(\pi|\Im(v_\delta r)|\le\pi|r|\). Young's inequality bounds the linear term by \[ (M+\pi)|r|\le \frac{\pi r^2}{2|\delta|} +\frac{|\delta|(M+\pi)^2}{2\pi}. \tag{23} \] Since \(\left|\Re\{-i\pi b^2/\delta\}\right| \le|\delta|M^2/(4\pi)\), the tail exponent relative to \(\Re S_\delta(\chi)\) is at most \[ \boxed{\quad E_{\max}+|\delta|B-\frac{\pi r^2}{2|\delta|}. \quad} \tag{24} \] At \(|r|\ge\rho\), (14) makes this less than \(-1\). Integrating the polynomial factors preserves a strict gap: for fixed \(\rho>0\), the elementary Gaussian tail inequality gives a polynomial prefactor, uniformly for \(0<|\delta|\le1\). For example, write \(|r|=\rho+s\), use \(r^2\ge\rho^2+2\rho s\), and integrate each fixed polynomial in \(s\). The factor \(\sqrt{N/|\delta|}\) in (19) is absorbed by the resulting factors \(|\delta|/N\). The \(A_N=e^{o(N)}\) factor in (10) is harmless. Hence the exterior is \[ N^\alpha e^{N\Re S_\delta(\chi)}O(e^{-N/2}), \tag{25} \] after enlarging the threshold in \(N\). The constants can depend on \(\rho\) and the fixed parameter set, but not on the sign of \(\delta\). On the local segment insert (11), use (21), and rescale \(r=\sqrt{|\delta|/N}\,u\). The oriented factors in (19) satisfy \(e^{i\,\operatorname{sgn}(\delta)\pi/4}v_\delta=1\). The Gaussian multiplier is exactly \[ \left(1-\frac{|\delta|v_\delta^2}{2\pi}S''(z)\right)^{-1/2} =\left(1+\frac{i\delta}{2\pi}S''(z)\right)^{-1/2}. \tag{26} \] On the inner segment \(|r|\le\rho/2\), Cauchy's estimates on the reserved \(\rho\)-discs bound the required derivatives uniformly. The remaining local annulus has the strict quadratic gap (21). The odd Taylor terms integrate to zero on the symmetric inner segment; the remaining Taylor errors have relative order \(N^{-1}\), uniformly for the steps in (14). Analyticity on a neighborhood of the closed initial disc supplies all needed bounded derivatives. The holomorphic initial remainder contributes the same error order. Further Taylor terms give the all-order assertion. Cauchy's formula on smaller output domains gives the derivative statement. This proves Theorem 1. For several charge coordinates, apply the theorem successively in the changed coordinates, treating the others as compact holomorphic parameters. Every step is the exact original source, and every discarded tail has its own bound (24). This covers mixed signs and unchanged zero-step coordinates. It is not an instruction to replace the full source by a product of scalar observations. ## 3. The small-charge initializer has a complex neighborhood The frozen small-charge source theorem is stated on the physical charge lattice in the compact real box \[ [1/4000,1/2000]^I . \tag{27} \] For its specified fixed graph, fixed signed powers and complete outside angles, its proof also gives a uniform holomorphic initializer for the entire coupon family (3) on a sufficiently small fixed complex neighborhood of (27). This assertion does not follow merely from agreement on increasingly fine lattices. The exact even-coupon trace identity continues to complex \(\chi\) by the full physical jets, as proved in the dominant-saddle source note, Section 9. In the small-charge proof retain its physical-row decomposition and its actual mixed horizontal/vertical contours. At a fixed real charge in (27), all noncentral terms have uniform strict gaps, and every retained angular contour is bounded. Moving the charges by at most \(\varepsilon\) changes each coupon exponential bound by at most \(e^{C_1N\varepsilon}\), with a fixed constant for this finite graph. The required normal derivatives cost polynomial factors. The same bound applies to removed physical rows; their angles lie in \([-\pi,\pi]\). Explicitly, \[ |\cos(N(1-\chi)\tau)|\le e^{\pi N|\Im\chi|}, \qquad |\partial_\tau\cos(N(1-\chi)\tau)| \le N|1-\chi|e^{\pi N|\Im\chi|}. \] The first spectral normals add only the already retained polynomial reciprocal of \(\sin\tau\); the odd simple node remains a value term. Choose \(\varepsilon>0\) below the finitely many gap margins divided by the resulting constants. The mixed-current and removed-row gaps then remain strict relative to the continued selected action. The central saddle moves holomorphically and stays in the same pole-free thin rectangle. A small contour displacement through it is legitimate there, with the connecting faces still in the strict-gap region. The nonzero sine factors, edge amplitudes and Gaussian determinant remain nonzero after one further shrinkage. The exact companion and alias estimates also persist because the real box is separated from both charge endpoints and its heights are uniformly positive. Compactness of (27) supplies one fixed complex neighborhood. The original proof's Taylor expansion on these contours gives uniform holomorphic errors to every fixed order there, through both level parities. Thus this is an actual initializer for Theorem 1. Its radius may depend on the fixed graph and powers. No lower bound independent of that data or extension to charge one is asserted. The same local conclusion holds uniformly on a fixed bounded real-power box after using the canonical real powers. The physical values and normals have the uniform bounds used in (6); the small-charge fixed-point denominators obey \(|n_v+iC_v|\ge\sqrt{n_v^2+d_v^2}-d_v/30000\) for real \(n_v\) as well. The signed vertical-side estimates use only \(n_v\operatorname{sgn}(n_v)=|n_v|\), not integrality. One may retain either side at zero power. The full real-power trace identity keeps its endpoint currents. These observations give the same compactness argument without assigning noninteger powers an additional topological meaning. ## 4. Domain accounting under iteration The local theorem is an effective propagation result, but it has two explicit restrictions. First, suppose a regular phase has initial derivative \(t_0(\zeta)=iS_0'(\zeta)\). The classical heat characteristic is \[ \chi_s=\Phi_s(\zeta) =\zeta+\frac{s}{2\pi}t_0(\zeta). \tag{28} \] Indeed differentiating (16) gives \(S_{\delta,\chi}(\Phi_\delta(\zeta))=S'(\zeta)\). Thus the angle is constant along the characteristic. The maps for successive steps compose to (28) with the total power change. In several coordinates the corresponding formula is \[ \boldsymbol\chi_{\mathbf n} =\boldsymbol\zeta+ \frac1{2\pi}\operatorname{diag}(\mathbf n-\mathbf b) \mathbf t_0(\boldsymbol\zeta). \tag{29} \] The coordinate flows commute wherever these charts are regular. Each use of Theorem 1 requires the input saddle to lie inside the previously certified complex domain with a reserved margin. Consequently this procedure transports a subset of the initial angle labels. Recentring overlapping output discs does not add initial labels that were not already certified. This statement concerns the present local procedure, not an impossibility theorem for analytic continuation by other source estimates. Second, the explicit envelope recipe (14) spends a quadratic time budget. For a one-coordinate nested-disc certificate, suppose the characteristic charts extend injectively to neighborhoods of the closed initial-label discs and their inverses have a common Lipschitz bound \(K\ge1\). If these discs have radii \(R_j\), reserve a charge margin \(\rho_j=(R_j-R_{j+1})/K\). It lies inside the preceding charge image: the inverse Lipschitz bound gives that lower bound on the distance to its boundary. With a common chosen \(E_*\), the sufficient steps in (14) obey \[ \sum_j|\delta_j| \le\frac{\pi}{4E_*}\sum_j\rho_j^2 \le\frac{\pi}{4E_*K^2}(R_0-R_{\rm final})^2 . \tag{30} \] This is the limitation of that stated conservative certificate, not a necessary inequality for the actual source or for all possible contour estimates. Subdivision into more steps does not increase its guaranteed total time. If one has sharper exterior information than (10), a better domain estimate may be possible. Neither positivity of a local Hessian nor a fixed global envelope alone supplies that sharper information. For a fixed unit-charge positive point \(t^*=s-iH\), \(H>0\), the initial charge at any real base power \(b\) is \[ y_b=1-\frac{(n-b)t^*}{2\pi}. \tag{31} \] Successive real-power steps give the same initial label (31). It is real only if \(b=n\), in which case it is one. For a real initializer interval \([\alpha,\beta]\), \(\beta<1\), orthogonal projection onto this line gives exactly \[ \inf_{\substack{b\in\mathbb R\\x\in[\alpha,\beta]}}|y_b-x| =(1-\beta)\frac{H}{|t^*|}>0 . \tag{32} \] The complex neighborhood of Section 3 must actually contain the required label; its existence alone does not establish this. Formula (32) does not rule out containment in a sufficiently large proved neighborhood, nor does it rule out a different continuation. The new conclusion is therefore local and quantitative: a known actual complex initializer admits a nonzero signed heat step with an explicitly bounded whole-source exterior. Establishing enough initial-label coverage or replenishing the complex domain to reach every arbitrary short partial filling remains a separate problem. ## Direct sources and author readback - [Exact entire charged-source heat reduction](research_entire_charged_source_heat_reduction.md): faithful charge space, all physical normals, exact Gaussian identity and finite translated contours. SHA256 33213425be9cac699860a48b23830399c82cd89bea3140cc776274aafe115fba. - [Actual small-charge initializer](research_small_charge_path_source.md): complete original graph source, strict alias/current/removed-row estimates, nonzero local amplitude and all-order expansion. SHA256 c6d0ce2a4ecf1412aa3752cb8a94c6933bb47acab5d96d879c6f1b17b2db2a90. - [Canonical real-power source](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_real_power_source_transport.md): real physical value/normal bounds, full trace and endpoint currents for noninteger powers. SHA256 7dac43d1a5fac6b4602a3aab12bfe977cb42a61b36d40a2fb8517e29566df8ea. - [Entire coupons and continuation scope](research_dominant_saddle_transport.md): Section 9, exact complex coupon trace family and its original current scope. SHA256 413940497a23e884d726b91f9c0ebc01994fef8216811ed2c6fb0838fc80bb04. Only written mathematics and text/hash inspection are used. No mathematical code, numerical computation, tests or compilation were run. The author read the entire final proof. The small-charge source was read in full in this sequence; matching complete reads of the other three sources were retained, their used implications reread, and all four pinned versions verified. Independent peer and root review are required before adoption.

title: Physical charge pressure and its geometric excess
text:
# Physical charge pressure and its geometric excess Private written proof, 16 November 2026. The whole original charged source has a graph-dependent exponential envelope sharper than a constant plus its exponential type. All physical first normals are included. The envelope is the pressure of the positive physical kernel values, and does not depend on the real crossing powers. At a supplied positive complex-charge geometric point its excess over the selected zero-power action is an explicit positive convex-energy difference. The resulting Fresnel-tail bound retains that excess rather than replacing the physical pressure by the filled action. ## 1. The original source and its real pressure Fix a finite original circle tree, a nonempty selected set \(I\), and all edges incident to \(I\), counted once. Write \(k=|I|\) and \(m\) for the number of these edges. Every selected vertex has positive degree. Outside endpoints of these edges are fixed at their complete angle \(0\), hence spectral value \(-2\). This is the specified complete-boundary source. Edges having neither endpoint in \(I\) are not included; their independent factors in a larger contraction must be restored. No arbitrary exterior is discarded.
