Put \(D=N-1\), \(\eta=(-1)^D\), and \[  egin{gathered} c_j=2\cos((2j+1)\pi/N),\qquad S_r=\prod_{
u=1}^r2\sin(\pi
u/N),\ e_r(z)=S_r^{-2}\prod_{
u<r}(c_
u-z),\qquad K_N(z,w)=\sum_{r=0}^{D}e_r(z)e_r(w),\ P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2,\qquad \phi_N(f)=\eta N^2[z^D]\operatorname{rem}_{P_N}f . 	ag{1} \end{gathered} \] The distinct physical roots have angles \[ 	au_j=\pi(D-2j)/N,\qquad c_j=-2\cos	au_j,\qquad 0\le j\le\lfloor D/2floor . 	ag{2} \] Every \(	au_j>0\) represents a double root; at odd \(N\) the last angle is zero and represents the simple root \(-2\). The full trace is \[ \phi_N(f)=\eta\sum_{	au_j>0} \{4\sin^2	au_j\,f'(c_j)-c_jf(c_j)\} +\mathbf1_{N\ {m odd}}f(-2). 	ag{3} \] Use the canonical real-power element \(R_n\) and entire charge coupon \[  egin{aligned} C_\chi(c_j)&=\cos(N(1-\chi)	au_j),\ C_\chi'(c_j)&=- rac{N(1-\chi)}{2\sin	au_j} \sin(N(1-\chi)	au_j),\qquad 	au_j>0,\ C_\chi(-2)&=1\quad(N\ {m odd}). \end{aligned} 	ag{4} \] For real \(n\), the physical values of \(R_n\) have modulus one and its first normals have polynomial bounds uniform on bounded real power intervals. At integral \(n\) it is the original signed crossing power. Define \[ Z_N(\mathbf n, oldsymbol\chi)=\phi_N^{\otimes I} \left[\prod_{e=vw}K_N(z_v,z_w) \prod_{v\in I}R_{n_v}(z_v)C_{\chi_v}(z_v)ight]. 	ag{5} \] The exact carriers \(C_{N,n}=\exp(\pi i nD^2/(4N))\) have modulus one for real \(n\); all bounds also apply to \(\widetilde Z_N=(\prod_vC_{N,n_v}^{-1})Z_N\). Let \(\psi(t,u)\) be the canonical original edge action and \(M_\infty=\psi(0,0)\). On \((-\pi,\pi)^2\) it is real and separately even, and extends continuously to the closed real square. Set \[ W(\mathbf s)=\sum_{e=vw}\psi(s_v,s_w),\qquad s_b=0\ (b
otin I), \qquad \mathcal P(\mathbf b)=\max_{\mathbf s\in[-\pi,\pi]^I} \{W(\mathbf s)+\mathbf b\cdot\mathbf s\}. 	ag{6} \] This finite convex function is even in every \(b_v\), with \[ |\mathcal P(\mathbf b)-\mathcal P(\mathbf b')| \le\pi\|\mathbf b-\mathbf b'\|_1 . 	ag{7} \] All included outside-edge constants occur in \(W\); in particular \(W(\mathbf0)=mM_\infty\). The same notation \(W(\mathbf t)=\sum_e\psi(t_v,t_w)\) denotes its canonical holomorphic extension on the original positive edge chart, with the complete logarithmic branches retained. **Theorem 1.** For a fixed graph and bounded real power box, constants \(C,a\) independent of \(N\), its parity, and \( oldsymbol\chi\) satisfy \[ |Z_N(\mathbf n, oldsymbol\chi)| \le C N^a\prod_{v\in I}(1+|\chi_v|) e^{N\mathcal P(\operatorname{Im} oldsymbol\chi)}. 	ag{8} \] Every repeated-root normal and every mixed normal from the original tensor trace is retained. Its positive physical partition \[ \mathcal M_N(\mathbf b)=\sum_{\mathbf j} \prod_{e=vw}K_N(c_{j_v},c_{j_w}) e^{N\sum_{v\in I}|b_v|	au_{j_v}}, \qquad c_{j_b}=-2\ (b
otin I), 	ag{9} \] has the sharp rate \[ \lim_{N	o\infty}N^{-1}\log\mathcal M_N(\mathbf b) =\mathcal P(\mathbf b). 	ag{10} \] This is a rate for (9), not for the signed scalar (5). **Proof.** At a physical root, \[ e_r(c_j)>0\ (0\le r\le j),\qquad e_r(c_j)=0\ (r>j). 	ag{11} \] Also \(e_r(-2)\ge0\), so every kernel value in (9) is at least one. The archived full-normal identities give \[  egin{aligned} |K_z(c_j,w)|&\le N^{11}K_N(c_j,w) &&(-2\le w\le c_0,\ c_j	ext{ double}),\ |\partial_z\partial_w\log K_N(c_j,c_l)|&\le N^{16} &&(c_j,c_l	ext{ double}),\ |K_{zw}(c_j,c_l)|&\le(N^{16}+N^{22})K_N(c_j,c_l). \end{aligned} 	ag{12} \] These are full polynomial derivative identities, not derivatives of the terminating values (11). At odd simple roots only evaluation is required, and the first bound handles the other endpoint. The same bound handles outside endpoints \(-2\). Expand (3) by Leibniz at every vertex. Each edge receives at most one derivative at either selected endpoint, and there are only a fixed number of derivative placements per assignment. Thus (12) costs a fixed polynomial relative to the positive kernel product. Crossing normals also have polynomial cost. Since \(N	au_j=\pi D-2\pi j\) and \(\sin	au_j\ge2/N\) at double roots, \[ |C_\chi(c_j)|\le e^{N|\operatorname{Im}\chi|	au_j},\qquad |C_\chi'(c_j)|\le C N^2(1+|\chi|) e^{N|\operatorname{Im}\chi|	au_j}. 	ag{13} \] The finite \(N=2\) case is absorbed in the constant. Hence \[ |Z_N|\le C N^{a_0}\prod_v(1+|\chi_v|) \mathcal M_N(\operatorname{Im} oldsymbol\chi). 	ag{14} \] For the real action, use the continuous primitives and entropy \[  egin{gathered} J(x)=\int_0^x\log(2\sin\pi r)\,dr,\qquad L(x)=\int_0^x\log|2\cos\pi r|\,dr,\ V_t(x)=L(x+t/(2\pi))+L(x-t/(2\pi))-2J(x). 	ag{15} \end{gathered} \] The uniform real Newton estimate is \[ |e_r(-2\cos t)|\le C N^a e^{NV_t(r/N)}. 	ag{16} \] It follows from the shifted midpoint logarithmic sum with uniform \(O(\log N)\) upper error and the two-sided sine-factorial estimate; zero samples only improve the upper bound. For \(0\le t,u<\pi\), the function \(V_t(x)+V_u(x)\) is strictly concave on \[ 0<x<(\pi-\max(t,u))/(2\pi). 	ag{17} \] Indeed, with \(C_x=\cos(2\pi x)\), its derivative is \[ \log rac{(C_x+\cos t)(C_x+\cos u)}{(1-C_x)^2}. 	ag{18} \] This decreases from \(+\infty\) to \(-\infty\). Its unique maximum is \[ x_*=\pi^{-1}\arctan(1/q),\qquad q=\sqrt{1+	an^2(t/2)+	an^2(u/2)}>0, 	ag{19} \] and its value is \(\psi(t,u)\) with the original complete constant. This is the real restriction of the canonical unsummed-wire critical-value identity. Every actual nonzero term (11) lies inside the closed version of (17); its cutoff is smaller by \(1/(2N)\). Thus \[ K_N(c_j,c_l)\le C N^{a_1}e^{N\psi(	au_j,	au_l)} 	ag{20} \] uniformly, also with \(u=0\) at outside endpoints. Boundary limits follow by continuity. There are polynomially many physical assignments, so (6), (9), and (20) prove (8) and the upper half of (10). For the lower half, first fix any real angles strictly inside the box and approximate their absolute values by the physical angles (2). For every edge, an integer \(r\) nearest (19) lies in both physical supports for large \(N\). Two-sided product estimates on this strict region give that positive term rate \(\psi(t,u)\). The corresponding single assignment in (9) therefore has rate \(W(\mathbf s)+\sum_v|b_v||s_v|\). The continuous closed-box maximum can be approximated by interior points, and separate evenness chooses their signs. Taking the supremum proves the lower limit. Both parity grids approximate the same points. This positive partition argument uses no normal lower bound. \(\square\) ## 2. The exact excess at a positive target Suppose the canonical positive original chart contains \[ t_v=s_v+i h_v,\qquad r_{v,e}=k_{v,e}+i g_{v,e}, \qquad t_b=0\ (b
otin I). 	ag{21} \] At zero crossing powers define its induced charge by \[ P_{0,v}(t):=\sum_{e
i v}r_{v,e}=-\pi i y_v,\qquad y_v=A_v+iB_v . 	ag{22} \] Thus \(\sum_e g_{v,e}=-\pi A_v\) and \(\sum_e k_{v,e}=\pi B_v\), with the complete original logarithmic periods. Its selected classical critical action is \[ S_0(\mathbf y)=W(\mathbf t)-i\mathbf y\cdot\mathbf t . 	ag{23} \] No quantum asymptotic at this charge is assumed. For an oriented edge \(e=(v,w)\), put \[  egin{array}{ll} a_P=s_v/4-g_{w,e}/2,&a_Q=s_v/4+g_{w,e}/2,\ b_P=g_{v,e}/2+s_w/4,&b_Q=g_{v,e}/2-s_w/4 . \end{array} 	ag{24} \] All four coordinates lie in \((-\pi/4,\pi/4)\). The square energy \(E_\square(0,0)=0\) has derivatives \[ (E_\square)_a=	frac12\operatorname{arsinh}(	an(2a)\cos(2b)), \qquad (E_\square)_b=	frac12\operatorname{arsinh}(	an(2b)\cos(2a)). 	ag{25} \] It is even in each variable, has positive definite Hessian, and extends continuously and convexly to its closed square. Define \[ E_e=E_\square(a_P,b_P)+E_\square(a_Q,b_Q),\qquad \mathcal E(\mathbf s,\mathbf g)=4\sum_eE_e . 	ag{26} \] The outside work term is zero here because the prescribed outside imaginary angles are zero. It is not dropped for arbitrary complex outside data. **Theorem 2.** At every supplied point (21)--(22), \[  egin{split} \mathcal P(\mathbf B)-\operatorname{Re}S_0(\mathbf A+i\mathbf B) ={}& rac{\mathcal E(\mathbf s,\mathbf g) -\mathcal E(\mathbf s,\mathbf0)}{\pi}\ &+\mathcal P(\mathbf B)-W(\mathbf s)-\mathbf B\cdot\mathbf s . \end{split} 	ag{27} \] Both terms on the right are nonnegative, and the first is positive if some \(h_v
e0\). At a supplied positive target, \(\mathbf A=0\) if and only if every \(h_v=0\); in that case both terms vanish. Hence the excess is strictly positive at every nonreal positive target, uniformly on compact sets avoiding the real locus. **Proof.** The globally calibrated edge identity is \[ \pi\operatorname{Re}\psi(t_v,t_w)+4E_e -g_{v,e}h_v-g_{w,e}h_w=\pi M_\infty . 	ag{28} \] Sum it and use (22), retaining the real part of the charge term: \[ \operatorname{Re}S_0=mM_\infty-\mathcal E(\mathbf s,\mathbf g)/\pi +\mathbf B\cdot\mathbf s . 	ag{29} \] At real angles all \(g\) vanish, so \[ W(\mathbf s)=mM_\infty-\mathcal E(\mathbf s,\mathbf0)/\pi . 	ag{30} \] This proves (27), including all outside-edge constants. Reverse every incidence \(g\), keeping \(\mathbf s\) fixed. On each edge the pairs (24) transform as \[ (a_P,b_P)\mapsto(a_Q,-b_Q),\qquad (a_Q,b_Q)\mapsto(a_P,-b_P). 	ag{31} \] Thus \(\mathcal E(\mathbf s,-\mathbf g)=\mathcal E(\mathbf s,\mathbf g)\). The segment \((\mathbf s,\lambda\mathbf g)\), \(-1\le\lambda\le1\), stays strictly inside the angle body, whose inequalities are \[ |s_v|+2|g_{w,e}|<\pi,\qquad |s_w|+2|g_{v,e}|<\pi. 	ag{32} \] Strict Hessian convexity gives a positive energy difference unless \(\mathbf g=0\), explicitly \[ \mathcal E(\mathbf s,\mathbf g)-\mathcal E(\mathbf s,\mathbf0) =\int_0^1(1-\lambda)\, \mathbf g^{\mathsf T}\mathcal E_{gg} (\mathbf s,\lambda\mathbf g)\mathbf g\,d\lambda . 	ag{33} \] If \(\mathbf g=0\), the inverse square formulas give all matched \(h_v=0\). The second term in (27) is nonnegative by (6). The target is an interior stationary point, hence the unique global minimizer, of \[ \mathcal E-\pi\mathbf B\cdot\mathbf s \quad	ext{subject to}\quad \sum_e g_{v,e}=-\pi A_v . 	ag{34} \] Its incidence multipliers are the original \(h_v\), and its \(\mathbf s\)-equations are the real parts of (22). Strict convexity compares it strictly with boundary assignments as well. When \(\mathbf A=0\), its reflected point and their midpoint \((\mathbf s,\mathbf0)\) are feasible. Strict convexity forces \(\mathbf g=0\), hence \(\mathbf h=0\). Conversely real original angles have real returns, giving \(\mathbf A=0\). In that case (34), restricted to \(\mathbf g=0\), says that \(\mathbf s\) maximizes (6), so the second term vanishes too. Continuity and (33) prove compact uniformity. \(\square\) Equivalently, on the compact weak angle body define \[ \mathfrak m(\mathbf A,\mathbf B) =\min_{\sum_e g_{v,e}=-\pi A_v} \{\mathcal E-\pi\mathbf B\cdot\mathbf s\} 	ag{35} \] when this set is nonempty. Reflection gives \(\mathfrak m(\mathbf A,\mathbf B)=\mathfrak m(-\mathbf A,\mathbf B)\). Convex averaging allows the zero-charge minimum to be taken at \(\mathbf g=0\). At the supplied positive target, \[ \mathcal P(\mathbf B)-\operatorname{Re}S_0 =\{\mathfrak m(\mathbf A,\mathbf B) -\mathfrak m(\mathbf0,\mathbf B)\}/\pi . 	ag{36} \] This uses the original energy and charge rows, without changing any filling or peripheral marking. ## 3. The exact pressure-sensitive Fresnel tail Take the entire actual initial function \(f_N( oldsymbol\chi)=\widetilde Z_N(\mathbf n, oldsymbol\chi)\). Change the real powers by nonzero \(\delta_j\) in \(J\subset I\), and let \(E_J\) insert these coordinates into the full charge vector. Put \[ v_j=e^{-i\,\operatorname{sgn}(\delta_j)\pi/4}. 	ag{37} \] The exact heat representation uses product lines parallel to \(v_j\). Entirety and finite exponential type allow arbitrary finite translations; all normal data and closing operations are already combined in \(f_N\). For a holomorphic reference phase \(S\) near \( oldsymbol\zeta\), put \(a_j=\partial_jS( oldsymbol\zeta)\) and choose \[ \chi_j=\zeta_j+i\delta_j a_j/(2\pi)\quad(j\in J),\qquad \chi_j=\zeta_j\quad(j
otin J). 	ag{38} \] Translate to \(\mathbf y= oldsymbol\zeta+E_J(v_jr_j)\) and set \[ T_*=S( oldsymbol\zeta)+\sum_{j\in J}i\delta_j a_j^2/(4\pi). 	ag{39} \] Define \[  egin{split} \mathcal B_\delta(\mathbf r; oldsymbol\zeta) ={}&\mathcal P igl(\operatorname{Im} oldsymbol\zeta+ \operatorname{Im}E_J(v_jr_j) igr) -\operatorname{Re}S( oldsymbol\zeta)\ &-\operatorname{Re}\sum_j a_jv_jr_j -\pi\sum_jr_j^2/|\delta_j|. \end{split} 	ag{40} \] **Proposition 3.** Apart from fixed polynomial prefactors in \(N\) and \(\mathbf r\), the absolute translated heat integrand divided by \(e^{N\operatorname{Re}T_*}\) is at most \(e^{N\mathcal B_\delta}\). If a closed tail region satisfies \(\sup\mathcal B_\delta\le-\kappa<0\), its actual contribution is \[ O igl(N^a e^{N(\operatorname{Re}T_*-\kappa/2)} igr). 	ag{41} \] The assertion is uniform on compact parameter sets with this strict gap, with the nonzero heat steps fixed away from zero. **Proof.** The Gaussian exponent is \(-i\pi\sum_j(y_j-\chi_j)^2/\delta_j\). Its difference from its value at \( oldsymbol\zeta\) is exactly \[ -\sum_j a_jv_jr_j-\pi\sum_jr_j^2/|\delta_j|. 	ag{42} \] Its constant is the second term of (39) and cancels in the relative bound. Apply Theorem 1 at \(\mathbf y\) to obtain (40). By (7), \(\mathcal B_\delta\le C_0+C_1|\mathbf r|-c|\mathbf r|^2\). Split the tail into a fixed compact part and its complement; the quadratic loss supplies an integrable Gaussian outside. The strict supremum bound then gives (41), absorbing polynomial factors. \(\square\) At a nonreal positive zero-power target, Theorem 2 gives \[ \mathcal B_\delta(\mathbf0; oldsymbol\zeta) =\mathcal P(\operatorname{Im} oldsymbol\zeta) -\operatorname{Re}S_0( oldsymbol\zeta)>0. 	ag{43} \] The sharper envelope therefore cannot by itself certify the local target term or replace a known complex initializer. It can estimate discarded parts once (40) is negative there. An actual nonzero local expansion, with its original coefficient, remains necessary on the retained region. No enlargement of its certified angle-label set, filled geometric rate, or arbitrary-short-filling noncancellation is proved. Complementary-index Conway edges and an arbitrary complex uncontracted exterior are not silently included in (5). ## Pinned direct sources * notes/research_all_color_path_normal_bound.md, SHA256 08f8932c2cdee4c7afadbb4db3cd85480603f8adb4c936ce29a5517b2d4799c7: the full polynomial normal decomposition and Lemma 5's first and mixed-normal bounds, including the original endpoint source. * notes/research_three_crossing_real_period_newton_bound.md, SHA256 8759b9d7784d0c96590410969b172c95a697d86261936fd1e09201d9d12dcc2e: the uniform all-color real Newton entropy (16). * notes/research_unsummed_network_phase_coercivity.md, SHA256 b5441bb508d3ffad3274e38dda2d6aeb099d08ae2ab043a0d12c25234e4a1e1e: the same-index wire phase and its canonical critical value \(\psi\), equations (25)--(28), without a global quantum estimate. * notes/research_positive_filling_convex_variation.md, SHA256 2777b2bcb149d64a79757ba64ccb16be5438cf37ce820ad50c5f532afd8fc6c0: the square energy, original incidence coordinates, Hessian convexity, continuous extension, and variational equations. * notes/research_positive_period_inverse_descent.md, SHA256 b9b5c3d61c704700e9431315cf50591c921ebeb95becdf6a52877606bdbc4565: the calibrated edge energy/action identity and complete constant. * notes/research_entire_charged_source_heat_reduction.md, SHA256 33213425be9cac699860a48b23830399c82cd89bea3140cc776274aafe115fba: the exact full-Hermite real-power/coupon source, carriers, entire Gaussian transform, and finite line translations. The polynomial cost of physical normals and uniform real Newton entropy are prior results. The additions are their joint pressure bound, its exact geometric excess, and the pressure-sensitive entire-source tail functional. Only written proofs, source-text reads, and file hashes were used. title: Closing phases and the limits of the charged variational bound
text: # Closing phases and the limits of the charged variational bound Private written deduction, 14 November 2026. Only written identities are used. No numerical calculation, test, or frozen-file change is part of this argument. The phase-sensitive charged upper bound retains substantial cancellation inside proper-length blocks. It does not retain all closing or clock cancellation. This can be seen in the exact Markov operation, which is a scalar operator before any exterior is attached. The calculation below identifies the missing information and the corresponding stationary equations. It is not a counterexample to a volume conjecture or to a bound restricted to a separately specified reduced hyperbolic presentation. ## 1. Full-length closing blocks are invisible to the limiting arc loss Use the functions from [the charged block theorem](research_charged_block_holonomy_rate_loss.md): \[ I_{\lambda,\rho}(\theta)=\frac1{2\pi} \int_{-\pi\lambda}^{\pi\lambda} \log|1+\rho e^{i(\theta+s)}|\,ds. \] For every \(\rho>0\), \[ I_{1,\rho}(\theta)=\log\max(1,\rho),\qquad I_{0,\rho}(\theta)=0. \tag{1} \] The first identity follows by integrating the logarithmic series for \(\rho<1\), applying inversion for \(\rho>1\), and taking the integrable limit at one. In particular both endpoint lengths have zero angular loss at every phase. Call a block proper when \(0<\lambda_e<1\). If the graph of proper blocks is a forest, vertex phases can align every proper block simultaneously: choose a phase at one vertex in each tree and propagate along its edges. All other arc terms are independent of phase by (1). Therefore \[ \max_{\vartheta}\sum_e I_{\lambda_e,r_v/r_u}(\omega_e+\vartheta_v-\vartheta_u) =\sum_e I_{\lambda_e,r_v/r_u}(0) \tag{2} \] at every radius. More generally the same statement holds if the proper-block connection is flat. A cycle using a full-length closing block can have nontrivial holonomy without changing (2). This is a structural limitation of the limiting functional, not an omitted term in its proof. Every finite closing block and its pivot are still present in the exact source. Its length is \(N-1\), whose normalized limit is one. That limit can lose an exact root zero of a Fourier coefficient while correctly retaining the logarithmic upper bound on the polynomial's modulus. ## 2. The Markov crossing is scalar before exterior contraction Put \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), and \(A_N=q^{-1/2}\), with the specified exponential square root. In the external basis let \(K_{\rm ext}e_i=q^{2i-d}e_i\). The original crossings satisfy \[ \begin{split} \operatorname{Tr}_2[(I\otimes K_{\rm ext})R_{{\rm ext},+}] &=q^{-d-d^2/2}I,\\ \operatorname{Tr}_2[(I\otimes K_{\rm ext})R_{{\rm ext},-}] &=q^{d+d^2/2}I. \tag{3} \end{split} \] Here is a finite operator proof, with the boundary indices retained. The [regular crossing adapter](research_rivin_jones_local_crossing_adapter.md) identifies the external crossings with the physical braided intertwiners of opposite sign and transports \(K_{\rm ext}\) to the physical \(K\). The partial-trace computation in [the prescribed-cut theorem](research_rivin_jones_prescribed_cut_and_hermite_recovery.md), Section 2, proves directly that the \(K\)-weighted partial trace of such an intertwiner commutes with \(E,F,K\). Its proof uses the displayed coproducts and cyclicity only in the traced factor. The physical \(K\) has distinct eigenvalues and the adjacent lowering arrows are nonzero. Hence this partial trace is scalar. The scalar can be evaluated in a single boundary coordinate. The external positive crossing sends \((i,j)\) to \((j+t,i-t)\). When the retained input is \(i=0\), the trace forces \(t=j=0\). The crossing entry is \(A_N^{d^2}\), and the pivot is \(q^{-d}\), giving the first line of (3). The negative crossing sends \((i,j)\) to \((j-t,i+t)\). At retained input \(i=d\), the trace forces \(j=d,t=0\). Its crossing entry is \(A_N^{-d^2}\), and its pivot is \(q^d\), giving the second line. Consequently an arbitrary exterior operator acting on the retained heads can be left in place: tracing the added head replaces its Markov crossing by the corresponding scalar in (3). No assumption that the exterior is scalar, or that its marked row may be averaged, is needed for this local replacement. In the original physical convention \(g=K/s\), \(x=q^d=-q^{-1}\), \(s=x^N\), and \(\kappa=q^{d^2/2}\), a positive physical crossing has scalar \(\kappa x/s\). Its prescribed framing cancels this unit factor. ## 3. Exact clock cancellation in the closed Markov operation The same operation can be inspected in the original charged representation, without changing its clocks. Consider the positive physical Markov crossing with its original two closing adapters. Write \(X\) for its over-input, \(Z\) for its over-output, and \(Y\) for its under-input. The under-output is \(xQ^{-h}Y\), where \(Q=q^2\), \(0\le h\le d\). The two crossing blocks have lengths \(d-h,h\); their directed anchor pairs are \(X\to Y\) and \(Y\to Z\). The two closures are \(Y\to X\) and \(Z\to Y\), each of length \(d\). The exact gains, obtained from equations (7),(17),(18) of [the charged source](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_global_charged_bridge_flow.md), are \[ w_0=q^{d-h},\qquad w_1=q^{h-d},\qquad w_A=q^{2h-d},\qquad w_B=q^{-2}. \tag{4} \] The last gain is the actual pivot. Let \(a,b\) be the head charges of the two crossing blocks. Conservation forces the closing head charges to be \(h+a,b\), respectively. All \(0\le a\le d-h\) and \(0\le b\le h\) are admissible. Closing block coefficients have magnitude one. Apart from the specified unit factors independent of \(a,b\), the entire fixed-clock coefficient is therefore \[ w_A^h B_{d-h,N}(w_0w_A)B_{h,N}(w_1w_B) =w_A^h B_{d-h,N}(q^h)B_{h,N}(-q^{h-1}). \tag{5} \] This is a sum over the complete source support, not a selected subset. The finite product formula gives \[ \begin{split} B_{h,N}(-q^{h-1})&=\prod_{r=0}^{h-1}(1-Q^r),\\ B_{d-h,N}(q^h)&=\prod_{r=h+1}^{d}(1-Q^r). \end{split} \tag{6} \] Thus every \(h\ge1\) coefficient vanishes exactly. At \(h=0\) the second product in (6) is \((Q;Q)_d=N\), and the first is one. Restoring \(\chi_N/N\) and the original unit factors gives the scalar \(\chi_N\kappa x/s\), in agreement with (3). All levels and both parities are included. The cancellation occurs already inside a fixed nonzero clock sector; it need not wait for the final sum over clocks. Nevertheless the limiting upper functional in [the angle-optimization theorem](research_charged_source_angle_optimization.md) has strictly positive value for this same presentation. Write \(t=h/N\) in the limit and \[ b_\lambda(y)=I_{\lambda,e^y}(0). \] The proper blocks form a path, so (2) applies. Set the \(X\) radius to one, the \(Y\) radius to \(e^u\), and the \(Z\) radius to \(e^{u+v}\). Direct substitution in that theorem's functional gives \[ \mathcal A_t(u,v)= t u+b_{1-t}(u)+\max(0,-u) +b_t(v)+\max(0,-v). \tag{7} \] The two radius minima are at zero. First take \(0<t<1\). Equation (16) of that theorem shows that \(b_\lambda'\) lies in \([0,\lambda]\), with \(b_\lambda'(0)=\lambda/2\), for \(0<\lambda<1\). Each term in (7) is convex; its one-sided derivatives at zero enclose zero. Hence \[ \inf_{u,v}\mathcal A_t(u,v) =b_t(0)+b_{1-t}(0) =-2J(t/2)-2J((1-t)/2). \tag{8} \] The endpoint lengths follow directly from (1), or by continuity. The derivative of the last expression is \(\log\cot(\pi t/2)\), so its maximum is at \(t=1/2\). If \(v_8\) denotes the regular ideal octahedron volume, then \[ \sup_{0\le t\le1}\inf_{u,v}\mathcal A_t(u,v) =-4J(1/4)=\frac{v_8}{2\pi}>0. \tag{9} \] The trivial one-head presentation has upper rate zero. Thus the variational functional is not Markov invariant, even though its finite source is. No positive loss from the full-length closing phases survives in (7). Equation (9) does not prove that an arbitrary attached hyperbolic exterior suffers this same additive excess; its coupled optimization would require a separate argument. ## 4. The missing half of the joint stationary equations The same loss can be located before any topological interpretation. On a regular complex block chart let \(z\) denote logarithmic anchor coordinates, so \(z_a=\log r_a+i\vartheta_a\), and let \(H(\lambda,z)\) be the holomorphic leading action of the anchor integrand, including the real clock-factor contribution \(-\sum_eJ(\lambda_e)\) and the original coefficient loads. The extracted clock and block phases contribute another term \(i\phi(\lambda)\). Both are fixed by the original source; \(\phi\) is not adjustable. Where the anchor phase maximum and radius minimum are smooth and interior, their first-order equations are \[ \operatorname{Re}\partial_z H=0,\qquad \operatorname{Im}\partial_z H=0. \tag{10} \] The second equation follows by differentiating in the anchor arguments, since \(\partial_\vartheta\operatorname{Re}H =-\operatorname{Im}\partial_zH\). Thus the anchor optimization retains complex anchor stationarity. At an interior smooth maximum over lengths, envelope differentiation in an allowed real length direction \(v\) gives only \[ \operatorname{Re}\,d_\lambda H[v]=0. \tag{11} \] The full original clock saddle additionally requires, with its actual lattice character retained, \[ \operatorname{Im}\,d_\lambda H[v]+d\phi[v] \quad\text{to equal the corresponding Fourier lattice character}. \tag{12} \] In primitive integer clock coordinates that character is an integer multiple of \(2\pi\). In dependent length coordinates one must use the induced lattice, rather than assigning unrelated integers to all block lengths. The variational upper bound is unchanged if the extracted unit clock factors are changed, while (12) changes. This statement describes exactly which factors its proof takes in absolute value; it does not propose changing the invariant. The original feedback equations (15)--(16) in [the clock-feedback normal form](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_clock_feedback_normal_form.md) retain these terms. A geometric identification based only on (10)--(11) would omit source equations. The Markov calculation also shows that even the anchor coefficient can have exact root cancellation not measured by a limiting maximum-modulus bound. The constructive conclusion is that exact local contractions such as (3) and (6) should be performed before this optimization when available. A genuinely joint geometric contour must retain (12), all closing factors, and their original relative cycle. The current upper bound remains valid and useful, but its value cannot be declared a topological volume merely from its concave angle dual. ## Direct source versions | Source | SHA-256 | | --- | --- | | actual_global_charged_bridge_flow.md | b444e487eab3ec0a56c40b22584837cefcbe374a137b0beeaa185116c2a81d8c | | research_rivin_jones_prescribed_cut_and_hermite_recovery.md | 1b0e105ffb67b2b8552f5fddc5f0a3ac009e9795b33e27599ac4726ebd74079e | | research_rivin_jones_local_crossing_adapter.md | c4a9a92ec22f31a035036642e0621ef9abe569646b2488dbac2d2add786500f0 | | research_charged_source_angle_optimization.md | 45b21fabb9cb65512bc3e576eb3d659b6fe14c3dcd90b4164bfdb12b8cedea64 | | research_charged_block_holonomy_rate_loss.md | dfd2cae48cd534a12602670145ee09c3c959cf663e304e62896d4b47e1184b6e | | actual_clock_feedback_normal_form.md | f58a4dfd06615ecace95959e58474837f7eb50ef7f01a3c00d517d3938cb06bf |

title: Coherent endpoint transport through original crossings
text: # Coherent endpoint transport through original crossings Written proof, 24 November 2026. A fixed positive sweep of overlapping original crossings preserves the endpoint-to-bulk norm rate for every coherent input in a sublinear endpoint box. The inputs may be entangled across all heads, with arbitrary level-dependent coefficients. The proof uses bounded conjugates of prefix Cartans rather than a possibly unbounded conjugate of an individual second-head Cartan. Every matrix entry of this sweep has one transfer path. Its column norms can therefore be estimated exactly. Multivariate selected-root filters then control cancellation between the columns. The full outgoing packet is retained; no endpoint projection is inserted between crossings. A separate exact returned block has a controlled inverse and two explicitly specified positive incident metrics. No original scalar closing is estimated below. ## 1. The original sweep and its endpoint inputs Fix an integer \(b\ge2\), independently of the level \(N\ge2\), and put \[ r=b-1,\quad d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\quad x=-q^{-1},\quad \kappa=q^{d^2/2}. \tag{1} \] The balanced physical head basis is orthonormal. Use \[ E|a\rangle=(Q^{-a}-1)|a-1\rangle,\quad F|a\rangle=(1-Q^{a+1})|a+1\rangle,\quad K|a\rangle=xQ^{-a}|a\rangle, \tag{2} \] with the missing endpoint arrows zero. Operator subscripts label physical heads. All vector norms are product Hilbert norms in these bases, not Newton coefficient norms. Let \(R_j\) be the original checked positive crossing on heads \(j,j+1\), including its Cartan scalar. Define \[ \mathsf W_{b,N}=R_r\cdots R_1,\qquad v_{\boldsymbol a}=|d-a_0,a_1,\ldots,a_r\rangle,\qquad \mathcal H_{m,b}=\operatorname{span} \{v_{\boldsymbol a}:0\le a_j<m\}. \tag{3} \] The \(a_j\) are independent integers. In particular the input need not have one fixed total degree. The physical degree and all finite head restrictions are nevertheless preserved by the actual crossings. Write \[ S_n=\prod_{\ell=1}^n2\sin(\pi\ell/N),\quad S_0=1,\qquad h(t)=\int_0^t\log(2\sin\pi y)\,dy,\quad h_*=h(5/6)=-h(1/6)>0, \tag{4} \] \[ \Lambda_{N,m}=m\log(eN/m)+\log N. \tag{5} \] **Theorem.** There is a constant \(C_b\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(N\), every integer \(1\le m\le N/(24b)\), and every \(v\in\mathcal H_{m,b}\), \[ e^{Nh_*-C_b\Lambda_{N,m}}\|v\| \le\|\mathsf W_{b,N}v\| \le e^{Nh_*+C_b\Lambda_{N,m}}\|v\|. \tag{6} \] Consequently, for every \(m_N=o(N)\), uniformly over nonzero coherent inputs in these spaces, \[ \frac1N\log\frac{\|\mathsf W_{b,N}v_N\|}{\|v_N\|} \longrightarrow h_*. \tag{7} \] The exponent is \(h_*\), not \(r h_*\). This is an open-packet norm theorem for the specified fixed sweep and endpoint orientation. ## 2. Two good checked identities, directly at the finite endpoints For one crossing, [G] gives the coefficient from \(|a,b_0\rangle\) to \(|b_0+k,a-k\rangle\): \[ c_{a,b_0}(k)= \kappa x^{-a-b_0+k}Q^{(a-k)b_0} \frac{(Q;Q)_{b_0+k}(Q;Q)_a} {(Q;Q)_k(Q;Q)_{b_0}(Q;Q)_{a-k}} . \tag{8} \] Its support is \(0\le k\le a\), \(b_0+k\le d\). Every displayed factorial is a unit. The checked identities are \[ RK_1R^{-1}=K_2-qE_2K_1F_1,\qquad RE_1R^{-1}=K_1E_2,\qquad R(K_1K_2)=(K_1K_2)R . \tag{9} \] The first is proved from these same entries in [E]. To fix its operator order explicitly, the first matrix on the right acts on \(|i,j\rangle\) with diagonal \(xQ^{-j}\) and coefficient \[ Q^{-i-1}(1-Q^{i+1})(Q^{-j}-1) \quad\hbox{to }|i+1,j-1\rangle . \tag{10} \] The adjacent-transfer ratio in (8) is \[ \frac{c_{a,b_0}(k+1)}{c_{a,b_0}(k)} =xQ^{-b_0} \frac{(1-Q^{b_0+k+1})(1-Q^{a-k})}{1-Q^{k+1}} . \tag{11} \] Using \(x^2Q=1\), this is exactly the eigenvector recurrence for (10) with eigenvalue \(xQ^{-a}\). Its initial diagonal has that eigenvalue, and its last arrow vanishes at \(j=0\) or \(i=d\). This verifies the first identity on every input. For the second identity one needs a different finite comparison: \[ \frac{c_{a-1,b_0}(k)}{c_{a,b_0}(k)} =xQ^{-b_0}\frac{1-Q^{a-k}}{1-Q^a}, \qquad 0\le k\le a-1 . \tag{12} \] Multiplication by \(Q^{-a}-1\) gives \(xQ^{-a-b_0}(1-Q^{a-k})\). This equals \(xQ^{-b_0-k}(Q^{-a+k}-1)\), the factor from applying \(K_1E_2\) after the original crossing. The possible extra term \(k=a\) is killed by \(E_2\) at its zero index; \(a=0\) vanishes on both sides. Recipient upper endpoints agree as well. Thus \(RE_1=K_1E_2R\) holds without adding any arrow or normal coupon. Finally each output in (8) has the same total occupation as its input, proving the last identity in (9). The scalar \(\kappa\) was present in all these comparisons and cancels equally. These are identities of the whole physical matrices, not evaluations of commuting principal symbols. ## 3. Bounded commuting observables for the whole sweep Let \(J_j=K_1\cdots K_j\), \(J_0=I\), and define \(\mathcal A_j=\mathsf W_{b,N}J_j\mathsf W_{b,N}^{-1}\). For \(1\le j\le r\), put \[ H_{j,r}=\sum_{\ell=j}^{r} (K_{r-1}K_{r-2}\cdots K_\ell)F_\ell . \tag{13} \] The product is empty at \(\ell=r\); all its Cartans stand to the left of \(F_\ell\). Then, exactly, \[ \mathcal A_j =J_{j-1}\bigl(K_b-qE_bK_rH_{j,r}\bigr)\quad(j\le r), \qquad \mathcal A_b=J_b . \tag{14} \] Indeed crossings wholly inside the first \(j\) heads preserve \(J_j\). The first crossing through its boundary gives the first identity in (9), with \(J_{j-1}\) outside. Each later crossing replaces the moving \(K\) by its good polynomial in (9), and the moving \(E\) by \(KE\). Induction appends precisely one term to (13), proving (14) in its displayed order. There are \(r-j+1\) terms in (13), each of norm at most two. Since all \(K_i\) are unitary and \(\|E_i\|,\|F_i\|\le2\), \[ \|\mathcal A_j\|\le1+4(r-j+1)\quad(j\le r), \qquad \|\mathcal A_b\|=1 . \tag{15} \] No inverse of an individual conjugated second-head Cartan occurs. All the \(\mathcal A_j\) commute exactly, as conjugates of the original commuting prefix Cartans. Let \(f_{\boldsymbol a}=\mathsf W_{b,N}v_{\boldsymbol a}\). Its joint eigenvalue indices are \[ t_j(\boldsymbol a)=a_0-\sum_{\ell=1}^{j-1}a_\ell,\qquad \mathcal A_jf_{\boldsymbol a} =\zeta_{j,t_j(\boldsymbol a)}f_{\boldsymbol a},\qquad \zeta_{j,t}=x^jQ^{1+t}. \tag{16} \] This follows directly from the input prefix occupations. The tuple of indices determines the input: \(a_0=t_1\) and \(a_\ell=t_\ell-t_{\ell+1}\). ## 4. The joint selected Gram has subexponential cost Each index in (16) belongs to the consecutive integer interval \[ I_j=[-(j-1)(m-1),\,m-1]\cap\mathbb Z,\qquad |I_j|=j(m-1)+1 . \tag{17} \] Its diameter is less than \(N/2\) in our range. Consequently \[ |\zeta_{j,t}-\zeta_{j,s}|\ge4|t-s|/N,\qquad t,s\in I_j . \tag{18} \] For each \(t\in I_j\), form the ordinary Lagrange polynomial \[ L_{j,t}(z)=\prod_{\substack{s\in I_j\\s\ne t}} \frac{z-\zeta_{j,s}}{\zeta_{j,t}-\zeta_{j,s}} . \tag{19} \] The numerator factors evaluated at \(\mathcal A_j\) have norm bounded by a constant depending only on \(b\). If \(n_j=|I_j|-1\), the denominator in (19) is at least \((4/N)^{n_j}(t-\min I_j)!(\max I_j-t)!\). Using the binomial bound and \(n!\ge(n/e)^n\) gives \[ \|L_{j,t}(\mathcal A_j)\| \le\frac{(C_bN)^{n_j}}{n_j!} \le\exp\{C_bm\log(eN/m)\}. \tag{20} \] Empty products have value one. Since \(n_j\le bm\), the last bound is uniform in every index. This is an operator-product estimate, not a scalar spectral supremum. The commuting product \(\Pi_{\boldsymbol a}=\prod_{j=1}^b L_{j,t_j(\boldsymbol a)}(\mathcal A_j)\) therefore has norm at most \(\exp\{C_bm\log(eN/m)\}\). It recovers one selected column and kills the other selected columns. The injectivity following (16) proves this without an interpolation of degree \(m^b\). No assertion about unselected joint eigenspaces is needed. Normalize each actual column internally: \(u_{\boldsymbol a}=f_{\boldsymbol a}/\|f_{\boldsymbol a}\|\), and let \(V_mc=\sum_{\boldsymbol a}c_{\boldsymbol a}u_{\boldsymbol a}\). All columns are nonzero because the original sweep is invertible. Applying the selected filters and summing over \(m^b\) tuples yields \[ e^{-C_b\Lambda_{N,m}}I \preceq V_m^*V_m\preceq m^bI . \tag{21} \] For the lower bound use \(|c_{\boldsymbol a}|\le\|\Pi_{\boldsymbol a}\|\|V_mc\|\). The upper bound is triangle and Cauchy--Schwarz. Thus all coherent cross terms are controlled. ## 5. Exact unique-path columns and their common norm rate For an input in (3), write \(A_0=d-a_0\), \(K_j=k_1+\cdots+k_j\), and \(A_j=A_0-K_j\). The outputs are \((a_1+k_1,\ldots,a_r+k_r,A_r)\), on the exact support \[ k_j\ge0,\quad K_r\le A_0,\quad a_j+k_j\le d . \tag{22} \] Each output fixes every \(k_j\), so there is no internal sum at one matrix entry. The exact formula of [F] is \[ (\mathsf W_{b,N})_{\rm out,in} =\Xi_N\frac{S_{A_0}}{S_{A_r}} \prod_{j=1}^r\frac{S_{a_j+k_j}}{S_{a_j}S_{k_j}}, \qquad \Xi_N=\prod_{j=1}^r\chi_N(A_j,a_j,k_j),\quad|\Xi_N|=1, \tag{23} \] where \[ \chi_N(j,a,k)=\kappa x^{-j-a}Q^{ja}(-i)^k q^{k(j+a)+k(k+1)/2}. \tag{24} \] In particular every common Cartan scalar and entry phase is retained. The endpoint-uniform factorial estimate proved in [E] gives \[ \log S_n=Nh(n/N)+O(\log N),\quad \max_n S_n,\ \max_n S_n^{-1}\le e^{Nh_*+C\log N}. \tag{25} \] Also \(S_{d-a}=N/S_a\), and, for \(1\le a\le m\), \[ S_a\ge(4/N)^a a!,\quad S_a\le2^a,\quad S_{a+k}/S_k\le2^a . \tag{26} \] At \(a=0\) the corresponding factors equal one. Equations (23)--(26) give the uniform entry upper bound \(\exp\{Nh_*+C_b\Lambda_{N,m}\}\). There are at most \(N^r\) outputs in one column, so the same form bounds its vector norm. For a lower bound choose \[ n_*=\lfloor N/6\rfloor,\qquad k_1=d-a_0-n_*,\qquad k_j=0\quad(j>1). \tag{27} \] For sufficiently large \(N\) and \(m\le N/(24b)\), this is a legal transfer in (22). The factors in \(S_{k_1+a_1}/S_{k_1}\) all lie on a fixed compact sine interval around \(5/6\), so this ratio is at least \(c^{a_1}\) for a fixed \(c>0\). All other recipient ratios in (23) equal one. Using \(S_{d-a_0}=N/S_{a_0}\), \(S_a\le2^a\), and \(S_{n_*}^{-1}=\exp\{Nh_*+O(\log N)\}\), this one entry has modulus at least \(\exp\{Nh_*-C_bm-C\log N\}\). Consequently every column obeys \[ e^{Nh_*-C_b\Lambda_{N,m}}\le\|f_{\boldsymbol a}\| \le e^{Nh_*+C_b\Lambda_{N,m}} . \tag{28} \] For the vacuum tuple \(\boldsymbol a=0\), (23)'s modulus is \(N/S_{d-K_r}=S_{K_r}\). Different compositions of the same total transfer give only a polynomial multiplicity at fixed \(b\). This explains why the column exponent does not add across crossings. Finally write \(\mathsf W_{b,N}v =V_m(c_{\boldsymbol a}\|f_{\boldsymbol a}\|)_{\boldsymbol a}\). Combining (21) and (28) proves (6), after increasing \(C_b\). Since \(\Lambda_{N,m_N}/N\to0\) for every \(m_N=o(N)\), it also proves (7). ## 6. An exact returned block and its incident metrics There is also a source-specific estimate when one explicitly observes the original endpoint band after a single crossing. Extend [E]'s definition to every \(1\le m\le N\): \(H_m^+=\operatorname{span}\{|d-\alpha,\alpha\rangle:0\le\alpha<m\}\) and \(H_m^-=\mathsf P H_m^+\). Let \(\mathcal Q_m^\pm\) be their orthogonal projections and \(\mathcal B_m^\pm=\mathcal Q_m^\pm R_N^\pm\mathcal Q_m^\pm\) on the indicated band. The exact identities below hold for all \(1\le m\le N\). The positive matrix is \[ (\mathcal B_m^+)_{\beta\alpha} =\kappa N x^{-\alpha-\beta} \frac{f_{\alpha+\beta}}{f_\alpha^2f_\beta^2}, \qquad f_j=(Q;Q)_j,\qquad 0\le\alpha,\beta<m . \tag{29} \] This is the literal checked entry (8), with output first index \(d-\beta\). To simplify it, retain the exact reflection \(f_t f_{d-t}=N(-1)^tQ^{t(t+1)/2}\). Its phase \(Q^{-\alpha\beta}\) cancels the original \(Q^{\alpha\beta}\). The same cross-collar kernel and its full normal-source conventions are given in [L]. When \(\alpha+\beta\ge N\), its numerator \(f_{\alpha+\beta}\) is zero, exactly as the original support requires. Its denominators are still units, since \(\alpha,\beta<N\); no \(f_N\) is divided out. Define the Gaussian polynomials by \({n\brack0}_Q={n\brack n}_Q=1\), zero outside \(0\le k\le n\), and \({n+1\brack k}_Q={n\brack k}_Q+Q^{n+1-k}{n\brack k-1}_Q\). Equivalently the coefficient of \(t^k\) in \(\prod_{j=0}^{n-1}(1+Q^jt)\) is \(Q^{k(k-1)/2}{n\brack k}_Q\). They can be specialized at the root for every \(n\), including \(n\ge N\). Put \(D_{\alpha\alpha}=x^{-\alpha}/f_\alpha\), \(L_{\alpha k}={\alpha\brack k}_Q\) for \(k\le\alpha\), and \(J_{kk}=Q^{k^2}\). The exact finite factorization is \[ \mathcal B_m^+=\kappa N D L J L^{\mathsf T}D . \tag{30} \] Here transpose does not conjugate coefficients. The identity \({\alpha+\beta\brack\alpha}_Q =\sum_kQ^{k^2}{\alpha\brack k}_Q{\beta\brack k}_Q\) proves (30). Its left side equals \(f_{\alpha+\beta}/(f_\alpha f_\beta)\), also when the numerator vanishes, since these two denominator factors are units. To verify the identity directly, expand \(\prod_{j=0}^{\alpha+\beta-1}(1+Q^jt)\), split after its first \(\alpha\) factors, and compare \(t^\alpha\). Setting \(k=\alpha-j\) in that coefficient gives exponent \(k^2\) after dividing the common \(Q^{\alpha(\alpha-1)/2}\). The triangular inverse is \[ (L^{-1})_{\alpha k} =(-1)^{\alpha-k}Q^{(\alpha-k)(\alpha-k-1)/2} {\alpha\brack k}_Q . \tag{31} \] Multiplication uses \({\alpha\brack j}_Q{j\brack k}_Q ={\alpha\brack k}_Q{\alpha-k\brack j-k}_Q\); the remaining finite sum is \((1;Q)_{\alpha-k}\), which vanishes for \(\alpha>k\) and equals one for \(\alpha=k\). Thus this is an exact inverse before any norm estimate. The finite \(q\)-Pascal recursion and \(|Q|=1\) imply \(|{\alpha\brack k}_Q|\le\binom{\alpha}{k}\). Both \(L,L^{-1}\) have row sums at most \(2^{m-1}\) and column sums at most \(2^m\), so their operator norms are at most \(2^m\). Also \(\|D^{-1}\|\le2^{m-1}\) and \(\|D\|\le H_N(m):=(eN/m)^m\) when \(m\le N/2\), by (26). Consequently \[ \begin{split} \|(\mathcal B_m^+)^{-1}\|&\le16^m/N,\quad |\det\mathcal B_m^+| =\frac{N^m}{\prod_{\alpha=0}^{m-1}S_\alpha^2} &&(1\le m\le N),\\ \|\mathcal B_m^+\|&\le N4^mH_N(m)^2 &&(1\le m\le N/2). \end{split} \tag{32} \] At \(m=N\), reflection gives \(\prod_{\alpha=0}^dS_\alpha^2=N^N\), so the full degree-\(d\) block has determinant of modulus one. The reflected negative block is its entrywise conjugate by \(R_N^-=\mathsf P\overline{R_N^+}\mathsf P\), so the same bounds hold on \(H_m^-\). The inverse in (32) is the inverse of the returned compression. It need not equal \(\mathcal Q_m^+R_N^{-1}\mathcal Q_m^+\); at \(m=N\) these do agree on the invariant degree block. The mirrored negative block must not be identified with that inverse. Complementary excursions distinguish compression and inversion in general. In particular every nonzero vector in a sublinear selected band has returned-vector norm with logarithmic rate zero: \[ \frac1N\log \frac{\|\mathcal Q_{m_N}^\pm R_N^\pm v_N\|}{\|v_N\|} \longrightarrow0,\qquad m_N=o(N). \tag{33} \] This differs from the positive rate of its entire outgoing packet. The factorization also specifies a genuine orthogonality relation with two incident metrics. Set \(U=DL\) and \[ G_{\rm out}=(U^{-1})^*U^{-1},\qquad G_{\rm in}=(U^{\mathsf T})^*U^{\mathsf T}. \tag{34} \] Both are positive definite for all \(m\le N\), and (30) gives exactly \[ (\mathcal B_m^+)^*G_{\rm out}\mathcal B_m^+ =N^2G_{\rm in}. \tag{35} \] Indeed the middle \(J\) is diagonal unitary. When \(m\le N/2\), \(\|U\|\le2^mH_N(m)\) and \(\|U^{-1}\|\le4^m\). Thus the two metrics and their inverses have norms at most \(\exp(C\Lambda_{N,m})\). They are two specified incident metrics, not one preserved inner product for the full crossing. One associated quadratic minimization can be evaluated completely: \[ \min_{\substack{c\in\mathbb C^m\\c_0=1}} \|\mathcal B_m^+c\|_{G_{\rm out}}^2 =\frac{N^2}{m}\qquad(1\le m\le N). \tag{36} \] Here \(\|z\|_G^2=z^*Gz\). Set \(y=U^{\mathsf T}c\). Then \(c_0=\sum_k a_ky_k\), where \(a_k=(U^{-1})_{k0}=(-1)^kQ^{k(k-1)/2}\) has modulus one. Equation (35) makes the objective \(N^2\|y\|^2\). Cauchy--Schwarz gives its minimum \(N^2/m\), attained at \(y_k=\overline{a_k}/m\). This is the weighted returned-block quadratic problem with one fixed endpoint coefficient; it is not the whole source quartic. There is an exact scalar linear-elimination consequence. Formulae (30)--(31) give \[ ((\mathcal B_m^+)^{-1})_{00} =\frac1{\kappa N}\sum_{k=0}^{m-1}Q^{-k},\qquad \operatorname{Schur}_{00}\mathcal B_m^+ =\frac{\kappa N}{\sum_{k=0}^{m-1}Q^{-k}} \quad(1\le m<N). \tag{37} \] Indeed the squared inverse-Pascal first-column phase times \(J^{-1}\) is \(Q^{-k}\). For \(m<N\) the geometric sum is nonzero, so the cofactor proves that the trailing principal submatrix is invertible; eliminating those indices gives the displayed Schur complement. Its modulus is \(N\sin(\pi/N)/\sin(\pi m/N)\), asymptotic to \(N/m\) when \(m=o(N)\). At \(m=N\) that cofactor is zero and this elimination is not available. This is a linear reduction of the specified returned block, not an evaluation of a whole Conway minimum or a closed knot scalar. The ordinary cap is not a Hermitian dual merely by (35). Inserting \(\mathcal Q_m^\pm\) into an internal network would change it unless all complementary excursion blocks and the original transported exterior were also retained. ## 7. Coverage, phases, and the original closing [F] already proves the exact unique-path sweep coefficient and its whole Hilbert--Schmidt Gaussian asymptotics. It also constructs one nonzero coefficient between prepared product Gaussian vectors. The present estimate instead controls every coherent endpoint input, using its actual joint column Gram and the bounded prefix observables (14). The single-crossing selected-filter method and endpoint column rate were proved in [E]; no general novelty is claimed for polynomial interpolation. [L] already evaluates the actual long-transfer endpoint kernel, its signed phases, factorial gauges and compensated Pascal limit. The exact returned-block inverse and the incident metrics above are additional source-specific consequences; the factorization is not a positivity claim for the original complex scalar. The width \(b\) and the crossing sweep are fixed. This proof does not cover a growing number of heads, an arbitrary sequence of crossing signs, repeated arbitrary sweeps, or a change of pairing by a Conway quarter-turn. Such operations have their literal matrices and currents; none is replaced by an endpoint projection. The theorem is at the original complete root and asserts no uniform moving-meridian or quantum-normal derivative estimate. The original cups, caps, pivots, marks and framing factors remain those of [P]. A subsequent prescribed closing may cancel a large open packet. Neither the joint Gram lower bound nor its common outgoing rate supplies a lower bound for that scalar, identifies a selected geometric framing cycle, or proves a new knot-volume or finite-exception statement. ## Complete chosen texts All five complete matching texts were read. The new estimates are proved above in the uniform physical metric. | Label | Complete text | SHA-256 | | --- | --- | --- | | G, direct | [Actual physical crossing entries](research_full_physical_crossing_gaussian_packet.md), 306 lines | 7f1b9932f88aa549bc55088b6f056f5a362548bc51c9fdd7c6b00469e725f531 | | P, direct | [Original uniform physical source](research_conway_uniform_physical_quartic.md), 477 lines | 39895b430535f565d30133b46ef57f67589207bc83f40597ffe96e2ce79bbda8 | | E, direct and coverage | [Coherent single-crossing endpoint transport](research_coherent_endpoint_to_bulk_crossing_norm.md), 392 lines | a860255c704f55bf252ed2c77a7d463661f652550ff1f5fdeaedce90495b7a02 | | F, direct and coverage | [Exact physical fan and its Gaussian packet](research_full_physical_fan_gaussian_packet.md), 501 lines | 1e89a7f8e4bf948fa8ffdd3e6314a01541af3177901747ece8274baf871dd83e | | L, direct and coverage | [Actual long-transfer cross-collar kernel](research_actual_long_transfer_cross_collar_kernel.md), 454 lines | 4639b15a335a0d0813d30f0ee2e9f84b5fa15fce3ea93b34d05f181805a39d90 | Only written mathematics, complete source reads and metadata hashes were used. No mathematical program, numerical test, build, git operation, prior-final edit or public-manuscript change was made.

title: Coherent endpoint inputs have a controlled bulk crossing norm
text: # Coherent endpoint inputs have a controlled bulk crossing norm Written proof, 24 November 2026. A small endpoint input need not stay near the endpoints after an original crossing. Here the entire outgoing packet has an explicit positive exponential norm rate, uniformly for every coherent input in a sublinear endpoint band. This includes coefficients and phases chosen separately at each level. A bounded checked Hurwitz observable controls cancellation between the actual crossing columns. The original binomial cut also has an exact weighted-cup realization. Its censored finite endpoint approximation gives the same outgoing norm rate for the full purified cut, with an arbitrarily small absolute error after crossing. The ordinary cap, pivot and all crossing phases remain explicit. No lower bound for a returned cap or an original closed knot scalar is inferred. ## 1. Actual physical matrices and the statement Fix \(N\ge3\), \(d=N-1\), and \[ q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\quad x=-q^{-1},\quad \kappa=q^{d^2/2},\quad F_j=(Q;Q)_j,\quad S_j=|F_j|,\quad S_0=1 . \tag{1} \] The original balanced head basis is orthonormal. Pair vectors have the product Hilbert norm, denoted \(\|\cdot\|\). This is not the Newton coefficient norm or the Hilbert--Schmidt norm of one box. The latter will only supply an upper bound for an operator norm. Let \(R=R_N^+\) be the original checked positive crossing, including its common Cartan line. On each head retain \[ E|a\rangle=(Q^{-a}-1)|a-1\rangle,\quad F|a\rangle=(1-Q^{a+1})|a+1\rangle,\quad K|a\rangle=xQ^{-a}|a\rangle , \tag{2} \] with missing extreme arrows zero. Operator subscripts below label the physical heads. Write \(\mathsf P\) for the physical head flip. The exact negative crossing is \[ R_N^-=\mathsf P\,\overline R\,\mathsf P . \tag{3} \] Conjugation here is entrywise in this physical basis, not adjoint. These source identities are those of [G,P]. Define the two sign-adapted input bands by \[ H_m^+=\operatorname{span}\{|d-a,a\rangle:0\le a<m\},\qquad H_m^-=\mathsf P H_m^+,\qquad 1\le m\le N/2 . \tag{4} \] All these vectors have total physical degree \(d\). Put \[ h(t)=\int_0^t\log(2\sin\pi y)\,dy,\qquad h_*=h(5/6)=-h(1/6)>0,\qquad \Lambda_{N,m}=m\log(eN/m)+\log N . \tag{5} \] **Theorem.** An absolute constant \(C\) exists such that, for all sufficiently large \(N\), all \(1\le m\le N/2\), and either sign, \[ e^{Nh_*-C\Lambda_{N,m}}\|v\| \le \|R_N^\pm v\| \le e^{Nh_*+C\Lambda_{N,m}}\|v\|, \qquad v\in H_m^\pm . \tag{6} \] In particular, for every \(m_N=o(N)\), uniformly over all nonzero vectors in the corresponding bands, \[ \frac1N\log\frac{\|R_N^\pm v_N\|}{\|v_N\|} \longrightarrow h_* . \tag{7} \] This is an estimate for the full outgoing vector. It does not compress that vector back to an endpoint band. ## 2. The exact joint high/low kernel Let \(f_a=R|d-a,a\rangle\), and use \(|i,d-i\rangle\) as output basis on this degree block. Substitution in the actual entry [G,(2)] gives, with every phase retained, \[ f_a(i)= \kappa x^{i-a-d}Q^{a(d-i)} \frac{F_iF_{d-a}}{F_{i-a}F_aF_{d-i}} \quad(a\le i\le d),\qquad f_a(i)=0\quad(i<a). \tag{8} \] No factorial at \(N\) occurs. The exact sine reflection \(S_jS_{d-j}=N\) therefore gives \[ |f_a(i)|=\frac{S_i^2}{S_{i-a}S_a^2} \quad(i\ge a). \tag{9} \] For example \(f_0\) has output moduli \(S_i\), including its bulk maximum near \(i=5N/6\). At fixed \(a\) and fixed upper-hole index \(b=d-i\), (9) is equivalently \(N S_{a+b}/(S_a^2S_b^2)\). Thus a fixed-endpoint matrix limit without additional scaling is not the norm statement being proved. We first control each whole column. Uniformly for \(0\le i<N\), \[ \log S_i=Nh(i/N)+O(\log N). \tag{10} \] Here is an elementary endpoint-uniform justification. Subtract \(\log t+\log(1-t)\) from \(\log(2\sin\pi t)\); the remainder extends smoothly to \([0,1]\). Its Riemann-sum error is bounded. For each of the two logarithms, integral comparison with \(\log(j!)\) gives error \(O(\log N)\), uniformly in the stopping index, including \(i=0,N-1\). Adding these three estimates proves (10). Also \(h(1)=0\), by the sine double-angle identity and reflection; hence \(h(1-t)=-h(t)\). Its derivative shows that its unique global maximum on \([0,1]\) is \(h_*\) at \(5/6\). The derivative is negative on \((0,1/6)\), proving \(h_*>0\). For \(1\le a\le N/2\), the sine chord bound gives \[ S_a\ge(4/N)^a a!,\qquad \frac{S_i}{S_{i-a}}\le2^a,\qquad |f_a(i)|\le \max_j S_j\, \exp\{2a\log(eN/a)+Ca\}. \tag{11} \] The last inequality uses \(a!\ge(a/e)^a\). For \(a=0\) its interpretation is simply \(|f_0(i)|=S_i\). For the converse choose \(i_*=\lfloor5N/6\rfloor\). When \(a\le N/2\), every factor of \(S_{i_*}/S_{i_*-a}\) lies on a fixed compact interval inside \((0,1)\), once \(N\) is large. Each is bounded below by a fixed positive constant. Since \(S_a\le2^a\), (9)--(10) imply \[ |f_a(i_*)|\ge \exp\{Nh_*-Ca-C\log N\}. \tag{12} \] Summing at most \(N\) squares in the upper bound and keeping this one entry for the lower bound now gives, simultaneously for \(0\le a<m\le N/2\), \[ e^{Nh_*-C\Lambda_{N,m}}\le \|f_a\| \le e^{Nh_*+C\Lambda_{N,m}}. \tag{13} \] Column estimates alone would not justify (6): the columns have their actual complex phases and can interfere. ## 3. A bounded physical observable separates the columns There is an exact checked identity on the whole pair: \[ A:=R K_1R^{-1}=K_2-qE_2K_1F_1,\qquad \|A\|\le5 . \tag{14} \] The bound follows from \(\|K\|=1\) and \(\|E\|,\|F\|\le2\). We verify the ordering and the finite endpoints directly rather than importing a commuting symbol. For an input \(|a_0,b_0\rangle\), put \(n=a_0+b_0\). Its successive positive-transfer outputs are \(|b_0+k,a_0-k\rangle\). The exact entry ratio from [G,(2)] is \[ \frac{r_{k+1}}{r_k} =xQ^{-b_0} \frac{(1-Q^{b_0+k+1})(1-Q^{a_0-k})}{1-Q^{k+1}} . \tag{15} \] On \(|i,j\rangle\), the right side of (14) has diagonal \(xQ^{-j}\) and the additional coefficient \[ Q^{-i-1}(1-Q^{i+1})(Q^{-j}-1) \quad\hbox{to }|i+1,j-1\rangle . \tag{16} \] Using \(x^2Q=1\), (15) says exactly that this output column is an eigenvector with eigenvalue \(xQ^{-a_0}\). Its first coefficient has that diagonal eigenvalue already. At the last allowed transfer the extra coefficient vanishes because \(j=0\) or \(i=d\). Thus the identity \(AR=RK_1\) holds on every input, including both endpoints. The original crossing is invertible, which proves (14). In degree \(d\), (16) simplifies further: \[ A|i,d-i\rangle =\zeta_i|i,d-i\rangle+s_{i+1}^2|i+1,d-i-1\rangle,\qquad \zeta_i=-qQ^i,\quad s_j=2\sin(\pi j/N). \tag{17} \] The last term at \(i=d\) is zero. The \(N\) eigenvalues are distinct, and the actual columns satisfy \(Af_a=\zeta_a f_a\). Let \(u_a=f_a/\|f_a\|\), and \(V_m c=\sum_{a<m}c_a u_a\). The internally normalized column Gram has the quantitative bound \[ e^{-C\Lambda_{N,m}}I \ \preceq\ V_m^*V_m\ \preceq\ mI . \tag{18} \] For completeness, use the selected Lagrange polynomials \[ L_a(z)=\prod_{\substack{0\le b<m\\b\ne a}} \frac{z-\zeta_b}{\zeta_a-\zeta_b}. \tag{19} \] They recover the selected column exactly: \(L_a(A)u_b=\delta_{ab}u_b\), for \(b<m\). For these consecutive endpoint roots, \[ |\zeta_a-\zeta_b|\ge4|a-b|/N,\qquad \|A-\zeta_b I\|\le6 . \tag{20} \] Thus, with the empty product interpreted as one, \[ \|L_a(A)\| \le\frac{(3N/2)^{m-1}}{a!(m-1-a)!} \le\frac{(3N)^{m-1}}{(m-1)!} \le \exp\{Cm\log(eN/m)\}. \tag{21} \] The estimate is a product of operator factors; a scalar supremum on the spectrum would not suffice for this nonnormal matrix. Applying (21) to \(V_mc\), then summing \(|c_a|^2\le\|L_a(A)\|^2\|V_mc\|^2\), gives the lower bound in (18). The upper bound follows by triangle and Cauchy--Schwarz. No filter is asserted to annihilate unselected eigenvectors. For \(v=\sum_{a<m}v_a|d-a,a\rangle\), apply (18) to coefficients \(c_a=v_a\|f_a\|\), then use (13). Absorbing the polynomial factors into \(C\Lambda_{N,m}\) proves (6) for the positive sign. Equation (3) sends \(v\) to \(\mathsf P\bar v\) without changing norms or support widths, proving the negative case. Since \(\Lambda_{N,m_N}=o(N)\) when \(m_N=o(N)\), (7) follows. The filter argument is the same finite-dimensional mechanism used in [C]. The new estimate concerns actual high/low crossing columns and their common bulk rate, not a new interpolation method. ## 4. The original cup gives the purified cut exactly At the complete root retain the literal source tensors [P]: \[ p=N\sum_{a=0}^d x^{-a}|d-a,a\rangle,\qquad \ell_{ij}=x^i\mathbf1_{i+j=d}/N,\qquad g=K^{1-N},\quad g_a=x^{2a-d}. \tag{22} \] Fix \(L<\infty\), and take real \(0\le\lambda\le L\). For sufficiently large \(N\), define the original binomial probabilities and their positive square root by \[ \beta_{N,a}=\binom da(\lambda/N)^a(1-\lambda/N)^{d-a}, \quad H_N=\operatorname{diag}(\sqrt{\beta_{N,a}}),\quad P_N=H_N^2 . \tag{23} \] Then the unit vector \[ \Psi_N^+=N^{-1}(I\otimes H_N)p =\sum_a x^{-a}\sqrt{\beta_{N,a}}|d-a,a\rangle \tag{24} \] has the exact physical dual and evaluation \[ (\Psi_N^+)^*=N\ell(I\otimes gH_N),\qquad (\Psi_N^+)^*(I\otimes C)\Psi_N^+ =\operatorname{Tr}(P_NC) \tag{25} \] for every finite head matrix \(C\). Indeed the coefficient of the dual on \(|d-a,a\rangle\) is \(x^{d-a}x^{2a-d}\sqrt{\beta_{N,a}}=x^a\sqrt{\beta_{N,a}}\). The remaining contraction has diagonal coefficient \(x^{d-a}g_ax^{-a}=1\), proving the second identity. The ordinary cap alone is not identified with a Hermitian dual; the original pivot and both displayed \(N\) factors are essential. For the negative orientation take \(\Psi_N^-=\mathsf P\overline{\Psi_N^+}\). Equivalently it is \(x^d(H_N\otimes I)p/N\), so its additional factor is a specified unit phase. It gives \((\Psi_N^-)^*(C\otimes I)\Psi_N^-=\operatorname{Tr}(P_NC)\). For an actual unmarked one-cut knot operator this is the same original scalar, by [W]. For arbitrary marked \(C\), its comparison with the highest cut retains exactly [W]'s finite Ward current. No new equality of arbitrary marked source probes is assumed. ## 5. Whole purified inputs and the paid tail Use [W]'s censored trace-one cut at \(m-1\): keep \(\beta_{N,a}\) for \(a<m-1\), put \(\sum_{a\ge m-1}\beta_{N,a}\) at \(m-1\), and use zero thereafter. Let \(\Psi_N^{\pm,[m]}\) be (24) and its negative counterpart with these censored probabilities. They are unit vectors in \(H_m^\pm\), with their exact cap/pivot dictionary (25). The artificial last mass and its Ward current have not been dropped. If \(t_{N,m}=\sum_{a\ge m}\beta_{N,a}\), elementary square-root algebra gives \[ \|\Psi_N^\pm-\Psi_N^{\pm,[m]}\|^2\le2t_{N,m},\qquad t_{N,m}\le C_L(C_L/m)^m . \tag{26} \] For the first inequality, the last-coordinate difference has square at most \(t_{N,m}\), and the removed coordinates have total square \(t_{N,m}\). The second is the actual finite factorial tail in [W], uniformly for all \(\lambda\in[0,L]\). Given \(A_0>0\), choose a fixed \(c>2(\log20+A_0)\) and \[ m_N=\lceil cN/\log N\rceil . \tag{27} \] For large \(N\), this is at most \(N/2\). The original physical crossing bound [P], \(\|R_N^\pm\|\le\|R_N^\pm\|_{\rm HS} \le20^{N-1}\), proves \[ \|R_N^\pm(\Psi_N^\pm-\Psi_N^{\pm,[m_N]})\| \le e^{(\log20-c/2)N+o(N)}=O(e^{-A_0N}) . \tag{28} \] In particular this is an absolute error estimate using exact finite-\(N\) coefficients, not substitution of Poisson weights. Apply (6) to the censored unit vectors and then (28). It follows uniformly on every real compact interval \(0\le\lambda\le L\) that \[ \frac1N\log\|R_N^\pm\Psi_N^\pm\| \longrightarrow h_* . \tag{29} \] This includes \(\lambda=0\). Positivity of the input probabilities is used only for the purification and its square-root tail bound; no positive crossing coefficients or closed period are asserted. ## 6. Relation to earlier endpoint models and source scope [E] already proves subexponential factorial-chart costs on sublinear head bands, with the exact Fourier source and endpoint arrows. [T] proves bounded Euler transitions for compressed single-interval head blocks in appropriate factorial gauges. It explicitly keeps the complementary and cross-collar blocks. The present result estimates the full outgoing high/low column family, including the bulk reached by long transfers, and controls arbitrary coherent combinations before taking their norm. [W]'s trace-class Poisson limit has error \(O(N^{-1})\). That algebraic error is not multiplied through a growing crossing here. Only its exact finite censored model is used in (26)--(28). A complex parameter can be treated by a holomorphic source/co-source pair on a square-root chart, but no positive Hermitian purification or uniform nonzero norm theorem for such complex parameters is claimed. Neither (6) nor (29) supplies a lower bound after a prescribed ordinary or marked cap. Nor do these estimates assert that arbitrary turns, branches, or neighboring short components preserve the selected endpoint spans or the exponent \(h_*\). The returned source still has its original coherent contraction; its overlap has not been estimated. In particular this is not a knot-volume or finite-exception theorem. ## Complete chosen inputs and coverage All six complete texts below were read at matching versions. title: The original marked cap becomes a corner in coherent coordinates
text: # The original marked cap becomes a corner in coherent coordinates 24 November 2026. Written research proof. The original transformed closing restricts to one physical corner in the coherent coordinates used to bound the shared boundary resolvent. The ordinary caps remain literal. Its intrinsic dual norm is bounded above and below by explicit powers of the level. No new closing functional is chosen. There is a further source-faithful reduction. The central integer-degree projection of the coherent packet retains the entire invariant tensor at every width. The original input and closing in this smaller packet have exact polynomial norm product. Earlier complete source modules already have central-degree coordinates; the new statements identify this particular orthogonal projection and this coherent marked row. They do not bound the remaining coherent word or prove its volume rate. ## 1. Actual source and coherent coordinates Use the complete physical conventions of [T,O,M,P,D]: \[ N\ge2,\quad d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\quad x=-q^{-1}=q^d,\quad \theta=\pi/(2N),\quad \xi=q^{-3}. \tag{1} \] On the original orthonormal head \(V=\mathbb C^N\), \[ E|a\rangle=(Q^{-a}-1)|a-1\rangle,\quad F|a\rangle=(1-Q^{a+1})|a+1\rangle,\quad K|a\rangle=xQ^{-a}|a\rangle . \tag{2} \] Missing arrows vanish. The unrolled weight is \(H|a\rangle=(d-2a)|a\rangle\), and the coproducts are \[ E_{12}=E_1K_2+E_2,\qquad F_{12}=F_1+K_1^{-1}F_2,\qquad K_{12}=K_1K_2. \tag{3} \] All norms below are unnormalized physical Euclidean norms or their induced dual norms. The actual pair Casimir is \(\Omega=F_{12}E_{12}+qK_{12}+q^{-1}K_{12}^{-1}\). Let \(b=2k\ge4\), \(W=V^{\otimes(b-2)}\), and let \(\mathcal I_b\) be the full root invariant space with unrolled weight zero. Let \(\mathcal S_b\subset\mathcal I_b\) be the actual saturated specialization of generic invariant tensors. The original turns are \[ p_{ab}=Nx^{-b}\delta_{a+b,d},\qquad \ell_{ab}=x^a\delta_{a+b,d}/N,\qquad m_{ab}=x^b/N^2. \tag{4} \] The marked row has no degree delta. The literal snakes hold, \(mp=1\), \(\ell p=0\), and \(\|p\|=N^{3/2}\), \(\|\ell\|=N^{-1/2}\). Write \[ \eta_a=\frac{1-q^3}{2}q^{3a},\qquad \zeta_a=\frac{1-q^{-3}}2x^a,\qquad \mathscr D_b=\eta\otimes I_W\otimes\zeta . \tag{5} \] By [O], this observation is faithful on \(\mathcal I_b\) and on \(\mathcal S_b\). Its inverse retains the unrolled and regular divided-current source equations. Put \(\mathcal Y_b=\mathscr D_b(\mathcal S_b)\). For a nilpotent argument \(t^N=0\), set \[ \mathsf e_N(t)=\sum_{r=0}^{d}\frac{t^r}{(Q;Q)_r},\qquad S_W=\mathsf e_N(E_WK_W^{-1}/\xi)^{-1}. \tag{6} \] The finite inverse exists, with the opposite Euler coefficients, as proved in [T]. This is the coherent change that makes \(E_W-\xi K_W\) unitary and bounds the normalized shared resolvent by three. The transformed actual source and its original row are \[ \overline{\mathcal Y}_b=S_W^{-1}\mathcal Y_b,\qquad \overline\Lambda_b(w)=\Lambda_b(S_Ww),\qquad \Lambda_b(y)=(\ell^{\otimes(k-1)}\otimes m)\Phi_{f_y}. \tag{7} \] Here \(\Phi_{f_y}\) is the literal source reconstruction, not an independently prepared exterior. The original external factor \(\chi_N\), when present, multiplies this row unchanged. ## 2. The source slice that selects the corner Let \(A=V\otimes V\). Literal currying identifies invariant tensors with the actual unrolled Hopf maps \(f:A\to W\): \[ \Phi_f=(I\otimes f\otimes I)(p_{12}\otimes p_{34}),\qquad \mathscr D_b\Phi_f=f(\mathbf u), \tag{8} \] \[ \mathbf u_{ab}=C_D\tau^a,\qquad \tau=-Q^{-1},\qquad C_D=N^2\sin^2(3\theta)q^{3d}. \tag{9} \] All these scalars are those of [O,T]. In particular they are nonzero at every \(N\ge2\). Let \(P_t^A\) denote the orthogonal projection onto pair integer degree \(a+b=t\), and define \[ c_{\rm edge}=\frac{2C_D\tau^d}{1-q^3}. \tag{10} \] The essential source identity is \[ \boxed{\qquad P_d^A S_A^{-1}\mathbf u =c_{\rm edge}|d,0\rangle .\qquad} \tag{11} \] We prove it with the finite root cutoff retained. On the pair put \[ A_1=E_1K_1^{-1},\qquad A_2=K_1^{-1}E_2K_2^{-1}. \] Then \(E_AK_A^{-1}=A_1+A_2\) and \(A_1A_2=QA_2A_1\). The root Gaussian expansion gives \[ S_A^{-1}=\sum_{i+j<N} \frac{\xi^{-(i+j)}A_2^jA_1^i}{(Q;Q)_i(Q;Q)_j}. \tag{12} \] The product \(\mathsf e_N(A_2/\xi)\mathsf e_N(A_1/\xi)\) has the same terms with \(i+j<N\), plus terms with \(i+j\ge N\). Each latter term lowers total physical degree by at least \(N\). It cannot contribute to output degree \(d\), since the required input degree is at least \(d+N=2d+1\), beyond the actual pair. Consequently \[ P_d^A S_A^{-1} =P_d^A\mathsf e_N(A_2/\xi)\mathsf e_N(A_1/\xi). \tag{13} \] This is a slice identity only. The two finite Euler factors have not been asserted to factor the whole operator in (6). On the first-head factor \((\tau^a)_a\), direct use of (2) gives \[ \frac{\mathsf e_N(A_1/\xi)(\tau^a)_a}{\tau^a} =\sum_{i=0}^{d-a}Q^i{a+i\brack i}_Q ={N\brack a+1}_Q=\delta_{a,d}. \tag{14} \] The finite sum follows by telescoping the Gaussian Pascal identity. For \(a<d\), its top index is \(N\), its lower index lies strictly between zero and \(N\), and its root value is zero. For \(a=d\) the sum has its single value one, as does \({N\brack N}_Q\). Thus the first factor collapses the first head to \(d\), including all endpoints. At that head, \(K_1^{-1}\) has eigenvalue \(x\). On the second-head all-ones vector the value at output zero of the remaining Euler factor is \[ \sum_{j=0}^{d}\xi^{-j} =(q^3Q;Q)_d=\frac{2}{1-q^3}. \tag{15} \] For the first equality, \((xE_2K_2^{-1})^j\mathbf1\) at zero has coefficient \((Q;Q)_j\). The geometric sum uses \(\xi^N=-1\). The product equality also follows from \((q^3Q;Q)_N=2\) by removing its last factor \(1-q^3\). Equations (13)--(15) prove (11), with its exact phase and factor two. No small-level exception is needed, including \(N=2\). ## 3. The original closing on the coherent source At four heads the actual curried map is an endomorphism of \(A\). By [P] it is a unique polynomial \(g(\Omega)\) modulo the complete Casimir polynomial, with every repeated-root derivative retained. Let \(J=\Omega|_{A_d}\) in the original degree-\(d\) basis \(|a,d-a\rangle\). The literal closing functional satisfies \[ \lambda_4(g)=\phi(g)=(g(J))_{0,d}. \tag{16} \] This is the fixed-root marked functional of [P,T], not an ordinary trace on the distinct Casimir values. The Casimir commutes with the total \(E,K\), and therefore with \(S_A\). It also preserves full integer degree. If \(w=S_A^{-1}g(\Omega)\mathbf u\), (11) implies \[ w_{0,d}=c_{\rm edge}(g(J))_{0,d}. \] Thus the original transformed row is exactly \[ \boxed{\qquad \overline\Lambda_4(w) =c_{\rm edge}^{-1}w_{0,d} \quad(w\in\overline{\mathcal Y}_4).\qquad} \tag{17} \] Equation (17) gives another physical extension of the same restricted functional as \(\alpha_4S_A\) from [T]. The intrinsic dual estimate below uses the new corner row. For \(b=2k\), let \[ L_{\rm int}=I\otimes\ell^{\otimes(k-2)}\otimes I:W\to A. \tag{18} \] These are exactly the interior ordinary caps in the original last-mark closing. They are actual Hopf maps and intertwine the finite Euler operators, so \(L_{\rm int}S_W=S_A L_{\rm int}\). For every source map \(f\), the map \(L_{\rm int}f:A\to A\) is an actual pair endomorphism. Apply (17) to it. The full-width original row therefore has the exact extension \[ \boxed{\qquad \overline\Lambda_b(w) =c_{\rm edge}^{-1}\langle0,d|L_{\rm int}w, \quad w\in\overline{\mathcal Y}_b . \qquad} \tag{19} \] No marked-cap relocation is used. All original powers of \(N\), the last mark and the external \(\chi_N\) remain on this formula. ## 4. Polynomial intrinsic dual norm on the actual saturated source Let \(\|\overline\Lambda_b\|_{\overline{\mathcal Y}_b^*}\) mean the dual norm with the physical norm restricted to this transformed source. From (10), \(|C_D|=N^2\sin^2(3\theta)\), and (19), \[ \|c_{\rm edge}^{-1}\langle0,d|L_{\rm int}\| =\frac{N^{-(k+2)/2}}{\sin3\theta}. \tag{20} \] This is an extension norm, hence an upper bound for that intrinsic norm. There is also a source witness with no unknown scalar in its definition. Prepend cups by the actual intertwiner \[ J_{\rm chain}(v\otimes w)=p^{\otimes(k-2)}\otimes v\otimes w. \tag{21} \] The caps (18) run through the seams of this chain. Repeated literal snake equations give \(L_{\rm int}J_{\rm chain}=I_A\). This differs from inserting cups between the two free heads, which would produce zero ordinary bubbles under (18). Set \(f_*=J_{\rm chain}(p\ell)\). Its curried tensor is a regular generic cup matching and therefore belongs to \(\mathcal S_b\). The original closing has value \(\phi(p\ell)=1\). Since \(S_A^{-1}p=p\), its transformed observation is \[ w_*=S_W^{-1}f_*(\mathbf u) =J_{\rm chain}p\,\ell(\mathbf u),\qquad \ell(\mathbf u)=\frac{2C_D}{N(1-\xi)}. \tag{22} \] For the last identity use \(x\tau=\xi\) in the literal cap (4). The norm of \(J_{\rm chain}p\) is \(N^{3(k-1)/2}\). Using this actual source vector in the dual norm gives \[ \boxed{\qquad \frac{N^{-(3k-1)/2}}{\sin3\theta} \ \le\ \|\overline\Lambda_b\|_{\overline{\mathcal Y}_b^*} \ \le\ \frac{N^{-(k+2)/2}}{\sin3\theta}. \qquad} \tag{23} \] These inequalities hold at every \(N\ge2\). In particular the intrinsic co-source norm has zero exponential rate at fixed width. If \(\chi_N\) is folded into the row, both bounds are multiplied by \(|\chi_N|\); no bound on that separate original factor is implied. This is a norm of a functional, not a nonzero lower bound for its value on an arbitrary word state. ## 5. A faithful orthogonal degree projection Put \(D=(k-1)d\), and let \(P_D^W\) be the physical orthogonal projection onto middle integer degree \(D\); write \(W_D=\operatorname{ran}P_D^W\). An unrolled map \(f:A\to W\) sends input degree \(t\) to degree \((k-2)d+t\). Therefore (8),(11) give \[ \boxed{\qquad \mathscr F_b\Phi_f:=P_D^W S_W^{-1}\mathscr D_b\Phi_f =c_{\rm edge} f(|d,0\rangle). \qquad} \tag{24} \] In the literal curry coordinates this is also \[ f(|d,0\rangle)=\frac{x^{2d}}{N^2}\Phi_{0,W,d}. \tag{25} \] The unsimplified scalar records the ordered cup normalization; \(x^{2d}=Q\). Evaluation at \(|d,0\rangle\) is faithful on all these intertwiners. Indeed [P]'s middle Casimir \(J\) is tridiagonal with every adjacent entry nonzero. The vectors \(J^r|d,0\rangle\), \(0\le r<N\), form a triangular basis of \(A_d\). The actual \(E,F\) surjections in [P] generate the whole pair from \(A_d\). Hence an intertwiner vanishing at \(|d,0\rangle\) vanishes everywhere. This argument retains the entire pair, including each Casimir Jordan direction. The complete dimension formula in [M] is \[ \dim\mathcal I_b=[z^{(k-1)d}](1+z+\cdots+z^d)^{2k-2} =\dim W_D . \tag{26} \] It follows that (24) is an isomorphism \(\mathcal I_b\to W_D\). The saturated image is the same explicit physical source kernel already identified in [D]: \[ \mathscr F_b(\mathcal S_b) =\ker(\mathcal J_E^W:W_D\longrightarrow W_{D-N}),\qquad \mathcal J_E^W= \left[\frac{E_W(\zeta)^N}{1-\zeta^{2N}}\right]_{\zeta=q}. \tag{26a} \] The target is zero if its degree is negative. To prove inclusion, take a regular generic invariant lift and its literal generic curry \(f_\zeta\). Since the input \(|d,0\rangle\) has degree \(d<N\), \(E_A(\zeta)^N|d,0\rangle=0\) identically. Thus \(E_W(\zeta)^N f_\zeta|d,0\rangle=0\). Division by the specified factor and specialization give the equation in (26a). The nonzero scalar \(c_{\rm edge}\) does not change its kernel. The dimension and surjectivity theorem in [D] gives \(\dim\mathcal S_b=\dim W_D-\dim W_{D-N}\), equal to that kernel's dimension, proving equality. Its redundant \(\mathcal J_F\) equation and differentiated inhomogeneous source equations retain [D]'s scope. In particular, the saturated source is not every vector of \(W_D\) when this divided-current condition is nontrivial. The prescribed input and row in these degree coordinates are especially simple: \[ z_{\rm in}=c_{\rm edge}|d\rangle\otimes p^{\otimes(k-2)}\otimes|0\rangle, \qquad \lambda_D=c_{\rm edge}^{-1}\langle0,d|L_{\rm int}. \tag{27} \] The row is already supported in degree \(D\). Its restriction to \(W_D\) has the same norm as the displayed physical extension. Consequently the exact polynomial boundary product is \[ \|z_{\rm in}\|\,\|\lambda_D\| =N^{k-2}. \tag{28} \] The exponential input cost of the full coherent packet in [T] is thus absent from this source-faithful projected input. This does not make the transported word norm inexpensive. For each original regular signed braid the correct reduced operator is \(\mathscr F_b R_i\mathscr F_b^{-1}\), restricted to (26a) when required. Products and the literal closing transport exactly. One cannot instead insert \(P_D^W\) between untransported crossings: the projection need not commute with those operators or reconstruct their components. ## 6. Actual generators on the projected packet The projected Casimirs also have direct formulas. Write \(n=b-2\), and let totals over the indicated proper blocks use (3). On \(W_D\), put \[ \begin{split} L&=q^{-1}F_1K_1E_{2,\ldots,n}-K_1-K_1^{-1},\\ R&=qK_n^{-1}E_nF_{1,\ldots,n-1}-K_n-K_n^{-1}. \end{split} \tag{29} \] Then the first and last original pair Casimirs transport to \(L,R\), and every interior one remains \(\Omega^W_{i-1,i}\). These operators preserve integer degree. Their full physical bounds are \[ \|L\|,\|R\|\le4(n-1)+2. \tag{30} \] These are bounds for the Casimirs, not for their level-dependent braid polynomials. Here is an endpoint derivation fixing the orders. Let \(z=f|d,0\rangle\); the common scalar in (24) is irrelevant to operator conjugation. The literal total actions on this input give \[ f|d-1,0\rangle=\frac{E_Wz}{x(Q-1)},\qquad f|d,1\rangle=\frac{F_Wz}{x(1-Q)}. \tag{31} \] The denominators are nonzero, and will cancel. Apply [T]'s two cup transpose operator identities before evaluating on this input. At the left endpoint the first input-head \(F\) term is zero, since \(F|d\rangle=0\). The resulting Casimir is \[ q^{-1}F_1K_1E_Wz+(Q-1)K_1z+2qz. \tag{32} \] On degree \(D\), the total \(K_W\) is one. In \(E_W=E_1K_{2,\ldots,n}+E_{2,\ldots,n}\), its first term therefore contributes \(qF_1E_1z\) to (32). The one-head identity \(FE=-2-qK-q^{-1}K^{-1}\) cancels the remaining diagonal terms, giving \(Lz\). The right cup transpose similarly gives \[ qK_n^{-1}E_nF_Wz+(Q-1)K_n^{-1}z+2qz. \tag{33} \] Use \(F_W=F_{1,\ldots,n-1}+K_{1,\ldots,n-1}^{-1}F_n\) and \(K_Wz=z\). The second term contributes \(qE_nF_nz\). The identity \(EF=-2-q^{-1}K-qK^{-1}\) now gives \(Rz\). This proves both formulas, including the physical endpoint zeros. The interior formulas follow by disjoint contraction. The bounds (30) use \(\|E_{2,\ldots,n}\|,\|F_{1,\ldots,n-1}\| \le2(n-1)\), and the local head bounds in (2). Put \(\kappa=q^{d^2/2}\). For the original degree-\(<N\) Hermite braid polynomial \(r_N\), the reduced positive crossings are \(\kappa r_N(L)\), \(\kappa r_N(R)\), and \(\kappa r_N(\Omega^W_{i-1,i})\). Their negatives use the literal inverse polynomial modulo the complete Casimir polynomial. All first derivatives at repeated roots remain. These matrices preserve (26a) and satisfy the original braid relations because they are exact transports. No sharp coherent product bound or bounded degree for \(r_N\) is inferred from (30). ## 7. Scope and earlier complete reductions [M] already gives complete all-width central-degree source modules, bounded-degree Casimir formulas and polynomial original boundaries. At four heads, the coordinate \(f|d,0\rangle\) is exactly \((x^d/N)Jw\) in its opposite highest chart, where \(w,J\) are [M]'s original multiplicity vector and recoupling matrix. [O] already proves faithful observations with explicit reconstruction and actual source constraints. [P] already retains every repeated-root Casimir normal and gives the original endpoint functional. [T] already gives the coherent metric, its full input cost and the literal physical closing row. [D] already proves the regular divided-current kernel and its exact source dimension. The additions are the exact source slice (11), the resulting cheap extension of the original coherent closing, the actual-source dual sandwich (23), and the identification of the faithful orthogonal degree projection (24), with the actual generators on that projected packet. The finite Euler tools, the existence of central multiplicity coordinates and the earlier source kernel are not claimed new. All statements concern the actual fixed-root source. Differentiated source families keep their original inhomogeneous normal equations. No geometric saddle, arbitrary coherent scalar noncancellation, or finite-exception volume theorem after general short partial fillings follows from the polynomial boundary budget alone. ## Complete inputs and closest coverage | Label | Complete text | Lines | SHA256 | | --- | --- | ---: | --- | | T | [Boundary Casimir transport](research_all_width_marked_boundary_casimir_transport.md) | 828 | 357eee1e3cd0e65149a77fb2fb714bdd75c3a5e64642ac1f26bb3c08daadf381 | | O | [All-width marked-mode observation](research_all_width_marked_mode_observation.md) | 591 | b2ec8912696338d23e67e2ceb3e69a3fd5a1e20dfcfbe49228cd514a7d40f3f7 | | M | [Complete original source multiplicities](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_complete_source_multiplicity_module.md) | 602 | 14cfb558f50c5b091cec9439692dfeb87129e31f38588cb1ebfd8e8547ac99a9 | | P | [Full physical pair commutant](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_pair_casimir_commutant_and_rotated_trace.md) | 331 | 00ab946b3eddb61256bdbd8ec487789a15991a80e1a28b4eee53bbb4a00f7666 | | D | [All-width divided-current source restriction](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_all_width_divided_source_projection.md) | 204 | dc83b5e232a3d258f516a479d7257e85b9e5663a38e166f07c6ad9ae81004a68 | Only written mathematics, source reads and text/hash operations were used.
