title: An exact auxiliary-height identity for the original marked closing
Balanced marked observations at every coideal height
Bidiagonal transport of full neighboring-height frames
text: # Bidiagonal transport of full neighboring-height frames 24 November 2026. Written research proof. The neighboring-height frame in P has an exact first-order update on each parity of the physical height grid. The update retains all \(N\) coordinates. A binomial estimate controls its accumulated full Gram, including every coherent cross term, at subexponential cost across any \(o(N)\) height steps. This is a simplification of the actual source coefficients, not an evaluation of the global quartic minimum. ## 1. Full frames and the specified source Let \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\), and \(\sqrt q=e^{\pi i/(2N)}\). All fractional phases below mean these exponentials. For \(0\le j\le d\), put \[ \alpha_j=(j+\tfrac12)\pi/N,\quad \lambda_j=2\sqrt q\cos\alpha_j=q^{j+1}+q^{-j},\quad \mu_j=\sin\alpha_j,\quad F_a=(Q;Q)_a=\prod_{h=1}^a(1-Q^h). \] The empty product is one. Use P's complete continuants \[ D_{-1}=0,\quad D_0=1,\qquad D_{a+1}(\lambda;\sigma)=(\lambda+qQ^a\sigma)D_a -q(1-Q^a)^2D_{a-1}, \] \[ (U_s)_{aj}=q^{-a}D_a(\lambda_j;\lambda_s)/F_a, \qquad 0\le a,j,s\le d. \tag{1} \] Here \(U_s\) means \(U_{\lambda_s}\) of P, not a truncation of that matrix. It is invertible. In coefficient coordinates let \(Ze_a=e_{a+1}\) for \(a<d\) and \(Ze_d=0\), with \(e_a\) the standard orthonormal basis. Thus \(Z^N=0\) and its counting operator norm is one. The specified height gauge and source are \[ f_j=e^{i\pi j(j+1)/(4N)},\quad S=\operatorname{diag}((-1)^j\mu_j/f_j),\quad W_s=U_sS,\quad G_s=W_s^\dagger W_s. \tag{2} \] The matrix \(G_s\) is the pullback of the coefficient counting metric. It is not identified with the earlier positive height metric \(G_{\rm ht}\). For a vector \(x\), write \(\|x\|_{G_s}^2=x^\dagger G_sx\). ## 2. One physical height update For \(0\le s\le N-3\), the exact full-frame relation is \[ A_s:=U_{s+2}U_s^{-1} =(I+q^{-s-2}Z)(I+q^{s+1}Z)^{-1}. \tag{3} \] Every inverse here is its finite geometric sum modulo \(Z^N\). In particular \[ (I+q^{s+1}Z)U_{s+2}=(I+q^{-s-2}Z)U_s. \tag{4} \] Both multipliers are unit lower bidiagonal. This constructs every physical frame from \(U_0\) or \(U_1\) by linear solves, without discarding an endpoint coordinate. For \(N=2\), no such update is required. For proof, define \[ \Phi_{\lambda,\sigma}(z) =\sum_{a=0}^dD_a(\lambda;\sigma)z^a/F_a. \] P(17)--(19) prove, modulo \(z^N\), \[ (1-\lambda z+qz^2)\Phi_{\lambda,\sigma}(z) =N_\sigma(z)\Phi_{\lambda,\sigma}(Qz),\qquad N_\sigma(z)=1+q\sigma z+q^3z^2. \] At the actual physical root \(\sigma=\lambda_s\), this numerator factors as \[ N_s(z)=(1+q^{s+2}z)(1+q^{1-s}z). \] The rational function \[ R_s(z)=\frac{1+q^{-s-1}z}{1+q^{s+2}z} \] has constant term one and satisfies \(R_s(z)N_s(z)=N_{s+2}(z)R_s(Qz)\) identically. The unique constant-one solution modulo \(z^N\) therefore gives \(\Phi_{\lambda,\lambda_{s+2}}=R_s\Phi_{\lambda,\lambda_s}\). Uniqueness uses only \(1-Q^a\ne0\) for \(0<a<N\), so includes composite \(N\). P's coefficient conversion substitutes \(z=q^{-1}Z\) into \(R_s\), proving (3). No top-degree boundary remainder occurs. ## 3. Accumulated cost for coherent packets For \(k\ge1\) with \(0\le s<s+2k\le d\), set \[ A_{s,k}=U_{s+2k}U_s^{-1} =\prod_{j=0}^{k-1} (I+q^{-s-2-2j}Z)(I+q^{s+1+2j}Z)^{-1},\qquad D_{N,k}=2^k\binom{N+k-1}{k}. \tag{5} \] The quotient denotes commuting matrix multiplication and inversion. For \(k=0\), set \(A_{s,0}=I\) and \(D_{N,0}=1\). Then \[ \|A_{s,k}\|_2,\ \|A_{s,k}^{-1}\|_2\le D_{N,k}, \] \[ D_{N,k}^{-2}G_s\preceq G_{s+2k}\preceq D_{N,k}^{2}G_s. \tag{6} \] The order in (6) is the Hermitian positive-semidefinite order. It controls arbitrary complex coherent packets simultaneously. The same inequality holds for \(U_s^\dagger U_s\) before the \(S\) gauge. To prove the bound, a product of \(k\) numerator factors has coefficient \(\ell^1\) norm at most \(2^k\). The coefficient of \(z^m\) in the inverse of the \(k\) denominator factors is a sum of \(\binom{m+k-1}{k-1}\) unit-modulus terms. Consequently its truncated coefficient \(\ell^1\) norm is at most \[ \sum_{m=0}^{N-1}\binom{m+k-1}{k-1}=\binom{N+k-1}{k}. \] Multiplication and truncation cannot increase the product \(\ell^1\) bound. For \(\sum_mc_mZ^m\), its operator norm is at most \(\sum_m|c_m|\). Interchanging numerator and denominator proves the inverse bound. Applying both bounds to \(W_sx\) proves the Gram comparison, with no omission of cross terms or replacement of a Gram matrix by the identity. The elementary factorial estimate gives \[ \log D_{N,k}\le k\log\frac{2e(N+k-1)}{k}. \tag{7} \] Thus \(k=k_N=o(N)\) implies \(\log D_{N,k}=o(N)\), uniformly in the starting physical height. This uses \((k/N)\log(N/k)\to0\); multiplying a separate \(2N\) bound at every step would lose this improvement. In particular, arbitrary nonzero \(N\)-dependent coherent packets have the same leading logarithmic norm in these frames across \(o(N)\) same-parity steps. All statements concern the full \(N\)-dimensional frames, not selected spectral windows. They do not identify the two parity starting frames. ## 4. Source and original marked observation P(11) fixes the source normalization exactly: \[ W_sf=q^{-d/2}e_d,\qquad \|f\|_{G_s}=1. \tag{8} \] Every \(A_{s,k}\) fixes \(e_d\). The full height-coordinate transport \[ H_{t\leftarrow s}=W_t^{-1}W_s,\qquad t=s+2k, \] satisfies \(H^\dagger G_tH=G_s\) and \(Hf=f\). In the same fixed metric \(G_s\), its norm and inverse norm are at most \(D_{N,k}\), since \(W_sHW_s^{-1}=A_{s,k}^{-1}\). Only for the marked primitive \(\nu=c=1+q\), P(13)--(16) give the canonical mode row \[ \ell_s=v^{\mathsf T}W_s,\quad v_a=(-Q)^a,\qquad \ell_sf=\omega_N=i(-1)^{N-2}q^{-3/2}. \] Its exact dual norm and initialized angle are therefore \[ \ell_sG_s^{-1}\ell_s^\dagger=N,\qquad \frac{|\ell_sf|}{\|f\|_{G_s}\|\ell_s\|_{G_s^{-1}}} =\frac1{\sqrt N},\qquad \ell_tH_{t\leftarrow s}=\ell_s. \tag{9} \] Indeed \(v^{\mathsf T}\overline v=N\) and \(W_sf\) has only its last coordinate. The physical row is \(\beta_N\ell_s\), with \(\beta_N=(T_*/A_c)\kappa(1-q)/2\) and \(\kappa=q^{d^2/2}\); \(T_*\) and \(A_c\) are P's original boundary constants. Its dual norm is \(|\beta_N|\sqrt N\) and its initialized period is \(\beta_N\omega_N\). The original exterior \(\chi_N\) remains external. No physical row is silently normalized to unit residue. ## 5. Relation to the fixed-degree problem Equations (4) are linear in the full packet coefficients. They compare frame columns, or \(U_sx\) and \(U_{s+2}x\) for one common vector \(x\); they impose no relation between independently summed physical height sectors. They may be retained as auxiliary linear equations when these frames are used; they introduce quadratic squared residuals rather than higher-degree products. Eliminating these constant-coefficient frame equations is a linear substitution and preserves polynomial degree. This does not identify the simple coideal module with the confluent Casimir algebra of the original Conway quartic compiler or remove its bilinear multiplication gates. The initialized marked angle in (9) is polynomially small. After an arbitrary original short tangle, the direction and observed scalar can change. The comparison retains the source, cap, phases and full Gram; it does not bound that later marked angle below or compare the norm rate with hyperbolic volume. No fixed \(G_{\rm ht}\) metric bound, universal braid unitarity, or finite-exception theorem follows from this note. ## Complete input and coverage The sole complete selected proof input is [P](research_coideal_normalized_marked_period.md), 410 lines, SHA256 \[ \texttt{e5e7ab88016f682411258ccab299f4b7bc2ab6e7052366729d59d993abf84d4b}. \] P already gives the general Toeplitz neighbor comparison and exact source/mark transport. The refinement here is its explicit bidiagonal physical update, the full coherent Gram bound (6)--(7), and its stated pullback metric normalization. No novelty for binomial counting or pullback inner products is claimed. Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used. Earlier final notes, public manuscripts and the progress ledger remain unchanged.

title: A crossing between an ordinary and a marked cap gives a cumulative sum
A common orthogonal basis for coherent crossing amplitudes
text: # A common orthogonal basis for coherent crossing amplitudes 24 November 2026. Research note. Written proof. For fixed actual neighboring heights, one real symmetric Jacobi matrix handles every input label in the cooriented crossing block. Its orthogonal basis is independent of that input. Consequently the actual sum over inputs is an exact finite Cauchy transform in each output mode, and its full cross-input Gram is a divided difference of a matrix resolvent. Here coherent means that the input sum is taken before an absolute square. These are exact finite source identities. The complementary input can contribute to the same output modes and remains inside those squares. Neither positivity of the Gram nor polynomial conditioning of the Jacobi matrix gives injectivity or a polynomial lower bound for that input map. ## 1. Fixed source domains without ordering the middle labels Use the complete conventions of G,H,N,T: \[ N\ge2,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\quad d=N-1,\quad \delta=\pi/N,\quad \sqrt q=e^{\pi i/(2N)},\quad \lambda_r=2\sqrt q\cos\alpha_r,\quad \alpha_r=(r+\tfrac12)\delta,\quad\mu_r=\sin\alpha_r. \tag{1} \] All indices are between zero and d. Write J(r,t;v,s) for G's actual phase-removed mixed-continuant coefficient. Fix the two physical neighbor indices (v,s), put S=max(v,s), T_0=N-S-2, and let \(\mathcal C=\{0,\ldots,T_0\}\). If T_0<0 this set is empty and the whole physical block is retained literally. Otherwise put \[ a=\max(\cos\alpha_v,\cos\alpha_s),\quad b=\min(\cos\alpha_v,\cos\alpha_s)=\cos\alpha_S,\quad x_t=\cos\alpha_t,\quad y_r=\cos\alpha_r . \tag{2} \] This is numerical ordering of two scalars. No physical neighbor swap or symmetry of a complementary block is asserted. G's amplitude symmetry allows its wall formula to use this S with the original (v,s). The source recurrence, algebraically valid for every input r, is \[ c_t^+J(r,t+2)+d_tJ(r,t)+c_t^-J(r,t-2)=2y_rJ(r,t), \] \[ c_t^\pm={(\cos(\alpha_t\pm\delta)+a) (\cos(\alpha_t\pm\delta)+b)\over \sin\alpha_t\sin(\alpha_t\pm\delta)},\qquad d_t={-2[x_t(1+ab)+(a+b)\cos\delta]\over \sin^2\alpha_t-\sin^2\delta}. \tag{3} \] It follows from N's finite cyclic relation and T's actual crossing intertwining, as derived in G. It is not restricted to r<=t. The positivity bound also needs no such ordering. Write c_delta=cos(delta), L_0=-cos((S+3/2)delta), u_0=c_delta+L_0 and K_0=(1-a)(1-b). For all \(r,t\in\mathcal C\), x_t,y_r>=L_0 and u_0>1-b. Therefore the row defect on every used interior row obeys \[ \omega_t(r)=2\left[y_r+c_\delta-{K_0\over c_\delta+x_t}\right] \ge2\left[u_0-{(1-b)^2\over u_0}\right] \ge4\sin(\delta/2)[\sin((S+1)\delta)-\sin(\delta/2)] \ge cN^{-2}. \tag{4} \] Here u_0-(1-b)=2sin(delta/2)[sin((S+1)delta)-sin(delta/2)]. Every edge coefficient used in the interiors I_p or their incident Dirichlet boundaries is positive and bounded by CN^2. For p=0,1 with p<=T_0 define the fixed interior \(I_p=\{p+2,p+4,\ldots\}\cap\mathcal C\). Keep the literal lower output row t=p. If the last interior is T_0, its outgoing coefficient is exactly zero. If it is T_0-1, retain the literal wall row u=T_0+1. The latter coefficient J(r,u;v,s) is the calibrated wall value proved in G, for every \(r\in\mathcal C\). Boundary couplings are always taken from the incident interior row. Equation (3) is used only on these interior output rows; it is valid for every input r. The lower rows p=0,1 remain literal boundary rows. For S=0 the possible terminal row t=N-2 has its upper folded edge killed by the actual source cut in N; (3) is used with that term omitted. Empty interiors require no recurrence or inverse. This includes every cooriented block at N=2,3 and the cases T_0=0,1. ## 2. One input-independent symmetric matrix For a nonempty I_p, let L_p be (3) on I_p, omitting boundary terms from its matrix but keeping the original diagonal d_t. Put D_p=diag(sqrt(mu_t)) on I_p and \[ y_*=\cos\alpha_{T_0},\quad A_p=D_p(2y_*I-L_p)D_p^{-1},\qquad \tau_r=2(y_r-y_*)\ge0\quad(r\in\mathcal C). \tag{5} \] Detailed balance is exact: \(\mu_tc_t^+=\mu_{t+2}c_{t+2}^-\). Thus A_p is real symmetric. More explicitly, with w=D_p^{-1}z, \[ \begin{split} z^*(A_p+\tau_rI)z={}& \sum_{\text{internal edges}}\mu_tc_t^+|w_{t+2}-w_t|^2\\ &+\sum_{\text{boundary exits}}\mu_tc_{\rm exit}|w_t|^2 +\sum_{t\in I_p}\mu_t\omega_t(r)|w_t|^2 . \end{split} \] Boundary coefficients are taken from the incident interior rows. Formula (4) therefore gives \[ cN^{-2}I\le A_p+\tau_rI\le CN^2I,\qquad 0\le\tau_r\le4. \tag{6} \] For the lower bound the displayed form is at least sum omega_t(r)|z_t|^2. For the upper bound the off-diagonal entries are minus sqrt(c_t^+c_{t+2}^-), and the diagonal is bounded by CN^2. These bounds include A_p itself and give condition at most CN^4. Choose a real orthogonal O_p with \(O_p^TA_pO_p=\operatorname{diag}(\kappa_1,\ldots,\kappa_m)\). It can be fixed canonically: order eigenvalues increasingly and choose each eigenvector's first coordinate positive. A nonempty irreducible Jacobi path has simple eigenvalues and no eigenvector with first coordinate zero, since its first row and recurrence determine all coordinates. The one-dimensional case uses O_p=1. Thus this is a finite algebraic choice depending on N and the actual neighbors, not on r or on a completed-word coefficient. Let b_L have its only nonzero entry sqrt(mu_first)c_first^-. On a wall branch let b_R have its only nonzero entry sqrt(mu_last)c_last^+; omit it on a natural branch. Set \[ B_p=(b_L\ b_R),\quad \rho_r=\sqrt{\mu_r}\binom{J(r,p;v,s)}{J(r,u;v,s)},\quad K_{tr}=\sqrt{\mu_t\mu_r}\,J(r,t;v,s),\quad t\in I_p,\ r\in\mathcal C, \tag{7} \] with just the first column and first component on a natural branch. All entries of rho are original finite source boundary values. The exact crossing recurrence now reads \[ (A_p+\tau_rI)K_{\bullet r}=B_p\rho_r,\qquad A_pK+K\operatorname{diag}(\tau_r)=B_p(\rho_r)_r . \tag{8} \] The right side has rank at most two. This is the actual finite Sylvester displacement relation for the cooriented crossing rectangle. ## 3. Coherent sums and the cooriented block's Gram Write R_p(s)=(A_p+sI)^{-1}. For any complex input vector xi on \(\mathcal C\), (8) gives, in the one fixed output basis, \[ (O_p^TK\xi)_k =\sum_{r\in\mathcal C} {(O_p^TB_p\rho_r)_k\over\kappa_k+\tau_r}\,\xi_r,\qquad \|K\xi\|^2=\sum_k\left| \sum_{r\in\mathcal C}{(O_p^TB_p\rho_r)_k\xi_r \over\kappa_k+\tau_r}\right|^2. \tag{9} \] The input sum is inside each square. Orthogonality does not replace it by a sum of column energies. The modes and boundary vectors can have signs, and xi can be complex. The entire Gram between different inputs also has an exact small response formula. For real s>=0 put \[ W_p(s)=B_p^TR_p(s)B_p,\qquad \mathcal L_p(s,t)= \begin{cases}[W_p(s)-W_p(t)]/(t-s),&s\ne t,\\-W_p'(s),&s=t. \end{cases} \tag{10} \] Resolvent multiplication gives \[ \mathcal L_p(s,t)=B_p^TR_p(s)R_p(t)B_p,\qquad (K^\dagger K)_{rq}=\rho_r^T\mathcal L_p(\tau_r,\tau_q)\rho_q . \tag{11} \] These formulas include coincident shifts without subtractive ambiguity. The matrix-valued kernel is positive semidefinite: for arbitrary real s_r>=0 and complex vectors h_r of the boundary dimension, \[ \sum_{r,q}h_r^*\mathcal L_p(s_r,s_q)h_q =\left\|\sum_rR_p(s_r)B_ph_r\right\|^2\ge0 . \tag{12} \] Rank at most two applies to the forcing in (8), not to K or its Gram. The literal output rows p=0,1 that lie in \(\mathcal C\) remain separate. Their entries are sqrt(mu_p mu_r)J(r,p); add their rank-one row Grams to (11), and sum over the disjoint interior parities. This gives the complete Gram of the cooriented rectangle, including every cross-input term. Empty interiors contribute no resolvent term. W_p is a finite rational response of this specified Jacobi matrix. Its poles are the negative eigenvalues -kappa_k. This is not asserted to be a peripheral parameter or an off-grid continuation of the entire original quantum source. The uniform condition of A_p does not imply injectivity or polynomial conditioning of K, its input Gram, or a coherent scalar observation. ## 4. The actual metric, phases and the complementary input Use H's absolute-height metric G_ht, not T's physical joint Haar form. In its globally orthonormal nested height coordinates, G and H give \[ \widetilde B^\epsilon_{tr} =(f_vf_s)^\epsilon\,(-1)^t f_t^{-\epsilon} \sqrt{\mu_t\mu_r}\,J(r,t;v,s)f_r^{-\epsilon},\quad f_r=e^{i\pi r(r+1)/(4N)},\quad\epsilon=\pm1, \tag{13} \] for the cooriented rectangle. The original scalar is included: \(\kappa=q^{d^2/2}\) and \(\kappa q^{d/2}i^{-d}=1\). There are no neighboring h_N volume corrections in this metric. All diagonal chirps displayed in (13) are unitary; their removal is only a change of coordinates, not a replacement of signed coefficients by positive ones. For each actual fixed (v,s) sector, extend the real O_p on its interiors by identity on its literal boundary rows and on t outside \(\mathcal C\). Together these blocks define one full conditional unitary O_ext. Keep the separate known diagonal phase matrices on all heights, even where (13)'s positive amplitude assertion is not used. The complete output basis change is V=P_epsilon O_ext, where P_epsilon has diagonal (-1)^t f_t^{-epsilon}. It is unitary in G_ht and preserves the full finite dimension. In particular the physical input need not lie in \(\mathcal C\). Split it only for bookkeeping as a=a_C+a_Q. In an interior output mode the full transformed output is \[ [V^\dagger\widetilde B^\epsilon a]_k =(f_vf_s)^\epsilon[O_p^TK\xi]_k +[V^\dagger\widetilde B^\epsilon a_Q]_k,\qquad \xi_r=f_r^{-\epsilon}(a_C)_r . \tag{14} \] Both terms remain inside the same absolute square. The boundary output rows and the complementary output rows are retained literally as well. There is no orthogonal separation by input support, and no discarded leakage block. Nor is symmetry of any complementary physical block inferred by numerically ordering a,b. ## 5. Exact sewing and its limits These full conditional unitaries may be used as coordinate changes at arbitrary stages of an actual finite composition. Interfaces are products of the neighboring full basis changes and hence are unitary, even for overlapping faces. They are retained as operators; they need not be the identity or preserve the diagonal Cauchy variables of the next crossing. For a full basis change V, the input becomes V^dagger u, the literal closing row becomes ell V, and any source constraint or projector P becomes V^dagger P V. No commutation or invariance of P is asserted. Thus the original scalar, marked position and external factor chi_N are unchanged. The source and cap norms already proved in H are unchanged in G_ht. All Casimir-normal data remain in these invertible full changes; no value-only quotient or source projection is inserted. This is not a claim that the braid operators themselves are unitary, or that G_ht is the physical Hilbert metric. It gives no additive rank bound for a whole word: consecutive Jacobi generators and their conditional bases depend on different neighboring heights. The exact cross-input Gram and the transformed marked row may still have a small or zero coherent overlap. No phase alignment, geometric cycle, global closed-scalar lower bound or arbitrary-short-filling theorem follows. J already treats a different original Newton-value Jacobi problem, its Fourier image and the distinct normal-weighted final observation. The abstract spectral theorem, resolvent identity and positive Gram identity are standard finite linear algebra. The additional content here is their exact common-output realization for all inputs of this coideal crossing rectangle, with the rank-at-most-two source forcing, full cross-input terms and literal source/closing transport. It does not replace the original global minimization by independent column energies. ## Complete inputs and closest coverage | Label | Complete text | Lines | SHA256 | | --- | --- | ---: | --- | | G | [All cooriented amplitudes](research_coideal_cooriented_volume_kernel.md) | 613 | 78fabcccdd4eb8e2bf4064ec281880cc551443d2d36eb72750f27c77506bd597 | | H | [Height pairing and marked boundary](research_coideal_height_pairing_and_marked_boundary.md) | 543 | bed81fcb12b20d16d41c55b476b13d8d69b1fe79d0d0620c31230ba652b1d82f | | N | [Actual coideal difference equation](research_coideal_marked_boundary_normal_gap.md) | 512 | bb9bd6d04480ae8733c0fd1c5901834bdf2ea3e8c7eb3617fb8eb58e66e57956 | | T | [Exact crossing transport](research_coideal_crossing_orthogonality_transport.md) | 595 | 4555fecc6377077dbdc4cfb3afac50f09d180efc5659716bac8497319310114c | | J | [Earlier physical Jacobi boundary](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_physical_jacobi_charge_boundary.md) | 432 | 530425b0c4504f2512954438465deb6d9a6e322fa58c641b6c678161baae6583 | Only written mathematics, complete source reads and text/hash operations were used. title: An explicit coideal kernel with the original cup calibration
text: # An explicit coideal kernel with the original cup calibration 24 November 2026. Written research proof. The actual conserved coideal admits polynomial kernel and cokernel maps, including its collision parameters. A trailing continuant removes the apparent inverse in their comparison. The original cup is the image of an explicit endpoint seed; at the source-selected parameter its spectral projection loses only a subexponential factor. The original marked closing remains a specified row on this kernel. No geometric cycle coefficient or scalar lower bound is inferred. ## 1. Actual matrices and continuants Use the complete balanced physical basis of C and S. Put \[ N\ge2,\quad d=N-1,\quad b=2k\ge2,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad \sqrt q=e^{\pi i/(2N)},\quad Q=q^2,\quad x=-q^{-1},\quad F_a=(Q;Q)_a,\quad F_0=1,\quad F_d=N . \tag{1} \] The basis is orthonormal. The actual one-head generators have entries \(Ke_a=xQ^{-a}e_a\), \(Ee_a=(Q^{-a}-1)e_{a-1}\), and \(Fe_a=(1-Q^{a+1})e_{a+1}\), with both missing endpoint arrows zero. For the ordered total generators define, as in C, \[ B_c=\mathsf F-(\mathsf E-cI)\mathsf K^{-1},\qquad T=B_c^{(b-1)},\qquad W=(\mathbb C^N)^{\otimes(b-1)} . \tag{2} \] Here \(c\) is an auxiliary parameter and \(B_c\) without a superscript acts on \(V=\mathbb C^N\otimes W\). Its first-head tridiagonal action is \[ (B_cu)_a=(1-Q^a)u_{a-1} +q(1-Q^{a+1})u_{a+1}-qQ^aTu_a . \tag{3} \] Only indices \(0,\ldots,d\) occur. Write \(\iota_a:W\to V\) and \(\pi_a:V\to W\) for coordinate insertion and extraction. Let \(D_a(\lambda;T)\) be the leading continuant on indices \(0,\ldots,a-1\) of \(\lambda I-B_c\), with \(T\) held fixed: \[ D_{-1}=0,\quad D_0=I,\qquad D_{a+1}=(\lambda+qQ^aT)D_a-q(1-Q^a)^2D_{a-1}. \tag{4} \] All its coefficients commute. Let \(E_d(\lambda;T)\) be the trailing continuant on indices \(1,\ldots,d\), and \(D_{\rm mid}\) the one on \(1,\ldots,d-1\); the empty determinant is \(I\). The monic polynomial and exact identity from C are \[ p_N(z)=2q^{N/2}T_N\!\left(\frac{z}{2\sqrt q}\right),\qquad D_N(\lambda;T)=p_N(\lambda)-\gamma p_N(T),\quad \gamma=(-1)^{N+1}. \tag{5} \] Here \(T_N\) is Chebyshev of the first kind. Since \(b\) is even, \(p_N(T)=\gamma^{b-1}p_N(c)\), so \(D_N(c;T)=0\). Below, an omitted argument means \(\lambda=c\), \(T=B_c^{(b-1)}\). ## 2. A polynomial inverse valid at collisions The tridiagonal determinant identity gives \[ D_dE_d-D_ND_{\rm mid} =\prod_{a=1}^dq(1-Q^a)^2=q^dN^2I . \tag{6} \] For clarity, the two cross-minors in the determinant identity are the products of the upper and lower arrows. Their signs cancel and give the displayed factor, including at \(N=2\). Thus, on this actual tail module, \[ D_dE_d=q^dN^2I,\qquad D_d^{-1}=\frac{E_d}{q^dN^2},\qquad E_d^{-1}=\frac{D_d}{q^dN^2}. \tag{7} \] These are polynomial matrix identities in \(c\). No tail spectral inverse or exclusion of collision parameters is needed. Define the explicit rectangular maps \[ L_c=\sum_{a=0}^d\iota_a\,\frac{q^{-a}D_a}{F_a}, \qquad M_c=\sum_{a=0}^d\frac{D_a}{F_a}\,\pi_a,\qquad Q_c=E_dM_c . \tag{8} \] The recurrence proves \[ (B_c-cI)L_c=0,\quad M_c(B_c-cI)=0,\quad \pi_0L_c=I,\quad M_c\iota_0=I . \tag{9} \] In particular \(L_c\) is a graph parameterization of the entire \(c\)-eigenkernel, not a selection of particular eigenvectors. There is an exact sequence at every \(c\): \[ 0\longrightarrow W\xrightarrow{L_c}V \xrightarrow{\,B_c-cI\,}V\xrightarrow{M_c}W \longrightarrow0 . \tag{10} \] One can prove exactness without a dimension argument. The equations in rows \(0,\ldots,d-1\) determine a kernel vector from its first coordinate, using the nonzero upper arrows in (3). For \(M_cw=0\), set \(z_0=0\) and solve \((cI-B_c)z=w\) successively in those rows. The remaining residual is supported at \(d\) and is killed by \(M_c\). Its last coefficient \(D_d/F_d\) is invertible by (7), so that residual is zero. The sign change to \(B_c-cI\) does not change its image. This proof already works over \(\mathcal O_N[c]\), where \(\mathcal O_N=\mathbb Z[\sqrt q,1/N]\). Every \(1-Q^a\), \(1\le a<N\), is a unit there because their product is \(N\). Equation (7) supplies the remaining unit. Thus the kernel and cokernel are free of tail rank over this ring; no field-rank argument or inversion of \(p_N'(c)\) enters (10). Replacing \(M_c\) by \(Q_c\) gives the same exact sequence. ## 3. The finite kernel and its natural comparison Put \[ r_c(z)=\frac{p_N(z)-p_N(c)}{z-c}. \tag{11} \] This is a monic polynomial of degree \(d\). The cofactor identity for the tridiagonal matrix gives \[ \boxed{\qquad r_c(B_c)=L_cE_dM_c=L_cQ_c.\qquad} \tag{12} \] Here is an algebraic verification including collisions. The adjugate of \(cI-B_c\), computed in the commutative coefficient ring generated by \(T\), equals \(r_c(B_c)\) by (5) and Cayley--Hamilton. Its columns lie in the kernel in (9), and its first row is a left kernel row. Their first-coordinate normalizations are \(L_0=M_0=I\). The \(00\) cofactor is \(E_d\), proving (12). The exact normalization is \[ M_cL_c=\frac{p_N'(c)D_d}{q^dN^2},\qquad Q_cL_c=p_N'(c)I . \tag{13} \] To check the derivative, first allow \(\lambda\) to vary with \(T\) fixed. The recurrence gives \[ (\lambda I-B_c)L(\lambda) =\iota_d\,\frac{D_N(\lambda;T)}{q^dF_d}. \tag{14} \] Differentiate in \(\lambda\), evaluate at \(c\), and multiply by \(M_c\). The term with \(L'\) vanishes by (9); \(M_c\iota_d=D_d/F_d\) and \(D_N'(c;T)=p_N'(c)\) give (13), using (7). This derivative is not differentiation of the tail \(T(c)\). Consequently \[ r_c(B_c)^2=p_N'(c)r_c(B_c). \tag{15} \] When \(p_N'(c)\ne0\), \(r_c(B_c)/p_N'(c)\) is the spectral projector onto \(\mathcal E_c=\ker(B_c-cI)\). At a collision \(p_N'(c)=0\), (12) is instead a nonzero square-zero map with image \(\mathcal E_c\) and kernel \(\operatorname{im}(B_c-cI)\). Indeed \(L_c\) is injective and \(Q_c\) is surjective by (7)--(10). The natural map from the kernel to the cokernel, using \(L_c,Q_c\), is multiplication by \(p_N'(c)\). It vanishes at a collision. The graph parameterization \(L_c\) itself remains valid there. ## 4. The actual endpoint seed and the unchanged closing Retain the literal cup and the full top rows from S and H: \[ p=N\sum_{a=0}^d x^{a-d}|a,d-a\rangle,\quad \ell_{\rm o}|a,b\rangle=\frac{x^a}{N}\delta_{a+b,d}, \quad \ell_{\rm m}|a,b\rangle=\frac{x^b}{N^2}. \tag{16} \] There is no degree delta in the marked row. Set \[ u_0=p^{\otimes k},\quad \ell_0=\ell_{\rm o}^{\otimes(k-1)}\otimes\ell_{\rm m},\quad y=|0\rangle_2\otimes p^{\otimes(k-1)},\quad \xi=\iota_0y . \tag{17} \] The actual source is invariant, so \(B_cu_0=cu_0\) for every \(c\). Its explicit seed calibration is \[ \boxed{\quad u_0=r_c(B_c)\xi=L_cE_dy,\qquad E_dy=Nx^{-d}|d\rangle_2\otimes p^{\otimes(k-1)} . \quad} \tag{18} \] To prove the first equality, use C's monic block Krylov basis. In that basis the kernel of multiplication by \(z-c\), modulo \(p_N(z)-p_N(c)\), consists exactly of \(r_c(z)\otimes y'\); this remains true at a multiple root. Its first-head \(d\) component is \(F_dy'=Ny'\). The same component of the literal cup \(u_0\) is \(Ny\), fixing \(y'=y\). Equation (12) and \(M_c\iota_0=I\) give the second expression. Extracting first-head coordinate zero from the literal cup proves the last formula, with its phase retained. Also (13) gives \(Q_cu_0=p_N'(c)E_dy\); hence the natural kernel-to-cokernel comparison kills this nonzero cup at a collision. For any original unmarked signed braid word \(R\), define \[ R_c=\pi_0RL_c,\quad z_0=Nx^{-d}|d\rangle_2 \otimes p^{\otimes(k-1)},\quad \ell_c=\ell_0L_c . \tag{19} \] Since \(R\) commutes with \(B_c\), \(RL_c=L_cR_c\). Thus the entire original paired-plat scalar, with its prescribed external factor \(\chi_N\), is exactly \[ \mathcal K_N=\chi_N\ell_cR_cz_0 . \tag{20} \] This graph reduction is source-faithful even at collisions. It does not replace \(\ell_c\) by an adjoint row. The saturated generic source \(\mathcal S_N\) lies inside \(\mathcal E_c\); the latter, of dimension \(N^{b-1}\), is not identified with \(\mathcal S_N\) or with the smaller complete invariant multiplicity. All original crossing factors and Casimir derivative channels remain. An inserted coupon not commuting with \(B_c\) needs its actual defect. ## 5. Uniform costs and the source-selected projection For fixed \(b\) and \(|c|\le C_*\), the actual tail satisfies \(\|T\|\le4(b-1)+C_*\). Recurrence (4) bounds the leading and trailing continuants by \(C^{a+1}\). Moreover \[ |F_a|^{-1}=\frac{|F_{d-a}|}{N}\le\frac{2^{d-a}}N . \tag{21} \] Consequently all maps in (8), \(D_d,E_d\), and their inverses in (7) have operator norm at most \(e^{C_{b,C_*}N}\). There is no \(N\log N\) cost or loss of uniformity at a collision. The forward representation and the original closing in (19)--(20) retain these frame costs. At \(c=2\), S proves \(p_N'(2)\ne0\) for every \(N\ge2\). Write \(\Pi_2=r_2(B_2)/p_N'(2)\). Since \(\|p\|=N^{3/2}\), (18) gives the exact source-leg estimate \[ \frac{\|r_2(B_2)\xi\|}{\|\xi\|}=N^{3/2},\qquad \frac{\|\Pi_2\xi\|}{\|\xi\|} =\frac{N^{3/2}}{|p_N'(2)|}. \tag{22} \] The coefficient has a sharp subexponential asymptotic: \[ \boxed{\quad \frac{N^{3/2}}{|p_N'(2)|} =2\sqrt\pi\,e^{-\sqrt{\pi N/2}}\bigl(1+O(N^{-1/2})\bigr). \quad} \tag{23} \] Indeed, with \(\theta=\pi/(2N)\), take \(w=\exp(\operatorname{arsinh}\sqrt{\sin\theta} -i\arcsin\sqrt{\sin\theta})\). S gives \[ |p_N'(2)|=\frac{N|w^N-w^{-N}|}{2\sqrt{2\sin\theta}} . \tag{24} \] Here \(N\log|w|=\sqrt{\pi N/2}+O(N^{-1/2})\) and \(|w^N-w^{-N}|=|w|^N(1+O(e^{-c\sqrt N}))\). Substitution proves (23). Thus the specified seed-to-cup leg has no exponential loss at the volume scale, although the global projector and graph frames need only satisfy exponential bounds. A quantum correction of the auxiliary parameter makes this coefficient polynomial while retaining the same principal parabolic generator. Set \[ c_N=1+q,\qquad p_N(c_N)=0,\qquad \lambda_j=Q^j+qQ^{-j}\quad(0\le j<N). \tag{25} \] The identity \(p_N(s+q/s)=s^N-s^{-N}\) proves these formulas. The roots are distinct: a collision for different \(s,t\) with \(s^N=t^N=1\) would require \(st=q\), which contradicts \(q^N=-1\). Differentiating that identity at \(s=Q^j\) gives \[ p_N'(\lambda_j)=\frac{2NQ^j}{Q^{2j}-q},\qquad p_N'(c_N)=\frac{2N}{1-q}. \tag{26} \] In particular all these derivative moduli are at least \(N\). The product formula for the spectral projectors, together with \(\|B_{c_N}\|\le4b+2\) and \(|\lambda_j|\le2\), bounds them by \(e^{C_bN}\). The actual seed-to-cup coefficient is now exactly \[ \boxed{\quad \frac{\|\Pi_{c_N}\xi\|}{\|\xi\|} =\frac{N^{3/2}}{|p_N'(c_N)|} =\sqrt N\sin\frac{\pi}{2N} =\frac{\pi}{2\sqrt N}(1+O(N^{-2})). \quad} \tag{27} \] Here \(\Pi_{c_N}=r_{c_N}(B_{c_N})/p_N'(c_N)\) is asserted over \(\mathbb C\); an integral projector requires localizing at \(p_N'(c_N)\). The exact zero-level generator satisfies \[ (B_{c_N}-c_NI)-(B_2-2I) =(q-1)(\mathsf K^{-1}-I),\qquad \|(B_{c_N}-c_NI)-(B_2-2I)\|\le2|q-1|=O(N^{-1}). \tag{28} \] The actual source and closing remain precisely (20). This correction does not calculate a geometric relative framing period or identify the finite projector with a geometric local cycle. There is a concrete finite cyclic realization at this corrected parameter. Define \(C_0(z)=2\), \(C_1(z)=z\), and \(C_{a+1}(z)=zC_a(z)-qC_{a-1}(z)\). Then \(C_a(s+q/s)=s^a+q^as^{-a}\), so \[ V_N=\frac{B_{c_N}-qC_{N-1}(B_{c_N})}{2},\qquad V_N^N=I,\qquad B_{c_N}=V_N+qV_N^{-1},\qquad \Pi_{c_N}=\frac1N\sum_{a=0}^{N-1}V_N^a . \tag{29} \] Indeed \(V_N\) has eigenvalue \(Q^j\) at \(\lambda_j\). For the full spectral idempotents \(\Pi_j\), character orthogonality gives \[ \frac1N\sum_{a=0}^{N-1}(V_N^a)^*V_N^a =\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}\Pi_j^*\Pi_j . \tag{30} \] This positive cyclic-average Gram retains all channels and has the controlled exponential cost above. The operator average in (29) fixes the actual source; it is not identified with a bounded-time geometric flow. ## 6. Coverage and the remaining source comparison C already proves the free companion form and controlled Krylov recurrence; H already gives a smaller exact invariant-source module. S selects \(c=2\) for the original cup and proves its stable projector bound. The additional assertions here are the collision-regular polynomial kernel (12), its free exact sequence over \(\mathcal O_N[c]\), and the literal seed calibration with coefficients (23) and (27). The cut and soft-cut texts keep different finite currents and the actual geometric framing form. The present finite coefficient is not identified with that form's relative period or with a geometric local kernel. In particular (20) retains a closing kernel and complex word phases; no nonzero lower bound for its particular scalar follows. title: Every cooriented coideal crossing has a positive volume amplitude
Exact channel transport for the first coideal crossing

# Exact channel transport for the first coideal crossing 24 November 2026. Written research proof. The first crossing in the actual coideal graph has an explicit finite transform. It decouples the neighboring total coideal into a one-head operator, with every original phase retained. Its action between two independently specified joint Haar metrics is diagonal in the channel labels, with an explicit positive gain. The weight in that gain is symmetric and has a uniform two-label ideal-octahedron volume profile. This gives an exact isometry after specified positive reweightings, and sharp exponential crossing costs before those reweightings. The two interface metrics differ. The original closing remains a prescribed complex row; no word-energy or scalar lower bound follows. ## 1. Actual generators and every external coideal channel Use the complete balanced physical basis of P and K. Put \[ N\ge2,\quad d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\quad x=-q^{-1}=q^d,\quad \kappa=q^{d^2/2},\quad c=1+q,\quad F_a=(Q;Q)_a,\quad F_0=1,\quad F_d=N . 	ag{1} \] The basis is physically orthonormal. Its actual generators are \[ Ke_a=xQ^{-a}e_a,\qquad Ee_a=(Q^{-a}-1)e_{a-1},\qquad Fe_a=(1-Q^{a+1})e_{a+1}. \] The missing endpoint arrows are zero. Retain the ordered coproducts \(E_{12}=E_1K_2+E_2\), \(F_{12}=F_1+K_1^{-1}F_2\). On \(r\) heads write \[ B_c^{(r)}=\mathsf F-(\mathsf E-cI)\mathsf K^{-1},\qquad B_c^{(0)}=c. \] C and K prove, on the entire tensor space, \[ p_N(B_c^{(r)})=0,\quad p_N(z)=2q^{N/2}T_N(z/(2\sqrt q)),\quad \mu_j=Q^j+qQ^{-j}\quad(0\le j<N), 	ag{2} \] where \(\sqrt q=e^{\pi i/(2N)}\) and \(T_N\) is Chebyshev. These roots are distinct. Every root occurs if \(r\ge1\). Also \(\overline{\mu_j}=q^{-1}\mu_j\), and \[ p_N'(\mu_j)= rac{2NQ^j}{Q^{2j}-q},\qquad |p_N'(\mu_j)|\ge N. 	ag{3} \] No simple-node quotient of a pair Casimir is being taken. Fix a width \(b\ge2\) and set \[ U=V_N^{\otimes(b-2)},\quad W=V_N\otimes U,\quad S=B_c^{(b-2)},\quad T=B_c^{(b-1)} =(F_2-E_2K_2^{-1})+K_2^{-1}S . 	ag{4} \] For \(b=2\), interpret \(U=\mathbb C\) and \(S=c\). The operators \(T,S\) commute. Choose any external root \(
u\in\{\mu_0,\ldots,\mu_d\}\), not necessarily \(c=\mu_0\). For scalar arguments define the monic continuants \[ D_{-1}=0,\quad D_0=1,\qquad D_{a+1}(\lambda;\sigma) =(\lambda+qQ^a\sigma)D_a(\lambda;\sigma) -q(1-Q^a)^2D_{a-1}(\lambda;\sigma). 	ag{5} \] They also have their commuting operator-coefficient meaning. The first-head tridiagonal determinant is \(D_N(\lambda;T)=p_N(\lambda)-(-1)^{N+1}p_N(T)\). Consequently \(D_N(
u;T)=0\) at every width. The graph \[ L_
u=\sum_{a=0}^d|aangle_1\otimes  rac{q^{-a}D_a(
u;T)}{F_a} 	ag{6} \] therefore parameterizes the whole kernel \(\ker(B_c^{(b)}-
u I)\), with inverse first-coordinate extraction \(\pi_0L_
u=I\). This follows by the unit upper-arrow recurrence, just as in K, without requiring \(
u=c\). Every original unmarked signed braid commutes with \(B_c^{(b)}\). Its graph action is thus \(\pi_0RL_
u\); these actions preserve products and inverses. For the first positive crossing put \[ C_
u=\pi_0R_1^+L_
u . 	ag{7} \] The source-selected case is \(
u=c\); write \(R_c=\pi_0RL_c\) for a whole reduced word. At even width \(b=2k\), K and G give the original cup, graph input, and full marked row: \[ u_0=p^{\otimes k}=L_cz_0,\quad z_0=Nx^{-d}|dangle_2\otimes p^{\otimes(k-1)},\quad \mathcal K_N=\chi_N\ell_0L_c\,R_cz_0 . 	ag{8} \] The external factor \(\chi_N\) and the full row \(\ell_0\) remain. Other external channels do not replace this original source. ## 2. The literal crossing transform and its neighboring coideal The full positive crossing in P sends \((a,b)\) to \((b+n,a-n)\). Output first occupation zero forces \(b=n=0\). Its surviving coefficient is exactly \(\kappa x^{-a}\). Substitution of (6), using \(x^{-a}q^{-a}=(-1)^a\), proves \[  oxed{\quad C_
u =\kappa\sum_{a=0}^d(-1)^a|aangle_2\otimes \left[(\langle0|_2\otimes I_U)  rac{D_a(
u;T)}{F_a}ight].\quad} 	ag{9} \] No physical shuffle or unrecorded phase was used. Finite propagation makes this lower triangular in the head-2 occupation. The leading \(T\)-coefficient of \(D_a(
u;T)\) is \(q^{a^2}\); a strict downward path in \(T\) has product \(q^aF_a\). Its diagonal is consequently \[ \kappa(-1)^a q^{a(a+1)}I_U . 	ag{10} \] In particular \(C_
u\) is invertible. This is its triangular diagonal, not an assertion that the physical matrix is diagonal. Let \(\mathcal D e_a=q^{-a}e_a\), and let \(B_
u^{(1)}\) mean the actual one-head coideal with auxiliary parameter \(
u\). Define on head 2, with identity on \(U\), \[ J_
u'=q\mathcal D\,\overline{B_
u^{(1)}}\,\mathcal D^{-1}. 	ag{11} \] It has the same \(N\) simple roots \(\mu_j\). Direct rearrangement of (5) in the rows of (9) gives \[  oxed{\quad C_
u T=J_
u'C_
u,\qquad C_
u S=SC_
u.\quad} 	ag{12} \] For explicit verification, \[ (J_
u'v)_a=(1-Q^{-a})v_{a-1} +q(1-Q^{-a-1})v_{a+1}-q^{-1}Q^{-a}
u v_a. 	ag{13} \] The recurrence writes \(TD_a\) as its next and previous continuants. The factors \((-1)^a/F_a\) give (13); \(D_{-1}=D_N(
u;T)=0\) gives both endpoints. Equation (11) follows because \( ar

u\). Thus the actual first crossing decouples the total tail \(T\) into this specified one-head coideal; the deeper \(S\) is unchanged. ## 3. Symmetric positive weights and a finite product For any two roots put \[ h_N(\lambda,\sigma)=\sum_{a=0}^d \left| rac{D_a(\lambda;\sigma)}{F_a}ight|^2. 	ag{14} \] An exact reciprocity will be useful: \[ D_a(\lambda;\sigma) =q^{a(a+1)}\overline{D_a(\sigma;\lambda)},\qquad h_N(\lambda,\sigma)=h_N(\sigma,\lambda). 	ag{15} \] It holds whenever \( ar\lambda=q^{-1}\lambda\) and \( ar\sigma=q^{-1}\sigma\). For a direct proof set the right side of the first identity equal to \(R_a\). Conjugating (5) and changing its normalization to \(R_{a+1}\) multiplies the linear coefficient by \(q^{2a+2}\): \[ q^{2a+2}(q^{-1}\sigma+q^{-2}Q^{-a}\lambda) =\lambda+qQ^a\sigma. \] The previous-term coefficient becomes \(q^{4a+1}(1-Q^{-a})^2=q(1-Q^a)^2\). The same recurrence and initial values prove (15) for every \(a\). Also \(D_a(-\lambda;-\sigma)=(-1)^aD_a(\lambda;\sigma)\). Write \(\lambda=\mu_j\), \(\sigma=\mu_l\), and \(m=\lfloor N/2floor\). Set \[ A= egin{cases}[m-j-l]_N,&N	ext{ even},\ [m+j-l]_N,&N	ext{ odd},\end{cases} \qquad B=d-A . \] Then the complete coefficient vector has the finite product \[  oxed{\quad \Phi_{j,l}(z):=\sum_{a=0}^d rac{D_a(\lambda;\sigma)}{F_a}z^a =(-qQ^lz;Q)_A(-q^2Q^{-l}z;Q)_B,\quad h_N(\lambda,\sigma)= rac1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi} |\Phi_{j,l}(e^{i	heta})|^2d	heta . \quad} 	ag{16} \] Indeed recurrence (5) gives, modulo \(z^N\), \[ (1-\lambda z+qz^2)\Phi(z) =(1+q\sigma z+qQz^2)\Phi(Qz). 	ag{17} \] Successive coefficients are determined by \(1-Q^a
e0\), \(a<N\). For the proposed product the two endpoint parameters are \(\{qQ^{-j},Q^j\}\), in that order for even \(N\), and reversed for odd \(N\). This proves (17) and then (16). It is a finite identity, not an infinite root-of-unity product. Every factor parameter has modulus one. In particular \[ 1\le h_N(\lambda,\sigma)\le4^d . 	ag{18} \] The upper bound follows by bounding each coefficient by \( inom da\) and using \(\sum_a inom da^2= inom{2d}d\le4^d\). ## 4. A uniform two-label volume profile Define folded angles by \[ \lambda=2\sqrt q\cos\alpha,\quad \sigma=2\sqrt q\cos eta,\qquad 0\le\alpha, eta\le\pi . 	ag{19} \] If \(\alpha+ eta>\pi\), replace them by \((\pi-\alpha,\pi- eta)\); simultaneous negation leaves \(h_N\) unchanged. This means replacing \((\lambda,\sigma)\) by \((-\lambda,-\sigma)\); its generating polynomial is the original one at \(-z\), so Parseval is unchanged. Relabel the roots accordingly. Hence assume \(\alpha+ eta\le\pi\), and put \[ \psi=(\pi-\alpha- eta)/2. \] For \(\psi>0\) define \[ 	heta_*=\arccos rac{\cos\alpha-\cos eta}{2},\qquad u_*=(	heta_*-\alpha)/2\in(0,\psi), \] \[ \mathcal V(\alpha, eta)=2\{ \Lambda(u_*)+\Lambda(\alpha+u_*)+ \Lambda(\psi-u_*)+\Lambda(\psi+ eta-u_*)\}, \quad \Lambda(v)=-\int_0^v\log|2\sin t|\,dt . 	ag{20} \] Use \(\mathcal V=0\) when \(\psi=0\). Extend \(\Lambda\) oddly and \(\pi\)-periodically when using it outside \([0,\pi]\). There is a universal constant \(C\) such that \[  oxed{\quad \left|\log h_N(\lambda,\sigma) - rac N\pi\mathcal V(\alpha, eta)ight| \le C\log N\qquad	ext{for every }N,j,l. \quad} 	ag{21} \] The assertion includes flat profiles, endpoint labels and both parities. Here is a uniform proof fixing the action constant. Put \(f(v)=\log|1-e^{iv}|\), of circle mean zero. After \(z=q^{-1/2}e^{i	heta}\), the endpoint quadratic in (17) is \((1-e^{i\alpha}e^{i	heta})(1-e^{-i\alpha}e^{i	heta})\). The starting quadratic is \((1+qe^{i eta}e^{i	heta})(1+qe^{-i eta}e^{i	heta})\). Thus the finite arc energy has the following mean-zero primitive, with \(\delta=\pi/N\): \[ E_\delta(	heta)= rac2\pi\left\{ -\Lambda rac{	heta+\alpha}{2} -\Lambda rac{	heta-\alpha}{2} +\Lambda rac{	heta+\delta+\pi- eta}{2} +\Lambda rac{	heta+\delta-\pi+ eta}{2}ight\}. 	ag{22} \] The arcs can be continued across a full turn: its integral of \(f\) is zero. This accounts for the different endpoint orders in (16). For \(E=E_0\), differentiation gives \[ E'(	heta)= rac1\pi \log\left| rac{\cos	heta-\cos\alpha} {\cos	heta+\cos eta}ight|. 	ag{23} \] For \(\alpha+ eta<\pi\), the sign comparison for the squared ratio is the sign of \((\cos\alpha+\cos eta)(\cos\alpha-\cos eta-2\cos	heta)\). The unique maximum is \(-	heta_*\), and the unique minimum is \(	heta_*\). Logarithmic cusps have the same derivative sign on their two sides and introduce no other extrema. Substitution in (22), using \(\Lambda(\pi-v)=-\Lambda(v)\), proves \[ \max E=E(-	heta_*)=\mathcal V(\alpha, eta)/\pi. 	ag{24} \] If \(\alpha+ eta=\pi\), (23) and its zero mean give \(E=0\). Each shifted \(\Lambda\) has zero circle mean, so no additive boundary action is left undetermined in these statements. For completeness the grid errors are uniform even at coalescing endpoints. On any interval \(I\) of length \(\ell\le1\), \[ \int_I|f(v)|\,dv\le C\ell\log(e/\ell),\qquad |\Lambda(v+\epsilon)-\Lambda(v)| \le C|\epsilon|\log(e/|\epsilon|). 	ag{25} \] The bound follows by separating the logarithmic zero from its bounded smooth remainder. Thus \(\|E_\delta-E\|_\infty\le C\log N/N\). For each finite product arc, compare its log samples with the integral over their grid cells. Away from the bounded number of cells nearest a zero, the summed oscillation is \(\int|f'|=O(\log N)\). Near a zero the cell average is \(-\log N+O(1)\), and the sample is at most that quantity plus a constant. This proves the uniform one-sided upper bound \[ \log|\Phi_{j,l}(q^{-1/2}e^{i	heta})|^2 \le NE(	heta)+C\log N . 	ag{26} \] It includes exact product zeros. Half-grid endpoints and one-cell length changes contribute only \(O(\log N)\) by (25). For the lower bound choose a midpoint of the actual \(q\)-grid nearest a maximizing circle point. All factor zeros of (16) lie on that grid; in the rotated coordinate it is the same shifted grid. The chosen point is at distance at least \(\pi/(2N)\) from every actual zero and within \(O(N^{-1})\) of a maximum of \(E\). By (25) the action lost is at most \(C\log N/N\). At these midpoint samples the zero-containing cells have both sample and average equal to \(-\log N+O(1)\). The grid comparison is therefore two-sided with error \(C\log N\). On an interval of width \(\kappa_0N^{-3}\) about this point every factor remains at distance at least \(\kappa_1/N\) from zero. Its total logarithmic derivative is at most \(CN^2\); the product logarithm changes by \(O(1)\). Parseval integration over this interval loses only \(O(\log N)\). Together with (24)--(26) this proves (21), including \(\psi=0\), without a channel cutoff. ## 5. The specified ideal octahedron The volume in (20) has a fixed-boundary angle interpretation. For \(0<u<\psi\), take two ideal tetrahedra of each type \[ (u,\psi-u,\pi-\psi),\qquad (\alpha+u,\psi+ eta-u,\psi). 	ag{27} \] All angles are positive and sum to \(\pi\). The internal edge has alternating angles \(\pi-\psi,\psi\), of sum \(2\pi\). Boundary angle sums are fixed as \(u\) varies. Their volume functional and derivatives are \[ W(u)=2\{\Lambda u+\Lambda(\alpha+u) +\Lambda(\psi-u)+\Lambda(\psi+ eta-u)\}, \] \[ W'(u)=2\log rac{\sin(\psi-u)\sin(\psi+ eta-u)} {\sin u\sin(\alpha+u)},\qquad W''(u)=-2\sin\psi\left\{  rac1{\sin u\sin(\psi-u)} + rac1{\sin(\alpha+u)\sin(\psi+ eta-u)}ight\}<0 . 	ag{28} \] The endpoint derivatives are \(+\infty,-\infty\). The unique maximum is \(u_*\): its equation is precisely \(\cos(\alpha+2u)=(\cos\alpha-\cos eta)/2\). Off-critical assignments need not have consistent tetrahedral moduli. At this maximum put \[ r= rac{\sin u_*}{\sin(\psi-u_*)},\qquad v=r e^{i(\pi-\psi)}. \] The stationary equation says \(r^{-1}=\sin(\alpha+u_*)/\sin(\psi+ eta-u_*)\). Consequently the alternating shapes \(v,-1/v,v,-1/v\) develop the four tetrahedra around the edge \(0\infty\). Their six ideal vertices are \[ 0,\ \infty,\ 1,\ v,\ -1,\ -v . 	ag{29} \] They form a convex ideal octahedron. The equator is centrally symmetric and strictly convex, and its vertical side planes support the four faces at \(\infty\). For an adjacent equatorial pair \(a,b\), the other face is the hemisphere through \(0,a,b\), with boundary circle \(|z|^2-\ell(z)=0\), \(\ell\) real linear. Its values at \(-a,-b\) are \(2|a|^2,2|b|^2>0\). Thus these four planes support as well, in the halfspace containing \(\infty\). All four positive tetrahedra fill the convex hull. Equatorial boundary angles alternate \(\psi,\pi-\psi\); pole-to-equator angles alternate \(\psi+\alpha,\psi+ eta\). They are positive and less than \(\pi\). Its volume is (20). In particular \(0\le\mathcal V\le4G_{m Cat}\). One direct upper proof writes the four positive arguments of \(\Lambda\) in \(W/2\) as \(x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4\), of sum \(\pi\). The functional \(W\) is twice the sum of the two tetrahedron volumes in (27). Each is strictly concave on its angle simplex: the negative Hessian in two angle coordinates has positive first diagonal and determinant \(\cot p\cot q+\cot q\cot r+\cot r\cot p=1\). The angle assignment depends injectively and linearly on the \(x_i\), so their sum is strictly concave on \(x_i>0,\sum x_i=\pi\). Its differential vanishes at \(x_i=\pi/4\). This gives the global maximum \(2\sum_i\Lambda(\pi/4)=4G_{m Cat}\), the regular octahedron. When \(\alpha=0\), (20) reduces to G's one-label family. When \(\psi=0\), use its flat zero-volume limit. No cell in a prescribed link complement has been identified here. ## 6. Independent joint Haar frames and exact crossing gains Let \(P_j(T)\), \(P_l(S)\) denote full spectral idempotents. For \(b=2\), only \(P_0(S)=I\) is present, since \(S=c=\mu_0\). For \(b\ge3\), every pair of labels occurs. Define \[ P_{j,l}=P_j(T)P_l(S),\qquad Q_{j,l}=P_j(J_
u')P_l(S),\qquad H_{m in}=\sum_{j,l}P_{j,l}^*P_{j,l},\quad H_{m out}=\sum_{j,l}Q_{j,l}^*Q_{j,l}. 	ag{30} \] These are independently specified positive metrics in the physical space \(W\), not definitions using \(C_
u\). They orthogonalize the indicated commuting pairs. They need not equal G's single-tail Haar metric. The projectors sum to identity, so their lower bound is \(N^{-2}I\). Their upper bounds are \(e^{C_bN}I\): use the bounded actual generators, the product formula for spectral projectors, and (3). Thus both metric logarithms have size \(O_b(N)\). For \(w\in\ker(S-\sigma)\), the complete joint input channel is \[ u_\lambda(\sigma;w) =\sum_{a=0}^d|aangle_2\otimes  rac{q^{-a}D_a(\lambda;\sigma)}{F_a}\,w . 	ag{31} \] Its first coordinate is \(w\), and unit upper-arrow elimination shows that these are all joint \((\lambda,\sigma)\) vectors. Because \(p_N(\lambda)=p_N(\sigma)=0\), its final recurrence closes. Equation (9) now gives the exact, phase-retaining action \[ C_
u u_\lambda(\sigma;w) =\kappa\,r_\lambda(
u)\otimes w,\qquad (r_\lambda(
u))_a=(-1)^aD_a(
u;\lambda)/F_a. 	ag{32} \] The output is a joint \((J_
u',S)\) eigenvector with the same labels. In (30) the norm of a vector in one joint channel is its original physical norm. Therefore \[  oxed{\quad  rac{\|C_
u u\|_{H_{m out}}^2}{\|u\|_{H_{m in}}^2} = rac{h_N(
u,\lambda)}{h_N(\lambda,\sigma)} \quad(0
e u	ext{ in the joint }(\lambda,\sigma)	ext{ channel}). \quad} 	ag{33} \] Multiplicities in \(w\) are unrestricted. This is an exact all-channel orthogonality calculation for the actual crossing, not a phase-free model. Writing \(\alpha_\xi\) for the folded angle of a root \(\xi\), (21) also computes its local energy increment uniformly: \[  rac1N\log rac{h_N(
u,\lambda)}{h_N(\lambda,\sigma)} = rac{\mathcal V(\alpha_
u,\alpha_\lambda) -\mathcal V(\alpha_\lambda,\alpha_\sigma)}{\pi} +O(\log N/N). 	ag{33a} \] The same intermediate label \(\lambda\) occurs in both terms. This is not a telescoping assertion for neighboring crossings without matching their different interface frames. Both signs use the same finite kernel. On a scalar deeper channel \(S=\sigma\), let \(U_\sigma\) have columns (31), with \(w=1\), and write \(C_{
u|\sigma}\) for the resulting \(N	imes N\) matrix. These columns form a complete simple eigenbasis. Reciprocity and \( ar F_a=(-1)^aq^{-a(a+1)}F_a\) give \[ C_{
u|\sigma}=\kappa\mathcal D\overline{U_
u}U_\sigma^{-1}, \qquad C_{
u|\sigma}^{-1} =\mathcal D\,\overline{C_{\sigma|
u}}\,\mathcal D^{-1}. 	ag{33b} \] The second equality uses \(\mathcal D\overline{\mathcal D}=I\) and \( ar\kappa=\kappa^{-1}\). Conjugation here is on the scalar channel matrix with its two parameters exchanged; it is not a replacement of an original marked row or a free permutation of heads. The positive functions in (33) have their joint spectral meaning. For example \(h_N(T,S)=\sum_{j,l}h_N(\mu_j,\mu_l)P_{j,l}\). Equation (33) is equivalently \[ C_
u^*H_{m out}C_
u =H_{m in} rac{h_N(
u,T)}{h_N(T,S)} . 	ag{34} \] All products on the right are Hermitian in their prescribed metric. There is a constant-one propagation law between explicit reweightings: \[ \widetilde H_{m in}=H_{m in}h_N(
u,T),\qquad \widetilde H_{m out}=H_{m out}h_N(J_
u',S),\qquad C_
u^*\widetilde H_{m out}C_
u=\widetilde H_{m in}. 	ag{35} \] The weights have the actual shared labels in (33); they are not independently maximized edges. By (18), or (21), their logarithmic cost is \(O(N)\), so the reweighted metrics also have radius \(O_b(N)\). They are different interface forms, not a common unitarizing metric. ## 7. Sharp source-channel costs and remaining scope Specialize \(
u=c\) and put \(g_N(\lambda)=h_N(c,\lambda)\), as in G. From (20)--(21), \[ 1\le h_N(\lambda,\sigma) \le\exp\{(4G_{m Cat}/\pi)N+O(\log N)\} 	ag{36} \] uniformly over all nodes. G gives the matching maximum for \(g_N\). The two-label formula also proves this bound directly by (29). Thus (33) and its inverse give upper exponent \(2G_{m Cat}/\pi\) for both crossing norms. This is sharp when \(b\ge3\): \[  oxed{\quad \log\|C_c\|_{H_{m in}	o H_{m out}} =\log\|C_c^{-1}\|_{H_{m out}	o H_{m in}} = rac{2G_{m Cat}}\pi N+O_b(\log N). \quad} 	ag{37} \] Indeed every \(\sigma\) occurs. The node \(-c\) is in the spectrum, \(g_N(-c)=h_N(c,-c)=N\) by the endpoint product in G, and \(h_N(-c,-c)=g_N(c)\) by simultaneous-negation symmetry. The channels \((\lambda,\sigma)=(c,-c)\), respectively \((-c,-c)\), give the lower bounds in (37). For \(b=2\), \(S=c\) and reciprocity instead gives \[ \|C_cu\|_{H_{m out}}=\|u\|_{H_{m in}} \quad	ext{for every }u . 	ag{38} \] This is still between two forms. It does not make the triangular matrix (9) physically diagonal or remove its possible Jordan behavior. For a general external \(
u\), (36) gives the same universal upper exponent for \(C_
u\) and its inverse; sharpness for every \(
u\) is not asserted. For an original paired source the specialization in (8) is retained through every actual reduced word. G's legal marked row remains a specified complex row, with its original external line. Changing to (30) or (35) must transport that row and the input too; G's boundary cost in a different metric is not silently reused. The channel norm calculation does not insert separate probabilities into the original scalar or bound its coherent channel sum below. All actual pair-Casimir normal directions remain inside the full maps. No peripheral or moving-\(q\) normal identity is asserted. R already constructs the exact reduced braid representation through a different \(F\)-prefix quotient, including a triangular Euler first generator. C and K already supply conserved channels and graph reduction, and G supplies the one-label volume slice. Thus neither triangular reduction nor general orthogonal-polynomial, Fourier, or Haar methods are claimed new. Twisted Clebsch--Gordan and \(q\)-orthogonal-polynomial models are established background; see Granovskii--Zhedanov, [Twisted Clebsch--Gordan coefficients for SUq(2)](https://doi.org/10.1088/0305-4470/25/17/002). No formula identification or proof from that paper is used here. The additional assertions are the actual coideal crossing transform, its two-label positive weights and volume profile, and the specified joint-Haar transport laws with their sharp costs. The sewn metric/phase comparison and the positive geometric scalar estimate for arbitrary fixed short components remain unproved. ## Complete inputs and closest coverage | Label | Complete text | Lines | SHA256 | | --- | --- | ---: | --- | | G | [Coideal graph Gram and volume](research_coideal_graph_gram_and_octahedral_volume.md) | 398 | 35ca803fb3262b1f85a08c3aa9b9112bcc2823ce380ce82362ef18bd382d6766 | | K | [Continuant source kernel](research_coideal_continuant_source_kernel.md) | 365 | 3ea997e5258c9413fd7c771a6a1475b90b39bf731ac55c0902fd136943b26f44 | | P | [Full physical crossing](research_full_physical_crossing_gaussian_packet.md) | 306 | 7f1b9932f88aa549bc55088b6f056f5a362548bc51c9fdd7c6b00469e725f531 | | C | [Conserved coideal channels](research_conserved_coideal_braid_channels.md) | 437 | b2a8c539742b4662ab8acbf4dc11c9bfa6acd27e895653ccfc47848278899fd4 | | R | [Earlier actual reduced braid source](research_actual_reduced_braid_source.md) | 330 | 9a472ef27b08305a519ff1f24b6d2b909e63a0acbdc49b3a29e001c52a2f2243 | Only written mathematics, source reads and text/hash operations were used. title: A signed coideal seam has a positive volume chamber
text:
# A signed coideal seam has a positive volume chamber 24 November 2026. Written research proof. The actual overlap of two coideal channel frames is a mixed finite Parseval kernel. On an explicit semialgebraic chamber, its whole signed integral agrees, up to its known phase and an exponentially small relative error, with its positive absolute integral. Its exponential rate is the volume of one convex ideal octahedron obtained by sewing two tetrahedral halves. The stationary equation closes their common edge moduli; the halves are not maximized independently. This gives nonzero coefficients of both actual signed crossings in a single nested channel frame, with its full neighboring metric weights. It does not show that an arbitrary component stays in this chamber or make its prescribed marked closing positive. ## 1. The actual mixed finite kernel Use T's and K's complete physical conventions \[ N\ge2,\quad d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\quad \sqrt q=e^{\pi i/(2N)},\quad c=1+q,\quad F_a=(Q;Q)_a,\quad F_0=1,\quad F_d=N. 	ag{1} \] The original crossing scalar is \(\kappa=q^{d^2/2}\). The simple coideal roots and monic continuants are \[ \mathcal R_N=\{\mu_j=Q^j+qQ^{-j}:0\le j<N\},\qquad p_N(z)=2q^{N/2}T_N(z/(2\sqrt q)), \] \[ D_{-1}=0,\quad D_0=1,\quad D_{a+1}(\lambda;\sigma) =(\lambda+qQ^a\sigma)D_a(\lambda;\sigma) -q(1-Q^a)^2D_{a-1}(\lambda;\sigma). 	ag{2} \] Here \(T_N\) is Chebyshev. All physical endpoint arrows are retained. For roots \(\lambda,\sigma\), put \[ \Phi_{\lambda,\sigma}(z) =\sum_{a=0}^d rac{D_a(\lambda;\sigma)}{F_a}z^a,\qquad h_N(\lambda,\sigma) =\sum_{a=0}^d|D_a(\lambda;\sigma)/F_a|^2. 	ag{3} \] T proves the complete degree-\(d\) product, including both parities: if \(\lambda=\mu_j,\sigma=\mu_l,m=\lfloor N/2floor\), then \[ \Phi_{\lambda,\sigma}(z) =(-qQ^lz;Q)_A(-q^2Q^{-l}z;Q)_{d-A},\quad A= egin{cases}[m-j-l]_N,&N\ {m even},\ [m+j-l]_N,&N\ {m odd}. \end{cases} 	ag{4} \] In particular every zero lies on the unit circle, on the actual \(\pi/N\) grid. No infinite product at a root is used. The exact functional equation is \[ (1-\lambda z+qz^2)\Phi_{\lambda,\sigma}(z) =(1+q\sigma z+qQz^2)\Phi_{\lambda,\sigma}(Qz). 	ag{5} \] For four roots define the full mixed coefficient and its positive absolute integral by \[ \Sigma_N(\lambda_1,\sigma_1;\lambda_2,\sigma_2) =\sum_{a=0}^d  rac{\overline{D_a(\lambda_1;\sigma_1)} D_a(\lambda_2;\sigma_2)}{|F_a|^2}, \] \[ A_N= rac1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi} |\Phi_{\lambda_1,\sigma_1}(e^{it}) \Phi_{\lambda_2,\sigma_2}(e^{it})|\,dt. 	ag{6} \] Ordinary finite Parseval identifies \(\Sigma_N\) with the same integral having integrand \(\overline{\Phi_{\lambda_1,\sigma_1}}\Phi_{\lambda_2,\sigma_2}\). Every coefficient and phase is still the actual one. ## 2. An explicit semialgebraic chamber Write the real root coordinates and principal angles as \[ a_i=\lambda_i/(2\sqrt q)=\cos\alpha_i,\qquad b_i=\sigma_i/(2\sqrt q)=\cos eta_i,\qquad 0\le\alpha_i, eta_i\le\pi,\quad i=1,2. \] Define the following relative open chamber in \([-1,1]^4\): \[ a_i+b_j>0\quad(1\le i,j\le2),\qquad \Delta=(b_1+b_2-a_1-a_2)^2-8(a_1a_2+b_1b_2)<0. 	ag{7} \] All uniform assertions mean uniformity on an arbitrary compact subset \(\mathcal C\) of this chamber, for the actual root quadruples lying there, and all sufficiently large levels. These are explicit inequalities on the specified finite channels, not a geometric placement assumption. They imply \(\alpha_i+ eta_j<\pi\) for every pair. Set \[ A=a_1+a_2+b_1+b_2>0,\qquad x_*= rac{a_1a_2-b_1b_2}{A},\quad \Theta_*=\arccos x_*, \] \[ \psi_i= rac{\pi-\alpha_i- eta_i}{2},\qquad u_i= rac{\Theta_*-\alpha_i}{2}. 	ag{8} \] Below we prove \(0<u_i<\psi_i\), uniformly away from their endpoints on \(\mathcal C\). Let \[ \Lambda(v)=-\int_0^v\log|2\sin t|\,dt,\qquad W_i(u)=2\{\Lambda u+\Lambda(\alpha_i+u) +\Lambda(\psi_i-u)+\Lambda(\psi_i+ eta_i-u)\}, \] \[ V_{m sew}= rac{W_1(u_1)+W_2(u_2)}2 . 	ag{9} \] The extension of \(\Lambda\) is odd and \(\pi\)-periodic. **Signed seam theorem.** Define \[ z_*=q^{-1/2}e^{-i\Theta_*},\qquad \eta_N=  rac{\overline{\Phi_{\lambda_1,\sigma_1}(z_*)} \Phi_{\lambda_2,\sigma_2}(z_*)} {|\Phi_{\lambda_1,\sigma_1}(z_*) \Phi_{\lambda_2,\sigma_2}(z_*)|}. 	ag{10} \] For sufficiently large \(N\) these values are nonzero. There are \(C_{\mathcal C},\epsilon_{\mathcal C}>0\) such that \[  oxed{\quad \Sigma_N=\eta_N A_N(1+O_{\mathcal C}(e^{-\epsilon_{\mathcal C}N})), \qquad \log A_N= rac N\pi V_{m sew}+O_{\mathcal C}(\log N). \quad} 	ag{11} \] In particular the whole signed coefficient is nonzero and has this same logarithmic rate. The phase in (10) is a specified finite product value, not an uncalibrated square root or an unknown source. The quantity \(V_{m sew}\) is the volume of the convex ideal octahedron constructed in Section 5. The acute box \(0\le\alpha_i, eta_i\le\pi/3\) is one uniform example: all \(a_i,b_i\ge1/2\), and \(\Delta\le1-4=-3\). It is only an illustration of the single chamber (7). ## 3. The global stationary calculation, including the sign Use the rotated circle \(z=q^{-1/2}e^{it}\). T's finite log-cell proof gives the following uniform energies: \[ E_i(t)= rac2\pi\left\{ -\Lambda rac{t+\alpha_i}2-\Lambda rac{t-\alpha_i}2 +\Lambda rac{t+\pi- eta_i}2 +\Lambda rac{t-\pi+ eta_i}2ight\}. 	ag{12} \] Each has zero circle mean. The actual arc primitive has \(t+\pi/N\) in its last two terms; this changes it uniformly by \(O(\log N/N)\). In particular, with \(E=E_1+E_2\), \[ E'(t)= rac1\pi\log\left|  rac{(\cos t-a_1)(\cos t-a_2)} {(\cos t+b_1)(\cos t+b_2)}ight|. 	ag{13} \] This formula retains the action constant, not only its derivative. Here is a global sign proof. Put \[ n(x)=(x-a_1)(x-a_2),\qquad d(x)=(x+b_1)(x+b_2). \] Their sum and difference satisfy \[ n-d=A(x_*-x),\qquad n+d=2x^2+(b_1+b_2-a_1-a_2)x+a_1a_2+b_1b_2>0. 	ag{14} \] The strict positivity is exactly the negative-discriminant condition in (7). Hence the sign of \(\log|n(x)/d(x)|\) is the sign of \(x_*-x\), off its finite zeros and poles. All cross sums are positive, so \[ \max(-b_1,-b_2)<x_*<\min(a_1,a_2). 	ag{15} \] Indeed at the upper endpoint \(n=0,d>0\); at the lower endpoint \(d=0,n>0\), and (14) gives the two strict inequalities. Thus \(-1<x_*<1\) and \[ \max(\alpha_1,\alpha_2)<\Theta_*< \min(\pi- eta_1,\pi- eta_2). 	ag{16} \] This proves the claims following (8). The unique global maximum of \(E\) is \(t=-\Theta_*\); the unique minimum is \(+\Theta_*\). On \((-\pi,0)\) the derivative in (13) changes from positive to negative only there; on \((0,\pi)\) it changes in the reverse direction. Logarithmic cusps have the same sign on their two sides. They introduce no additional maximum. In the common root-free interval (15), \[  rac{d}{dx}\log rac{n(x)}{d(x)} =-\sum_{i=1}^2\left\{ rac1{a_i-x}+ rac1{x+b_i}ight\}<0 . 	ag{17} \] The maximum is nondegenerate. Compactness supplies a uniform negative second derivative near it and a uniform strict loss on the complement of any sufficiently small fixed-radius neighborhood. For \(t=-\Theta\) in the common negative arc, put \(u_i(\Theta)=(\Theta-\alpha_i)/2\). The periodic primitive in (12) gives, exactly, \[ E_i(-\Theta)=W_i(u_i(\Theta))/\pi,\qquad  rac12\max E=V_{m sew}/\pi. 	ag{18} \] There is no free additive boundary constant. The sign distinction has a direct finite-kernel meaning. Writing \(\Phi_i(z)=\prod_{ho}(1-ho z)\), every \(|ho|=1\); therefore on \(|z|=1\), \[ \overline{\Phi_i(z)} =(-1)^d\overline{\prod_hoho}\ z^{-d}\Phi_i(z). 	ag{19} \] Consequently the analytic integrand of (6), up to that constant phase, is \(z^{-d}\Phi_1(z)\Phi_2(z)\). By (5) its exact \(Q\)-step ratio is \[ Q^{-d}\mathcal R_{\lambda_1,\sigma_1}(z) \mathcal R_{\lambda_2,\sigma_2}(z),\qquad \mathcal R_{\lambda,\sigma}(z) = rac{1-\lambda z+qz^2}{1+q\sigma z+qQz^2}. 	ag{20} \] The principal full-phase stationary equation is \(n(x)=d(x)\), not merely \(|n(x)|=|d(x)|\). The potential alternative \(n=-d\) has no real solution in (7), by (14). At the actual maximum each individual ratio is negative, and their product is positive one. ## 4. Whole-circle phase control and the quantitative lower bound The actual finite zeros stay away from a neighborhood of \(-\Theta_*\), uniformly on \(\mathcal C\). Here is an endpoint check rather than a continuum assumption. In the rotated variable, the two zero strings in (4) start at \(\pi-\pi/N\pm eta_i\) and run down with step \(2\pi/N\) to the two endpoints \(\pm\alpha_i\), with their last endpoints excluded. Since \(\alpha_i+ eta_i<\pi\), representatives can be chosen so both arcs run through the positive half-circle. They leave the negative interval \((-\pi+ eta_i,-\alpha_i)\) empty up to \(O(N^{-1})\) endpoint shifts. The two such gaps have the common interior (16). Their endpoint margins on \(\mathcal C\) are strictly positive. This pays the root phase, both string orders and all finite endpoints. On any connected zero-free arc, (19) says \(\Phi_i(q^{-1/2}e^{it})e^{-idt/2}\) has constant phase up to a constant sign. Thus the product \(\overline{\Phi_1(q^{-1/2}e^{it})}\Phi_2(q^{-1/2}e^{it})\) has exactly constant phase there. On the common dominant arc this phase is \(\eta_N\) from (10); there is no residual \(t\)-chirp. For explicit estimates, T's log-cell comparison yields globally \[ \log|\Phi_i(q^{-1/2}e^{it})|^2 \le NE_i(t)+C_{\mathcal C}\log N. 	ag{21} \] It remains valid at exact zeros. On a fixed neighborhood \(I_*\) of \(-\Theta_*\) inside the common gap, the same comparison is two-sided. The proof removes the finitely many cells closest to the logarithmic zeros, estimates the rest by \(\int|\cot(t/2)|=O(\log N)\), and uses the exact \(\pi/N\) endpoint correction in (12). In \(I_*\) all factors are uniformly away from zero; no omitted boundary current is used. Let \(M=	frac12 E(-\Theta_*)=V_{m sew}/\pi\). At the maximum the product magnitude is at least \(e^{NM}N^{-C_{\mathcal C}}\). Its logarithmic derivative on \(I_*\) is bounded by \(C_{\mathcal C}N\), since it is a product of \(2d\) uniformly nonzero circle factors. Integrating an interval of width \(N^{-2}\) gives \[ N^{-C_{\mathcal C}}e^{NM} \le rac1{2\pi}\int_{I_*}|\Phi_1\Phi_2|\,dt \le N^{C_{\mathcal C}}e^{NM}. 	ag{22} \] The global strict loss from Section 3 and (21) give \[  rac1{2\pi}\int_{I_*^c}|\Phi_1\Phi_2|\,dt \le N^{C_{\mathcal C}}e^{N(M-\gamma_{\mathcal C})}. 	ag{23} \] Both the signed and absolute complements obey this bound. On \(I_*\) their phases agree exactly. Dividing (23) by (22), and decreasing the positive exponent once to absorb the powers of \(N\), proves (11) for the entire circle. No local Gaussian prefactor or unproved contour replacement is needed. The phase has an exact single-height formula. Sort the roots as \(\lambda_r=2\sqrt q\cos\alpha_r\), \(\alpha_r=(r+	frac12)\delta\), \(0\le r\le d\), \(\delta=\pi/N\). For a cooriented pair \(r+s\le N-2\), use the RAW circle angle \(\vartheta\in(-\pi+s\delta,-(r+1)\delta)\). Then \[ \Phi_{\lambda_r,\lambda_s}(e^{i\vartheta}) =\gamma_{rs}e^{id\vartheta/2} |\Phi_{\lambda_r,\lambda_s}(e^{i\vartheta})|, \quad \gamma_{rs}=e^{i\pi d/4} rac{f_r}{f_s},\quad f_r=\exp\{i\delta r(r+1)/4\}. 	ag{24} \] Here is the sign and branch calculation. The two raw zero strings start at \(\xi_\pm=\pi-3\delta/2\pm\alpha_s\) and descend with step \(2\delta\), ending one step before \(-\delta/2\pm\alpha_r\). Their counts are \(n_\pm=(d\pm h)/2\), where \(h=s-r\) if \(N+r+s\) is odd and \(h=s+r+1\) otherwise. They are nonnegative integers. All unwrapped zeros lie outside the stated negative gap, with every \(\vartheta-\xi\in(-2\pi,0)\). Each factor therefore has phase \(+i e^{i(\vartheta-\xi)/2}\). Moreover \[ \sum\xi=d\pi-\delta d(d+1)/2+\alpha_s h-\delta h^2/2 =\pi d/2+\delta\{s(s+1)-r(r+1)\}/2. \] Thus \(\gamma_{rs}=i^d e^{-i\sum\xi/2}\), proving (24) at both parities, including \(N=2\). It also gives \(D_d(\lambda_r;\lambda_s)/N=\gamma_{rs}^2\). The common rotation to \(t\) multiplies each individual phase by \(q^{-d/4}\); it cancels from the mixed phase \(\eta_N\). For the two pairs in the theorem, (24) gives exactly \(\eta_N=\overline{\gamma_{r_1s_1}}\gamma_{r_2s_2}\). By (19) the phase-removed integrand is real on the entire circle, so \(\eta_N^{-1}\Sigma_N\) is exactly real. The lower bound above makes it strictly positive for large \(N\). This is a row/column phase factorization with explicit quadratic single-height factors. It does not assert a globally compatible gauge or alignment of the original cup and cap coefficients. ## 5. Sewing four tetrahedra into a convex ideal octahedron For each \(i=1,2\) take one tetrahedron of each type \[ A_i=(u_i,\psi_i-u_i,\pi-\psi_i),\qquad B_i=(\alpha_i+u_i,\psi_i+ eta_i-u_i,\psi_i). 	ag{25} \] All their angles are positive. Use the cyclic order \(A_1,B_1,A_2,B_2\) around a prospective common edge. Its angles sum to \(2\pi\), since each half contributes \(\pi\). Unlike the individual octahedra of T, each half here is not separately required to close its edge moduli. Put \[ z_i= rac{\sin u_i}{\sin(\psi_i-u_i)}e^{i(\pi-\psi_i)},\quad w_i= rac{\sin(\alpha_i+u_i)}{\sin(\psi_i+ eta_i-u_i)} e^{i\psi_i}, \] \[ ho_i=  rac{\sin u_i\sin(\alpha_i+u_i)} {\sin(\psi_i-u_i)\sin(\psi_i+ eta_i-u_i)}>0 . 	ag{26} \] Then \(z_iw_i=-ho_i\). The sine product identity and (8) give \[ ho_i=- rac{x_*-a_i}{x_*+b_i},\qquad ho_1ho_2=1. 	ag{27} \] The last equality is exactly \(n(x_*)=d(x_*)\). Thus the four successive shape ratios \(z_1,w_1,z_2,w_2\) have product one, including its argument. They develop with poles \(0,\infty\) and equatorial vertices \[ p_0=1,\quad p_1=z_1,\quad p_2=-ho_1,\quad p_3=-ho_1z_2,\quad p_4=p_0. 	ag{28} \] The ordinary sine rule gives precisely the angle triples (25). We check all supporting faces. The equator has strictly ordered arguments with increments \(\pi-\psi_1,\psi_1,\pi-\psi_2,\psi_2\), each in \((0,\pi)\). It is a simple star-shaped quadrilateral around zero. Its link angles at \(\infty\), at the two interior-half vertices and the two joins respectively, are \[ \psi_i+\alpha_i,\qquad  rac{\pi+ eta_1-\alpha_2}{2},\quad  rac{\pi+ eta_2-\alpha_1}{2}. 	ag{29} \] To see the joins, use \(u_1-u_2=(\alpha_2-\alpha_1)/2\); for example one is \(\psi_1+ eta_1-u_1+u_2\). All four angles are in \((0,\pi)\). The quadrilateral is therefore strictly convex, so its four vertical side planes support. At the other pole the interior-half angles are \(\psi_i+ eta_i\); its join angles are \[  rac{\pi+\alpha_1- eta_2}{2},\qquad  rac{\pi+\alpha_2- eta_1}{2}. 	ag{30} \] They too lie in \((0,\pi)\). Apply the boundary Möbius map \(z\mapsto-1/z\), exchanging \(0\) and \(\infty\). The reciprocal equatorial quadrilateral is again simple and star-shaped by its ordered arguments; (30) and the two remaining angles make it strictly convex. Its vertical side planes support. Undoing the isometry gives the four supporting hemispheres at zero. Hence all eight planes support the six vertices in (28), and the four positive tetrahedra fill their convex ideal octahedron. Its volume is the sum of their four ordinary tetrahedral volumes. The opposite \(\Lambda(\psi_i)\) terms cancel within each half, giving precisely \(V_{m sew}\) in (9). At the common classical corner \(\alpha_i= eta_i=0\), one has \(\Theta_*=\pi/2,u_i=\pi/4,ho_i=1\); this is the regular ideal octahedron of volume \(4G_{m Cat}\). This is a genuinely sewn cell: a shared phase variable and the full equation (27) impose its edge modulus, not independent maximization of two positive graph weights. ## 6.
