title: A cyclic quantum connection for the actual marked overlap
text: # A cyclic quantum connection for the actual marked overlap 24 November 2026. Written research proof. The opposed marked overlap satisfies an exact first-order equation on its finite coideal clock. The equation has determinant four and a polynomially bounded inverse. Its homogeneous second-order equation has one normalized cyclotomic source line, without inverting the level. Thus this particular local scalar can be computed by a conditioned quadratic residual problem. The same displayed coefficients select a unique rational solution of the unreduced cyclic equation. It is invariant under the actual two-sheeted height map. On each compact set outside the limiting height cut, this specified representative converges holomorphically to an explicit nonzero rational function. The result does not identify it with a moving-color period or authorize crossing its extra poles. ## 1. Actual scalar and finite clock Keep [G]'s complete conventions: \[ N\ge2,\quad d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\quad \delta=\pi/N,\quad \theta=\delta/2,\quad \kappa=q^{d^2/2}. \tag{1} \] The half-powers use the displayed exponential branch. The coideal roots are \(\mu_l=Q^l+qQ^{-l}\), \(0\le l<N\). For the original marked row \(r_l\), actual crossing matrices \(B^\pm\), and \(s_l=B^+e_*\), [G] retains the scalar \[ \gamma_l=r_lB^-e_*=r_l\overline{s_l},\qquad G_l=\kappa\gamma_l . \tag{2} \] The corresponding boundary coefficient is \(\beta_N\gamma_l\), with \[ \beta_N=\frac{T_*}{A_c}\frac{\kappa(1-q)}2,\qquad |\beta_N|=\frac1{N^2\sin3\theta}. \tag{3} \] Any original exterior factor \(\chi_N\) remains a further factor. The variable introduced below is an auxiliary height clock, not a knot peripheral eigenvalue. The exact tail formula of [G] is \[ U_t=\prod_{j=1}^t\frac{1-Q^{-j}}{1-q^{2j-1}},\quad W_t=|U_t|^2,\quad V_l=\frac2{U_l(1-q^{2l-1})},\quad E_t=q^{2t^2-t}, \] \[ H_l=\sum_{t=l}^{d}(E_t-E_{t+1})W_t,\qquad G_l=\frac{|V_l|^2}{2}E_l^{-1}H_l,\qquad E_N=-1 . \tag{4} \] In particular \(H_N=0\); it is not a periodic tail value. No positive interpolation of these scalars is assumed. Use the finite clock ring \[ \mathcal O=\mathbb Z[q,1/2]\subset\mathbb C,\qquad R_N=\mathcal O[z]/(z^N-1),\qquad (Sf)(z)=f(Qz). \tag{5} \] Here \(z\) is a unit and \(S^N=I\). This ring is free of rank \(N\) over the characteristic-zero domain \(\mathcal O\). Counting norms below mean the Euclidean norm of the values at \(z=Q^l\). The shift is a unitary permutation in that norm. Put \[ a(z)=(q-z)^2,\quad b(z)=z^2(1-Qz)^2,\quad h(z)=-2qz(1-qz^2), \] \[ \mathcal A=M_a-M_bS,\qquad \mathcal B=M_{1-qz^2}S-QM_{1-qQ^2z^2}. \tag{6} \] The notation \(M_f\) means multiplication by \(f\); coefficients in (6) are on the left of the shift. ## 2. The source equation, including its last row The tails obey \[ H_l=(E_l-E_{l+1})W_l+H_{l+1}. \] Use \[ \frac{E_{l+1}}{E_l}=qQ^{2l},\quad \frac{W_{l+1}}{W_l} =\frac{\sin^2((l+1)\delta)} {\sin^2((l+\tfrac12)\delta)},\quad |V_l|^2W_l=\frac1{\sin^2((l-\tfrac12)\delta)}. \tag{7} \] Substitution into (4) gives, for \(0\le l<d\), \[ 2\sin^2((l-\tfrac12)\delta)G_l -2qQ^{2l}\sin^2((l+1)\delta)G_{l+1} =1-qQ^{2l}. \tag{8} \] At \(l=d\) the second coefficient is zero. The same equation holds with the cyclic convention \(G_N=G_0\), since it multiplies that value by zero. Its last row is exactly \[ G_d=\frac2{1-q^3}. \tag{9} \] Thus no tail endpoint was replaced by a periodic boundary condition. Writing \(z=Q^l\) in (8) and clearing its nonzero sine denominator proves the actual clock equation \[ \boxed{\qquad \mathcal A G=h\quad\hbox{in }R_N\otimes\mathbb C.\qquad} \tag{10} \] The coefficients have bounded degree independently of \(N\). Their values at small levels are interpreted in the quotient ring; no assumption \(N>4\) is made. ## 3. Integral inverse and the normalized source line There are exact geometric-series identities in \(R_N\): \[ (q-z)^{-1} =-\frac12\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}q^{N-1-j}z^j,\qquad (1-qz^2)^{-1}=\frac12\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}(qz^2)^j. \tag{11} \] Indeed their products with the respective factors are \(-\tfrac12(q^N-z^N)=1\) and \(\tfrac12(1-q^Nz^{2N})=1\). Consequently \(a\) and \(h\) are units of this ring. Only the factor two has been inverted. Let \(\mathcal T=M_{a^{-1}b}S\). The full orbit product is \[ \mathcal T^N= M_{\prod_{j=0}^{N-1}b(Q^jz)/a(Q^jz)}=0 . \tag{12} \] Its numerator contains \(\prod_j(1-Q^{j+1}z)^2=(1-z^N)^2=0\); its denominator is a unit by (11). Therefore \[ \mathcal A^{-1} =\left(\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}\mathcal T^j\right)M_{a^{-1}} \quad\hbox{over }\mathcal O. \tag{13} \] It follows that the vector in (10) is the specialization of the distinguished integral vector \[ G_N=\mathcal A^{-1}h\in R_N . \tag{14} \] The equality with the actual values (2) follows from (10) and uniqueness. It is not an integrality assertion for the separate factors \(\gamma_l,\beta_N,\chi_N\). The exact counting-matrix determinant is \[ \det\mathcal A=4 . \tag{15} \] For example over \(\mathbb C\), evaluate at the roots \(Q^l\). The cyclic matrix has determinant \(\prod_l a(Q^l)-\prod_l b(Q^l)=(-2)^2-0=4\). This also proves the integral identity, since \(\mathcal O\) embeds in \(\mathbb C\). Equivalently (12) gives \(\det(I-\mathcal T)=1\), while the multiplication norm of \(a\) is four. Domain and codomain use the same basis, so the Fourier change to root values contributes no determinant normalization. The forcing is annihilated by the displayed operator: \[ \mathcal B h=0,\qquad \mathcal B(hu)=k(z)(Su-u),\quad k(z)=(1-qz^2)h(Qz)\in R_N^\times . \tag{16} \] For \(u=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}u_jz^j\), the equation \(Su=u\) says \((Q^j-1)u_j=0\). For \(1\le j<N\) this coefficient is nonzero in the domain \(\mathcal O\), so \(u_j=0\). Hence \[ \ker(S-I)=\mathcal O,\quad \ker\mathcal B=\mathcal O h,\quad \boxed{\qquad\ker(\mathcal B\mathcal A)=\mathcal O G_N.\qquad} \tag{17} \] Multiplication by \(h^{-1}\) followed by \(\mathcal A\) is an \(\mathcal O\)-linear automorphism sending \(G_N\) to \(1\). Thus this is a primitive free source line, normalized by (10). It does not say that \(G_N\) is a multiplicative unit. Nor is (17) asserted after arbitrary base change: torsion can make some \(Q^j-1\) vanish or become a zero divisor. ## 4. Polynomial inverse and a quadratic residual certificate On the counting grid every \(a(Q^l)\) is nonzero, and \[ |a(Q^l)|=4\sin^2((l-\tfrac12)\delta)\ge4/N^2. \tag{18} \] A nonzero product of successive absolute transfer coefficients from \(l\) to \(k\), \(l\le k\le d\), is exactly \[ \prod_{j=l}^{k-1}\left|\frac{b(Q^j)}{a(Q^j)}\right| =\frac{W_k}{W_l}\, \frac{\sin^2((k-\tfrac12)\delta)} {\sin^2((l-\tfrac12)\delta)} \le CN^3 . \tag{19} \] Here [G] gives \(1\le W_t\le CN\), and the smallest sine has magnitude at least \(1/N\). A product that reaches the last row is zero before it wraps. Since each \(\mathcal T^j\) is a diagonal times a permutation, (18)--(19) prove \[ \left\|(I-\mathcal T)^{-1}\right\|_2\le CN^4,\qquad \|\mathcal A^{-1}\|_2\le CN^6 . \tag{20} \] These bounds include both parities and \(N=2\). They are estimates for the actual source equation, not for an unspecified annihilator with the same classical zero set. For any trial clock vector \(g\) one obtains \[ \boxed{\quad \|g-G_N\|_2\le CN^6\|\mathcal A g-h\|_2 . \quad} \tag{21} \] The residual energy is quadratic in the \(N\) coordinates of \(g\). Thus this local scalar has a known fixed-degree replacement with a quantitative error certificate. It does not replace an entire short component by an \(N\)-dimensional compiler, or bound the residual of an unconstructed geometric trial field. For reference the homogeneous operator in (17), before taking the root quotient, has the commuting classical symbol \[ (1-z)^2(1-z^2)(L-1)(1-z^2L). \tag{22} \] On \(z\ne\pm1\), removing its displayed coefficient factors gives the two shift branches \(L=1\) and \(L=z^{-2}\). Those factors and their source/cut normal data remain in the exact state. This is an auxiliary height equation. It is not identified with the knot's peripheral curve or its geometric component. ## 5. A rigid rational lift of the displayed equation The finite root values do not alone determine an off-grid function. We now specify a lift by requiring the very same coefficients to satisfy an unreduced rational equation: \[ (q-z)^2\mathscr G_N(z) -z^2(1-Qz)^2\mathscr G_N(Qz) =-2qz(1-qz^2) \quad\hbox{in }\mathbb C(z). \tag{23} \] This requirement, rather than positivity or interpolation from a real asymptotic, selects the following representative. Set \(Z=z^N\) and regard \(1,z,\ldots,z^{N-1}\) as a basis over \(\mathbb C(Z)\). The shift \(S\) fixes \(Z\). The matrix of (23) has polynomial entries in \(Z\), with determinant \[ \mathfrak D(Z)=(1+Z)^2-Z^2(1-Z)^2 =(1+Z^2)(1+2Z-Z^2). \tag{24} \] To see the determinant, extend to a field in which \(z^N=Z\) splits, and evaluate on the orbit \(Q^jz\). The products of the diagonal and cyclic coefficients are \[ \prod_j(q-Q^jz)^2=(1+Z)^2,\qquad \prod_j(Q^jz)^2(1-Q^{j+1}z)^2=Z^2(1-Z)^2. \tag{25} \] The determinant of a diagonal minus a single cyclic shift is their difference. This proves (24) over the original field. It also applies at \(N=2\), where the two off-diagonal entries are the two directions of that cycle. Since \(\mathfrak D\) is not the zero polynomial, (23) has one and only one rational solution. Adjugate inversion shows that it can be written with denominator \(\mathfrak D(z^N)\); no extra poles at \(q-Q^jz=0\) are introduced by a partial division. In particular \(\mathfrak D(1)=4\), and reduction of (23) modulo \(z^N-1\) is legitimate. By (13), \[ \mathscr G_N(Q^l)=G_l . \tag{26} \] The apparent transfer singularity at \(Z=-1\) is removable in this cyclic solution, since \(\mathfrak D(-1)=-4\). ## 6. Exact height descent and its poles The involution of the physical height map is \[ \iota(z)=q/z,\qquad \rho=z+q/z. \tag{27} \] It preserves the solution of (23). Here is the coefficient check. Put \(v=q^{-1}/z\) and \(k_0=-q^2z^4\). Direct multiplication gives \[ k_0a(v)=-b(z),\qquad k_0b(v)=-a(z),\qquad k_0h(v)=h(z). \tag{28} \] The equation at \(v\), multiplied by \(k_0\), is therefore the same equation for \(z\mapsto\mathscr G_N(q/z)\), because \(Qv=q/z\) and \(q/(Qz)=v\). Rational uniqueness proves \[ \mathscr G_N(z)=\mathscr G_N(q/z) =\widehat G_N(\rho). \tag{29} \] The fixed field is \(\mathbb C(\rho)\): \(z\) satisfies \(z^2-\rho z+q=0\), and any rational function reduces to a sum of a rational function of \(\rho\) and \(z\) times another one. Invariance kills the latter coefficient. The only possible finite poles of \(\widehat G_N\) are \[ p_N(\rho)=2,\quad 2i,\quad -2i . \tag{30} \] Indeed \(p_N(z+q/z)=Z-Z^{-1}\). The roots \(Z=\pm i\) of the first factor in (24) give \(p_N=\pm2i\); the roots \(Z=1\pm\sqrt2\) of the second give \(p_N=2\). Some of these possible poles may be removable; none is added by this statement. At finite \(\rho\) its two preimages \(z\) are nonzero, so the list is exhaustive. At \(z=0\), (24) is nonzero and (23) gives \[ \mathscr G_N(z)=-2q^{-1}z+O(z^2),\qquad \widehat G_N(\rho)=-2/\rho+O(\rho^{-2}) \quad(\rho\longrightarrow\infty). \tag{31} \] Thus the normalization at infinity is fixed, not an unknown scalar multiple of a homogeneous branch. Equation (26) is an exact source statement. In particular, on an actual finite tail coideal with these simple eigenvalues, rational functional calculus in (29) is defined, since \(p_N=0\) on its spectrum. It gives exactly this original block-diagonal tail coefficient with values \(\kappa\gamma_l\), on its full multiplicity spaces. No commutation with an arbitrary crossing is asserted. This does not replace the original repeated-root Casimir algebra by its values: its first-normal directions remain in those full physical multiplicities, as in the inputs. ## 7. A holomorphic off-cut limit with no exponential loss Let \[ \Omega=\mathbb C\setminus[-2,2]. \tag{32} \] For every compact \(K\subset\Omega\), the function \(\widehat G_N\) is holomorphic and nonzero on a buffered neighborhood of \(K\) for all sufficiently large \(N\), depending on \(K\), and \[ \boxed{\qquad \widehat G_N(\rho)=\frac2{2-\rho}+O_K(N^{-1}) \quad\hbox{locally uniformly on }\Omega . \qquad} \tag{33} \] Its fixed-order holomorphic derivatives have the same local error bound after enlarging the compact set. We prove the assertion without continuation of the real-grid asymptotic in [G]. Fix \(0<r<1\) and rewrite (23) as \[ \mathscr G_N(z)=\alpha_N(z) +\tau_N(z)\mathscr G_N(Qz), \] \[ \alpha_N(z)=\frac{-2qz(1-qz^2)}{(q-z)^2},\qquad \tau_N(z)=\frac{z^2(1-Qz)^2}{(q-z)^2}. \tag{34} \] Uniformly on \(|z|\le r\), \[ \tau_N(z)=z^2+O_r(N^{-1}),\qquad \sup_{|z|\le r}|\tau_N(z)|\le r_*^2<1 \tag{35} \] eventually, for some fixed \(r<r_*<1\). The shift preserves that disk. Iterating around its finite orbit proves that the inverse of \(I-M_{\tau_N}S\) is bounded there by \(1/(1-r_*^2)\). Alternatively this is its convergent geometric series on bounded holomorphic functions. There are no poles of \(\mathscr G_N\) on this fixed disk eventually: every nonzero root of \(\mathfrak D(z^N)\) has modulus \(|Z_0|^{1/N}\longrightarrow1\). Put \[ g(z)=\frac{-2z}{(1-z)^2}. \tag{36} \] At \(q=1\) it solves \(g(z)-z^2g(z)=\alpha_\infty(z)\). Direct substitution, with \(Qz=z+O_r(1/N)\), gives \[ \sup_{|z|\le r} |g(z)-\tau_N(z)g(Qz)-\alpha_N(z)|=O_r(N^{-1}). \tag{37} \] The inverse just proved therefore yields \[ \mathscr G_N(z)=g(z)+O_r(N^{-1}) \quad(|z|\le r). \tag{38} \] For a buffered compact \(K\subset\Omega\), the equation \(z^2-\rho z+q=0\) has a unique root \(z_N(\rho)\) of modulus less than one eventually. It is holomorphic near \(K\), with \[ 0<a_K\le|z_N(\rho)|\le r_K<1 . \tag{39} \] To check this, at \(q=1\) these are the usual two reciprocal roots off the segment. A unit-modulus root at general \(q\) would place \(\rho\) on \(\sqrt q[-2,2]\). This moving segment stays a positive distance from \(K\) eventually. Compactness and the product of the roots, \(q\), then prove (39). The branch is the one with \(z_N\sim q/\rho\) at infinity. Use (29),(38) and \(\rho-(z_N+z_N^{-1})=(q-1)/z_N=O_K(1/N)\). The identity \(g(z)=2/(2-z-z^{-1})\) proves (33). Its limit is bounded away from zero on the enlarged compact, proving the asserted eventual zero-free neighborhood. Cauchy's formula proves the derivative assertion. Consequently the specified original-boundary representative obeys \[ \frac{c_K}{N}\le |\beta_N\bar\kappa\,\widehat G_N(\rho)| \le\frac{C_K}{N}\qquad(\rho\in K) \tag{40} \] eventually. The factor \(\chi_N\), if present, is still separate. No single threshold making (33) pole-free on all of the unbounded domain \(\Omega\) is asserted. ## 8. What is and is not selected The lift (23) is fixed by an explicit source-derived coefficient equation and cyclic consistency. It agrees with the whole finite scalar operator and supplies a nonzero complex-height representative on every fixed off-cut compact. It is not the assertion that the degree-\(<N\) polynomial interpolant has the same off-grid bound. Those are different representatives of the same finite clock class. The possible poles (30) accumulate at the limiting cut. A contour deformation crossing them must keep its residue terms. Nor does the grid congruence identify this rational lift with an independently defined color-deformed source, its meridian derivatives, or a moving quantum-parameter family. Such an identification requires its actual intertwiners and source comparison. No arbitrary complex continuation has been inferred from the real asymptotic. [W] already proves whole-source clock recovery, cleared equations and the distinction between abstract normal fibers and value fibers. [C] already gives explicit cyclic scalar connections, source lattices and resonant flags with their actual caps. No novelty for quantum connections, finite geometric inverses or cyclic period methods is claimed. The additions are this overlap's normalized rank-one cyclotomic source, exact determinant and inverse bounds, and the specified rational height representative with its quantitative off-cut asymptotic. The missing global quantity remains the original coherent scalar after an arbitrary fixed short partial filling. title: Two boundary rows retain the full coideal period
A full Fourier compiler for the actual coideal crossing
The coideal graph Gram has an octahedral volume action
text: # The coideal graph Gram has an octahedral volume action 24 November 2026. Written research proof. The actual corrected coideal graph has an explicit positive Gram on every tail channel. Its complete finite product gives a uniform large-level profile, including the endpoint channels. That profile is the volume of a specified convex ideal octahedron. The graph and its projector therefore have sharp whole-space exponential costs. The original marked row also simplifies in this graph. Its observed channel has Gram value exactly \(N\), rather than the maximal volume rate. These are source-specific metric and boundary calculations; they do not bound the original scalar below or identify a global geometric cycle after an arbitrary short component. ## 1. The actual graph and its prescribed metrics Use the complete balanced physical modules in K and H. Put \[ N\ge2,\quad d=N-1,\quad b=2k\ge2,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\quad x=-q^{-1},\quad F_a=(Q;Q)_a,\quad F_0=1,\quad F_d=N,\quad c=1+q. \tag{1} \] All missing physical endpoint arrows remain zero. On an ordered tensor power let \(B_c=\mathsf F-(\mathsf E-cI)\mathsf K^{-1}\), with the actual coproducts and generator order in K. Write \(W=V_N^{\otimes(b-1)}\), \(T=B_c^{(b-1)}\), and \(\mathsf B=B_c^{(b)}\) on \(V_N\otimes W\). K gives \(p_N(T)=p_N(\mathsf B)=0\), where \[ p_N(z)=2q^{N/2}T_N(z/(2\sqrt q)),\qquad \mu_j=Q^j+qQ^{-j}\quad(0\le j<N). \tag{2} \] The \(N\) roots are distinct at every level. Indeed a collision of \(s+q/s\) and \(t+q/t\), for distinct \(N\)-th roots \(s,t\), would force \(st=q\), contrary to \(q^N=-1\). Every root occurs in the tail. Let \(P_j\) be its full tail spectral idempotent and prescribe \[ G=\sum_jP_j^*P_j,\qquad \|v\|_G^2=v^*Gv,\qquad \|u\|_{\rm mix}^2=u^*(I\otimes G)u. \tag{3} \] The star is the physical Euclidean adjoint. K's finite cyclic average gives the same \(G\), with \(N^{-1}I\le G\le e^{C_bN}I\). The tail eigenspaces are orthogonal in \(G\). Adjoint symbols below always refer to the displayed domain and range metrics. Let \(D_a=D_a(c;T)\) be the leading continuants: \[ D_{-1}=0,\quad D_0=I,\qquad D_{a+1}=(c+qQ^aT)D_a-q(1-Q^a)^2D_{a-1}. \tag{4} \] If \(E_d\) is the trailing continuant, K proves \[ L=\sum_{a=0}^d|a\rangle\otimes q^{-a}D_a/F_a,\qquad M=\sum_{a=0}^d\langle a|\otimes D_a/F_a,\qquad \Pi=\frac{L E_d M}{p_N'(c)},\quad p_N'(c)=\frac{2N}{1-q}. \tag{5} \] Here \(L:W\to V_N\otimes W\), \(M:V_N\otimes W\to W\), and \(\Pi\) is the actual projector onto \(\ker(\mathsf B-cI)\). Until the graph pullback is introduced, their adjoints and operator norms use \(G\) on \(W\) and \(I\otimes G\) on \(V_N\otimes W\). We will use the following exact tail-density identity in metric \(G\): \[ E_d=q^dD_d^{\dagger_G},\qquad D_d^{\dagger_G}D_d=N^2I. \tag{6} \] Here is a direct proof. Each root and \(c\) obey \(\overline\mu=q^{-1}\mu\), \(\bar c=q^{-1}c\). For a scalar tail root, multiplying conjugated diagonal entries \(c+qQ^a\mu\) by \(q\) reverses \(a\mapsto d-a\). The conjugated edge product multiplied by \(q^2\) is \(q(1-Q^{-a})^2\), the reversed edge indexed \(N-a\). Thus \(E_d(c;\mu)=q^d\overline{D_d(c;\mu)}\). K's determinant identity \(D_dE_d=q^dN^2I\) gives \(|D_d(c;\mu)|=N\). Orthogonality of the tail eigenspaces proves (6). Define the actual scalar graph weight by \[ g_N(\mu)=\sum_{a=0}^d\left|\frac{D_a(c;\mu)}{F_a}\right|^2, \qquad g_N(T)=\sum_jg_N(\mu_j)P_j. \tag{7} \] On each tail eigenspace the maps in (5) are one scalar column and row tensored with the identity. Consequently \[ L^\dagger L=g_N(T),\qquad MM^\dagger=g_N(T),\qquad g_N(\mu)\ge\frac{|p_N'(c)|}{N}=\csc\frac\pi{2N}. \tag{8} \] The last bound is Cauchy--Schwarz applied to \(ML=p_N'(c)D_d/(q^dN^2)\), using (6). Thus \(G_{\rm graph}=Gg_N(T)\) is a specified positive Hermitian Gram, and \(L:(W,G_{\rm graph})\to(V_N\otimes W,I\otimes G)\) is an exact isometry. No frame has been discarded. ## 2. One finite product on every tail channel For the unique \(j\) in (2), set \[ A=[\lfloor N/2\rfloor-j]_N\in\{0,\ldots,d\},\qquad B=d-A, \qquad \mathscr F_{N,j}(z)=\sum_{a=0}^dD_a(c;\mu_j)z^a/F_a. \tag{9} \] Then the entire scalar graph column is generated by \[ \boxed{\quad \mathscr F_{N,j}(z)=(-qQ^jz;Q)_A(-q^2Q^{-j}z;Q)_B, \qquad g_N(\mu_j)=\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi} |\mathscr F_{N,j}(e^{i\vartheta})|^2d\vartheta. \quad} \tag{10} \] The second identity is ordinary finite Fourier Parseval. For the first, recurrence (4) gives, modulo \(z^N\), \[ (1-z)(1-qz)\mathscr F(z) =(1+q\mu_jz+qQz^2)\mathscr F(Qz). \tag{11} \] The coefficient of each new degree \(1\le a<N\) is multiplied by \(1-Q^a\ne0\); the constant term one therefore determines the whole degree-\(d\) polynomial. In the proposed product the two end factors are \(\{1,q\}\): their order is \(q,1\) for even \(N\), and \(1,q\) for odd \(N\). Its quotient at \(z,Qz\) is precisely the quotient in (11), proving (10) without an infinite product. In particular, for even \(N\) this product is \[ \prod_{l=1}^A(1-q^{-(2l-1)}z) \prod_{l=1}^B(1-q^{-2l}z); \tag{12} \] for odd \(N\) the odd and even strings exchange places. This formula keeps both parity-dependent half-grid marks. ## 3. A uniform profile on the whole finite spectrum Put \[ t=A/N,\quad \psi=\pi\min(t,1-t),\quad \eta=\arcsin(\sin\psi/\sqrt2),\quad \Lambda(u)=-\int_0^u\log(2\sin v)\,dv\quad(0\le u\le\pi), \] \[ \mathcal V_\psi =2\{2\Lambda(\eta)+\Lambda(\psi-\eta)-\Lambda(\psi+\eta)\}. \tag{13} \] At \(\psi=0\) use the continuous value \(\mathcal V_0=0\). There is a universal constant \(C\) such that \[ \boxed{\qquad \left|\log g_N(\mu_j)-\frac N\pi\mathcal V_{\psi_j}\right| \le C\log N \qquad(N\ge2, 0\le j<N).\qquad} \tag{14} \] No channel cutoff or nondegenerate-endpoint assumption enters this bound. Here are uniform estimates paying the logarithmic zeros. Write \(f(v)=\log|1-e^{iv}|\), a periodic integrable function of mean zero. For a grid string of length \(r\le N\), with spacing \(2\pi/N\) and either endpoint or half-grid samples, its sum is bounded above by \(N/(2\pi)\) times its arc integral plus \(C\log N\), uniformly in the arc and its rotation. Remove the at-most-two cells nearest each logarithmic zero. On the other cells the total oscillation is bounded by \(\int|f'|=O(\log N)\). A removed sample is at most \(-\log N+C\), whereas its cell average is at least \(-\log N-C\), proving the upper estimate even at an exact zero. If all samples and their arcs stay at distance at least \(\kappa/N\) from a zero, the same estimate is two-sided, with constant depending only on \(\kappa>0\). An endpoint cell changes the normalized arc integral by at most \(C\log N\). These observations also cover (12)'s half shifts. The corresponding limiting energy on the circle is \[ \mathcal E_t(\vartheta)=\frac1\pi\left\{ \int_0^{2\pi t}f(\vartheta-v)dv+ \int_0^{2\pi(1-t)}f(\vartheta-v)dv\right\}. \tag{15} \] Replacing \(B/N\) by \(1-t\) costs just the endpoint cell above. Thus globally \(\log|\mathscr F_{N,j}(e^{i\vartheta})|^2 \le N\mathcal E_t(\vartheta)+C\log N\). The function is unchanged by \(t\mapsto1-t\). For \(0<t<1\), endpoint differentiation gives \[ \mathcal E_t'(\vartheta)=\frac1\pi \log\frac{1-\cos\vartheta}{|\cos\vartheta-\cos(2\psi)|}. \tag{16} \] Its only ordinary critical points satisfy \(\cos\vartheta=\cos^2\psi\), hence are \(\vartheta=\pm2\eta\). The negative angle is the unique maximum, the positive angle the minimum. At the logarithmic cusps the derivative diverges with the same sign on both sides, so there is no further extremum. Using \(\Lambda(\pi-u)=-\Lambda(u)\) in (15) proves \[ \max\mathcal E_t=\mathcal E_t(-2\eta) =\mathcal V_\psi/\pi. \tag{17} \] This proves the upper half of (14) by Parseval. For its lower half suppose \(1\le A\le N-1\), and put \(m=\min(A,N-A)\). Every actual factor zero in (12) has angle in \([\pi/N,\,2\pi-2\psi]\), because \(\max(A,B)\le N-m\). The preferred angle \(2\pi-2\eta\) therefore has distance at least \(\min(2\eta,2(\psi-\eta))\ge\kappa_0\psi\ge\kappa_1/N\) from every zero and from the corresponding continuum arcs. Here \(\kappa_2\psi\le\eta\le\psi/\sqrt2\) follows directly from its definition. The two-sided grid estimate at this angle is therefore uniform. On an interval of width \(\kappa_3N^{-3}\) about it, each logarithmic derivative is at most \(CN\); their sum is at most \(CN^2\). The product logarithm changes by only \(O(1)\). Integrating this interval in (10) loses only \(O(\log N)\), proving the lower bound. If \(A=0\), the product is a unit-phase geometric series with all \(N\) coefficients of modulus one, so \(g_N=N\). This also proves (14) there. The case \(A=N-1\) was already included. ## 4. The actual convex ideal octahedron For \(0<\psi\le\pi/2\), consider the one-parameter angle assignment consisting of two tetrahedra with angles \((u,\psi-u,\pi-\psi)\) and two with \((u,\psi,\pi-\psi-u)\), where \(0<u<\psi\). Their common internal edge has alternating angles \(\pi-\psi,\psi\), of sum \(2\pi\); all boundary angle sums are \(\psi\) or \(\pi-\psi\). These are off-critical angle assignments. They need not yet develop with consistent tetrahedral moduli; that gluing equation is imposed below. Its volume functional is \[ \mathcal W_\psi(u)= 2\{2\Lambda(u)+\Lambda(\psi-u)-\Lambda(\psi+u)\},\qquad \mathcal W_\psi'(u)= 2\log\frac{\sin(\psi-u)\sin(\psi+u)}{\sin^2u}. \tag{18} \] The ratio decreases strictly from infinity to zero. Its unique maximum is \(u=\eta\), since \(2\sin^2\eta=\sin^2\psi\). Thus this is a concrete strictly concave angle-volume maximization, not an assignment of volumes to arbitrary signed summands. The maximizing tetrahedra develop into a convex ideal octahedron. In the upper half-space boundary take \[ 0,\ \infty,\ 1,\ v,\ -1,\ -v,\qquad v=r e^{i(\pi-\psi)},\quad r=\frac{\sin\eta}{\sin(\psi-\eta)}. \tag{19} \] The four tetrahedra around \(0\infty\) have alternating shapes \(v,-1/v,v,-1/v\). The first has angles \((\eta,\psi-\eta,\pi-\psi)\), by the ordinary sine rule. The maximizing equation gives \(r^{-1}=\sin\eta/\sin(\psi+\eta)\), so the second has angles \((\eta,\psi,\pi-\psi-\eta)\). For completeness all eight boundary planes support the convex hull. The equator \((1,v,-1,-v)\) is a strictly convex centrally symmetric quadrilateral. The four planes through \(\infty\) are its vertical side planes. For an adjacent equatorial pair \(a,b\), the other face is the hemisphere through \(0,a,b\). Its boundary circle has equation \(|z|^2-\ell(z)=0\), with \(\ell\) real linear, \(\ell(a)=|a|^2\), \(\ell(b)=|b|^2\). At the two remaining vertices \(-a,-b\) its values are \(2|a|^2,2|b|^2>0\), in the halfspace containing \(\infty\). Thus these too are supporting planes. The four positive tetrahedra fill this convex ideal octahedron, and their boundary dihedral sums are precisely \(\psi\) or \(\pi-\psi\). Its volume is (13). This proves the local Rivin interpretation of the actual Gram rate. The maximizing volume increases with \(\psi\): its derivative is \(2\log[\sin(\psi+\eta)/\sin(\psi-\eta)]>0\) below \(\pi/2\). At \(\psi=\pi/2\), \(\eta=\pi/4,r=1\), giving the regular ideal right-angled octahedron, of volume \(4G_{\rm Cat}\). Here \(G_{\rm Cat}=\sum_{n\ge0}(-1)^n/(2n+1)^2\), and \(\Lambda(\pi/4)=G_{\rm Cat}/2\), directly from the sine series. The limiting volume at \(\psi=0\) is zero. ## 5. Sharp full-graph costs and the retained original row The label \(j=0\) has \(A=\lfloor N/2\rfloor\), hence \(\psi=\pi/2+O(N^{-1})\). Equations (14), (18) therefore give \[ \log\max_jg_N(\mu_j)=\frac{4G_{\rm Cat}}\pi N+O(\log N),\qquad \log\|L\|=\log\|M\|=\frac{2G_{\rm Cat}}\pi N+O(\log N). \tag{20} \] The norms use the two metrics in (3). On a tail channel the column and row in (5) each have squared norm \(g_N\), while \(E_d\) has modulus \(N\). Thus the actual full projector satisfies \[ \|\Pi\|_{\rm mix}=\sin\frac\pi{2N}\max_jg_N(\mu_j),\qquad \log\|\Pi\|_{\rm mix}=\frac{4G_{\rm Cat}}\pi N+O(\log N). \tag{21} \] This is a sharp mixed-metric operator estimate, not a physical condition-number identification or an arbitrary-word estimate. Retain the actual cup and caps from H: \(p_{ab}=Nx^{-b}\delta_{a+b,d}\), \(\ell_{ab}=x^a\delta_{a+b,d}/N\), and \(m_{ab}=x^b/N^2\), with no degree delta on \(m\). Put \(h_a=x^a\) and \(\mu_*=x+q/x=-q^{-1}-q^2\). For the one-head tail matrix, including its zero end arrows, \[ (hT)_a/x^a=x+q/x-Q^a(xQ+q/x+qc)=\mu_*, \] because the bracket vanishes. Recurrence (4), starting from \(D_0=1,D_1=q(1-Q)\), then gives \(D_a(c;\mu_*)=q^aF_a\), so on the entire one-head graph \(mL_2=N^{-2}h\sum_aq^{-a}D_a/F_a=h/N\). Ordinary caps intertwine the total generators, hence all tail continuants. Therefore, on the entire \((b-1)\)-head graph input, \[ a:=(m_{12}\otimes\ell^{\otimes(k-1)})L =(h/N)\otimes\ell^{\otimes(k-1)},\qquad \|a\|_{\rm ph,*}=N^{-k/2},\quad aT=\mu_*a,\quad g_N(\mu_*)=N. \tag{22} \] For odd \(N\) this is \(A=0\); for even \(N\) it is \(A=N-1\), including \(N=2\). Its geometric profile is asymptotically flat, although its exact Gram value is \(N\) at every level. The prescribed last marked cap can be moved to the first only on the true saturated generic source \(\mathcal S_N\). This is the existing mark-transport result, with the following regular proof also covering \(N=2\). Lift a vector of \(\mathcal S_N\) to a generic invariant tensor. Closing all but any one pair by the regular generic ordinary caps leaves a scalar times its unique generic cup. The same fully ordinary closure is that scalar times the same nonzero generic quantum-dimension bubble, so all these scalars agree. Every matrix and normalized mark is regular at the root: factorial indices are \(<N\), the common pivot correction is independent of the marked pair, and \(mp=1\). A generic mark extension can be normalized by its cup pairing, which is a unit at the root. Equality thus specializes, without dividing the zero root bubble. The root cap formulas are not used as their generic extensions. No assertion for larger root-only invariants, selected windows, or omitted normal currents is made. For an actual regular unmarked braid \(\mathcal R\), let \(\mathcal R_c=\pi_0\mathcal R L\) and \(z_0=Nx^{-d}|d\rangle\otimes p^{\otimes(k-1)}\). K and this legal relocation give the original scalar exactly as \[ \mathcal K_N=\chi_N a\mathcal R_cz_0,\qquad \|a\|_{G,*}\le N^{-k/2},\qquad \|a\|_{G_{\rm graph},*}\le N^{-(k+1)/2}. \tag{23} \] Indeed \(aP_j\) vanishes except at \(\mu_*\), while \(\|v\|_G^2=\sum_j\|P_jv\|_{\rm ph}^2\); this proves the first dual bound from (22). The graph metric adds exactly the factor \(g_N(\mu_*)=N\) on that observed channel, proving the second. Consequently \( |\mathcal K_N|\le|\chi_N|N^{-(k+1)/2} \|\mathcal R_cz_0\|_{G_{\rm graph}}\). The full marked row and external factor remain. No lower bound on its value on this particular propagated vector follows. K already supplies the exact graph/source reduction. P proves top-mark transport; the argument above makes its \(N=2\) scope explicit. C already uses finite products, Parseval and Laplace for a different centered-input family; E already interprets native magnetic costs through ideal polyhedra. These methods and the general Al-Salam--Chihara recurrence are not claimed new. The assertions here are the full coideal spectrum product/profile, its specified local octahedron, sharp graph costs, and the explicit original graph row. Its phase-bearing transitions through arbitrary overlapping blocks and the required geometric word-energy estimate remain unproved. All results concern complete-root values with full Casimir channels; no peripheral or moving-\(q\) jet theorem is inferred. ## Complete inputs and closest coverage | Label | Complete text | Lines | SHA256 | | --- | --- | ---: | --- | | K | [Continuant source kernel](research_coideal_continuant_source_kernel.md) | 365 | 3ea997e5258c9413fd7c771a6a1475b90b39bf731ac55c0902fd136943b26f44 | | H | [Complete invariant source](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_complete_source_multiplicity_module.md) | 602 | 14cfb558f50c5b091cec9439692dfeb87129e31f38588cb1ebfd8e8547ac99a9 | | P | [Original top-mark transport](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_arbitrary_casimir_top_mark_transport.md) | 240 | 7eeb576697c96e8074688dc1934bf1a7cd0d9def4b5928f9275b491daf28508a | | C | [Centered coherent product energy](research_centered_coherent_product_energy.md) | 393 | 73152328a77ba5d63a2a8eaa17647ed38b7683c613e0947e3bda9e451dda76e2 | | E | [Native magnetic energy geometry](actual_native_magnetic_energy_local_geometry.md) | 270 | 96431ecb009a9485527646d6d5822aaa337b18d66801b3ab2093ac5add029cb3 | Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used. # A signed height pairing gives a positive metric with polynomial source costs 24 November 2026. Written research proof. The actual tensor Krein form, after an explicit half-Cartan twist, is diagonal in the complete nested coideal frame. Its diagonal entries are signed cosecants independent of neighboring heights. Taking the absolute values of this coordinate diagonal gives a specified positive metric. In that metric the actual crossing coefficients have their sewn volume rate without additional graph weight corrections, and both original boundary packets have polynomial norms. An original marked cap followed by a crossing between its two legs has a further exact all-channel formula: a known quadratic phase times a positive weight between polynomial bounds. This is a boundary coefficient estimate, not a lower bound for its contraction with an arbitrary coherent exterior. ## 1. Complete physical conventions and the conserved source channel Keep the conventions of [S], [T], [K] and [G]: \[ N\ge2,\quad d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\quad x=-q^{-1}=q^d,\quad c=1+q,\quad F_a=(Q;Q)_a,\quad F_d=N. 	ag{1} \] All fractional powers below mean the displayed exponential branch. The physical heads \(e_a\), \(0\le a\le d\), are orthonormal. Put \[ Ke_a=xQ^{-a}e_a,\quad Ee_a=(Q^{-a}-1)e_{a-1},\quad Fe_a=(1-Q^{a+1})e_{a+1}. 	ag{2} \] Missing endpoint arrows are zero. The coproducts are \(\Delta E=E_1K_2+E_2\), \(\Delta F=F_1+K_1^{-1}F_2\). On any ordered suffix use the actual operator \[ B_c^{(b)}=F_*-(E_*-cI)K_*^{-1},\qquad B_c^{(0)}=c. 	ag{3} \] Its roots are simple at this corrected auxiliary parameter: \[ p_N(z)=2q^{N/2}T_N(z/(2\sqrt q)),\quad \lambda_r=2\sqrt q\cos\alpha_r,\quad \alpha_r=(r+	frac12)\pi/N,\quad0\le r<N. \] Here \(p_N(B_c^{(b)})=0\), and \[ p_N'(\lambda_r)=Nq^{d/2}(-1)^r/\sin\alpha_r. 	ag{4} \] Every actual signed braid commutes with its total coideal. Write \(	heta=\pi/(2N)\), so \(c=\lambda_0\). For \(b=2k\) heads, \(k\ge1\), the original source is \[ u_0=p^{\otimes k},\quad p_{ab}=Nx^{-b}\mathbf1_{a+b=d},\quad \ell_{ab}=x^a\mathbf1_{a+b=d}/N,\quad m_{ab}=x^b/N^2, \] \[ \mathcal K_N=\chi_N\ell_0R u_0,\qquad \ell_0=\ell_{12}\cdots\ell_{2k-3,2k-2}m_{2k-1,2k}. 	ag{5} \] The marked row has no degree delta. All original exterior factors remain in \(\chi_N\). Direct endpoint substitution gives \(E_*u_0=F_*u_0=0\), \(K_*u_0=u_0\), hence \(B_cu_0=cu_0\). We may therefore restrict the whole word and its observation to \(\mathcal E_c=\ker(B_c^{(2k)}-cI)\). This is one globally conserved channel; no projector is inserted between crossings. All subsequent boundary norms are on this full source channel. Their dual norms use the restriction of the specified positive form. ## 2. A physical half-Cartan twist of the known Krein form [R] proves that the actual full crossings preserve the tensor form \[ H_Ne_a=qQ^ae_{d-a},\qquad H_N^\dagger=H_N,\quad H_N^2=I. \] Use the explicit unrolled square root and its twist \[ K^{1/2}e_a=q^{d/2-a}e_a,\qquad H'_N=H_NK^{1/2},\qquad H'_Ne_a=q^{1+d/2+a}e_{d-a}. 	ag{6} \] Thus \(H'_N\) too is a Hermitian unitary involution. Write \(A^{\sharp'}=H'_NA^\dagger H'_N\) on one head. This does not choose a square root separately at each clock node. The original crossings preserve integer total degree, so commute with \(K^{1/2}\otimes K^{1/2}\). Consequently every signed word obeys \[ R^\dagger(H'_N)^{\otimes b}R=(H'_N)^{\otimes b}. 	ag{7} \] This is an explicit consequence of the already known physical Krein conservation, not a first conserved-form construction. At completeness [R]'s raising generator is \(e_x=qE\). Its head adjoints therefore give \(E^\sharp=QE\), \(F^\sharp=Q^{-1}F\), \(K^\sharp=K\). Conjugation by the displayed \(K^{1/2}\) changes these to \[ F^{\sharp'}=q^{-1}F,\quad E^{\sharp'}=qE,\quad (EK^{-1})^{\sharp'}=q^{-1}EK^{-1}. \] For any root \(\sigma\), \( ar\sigma=q^{-1}\sigma\). Thus the one-head conditional operator satisfies \[ (B_\sigma^{(1)})^{\sharp'}=q^{-1}B_\sigma^{(1)}. 	ag{8} \] All these identities include the bottom and top zero arrows. ## 3. Exact signed orthogonality of every height Use the leading continuants and their eigenvectors \[ D_{-1}=0,\quad D_0=1,\quad D_{a+1}(\lambda;\sigma) =(\lambda+qQ^a\sigma)D_a-q(1-Q^a)^2D_{a-1}, \] \[ u_\lambda(\sigma)_a=q^{-a}D_a(\lambda;\sigma)/F_a,\quad M_\lambda(\sigma)_a=D_a(\lambda;\sigma)/F_a. 	ag{9} \] The first component of every \(u_\lambda\) is one. Let \(E_d\) denote the trailing continuant, and \(L_\lambda=D_d(\lambda;\sigma)/N\). [K] and [S] give \[ M_\lambda u_\lambda ={p_N'(\lambda)L_\lambda\over q^dN},\quad E_d=q^d\overline{D_d},\quad |L_\lambda|=1. 	ag{10} \] The finite polynomial \(\Phi_{\lambda,\sigma}(z)=\sum_aD_a(\lambda;\sigma)z^a/F_a\) has degree \(d\), constant term one and all its roots on the unit circle. Self-inversivity therefore gives, with \(\varphi_a=D_a(\lambda;\sigma)/F_a\), \( ar\varphi_{d-a}= ar L_\lambda\varphi_a\). Direct multiplication yields \[ u_\lambda^\dagger H'_N =q^{1+3d/2} ar L_\lambda M_\lambda. \] Equation (8) makes distinct eigenvectors orthogonal; (10) now gives \[  oxed{\quad u_{\lambda_r}(\sigma)^\dagger H'_N u_{\lambda_t}(\sigma) =\delta_{rt}\,w_r,\qquad w_r=(-1)^{r+1}\csc\alpha_r . \quad} 	ag{11} \] Indeed the diagonal is \(q^{1+d/2}p_N'(\lambda_r)/N\); substitute (4) and \(q^{d+1}=-1\). The signed norm is independent of \(\sigma\). Write \(U_\sigma\) for the invertible matrix with columns \(u_\lambda(\sigma)\). This calculation uses every physical coordinate, rather than a reduced value-only Casimir quotient. For a width \(b\) choose successive suffix roots \(
u_0,\ldots,
u_{b-1}\), and set \(
u_b=c\). The exact path vector is \[ v_{ oldsymbol
u}=  igotimes_{j=1}^b u_{
u_{j-1}}(
u_j). 	ag{12} \] Tail-up graph elimination gives a basis of all \(N^b\) physical states, as in [S]. For two different paths choose their deepest differing height; the next heights agree, so (11) makes that tensor factor orthogonal. Hence, if \(\Psi\) has these columns, \[ \Psi^\dagger(H'_N)^{\otimes b}\Psi =\mathcal W,\qquad \mathcal W_{ oldsymbol
u} =\prod_{j=0}^{b-1}w_{r_j},\quad 
u_j=\lambda_{r_j}. 	ag{13} \] The external factor \(w_{r_0}\) is included. On the integer-degree \(kd\) source, \((K^{1/2})^{\otimes 2k}=1\). Thus this is the old tensor Krein form there, not a new positive flux for invariant states. For example the ordinary cup still has signed square zero. ## 4. The specified positive metric and its crossing normalization Define the positive form by the absolute coordinate diagonal: \[ \mathcal D_{ oldsymbol
u} =|\mathcal W_{ oldsymbol
u}| =\prod_{j=0}^{b-1}\csc\alpha_{r_j},\qquad G_{m ht}=\Psi^{-\dagger}\mathcal D\Psi^{-1}. 	ag{14} \] Thus the paths are orthogonal with the displayed positive norms. This is not the physical spectral absolute value of \((H'_N)^{\otimes b}\), which is \(I\). The basis \(\Psi\) is nonunitary, and its specific coideal definition is part of (14). It uses no completed-word value or unknown closing coefficient. This positive metric is admissible in the exponential window. Indeed \(\|u_\lambda(\sigma)\|_{m ph}^2=h_N(\lambda,\sigma) \le4^d\), so \(\|\Psi\|\le N^{b/2}2^{bd}\). Since \(|\mathcal W_{ oldsymbol
u}|\ge1\), (13) gives \[ \Psi^{-1}=\mathcal W^{-1}\Psi^\dagger(H'_N)^{\otimes b}, \qquad \|\Psi^{-1}\|\le\|\Psi\| . \] Also \(\|\mathcal D\|\le\csc^b	heta=O_b(N^b)\). Consequently \[ \|G_{m ht}^{\pm1}\|\le e^{C_bN},\qquad \|\log G_{m ht}\|=O_b(N). 	ag{15} \] Operator norms here are induced physical norms. The same bounds hold on the conserved external channel. Let \(R_i\) change only the middle height \(\lambda_r\) to \(\lambda_{r'}\), with neighboring heights \(\lambda_v,\lambda_s\). [S] gives the exact phases and, on its explicit compact signed chambers, one positive amplitude: \[ B^+_{r',r}=(-1)^{r'}\sin\alpha_{r'} {f_vf_s\over f_{r'}f_r}J_N,\qquad B^-_{r',r}=\overline{B^+_{r',r}},\qquad f_r=e^{i\pi r(r+1)/(4N)}. \] Here \(J_N>0\) eventually and \(\log J_N=NV_{m sew}/\pi+O(\log N)\). The full original Cartan scalar is included: \(\kappa q^{d/2}i^{-d}=1\). Normalizing (12) in (14) multiplies an entry only by \(\sqrt{\sin\alpha_r/\sin\alpha_{r'}}\). Therefore \[  oxed{\quad \widetilde B^+_{r',r} =(-1)^{r'}\sqrt{\sin\alpha_r\sin\alpha_{r'}} {f_vf_s\over f_{r'}f_r}J_N,\quad \widetilde B^-=\overline{\widetilde B^+},\quad \log|\widetilde B^\pm|=NV_{m sew}/\pi+O(\log N). \quad} 	ag{16} \] There are no neighboring \(h_N\)-volume corrections in this metric. Those in [S]'s physical joint Haar metric were correct for that different metric; no physical comparison of subexponential size is claimed. ## 5. General ordinary boundary tensors, with their phases For any actual tail vector \(z_\sigma\) of height \(\sigma\), put \[ A_\lambda={N^2q^dx^{-d}\over p_N'(\lambda)}. \] The original cup is a Hopf invariant. Its first-head zero coordinate is \(Nx^{-d}e_d\otimes z_\sigma\). The inverse row from [K] has endpoint \[ (U_\sigma^{-1})_{\lambda,d} ={E_d(\lambda;\sigma)D_d(\lambda;\sigma)\over Np_N'(\lambda)} ={q^dN\over p_N'(\lambda)}. \] Graph reconstruction therefore proves \[ p_{12}\otimes z_\sigma =\sum_\lambda A_\lambda u_\sigma(\lambda)\otimes u_\lambda(\sigma)\otimes z_\sigma. 	ag{17} \] This is valid at every tail height; \(|A_{\lambda_r}|=N\sin\alpha_r\). The ordinary cap coefficient is \[ t_{\eta,\lambda,\sigma} =\ell[u_\eta(\lambda)\otimes u_\lambda(\sigma)] ={q^{-d}\over N}\sum_{a=0}^d {x^aD_a(\eta;\lambda)D_{d-a}(\lambda;\sigma)\over F_aF_{d-a}}. \] As a polynomial in \(\eta\), it has degree at most \(d\) and leading coefficient \(q^{-d}x^d/N^2\), independent of \(\lambda,\sigma\). Hopf intertwining annihilates it at every root \(\eta
e\sigma\). Lagrange uniqueness, without dividing an ordinary bubble, gives \[  oxed{\quad t_{\eta,\lambda,\sigma} =\delta_{\eta,\sigma}\,{q^{-d}x^dp_N'(\sigma)\over N^2} =\delta_{\eta,\sigma}/A_\sigma .\quad} 	ag{18} \] These identities include \(N=2\) and every level parity. They retain the actual pivot and the full finite support. In particular an ordinary cup-cap bubble can vanish by the sum of the \(A_\lambda\); it has not been normalized to one. These general formulas also control genuine ordinary turns on arbitrary tail sectors. Inserting a cup adds the two weights \(\csc\alpha_\sigma\csc\alpha_\lambda\) to the old tail weight. The exact sector map norms are therefore \[ \|\operatorname{Cup}_\sigma\|^2 =N^2\csc	heta\csc\alpha_\sigma,\qquad \|\operatorname{Cap}_\sigma\|^2 =N^{-2}\csc	heta\csc\alpha_\sigma . 	ag{18a} \] The sine sum used below proves both identities directly from (17)--(18). Uniformly the ordinary cup has norm at most \(N\csc	heta=O(N^2)\), and the cap at most \(\csc	heta/N=O(1)\). The rank-one middle-height factor of their cup-cap composition has norm \(\csc	heta\csc\alpha_\sigma\); no positive bubble is substituted. ## 6. The full marked tensor and the original boundary norms The unrestricted original marked row factors exactly: \[ m[u_\eta(\lambda)\otimes u_\lambda(\sigma)] ={1\over N^2}\Phi_{\eta,\lambda}(q^{-1}) \Phi_{\lambda,\sigma}(-q^{-2}). 	ag{19} \] Write \(m_{\eta,\lambda,\sigma}\) for this coefficient. There is no height delta in this formula. For outer and deeper height \(c\), [G] instead gives the useful full graph-row identity \(mL_c=h/N\), \(h_a=x^a\). Directly \(hB_c^{(1)}=\mu_*h\), where \[ \mu_*=-q^{-1}-q^2=\lambda_{N-2},\qquad \alpha_*=\pi-3	heta,\quad s_*=\sin\alpha_*=\sin3	heta. \] The recurrence or reciprocity gives \(D_a(\mu_*;c)/F_a=x^a\). Hence \[ m_{c,\lambda,c}=\delta_{\lambda,\mu_*}\,T_*, \qquad T_*={2\over N(1-q^{-3})} ={x^dp_N'(\mu_*)\over q^dN^2}. 	ag{20} \] For example \(h u_{\mu_*}(c)=\sum_{a=0}^dq^{-3a} =2/(1-q^{-3})\). No denominator vanishes for \(N\ge2\). On the external channel \(
u_0=c\), (17) expands the actual \(u_0\) with even heights \(
u_{2j}=c\) and odd coefficients \(\prod_{j=1}^k A_{
u_{2j-1}}\). The literal LAST-mark row in (5), by repeated (18) and then (20), is \[ \ell_0(v_{ oldsymbol
u}) =A_c^{-(k-1)}T_* \prod_{j=1}^{k-1}\delta_{
u_{2j},c}\, \delta_{
u_{2k-1},\mu_*}. 	ag{21} \] This proves the original ordering directly. It needs no mark relocation. Other individual marked rows need not agree on arbitrary channels; the already proved relocation on actual regular invariant sources retains precisely that narrower scope. Use \(\sum_{r=0}^d\sin\alpha_r=\csc	heta\), obtained by summing the finite geometric progression. The outer \(c\) factor in (14) is retained. Equations (17)--(21) give the exact source norms \[  oxed{\quad \|u_0\|_{G_{m ht}}^2=(N^2\csc^2	heta)^k,\qquad \|\ell_0|_{\mathcal E_c}\|_{G_{m ht}^{-1}}^2 ={1\over(N^2\sin^2	heta)^{k-1}}\, {\sin	heta\over N^2s_*}. \quad} 	ag{22} \] For the second formula the reciprocal path weight on its support is \(\sin^k	heta\,s_*\prod_{j<k}\sin\alpha_{
u_{2j-1}}\). Sum the \(k-1\) free odd heights and use the displayed sine sum. The remaining factors are \(|A_c|^{-2k+2}|T_*|^2\), proving (22). Since \(\sin	heta\le s_*\le3\sin	heta\), these are polynomial at every fixed width, and \(\|\ell_0|_{\mathcal E_c}\|=\Theta_k(N^{-1})\). Multiplying by \(|\chi_N|\) restores any external scalar in the row. The claim is not a bound for the unrestricted marked row on all external heights of the full physical tensor space. ## 7. One signed crossing between the legs of the marked pair The following is an all-channel row identity, before estimating any adjoining coherent exterior. The crossing is between the two legs of the marked pair, with outer and deeper heights \(c\). Put \[ b^\pm_\lambda=(mR^\pm) [u_c(\lambda)\otimes u_\lambda(c)]. \] The phase-exact reduced crossing sends \(u_\lambda(c)\) to \(\kappa\,\overline{D_a(\lambda;c)/F_a}\) in coordinate \(a\). The graph row \(h/N\) thus gives \[ b^+_\lambda={\kappa\over N} \overline{\Phi_{\lambda,c}(-q)}. 	ag{23} \] For \(\lambda=\mu_j\), (4) of [S] gives \[ \Phi_{\lambda,c}(-q)=(Q;Q)_A(q^3;Q)_B,\quad B=d-A,\quad A= egin{cases}[\lfloor N/2floor-j]_N,&N\ {m even},\ [\lfloor N/2floor+j]_N,&N\ {m odd}. \end{cases} \] Every sine half-angle in this product is in \((0,\pi)\). Its exact phase and positive magnitude are therefore \[ b^+_\lambda=\eta_{N,A}W_{N,A},\quad \eta_{N,A}=\kappa i^dq^{-[A(A+1)+B(B+2)]/2},\quad W_{N,A}={R_A\over N\sin	heta},\quad R_A=\prod_{h=1}^A{\sin(h\pi/N)\over\sin((h-	frac12)\pi/N)}. 	ag{24} \] The half-grid sine product is \(2\); reflection of its omitted last \(A\) factors proves the formula for \(W\). The ratio \(R_A/R_{A-1}\) crosses one only once, so \(R_A\) is unimodal. Its endpoints are \(1\) and \(N\sin	heta\ge1\). Moreover \(\sin t/t\) decreases on \((0,\pi)\), so \[ R_A\le\prod_{h=1}^A{h\over h-	frac12} \le C\sqrt{A+1}\le C\sqrt N . \] The middle inequality follows by taking logarithms and using \(\sum_{h=1}^A(2h-1)^{-1}\le	frac12\log(A+1)+C\). Thus, with universal constants, \[ 2/\pi\le W_{N,A}\le C\sqrt N . 	ag{25} \] This lower bound is for every actual channel, not just a largest mode. The boundary phase is the same height chirp already present in [S]. For sorted \(\lambda=\lambda_r\), its physical root permutation gives \(2A=N-	frac12+(-1)^{N+r}(r+	frac12)\). Substitute this in the quadratic exponent of (24): \[ \eta_{N,A}=\zeta_N f_r^{-1},\qquad \zeta_N=i^dq^{d(N-4)/4}. 	ag{26} \] All quarter powers are the stated exponential branches. For \(r=N-2\), \(A=d\), \(W=1\), and \(b^+=\kappa\). The graph eigen-row \(h/N\) annihilates all but \(\mu_*\) before the crossing. Since [S] proves \(B^-=\overline{B^+}\) entrywise in this same frame, (20) gives the exact negative row \[ b^-_\lambda={T_*\over ar T_*}\,\overline{b^+_\lambda} =-q^3\overline{b^+_\lambda}. 	ag{27} \] No free flip or reversal of the original marked ordering is used. In the positive metric the two-head path norm is \(\csc	heta\,\csc\alpha_r\), not \(h_N(c,\lambda)^2\). Its normalized boundary coefficient is therefore \[ \widehat b^\pm_r=b^\pm_r\sqrt{\sin	heta\sin\alpha_r}, \qquad  oxed{\quad c_0/N\le|\widehat b^\pm_r|\le C_0 \quad(N\ge2,\ 0\le r<N).\quad} 	ag{28} \] Use (25), \(\sin\alpha_r\ge\sin	heta\ge1/N\), and \(\sin	heta\le\pi/(2N)\). The constants are universal. Ordinary caps on the other pairs multiply the exact tensor (21). In particular the same statement applies to a crossing on the literal final marked pair, retaining all earlier ordinary caps. It is not necessary to move that mark across an arbitrary exterior. There is also an actual row-norm bound, with that crossing included: \[ \|\ell_0R_{2k-1}^{\pm}|_{\mathcal E_c}\|_{G_{m ht}^{-1}}^2 ={\,\sin	heta\sum_r W_{N,A(r)}^2\sin\alpha_r\over (N^2\sin^2	heta)^{k-1}}, \qquad c_k\le\|\ell_0R_{2k-1}^{\pm}|_{\mathcal E_c}\|_{G_{m ht}^{-1}} \le C_k\sqrt N . 	ag{29} \] For the lower bound use \(W\ge2/\pi\), and for the upper use \(W^2\le CN\); the same exact sine sum proves both. These are norms of the unscaled original row. An included \(\chi_N\) multiplies them by \(|\chi_N|\), which is not declared polynomial. ## 8. What has been simplified This explicit positive path metric has polynomial original input and marked-output costs on the globally conserved source channel. Its local signed crossing rate is the sewn-cell volume itself, without the neighboring graph-weight corrections of the physical joint Haar metric. The marked cap followed by a crossing between its two legs has nonzero polynomially bounded coefficients in every channel, with an explicit single-height quadratic phase. These are actual source-dependent normalization and boundary estimates. The boundary statement is a row on all graph exteriors in \(\mathcal E_c\), not a new terminal-curl survival statement on saturated regular invariant sources. They do not make the original observation positive. The signed pairing (13) is still indefinite; the ordinary cup source and its actual braid images remain isotropic. Taking its absolute coordinate diagonal changes the norm, not that algebraic fact. A row with all nonzero coefficients can annihilate a coherent exterior vector. The phases in (16), (24) and (27), unselected height channels, and the full marked functional remain in a whole component. No arbitrary short-word scalar lower bound or finite-exception volume theorem follows. The construction is on the full \(N^b\)-dimensional physical head space and its complete external channel. It does not silently reuse the \(N\)-dimensional Conway packet budgets in another compiler. Any quartic or capacity implementation must retain these actual spaces, measures, positive metrics and known normalization factors. [G] already supplies polynomial marked-row bounds in a different graph metric and retains the source-selected reduction. [R] already proves physical Krein conservation and its meridian-jet extensions. [P] already proves coherent ordinary-cap simplifications and keeps the unrestricted marked packet. The additions here are the exact height diagonal of a specified physical Krein twist, its explicit positive absolute-diagonal metric with both original boundary norms, and the all-channel marked-cap/crossing product and bounds. No first polynomial boundary frame or new general positivity principle is claimed. ## Complete proof inputs and closest coverage | Label | Complete text | Lines | SHA256 | | --- | --- | ---: | --- | | S | [Signed coideal chamber](research_coideal_crossing_signed_volume_chamber.md) | 634 | 7bf6fb943d2c8080875375c4529776159fc72fbde2e5d8a7d0742e0cbdb10fc0 | | T | [Exact crossing transport](research_coideal_crossing_orthogonality_transport.md) | 595 | 4555fecc6377077dbdc4cfb3afac50f09d180efc5659716bac8497319310114c | | K | [Continuant source kernel](research_coideal_continuant_source_kernel.md) | 365 | 3ea997e5258c9413fd7c771a6a1475b90b39bf731ac55c0902fd136943b26f44 | | G | [Graph Gram and local volume](research_coideal_graph_gram_and_octahedral_volume.md) | 398 | 35ca803fb3262b1f85a08c3aa9b9112bcc2823ce380ce82362ef18bd382d6766 | | R | [Physical real-meridian Krein form](research_real_meridian_krein_transport.md) | 310 | caf18090cb75a0527ffccdf4a3217fe422876d683271eda8e3e6d591259e92dc | | P | [Ordinary and marked cap reassociation](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_pivotal_cap_reassociation_angle_packet.md) | 243 | c822bbcc34b86c600f291f7e66c210253f341319a9d92007fcc51e6633424b14 | Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used. title: A polynomial normal gap at the original marked boundary
text:
# A polynomial normal gap at the original marked boundary 24 November 2026. Written research proof. The original marked boundary selects a particular path block of an actual adjacent-crossing difference equation. Its left and right eigenvectors are explicit finite products. They turn the normal operator into a complex weighted path Laplacian, whose compatible inverse has polynomial norm. No positivity of the complex weights is assumed. In the already specified positive height metric the normal gap is at least \(c_0N^{-12}\). Here normal means transverse to the specified vector line, not a Casimir derivative or a moving-level normal. This controls the part transverse to the marked boundary mode. It leaves that mode's amplitude free and does not bound the original closed scalar below. In particular, an interior crossing with the opposite sign still requires a signed overlap between different normal operators. ## 1. The original source and the statement Fix \(N\ge2\), and use the conventions of the complete inputs: \[ q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\quad d=N-1,\quad c=1+q,\quad x=-q^{-1},\quad \kappa=q^{d^2/2},\quad F_a=(Q;Q)_a . 	ag{1} \] In particular \(F_d=N\). Write \(\mu_j=Q^j+qQ^{-j}\), \(0\le j<N\), for the distinct coideal roots, and \(p_N\) for their monic polynomial. They are the sorted roots \(2\sqrt q\cos\alpha_r\), with \(\alpha_r=(r+	frac12)\pi/N\), in a different order. All indices on \(\mu_j\) are read modulo \(N\). The finite continuants and their generating polynomial are \[  egin{split} D_{-1}&=0,\quad D_0=1,\ D_{a+1}(\lambda;\sigma) &=(\lambda+qQ^a\sigma)D_a(\lambda;\sigma) -q(1-Q^a)^2D_{a-1}(\lambda;\sigma),\ \Phi_{\lambda,\sigma}(z)&=\sum_{a=0}^d D_a(\lambda;\sigma)z^a/F_a . \end{split} 	ag{2} \] Only \(F_a\) with \(a<N\) occurs in a denominator. For four physical heads the literal row is \((\ell_{12}\otimes m_{34})R_{23}^+\), with the last marked cap in its original position. On the external channel \(\mathcal E_c\), its last height is \(\mu_*=-q^{-1}-q^2\). Its other two input heights are \(
u,ho\), and [C] gives \[ M^+_{
u,ho} = eta_N\overline{\Phi_{ho,
u}(q^{-1})} = eta_N\Phi_{
u,ho}(-q),\qquad  eta_N= rac{T_*}{A_c} rac{\kappa(1-q)}2 . 	ag{3} \] Here \(A_c,T_*\) are the original nonzero boundary constants. The second equality is continuant reciprocity, including the conjugation of \(F_a\). Neither \( eta_N\) nor a further original external factor \(\chi_N\) is deleted from the source. Fix \(ho=\mu_l\), put \(m=\lfloor N/2floor\), and define \[ t(j)=  egin{cases}[m-j]_N,&N	ext{ even},\[m+j]_N,&N	ext{ odd}, \end{cases} \qquad I_l=\{j:l\le t(j)\le d\},\qquad M_l=N-l . 	ag{4} \] The selected set is ordered by \(t=l,\ldots,d\). It is precisely the nonzero support of the boundary column in (3); in this order its path is \(l\longleftrightarrow l+1\longleftrightarrow \cdots\longleftrightarrow d\). We construct below an actual adjacent-crossing matrix \(J_{c,ho}\). The set \(I_l\) is a reducing path block for this matrix. Write \(J_l\) for its restriction, and use counting Euclidean norms in these raw height coordinates. There are explicit nonzero vectors \(s_l\) and rows \(r_l\) with \[ r_l(J_l-\mu_*I)=0,\quad (J_l-\mu_*I)s_l=0,\quad r_ls_l= rac{2\kappa}{1-q^3}. 	ag{5} \] **Theorem.** There is a universal \(C>0\) such that \[ \operatorname{dist}_2(w,\mathbb Cs_l) \le CN^{11}\|(J_l-\mu_*I)w\|_2 . 	ag{6} \] Every compatible right side \(f\), meaning \(r_lf=0\), has an explicit solution of \((J_l-\mu_*I)w=f\) with \(\|w\|_2\le CN^{11}\|f\|_2\). In [H]'s original absolute-height metric, restricted to this block, \[ \operatorname{dist}_{m ht}(w,\mathbb Cs_l) \le CN^{12}\|(J_l-\mu_*I)w\|_{m ht}. 	ag{7} \] The constants are independent of \(l\), all selected coordinates, and \(N\). For \(M_l=1\) the compatible right side is zero. This is a normal equation on the specified block, not a claim that an arbitrary braid preserves that block. ## 2. A finite cyclic difference equation Let \(T_ho\) be the actual one-head tridiagonal matrix \[ (T_ho v)_a=(1-Q^a)v_{a-1} +q(1-Q^{a+1})v_{a+1}-qQ^aho v_a . 	ag{8} \] The endpoint coefficients vanish at \(a=0,d\). Its eigenmatrix is \[ (U_ho)_{a,j}=q^{-a}D_a(\mu_j;ho)/F_a,\qquad T_ho U_ho=U_ho X,\quad X=\operatorname{diag}(\mu_j). 	ag{9} \] It is invertible by the full simple-root graph construction in [K]. No bound for \(U_ho^{-1}\) is used in the theorem. Here is a finite proof of the needed difference relation. Put \(u=Q^j,v=q/u\), and define \[  egin{split} a_j&=- rac{v^2+qho v+qQ}{(u-v)(v-Qu)},\ b_j&= rac{u^2+qho u+qQ}{(u-v)(u-Qv)},\ (\mathscr D_ho f)_j &=a_j(f_{j+1}-f_j)+b_j(f_{j-1}-f_j). \end{split} 	ag{10} \] Every denominator factor is a unit phase times a difference of odd powers of \(q\), and is nonzero at all levels in question. The recurrence (2), including its final row \(D_N=0\), gives \[ (1-\mu_jz+qz^2)\Phi_{\mu_j,ho}(z) =(1+qho z+qQz^2)\Phi_{\mu_j,ho}(Qz). 	ag{11} \] In particular its coefficients below \(z^N\), with constant one, are unique, since \(1-Q^a
e0\) for \(0<a<N\). Applying this uniqueness after shifting \(j\) gives the formal ratios \[  rac{\Phi_{\mu_{j+1},ho}(z)}{\Phi_{\mu_j,ho}(z)} \equiv rac{1-uz}{1-vz/Q},\qquad  rac{\Phi_{\mu_{j-1},ho}(z)}{\Phi_{\mu_j,ho}(z)} \equiv rac{1-vz}{1-uz/Q}\pmod {z^N}. 	ag{12} \] For example the first rational multiplier changes the two denominator roots \(u,v\) to \(Qu,v/Q\) in (11). All these formal denominators have constant one. Substitute (12) into (10) and take a common denominator. The resulting identity is \[ a_j\left( rac{1-uz}{1-vz/Q}-1ight) +b_j\left( rac{1-vz}{1-uz/Q}-1ight) = rac{1+qho z/Q+qz^2/Q} {(1-uz/Q)(1-vz/Q)}-1 . 	ag{13} \] The right side is \(\Phi_{\mu_j,ho}(z/Q)/\Phi_{\mu_j,ho}(z)-1\) by (11). Coefficient comparison proves, for every \(0\le a<N\), \[ \mathscr D_ho igl(D_a(\mu_j;ho)/F_a igr) =(Q^{-a}-1)D_a(\mu_j;ho)/F_a . 	ag{14} \] Thus, with \(Z=\operatorname{diag}(Q^a)\) on the physical head, \[ K_ho:=U_ho^{-1}Z^{-1}U_ho=I+\mathscr D_ho^{\mathsf T}. 	ag{15} \] The transpose is important: (14) acts on a row of \(U_ho\). This is a cyclic tridiagonal matrix, with the coincident shifts at \(N=2\) interpreted by addition. The relation is a finite version of the usual Al-Salam--Chihara difference equation; that general mechanism is not claimed new. Equations (11)--(14) supply its proof and exact root conventions here without importing an analytic extension. ## 3. The actual adjacent crossing and its selected path Let \(\mathcal D=\operatorname{diag}(q^{-a})\). The actual positive crossing in the unchanged height frame is \[ B^+_{c,ho}=\kappa U_ho^{-1}\mathcal D\overline{U_c}, \qquad B^-_{c,ho}=\overline{B^+_{c,ho}} =(B^+_{c,ho})^{-1}. 	ag{16} \] These are the source matrices of [S,T], not arbitrary connections. The corresponding physical output operator is \[ (J_c'v)_a=(1-Q^{-a})v_{a-1} +q(1-Q^{-a-1})v_{a+1}-q^{-1}Q^{-a}cv_a . 	ag{17} \] Define \(J_{c,ho}=U_ho^{-1}J_c'U_ho\) at every \(N\). It obeys \[ J_{c,ho}B^+_{c,ho}=B^+_{c,ho}X,\qquad B^-_{c,ho}J_{c,ho}=XB^-_{c,ho}. 	ag{18} \] For \(N\ge3\) it has a directly sparse height formula: \[ J_{c,ho} =- rac{K_ho X+XK_ho+2qho I}{1+Q} -q^{-1}cK_ho . 	ag{19} \] Indeed, decompose (8) into its lower arrow, upper arrow and diagonal. Multiplication by \(Z^{-1}\) in (17) gives \((1+Q)J_c'=-(Z^{-1}T_ho+T_ho Z^{-1}+2qho I) -q^{-1}c(1+Q)Z^{-1}\), entry by entry. Conjugation proves (19). Here \(|1+Q|\ge1\), so no large division occurs. The two directions on the edge \(j,j+1\) have the same extra factor: \[ (J_{c,ho})_{j,j+1}=b_{j+1}h_j,\quad (J_{c,ho})_{j+1,j}=a_jh_j,\quad h_j=-q^{-1}(\mu_{-j}+c) =-q^{-1}(1+Q^j)(q+Q^{-j}). 	ag{20} \] For \(ho=\mu_l\), \(a_j\) and \(b_{j+1}\) vanish at the same single edge \(j=t(l)\). To check both parities explicitly, the numerator of \(a_j\), up to a unit, factors as \((1+Q^{j+l})(1+qQ^{j-l})\). At even \(N\) only the first factor can vanish, at \(j=m-l\); at odd \(N\) only the second can vanish, at \(j=m+l\). The factors for \(b_{j+1}\) give the same edge. The additional factor \(h_j\) vanishes precisely at \(j=m=t(0)\). These are two cuts of the cycle, with coincident cuts allowed. There is no one-way edge left at a cut. The support \(I_l\) in (4) is one of the resulting path blocks. For \(l=0\) it is the whole cycle opened at its one cut. For \(l=d\) it is a singleton. Every internal edge is nonzero. The cut coefficients were zero in the original operator, so passing to this path discards no cycle current at its endpoints. The elementary root-grid bound for a nonzero factor \(1-q^h\) or \(1+q^h\) is \(c_0/N\). The numerator factors above and denominators of modulus at most four therefore give \[ c_0N^{-4}\le |(J_l)_{i,i+1}|,\ |(J_l)_{i+1,i}| \le CN^2\qquad(0\le i<M_l-1). 	ag{21} \] Indices \(i\) here refer to the ordered path, not the cyclic labels. The upper bound also uses that the denominators in (10) have modulus at least \(c_0N^{-2}\). No lower joint-frame bound enters. ## 4. The exact marked left and right modes Let \(r_j=\Phi_{\mu_j,ho}(-q)\). Reciprocity gives the first equality in (3). The cumulative product of [C] now says \[ r_j=\overline{U_{t(j)}V_l}\quad(j\in I_l),\qquad r_j=0 \quad(j
otin I_l), 	ag{22} \] where \(U,V\) are exactly [C]'s finite product factors. Their bounds \(1\le|U_t|\le C\sqrt N\) and \(c_0N^{-1/2}\le|V_l|\le N\) show \[ c_0N^{-1/2}\le |r_j|\le CN^{3/2}\quad(j\in I_l). 	ag{23} \] Here is an exact normalization of the modes. Put \(w_a=(-Q)^a\). By (9), \(r=w^{\mathsf T}U_ho\), so (16) gives \[ rB^+_{c,ho} =\kappa igl(\overline{\Phi_{\mu_j,c}(-Q^{-1})} igr)_j = rac{2\kappa}{1-q^3}\,e_*^{\mathsf T}. 	ag{24} \] The last finite product contains \((1;Q)_B\); it vanishes unless \(B=0,A=d\), precisely the label \(\mu_*\). At that label its unconjugated value is \((q^{-1};Q)_d=2/(1-q^{-3})\). Thus (24) is the ordinary same-sign cap slide, with its actual scalar. Combining (18) and (24) proves \(rJ_{c,ho}=\mu_*r\). The right mode is \(s=B^+_{c,ho}e_*\). The graph inverse from [K] gives the entries explicitly: \[ s_j=\kappa\, rac{E_d(\mu_j;ho)}{p_N'(\mu_j)}\,r_j . 	ag{25} \] In fact \(D_a(c;\mu_*)=q^aF_a\); reciprocity implies \(D_a(\mu_*;c)/F_a=(-q^{-1})^a\), and hence \(\mathcal D\overline{U_c}e_*\) has entries \((-q)^a\). The inverse row of \(U_ho\) is \((E_d/p_N')\,(D_a/F_a)_a\), proving (25). The same continuant reflection and determinant identity as in [K,S] give, for any two of these rotated-real roots, \[ E_d(\lambda;ho)=q^d\overline{D_d(\lambda;ho)},\quad D_dE_d=q^dN^2,\quad \left| rac{E_d(\lambda;ho)}{p_N'(\lambda)}ight| =\sin\alpha_\lambda . 	ag{26} \] One can check the reflection directly: conjugate the leading minor, multiply each row by \(q\), and reverse its order. The diagonals and adjacent-arrow products become those of the trailing minor. The derivative formula is \(|p_N'(\lambda)|=N/\sin\alpha_\lambda\). Consequently \(s\) has exactly the support \(I_l\), and \[ c_0N^{-3/2}\le|s_j|\le CN^{3/2},\qquad rs=w^{\mathsf T}U_ho B^+e_* =\kappa\sum_{a=0}^d q^{3a} = rac{2\kappa}{1-q^3}. 	ag{27} \] This pairing is bilinear, not a positive inner product. Since \(|rs|=\csc(3\pi/(2N))\ge c_0N\), the known mode projector \(\Pi=sr/(rs)\) has norm at most \(CN^3\). Its normalization is not chosen from an unknown closed source value. For clarity, \(N=2\) needs no division by \(1+Q\). Here \(q=i,c=\mu_*=1+i\). At \(ho=c\), direct use of (8),(17) gives \[ J_{c,c}= egin{pmatrix}3c&4i\-4&-3c\end{pmatrix}, \quad r=(2,c),\quad s=\kappa(1-i,i)^{\mathsf T}. 	ag{28} \] Their pairing is \(\kappa(1-i)=2\kappa/(1-q^3)\). At \(ho=-c\), \(J=X\), the selected block is \(j=0\), and its modes are \(r=1-i,s=\kappa\). Thus all assertions above hold after enlarging universal constants. ## 5. Compatible elimination by first differences Restrict now to the selected ordered block. Write \(L_l=J_l-\mu_*I\), \(D_r=\operatorname{diag}(r_i)\), \(D_s=\operatorname{diag}(s_i)\), and \[ \omega_i=r_i(L_l)_{i,i+1}s_{i+1}\quad(0\le i<M_l-1). 	ag{29} \] Every \(\omega_i\) is nonzero, with \(c_0N^{-6}\le|\omega_i|\le CN^5\), by (21),(23),(27). The two null equations imply \[ D_rL_lD_s=-
abla^{\mathsf T} \operatorname{diag}(\omega_i)
abla,\qquad (
abla y)_i=y_{i+1}-y_i . 	ag{30} \] Here is a proof including the endpoints. The left side has zero row and column sums. At its first vertex these equalities force the two off-diagonal entries across the first edge to agree. Induction does the same at every following edge. Each diagonal is minus the sum of its incident edge weights, giving (30). Equivalently, the difference between the forward and backward flux is constant along the path and vanishes at its end. This factorization is complex symmetric; it is not a positive quadratic form. Nevertheless \(
abla\) maps the counting orthogonal complement of the constant vector bijectively onto \(\mathbb C^{M_l-1}\), with least singular value \(2\sin(\pi/(2M_l))\ge c_0/N\). Its transpose maps that space back bijectively. Thus the restriction of the right side of (30) to constants perpendicular is invertible and its inverse norm is at most \(CN^8\). This is a product bound for three invertible maps between the stated spaces; it does not infer positivity from complex weights. There is also a direct flux solution. For \(r_lf=0\), set \[ g_i=r_if_i,\quad F_i=\sum_{a=0}^i g_a,\quad y_{i+1}-y_i=F_i/\omega_i,\quad \sum_{i=0}^{M_l-1}y_i=0 . 	ag{31} \] The compatibility condition says \(\sum_i g_i=0\). It is exactly the last-vertex equation, not an additional imposed endpoint value. There is no requirement \(y_{M_l-1}=0\). The vector \(w=D_sy\) solves \(L_lw=f\). For a singleton the compatible datum and this chosen solution are both zero. The inverse bound for (30) and the upper component bounds yield \[ \|w\|_2\le \|D_s\|\,CN^8\,\|D_r\|\,\|f\|_2 \le CN^{11}\|f\|_2 . 	ag{32} \] Also (30) proves \(\ker L_l=\mathbb Cs_l\) and \(\operatorname{range}L_l=\ker r_l\), without a rank guess. For arbitrary \(w\), apply (32) to \(f=L_lw\); subtracting the constructed solution changes \(w\) by a kernel vector. This proves (6). At fixed neighboring heights all other factors in [H]'s complete height metric are a common scalar. Its remaining weights are \(\csc\alpha_j\), between \(1\) and \(CN\). The change from counting norm to this prescribed norm costs at most \(C\sqrt N\). Equation (32) therefore gives the clean uniform exponent \(12\) in (7). No physical Hilbert--Schmidt frame comparison is used. There is also a unique gauge that preserves the marked row. The projector \(\Pi=s_lr_l/(r_ls_l)\) satisfies \[ \|\Pi\|_2\le CN^3,\quad \|\Pi\|_{m ht}\le CN^{7/2}, \qquad \|(I-\Pi)w\|_{m ht} \le CN^{15}\|L_lw\|_{m ht}. 	ag{32a} \] Indeed choose a best raw approximation to \(w\) on its \(s_l\) line, and apply \(I-\Pi\) to their difference. Equation (6) and \(\|I-\Pi\|_2\le CN^3\) give raw cost \(CN^{14}\); the height change contributes at most \(C\sqrt N\). For \(r_lf=0\), applying \(I-\Pi\) to (31)'s solution gives the unique solution of \(L_lw=f,\ r_lw=0\), with this bound. Write \(H_{m ht}\) for the restricted height Gram. The explicit positive marked Gram is \[ H_{m mark}=\Pi^\dagger H_{m ht}\Pi +(I-\Pi)^\dagger H_{m ht}(I-\Pi), \qquad 	frac12H_{m ht}\le H_{m mark}\le CN^7H_{m ht}. 	ag{32b} \] The lower bound follows by adding the two components of \(w\) and using the triangle inequality; the upper follows from (32a). It makes \(\mathbb Cs_l\) orthogonal to \(\ker r_l\), and equals \(H_{m ht}\) exactly on each of those two subspaces. Thus the row \(r_l\) is retained as the known marked coordinate, not replaced by a new functional. Both \(L_lw\) and \((I-\Pi)w\) lie in \(\ker r_l\), so (32a) holds in \(H_{m mark}\) as well. Its left side is then the exact orthogonal distance to the mode. Nonzero scalar rescalings of the original marked row do not change \(\Pi\). ## 6. What this eliminates in the original source The coefficients in (31) are all known finite source data. The compatible normal problem can therefore be eliminated by cumulative sums and first differences with polynomial loss. Its residual energy remains quadratic in that linear problem. It does not require a dense inverse with an unknown condition number, or an estimate for a discarded boundary coordinate. At greater fixed width the earlier ordinary caps and their constraints remain exactly those of [C,H]; the same local block calculation has the same constants. This selected normal problem still applies to every attached state at the literal boundary. Let \(P_l\) be coordinate projection onto \(I_l\). It commutes with \(J\), has height norm one, and \(r=rP_l\). Thus \(rw=rP_lw\) for any full incoming height vector, and the gap applies to \(P_lw\) with residual \(P_l(J-\mu_*I)w\). The whole preceding word remains in \(w\). This does not permit inserting \(P_l\) before other crossings or give a bound for the unselected component. The one-dimensional kernel remains. Its coefficient is not controlled by a normal residual and has not been fixed by minimization. The original marked row, its factor \( eta_N\), and the original exterior factor \(\chi_N\) must still be used when recovering the scalar. The unresolved opposite-sign seam is explicit. Conjugating (18) gives \(q\overline J\,B^-=B^-X\), whereas the marked row is a left mode of \(J\). More concretely, if \(f_ho(z)=(\Phi_{\mu_j,ho}(z))_j\) and \(g_ho(z)=f_ho(z)B^-\), then the literal opposed row is \( eta_Ng_ho(-q)\), and (11),(18) give \[ g_ho(z)J=(z^{-1}+qz)g_ho(z) -(z^{-1}+qho+qQz)g_ho(Qz). 	ag{33} \] No lower bound for that signed mode overlap is proved here. Nor is \(I_l\) declared invariant under arbitrary crossings. These are full coideal source coordinates; no Casimir first normal, original cap, or boundary phase has been replaced. The general difference equation and cap slide are established mechanisms. The additional assertion is the polynomial normal gap on the block selected by the actual marked boundary, with its explicit compatible flux inverse and existing height metric. The older pivotal-cap reassociation [P] is a different source-basis reduction. The positive Jacobi boundary problem [J] concerns Newton value data in a spectral half-plane and its positive Green resolvent. Here the operator is non-Hermitian, the data are the marked coideal mode, and the estimate holds on every selected path without a half-plane assumption. Neither result supplies a lower bound for a prescribed coherent exterior or the finite-exception volume theorem after arbitrary short partial fillings. ## Complete inputs and closest coverage | Label | Complete text | Lines | SHA256 | | --- | --- | ---: | --- | | C | [Cumulative marked boundary](research_coideal_cap_straddling_cumulative_kernel.md) | 450 | 3ff48e5998f325e1391c088b688a01388f5b8e21d3c8ce53f9ed556e9b289c71 | | H | [Height pairing and original boundary](research_coideal_height_pairing_and_marked_boundary.md) | 543 | bed81fcb12b20d16d41c55b476b13d8d69b1fe79d0d0620c31230ba652b1d82f | | S | [Signed crossing and exact phases](research_coideal_crossing_signed_volume_chamber.md) | 634 | 7bf6fb943d2c8080875375c4529776159fc72fbde2e5d8a7d0742e0cbdb10fc0 | | T | [Actual coideal crossing transport](research_coideal_crossing_orthogonality_transport.md) | 595 | 4555fecc6377077dbdc4cfb3afac50f09d180efc5659716bac8497319310114c | | K | [Continuant source kernel](research_coideal_continuant_source_kernel.md) | 365 | 3ea997e5258c9413fd7c771a6a1475b90b39bf731ac55c0902fd136943b26f44 | | P | [Original pivotal cap reassociation](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_pivotal_cap_reassociation_angle_packet.md) | 243 | c822bbcc34b86c600f291f7e66c210253f341319a9d92007fcc51e6633424b14 | | J | [Earlier positive Jacobi charge boundary](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_physical_jacobi_charge_boundary.md) | 432 | 530425b0c4504f2512954438465deb6d9a6e322fa58c641b6c678161baae6583 | Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used. title: An initialized coideal period has a flat abelian framing
A signed lower bound for the opposed marked mode
text: # A signed lower bound for the opposed marked mode 24 November 2026. Written research proof. The original marked boundary has explicit left and right modes in the coideal height frame. With the same crossing sign their pairing is an elementary cap slide. With the opposite sign it is a quadratic oscillatory sum. This note proves that the latter pairing has a positive real part after one specified, label-independent phase is removed, at every height and all sufficiently large levels. The lower bound is polynomial. The estimate also solves the opposite-sign normal equation in the gauge specified by the original marked row. It does not give a lower bound for contraction against an arbitrary coherent exterior or for the original closed knot scalar. ## 1. Actual modes, source factors and the statement Use the complete conventions of [N,C,H,S,K]: \[ N\ge2,\quad d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\quad \delta=\pi/N,\quad\theta=\delta/2,\quad c=1+q,\quad \kappa=q^{d^2/2},\quad F_a=(Q;Q)_a . \tag{1} \] All fractional powers have these exponential branches. The distinct coideal roots are \(\mu_j=Q^j+qQ^{-j}\), \(0\le j<N\). They are a permutation of \(\lambda_r=2\sqrt q\cos((r+\tfrac12)\delta)\). The continuants, their trailing minor and their generating polynomial are \[ \begin{split} D_{-1}&=0,\qquad D_0=1,\\ D_{a+1}(\lambda;\rho) &=(\lambda+qQ^a\rho)D_a(\lambda;\rho) -q(1-Q^a)^2D_{a-1}(\lambda;\rho),\\ \Phi_{\lambda,\rho}(z) &=\sum_{a=0}^dD_a(\lambda;\rho)z^a/F_a,\qquad E_d(\lambda;\rho)=\text{trailing continuant}. \end{split} \tag{2} \] Here \(F_d=N\), and \(p_N\) is the monic polynomial with roots \(\mu_j\). No denominator \(F_a\) with \(a\ge N\) is used. Fix \(\rho=\mu_l\), put \(m=\lfloor N/2\rfloor\), and set \[ t(j)= \begin{cases}[m-j]_N,&N\text{ even},\\[m+j]_N,&N\text{ odd}, \end{cases} \qquad I_l=\{j:l\le t(j)\le d\}. \tag{3} \] The actual marked row and right mode from [N] are \[ r_{l,j}=\Phi_{\mu_j,\rho}(-q),\qquad s_{l,j}=\kappa\,\frac{E_d(\mu_j;\rho)}{p_N'(\mu_j)}\,r_{l,j}. \tag{4} \] Both vanish off \(I_l\). The rows and columns below use these raw height coordinates and their counting Euclidean norm. If \(B^\pm_{c,\rho}\) are the actual crossing matrices in this unchanged frame, [N,S] give \[ B^-=\overline{B^+}=(B^+)^{-1},\qquad s_l=B^+e_*,\qquad r_ls_l=\frac{2\kappa}{1-q^3},\qquad \mu_*=-q^{-1}-q^2 . \tag{5} \] The star labels the root \(\mu_*\), not an adjoint. The new scalar is the literal opposed-mode coefficient \[ \boxed{\quad \gamma_l=r_lB^-e_*=r_l\overline{s_l} =\bar\kappa\sum_{j\in I_l} \overline{\frac{E_d(\mu_j;\rho)}{p_N'(\mu_j)}}\,|r_{l,j}|^2 . \quad} \tag{6} \] For example, the cap-straddling boundary row of [C] is \(\beta_Nr_l\), where its original factor satisfies \[ \beta_N=\frac{T_*}{A_c}\frac{\kappa(1-q)}2,\qquad |\beta_N|=\frac1{N^2\sin3\theta}\asymp N^{-1}. \tag{7} \] Its opposed coefficient is \(\beta_N\gamma_l\). Any original external scalar \(\chi_N\) is retained as a further factor. **Theorem.** There are universal constants \(N_0,c_0,C>0\) such that for every \(N\ge N_0\) and every \(0\le l<N\), \[ \boxed{\qquad \operatorname{Re}(\kappa\gamma_l)\ge c_0N^{-3}, \qquad c_0N^{-3}\le|\gamma_l|\le CN^4 . \qquad} \tag{8} \] Consequently \(|\beta_N\gamma_l|\ge c_0N^{-4}\). The phase removed in the real-part inequality is the same for all labels. For nonnegative real numbers \(a_l\), \[ \operatorname{Re}\!\left(\kappa\sum_l a_l\gamma_l\right) \ge c_0N^{-3}\sum_l a_l . \tag{9} \] This last assertion assumes those actual nonnegative coefficients; it does not assign that sign to an arbitrary attached packet. On any fixed bulk interval \(\varepsilon N\le l\le(1-\varepsilon)N\), the more precise, uniform estimate is \[ \kappa\gamma_l= \frac{1}{2\sin^2((l-\tfrac12)\delta)} \bigl(1+O_\varepsilon(N^{-1/2})\bigr). \tag{10} \] The error in (10) is complex. In particular the principal amplitude is positive and has zero exponential rate. ## 2. Exact reduction to one quadratic tail The cumulative kernel of [C] supplies \[ U_t=\prod_{k=1}^t\frac{1-Q^{-k}}{1-q^{2k-1}},\quad U_0=1,\qquad V_l=\frac2{U_l(1-q^{2l-1})},\qquad W_t=|U_t|^2 . \tag{11} \] Thus \(r_{l,j}=\overline{U_{t(j)}V_l}\) on \(I_l\), and \[ W_t=\prod_{k=1}^t \frac{\sin^2(k\delta)}{\sin^2((k-\tfrac12)\delta)},\qquad 1\le W_t\le CN,\qquad |V_l|^2\ge c_0/N . \tag{12} \] The endpoint \(l=0\) still has the denominator \(1-q^{-1}\) in \(V_0\). It is not replaced by a missing factor. We record the phase needed from the continuants, rather than using their modulus alone. On the selected support, write \(t=t(j)\), \(A=t-l\), \(B=d-A\). The exact finite product is \[ \Phi_{\mu_j,\mu_l}(z) =(-qQ^lz;Q)_A(-q^2Q^{-l}z;Q)_B . \tag{13} \] Its leading coefficient is \[ \frac{D_d(\mu_j;\mu_l)}N =q^{A^2+B^2+B+2l(A-B)} =(-1)^d q^{2t^2+t-2l^2+l}. \tag{14} \] For the second equality substitute \(A=t-l\), use \(d=N-1\), and remove the integer multiple \(2Nt\) from the exponent. This computation works at both level parities. The cyclic derivative of \(p_N(s+q/s)=s^N-s^{-N}\), at \(s^N=1\), similarly gives \[ p_N'(\mu_j)=(-1)^N\frac{2NQ^t}{qQ^{2t}-1}. \tag{15} \] Indeed \(Q^j=-Q^{-t}\) at even \(N\), and \(Q^j=-qQ^t\) at odd \(N\). Continuant reflection gives \(E_d=q^d\overline{D_d}\), while \(\overline{p_N'}=q^{-d}p_N'\) on these roots. Hence \(\overline{E_d/p_N'}=D_d/p_N'\). Equations (6),(11),(14),(15) now give the exact identity \[ \boxed{\quad \gamma_l=\bar\kappa\,\frac{|V_l|^2}{2}\,\overline{E_l}\,H_l, \qquad E_t=q^{2t^2-t},\qquad H_l=\sum_{t=l}^d(E_t-E_{t+1})W_t,\qquad E_N=-1 . \quad} \tag{16} \] Here \(q^{-2l^2+l}=\overline{E_l}\) is precisely the phase that arises from (14); it is not an independently chosen row rephasing. In particular \[ \operatorname{Re}(\kappa\gamma_l) =\frac{|V_l|^2}{2}\operatorname{Re}(\overline{E_l}H_l). \tag{17} \] The problem is therefore a signed scalar tail with all endpoint factors kept. ## 3.
