An exact positive identity on the decreasing half The ratio \(W_t/W_{t-1}\) crosses one once. More precisely \(W_t\) increases up to \(t=m\) and decreases thereafter. Its endpoint is \[ W_d=N^2\sin^2\theta\ge1 . \tag{18} \] For \(l\ge m\), put \(a_t=W_{t-1}-W_t\ge0\), \(t>l\). Summation by parts in (16) gives \[ \operatorname{Re}(\overline{E_l}H_l) =\frac{W_d}{2}|1+E_l|^2 +\frac12\sum_{t=l+1}^d a_t|E_t-E_l|^2 . \tag{19} \] To verify the constants, before taking the real part the same identity is \(H_l=E_lW_l+W_d-\sum_{t>l}a_tE_t\); use \(W_l=W_d+\sum_{t>l}a_t\). For \(N\ge3\), the last decrement satisfies \[ a_d=W_d\,\frac{\sin5\theta\,\sin\theta}{\sin^22\theta} \ge\frac14 . \tag{20} \] Here \(\theta\le\pi/6\), \(\sin5\theta\ge\sin\theta\), and \(\sin2\theta\le2\sin\theta\). If \(l<d\), retain only the first and last terms in (19). Since \(E_d=-q^3\), the triangle inequality gives \[ \operatorname{Re}(\overline{E_l}H_l) \ge\frac1{16}|1+E_d|^2 =\frac1{16}|1-q^3|^2\ge\frac1{4N^2}. \tag{21} \] The same bound follows directly from (19) for \(l=d\). At \(N=2\), \(m=d=1\), and the only decreasing-half tail has \(\operatorname{Re}(\overline{E_1}H_1)=2\). Thus (21) holds on this half at every level, after no finite-level exclusion. ## 4. Uniform Wallis estimates and the Abel reduction For the other half we first prove, uniformly over every \(0\le t<N\), \[ \boxed{\quad W_t=N\sin(t\delta)+O(1),\qquad W_t-W_{t-1}=\pi\cos(t\delta) +O\!\left(\frac1t+\frac1{N-t}\right) \quad(1\le t<N). \quad} \tag{22} \] These estimates do not treat the two endpoints as bulk points. For \(1\le t\le N/2\), let \[ W_t^{(0)}=\prod_{k=1}^t\left(\frac{k}{k-\tfrac12}\right)^2, \qquad f(x)=\log(\sin x/x),\quad f(0)=0. \tag{23} \] The elementary Wallis bounds are \(\pi t\le W_t^{(0)}\le\pi(t+\tfrac12)\). For completeness, if \(I_n=\int_0^{\pi/2}\sin^n x\,dx\), then \(I_{2t}=\pi/(2\sqrt{W_t^{(0)}})\), \(I_{2t+1}=\sqrt{W_t^{(0)}}/(2t+1)\), and \(I_{2t-1}=\sqrt{W_t^{(0)}}/(2t)\). The inequalities \(I_{2t+1}\le I_{2t}\le I_{2t-1}\) prove the bounds. On \([0,\pi/2]\), \(f''\) is bounded. Comparing the two halves of each interval of length \(\delta\) gives \[ 2\sum_{k=1}^t [f(k\delta)-f((k-\tfrac12)\delta)] =f(t\delta)+O(N^{-1}). \tag{24} \] Indeed each difference from \(f(k\delta)-f((k-1)\delta)\) is \(O(\delta^2)\), and there are at most \(N/2\) intervals. Therefore \(W_t=W_t^{(0)}e^{f(t\delta)+O(1/N)} =N\sin(t\delta)+O(1)\) on this half. It also gives \(W_t=N\sin(t\delta)(1+O(1/t))\) for \(t\ge1\). The exact reflection identity is \[ W_tW_{d-t}=N^2\sin^2((t+\tfrac12)\delta). \tag{25} \] It follows by reversing the full sine products in (12). For \(s=d-t\ge1\), insert the preceding lower-half estimate for \(W_s\). The relative error \(O(1/s)\) contributes only \(O(1)\), since \(\sin((s+\tfrac12)\delta)/\sin(s\delta)\) is bounded. Use also \[ \sin^2((s+\tfrac12)\delta) -\sin(s\delta)\sin((s+1)\delta)=\sin^2\theta . \tag{26} \] This proves the first estimate in (22) on the upper half as well. For \(s=0\), (18) gives the required \(O(1)\) endpoint bound directly. For the difference estimate use the exact formula, \(x=t\delta\), \[ W_t-W_{t-1} =W_t\,\frac{\sin\theta\,\sin(2x-\theta)}{\sin^2x}. \tag{27} \] Substitute the first estimate of (22). Its main term is \(\pi\cos x+O(1/(N\sin x))\), since \(N\sin\delta=\pi+O(N^{-2})\). The \(O(1)\) remainder contributes \(O((N\sin x)^{-1}+(N\sin x)^{-2})\), using \(|\sin(2x-\theta)|\le2\sin x+\sin\theta\). Finally \(N\sin(t\delta)\ge c_0\min(t,N-t)\), proving (22). Abel summation, \(W_d=O(1)\), and the summable error in (22) yield \[ H_l=E_lW_l+\frac\pi2\sum_{t=l+1}^d(A_t+B_t)+O(\log N), \quad A_t=e^{2\pi it^2/N},\quad B_t=e^{2\pi i(t^2-t)/N}. \tag{28} \] Indeed \(E_t\cos(t\delta)=(A_t+B_t)/2\). The constant in this error is universal, including \(l=0,d\). ## 5. Quadratic sums with their exact common phase We need two elementary facts: \[ \sup_{a\le b}\left|\sum_{t=a}^b A_t\right| +\sup_{a\le b}\left|\sum_{t=a}^b B_t\right|\le C\sqrt N, \qquad 0\le a\le b<N, \tag{29} \] and \[ \sum_{t=0}^{N-1}A_t+\sqrt q\sum_{t=0}^{N-1}B_t =(1+i)\sqrt N . \tag{30} \] We include the phase proof because a modulus estimate alone is insufficient. For (29), the consecutive phase increments are \(2\pi(2t+1)/N\) and \(4\pi t/N\), respectively. Remove intervals of \(O(\sqrt N)\) indices around their at most three aliases \(0,2\pi,4\pi\). Their contribution is \(O(\sqrt N)\). The remaining \(O(1)\) intervals have monotone phase increments modulo \(2\pi\), at distance at least \(c_0/\sqrt N\) from \(2\pi\mathbb Z\). For \(z_t=e^{i\phi_t}\), write \[ z_t=d_t(z_t-z_{t+1}),\qquad d_t=(1-e^{i(\phi_{t+1}-\phi_t)})^{-1} =\tfrac12+\tfrac i2\cot((\phi_{t+1}-\phi_t)/2). \tag{31} \] On each such interval \(\sup|d_t|+\operatorname{Var}(d_t)\le C\sqrt N\). Summation by parts proves (29), for every truncated subinterval too. This argument has no logarithmic loss. To prove (30), first set \(G(M)=\sum_{n=0}^{M-1}e^{2\pi in^2/M}\), \(M=4N\). For \(\epsilon>0\), group the absolutely convergent sum \[ S_\epsilon=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z} e^{-(\epsilon-2\pi i/M)n^2},\qquad \lim_{\epsilon\downarrow0}\sqrt\epsilon\,S_\epsilon =\frac{\sqrt\pi}{M}\,G(M). \tag{32} \] The asymptotic follows separately on each residue class modulo \(M\) from the ordinary Gaussian Riemann sum. Gaussian Fourier transformation and periodization give, exactly, \[ S_\epsilon= \sqrt{\frac{\pi}{\epsilon-2\pi i/M}}\, \sum_{k\in\mathbb Z} \exp\!\left(-\frac{\pi^2k^2}{\epsilon-2\pi i/M}\right). \tag{33} \] All square roots are continued from the right half-plane. This identity follows by integrating the Gaussian Fourier transform and summing its absolutely convergent Fourier series; it first holds for positive real Gaussian parameter and then by analyticity for positive real part. Put \(a=2\pi/M\). The exponent in the last sum is \[ -b_\epsilon k^2-i\pi Mk^2/2+i c_\epsilon k^2,\qquad b_\epsilon=\frac{\pi^2\epsilon}{\epsilon^2+a^2} \sim M^2\epsilon/4,\quad c_\epsilon=\frac{\pi^2\epsilon^2}{a(\epsilon^2+a^2)} =O_M(\epsilon^2). \tag{34} \] The middle exponential is one because \(M\) is divisible by four. Replacing \(e^{ic_\epsilon k^2}\) by one costs at most \(O_M(\epsilon^2\sum k^2e^{-b_\epsilon k^2})=O_M(\sqrt\epsilon)\). The remaining sum is asymptotic to \(2\sqrt\pi/(M\sqrt\epsilon)\), and the prefactor tends to \((1+i)\sqrt M/2\). Comparison with (32) proves the exact phase \[ G(4N)=(1+i)\sqrt{4N}. \tag{35} \] Here \(N\) was fixed during the auxiliary \(\epsilon\) limit, so no uniform regularization error has been assumed. The even terms of \(G(4N)\) equal twice the full \(A\) sum. The odd terms equal twice \(\sqrt q\) times the full \(B\) sum (replace \(t\) by \(-t\) in the odd quadratic). This proves (30). Finally difference orthogonality gives \[ \left|\sum_{t=0}^{N-1}B_t\right|^2 =N\sum_{\substack{0\le h<N\\2h=0\ {\rm mod}\ N}} e^{2\pi i(h^2-h)/N}\le2N . \tag{36} \] The expression is real and nonnegative before the last bound. Since \(1-\sqrt q=O(N^{-1})\), (30),(36) imply the parity-free formula \[ \sum_{t=0}^{N-1}(A_t+B_t) =(1+i)\sqrt N+O(N^{-1/2}). \tag{37} \] These are the classical Gaussian-Poisson mechanisms, with the exact normalization needed here; see the primary coverage in [DLMF 20.11(i)](https://dlmf.nist.gov/20.11#i). ## 6. The endpoint symbol is uniformly positive Equations (28),(29) first show, uniformly in every label, \[ H_l=E_lW_l+O(\sqrt N). \tag{38} \] For \(l\) in a bounded square-root layer put \(a=l/\sqrt N\). For each fixed \(A>0\), ordinary Riemann sums give, uniformly for \(0\le a\le A\), \[ \frac1{\sqrt N}\sum_{t=0}^l(A_t+B_t) =2\int_0^a e^{2\pi ix^2}\,dx+O_A(N^{-1/2}). \tag{39} \] The derivative of the fixed-interval integrand is bounded. Also \(B_t/A_t=e^{-2\pi it/N}=1+O_A(N^{-1/2})\) on this range, whose accumulated normalized error is \(O_A(N^{-1/2})\). Together with (22),(28),(37), this proves \[ \frac{H_l}{\sqrt N} =\pi\left[ a e^{2\pi ia^2}+C_F+I(a)\right] +O_A\!\left(\frac{\log N}{\sqrt N}\right), \quad C_F=\frac{1+i}{4},\quad I(a)=\int_a^\infty e^{2\pi ix^2}\,dx . \tag{40} \] The Fresnel integral has its usual improper meaning. Its value \(I(0)=C_F\) follows by letting the positive real part of the Gaussian parameter tend to zero. Integration by parts controls the improper tail in that limit. Definitions and the classical values are recorded in [DLMF 7.2(iii)](https://dlmf.nist.gov/7.2#iii). The real symbol after the actual phase is removed is \[ \mathcal F(a)= a+\operatorname{Re}(e^{-2\pi ia^2}C_F) +\operatorname{Re}(e^{-2\pi ia^2}I(a)). \tag{41} \] It obeys the explicit lower bound \[ \mathcal F(a)\ge \frac{2-\sqrt2}{6}(1+a)>0 \qquad(a\ge0). \tag{42} \] Here is a direct proof of the sign, including the oscillatory tail. Rotation along a quadrant centered at \(a\) gives \[ e^{-2\pi ia^2}I(a) =i\int_0^\infty e^{-4\pi ay}e^{-2\pi iy^2}\,dy . \tag{43} \] For \(a>0\) the vertical integral is absolutely convergent; the connecting quarter-circle tends to zero, since its magnitude is \(\exp[-4\pi aR\sin u-2\pi R^2\sin2u]\). At \(a=0\) use the improper limit, or the same endpoint arc estimate. Consequently the last real term of (41) is \[ T(a)=\int_0^\infty e^{-4\pi ay}\sin(2\pi y^2)\,dy>0 . \tag{44} \] Indeed \(u=2\pi y^2\) turns it into a positive constant times \(\int_0^\infty u^{-1/2}e^{-2\sqrt{2\pi}a\sqrt u}\sin u\,du\). The weight is strictly decreasing. Pairing successive positive and negative half-periods gives a strictly positive sum, with convergence by Dirichlet's test. This includes \(a=0\), where the value is \(1/4\). For \(0\le a\le1/2\), \(\operatorname{Re}(e^{-2\pi ia^2}C_F) =(\cos(2\pi a^2)+\sin(2\pi a^2))/4\ge1/4\). For \(a\ge1/2\), its absolute value is at most \(\sqrt2/4\). Thus \(\mathcal F(a)\ge a+1/4\) on the first range and \(\mathcal F(a)\ge a-\sqrt2/4\) on the second. These two inequalities imply (42). Since \(E_l=e^{2\pi ia^2}(1+O_A(N^{-1/2}))\), (40) gives \[ \frac{\operatorname{Re}(\overline{E_l}H_l)}{\sqrt N} =\pi\mathcal F(a) +O_A\!\left(\frac{\log N}{\sqrt N}\right). \tag{45} \] The error is uniform on every fixed compact \(a\)-interval. This uniformity, rather than a pointwise endpoint limit, is used next. ## 7. Joining the ranges and the bulk amplitude For \(1\le l\le m\), the lower-half proof of (22) also gives \(W_l\ge c_1l\), with a universal \(c_1>0\). Choose a fixed \(A\) larger than twice the constant in (38) divided by \(c_1\). Then (38) implies \[ \operatorname{Re}(\overline{E_l}H_l)\ge c_2\sqrt N \qquad(A\sqrt N\le l\le m). \tag{46} \] On \(0\le l\le A\sqrt N\), (42),(45) give the same lower bound for all sufficiently large \(N\), uniformly in \(l\). This includes \(l=0\). The threshold depends only on the fixed universal \(A\); it is independent of the selected channel. Thus the entire left half has a positive lower bound \(c_2\sqrt N\) eventually. The exact right-half estimate (21) gives \(1/(4N^2)\). Use (12),(17) to obtain (8) at every label. The upper bound in (8) also follows directly from (6), since [N] gives \(\|r_l\|_2,\|s_l\|_2\le CN^2\). Multiplication by the exact nonzero factor (7) proves the stated original-boundary lower bound. No claim about \(\chi_N\) is needed. For (10), (22) gives \(W_l\ge c_\varepsilon N\) on the bulk, so (38) yields \(\overline{E_l}H_l/W_l=1+O_\varepsilon(N^{-1/2})\). But (11) gives the exact cancellation \[ |V_l|^2W_l= \frac1{\sin^2((l-\tfrac12)\delta)} . \tag{47} \] Equations (16),(47) prove (10). If \(l/N\to a\in(0,1)\), its limiting amplitude is \(1/(2\sin^2\pi a)\). With the auxiliary variable \(z=e^{2\pi ia}\) this is \(-2z/(1-z)^2\), which has no zero away from \(z=1\). This \(z\) is a height parameter, not a peripheral knot eigenvalue. The endpoint proof above handles the poles without extending a bulk relative error into either boundary layer. ## 8. An opposed normal equation in the original marked gauge Let \(J_l\) be the selected actual path operator of [N], and \[ T_l=J_l-\mu_*I,\qquad T_l^{\rm opp}=q\,\overline{T_l}=q\overline{J_l}-\mu_*I . \tag{48} \] The last equality uses \(q\overline{\mu_*}=\mu_*\). Thus the opposed operator has right kernel \(\mathbb C\bar s_l\) and left kernel \(\mathbb C\bar r_l\). The original observation is still \(r_l\), rather than its conjugate. The new scalar estimate supplies the explicit projector \[ \Pi_l^{\rm opp}=\frac{\bar s_l r_l}{\gamma_l},\qquad r_l\Pi_l^{\rm opp}=r_l,\quad T_l^{\rm opp}\Pi_l^{\rm opp}=0,\quad \|\Pi_l^{\rm opp}\|_2\le CN^7 . \tag{49} \] Its norm bound follows from (8) and the two mode norms. Equivalently the actual two-line overlap satisfies \[ \frac{|r_l\bar s_l|}{\|r_l\|_2\|s_l\|_2}\ge c_0N^{-7}. \tag{50} \] This is a statement about these specified source modes. Conjugating [N]'s raw normal gap gives \(\operatorname{dist}_2(w,\mathbb C\bar s_l) \le CN^{11}\|T_l^{\rm opp}w\|_2\). Apply \(I-\Pi_l^{\rm opp}\) after choosing a best approximation on that line. It follows that \[ \|(I-\Pi_l^{\rm opp})w\|_2\le CN^{18}\|T_l^{\rm opp}w\|_2, \qquad \|(I-\Pi_l^{\rm opp})w\|_{\rm ht} \le CN^{19}\|T_l^{\rm opp}w\|_{\rm ht}. \tag{51} \] The last height norm is exactly [H]'s real positive diagonal norm on the selected block. Its condition number is at most \(CN\); the comparison costs at most \(C\sqrt N\). For every compatible forcing \(\bar r_l f=0\), there is therefore a unique solution \[ T_l^{\rm opp}w=f,\qquad r_lw=0 , \tag{52} \] with the same polynomial bound. Existence follows by subtracting \(\Pi_l^{\rm opp}\) from any compatible solution supplied by the conjugated [N] construction; uniqueness follows from \(r_l\bar s_l=\gamma_l\ne0\). For a singleton the compatible forcing is zero. The projector in (49) is not asserted to commute with \(T_l^{\rm opp}\): the preserved row \(r_l\) differs from its left null row. ## 9. Source scope and coverage The new assertion is a signed scalar lower bound for the actual opposed marked modes, uniformly over all their height channels eventually, and the resulting local normal equation with the original marked gauge. Its bulk leading amplitude is explicit. The Gaussian, Wallis, Abel and Fresnel tools themselves are classical. The proofs above retain their phases and endpoint normalizations. The normal residual in (51) is transverse to a vector line. It is not a pair-Casimir derivative or a moving-level first normal. The full physical height frames retain those original normal channels. At larger fixed width the original earlier ordinary caps, their Kronecker constraints and their source factors remain exactly [C,H]'s. The factor \(\beta_N\) in (7), and any original \(\chi_N\), must be restored when reading (6) as a boundary coefficient. The row is observed at the literal marked boundary. As in [N], \(r_l=r_lP_l\) permits selecting its support only at that final observation. The path \(I_l\) is not declared invariant under an arbitrary preceding crossing word. Neither (8) nor (51) assigns nonnegative coefficients to an arbitrary coherent exterior. The remaining marked amplitude after general transport is not controlled by a normal residual alone. No geometric gluing cycle, original whole-knot lower bound or finite-exception volume theorem follows from this local estimate. ## Complete inputs and closest coverage | Label | Complete text | Lines | SHA256 | | --- | --- | ---: | --- | | N | [Marked boundary normal gap](research_coideal_marked_boundary_normal_gap.md) | 512 | bb9bd6d04480ae8733c0fd1c5901834bdf2ea3e8c7eb3617fb8eb58e66e57956 | | C | [Cap-straddling cumulative kernel](research_coideal_cap_straddling_cumulative_kernel.md) | 450 | 3ff48e5998f325e1391c088b688a01388f5b8e21d3c8ce53f9ed556e9b289c71 | | H | [Height pairing and original boundary](research_coideal_height_pairing_and_marked_boundary.md) | 543 | bed81fcb12b20d16d41c55b476b13d8d69b1fe79d0d0620c31230ba652b1d82f | | S | [Signed crossing and exact phases](research_coideal_crossing_signed_volume_chamber.md) | 634 | 7bf6fb943d2c8080875375c4529776159fc72fbde2e5d8a7d0742e0cbdb10fc0 | | K | [Continuant source kernel](research_coideal_continuant_source_kernel.md) | 365 | 3ea997e5258c9413fd7c771a6a1475b90b39bf731ac55c0902fd136943b26f44 | Only written mathematics, source reads and text/hash operations were used. Earlier final notes, the ledger and public manuscripts are unchanged.

title: Exact finite quadrature extends the signed coideal volume chamber
text:
# Exact finite quadrature extends the signed coideal volume chamber 24 November 2026. Research note. Written proof. The actual mixed coideal coefficient has an exact positive quadrature on a specified index parity. Its finite zero strings annihilate every sample outside the common negative gap. This replaces the global absolute-integral comparison in C by exact finite orthogonality. Consequently the signed coefficient has the sewn octahedral volume rate throughout the cooriented domain on that parity, including points outside C's discriminant chamber. The assertion concerns the full actual local coefficient, with its quadratic height phase and both neighboring metric weights. It does not place an arbitrary geometric character or original marked closing in the stated channels. ## 1. Exact source data and statement Use the complete physical conventions of C and T: \[ N\ge2,\quad d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\quad \delta=\pi/N,\quad \sqrt q=e^{\pi i/(2N)},\quad \kappa=e^{i\pi d^2/(2N)},\qquad F_a=\prod_{j=1}^a(1-Q^j),\quad F_0=1,\quad F_d=N. 	ag{1} \] Sort the simple coideal roots by \[ \lambda_r=2\sqrt q\cos\alpha_r,\qquad \alpha_r=(r+	frac12)\delta,\qquad 0\le r\le d. 	ag{2} \] The complete continuants and finite polynomials are \[ D_{-1}=0,\quad D_0=1,\qquad D_{a+1}(\lambda;\sigma) =(\lambda+qQ^a\sigma)D_a(\lambda;\sigma) -q(1-Q^a)^2D_{a-1}(\lambda;\sigma), \qquad \Phi_{rs}(z)=\sum_{a=0}^d  rac{D_a(\lambda_r;\lambda_s)}{F_a}z^a. 	ag{3} \] In particular all endpoint arrows and the original crossing scalar are fixed. For two pairs of indices write \[ \Sigma_N=\sum_{a=0}^d  rac{\overline{D_a(\lambda_{r_1};\lambda_{s_1})} D_a(\lambda_{r_2};\lambda_{s_2})}{|F_a|^2}. 	ag{4} \] Assume cross-coorientation and the following index parity: \[ r_i+s_j\le N-2\quad(1\le i,j\le2),\qquad R=\max(r_1,r_2),\quad S=\max(s_1,s_2),\qquad N+R+S\ \hbox{is even}. 	ag{5} \] Cross-coorientation is equivalently \(\cos\alpha_{r_i}+\cos\alpha_{s_j}>0\) for every pair. The parity in (5) depends on the selected indices as well as the level. Put \[ f_r=\exp\{i\delta r(r+1)/4\},\qquad \gamma_{rs}=e^{i\pi d/4}f_r/f_s , 	ag{6} \] and choose \(p\in\{0,1\}\) congruent to \(1-R\), equivalently to \(N+S-1\), modulo two. Define \[ M= rac{N-R-S}{2}\ge1,\qquad k_a=-N+S+1+2a\quad(0\le a<M). 	ag{7} \] **Positive quadrature theorem.** At every level and every quadruple satisfying (5), \[  oxed{\quad \Sigma_N=\overline{\gamma_{r_1s_1}}\gamma_{r_2s_2}J_N,\qquad J_N= rac1N\sum_{a=0}^{M-1} |\Phi_{r_1s_1}(q^{k_a})\Phi_{r_2s_2}(q^{k_a})|>0 . \quad} 	ag{8} \] No discriminant inequality is required. On compact subsets of the cross-cooriented domain the logarithmic rate of this positive sum is the sewn octahedral volume defined in Section 4, uniformly over the actual roots satisfying the parity. ## 2. The exact zero intervals on both parity grids We first record the finite product information with all endpoints. C's exact root calculation, equivalently T's finite product, gives two descending strings of raw zero indices, in units of \(\delta\): \[ N+s-1,\ N+s-3,\ldots;\qquad N-s-2,\ N-s-4,\ldots . 	ag{9} \] If \(N+r+s\) is even, their last included indices are respectively \(1-r,r+2\); if it is odd, these last indices are interchanged. Their counts are \((d+h)/2,(d-h)/2\), with \(h=s+r+1\) in the even case and \(h=s-r\) in the odd case. These are nonnegative integers. A string with count zero is empty; its putative upper endpoint is its lower endpoint minus two. For completeness, these strings follow from the roots of the two factors in T's degree-\(d\) product, or directly from \((1-\lambda z+qz^2)\Phi(z) =(1+q\sigma z+qQz^2)\Phi(Qz)\). Their first points are the roots of the numerator on the right, and successive roots advance by \(Q^{-1}\) until reaching a root of the factor on the left. The counts just given end at the two required left roots and total \(d\). The product has constant term one and satisfies this equation; successive coefficients through degree \(d\) are unique since \(1-Q^a
e0\) for \(0<a<N\). Thus it is the actual polynomial (3), not a limiting product. On a chosen grid \(k\equiv p\pmod2\), the zeros of \(\Phi_{rs}\) are exactly the step-two interval from \(L_r^p\) to \(U_s^p\), where \[ L_r^p=  egin{cases}1-r,&p\equiv1-r\pmod2,\ r+2,&	ext{otherwise},\end{cases} \qquad U_s^p=  egin{cases}N+s-1,&p\equiv N+s-1\pmod2,\ N-s-2,&	ext{otherwise}. \end{cases} 	ag{10} \] An interval is empty when its upper endpoint is its lower endpoint minus two. The complete roots on both grids lift to \([1-r,N+s-1]\), whose length is less than \(2N\) under (5). Hence no zero is lost or repeated by reduction modulo \(2N\). For the parity selected in Section 1, an \(R\)-polynomial supplies the left endpoint \(1-R\), and an \(S\)-polynomial supplies the right endpoint \(N+S-1\). These supplying intervals are nonempty: their endpoint differences are respectively at least \(2R-1\) and \(2S-1\), and are even integers, hence nonnegative. For any two selected intervals cross-coorientation also gives \(L_{r_i}^p\le r_i+2\le N-s_j\le U_{s_j}^p+2\). The two nonempty extreme intervals therefore overlap or are adjacent in the step-two grid. Their union, including any other selected interval, is exactly \[ \{k:\Phi_{r_1s_1}(q^k)\Phi_{r_2s_2}(q^k)=0,\ k\equiv p\} =[1-R,N+S-1]\cap(p+2\mathbb Z)\quad mod 2N. 	ag{11} \] It contains \((N+R+S)/2\) nodes. Its complement on the \(N\)-point grid is precisely (7), ending at \(k_{M-1}=-R-1\). All roots of both polynomials, on either parity grid, lie in the lifted interval used in (11). Therefore every surviving node lies in the common actual zero-free component \(((-N+S-1)\delta,(1-R)\delta)\). In particular the last node is not a zero: the next possible zero is \(1-R\), two grid units later. This endpoint fact matters when extending the phase from C's smaller safe interval. ## 3. Exact orthogonality removes every other sample Finite Parseval on either of the two grids gives directly \[ \Sigma_N= rac1N \sum_{\substack{k\equiv p\ (2)\ mod 2N}} \overline{\Phi_{r_1s_1}(q^k)}\Phi_{r_2s_2}(q^k). 	ag{12} \] Indeed the difference of two polynomial exponents lies in \([-d,d]\); its only multiple of \(N=d+1\) is zero. Thus (12) is an exact unitary finite Fourier identity, with no alias term or large-level approximation. Equation (11) annihilates every summand except the nodes (7). The phase at every remaining node is also exact. For a cooriented pair the raw root lifts \(\xi\) in Section 2 satisfy \[ \sum\xi=\pi d/2+ \delta\{s(s+1)-r(r+1)\}/2,\qquad \Phi_{rs}(e^{i\vartheta}) =\gamma_{rs}e^{id\vartheta/2} |\Phi_{rs}(e^{i\vartheta})| 	ag{13} \] on its negative zero-free component. To check the sign, each root factor has \(\vartheta-\xi\in(-2\pi,0)\), so its phase is \(+i e^{i(\vartheta-\xi)/2}\). The sum of the two arithmetic root strings is the first identity in (13); their product phase is \(i^d e^{-i\sum\xi/2}=\gamma_{rs}\). This proves the formula on C's safe interval and, since there is no intervening root, on the whole component used here. It includes both endpoint parities and \(N=2\). At a surviving node the factors \(e^{id\vartheta/2}\) cancel in the mixed product. Its phase is \(\overline{\gamma_{r_1s_1}}\gamma_{r_2s_2}\) and its magnitude is strictly positive. Substitution in (12) proves (8). Unwanted large peaks elsewhere on the circle have been removed by exact zero samples. We have not bounded them by the gap maximum or replaced the whole integral by its absolute value. ## 4. Uniform sewn-volume rate on the cooriented domain Write \(\alpha_i=\alpha_{r_i}\), \( eta_i=\alpha_{s_i}\), \(a_i=\cos\alpha_i\), \(b_i=\cos eta_i\), and put \[ A=a_1+a_2+b_1+b_2>0,\qquad x_*= rac{a_1a_2-b_1b_2}{A},\quad \Theta_*=\arccos x_*, \qquad \psi_i= rac{\pi-\alpha_i- eta_i}{2},\quad u_i= rac{\Theta_*-\alpha_i}{2}. 	ag{14} \] Let \(\Lambda(v)=-\int_0^v\log|2\sin t|\,dt\), extended as an odd, \(\pi\)-periodic function, and define \[ W_i(u)=2\{\Lambda u+\Lambda(\alpha_i+u) +\Lambda(\psi_i-u)+\Lambda(\psi_i+ eta_i-u)\}, \qquad V_{m sew}= rac{W_1(u_1)+W_2(u_2)}2. 	ag{15} \] Here and below compact uniformity means any compact subset of \(\{(\alpha_1, eta_1,\alpha_2, eta_2)\in[0,\pi]^4: \alpha_i+ eta_j<\pi\ 	ext{for all }i,j\}\). Only the actual root quadruples with parity (5) are being estimated. Set \(\Phi_i=\Phi_{r_i s_i}\) and use the rotated circle \(z=q^{-1/2}e^{it}\). T's uniform log-cell comparison supplies \[ E_i(t)= rac2\pi\left\{ -\Lambda rac{t+\alpha_i}2-\Lambda rac{t-\alpha_i}2 +\Lambda rac{t+\pi- eta_i}2 +\Lambda rac{t-\pi+ eta_i}2ight\}, \quad \log|\Phi_i(q^{-1/2}e^{it})|^2\le NE_i(t)+C\log N. 	ag{16} \] The estimate is two-sided on a fixed interior subarc of the common gap. It is global as an upper estimate, including at zeros. The exact finite arc has \(t+\delta\) in its last two primitive terms; the modulus of continuity of \(\Lambda\) makes this an \(O(\log N)\) error after multiplication by \(N\). Thus no action constant is discarded. Let \(E=E_1+E_2\), \(n(x)=(x-a_1)(x-a_2)\), \(b(x)=(x+b_1)(x+b_2)\). On \(I=(\max(-b_1,-b_2),\min(a_1,a_2))\), \[ n,b>0,\qquad n(x)-b(x)=A(x_*-x),\qquad  rac{d}{dx}\log rac{n(x)}{b(x)} =-\sum_{i=1}^2\left\{ rac1{a_i-x}+ rac1{x+b_i}ight\}<0, \qquad E'(t)= rac1\pi\log rac{n(\cos t)}{b(\cos t)} . 	ag{17} \] The endpoint signs put \(x_*\) strictly in \(I\). Consequently \(0<u_i<\psi_i\), and \(E\) has exactly one maximum on the closed common negative arc \([-\pi+\max eta_i,-\max\alpha_i]\), at \(-\Theta_*\). It is nondegenerate, uniformly on every specified compact subset. Integrating the log-sine primitive in (16) gives \(E(-\Theta_*)/2=V_{m sew}/\pi\). This argument uses no discriminant: it concerns the common gap, where both \(n\) and \(b\) are positive. The rotated surviving nodes are exactly \(t_a=k_a\delta+\delta/2\), ranging from \(-\pi+\alpha_S+\delta\) to \(-\alpha_R\) in steps \(2\delta\). They all lie in the closed common continuum arc. Thus (16)--(17) bound every summand of (8) by \(N^C\exp(NV_{m sew}/\pi)\). For large \(N\), some surviving node is within \(\delta\) of \(-\Theta_*\). On compact subsets this node is a fixed distance from the actual zero strings. The two-sided version of (16) and smoothness near the maximum bound its summand below by \(N^{-C}\exp(NV_{m sew}/\pi)\). Retaining that node and averaging at most \(N\) nodes proves \[ \log J_N= rac N\pi V_{m sew}+O_{\mathcal C}(\log N) 	ag{18} \] uniformly on every compact cooriented subset. Strict positivity in (8) itself holds at every allowed level, independently of the sufficiently-large-level restriction in (18). ## 5. The same genuinely sewn convex octahedron C's geometric construction needs cross-coorientation and \(x_*\in I\), which were proved without its discriminant condition. Here are the supporting-face checks so this extension does not assume that separate local volume maxima sew. Take four tetrahedra in cyclic order \(A_1,B_1,A_2,B_2\), with their angle triples \[ A_i=(u_i,\psi_i-u_i,\pi-\psi_i),\qquad B_i=(\alpha_i+u_i,\psi_i+ eta_i-u_i,\psi_i). 	ag{19} \] All angles are positive. Their common-edge angles sum to \(2\pi\). Put \[ z_i= rac{\sin u_i}{\sin(\psi_i-u_i)}e^{i(\pi-\psi_i)},\qquad w_i= rac{\sin(\alpha_i+u_i)}{\sin(\psi_i+ eta_i-u_i)}e^{i\psi_i}, \qquad ho_i=- rac{x_*-a_i}{x_*+b_i}>0. \quad z_iw_i=-ho_i,\qquad ho_1ho_2=1 . 	ag{20} \] The last equality is precisely \(n(x_*)=b(x_*)\). Thus the shapes close in modulus and argument. With poles \(0,\infty\), their equatorial vertices are \(1,z_1,-ho_1,-ho_1z_2\). Their argument increments are \(\pi-\psi_1,\psi_1,\pi-\psi_2,\psi_2\), all in \((0,\pi)\). They form a simple star-shaped quadrilateral. At the pole \(\infty\), its two interior-half link angles are \(\psi_i+\alpha_i\); the joins are \((\pi+ eta_1-\alpha_2)/2\) and \((\pi+ eta_2-\alpha_1)/2\). The join formula follows from \(u_1-u_2=(\alpha_2-\alpha_1)/2\). All four angles lie in \((0,\pi)\), so the quadrilateral is strictly convex and its four vertical side planes support. At zero use the Möbius map \(z\mapsto-1/z\). The reciprocal link has interior-half angles \(\psi_i+ eta_i\) and joins \((\pi+\alpha_1- eta_2)/2\), \((\pi+\alpha_2- eta_1)/2\), again in \((0,\pi)\). Its ordered arguments and these angles give the other four supporting planes. Hence the four positive tetrahedra fill the convex ideal octahedron bounded by all eight supporting faces. Their ordinary tetrahedral volumes sum to (15); the opposite \(\Lambda(\psi_i)\) terms cancel within each half. Thus the action in (18) is the volume of this one sewn octahedron. No independent maximization of the two halves was used. ## 6. Actual signed crossing coefficients and scope For an actual same-frame face let the input, output, external and deeper sorted indices be \(r,r',v,s\). Apply the theorem to \((r_1,s_1)=(r,v)\), \((r_2,s_2)=(r',s)\). When its cross-coorientation and index parity hold, C's exact inverse-row and central-coefficient identities give \[ B^+_{r',r}=(-1)^{r'}\sin\alpha_{r'}  rac{f_vf_s}{f_{r'}f_r}J_N,\qquad B^-_{r',r}=\overline{B^+_{r',r}} . 	ag{21} \] The scalar has not been discarded: \(\kappa q^{d/2}i^{-d}=1\) with the lift (1), since \(d+1=N\). C's separate symmetry in the two middle and two neighboring labels shows that both signs have this same positive amplitude. The sine factor and its inverse have polynomial size. Therefore both actual entries have rate (18). For clarity define \(
u=\lambda_v,\lambda=\lambda_r,\lambda'=\lambda_{r'}, \sigma=\lambda_s\), and \(h_N(\xi,\zeta)=\sum_{a=0}^d|D_a(\xi;\zeta)/F_a|^2\). In the complete nested physical joint Haar frame the additional positive normalization is exactly \[ \left[ rac{h_N(
u,\lambda')h_N(\lambda',\sigma)} {h_N(
u,\lambda)h_N(\lambda,\sigma)}ight]^{1/2}. 	ag{22} \] Both incident edges are retained. T's uniform two-label volume profile gives the same four-term volume correction as C(36). The removed-head tail-pair form is a different normalization. None of these full finite changes removes a Casimir normal channel. The other index parity is not settled by this argument. For the parity proved here no comparison with the whole absolute-circle integral is asserted outside C's original chamber. The theorem instead evaluates the signed coefficient by an exact positive sampled sum, even when additional absolute-value peaks occur away from its supporting samples. The original input, marked closing and external scalar \(\chi_N\) must still be retained in any assembled word. The argument does not show that all intermediate channels lie in this domain, that the resulting face phases align with those boundaries, or that an arbitrary coherent closed sum has a lower bound. No global cycle, new finite-exception theorem or knot-volume identity follows from the local result. Finite Fourier orthogonality and log-cell estimates are elementary or already available in T and C. The additional statement is the source-specific root-support identity (11), its exact positive quadrature, and the resulting removal of the discriminant restriction on the specified parity. ## Complete inputs and closest coverage | Label | Complete text | Lines | SHA256 | | --- | --- | ---: | --- | | C | [Signed coideal volume chamber](research_coideal_crossing_signed_volume_chamber.md) | 634 | 7bf6fb943d2c8080875375c4529776159fc72fbde2e5d8a7d0742e0cbdb10fc0 | | T | [Exact coideal crossing transport](research_coideal_crossing_orthogonality_transport.md) | 595 | 4555fecc6377077dbdc4cfb3afac50f09d180efc5659716bac8497319310114c | Only written mathematics, complete source reads and text/hash operations were used. Earlier final notes, public manuscripts and the ledger are unchanged.

title: Complete physical residue packets on compact positive contours
text: # Complete physical residue packets on compact positive contours Private written proof, 16 November 2026. The physical-row Jacobi formula already supplies an exact replacement for an independent first normal inside a subsequent original trace. Here its determinant form removes all apparent resolvent poles, and the all-row slit theorem bounds that replacement by the action of the original physical row. This gives a uniform estimate for complete physical residue packets of a fixed graph, including edges between frozen vertices and all mixed first normals. The result controls the local cost of crossing original grid poles on compact positive-angle contours. It does not construct the remaining joint contour, bound its untouched kernel factors, or change an ordinary free-boundary polynomial. ## 1. Original rows and the pole-free normal representative Let \(N\ge2\), and put \[ \theta=\pi/N,\quad D=N-1,\quad\eta=(-1)^D,\quad c(x)=2\cos((2x+1)\theta),\quad c_j=c(j),\quad s_x=2\sin(x\theta), \] \[ P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2,\qquad e_k(z)=\frac{\prod_{a<k}(c_a-z)}{\prod_{a=1}^k s_a^2}, \qquad K_N(z,w)=\sum_{k=0}^{D}e_k(z)e_k(w). \tag{1} \] All algebra operations and traces are the original ones, \(\phi_N(f)=\eta N^2[z^D]\operatorname{rem}_{P_N}f\). The distinct physical rows are \[ 0\le j\le J_N=\lfloor(N-1)/2\rfloor,\qquad F_j(w)=K_N(c_j,w). \tag{2} \] Only \(0\le j\le\lfloor(N-2)/2\rfloor\) have an independent first spectral normal. For those rows set \[ G_j(w)=\partial_zK_N(c_j,w),\qquad Q_0(w)=G_0(w). \tag{3} \] Use the original Jacobi coefficients \[ A(x)=\frac{s_{x+1}^4}{s_{2x+1}s_{2x+2}},\qquad C(x)=\frac{s_x^4}{s_{2x}s_{2x+1}},\qquad C(0)=0. \tag{4} \] For \(j\ge1\), let \(\mathcal J_j(\varepsilon)\) be the symmetric \(j\)-row matrix with diagonal \(c_0+A(r+\varepsilon)+C(r+\varepsilon)\) and off-diagonal \(-\sqrt{A(r+\varepsilon)C(r+1+\varepsilon)}\). The branches are the positive ones at \(\varepsilon=0\). Define the polynomials \[ F_j^{(\varepsilon)}(w)= \frac{\det(\mathcal J_j(\varepsilon)-wI)} {\prod_{r<j}A(r+\varepsilon)},\qquad R_j(w)=\left.\partial_\varepsilon F_j^{(\varepsilon)}(w)\right|_{\varepsilon=0}. \tag{5} \] Set \(R_0=0\). The exact ordinary range in (5) is the range in (2); no equation beyond the last ordinary row is imposed. At zero, (5) is the original \(F_j\). Write \(w(t)=-2\cos t\). The archived logarithmic-factorial representative of \(Q_0\) is \[ \widetilde Q_N(t)= -\frac{g_N'(D/2-t/(2\theta))-g_N'(0)} {2\theta\sin\theta},\qquad g_N'(z)=\frac{\pi}{N^2} \sum_{a=0}^{D}(z-a)\cot\frac{\pi(z-a)}N . \tag{6} \] The removable terms in the finite sum have their continuous values. This is even and holomorphic on \(|\Re t|<\pi+\theta\); it has exactly the values and required first spectral normals of \(Q_0(w(t))\). For each fixed height \(H\), \[ \sup_{|\Re t|\le\pi,\ |\Im t|\le H} |\widetilde Q_N(t)| \le C_H N^2(1+\log N). \tag{7} \] These are full-jet identities, not an off-grid approximation to the canonical polynomial \(Q_0\). For a double physical row define \[ \boxed{\quad \widehat G_j(t)= \frac{c'(0)F_j(w(t))\widetilde Q_N(t)+R_j(w(t))} {c'(j)},\qquad c'(j)=-4\theta\sin((2j+1)\theta). \quad} \tag{8} \] For \(j=0\), this gives \(\widehat G_0=\widetilde Q_N\). **Proposition 1.** Formula (8) is even and holomorphic on the whole strip \(|\Re t|<\pi+\theta\). It has no Jacobi resolvent poles. On the original window \(|\Re t|<\pi\), it descends to a holomorphic function \(\widehat G_j(w)\) on \(\Omega=\mathbb C\setminus[2,\infty)\), including \(w=-2\). At every physical second endpoint it has exactly the value and required first \(w\)-normal of \(G_j(w)\). Consequently \(G_j\) can be replaced by \(\widehat G_j\) inside every subsequent original trace in that endpoint, with arbitrary original spectators. Products preserve all mixed first normals under further original traces. No equality at an untraced complex endpoint is asserted. **Proof.** For \(j\ge1\), the exact Jacobi normal formula in the pinned source is \[ \begin{split} c'(j)G_j(w)={}&c'(0)F_j(w)Q_0(w)+R_j(w)\\ &+\frac{c'(0)P_N(w)}{N^2s_1^2} F_j(w)[(\mathcal J_j-wI)^{-1}]_{00}. \end{split} \tag{9} \] The last term is \(P_N\) times a polynomial cofactor. It has zero required jets at every second-endpoint double node, since \(P_N=P_N'=0\); at the odd simple node only its value is required and \(P_N=0\). The remaining endpoint term can be replaced by (6), with all its physical jets. At \(j=0\) the assertion is directly (6); this also covers the only double row when \(N=2\). This proves the exact jet assertion. Equation (5) makes \(R_j\) a polynomial without division by \(\det(\mathcal J_j-wI)\). Thus (8) is holomorphic on the asserted strip, even where the resolvent expression for \(R_j/F_j\) would have a pole. Evenness supplies holomorphic descent through \(t=0\), because \(w+2=t^2+O(t^4)\). The map \(t\mapsto-2\cos t\) from \(|\Re t|<\pi\), modulo \(t\mapsto-t\), parametrizes \(\Omega\); this proves the spectral assertion. The ordinary product rule proves every subsequent trace and mixed-normal statement. \(\square\) ## 2. Uniform slit bounds with the row's own action **Theorem 2.** Fix a compact \(\mathcal K\Subset\Omega\) and an integer \(k\ge0\). For all sufficiently large \(N\), uniformly in every eligible row and \(w\in\mathcal K\), \[ |\partial_w^k F_j(w)|\le C_k N^k|F_j(w)|,\qquad |\partial_w^k\widehat G_j(w)| \le C_k N^{6+k}(1+\log N)|F_j(w)|. \tag{10} \] The second inequality concerns the double-row range only. Every fixed derivative is an ordinary spectral derivative; in particular it remains meaningful at \(w=-2\). Define, on its original branch, \[ \Psi_x(w)=\int_0^x 2\operatorname{arsinh} \left(\frac{\sqrt{2-w}}2\cot(\pi s)\right)\,ds, \qquad 0\le x\le\tfrac12, \tag{11} \] where the square root has positive real part. For every \(\epsilon>0\), the right sides of (10) are bounded by \[ C_{\epsilon,k}N^{6+k}(1+\log N) \exp N\{\Re\Psi_{j/N}(w)+\epsilon\}. \tag{12} \] On compact subsets of \(\Re w<2\), the fixed exponential tolerance can instead be replaced by a fixed power of \(N\). **Proof.** The spectrum of \(\mathcal J_j\) lies in \((c_0,\infty)\), and \(c_0\to2\). On a slightly larger compact slit neighborhood of \(\mathcal K\), its distance from this ray is bounded below independently of \(N,j\). Hence the resolvent and every fixed \(w\)-derivative of it are uniformly bounded there. The source bounds \[ \|\mathcal J_j'\|\le6\pi N^3,\qquad |A'(r)/A(r)|\le4\pi,\qquad |c'(j)|\ge8\pi/N^2,\qquad |c'(0)/c'(j)|\le1 \tag{13} \] hold throughout the stated double-row range. Differentiating the determinant in (5) gives exactly \[ \frac{R_j(w)}{F_j(w)} =\operatorname{Tr}((\mathcal J_j-wI)^{-1}\mathcal J_j') -\sum_{r<j}A'(r)/A(r). \tag{14} \] This and every fixed spectral derivative are \(O_k(N^4)\). The spectral form of (7), with Cauchy on a larger compact slit neighborhood, bounds all fixed derivatives of \(\widetilde Q_N\) by \(O_k(N^2(1+\log N))\). Thus (8) divided by \(F_j\) has all these derivatives bounded by \(C_kN^6(1+\log N)\). The logarithmic determinant formula also gives \[ |\partial_w^\ell\log F_j(w)| \le(\ell-1)!\,j\,\operatorname{dist} (w,[c_0,\infty))^{-\ell}\quad(\ell\ge1). \tag{15} \] Differentiating the exponential of this logarithm proves the first inequality of (10), and the product rule proves the second. The zero row is handled directly by (7). The complete all-row slit theorem gives, uniformly in \(j\), \[ N^{-1}\log F_j(w)=\Psi_{j/N}(w)+o(1), \tag{16} \] with the logarithm positive-real normalized at \(w=-2\). Its stronger half-plane statement has error \(O(\log N)/N\). Combining these with (10) proves the remaining assertions. \(\square\) The original angular edge phase with one real angle can be calibrated directly from (11): \[ \psi(t,s)=\Psi_{(\pi-|s|)/(2\pi)}(-2\cos t), \qquad -\pi<s<\pi,\quad |\Re t|<\pi. \tag{17} \] It has \(\psi(t,\pi)=0\) by the limiting value \(x=0\). For \(s>0\), \[ \partial_s\psi(t,s)= -\pi^{-1}\operatorname{arsinh} \{\cos(t/2)\tan(s/2)\}. \tag{18} \] This is the original positive edge return, with its complete constant fixed by \(\Psi_{1/2}\). The expression extends evenly and analytically through \(s=0\). For two real arguments it is symmetric: apply the exact symmetry of \(K_N\), (16), and approximation by physical nodes on real compact sets. In an incident-edge expression with only one real endpoint, put that endpoint second in (17). At the positive physical angle \(\tau_j=\pi-(2j+1)\pi/N\), the exact relation is \[ \Psi_{j/N}(-2\cos t)=\psi(t,\tau_j+\pi/N). \tag{19} \] On any compact \(|\tau_j|\le\pi-\delta\), the difference between (19) and \(\psi(t,\tau_j)\) is \(O(N^{-1})\), uniformly on compact first-angle sets. At the odd simple node \(\tau_{J_N}=0\), the same statement holds for its value. Even without such a row buffer, the upper comparison \(\Re\Psi_{j/N}\le \Re\Psi_{(j+1/2)/N}\) follows because the integrand in (11) has positive real part. Thus using the actual physical angle introduces no larger upper action. Every compact family of original positive angles lies in the slit charts used here. Indeed positivity includes \(|\Re t|<\pi\). If \(-2\cos(s+ih)\) is real, then \(\sin s\,\sinh h=0\). When \(h=0\), its value is less than 2; otherwise \(s=0\), and its value is at most \(-2\). The value can therefore never belong to \([2,\infty)\). Compactness supplies a uniform slit distance. This argument does not impose a half-plane restriction on the positive family. For an edge with both endpoints physical, the separate all-color estimate from the pinned physical-pressure source is stronger than a fixed-slit continuation. Uniformly over the entire physical grids, including colors approaching \(2\), \[ \begin{split} K_N(c_j,c_k)&\le C N^a e^{N\psi(\tau_j,\tau_k)},\\ |\partial_zK_N(c_j,c_k)|&\le N^{11}K_N(c_j,c_k),\\ |\partial_z\partial_wK_N(c_j,c_k)| &\le (N^{16}+N^{22})K_N(c_j,c_k). \end{split} \tag{19a} \] Each derivative is asserted only at endpoints having that original first normal. The first-derivative bound also covers an odd simple node at the other endpoint. The value estimate follows from the zero-inclusive uniform real Newton entropy and the literal terminating support; its maximum is the original \(\psi\). Thus it has a polynomial prefactor even when both indices are \(o(N)\). The normal estimates are for the original full polynomials, including high Newton terms. They do not come from differentiating the terminating values. ## 3. Complete frozen-vertex residue packets Let \(\Gamma\) be a fixed finite loopless graph, with the original same-index edge \(K_N\) on every edge and a fixed signed integer crossing power at each traced vertex. Repeated edges cause no change. Choose a set \(S\) of traced vertices to freeze at one of the distinct physical spectral nodes for each vertex; different vertices may use the same node. No condition on the signs or nonvanishing of the powers is needed. For a double node define the original local trace functional \[ \mathcal R_{j,N}f =\eta\{(4-c_j^2)f'(c_j)-c_jf(c_j)\}. \tag{20} \] At the odd simple node define \(\mathcal R_{J_N,N}f=f(-2)\). Their sum is the original \(\phi_N\). In particular the simple node has one value and no independently prescribed spectral normal. Formula (20) includes the complete node, with its original normalization; when angular pole pairs are treated separately their original orientations and multiplicities are retained. Apply the product of (20) over \(S\) to the original source. Edges disjoint from \(S\), and every other factor independent of the frozen variables, remain outside this local operation. Let \(E_S\) denote the edges incident to \(S\). The resulting incident-edge packet is exactly \[ A_{S,N}(\mathbf w)= \left(\prod_{v\in S}\mathcal R_{j_v,N}^{(z_v)}\right) \left[\prod_{v\in S}R(z_v)^{n_v} \prod_{vw\in E_S}K_N(z_v,z_w)\right], \qquad z_v=w_v\quad(v\notin S). \tag{20a} \] The crossing powers in this formula retain their original value and first-normal data. Expanding (20a) is a finite sum of products of: * values and first or mixed first normals of \(K_N\) on edges with both endpoints in \(S\); * \(F_{j_v}(w)\) or \(G_{j_v}(w)\) on edges from \(v\in S\) to a remaining endpoint; * the original physical crossing values and first normals, and the coefficients in (20). This expansion is literal: each frozen variable is differentiated at most once, and an internal frozen edge can receive one derivative at each endpoint. **Theorem 3.** Allow every frozen vertex to use any physical node, with no angle buffer or index restriction. Suppose the remaining traced angles range over a fixed compact positive-angle family. On every edge from \(S\) to a remaining traced endpoint, replace \(G_j\) by (8), leaving \(F_j\) unchanged. Denote the resulting incident packet by \(\widehat A_{S,N}\). This packet has exactly the original full mixed physical data in every remaining traced variable. Its product with the untouched remainder has the same value under all remaining original traces, coefficientwise in any retained free boundary polynomial. Let \(t_v\) be the actual real physical angle at \(v\in S\) and the retained complex angle otherwise. For every \(\epsilon>0\) and every fixed multi-index \(\beta\) in the remaining spectral variables, there are \(C,M\) such that \[ |\partial_{\mathbf w}^{\beta}\widehat A_{S,N}| \le C N^M \exp N\left\{ \sum_{vw\in E_S}\Re\psi(t_v,t_w)+\epsilon \right\}. \tag{21} \] Only the incident-edge packet is bounded in (21). Untouched edge kernels and their original remaining currents are not included in this estimate. If their own bounds are available, (21) can be multiplied with them without altering the incident-edge action. If all remaining spectral arguments lie in a compact subset of \(\Re w<2\), the fixed tolerance in (21) can instead be replaced by an additional polynomial factor. If an incident endpoint is genuinely free and untraced, its \(G_j\) is not replaced. Keep that exact ordinary free-boundary factor in the packet. The corresponding bound contains its actual norm and derivatives as an additional supplied factor instead of an asserted \(\psi\)-bound. The same convention applies to additional spectators whose source-specific norms have not been proved. **Proof.** Proposition 1 applies at every remaining traced endpoint before it is contracted. Its product assertion retains all mixed normals, including when several frozen vertices meet the same remaining vertex. It is immaterial that the physical colors at different vertices coincide. The product rule gives the exact statement with all untouched spectators and free boundary parameters. For a frozen internal edge, use (19a) for its value and each possible first or mixed first normal. This retains the original ordinary derivatives at both endpoints uniformly even when either spectral argument tends to \(2\); no fixed slit distance is claimed there. Equivalently, Proposition 1 identifies a first normal with \(\widehat G_j(c_k)\) and a mixed normal with \(\partial_w\widehat G_j(c_k)\), but the uniform bound at these moving real arguments is supplied by (19a). If an endpoint is the odd simple node it is never differentiated, and (19a) includes its value contribution. Theorem 2 also applies to every edge going to a remaining traced endpoint and to its fixed derivatives, uniformly over every frozen row. Use the monotone upper comparison after (19) to replace its row profile by the action at the actual physical angle, without an endpoint error. Allocate a fixed small part of \(\epsilon\) to each edge in the finite graph. All crossing values have modulus one at physical nodes; their first normals are bounded by a fixed power of \(N\), for every fixed signed power, including zero. The factors in (20) are bounded. There are only finitely many product-rule terms, independently of \(N\). Multiplication proves (21). The stronger half-plane alternative follows from the last assertion of Theorem 2 and the polynomial bound (19a). The proof never replaces a factor at an untraced endpoint, which gives the last assertion. It also proves the corresponding estimate for fixed spectral derivatives near the odd simple endpoint by holomorphic spectral descent, rather than division by \(\sin t\). \(\square\) For a polynomially sized collection of crossed physical-node assignments, (21) bounds their sum by the supremum of the displayed action, with an additional polynomial factor. For example all assignments on a fixed frozen set have at most \(N^{|S|}\) members. Actual contour orientations, any different crossing multiplicities, and the untouched remaining integrals still belong to the original source. ## 4. Scope for contour transport This theorem removes a specific local obstacle: crossing an original physical pole does not force an additional exponential cost from the independent first normal once the other endpoint is subsequently traced on a compact positive contour. The bound keeps the physical angle of that pole rather than replacing it by the complete-end maximum. It is a relative-source assertion. The omitted term of (9) and the change \(Q_0\mapsto\widetilde Q_N\) are not discarded as separate functions on an arbitrary open current. Their full physical jets agree before the remaining original traces are represented by contours. Any later open contour decomposition must retain its own endpoints and seams. The logarithmic-factorial representative has poles outside the original angular window; this argument does not shift that window across them. No global deformation, rate for the untouched remaining kernel product, bound on its joint wire connectors, or nonzero scalar coefficient follows. In particular a geometric action decrease along a proposed flow and (21) still require a source-preserving construction of that flow and control of its complete remaining boundary. ## Direct sources The complete texts and their directly used implications were read at these versions: * [Physical Jacobi boundary](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_physical_jacobi_charge_boundary.md), SHA256 530425b0c4504f2512954438465deb6d9a6e322fa58c641b6c678161baae6583: the exact row and normal formulas, determinant normalization, source-preserving logarithmic-factorial replacement and its bounds. * [All-row slit theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_mixed_next_first_short_edge_slit_plane_bound.md), SHA256 efe1c1c89bb01f5a0aca9468917595926648780bca265f73000ede095f432e7b: uniform own-row logarithmic asymptotics, stronger half-plane error, normalization of the original edge phase and its slit branch. * [Physical normal lift](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_physical_normal_lift.md), SHA256 115c38aa6ce5e683f49f1f9be3a4cc6b2362e451307fe50e5f35c60db10a272d: the complete original residue trace, crossing normals and odd simple-node convention. * [Physical charge pressure](research_charged_source_physical_pressure.md), SHA256 1e127c0842c0d6d5727a517cc66c39e73baa2846848c284d257c1ebe49679091: equations (12) and (20), the uniform real two-row own-action upper estimate and complete first/mixed-normal bounds, including every physical endpoint regime. Only written proofs, source-text reads and file hashes were used. No mathematical program, numerical calculation, test or compilation was run. Frozen notes, manuscripts and public files were unchanged.

title: Fourier cancellation and a strict upper bound for the complete source
text:
# Fourier cancellation and a strict upper bound for the complete source Private written proof, 23 November 2026. The full vertex closing, including its first spectral normals, is a sampled total derivative. In its Gaussian Fourier representation the zero alias therefore cancels exactly. Away from explicitly retained angular cuts and coefficient-band boundaries, its positive Fourier energy is exponentially concentrated near nonzero integer aliases. Combining this dual estimate with the exact edge-source estimate gives a joint real localization of the original marked contraction. This is an upper bound for its complementary contribution, relative to the original incidence norm. No geometric lower bound or complex hyperbolic-cycle coefficient is inferred. ## 1. The original root functional and its canonical Riesz row Fix the quantum root throughout: \[ N\ge2,\quad d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\quad \eta=(-1)^d,\quad \kappa=q^{d^2/2},\quad C_{N,n}=q^{nd^2/4}. 	ag{1} \] Every fractional power means the displayed exponential. The signed integer \(n\) is fixed before the limit. Let \(\phi_N\) be the original full Frobenius functional on \(\mathbb C[X]/(2T_N(X/2)+2)\), and let \(R^n\) be the original crossing power with its scalar \(\kappa^n\) retained. Put \[ \psi_j=-\pi+(2j+1)\pi/N,\qquad G_{N,n}(\psi)=\exp(inN\psi^2/(4\pi)),\qquad 0\le j<N . 	ag{2} \] The actual full-Hermite data of \(R^n\) are those of \(C_{N,n}G_{N,n}(\psi)\) at \(X=-2\cos\psi_j\). The double nodes retain their first derivatives. At odd levels the simple node \(X=-2\), corresponding to \(\psi=0\), retains its value. These are the fixed-branch data in [S], equations (7)–(8). For every ordinary polynomial \(A\), the exact derivative sampling is \[ \phi_N(R^nA)= \eta C_{N,n}\sum_{j=0}^{N-1} \left.\partial_\psi \{\sin\psi\,G_{N,n}(\psi)A(-2\cos\psi)\} ight|_{\psi=\psi_j}. 	ag{3} \] For clarity, this also follows directly from [J], equation (12). Write \(w=-e^{i\psi}\), so \(w-w^{-1}=-2i\sin\psi\) and \(w\partial_w=-i\partial_\psi\). The fixed original Gaussian in [S] is \[ q^{-nd^2/4} \exp\{n(x-\pi i)^2/(2\hbar)\},\qquad x=i(\psi+\pi),\quad \hbar=2\pi i/N . \] Multiplication by \(\kappa^n\), followed by this substitution in [J], equation (12), gives (3). At an inversion pair (3) gives the original value-plus-normal residue. At the odd simple node its summand is exactly \(R^n(-2)A(-2)\). Thus no auxiliary normal has been added. Consider a vertex of valence \(h\ge1\). Before identifying its incidences, use Laurent variables \(z_i=e^{i	heta_i}\) and the canonical space \[ \mathcal V_{N,h}= \{f:	ext{separately even Laurent polynomials of band }[-d,d]\}. 	ag{4} \] The original vertex functional identifies all \(X_i=-z_i-z_i^{-1}\), multiplies by \(R^n\), and applies \(\phi_N\). It uses the whole product before reduction in the physical relation. Here is a convenient extension to individual Laurent monomials. For \(m=(m_1,\ldots,m_h)\), put \(s=\sum_i m_i\) and define \[ \lambda_{N,n,h}(m)= \eta C_{N,n}\sum_{j=0}^{N-1} \left.\partial_\psi \{\sin\psi\,G_{N,n}(\psi)e^{is\psi}\} ight|_{\psi_j}. 	ag{5} \] For a separately even polynomial this is exactly the prescribed functional, by (3). Let \(\Pi_{N,h}\) retain the band and average independently under \(m_i\mapsto-m_i\). Its canonical Hermitian Riesz row is \[ H_{N,n,h}=\Pi_{N,h}\overline{\lambda_{N,n,h}},\qquad \Lambda_{N,n,h}(f)=\langle H_{N,n,h},fangle . 	ag{6} \] The inner product is conjugate linear in its first argument. The evenization in (6) is a fixed average over \(2^h\) orientations. It does not identify a value-only quotient with the original algebra. On the band, \(|s|\le hd\). Differentiating (5) bounds each summand by \(C_{n,h}N\), hence \[ |\lambda_{N,n,h}(m)|\le C_{n,h}N^2,\qquad \|H_{N,n,h}\|_2^2\le C_{n,h}N^{h+4}. 	ag{7} \] This polynomial bound includes the complete original normal. ## 2. The real alias set and the quantitative statement Use the exact coefficient-space Gaussian frame of [A] and [E]. In \(h\) variables, with fixed width \(\sigma>0\), \[ (\mathcal F_N f)(	heta,\xi)= c_N^h\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z^h} f_m e^{-|m-N\xi|^2/(2\sigma N)}e^{im\cdot	heta}, \qquad c_N=(N/(\pi\sigma))^{1/4}. 	ag{8} \] Its measure is \(d
u=d\xi\,d	heta/(2\pi)^h\), and it is an exact isometry. The angles below use the principal interval \([-\pi,\pi)\); the cut is retained explicitly. For \(\epsilon\in\{\pm1\}^h\), put \[  egin{split} r_{n,h}(	heta,\xi)^2 =\min_\epsilon\inf_{\vartheta\in[-\pi,\pi]} \left\{ \sum_i|\epsilon_i	heta_i-\vartheta|^2+ \operatorname{dist}\left( \sum_i\epsilon_i\xi_i+ rac{n\vartheta}{2\pi}, \mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}ight)^2 ight\}. \end{split} 	ag{9} \] Thus its zero set is the oriented copy relation together with a nonzero integer alias. Both angle and momentum change sign under an incidence inversion. For \(0<\delta\le1/4\), retain the following regions: \[  egin{split} \mathcal C_\delta&=\{\min_i(\pi-|	heta_i|)\le\delta\}, &&	ext{angular-cut strips},\ \mathcal B_\delta&=\{\min_i igl||\xi_i|-1 igr|\le\delta\}, &&	ext{band-boundary strips},\ \mathcal L_{n,h,\delta} &=\{r_{n,h}\le\delta\}\cup\mathcal C_\delta \cup\mathcal B_\delta . \end{split} 	ag{10} \] The first set keeps the actual spectral-window endpoints. The second keeps truncation at the full physical coefficient band. **Theorem 1.** For every fixed \(n,h,\sigma\), there are \(C,A,c>0\) such that, at every level and \(0<\delta\le1/4\), \[  oxed{\quad \int_{\mathcal L_{n,h,\delta}^{\,c}} |\mathcal F_NH_{N,n,h}|^2\,d
u \le CN^A e^{-cN\delta^2}. \quad} 	ag{11} \] The constants may depend on \(n,h,\sigma\). Neither primality nor level parity is restricted. The cut strips in (10) are part of the assertion, rather than errors set equal to zero. ## 3. Known Gaussian sums and the exact zero-alias cancellation It suffices first to analyze the unaveraged row in (5). The elementary Gaussian Poisson formula is \[ \sum_{m\in\mathbb Z}e^{-(m-N\xi)^2/(2\sigma N)}e^{imu} =\sqrt{2\pi\sigma N}\sum_{l\in\mathbb Z} e^{-\sigma N(u-2\pi l)^2/2} e^{iN\xi(u-2\pi l)}. 	ag{12} \] It follows by taking the Fourier coefficients of the periodized Gaussian. Both sides and their fixed derivatives converge normally on compact real parameter sets. Only known Gaussian test functions are being transformed. Work first on \(|\xi_i|\le2\), outside the strips in (10). If some \(|\xi_i|\ge1+\delta\), the finite band is a distance at least \(N\delta\) from that Gaussian center. Cauchy--Schwarz and (7) give the required polynomial times \(e^{-cN\delta^2}\) bound. It remains to consider \(|\xi_i|\le1-\delta\) for every \(i\). Replacing the finite \(m_i\)-sum by the full lattice then has the same bound: every omitted \(m_i\) satisfies \(|m_i-N\xi_i|\ge N\delta\). The derivative in (5) adds only fixed polynomial factors in \(N,|m|,|j|\). Gaussian tail estimates absorb those factors. In (12), with \(u=	heta_i-\psi_j\), every \(l
e0\) is also exponentially small on the original \(j\)-range when \(\pi-|	heta_i|\ge\delta\). Indeed \[ |	heta_i-\psi_j-2\pi l|\ge\delta \quad(l
e0,\ 0\le j<N). 	ag{13} \] The sum over all these aliases and its derivative have a fixed polynomial cost. For the remaining \(l=0\) term put \[  egin{split}  ar	heta&=h^{-1}\sum_i	heta_i,\qquad S_	heta=\sum_i(	heta_i- ar	heta)^2,\ j_0&=N( ar	heta+\pi)/(2\pi)-1/2,\qquad  eta=\sum_i\xi_i+n ar	heta/(2\pi),\ a&=2\pi^2\sigma h+i\pi n,\qquad \Re a>0 . \end{split} 	ag{14} \] After the explicit constant of unit modulus \(\Gamma=\exp\{iN\sum_i\xi_i(	heta_i- ar	heta) -inN ar	heta^2/(4\pi)\}\) is removed, the function being differentiated is \[ \mathcal H(j)= e^{-\sigma NS_	heta/2} \sin\psi_j\, \exp\{-a(j-j_0)^2/N-2\pi i eta(j-j_0)\}. 	ag{15} \] Since every \(	heta_i\) is away from the cut, so is \( ar	heta\). Extending the \(j\)-sum from \(0,\ldots,N-1\) to the whole lattice changes the answer by at most \(CN^A e^{-cN\delta^2}\). This follows directly from its real Gaussian factor; its derivative has the same tail estimate. Crucially, the row is the derivative of the entire expression. After the estimated band, nonprincipal-lift and finite-window errors are removed, its remaining whole-lattice contribution is exactly, with the factors from (8) and (12), \[ \eta\overline{C_{N,n}}\Gamma rac{N}{2\pi} c_N^h(2\pi\sigma N)^{h/2} \sum_{j\in\mathbb Z}\mathcal H'(j). 	ag{16} \] The function \(\mathcal H\) is Schwartz on the real line. Poisson summation and integration by parts therefore give \[ \sum_{j\in\mathbb Z}\mathcal H'(j) =\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}2\pi i k\,\widehat{\mathcal H}(k) =\sum_{k
e0}2\pi i k\,\widehat{\mathcal H}(k). 	ag{17} \] The zero alias vanishes exactly. This uses the value term, the first normal and the derivative of the sine together. To bound the remaining terms, expand \(\sin\psi_j\) into its two exponentials. Their shifts of \( eta\) are exactly \(+1/N\) and \(-1/N\). The Gaussian Fourier integral, with the square root chosen continuously from positive real \(a\), is \[ \int_{\mathbb R}e^{-ax^2/N}e^{-2\pi i b x}\,dx =\sqrt{\pi N/a}\,e^{-\pi^2Nb^2/a}. 	ag{18} \] Here \(\Re(1/a)>0\). Since \( eta\) stays in a fixed bounded interval on the present \(\xi\)-box, (17)--(18) imply \[ \left|\sum_j\mathcal H'(j)ight| \le C N^{1/2}e^{-cNS_	heta} \exp\{-cN\operatorname{dist} ( eta,\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\})^2\}. 	ag{19} \] For example, use \((u\pm1/N)^2\ge u^2/2-N^{-2}\), and sum the remaining Gaussian tails with their factor \(|k|\). All constants are uniform in the real centers under consideration. The Gaussian in [S] must keep its actual logarithmic lift. At the sampled integers its phase can also be written with \(j(j+N+1)\), but this changes the interpolating function by \(e^{2\pi i n j}\). Its derivative then labels the zero alias incorrectly. The phase used in (15) comes from \(j(j+1)-Nj\), exactly as fixed in (2)--(3). ## 4. Completion of the dual estimate and a central gap For the chosen orientation, evaluating the infimum in (9) at \(\vartheta= ar	heta\) gives \[ r_{n,h}^2\le S_	heta+ \operatorname{dist}( eta,\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\})^2. 	ag{20} \] Thus (19) is exponentially small off \(\{r_{n,h}\le\delta\}\). The band and cut errors above have the same estimate. Evenization replaces \((	heta_i,\xi_i)\) by \((\epsilon_i	heta_i,\epsilon_i\xi_i)\) and averages finitely many terms. The definition (9) keeps all of them. Integration on \(|\xi_i|\le2\) costs only its fixed finite volume. Outside that box, angular Parseval and the original coefficient band give \[ \int_{\max_i|\xi_i|>2}|\mathcal F_NH_{N,n,h}|^2\,d
u \le Ce^{-cN}\|H_{N,n,h}\|_2^2 . 	ag{21} \] This is the same elementary Gaussian tail estimate as [E], equation (20). Equations (7) and (13)--(21) prove Theorem 1, including the regime where \(N\delta^2\) is bounded. There is a useful actual cancellation consequence. Choose \[ 0<r\le \min\{\pi/4,\,[4(h+|n|+1)]^{-1}\}. 	ag{22} \] On the central box \(|	heta_i|,|\xi_i|\le r\), every orientation has its mean angle in this interval and \(| eta|\le hr+|n|r/(2\pi)<1/2\). The proof above, with its cuts and band boundaries separated by fixed distances, gives \[ \int_{\substack{|	heta_i|\le r\|\xi_i|\le r}} |\mathcal F_NH_{N,n,h}|^2\,d
u \le CN^A e^{-cN}. 	ag{23} \] This is the closing's cancellation of the central zero-alias packet. It is not obtained by bounding its separate normal channels in absolute value. ## 5. Joint localization with the original edge source Use the root specialization of the original compiler [F] on a fixed finite graph. At vertex \(v\), keep its prescribed signed power \(R^{n_v}\) and all \(h_v\) incidence variables until the original identification and trace. Any isolated vertex contributes its unchanged scalar trace, of polynomial size; it may be factored out. Let \(\Lambda_N\) be the resulting original marked functional. The complete row on the remaining incidence space is the tensor product of (6), with its prescribed outside root scalars retained. Let \(F_N\) be the actual same-index source [E], equation (2), allowing arbitrary activity-independent coupled coefficients. Write \(p_{e,0}\) for the full real edge symbol [E], equation (4), including its prefactor. Set \[ \Omega_\delta= \{\max_e|p_{e,0}|<\delta\} \cap igcap_v\mathcal L_{n_v,h_v,\delta}. 	ag{24} \] The incidence Gaussian frame tensorizes. Theorem 1 and the polynomial row bounds therefore control its dual mass off any vertex region. The edge theorem [E], equation (5) controls the primal mass off the edge region. Applying Cauchy--Schwarz in the exact frame pairing proves \[  oxed{\quad |\Lambda_N(F_N)-\Lambda_N(Q_{\Omega_\delta}F_N)| \le C N^A e^{-cN\delta^2}\|F_N\|_2,\qquad Q_\Omega=\Pi_N\mathcal F_N^\dagger \mathbf1_\Omega\mathcal F_N\Pi_N . \quad} 	ag{25} \] Here \(\Pi_N\) is the full incidence band-and-even projection. Its row and input are both canonical, so \(\Lambda_N(Q_\Omega F_N)\) is exactly the restricted frame pairing. One uses the primal off-edge estimate on that part of the complement, and the dual off-vertex estimate on the rest. No cutoff is commuted through a vertex tensor or through the closing. The constants depend on the fixed graph, powers and Gaussian width, not on the coupled coefficient array. The original complete main-color root scalar has its compiler framing and reduced-cut factors unchanged. The assertion is at the fixed root; it does not infer a moving-meridian identity from activity-independent normal insertion weights. ## 6. A strict upper gap below the unfilled circle-graph rate There is a source-specific consequence beyond complementary-region localization. Use precisely the original root circle compiler [F], with at least one edge, all its vertex traces closed, and any fixed signed integer powers. There is no largeness or hyperbolicity assumption on those powers. Write \[  egin{gathered} I=[1/5,3/10],\qquad g(x)=2\int_0^x\log(\cot\pi t)\,dt,\quad 0\le x\le1/2,\ G_0=\max_{0\le x\le1/2}g(x)=g(1/4) = rac{2G_{\mathrm{Cat}}}{\pi},\qquad F_0=2|E|G_0= rac{4|E|G_{\mathrm{Cat}}}{\pi}. \end{gathered} 	ag{26} \] The endpoint integrals defining \(g\) are improper integrals. Here \(G_{\mathrm{Cat}}=\int_0^{\pi/4}\log(\cot u)\,du\) is Catalan's constant. The substitution \(u=\pi t\) gives the displayed value of \(G_0\); \(g'(x)=2\log(\cot\pi x)\) fixes its unique maximum. This is the original Newton entropy in [F]. Then there are \(C,A,\eta_*>0\), depending on the fixed compiler and powers, such that \[  oxed{\qquad |K_N|\le CN^A e^{N(F_0-\eta_*)}.\qquad} 	ag{27} \] The same estimate holds for the compiler scalar before its prescribed root framing phase. This is a strict gap from the unfilled circle envelope \(F_0\); it is not a comparison with the filled volume. Here is the full retained-source proof. In separate incidence variables let \[ f_N=\prod_{e}\sum_{k/N\in I}B_k(z_e)B_k(y_e),\qquad b_N=f_N(\mathbf1)>0 . 	ag{28} \] At the root the actual edge weights \(H_N/W_k\) and their scalar turn factors are one. The original powers remain in \(\Lambda_N\). The root specialization of [F] bounds the complete sum of all discarded index assignments by \(CN^A e^{N(F_0-\eta_0)}\), with its fixed \(\eta_0>0\). It is thus enough to prove (27) for \(\Lambda_N(f_N)\). The factor-pairing proof in [P] gives nonnegative Laurent coefficients for each \(B_k\), \(k/N\in I\), once \(N\) is sufficiently large. A negative cosine parameter is paired with a positive one before expanding; the paired quadratic Laurent product has positive coefficients. All remaining single parameters are nonnegative. In particular \(B_k/B_k(1)\) is the generating function of a symmetric probability measure. Its same proof gives \[  rac{B_k(e^t)}{B_k(1)}\le e^{4Nt^2},\quad |t|\le1/4, \qquad |B_k(e^{i	heta})| \le B_k(1)e^{-aN d_{\mathbb T}(	heta,0)^2} 	ag{29} \] with an absolute \(a>0\). The latter is [P]'s full-period raw angular bound. Positivity preserves both estimates under the retained edge sum and products. Consequently the coefficients \(f_{N,m}\) are nonnegative, \(\sum_m f_{N,m}=b_N\), and \[ |f_N(e^{i	heta})|\le b_N e^{-aN\sum_i	heta_i^2},\qquad \|f_N\|_2\le b_N,\qquad  rac{f_N(1,\ldots,e^t,\ldots,1)}{b_N}\le e^{4Nt^2}. 	ag{30} \] Every incidence belongs to exactly one edge factor; the last bound therefore holds separately in each coordinate, despite the shared index within an edge. We record both Fourier-energy marginals rather than infer them from a pointwise transform. If \(J=2|E|\) is the number of incidences, direct Gaussian integration in (8) gives exactly \[ \int_{\mathbb R^J}|\mathcal F_N f(	heta,\xi)|^2d\xi =e^{\Delta_	heta/(4\sigma N)} |f(e^{i	heta})|^2 . 	ag{31} \] Indeed the \(m,m'\) entry is multiplied by \(\exp(-|m-m'|^2/(4\sigma N))\). This is the positive periodic heat kernel. Convolving its Gaussian bound with (30) proves that, for every fixed \(r>0\), the Fourier energy where some \(|	heta_i|\ge r\) is at most \(CN^A e^{-cNr^2}b_N^2\). One may check the convolution by completing the square in each periodic Gaussian lift; all other lifts have the same tail bound. For the other marginal, positivity and the last bound of (30), with \(t=r/16\), give \[ \sum_{|m_i|\ge rN/2}f_{N,m} \le2e^{-Nr^2/64}b_N,\qquad 0<r\le1 . 	ag{32} \] The estimate is just \(\exp(-trN/2+4Nt^2)\) for each of the two tails. Split \(f_N\) into these high coefficients and their complement. The high part has coefficient norm at most the left side of (32). For the low part, angular Parseval in (8) leaves Gaussian centers \(|m_i|\le rN/2\); integration over \(|\xi_i|\ge r\) is exponentially small. The frame isometry bounds the high part without any change of metric. Union over the fixed incidences, and (31), therefore show \[ \int_{\{\max_i(|	heta_i|,|\xi_i|)>r\}} |\mathcal F_Nf_N|^2d
u \le CN^A e^{-cNr^2}b_N^2 . 	ag{33} \] Choose one positive-valence vertex and fix \(r\) as in (22) for its actual power. Such a vertex exists because \(E
e\varnothing\). The row on the whole graph is a tensor product. Its full norm is polynomial by (7), while its mass in the central box of all incidences is exponentially small by (23) at this one vertex. Use exact frame pairing and Cauchy--Schwarz on that box and its complement. Equation (30) controls the primal full norm; (33) controls its complementary norm. We obtain \[ |\Lambda_N(f_N)|\le CN^A e^{-c_*N}b_N \qquad(c_*>0). 	ag{34} \] No separate first-normal term was dropped: the dual estimate on the central box used their exact total derivative. Finally [F]'s uniform entropy comparison gives \(B_k(1)=\exp\{Ng(k/N)+O(\log N)\}\) on \(I\). The positive sum in (28) has an index within \(O(N^{-1})\) of the unique maximum \(1/4\). Thus \[ b_N=e^{NF_0+O(\log N)} . 	ag{35} \] Combine (34)--(35) with the original discarded-assignment bound, and take \(\eta_*=\min(c_*,\eta_0)>0\), decreasing it if needed to absorb fixed polynomial prefactors. The original external root framing has modulus one and is retained. This proves (27). Increasing \(C\) covers the finitely many small levels. The gap is not asserted uniform in unbounded powers or changing graphs. It proves neither nonvanishing of \(K_N\) nor the required filled-volume rate. It differs from the existing charge-increment norm, which has the unfilled rate, and from the prior braid crossing-count bound: the envelope here counts this compiler's circle edges. There is a useful uniform-rate consequence after fixing a short coordinate. Write \(V\) for the vertex set of this fixed compiler graph, choose a positive-valence vertex \(v_0\), and fix its signed integer power \(n_0\). Then there is \(\eta_{v_0,n_0}>0\), independent of every other fixed signed power, such that \[  oxed{\quad \sup_{\mathbf m\in\mathbb Z^{\,V\setminus\{v_0\}}} \limsup_{N	o\infty} rac1N \log|K_N(n_0,\mathbf m)| \le F_0-\eta_{v_0,n_0}. \quad} 	ag{36} \] Here \(\log0=-\infty\), and each completion \(\mathbf m\) is held fixed before \(N\) tends to infinity. Indeed choose \(r\) in (22) using only \(v_0,n_0\). The central dual exponent (23) then uses only that vertex. All other rows enter through (7), where their powers affect polynomial prefactors rather than exponential rates. The source concentration (29)--(33) contains no crossing power. The discarded-index loss \(\eta_0\) in [F] is also independent of the fixed powers. Thus the same positive loss can be used in (34) and (27) for every fixed completion. The prefactors and starting level may depend on that completion. Restricting the supremum to any additional fixed partial assignment preserves (36). The order of quantifiers is essential. Equation (36) does not interchange the supremum with the \(N\)-limit, permit powers that vary with \(N\), or give a uniform finite-level prefactor. Its reference rate is still the unfilled envelope \(F_0\), rather than the volume of a partially or completely filled hyperbolic manifold. ## 7. Scope and complete sources The nonzero alias is defined on the retained angular lift. It cannot be relabeled cyclically while discarding the cut currents. Equation (25) retains those strips, every physical coefficient and every first spectral normal. The permitted vertex regions depend on the actual signed powers; their zero alias is absent for every such power. This supplies a real joint complementary-region estimate for the original source. It does not identify its incidence energy with an ordinary-color Plancherel energy, compare the retained region with a complex Casson--Rivin chart, or prove a nonzero geometric contribution. The band and angular-cut regions in (10) require their own estimates if they are to be removed. No arbitrary short-component volume theorem or finite-exception theorem follows from (25). The following complete proof texts were read at matching pins: * [S], [Signed original Gaussian and its full Ward data](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_signed_gaussian_ward_endpoint_packet.md), 503 lines, SHA256 6bdced1b01917e41631386a24b337b60dfe5b04d35d70007cb56badc511a0191. * [J], [Original first-order jets and full closing](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_first_order_gaussian_jet_transport.md), 365 lines, SHA256 baf7987b6550df2ee7a11f5433b27b04938d1ca54697b129c42a955bd5ad3d10. * [F], papers/circle-tree-asymptotics/finite-bounds.tex, 227 lines, SHA256 e4cf66544703af6d9a78208deae971c4d9f4367ba4b2ad660694ee489ef67ea1. * [E], [Exponential actual edge-source bound](research_same_index_edge_exponential_characteristic_bound.md), 474 lines, SHA256 f349e8fa328b0acd4f3d4519eb2c074504e56d44d5f4d2ae643e4e9d87516d2e. * [A], [Exact incidence Gaussian frame and edge equation](research_same_index_edge_fourier_characteristic_bound.md), 302 lines, SHA256 2e5788e51a5586966b53f0eb5a864b83415c134a083de939fca141cc7ae434ee. * [P], papers/circle-tree-asymptotics/edge-packet.tex, 268 lines, SHA256 53eb6dbfbda3ca639db35911ed50947c29655840337f9d1f1ce909d435013dbb. Whole comparison texts were also retained at matching pins: [Full-period currents and charge convolution](research_full_period_current_charge_convolution.md), 596 lines, 3f74b9824ecbf0b71a79b17959c7208f650103f95932192cfba87c7a7aa05595; [Gaussian Newton frame and original operators](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_gaussian_frame_newton_transport.md), 335 lines, b6ed7fa19097323f76b0b22fb4fc7361b9d4e52c3f19d17c12d94c6fff623af9; [Gabor source sewing](research_finite_gabor_pointed_source_sewing.md), 455 lines, 8a954f9f2bec9e0fc8971b08ea0ca493f712d4e2ace6bb9fc2c1fcf705699c37; the [Charge-increment graph norm](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_charge_increment_graph_norm.md), 355 lines, 8636d7606113873e8fa3ed3512dcf22b3eb359efac6d1dce4499fc321f00100c; and [Complete-source real saddle exclusion](research_complete_source_real_saddle_exclusion.md), 528 lines, 9e15defd27cabf3425f11be830fc8d385948023c791fb3fb4e8d696ea2b13572. These already supply exact derivative sampling, current bookkeeping, positive frames and comparisons with other source envelopes. The added estimates are the exponentially localized dual row with its zero alias canceled before absolute values, the joint source bound (25), and the whole-scalar strict circle-envelope gap (27), including its anchored rate consequence (36). Only written mathematics and source-text/hash operations were used. No mathematical program, numerical experiment, test, build, git operation, or edit of an adopted source was performed. [S]: https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_signed_gaussian_ward_endpoint_packet.md [J]: https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_first_order_gaussian_jet_transport.md [E]: research_same_index_edge_exponential_characteristic_bound.md

title: The complete source has an exponentially small fixed-time observation
text:
# The complete source has an exponentially small fixed-time observation Research proof, 3 November 2026. Frozen manuscripts are unchanged. The positive crossing form can be tested on the specified complete-end source, rather than on an arbitrarily chosen vector. For every fixed positive crossing horizon, its observation energy is exponentially smaller than the squared norm of that source. The loss comes from an alternating physical-value observation. The complete source is concentrated near the complete color, but that concentration does not give a lower bound for this observation. Sections 1–4 give the upper bound for every fixed positive real crossing horizon. Sections 5–6 determine the nonzero leading term of the observation and its positive energy for every fixed real horizon at least three. These are statements about the specified complete source. The original signed internal-pair closure is a different bilinear observation. ## 1. The original source and its observation Let \(N=2m\) be even, and use the physical nodes and weights \[ c_a=2\cos((2a+1)\pi/N),\quad \sigma_a=2(-1)^a\sin((2a+1)\pi/N),\quad Q(z)=2T_m(z/2),\qquad 0\le a<m. 	ag{1} \] Thus \(\sigma_a=N/Q'(c_a)\). Write \[ 	au_a=\arccos(-c_a/2),\qquad T_a=N	au_a^2/(4\pi),\qquad F_a=\mathcal L_N(c_a), \quad \mathcal L_N(z)=\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}e_j(z)e_j(-2). 	ag{2} \] These are the actual complete-kernel values: \(F_a=K_N(c_a,-2)>0\). Define, for real \(s>2\), \[ (\mathcal O_tF)(s)= \sum_{a=0}^{m-1} rac{\sigma_a e^{itT_a}F_a}{s-c_a}. 	ag{3} \] The scalar crossing carrier has modulus one and cancels from this energy. The [exact Gramian theorem](research_trace_normal_defect_positive_form.md#6-exact-transport-through-ordinary-value-observations) gives \[ F^*H_{n,N}F=  rac{N}{2\pi}\int_0^n\int_2^\infty \operatorname{arcosh}(s/2)|(\mathcal O_tF)(s)|^2\,ds\,dt. 	ag{4} \] **Theorem 1.** Fix a real \(n>0\). There are \(\delta_n>0\), \(A<\infty\), and \(C<\infty\), independent of the even level, such that \[ |(\mathcal O_tF)(s)| \le  rac{CN^A}{s+1}e^{N(M_\infty-\delta_n)} \quad(0\le t\le n,\ s>2), \qquad M_\infty=4G/\pi. 	ag{5} \] Consequently, \[ 0< rac{F^*H_{n,N}F}{\|F\|_2^2} \le CN^A e^{-2\delta_nN},\qquad  rac{\|H_{n,N}F\|_2}{\|F\|_2} \le CN^A e^{-\delta_nN}, 	ag{6} \] after increasing the constants and polynomial powers. This is the original complete vector at every even level. No spectral projection or prepared component is assumed. ## 2. Two existing bounds for the complete factor Write \(L_N(	au)=\mathcal L_N(-2\cos	au)\). The complete edge packet and its ordinary real-period bound imply the following two estimates. There are \(r,c,C_1>0\) and polynomial factors such that \[ |L_N(a+ib)|\le CN^A e^{N(M_\infty-ca^2+C_1b^2)} \qquad(|a|,|b|\le r). 	ag{7} \] For every fixed \(b_0>0\), there is \(d(b_0)>0\) with \[ |L_N(	au)|\le CN^A e^{N(M_\infty-d(b_0))} \qquad b_0\le|	au|\le\pi. 	ag{8} \] For (7), use the [thin complete-kernel theorem](research_bare_kernel_thin_rectangle.md) and \(\psi(	au,0)=M_\infty-	au^2/(4\pi)+O(	au^4)\). The omitted original high indices have a smaller rate on a sufficiently small complex neighborhood, so the same estimate holds for the literal low polynomial \(L_N\).
