For (8), keep the thin theorem's fixed wire contour at the complete point. The [factorial angular-loss inequality](research_uniform_factorial_and_boundary_decay.md#4-decay-in-the-real-boundary-angle) adds a uniform loss \(c_2(1-\cos	au)\) to every retained contour piece. The original omitted low indices retain their strict gap, since their positive Fourier coefficients give \(|e_j(-2\cos	au)|\le e_j(-2)\) on the real period. These two bounds prove (8) directly for the low polynomial. They are also the thin-contour argument used to extend the [whole outside-period estimate](research_pair_free_boundary_kernel.md#7-whole-outside-period-decay-and-a-complex-strip) to zero selected charge; no application of that theorem's strictly positive compact domain at its excluded endpoint is needed. These arguments keep the full physical values. The same packet at the nearest physical angle \(\pi/N\) gives \[ \|F\|_2^2\ge c_0N^{-3}e^{2NM_\infty} 	ag{9} \] for all sufficiently large even levels. A single physical entry suffices for (9). ## 3. The exact simple-pole contour Choose a fixed \(b>0\), small enough that \[ 2b<r,\qquad  rac{2nb}{2\pi}< rac18. 	ag{10} \] Choose midpoint cuts \(b_N=2\pi k_N/N\) tending to \(b\). For all sufficiently large levels \(b/2<b_N<2b\). Let \(\mathcal R_N\) be the positively oriented rectangle with corners \(\pm b_N\pm ih\), where \(h>0\) is fixed and small. On its closure arrange \[ C_1h\le1/8,\qquad \Re\cos	au>1/2,\qquad h<r. 	ag{11} \] The part of (3) with \(	au_a<b_N\) has the exact contour representation \[  oxed{\quad (\mathcal O_tF)_{m in}(s) = rac{N}{4\pi i}\oint_{\partial\mathcal R_N}  rac{2\sin	au\,e^{itN	au^2/(4\pi)}L_N(	au)} {(s+2\cos	au)\,2(-1)^m\cos(N	au/2)}\,d	au . \quad} 	ag{12} \] Indeed \(Q(-2\cos	au)=2(-1)^m\cos(N	au/2)\). The substitution \(z=-2\cos	au\), with \(dz=2\sin	au\,d	au\), puts a simple pole at each of the two angles \(\pm	au_a\). Each residue is \(e^{itT_a}F_a/((s-c_a)Q'(c_a))\). The factor \(1/2\) in (12) compensates for these two copies. There is no pole at \(	au=0\), and the condition in (11) excludes a pole from \(s+2\cos	au\). This proves (12) directly at every level, including its sign. On the horizontal sides, \[ |\cos(N	au/2)|^{-1}\le C e^{-Nh/2}. 	ag{13} \] On a midpoint vertical side the same bound is \(|\cos(N(b_N+iv)/2)|^{-1}\le2e^{-N|v|/2}\). The crossing factor costs at most \(\exp(nN|a||v|/(2\pi))\), uniformly for \(0\le t\le n\). Also \(|s+2\cos	au|^{-1}\le(s+1)^{-1}\). On a horizontal side, (7), (10), and (11) bound the total rate by \(M_\infty-h/4\). On a vertical side they bound it by \[ M_\infty-cb^2/4-|v|/4. 	ag{14} \] The original sine factor, contour lengths, and prefactors cost only a polynomial. Thus the retained observation satisfies (5) with a loss at least \(\min(h/4,cb^2/4)\). For the omitted physical rows, use (8) with \(b_0=b/2\). The smallest distance of a node from 2 is \[ 2-c_0=4\sin^2(\pi/(2N))\ge4/N^2. 	ag{15} \] Consequently \(1/(s-c_a)\le N^2/(s+1)\), uniformly for \(s>2\). The weights satisfy \(|\sigma_a|\le2\), the crossing values have modulus one, and there are at most \(N\) rows. Hence the omitted observation also satisfies (5), with loss \(d(b/2)\). Take the smaller of these three positive losses. Finitely many small levels are absorbed in the constant. ## 4. Integration and the meaning of the loss The remaining majorant in \(s\) is integrable, with the exact value \[ \int_2^\infty rac{\operatorname{arcosh}(s/2)}{(s+1)^2}\,ds =\int_0^\infty rac{du}{2\cosh u+1} = rac{\pi}{3\sqrt3}. 	ag{16} \] The first equality follows by integration by parts and \(s=2\cosh u\); the second uses \(	anh(u/2)\). Substitute (5) in (4) and divide by (9) to obtain the first bound in (6). The exact entries of \(H_{n,N}\) also give \(\|H_{n,N}\|\le C_nN^3\): its diagonal is \(O(nN)\), the off-diagonal cardinal denominators have inverse at most polynomial size \(O(N^2)\), and there are \(O(N)\) entries in each row. Since \(H_{n,N}\) is positive, \(\|H_{n,N}F\|^2\le\|H_{n,N}\|F^*H_{n,N}F\). This proves the second bound in (6). Thus the actual complete source is an approximate null vector of the fixed-time positive observation, with an exponentially small relative defect. This does not assert invariance under the crossing unitaries themselves. Nor does it determine the smaller observation rate: (5) alone is only a strict upper bound below \(M_\infty\). ## 5. A nonzero half-charge observation Put \(\Psi(t)=\psi(t,0)\), on its original complete branch. Thus \[ \Psi(0)=M_\infty,\qquad \Psi'(t)=- rac1\pi\operatorname{asinh}(	an(t/2)),\qquad \Psi''(t)=- rac{\sec(t/2)}{2\pi}. 	ag{17} \] For a fixed real \(n\ge3\), let \(t_n=a_n-iH_n\) be the positive complete-end leaf with charge \(1/2\): \[ n t_n+2i\operatorname{asinh}(	an(t_n/2))=\pi. 	ag{18} \] The elementary continuation argument below constructs this solution uniquely; no asymptotic source coefficient is used in its definition. Define \[  egin{split} S_n(t)&=\Psi(t)+ rac{in t^2}{4\pi}- rac{it}{2},& \mathcal S_n&=S_n(t_n),& M_n&=\Re\mathcal S_n,\ A_n&=-S_n''(t_n) = rac{\sec(t_n/2)-in}{2\pi},& b_n(s)&= rac{\sqrt{2\pi}}{\pi i}  rac{\sin t_n\,a_e(t_n,0)} {(s+2\cos t_n)\sqrt{A_n}}. \end{split} 	ag{19} \] Here \(a_e\) is the original nonzero edge amplitude in the [free-boundary kernel theorem](research_pair_free_boundary_kernel.md#1-domain-and-statement). The square root of \(A_n\) has positive real part. **Theorem 2.** For every fixed real \(n\ge3\), uniformly for real \(s>2\), through the even levels, \[ (\mathcal O_nF)(s) =(-1)^{N/2}N^{-1}b_n(s)e^{N\mathcal S_n} (1+O(N^{-1})). 	ag{20} \] The coefficient never vanishes and satisfies \(c_n/(s+1)\le |b_n(s)|\le C_n/(s+1)\). The expansion is uniform also for real crossing times in a fixed neighborhood of \(n\), using the analytic continuation of (18). It includes all fixed parameter derivatives on smaller neighborhoods. In particular this is an asymptotic for the original alternating sum (3), not for a positive replacement. *Existence of the scalar saddle.* Set \(f_n(t)=nt+2i\operatorname{asinh}	an(t/2)\). On the rectangle \(0<a<\pi/3,\ 0<H<2/5\), \(\Re f'_n(t)=n-\Im\sec(t/2)>n\). Thus \(f_n\) is one-to-one there: integrate its derivative on the straight segment between any two points. The small-charge equation \(f_n(t)=2\pi\chi\) starts with \(t=2\pi\chi/(n+i)+O(\chi^3)\). It cannot reach \(a=0\) or \(H=0\) at positive charge: the imaginary equation would force the other coordinate to vanish as well. At \(a=\pi/3\), \(\Re f_n=na-2\Im r>\pi\). At \(H=2/5\), \(\Im f_n=-nH+2\Re r< -6/5+\log3<0\), because \(\Re r(a-iH)\le r(a)\le(\log3)/2\). These exclude every boundary for \(0<\chi\le1/2\). The nonzero derivative and compactness continue the initial solution through that whole interval. This proves existence and uniqueness, also for noninteger real \(n\ge3\). *Separation from the physical tails.* Write \(r(t)=\operatorname{asinh}(	an(t/2))=k+ig\). On the positive leaf, \(g<0\), \(k>0\). At charge \(\chi\in(0,1/2]\), the period relation \(g=na/2-\pi\chi\) gives \(0<a<2\pi\chi/n\). Furthermore \[ \partial_H\Re r(a-iH)=	frac12\Im\sec((a-iH)/2)<0. \] Consequently \[ H= rac{2k}{n} \le rac2n\operatorname{asinh}	an(\pi\chi/n) \le rac23\operatorname{asinh}	an(\pi\chi/3) \le rac{2\log3}{3}\chi. 	ag{21} \] The last inequality is the chord bound for the convex function \(\operatorname{asinh}	an x\) on \([0,\pi/6]\); its endpoint value is \((\log3)/2\). In particular \[ 0<a_n<\pi/3,\qquad 0<H_n<\log3/3<2/5. 	ag{22} \] At the stationary point the derivative of the real action with respect to charge is \(-H\). Integration of (21) gives \[ M_n>M_\infty- rac{\log3}{12}. 	ag{23} \] On the real interval, (17) gives \[ \Psi(\pi/2)\le M_\infty- rac{\pi}{16} <M_n- rac7{80}. 	ag{24} \] For the last strict inequality use \(\pi>3\) and \(\log3<6/5\). The local edge packet used in (19) is legitimate at \(t_n\). Indeed \(\Re r(a-iH)\le r(a)\le3a/4\) for \(0\le a\le\pi/3\), since \(r'(a)=\sec(a/2)/2<3/4\). Thus \(H_n\le a_n/2\). As \(\cosh(2/5)<6/5\), \[ \cosh H_n-1\le rac35H_n^2 \le rac3{20}a_n^2 <1-\cos a_n. 	ag{25} \] Here \(1-\cos a\ge a^2/3\) on \([0,\pi/3]\), for example by the Taylor bound \(1-\cos a\ge a^2/2-a^4/24\). Therefore \(|\cos(t_n/2)|<1\). The saddle lies strictly inside the free-boundary theorem's domain, with height less than \(2/5\). *The literal contour and its side terms.* Choose midpoint cuts \(T_N=2\pi k_N/N\) with \(|T_N-\pi/2|\le2\pi/N\). Use (12) on the rectangle with real ends \(\pm T_N\) and heights \(\pm H_n\). Its integrand is odd in the angular variable, so the upper horizontal integral equals the lower horizontal integral after reversing the parameter. They add. On the lower side, \[  rac1{2(-1)^{N/2}\cos(Nt/2)} = rac{(-1)^{N/2}e^{-iNt/2}}{1+e^{-iNt}}. 	ag{26} \] Thus the principal lower integral, including its exact scalar, is \[  rac{(-1)^{N/2}N}{\pi i} \int_{-T_N-iH_n}^{T_N-iH_n}  rac{\sin t\,L_N(t)e^{inNt^2/(4\pi)-iNt/2}} {(s+2\cos t)(1+e^{-iNt})}\,dt. 	ag{27} \] The denominator in (26) differs from one exponentially uniformly on this segment. The [complete-edge logarithmic theorem](research_internal_pair_complete_edge_gap.md#3-the-full-complete-end-kernel-at-both-parities) gives \(L_N(t)=\exp\{N\Psi(t)+O(\log N)\}\) on a neighborhood of \(\{|\Re t|\le\pi/2,\ |\Im t|\le2/5\}\). Reflection and conjugation give the negative-real and upper parts of this rectangle from the stated positive one. The small midpoint enlargement is contained in the same neighborhood for large \(N\). On each fixed-height line in this rectangle, \[  rac{d^2}{da^2}\Re S_n(a-iH_n) =- rac{\Re\sec((a-iH_n)/2)}{2\pi}<0. 	ag{28} \] The critical point \(a=a_n\) is therefore the unique strict maximum of the whole lower horizontal segment. All vertical sides retain their exact cosine denominator. At a midpoint its reciprocal is bounded by \(2e^{-N|h|/2}\). For the lower right side the resulting rate is \(\Re S_n(T_N-ih)\), \(0\le h\le H_n\), and \[ \partial_h\Re S_n(T_N-ih) =- rac{\Im r(T_N-ih)}{\pi} + rac{nT_N}{2\pi}- rac12>0 	ag{29} \] for all large \(N\). Its maximum is at \(h=H_n\), strictly below \(M_n\) by (28). On the lower left side, \(-\pi/2<\Im r(-T_N-ih)\le0\); the derivative is \(-\Im r/\pi-nT_N/(2\pi)-1/2<0\). Its maximum is \(\Psi(T_N)\), below \(M_n\) by (24). The upper sides have the same bounds by \(t\mapsto-t\). Every connector therefore has a fixed strict exponential gap. For completeness, the omitted physical rows require no off-grid approximation near \(t=\pi\). At \(w=-2\), the actual positive Jacobi ratios \(F_{a+1}(-2)/F_a(-2)>1\) show that the physical values \(F_a=L_N(	au_a)\) decrease as \(	au_a\) increases. The largest omitted value is bounded by a physical value at \(T_N+O(N^{-1})\), whose logarithmic rate is \(\Psi(\pi/2)\). The estimate (15) controls the denominator uniformly in \(s>2\). Hence the entire omitted physical sum has the same strict gap. Finally, \(\Re\cos t\) is bounded below by a fixed number greater than \(-1/2\) on these contours. Thus \(|s+2\cos t|^{-1}\le C/(s+1)\). All fixed angular derivatives obey the corresponding bound. Near \(t_n\) insert the actual edge expansion \(L_N=N^{-3/2}a_e(t,0)e^{N\Psi(t)}(1+O(N^{-1}))\) into (27). The ordinary complex Gaussian integral, with \(\Re A_n>0\), gives exactly (19)–(20). The sine, the edge amplitude, and \(A_n\) are all nonzero. The relative error is uniform for \(s>2\), since after multiplication by \(s+1\) the rational amplitude and its derivatives form a compact bounded family with nonzero leading value. All gaps persist on a small complex crossing-time neighborhood of \(n\), by continuity on the fixed contours. The finite observation and its normalized remainder are holomorphic there; Cauchy's formula supplies the asserted parameter derivatives on smaller neighborhoods. This proves the theorem. \(\square\) ## 6. The exact exponential rate of the positive energy **Corollary 3.** For each fixed real \(n\ge3\), \[ F^*H_{n,N}F =C_nN^{-2}e^{2NM_n}(1+O(N^{-1})),\qquad C_n= rac1{4\pi M'_n} \int_2^\infty\operatorname{arcosh}(s/2)|b_n(s)|^2\,ds>0, \quad M'_n= rac{a_nH_n}{2\pi}>0. 	ag{30} \] The derivative here is with respect to the real crossing time on the local continuation of (18). *Proof.* The stationary derivative gives \(\partial_n\mathcal S_n=it_n^2/(4\pi)\), hence the displayed formula for \(M'_n\). It remains to control the part of the time integral outside the neighborhood where (20) holds; positivity alone would not give its upper bound. Use the same rectangle of height \(H_n\) for every time \(0\le v\le n\). On its lower horizontal side the real rate is \[ R_v(a)=\Re\Psi(a-iH_n) + rac{v aH_n}{2\pi}- rac{H_n}{2}. 	ag{31} \] For \(a\ge0\), \(R_v(a)\le R_n(a)\); for \(a\le0\), \(R_v(a)\le R_n(-a)\). If \(v\le n-\epsilon\), equality with \(M_n\) is impossible: the only maximizer of \(R_n\) is \(a_n>0\), where a strict crossing-time loss remains. Compactness gives a uniform strict gap on this earlier time interval. The connectors are bounded by the same \(n\)-time right side or by the strictly smaller real endpoint rate. The original physical tails are independent of \(v\) in absolute value. Thus the earlier-time contribution is exponentially smaller, with the integrable majorant \(C/(s+1)^2\). Near \(v=n\), substitute the uniform expansion (20) into (4). Since \(M'_n>0\), the ordinary endpoint Laplace integral in \(v\) contributes \((2NM'_n)^{-1}\). The factors are \(N/(2\pi)\) from the Gramian, \(N^{-2}\) from the squared observation, and this endpoint factor. This proves (30), including its coefficient. The integral is finite by (16) and positive by the nonvanishing in Theorem 2. \(\square\) The positive form therefore measures a specific smaller action, the half-charge leaf action. It still does not identify the nonzero coefficient of the original same-sign internal pair: that closure uses the signed bilinear convolution, not the absolute square in (4). ## 7. Complex colors and the exact normal defect The interpolation formula also specifies which residue is added when the observation color enters the shifted contour. This distinction matters when the observation is subsequently used inside an original trace. Let \(\mathcal I_{n,N}\) be the polynomial of degree less than \(N/2\) interpolating \(\exp(inT_a)F_a\) at all the nodes \(c_a\). On the slit plane \(\mathbb C\setminus[2,\infty)\), put \[ h_{n,N}(w)= \exp\!\left( rac{inN\,\arccos(-w/2)^2}{4\pi}ight) \mathcal L_N(w),\qquad \mathscr D_{n,N}(w)=  rac{h_{n,N}(w)-\mathcal I_{n,N}(w)}{Q(w)}. 	ag{32} \] The square of the inverse cosine is holomorphic through \(w=-2\), on the branch fixed by the positive real angular interval. The numerator in \(\mathscr D\) vanishes at every root of \(Q\), so this function is holomorphic through all physical nodes. It satisfies exactly \[ \mathcal O_nF(w)=N rac{\mathcal I_{n,N}(w)}{Q(w)},\qquad h'_{n,N}(c_a)-(\mathcal I_{n,N})'(c_a) =Q'(c_a)\mathscr D_{n,N}(c_a). 	ag{33} \] Thus \(\mathscr D\) represents the full interpolation-normal defect in the original trace. The unit scalar crossing carrier, omitted from \(\mathcal O_n\), multiplies both sides when the original \(R^n\) is restored. Let \(\mathcal J_{n,N}(w)\) denote the contour integral on the right side of (12), with \(b_N=T_N\), \(h=H_n\), and \(s=w\). Let \(\mathcal T_{n,N}(w)\) be the original omitted physical sum with \(	au_a\ge T_N\). For \(w=-2\cos(a-iH)\), \(0<a<\pi/2\), \(H>0\), away from the contour, write \(
u_N(w)=1\) if \(a<T_N\) and \(H<H_n\), and zero otherwise. Then the exact identities are \[  egin{split} \mathcal J_{n,N}(w) &=\mathcal O_nF(w)-\mathcal T_{n,N}(w) -N
u_N(w) rac{h_{n,N}(w)}{Q(w)},\ \mathscr D_{n,N}(w) &=(1-
u_N(w)) rac{h_{n,N}(w)}{Q(w)} - rac{\mathcal J_{n,N}(w)+\mathcal T_{n,N}(w)}{N}. \end{split} 	ag{34} \] Indeed the extra two angular poles are at \(t=\pm(a-iH)\). Each has residue \(-h_{n,N}(w)/Q(w)\), because the factor \(2\sin t\) in (12) cancels the derivative of \(w+2\cos t\). Multiplication by \(N/(4\pi i)\) and the two residues gives exactly \(-Nh_{n,N}(w)/Q(w)\). This proves (34) with its sign and scalar. **Corollary 4.** Fix \(n\ge3\). On every compact set of colors \(w=-2\cos(a-iH)\) with \(0<a<\pi/2\) and \(H>H_n\), \[  egin{split}  rac{\mathcal I_{n,N}(w)}{Q(w)} &=(-1)^{N/2}N^{-2}b_n(w)e^{N\mathcal S_n} (1+O(N^{-1})),\ \mathscr D_{n,N}(w) &= rac{h_{n,N}(w)}{Q(w)} -(-1)^{N/2}N^{-2}b_n(w)e^{N\mathcal S_n} (1+O(N^{-1})). \end{split} 	ag{35} \] Here \(b_n(w)\) is the same rational function of the observation color as in (19). All fixed complex-color derivatives have the corresponding holomorphic expansions on smaller neighborhoods. *Proof.* Such a compact set is separated from the image of the rectangle boundary and from the real physical nodes. The proof of Theorem 2 therefore applies to \(\mathcal J_{n,N}(w)\), with bounded complex denominators and the same nonzero leading coefficient. The omitted physical sum has the rate in (24), uniformly on this compact set. Here \(
u_N=0\) for all large levels. Equations (33)–(34) give (35); Cauchy's formula gives the derivative statements. \(\square\) This corollary does not assume that the first term in the normal defect dominates the second. That comparison requires the actual observation color. Formula (34) also shows why one cannot analytically continue the exterior formula through the shifted contour without its extra residue. There is also an exact trace reduction that uses this same holomorphic defect. For \(0\le j<N/2\), set \[ S_{j,N}=\prod_{r=1}^j2\sin(r\pi/N),\qquad Q_{j,N}(z)=\prod_{a=j}^{N/2-1}(z-c_a),\qquad S_{0,N}=1. 	ag{36} \] Let \(\Gamma_j\) be any positively oriented contour in the slit plane enclosing precisely these remaining nodes. The original complete-source trace satisfies \[  oxed{\quad \phi_N[R^n\mathcal L_N e_j] = rac{\eta C_{N,n}N^2(-1)^j}{2\pi i S_{j,N}^2} \oint_{\Gamma_j}  rac{\mathscr D_{n,N}(z)}{Q_{j,N}(z)}\,dz . \quad} 	ag{37} \] Here \(C_{N,n}=\exp(\pi i n(N-1)^2/(4N))\) is the original scalar crossing carrier; \(R^n\) denotes the original Hermite crossing flow when \(n\) is noninteger. The [normal-defect trace identity](research_trace_normal_defect_positive_form.md#1-the-interpolation-identity-at-both-parities) gives its left side as \(\eta C_{N,n}\sum_a(4-c_a^2)Q'(c_a) \mathscr D_{n,N}(c_a)e_j(c_a)\). At even physical nodes \((4-c_a^2)Q'(c_a)^2=N^2\), whereas \[  rac{e_j(z)}{Q(z)} = rac{(-1)^j}{S_{j,N}^2Q_{j,N}(z)}. 	ag{38} \] The residue theorem proves (37). Every below-triangle first normal has been retained in \(\mathscr D\); there are no poles left at \(a<j\). In angular coordinates the remaining positive roots have \(0<	au_a\le\pi-(2j+1)\pi/N\). They lie precisely in the original regular factorial order for the shared index \(j\). This is an exact reduction of the signed source, rather than a bound on its absolute terms. A global estimate for the contour in (37) still has to retain both terms of (35). **Corollary 5.** Fix integer \(n,p\ge3\), and let \(t\) be the selected angle at the power-\(n\) vertex of their unit-charge complete-ended internal pair. On a fixed complex neighborhood of \(t\), through even levels, \[  egin{split} \mathscr D_{n,N}(-2\cos z) &= rac{h_{n,N}(-2\cos z)}{Q(-2\cos z)} (1+O(e^{-\delta N}))\ &=(-1)^{N/2}N^{-3/2}a_e(z,0)e^{NS_n(z)} (1+O(N^{-1})) \end{split} 	ag{39} \] for some \(\delta>0\). In particular this original normal defect is nonzero there for all large even levels. The same expansion holds with every fixed ordinary spectral derivative, in the usual differentiated holomorphic sense. *Proof.* The [pair-to-half-charge comparison](research_pair_half_charge_action_gap.md) proves both \(H(t)>H_n\) and \(\Re S_n(t)>M_n\), with a strict quantitative gap. Both inequalities persist on a fixed neighborhood. Corollary 4 applies there. Meanwhile (26) and the actual complete-edge packet give \[  rac{h_{n,N}(-2\cos z)}{Q(-2\cos z)} =(-1)^{N/2}N^{-3/2}a_e(z,0)e^{NS_n(z)} (1+O(N^{-1})). \] In (35) the interpolation correction is therefore exponentially smaller, including its polynomial prefactor. Cauchy's formula on smaller neighborhoods proves the same comparison for the normalized holomorphic remainders and all fixed derivatives. Since \(\sin t
e0\), passage from angular to ordinary spectral derivatives is legitimate. This proves (39). \(\square\) The local conclusion (39) and the exact global identity (37) serve different purposes. The former supplies an independently nonzero source near each geometric pair angle. The latter still requires control of the complete integration cycle before yielding a lower bound for the signed pair coefficient. ## 8. Reproduction The [focused checker](../experiments/check_complete_source_pick_observation.py) compares (12) directly with the original physical-value sum at complex contour points and checks (16). It checks the elementary rational comparisons used above and records direct original-sum comparisons with (20), including both signs of \((-1)^{N/2}\). The asymptotic ratios are finite diagnostics; the uniform statements are proved analytically above. ~~~sh python3 experiments/check_complete_source_pick_observation.py ~~~ Its [saved record](../repro/results/research-complete-source-pick-observation.json) contains the proof and input hashes.

title: The complete knot source has no regular real interior saddle
text: # The complete knot source has no regular real interior saddle Private written deduction, 15 November 2026. No mathematical code, numerical calculation, test, or saved numerical evidence is used. Frozen notes and public manuscripts are unchanged. The selected local clock amplitude does not initialize a positive real saddle of the complete closed source. For every nonempty braid whose closure is a knot, the full incidence action has no real interior stationary point, even after any integer Fourier character is retained. The same statement holds with the original cut degree fixed. This is an exact consequence of the source's clock equations and integral transfer lattice; it is not an abstract cancellation example. For alternating generator signs, the central incidence packet also has an actual midpoint-rectangle deformation with a strict exponential loss, including both cotangent lips. This local contour statement is recorded separately from the stronger scalar upper bound already available by cut peeling. The statement does not exclude a complex geometric saddle or a source-preserving deformation to it. It identifies where such a deformation must do more than multiply the positive local clock initializers. ## 1. The complete source and its real interior Use the physical sign convention of the [joint clock phase](research_joint_clock_phase_equations.md). At crossing \(j\), let its sign be \(\sigma_j\), its adjacent head index be \(i_j\), and its normalized physical coordinates be \(U_j,V_j,J_j\). The overstrand goes from \(U_j+V_j\) to \(V_j\), and the understrand goes from \(J_j\) to \(J_j+U_j\). The clock is \(H_j\). Its four normalized incidences are \[ (1-U_j-V_j,\ U_j-H_j+V_j,\ H_j-V_j,\ V_j). \tag{1} \] The closing row on head \(i\) is \((1-A_i,A_i)\). All wire conservation and the original closing equations remain imposed. The real regular interior means all incidences in (1) and all closing incidences are positive. In this interior every physical head degree lies strictly between zero and one. To check the under degrees as well as the over degrees, follow a segment from one over-output or closing event to the next over-input or closing event. Its intermediate under degrees increase by the positive transfers \(U_j\). Both endpoint degrees lie in \((0,1)\), hence so do the intermediate ones. In particular \[ 0<U_j<1,\qquad 0<J_j<J_j+U_j<1 . \tag{2} \] Let \[ \mathcal J(x)=\int_0^x\Log(2\sin\pi t)\,dt \tag{3} \] with its branch real on \((0,1)\). The complete leading action on the specified source lift is \[ \begin{split} \mathscr S&=-\sum_{\text{all incidences }e}\mathcal J(x_e) +\pi i\,\varphi,\\ \varphi&=\sum_j \{H_j+\sigma_jH_j(U_j+2J_j)-\sigma_jJ_j\}. \end{split} \tag{4} \] This follows from the full phase (3) of the [integral midpoint theorem](research_incidence_burau_gauss_reduction.md). The exact \(N-1\) shifts and the closing pivots contribute the already specified finite amplitudes; none changes (4). The closing rows have zero entropy by \(\mathcal J(1-A)=-\mathcal J(A)\). Let \(L\) be the homogeneous integral incidence lattice. As in the source, it is the direct sum of the closed physical-flow lattice and the independent integral clock coordinates. A real point is stationary in some integer Fourier lift only if \[ D_\ell\mathscr S\in2\pi i\mathbb Z \quad\hbox{for every }\ell\in L. \tag{5} \] For the fixed-cut version use the sublattice with \(dA_1=0\). Condition (5) is necessary independently of the choice of lattice basis. Subtracting any integral Fourier character changes its left side by a multiple of \(2\pi i\). ## 2. Transfers are independent integral coordinates after fixing the cut Let \(b\) be the braid width and \(c>0\) its crossing count. Write \(y\in\mathbb Z^b\) for its initial head degrees and \(u\in\mathbb Z^c\) for its transfers, with inequalities temporarily removed. Let \(P_j\) be the transposition of the two heads at crossing \(j\), and put \(e_j=e_{i_j}-e_{i_j+1}\). The exact checked degree dynamics are \[ y^{\mathrm{out}}=P_jy^{\mathrm{in}} +\sigma_j u_j e_j . \tag{6} \] For a positive crossing this says \((I,J)\mapsto(J+u,I-u)\); for a negative crossing it says \((J,I)\mapsto(I-u,J+u)\). Thus the original role conventions give (6) at both signs. Compose these equations. With \(P=P_c\cdots P_1\) and integer columns \(E_j=\sigma_jP_c\cdots P_{j+1}e_j\), the closed physical-flow lattice is \[ (I-P)y=Eu . \tag{7} \] Every column of \(E\) has coordinate sum zero. Because the closure is a knot, \(P\) is a single cycle, and \[ \ker_{\mathbb Z}(I-P)=\mathbb Z\mathbf1,\qquad (I-P)\mathbb Z^b=\mathbb Z_0^b . \tag{8} \] For completeness, writing the coordinates in the order of the cycle turns \((I-P)y=z\) into successive integral differences. They can be solved by cumulative sums exactly when \(\sum z_i=0\); their sole free value adds a constant to every coordinate. This proves both assertions in (8) without division. Consequently every \(u\in\mathbb Z^c\) has a closed integral physical flow. There is a unique one with any prescribed initial degree \(y_1\). In particular, on the homogeneous fixed-cut lattice, the transfer map is an isomorphism \[ \{ \text{closed integral physical variations}, \ dA_1=0\}\ \simeq\ \mathbb Z^c . \tag{9} \] Every single-transfer variation \(du_j=1,\ du_k=0\) for \(k\ne j\) is therefore a legitimate integral tangent vector. At a strictly interior real point, small real multiples of each such vector stay feasible. The clocks can be held fixed. ## 3. The only possible simultaneous positive clock base slice At a real point put \(R_j=H_j-V_j\). Differentiating (4) in its independent clock direction gives \[ \partial_{H_j}\mathscr S =\log\frac{\sin\pi(U_j-R_j)}{\sin\pi R_j} +\pi i\{1+\sigma_j(U_j+2J_j)\}. \tag{10} \] Here \(0<R_j<U_j<1\). If (5) holds in this direction, its real part is zero. The identity \[ \sin\pi(U-R)-\sin\pi R =2\cos(\pi U/2)\sin\pi(U/2-R) \tag{11} \] then gives \(R_j=U_j/2\). By (2), the midpoint \(M_j=U_j+2J_j\) belongs to \((0,2)\). The imaginary part of (10) is an integral multiple of \(2\pi\) only when \[ M_j=1,\qquad H_j=V_j+U_j/2 . \tag{12} \] These are exactly the central local clock slices, with their Fourier characters retained. The integral midpoint theorem identifies the kernel of \(p\mapsto(U_j+2J_j)_j\) for a knot braid. Its rank is one, and its initial-head vector is \[ \varepsilon=(1,-1,1,-1,\ldots). \tag{13} \] This uses the independently proved Burau--Alexander minor calculation at \(-1\), including even braid width. The constant flow with every head degree \(1/2\) and all transfers zero has every midpoint one. Hence every real closed physical flow with all midpoints one is that flow plus \(\tau\varepsilon\). The homogeneous zero-midpoint dynamics fix \(\varepsilon\) at every horizontal slice. At crossing \(j\) the over-head component of \(\varepsilon\) is \(\sigma_j\varepsilon_{i_j}\), and its under-head component is \(-\sigma_j\varepsilon_{i_j}\). Therefore \[ \begin{split} U_j&=2\tau\sigma_j\varepsilon_{i_j},\\ J_j=V_j&=\frac12-\tau\sigma_j\varepsilon_{i_j},\\ H_j&=\frac12 . \end{split} \tag{14} \] The last identity uses (12). In particular the simultaneous central slice meets the strict real interior if and only if all signs \(\sigma_j\varepsilon_{i_j}\) are the same. This is precisely the alternating generator-sign pattern \[ \sigma_j=\epsilon(-1)^{i_j-1}, \qquad \epsilon\in\{1,-1\}. \tag{15} \] In this case choose \(\tau\) with \(0<\tau\epsilon<1/2\). All transfers have one common value \(U=2|\tau|\), and every crossing row is \[ ((1-U)/2,\ U/2,\ U/2,\ (1-U)/2). \tag{16} \] The closing degrees are \(1/2+\tau\varepsilon_i\). Thus this is a one-dimensional affine slice, not an open family of physical flows. Fixing the first cut degree fixes \(\tau\) as well. ## 4. No Fourier lift makes it a full real saddle **Theorem.** For every nonempty braid with knot closure, the action (4) has no real stationary point in its regular interior in any integer Fourier lift. The same assertion holds on every fixed-cut interior slice. **Proof.** A purported point must satisfy (12), and hence (14). Vary only the physical flow, holding all \(H_j\) fixed. Since \(H_j=1/2\), the differential of the complete phase is \[ \begin{split} d\varphi &=\sum_j\sigma_j \{H_j\,dU_j+(2H_j-1)\,dJ_j\}\\ &=\frac12\sum_j\sigma_j\,dU_j . \end{split} \tag{17} \] Choose the integral fixed-cut tangent in (9) with a single \(du_j=1\). The entropy differential is real at the real point, while (17) gives \[ \operatorname{Im}D_\ell\mathscr S =\sigma_j\pi/2 . \tag{18} \] This is not in \(2\pi\mathbb Z\). Subtracting an integer Fourier character cannot change that fact. It contradicts (5), proving both versions. \(\square\) The fixed-cut qualification uses the actual operator scalarity before insertion, as in [marked-cut observability](research_incidence_marked_cut_observability.md). It does not replace the prescribed cut in a separate clock sector. The proof of (18) is on the whole conserved lattice and keeps the original closing equations. The earlier [alternating real-phase obstruction](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/alternating_braid_real_phase_obstruction.md) already excludes a real saddle through a particular consecutive opposite-sign variation of the cyclic source. The theorem above is a different, general calculation on the full singleton incidence lattice: it covers every nonempty knot braid and every regular real interior point, including every fixed cut. It does not make a claim about boundary strata. ## 5. The actual complex chart still available This exclusion does not remove the complex interpolation. Let \(G_N\) be the exact sine-factorial function of [the factorial source](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/exact_factorial_interpolation_and_complex_contours.md), with \(G_N(a)=S_a\) at the original integers. The selected clock sum has the following specified extension in all its physical variables: \[ \widetilde C_{\sigma,N}(U,V,j) =\frac{G_N(N(j+U))} {G_N(Nj)G_N(NU)} \exp\left[ N\sigma\pi i\{V(U+2j-1)+jU+U^2/2-U/2\} +\sigma\pi i(V+U/2)\right]. \tag{19} \] For \(NU=u,\ NV=v\) integral, this is exactly the finite clock sum of the [selected-amplitude theorem](research_exact_clock_selected_amplitude.md), for every complex \(j\) in its domain. Indeed the exact functional equation of \(G_N\) turns its first ratio into \(\prod_{r=1}^u2\sin\pi(j+r/N)\); the displayed phase is exactly the marked Pochhammer phase and \(a_{\sigma,N}^v\). Thus the equality fixes the continuation and its marks rather than choosing a new saddle normalization. Multiplying (19) by the remaining exact row factors gives \[ \widetilde{\mathcal R}_{\sigma,N} =\kappa^\sigma \frac{G_N(N(U+V))}{G_N(NV)} e^{-\sigma\pi i(N-1)j}\, \widetilde C_{\sigma,N}. \tag{20} \] This is holomorphic and nonzero on the convex tube \[ \begin{gathered} 0<\Re U<1,\qquad 0<\Re V<\Re(U+V)<1,\\ 0<\Re j<\Re(j+U)<1 . \end{gathered} \tag{21} \] The exact factorial expansion supplies its nonzero local complex symbol uniformly on compact subsets, with the original finite Cartan and framing phases. Products of these row charts retain the literal physical wire equations. This is the existing factorial interpolation expressed in the coordinates of the new exact clock contraction. The original cycle is still the sum of residue tori around the actual allowed physical lattice states, with every endpoint state included. Points on its boundary are not contained in fixed compact subsets of (21). The theorem does not transform that cycle into a geometric descending cycle or bound the side currents of such a transformation. The raw positive Fourier charts also have the independently proved [sewing obstruction](research_rivin_jones_positive_chart_sewing_obstruction.md); switching to them does not supply the missing transport. The conclusion for the proposed route is precise. The local clock contraction has a selected nonzero amplitude, but its positive real initializer cannot be made a full interior saddle by the actual conserved-flow equations or by a Fourier relabeling. A geometric contribution must be located on a genuinely complex chart or after further source contractions or boundary reductions. No nonzero intersection with the original residue cycle has been proved here. The additional global conditions in [dominant-saddle transport](research_dominant_saddle_transport.md) remain to be established for that actual complex source. ## 6. Exponential cancellation of the actual central packet For the alternating sign class (15), the source obstruction has an explicit contour realization. This gives a cancellation estimate in the singleton incidence presentation. It is not a new claim of a strict crossing-count bound: the older [cyclic cut peeling theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/original_source_cyclic_variation_peeling.md), Section 2, already gives a stronger scalar loss by making the first and last cut-crossing weights have modulus one. They are the same crossing if the marked position occurs only once. Fix a nonempty knot braid satisfying (15), put \(a_*=1/2+\epsilon/4\), and choose \(r_N\in\{0,\ldots,N-1\}\) with \(|r_N-Na_*|\le1/2\). Fix the literal first cut degree to \(r_N\). The exact marked-cut theorem permits this choice for the complete sum with its original normalization. By (9), the remaining \((u,h)\) are independent integral coordinates, with their original inequalities. At the limiting point \(z_*=(U,H)=(\mathbf{1}/2,\mathbf{1}/2)\), the horizontal heads are \(1/2+\epsilon\varepsilon_i/4\). Every crossing has over-input \(3/4\), under-input and over-output \(1/4\), and transfer \(1/2\). Its four incidences are all \(1/4\). The closing incidences are \(1/4\) or \(3/4\). The strict row concavity in [the angle optimization](research_charged_source_angle_optimization.md) makes this the unique absolute-action maximum on the fixed-cut limiting fiber, with value \[ M_c=-4c\,\mathcal J(1/4) =\frac{c\,v_8}{2\pi}. \tag{22} \] Here \(v_8\) is the regular ideal octahedron volume. Uniqueness follows because the crossing incidences recover all \(U_j,H_j\), and (9) then recovers the physical flow. Closing rows have zero entropy. Choose a sufficiently small fixed \(\rho>0\) and retain the actual rectangular packet \[ \mathcal B_N=\{(u,h)\text{ in the allowed fixed-cut fiber}: |u_j/N-1/2|\le\rho,\quad |h_j/N-1/2|\le\rho \text{ for every }j\}. \tag{23} \] For large \(N\), the entire box is feasible, since all incidence forms are affine and strictly interior at \(z_*\). Let \(w_N=q^{\Phi_N}/\prod_eS_{n_e}\) be the complete incidence weight on this fixed-cut slice, including its original closing pivots. **Packet theorem.** There are \(C,B,\delta>0\), depending only on this fixed braid and packet, such that \[ \left|\sum_{\mathcal B_N}w_N\right| \le C N^B e^{N(M_c-\delta)} \tag{24} \] for every sufficiently large \(N\), with no parity or coprimality restriction. Enlarging \(C\) covers the finitely many remaining levels as well. **Proof.** Extend the exact degree forms affinely and use the specified factorial function \(G_N\). Its exact reflection contracts each closing denominator: \[ \mathcal I_N(u,h) =N^{-b}\exp\{\pi i\Phi_N(u,h)/N\} \prod_{\substack{j\text{ a crossing}\\0\le k\le3}} G_N(n_{jk}(u,h))^{-1}. \tag{25} \] This is the original weight at all integer points. All \(N-1\) shifts, the difference \(r_N-Na_*\), and the pivotal phases remain in (25). On a fixed small complex neighborhood of \(z_*\), its scaled factorial arguments have real parts strictly between zero and one. The exact compact complex expansion therefore gives \[ |\mathcal I_N(Nz)| \le C N^{B_0}e^{N\Re\mathscr S_*(z)}, \tag{26} \] where \(\mathscr S_*\) is (4) with cut \(A_1=a_*\). The bounded finite offsets change the exponent by \(O(1)\) on this compact chart. The exact finite phase shifts are also retained in the bounded factor. No leading state-dependent phase is removed. Choose one crossing \(j\), set \(t=\sigma_j u_j\), and write \(x=t/N\), centered at \(x_*=\sigma_j/2\). All other \(2c-1\) coordinates remain real and fixed. By (17), \[ \Im\partial_x\mathscr S_*(z_*)=\pi/2. \tag{27} \] Shrink \(\rho\) and choose a small fixed height \(\beta>0\) so that throughout the resulting complex box \[ \pi/4\le\Im\partial_x\mathscr S_*\le3\pi/4. \tag{28} \] The two real faces \(|x-x_*|=\rho\) have a uniform entropy gap \(\eta>0\) below \(M_c\), by uniqueness and compactness. Shrink it once to include the \(O(N^{-1})\) endpoint changes below, and choose \((3\pi/4)\beta\le\eta/2\). If the integers \(t\) in the packet run from \(A_N\) to \(B_N\), take the positively oriented rectangle with vertical sides \(A_N-1/2,\ B_N+1/2\) and horizontal sides \(\Im t=\pm N\beta\). Holomorphy gives exactly \[ \sum_{t=A_N}^{B_N}\mathcal I_N(t,\ldots) =\frac1{2\pi i}\int_{\partial\mathcal R_N} \mathcal I_N(t,\ldots)\, \pi\{\cot(\pi t)-i\}\,dt . \tag{29} \] The subtraction is \(\pi i\), not \(i\); its contour integral is zero. Every original integer residue in the interval remains, also when \(t\) ranges over negative integers for the negative sign. On the upper lip the cotangent factor is bounded, and (28) lowers \(\Re\mathscr S_*\) by at least \(\pi\beta/4\). On the lower lip the density increases by at most \(3\pi\beta/4\), but its exact kernel obeys \[ |\cot(\pi t)-i| \le C e^{-2\pi N\beta}. \tag{30} \] The combined exponent there is at most \(M_c-5\pi\beta/4\). On a half-integer vertical side, \(|\cot(\pi t)-i|\le2\), and the entropy gap with (28) bounds the exponent by \(M_c-\eta/2\). The contour length is \(O(N)\). Equations (26)--(30) therefore bound this one-variable sum by a polynomial times \(e^{N(M_c-\delta)}\), uniformly in the other coordinates, with \(\delta=\min(\pi\beta/4,\eta/2)>0\). There are only polynomially many choices of those real integer coordinates. Summing proves (24). \(\square\) The complement of (23) has a strict absolute entropy gap below \(M_c\): otherwise compactness gives another maximum with some transfer or clock separated from \(1/2\). The endpoint-uniform factorial estimate and the exact margin \(N-1\) control this complement with a polynomial prefactor. Combining it with (24) recovers a strict scalar gap after multiplication by the known original external source factor. As already noted, cyclic cut peeling gives a stronger scalar bound; the additional assertion here is the explicit complex deformation and loss of the central incidence packet itself. The cotangent kernel is essential. Its lower density may grow while its exact source factor decays. Thus the proof does not give a low-modulus deformation for all individual lattice evaluations. It retains the prescribed packet period and does not identify the surviving geometric contour. In particular \(\delta\) is not compared with the difference between the crossing envelope and hyperbolic volume. ## Direct written source versions | Source | SHA-256 | | --- | --- | | research_joint_clock_phase_equations.md | 71393aa353909dfa2dd19b078b1d3fccdf8561520aa071b7537e4bbfc50bb867 | | research_incidence_burau_gauss_reduction.md | 7ca4c1534d3dd4c75e4200b8b221c5b92cae8c2835487b2c97f9014fdbdda1d6 | | research_incidence_marked_cut_observability.md | c0b9f010a8ab4b69b96bbcb0a32a6b8dad6ed8c39fca1029834f2ba74c13cbfc | | research_exact_clock_selected_amplitude.md | a94cdff7db9a704af71f1794bf969d6c00809b7ac13b776f153034a10e1fb617 | | exact_factorial_interpolation_and_complex_contours.md | 1f34f65437dfe0bfb4062a7a74840beae1676353cf13bb8a86f8849a8a36bc72 | | alternating_braid_real_phase_obstruction.md | 954628d08257f57559fd130f5ac5b0d69271852b751eac71399f55e7d2f646d5 | | research_rivin_jones_positive_chart_sewing_obstruction.md | 7809489b46a1eb50accca9910428ca929fd98622734060e39b42e1e2070c7910 | | research_dominant_saddle_transport.md | 413940497a23e884d726b91f9c0ebc01994fef8216811ed2c6fb0838fc80bb04 | | research_charged_source_angle_optimization.md | 45b21fabb9cb65512bc3e576eb3d659b6fe14c3dcd90b4164bfdb12b8cedea64 | | original_source_cyclic_variation_peeling.md | a050e02461edd0ae5d7da1caf1ad673b81921c5a5acebcd6a0153f39e13aca1a |

title: The original-source error as a Euclidean boundary-kernel norm
text:
# The original-source error as a Euclidean boundary-kernel norm Private written proof, 19 November 2026. The polynomial Ward primitive sees only a specified vacuum-input block of the marked current. This note gives an exact positive coherent resolution for that block in the physical coefficient Euclidean metric, and an explicit bound for the original-source error by its unnormalized mixed-kernel \(L^2\) norm. No change of metric is hidden in the bound. The sole complete direct W supplies the actual primitive, source identity, and whole-meridian polynomial bounds. The support compression, coherent resolution, exact Hilbert--Schmidt constant, and metric comparison are proved here. They do not estimate the required kernel at a geometric window or select a contributing relative cycle. ## 1. The literal source and the supported current Fix \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(m\ge2\), and \[ q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\quad M=e^\mu,\quad x=-M/q,\quad x_0=-q^{-1}. 	ag{1} \] The quantum root is fixed in every meridian derivative. On the physical head \(V=\operatorname{span}\{w_0,\ldots,w_d\}\), the vectors \(w_a\) are orthonormal. All tensor products have the corresponding Euclidean metric. Write \(Jw_a=aw_a\), \(\Pi_0=|0angle\langle0|\), and use \[ E(M)w_a=(MQ^{-a}-M^{-1})w_{a-1}\ (a>0),\qquad E(M)w_0=0, \qquad K(M)w_a=xQ^{-a}w_a. 	ag{2} \] Put \(Z=V^{\otimes(m-2)}\). The empty spectator tensor for \(m=2\) means \(Z=\mathbb C\), \(K_Z=I\), and \(E_Z=0\). With the actual ordered coproduct, \[ E_\Sigma=(E_1K_2+E_2)K_Z+E_Z. \] The original and top coupons are \[  egin{split} Q_{m pt}&=\Pi_0\otimes K_2^{-d}\otimes K_Z^{-d},\ Q_{m top}&=|0angle\langle d|\otimes|dangle\langle0| \otimes K_Z^{-d},\ \Phi_M(C)&=\operatorname{Tr}(Q_{m pt}C),\qquad \Delta_M(C)=\Phi_M(C)-\operatorname{Tr}(Q_{m top}C). \end{split}	ag{3} \] The matrix \(C\) may contain arbitrary prescribed marks. Crossing scalars, framing factors, and any outside normalization remain in \(C\), or outside every term with their full product rule. Here is the primitive from W, in notation sufficient for the support calculation. Let \(Rw_a=w_{a+1}\) for \(a<d\), \(Rw_d=0\), and set \[ \mathcal A_{12,0} =\sum_{a=0}^{d-1}  rac{x_0^{a-d}}{1-Q^{-a-1}}\,|0angle\langle a|\otimes R^{a+1}. 	ag{4} \] This \(R\) is the unit raising shift, not a crossing. Define \[ h_a(M)=M^{-a} rac{(Q;Q)_a}{(M^{-2}Q;Q)_a},\quad D_h w_a=h_a w_a,\quad \mathcal D_{12}=(D_hM^{-J_1})\otimes D_h, \] \[ \mathcal A(M) =M^{-d}\mathcal D_{12}\mathcal A_{12,0}\mathcal D_{12}^{-1} \otimes K_Z^{-N}. 	ag{5} \] Here \((z;Q)_a=\prod_{j=0}^{a-1}(1-zQ^j)\). W proves, on the meridian germ and on the scaled collars used below, \[ [\mathcal A,E_\Sigma]=Q_{m pt}-Q_{m top},\qquad \Delta_M(C)=\operatorname{Tr} igl(\mathcal A[E_\Sigma,C] igr). 	ag{6} \] All bottom and top arrows in this identity are the finite physical ones. Define two fixed orthogonal projections: \[ P=\Pi_0^{(1)}\otimes(I-\Pi_0)^{(2)}\otimes I_Z,\qquad L=\mathbf1_{\{J_1+J_2\le d-1\}}\otimes I_Z. 	ag{7} \] Every nonzero entry of the summand indexed by \(a\) in (4) sends \[ |a,bangle\longmapsto |0,b+a+1angle, \qquad 0\le b\le d-a-1. 	ag{8} \] Its input pair degree is at most \(d-1\), and its second output occupation lies in \(1,\ldots,d\). The diagonal matrices in (5) commute with \(P,L\). Consequently, exactly throughout the family, \[ \mathcal A=P\mathcal A L,\qquad \partial_\mu^k\mathcal A=P(\partial_\mu^k\mathcal A)L. 	ag{9} \] For \[ Y=L[E_\Sigma,C]P 	ag{10} \] cyclicity of the finite trace therefore gives \[  oxed{\ \Delta_M(C)=\operatorname{Tr}(\mathcal A Y).\ } 	ag{11} \] No hypothesis that \(C\) preserves degree or intertwines a generator is needed. In particular only this supported current, rather than the entire commutator, is needed in any trace-, operator-, or Hilbert--Schmidt-norm estimate from W. ## 2. An exact resolution in the stated metric For \(z\in\mathbb C\), define the unit vector \[ \psi_z=(1+|z|^2)^{-d/2} \sum_{a=0}^d\sqrt{ inom da}\,z^a w_a,\qquad d
u(z)= rac{d\Re z\,d\Im z}{\pi(1+|z|^2)^2}. 	ag{12} \] The measure has mass one. At infinity the projector extends with range \(\mathbb Cw_d\); choices of vector phase do not affect the following integrals. The angular integral removes distinct powers, and the radial integral gives \[  inom da\int_0^\infty  rac{t^a}{(1+t)^{d+2}}\,dt= rac1{d+1}= rac1N. 	ag{13} \] For example the substitution \(u=t/(1+t)\), followed by repeated integration by parts, evaluates the integral as \(a!(d-a)!/(d+1)!\). Thus, exactly, \[ N\int|\psi_zangle\langle\psi_z|\,d
u(z)=I. 	ag{14} \] Write \(\psi_{\mathbf z}\) for tensor products. If \(Y=YP\), its first input head is fixed at \(w_0\). Applying (14) on all output heads and on the remaining input heads proves \[  oxed{\quad \|Y\|_{m HS}^{\,2} =N^{2m-1}\int \left|\left\langle\psi_{\mathbf y}, Y(w_0\otimes\psi_{\mathbf z})ightangleight|^2 d
u^{[m]}(\mathbf y)d
u^{[m-1]}(\mathbf z). \quad}	ag{15} \] Indeed the output resolution first gives the squared norm of \(Y(w_0\otimes\psi_{\mathbf z})\); the input resolution then gives the trace of \(Y^*Y\) on the subspace with first head \(w_0\). That is its full Hilbert--Schmidt norm because \(Y=YP\). The second-head factor \(I-\Pi_0\) and the output projection \(L\) remain inside \(Y\); neither has been replaced by a scalar. Denote the unnormalized mixed kernel in (15) by \(\mathcal K_Y(\mathbf y,\mathbf z)\), and its norm for the displayed probability product measure by \(\|\mathcal K_Y\|_{L^2}\). Then \(\|Y\|_{m HS}=N^{m-1/2}\|\mathcal K_Y\|_{L^2}\). This includes all occupation caps and every point of the compact coherent resolutions. ## 3. The exact root constant In (4), different \(a\)'s have disjoint input columns and \(\|R^{a+1}\|_{m HS}^2=d-a\). At \(M=1\), the spectator scalar \(K_Z^{-N}\) has modulus one. Hence \[ \|\mathcal A_0\|_{m HS}^2 =N^{m-2}\sum_{j=1}^{N-1}  rac{N-j}{|1-Q^j|^2}. 	ag{16} \] The finite polynomial \(p(t)=1+t+\cdots+t^{N-1}\) has roots \(Q^j\), \(1\le j<N\). Logarithmic differentiation at \(t=1\) gives \[ \sum_{j=1}^{N-1}|1-Q^j|^{-2} =\left. rac{d}{dt}\left(t rac{p'(t)}{p(t)}ight)ight|_{t=1} = rac{N^2-1}{12}. 	ag{17} \] The first equality uses \(-Q^j/(1-Q^j)^2=|1-Q^j|^{-2}\). For the last equality use \(p(1)=N\), \(p'(1)=N(N-1)/2\), and \(p''(1)=N(N-1)(N-2)/3\). Pairing \(j\) with \(N-j\) in (16) therefore proves, for every level, including even or composite ones, \[ \|\mathcal A_0\|_{m HS}^2 = rac{N^{m-1}(N^2-1)}{24}. 	ag{18} \] Hilbert--Schmidt trace duality and (15) now give the explicit source bound \[  oxed{\quad |\Delta_{M=1}(C)| \le \sqrt{ rac{N^{3m-2}(N^2-1)}{24}}\, \|\mathcal K_{\,L[E_{\Sigma,0},C]P}\|_{L^2}. \quad}	ag{19} \] Equivalently the left side is \(|\Phi_{M=1}(C)-\operatorname{Tr}(Q_{{m top},0}C)|\). The separate root estimates from W remain valid with the same supported current: \[ |\Delta_{M=1}(C)|\le \min\left\{ rac N2\|Y_0\|_1,\,  rac{N^m}{2}\|Y_0\|,\, \sqrt{ rac{N^{m-1}(N^2-1)}{24}}\|Y_0\|_{m HS}ight\}. 	ag{20} \] These are separate trace-duality estimates, not a chain of norm inequalities. A relative geometric error requires a relative bound for the actual kernel in (19); (19) does not assert such a bound. ## 4. The whole meridian family and true normals Let \(C(M)\) be a holomorphic marked matrix on the meridian collar. Fix \(0<\eta<\eta'<\pi\) and \(m\). W proves on \(|N\mu|\le\eta\), for each fixed \(k\), \[ \|\partial_\mu^k\mathcal A\| \le C_kN^k(N+1)^{p_{\eta'}},\qquad \operatorname{rank}(\partial_\mu^k\mathcal A)\le dN^{m-2}. 	ag{21} \] The exponent \(p_{\eta'}\) does not depend on \(m\). All displayed families are holomorphic on the larger buffered collar. Because \(P,L\) and the coherent frame are independent of \(\mu\), (15) applies unchanged to every \(\partial_\mu^\ell Y\). The product rule in (11), followed by (21), yields \[ N^{-k}|\partial_\mu^k\Delta_M(C(M))| \le C_k(N+1)^{p_{\eta'}}N^{(3m-2)/2} \sum_{\ell=0}^k N^{-\ell} \|\mathcal K_{\partial_\mu^\ell Y}\|_{L^2}. 	ag{22} \] The constants may depend on \(m,\eta,\eta'\) and \(k\). No derivatives of a root-only symbol are used. In particular, with subscripts now denoting the value and true first derivative at \(\mu=0\), \[ Y_0=L[E_{\Sigma,0},C_0]P,\qquad Y_1=L igl([E_{\Sigma,1},C_0]+[E_{\Sigma,0},C_1] igr)P, \] \[ \left.\partial_\mu\Delta_M(C(M))ight|_0 =\operatorname{Tr}(\mathcal A_1Y_0+\mathcal A_0Y_1). 	ag{23} \] The left side contains the actual pivot derivatives: it equals \(\operatorname{Tr}Q_{{m pt},0}(C_1-d(m-1)C_0) -\operatorname{Tr}Q_{{m top},0}(C_1-d(m-2)C_0)\). An outside scalar is multiplied into every term before differentiation. Root commutation alone kills \(Y_0\), not \(Y_1\). ## 5. Why the metric and the mixed kernel matter The other common coherent metric has \(\|w_a\|_{m bin}^2= inom da^{-1}\), so its orthonormal basis is \(u_a=\sqrt{ inom da}\,w_a\). It is not the metric of (12)--(22). This distinction is visible in this very primitive. On the root input \((a,d-a-1)\) and output \((0,d)\), its matrix entry in the binomial orthonormal basis has modulus \[  rac{\sqrt{ inom da inom d{a+1}}}{|1-Q^{-a-1}|}. 	ag{24} \] Take \(a=\lfloor(d-1)/2floor\). The largest binomial coefficient is at least \(2^d/(d+1)\), its indicated adjacent coefficient is at least half as large, and \(|1-Q^{-a-1}|\le2\). Thus (24) is at least \(2^d/(2\sqrt2(d+1))\). This particular primitive has exponential binomial-metric norm. This does not claim the same lower bound for every possible Ward primitive. The top source is the mixed corner \(\langle d,0|C|0,dangle\), with spectators closed by their literal pivot. In (12), \(w_0\) and \(w_d\) are the two antipodal coherent endpoints. Their identity overlap is zero for \(N\ge2\). Consequently (15) uses the unnormalized mixed kernel and never divides by an identity overlap such as \((1+wz)^d\). Local normalized symbol estimates, estimates in the binomial metric, and estimates on a small output disk do not by themselves bound the full integral in (15). The bridge retains the original source and all its true normals, but supplies no geometric window, mixed-kernel decay estimate, opposite-polarization return, or nonzero closing coefficient. No new volume-conjecture case is asserted. ## Complete direct and author verification * W: [research_polynomial_top_source_ward_transport.md](research_polynomial_top_source_ward_transport.md), 376 lines, SHA256 \(	exttt{fe6493819fa24ce3ccf27b4625be57f34513d6542830f9aeb591fed6e495d8ad}\). Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used. No mathematical programs, numerical tests, builds, or frozen-file edits were performed.
