title: A convexity criterion for the original edge phase
text:
# A convexity criterion for the original edge phase Research note, 2 November 2026. This note gives an exact test for the real part of the Hessian of the circle-tree edge phase. A simple sufficient condition can be checked without solving any filling equations. The test is unchanged by arbitrary signed filling powers. The conclusion is a uniqueness and comparison theorem inside a specified convex complex region. It does not assert that every critical point of the original source lies in that region. In particular, it does not supply the global hypothesis in [the dominant-saddle transport theorem](research_dominant_saddle_transport.md). ## 1. The original phase and its branches Use the edge phase of [the circle-tree geometry paper](../papers/circle-tree-geometry/main.tex), with its normalization \[ \psi(0,0)= rac{v_{m oct}}{\pi},\qquad \psi_t(t,u)=- rac1\pi\operatorname{arsinh}  igl(	an(t/2)\cos(u/2) igr). 	ag{1} \] The formula for \(\psi_u\) is obtained by interchanging \(t,u\). Here \(v_{m oct}\) is the volume of a regular ideal octahedron. The logarithms initially have their values at \(t=u=0\), and are then continued along the specified geometric path. When a larger domain is used, a single-valued lift of this phase is part of the data. The Hessian calculated below does not forget that choice; it is the continuation of the Hessian in (1). Put \[ a=	an(t/2),\qquad b=	an(u/2),\qquad q=\sqrt{1+a^2+b^2},\qquad q(0,0)=1. 	ag{2} \] We work where \(\cos(t/2)\), \(\cos(u/2)\), and \(q\) are nonzero. In the test below the continued root is required to satisfy \(\Re q>0\). This specifies a root, rather than just the equation for its square. Differentiating (1) on its original branch gives \[ -2\pi\,\psi''(t,u) =H(t,u) = rac1q  egin{pmatrix} 1+a^2&-ab\ -ab&1+b^2 \end{pmatrix}. 	ag{3} \] For example, the square root in the derivative of \(\operatorname{arsinh}(a\cos(u/2))\) is \(q\cos(u/2)\), by continuation from completeness. This gives the first diagonal entry in (3); differentiating with respect to \(u\) gives the off-diagonal entry. Equivalently, with \[ \Delta=q\cos(t/2)\cos(u/2), \] the same matrix is \[ H= rac1\Delta  egin{pmatrix} \cos(u/2)/\cos(t/2)&-\sin(t/2)\sin(u/2)\ -\sin(t/2)\sin(u/2)&\cos(t/2)/\cos(u/2) \end{pmatrix}. 	ag{4} \] In particular, \[ \det H=1,\qquad \operatorname{tr}H=q+q^{-1}. 	ag{5} \] All these are identities for the original edge phase. They do not use an approximation to it. ## 2. The exact positivity test For a complex symmetric matrix \(H\), its Hermitian part is the real symmetric matrix obtained by taking the real part of each entry. We write this matrix as \(\Re H\). **Proposition 1.** Suppose that the branch in (2) has \(\Re q>0\). Then \[ \Re H>0 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \Re q> igl|\Im(a\overline b) igr|. 	ag{6} \] Here \(>0\) means positive definite. More explicitly, \[ \det(\Re H) = rac{(\Re q)^2- igl(\Im(a\overline b) igr)^2}{|q|^2}, \qquad \operatorname{tr}(\Re H) =\Re q\,(1+|q|^{-2}). 	ag{7} \] **Proof.** Write \(H=\left( egin{smallmatrix}A&B\B&C\end{smallmatrix}ight)\). The identity \(AC-B^2=1\) gives \[ \det(\Re H) = rac{1+\Re(A\overline C)-|B|^2}{2}. 	ag{8} \] For (3), the difference in the numerator is \[  egin{aligned} \Re(A\overline C)-|B|^2 &=|q|^{-2} \left[\Re\{(1+a^2)(1+\overline b^{\,2})\}-|ab|^2ight]\ &=|q|^{-2} \left[\Re(q^2)-2\{\Im(a\overline b)\}^2ight]. \end{aligned} \] Since \(|q|^2+\Re(q^2)=2(\Re q)^2\), substitution into (8) proves the determinant formula. The trace formula follows from (5). Its right-hand side is positive. A real symmetric two-by-two matrix with positive trace is positive definite exactly when its determinant is positive. This proves (6). \(\square\) The test is strict. At equality in (6), the real part of the Hessian has a zero eigenvalue, even though the complex determinant in (5) is still one. ## 3. An explicit sufficient region Define \[ \mathcal C= \left\{(t,u): |\Re t|<\pi,\quad |\Re u|<\pi,\quad \{\Im	an(t/2)\}^2+\{\Im	an(u/2)\}^2<1 ight\}. 	ag{9} \] On this region \(1+a^2+b^2\) has positive real part. Consequently its principal square root is holomorphic and has positive real part. It agrees with the complete branch wherever that branch is continued inside this region. **Corollary 2.** The matrix \(\Re H(t,u)\) is positive definite throughout \(\mathcal C\). **Proof.** Write \(a=A+iC\), \(b=B+iD\), and set \[ X=A^2+B^2,\qquad Y=C^2+D^2<1,\qquad Z=AC+BD. \] Then \(q^2=1+X-Y+2iZ\), so \[ (\Re q)^2 = rac{|1+X-Y+2iZ|+1+X-Y}{2} \ge 1+X-Y. \] Also \(\{\Im(a\overline b)\}^2=(BC-AD)^2\le XY\), whereas \[ (1+X-Y)-XY=(1-Y)(1+X)>0. \] Thus (6) holds strictly. \(\square\) Condition (9) is sufficient, not necessary. For example, take \[ t= rac{2\pi}{3}-2i\log2,\qquad u=0. 	ag{10} \] Then \(\Im	an(t/2)=-15/13\), so (9) fails. Nevertheless \[ H(t,0)= \operatorname{diag} igl(\sec(t/2),\cos(t/2) igr) 	ag{11} \] has positive real part. In fact (11) has positive real part on the entire strip \(|\Re t|<\pi\), at every imaginary height. Its branch is \(q=\sec(t/2)\). The example also lies in the positive single-edge geometric chart: \(e^{it/2}\), its reciprocal, and \(\sec(t/2)+	an(t/2)\) and its reciprocal all have positive real part. The eight shapes in Section 3 of [the isolated-vertex geometry note](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_isolated_internal_vertex_geometry.md) therefore have positive imaginary part. Thus (9) is not being proposed as a characterization of positive tetrahedra. No equivalence between positivity of all eight shapes and (6) is claimed here. ## 4. Arbitrary powers and arbitrary connected sets of vertices Let \(S\) be a finite set of selected vertices in an original circle tree. Include each original edge incident to \(S\) once. At an endpoint outside \(S\), fix the boundary angle at zero. Let \[ \Psi_S(\mathbf t)=\sum_{vw}\psi(t_v,t_w), \qquad F_{\mathbf n, oldsymbol c}(\mathbf t) =\Psi_S(\mathbf t) + rac{i}{4\pi}\sum_{v\in S}n_vt_v^2 -i\sum_{v\in S}c_vt_v, 	ag{12} \] where \(n_v\) are real numbers (in particular, any fixed signed integer powers), and \(c_v\) are real cone charges. Each selected vertex is assumed to have at least one incident edge. All phases are on one specified lift. Let \(\Omega\subset\mathbb C^S\) be an open convex region. Suppose that at every point of \(\Omega\), each edge with both endpoints selected satisfies (6) on the continued branch. An edge with only one selected endpoint is required to satisfy the corresponding positive real diagonal test. For instance, these assumptions hold if every edge pair belongs to \(\mathcal C\); for an outside endpoint zero, (11) gives the larger strip directly. **Theorem 3.** Under these assumptions, \[ \Re[-F''_{\mathbf n, oldsymbol c}]>0 \quad\hbox{on }\Omega. 	ag{13} \] For every fixed choice of the powers and cone charges, there is at most one critical point of \(F_{\mathbf n, oldsymbol c}\) in \(\Omega\). If that critical point is \(z_*\), its Hessian is nonsingular. On every real horizontal segment \(z_*+sx\subset\Omega\), \(x\in\mathbb R^S\), \(0\le s\le1\), the real action is strictly smaller than at \(z_*\), unless \(x=0\). If \(\Re[-F'']\ge\gamma I\) on such a segment, then the quantitative comparison is \[ \Re F(z_*+x)\le \Re F(z_*)- rac{\gamma}{2}|x|^2. 	ag{14} \] **Proof.** The Hessian of \(-\Psi_S\) is the sum of the edge matrices \(H/(2\pi)\), inserted in their original vertex coordinates. Each summand has positive real part on its endpoint coordinates. Every nonzero vector has a nonzero coordinate at a vertex incident to one of these edges, so the sum is positive definite. The filling quadratic contributes \(-i\operatorname{diag}(n_v)/(2\pi)\); this is skew-Hermitian and contributes zero to the Hermitian part. The charge term contributes no Hessian. This proves (13). Put \(G=-
abla F\). If \(z,w\in\Omega\) and \(v=z-w
e0\), convexity permits integration along the straight segment: \[ \Re igl(v^*[G(z)-G(w)] igr) =\int_0^1 \Re igl(v^*DG(w+sv)v igr)\,ds>0. 	ag{15} \] For a complex symmetric matrix the Hermitian part is its entrywise real part, so (13) applies also to complex vectors \(v\). Thus \(G(z)
e G(w)\). In particular there cannot be two critical points. If \(F''v=0\), (13) applied to \(v\) would give a contradiction, proving nonsingularity. Finally, along the real horizontal segment the first derivative at \(s=0\) is zero and the second derivative is \(\Re(x^TF''x)<0\). Twice integrating proves the strict comparison and (14). \(\square\) Convexity of \(\Omega\) is an actual hypothesis. Neither \(\mathcal C\) nor the full locus (6) has been asserted to be convex. One may use convex subsets of these loci, or verify (6) directly on a specified convex region. ## 5. Which existing geometric paths satisfy the test? For the regular all-zero subtree geometry, the selected angles are \(t_v=-ih_v\), with \(h_v\ge0\). Write \(r_v=	anh(h_v/2)\). On an edge \(vw\), condition (9) becomes \[ r_v^2+r_w^2<1. 	ag{16} \] This is exactly the regular-edge condition already used there: \[ r_v^2+r_w^2<1 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \sinh(h_v/2)\sinh(h_w/2)<1. 	ag{17} \] To verify the equivalence, square the nonnegative product and use \(\sinh^2(h/2)=r^2/(1-r^2)\). The resulting inequality is \(r_v^2r_w^2<(1-r_v^2)(1-r_w^2)\), which is (16). Consequently the entire straight-height cone path in [the regular zero-subtree geometry note](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_regular_zero_subtree_geometry.md) satisfies (13) at its selected point. This includes its uniform sufficient class \[ 	an(\pi/d_v)	an(\pi/d_w)\le1 	ag{18} \] on each internal selected edge, in particular all selected degrees at least four. The strict endpoint inequalities in that note ensure (17) even when equality holds in (18). This is a conclusion about that path and its small neighborhoods. It does not put an entire period contour inside one common convex region. The small complex charts in [the connected-filling geometry note](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_connected_short_filling_geometry.md) also satisfy (9). For example, if \(|t|,|u|\le1/64\), then \(|	an(t/2)|,|	an(u/2)|<1/127\), and the sum in (9) is less than \(2/127^2\). For an isolated selected vertex all its neighboring angles are zero. Formula (11) supplies (13) on the entire convex strip \(|\Re t|<\pi\), for every signed power \(n\). The existence theorem in [the isolated-vertex note](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_isolated_internal_vertex_geometry.md) therefore supplies the unique selected critical point in that strip whenever \(d+|n|>2\). No restriction to large \(|n|\) or large degree is needed for this uniqueness. ## 6. The geometric value and what this comparison does not prove The original peripheral formulas must still be retained. With \(n_v=\eta_v-2p_v\), where \(\eta_v\) is the original carrier and \(p_v\) is the integer filling coefficient, they are \[ U_v=-2\pi(\Psi_S)_{t_v}-i\eta_vt_v,\qquad V_v=2it_v. 	ag{19} \] The stationary equations for (12) give the full primitive cone periods \[ U_v+p_vV_v=-2\pi i c_v. 	ag{20} \] Suppose a marked positive geometric path \(t(s)\), with charges \(c_v(s)\), has actually been constructed, using the original face pairings and the continued logarithms in (19). Its core lengths are \(-2\Im t_v(s)\). Stationarity then gives \[  rac{d}{ds}\Re F_{\mathbf n, oldsymbol c(s)}(\mathbf t(s)) =\sum_v\Im t_v(s)\,c_v'(s). 	ag{21} \] Schläfli's formula for this same cone path gives \(2\pi\) times (21) as the volume derivative. Starting with its complete octahedral volume fixes the additive constant. This is the geometric calibration already proved for the paths cited above. It is not a consequence of Hessian positivity alone. For \(0<c_v<1\), the meridian in (20) generally has nontrivial elliptic holonomy. Its representation is a representation of the unfilled exterior; it need not factor through the group of the smoothly filled manifold. An upper bound for volumes of representations of that smoothly filled manifold therefore does not apply to this intermediate path without another argument. There are three distinct gaps between Theorem 3 and the required dominant-saddle transport statement: 1. Other critical points need not lie in the convex region of Theorem 3. Positive shapes of the selected point do not place the other solutions of the gluing equations in the same positive angle domain or logarithmic lift. 2. A strictly concave horizontal action does not compare that action with critical values or endpoint contributions on other sheets. The [adjacent-pair alias identity](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_adjacent_alias_bloch_identity.md) gives an actual equal-real-action end. Its removal uses the exact source identities, not a strict inequality from geometry. 3. Even uniqueness of all finite critical points in a region does not prove that the original relative cycle can be deformed into it without additional divisors, residues, or ends. The nonzero coefficient of the selected cycle and estimates on the remaining chains are separate requirements. Thus the result supplies a general, elementary criterion for local and regional convexity that retains the actual filling powers. For arbitrary fixed short partial fillings, the still missing statement is a global comparison or an exact reduction of the original period to a region where such a comparison applies.

title: Confluent physical rows, the original closing, and the turn-invariant positive quotient
text:
# Confluent physical rows, the original closing, and the turn-invariant positive quotient Private written proof, 17 November 2026. The full physical value and normal rows give an exact block formula for the original Frobenius closing. They also identify the largest positive quotient on which every original \(V_n\) is an isometry. The prescribed closing has dual norm one on this quotient, but one literal multiplication crossing does not descend to it. In fact the same obstruction applies to every positive semidefinite form invariant under \(V_1\) which controls that closing. These are statements about the original finite source and its full normal channels. They give neither a lower bound for a prescribed filled scalar nor a source-specific geometric asymptotic. ## 1. Full original rows and conventions Put \[ N\ge2,\quad D=N-1,\quad J=\lfloor D/2floor,\quad 	heta=\pi/N,\quad q=e^{i	heta},\quad \eta=(-1)^D,\quad \kappa=q^{D^2/2}, \] \[ c_j=2\cos((2j+1)	heta),\quad P_N(Z)=2T_N(Z/2)+2,\quad \mathcal A_N=\mathbb C[Z]/(P_N). 	ag{1} \] Here \(T_N\) in \(P_N\) is the Chebyshev polynomial. The distinct double-node indices form \(\mathcal D_N=\{0,\ldots,\lfloor N/2floor-1\}\). At odd \(N\), the remaining index \(j=J\), denoted by \(*\) when convenient, is the simple node \(c_*=-2\). With \(s_r=2\sin(r	heta)\), \(S_r=\prod_{a=1}^r s_a\), and \(S_0=1\), retain \[ e_r(Z)=S_r^{-2}\prod_{a<r}(c_a-Z),\qquad K_N(w,Z)=\sum_{r=0}^{D}e_r(w)e_r(Z), \] \[ \phi_N(f)=\eta N^2[Z^D]\operatorname{rem}_{P_N}f,\qquad Te_r=e_{D-r},\qquad V_n=\kappa^nTR^{-n}T . 	ag{2} \] Here \(R\) and its powers mean the original multiplication crossings, with their common Cartan scalar retained. The physical rows are \[ F_j=K_N(c_j,\cdot),\qquad G_j=\partial_wK_N(c_j,\cdot)\quad(j\in\mathcal D_N). 	ag{3} \] The signed linearization source proves that these rows form a basis: \(\deg F_j=j\), \(\deg G_j=D-j\). There is no \(G_*\) at the odd simple node. The original Newton identities give \[ \phi_N(e_r e_s)=\mathbf1_{r+s=D},\qquad \phi_N(Tf\,Tg)=\phi_N(fg),\qquad \phi_N(Tf)=f(c_0). 	ag{4} \] The middle identity follows directly by reversing both indices in the first identity. Thus \(T\) preserves this bilinear Frobenius form. It is not an algebra homomorphism. ## 2. Exact confluent Gram and coordinate recovery For a double node define \[ a_j=4-c_j^2,\qquad  eta_j= rac{\eta}{a_j},\qquad \gamma_j= rac{\eta c_j}{a_j^2}. 	ag{5} \] Both \(a_j\) and \( eta_j\) are nonzero. **Theorem 1.** In the basis (3), distinct physical nodes are orthogonal for the bilinear form \((f,g)\mapsto\phi_N(fg)\). The double-node block and odd simple block are respectively \[  oxed{\quad  egin{pmatrix} \phi_N(F_j^2)&\phi_N(F_jG_j)\ \phi_N(F_jG_j)&\phi_N(G_j^2) \end{pmatrix} =  egin{pmatrix}0& eta_j\  eta_j&\gamma_j\end{pmatrix}, \qquad \phi_N(F_*^2)=1 . \quad} 	ag{6} \] For \[ f=\sum_{j\in\mathcal D_N}(A_jF_j+B_jG_j) +\mathbf1_{N\ {m odd}}A_*F_*, 	ag{7} \] its coefficients are exactly \[  oxed{\quad B_j= eta_j^{-1}(Tf)(c_j),\qquad A_j= eta_j^{-1}(Tf)'(c_j) -\gamma_j eta_j^{-2}(Tf)(c_j),\qquad A_*=(Tf)(-2). \quad} 	ag{8} \] In particular the actual prescribed closing is \[  oxed{\ \phi_N(f)= eta_0 B_0.\ } 	ag{9} \] **Proof.** The ordinary reproducer and its first normal give \[ TF_j=\delta_j= rac{P_N(Z)}{\eta N^2(Z-c_j)},\qquad TG_j=\epsilon_j= rac{P_N(Z)}{\eta N^2(Z-c_j)^2}, 	ag{10} \] \[ \phi_N(\delta_j f)=f(c_j),\qquad \phi_N(\epsilon_j f)=f'(c_j). 	ag{11} \] The second identity is only used at double nodes. All fractions in (10) are polynomials; (11) includes canonical multiplication and the full repeated-root relation. The Chebyshev differential equation and its derivative are \[ (4-Z^2)P_N''-ZP_N'+N^2(P_N-2)=0, \] \[ (4-Z^2)P_N'''-3ZP_N''+(N^2-1)P_N'=0 . 	ag{12} \] At a double root these imply \[  rac{P_N''(c_j)}{2\eta N^2}= eta_j,\qquad  rac{P_N'''(c_j)}{6\eta N^2}=\gamma_j . 	ag{13} \] Thus \(\delta_j(c_j)=0\), \(\delta_j'(c_j)= eta_j\), \(\epsilon_j(c_j)= eta_j\), and \(\epsilon_j'(c_j)=\gamma_j\). At every other double node both polynomials have the required zero value and first normal, except that only the value is required at the odd simple node. At that simple node \(\delta_*(-2)=P_N'(-2)/N^2=1\). Equations (4), (10), and (11) now give (6). The physical jets of \(Tf\) in (10) give (8). Finally \(\phi_N(f)=(Tf)(c_0)\), by applying (4) to \(Tf\). The value at \(c_0\) in (8) is \( eta_0B_0\), proving (9). The simple row contributes nothing to (9). \(\square\) For the coefficient reflection \(f^\sharp(Z)=\overline{f( ar Z)}\), the Hermitian form \(\phi_N(f^\sharp g)\) has the same real blocks (6). Every double block has determinant \(- eta_j^2<0\). Its total signature is \((\lceil N/2ceil,\lfloor N/2floor)\). In particular the span of the value rows is totally isotropic at even levels. At odd levels its only nonzero pairing is the simple-row square. These conclusions also follow from the degrees in (3), but (6) retains the missing normal pairings. ## 3. Actual Jordan phases and all invariant positive forms Write \[ 
u_j=(-1)^j q^{j(j+1)},\qquad \lambda_{n,j}=
u_j^{-n},\qquad \alpha_j= rac{R'(c_j)}{R(c_j)} = rac{i(D-2j)}{4\sin((2j+1)	heta)} \quad(j\in\mathcal D_N). 	ag{14} \] The original crossing values are \(R(c_j)=\kappa
u_j\). The number \(\alpha_j\) is purely imaginary and nonzero at every double node, at every \(N\ge2\). The retained Jordan action from the signed-turn source is \[ V_nF_j=\lambda_{n,j}F_j,\qquad V_nG_j=\lambda_{n,j}(G_j-n\alpha_jF_j). 	ag{15} \] The odd simple row has only its first formula. Thus (7) transforms by \[ (A_j,B_j)\longmapsto \lambda_{n,j}(A_j-n\alpha_jB_j,B_j). 	ag{16} \] The normal coefficient is not discarded. The Hermitian indefinite form (6) is preserved by (16), since \(\alpha_j+\overline{\alpha_j}=0\) and \(|\lambda_{n,j}|=1\). Define the surjective value map and its seminorm by \[ \mathcal U_N f=((Tf)(c_j))_{0\le j\le J},\qquad \|f\|_{\mathcal Q_N}^2 =\sum_{j=0}^{J}|(Tf)(c_j)|^2 . 	ag{17} \] Surjectivity follows from ordinary value interpolation, followed by \(T\); prescribing no normals is required for it. **Theorem 2.** The form (17) has exactly the kernel \[ \mathcal L_N=\operatorname{span} \{F_j:j\in\mathcal D_N\}. 	ag{18} \] It gives a positive definite norm on \(\mathcal A_N/\mathcal L_N\), and every \(V_n\) induces an isometry there. The original closing descends and satisfies \[ |\phi_N(f)|\le\|f\|_{\mathcal Q_N} 	ag{19} \] with exact dual norm one. Moreover, every positive semidefinite Hermitian form \(\mathfrak h\) on \(\mathcal A_N\) satisfying \(\mathfrak h(V_1f,V_1g)=\mathfrak h(f,g)\) kills \(\mathcal L_N\). Precisely all such forms are \[ \mathfrak h(f,g)=(\mathcal U_N f)^* B(\mathcal U_N g), \quad B\ge0,\quad B_{jk}=0\ \hbox{if }\lambda_{1,j}
e\lambda_{1,k}. 	ag{20} \] Possible repeated crossing phases are retained in the blocks of \(B\), including at composite levels. **Proof.** Equation (8) proves (18). Also, directly from (2), \[ \mathcal U_N(V_nf)_j =\kappa^nR(c_j)^{-n}(Tf)(c_j) =\lambda_{n,j}\mathcal U_N(f)_j . 	ag{21} \] This proves isometry. Equation (9) identifies the closing with the zeroth coordinate of (17), proving (19). Equality is achieved by \(f= eta_0^{-1}G_0\), whose \(\mathcal U_N\) vector is the zeroth standard vector. For any invariant \(\mathfrak h\), iterate (15) with \(n=m\) and \(m\) an arbitrary positive integer: \[ \mathfrak h(G_j-m\alpha_jF_j,G_j-m\alpha_jF_j) =\mathfrak h(G_j,G_j). 	ag{22} \] The coefficient of \(m^2\) is \(|\alpha_j|^2\mathfrak h(F_j,F_j)\), so it is zero. Positivity and Cauchy--Schwarz then give \(\mathfrak h(F_j,g)=0\) for every \(g\). Thus the form factors through (17), giving a unique matrix \(B\ge0\). Invariance under the unit diagonal matrix in (21) is precisely the block condition in (20). Conversely that condition proves invariance, and also invariance under every \(V_n=V_1^n\). \(\square\) The quotient in (18) is a quotient of vector spaces with the specified \(V_n\) action. It is not an algebra quotient: it kills \(F_0=1\). It retains the normal coefficients \(B_j\) through \((Tf)(c_j)= eta_j B_j\), but forgets their value-row partners. No assertion about serial products follows from its positive norm. For \(N\ge3\), (19) has no converse lower bound on the full quotient. A coordinate of \(\mathcal U_N f\) other than zero can be nonzero while \(\phi_N(f)=0\); take \(G_j\) with \(j>0\) when available, or the odd simple row. At \(N=2\) the quotient has dimension one, but the crossing obstruction below still holds. ## 4. One original crossing leaves every such null quotient The original finite crossing formulas are \[ R^\sigma=\kappa^\sigma \sum_{r=0}^{D}(-q)^{\sigma r}e_r,\qquad \sigma\in\{1,-1\}. 	ag{23} \] They imply the exact polynomial identities \[ TR^\sigma=R^{-\sigma},\qquad \phi_N(R^\sigma)=\kappa^\sigma(-q)^{\sigma D}, \qquad |\phi_N(R^\sigma)|=1 . 	ag{24} \] For the first identity reverse (23) and use \(\kappa^2(-q)^D=1\). All original phases are retained. **Theorem 3.** There is no positive semidefinite Hermitian form \(\mathfrak h\) satisfying all three properties \[ \mathfrak h(V_1f,V_1f)=\mathfrak h(f,f),\qquad |\phi_N(f)|^2\le C_N\mathfrak h(f,f), \] \[ \mathfrak h(R^\sigma f,R^\sigma f) \le B_N\mathfrak h(f,f) \quad\hbox{for every } f\in\mathcal A_N, 	ag{25} \] where \(C_N,B_N\) are finite and \(\sigma\) is either one of the two original crossing signs. This holds separately at each level \(N\ge2\). **Proof.** Theorem 2 forces \(\mathfrak h(1,1)=0\). The last inequality in (25) then forces \(\mathfrak h(R^\sigma,R^\sigma)=0\), and the second forces \(\phi_N(R^\sigma)=0\). This contradicts (24). \(\square\) The contradiction uses the actual unit input and one literal crossing; it does not require a coupon depending on an unknown closed scalar. In particular no finite crossing bound exists for (17), even if a level-dependent exponential constant is allowed. The full prescribed one-crossing observation in the confluent basis is also explicit: \[ \phi_N(R^\sigma F_j)=R(c_j)^{-\sigma},\qquad \phi_N(R^\sigma G_j) =-\sigma\alpha_j R(c_j)^{-\sigma}. 	ag{26} \] Indeed \(\phi_N(F_jf)=(Tf)(c_j)\) and \(\phi_N(G_jf)=(Tf)'(c_j)\), so (26) follows from (24). The odd simple row uses only the first formula. Combining (16) with (26), for every integer \(n\), \[ \phi_N(R^\sigma V_nf) =\kappa^{-\sigma} \sum_{j\in\mathcal D_N} \lambda_{n+\sigma,j} \{A_j-(n+\sigma)\alpha_jB_j\} +\mathbf1_{N\ {m odd}}\kappa^{-\sigma} \lambda_{n+\sigma,*}A_* . 	ag{27} \] Thus the crossing which exposes the null value rows also retains the normal shears and their original quadratic phases. Equation (27) is a coherent scalar sum, not a positive sum or a lower estimate. ## 5. Scope and complete direct sources The general indefinite-closing obstruction, the positive Newton metric, and twist observation norms already have separate proofs. The added statements here are the explicit full \(F/G\) Gram and coordinate closing, the classification (20) with its largest quotient (18), and the source-specific incompatibility (25). Positive low-degree linearization alone does not determine the \(G_0\) coefficient extracted in (9). The positive Newton multiplication cone is also already known; no new positivity theorem for that cone is claimed here. Exact identities hold with arbitrary ordinary free spectator coefficients. The positive forms and inequalities mean a fixed complex specialization of those coefficients. Subsequent products, turns, and traces remain the original ones. Theorem 3 concerns exact \(V_1\) isometry on the whole space; it does not exclude controlled distortion on a restricted received source or a geometric norm with retained exponential costs. All three complete direct texts were read at the following pins and their used implications checked: * [Alternating physical-row linearization](research_physical_row_alternating_linearization.md), SHA256 326c55623da9155b6f5a0be4ab3e3b2584bdf7c568cd288d1e69569473c36342: full \(F/G\) basis, ordinary reproducers, and signed Jordan action. * [Original positive Newton Gram](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_newton_turn_positive_gram.md), SHA256 d8b21fa8db909120035e86e997a0e02cb84f8dce2dcf6fb244bb5c85c17e28a3: full Frobenius pairing, actual turn, and finite signed crossings. * [Original twist observations](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_original_twist_observation_tomography.md), SHA256 6885ad1b82b8f67ddda497f969337a9230b17925fd88b4326b0152dfdc738a1c: exact crossing values and first normals, including all levels. Only written proof, source-text reads, and metadata hashes were used. No mathematical program, numerical experiment, test, build, or compilation was run. Frozen sources and public manuscripts are unchanged.

title: Boundary energy of a connected Conway block
text:
# Boundary energy of a connected Conway block 21 November 2026. A connected collection of short pieces can be removed from the normalized Conway energy while retaining its exact full boundary map. This note proves a pointwise comparison, before the remaining boundary packets are optimized. The comparison factor is uniform in the level, the block size, and the chosen fixed filling coefficients. The boundary map itself remains coherent and marked. The theorem does not replace it by an operator norm or prove that its geometric closing coefficient is nonzero. ## 1. A block with clamped input and output packets Use the complete boundary spaces, original markings and normalized local maps of the [convex source theorem](research_convex_normalized_conway_source.md). Thus every leaf and linear or bilinear map has norm at most \(\sigma=1/16\). The per-vertex budgets and their original product \(B_{m tot}\) are retained. In particular a normalized product is the actual full Newton multiplication divided by its known local budget. All budgets are held fixed while boundary packets vary. No repeated-root derivative is discarded. Let \(\Omega\) be a nonempty connected set of vertices in the rooted compiler tree. It has one top vertex \(\omega\), with one outgoing boundary leg. Every child leg entering \(\Omega\) from below is a cut input leg. Write its clamped packet as \(u_j\), and assume \(\|u_j\|\le1\). Inputs may also be prescribed normalized leaf packets. Clamp the top output to a packet \(y\), with \(\|y\|\le1\), in the top output Hilbert space. All other packets \(z_v\), for \(v\in\Omega\setminus\{\omega\}\), are internal variables in their unit balls. In each local recursion put \(x_\omega=y\), \(x_v=z_v\) at internal vertices, and use \(u_j\) at cut inputs. Define \[ S_\Omega(z;u,y) =\sum_{v\in\Omega}\|\Phi_v((x_c)_c)-x_v\|^2,\qquad C_\Omega(u,y)=\min_{\|z_v\|\le1}S_\Omega(z;u,y). 	ag{1} \] When there are no internal variables, this is the displayed local squared residual itself. The block may contain the physical closing root. In that case its normalized local map is the original row \(L\), its output space is \(\mathbb C\), and its clamped output is \(y=0\). The root residual is then \(|Lx_{v_0}|^2\), exactly as in the original energy. For the estimates below one can also let this scalar \(y\) vary over its unit disk. Let \(F_\Omega(u)\) be the exact normalized composite obtained by performing the recursions inside \(\Omega\). It retains every original phase and all cut boundary coordinates. Since the cut inputs have norm at most one, every exact internal packet and \(F_\Omega(u)\) have norm at most \(\sigma\). ## 2. Internal elimination and the output Hessian **Theorem.** For each fixed clamped input \(u\), the internal minimum in (1) exists uniquely and is interior. The boundary value is smooth in the real and imaginary output coordinates, with \[  rac{63}{32}I\le D_y^2C_\Omega(u,y)\le2I. 	ag{2} \] Consequently, with \(c=63/64\), \[  oxed{\quad c\|y-F_\Omega(u)\|^2\le C_\Omega(u,y) \le\|y-F_\Omega(u)\|^2. \quad} 	ag{3} \] All constants are independent of \(N\), the number of block vertices, and the filling coefficients after the stated budgets are retained. **Proof.** First let every vertex output in \(\Omega\), including the top output, vary in its unit ball, while the cut inputs remain fixed. The residual Jacobian is \(-I+A\). Each child block has norm at most \(\sigma\), each row has at most two such blocks, and each child appears in at most one parent row. Hence \(\|A\|\le\sqrt2\sigma\le1/8\). The half-Hessian residual-curvature term is bounded in absolute value by \(\sigma(1+\sigma)\) times the squared variation norm: at a product it is \[ 2\operatorname{Re}\langle\mathcal R_v, \Phi_v(\xi_L,\xi_R)angle, \] and distinct parents have disjoint sibling pairs. This gives \[ I\le D^2S_\Omega\le3I 	ag{4} \] on these balls, by the same bounds \(2[(7/8)^2-1/8]>1\) and \(2[(9/8)^2+1/8]<3\). Clamping \(y\) retains (4) on the internal variables. At an internal vertex the half-gradient step for those variables is \[ z_v-	frac12(
abla_z S_\Omega)_v =\Phi_v-(D_v\Phi_{\operatorname{parent}(v)})^* \mathcal R_{\operatorname{parent}(v)}. \] Every internal vertex has its parent in \(\Omega\). This step has component norm at most \(\sigma+\sigma(1+\sigma)=33/256<1\), including when that parent is the clamped top. By (4) it is a contraction with factor \(1/2\). Its unique fixed point is the unique internal minimizer and is interior. The statement is immediate if there are no internal variables. At this interior minimum the internal Hessian block \(H_{zz}\) is positive definite, with \(H_{zz}\ge I\). The real implicit function theorem applied to \(
abla_zS_\Omega=0\) therefore gives a smooth minimizer as the parameters \((u,y)\) vary. The interior margin also gives a local extension at points where an input or output is on its unit sphere. Differentiating the stationary equations gives \[ D_y^2C_\Omega =H_{yy}-H_{yz}H_{zz}^{-1}H_{zy}. 	ag{5} \] The top variable appears only as minus its identity in the top residual, so \(H_{yy}=2I\). Moreover \[ H_{yz}=-2D_z\Phi_\omega,\qquad \|H_{yz}\|\le2\sqrt2\sigma. \] Only the internal children of the top occur in this row. There are at most two, and their derivative blocks have norm at most \(\sigma\). Thus \(\|H_{yz}\|^2\le8\sigma^2=1/32\). Formula (5) and \(H_{zz}^{-1}\le I\) prove (2). With no internal variables, the Hessian is exactly \(2I\). At \(y=F_\Omega(u)\), the exact recursion gives zero cost. The first output derivative is therefore zero there. The segment from this point to any allowed \(y\) stays in the unit ball. Integrating (2) twice along that segment proves (3). \(\square\) The output derivative has the concrete boundary-flux formula \[ 
abla_y C_\Omega(u,y) =2\{y-\Phi_\omega(z_*(u,y),u)\}. 	ag{6} \] Its half differs from \(y-F_\Omega(u)\) by at most \(\|y-F_\Omega(u)\|/64\), by integrating (2) once. Only output convexity, with the inputs clamped, has been asserted. Joint convexity in the cut inputs is false. For example, the actual Newton algebra has \(M(b_0,b_0)=b_0\). A single product vertex on the real input lines \(u_1=\alpha b_0\), \(u_2= eta b_0\), with fixed output \(y=t b_0\), has energy \[ |a\alpha eta-t|^2, \qquad a=1/b_\omega>0,\quad 0<t\le1. \] At \(\alpha= eta=0\) its real input Hessian has off-diagonal entries \(-2at\) and zero diagonal entries. It is indefinite. ## 3. Exact linear corridors When the clamped block is a chain of normalized linear maps \(A_i\), the boundary energy has an explicit formula. This includes turns and multiplication by a fixed retained packet, with every full Newton coordinate present. Suppose \[ x_0=u,\quad x_L=y,\qquad S=\sum_{i=1}^L\|x_i-A_ix_{i-1}\|^2,\qquad \|A_i\|\le\sigma. \] Put \[ P_i=A_LA_{L-1}\cdots A_{i+1},\quad P_L=I,\qquad W=\sum_{i=1}^LP_iP_i^*. \] Then \[ C(u,y)=\langle y-A_L\cdots A_1u,\, W^{-1}(y-A_L\cdots A_1u)angle. 	ag{7} \] Indeed the errors \(r_i=x_i-A_ix_{i-1}\) satisfy \(y-A_L\cdots A_1u=\sum_iP_ir_i\). The map on the right is surjective because \(P_L=I\). Its least-norm solution is \(r_i=P_i^*W^{-1}(y-A_L\cdots A_1u)\), as follows by orthogonality to its kernel. This proves (7) without ball constraints. The internal minimum with balls is interior by the preceding theorem. It satisfies the same strictly convex quadratic stationary equations, so it is also the unconstrained minimum and (7) is valid with the original balls. In particular \[ I\le W\le rac{256}{255}I,\qquad  rac{255}{256}I\le W^{-1}\le I. 	ag{8} \] These follow from \(\|P_i\|\le\sigma^{L-i}\) and a geometric series. No inverse of an individual \(A_i\) is used; the maps can be singular. The metric estimate concerns the residual from the exact transported center. It is not a lower bound on the norm of that center. ## 4. Several short blocks in the original source Choose any collection of pairwise vertex-disjoint connected blocks. Retain every block output and every cut input as boundary variables, except for the physical root output, which is fixed at zero if present. Eliminate all other variables inside the blocks. Original local terms outside the blocks remain in a nonnegative function \(A\). For fixed remaining boundary packets, exact elimination gives \[ E_{m red}=A+\sum_jC_{\Omega_j}(u_j,y_j). \] There is no remaining coupling through an eliminated variable: a vertex outside a connected block can see only that block's retained top output. Define the compressed residual energy \[ E_{m comp} =A+\sum_j\|y_j-F_{\Omega_j}(u_j)\|^2. 	ag{9} \] Each composite map uses the same normalized gates as before. In particular \(B_{m tot}\) is unchanged; no new budget is silently assigned to a fused map. Equation (3), together with \(A\ge0\), gives the pointwise inequalities \[ cE_{m comp}\le E_{m red}\le E_{m comp}. \] Taking minima over all remaining unit-ball variables proves \[ c\min E_{m comp}\le\min E_N\le\min E_{m comp}. 	ag{10} \] The factor \(c\) occurs once, independently of the number of blocks, because the energies add. No joint input convexity or convexity of \(E_{m comp}\) is used in this argument. Let \(\gamma=197/196\) be the source constant from the convex theorem. Its original scalar comparison and (10) imply \[  oxed{\quad cB_{m tot}^2\min E_{m comp}\le|K_N|^2 \le\gamma B_{m tot}^2\min E_{m comp}. \quad} 	ag{11} \] Thus absorbing any such collection of fixed short pieces preserves the original exponential rate with a constant loss independent of their number. This is a boundary comparison before the final minimization, not a replacement of the marked invariant by a norm of individual pieces. ## 5. What this removes, and what remains The internal energy of an arbitrary connected short block is comparable to its exact boundary residual with uniform constants. This removes an internal metric or assembly loss as a separate exponential obstacle. The fixed filling coefficients can enter the known per-gate budgets and the exact composite maps; all of those factors remain in (11). What remains is the asymptotic behavior of the compressed source with those actual coherent maps. The estimates do not supply a subexponential bound on an inverse map. Neither (3) nor (11) establishes the map's value on a geometric boundary field or a nonzero marked closing coefficient. A geometric lower certificate for the remaining boundary problem is still required for the finite-exception volume theorem. ## Complete direct source The sole direct proof source was read in full at the matching pin: | Source | SHA-256 | |---|---| | [Unweighted convex Conway source](research_convex_normalized_conway_source.md) | 6b89b4c6a67ef7a32cc41a5966c650f32de65d284ae7b70d94a71bddba21df3c | The clamped boundary problem, Schur estimate, corridor formula and assembly inequalities are proved above. Only written mathematics and text operations were used. No mathematical program, test, build, numerical iteration, git operation or previous-final edit was performed.

title: Conserved coideal channels with the original braid source
text:
# Conserved coideal channels with the original braid source 24 November 2026. Research note. Written proof. A particular conserved combination of the actual total generators has an exact degree-\(N\) polynomial on every complete-color tensor power. Its full matrix is a repeated companion matrix, including the Jordan directions at the exceptional parameters. For a stable exterior range of the auxiliary parameter, its conserved channels can be made orthogonal with metric logarithm of order at most the level. Pinching the original closing into these channels is exact against the original intertwining word. The closing is retained and is not made positive. The corresponding classical Hamiltonian is an explicit simultaneous conjugation flow. Its zero level gives the residual parabolic framing motion. These facts do not identify a selected quantum channel with a geometric period or establish a nonzero scalar coefficient. ## 1. Complete finite matrices and the conserved element Fix \(N\ge2\), width \(b\ge1\), and \[ q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\quad h=2\pi i/N,\quad x=-q^{-1},\quad \gamma=x^N=(-1)^{N+1},\quad \sqrt q=e^{\pi i/(2N)}. 	ag{1} \] Use the factorial basis of W, declared orthonormal for the estimates below. At the complete meridian \(M=1\), its actual generators are \[ K e_a=xQ^{-a}e_a,\quad E e_a=(Q^{-a}-1)e_{a-1},\quad F e_a=(1-Q^{a+1})e_{a+1}. 	ag{2} \] The absent arrows at \(a=0,N-1\) are zero. Here \(E\) is W's scaled \(\mathcal E\), not an unscaled unrolled generator. Retain the ordered coproducts \[ K_{12}=K_1K_2,\qquad E_{12}=E_1K_2+E_2,\qquad F_{12}=F_1+K_1^{-1}F_2. 	ag{3} \] Write their width-\(b\) iterates as \(\mathsf K,\mathsf E,\mathsf F\). Every literal unmarked checked braid word \(R\) commutes with all three, including its original signed crossing scalars. For an auxiliary scalar \(c\in\mathbb C\), define \[ B_c^{(b)}=\mathsf F-(\mathsf E-cI)\mathsf K^{-1},\qquad H_c^{(b)}=B_c^{(b)}-2I. 	ag{4} \] These commute with \(R\). The order in (4) is fixed. In particular \(H_c\mathsf K=-(2\mathsf K+\mathsf E-\mathsf F\mathsf K-cI)\); replacing \(\mathsf F\mathsf K\) by \(\mathsf K\mathsf F\) would change the finite operator. Direct substitution in (3) gives \[ B_c^{(b)}=(F_1-E_1K_1^{-1})\otimes I +K_1^{-1}\otimes B_c^{(b-1)},\qquad B_c^{(0)}=c. 	ag{5} \] Equivalently \(Y_c=B_c-cI\) satisfies \(\Delta Y_c=Y_c\otimes1+K^{-1}\otimes Y_c\). Since \(K\) is unitary and \(\|E\|,\|F\|\le2\), \[ \|\mathsf E\|,\|\mathsf F\|\le2b,\qquad \|B_c^{(b)}\|\le4b+|c|. 	ag{6} \] ## 2. A finite cyclic determinant with all zero arrows retained Define the monic polynomial \[ p_N(z)=\prod_{s^N=1}(z-s-q/s) =2q^{N/2}T_N\!\left( rac{z}{2\sqrt q}ight), \qquad q^{N/2}=i. 	ag{7} \] Here \(T_N\) is Chebyshev of the first kind. To verify (7), put \(z=\sqrt q(v+v^{-1})\). Both monic sides vanish when \(v=s/\sqrt q\), since \(v^N=-i\) and \(v^{-N}=i\). These \(N\) values of \(z\) are distinct: a collision of two different \(s,t\) would require \(st=q\), impossible after taking \(N\)-th powers. Thus the monic polynomials agree. On one head let \(S e_a=e_{a+1 mod N}\) and \(C e_a=Q^ae_a\). Formula (2) gives the exact identity \[ B_c^{(1)}=A(S)-T_c(S)C,\qquad A(s)=s+q/s,\qquad T_c(s)=Qs+q/s+cq. 	ag{8} \] Indeed \(F=S(1-QC)\), \(-EK^{-1}=qS^{-1}(1-C)\), and \(cK^{-1}=-cqC\). The two apparent cyclic boundary arrows vanish individually. No wrap term was inserted or removed in (8). Diagonalize the unitary cyclic shift \(S\). In that basis \(C\) is a single cyclic permutation. The determinant of \(z-A(S)+T_c(S)C\) has only its diagonal permutation and its complete-cycle permutation. Since \(T_c(s)/q=A(s^{-1})+c\) and \(q^N=-1\), this proves \[ \det(zI-B_c^{(1)}) =p_N(z)+(-1)^{N-1}\prod_{s^N=1}T_c(s) =p_N(z)+p_N(-c). 	ag{9} \] The argument is polynomial in \(c\); no coefficient is assumed nonzero. It includes \(N=2\). For example then \(p_2(z)=z^2-2i\) and \((B_c^{(1)})^2=(4i-c^2)I\). Cayley--Hamilton and \(p_N(-z)=(-1)^Np_N(z)\) yield \(p_N(B_c^{(1)})=\gamma p_N(c)I\). This is a polynomial matrix identity in the scalar parameter. Substitute the commuting tail matrix from (5) for that parameter and induct. The result is \[  oxed{\quad p_N(B_c^{(b)})=\gamma^b p_N(c)I,\qquad q_{N,b,c}(z):=p_N(z)-\gamma^bp_N(c).\quad} 	ag{10} \] This proof applies to the entire tensor power, without semisimplifying its quantum-group module. ## 3. Exact free companion form and its cost Put \(d_b=N^{b-1}\) and \(\mathfrak f_k=(Q;Q)_k=\prod_{a=1}^k(1-Q^a)\), \(\mathfrak f_0=1\). Consider the block Krylov matrix \[ \mathcal S_b=[\,e_0\otimes I_{d_b},\ B_c(e_0\otimes I_{d_b}), \ldots,B_c^{N-1}(e_0\otimes I_{d_b})\,]. 	ag{11} \] To reach first-head index \(k\) from zero in \(k\) steps, every step must use \(F_1\). Consequently (11) is block triangular with diagonal blocks \(\mathfrak f_k I_{d_b}\), all nonzero. Relation (10) now gives \[  oxed{\quad \mathcal S_b^{-1}B_c^{(b)}\mathcal S_b =\operatorname{Comp}(q_{N,b,c})\otimes I_{d_b}.\quad} 	ag{12} \] The companion convention is the basis \(1,z,\ldots,z^{N-1}\). Thus \(q_{N,b,c}\) is the minimal polynomial, and the characteristic polynomial is \(q_{N,b,c}^{\,d_b}\), for every \(c\). Every Jordan block of the scalar companion occurs \(d_b\) times. No normal channel is lost at a collision. Equivalently the full head space is free of rank \(d_b\) over \(A_{N,b,c}=\mathbb C[t]/q_{N,b,c}(t)\), and the full commutant of \(B_c\) is \[ \operatorname{End}_{A_{N,b,c}}(V_N^{\otimes b}) \simeq\operatorname{Mat}_{d_b}(A_{N,b,c}). 	ag{12a} \] Every original braid word lands in this algebra. If \(\gamma^bp_N(c)=-2i\), the substitution \(t=\sqrt q\,z\) identifies \(A_{N,b,c}\) with F's full Conway quotient \(\mathbb C[z]/(2T_N(z/2)+2)\), retaining its double-root normals. This does not identify the transported original closing with that quotient's canonical Frobenius functional or with a knot A-polynomial. There are controlled inverse bounds for (11), not merely a nonzero determinant. For \(T=B_c^{(b-1)}\), let the monic polynomials with commuting operator coefficients satisfy \[ D_0=I,\quad D_{-1}=0,\qquad D_{k+1}(z;T)=(z+qQ^kT)D_k(z;T) -q(1-Q^k)^2D_{k-1}(z;T). 	ag{13} \] The first-head tridiagonal entries give \(D_k(B_c;T)(e_0\otimes I)=\mathfrak f_k(e_k\otimes I)\). For fixed width and \(|c|\le C_*\), (6) and (13) bound the sum of coefficient norms of \(D_k\) by \(C_1^k\). Also sine complementation gives \[ |\mathfrak f_{N-1}|=N,\qquad |\mathfrak f_k|^{-1} =|\mathfrak f_{N-1-k}|/N\le2^{N-1-k}/N. 	ag{14} \] Expanding the identities after (13) expresses each coordinate block in the Krylov columns. Together with (6), this proves \[ \|\mathcal S_b\|+\|\mathcal S_b^{-1}\| \le \exp(C_{b,C_*}N). 	ag{15} \] All these bounds include the exceptional parameters. The recurrence (13) is an Al-Salam--Chihara specialization; no new recurrence or orthogonal-polynomial technique is claimed. The roots of (10) are simple except when its right side is a critical value of \(p_N\). For \(N\ge3\) these values are \(\pm2i\); for \(N=2\) only \(-2i\) is critical. At a critical value all multiple roots have multiplicity exactly two. Formula (12) therefore specifies the whole exceptional Jordan form, with block length at most two, rather than replacing it by its value quotient. These normal channels are generalized eigenspaces; this does not transport meridian or off-root quantum-parameter derivatives. ## 4. An orthogonal channel metric on a stable parameter range Assume \(4\le|c|\le C_*\). Choose \(w\) with \(w+w^{-1}=c/\sqrt q\) and \(|w|>1\), and choose \(\varepsilon^N=\gamma^b\), \(|\varepsilon|=1\). The roots are \[ \lambda_j=\sqrt q(\varepsilon wQ^j+ \varepsilon^{-1}w^{-1}Q^{-j}), \qquad 0\le j<N, \qquad |w|\ge2+\sqrt3. 	ag{16} \] They are distinct. For \(j
e k\), factoring their difference gives \[ |\lambda_j-\lambda_k| \ge(|w|-|w|^{-1})|Q^j-Q^k|, \quad \prod_{k
e j}|\lambda_j-\lambda_k| \ge N(|w|-|w|^{-1})^{N-1}. 	ag{17} \] Use the full spectral idempotents \[ \Pi_j=\prod_{k
e j}  rac{B_c-\lambda_kI}{\lambda_j-\lambda_k}, \qquad G_c=\sum_j\Pi_j^*\Pi_j. 	ag{18} \] Equations (6), (16)--(17) prove \(\|\Pi_j\|\le e^{C_{b,C_*}N}\). Their sum is the identity, so Cauchy--Schwarz also proves \[ N^{-1}I\le G_c\le N e^{C_{b,C_*}N}I,\qquad \|\log G_c\|=O_{b,C_*}(N). 	ag{19} \] Indeed \(G_c\Pi_j=\Pi_j^*\Pi_j=\Pi_j^*G_c\). The \(N\) full eigenspaces have dimension \(d_b\) and are exactly orthogonal in \(G_c\). Nothing inside a conserved eigenspace has been projected away. The estimates survive the explicit factorial coordinate adapter. If \(v_a=\mathfrak f_a e_a\), then \(Fv_a=v_{a+1}\), \(Ev_a=(1-Q^a)(Q^{-a}-1)v_{a-1}\), and \(K\) is unchanged. This is the undivided complete module with its scaled \(E\). The diagonal change and its inverse have norms \(e^{O(N)}\) by (14) and \(|\mathfrak f_a|\le2^a\). On fixed tensor width, transporting (19) to those raw physical coordinates still has logarithmic radius \(O(N)\). This is an exponential controlled adapter, not a polynomial equivalence of the two Hilbert metrics. The original diagonal pivot and cut commute with that adapter. For M's operator packets use the induced Hilbert--Schmidt metric \(\|A\|_{{m HS}(G_c)}=\|G_c^{1/2}AG_c^{-1/2}\|_{m HS}\). Its column-vectorization Gram is \(\overline{G_c}^{-1}\otimes G_c\), with logarithmic radius at most \(2\|\log G_c\|=O(N)\). Simultaneous conjugation transports multiplication and its original root row exactly. Putting this packet metric on the complete-color block and the identity metric on M's ordinary anchor block therefore lies in a known color-preserving window of the same \(O(N)\) order, enlarged if necessary. The head metric and the operator-packet metric have different dimensions. The polynomial (10) itself is asserted only at the complete meridian. At other colors the deleted lower arrow does not equal the corresponding cyclic coefficient; no ordinary-color or whole-meridian polynomial identity is inferred from (8). ## 5. The original closing and its exact channel sum Retain W's whole original source at this complete root: \[ P=T_0\otimes g^{\otimes(b-1)},\qquad T_0=e_0e_0^*,\quad g=K^{1-N},\qquad \Phi(O)=\varkappa_ eta\operatorname{Tr}(PO). 	ag{20} \] The framing/peripheral scalar \(\varkappa_ eta\) is unchanged. For a simple spectrum define \(P^{m diag}=\sum_j\Pi_jP\Pi_j\). Whenever \([O,B_c]=0\), cyclicity and \(\Pi_j\Pi_k=0\) give the exact identity \[  oxed{\quad \operatorname{Tr}(PO)=\sum_j\operatorname{Tr}(\Pi_jP\Pi_jO) =\operatorname{Tr}(P^{m diag}O). \quad} 	ag{21} \] In particular this applies to the literal unmarked braid word. All its conserved channels and every compressed closing remain. At exceptional parameters the primary idempotents, rather than individual eigenvalue quotients, give the same identity. The size-two blocks from (12) stay inside them. No near-collision version of (19) is claimed without a separate separation bound. For (19), the \(\Pi_j\) are orthogonal projections in the indicated head metric. Thus pinching also has the exact observation-norm consequences \[ \|P^{m diag}\|_{G_c	o G_c}\le\|P\|_{G_c	o G_c},\qquad \|P^{m diag}\|_{{m HS}(G_c)}\le\|P\|_{{m HS}(G_c)}. 	ag{22} \] The second inequality is the corresponding contraction of root-row dual norms. For the original row it is usable on the commuting subalgebra in (21), where the two rows agree. Neither matrix is asserted positive. General inserted clocks need not commute with \(B_c\); their off-diagonal channel terms must then be retained. Equation (21) is not an equality of all marked-current functionals. This distinction is essential at the original cut. In the simple-spectrum case there is nevertheless an exact source advantage: \([P^{m diag},B_c]=[P^{m diag},H_c]=0\). Thus its inner Ward boundary vanishes, while its pairing with every unmarked original braid is unchanged. For a general inserted \(O\), the exact correction is still \[ \operatorname{Tr}(PO)=\operatorname{Tr}(P^{m diag}O) +\operatorname{Tr}((P-P^{m diag})O). 	ag{22a} \] At a collision, primary pinching alone need not commute with the nilpotent part. The invariant-probe assertion is not extended to it. ## 6. The classical Hamiltonian and the finite flow Use W's regular Gauss symbols and ordered meridians \(H_j\). Their product is \[ G=H_b\cdots H_1=  egin{pmatrix}K&e\Kf&K^{-1}+ef\end{pmatrix},\qquad J= egin{pmatrix}1&-1\1&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad B_0=\operatorname{Tr}((I+J)G)=2K+e-Kf. 	ag{23} \] The ordered product follows directly from the triangular factors in W and G. For the scalar Hamiltonian \[ H_c=f-2-(e-c)/K=-(B_0-c)/K 	ag{24} \] its derivatives, inserted in W's three exact principal Ward fields, give simultaneous conjugation by \[ X_H=-J-	frac12H_cD,\qquad D=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1). 	ag{25} \] Indeed the coefficients are \(-1/K,1,(e-c)/K^2\); their commutator matrix has lower entry \(-1\), upper entry \(1\), and diagonal entries \(-1-H_c/2,1+H_c/2\). The Hamiltonian is conserved. On its level \(H_c=a\), put \(\lambda=a+2\) and \(M_\lambda=\left( egin{smallmatrix}\lambda&-1\1&0\end{smallmatrix}ight)\). Then \[ \operatorname{Tr}(M_\lambda G)=c,\quad X_a=-M_\lambda+\lambda I/2,\quad X_a^2=a(a+4)I/4,\quad H_j(r)=e^{rX_a}H_j(0)e^{-rX_a}. 	ag{26} \] This is the Hamiltonian trajectory while the required Gauss entries remain nonzero; the matrix-conjugation expression itself extends farther. On \(H_c=0\), this is conjugation by \(e^{-rJ}\). For the complete frame with cut meridian \(\mu=I+sJ\), it fixes that meridian and is precisely the \(r\)-translation of W. Multiplying the Hamiltonian by the fixed \(s\) gives W's normalization \(s\partial_r\). The other parabolic level is \(a=-4\). The actual finite generator in (4) is an inner derivation, unlike the different field-dependent current in I. Its exact flow is \[ U(r)=\exp(rH_c^{(b)}/h),\qquad P_r=U(r)PU(r)^{-1},\qquad \operatorname{Tr}(P_rR)=\operatorname{Tr}(PR),\qquad \|U(r)\|,\|U(r)^{-1}\|\le e^{C_{b,C_*}|r|N}. 	ag{27} \] This preserves the whole cut and tail pivot by transporting them. It does not make them invariant as individual matrices. In fact W's endpoint and pivot relations give, at this complete root, \[ \|[P,H_c]\|\le(4b-2)|Q-1|,\qquad ([P,H_c])_{10}=-(1-Q)g^{\otimes(b-1)}
e0. 	ag{28} \] Here \(10\) denotes the first-head block. To check the bound, use \([P,K_*^{-1}]=0\), \([P,H_c]=[P,F_*]-[P,E_*]K_*^{-1}\), the two cut arrows of size \(|Q-1|\), and tail norms at most \(2(b-1)\). Thus \(\|[P,H_c]/h\|\le4b-2\). Every meridian derivative and marked internal defect would still require its own retained source. ## 7. Coverage and remaining comparison Coideal minimal-polynomial and semisimplicity questions are already treated at odd-order roots by Shimizu--Sugitani, *Coideal subalgebras of quantum SL2 at roots of unity*, introduction and Theorem 4.10 ([primary text](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.10064v2)). No formula identification or proof technique from that paper is a premise here. The standard recurrence also appears in a different Casimir problem in F. The source-specific assertions proved here use the literal complete matrices at every \(N\), their free companion form with controlled cost, and the unchanged braid closing. G already constructs a different collective trace-Hamiltonian graph, with an initialized factorial kernel. W already supplies the weighted centralizer field, and C supplies a finite additive E-flow and relative endpoints. The present autonomous Hamiltonian does not identify those different finite currents or import their selected coefficients. In particular (26) is a principal interior statement, not a whole finite Egorov estimate through the highest-cut wall. It neither transports the central highest-cut augmentation to a noncentral parabolic point nor identifies a relative geometric framing chain. The auxiliary \(c\), the classical level \(a\), and a quantum eigenvalue \(\lambda_j\) are distinct data. No projection to \(\ker H_c\) is made. The full sum (21) can cancel. The metric cost is controlled exponential, not asserted negligible at the volume scale. No original scalar lower bound or finite-exception theorem is inferred. ## Complete inputs and closest coverage | Label | Complete text | Lines | SHA256 | | --- | --- | ---: | --- | | W | [Actual weighted Ward lift](research_actual_weighted_ward_centralizer_lift.md) | 345 | e689364ab8e756ef51f8da43a7ea86d84086afd6bf57ffbe0af1a4f508c2648a | | I | [The different nonderivation current](research_weighted_centralizer_current_and_inner_gauge.md) | 149 | 0e8f912fe7eff45b9a499619286988b47f5d8e2986b01b3cb8c0d52b5524d568 | | M | [Bounded two-color source metrics](research_main_color_block_regularized_compactness.md) | 357 | 34639ac940ec4b4cd2d290757b378ac846139c2e581e63410d9c5d627c822e1e | | C | [Original cut and relative E-Ward class](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/coherent_cut_obstruction_and_ward_relative_class.md) | 336 | 28141e28d4bc08a8acfa4cef9a8549ed7aadb1344f8796617e68282f7b351e4d | | G | [Initialized collective Gauss graph](research_actual_gauss_collective_canonical_graph.md) | 532 | 8ca0a51e9c2f3c11854e33809a349772d373b3da555286109acdbbc122e6b9bb | | F | [Earlier centered Fourier recurrence](research_centered_fourier_conway_compiler.md) | 405 | 0edbabe42280d70e4d5dcbcb55b188a3e773c14b99fbd212eb0fe8c5b176a413 | Only written mathematics, source reads and text/hash operations were used.
