title: Backward source transport and one forward pass solve the Conway minimum
text: # Backward source transport and one forward pass solve the Conway minimum 23 November 2026. Written research proof. The original normalized quartic admits a contracting iteration consisting of one backward source pass and one forced forward pass. Its contraction factor is at most \(15/2744\), independently of the quantum level and the size of the literal tree. After exact elimination of the closing turn corridor, the factor is at most \(5\zeta^2/C\), with the original, explicit endpoint coefficient \(\zeta\) and corridor factor \(C\). Thus that second factor decreases exponentially with the level. This is an iteration for the same minimum, not an evaluation of its geometric rate. Starting at zero makes its first forward pass the actual open-source evaluation. Full boundary packets, all their Hermite directions, the original closing, and every normalization budget remain. ## 1. The exact normalized source Fix \(N\ge2\). Use the literal normalized Conway tree of [C], with one packet in the complete Newton space \(H_N\cong\mathbb C^N\) at each proper vertex. Put \[ \sigma=1/16,\qquad \mathcal X=\bigoplus_v H_N,\qquad \mathcal D=\prod_v\{x_v:\|x_v\|\le1\}. \tag{1} \] Each normalized leaf, turn, and bilinear product \(\Phi_v\) has norm at most \(\sigma\). The original closing row is \(c\), supported at the top packet, with \(\|c\|\le\sigma\). Let \[ G(x)=\Phi(x)-x,\quad A_x=D\Phi(x),\quad S_x=I-A_x, \qquad E(x)=\|G(x)\|^2+|cx|^2. \tag{2} \] The positive budget \(B_{\rm tot}\), all original phases, and the marking are exactly those in [C]. If \(e_* =\min_{\mathcal D}E\), then \[ B_{\rm tot}^2e_*\le |K_N|^2 \le\frac{197}{196}B_{\rm tot}^2e_*. \tag{3} \] The unique minimizer is interior, and \(I\le D^2E\le3I\). All gradients are real gradients for \(\operatorname{Re}(u^*v)\); the local maps themselves are complex multilinear. We also use the following direct consequences of the literal tree: \[ \|A_x\|\le1/8,\quad \|S_x^{-1}\|\le\rho:=8/7, \qquad \|A_x-A_y\|\le\sigma\|x-y\|. \tag{4} \] The norm is the Hilbert direct-sum norm. For the last assertion, only products have a second derivative. At one product it is \(\Phi_v(h_L,k_R)+\Phi_v(k_L,h_R)\). The two child slots of distinct products are disjoint. Cauchy--Schwarz first on a sibling pair and then over those pairs gives \(\|D^2\Phi(x)[h,k]\|\le\sigma\|h\|\|k\|\). Integration along the feasible segment proves (4). Its first two bounds are also proved in [C]. ## 2. Exact inversion of the residual by a forward pass Given a forcing \(r=(r_v)_v\), define \(Y(r)\) from leaves to root by \[ Y(r)_v=\Phi_v((Y(r)_j)_{j\text{ child of }v})-r_v. \tag{5} \] This finite recursion is the unique solution of \(G(Y(r))=r\). It contains no solve for a simultaneous nonlinear system. If \(\|r\|\le\varepsilon\) and \(\sigma+\varepsilon\le1\), induction from the leaves gives \[ \|Y(r)_v\|\le\sigma+\varepsilon. \tag{6} \] In particular these fields are feasible. For any two forcings whose fields are feasible, (4), integrated between the fields, gives \[ \|Y(r)-Y(s)\|\le\rho\|r-s\|. \tag{7} \] Indeed \(G(u)-G(v)=-(u-v)+\int_0^1A_{v+t(u-v)}(u-v)\,dt\), whose norm is at least \(7\|u-v\|/8\). Feasibility in this argument comes from (6), before the Lipschitz estimate is used. For a known complex-linear row \(b_x\), the row \(d_x=b_xS_x^{-1}\) is computed in one backward pass. Its blocks obey \[ (d_x)_v=(b_x)_v+ (d_x)_{\operatorname{parent}(v)} D_v\Phi_{\operatorname{parent}(v)}(x), \tag{8} \] with the second term absent at a top vertex. This is the finite triangular identity \(d_x=b_x+d_xA_x\), not a dense inverse. ## 3. The original quartic: contraction by \(15/2744\) Set \[ d_x=cS_x^{-1},\qquad r_x=d_x^*(cx),\qquad \mathcal T(x)=Y(r_x). \tag{9} \] Everything on the right is known from the trial packets and original source tensors. Neither \(K_N\) nor the true field is an input. From (4) and the resolvent identity, \[ \|d_x\|\le1/14,\qquad \|d_x-d_y\|\le\sigma^2\rho^2\|x-y\| =\frac1{196}\|x-y\|. \tag{10} \] Since \(|cx|\le\sigma\) on \(\mathcal D\), \[ \|r_x\|\le1/224,\qquad \|r_x-r_y\|\le \left(\frac1{14}\frac1{16}+\frac1{196}\frac1{16}\right) \|x-y\|=\frac{15}{3136}\|x-y\|. \tag{11} \] Equations (6)--(7) now prove \[ \boxed{\quad \mathcal T(\mathcal D)\subset(15/224)\mathcal D, \qquad \operatorname{Lip}(\mathcal T)\le15/2744<1/180. \quad} \tag{12} \] The fixed point is exactly the original quartic minimizer. In fact \[ \tfrac12\nabla E(x)=-S_x^*G(x)+c^*cx=0 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad G(x)=d_x^*cx \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x=\mathcal T(x). \tag{13} \] The last equivalence uses uniqueness of the causal recursion (5). Contraction produces a unique feasible fixed point; its image bound makes it interior. Stationarity and [C]'s convexity identify it with the same minimum appearing in (3). For the scalar dual problem of [S], fix \(|\lambda|\le\sigma\) and put \[ \mathcal T_\lambda(x)=Y(d_x^*\lambda),\qquad J_\lambda(x)=\|G(x)\|^2+2\operatorname{Re}(\bar\lambda cx). \tag{14} \] The same forcing bound applies, while the variation of \(cx\) is now absent. Therefore \[ \mathcal T_\lambda(\mathcal D)\subset(15/224)\mathcal D, \qquad \operatorname{Lip}(\mathcal T_\lambda)\le1/2744. \tag{15} \] Its fixed point solves \(-S_x^*G(x)+c^*\lambda=0\), and hence is the unique inner minimizer in [S]. This supplies a faster certified field iteration for that already established scalar response. ## 4. The exactly eliminated closing corridor Suppose the literal tree has a highest binary product. Eliminate only its output and the turns above it exactly as in [F]. The remaining variables are all packets strictly below that product, including its two input packets. Their residual still has the form \(G=\Phi-x\), on a forest, with the same bounds (4). The reduced objective is exactly \[ F(x)=\|G(x)\|^2+|g(x)|^2, \qquad g(x)=x_L^{\mathsf t}B x_R/\sqrt C, \qquad \|B\|=\zeta,\quad t:=\zeta/\sqrt C. \tag{16} \] Here \(C=1+\nu_{\rm corr}\) is the explicit inclusive corridor factor of [F]. In the original notation, \(B=(\eta/b_*)J\) or \((\eta/b_*)e_0e_0^{\mathsf t}\), according to the original closing, and \(\eta=\chi/(b_{\rm root}\prod_i\beta_i)\). All corridor budgets, the physical scalar \(\chi\), and the product budget \(b_*\) remain in \(\zeta=|\eta|/b_*\). In particular \(C\ge1\), \(\zeta\le1/256\), and [F] proves that the minimum in (16) is the original full minimum \(e_*\). On the feasible balls, \[ |g|\le t,\qquad \|Dg\|\le\sqrt2t, \|D^2g\|\le t. \tag{17} \] Define now \[ d_x=Dg(x)S_x^{-1},\qquad r_x=d_x^*g(x),\qquad \mathcal T_F(x)=Y(r_x). \tag{18} \] The backward pass (8) starts with the known row \(Dg(x)\), supported at the two input packets. The scalar \(g(x)\) is also a known trial contraction. The resolvent identity and (17) give \[ \|d_x\|\le\rho\sqrt2t,\qquad \operatorname{Lip}(d)\le t(\rho+\rho^2\sqrt2\sigma). \tag{19} \] Consequently \[ \|r_x\|\le\rho\sqrt2t^2\le2t^2,\qquad \operatorname{Lip}(r)\le t^2(3\rho+\rho^2\sqrt2\sigma). \tag{20} \] First (6) proves feasibility; then (7) proves \[ \boxed{\quad \mathcal T_F(\mathcal D)\subset(\sigma+2t^2)\mathcal D, \qquad \operatorname{Lip}(\mathcal T_F) \le\left(\frac{192}{49}+\frac{32\sqrt2}{343}\right)t^2 \le5\zeta^2/C\le5/65536<1/13000. \quad} \tag{21} \] As in (13), its fixed points are exactly stationary points of (16). The eliminated objective is strongly convex by [F], so the fixed point is its unique minimum. The exact corridor formulas then recover all eliminated packets, with their ball constraints inactive. For a fixed literal tree with a product, [F] also gives \[ \zeta\le\exp\{-2G_{\rm Cat}N/\pi+O(\log N)\}. \tag{22} \] Thus the contraction bound in (21) is at most \(\exp\{-4G_{\rm Cat}N/\pi+O(\log N)\}\). This is a convergence bound, not a lower bound for the source. If there is no product, [F]'s corridor elimination is already exact with no remaining optimization. A zero closing is likewise harmless. ## 5. What the passes do and do not remove Each iteration uses the actual local derivatives in one backward pass and the actual local gates in one forward pass. Their number is linear in the number of literal vertices. The packet dimension remains \(N\); no bound independent of \(N\) is asserted for tensor arithmetic, storage, bit complexity, or the precision needed to resolve a small scalar. The causal compositions can have higher degree than four. The objective being minimized, rather than this iteration map, is the original quartic. For any of these contractions with factor \(q<1\), \[ \|x_j-x_*\|\le q^j\|x_0-x_*\|, \qquad \|x_j-x_*\|\le\frac{\|x_{j+1}-x_j\|}{1-q}. \tag{23} \] These are absolute field bounds. In particular they do not supply relative precision for an exponentially small minimum or a nonzero geometric coefficient. At \(x=0\), the frozen scalar forcing is zero for both full objectives. Thus \(\mathcal T(0)=a\), and \(\mathcal T_F(0)=a_{\rm below}\): the first forward pass is precisely the true open recursion. No difficulty in the coherent closing is removed by naming it a field iteration. There are nevertheless direct value certificates. The eliminated objective has \(D^2F\le3I\): in the Schur formula of [F], test the eliminated variation by zero and use [C]'s upper Hessian bound. Consequently, for \(q=5t^2\), \[ F(u)-\frac{3\|\mathcal T_F(u)-u\|^2}{2(1-q)^2} \le e_*\le F(u). \tag{24} \] This follows from (23) and Taylor's theorem at the minimizer. Restoring the original source uses (3), with its unchanged \(B_{\rm tot}^2\). For a sharper comparison of minimum values, begin at the known forward field \(u_0=a_{\rm below}=\mathcal T_F(0)\), and let \(u_j=\mathcal T_F^j(u_0)\). The lower Hessian bound \(m=41/32\), the upper bound \(3\), and [F]'s estimate \(F(u_0)-e_*\le t^2F(u_0)/82\) give \[ 0\le F(u_j)-e_* \le\frac{3}{m}q^{2j}(F(u_0)-e_*) \le\frac{48}{1681}t^2q^{2j}\frac{|k|^2}{C}. \tag{25} \] Indeed strong convexity bounds \(\|u_0-u_*\|^2\) by \(2(F(u_0)-e_*)/m\), then (23) and the upper Hessian bound apply. This includes zeros. Each extra pass pair therefore improves the minimum approximation by two powers of \(q\). It does not improve the previous comparison of \(CB_{\rm tot}^2e_*\) with \(|K_N|^2\): \(F(u_0)=|k|^2/C\) already evaluates the same coherent source exactly. ## Complete sources and coverage The complete proof inputs are [C] and [F], at the matching pins below. [C] supplies the original normalized tensors, source comparison and convexity; [F] supplies the exact original corridor elimination, endpoint form, constants and exponential estimate (22). The two-pass iteration and its contraction bounds are proved here. | Label | Complete source | SHA256 | |---|---|---| | C | [Normalized quartic](research_convex_normalized_conway_source.md) | 6b89b4c6a67ef7a32cc41a5966c650f32de65d284ae7b70d94a71bddba21df3c | | F | [Explicit corridor factor](research_conway_explicit_corridor_minimum_factor.md) | 85d482ef7121621447ea5ec2b158c9445d413add7495700964792d205a224938 | The following complete comparison texts were also read at matching pins: | Complete comparison | SHA256 | |---|---| | [S: scalar cap response](research_conway_scalar_cap_response.md) | 6b9b73ae429713bdff63120a9841c06d2311d249f058f3da6b1f4e89dbfaecfb | | [Source normal and Gauss--Newton](research_conway_source_normal_gauss_newton_certificate.md) | 36cea2a5e40cc515e0034e91f41eeb23cb75f57d0f4750d5d341f2dcbd9081f3 | | [Residual transport and finite repair](research_conway_source_visible_residual_transport.md) | 0d344301b0df65246551cf81498eff84582f796a03271b201f8fbba6c7742007 | | [Compressed convex source](research_conway_compressed_convex_source.md) | 065989bd50a891d1e3a67ce7b556921a8050ac83f019b8ba27360a6386a2189c | | [Internal-edge scalar response](research_conway_internal_edge_scalar_response.md) | a9f55feb64ed941faced7ecd1eb0baa4f1a4eb7f6b85aeeb7827113c945aa7a2 | Those notes already provide scalar duality, the stationary identity, finite residual repairs, and other contracting optimizations. The Gauss--Newton occurrence of \(1/2744\) bounds one displacement; it is not the contraction (15). The compressed objective is a different reduction. No general novelty is asserted for alternating forward and adjoint passes or for contraction methods. Only written mathematics and text operations were used; no mathematical programs or tests ran.

title: A quartic source minimum on the internal Conway edges
text:
# A quartic source minimum on the internal Conway edges 21 November 2026. Earlier finals and public manuscripts remain unchanged. Retaining both inputs of each binary product permits every other packet to be removed exactly. The reduced objective is still a polynomial of degree at most four. Its coefficients require only constant linear-corridor metrics and one scalar root response; there is no linear solve depending on the trial field. If there are \(p\ge1\) binary products, this first step leaves exactly \(2p\) packets and preserves the minimum exactly. Fixing the \(p+1\) known leaf inputs then leaves only \(p-1\) full packets, one on each connection between binary products. The latter minimum may change, but satisfies the same original source comparison. In the literal Conway compiler all corridor weights are explicit positive scalars. This is a simplification of the finite variational problem, not a new geometric lower bound. ## 1. Which original variables are retained Use the normalized full source from the convex theorem. At level \(N\), every proper packet belongs to the complete Newton space \(H_N\cong\mathbb C^N\), including its repeated-Casimir directions. There are \(s\) proper vertices. A vertex is a prescribed leaf, a constant linear gate, or a bilinear product. The original normalized closing is the row \(c\). The energy is \[ E(x)=\sum_{v\ {m proper}} \|\Phi_v((x_j)_{j	ext{ child of }v})-x_v\|^2 +|cx_{m top}|^2 . 	ag{1} \] Every trial packet lies in its unit ball. Each normalized leaf, linear or bilinear map and closing row has norm at most \(\sigma=1/16\). A constant linear gate may depend on \(N\) and the fixed source data, but not on any trial packet. The original budgets and their product \(B_{m tot}\) are fixed. The complete source theorem gives \[ I\le D_{\mathbb R}^2E\le3I,\qquad \left(x-	frac12
abla E(x)ight)_v \in rac{33}{256}\overline{\mathbb B}, 	ag{2} \] and, with \(\gamma=197/196\), \[ B_{m tot}^2\min E\le |K_N|^2 \le\gamma B_{m tot}^2\min E . 	ag{3} \] All gradients use the real inner product \(\operatorname{Re}\sum_vh_v^*k_v\). Let \(p\) be the number of binary vertices. Retain the output packet at each of their two immediate child vertices. Call this list \(u\), and call every other proper packet \(z\). These \(2p\) child occurrences are distinct: a vertex has exactly one parent. If a child is itself binary, its output and its parent's input are the same variable and are counted once. The top proper packet is never retained. Thus \[ \#u=2p\le s-1\quad(p\ge1). 	ag{4} \] When \(p=0\), retain no variable. **Theorem.** The exact partial minimum \[ F(u)=\min_{\|z_v\|\le1}E(u,z) 	ag{5} \] is a real polynomial of degree at most four. Its eliminated minimizer is unique, strictly interior, and polynomial of degree at most two in the retained real coordinates. On the retained product of balls, \[ I\le D^2F\le3I . 	ag{6} \] Its half-gradient step stays in the \(33/256\) packet balls and contracts by \(1/2\). The exact minimum in (3) may be replaced by \(\min F\). For \(p=0\), the reduced problem is a constant with no optimization. The explicit formulas below evaluate \(F\) without a trial-dependent matrix inverse. ## 2. Why the inner quadratic system has constant coefficients By construction, both inputs of every bilinear gate are retained. Thus no omitted variable occurs as an input of a bilinear map. Every full residual in (1), including the closing component, is jointly affine in \(z\), with constant coefficient matrix: \[ E(u,z)=\|Az+b(u)\|^2 . 	ag{7} \] The vector \(b\) is polynomial of degree at most two. For example an omitted binary output contributes its prescribed bilinear forcing \(\Phi_v(u_L,u_R)\) and minus that output variable. A retained binary output has the same forcing but its negative output is already part of \(b\). All remaining gates are linear or constant. The principal Hessian bounds in (2) imply \[ 	frac12I\le A^*A\le	frac32I . 	ag{8} \] These bounds hold for the entire unconstrained inner quadratic problem, because its Hessian is independent of \(z\). For fixed feasible \(u\), the map \[ z\longmapsto z-	frac12
abla_zE(u,z) 	ag{9} \] sends the omitted product of balls into its strict \(33/256\) contraction, by the omitted components of (2). Its derivative has norm at most \(1/2\), by (8). Iteration within those balls therefore has a unique fixed point. It is stationary for the unconstrained quadratic, so \[ z_*(u)=-(A^*A)^{-1}A^*b(u) 	ag{10} \] is that point and is feasible. This proves the inactive-ball assertion and its uniform interior margin. Since \(A\) is constant, \(z_*\) has degree at most two, and \[ F(u)=b(u)^*\! \left[I-A(A^*A)^{-1}A^*ight]b(u) 	ag{11} \] has degree at most four. Equation (11) proves the degree claim; it need not be used to assemble a dense projection. The difference from retaining only one child per product is important. In that reduction the omitted child enters a product with a retained child, so the inner matrix depends on the retained field. Here the inner matrix is constant. ## 3. Constant corridor metrics give an explicit formula The following description avoids the dense matrix in (11). Start at each prescribed leaf or binary gate and follow its output upward through the subsequent linear gates. Stop when the output is a retained packet, or when the closing root is reached. Every original residual belongs to exactly one such block. Distinct blocks share only their retained boundary packets. At the initial gate let \[ f(u)=  egin{cases} a,&	ext{for its prescribed normalized leaf},\ \Phi_v(u_L,u_R),&	ext{for its binary product}. \end{cases} 	ag{12} \] The linear maps above it are \(A_1,\ldots,A_m\), with \(\|A_i\|\le\sigma\). Write \(x_0\) for the initial gate output and \(x_i\) for the subsequent linear outputs. ### A block ending at a retained packet Let \(x_m=y\) be its retained top packet. The block energy is \[ \|x_0-f(u)\|^2+ \sum_{i=1}^m\|x_i-A_ix_{i-1}\|^2 . 	ag{13} \] For \(m=0\), this means simply \(\|y-f(u)\|^2\); in particular adjacent binary gates share this one packet. Define \[ P_i=A_mA_{m-1}\cdots A_{i+1},\quad P_m=I,\quad P=P_0,\qquad W=\sum_{i=0}^mP_iP_i^* . 	ag{14} \] Its exact eliminated cost is \[  oxed{\quad (y-Pf(u))^*W^{-1}(y-Pf(u)). \quad} 	ag{15} \] To verify it, put \(r_0=x_0-f(u)\) and \(r_i=x_i-A_ix_{i-1}\). Then \(y-Pf(u)=\sum_iP_ir_i\). The least-norm errors are \[ r_i=P_i^*W^{-1}(y-Pf(u)). 	ag{16} \] They are orthogonal to the kernel of the displayed surjective error map, since \(P_m=I\). Thus they give the unconstrained minimum. The omitted balls are inactive by Section 2, so this is also the original constrained minimum. The metric is constant and obeys \[ I\le W\le rac{256}{255}I. 	ag{17} \] This follows from \(\|P_i\|\le\sigma^{m-i}\) and a geometric series. No inverse of any individual \(A_i\) is used. ### The block ending at the original closing row There is exactly one root block. Its energy is (13), with \(x_m\) now omitted, together with \(|cx_m|^2\). Put \[ b_i=cP_i,\qquad D=1+\sum_{i=0}^m\|b_i\|^2,\qquad s(u)=cP f(u). 	ag{18} \] The exact root cost is the scalar expression \[  oxed{\quad |s(u)|^2/D.\quad} 	ag{19} \] Indeed \(cx_m=s(u)+\sum_ib_ir_i\), and minimizing \(\sum_i\|r_i\|^2+|s(u)+\sum_ib_ir_i|^2\) gives \[ r_i=-b_i^*s(u)/D . 	ag{20} \] Substitution proves (19); inactivity of the balls again identifies it with the constrained minimum. The scalar denominator satisfies \[ 1\le D\le rac{256}{255}. 	ag{21} \] Here \(\|b_i\|\le\sigma^{m-i+1}\). The row \(c\), every \(A_i\), and their original phases remain in (18). The symbol \(s(u)\) is a known scalar polynomial computed from this local block; it is not an unknown invariant inserted into the coefficients. For \(p\ge1\), the initial gate of the root block is the highest binary gate, so (19) is a bilinear square with a constant scalar weight. For \(p=0\), the root block starts at the sole leaf; (19) evaluates the whole minimum. Summing (15) over the nonroot blocks and adding (19) is the desired explicit \(F\). All matrices \(W^{-1}\) and the scalar \(D^{-1}\) can be computed once per level from the known linear operators. Evaluating \(F\) at a trial field then uses only known quadratic forms and the original linear and bilinear maps. There is no trial-dependent inner solve. Each \(f(u)\) in (12) has degree at most two. Thus these explicit expressions also prove directly that \(F\) is quartic, even when the original tree contains arbitrarily long linear corridors. They preserve the same \(B_{m tot}\); no new budget is assigned to \(Pf\). ### In the literal Conway compiler the metrics are scalar Its only unary operation is the normalized turn \(A_i=J/ eta_i\), where \( eta_i\) is its original positive budget. Since \(J\) is unitary and \(J^2=I\), put \[ ho_i=\prod_{h=i+1}^m eta_h^{-1},\qquad P_i=ho_iJ^{m-i},\qquad w=\sum_{i=0}^mho_i^2. 	ag{21a} \] Then \(W=wI\). The costs (15) and (19) become respectively \[  rac{\|y-ho_0J^mf(u)\|^2}{w},\qquad  rac{|cho_0J^mf(u)|^2}{1+\|c\|^2w}. 	ag{21b} \] Every denominator is a known positive scalar. Thus the actual reduced objective is a weighted sum of squared bilinear residuals and one squared scalar closing. No matrix inverse, even a constant one, is needed for its corridor coefficients. ## 4. Convexity, the inward step, and the original source The stationary inner solution (10) is smooth on a neighborhood of the retained balls. Differentiating its stationary equations gives the usual real Schur complement \[ D^2F=H_{uu}-H_{uz}H_{zz}^{-1}H_{zu}, \qquad H=D^2E(u,z_*(u)). 	ag{22} \] For a retained variation \(h\), \[ h^{\mathsf T}D^2Fh =\min_k(h,k)^{\mathsf T}H(h,k). 	ag{23} \] The lower bound in (2) gives at least \(\|h\|^2\); choosing \(k=0\) gives at most \(3\|h\|^2\). This proves (6), including boundary points by the smooth formula. The inward step needs more than the Schur bound. The envelope identity, because the omitted gradient is zero, is \[ 
abla F(u)= 
abla_uE(u,z_*(u)). 	ag{24} \] Thus \(u-
abla F(u)/2\) is exactly the retained component of the original full half-gradient step at the feasible field \((u,z_*(u))\). Equation (2) puts every component in its \(33/256\) ball. Averaging (6) along a segment gives the same contraction factor \(1/2\) as in the full problem. Consequently the reduced minimum is unique and interior. Exact partial minimization and (3) now give \[ B_{m tot}^2\min F\le |K_N|^2 \le\gamma B_{m tot}^2\min F . 	ag{25} \] The equality of minima is exact, not merely a comparison by the corridor metric constants. The constants (17) and (21) describe the explicit coefficients of the reduced polynomial. ## 5. Only the internal connections need remain free Suppose \(p\ge1\). Suppress the unary corridors only for counting. The resulting rooted binary tree has \(p\) binary vertices and \(p+1\) prescribed leaves. Of its \(2p\) inputs, exactly \(p+1\) come from a leaf through unary gates; the other \(p-1\) come from a nontop binary output through unary gates. For each leaf block, fix its retained endpoint to its known exact center \(y=Pa\), using (12)--(15). These are prescribed leaf transports, independent of every free packet. They have norm at most \(\sigma\), so the restriction is feasible. Each such block now contributes exactly zero. No output of a binary product is fixed at its unknown true value. Let \(\widetilde F\) be this restriction of \(F\), and write \[ e_*=\min E,\qquad \widetilde e_*=\min\widetilde F. 	ag{26} \] It is quartic on precisely \(p-1\) full packets, or \(2N(p-1)\) real coordinates. Its Hessian remains between \(I\) and \(3I\), by taking the corresponding principal restriction of (6). Its free half-gradient components are those of the full step used in (24), with the leaf inputs fixed. They therefore remain in their \(33/256\) balls and contract by \(1/2\). The minima need not be equal. The restricted feasible set gives \(e_*\le\widetilde e_*\). On the other hand, the true normalized field satisfies every prescribed leaf transport. Using its internal connection packets in the restricted problem, and then minimizing the omitted packets, gives \[ e_*\le\widetilde e_* \le |K_N/B_{m tot}|^2. 	ag{27} \] Combining this with (3) yields the unchanged source sandwich \[  oxed{\qquad B_{m tot}^2\widetilde e_*\le |K_N|^2 \le\gamma B_{m tot}^2\widetilde e_* . \qquad} 	ag{28} \] This includes zeros. The comparison uses the same normalization budget and the same \(\gamma=197/196\); it does not multiply a separate loss for each clamped leaf. For \(p=1\), there is no remaining minimization: the two known leaf transports enter the sole product, followed by (19). For \(p=0\), the entire source is the single linear chain already evaluated by (19). These statements evaluate the stated finite source expressions; they assert no asymptotic estimate. ## 6. Scope and complete proof sources Every retained packet is still the full \(H_N\). Omitted packets were minimized over all their physical coordinates; their effect remains in (15) and (19). This is not a semisimple quotient or a deletion of Hermite directions. The smaller one-child reduction retains \(p\) packets, but its exact least-squares objective generally has variable coefficients and is rational. The corresponding unweighted compressed objective may have degree above four. The present exact partial minimum retains \(2p\) packets to preserve the quartic degree and constant corridor metrics. The additional prescribed-leaf restriction reduces this to \(p-1\) packets while preserving the source comparison, rather than preserving the numerical minimum. All linear maps in the corridors must be independent of trial packets. A bilinear gate cannot be reclassified by silently fixing one of its variational inputs at its true value. Nor does algebraically expanding a crossing power preserve a previously chosen normalization budget if it changes the compiler tree. The reduction evaluates no hyperbolic exponential rate and supplies no additional geometric lower certificate. An exponentially small minimum still requires relative control; uniform conditioning alone does not supply it. Degree-four exactness of a new sum-of-squares or semidefinite relaxation is not inferred from the reduced objective's convexity. The original lifted certificates remain available. Both complete proof sources were read at the matching pins: | Source | SHA-256 | |---|---| | [Normalized complete source](research_convex_normalized_conway_source.md) | 6b89b4c6a67ef7a32cc41a5966c650f32de65d284ae7b70d94a71bddba21df3c | | [Connected-block boundary energy](research_connected_conway_block_boundary_energy.md) | 426b0eba0c7f4c502cf2b82052daf4d5a224ad8ec8419b3e2d8a624771f192ae | The complete matching orthogonal-elimination, compressed-source and source-normal notes were read for coverage, at pins aa53b79685296193d5bf7fc66e53f3a3fbe03fc72a36481fb3aee23afe2ae113, 065989bd50a891d1e3a67ce7b556921a8050ac83f019b8ba27360a6386a2189c, and 36cea2a5e40cc515e0034e91f41eeb23cb75f57d0f4750d5d341f2dcbd9081f3. The corridor response itself is already in the connected-block theorem. The additional assembly here is the constant-coefficient inner system, the \(2p\)-packet quartic formula, its prescribed-leaf reduction to \(p-1\) packets with the same source comparison, and the preserved convexity and inward iteration. No novelty is claimed for least squares or Schur complements. Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used. No mathematical program, numerical experiment, test, build, git operation or earlier-final edit was performed.

title: A quartic source minimum at the branching products
text:
# A quartic source minimum at the branching products 21 November 2026. Research note. Earlier finals and public manuscripts remain unchanged. After the prescribed leaf transports have been fixed, many remaining products are linear in the unknown boundary packets. They can be eliminated exactly with constant coefficients. Only a product whose two inputs both come from other products needs nonlinear variables. If there are \(q\) such products, the quartic minimum needs only \(2q\) full boundary packets. Its minimum and original source comparison are unchanged. Its Hessian still lies between \(I\) and \(3I\), and its half-gradient step is an inward contraction. The eliminated linear responses require no solve depending on a trial packet. Their coherent action remains part of the coefficients. ## 1. Start from the already clamped source Use the source theorem on the internal Conway edges. Fix a level \(N\ge2\) and a literal expression with \(p\ge1\) binary products. Each packet belongs to the full \(N\)-dimensional Newton boundary space \(H_N\), including all repeated-Casimir directions. The original positive packet norm is used. That theorem first eliminates the unary corridors and then fixes each leaf-to-product input at its known normalized transport. There remain \(p-1\) packet variables \(y_e\), one for each connection from a nontop product to its next product ancestor. They lie in their unit balls. Denote the resulting objective by \(\widetilde F(y)\). Its original normalization satisfies \[ B_{m tot}^{\,2}\min\widetilde F\le |K_N|^2 \le\gamma B_{m tot}^{\,2}\min\widetilde F, \qquad \gamma= rac{197}{196}. 	ag{1} \] The original budget \(B_{m tot}\), closing row and markings are fixed. The complete real Hessian and half-gradient bounds are \[ I\le D^2\widetilde F\le3I,\qquad \left(y-	frac12
abla\widetilde F(y)ight)_e \in rac{33}{256}\overline{\mathbb B}. 	ag{2} \] The half-gradient map contracts by \(1/2\). Gradients use the real inner product \(\operatorname{Re}\sum_e h_e^*k_e\). Here is the local form of the same objective. Let \(v_*\) be the highest product. For each product \(v\), its two inputs \(z_{v,L},z_{v,R}\) are either known leaf transports or the appropriate variables \(y_e\). Its normalized bilinear map is \(\Phi_v\). There are known constant linear corridor maps \(P_v\), positive matrices \(W_v\), a known closing row \(c\), and a positive scalar \(D_*\), such that \[  egin{split} \widetilde F(y) ={}&\sum_{v
e v_*} \|y_{e(v)}-P_v\Phi_v(z_{v,L},z_{v,R})\|_{W_v^{-1}}^2\ &+ rac{|cP_{v_*}\Phi_{v_*}(z_{v_*,L},z_{v_*,R})|^2}{D_*}. \end{split} 	ag{3} \] Here \(e(v)\) is the outgoing internal connection of \(v\), and \(\|w\|_H^2=w^*Hw\). Formula (3) is precisely the constant-corridor and scalar-root formula from the direct source. All omitted leaf-block costs are zero at their prescribed centers. ## 2. Count the products that remain bilinear Classify a product by the number of its inputs represented by internal variables: * With no internal input, its output expression is a known constant. * With one internal input, its output expression is a known linear function of that packet, because its other input is prescribed. * With two internal inputs, its output expression remains bilinear. Let \(u\) count the middle class and \(q\) the last class. Every nontop product contributes exactly one internal connection to one input of a product above it. Therefore \[ p-1=u+2q. 	ag{4} \] In particular \(2q\le p-1\). Retain the input packet on each of the two incoming internal connections of every product in the last class. These \(2q\) packets are distinct, since a product output has only one parent. Call their list \(w\), and call the other \(p-1-2q\) packets \(z\). The classification is made from the expression tree and the already prescribed leaf inputs. No unknown internal product output is set to its true value. **Theorem.** The exact partial minimum \[ F_{m br}(w)=\min_{\|z_e\|\le1}\widetilde F(w,z) 	ag{5} \] is a real polynomial of degree at most four on \(2q\) full packets, or \(4Nq\) real coordinates. Its inner minimizer is unique and interior. On the retained product of balls, \[ I\le D^2F_{m br}\le3I. 	ag{6} \] Its half-gradient step stays in the \(33/256\) packet balls and contracts by \(1/2\). Its minimum equals that of \(\widetilde F\) exactly. Consequently \[  oxed{\quad B_{m tot}^{\,2}\min F_{m br}\le |K_N|^2 \le\gamma B_{m tot}^{\,2}\min F_{m br}. \quad} 	ag{7} \] All constants and the budget are those in (1). ## 3. A constant linear system removes all other packets Every input of a product with two internal inputs has been retained. No omitted packet can therefore occur in a product with another variable input. The one-input products in Section 2 are already known linear maps. Taking constant positive square roots of the metrics in (3), and including its scalar closing component, gives the exact residual form \[ \widetilde F(w,z)=\|Az+b(w)\|^2. 	ag{8} \] The complex matrix \(A\) is constant in both \(w,z\). The vector \(b(w)\) is polynomial of degree at most two. It uses the actual normalized products, fixed leaf packets, corridor metrics and closing row; no coefficient is an unknown knot value. If \(z\) is nonempty, (2) implies \[ 	frac12 I\le A^*A\le	frac32 I. 	ag{9} \] For each feasible \(w\), consider the partial half-gradient map \[ z\longmapsto z-	frac12
abla_z\widetilde F(w,z). 	ag{10} \] Its components are components of the full map in (2), so it sends the omitted product of balls into their \(33/256\) balls. Its derivative has norm at most \(1/2\), by (9). The iteration converges to a unique interior fixed point. Since (8) is a strictly convex quadratic in \(z\), this is its unconstrained stationary point: \[ z_*(w)=-(A^*A)^{-1}A^*b(w). 	ag{11} \] Thus the original ball constraints are inactive in this inner problem, rather than being removed by assumption. The projection formula is consequently \[  egin{gathered} \Pi=I-A(A^*A)^{-1}A^*,\ F_{m br}(w)=b(w)^*\Pi b(w). \end{gathered} 	ag{12} \] Both \(\Pi\) and the operator in (11) are constant. They can be formed once for each level and fixed source expression. Each subsequent objective evaluation uses only fixed linear maps and degree-two expressions. There is no trial-dependent linear solve. Since \(b\) has degree at most two, (12) proves the degree-four assertion. If no packet is omitted, take \(F_{m br}=\widetilde F\); no inverse is needed. If \(q=0\), no outer packet remains: (11)--(12) evaluate a constant quadratic-response minimum. The same convention covers an already constant objective. The linear responses can also be assembled along their constant corridors instead of forming a dense global projection. After a fixed leaf input is inserted, the resulting map may be multiplication by a known packet. Such a map need not be unitary. Its response Gram is constant but need not be a scalar multiple of the identity, unlike a corridor containing only genuine turns. Those matrices and all their phases must remain. ## 4. Conditioning and the original source survive elimination The inner point (11) depends smoothly on \(w\). At that point, write \(H=D^2\widetilde F\) in retained and omitted coordinates. The real Schur formula gives \[ D^2F_{m br}=H_{ww}-H_{wz}H_{zz}^{-1}H_{zw},\qquad h^{\mathsf T}D^2F_{m br}h =\min_k(h,k)^{\mathsf T}H(h,k). 	ag{13} \] The lower bound in (2) gives at least \(\|h\|^2\); choosing \(k=0\) gives at most \(3\|h\|^2\). This proves (6). The formulas extend to the boundary of the retained balls, using the same interior margin for \(z_*\). The inward statement follows from the envelope identity \[ 
abla F_{m br}(w) =
abla_w\widetilde F(w,z_*(w)). 	ag{14} \] Its half-step is the retained component of the full feasible half-step in (2). The \(33/256\) bound follows directly. Averaging the Hessian bound (6) along a segment proves contraction by \(1/2\). The minimum is therefore unique and interior whenever variables remain. Exact partial minimization gives \(\min F_{m br}=\min\widetilde F\), proving (7), including zeros. The only restriction of a previous feasible set was the earlier, explicit leaf-transport clamp in the direct source. This note adds elimination, not further clamping. No normalization budget is reassigned to a fused linear map. When \(p=0\), the source has only its prescribed leaf and linear transport; the direct source already evaluates its scalar response. When \(p\ge1\) but \(q=0\), all remaining maps after the known leaf inputs are inserted are linear or constant. Equation (12) then contains the whole finite problem without an outer minimization. This does not simplify the geometric asymptotics of that coherent linear expression. ## 5. What this does not remove Every retained packet is still the full \(H_N\). Eliminated coordinates contribute through the exact constant response; no Casimir derivative or original marked closing is quotiented out. The result changes neither the original tangle nor its finite source. The smaller number of nonlinear packets does not make a source coefficient positive, or give it the hyperbolic-volume rate. Known linear maps can still carry strong phases and cancellation. A geometric trial certificate must control those actual responses and the original closing. Nor does convexity alone imply an exact degree-four semidefinite relaxation of the newly reduced objective; no such assertion is made. ## Complete proof source The sole complete proof direct was read at its matching pin: | Source | SHA-256 | |---|---| | [Quartic minimum on the internal Conway edges](research_conway_binary_skeleton_quartic.md) | 294220039d913fd349b867f9705670215c3ca98f581461c6f406db0dac20c7a3 | It supplies the clamped objective, its constant response metrics, conditioning, source comparison and original normalization. The additional reduction here uses the count (4), known linear responses after prescribed leaf inputs, and a second exact constant-coefficient elimination. No novelty is claimed for least squares or Schur complements. Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used. No mathematical program, numerical experiment, test, build, git operation or earlier-final edit was performed.

title: A compact unweighted reciprocal integral for the original Conway source
text:
# A compact unweighted reciprocal integral for the original Conway source 24 November 2026. Research proof. A known polynomial change of the normalization budgets makes the positive source integral compact and unweighted after all linearly entering packets have been integrated out. One packet per binary product remains. Its polynomial residual vector retains the original scalar closing, including its phases and all first-normal directions. For a fixed tree the compact integral approximates the reciprocal squared normalized source with relative error \(O(N^{-1})\). The proof also works in any prescribed positive packet metrics after consistent normalization. It does not evaluate the compact integral from hyperbolic geometry or prove a new volume lower bound. ## 1. The source and the polynomial normalization Fix a literal Conway tree with \(s\ge1\) proper vertices, \(L\ge1\) prescribed leaf occurrences and \(p=L-1\) binary products. Every packet is the complete \(N\)-dimensional physical algebra \(\mathcal A_N\), \(N\ge2\), including the independent first normals at double Casimir roots. Use the original products, genuine turns and original scalar closing of [P]. The leaf choices may be arbitrary complex physical packets, including prescribed short fillings. Initially choose known positive budgets \(b_v\), including the scalar root budget, so that the normalized leaves, turns, bilinear products and closing row have their respective norms at most \(1/16\). The product norm here is the supremum over two separately unit inputs. No small coefficient-tensor Hilbert--Schmidt norm is assumed. The physical budgets of [P] give one such choice. Write \[ B_N=\prod_v b_v,\qquad \widehat b_v=Nb_v,\qquad \widehat B_N=N^{s+1}B_N,\qquad \sigma_N={1\over16N}. 	ag{1} \] There are \(s\) proper budgets and one scalar root budget. In the rest of the proof use these new budgets, and abbreviate \(\sigma=\sigma_N\). Their normalized maps are \(\Phi_v\); their normalized original closing row is \(c\), extended by zero off the top packet. All their respective norms are at most \(\sigma\). The original framing, mark and external scalars remain in these maps. Choose orthonormal coordinates on every packet and product real Lebesgue measure. Put \(D=Ns\), and set \[ G_v(x)=\Phi_v((x_j)_{j	ext{ child of }v})-x_v,\qquad E_N(x)=\|G(x)\|^2+|cx|^2,\qquad \mathcal P_N={D!\over\pi^D}\int_{\mathbb C^D}E_N(x)^{-D-1}dx. 	ag{2} \] This is the reciprocal construction with the newly recorded budgets; its numerical value need not equal an earlier normalized integral. The base \(E_N\) has degree at most four. The exact forward field \(a\) satisfies \(G(a)=0\). If \(s_v\) is the number of proper vertices in the subtree at \(v\), induction gives \[ \|a_v\|\le\sigma^{s_v},\qquad k:=ca={K_N\over\widehat B_N},\qquad |k|\le\sigma^{s+1}. 	ag{3} \] Indeed a leaf supplies one factor, a turn adds one factor, and a product multiplies its two child bounds and adds one factor. Neither \(a\) nor \(k\) is input to define the integral. ## 2. The compact polynomial integral At every binary product retain exactly one child occurrence, as in [L,F]. These are \(p\) distinct packets because each proper packet has a unique parent. Write their coordinates as \(u\in\mathbb C^n\), \(n=Np\), and the remaining coordinates as \(z\in\mathbb C^h\), \(h=D-n\). The top packet is among the eliminated variables \(z\). At fixed \(u\), every product is linear in its remaining variable. Split the proper residual rows according to their output packets, and include the scalar closing in the second list: \[ r_z=T(u)z+b_z(u),\qquad r_o=C(u)z+b_o(u),\qquad r_o\in\mathbb C^{n+1}. 	ag{4} \] In the tree order \(T=-I+A_{zz}\), with \(A_{zz}\) strictly triangular. Thus \(T^{-1}\) is a finite polynomial for every \(u\in\mathbb C^n\), and \(|\det T|=1\). Define the known maps \[ z_0=-T^{-1}b_z,\qquad \mathsf D=CT^{-1},\qquad F=b_o-CT^{-1}b_z,\qquad R=I_{n+1}+\mathsf D\mathsf D^*,\quad q=F^*R^{-1}F. 	ag{5} \] The field \(z_0(u)\) solves all eliminated gate equations exactly by forward substitution. The components of \(F(u)\) are precisely the retained gate residuals and the original scalar closing at this field. In particular \(F\) is a known holomorphic polynomial vector. Every component has degree at most \(L\). To check this, treat each retained child as an independent input of degree one, bounded by its original subtree leaf count. Solved leaves are constant, turns preserve the bound and products add the two child bounds. The extra retained residual term \(-u_v\) has degree one. This proves the assertion for the retained rows and the top closing as well. Let \(\mathcal U_N\) be the product of the \(p\) closed unit packet balls. Our compact unweighted integral is \[  oxed{\qquad \mathcal J_N={n!\over\pi^n}\int_{\mathcal U_N} \|F(u)\|^{-2(n+1)}du .\qquad} 	ag{6} \] All integrals are extended and nonnegative. When \(p=0\), use the one-point convention for \(\mathbb C^0\); then \(F=k\) and \(\mathcal J_N=|k|^{-2}\), with value \(+\infty\) at zero. The polynomial \(\|F\|^2\) can have degree \(2L\); it is not asserted to be a quartic after elimination. For reference, the exact full-space integration of the linear packets from [F] is \[ \mathcal P_N={n!\over\pi^n}\int_{\mathbb C^n} {du\over\det R(u)\,q(u)^{n+1}} . 	ag{7} \] Indeed the change \(v=Tz+b_z\) preserves measure and gives \(E_N=\|v\|^2+\|\mathsf Dv+F\|^2\). Completing its Hermitian square uses \(I_h+\mathsf D^*\mathsf D\), whose determinant is \(\det R\), and residual constant \(q\). The radial beta integral is \(\pi^h n!/[D!\det R\,q^{n+1}]\). Tonelli proves (7), also when either side is infinite. No bounded-field estimate is used here. ## 3. The determinant and the omitted exterior are controlled On \(\mathcal U_N\), each row of \(A_{zz}\) has at most one eliminated child, and each column enters at most one parent row. Its nonzero blocks have norm at most \(\sigma\). The same holds for \(C\), counting the closing as the top packet's unique parent. Consequently the argument of [L] uses only bilinear operator norms and gives \[ \|A_{zz}\|\le\sigma,\quad \|C\|\le\sigma,\quad \|T^{-1}\|\le(1-\sigma)^{-1},\quad \|\mathsf D\|\le{\sigma\over1-\sigma}. 	ag{8} \] Set \[ \eta_N=(16N-1)^{-2},\qquad 	au_N=(n+1)\log(1+\eta_N),\qquad \delta_N=16DL\sigma^{2s+2}. 	ag{9} \] Every eigenvalue of \(R\) lies between \(1\) and \(1+\eta_N\). Also \(\|F\|^2/(1+\eta_N)\le q\le\|F\|^2\). Therefore, pointwise with the extended convention at \(F=0\), \[ e^{-	au_N}\|F\|^{-2(n+1)} \le {1\over\det R\,q^{n+1}} \le e^{	au_N}\|F\|^{-2(n+1)}. 	ag{10} \] Let \(\mathcal P_{N,\mathcal U}\) denote (7) restricted to \(\mathcal U_N\). Integration proves \(e^{-	au_N}\mathcal P_{N,\mathcal U}\le\mathcal J_N \le e^{	au_N}\mathcal P_{N,\mathcal U}\). To control the rest of (7), use the global residual coordinates \[ x=H(r),\qquad H(r)_v=\Phi_v((H(r)_j)_j)-r_v,\qquad |\det_{\mathbb R}DH|=1. 	ag{11} \] The inverse is polynomial and triangular. On \(\|r\|\le1/4\), upward induction bounds every packet by \(\sigma+1/4<1\): maps on previously bounded inputs have norm at most \(\sigma\). Hence a point whose retained packet lies outside \(\mathcal U_N\) must satisfy \(\|r\|>1/4\). Since \(E_N(H(r))\ge\|r\|^2\), \[ 0\le\mathcal P_N-\mathcal P_{N,\mathcal U} \le {D!\over\pi^D}\int_{\|r\|>1/4}\|r\|^{-2D-2}dr=16D 	ag{12} \] when the integrals are finite; the exterior bound remains valid in the extended case. The source polynomial \(f(r)=cH(r)\) has degree at most \(L\) and \(f(0)=k\). Finite-fiber orthogonality [F] gives \(\mathcal P_N\ge1/(L|k|^2)\) when \(k
e0\). Equations (3) and (12) thus make the omitted exterior a relative error at most \(\delta_N\). Combining with (10) proves the all-level comparison \[  oxed{\qquad (1-\delta_N)e^{-	au_N}\mathcal P_N \le\mathcal J_N\le e^{	au_N}\mathcal P_N .\qquad} 	ag{13} \] Here \(L\le s\) implies \(\delta_N\le1/(4096N^3)<1\): the successive ratio of \(s^2\sigma^{2s+2}\) is at most \(4\sigma^2<1\), so its maximum is at \(s=1\). The full integral is finite exactly when \(k
e0\), by [F] or the residual-coordinate argument below. At \(k=0\), (12) has finite exterior, so \(\mathcal P_{N,\mathcal U}=\mathcal J_N=+\infty\). For nonzero \(k\), (13) also proves finiteness and positivity of \(\mathcal J_N\). In particular, with reciprocal zero at infinity, \[ |K_N|^2\ge{(1-\delta_N)e^{-	au_N}\widehat B_N^2 \over L\mathcal J_N} 	ag{14} \] at every level, including zeros. ## 4. A short two-sided calibration in the same metrics Assume \(k
e0\) until the separate zero case below. The polynomial normalization also supplies a direct affine comparison. On the residual ball of radius \(1/4\), write \(DG=-I+A\). The unique-parent pattern and the two children per product give \(\|A\|\le\sqrt2\sigma\le1/8\), hence \(\|DH\|\le8/7\). At a product the second derivative is \(\Phi(h_L,k_R)+\Phi(k_L,h_R)\). Cauchy--Schwarz on sibling pairs, followed by their disjointness, bounds its direct-sum norm by \(\sigma\|h\|\|k\|\). Twice differentiating \(G(H(r))=r\) therefore gives \[ \|D^2f\|\le M_N:=\sigma^2(8/7)^3<2\sigma^2\le1, \quad f(r)=k+dr+p(r),\quad |p(r)|\le{M_N\over2}\|r\|^2 .	ag{15} \] This uses \(\|c\|\le\sigma\), with no sharper physical closing estimate. Put \(E_{m aff}=\|r\|^2+|k+dr|^2\). Completing its Hermitian square gives the exact cancellation of slope and determinant: \[ {D!\over\pi^D}\int_{\mathbb C^D}E_{m aff}^{-D-1}dr ={1\over|k|^2}\qquad(k
e0). 	ag{16} \] Specifically the square has determinant \(1+\|d\|^2\) and residual constant \( |k|^2/(1+\|d\|^2)\); their product is \( |k|^2\). On this ball, \(|p|\le(M_N/8)\sqrt{E_{m aff}}\). Applying the triangle inequalities to the augmented vector \((r,k+dr)\) yields \[ (1-M_N/8)^2E_{m aff}\le E_N(H(r)) \le(1+M_N/8)^2E_{m aff}.	ag{17} \] Since \(-\log(1-t)\le t/(1-t)\), the relative integrand error is at most \(\exp[(2/7)(D+1)M_N]-1\). Both energies dominate \(\|r\|^2\), so each normalized exterior integral is at most \(16D\). Comparing inside and outside, as in [R], proves \[  ig||k|^2\mathcal P_N-1 ig|\le\epsilon_N^{m aff},\quad \epsilon_N^{m aff}:= e^{(2/7)(D+1)M_N}-1+32D\sigma^{2s+2}. 	ag{18} \] In particular no lower bound on the possibly tiny nonzero source was used. Its energy has no zero on a compact set, and the exterior is integrable. At \(k=0\), \(f(r)=O(\|r\|)\) near zero makes the radial integral dominate a multiple of \(\int_0^{1/4}t^{-3}dt\), which verifies the divergence assertion used above. For a fixed tree, \(	au_N=O_T(N^{-1})\), \(\epsilon_N^{m aff}=O_T(N^{-1})\) and \(\delta_N=O(N^{-3})\). For nonzero sources a fully known common error is \[ \epsilon_N=e^{	au_N}(1+\epsilon_N^{m aff})-1+\delta_N =O_T(N^{-1}),\qquad  ig||k|^2\mathcal J_N-1 ig|\le\epsilon_N. 	ag{19} \] The lower estimate follows from (13) and (18); if \(\epsilon_N^{m aff}>1\), it follows instead from nonnegativity. For all sufficiently large levels, \(\epsilon_N<1\), and hence \[ (1-\epsilon_N){\widehat B_N^2\over\mathcal J_N} \le |K_N|^2\le (1+\epsilon_N){\widehat B_N^2\over\mathcal J_N}. 	ag{20} \] The zero convention makes (20) valid at source zeros too. ## 5. Metric choice, normalization and the remaining lower bound One may prescribe any positive Hermitian metric on each complete packet space, independently of the unknown closed value. In its orthonormal coordinates choose known base budgets making the actual leaf, linear, bilinear and closing norms at most \(1/16\), then use (1). The unique-parent arguments, triangular real Jacobian one, finite-fiber degree bound and affine proof remain unchanged. The measure and every norm in (2)--(7) must be rebuilt consistently. No comparison with the old packet metrics is required. The added budget factor is exactly \(N^{s+1}\). For a fixed tree its logarithm is \(o(N)\); every actual budget and external phase still has to be restored. Neither the numerical integral nor its polynomial residual vector is claimed to be metric independent. The denominator exponent \(n+1\) grows with the level. The improvement is removal of the unbounded retained integration domain and its Gram determinant after a specified polynomial normalization, together with a short two-sided comparison in those same metrics. The fixed-ball affine argument is already in [R]; [U] proves an undamped physical comparison with unchanged budgets. Here no physical shrinking-row estimate or Wick coefficient estimate is needed. The present proof does not improve their original normalization constants. To prove a geometric lower bound one still needs a geometric upper estimate on \(\mathcal J_N/\widehat B_N^2\). The original signed closing remains a component of \(F\); a zero source gives an infinite integral. Compactness and positivity alone supply no such upper estimate. Both its dimension \(n=Np\) and denominator exponent \(n+1\) still grow with the level; the prefactor \(n!/\pi^n\) remains. This is not a fixed-dimensional Laplace reduction or an identification with a classical angle integral. There is no new arbitrary-short-filling or finite-exception volume theorem. ## Complete inputs and coverage The five complete matching texts fix the actual source and the closest reductions. The new compact estimates and normalization are proved above. | Label | Complete text | Lines | SHA-256 | | --- | --- | ---: | --- | | P | [Physical compiler](research_conway_uniform_physical_quartic.md) | 477 | 39895b430535f565d30133b46ef57f67589207bc83f40597ffe96e2ce79bbda8 | | F | [Finite fibers and exact linear integration](research_conway_reciprocal_finite_fiber_lower_bound.md) | 285 | 4e708365d2d6f14a557c3af4d17bd7c489f784faf905b490e6e4bcfeec0f26cb | | L | [Linear packet elimination](research_conway_orthogonal_linear_elimination.md) | 344 | aa53b79685296193d5bf7fc66e53f3a3fbe03fc72a36481fb3aee23afe2ae113 | | U | [Unchanged undamped physical integral](research_conway_undamped_reciprocal_source.md) | 311 | 4ce9ae44a5ed6f7f54145d96712a7937f2e8c4181e2292aa5f2c44e84ffb3a8a | | R | [Fixed-ball affine comparison](research_conway_reciprocal_quartic_source_formula.md) | 233 | ead3945544c91ed81b87423f05c80dde29439d2be183b391005b133610e84e97 | Only written mathematics, text reads and metadata operations were used.
