title: A convex source minimum without the linear corridor variables
text:
# A convex source minimum without the linear corridor variables 21 November 2026. Research note. Earlier finals and public manuscripts remain unchanged. One packet at each binary product is enough for a uniformly convex minimum representing the original Conway source. The other packets can be evaluated by forward substitution. The inverse Gram matrix from exact least-squares elimination can then be omitted: the resulting unweighted objective is itself strongly convex, has a unique interior minimum, and admits a projection-free iteration with contraction factor \(1/4\). The source comparison keeps the original normalization budget. This removes linear solves from the reduced optimization; it does not evaluate its geometric exponential rate. ## 1. The original normalized source and the retained packets Use the complete normalized source of [the convex theorem](research_convex_normalized_conway_source.md). At level \(N\ge2\), every packet belongs to the full Newton space \(H_N\cong\mathbb C^N\), including all repeated-Casimir directions. The local normalized leaf, turn, product and original scalar closing have norm at most \[ \sigma= rac1{16}. \] For a map, the recorded Hilbert--Schmidt budget implies this operator bound. All phases and source markings are retained. Write \[ a_v=\Phi_v((a_c)_c),\qquad k= rac{K_N}{B_{m tot}}=La_{m top}. 	ag{1} \] Here \(B_{m tot}\) is exactly the product of the original local budgets, not a new geometric normalization. The true packets satisfy \(\|a_v\|\le\sigma\), and \(\|L\|\le\sigma\). Let \(p\) be the number of binary product vertices. Choose one child occurrence at each such vertex and retain that packet as a variable. Each occurrence has one parent, so this selects \(p\) distinct packets. Call them \(u=(u_1,\ldots,u_p)\), and call all other proper packets \(z\). The top packet is eliminated, since its parent is the scalar closing root. For each feasible \(u\), meaning \(\|u_i\|\le1\), define \(z_0(u)\) by solving every eliminated-output gate equation exactly from the leaves toward the root. A retained packet is a prescribed input when its parent is evaluated. Every eliminated packet has norm at most \(\sigma\): the inputs are in their unit balls, and each normalized gate has norm at most \(\sigma\). Let \(\Psi(u)\) denote the gate outputs at the retained vertices, evaluated at \((u,z_0(u))\), and retain the original closing \[ c(u)=L(z_0(u))_{m top}. \] Thus \[ G_o(u)=\Psi(u)-u,\qquad F(u)=(G_o(u),c(u)),\qquad H(u)=\|F(u)\|^2. 	ag{2} \] In particular \(\|\Psi_i(u)\|\le\sigma\) and \(|c(u)|\le\sigma^2\). The original scalar is still the last component of \(F\); it has not been replaced by a norm. The earlier [orthogonal elimination theorem](research_conway_orthogonal_linear_elimination.md) proved \[  rac{|k|^2}{\gamma_{m ret}} \le \min_{\|u_i\|\le1}H(u)\le |k|^2,\qquad \gamma_{m ret}=1+224^{-2}. 	ag{3} \] It did not assert convexity of \(H\). That is the additional statement proved here. If \(p=0\), there is no optimization: forward substitution gives \(H=|k|^2\). Below assume \(p\ge1\). ## 2. First derivatives of the forward substitution At a feasible field, let \(A_{ij}\) be the block derivative of the normalized forward maps from variable class \(j\) to output class \(i\), where \(i,j\in\{u,z\}\). These are derivatives of the forward maps, before subtracting the output variables. Every original product has exactly one retained child and one eliminated child. Consequently each of these four block matrices has at most one input block in each row and at most one parent block in each column. Its operator norm is at most \(\sigma\). The eliminated matrix \(A_{zz}\) is strictly triangular, so \[  egin{split} Dz_0&=(I-A_{zz})^{-1}A_{zu},& \|Dz_0\|&\le rac1{15},\ D\Psi&=A_{uu}+A_{uz}(I-A_{zz})^{-1}A_{zu},& \|D\Psi\|&\le rac1{15},\ &&\|Dc\|&\le rac1{240}. \end{split} 	ag{4} \] The last estimate uses that the top packet is eliminated. These bounds can also be obtained directly by summing the attenuated derivatives along the eliminated corridors. In particular \[  rac{14}{15}\|h\|\le\|DG_o(u)h\| \le rac{16}{15}\|h\|. 	ag{5} \] The product norm and all differential statements use the real inner product \(\operatorname{Re}\sum_i h_i^*k_i\). ## 3. A dimension-independent second-variation estimate The important point is that second variations do not accumulate with the number or length of corridors. Fix a retained variation \(h\), put \(\delta z=Dz_0(u)h\), and differentiate the exact eliminated gate equations twice along this variation. At a binary gate \(v\), the direct second-derivative forcing is \[ q_v=2\Phi_v(h_{m retained\ child}, \delta z_{m eliminated\ child}). 	ag{6} \] At leaves and linear gates it is zero. The child pairs at distinct binary gates are disjoint. Cauchy--Schwarz and (4) therefore give \[ \sum_{	ext{all binary }v}\|q_v\| \le2\sigma\|h\|\,\|\delta z\| \le rac1{120}\|h\|^2. 	ag{7} \] Separate this forcing into eliminated-output and remaining-output rows, with sums of packet norms \(Q_z,Q_o\), respectively. The scalar closing has no direct second derivative. Write \(\eta_z=D^2z_0(u)[h,h]\). Differentiating its forward recursion gives \[ \eta_z=A_{zz}\eta_z+q_z. 	ag{8} \] Use the block \(\ell^1\) norm, the sum of the packet norms, just for this estimate. Each eliminated variable has one parent, so \(\|A_{zz}\|_{1	o1}\le\sigma\). The derivative from eliminated packets into the remaining retained-output equations and the scalar closing also has block \(\ell^1\) norm at most \(\sigma\). Consequently \[ \|\eta_z\|_1\le rac{Q_z}{1-\sigma},\qquad \sum_{	ext{remaining rows}} \|D^2(\Psi,c)[h,h]\| \le Q_o+ rac{\sigma}{1-\sigma}Q_z \le Q_o+Q_z. 	ag{9} \] Combining with (7) proves \[  oxed{\quad \sum_{	ext{remaining rows}}\|D^2F(u)[h,h]\| \le rac1{120}\|h\|^2. \quad} 	ag{10} \] The explicit \(-u\) term has zero second derivative. No factor depending on \(N\), \(p\), or the corridor lengths occurs. Since \(\|(G_o)_i\|\le1+\sigma\) and \(|c|\le\sigma^2\), (10) yields the residual-curvature estimate \[ \left|\operatorname{Re}\langle F,D^2F[h,h]angleight| \le rac{17}{1920}\|h\|^2. 	ag{11} \] ## 4. Strong convexity and an interior contracting iteration **Theorem.** On the product of retained unit balls, \[  rac32 I\le D^2H\le rac52 I. 	ag{12} \] The minimum is unique and interior. The iteration \[ u^{(j+1)} =u^{(j)}- rac12
abla H(u^{(j)}) 	ag{13} \] stays feasible and contracts distances to that minimum by at most \(1/4\) at every step. **Proof.** The half-Hessian is \[ 	frac12D^2H[h,h] =\|DFh\|^2+\operatorname{Re}\langle F,D^2F[h,h]angle. \] Equations (4), (5), and (11) bound the full Hessian between \[ 2\left[\left( rac{14}{15}ight)^2- rac{17}{1920}ight]I \quad	ext{and}\quad 2\left[\left( rac{16}{15}ight)^2+  rac1{240^2}+ rac{17}{1920}ight]I. 	ag{14} \] These imply (12). It remains to check feasibility without projection. A retained input can affect exactly one remaining output equation: follow its unique parent path through eliminated vertices until reaching the first retained output, or the scalar closing. A retained output is prescribed, so its equation stops that forward influence. There is no cycle and \(\Psi_i\) is independent of its own \(u_i\). The derivative into that one downstream row is a product of local derivative blocks. Its norm is at most \(\sigma\), since the path has at least one gate. There is no sum over competing paths. From (2), the \(i\)-th component of the half-gradient step is \[ \left(u-	frac12
abla H(u)ight)_i =\Psi_i(u)-(D_i(\Psi,c))^*F(u). 	ag{15} \] Only the one downstream row occurs in the adjoint term. Thus \[ \left\|\left(u-	frac12
abla H(u)ight)_iight\| \le\sigma+\sigma(1+\sigma)= rac{33}{256}<1. 	ag{16} \] The scalar-root case has the smaller bound \(|c|\le\sigma^2\). For two feasible fields, average the Hessian along their segment. By (12), the operator \(I-	frac12\overline{D^2H}\) has norm at most \(1/4\). Hence (13) is a contraction on the complete product of closed balls. Its iterates converge to a unique fixed point \(u_*\), with \[ \|u^{(j)}-u_*\|\le4^{-j}\|u^{(0)}-u_*\|. 	ag{17} \] At the fixed point the gradient vanishes. Strong convexity makes it the unique minimum, and (16) places it in the interior. \(\square\) Forward substitution and its reverse adjoint pass evaluate \(H\) and its gradient. The iteration uses neither the inner normal equations nor an inverse boundary Gram matrix. This does not assert a cheap implementation of the original tensor contractions. ## 5. The source and its reduced lower certificate Let \(h_*=\min H\). The original comparison (3) is unchanged: \[ B_{m tot}^2 h_*\le |K_N|^2 \le\gamma_{m ret}B_{m tot}^2h_*. 	ag{18} \] It includes exact zeros. In particular \(Q_N^{m ret}=\gamma_{m ret}B_{m tot}^2h_*\) differs from \(|K_N|^2\) by at most the fixed factor \(\gamma_{m ret}\). Strong convexity gives the reduced lower certificate \[ D_{m ret}(u)=H(u)- rac13\|
abla H(u)\|^2,\qquad D_{m ret}(u)\le h_*\le H(u). 	ag{19} \] Indeed the quadratic minorant with Hessian \(3I/2\) has unrestricted minimum \(H-\|
abla H\|^2/3\). At \(u_*\) equality holds, so \[ h_*=\max_{\|u_i\|\le1}D_{m ret}(u). 	ag{20} \] The certificate need not be concave. Combining with (18) gives \[ B_{m tot}^2\max(0,D_{m ret}(u)) \le |K_N|^2 \le\gamma_{m ret}B_{m tot}^2H(u). 	ag{21} \] Only the \(2Np\) retained real-coordinate derivatives are needed. A geometric trial family with \(\|
abla H(u_N)\|^2\le3(1-\eta_N)H(u_N)\), \(0<\eta_N\le1\), and \(\log\eta_N=o(N)\) would have a lower witness at the same exponential rate as its upper value. Such a family is not supplied here. ## 6. Degree, scope, and complete proof sources Every forward expression is multiaffine in the retained packet groups, meaning affine in each packet separately. A literal tree uses each occurrence once, and eliminating a corridor does not duplicate it inside one output expression. Thus \(H\) is separately quadratic in each retained packet. Its total real degree is at most \(2\max(1,p)\). This can exceed four. The original lifted formulation retains degree four; the reduction trades that degree bound for fewer variables and no inner linear solve. The correct Gram of exact least-squares elimination has not been declared equal to the identity. The unweighted objective is a different minimum with its own proved source comparison and the additional convexity theorem above. All original normal directions remain in each retained full packet. The minimum remains a representation of a coherent quantum scalar. Uniform convexity, a faster iteration, and fewer packet variables do not determine its hyperbolic volume rate or the coefficient of a geometric contribution after arbitrary fixed short partial fillings. Absolute and relative accuracy for an exponentially small minimum are different requirements. Both complete proof texts were read at the matching pins: | Source | SHA-256 | |---|---| | [Normalized complete source](research_convex_normalized_conway_source.md) | 6b89b4c6a67ef7a32cc41a5966c650f32de65d284ae7b70d94a71bddba21df3c | | [Exact orthogonal elimination](research_conway_orthogonal_linear_elimination.md) | aa53b79685296193d5bf7fc66e53f3a3fbe03fc72a36481fb3aee23afe2ae113 | Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used. No mathematical program, numerical iteration, test, build, git operation or earlier-final edit was performed.

title: An explicit corridor factor for the quartic Conway minimum
text:
# An explicit corridor factor for the quartic Conway minimum Research proof, 23 November 2026. The original quartic minimum differs from an explicit multiple of the original squared source by an exponentially small relative error. The factor uses only the known closing row and the turns above the highest product. No unknown internal response appears in it. This does not evaluate the minimum or establish its geometric rate. ## 1. The original minimum and the known factor Use the full normalized Conway compiler of [C], with its prescribed leaves, products, turns and original closing. At every level \(N\ge2\), all packets belong to the full Newton space, including its Hermite directions. Put \[ \sigma= rac1{16},\qquad E(x)=\sum_v\|\Phi_v(x_{m children})-x_v\|^2 +|Lx_{m top}|^2, \qquad e_* =\min_{\|x_v\|\le1}E(x). 	ag{1} \] The actual normalized forward field is \(a\), and \[ \|a_v\|\le\sigma,\qquad k=La_{m top}=K_N/B_{m tot},\qquad L=\chi\lambda_\varepsilon/b_ho, \quad \varepsilon\in\{0,N-1\}. 	ag{2} \] Every physical budget remains the original \[ b_v=16\max(1,\|T_v\|_{m HS}), \qquad \Phi_v=M/b_v\ 	ext{or }J/b_v. 	ag{3} \] Suppose first that the tree has a product. Starting at the closing, let \(v_*\) be the highest product. Its output is followed by turns with normalized maps \(A_1,\ldots,A_m\), ordered upward. Thus the proper corridor consists of the output of \(v_*\) and those \(m\) turn outputs. Set \[ P_i=A_m\cdots A_{i+1}\quad(0\le i\le m), \quad P_m=I,\quad b_i=LP_i, \quad C=1+
u_{m corr},\quad 
u_{m corr}=\sum_{i=0}^m\|b_i\|^2. 	ag{4} \] The \(b_i\) in (4) are rows, distinct from the vertex budgets \(b_v\). All terms in (4) are known physical data. If the turn budgets in upward order are \( eta_1,\ldots, eta_m\), then explicitly \[ 
u_{m corr} = rac{|\chi|^2}{b_ho^2} \sum_{i=0}^m\prod_{j=i+1}^m eta_j^{-2}, \qquad 1\le C\le rac{256}{255}. 	ag{5} \] The bound follows from \(\|L\|\le\sigma\) and \(\|A_j\|\le\sigma\). Empty products have value one. Write \[ \eta= rac{\chi}{b_ho\prod_{j=1}^m eta_j}, \qquad \zeta= rac{|\eta|}{b_{v_*}}. 	ag{6} \] The endpoint identities of [G] give, with no conjugation in the bilinear form, \[ LP_0\Phi_{v_*}(u,w)=u^{\mathsf T}Bw, \qquad B= rac{\eta}{b_{v_*}}J \ 	ext{or } rac{\eta}{b_{v_*}}e_0e_0^{\mathsf T}, \qquad \|B\|=\zeta. 	ag{7} \] This includes both original endpoint closings and every parity of the turn corridor. In particular, the true field satisfies \(|k|\le\sigma^2\zeta\). **Theorem.** With the known \(C,\zeta\) above, \[  oxed{\quad \left(1- rac{\zeta^2}{82C}ight) rac{|k|^2}{C} \ \le e_*\le rac{|k|^2}{C}. \quad} 	ag{8} \] Equivalently, preserving the original budget and scalar, \[ C B_{m tot}^2 e_*\le |K_N|^2 \le rac{C B_{m tot}^2 e_*} {1-\zeta^2/(82C)}. 	ag{9} \] These inequalities include \(K_N=0\). If there is no product, put \(\zeta=0\), define the corridor to be the whole proper chain and define \(C\) by (4) for that chain. Then \[ e_*=|k|^2/C 	ag{10} \] exactly. If \(\chi=0\), both sides of (8)--(10) vanish. In particular the explicitly rescaled minimum \(\widetilde Q_N=C B_{m tot}^2e_*\) satisfies \[ \left(1- rac{\zeta^2}{82C}ight)|K_N|^2 \le\widetilde Q_N\le|K_N|^2. 	ag{10a} \] The variational presentation and its budgets depend on the chosen compiler. Equation (10a) compares that presentation to the unchanged original source; it does not assert that the minimum is itself a topological invariant. ## 2. Exact elimination of the final linear corridor Keep every packet below \(v_*\) as a variable \(u\). For fixed feasible \(u\), put \(f=\Phi_{v_*}(u_L,u_R)\). Write \(y_0\) for the output of \(v_*\), and \(y_1,\ldots,y_m\) for the turn outputs. The part of (1) involving these variables is exactly \[ \|y_0-f\|^2+\sum_{i=1}^m\|y_i-A_i y_{i-1}\|^2 +|Ly_m|^2. 	ag{11} \] Set \(r_0=y_0-f\) and \(r_i=y_i-A_i y_{i-1}\). Then \[ Ly_m=s+\sum_{i=0}^m b_i r_i,\qquad s=LP_0f. 	ag{12} \] The unconstrained least-squares minimum and its residuals are \[ \min_r\left\{\sum_i\|r_i\|^2+ \left|s+\sum_i b_i r_iight|^2ight\} = rac{|s|^2}{C},\qquad r_i=-b_i^*s/C. 	ag{13} \] For example, substitution gives the value in (13), and the stationary equations are \(r_i+b_i^*(s+\sum_jb_jr_j)=0\). The positive identity term makes that stationary point unique. The original corridor ball constraints do not alter this minimum. Indeed, with feasible \(u\) fixed, (11) is a strictly positive quadratic in the corridor packets. Its half-gradient step is the corresponding component of the full step of [C]. That step maps every corridor packet ball into its \(33/256\) ball and contracts by at most \(1/2\). Its fixed point is therefore feasible, interior and stationary for the unconstrained quadratic. It is the unique minimum in (13). Consequently exact partial minimization of (1) gives \[ F(u)=R(u)+|g(u)|^2,\qquad g(u)= rac{u_L^{\mathsf T}Bu_R}{\sqrt C}, \qquad \min F=e_*. 	ag{14} \] Here \(R\ge0\) is the sum of the unchanged residuals below the corridor. For the corresponding part \(u_a\) of the true field, \[ R(u_a)=0,\qquad DR(u_a)=0,\qquad g(u_a)=k/\sqrt C,\qquad F(u_a)=|k|^2/C. 	ag{15} \] All omitted coefficients have been eliminated, rather than projected to semisimple values. Formula (13) is the familiar root-corridor least-squares formula; the quantitative improvement below concerns how much further internal minimization can lower (15). ## 3. Further minimization has an exponentially small relative effect The more explicit Hessian estimate proved in [C] is \[ D^2E\succeq rac{41}{32}I. 	ag{16} \] The partial minimum \(F\) inherits the same lower bound. To see this, its eliminated quadratic minimizer is smooth in \(u\), and its Hessian is the Schur complement of the full Hessian at that minimizer. For every variation \(h\), \[ D^2F(u)[h,h] =\min_j D^2E(u,y_*(u))[(h,j),(h,j)] \ge rac{41}{32}\|h\|^2. 	ag{17} \] The smooth formula extends to the closed feasible balls. Thus the strong-convexity minorant, minimized over all real variations, gives \[ e_*\ge F(u_a)- rac{16}{41}\|
abla F(u_a)\|^2. 	ag{18} \] Only the two immediate inputs of \(v_*\) occur in \(g\). At the true field both have norm at most \(\sigma\). Therefore, in the original coefficient metric, \[ \|Dg(u_a)\|^2 \le rac{\|B\|^2}{C} (\|(u_a)_L\|^2+\|(u_a)_R\|^2) \le rac{2\sigma^2\zeta^2}{C}. 	ag{19} \] The derivatives and gradients in (16)--(19) are real derivatives for \(\operatorname{Re}\sum x_v^*y_v\). A complex-linear scalar row has the same operator norm in these real coordinates. Using (15), \[ \|
abla F(u_a)\|^2 =\|2(Dg(u_a))^*g(u_a)\|^2 \le rac{8\sigma^2\zeta^2}{C}F(u_a). 	ag{20} \] Substituting into (18), and using \(\sigma^2=1/256\), proves \[ e_*\ge\left(1- rac{128\sigma^2\zeta^2}{41C}ight)F(u_a) =\left(1- rac{\zeta^2}{82C}ight)F(u_a). 	ag{21} \] The competitor \(u_a\) gives the reverse inequality \(e_*\le F(u_a)\). This proves (8). If \(k=0\), (15) directly gives \(e_*=0\), so no division by \(k\) is needed. With no product there is no remaining variable \(u\), and (13) gives (10). Finally, [G] gives the all-level estimate and its large-level rate \[ \zeta\le rac1{256\max(1,\|M\|_{m HS})},\qquad \zeta\le\exp\left\{- rac{2G_{m Cat}}\pi N+O(\log N)ight\}. 	ag{22} \] Here \(G_{m Cat}=\int_0^{\pi/4}\log(\cot t)\,dt\). Thus the relative loss in (8) is at most \[  rac{\zeta^2}{82C} \le\exp\left\{- rac{4G_{m Cat}}\pi N+O(\log N)ight\}. 	ag{23} \] ## 4. Prescribed leaves and smaller quartics Suppose the feasible set for (14) is further restricted to a set containing \(u_a\), and let \(e_{m cl}\) be its minimum. Then the same comparison holds: \[ \left(1- rac{\zeta^2}{82C}ight) rac{|k|^2}{C} \le e_*\le e_{m cl}\le rac{|k|^2}{C}. 	ag{24} \] Indeed restriction gives the middle inequality, and the feasible competitor \(u_a\) gives the last one. Exact elimination of any remaining linear variables preserves that restricted minimum. This includes the prescribed-leaf restriction in [B]: the fixed inputs are the known leaf packets transported through their turn corridors, and the true field obeys those restrictions. Eliminating the final corridor at the same time is feasible, because none of its packets is one of those fixed inputs. Thus (24) applies to the smaller quartic on the connections between binary products, with its original budgets. No unknown binary output is fixed in making this restriction. Consequently \(C B_{m tot}^2e_{m cl}\) also obeys (10a). This asserts the stated comparison, rather than equality between the unrestricted and restricted numerical minima. ## 5. What has and has not been reduced The leading comparison factor \(C\) is an explicit finite sum of known corridor budgets. It requires neither the full forward field nor its backward response. All other internal optimization can change the corresponding value only by the relative amount in (8). The proof may use the true field as a competitor without inserting that unknown field into the definition of \(C\), \(E\), or the original source. This improves the fixed constant source comparison of [C] and removes the unknown response coefficient from the leading comparison in [S]. It does not turn evaluation of \(e_*\) into a scalar secular equation. The coherent value or a positive geometric lower witness for that minimum is still required. The original marking, scalar \(\chi\), budget product, and every physical Hermite direction remain present. No finite-exception theorem or new filling class follows. The literal product/turn tree and its original endpoint closing are essential. General precomposed unary maps or shared descendants need their own estimates; none is silently treated as a unitary turn. ## Complete inputs and comparison The following four complete matching texts were read. The exact corridor calculation is written in full above; [C] supplies its inactive balls and Hessian bound, and [G] supplies the endpoint contraction and quantitative rate. The complete binary-skeleton note [B] supplies the prescribed-leaf restriction used in Section 4 and already gives the exact corridor elimination. The complete scalar-response note [S] was read for coverage; it retains an internal response in its leading scalar comparison. The new assertion here is the explicit exponentially small relative loss in (8) and (24). - [C] [Normalized original source](research_convex_normalized_conway_source.md), SHA-256 `6b89b4c6a67ef7a32cc41a5966c650f32de65d284ae7b70d94a71bddba21df3c`. - [G] [Global closing curvature](research_conway_global_closing_curvature.md), SHA-256 `863f170da9a9017aa8b83b1ace44ee3e2c851f57c806c77678b3699e3f2f305f`. - [B] [Binary-skeleton quartic](research_conway_binary_skeleton_quartic.md), SHA-256 `294220039d913fd349b867f9705670215c3ca98f581461c6f406db0dac20c7a3`. - [S] [Scalar cap response](research_conway_scalar_cap_response.md), SHA-256 `6b9b73ae429713bdff63120a9841c06d2311d249f058f3da6b1f4e89dbfaecfb`. Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used. No earlier final, manuscript or public document was edited.

title: Orthogonal boundary packets under Conway composition
text: # Orthogonal boundary packets under Conway composition 20 November 2026. Research note; the public manuscripts remain frozen. The full Newton packet already makes a genuine quarter-turn unitary. Multiplication of neighboring tangles requires a further metric. At \(N\ge3\), different output rows overlap, so row-by-row normalization does not give a coisometry. This note constructs that metric for every finite expression made from Conway multiplication and quarter-turns. It keeps the entire boundary algebra and both original closing rows. The result is an exact finite-dimensional compatibility theorem. It identifies two quantitative losses that remain to be estimated: the projection of the actual leaf data onto the surviving boundary packet, and its angle with the prescribed closing row. Neither loss is given a positive lower bound here. In particular, this note proves no new hyperbolic-volume identity or finite-exception theorem. ## 1. The actual boundary algebra Fix an integer level \(N\ge2\), and put \[ d=N-1,\qquad q=e^{\pi i/N},\qquad Q=q^2,\qquad c_j=q^{2j+1}+q^{-2j-1}, \] \[ s_0=1,\qquad s_r=\prod_{u=1}^r2\sin(\pi u/N) \quad(1\le r\le d). \] The boundary space is the actual pair-Casimir algebra \[ H_N=\mathbb C[z]/\bigl(2T_N(z/2)+2\bigr). \] Here \(T_N\) is the Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind. The normalized Newton basis is \[ b_r(z)=\frac{\prod_{j=0}^{r-1}(c_j-z)}{s_r^2}, \qquad 0\le r\le d. \tag{1} \] The empty product gives \(b_0=1\). Coefficient vectors in this basis are columns in \(\mathbb C^N\), equipped initially with the usual Hermitian inner product. A superscript \(*\) means its conjugate transpose. The algebra retains the value and first derivative at every double Casimir root and the simple value at \(-2\) when \(N\) is odd. It is not the algebra of functions on the distinct roots alone. We use the actual source identities proved in [the Newton turn note](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_newton_turn_positive_gram.md) and [the multiplication note](../papers/newton-calculus/README.md). The genuine quarter-turn has coefficient matrix \[ J e_r=e_{d-r},\qquad J=J^*=J^{-1}. \tag{2} \] Multiplication is the linear map \[ M:H_N\otimes H_N\longrightarrow H_N, \qquad M(e_i\otimes e_j)=\sum_r\mu_{ijr}e_r. \tag{3} \] If \(i+j\le d\), its nonzero coefficients are \[ \mu_{ijr} =\frac{s_{i+j}s_r} {s_i s_j s_{r-i}s_{r-j}s_{i+j-r}}, \qquad \max(i,j)\le r\le i+j. \tag{4} \] All other coefficients are zero, including every product with \(i+j\ge N\). Equations (2)--(4) hold in the full repeated-root algebra. In particular \[ M(e_0\otimes f)=f,\qquad \mu_{ij0}=\delta_{i0}\delta_{j0},\qquad \mu_{ij,d}=\delta_{i+j,d}. \tag{5} \] The first equality makes \(M\) surjective. There are two original scalar closures. For \(f=\sum_r f_rb_r\), the original cup followed by the marked cap evaluates \(f(c_0)=f_0\). The cylindrical closure, with one ordinary pivotal trace and the prescribed mark, is \(\phi(f)=f_d\). We retain both rows: \[ \lambda_0=e_0^{\mathsf T},\qquad \lambda_d=e_d^{\mathsf T}. \tag{6} \] In particular the ordinary pivotal trace in the cylindrical closure has not been substituted for the marked cap. The exact Frobenius identity is \[ \phi(fg)=f^{\mathsf T}Jg. \tag{7} \] The positive fixed Newton metric is \(\langle f,g\rangle=\phi(\overline f\,Jg)=f^*g\), where coefficient conjugation is well-defined because (1) has real coefficients. Both rows (6) have dual norm one in that fixed metric. The literal ribbon operations and normalizations are also recorded in [the complete-circle Conway note](../papers/newton-calculus/README.md). Any external framing or normalization factor remains attached to the original diagram; the constructions below introduce no new such factor. ## 2. Keep every leaf variable before inserting its filling Let \(E\) be a finite expression obtained from leaves by products \(EF\) and quarter-turns \(\mathscr R E\). A leaf stands for an arbitrary boundary packet in \(H_N\). It does not stand for a one-dimensional space spanned by the already computed tangle value. Every occurrence of a leaf receives its own copy of \(H_N\). If \(n(E)\) is the number of leaf occurrences, define \[ B_E:H_N^{\otimes n(E)}\longrightarrow H_N \tag{8} \] by the following actual coefficient operations: \[ B_{\mathrm{leaf}}=I,\qquad B_{\mathscr R E}=JB_E,\qquad B_{EF}=M(B_E\otimes B_F). \tag{9} \] Ordered leaf tensor factors are inherited from the planar expression. Thus no permutation convention is left implicit. If the actual leaf packets are \(f_1,\ldots,f_{n(E)}\), then \[ v=f_1\otimes\cdots\otimes f_{n(E)},\qquad y=B_Ev \tag{10} \] is the full actual boundary packet of the composed tangle. This follows by induction from the full operator identities (2)--(4). It includes the Hermite directions even when a component has zero value at every distinct root. An actual signed crossing power can be inserted as a leaf packet. Its Newton coefficients include its original common Cartan scalar and all first derivatives. No crossing is replaced by its nodal phases. Fixed short tangles can likewise be inserted as their full packets. With this convention, \(B_E\) depends on the unfilled expression and \(N\), but not on the numerical twist assignments or an unknown closed invariant. **Lemma 1.** Every \(B_E\) is surjective. **Proof.** This is true at a leaf. A turn preserves surjectivity because \(J\) is invertible. If \(B_E\) and \(B_F\) are surjective, their tensor product is surjective, and (5) says that \(M\) is surjective. Their composite in (9) is therefore surjective. Induction proves the claim. \(\square\) ## 3. The boundary quotient metric and the expanded Gram Define the real symmetric positive-definite matrices \[ C_E=B_EB_E^*,\qquad G_E=C_E^{-1}. \tag{11} \] Positive definiteness follows from Lemma 1. Reality follows because the universal matrices \(I,J,M\) are real; the actual leaf vectors in (10) can still be complex. The recursion is explicit: \[ C_{\mathrm{leaf}}=I,\qquad C_{\mathscr R E}=JC_EJ,\qquad C_{EF}=M(C_E\otimes C_F)M^*. \tag{12} \] Consequently \(G_{\mathscr R E}=JG_EJ\). In the remainder, \(\|y\|_{G_E}^2=y^*G_Ey\). Two different Grams must be distinguished. The matrix \(B_E^*B_E\) acts on the expanded leaf tensor space and is generally singular. It gives the fixed Newton boundary norm \(\|B_Ev\|^2=v^*B_E^*B_Ev\). The matrix \(G_E\) acts on the \(N\)-dimensional boundary and is nonsingular. It gives the quotient norm inherited from the entire expanded leaf space. **Theorem 2.** The least-norm expanded lift of \(y\in H_N\) is \[ S_Ey=B_E^*C_E^{-1}y. \tag{13} \] Its squared norm is \(y^*G_Ey\). The matrix \[ P_E=B_E^*C_E^{-1}B_E \tag{14} \] is the orthogonal projection onto \((\ker B_E)^\perp\), and \[ \|B_Ev\|_{G_E}^2=\|P_Ev\|^2,\qquad \|v\|^2=\|P_Ev\|^2+\|(I-P_E)v\|^2. \tag{15} \] **Proof.** Equation (11) gives \(B_ES_E=I\). The range of \(S_E\) lies in \(\operatorname{ran}B_E^*=(\ker B_E)^\perp\). Every other lift of \(y\) is \(S_Ey+k\), with \(k\in\ker B_E\), and the summands are orthogonal. This proves minimality and uniqueness. Direct multiplication gives \[ S_E^*S_E=C_E^{-1}B_EB_E^*C_E^{-1}=C_E^{-1}. \] Likewise \(P_E^*=P_E\), \(P_E^2=P_E\), and its kernel is \(\ker B_E\). These identities prove the projection claim and both equalities in (15). \(\square\) In particular this is the canonical quotient metric once the full leaf Newton inner products have been fixed: \[ y^*C_E^{-1}y=\min_{B_Ec=y}\|c\|^2. \] Equivalently, \(C_E^{-1/2}B_E\) is a coisometry: its product with its adjoint is the rank-\(N\) identity on the boundary. This is an exact orthogonal packet for the actual synthesis, with no deleted boundary channel. ## 4. Compatibility at every multiplication and turn Consider neighboring subexpressions \(E,F\). Set \(C=C_{EF}\), and define the normalized multiplication map \[ A_{E,F}=C^{-1/2}M(C_E^{1/2}\otimes C_F^{1/2}). \tag{16} \] Equation (12) gives \[ A_{E,F}A_{E,F}^*=I. \tag{17} \] Thus the original multiplication is a coisometry from the product of the two child quotient metrics to the parent quotient metric. The metric is transported at the gluing; it is not held fixed while an unproved isometry is imposed on \(M\). For arbitrary actual child packets \(f,g\), put \[ x=(C_E^{-1/2}f)\otimes(C_F^{-1/2}g),\qquad P_{E,F}=A_{E,F}^*A_{E,F}. \] Then \(P_{E,F}\) is an orthogonal projection, and the exact loss is \[ \boxed{\quad \|f\|_{G_E}^2\|g\|_{G_F}^2-\|fg\|_{G_{EF}}^2 =\|(I-P_{E,F})x\|^2.\quad} \tag{18} \] Indeed the two terms on the left are \(\|x\|^2\) and \(\|A_{E,F}x\|^2=\|P_{E,F}x\|^2\), respectively. Orthogonal decomposition proves (18). For a turn the corresponding equality is \[ \|Jf\|_{G_{\mathscr R E}}=\|f\|_{G_E}. \tag{19} \] This proves exact compatibility through arbitrarily many finite neighboring Conway gluings and turns. At a product, the loss can be nonzero; (18) computes it rather than asserting that it is small. There is also a parenthesization check. For expressions involving products alone, the two maps associated with \((EF)H\) and \(E(FH)\) coincide, after the usual tensor associator, because they are multiplication in the same actual algebra. Their \(B,C,G,P\) therefore coincide. A genuine turn is not an algebra homomorphism, so no analogous unproved interchange of turns and products is used. The nullspace removed here is safe in any exterior: if \(B_Ev=0\), the full actual boundary operator is zero. Every further linear or multilinear tangle context therefore gives zero. This statement concerns redundant expanded descriptions of a boundary operator. It does not remove a nonzero vector from the boundary space \(H_N\). In particular it does not quotient by the kernel of one closing row. That row kernel can be exposed by a different exterior. This distinction agrees with the contextual source-quotient criterion in [the two-sided quotient note](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_source_two_sided_quotients.md), Section 1. The stronger observability results in [the adjacent-observable note](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_adjacent_observable_source_filtration.md), Sections 2--3, concern quotients of the true boundary representation; they do not forbid removal of redundant expanded descriptions. ## 5. Both original closing costs and the remaining angle For a nonzero boundary row \(\lambda\), its squared dual norm is \[ a_\lambda(E)=\lambda G_E^{-1}\lambda^* =\lambda C_E\lambda^*. \tag{20} \] It is strictly positive. In particular the two original rows (6) cost \[ a_0(E)=(C_E)_{00},\qquad a_d(E)=(C_E)_{dd}. \tag{21} \] Equivalently \(a_\lambda(E)=\|\lambda B_E\|^2\): it is an explicit contraction of the expression with its adjoint. This does not identify it with a hyperbolic volume or a regulator. A turn exchanges these two costs. A product has the explicit updates \[ a_0(EF)=a_0(E)a_0(F), \tag{22} \] \[ a_d(EF)=\sum_{i,k=0}^d(C_E)_{ik}(C_F)_{d-i,d-k} =\operatorname{tr}(C_EJC_FJ). \tag{23} \] For (22), only the input \((0,0)\) contributes to row zero of \(M\). For (23), row \(d\) is the antidiagonal selector in (5). The displayed trace uses the real symmetry established after (11). For a general complex Hermitian covariance the sum is still valid, but its trace form is \(\operatorname{tr}(C_EJC_F^{\mathsf T}J)\). Equations (20)--(23) compute the original source cost before the numerical filling packets are inserted. Cauchy gives \[ |\lambda B_Ev|^2\le a_\lambda(E)\,\|P_Ev\|^2. \tag{24} \] It is useful to retain the exact difference between this upper bound and the desired scalar. Suppose first that \(v\ne0\), and put \[ t=C_E^{-1/2}B_Ev,\qquad r=\frac{C_E^{1/2}\lambda^*}{\sqrt{a_\lambda(E)}}, \qquad \|r\|=1. \] Define \[ \eta_E(v)=\frac{\|P_Ev\|^2}{\|v\|^2},\qquad \gamma_{E,\lambda}(v)= \begin{cases}|r^*t|^2/\|t\|^2,&t\ne0,\\0,&t=0. \end{cases} \tag{25} \] Both numbers lie in \([0,1]\). Since \(\lambda B_Ev=\sqrt{a_\lambda(E)}\,r^*t\), there is an exact identity \[ \boxed{\quad |\lambda B_Ev|^2 =a_\lambda(E)\,\|v\|^2\,\eta_E(v)\, \gamma_{E,\lambda}(v).\quad} \tag{26} \] For \(v=0\), define both factors in (25) to be zero; (26) remains valid. For the actual tensor input (10), \(\|v\|^2=\prod_j\|f_j\|^2\). The first factor in (25) measures how much expanded leaf data survives as a boundary operator. The second is the squared angle with the prescribed closing vector. A nonzero boundary packet can still be orthogonal to that closing vector. An orthogonal change of coordinates does not prevent either factor from being zero or exponentially small. No lower estimate for these factors is asserted. Consistent unitary coordinate changes on the expanded and boundary spaces leave these norms, projections, and angles unchanged; changing an orthonormal basis alone cannot improve \(\eta_E\gamma_{E,\lambda}\). ## 6. A single gluing already has exponential metric cost The metric update cannot in general be replaced by a harmless scalar normalization. For two variable leaves, \[ C=MM^*,\qquad C_{00}=1,\qquad C_{dd}=N. \tag{27} \] The last two claims follow from the two distinct row descriptions in (5). Hence \(C\) is not a scalar matrix at any \(N\ge2\). In particular the actual multiplication is not a coisometry, even after one common scalar rescaling, in the fixed Newton metric. For \(N\ge3\), its covariance is not even diagonal: the input \((1,d-1)\) contributes positively to both output rows \(d-1\) and \(d\), by (4)--(5). Hence \(C_{d-1,d}>0\), and diagonal row rescaling alone cannot make these rows orthogonal. At \(N=2\) the rows have disjoint supports; (27) still excludes a common scalar normalization, while separate row normalization does work at that level. There is a stronger quantitative separation. Take \(a=\lfloor N/3\rfloor\). For every \(N\ge3\), \(1\le a\) and \(2a\le d\), so (4) applies exactly and gives \[ \mu_{a,a,a}=\frac{s_{2a}}{s_a^2}. \tag{28} \] Let \(\kappa_2(C)\) be the ratio of the largest to the smallest eigenvalue. Its smallest eigenvalue is at most \(C_{00}=1\), whereas its largest is at least \(C_{aa}\ge\mu_{a,a,a}^2\). Thus \[ \kappa_2(C)\ge\mu_{a,a,a}^2. \tag{29} \] We use the Lobachevsky convention \[ \Lambda(\theta)=-\int_0^\theta\log|2\sin u|\,du. \] For fixed \(0<x<1\), the integrable Riemann-sum limit is \[ \frac1N\log s_{\lfloor Nx\rfloor} \longrightarrow-\frac{\Lambda(\pi x)}\pi. \tag{30} \] For completeness, subtract \(\log t\) from \(\log(2\sin\pi t)\) near zero; the difference extends continuously. The continuous part has ordinary Riemann sums, and the monotone integral bounds for \(\log t\) give its integrable Riemann sum. This proves (30) and also applies when the index differs by a bounded integer from \(Nx\), as needed for \(2a\). Since \(\Lambda(2\pi/3)=-\Lambda(\pi/3)\), equations (28)--(30) give \[ \frac1N\log\mu_{a,a,a}\longrightarrow \frac{3\Lambda(\pi/3)}\pi>0, \] \[ \liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\kappa_2(MM^*) \ge\frac{6\Lambda(\pi/3)}\pi. \tag{31} \] The positivity follows from \(\Lambda(\pi/2)=0\) and \(\Lambda(\pi/3)=\int_{\pi/3}^{\pi/2}\log(2\sin u)\,du>0\). These are lower bounds on conditioning, not an assertion of its optimal exponent. The inverse metric \(G=C^{-1}\) has the same condition number. ## 7. What changes relative to the existing packet results The fixed Newton metric, the unitary actual turn, and the two closing rows were already known. The [ordinary-cap tree theorem](actual_cap_tree_angle_energy.md), Sections 3--4, also gives an exact coisometry after its known diagonal row normalization. That diagonal normalization works because different root rows of that particular cap kernel have disjoint supports. The same note explicitly leaves arbitrary adjoining interior operations outside that conclusion. Here the neighboring actual Conway multiplication is included. Its overlapping rows are handled by the full covariance (12), rather than by a diagonal weight or an unspecified positive global metric. The recursive metric depends on all unfilled child expressions, remains full dimensional, and has exact multiplication and turn interfaces. The price can be exponential, as (31) already shows for one gate. This gives a precise version of choosing the orthogonality adapted to the synthesis: redundant expanded directions are orthogonally removed without changing any exterior. It does not make the remaining closing coefficient positive. To use (26) in a volume theorem, one must still estimate the combined exponential rate of its explicit source cost, leaf norms, projection factor, and closing angle. Their separate upper bounds do not supply the missing lower bound. In particular no assertion about generic or finitely many exceptional fillings follows here. ## 8. Long powers do not change an exact span by themselves There is a simple limitation on using a smaller exact leaf space for long fillings. Let \(T\) be an invertible operator on a finite-dimensional space and let \(U\) be any prescribed subspace. For every integer \(p\ge0\), \[ \operatorname{span}\{T^nu:n\ge p,\ u\in U\} =\operatorname{span}\{T^nu:n\ge0,\ u\in U\}. \tag{32} \] Indeed the space on the right, call it \(W\), is \(T\)-invariant. The restriction \(T|_W\) is injective and \(W\) is finite dimensional, so \(T(W)=W\). The left side is \(T^pW=W\), proving (32). This applies to multiplication by the actual crossing or full twist, with its complete Hermite inverse and original Cartan factor. Thus replacing a nonnegative filling half-line by a sufficiently long half-line does not by itself reduce the exact space of allowed leaf packets or the family of linear tests that annihilate it. The advantage of long filling must enter a quantitative estimate. This assertion uses no diagonalization and remains valid for Jordan blocks. ## Direct sources read for this note The first two sources supply the algebraic identities used in the proof. The remaining sources establish the physical-operation conventions and the precise scope of the earlier orthogonality and quotient statements. | Source | SHA-256 | |---|---| | [Newton turn and metric](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_newton_turn_positive_gram.md) | `d8b21fa8db909120035e86e997a0e02cb84f8dce2dcf6fb244bb5c85c17e28a3` | | [Actual Newton multiplication](../papers/newton-calculus/README.md) | `543b5be6035ecec349ce8e78ee47085345ceefe4fc51e5f2005b802d999805bb` | | [Literal complete-circle Conway operations](../papers/newton-calculus/README.md) | `f7e5bfbb1c556c1ea357a6880619851308cd73afc4402e8b42680963410edd58` | | [Ordinary-cap trees](actual_cap_tree_angle_energy.md) | `ecaf7177962dfa5a944a532fed37d505b97e81361926039f69cbf7f9b674a2da` | | [Contextual source quotients](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_source_two_sided_quotients.md) | `7ec8b1482c6c312c3f103d148322219b31d318a79f6bf87dd5609071d0d184c0` | | [Adjacent-observable source filtration](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_adjacent_observable_source_filtration.md) | `c115426182ba06c5db16fc1c3292dabfdec187182c4666aacd53b91e13073f44` | No mathematical program, numerical test, build, or public-document edit was used to establish the assertions of this note.

title: A global source-error bound from the original Conway closing
text:
# A global source-error bound from the original Conway closing Research proof, 23 November 2026. The highest product's endpoint identity controls every lower quadratic error, giving a global exponentially small remainder coefficient without local polar decompositions. The computed polar radius of [P] remains at least as strong; the improvement is over its earlier inexpensive global radius. ## 1. The original tree and its coherent correction Fix \(N\ge2\), put \(D=N-1\), and use \(H_N=\mathbb C[X]/(2T_N(X/2)+2)\) with Newton basis \(e_0,\ldots,e_D\). The coefficient Hermitian norm makes these basis vectors orthonormal. All first normals at repeated roots are retained. The original turn, Frobenius row and marked evaluation row satisfy \[ Je_j=e_{D-j},\quad \phi(f)=f_D,\quad \lambda_0(f)=f_0, \quad \phi(uv)=u^{\mathsf T}Jv,\quad \lambda_0(uv)=u_0v_0,\quad \lambda_0J=\phi,\quad\phi J=\lambda_0. 	ag{1} \] Here \(f_j\) denotes a Newton coefficient, and transpose has no complex conjugation. These are the full original algebra identities in [P,C]. Take a fixed literal Conway tree with distinct child occurrences. Its proper gates are prescribed leaves, turns \(J\), and products \(M(u,w)=uw\). Use the original budgets of [C], with \(\sigma=1/16\): \[ b_v=16\max(1,\|T_v\|_{m HS}),\qquad \Phi_v=M/b_v\ 	ext{at a product},\qquad \Phi_v=J/b_v\ 	ext{at a turn}. 	ag{2} \] Here \(T_v\) is the corresponding unnormalized physical tensor. The original closing is \(L=\chi\lambda_\varepsilon/b_ho\), with \(\varepsilon\in\{0,D\}\) and \(\lambda_D=\phi\). The scalar \(\chi\), its closing budget \(b_ho\), every other budget, and their product \(B_{m tot}\) are retained. In particular \(\|L\|=|\chi|/b_ho\le\sigma\). Let \(a\) be the true normalized forward field and \(x\) any feasible trial field, meaning \(\|x_v\|\le1\) at every proper vertex. Define \[ e=a-x,\quad r=\Phi(x)-x,\quad A=D\Phi(x),\quad c=(0,\ldots,L	ext{ on the top packet},\ldots,0), \] \[ d=c(I-A)^{-1},\qquad z=Lx_{m top},\qquad k=K_N/B_{m tot},\qquad \widehat k=z+dr. 	ag{3} \] The inverse is a finite triangular sum. If \(Q_v(h)=\Phi_v(h_L,h_R)\) at products and is zero elsewhere, [R] proves the exact identities \[ (I-A)e=r+Q(e),\qquad k-\widehat k=dQ(e). 	ag{4} \] Because the tree has one parent per packet, its backward rows obey \[ d_{m top}=L,\qquad d_u=d_vD_u\Phi_v(x)\quad(u	ext{ a child of }v). 	ag{5} \] ## 2. The highest product fixes the global coefficient Suppose first that the tree contains a product, and let \(v_*\) be the first product encountered going downward from the closing. Every proper gate above it is a turn. Let \(\mathcal U\) be that turn corridor and put \[ \eta= rac{\chi}{b_ho\prod_{u\in\mathcal U}b_u},\qquad \zeta= rac{|\eta|}{b_{v_*}}. 	ag{6} \] Empty products equal one. By (1) and (5), \(d_{v_*}=\eta\lambda_
u\), with \(
u\in\{0,D\}\) determined by the corridor parity. No turn has been moved through a product. Thus the contracted bilinear matrix at \(v_*\) is exactly \[ B_{v_*}= egin{cases} (\eta/b_{v_*})J,&
u=D,\ (\eta/b_{v_*})e_0e_0^{\mathsf T},&
u=0, \end{cases} \qquad \|B_{v_*}\|=\zeta. 	ag{7} \] Here \(u^{\mathsf T}B_vw=d_v\Phi_v(u,w)\). For either child \(u\) of \(v_*\), its sibling packet \(x_{m sib}\) gives, by (1), \[ \|d_u\|\le\zeta\|x_{m sib}\|\le\zeta. 	ag{8} \] This uses the endpoint contraction. Each lower derivative block has norm at most \(\sigma\). At a product this follows from \(\|D_u\Phi_v(x)\|\le\|\Phi_v\|_{m bil}\|x_{m sib}\| \le\sigma\); at a turn it follows from (2). Consequently a proper descendant \(v\) at distance \(j\ge1\) below \(v_*\) satisfies \[ \|d_v\|\le\zeta\sigma^{j-1},\qquad \|B_v\|\le\sigma\|d_v\|\le\zeta\sigma^j \quad	ext{if }v	ext{ is a product}. 	ag{9} \] All product matrices have norm at most \(\zeta\), with equality at the highest one. Thus the block polar majorant \(\mathcal S_x\) of [P,(10a)] satisfies, uniformly over feasible \(x\), \[ \|\mathcal S_x\|=\zeta. 	ag{10} \] ## 3. The whole remainder and an inexpensive source disk For any full variation field \(h\), distinct product sibling pairs are disjoint. Equations (7)--(9) and \(2ab\le a^2+b^2\) give \[ |dQ(h)|\le\sum_{v\ {m product}}\|B_v\|\|h_L\|\|h_R\| \le rac\zeta2\|h\|^2. 	ag{11} \] The true and trial fields lie in the original product of unit balls. On their joining segment, the derivative of \(\Phi\) has norm at most \(\sqrt2\sigma\le1/8\): a row has at most two child blocks and every child occurs once. Integrating that derivative, or using [R]'s residual estimate, proves \(\|e\|\le(8/7)\|r\|\). Combining this with (4),(11) yields \[ |k-\widehat k|\le R_{m end}(x),\qquad R_{m end}(x)= rac{32\zeta}{49}\|r\|^2, \] \[ B_{m tot}(|\widehat k|-R_{m end})_+ \le |K_N|\le B_{m tot}(|\widehat k|+R_{m end}). 	ag{12} \] Here \((t)_+=\max(t,0)\). With no product, \(Q=0\), \(k=\widehat k\) exactly, and the radius is zero. Write \(H_M=\max(1,\|M\|_{m HS})\). Since all corridor budgets are at least one and \(b_{v_*}=16H_M\), \[ \zeta\le rac1{256H_M},\qquad R_{m end}\le rac{\|r\|^2}{392H_M} \le rac{\|r\|^2}{392}< rac{\|r\|^2}{343} \quad(r
e0). 	ag{13} \] Thus (12) improves the earlier inexpensive global coefficient uniformly. It does not improve the computed polar radius \(R_{m pol}\) of [P]. Indeed its scalar majorants obey \(\Delta_v=\|r_v\|+\sigma\sum_c\Delta_c\), hence \(\|\Delta\|\le(8/7)\|r\|\) by the same one-parent norm bound. Since [P]'s \(t_{vc}\le\sqrt{\|B_v\|}\Delta_c\), \[ R_{m pol}\le rac\zeta2\|\Delta\|^2\le R_{m end}. 	ag{14} \] One may use (12) without forming any polar matrix, or keep the stronger computed polar disk. The coherent center and every budget are identical. ## 4. Exponential saving and scope For \(j=\lfloor N/4floor\), [P,(20)] proves from the actual sine-factorial coefficient that \[ \|M\|_{m HS}\ge\|M\|_{m bil}\ge  rac{s_{2j}^{\,2}}{s_j^{\,4}} =\exp\{(2G_{m Cat}/\pi)N+O(\log N)\}, \qquad s_j=\prod_{a=1}^j2\sin(\pi a/N). 	ag{15} \] Here \(G_{m Cat}=\int_0^{\pi/4}\log(\cot t)dt\). Consequently \(\zeta\le\exp\{-(2G_{m Cat}/\pi)N+O(\log N)\}\). The saving is global for the stated literal compiler, at every parity and composite level; (15) is its large-level quantitative consequence. Restoring \(B_{m tot}\) retains all lower product budgets. No claim that every multiplication cost disappears is made. For a sequence of feasible trials, suppose \(|\widehat k_N|=\exp(-\alpha N+o(N))\), \(\|r_N\|\le\exp(- eta N+o(N))\), and \(\zeta_N\le\exp(-\gamma N+o(N))\). Then (12) is negligible relative to its coherent center whenever \(2 eta+\gamma>\alpha\). With the older constant coefficient, the corresponding sufficient condition was \(2 eta>\alpha\). A bounded residual permits \( eta=0\); the hypotheses still require the stated actual center estimate. The pure-turn corridor and the two original endpoint closings are essential hypotheses. Fixed short proper subtrees may be inserted as their full prescribed leaves. General precomposed unary maps and shared descendants are outside this literal compiler; parameter derivatives of the closing need their own transport. All physical Hermite normals and original phases remain present. No actual center or positive difference has been assigned a geometric rate, and no finite-exception theorem follows. ## Complete proof sources All three complete matching proof texts were read: - [P] [Source-sensitive polar bound](research_conway_source_polar_error_bound.md), 321 lines, SHA-256 `3d1e77ad6f3cac830a5290145e4f05111bb39856f67866a126782f6dd27debc4`. - [R] [Source-visible residual transport](research_conway_source_visible_residual_transport.md), 420 lines, SHA-256 `0d344301b0df65246551cf81498eff84582f796a03271b201f8fbba6c7742007`. - [C] [Normalized original source](research_convex_normalized_conway_source.md), 329 lines, SHA-256 `6b89b4c6a67ef7a32cc41a5966c650f32de65d284ae7b70d94a71bddba21df3c`. Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used. No earlier final, manuscript or public document was edited.

title: Global critical-point localization for the original Conway quartic
text:
# Global critical-point localization for the original Conway quartic Written proof, 23 November 2026. The normalized Conway quartic has one real critical point on the entire packet space. A single sweep of real scalar path minimizations brings any field into the radius-\(1/16\) packet balls without increasing the energy. The known contracting iteration then applies. A gradient test and continuous-flow convergence are also proved. These finite-level statements concern the literal uncompressed tree, not the minimum's hyperbolic-volume rate. ## 1. Complete physical packets and the original closing Use [P]'s full \(N\)-dimensional physical pair algebra \(H_N\) with its uniform physical Hilbert metric, for every \(N\ge2\). All independent first normals at repeated Casimir roots remain. The proof also applies in [C]'s normalized Newton metric, keeping that metric's own maps and budgets together. Fix a finite rooted literal Conway tree with distinct child occurrences. Every proper vertex is a prescribed constant leaf, a homogeneous complex-linear turn, or a complex-bilinear product. Every proper packet has one parent. There are no shared variables or compressed affine gates. The closing root is the original complex-linear row \(L\), with all its recorded scalar factors. Equal prescribed leaf data still have distinct trial variables. Write \(V\) for the proper vertices, \(v_0\) for the top one, and \[ \mathcal X= igoplus_{v\in V}H_N,\qquad \mathcal D=\prod_{v\in V}\{\|x_v\|\le1\},\qquad \sigma=1/16. 	ag{1} \] Keep exactly one of the normalizations above. Its prescribed leaf vectors \(a_\ell\), unary maps, bilinear maps, and closing row all have their respective vector, operator, or bilinear norms at most \(\sigma\). Define on the whole space \(\mathcal X\) \[ G_v(x)=\Phi_v((x_c)_c)-x_v,\qquad E(x)=\sum_{v\in V}\|G_v(x)\|^2+|Lx_{v_0}|^2. 	ag{2} \] At a leaf, \(\Phi_\ell=a_\ell\). Gradients are real gradients for \(\operatorname{Re}\sum_v x_v^*y_v\). The actual source theorem gives, with its unchanged budget product \(B\), \[ I\le D_{\mathbb R}^2E\le3I\quad\hbox{on }\mathcal D, \qquad B^2\min_{\mathcal D}E\le |K_N|^2 \le rac{197}{196}B^2\min_{\mathcal D}E. 	ag{3} \] No change of metric, cap, framing, or peripheral normalization is made in applying these estimates. ## 2. The exact leaf-path identity For a literal leaf \(\ell\), let \(P_\ell\subset V\) be its ancestor path, including the leaf and the top packet. Put \[ X^{(\ell)}_v= egin{cases}x_v,&v\in P_\ell,\0,&v
otin P_\ell. \end{cases} \] Scale these path packets by a real number \(t\), leaving all other packets fixed. Exactly one child of each internal path vertex is scaled. Homogeneity therefore scales its entire residual by \(t\). The original closing also scales by \(t\). Only the leaf residual has the form \(a_\ell-tx_\ell\). Differentiating at \(t=1\) proves the identity, valid for every field without a feasibility assumption, \[  oxed{\quad \left\|x_\ell- rac{a_\ell}{2}ight\|^2 +\sum_{v\in P_\ell\setminus\{\ell\}}\|G_v(x)\|^2 +|Lx_{v_0}|^2 = rac{\|a_\ell\|^2}{4} + rac12\langle
abla E(x),X^{(\ell)}angle_{\mathbb R}. \quad} 	ag{4} \] Every internal proper vertex is on at least one such path. Distinct leaf occurrences, rather than identified repeated inputs, are essential to this scaling argument. ## 3. A global gradient membership test Set \[ g=\|
abla E(x)\|,\qquad h=\|x\|,\qquad q_x=\sqrt{ rac{\sigma^2}{4}+ rac{gh}{2}},\qquad R(q)=\max\left\{ rac\sigma2+q, rac{q}{1-\sigma}ight\}. 	ag{5} \] Cauchy--Schwarz in (4), with \(\|X^{(\ell)}\|\le h\), gives \[ \|x_\ell-a_\ell/2\|\le q_x\quad\hbox{at every leaf}, \qquad \|G_v(x)\|\le q_x\quad\hbox{at every internal vertex}. 	ag{6} \] If \(q_x\le1-\sigma\), then \(R(q_x)\le1\) and \[ \|x_v\|\le R(q_x)\quad(v\in V). 	ag{7} \] Indeed leaves satisfy this by (6). If all children obey this bound, a unary gate has output norm at most \(\sigma R\), and a binary gate at most \(\sigma R^2\le\sigma R\). Thus \(\|x_v\|\le\sigma R+q_x\le R\), proving (7) inductively. In particular the following tests are valid on the entire space: \[  oxed{\quad gh\le rac{899}{512}\ \Longrightarrow\ x\in\mathcal D, \qquad gh\le rac7{16}\ \Longrightarrow\ \max_v\|x_v\|\le rac1{32} +\sqrt{ rac1{1024}+ rac{gh}{2}}\le rac12. \quad} 	ag{8} \] For the first constant use \(2[(1-\sigma)^2-\sigma^2/4]=899/512\). For the second, \(q_x\le15/32=(1-\sigma)/2\), so the first term in the maximum defining \(R\) is the larger one. These tests bound \(gh\), not the gradient norm alone. ## 4. One real critical point on the whole space The causal residual map is a polynomial automorphism. Given any residual field \(r\), solve successively from leaves to root by \[ x_v=\Phi_v((x_c)_c)-r_v. 	ag{9} \] This is its polynomial inverse. Consequently \(E\) is coercive: an energy sublevel is a closed subset of the compact image under \(G^{-1}\) of a closed residual ball. A global minimum therefore exists and is a real critical point. At any real critical point, \(g=0\). Equations (5)--(7) give \[  oxed{\qquad \|x_v\|\le\sigma\quad(v\in V),\qquad \|G_v(x)\|\le\sigma/2\quad(v\hbox{ internal}). \qquad} 	ag{10} \] For example every internal packet has the sharper bound \(\sigma^2+\sigma/2=9/256<\sigma\). All real critical points thus lie inside \(\mathcal D\), where (3) makes the gradient strictly monotone. There can be only one. It is the unique global minimum \(x_*\), and \[ \min_{\mathcal X}E=\min_{\mathcal D}E=E(x_*). 	ag{11} \] Thus the real stationary equations of degree at most three specify the minimum without any competing real critical points. This is not a statement about critical points of a complexification of the real polynomial. ## 5. One scalar sweep enters the convex region At any current field, process a leaf \(\ell\) by scaling its path packets by one real scalar. With current quantities put \[ u=\|x_\ell\|,\quad A=u^2+\sum_{v\in P_\ell\setminus\{\ell\}}\|G_v(x)\|^2 +|Lx_{v_0}|^2,\quad b=\operatorname{Re}\langle a_\ell,x_\ellangle. 	ag{12} \] The same homogeneity gives \(E(t)=C_\ell-2bt+At^2\). Minimize this quadratic on the segment \([0,1]\): choose \[ t=\min\{1,\max\{0,b/A\}\}\quad(A>0),\qquad t=1\quad(A=0). 	ag{13} \] Energy cannot increase, since \(t=1\) is allowed. The updated leaf has norm at most \(\sigma\), and every updated internal path residual has norm at most \(\sigma/2\). If \(A>0\) and \(b\le0\), this follows from \(t=0\). If \(0<b<A\), use \(b\le\sigma u\) to obtain \(tu\le\sigma u^2/A\le\sigma\) and \(t\|G_v\|\le\sigma u\|G_v\|/A\le\sigma/2\). Here \(2u\|G_v\|\le u^2+\|G_v\|^2\le A\). If \(b\ge A>0\), then \(t=1\), \(u^2\le A\le\sigma u\), and \(\|G_v\|^2\le A-u^2\le\sigma u-u^2\le\sigma^2/4\). If \(A=0\), the leaf and all these residuals are already zero. Homogeneity then forces all path packets to be zero successively. The update is continuous even there, since \(0\le t\le1\). Process every literal leaf once, in any order. An off-path residual is unchanged. Distinct leaf paths never include another leaf, so a processed leaf stays bounded by \(\sigma\). Every subsequent touch of an internal residual preserves its bound; packet norms and internal residual norms never increase. Every internal vertex is touched. At the end, upward induction as in (10) bounds all packets by \(\sigma\). Thus this finite sweep maps \(\mathcal X\) into \(\sigma\mathcal D\) with nonincreasing energy, using no unknown closed source. Starting there, the known step \(x^{j+1}=x^j-
abla E(x^j)/2\) stays in \(\mathcal D\) and contracts by \(1/2\). If \(s=|V|\), \[ \|x^j-x_*\|\le2\sigma\sqrt{s}\,2^{-j},\qquad 0\le E(x^j)-E(x_*)\le6\sigma^2s\,4^{-j}. 	ag{14} \] This is global initialization followed by the established local-domain iteration, not a claim about the raw fixed step outside that domain. The errors in (14) are absolute; source-relative precision does not follow when the minimum is exponentially small. ## 6. Continuous gradient flow from arbitrary initial data For any finite initial field solve \(\dot x=-
abla E(x)\). The polynomial vector field is locally Lipschitz and \[  rac d{dt}E(x(t))=-\|
abla E(x(t))\|^2. 	ag{15} \] The compact initial energy sublevel contains the trajectory, so local existence extends to all \(t\ge0\) and \(\int_0^\infty g(t)^2dt<\infty\). The gradient and Hessian are bounded there. Thus \(g(t)^2\) has bounded derivative and is uniformly continuous. It tends to zero: otherwise disjoint intervals would contribute a fixed positive amount to its integral. Every cluster point is therefore critical. Compactness and uniqueness imply \(x(t)	o x_*\). Since \(h\) stays bounded, (8) eventually applies. No uniform flow entry time, global Polyak--Lojasiewicz inequality, or global flow rate is asserted. ## 7. Scope, coverage, and complete inputs Fixed signed twists and fixed short fillings remain their full leaf packets in the unchanged literal tree, with the original cap and all physical normals. A component with unknown incoming packets is not replaced by a known constant leaf. [J] already proves coercivity and the unique global minimum. The path identity and initialization add global critical-point control. The original comparison (3) is unchanged; its minimum can still be zero or exponentially small. Uniqueness here concerns the real quartic, not complex source-phase saddles or geometric thimbles. No source growth rate or finite-exception volume theorem is proved.
