No mathematical program, test, build, git operation, manuscript edit, public-document edit, or earlier-final edit was performed.

title: A scalar response for the quartic on internal Conway edges
text:
# A scalar response for the quartic on internal Conway edges 21 November 2026. Research note. Earlier finals and public manuscripts remain unchanged. The quartic source problem on \(p-1\) internal packets still has an exact scalar dual. Its root term is now bilinear rather than linear, but the original tensor normalization makes that term small enough to preserve uniform convexity of the scalar-forced inner problems. The outer response is a contraction in two real coordinates. This does not eliminate the internal packets. It gives a dimension-independent certificate for the final closing once its internal response is controlled. No geometric rate or finite-exception theorem is proved. ## 1. The original weighted root term Use the prescribed-leaf restriction of the binary-skeleton theorem. There are \(p\) binary products and \(p-1\) free full packets when \(p\ge1\); the feasible set \(\mathcal D\) is their product of unit balls in the full \(N\)-dimensional Newton space. The exact source budget \(B=B_{m tot}\) and original markings are retained. Write the clamped quartic as \[ E(u)=R(u)+|g(u)|^2,\qquad m=\min_{\mathcal D}E,\qquad B^2m\le |K_N|^2\le\gamma B^2m,\quad \gamma= rac{197}{196}. 	ag{1} \] Here \(R\) is the sum of all nonroot corridor costs. It is nonnegative. The exact root-corridor formula is \[ g(u)=  rac{cP\,\Phi_{m top}(u_L,u_R)} {\sqrt{\,1+\sum_i\|cP_i\|^2\,}} . 	ag{2} \] The row \(c\) is the normalized original closing; \(P,P_i\) are the known products of normalized turns in that root corridor. The inputs in (2) are either free packets or prescribed leaf-only transports. The square root is positive. In particular its known denominator has not been discarded or inserted into a new budget. Put \(\sigma=1/16\). The norm bounds in the binary-skeleton theorem give, on \(\mathcal D\), \[ |g|\le\sigma^2,\qquad \|Dg\|\le\sqrt2\,\sigma^2,\qquad \|D^2g\|\le\sigma^2,\qquad I\le D^2E\le3I. 	ag{3} \] The derivatives are real derivatives for \(\langle h,kangle_{\mathbb R}=\operatorname{Re}(h^*k)\). The scalar \(g\) takes values in \(\mathbb C\), regarded as two real coordinates. The derivative bounds follow from the coefficient norm \(\sigma^2\) of the bilinear form in (2). A fixed input makes the corresponding expression linear, or constant, and only improves these bounds. The original half-gradient step for this quartic has each free packet in its \(33/256\) ball. There also exists a feasible field \(a\) with \[ R(a)=0. 	ag{4} \] Indeed the true normalized forward packets satisfy every nonroot corridor equation and the prescribed leaf transports. This field is used only to prove (4); no unknown binary packet or knot value is inserted in the coefficients of (1)--(2). ## 2. Uniform scalar-forced inner problems For \(\lambda\in\mathbb C\), define \[ h(\lambda)=\min_{u\in\mathcal D} \{R(u)+2\operatorname{Re}( ar\lambda g(u))\}, \qquad q(\lambda)=h(\lambda)-|\lambda|^2 . 	ag{5} \] The minimum exists for every \(\lambda\), by compactness. For \(|\lambda|\le\sigma^2\), it has a unique interior minimizer \(u(\lambda)\). **Proof of the inner assertion.** Equation (3) implies \[ \|D^2|g|^2\|\le 2\|Dg\|^2+2|g|\|D^2g\|\le6\sigma^4. \] Thus for the inner objective \(J_\lambda=R+2\operatorname{Re}( ar\lambda g)\), \[ \mu I\le D^2J_\lambda\le(3+8\sigma^4)I,\qquad \mu:=1-8\sigma^4>0 . 	ag{6} \] To check the original ball constraints, its half-gradient step differs from that of \(E\) by \[ (Dg)^*(g-\lambda). 	ag{7} \] The derivative of \(g\) in either of its at most two free input packets has norm at most \(\sigma^2\). Therefore the correction in each packet, separately, has norm at most \(2\sigma^4\). All other packet corrections are zero. The step maps \(\mathcal D\) strictly into packet balls of radius \[  rac{33}{256}+2\sigma^4<1. 	ag{8} \] The Hessian interval (6) makes this step a contraction with factor \[  rac12+4\sigma^4<1 . 	ag{9} \] Its unique fixed point is interior and stationary, hence is the unique global inner minimum. The real implicit function theorem gives a smooth response on a neighborhood of the scalar disk. \(\square\) Define the scalar response \[ s(\lambda)=g(u(\lambda)). 	ag{10} \] It maps \(|\lambda|\le\sigma^2\) into the same closed disk. Writing \(H_\lambda=D^2J_\lambda(u(\lambda))\), implicit differentiation gives the real \(2	imes2\) matrix \[ Ds(\lambda)=-2Dg\,H_\lambda^{-1}(Dg)^*,\qquad \|Ds(\lambda)\|\le \vartheta:= rac{4\sigma^4}{1-8\sigma^4} = rac1{16382}. 	ag{11} \] This matrix is negative semidefinite. The response is a real smooth map; no complex holomorphy is asserted. ## 3. The exact scalar dual and its gap **Theorem.** The clamped quartic minimum is exactly \[  oxed{\qquad m=\max_{\lambda\in\mathbb C}q(\lambda). \qquad} 	ag{12} \] The maximizer is unique, lies in \(|\lambda|\le\sigma^2\), and satisfies \(\lambda_*=s(\lambda_*)\). Iteration of \(s\) from any point of that disk converges with factor at most \(\vartheta\). **Proof.** For every feasible \(u\) and every \(\lambda\), \[ E(u)-\{J_\lambda(u)-|\lambda|^2\} =|g(u)-\lambda|^2\ge0. 	ag{13} \] Hence \(q(\lambda)\le m\). Let \(u_*\) be the unique interior minimum of \(E\), and put \(\lambda_*=g(u_*)\). Its modulus is at most \(\sigma^2\). The stationary equation for \(E\) is exactly the stationary equation for \(J_{\lambda_*}\). The convexity and interior assertion already proved show that \(u_*=u(\lambda_*)\). Equality holds in (13) there, proving (12). The function \(h\) is concave on the whole scalar plane because it is an infimum of affine functions of \(\lambda\). Subtracting \(|\lambda|^2\) makes \(q\) strictly concave, so its maximizer is unique. On the disk, \(
abla q=2(s-\lambda)\); alternatively (11) directly gives the unique fixed point and its contracting iteration. \(\square\) At any exact inner response, the entire remaining primal-dual gap is one complex scalar: \[  oxed{\qquad q(\lambda)\le m\le E(u(\lambda)),\qquad E(u(\lambda))-q(\lambda)=|s(\lambda)-\lambda|^2. \qquad} 	ag{14} \] Computing this response still solves for the \(p-1\) full packets. The scalar identity is not a claim that those packets have been replaced by two real unknowns. ## 4. A relative certificate for the original closing The zero-residual fact (4) is useful here. Since \(D^2R\ge\mu I\), the quadratic strong-convexity inequality at a field \(u\), tested against its zero-cost minimum, gives \[ R(u)\le rac{\|
abla R(u)\|^2}{2\mu}. \] At the exact inner response, \(
abla R=-2(Dg)^*\lambda\). Equations (3) and (11) imply \[ R(u(\lambda))\le\vartheta|\lambda|^2. 	ag{15} \] Suppose \(\lambda
e0\), \(|\lambda|\le\sigma^2\), and \[ |s(\lambda)-\lambda|\le\epsilon|\lambda|, \qquad 0\le\epsilon<1/2 . 	ag{16} \] Writing \(\delta=s-\lambda\) in (5) gives \[  egin{aligned} q(\lambda)&=R(u(\lambda))+|\lambda|^2 +2\operatorname{Re}( ar\lambda\delta) \ge(1-2\epsilon)|\lambda|^2,\ E(u(\lambda))&\le [\vartheta+(1+\epsilon)^2]|\lambda|^2. \end{aligned} \] Combining with (1) and (14) proves \[  oxed{\quad B^2(1-2\epsilon)|\lambda|^2 \le |K_N|^2 \le\gamma B^2[\vartheta+(1+\epsilon)^2]|\lambda|^2. \quad} 	ag{17} \] Thus if a fixed construction has eventually nonzero scalar trials \(\lambda_N\) satisfying (16) for a fixed \(\epsilon<1/2\), and if \(2\pi N^{-1}\log(B|\lambda_N|)	o V\), then the original full-sequence source has the same limit \(V\). The ratio of \(|K_N|\) to \(B|\lambda_N|\) is bounded between the two explicit positive square-root constants in (17). No geometric construction of these trials or their response bound is supplied here. For \(p=1\), there are no free internal packets after the prescribed leaf restriction. For \(p=0\), the linear-chain root formula likewise has no optimization. In both cases take \(R=0\), with \(g\) the known constant root-corridor value; (12)--(17) hold with the empty inner problem and constant response. Their evaluation asserts no asymptotic rate. ## 5. Why the actual source structure matters Fixed degree and coercivity alone do not give this scalar dual. Even the uniformly convex real quartic \[ R(x)=(x^2-1)^2,\quad g(x)=\sqrt3\,x,\quad E(x)=R(x)+|g(x)|^2=x^4+x^2+1 \] has \(\min E=1\), whereas \(\max_\lambda[\min_x(R+2\lambda g)-\lambda^2]=0\): testing \(x=\pm1\) bounds that expression by \(-2\sqrt3|\lambda|-\lambda^2\), with equality zero at \(\lambda=0\). This is a counterexample to a generic optimization inference, not a knot counterexample. Here the small root map, residual convexity, zero-cost forward field and source comparison come from the retained Conway normalization. They provide the response estimates but no geometric exponential rate by themselves. No dimension-independent bound on algebraic elimination degree, and no complete elimination of the quantum packets, is claimed. The theorem concerns the original \(p-1\)-packet quartic; it does not assume that a further partial minimization preserves its root-square decomposition. ## Complete proof source The entire matching source is [the quartic on internal Conway edges](research_conway_binary_skeleton_quartic.md), SHA-256 \(	exttt{294220039d913fd349b867f9705670215c3ca98f581461c6f406db0dac20c7a3}\). It supplies the exact corridor weights, original normalization, source sandwich, Hessian bounds and inward step. The scalar assembly and response estimates are proved above. The complete proof source was read at the displayed matching pin. Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used. No mathematical program, numerical experiment, test, build, git operation or earlier-final edit was performed.

title: Logarithmic degree after exact Conway source compression
text: # Logarithmic degree after exact Conway source compression 24 November 2026. Research note. Written proof. Earlier final notes and public manuscripts remain unchanged. The retained residual vector in the compact reciprocal construction need not have degree as large as the number of leaves. First compose the known linear parts of the actual source. Then retain the larger child at each remaining product. An eliminated continuation halves its descendant leaf count at every product. This gives a logarithmic degree bound for the reduced residual, with the original scalar closing still present. The construction changes the auxiliary energy and integral, but keeps the original closed source and the product of its recorded budgets. It does not estimate that scalar at the hyperbolic volume rate. ## 1. Compress the actual normalized source Use the full physical packet space \(\mathcal A_N\) and the literal source of [P], for every \(N\ge2\). Its dimension is \(N\); all first-normal directions at repeated Casimir roots are included. Write the original normalized recursion and closing as \[ a_v=\Phi_v((a_c)_c),\qquad K_N=B_N\,c_Na_{\rm top},\qquad \sigma=\frac1{16}. \tag{1} \] Here \(B_N\) is the product of all recorded original budgets, including the original root budget and external scalar convention. Each leaf constant, unary map, bilinear map and closing row has norm at most \(\sigma\). Bilinear norms use two separately unit inputs, as in [P]. True normalized packets have norm at most \(\sigma\). Suppress the unary turns only for counting the product tree. A product then has zero, one or two inputs coming from another product; an input not coming from a product is the known transport of an original leaf. Let \(n_0,n_1,q\) count these three classes. If there is at least one product, counting the edges of this product tree gives \[ n_0+n_1+q=p,\qquad n_1+2q=p-1,\qquad n_0=q+1. \tag{2} \] Evaluate each zero-product-child vertex at its actual two known inputs. At a one-product-child vertex, insert its actual fixed other input. It is now a known complex-linear map on its remaining input. Compose these maps and the genuine turns along their paths. The vertices with two product children remain bilinear. The resulting literal source has \[ \ell=q+1\ \hbox{constant leaves},\qquad q\ \hbox{bilinear gates}, \qquad s_c=2q+1\ \hbox{proper vertices}. \tag{3} \] Its top linear corridor is composed with the original closing row. If the original source has no product, take \(q=0\), compose its unary corridor, and use the same convention of one constant leaf. This is a composition of the recursion (1), not the Schur-complement objective of [B]. In particular no minimizer of an earlier auxiliary energy is substituted for a source packet. The original budgets are grouped, rather than replaced by estimates for newly fused unscaled maps. Partition the old vertices into the bottom constant regions with their outgoing linear corridors, the bilinear vertices with their outgoing linear corridors, and the top closing region. Every proper region stops at the next bilinear input; the corridor above the highest product belongs only to the closing region. Fixed side-leaf subtrees belong to the region in which they are inserted. Every old vertex belongs to exactly one region. The new region budget is the product of its old budgets; bilinearity makes its normalized map exactly the corresponding composition of the old normalized maps. Consequently \[ \prod_{\rm regions}b_{\rm region}=B_N,\qquad K_N=B_N\,\widetilde c_N\widetilde a_{\rm top}. \tag{4} \] Every proper region contains an old proper gate or leaf, and the root region contains the old closing row. All remaining normalized factors have norm at most one. Thus each new constant, bilinear map and closing row has norm at most \(\sigma\). This argument keeps every actual fixed packet, phase, original mark and first normal in its coefficient; it uses no inverse or cancellation of a fixed packet. For \(q=0\), the whole proper source has simply become one known packet. Computing that packet is exact source evaluation, not an asymptotic estimate for its closing. ## 2. Choose the retained child by leaf count The following argument applies to any binary packet source with \(\ell\) constant leaves and no unary vertices, including (3). For a proper vertex \(v\), let \(\ell(v)\) be its number of descendant leaves. At every product retain its child with larger \(\ell(v)\); break ties arbitrarily. The other child is eliminated. There is one retained packet per product, so the retained vector is \[ u\in\mathbb C^{Nq},\qquad n=Nq . \tag{5} \] Occurrences are distinct because every proper vertex has one parent. The top proper packet is always eliminated. Fix \(u\) and solve the eliminated gate equations exactly, as in [L]. Denote their solution by \(z_0(u)\). A solved leaf is constant. At a solved product, the larger child is its retained independent packet and the smaller child is solved recursively. Therefore the degree \(d(v)\) of its solved value satisfies \[ d(v)=0\quad(v\hbox{ a leaf}),\qquad d(v)\le1+d(v_{\rm small}) \quad(v\hbox{ a product}). \tag{6} \] After \(h\) such steps, the remaining subtree has at most \(\ell(v)/2^h\) leaves. Equivalently, induction in (6) gives \[ d(v)\le\lfloor\log_2\ell(v)\rfloor . \tag{7} \] The estimate is valid for a product whose own output is retained as well: only its right-hand side is evaluated by this rule. Let \(F(u)\) be the vector consisting of the retained gate residuals and the original scalar closing evaluated at \(z_0(u)\). A retained leaf contributes its prescribed constant minus \(u_v\). A retained product contributes its right-hand side minus \(u_v\). The closing is linear in the solved top packet. Hence \[ \boxed{\quad F:\mathbb C^{Nq}\longrightarrow\mathbb C^{Nq+1},\qquad \deg F\le d_\ell:=\max\{1,\lfloor\log_2\ell\rfloor\}. \quad} \tag{8} \] Every component is affine separately in every retained packet slot. Indeed the retained child at a product is independent of all variables in the other child's subtree. The tree has no repeated descendant, so no retained slot is multiplied by itself. Induction in (6), followed by the affine term \(-u_v\), proves the assertion. Thus the real polynomial \(\|F(u)\|^2\) has degree at most \(2d_\ell\). For \(q=1,2\), in particular, \(F\) is affine. For \(q=0\) no retained variable remains: \(F\) is the scalar \(\widetilde c_N\widetilde a_{\rm top}\), of degree zero. The convention \(d_\ell=1\) in (8) is only a harmless uniform bound. The full lifted energy before elimination still has degree at most four, independently of this improvement. ## 3. The exact source and compact reciprocal normalization Apply [C] to this compressed source, multiplying each of its \(s_c\) proper region budgets and its root budget by \(N\). The new normalized local maps have norm at most \(\sigma_N=1/(16N)\), and \[ \widehat B_N=N^{s_c+1}B_N=N^{2q+2}B_N,\qquad k_N=K_N/\widehat B_N . \tag{9} \] The rescaling only changes known coefficients, so the degree and slotwise multiaffinity in (8) are unchanged. Write \(c_N^{\rm new}=\widetilde c_N/N\) for the rescaled closing. Write \(a_{\rm leaf}^{\rm new}\) for the rescaled constant leaf packets. Hereafter \(F\) denotes the residual vector for these rescaled maps. For clarity, its exact construction is \[ r_z=T(u)z+b_z(u),\qquad r_o=C(u)z+b_o(u),\qquad T=-I+A_{zz}, \] \[ D(u)=C(u)T(u)^{-1},\quad F(u)=b_o(u)-C(u)T(u)^{-1}b_z(u),\quad R(u)=I+D(u)D(u)^* . \tag{10} \] The matrix \(A_{zz}\) is strictly triangular, even for complex unbounded \(u\), so \(T^{-1}\) is polynomial and \(|\det T|=1\). No root or first-normal quotient has been taken. Put \(D_c=Ns_c\), let \(E\) be the sum of all squared rescaled proper residuals and \(|c_N^{\rm new}x_{\rm top}|^2\), and define \(\mathcal P_N=(D_c!/\pi^{D_c})\int_{\mathbb C^{D_c}} E(x)^{-D_c-1}dx\). Exact linear integration gives \[ \mathcal P_N=\frac{n!}{\pi^n}\int_{\mathbb C^n} \frac{du}{\det R(u)\,[F(u)^*R(u)^{-1}F(u)]^{n+1}} . \tag{11} \] In particular the determinant is present in the exact full-space formula. We use [C]'s specified normalization to obtain its compact unweighted proxy, rather than discard this determinant by assumption. Let \(\mathcal U_N\) be the product of the \(q\) retained physical unit packet balls. The compact integral is \[ \boxed{\quad \mathcal J_N=\frac{(Nq)!}{\pi^{Nq}}\int_{\mathcal U_N} \|F(u)\|^{-2(Nq+1)}du,\qquad \deg\|F\|^2\le2d_{q+1}. \quad} \tag{12} \] Lebesgue measure is in the chosen physical orthonormal coordinates. Its dimension, denominator power and factorial are part of the formula. For every fixed source tree, uniformly over prescribed packets with the recorded normalized bounds, [C] proves \[ |K_N|^2=\frac{\widehat B_N^{\,2}}{\mathcal J_N} (1+O_{\mathscr T}(N^{-1})) \quad(K_N\ne0). \tag{13} \] This statement is for all sufficiently large levels. At a source zero, \(\mathcal J_N=+\infty\) and its reciprocal is zero. When \(q=0\), use the one-point integral: \(\mathcal J_N=|k_N|^{-2}\), including the same zero convention. Then the equality in (13) is exact. To check applicability, the compressed compiler has the same unique-parent pattern, local arity at most two, closing norm bound and triangular real Jacobian one as the source in [C]. On the retained unit balls, its proof gives \(\|D(u)\|\le\sigma_N/(1-\sigma_N)\). Outside those balls the full residual norm exceeds \(1/4\). These are precisely the two source-specific inputs in [C]'s determinant and exterior estimates. All constants depend on the fixed compressed tree and not on a possibly small nonzero \(K_N\). ## 4. What the degree bound does and does not simplify The earlier branching result [B] eliminates constant-coefficient linear response variables from a clamped quartic minimum, retaining \(2q\) packets and preserving that auxiliary minimum. Here we instead compose the actual normalized recursion first, then apply the one-child reduction. This gives \(q\) retained packets and a new auxiliary energy and integral. Their numerical values are not identified with those in [B], [L], or the uncompressed [C]. The closed source and the original budget product in (4) are exact. The logarithmic count in [S] concerns termination of triangular Newton repairs, via Strahler rank. It does not state (8). The argument above bounds the degree of the explicitly eliminated residual vector by choosing which child to retain. No novelty is claimed for the combinatorial principle that repeated halving gives a logarithmic bound. This degree bound must not replace the scalar degree in the finite-fiber argument. Let \(G\) be the full compressed residual automorphism and \(f(r)=c_N^{\rm new}(G^{-1}(r))_{\rm top}\) for the rescaled compiler. Its degree is still at most \(\ell\). In fact put every internal residual equal to zero and set \(r_{\rm leaf}=t\,a_{\rm leaf}^{\rm new}\), using the true rescaled leaf constants. Homogeneity gives the exact restriction \[ f(r(t))=k_N(1-t)^\ell . \tag{14} \] If \(K_N\ne0\), this proves \(\deg f=\ell\). Thus (8) concerns the vector after integrating linear packet variables, not a lower generic degree for the original scalar fibers. Even when \(F\) is affine, its coefficients contain the complete actual short components and the prescribed closing row. They can carry cancellation. The remaining geometric task is an upper estimate on \(\mathcal J_N/\widehat B_N^2\) with the original cap retained. The reduced degree, slotwise multiaffinity and compact domain do not supply that estimate or a finite-exception theorem. Overlapping contraction networks with shared descendants are outside the tree argument. ## Complete inputs and closest coverage The five complete texts were read at matching versions. [P] supplies the actual full physical source; [L,C] supply exact elimination and compact calibration; [B,S] identify the closest existing tree reductions. title: A faithful middle-weight model for Conway face operators

# A faithful middle-weight model for Conway face operators 21 November 2026. Research note. Earlier final notes and the public manuscripts remain unchanged. The second-head wrap correction between the first and middle local five-point descriptions vanishes on a particular invariant physical subspace. That subspace still represents the entire Conway boundary algebra faithfully, including its repeated-root derivatives. Thus the correction can be removed there before taking any asymptotic estimate. The original closing and turn must be reconstructed from the complete boundary packet. The all-array physical trace is not simply restricted to this subspace. Other endpoint projectors and the full relative coefficient cycles remain. ## 1. The physical subspace Fix \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), and \(Q=q^2\). The original two physical heads have basis \(|a,bangle\), \(0\le a,b\le d\). Their clock operators are \[ Z|a,bangle=Q^a|a,bangle,\qquad T|a,bangle=Q^b|a,bangle . 	ag{1} \] Use the actual cyclic face unit \(X=xS_2S_1^{-1}\), with \(x=-q^{-1}\) and the original nonzero wrap marks. It lowers the first index and raises the second, cyclically, and satisfies \[ XZ=QZX,\qquad XT=Q^{-1}TX. 	ag{2} \] Here \(S_i\) raises head \(i\), with coefficient one before its last index and wrap coefficient \(\mu_i
e0\); the original marks obey \(\mu_2=x^N\mu_1\). Define \[ \mathcal M_N=\operatorname{span}\{v_a=|a,d-aangle:0\le a\le d\}. 	ag{3} \] The clock \(ZT\) has eigenvalue \(Q^{a+b}\) at \(|a,bangle\). Because \(0\le a+b\le2N-2\), the congruence \(a+b\equiv d\pmod N\) forces \(a+b=d\). Consequently \(\mathcal M_N\) is the entire \(ZT=Q^d\) eigenspace. Equations (1)--(2) show that \(X,Z,T\), their spectral projectors, and every expression in these operators preserve \(\mathcal M_N\). An inverse, when defined on the full space, preserves it as well. On this subspace, \[ T=Q^{-1}Z^{-1}. 	ag{4} \] ## 2. The first/middle wrap correction disappears exactly In the same physical frame, the first and middle face descriptions use \[ n=e_1S_2=(Q-Z^{-1})X,\qquad c=n(I-E_d(T)), 	ag{5} \] where \(E_d(T)\) projects onto second-head index \(d\). Similarly \(E_j(Z)\) projects onto first-head index \(j\). The right-hand expression in (5) defines \(n\) directly; \(e_1\) is the original first-head Gauss lowering operator. The original finite Euler polynomial is \[ P_Q(A)=\sum_{h=0}^{d}  rac{(-1)^hQ^{h(h-1)/2}}{(Q;Q)_h}A^h. 	ag{6} \] Here \((Q;Q)_h=\prod_{j=1}^{h}(1-Q^j)\), with empty product one. Both \(n\) and \(c\) are nilpotent of order at most \(N\), and their Euler matrices are invertible. **Proposition 1.** On all of \(\mathcal M_N\), \[ n=c,\qquad P_Q(n)=P_Q(c). 	ag{7} \] **Proof.** The only vector of \(\mathcal M_N\) in the range of \(E_d(T)\) is \(v_0=|0,dangle\). The first lowering operator \(e_1\) kills first-head index zero. Therefore \(nE_d(T)|_{\mathcal M_N}=0\), which proves the first identity. Both operators preserve the subspace, so every power agrees there, giving the second identity. \(\square\) Equivalently the full-space transition \(P_Q(n)P_Q(c)^{-1}-I\) restricts to zero. Every local face factor in the two displayed five-point descriptions preserves this subspace, so subsequent such factors cannot make that restricted zero visible. No estimate of the correction's norm or geometric volume is needed for this representation. This removes precisely the second-head wrap correction in (5). It does not remove the strict first-head endpoint already present in \(n\), or the middle factor \(QX(I-E_0(Z))\). The projector \(E_0(Z)|_{\mathcal M_N}\) is nonzero. ## 3. Why the restriction retains the full boundary algebra Let \(\Omega_d\) be the original pair Casimir on \(\mathcal M_N\). In the ordered basis \(v_0,\ldots,v_d\), it is irreducible tridiagonal. The complete source theorem gives its characteristic and minimal polynomial \[ P_N(z)=\prod_{j=0}^{d}(z-c_j)=2T_N(z/2)+2,\qquad c_j=2\cos rac{(2j+1)\pi}{N}. 	ag{8} \] Here \(T_N\) is the Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind. Thus the representation \[ ho_N:H_N=\mathbb C[z]/(P_N)\longrightarrow \operatorname{End}(\mathcal M_N),\qquad ho_N(f)=f(\Omega_d) 	ag{9} \] is injective. In particular it retains the first derivatives at every double root. It is not the representation by values at distinct roots. Here a whole Hopf box means an actual two-head operator \(f(\Omega)\) from the complete Conway compiler. An individual face factor need not belong to this algebra. There is an explicit packet isomorphism as well. Put \[ s_r=\prod_{j=1}^{r}2\sin(\pi j/N),\qquad b_r(z)=s_r^{-2}\prod_{j=0}^{r-1}(c_j-z),\qquad s_0=1, \] \[ C_N= ig[b_0(\Omega_d)v_0\ \cdots\ b_d(\Omega_d)v_0 ig]. 	ag{10} \] A polynomial of degree \(r\) in an irreducible tridiagonal matrix, applied to \(v_0\), has support only in indices \(0,\ldots,r\). Its index-\(r\) coefficient is its leading coefficient times the nonzero unique outer path. Hence \(C_N\) is triangular with nonzero diagonal and is invertible. The map \[ \Xi_N(f)=f(\Omega_d)v_0=C_N\alpha,\qquad f=\sum_{r=0}^{d}\alpha_rb_r 	ag{11} \] is an isomorphism from the full packet space onto \(\mathcal M_N\). The original marked cap and Frobenius closing, and the genuine quarter-turn, are therefore exactly \[ m_N(y)=\mathbf e_0^{\mathsf T}C_N^{-1}y,\qquad \phi_N^{m pkt}(y)=\mathbf e_d^{\mathsf T}C_N^{-1}y,\qquad J_N^{m pkt}=C_NP_{m rev}C_N^{-1}. 	ag{12} \] The \(\mathbf e_i\) are standard coordinate vectors, and \(P_{m rev}\alpha\) reverses the \(N\) Newton coefficients; \(\phi_N^{m pkt}\) is a functional, not the scalar used below. These are the actual original closures and turn, since in Newton coordinates they are \(\alpha_0,\alpha_d\), and reversal. The turn is a linear packet operation; it is not asserted to be multiplicative on matrices. The Frobenius closing has a particularly simple extension to all middle-block matrices. Let \[ \Lambda_N= rac{(-1)^dN^2} {\prod_{j=0}^{d-1}(\Omega_d)_{j+1,j}},\qquad \Phi_N^{m end}(A)=\Lambda_N A_{d,0}. 	ag{12a} \] Every factor in the denominator is nonzero. For a polynomial of degree at most \(d\), only its leading term can reach the outer entry \((d,0)\). Since the original Frobenius functional is \((-1)^dN^2[z^d]f\), this proves \(\Phi_N^{m end}(f(\Omega_d))=\phi_N(f)\). It is the same closing as (12), with its full scalar retained. Multiplication of whole Hopf boxes is also exact: \[ ho_N(f)\Xi_N(g)=\Xi_N(fg). 	ag{13} \] One may use (13) or reconstruct the original bilinear Newton product through \(C_N^{-1}\). Together with (12), induction through any fixed literal Conway expression gives its original full packet and scalar. All recorded Cartan, framing and peripheral factors remain attached. For a local crossing factorization, restrict each displayed physical face factor to \(\mathcal M_N\) and multiply these full \(N\)-by-\(N\) matrices in the original order. The complete crossing is then the same whole Hopf box as before. One must not replace an individual non-Hopf face factor \(A\) by the polynomial packet reconstructed from \(Av_0\): the identity \((AB)v_0=ho_N(\Xi_N^{-1}(Av_0))Bv_0\) is not true for arbitrary face matrices. Formula (13) applies to whole Hopf boxes. ## 4. The factorial interface is an explicit unitary diagonal Write \(F_a=(Q;Q)_a\), \(0\le a<N\), and retain the original marked scalar \[ \varpi_N=\sqrt N\exp\left\{i\pi \left[ rac14- rac{N+N^{-1}}{12}ight]ight\}. 	ag{14} \] The middle marked clock and the inverse clock used in the first description are \[ \mathcal F_Z=\varpi_N\operatorname{diag}(F_a^{-1}),\qquad \mathcal F_T^{-1}=\varpi_N^{-1}\operatorname{diag}(F_b). 	ag{15} \] Their clock marks and endpoint logarithmic lifts are the original ones. Since \(b=d-a\) on \(\mathcal M_N\), \[ F_aF_{d-a}=N
u_a,\qquad 
u_a=(-1)^aQ^{a(a+1)/2} 	ag{16} \] gives the exact interface \[ \mathcal F_T^{-1}|_{\mathcal M_N} = rac{N}{\varpi_N^2}D_
u\, \mathcal F_Z|_{\mathcal M_N}. 	ag{17} \] To prove (16), use \(F_d=N\) and \(\prod_{j=N-a}^{N-1}(1-Q^j) =(-1)^aQ^{-a(a+1)/2}F_a\). All diagonal entries of \(D_
u\) and the scalar \(N/\varpi_N^2\) have modulus one. The diagonal is retained as an actual finite matrix. Its continuation satisfies \(
u_{a+N}=-
u_a\), so its cyclic conjugation has an endpoint correction. In the physical middle basis, \[ D_
u X D_
u^{-1} =-XZ^{-1}(I-2E_0(Z)). 	ag{18} \] At input \(a\ge1\) the diagonal ratio is \(
u_{a-1}/
u_a=-Q^{-a}\); at input zero it is \(
u_d/
u_0=1\). This proves (18), including the wrap. Multiplying by the actual nilpotent coefficient removes that one reflection: \[ D_
u nD_
u^{-1}=-nZ^{-1}, 	ag{18a} \] because \(nE_0(Z)=0\) on this subspace. This is an exact identity for \(n\), not permission to erase the wall in the cyclic unit \(X\). Also \(
u_0=
u_d=1\). Thus the reconstructed Frobenius extension has, for every middle-block matrix \(A\), \[ \Phi_N^{m end}(D_
u A) =\Phi_N^{m end}(A D_
u) =\Phi_N^{m end}(D_
u A D_
u^{-1}) =\Phi_N^{m end}(A). 	ag{18b} \] This can be used at those exterior interfaces, or with a fully conjugated word. It does not delete an interior \(D_
u\) from an otherwise unchanged product, and it makes no such assertion for the other marked cap in (12). Unitarity in this paragraph concerns the literal physical basis \(v_a\). The Newton-coordinate matrix \(C_N^{-1}D_
u C_N\) need not be unitary or uniformly conditioned. No energy estimate is inferred from the unit-modulus diagonal alone. ## 5. Source and geometric scope The reconstructed source (12) is used on whole Hopf boxes. It is not the restriction of the all-array physical source \[ \Phi(W)= rac1N\sum_{a,c,b}g_bW_{(c,b),(a,b)} 	ag{19} \] to arbitrary face matrices, where \(g_b=(xQ^{-b})^{1-N}\). Indeed the projector onto \(|1,dangle\) has zero middle block but (19) has value \(g_d/N
e0\). Thus (19) cannot be recovered from a middle block on all arrays. The Hopf reconstruction is indispensable. Every local full-function coefficient realization remains its original circle-minus-radial functional. Restricting a finite matrix identity commutes with these exact finite-dimensional coefficient integrals. It does not select one component of their cycles or replace a full-function moment by a scalar evaluation. The result gives an exact, smaller local representation in which the specified first/middle wrap correction disappears, without losing any repeated-root Casimir direction. This is a fixed-root statement, not an off-root quantum-family identity. It neither places every geometric point in a common positive face polarization nor proves that the turn kernel transports a Rivin contour. The surviving first-head walls, marked relative cycles, source coefficient, and coordinate-change costs still require their own geometric estimates. No new volume identity or finite-exception theorem follows here. ## Complete proof sources All four complete matching texts were read. The first supplies the faithful Casimir block, full Newton source and genuine turn. The next two supply the actual face operators and marked factorials. title: A mixed physical and Newton metric for the original Conway source
text: # A mixed physical and Newton metric for the original Conway source 24 November 2026. Written research proof. Multiplication takes one uniform physical packet and one Newton packet to a Newton packet with bilinear norm at most one. This follows from the actual adjoint formulas, without comparing the condition numbers of the two metrics. A fixed Conway tree can consequently retain one Newton leaf, or two leaves meeting at its highest product, while all other branches use the physical metric. The structural normalization cost is constant except for a possible factor \(\sqrt N\) at the root. The resulting compact reciprocal integral keeps the original closing. No geometric lower bound is proved. ## 1. The two complete packet metrics Fix \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\), and \(x=q^d=-q^{-1}\). Use the actual physical pair algebra of [P]: \[ \mathcal A_N=\mathbb C[\Omega]\simeq\mathbb C[z]/P_N,\qquad P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2,\qquad \dim\mathcal A_N=N . \tag{1} \] Here \(T_N\) is the Chebyshev polynomial. Every double-root first normal and the odd simple-root value remain in (1). Give the original balanced head basis \(w_0,\ldots,w_d\) its uniform orthonormal metric. For \(f\in\mathcal A_N\), write \[ \iota(f)=f(\Omega),\qquad \|f\|_{\rm ph}=\|\iota(f)\|_{\rm HS},\qquad \|f\|_{\rm mat}=\|\iota(f)\|_{\rm op}. \tag{2} \] The Hilbert--Schmidt norm is unnormalized, so \(\|1\|_{\rm ph}=N\). The other Hilbert norm makes the full Newton basis orthonormal: \[ c_j=q^{2j+1}+q^{-2j-1},\qquad S_r=\prod_{h=1}^r2\sin(\pi h/N),\quad S_0=1,\qquad b_r(z)=S_r^{-2}\prod_{j<r}(c_j-z),\quad 0\le r\le d . \tag{3} \] Write \(\|\cdot\|_{\rm Newt}\) for this norm and \(f^\sharp(z)=\overline{f(\bar z)}\) for coefficient reflection. All \(b_r\) have real coefficients. The original unscaled turn \(\mathcal T\), multiplication \(M_f:g\mapsto fg\), and both original closing rows obey [A,P] \[ \begin{gathered} \mathcal T b_r=b_{d-r},\qquad \mathcal T^2=I,\\ \|\mathcal T f\|_{\rm Newt}=\|f\|_{\rm Newt},\qquad \|\mathcal T f\|_{\rm ph}=\|f\|_{\rm ph},\\ M_f^{\dagger_{\rm Newt}}=\mathcal T M_{f^\sharp}\mathcal T,\\ \lambda_0(f)=f(c_0),\qquad \lambda_d(f)=\phi(f),\qquad \|\lambda_0\|_{{\rm Newt},*} =\|\lambda_d\|_{{\rm Newt},*}=1,\qquad \lambda_0\mathcal T=\lambda_d . \end{gathered} \tag{4} \] The physical dual norms of these two rows are at most one. The ordinary cups, cap, unrestricted mark, pivot and framing are exactly those fixing (4); no new closure is introduced here. ## 2. A constant-one bridge, including matrix coefficients Let \(\mathsf S\) exchange the two physical heads. In the balanced metric the literal generators satisfy \[ E^*=-F,\qquad F^*=-E,\qquad K^*=K^{-1}. \tag{5} \] Using \(E_\Sigma=E_1K_2+E_2\), \(F_\Sigma=F_1+K_1^{-1}F_2\), and the original \(\Omega=F_\Sigma E_\Sigma+qK_1K_2+q^{-1}K_1^{-1}K_2^{-1}\), this gives \[ E_\Sigma^*=-\mathsf S F_\Sigma\mathsf S,\quad F_\Sigma^*=-\mathsf S E_\Sigma\mathsf S,\quad \Omega^*=\mathsf S\Omega\mathsf S . \tag{6} \] Indeed adjoint reverses \(F_\Sigma E_\Sigma\), and the first two identities restore that order after the exchange; the two Cartan terms are exchanged by conjugating their scalars. Polynomial functional calculus therefore proves \[ \iota(f)^*=\mathsf S\iota(f^\sharp)\mathsf S,\qquad \|f^\sharp\|_{\rm mat}=\|f\|_{\rm mat}. \tag{7} \] **Theorem 1.** For every two complete packets, \[ \boxed{\quad \|M_f\|_{{\rm Newt}\to{\rm Newt}}\le\|f\|_{\rm mat}, \qquad \|fg\|_{\rm Newt}\le\|f\|_{\rm ph}\|g\|_{\rm Newt}. \quad} \tag{8} \] Commutativity permits exchange of the two inputs. *Proof.* The same finite linear map \(B=(\mathcal T M_{f^\sharp}\mathcal T)M_f\) is positive in the Newton metric, by (4). Its spectral radius is thus \(\|M_f\|_{\rm Newt}^2\). Compute its radius instead using its operator norm in the physical packet metric. Actual composition of pair matrices gives \(\|M_h\|_{{\rm ph}\to{\rm ph}}\le\|h\|_{\rm mat}\). The physical unitarity of the genuine turn and (7) imply \[ \|M_f\|_{\rm Newt}^2 =\operatorname{rad}(B) \le\|B\|_{{\rm ph}\to{\rm ph}} \le\|f^\sharp\|_{\rm mat}\|f\|_{\rm mat} =\|f\|_{\rm mat}^2. \tag{9} \] Finally \(\|f\|_{\rm mat}\le\|f\|_{\rm ph}\) proves (8). No change-of-frame bound between the metrics was used. \(\square\) There is also a full matrix amplification. Let \(\mathbf f=(f_{ij})\in M_{a,b}(\mathcal A_N)\), let \(\mathbf M_{\mathbf f}\) act on \(b\) Newton packets by \((g_j)_j\mapsto(\sum_j f_{ij}g_j)_i\), and put \(\mathbf F=(\iota(f_{ij}))\), acting on \(b\) physical pairs. Then \[ \boxed{\qquad \|\mathbf M_{\mathbf f}\|_{{\rm Newt}^b\to{\rm Newt}^a} \le\|\mathbf F\|_{\rm op}. \qquad} \tag{10} \] For completeness, set \(\mathbf f^\ddagger=(f_{ji}^\sharp)\) and \(\mathcal T_b=I_b\otimes\mathcal T\). Equation (4) gives \(\mathbf M_{\mathbf f}^\dagger =\mathcal T_b\mathbf M_{\mathbf f^\ddagger}\mathcal T_a\). The coefficient block matrix \((\iota(f_{ji}^\sharp))\) is \((I_b\otimes\mathsf S)\mathbf F^*(I_a\otimes\mathsf S)\). Physical left multiplication by a block matrix has norm at most that block matrix's operator norm on the direct sum of pair spaces. The outer packet turns also have physical norm one. Applying (9) to \(\mathbf M_{\mathbf f}^\dagger\mathbf M_{\mathbf f}\) proves (10), also for rectangular sizes. The bound is independent of \(a,b\). It is not a claim that the Hilbert tensor flattening of the bilinear map in (8) has norm one. Taking \(g=1\) in the first inequality of (8) gives the useful same-packet comparison \[ \|f\|_{\rm Newt}\le\|f\|_{\rm mat} \le\|f\|_{\rm ph}. \tag{11} \] ## 3. One Newton path through an arbitrary literal tree Fix a literal tree with \(L\) prescribed leaf occurrences, \(s\) proper vertices, products and genuine turns. Its original scalar is \(K_N=\eta_N\lambda(A_{\rm top})\), where \(\lambda\in\{\lambda_0,\lambda_d\}\) and \(\eta_N\) is its recorded known external factor. Every prescribed leaf is its entire actual packet \(A_\ell\), not its distinct-root values. Choose any leaf \(\ell_*\). Give every vertex on its path to the root the Newton metric and every off-path vertex the physical metric. At a product on the path, exactly one child has the Newton metric. Equation (8) bounds that bilinear map by one. Off-path products have physical bilinear norm at most one by matrix composition. Turns have norm one in either metric, and the root row has dual norm one. These assertions hold on all packet inputs, not only on the prescribed forward field. For each proper vertex and the scalar root choose the known budgets \[ b_v= \begin{cases} 16\max(1,\|A_\ell\|_{\rm Newt}),&v=\ell=\ell_*,\\ 16\max(1,\|A_\ell\|_{\rm ph}),&v=\ell\ne\ell_*,\\ 16,&v\text{ is a product or turn}, \end{cases} \qquad b_{\rm root}=16\max(1,|\eta_N|). \tag{12} \] Thus every normalized map, leaf and closing has its respective bilinear, linear or vector norm at most \(1/16\). There is no exponential Newton multiplication budget. Relative to the physical budgets of [P], only one leaf factor changes: \[ {B_{\rm one}\over B_{\rm ph}} ={\max(1,\|A_{\ell_*}\|_{\rm Newt}) \over\max(1,\|A_{\ell_*}\|_{\rm ph})} \le1,\qquad B_{\rm one}=\prod_v b_v . \tag{13} \] This is a comparison of known normalization products, not of the numerical minima or integrals in different packet metrics. ## 4. Two Newton paths and one terminal quotient metric Suppose \(L\ge2\). Let \(v_*\) be the highest binary product; above it there are only genuine turns before the scalar closing. Choose one leaf in each child subtree of \(v_*\). Use the one-path assignment inside each child subtree, making both packets entering \(v_*\) Newton packets. All remaining vertices below it are physical. At \(v_*\) use the already constructed multiplication quotient of [Q]. In fixed Newton coordinates let \[ M:\mathcal H_{\rm Newt}\otimes_2\mathcal H_{\rm Newt} \longrightarrow\mathcal A_N,\qquad C=MM^\dagger,\qquad \|y\|_{\rm quot}^2=y^\dagger C^{-1}y . \tag{14} \] Multiplication is surjective since \(M(y\otimes1)=y\); hence \(C>0\), with every boundary coordinate retained. The map \(C^{-1/2}M\) is a coisometry, so the product into this quotient metric has bilinear norm at most one. Transport the quotient metric through each turn above \(v_*\): define \(\|\mathcal T y\|_{\rm next}=\|y\|_{\rm previous}\). Every such turn has norm one by definition, with its literal unscaled matrix retained. If there are \(h\) turns above \(v_*\), put \(\lambda'=\lambda\mathcal T^h\). This is either \(\lambda_0\) or \(\lambda_d\). The exact original rows give [A,Q] \[ \|\lambda_0M\|_{\otimes_2,*}=1,\qquad \|\lambda_dM\|_{\otimes_2,*}=\sqrt N . \tag{15} \] Indeed \(\lambda_0(ab)=a_0b_0\), while \(\lambda_d(ab)=a^{\mathsf T}Jb\) with \(J\) the reversal matrix. Their flattened rows have respectively one and \(N\) unit entries. Consequently the final transported quotient has root dual cost \[ \gamma_N= \begin{cases}1,&\lambda'=\lambda_0,\\ \sqrt N,&\lambda'=\lambda_d. \end{cases} \tag{16} \] Use Newton leaf budgets at the two selected leaves, physical budgets at all others, budget \(16\) at every product and turn, and \[ b_{\rm root}=16\max(1,|\eta_N|\gamma_N). \tag{17} \] This gives a second full-dimensional compiler with every normalized local norm at most \(1/16\). Its budget product satisfies \[ {B_{\rm two}\over B_{\rm ph}} ={\max(1,|\eta_N|\gamma_N)\over\max(1,|\eta_N|)} \prod_{\ell\ {\rm selected}} {\max(1,\|A_\ell\|_{\rm Newt}) \over\max(1,\|A_\ell\|_{\rm ph})}. \tag{18} \] The quotient and its transport depend only on the original operations, not on the selected leaf values or the unknown scalar. No comparison of its condition number with the physical metric is used. The direct scalar upper bound is slightly sharper than the flattened root budget: both bilinear rows \(\lambda_0(ab)\) and \(\lambda_d(ab)\) have norm one on separately unit Newton inputs. Inducting below \(v_*\) therefore gives \[ |K_N|\le|\eta_N| \prod_{\ell\ {\rm selected}}\|A_\ell\|_{\rm Newt} \prod_{\ell\ {\rm other}}\|A_\ell\|_{\rm ph}. \tag{19} \] There is no factor \(\sqrt N\) in (19). That factor in (16) is the linear dual norm required for the full quotient packet compiler. ## 5. The same original scalar in a compact reciprocal integral Apply [C] to either assignment above, with its actual packet metrics and budget product \(B_{\rm mix}\). Multiply all \(s\) proper budgets and the root budget by \(N\): \[ \widehat B_{\rm mix}=N^{s+1}B_{\rm mix},\qquad \sigma_N=(16N)^{-1}. \tag{20} \] In orthonormal coordinates for these metrics the residual map still has own-output coefficient \(-I\), polynomial triangular inverse, and real Jacobian one. Its energy, including the original scalar row, has degree at most four. Keep one child per binary product and solve the other packet equations exactly. Write \(F_{\rm mix}(u)\) for the remaining residuals and scalar row. Then, with \(n=N(L-1)\) and the product \(\mathcal U_N\) of retained unit balls, \[ \mathcal J_{\rm mix}={n!\over\pi^n} \int_{\mathcal U_N}\|F_{\rm mix}(u)\|^{-2(n+1)}du . \tag{21} \] The measure is rebuilt in the stated orthonormal coordinates. For a fixed tree, [C] proves uniformly over its normalized leaf choices \[ \boxed{\qquad |K_N|^2={\widehat B_{\rm mix}^{\,2}\over\mathcal J_{\rm mix}} \bigl(1+O_{\mathscr T}(N^{-1})\bigr) \qquad(K_N\ne0). \qquad} \tag{22} \] At a source zero the integral is infinite and its reciprocal is zero. The one-point convention covers \(L=1\). All phases and full Hermite directions survive these metric choices and forward substitutions. The actual single signed crossing has, with \(\kappa=q^{d^2/2}\), [A] \[ R^{\pm1}=\kappa^{\pm1}\sum_{r=0}^d(-q)^{\pm r}b_r,\qquad \|R^{\pm1}\|_{\rm Newt}=\sqrt N . \tag{23} \] Thus one or two such selected leaves have this explicit polynomial leaf budget. An arbitrary fixed \(R^p\) must retain its actual Newton norm; no polynomial bound for all powers is asserted. The gain is a source-exact choice of packet metrics with smaller known leaf factors and no large Newton structural multiplication budget. Equations (21)--(22) define new normalized integrals, not a free change in the value of an earlier integral. The original cap and the new budgets must both remain. The dimension and denominator power grow with \(N\) when \(L>1\). A geometric upper estimate on \(\mathcal J_{\rm mix}/\widehat B_{\rm mix}^{\,2}\), or an original closing lower certificate, is still required. There is no new volume-conjecture case or finite-exception theorem. ## Complete inputs and coverage The complete matching texts below fix the two source metrics, the existing quotient construction, and the compact integral comparison. The mixed inequality and its path assignments are proved above. | Label | Complete text | Lines | SHA256 | | --- | --- | ---: | --- | | A | [Newton turn, adjoints and original rows](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_newton_turn_positive_gram.md) | 434 | d8b21fa8db909120035e86e997a0e02cb84f8dce2dcf6fb244bb5c85c17e28a3 | | P | [Uniform physical source compiler](research_conway_uniform_physical_quartic.md) | 477 | 39895b430535f565d30133b46ef57f67589207bc83f40597ffe96e2ce79bbda8 | | Q | [Full multiplication quotient and closing costs](research_conway_full_boundary_quotient_gram.md) | 463 | debe56dbad8151b90d44d0fccbf0dcf33dafb780370e01c8acdadbd2939dc077 | | C | [Compact reciprocal source comparison](research_conway_compact_reciprocal_source.md) | 321 | 94f261ac94d20b676cf02c3fb39514ebcb7e2a7c42e114bc5bb0ecb413a7e2b4 |

title: Orthogonal elimination of the linear Conway packet variables
status: Exact elimination and controlled boundary Gram; geometric rate open
text:
# Orthogonal elimination of the linear Conway packet variables 21 November 2026. Research note. Earlier final notes and public manuscripts remain unchanged. After retaining one child packet at each binary gate, every other packet can be eliminated by an unconstrained, uniformly positive definite linear solve. The original unit-ball constraints on those variables are automatically inactive. The resulting objective is the norm of a genuine orthogonal projection, with its full Gram matrix retained. A second form uses only the retained gate equations and the original scalar closing row. Its boundary Gram matrix lies between \(I\) and \((226/225)I\), uniformly in the level and tree size. This is a reduction of the actual finite variational problem, not a geometric evaluation of its minimum. ## 1. The original energy and the variables to retain Use the complete normalized compiler of the [convex source theorem](research_convex_normalized_conway_source.md). At level \(N\), there are \(s\) proper packet variables in the full complex Newton space \(H_N\), including the repeated-root directions. Each prescribed leaf, linear turn and bilinear product has recorded Hilbert--Schmidt norm at most \(\sigma=1/16\). The original normalized closing row is \(L\), with \(\|L\|\le\sigma\). The energy is \[ E(x)=\sum_{v	ext{ proper}}\|\Phi_v((x_c)_c)-x_v\|^2 +|Lx_{m top}|^2. 	ag{1} \] Its feasible set is the product of unit packet balls. Its real Hessian lies between \(I\) and \(3I\). The complete original marked source satisfies \[ B_{m tot}^2e_*\le |K_N|^2 \le\gamma B_{m tot}^2e_*,\qquad e_*:=\min E,\quad\gamma=197/196. 	ag{2} \] The normalization budget \(B_{m tot}\) is retained throughout. Let \(p\) be the number of binary product gates. At each such gate choose exactly one of its two child occurrences. Retain the packets at the chosen occurrences and call their list \(u\). Distinct gates choose distinct variables, because every proper variable has one parent. There are exactly \(p\) retained packets. The top packet is never chosen: its parent is the scalar closing root. Call the other \(q=s-p\) packets \(z\). Fix \(u\) in its product of unit balls. At each product, one child is retained and the other is eliminated. Therefore the stacked vector of **all** proper residuals, together with the original scalar closing term, has the form \[ \mathcal R(u,z)=A(u)z+b(u) \in H_N^{\oplus s}\oplus\mathbb C. 	ag{3} \] The matrix \(A(u)\) is complex linear in \(z\); both \(A\) and \(b\) are affine functions of the complex retained coordinates. Indeed a product contributes a term bilinear in its retained child and its eliminated child, and its output contributes either \(-z_v\) or \(-u_v\). Leaves and turns are affine, and the closing component is the original row \(Lz_{m top}\). Thus \[ E(u,z)=\|A(u)z+b(u)\|^2. 	ag{4} \] Every complex phase remains in these coefficients. ## 2. The eliminated ball constraints are inactive In real coordinates, the \(z\)-Hessian of (4) is twice the real form of \(A^*A\). The principal Hessian bounds for (1) imply \[ 	frac12I\le A(u)^*A(u)\le	frac32I. 	ag{5} \] For fixed \(u\), this Hessian is independent of \(z\), so these bounds hold for the entire unconstrained quadratic problem. It remains to show that its unconstrained solution lies in the original balls. The half-gradient map of the full source theorem obeys \[ x-	frac12
abla E(x)\in	frac{33}{256}\mathcal D 	ag{6} \] whenever \(x\) is feasible. Freeze the retained variables and apply only its eliminated components: \[ T_u(z)=z-	frac12
abla_zE(u,z). 	ag{7} \] This map sends the eliminated product balls into their strict \(33/256\) contraction. Its derivative is the real form of \(I-A^*A\), whose norm is at most \(1/2\) by (5). Thus its iterates converge to a unique fixed point in those balls. The stationary equation there is the unconstrained normal equation. Consequently \[  oxed{\quad z_*(u)=-(A(u)^*A(u))^{-1}A(u)^*b(u),\quad} \qquad \|(z_*(u))_v\|\le33/256. 	ag{8} \] There are no active-ball cases in this inner problem. Define \(f(u)=E(u,z_*(u))\). The exact reduction of the original minimum is \[ e_*=\min_{\|u_v\|\le1}f(u). 	ag{9} \] Only \(2Np\) outer real variables remain. For \(p=0\), there is no outer minimization and (8) evaluates the entire quadratic minimum. ## 3. The correct orthogonal projection The matrix \[ \Pi(u)=I-A(u)(A(u)^*A(u))^{-1}A(u)^* 	ag{10} \] is Hermitian and satisfies \(\Pi^2=\Pi\). It is the orthogonal projection onto \(\ker A(u)^*\) in the stacked residual space of (3). Equations (8)--(10) give \[  oxed{\quad f(u)=\|\Pi(u)b(u)\|^2.\quad} 	ag{11} \] Because \(A\) has full column rank \(Nq\), this projection has complex rank \[ Ns+1-Nq=Np+1. 	ag{12} \] In particular the original scalar closing component is retained in this orthogonal complement. Squaring arbitrary coefficients in a different spanning family would not give (11); the inverse Gram matrix \((A^*A)^{-1}\) is required. The function \(f\) is a real rational function of the retained coordinates, smooth on a neighborhood of their closed product of balls. Its real Hessian still satisfies \[ I\le D^2f\le3I. 	ag{13} \] To prove this, differentiate the stationary equation in (8). The Hessian of \(f\) is the Schur complement \[ D^2f=H_{uu}-H_{uz}H_{zz}^{-1}H_{zu} 	ag{14} \] of the Hessian of \(E\) at \((u,z_*(u))\). For a retained variation \(h\), its quadratic form is \[ h^{\mathsf T}D^2f h =\min_k (h,k)^{\mathsf T}D^2E(h,k). \] The lower bound is at least \(\|h\|^2\). Choosing \(k=0\) gives the upper bound \(3\|h\|^2\). This proves (13), including at boundary points by the smooth formula (8). It does not assert that the reduced rational function is a polynomial of degree four. For a feasible retained trial field there is also the smaller gradient certificate \[ f(u)-	frac12\|
abla_u f(u)\|^2\le e_*\le f(u). 	ag{14a} \] Complete the square in the lower Hessian inequality (13), exactly as for the original energy. At \((u,z_*(u))\) the eliminated gradient is zero, and \(
abla_u f=
abla_u E\), so only the retained \(2Np\) real derivatives are required. The witness after elimination is rational; evaluating it in the original lifted variables recovers the original degree-six expression. ## 4. A smaller boundary Gram matrix There is another exact form of (11) that displays the retained equations explicitly. Split the residual rows into those whose gate outputs are eliminated and all the other rows: \[ r_z=T(u)z+b_z(u),\qquad r_o=C(u)z+b_o(u). 	ag{15} \] The second list contains the \(p\) retained gate equations and the original scalar closing row. The first square matrix has form \[ T=-I+A_{zz}. 	ag{16} \] Order vertices by ancestry. Then \(A_{zz}\) is strictly triangular. Every row has at most one eliminated child, and every column occurs in at most one parent row. Each block has norm at most \(\sigma\), so \[ \|A_{zz}\|\le\sigma,\qquad T^{-1}=-\sum_{j=0}^{q-1}A_{zz}^{j},\qquad \|T^{-1}\|\le16/15. 	ag{17} \] Likewise every row of \(C\) has at most one eliminated child. Its columns occur in at most one such row, counting the closing row as the top packet's unique parent. Hence \(\|C\|\le\sigma\). Set \[ D=CT^{-1},\qquad F=b_o-CT^{-1}b_z. 	ag{18} \] Then \(\|D\|\le1/15\). Changing variables from \(z\) to \(r_z\) in the unconstrained quadratic problem gives \[ f(u)=\min_r\{\|r\|^2+\|Dr+F\|^2\} =F(u)^*(I+D(u)D(u)^*)^{-1}F(u). 	ag{19} \] For example, the minimizing residuals are \(r= -D^*(I+DD^*)^{-1}F\) and \(r_o=(I+DD^*)^{-1}F\). Thus \[  oxed{\quad  rac{225}{226}\|F(u)\|^2\le f(u)\le\|F(u)\|^2. \quad} 	ag{20} \] This is the boundary Gram matrix for the residual elimination. Its size is \(Np+1\), its spectrum lies in \([1,226/225]\), and its conditioning does not grow with the length of an eliminated corridor. The vector \(F\) has a direct meaning. Put \[ z_0(u)=-T(u)^{-1}b_z(u). 	ag{21} \] It solves every eliminated gate equation exactly, by the original forward recursion with the retained packets prescribed. Each of its packets has norm at most \(\sigma\). The remaining residuals and the original closing value at this field are exactly \(F(u)\). The finite triangular inverse in (17) makes \(z_0\), and hence \(F\), polynomial in \(u\). Their degrees can grow with the fixed expression; their evaluation is still a finite sequence of the original local operations. ## 5. An unweighted retained-packet comparison One can compare \(\|F\|^2\) directly with the source with a smaller constant than follows by combining (2) and (20). Split the derivative of the forward maps at \((u,z_0(u))\) into its retained and eliminated blocks \(A_{uu},A_{uz},A_{zu},A_{zz}\). Each of these four block matrices has at most one input block in each row and one parent block in each column. Thus all four have norm at most \(\sigma\). Implicit differentiation of the gate-exact equations in (21) gives \[ z_0'(u)=(I-A_{zz})^{-1}A_{zu},\qquad \|z_0'(u)\|\le1/15. 	ag{22} \] Write \(F=(G_o,c)\), where \(G_o\) is the list of retained gate residuals and \(c(u)=L(z_0(u))_{m top}\) is the original scalar closing component. Then \[  egin{split} DG_o&=-I+A_{uu}+A_{uz}(I-A_{zz})^{-1}A_{zu},\ \|DG_o+I\|&\le1/15,\qquad \|Dc\|\le1/240. \end{split} 	ag{23} \] The last bound uses the fact that the top proper packet is always eliminated. These bounds hold on the whole retained product of balls: the forward recursion in (21) keeps all eliminated packets feasible. Let \(a\) be the true normalized packet field, let \(u_a\) be its retained coordinates, and put \(k=K_N/B_{m tot}\). We have \(G_o(u_a)=0\) and \(c(u_a)=k\). Integrating (23) along a feasible segment gives \[ \|G_o(u)-G_o(u_a)\|\ge	frac{14}{15}\|u-u_a\|, \qquad |c(u)-k|\le	frac1{224}\|G_o(u)\|. 	ag{24} \] Consequently Cauchy--Schwarz, followed by the competitor \(u_a\), proves the direct comparison \[  oxed{\quad  rac{|k|^2}{1+224^{-2}} \le\min_{\|u_v\|\le1}\|F(u)\|^2\le|k|^2. \quad} 	ag{25} \] It includes source zeros. When there are no retained variables, \(F\) is simply the scalar \(k\), so the unweighted value is exactly \(|k|^2\). For a fixed tree, restoring \(B_{m tot}^2\) in (25) gives the same exponential rate as the original source, with no uncontrolled Gram loss. This does not assert convexity or degree four for the compressed polynomial \(\|F(u)\|^2\). ## 6. Scope of the simplification The exact reduced minimum in (9) satisfies the unchanged source bounds (2). Equation (20) also permits replacing its boundary Gram by the identity with an explicitly proved constant comparison. That step is valid because (17)--(20) control this particular Gram matrix. It is not a rule for discarding arbitrary quantum boundary metrics. This construction concerns the budget-normalized recursion errors. It is distinct from a quotient metric on the physical tangle synthesis map, which can have exponential condition number. All original normalization factors remain in \(B_{m tot}\). No actual crossing or product is asserted to be unitary in an unscaled physical metric. Elimination has removed the inner constrained optimization, exposed a true orthogonal projection and reduced the number of nonlinear packet variables. It has not supplied a positive geometric trial value at the volume rate. The original coherent closing remains one component of \(F\), and exact source cancellation remains possible. The finite degree-four formulation can be retained by keeping the linear variables and the original gate equations; explicit elimination instead produces the rational function (11), or the higher-degree polynomial vector in (18). Neither representation alone gives the missing hyperbolic lower bound after arbitrary fixed partial fillings. ## Complete proof source and coverage The sole complete proof source was read at the matching version: | Source | SHA-256 | |---|---| | [Complete normalized Conway source](research_convex_normalized_conway_source.md) | 6b89b4c6a67ef7a32cc41a5966c650f32de65d284ae7b70d94a71bddba21df3c | Projecting out variables that enter linearly is the established variable-projection method; see the primary record of [Golub--Pereyra (1973)](https://epubs.siam.org/doi/10.1137/0710036). Its proof is not used here. The source-specific assertions proved above are the inactive packet balls, uniform Gram bounds, exact retained closing component and full-Hermite reduction for the actual tree. No novelty is claimed for least squares or orthogonal projection. Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used. No mathematical program, numerical optimization, test, build, git operation or earlier-final edit was performed.

# Finite-fiber orthogonality and exact integration of linear Conway packets Written proof, 24 November 2026. The unchanged positive reciprocal integral gives an all-level lower bound for the original scalar with loss at most the number of leaves. The proof uses the finite degree of the actual residual closing and orthogonal projection on the fibers of an explicit rational map. It is a shorter, weaker comparison than the relative asymptotic of [W]. All linearly entering packets can also be integrated out exactly, leaving one variable packet per binary product. It does not estimate the integral from hyperbolic geometry. ## 1. The original source and statement Use the full physical Conway compiler of [P] at any level \(N\ge2\). Fix a literal tree with \(s\ge1\) proper vertices and \(L\ge1\) prescribed leaf occurrences. Each packet has all \(N\) complex coordinates of \(\mathcal A_N\), including the first normals at double Casimir roots. Put \(D=Ns\), and use physical orthonormal coordinates \(x\in\mathbb C^D\), with real Lebesgue measure \(dx\). Keep the normalized maps, the original closing row \(c\), and the positive budget product \(\mathcal B_N\) unchanged. Set \[ G_v(x)=\Phi_v((x_j)_{j	ext{ child of }v})-x_v,\qquad E_N(x)=\|G(x)\|^2+|cx|^2,\qquad \mathcal P_N={D!\over\pi^D} \int_{\mathbb C^D}E_N(x)^{-D-1}\,dx . 	ag{1} \] This is exactly the undamped integral of [U,W]. Its base has degree at most four; its denominator exponent grows with \(D\). The entire original mark, phases, turns, framing and external factors remain in (1). e0\), and infinite when \(K_N=0\). No prior nonvanishing assumption, physical coefficient smallness estimate, or large-level asymptotic is needed for (2). Order children before parents. The exact inverse of the residual map is the polynomial recursion \[ H(r)_v=\Phi_v((H(r)_j)_j)-r_v,\qquad \det_{\mathbb C}DG=(-1)^D,\qquad |\det_{\mathbb R}DH|=1 . 	ag{3} \] Indeed each step solves uniquely for its output packet. A leaf has degree one in \(r\); a turn preserves degree; at a product, the two child degree bounds add. Each subtree has at least one leaf, so the additional term \(-r_v\) respects that bound. The scalar \(k\) is used in the proof, not supplied to define (1). Changing variables by (3) makes its denominator \(\|r\|^2+|f(r)|^2\), with exactly the same measure. ## 2. For a generic \(w\), all points of its fiber have the form \[ r_j=t_jw,\qquad p_w(t_j)=0,\qquad p_w(t)=f(tw)-t . 	ag{8} \] Its constant coefficient is \(k\), so no \(t_j\) is zero.
