If \(f(0)=0\), holomorphy gives \(|f(r)|\le C\|r\|\) near zero. The integral then dominates a positive multiple of \(\int_0^ho t^{-3}dt\), and is infinite. ## 4. Consequence for the unchanged Conway quartic Apply (14) to (4). For nonzero source, \(
u\le L\), so \(\mathcal P_N\ge1/(L|k|^2)\). Multiplying and rearranging proves (2). At a source zero the radial divergence just proved makes its right-hand comparison zero as prescribed. All levels, arbitrary complex leaf phases, and every full Hermite direction are retained. The same lower comparison holds for any prescribed positive Hermitian metric on each complete packet space, with any known nonzero scalar normalizations retaining \(K_N=\mathcal B_N f(0)\). Choose new orthonormal coordinates and rebuild both the residual energy and its product Lebesgue measure in them. Each residual still has coefficient \(-I\) in its own output variable; thus (3), the degree bound, and the proof are unchanged. Restore the known normalization by \(|\mathcal B_N|^2\) if it is complex. No comparison with the old metric is required. This permits a metric specified from geometric data, independently of the unknown source. It does not keep the same numerical integral under a metric change, or give a two-sided approximation for arbitrary new metrics. For fixed \(L\), the logarithmic lower comparison is \[ {2\pi\over N}\log|K_N| \ge -{\pi\over N}\log(\mathcal P_N/\mathcal B_N^2) -{\pi\over N}\log L . 	ag{15} \] Use extended logarithms at zeros. The last term tends to zero. Thus a lower-bound argument can use this finite-fiber proof in place of the longer asymptotic calibration in [W]. The latter remains stronger: it gives a two-sided relative error tending to zero. Neither comparison supplies a geometric upper estimate for \(\mathcal P_N/\mathcal B_N^2\). Such an estimate is still required to obtain a hyperbolic-volume lower bound. No new knot class or finite-exception theorem is established here. ## 5. Integrating all packets that enter linearly There is also an exact reduction of the same integral to its nonlinear packets. Follow [L]: at each of the \(p=L-1\) binary products retain one child packet. These selected packets are distinct because every proper packet has a unique parent. Write their coordinates as \(u\in\mathbb C^n\), \(n=Np\), and all remaining coordinates as \(z\in\mathbb C^m\), \(m=D-n\). At fixed \(u\), no product has two variable children. Split the original residuals into the eliminated packets' own equations and all other equations, including the scalar closing: \[ r_z=T(u)z+b_z(u),\qquad r_o=C(u)z+b_o(u),\qquad E_N(u,z)=\|r_z\|^2+\|r_o\|^2 . 	ag{16} \] Here \(r_z\in\mathbb C^m\), \(r_o\in\mathbb C^{n+1}\), and \(T=-I+	ext{strictly triangular}\) in the tree order. These identities hold on the whole complex spaces. Thus \(T\) is invertible for every \(u\), with \(|\det T|=1\); its inverse is a finite polynomial. No packet-ball restriction or small norm of \(u\) is used. Set \[ \mathsf D=CT^{-1},\qquad F=b_o-CT^{-1}b_z,\qquad R=I_{n+1}+\mathsf D\mathsf D^*,\qquad q=F^*R^{-1}F . 	ag{17} \] The matrix and scalar depend on \(u\), and \(R\) is positive definite. Changing to \(v=Tz+b_z\) preserves Lebesgue measure and gives \(E_N=\|v\|^2+\|\mathsf Dv+F\|^2\). Complete its Hermitian square with \(A=I_m+\mathsf D^*\mathsf D\). The remaining constant is \(q\), and \(\det A=\det R\). Diagonalization and radial integration give \[ \int_{\mathbb C^m} (\|v\|^2+\|\mathsf Dv+F\|^2)^{-n-m-1}\,dv ={\pi^m n!\over(n+m)!\,\det R\,q^{n+1}} . 	ag{18} \] For \(q>0\), the radial beta integral proves the displayed constant; for \(q=0\), both sides are infinite. Tonelli now proves the exact whole-source formula \[  oxed{\qquad \mathcal P_N={n!\over\pi^n} \int_{\mathbb C^n}{du\over\det R(u)\,q(u)^{n+1}} . \qquad} 	ag{19} \] It is an extended nonnegative equality, including source zeros. If \(p=0\), then \(n=0\), \(R\) is scalar and \(\det R\,q=|k|^2\), recovering the exact affine reciprocal. For branching trees, (19) retains both the boundary Gram and its determinant. It integrates the eliminated packets rather than minimizing them, so its normalization differs from a Schur minimum. The scalar closing is still a row of (16), with all original phases. Equation (2) applies to precisely this reduced integral as well. The lower comparison and this elimination remain valid in the consistently rebuilt packet metrics described in Section 4. ## Complete inputs and standard coverage All four complete matching texts were read. The residual recursion, degree bound and finite-fiber integral proof are written above. | Label | Complete text | Lines | SHA-256 | | --- | --- | ---: | --- | | P | [Original physical compiler](research_conway_uniform_physical_quartic.md) | 477 | 39895b430535f565d30133b46ef57f67589207bc83f40597ffe96e2ce79bbda8 | | U | [Unchanged undamped reciprocal source](research_conway_undamped_reciprocal_source.md) | 311 | 4ce9ae44a5ed6f7f54145d96712a7937f2e8c4181e2292aa5f2c44e84ffb3a8a | | W | [Stronger Wick calibration](research_conway_wick_undamped_reciprocal_asymptotic.md) | 331 | 6ffed298445828f2476989d29505c568a78a0793c03062eb37333cbd14dc5c83 | | L | [Linear packet elimination](research_conway_orthogonal_linear_elimination.md) | 344 | aa53b79685296193d5bf7fc66e53f3a3fbe03fc72a36481fb3aee23afe2ae113 | Change of variables, partial fractions and orthogonal projection are standard. For residue context see [NIST DLMF, Section 1.10(iv)](https://dlmf.nist.gov/1.10#iv). [Cattani, Dickenstein and Sturmfels, *Computing Multidimensional Residues*](https://arxiv.org/abs/alg-geom/9404011) provides primary coverage for the broader global-residue and trace setting; only its title and abstract were consulted, and no proof is imported. Only written mathematics, text reads and metadata operations were used. Earlier final notes and public manuscripts remain unchanged.

title: A positive reciprocal integral for the original Conway quartic
text:
# A positive reciprocal integral for the original Conway quartic 23 November 2026. Research proof. Earlier finals and public manuscripts remain unchanged. Supersedes [the initial version](research_conway_reciprocal_quartic_source_formula.md). The actual normalized source has a positive integral which approximates its reciprocal squared modulus with a uniform relative error. A known polynomial damping of the original closing row suffices. Neither a minimizer, its Hessian determinant, nor a chosen temperature is input. The proof uses the triangular residual map and a fixed residual ball. It does not evaluate the integral from hyperbolic geometry. ## 1. The original physical source and the integral Use the complete physical compiler of [P]. At level \(N\ge2\), every proper packet belongs to its full \(N\)-dimensional complex physical algebra, with the uniform Hilbert--Schmidt metric. This retains the first derivatives at double Casimir roots. Fix a literal expression with \(s\ge1\) proper vertices, and put \(D=Ns\), \(m=D+1\). Choose physical orthonormal coordinates on their direct sum \(\mathbb C^D\); \(dx\) means real Lebesgue measure in these coordinates. Keep [P]'s known budgets and their positive product \(B\). Each normalized leaf has norm at most \(\sigma=1/16\); turns and the original closing row have operator norm at most \(\sigma\); products have bilinear norm at most \(\sigma\). No small coefficient-tensor Hilbert--Schmidt norm for constant-budget physical multiplication is assumed. Write \(c\) for the normalized original row, extended by zero off the top packet, and \[ G_v(x)=\Phi_v((x_j)_{j	ext{ child of }v})-x_v,\qquad G(a)=0,\qquad k=ca=K_N/B,\qquad |k|\le\sigma^2. 	ag{1} \] Here \(a\) is the exact forward field. It is used in the proof, not supplied to define the integral. All original phases, turns, markings, and prescribed short-filling packets remain in the known coefficients. For \(0<\varepsilon\le1\), damp only the closing row and record the compensating budget: \[ E_\varepsilon(x)=\|G(x)\|^2+\varepsilon^2|cx|^2,\qquad B_\varepsilon=B/\varepsilon,\qquad k'=\varepsilon k. 	ag{2} \] The base \(E_\varepsilon\) has degree at most four. Define the extended nonnegative integral \[ \mathcal P_\varepsilon=  rac{D!}{\pi^D}\int_{\mathbb C^D} E_\varepsilon(x)^{-D-1}\,dx . 	ag{3} \] The exponent grows with \(D\): the rational integrand does not have bounded total degree. For the rational damping used below, its base coefficients are algebraic at each level for the original finite source. The normalization \(\pi^{-D}\) is explicit; no assertion about an algebraic period class is needed. **Theorem.** Take the known damping \(\varepsilon=m^{-3}\), and put \(\delta=m^{-2}\). If \(K_N
e0\), the integral is finite and positive, and \[ \left||k'|^2\mathcal P_\varepsilon-1ight|\le\delta,\qquad (1-\delta) rac{B_\varepsilon^2}{\mathcal P_\varepsilon} \le |K_N|^2\le (1+\delta) rac{B_\varepsilon^2}{\mathcal P_\varepsilon}. 	ag{4} \] If \(K_N=0\), then \(\mathcal P_\varepsilon=+\infty\); with \(1/(+\infty)=0\), the two source inequalities remain exact at zero. There is no parity or nonvanishing assumption in this convention. ## 2. Source-exact residual coordinates and a local bound Order children before parents. The inverse of \(G\) is the finite polynomial recursion \[ x_v=\Phi_v((x_j)_j)-r_v,\qquad \det_{\mathbb C}DG=(-1)^D,\qquad |\det_{\mathbb R}DG|=1. 	ag{5} \] Thus \(G\) is a global polynomial automorphism. This is the residual change already used in [R], now in the physical coordinates of [P]. Let \(H=G^{-1}\) and \(f_\varepsilon(r)=\varepsilon cH(r)\). Then (3) is exactly the same integral with denominator \(\|r\|^2+|f_\varepsilon(r)|^2\). Fix \(ho=1/4\). For \(\|r\|\leho\), upward induction in (5) gives \(\|H(r)_v\|\le\sigma+ho=5/16<1\). Indeed a leaf is bounded by \(\sigma+ho\); a turn or product of previously bounded inputs has norm at most \(\sigma\), before subtracting \(r_v\). This also covers prescribed constant leaves. On these packet balls write \(DG=-I+A\). Each child enters one parent row and each row has at most two children, so \(\|A\|\le\sqrt2\sigma\le1/8\) and \(\|DH\|\le8/7\). Only products contribute to \(D^2G\). At one product the two terms are \(\Phi(h_L,k_R)+\Phi(k_L,h_R)\). Cauchy--Schwarz on that pair, followed by disjointness of sibling pairs, proves \[ \|D^2G[h,k]\|\le\sigma\|h\|\|k\|,\qquad \|D^2(cH)\|\le\sigma^2(8/7)^3<1. 	ag{6} \] The second inequality follows by twice differentiating \(G(H(r))=r\); there are three factors of \(DH\) and one of \(D^2G\). No dimension factor or unknown source value occurs. Taylor's formula on the residual ball consequently gives \[ f_\varepsilon(r)=k'+d'r+p(r),\qquad d'=Df_\varepsilon(0),\qquad |p(r)|\le rac{\varepsilon}{2}\|r\|^2 . 	ag{7} \] These are holomorphic derivatives, equivalently their real variations. ## 3. The affine reciprocal and both tails Suppose first that \(k'
e0\), and put \(E_{m aff}(r)=\|r\|^2+|k'+d'r|^2\). Completing the Hermitian square uses \(A_0=I+d'^*d'\), whose determinant is \(1+\|d'\|^2\). The remaining constant is \(e_0=|k'|^2/(1+\|d'\|^2)\). Radial integration after this linear change gives \[  rac{D!}{\pi^D}\int_{\mathbb C^D}E_{m aff}^{-D-1}\,dr = rac1{e_0\det A_0}= rac1{|k'|^2}. 	ag{8} \] For example, the radial substitution reduces the scalar integral to \(\int_0^\infty t^{D-1}(t+e_0)^{-D-1}dt=1/(De_0)\). The last equality follows by \(u=t/(t+e_0)\). Thus the affine slope cancels exactly, not approximately. Both residual energies dominate \(\|r\|^2\). For either one, the normalized integral outside the fixed ball is bounded by \[  rac{D!}{\pi^D}\int_{\|r\|>ho}\|r\|^{-2D-2}\,dr = rac D{ho^2}=16D. 	ag{9} \] This controls the entire nonlinear exterior without a large-field estimate for \(H\). If \(k'
e0\), the energy has no zero: a zero would require \(r=0\) and \(f_\varepsilon(0)=k'=0\). Continuity on the remaining compact ball proves finiteness of (3). ## 4. Uniform relative error without a source lower bound On \(\|r\|\leho\), (7) gives \[ |p(r)|\le(\varepsilon/8)\sqrt{E_{m aff}(r)},\qquad (1-\varepsilon/8)^2E_{m aff} \le\|r\|^2+|f_\varepsilon(r)|^2 \le(1+\varepsilon/8)^2E_{m aff}. 	ag{10} \] This follows by applying the triangle and reverse triangle inequalities to the augmented vector \((r,k'+d'r)\). Since \(-\log(1-t)\le t/(1-t)\), the relative integrand error is at most \(\exp[(2/7)m\varepsilon]-1\). Indeed \(t=\varepsilon/8\le1/8\) and the exponent of each square is \(-m\). Comparing the two inside integrals, then using both tails (9), proves \[ \left||k'|^2\mathcal P_\varepsilon-1ight| \le \exp[(2/7)m\varepsilon]-1+32D|k'|^2. 	ag{11} \] No lower bound on \(|k'|\) has been used. For \(\varepsilon=m^{-3}\), one has \(|k'|\le\varepsilon/256\). Writing \(a=(2/7)m^{-2}\), the elementary series bound \(e^a-1\le a/(1-a)\) gives \[ e^a-1\le rac25m^{-2},\qquad 32D|k'|^2\le rac{D}{2048m^6}\le rac1{2048}m^{-2}. 	ag{12} \] Their sum is less than \(\delta=m^{-2}\). Multiplication by \(B_\varepsilon^2/\mathcal P_\varepsilon\) proves (4). More generally (11) with any fixed integer damping \(\varepsilon=m^{-p}\), \(p>1\), gives relative error \(O(m^{1-p})\). If \(k'=0\), holomorphy gives \(f_\varepsilon(r)=O(\|r\|)\) near zero. The energy is therefore at most \(C\|r\|^2\) there, and its integral dominates a positive constant times \(\int_0^ho t^{-3}dt\). It diverges, proving the stated zero convention. ## 5. Temperatures, normalization, and the remaining geometric task For \(t>0\), define \(Z_\varepsilon(t)=(t/\pi)^D\int e^{-tE_\varepsilon(x)}dx\). Residual coordinates show \(0<Z_\varepsilon(t)\le1\). Tonelli and the elementary scalar Gamma integral give the exact identity \[ \mathcal P_\varepsilon =\int_0^\infty Z_\varepsilon(t)\,dt . 	ag{13} \] This also holds as an extended nonnegative equality at a source zero. All temperatures are integrated; the intrinsic small-source scale has not disappeared from the value of the integral. For a fixed expression \(D=Ns\), (4) has relative error \(O(N^{-2})\). The extra budget \(m^3\) is polynomial and explicitly restored. This improves the previous constant-factor minimum comparison to a relative reciprocal-integral comparison, including arbitrarily small nonzero sources. Unlike [L], no selected temperature, minimum or Gaussian determinant is needed. The argument uses only the bilinear physical bounds; [R]'s coefficient-Hilbert--Schmidt determinant theorem is not transferred to a different metric. The original signed closing is still inside \(E_\varepsilon\). Neither positivity nor (13) evaluates the integral at a hyperbolic-volume rate. No geometric source coefficient, arbitrary-short-filling volume theorem, or finite-exception result follows. ## Complete inputs and coverage All four complete matching texts were read; [P] is the source input, and [C], [R], [L] locate the preceding constructions. Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used. | Label | Complete text | SHA-256 | | --- | --- | --- | | P, 477 lines | [Uniform physical source](research_conway_uniform_physical_quartic.md) | 39895b430535f565d30133b46ef57f67589207bc83f40597ffe96e2ce79bbda8 | | C, 329 lines | [Normalized convex source](research_convex_normalized_conway_source.md) | 6b89b4c6a67ef7a32cc41a5966c650f32de65d284ae7b70d94a71bddba21df3c | | R, 265 lines | [Residual Jacobian and Gaussian determinant](research_conway_residual_jacobian_gaussian_determinant.md) | db22b86a97302926fed77385f82ff2284109e288ec3d03dd99538d3671c926b2 | | L, 257 lines | [Uniform growing-level Laplace comparison](research_conway_uniform_growing_level_laplace.md) | 98e509be87f5445b43400df8341c8d902cab2ac9206c49ec248427dc32099e6f |

title: The residual Jacobian and Gaussian determinant of the Conway minimum
text: # The residual Jacobian and Gaussian determinant of the Conway minimum 21 November 2026. Research note; previous finals and public manuscripts remain unchanged. The normalized source minimum has a uniformly bounded real Hessian, but its number of variables grows with the quantum level. Bounding its Gaussian determinant by a power of the Hessian condition number would therefore introduce an artificial exponential factor. The tree structure and the Hilbert--Schmidt normalization remove that loss. The determinant below stays within universal constants of one. This controls a Gaussian normalization, not the value of the minimum. No simultaneous limit in quantum level and temperature, or comparison with hyperbolic volume, is claimed. ## 1. Actual normalized data and residual coordinates Use the actual complete Conway compiler of the [convex source theorem](research_convex_normalized_conway_source.md). There are \(s\) proper vertices. At level \(N\), each proper packet lies in the full complex Newton space \(H_N\), including its confluent normal directions. Put \(D=Ns\) and identify their direct sum with \(\mathbb C^D\). Every prescribed leaf, linear gate, bilinear gate and original closing row has been divided by its stated budget \(16\max(1,\|T_v\|_{\rm HS})\). Thus its Hilbert--Schmidt norm, and therefore its operator norm, is at most \(\sigma=1/16\). Write \(\Phi_v\) for these local maps, and \(c\) for the row on the whole direct sum which is the normalized original closing row at the top packet and zero elsewhere. Define \[ G_v(x)=\Phi_v((x_j)_{j\text{ child of }v})-x_v,\qquad E(x)=\|G(x)\|^2+|cx|^2. \tag{1} \] The feasible set is the product \(\mathcal D\) of the proper unit balls. All scalar source budgets are retained; if \(a\) is the exact normalized recursion, then \[ G(a)=0,\qquad \|a_v\|\le\sigma,\qquad k=ca=K_N/B_{\rm tot},\quad |k|\le\sigma^2. \tag{2} \] The cited theorem proves that \(E\) has a unique interior minimizer \(x_*\) on \(\mathcal D\), and \(I\le D_{\mathbb R}^2E\le3I\) there. Set \(r_*=G(x_*)\). Evaluating at \(a\) gives \[ \|r_*\|^2\le E(x_*)\le|k|^2\le\sigma^4. \tag{3} \] Real inner products mean \(\operatorname{Re}(u^*v)\), and real Lebesgue measure is used throughout. Order children before parents. Then \[ T(x)=DG(x)=-I+A(x),\qquad A(x)^s=0,\qquad \det_{\mathbb C}T(x)=(-1)^D. \tag{4} \] In fact \(G\) is a polynomial automorphism of \(\mathbb C^D\): given \(r\), its inverse is obtained successively from \(x_v=\Phi_v((x_j)_j)-r_v\). Consequently its real Jacobian is exactly one everywhere. There is no lower minimum hidden outside the feasible balls. If \(x\notin\mathcal D\), choose a violating vertex all of whose children are in their unit balls. Then \(\|\Phi_v\|\le\sigma\) and \(\|x_v\|>1\), so \[ E(x)\ge\|G_v(x)\|^2>(1-\sigma)^2. \tag{5} \] This exceeds (3). Since a polynomial automorphism is proper (its continuous polynomial inverse takes compact sets to compact sets), \(E\) is coercive. Thus \(x_*\) is also its unique global minimum on the entire real coordinate space. ## 2. A determinant bound independent of the number of variables Let \[ T_*=DG(x_*),\qquad d_*=c(I-A(x_*))^{-1},\qquad H_*=D_{\mathbb R}^2E(x_*). \tag{6} \] The row \(d_*\) is the actual closing row transported backwards through the linearized tree. Since each child derivative has norm at most \(\sigma\), each parent has at most two children, and each child belongs to one parent, \[ \|A(x_*)\|\le\sqrt2\sigma\le\tfrac18,\qquad \|T_*^{-1}\|\le\tfrac87,\qquad \|d_*\|\le\tfrac1{14}. \tag{7} \] **Theorem.** The real Gaussian determinant satisfies \[ \boxed{\quad (1+\|d_*\|^2)^2(1-4\sigma^2\|r_*\|^2) \le\det_{\mathbb R}(H_*/2) \le(1+\|d_*\|^2)^2 . \quad} \tag{8} \] In particular, with \(\gamma=197/196\), \[ 1-2^{-22}\le\det_{\mathbb R}(H_*/2)\le\gamma^2. \tag{9} \] These constants do not depend on the level, the tree size or its fixed crossing powers after the original budgets are retained. **Proof.** Only bilinear gates contribute to the residual curvature. At a product vertex \(v\), write the normalized gate coefficients as \(B_{v,kij}\), and define a complex matrix \[ (C_v)_{ij}=\sum_k\overline{(r_*)_{v,k}} B_{v,kij}. \] Cauchy--Schwarz and the normalized Hilbert--Schmidt budget give \(\|C_v\|_{\rm F}\le\sigma\|(r_*)_v\|\), where \(\|\cdot\|_{\rm F}\) is matrix Frobenius norm. Let \(C_0\) be the complex symmetric matrix with blocks \(C_v\) between the left and right child variables and \(C_v^T\) in the reverse positions, with every other block zero. Distinct parents have disjoint sibling pairs. Therefore \[ \|C_0\|_{\rm F}^2 \le2\sigma^2\|r_*\|^2. \tag{10} \] The exact half-Hessian quadratic form is \[ \tfrac12H_*[h,h] =\|T_*h\|^2+|ch|^2+\operatorname{Re}(h^TC_0h). \tag{11} \] Make the complex-linear change \(u=T_*h\). Its real determinant is one by (4). Put \(\lambda=cT_*^{-1}=-d_*\), and \(H_0=I+\lambda^*\lambda\) as a complex Hermitian matrix. The first two terms of (11) become \(u^*H_0u\). Since this is a rank-one update, \[ \det_{\mathbb R}H_0=(1+\|\lambda\|^2)^2. \tag{12} \] The further complex-linear change \(v=H_0^{1/2}u\) leaves the curvature in the form \(\operatorname{Re}(v^TC_1v)\), where \[ C_1=H_0^{-T/2}T_*^{-T}C_0T_*^{-1}H_0^{-1/2}. \] As \(\|H_0^{-1/2}\|\le1\), (7) and (10) imply \[ \|C_1\|_{\rm F}^2 \le(8/7)^4\,2\sigma^2\|r_*\|^2 \le4\sigma^2\|r_*\|^2. \tag{13} \] For completeness, the real symmetric matrix representing \(\operatorname{Re}(v^TC_1v)\), in real and imaginary coordinates, is \[ \mathcal C= \begin{pmatrix} \operatorname{Re}C_1&-\operatorname{Im}C_1\\ -\operatorname{Im}C_1&-\operatorname{Re}C_1 \end{pmatrix}. \] It anticommutes with multiplication by \(i\). Its eigenvalues therefore occur as \(t_j,-t_j\), \(1\le j\le D\), including zeros, and \(\sum_jt_j^2=\|C_1\|_{\rm F}^2\). In view of (3) and (13), every \(t_j^2<1\). Taking the determinants in (11)--(12) gives the exact identity \[ \det_{\mathbb R}(H_*/2) =(1+\|d_*\|^2)^2\prod_{j=1}^D(1-t_j^2). \tag{14} \] For \(0\le b_j\le1\), induction gives \(1-\sum_jb_j\le\prod_j(1-b_j)\le1\). Apply this with \(b_j=t_j^2\) and use (13). This proves (8). Finally \(4\sigma^2\|r_*\|^2\le4\sigma^6=2^{-22}\), and \((1+\|d_*\|^2)^2\le(1+1/196)^2=\gamma^2\). This proves (9). \(\square\) The Hilbert--Schmidt normalization is substantive in this argument. An operator-norm bound on each bilinear gate alone would not give (10) without a dimension factor. ## 3. The exact integral and its Gaussian normalization For a real inverse temperature \(\tau>0\), define the normalized positive integral on the whole coordinate space \[ Z_N(\tau)=\left(\frac{\tau}{\pi}\right)^D \int_{\mathbb C^D}e^{-\tau E(x)}\,dx. \tag{15} \] The change of variables \(r=G(x)\), with its exact Jacobian one, gives \[ \boxed{\quad Z_N(\tau)= \mathbb E_{\,r\sim\mathcal N_{\mathbb C}(0,\tau^{-1}I)} \exp\{-\tau|cG^{-1}(r)|^2\},\qquad 0<Z_N(\tau)\le1 . \quad} \tag{16} \] Here the complex Gaussian has density \((\tau/\pi)^D e^{-\tau\|r\|^2}\). The inverse \(G^{-1}\) is the actual polynomial recursion from Section 1. The scalar \(cG^{-1}(0)\) is the original normalized source \(k\); it is not replaced by an unsigned model. The quadratic approximation has the exact integral \[ \left(\frac{\tau}{\pi}\right)^D \int e^{-\tau\{E(x_*)+\tfrac12H_*[h,h]\}}\,dh =\frac{e^{-\tau E(x_*)}} {\sqrt{\det_{\mathbb R}(H_*/2)}}. \tag{17} \] By (9), its prefactor lies in \[ \left[\frac{196}{197},\, (1-2^{-22})^{-1/2}\right]. \tag{18} \] In particular the logarithm of this prefactor is uniformly bounded, despite the growing number of coordinates. For each **fixed** \(N\), the same is the usual large-\(\tau\) prefactor of (15): \[ Z_N(\tau)= \frac{e^{-\tau E(x_*)}}{\sqrt{\det_{\mathbb R}(H_*/2)}} (1+o_N(1)), \qquad \tau\longrightarrow\infty. \tag{19} \] Indeed the unique global minimum is interior and nondegenerate. Taylor expansion and \(h=\tau^{-1/2}u\) give (19) locally, dominated by a fixed positive quadratic form. On the complement of a fixed neighborhood there is a positive energy gap, by coercivity and uniqueness. Its integral is negligible: integrability of \(e^{-E}\) follows directly from the change of variables in (16), and \(e^{-\tau E}\le e^{-(\tau-1)(E(x_*)+\delta)}e^{-E}\) on a region with gap \(\delta>0\). No uniform error bound for (19) when \(N\) also varies has been proved here. In particular neither a polynomial temperature nor an exponentially increasing temperature is substituted into it. The theorem removes a spurious determinant factor from the local Gaussian normalization; it does not determine \(E(x_*)\). Its source-compatible geometric rate, and a nonzero geometric lower certificate after arbitrary fixed short fillings, remain necessary. ## Complete direct source The following complete matching text was read. It supplies the actual compiler, its Hilbert--Schmidt budgets, the marked closing row, and the interior source minimum. The polynomial change of variables and the dimension-independent determinant estimate are proved above. | Source | SHA-256 | |---|---| | [Normalized convex Conway source](research_convex_normalized_conway_source.md) | 6b89b4c6a67ef7a32cc41a5966c650f32de65d284ae7b70d94a71bddba21df3c | Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used. No mathematical program, test, numerical experiment, build, git operation, previous-final edit or public-document change was performed.

title: Separating the closing functional in the convex Conway energy
text:
# Separating the closing functional in the convex Conway energy 21 November 2026. The final closing functional in the normalized Conway energy has complex rank one. This note separates it by an exact scalar dual problem. The scalar response is a contraction, and its first nonlinear correction has a bound independent of the quantum level and the size of the expression tree. Keeping this rank-one term in the quadratic minorant also improves the explicit lower certificate. The internal minimization still retains all physical boundary packets. None of the formulas below evaluates their geometric asymptotic rate. ## 1. The original closing row and the residual energy Use the complete boundary spaces, fixed local budgets, and normalized maps of the [convex Conway source](research_convex_normalized_conway_source.md). Write the product of unit balls as \(\mathcal D\), the true normalized field as \(a\), and the full residual map as \(G\). Put \[ R(x)=\|G(x)\|^2,\qquad cx=Lx_{v_0},\qquad E(x)=R(x)+|cx|^2,\qquad k=ca=K_N/B_{m tot}. 	ag{1} \] Here \(v_0\) is the proper vertex immediately below the closing root, and \(L\) is the original marked closing row divided by its recorded local budget. The full scalar \(B_{m tot}\) is unchanged. In particular, a framing phase or recorded power of \(N\) in the physical closing row stays in (1). Set \(\sigma=1/16\) and \(\ell=\|L\|\le\sigma\). The coefficient norms are the Euclidean norms in the complete Newton basis. Repeated-root derivatives and both original closing directions remain present. All gradients and Hessians below are real, for the inner product \(\operatorname{Re}\sum_vx_v^*y_v\). Thus a scalar complex coordinate has two real coordinates. The complex-linear row \(c\) satisfies \(cc^*=\ell^2I_2\) in these real coordinates. We use the following estimates, proved in the complete source theorem: \[ G(a)=0,\quad \|a_v\|\le\sigma,\quad |k|\le\sigma^2, \qquad I\le D^2R\le3I,\qquad I\le D^2E\le3I \quad\hbox{on }\mathcal D. 	ag{2} \] The stated estimate for \(R\) follows from that theorem's residual Hessian proof before adding the nonnegative closing Hessian. If \(e_* =\min_{\mathcal D}E\), the original source comparison is \[ B_{m tot}^2e_*\le |K_N|^2 \le\gamma B_{m tot}^2e_*,\qquad \gamma=197/196. 	ag{3} \] ## 2. An exact scalar dual problem For \(\lambda\in\mathbb C\), define \[ h(\lambda)=\min_{x\in\mathcal D} \{R(x)+2\operatorname{Re}( ar\lambda cx)\},\qquad q(\lambda)=h(\lambda)-|\lambda|^2. 	ag{4} \] This definition uses only the known local maps and the prescribed closing row. It does not take \(K_N\) or the true field \(a\) as an input. **Theorem 1.** The exact minimum is \[  oxed{\quad e_* =\max_{\lambda\in\mathbb C}q(\lambda). \quad} 	ag{5} \] The maximum is unique. It lies in \(|\lambda|\le\sigma\), where the inner minimum has a unique interior minimizer \(x(\lambda)\). Writing \(s(\lambda)=cx(\lambda)\), the maximizer is characterized by \[ \lambda_*=s(\lambda_*),\qquad \|Ds(\lambda)\|\le2\ell^2\le1/128. 	ag{6} \] Thus the iteration \(\lambda_{j+1}=s(\lambda_j)\) converges to \(\lambda_*\) from any point in this disk. **Proof.** For any \(x,\lambda\), \[ |cx|^2-2\operatorname{Re}( ar\lambda cx)+|\lambda|^2 =|cx-\lambda|^2\ge0. \] Consequently \(q(\lambda)\le e_*\). Let \(x_*\) be the unique interior minimizer of \(E\), whose existence and stationarity were proved in the source theorem. Put \(\lambda_*=cx_*\), so \(|\lambda_*|\le\ell\le\sigma\). The stationary equations give \[ 
abla R(x_*)+2c^*\lambda_*=0. \] Since the objective in the inner problem is strongly convex, this equation makes \(x_*\) its unique minimum at \(\lambda_*\). The displayed square vanishes there, proving (5). For \(|\lambda|\le\sigma\), the inner half-gradient map has, at a nontop vertex \(v\), the same component as the residual energy: \[ \Phi_v-(D_v\Phi_{\operatorname{parent}(v)})^* \mathcal R_{\operatorname{parent}(v)}. \] Its norm is at most \(\sigma+\sigma(1+\sigma)=33/256\). The top component is \(\Phi_{v_0}-L^*\lambda\), with norm at most \(\sigma+\sigma^2=17/256\). The Hessian is \(D^2R\), so this map is a contraction with factor \(1/2\). It maps \(\mathcal D\) strictly inside itself. Its unique fixed point is the unique interior inner minimum. The implicit function theorem therefore gives a smooth real response \(x(\lambda)\) on a neighborhood of the closed disk. Differentiating its stationary equation gives \[ Dx(\lambda)=-2H(\lambda)^{-1}c^*,\qquad Ds(\lambda)=-2cH(\lambda)^{-1}c^*,\qquad H(\lambda)=D^2R(x(\lambda)). 	ag{7} \] Equation (2) implies (6). Also \(|s(\lambda)|\le\sigma(\sigma+\sigma^2)<\sigma\), because the top fixed-point equation has that same component bound. The disk is therefore preserved by the scalar contraction. The function \(h\) is concave on the whole scalar plane, being an infimum of affine functions of \(\lambda\). Hence subtracting \(|\lambda|^2\) makes \(q\) strictly concave, so its global maximum is unique. On the disk, \[ 
abla q=2(s-\lambda),\qquad -(2+4\ell^2)I_2\le D^2q\le-2I_2. 	ag{8} \] This proves the remaining assertions. \(\square\) The reduction is scalar at the outside. Each evaluation of \(s\) still solves a problem involving the actual internal packets. It has not converted their coherent value into a known local norm. ## 3. Positive response and its first nonlinear correction Since \(x(0)=a\), integrating (7) along the scalar segment gives \[ s(\lambda)=k-\mathsf B(\lambda)\lambda,\qquad \mathsf B(\lambda)=2\int_0^1 cH(t\lambda)^{-1}c^*\,dt. 	ag{9} \] This is a real \(2	imes2\) response matrix, with \[ 	frac23\ell^2I_2\le\mathsf B(\lambda)\le2\ell^2I_2. 	ag{10} \] In particular \(k=(I_2+\mathsf B(\lambda_*))\lambda_*\). The response correction is positive and close to the identity. It is not asserted to be a complex-holomorphic scalar function. There is a uniform expansion at the exact residual field. Set \[ T=DG(a),\qquad 
u=\|cT^{-1}\|^2\le1/196. 	ag{11} \] The inverse exists because \(T=-I+A(a)\), with \(\|A(a)\|\le1/8\). At \(\lambda=0\), \(H(0)=2T^*T\), so \(\mathsf B(0)=
u I_2\). This scalar form uses the fact that \(T\) and \(c\) are complex-linear at the zero residual. **Theorem 2.** With the normalizations above, \[ \left|e_*- rac{|k|^2}{1+
u}ight| \le rac{|k|^3}{4096},\qquad \left|\lambda_*- rac{k}{1+
u}ight| \le rac{|k|^2}{4096}. 	ag{12} \] The constants are independent of \(N\), the expression tree, and its fixed filling coefficients after the recorded budgets are retained. **Proof.** The full residual is quadratic. For a displacement \(e\), \[ G(a+e)=Te+Q(e),\qquad \|Q(e)\|\le	frac\sigma2\|e\|^2,\qquad \|DQ(e)\|\le\sigma\|e\|. 	ag{13} \] Indeed \(Q_v(e)=\Phi_v(e_L,e_R)\) at a product and is zero at other vertices. Sibling pairs are disjoint. For two variations, the second derivative has components \(\Phi_v(u_L,v_R)+\Phi_v(v_L,u_R)\). Cauchy--Schwarz on each sibling pair and then on their disjoint sum bounds its norm by \(\sigma\|u\|\|v\|\), which proves (13). The quadratic model is \[ E_0(e)=\|Te\|^2+|k+ce|^2. \] Putting \(d=cT^{-1}\) and minimizing first in \(Te\) gives \[ e_0=-T^{-1}d^*k/(1+
u),\quad \min E_0=|k|^2/(1+
u),\quad k+ce_0=k/(1+
u). 	ag{14} \] Moreover \(\|e_0\|\le4|k|/49<|k|/8\). Write \(u_*=x_*-a\) for the actual minimizing displacement. Strong monotonicity of \(
abla E\) gives \[ \|u_*\|\le\|
abla E(a)\| =2\|c^*k\|\le |k|/8. 	ag{15} \] Both comparison points are feasible, since \(\|a_v\|\le1/16\) and \(|k|\le1/256\). For \(\|e\|\le1\), let \(W(e)=E(a+e)-E_0(e)\). From \(\|T\|\le9/8\) and (13), \[ |W(e)|\le	frac18\|e\|^3,\qquad \|
abla W(e)\|\le	frac14\|e\|^2. 	ag{16} \] For clarity, the first coefficient is bounded by \(\sigma\|T\|+\sigma^2/4=73/1024<1/8\). The second is bounded by \(3\sigma\|T\|+\sigma^2=55/256<1/4\). Evaluating the two objectives at their respective minima, using (15) and the bound for \(e_0\), proves the value bound in (12). Finally \(D^2E_0\ge I\), and the actual stationary equation is \(
abla E_0(u_*)=-
abla W(u_*)\). Hence \[ \|u_*-e_0\|\le	frac14\|u_*\|^2 \le |k|^2/256. \] Applying \(c\), whose norm is at most \(1/16\), and using (14) proves the second bound. \(\square\) The field \(a\) and the row in (11) can be obtained by the exact open recursions and their backward linear response. They are not supplied by hyperbolic gluing data in this argument. Thus (12) isolates the effect of the final scalar closing inside the variational problem, while leaving the geometric estimate for the actual source outstanding. ## 4. A stronger explicit lower certificate The closing Hessian can also be kept exactly in the quadratic minorant. For \(g=
abla E(x)\), define \[  oxed{\quad D_{m cap}(x)=E(x)-	frac12\|g\|^2 + rac{|cg|^2}{1+2\ell^2}. \quad} 	ag{17} \] This is a real polynomial of degree at most six. Its coefficients use only the prescribed source maps and closing row. Since \(D^2E\ge I+2c^*c\), strong convexity with this constant matrix gives the lower bound \[ D_{m cap}(x)\le e_*\le E(x). 	ag{18} \] Indeed the unconstrained minimum of the corresponding quadratic minorant is \(E-	frac12\langle g,(I+2c^*c)^{-1}gangle\). The identity \[ (I+2c^*c)^{-1}=I- rac{2c^*c}{1+2\ell^2} \] gives (17). At the interior minimizing field \(g=0\), so \[ \max_{x\in\mathcal D}D_{m cap}(x)=e_*. 	ag{19} \] No concavity of this polynomial is asserted. It improves the earlier certificate by the nonnegative term \(|cg|^2/(1+2\ell^2)\). Equivalently, apply the quadratic minorant to the inner problem in (4) at a trial field \(x\), then maximize its explicit scalar lower bound. With \(b=
abla R(x)\) and \(s=cx\), that maximum is attained at \[ \lambda_{m trial}= rac{s-cb}{1+2\ell^2}, \] and its value is \[ R(x)-	frac12\|b\|^2 + rac{|s-cb|^2}{1+2\ell^2}=D_{m cap}(x). 	ag{20} \] This calculation is a lower bound even when the displayed trial scalar lies outside the disk used for the smooth response theorem. Combining (3) and (18), every feasible trial field gives \[ B_{m tot}^2\max(0,D_{m cap}(x)) \le |K_N|^2\le\gamma B_{m tot}^2 E(x). 	ag{21} \] This is an explicit lower witness for the original marked source. A positive witness at the hyperbolic volume rate is still required; the scalar reduction does not establish it. ## Sources and relation to previous boundary elimination The complete sole proof source was read at the matching pin: | Source | SHA-256 | |---|---| | [Convex normalized Conway source](research_convex_normalized_conway_source.md) | 6b89b4c6a67ef7a32cc41a5966c650f32de65d284ae7b70d94a71bddba21df3c | The [connected-block energy](research_connected_conway_block_boundary_energy.md) was also read in full for comparison, at pin `426b0eba0c7f4c502cf2b82052daf4d5a224ad8ec8419b3e2d8a624771f192ae`. It eliminates arbitrary internal blocks with clamped input and output packets. The present argument instead separates the original scalar closing by its convex conjugate. Both arguments retain the original budgets; neither substitutes an operator norm for the coherent boundary map. The older [effective boundary response](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_global_cap_effective_response_criterion.md), read at pin `14bbf99f1422b4d11d969c65919132824680be1a33bba6875c0e757d3b206754`, concerns the variance of a particular endpoint-sector coefficient and does not assert the exact scalar source dual proved here. Only written reasoning and text operations were used. No mathematical program, test, numerical iteration, build, git operation, or edit to an existing final note was performed.

title: A source normal and a tangential error certificate
text:
# A source normal and a tangential error certificate 21 November 2026. Research note. Previous finals and public manuscripts remain unchanged. The normalized Conway source is a sum of squared recursion residuals and one complex closing component. Its linearization therefore has a one-dimensional complex normal. Projecting onto that normal gives a computable scalar quantity. The error in its prediction of the minimum is bounded by the tangential energy, with constants independent of the level and the number of vertices. The resulting radius vanishes at the minimizing field, even though the recursion residual there need not vanish. This differs from the earlier complex-source error disk, whose radius uses the full residual. No geometric trial field or new volume identity is supplied below. ## 1. The original source and the lifted residual Use the actual normalized compiler of the complete source theorem. At level \(N\ge2\), let \(\mathcal X= igoplus_{v=1}^s H_N\) be the direct sum of its proper packet spaces. Each \(H_N\) is the full \(N\)-dimensional Newton space, including the repeated-root normal directions. The feasible set \(\mathcal D\subset\mathcal X\) is the product of the unit balls. Each prescribed leaf, linear gate, bilinear gate and original closing row has been divided by its known budget \(16\max(1,\|T_v\|_{m HS})\). Put \(\sigma=1/16\). The resulting local maps \(\Phi_v\), and the normalized original closing row \(L\), have norm at most \(\sigma\). Define \[ G_v(x)=\Phi_v((x_j)_{j	ext{ child of }v})-x_v,\qquad cx=Lx_{v_0},\qquad E(x)=\|G(x)\|^2+|cx|^2 , 	ag{1} \] where \(v_0\) is the proper child of the closing root. The row \(c\) is zero on all other packet slots. Write \(B=B_{m tot}>0\) for the retained product of all local budgets, and let \(K_N\) be the original reduced source. No phase, marked cap, Cartan factor or peripheral line has been reset. If \[ e_*=\min_{x\in\mathcal D}E(x), \qquad \gamma= rac{197}{196}, \] the complete source theorem gives \[ B^2e_*\le |K_N|^2\le\gamma B^2e_* . 	ag{2} \] It also proves that \(E\) has a unique interior minimizer \(x_*\) and real Hessian \[ I\le D_{\mathbb R}^2E\le3I \quad\hbox{on }\mathcal D. 	ag{3} \] Real inner products are \(\operatorname{Re}(u^*v)\). Fix any feasible trial field \(x\). All operators below are evaluated at this field. Put \[ r=G(x),\quad z=cx,\quad DG(x)=-I+A,\quad S=I-A,\quad d=cS^{-1},\quad 
u=\|d\|^2 . 	ag{4} \] The child-to-parent matrix \(A\) is strictly triangular. Its finite inverse, backward source row and bounds are \[ S^{-1}=\sum_{j=0}^{s-1}A^j,\qquad \|A\|\le rac18,\qquad \|S^{-1}\|\le rac87,\qquad \|d\|\le rac1{14}. 	ag{5} \] Thus \(d\) is computable by the actual backward tree recursion. It is not chosen using \(K_N\). Introduce the lifted residual and its complex-linear derivative: \[ F(x)=(G(x),cx)\in\mathcal X\oplus\mathbb C,\qquad J=DF(x)= inom{-S}{c}. 	ag{6} \] All phases in the source correction \[ w=z+dr 	ag{7} \] are added before taking a norm. ## 2. The exact normal and tangential energies Since \(S\) is invertible, \(J\) is injective. Its image has complex codimension one in \(\mathcal X\oplus\mathbb C\). Its orthogonal complement is spanned by \[  inom{d^*}{1}, \] because \(-S^*d^*+c^*=0\). Let \(P_{m n}\) and \(P_{m t}\) denote the orthogonal projections onto this normal line and onto \(\operatorname{ran}J\), respectively. Define \[  oxed{\quad \mathfrak n(x)=\|P_{m n}F(x)\|^2 = rac{|z+dr|^2}{1+
u},\qquad \mathfrak t(x)=\|P_{m t}F(x)\|^2=E(x)-\mathfrak n(x). \quad} 	ag{8} \] Both quantities are nonnegative. This is a projection in the **lifted residual space**, not deletion of a physical boundary channel: every Hermite direction still occurs in \(\mathcal X\). In particular \(\mathfrak n(x)\) may be zero; orthogonality does not prove that the coherent scalar (7) survives. Write \(H_0=J^*J=S^*S+c^*c\). Equation (5) and \(\|c\|\le1/16\) give \[  rac{49}{64}I\le H_0\le rac{325}{256}I. 	ag{9} \] The full real gradient is \(
abla E(x)=2J^*F(x)\). Since \(J^*P_{m n}=0\), \[ \|
abla E(x)\|^2 \le  rac{325}{64}\mathfrak t(x). 	ag{10} \] Moreover \(\mathfrak t(x)=0\) if and only if this gradient is zero. By (3), that happens precisely at \(x=x_*\). For comparison with the residual coordinates, stationarity is exactly \[ r=d^*z . 	ag{11} \] It follows that \(E(x_*)=\mathfrak n(x_*)=e_*\) and \(\mathfrak t(x_*)=0\). The original closing is kept in this identity; the entire residual \(r\) need not be zero at \(x_*\). ## 3. A feasible Gauss–Newton field The Gauss–Newton displacement is the unique least-squares solution \[ \delta=-H_0^{-1}J^*F(x). 	ag{12} \] It satisfies \[ F(x)+J\delta=P_{m n}F(x),\qquad \|J\delta\|^2=\mathfrak t(x),\qquad \|\delta\|^2\le rac{64}{49}\mathfrak t(x). 	ag{13} \] In this source problem the field \(y=x+\delta\) is feasible without a projection onto the balls. To check this, first take the exact residual-Newton repair \[ y_0=x+S^{-1}r . 	ag{14} \] The earlier tree repair proof gives \(\|(y_0)_v\|\le1/14\) for every packet. Indeed \(Sy_0=\Phi(x)-A(x)x\), whose blocks have norm at most \(\sigma\); upward solution of this equation bounds each packet by \(\sigma/(1-2\sigma)=1/14\). Its original closing is \(cy_0=w\), so \[ |w|\le rac1{224}. 	ag{15} \] The explicit rank-one least-squares correction is \[ y=y_0-S^{-1}d^* rac{w}{1+
u}. 	ag{16} \] For verification, its linearized residual and closing are \[ r-S\delta=d^* rac{w}{1+
u}, \qquad z+c\delta= rac{w}{1+
u}, \] which give precisely the normal component in (13). Using (5) and (15), the correction in (16) has total norm at most \[  rac87 rac1{14} rac1{224} = rac1{2744}. 	ag{17} \] Thus every packet of \(y\) has norm at most \(1/14+1/2744=197/2744<1\). No unknown source value enters the construction. ## 4. A two-sided certificate for the minimum For any displacement \(h\), the bilinear tree gives the exact expansion \[ F(x+h)=F(x)+Jh+(\mathcal Q(h),0),\qquad \|\mathcal Q(h)\|\le rac{\|h\|^2}{32}. 	ag{18} \] Here \(\mathcal Q_v(h)=\Phi_v(h_L,h_R)\) at a binary product and is zero elsewhere. Different sibling pairs are disjoint, so the stated bound follows from \(\sum_v\|h_L\|^2\|h_R\|^2\le\|h\|^4/4\). There is no higher Taylor remainder. **Theorem.** Every feasible trial field satisfies \[  oxed{\quad \max\left\{0,\sqrt{\mathfrak n(x)} - rac{325}{2048}\mathfrak t(x)ight\} \ \le\sqrt{e_*}\ \le\ \sqrt{\mathfrak n(x)}+ rac{2}{49}\mathfrak t(x). \quad} 	ag{19} \] All constants are independent of \(N\), the tree size and the fixed crossing powers after their original budgets are retained. **Proof.** Strong monotonicity from (3), with \(
abla E(x_*)=0\), and (10) give \[ \|x_*-x\|^2\le\|
abla E(x)\|^2 \le rac{325}{64}\mathfrak t(x). 	ag{20} \] Apply \(P_{m n}\) to (18) with \(h=x_*-x\). The linear term disappears exactly. The reverse triangle inequality yields \[ \sqrt{e_*}=\|F(x_*)\| \ge\sqrt{\mathfrak n(x)}-\|\mathcal Q(x_*-x)\| \ge\sqrt{\mathfrak n(x)}- rac{325}{2048}\mathfrak t(x). \] Clipping the right side at zero proves the lower bound. For the upper bound, use the feasible field (16) in (18). Equations (13) and (18) imply \[ \sqrt{e_*}\le\|F(y)\| \le\sqrt{\mathfrak n(x)}+ rac1{32}\|\delta\|^2 \le\sqrt{\mathfrak n(x)}+ rac{2}{49}\mathfrak t(x). \] This proves (19). \(\square\) The radius now uses the tangential energy, which vanishes at stationarity. It is not the previous bound for the complex error \(|K_N/B-w|\) in terms of \(\|r\|^2\). Equation (19) controls the minimum and hence the magnitude of the original source through (2); it does not identify its complex phase with \(w\). ## 5. An explicit original-source lower witness Combining (2) and (19) gives \[  oxed{\quad B\left[\sqrt{\mathfrak n}- rac{325}{2048}\mathfrak tight]_+ \le |K_N| \le\sqrt\gamma B \left(\sqrt{\mathfrak n}+ rac{2}{49}\mathfrak tight). \quad} 	ag{21} \] Here \([u]_+=\max(0,u)\), and both energies are evaluated at the chosen field. The only source-dependent scalar in them is the computable coherent correction (7), not an assumed value of \(K_N\). For a fixed construction, suppose feasible fields \(x_N\) satisfy \(\mathfrak n(x_N)>0\) eventually and \[ \mathfrak t(x_N)\le a\sqrt{\mathfrak n(x_N)},\qquad 0\le a< rac{2048}{325}, 	ag{22} \] with \(a\) independent of \(N\). If \[  rac{2\pi}{N}\log igl(B_{m tot} \sqrt{\mathfrak n(x_N)} igr)\longrightarrow V, 	ag{23} \] then (21) proves \[  rac{2\pi}{N}\log|K_N|\longrightarrow V. 	ag{24} \] More explicitly the ratio to the quantity inside the logarithm in (23) lies between the positive constants \(1-325a/2048\) and \(\sqrt\gamma(1+2a/49)\). The discrepancy of the scaled logarithms is therefore \(O(N^{-1})\), with these explicit constants. A volume proof must still construct actual geometric fields satisfying (22) and identify the rate (23). Angle stationarity alone does not control \(\mathfrak t\), which contains the complete quantum linearization. Fixed short subtrees may be contracted with their full packets before applying the same argument, but no lower bound for their geometric coupling is inferred here. No new filling case or finite-exception theorem is claimed. ## Complete proof sources and coverage Both complete proof texts were read at the matching pins below. The first supplies the actual normalized compiler, source comparison and interior minimum. The second supplies the original backward row, exact bilinear remainder and feasible residual-Newton repair. | Source | SHA-256 | |---|---| | [Normalized complete source](research_convex_normalized_conway_source.md) | 6b89b4c6a67ef7a32cc41a5966c650f32de65d284ae7b70d94a71bddba21df3c | | [Source-visible residual transport](research_conway_source_visible_residual_transport.md) | 0d344301b0df65246551cf81498eff84582f796a03271b201f8fbba6c7742007 | The complete scalar-cap response note was read at pin 6b9b73ae429713bdff63120a9841c06d2311d249f058f3da6b1f4e89dbfaecfb, and the complete residual-Jacobian Gaussian note at pin db22b86a97302926fed77385f82ff2284109e288ec3d03dd99538d3671c926b2, for coverage. They respectively give a scalar nonlinear response and a determinant bound at the exact minimum. Neither asserts the trial-field tangential-energy radius (19). Orthogonal least squares and Gauss–Newton correction are standard methods; no general novelty is claimed for them. Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used. No mathematical program, numerical iteration, test, build, git operation or earlier-final edit was performed.

title: A source-sensitive polar bound for Conway correction errors
text: # A source-sensitive polar bound for Conway correction errors Private written proof, 23 November 2026. The backward closing row in the normalized Conway recursion determines a positive seminorm for each bilinear error term. This gives a computable error disk which is never worse than the earlier local full-norm disk. At the original cylindrical closing it removes an exponentially large multiplication cost. Every genuine turn changes the transported carrier explicitly; no boundary direction is removed permanently, and no positive lower rate is inferred. ## 1. The original normalized recursion and Frobenius carriers Fix \(N\ge2\), and use the complete normalized source of [C] and [R]. The actual Newton space is \[ H_N=\mathbb C[X]/(P_N),\quad P_N=2T_N(X/2)+2,\quad d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad c_j=q^{2j+1}+q^{-2j-1}, \] \[ s_r=\prod_{a=1}^r2\sin(\pi a/N),\qquad e_r(X)=s_r^{-2}\prod_{j<r}(c_j-X),\qquad e_0=1. \tag{1} \] Empty products are one. Coefficient vectors have the Euclidean Hermitian norm. With \(J e_r=e_{d-r}\), [F] gives the actual quarter-turn and original Frobenius functional: \[ J=J^*=J^{-1},\qquad \phi(f)=f_d=(-1)^dN^2[X^d]\operatorname{rem}_{P_N}f, \qquad \phi(fg)=f^{\mathsf T}Jg. \tag{2} \] Thus the full values and first normals at double roots, and the odd simple-root value, remain in this algebra. The two original closing rows are \(\lambda_d=\phi\) and \(\lambda_0(f)=f(c_0)\). Let \(b_v\) be the recorded normalization budget of each original tensor. At a product the normalized map is \(\Phi_v(u,w)=uw/b_v\); at a turn it is \(Ju/b_v\). All normalized tensor norms are at most \(\sigma=1/16\). Keep the original normalized closing \(L\), budget product \(B_{\rm tot}\), and true packets \(a\): \[ a_v=\Phi_v((a_c)_c),\qquad k:=K_N/B_{\rm tot}=La_{\rm top},\qquad \|a_v\|\le\sigma. \tag{3} \] All original framing or other prescribed scalars stay in these data. Any separately recorded exterior scalar multiplies the final disk. For a feasible trial \(x\), set \[ e=a-x,\quad r_v=\Phi_v((x_c)_c)-x_v,\quad A=D\Phi(x),\quad z=Lx_{\rm top},\quad d=c(I-A)^{-1}, \tag{4} \] where \(c\) is \(L\) on the top packet and zero elsewhere. The matrix \(A\) is strictly triangular, so the displayed inverse of \(I-A\) is a finite sum. These are the source-preserving rows of [R]. At each proper vertex define the full algebra carrier \[ h_v=Jd_v^{\mathsf T}. \tag{5} \] There is no conjugation in (5): (2) gives \(d_v(f)=\phi(h_vf)\). The backward recursion becomes \[ \begin{split} h_c&=h_vx_{c'}/b_v &&\text{at a product, with sibling }c',\\ h_c&=Jh_v/b_v&&\text{at a genuine turn}. \end{split} \tag{6} \] The product rule follows from associativity inside \(\phi\). For the turn, \(d_c=d_vJ/b_v\) and (5) give the second rule. It uses the literal turn, not an algebra automorphism. Hence these carriers retain every later return through the specified exterior. ## 2. A sharp polar estimate at a product Write \(M_h\) for multiplication by \(h\) in the full algebra. At a product define \[ B_v=JM_{h_v}/b_v,\qquad S_v=(B_v^*B_v)^{1/2}=|M_{h_v}|/b_v\succeq0. \tag{7} \] These are known matrices once \(x\) and its backward rows are known. Commutativity and (2) imply \[ u^{\mathsf T}B_vw=d_v\Phi_v(u,w),\qquad B_v^{\mathsf T}=B_v. \tag{8} \] For every \(u,w\in H_N\), \[ \boxed{\quad |d_v\Phi_v(u,w)| \le (u^*S_vu)^{1/2}(w^*S_vw)^{1/2}. \quad} \tag{9} \] Here is a finite-dimensional proof including the complex conjugations. For any matrix \(B\), singular-value decomposition gives \[ |\langle f,Bg\rangle| \le\langle f,|B^*|f\rangle^{1/2} \langle g,|B|g\rangle^{1/2}. \] If \(B^{\mathsf T}=B\), then \(|B^*|=|B|^{\mathsf T}\). Apply this with \(f=\bar u\), \(g=w\); its first quadratic form is \(u^*|B|u\). This proves (9), also when the matrices are singular. Singular vectors show that its constant one is sharp whenever \(B_v\ne0\). No claim of a Loewner-smallest majorizing metric is made. Let \(\beta_v=\sup_{\|u\|=\|w\|=1}\|\Phi_v(u,w)\|\) be the bilinear operator norm. It is at most the normalized full tensor norm, hence at most \(\sigma\). From (8), \[ \|S_v\|=\|B_v\|\le\|d_v\|\beta_v,\qquad \ker S_v=\operatorname{Ann}(h_v). \tag{10} \] The first equality and bound use decomposable inputs \(u\otimes w\). They do not identify a bilinear norm with the norm of a row on the whole tensor product. The kernel statement is the exact equality \(\ker M_{h_v}=\{u:h_vu=0\}\), including nilpotent directions. It concerns this particular contraction, not a quotient which can be transported unchanged through another turn. These Grams also assemble on the literal tree. Each packet is a child of at most one product, so distinct sibling pairs are disjoint. Let \(\mathcal B\) have blocks \(\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&B_v\\B_v&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)\) on those pairs and zero on unused packets. Then \[ \sum_{v\ {\rm product}}e_L^{\mathsf T}B_ve_R =\tfrac12e^{\mathsf T}\mathcal Be,\qquad |\mathcal B|=\mathcal S =\bigoplus_{v\ {\rm product}}(S_v\oplus S_v)\oplus0, \qquad \left|\tfrac12e^{\mathsf T}\mathcal Be\right| \le\tfrac12e^*\mathcal Se. \tag{10a} \] This is a positive majorant for the error at the fixed trial field. It makes no positivity assertion for the original complex source. ## 3. A computable disk for the original scalar The exact error identity in [R] is \[ (I-A)e=r+Q(e),\qquad k=z+dr+\sum_{v\ {\rm product}}d_v\Phi_v(e_L,e_R), \tag{11} \] where \(Q_v(e)=\Phi_v(e_L,e_R)\) at products and zero otherwise. Only the last sum requires an estimate. Compute the known correction and nonnegative scalar majorants upward through the actual tree: \[ \delta=(I-A)^{-1}r,\qquad \Delta_v=\|r_v\|+\sigma\sum_{c}\Delta_c, \tag{12} \] \[ \omega_v=\sum_c\|A_{vc}\|\omega_c+ \mathbf1_{v\ {\rm product}}\beta_v\Delta_L\Delta_R. \tag{13} \] Empty sums are zero. The argument in [R], equations (16)–(18) gives \(\|e_v\|\le\Delta_v\): at a product use the ordered difference \(\Phi(e_L,a_R)+\Phi(x_L,e_R)\), with the true and trial packets in their prescribed balls. Subtracting \(\delta\) from (11) gives \((I-A)(e-\delta)=Q(e)\). Its triangular equations and (13) therefore prove \[ \|e_v-\delta_v\|\le\omega_v. \tag{14} \] Thus both majorants are explicit finite calculations, with no unknown closed invariant used as input. At a product put \(s_v=\|S_v\|\), and, for either child \(c\), set \[ t_{vc}=\min\left\{\sqrt{s_v}\,\Delta_c, (\delta_c^*S_v\delta_c)^{1/2} +\sqrt{s_v}\,\omega_c\right\}, \qquad R_{\rm pol}(x)=\sum_{v\ {\rm product}}t_{vL}t_{vR}. \tag{15} \] Triangle inequality for the seminorm \(\|S_v^{1/2}\cdot\|\), (12), and (14) bound \(\|S_v^{1/2}e_c\|\) by \(t_{vc}\). Equations (9)--(11) consequently give \[ |k-(z+dr)|\le R_{\rm pol}(x) \le\sum_{v\ {\rm product}} \|d_v\|\beta_v\Delta_L\Delta_R =R_{\rm loc}(x). \tag{16} \] The last expression is the earlier local radius of [R], with its actual local bilinear norms. For evaluation, \(\beta_v\) may everywhere be replaced by its recorded full tensor upper bound; no bilinear maximization is required, and the same comparison remains valid. Keep also [R]'s global quadratic radius. The fully computable result is \[ \widehat k=z+dr,\qquad R(x)=\min\{R_{\rm pol}(x),\ \|r\|^2/343\}, \tag{17} \] \[ \boxed{\quad B_{\rm tot}(|\widehat k|-R)_+ \le |K_N|\le B_{\rm tot}(|\widehat k|+R). \quad} \tag{18} \] It is never a worse disk than the earlier minimum of the local and global radii. Vanishing carriers and singular polar matrices require no inversion or exceptional case. The center remains the original coherent correction, before taking an absolute value. ## 4. An exponential saving at the actual cylindrical closing Suppose the top proper gate is a product with budget \(b_v\), and the original normalized closing is \(L=\chi\phi/b_\rho\). The prescribed scalar \(\chi\) and its actual closing budget \(b_\rho\) are retained. Then \[ h_v=\chi/b_\rho,\qquad B_v=\frac{\chi}{b_\rho b_v}J,\qquad S_v=\frac{|\chi|}{b_\rho b_v}I. \tag{19} \] Thus the top contribution to (16) is at most \(|\chi|\Delta_L\Delta_R/(b_\rho b_v)\). The old local bound instead charges \(|\chi|\|M\|_{\rm bil}\Delta_L\Delta_R/(b_\rho b_v)\), where \(M\) is actual multiplication. This is a bilinear saving: \(|\phi(uw)|\le\|u\|\|w\|\), whereas the full tensor row \(\phi M\) has Euclidean norm \(\sqrt N\). The difference is exponential. For \(k=\lfloor N/4\rfloor\) and all sufficiently large levels, the exact formula in [M], equation (2) gives \[ \|M\|_{\rm bil}\ge\mu_{k,k,2k} =s_{2k}^{\,2}/s_k^{\,4},\qquad \log\mu_{k,k,2k}=\frac{2G_{\rm Cat}}\pi N+O(\log N). \tag{20} \] For completeness, let \(J_0(x)=\int_0^x\log(2\sin\pi t)dt\). Subtracting \(\log t\) leaves a smooth function on every interval \([0,b]\), \(b<1\); its Riemann-sum error is bounded. Integral comparison for \(\sum\log(a/N)\) gives \(\log s_n=NJ_0(n/N)+O(\log N)\) in the ranges used here. The elementary sine double-angle identity gives \(J_0(1/2)=0\) and \(J_0(1/4)=-G_{\rm Cat}/(2\pi)\), where \(G_{\rm Cat}=\int_0^{\pi/4}\log(\cot t)dt\). Indeed the integrals of \(\log(2\sin t)\) and \(\log(2\cos t)\) on \([0,\pi/4]\) sum to zero; the cosine integral minus the sine integral is \(G_{\rm Cat}\). These facts prove (20), with the rounding of \(k\) changing only the stated error. The same normalization budgets occur on both sides of this comparison. Restoring \(B_{\rm tot}\) preserves the ratio. The saving comes from composing multiplication with the original closing before estimating it. Other products can still control the radius of a larger expression. ## 5. Turns, marked caps, and scope For the other original closure \(L=\chi\lambda_0/b_\rho\), (2) gives \(h_v=\chi e_d/b_\rho\). Since \(M_{e_d}u=u_0e_d\), its polar matrix at a product is \[ S_v=\frac{|\chi|}{b_\rho b_v} |e_0\rangle\langle e_0|. \tag{21} \] Only the two value errors at \(c_0\) enter that contraction. But the next genuine turn sends this carrier to a scalar multiple of \(1\), by (6), and the full-rank matrix (19) returns. Thus neither normal directions nor a future return have been discarded. The matrices and radii above apply to arbitrary feasible trial fields, all levels and both parities, with the literal original closing. They do not reduce the physical dimension, assert positivity of the complex error, or supply an asymptotic estimate for \(\widehat k\). A lower bound still needs that corrected center to exceed its proved radius at the desired rate. No volume identity or finite-exception theorem is inferred. The new quantitative assertions are the source-sensitive no-worse disk (15)--(18) and the exponential local saving (19)--(20), rather than a claim of novelty for polar decomposition or adjoint-weighted error estimation. ## Complete sources All four complete proof texts were read at matching versions: | Label | Complete source | SHA256 | |---|---|---| | R | notes/research_conway_source_visible_residual_transport.md | 0d344301b0df65246551cf81498eff84582f796a03271b201f8fbba6c7742007 | | F | notes/research_conway_full_boundary_quotient_gram.md | debe56dbad8151b90d44d0fccbf0dcf33dafb780370e01c8acdadbd2939dc077 | | M | notes/actual_positive_newton_multiplication.md | 543b5be6035ecec349ce8e78ee47085345ceefe4fc51e5f2005b802d999805bb | | C | notes/research_convex_normalized_conway_source.md | 6b89b4c6a67ef7a32cc41a5966c650f32de65d284ae7b70d94a71bddba21df3c | The complete comparison text notes/research_conway_orthogonal_linear_elimination.md, SHA256 aa53b79685296193d5bf7fc66e53f3a3fbe03fc72a36481fb3aee23afe2ae113, retains an inverse boundary Gram after eliminating linear residuals; it does not give the polar product disk above. Only written mathematics and source-text/hash operations were used. No mathematical program, test, build, git operation or earlier-final edit was made.
