title: Source-visible residuals and exact correction on a Conway tree
text:
# Source-visible residuals and exact correction on a Conway tree 21 November 2026. Research note; previous finals and public manuscripts remain unchanged. A trial boundary packet can have a large error which is nearly invisible to the prescribed closing functional. Bounding the norm of that error before applying the closing row loses this information. Here we transport the actual closing row backwards through the linearization of the complete Conway compiler. The resulting correction is a coherent complex scalar. Its remaining error has an explicit quadratic bound. This is a finite-level error estimate for the original source. It does not establish that a geometric trial field has a nonzero corrected closing or the required volume rate. Its advantage over a full-norm criterion is precise: the first-order error is retained as a source-visible scalar, and only the nonlinear remainder is bounded by a norm. ## 1. The normalized physical tree Use the complete physical boundary data of [the normalized source theorem](research_convex_normalized_conway_source.md). At level \(N\ge2\), every proper edge carries the full \(N\)-dimensional Newton coefficient space \(H_N\), including its repeated-root normal directions. The original product, turn, signed crossing packets and marked closing row are unchanged. There are \(s\ge1\) proper vertices. The closing root has a unique child \(v_0\). At every physical vertex, including leaves and the closing root, the known budget is \[ b_v=16\max(1,\|T_v\|_{m HS}),\qquad \sigma= rac1{16}. \] Let \(B_v\) be the product of the budgets in the proper subtree at \(v\), and \(B_{m tot}\) the product over the whole compiler. If \(f_v\) is the actual open packet, put \(a_v=f_v/B_v\). Then \[ a_v=\Phi_v((a_c)_c),\qquad k_N= rac{K_N}{B_{m tot}}=La_{v_0}. 	ag{1} \] Here \(\Phi_v\) is a prescribed constant at a leaf, a linear map at a turn, and a bilinear map at a product. Each normalized map, constant, and the original normalized closing row \(L\) has norm at most \(\sigma\). In particular \(\|a_v\|\le\sigma\). Choose a feasible trial field \[ x=(x_v)_v\in\mathcal D_N =\prod_v\{x_v\in H_N:\|x_v\|\le1\}. \] Define the error, residual and trial closing by \[ e=a-x,\qquad r_v=\Phi_v((x_c)_c)-x_v,\qquad r=G(x),\qquad z=Lx_{v_0}. 	ag{2} \] All norms on direct sums are Euclidean. Rows act by their ordinary complex-linear composition. A star denotes a Hermitian adjoint and is used only when identifying a row with a vector or estimating a norm. In particular, complex residual contributions are added before their absolute values are taken. ## 2. Backward transport of the actual closing row Let \(A=A(x)\) be the derivative of the map \(x\mapsto(\Phi_v((x_c)_c))_v\). Thus \[ DG(x)=-I+A. \] Its block from a child \(c\) to its proper parent \(v\) is \(D_c\Phi_v(x)\); all other blocks vanish. Ordering children before parents makes \(A\) strictly triangular, so \(A^s=0\). Consequently \[ (I-A)^{-1}=\sum_{j=0}^{s-1}A^j. 	ag{3} \] Each derivative block has norm at most \(\sigma\). Each row has at most two child blocks and each child occurs in at most one parent row. It follows that \[ \|A\|\le\sqrt2\sigma\le rac18,\qquad \|(I-A)^{-1}\|\le rac87. 	ag{4} \] Let \(c\) be the row on the full direct sum which is \(L\) at \(v_0\) and zero elsewhere. Define \[ d=c(I-A)^{-1},\qquad \eta=d^*=(I-A^*)^{-1}c^*. 	ag{5} \] No unknown closed invariant enters (5). The individual rows \(d_v\) are obtained by the following actual backward recursion: \[ d_{v_0}=L,\qquad d_c=d_vD_c\Phi_v(x) \quad(c	ext{ a child of the proper vertex }v). 	ag{6} \] This follows either from \(d=c+dA\) or from the unique path from the closing root to each vertex. If \(r_v^{m dep}\) is the depth of \(v\) from that root, then \[ \|d_v\|\le\sigma^{r_v^{m dep}},\qquad \|\eta\|=\|d\|\le rac1{14}. 	ag{7} \] The second estimate uses (4) and \(\|c\|=\|L\|\le1/16\). The linearized source error is the computable complex scalar \[ dr=\sum_vd_vr_v=\eta^*r. 	ag{8} \] Equation (8) is not a sum of absolute values and is not a replacement of the original marked closing row by an ordinary trace. ## 3. The exact nonlinear error identity For a field \(h\), define \(Q(h)\) to be zero at leaves and turns, and at a product vertex define \[ Q_v(h)=\Phi_v(h_L,h_R). 	ag{9} \] The exact bilinear expansion of (1) gives \[ (I-A)e=r+Q(e). 	ag{10} \] There is no Taylor remainder beyond (9). Applying the actual source row to (10) proves \[  oxed{\quad k_N=z+dr+\sum_{v\ {m product}}d_v\Phi_v(e_L,e_R). \quad} 	ag{11} \] Define the corrected trial closing \[ \widehat k(x)=z+dr. 	ag{12} \] Thus the first-order residual has been evaluated in the actual exterior determined by \(x\), rather than bounded in every exterior. No direction of the physical boundary space has been quotiented out. There is a uniform quadratic bound. Since sibling pairs belonging to different parents are disjoint, \[  egin{split} \|Q(h)\|^2 &\le\sigma^2\sum_{v\ {m product}}\|h_L\|^2\|h_R\|^2\ &\le rac{\sigma^2}{4}\|h\|^4. \end{split} 	ag{13} \] Integrating \(DG=-I+A\) along the segment from \(x\) to the true field \(a\), as in the normalized source theorem, gives \[ \|e\|\le rac87\|r\|. 	ag{14} \] Equations (7), (11), (13) and (14) now imply \[  oxed{\quad |k_N-\widehat k(x)| \le rac1{14} rac1{32}\left( rac87ight)^2\|r\|^2 = rac{\|r\|^2}{343}. \quad} 	ag{15} \] If \(dr=0\), the uncorrected closing \(z\) already has this quadratic error bound. A first-order source-invisible residual is therefore harmless only after its nonlinear contribution has also been controlled. Equation (15) does not license discarding an arbitrary residual. ## 4. A sharper local radius An alternative bound keeps the original incidence and the actual transported rows. Define nonnegative numbers \(\Delta_v\) upwards through the tree by \[ \Delta_v=\|r_v\|+\sigma\sum_{c\ {m child\ of}\ v}\Delta_c. 	ag{16} \] The empty sum at a leaf is zero. Then \[ \|e_v\|\le\Delta_v. 	ag{17} \] For a turn this follows by linearity. For a product use the exact ordered identity \[ \Phi_v(a_L,a_R)-\Phi_v(x_L,x_R) =\Phi_v(e_L,a_R)+\Phi_v(x_L,e_R), 	ag{18} \] and the unit-ball bounds on \(a_R,x_L\). Induction proves (17). The bound can be improved, without changing any conclusion below, by using the local map norm and the minimum of \[ \sigma\Delta_L+\|x_L\|\Delta_R,\qquad \|x_R\|\Delta_L+\sigma\Delta_R 	ag{19} \] in place of \(\Delta_L+\Delta_R\) at a product. The factor multiplying this minimum is \(\|\Phi_v\|_{m op}\). Each choice in (19) follows from one of the two ordered versions of (18), using \(\|a_L\|,\|a_R\|\le\sigma\). The explicit local radius is \[ \mathcal R_{m loc}(x) =\sum_{v\ {m product}}\|d_v\|\,\|\Phi_v\|_{m op} \Delta_L\Delta_R. 	ag{20} \] Equations (11) and (17) prove \[ |k_N-\widehat k(x)|\le \mathcal R(x):=\min\left\{\mathcal R_{m loc}(x),  rac{\|r\|^2}{343}ight\}. 	ag{21} \] Thus one backward row flow and one forward scalar majorant flow give a rigorous source-specific error disk. All operations involve the actual finite quantum packets and their original phases. ## 5. A phase-sensitive lower bound at one trial field The error disk immediately gives \[  oxed{\quad B_{m tot}\max(0,|\widehat k(x)|-\mathcal R(x)) \le |K_N| \le B_{m tot}(|\widehat k(x)|+\mathcal R(x)). \quad} 	ag{22} \] This does not require minimizing a new function. For a sequence of feasible trial fields, suppose that eventually \[ \mathcal R(x_N)\le(1-	heta_N)|\widehat k(x_N)|,\qquad 0<	heta_N\le1,\qquad \log	heta_N=o(N). 	ag{23} \] If also \[  rac{2\pi}{N}\log igl(B_{m tot}|\widehat k(x_N)| igr) \longrightarrow V>0, 	ag{24} \] then (22) proves \[  rac{2\pi}{N}\log|K_N|\longrightarrow V. 	ag{25} \] Indeed the lower and upper factors relative to the center in (22) are at least \(	heta_N\) and at most \(2\), respectively. The uniform radius (15) can reduce the required exponential accuracy of a residual estimate. If the corrected normalized closing has size \(\exp\{-\alpha N+o(N)\}\), it suffices for its quadratic remainder to have a strictly smaller rate; for example \(\|r_N\|\le\exp\{-(\alpha/2+\varepsilon)N+o(N)\}\) with \(\varepsilon>0\). A direct linear residual disk instead requires an error on the scale of the closing itself. The correction \(dr_N\), its complex phase, and the nonzero leading behavior in (24) must still be established. A formal small residual alone does not prove a volume lower bound. ## 6. Fixed short components and exact linear corridors Any fixed proper short subtree may first be contracted to its complete actual open packet and inserted as one prescribed leaf. Recompute the known budgets in (1). This preserves the original knot source and all Hermite directions, including a packet which vanishes on the distinct Casimir roots but has a nonzero normal part. Put the true normalized value at such a leaf. Its residual and error are exactly zero. At a product with one exact child, the corresponding term \(Q_v(e)=\Phi_v(e_L,e_R)\) in (11) is zero. Attachments through a sequence of exact short sibling components therefore transport the remaining error linearly, with their actual complex matrices. The backward rows in (6) retain those matrices and their phases exactly. Nonlinear remainder terms occur only where two uncertain branches meet. This is a structural simplification for arbitrary fixed short components; it is not a positivity or nonvanishing theorem for their closing coefficients. The estimates are for the specified original exterior. They do not declare a direction invisible to every other possible exterior. ## 7. Exact Newton repair and finite pruning The correction in (12) has a direct transport interpretation. Solve the triangular linear system \[ (I-A(x))\delta=r,\qquad x^+=x+\delta. 	ag{26} \] Equation (3) makes this an explicit finite operation. Its closing is exactly \[ Lx^+_{v_0}=z+dr=\widehat k(x). 	ag{27} \] The next residual is exactly \[ G(x^+)=Q(\delta). 	ag{28} \] Expanding \(G\) at \(x\) proves this: the linear terms are \(r+(-I+A)\delta=0\), and the only remaining terms are (9). Consequently \[ \|G(x^+)\|\le rac{2}{49}\|G(x)\|^2. 	ag{29} \] Here \(\|\delta\|\le8\|r\|/7\) and (13) give the stated constant. All these repairs remain feasible. In fact \[ (I-A)x^+=\Phi(x)-Ax. 	ag{30} \] The right side is the prescribed constant at a leaf, zero at a turn, and \(-\Phi_v(x_L,x_R)\) at a product. Every block has norm at most \(\sigma\). Solving (30) upwards and using the derivative block bound \(\sigma\) gives \[ \|x_v^+\|\le rac{\sigma}{1-2\sigma} = rac1{14} \quad	ext{for every }v. 	ag{31} \] For example, if both children satisfy this bound, the parent is bounded by \(\sigma+2\sigma/14=1/14\); leaves start the induction. Thus (21) and (29) can be applied at every repair. There is also an exact termination statement in exact arithmetic. Give a leaf rank one and a turn the rank of its child. At a product set \[ 
u_v=\max\{
u_L,
u_R,\min(
u_L,
u_R)+1\}. 	ag{32} \] This is the usual Strahler rank, with leaves numbered one. Starting from any feasible trial field and applying (26) repeatedly, \[ x_v^{(j)}=a_v\qquad(j\ge
u_v). 	ag{33} \] To prove this, put \(e^{(j)}=a-x^{(j)}\). Subtracting (26) from (10) gives the exact recurrence \[ (I-A(x^{(j)}))e^{(j+1)}=Q(e^{(j)}). 	ag{34} \] Leaves are exact after one repair. At a turn, exactness of the new child implies exactness of the new parent. At a product, both new children are exact once \(j+1\ge\max(
u_L,
u_R)\); its remaining quadratic term is zero once \(j\ge\min(
u_L,
u_R)\). These are precisely the conditions in (32). Induction through the tree proves (33). If the tree has \(n\) leaves, a vertex of rank \(
u\) has at least \(2^{
u-1}\) descendant leaves: an increase of rank requires two children of the same preceding rank. Therefore \[ 
u_{v_0}\le1+\lfloor\log_2nfloor. 	ag{35} \] After this many repairs the whole actual normalized field, and hence its original closing, is exact. The proof needs the bilinear tree structure; a network with shared descendants or contraction loops is outside this assertion. This finite repair theorem does not solve the asymptotic problem. It is an alternative exact evaluation and error-reduction mechanism. An asymptotic use of (22) still requires control of its coherent corrected closing, or of the successive corrected closings, at the hyperbolic volume rate. ## 8. Relation to earlier residual estimates The existing [stationary-observable estimate](research_stationary_observable_residual_cancellation.md) subtracts stationary equations from a scalar observable to cancel its uncertain first derivatives, retaining a quadratic Taylor remainder. The [pointed transport estimate](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_pointed_metric_transport_and_crossing_obstruction.md), Section 4, gives an exact adjoint-defect identity for a linear cocycle. Those are relevant precedents within these notes. No novelty is claimed for adjoint-weighted residual estimation as a general technique. Here the backward row is constructed from the actual complete Conway tree, its nonlinear remainder is exactly the finite bilinear expression (11), and both the local radius and the finite repair/pruning statements are proved explicitly. No new knot volume identity or finite-exception class is concluded without the quantitative conditions (23)--(24). ## Complete proof and coverage sources The following complete matching texts were read. The normalized source note supplies the actual physical compiler and its norm convention. The other two are coverage sources; none of their analytic estimates is an assumption in the identities proved above. | Source | SHA-256 | |---|---| | [Normalized actual source](research_convex_normalized_conway_source.md) | 6b89b4c6a67ef7a32cc41a5966c650f32de65d284ae7b70d94a71bddba21df3c | | [Stationary observable and residual cancellation](research_stationary_observable_residual_cancellation.md) | 85c3c5410cb1279ff8142f7678c65a6fdb4e6860323f8e810c27d68ae3ea2448 | | [Pointed transport and adjoint defects](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_pointed_metric_transport_and_crossing_obstruction.md) | 46a0109371f7e39438232e059a8de9708734a68439b5b610b78ce78fd1faf392 | Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used. No mathematical program, test, numerical iteration, build, git operation, previous-final edit, or public-document change was performed.

title: The original undamped Conway quartic has a reciprocal source integral
text:
# The original undamped Conway quartic has a reciprocal source integral 24 November 2026. Research proof. Earlier finals and manuscripts are unchanged. The original physical quartic needs no damping of its closing row for a reciprocal-integral comparison at exponential scale. Its positive integral approximates the reciprocal squared source with a universal relative error, independent of the level, tree size and leaf packets. No minimizer, temperature, or Hessian determinant is input. The addition to [R] is removal of its level-dependent damping and compensating budget. The original objective and budgets are retained. The comparison here has a fixed error, whereas [R]'s damped formula has a relative error tending to zero. Neither formula evaluates its integral from geometry. ## 1. The unchanged source and the statement Use [P]'s literal physical compiler at every integer level \(N\ge2\). Every proper packet lies in the full algebra \[ \mathcal A_N=\mathbb C[\Omega]\subset \operatorname{End}(V_N\otimes V_N),\qquad \|F\|_{m ph}^2=\operatorname{Tr}(F^*F),\qquad \dim_{\mathbb C}\mathcal A_N=N. 	ag{1} \] Here \(\Omega\) is the original two-head Casimir of [P,H]. This retains the first-normal directions at double Casimir roots. All packet coordinates below are physical orthonormal coordinates. Fix a literal tree with \(s\ge1\) proper vertices, and put \(D=Ns\), \(m=D+1\), and \(\sigma=1/16\). Keep exactly [P]'s budgets: a prescribed leaf \(A_v\) has budget \(16\max(1,\|A_v\|_{m ph})\), products and genuine turns have budget \(16\), and an original root \(\eta_N\lambda\), with \(\lambda\in\{\lambda_0,\phi\}\), has budget \(16\max(1,|\eta_N|)\). Let \(\mathcal B_N\) be their product. All original phases, markings and external normalizations remain. The normalized leaves, linear maps and bilinear maps have norm at most \(\sigma\). Let \(\Phi_v\) denote these actual maps, and let \(c_N\) be the normalized original closing row, extended by zero off the top packet. On \(\mathbb C^D\) set \[ G_v(x)=\Phi_v((x_j)_{j	ext{ child of }v})-x_v,\qquad E_N(x)=\|G(x)\|^2+|c_Nx|^2. 	ag{2} \] This is the original degree-at-most-four objective of [P], without changing its closing. The exact forward field \(a\) satisfies \(G(a)=0\) and \(k=c_Na=K_N/\mathcal B_N\). The field and \(k\) are used only in the proof. Define the extended nonnegative integral, with physical real Lebesgue measure, \[ \mathcal P_N= rac{D!}{\pi^D} \int_{\mathbb C^D}E_N(x)^{-D-1}\,dx. 	ag{3} \] Its base is quartic; its denominator exponent and integration dimension grow with \(N\). No bounded-total-degree assertion for the rational integrand is intended. Put \[ \delta_0= rac1{8192},\qquad \delta= rac1{2048}. 	ag{4} \] **Theorem.** If \(K_N
e0\), then \(0<\mathcal P_N<\infty\) and \[  oxed{\quad \left||k|^2\mathcal P_N-1ight|\le\delta,\qquad (1-\delta) rac{\mathcal B_N^2}{\mathcal P_N} \le |K_N|^2\le (1+\delta) rac{\mathcal B_N^2}{\mathcal P_N}. \quad} 	ag{5} \] If \(K_N=0\), then \(\mathcal P_N=+\infty\); with reciprocal zero, the source inequalities in (5) hold there as well. The constant is uniform over all tree sizes and normalized actual leaf choices, including fixed short-filling packets. There is no parity or prior nonvanishing hypothesis. ## 2. The physical closing estimate, at every level Here is the multiplicity argument needed for the level dependence; it repeats the existing physical closing estimate explicitly. Put \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), and \[ c_j=q^{2j+1}+q^{-2j-1},\qquad P_N(t)=2T_N(t/2)+2=\prod_{j=0}^{d}(t-c_j). \] Here \(T_N\) is the Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind. The analytic generic ordinary highest-weight family constructed in [H, Section 4] has pair Casimir eigenvalues \(\zeta^{2d-2j+1}+\zeta^{-2d+2j-1}\), on summands of dimensions \(2d-2j+1\), for \(0\le j\le d\). Their dimensions sum to \(N^2\). Its finite matrices are analytic at \(\zeta=q\). At that root, \(j\) and \(d-j\) have the same eigenvalue \(c_j\), and their dimensions sum to \(2N\). The odd self-pair has dimension \(N\) and eigenvalue \(-2\). Specializing the characteristic polynomial therefore proves, without root semisimplicity, \[ \det(tI_{N^2}-\Omega)=P_N(t)^N. 	ag{6} \] In particular \(c_0=q+q^{-1}\) has algebraic multiplicity \(2N\) at every \(N\ge2\), including \(N=2\) and all composite levels. An orthonormal invariant flag makes \(\Omega\) upper triangular. The diagonal of \(f(\Omega)\) has values \(f(c_j)\) in those multiplicities, so \[ \|f(\Omega)\|_{m ph}^2 \ge N\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}|f(c_j)|^2 \ge2N|f(c_0)|^2. 	ag{7} \] All offdiagonal and independent first-normal entries remain in the norm. The original rows obey \(\lambda_0(f(\Omega))=f(c_0)\) and \(\lambda_0=\phi\circ\mathcal T\), with the genuine physical turn \(\mathcal T\) unitary by [P]. Hence \[ N^{-1}\le\|\lambda_0\|_* =\|\phi\|_* \le(2N)^{-1/2},\qquad \|c_N\|\le rac{\sigma}{\sqrt{2N}}. 	ag{8} \] For the lower row bound use \(\lambda_0(I)=1\), \(\|I\|_{m ph}=N\). The normalized root budget above proves the last inequality even when its original scalar \(\eta_N\) varies with the level. If \(s_v\) counts proper vertices in a subtree, forward induction gives \(\|a_v\|\le\sigma^{s_v}\): a leaf contributes one factor, a turn contributes one more, and a product multiplies the two child bounds and one more factor. Consequently \[ |k|\le rac{\sigma^{s+1}}{\sqrt{2N}},\qquad 16Ds^2|k|^2\le8s^3\sigma^{2s+2}\le\delta_0. 	ag{9} \] The last bound is maximal at \(s=1\), since the ratio of successive terms \(s^3\sigma^{2s}\) is at most \(8\sigma^2=1/32<1\). It uses no lower bound on the source. ## 3. Exact residual coordinates and the small nonlinear cap Order children before parents. The recursion \(x_v=\Phi_v((x_j)_j)-r_v\) gives a global polynomial inverse \(H=G^{-1}\). Its complex Jacobian determinant is \((-1)^D\), so its real Jacobian has absolute value one. In these exact coordinates (3) has denominator \[ \|r\|^2+|f(r)|^2,\qquad f(r)=c_NH(r),\quad f(0)=k. 	ag{10} \] Use the proof radius \(R_s=1/(4s)\), which changes neither the integral nor its coefficients. On \(\|r\|\le R_s\), induction in the inverse recursion bounds every packet by \(\sigma+R_s\le5/16<1\). There \(DG=-I+A\) with \(\|A\|\le\sqrt2\sigma\le1/8\): each child enters one parent row, and each row has at most two children. Thus \(\|DH\|\le8/7\). Only products contribute to \(D^2G\). Their two bilinear terms, Cauchy--Schwarz on each sibling pair, and disjointness of sibling pairs give \(\|D^2G[h_1,h_2]\|\le\sigma\|h_1\|\|h_2\|\). Twice differentiating \(G(H(r))=r\), and then using (8), proves \[ \|Df(0)\|\le rac1{14\sqrt{2N}},\qquad \|D^2f\|\le rac2{343\sqrt{2N}} \quad(\|r\|\le R_s). 	ag{11} \] No coefficient-tensor Hilbert--Schmidt bound for multiplication is used. Taylor's formula therefore gives \[ f(r)=k+dr+p(r),\qquad d=Df(0),\qquad |p(r)|\le rac{\|r\|^2}{343\sqrt{2N}}. 	ag{12} \] Set \(E_{m aff}(r)=\|r\|^2+|k+dr|^2\). Writing \(u=\|r\|\le R_s\), expansion of the squared cap, rather than a relative bound on the cap itself, gives \[  egin{split} |\|r\|^2+|f(r)|^2-E_{m aff}(r)| &\le 2(|k|+\|d\|u)|p(r)|+|p(r)|^2\ &\le rac{u^2}{N}\left\{  rac{\sigma^{s+1}}{343} + rac{u}{14\cdot343}+ rac{u^2}{2\cdot343^2}ight\}. \end{split} 	ag{13} \] Since \(s\sigma^{s-1}\le1\), the braces are at most \(C_*/s\), where \[ C_* = rac1{87808}+ rac1{19208}+ rac1{3764768} = rac{1919}{256\cdot7^6}< rac1{8192}=\delta_0. \] Indeed the three terms are bounded respectively by \(1/(87808s)\), \(1/(19208s)\), and \(1/(3764768s^2)\). The inequality \(s\sigma^{s-1}\le1\) follows because its successive ratio is at most \(2\sigma=1/8\). Thus on this ball, including its origin by continuity, \[ (1-\delta_0/D)E_{m aff} \le \|r\|^2+|f(r)|^2 \le(1+\delta_0/D)E_{m aff}. 	ag{14} \] This order \(D^{-1}\) energy comparison is what removes damping. ## 4. The affine integral and the entire exterior For \(k
e0\), completing the Hermitian square with \(A_0=I+d^*d\) gives residual constant \(|k|^2/(1+\|d\|^2)\) and determinant \(1+\|d\|^2\). Radial integration consequently gives the exact slope cancellation \[  rac{D!}{\pi^D}\int_{\mathbb C^D} E_{m aff}(r)^{-D-1}\,dr=|k|^{-2}. 	ag{15} \] The scalar radial integral is \(\int_0^\infty t^{D-1}(t+e)^{-D-1}dt=1/(De)\), obtained by \(u=t/(t+e)\). Both the actual residual energy and \(E_{m aff}\) dominate \(\|r\|^2\). Their normalized exterior integrals satisfy \[  rac{D!}{\pi^D}\int_{\|r\|>R_s}\|r\|^{-2D-2}\,dr = rac D{R_s^2}=16Ds^2. 	ag{16} \] This controls the entire nonlinear exterior, without a large-field estimate for \(H\). If \(k
e0\), the actual energy has no zero: a zero would require \(r=0\) and \(f(0)=0\). Compactness on the remaining ball and (16) prove that (3) is finite and positive. Put \(\xi_N=\delta_0/D\) and \(	au_N=16Ds^2|k|^2\le\delta_0\). Using (14)--(16) on the inside and outside separately gives \[ (1+\xi_N)^{-m}(1-	au_N) \le |k|^2\mathcal P_N \le(1-\xi_N)^{-m}+	au_N. 	ag{17} \] Since \(D\ge2\), put \(v=m\xi_N\le3/16384\). Convexity gives \((1+\xi_N)^{-m}\ge1-v\). Bernoulli's inequality gives \((1-\xi_N)^m\ge1-v\), hence \((1-\xi_N)^{-m}\le(1-v)^{-1}\le1+2v\). The two sides of (17) are therefore bounded by \[ 1- rac5{16384}\le |k|^2\mathcal P_N \le1+ rac8{16384}=1+\delta. \] Since \(5/16384<\delta\), this proves (5). If \(k=0\), holomorphy gives \(f(r)=O(\|r\|)\) near zero. The actual energy is at most a constant times \(\|r\|^2\) there, and (3) dominates a positive multiple of \(\int_0^{R_s}u^{-3}du\). It diverges, proving the zero convention. ## 5. Logarithmic consequence and scope Let \(S_N^{m rec}=\mathcal B_N^2/\mathcal P_N\), with reciprocal zero at infinity. For every nonzero source, (5) gives \[ \left| rac\pi N\log S_N^{m rec} - rac{2\pi}N\log|K_N|ight| \le- rac\pi N\log(1-\delta) \le rac\pi{2047N}. 	ag{18} \] Zeros coincide exactly. The same bound holds between \(\pi N^{-1}\log(1+S_N^{m rec})\) and \(\pi N^{-1}\log(1+|K_N|^2)\), including at zeros. For any fixed positive target rate, convergence to that rate for the reciprocal expression is therefore equivalent to convergence for the original squared source. No eventual nonvanishing was assumed. The comparison constant is universal, not chosen from any source value or filling packet. The closing row, full physical algebra, normal channels, objective and original budgets have not changed. The integral is not claimed to be a separately topological quantity at each finite level. Its signed source remains inside the denominator. No geometric energy estimate, contributing-cycle coefficient, arbitrary-short-filling volume theorem or finite-exception theorem is supplied by this representation. ## Complete inputs and coverage The full texts [P] and [H] fix the source and multiplicities. [R] already supplies the damped reciprocal construction, affine identity and fixed-ball strategy. Those steps are proved again here with the physical closing bound retained sharply; the addition is the undamped comparison (5), with no new budget factor. All three complete matching texts were read. title: A uniform Gaussian integral for the normalized Conway minimum
text: # A uniform Gaussian integral for the normalized Conway minimum 23 November 2026. Research note. The manuscripts and earlier final notes remain unchanged. The source minimum is a polynomial of degree four, although its number of variables grows with the quantum level. This permits a uniform comparison with a positive integral. In particular the inverse temperature can be chosen as \(N^4\), simultaneously with the quantum level \(N\). The comparison keeps the Gaussian determinant, whose dimension-independent bound was proved previously. This closes the simultaneous-limit qualification in the earlier Gaussian calculation. It does not evaluate the minimum. An absolute error of polynomial size can still exceed an exponentially small minimum, so the result does not prove a volume lower bound. ## 1. The original normalized source Use the full Newton boundary spaces and the Hilbert--Schmidt budgets of the [normalized source](research_convex_normalized_conway_source.md). If the fixed literal Conway expression has \(s\) proper vertices, put \(D=Ns\), and identify its packets with \(\mathbb C^D\). Here \(N\ge2\) is the quantum level. All repeated-root derivatives remain in these spaces. Write the original normalized maps as \(\Phi_v\), and put \[ G_v(x)=\Phi_v((x_c)_c)-x_v,\qquad E(x)=\|G(x)\|^2+|cx|^2,\qquad \sigma=\frac1{16}. \tag{1} \] The row \(c\) is the original marked closing row at the top packet, divided by its recorded budget. No cap, phase, or framing factor is changed. Each normalized local tensor has Hilbert--Schmidt norm at most \(\sigma\). The feasible set \(\mathcal D\) is the product of the packet unit balls. The complete source proof and the [residual-Jacobian calculation](research_conway_residual_jacobian_gaussian_determinant.md) give the following facts. The minimum \(x_*\) is unique, is the global minimum on the whole coordinate space, and satisfies \[ \|(x_*)_v\|\le\frac{33}{256},\qquad e:=E(x_*)\le\sigma^4,\qquad I\preceq D_{\mathbb R}^2E(x)\preceq3I\quad(x\in\mathcal D). \tag{2} \] Let \(H=D_{\mathbb R}^2E(x_*)\) and \[ g=\sqrt{\det_{\mathbb R}(H/2)},\qquad \gamma=\frac{197}{196}. \] The positive square root is understood. The earlier determinant theorem gives \[ \sqrt{1-2^{-22}}\le g\le\gamma. \tag{3} \] Its Hilbert--Schmidt hypothesis is retained here; this is not an unproved determinant assertion for a different physical metric. For a real inverse temperature \(\tau>0\), define the positive normalized integral, using real Lebesgue measure on \(\mathbb C^D\), \[ Z(\tau)=\left(\frac{\tau}{\pi}\right)^D \int_{\mathbb C^D}e^{-\tau E(x)}\,dx. \tag{4} \] Ordering children before parents makes \(DG\) triangular with diagonal blocks \(-I\). The map \(G\) is a polynomial automorphism, with real Jacobian one: its inverse is the finite upward recursion \(x_v=\Phi_v((x_c)_c)-r_v\). In particular, \[ \int_{\mathbb C^D}e^{-E(x)}\,dx \le\int_{\mathbb C^D}e^{-\|G(x)\|^2}\,dx=\pi^D. \tag{5} \] The integral in (4) is therefore finite when \(\tau\ge1\). ## 2. An explicit finite-level estimate Suppose \(\tau\ge2\), and set \[ r^2=\frac{8(D+1)\log\tau}{\tau}\le\frac14,\qquad \epsilon=\tau^{-D-2},\qquad \delta=\tau\left(\frac9{128}r^3+\frac1{1024}r^4\right). \tag{6} \] The symbol \(r\) here is a positive real radius in the entire packet direct sum. It is unrelated to the recursion residual \(G(x)\). **Theorem.** For the original objective (1), \[ \boxed{\quad e^{-\delta}(1-\epsilon) \le g\,e^{\tau e}Z(\tau) \le e^\delta+\gamma e^{\sigma^4}\epsilon . \quad} \tag{7} \] Consequently, \[ \left|\log Z(\tau)+\tau e+\log g\right| \le\delta+4\epsilon . \tag{8} \] All quantities refer to the same objective and its original budgets. **Proof.** Put \(T=DG(x_*)\). Since \(G\) is quadratic, its Taylor formula is exact: \[ G(x_*+h)=G(x_*)+Th+\mathcal Q(h),\qquad \|\mathcal Q(h)\|\le\frac1{32}\|h\|^2,\qquad \|T\|\le\frac98. \tag{9} \] Only product vertices contribute to \(\mathcal Q\). At one such vertex its value is \(\Phi_v(h_L,h_R)\). The disjointness of sibling pairs bounds the direct-sum norm by \(\sigma\|h\|^2/2\), giving (9). The linear term in \(E\) vanishes at the interior minimum. Its quadratic term includes \(2\operatorname{Re}\langle G(x_*),\mathcal Q(h)\rangle\); that term belongs to \(H\), and must not be discarded. The remaining terms are precisely \[ E(x_*+h)=e+\tfrac12H[h,h] +2\operatorname{Re}\langle Th,\mathcal Q(h)\rangle +\|\mathcal Q(h)\|^2. \tag{10} \] Thus on the radius-\(r\) ball the absolute value of the last two terms, multiplied by \(\tau\), is at most \(\delta\). This ball is contained in \(\mathcal D\), since \(r\le1/2\) and \(33/256+1/2<1\). Consider the probability density \[ d\mu(h)=g\left(\frac{\tau}{\pi}\right)^D e^{-\tau H[h,h]/2}\,dh . \tag{11} \] Diagonalizing the real positive matrix \(H/2\succeq I/2\) and integrating each one-dimensional Gaussian gives \[ \mathbb E_\mu e^{\tau\|h\|^2/4}\le2^D . \tag{12} \] Indeed each of the \(2D\) real coordinates contributes a square-root factor at most \(\sqrt2\). Markov's inequality, which follows by integrating the pointwise indicator bound, now yields \[ \mu\{\|h\|\ge r\} \le2^De^{-\tau r^2/4} =2^D\tau^{-2(D+1)} \le\epsilon . \tag{13} \] The contribution of the radius-\(r\) ball to the middle quantity in (7) is therefore between \(e^{-\delta}(1-\epsilon)\) and \(e^\delta\). It remains to bound the original integral outside that ball. For \(x\in\mathcal D\), segment integration of the lower Hessian bound gives \(E(x)\ge e+\|x-x_*\|^2/2\). For \(x\notin\mathcal D\), choose a vertex outside its packet ball whose children are inside theirs. Its normalized output has norm at most \(\sigma\), so \[ E(x)>(1-\sigma)^2=\frac{225}{256}. \] Since \(e\le\sigma^4\) and \(r^2/2\le1/8\), this also exceeds \(e+r^2/2\). Consequently that same energy gap holds on the entire complement of the radius-\(r\) ball. Using (5), its contribution to \(e^{\tau e}Z(\tau)\) is at most \[ \tau^D \exp\left\{e-\frac{\tau-1}{2}r^2\right\} \le e^{\sigma^4}\tau^{-D-2}. \tag{14} \] The last inequality uses \((\tau-1)/\tau\ge1/2\) in (6). Multiplication by \(g\le\gamma\) proves (7). Finally \(\epsilon\le1/8\) and \(\gamma e^{\sigma^4}<4\). Taking logarithms of (7), using \(-\log(1-\epsilon)\le2\epsilon\) and \(\log(1+u)\le u\) for \(u\ge0\), proves (8). This completes the proof. ## 3. Simultaneous quantum level and temperature Fix the literal expression, hence \(s\). Take \(\tau_N=N^4\). For all sufficiently large \(N\), the radius condition in (6) holds. Its error satisfies \[ \delta_N \le\frac{9\sqrt2}{8} \frac{((Ns+1)\log\tau_N)^{3/2}}{\sqrt{\tau_N}} +\frac1{16} \frac{((Ns+1)\log\tau_N)^2}{\tau_N} =O_s\left(\frac{(\log N)^{3/2}}{\sqrt N}\right). \tag{15} \] In particular, with the same \(e_N\) and \(g_N\) as in (2)--(3), \[ \boxed{\qquad Z_N(N^4)=\frac{e^{-N^4e_N}}{g_N}\,(1+o(1)). \qquad} \tag{16} \] The error tends to zero as \(N\) and \(\tau_N\) grow together. More generally (7) applies to any temperature sequence satisfying its radius condition, with a relative error tending to zero whenever \((D+1)^3(\log\tau)^3/\tau\to0\). If \(B_N\) is the unchanged product of all source budgets, the original comparison remains \[ B_N^2e_N\le |K_N|^2\le\gamma B_N^2e_N. \tag{17} \] Thus (16) gives a controlled positive integral for this particular minimum. It does not give its value from the geometry. For example, (8) estimates \(e_N\) with an absolute error \((\delta_N+4\epsilon_N)/N^4\) after the determinant is retained. Such an error need not be small relative to \(e_N\). If \(e_N\) is exponentially small, the determinant term and this absolute error cannot be omitted when extracting its rate. No nonzero geometric coefficient, arbitrary-short-filling lower bound, or finite-exception volume theorem follows from (16). ## Complete sources and coverage Both complete texts were read at the matching versions below. The finite-level tail bounds and the simultaneous estimate are proved in Sections 2--3. | Source | SHA-256 | |---|---| | [Normalized source and its exact budgets](research_convex_normalized_conway_source.md) | 6b89b4c6a67ef7a32cc41a5966c650f32de65d284ae7b70d94a71bddba21df3c | | [Residual automorphism and Gaussian determinant](research_conway_residual_jacobian_gaussian_determinant.md) | db22b86a97302926fed77385f82ff2284109e288ec3d03dd99538d3671c926b2 | The full uniform-physical-quartic note was read for coverage at 39895b430535f565d30133b46ef57f67589207bc83f40597ffe96e2ce79bbda8. It uses different budgets and is not assigned the determinant bound (3) here. The previous Gaussian note proves its Laplace limit only at each fixed quantum level; (7) supplies the missing uniform error. No general novelty is claimed for Laplace's method, Gaussian tails, or Taylor's formula. Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used. No mathematical program, numerical experiment, build, git action, or earlier-final edit was performed.

title: Polynomial structural costs in the uniform physical Conway metric
text: # Polynomial structural costs in the uniform physical Conway metric 22 November 2026. Research note. Earlier finals and public manuscripts remain unchanged. The full physical pair algebra has a positive metric in which the actual quarter-turn is unitary, multiplication has polynomial tensor norm, and both original closing rows have polynomial dual cost. Consequently the synthesis covariance of every fixed unfilled Conway tree has polynomial condition number. This uses the uniform balanced physical metric, rather than the normalized Newton coefficient metric or the binomial head metric. Recompiling the known convex quartic in this metric permits constant structural budgets. Its leaf norms and its numerical minimum change. This is not a bound on the surviving projection of the actual leaf data or on its overlap with the original closing. ## 1. The full physical algebra and the chosen positive metric Fix \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), and \[ q=e^{\pi i/N},\qquad Q=q^2,\qquad x=q^d=-q^{-1}. \tag{1} \] Declare the recorded balanced physical basis \(w_0,\ldots,w_d\) orthonormal. This is the **uniform** head metric: \(\|w_a\|=1\), not \(\binom da^{-1/2}\). Give \(V_N\otimes V_N\) its product metric and its endomorphisms the unnormalized Hilbert--Schmidt inner product \[ \langle A,B\rangle_{\mathrm{ph}}=\operatorname{Tr}(A^*B). \tag{2} \] In particular the identity on the physical pair has norm \(N\). The original balanced generators and the actual pair Casimir are \[ Ew_a=(Q^{-a}-1)w_{a-1},\quad Fw_a=(1-Q^{a+1})w_{a+1},\quad Kw_a=xQ^{-a}w_a, \] \[ E_\Sigma=E_1K_2+E_2,\quad F_\Sigma=F_1+K_1^{-1}F_2,\quad \Omega=F_\Sigma E_\Sigma+qK_1K_2+q^{-1}K_1^{-1}K_2^{-1}. \tag{3} \] Missing extreme arrows are zero. The complete physical commutant theorem identifies \[ \begin{gathered} \mathcal A_N=\mathbb C[\Omega]\simeq\mathbb C[z]/P_N(z), \qquad\mathcal A_N\subset\operatorname{End}(V_N\otimes V_N),\\ P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2 . \end{gathered} \tag{4} \] faithfully, and \(\dim_{\mathbb C}\mathcal A_N=N\). Here \(T_N\) is the Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind. All first derivatives at double Casimir roots remain independent directions of this space, including at even and composite levels. Restriction of (2) to \(\mathcal A_N\) is positive definite. We do not replace (4) by its distinct-root value quotient. All physical coefficients below are known before evaluating a closed source. One can choose a concrete Hilbert--Schmidt orthonormal basis \(F_1,\ldots,F_N\) of \(\mathcal A_N\) by Gram--Schmidt applied to \(I,\Omega,\ldots,\Omega^d\), with positive normalizing square roots. These powers are independent by the full minimal polynomial (4). Their finite entries, Gram matrix, and resulting basis are algebraic at each level. No source value or chosen leaf packet enters this choice. No numerical conditioning of that basis construction is asserted. ## 2. Actual turns, products, and both original closures The actual cup, ordinary cap, and unrestricted marked cap in the recorded all-primal chart are \[ p_{ab}=Nx^{-b}\mathbf1_{a+b=d},\qquad \ell_{ab}=x^a\mathbf1_{a+b=d}/N,\qquad m_{ab}=x^b/N^2. \tag{5} \] Their fixed duality conventions and snakes are those of the source directs. In particular \(mp=1\). The marked cap is not substituted for the ordinary cap inside a turn. Let \(\mathcal T\) be the genuine unscaled quarter-turn. On a whole physical Hopf box \(B\in\mathcal A_N\), its exact formula is \[ (\mathcal TB)_{(a,b);(c,e)} =x^{a-e}B_{(d-a,c);(b,d-e)}. \tag{6} \] This formula uses the symmetry of actual Hopf boxes in the recorded chart; no all-array identification of different oriented bends is needed here. It is the original cup/cap contraction on \(\mathcal A_N\), with their \(N\) and \(1/N\) factors canceled exactly, not an additional crossing or a rescaling of the turn. It preserves \(\mathcal A_N\) and obeys \(\mathcal T^2=I\). The index map on the right of (6) permutes the entire four-index array, and \(|x^{a-e}|=1\). Summing the absolute squares of all entries therefore proves \[ \boxed{\quad \|\mathcal TB\|_{\mathrm{ph}}=\|B\|_{\mathrm{ph}},\qquad \|\mathcal T\|_{\mathrm{op}}=1,\qquad \|\mathcal T\|_{\mathrm{HS}(\mathcal A_N)}=\sqrt N . \quad} \tag{7} \] The last norm is the coefficient-tensor norm of this linear map on the \(N\)-dimensional positive space, not a norm of one box. Product is ordinary physical composition \(M(A,B)=AB\). The elementary matrix inequality \[ \|AB\|_{\mathrm{ph}} \le \|A\|_{\mathrm{ph}}\|B\|_{\mathrm{op}} \le \|A\|_{\mathrm{ph}}\|B\|_{\mathrm{ph}} \tag{8} \] gives its bilinear norm at most one. In the orthonormal basis above, \[ \|M\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^2 =\sum_{i,j=1}^N\|F_iF_j\|_{\mathrm{ph}}^2\le N^2. \tag{9} \] Thus its tensor operator norm is also at most \(N\). This sharper restriction bound is sufficient; the full ambient pair-matrix composition tensor has Hilbert--Schmidt norm \(N^3\). Retain the original two normalized closing rows \[ \lambda_d(B)=\phi(B) =\frac1N\operatorname{Tr}[(I\otimes g)B], \quad g=K^{1-N}=(-1)^dK, \qquad \lambda_0(B)=mBp . \tag{10} \] The exact sewing identity, including the unrestricted mark, is \[ \lambda_0=\phi\circ\mathcal T \quad\hbox{on }\mathcal A_N . \tag{11} \] It retains every Hermite channel. For example, on \(f(\Omega)\), these are the full Frobenius functional and \(f(q+q^{-1})\). Since \(g\) is diagonal unitary, the ambient functional \(\phi\) has Hilbert--Schmidt dual norm \(\|I\otimes g\|_{\mathrm{HS}}/N=1\). Restriction and (7)--(11) give \(\|\lambda_d\|_*,\|\lambda_0\|_*\le1\). Conversely \(\lambda_0(I)=1\) and \(\phi(\mathcal TI)=1\); both \(I\) and \(\mathcal TI\) have physical norm \(N\). Hence \[ \boxed{\qquad N^{-1}\le\|\lambda_0\|_*=\|\lambda_d\|_*\le1 . \qquad} \tag{12} \] The equality of the two norms follows from the unitary involution. Off this physical algebra the marked functional \(B\mapsto mBp\) has ambient dual norm \(\sqrt N\), since \(\|p\|=N^{3/2}\) and \(\|m\|_*=N^{-1}\). The stronger bound in (12) uses the exact restricted identity (11). No ordinary cap has replaced the original mark on arbitrary arrays. ## 3. Polynomial covariance for every unfilled Conway tree Let \(E\) be a fixed finite expression whose leaves are independent copies of the entire space \(\mathcal A_N\), with binary products and genuine turns. If there are \(l\) leaf occurrences and \(p\) products, then \(p=l-1\). The actual synthesis map is \[ B_E:\mathcal A_N^{\otimes l}\longrightarrow\mathcal A_N, \quad B_{\mathrm{leaf}}=I,\quad B_{\mathcal TE}=\mathcal TB_E,\quad B_{EF}=M(B_E\otimes B_F). \tag{13} \] All tensor products use the physical Hilbert metrics. The map depends on the unfilled expression, not on the eventual filling leaf values. **Theorem.** There is an explicit linear right inverse \(S_E\), using only (13), the physical identity box, and turns, with \[ B_ES_E=I,\qquad \|B_E\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le N^p,\qquad \|S_E\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le N^p . \tag{14} \] Consequently, for \(C_E=B_EB_E^*\), \[ \boxed{\qquad N^{-2p}I\le C_E\le N^{2p}I,\qquad \operatorname{cond}_2(C_E)\le N^{4p}. \qquad} \tag{15} \] For either original normalized row in (10), its squared dual cost in the synthesis quotient norm is \[ a_\lambda(E)=\lambda C_E\lambda^*,\qquad N^{-2p-2}\le a_\lambda(E)\le N^{2p}. \tag{16} \] These bounds are uniform over the filling assignments at the leaves. **Proof.** Equations (7) and (9) give \(\|B_E\|\le N^p\) by induction. Define \[ S_{\mathrm{leaf}}=I,\qquad S_{\mathcal TE}=S_E\mathcal T,\qquad S_{EF}=(S_E\otimes S_F)\iota,\quad \iota(y)=y\otimes I . \tag{17} \] The last \(I\) is the known physical identity box, not an identity depending on an unknown tangle value. Since \(M(y,I)=y\) and \(\mathcal T^2=I\), induction gives \(B_ES_E=I\). Also \(\|\iota\|=\|I\|_{\mathrm{ph}}=N\), proving the right-inverse bound in (14). For any \(y\), the identity \(B_ES_E=I\) gives \[ \|y\|^2 =|\langle B_E^*y,S_Ey\rangle| \le N^p\|B_E^*y\|\|y\|. \] Thus \(\|B_E^*y\|\ge N^{-p}\|y\|\). Together with the upper bound in (14), this proves (15). Applying (15) to the Riesz vector of \(\lambda\) and using (12) proves (16). \(\square\) For example the least-norm expanded lift is \(B_E^*C_E^{-1}y\), and its squared norm is \(y^*C_E^{-1}y\). This follows directly by splitting any other lift into that vector and a vector in \(\ker B_E\). The latter is orthogonal to \(\operatorname{ran}B_E^*\). Equation (15) therefore makes this quotient norm polynomially equivalent to the fixed physical norm. It does not identify a prescribed leaf tensor with its least-norm lift. The exponent \(p\) is fixed by the template. No bound independent of a growing tree size, and no filling-dependent cancellation estimate, is being deduced from (15). Every leaf in (13)--(17) is still an independent copy of the full algebra. The right inverse is allowed to insert the identity into those slots. It need not respect a prescribed short filling at a leaf. Thus (15) does not give a lower singular-value bound for a partially specialized boundary channel after some incoming packets have been fixed. Such a channel can have a kernel or poor conditioning. For the filling application, keep all crossing blocks as variable leaf slots when constructing \(B_E\), and only then insert their actual fixed or free filling packets as the input tensor \(v\). Their surviving projection and closing angle remain separate data. ## 4. The convex quartic with constant structural budgets Take an actual literal source expression with prescribed full leaf boxes \(A_v\in\mathcal A_N\). The root is one of (10), multiplied, if necessary, by its recorded known scalar \(\eta_N\). All framing phases and any specified cut or peripheral normalization remain in this scalar; it is not chosen from the value of the source. Choose the following known budgets: \[ \begin{array}{c|c} \text{vertex}&b_v\\ \hline \text{prescribed leaf }A_v&16\max(1,\|A_v\|_{\mathrm{ph}})\\ \text{product}&16\\ \text{genuine turn}&16\\ \text{root }\eta_N\lambda&16\max(1,|\eta_N|) \end{array} \qquad B_{\mathrm{ph}}=\prod_v b_v . \tag{18} \] In particular an identity leaf has budget \(16N\). Every normalized leaf has norm at most \(\sigma=1/16\); every normalized linear map and closing row has operator norm at most \(\sigma\); and every normalized product has bilinear norm at most \(\sigma\), by (7), (8), and (12). This last norm is the supremum over two separately unit inputs. It is not the norm of the linear map on the Hilbert tensor product or the coefficient Hilbert--Schmidt norm. In particular (9) only bounds the normalized product's coefficient norm by \(N/16\). The convexity and source proof below uses the bilinear bound, not a level-independent coefficient norm. One may instead use the larger polynomial budgets \(16N\) and \(16\sqrt N\) for products and turns if a separate argument requires small coefficient norms. That gives another valid recompilation, not the same numerical minimum. For each proper vertex \(v\), divide its true physical packet by the product of the budgets in the subtree rooted at \(v\), including the budget at \(v\) itself. Denote the result by \(a_v\). The normalized maps \(\Phi_v\) are the actual leaf, product, or turn divided by its own budget. Their exact recursion and the normalized original root row \(L\) give \[ a_v=\Phi_v((a_c)_c),\qquad La_{\mathrm{top}}=K_N/B_{\mathrm{ph}} . \tag{19} \] The true field has each packet norm at most \(\sigma\). All derivatives below use the real part of the direct-sum physical inner product. On the product \(\mathcal D\) of physical unit balls put \(\mathcal R_v(z)=\Phi_v((z_c)_c)-z_v\), \(G=(\mathcal R_v)_v\), and \[ E_{\mathrm{ph}}(z)= \sum_{v\ {\rm proper}} \|\Phi_v((z_c)_c)-z_v\|_{\mathrm{ph}}^2 +|Lz_{\mathrm{top}}|^2 . \tag{20} \] There are \(2Ns\) real variables for \(s\) proper vertices, and the degree is at most four. The dimension-free normalized source proof applies in these new orthonormal coordinates using the bounds just stated. Explicitly \(DG=-I+A\), with each child appearing in one parent row and at most two children per row, so \(\|A\|\le\sqrt2\sigma\le1/8\). The half-Hessian residual curvature is bounded by \(\sigma(1+\sigma)\sum_v\|h_v\|^2\), using disjoint sibling pairs. The scalar closing adds a positive term of norm at most \(\sigma^2\). These are the same bounds as in the normalized convex theorem and give \[ I\le D_{\mathbb R}^2E_{\mathrm{ph}}\le3I,\qquad \left\|z_v-\tfrac12(\nabla E_{\mathrm{ph}})_v\right\| \le33/256 . \tag{21} \] Thus the half-gradient map is a contraction with factor \(1/2\), the unique minimum is interior, and the Hessian bounds are uniform in the level and the number of vertices. Indeed the half-step at a nontop packet is \(\Phi_v-(D_v\Phi_{\mathrm{parent}})^*\mathcal R_{\mathrm{parent}}\), of norm at most \(\sigma+\sigma(1+\sigma)=33/256\); at the top it is \(\Phi_v-L^*Lz_v\), of norm at most \(\sigma+\sigma^2=17/256\). For completeness, segment integration gives \(\|G(z)-G(a)\|\ge(7/8)\|z-a\|\). Since \(\|L\|\le1/16\), \[ |K_N/B_{\mathrm{ph}}-Lz_{\mathrm{top}}| \le\|G(z)\|/14 . \] One Cauchy--Schwarz inequality and the true competitor (19) prove \[ \boxed{\qquad B_{\mathrm{ph}}^2\min_{\mathcal D}E_{\mathrm{ph}} \le |K_N|^2 \le\frac{197}{196}B_{\mathrm{ph}}^2 \min_{\mathcal D}E_{\mathrm{ph}} . \qquad} \tag{22} \] This includes zeros and uses the original scalar closing. At any feasible trial, \[ D_{\mathrm{ph}}(z)=E_{\mathrm{ph}}(z) -\tfrac12\|\nabla E_{\mathrm{ph}}(z)\|^2 \le\min E_{\mathrm{ph}}, \tag{23} \] by completing the square in the strong-convexity inequality. Hence the original lower witness remains available with the new budget: \[ B_{\mathrm{ph}}^2\max(0,D_{\mathrm{ph}}(z)) \le |K_N|^2 \le(197/196)B_{\mathrm{ph}}^2E_{\mathrm{ph}}(z). \tag{24} \] The polynomial degree assertion here concerns the objective. No degree-four semidefinite exactness theorem under the constant bilinear-norm budgets is inferred. For a fixed template, all nonleaf factors in (18) are constant, apart from the explicitly retained scalar \(\eta_N\). Thus structural gluing contributes no level-dependent budget. This does not estimate the leaf packets by their nodal eigenvalues. For a coarse finite growth check, (3) gives \(\|\Omega\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le18\). For the full Newton polynomials \[ c_j=q^{2j+1}+q^{-2j-1},\quad s_r=\prod_{j=1}^r2\sin(\pi j/N),\quad s_0=1,\quad b_r(z)=s_r^{-2}\prod_{j<r}(c_j-z), \] one has \[ \|b_r(\Omega)\|_{\mathrm{ph}}\le N20^r/s_r^2 \le20^d/N,\qquad 0\le r\le d. \] Indeed \(s_rs_{d-r}=N\) and \(s_{d-r}\le2^{d-r}\). The exact signed packets \(R^{\pm1}=\kappa^{\pm1}\sum_r(-q)^{\pm r}b_r\), where \(\kappa=e^{\pi i d^2/(2N)}\), therefore obey \(\|R^{\pm1}\|_{\mathrm{ph}}\le20^d\). Fixed products and turns of these packets have at most exponential growth, by (7)--(8). Thus a fixed literal construction from signed crossing packets and identities, products, and turns still has \(\log B_{\mathrm{ph}}=O(N)\). This is a coarse upper bound, not a selected geometric rate. ## 5. What has and has not changed The earlier fixed Newton coefficient metric makes the turn unitary and the two closing rows unit vectors, but its multiplication and unfilled synthesis covariance can have exponential cost. The present theorem changes the positive metric to the inherited uniform physical Hilbert--Schmidt metric. It proves polynomial structural costs in that metric, rather than contradicting those Newton-metric lower bounds. In particular \(B_{\mathrm{ph}}\), the normalized trial coordinates, and the raw minimum (20) are new. They are not asserted to agree with their counterparts in the earlier quartic. Both constructions retain the same original source and have their stated constant-factor comparisons to it. No uniformly conditioned change to Newton coordinates is needed to evaluate (20) from full physical matrices. If a full physical matrix approximation to a true box is supplied, orthogonal projection onto \(\mathcal A_N\) cannot increase its Hilbert--Schmidt error. This retains all \(N\) physical Hermite coordinates. It does not turn a one-coherent-input estimate into a whole-matrix estimate. For actual leaf tensors \(v=\bigotimes_jA_j\), there remains the projection onto \((\ker B_E)^\perp\) and then the angle with the prescribed closing row. Neither (15) nor (16) bounds these quantities below. In particular a polynomially conditioned synthesis covariance does not make an arbitrary signed closed period a positive norm. The physical metric here also differs from the binomial metric used in the small-activity full-norm Euler packet estimates. No estimate is transferred between those metrics without its actual cost. There is no new original-source lower bound, geometric trial field, or arbitrary-short-filling volume theorem in this note. ## Complete proof sources and coverage The following entire matching sources were read. Their actual finite identities are used above; all new norm, covariance and recompilation estimates are proved inline. | Source | SHA-256 | |---|---| | [Full physical pair commutant and original trace](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_pair_casimir_commutant_and_rotated_trace.md) | 00ab946b3eddb61256bdbd8ec487789a15991a80e1a28b4eee53bbb4a00f7666 | | [Actual Newton turn, signed packets and both closures](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_newton_turn_positive_gram.md) | d8b21fa8db909120035e86e997a0e02cb84f8dce2dcf6fb244bb5c85c17e28a3 | | [Full-circle sewing and the literal marked closure](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/general_augmented_graph_source_extension.md) | 74487abaae10416cc967b21f442bc05502cc634acd03cd43a38deeaafa5ef86a | | [Dimension-free normalized convex source](research_convex_normalized_conway_source.md) | 6b89b4c6a67ef7a32cc41a5966c650f32de65d284ae7b70d94a71bddba21df3c | For coverage, the entire boundary-quotient note at debe56dbad8151b90d44d0fccbf0dcf33dafb780370e01c8acdadbd2939dc077 and the entire balanced bridge-source note at 6f4d4847218954dc0eff16b2269ada870f36afbaaddd7e1708e8f9e05b5d896f were read at matching versions. The former already constructs the synthesis quotient metric in Newton coordinates; the latter already proves polynomial physical cup/cap norms. The addition here is the uniform-physical restricted multiplication bound, the explicit polynomial right inverse and all-tree covariance comparison, and the resulting source-exact quartic with constant structural budgets. No general novelty is claimed for Hilbert--Schmidt inequalities, least-norm lifts, or strongly convex residual formulations. Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used. No mathematical program, numerical test, build, git operation, or earlier-final edit was performed.

title: A relative asymptotic for the original undamped reciprocal source
text: # A relative asymptotic for the original undamped reciprocal source 24 November 2026. Research proof. Earlier finals and manuscripts are unchanged. The original physical reciprocal integral has relative error tending to zero, without damping its closing row or changing its budgets. The additional input is specific to the original source: either closing after a product has bilinear norm at most \(1/N\). This bounds every nonlinear residual coefficient more strongly than the generic bilinear budget does. Fixed leaf degree then controls its Gaussian moments and the full reciprocal integral. The antichain expansion and its orthogonality were already available in [O]. The reciprocal construction and the shrinking physical closing row were established in [U]. The result below combines these with the source-specific coefficient estimate, not a geometric evaluation of the integral or a lower bound for the knot scalar. ## 1. Original physical source and statement Use the full \(N\)-dimensional physical algebra \(\mathcal A_N=\mathbb C[\Omega]\), with the inherited matrix Hilbert--Schmidt norm of [P,H], at every \(N\ge2\). All double-root derivative directions remain independent. Fix a literal normalized Conway expression tree \(\mathscr T\), with \(s\) proper vertices and \(L\ge1\) prescribed leaf occurrences. Its only internal maps are the actual product and genuine turn, with exactly [P]'s constant structural budgets \(16\). Prescribed leaf budgets and the original root budget are also unchanged. Write their product as \(\mathcal B_N\). Let \(\Phi_v\) denote the normalized maps, \(c_N\) the original normalized closing row, and \(D=Ns\). Set \[ G_v(x)=\Phi_v((x_j)_{j\ {\rm child\ of}\ v})-x_v,\qquad E_N(x)=\|G(x)\|^2+|c_Nx|^2,\qquad \mathcal P_N=\frac{D!}{\pi^D}\int_{\mathbb C^D}E_N(x)^{-D-1}\,dx . \tag{1} \] The integral is extended and nonnegative. Its base is the original degree-at-most-four objective, with the same full matrices, phases, turns, mark, framing and external source factors. The inverse \(H=G^{-1}\) is the triangular polynomial recursion \[ H(r)_v=\Phi_v((H(r)_j)_j)-r_v,\qquad |\det_{\mathbb R}DH|=1 . \tag{2} \] Put \[ f(r)=c_NH(r)=k+dr+p(r),\qquad k=f(0)=K_N/\mathcal B_N,\quad d=Df(0),\quad p(0)=Dp(0)=0 . \tag{3} \] The true forward field and \(k\) are used only in the proof. Neither is input to (1). The actual physical estimates of [U] give, uniformly over all normalized leaf choices, \[ |k|^2\le N^{-1},\qquad \|d\|^2\le C/N , \tag{4} \] with an absolute constant \(C\). The stronger displayed constants in [U] are unnecessary here. Define \[ \rho_L(N)= \begin{cases} 0,&L=1,\\ N^{-1},&L=2,\\ N^{-1}\log(2N),&L=3,\\ N^{-2/(L-1)},&L\ge4 . \end{cases} \tag{5} \] **Theorem.** There are constants \(C_{\mathscr T},N_{\mathscr T}\), independent of the actual normalized leaf packets and their phases, such that every nonzero original source satisfies \[ \boxed{\qquad \bigl||k|^2\mathcal P_N-1\bigr| \le C_{\mathscr T}\rho_L(N) \quad(N\ge N_{\mathscr T}). \qquad} \tag{6} \] If \(L=1\), the equality \(|k|^2\mathcal P_N=1\) is exact. At \(K_N=0\), \(\mathcal P_N=+\infty\), as in [U]. The theorem has no parity restriction or prior lower bound on \(|K_N|\). It is uniform for arbitrary prescribed short-filled leaf packets in the fixed literal tree. For nonzero sources, (6) gives the same relative comparison between \(|K_N|^2\) and \(\mathcal B_N^2/\mathcal P_N\), with error \(C_{\mathscr T}\rho_L(N)=o(1)\). No additional normalization factor is restored. ## 2. The two physical closing forms after a product The original rows of [P,H] satisfy \[ \lambda_0(AB)=\lambda_0(A)\lambda_0(B),\qquad \|\lambda_0\|_*\le(2N)^{-1/2},\qquad \phi(AB)=\frac1N\operatorname{Tr}[(I\otimes g)AB], \tag{7} \] where \(g\) is the actual unitary pivot. The first identity is evaluation at the physical Casimir node \(q+q^{-1}\), on the full algebra, including its derivative directions. The row bound is proved in [U, Section 2] from the actual pair characteristic polynomial and multiplicity \(2N\). The trace identity is [H, (11)]. Matrix Cauchy--Schwarz therefore gives, for either \(\lambda\in\{\lambda_0,\phi\}\), \[ |\lambda(AB)| \le \frac1N\|A\|_{\rm ph}\|B\|_{\rm ph}. \tag{8} \] For \(\lambda_0\), (7) in fact gives the constant \(1/(2N)\). The genuine turn obeys \(\lambda_0\mathcal T=\phi\), \(\phi\mathcal T=\lambda_0\). Consequently any top unary corridor carries the original row to a scalar of modulus at most one times one of these two rows. Its residual terms are linear. Thus the first binary gate below that corridor, if one exists, is observed through the bilinear form (8), with all its normalized scalar factors having modulus at most one. This is stronger than estimating multiplication and the closing separately. ## 3. Complete antichain coefficients and their physical saving An antichain \(A\) is a set of proper vertices with no member an ancestor of another. The exact recursion (2) gives \[ f(r)=k+\sum_{A\ne\varnothing,\ A\ {\rm antichain}} C_A((r_v)_{v\in A}) . \tag{9} \] Here \(C_A\) is complex multilinear in its \(|A|\) packet inputs; the signs from the terms \(-r_v\) are included. To obtain it, replace the subtrees at \(A\) by their free inputs and evaluate every other branch with the actual normalized maps and prescribed constants. This is the antichain expansion already used in [O, (20)]. A choice of a residual stops its subtree, so an admissible set contributes once. There is no repeated occurrence or hidden combinatorial multiplicity. Distinct literal child subtrees have disjoint variables. An antichain has at most \(L\) members. For every nonlinear term, with \(a=|A|\ge2\), we claim \[ \|C_A\|_{\rm HS}^2\le N^{a-3}. \tag{10} \] All coefficient norms here use physical orthonormal packet bases. After fixing some inputs of an antichain coefficient to unit basis vectors, each remaining subtree linear slice has norm at most one. This follows inductively from the normalized product and turn bounds, and from the forward constants of norm at most \(1/16\). Consider the first binary gate below the top unary corridor. Every nonlinear antichain lies below that gate. If it meets both children, fix all but one free input in each child. The resulting scalar bilinear form is (8) composed with two linear contractions. Its operator norm is at most \(1/N\). An \(N\)-by-\(N\) coefficient matrix with that operator norm has squared Hilbert--Schmidt norm at most \(1/N\). Summing over the \(N^{a-2}\) fixed input choices proves (10). If the antichain lies in one child only, the other child supplies its true forward constant, of norm at most one. Formula (8) then gives a row of norm at most \(1/N\) on the active child. Fix \(a-1\) inputs. The remaining row still has norm at most \(1/N\). Summing its squared norm over \(N^{a-1}\) choices again gives (10). This uses the actual signed constants before any norm; it is not a positive replacement of the source. If there is no binary gate, \(f\) is affine and \(p=0\). ## 4. Dimension-independent fixed Gaussian moments Let \(Z=(Z_v)_v\) be standard complex Gaussian in \(\mathbb C^D\), with density \(\pi^{-D}e^{-\|Z\|^2}\), in the physical coordinates. Different antichain terms in (9) are orthogonal in \(L^2\): a packet variable present in only one term is centered and independent. For a single antichain, \[ \mathbb E|C_A(Z_A)|^2=\|C_A\|_{\rm HS}^2 . \tag{11} \] Thus, for \(k\ne0\) and \(u>0\), put \[ q_u=dZ/\sqrt u,\qquad b_u=p(kZ/\sqrt u)/k . \tag{12} \] Equations (4), (9)--(11), and the fixed number of antichains give \[ \|q_u\|_{L^4}\le C N^{-1/2}u^{-1/2},\qquad \|b_u\|_{L^2}\le C_{\mathscr T}N^{-1}(u^{-1}+u^{-L/2}). \tag{13} \] Indeed the squared contribution of an antichain of size \(a\ge2\) to the latter norm is at most \(|k|^{2a-2}u^{-a}N^{a-3}\le N^{-2}u^{-a}\). The same bound for \(b_u\) holds in \(L^4\), with a new tree-dependent constant. Here is an elementary Wick justification, without a dimension-dependent moment estimate. Write a homogeneous holomorphic Gaussian polynomial of degree \(a\) using its symmetric coefficient tensor \(T\). Pairing each Gaussian coordinate with its conjugate gives \[ \mathbb E|F(Z)|^2=a!\|T\|^2,\qquad \mathbb E|F(Z)|^{2p} =(pa)!\|\operatorname{Sym}(T^{\otimes p})\|^2 \le\frac{(pa)!}{(a!)^p}(\mathbb E|F(Z)|^2)^p . \tag{14} \] Symmetrization is an orthogonal projection and has norm one. These identities also follow by expanding Gaussian monomials, whose moments are \(\mathbb E|Z_i|^{2n}=n!\). Take \(p=2\), and use the triangle inequality over the finitely many antichains and degrees, all at most \(L\). Together with (13) this proves, in particular, \[ \mathbb E|b_u|^4\le C_{\mathscr T}N^{-4}u^{-4} \qquad(u\ge1). \tag{15} \] The linear fourth moment in (13) is the ordinary scalar Gaussian moment with variance \(\|d\|^2/u\). ## 5. Exact Laplace identity and the three integration ranges The Jacobian in (2) and Tonelli give the exact identity \[ \mathcal P_N=\int_0^\infty \mathbb E\exp\{-t|f(Z/\sqrt t)|^2\}\,dt . \tag{16} \] The scalar formula \(\int_0^\infty t^D e^{-tE}dt=D!E^{-D-1}\) fixes its normalization. All integrands are nonnegative. Substitute \(u=t|k|^2\); rotational invariance of \(Z\) permits replacing \(|k|Z\) by \(kZ\). Therefore \[ |k|^2\mathcal P_N =\int_0^\infty \mathbb E e^{-u|1+q_u+b_u|^2}\,du . \tag{17} \] The affine version with \(b_u=0\) integrates to exactly one by [U, (15)], including its affine slope. On \(0<u<\alpha\le1\), the difference of the two integrands has integral at most \(\alpha\), since each lies in \([0,1]\). On \(\alpha\le u\le1\), the global Lipschitz norm of \(z\mapsto e^{-u|z|^2}\) is at most \(C\sqrt u\). The \(L^2\) bound (13) consequently gives \[ \int_\alpha^1 \mathbb E\left|e^{-u|1+q_u+b_u|^2} -e^{-u|1+q_u|^2}\right|du \le\frac{C_{\mathscr T}}N \int_\alpha^1u^{-(L-1)/2}\,du . \tag{18} \] For \(u\ge1\), split off the event \(\{|q_u|>1/4\}\cup\{|b_u|>1/4\}\). On its complement every segment \(1+q_u+\theta b_u\), \(0\le\theta\le1\), has modulus at least \(1/2\). Its exponential derivative is at most \(C\sqrt u\,e^{-u/8}\). The good-event difference is thus bounded by \(C_{\mathscr T}N^{-1}u^{-1/2}e^{-u/8}\). On the bad event use the bound one and the fourth moments: \[ \mathbb P(|q_u|>1/4)+\mathbb P(|b_u|>1/4) \le C_{\mathscr T}(N^{-2}u^{-2}+N^{-4}u^{-4}). \tag{19} \] Both terms are integrable. Hence the entire \(u\ge1\) difference is \(O_{\mathscr T}(N^{-1})\). No small-source tail cutoff or field-size hypothesis was used. Combining the three ranges proves \[ \bigl||k|^2\mathcal P_N-1\bigr| \le \alpha+\frac{C_{\mathscr T}}N \int_\alpha^1u^{-(L-1)/2}\,du +C_{\mathscr T}N^{-1}. \tag{20} \] For \(L=2,3\), take \(\alpha=N^{-1}\). For \(L\ge4\), take \(\alpha=N^{-2/(L-1)}\). Elementary integration gives exactly (5)--(6). For \(L=1\), the affine identity is exact. At \(k=0\) the already proved local radial divergence of [U] gives \(\mathcal P_N=+\infty\); no division by zero is made above. ## 6. Scope and complete inputs The theorem uses fixed leaf degree through the antichain expansion and fixed Wick moments. The closing estimate (8) is essential: a generic scalar polynomial with small separate operator bounds does not supply the physical coefficient saving (10). Neither smallness of a real minimizer nor a Hessian determinant enters the argument. This improves the universal constant-error undamped comparison of [U] to a relative error tending to zero for the unchanged quartic and budget. It does not evaluate \(\mathcal P_N\), remove the signed source from its denominator, construct a geometric trial field, or prove eventual nonvanishing. The arbitrary-short- filling volume theorem and finite-exception assertion remain open. No novelty is claimed for Gaussian moments or Laplace integration. All four complete matching texts were read. Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used. No earlier final was edited. | Label | Complete text | SHA-256 | | --- | --- | --- | | P, source, 477 lines | [Original uniform physical compiler](research_conway_uniform_physical_quartic.md) | 39895b430535f565d30133b46ef57f67589207bc83f40597ffe96e2ce79bbda8 | | H, source, 331 lines | [Actual pair and original closing](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_pair_casimir_commutant_and_rotated_trace.md) | 00ab946b3eddb61256bdbd8ec487789a15991a80e1a28b4eee53bbb4a00f7666 | | U, source, 311 lines | [Undamped reciprocal source](research_conway_undamped_reciprocal_source.md) | 4ce9ae44a5ed6f7f54145d96712a7937f2e8c4181e2292aa5f2c44e84ffb3a8a | | O, coverage, 407 lines | [Antichain expansion and orthogonal errors](research_orthogonal_error_positive_conway_recursion.md) | 5506f489642f2ec118c4fef25cccc0485fecdc32ffccf09c700ac923c9da98dd |

title: An exact Gamma section and affine extension of the original crossing source
text: # An exact Gamma section and affine extension of the original crossing source 22 November 2026. Written research proof. Earlier author-final notes and public manuscripts remain unchanged. The original crossing source has an exact canonical Gamma solution of its homogeneous boundary equation. The physical polynomial period is a different, explicitly sourced solution: its first-order defect is a known polynomial in the cyclic boundary characters. Keeping that defect gives a flat affine extension and its full cyclic monodromy. It does not identify the physical period with the Gamma section. The constructions below concern solution and source channels over a boundary-parameter difference field. They do not replace an original Conway leg by a two-dimensional vector space. ## 1. The original scalar and canonical factorial Fix \[ N\ge2,\qquad d=N-1,\qquad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2, \quad \eta=(-1)^d,\quad \kappa=e^{\pi i d^2/(2N)}. \tag{1} \] Every fractional power of \(q\) means the displayed exponential. Use the complete Frobenius algebra and centered basis of [B], with \(U_x=\sum_{j=0}^d x^j f_j\), \(R^+=\sqrt N f_0\), and the original closing \(\phi\). In particular, all first spectral normals at repeated Casimir roots are retained. Set \[ \Phi(C,H,K)=\phi(f_0U_{-C}U_{-H}U_{-K}) =N^{-1/2}\phi(R^+U_{-C}U_{-H}U_{-K}),\qquad r=HK. \tag{2} \] The level \(N\) is fixed in algebraic identities unless stated otherwise. The function \(\Phi\) is the original polynomial, of degree at most \(d\) separately in \(C,H,K\), and is symmetric in these three variables. No scalar closing is replaced by a norm. Let \(\mathfrak F=\mathfrak F_N\) be the canonical factorial of [F]. Its identities needed here are \[ \begin{gathered} \mathfrak F(j)=(Q;Q)_j\quad(0\le j<N),\qquad \mathfrak F(w+1)=(1-Q^{w+1})\mathfrak F(w),\\ \mathfrak F(w)\mathfrak F(d-w)=Nq^{w(w-d)},\qquad \mathfrak F(w+N)=(1-e^{2\pi iw})\mathfrak F(w). \end{gathered} \tag{3} \] The whole meromorphic identities, with their canonical logarithmic marks, are used; singular factors are canceled before specialization. Write \[ C=e^{-2\pi ic},\qquad H=e^{-2\pi ih},\qquad K=e^{-2\pi ik} \tag{4} \] on the angle cover, and define \[ \boxed{\quad G_N(c,h,k)=\frac{\kappa^2}{N^2} \frac{\displaystyle\prod_{a\in\{c,h,k\}} \mathfrak F(N(1-a)-\tfrac12)^2} {\displaystyle\prod_{\{a,b\}\subset\{c,h,k\}} \mathfrak F(N(1-a-b))}.\quad} \tag{5} \] The products count labelled singles and pairs, even when numerical angles coincide. This is an explicit symmetric meromorphic section on the marked cover, not a prescribed periodic function of \(C,H,K\). ## 2. Its exact shift and homogeneous boundary equation Let \[ \sigma(C,H,K)=(C,H/Q,QK),\qquad (\sigma h,\sigma k)=(h+N^{-1},k-N^{-1}). \tag{6} \] Single steps in (3), with every phase retained, give \[ \boxed{\qquad \sigma G_N=g\,G_N,\qquad g=\frac{(1-qK)^2(1-CH)}{(1-H/q)^2(1-QCK)}. \qquad} \tag{7} \] For example, increasing \(h\) lowers its single factorial argument by one, producing \((1-H/q)^{-2}\). Decreasing \(k\) produces \((1-qK)^2\); the two changed pair denominators supply the other two factors in (7). The original polynomial equation [B], at its first coherent parameter zero, is \[ D\,\sigma\Phi-(B+D+Q-1)\Phi+B\,\sigma^{-1}\Phi=0, \tag{8} \] where \[ B=\frac{(q-K)^2(1-QCH)}{(H-K)(QH-K)},\qquad D=\frac{(q-H)^2(1-QCK)}{(H-QK)(H-K)}. \tag{9} \] Here \(\sigma\) is the forward shift; it is the inverse of the shift called \(\sigma\) in [B]. Initially (8)--(9) are read off their denominator locus, and then as the cleared polynomial identity. We verify directly that \(G_N\) solves (8). Put \[ F_q(X,Y)=2q-X-QY+QC(XY-1). \tag{10} \] The elementary polynomial factorization \[ Q(1-qY)^2(1-CX)-(q-X)^2(1-QCY) =(X-QY)F_q(X,Y) \tag{11} \] follows by separating its constant and linear terms in \(C\). The former are \((X-QY)(2q-X-QY)\); the latter are \(QC(X-QY)(XY-1)\). Direct cancellation using (7) now gives \[ \begin{split} Dg-D&=\frac{F_q(H,K)}{H-K},\\ B/(\sigma^{-1}g)-B&=-\frac{F_q(K,H)}{H-K}. \end{split} \tag{12} \] Since \(F_q(H,K)-F_q(K,H)=(Q-1)(H-K)\), their sum is \(Q-1\). This proves \[ Dg+B/(\sigma^{-1}g)=B+D+Q-1, \tag{13} \] and hence the exact homogeneous equation for the Gamma section. This proof does not infer an exact equation from a classical symbol or from an asymptotic expansion. ## 3. The initialized Gamma value and its analytic branch At \(h=1/(2N)\), put \(R=h+k\), \(p=NR\), \(L=N-p\), and \[ B_* =N(1-c)-\tfrac12,\qquad D_* =N(1-c-R)+\tfrac12. \] The single factorial for \(h\) is \(\mathfrak F(d)=N\), and the three pair arguments are \(B_*,D_*,L\). Thus (5) gives exactly \[ G_N(c,\tfrac1{2N},R-\tfrac1{2N}) =\frac{\kappa^2\mathfrak F(B_*)\mathfrak F(L)} {\mathfrak F(D_*)}. \tag{14} \] This is the initialized Gamma term \(\mathcal G_1^0\) of [P]. The actual source there is \(\Phi_1^0=\mathcal G_1^0+I_1^0\), with its retained vertical current \(I_1^0\), not simply \(G_N\). The same source also has the exact readout \[ \Phi_1^0=\kappa\sqrt N\,\mathcal C_N(0,-C,-qr), \qquad r=e^{-2\pi iR}. \tag{15} \] Consequently (14) retains the original \(\kappa^2\) normalization and the actual source anchor, while leaving its correction visible. For completeness, the canonical factorial also specifies the Gamma section on complex shape charts. Suppose the angles lie in a fixed complex compact set with \[ 0<\Re a<1,\qquad 0<\Re(a+b)<1 \quad(a,b\in\{c,h,k\},\ a\ne b\text{ as labels}). \tag{16} \] Keep positive margins in these inequalities. All nine arguments in (5) lie in the full nonzero strips of [F]. Its uniform formula is \[ \mathfrak F(Nw+\tau)=\sqrt N\,\mathfrak h(w) (1-e^{2\pi iw})^\tau e^{N\mathfrak f(w)}(1+O(N^{-1})), \tag{17} \] where \(\mathfrak h(w)^2=i(1-e^{2\pi iw})\) and \(\mathfrak f(w)=-i\pi/12+i\operatorname{Li}_2(e^{2\pi iw})/(2\pi)\), on the canonical strip branches. Applying this to (5) proves an asymptotic for the Gamma section itself: \[ \begin{gathered} G_N=\kappa^2N^{-1/2}\mathcal B(c,h,k) e^{N\mathcal S(c,h,k)}(1+O(N^{-1})),\\ \mathcal S=\frac{\sum_{\{a,b\}}\operatorname{Li}_2(e^{-2\pi i(a+b)}) -2\sum_a\operatorname{Li}_2(e^{-2\pi ia}) +3\operatorname{Li}_2(1)}{2\pi i},\\ \mathcal B=\frac{-i}{\displaystyle\prod_{\{a,b\}} \mathfrak h(1-a-b)}. \end{gathered} \tag{18} \] Indeed each squared single factorial, including its shift \(-1/2\), contributes the amplitude \(i\); the denominator contributes its three \(\mathfrak h\)'s. The net power of \(N\), including \(N^{-2}\), is \(N^{-1/2}\). The constant in the exponent is \(+3\operatorname{Li}_2(1)\) in the numerator of (18). On real positive angles with \(c+h+k<1\), the amplitude is \[ \mathcal B= \frac{e^{\pi i(c+h+k)}} {2\sqrt{2\sin\pi(c+h)\sin\pi(c+k)\sin\pi(h+k)}}. \tag{19} \] This follows from \(\mathfrak h(1-u)=i e^{-\pi iu/2}\sqrt{2\sin\pi u}\). Formula (18) is a holomorphic statement for the specified Gamma section. It is not, by itself, a holomorphic asymptotic for the physical scalar \(\Phi\). ## 4. Exact affine forcing of the physical polynomial The homogeneous solution gives an elementary factorization, but the inhomogeneous term is fixed by the original source. Define \[ F(C,H,K)=\frac{H-QK}{(1-H/q)^2(1-QCK)}. \tag{20} \] We will prove the following cleared identity of the original polynomial family: \[ \boxed{\quad (1-H/q)^2(1-QCK)\,\sigma\Phi -(1-qK)^2(1-CH)\Phi =\frac\eta N(H-QK) [2+H^N+K^N+C^N(1-r^N)].\quad} \tag{21} \] In particular, on its regular locus, \[ \sigma\Phi=g\Phi+JF,\qquad J=\frac\eta N[2+H^N+K^N+C^N(1-r^N)]. \tag{22} \] The scalar \(J\) is invariant under \(\sigma\). It is explicit source data, not a freely chosen forcing or an unknown closed period. Here is the complete determination of \(J\). Put \(R_\Phi=\sigma\Phi-g\Phi\). Subtract the homogeneous identity (13) from (8), without dividing by \(\Phi\). This gives \[ DR_\Phi=\frac{B}{\sigma^{-1}g}\,\sigma^{-1}R_\Phi. \tag{23} \] Direct substitution of (7), (9), and (20) shows \[ \frac{B}{D\,\sigma^{-1}g} =\frac{(1-qH)^2}{(1-H/q)^2} \frac{1-CK}{1-QCK}\frac{H-QK}{QH-K} =\frac{F}{\sigma^{-1}F}. \tag{24} \] Hence \(R_\Phi/F\) is invariant under \(\sigma\). At fixed \(r\), \(\Phi\) is a symmetric Laurent polynomial in \(H,K=r/H\) of degree at most \(d\) in either direction. The cleared numerator of \(R_\Phi/F\) vanishes whenever \(H=QK\): the shift then exchanges \(H,K\), and its two coefficients coincide. Therefore division by \(H-Qr/H\) gives a Laurent polynomial. Before that division its exponent range is contained in \([-N-1,N+1]\); afterwards it is contained in \([-N,N]\). Since \(Q\) is primitive, an invariant Laurent polynomial in this range has the form \[ R_\Phi/F=A_+H^N+A_0+A_-H^{-N}. \tag{25} \] The extreme coefficient [B, equation (20)] says that the coefficient of \(H^d\) in \(\Phi(C,H,r/H)\) is \(\eta/N\); by symmetry the coefficient of \(H^{-d}\) is \(\eta r^d/N\). In the numerator of \(R_\Phi/F\), the highest term is the \(H^2/q^2\) term multiplying \(\sigma\Phi\); its coefficient is \((\eta/N)Q^{-d-1}=\eta/N\). The lowest term is the negative \(q^2K^2\Phi\) term. Dividing at the two extremes proves \[ A_+=\eta/N,\qquad A_-=\eta r^N/N. \tag{26} \] The constant coefficient follows from a different original source readout, rather than a normalization of \(G_N\). Set \(H=q\), so \(K=r/q\). The socle identity [B, equation (25)] gives \[ \Phi(C,q,r/q)=\frac{\kappa^2}{N}F_N(-C)G_N(r). \tag{27} \] Here \(F_N(-C)=(1+C^N)/(1-qC)\), with its polynomial meaning. The first coefficient on the left of (21) vanishes at \(H=q\). Using \(\kappa^2/q=-\eta\) and \((1-r)G_N(r)=1-r^N\) consequently gives \[ (R_\Phi/F)|_{H=q} =\frac\eta N(1-r^N)(1+C^N). \tag{28} \] Since \(H^N=-1\) and \(K^N=-r^N\) there, equations (25)--(28) give \(A_0=(\eta/N)[2+C^N(1-r^N)]\). This proves (21)--(22). All divisions in this proof were on a generic locus. Equation (21) is polynomial in \(C,H,K\), so it continues through its folds and coefficient-zero loci. At a resonance one keeps that cleared identity and its family derivatives, not a division by \(J\), \(H-QK\), or a cyclic norm difference. Internal Hermite normals were already included in the exact source (2); external parameter derivatives are obtained by differentiating the whole polynomial identity. ## 5. The full cyclic norm and affine monodromy The rational multiplier has the exact product \[ M:=\prod_{j=0}^{N-1}\sigma^j g =\frac{(1+K^N)^2}{(1+H^N)^2} \frac{1-(CH)^N}{1-(CK)^N}. \tag{29} \] For example \(\prod_{j=0}^{N-1}(1-qQ^jK)=1+K^N\); the other three products give the remaining factors. Thus \(M\) need not equal one. On the canonical angle cover the Gamma section obeys \(\sigma^NG_N=MG_N\). Resetting its marks after \(N\) steps is not the same operation. Write \(x=H^N,y=K^N,w=C^N\). A direct factorization gives \[ M-1=\frac{(y-x)[2+x+y+w(1-xy)]} {(1+x)^2(1-wy)} =\frac{N}{\eta}\frac{(y-x)J}{(1+x)^2(1-wy)}. \tag{30} \] This is an identity, not a license to cancel \(J\) at its zeros. The natural affine system is \[ \sigma\begin{pmatrix}\Phi\\1\end{pmatrix} =\mathcal B_\sigma \begin{pmatrix}\Phi\\1\end{pmatrix},\qquad \mathcal B_\sigma=\begin{pmatrix}g&JF\\0&1\end{pmatrix}. \tag{31} \] Its Gamma subline has section \((G_N,0)^t\). Since the physical polynomial satisfies \(\sigma^N\Phi=\Phi\), the full product is \[ \mathcal B_\sigma^{(N)} =\begin{pmatrix}M&(1-M)\Phi\\0&1\end{pmatrix}. \tag{32} \] The off-diagonal entry can equivalently be computed as the explicit finite sum \[ \sum_{j=0}^{N-1} \left(\prod_{\ell=j+1}^{N-1}\sigma^\ell g\right) \sigma^j(JF). \tag{33} \] Iteration of (22) proves both descriptions. In particular the off-diagonal current, not only the determinant \(M\), is retained. When \(M=1\), the original family (21), (32)--(33) is still the data; a formula obtained by dividing by \(1-M\) is not a substitute. There is nevertheless a useful generic selection statement. Two rational solutions of the forced equation (22), at fixed \(C,r\), differ by \(u\) satisfying \(\sigma u=gu\). Rational functions of \(H\) have \(\sigma^Nu=u\), whereas this homogeneous equation gives \(\sigma^Nu=Mu\). Thus \(u=0\) wherever \(M\ne1\). The physical polynomial is the unique rational solution on that generic locus. At a norm resonance it is the continuation of this entire original family; this uniqueness argument supplies no asymptotic lower bound. Permuting the three boundary variables gives the same construction for every balanced shift \((A,B)\mapsto(A/Q,QB)\), with the third variable fixed. Two independent such shifts commute and preserve \(CHK\). Their affine matrices are flat. Indeed symmetry of (5) gives the homogeneous top-left cocycle. Applying the two orders to the actual polynomial section \((\Phi,1)^t\) then cancels that top-left term and forces the off-diagonal cocycle identity, with no division by \(\Phi\). Equivalently, on a nonzero Gamma chart, \(\left(\begin{smallmatrix}G_N&\Phi\\0&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)\) is a common fundamental frame. This is a lattice action with its displayed cyclic norms; it has not been descended to a finite cyclic action with identity monodromy. ## 6. Direct summation on real fractional orbits The first-order equation has an elementary analytic consequence that does not require second-order tracking. Fix a compact set of pairs \(c,R>0\), \(c+R<1\), put \(k=R-h\), and let \(0\le h\le R\).
