Write \[ \begin{split} L(x)&=\int_0^x\log|2\sin\pi t|\,dt,\\ \mathcal A_0(c,h,k)&=L(c+h)+L(c+k)+L(h+k) -2[L(c)+L(h)+L(k)],\\ M_0(c,R)&=L(c+R)-L(c)-L(R)>0. \end{split} \tag{33a} \] Use the odd one-periodic continuation of \(L\) when needed. Uniformly on this entire real interval, including its two endpoints, \[ \log|G_N(c,h,R-h)|=N\mathcal A_0(c,h,R-h)+O(\log N), \qquad \mathcal A_0(c,h,R-h)\ge M_0(c,R). \tag{33b} \] Here is a factorial proof of the endpoint uniformity, so (18) is not being used beyond its strict compact shape scope. For real \(-1/2\le x\le(1-\delta)N\), write \(x=n+\theta\), where \(n\ge0\) is an integer and \(-1/2\le\theta\le1/2\). The endpoint formula [F, equation (12)] and exact shifts (3) give \[ \mathfrak F(x)=\mathfrak F(\theta) \prod_{j=1}^n(1-Q^{j+\theta}),\qquad \mathfrak F(\theta)=(-2\pi i/N)^\theta\Gamma(1+\theta) (1+O(N^{-1})). \] For \(n\ge1\), the product factors have strictly positive sine moduli. Separate \(\log(2\sin\pi u)=\log(2\pi u)+ \log(\sin\pi u/(\pi u))\). The second term has a bounded derivative on \([0,1-\delta]\). Integral comparison for the shifted logarithms in the first term, or the ordinary Gamma formula for their product, has an error \(O(\log N)\), uniformly in \(n,\theta\). For \(n=0\), both the endpoint formula and the corresponding short integral have this bound directly, including \(x<0\). Consequently \[ \log|\mathfrak F(x)|=N L(x/N)+O(\log N) \qquad(-1/2\le x\le(1-\delta)N). \] For a real single argument in (5), reflect instead: \[ \log|\mathfrak F(N(1-a)-1/2)| =\log N-\log|\mathfrak F(Na-1/2)| =-NL(a)+O(\log N). \] The reflection phase has modulus one. The last comparison is uniform at \(a=0\), because shifting an endpoint by \(1/(2N)\) changes its log-sine integral by at most \(O((\log N)/N)\). All pair arguments are in strict strips since \(c+h,c+k,R\) stay uniformly between zero and one. Substitution in (5) proves the first part of (33b). These factorials are nonzero on the stated real interval for all sufficiently large \(N\). For the second part, write \(T(a,b)=L(a+b)-L(a)-L(b)\). On \(a,b>0,a+b<1\), its Hessian divided by \(\pi\) is \[ \begin{pmatrix} \cot\pi(a+b)-\cot\pi a&\cot\pi(a+b)\\ \cot\pi(a+b)&\cot\pi(a+b)-\cot\pi b \end{pmatrix}. \] Its diagonal entries are negative and its determinant is one, by the cotangent addition formula. It is therefore negative definite. Since \(\mathcal A_0=T(c,h)+T(c,k)+T(h,k)\), it is concave as a function of \(h\) at fixed \(c,R\), and continuous at the endpoints. Its endpoint values are both \(M_0\), which proves the lower bound. The strict sign of \(M_0\) follows by fixing \(c\): its derivative in \(R\) is \(\log[\sin\pi(c+R)/\sin\pi R]\), positive before \(R=(1-c)/2\) and negative afterwards, with zero endpoint values. Define the source-relative error on this interval by \(E_N(h)=\Phi(C,H,K)/G_N(c,h,k)-1\). Dividing the exact equation (22) by \(\sigma G_N=gG_N\), rather than approximating a scalar ratio, gives \[ E_N(h+N^{-1})-E_N(h) =\frac{JF}{G_N(c,h+N^{-1},k-N^{-1})}. \tag{33c} \] This is used only when both endpoints lie in \([0,R]\). On such real parameters, \(|J|\le6/N\). Also \(|1-H/q|\ge c/N\) and \(|1-QCK|\ge c\), so \(|F|\le CN^2\). Equation (33b) now gives the uniform estimate \[ |E_N(h+N^{-1})-E_N(h)| \le N^C e^{-NM_0(c,R)}. \tag{33d} \] There is no division by a fold distance in this formula. The first-order coefficients are regular for the steps used, even when the interval crosses the central fold. At a zero of \(H-QK\) the numerator simply vanishes. Two points on the same fractional orbit inside \([0,R]\) differ by at most \(N\) such steps. Summing (33d), with its polynomial factor enlarged if necessary, proves \[ |E_N(h_2)-E_N(h_1)|\le N^C e^{-NM_0(c,R)},\qquad N(h_2-h_1)\in\mathbb Z. \tag{33e} \] This controls variation on every fractional orbit. It does not determine the orbit-dependent constant. For the anchored orbit there is also an initialized value. Retain the additional hypothesis \(L(c+R)-L(R)>0\) from [P], on a compact set. Equations (14) and [P] give \(\Phi_1^0-G_N(c,1/(2N),R-1/(2N))=I_1^0\), with \(|I_1^0|\le N^C\). Thus (33b)--(33e) prove \[ \frac{\Phi(C,H,K)}{G_N(c,h,R-h)} =1+O\!\left(N^C e^{-NM_0(c,R)}\right),\qquad h=(j+1/2)/N\in[0,R]. \tag{33f} \] This is an exponentially accurate agreement on the whole indicated anchored grid, with the original source current still accounted for. It is not an exponential estimate at arbitrary fractional offsets; an additional initializer is needed to fix those constants. ## 7. Integer packets agree exactly with the Gamma section There is a useful exact check of the initialized residue family, beyond its leading asymptotic. In the notation of [P], let \(a=m\) be an integer with \(1\le m<N\), put \(h=(m-1/2)/N\), \(k=R-h\), and let \(\mathcal G_m^0\) be its pole-free prefactor from [P, equation (22)]. The arguments of (5) are \[ \begin{array}{c|ccc} \text{singles}&B_*&N-m&L+m-1\\ \text{pairs}&B_*-m+1&D_*+m-1&L . \end{array} \] Using the exact prefactor there and reflection in (3) gives \[ \boxed{\quad \frac{G_N(c,(m-1/2)/N,R-(m-1/2)/N)}{\mathcal G_m^0} =(rQ^m)^{m-1} \frac{(q^3CQ^{-m};Q)_{m-1}}{(q^3rC;Q)_{m-1}}. \quad} \tag{34} \] For the scalar phase in this simplification, use \(\mathfrak F(m-1)\mathfrak F(N-m) =Nq^{-(m-1)(N-m)}\). The remaining \(p,L\) factors reduce to \((-1)^{m+1}r^{m-1}Q^{m(m-1)/2}\); multiplying the reflection phase gives \((rQ^m)^{m-1}\), including at even levels. The right side is the elementary terminating sum \[ \sum_{j=0}^{m-1} \frac{Q^j(Q^{1-m},rQ^m;Q)_j}{(Q,q^3rC;Q)_j}. \tag{35} \] Here is a finite proof, so no root-of-unity summation or infinite product limit is assumed. For generic \(Q\), \(n\ge0\), multiply the proposed identity \[ \sum_{j=0}^n\frac{Q^j(Q^{-n},b;Q)_j}{(Q,c;Q)_j} =\frac{b^n(c/b;Q)_n}{(c;Q)_n} \tag{36} \] by \((c;Q)_n\). The result is the polynomial identity \[ \sum_{j=0}^n(-1)^j Q^{j(j-1)/2-(n-1)j} {n\brack j}_Q(b;Q)_j(cQ^j;Q)_{n-j} =\prod_{\ell=0}^{n-1}(b-cQ^\ell). \tag{37} \] It follows by induction using \(b(b;Q)_j=Q^{-j}[(b;Q)_j-(b;Q)_{j+1}]\) and the two equivalent \(Q\)-Pascal recurrences. More explicitly, if the coefficient of \((b;Q)_j\) is \(A_{n,j}\), multiplication by \(b-cQ^n\) gives \(A_{n+1,j}=(Q^{-j}-cQ^n)A_{n,j}-Q^{1-j}A_{n,j-1}\); the coefficients displayed in (37) obey this recurrence, including its two endpoints. This proves (36). Set \(n=m-1\), \(b=rQ^m\), \(c=q^3rC\). Since every \((Q;Q)_j\) has \(j<N\), specialization at the stated primitive root is legal after canceled continuation. This proves (35). The actual finite rectangle packet of [P] stops at \(K_*=\lfloor NR+\zeta\rfloor\). It equals the full terminating sum (35) only when \(K_*\ge m-1\). This holds for each fixed finite collection of positive integers and sufficiently large \(N\); it is not asserted for every \(m<N\) at a fixed \(R\). Even when the packet equals (35), the actual source still includes its vertical current. Neither these integer identities nor formal interpolation alone gives an exponentially accurate generic-offset comparison. ## 8. What can and cannot be sewn from this extension Affine source extensions and their tensor face and corner terms are already present in the earlier factorial cut-source treatment. The new information here is the explicit original-crossing multipliers \(g,J,F\), their exact norm, and their calibration to the physical polynomial source. No novelty is claimed for upper-triangular extensions or variation of constants as general methods. Tensoring (31) keeps all source terms. For example, the shifted product of two sourced components contains the two single-source terms and the double-source term; the latter cannot be omitted before an actual contraction. Compatible changes of frame cancel on an internal edge only when the specified dual pairing and the original boundary vectors and closing row are transported as well. These are solution/source channels over the boundary difference field. They do not span the \(N\)-dimensional full Hermite Conway leg, and no intertwiner for its multiplication or genuine turn has been constructed here. Flatness at fixed \(CHK\) does not establish control in the remaining total-center direction, a bounded-rank replacement of arbitrary components, or a positive sewing cycle. The coherent parameters and balanced shifts have not been identified with a knot's marked meridian, longitude, or surgery equations. All cyclic norms, zeros, and original peripheral factors must remain until a whole-source pushforward is proved. The direct-summation corollary controls all fractional-orbit variation and gives anchored-grid exponential agreement. This note proves no exponential generic-offset initializer, no exact equality \(\Phi=G_N\), and no knot-volume or finite-exception theorem. It supplies exact local data for that separate analytic and geometric comparison. The complete direct proof sources are: | Label | Source | SHA-256 | |---|---|---| | B | [Original four-input polynomial source](research_four_coherent_boundary_polynomial_source.md) | 93241074830ff4b844ba5baafd06a15bf08ec6bddc3a1498727f110ebe297d84 | | F | [Canonical factorial and full-strip estimates](research_four_coherent_fractional_boundary_source.md) | 8126481cadaa4b1b0ba287495de14cb3263baf8343fbfca9aa4d5b6d962595b1 | | P | [Original crossing initializer and retained packet](research_four_coherent_zero_radius_boundary_source.md) | f74a6b951936f29f5cf66e4b34cfc84b2c890b1ba5464f472ca023aa70c5c621 | All three complete matching sources were read at their renewed pins. Only written mathematics and text operations were used.

title: Cyclic crossing walls are exact integer-degree sectors
text:
# Cyclic crossing walls are exact integer-degree sectors Private written proof, 19 November 2026. The two cross-wall periods of S have a concrete meaning: they are the low and high integer pair-degree blocks of the original truncated transfer. Consequently the three wall choices inside one crossing must agree. A word with \(c\) crossings has at most \(2^c\) surviving sectors, rather than the \(2^{3c}\) choices in its Euler-slot expansion. Each sector also has an exact nilpotent completion. Its ordinary Hankel period equals the complete regularized cyclic-wall period, including P's endpoint finite parts and cyclic-pole residues. With the original diagonal first cut fixed throughout, H's complex meridian-collar and genuine jet bounds hold for every completed sector. These are identities of complete periods and absolute tail estimates. They do not identify localized densities or prove a nonzero geometric coefficient. The complete directs are S (cyclic sewing), P (its regularized cut prescription), and H (actual meridian Hankel transport). The finite residue calculation and the crossing-sector reduction are proved here. ## 1. The two paths in one actual residue fibre Fix \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), and a nonzero scalar \(a\). On two physical heads with basis \(e_0,\ldots,e_d\), let \(J_+\) and \(J_-\) be the truncated unit shifts and let \(S\) be cyclic raising. Set \[ T=aJ_+\otimes J_-,\qquad A=aS\otimes S^{-1},\qquad R_A(t)=(tI-A)^{-1}. 	ag{1} \] The letter S in (1) denotes a matrix; the proof-source S is cited by its section or equation when needed. Both operators preserve the sum of the occupations modulo \(N\). In the residue \(k\), put \[ h=k+1\in\{1,\ldots,N\},\qquad b_n=e_n\otimes e_{(k-n) mod N},\quad 0\le n<N. 	ag{2} \] Then \(Ab_n=ab_{n+1 mod N}\). The physical \(T\) deletes the arrows from \(h-1\) to \(h\) and from \(N-1\) to zero. When \(h=N\), these are the same arrow. Thus its two paths are \([0,h-1]\) and \([h,N-1]\), with the latter empty at \(h=N\). Their exact integer pair totals are respectively \(k\) and \(k+N\). Write \(\Pi_{h,0}\) and \(\Pi_{h,1}\) for their diagonal projectors. Put \(z=a/t\), interpret \(b_h=b_0\) if \(h=N\), and define S's two cross-wall matrices in their actual order: \[  egin{split} C_{h,1}(t)&=R_A(t)b_0z^{N-h}b_h^t A R_A(t),\ C_{h,0}(t)&=R_A(t)b_hz^h b_0^t A R_A(t). \end{split} 	ag{3} \] The transpose here is the coordinate row, not a Hermitian dual. S(2)--(4) says that the other three terms of the resolvent sewing formula are holomorphic at zero. We will identify the two surviving terms separately. **Finite residue identity.** For every germ \(f(t)=\sum_{
u\ge0}f_
u t^
u\) holomorphic at zero, and a sufficiently small positive circle \(\gamma\) with radius less than \(|a|\), \[  oxed{\quad  rac1{2\pi i}\int_\gamma f(t)C_{h,b}(t)\,dt =f(T)\Pi_{h,b},\qquad b=0,1, \quad} 	ag{4} \] where \(f(T)=\sum_{
u=0}^{d}f_
u T^
u\). To prove it, use the convergent series at zero \[ R_A(t)=-\sum_{p\ge0}t^p A^{-p-1},\qquad A R_A(t)=-\sum_{q\ge0}t^q A^{-q}. 	ag{5} \] For the high wall in (3), a residue can occur only when \[ p+q+
u=N-h-1. 	ag{6} \] If \(h=N\), this is impossible and the high wall has zero period. Otherwise (6) bounds \(p,q\le N-h-1\), so no cyclic ambiguity remains in \[ A^{-p-1}b_0=a^{-p-1}b_{N-1-p},\qquad b_h^tA^{-q}=a^{-q}b_{h+q}^t. 	ag{7} \] Its output \(u=N-1-p\) and input \(v=h+q\) satisfy \(h\le v\le u<N\), \(u-v=
u\), and the scalar is \(a^{N-h-p-q-1}f_
u=a^{u-v}f_{u-v}\). Conversely every such pair \((u,v)\) occurs exactly once, with \(p=N-1-u\), \(q=v-h\). This is precisely \(f(T)\Pi_{h,1}\). For the low wall, the residue condition is \(p+q+
u=h-1\). Now the output and input are \(u=h-1-p\) and \(v=q\), with \(0\le v\le u<h\), and the same scalar is \(a^{u-v}f_{u-v}\). Every such pair occurs once. This calculation remains valid at \(h=N\): the cyclic symbol \(b_h=b_0\) in (3) gives the displayed representatives without an extra wrap term. It proves (4) also at the coincident wall. All sums contributing to a residue are finite. Summing over the residue fibres gives the physical projectors \[ \Pi_0=\mathbf1_{J_1+J_2\le d},\qquad \Pi_1=\mathbf1_{J_1+J_2\ge N},\qquad \Pi_0+\Pi_1=I. 	ag{8} \] Here \(J_ie_j=je_j\); the inequalities use integer degree, not degree modulo \(N\). Reversing the transfer exchanges the two heads and leaves both projectors unchanged. No parity or primality assumption entered the proof. ## 2. Nilpotent completion retains the cyclic-pole currents Let \(\operatorname{pp}_0\) denote the negative Laurent part at zero. Testing (4) on every monomial \(f(t)=t^
u\) proves entrywise \[ \operatorname{pp}_0 C_{h,b}(t) =\sum_{
u=0}^{d}t^{-
u-1}T^
u\Pi_{h,b} =(tI-T)^{-1}\Pi_{h,b}. 	ag{9} \] Thus the difference \[ D_{h,b}(t)=C_{h,b}(t)-(tI-T)^{-1}\Pi_{h,b} 	ag{10} \] is holomorphic at zero. This is an exact change of completion for the same small-circle functional. The second term has no nonzero finite pole; the first generally has the cyclic poles \(t^N=a^N\). They are not equal rational matrices. For the actual root transfers in H, \(|a|=1\), and the scalar germ is one of the marked inverse cyclic dilogarithms \[ \mathscr A_\epsilon(t)= \prod_{j=1}^{N-1}(1-Q^{\epsilon j}t)^{-j/N}, \qquad Q=e^{2\pi i/N},\quad \mathscr A_\epsilon(0)=1. 	ag{11} \] P's regularized Hankel formula applies to \(C_{h,b}\) and to \(D_{h,b}\). Both have at most double nonzero poles and are \(O(t^{-1})\) at infinity. Its prescribed functional is the sum of the marked bank finite parts **minus** the residues at unramified cyclic poles. At a branch endpoint of exponent \(-u\), it subtracts the two Laurent terms \(b_{-2}x^{-2},b_{-1}x^{-1}\) and retains the finite constants \(-b_{-2}/(u+1)-b_{-1}/u\). Apply that formula to (10). Its original small-circle period is zero, because \(D_{h,b}\) is holomorphic there. The result is exactly \[  oxed{\quad \mathcal H^{m reg}_{\epsilon}[C_{h,b}] =\mathcal H^{m ord}_{\epsilon} [(tI-T)^{-1}\Pi_{h,b}]. \quad} 	ag{12} \] On the right, the ordinary Hankel integral converges at every branch endpoint and infinity, as in H. Thus (12) incorporates the cyclic-pole currents into the nilpotent completion. It does not omit them from the left side. It holds at odd, even, and composite levels, including the collisions of cyclic poles with branch endpoints. P's marked sheet and cut-arc convention is retained at infinity. The independent slot variables permit repeated use of (12) inside any fixed ordered tensor contraction. Equivalently, start from its compact product of small circles, apply (9) one variable at a time, then use the proved cut prescriptions. This argument does not assume absolute convergence of a raw, unregularized cyclic-wall integral. Nor does (12) identify restrictions to a chosen radial subregion or geometric window: the completion change can redistribute its currents. ## 3. Three slot choices reduce to one choice per crossing Use H's root factorization of a physical crossing, with \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(x_0=-q^{-1}\), and \(F_a=(Q;Q)_a\): \[  egin{split} C&=F_2u_N(T_-)F_1F_2^{-1},& C^{-1}&=F_2F_1^{-1}v_N(T_-)F_2^{-1},\ \widehat R_0^+&=CDu_N(T_+)C^{-1},& \widehat R_0^-&=Cv_N(T_+)D^{-1}C^{-1}. \end{split} 	ag{13} \] The matrices \(F_i\) and \(D\) are diagonal; \(T_\pm\) are the opposite truncated transfers. The hat removes only the common crossing scalar. As defined in H, \(u_N(t)=\sum_{a<N}t^a/F_a\) and \(v_N(t)=\sum_{a<N}(-1)^aQ^{a(a-1)/2}t^a/F_a\). Each signed crossing has three transfer slots and six factorial slots. Every one of its factors preserves the same integer pair degree, so every factor commutes with both projectors (8). In S's five-term sewing expansion, any term having even one pure cyclic or diagonal sewing slot has zero complete period: integrate that variable first, whose integrand is holomorphic inside its small circle. All other slots and the chosen coupon are independent of it. Thus a surviving word must choose a cross wall at every transfer slot. In the all-inverse realization, a \(u_N(T)\) slot uses \(\mathscr A_-(t)(tI-Q^{-1}T)^{-1}\); the scalar rotation changes neither its two paths nor its projectors. By (4), choosing wall \(b\) at any slot replaces that slot's integrated operator by \(u_N(T)\Pi_b\) or \(v_N(T)\Pi_b\), respectively. For a three-slot choice \((b_1,b_2,b_3)\), its block period is therefore \[ \widehat R_0^{\pm}\Pi_{b_1}\Pi_{b_2}\Pi_{b_3}. 	ag{14} \] It vanishes unless all three choices agree, in which case it is \(\widehat R_0^{\pm}\Pi_b\). Factorial integrations may be performed before or after this calculation, since they are independent and their matrix kernels are diagonal. In the nilpotent completion the projectors commute already with those kernels and the transfer resolvents, so mismatched choices vanish pointwise in that completed network. This last statement is not asserted for the raw cyclic walls. For the true meridian family, put \(M=e^\mu\) and \(x=-M/q\). H(3) expresses each \(R_i^{\pm}(M)\) as its root crossing between the literal moving diagonal frames and \(M^{\mp(J_i+J_{i+1})}\), with \(\kappa(M)^{\pm1}\) retained. All these matrices commute with \(\Pi_{i,b}\), the projector (8) on that adjacent pair. Consequently the surviving block period is exactly \[ R_i^{\pm}(M)\Pi_{i,b}. 	ag{15} \] This uses fixed root transfer variables and fixed root cyclic poles; no off-root strict Euler factorization is differentiated. Let a word act in the order \(W_ eta=R_{i_c}^{\sigma_c}\cdots R_{i_1}^{\sigma_1}\), \(\sigma_\ell\in\{+1,-1\}\). Define its degree-sector operator \[ W_{ eta,\mathbf b}(M)= (R_{i_c}^{\sigma_c}(M)\Pi_{i_c,b_c})\cdots (R_{i_1}^{\sigma_1}(M)\Pi_{i_1,b_1}), \qquad \mathbf b\in\{0,1\}^c. 	ag{16} \] Then the complete all-wall period is exactly \[ W_ eta(M)=\sum_{\mathbf b}W_{ eta,\mathbf b}(M). 	ag{17} \] More than an insertion of \(I=\Pi_0+\Pi_1\), (14)--(16) identify which original cyclic-wall periods give these terms and prove that every other three-slot pattern has zero complete period. Each surviving term has the nilpotent completion (12). There is no claim that projectors for one pair commute through a crossing on an overlapping pair. The order in (16) stays fixed. In literal occupation paths, \(b_\ell\) is the indicator that the input sum at crossing \(\ell\) is at least \(N\); its output sum is identical. Thus the sectors partition the original capped flow. ## 4. The original pointed source and sectorwise meridian tails Fix the original coupon before splitting any crossing. For \(m\) heads and writhe \(w=\sum\sigma_\ell\), set \[ \mathcal P_{\mathbf b,N}(M)=\Xi_N(M) \operatorname{Tr}[(P_0\otimes K_{m r}(M)^{1-N}) W_{ eta,\mathbf b}(M)], \qquad P_0=|0angle\langle0|. 	ag{18} \] The external line \(\Xi_N\) is unchanged in every term. Equations (12),(17) give \(\mathcal P_N=\sum_{\mathbf b}\mathcal P_{\mathbf b,N}\) as actual meridian germs, including all their true fixed-\(q\) jets. These sectors need not be total \(E,F\) intertwiners: pair raising or lowering crosses the threshold in (8). Scalar-cut identities therefore cannot replace (18) by a different coupon sectorwise. More explicitly, let \(E_{m pair}\) and \(F_{m pair}\) be the actual total lowering and raising operators on that pair. They lower and raise \(J=J_i+J_{i+1}\) by one, respectively, including their physical endpoint zeros. Directly on each integer-degree subspace, \[ [E_{m pair},\Pi_0]=-E_{m pair}\mathbf1_{J=N},\qquad [F_{m pair},\Pi_0]=F_{m pair}\mathbf1_{J=d}. 	ag{18a} \] For instance, only an input of degree \(N\) is lowered from outside the low sector into it. The corresponding high-sector commutators have the opposite signs. Thus for a scalar mark \(\zeta\), \[  egin{split} [E_{m pair},\Pi_0+\zeta\Pi_1] &=(\zeta-1)E_{m pair}\mathbf1_{J=N},\ [F_{m pair},\Pi_0+\zeta\Pi_1] &=(1-\zeta)F_{m pair}\mathbf1_{J=d}. \end{split} 	ag{18b} \] These are retained threshold currents, not errors in the sector construction. Their cancellation when \(\zeta=1\) does not make the separately marked sectors intertwining sources. Write \(\mathcal E_N=\Xi_N\kappa(M)^w\) and define the stripped sector directly by removing the crossing scalars. Apply H's all-inverse fixed-bank construction to the nilpotent completion of (16). It has the same \(s=9c\) variables as H, with constant orthogonal projectors inserted in their literal positions. Their norm is one; they introduce no poles or meridian derivatives. All H's moving frames remain at their original stages. For \(0<\eta<\eta'<\pi\), put \(M=e^{u/N}\), \(|u|\le\eta'\). The complete rational source of each sector obeys, uniformly in \(\mathbf b\), \[ |\mathcal R_{\mathbf b,N}( oldsymbolho, oldsymbol j;u)| \le C(N+1)^B\prod_{\ell=1}^{s}ho_\ell^{-1}. 	ag{19} \] Indeed H bounds the moving diagonals and inverses by powers of \(N\), the actual coupon by \(e^{(m-1)\eta'}N^{m-1}\), each transfer or direct-factorial kernel by \(N/ho\), and each inverse-factorial kernel by \(1/ho\). Inserting norm-one projectors changes none of these estimates. Constants depend on the fixed word and collar. Let \(\widehat{\mathcal P}^{m nil}_{\mathbf b,N,tail}(R,u)\) denote the ordinary completed Hankel integral restricted to \(\maxho_\ell\ge R\), \(R\ge1\). Define \[ G_j= rac{|(Q;Q)_j|}{N^{j/N+1/2}},\qquad c_N= rac{(N-1)(N-2)}{4N}. 	ag{20} \] H's integrable endpoint envelope and Cauchy's formula on the buffered \(u\)-disk give, for every fixed integer \(k\ge0\), \[ \sup_{|u|\le\eta} |\partial_\mu^k\widehat{\mathcal P}^{m nil}_{\mathbf b,N,tail}(R,u)| \le  rac{k!N^k}{(\eta'-\eta)^k} C(N+1)^B sR^{-c_N}\Big(\sum_{j=1}^{N-1}G_j\Big)^s. 	ag{21} \] The full absolute integral has the analogous bound without \(sR^{-c_N}\). The banks and endpoint exponents do not depend on \(u\), so the same envelope justifies holomorphy and differentiation under the integral. These are genuine meridian derivatives of the stripped family associated with (18), including its pivot and moving frames, rather than derivatives of a root-only symbol. The external line is restored by its full product rule below. Writing \(v_3\) for the regular ideal tetrahedron volume, H's uniform estimate for \(G_j\) proves \[ \limsup_{N	o\infty} rac1N\log \sup_{|u|\le\eta} |\partial_\mu^k\widehat{\mathcal P}^{m nil}_{\mathbf b,N,tail}(R,u)| \le rac{9cv_3}{2\pi}- rac14\log R. 	ag{22} \] The bound is uniform over the finite \(2^c\) sectors and also bounds their sum of absolute tail values. For the standard zero-framed source, H(16) gives \(\mathcal E_N=x^{dw}\), bounded on the collar, with derivative \((dw)^a x^{dw}\) of order \(a\). Thus (22) holds for its full sector jets. H's explicit normalized dimension lines remain permitted; an additional prescribed line retains its exact product rule and needs its stated buffered subexponential bound. At \(N=2\), \(c_N=0\); (22) is a large-level statement. For an empty word there is one sector and no radial tail. The superscript in (21)--(22) is essential. These tails belong to the nilpotent completion. Their estimate is not transferred to a partial raw cyclic-wall bank by equality of complete periods. ## 5. The actual coherent projector kernels There is a useful complex domain on which one sector projector has an identity-like normalized kernel. There are also regular complex points where both normalized kernels grow exponentially and cancel. Both facts follow directly from the finite binomial coefficients. For two heads put \(v_i=z_iw_i\), where \(z_i,w_i\) are the ordinary binomial coherent variables, and assume \(1+v_i
e0\). Their identity kernel is \(I_N=(1+v_1)^d(1+v_2)^d\). Inserting the diagonal projectors (8) and dividing by this kernel gives exactly \[ L_N(v_1,v_2)= rac{\displaystyle\sum_{a+b\le d}  inom da inom db v_1^av_2^b}{I_N},\qquad H_N(v_1,v_2)=1-L_N(v_1,v_2). 	ag{23} \] These are kernels of the actual finite projectors, without an interpolation of their occupation thresholds. Write \(x=|v_1|\), \(y=|v_2|\), and \[ \Gamma(v_1,v_2)=  rac{(\sqrt x+\sqrt y)^2}{|1+v_1|\,|1+v_2|}. 	ag{24} \] If \(xy<1\), then \[ |H_N|\le\sqrt{xy}\,\Gamma^d; \qquad xy>1\quad\Longrightarrow\quad |L_N|\le\Gamma^d. 	ag{25} \] For the first bound use any \(R>1\): on the high range \(a+b\ge d+1\), \(R^{-a-b}\le R^{-d-1}\), whence \[ |H_N|\le R^{-1} \left[ rac{(1+Rx)(1+Ry)}{R|1+v_1||1+v_2|}ight]^d. 	ag{26} \] For \(0<R<1\), the low range instead gives the same bound for \(|L_N|\) without the initial \(R^{-1}\). Choose \(R=(xy)^{-1/2}\); the bracket becomes \(\Gamma\), proving (25) when \(xy
e0\). If \(xy=0\), the high kernel vanishes identically, so the first conclusion holds by continuity. Consequently on every compact subset of \(\{\Gamma<1,\ xy<1\}\), \(L_N=1+O(\gamma^d)\), and on every compact subset of \(\{\Gamma<1,\ xy>1\}\), \(H_N=1+O(\gamma^d)\), for some \(\gamma<1\). The same estimates hold for every fixed holomorphic derivative of the exponentially small difference. Indeed the strict inequalities admit a fixed complex neighborhood with \(\Gamma\le\gamma<1\); (25) there and Cauchy's formula prove the derivative bounds. This is a statement about a single actual kernel, not a rule for multiplying normalized symbols in an unevaluated network. The chamber condition is substantive. Set \(v_1=v_2=v\) and write \(H_d(v)=H_N(v,v)\). Vandermonde's finite binomial identity gives \[ H_d(v)= rac{ inom{2d}{d}v^d}{(1+v)^{2d}} \sum_{j=1}^d R_{d,j}v^j,\qquad R_{d,j}= rac{ inom{2d}{d+j}}{ inom{2d}{d}} =\prod_{\ell=1}^j rac{d-\ell+1}{d+\ell}. 	ag{27} \] Here \(0\le R_{d,j}\le1\) and \[ 0\le1-R_{d,j} \le\sum_{\ell=1}^j rac{2\ell-1}{d+\ell} \le rac{j^2}{d}. 	ag{28} \] For every \(ho<1\), summing this error against \(ho^j\) and bounding the omitted geometric tail proves uniformly on \(|v|\leho\) that \(\sum_{j=1}^d R_{d,j}v^j=v/(1-v)+O(d^{-1})\). The elementary central-binomial estimate \( inom{2d}{d}=4^d(\pi d)^{-1/2}(1+O(d^{-1}))\) therefore gives \[ H_d(v)= rac{v}{1-v} rac1{\sqrt{\pi d}} \left[ rac{4v}{(1+v)^2}ight]^d (1+O(d^{-1})) 	ag{29} \] uniformly on every compact subset of \(0<|v|<1\). The relative error is legitimate because \(v/(1-v)\) is a unit there. For a concrete open counterdomain put \[ u= rac14+i,\qquad v= rac{u}{1-u}= rac{-13+16i}{25}. 	ag{30} \] Then \(|v|=\sqrt{17}/5<1\), \(u=v/(1+v)\), and \(\operatorname{Re}(u+u)=1/2<1\). Nevertheless \[  rac{4v}{(1+v)^2}=4u(1-u)= rac{19}{4}+2i, \qquad \left| rac{4v}{(1+v)^2}ight|= rac{5\sqrt{17}}4>1. 	ag{31} \] Equations (29)--(31) show exponential growth of both \(H_N\) and \(L_N=1-H_N\), whose sum remains exactly one. The same conclusion holds uniformly near this point within the diagonal family \(v_1=v_2\), by (29). Even an off-unit limiting Cartan symbol does not exclude this behavior: the literal one-head normalized kernel is \[ x_0\left( rac{1+Q^{-1}v}{1+v}ight)^d =-\exp(-2\pi i u)(1+O(N^{-1})), 	ag{32} \] uniformly on fixed incidence-free compact sets. This follows by summing \( inom da Q^{-a}v^a\) and expanding the fixed compact ratio; at (30) its limiting modulus is \(e^{2\pi}\). Equation (32) is a coherent-kernel limit, not an off-grid operator identity or an identification of a central power. No assertion is made that (30) represents a faithful geometric representation. ## 6. What the reduction does and does not simplify If \(f(0)
e0\), \(f(T)\) is invertible on each nonempty path. In particular the Euler germs have constant term one, so the two integrated branches on a full pair have ranks \[ \operatorname{rank}\Pi_0= rac{N(N+1)}2, \qquad \operatorname{rank}\Pi_1= rac{N(N-1)}2. 	ag{33} \] The boundary vectors in (3) therefore do not localize the integrated crossing to a thin endpoint or a rank-one state. The reduction removes redundant wall histories and supplies ordinary convergent contours for the remaining actual degree sectors. It leaves the coupled occupation-flow sum and its original pivotal phases intact. The physical norm-one projectors do not imply a uniformly bounded normalized coherent symbol at an arbitrary complex point. No determinant formula, positivity, geometric cycle coefficient, or arbitrary-short-component lower bound follows. No asymptotic bound on a separate reduced axis sample is inferred from (18). The conclusions concern the specified original source, its exact sectors and completed absolute meridian tails, together with the single-projector kernel estimates of Section 5. ## Complete proof-source pins * S: `notes/exact_quantum_quad_source_transport.md` (318 lines), SHA256 `7f88f3a12212acacfce7e96abb6a1440be93ba507ba7225d73650435a93fc474`. * P: `notes/cyclic_sewing_regularized_cut_cycle.md` (212 lines), SHA256 `b61b7d077e183c91c023de8ff23700796a7695521c692af06e548910698982b5`. * H: `notes/research_actual_meridian_hankel_transport.md` (271 lines), SHA256 `e50f4257e3464863167d8a04c060753d937921d27c551d8ee18f882add1111e9`. title: Hardy norms of the cyclic dilogarithm and its finite coefficients
status: Cyclic/Hardy norm comparison; coherent lower bound open
text: # Hardy norms of the cyclic dilogarithm and its finite coefficients 24 November 2026. Written research proof. The original norm-one cyclic dilogarithm and its inverse belong to Hardy space. Projecting either symbol to its actual first \(N\) Taylor coefficients loses at most a power of the level in norm. The same comparison holds on every concentric disk, uniformly down to radius zero. This controls scalar symbol norms, with their original phases and normalizations; it does not estimate a marked word from below. ## 1. The actual functions and their physical heads Let \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(Q=e^{2\pi i/N}\), and \(F_a=(Q;Q)_a\), \(F_0=1\). Retain the anchored functions of C: \[ V_N(z)=(1-z^N)^{(N-1)/(2N)} \prod_{j=1}^{N-1}(1-Q^jz)^{-j/N}, \qquad U_N(z)=V_N(z)^{-1}. \tag{1} \] They are holomorphic on the open unit disk, with value one at zero. Use the coefficient Hardy norm \[ \|f\|_{H^2}^2=\sum_{a\ge0}|f_a|^2 =\sup_{0<r<1}\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}|f(re^{i\theta})|^2d\theta, \qquad f(z)=\sum_{a\ge0}f_a z^a, \] and let \(\Pi_N\) be the orthogonal projection to degrees below \(N\). Then the exact physical scalar heads are \[ \Pi_NU_N=u_N(z)=\sum_{a=0}^d\frac{z^a}{F_a},\qquad \Pi_NV_N=v_N(z)=\sum_{a=0}^d \frac{(-1)^aQ^{a(a-1)/2}z^a}{F_a}. \tag{2} \] Here is a direct normalization check. Reindexing the product (1), with all roots anchored at zero, gives \[ (1-z)V_N(Qz)=(1-z^N)^{1/N}V_N(z),\qquad U_N(Qz)=(1-z)(1-z^N)^{-1/N}U_N(z). \] Below degree \(N\), the norm-root factors equal one. The two coefficient recurrences, initialized by one, are respectively \((Q^a-1)v_a=Q^{a-1}v_{a-1}\) and \((Q^a-1)u_a=-u_{a-1}\). These prove (2), including its phases. **Theorem.** There is a universal \(C\) such that for every \(N\ge2\), every \(0\le r\le1\), and either pair \((A_N,p_N)=(V_N,v_N)\) or \((U_N,u_N)\), \[ \|p_N(r\,\cdot)\|_{H^2} \le\|A_N(r\,\cdot)\|_{H^2} \le N^C\|p_N(r\,\cdot)\|_{H^2}. \tag{3} \] At radius one all four norms have the sharp logarithmic rate \[ \log\|V_N\|_{H^2},\ \log\|U_N\|_{H^2},\ \log\|v_N\|_{H^2},\ \log\|u_N\|_{H^2} =\frac{Nv_3}{2\pi}+O(\log N), \tag{4} \] where \(v_3\) is the regular ideal-tetrahedron volume used in P. The assertion in (4) is about radius one; (3) also permits radii depending arbitrarily on \(N\). ## 2. Square integrability at every root Put \(\zeta_j=Q^{-j}\), \(\beta_j=(N-1-2j)/(2N)\). P's exact factorization is \[ V_N(z)=\prod_{j=0}^{N-1}(1-Q^jz)^{\beta_j},\qquad -\tfrac12<\beta_j<\tfrac12. \tag{5} \] For each fixed \(N\), near \(\zeta_j\) the other factors form a holomorphic unit. The two boundary square moduli therefore have local powers \(2\beta_j\) and \(-2\beta_j\), both greater than \(-1\). They are integrable. The same powers dominate radial approaches: for \(r\ge1/2\), \(|1-re^{i\varphi}|\ge c|\varphi|\) near zero, while positive powers stay bounded. With the other factors bounded away from their roots, this gives an integrable dominating function for each fixed \(N\). Away from the roots the radial limits are uniform. Dominated convergence and Parseval for \(r<1\) prove that both functions belong to \(H^2\), and their norms equal their boundary \(L^2\) norms. No bound uniform in \(N\) is claimed in this preliminary argument; the next step supplies it. P gives on the unit circle, off the roots, \[ |V_N(t)|^2\le N^C e^{Nv_3/\pi} \begin{cases}(N|t-\zeta_j|)^{2\beta_j},&|t-\zeta_j|<1/N,\\ 1,&\operatorname{dist}(t,\mu_N)\ge1/N, \end{cases} \tag{6} \] where \(\mu_N=\{\zeta_j\}\). The estimate for \(U_N\) has \(-2\beta_j\) in place of \(2\beta_j\). The root arcs are disjoint. On such an arc, put \(s=|t-\zeta_j|=2|\sin(\varphi/2)|\). Since \(s<1/N\le1/2\), its angular measure is bounded by a universal constant times \(ds\) on each side. For either sign, \[ \frac1{2\pi}\int_{|t-\zeta_j|<1/N} (N|t-\zeta_j|)^{\pm2\beta_j}\,d\theta \le\frac{C}{N(1\pm2\beta_j)}. \] The sums of these bounds are at most \(C\log(2N)\), since \[ N(1-2\beta_j)=2j+1,\qquad N(1+2\beta_j)=2N-1-2j. \] Integrating (6) on all arcs and their complement therefore proves \[ \|V_N\|_{H^2}^2,\ \|U_N\|_{H^2}^2 \le N^C e^{Nv_3/\pi}. \tag{7} \] This includes the nearly nonintegrable endpoint exponents, all parities, and the removable root when \(\beta_j=0\). ## 3. The original coefficients retain the exponential norm Both physical heads in (2) have the identical energy \[ E_N=\|u_N\|_{H^2}^2=\|v_N\|_{H^2}^2 =\sum_{a=0}^d|F_a|^{-2}. \tag{8} \] P proves, uniformly for \(0\le a<N\), \(\log|F_a|=NJ(a/N)+O(\log N)\), where \(J(s)=\int_0^s\log(2\sin\pi u)du\). Also \(J(1/6)=-v_3/(2\pi)\). Choose \(a\) nearest to \(N/6\). For sufficiently large \(N\), \(J\) has bounded derivative on the intervening fixed interval, so \(N|J(a/N)-J(1/6)|\le C\). One actual summand in (8) gives \[ E_N\ge N^{-C}e^{Nv_3/\pi}. \tag{9} \] Increasing \(C\) includes the finitely many smaller levels. Orthogonal projection gives \(E_N\le\|A_N\|_{H^2}^2\). Together with (7),(9) this proves (4) and (3) at radius one. Only coefficient magnitudes enter this norm comparison; the phase-bearing coefficients themselves remain exactly (2). ## 4. Uniform comparison on every smaller disk Fix either pair and write \(A_N=\sum a_mz^m\). Put \[ E_r=\sum_{m<N}|a_m|^2r^{2m},\qquad T_r=\sum_{m\ge N}|a_m|^2r^{2m}. \] For \(0<r\le1\), termwise comparison gives \[ T_r\le r^{2N}T_1,\qquad E_r\ge r^{2(N-1)}E_1,\qquad \frac{E_r+T_r}{E_r}\le1+r^2\frac{T_1}{E_1} \le\frac{E_1+T_1}{E_1}. \tag{10} \] The last ratio is bounded by a power of \(N\), by Section 3. Taking square roots proves (3). At \(r=0\), both functions and both heads equal one, so the assertion is exact. No limiting assumption on the radius is needed. The same comparison retains the actual positive-factorial scalar. Since \(F_d=N\), finite factorial reversal gives \[ \mathcal F_N(z)=Nz^dV_N(Q/z),\qquad f_N(z)=\sum_{a=0}^dF_az^a=Nz^dv_N(Q/z). \tag{11} \] Indeed \(NQ^{d-a}[z^{d-a}]v_N=F_a\); this follows by replacing \(h\) with \(N-h\) in \(F_d/F_{d-a}\). For every \(R\ge1\), reflection of Fourier modes multiplies both norms by the same factor \(NR^d\) and changes the inner radius to \(1/R\). Thus (3) gives \[ \|f_N(R\,\cdot)\|_{L^2(\mathbb T)} \le\|\mathcal F_N(R\,\cdot)\|_{L^2(\mathbb T)} \le N^C\|f_N(R\,\cdot)\|_{L^2(\mathbb T)}. \tag{12} \] Its finite part is the orthogonal projection to modes \(0,\ldots,d\). The original factor \(N\) and reflected monomial have not been removed. ## 5. Source meaning and scope H already identifies (2) as the physical jets and proves the exact ordered support identities for the completed cyclic/Hardy network. C retains the full original source, reflected factorials, Gaussian weights, caps, Cartan factors and external scalar. This note changes none of those operators or projectors. The new conclusion is the polynomial norm comparison with the full scalar symbols, including all radii and the reflected normalization in (11). These are estimates for the two symbol vectors and their dilates. They do not assert a bounded multiplication operator on arbitrary Hardy inputs, a lower bound for a coherent word contraction, or nonvanishing of its last marked observation. Norm comparison does not select a geometric cycle or prove the finite-exception theorem. ## Complete inputs and coverage | Key | Complete text | Lines | SHA256 | | --- | --- | ---: | --- | | P | [Uniform cyclic-root estimate](research_cyclic_atom_near_unit_circle.md) | 258 | a7de0218d347cea79b90e46bb11b6c1c0fd594d43b385f0d40a8bd6a4b9e511e | | C | [Actual continuous source](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_continuous_gaussian_cyclic_network.md) | 378 | ee47ebbb53258d84ded684e22b1bdfaf193b7fa9a3c852889bf86cb99eb6930c | | H | [Cyclic/Hardy source coverage](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_cyclic_hardy_dilog_network.md) | 399 | bdde89f19901f1df29eeee174c163312bbb40b905852083bd75f0d138e5c65c5 | P and C are complete proof inputs; H is complete coverage. # The original cyclic dilogarithm near the unit circle 24 November 2026. Written research proof. The norm-one cyclic dilogarithm in the original knot period has a uniform logarithmic estimate through the unit circle. Polynomial separation from its root divisors gives a logarithmic error. At closer approaches an explicit root factor gives the same error, even when the distance is superexponentially small in the level. All factors belong to the actual function; no closed-period lower bound is inferred. ## 1. The actual atom and the estimate Put \(N\ge2\), \(Q=e^{2\pi i/N}\), and \(\mu_N=\{Q^j:0\le j<N\}\). Use C's unchanged functions \[ D_N(t)=\prod_{j=1}^{N-1}(1-Q^jt)^{j/N},\qquad V_N(t)= rac{(1-t^N)^{(N-1)/(2N)}}{D_N(t)},\qquad U_N(t)=V_N(t)^{-1}. 	ag{1} \] All branches start at one at zero and are continued along the specified path avoiding \(\mu_N\). Their moduli are independent of that path, since every exponent in (1) is real. Define the continuous function \[ F(t)= egin{cases} \operatorname{Im}\operatorname{Li}_2(t)/(2\pi),&0<|t|\le1,\ -\operatorname{Im}\operatorname{Li}_2(1/t)/(2\pi),&|t|>1. \end{cases} 	ag{2} \] Here \(\operatorname{Li}_2(z)=\sum_{m\ge1}z^m/m^2\) on the closed unit disk. Its continuity and conjugation symmetry show that the two boundary values in (2) agree. Write \(\zeta_j=Q^{-j}\), \( eta_j=(N-1-2j)/(2N)\), and \(\delta=\operatorname{dist}(t,\mu_N)\). For \(t
otin\mu_N\), put \[ B_N(t)= egin{cases}  eta_j\log(N|t-\zeta_j|),&|t-\zeta_j|<1/N,\ 0,&\delta\ge1/N. \end{cases} \] The first case has at most one index, because distinct roots are separated by at least \(4/N\). **Theorem.** Fix \(R\ge1\). Uniformly for all \(N\ge2\) and \(R^{-1}\le|t|\le R\), \(t
otin\mu_N\), \[ \left|\log|V_N(t)|-NF(t)-B_N(t)ight|\le C_R\log N, \quad \left|\log|U_N(t)|+NF(t)+B_N(t)ight|\le C_R\log N. 	ag{3} \] Consequently, for every fixed \(A>0\), \[ \operatorname{dist}(t,\mu_N)\ge N^{-A} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \left|\log|V_N(t)|-NF(t)ight|\le C_{A,R}\log N. 	ag{4} \] The inverse has the same assertion with leading term \(-NF\). These statements allow arbitrary level-dependent arguments satisfying the displayed conditions. ## 2. A weighted logarithmic sum away from the root disks For this section suppose \(\delta\ge1/N\). Write \(t=re^{i	heta}\), \(g_t(u)=\log|1-te^{2\pi iu}|\), and \(I(t)=\int_0^1u g_t(u)\,du\), using the ordinary improper integral when \(r=1\). Let \(u_0=-	heta/(2\pi)\) modulo one, and let \(d(u,u_0)\in[0,1/2]\) denote circular distance. Exactly \[ |1-te^{2\pi iu}|^2=(1-r)^2+4r\sin^2\! igl(\pi(u-u_0) igr). 	ag{5} \] On the stated annulus, almost everywhere, \[ |g_t(u)|\le C_R+|\log d(u,u_0)|,\qquad \int_0^1|g_t(u)|\,du\le C_R. \] Indeed the modulus is at most \(1+R\) and at least \(2\sqrt r|\sin\pi(u-u_0)|\ge4R^{-1/2}d(u,u_0)\). Where \(d>0\), differentiation also gives \[ |g_t'(u)|\le\pi|\cot\pi(u-u_0)|\le C/d(u,u_0). 	ag{6} \] Partition \([0,1]\) into \(I_j=[j/N,(j+1)/N]\), and put \(w_j=j/N\). Mark as exceptional every cell meeting the circular \(2/N\)-neighborhood of \(u_0\). There are at most eight, including when this neighborhood crosses the seam at zero and one. Every sample satisfies \(g_t(j/N)=\log|t-Q^{-j}|\ge-\log N\), and its upper bound depends only on \(R\). On an interval of length \(h\le1/2\), the integral of \(|\log d(u,u_0)|\) is at most \(Ch\log(e/h)\), uniformly in its position; split at the seam if needed. Thus \(N\int_{I_j}|g_t|\le C_R+C\log N\), and all exceptional sample-versus-average errors total \(O_R(\log N)\). On the remaining cells, the sum of the oscillations is at most \(\int|g_t'|\) over those cells. By (6) this is \(O(\log N)\), as their distance from \(u_0\) is at least \(2/N\). Consequently \[ \sum_{j=0}^{N-1}w_j\left(g_t(j/N)-N\int_{I_j}g_t(u)\,duight) =O_R(\log N). \] Replacing \(w_j\) by \(u\) in the integrals costs at most \(\int_0^1|g_t|\le C_R\), since \(|w_j-u|\le1/N\). Hence \[ \sum_{j=1}^{N-1} rac jN\log|1-Q^jt| =NI(t)+O_R(\log N). 	ag{7} \] This treats the weight's seam explicitly, without extending \(u\) periodically. ## 3. The central norm and the two chambers For every nonzero \(t\), with \(\delta=\operatorname{dist}(t,\mu_N)\), there is an absolute \(c>0\) such that \[ c\min(1,N\delta)\le  rac{|1-t^N|}{\max(1,|t|^N)}\le2. 	ag{8} \] Choose the nearest root in angle and write \(t=rQ^ke^{i\varphi}\), \(|\varphi|\le\pi/N\). Put \(a=N|\log r|\), \(b=N\varphi\). The squared ratio in (8) is \((1-e^{-a})^2+4e^{-a}\sin^2(b/2)\). If \(a\ge1\), it has a fixed positive lower bound. If \(a\le1\), its square root is at least \(c\sqrt{a^2+b^2}\), while \(|r e^{i\varphi}-1|\le C\sqrt{a^2+b^2}/N\). The chosen root is also nearest in Euclidean distance. This proves the lower bound; the upper bound is the triangle inequality. When \(\delta\ge1/N\), (8) gives \(\log|1-t^N|=N\log^+|t|+O(1)\). Thus (1),(7) imply \[ \log|V_N(t)|= N\left(	frac12\log^+|t|-I(t)ight)+O_R(\log N). 	ag{9} \] The remaining term \(-	frac12\log^+|t|\) is bounded on the annulus. The central norm factor itself has not been omitted. For \(|t|<1\), integrating the absolutely convergent logarithmic series, with \(\int_0^1u e^{2\pi imu}du=1/(2\pi im)\), gives \(I(t)=-\operatorname{Im}\operatorname{Li}_2(t)/(2\pi)\). For \(|t|>1\), write \(g_t(u)=\log|t|+\log|1-t^{-1}e^{-2\pi iu}|\); then \(I(t)=	frac12\log|t|+\operatorname{Im}\operatorname{Li}_2(1/t)/(2\pi)\). The uniform small-interval integral bound following (5), together with continuity away from the singular angle, proves continuity of these integrals at the unit circle. Equation (9) therefore proves (3) outside the root disks. There is also an exact modulus identity: \[ |V_N(t)V_N(1/t)|= rac{|1-t|}{|1-t^N|^{1/N}}. 	ag{10} \] Indeed reindexing \(j\mapsto N-j\) gives \(|D_N(t)D_N(1/t)|=|t|^{-(N-1)/2}|1-t^N|/|1-t|\). The numerator norm factors in (1) give (10). This identity is understood off \(\mu_N\), without resetting any branch. ## 4. Uniform estimates inside every root disk Factoring \(1-t^N\), with the same anchor at zero, gives exactly \[ V_N(t)=\prod_{k=0}^{N-1}(1-Q^kt)^{ eta_k},\qquad W_{N,j}(t):=V_N(t)(1-Q^jt)^{- eta_j} =\prod_{k
e j}(1-Q^kt)^{ eta_k}. 	ag{11} \] Every continued branch of \(W_{N,j}\) extends holomorphically and without zeros to \(|t-\zeta_j|<1/N\). Its modulus at the center is \[ |W_{N,j}(\zeta_j)|=|(Q;Q)_j|\,N^{-(j+1/2)/N}, \qquad (Q;Q)_0=1. 	ag{12} \] For a direct verification put \(L_l=\log|1-Q^l|\). The product of the nontrivial roots gives \(\sum_{l=1}^{N-1}L_l=\log N\), and symmetry gives \(\sum lL_l=(N/2)\log N\). Reindexing \(k=j+l\) modulo \(N\) in (11) yields \[ \log|W_{N,j}(\zeta_j)| =\left( rac{N-1}{2N}- rac jN- rac12ight)\log N +\sum_{l=N-j}^{N-1}L_l, \] which is (12), including the empty sum at \(j=0\). Let \(s=\min(|k-j|,N-|k-j|)\ge1\). On the disk, \(|t-\zeta_k|\ge(4s-1)/N\), because \(2\sin(\pi s/N)\ge4s/N\). Since \(| eta_k|\le1/2\), \(|(\log W_{N,j})'(t)|\le CN\log N\). Integrating along the straight segment from the center changes \(\log|W_{N,j}|\) by at most \(C\log N\). Here is the endpoint-aware factorial estimate needed in (12). Set \(J(v)=\int_0^v\log(2\sin\pi u)\,du\). Uniformly for \(0\le j<N\), \(\log|(Q;Q)_j|=NJ(j/N)+O(\log N)\). To prove it, split \(\log(2\sin\pi u)=\log u+\log(1-u)+h(u)\), where \(h\) extends smoothly to \([0,1]\). The right Riemann sums for the two monotone logarithms differ from their integrals by \(O(\log N)\), including the first cell of \(\log u\) and the final allowed sample \(j=N-1\). The smooth remainder costs \(O(1)\). The case \(j=0\) is exact. Differentiating the boundary dilogarithm and using its value at one gives \(J(v)=F(e^{-2\pi iv})\). Therefore \[ \left|\log|W_{N,j}(t)|-NF(\zeta_j)ight|\le C\log N \qquad (|t-\zeta_j|<1/N), 	ag{13} \] including the center itself. For \(|z|,|w|\le1\), \(d=|z-w|\le1/2\), the series estimate \(|z^m-w^m|\le\min(md,2)\) gives \(|\operatorname{Li}_2(z)-\operatorname{Li}_2(w)| \le Cd\log(e/d)\). Apply it directly inside the unit disk and to \(1/t,1/\zeta_j\) outside. If \(\delta=|t-\zeta_j|<1/N\), then \(N|F(t)-F(\zeta_j)|\le C\log N\). Combining (11),(13), and \(| eta_j|\le1/2\) proves (3) inside the root disk, with \( eta_j\log(N\delta)\) retained. Inversion proves the assertion for \(U_N\). If additionally \(\delta\ge N^{-A}\), this root correction has magnitude at most \(	frac12\max(A-1,0)\log N\), proving (4). ## 5. Sharp envelope and scope Put \(v_3=\operatorname{Im}\operatorname{Li}_2(e^{\pi i/3})\), the volume of a regular ideal tetrahedron. Harmonicity and boundary continuity reduce the disk extrema to the unit circle. There the angular derivative is \(-\log|2\sin(	heta/2)|\), so the maximum is \(v_3\) at \(	heta=\pi/3\), and the minimum is \(-v_3\) at \(5\pi/3\). Formula (2) gives the same bounds outside. Consequently \[ |V_N(t)|\le N^{C_R}e^{Nv_3/(2\pi)+B_N(t)},\qquad |U_N(t)|\le N^{C_R}e^{Nv_3/(2\pi)-B_N(t)}. 	ag{14} \] Under polynomial root separation, the correction is absorbed in a power of \(N\). At closer approaches its original exponent is mandatory. H already gives the sharp per-atom constant \(v_3/(2\pi)\), and S gives the two chamber actions and exact resonant source values. The refinement is uniform control near the circle, including the regularized functions throughout every root disk. It does not reduce the number of atoms in an actual word or replace H's endpoint integrals. No unrestricted finite value of the unregularized atom is assigned at its roots. C's source, inverse atoms, reflected monomials, Gaussian weights, Cauchy factors and external scalar remain unchanged. These function estimates neither bound a coherent contraction below nor transport its selected geometric cycle. ## Complete input and coverage | Key | Complete text | Lines | SHA256 | | --- | --- | ---: | --- | | C | [Actual continuous source](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_continuous_gaussian_cyclic_network.md) | 378 | ee47ebbb53258d84ded684e22b1bdfaf193b7fa9a3c852889bf86cb99eb6930c | | H | [Actual cut cycle and endpoint envelope](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_cyclic_dilog_hankel_cycle.md) | 316 | 502ddfc4b13c7bd775bf27398592085f3951019ff959e1fe6e363a1a468993ea | | S | [Earlier chamber actions and resonant source flags](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/cyclic_source_connection_and_resonant_flags.md) | 401 | cdb07713bec8bd0b45b1a36a9676d2f1bb890b842c7d85d947cfa7e978c2d7b3 | C is the sole complete selected proof input; H and S are complete coverage. title: Actual cyclic crossings: a sharp wrap gap and a Gaussian Morse adapter
text: # Actual cyclic crossings: a sharp wrap gap and a Gaussian Morse adapter 24 November 2026. Research proof. Earlier finals and manuscripts are unchanged. The actual complete-color E-cyclic crossing differs from the original nilpotent crossing by a one-wrap matrix. Its sharp physical norm exponent is the regular ideal tetrahedron volume divided by \(\pi\), strictly smaller than the full crossing's Gaussian exponent. Consequently the existing whole physical Gaussian model approximates the actual cyclic crossing to every fixed algebraic order. Projecting this model onto the complete actual pair intertwiner space makes its error an exact intertwiner. The opposite-source Morse Gram then bounds that error, after any spectator embedding, by its pair physical Hilbert--Schmidt norm. No Gram condition number or spectator dimension factor occurs. This is an absolute approximation at the full crossing norm scale, not a geometric scalar lower bound. ## 1. Actual changing-source matrices and physical conventions Fix \(N\ge2\), and put \[ d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\quad x=-q^{-1},\quad \gamma=x^N=(-1)^{N+1},\quad \kappa=q^{d^2/2}, \] \[ F_j=(Q;Q)_j,\qquad s_j=|F_j|=\prod_{h=1}^j2\sin(\pi h/N),\qquad F_0=s_0=1. \tag{1} \] All pair matrices use the original balanced orthonormal physical basis \(w_a\otimes w_b\). Let \(E_\mu,F,K\) be [M, (2)]: \[ E_\mu w_a=(Q^{-a}-1)w_{a-1}\ (a>0),\quad E_\mu w_0=\mu w_d, \quad Fw_a=(1-Q^{a+1})w_{a+1},\quad Kw_a=xQ^{-a}w_a . \tag{2} \] Missing end arrows are zero. Take \(|\mu_1|=|\mu_2|=1/N\). Write \(R^\sigma_{\boldsymbol\mu}\) for the genuine checked crossing of [B], with its complete Cartan scalar retained. For either sign its input pair \(\boldsymbol\mu=(\mu_1,\mu_2)\) has output source \[ \boldsymbol\mu' =(\gamma\mu_2,\gamma\mu_1). \tag{3} \] The two signs are inverses with the appropriate intermediate fibers. They are not obtained by leaving the nilpotent matrix unchanged. Let \(R^\sigma_0\) be the original nilpotent crossing, in the same metric and normalization, and define \[ \Delta^\sigma_{\boldsymbol\mu} =R^\sigma_{\boldsymbol\mu}-R^\sigma_0 . \tag{4} \] No deformation of the meridian or of the quantum root is used. ## 2. The exact one-wrap entries, including the negative sign The checked positive matrix is \(\kappa\mathsf S D\) times the finite Euler sum [B, (7)] \[ \sum_{k=0}^{d} \frac{(-1)^kq^{k^2}}{F_k}\,E_{\mu_1}^k\otimes F^k , \tag{5} \] where \(\mathsf S\) flips the heads and \(D\) is the original unitary Cartan diagonal at complete color. For input \((a,b)\), a nonzero term requires \(b+k\le d\). If \(k\le a\), it is precisely the nilpotent entry. If \(a<k\), it wraps once, has output \((b+k,r)\) with \(r=a-k+N\), and belongs to \(\Delta^+_{\boldsymbol\mu}\). There is at most one term at any specified input and output. Since \(s_d=N\) and \(|\mu_1|=1/N\), the wrapped lowering product has modulus \(s_a/s_r\). Therefore the exact wrapped entry obeys \[ \left|(\Delta^+_{\boldsymbol\mu})_{(b+k,a-k+N);(a,b)}\right| =\frac{s_a s_{b+k}}{s_{a-k+N}s_b s_k} =\frac{s_a s_{b+k}s_{k-a-1}}{N s_b s_k}, \quad 0\le a<k\le d-b . \tag{6} \] The last equality is the exact reflection identity \(s_j s_{d-j}=N\); in particular its index is \(k-a-1\). All other entries of this difference are zero. Every such entry raises total integer degree by \(N\). For the actual negative crossing first flip the input, apply \(D^{-1}\), and then use the inverse Euler coefficients \(q^k/F_k\), in the recovered positive-source fiber, as prescribed in [B, Section 4]. The recovered donor source still has modulus \(1/N\). Its wrapped terms have donor \(b\), recipient \(a\), \(b<k\le d-a\), and output \((b-k+N,a+k)\). Consequently \[ \left|(\Delta^-_{\boldsymbol\mu})_{(b-k+N,a+k);(a,b)}\right| =\frac{s_b s_{a+k}}{s_{b-k+N}s_a s_k}. \tag{7} \] The inverse Euler coefficients have the same moduli as those in (5); the preceding Cartan and flip are unitary. This proves (7) directly, without asserting a conjugation identity for the full cyclic matrices. Both signs thus have the same set of wrapped entry magnitudes. The external phases and source phases remain in the actual matrices. ## 3. Sharp physical norm exponent on the entire wrapped support Let \[ h(u)=\int_0^u\log(2\sin\pi v)\,dv,\quad \Lambda(\theta)=-\int_0^\theta\log(2\sin v)\,dv,\quad v_3=3\Lambda(\pi/3). \tag{8} \] The endpoint-uniform sine-product estimate in [G] is \(\log s_j=Nh(j/N)+O(\log N)\) for every \(0\le j<N\). Apply it to the first expression in (6). With \((u,v,t)=(a,b,k)/N\), its logarithm is \[ NS_{\rm w}(u,v,t)+O(\log N),\qquad S_{\rm w}=h(u)+h(v+t)+h(t-u)-h(v)-h(t), \] \[ 0\le u\le t,\qquad 0\le v\le1-t. \tag{9} \] Here \(h(1+u-t)=-h(t-u)\) was used. The actual grid has \(a<k\) and \(b+k\le N-1\); using its compact closure is valid for the upper bound. All boundary factorial lengths are included. For \(0<t<1\), the function \(h(u)+h(t-u)\) is strictly convex: \[ \frac{d^2}{du^2}\{h(u)+h(t-u)\} =\frac{\pi\sin\pi t}{\sin\pi u\,\sin\pi(t-u)}>0 . \tag{10} \] It therefore has maximum \(h(t)\) at the two endpoints. The recipient interval \(h(v+t)-h(v)\) is strictly concave, with unique maximum at \(v=(1-t)/2\) and value \(-2h((1-t)/2)\). Thus \[ \max S_{\rm w} =\max_{0\le t\le1}-2h((1-t)/2) =-2h(1/6)=:M_{\rm w}=v_3/\pi . \tag{11} \] The last maximum has \(t=2/3\). Both closure points \(u=0,t\) attain it, with \(v=1/6\); no uniqueness of the full boundary maximizer is asserted. To obtain the value, \(h'\) changes sign at \(1/6\) on \([0,1/2]\). The identity \(h(t)=2h(t/2)-2h((1-t)/2)\), proved by differentiation, gives \(3h(1/3)=2h(1/6)\), hence the last equality in (11). Continuity includes \(t=0,1\). There are at most \(N^3\) wrapped entries. This proves the upper Hilbert--Schmidt and operator bounds with logarithmic error. For the lower bound take \(a=0\), \(k\) nearest \(2N/3\), and \(b\) nearest \(N/6\), chosen within \(b+k\le d\). For all sufficiently large \(N\) this is admissible, and its exact modulus is \(s_{b+k}s_{k-1}/(N s_b s_k)\). The same uniform factorial estimate gives its logarithm \(NM_{\rm w}+O(\log N)\). A matrix norm dominates an entry. Equation (7) proves the same bounds for the negative sign. We have therefore proved, uniformly in the source phases, \[ \boxed{\quad \log\|\Delta^\sigma_{\boldsymbol\mu}\|_{\rm op} =\log\|\Delta^\sigma_{\boldsymbol\mu}\|_{\rm HS} =NM_{\rm w}+O(\log N). \quad} \tag{12} \] The equalities in (12) are asymptotic statements, not equality of norms. ## 4. A whole Gaussian in the updated cyclic fibers Let \(\mathfrak G^\sigma_{N,J}\) be the untilted whole physical Gaussian model of [G, (10)], at a fixed order \(J\ge0\). It keeps the original unwrapped entry phase and support. That theorem proves \[ \|R^\sigma_0-\mathfrak G^\sigma_{N,J}\|_{\rm HS} \le C_JN^{-(J+1)/2}\|R^\sigma_0\|_{\rm HS},\qquad \|R^\sigma_0\|_{\rm HS} =\tfrac12 N^{1/4}e^{NM_0}(1+O(N^{-1})), \quad M_0=2G_{\rm Cat}/\pi . \tag{13} \] Here \(G_{\rm Cat}=\sum_{r\ge0}(-1)^r/(2r+1)^2\). There is a strict exponent gap \(M_0>M_{\rm w}\), without needing a numerical comparison. Indeed [G]'s reduced unwrapped action at Euler length \(t=2/3\) is \[ -4h(1/6)-h(2/3) =-\tfrac{10}{3}h(1/6)=\tfrac53 M_{\rm w}>M_{\rm w}. \tag{14} \] Since \(M_0\) is its maximum, this proves the gap. The polynomial factors in (12) are consequently absorbed by every fixed power of \(N^{-1}\) relative to (13). The triangle inequality gives \[ \|R^\sigma_{\boldsymbol\mu}-\mathfrak G^\sigma_{N,J}\|_{\rm HS} \le C'_JN^{-(J+1)/2}\|R^\sigma_0\|_{\rm HS} \tag{15} \] for all sufficiently large integer levels, with no parity restriction. The constants are uniform in \(|\mu_1|=|\mu_2|=1/N\). Define the complete physical intertwiner space by full matrix equations: \[ \mathcal I^\sigma_{\boldsymbol\mu} =\{A:\ A E_{\rm in}=E_{\rm out}A,\ A F_{\rm in}=F_{\rm out}A,\ A K_{\rm in}=K_{\rm out}A\}. \tag{16} \] The total pair generators use (2), its actual coproduct, and the input/output sources (3). Let \(\Pi^\sigma_{\boldsymbol\mu}\) be the physical Hilbert--Schmidt orthogonal projection onto (16), and set \[ \widehat R^\sigma_{\boldsymbol\mu,N,J} =\Pi^\sigma_{\boldsymbol\mu}\mathfrak G^\sigma_{N,J}, \qquad \mathcal E^\sigma_{\boldsymbol\mu,N,J} =R^\sigma_{\boldsymbol\mu} -\widehat R^\sigma_{\boldsymbol\mu,N,J}. \tag{17} \] This is a specified finite projection, determined by the displayed head matrices, not by an unknown knot scalar. The space (16) is closed and contains the actual \(R^\sigma_{\boldsymbol\mu}\). Orthogonal projection therefore proves \[ \mathcal E^\sigma_{\boldsymbol\mu,N,J}\in \mathcal I^\sigma_{\boldsymbol\mu},\qquad \|\mathcal E^\sigma_{\boldsymbol\mu,N,J}\|_{\rm HS} \le C'_JN^{-(J+1)/2}\|R^\sigma_0\|_{\rm HS}. \tag{18} \] All physical matrix coordinates and all intertwining constraints are used. No intermediate Casimir is replaced by nodal eigenvalues. No constant dimension or smooth variation of (16) is required. The projection need not preserve the Gaussian's entrywise phase description, and no cost bound for explicitly computing it is asserted. ## 5. Spectator-free error in the source-compatible Morse Gram Embed the error (17) on its actual neighboring pair in any opposite-source odd-width slice of [M], using identities on spectators. Use its correctly updated output labels. Pair \(E,F,K\) intertwining implies intertwining of the full iterated coproduct: the earlier terms contain the pair \(K\), the local terms its \(E\), and the later terms pass unchanged. In particular \(T_{\rm out}\mathcal E=\mathcal E T_{\rm in}\) for the common normalization of [M, (15)]. Apply the exact averaging inequality [M, (18)] to this embedded map. Its physical operator norm is the pair operator norm, which is bounded by the pair Hilbert--Schmidt norm in (18). Hence \[ \boxed{\quad \|\mathcal E^\sigma_{\boldsymbol\mu,N,J}\otimes I_{\rm spec} \|_{J_{\rm out}\leftarrow J_{\rm in}} \le C'_JN^{-(J+1)/2}\|R^\sigma_0\|_{\rm HS} \le C''_J N^{1/4-(J+1)/2}e^{NM_0}. \quad} \tag{19} \] No condition number of \(J_{\rm in}\) or \(J_{\rm out}\) is used. There is no spectator Hilbert--Schmidt dimension factor. In particular (19) is valid at an opposite-center pair whose total pair \(E^N\) is zero: the averaging is on the odd whole slice, not on a nonexistent cyclic pair normalization. The corrected models and the literal cups/caps of [M] can be composed as intertwiners in the fixed original Morse presentation. Their errors remain absolute estimates at the scale in (19). The two corrected signs are not asserted mutual inverses or a new braiding, and their products are not asserted equal to the original word. Every original cap, marked closing, framing and external scalar remains. The error may exceed the actual geometric packet or closing overlap; no nonzero cap projection or scalar geometric lower follows. ## Complete inputs and closest coverage [G, Section 4] already projects its nilpotent Gaussian onto the full physical algebra. [P, Section 4] already uses physical \(E,F,K\) projection and warns that it changes a phase representation. [C] already controls a different positive-degree Euler completion and can damp its carry exponentially without changing the source. No novelty is claimed for orthogonal projection or finite-group averaging. The addition is (6)--(12) for the actual semicyclic wraps, followed by the updated-fiber Gaussian estimate and the no-condition-number, spectator-free Morse estimate (19). It supplies no off-root normal continuation, geometric relative error, or finite-exception theorem. All five complete matching texts were read. Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used. title: A uniform-sign normal form for every fixed rational corridor
text: # A uniform-sign normal form for every fixed rational corridor Every fixed rational corridor can be changed to a chain whose internal crossing powers have one sign. Except for the integral and unit cases, all their magnitudes can be taken at least two. The change preserves both arbitrary outside attachments. It introduces fixed integral twists at the ends and a specified proper half-turn, rather than a condition on the surviving filling parameters. The associated tridiagonal chain matrix is definite. Neither definiteness nor the tangle isotopy proves a quantum asymptotic. The exact quantum transformation below retains its scalar, boundary twists and all repeated-root normal data. ## 1. The original word and its boundary map Use the original physical crossing \(R\), clockwise turn \(T\), and the supported pillowcase representatives \[ \widetilde R^{\,n}(x,y)=(x+ny+n/2,y),\qquad \widetilde T(x,y)=(-y,x+1/2). \tag{1} \] Their linear parts are \[ A_n=\begin{pmatrix}1&n\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad S=\begin{pmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}. \tag{2} \] The four marked points are the half-lattice points of the torus, modulo the deck involution \(z\mapsto-z\). The [corridor compression note](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_rational_corridor_compression.md) explains how these representatives are obtained from the actual supported crossings and how an equality of their affine maps gives an isotopy carrying arbitrary attached tangles. Let \(W\) be a fixed finite word, and write its full affine lift as \[ \widetilde W(z)=Gz+v,\qquad G=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix},\quad \det G=1,\quad v\in\tfrac12\mathbb Z^2. \tag{3} \] All powers inside this word are fixed before any remaining outside filling parameter is varied. ## 2. The ceiling Euclidean algorithm and the full matrix identity Suppose \(|c|=C\ge2\). Multiply \(G\) by its deck sign \(\varepsilon=\operatorname{sgn}(c)\), so its lower-left entry is \(C>0\). There are unique integers \(r,s\) such that \[ G_0=A_{-r}(\varepsilon G)A_{-s} =\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\C&D\end{pmatrix}, \qquad 1\le A,D<C. \tag{4} \] Indeed \(A\) and \(D\) are the nonzero residues of \(\varepsilon a,\varepsilon d\) modulo \(C\), and \[ r=\frac{\varepsilon a-A}{C},\qquad s=\frac{\varepsilon d-D}{C}. \tag{5} \] The residues are nonzero because the determinant is one. It also gives \(AD\equiv1\pmod C\) and \(B=(AD-1)/C\ge0\). Starting with \(q_1=C,p_1=A\), repeat \[ b_j=\left\lceil\frac{q_j}{p_j}\right\rceil,\qquad r_j=b_jp_j-q_j. \tag{6} \] If \(r_j=0\), stop. Otherwise set \((q_{j+1},p_{j+1})=(p_j,r_j)\). At every step \(q_j>p_j>0\), so \(b_j\ge2\). Also \(0\le r_j<p_j\). The algorithm terminates, preserves coprimality, and gives \[ \frac CA=[b_1,\ldots,b_k]_- :=b_1-\frac1{b_2-\dfrac1{\cdots-\dfrac1{b_k}}}. \tag{7} \] In particular \(k\le A\le C-1\). The output is unique: at any nonintegral step the first coefficient of an expansion with all later complete quotients greater than one must be the ceiling. **Proposition 1.** With (4)--(7), \[ G_0=(-1)^k S A_{-b_1}S A_{-b_2}\cdots S A_{-b_k}S. \tag{8} \] **Proof.** Let \(H\) denote the matrix on the right. For \(k=1\), it is \(\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&0\\b_1&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)\). Adding a new first coefficient sends a tail matrix \(\left(\begin{smallmatrix}a'&b'\\c'&d'\end{smallmatrix}\right)\) to \[ \begin{pmatrix}c'&d'\\b_1c'-a'&b_1d'-b'\end{pmatrix}. \tag{9} \] Thus the ratio of its lower-left to upper-left entries is the negative continued fraction (7). The continuant recurrence \[ K_j=b_jK_{j-1}-K_{j-2},\qquad K_0=1,\quad K_{-1}=0 \tag{10} \] shows \(K_j>K_{j-1}>0\) for \(j\ge1\). Applied to prefixes and reversed suffixes, it shows that the two diagonal entries of \(H\) lie strictly between zero and its lower-left entry. All matrices have determinant one, so that entry and the upper-left entry are coprime. Their ratio in (7) therefore identifies them as \(C,A\), with no common factor. The lower-right entry is the unique integer in \(\{1,\ldots,C-1\}\) whose product with \(A\) is one modulo \(C\); hence it is \(D\). The determinant then identifies the remaining entry as \(B\). This proves (8). \(\square\) Combining the equations gives an equality in \(\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb Z)\): \[ G=A_r S A_{-b_1}S\cdots S A_{-b_k}S A_s . \tag{11} \] This is a full matrix statement, not just equality of one rational-tangle slope. ## 3. The actual two-boundary tangle identity Form the physical word \[ B=R^r T R^{-b_1}T\cdots T R^{-b_k}T R^s. \tag{12} \] Its affine lift is obtained from (1). Its linear part agrees with \(G\) up to the one deck sign. Consequently \[ \widetilde B^{-1}\widetilde W(z) =\lambda z+w,\qquad \lambda\in\{1,-1\},\quad w\in\tfrac12\mathbb Z^2. \tag{13} \] After the deck involution this is translation by \(\delta=\lambda w\bmod\mathbb Z^2\). Use the actual proper rotation \[ \begin{array}{c|cccc} \delta&(0,0)&(1/2,0)&(0,1/2)&(1/2,1/2)\\ \hline H_\delta&1&\rho&K&\tau . \end{array} \tag{14} \] The supported collar isotopy gives, for every attached tangle \(F\), \[ \boxed{\; W(F)\simeq R^rT\!\left(R^{-b_1}T\!\left(\cdots T\!\left(R^{-b_k}T(R^sH_\delta(F))\right) \cdots\right)\right). \;} \tag{15} \] It carries all marked arcs, closed components, and any supplied ribbon. In particular the rotation in (14) cannot be erased on an arbitrary outside branch. This proves that every corridor with \(|c|\ge2\) has a uniform-negative form with all internal magnitudes at least two. Applying the same construction to the mirrored word and then mirroring the whole equality gives a uniform-positive form as well. Both sides of that resulting equality are in the original oriented ambient manifold; the argument does not replace just one tangle by its mirror. If \(|c|=1\), the one-vertex criterion gives a single unit power with integral twists at both ends. If \(c=0\), the word reduces to an integral twist and a proper half-turn with no intervening turn. The last case can merge two variable outside parameters and must retain its fiber information. For example, the mixed two-boundary corridor has \[ S A_{-2}S A_2S =\begin{pmatrix}-2&1\\-5&2\end{pmatrix}. \] After the deck sign, \(C=5,A=2,D=3\), and \(5/2=[3,2]_-\). Here \(r=0,s=-1\). Thus its common-sign replacement has internal powers \(-3,-2\), with a twist \(-1\) on its inner retained end and the rotation computed from (13). It is not a reduction to a single internal vertex. ## 4. The exact quantum scalar and the boundary chirps Let \(M_N\) be original multiplication by \(R\) and \(J_N\) the original Newton reversal. Put \[ D=N-1,\qquad \kappa_N=\exp\frac{\pi iD^2}{2N}. \tag{16} \] The full algebra includes the first normals at the double roots. Its established identities are \[ J_N^2=I,\qquad J_NM_NJ_N=\kappa_N M_N^{-1}J_NM_N^{-1}. \tag{17} \] Use the displayed logarithm of \(\kappa_N\) and set \(\widehat M_N=\kappa_N^{-1/3}M_N\). Direct multiplication in (17) gives \[ J_N^2=I,\qquad (J_N\widehat M_N)^3=I. \tag{18} \] These are the defining relations of \(\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb Z)\) for \(S,A_1\). One elementary verification of that presentation uses the Farey ideal triangulation: its dual, subdivided at edge midpoints, is a tree, the modular group acts transitively on its edges, an edge has trivial stabilizer, and the endpoint stabilizers have orders two and three. A reduced alternating product of nonidentity elements in these stabilizers moves the base edge along a nonbacktracking path, so cannot be the identity. The two generators also generate every integral determinant-one matrix by the Euclidean algorithm. This proves the presentation used in (18). For a word \(W\), let \(e(W)\) be the sum of its signed crossing exponents; turns contribute zero. Equations (11), (18) give the exact operator equality \[ \boxed{\; \mathcal Q_N(W) =\kappa_N^\ell M_N^r \bigl[J_NM_N^{-b_1}J_N\cdots J_NM_N^{-b_k}J_N\bigr]M_N^s, \qquad \ell=\frac{e(W)-r-s+\sum_jb_j}{3}. \;} \tag{19} \] The exponent \(\ell\) is an integer. Indeed the same modular presentation has a homomorphism to \(\mathbb Z/3\mathbb Z\) sending \(A_1\) to one and \(S\) to zero, so equal matrices have equal crossing-exponent sums modulo three. The actual physical rotation in (15) is still carried in the topological statement. Equation (19) is proved separately on the full original quantum algebra; it is not an inference that the rotation fixes every arbitrary tangle. Here is the corresponding boundary interpretation. An operator \(Q\) has Frobenius kernel coefficient matrix \(QJ_N\). The identity \[ M_N^sJ_N=J_N(M_N^s)^T \tag{20} \] therefore makes the end factors in (19) multiplication by \(R^r\) and \(R^s\) in its two boundary variables, followed by canonical reduction. Thus, if the uniform-negative kernel has an already proved whole-boundary phase \(\Phi(u,v)\), the [canonical boundary-multiplication theorem](research_boundary_crossing_packet_preservation.md) and its [two-boundary version](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_internal_two_crossing_chain.md) give the transformed phase \[ \Phi(u,v)+\frac{i}{4\pi}(ru^2+sv^2). \tag{21} \] The exact additional scalar is \[ \kappa_N^\ell C_{N,r}C_{N,s},\qquad C_{N,j}=\exp\frac{\pi i jD^2}{4N}. \tag{22} \] The amplitudes and the polynomial power of \(N\) are unchanged by those multiplication operations. Equations (21)--(22) are conditional on the stated whole-boundary estimate for the new kernel. The exact finite identity (19) needs no asymptotic assumption and retains all normal data. ## 5. Pendant words and their cap scalar For a pendant word the rational slope is the second-column ratio \(p/q\), \(q\ge0\). If \(q\ge2\), write \[ p/q=r+x,\qquad r=\lfloor p/q\rfloor,\quad 0<x<1. \tag{23} \] The ceiling algorithm for \(1/x\) gives \[ x=\frac1{b_1-\dfrac1{b_2-\cdots-1/b_k}}, \qquad b_j\ge2. \tag{24} \] The pendant word \[ B=R^rTR^{-b_1}T\cdots TR^{-b_k} \tag{25} \] has precisely that slope. The actual cap-stabilizer argument in the corridor note identifies \(W(I)\) with \(B(I)\), where \(I\) is the through tangle. No constraint is imposed on any remaining outside power. There is an exact scalar even though the two full matrices need not agree. Normalize the relative linear matrix to \[ B^{-1}W=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\h&1\end{pmatrix} \quad\hbox{in }\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb Z). \tag{26} \] It is the matrix of \(TR^{-h}T\). The last Newton vector is an eigenvector of the actual crossing with eigenvalue \(\kappa_N\): the diagonal entry is \(\kappa_N(-1)^D e^{\pi iD(D+1)/N}=\kappa_N\). Therefore \[ J_NM_N^{-h}J_Ne_0=\kappa_N^{-h}e_0. \] Combining this with (18) yields \[ \boxed{\; \mathcal Q_N(W)e_0 =\kappa_N^{\ell_{\rm cap}}\mathcal Q_N(B)e_0, \qquad \ell_{\rm cap}=\frac{e(W)-e(B)-2h}{3}\in\mathbb Z . \;} \tag{27} \] This equality is between the full original canonical boundary elements. Any outer \(R^r\) in (25) is handled by canonical multiplication, with its chirp and scalar retained as above. In the mixed example, \[ TR^{-2}TR^2(I)\simeq TR^{-3}TR^{-2}(I), \tag{28} \] and \(h=1\), \(\ell_{\rm cap}=1\). Thus its exact boundary polynomial is \(\kappa_N\) times that of the uniform-negative word in (28). The known mixed-word theorem consequently also estimates this particular uniform-negative word. It does not estimate arbitrary such words. If \(q=1\), the pendant word is an integral braid. If \(q=0\), it is the cup-cap tangle. The latter case uses the literal cap-sum decomposition and can retain an unresolved closed core. It is not silently put into the positive boundary class. ## 6. The definite chain matrix The expansion (7) has the real symmetric matrix \[ Q_{\mathbf b}= \begin{pmatrix} b_1&-1\\ -1&b_2&-1\\ &\ddots&\ddots&\ddots\\ &&-1&b_k \end{pmatrix}. \tag{29} \] For any real vector \(z\), \[ z^TQ_{\mathbf b}z =\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}(z_j-z_{j+1})^2 +z_1^2+z_k^2+\sum_{j=1}^k(b_j-2)z_j^2. \tag{30} \] This is strictly positive for \(z\ne0\), also when every \(b_j=2\). Its determinant is \(C\), and the principal minor deleting the first row and column is \(A\), by (7), (10). Its Schur effective first weight is the same fraction \(C/A\). This is the definite tridiagonal form associated with the negative continued fraction. In the usual continued-fraction surgery presentation, the corresponding chain has the opposite form \(-Q_{\mathbf b}\). No identification of this intersection form with a quantum phase Hessian is made here. ## 7. Surviving original parameters and branching Normalize finitely many disjoint fixed degree-two corridors in an ordered circle tree. They may share retained branch vertices. The end factors in (15) are collected with the original branch powers by the supported twist-sliding isotopy; each passed factor receives its prescribed proper rotation. The total change at a retained vertex is a fixed integer \(\Delta_v\): \[ n'_v=n_v+\Delta_v. \tag{31} \] After choosing the transported carrier parity, \[ p'_v=p_v+ \frac{\eta'_v-\eta_v-\Delta_v}{2}, \qquad n_v=\eta_v-2p_v. \tag{32} \] These are injective translations of the surviving integer assignments. Independent eventual longness is preserved. Internal old powers were already fixed; the added coefficients in (7) are fixed integers, not new freely variable surgery parameters. Rotations do not change the signed crossing power of an integral braid. Propagating a rotation through an already normalized chain can reverse its order, but does not change its uniform sign or the condition \(b_j\ge2\). Thus normalizing disjoint corridors does not undo a neighboring corridor's normalization. The actual branch weights do receive the constant shifts (31), which must be retained. This does not make an arbitrary branching tree definite. For a weighted tree the symmetric matrix with diagonal weights \(b_v\) and off-diagonal edge entries \(-1\) is positive definite exactly when successive leaf elimination produces positive effective weights \[ q_v=b_v-\sum_{w\ {\rm child\ of}\ v}q_w^{-1}. \tag{33} \] The assertion follows by completing squares at each leaf; the resulting diagonal factors are the \(q_v\). It is independent of which vertex is chosen as root. For example a star with central weight two and five leaves of weight two has central effective weight \(2-5/2=-1/2\). Every edge or chain in that star has positive weights at least two, but the whole tree matrix is indefinite. Nor does (30) turn the full root-of-unity source into a positive sum. The original crossings still have their complex entries, and the full trace still retains its normal terms. Equation (19) preserves those facts exactly. A general theorem for uniform-sign chains would be a substantive new analytic input; definite integral surgery data alone does not supply it. ## 8. Scope of the reduction The normal form gives a concrete common target for every fixed rational corridor. Its quantum and topological transformations are both exact. In particular a future whole-boundary theorem for all uniform-negative chains of magnitudes at least two would immediately transfer to all fixed rational corridors with \(c\ne0\), with the original two boundary variables and their normal data retained. The zero case \(c=0\), the pendant cap case, and connected regions with branching remain separate. A zero merger has infinite parameter fibers when its two ends are still variable. The existing [fiber criterion](research_affine_reduction_fibers_and_core_obligation.md) must accompany those reductions; it is not replaced by the continued-fraction algorithm. For a general arborescent component, normalizing its maximal degree-two paths leaves its actual branching pieces in place. The rational-tangle normal-form background is classical; see [Kauffman–Lambropoulou](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0311499). The independent ceiling algorithm, full affine marking, scalar (19), and original parameter map specify what is used here. No claim of a new rational-tangle classification or of cofinite volume coverage follows from them. There is now a geometric theorem for the subfamily whose normalized magnitudes are all at least four: [the negative-corridor variation](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_negative_corridor_variational_bounds.md) has an interior minimum, and [the marked-completion theorem](research_positive_point_marked_completion.md) identifies its actual filling when the retained outside cusps are complete. The boundary shifts and rotations above still have to be transported. This geometric result does not estimate the original quantum source, and coefficients two and three remain in the general normal form. ## 9. Reproducing the finite checks Run the separate checker from the repository root: .venv/bin/python experiments/check_definite_rational_corridor_normal_form.py \ --output repro/results/research-definite-rational-corridor-normal-form.json The [checker](../experiments/check_definite_rational_corridor_normal_form.py) uses exact integers and rational translations for all words of lengths one through four with powers between minus three and three. Of the 2,800 words, 2,220 have the two-boundary normal form with \(|c|\ge2\), and 2,220 have a nonintegral finite pendant slope. It verifies the full affine identity, retained half-turn, integral scalar exponent, determinant and tail minor. The two sets of 2,220 words need not be the same. Separately, it compares the original quantum matrices and pendant vectors for five displayed words at levels two through seven, using 100 decimal digits. These 30 matrix and 30 pendant comparisons check the scalar and ordering conventions numerically. The written operator argument proves the identities for all levels. The [saved output](../repro/results/research-definite-rational-corridor-normal-form.json) contains the script and dependency hashes. Its script SHA256 is 6352af92a2124a407b2a2893560e4987c7679f80837cc2d3f39ee72d430bd354. The output path can be changed for an independent replay. A [140-digit replay](../repro/results/research-definite-rational-corridor-normal-form-root.json) checks the same exact word set and extends the quantum comparisons through level nine, giving 40 matrix and 40 pendant comparisons.

title: Quantum sums on branching circle trees
text:
# Quantum sums on branching circle trees The wide-rectangle edge theorem permits a complete source proof on branching graphs. A sufficient local condition is \(|n_v|\ge\max(8,4d_v)\), where \(d_v\) is the original degree of the filled vertex. The condition allows unrelated powers and independent signs. Every graph and every power are fixed before the level tends to infinity. The analytic theorem below concerns an explicit finite graph sum.
