Original coefficients and the exact positive sum Use the original normalization \[ \theta=\pi/N,\quad q=e^{i\theta},\quad D=N-1,\quad \eta=(-1)^D,\qquad s_j=2\sin(j\theta),\quad S_j=\prod_{r=1}^j s_r,\quad S_0=1, \] \[ c_j=2\cos((2j+1)\theta),\quad e_j(Z)=S_j^{-2}\prod_{h<j}(c_h-Z),\quad K_N(w,Z)=\sum_{j=0}^{D}e_j(w)e_j(Z), \] \[ P_N(Z)=2T_N(Z/2)+2=\prod_{j=0}^{D}(Z-c_j). \tag{1} \] Here \(N\ge2\). Fix real \(\alpha\), put \[ w=w_N(\alpha)=2\cosh(\alpha/N), \qquad K_N(w,-z-z^{-1}) =b_{0,N}+\sum_{k=1}^{D}b_{k,N}(z^k+z^{-k}). \tag{2} \] In angular notation \(z=e^{-it}\). These are ordinary Laurent coefficients, before taking any physical quotient. **Proposition 1.** For \(1\le s\le\lfloor N/2\rfloor\), \[ b_{N-s,N}=\eta(-1)^{s-1}\beta_{s,N},\qquad \beta_{s,N}=\sum_{m=1}^{s}T_{m,s,N}>0, \tag{3} \] where \[ T_{m,s,N}= \frac{P_N(w)S_{m-1}^{\,4}}{N^4} \frac{S_{s+m-1}} {S_{s-m}S_{2m-1}\prod_{h=0}^{m-1}(w-c_h)}. \tag{4} \] For \(1\le m<s\), \[ \frac{T_{m+1,s,N}}{T_{m,s,N}} =\frac{s_m^4s_{s+m}s_{s-m}} {(w-c_m)s_{2m}s_{2m+1}}. \tag{5} \] The formulas apply at both parities, including \(N=2\). **Proof.** The elementary sine product gives \(S_{N-1}=N\), hence \(S_{N-m}=N/S_{m-1}\). The last \(m\) roots in (1) are \(c_0,\ldots,c_{m-1}\) in reverse order. Therefore \[ e_{N-m}(w)= (-1)^{N-m}\frac{P_N(w)S_{m-1}^2} {N^2\prod_{h<m}(w-c_h)}. \tag{6} \] Also \[ P_N(-z-z^{-1})=(-1)^Nz^{-N}(1-\eta z^N)^2. \tag{7} \] Writing \[ \Pi_m(z)=\prod_{h=0}^{m-1} (1+q^{2h+1}z)(1+q^{-(2h+1)}z), \] substitution in (6) gives the exact rational expression \[ e_{N-m}(-z-z^{-1}) =\frac{S_{m-1}^2}{N^2}\, \frac{z^{m-N}(1-\eta z^N)^2}{\Pi_m(z)}. \tag{8} \] The right side is the displayed ordinary Laurent polynomial. Equivalently, multiplying by \(W_N(z)=z^N/(1-\eta z^N)^2\) cancels the full spectral relation. The factors of \(\Pi_m\) are consecutive: \[ \Pi_m(z)=\prod_{j=0}^{2m-1} (1+q^{-(2m-1)+2j}z). \] For \(0\le\ell\le s-m\), \[ [z^\ell]\Pi_m(z)^{-1} =(-1)^\ell\frac{S_{2m+\ell-1}}{S_\ell S_{2m-1}}. \tag{9} \] For completeness, set \(Q=q^2\), \(a=q^{-(2m-1)}\), and \(f(z)=\prod_{j=0}^{2m-1}(1+aQ^jz)^{-1}\). The identity \((1+aQ^{2m}z)f(Qz)=(1+az)f(z)\) gives, for its coefficients, \[ [z^\ell]f=-a\,\frac{1-Q^{2m+\ell-1}}{1-Q^\ell} [z^{\ell-1}]f. \] No denominator vanishes in the range in question. Replacing \(1-Q^r\) by \(-iq^rs_r\) cancels all powers of \(q\) and proves (9), starting at \([z^0]f=1\). Only Newton indices \(N-m\) with \(m\le s\) contribute to the coefficient of \(z^{s-N}\) in (2). In (8) its coefficient comes from \(\ell=s-m<N\), so the nonconstant terms of \((1-\eta z^N)^2\) do not contribute. Multiply (6), (8), and (9). The sign is \((-1)^{N-m+s-m}=(-1)^{N+s}=\eta(-1)^{s-1}\), independent of \(m\). This proves (3)--(4). All remaining factors are positive: their sine indices lie between \(1\) and \(2s-1\le N-1\), \(w-c_h>0\), and \[ P_N(w)=4\cosh^2(\alpha/2)>0. \tag{10} \] Taking the quotient of consecutive terms proves (5). \(\square\) ## 2. A uniform ratio below the fold Fix \(b<1/2\), put \(z_b=\sin^2(\pi b)<1\) and \(c_b=\cos(\pi b)>0\). For all sufficiently large \(N\), uniformly in real \(\alpha\) and \(1\le m<s\le bN\), \[ 0<\frac{T_{m+1,s,N}}{T_{m,s,N}} \le q_b:=\frac{1+z_b}{2}<1. \tag{11} \] One sufficient level threshold is \[ N\ge\frac{\pi z_b}{c_b(1-z_b)}. \tag{12} \] This is an eventual-level bound on a fixed bulk interval, not a bound uniform up to the moving fold. To prove it, put \(u=m\theta\), \(v=(m+1/2)\theta\), and \(z_s=\sin^2(s\theta)\). Since \(w\ge2\), \(w-c_m\ge4\sin^2v\). The sine products in (5) yield \[ \frac{T_{m+1,s,N}}{T_{m,s,N}} \le \left(\frac{\sin u}{\sin v}\right)^3 \frac{z_s-\sin^2u}{\cos u\cos v}. \tag{13} \] Here \(0<u<v<s\theta\le\pi b\), and \(z_s-\sin^2u\le z_s\cos^2u\). Consequently (13) is at most \[ z_s\frac{\cos u}{\cos v} \le z_b\left(1+\frac{\pi}{2Nc_b}\right), \tag{14} \] because \(\cos u-\cos v\le\theta/2\). Equations (11)--(12) follow. ## 3. Analytic prefix and its nonzero leading coefficient Fix \[ 0<a<b<\tfrac12,\qquad |\alpha|\le A,\quad \alpha\in\mathbb R, \qquad A<\infty. \tag{15} \] Choose \(0<a_0<a<b<b_0<1/2\), and \[ 0<\sigma<\min\{a_0,\tfrac12-b_0\},\qquad M_N=\lfloor\sigma N\rfloor. \tag{16} \] All following assertions are for sufficiently large \(N\), in particular \(M_N\ge1\). Replace the only degree-dependent factorial quotient in (4) by its literal finite product: \[ T_{m,N}(x,\alpha)= \frac{P_N(w)S_{m-1}^{\,4}} {N^4 S_{2m-1}\prod_{h<m}(w-c_h)} \prod_{r=-m+1}^{m-1}2\sin\pi(x+r/N), \] \[ \widehat\beta_N(x,\alpha) =\sum_{m=1}^{M_N}T_{m,N}(x,\alpha). \tag{17} \] Thus no factorial interpolation in \(x\) is used. At physical nodes these are exactly the first \(M_N\) terms of (3). Positivity and (11), applied with \(b_0\), give \[ 0\le \beta_{s,N}-\widehat\beta_N(s/N,\alpha) \le\frac{T_{1,N}(s/N,\alpha)q_{b_0}^{M_N}}{1-q_{b_0}}, \qquad s/N\in[a,b]. \tag{18} \] In particular the relative error is exponentially small, both relative to \(\beta_{s,N}\) and to the prefix. There is a fixed \(h_0>0\), independent of \(N,\alpha\), on which the prefix and all its fixed \(x\)-derivatives are controlled. Here and below one may reduce the real interval slightly from \([a_0,b_0]\) while retaining a neighborhood of \([a,b]\). Indeed its consecutive ratio is the entire-in-\(x\) expression \[ R_{m,N}(x,\alpha)= \frac{4s_m^4\{\sin^2(\pi x)-\sin^2(m\pi/N)\}} {(w-c_m)s_{2m}s_{2m+1}},\qquad m<M_N . \tag{19} \] On the real interval (14) applies even when \(Nx\) is not integral, since \(m+1/2<Nx\) for all large \(N\). The coefficient of the braces in (19) is bounded above by a constant independent of \(m,N\) and real \(\alpha\), by the same sine calculation in (13). The change of \(\sin^2(\pi x)\) under a small imaginary displacement is uniformly \(O(|\Im x|)\). Shrink \(h_0\) so that, on a complex rectangle containing \([a,b]\), \[ |R_{m,N}(x,\alpha)|\le q_1<1 \qquad(m<M_N). \tag{20} \] We can also arrange \(|\sin^2(\pi x)|\le q_1\), enlarging \(q_1<1\) if necessary. The real-part buffer and \(x-m/N>0\) in (16) keep the individual prefix sine factors nonzero there. The following leading coefficient makes the unit assertion precise. For \(|z|<1\), define \[ \mathcal H_\alpha(z)= \sum_{\ell=0}^{\infty}z^\ell \prod_{j=1}^{\ell} \frac{j^3}{(j+\tfrac12) \{(j+\tfrac12)^2+(\alpha/(2\pi))^2\}}, \tag{21} \] with empty product one, and put \[ \mathcal B_\alpha(x)= \frac{4\cosh^2(\alpha/2)\sin(\pi x)} {\pi(\alpha^2+\pi^2)} \mathcal H_\alpha(\sin^2\pi x). \tag{22} \] Every product factor in (21) lies in \((0,1)\) for real \(\alpha\). The series is holomorphic for \(|z|<1\), uniformly for \(\alpha\) in the fixed real compact interval. On real \(0<x<1/2\), \(\mathcal B_\alpha(x)>0\). **Theorem 2.** After reducing the fixed rectangle if necessary, \[ N\widehat\beta_N(x,\alpha) =\mathcal B_\alpha(x)+O_{\rm hol}(N^{-2}), \qquad \frac{c}{N}\le|\widehat\beta_N(x,\alpha)|\le\frac{C}{N}. \tag{23} \] Here \(c,C>0\) are uniform in (15). The holomorphic error notation includes every fixed \(x\)-derivative on smaller fixed rectangles. **Proof.** The first term is \[ T_{1,N}(x,\alpha) =\frac{4\cosh^2(\alpha/2)\,2\sin\pi x} {N^4(2\sin(\pi/N)) \{2\cosh(\alpha/N)-2\cos(\pi/N)\}}, \] so its normalized limit is the factor in front of \(\mathcal H\) in (22), with uniform holomorphic error \(O(N^{-2})\). The fixed-index limiting ratio of (19) is \[ r_m(x,\alpha)= \frac{m^3\sin^2(\pi x)} {(m+\tfrac12)\{(m+\tfrac12)^2+(\alpha/(2\pi))^2\}}. \tag{24} \] Taylor bounds for sine and cosh on the fixed compact ranges give \[ |R_{m,N}-r_m|\le C\frac{(m+1)^2}{N^2}, \qquad 1\le m<M_N . \tag{25} \] To check uniformity through this growing range, divide the sine factors by their linear terms. On \(m/N\le\sigma<1/2\) these quotients and their inverses are uniformly bounded, and their errors from one are \(O((m+1)^2/N^2)\). Similarly \[ 2\cosh(\alpha/N)-2\cos((2m+1)\pi/N) =\frac{\alpha^2+(2m+1)^2\pi^2}{N^2} \{1+O((m+1)^2/N^2)\}. \] Its relative error and inverse are controlled uniformly because the real denominator is positive and sine divided by its argument is bounded below on that interval. Finally the numerator \(\sin^2\pi x-\sin^2(m\pi/N)\) differs from \(\sin^2\pi x\) by \(O(m^2/N^2)\). This proves (25). Both ratio sequences have modulus at most a fixed \(q_1<1\). Telescoping their \(\ell\)-fold products gives the error \[ C N^{-2}(\ell+1)^3 q_1^{\ell-1}. \tag{26} \] Summing this bound and the geometric tail after \(M_N-1\) proves (23)'s expansion. The positive continuous function \(\mathcal B_\alpha\) is bounded below on the real compact set in (15). Its uniformly convergent series and continuity allow a single smaller complex rectangle where it remains bounded away from zero, uniformly in real \(\alpha\). The expansion proves the two-sided bounds in (23). Cauchy's formula on a larger fixed rectangle proves the stated derivative bounds. \(\square\) Thus the positive coefficient has zero extensive action on this bulk interval: after multiplying by \(N\), it has a nonzero bounded analytic limit. This assertion excludes the checkerboard in (3). ## 4. One exact analytic interpolation The exponentially accurate prefix can be made exact without a new extensive phase. This is the localized sinc method of the pinned physical-row interpolation source, here with zero action in the amplitude. We give the estimate in this simpler normalization. Let \(s_0=\lceil Na\rceil\), \(s_1=\lfloor Nb\rfloor\), and \[ d_{s,N}(\alpha)= \beta_{s,N}(\alpha)-\widehat\beta_N(s/N,\alpha). \] By (18) and (23), there are \(C,\kappa>0\) such that \[ |d_{s,N}|\le C N^{-1}e^{-\kappa N}. \tag{27} \] For example, decreasing an exponent if needed, one can take \(\kappa=\sigma|\log q_{b_0}|/2\). Define the finite analytic function \[ \mathfrak b_N(x,\alpha)=\widehat\beta_N(x,\alpha) +\sum_{s=s_0}^{s_1}d_{s,N}(\alpha) \operatorname{sinc}(Nx-s)e^{-N(x-s/N)^2}, \qquad \operatorname{sinc}z=\frac{\sin\pi z}{\pi z}. \tag{28} \] The removable value at zero is one. Hence \[ \mathfrak b_N(s/N,\alpha)=\beta_{s,N}(\alpha) \quad(s_0\le s\le s_1). \tag{29} \] Choose a fixed strip half-height \[ 0<H\le \min\{h_0/2,\ \kappa/(8\pi),\ \sqrt{\kappa/8}\}, \tag{30} \] inside the rectangle where (23) holds, with a fixed real enlargement of \([a,b]\) still included. If \(x=X+iY\), then \[ |\operatorname{sinc}(Nx-s)|\le e^{\pi N|Y|},\qquad |e^{-N(x-s/N)^2}| =e^{-N(X-s/N)^2+NY^2}. \tag{31} \] The first inequality follows from \(\operatorname{sinc}z=\tfrac12\int_{-1}^{1}e^{i\pi zu}\,du\). There are at most \(N\) summands. Dividing their absolute bound by the lower bound \(c/N\) in (23) gives \[ \left|\frac{\mathfrak b_N}{\widehat\beta_N}-1\right| \le CN\exp\{-N(\kappa-\pi|Y|-Y^2)\} \le C e^{-\kappa N/2}. \tag{32} \] Consequently \(\mathfrak b_N\) is a holomorphic unit on this fixed strip for all sufficiently large \(N\), and \[ N\mathfrak b_N(x,\alpha) =\mathcal B_\alpha(x)+O_{\rm hol}(N^{-2}),\qquad c/N\le|\mathfrak b_N|\le C/N . \tag{33} \] Every fixed derivative of the relative error in (32) has the same exponential bound on a smaller fixed strip, by Cauchy. The physical values (29) are exact, not asymptotic. The actual signed coefficient is interpolated by \[ -\eta e^{i\pi Nx}\mathfrak b_N(x,\alpha), \tag{34} \] since its value at \(x=s/N\) is (3). Its checkerboard character has not been absorbed into the bounded amplitude or discarded. For example, for any holomorphic spectator \(f\) and a positively oriented contour \(\Gamma\) in this strip enclosing exactly \(s_0/N,\ldots,s_1/N\), \[ \sum_{s=s_0}^{s_1}b_{N-s,N} f(s/N) =\frac1{2\pi i}\int_\Gamma \frac{2\pi iN}{e^{2\pi iNx}-1} [-\eta e^{i\pi Nx}\mathfrak b_N(x,\alpha)]f(x)\,dx . \tag{35} \] The sampling kernel has residue one at every displayed degree node. Its aliases, the checkerboard, the spectator, and all connector integrals remain in this identity. ## 5. Scope and direct-source readbacks The original ordinary polynomial was used throughout Proposition 1. Thus both parities, including the odd simple physical node, and every physical first normal are retained automatically. The degree variable \(x\) in (28) is an interpolation variable; its derivative is not being substituted for a spectral normal. The theorem concerns a single endpoint kernel and the coefficients with \(s/N\) in a fixed compact subinterval of \((0,1/2)\). It gives no uniform endpoint or fold limit. Fourier coefficients of shared products require their actual convolutions and are not identified with (3). Real bounded \(\alpha\) is the parameter range proved here; no complex-\(\alpha\) unit assertion is needed. Neither positivity of \(\beta\) nor the moderate interpolation estimates the joined central, outer, and vertical source. In particular (35) does not suppress the external degree connectors or imply a filled-action upper bound or scalar noncancellation. The ordinary endpoint bounds and the general localized interpolation method are earlier results. The new input is the exact signed positive Fourier sum, its uniform bulk contraction, and the explicit nonzero analytic symbol for these actual coefficients. The full texts of the following direct sources were read at the displayed matching versions, and their used implications checked: * [Original edge kernel and physical polynomial](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_edge_kernel_difference_and_endpoint_bound.md), SHA256 5d0d07d4d97d82cca66e0e0c3bf2cecad8e5f58ef8329178278b297cf0d6c5da: ordinary Newton normalization and exact physical polynomial (1). * [Coherent full endpoint kernel](research_full_period_endpoint_kernel_reduction.md), SHA256 a1d67ac803c0160bbfdacaa96a6fde9dc1ffae06fc39eb94f0416dcf2ecef76e: placement as the original ordinary endpoint kernel, with its low sector and full radical both retained. * [Exact moderate degree interpolation](research_physical_row_analytic_degree_interpolation.md), SHA256 f7d673e6633c0f46498a6c023512a3c64724d35c53ea168dabbd7f1e59f72d51: the single-strip Gaussian-localized sinc construction and its relative-error budget, specialized and proved in Section 4. Only written proofs, text reads, and hashes were used. No mathematical program, numerical experiment, test, or compilation was run. Previously frozen notes and public manuscripts are unchanged.

title: The original central high band is an exact half-charge source
text:
# The original central high band is an exact half-charge source Private research note, 16 November 2026. Written proof only. The controlled endpoint amplitude is the factor of a literal band of the original Newton kernel. Thus it can be inserted into a coupled graph before any remaining trace is estimated. At even levels the band is a half-charge coupon times one polynomial amplitude. At odd levels it is the difference of the two neighboring lattice half-charge coupons times that same amplitude. The omitted high band has explicit macroscopic physical support and polynomial coefficient cost. The low endpoint coupon remains separate. ## 1. Original conventions and the ordinary polynomial identity For \(N\ge2\), put \(D=N-1\), \(m=\lfloor N/2floor\), \(k_0=N-m\), \(\eta=(-1)^D\), and \(	heta=\pi/N\). Retain \[ s_j=2\sin(j	heta),\quad S_j=\prod_{h=1}^j s_h,\quad c_a=2\cos((2a+1)	heta),\quad e_k(z)=S_k^{-2}\prod_{h<k}(c_h-z), \] \[ P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2,\qquad \phi_N(f)=\eta N^2[z^D]\operatorname{rem}_{P_N}f,\qquad w_N(\alpha)=2\cosh(\alpha/N). 	ag{1} \] The source charge coupon \(\mathcal C_{N,\chi}\) has the full Hermite data of \(\cos(N(1-\chi)t)\) under \(z=-2\cos t\). For an integer \(j=N(1-\chi)\) with \(0\le j\le D\), it is the ordinary polynomial \(T_j(-z/2)\). Values and normals both agree, and the odd simple node has value one. For \(0\le L\le m-1\), define the original central high band \[ B^{[L]}_{N,\alpha}(z)= \sum_{l=0}^L e_{k_0+l}(w_N(\alpha))e_{k_0+l}(z). 	ag{2} \] Use the exact ratios and polynomial amplitude \[ (A_l,B_l)=  egin{cases} ((l+	frac12)	heta,(l+1)	heta),&N\ {m even},\ ((l+1)	heta,(l+	frac32)	heta),&N\ {m odd}, \end{cases} \] \[ ho_{l,N}(\alpha,t)=  rac{[\cos^2 A_l+\sinh^2(\alpha/(2N))] [\sin^2(t/2)-\sin^2 A_l]}{\cos^4 B_l}, \quad H_{N,L}(\alpha,t)= \sum_{l=0}^L\prod_{j=0}^{l-1}ho_{j,N}(\alpha,t). 	ag{3} \] Because \(\sin^2(t/2)=(z+2)/4\), this is an ordinary polynomial of degree at most \(L\) in \(z\); denote it by \(\mathcal H_{N,L,\alpha}(z)\). Its denominators are nonzero for all ratios actually used in (3). **Theorem 1 (ordinary band factorization).** Exactly as ordinary polynomials, before any physical quotient, \[ B^{[L]}_{N,\alpha}=  egin{cases} \displaystyle d_{N,\alpha}\, \mathcal C_{N,1/2}\mathcal H_{N,L,\alpha}, &N=2m,\[3pt] \displaystyle d_{N,\alpha}  igl(\mathcal C_{N,(m+1)/N} -\mathcal C_{N,m/N} igr) \mathcal H_{N,L,\alpha},&N=2m+1, \end{cases} 	ag{4} \] where \[ d_{N,\alpha}=  egin{cases} \displaystyle rac{(-1)^m\cosh(\alpha/2)}{N^2},&N=2m,\[3pt] \displaystyle rac{(-1)^m\cosh(\alpha/2)\cosh(\alpha/(2N))} {2N^2\cos^4(	heta/2)},&N=2m+1. \end{cases} 	ag{5} \] *Proof.* Consecutive Newton products give \[  rac{e_{k_0+l+1}(w)e_{k_0+l+1}(z)} {e_{k_0+l}(w)e_{k_0+l}(z)} = rac{(c_{k_0+l}-w)(c_{k_0+l}-z)} {s_{k_0+l+1}^4}. 	ag{6} \] The two minus signs multiply to plus. Put \(r=m-1-l\). Then \(c_{k_0+l}=c_r\) and \(s_{k_0+l+1}=s_r\). Substitution of \(w=w_N(\alpha)\), \(z=-2\cos t\) turns (6) into (3). Ratio statements are polynomial multiplicative identities, including at zeros. The distinct-root products of \(P_N\) and the sine products \(S_m^2=2N\) (even), \(S_m^2=N\) (odd), give \[ e_{k_0}(-2\cos t)=  egin{cases} \cos(Nt/2)/N,&N=2m,\ -[\cos(mt)-\cos((m+1)t)]/[2N\cos^2(	heta/2)], &N=2m+1, \end{cases} 	ag{7} \] and \[ (-1)^{k_0}e_{k_0}(w_N(\alpha))=  egin{cases} \cosh(\alpha/2)/N,&N=2m,\ \cosh(\alpha/2)\cosh(\alpha/(2N)) /[N\cos^2(	heta/2)],&N=2m+1. \end{cases} 	ag{8} \] For the odd identity use \(\cos(mt)-\cos((m+1)t)=2\sin(Nt/2)\sin(t/2)\); it includes the simple root at \(t=0\). Equations (6)--(8) prove (4). Its degree is at most \(k_0+L\le D\), so no hidden reduction or discarded normal occurs. \(\square\) ## 2. The omitted band has only macroscopic physical support The full high coupon and its omitted band are \[ B^{m high}_{N,\alpha} =\sum_{r=0}^{m-1}e_{D-r}(w_N(\alpha))e_{D-r}(z), \qquad E^{[L]}_{N,\alpha} =B^{m high}_{N,\alpha}-B^{[L]}_{N,\alpha}. 	ag{9} \] Set \(r_*=m-L-2\). If \(r_*<0\), \(E^{[L]}=0\). Otherwise the original radical contraction gives \[ \phi_N(R_nE^{[L]}_{N,\alpha}f) =\sum_{a=0}^{r_*}\omega_{a,N,L}(\alpha) R_n(c_a)f(c_a), \] \[ \omega_{a,N,L}(\alpha)= \sum_{r=a}^{r_*}e_{D-r}(w_N(\alpha))b_{ra},\qquad b_{ra}=(-1)^{r+a}  rac{s_{2a+1}S_r^2}{S_{r-a}S_{r+a+1}}. 	ag{10} \] Here \(R_n\) is the original crossing at integer powers and its canonical full-Hermite real-power extension otherwise, with the original scalar retained. At real \(n\), \(|R_n(c_a)|=1\). The surviving angles necessarily satisfy \[ 	au_a=(D-2a)	heta\ \ge\  egin{cases} (2L+3)	heta,&N\ {m even},\ (2L+4)	heta,&N\ {m odd}. \end{cases} 	ag{11} \] Thus \(L=\lfloor\delta Nfloor\), \(0<\delta<1/2\), removes only physical rows at angles tending to at least \(2\pi\delta\). Uniformly on every bounded complex \(\alpha\)-set, \[ |\omega_{a,N,L}(\alpha)|\le C N^{3/2},\qquad \sum_a|\omega_{a,N,L}(\alpha)| \le C N^{5/2}. 	ag{12} \] Indeed the full-radical source proves \(|b_{ra}|\le2\) and \[ |e_{D-r}(-2\cos t)|\le\sqrt{N-1}e^{D|\Im t|}. 	ag{13} \] Take \(t=\pi-i\alpha/N\), and sum at most \(m\) terms in each coefficient. The finite exceptional level \(N=2\) is immediate; its omitted band is empty. Every derivative in a free exterior variable commutes with (10), without a new coefficient cost. The trace in (10) still includes its original normal. Since the radical value is zero, that normal differentiates the radical, and only the spectator value survives. The odd simple value vanishes. No value-only substitute for a full trace is assumed. ## 3. Exact assembly inside an arbitrary coupled graph Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite original graph, \(S\) its traced vertices, and \(T\subseteq S\) a set of vertices receiving one chosen high endpoint coupon each. Set \[ F_N(\mathbf z)=A_N(\mathbf z)\prod_{vw\in E}K_N(z_v,z_w), 	ag{14} \] where \(A_N\) is any joint polynomial spectator. It may contain additional fixed coupons at the same vertices. Every edge is kept once, and outside variables remain ordinary free variables or their prescribed values. At \(T\) start with unit charge; at \(S\setminus T\) retain arbitrary original charges \(\chi_v\). Write \[ Z_{m band}= \left(\prod_{v\in S}\phi_N^{(z_v)}ight) \left[ F_N\prod_{v\in S}R_{n_v}(z_v) \prod_{v\in S\setminus T}\mathcal C_{N,\chi_v}(z_v) \prod_{v\in T}B^{[L]}_{N,\alpha_v}(z_v) ight]. 	ag{15} \] Equation (4) gives an exact source formula. At even levels it is \(\prod_{v\in T}d_{N,\alpha_v}\) times the same graph source with charges \(1/2\) at \(T\) and common inserted spectator \[ F_N\prod_{v\in T}\mathcal H_{N,L,\alpha_v}(z_v). 	ag{16} \] At odd levels it is that same scalar times the sum over \(\epsilon\in\{+,-\}^{T}\), with sign \((-1)^{\#\{v:\epsilon_v=-\}}\), of the same sources (16), with charges \[ \chi_v^+=(m+1)/N=	frac12+	frac1{2N},\qquad \chi_v^-=m/N=	frac12-	frac1{2N}\quad(v\in T). 	ag{17} \] All remaining charges, full traces, powers, carriers, shared edges and spectator factors stay exactly as written. Parameters in \(A_N\) are held fixed when comparing the indicated charges. No independent-neighbor or product-spectator assumption enters the identity. There is also a bound for restoring the entire high coupon which retains actual coherent reduced sources. Define \(Z_{m high}\) by replacing every band in (15) with its full high coupon. For \(\varnothing
e U\subseteq T\), define \(\mathscr Z_U(\mathbf a)\) by evaluating \(z_v=c_{a_v}\) for \(v\in U\) in (14), retaining every resulting kernel and shared spectator, and taking all original traces over \(S\setminus U\). Those traces keep the original powers and charges and the band coupons at \(T\setminus U\). The factors \(R_{n_v}(c_{a_v})\) for \(v\in U\) are kept outside this definition. Expansion of (9), followed by (10), gives exactly \[ Z_{m high}-Z_{m band} =\sum_{\varnothing
e U\subseteq T}\ \sum_{0\le a_v\le r_*} \left[\prod_{v\in U} \omega_{a_v,N,L}(\alpha_v)R_{n_v}(c_{a_v})ight] \mathscr Z_U(\mathbf a). 	ag{18} \] Consequently, for real powers and bounded microscopic parameters, \[ |Z_{m high}-Z_{m band}| \le\sum_{\varnothing
e U\subseteq T} (C N^{5/2})^{|U|} \max_{0\le a_v\le r_*}|\mathscr Z_U(\mathbf a)|. 	ag{19} \] An empty tail contributes zero. Fixed ordinary outside derivatives satisfy the identical statement with the corresponding derivatives of \(\mathscr Z_U\). In particular edges joining two evaluated vertices remain \(K_N(c_{a_v},c_{a_w})\); edges to surviving traces remain their original physical-boundary kernels. Equation (19) does not replace them by an unfilled absolute spectator. ## 4. Analytic use and its precise remaining scope For \(L=\lfloor\delta Nfloor\), the adopted general-domain theorem gives, uniformly with all fixed derivatives on compact subsets of \[ |\cos t-\cos(2\pi\delta)|<1+\cos(2\pi\delta), \qquad H_{N,L}(\alpha,t)=\sec^2(t/2)+O_{m hol}(N^{-2}). 	ag{20} \] The normalized polynomial amplitude is therefore a unit there for large \(N\). The scalar (5) also is a unit after its \(N^{-2}\) factor is removed on compact \(\alpha\)-sets avoiding \(\cosh(\alpha/2)=0\). For \(\delta=1/8\), the entire closed rectangle \(|\Re t|\le\pi/4,\ |\Im t|\le\log3\) lies in this domain. Thus (15)--(17) put the band into actual original near-half-charge sources with a common controlled local multiplier. This is stronger than identifying a formal off-grid phase or merely matching central physical values. At odd levels the difference in (17) must remain coherent. Its cosine factor is exactly \(2\sin(Nt/2)\sin(t/2)\); at even levels the factor is \(\cos(Nt/2)\). Their insertion in the original double-pole horizontal trace cancels one denominator factor, giving the same simple-pole half-charge kernel as in the amplitude theorem. All original vertical terms are still present. The theorem does not bound the full near-half-charge sources, prove a gap for the physical sources in (19), or compare their combined rate with the filled action. It also does not factor the low part of \(K_N(w_N(\alpha),z)\) through a radical charge coupon. Combining that low part with (18), and controlling the remaining full graph source, are separate tasks. ## 5. Direct source versions All three complete direct proofs were read at the following versions; the implications used above and their hashes were checked. * [Full high Newton radical](research_high_newton_radical_contraction.md), SHA256 1faa5d2e02edf0a1462cc43b243e0ab4403bf56e9f1af0befb6b492441d9dd03: original Newton data, full trace, coefficients (5)--(6), bounds (12), and the full Fourier estimate (34)--(36). * [Endpoint general domain](research_endpoint_radical_general_domain.md), SHA256 600ae0d78f29946272ed54b600cb1f5fdf170965985a08d6e3d9201303722074: exact lowering amplitude, its compact-domain symbol and the rectangle used in (20). * [Full-period current charge convolution](research_full_period_current_charge_convolution.md), SHA256 3f74b9824ecbf0b71a79b17959c7208f650103f95932192cfba87c7a7aa05595: original cosine coupons and real-power carriers, full-Hermite charge substitution, and full-survivor source placement.

title: When an endpoint current has an original angle-boundary action
text:
# When an endpoint current has an original angle-boundary action Private written proof, 15 November 2026. The exact grouped endpoint current deletes vertices and decorates the remaining forest with full Ward coupons. Its deleted-forest action is not automatically a boundary value of the original constrained angle problem. There is an explicit necessary and sufficient condition for the endpoint-pinned boundary realization that preserves the surviving angle data. When it holds, the action comparison is exact and the original convex minimum gives a strict gap. The condition can fail at positive primitive fillings. Its failure does not prove that the current has a larger action; it identifies why the proposed boundary-value proof cannot cover all currents. No quantum contour or scalar asymptotic is inferred from the angle comparison alone. ## 1. The original polytope and the deleted angle assignment Let \(G\) be the original finite circle tree, with selected vertices \(S\), fixed full outside angles \(t_b=s_b+i h_b\), and signed integer powers \(n_v\). Include every edge incident to \(S\), counted once, and suppose each selected vertex has positive original degree. The full primitive equations are assumed to have a positive solution in the original edge decomposition. Use the original real angle variables \(s_v=\Re t_v\) and \(g_{v,e}=\Im r_{v,e}\). The closed angle polytope is given by \[ |s_v|+2|g_{w,e}|\leq\pi,\qquad |s_w|+2|g_{v,e}|\leq\pi \quad(e=\{v,w\}), 	ag{1} \] \[ \sum_{e
i v}g_{v,e}- rac{n_v}{2}s_v=-\pi \quad(v\in S). 	ag{2} \] The prescribed outside \(s_b\)'s are unchanged. The original energy is \[ \mathcal E_G =4\sum_e(E_{P,e}+E_{Q,e}) -\sum_{b
otin S}h_b\sum_{e
i b}g_{b,e}. 	ag{3} \] The square coordinates and their energy are those of the pinned convex variation theorem. In particular, if \(v\) is the first endpoint, \[ A_P=s_v/4-g_{w,e}/2,\quad A_Q=s_v/4+g_{w,e}/2,\qquad y_P=g_{v,e}/2+s_w/4,\quad y_Q=g_{v,e}/2-s_w/4. 	ag{4} \] Let \(z_0\) be the positive full solution, \(m\) the number of included edges, and \(M_G\) its calibrated real action. The existing theorems give \[ M_G=mM_\infty-\mathcal E_G(z_0)/\pi,\qquad \Delta_G=\min_{\partial\mathcal P_G}\mathcal E_G -\mathcal E_G(z_0)>0. 	ag{5} \] Here \(M_\infty=\psi(0,0)=4G_{m Cat}/\pi\), where \(G_{m Cat}=\sum_{j\geq0}(-1)^j/(2j+1)^2\). The boundary and interior are relative to the original affine constraint space. Fix a nonempty removed set \(C\subseteq S\). Delete every edge incident to \(C\), and let \(r\) be the number of deleted edges. Retain an angle assignment \(z'\) on the resulting forest that satisfies its weak edge inequalities and all its surviving primitive rows, with \(|s_w|\leq\pi\) at every surviving vertex, including isolated ones. All surviving real angles, incidence variables and outside data are prescribed by \(z'\). An isolated surviving vertex must still satisfy its row (2) with an empty incidence sum; it is not silently removed. If these conditions have no solution, there is no assignment \(z'\) to which the theorem applies. A degenerate assignment is given only its angle-energy value (16), not a geometric or quantum action without further justification. For a removed vertex let \[ d_C(v)=\#\{e=\{v,w\}:w
otin C\},\qquad L_v(z')=\sum_{\substack{e=\{v,w\}\w
otin C}} (1-|s_w|/\pi). 	ag{6} \] All incidences in this sum are counted individually, including those to prescribed outside vertices. ## 2. Exact feasibility of the endpoint face The actual current is supported at \(c_0=2\cos(\pi/N)\) in the original spectral coordinate \(c=-2\cos t\). Its two real angular endpoints tend to \(s=\pi\) and \(s=-\pi\). Keep a specified sign \(\varepsilon_v\in\{-1,1\}\) at each removed vertex. **Theorem 1.** There is an extension \(\widetilde z\) of \(z'\) to the original closed polytope, with \[ s_v=\varepsilon_v\pi\quad(v\in C), 	ag{7} \] if and only if \[ |\varepsilon_v n_v-2|\leq L_v(z') \quad(v\in C). 	ag{8} \] Here an extension retains all surviving coordinates and all original rows (2). If the endpoint signs may be chosen independently, the equivalent condition is \[  oxed{\qquad  igl||n_v|-2 igr| +\sum_{\substack{e=\{v,w\}\w
otin C}}|s_w|/\pi \leq d_C(v)\quad(v\in C). \qquad} 	ag{9} \] **Proof.** Equation (1) at a removed endpoint immediately forces \[ g_{w,e}=0 \quad\hbox{whenever }v\in C,\ e=\{v,w\}. 	ag{10} \] Consequently both incidences of an internal \(C\)-edge are zero. At a surviving vertex every restored incidence is zero, so its old primitive row remains exactly the deleted-forest row. At \(v\in C\), the only adjustable incidences are on its edges to \(w
otin C\). Independently, each has the allowed closed interval \[ - rac{\pi-|s_w|}{2}\leq g_{v,e} \leq rac{\pi-|s_w|}{2}. 	ag{11} \] Its primitive row requires \[ \sum_{\substack{e
i v\e
otin E(C)}}g_{v,e} = rac\pi2(\varepsilon_v n_v-2). 	ag{12} \] The sum of the intervals (11) is the closed interval with endpoint magnitudes \(\pi L_v/2\). Thus (12) is possible exactly when (8) holds. These choices are independent for different removed vertices, even if they share a surviving neighbor: the opposite incidences at that neighbor have already been fixed to zero. This proves both necessity and sufficiency, including equality and \(d_C(v)=0\). Finally \(\min_{\varepsilon=\pm1}|\varepsilon n-2|=||n|-2|\). Since the signs have no further coupling, this proves (9). \(\square\) This theorem concerns an angle-boundary value. It does not assert a matched complex degeneration along which every reconstructed imaginary angle remains the prescribed one. At corner squares those reconstructions can depend on the approach. Such a complex path is unnecessary for the energy comparison below and is not supplied by the theorem. ## 3. The exact boundary energy and the strict action gap The absolute energy of a removed edge is fixed, not an estimate. **Lemma 2.** The square energy is constant on its entire boundary, with value \[ E_\square ig|_{\partial[-\pi/4,\pi/4]^2} =G_{m Cat}/2=\pi M_\infty/8. 	ag{13} \] **Proof.** On an open vertical side the derivative in the side direction is the continuous limit \[ E_y(A,y)=	frac12\operatorname{arsinh} (	an(2y)\cos(2A))\longrightarrow0. 	ag{14} \] The convergence is uniform on compact subintervals of that side, so integrating before taking the limit shows that its value is constant. The same argument works on a horizontal side. The established continuous extension to the closed square joins their constants at the corners. At \(y=0\), integrate the other original derivative: \[  egin{split} E_\square(\pi/4,0) &= rac12\int_0^{\pi/4}\operatorname{arsinh}(	an(2A))\,dA\ &= rac14\int_0^{\pi/2}\log(\sec u+	an u)\,du = rac12\int_{\pi/4}^{\pi/2}\log	an v\,dv =G_{m Cat}/2. \end{split} 	ag{15} \] The last equality follows by reflection from \(\int_0^{\pi/4}\log	an v\,dv=-G_{m Cat}\). For instance, integrate the Abel-regularized sine/cosine logarithm series and then let its regularization tend to one; the integrated series is absolutely convergent. The normalization of \(M_\infty\) in (5) gives the second equality in (13). \(\square\) Let \(\mathcal E_{G\setminus C}(z')\) denote the sum (3) over surviving edges, with the same outside term on those edges, and put \[ \mathcal M_{G\setminus C}(z') =(m-r)M_\infty-\mathcal E_{G\setminus C}(z')/\pi. 	ag{16} \] This definition is an angle-energy value; no stationary or quantum interpretation is assumed at a general \(z'\). **Theorem 3.** Whenever (8) holds, every extension constructed in Theorem 1 satisfies the exact identity \[ \mathcal E_G(\widetilde z) =\mathcal E_{G\setminus C}(z')+r\pi M_\infty. 	ag{17} \] Consequently \[  oxed{\qquad \mathcal M_{G\setminus C}(z') \leq M_G-\Delta_G/\pi<M_G . \qquad} 	ag{18} \] If \(z'\) is a positive primitive solution of the deleted forest, with its original outside data, then (16) is its actual calibrated classical action. Thus (18) is a strict geometric-action comparison in that case. **Proof.** Every deleted edge has at least one removed endpoint. If that endpoint is first in (4), equations (7) and (10) put both square \(A\)-coordinates on the boundary. If it is second, both square \(y\)-coordinates are on the boundary. Lemma 2 therefore gives \[ 4(E_{P,e}+E_{Q,e})=\pi M_\infty 	ag{19} \] for each deleted edge, including an edge with two removed endpoints. Every surviving square is unchanged. Any original outside incidence on a deleted edge is zero by (10), so the outside linear term in (3) loses exactly zero. Summing proves (17). Because \(C
e\varnothing\) and its vertices have positive original degree, at least one square of \(\widetilde z\) lies on its boundary. The full original polytope has an interior positive solution. Hence \(\widetilde z\in\partial\mathcal P_G\), and (5) gives \(\mathcal E_G(\widetilde z)\geq\mathcal E_G(z_0)+\Delta_G\). Combining this with (17) gives (18). For a positive deleted-forest solution, the pinned action-energy identity identifies (16) with its actual action, with the unchanged outside imaginary-angle term. An isolated surviving vertex, if present, has period equation \(n_vt_v=2\pi\). Thus \(n_v
e0\), its \(t_v\) is real and its crossing-plus-charge action is purely imaginary; it contributes zero to both sides of (16). This observation does not supply its quantum asymptotic. \(\square\) ## 4. What this says about the grouped original currents The actual finite source identity is kept before making a comparison. For the removed set \(C\), its simultaneous one-step Ward insertions give exactly \[ \mathcal E_{C,N}(\mathbf w)= \sum_{\substack{M\subset E(C_{m odd})\M\ {m matching}}} d_N^{|M|}\prod_{v\in C\setminus V(M)}A_v(\mathbf w), 	ag{20} \] with the original monomers, outside coupons \(T\Pi_0\), and \(d_N=s_1^2(N^2-1)/3\) from the grouped-current theorem. All first and mixed normals are included, and shared outside variables remain shared. Multiplying (20) by the original exterior and performing its prescribed traces is the exact current. The removed crossing carriers are the original modulus-one units. This is the specified simultaneous one-step current. An arbitrary logarithmic-window translation or other relative-cycle defect is not identified with (20). An even zero power makes this particular current identically zero. Otherwise the matching boundary-unit theorem proves that (20) is a unit at every full physical boundary assignment for \(N\geq3\), with polynomially bounded inverse mixed normals. Thus a failure of the angle-face condition is not explained by algebraic vanishing of the grouped current. If a complete contour theorem for the deleted exterior already justifies the full Ward representatives and its selected nonzero packet, Section 3 of the grouped-current theorem gives a nonzero common-phase leading coefficient for (20). Its extra factors are powers of \(\log N\) and fixed powers of \(N\); its exponential action is the deleted exterior's action. When that action satisfies the endpoint-face test, (18) then puts this packet strictly below the original positive action. A whole-current bound still requires the stated exterior contour and complement bounds. In particular, ordinary free-boundary polynomial evaluation is not replaced by a different Hermite representative without its original trace adapter. The endpoint-face test is not automatic. It is already impossible if, for one removed vertex, \[ |n_v|>d_C(v)+2. 	ag{21} \] This failure occurs within the original positive geometry: the isolated positive-branch theorem recalled in the pinned action note applies for \(d+|n|>2\), whereas removing that selected vertex with \(|n|>d+2\) violates (9) for every endpoint sign. This observation is only a nonvacuity check of the face obstruction, not an action-gap counterexample or a new knot case. More generally the actual neighboring real angles enter (9), so even the degree inequality alone is insufficient. Internal edges of the removed set provide no capacity in (12): both of their incidences are forced zero. These are constraints of the original primitive rows and original endpoint support, not a norm estimate. Thus one cannot identify every decorated deleted forest with the endpoint boundary of the original constrained problem and invoke convexity without a test. Failure of (9) does not disprove a strict action gap obtained by another argument. Nor does the boundary identity construct the relative contour, bound other lattice modes, or establish the desired arbitrary-short-filling volume theorem. ## Direct sources The complete written proofs below were read; archived numerical records and computational instructions are not used. * [Grouped endpoint currents](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_grouped_endpoint_current_matchings.md), SHA256 \(	exttt{4047782f665e9e6631e73aac42d55057d6f3cd5ae1e813d89111a0a5caaa21bb}\): exact original endpoint support, simultaneous matching polynomial, and the stated controlled-exterior leading-coefficient theorem. * [Original convex filling problem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_positive_filling_convex_variation.md), SHA256 \(	exttt{2777b2bcb149d64a79757ba64ccb16be5438cf37ce820ad50c5f532afd8fc6c0}\): square derivatives, original angle inequalities and primitive rows, continuous boundary energy and strict interior minimum. * [Calibrated inverse-period energy](research_positive_period_inverse_descent.md), SHA256 \(	exttt{b9b5c3d61c704700e9431315cf50591c921ebeb95becdf6a52877606bdbc4565}\): action-energy identity with full outside data and the positive original boundary gap \(\Delta_G\). * [Full boundary current unit](research_endpoint_matching_boundary_unit.md), SHA256 \(	exttt{ce79146b4a69206ec3daef0f6cd6db73ac2fc99ad88f61499b58b67bdbc6889f}\): all-node nonvanishing and the polynomial inverse including mixed first normals, with its prescribed-closing limitation. * [Original isolated action normalization](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_isolated_vertex_action_gap.md), SHA256 \(	exttt{106edadc0c02b086af35d594566b086df7cb55d2491418622e30213726bed7d5}\): the original value \(M_\infty=4G_{m Cat}/\pi\) and the recalled positive isolated branch used only to check that (21) is nonvacuous. Only written mathematics, text reads and file hashes are used. No mathematical execution, numerical evaluation, tests or compilation were performed. Other notes and frozen or public files are unchanged.

title: Endpoint asymptotics on a fixed complex neighborhood
text:
# Endpoint asymptotics on a fixed complex neighborhood Private written proof, 16 November 2026. The bulk value formula extends to a fixed, sufficiently thin complex neighborhood after reducing its power saving. Combined with the exact scalar compatibility theorem, this gives an asymptotic formula for one representative of the actual values and first spectral derivatives. At the complete endpoint its leading factor is a holomorphic unit. The same remains true in a specified shrinking neighborhood of that endpoint. This is a local statement; it does not supply the coefficient of a geometric cycle in the whole original trace. ## 1. A quantitative continuation lemma Let \(a<b\), \(H>0\), and let \(r_N\) be holomorphic on a neighborhood of the closed rectangle \[ a\le\Re z\le b,\qquad |\Im z|\le H. \] Suppose, uniformly in any additional real parameters, \[ |r_N(z)|\le C N^P,\qquad |r_N(x)|\le C N^{-q}\quad(a\le x\le b), \qquad P\ge0,\quad q>0. 	ag{1} \] Enlarge the common constant \(C\) if necessary. Fix \(0<d<(b-a)/2\) and \(0<\lambda<q\). Set \[ B= rac1H+ rac4{\pi d},\qquad h=\min\left\{ rac H2, rac{\lambda}{B(P+q)}ight\}. 	ag{2} \] Then \[ |r_N(x+iy)|\le C N^{-q+\lambda} \quad(a+d\le x\le b-d,\ |y|\le h). 	ag{3} \] On any smaller rectangle, every fixed complex derivative has the same bound, with a derivative-dependent constant. Here is a direct barrier proof. In the upper rectangle define \[ w(x,y)= rac yH+ rac2\pi \left\{\arctan rac y{x-a} +\arctan rac y{b-x}ight\}. 	ag{4} \] The two arctangents are arguments of nonvanishing linear functions in their respective half-planes; both are harmonic. Thus \(w\) is harmonic. It vanishes on the open bottom edge, is at least one on each other edge, and is nonnegative. The subharmonic function \[ \log|r_N|-\log C+q\log N-(P+q)(\log N)w \] has nonpositive boundary upper limits. At a bottom corner this also holds by continuity of \(r_N\), since its value there satisfies the second bound in (1). The maximum principle therefore gives \[ |r_N(x+iy)| \le C N^{-q+(P+q)w(x,y)}. 	ag{5} \] For the indicated buffered real parts, \[ w(x,y)\le y\left( rac1H+ rac2\pi \left\{ rac1{x-a}+ rac1{b-x}ight\}ight) \le By . \] This proves (3) above the real axis; reflection gives the lower half. Cauchy's formula on fixed-radius disks in a smaller rectangle proves the derivative assertion. Zeros of \(r_N\) are harmless in the subharmonic argument. In particular, if \(q=1+\epsilon\), a fixed strip can retain the bound \(O(N^{-1-\epsilon/2})\), by taking \(\lambda=\epsilon/2\). A strip of width \(1/\log N\) is useful for keeping the original exponent without loss; it is unnecessary when a smaller positive power saving suffices. ## 2. The actual endpoint representative Retain the original notation \[  egin{gathered} c_j=2\cos((2j+1)\pi/N),\qquad c_N(x)=2\cos(2\pi x+\pi/N),\ w_N(\alpha)=2\cosh(\alpha/N),\qquad K_N(w,Z)=\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}e_k(w)e_k(Z),\ S_N(x)= rac N\pi\sin(\pi x). \end{gathered} 	ag{6} \] The \(e_k\) are the original normalized Newton polynomials. Fix a closed interval \(I\Subset(0,1/2)\) and a compact real parameter interval \(|\alpha|\le A\). The scalar compatibility theorem supplies, on a fixed complex neighborhood of a slightly larger real interval, a polynomially bounded holomorphic function \(h_N(x,\alpha)\) with \[  egin{split} h_N(j/N,\alpha)&=K_N(w_N(\alpha),c_j),\ \partial_xh_N(j/N,\alpha) &=c_N'(j/N)\partial_ZK_N(w_N(\alpha),c_j). \end{split} 	ag{7} \] It is jointly holomorphic in bounded complex endpoint parameters. For the asymptotic assertion below the parameters are real. Put \(
u=\alpha/\pi\), and set \[ k_\pm(
u)= rac{\Gamma(\pm i
u)} {\Gamma(1/2\pm i
u/2)^4},\quad C_0(
u)=k_+(
u)+k_-(
u),\quad C_1(
u)=i
u(k_+(
u)-k_-(
u)). 	ag{8} \] The two \(C_i\) are regular and even at zero, with \[ C_0(0)= rac{2(\gamma_E+4\log2)}{\pi^2}, \qquad C_1(0)= rac2{\pi^2}. \] Define, using the removable value of \(\sin(
u\log s)/
u\), \[ g_\alpha(s)= rac1s \left\{C_0(
u)\cos(
u\log s) +C_1(
u) rac{\sin(
u\log s)}{
u}ight\}. 	ag{9} \] For \(s=S_N(x)\), choose \(\log\sin(\pi x)\) to be real on the real interval. It has a single holomorphic branch on a sufficiently small fixed neighborhood of that interval. **Theorem 1.** There exist a fixed complex neighborhood \(U\) of \(I\) and \(\epsilon_*>0\) such that, for real \(|\alpha|\le A\), \[ h_N(x,\alpha)=g_\alpha(S_N(x))+O(N^{-1-\epsilon_*}) \quad(x\in U). 	ag{10} \] The error is holomorphic in \(x\). Every fixed \(x\)-derivative has the same bound on smaller fixed neighborhoods. Both level parities are included. The neighborhood can be thin, and its size is not a claim about the location of a geometric critical point. *Proof.* The value connection theorem applies to \(h_N\), since it is a moderate exact value interpolation. On a buffered real interval containing \(I\) it gives \[ h_N(x,\alpha)-g_\alpha(S_N(x)) =O(N^{-1-\epsilon}) 	ag{11} \] for some \(\epsilon>0\), uniformly for the stated real parameters. On a fixed larger rectangle \(h_N\) has a bound \(CN^P\). On that same rectangle the second term is \(O_A((1+\log N)/N)\): the imaginary part of \(\log S_N(x)\) is bounded, \(
u\) is real and bounded, and the removable expression in (9) costs at most \(C_A(1+\log N)\). Thus their difference satisfies (1), with \(q=1+\epsilon\) and some \(P\ge0\). Apply (2)--(3) with \(\lambda=\epsilon/2\), then shrink the rectangle to retain fixed derivative buffers. This proves (10) with \(\epsilon_*=\epsilon/2\). No off-real small-error estimate from the value theorem was assumed. \(\square\) At the physical nodes, (7) and (10) give the actual spectral derivative, by division by \[ c_N'(x)=-4\pi\sin(2\pi x+\pi/N), \] which is uniformly nonzero on a smaller fixed bulk neighborhood. Thus the result does not concern a substitute derivative obtained by moving recurrence coefficients. ## 3. A nonzero factor near the complete endpoint Write \(\operatorname{sinc}u=\sin u/u\), with \(\operatorname{sinc}0=1\). Let \( eta\) be real and range over a fixed bounded interval, and put \[ \alpha_N= rac{ eta}{\log N}. \] On the fixed complex neighborhood from Theorem 1, \[ h_N(x,\alpha_N)=  rac{2\log N}{\pi N\sin(\pi x)} \operatorname{sinc}( eta/\pi) +O(N^{-1}). 	ag{12} \] All fixed \(x\)-derivatives have the same additive error on smaller neighborhoods, uniformly for bounded real \( eta\). To prove this, put \(\lambda(x)=\log(\sin(\pi x)/\pi)\), so \(\log S_N(x)=\log N+\lambda(x)\). In (9), \(
u= eta/(\pi\log N)\), and analyticity at zero gives \[  egin{split} C_0(
u)&=C_0(0)+O((\log N)^{-2}),\ C_1(
u)&=2/\pi^2+O((\log N)^{-2}),\  rac{\sin(
u\log S_N(x))}{
u} &=(\log N)\operatorname{sinc}( eta/\pi) +\lambda(x)\cos( eta/\pi) +O((\log N)^{-1}). \end{split} \] The last expansion is uniform also at \( eta=0\), by its entire power series. Substitution proves (12), including the derivative bounds. If \(| eta|\le B<\pi^2\), the real factor \(\operatorname{sinc}( eta/\pi)\) is positive and bounded away from zero. Consequently \[ h_N(x, eta/\log N)=  rac{2\log N}{\pi N\sin(\pi x)} \operatorname{sinc}( eta/\pi) \{1+O_{\mathrm{hol}}((\log N)^{-1})\}. 	ag{13} \] For all large \(N\) this is a holomorphic unit on a smaller neighborhood. At \( eta=0\) it applies to the complete endpoint \(w_N(0)=2\). For any fixed number \(r\) of factors sharing the same variable, their ordinary product therefore satisfies \[ \prod_{i=1}^r h_N(x, eta_i/\log N) =\left( rac{2\log N}{\pi N\sin(\pi x)}ight)^r \prod_{i=1}^r\operatorname{sinc}( eta_i/\pi) \{1+O_{\mathrm{hol}}((\log N)^{-1})\}, 	ag{14} \] uniformly for \(| eta_i|\le B<\pi^2\). It retains the original shared first normal by the product rule and (7). The analogous product over finitely many variables retains every mixed first normal. No spectral variable is reduced before its actual closing functional is applied. For fixed nonzero real \(\alpha\), Theorem 1 still applies, but the leading expression (9) oscillates in \(\log N\). Equation (13) is not extended to those parameters. In particular no nonvanishing assertion is made at the first zeros \( eta=\pm\pi^2\). ## 4. What this proves for a local saddle integral There is a useful precise consequence of (14). Suppose a particular local contour through a nondegenerate critical point \(z_*\), in the product of the neighborhoods above, has already been chosen for a bare source. Suppose its local integral has the form \[ I_N=e^{N\Phi(z_*)}N^{-d/2}\{A_*+o(1)\},\qquad A_*
e0, 	ag{15} \] and its integrand \(a_N(z)e^{N\Phi(z)}\,dz\) obeys the usual absolute Gaussian estimate on that contour: in real local coordinates \(u\), \[ |a_N(z(u))\,dz|\le C\,du,\qquad \Re(\Phi(z(u))-\Phi(z_*))\le-c|u|^2. 	ag{16} \] The parametrization is Lipschitz near zero; the fixed local contour has no other point of equal real phase. Polynomial scalar prefactors can be taken outside (15). Insert the products in (14), with total number of factors \(r\). After dividing them by \((\log N/N)^r\), write the multiplier as \(b_N(z)\). Equation (14) gives \[ b_N(z)=b(z)+O_{\mathrm{hol}}((\log N)^{-1}),\quad b(z)=\left( rac2\piight)^r \prod_v\sin(\pi x_v)^{-r_v} \prod_i\operatorname{sinc}( eta_i/\pi). 	ag{17} \] Here \(r_v\) counts factors at variable \(x_v\), and \(\sum_v r_v=r\). On compact sets \(b(z_*)
e0\), uniformly for the indicated real parameters. It follows that the decorated local integral equals \[ \left( rac{\log N}{N}ight)^r e^{N\Phi(z_*)}N^{-d/2}\{b(z_*)A_*+o(1)\}. 	ag{18} \] Indeed \[ |b_N(z(u))-b(z_*)|\le C\{(\log N)^{-1}+|u|\}. \] Multiplying by (16) and integrating bounds the difference from \(b(z_*)I_N\) by \[ C e^{N\Re\Phi(z_*)}N^{-d/2} \{(\log N)^{-1}+N^{-1/2}\}. \] This proves (18) directly from the stated local hypotheses. In particular these endpoint factors cannot make that already specified local Gaussian coefficient zero. This consequence does not supply (15), choose a contributing contour, or show that \(z_*\) lies in the thin neighborhood furnished by Theorem 1. Nor does it exclude cancellation with another part of the original closed sum. The full trace retains its outer vertical integrals and complementary physical rows. ## 5. Direct sources and scope The complete source proofs were read at these unchanged versions, and their used implications and hashes checked: * [Scalar compatibility](research_microscopic_endpoint_bulk_scalar_compatibility.md), SHA256 2b8713ed16b66f5faa004403ac1d032021eee0a6f8f38082481d002c672c0b2e: a polynomially bounded scalar matching the actual values and spectral normals, including bounded complex endpoint parameters. * [Value connection and overlap](research_endpoint_value_connection_and_overlap.md), SHA256 87801bd8baca255a86fdbcd5170662fd9f2b366f983507f776d5676fd8a324da: the explicit \(C_0,C_1\), their removable zero-parameter values, and the uniform real-interval error for any moderate exact value interpolation. The additional arguments here are the explicit fixed-strip barrier, the shrinking-parameter unit formula, and its local multiplier consequence. They give neither a whole-source exponential bound nor the finite-exception filling theorem. Only written mathematics, source-text reads and hashes were used; no numerical experiment, mathematical program, test or build was run. Frozen manuscripts and public documentation remain unchanged.

title: Exponential cancellation of the actual low and central high endpoint bands
text: # Exponential cancellation of the actual low and central high endpoint bands Private written proof, 16 November 2026. The low endpoint polynomial and the central portion of its original high Newton band cancel exponentially after division by the distinct-node polynomial, on fixed lower angular compact sets. This holds at both level parities. It follows from the exact original kernel difference equation and a holomorphic iteration with a fixed domain buffer. No formal asymptotic series is used to infer the exponential error. The result combines the actual low term with the half-character term before estimating them. It extends to arbitrary fixed products of endpoint coupons at a shared surviving vertex. It does not discard the vertical sides or the remaining physical rows. The positive exponential constant obtained here is not compared with a filled action deficit, and no full-source asymptotic or nonzero cycle coefficient follows. ## 1. Exact original polynomials and the general central band Put \[ N\ge2,\quad D=N-1,\quad m=\lfloor N/2\rfloor,\quad k_0=N-m,\quad J=k_0-1,\quad \theta=\pi/N,\quad\eta=(-1)^D, \] \[ c_a=2\cos((2a+1)\theta),\quad s_j=2\sin(j\theta),\quad S_j=\prod_{b=1}^j s_b,\qquad e_j(Z)=S_j^{-2}\prod_{a<j}(c_a-Z), \] \[ K_N(w,Z)=\sum_{j=0}^{D}e_j(w)e_j(Z),\qquad Z(t)=-2\cos t,\qquad w_N(\alpha)=2\cosh(\alpha/N). \tag{1} \] The monic polynomial of distinct physical nodes is \[ Q_N(Z)= \begin{cases} 2T_m(Z/2),&N=2m,\\ (Z+2)\{U_m(Z/2)-U_{m-1}(Z/2)\},&N=2m+1. \end{cases} \tag{2} \] Its degree is \(k_0=J+1\). In angular coordinates, \[ Q_N(Z(t))= \begin{cases} 2(-1)^m\cos(Nt/2),&N=2m,\\ 4(-1)^m\sin(t/2)\sin(Nt/2),&N=2m+1. \end{cases} \tag{3} \] All of these are ordinary polynomial identities. The original closing, used below, is \[ \phi_N(h)=\eta\sum_{a<m} \{(4-c_a^2)h'(c_a)-c_ah(c_a)\} +\mathbf1_{N\ {\rm odd}}h(-2). \tag{3a} \] Fix \(0<\delta<1/2\), put \(L_N=\lfloor\delta N\rfloor\), and take \(N\) sufficiently large that \(k_*:=k_0+L_N\le D\). Define \[ \begin{split} \mathcal L_N(\alpha,Z)&=\sum_{j=0}^{J}e_j(w_N(\alpha))e_j(Z),\\ \mathcal P_N^\delta(\alpha,Z) &=\sum_{j=0}^{k_*}e_j(w_N(\alpha))e_j(Z),\\ \mathcal E_N^\delta(\alpha,t) &=\frac{\mathcal P_N^\delta(\alpha,Z(t))}{Q_N(Z(t))}. \end{split} \tag{4} \] The notation \(\mathcal P_N^\delta\) is a partial kernel, not the physical relation \(P_N(Z)=2T_N(Z/2)+2\). The low polynomial \(\mathcal L_N\) has degree at most \(J\). Use the general-domain source's exact ratios \[ (a_l,b_l)= \begin{cases} ((l+\tfrac12)\theta,(l+1)\theta),&N=2m,\\ ((l+1)\theta,(l+\tfrac32)\theta),&N=2m+1, \end{cases} \] \[ \rho_{l,N}(\alpha,t)= \frac{[\cos^2a_l+\sinh^2(\alpha/(2N))] [\sin^2(t/2)-\sin^2a_l]}{\cos^4b_l}, \qquad H_N^\delta=\sum_{l=0}^{L_N}\prod_{j<l}\rho_{j,N}. \tag{5} \] An empty product is one. Direct Newton multiplication gives \[ \frac{e_{k_0+l}(w_N(\alpha))e_{k_0+l}(Z(t))} {Q_N(Z(t))} =\beta_N(\alpha)\prod_{j<l}\rho_{j,N}(\alpha,t), \tag{6} \] where \[ \beta_N(\alpha)= \begin{cases} \displaystyle\frac{\cosh(\alpha/2)}{2N^2},&N=2m,\\[4pt] \displaystyle \frac{\cosh(\alpha/2)\cosh(\alpha/(2N))} {4N^2\cos^4(\theta/2)},&N=2m+1. \end{cases} \tag{7} \] For clarity, at \(l=0\) one uses \[ e_{k_0}(Z)/Q_N(Z)=(-1)^{k_0}/S_{k_0}^2, \quad S_{k_0}^2= \begin{cases}2N,&N\ {\rm even},\\4N\cos^2(\theta/2),&N\ {\rm odd}, \end{cases} \] and the exact endpoint value given by the sine products. Equivalently, evaluate (2) directly at \(w_N(\alpha)\): its values are \(2\cosh(\alpha/2)\) at even levels and \(4\cosh(\alpha/2)\cosh(\alpha/(2N))\) at odd levels. Together with the displayed \(S_{k_0}^2\), this gives (7). The ratio of the left side of (6) at \(l+1\) to that at \(l\) is \[ \frac{(c_{k_0+l}-w_N(\alpha))(c_{k_0+l}-Z(t))} {s_{k_0+l+1}^{\,4}}, \tag{8} \] which is precisely (5). This proves (6) without identifying polynomials from values alone. In particular, \[ \mathcal E_N^\delta =\frac{\mathcal L_N}{Q_N}+\beta_NH_N^\delta. \tag{9} \] The fixed contraction domain is \[ \mathcal D_\delta =\{t:|\sin^2(t/2)-\sin^2(\pi\delta)|<\cos^2(\pi\delta)\}. \tag{10} \] The general-domain theorem proves that on each compact subset of \(\mathcal D_\delta\), uniformly for bounded complex \(\alpha\), there are \(q<1\) and \(N_0\) such that \[ |\rho_{l,N}|\le q\quad(0\le l<L_N). \tag{11} \] The upper bound on complex \(\alpha\) in the theorem below is stronger, \(|\alpha|<\pi\), because its a priori low-polynomial bound uses the endpoint root disk. ## 2. An a priori bound with no low/high cancellation assumed Fix \(A<\pi\). For \(|\alpha|\le A\), the endpoint root theorem gives, for every distinct physical node and all sufficiently large \(N\), \[ |K_N(w_N(\alpha),c_a)|\le1. \tag{12} \] Indeed \[ |w_N(\alpha)-2|\le2(\cosh(A/N)-1)\le2-c_0 \] eventually, since \(A<\pi\). This is a complex disk estimate, not a positivity assertion for complex endpoint colors. The high Newton terms vanish at every distinct node. Thus ordinary Lagrange interpolation gives the exact partial fractions \[ \frac{\mathcal L_N(\alpha,Z)}{Q_N(Z)} =\sum_{\text{distinct }a} \frac{K_N(w_N(\alpha),c_a)} {Q_N'(c_a)(Z-c_a)}. \tag{13} \] The reciprocal derivative weights satisfy \[ |Q_N'(c_a)|^{-1}= \begin{cases} 2\sin\tau_a/N,&N\ {\rm even},\\ 2\cos(\tau_a/2)/N,&N\ {\rm odd},\ a<m,\\ 1/N,&N\ {\rm odd},\ c_a=-2, \end{cases} \quad \tau_a=\pi(D-2a)/N. \tag{14} \] These follow by differentiating (3); the last follows at its ramified angular zero or directly from the polynomial in (2). Their sum is at most one. Hence, for \(Z\notin[-2,2]\), \[ \left|\frac{\mathcal L_N(\alpha,Z)}{Q_N(Z)}\right| \le\frac1{\operatorname{dist}(Z,[-2,2])}. \tag{15} \] This retains the odd simple node. Let \[ \mathcal U_\delta =\mathcal D_\delta\cap\{\Im t<0\}. \tag{16} \] For every compact \(\mathcal K_0\Subset\mathcal U_\delta\), \(Z(\mathcal K_0)\) has positive distance from \([-2,2]\). Equations (7), (9), (11), and (15) therefore give \[ \sup_{|\alpha|\le A,\ t\in\mathcal K_0} |\mathcal E_N^\delta(\alpha,t)|\le C. \tag{17} \] No asymptotic of the Cauchy transform in (13), nor any cancellation between the two terms in (9), is used in (17). ## 3. The exact gauged difference equation Define the original angular difference coefficients \[ A_N(t)=\frac{4\cos^4((t-\theta)/2)} {\sin t\,\sin(t-\theta)},\qquad C_N(t)=\frac{4\cos^4((t+\theta)/2)} {\sin t\,\sin(t+\theta)}. \tag{18} \] The full kernel difference source, after the substitution \(x=(\pi-t-\theta)/(2\theta)\) in its physical-color index, gives \[ (\mathscr L_N f)(t) =(c_0+A_N+C_N)f(t)-A_Nf(t-2\theta)-C_Nf(t+2\theta), \] \[ \mathscr L_N e_j=c_je_j-s_j^2e_{j-1}. \tag{19} \] The \(j=0\) lowering term is zero. The multiplication identity \(w e_j(w)=c_je_j(w)-s_{j+1}^2e_{j+1}(w)\) consequently telescopes: \[ (\mathscr L_N-w_N)\mathcal P_N^\delta =s_{k_*+1}^2e_{k_*+1}(w_N)e_{k_*}(Z). \tag{20} \] We use (20) only for sufficiently large \(N\), when \(k_*<D\); this holds for the fixed \(\delta<1/2\). It is an ordinary polynomial identity, including every physical normal. The exact shift ratios of \(Q_N\) are \[ \frac{Q_N(Z(t\pm2\theta))}{Q_N(Z(t))} =\begin{cases} -1,&N\ {\rm even},\\ -\sin(t/2\pm\theta)/\sin(t/2),&N\ {\rm odd}. \end{cases} \tag{21} \] Set \(\widetilde A_N=A_N,\widetilde C_N=C_N\) in the even case; in the odd case set \[ \widetilde A_N=A_N\frac{\sin(t/2-\theta)}{\sin(t/2)},\qquad \widetilde C_N=C_N\frac{\sin(t/2+\theta)}{\sin(t/2)}. \] Then (20), divided by \(Q_N\), becomes \[ M_N\mathcal E_N^\delta +\widetilde A_N\{\mathcal E_N^\delta(t-2\theta)-\mathcal E_N^\delta(t)\} +\widetilde C_N\{\mathcal E_N^\delta(t+2\theta)-\mathcal E_N^\delta(t)\} =\mathcal F_N, \tag{22} \] where \[ \begin{split} M_N&=c_0-w_N+A_N+C_N+\widetilde A_N+\widetilde C_N,\\ \mathcal F_N &=(c_{k_*}-w_N)\beta_N \prod_{l=0}^{L_N-1}\rho_{l,N}. \end{split} \tag{23} \] The last formula follows from (6) and \(s_{k_*+1}^2e_{k_*+1}(w_N)=(c_{k_*}-w_N)e_{k_*}(w_N)\). Thus on every fixed compact in (16), \[ |\mathcal F_N|\le CN^{-2}q^{L_N}. \tag{24} \] There is no undetermined homogeneous error in (22). All its coefficients are holomorphic on fixed lower neighborhoods for large \(N\). Uniformly on them and on \(|\alpha|\le A\), \[ A_N,\ C_N,\ \widetilde A_N,\ \widetilde C_N \longrightarrow \cot^2(t/2),\qquad M_N\longrightarrow4\cot^2(t/2). \tag{25} \] The limiting multiplier is nonzero off the real axis. In particular \(M_N^{-1}\) is uniformly bounded on the neighborhoods used below. No positivity of this complex multiplier is assumed. ## 4. Exponential cancellation by holomorphic iteration **Theorem 1.** For every \(0<\delta<1/2\), every \(A<\pi\), and every compact \(\mathcal K\Subset\mathcal U_\delta\), there are \(C,\kappa>0\) and \(N_0\) such that, at both level parities, \[ \boxed{\qquad \sup_{|\alpha|\le A,\ t\in\mathcal K} \left|\frac{\mathcal P_N^\delta(\alpha,Z(t))} {Q_N(Z(t))}\right| \le C e^{-\kappa N} \qquad(N\ge N_0). \qquad} \tag{26} \] All fixed derivatives in \(\alpha,t\) have the same form of bound on smaller compact sets. In the endpoint spectral color, for fixed nonnegative integers \(a,b\), \[ \left|\partial_w^a\partial_Z^b \frac{\sum_{j=0}^{k_*}e_j(w)e_j(Z)}{Q_N(Z)} \right|_{\substack{w=w_N(\alpha)\\Z=Z(t)}} \le C_{a,b}N^{2a}e^{-\kappa N} \tag{27} \] on compact parameter sets as above, after choosing a larger parameter/domain neighborhood for the proof. These are derivatives of the displayed quotient, not of its numerator alone. **Proof.** Choose a larger \(\alpha\)-disk still of radius less than \(\pi\). Choose \(\rho>0\) such that the closed \(3\rho\) neighborhood of \(\mathcal K\) lies in \(\mathcal U_\delta\). On that neighborhood use (11), (17), and (25), and put \[ B=\sup\frac{|\widetilde A_N|+|\widetilde C_N|}{|M_N|}<\infty, \qquad G_N=M_N^{-1}\mathcal F_N, \] \[ (\mathscr P_N f)(t)= -M_N^{-1}\{\widetilde A_N(f(t-2\theta)-f(t)) +\widetilde C_N(f(t+2\theta)-f(t))\}. \tag{28} \] The bounds are uniform for all sufficiently large \(N\) and all parameters in the chosen disk. Equation (22) is exactly \(\mathcal E_N^\delta=G_N+\mathscr P_N\mathcal E_N^\delta\). Here is the domain estimate needed for an increasing number of iterations. If two nested tubular neighborhoods have gap \(d\) and \(d\ge4\theta\), Cauchy's inequality on the outer neighborhood and integration along the real shift segment give \[ \|\mathscr P_N f\|_{\rm inner} \le \frac{4\theta B}{d}\|f\|_{\rm outer}. \tag{29} \] The intermediate segment remains at distance at least \(d/2\) from the outer boundary. This proves (29) without a derivative bound on \(f\) assumed in advance. Choose a fixed \(a_*>0\) so small that \[ a_*\le\frac{\rho}{16\pi\max(1,B)},\qquad a_*\le\frac14, \] and put \(k_N=\lfloor a_*N\rfloor\). Use \(k_N\) successive gaps \(d=\rho/k_N\), from the \(2\rho\) neighborhood to the \(\rho\) neighborhood. Then \(d\ge4\theta\) and the norm in (29) is at most \(1/2\). Repeated substitution in the exact equation gives \[ \mathcal E_N^\delta =\sum_{j=0}^{k_N-1}\mathscr P_N^{\,j}G_N +\mathscr P_N^{\,k_N}\mathcal E_N^\delta. \tag{30} \] Each composition is taken between the indicated nested domains. Consequently \[ \|\mathcal E_N^\delta\|_{\rho} \le2\|G_N\|_{2\rho} +2^{-k_N}\|\mathcal E_N^\delta\|_{2\rho} \le C N^{-2}q^{L_N}+C2^{-k_N}. \tag{31} \] Since \(L_N\ge\delta N/2\) and \(k_N\ge a_*N/2\) for large \(N\), one may, for example, take \[ \kappa=\min\left\{\frac{\delta}{2}\log\frac1q,\ \frac{a_*}{2}\log2\right\}>0. \tag{32} \] This proves (26). It is an estimate for an actual finite function, not optimal truncation of a formal series. The unused domain buffer and Cauchy's formula give fixed angular and parameter derivatives. Since \(dZ/dt=2\sin t\) is nonzero on the lower compact, spectral \(Z\)-derivatives follow there too. The function is even in \(\alpha\), so it descends holomorphically to \(u=\alpha^2\). On bounded \(u\)-disks, \[ N^2(w_N(\alpha)-2)=u+O(N^{-2}) \] with all fixed derivatives, and this map has a uniformly regular inverse on slightly smaller disks for large \(N\). Thus each endpoint derivative costs at most \(C_aN^{2a}\); this includes \(\alpha=0\). It proves (27). \(\square\) For example, the entire rectangle \(|\Re t|\le\pi/4,\ |\Im t|\le\log3\) lies compactly in \(\mathcal D_{1/8}\), by the general-domain theorem. Every fixed closed lower subrectangle with \(\Im t\le-h_0<0\) therefore satisfies (26). The constants depend on its buffer, on \(\delta\), and on the parameter disk. No universal action gap is claimed from their positivity. ## 5. Exact cancellation in the half-charge horizontal density Let \(\Gamma_N^\delta\) be the actual high-character amplitude in the general-domain source. Equations (5)--(9) give exactly \[ \Gamma_N^\delta+ 2N\sin t\,\frac{\mathcal L_N}{Q_N} =2N\sin t\,\mathcal E_N^\delta \quad(N\ {\rm even}), \] \[ \Gamma_N^\delta+ 4N\sin t\sin(t/2)\,\frac{\mathcal L_N}{Q_N} =4N\sin t\sin(t/2)\,\mathcal E_N^\delta \quad(N\ {\rm odd}). \tag{33} \] Thus the actual low term cancels the central high amplitude to exponential accuracy on the domains of Theorem 1. The separate leading profiles of these two terms are not whole-source coefficients. To see the original contour normalization directly, set \(\zeta=e^{-iNt}\), and keep the original Gaussian carrier \[ \mathfrak c_{N,n}=e^{\pi i nD^2/(4N)},\qquad G_n(t)=e^{inNt^2/(4\pi)}. \] For a unit-charge central rectangle with grid-midpoint end \(b_N\), the low horizontal coefficient is \(-N^2\mathfrak c_{N,n}/(\pi i)\) with kernel \(\zeta/(1-\eta\zeta)^2\). The exact high horizontal coefficient is \(N i^{-D}\mathfrak c_{N,n}/(2\pi)\) with kernel \(\zeta^{1/2}/(1-\eta\zeta)\). Here \(\zeta^{1/2}\) means the specified entire character \(e^{-iNt/2}\). Their common amplitude is \[ \Gamma_N^\delta+ 2i^{D+1}N\sin t\,\mathcal L_N \frac{\zeta^{1/2}}{1-\eta\zeta}. \tag{34} \] Substituting (3) into (34) gives precisely (33). Every horizontal alias is retained in these identities. The original low and high vertical integrals remain; they have not been assigned the lower-compact estimate (26) at height zero. ## 6. Shared coupons and the exact retained central trace The preceding cancellation takes place before evaluating any spectator. It can be used for an arbitrary fixed number \(r\ge1\) of endpoint coupons at one original traced vertex, with bounded parameters \(|\alpha_i|<\pi\). First, the omitted polynomial \[ \mathcal O_N^\delta(\alpha,Z) =K_N(w_N(\alpha),Z)-\mathcal P_N^\delta(\alpha,Z) \] is a sum of the original high modes with \(j\ge k_0+L_N+1\). Its physical values all vanish. Its first normal can occur only at nodes with \[ \tau_a\ge \begin{cases} (2L_N+3)\theta,&N\ {\rm even},\\ (2L_N+4)\theta,&N\ {\rm odd}. \end{cases} \tag{35} \] Indeed put \(j=D-r'\). The full-high contraction has normal support \(a\le r'\): in the defining Newton product the two occurrences of \(c_a\) have indices \(a\) and \(D-a\), so the derivative vanishes once \(j>D-a\). Here \(r'\le m-2-L_N\); substituting the largest allowed \(a\) into \(\tau_a=(D-2a)\theta\) gives (35). The odd simple value is also zero. The omitted band is therefore the following exact value functional, with its original normal weights: \[ \phi_N(\mathcal O_N^\delta f) =\eta\sum_{a=0}^{m-2-L_N} (4-c_a^2)(\mathcal O_N^\delta)'(c_a)f(c_a). \tag{35a} \] For several coupons, write \(B_i=K_N(w_N(\alpha_i),\cdot)\), \(P_i=\mathcal P_N^\delta(\alpha_i,\cdot)\), and \(O_i=B_i-P_i\). Every \(O_i\) vanishes at all physical nodes, so the product of two of them has zero values and first normals. Consequently \[ \begin{split} \phi_N\!\left[\left(\prod_iB_i-\prod_iP_i\right)f\right] &=\sum_{a=0}^{m-2-L_N}\omega_a f(c_a),\\ \omega_a&=\eta(4-c_a^2) \sum_i O_i'(c_a)\prod_{j\ne i}B_j(c_a). \end{split} \tag{35b} \] Each shared physical color in (35b) is kept, together with the entire remaining spectator. These identities do not give a filled-action estimate for that physical sum. Consequently, for every fixed \(b<2\pi\delta\) and all large \(N\), the full values and first normals of \[ \prod_{i=1}^rK_N(w_N(\alpha_i),Z) \quad\hbox{and}\quad \prod_{i=1}^r\mathcal P_N^\delta(\alpha_i,Z) \tag{36} \] agree at every physical node with \(|t|\le b\), including the odd simple node. This follows by the product rule, not from a value-only replacement. Thus (36) can be made inside the original central trace with any shared polynomial spectator, retaining all other traces coefficientwise. Here is the full contour statement. Let \(b_N\le b<2\pi\delta\) be a positive midpoint, \(e^{iNb_N}=-\eta\), and let \(H>0\). Let \(f(Z(t))\) be even and holomorphic near the closed rectangle \([-b_N,b_N]+i[-H,H]\). Write \[ p_N(t)=\prod_{i=1}^r\mathcal P_N^\delta(\alpha_i,Z(t)), \quad g_N(t)=\sin t\,p_N(t)f(Z(t))G_n(t). \] The original central full-normal trace, at unit charge, is exactly \[ -\frac{N^2\mathfrak c_{N,n}}{\pi i} \int_{-b_N-iH}^{b_N-iH} g_N(t)\frac{e^{-iNt}}{(1-\eta e^{-iNt})^2}\,dt +\frac{\eta N^2\mathfrak c_{N,n}}{\pi} \int_{-H}^{H}\frac{g_N(b_N+ih)}{4\cosh^2(Nh/2)}\,dh . \tag{37} \] The source derivative-sampling residue proof applies on this midpoint rectangle exactly as on the full-period rectangle. At each double node the two angular copies give its value and first normal; at the odd zero angle the derivative sampling gives the original simple value. The replacement (36) therefore changes neither contribution. The second integral and the actual midpoint orientation are part of (37). Define \[ \xi_N(t)= \begin{cases} (-1)^m,&N\ {\rm even},\\ -2i(-1)^m\sin(t/2),&N\ {\rm odd}. \end{cases} \] Equation (3) is \(Q_N(Z(t))=\xi_N(t)e^{iNt/2}(1-\eta e^{-iNt})\). The horizontal density in (37) consequently becomes exactly \[ \sin t\,\xi_N(t)^r f(Z(t))G_n(t) \left(\prod_{i=1}^r\mathcal E_N^\delta(\alpha_i,t)\right) e^{-iN(1-r/2)t}(1-\eta e^{-iNt})^{r-2}. \tag{38} \] All shared variables remain in \(f\). On a fixed lower compact contained in \(\mathcal U_\delta\), the product of quotients in (38) is \(O(e^{-r\kappa N})\), with its fixed derivatives. For fixed \(H>0\) and a family of lower segments in such a compact, the horizontal integral in (37) is therefore bounded by \[ C_r N^2|\mathfrak c_{N,n}|e^{-r\kappa N} \int_{-b_N-iH}^{b_N-iH} |f(Z(t))G_n(t)e^{-iN(1-r/2)t}|\,|dt|. \tag{39} \] The remaining factors in (38) are uniformly bounded there, including the inverse factor when \(r=1\). Formula (39) is an actual relative gain in the coherent horizontal density with the spectator retained. Its charge character and its spectator are not replaced by a claimed filled-action estimate. The full physical trace is the central trace (37) plus the literal sum of its remaining physical rows. No row outside the window in (35), or vertical term in (37), is discarded. The theorem gives no bound for those terms at the filled rate. It also does not assert that (39)'s \(\kappa\) exceeds any independently arising action loss. ## 7. Direct-source readback The following complete direct sources were read, their used identities checked, and their hashes verified: * [Original kernel difference equation](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_edge_kernel_difference_and_endpoint_bound.md), SHA256 5d0d07d4d97d82cca66e0e0c3bf2cecad8e5f58ef8329178278b297cf0d6c5da: original lowering operator, physical angular conversion and the ordinary finite-kernel defect. Its weaker root bound is not used. * [Coherent endpoint kernel reduction](research_full_period_endpoint_kernel_reduction.md), SHA256 a1d67ac803c0160bbfdacaa96a6fde9dc1ffae06fc39eb94f0416dcf2ecef76e: the stronger physical-row root disk, exact low interpolation and both-parity full-normal trace conventions. * [General endpoint half-character domain](research_endpoint_radical_general_domain.md), SHA256 600ae0d78f29946272ed54b600cb1f5fdf170965985a08d6e3d9201303722074: exact lowering ratios, general-cutoff contraction domain, original character amplitude and midpoint contour with its vertical term. * [Full-period current and charge convolution](research_full_period_current_charge_convolution.md), SHA256 3f74b9824ecbf0b71a79b17959c7208f650103f95932192cfba87c7a7aa05595: original Gaussian carrier, derivative sampling, full-normal rectangle orientation, and coefficientwise spectator convention. Only written mathematics, text reads and hashes were used. No mathematical program, numerical experiment, test or compilation was run. Frozen notes and public manuscripts are unchanged.

title: Endpoint-current matchings are units in the full boundary algebra
text: # Endpoint-current matchings are units in the full boundary algebra Private research note, 15 November 2026. The exact simultaneous endpoint-current polynomial has no zero at any physical assignment of its remaining boundary variables, for every level \(N\ge3\) and every choice of signed current powers, except when one of its even powers is zero. More strongly, its inverse retains all mixed first Hermite normals with a polynomial bound uniform in those powers. This follows from an accretive determinant for the actual current coefficients. This is a finite boundary-algebra statement. It does not give a lower bound after the prescribed exterior trace, nor identify a selected geometric coefficient of the original scalar. The earlier matching theorem already proves a nonzero leading current coefficient when a complete exterior contour theorem is supplied. The result here requires no such contour theorem. ## 1. The actual polynomial and its determinant Use the original notation \[ D=N-1,\quad \eta=(-1)^D,\quad \sigma=(-1)^N=-\eta,\quad \theta=\pi/N,\quad c_0=2\cos\theta,\quad s_1=2\sin\theta,\quad \rho=i s_1. \tag{1} \] Let \(G\) be a finite circle tree, \(S\) a subset of its vertices, and \(n_v\in\mathbb Z\) the signed one-step Ward-current power at \(v\in S\). Let \(O\subset S\) be its odd-power vertices and \(E=S\setminus O\). The remaining boundary variables are \(w_j\), indexed by the outside vertices adjacent to \(S\); write their set as \(B\), with \(b=|B|\). Put \(U_N=T\Pi_0\), the original turned full endpoint idempotent. Let \(m_{vj}\) be the number of actual incidences from \(v\) to outside vertex \(j\), and \(d_v=\sum_jm_{vj}\). For a simple tree these numbers are zero or one, but their incidence notation keeps shared outside variables explicit. The exact monomers are \[ A_v(\mathbf w)= \begin{cases} \sigma n_vN\rho,&v\in E,\\[1mm] 2\sum_jm_{vj}U_N(w_j) +\eta\{n_v\rho+2(d_v-1)c_0\},&v\in O, \end{cases} \qquad d_N=\frac{s_1^2(N^2-1)}3>0. \tag{2} \] The full boundary polynomial of these inserted currents is exactly \[ \mathcal E_{S,N}(\mathbf w) =\sum_{\substack{M\subset E(G[O])\\M\ {\rm matching}}} d_N^{|M|}\prod_{v\in S\setminus V(M)}A_v(\mathbf w). \tag{3} \] This is Theorem 1 of the [grouped endpoint-current note](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_grouped_endpoint_current_matchings.md). It is an ordinary polynomial identity before any boundary reduction; every internal mixed first normal and every actual outside incidence is retained. If any \(v\in E\) has \(n_v=0\), (3) is identically zero. Henceforth assume all even powers are nonzero. Define \[ B_E=\prod_{v\in E}\sigma n_vN\rho,\qquad m=|O|,\qquad x_v=\sigma A_v\quad(v\in O), \qquad \mathsf D(\mathbf w)=\operatorname{diag}(x_v) +i\sqrt{d_N}\,\operatorname{Adj}(G[O]). \tag{4} \] Empty determinants and products equal one. Then \[ \boxed{\ \mathcal E_{S,N} =B_E\,\sigma^m\det\mathsf D.\ } \tag{5} \] Indeed a permutation supported by a forest has only fixed points and edge transpositions. A transposition contributes \(-[i\sqrt{d_N}]^2=d_N\). Factoring \(\sigma\) from each unmatched odd monomer contributes \(\sigma^{m-2|M|}=\sigma^m\), proving (5). No sum over physical colors or contraction of the exterior has been taken in this determinant. For any complex boundary assignment satisfying \(\Re x_v>0\) at every odd vertex, write \[ \mathsf D=\mathsf R+i\mathsf H,\qquad \mathsf R=\operatorname{diag}(\Re x_v)>0,\qquad \mathsf H=\operatorname{diag}(\Im x_v) +\sqrt{d_N}\operatorname{Adj}(G[O]). \tag{6} \] The matrix \(\mathsf H\) is Hermitian. Therefore \[ |\det\mathsf D| =\det\mathsf R\, \left|\det\!\left(I+i\mathsf R^{-1/2} \mathsf H\mathsf R^{-1/2}\right)\right| \ge\prod_{v\in O}\Re x_v, \qquad \|\mathsf D^{-1}\|\le(\min_v\Re x_v)^{-1}. \tag{7} \] The determinant inequality follows from the real eigenvalues of \(\mathsf R^{-1/2}\mathsf H\mathsf R^{-1/2}\). For the inverse estimate, Cauchy--Schwarz and \(\Re\langle u,\mathsf Du\rangle\ge (\min\Re x_v)\|u\|^2\) give the least-singular-value bound. ## 2. Every physical boundary assignment is in this sector Let \[ c_a=2\cos((2a+1)\theta),\qquad 0\le a\le\lfloor D/2\rfloor \tag{8} \] be the distinct physical nodes. All are double except the last node \(-2\) when \(N\) is odd. The exact full Ward-coupon formulas are \[ \begin{split} \sigma U_N(c_a) &=c_0+2\sin\theta\sum_{r=1}^a\cot(r\theta),\\ U_N'(c_a) &=-\sigma\frac{\sin\theta}{4\sin((2a+1)\theta)} \sum_{r=a+1}^{N-1-a}\csc^2(r\theta) \quad\text{at double nodes}. \end{split} \tag{9} \] These are equations (21)--(22) of the [signed Ward note](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_signed_gaussian_ward_endpoint_packet.md). The first formula includes the odd simple node. Every cotangent in it is positive, unless the sum is empty. At an arbitrary physical outside assignment \(\mathbf c=(c_{a_j})_{j\in B}\), (2) and (9) give, for \(v\in O\), \[ \begin{split} x_v(\mathbf c)&=r_v(\mathbf c)-i n_vs_1,\\ r_v(\mathbf c) &=2c_0+ 4\sin\theta\sum_jm_{vj}\sum_{r=1}^{a_j}\cot(r\theta) \ \ge\ 2c_0. \end{split} \tag{10} \] In particular all powers affect only the imaginary parts of these odd monomers. For \(N\ge3\), put \(\delta_N=2c_0=4\cos(\pi/N)\ge2\). Equations (5), (7), and (10) prove the exact bound \[ \boxed{\quad |\mathcal E_{S,N}(\mathbf c)| \ge (Ns_1)^{|E|}\!\left(\prod_{v\in E}|n_v|\right) \prod_{v\in O}r_v(\mathbf c) \ge (Ns_1)^{|E|}\!\left(\prod_{v\in E}|n_v|\right) \delta_N^m>0 . \quad} \tag{11} \] This holds simultaneously for all assignments, all signed integer powers, and both level parities. Powers may even depend on \(N\). Restoring the original common crossing units \(\kappa_N^{n_v}\) does not change (11), since those units have modulus one. The restriction \(N\ge3\) is necessary. At \(N=2\), two adjacent odd current vertices with no exterior and powers \(n_1=n_2=1\) have \(A_1=A_2=-2i\) and \(d_N=4\), so (3) is exactly zero. This is a degeneracy of the actual current polynomial, not an asymptotic example. ## 3. Inversion retains every mixed first normal Let \[ \mathcal A_N=\mathbb C[w]/(2T_N(w/2)+2),\qquad \mathcal B_N=\bigotimes_{j\in B}\mathcal A_N. \tag{12} \] Use its full Hermite seminorm \[ \|f\|_{\mathcal J,B} =\max_{\mathbf c,J} |\partial_J f(\mathbf c)|,\qquad \partial_J=\prod_{j\in J}\partial_{w_j}, \tag{13} \] where \(J\subset B\) contains only variables assigned to double nodes; each variable is differentiated at most once. These are all local tensor-algebra coordinates, so (13) is a norm on \(\mathcal B_N\). **Theorem.** Under the hypotheses of (11), the class of \(\mathcal E_{S,N}\) is a unit of \(\mathcal B_N\). For every allowed \(J\), \(r=|J|\), its inverse satisfies \[ \boxed{\quad |\partial_J\mathcal E_{S,N}^{-1}(\mathbf c)| \le \frac{1}{(Ns_1)^{|E|}\prod_{v\in E}|n_v|} \,\delta_N^{-m-r}(m)_r \prod_{j\in J}\frac{M_j(N^2-1)}6 , \quad} \tag{14} \] where \(M_j=\max_{v\in O}m_{vj}\), with \(M_j=0\) if \(O\) is empty, \((m)_0=1\), and \((m)_r=m(m+1)\cdots(m+r-1)\) for \(r>0\). If \(O\) is empty, its positive-order inverse derivatives vanish. In particular there is a constant depending only on the fixed incidence pattern such that \[ \|\mathcal E_{S,N}^{-1}\|_{\mathcal J,B} \le C_{G,S}N^{2b}. \tag{15} \] The constant is independent of all current powers. **Proof.** The Chinese remainder decomposition of (12) is a product over physical assignments of rings \[ \mathbb C[\epsilon_j:j\ {\rm double}] /(\epsilon_j^2:j\ {\rm double}). \tag{16} \] An element in any such ring is a unit precisely when its constant coefficient is nonzero. Equation (11) proves that condition at every assignment. Its inverse data are those of the analytic function \(1/\mathcal E_{S,N}\) near each assignment.
