On those rays \(|z|^{-j-1}\le C e^{-cjt}\). The small circle and \(\int_{1/j}^{r}t^{1-\sigma}e^{-cjt}\,dt\) are both \(O(j^{-2+\sigma})\); the outer arcs are exponentially small. Multiplication by \(1-z\) gives \(O(j^{-3+\sigma})\) for the coefficient difference. Together with (23)--(24), this proves (22) away from zero. The same argument for the explicit leading powers gives their first-difference accuracy as stated. For uniformity at zero, use a fixed small parameter circle \(|
u|=\sigma/2\). The expressions \[ k_+j^{-1+i
u}+k_-j^{-1-i
u},\qquad k_++k_-,\qquad i
u(k_+-k_-) \] have removable singularities at \(
u=0\). Both the exact coefficients and their differences are holomorphic inside this circle. The estimates just proved on its boundary, with an exponent smaller than the chosen \(\sigma\), extend to the disk by the maximum principle. A finite compact cover treats the remaining real parameters and proves (22). Finally the expansions \(\Gamma(z)=z^{-1}-\gamma_{\!E}+O(z)\) and \(\psi(1/2)=-\gamma_{\!E}-2\log2\), the latter following from the gamma duplication identity, give (4). In particular \[ g_0(s)= rac{2}{\pi^2s} \{\log s+\gamma_{\!E}+4\log2\}. 	ag{25} \] The coalescence is part of one uniform real-parameter estimate, not a limit taken after \(j\) or \(N\). ## 4. A growing finite-level endpoint overlap For \(j\ge1\), use the balanced state \[ Z_{j,N}=  inom{jF_{j,N}}{j^2(F_{j,N}-F_{j-1,N})}. 	ag{26} \] Equation (12) gives the exact transfer \[ Z_{j+1,N}=M_{j,N}Z_{j,N},\qquad M_{j,N}=  egin{pmatrix} (j+1)(1+d_{j,N})/j&(j+1)q_{j,N}/j^2\ (j+1)^2d_{j,N}/j&(j+1)^2q_{j,N}/j^2 \end{pmatrix}. 	ag{27} \] Let \(M_j^0\) be the matrix with the limiting coefficients (13); it transports \(Z_j^0=(jv_j,j^2(v_j-v_{j-1}))^t\). Uniformly for \(1\le j\le J=o(N)\), the exact sine quotients imply \[ q_{j,N}-q_j^0=O_A(j/N^2),\qquad d_{j,N}-d_j^0=O_A(N^{-2}),\qquad M_{j,N}-M_j^0=O_A(j/N^2). 	ag{28} \] For the first estimate, the exact quotient is \[ q_{j,N}= \left( rac{\sin(j\pi/N)}{\sin((j+1)\pi/N)}ight)^4  rac{\sin((2j+2)\pi/N)}{\sin(2j\pi/N)}. \] After extracting \(q_j^0\), the logarithms of the remaining sinc quotients are differences over intervals of length \(O(N^{-1})\). Since \((\log\operatorname{sinc})'(u)=O(u)\) near zero, their total is \(O(j/N^2)\). For \(d\), the relative error of its sine denominator is \(O((j+1)^2/N^2)\), whereas \(d_j^0=O_A(j^{-2})\); the numerator has relative error \(O_A(N^{-2})\). This proves (28), also for the finitely many initial indices. There is a constant \(B_A\ge1\) such that, throughout this range for sufficiently large \(N\), \[ \|M_j^0\|,\ \|M_{j,N}\|\le1+B_A/j,\qquad \left\|\prod_{r=k}^{j-1}M_{r,N}ight\| \le C_A(j/k)^{B_A}. 	ag{29} \] Indeed the limiting expansion is \[ M_j^0=I+ rac1j  egin{pmatrix}1&1\-(1+
u^2)&-1\end{pmatrix} +O_A(j^{-2}), \] and (28) is absorbed into \(C_A/j\) when \(j=o(N)\). Increase \(B_A\) to cover the initial indices. The initial vector at \(j=1\) differs by \(O_A(N^{-2})\) from its limiting vector, directly from (12). Equation (22) gives \(\|Z_j^0\|\le C_A(1+\log(j+1))\) for real parameters. Variation of constants in (27), using (28)--(29), therefore gives the deliberately conservative estimate \[ \|Z_{J,N}-Z_J^0\| \le C_A N^{-2}J^{B_A+2}(1+\log J). 	ag{30} \] For example, bound each summand by \(C_A(J/k)^{B_A}(k/N^2)(1+\log k)\) and sum; the displayed bound is larger and valid for every \(B_A\ge1\). Fix once and for all \[ 0<\kappa< rac1{4(B_A+3)},\qquad J=\lfloor N^\kappafloor. 	ag{31} \] Then (30) tends to zero much faster than \(J^{-1+\sigma}\). Combining it with (22) yields the actual growing-overlap estimate \[ Z_{J,N}=  inom{Jg_\alpha(J)} {J^2\{g_\alpha(J)-g_\alpha(J-1)\}} +O_A(J^{-1+\sigma}). 	ag{32} \] All comparisons have used the exact finite recurrence up to \(J\). This is the step that prevents an exchange of nonuniform limits. ## 5. Transport from the overlap to a fixed bulk interval Choose \(0<b_*<1/2\) larger than the bulk intervals to be used. For real \(x\in(0,b_*]\), set \[ y_{0,N}(x)=S_N(x)^{-1}\cos(
u\log S_N(x)),\qquad y_{1,N}(x)=S_N(x)^{-1}  rac{\sin(
u\log S_N(x))}{
u}. 	ag{33} \] Their linear combination with coefficients \(C_0,C_1\) is \(g_\alpha(S_N(x))\). Multiplying the coalescence-safe Euler modes in the pinned source by constant factors and taking linear combinations shows, or direct differentiation verifies, that both solve \[ y''+\pi(3\cot\pi x+	an\pi x)y' +(\pi^2+\alpha^2)\cot^2(\pi x)y=0. 	ag{34} \] Their Wronskian in \(x\) is \[ y_{0,N}y_{1,N}'-y_{1,N}y_{0,N}' = rac{N\cos(\pi x)}{S_N(x)^3}. 	ag{35} \] Form their sampled balanced matrix \[ \Psi_{j,N}=  egin{pmatrix} j y_{0,N}(j/N)&j y_{1,N}(j/N)\ j^2[y_{0,N}(j/N)-y_{0,N}((j-1)/N)]& j^2[y_{1,N}(j/N)-y_{1,N}((j-1)/N)] \end{pmatrix}. 	ag{36} \] Uniformly for \(J\le j\le b_*N\), \[ \|\Psi_{j,N}\|+\|\Psi_{j,N}^{-1}\| \le C_A(1+\log N), 	ag{37} \] for sufficiently large \(N\). To check the inverse, Taylor's formula in the unscaled index gives \[ \det\Psi_{j,N} = rac{j^3\cos(\pi j/N)}{S_N(j/N)^3} +O_A((1+\log N)^2/j). 	ag{38} \] The leading term is bounded above and below by positive constants on this range. The error tends to zero because \(J=N^\kappa+O(1)\). The entry bounds follow from \(S_N(j/N)\asymp j\) and (33). This proves (37), including \(
u=0\). The sampled columns are approximate solutions of the exact recurrence: \[ \|\Psi_{j+1,N}-M_{j,N}\Psi_{j,N}\| \le C_A(1+\log N)/j^2. 	ag{39} \] Here is an estimate retaining the singular endpoint scale. Regard a column \(y(j/N)\) as a function of \(j\). Its first four index derivatives have bounds \[ C_A(1+\log N)j^{-1-r},\qquad 0\le r\le4. 	ag{40} \] The exact quotients satisfy, for \(J\le j\le b_*N\), \[ q_{j,N}=1-P_j+O_A(j^{-2}),\qquad d_{j,N}=-Q_j+O_A(j^{-3}), \] \[ P_j= rac{\pi}{N}(3\cot(\pi j/N)+	an(\pi j/N)),\qquad Q_j= rac{\pi^2+\alpha^2}{N^2}\cot^2(\pi j/N). 	ag{41} \] Taylor expansion of the sine quotients proves these bounds uniformly: their logarithmic derivatives cost \(O(1/j)\), with the next derivatives \(O(1/j^2)\). The numerator in \(d\) has error \(O_A(N^{-4})\), while its denominator has relative error \(O(1/j)\) from \(	an^2(\pi j/N)\). Expanding the scalar residual from (12), its leading part is \(y_{jj}+P_jy_j+Q_jy\), zero by (34). Equations (40)--(41) bound the residual by \(C_A(1+\log N)j^{-4}\). The two balanced residual entries multiply that scalar residual by \(j+1\) and \((j+1)^2\), respectively. This proves (39). Write \(Z_{j,N}=\Psi_{j,N}a_{j,N}\). Its exact coefficient transfer is \[ a_{j+1,N}=\{I+R_{j,N}\}a_{j,N},\qquad \|R_{j,N}\|\le C_A(1+\log N)^2/j^2. 	ag{42} \] Thus \[ \sum_{j=J}^{\lfloor b_*Nfloor}\|R_{j,N}\| \le C_A(1+\log N)^2/J=o(1). 	ag{43} \] At the overlap, \(S_N(J/N)=J\{1+O(J^2/N^2)\}\). Using this and its first index difference in (32)--(33), then (37), gives \[ a_{J,N}=  inom{C_0(
u)}{C_1(
u)} +O_A((1+\log N)^2J^{-1+\sigma}). 	ag{44} \] The \(J^2/N^2\) error and (30) are smaller by (31). The elementary product bound \(\prod(1+\|R_j\|)\le\exp(\sum\|R_j\|)\) and (43) now show that (44), with another fixed logarithmic power, holds for every \(J\le j\le b_*N\). On a fixed bulk interval, both balanced entries are converted back to \(F\) and \(N\Delta F\) with a factor \(O(N^{-1})\). Consequently the errors are at most \[ C_A N^{-1}(1+\log N)^M J^{-1+\sigma} 	ag{45} \] for an absolute finite power \(M\) in this proof. Replacing the sampled first difference of (33) by its \(x\)-derivative costs only \(O_A(N^{-2}(1+\log N))\) on that interval. For example any \(\epsilon<\kappa/2\), reduced if necessary, is valid in (7)--(8), because \(\sigma<1/4\). This proves the first part of the theorem with an explicit permitted choice of overlap exponent (31). ## 6. Derivatives of the actual moderate value interpolation We record the elementary interpolation principle used here. Suppose \(r_N\) is holomorphic and polynomially bounded on a fixed complex neighborhood of a real interval \(I_2\). Suppose its values on the spacing-\(N^{-1}\) grid obey \[ |r_N(j/N)|\le\varepsilon_N \quad(j/N\in I_2), 	ag{46} \] where \(\varepsilon_N\) is bounded below by some negative power of \(N\). On any buffered interval \(I_1\), interpolation at a fixed number \(M+1\) of neighboring grid nodes gives \[ |r_N(x)|\le C_M\varepsilon_N+O(N^{P-M-1}) \qquad(x\in I_1). 	ag{47} \] The Lagrange coefficients are bounded since all spacings are \(N^{-1}\) and the interpolation point is within a fixed number of spacings of those nodes. Cauchy's formula bounds the derivative in the usual interpolation remainder by \(C_MN^P\) on a fixed larger neighborhood; its product of spacings is \(O_M(N^{-M-1})\). Choose a fixed \(M\) making that error smaller than (46). This real bound extends with only a constant factor to a shrinking strip \[ x\in I_0,\qquad |\Im x|\le c/\log N,\qquad I_0\Subset\operatorname{int}I_1. 	ag{48} \] Indeed apply the two-constants theorem to upper and lower fixed rectangles based on \(I_1\). On their real base use (47); on all other sides use \(CN^P\). At points over \(I_0\), the harmonic measure of the other sides is at most \(C|\Im x|\): this follows from the bounded normal derivative of that fixed harmonic function on a buffered segment of the straight base. Hence its contribution to the logarithm of the bound is at most \(C|\Im x|\log N\). Equation (48) makes it bounded. Cauchy's formula on disks of radius \(c/(2\log N)\) then gives \[ |\partial_x^r r_N(x)|\le C_r(\log N)^r\varepsilon_N \qquad(x\in I_0). 	ag{49} \] The same reasoning works if a harmless fixed logarithmic power is included in \(\varepsilon_N\). Apply this principle to \[ r_N(x,\alpha)=f_N(x,\alpha) -g_\alpha(S_N(x)). \] The second function is holomorphic and polynomially bounded on a fixed buffered bulk strip: choose the branch of \(\log\sin\pi x\) real on the real interval. Its bound for real compact \(\alpha\) is \(O_A((1+\log N)/N)\) on that strip. The first has its hypothesized bound (9). Equation (7), proved on a slightly larger interval, supplies (46). All constants in (47)--(49) are uniform in the real parameter. Absorb the fixed logarithmic factors into a smaller positive \(\epsilon\). This proves (10) for every fixed derivative order, without asserting a fixed-strip small-error estimate. ## 7. Source placement and limits of the conclusion At zero parameter, the explicit leading value is \[  rac{2}{\pi N\sin(\pi x)} \left\{\log\!\left( rac{N\sin(\pi x)}{\pi}ight) +\gamma_{\!E}+4\log2ight\}. 	ag{50} \] For real nonzero parameter \(k_-=\overline{k_+}\), so (6) is an oscillatory real expression. This theorem asserts an additive power-saving error, not a relative error or a nonzero scalar unit. Let \(G_{j,N}=\partial_ZK_N(c(j),w_N(\alpha))\) be the original spectral normal and \(f_N\) any interpolation (9). Its true defect is \[ \Delta_j=Nc'(j)G_{j,N}-\partial_x f_N(j/N). \] The proved value matching therefore gives the actual subtraction term in that source equation: \[ \Delta_j=Nc'(j)G_{j,N} -\left.\partial_xg_\alpha(S_N(x))ight|_{x=j/N} +O(N^{-1-\epsilon}). 	ag{51} \] No common-index coefficient derivative is substituted for \(\partial_x f_N\). Equation (51) does not set \(\Delta_j\) to zero. If a separately proved scalar-compatibility theorem controls that defect, it can be combined with (51) to obtain the actual normal asymptotic. The two-ended endpoint normal and its propagated source are not dropped merely because (11) is terminating. All external index endpoints, odd simple-node closing, full trace currents, and other graph spectators remain outside this buffered value asymptotic. No filled-action estimate, original cycle coefficient, or noncancellation of the whole source follows. ## 8. Coverage and direct source A search of the endpoint and physical-row notes found the exact finite recurrence, moderate value interpolation and Euler modes, but not their universal generating connection or a growing endpoint overlap. The complete direct source was read at its unchanged pin, with all used implications and the hash checked: * [Original two-mode transport and exact finite recurrence](research_endpoint_normal_defect_two_mode_transport.md), SHA256 91620d1ea26793157843f78fff32c7d3eca62509799114a2d3069af8b96b47dc: the original kernel, recurrence, coalescence-safe Euler modes, existence and meaning of moderate value interpolation, and the distinction between that derivative and the actual normal. The generating identity, beta connection, uniform coefficient transfer, growing overlap and derivative bridge are proved here. Only written proofs, text reads and hashes were used. No mathematical program, numerical experiment, test or build was run. Adopted notes and public manuscripts are unchanged.

title: An exact heat reduction of the entire charged original source
text:
# An exact heat reduction of the entire charged original source Private written proof, 16 November 2026. The canonical real-power crossing and the full-Hermite charge coupon give a scalar heat equation for the original source. Its initial datum is the entire zero-power charged source, with every original kernel, trace and outside polynomial retained. A convergent Gaussian integral implements every fixed signed real power, and its charge contours can be translated through any prescribed finite point without crossing a pole. These are exact finite-source statements. They do not replace the initial datum by one of its asymptotic branches. The real-power semigroup and the analytic charge coupons were already proved separately. The Gaussian-window Newton frame also already gives exact crossing integrals. The reduction here acts on the prescribed charged scalar itself, uses its faithful finite exponential-polynomial space, and retains the nilpotent normal through the heat operator. It does not use a positive norm in place of the original closing. ## 1. Original data and the entire charged observation Let \[ N\ge2,\qquad D=N-1,\qquad \eta=(-1)^D,\qquad \mathcal A_N=\mathbb C[z]/(P_N(z)),\qquad P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2, \] \[ \phi_N(f)=\eta N^2[z^D]\operatorname{rem}_{P_N}f. 	ag{1} \] The double nodes and their positive angular lifts are \[ c_a=2\cos((2a+1)\pi/N)=-2\cos	au_a,\qquad 	au_a=\pi(D-2a)/N,\qquad 0\le a<\lfloor N/2floor. 	ag{2} \] At odd \(N\), the remaining simple node is \(-2\), with angle zero. The exact trace is \[ \phi_N(f)= \eta\sum_{a<\lfloor N/2floor} \{4\sin^2	au_a\,f'(c_a)-c_a f(c_a)\} +\mathbf1_{N\ {m odd}}f(-2). 	ag{3} \] In particular the factor \(\eta N^2\) in (1) is not changed below. Let \(\mathscr T_N\in\mathcal A_N\) have the full physical data \[ \mathscr T_N(c_a)=	au_a^2,\qquad \mathscr T_N'(c_a)= rac{	au_a}{\sin	au_a}, \qquad \mathscr T_N(-2)=0\quad(N\ {m odd}). 	ag{4} \] Define the canonical crossing family and its known carrier by \[ C_{N,n}=\exp\!\left( rac{\pi i nD^2}{4N}ight),\qquad R_n=C_{N,n} \exp_{\mathcal A_N}\!\left( rac{i nN}{4\pi}\mathscr T_Night), \qquad n\in\mathbb C. 	ag{5} \] This is the entire family in the real-power source theorem. At every signed integer \(n\), it equals the actual physical \(R^n\), including the first normals. Its angular jet representative on the specified physical lifts is \[ C_{N,n}\exp(i nNt^2/(4\pi)). 	ag{6} \] No periodic resetting of this representative is made. Although the prior real-power note states \(N\ge3\), its direct local-algebra proof also proves (4)--(6) for \(N=2\): there is one double node with \(c_0=0,	au_0=\pi/2\) and no simple-node term. The original entire charge coupon \(\mathcal C_{N,\chi}\) has data \[  egin{split} \mathcal C_{N,\chi}(c_a) &=\cos\! igl(N(1-\chi)	au_a igr),\ \mathcal C_{N,\chi}'(c_a) &=- rac{N(1-\chi)\sin\! igl(N(1-\chi)	au_a igr)} {2\sin	au_a}, \end{split} \qquad \mathcal C_{N,\chi}(-2)=1\quad(N\ {m odd}). 	ag{7} \] Full Hermite interpolation defines it for every complex \(\chi\). The exact endpoints are \[ \mathcal C_{N,1}=1,\qquad \mathcal C_{N,0}=\eta\,1. 	ag{8} \] At \(\chi=j/N\), \(0\le j\le N\), it is the original Chebyshev coupon \(T_{N-j}(-z/2)\), reduced only in a traced variable. Fix an original compiled numerator \(F_N(z_1,\ldots,z_m;\mathbf u)\), independent of the parameters below. The \(z_v\) are distinct contracted algebra copies. Every original identity/turn kernel, other coupon and fixed scalar remains in \(F_N\); the variables \(\mathbf u\) remain ordinary free-boundary variables. For the circle-tree source one can take the original product of same-index kernels. Define \[ Z_N(\mathbf n, oldsymbol\chi;\mathbf u)= \phi_N^{\otimes m}\! \left[F_N\prod_{v=1}^m R_{n_v}(z_v) \mathcal C_{N,\chi_v}(z_v)ight], \qquad \widetilde Z_N= \left(\prod_v C_{N,n_v}^{-1}ight)Z_N. 	ag{9} \] If two variable crossing insertions occur at different positions of a compiled word, they are kept in their separate algebra copies; they are not commuted through a physical turn. Formula (9) covers them by the original finite kernel compiler. At integral \(\mathbf n\) and \( oldsymbol\chi=\mathbf1\), (9) is the original prescribed source. At other parameters it is a specified analytic family, not a new topological filling operation. ## 2. The charge space is faithful, and the heat equation is exact Write \(y=1-\chi\), and let \(\mathcal E_N\) be the span of \[ \cos(N	au_a y),\qquad y\sin(N	au_a y) \quad(0\le a<\lfloor N/2floor), \qquad 1\quad(N\ {m odd}). 	ag{10} \] These are functions of \(\chi\), with the indicated \(y=1-\chi\). **Theorem 1.** The map \[ \mathcal O_N:\mathcal A_N\longrightarrow\mathcal E_N,\qquad f\longmapsto\phi_N(f\mathcal C_{N,\chi}) 	ag{11} \] is an isomorphism. In particular \(\dim\mathcal E_N=N\). It intertwines multiplication by \(\mathscr T_N\) with \(-N^{-2}\partial_\chi^2\). Consequently (9) is entire in all its parameters and satisfies \[  oxed{\qquad \partial_{n_v}\widetilde Z_N =- rac{i}{4\pi N}\partial_{\chi_v}^2\widetilde Z_N \qquad(1\le v\le m). \qquad} 	ag{12} \] Its initial datum is exactly \(\widetilde Z_N(\mathbf0, oldsymbol\chi;\mathbf u)\). The equations uniquely determine it in \(\mathcal E_N^{\otimes m}\), coefficientwise in the free variables. *Proof.* From (3) and (7), the observation (11) is \[ \mathcal O_N(f)=\sum_a\{A_a(f)\cos(N	au_a y) +B_a(f)y\sin(N	au_a y)\} +\mathbf1_{N\ {m odd}}f(-2), 	ag{13} \] where \[ A_a(f)=\eta\{4\sin^2	au_a\,f'(c_a)-c_af(c_a)\},\qquad B_a(f)=-2\eta N\sin	au_a\,f(c_a). 	ag{14} \] The positive \(	au_a\) are distinct, and none has zero sine. Exponential polynomials at distinct frequencies are independent; expanding the sine and cosine in their two frequencies also proves independence of the two functions at each \(a\). The optional constant has a different frequency. Thus (10) has dimension \(N\). Equations (14) recover each value first and then each derivative, while the constant recovers the odd simple-node value. This proves the isomorphism, including the nilpotent coordinates. The equality \[ \partial_\chi^2\mathcal C_{N,\chi} =-N^2\mathscr T_N\mathcal C_{N,\chi} \quad\hbox{in }\mathcal A_N 	ag{15} \] can be checked on the angular representatives \(\partial_\chi^2\cos(N(1-\chi)t)=-N^2t^2\cos(N(1-\chi)t)\). Taking their spectral first derivatives gives exactly the product rule in the double local factors. The odd simple value is zero on both sides. This is a full-Hermite identity, not just a nodal one. It proves the intertwining assertion. Differentiating (5) and using (15) inside (9) proves (12). The space \(\mathcal E_N\) is invariant under \(\partial_\chi^2\). For example, if \(\lambda=N	au_a\), then \[ \partial_\chi^2\cos(\lambda y)=-\lambda^2\cos(\lambda y),\qquad \partial_\chi^2(y\sin(\lambda y)) =-\lambda^2y\sin(\lambda y)+2\lambda\cos(\lambda y). 	ag{16} \] These are the actual size-two normal blocks; the odd constant is the remaining simple block. Thus (12) is an ordinary finite-dimensional constant-matrix evolution, independently in each coordinate: \[ \widetilde Z_N(\mathbf n, oldsymbol\chi) =\exp\!\left[- rac{i}{4\pi N} \sum_v n_v\partial_{\chi_v}^2ight] \widetilde Z_N(\mathbf0, oldsymbol\chi). 	ag{17} \] The operators commute, proving uniqueness and tensorization. All statements commute with ordinary free-boundary differentiation. \(\square\) Faithfulness here concerns the whole function of the charges. A single value of that function, in particular its value at \( oldsymbol\chi=\mathbf1\), is still one prescribed observation. The \(N\)-dimensional initial datum has not been compressed to a geometric line. This theorem also retains coherent low Newton coefficients. With the original basis and pairing \(\phi_N(e_i e_j)=\mathbf1_{i+j=D}\), set \(\alpha_r(f)=[e_r]\operatorname{rem}_{P_N}f=\phi_N(e_{D-r}f)\). Putting \(e_{D-r}f\) in (11) gives (12)--(17) for the entire charged extension of \(\alpha_r(R_n f)\). Finite sums such as \[ \sum_{r<\lfloor N/2floor} \alpha_r(R_n f)\alpha_r(R_p g) 	ag{18} \] therefore have the same tensorized exact reduction, with their original signs and common index retained. No termwise absolute value or semisimple projection enters this step. ## 3. Convergent Gaussian contours and arbitrary translations For one real \(n
e0\), put \[ \sigma=\operatorname{sgn}n,\qquad v_n=e^{-i\sigma\pi/4}, \qquad \mathfrak G_n[f](\chi) =\sqrt{ rac{N}{|n|}} \int_{\mathbb R}e^{-\pi Nr^2/|n|} f(\chi+v_n r)\,dr. 	ag{19} \] This integral is absolutely convergent for every \(f\in\mathcal E_N\), including its derivatives in any of the finite parameters. **Theorem 2.** For all \(f\in\mathcal E_N\), \[ \mathfrak G_n[f] =\exp[-i n\partial_\chi^2/(4\pi N)]f. 	ag{20} \] Equivalently, with the line oriented by increasing real \(r\), \[ \mathfrak G_n[f](\chi) =e^{i\sigma\pi/4}\sqrt{ rac{N}{|n|}} \int_{\chi+v_n\mathbb R} e^{-i\pi N(y-\chi)^2/n}f(y)\,dy. 	ag{21} \] The line in (21) may be replaced by \(\chi+b+v_n\mathbb R\) for any finite \(b\in\mathbb C\). For \(J=\{v:n_v
e0\}\), applying these formulas in every coordinate of (17), and leaving the others fixed, gives an exact absolutely convergent integral for the whole original source: \[  oxed{\quad Z_N(\mathbf n, oldsymbol\chi;\mathbf u) =\left(\prod_v C_{N,n_v}ight) \left(\prod_{v\in J}\mathfrak G_{n_v}^{(\chi_v)}ight) Z_N(\mathbf0, oldsymbol\chi;\mathbf u). \quad} 	ag{22} \] Each of its charge lines can be independently translated through a specified target charge. All attached spectators, mixed normals and ordinary free-boundary derivatives remain in the initial function. *Proof.* For \(f(\chi)=e^{\lambda\chi}\), elementary completion of the square in the real Gaussian gives \[ \mathfrak G_n[f](\chi) =e^{\lambda\chi} \exp\!\left( rac{|n|v_n^2\lambda^2}{4\pi N}ight) =e^{\lambda\chi-i n\lambda^2/(4\pi N)}. 	ag{23} \] The identity holds for every complex \(\lambda\) by absolute convergence and the entire Gaussian identity. Differentiating in \(\lambda\) also proves it for \(\chi e^{\lambda\chi}\). Every function in (10) is a linear combination of these functions, so (20) follows, with the normal blocks included. Changing variable \(y=\chi+v_n r\) proves the prefactor and orientation in (21). For a compact set of free-boundary parameters, every initial function in \(\mathcal E_N^{\otimes m}\) has a bound of the form \[ |Z_N(\mathbf0,\mathbf y;\mathbf u)| \le A_N\prod_v(1+|y_v|) \exp\!\left(\pi D\sum_v|\Im y_v|ight). 	ag{24} \] The finite number \(A_N\) retains the actual full source and can grow exponentially with \(N\); no uniform estimate for it is asserted. The same form of bound holds for fixed derivatives, with their actual constants. Formula (24) follows directly from (10)--(14). On the two connectors \(y=\chi\pm v_n R+s b\), \(0\le s\le1\), the real Gaussian exponent is at most \[ - rac{\pi N}{|n|}R^2+O_N(R+1). 	ag{25} \] The source in (24) contributes only another exponential linear in \(R\), times a polynomial. The connector integrals tend to zero as \(R	o\infty\). The integrand is entire, so Cauchy's theorem proves the translated-line identity. This argument is at each fixed \(N\); it does not replace (24) by a subexponential estimate. In several coordinates the Gaussian quadratic dominates the sum of the linear growth bounds. Fubini's theorem and successive one-variable translations are therefore legitimate, proving (22). Coefficientwise polynomial dependence, or uniformity on a compact set of ordinary boundary variables, proves the derivative statements. \(\square\) In particular the new charge contours have no factorial poles or physical grid poles. Those finite-source contributions have already been combined into the entire initial function. Passing through a target point by translation is an exact contour statement; it is not yet a descent estimate for the full integrand. ## 4. The original primitive action and the two Schur complements Here specialize to an original circle-tree component on a regular canonical positive edge chart. Keep every outside complex angle fixed. Write \[ W(\mathbf t)=\sum_{e=vw}\psi(t_v,t_w),\qquad P_0(\mathbf t)=\left(\sum_{e
i v}r_{v,e}ight)_v,\qquad J_0=\partial_{\mathbf t}P_0,\qquad W_{\mathbf t}=-P_0/\pi. 	ag{26} \] The phases and meridian increments have their original normalization. Let \(D_{\mathbf n}=\operatorname{diag}(n_v)\). The filled primitive phase, excluding only the explicit carrier in (5), is \[ \Phi_{\mathbf n, oldsymbol\chi}(\mathbf t) =W(\mathbf t)+ rac{i}{4\pi}\mathbf t^{\mathsf T} D_{\mathbf n}\mathbf t -i oldsymbol\chi^{\mathsf T}\mathbf t. 	ag{27} \] Its critical equation and Hessian are \[ P_{\mathbf n}:=P_0- rac i2D_{\mathbf n}\mathbf t =-\pi i oldsymbol\chi,\qquad \Phi_{\mathbf t\mathbf t}=-J_{\mathbf n}/\pi,\qquad J_{\mathbf n}=J_0- rac i2D_{\mathbf n}. 	ag{28} \] Let \(J=\{v:n_v
e0\}\), let \(E:\mathbb C^J	o\mathbb C^m\) be the coordinate inclusion, and set \(D_J=\operatorname{diag}(n_v)_{v\in J}\). The charge variables outside \(J\) are kept equal to \(\chi_v\). Before any stationary elimination the corresponding joint phase is \[ \mathcal Q(\mathbf t,\mathbf y_J) =W(\mathbf t)-i\mathbf y^{\mathsf T}\mathbf t -i\pi(\mathbf y_J- oldsymbol\chi_J)^{\mathsf T} D_J^{-1}(\mathbf y_J- oldsymbol\chi_J). 	ag{29} \] Its charge stationarity is exactly \[ \mathbf y_J= oldsymbol\chi_J- rac{D_J\mathbf t_J}{2\pi}. 	ag{30} \] Substitution in (29) gives (27) with no additive constant. Thus the charge Gaussian supplies the actual signed quadratic crossing action. At any original positive critical point \(\mathbf t_*\), (30) is a finite charge point. Theorem 2 permits the actual charge lines to pass through it. The positive period theorem gives \(\Re J_0>0\); adding the purely imaginary diagonal in (28) preserves this property for real signed \(\mathbf n\). Hence both \(J_0\) and \(J_{\mathbf n}\) are invertible there. Locally solve \(P_0(\mathbf t)=-\pi i\mathbf y\), with the outside angles fixed, and define the zero-power critical action \[ S_0(\mathbf y)=W(\mathbf t(\mathbf y)) -i\mathbf y^{\mathsf T}\mathbf t(\mathbf y). 	ag{31} \] This is a local classical generating function. We have not asserted that the entire zero-power source has a single asymptotic with phase \(S_0\) on the translated charge lines. Differentiation gives \[ (S_0)_{\mathbf y}=-i\mathbf t,\qquad (S_0)_{\mathbf y\mathbf y}=-\pi J_0^{-1}. 	ag{32} \] The charge phase obtained by eliminating \(\mathbf t\) is \[ \Psi(\mathbf y_J)=S_0(\mathbf y) -i\pi(\mathbf y_J- oldsymbol\chi_J)^{\mathsf T} D_J^{-1}(\mathbf y_J- oldsymbol\chi_J). 	ag{33} \] At (30), its Hessian and determinant are \[ H_{m ch}=-\pi E^{\mathsf T}J_0^{-1}E-2\pi iD_J^{-1}, \qquad  oxed{\quad \det H_{m ch}=(-2\pi i)^{|J|}  rac{\det J_{\mathbf n}} {\det J_0\det D_J}. \quad} 	ag{34} \] In particular this charge critical point is nondegenerate. For a direct verification, the joint Hessian of (29), in the order \((\mathbf t,\mathbf y_J)\), is \[  egin{pmatrix} -J_0/\pi&-iE\ -iE^{\mathsf T}&-2\pi iD_J^{-1} \end{pmatrix}. 	ag{35} \] Its \(\mathbf t\)-Schur complement is \(H_{m ch}\), while its \(\mathbf y_J\)-Schur complement is \(-J_{\mathbf n}/\pi\). Equating the two determinant factorizations proves (34), including mixed signs and zero powers omitted from \(J\). If a separately justified local term of the zero-power charged source has amplitude \(A_0\), the square of its formal Gaussian density after (21) is multiplied by \[  rac{\det J_0}{\det J_{\mathbf n}}. 	ag{36} \] Indeed the square of the exact prefactor in (21), multiplied by \((2\pi/N)^{|J|}/\det(-H_{m ch})\), is precisely that ratio. This is a local density identity. A contributing cycle and its orientation are still needed to infer any actual leading coefficient. At \(J=\varnothing\) the Gaussian transformation is the identity. Finally the carrier has not been suppressed from the original answer: \[ \prod_v C_{N,n_v} =\exp\!\left(N rac{i\pi}{4}\sum_vn_vight) \exp\!\left(- rac{i\pi}{2}\sum_vn_v + rac{i\pi}{4N}\sum_vn_vight). 	ag{37} \] Thus (27)--(36) compare the carrier-normalized actions; (22) and (37) restore their original phase and finite subscalar exactly. ## 5. What the reduction leaves to estimate The initial datum in (22) is the full function \(Z_N(\mathbf0, oldsymbol\chi;\mathbf u)\), not its value at \( oldsymbol\chi=\mathbf1\), and not a local formal geometric unit. For example, (8) gives the exact identity \[ Z_N(\mathbf0,\mathbf0;\mathbf u) =\eta^m Z_N(\mathbf0,\mathbf1;\mathbf u). 	ag{38} \] The known small-charge initializer is on a box separated from zero; the original coupon source at zero is not a fresh complete-edge initial value. Its companion phases and full Hermite aliases cannot be replaced by one chosen primitive branch inside the Gaussian integral. The new entire contours remove pole avoidance as a condition on charge translations. They do not remove the initial source's exponential growth, its competing actions, or cancellation among its branches. To use (33) for the complete integral still requires a controlled expansion of that actual initial function on the chosen charge contours and a bound on their complement. Formula (34) proves local nondegeneracy, not that the straight translated contour is a descent contour or that its geometric contribution survives the rest. The earlier Gaussian Newton frame resolves coefficient vectors by a positive family and expresses the crossing of a frame vector by a Gaussian integral of a finite Pochhammer product. It retains separate cup and closing observations. Here the heat operator acts directly on the original entire charged observation, its initial datum is the actual zero-power compiled source, and the size-two charge blocks in (16) preserve the normal data. Neither representation by itself proves a filled-action upper bound or noncancellation for arbitrary short components. ## Pinned direct sources * notes/research_real_power_source_transport.md, SHA256 7dac43d1a5fac6b4602a3aab12bfe977cb42a61b36d40a2fb8517e29566df8ea: the canonical entire crossing group, its angular logarithm and exact carrier, all physical normals, and prior finite-generator scope. * notes/research_dominant_saddle_transport.md, SHA256 413940497a23e884d726b91f9c0ebc01994fef8216811ed2c6fb0838fc80bb04: the original entire full-Hermite coupon in Section 9, its exact endpoints, and the distinction between an integrand coefficient and the original cycle coefficient. * notes/research_actual_source_dualizing_residue.md, SHA256 806f8e4530736632830a15cff19f4c0f72e659fa6280d48005c4184a6ffc9afb: original trace normalization, perfect Newton pairing, kernels and arbitrary compiled contractions with unreduced free boundaries. * notes/research_positive_period_inverse_descent.md, SHA256 b9b5c3d61c704700e9431315cf50591c921ebeb95becdf6a52877606bdbc4565: original phase derivatives, canonical period normalization and accretive Jacobian on the positive circle-tree domain. * notes/research_gaussian_frame_newton_transport.md, SHA256 b6ed7fa19097323f76b0b22fb4fc7361b9d4e52c3f19d17c12d94c6fff623af9: prior exact positive Gaussian frame and crossing integral, cited for coverage and the different role of its boundary observations. Only written proofs, source-text reads and file hashes enter this note. No mathematical code, numerical evaluation, test or compilation was run. Frozen manuscripts and other authors' notes were not edited.

title: Actual Euclidean off-matching windows and their Ward current
text:
# Actual Euclidean off-matching windows and their Ward current Private written proof, 19 November 2026. An actual total intertwiner can be restricted by a correlated coherent window which keeps the entire real lowering-observable matching locus and every occupation endpoint. The discarded operator and the resulting Ward current have exponentially small trace norm relative to the norm of the original whole operator. The estimate is in the physical coefficient Euclidean metric, with the actual meridian family and caps. This is a positive norm estimate for an explicit marked operator. Its budget is the whole-operator norm, not a selected geometric contribution. It neither isolates a geometric component nor estimates the contribution of the original relative cycle. The complete directs W and B, pinned below, supply the actual source comparison and its Euclidean boundary-kernel bridge. The localization argument is proved here from the finite lowering matrices; no estimate in the binomial Hilbert metric is transferred to this metric. ## 1. Actual matrices, real observable, and window Fix \(m\ge2\), \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), and \[ h=N^{-1},\quad c_0=2\pi i,\quad Q=e^{c_0h},\quad q=e^{\pi ih},\quad M=e^\mu,\quad x=-M/q. 	ag{1} \] On \(V=\operatorname{span}\{w_0,\ldots,w_d\}\), the displayed vectors are orthonormal. All norms use the tensor coefficient metric; \(\|\cdot\|\) is operator norm and \(\|\cdot\|_1\) is trace norm. Use exactly \[ Ew_a=(MQ^{-a}-M^{-1})w_{a-1}\ (a>0),\quad Ew_0=0,\qquad Kw_a=xQ^{-a}w_a, \] \[ E_\Sigma=\sum_{j=1}^m E_jK_{j+1}\cdots K_m. 	ag{2} \] Every operator in this note acts on \(V^{\otimes m}\). Let \(W_N(M)\) be a holomorphic actual family on a buffered scaled meridian disk, with \[ E_\Sigma(M)W_N(M)=W_N(M)E_\Sigma(M). 	ag{3} \] In particular any actual fixed braid word satisfies the required lowering identity. Its original scalar and prescribed current-free marks remain in \(W_N\). No norm bound for \(W_N\) is assumed. Use B's coefficient-Euclidean coherent vectors and probability measure, \[ \psi_z=(1+|z|^2)^{-d/2}\sum_{a=0}^d\sqrt{ inom da}\,z^a w_a, \qquad d
u(z)= rac{d\Re z\,d\Im z}{\pi(1+|z|^2)^2}. 	ag{4} \] Write tensor products as \(\psi_{\mathbf z}\). On a chart with \(z_j
e0,\infty\), define \[ p_j= rac{|z_j|^2}{1+|z_j|^2},\qquad e(z_j)= rac{z_j}{|z_j|}(e^{-c_0p_j}-1),\qquad k(z_j)=-e^{-c_0p_j}, \] \[ \epsilon(\mathbf z) =\sum_{j=1}^m e(z_j)\prod_{\ell>j}k(z_\ell). 	ag{5} \] These are the principal values for the real Euclidean coherent states in (4), as verified below. They are not the weak values of an arbitrary off-diagonal kernel. They extend continuously to the endpoints by \(e(0)=e(\infty)=0\) and \(k(0)=k(\infty)=-1\); analytic estimates use only strict charts. Here is an explicit fixed window. Choose a smooth \(0\le\kappa\le1\) with compact support in \((\mathbb C^	imes)^m	imes(\mathbb C^	imes)^m\), a number \(\gamma>0\), and a smooth function \(0\le\vartheta\le1\) on \([0,\infty)\) which is zero on \([0,\gamma^2]\) and one on \([4\gamma^2,\infty)\). Set \[ b(\mathbf y,\mathbf z) =\kappa(\mathbf y,\mathbf z)\, \vartheta(|\epsilon(\mathbf y)-\epsilon(\mathbf z)|^2), \qquad \chi=1-b. 	ag{6} \] Extend \(b\) by zero outside the protected chart. Thus \(\chi=1\) near every pair with \(\epsilon(\mathbf y)=\epsilon(\mathbf z)\), and near every occupation endpoint in either set of variables. On the support of \(b\) the observable gap is at least \(\gamma\). Both functions are independent of \(N\) and \(\mu\). Define the actual correlated marked operator \[ C_{\chi,N}(M)=N^{2m}\int\chi(\mathbf y,\mathbf z) |\psi_{\mathbf y}angle \langle\psi_{\mathbf y},W_N(M)\psi_{\mathbf z}angle \langle\psi_{\mathbf z}|\, d
u^{[m]}(\mathbf y)d
u^{[m]}(\mathbf z), \] \[ R_N=W_N-C_{\chi,N}. 	ag{7} \] This is a finite matrix integral. A correlated \(\chi\) need not factor into separate input and output windows, and \(C_{\chi,N}\) is not asserted to be positive or a projection. **Theorem.** Fix \(0<\eta<\eta'<\pi\). There are \(C,c>0\), independent of \(N,W_N\), such that on \(|N\mu|\le\eta'\), \[ \|R_N(M)\|_1+\|[E_\Sigma(M),C_{\chi,N}(M)]\|_1 \le C N^{2m}e^{-cN}\|W_N(M)\|. 	ag{8} \] Constants may depend on \(m,\eta'\) and the fixed window. Put \(\mathcal W_N=\sup_{|N\mu|\le\eta'}\|W_N(e^\mu)\|\). They do not depend on the word length or integer filling powers inside \(W_N\). Holomorphy is assumed on a neighborhood of this closed larger disk. For every fixed \(r\ge0\), on the smaller disk, \[ N^{-r}\left(\|\partial_\mu^rR_N\|_1+ \|\partial_\mu^r[E_\Sigma,C_{\chi,N}]\|_1ight) \le C_rN^{2m}e^{-cN}\mathcal W_N. 	ag{9} \] The norms are literal matrix norms in the stated metric. The constants and exponent do not depend on a phase choice or a nonzero entry of \(W_N\). All finite levels are included after enlarging \(C,C_r\). ## 2. Exact local rows and the cap-safe power estimate Represent a vector locally as \(\psi_z(a)H(a/N)\), and write \(t=a/N\). Ratios of the coefficients in (4) give the exact rows \[  egin{split} \mathcal E_{z,h,\mu}H(t) &=z\sqrt{ rac{1-h-t}{t+h}}\, (e^\mu e^{-c_0(t+h)}-e^{-\mu})H(t+h),\ \mathcal K_{z,h,\mu}H(t) &=-e^\mu e^{-\pi ih}e^{-c_0t}H(t). \end{split}	ag{10} \] They are used only in a fixed complex tube about a strict subinterval of \((0,1)\), where the square roots have analytic branches agreeing with their positive real values. No analytic extension across a cap is asserted. The actual adjoint lowering row is \[ \mathcal E^*_{z,h,\mu}H(t) =z^{-1}\sqrt{ rac{t}{1-t}}\, (e^{ ar\mu}e^{c_0t}-e^{- ar\mu})H(t-h), 	ag{11} \] and the Cartan adjoint is the conjugate diagonal row. The adjoint rows are pointwise statements in \(\mu\), not holomorphic differentiation in \( ar\mu\). Compose these rows in the ordered sum (2). On each protected compact coherent chart, both \(E_\Sigma\) and its adjoint act on amplitudes by a fixed finite set of shifts of size at most \(h\) in each coordinate, with uniformly bounded holomorphic coefficients on a fixed tube about the corresponding binomial means. At \(h=\mu=0\), their multiplication values at the mean are respectively \(\epsilon(\mathbf z)\) and \(\overline{\epsilon(\mathbf z)}\). This follows directly from (10)--(11) at \(t_j=p_j\), including every factor in (2). For \(|\mu|\le\eta'h\), the sum of the local coefficients differs from that principal value by at most \[ C(|\mathbf t-\mathbf p|+h). 	ag{12} \] Independently, the finite matrices in (2) and their adjoints have uniformly bounded Euclidean norm on the scaled collar. Indeed \(\|E\|\le |M|+|M|^{-1}\) and \(\|K^{\pm1}\|=|M|^{\pm1}\). They have propagation at most one in the maximum occupation distance. These global facts use the exact zero arrows at the caps. Let \(D_N=E_\Sigma-\epsilon(\mathbf z)I\). The same argument below applies to \(E_\Sigma^*-\overline{\epsilon(\mathbf z)}I\). Choose \(k=\lfloor\delta Nfloor\ge1\), and put \[ ho=A\sqrt{k/N}. 	ag{13} \] Choose \(A\) first and then \(\delta\) sufficiently small. The polydisk of radius \(2ho\) about the mean lies in the coefficient tube. Use \(k\) nested polydisks between radii \(2ho\) and \(ho\), with radius decrement \(ho/k\). The shift condition \(kh\leho/2\) holds after reducing \(\delta\). Multiplication estimate (12), and Cauchy's estimate for each shifted difference \(H(\mathbf t+h\mathbf s)-H(\mathbf t)\), give at every step \[ \|\mathcal D_N H\|_{m next} \le C\left(ho+h+ rac{k}{Nho}ight)\|H\|_{m previous}. 	ag{14} \] Thus, for all \(0\le j\le k\), the exact sampled amplitude of \(D_N^j\psi_{\mathbf z}\) on \(|\mathbf a/N-\mathbf p|\leho\) is bounded by \[ q_\delta^j,\qquad q_\delta=C(A+A^{-1}+1)\sqrt\delta. 	ag{15} \] Every contributing path there stays in the local tube. The same nested \(k\) domains are used for all \(j\le k\). The complementary output indices require a different argument. Let \(P_{m out}\) project onto \(|\mathbf a/N-\mathbf p|>ho\). Exact finite propagation gives \[ P_{m out}D_N^j =P_{m out}D_N^j \mathbf1_{\{|\mathbf a/N-\mathbf p|>ho-jh\}}. 	ag{16} \] Since \(jh\leho/2\), only the initial binomial tail outside \(ho/2\) can reach these outputs. Intermediate paths may touch a cap; the global finite matrix norm, rather than (10), bounds them. The squared coefficients of \(\psi_{\mathbf z}\) are independent binomial probabilities with means \((1-h)p_j\). Their tail obeys \[ \mathbb P(|\mathbf a/N-\mathbf p|>r) \le C e^{-c_1Nr^2} 	ag{17} \] when \(h\le r/2\). One direct proof uses the Bernoulli moment generating function: the second derivative of \(\log(1-p+pe^\lambda)\) is at most \(1/4\) for real \(\lambda\). Integration twice, Markov's inequality, optimization in \(\lambda\), and a union bound give (17), including the \(O(h)\) shift of the mean. Equations (16)--(17) and \(\|D_N\|\le C_0\) show that the outside norm is at most \(C C_0^j e^{-c_2A^2k}\). Therefore \[ \|D_N^j\psi_{\mathbf z}\| \le q_\delta^j+C C_0^j e^{-c_2A^2k}, \qquad 0\le j\le k. 	ag{18} \] For any prescribed fixed \(B>0\), choose \(A\) so large that the second term is at most \(Ce^{-Bk}\) for every \(j\le k\). Then choose \(\delta\) to make \(q_\delta\) small and all tubes valid. The two terms remain a sum: the tail is not absorbed into \(q_\delta^j\). ## 3. Intertwining and the correlated trace-norm estimate Fix protected \(\mathbf y,\mathbf z\), and put \(\alpha=\epsilon(\mathbf y)\), \( eta=\epsilon(\mathbf z)\), \(D_+=E_\Sigma-\alpha I\), \(D_-=E_\Sigma- eta I\). Equation (3) gives \[ (\alpha- eta)W_N=W_ND_- -D_+W_N. 	ag{19} \] Left and right multiplication commute. Expanding its \(k\)-th power exactly and taking the coherent entry proves \[ |\alpha- eta|^k|\langle\psi_{\mathbf y},W_N\psi_{\mathbf z}angle| \le\|W_N\|\sum_{j=0}^k inom kj \|(D_+^*)^j\psi_{\mathbf y}\|\, \|D_-^{k-j}\psi_{\mathbf z}\|. 	ag{20} \] Apply (18) to both factors. The sum is bounded by \[ (2q_\delta)^k+ C e^{-Bk}(1+q_\delta)^k+C e^{-2Bk}2^k. 	ag{21} \] First choose \(B\) sufficiently large in terms of \(\gamma\), then \(A\) as above, and finally \(\delta\) with \(q_\delta<\min(1/4,\gamma/4)\). Dividing (21) by \(|\alpha- eta|^k\ge\gamma^k\) gives, uniformly on the support of \(b\) in (6) and on the scaled meridian collar, \[ |\langle\psi_{\mathbf y},W_N(M)\psi_{\mathbf z}angle| \le C e^{-cN}\|W_N(M)\|. 	ag{22} \] B's exact resolution is \(N\int|\psi_zangle\langle\psi_z|d
u=I\). Applying it on both sides of \(W_N\) shows that (7) with \(\chi=1\) is exactly \(W_N\). Hence \(R_N\) is the same integral with multiplier \(b=1-\chi\). Each outer rank-one matrix has nuclear norm one. Its middle scalar satisfies (22), and the product measure has mass one. Therefore \[ \|R_N(M)\|_1 \le C N^{2m}e^{-cN}\|W_N(M)\|. 	ag{23} \] Since \(W_N\) intertwines \(E_\Sigma\), \([E_\Sigma,C_{\chi,N}]=-[E_\Sigma,R_N]\). The inequality \(\|[E_\Sigma,R_N]\|_1\le2\|E_\Sigma\|\|R_N\|_1\) proves (8). The fixed cutoff and coherent vectors make \(R_N\) a holomorphic matrix family in \(\mu\). Its commutator is holomorphic as well. Cauchy's formula in the finite-dimensional trace-norm space, on the buffer between \(\eta/N\) and \(\eta'/N\), proves (9). In particular these are actual derivatives of the capped meridian matrices, not derivatives of a root coherent symbol. For example the first current derivative is \([\,\partial_\mu E_\Sigma,C_{\chi,N}\,] +[\,E_\Sigma,\partial_\mu C_{\chi,N}\,]\); neither term is omitted. ## 4. Degree pinching and the original closed source If the actual word has integer degree zero, put \(J_\Sigma=\sum_jJ_j\), \(U_	heta=e^{i	heta J_\Sigma}\), and \[ \overline C_{\chi,N} = rac1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi} U_	heta C_{\chi,N}U_	heta^{-1}\,d	heta. 	ag{24} \] Then \(\overline C_{\chi,N}\) has degree zero and \(W_N-\overline C_{\chi,N}\) is the same average of \(R_N\). Unitary invariance and the triangle inequality contract its trace norm. Since \(U_	heta E_\Sigma U_	heta^{-1}=e^{-i	heta}E_\Sigma\), \[ [E_\Sigma,\overline C_{\chi,N}] = rac1{2\pi}\int e^{i	heta} U_	heta[E_\Sigma,C_{\chi,N}]U_	heta^{-1}\,d	heta. 	ag{25} \] Thus (8)--(9) hold for the degree-preserving window too, including every true meridian jet. For clarity the original coupons and supported projections of W and B are \[  egin{split} Q_{m pt}&=\Pi_0\otimes K_2^{-d}\otimes K_Z^{-d},& Q_{m top}&=|0angle\langle d|\otimes|dangle\langle0| \otimes K_Z^{-d},\ P&=\Pi_0\otimes(I-\Pi_0)\otimes I_Z,& L&=\mathbf1_{\{J_1+J_2\le d-1\}}\otimes I_Z , \end{split} \] where \(Z=V^{\otimes(m-2)}\), \(\Pi_0=|0angle\langle0|\), and the empty spectator tensor has \(K_Z=I\). Put \(\Phi_M(C)=\operatorname{Tr}(Q_{m pt}C)\). Both coupons have degree zero, so (24) changes neither trace pairing. For either choice \(C=C_{\chi,N}\) or \(\overline C_{\chi,N}\), the actual compressed current is \[ Y=L[E_\Sigma,C]P. 	ag{26} \] Compression contracts trace norm. B's exact vacuum-input resolution then supplies a concrete boundary-kernel estimate: \[ N^{-r}\|\mathcal K_{\partial_\mu^rY}\|_{L^2} \le C_rN^{m+1/2}e^{-cN}\mathcal W_N. 	ag{27} \] Indeed \(\|\mathcal K_Y\|_{L^2}=N^{-m+1/2}\|Y\|_{m HS}\) and \(\|Y\|_{m HS}\le\|Y\|_1\). The kernel is unnormalized, with the first input head at the vacuum and all remaining caps retained. There are also direct closed-source estimates. The coupons have uniformly bounded operator norm on a fixed scaled collar, and \(\Phi_M(W_N)=\operatorname{Tr}(Q_{m top}W_N)\) by (3) and W. Consequently, for every fixed \(r\), on the smaller collar, \[  egin{split} N^{-r}\left|\partial_\mu^r \{\Phi_M(C)-\Phi_M(W_N)\}ight| &\le C_rN^{2m}e^{-cN}\mathcal W_N,\ N^{-r}\left|\partial_\mu^r \{\Phi_M(C)-\operatorname{Tr}(Q_{m top}C)\}ight| &\le C_rN^{2m}e^{-cN}\mathcal W_N . \end{split}	ag{28} \] For the second row subtract the exact zero discrepancy for \(W_N\) and pair \(C-W_N\) with \(Q_{m pt}-Q_{m top}\); this gives the stated bound without an additional primitive factor. All pivot derivatives are included. Equivalently W's polynomial Ward identity applies to the small current in (26). Root-only commutation would not justify (9), (27), or (28); the whole-family identity (3) is used. The budget \(\mathcal W_N\) may itself grow exponentially. Neither \(c\) nor \(\mathcal W_N\) is calibrated here against a geometric action or a nonzero top-source contribution. The window keeps the whole real matching locus and all endpoint charts, so no geometric component or original relative-cycle coefficient has been selected. Independent coherent arguments can describe complex mixed coordinates, but this fact does not turn the real principal values in (5) into a proved geometric boundary-decay estimate. title: The low-index complete-end kernel at even levels
text: # The low-index complete-end kernel at even levels Research proof, 3 November 2026. Frozen manuscripts are unchanged. The last physical color at an even level is close to the complete color, but they are different. The full kernel cannot simply be evaluated at the last physical row and called the complete-end kernel. This note proves the needed comparison for its low-index part. The comparison is relative, so it preserves the nonzero coefficient. The proof uses an exact Chebyshev interpolation formula. Its alternating weights have sum one. The actual row recurrence controls the variation of the values against those weights; no positivity of the final quantum trace is assumed. ## 1. The original low-index kernel Let \(N=2m\), \(J=m-1\), and \(\theta=\pi/N\). Use the original Newton polynomials and physical colors \[ e_k(z)=\frac{\prod_{a=0}^{k-1}(c_a-z)}{S_k^2},\qquad c_a=2\cos((2a+1)\theta),\qquad S_k=\prod_{a=1}^k2\sin(a\theta). \tag{1} \] Define \[ L_N(w)=\sum_{k=0}^{m-1}e_k(-2)e_k(w),\qquad F_{j,N}(w)=K_N(c_j,w). \tag{2} \] Thus \(L_N\) is the original complete-end kernel with its radical Newton indices \(k\ge m\) removed. At every physical color those removed polynomials vanish. In particular \[ F_{j,N}(w)=\sum_{k=0}^{m-1}e_k(c_j)e_k(w) \quad(0\le j\le J). \tag{3} \] Fix a compact set of free colors \[ \mathcal W_{\gamma,R} =\{w:\Re w\le2-\gamma,\ |w|\le R\}, \qquad \gamma>0, \tag{4} \] and allow constants to depend on this set. All asymptotic statements below are uniform on (4) as the even level tends to infinity. **Theorem 1.** The original low-index kernel satisfies \[ \boxed{\qquad \frac{L_N(w)}{F_{J,N}(w)}=1+O(N^{-1/2}). \qquad} \tag{5} \] The same estimate holds after every fixed number of derivatives in \(w\). In particular, \(L_N\) is nonzero on (4) for all sufficiently large even levels. ## 2. Exact alternating interpolation The \(m\) distinct physical colors are the zeros of \(T_m(z/2)\). Lagrange interpolation of the polynomial of degree at most \(m-1\) in the first variable in (3) therefore gives \[ L_N(w)=\sum_{h=0}^{m-1}(-1)^h a_{h,N} F_{J-h,N}(w),\qquad a_{h,N}=\frac1m\cot\bigl((h+\tfrac12)\theta\bigr)>0. \tag{6} \] For completeness, put \(\varphi_j=(2j+1)\theta\). The Lagrange coefficient at \(z=-2\) is \[ \frac{T_m(-1)}{(-2-c_j)T_m'(c_j/2)/2} =\frac{(-1)^{m+j+1}}m\tan(\varphi_j/2). \tag{7} \] Here \(T_m'(\cos\varphi_j)=m(-1)^j/\sin\varphi_j\). Substitution of \(j=J-h\) proves (6). Applying interpolation to the constant polynomial also proves the exact identity \[ \sum_{h=0}^{m-1}(-1)^h a_{h,N}=1. \tag{8} \] The weights decrease with \(h\), and elementary differentiation of the cotangent gives constants independent of \(N\) such that \[ a_{h,N}\le\frac C{h+1},\qquad 0<a_{h,N}-a_{h+1,N}\le\frac C{(h+1)^2}. \tag{9} \] The second estimate is needed only when \(h<m-1\). For example, use \(\sin x\ge2x/\pi\) on \([0,\pi/2]\) in the derivative \(m^{-1}\theta\csc^2((h+1/2)\theta)\). Also \(a_{m-1,N}=O(N^{-2})\). ## 3. The actual rows vary slowly near the last row The [endpoint Riccati theorem](research_last_physical_row_riccati.md) applies to the original normalized solution, not to an independently chosen approximate solution. Write \[ \rho_r=F_{r,N}/F_{r-1,N},\qquad u_r=\rho_r-1,\qquad Q_r=\frac{\cos(r\theta)}{\sin^3(r\theta)},\qquad r_0=\lfloor N/4\rfloor. \tag{10} \] For all sufficiently large \(N\), it gives, on the entire tail, \[ \Re u_r\ge c Q_r,\qquad |u_r|\le C Q_r, \qquad r_0\le r\le J, \qquad Q_r\asymp (N/2-r)/N. \tag{11} \] The upper bound throughout this tail follows explicitly from that proof. At distance at least \(\sqrt N\) from the endpoint, its ratio error is \(O((N/2-r)^{-1})\), which is \(O((N/2-r)/N)\) there; its limiting root differs from one by \(O(Q_r)\). In the final square-root layer the proof gives \(|u_r|\le C Q_r\) directly. The lower bound is its propagated positive-real barrier. At every earlier row one still has \(\Re\rho_r>1\). Set \[ B_h=F_{J-h,N}/F_{J,N},\qquad B_0=1. \tag{12} \] All ratios are defined by the zero-free physical solution. Equations (11) imply, for \(0\le h\le J-r_0\), \[ \begin{split} |B_h|&\le C\exp(-c h^2/N),\\ |B_h-1|&\le C\min\{h(h+1)/N,1\},\\ |B_{h+1}-B_h|&\le \frac{C(h+1)}N\exp(-c h^2/N). \end{split} \tag{13} \] The final line is used when \(J-h\ge r_0\). Indeed \[ B_{h+1}=B_h/\rho_{J-h},\qquad |\rho_r|\ge1+cQ_r. \tag{14} \] Taking the product in (14), and using \(\log(1+cQ_r)\ge c'Q_r\) on this bounded tail, proves the first estimate in (13). Summing the elementary difference bound \(|B_{h+1}-B_h|\le |u_{J-h}|\), and using \(|B_h|\le1\), proves the second. Retaining the first estimate in the difference bound proves the third. After this tail, monotonicity of the moduli \(|F_{j,N}|\) gives \[ |B_h|\le C e^{-cN},\qquad |B_{h+1}-B_h|\le C e^{-cN} \quad(h>J-r_0). \tag{15} \] ## 4. The alternating sum preserves its coefficient Divide (6) by \(F_{J,N}\), and subtract (8). The error is exactly \[ \sum_{h=0}^{m-1}(-1)^h d_h, \qquad d_h=a_{h,N}(B_h-1). \tag{16} \] Partial sums of \((-1)^h\) have modulus at most one. Summation by parts therefore bounds (16) by \[ |d_{m-1}|+ \sum_{h=0}^{m-2}(a_{h,N}-a_{h+1,N})|B_h-1| +\sum_{h=0}^{m-2}a_{h+1,N}|B_{h+1}-B_h|. \tag{17} \] The endpoint term is \(O(N^{-2})\). By (9), (13), and the bound \(|B_h-1|\le2\), the first sum is at most a constant times \[ \sum_{h\le\sqrt N}\frac1{(h+1)^2}\frac{h(h+1)}N +\sum_{h>\sqrt N}\frac1{(h+1)^2} =O(N^{-1/2}). \tag{18} \] The second sum, through the tail, is bounded by \[ \frac CN\sum_{h\ge0}e^{-c h^2/N} =O(N^{-1/2}). \tag{19} \] Its remaining terms are exponentially small by (15). This proves (5). Apply the argument on a slightly larger compact subset of \(\Re w<2\); Cauchy's formula then proves the derivative estimates. The cancellation in (16) has been estimated relative to the actual last row. This is the point that an absolute bound for the interpolation weights would miss. ## 5. Consequence for the geometric exponential rate Put \[ \Psi(w)=\int_0^{1/2}\Log\lambda(x,w)\,dx, \qquad \lambda(x,w)=\exp\left(2\operatorname{asinh} \left(\frac{\sqrt{2-w}}2\cot\pi x\right)\right). \tag{20} \] The branches and normalization are those of the endpoint theorem. In particular \(\Psi(-2\cos t)=\psi(t,0)\) on the original branch. Since \(J/N=1/2-1/N\), the omitted part of the integral contributes only \(O(N^{-1})\) to its exponent. Combining Theorem 1 with the endpoint theorem gives \[ L_N(w)=\exp\{N\Psi(w)+\widetilde E_N(w)\},\qquad |\partial_w^\ell\widetilde E_N(w)|\le C_\ell\log N \tag{21} \] for every fixed \(\ell\). The logarithm of the quotient in (5) is the branch near zero, so it adds only \(O(N^{-1/2})\), with the same derivative bounds, to the logarithm of the physical row. At odd levels the low-index part at a complete end equals the full kernel, because every radical polynomial vanishes at the simple physical node \(-2\). The odd-level conclusion of the endpoint theorem and (21) thus give a nonzero complete-end **low-index** factor at both parities. In a source calculation the removed radical terms must still be retained and bounded after their original traces. No estimate of the full even-level off-grid kernel is inferred. This qualification is necessary. The [exact radical asymptotic](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_even_complete_radical_asymptotic.md) gives the full kernel different odd- and even-level exponential rates at \(w=(1-3\sqrt3\,i)/2\). At that color the low sector still has the rate proved here. The additional even-level sector is larger before the original traces are taken. ## 6. Reproducing the finite identities The accompanying checker constructs the original Newton polynomials, their last physical rows and their low complete-end sums separately. It checks the interpolation weights and the full finite identity (6). The reported relative errors in (5) are diagnostics; the proof of the uniform estimate is (10)--(19). ~~~sh python3 experiments/check_even_complete_low_kernel.py ~~~ The [saved results](../repro/results/research-even-complete-low-kernel.json) record the code and proof dependencies.

title: Even crossing representatives on the full cover and their left-cut current
Even-twist Ward transport with the original half crossing retained
text: # Even-twist Ward transport with the original half crossing retained Private written proof, 15 November 2026. Every original integer crossing power can be split into its even twist and a retained half crossing. Applying the Ward operation to the even factor gives scalar endpoint deletion on an arbitrary circle tree, without the odd-power derivative coupons. The retained half crossing has a canonical zero-free analytic representative, so its conjugated Ward operator has an explicit local symbol with the original total power. A rank-two endpoint formula records exactly what changes if the canonical spectral sheet is replaced by an unwrapped Gaussian. This organizes an available even-twist factorization into an all-exterior operator and simultaneous-current statement. It does not establish a global contour deformation or the original geometric cycle coefficient. ## 1. Original algebra, normalization and factorization Fix \(N\geq2\) and write \[ D=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\quad \hbar=2\pi i/N,\quad \rho=q-q^{-1},\quad \eta=(-1)^D,\quad \sigma=(-1)^N=-\eta, \qquad \kappa=q^{D^2/2}. \tag{1} \] Every fractional power of \(q\) uses this displayed logarithm. The original algebra, trace and crossing are \[ \mathcal A_N=\mathbb C[z]/(P_N),\quad P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2,\qquad \phi_N=\eta N^2[z^D]\operatorname{rem}_{P_N},\qquad R=\kappa r_N. \tag{2} \] Let \(f_j\) be the degree-below-\(N\) representative of \(r_N^j\). For all signed integers, multiplication in \(\mathcal A_N\) gives \(f_a f_b=f_{a+b}\). In particular every \(f_j\) is a unit. Choose \[ n=m+\epsilon,\qquad m=2P\in2\mathbb Z, \quad\epsilon\in\{0,1,-1\}. \tag{3} \] Keep the half crossing specified by the original marking: when the physical convention is \(n=\epsilon-2p\), take \(P=-p\). No change of the primitive peripheral basis is being made. Set \(c_0=q+q^{-1}\). Let \(\Pi_0\) be its spectral idempotent and \(\Xi_0\) its first-normal element: their respective value/derivative data at \(c_0\) are \((1,0)\) and \((0,1)\), with all other physical data zero. These include the double node at \(N=2\). The original crossing data give \[ f_j(c_0)=1,\qquad f_j'(c_0)=-\frac{jD}{2\rho},\qquad f_j\Xi_0=\Xi_0,\qquad \phi_N(\Xi_0 A)=\sigma\rho^2 A(c_0). \tag{4} \] The last formula is the full Hermite residue, not a reduced-spectrum evaluation rule for arbitrary insertions. ## 2. An exact conjugated Ward operator and scalar current Put \(z(x)=e^x+e^{-x}\). For \(k\geq1\), define the original two adjoint spectral shifts \[ (\mathcal T_k u)(z(x))=u(z(x+k\hbar))+u(z(x-k\hbar)), \tag{5} \] \[ (\mathcal L_k A)(z(x))= \sum_{\delta=\pm1} \frac{\sinh(x+\delta k\hbar)}{\sinh x} A(z(x+\delta k\hbar)). \tag{6} \] Their apparent singularities are removable. Both preserve the full ideal \((P_N)\), and \(\phi_N(A\mathcal T_k u)=\phi_N(u\mathcal L_k A)\). Define, in this full algebra, \[ \begin{split} \mathcal T_k^\epsilon&=M_{f_\epsilon}\mathcal T_kM_{f_\epsilon}^{-1},\\ \mathcal L_k^\epsilon&=M_{f_\epsilon}^{-1}\mathcal L_kM_{f_\epsilon},\\ \mathcal D_{m,k}^\epsilon &=\mathcal L_k^\epsilon -2q^{mk^2}M_{T_{mk}(z/2)}. \end{split} \tag{7} \] Here \(M_f\) means multiplication by \(f\). The inverse and the adjoint have opposite conjugation orders; they have not been identified. **Theorem 1.** For every original polynomial spectator \(A\), including coefficients in a retained boundary algebra, \[ \phi_N\bigl(f_n\mathcal D_{m,k}^\epsilon A\bigr) =E_{m,k}(f_\epsilon A), \tag{8} \] where \(E_{m,k}\) is the original translated Gaussian contour current. In particular, \[ \boxed{\quad \mathcal T_1^\epsilon f_n-2q^mT_m(z/2)f_n =\frac{mN}{\rho}\Xi_0, \qquad \phi_N(f_n\mathcal D_{m,1}^\epsilon A) =\sigma mN\rho\,A(c_0). \quad} \tag{9} \] At a full logarithmic turn, \[ \mathcal D_{m,N}^\epsilon=0. \tag{10} \] **Proof.** The actual even Gaussian satisfies \(\mathcal T_1f_m-2q^mT_mf_m=(mN/\rho)\Xi_0\). Multiply by \(f_\epsilon\), use (4), and then take the original adjoint pairing. This proves (9). More generally the original exact current identity applied to the spectator \(f_\epsilon A\) gives (8), since \(f_mf_\epsilon=f_n\). There is no division by an unknown scalar and no change of the exterior. For (10), \(\mathcal L_N=2I\), \(q^{mN^2}=1\), and \(T_{mN}(z/2)=(-1)^m=1\) in the full quotient. \(\square\) The physical current in (9) has the additional original factor \(\kappa^n\). The scalar is therefore \(\kappa^n\sigma mN\rho\), not \(\kappa^m\sigma mN\rho\). All external framing and cut lines stay where they were. For fixed \(m\), its magnitude is bounded by \(2\pi|m|\); it is zero when \(m=0\). For the original circle-tree kernel \[ K_T(z,w)=\sum_{j=0}^D e_j(z)e_j(w),\qquad K_T(c_0,w)=1, \tag{11} \] equation (9) immediately has a simultaneous version. Replace the crossing factor at every vertex in a set \(C\) by its split Ward difference, before contracting any boundary variable. Then \[ \boxed{\quad \mathcal J^{\mathrm{even}}_{C,N} =\left(\prod_{v\in C}\kappa^{n_v}\sigma m_vN\rho\right) Z_{G\setminus C,N}. \quad} \tag{12} \] The deleted forest keeps all surviving powers and original closures; the displayed product retains the removed crossing carriers. Other global scalar factors appear identically on both sides. All boundary variables remain shared, and all their normals are retained. Indeed each current is a value functional, so every incident turn kernel contributes one and every internal edge contributes one only once. There is no derivative matching polynomial and no \(T\Pi_0\) coupon. For a more general compiled exterior the statement is the simultaneous evaluation in (9); an identity kernel, for example, contributes \(K_I(c_0,w)=e_D(w)\) and must not be silently deleted. ## 3. A canonical analytic unit, with no polynomial inverse zeros Use the canonical branch \[ K(z)=\operatorname{arccosh}(-z/2)^2, \qquad z\in\mathbb C\setminus[2,\infty), \tag{13} \] with its removable value at \(-2\). The original full-Hermite functional calculus gives the holomorphic nonvanishing functions \[ F_j(z)=q^{-jD^2/4}\exp\!\left(\frac{jK(z)}{2\hbar}\right), \qquad [F_j]=f_j\text{ in }\mathcal A_N,\qquad F_aF_b=F_{a+b}. \tag{14} \] Square brackets mean the actual Hermite class. Thus \(F_\epsilon\), rather than the polynomial \(f_\epsilon\), supplies a zero-free analytic inverse on this cut plane. The canonical analytic representatives of (7) are \[ (\mathcal T_{k,\mathrm{can}}^\epsilon u)(z(x)) =F_\epsilon(z(x)) \sum_{\delta=\pm1} \frac{u(z(x+\delta k\hbar))} {F_\epsilon(z(x+\delta k\hbar))}, \tag{15} \] \[ (\mathcal L_{k,\mathrm{can}}^\epsilon A)(z(x)) =\sum_{\delta=\pm1} \frac{\sinh(x+\delta k\hbar)}{\sinh x} \frac{F_\epsilon(z(x+\delta k\hbar))}{F_\epsilon(z(x))} A(z(x+\delta k\hbar)). \tag{16} \] Wherever these arguments avoid the cut, they are holomorphic, with removable differential singularities interpreted by continuation. At every physical node their required jets are exactly those of (7): each shifted argument is another physical node, and the chain rule uses only its prescribed value and first normal. At the simple odd node the ramification kills the unneeded derivative. Hence (15)--(16) are source-specific lifts of the finite operators, with no arbitrary spectator residual. There is also an exact residue formulation. On the original logarithmic window, put \[ G_j(x)=q^{-jD^2/4}e^{j(x-\pi i)^2/(2\hbar)},\qquad \mathcal C=\sum_{a=0}^{N-1}\gamma_{(2a+1)\pi i/N}. \tag{17} \] The circles are positively oriented and sufficiently small. For every polynomial \(A\), \[ \phi_N(f_nA) =\frac{\eta N^2}{4\pi i}\int_{\mathcal C} \frac{G_m(x)F_\epsilon(z(x))A(z(x))z'(x)}{P_N(z(x))}\,dx. \tag{18} \] On this window \(F_\epsilon(z(x))=G_\epsilon(x)\), so the product is exactly \(G_n\). The original factor \(1/2\) in the angular double cover, including the ramified simple spectral node, has been retained. ## 4. Local symbol and the original total power Fix a compact chart inside \[ 0<\Im x<2\pi, \qquad x=\pi i+it,\qquad |\Re t|<\pi. \tag{19} \] For a fixed \(k\), take \(N\) sufficiently large that the chart and its \(\pm k\hbar\) translates remain in this strip. This is the explicit common-chart hypothesis. In particular it holds on every fixed compact positive proper-return chart. On this common chart, \(K(z(x))=(x-\pi i)^2\), so (15)--(16) have the exact ratios \[ \frac{G_\epsilon(x+\delta k\hbar)}{G_\epsilon(x)} =q^{\epsilon k^2}e^{\delta\epsilon k(x-\pi i)}. \tag{20} \] Thus the retained half crossing is part of the leading action, not a bounded spectator amplitude. In the original angular coordinate, \[ \kappa^nF_m(-2\cos t)F_\epsilon(-2\cos t) =q^{nD^2/4}\exp\!\left(\frac{i nNt^2}{4\pi}\right). \tag{21} \] Together with the original edge and trace factors, this restores the selected primitive phase \[ \sum_e\psi(t_v,t_w) +\frac{i}{4\pi}\sum_v n_vt_v^2-i\sum_vt_v, \tag{22} \] with its original base-only carriers. Splitting \(n\) has not replaced it by \(m\) in the filling equation or in the calibrated action. For clarity, this is not equality of the entire split and unsplit characteristic varieties. In the kernel orientation of (15), write a trial local solution as \(e^{S(x)/\hbar}\), with momentum \(p=S'(x)\). At \(k=1\), the principal split characteristic is \[ \cosh\bigl(p-\epsilon(x-\pi i)\bigr)=\cosh(mx). \tag{23} \] Since \(m\) is even, its two branches, with their logarithmic lifts, are \[ p=n(x-\pi i)\quad\hbox{and}\quad p=(\epsilon-m)(x-\pi i)\pmod{2\pi i}. \tag{24} \] The first is the original selected total-power Gaussian branch; indeed (15) applied to \(F_n\) satisfies the homogeneous Gaussian equation exactly on the common chart. The other branch is generally different from the unsplit opposite branch \(-n\). At \(m=0\) the two split branches coincide. No exclusion of this other branch or global cycle selection is claimed. ## 5. The canonical-sheet seam is an explicit endpoint operator For \(\epsilon=\pm1\), define the *unwrapped* kernel operator by using (20) everywhere, even beyond (19): \[ (\mathcal T_{1,\mathrm{unw}}^\epsilon u)(z(x)) =q^{-\epsilon}\sum_{\delta=\pm1} e^{-\delta\epsilon(x-\pi i)}u(z(x+\delta\hbar)). \tag{25} \] For a polynomial \(u\), this is a symmetric Laurent polynomial in \(e^x\), hence a polynomial in \(z\). It therefore has a full Hermite class, but it is not the same finite operator as (15). The sheet change itself is explicit. In the immediately adjacent lower and upper logarithmic strips, respectively, \[ \frac{F_\epsilon(z(x))}{G_\epsilon(x)} =e^{\epsilon Nx}\quad(-2\pi<\Im x<0),\qquad \frac{F_\epsilon(z(x))}{G_\epsilon(x)} =e^{-\epsilon N(x-2\pi i)}\quad(2\pi<\Im x<4\pi). \tag{25a} \] These follow by replacing \(x\) by \(-x\) or \(4\pi i-x\) to return to (19) in the quadratic defining \(G_\epsilon\). The separating cut itself is excluded. At the first translated physical endpoint the ratio is \(-1\); its derivative must also be retained. **Proposition 2.** In the original full algebra, for every polynomial \(u\), \[ \boxed{\quad (\mathcal T_{1,\mathrm{can}}^\epsilon -\mathcal T_{1,\mathrm{unw}}^\epsilon)u =2u(c_0)\Pi_0+ \left\{\frac{\epsilon(1-D)}{\rho}u(c_0) -2u'(c_0)\right\}\Xi_0. \quad} \tag{26} \] Equivalently the adjoint difference is \[ (\mathcal L_{1,\mathrm{can}}^\epsilon -\mathcal L_{1,\mathrm{unw}}^\epsilon)A =-2A(c_0)\Pi_0+ \left\{2A'(c_0)+ \left(\frac{4c_0}{\rho^2}+\frac{\epsilon(1-D)}\rho\right) A(c_0)\right\}\Xi_0, \tag{27} \] where \(\mathcal L_{1,\mathrm{unw}}^\epsilon\) is the original Frobenius adjoint of (25), or (16) with the unwrapped ratios (20). **Proof.** Interior logarithmic nodes and their first derivatives agree, since both adjacent nodes stay in the original window. At \(x_0=\pi i/N\), only the backward term differs. Its canonical inverse half crossing has the value and logarithmic derivative at \(x_D\), whereas the unwrapped inverse is evaluated at \(x_{-1}\). These data are respectively \[ (1,-\epsilon D/2),\qquad (-1,-\epsilon(N+1)/2). \tag{28} \] Their difference is \((2,\epsilon)\). Multiplying by the input \(F_\epsilon(z(x))\), whose data are \((1,-\epsilon D/2)\), and by \(u(z(x-\hbar))\), whose derivative is \(-\rho u'(c_0)\), gives value \(2u(c_0)\) and logarithmic derivative \(\epsilon(1-D)u(c_0)-2\rho u'(c_0)\). Divide the latter by \(z'(x_0)=\rho\). At the paired endpoint both logarithmic derivatives change sign, giving the same spectral normal. All other required data vanish, proving (26). For (27), take the original adjoint using \(\phi_N(\Pi_0 A)=\sigma\{c_0A(c_0)+\rho^2A'(c_0)\}\) and (4). Coefficients of \(u(c_0)\) and \(u'(c_0)\) give exactly the displayed formula. This also proves that the differentiated source has not lost a normal term. \(\square\) In particular, applying (26) to \(f_n\) yields \[ \mathcal T_{1,\mathrm{unw}}^\epsilon f_n -2q^mT_m(z/2)f_n =-2\Pi_0+\frac{m-\epsilon}{\rho}\Xi_0. \tag{29} \] Thus changing sheets reintroduces a value projector and a normal. They are absent from the correctly retained canonical-sheet current (9). Equation (29) is not the unsplit odd-power Ward identity, since its operator is different. There is no contradiction with (18): equality of original residues does permit replacing the polynomial half crossing by its canonical analytic unit. It does not permit replacing its values at translated arguments by the unwrapped Gaussian after a logarithmic endpoint has been crossed. Equations (26)--(29) quantify precisely that distinction. ## 6. Coverage and scope The even Gaussian, the retained-half-crossing factorization, the even scalar current, and its full-turn cancellation are prior results in the sources below. The added organization is their exact conjugated all-exterior operator, simultaneous scalar deletion on arbitrary circle trees, zero-free canonical analytic lift, and explicit seam operator. This removes the odd-current matching coupons from this particular Ward implementation. It does not make every contour boundary a split Ward current, prove that deleted-forest rates are smaller, or give a nonzero original geometric coefficient. The canonical analytic lift does not bound the original polynomial representative away from the spectrum; such a bound is unnecessary for its exact initial residue identity but cannot be assumed during a different contour comparison. The common-chart symbol statement likewise supplies no global contour across the cut or the endpoint seams. ## Direct sources The complete source proofs were read; no numerical records or computational instructions are used. * [Original Gaussian and retained half crossing](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_coherent_filling_gaussian_chirp.md), SHA256 `d72f50bf1e9af5b15da89784c198a3cb5060b9ee9c3e6cc04b901049be516522`: exact full-Hermite Gaussian and the original half-crossing/turn placement. * [All signed analytic crossing powers](actual_direct_long_power_source.md), SHA256 `7c69dbee41401b1d46fa1db1e6046eca0dbde73429eecbead01e6a3bc6067df0`: canonical analytic branch of \(K\) and its original crossing scalar. * [Signed endpoint packet](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_signed_gaussian_ward_endpoint_packet.md), SHA256 `6bdced1b01917e41631386a24b337b60dfe5b04d35d70007cb56badc511a0191`: endpoint values, first normals and the even Ward identity at both level parities. * [Original logarithmic contour transport](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_gaussian_logarithmic_contour_transport.md), SHA256 proper-return phases](research_global_proper_return_phases.md), SHA256 `776df73f66a9d790c2ae6703caa365397e068d9b1a16c8cc5541fba93bd30a78`: original phase marking, positive proper-return charts and the title: The selected amplitude of the exact finite clock contraction
text: # The selected amplitude of the exact finite clock contraction Private written proof, 15 November 2026. No mathematical code, numerical calculation, test, or saved numerical evidence is used. Frozen notes and public manuscripts are unchanged. The complete singleton clock contraction has an all-orders relative asymptotic on a complex domain containing the physical interior colors. Its leading amplitude is explicit and nonzero. With the canonical Fourier character retained, that amplitude is precisely the normalized Gaussian amplitude of the clock critical point, with coefficient one. This is proved for the actual finite contraction, including both endpoints, by evaluating its exact Pochhammer product. The conclusion concerns the clock contraction conditional on the physical colors. It does not assert that the remaining physical color sum of an arbitrary short tangle has a nonzero geometric contribution. ## 1. Sources and the exact contraction The direct written sources are: * [Joint clock phase](research_joint_clock_phase_equations.md), SHA-256 71393aa353909dfa2dd19b078b1d3fccdf8561520aa071b7537e4bbfc50bb867: the full original source, exact clock sum (19), canonical primitive (27e)--(27g), and clock Hessian (27i). * [Exact factorial interpolation](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/exact_factorial_interpolation_and_complex_contours.md), SHA-256 1f34f65437dfe0bfb4062a7a74840beae1676353cf13bb8a86f8849a8a36bc72: its specified nonzero function \(G_N\), lattice values, reflection, marked complex expansion, and finite residue cycle. * [Root-Pochhammer interpolation](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_root_pochhammer_interpolation.md), SHA-256 46c1a27ca67045f6afdd2fd695f74b735ec611eabedb6f07b50b9bfbaccad4e2: the existing all-orders product expansion on disk charts. The last source already establishes the general asymptotic method. The additional statement here is the selected amplitude and its Gaussian normalization for this complete original clock contraction, on the physical strip and its complex neighborhoods. Put \[ N\ge2,\quad d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\qquad S_a=\prod_{r=1}^a2\sin(\pi r/N),\quad S_0=1. \tag{1} \] Let \(u,v\) be nonnegative integers with \(u+v\le d\), and set \(U=u/N,\ V=v/N\). The sign \(\sigma\in\{1,-1\}\) is the physical sign, as in the joint clock source. Write the lifted complex undercolor as \(j\), with \[ T=e^{2\pi i j}. \] At an original physical state \(j=J/N\), where \(J\) is the integer under-input degree. Define \[ a_{\sigma,N}(U,j) =\exp\{\sigma\pi i(U+2j-1+1/N)\} =-q^{\sigma(u+1)}T^\sigma , \] and keep the entire finite clock sum \[ C_{\sigma,N}(u,v;j)= \sum_{h=v}^{u+v} \frac{a_{\sigma,N}(U,j)^h} {S_{h-v}S_{u-h+v}} . \tag{2} \] This is the exact clock sum from the original source. For the positive sign its chosen exponential lift differs from the source's initial lift by \(-2\pi i h\); for the negative sign it is the initial lift. Since \(h\) is integral, (2) is unchanged. This is the canonical Fourier character already fixed by the joint action calculation. The finite binomial identity proves, for every nonzero complex \(T\), not just for its physical samples, \[ \begin{split} C_{\sigma,N} &=\frac{a_{\sigma,N}^{\,v}}{S_u}\,P_{\sigma,N}(u,j),\\ P_{\sigma,N}(u,j) &=\prod_{r=1}^u(1-e^{2\pi i\sigma(j+r/N)}). \end{split} \tag{3} \] For \(\sigma=1\) the product is \((TQ;Q)_u\). For \(\sigma=-1\) it is \((T^{-1}Q^{-u};Q)_u\), with its factors reversed. Thus (3) is exactly the two products of the prior clock theorem, including their first shifts and both endpoints. ## 2. Complex domain and all-orders product estimate Use the open parameter domain \[ \mathfrak D=\{(U,j):U\in(0,1),\ 0<\operatorname{Re}j< \operatorname{Re}(j+U)<1\}. \tag{4} \] Here \(U\) is real and is evaluated on \(u/N\); \(j\) is complex. Uniformity means compact subsets of (4), with the original allowed \(v\)'s, \(0\le v\le d-u\). For example one can impose \[ U\ge\epsilon,\quad \operatorname{Re}j\ge\epsilon,\quad \operatorname{Re}(j+U)\le1-\epsilon,\quad |\operatorname{Im}j|\le M . \tag{5} \] In terms of \(T\), this is a specified nonzero domain with argument lift \(2\pi\operatorname{Re}j\), bounded modulus, and no zero of any product arc in (3). It includes every compact subset of the physical interior \(0<U,\ 0<j,\ j+U<1\). No uniformity through its integer divisors is claimed. On \(0<\operatorname{Re}z<1\), set \[ s(z)=2\sin\pi z,\qquad \ell(z)=\Log s(z),\qquad \mathcal J(z)=\int_0^z\ell(t)\,dt, \tag{6} \] with the principal analytic logarithm and the primitive real on \((0,1)\), \(\mathcal J(0)=0\). The sine has positive real part in this strip, so these marks are unambiguous. Define \[ f_\sigma(z)=\ell(z)+\sigma\pi i(z-1/2). \tag{7} \] Then \(e^{f_\sigma(z)}=1-e^{2\pi i\sigma z}\). These are the logarithms used for every factor of (3). Let \(B_{2r}\) be the Bernoulli numbers, \(B_2=1/6\). For every fixed \(p\ge0\), Euler summation gives \[ \begin{split} \log P_{\sigma,N} ={}&N\int_0^U f_\sigma(j+t)\,dt +\frac{f_\sigma(j+U)-f_\sigma(j)}2\\ &+\sum_{r=1}^p \frac{B_{2r}}{(2r)!\,N^{2r-1}} \{\ell^{(2r-1)}(j+U)-\ell^{(2r-1)}(j)\}\\ &+O(N^{-2p-1}). \end{split} \tag{8} \] The logarithm on the left is the actual sum of the marked factor logarithms, not an independent logarithm of the final product. The estimate is uniform on the compacts specified above. Every fixed \(j\)-derivative of the normalized remainder obeys the same bound on a smaller compact neighborhood. For a direct remainder proof, apply the finite Euler--Maclaurin identity through its \(p+1\) term. The derivatives of \(f_\sigma\) through order \(2p+2\) are uniformly bounded on the compact union of arcs \(j+[0,U]\). Its integral remainder and last term are \(O(N^{-2p-1})\); absorb that last term. This proves (8). The linear term of \(f_\sigma\) contributes no derivative difference in (8), including when \(r=1\). Holomorphy and Cauchy's formula prove the derivative assertion. In particular this proof applies on both sides of the unit circle in \(T\), rather than only on the disk chart of the earlier interpolation note. The corresponding all-orders real factorial formula is \[ \log S_u=N\mathcal J(U)+\frac12\log(Ns(U)) +\sum_{r=1}^p \frac{B_{2r}\ell^{(2r-1)}(U)} {(2r)!\,N^{2r-1}} +O(N^{-2p-1}). \tag{9} \] Here \(U\) lies in a compact subset of \((0,1)\). One proof, including the normalization, is to write \(\ell(t)=\log(2\pi t)+g(t)\), where \(g\) is smooth at zero and every odd derivative of \(g\) vanishes there. Apply Stirling's expansion with remainder to \((2\pi/N)^u u!\), and Euler--Maclaurin to \(\sum_{r=1}^u g(r/N)\). The endpoint terms combine to \(\frac12\log(Ns(U))\); the odd derivatives of \(\log(2\pi U)\) in Stirling combine with those of \(g(U)\) to give exactly (9). Taking one further Bernoulli term bounds the stated remainder. The first correction is \(\pi\cot(\pi U)/(12N)\), agreeing with the exact factorial interpolation. ## 3. The selected clock amplitude Define \[ \begin{split} W_\sigma(U,V,j) ={}&\mathcal J(j+U)-\mathcal J(j)-\mathcal J(U)\\ &+\sigma\pi i\{V(U+2j-1)+jU+U^2/2-U/2\},\\ A_\sigma(U,V,j) ={}&e^{\sigma\pi i(V+U/2)} \exp\left\{\frac{\ell(j+U)-\ell(j)-\ell(U)}2\right\},\\ D_m(U,j) ={}&\ell^{(m)}(j+U)-\ell^{(m)}(j)-\ell^{(m)}(U). \end{split} \tag{10} \] All powers and square roots mean these displayed logarithms. In particular \(A_\sigma\) is holomorphic and nonzero throughout (4). **Theorem 1.** For every fixed \(p\ge0\), the exact finite sum (2) satisfies \[ \boxed{\displaystyle C_{\sigma,N} =N^{-1/2}A_\sigma e^{NW_\sigma} \exp\left\{ \sum_{r=1}^p \frac{B_{2r}D_{2r-1}(U,j)} {(2r)!\,N^{2r-1}} +O(N^{-2p-1})\right\}.} \tag{11} \] The estimates are uniform on every compact in (4), uniformly in all allowed \(v\), and hold with every fixed complex-undercolor derivative of the normalized error. Exponentiating the finite correction series gives a full relative expansion in integral powers of \(N^{-1}\). Indeed \[ a_{\sigma,N}^{\,v} =e^{N\sigma\pi iV(U+2j-1)}e^{\sigma\pi iV}. \] Insert (7)--(9) into the exact identity (3). The integral of the linear part of (7) gives \(\sigma\pi i(jU+U^2/2-U/2)\); its half-endpoint difference gives \(\sigma\pi iU/2\). These are exactly (10)--(11). No endpoint summand has been estimated away. On a compact parameter set there are constants \(0<c_K<C_K<\infty\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(N\), \[ c_K N^{-1/2}e^{N\operatorname{Re}W_\sigma} \le |C_{\sigma,N}| \le C_K N^{-1/2}e^{N\operatorname{Re}W_\sigma}. \tag{12} \] In fact \(C_{\sigma,N}\ne0\) at every level on (4), already by (3). The new information in (11)--(12) is the exact selected rate, power, nonzero amplitude, and all relative corrections.
