It is not an assertion that this particular boundary class is a prescribed knot numerator. The polynomial factor in (15) is not claimed optimal. There is also exponential instability when only a short real charge interval is supplied. Let \(N\ge4\), \(0<L<1\), and \(I=[y_c-L/2,y_c+L/2]\). The function \[ G_N(y)=e^{\sigma i\pi Dy} \bigl(1-e^{-\sigma2\pi i(y-y_c)}\bigr)^{m-1} \tag{24} \] lies in the span of pure exponentials in (3): its binomial expansion uses precisely the allowed frequencies \(\sigma\lambda_a\), \(0\le a<m\). For a real target \(y_*\) with \[ |\sin\pi(y_*-y_c)|>\sin(\pi L/2), \qquad r=\frac{\sin(\pi L/2)} {|\sin\pi(y_*-y_c)|}<1, \tag{25} \] one has \[ \sup_{y\in I}\left|\frac{G_N(y)}{G_N(y_*)}\right| \le r^{m-1}, \qquad \frac{G_N(y_*)}{G_N(y_*)}=1. \tag{26} \] Indeed \(|1-e^{i\theta}|=2|\sin(\theta/2)|\), and the carrier has modulus one on the real line. Thus even samples at every lattice point of \(I\) cannot give a uniform polynomial-cost extrapolation to \(y_*\) on this exact finite space: the norm of any exact linear reconstruction is at least \(r^{-(m-1)}\). The same two-data-set uncertainty applies to reconstruction from inexact samples. This is an observation-operator estimate, not an actual-knot cancellation example. ## 4. The finite-space restriction and the height-current distinction The canonical functions (3) have at most linear growth on the real \(y\)-axis. Their frequencies are one-sided and their maximal frequency is \(\pi(N-1)\), strictly below the lattice Nyquist frequency \(\pi N\). Reconstruction above uses the exact physical frequency set and its size-two normal blocks, not an unsupported claim that exponential type alone characterizes those functions. For comparison, the exact full-midpoint zero-power height current from the height-transport note is \[ J_{\sigma,0,1-y}^{h}[A] =\frac{\sigma\eta N^2}{2\pi}A^\sharp(2\cosh h) \frac{\sinh h\cosh(Nyh)}{\cosh^2(Nh/2)} \sin(\pi Ny). \tag{27} \] It vanishes at every sample \(y=j/N\). When \(h>0\) and its displayed spectator value is nonzero, it is not in (3) or (6): along real \(y\), the factor \(\cosh(Nyh)\) has exponential growth on subsequences with \(|\sin(\pi Ny)|=1\). It also contains the excluded Nyquist sine factor. Thus (12) does not identify different contour heights off the lattice. A restriction to the canonical finite charge space distinguishes this exact current, but does not prove that the contour-polarized initializer belongs to that space. The existing local small-charge asymptotic supplies neither the full unit block in (10c) nor the action-relative error required by (20). The positive zero-subtree theorem at fixed selected charge one supplies a different boundary-angle family. None of these facts is replaced by (12). What is established here is a stable full-normal finite reconstruction and its explicit continuation cost, available if the required actual charge samples are controlled. ## Direct sources and coverage The author read the complete final proof and all three complete direct sources at the versions below; all used implications were checked. - [Canonical finite charge polarization](research_polarized_charge_heat_source.md), SHA256 860801dedc3f1093d58c0413f580599512bd2566c00f4a94d0ebf99636343db1: actual full-normal spaces (3)–(5), faithful observations and source placement. - [Exact polarized height current](research_polarized_height_current_transport.md), SHA256 63273441891ce682acf46495e2707a8a72c28d2b74b3d4bed2d6861d568014fb: formula (27), its literal polynomial spectator and lattice scope. - [Entire original-source heat reduction](research_entire_charged_source_heat_reduction.md), SHA256 33213425be9cac699860a48b23830399c82cd89bea3140cc776274aafe115fba: the original heat-characteristic convention used in (21). For prior-coverage comparison, the full Fourier–Hermite Gram and one-sided angular-projection notes were read, and §§12–13 of the current-free charge equation were read. Their coordinate/period constructions are credited above; no additional conclusion from them is needed in this proof. No mathematical computation or numerical experiment is used.

title: What the short-filling results imply about finite exceptions
text: # What the short-filling results imply about finite exceptions Research scope note, updated 3 November 2026. The target continues to count the original integer filling assignments. It has not been replaced by a statement about distinct knot types, essential parameters, or density. The manuscripts remain frozen. The new boundary theorems allow many more partial fillings. They do not yet prove that every fixed template has only finitely many untreated assignments. There are two distinct issues already on small paths: adjacent short vertices require a composition estimate or a marked reduction to an already treated family, and a zero vertex can give infinitely many assignments of the same unresolved knot. The joint estimate is now proved for the pendant pair of powers \(2,2\). An exact marked reduction now covers every same-sign pendant chain of powers \(2\) or \(-2\), and boundary multiplication gives its canonical boundary asymptotic. The mixed pair \((2,-2)\) now also has a complete analytic boundary theorem whose complete rate is the volume of the specified augmented complement. Its original peripheral marking and geometric deformation are now proved as well, giving the volume identity for every sufficiently large fixed odd signed final twist in its literal closure. Every isolated pair with \(d+|n|>2\) now has a complete boundary theorem. The finite remainder of 6,369 pairs passed the common interval certificate and a separate archive-coverage check. Consequently arbitrary nonadjacent short fillings in that domain can precede sufficiently long remaining fillings. Same-sign internal \(2\)-crossing chains are also estimated at every fixed length. The mixed pair and its mirror have now been proved eligible as one-boundary pendant pieces in the hybrid tree theorem. Arbitrary adjacent short assignments remain untreated. ## 1. Adjacent short vertices and the two-crossing reduction Use the original crossing \(R\), physical quarter-turn \(T\), and cylindrical closure \(C\). The three-vertex path has the expression \[ K_3(a,b,c)=C\bigl(R^aT(R^bT(R^c))\bigr). \tag{1} \] Fix \(a=b=2\), and let \(c\) vary through the odd integers. The endpoint matching gives one component: an even integral braid has the through pairing, an odd braid has the crossed pairing, and the quarter-turn preserves the crossed pairing. Thus (1) has the crossed pairing before cylindrical closure, which closes to one component. As in the finite-exception target, restrict to assignments whose resulting knot is hyperbolic. No assertion about hyperbolicity is being inferred from the quantum expression below. The fixed vertex \(a\) is an original leaf of power two. The fixed vertex \(b\) has original degree two and power two. Each has its own proved whole-boundary theorem. However, they are adjacent. If \(u\) is the angle at the remaining vertex, their exact joint polynomial is \[ Z_N(u)=\mathcal D_{2,N}^{(t)} \bigl[H_{2,N}(t)K_N(t,u)\bigr], \qquad H_{2,N}(t)=\mathcal D_{2,N}^{(s)}K_N(s,t). \tag{2} \] Here \(K_N\) is the original complete edge polynomial and \(\mathcal D_{n,N}f=\phi_N(R^nf)\) is the complete closing functional, including its first derivatives at repeated roots. Expression (2) is neither an original leaf polynomial nor the degree-two singleton polynomial \(\mathcal D_{2,N}[K_N(t,u)K_N(t,v)]\). Replacing the first kernel by the already traced function \(H_{2,N}\) changes the phase and its global estimates. The [nonadjacent assembly](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_nonadjacent_short_fillings_and_long_remainder.md) therefore does not apply. The [connected-cluster criterion](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_connected_short_filling_clusters.md) also does not apply: the selected original degrees are \(1,2\), and both powers are \(2\). The earlier [degree-two marked simplifications](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_marked_degree_two_tangle_moves.md) concern powers \(0,\pm1\), so they do not remove this pair. This is the smallest tree on which adjacent selected vertices can leave an unfilled boundary. Separate singleton theorems alone do not estimate (2). A direct joint theorem for (2) is proved in [the adjacent-pair boundary calculation](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_adjacent_two_crossing_boundary_theorem.md). It uses the exact double sum, its calibrated positive geometry, the horizontal maximum, and a new full-period contour. The added lattice terms outside the original triangle are exactly zero. The lower first-variable contours consequently form complete circles; their main integrals cancel after an explicit normalization, with exponentially small errors. Combining the two vertical sides before taking absolute values retains the peripheral multiplier and removes the former diagonal-corner obstruction. The written endpoint bounds and the interval certificate account for every remaining contour term. There is now a second proof of the closed volume conclusion. The [repeated-two-crossing reduction](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_repeated_two_crossing_chain_reduction.md) replaces the pendant pair by a terminal power \(-3\) and shifts its parent power by \(-1\). The terminal theorem then applies when the remaining power is sufficiently long. Thus a joint estimate of the unreduced polynomial was not logically necessary for that closed conclusion. More generally, a pendant chain of \(k\) powers \(2\sigma\), \(\sigma=\pm1\), becomes a terminal power \(-\sigma(k+1)\) and a parent shift by \(-\sigma\), with the actual branch rotations retained. The [boundary multiplication theorem](research_boundary_crossing_packet_preservation.md) also upgrades this quotient identity to a full asymptotic for the canonical unreduced boundary polynomial. These arguments treat all same-sign chains, but they do not validate an arbitrary iteration of singleton theorems. The mixed pair now has a separate [complete analytic theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_mixed_two_crossing_boundary_theorem.md). It estimates the original polynomial \(T(R^{-2}T(R^2))\) on a fixed complex neighborhood, proves a nonzero leading coefficient, and controls the whole boundary period. The proof accounts for all terms in an exact contour identity; it does not infer this estimate from the two singleton results. The [positive ideal subdivision](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_mixed_two_crossing_positive_subdivision.md) also proves its complete volume normalization, by exact gluing and dilogarithm identities. The [original word and collar proof](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_mixed_word_collar_representation.md) now identifies the full marked geometric germ and proves the volume theorem for its literal long odd final closure, of either sign. The proof uses the exact original diagram meridian and disk longitude, not just a comparison of complete cusp traces. Other adjacent short powers still need a composition proof. For comparison, neighboring zero-power vertices of original degrees at least three are now covered by their [joint Newton-coordinate theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_all_zero_subtree_newton_packet.md) and [literal strict Conway geometry](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_zero_subtree_conway_geometry.md). That proof treats the combined polynomial and applies to connected sets of any size. The nonzero pair in (2) uses the separate full-period argument just described. ## 2. An infinite fiber on a four-vertex path For the four-vertex path, write \[ K_4(a,v,b,c) =C\bigl(R^aT(R^vT(R^bT(R^c)))\bigr). \tag{3} \] All powers refer to their original local crossing frames. Let \(\tau=T^2\) be the actual physical half-turn. The [ordered rotation and closure isotopies](../papers/conway-reductions/moves.tex) give \[ \tau(FG)=\tau(G)\tau(F),\qquad \tau(TF)=T\tau(F),\qquad \tau(R^r)=R^r, \qquad C(FG)\simeq C(GF). \tag{4} \] In particular, the reversal of the product by \(\tau\) must be retained. At \(v=0\), equations (3)--(4) give an ambient isotopy \[ \begin{aligned} K_4(a,0,b,c) &=C\bigl(R^a\tau(R^bT(R^c))\bigr)\\ &=C\bigl(R^aT(R^c)R^b\bigr)\\ &\simeq C\bigl(R^{a+b}T(R^c)\bigr) =K_2(a+b,c). \end{aligned} \tag{5} \] The first equality uses the through identity \(R^0\), before applying the two turns. The last isotopy uses closed cyclicity and then concatenation of integral braids. No open tangles have been commuted, and no half-turn has been erased. These are the same physical moves used in the [marked degree-two zero reduction](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_marked_degree_two_tangle_moves.md#4-a-zero-power-merges-two-twist-regions). The isotopy carries the main knot, its marked arcs, orientations, and any supplied ribbon. Consequently it identifies the filled knot complements and their preferred meridian and longitude, after the same orientation convention, and identifies the reduced zero-framed Kashaev invariant. A raw diagram evaluation can retain a framing factor of modulus one. Equation (5) is not a claimed homeomorphism between exteriors having two unfilled auxiliary tori and an exterior having only one: all the displayed powers are evaluated. **Proposition.** Suppose the finite-assignment conclusion holds for every fixed parity pattern of the four-vertex path (3). Then every hyperbolic two-circle knot \(K_2(s,c)\), at every fixed pair of integer powers \(s,c\), satisfies the original Kashaev volume identity. **Proof.** Fix such a hyperbolic knot and choose a parity \(\epsilon\in\{0,1\}\). For every integer \(r\), take \[ (a,v,b,c)=(\epsilon+2r,\ 0,\ s-\epsilon-2r,\ c). \tag{6} \] This is one fixed parity pattern: the parities are \(\epsilon,0,s-\epsilon,c\) modulo two. The carrier at the zero vertex is \(0\). Choose the original other carriers with these parities. Since \(n_j=\eta_j-2p_j\), every tuple (6) is an allowed integer surgery assignment; as \(r\) increases by one, the first surgery coefficient decreases by one and the third increases by one. Thus the assignments are distinct. Equation (5) identifies all of them with the same hyperbolic knot \(K_2(s,c)\). In particular their fixed matching is a knot matching. If that knot failed the volume identity, infinitely many assignments of this one marked four-vertex template would fail it. This contradicts the assumed finite-exception conclusion. Hence the knot satisfies the identity. The fixed pair \(s,c\) was arbitrary. QED. This proposition is an implication, not a proof of its conclusion. The proved [two-circle result](research_two_circle_finite_exceptions.md) leaves a finite set of pairs untreated. Any one hyperbolic pair in that untreated set has infinitely many preimages in (6). It therefore cannot be discarded as finitely many assignments of the larger path. This gives a small explicit instance of the [zero-cap padding issue](research_finite_exceptions_under_partial_fillings.md#8-a-consequence-of-counting-assignments-strict-padding). The [reflected even knot theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_reflected_even_kashaev_volume_theorem.md) now settles the pairs \((s,c)=(-2k,2k)\) for every integer \(k\ge2\), and their mirrors. Therefore every assignment \((m,0,-2k-m,2k)\) satisfies the original volume identity. With fixed parity \(m=\epsilon+2r\), its original filling coefficients are \((-r,0,k+\epsilon+r,-k)\). All of these infinite fibers are covered. The argument does not extend the same conclusion to an arbitrary unequal pair \((s,c)\). ## 3. What exact simplification can transfer safely There is a useful elementary criterion. Suppose a fixed partial assignment is transformed by proved marked isotopies into a family with a cofinite theorem, and let \(f\) be the induced map from its remaining original assignments to the new assignments. If every fiber of \(f\) is finite, the inverse image of the finite untreated set is finite. This transfers the cofinite conclusion without any new source estimate. Alternatively, an infinite fiber is harmless when the volume identity is already proved for its knot. A fixed degree-two power \(\sigma=\pm1\) has precisely the first behavior: it deletes that vertex and shifts both neighboring powers by \(-\sigma\), with the prescribed physical rotations. On the remaining parameter lattice the map is injective. A finite sequence of such proved moves can therefore transfer the two-circle cofinite theorem to a template with those extra powers already fixed. It does not prove the theorem when those powers are also arbitrary free parameters. For example, on the three-vertex path, each fixed slice \(b=\pm1\) reduces to \(K_2(a\mp1,c\mp1)\). A fixed endpoint power \(a=\sigma\) reduces, by closed turn transfer, to \(K_2(b-\sigma,c)\); the other endpoint is the same calculation from the opposite root. Thus the union of these six fixed slices has only finitely many untreated hyperbolic assignments. At a zero power the cap rules or the degree-two zero move leave an integral braid closure or an unknot, so there are no hyperbolic assignments on those zero slices. Those particular reductions do not treat the adjacent pair in Section 1; the separate two-crossing chain identity does. A zero merger \((a,b)\mapsto a+b\) has infinite fibers when both powers remain free. If one is already fixed, that particular merger is injective on the other power; otherwise finite exceptions cannot be pulled back without resolving the affected knots. The same test must be applied to deleted parameters in a cap splitting. Merely having finitely many resulting diagrams does not make the parameter fibers finite. ## 4. Recommendation for the next theorem The joint polynomial (2) is now controlled, as are the same-sign chains described above. The next missing composition estimate concerns general short connected regions, including mixed-sign chains beyond the now treated pair. For that pair, both the full boundary asymptotic and its original marked geometric identification are proved, so the stated long-filling volume conclusion follows. Multiplication and fixed boundary crossings preserve the proved concentrated boundary asymptotics. Quarter-turns do not preserve that class in general: \(T(H_p)=R^p\) for \(H_p=T(R^p)\), and \(R^p\) has unit-modulus values throughout the physical spectrum. The missing theorem must therefore use the geometry of the actual compositions, or include intermediate sources without strict concentration. More isolated estimates do not by themselves establish such a theorem. The new [fixed-domain turn theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_fixed_domain_long_power_turns.md) does give a uniform composition result when the subsequent powers are long. One threshold works for chains of arbitrary fixed length, with either sign at each step and any initial terminal power of magnitude at least two. It preserves the complete complex boundary domain and global estimates. The proof therefore removes an actual iteration problem, but does not establish the required stability under arbitrary fixed short turns. A noninitial power can still remain short in infinitely many assignments. For the general target, the required statement is a boundary theorem stable under the actual connected partially filled sources, together with exact treatment of their degenerations. The finite-branching lemma then applies to the original assignments. Zero mergers and cap padding require additional care: the four-path proposition shows that even an unresolved finite list of two-circle knots cannot simply be left behind. Neither the independent-set assembly nor the current high-degree connected-cluster theorem supplies this general result.

title: The finite-exception problem: current research status
status: Current research status; finite-exception theorem open
text: # The finite-exception problem: current research status 25 November 2026. The finite-exception theorem is open. This note records the current question and the general reductions being pursued. The [papers](../papers/README.md) contain the established volume results; the research reductions below do not enlarge their hypotheses. ## The established result and the stronger question Fix one finite strict Conway construction, its crossing circles and a half-twist pattern whose strand connections give a knot. Write \(p=(p_1,\ldots,p_b)\in\mathbb Z^b\) for its auxiliary integral filling coefficients. The [Conway theorem](../papers/conway-asymptotics/README.md) gives a threshold \(P_0\) such that the volume identity holds whenever every \(|p_i|>P_0\). All these coefficients are fixed before the quantum level \(N\) tends to infinity. This covers density one in the assignment lattice; its complement still contains infinitely many assignments. The stronger target is: > After fixing any short partial filling, all sufficiently long fillings > of the remaining coordinates that produce hyperbolic knots satisfy the > volume identity, with a threshold allowed to depend on the fixed data. The [finite-branching argument](research_finite_exceptions_under_partial_fillings.md) explains how the required statements for successive partial fillings would imply finitely many exceptional assignments for one template. The [definitions](research_strict_conway_family_definitions.md) specify the tangle operations, primitive slopes, component test and quantifiers. Exact tangle reductions can have infinite fibers: infinitely many assignments can describe one unresolved core knot. The [affine-fiber theorem](research_affine_reduction_fibers_and_core_obligation.md) decides this on each recorded reduction branch. The padding argument in the finite-branching note shows why the general assignment statement already entails a volume theorem for every hyperbolic core allowed by the construction. Redundant assignments cannot simply be discarded. ## What orthogonality changes For a finite synthesis map \(B\), an expanded state \(Bc\) has energy \(c^*B^*Bc\). The Gram matrix \(B^*B\) retains exact linear relations; replacing it by the identity can create spurious energy. The [conceptual chapter](../manuscript/sections/02-exact-concepts.tex) and its [formal statements](../repro/PAPER_FORMAL_COVERAGE.md) give this algebra and its limitations. A norm estimate alone gives no lower bound for a specified closing functional. The [normalized finite-source construction](research_convex_normalized_conway_source.md) encodes the actual packet equations and scalar closing in one residual energy. Its proof retains the normalization budget that connects this energy to the original invariant. The [linear-elimination theorem](research_conway_orthogonal_linear_elimination.md) then removes every linearly entering packet exactly. In its notation, retain one child packet \(u\) at each binary product and call the other packets \(z\). The stacked residual is \(A(u)z+b(u)\), with \(A(u)\) of full column rank. Minimizing in \(z\) gives \[ z_*(u)=-(A(u)^*A(u))^{-1}A(u)^*b(u),\qquad f(u)=\|\Pi(u)b(u)\|^2, \] where \[ \Pi(u)=I-A(u)(A(u)^*A(u))^{-1}A(u)^*. \] Here \(\Pi(u)\) is the orthogonal projection onto \(\ker A(u)^*\). The proof checks that the eliminated ball constraints are inactive and retains the original scalar closing. This reduces the finite problem with its full Gram matrix present. The [reciprocal-source comparison](research_conway_reciprocal_finite_fiber_lower_bound.md) uses orthogonal projection on finite fibers. The [residual-degree reduction](research_conway_logarithmic_reduced_residual_degree.md) compresses the remaining nonlinear dependence further. These are finite algebraic or variational comparisons. Neither evaluates the remaining minimum at the hyperbolic-volume rate. ## The other current source calculations Two related lines of work retain exact phases and the prescribed source. - The [coideal Fourier compiler](research_coideal_full_fourier_crossing.md) expresses the actual crossing in orthogonal coordinates, with the neighboring-height channels and original cup retained. The [initialized period](research_coideal_normalized_marked_period.md) and [quantum flag source](research_true_cup_quantum_flag_source.md) make the corresponding source and marked observation explicit. These identities do not supply a lower bound for every closed word. - The [cyclic Hardy comparison](research_cyclic_atom_hardy_head_comparison.md) proves that the physical coefficient projection loses at most a polynomial factor in the scalar function norm. It builds on the [near-unit-circle estimates](research_cyclic_atom_near_unit_circle.md). Gluing these functions and estimating their original marked scalar remain separate requirements. The [Rivin boundary comparison](research_rivin_jones_partial_filling_assessment.md) keeps the exact matrix presentation distinct from geometric optimization. Casson--Rivin optimization identifies a geometric action under its hypotheses; it does not show that its point occurs with a nonzero coefficient in the original finite sum. A [filled-cover obstruction](research_filled_cover_slope_length_obstruction.md) also rules out making a short filling slope long by an unbranched cover compatible with that filling. ## The remaining theorem The task is to evaluate the retained finite source at the geometric exponential rate, including its normalization budget, for arbitrary fixed short partial fillings. A successful argument must control the original closing observation and possible cancellation, beyond the existence of a local geometric critical point or a positive ambient norm. The previous append-only record mixed these questions with thousands of earlier case calculations and changing status reports. Its complete text remains in the [pre-cleanup snapshot](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_finite_exceptions_progress.md). Earlier partial cases are not additional premises of the manuscripts.

title: From long fillings to finitely many exceptions
status: Quantified extension target and finite-branching implication
text: # From long fillings to finitely many exceptions Research note, 2 November 2026. The manuscripts remain frozen. This note proves elementary consequences of their stated hypotheses and a limitation of the printed directed criterion. It does not prove a new volume theorem for short fillings. ## 1. The target and the present quantifiers The target is Kashaev's original volume identity for a hyperbolic knot K: \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N}\log|\langle K\rangle_N| =\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K). \] There are two different finite-exception questions: 1. For one fixed marked tangle template, are only finitely many integer filling assignments that give hyperbolic knots untreated? 2. Among all hyperbolic knot types, are only finitely many untreated? The second statement does not follow from the first for infinitely many templates. Parameter assignments also need not give distinct knot types. For a fixed admissible template with d filling parameters, the current theorem supplies a finite nonnegative integer B such that every assignment with |p_i| > B for every i satisfies the volume identity. All parameters are fixed before the level N tends to infinity. The threshold can depend on the template. A retained half-twist pattern is fixed, so integer surgery parameters already preserve the relevant crossing parities. ## 2. The density consequence For an integer H > B, the fraction of assignments in [-H,H]^d covered by this sufficient condition is exactly \[ \left(\frac{2(H-B)}{2H+1}\right)^d. \] Indeed each coordinate has 2(H-B) choices outside [-B,B]. The number not certified by this condition is at most \[ d(2B+1)(2H+1)^{d-1}, \] by the union bound over coordinates. Thus the covered assignments have density one in this fixed parameter space. For d >= 2, the complement of this sufficient condition is nevertheless infinite: p_1 can remain zero while p_2 tends to infinity. This is a statement about untested assignments, not about failures of the volume conjecture or necessarily about infinitely many distinct untested knot types. For a single free parameter the corresponding exceptional assignments are already finite. No counting statement here concerns knots ordered by crossing number. ## 3. A finite-exception lemma for one template Let D be any subset of Z^d. In the intended application, D consists of the assignments giving hyperbolic knots with the prescribed marking. Let P(p) be a property defined for p in D; here P is the volume identity. For I a proper subset of {1,...,d} and a in Z^I, fixing p_i=a_i for i in I is called a partial assignment. The coordinates outside I remain free. **Proposition.** Suppose that every partial assignment (I,a) has a finite integer B(I,a) >= 0 such that \[ \mathbf p\in D,\quad p_i=a_i\ (i\in I),\quad |p_j|>B(I,a)\ (j\notin I) \quad\Longrightarrow\quad P(\mathbf p). \] Then D contains only finitely many points where P fails. **Proof.** Begin with I empty. A point where P fails has a free coordinate j with |p_j| <= B(I,a). Branch over the finitely many choices of j and of the integer p_j in that interval, adding this coordinate to I. Apply the same argument at each new partial assignment. There are finitely many children at every node, and every step fixes one previously free coordinate. After at most d steps each remaining branch specifies one complete tuple. A finite tree of bounded depth has finitely many leaves. Every point of D where P fails belongs to this finite set of complete tuples. QED. The thresholds may depend arbitrarily on the previously fixed values; no uniform threshold over all partial assignments is assumed. If the thresholds and applicable source theorems are effective, the argument also gives an effective finite list. It does not settle the points on that list. The lemma only needs the partial assignments visited by the finite branching procedure. Proving a theorem stable under all fixed partial fillings is a convenient sufficient hypothesis, stronger than that finite collection of needed cases. ## 4. The missing stability theorem The next substantive target is the following statement, currently unproved in this project: > Fix an admissible marked parent, choose one of its crossing circles, > and give that circle any fixed integer filling, provided at least one > crossing circle remains unfilled. For all independently > sufficiently long fillings of the remaining crossing circles that > produce hyperbolic knots, prove the original Kashaev volume identity. > Establish the same statement for the partially filled sources so > that it can be applied repeatedly. Stop the iteration when no free coordinate remains. Those finitely many fully assigned leaves are the possible exceptions; no theorem for them is being smuggled in through a vacuous longness condition. One application alone is insufficient in three or more parameters: there can be two or more short coordinates. The class of sources must be stable under iteration, or each required partial assignment must be treated separately. The existing filling-functional norm estimate is already valid for every fixed integer crossing power n: \[ |\mathcal L_N^n H|\le(1+|n|/2)\|H\|_{[-2,2]}. \] Its prefactor has zero exponential rate as N tends to infinity. Therefore an upper bound for the short filling is not the main missing step. The problem is to identify the geometric stationary point after the partial filling, prove that its contribution is nonzero, and bound the other contributions below it. A closed-tangle volume limit does not provide the uniform open-boundary estimates needed for further gluing. Intermediate partial fillings need not remain in the current geometric class. One cannot silently discard an intermediate nonhyperbolic exterior without proving that its relevant descendants are absent or already controlled. The abstract proposition uses only the final domain D and hides no assumption about intermediate hyperbolicity. ## 5. A concrete limitation of the current directed estimates The directed criterion in [the circle-tree manuscript](../papers/circle-tree-volume/directed-criterion.tex) fixes k_0=2^{-16} and t_0=2^{-14}. At a nonroot leaf, the degree is one and there are no child contributions. Its quantities are \[ A=\frac{2k_0}{\pi^2},\qquad C=16+\frac{n^2}{32k_0},\qquad |D|^2=\frac{1+n^2}{4\pi^2},\qquad \beta=\frac{420\pi}{361(1+n^2)}. \] The printed contour-height and error estimates give \[ y\le\frac{t_0|D|}{4C},\qquad \eta\le\frac{t_0|D|y}{2} \le\frac{t_0^2|D|^2}{8C}. \] For n nonzero, the required inequality beta < eta/2 therefore implies \[ n^2+2+n^{-2}> \frac{840\pi^3}{361t_0^2k_0}. \] Since pi > 31/10 and t_0^2 k_0=2^{-44}, the right side exceeds 69 times 2^{44}. If 1 <= |n| <= 2^{25}, the left side is at most 2^{50}+3, which is smaller. For n=0 the separate required condition t_0|D| >= 2 fails. Thus: **Proposition.** No nonroot leaf with |n| <= 2^{25} satisfies the printed directed criterion, for any choice of its adjustable decay parameters. Every finite tree with at least two vertices has a nonroot leaf, whatever root is selected. This limitation concerns this sufficient criterion alone. It is not a necessary condition for the volume identity, nor a limitation on all other methods in the project. It shows why optimizing the final 2^{27} rounding cannot reach ordinary short twists without changing the analytic estimates. ## 6. The additional issue for all hyperbolic knots To pass from fixed templates to finitely many excluded knot types, one sufficient statement would be a universal C such that every hyperbolic knot either has an established volume proof or has crossing number at most C. There are finitely many knot types of bounded crossing number. The current degree-and-twist criteria supply no such bound on untreated knots. Two weaker conclusions must not be mistaken for this statement: - Finitely many short local tangle types can form arbitrarily large diagrams. - Finitely many unresolved reduced cores can have infinitely many unresolved extensions. A reduction that only transports a proof from a core to its extensions does not control those extensions when the core remains unresolved. Nor can all hyperbolic knots be fillings of a finite list of fixed hyperbolic parents: filling decreases hyperbolic volume, whereas hyperbolic knot volumes are unbounded. Explicit weaving-knot bounds are given by [Champanerkar--Kofman--Purcell](https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.04139). The general finite-exception target needs a theorem handling unbounded diagram complexity, in addition to the partial-filling theorem above. ## 7. Attribution and novelty [Kashaev's original conjecture](https://arxiv.org/abs/q-alg/9601025) is the target. Chen and Yang explicitly credit it in the introduction to their [different conjectures for Turaev--Viro and Reshetikhin--Turaev invariants](https://arxiv.org/html/1503.02547v4). A theorem about those invariants does not automatically prove the original Kashaev evaluation. The [long-filling theorem stated by Shen](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11839v3) belongs in related work rather than direct coverage of our main knot theorem. A reflection or cancellation argument taken from it must nevertheless be credited, and its existing scope matters to any claim that a particular analytic technique is new. The counting and finite-branching propositions above are elementary deductions. They are not being advertised as new knot theorems. The research contribution still sought is the stability under short partial fillings and the control of arbitrarily long compositions of short tangles. ## 8. A consequence of counting assignments: strict padding The literal finite-assignment target is stronger than a statement about distinct knot types. The following observation was obtained while pursuing the active goal. It uses the ordered conventions and the explicit cap isotopies of [Ordered tangle reductions and long net twists](../papers/conway-reductions/closures.tex). Here "strict" means the enlarged literal grammar in [the Conway asymptotics manuscript](../papers/conway-asymptotics/main.tex): the closing children may be elementary or turned elementary boxes. The construction below is not asserted to belong to the older, narrower grammar requiring two completed closing children. Write T for a physical quarter-turn, h(n)=T(R^n) for an elementary leaf, C for cylindrical closure, D for cap closure, and tau=T^2 for the physical half-turn. An unframed cap closure D(R^a) is an unknot for every integer a: its crossings are removable curls. The zero leaf h(0) closes an adjacent tangle by caps. Consequently \[ C(h(0)F)\simeq D(F),\qquad D(FG)\simeq D(F)\mathbin\# D(G),\qquad D(TQ)\simeq C(\tau Q). \] The connected sum uses the two specified cap components; internal components are retained. If C(Q) is a knot, the application below contains no extra component. Rotating the entire cylindrical closure identifies C(tau Q) with C(Q). **Proposition.** For the class of strict Conway templates, these two statements are equivalent: 1. Each fixed admissible template has only finitely many hyperbolic filling assignments at which the original Kashaev volume identity fails. 2. Every hyperbolic knot represented by a strict Conway template satisfies that identity, at every integer assignment of its powers. **Proof.** The second statement implies the first with no exceptions. For the converse, fix an arbitrary strict core K=C(Q), with all its powers fixed, and assume K is hyperbolic. Add two new leaves and form \[ E(a,b)=C\bigl(h(b)[R^aT(Q)]\bigr). \] The factor R^a can be written T^3(h(a)), so the displayed expression uses precisely the permitted leaves, turns, and products. This is formally strict. When Q is inserted as an open tangle, its former closing product becomes an ordinary retained product. This is allowed: each permitted closed pair AA, AL, AH, LH (in either order) also has a nonempty open product, respectively of type A, A, H, H. All products below it were already strict. Thus Q, now considered open, has output type A or H in the [original type table](../papers/newton-calculus/supports.tex). This is an existence argument for a new strict state; it does not reuse the old closed optimizer. Consequently T(Q) has type A or L, while R^a=T^3(h(a)) has type H. Their product has type H, and the outer closing pair consists of types L and H, which is allowed. None of these formal type assertions depends on the numerical powers. At b=0 the cap identities give \[ E(a,0)\simeq D(R^aT(Q)) \simeq D(R^a)\#D(T(Q)) \simeq U\#C(\tau Q)\simeq K \] for every integer a. Fix either parity for a, use even parity at b, and retain the core parities. These are infinitely many distinct filling assignments in one fixed admissible marked template, all giving the same hyperbolic knot. After the prescribed zero-framing correction they have the same reduced invariant and volume. If K failed the identity, the first statement would be contradicted. Therefore K satisfies it. Since the core was arbitrary, the second statement follows. QED. More explicitly, choose retained carriers \(\eta_a=\eta_b=0\) at the two new circles and keep the fixed core carriers. In the original primitive surgery coordinates, the assignments \[ (p_a,p_b,\mathbf p_Q)=(r,0,\mathbf p_Q), \qquad r\in\mathbb Z, \] give \(a=-2r\), \(b=0\), and the same fixed core. They are distinct tuples of the original template. Its retained pattern passes the knot test: changing a braid power by an even integer changes no endpoint pairing or internal component, and every displayed closure is the knot \(K\). The physical half-turn \(\tau\) permutes the cylindrical closing pairs \(\{0,3\},\{1,2\}\), carrying the prescribed empty outside arcs to one another. Thus the last isotopy above is the rotation of the entire closed picture, with no unrecorded boundary Dehn twist. This does not disprove the requested theorem. It identifies its actual strength: a proof for every strict template cannot leave any unresolved hyperbolic strict core behind a finite list of assignments. Replacing assignments by distinct knot types, or excluding inessential parameters, would change the goal and is not done here. The same construction explains why a short partially filled exterior that is nonhyperbolic cannot simply be ignored. Its remaining circle can control a removable curl while all its fillings still produce the fixed hyperbolic knot K. The proposed partial-filling theorem must handle this possibility rather than assume that every intermediate exterior remains in the original augmented geometric class.

title: Finite Gabor seams for the original pointed meridian source
text:
# Finite Gabor seams for the original pointed meridian source Private written proof, 19 November 2026. This note gives a finite packet expansion of the original all-width pointed source, including its two pivotal carrier shifts and its true meridian normals. Every physical occupation, closing factor, and partial-label current remains. The complete seam sum removes the additional packet damping exactly; a selected packet estimate is therefore not a noncancellation estimate for the complete source. The sole complete proof direct is J, pinned below. The earlier research_gaussian_frame_newton_transport.md already gives a continuous Gaussian resolution, exact Newton-word composition, and original boundary functions. It also retains the inverse frame operator under weights. The frame principle is not new here. The present calculation records the finite all-width pointed closing row, its meridian connection and relative Laurent terms, and its exact seam cancellation. No assertion from that coverage note is used as a proof premise. ## 1. Physical space and a finite auxiliary frame Fix \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\), \(r\ge1\), \(m=r+1\), and \(x_0=-q^{-1}\). The physical remaining space is \(U=V_N^{\otimes r}\), with occupation basis \(e_{\mathbf n}\), \(0\le n_i\le d\). Write \[ J_{m occ}e_{\mathbf n}=|\mathbf n|e_{\mathbf n},\qquad K_0=x_0^rQ^{-J_{m occ}},\qquad K_{m r}(M)=M^rK_0,\qquad K_0^N=\varepsilon I,\quad \varepsilon=(-1)^{(N+1)r}. 	ag{1} \] These are finite matrices. The last identity will only be used on this physical space, never at a continued classical clock argument. Choose any fixed Euclidean-unit vector \(g\in V_N\). One useful choice, with \(0\le L<N\), is \[ g(n)= rac{2^{-L} inom Ln}{
u_L}\quad(0\le n\le L),\qquad g(n)=0\quad(L<n<N),\qquad 
u_L^2=4^{-L} inom{2L}L . 	ag{2} \] The normalization follows by taking the coefficient of \(z^L\) in \((1+z)^L(1+z)^L\). Define auxiliary cyclic translations and modulations \[ (T_ag)(n)=g(n-a mod N),\qquad (M_sg)(n)=Q^{sn}g(n),\qquad g_{a,s}=M_sT_ag,\quad a,s\in\mathbb Z/N. 	ag{3} \] Only these auxiliary labels and translations are cyclic. A physical raising arrow at occupation \(d\) is not replaced by a wrap arrow. For (2) all wrapped windows are included in (3), with their literal entries; the unwrapped center is \(a+L/2\). The exact identity is \[  rac1N\sum_{a,s}|g_{a,s}angle\langle g_{a,s}|=I_{V_N}. 	ag{4} \] Indeed its \(n,k\) entry is \[  rac1N\sum_sQ^{s(n-k)} \sum_a g(n-a)\overline{g(k-a)} =\delta_{nk}\sum_a|g(n-a)|^2=\delta_{nk}. 	ag{5} \] The star in this calculation is the fixed occupation-coordinate Euclidean dual. It does not change the ordinary matrix trace or replace J's coherent metric. Choose one such window on each head, set \(\Psi_\lambda= igotimes_i g^{(i)}_{a_i,s_i}\), and let \(\mathcal L=(\mathbb Z/N)^{2r}\). Tensoring (4) gives \[ N^{-r}\sum_{\lambda\in\mathcal L} |\Psi_\lambdaangle\langle\Psi_\lambda|=I_U. 	ag{6} \] For an invertible diagonal holomorphic matrix \(D(M)\), the corresponding exact resolution is \[ N^{-r}\sum_\lambda D(M)|\Psi_\lambdaangle\langle\Psi_\lambda|D(M)^{-1}=I_U. 	ag{7} \] Its row is the analytic algebraic row \(\Psi_\lambda^*D(M)^{-1}\). It is generally not the Hermitian dual of \(D(M)\Psi_\lambda\). The windows in (2)--(7) are fixed in \(M\); no complex conjugation of a moving meridian is introduced. ## 2. Exact open and closed words, including the pivotal carriers Let \(B(M)=X_L(M)\cdots X_1(M)\), \(L\ge1\), be a literal factorization on \(U\). Factors may include actual reduced crossings, their scalars, turns, and prescribed framing coupons. In particular \(\kappa(M)\) and the prescribed zero-framing factor remain in \(B\). For seam frames \(D_0,\ldots,D_L\), put \[ Y_j=D_j^{-1}X_jD_{j-1},\qquad \widetilde v=D_0^{-1}v,\qquad \widetilde\ell=\ell D_L. 	ag{8} \] There is no commutation assumption on the \(X_j\)'s. Direct insertion of (6) at the \(L-1\) internal seams gives \[  egin{split} \ell Bv={}&N^{-r(L-1)} \sum_{\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_{L-1}} (\widetilde\ell Y_L\Psi_{\lambda_{L-1}}) \prod_{j=2}^{L-1} (\Psi_{\lambda_j}^*Y_j\Psi_{\lambda_{j-1}}) (\Psi_{\lambda_1}^*Y_1\widetilde v). \end{split} 	ag{9} \] For \(L=1\) this means \(\widetilde\ell Y_1\widetilde v\), with no inserted resolution. Thus the original open boundary vectors, rather than arbitrarily chosen packets, are retained. On a tensor network the coefficient is \(N^{-E}\), where \(E\) is the number of resolved one-head internal edges. For a closed word choose \(D_L=D_0\). Define \[ \mathcal T_\sigma(B)=\operatorname{Tr}(K_0^\sigma B), \qquad \sigma\in\{+1,-1\}. 	ag{10} \] The literal Cartan action is \[ K_0^\sigma\Psi_{\mathbf a,\mathbf s} =x_0^{\sigma r}\Psi_{\mathbf a,\mathbf s-\sigma\mathbf1}, \qquad \Psi_{\mathbf a,\mathbf s}^*K_0^\sigma =x_0^{\sigma r}\Psi_{\mathbf a,\mathbf s+\sigma\mathbf1}^*. 	ag{11} \] The coefficient in the row is \(x_0^{\sigma r}\), not its conjugate: this is multiplication of a fixed row by the matrix \(K_0^\sigma\). Since \(D_0\) is diagonal it commutes with \(K_0\). Consequently the exact closed formula is \[  oxed{ egin{split} \mathcal T_\sigma(B) ={}&x_0^{\sigma r}N^{-rL} \sum_{\lambda_0,\ldots,\lambda_{L-1}}  igl(\Psi_{\mathbf a_0,\mathbf s_0+\sigma\mathbf1}^* Y_L\Psi_{\lambda_{L-1}} igr)\ &\hspace{10mm}\cdot \prod_{j=1}^{L-1}  igl(\Psi_{\lambda_j}^*Y_j\Psi_{\lambda_{j-1}} igr). \end{split}}	ag{12} \] For \(L=1\) the first factor contains \(Y_1\Psi_{\lambda_0}\). There are \(L\), not \(L+1\), resolutions. A choice \(D_L
e D_0\) leaves the actual closing coupon \(D_0^{-1}D_L\); it cannot be reset by identifying the two seam labels. For clarity about half-clock marks, let \(W e_n=e_{d-n}\). For the symmetric window (2), direct substitution gives \[ Wg_{a,s}=Q^{sd}g_{d-a-L,-s}. 	ag{13} \] The equality uses the periodic extension of \(g(t)=g(L-t)\). A diagonal \(q^{J_{m occ}}\) gives instead the literal entries \(q^nQ^{sn}g(n-a)\) on a head. This is a marked half-frequency frame, not a reset integer modulation: \(q^N=-1\). The corresponding inverse must remain in the dual row, as in (7). Arbitrary balanced turnover coefficients are similarly retained as actual matrices. Formula (12) requires only the integer Cartan shifts (11), not an identification of all other closing coupons with those shifts. ## 3. The original pointed meridian functional Let \(W(M)\) be an actual analytic total intertwiner in J, and \(B(M)=q_F(M)W(M)i_F(M)\) its actual reduced matrix. J(21) identifies the original highest-cut and pivotal functional: \[ \Phi_0(W(M)) =\operatorname{Tr}_V((P_0\otimes K_{m r}^{1-N})W(M)) =D_N(M)\operatorname{Tr}_U(H(M)^{-1}B(M)), 	ag{14} \] where \(D_N(z)=(z^N-z^{-N})/(z-z^{-1})\) and \(H(M)=D_N(M^mK_0)\). By the physical identity (1), \[ H(M)^{-1} = rac{M^mK_0-M^{-m}K_0^{-1}} {\varepsilon(M^{mN}-M^{-mN})}. 	ag{15} \] The equality holds on the punctured meridian germ and with its prescribed continuation. Combining (12)--(15) gives \[  oxed{\displaystyle \Phi_0(W(M)) = rac{D_N(M)} {\varepsilon(M^{mN}-M^{-mN})} \left[M^m\mathcal T_+(B(M))-M^{-m}\mathcal T_-(B(M))ight]. }	ag{16} \] Thus the all-width packet source has the exact coefficient \(N^{-rL}\) and two opposite closing carrier shifts, with the displayed original prefactor. Neither a normalized trace nor a positive packet norm has replaced the source. Put \(\mu=\Log M\), and \(B_j=\partial_\mu^jB(e^\mu)|_{\mu=0}\). Analyticity of the left side of (14) implies \[ \mathcal T_+(B_0)=\mathcal T_-(B_0). 	ag{17} \] Expanding \(D_N(e^\mu)=N+O(\mu^2)\) and the denominator in (16) now gives the original first-jet row \[  oxed{\displaystyle \Phi_0(W(1)) = rac{\mathcal T_+(B_0)+\mathcal T_-(B_0)}{2\varepsilon} + rac{\mathcal T_+(B_1)-\mathcal T_-(B_1)} {2\varepsilon m}. }	ag{18} \] Every \(B_j\) is a true fixed-\(q\) meridian derivative, including the derivatives of crossing scalars, framing, and the actual quotient maps. Equations (17)--(18) are not imposed on an arbitrary inserted mark which is not covered by (14). All occupations remain physically capped. If \(P_T\) denotes the actual integer-degree projection, \(0\le T\le rd\), then \[ N^{-r}\sum_\lambda P_T|\Psi_\lambdaangle\langle\Psi_\lambda|P_T=P_T. 	ag{19} \] There is no normalization of the projected vectors; in general they are no longer products of one-head packets. When \(B\) preserves degree, (16) is the sum of these exact sector traces, with \(K_0|_{U_T}=x_0^rQ^{-T}\). For an actual braid word, J(30b)--(30d) supplies the removable paired sector contributions. Degree preservation alone does not imply that reciprocity. An individual sector or partial label set need not have a removable source term. No noninteger degree projection is defined here. ## 4. Moving frames and restricted meridian currents Write \(A_j=D_j^{-1}\partial_\mu D_j\). Differentiating the actual matrices (8), without differentiating the fixed packet rows, gives \[ \partial_\mu Y_j =D_j^{-1}(\partial_\mu X_j)D_{j-1} -A_jY_j+Y_jA_{j-1}. 	ag{20} \] In the complete product every adjacent connection cancels: the contribution \(Y_{j+1}A_jY_j\) from \(Y_{j+1}'\) cancels the contribution \(-Y_{j+1}A_jY_j\) from \(Y_j'\). The two endpoint terms are \(-A_LY_L\cdots Y_1+ Y_L\cdots Y_1A_0\). For a closed seam they form a commutator. Cyclicity and \([A_0,K_0]=0\) make its pivotal trace zero. For an open word they cancel with the derivatives of the two boundary adapters in (8). All actual \(X_j'\) remain. For a fixed subset \(\Lambda\subset\mathcal L\), put \[ Q_\Lambda=N^{-r}\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda} |\Psi_\lambdaangle\langle\Psi_\lambda|,\qquad P_\Lambda(M)=D(M)Q_\Lambda D(M)^{-1}. 	ag{21} \] The matrix \(Q_\Lambda\) is a positive contraction, but need not be idempotent. Its similarity need not be Hermitian. Exactly, \[ \partial_\mu P_\Lambda =[\partial_\mu D\,D^{-1},P_\Lambda]. 	ag{22} \] If an internal identity is replaced by \(Q_\Lambda\), the two terms in the preceding cancellation leave \(Y_{j+1}[A_j,Q_\Lambda]Y_j\). Equivalently this is the moving-window current (22) in physical coordinates. Thus normal connection cancellation belongs to the complete resolution, not to a selected collection of labels. For example, replacing \(B\) by a partially resolved analytic matrix \(B^\Lambda\) in the right side of (16) defines an exact meromorphic marked expression. Its residue is \[  rac{\mathcal T_+(B^\Lambda_0) -\mathcal T_-(B^\Lambda_0)} {2\varepsilon m}. 	ag{23} \] The complementary label terms cancel this residue when the complete expression returns to (14). There is no assertion that the selected part itself is an original analytic total-intertwiner source. Moving windows in (23) carry (22). The paired opposite-polarization source makes the retained higher normal terms particularly explicit. With J's matrices \(\mathcal J(\mu)=J(e^\mu)\), \(B^-(\mu)=B_-(e^\mu)\), its exact complete finite frame period is \[  egin{split} \Phi_0(W_ eta(e^\mu)) ={}&s(\mu)N^{-3r} \sum_{\lambda_0,\lambda_1,\lambda_2} (\Psi_{\lambda_0}^*\mathcal J(\mu)\Psi_{\lambda_1}) (\Psi_{\lambda_1}^*B^-(-\mu)\Psi_{\lambda_2})\ &\hspace{29mm}\cdot (\Psi_{\lambda_2}^*\mathcal J(-\mu)\Psi_{\lambda_0}),\qquad s(\mu)=D_N(e^\mu)/a_N(e^\mu). \end{split} 	ag{24} \] This is J(23) with three complete insertions of (6); no order is changed. Its entire scalar is \(a_N(M)=(-1)^{d(m+1)}N(D_N(M)/N)^m\). Independent seam frames telescope as before. Restricting the three label sets gives exactly \[ s(\mu)\operatorname{Tr} (P_0(\mu)\mathcal J(\mu)P_1(\mu) B^-(-\mu)P_2(\mu)\mathcal J(-\mu)). 	ag{25} \] Here \(P_i\) denote the partial resolutions (21), not highest-cut projectors. For fixed \(P_i\), write \(\mathcal J(\mu)=R/\mu+J_0+\mu J_1+O(\mu^2)\) and \(B^-(\mu)=B_0+\mu B_1+\mu^2B_2/2+O(\mu^3)\). The trace in (25) has coefficients \[  egin{split} C_{-2}&=-\operatorname{Tr}(P_0RP_1B_0P_2R),\ C_{-1}&=\operatorname{Tr}(P_0RP_1B_0P_2J_0 -P_0J_0P_1B_0P_2R+P_0RP_1B_1P_2R),\ C_0&=\operatorname{Tr}(P_0J_0P_1B_0P_2J_0 -P_0RP_1B_0P_2J_1-P_0J_1P_1B_0P_2R\ &\hspace{15mm}-P_0RP_1B_1P_2J_0 +P_0J_0P_1B_1P_2R-	frac12P_0RP_1B_2P_2R). \end{split} 	ag{26} \] J(28) gives \[ s(\mu)=\sigma+s_2\mu^2+O(\mu^4),\qquad \sigma=(-1)^{d(m+1)},\qquad s_2=-\sigma(m-1)(N^2-1)/6. 	ag{27} \] The finite part of (25) is consequently \(\sigma C_0+s_2C_{-2}\). For moving \(P_i\), their full Taylor coefficients, including second derivatives against \(C_{-2}\), are included before extracting that finite part. Formula (22) determines those derivatives for the stated frame motion. For complete resolutions \(P_i=I\), J(26) gives \(R^2=0\). It kills the double trace pole and the \(B_2\) trace, while the remaining terms give J(29)--(30), equivalently (18). Intervening partial resolutions do not permit that simplification. The finite sums commute with Laurent coefficient extraction; there is no pointwise pole cancellation hypothesis. The actual opposite-polarization window current is retained too. For two packet partial resolutions \(P,Q\), let \(T(M)\) be J(9), put \(B_{m ref}=B_-(M^{-1})\), and set \(\Delta_{P,Q}=PT-TQ\). J(11),(19) give directly \[ J(M)Q B_{m ref}J(M^{-1}) =a_N(M)H(M)^{-1}P B_+(M) -H(M)^{-1}\Delta_{P,Q}B_{m ref}J(M^{-1}). 	ag{27a} \] Indeed \(B_+T=TB_{m ref}\); multiply \(PB_+T-TQB_{m ref}=\Delta_{P,Q}B_{m ref}\) by \(H^{-1}\) and \(J(M^{-1})\), then use \(TJ(M^{-1})=a_NI\). The defect is zero for the complete resolutions \(P=Q=I\). No equation identifying two selected packet windows is assumed. Their meridian derivatives include both (22) and the actual derivative of \(T\). Formula (27a) is a marked matrix identity, not an extension of (14) to arbitrary nonintertwining marks. ## 5. The complete seam removes the added damping At any one-head seam the exact contraction is already (5): \[  rac1N\sum_{a,s} g_{a,s}(n)\overline{g_{a,s}(k)}=\delta_{nk}. 	ag{28} \] The frequency sum first enforces equality of the physical occupations. The center sum then has value one. With the analytic dual in (7), diagonal weights cancel on this diagonal as well. Tensoring proves the same assertion on every wire. Thus summing all packet centers and carriers restores the original capped word, including its original signs and phases. It does not leave four independent positive packet penalties at each previously estimated local kernel. There is a precise quadratic version of the same fact. Let \(x\in\mathbb R^k\) denote physical seam variations and \(a\) the corresponding free center variations. Suppose the original real quadratic form is \(	frac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx\), and the added packet penalty is \(-	frac12(x-a)^{\mathsf T}C(x-a)\), \(C>0\). The combined Hessian and its Schur complement in \(a\) are \[  egin{pmatrix}H-C&C\C&-C\end{pmatrix},\qquad (H-C)-C(-C)^{-1}C=H. 	ag{29} \] The direction \(a=x\) displays the loss of the extra penalty directly. Integrating the center Gaussian gives the same result, up to its normalization. This calculation does not assert a Gaussian approximation to every finite frame mode; (28) proves the cancellation without such an approximation. A prospective selected source contribution must therefore specify compatible center and carrier labels, including (11), an actual stationary cycle for the enlarged finite sum, and the remaining normal and boundary coupons. It must control all complementary labels, wrapped windows, and Fourier aliases relative to that contribution. A local nonzero packet kernel, or a positive frame operator, supplies none of these comparisons by itself. The frame identity also does not select a geometric relative cycle or make its coefficient nonzero. The result here is the original finite source expansion (12),(16),(24), its physical caps and boundary data, its true moving-frame normal currents (20)--(27), and the exact seam cancellation (28)--(29). No new volume-conjecture case, source positivity, coherent inverse estimate, or geometric contribution is claimed. ## Complete proof direct and author protocol * J: notes/research_opposite_polarization_source_kernel.md, SHA256 d52c6dd8e62f575a262fc7af460e258f7cb0e40b5a9c037ac46dd8d151002d44, complete 639 lines.
