title: A finite Sears certificate for the actual local full-normal source
text: # A finite Sears certificate for the actual local full-normal source Private written proof, 16 November 2026. The terminating Sears expression for a physical kernel row has a four-factorial lift. An explicit finite telescoper identifies its degree derivative with the original consumed-normal representative. Consequently appropriate local cutoffs give all four physical jets of the original kernel, including its independent mixed normal. The diagonal factorial divisor is retained throughout. This is an exact local source statement. It does not bound a tall wire contour, eliminate its endpoint packets, or assert that one cutoff is holomorphic on the whole angular box. ## 1. Original data and the canceled finite row Set \[ N\ge2,\quad D=N-1,\quad \theta=\pi/N,\quad q=e^{i\theta}, \quad Q=q^2,\quad s_z=2\sin(\theta z), \quad c(z)=2\cos((2z+1)\theta),\quad c_0=q+q^{-1}. \tag{1} \] All powers of \(Q\) use \(Q^z=e^{2i\theta z}\). The original kernel and physical rows are \[ K_N(z,w)=\sum_{k=0}^{D}e_k(z)e_k(w),\qquad F_j(w)=K_N(c(j),w),\qquad 0\le j\le J=\lfloor D/2\rfloor. \tag{2} \] A first spectral normal is required only for \(0\le j\le J_d=\lfloor(N-2)/2\rfloor\). Let \(G=G_N\) be the specified canonical factorial in the pinned factorial source. Its normalization and exact shift are \[ G(0)=1,\qquad G(z+1)=s_{z+1}G(z). \tag{3} \] It is a holomorphic unit on \(-1<\Re z<N\). Its finite logarithmic derivative formula also gives the exact reflection \[ G(z)G(D-z)=N. \tag{4} \] Indeed that formula is invariant under \(z\mapsto D-z\), so the derivative of the logarithm of the left side is zero. At zero its value is \(G(D)=\prod_{r=1}^{N-1}2\sin(r\theta)=N\). Continuation proves (4) wherever defined. From (3), \(G\) has a simple pole at each \(-1,\ldots,-D\), and its reciprocal is holomorphic with a simple zero there. These are local divisor statements, not an assertion that the reciprocal is entire. For an angular variable \(u\), put \[ C_k^\pm(u)=\prod_{r=0}^{k-1} \frac{\cos(u/2\pm(r+1/2)\theta)}{\sin((r+1)\theta)}, \qquad C_0^\pm=1. \tag{5} \] Then the exact physical row has the canceled convolution \[ \boxed{\quad F_j(-2\cos u) =\sum_{k=0}^j[C_k^+(u)C_{j-k}^-(u)]^2.\quad} \tag{6} \] In particular there are no spectral denominators in this finite formula. It is even in \(u\), by interchanging \(k\) and \(j-k\). Here is the normalization directly from the finite Sears identity. Write \(w=v+v^{-1}\), with \(v=-e^{iu}\). Converting the original Newton products to Pochhammers gives \[ F_j(w)={}_4\phi_3(Q^{-j},Q^{j+1},qv,q/v;Q,Q,Q;Q,Q). \tag{7} \] The pinned finite identity, retaining the parameter \(qv\), gives \[ F_j(w)=(qv)^j\left[\frac{(q/v;Q)_j}{(Q;Q)_j}\right]^2 \sum_{k=0}^j Q^k \left[\frac{(Q^{-j};Q)_k(qv;Q)_k} {(Q;Q)_k(qvQ^{-j};Q)_k}\right]^2. \tag{8} \] This first holds away from its apparent spectral poles. The phase in each quotient of four factors \(1-e^{i\varphi}\) is \(e^{-i\theta}\); its square cancels \(Q\). The phase in the prefactor similarly cancels \((qv)^j\). Its cosine product has indices \(0,\ldots,j-1\). The denominator cosine product of the \(k\)-th term has precisely its last \(k\) indices, in reverse order. Canceling them, and then canceling the corresponding sine factorials, gives (6). Thus (6) also holds at every removable spectral pole of (8). No phase or scalar carrier is left over. ## 2. The four-factorial lift and its necessary local domain For independent complex degree variables \(\alpha,\beta\), define the meromorphic summand \[ T_k(\alpha,\beta)= \frac{G(\alpha+\beta-k)^2} {G(\alpha-k)^2G(\beta-k)^2G(k)^2},\qquad 0\le k<N. \tag{9} \] It is symmetric in \(\alpha,\beta\). By (4), equivalently \[ T_k(\alpha,\beta)= \frac{N^2} {[G(k)G(\alpha-k)G(\beta-k) G(D-\alpha-\beta+k)]^2}. \tag{10} \] These are identities of meromorphic functions; apparent factors are combined before a limiting value is taken. For \(\beta=D/2-Nu/(2\pi)\), one has \(c(\beta)=-2\cos u\). The shift formula gives \[ C_k^+(u)=\frac{G(\beta)}{G(\beta-k)G(k)},\qquad C_l^-(u)=\frac{G(\beta+l)}{G(\beta)G(l)}. \tag{11} \] Consequently (6) is exactly \[ F_j(c(\beta))=\sum_{k=0}^jT_k(j,\beta). \tag{12} \] Its interpretation at exceptional factors is the holomorphic continuation supplied by (6). The diagonal divisor must not be suppressed. For example at \((\alpha,\beta)=(0,0)\), a term with \(1\le k<N\) has a nonzero holomorphic unit times \[ \frac{\alpha^2\beta^2}{(\alpha+\beta)^2}. \tag{13} \] Separate vanishing in either variable therefore does not give a joint holomorphic germ there. We will use the finite cutoff \[ S_M(\alpha,\beta)=\sum_{k=0}^MT_k(\alpha,\beta). \tag{14} \] At a physical pair \((j,l)\), the safe local condition is \[ \max(j,l)\le M\le j+l,\qquad M<N. \tag{15} \] Every numerator argument in (9) then has nonnegative base value, and every reciprocal denominator is holomorphic near its base integer, which is less than \(N\). Thus (14) is jointly holomorphic on a neighborhood of that pair. Equivalently, a sufficient open restriction for the numerator is \(\Re(\alpha+\beta)>M-1\); all other factors retain their own local pole exclusions. No full-box assertion follows. ## 3. An explicit finite contiguous certificate Use the original coefficients \[ A(\alpha)=\frac{s_{\alpha+1}^4}{s_{2\alpha+1}s_{2\alpha+2}}, \qquad C(\alpha)=\frac{s_\alpha^4}{s_{2\alpha}s_{2\alpha+1}}, \qquad C(0)=0. \tag{16} \] The following is a meromorphic finite identity, so it can first be checked where all displayed denominators are nonzero. Put \[ X=Q^\alpha,\quad Y=Q^\beta,\quad z=Q^k,\quad s=QX, \quad \mathcal D=(1-Xs)(1+s)(1+X), \quad \mathcal K=\frac{q^{-1}s^2}{Y\mathcal D},\quad \xi=z/s, \tag{17} \] and define the Laurent polynomial \[ \begin{split} \mathcal P(z)=\mathcal K\big[& 2\{(1+X)-(1+s)Y\}\xi\\ &+(1+s)(1+X)(Y^2-1)-4(X-s)Y\\ &+2Y\{X(1+s)-s(1+X)Y\}\xi^{-1}\big]. \end{split} \tag{18} \] The exact flux is \[ \mathcal H_k(\alpha,\beta)=T_k(\alpha,\beta) \frac{(1-Q^k)^2\mathcal P(Q^k)}{(Q^k-QX)^2}. \tag{19} \] The summand and rational factor in (19) are combined before specializing. In particular a zero of the summand is not counted before checking the denominator in the flux. **Proposition 1.** Where its terms are defined, the finite sum obeys \[ \boxed{\begin{split} &A(\alpha)S_M(\alpha+1,\beta)+C(\alpha)S_M(\alpha-1,\beta)\\ &\quad-[A(\alpha)+C(\alpha)+c_0-c(\beta)]S_M(\alpha,\beta) =\mathcal H_{M+1}(\alpha,\beta). \end{split}} \tag{20} \] It is enough here to use \(M+1<N\). The right side is the actual finite boundary, not an infinite-series limit. *Proof.* The shift relation gives the three exact ratios \[ \frac{T_k(\alpha+1,\beta)}{T_k(\alpha,\beta)} =Y^{-1}\frac{(z-QXY)^2}{(z-QX)^2},\qquad \frac{T_k(\alpha-1,\beta)}{T_k(\alpha,\beta)} =Y\frac{(z-X)^2}{(z-XY)^2}, \tag{21} \] \[ \frac{T_{k+1}}{T_k} =Q\frac{(z-X)^2(z-Y)^2}{(1-Qz)^2(z-XY)^2}. \tag{22} \] Thus the flux difference divided by \(T_k\) is \[ \frac{\mathcal H_{k+1}-\mathcal H_k}{T_k} =\frac{(z-Y)^2\mathcal P(Qz)}{Q(z-XY)^2} -\frac{(1-z)^2\mathcal P(z)}{(z-QX)^2}. \tag{23} \] We verify that this equals the expression obtained from the left side of (20) using (21). Here are explicit checks of the rational identity, including its simple poles. Write \(s=QX\). The required values and logarithmic derivatives of \(\mathcal P\) at its two relevant arguments are \[ \begin{split} P_0:=\mathcal P(s) &=-\frac{A}{Y}\frac{s^2(1-Y)^2}{(1-s)^2},\\ P_1:=\mathcal P(sY) &=\frac{CQX^2(1-Y)^2}{Y(1-X)^2},\\ \frac{\mathcal P'(s)}{P_0} &=\frac2{s(1-Y)}+\frac2{1-s},\\ \frac{\mathcal P'(sY)}{P_1} &=-\frac2{s(1-Y)}+\frac2{QY(1-X)}. \end{split} \tag{24} \] They follow by substituting (18); equalities with a vanishing denominator mean their cleared versions. In particular \[ \frac{P_1}{P_0}=-\frac{(1-X)(1+s)}{(1+X)(1-s)}. \tag{25} \] Equations (24) match both principal parts at \(z=s\) and \(z=XY\) in (23). The possible simple pole at zero cancels: if the \(z^{-1}\) coefficient of \(\mathcal P\) is \(p_{-1}\), both terms have coefficient \(p_{-1}/(Q^2X^2z)\). At infinity the linear terms cancel as well. The difference of the two sides is therefore constant. For completeness, the constant term of (23) is \[ p_0(Q^{-1}-1)+2p_1\{Y(X-1)-(s-1)\}, \qquad \mathcal P(z)=p_1z+p_0+p_{-1}/z. \tag{26} \] Substituting (18) into (26) gives \[ (C+q)Y+(A+q^{-1})Y^{-1} -\frac{8qX}{(1+X)(1+QX)}. \tag{27} \] Directly from (16), \[ \begin{split} A&=-q^{-1}\frac{(1-QX)^4}{(1-QX^2)(1-Q^2X^2)},\\ C&=-q\frac{(1-X)^4}{(1-X^2)(1-QX^2)},\\ A+C+c_0&=\frac{8qX}{(1+X)(1+QX)}. \end{split} \tag{28} \] Since \(c(\beta)=qY+q^{-1}Y^{-1}\), (27) is precisely the constant term required by (21). This proves the single-summand identity. Summing it telescopes, and \(\mathcal H_0=0\) by the factor \((1-Q^0)^2\), initially at regular parameters. Meromorphic continuation proves (20). \(\square\) At a regular physical degree \(\alpha=j\), if \(M\ge j+1\) and \(\Re(\alpha+\beta)>M\) in the local neighborhood, the boundary in (20) is holomorphic and \[ \mathcal H_{M+1}=O((\alpha-j)^2). \tag{29} \] Indeed \(1/G(\alpha-M-1)^2\) has that double zero, the numerator in (9) is regular, and \(Q^{M+1}-Q^{j+1}\ne0\) for the stated finite range. In contrast, at \(M=j\) the denominator in (19) can cancel that zero. That boundary cannot be discarded. The recurrence use below is for \(N\ge3\), with all flux indices strictly below \(N\); the \(N=2\) source is handled directly. ## 4. The actual independent normal Define the short degree derivative \[ H_j(\beta)= \left.\partial_\alpha\sum_{k=0}^jT_k(\alpha,\beta) \right|_{\alpha=j}. \tag{30} \] This is not the derivative of a terminating sum whose upper limit has been differentiated. It is the derivative of the displayed fixed finite formula. Let \(\widetilde Q_N\), \(R_j\), and \(\widehat G_j\) have exactly the normalization in the pinned physical residue source: \[ \widehat G_j(w)= \frac{c'(0)F_j(w)\widetilde Q_N(w)+R_j(w)}{c'(j)}, \qquad c'(j)=-4\theta\sin((2j+1)\theta). \tag{31} \] Here \(R_j\) is the common-shift Jacobi determinant derivative, with \(c_0\) fixed, and \[ c'(0)\widetilde Q_N(c(\beta)) =2[g_N'(\beta)-g_N'(0)]. \tag{32} \] **Theorem 2.** For every double physical degree \(0\le j\le J_d\), as an identity on the original \(\beta\)-strip, \[ \boxed{\quad H_j(\beta) =c'(0)F_j(c(\beta))\widetilde Q_N(c(\beta)) +R_j(c(\beta)) =c'(j)\widehat G_j(c(\beta)).\quad} \tag{33} \] In particular this retains the actual normal anchor, rather than only a formally differentiated homogeneous row equation. *Proof.* At \(j=0\), (9) gives \[ T_0(\alpha,\beta)=\frac{G(\alpha+\beta)^2}{G(\alpha)^2G(\beta)^2}, \qquad H_0(\beta)=2[g_N'(\beta)-g_N'(0)], \tag{34} \] which is exactly (32). For a recurrence step at \(\alpha=j\), first choose \(M=j+1\) and an open \(\beta\)-domain sufficiently far to the right of this finite cutoff, avoiding every displayed divisor. The finite shift identity (20) and (29) hold there with zero value and zero first \(\alpha\)-derivative of the boundary. At each of the integer rows \(j-1,j,j+1\), the terms beyond that row have a double degree zero. Thus differentiating (20) gives \[ \begin{split} A(j)H_{j+1}+C(j)H_{j-1} -[A(j)+C(j)+c_0-c(\beta)]H_j ={}&-A'(j)[F_{j+1}-F_j]\\ &-C'(j)[F_{j-1}-F_j], \end{split} \tag{35} \] where all rows on the right are evaluated at \(c(\beta)\). The step at zero uses \(C(\alpha)=O(\alpha^3)\), so its backward contribution and its first derivative vanish. This is also obtained directly on the same regular initial domain; at \(j=0\) the backward terms in (35) are omitted, without assigning an additional \(F_{-1}\) or \(H_{-1}\) datum. The common-shift determinant \(F_j^{(\varepsilon)}\) obeys the same three-term recurrence with \(A(j+\varepsilon)\), \(C(j+\varepsilon)\), and fixed \(c_0\). Its derivative \(R_j\) satisfies (35), with initial value zero. The physical row \(F_j\) solves the homogeneous equation. Therefore the right side of (33) satisfies (35) with the initial datum (34). Forward uniqueness proves (33). Only regular steps below the last needed row are used; no recurrence is imposed through the fold. For \(N=2\) the sole required row is the already proved initial identity. Finally (30) is holomorphic for \(-1<\Re\beta<N\). For \(k\le j\), its numerator argument at \(\alpha=j\) is \(\beta+j-k\), which has no factorial pole in this region. Possible zeros beyond the original factorial strip cause no pole in the numerator or its derivative. Each reciprocal \(G(\beta-k)^{-2}\) is holomorphic there; its possible negative integer factors are zeros, and its argument never reaches the positive zero divisor of \(G\). The other denominator is a nonzero physical factorial. This proves the claimed holomorphy, also after the single \(\alpha\)-derivative. The right side of (33) is holomorphic on the same original angular window by its pinned source formula. Analytic continuation from the initial open domain proves the identity throughout that window. No joint continuation of an excessive cutoff through its diagonal pole is used. \(\square\) ## 5. Exact local full jets and cutoff transitions Fix a physical pair \((j,l)\) and a cutoff satisfying (15). In its joint holomorphic neighborhood, \[ S_M(j,\beta)=F_j(c(\beta)),\qquad S_M(\alpha,l)=F_l(c(\alpha)). \tag{36} \] For a double first row, every excess term \(k>j\) has a double \(\alpha-j\) zero with holomorphic coefficient. Hence \[ \partial_\alpha S_M(j,\beta) =c'(j)\widehat G_j(c(\beta)). \tag{37} \] The same assertion holds with the endpoints interchanged. The pinned representative preserves the value and required first normal at every physical second endpoint. Thus, when both rows are double, \[ \begin{split} S_M(j,l)&=K_N(c_j,c_l),\\ \partial_\alpha S_M(j,l)&=c'(j)K_z(c_j,c_l),\\ \partial_\beta S_M(j,l)&=c'(l)K_w(c_j,c_l),\\ \partial_\alpha\partial_\beta S_M(j,l) &=c'(j)c'(l)K_{zw}(c_j,c_l). \end{split} \tag{38} \] No terminating-value differentiation has replaced the independent high Newton normal in this formula; it entered through (32)--(35). At \(N=2\), the only physical pair is \((0,0)\), and (15) requires \(M=0\). The original kernel is \(K_2(z,w)=1+zw/16\). The factorial formula gives \(\partial_\alpha\partial_\beta S_0(0,0)=2g_2''(0)\). The finite logarithmic-derivative formula yields \(g_2''(0)=\pi^2/8\), while \(c'(0)=-2\pi\); hence \(2g_2''(0)/c'(0)^2=1/16\), as required. No isolated \(T_N\) or singular flux factor is evaluated in this check. If an endpoint is the odd simple node, only its value and the other endpoint's required normal are prescribed. There is no division by its vanishing \(c'(J)\). To obtain a local spectral germ there, average the local angular germ under \(\alpha\mapsto D-\alpha\), or under the corresponding \(\beta\) reflection. Use both averages if both endpoints are simple. This preserves every prescribed datum and gives holomorphic descent through the spectral fold. The same operation does not assert global evenness of an unsymmetrized fixed cutoff. If two cutoffs both satisfy (15) at the same physical pair, their difference is a sum of terms with \(k>\max(j,l)\). Each is a holomorphic unit times a factor divisible by \((\alpha-j)^2(\beta-l)^2\), or has still higher vanishing. All four prescribed jets therefore agree on overlaps where the respective local cutoff conditions hold. The same holds after the odd-fold symmetrization. Products at a shared color retain these exact full jets by the ordinary product rule. They may be consumed by subsequent original traces, with their original crossings and spectators retained. These transitions are local full-Hermite-null source changes. They do not establish an untraced free-polynomial identity, one global holomorphic kernel, a bounded relative primitive, or a small norm for the transition away from the physical grid. In particular the finite boundary (20) and the diagonal divisor (13) remain relevant to every attempted moving-wire contour. ## Direct sources and proof scope The complete direct texts and the used implications were read at these versions: * [Finite balanced Sears proof](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/finite_balanced_sears_operator_proof.md), SHA256 4b32a5c71f5cc4484f773007e34d980266e0ba9688b0237d30f108e8a8e4ab8d: the terminating rational transformation with its complete prefactor. * [Canonical factorial](research_exact_cyclotomic_factorial.md), SHA256 0f989261f53747266ac62dba40ca7548138012b266521e98a03bd94b450c657b: the specified factorial, exact shift, finite logarithmic derivative, and normalization used to prove (4) and the local divisors. * [Original physical residue packets](research_compact_positive_contour_residue_control.md), SHA256 cac1016d5f515510b95071a25c8d97345b334043492a6b430c4e924f87d82bb0: the Newton source, common-shift Jacobi determinant, actual normal anchor and representative, full mixed jets and the odd simple node. The explicit finite flux and its source normalization are proved above. Only written mathematics, source-text reads, and hashes were used. No mathematical program, numerical experiment, test or compilation was run. Adopted notes and public manuscripts are unchanged.

title: Finite trace observables for the opposite-polarization characteristic
text:
# Finite trace observables for the opposite-polarization characteristic Private written proof, 18 November 2026. A finite explicit family of actual transported Casimirs separates the ordered irreducible \(SL_2\) tuple up to one common conjugation. Both the full operators and their first-head quotients have Laurent degree bounded independently of the color \(N\). Their complete-root coherent symbols can therefore be computed directly, without a symbol theorem for a full crossing or the prefix change of basis. Applied to the actual root kernel \(T(1)\) and the Laurent residue of \(J\), these observables give explicit homogeneous characteristic equations. They recover the turned ordered character and reverse the selected regular total-product eigenvalue wherever such a characteristic relation exists. The finite part of \(J\) instead retains an inhomogeneous normal row. No nonzero kernel amplitude, integration cycle, or geometric contribution is constructed. The complete directs are M, the actual classical meridians; Q, the literal rational quantum conjugation; R, the actual prefix quotient; and J, the actual opposite-polarization kernel. All trace separation, four-entry transport, and bounded-degree calculations are below. ## 1. Actual quantum based meridians Fix \(N\ge2\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\), \(d=N-1\), and \(m\ge2\). Keep the actual balanced generators, with \(E\) denoting the scaled lowering operator: \[ KE=QEK,\qquad KF=Q^{-1}FK,\qquad [E,F]=(q-q^{-1})(K-K^{-1}). 	ag{1} \] Different heads commute. Put \(e_i=qE_i\), and form matrices whose entries are the actual finite operators: \[ L_i^+= egin{pmatrix}K_i&e_i\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad L_i^-= egin{pmatrix}1&0\-K_iF_i&K_i\end{pmatrix},\qquad G_i=(L_i^-)^{-1}L_i^+ = egin{pmatrix}K_i&e_i\F_iK_i&F_ie_i+K_i^{-1}\end{pmatrix}. 	ag{2} \] Only \(K_i\), an actual invertible diagonal matrix, is inverted. For instance \((L_i^-)^{-1}=\left( egin{smallmatrix}1&0\F_i&K_i^{-1} \end{smallmatrix}ight)\). Define the ordered prefixes and based matrices by \[ B_j^\pm=L_j^\pm\cdots L_1^\pm,\qquad H_j=(B_{j-1}^-)^{-1}G_jB_{j-1}^-,\qquad B_0^\pm=I. 	ag{3} \] All matrix products retain their noncommutative entry order. Telescoping, without cyclically moving any entries, gives \[ H_s\cdots H_1=(B_s^-)^{-1}B_s^+. 	ag{4} \] The ordered coproducts have \[ B_s^+= egin{pmatrix}K_{[s]}&qE_{[s]}\0&1\end{pmatrix}, \quad B_s^-= egin{pmatrix}1&0\-K_{[s]}F_{[s]}&K_{[s]}\end{pmatrix}. 	ag{5} \] For example the lower-left entry of \(L_2^-L_1^-\) is \(-K_2F_2-K_2K_1F_1=-K_1K_2(F_1+K_1^{-1}F_2)\). Induction proves (5). Thus with \(\operatorname{tr}_q A=qA_{11}+q^{-1}A_{22}\), \[ \operatorname{tr}_q(H_s\cdots H_1) =F_{[s]}E_{[s]}+qK_{[s]}+q^{-1}K_{[s]}^{-1} =:\Omega_{[s]}. 	ag{6} \] This fixes the normalization of every observable. Ordinary matrix trace cyclicity has not been substituted for quantum trace. ### The four-entry checked-crossing calculation Let \(\mathcal R\) be the literal positive checked crossing on two equal-color heads, including its original scalar. The scalar cancels in its conjugation action. Q's exact rational formulas, expressed using the scaled \(E\), give \[ u=e_2K_2^{-1}K_1F_1,\quad G=(1-Q^{-1}u)^{-1},\quad Z=K_2(1-Q^{-1}u)=K_2-e_2K_1F_1, 	ag{7} \] \[ \operatorname{Ad}_{\mathcal R}K_1=Z,\qquad \operatorname{Ad}_{\mathcal R}e_1=e_2K_1,\qquad \operatorname{Ad}_{\mathcal R}F_1 =F_1+F_2K_1^{-1}-GK_2^{-2}F_1=:F'. 	ag{8} \] These are Q's algebra-conjugation formulas, rather than its contravariant classical point map. On the actual root heads \(u^N=0\), so every displayed inverse is an actual finite inverse. Its degree-\(N\) expansion will not be used for a symbol calculation. Direct multiplication gives \[ (L_1^-)^{-1}G_2L_1^-=  egin{pmatrix} Z&e_2K_1\ F_1Z+K_1^{-1}F_2K_2-F_2e_2F_1-K_2^{-1}F_1& e_2F_1K_1+F_2e_2+K_2^{-1} \end{pmatrix}. 	ag{9} \] The first two entries agree with (8). For the third, the exact relations \(F_1u=QuF_1\) and \(K_2^{-1}u=Q^{-1}uK_2^{-1}\) give \[ GK_2^{-2}F_1 Z =GK_2^{-1}(1-u)F_1=K_2^{-1}F_1. 	ag{10} \] Consequently \(F'Z\) is the lower-left entry in (9). For the fourth, \[ F'e_2K_1+Z^{-1} =e_2F_1K_1+F_2e_2+ G(K_2^{-1}-K_2^{-2}e_2F_1K_1). 	ag{11} \] Here \(K_2^{-2}e_2F_1K_1=Q^{-1}uK_2^{-1}\), so the last summand is \(K_2^{-1}\). This verifies all four entries and proves \[ \operatorname{Ad}_{\mathcal R}G_1=(L_1^-)^{-1}G_2L_1^-. 	ag{12} \] The inverse denominators in (8) have cancelled in this observable. Actual total intertwining preserves both products \(L_2^\pm L_1^\pm\). Together with (4),(12), this proves the exact matrix rule \[ \operatorname{Ad}_{\mathcal R}(H_1,H_2) =(H_2,H_2H_1H_2^{-1}). 	ag{13} \] The \(H_i\) are invertible products of triangular matrices, so this step needs no scalar trace division. With earlier heads present, conjugate (13) by their unchanged \(B^-_{i-1}\). Later prefixes stay unchanged because \(L^-_{i+1}L^-_i\) is preserved. Thus the same rule holds at any adjacent positions, fixing all other based matrices. Its inverse is obtained by actual inverse conjugation. The rule is the inverse Hurwitz action, as appropriate for conjugation of observables. ## 2. A finite explicit family of transported Casimirs For every increasing subset \(I=\{i_1<\cdots<i_s\}\), \(1\le s\le3\), define \[ \mathcal O_I=\operatorname{tr}_q(H_{i_s}\cdots H_{i_1}). 	ag{14} \] There is a specified braid implementing (14). Starting with the ordered list, move \(i_1\) left to position one by consecutive rules (13); then move \(i_2\) to position two, and \(i_3\) to position three when present. In a swap \((X,Y)\mapsto(Y,YXY^{-1})\), the right member moves left unchanged. Induction shows that the selected matrices have become the first \(s\) entries unchanged and in their original order. Therefore, for the resulting literal finite braid operator \(\mathcal R_{	au_I}\), \[ \mathcal O_I =\operatorname{Ad}_{\mathcal R_{	au_I}}\Omega_{[s]}. 	ag{15} \] Precisely, start with \(\mathcal U=I\) and, for each such row move at position \(i\), update \(\mathcal U\leftarrow\mathcal U\mathcal R_i\). Then \(\operatorname{Ad}_{\mathcal U}(H_j)\) is the updated list: the new row formula is applied inside the existing conjugation. This fixes the product order in \(\mathcal R_{	au_I}=\mathcal U\). There are \(\sum_{s=1}^3 inom ms\) observables, omitting empty binomial coefficients. This is independent of \(N\). Each \(\Omega_{[s]}\) commutes with the full ordered total generators: its own block Casimir commutes with its block generators, and the remaining coproduct factors commute with that block. Actual braid intertwining therefore proves the same total invariance for \(\mathcal O_I\). Equation (14) is an explicit bounded-degree expression for this invariant, not just the definition by conjugation with a growing matrix. Indeed every entry of \(L_i^\pm\) and its inverse is a Laurent polynomial in \(K_i\) and a polynomial in \(E_i,F_i\). Equations (3),(14) give a finite expression with a degree bound depending only on \(m\). Its coefficients are Laurent polynomials in \(q\), with no inverse \(q-q^{-1}\). No original endpoint, crossing scalar, or changed cut is needed to obtain (15). ## 3. The quotient also has bounded degree Write \(x=-M/q\), \(f_n=\prod_{j=1}^n(1-Q^j)\). R's actual quotient of any total intertwiner is \[ \mathcal B(O)=p_0S^{-1}Oi_0,\qquad S^{-1}=\sum_{n=0}^d  rac{(-1)^nQ^{n(n-1)/2}x^{-n}L_1^nF_{m r}^n}{f_n}. 	ag{16} \] Here \(i_0\) inserts first occupation zero. The following bounded formula in fact computes \(p_0S^{-1}Oi_0\) for any fixed Laurent polynomial word \(O\), without an intertwining hypothesis. Use (1) to order the first head as \[ O=\sum_{n,a,c}F_1^nK_1^aE_1^c\otimes O_{nac}. 	ag{17} \] The finite sum has bounded indices depending only on the given word degree. Commuting \(E_1\) past \(F_1\) introduces \((q-q^{-1})(K_1-K_1^{-1})\), not its inverse. Every term with \(c>0\) kills \(i_0\), and the other terms give \(p_nOi_0=f_n\sum_a x^aO_{na0}\). Substitution in (16) cancels the factorial exactly: \[  oxed{\quad \mathcal B(O)= \sum_n(-1)^nQ^{n(n-1)/2}x^{-n}F_{m r}^n \sum_a x^aO_{na0}. \quad}	ag{18} \] The remaining-head factors have their displayed order. Terms \(n\ge N\) vanish on both sides: on the first head \(F_1^N=0\), and on the remaining ordered tensor \(F_{m r}^N=0\). The latter follows from the root Gaussian binomial formula. Thus (18), with its fixed finite index set, applies at every level. It neither divides by \(f_N\) nor expands the entire prefix matrix. In particular all \(\mathcal B(\mathcal O_I)\) have Laurent degree bounded independently of \(N\), with coefficients regular as \(q	o1\). Their commutative leading expression is the substitution \[ E_1=0,\qquad K_1=x,\qquad F_1=-x^{-1}F_{m r} 	ag{19} \] in the full observable. This is the actual \(F_\Sigma=0\) section, since \(F_\Sigma=F_1+K_1^{-1}F_{m r}\). It gives \(K_\Sigma=xK_{m r}\), \(E_\Sigma=E_{m r}\). It is an observable calculation through the first vacuum, not a generating-function or amplitude assertion for that vacuum. ## 4. Complete-root coherent symbols without missing arrows This section concerns \(M=1\) only. On a finite head let \(Xw_a=Q^aw_a\), and let \(S_0\) be the cyclic unit raising shift. The actual matrices are exactly \[ E=S_0^{-1}(X^{-1}-1),\qquad F=S_0(1-QX),\qquad K=-q^{-1}X^{-1}. 	ag{20} \] The putative bottom wrap of \(E\) has coefficient zero, as does the top wrap of \(F\). Thus (20) is an equality of the original nilpotent matrices, not a replacement by a different cyclic module. Use the original binomial coherent kernel from J and divide it by \((1+wz)^d\). A fixed word in (20) can be ordered as a finite sum of \(S_0^sX^j\) with coefficient polynomials vanishing at every input that would wrap. For \(N\) larger than its fixed degree, its exact kernel is therefore a finite sum of \[ c_{sj}(q)\,w^s(1+Q^jwz)^d. 	ag{21} \] To see the endpoint assertion, follow the word before ordering: any path leaving the finite interval meets one of the two zero coefficients in (20). Ordering gives the same matrix, so its coefficient on a wrapping input is still zero. The usual binomial sum then proves (21), with no unretained endpoint summand. On a fixed compact complex chart with \(w
e0\) and \(1+wz
e0\), put \(t=wz/(1+wz)\), \(c_0=2\pi i\). For bounded \(j\), \[ \left( rac{1+Q^jwz}{1+wz}ight)^d =\exp(c_0jt) igl(1+O(N^{-1}) igr). 	ag{22} \] Taylor expansion of the logarithm proves this uniformly with every fixed number of chart derivatives. Finite sums and tensor products give the principal substitution \[ A=\exp(c_0t),\quad p=w^{-1},\qquad E=p(A^{-1}-1),\quad F=(1-A)/p,\quad K=-A^{-1}. 	ag{23} \] It applies to the full and reduced observables above, including their zeros, since no division by \(E\) or \(F\) was made. Away from \(M=1\), the cyclic formula for \(E\) has an additional endpoint row. It must be retained in meridian derivatives. Equations (20)--(23) make no meridian-normal or whole-\(q\)-normal claim. They are also not uniform symbol statements for a degree-growing crossing, prefix star, or \(T\) kernel. By M's Gauss reconstruction, (23) turns (3) into its actual ordered classical \(SL_2\) meridians. The principal of (14) is precisely \[ o_I=\operatorname{tr}(H_{i_s}\cdots H_{i_1}). 	ag{24} \] The conventional physical meridians are \(-H_i\); multiplying each length-\(s\) trace by \((-1)^s\) is an explicit equivalent convention. ## 5. The finite trace family separates irreducible tuples We prove this algebraically, including its local scheme meaning. For \(A,B,C\in SL_2\), Cayley--Hamilton and trace give \[ AB+BA=(\operatorname{tr}A)B+(\operatorname{tr}B)A+  igl(\operatorname{tr}(AB)-\operatorname{tr}A\operatorname{tr}B igr)I, 	ag{25} \] \[  egin{split} \operatorname{tr}(ABC)+\operatorname{tr}(ACB) ={}&\operatorname{tr}(AB)\operatorname{tr}C+ \operatorname{tr}(AC)\operatorname{tr}B+ \operatorname{tr}(BC)\operatorname{tr}A\ &-\operatorname{tr}A\operatorname{tr}B\operatorname{tr}C. \end{split}	ag{26} \] For (25), apply the squared traceless-matrix identity to \(A-\operatorname{tr}(A)I/2\) and \(B-\operatorname{tr}(B)I/2\). Taking its product with \(C\) proves (26). Together with cyclicity of ordinary trace, (26) recovers the other orientation of every distinct triple from (24). Repeated indices reduce by Cayley--Hamilton. Thus the one chosen order in (14) supplies every trace of length at most three. There are two explicit types of reconstruction charts. First choose two generators \(A,B\), and write \[ a=\operatorname{tr}A,\quad b=\operatorname{tr}B,\quad c=\operatorname{tr}(AB),\qquad \Delta=a^2+b^2+c^2-abc-4. 	ag{27} \] The trace Gram determinant of \(I,A,B,AB\) is \(-\Delta^2\). Indeed for \(u=A-aI/2\), \(v=B-bI/2\), write \(u^2=\alpha I\), \(v^2= eta I\), \(uv+vu=\gamma I\). Then \(\gamma^2-4\alpha eta=\Delta\). The basis \(I,u,v,uv-\gamma I/2\) has Gram determinant \(2(4\alpha eta-\gamma^2)(\Delta/2)=-\Delta^2\). The change to \(I,A,B,AB\) has determinant one. When \(\Delta\) is a unit these four matrices are a basis of \(\operatorname{Mat}_2\). The traces against them recover the coordinates of every \(H_j\) by this explicit Gram inverse. They use only single, pair, and triple traces. The multiplication table is fixed by \(A^2=aA-I\), \(B^2=bB-I\), and (25). Second, choose three generators \(A,B,C\) for which the trace Gram matrix of \(I,A,B,C\) is invertible. Again pair traces recover all generator coordinates. Every multiplication constant of this basis is recovered by taking the traces of a product of two basis members against a third and applying that Gram inverse. These are precisely traces of length at most three, already supplied by (24),(26). These finitely many charts cover every irreducible complex tuple. Let \(L\) be the span of its traceless generator parts in \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\). If \(\dim L=3\), the second chart applies. If \(\dim L\le1\), all generators have a common eigenline. If \(\dim L=2\) and the trace form on it is degenerate, its radical contains a nonzero isotropic traceless matrix, hence a nilpotent. Conjugate it to a nonzero multiple of \(e_{12}\). Orthogonality forces the lower-left entry of every member of \(L\) to vanish, again giving a common eigenline. In the remaining two-dimensional case the trace form is nondegenerate; any two generator parts forming a basis have \(\Delta
e0\), giving the first chart. For a complete irreducible parabolic tuple one can simply choose two distinct parabolic flags. Their nilpotent parts have nonzero product trace, so (27) is nonzero. Suppose two tuples on one of these charts have the same data (24). The corresponding basis map preserves every multiplication constant just computed. It is therefore an algebra isomorphism between their full matrix algebras, sending every ordered generator to its mate. This isomorphism is inner. Here is also the local Artin-ring proof of that last assertion. Let \(F_{ij}\) be the images of ordinary matrix units. Choose \(v\) in the image of \(F_{11}\) lifting a nonzero vector of its residue line, and put \(w=F_{21}v\). The relations of the \(F_{ij}\) show that \((v,w)\) is a basis after reduction, hence over the local ring. In this basis all \(F_{ij}\) are ordinary matrix units. The change-of-basis determinant is a unit; a square root of it exists locally over a complex Artin ring if an \(SL_2\) representative is desired. Uniqueness is up to scalars, since a matrix commuting with the full matrix algebra is scalar. This proves equality of the local ordered-character relations, not only a count of dimensions or separation of closed points. The Gram denominators are the specified chart units. All conjugations are one common conjugation of the whole tuple. ## 6. The actual opposite-kernel characteristic rows Use J's actual operators, with all original scalars retained: \[ T=q_FE_\Sigma^d\mathscr C\,i_F(M^{-1}),\qquad J=H^{-1}T,\qquad H=D_N(MK_{m r}), \qquad K_0T=TK_0^{-1}. 	ag{28} \] For each total-invariant \(\mathcal O_I\), define its literal turned operator on the reflected space by \[ \mathcal O_I^\vee(M^{-1}) =\mathscr C(M)^{-1}\mathcal O_I(M)\mathscr C(M). 	ag{29} \] Turnover exchanges \(E,F\), inverts \(K\), and reverses the head labels. Consequently (29) and its quotient also have the bounded Laurent expressions just proved. The quotient descent and commutation with \(E_\Sigma^d\) give the exact identities \[  oxed{\quad \mathcal B(\mathcal O_I(M))T(M) =T(M)\mathcal B(\mathcal O_I^\vee(M^{-1})),\qquad \mathcal B(\mathcal O_I(M))J(M) =J(M)\mathcal B(\mathcal O_I^\vee(M^{-1})). \quad}	ag{30} \] For \(J\), use also that every \(\mathcal B(\mathcal O_I)\) commutes with \(K_{m r}\), hence with \(H\). These are finite actual source-compatible operator rows. They do not require the kernel to have an asymptotic phase. The whole normal row is also explicit. Set \(u=\log M\), write \(A(u)=\mathcal B(\mathcal O_I(e^u))\), and let \(A^\vee(v)\) be the quotient on the color-\(e^v\) module of the turned word. Thus the right member of (30) is \(J(u)A^\vee(-u)\). Turnover on the generators is exactly \(E\leftrightarrow F,\ K\mapsto K^{-1}\), with reversed heads, so this is one analytic bounded word, not an independently chosen reflected symbol. Write \[ A(u)=A_0+uA_1+\cdots,\quad A^\vee(v)=A^\vee_0+vA^\vee_1+\cdots,\quad J(u)=\mathsf R/u+J_0+O(u). 	ag{30a} \] J proves this simple-pole expansion. Comparing its two first orders in (30) gives \[ A_0\mathsf R=\mathsf R A^\vee_0,\qquad A_0J_0-J_0A^\vee_0 =-A_1\mathsf R-\mathsf R A^\vee_1. 	ag{30b} \] These retain the original finite endpoint rows and scalar normalizations. In particular the finite part \(J_0\) is not asserted to intertwine the root observables by itself. Section 4 does not provide a principal symbol for the normal terms in (30b). Precisely, put \(T_0=T(1)\). Both actual root kernels \(\mathcal K=T_0\) and \(\mathcal K=\mathsf R\) satisfy the homogeneous rows \[ A_0\mathcal K=\mathcal K A^\vee_0,\qquad K_0\mathcal K=\mathcal K K_0^{-1}. 	ag{30c} \] For \(T_0\) this is direct specialization of (30); for \(\mathsf R\) it is the residue equation (30b). If either of these sequences of root kernels has a regular semiclassical characteristic relation on the coherent charts of Section 4, its principal left and right actions, with the usual dual input covector convention, impose \[ o_I(y)=o_I^\vee(z)\quad\hbox{for every }|I|\le3,\qquad k_{m r}(y)=k_{m r}(z)^{-1}. 	ag{31} \] This assertion concerns \(T_0\) or \(\mathsf R\), not \(J_0\). No homogeneous characteristic row for \(J_0\) follows without controlling the two normal forcing terms in (30b). Nor is a meromorphic phase across \(M=1\) asserted. All principal functions in (31) were computed from bounded operators in Sections 3--4. On the irreducible trace charts of Section 5, its first equations identify the output ordered tuple with the explicitly turned input tuple up to one common conjugation. The oriented triple data remove the ambiguity that interval traces alone could leave. The label and frame transformation can be written explicitly. At the complete classical point, let \(J_{m mat}=\left( egin{smallmatrix}0&1\1&0\end{smallmatrix}ight)\). Turnover has \[ (L_i^+)'=J_{m mat}(L_{m+1-i}^-)^{-1}J_{m mat}, \qquad (L_i^-)'=J_{m mat}(L_{m+1-i}^+)^{-1}J_{m mat}. 	ag{32} \] Put \(g=J_{m mat}B_m^-\), \(P=H_m\cdots H_1\). Multiplying the ordered prefixes in (32) gives \[ g^{-1}H'_{m+1-j}g =(H_m\cdots H_{j+1})H_j(H_m\cdots H_{j+1})^{-1}, \qquad P'=gPg^{-1}. 	ag{33} \] For example before cancellation the first expression is \(P P_{j-1}^{-1}H_jP_{j-1}P^{-1}\). Equation (33) is the inverse-half-twist Hurwitz tuple. It retains its explicit common conjugator, rather than declaring the turned ordered tuple unchanged. The corresponding half-twist presentation return identifies the underlying ordered character. On the actual \(F_\Sigma=0\) section the total matrix \(P\) is triangular and its selected first-axis eigenvalue is \(K_\Sigma=xK_{m r}\). At completeness \(x=-1\). Thus the last row of (31) changes this eigenvalue to its reciprocal. If \(K_\Sigma^2
e1\), the two total-product eigenlines are distinct; the row selects the opposite eigenline, after the explicit character identification (33). Turnover by itself transports the original eigenline with its old eigenvalue into the \(E_\Sigma=0\) polarization; the additional row in (31) is what distinguishes the other \(F_\Sigma=0\) choice. This conclusion is on the local augmented character quotient. The common frame, its residual moment constraint, the actual half-twist, and all relative source windows remain. No pointwise map of the original integration chains is inferred. In particular the relative-window defect specified in J is not set to zero. ## 7. Scope and complete proof directs The new result is the explicit finite quantum separator (14)--(15), the bounded quotient formula (18), and the homogeneous root rows (30c). Their local characteristic equations (31), when defined, have the ordered-character and reciprocal-flag interpretation above. The trace-chart proof works over local Artin rings. The uniform coherent-symbol calculation is only at \(M=1\); the finite part \(J_0\) retains its exact normal forcing. It does not prove that \(T\) or \(J\) has a nonzero Fourier-integral amplitude on that relation, that any geometric branch occurs in the original cycle, or that short-tangle and complementary-source contributions cannot cancel. Meridian and quantum normals retain their complete original endpoint rows and scalar lines. * M: notes/marked_braid_holonomy.md, SHA256 eff47c757d0e44bda0c396c094315b8e1fce11f1fc2d6445d636c6d2d3a46c4f. * Q: notes/regular_holonomy_braiding.md, SHA256 5be349365f59c89d4e20ce411a93baa850562056b62b13ad4d465b1b1607f9ef. * R: notes/research_actual_reduced_braid_source.md, SHA256 9a472ef27b08305a519ff1f24b6d2b909e63a0acbdc49b3a29e001c52a2f2243. * J: notes/research_opposite_polarization_source_kernel.md, SHA256 d52c6dd8e62f575a262fc7af460e258f7cb0e40b5a9c037ac46dd8d151002d44. title: A fixed interior cut for the original physical scalar
text:
# A fixed interior cut for the original physical scalar Private written proof, 18 November 2026. The original unmarked invariant can be evaluated at one interior cut occupation, instead of at the highest vector. The exact Ward current between the two probes has polynomial size in the level, including every fixed meridian derivative on a specified shrinking disk. In the existing classical cut chart, an interior occupation selects a noncentral complete meridian. This provides a possible regular presentation of the same scalar. It does not identify its stationary scheme or cycle with that of the highest-cut Borel source. ## 1. Exact finite cut identities Keep the original finite knot word, framing and pivotal partial trace. Let \(C_N(M)\) be its resulting endomorphism on the remaining head, in the factorial basis of [M]. Write \[ N\ge2,\quad Q=e^{2\pi i/N},\quad \mathcal E e_{r+1}=\epsilon_r(M)e_r,\quad \epsilon_r(M)=M Q^{-r-1}-M^{-1}, \quad 0\le r<N-1. 	ag{1} \] The final wrap arrow is zero. Total occupation conservation makes \(C_N\) diagonal. Actual quantum-group intertwining gives \([\mathcal E,C_N]=0\), with the original pivots included [W]. For generic \(M\), every \(\epsilon_r(M)
e0\). Thus \[ \epsilon_r(M) igl((C_N)_{r+1,r+1}-(C_N)_{rr} igr)=0 \] forces all diagonal entries to be equal. The entries are Laurent functions of the retained meridian; continuation gives the whole matrix identity at exceptional values as well. Consequently, with the unchanged original scalar normalization, \[ C_N(M)=F_N(M)I,\qquad \operatorname{Tr}(T_a C_N(M))=F_N(M),\quad T_a=e_ae_a^*,\quad 0\le a<N . 	ag{2} \] At \(M=1\) this is the original physical Kashaev scalar. No framing factor or additional circle normalization is inserted. For \(a>0\), define the actual finite current \[ B_{N,a}(M)=-\sum_{r=0}^{a-1} \epsilon_r(M)^{-1}E_{r+1,r}. 	ag{3} \] It is initially defined off its displayed poles. Direct matrix multiplication telescopes to \[ [\mathcal E,B_{N,a}]=T_a-T_0 . 	ag{4} \] The negative sign is fixed: the diagonal at zero is \(-1\), at \(a\) it is \(+1\), and all intermediate terms cancel. For an arbitrary marked cut endomorphism \(C_N^{m mark}\), ordinary cyclicity gives the exact identity \[ \operatorname{Tr}((T_a-T_0)C_N^{m mark}) =\operatorname{Tr} (B_{N,a}[C_N^{m mark},\mathcal E]). 	ag{5} \] For the unmarked knot the right side is zero. For inserted clocks or other coupons it remains the prescribed defect current. Equation (5) does not assert unchanged marked families. There is an exact coefficient presentation too. Define the literal cut grading \(D_N(z)e_a=z^ae_a\). Then \[ \operatorname{Tr}(D_N(z)C_N(M)) =F_N(M)\sum_{a=0}^{N-1}z^a,\qquad [z^a]\operatorname{Tr}(D_N(z)C_N)=F_N(M). 	ag{6} \] This finite polynomial identity puts no pivot on the open head. It does not replace \(D_N(z)\) by a single matrix entry \(z\). ## 2. A polynomial bound for the current and its meridian jets Declare the factorial basis orthonormal for this estimate. A matrix with one weighted subdiagonal has operator norm the largest weight. At \(M=1\), \[ |\epsilon_r(1)|= 2\left|\sin rac{\pi(r+1)}Night|\ge rac4N . 	ag{7} \] Here the minimum occurs at an end of \(1,\ldots,N-1\), and \(\sin x\ge2x/\pi\) on \([0,\pi/2]\). For \(|M-1|\le1/(4N)\), one has \(|M|\ge7/8\) and \[ |\epsilon_r(M)-\epsilon_r(1)| \le |M-1|+|M^{-1}-1| <3|M-1|\le rac{3}{4N}. 	ag{8} \] Thus all denominators in (3) are bounded below by \(3/N\) on that disk, independently of \(a\), and \[ \|B_{N,a}(M)\|\le N/3 . 	ag{9} \] On the smaller disk \(|M-1|\le1/(8N)\), the Cauchy formula therefore gives, for every fixed \(j\ge0\), \[ \|\partial_M^jB_{N,a}(M)\| \le C_j N^{j+1}. 	ag{10} \] The constants do not depend on \(a\) or \(N\). This bound includes the retained meridian normals; it is not merely a value at \(M=1\). The disk shrinks with the level, and no estimate on a fixed-radius meridian disk is claimed. The estimates concern the current, not a relative error in a scalar pairing. In particular they do not bound (5) relative to the possibly small value \(\operatorname{Tr}(T_0 C_N^{m mark})\). ## 3. One fixed bulk choice has a regular complete meridian Choose once and for all \(0<	heta<1\), and take \[ a_N=\lfloor	heta Nfloor 	ag{11} \] for sufficiently large \(N\). The midpoint choice \(	heta=1/2\) is available at both parities. The exact identities (2)--(6) apply for every such level. The discrete position is \(A_N=Q^{a_N}\). In the actual regular classical cut chart of [M,J], the position and framing coordinates satisfy \[ A_{m cut}= rac{M}{M+s},\qquad A_N\longrightarrow A_	heta=e^{2\pi i	heta}. 	ag{12} \] Thus the selected classical position is \(A_{m cut}=A_	heta\). This statement does not drop any finite Weyl shift from the matrices in Section 1. At the complete value \(M=1\), it selects \[ s_	heta=e^{-2\pi i	heta}-1
e0 . 	ag{13} \] On the existing \(p_{m cut}=1\) framing chart, its meridian is \[ \mu_{s_	heta} = egin{pmatrix}1+s_	heta&-s_	heta\ s_	heta&1-s_	heta\end{pmatrix}. 	ag{14} \] This is noncentral parabolic: its determinant is one, its trace is two, and \(\mu_{s_	heta}-I
e0\). For \(	heta=1/2\), \(s_	heta=-2\). The frame \[ F(r,s)= egin{pmatrix}r&1-r\s&-s\end{pmatrix},\qquad \mu_s=F^{-1} egin{pmatrix}1&1\0&1\end{pmatrix}F 	ag{15} \] has determinant \(-s\). With \(s\) near \(s_	heta\) and \(r\) in a fixed compact set, both this matrix and its inverse are bounded independently of the level. Thus the selected noncentral geometric framing itself need not escape merely because the complete eigenvalues coincide. This is an explicit change of the finite cut presentation, not a regularization of all matrices in the old highest-cut chart. It does not put every source configuration or the remaining centralizer coordinate \(r\) in a compact set. ## 4. What remains to justify in the new presentation Equations (2)--(11) justify using the fixed interior probe to compute the original unmarked invariant. Its cut occupation grows with \(N\). It is therefore a new semiclassical source presentation; it is not the fixed-occupation \(h\)-expansion of the old highest-cut germ. At a known geometric critical configuration, (12) fixes the coadjoint framing parameter \(s\), leaving the centralizer parameter \(r\). Fixing a cut occupation also removes a stationarity equation. The equivalence of the entire new critical scheme with the original geometric representation scheme has not followed from (2). The exact interior Ward recurrence is available, but turning it into that scheme or a relative-chain map requires its actual source analysis. Likewise (5) retains every marked defect. It cannot be used to carry a previously defined marked Borel period unchanged into the new presentation. A new phase, amplitude, endpoint analysis and normalization must be derived from its literal coefficient extraction. No geometric coefficient or volume limit is claimed. ## 5. W already proves arbitrary normalized diagonal Ward transgression; there is no novelty claim for (4)--(5). M supplies the literal finite module and scalar normalization, J the actual classical position/frame relation. The fixed bulk choice, bounds and geometric scope are explicit above. No mathematical program, numerical test or build was used. Frozen/public files are unchanged.

title: Actual fixed-width Gauss boundary kernels, their branches and vacuum layer
text:
# Actual fixed-width Gauss boundary kernels, their branches and vacuum layer Private written proof, 18 November 2026. The initialized first column of the universal Gauss operator admits an exact width recursion and an exact finite divided-difference lift. For every fixed number of tail heads these determine its vacuum normalization, its microscopic limit, and actual exponential branches on explicitly separated sectors. No spectral channel sum is introduced. The original vacuum forcing remains in the recursion. A fixed zero-free disk at the origin does not persist to three tail heads: the actual normalized column has zeros at distance \(O(N^{-1})\). Thus the wider initializer must retain its branches and their confluent derivatives. This is a boundary-kernel theorem, not a higher-dimensional Goursat theorem or a closed-source estimate. ## 1. Actual spaces and all-width first columns Use the fixed root and complete meridian: \[ c_0=2\pi i,\quad Q=e^{c_0/N},\quad q=e^{c_0/(2N)},\quad d=N-1,\quad x=-q^{-1},\quad f_a=(Q;Q)_a. \] Fix an integer number \(r\geq2\) of tail heads. The universal actual operator \(A_N^{(r)}=q_FE_\Sigma^d i_d\) and its place in the original opposite kernel are those of [G]. At completeness its ordered formula is \[ A_N^{(r)}=(-1)^dN\sum_{n=0}^d  rac{(-1)^nq^{n^2}}{f_n^2}F^nE^nK^{d-n}. 	ag{1} \] Here \(E,F,K\) are the actual ordered totals on these \(r\) heads. Work in integer degree \(0\leq T\leq d\), and initialize on \[ v_{m in}=|0,\ldots,0,Tangle,\qquad \sigma_N=(T+1)/N\in I\Subset(1/2,1). \] Put \[ C=Q^{-T-1},\quad K_{r,T}=x^rQ^{-T},\quad s=r-1,\quad p=r-2,\quad \alpha=x^s. 	ag{2} \] The letter \(C\) is the two-tail reference clock and is not the total Cartan \(K_{r,T}\) when \(r
e2\). For the first \(s\) heads, the literal divided vacuum descendants are \[ \mathbf v_a= rac{F_{[1,s]}^a}{f_a}|0,\ldots,0angle =\sum_{\substack{b_1+\cdots+b_s=a\b_i\geq0}} x^{-\sum_{i=1}^s(i-1)b_i}|b_1,\ldots,b_sangle. 	ag{3} \] We only use \(a\leq T<N\), so every factorial and head index is physical. To prove (3), order the \(Q\)-multinomial expansion of \(\sum_iK_1^{-1}\cdots K_{i-1}^{-1}F_i\) with the smaller-index factor to the left. Its rightmost factors act while their preceding heads still have occupation zero. The multinomial \(f_a/\prod f_{b_i}\) cancels the individual raising products and leaves exactly (3). The prefix vacuum is killed by its total \(E\) and has Cartan \(\alpha\). In particular \(E\) on \(v_{m in}\) lowers only the last head. Expanding the total \(F\) between this prefix and the last head, as in [B, (10)], but with the vacuum Cartan \(\alpha\), gives \[ A_N^{(r)}v_{m in} =(-1)^dNK_{r,T}^d\sum_{a=0}^T \alpha^a V_a^{(r)}\,\mathbf v_a\otimes|T-aangle, 	ag{4} \] where the complete finite scalar sum is \[ V_a^{(r)} =\sum_{n=a}^T Q^{n(n+r-1)} {T rack n}_Q{T-a rack n-a}_Q. 	ag{5} \] For verification of the phase, the intermediate coefficient of \(F^nE^n\) is \[ {n rack a}_Q\alpha^{-(n-a)}  rac{f_a f_{T-a}}{f_{T-n}}\, Q^{-nT+n(n-1)/2} rac{f_T}{f_{T-n}} \] in the \(\mathbf v_a\otimes|T-aangle\) basis. Multiplication by (1) leaves \(\alpha^a Q^{n(n-1)}(\alpha x)^{-2n} =\alpha^aQ^{n(n+r-1)}\), proving (4),(5). This is an actual physical column, not a scalar Casimir evaluation. Let \[ {\cal V}_r(ho)=\sum_{a=0}^T V_a^{(r)}ho^a,\qquad v_r={\cal V}_r(0). \] The original vacuum entry is exactly \[ a_{00}^{(r)} =(-1)^dNK_{r,T}^d v_r. 	ag{6} \] For \(r=2\), [B] proves \[ v_2=f_T^2/N,\qquad G_2(ho):={\cal V}_2(ho)/v_2 =e^{N\phi(ho;C)}A(ho;C)(1+O(N^{-1})) 	ag{7} \] on a fixed disk, with holomorphic relative error and derivatives. The phase and amplitude used below are exactly these marked functions, with \(D=ho\partial_ho\): \[  egin{split} CY^2-(1+C-ho)Y+1-Cho&=0,\qquad Y(0)=1,\ \phi(ho;C)&=\operatorname{Li}_2(ho)/c_0 +c_0^{-1}\int_0^ho\log Y(t)\,dt/t,\ A(ho;C)&=(1-ho)^{-1/2} \exp\left(\int_0^ho Z(t)\,dt/(tY(t))-	frac12\log Y(ho)ight),\ Z&=-[CY\,DY+ho Y-Cho]/[2CY-(1+C-ho)]. \end{split} 	ag{8} \] Thus \(\phi(0)=0\), \(A(0)=1\), \(\phi'(0)=a:=2/c_0\). Every estimate below is uniform for \(\sigma_N\in I\). No \(M\) or \(q\) derivative of these root formulas is taken. ## 2. Exact width recursion with its vacuum source For \(a<T\), the finite Gaussian identity \[ (1-Q^{n-a}){T-a rack n-a}_Q =(1-Q^{T-a}){T-a-1 rack n-a-1}_Q \] and (5) give, with \(V_{T+1}^{(r)}=0\), \[ V_a^{(r+1)} =Q^aV_a^{(r)}-Q^a(1-Q^{T-a})V_{a+1}^{(r)}. 	ag{9} \] The boundary case \(a=T\) follows directly from (5). Summing gives the exact polynomial equation \[  oxed{\quad ho{\cal V}_{r+1}(ho) =(ho-Q^{-1}){\cal V}_r(Qho) +Q^T{\cal V}_r(ho)+(Q^{-1}-Q^T)v_r. \quad} 	ag{10} \] The numerator on the right vanishes at zero, so its division by \(ho\) is literal polynomial division. The last term is the initialized vacuum source. It must remain, even though the two-tail seed has a zero-free exponential description. As a check with no limit, (9) and the exact coefficient [B, (9a)] give \[ v_3= rac{2(1-Q^{T+1})}{1-Q}\, rac{f_T^2}{N}. 	ag{11} \] It is nonzero in the present chamber, although it vanishes at \(T=d\). The general fixed-width vacuum normalization will follow from the same forced recursion, rather than from an assumed closed product. ## 3. Microscopic normalization, uniformly through the origin Set \[ b=C^{-1}-1,\qquad p=r-2,\qquad W_{r,N}(z)= rac{{\cal V}_r(z/N)}{v_2N^p}. \] Uniformly for \(z\) in any fixed compact complex disk, \[  oxed{\quad W_{r,N}(z) =b^p rac{e^{az}-\sum_{j=0}^{p-1}(az)^j/j!}{z^p} +O(N^{-1}). \quad} 	ag{12} \] For \(p=0\), the empty sum is zero and the quotient is \(e^{az}\). Every quotient at \(z=0\) is its holomorphic removable value. All fixed \(z\)-derivatives of the error have the same bound on smaller disks. Here is a proof that includes the repeated removals at zero. Equation (7), evaluated at \(z/N\), gives \(W_{2,N}=e^{az}+O(N^{-1})\) with fixed derivatives on every fixed disk. On inserting \(ho=z/N\) in (10), the exact recurrence is \[ zW_{r+1,N}(z) =(z/N-Q^{-1})W_{r,N}(Qz) +Q^TW_{r,N}(z)+(Q^{-1}-Q^T)W_{r,N}(0). 	ag{13} \] Since \(Q^T=Q^{-1}C^{-1}\), its limiting recurrence is \[ zW_{r+1}(z)=b[W_r(z)-W_r(0)]. 	ag{14} \] This gives exactly (12). To propagate the error, work on nested fixed complex disks, finitely many because \(r\) is fixed. The comparison functions use the exact \(C\) at each \(N\); no convergence of the discrete parameters \(\sigma_N\) is assumed. Cauchy bounds give \(W_{r,N}(Qz)-W_{r,N}(z)=O(N^{-1})\) uniformly on the next smaller disk. The difference between the numerators in (13),(14) is analytic, vanishes exactly at \(z=0\), and is \(O(N^{-1})\) on a larger disk. Its quotient by \(z\) is therefore \(O(N^{-1})\), including at zero, by the maximum principle or the Cauchy integral for the divided difference. This proves the induction and all the derivative assertions. No bound with an uncontrolled factor \(1/|z|\) is used. At zero, (12) gives the actual normalization \[  oxed{\quad  rac{v_r}{v_2} =N^p rac{(ab)^p}{p!}(1+O(N^{-1})). \quad} 	ag{15} \] The factor \(b\) is uniformly nonzero on \(I\). Thus \(v_r\), and consequently (6), are nonzero for all sufficiently large \(N\), uniformly in the stated chamber. In particular \[ a_{00}^{(r)} =(-1)^dK_{r,T}^d f_T^2 N^p rac{(ab)^p}{p!}(1+O(N^{-1})). 	ag{16} \] The exact finite factors \(K_{r,T}^d f_T^2\) have not been replaced by asymptotic scalars. Define \(G_r={\cal V}_r/v_r\) for these \(N\). The normalized microscopic limit is \[  oxed{\quad G_r(z/N)=g_p(z)+O(N^{-1}),\qquad g_p(z)=p!\sum_{n=0}^\infty rac{(az)^n}{(n+p)!}. \quad} 	ag{17} \] For three heads \(p=1\), \(g_1(z)=(e^{az}-1)/(az)\) has a simple zero at \(z=-2\pi^2\), and at its nonzero integer multiples. On a small circle about this simple zero, the uniform approximation (17) and Rouché's theorem give an actual zero of \(G_3(z/N)\) inside for all large \(N\). Taking smaller circles shows its location is \[ ho_N=-2\pi^2/N+o(N^{-1}). 	ag{18} \] Consequently no fixed disk at zero is zero-free for this actual three-tail initializer. This is a statement about the actual finite column, with the original vacuum source in (10). ## 4. Quantitative competing bound and a nonzero sector branch Shrink the seed disk in (7) once. On it put \[ Y_G=e^{c_0D\phi}= rac{Y}{1-ho},\qquad W(ho;C)= rac{C^{-1}-Y(ho;C)}{ho}. 	ag{19} \] Its numerator is \(b+O(ho)\), uniformly; hence it has no zeros on a sufficiently small punctured disk. It has a pole at zero. It is not a holomorphic unit on the full disk. First the following bound retains both the exponential and vacuum: \[ |G_r(ho)|\leq C_r  igl(1+e^{N\Re\phi(ho;C)} igr) 	ag{20} \] uniformly on a fixed smaller closed disk. For \(|ho|\geq1/N\), prove by induction that \[ |{\cal V}_r(ho)/v_2| \leq C_rN^p(1+e^{N\Re\phi(ho;C)}). \] The seed is (7). In (10), \(|ho|^{-1}\leq N\), (15) bounds the vacuum term, and \(e^{N(\Re\phi(Qho)-\Re\phi(ho))}\) is uniformly bounded by analyticity of the seed phase and \(|Q-1|=O(N^{-1})\). This proves the next-width bound, which becomes (20) after (15). For \(|ho|\leq1/N\), (17) supplies a uniform bound directly. This proves (20) on the whole disk, including the origin. The same argument on slightly larger disks and Cauchy circles of radius proportional to \(1/N\) gives the corresponding fixed derivative bounds with at most the expected powers of \(N\). Let \(\mathcal S\) be any compact set in this punctured disk, with \(\sigma\in I\), on which \(\Re\phi(ho;C)\geq\eta>0\). Then the actual scalar initializer has the stronger asymptotic \[  oxed{\quad G_r(ho)=N^{-p}e^{N\phi(ho;C)}  rac{p!\,A(ho;C)W(ho;C)^p}{(ab)^p} (1+O(N^{-1})). \quad} 	ag{21} \] Its displayed amplitude is nonzero on \(\mathcal S\). Such sets exist: \(\phi(ho)=2ho/c_0+O(ho^2)\), so a small upper-half-plane sector, restricted away from zero, has this property. To prove (21), first work without the normalization: \[ {\cal V}_r/v_2=e^{N\phi}A W^p(1+O(N^{-1})). \] It holds for \(r=2\). In (10), the seed phase shift is \({\cal V}_r(Qho)/{\cal V}_r(ho)=Y_G(1+O(N^{-1}))\) on slightly enlarged compact sets. The leading multiplier is \[  rac{(ho-1)Y_G+C^{-1}}{ho} = rac{C^{-1}-Y}{ho}=W. \] The retained vacuum has only polynomial size by (15), and is exponentially smaller than this branch since \(\Re\phi\geq\eta\). Its contribution and all fixed derivative errors are therefore controlled. Division by (15) proves (21). This proof applies to compact subsets of the sector; it does not claim uniformity as \(ho	o0\) or as the positive gap closes. ## 5. Entire multivariable boundary and all its branches Let \(h_a(z_1,\ldots,z_s)\) denote the complete homogeneous polynomial of degree \(a\). Evaluation of (3),(4) on the original monomial output row gives the exact source column \[  egin{split} v_{\mathbf w}A_N^{(r)}v_{m in} &=a_{00}^{(r)}w_r^T\,{\cal G}_r(z_1,\ldots,z_s),\ z_i&=x^{r-i}w_i/w_r,\qquad {\cal G}_r(\mathbf z)=\sum_{a=0}^T  rac{V_a^{(r)}}{v_r}h_a(\mathbf z). \end{split} 	ag{22} \] The input is the fixed physical column. If extracted from the original compact coherent input, its original binomial coefficient is kept outside (22). For distinct \(z_i\), the elementary partial fractions of \(\prod_i(1-z_it)^{-1}\) give \[  oxed{\quad {\cal G}_r(\mathbf z) =\sum_{i=1}^s  rac{z_i^p}{\prod_{j
e i}(z_i-z_j)}G_r(z_i). \quad} 	ag{23} \] Equation (22) is the definition at collisions; (23) continues there by confluent divided differences, not by discarding any summand. For example on the full diagonal it is \[ {\cal G}_r(z,\ldots,z)=  rac1{p!}\partial_z^p[z^pG_r(z)]. 	ag{24} \] Here is a genuine single-branch sector consequence, with all complements estimated. On a compact configuration set require the \(z_i\) to be distinct with a fixed separation, and select an index \(i_*\) such that \[ \Re\phi(z_{i_*})\geq\eta,\qquad \Re\phi(z_{i_*})\geq \max_{j
e i_*}\{0,\Re\phi(z_j)\}+\eta. 	ag{25} \] All coordinates stay in the small disk; the winning coordinate is automatically bounded away from zero. Its coefficient in (23) is nonzero and bounded away from zero on the compact set. Equations (20),(21) now give the actual estimate \[  egin{split} {\cal G}_r(\mathbf z) ={}&N^{-p}e^{N\phi(z_{i_*};C)}  rac{z_{i_*}^p}{\prod_{j
e i_*}(z_{i_*}-z_j)}  rac{p!\,A(z_{i_*};C)W(z_{i_*};C)^p}{(ab)^p}\ &\hspace{35mm}\cdot(1+O(N^{-1})). \end{split} 	ag{26} \] Every losing term, including a coordinate at zero, is bounded by (20); relative to the displayed term it is at most \(C N^p e^{-N\eta}\). Thus (26) is not a selection based solely on formal phases. It estimates the original finite boundary sum. The exact normalization and monomial in (22) remain outside it. At phase ties or collisions the sum (23), or its confluent version, must instead remain. There is a uniform microscopic formula making this explicit. On every fixed compact \(\mathbf z\)-set, \[ {\cal G}_r(z_1/N,\ldots,z_s/N) =p!a^{-p}\sum_{i=1}^s  rac{e^{az_i}}{\prod_{j
e i}(z_i-z_j)} +O(N^{-1}), 	ag{27} \] with the entire divided-difference continuation at collisions. Indeed insert (17) in (23); the polynomial of degree \(p-1\) subtracted from the exponential has zero divided difference. Uniformity through collisions follows from the fixed-order Cauchy integral for divided differences on a surrounding circle and (17). The same argument proves fixed derivatives. On the full diagonal the right side is \(e^{az}\). For \(r=3\) with the second coordinate zero it is exactly the profile in (17),(18). This retains both nonzero diagonal behavior and genuine nearby interference zeros. ## 6. Scope and complete directs This is an actual arbitrary-fixed-width initialization result: (4),(10),(22) preserve all physical coefficients and endpoint support; (15) pays the vacuum normalization; (20) controls every competing boundary term; (21),(26) give nonzero local branches where the stated quantitative gaps hold. The microscopic and confluent rows are retained when these hypotheses fail. No replacement positive packet is used. The universal operator also commutes with its consecutive partial Casimirs: each commutes with the total \(E,F,K\) by the ordered coproduct and centrality on its own interval, hence with (1). This note does not solve their multi-variable kernel equations. In particular it makes no higher-width full-kernel, meridian-normal, inverse-frame, geometric-chart, relative-cycle or volume assertion. All exterior factors in [G]'s original opposite kernel remain. title: Actual fixed-width Gauss coherent boundaries from the complete input sum
