title: A flat cap has no uniform local exponential angular mismatch bound
status: Exact flat-cap obstruction to a local exponential angular gap
text: # A flat cap has no uniform local exponential angular mismatch bound The flat-cap example is a local limitation on phase suppression. It is not a lower bound for the full source or a filling period. At the residual cap \(x=b=0\), \(\sigma=2\), the literal raw coefficient is \[ [c^{d-j}y^j]H_V=(-1)^j A_j,\qquad A_j=\csc^2\frac{\theta}{2}\prod_{r=1}^j \frac{\sin^2(r\theta)}{\sin^2((r+\tfrac12)\theta)}, \qquad \theta=\frac{\pi}{N},\quad d=N-1. \tag{1} \] This follows directly from the [full-interval source identity](research_original_one_sided_four_state_transfer.md). At \(x=b=0\), the only start is \(i=0\) and \[ K_{0,j}=y^j\prod_{r=1}^j4\sin^2(r\theta),\qquad \alpha_r=-4\sin^2((r+\tfrac12)\theta). \] The exact product \[ \prod_{r=0}^{d}4\sin^2((r+\tfrac12)\theta)=4 \] then gives (1), including the sign from the original unused factors and the common raw sign. No factor is removed. For \(0\le j\le M=\lfloor N/2\rfloor-1\), the sequence \(A_j\) is positive and decreasing, because \(\sin(j\theta)\le\sin((j+\tfrac12)\theta)\) on this range. Also \[ A_j\le A_0=\csc^2(\theta/2)\le N^2. \tag{2} \] The monotonicity of sine gives the telescoping lower bound \[ \prod_{r=1}^j\frac{\sin(r\theta)}{\sin((r+\tfrac12)\theta)} \ge\prod_{r=1}^j\frac{\sin(r\theta)}{\sin((r+1)\theta)} =\frac{\sin\theta}{\sin((j+1)\theta)}. \] Consequently, for \(N\ge3\), \[ A_j\ge\frac{4\cos^2(\theta/2)}{\sin^2((j+1)\theta)} \ge4\cos^2(\theta/2)\ge3. \tag{3} \] Fix \(0<a<b<1/2\) and choose integer endpoints \(L_N\sim aN\), \(U_N\sim bN\) with \(U_N-L_N\) even. They lie in the original LEFT range for all sufficiently large \(N\). At the ordinary positive radius and common phase \(c=y=1\), the sharp stop-window polynomial and its actual absolute envelope are \[ W_N=\sum_{j=L_N}^{U_N}(-1)^j A_j,\qquad E_N=\sum_{j=L_N}^{U_N}A_j. \] Pairing consecutive terms of the decreasing sequence and keeping the last term gives \[ |W_N|\ge A_{U_N}\ge3,\qquad E_N\le N^3,\qquad \frac{|W_N|}{E_N}\ge\frac3{N^3}. \tag{4} \] The actual cap character is aligned only when the \(c\) and \(y\) phases differ by \(\pi\). At the phases used in (4), they are equal, so their distance to that supported alignment is \(\pi/2\), measured by the smallest maximum circular distance after optimizing the common phase. Nevertheless no fixed constants \(C,\kappa>0\) can satisfy \(\lvert W_N\rvert\le C e^{-\kappa N}E_N\) on all these levels. The retained alternating terms leave endpoint currents of at least polynomial size; there is no strict local stop-action gap at the cap. Therefore the regular-window angular theorem cannot be extended to a flat cap merely by assigning it the same opposite-sign incidence labels. An odd MAIN cycle involving such a cap does not by itself supply the product-envelope exponential loss used by the regular cycle-packing argument. This does not exclude cancellation after original shared coefficient extraction, a combined analytic block estimate with other ports, or a different source-preserving treatment of the cap boundaries. It makes no assertion that \(W_N\) occurs uncoupled in the full invariant. The proof is exact for every \(N\ge3\) and window lying in the stated range. It uses no asymptotic coefficient formula or numerical experiment. The [stationary MAIN-cycle theorem](research_stationary_noncross_main_cycle_obstruction.md) uses the cap character while keeping this limitation explicit.

title: An exact positive moment form for the original flat-cap coefficients
text: # An exact positive moment form for the original flat-cap coefficients 31 October 2026. analytical research lemma. Root derived the proof; two independent readers checked it in full. This constructs a positive inner product from the original cap weights. It does not prove that the adjacent CROSS polynomial is a contraction for that form, or establish the open original-demand convolution bound. ## 1. The actual finite weights Fix an integer N>=3, d=N-1 and theta=pi/N. The raw protected cap coefficient is (-1)^j U_j, where U_j=csc^2(theta/2) product_(r=1)^j sin^2(r theta)/sin^2((r+1/2)theta), 0<=j<=d. Write m_j=U_j/U_0. The statement is that there is a positive random variable X_N such that E X_N^j=m_j, 0<=j<=d. (1) Its support is not confined to [0,1]. In particular no Hausdorff-moment or pointwise contraction conclusion follows from (1). ## 2. Exact Euler product and beta factors Euler's sine product gives, with positive factors for this whole range, m_j=[Gamma(j+1)Gamma(3/2)/Gamma(j+3/2)]^2 product_(k>=1) B_(kN)(j)^2, (2) where B_a(s)= Gamma(a)Gamma(a-s-1/2) /[Gamma(a-1/2)Gamma(a-s)] * Gamma(a+s+1)Gamma(a+3/2) /[Gamma(a+1)Gamma(a+s+3/2)]. (3) Indeed each k contributes, before squaring, product_(r=1)^j [(kN-r)/(kN-r-1/2)] [(kN+r)/(kN+r+1/2)], which is exactly (3). The remaining product r/(r+1/2) is the prefactor in (2). This derives the shifts and constants from the literal cap, not from a free choice of moment functional. Let T_1,T_2 be independent Beta(1,1/2) variables. For each k>=1 and i=1,2 let independently A_(k,i) ~ Beta(kN-1/2,1/2), B_(k,i) ~ Beta(kN+1,1/2), Z_(k,i)=B_(k,i)/A_(k,i). All variables mentioned are mutually independent. The elementary beta integral gives E T_i^s=Gamma(s+1)Gamma(3/2)/Gamma(s+3/2), E Z_(k,i)^s=B_(kN)(s), (4) for -1<s<N-1/2; these restrictions are sufficient simultaneously for the factors here. In particular all moments in (1) are finite. Define finite positive products X_(N,K)=T_1 T_2 product_(k=1)^K Z_(k,1)Z_(k,2). Equations (2)--(4) give the desired moments in the limit, once convergence and uniform integrability are checked. ## 3. Convergence with no formal infinite-product inference For fixed s in a compact subinterval of (-1,N-1/2), the gamma ratio expansion in (3) gives log B_a(s)=O_s(a^-2), a->infinity. (5) The a^-1 terms of the inverse-beta and beta factors are respectively s/(2a) and -s/(2a), and cancel. The expansion and its first two s derivatives are uniform on a small neighborhood of zero. Consequently E log Z_(k,i)=O((kN)^-2), Var(log Z_(k,i))=O((kN)^-2). (6) Also log T_i belongs to L2 by its beta density at zero and one. The means are absolutely summable. Independence makes the centered partial sums Cauchy in L2, since their tail variance is the sum of the tail variances. Thus log X_(N,K) converges in L2 to a finite real random variable Y_N. Set X_N=exp(Y_N)>0. The products converge in probability. Fix an integer 1<=j<=d. Choose epsilon>0 with j+epsilon<N-1/2. The beta moments at that exponent exist; (5) shows sup_K E X_(N,K)^(j+epsilon)<infinity. (7) Hence X_(N,K)^j are uniformly integrable. Convergence in probability and uniform integrability give convergence of their expectations to E X_N^j. Equations (2)--(4) identify the limit as m_j. The zero moment is one. This proves (1) with every original weight retained. Removing any one factor leaves the same convergent log series, measurable in the other independent variables. Thus the separated factor remains independent of the positive limiting remainder. The measure is non-atomic and has unbounded support. For non-atomicity, separate the independent T_1 factor, which has a continuous positive density on (0,1). For unbounded support, separate the independent 1/A_(1,1) factor, which is unbounded, from the remaining positive random product. The remainder is bounded below by some positive number on an event of positive probability. Independence then gives arbitrarily large X_N with positive probability. ## 4. Exact finite-dimensional Cauchy inequality For m with 2m<=d, put on polynomials of degree at most m <p,q>_N=U_0 E[p(X_N) conjugate(q(X_N))]. Its matrix in the monomial basis is EXACTLY (U_(i+j))_(0<=i,j<=m). It is positive definite: a nonzero polynomial has finitely many roots, while X_N is non-atomic. Thus |<p,q>_N|^2 <= <p,p>_N <q,q>_N. (8) At the even levels N=2m0 of the original cap/CROSS problem, its cutoff M=m0-1 satisfies 2M=d-1. The entire original cutoff polynomial space therefore carries this positive Gram form. The alternating cap character is retained by evaluating p at -X_N, rather than deleting (-1)^j. To express the precise missing step, use the coefficients C_(j,h) and range J_n of the original-demand convolution. Define the literal projected polynomial F_(N,n)(t)=sum_(j in J_n) C_(j,n-j) t^j. Then its actual signed coefficient is exactly (-1)^d U_0 E F_(N,n)(-X_N). (9) For n>M the cutoff in J_n remains in F; (9) is not a full-sum replacement or an orthogonality claim. Formula (8) supplies a genuine positive inner product, but no bound here compares its quadratic norm of F_(N,n)(-t) with the endpoint convolution involving V_j. That comparison is the remaining issue. In particular unbounded support prevents replacing the expectation by a maximum on [0,1]. No numerical asymptotic test is needed for (1)--(9). They neither transport projected sectors through the full Casimir source nor prove the original invariant's volume conjecture. ## 5. The moment threshold and the original even-level cutoff The convergence argument also gives E X_N^s<infinity for EVERY real 0<=s<N-1/2: choose a slightly larger moment exponent still inside that interval and apply the same uniform-integrability argument. Conversely, separate the independent factor A_(1,1)^(-1) from the limiting product. The beta density gives E A_(1,1)^(-s)=infinity whenever s>=N-1/2. The remaining factor is strictly positive and independent. Tonelli's theorem therefore gives the sharp statement E X_N^s<infinity iff 0<=s<N-1/2. (10) Here the equivalence is restricted to nonnegative s. No assertion about negative moments is needed. A nonzero polynomial p of degree r satisfies |p(t)|^2>=c t^(2r) for all sufficiently large positive t, while the lower degree terms bound its squared modulus above by C(1+t^(2r)). Consequently its squared norm is finite exactly when 2r<N-1/2. At even N=2m0 this is r<=m0-1=M, precisely the original RIGHT cutoff. Thus that entire polynomial space has finite positive norm, while every polynomial of the next or a higher degree has infinite norm. At odd levels the maximal degree is floor((N-1)/2); its identification with an original one-sided sector is NOT asserted, since the odd central row belongs to CROSS. There is also an exact finite functional relation. Define L_N(p)=U_0 E p(X_N), and let D=t partial_t act diagonally on monomials. Sines of D mean the corresponding finite diagonal operators. The literal ratio U_(j+1)/U_j gives L_N( t sin^2(theta(D+3/2))p - sin^2(theta(D+1))p )=0, deg p<=d-1. (11) Indeed (11) on t^j is exactly sin^2((j+3/2)theta)U_(j+1)-sin^2((j+1)theta)U_j=0. The degree restriction is essential. At j=d the formal numerator sin^2(N theta) vanishes, but the other term would require the divergent Nth moment. Equation (11) is not an identity on all degree-d polynomials and does not authorize deleting that terminal contribution. It supplies no self-adjointness or contraction claim for the adjacent continuant. ## 6. A finite algebraic evaluation at even levels The beta product proves positivity, but the required finite functional also has an exact algebraic realization. Keep N=2m0 and M=m0-1, so d=2M+1. In this section L_N includes the original factor U_0. Gram--Schmidt on 1,t,...,t^M gives monic orthogonal polynomials p_r and positive squared norms h_r=L_N(p_r^2), 0<=r<=M. All these coefficients are real algebraic: the moments U_j are products of squared sines at rational multiples of pi, hence belong to a real cyclotomic field, and Gram--Schmidt uses only field operations. Define the (M+1)-by-(M+1) symmetric tridiagonal matrix J_cap by (J_cap)_(r,r)=L_N(t p_r^2)/h_r, 0<=r<=M, (J_cap)_(r-1,r)=(J_cap)_(r,r-1)=sqrt(h_r/h_(r-1)), 1<=r<=M. Every displayed moment is finite: the largest degree is 2M+1=d. For any vector v, let P_v=sum_r v_r p_r/sqrt(h_r). Orthogonality implies that multiplication by t has exactly the displayed entries, since t p_r has degree r+1. Thus v^* J_cap v=L_N(t |P_v(t)|^2)>0 for v!=0. The matrix is positive definite; its off-diagonal entries are positive. Its eigenvalues lambda_1,...,lambda_(M+1) are therefore positive and simple, and every eigenvector has nonzero first coordinate (use the tridiagonal recurrence starting at that coordinate). Define w_a=U_0 |(unit eigenvector at lambda_a)_0|^2>0. The characteristic polynomial p_(M+1) is still orthogonal to every polynomial of degree at most M. To check this without asserting its squared norm, define it by the last tridiagonal recurrence: the t p_M term pairs to zero against p_s for s<=M-2 by symmetry, and the chosen last two recurrence coefficients cancel its pairings with p_(M-1) and p_M. Only moments through 2M+1 occur. Its square need not be integrable, and in fact is not. For any polynomial f of degree at most 2M+1, divide it by p_(M+1): f=p_(M+1) q+r, deg q<=M, deg r<=M. The first term has zero L_N value and vanishes at every eigenvalue. The spectral measure above reproduces L_N on degree<=M: by the tridiagonal recurrence, p_j(J_cap)e_0 is a multiple of e_j for j<=M, so both functionals vanish on p_j for 1<=j<=M and give U_0 on p_0. It follows that L_N(f)=sum_(a=1)^(M+1) w_a f(lambda_a), deg f<=d. (12) All nodes and weights are real algebraic in a finite algebraic extension of the moment field. In particular the original cap convolution (9) is an exact finite algebraic evaluation with positive weights. Its original cutoff remains in F_(N,n). Formula (12) does not extend to degree d+1: the original moment there diverges, while the finite quadrature would assign it a finite number. This constructs the cap's own positive Jacobi matrix. It does not identify it with the different Jacobi matrix obtained by normalizing the adjacent continuant. No norm comparison between those two metrics, or volume bound for the original source, follows from (12). ## Inputs The weights are those of the [exact protected cap](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_trace_one_mark_and_cap_turn_interface.md). The polynomial in (9) is precisely the [original-demand cap/CROSS convolution](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_two_port_main_cap_original_demand_convolution.md). No triangle factor, unused spectral product or projected endpoint is changed by defining this inner product. The positive moment metric retains the stated degree cutoff. The endpoint norm comparison remains unproved, and the next square moment diverges.

title: Positive boundary transport gives the cube rate on an anchored grid
text: # Positive boundary transport gives the cube rate on an anchored grid 22 November 2026. Research note. Earlier final notes and public manuscripts remain unchanged. The original four-coherent scalar has a noncancelling geometric asymptotic on a continuous family of half-grid boundary paths. An exact three-input source initializes a positive recurrence. Its growth exponent equals the action of the actual ideal cube. This is a source estimate, with its original closing and phase, rather than an estimate for a norm or for a formal critical value. The result requires the displayed anchor and stops a fixed distance before the boundary fold. Generic grid offsets and pair-wall starts are not included. ## 1. Source, geometric domain and theorem Use the full algebra of the [four-boundary source theorem](research_four_coherent_boundary_polynomial_source.md). Put \[ N\ge2,\quad d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\quad \kappa=e^{\pi i d^2/(2N)},\quad U_a=\sum_{\ell=0}^d a^\ell f_\ell , \tag{1} \] where the centered basis is orthonormal in the positive Newton coefficient norm. All repeated-root Hermite coordinates, original products, turns and Frobenius closings remain present. Define \[ \Phi_N(y,z;s,t)=\phi(U_yU_zU_sU_t). \tag{2} \] Write \(S=b+c\). Our parameter domain is \[ \begin{gathered} b,c>0,\qquad S<1,\qquad 1-S<R<1-\max(b,c),\\ 0<h<R/2 . \end{gathered} \tag{3} \] For fixed \(b,c,R\), put \[ \begin{gathered} y=-e^{-2\pi ib},\quad z=-e^{-2\pi ic},\quad r=e^{-2\pi iR},\\ h_j=(j+\tfrac12)/N,\quad k_j=R-h_j,\quad s_j=-q^{-1}Q^{-j},\quad t_j=-qrQ^j . \end{gathered} \tag{4} \] Thus \(s_j=-e^{-2\pi ih_j}\), \(t_j=-e^{-2\pi ik_j}\), and \(s_jt_j=r\). The entries \(j=-1,0\) will initialize transport. Let \(L(x)=\int_0^x\log|2\sin\pi v|\,dv\), with its odd, one-periodic extension. On its strict multiplication domain set \[ m(x,y,u)=L(x+y)+L(u)-L(x)-L(y) -L(u-x)-L(u-y)-L(x+y-u). \tag{5} \] For \(k=R-h\), define \[ \begin{split} I_h&=\bigl(\max(b,c,1-R),\ \min(S,1-h,1-k)\bigr),\\ \mathcal F(b,c,R,h)&= \max_{u\in I_h}\{m(b,c,u)+m(h,k,1-u)\}. \end{split} \tag{6} \] Every quadruple in (3) has all six pair sums below one and total \(S+R>1\). The [positive cube theorem](../papers/strict-conway-geometry/README.md) therefore gives a unique strict interior maximizer and an actual convex ideal cube of volume \(\pi\mathcal F\). Its usual second action \(m(u,h,1-k)\) equals \(m(h,k,1-u)\) by \(L(1-x)=-L(x)\). **Theorem.** For every compact \(\mathcal K\) in (3), there are constants \(C_{\mathcal K},N_{\mathcal K}\) such that, whenever \(N\ge N_{\mathcal K}\), \(j\ge0\), and \((b,c,R,h_j)\in\mathcal K\), \[ \boxed{\quad \Phi_N(y,z;s_j,t_j)= e^{-\pi i d(S+R)}\,P_{N,j},\qquad P_{N,j}>0,\qquad |\log P_{N,j}-N\mathcal F(b,c,R,h_j)| \le C_{\mathcal K}\log N . \quad} \tag{7} \] The assertion includes both parities and composite levels. The original normalized closing of the two turned products is \(\Phi_N/N^2\), since all four coherent inputs have norm \(\sqrt N\). It has the same exponential rate. In particular, on convergent shape sequences in this compact domain, \(\pi N^{-1}\log|\Phi_N/N^2|\) tends to the volume of this cube. No knot-volume conclusion is asserted. ## 2. The exact carrier and the two source initial values The common phase in (7) is an exact source property, not a choice of a positive replacement. Here is a verification from the full coefficients in the four-boundary theorem. For a unit pair of angles \(v,w\), write \(U_{-e^{-2\pi iv}}U_{-e^{-2\pi iw}}=\sum_\ell B_\ell e_\ell\). At generic parameters its consecutive ratio is real: \[ \frac{B_{\ell+1}}{B_\ell} =-\frac{\sin\pi x\,\sin\pi(x-v-w)} {\sin\pi(x-v+\tfrac1{2N})\, \sin\pi(x-w+\tfrac1{2N})},\qquad x=(\ell+1)/N . \tag{8} \] Its first coefficient divided by \[ \theta_N(v+w)= -\kappa^2 e^{-\pi i[d(v+w)+1/N]} \tag{9} \] is real, as follows by writing its finite geometric products as sines and cosines. Thus every \(B_\ell/\theta_N(v+w)\) is real. Continuity extends this assertion across exact source zeros. The original four-input contraction is \(\sum_\ell B_\ell(y,z)B_{d-\ell}(s,t)\). Since \(\kappa^4=Q\), the product of its two carriers is exactly \[ \omega_N=e^{-\pi i d(S+R)} . \tag{10} \] Consequently \(H_j=\omega_N^{-1}\Phi_N(y,z;s_j,t_j)\) is real, including at the two anchor entries. The exact unit and socle readouts give \[ \begin{split} \Phi_N(y,z;s_0,t_0) &=\kappa\sqrt N\,\mathcal C_N(y,z,t_0),\\ \Phi_N(y,z;s_{-1},t_{-1}) &=\frac{\kappa^2}{N}F_N(y)F_N(z)F_N(t_{-1}),\qquad F_N(a)=\sum_{\ell=0}^d(-qa)^\ell . \end{split} \tag{11} \] Here \(t_0\) has angle \(R_N=R-1/(2N)\), whereas \(t_{-1}\) has angle \(R+1/(2N)\). The triple \(b,c,R_N\) ranges in a compact strict prism family. The [initialized three-input theorem](research_single_leg_radial_turn_source.md) therefore applies with all radii equal to one. For completeness, its calibrated phase fixes the sign of the initial value. Let \(A_N=S+R_N\), and denote its action and amplitude by \(\Psi_3,B_3\), with the canonical branches of that theorem. The elementary unit-circle dilogarithm formulas give \[ \begin{split} \Re\Psi_3&=\pi(1-A_N),\qquad \arg B_3=-3\pi/4+\pi A_N,\\ -\Im\Psi_3&=M(b,c,R_N),\qquad M(b,c,R)=m(b,c,1-R)>0 . \end{split} \tag{12} \] Indeed \(\Im\operatorname{Li}_2(e^{-2\pi ix})/(2\pi)=L(x)\). For the real part, apply \(\Re\operatorname{Li}_2(e^{2\pi ix}) =\pi^2(x^2-x+1/6)\) on \(0\le x\le1\), reducing the total angle by one. The amplitude phase is the sum of its three canonical logarithm phases, not a newly chosen square root. The identity \(L(1-x)=-L(x)\) gives the last equality in (12). Including both \(\kappa\)'s, the complete initial phase is \[ \kappa^2e^{\,i\pi/4-\pi i/(2N)} e^{\,i(-3\pi/4+\pi A_N)}e^{\,iN\pi(1-A_N)} =\omega_N . \tag{13} \] The initialized relative error is \(O_{\mathcal K}(N^{-1})\). Its nonzero amplitude is uniformly bounded above and below. Because \(H_0\) is exactly real, (11)--(13) imply, uniformly, \[ H_0>0,\qquad \log H_0=N M(b,c,R)+O_{\mathcal K}(\log N),\qquad |H_{-1}|\le C_{\mathcal K}/N . \tag{14} \] The last bound follows from the geometric sums in (11): their denominators stay away from zero on this compact angle family. Also \(M\) has a positive compact minimum. Hence \(\Delta_0:=H_0-H_{-1}>0\) and \(\Delta_0/H_0=1+O_{\mathcal K}(e^{-c_{\mathcal K}N})\). ## 3. Positive transfer before the fold The exact source equation, with \(\sigma(s,t)=(Qs,Q^{-1}t)\), is \[ B(\sigma\Phi_N-\Phi_N)+D(\sigma^{-1}\Phi_N-\Phi_N) =\lambda_N\Phi_N,\qquad \lambda_N=(Q-1)(1-Qyz), \tag{15} \] \[ B=\frac{(t+q)^2(1-Qys)(1-Qzs)}{(t-s)(t-Qs)},\qquad D=\frac{(s+q)^2(1-Qyt)(1-Qzt)}{(Qt-s)(t-s)}. \tag{16} \] On (4), \(\sigma\) replaces \(j\) by \(j-1\). Set \(g_N=-4e^{\pi i(2/N-S)}\), \(\mathsf b_j=B_j/g_N\), \(\mathsf d_j=D_j/g_N\), and \(\Lambda_N=\lambda_N/g_N\). With \(\delta_j=k_j-h_j\), direct sine conversion gives \[ \begin{split} \mathsf b_j&= \frac{\sin^2\pi(k_j+\tfrac1{2N})\, \sin\pi(b+h_j-\tfrac1N)\sin\pi(c+h_j-\tfrac1N)} {\sin\pi\delta_j\,\sin\pi(\delta_j+\tfrac1N)},\\ \mathsf d_j&= \frac{\sin^2\pi(h_j+\tfrac1{2N})\, \sin\pi(b+k_j-\tfrac1N)\sin\pi(c+k_j-\tfrac1N)} {\sin\pi\delta_j\,\sin\pi(\delta_j-\tfrac1N)},\\ \Lambda_N&=\sin(\pi/N)\sin\pi(S-\tfrac1N). \end{split} \tag{17} \] All are positive along the transport path, for large \(N\). The fixed fold margin supplies \(\mathsf b_j\ge c_{\mathcal K}>0\) and \(\Lambda_N/\mathsf b_j\le C_{\mathcal K}/N\). No uniform lower bound on \(\mathsf d_0\), which is of order \(N^{-2}\), is asserted. Put \(\rho_j=\mathsf b_j/\mathsf d_j\). To control it uniformly even near the initial layer, define \[ f_N(v)= \frac{\sin^2\pi v} {\sin\pi(b-\tfrac3{2N}+v)\sin\pi(c-\tfrac3{2N}+v)}. \tag{18} \] Then exactly \[ \rho_j= \frac{f_N(k_j+\tfrac1{2N})}{f_N(h_j+\tfrac1{2N})} \frac{\sin\pi(R-\tfrac{2(j+1)}N)} {\sin\pi(R-\tfrac{2j}N)} . \tag{19} \] On the relevant interval, the cotangent is decreasing, so \((\log f_N)'\ge c_{\mathcal K}>0\). Explicitly it is the sum of the two positive differences \(\pi[\cot\pi v-\cot\pi(b-\tfrac3{2N}+v)]\) and its \(c\)-analogue. All their arguments lie in \((0,1)\). The identity \(\cot x-\cot(x+a)=\sin a/[\sin x\sin(x+a)]\) gives the stated uniform positive lower bound even as \(v\) tends to zero. The two arguments of \(f_N\) in (19) have a fixed positive separation. The last factor is \(1+O_{\mathcal K}(N^{-1})\). Consequently, throughout transport to a target in \(\mathcal K\), \[ \rho_j\ge1+c_{\mathcal K}. \tag{20} \] For \(\Delta_j=H_j-H_{j-1}\), (15) now gives \[ \Delta_{j+1}=\rho_j\Delta_j+ \frac{\Lambda_N}{\mathsf d_j}H_j . \tag{21} \] Starting from (14), all \(H_j,\Delta_j\) are positive. Moreover \(\Delta_{j+1}\ge(1+c_{\mathcal K})\Delta_j\); geometric summation of \(H_j=H_0+\sum_{m=1}^j\Delta_m\) gives \[ c_{\mathcal K}\le H_j/\Delta_j \le C_{\mathcal K}. \tag{22} \] Thus (21) has the sharper form \[ \Delta_{j+1}=\rho_j\Delta_j \left[1+ \frac{\Lambda_N}{\mathsf b_j}\frac{H_j}{\Delta_j}\right] =\rho_j\Delta_j[1+O_{\mathcal K}(N^{-1})]. \tag{23} \] There are \(O_{\mathcal K}(N)\) steps. Taking logarithms and using (14), (22) proves \[ \log H_j=\log H_0+\sum_{m=0}^{j-1}\log\rho_m +O_{\mathcal K}(1). \tag{24} \] In particular the small coupling in (21) has not changed the leading exponent. ## 4. The rate integral and the actual cube action Define the classical ratio \[ \rho_0(h)= \frac{\sin^2\pi(R-h)\sin\pi(b+h)\sin\pi(c+h)} {\sin^2\pi h\sin\pi(b+R-h)\sin\pi(c+R-h)}. \tag{25} \] In the product of (19), its last factors telescope to \(\sin\pi(R-2j/N)/\sin\pi R\), bounded above and below. All remaining factors are smooth log-sine Riemann sums except the explicit denominator \(\sin(\pi(m+1)/N)\) at zero. On this interval, \(\log\sin\pi v=\log v+\) a smooth function. Integral comparison for \(\log(j!)\) bounds its Riemann error by \(O(\log N)\). The bounded shifts of the other arguments cost \(O_{\mathcal K}(1)\). Moving the upper integration limit from \(j/N\) to \(h_j\) costs at most \(O(\log N)\) after multiplication by \(N\). Hence \[ \sum_{m=0}^{j-1}\log\rho_m =N\int_0^{h_j}\log\rho_0(v)\,dv +O_{\mathcal K}(\log N). \tag{26} \] We next identify this primitive with the cube, rather than only with a formal boundary characteristic. Let \(u\) be the unique critical point in (6), and set \(k=R-h\). Its equation is \[ \sin\pi(S-u)\sin\pi(u+h)\sin\pi(u+k) +\sin\pi(u+R)\sin\pi(u-b)\sin\pi(u-c)=0 . \tag{27} \] Put \[ X=\cot\pi u,\quad B_0=\cot\pi b,\quad C_0=\cot\pi c,\quad H=\cot\pi h,\quad K=\cot\pi k . \tag{28} \] After division by the positive sine factors, (27) becomes \[ \begin{split} &[(B_0+C_0)X-B_0C_0+1](X+H)(X+K)\\ &\hspace{5mm} +[(H+K)X+HK-1](X-B_0)(X-C_0)\\ &\hspace{5mm} =(X^2+1)[(B_0+C_0+H+K)X+HK-B_0C_0]=0. \end{split} \tag{29} \] Here \(B_0+C_0>0\) and \(H+K>0\), since \(S,R<1\). It follows that \[ \frac{X+H}{X+K} =\frac{(B_0+H)(C_0+H)}{(B_0+K)(C_0+K)},\qquad \frac{\sin\pi(u+h)}{\sin\pi(u+k)} =\frac{\sin\pi k}{\sin\pi h} \frac{\sin\pi(b+h)\sin\pi(c+h)} {\sin\pi(b+k)\sin\pi(c+k)}. \tag{30} \] No denominator vanishes in the displayed strict domain. The envelope derivative of (6), at fixed \(b,c,R\), is \[ \partial_h\mathcal F =\log\left[ \frac{\sin\pi k}{\sin\pi h} \frac{\sin\pi(u+h)}{\sin\pi(u+k)}\right] =\log\rho_0(h). \tag{31} \] Smoothness follows either from the strict stationary maximum or the explicit critical cotangent in (29). As \(h\downarrow0\), the interval \(I_h\) shrinks to \(u=1-R\), by (3). The second action tends to \(m(0,R,R)=0\); continuity of \(L\) therefore gives \[ \mathcal F(b,c,R,0)=m(b,c,1-R)=M(b,c,R),\qquad \mathcal F=M+\int_0^h\log\rho_0(v)\,dv . \tag{32} \] Thus (14), (24), (26), and (32) prove (7). ## 5. Scope and complete proof sources Only \(s_j\), not a generic boundary parameter, lies on the anchored half-grid. Fixed \(st\) shifts preserve a fractional grid offset. This proof does not control arbitrary offsets, a boundary layer connecting them to the anchor, or pair-wall initializations when \(R\ge1-\max(b,c)\). It does not cross the fold \(h=R/2\) or estimate its pole-cancelled normal readout. Symmetry does not automatically cover \(h>R/2\): the smaller parameter need not lie on this anchored grid after the swap. The theorem proves a nonzero original source coefficient and its geometric rate on the stated universal cell family. It does not assert a full output approximation, arbitrary Conway composition, or a finite-exception knot-volume theorem. All coefficients and carriers come from the original full-Hermite scalar. The following three complete proof directs were read at their matching pins: | Source | SHA-256 | |---|---| | Four-boundary source, 409 lines | 93241074830ff4b844ba5baafd06a15bf08ec6bddc3a1498727f110ebe297d84 | | Single-leg initialized source, 326 lines | c624e0edbaadb57279c00420d3f552e93c67cb84972926aad27ff51c2c973e7e | | Actual prism and cube geometry, 377 lines | c29321805df39a49854665df1255db1ec7180397a5dd689f19289d61335871c9 | Only written mathematics and text operations were used. This research proof is author-final.

title: A polynomial boundary equation for the original four-coherent source

# A polynomial boundary equation for the original four-coherent source 22 November 2026. Written research proof. Earlier final notes and public manuscripts remain unchanged. The original pairing of two coherent products has an exact finite boundary equation. On a fixed product of two boundary parameters it is a polynomial eigenfunction with a known extreme coefficient. Away from specified color resonances, these data determine that polynomial uniquely. At the resonances the actual polynomial family, rather than a normalization by a vanished coefficient, retains the source. This concerns the full Frobenius contraction. It is not a positive orthogonality assertion, a scalar lower estimate, or a volume theorem. ## 1. The original scalar and its finite sum Fix \(N\ge2\), and put \[ d=N-1,\qquad q=e^{\pi i/N},\qquad Q=q^2,\qquad \eta=(-1)^d,\qquad \kappa=e^{\pi i d^2/(2N)}. 	ag{1} \] Use the full original algebra and the centered basis \(f_0,\ldots,f_d\) of [C]. In particular, in its Newton basis, \[ \phi(e_i e_j)=\delta_{i+j,d},\qquad Je_i=e_{d-i},\qquad R^+=\sqrt N f_0,\quad R^-=\sqrt N f_d,\quad R^+R^-=1. 	ag{2} \] All first derivatives at repeated Casimir roots are included in this algebra and in \(\phi\). No distinct-root replacement is made. Define unnormalized coherent polynomials and their actual scalar by \[ U_a=\sum_{j=0}^d a^j f_j,\qquad \Phi_N(y,z;s,t)=\phi(U_yU_zU_sU_t). 	ag{3} \] It is a polynomial of degree at most \(d\) in each of its four parameters. Write \[  egin{split} D_N(a)&=1-\eta a^N,\qquad F_N(a)=\sum_{j=0}^d(-qa)^j= rac{D_N(a)}{1+qa},\ G_N(r)&=\sum_{j=0}^d r^j,\qquad b=yz,\quad r=st. \end{split} 	ag{4} \] The quotients in (4) denote the displayed polynomials at their removable points. Also set \[ H_j(y,z)=  rac{(Q;Q)_j(Qyz;Q)_j} {(-qy;Q)_{j+1}(-qz;Q)_{j+1}},\qquad (a;Q)_j=\prod_{h=0}^{j-1}(1-aQ^h). 	ag{5} \] The full output coefficient formula [E, equation (5)] gives \[ U_yU_z=\sum_{j=0}^d B_j(y,z)e_j,\qquad B_j(y,z)= rac{\kappa^2(-q)^jD_N(y)D_N(z)}{N}H_j(y,z). 	ag{6} \] Initially (5)--(6) can be read off the displayed denominator locus. After cancellation they are identities of the original polynomial family, including at its source resonances. The elementary phase identity \(\kappa^2(-q)^d=1\), together with (2), proves the exact finite formula \[ \Phi_N=  rac{\kappa^2D_N(y)D_N(z)D_N(s)D_N(t)}{N^2} \sum_{j=0}^d H_j(y,z)H_{d-j}(s,t). 	ag{7} \] Thus this sum already contains the original closing and all its Hermite channels. For later use, reflection of the finite products gives \[ B_{d-j}(s,t)=G_N(r)(-q)^j  rac{(-q/s,-q/t;Q)_j}{(Q,Q/r;Q)_j}. 	ag{8} \] Here and below a tuple in a shifted factorial means a product. For an explicit verification, \((Q;Q)_d=N\), and \[ (Q;Q)_{d-j}=  rac{N(-1)^jQ^{j(j+1)/2}}{(Q;Q)_j}. \] Removing the last \(j\) factors of the other three products in (6) produces, for \(1\le h\le j\), the ratio \[  rac{(1+qsQ^{-h})(1+qtQ^{-h})}{1-rQ^{-h}} =-Q^{1-h}  rac{(1+qQ^{h-1}/s)(1+qQ^{h-1}/t)}{1-Q^h/r}. \] Its product and \(\kappa^2(-q)^d=1\) give exactly (8), including the factor \((-q)^j\). No parity sign has been suppressed. Let \[  egin{split} \mathfrak p_N(y,z;r)&= rac{\kappa^2}{N}F_N(y)F_N(z)G_N(r),\ U&=-q/s,\quad V=-q/t,\quad \mu=U+V,\quad UV=Q/r,\ W_j&=(U,V;Q)_j,\qquad a_j= rac{Q^j(Qb;Q)_j}{(-q^3y,-q^3z,Q/r;Q)_j}. \end{split} 	ag{9} \] Equations (6) and (8) now prove \[  oxed{\quad \Phi_N=\mathfrak p_N\sum_{j=0}^d a_jW_j.\quad} 	ag{10} \] The entire prefactored expression in (10), not each potentially singular factor separately, is continued at removable parameters. Equivalently this is the finite \(j=0,\ldots,d\) series \[ \Phi_N=\mathfrak p_N\, {}_4\phi_3\!\left(  egin{matrix}Q^{-d},\ Qb,\ -q/s,\ -q/t\ -q^3y,\ -q^3z,\ Q/r\end{matrix};Q,Qight). 	ag{11} \] At the root, \((Q^{-d};Q)_j/(Q;Q)_j=1\) for \(j<N\). Formula (11) means this finite series; cancellation does not authorize extending its index beyond \(d\). ## 2. A finite triangular operator calculation The following calculation supplies its own proof of the boundary operator. Temporarily use a generic base \(p\), generic parameters \(\alpha, eta,\gamma\), and \(h=\gamma p\). For symmetric Laurent polynomials under \(u\mapsto h/u\), define \[  egin{split} \mathcal B(u)&=  rac{(u-\alpha p)(u- eta p)(u-\gamma p)(u-h)} {(u^2-h)(u^2-ph)},\ \mathcal D(u)&=  rac{p(u-1)^2( eta u-\gamma)(\alpha u-\gamma)} {(u^2-h/p)(u^2-h)},\ \mathcal L f(u)&=\mathcal B(u)[f(u/p)-f(u)] +\mathcal D(u)[f(pu)-f(u)]. \end{split} 	ag{12} \] Put \(w_k(u)=(u,h/u;p)_k\), with \(w_0=1\). Then \[  egin{split} \mathcal L w_k&=\lambda_k w_k+\chi_k w_{k-1},\ \lambda_k&=(p^{-k}-1)(1-\alpha eta p^{k+1}),\ \chi_k&=-p^{-k}(1-p^k)(1-\alpha p^k) (1- eta p^k)(1-\gamma p^k) \qquad(k\ge1). \end{split} 	ag{13} \] Also \(\mathcal Lw_0=0\). Here are the polynomial and endpoint details. Direct substitution gives \(\mathcal B(h/u)=\mathcal D(u)\), so (12) preserves symmetry. At \(u^2=ph\), the first shift exchanges \(u,h/u\), and its difference vanishes; the other shifted fold is identical. At \(u^2=h\), the residues of \(\mathcal B,\mathcal D\) are opposite, and the two shifted values of a symmetric function agree. Thus these apparent poles cancel. At zero and infinity the Laurent degree does not increase. Every symmetric Laurent polynomial of degree at most \(k\) is a polynomial of degree at most \(k\) in \(u+h/u\): subtract its extreme symmetric Laurent pair and induct. Consequently \(\mathcal Lw_k\) is such a polynomial. At infinity, \(\mathcal B	o1\), \(\mathcal D	o p\alpha eta\), and the leading terms of the two shifts are \(p^{-k}\) and \(p^k\) times the original. Their combination gives \(\lambda_k\). At \(u=p^{-m}\), for \(0\le m\le k-2\), both neighboring values of \(w_k\) vanish. For \(m=0\) the reverse coefficient vanishes instead. Thus \(\mathcal Lw_k\) has all the \(k-1\) generic roots of \(w_{k-1}\). It follows that the remaining coefficient in (13) is a scalar \(\chi_k\). Evaluate at \(u=p^{1-k}\). Only the forward shifted term survives. The ratio of its first shifted factorial to the corresponding factor of \(w_{k-1}\) is \(1-p^{-k}\). The other ratio is \[  rac{(hp^k;p)_k}{(hp^{k-1};p)_{k-1}} = rac{(1-hp^{2k-2})(1-hp^{2k-1})}{1-hp^{k-1}}. \] These factors cancel exactly against the two denominators and the last numerator of \(\mathcal B(p^{1-k})\). What remains is \((1-p^{-k})(1-\alpha p^k)(1- eta p^k)(1-\gamma p^k)\), which is the coefficient in (13). This proves the finite identity. Clearing its rational denominators extends it to all specializations where the resulting polynomial expressions are defined; no assertion about distinct roots after specialization is required. ## 3. The exact original boundary equation and its folds In (12)--(13), specialize \[ p=Q,\qquad \alpha=-qy,\quad eta=-qz,\quad\gamma=r^{-1}, \qquad u=U=-q/s. 	ag{14} \] Let \(\sigma(s,t)=(Qs,Q^{-1}t)\). Direct simplification gives \[  egin{split} B&= rac{(t+q)^2(1-Qys)(1-Qzs)}{(t-s)(t-Qs)},\ D&= rac{(s+q)^2(1-Qyt)(1-Qzt)}{(Qt-s)(t-s)},\ L&=B(\sigma-1)+D(\sigma^{-1}-1),\ \lambda_k&=(Q^{-k}-1)(1-Q^{k+2}b),\ \chi_k&=-Q^{-k}(1-Q^k)(1+qyQ^k)(1+qzQ^k)(1-Q^k/r). \end{split} 	ag{15} \] Thus \(LW_k=\lambda_kW_k+\chi_kW_{k-1}\). The elementary coefficient check for (10), directly at the root, is \[ a_{j+1}\chi_{j+1} =-Q^{-j}(1-Q^{j+1})(1-bQ^{j+1})a_j =(\lambda_d-\lambda_j)a_j,\qquad 0\le j<d. 	ag{16} \] Here \(Q^N=1\) and \(d=N-1\) were used in the last equality. The coefficient of \(W_d\) already has eigenvalue \(\lambda_d\). Summing (13) therefore proves the source identity \[  oxed{\quad L\Phi_N=\lambda_d\Phi_N,\qquad \lambda_d=(Q-1)(1-Qyz).\quad} 	ag{17} \] The prefactor \(\mathfrak p_N\) is invariant under \(\sigma\), so it has not been removed by a gauge or changed by this calculation. Only \(0\le j\le d\) occurs in (16). There is no assumed equality of the two endpoints of a continued summand. For a version without a fold denominator, write \(B_{m num},D_{m num}\) for the two numerators in (15) and set \[ \Delta=(t-s)(t-Qs)(Qt-s). \] Then the exact polynomial identity is \[  oxed{\quad \lambda_d\Delta\Phi_N =B_{m num}(Qt-s)(\sigma\Phi_N-\Phi_N) +D_{m num}(t-Qs)(\sigma^{-1}\Phi_N-\Phi_N). \quad} 	ag{18} \] It holds for all four complex parameters, including \(s=0,t=0\), the shifted folds, and every individual color resonance. It was proved on a dense open set and both sides are polynomials. At a fold, source derivatives are retained by differentiating this whole polynomial identity. In particular, no value-only boundary condition is substituted for the full source there. Coincident shifted folds at \(N=2\) require no exception to (18). The argument uses only \(Q^j
e1\) for \(0<j<N\), so composite levels are included. There is a precise generic-base caution. If \(n=N-1\) is fixed and the base is moved to \(p\), the terminating series associated with (12) has second numerator \[ \alpha eta p^{n+1}=p^{N+1}yz, \qquad \lambda_n=(p^{1-N}-1)(1-p^{N+1}yz),\qquad q^2=p. 	ag{19} \] Keeping the root expression \(Qyz\) unchanged during that movement would give the wrong auxiliary eigenfunction. This note instead uses the root coefficient check (16). Its generic calculation (12)--(13) is a finite rational proof device, not an identification of a generic-\(q\) quantum source or of its quantum-normal derivatives. ## 4. The selected polynomial and its resonant family Fix \(r
e0\). Since \(\Phi_N(y,z;s,r/s)\) is symmetric under \(s\leftrightarrow r/s\), it is a polynomial of degree at most \(d\) in \(\mu=-q(s+t)/r\). The \(W_k\), \(0\le k\le d\), form a basis: their leading coefficients in \(\mu\) are \((-1)^kQ^{k(k-1)/2}\), which do not vanish. Its leading coefficient is known from the original source: \[  oxed{\quad [\mu^d]\Phi_N = rac{\kappa^2r^d}{N}G_N(yz).\quad} 	ag{20} \] Indeed the coefficient of \(s^d\) at fixed \(r\) is \(\phi(U_yU_zf_df_0)=\phi(U_yU_z)/N=G_N(yz)/N\), by (2) and \(\phi(f_af_b)=\delta_{ab}\). Since the extreme term of \(\mu^d\) is \((-q/r)^ds^d\), (20) follows from \((-q)^{-d}=\kappa^2\). For \(0\le k<d\), \[ \lambda_d-\lambda_k =-Q^{-k}(1-Q^{k+1})(1-yzQ^{k+1}). 	ag{21} \] Consequently, if \(yz
otin\{Q^{-1},\ldots,Q^{-d}\}\), the triangular equation (17), restricted to degree at most \(d\), has a unique eigenpolynomial with the leading coefficient (20). That coefficient is nonzero, since precisely the excluded values are the zeros of \(G_N(yz)\). This determines the original four-boundary source without fitting an unknown closed period. At \(yz=Q^{-h}\), \(1\le h\le d\), the actual source satisfies \[ \deg_\mu\Phi_N\le h-1. 	ag{22} \] To see this, work first where the other displayed denominators do not vanish. The factor \((Qyz;Q)_j\) is zero for every \(j\ge h\), so (10) has degree at most \(h-1\). The higher polynomial coefficients then vanish identically on this color fiber by continuation, including its simultaneous resonances. A normalization by (20) at that fiber would discard the actual source. The original polynomial family in \(y,z,s,t\) supplies its full continuation. For example, fixing \(y
e0,r
e0\) and writing \(z=b/y\), differentiation gives, off the fold denominators, \[ (L_b-\lambda_d(b))\partial_b\Phi_N =(\lambda_d'(b)-\partial_bL_b)\Phi_N. 	ag{23} \] At the folds the same statement is read by differentiating (18). All derivatives of the known prefactor are included. These are external parameter derivatives; the internal repeated-root Hermite data were already present in (2)--(7). No extension in the quantum level is inferred from this family statement. ## 5. Two exact source readouts and actual gluing The centered compiler gives \(U_{ja}=\kappa(-q)^j(-qQ^j)^a/\sqrt N\). The finite geometric sum therefore proves, with their original phases, \[ U_{-q}=\kappa^{-1}\sqrt N e_d,\qquad U_{-q^{-1}}=\kappa\sqrt N\,1. 	ag{24} \] The Newton factors show that \(m\) is evaluation at the first Casimir node: every \(e_j\), \(j>0\), vanishes there. Thus it is an algebra character. In particular, \(\phi(e_dv)=m(v)\) and \(m(U_a)=\kappa F_N(a)/\sqrt N\). Hence \[  oxed{\quad \Phi_N(y,z;-q,t)= rac{\kappa^2}{N}F_N(y)F_N(z)F_N(t), \qquad \Phi_N(y,z;-q^{-1},t)=\kappa\sqrt N\,\mathcal C_N(y,z,t). \quad} 	ag{25} \] Here \(\mathcal C_N(y,z,t)=\phi(U_yU_zU_t)\) is the original three-coherent generating scalar, including its entire source. The first identity also follows from (10): at \(s=-q\), \(U=1\), all \(W_j\) with \(j>0\) vanish, leaving its original prefactor. Both identities hold at both parities, including \(N=2\). Finally, \(\phi(Jv\,Jw)=\phi(vw)\) follows directly from (2). Put \(u_N(a)=U_a/\sqrt{Z_N(a)}\), where \(Z_N(a)=\sum_{j=0}^d|a|^{2j}\). The actual closing of two turned coherent products is \[ \phi\!\left(J(u_N(y)u_N(z))J(u_N(s)u_N(t))ight) = rac{\Phi_N(y,z;s,t)} {\sqrt{Z_N(y)Z_N(z)Z_N(s)Z_N(t)}}. 	ag{26} \] The root shifts in (15) preserve these four normalization factors. There is no replacement of this bilinear closing by a Hermitian norm. Equations (17)--(26) describe a universal four-boundary primitive, not a new knot case or closure theorem for arbitrary trees. ## 6. Coverage, scope, and complete proof sources The terminating series in (11) has the standard \(q\)-Racah parameter pattern. See Koekoek--Swarttouw, [equation (3.2.1)](https://tudelft.roelofkoekoek.nl/documents/as98.pdf), with parameters \(\alpha=-qy, eta=-qz,\gamma=(st)^{-1},\delta=1\). Its standard difference equation is recorded there as (3.2.6). These are coverage references, not proof premises: (12)--(18) give the finite calculation here. No novelty is claimed for the named polynomial or its general difference equation, and no positive finite orthogonality theorem is used. The new source statements identify the literal four-coherent period, its known normalization, its full resonant family, and its exact unit and socle readouts. No nonzero value at an arbitrary boundary point, geometric action estimate, positive-cycle metric, or finite-exception volume theorem follows. Scalar cancellation remains in the original source polynomial. The two complete proof directs were read at the matching pins below.
