title: Anchored source transport reaches the central fold value
text: # Anchored source transport reaches the central fold value 22 November 2026. Research note. Author-final. Earlier final notes and public manuscripts remain unchanged. The original four-coherent scalar has the positive ideal-cube rate uniformly along its entire anchored half-grid up to the central fold. No fixed distance from that fold is required. If the grid lands on the fold, the estimate includes its actual value, without using the singular boundary-equation row there. An explicit sine factor removes the potentially shrinking first difference. The resulting positive flux has a bounded total correction, and converting back costs at most a polynomial factor. No source, seam, or repeated-root coordinate is replaced. ## 1. The original source and the extended range Let \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), and \(Q=q^2\). In the full centered basis put \[ U_a=\sum_{\ell=0}^d a^\ell f_\ell,\qquad \Phi_N(y,z;s,t)=\phi(U_yU_zU_sU_t). \tag{1} \] This is the original Frobenius contraction, including all internal Hermite derivative coordinates and its original phases. Fix a compact subset \(K\) of the three-parameter domain \[ b,c>0,\qquad S=b+c<1,\qquad 1-S<R<1-\max(b,c). \tag{2} \] Set \(\varepsilon=N^{-1}\) and \[ \begin{gathered} y=-e^{-2\pi ib},\quad z=-e^{-2\pi ic},\quad r=e^{-2\pi iR},\\ h_j=(j+\tfrac12)\varepsilon,\quad k_j=R-h_j,\quad s_j=-q^{-1}Q^{-j},\quad t_j=-qrQ^j,\\ \Phi_j=\Phi_N(y,z;s_j,t_j),\qquad \omega_N=e^{-\pi i d(S+R)} . \end{gathered} \tag{3} \] The allowed targets are all integers \[ J\ge0,\qquad 0<h_J\le R/2. \tag{4} \] Thus the target can be \(O(N^{-1})\) from the fold or exactly at it. The entries \(-1,0\) initialize the same anchored orbit. Use the actual source action \[ \begin{split} L(x)&=\int_0^x\log|2\sin\pi v|\,dv,\\ m(x,y,u)&=L(x+y)+L(u)-L(x)-L(y)\\ &\hspace{10mm}-L(u-x)-L(u-y)-L(x+y-u), \end{split} \tag{5} \] where \(L\) has its odd, one-periodic extension. Put \[ \begin{split} I_h&=(\max(b,c,1-R),\ \min(S,1-h,1-R+h)),\\ \mathcal F(b,c,R,h)&= \max_{u\in I_h}\{m(b,c,u)+m(h,R-h,1-u)\}. \end{split} \tag{6} \] The [actual cube theorem](../papers/strict-conway-geometry/README.md) identifies \(\pi\mathcal F\) with the volume of its convex ideal cube. This remains a strict cube at \(h=R/2\): all six external pair sums are below one, and their total is \(S+R>1\). The fold is in the boundary parametrization, not a degeneration of this ideal cube. **Theorem.** There are constants \(C_K,N_K\) such that for every \(N\ge N_K\), every \((b,c,R)\in K\), and every target (4), \[ \boxed{\quad \Phi_J=\omega_N P_{N,J},\qquad P_{N,J}>0,\qquad |\log P_{N,J}-N\mathcal F(b,c,R,h_J)|\le C_K\log N . \quad} \tag{7} \] The estimate is uniform even when \(h_J\) tends to zero or to the fold at a level-dependent rate. Both parities and composite levels are included. The normalized original closing of the two turned products is \(\Phi_J/N^2\), and has the same rate. ## 2. Exact source initialization and the rows actually used The [anchored-grid theorem](research_four_coherent_anchored_grid_volume.md) supplies the exact common carrier in (3), the two original readouts, and their calibrated asymptotics. Consequently \[ \begin{gathered} H_j=\omega_N^{-1}\Phi_j\in\mathbb R,\qquad H_0>0,\qquad \Delta_0:=H_0-H_{-1}>0,\\ \log H_0=N M(b,c,R)+O_K(\log N),\qquad M(b,c,R)=m(b,c,1-R)>0,\\ |H_{-1}|\le C_K/N,\qquad \Delta_0/H_0=1+O_K(e^{-c_KN}). \end{gathered} \tag{8} \] Only the compact parameters in (2) enter these bounds. Indeed the entry \(0\) is an original three-input scalar at angles \(b,c,R-1/(2N)\); these remain in a compact strict prism family. The entry \(-1\) is its elementary socle readout. For a fixed target \(J\), put \[ \delta_j=R-2h_j,\qquad \alpha_j=\sin\pi(R-2j\varepsilon) =\sin\pi(\delta_j+\varepsilon). \tag{9} \] For every row \(0\le j<J\), \[ \delta_j=\delta_J+2(J-j)\varepsilon\ge2\varepsilon,\qquad 0<\delta_j-\varepsilon<\delta_j+\varepsilon\le R<1. \tag{10} \] Therefore every boundary row used in the proof is regular. In particular \(\alpha_{j+1}=\sin\pi(\delta_j-\varepsilon)>0\). At the terminal point, \[ c_K/N\le\alpha_J\le1, \tag{11} \] including \(\alpha_J=\sin(\pi/N)\) when \(\delta_J=0\). No boundary equation is imposed at row \(J\). Write the positive numerators of the sine-converted coefficients as \[ \begin{split} \mathcal B_j={}& \sin^2\pi(k_j+\varepsilon/2) \sin\pi(b+h_j-\varepsilon)\sin\pi(c+h_j-\varepsilon),\\ \mathcal D_j={}& \sin^2\pi(h_j+\varepsilon/2) \sin\pi(b+k_j-\varepsilon)\sin\pi(c+k_j-\varepsilon). \end{split} \tag{12} \] Then the exact source recurrence, with \(\Delta_j=H_j-H_{j-1}\), is \[ \begin{gathered} \Delta_{j+1}=\rho_j\Delta_j+ \frac{\Lambda_N}{\mathsf d_j}H_j,\\ \mathsf b_j=\frac{\mathcal B_j}{\sin\pi\delta_j\,\alpha_j}, \quad \mathsf d_j=\frac{\mathcal D_j}{\sin\pi\delta_j\,\alpha_{j+1}}, \quad \rho_j=\mathsf b_j/\mathsf d_j,\\ \Lambda_N=\sin(\pi/N)\sin\pi(S-\varepsilon). \end{gathered} \tag{13} \] All coefficients in these used rows are positive for large \(N\). Uniformly there, \[ \mathcal B_j\ge c_K>0,\qquad 0<\Lambda_N\le C_K\varepsilon . \tag{14} \] For example \(k_j+\varepsilon/2\) stays between \(R/2\) and \(R\); the other two arguments in \(\mathcal B_j\) stay in compact subintervals of \((0,1)\). This proves (14) without bounding the possibly large divided coefficients near the fold. ## 3. Removing the shrinking sine from the first difference Set \[ q_j=\mathcal B_j/\mathcal D_j,\qquad E_j=\Delta_j/\alpha_j . \tag{15} \] The exact relation between the two transfer factors is \[ \rho_j=q_j\,\alpha_{j+1}/\alpha_j . \tag{16} \] Unlike \(\rho_j\), the factor \(q_j\) stays above one throughout the used half-path. For a quantitative bound define \[ f_N(v)=\frac{\sin^2\pi v} {\sin\pi(b-3\varepsilon/2+v)\sin\pi(c-3\varepsilon/2+v)} . \tag{17} \] Then \(q_j=f_N(k_j+\varepsilon/2)/f_N(h_j+\varepsilon/2)\). Its logarithmic derivative is the sum of two positive cotangent differences. The identity \(\cot x-\cot(x+a)=\sin a/[\sin x\sin(x+a)]\) gives a lower bound \(c_K>0\), even when the first argument is of order \(N^{-1}\). Since the two arguments differ by \(\delta_j\), \[ q_j-1\ge c_K\delta_j . \tag{18} \] Here the shifted \(b,c\) are positive for large \(N\), and all shifted arguments remain in \((0,1)\), by (2). Dividing (13) by \(\alpha_{j+1}\) now gives \[ E_{j+1}=q_jE_j \left(1+\beta_j\frac{H_j}{E_j}\right),\qquad \beta_j=\frac{\Lambda_N\sin\pi\delta_j}{\mathcal B_j}, \qquad 0<\beta_j\le C_K\varepsilon\delta_j . \tag{19} \] Starting with (8), induction proves \(E_j,\Delta_j,H_j>0\) for every \(0\le j\le J\). In particular \(E_{j+1}\ge q_jE_j\). We next bound \(H_j/E_j\) without a fixed fold margin. For every \(j<J\), (10) and (18) imply \[ \alpha_jE_j\le C_K\delta_jE_j \le C_K(E_{j+1}-E_j). \tag{20} \] For a target \(1\le n\le J\), use \[ H_n=H_0+\sum_{j=1}^n\alpha_jE_j. \tag{21} \] Apply (20) up to \(n-1\), and bound the final term by \(E_n\). Since \(E_n\ge E_0=\Delta_0/\sin\pi R\), (8) gives \(H_n/E_n\le C_K\). Conversely \(H_n\ge\Delta_n=\alpha_nE_n\). At \(n=0\) the analogous comparison follows directly from (8). Thus, uniformly along the entire path, \[ c_K/N\le H_n/E_n\le C_K . \tag{22} \] The lower bound uses \(\alpha_n\ge c_K/N\) for all \(n\le J\), not a lower bound independent of \(N\). By (19) and (22), the logarithmic correction to the product of the \(q_j\)'s is at most \(C_K\varepsilon\sum_{j<J}\delta_j\), which is bounded. Therefore \[ \log E_J=\log E_0+\sum_{j=0}^{J-1}\log q_j+O_K(1),\qquad \log H_J=\log H_0+\sum_{j=0}^{J-1}\log q_j+O_K(\log N). \tag{23} \] Equivalently, an explicit finite-level estimate is \[ \frac{c_K}{N}\prod_{j<J}q_j \le\frac{\Phi_J}{\Phi_0} \le C_K\prod_{j<J}q_j . \tag{24} \] The ratio is real and positive, with the original source carrier retained. Empty sums and products cover \(J=0\). ## 4. The same geometric action, uniformly at the terminal fold The product now contains no divided fold factor: \[ q_j=\frac{\sin^2\pi(R-j\varepsilon)} {\sin^2\pi((j+1)\varepsilon)} \frac{\sin\pi(b+(j-\tfrac12)\varepsilon) \sin\pi(c+(j-\tfrac12)\varepsilon)} {\sin\pi(b+R-(j+\tfrac32)\varepsilon) \sin\pi(c+R-(j+\tfrac32)\varepsilon)} . \tag{25} \] All its factors are smooth log-sine samples on fixed strict intervals, apart from the explicit denominator at the initial endpoint. The usual integral comparison for \(\log(J!)\), together with \(\log\sin\pi v=\log v+\) a smooth function near zero, gives uniformly up to \(h_J=R/2\), \[ \begin{split} \sum_{j<J}\log q_j &=N\int_0^{h_J}\log\rho_0(v)\,dv+O_K(\log N),\\ \rho_0(v)&= \frac{\sin^2\pi(R-v)\sin\pi(b+v)\sin\pi(c+v)} {\sin^2\pi v\sin\pi(b+R-v)\sin\pi(c+R-v)} . \end{split} \tag{26} \] The bounded shifts cost \(O_K(1)\); changing \(J/N\) to \(h_J\) costs at most \(O_K(\log N)\) after multiplication by \(N\). There is no singularity at the upper endpoint: \(\rho_0(R/2)=1\). The anchored-grid proof identifies, on \(0<h<R/2\), \[ \mathcal F(b,c,R,h) =M(b,c,R)+\int_0^h\log\rho_0(v)\,dv . \tag{27} \] This identity extends to \(h=R/2\) by continuity. The actual cube theorem applies there as well: its two prism actions still have a unique strict stationary maximum. Combining (8), (23), and (26)--(27) proves (7). No singular target row was used to obtain that value. ## 5. What has and has not been extended This removes the fixed fold margin for actual values on the anchored orbit. In particular every closest prefold grid point is covered, and an exact central grid value is covered whenever it occurs. The proof uses only the original finite boundary equation in regular rows and its original two source anchors. It does not estimate a derivative normal to the folded boundary coordinate, nor does it apply the pole-cancelled target equation to identify such a derivative. It does not prove transport to a fixed postfold interval, use a reflected fractional orbit, or remove the anchored-grid and initial pair-wall restrictions in (2)--(4). The original scalar and its \(N^{-2}\) coherent normalization are unchanged. No general Conway attachment or finite-exception knot-volume theorem follows. The complete direct proof sources are: | Source | SHA-256 | |---|---| | [Anchored original-source transport, 418 lines](research_four_coherent_anchored_grid_volume.md) | d79b3f5bb0f2cb325214015cf9b4b15ca4ac8892ff5d1d42df794b89f7d2771d | | [Actual prism and cube geometry, 377 lines](../papers/strict-conway-geometry/README.md) | c29321805df39a49854665df1255db1ec7180397a5dd689f19289d61335871c9 | Both whole texts were read at their matching pins. The flux change, uniform bounds and terminal-value extension are proved above. Only written mathematics and text operations were used.

title: Fractional boundary data for the original four-input scalar
text: # Fractional boundary data for the original four-input scalar 22 November 2026. Written research proof. Earlier author-final notes and public manuscripts remain unchanged. We retain the full finite pole packet that replaces the three-input Cauchy pole when one boundary angle is of order \(N^{-1}\). A second finite rectangle evaluates this packet. Its right connector has a smaller exponential rate; it is not discarded as a polynomial error. The resulting estimate concerns the original scalar. ## 1. Source and statement Use the original source and conventions of [B]: \[ d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\quad \eta=(-1)^d,\quad\kappa=e^{\pi i d^2/(2N)},\qquad U_x=\sum_{j=0}^d x^jf_j . \tag{1} \] The full repeated-root algebra and its original Frobenius functional \(\phi\) are retained. Fix a compact set of triples satisfying \[ b,c>0,\quad S=b+c<1,\qquad 1-S<R<1-\max(b,c). \tag{2} \] Put \[ \begin{gathered} y=-e^{-2\pi ib},\quad z=-e^{-2\pi ic},\quad r=e^{-2\pi iR},\quad p=NR,\quad L=N-p,\quad u=1-R,\\ a\in\mathcal A=[a_-,a_+]\Subset(0,\infty),\qquad s_a=-e^{-2\pi i(a-1/2)/N},\quad t_a=r/s_a,\\ \Phi_a=\phi(U_yU_zU_{s_a}U_{t_a}). \end{gathered} \tag{3} \] Thus \(a=1\) is the exact unit readout of [B]. Define \[ \mathfrak g(b,c,u)= \frac{\sin^2(\pi u)\sin(\pi b)\sin(\pi c)} {\pi^2\sin(\pi(u-b))\sin(\pi(u-c))}>0 . \tag{4} \] All constants below are uniform on the fixed compact set and on \(\mathcal A\). Enlarge this interval to include \(1\), if necessary. **Theorem.** For all sufficiently large \(N\), the original source \(\Phi_1\) is nonzero, and \[ \boxed{\qquad \frac{\Phi_a}{\Phi_1} =\frac{N^{2a-2}}{\Gamma(a)^2}\, \mathfrak g(b,c,u)^{a-1} (1+O(N^{-1})). \qquad} \tag{5} \] In particular the entire displayed boundary layer is nonzero. The powers of the positive number in (4) use its real logarithm. The baseline in (5) is the actual three-input source, \[ \Phi_1=\kappa\sqrt N\,\mathcal C_N(y,z,-qr). \tag{6} \] The four unit-circle inputs have norm \(\sqrt N\); dividing each scalar in (5) by \(N^2\) leaves the same ratio. All phases and internal Hermite normals belong to the original scalar. No transport through a boundary fold or arbitrary further attachment is claimed. ## 2. Canonical factorial estimates used below Write \(\mathscr F_N\) for the canonical factorial of [P, equations (9)--(11)], to distinguish it from the polynomial \(F_N\) in [B]. Its exact identities are \[ \begin{gathered} \mathscr F_N(0)=1,\quad \mathscr F_N(j)=(Q;Q)_j,\\ \mathscr F_N(w+1)=(1-Q^{w+1})\mathscr F_N(w),\\ \mathscr F_N(w+N)=(1-e^{2\pi iw})\mathscr F_N(w),\\ \mathscr F_N(w)\mathscr F_N(d-w)=Nq^{w(w-d)} . \end{gathered} \tag{7} \] The negative poles start at \(-1\); the first positive zeros are the simple zeros \(N,\ldots,2N-1\). In particular \[ \mathscr F_N'(N+k)=-2\pi i\,\mathscr F_N(k) \quad(0\le k<N). \tag{8} \] Let \(f,h\) have their canonical branches from [P]: \[ f'(w)=\operatorname{Log}(1-e^{2\pi iw}),\quad \Re f(x)=\mathcal L(x),\quad h(w)^2=i(1-e^{2\pi iw}),\quad \mathcal L(x)=\int_0^x\log|2\sin\pi v|\,dv . \tag{9} \] The primitive \(\mathcal L\) is extended oddly and periodically. On fixed strict vertical substrips, for every bounded real shift \(\tau\), \[ \mathscr F_N(Nw+\tau) =\sqrt N\,h(w)(1-e^{2\pi iw})^\tau e^{Nf(w)}(1+O(N^{-1})). \tag{10} \] This is uniform at arbitrary imaginary height. It follows from [P, equations (32)--(34)] by Taylor expansion; the needed logarithmic derivatives are bounded there. We also use (10) when \(\Re w=0,\ |\Im w|\ge\epsilon\). Here is the extra justification. In the Gamma product defining \(\mathscr F_N\), the arguments \(Nw,N(m+w),N(m-w)\) remain in closed sectors excluding the negative real axis and away from zero. The summed Stirling remainder is bounded by \[ CN^{-3}\left(|w|^{-3} +\sum_{m\ge1}(|m+w|^{-3}+|m-w|^{-3})\right) \le C_\epsilon N^{-3}. \tag{11} \] The identities for the main terms continue from \(\Re w>0\). This proves (10) on these two additional half-lines with the continued canonical branches. At bounded arguments the same Gamma product gives \[ \mathscr F_N(v)=(-2\pi i/N)^v\Gamma(v+1) \exp E_N(v),\qquad |E_N(v)|\le C(1+|v|)^2/N \tag{12} \] when \(\Re v\) ranges in a fixed compact subset of \((-1,\infty)\) and \(|\Im v|\le\epsilon N\), for sufficiently small fixed \(\epsilon\). For completeness, after the leading Gamma factor is removed, each paired term is \[ \log\frac{\Gamma(Nm+v+1)} {\Gamma(Nm-v)(Nm)^{2v+1}} =O((1+|v|)^3/(Nm)^2). \tag{13} \] The coefficient of \((Nm)^{-1}\) vanishes because the two Gamma shifts sum to one. Summation and the exact quadratic phase in \(\mathscr F_N\) prove (12). The logarithm in (12) is continued from \(v=0\); no Gamma pole meets the uses below. We also need a fixed-shift comparison at the current endpoint. For real \(c,c'\) in fixed compact subsets of \((-1,\infty)\), uniformly for \(|T|\le\epsilon N\), \[ \left|\frac{\mathscr F_N(c+iT)} {\mathscr F_N(c'+iT)}\right| \le C N^C(1+|T|)^C e^{C|T|/N}. \] The ordinary Gamma ratio has only the indicated polynomial cost. In the paired product (13), taking a fixed difference in the real shift bounds its logarithm by \(C(1+|T|)^2/N^2\), rather than the cubic bound for an individual term. Its quadratic phase costs \(e^{C|T|/N}\). This proves the comparison and justifies using the exact half-step modulus [P, equation (35)] at other bounded real endpoint shifts. These estimates have a useful quantitative consequence. In any factorial quotient below, all macroscopic real arguments stay in strict substrips, except specified endpoint factors. For \(|Y|\ge\epsilon\), apply (10)--(11) to those endpoint factors as well. The powers of \(1-e^{2\pi iw}\) then determine the entire remaining height dependence. We will record the resulting integrable majorants explicitly, rather than use a fixed-\(N\) asymptotic as an integral bound. ## 3. The exact rectangle retains the third pole family Set \[ \begin{gathered} A=N(1-b)-\tfrac12,\quad B_0=N(1-c)-\tfrac12,\quad C=N(1-S),\quad A+B_0-C=d,\\ W(w)=\frac{\mathscr F_N(w)\mathscr F_N(w+C) \mathscr F_N(A)\mathscr F_N(B_0)} {\mathscr F_N(C)\mathscr F_N(w+1+A)\mathscr F_N(w+1+B_0)},\\ K_a(w)= \frac{\mathscr F_N(w+a-1)} {\mathscr F_N(a-1)\mathscr F_N(w)} \frac{\mathscr F_N(w+p-a)\mathscr F_N(p)} {\mathscr F_N(p-a)\mathscr F_N(w+p)},\qquad T_a(w)=Q^wW(w)K_a(w). \end{gathered} \tag{14} \] The finite source formula [B, equations (9)--(10)] gives exactly \[ \Phi_a=\frac{\kappa^2D_N(y)D_N(z)G_N(r)}{N} \sum_{j=0}^dT_a(j),\quad D_N(x)=1-\eta x^N,\quad G_N(r)=\sum_{j=0}^d r^j . \tag{15} \] At \(a=1\), \[ Q^wK_1(w)= \frac{1-r}{1-rQ^{-w}}, \tag{16} \] which is precisely the three-input Cauchy kernel. Put \(\delta_*=\min(1/8,a_-/8)\). Choose \(\zeta\) from \(-\delta_*,-3\delta_*\), so that \(\operatorname{dist}(p+\zeta,\mathbb Z)\ge\delta_*/2\). One of these choices always works. Both are greater than \(-a_-\) and \(-1\). The choice also makes \(1-r^{-N}e^{2\pi i\zeta}\) uniformly separated from zero. Put \(K=\lfloor p+\zeta\rfloor\). The sample-preserving differential is \[ \Omega_a(w)=\frac{\kappa^2G_N(r)}{N}\,2\pi i\, \frac{(1-\eta y^N\tau)(1-\eta z^N\tau)}{\tau-1} T_a(w)\,dw,\qquad \tau=e^{2\pi iw}. \tag{17} \] Its residue at the integer \(j\) is the \(j\)-th term of (15). Work first off collisions of integer and moving poles. The final canceled formulas will remove this restriction. Use the rectangle \(\zeta<\Re w<N+\zeta\), with horizontal heights tending to infinity. The two periodic numerator factors in (17) cancel exactly the two old outer denominator families from \(\mathscr F_N(w+1+A)\) and \(\mathscr F_N(w+1+B_0)\), as in [P]. The third family is not canceled: its poles are \[ w=L+k,\qquad 0\le k\le K. \tag{18} \] They come from the first zero block of \(\mathscr F_N(w+p)\). There is no further zero block in the rectangle. The numerator \(\mathscr F_N(w+a-1)\) has its first negative pole at \(-a\), strictly to the left of both possible left sides. The other numerator poles are farther left. This lists every pole. The horizontal sides do vanish at fixed \(N\). After the common factor \(\mathscr F_N(w)\) is canceled, \(T_a\) has three numerator and three denominator factorials. The difference of their total shifts is \(-N-2\). Including \(Q^w\), its lower end decays as \(e^{-2\pi(1+1/N)|\Im w|}\). The degree-two periodic numerator divided by \(\tau-1\) costs \(e^{2\pi|\Im w|}\) below. Thus both ends retain decay \(e^{-2\pi|\Im w|/N}\). No degree-three cancellation or additional periodic denominator has been introduced. For the paired vertical current, write \[ Y_0=y^N,\quad Z_0=z^N,\quad \rho=r^{-N},\quad a_0=e^{2\pi ia}, \] \[ \begin{split} A_a&=\eta(Y_0+Z_0)+\rho-Y_0Z_0-a_0-\rho/a_0,\\ B_a&=Y_0Z_0(a_0+\rho/a_0-1)+\rho[1-\eta(Y_0+Z_0)] . \end{split} \tag{19} \] The exact factorial monodromy gives \[ \frac{T_a(w+N)}{T_a(w)} =\frac{(1-Y_0Z_0\tau)(1-a_0\tau)(1-\rho\tau/a_0)} {(1-\eta Y_0\tau)(1-\eta Z_0\tau)(1-\rho\tau)}. \tag{20} \] Subtracting one cancels both the constant and cubic terms. Consequently the whole paired current is \[ I_a=\frac{\kappa^2G_N(r)}{N} \int_{\zeta-i\infty}^{\zeta+i\infty} \frac{\tau(A_a+B_a\tau)}{(\tau-1)(1-\rho\tau)} T_a(w)\,dw . \tag{21} \] The factor \(A_a+B_a\tau\) remains a numerator. In particular its zeros have not produced an unrecorded orbit of poles. Uniformly in the parameters, \[ |I_a|\le C N^C . \tag{22} \] Here are bounds for this assertion. The rational kernel in (21) is at most \(C e^{-2\pi N Y}\) for \(Y\ge0\), and at most \(C\) for \(Y\le0\), on \(w=\zeta+iNY\). The choice of \(\zeta\) bounds both denominators below by a positive constant times \(1+|\tau|\). The bounded shifts in \(K_a\), using (10)--(13), cost at most \(N^C(1+|Y|)^C e^{C|Y|}\) relative to the old left weight and its Cauchy factor. For unit \(y,z\), the rate \(R_0\) of [P, equations (37)--(41)] satisfies \(R_0(Y)\le\pi Y\) on both half-lines. Indeed its three radii there are equal. For every \(k>0\), the ratio \[ Z_k=\frac{(1-ke^{-2\pi ib})(1-ke^{-2\pi ic})} {1-ke^{-2\pi iS}} \tag{23} \] has positive imaginary part: after clearing its denominator, the imaginary numerator is \[ 2k(1+k)\sin(\pi S) [\cos\pi(b-c)-\cos\pi S]>0. \] Thus its continuous argument lies in \((0,\pi)\), requiring only \(b,c>0,S<1\). The proof does not require \(b,c<1/2\). The current is bounded by \[ C N^C\int_{\mathbb R}(1+|Y|)^C e^{-\pi N|Y|+C|Y|}\,dY , \tag{24} \] after absorbing the factor \(dw=iN\,dY\) into \(N^C\). This is a quantitative integrable majorant for (22). ## 4. The exact retained packet and its pole-free amplitude Define \[ D_y=L-Nb+\tfrac12,\qquad D_z=L-Nc+\tfrac12. \tag{25} \] All of \(A,B_0,C,L,L+C,D_y,D_z,p\), with bounded shifts as used below, stay in fixed strict factorial strips. The same quasiperiod identity that canceled the two outer families gives \[ (1-\eta y^N\tau)(1-\eta z^N\tau)W(w) =\frac{\mathscr F_N(w)\mathscr F_N(w+C) \mathscr F_N(A)\mathscr F_N(B_0)} {\mathscr F_N(C)\mathscr F_N(w-Nb+1/2) \mathscr F_N(w-Nc+1/2)}. \tag{26} \] Using (8) at every pole in (18), with the orientation of the rectangle, proves the exact decomposition \[ \Phi_a=\mathcal G_a S_{N,a}+I_a, \tag{27} \] where \[ \begin{split} S_{N,a}&=\sum_{k=0}^{K}R_k,\qquad R_k=\frac{Q^k(Q^{1-a},\,rQ^a,\,Qr yz;Q)_k} {(Q,\,-q^3ry,\,-q^3rz;Q)_k},\\ \mathcal G_1&= \frac{\kappa^2\mathscr F_N(A)\mathscr F_N(B_0) \mathscr F_N(L)\mathscr F_N(L+C)} {\mathscr F_N(C)\mathscr F_N(D_y)\mathscr F_N(D_z)},\\ \frac{\mathcal G_a}{\mathcal G_1} &=-\frac r{1-r}\frac{\mathscr F_N(p)}{\mathscr F_N(p-a)} \frac{\mathscr F_N(L+a-1)}{\mathscr F_N(L)} \frac{q^{(N-a)(1-a)}}{\mathscr F_N(a-1)^2}. \end{split} \tag{28} \] Every denominator in (28) is nonzero in our domain for large \(N\). The two macroscopic packet denominator families stay uniformly away from zero, since their factorial intervals lie strictly between \(0\) and \(N\). The light factor \((Q;Q)_k\) is only asserted nonzero for \(k<N\); its small factors are retained exactly in the endpoint Gamma estimates. To check the source sign and normalization, before cancellation the residue at \(L+k\) contains \((1-e^{-2\pi ia})\mathscr F_N(k-a)/\mathscr F_N(k)\); the negative derivative in (8) is canceled by the minus sign when the moving residues are moved to the right side of the residue theorem. The \(k=0\) amplitude includes \(G_N(r)/(r^N-1)\). Cancel it as \(-1/(1-r)\). Finally use \[ (1-e^{-2\pi ia})\mathscr F_N(-a)=\mathscr F_N(N-a), \quad \mathscr F_N(N-a)\mathscr F_N(a-1) =Nq^{(N-a)(1-a)} \tag{29} \] to get the pole-free last line of (28). Thus (27)--(28) continue through every positive integer \(a\) and through \(r^N=1\), with the actual whole source, not a value-only cancellation. At \(a=1\), \(R_0=1\) and every \(R_k\), \(k>0\), vanishes, while \(\mathcal G_a/\mathcal G_1=1\). This is precisely the original three-input geometric residue. Collisions with old outer families are covered by the exact canceled expression (26). ## 5. The strict connector gap Set \[ \begin{split} h_0&=\mathcal L(S)-\mathcal L(b)-\mathcal L(c)>0,\\ P(v)&=\mathcal L(v)+\mathcal L(v-S)+\mathcal L(S) -\mathcal L(b)-\mathcal L(c) -\mathcal L(v-b)-\mathcal L(v-c),\\ M&=P(u),\qquad u=1-R . \end{split} \tag{30} \] These are the rates of the explicit factorials above. Uniformly on compact sets, \[ M-h_0\ge\delta>0 . \tag{31} \] Here is a direct verification. For \(x,y>0,x+y<1\), \(\mathcal L(x+y)-\mathcal L(x)-\mathcal L(y)>0\). Its derivative in \(x\) is \(\log[\sin\pi(x+y)/\sin\pi x]\); it has one maximum, zero limits at the two ends, and is positive between them. This proves \(h_0>0\). On \((\max(b,c),S)\), \(P'\) is the logarithm of \[ \left|\frac{(1-v_0)(1-yzv_0)} {(1+yv_0)(1+zv_0)}\right|, \qquad v_0=e^{2\pi iv}. \tag{32} \] The numerator of its squared modulus minus one is \[ 16\sin(\pi b)\sin(\pi c) [\cos(2\pi v-\pi S)-\cos(\pi b)\cos(\pi c)]. \] If \(\omega=\pi^{-1}\arccos(\cos\pi b\cos\pi c)\), then \(|b-c|<\omega<S\). Its two crossings \((S-\omega)/2,(S+\omega)/2\) therefore lie respectively below \(\min(b,c)\) and strictly between \(\max(b,c)\) and \(S\). This gives one maximum and no interior minimum for \(P\) on the interval in question. Also \(P(S)=2h_0\). If \(b\ge c\), \[ P(b)-h_0=\mathcal L(b)-\mathcal L(c)-\mathcal L(b-c)\ge0, \tag{33} \] with equality only at \(b=c\). In that case \(P\) increases strictly immediately to the right of the endpoint. Thus \(P>h_0\) throughout the open interval; compactness proves (31). For later contour bounds, put \[ \mathcal R(v)=\frac{(1-v)(1-yzv)}{(1+yv)(1+zv)},\qquad \chi=-\mathcal R(r)>0 . \tag{34} \] For \(v=re^{-2\pi Y}\), set \(w=ve^{-\pi iS}\), \(s_0=2\cos\pi(b-c)>t_0=2\cos\pi S\). Since \(\arg(re^{-\pi iS})=\pi(2u-S)\in(0,\pi)\), \[ \mathcal R(v)=\frac{1-t_0w+w^2}{1-s_0w+w^2},\quad \Im\mathcal R(v)= \frac{(s_0-t_0)(1-|w|^2)\Im w}{|1-s_0w+w^2|^2}. \tag{35} \] Thus its argument continued from \(\pi\) at \(Y=0\) lies in \((0,\pi)\) above, and \((\pi,2\pi)\) below. Let \(\mathcal V(Y)\) be the real rate, normalized to zero at zero, of \[ \frac{\mathscr F_N(Nu+iNY)\mathscr F_N(N(u+1-S)+iNY)} {\mathscr F_N(N(u-b)+iNY)\mathscr F_N(N(u-c)+iNY)} \] including the rate \(2\pi Y\) for \(Y<0\) of the one-sided Barnes kernel. Its derivative is \(-\arg\mathcal R(v)\) for \(Y>0\), and \(2\pi-\arg\mathcal R(v)\) for \(Y<0\). Consequently its unique maximum is zero, its one-sided slopes there are \(-\pi,+\pi\), and \[ \sup_{|Y|\ge\epsilon}\mathcal V(Y)\le-\delta_\epsilon<0, \qquad \lim_{Y\to\pm\infty}\mathcal V(Y)=h_0-M . \tag{36} \] The limits follow from (9): the real part of the upper constant of \(f\), and of its lower constant after subtracting \(i\pi(w^2-w)\), is zero. They can also be read off the normalized dilogarithm primitive. All limits and losses are uniform. ## 6. An exact finite Barnes identity without pinched integer parameters Fix an integer \(\ell\ge a_+\). For \(0\le k\le\ell\), the finite products in (28) give, uniformly even at their integer zeros, \[ R_k=r_k+O(N^{-1}),\qquad r_k=\frac{(1-a)_k(-\chi)^k}{k!} =\binom{a-1}{k}\chi^k . \tag{37} \] Here \((1-a)_k\) is the ordinary rising factorial. Remove the first \(\ell\) terms before deforming the packet. Define \[ \begin{split} T_N(v)={}&Q^v \frac{\mathscr F_N(v+\ell-a)\mathscr F_N(\ell)} {\mathscr F_N(\ell-a)\mathscr F_N(v+\ell)}\\ &\times \frac{\mathscr F_N(L+a+\ell-1+v)\mathscr F_N(L+C+\ell+v)} {\mathscr F_N(L+a+\ell-1)\mathscr F_N(L+C+\ell)}\\ &\times \frac{\mathscr F_N(D_y+\ell)\mathscr F_N(D_z+\ell)} {\mathscr F_N(D_y+\ell+v)\mathscr F_N(D_z+\ell+v)} . \end{split} \tag{38} \] The finite product identity is \(R_{k+\ell}=R_\ell T_N(k)\). The explicit right side (38) stays regular when \(R_\ell=0\); no division by that coefficient defines the interpolation. Use left line \(\Re v=\gamma=-1/4\), right line \(\Re v=\beta=p+\zeta-\ell\), and kernel \[ \mathcal B(v)=\frac{2\pi i}{e^{2\pi iv}-1}. \tag{39} \] The only poles in this rectangle are the integer samples \(0,\ldots,K-\ell\). In particular, the negative poles of \(\mathscr F_N(v+\ell-a)\) are at \(v=a-\ell-1-m\), all to the left. The denominator arguments in (38) stay within their zero-free first strips; no hidden outer family is crossed. Horizontal sides vanish at fixed \(N\). The total factorial shift difference in (38) is \(N-2\). Below, including \(Q^v\) and (39), the net decay is \(e^{-2\pi|\Im v|/N}\); above it is the same. Therefore, with both integrals upward, \[ S_{N,a}=\sum_{k=0}^{\ell-1}R_k+ R_\ell(J_{\rm right}-J_{\rm left}),\qquad J_{\rm line}=\frac1{2\pi i}\int_{\rm line}\mathcal B(v)T_N(v)\,dv . \tag{40} \] This is finite, and retains the right connector explicitly. ## 7. Central estimate, macroscopic tails, and right connector On the left line, uniformly for \(|\Im v|\le\epsilon N\), (10)--(13) give \[ T_N(v)=e^{i\pi v}\chi^v \frac{\Gamma(v+\ell+1-a)\Gamma(\ell+1)} {\Gamma(\ell+1-a)\Gamma(v+\ell+1)} \exp\{O((1+|v|)^2/N)\}. \tag{41} \] The logarithm of \(\mathcal R(r)\) here is \(i\pi+\log\chi\), fixed by the canonical factorials. The model Barnes integrand has bound \(C(1+|\Im v|)^C e^{-\pi|\Im v|}\). Choose \(\epsilon\) small enough that the error exponential in (41) is absorbed by half of this decay. Its integrated error is then \(O(N^{-1})\), by \[ \frac C N\int_{\mathbb R}(1+|T|)^C e^{-\pi|T|/2}\,dT . \tag{42} \] Here are quantitative majorants for both remaining infinite pieces. For \(v=\gamma+iNY,\ |Y|\ge\epsilon\), the exact bounds (10)--(11), with the continued endpoint branches, give \[ |\mathcal B(v)T_N(v)| \le C N^C e^{N\mathcal V(Y)}e^{-\pi|Y|}. \tag{43} \] To verify the integrable last factor, the fixed-shift amplitude of the two macroscopic numerator factors relative to the two denominators is \(e^{2\pi(a-2)|Y|}\) below. The light factorial ratio supplies \(e^{-2\pi a|Y|}\), and \(Q^v\) supplies \(e^{2\pi|Y|}\). The Barnes kernel's exponential \(e^{-2\pi N|Y|}\) is already in \(\mathcal V\). Their remaining product is exactly \(e^{-2\pi|Y|}\). Above only \(Q^v\) has a nonconstant limiting modulus and gives the same decay. Full-strip Stirling errors are uniformly bounded. Replacing \(2\pi\) by \(\pi\) absorbs bounded-height transitions, uniformly for the bounded shifts and angles. This proves (43) with an integrable majorant after the \(N^C\) factor. Equations (36), (43) bound this left tail by \(C N^C e^{-\delta_\epsilon N}\). On the right line, write \(v=p+\zeta-\ell+iNY\). The two numerator arguments in (38) become \(N+a+\zeta-1+iNY\) and \(N+C+\zeta+iNY\). Apply (7) once to each. They contribute two periodic numerator factors. The denominator arguments are \(N(1-b)+\zeta+1/2+iNY\) and its \(c\)-analogue. Let \(R_0\) be the rate in the proof of (22). The resulting rates, including (39) and normalization by the central factorials, are \[ \mathcal W(Y)= \begin{cases} R_0(Y)-M,&Y\ge0,\\ R_0(Y)-2\pi Y-M,&Y\le0 . \end{cases} \tag{44} \] The argument computation in (23) gives \[ R_0'(Y)=T(Y)\quad(Y>0),\qquad R_0'(Y)=\pi+T(Y)\quad(Y<0),\qquad 0<T(Y)<\pi. \tag{45} \] Both \(R_0(Y)\) above and \(R_0(Y)-2\pi Y\) below increase toward the same end value \(h_0\), when moving away from zero. Consequently \(\mathcal W(Y)\le h_0-M\le-\delta\). The fixed-shift amplitude count on this line is again \(e^{2\pi(a-2)|Y|}\), from the two shifted numerators and denominators; the light ratio and \(Q^v\) complete it to \(e^{-2\pi|Y|}\). Its two periodic factors, with the Barnes kernel, supply exactly the macroscopic correction in (44). For \(|Y|\ge\epsilon\), (10)--(11) therefore give \[ |\mathcal B(v)T_N(v)| \le C N^C e^{-N(M-h_0)}e^{-\pi|Y|}. \tag{46} \] For \(|Y|\le\epsilon\), the sole endpoint numerator has bounded real shift greater than \(-1\). Its Gamma product, or comparison with the exact half-step formula [P, equation (35)], costs at most \(N^C(1+N|Y|)^C e^{C|Y|}\). The remaining factors use (10). Their rate is still (44). Thus this finite interval is bounded by \(C N^C e^{-N(M-h_0)}\) after increasing the polynomial power. Integration, with \(dv=iN\,dY\), proves \[ |J_{\rm right}| \le C N^C e^{-\delta N}. \tag{47} \] The connector is exponentially negligible relative to the central packet, even though it need not be polynomial before normalization. The model left integral is elementary. Using \(\Gamma(-v)\Gamma(v+1)=-\pi/\sin\pi v\), (41) gives \[ -J_{\rm left}= \frac1{2\pi i}\int_{\gamma-i\infty}^{\gamma+i\infty} \frac{\Gamma(-v)\Gamma(v+\ell+1-a)\Gamma(\ell+1)\Gamma(v+1)} {\Gamma(\ell+1-a)\Gamma(v+\ell+1)} \,\chi^v\,dv+O(N^{-1}) =\ell\int_0^1(1-x)^{\ell-1}(1+\chi x)^{a-\ell-1}\,dx +O(N^{-1}). \tag{48} \] For a direct proof of the last equality, first close the ordinary Gamma Barnes contour at \(|\chi x|<1\) and sum its binomial residues; the exponentially convergent vertical integral continues this identity to positive \(\chi x\). Integrating in \(x\) is justified by \(\gamma>-1\). The Gamma parameter \(\ell+1-a\) is at least one. Thus there is no restriction \(\chi<1\), and the same contour works through every integer \(a\). Taylor's integral remainder gives the exact model identity \[ \sum_{k=0}^{\ell-1}r_k+ r_\ell\ell\int_0^1(1-x)^{\ell-1}(1+\chi x)^{a-\ell-1}\,dx =(1+\chi)^{a-1}. \] Combining this with (37), (40), (47)--(48) proves \[ S_{N,a}=(1+\chi)^{a-1}(1+O(N^{-1})). \tag{49} \] The model is positive and bounded away from zero uniformly on our compact parameters. At \(a=1\), (49) is the exact identity \(S_{N,1}=1\). ## 8. Prefactor, source-relative error, and scope The pole-free ratio (28) and (10), (12) give \[ \frac{\mathcal G_a}{\mathcal G_1} =\frac{N^{2a-2}}{\Gamma(a)^2} \left(\frac{\sin\pi R}{\pi}\right)^{2a-2} (1+O(N^{-1})). \tag{50} \] To check its phase, the two macroscopic ratios give \((1-r^{-1})^a(1-r)^{a-1}\); the small factorial is \((-2\pi i/N)^{a-1}\Gamma(a)(1+O(N^{-1}))\). Use the canonical arguments \(\arg(1-r)=\pi u-\pi/2\), \(\arg(1-r^{-1})=-\arg(1-r)\), and \(-r(1-r^{-1})/(1-r)=1\). The phase of \(q^{(N-a)(1-a)}\) cancels the remaining endpoint phase. This gives the positive factor in (50), not just its modulus. By (10) and (30), \(|\mathcal G_1|\ge N^{-C}e^{NM}\). Equations (22), (27), (49)--(50), with \(M>h_0>0\), now control the error relative to the actual geometric source. In particular \(\Phi_1/\mathcal G_1=1+O(N^Ce^{-NM})\). Finally \[ 1+\chi=\frac{\sin\pi b\sin\pi c} {\sin\pi(u-b)\sin\pi(u-c)} \tag{51} \] follows directly from (34). Equations (49)--(51) prove (5). No estimate of a weighted signed sum has been substituted for the retained packet/current decomposition. This theorem supplies only the displayed small-angle boundary data. It does not itself propagate a generic offset to a fixed positive boundary angle, cross a fold, initialize another prism face, or control an arbitrary attached short component. No knot-volume or finite-exception conclusion is asserted. The complete direct proof sources are: | Label | Complete source | SHA-256 | |---|---|---| | B | notes/research_four_coherent_boundary_polynomial_source.md | 93241074830ff4b844ba5baafd06a15bf08ec6bddc3a1498727f110ebe297d84 | | P | notes/research_centered_tensor_full_prism_source_transport.md | eb43e287eca5933b70de3b6362a81f92d46bb2e121f0eb5716793c107adaef10 | Both entire matching proof texts were read. Only written mathematics and text reads, edits and hashes were used. No mathematical programs, tests, numerical experiments, builds or git operations were run. This research proof is author-final.

title: Fractional boundary data with an original crossing leaf
text:
# Fractional boundary data with an original crossing leaf 22 November 2026. Written research proof. Earlier author-final notes and public manuscripts remain unchanged. We put one coherent input exactly at zero, where it is the original positive crossing element divided by \(\sqrt N\). The fractional boundary packet then has two numerator families instead of three. Its infinite upper end has a nonzero limiting rate. We retain that end and prove a relative estimate only where it has a strict gap. The result supplies two adjacent initial values on every fractional boundary orbit in this region. ## 1. Original source and statement Use the full Frobenius algebra and centered basis of [B]: \[  egin{gathered} N\ge2,\quad d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\quad \eta=(-1)^d,\quad\kappa=e^{\pi i d^2/(2N)},\ U_x=\sum_{j=0}^d x^jf_j,\qquad U_0=f_0=R^+/\sqrt N . \end{gathered} 	ag{1} \] No quotient of the repeated-root directions is taken. The functional \(\phi\), multiplication and all phase carriers are the original ones. Write \[ \mathcal L(v)=\int_0^v\log|2\sin\pi t|\,dt , \] extended oddly and periodically. Fix a compact set in \[ c,R>0,\qquad c+R<1,\qquad \Delta=\mathcal L(c+R)-\mathcal L(R)>0 . 	ag{2} \] This is an open nonempty region; for example \(1/6<R<c+R<5/6\) implies its last inequality. Define \[  egin{gathered} z=-e^{-2\pi ic},\quad r=e^{-2\pi iR},\quad p=NR,\quad L=N-p,\quad a\in\mathcal A=[a_-,a_+]\Subset(0,\infty),\ s_a=-e^{-2\pi i(a-1/2)/N},\quad t_a=r/s_a,\qquad \Phi_a^0=\phi(f_0U_zU_{s_a}U_{t_a}),\ M_0=\mathcal L(c+R)-\mathcal L(c)-\mathcal L(R)>0,\ g_0=e^{-\pi iR}  rac{\sin^2(\pi R)\sin(\pi c)} {\pi^2\sin(\pi(c+R))}. \end{gathered} 	ag{3} \] The strict positivity of \(M_0\) follows by fixing \(c\): its derivative in \(R\) is \(\log[\sin\pi(c+R)/\sin\pi R]\), which changes from positive to negative once, and its values at \(R=0,1-c\) are zero. All constants below are uniform on the chosen compact sets. Enlarge \(\mathcal A\) to contain \(1\), if necessary. **Theorem.** For all sufficiently large \(N\), the actual scalar \(\Phi_1^0\) is nonzero and \[  oxed{\quad  rac{\Phi_a^0}{\Phi_1^0} = rac{N^{2a-2}}{\Gamma(a)^2} g_0^{\,a-1}(1+O(N^{-1})). \quad} 	ag{4} \] Here \(\log g_0\) has imaginary part \(-\pi R\). In particular, this whole fractional boundary layer is nonzero. The baseline is exactly the original three-input source \[ \Phi_1^0=\kappa\sqrt N\,\mathcal C_N(0,z,-qr). 	ag{5} \] The norm of \(f_0\) is one and the other three coherent inputs have norm \(\sqrt N\). Normalizing all four inputs divides (4)'s two scalars by \(N^{3/2}\). Replacing \(f_0\) by \(R^+\) multiplies both by \(\sqrt N\). Neither operation changes (4). The statement includes both parities, composite levels and all internal first Hermite normals. It makes no assertion outside (2). ## 2. Exact finite source and retained moving poles Write \(\mathscr F=\mathscr F_N\) for the canonical factorial of [F, section 2]. We use its proved identities \[  egin{gathered} \mathscr F(j)=(Q;Q)_j,\quad \mathscr F(w+1)=(1-Q^{w+1})\mathscr F(w),\ \mathscr F(w+N)=(1-e^{2\pi iw})\mathscr F(w),\ \mathscr F(w)\mathscr F(d-w)=Nq^{w(w-d)},\qquad \mathscr F'(N+k)=-2\pi i\,\mathscr F(k)\quad(0\le k<N). \end{gathered} 	ag{6} \] Let \(f,h\) be its canonical Stirling functions. Thus \[ f'(w)=\operatorname{Log}(1-e^{2\pi iw}),\quad \Re f(v)=\mathcal L(v),\quad h(w)^2=i(1-e^{2\pi iw}), 	ag{7} \] and, uniformly on full strict vertical strips and bounded real shifts, \[ \mathscr F(Nw+	au) =\sqrt N\,h(w)(1-e^{2\pi iw})^	au e^{Nf(w)}(1+O(N^{-1})). 	ag{8} \] The endpoint half-lines and Gamma comparisons needed below are also proved in [F, section 2]. In particular, for bounded real part greater than \(-1\) and \(|\Im v|\le\epsilon N\), \[ \mathscr F(v)=(-2\pi i/N)^v\Gamma(v+1) \exp\{O((1+|v|)^2/N)\}. 	ag{9} \] All branches here are the canonical ones, not new principal choices on the negative imaginary endpoint half-line. Put \[  egin{gathered} B=N(1-c)-	frac12,\qquad D=L-Nc+	frac12,\ W_0(w)= rac{\mathscr F(w)\mathscr F(B)} {\mathscr F(w+1+B)},\ K_a(w)=  rac{\mathscr F(w+a-1)} {\mathscr F(a-1)\mathscr F(w)}  rac{\mathscr F(w+p-a)\mathscr F(p)} {\mathscr F(p-a)\mathscr F(w+p)},\qquad T_a(w)=Q^wW_0(w)K_a(w). \end{gathered} 	ag{10} \] Specializing the exact finite formula [B, equations (9)--(10)] at its first coherent parameter equal to zero gives \[ \Phi_a^0= rac{\kappa^2D_N(z)G_N(r)}N \sum_{j=0}^dT_a(j),\qquad D_N(z)=1-\eta z^N,\quad G_N(r)=\sum_{j=0}^dr^j . 	ag{11} \] Equivalently the finite sum in (11) has terms \[ T_a(j)=  rac{Q^j(Q^a,Q^{1-a}/r;Q)_j} {(1+qz)(-q^3z,Q/r;Q)_j}. 	ag{12} \] As throughout [B], quotients at exceptional parameters have their polynomial interpretation. We first prove contour identities off collisions and then continue the canceled identities. Choose \(\zeta\) exactly as in [F]: if \(\delta_*=\min(1/8,a_-/8)\), choose \(\zeta\in\{-\delta_*,-3\delta_*\}\) with \(\operatorname{dist}(p+\zeta,\mathbb Z)\ge\delta_*/2\). Then \(\zeta>-a_-\), and put \(K=\lfloor p+\zetafloor\). The sample-preserving differential is \[ \Omega_a(w)= rac{\kappa^2G_N(r)}N\,2\pi i  rac{1-\eta z^N	au}{	au-1}T_a(w)\,dw, \qquad 	au=e^{2\pi iw}. 	ag{13} \] Use \(\zeta<\Re w<N+\zeta\). Its periodic numerator cancels the entire old outer family from \(\mathscr F(w+1+B)\). The remaining moving poles are exactly \[ w=L+k,\qquad 0\le k\le K . 	ag{14} \] They are the first zero block of \(\mathscr F(w+p)\). The first negative pole of \(\mathscr F(w+a-1)\) is \(-a\), to the left; the other numerator poles are farther left. There is no second zero block inside this width-\(N\) rectangle. The horizontal sides vanish. After cancellation of \(\mathscr F(w)\), the numerator-minus-denominator shift sum in \(T_a\) is \(-N(1-c)-3/2\). Below, including \(Q^w\), the decay is \[ e^{-2\pi(1-c)|\Im w|}e^{-\pi|\Im w|/N}. 	ag{15} \] The degree-one periodic numerator divided by \(	au-1\) is bounded there. Above, the decay is \(e^{-2\pi|\Im w|/N}\). Thus no additional periodic denominator or pole orbit is needed. For completeness set \(Z=z^N,ho=r^{-N},a_0=e^{2\pi ia}\). The exact monodromy is \[  rac{T_a(w+N)}{T_a(w)} = rac{(1-a_0	au)(1-ho	au/a_0)} {(1-\eta Z	au)(1-ho	au)} . 	ag{16} \] Consequently the whole paired vertical current is \[  egin{split} I_a^0={}& rac{\kappa^2G_N(r)}N \int_{\zeta-i\infty}^{\zeta+i\infty}  rac{	au(A_a+B_a	au)}{(	au-1)(1-ho	au)} T_a(w)\,dw,\ A_a={}&\eta Z+ho-a_0-ho/a_0,\qquad B_a=ho(1-\eta Z). \end{split} 	ag{17} \] The coefficient \(B_a\) in this display is distinct from the factorial argument \(B\). Its numerator is never divided out. ## 3. The current is polynomial and the geometric baseline grows Here are explicit rate bounds, including the infinite ends. Set \( eta=1-c\). The rate of \(W_0(\zeta+iNY)\) is \[ R_0(Y)=\Re[f(iY)+f( eta)-f( eta+iY)],\qquad R_0(0)=0. 	ag{18} \] The endpoint value uses the canonical continuation in (8)--(9). For \(k=e^{-2\pi Y}\) put \(Z_k=1-ke^{-2\pi ic}\), with its continuous argument in \((-\pi,\pi)\). Direct differentiation gives \[ R_0'(Y)=  egin{cases} \arg Z_k,&Y>0,\ \pi+\arg Z_k,&Y<0, \end{cases} \quad R_0(+\infty)=-\mathcal L(c),\qquad R_0(Y)<0\quad(Y<0). 	ag{19} \] Above, the sign of the derivative is the sign of \(\sin2\pi c\). Below, \(\pi+\arg Z_k\) is uniformly positive on compact \(c\)-sets. In particular \[ R_0(Y)\le\max(0,-\mathcal L(c))\quad(Y\in\mathbb R). 	ag{20} \] The kernel in (17) has bound \(Ce^{-2\pi NY}\) above and \(C\) below. Since \(|\arg Z_k|<\pi\), its upper rate is at most \(-\pi Y\); its lower rate is at most \(-c_K|Y|\) for a compact-dependent \(c_K>0\). Bounded-shift comparisons (8)--(9) cost only a power of \(N\) and a fixed polynomial in \(|Y|\) on the finite transition interval. At infinity their powers can be counted directly: above \(Q^wK_1(w)\) gives \(e^{-2\pi Y}\); below the residual amplitude is \(e^{\pi Y}\). Thus (17) has a quantitative integrable majorant \[ C N^C(1+|Y|)^C e^{-c_KN|Y|+C|Y|}. 	ag{21} \] The small fixed-shift deformation from \(a=1\) has the same bound, by (8)--(9). This proves \(I_a^0=O(N^C)\). Using every residue in (14), (6) gives the exact identity \[  egin{gathered} \Phi_a^0=\mathcal G_a^0 S_{N,a}^0+I_a^0,\qquad S_{N,a}^0=\sum_{k=0}^K R_k,\ R_k= rac{Q^k(Q^{1-a},rQ^a;Q)_k} {(Q,-q^3rz;Q)_k},\qquad \mathcal G_1^0=  rac{\kappa^2\mathscr F(B)\mathscr F(L)}{\mathscr F(D)},\  rac{\mathcal G_a^0}{\mathcal G_1^0} =- rac r{1-r} rac{\mathscr F(p)}{\mathscr F(p-a)}  rac{\mathscr F(L+a-1)}{\mathscr F(L)}  rac{q^{(N-a)(1-a)}}{\mathscr F(a-1)^2}. \end{gathered} 	ag{22} \] The source sign follows from the negative derivative in (6) and moving the moving-pole residues to the other side of the rectangle. Before simplification the \(k=0\) factor contains \((1-e^{-2\pi ia})\mathscr F(-a)\); replace it by \(\mathscr F(N-a)\), and then reflect with (6). Also cancel \(G_N(r)/(r^N-1)=-1/(1-r)\). This proves (22) without poles at positive integer \(a\) or \(r^N=1\). The sole old outer family was canceled before residues were computed, so collisions with it also have their full family continuation. All macroscopic arguments \(B,L,D,p\), with their bounded shifts, stay strictly between \(0\) and \(N\). Equation (8) therefore gives \[ |\mathcal G_1^0|\asymp\sqrt N\,e^{NM_0}. 	ag{23} \] At \(a=1\), \(R_0=1\) and \(R_k=0\) for \(k>0\); here \(R_0\) denotes the packet coefficient, not the rate (18). Consequently the baseline actual source differs from the geometric term by the retained polynomial current. Formula (23) and \(M_0>0\) prove its nonvanishing. The exact three-input identity is (5); the Gamma quotient alone is not substituted for that actual source. ## 4. The left packet has a strict upper-end gap The central packet ratio is \[ \mathscr R(v)= rac{1-v}{1+zv},\qquad \chi=-\mathscr R(r) =-e^{\pi ic} rac{\sin\pi R}{\sin\pi(c+R)},\qquad 1+\chi=e^{-\pi iR} rac{\sin\pi c}{\sin\pi(c+R)}. 	ag{24} \] Thus \(\arg\chi=-\pi(1-c)\), uniformly away from the negative-real cut on the chosen compact set. The branch of \(\log\mathscr R(r)\) is \(i\pi+\log\chi\), of imaginary part \(\pi c\). The last expression in (24) has argument \(-\pi R\). Write \(u=1-R,
u=1-R-c\). The normalized left-line rate is \[ V(Y)=\Re[f(u+iY)-f(
u+iY)-f(u)+f(
u)] +2\pi Y\,1_{\{Y<0\}}. 	ag{25} \] Its value at zero is zero, while its upper end is \[ V(+\infty)=-\Delta<0 . 	ag{26} \] To control the entire line, let \(k=e^{-2\pi Y}\) and \[ \mathscr R_k=  rac{1-ke^{-2\pi iR}}{1-ke^{-2\pi i(R+c)}} . \] At \(k=1\) its continued argument is \(\pi c\), and \[ \operatorname{Im}\mathscr R_k = rac{2k\sin\pi c\,[k\cos\pi c-\cos\pi(2R+c)]} {|1-ke^{-2\pi i(R+c)}|^2}. 	ag{27} \] For \(0<k<1\) there is at most one zero of this imaginary part. If it occurs, it is on the positive real axis: for \(k<1\) both \(1-ke^{-2\pi iR}\) and \(1-ke^{-2\pi i(R+c)}\) lie in the open right half-plane, so their argument difference cannot equal \(\pm\pi\). The affine numerator in (27) is positive at \(k=1\); a crossing as \(k\) decreases can only change its sign from positive to negative. Thus as \(Y\) increases the argument changes from positive to negative there. Since \(V'=-\arg\mathscr R_k\), this is a minimum, never a maximum. Otherwise \(V\) is decreasing. These assertions also follow directly when \(\cos\pi c=0\). For \(k>1\), the continued argument stays in \((0,2\pi)\), tending to \(2\pi c\): at any real crossing the real numerator after clearing the denominator in (27) is \(1-k^2<0\), so no positive-real crossing can leave that argument interval. Hence \(V'=2\pi-\arg\mathscr R_k>0\) below zero. Together with (26), this proves \[ V(Y)<0\ (Y
e0),\qquad \sup_{|Y|\ge\epsilon}V(Y)\le-\delta_\epsilon<0 . 	ag{28} \] The last bound is uniform on the fixed compact sets. Below, \(V\) also decreases at least linearly toward negative infinity. The condition \(\Delta>0\) is used exactly at the upper infinite end; it has not been inferred merely from \(M_0>0\). ## 5. Finite Barnes evaluation, with the right connector retained Choose an integer \(\ell\ge a_+\). For fixed \(0\le k\le\ell\), \[ R_k=r_k+O(N^{-1}),\qquad r_k= rac{(1-a)_k(-\chi)^k}{k!} = inom{a-1}{k}\chi^k . 	ag{29} \] This holds uniformly at the integer zeros of the finite products. Remove the first \(\ell\) terms and define explicitly \[ T_N(v)=Q^v  rac{\mathscr F(v+\ell-a)\mathscr F(\ell)} {\mathscr F(\ell-a)\mathscr F(v+\ell)}  rac{\mathscr F(L+a+\ell-1+v)}{\mathscr F(L+a+\ell-1)}  rac{\mathscr F(D+\ell)}{\mathscr F(D+\ell+v)}. 	ag{30} \] Then \(R_{k+\ell}=R_\ell T_N(k)\), including when \(R_\ell=0\); the displayed interpolation is not defined by division by that coefficient. With \(\gamma=-1/4,\  eta_N=p+\zeta-\ell\), use \(\mathcal B(v)=2\pi i/(e^{2\pi iv}-1)\) on the rectangle \(\gamma<\Re v< eta_N\). Its only poles are samples \(0,\ldots,K-\ell\). The first negative pole of the light numerator is at \(a-\ell-1\le-1\). The other numerator poles are farther left. Both denominator zero blocks start strictly to the right of this rectangle. The numerator-minus-denominator shift sum is \(Nc-3/2\). Below, the Barnes kernel and \(Q^v\) leave decay \[ e^{-2\pi(1-c)|\Im v|}e^{-\pi|\Im v|/N}; 	ag{31} \] above the decay is \(e^{-2\pi|\Im v|/N}\). Thus the exact finite identity, with both vertical integrals upward, is \[  egin{gathered} S_{N,a}^0=\sum_{k=0}^{\ell-1}R_k+ R_\ell(J_{m right}-J_{m left}),\ J_{m line}= rac1{2\pi i}\int_{m line} \mathcal B(v)T_N(v)\,dv . \end{gathered} 	ag{32} \] On the central left line, for \(|\Im v|\le\epsilon N\), (8)--(9) give \[ T_N(v)=e^{i\pi v}\chi^v  rac{\Gamma(v+\ell+1-a)\Gamma(\ell+1)} {\Gamma(\ell+1-a)\Gamma(v+\ell+1)} \exp\{O((1+|v|)^2/N)\}. 	ag{33} \] After multiplication by \(\mathcal B\), the model is bounded by \(C(1+|\Im v|)^C e^{-\delta|\Im v|}\), uniformly since \(-\pi<\arg\chi<0\). Choose \(\epsilon\) sufficiently small. The error exponential is absorbed by half this decay, and its integrated error is \(O(N^{-1})\). For \(v=\gamma+iNY,\ |Y|\ge\epsilon\), full-strip estimates give the quantitative bound \[ |\mathcal B(v)T_N(v)| \le C N^C e^{NV(Y)}  egin{cases} e^{-\pi Y},&Y\ge\epsilon,\ e^{\pi Y/2},&Y\le-\epsilon . \end{cases} 	ag{34} \] Here is the fixed-shift count behind the integrable factors. Above, all factorial height amplitudes tend to constants and \(Q^v\) supplies \(e^{-2\pi Y}\). Below, the light ratio supplies \(e^{2\pi aY}\), the macroscopic shifted ratio supplies \(e^{-2\pi(a-3/2)Y}\), and \(Q^v\) supplies \(e^{-2\pi Y}\). Their product is \(e^{\pi Y}\). The Barnes exponential below is already included in (25). Reducing these decay constants by one half absorbs bounded-height transitions and uniformly bounded Stirling remainders. Equations (28), (34) bound this whole left tail by \(CN^Ce^{-\delta_\epsilon N}\), including \(dv=iN\,dY\). The right line has \(v=p+\zeta-\ell+iNY\). Its sole macroscopic numerator crossing \(N\) is \(\mathscr F(N+a+\zeta-1+iNY)\). Shift it once by \(N\) using (6). Above its periodic factor has zero rate; below its rate is \(-2\pi Y\), exactly canceled by the Barnes kernel's rate \(2\pi Y\). The remaining normalized rate on **both** half-lines is therefore \[ R_0(Y)-M_0 . 	ag{35} \] By (20) it is at most \[ -\gamma_0,\qquad \gamma_0=\min(M_0,M_0+\mathcal L(c)) =\min(M_0,\Delta)>0 . 	ag{36} \] For \(|Y|\ge\epsilon\), the same fixed-shift count as in (34) gives its integrable majorant with \(e^{-\gamma_0N}\) in place of \(e^{NV}\). For \(|Y|\le\epsilon\), the sole endpoint numerator has real shift \(a+\zeta-1>-1\); (9) and its fixed-shift Gamma comparison give a cost \(N^C(1+N|Y|)^Ce^{C|Y|}\). The remaining factors use (8), still with rate (35). Thus the whole connector satisfies \[ |J_{m right}| \le CN^Ce^{-\gamma_0N}. 	ag{37} \] This is a relative exponential gap, not an assertion that the un-normalized connector is a polynomial error. The central model evaluates without a restriction on \(|\chi|\). Reflection of the ordinary Gamma factor gives \[  egin{split} -J_{m left} &= rac1{2\pi i}\int_{\gamma-i\infty}^{\gamma+i\infty}  rac{\Gamma(-v)\Gamma(v+\ell+1-a)\Gamma(\ell+1)\Gamma(v+1)} {\Gamma(\ell+1-a)\Gamma(v+\ell+1)} \chi^v\,dv+O(N^{-1})\ &=\ell\int_0^1(1-x)^{\ell-1} (1+\chi x)^{a-\ell-1}\,dx+O(N^{-1}). \end{split} 	ag{38} \] First prove this at \(|\chi|<1\) by the ordinary binomial residues and the beta integral. Continue the identity through the lower half-plane, where the Gamma Barnes integral has uniform vertical decay on compact sets. The Euler integral has its usual larger domain \(\mathbb C\setminus(-\infty,-1]\). Our \(\chi\) stays in a compact subset of the lower half-plane, so this proves (38) with its specified branch. Taylor's integral remainder now gives \[ \sum_{k=0}^{\ell-1}r_k+ r_\ell\ell\int_0^1(1-x)^{\ell-1}(1+\chi x)^{a-\ell-1}\,dx =(1+\chi)^{a-1}. 	ag{39} \] No division by an integer-zero coefficient occurs. Combining (29), (32)--(39) proves \[ S_{N,a}^0=(1+\chi)^{a-1}(1+O(N^{-1})). 	ag{40} \] The model is complex but bounded away from zero on our compact sets, and at \(a=1\) the packet identity is exactly one. ## 6. Prefactor, source-relative error, and scope The pole-free amplitude ratio in (22), with (8)--(9), is exactly the one evaluated in [F]. For clarity, its two macroscopic factors give \((1-r^{-1})^a(1-r)^{a-1}\); the endpoint factor is \[ \mathscr F(a-1)=(-2\pi i/N)^{a-1}\Gamma(a)(1+O(N^{-1})). \] Use \(-r(1-r^{-1})/(1-r)=1\). The remaining endpoint phase is canceled by \(q^{(N-a)(1-a)}\). Consequently \[  rac{\mathcal G_a^0}{\mathcal G_1^0} = rac{N^{2a-2}}{\Gamma(a)^2} \left( rac{\sin\pi R}{\pi}ight)^{2a-2} (1+O(N^{-1})). 	ag{41} \] Equations (21)--(23), (40)--(41) control every error relative to the growing actual baseline. The packet contributes the factor \((1+\chi)^{a-1}\), whose phase is \(-\pi R(a-1)\), by (24). This proves (4), including its full phase, not just its modulus. The prefactor and current identities continue through integer \(a\), the roots \(r^N=1\), and all old outer-pole collisions. The strict upper-end loss in (26) is essential to this proof. No result is claimed when \(\Delta\le0\), nor is a signed packet replaced by its termwise modulus. The result is boundary-layer data for a literal crossing-leaf observation. It does not by itself transport to a fixed positive boundary angle, evaluate an arbitrary short component, or prove a knot-volume or finite-exception theorem. The complete direct proof texts are: | Label | Complete source | SHA-256 | |---|---|---| | B | notes/research_four_coherent_boundary_polynomial_source.md | 93241074830ff4b844ba5baafd06a15bf08ec6bddc3a1498727f110ebe297d84 | | F | notes/research_four_coherent_fractional_boundary_source.md | 8126481cadaa4b1b0ba287495de14cb3263baf8343fbfca9aa4d5b6d962595b1 | Both entire matching proof texts are retained at their renewed pins. The earlier zero-radius three-input source is already treated in research_single_leg_radial_turn_source.md; the present proof computes the additional fractional four-input packet and both of its currents. Only written mathematics and text operations were used.

title: Fourier lower bounds and almost-invariant vectors
text: # Fourier lower bounds and almost-invariant vectors Research note, updated 4 November 2026. There are two different uses of a positive norm in this problem. For the complete-color Fourier state, its norm differs from the squared Kashaev invariant by a proved polynomial remainder. A lower bound for that norm would therefore prove a lower bound for the invariant. For the positive sums obtained by replacing local terms by their absolute values, the available comparison goes in the other direction. Positivity of the comparison sum does not supply the missing lower bound. There is now an actual initial family for changing the Fourier charge. The [small-charge theorem](research_small_charge_path_source.md) proves a nonzero leading contribution for every fixed positive path with crossing powers at least three, after inserting \(T_{N-j_v}(-w_v/2)\) in its original traces and taking \(j_v/N\in[1/640,1/320]\). The coefficient is computed from the exact trace contour; every competing charge and endpoint term is bounded. Continuing this coefficient to \(j_v=N\), where the insertions disappear, remains the lower-bound problem. A nonzero starting contribution and a continuous geometric critical point do not themselves prove that continuation. On \([1/4000,1/2000]\), the statement extends to any fixed finite graph carrying these edge kernels, with no isolated selected vertex, and allows arbitrary fixed signed integer crossing powers, including zero. Section 16 verifies the Gaussian analogue of almost-invariance for this initialized source: its rescaled integrand has a nonzero independently computed norm and an \(O(N^{-1/2})\) relative annihilation residual. These estimates currently hold on the small charge box; a knot realization of an arbitrary such graph is not part of the assertion. The [exact charge recurrence](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_current_free_aw_crossing_transport.md#10-a-closed-recurrence-for-the-original-charge-observations) retains the free boundary color and has nonvanishing outer coefficients. With the physical period and reflection relations imposed, its solution space has dimension two at every free color. The original endpoint condition selects the actual source line. The extra solution has zero physical values and only first-normal data. This removes an ambiguity in the finite equation, but line uniqueness does not bound a particular Fourier observation of that line. The [charge-increment norm](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_charge_increment_graph_norm.md) now gives an exact positive identity and a sharp asymptotic for every fixed graph carrying these same-index kernels. Its increments discard the normals by an exact period difference, and Parseval removes the unit crossing phases from their squared norm. The resulting growth is the sum of the unfilled edge rates, independent of the twists. For the proved three-crossing terminal source, the central coefficient divided by this norm is exponentially small. The full charge vector therefore has a rigorous lower bound without a corresponding lower bound for its specified central entry. This is an actual-source limitation of this particular positive Fourier norm. There is already a stronger local lower bound in the [all-color theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_all_color_path_normal_bound.md#5-the-complete-normal-determinant-at-every-color-assignment). For a fixed filled tree with crossing powers of one sign, suppose \(Q_G=\operatorname{diag}(|n_v|)-\operatorname{Adj}(G)\) is positive definite. At each physical color assignment, the complete first-normal factor is a determinant with a positive definite imaginary part after the stated normalization. Its modulus is bounded below by a power of \(N\) times the positive kernel product, and bounded above at polynomial additional cost. Thus cancellation within one color assignment is already controlled under this condition. The outstanding cancellation is between different assignments, which retain their original crossing and determinant phases. The tree determinant estimate is an established input, not a new consequence of the charge-increment calculation. The [explicit source reconstruction](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_physical_normal_lift.md) connects these facts for one charged edge with real free color. The period increment determines its double-node values by inverse Fourier transformation. A final Jacobi recurrence recovers the odd simple node, and the existing relative normal formula reconstructs all derivatives with polynomial cost. The resulting map from the increment vector to all original charge observations has polynomial operator norm. Its particular closing row can still be exponentially small on the source; the positive norm theorem supplies an example. The positivity now extends to an exact boundary problem with a complex geometric free color. The [cosine-phase maximum principle](research_geometric_phase_maximum_principle.md) places every such color in \(\Re w<7/4\) along the positive-path charge cube. For \(N\ge16\), the ordinary Jacobi inverse has norm at most \(5\). Its [Fourier image](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_physical_jacobi_charge_boundary.md) is coercive in an explicit positive metric of condition number at most \(N/2\), with the original endpoint forcing. A Ward representative bounds the first normals by a polynomial in \(N\) inside subsequent original traces, preserving the mixed derivatives. This is a positive transport equation; its closing row is still the original signed observation. The [Riccati estimate](research_physical_row_riccati_transport.md) also proves a nonzero local transport factor directly from the normalized physical solution. Its consecutive ratios contract in a right half-plane and approach the growing root uniformly, even with complex free color. The product over an interior row interval has the original edge-phase difference as exponent, with a factor bounded above and below independently of \(N\). This establishes the local coefficient for physical rows. The endpoint normalization also gives the absolute bound \[ N^{-C}e^{N\Re\psi(\tau_j,u)} \le |K_N(c_j,-2\cos u)| \le N^C e^{N\Re\psi(\tau_j,u)} \] on compact physical-row intervals, uniformly over the stated complex free-color region and for sufficiently large \(N\), after increasing \(C\) if needed. The [endpoint extension](research_last_physical_row_riccati.md) now reaches the last physical row, with logarithmic error and all fixed free-color derivatives. At odd levels this row is the complete color. At even levels the [Chebyshev interpolation argument](research_even_complete_low_kernel.md) proves that the original low-index complete-end kernel divided by the last row is \(1+O(N^{-1/2})\). Its alternating weights have sum one, and the exact row recurrence controls their cancellation. Thus the low complete-end factors have a nonzero holomorphic amplitude of polynomial size at both parities. This still does not estimate their signed trace over the selected colors. The [bare-kernel parity example](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_even_complete_radical_asymptotic.md) shows that the restriction to the low sector matters: at an explicit complex color the full even-level kernel has a strictly larger exponential rate than its odd-level counterpart. This is a kernel evaluation before tracing, not a statement about a knot invariant. This distinction can be tested on the original source itself. The [central-readout polynomial](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_central_readout_half_plane_zeros.md) has a zero in the positive Jacobi half-plane at every level and power. At that zero, the row values remain nonzero and the Jacobi inverses are bounded by one. Hence those two facts alone cannot force a positive overlap with the closing row. The zeros have not been located on the actual geometric locus, so this does not exclude a more specific lower-bound theorem there. The [charge characteristic](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_charge_characteristic_two_mode_block.md) explains a further difficulty with a universal almost-invariance argument. For every positive power at least three, the geometric mode belongs to an isolated two-dimensional block in the interior charge interval. The two moduli cross at charge \(1/2\), and the block collides with additional modes at the endpoints. Its one-step leakage is \(O(N^{-1})\), but faster complementary modes prevent summing that estimate as a relative error. A source-level bound for this transport and the prescribed scalar observation is still needed. The geometric domain needed for a central contour comparison is now known at every actual geometric critical point of a positive path with powers at least three. The [wire-order proof](research_positive_path_real_wire_order.md) keeps that saddle in the original regular factorial chart, using the coupled period equations. The [horizontal-concavity proof](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_positive_path_horizontal_concavity.md) puts the angular saddle inside the rectangle where the reduced phase is strictly concave. For an internal pair with complete outer ends, the full mixed phase has a strictly concave central domain as well. Thus this part of the geometric location problem no longer requires a separate check for each short pair. The [pair-angle theorem](research_internal_pair_angle_bound.md) also places both selected angles below \(\pi/2\) when the outside ends are complete and the two powers are integers at least three. The [complete-edge gap](research_internal_pair_complete_edge_gap.md) sharpens their heights to \(H<107/100\) and proves \(\Re\psi(t,0)-H>1/500\) throughout this smaller angular box. The full complete-end kernel therefore has the same nonzero geometric factor there at both parities. The bare-kernel parity example lies outside this box. There is now a source-level local lower bound for **every fixed such pair**, at both level parities. The [local Gaussian theorem](research_internal_pair_local_gaussian.md) uses the actual complete outside kernels, the exact shared-wire interpolation, and the full double-pole trace factors. The endpoint recurrence supplies the nonzero normalization. After scaling by \(N^{-1/2}\) around the geometric point, the density has a positive limiting norm and relative Gaussian annihilation residual \(O(N^{-1/2})\), using the sharper normalization in Section 7. Its local integral has an explicit nonzero coefficient multiplying \(N^{-3/2}\) at the geometric exponential rate, with a fixed complex neighborhood in both outside colors. Its proof first controls the low-index factors, then bounds the outside radical both locally and after the original traces. This supplies the proposed almost-invariance from actual finite equations. The remaining task is to show that this local piece occurs in the deformation of the whole source and to control its complementary currents. No global lower bound for arbitrary short pairs follows from the local result. The [free-boundary edge theorem](research_pair_free_boundary_kernel.md) now extends each outside edge factor to a fixed complex neighborhood of its complete color. It gives the explicit nonzero coefficient and the full Gaussian expansion of the original finite kernel at both level parities, including ordinary outside-color derivatives. Its whole-real-period estimate and quadratic complex-strip bound also retain ordinary outside normals. These prepare the edge factors needed for composition. They do not choose the joint two-trace cycle or bound its entire complement. The subsequent [finite contour reduction](research_internal_pair_combined_contour_reduction.md) makes that complement explicit: one shared-index contour and two exact folded trace identities give sixteen currents. Its principal local piece has coefficient one, but another current could still cancel its leading term. The [joint endpoint taper](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_internal_pair_endpoint_taper.md) now proves a strict gap for both shared-index endpoint collars, including their trace and wire endpoint currents. The middle interval requires the further comparisons described next. The [angular-tail transport theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_internal_pair_angular_tail_transport.md) now removes the omitted original physical trace rows even after shifting the shared circle to its actual height. Its proof combines nonnegative coefficients in the exact row recurrence with \(2\pi\Im x_*<3/4\) and separate half-band Fourier inversion. The [positive physical Pick form](research_trace_normal_defect_positive_form.md) offers another useful positive observation, with its explicitly chosen adjoint cap. It does not identify that cap with the original one in (94). The full-jet construction therefore gives a natural positive representation, but a lower bound for the original closing still requires its actual antiunitary overlap.

title: The half-charge observation with a free outside color
text: # The half-charge observation with a free outside color Research proof, 4 November 2026. Frozen manuscripts are unchanged. The half-charge observation and its physical normal-defect rows retain their nonzero packets when the complete outside color is replaced by a fixed small complex neighborhood. The input is the literal full Newton kernel. A polynomial interpolation estimate controls it on the whole observation contour; the local free-edge theorem supplies the coefficient only near the saddle. Actual first normals control the omitted physical rows. All outside derivatives below are derivatives in the ordinary spectral color, including at the complete color \(-2\). No conclusion about a global coupled pair coefficient is inferred. ## 1. A whole-contour bound from the actual physical rows Put \[ D=N-1,\qquad J_N=\lfloor(N-1)/2\rfloor,\qquad c_a=2\cos((2a+1)\pi/N),\quad 0\le a\le J_N, \] and retain the original polynomials \[ K_N(w,\zeta)=\sum_{j=0}^{D}e_j(w)e_j(\zeta),\qquad L_N(w,\zeta)=\sum_{j=0}^{J_N}e_j(w)e_j(\zeta),\qquad F_{a,N}(w)=K_N(c_a,w). \tag{1} \] Every omitted \(e_j\) is radical, and vanishes at every distinct physical node. Thus \(L_N(c_a,w)=F_{a,N}(w)\) exactly. Let \(Q_N\) be the monic distinct-node polynomial: \[ Q_N(w)= \begin{cases} 2T_m(w/2),&N=2m,\\ (w+2)\{U_m(w/2)-U_{m-1}(w/2)\},&N=2m+1. \end{cases} \tag{2} \] Its degree is \(J_N+1\). The exact Chebyshev formulas give \[ \|Q_N\|_{[-2,2]}\le4,\qquad |Q_N'(c_a)|^{-1}\le2/N. \tag{3} \] The odd simple node is included in (3). **Lemma 1.** On each compact subset \(\mathcal W\) of \(\Re w<2\), for all large \(N\), \[ |F_{a,N}(w)|\le |F_{J_N,N}(w)| \le C N^A e^{N\Re\Psi(w)}. \tag{4} \] For every fixed ordinary derivative order \(k\), uniformly for \(w\in\mathcal W\) and all \(u\in\mathbb C\), \[ \left|\partial_\zeta^k L_N(w,\zeta) \big|_{\zeta=-2\cos u}\right| \le C_k N^{A+2k+2} e^{N\Re\Psi(w)+J_N|\Im u|}. \tag{5} \] Here \(\Psi(-2\cos t)=\psi(t,0)\) has its original complete constant. *Proof.* The [actual Riccati recurrence](research_physical_row_riccati_transport.md) has positive coefficients in its entire ordinary physical range, including the last row at each parity: \[ \rho_{r+1}=1+\frac{c_0-w}{A_r} +\frac{C_r}{A_r}(1-\rho_r^{-1}),\qquad \rho_1=1+\frac{c_0-w}{A_0},\quad A_r>0,\quad C_r\ge0. \tag{6} \] For large \(N\), \(\Re w<c_0\) on \(\mathcal W\). If \(\Re\rho>1\), then \(\Re(1-\rho^{-1})>0\). Induction therefore gives \(\Re\rho_r>1\), and hence \(|\rho_r|>1\), for the normalized original solution. This proves the first inequality in (4), without selecting a formal recurrence mode. The second is the [last-row logarithmic theorem](research_last_physical_row_riccati.md). The polynomial \(L_N(w,\zeta)\), of degree at most \(J_N\) in \(\zeta\), is exactly the ordinary interpolant of the values \(F_{a,N}(w)\). Its cardinal polynomial is \[ \ell_a(v)=\frac{Q_N(v)}{(v-c_a)Q_N'(c_a)}. \] On the real interval, the mean-value bound and Markov's inequality give \(\|\ell_a\|_\infty\le C N\), using (3). Consequently \[ \|L_N(w,\cdot)\|_{[-2,2]} \le C N^2 |F_{J_N,N}(w)|. \tag{7} \] The same argument applies to complex coefficients, since the cardinal polynomials are real. Markov's inequality costs at most a factor \(C_k N^{2k}\) for \(\partial_\zeta^k\). For a polynomial \(P\) of degree \(d\), the elementary Bernstein ellipse bound is \[ |P(-2\cos u)|\le \|P\|_{[-2,2]}e^{d|\Im u|}. \tag{8} \] It follows by applying the maximum principle to the polynomial in \(z\) obtained from \(z^dP(-z-z^{-1})\); equivalently apply the exterior maximum principle to the reversed polynomial. Equations (4), (7), and (8) prove (5). \(\square\) The original radical Fourier bound and ordinary Markov inequality also give, for every fixed \(k\), \[ \left|\partial_\zeta^k(K_N-L_N)(-2\cos t,-2\cos u)\right| \le C_k N^{A_k} e^{D(|\Im t|+|\Im u|)}. \tag{9} \] Indeed every radical \(e_j\) has real interval norm at most \(\sqrt{N-1}\); apply (8) to its two factors and sum at most \(N\) terms. This retains the full radical, at both parities. Choose a fixed neighborhood of the half-charge observation rectangle \(|\Re t|\le\pi/2,\ |\Im t|\le2/5\). On a sufficiently small such neighborhood, the [complete-edge gap](research_internal_pair_complete_edge_gap.md) and reflection give \(\Re\psi(t,0)>|\Im t|+\delta_0\), for some \(\delta_0>0\). The mapped colors form a compact subset of \(\Re w<2\). Combining (5) and (9) proves the whole-contour estimate \[ \left|\partial_\zeta^k K_N(-2\cos t,\zeta) \big|_{\zeta=-2\cos u}\right| \le C_kN^{A_k} e^{N\{\Re\psi(t,0)+|\Im u|\}}. \tag{10} \] Every fixed derivative in the selected variable has the same exponent and an additional polynomial cost: use Cauchy's formula on radius \(1/N\) inside a slightly larger compact set. This estimate comes from the finite polynomial, not from continuation of a relative complete-end error. ## 2. Original physical tails and their normals Write \(G_{a,N}(\zeta)=\partial_wK_N(c_a,\zeta)\) at a double physical node. For every such \(a\), every fixed \(k\), and all complex \(u\), \[ \begin{split} |\partial_\zeta^kF_{a,N}(-2\cos u)| &\le C_kN^{A_k}F_{a,N}(-2)e^{D|\Im u|},\\ |\partial_\zeta^kG_{a,N}(-2\cos u)| &\le C_kN^{A_k}F_{a,N}(-2)e^{D|\Im u|}. \end{split} \tag{11} \] The first line includes the odd simple node; no original first normal is assigned to that node. Here is a proof of the real bounds needed for (11). Put \(\delta=c_0-\zeta\) and \(\Delta F_r=F_r-F_{r-1}\). The original row recurrence is \[ \Delta F_{r+1}=(C_r/A_r)\Delta F_r+(\delta/A_r)F_r,\qquad F_0=1,\quad \Delta F_1=\delta/A_0. \tag{12} \] It proves that every \(F_r\) has nonnegative coefficients in \(\delta\). Since \(|c_0-\zeta|\le c_0+2\) on \([-2,2]\), one obtains \(|F_a(\zeta)|\le F_a(-2)\) throughout that interval. For the second line, the actual [first-normal estimate, Lemma 5](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_all_color_path_normal_bound.md) gives \[ |G_a(\zeta)|\le N^{11}F_a(\zeta) \le N^{11}F_a(-2),\qquad -2\le\zeta\le c_0. \tag{13} \] It concerns the full original normal. It must not be obtained by differentiating a physical value asymptotic. The missing real interval \([c_0,2]\) has length \(O(N^{-2})\). The affine map of \([-2,c_0]\) to \([-1,1]\) sends its right endpoint \(2\) to \[ 1+\frac{2(2-c_0)}{c_0+2}=1+O(N^{-2}). \] A polynomial of degree at most \(D\) therefore incurs at most \(\exp\{D\operatorname{arcosh}(1+O(N^{-2}))\}=O(1)\) in the Bernstein bound on this small extension. Thus (13), up to a constant, holds in absolute value on all of \([-2,2]\). Ordinary Markov inequalities and (8) now prove both lines of (11), including all fixed outside normals. For the parity-appropriate midpoint cuts \(T_N\to\pi/2\), the positive complete rows and the absolute row normalization give \[ \max_{\tau_a>T_N}F_{a,N}(-2) \le CN^A e^{N\psi(\pi/2,0)},\qquad \tau_a=\arccos(-c_a/2). \tag{14} \] Multiplication by the original Gaussian crossing value changes no physical modulus for real \(n\). Its logarithmic first normal is \(O_n(N^2)\). Consequently (11)–(14) bound the omitted source values and their actual selected first normals by \[ C_kN^{A_k} e^{N\{\psi(\pi/2,0)+|\Im u|\}}. \tag{15} \] All constants are uniform in the physical row. The complete half-charge gap is \(\psi(\pi/2,0)<M_n-7/80\). Thus (15) retains a fixed gap for a sufficiently small fixed outside-color neighborhood. ## 3. The free-outside observation packet Fix an integer \(n\ge3\). Let \(\zeta\) denote the ordinary outside color. Near \(\zeta=-2\), the even analytic functions \(\psi(t,u)\) and \(a_e(t,u)\), where \(\zeta=-2\cos u\), descend to holomorphic functions \(\widehat\psi(t,\zeta)\) and \(\widehat a_e(t,\zeta)\). This is the [actual free-edge theorem](research_pair_free_boundary_kernel.md). Set \[ S_n(t;\zeta)=\widehat\psi(t,\zeta)+\frac{int^2}{4\pi}-\frac{it}{2}. \tag{16} \] The nondegenerate complete half-charge saddle continues uniquely to \(t_n(\zeta)\) on a fixed disk about \(-2\). Define \[ \mathcal S_n(\zeta)=S_n(t_n(\zeta);\zeta),\qquad \mathcal A_n(\zeta)=-\partial_t^2S_n(t_n(\zeta);\zeta). \tag{17} \] At \(\zeta=-2\), \(\mathcal A_n=(\sec(t_n/2)-in)/(2\pi)\) has positive real part. All square roots below continue this Gaussian root. Use the full source and its ordinary distinct-node interpolant: \[ \begin{split} h_{n,N}(w;\zeta) &=e^{inN\arccos(-w/2)^2/(4\pi)}K_N(w,\zeta),\\ I_{n,N}(\,\cdot\,;\zeta) &=\text{its interpolant of degree at most \(J_N\) at all \(c_a\)},\\ D_{n,N}(w;\zeta)&=(h_{n,N}(w;\zeta)-I_{n,N}(w;\zeta))/Q_N(w),\\ \mathcal O_{n,N}(w;\zeta) &=\sum_a\frac{N e^{inN\tau_a^2/(4\pi)} K_N(c_a,\zeta)} {Q_N'(c_a)(w-c_a)} =\frac{NI_{n,N}(w;\zeta)}{Q_N(w)}. \end{split} \tag{18} \] The squared inverse cosine is the original branch holomorphic on \(\mathbb C\setminus[2,\infty)\), including \(w=-2\). Put \(\epsilon_N=(-1)^{\lfloor N/2\rfloor}\), and define \[ \begin{split} b_n^{\rm e}(w;\zeta) &=\frac{\sqrt{2\pi}}{\pi i} \frac{\sin t_n(\zeta)\,\widehat a_e(t_n(\zeta),\zeta)} {(w+2\cos t_n(\zeta))\sqrt{\mathcal A_n(\zeta)}},\\ b_n^{\rm o}(w;\zeta) &=\frac{\sqrt{2\pi}}{\pi} \frac{\cos(t_n(\zeta)/2)\,\widehat a_e(t_n(\zeta),\zeta)} {(w+2\cos t_n(\zeta))\sqrt{\mathcal A_n(\zeta)}} . \end{split} \tag{19} \] **Theorem 2.** There is \(r_n>0\), independent of \(N\), such that for \(|\zeta+2|<r_n\), through both level parities, \[ \mathcal O_{n,N}(w;\zeta) =\epsilon_NN^{-1}b_n^{\rm e/o}(w;\zeta) e^{N\mathcal S_n(\zeta)}(1+O(N^{-1})), \qquad w>2. \tag{20} \] This is uniform over all real \(w>2\). The coefficient is nonzero and comparable to \(1/(w+1)\). The normalized error is holomorphic in \(\zeta\), with every fixed ordinary \(\zeta\)-derivative \(O(N^{-1})\) on a smaller fixed disk. Fixed observation-color derivatives have the corresponding holomorphic expansion. *Proof.* Keep the exact angular contours and their orientation from the [even](research_complete_source_pick_observation.md#5-a-nonzero-half-charge-observation) and [odd](research_odd_half_charge_observation.md#1-the-full-node-polynomial-and-exact-angular-contour) source identities, replacing their complete kernel by \(K_N(-2\cos t,\zeta)\). Their residues are precisely (18); no interpolation in the selected angle is introduced. The odd ramified pole at \(t=0\) still contributes \(\epsilon_N h_{n,N}(-2;\zeta)/(w+2)\), exactly once. At \(\zeta=-2\), all connectors and all noncritical horizontal parts have a strict exponential gap. Estimate (10) increases their upper exponents by at most \(|\Im u|\), while (15) does the same for the omitted physical rows. If \(|\zeta+2|\) is small, either local solution of \(-2\cos u=\zeta\) has \(|u|\) small. Thus these gaps persist uniformly on a fixed ordinary color disk, also relative to the continuously varying \(\Re\mathcal S_n(\zeta)\). Near the complete saddle use the genuine two-variable free-edge packet, valid on one fixed neighborhood. The local contour may be deformed inside this neighborhood through \(t_n(\zeta)\); its endpoints stay in the gapped portion, and the observation pole is uniformly separated. No global contour claim is needed for this local deformation. The exact folded lower denominators are \(1+e^{-iNt}\) and \(1-e^{-iNt}\), respectively. Their nonconstant parts stay exponentially small because the height is bounded below by a positive constant near the saddle. The folded scalars and amplitudes are respectively \(\epsilon_NN\sin t/(\pi i)\) and \(\epsilon_NN\cos(t/2)/\pi\). Combining the factor \(N^{-3/2}\widehat a_e\) with the Gaussian factor \(\sqrt{2\pi/N}/\sqrt{\mathcal A_n}\) gives exactly (19)–(20).
