At that tilt their actual outer allocations sum to the original \(\xi\); when both outer weights are positive, each positive-length half has a strict outer split. No new independent angle flow is introduced. At (7) the weighted action is the sum of one branch from \(\{Q_b,J_b\}\) and one from \(\{Q_c,J_c\}\), with a protected middle interpreted as \(Q_0\). Its free spectral derivative is their sum. Every summand is nonpositive by (11). Equality of a summand is possible only for a monomial half with its middle and one outer weight zero. Both halves cannot be monomial: both outer weights cannot vanish, and otherwise it would require one outer and both distinct middles to be protected, although there are only two protected faces. Hence the sum is strictly negative. This contradicts interior spectral stationarity for every strict-spectrum CROSS port, including all allowed protected patterns. Now suppose \(
u=1/2\) and \(\mu<1/2\). The row \(
u\) is ordinary and is a free coordinate in the full local simplex. Its row equation is \(c=q_{\mathrm{end}}\). The local action is \[ U_b(\delta)+	frac12\log c, \qquad U_b\in\{Q_b,J_b\}. 	ag{12} \] Taking the spectral derivative at the stationary rows gives \(U_b'\). It is strictly negative unless \(b=P=0\), in which case the input start is zero and this is exactly the double-protected half-terminal monomial. That case has already been excluded by the cost-free \(\delta=0\) retuning in the boundary theorem. Thus no strict-spectrum half seam remains. Exact original row reflection proves the same for \(\mu=1/2<
u\). This uses an equality row equation, not a one-sided terminal KKT test: the problem is the full original fiber, and \(1/2\) is not one of its local row boundaries. The only fixed row boundaries are those forced by protected zero middles. ## 5. The remaining noncap Green branches The boundary theorem already makes every \(\delta=0\) port strict CROSS. Sections 3--4 leave, at a strict spectrum, a strict lower-half interval \(0\le\mu<
u<1/2\) or its reflected upper-half interval. For the lower interval (6) has the following exact stationary actions: \[  egin{array}{c|c|c} 	ext{row positions}&F&\partial_\delta F\ \hline 	ext{before/before}&Q_b-Q_c+\log c&\log(E_c/E_b)\ 	ext{after/after}&J_b-J_c+\log c&\log(T_c/T_b)\ 	ext{before/after}&Q_b-J_c+\log c&\log(T_c/E_b). \end{array} 	ag{13} \] Before/before forces \(b<c\), so its derivative is positive. After/after forces \(b>c>q_{\mathrm{end}}\), so its derivative is negative. A protected input uses \(Q_0\) and has only the first or third possibility. Consequently a spectral critical point must straddle the lower pole and satisfy \(T_c=E_b\). The two numbers have the common product parameter \(D\): \[ E_b=C_b+\sqrt{C_b^2-D},\quad C_b=A+2bz, \qquad T_c=C_c+\sqrt{C_c^2-D},\quad C_c=2cz-A. 	ag{14} \] The larger-root function is strictly increasing, so the equality is equivalent to \[ \mu<p<
u<	frac12,\qquad (c-b)\sin^2(\pi\delta)=x+y. 	ag{15} \] The established real primitive ratio is \(-E_b/T_c=-1\). Here this is only a local stationary identity, not a face-sign solution or a developing representation. If one outer is protected, \(P=0\), (13)--(15) follow from the exact monomer. If the input middle is protected and both outers are positive, the fixed start is \(\mu=0\), and the same argument gives \(c=(x+y)/z\) with a strict post-pole stop. If both that middle and one outer are protected, \(E_0=A=\sqrt D\); every strict post-pole \(T_c\) is greater than \(A\). Therefore no strict nonterminal Green critical point has that double-protected pattern. Its equality case would be the half-terminal monomial already excluded. Original row reflection gives the corresponding RIGHT branch, with \((b-c)\sin^2(\pi\delta)=x+y\) and the reflected strict endpoint inequalities. A protected overloaded middle cannot occur because its degree exceeds \(1/2\), while its target is zero. For free ordinary endpoints, the row second derivatives of (6) are \(-\partial_t\log\mathcal L(\mu)<0\) and \(\partial_t\log\mathcal L(
u)<0\) on the straddling branch. Thus the regular-window endpoint maxima follow on compact subcharts. A protected start remains the literal fixed start; no false interior start saddle is introduced. This does not assert local weighted maximality in the spectral variable or eliminate a constrained shared maximum by following separately stationary rows. ## 6. The residual cap equation and the remaining scope For a surviving cap corner, orient it as \(x=b=0\), \(q=(0,0,1-
u,
u)\), \(0<
u<1/2\). Both remaining faces are ordinary. The fixed-cap entropy is identically zero, and its local stationarity equation in the genuinely free degree \(
u\) is \[ 0=\partial_
u igl[(1-
u)\log c+
u\log y igr] =\log(y/c),\qquad c=y>0. 	ag{16} \] Use outer exchange or exact row reflection for the other orientation. There are still at most two such ports, at the original marked pair. Equation (16) is not a spectral boundary derivative equality and constructs no finite cap collar or geometric pairing. Thus every maximum in section 1 has finite common positive ordinary face weights. Every noncap port is either complete strict CROSS at \(\delta=0\), or a strict positive-spectral straddling LEFT/RIGHT branch, including its allowed protected single-line specialization. No other positive-length half seam survives. The only cap configurations not removed by this addendum are the already classified double-protected monomial corners, now with equal remaining weights. These conclusions concern the proved original-source upper functional; the global closed-domain coefficient-limsup theorem is a separate input. No lower coefficient asymptotic, finite-level relabeling, loss of an unused scalar, shared sign compatibility, geometric cap continuation, absolute bound by \(\Phi_D\), or filling-period conclusion is inferred. ## Inputs The source functional and both-parity closed-domain upper scope are in the [global closed-domain coefficient majorant](research_global_sharp_coefficient_limsup_majorant.md). The reduction to ordinary positivity and the global/NC hypotheses is [full-fiber boundary activation theorem](research_full_fiber_sharp_boundary_activation.md). The weighted roots, original normalization and derivatives in (9)--(15) are those proved in the [original LEFT spectral envelope and normalized primitives](actual_global_left_weighted_spectral_envelope.md); their use in the present full-fiber setting is shown in sections3--5. The present new points are applying smoothness to the entire reduced protected face, obtaining finite multipliers without an extra hypothesis, using the full-fiber row equation at a half seam, and recording (16).

title: An exact full-grid lens for the original charged source
text: # An exact full-grid lens for the original charged source Private written proof, 15 November 2026. The full original Hermite trace can be represented by a lower angular arc whose endpoints are the real grid midpoints \(-\pi,\pi\). There is then no separate vertical term and no discarded physical row. This gives an exact family of joint source contours through any supplied path in the lower canonical strip. It does not show that the geometric contribution of those contours is nonzero, or bound their remaining parts at the geometric rate. ## 1. The original finite source and its angular representative Fix \(N\ge2\), and put \[ D=N-1,\qquad q=e^{\pi i/N},\qquad \eta=(-1)^D,\qquad C_{N,n}=q^{nD^2/4}, \qquad \tau_a=\frac{\pi(D-2a)}N. \tag{1} \] Use the original algebra and closing \[ \mathcal A_N=\mathbb C[z]/(P_N),\qquad P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2,\qquad \phi_N(F)=\eta N^2[z^D]\operatorname{rem}_{P_N}F . \tag{2} \] All powers of \(q\) use the logarithm in (1). Let \(n\) be any signed integer and let \(A(z)\) be an arbitrary ordinary polynomial. Its coefficients may be polynomials in other untraced boundary variables; no reduction of those variables is made. For \(\chi\in\mathbb C\), write \(L=N(1-\chi)\). The canonical degree-less-than-\(N\) coupon \(\mathcal C_{N,\chi}\) has the full physical data \[ \begin{split} \mathcal C_{N,\chi}(-2\cos\tau)&=\cos(L\tau),\\ \mathcal C_{N,\chi}'(-2\cos\tau) &=-\frac{L\sin(L\tau)}{2\sin\tau} \quad\text{at every double root}. \end{split} \tag{3} \] At the odd simple root \(-2\), its prescribed value is one and there is no normal condition. The two choices \(\tau,-\tau\) at a double root give the same data. Finite Hermite interpolation therefore defines the coupon uniquely, with coefficients entire in \(\chi\). The original scalar is \[ Z_{n,N,\chi}[A]=\phi_N(R^n\mathcal C_{N,\chi}A). \tag{4} \] The exact Gaussian physical jets give the derivative-sampling formula \[ Z_{n,N,\chi}[A] =\eta C_{N,n}\sum_{a=0}^{N-1}g'(\tau_a),\qquad g(t)=\sin t\,A(-2\cos t) \exp\!\left(\frac{inNt^2}{4\pi}\right)\cos(Lt). \tag{5} \] The function \(g\) is odd and entire. Neither the Gaussian nor \(\cos(Lt)\) is being asserted periodic. The formula uses their original physical values and first normals only. At odd \(N\), the single point \(\tau=0\) contributes \(g'(0)=A(-2)\), with the displayed original scalar \(C_{N,n}\). The pinned trace source states its calculation for \(N\ge3\). The same residue and full-Hermite argument applies at \(N=2\): there is one double Casimir root, represented by the two angular points \(\pm\pi/2\), and no simple-root term. Thus (5) and the arguments below include that level. ## 2. The full-grid lens identity Define the exact double-pole kernel \[ W_N(t)=\frac{e^{-iNt}}{(1-\eta e^{-iNt})^2}, \qquad K_N^{\rm grid}(t)=\frac{iNe^{iNt}}{e^{iNt}-\eta}. \tag{6} \] Then \[ (K_N^{\rm grid})'=N^2\eta W_N,\qquad W_N(-t)=W_N(t),\qquad W_N(\pi)=W_N(-\pi)=-\eta/4. \tag{7} \] In particular the two endpoints are not poles at either parity. The nearest physical points are \(\pm(\pi-\pi/N)\). Let \(\Gamma\) be a piecewise smooth arc from \(-\pi\) to \(\pi\) whose interior lies in the open lower half-plane. It may be chosen inside \(|\operatorname{Re}t|<\pi\). The integrals at its endpoints are ordinary convergent integrals. **Theorem 1.** For every such arc, \[ \boxed{\quad Z_{n,N,\chi}[A] =-\frac{N^2C_{N,n}}{\pi i} \int_\Gamma g(t)W_N(t)\,dt . \quad} \tag{8} \] This is an exact finite-\(N\) identity, with every original physical row and every first normal retained. **Proof.** First suppose the arc is simple. Reflection \(t\mapsto-t\) gives an upper arc \(-\Gamma\), directed from \(\pi\) to \(-\pi\). The resulting positively oriented lens encloses exactly the \(N\) physical grid points in (5). At each, \(K_N^{\rm grid}\) has residue one. The residue theorem and integration by parts give \[ \begin{split} Z_{n,N,\chi}[A] &=\frac{\eta C_{N,n}}{2\pi i} \oint K_N^{\rm grid}(t)g'(t)\,dt\\ &=-\frac{\eta C_{N,n}}{2\pi i} \oint (K_N^{\rm grid})'(t)g(t)\,dt . \end{split} \tag{9} \] The integrands are regular at the two lens endpoints. Oddness of \(g\) and evenness of \(W_N\) make the upper integral equal to the lower one, with the reflected orientation. Equations (7) and (9) prove (8). A general arc has the same integral by a fixed-end homotopy in the lower half-plane, where \(gW_N\) has no poles. Equivalently, use the corresponding oriented chains. \(\square\) Here is the endpoint audit in the original rectangle formulation. For height \(y>0\), its exact vertical contribution is \[ \frac{\eta N^2C_{N,n}}{\pi} \int_{-y}^{y} \frac{g(\pi+iv)}{4\cosh^2(Nv/2)}\,dv . \tag{10} \] For fixed \(N,\chi,A\), the integrand is analytic near \(v=0\), and \(g(\pi)=0\). The integral tends to zero; its symmetric Taylor expansion is in fact \(O_{N,\chi,A}(y^3)\). Individually, short endpoint connectors have size \(O_{N,\chi,A}(\epsilon^2)\), because \[ g(t)W_N(t)=O_{N,\chi,A}(|t\mp\pi|) \quad(t\longrightarrow\pm\pi). \tag{11} \] Thus the fixed-\(N\) limit \(y\downarrow0\) produces precisely (8), without an endpoint half-residue. The constants in (11) are not asserted uniform in \(N\); this exact limit is taken before any asymptotic estimate. No interchange of limits is used. ## 3. Spectral branches, half crossings and all aliases The endpoints map to \(z=2\), where the canonical function \(\operatorname{arccosh}(-z/2)^2\) has a branch. This causes no endpoint pole in the proof: (5)--(11) are angular identities of entire functions and the explicit grid kernel. Moreover \(P_N(2)=4\), so \(z=2\) is not an original spectral pole. No contour is moved across the spectral branch cut in this argument. The connection with the adopted even split is exact. Write \(n=m+\epsilon\), with \(m\) even and \(\epsilon\in\{0,\pm1\}\), and retain the physical factor \(\kappa^n\), where \(\kappa=q^{D^2/2}\). Here \[ \hbar=2\pi i/N,\qquad F_j(z)=q^{-jD^2/4} \exp\!\left(\frac{j\,\mathfrak K(z)}{2\hbar}\right), \qquad \mathfrak K(z)=\operatorname{arccosh}(-z/2)^2 \] uses the canonical branch on \(\mathbb C\setminus[2,\infty)\), with its removable value at \(-2\). In the open canonical strip \(|\operatorname{Re}t|<\pi\), \[ \kappa^n F_m(-2\cos t)F_\epsilon(-2\cos t) =C_{N,n}\exp\!\left(\frac{inNt^2}{4\pi}\right). \tag{12} \] Hence an interior deformation staying in this strip crosses no half-crossing seam. At its angular endpoints the entire right side and its product with \(\sin t\) have the regular limits already used in (11). A spectral derivative of \(F_\epsilon\) at \(z=2\) is neither needed nor substituted for an original normal. For continuous \(\chi\), the coupon representative \(\cos(Lt)\) may have different values on lifts differing by \(2\pi\). The proof of (8) compares \(t\) with \(-t\), where it is even; it never compares \(t\) with \(t+2\pi\). Thus its possible nonperiodicity creates no omitted endpoint term. Subsequent logarithmic lattice translations still require the actual canonical coupon or its exact wrap corrections. The complete Fourier-alias kernel is retained: \[ W_N(t)\cos(N(1-\chi)t) =\frac12e^{-iN\chi t} \frac{1+e^{-2iN(1-\chi)t}} {(1-\eta e^{-iNt})^2}. \tag{13} \] At \(\chi=1\) the numerator is two, giving the original unit-charge coefficient one. At \(\chi=0\), the coupon in the finite algebra is \(\eta\); this is not a known scalar initializer. Near the real endpoints, (13) is used exactly. No estimate that discards its other terms is asserted there. ## 4. Joint original sources and an explicit continuation candidate For a fixed original circle tree, let \(S\) be the traced vertices. Keep the original full turn kernels \(\mathcal K_N(t_v,t_w)=\sum_{j=0}^D e_j(-2\cos t_v)e_j(-2\cos t_w)\), all ordinary outside polynomials, and all original integer powers. Applying (8) at each selected vertex gives exactly \[ \begin{split} Z_{\boldsymbol\chi,N} ={}&\prod_{v\in S}\left(-\frac{N^2C_{N,n_v}}{\pi i}\right) \int_{\prod_{v\in S}\Gamma_v} \prod_e\mathcal K_N(t_v,t_w)\\ &\qquad\cdot \prod_{v\in S}\left[ \sin t_v\, e^{in_vNt_v^2/(4\pi)} W_N(t_v)\cos(N(1-\chi_v)t_v)\,dt_v \right]. \end{split} \tag{14} \] The identical statement applies to compiled identity or turn kernels and further polynomial spectators, with those actual factors left in place. Fubini is legitimate for these finite compact integrals. The identity is coefficientwise in the untraced ordinary variables, so subsequent boundary derivatives retain the original normals. Compact joint deformations are also exact when their interiors stay in the product lower domain and each boundary face stays in its original hyperplane \(t_v=\pm\pi\). The holomorphic top form is closed. On the side of such a deformation belonging to that boundary face, the pullback of \(dt_v\) is zero. Stokes' theorem therefore adds no face integral. This statement uses the full integrand in (14), not a selected exponential summand. There is an explicit contour family through any supplied continuous path \[ t_v^*(\chi)=s_v(\chi)-iH_v(\chi),\qquad |s_v(\chi)|<\pi,\quad H_v(\chi)>0, \tag{15} \] on a compact parameter interval. Choose a radius \(r>0\) smaller than a quarter of the distance of all \(s_v(\chi)\) from the ends. Let a smooth bump \(\beta\) equal one on \([-r,r]\), vanish outside \([-2r,2r]\), and take values in \([0,1]\). For any fixed \(h_0>0\), set \[ h_{v,\chi}(s) =\beta(s-s_v(\chi))H_v(\chi) +(1-\beta(s-s_v(\chi)))h_0(\pi^2-s^2),\qquad \Gamma_{v,\chi}(s)=s-i h_{v,\chi}(s). \tag{16} \] These arcs have the required fixed real endpoints, stay in the lower canonical strip, and are horizontal near the selected points. Equation (14) holds on them for every parameter and every \(N\). For a piecewise smooth supplied path they form a piecewise smooth fixed-end isotopy. No existence of the path (15) is proved here. The small-charge theorem supplies a nonzero initial asymptotic for the same original source with complete outside angles, arbitrary fixed signed powers, and the stated same-index graph kernels. Its proof also applies to the real continuous coupons (3) on its small charge box: on physical real angles the coupon has modulus at most one and first angular derivative at most \(N\), and its exact reflected contour formula requires evenness, not periodicity. All its strict estimates are unchanged. Formula (14) represents that initialized source and its exact continuation to unit charge. This removes neither the analytic continuation problem for the geometric projection nor the need for a whole-source estimate. The full edge kernels have not been replaced by their geometric packets. A local descending classical collar can be inserted only as an exact chain deformation with its remaining connecting chain retained. This note gives no bound on that chain, no source-compatible projection onto the local geometric block, and no noncancellation conclusion. The split-current action gap applies when the actual remaining operation is the specified Ward deletion; a general part of the lens integrand has not been identified with such a deletion. ## Direct written sources Full source readbacks were retained at the matching pinned versions, and the directly used implications were reread. * [Exact original trace](research_exact_complete_trace_contour.md), SHA256 a63c66e8078457fa84e8044dc876beca36126348e816de9c6997d2a2610474e8: derivative sampling, residue normalization, complete double-pole kernel and exact vertical sides. * [Analytic coupon family](research_dominant_saddle_transport.md), SHA256 413940497a23e884d726b91f9c0ebc01994fef8216811ed2c6fb0838fc80bb04: Section 9 defines the canonical full-Hermite family and its nonperiodic angular representative and retained aliases. * [Original source compiler](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_arbitrary_power_source_compilation.md), SHA256 55e2de84870cfd20dac5922791dbc2bed54909439dfbf4663f17c70a1089445f: actual turn/identity kernels, arbitrary signed powers and unreduced free-boundary source. * [Even-factor reduction](research_even_twist_ward_source_reduction.md), SHA256 7cd055df1b070ecc8a5f4a4b62e821e37c616e1bbb935aa274939cf44e8e0b18: canonical analytic units, original \(\kappa^n\), total-power Gaussian and the distinction from unwrapped seam transport. * [Small-charge initializer](research_small_charge_path_source.md), SHA256 c6d0ce2a4ecf1412aa3752cb8a94c6933bb47acab5d96d879c6f1b17b2db2a90: its original finite source, both-parity initial asymptotic, arbitrary fixed signed powers, full kernel and endpoint estimates. Only written reasoning, text reads and file hashes were used. No mathematical code, numerical evaluation, tests or compilation were run. Frozen notes, public documents and manuscripts were not edited.

title: Full-period vertical currents as charge convolutions of reduced sources
text:
# Full-period vertical currents as charge convolutions of reduced sources Private written proof, 16 November 2026. The full angular trace rectangle admits an exact inclusion–exclusion expansion in which every surviving vertex keeps its full original trace. Pairing the two ends of each vertical side then gives an integral of reduced graph sources with explicit endpoint kernel coupons. Multiplying all coupons at a shared surviving vertex before expanding them turns those insertions into finite symmetric charge convolutions. The resulting bound uses actual reduced sources, with their signed powers and full normals, instead of an absolute unfilled spectator norm. This is the full-\(\pi\) vertical current of the original trace rectangle. It is not the older [one-step Ward current](research_even_twist_ward_source_reduction.md). The decorated Ward identities and the [classical saturated-face factorization](research_saturated_angle_face_energy.md) remain distinct. The formula below does not assume their face gap is a bound for this current, and proves no source noncancellation. ## 1. Original full trace and charge convention Let \(N\ge2\), \(D=N-1\), \(\eta=(-1)^D\), and \[ P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2,\qquad \mathcal A_N=\mathbb C[z]/(P_N),\qquad \phi_N(f)=\eta N^2[z^D]\operatorname{rem}_{P_N}f. 	ag{1} \] Use the original full Newton kernel \[ K_N(z,w)=\sum_{j=0}^{D}e_j(z)e_j(w),\qquad z(t)=-2\cos t. 	ag{2} \] The double physical roots have positive angular lifts \[ c_a=-2\cos	au_a,\qquad 	au_a=\pi(D-2a)/N>0,\qquad 0\le a<\lfloor N/2floor. 	ag{3} \] At odd levels \(-2\) is an additional simple root. Keep the full crossing scalar \[ C_{N,n}=\exp\{\pi i nD^2/(4N)\}. 	ag{4} \] For an integer signed power \(n\), the original crossing \(R^n\) has the same full physical data as \(C_{N,n}\exp(inNt^2/(4\pi))\). The same data define the canonical entire real-power extension \(R_n\). We use this extension when \(n\) is not integral, without changing the integer crossing convention. The original entire cosine coupon \(\mathcal C_{N,\chi}\) is the unique class with the value and spectral derivative of \(\cos(N(1-\chi)t)\) at every double node and value \(1\) at the odd simple node. Put \[ L_{n,\chi}[f]=\phi_N(R_n\mathcal C_{N,\chi}f),\qquad \ell=N(1-\chi). 	ag{5} \] For an arbitrary ordinary polynomial \(f(z)\), define \[ g_{n,\chi,f}(t)= \sin t\,f(-2\cos t)\exp(inNt^2/(4\pi))\cos(\ell t), \qquad W_N(t)= rac{e^{-iNt}}{(1-\eta e^{-iNt})^2}. 	ag{6} \] For every fixed \(H>0\), the exact trace contour is \[  egin{split} L_{n,\chi}[f]&=H_{n,\chi}^{H}[f]+V_{n,\chi}^{H}[f],\ H_{n,\chi}^{H}[f]&= - rac{N^2C_{N,n}}{\pi i} \int_{-\pi-iH}^{\pi-iH}g_{n,\chi,f}(t)W_N(t)\,dt,\ V_{n,\chi}^{H}[f]&=  rac{\eta N^2C_{N,n}}{\pi} \int_{-H}^{H}  rac{g_{n,\chi,f}(\pi+ih)}{4\cosh^2(Nh/2)}\,dh . \end{split} 	ag{7} \] All local functionals are extended coefficientwise in any other variables. Heights are fixed, rather than differentiated with respect to powers or charges. For completeness, the derivative sampling identity behind (7) is \[ L_{n,\chi}[f]=\eta C_{N,n} \sum_{j=0}^{N-1}g_{n,\chi,f}' igl(\pi(D-2j)/N igr). 	ag{8} \] At each double node the two opposite angles give exactly the value and first-normal terms of \(\phi_N\); at the odd angle zero the term is \(C_{N,n}f(-2)\). This verifies (8), including \(N=2\), from the full physical data. The residue proof of (7) then applies without change: \(g\) is odd and entire, and the double-pole grid kernel has no boundary pole on the rectangle. It does not require \(\cos(\ell t)\) to be periodic. Thus (7) holds for all complex \(\chi,n\) as an identity of entire parameter families, and for the actual integer-power source. ## 2. The paired vertical current Write \[ w_h=2\cosh h,\qquad b=nNh/2,\qquad E_n(h)=\exp\{inN(\pi^2-h^2)/(4\pi)\}. 	ag{9} \] The polynomial spectator takes the same value \(f(w_h)\) at \(t=\pi+ih\) and \(t=\pi-ih\). Directly pairing these two terms gives \[ V_{n,\chi}^{H}[f]=\int_0^H ho_{N,n,\chi}(h)f(w_h)\,dh, 	ag{10} \] where the entire parameter-dependent scalar is \[  egin{split} ho_{N,n,\chi}(h) ={}& rac{2\eta N^2C_{N,n}}{\pi}  rac{\sinh h\,E_n(h)}{4\cosh^2(Nh/2)}\ &\quad\cdot \left\{i\cos(\pi\ell)\cosh(\ell h)\sinh b -\sin(\pi\ell)\sinh(\ell h)\cosh bight\}. \end{split} 	ag{11} \] Indeed \(\sin(\pi\pm ih)=\mp i\sinh h\), the Gaussian multipliers are \(E_n(h)e^{\mp b}\), and \(\cos(\ell(\pi\pm ih))=\cos(\pi\ell)\cosh(\ell h) \mp i\sin(\pi\ell)\sinh(\ell h)\). These identities give both signs and the factor two in (11). At a lattice charge \(\chi=J/N\), \(J\in\mathbb Z\), this simplifies to \[ ho_{N,n,J/N}(h)=  rac{2i\eta(-1)^{N-J}N^2C_{N,n}}{\pi}  rac{\sinh h\,E_n(h)\cosh((N-J)h)\sinh(nNh/2)} {4\cosh^2(Nh/2)}. 	ag{12} \] In particular the unit-charge formula has no cosine sign or hyperbolic charge factor. Also \[ V_{0,J/N}^{H}=0\quad(J\in\mathbb Z). 	ag{13} \] This is an exact full-current identity, not a bound or a value-only observation. Off the lattice the second term of (11) need not vanish. For bounded real \(n,\chi\), the direct estimate of (11) gives \[ |ho_{N,n,\chi}(h)| \le C N^2\sinh H\, \exp\{N(|n|/2+|1-\chi|-1)h\}\quad(0\le h\le H). 	ag{14} \] The constant is uniform in such real parameter boxes. It uses the full \(4\cosh^2(Nh/2)\) denominator, rather than its first Fourier alias. ## 3. Full traces at all surviving vertices Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a fixed finite original graph, \(S\subseteq V\) its selected vertices, and \(B=V\setminus S\) the outside vertices. There is no restriction on the selected degrees or on the size of \(S\). The algebra below works for any finite graph with the original same-index kernel (2), in particular every original circle tree. Include each edge once. Outside variables remain prescribed or free. Let \(A_N(\mathbf z)\) be any joint polynomial spectator, independent of the charges on which the shift operators below act. Parameters of that spectator can instead be held fixed during the shifts. Define \[ F_G(\mathbf z)=A_N(\mathbf z)\prod_{e=vw\in E}K_N(z_v,z_w), \qquad Z_{G,N}(\mathbf n, oldsymbol\chi;\mathbf z_B) =\left(\prod_{v\in S}L_{n_v,\chi_v}^{(z_v)}ight)F_G . 	ag{15} \] Choose fixed heights \(H_v>0\) and abbreviate the functionals in (7) by \(L_v,H_v^{m op},V_v^{m op}\); the superscript distinguishes operators from their height parameters. **Theorem 1 (full-survivor current expansion).** Exactly, \[ \prod_{v\in S}L_v =\prod_{v\in S}H_v^{m op} +\sum_{\varnothing
e C\subseteq S}(-1)^{|C|+1} \left(\prod_{v\in C}V_v^{m op}ight) \left(\prod_{w\in S\setminus C}L_wight). 	ag{16} \] Consequently every correction to the product of full lower horizontal contours is an integral with full original traces at every surviving vertex. **Proof.** Expand \(\prod H_v^{m op}=\prod(L_v-V_v^{m op})\) and rearrange. Operators in distinct variables commute, even when their common input contains shared edges and a nonfactorized spectator. Finite integrals and finite Hermite functionals may be interchanged directly. \(\square\) Here is the exact graph content of a term of (16). Put \(Y=S\setminus C\) and \(G'=G\setminus C\), deleting every edge incident to \(C\), but retaining every surviving vertex, including isolated selected vertices. For \(w\in Y\), let \(r_w\) count its edges to \(C\). Set \[  egin{split} A_{N,C,\mathbf h}(\mathbf z_{V\setminus C}) &=A_N(\mathbf w_{\mathbf h},\mathbf z_{V\setminus C}),\ Q_{w,N,\mathbf h}(z) &=\prod_{\substack{e=vw\v\in C}}K_N(w_{h_v},z),\ D_{C,N}(\mathbf h;\mathbf z_B) &=\prod_{\substack{e=vv'\v,v'\in C}} K_N(w_{h_v},w_{h_{v'}}) \prod_{\substack{e=vb\v\in C,\ b\in B}} K_N(w_{h_v},z_b). \end{split} 	ag{17} \] Empty products are one. Denote the literal reduced source, with spectator \(A_{N,C,\mathbf h}\), by \(Z_{G',N}^{A_{C,\mathbf h}}\). Then the \(C\)-term before its inclusion–exclusion sign is \[  egin{split} I_{C,N}={}& \int_{\prod_{v\in C}[0,H_v]} \left(\prod_{v\in C}ho_{N,n_v,\chi_v}(h_v)\,dh_vight) D_{C,N}(\mathbf h;\mathbf z_B)\ &\quad\cdot \left(\prod_{w\in Y}L_{n_w,\chi_w}ight) \left[ A_{N,C,\mathbf h} \prod_{e\in E(G')}K_N \prod_{w\in Y}Q_{w,N,\mathbf h}(z_w) ight]. \end{split} 	ag{18} \] This follows by (10) in each removed variable. In particular internal removed edges have not been replaced by one. Several removed vertices meeting one survivor produce the single product \(Q_w\) at that survivor; they are not independently traced there. No factorization of \(A_N\) or of the reduced graph is assumed. ## 4. Exact finite charge convolution Expand the ordinary polynomial product at each survivor as \[ Q_{w,N,\mathbf h}(z) =\sum_{k=0}^{r_wD} eta_{w,k}(\mathbf h)T_k(-z/2). 	ag{19} \] This is an identity before taking any quotient. Define \[ (\mathcal S_{w,k}f)( oldsymbol\chi) =	frac12\{f( oldsymbol\chi+(k/N)\mathbf e_w) +f( oldsymbol\chi-(k/N)\mathbf e_w)\}, \qquad \mathcal B_{w,N,\mathbf h} =\sum_{k=0}^{r_wD} eta_{w,k}(\mathbf h)\mathcal S_{w,k}. 	ag{20} \] For \(r_w=0\) the operator is the identity. **Theorem 2 (actual reduced-source formula).** The surviving-trace factor in (18), including all its endpoint coupons, is exactly \[ \left(\prod_{w\in Y}\mathcal B_{w,N,\mathbf h}ight) Z_{G',N}^{A_{C,\mathbf h}} (\mathbf n_Y, oldsymbol\chi_Y;\mathbf z_B). 	ag{21} \] All charges here are literal original charge parameters; no source amplitude is divided out. **Proof.** In the full physical algebra, \[ T_k(-z/2)\mathcal C_{N,\chi} =	frac12\{\mathcal C_{N,\chi-k/N} +\mathcal C_{N,\chi+k/N}\}. 	ag{22} \] At every positive physical angle this is the cosine product identity. Differentiating that identity in \(t\), then dividing by \(2\sin t\), proves the first-normal equality. At the odd simple node both sides have value one. These are all physical data, proving (22). Apply (22) to (19) inside the original surviving trace; arbitrary shared spectators and all other variables stay fixed. Operators in different charges commute, proving (21). \(\square\) The identical product identity holds for the finite one-sided coupons \(Q_{N,\sigma}\), using the two shifted exponentials. It also holds termwise in any fixed-height angular cosine decomposition because multiplication by \(\cos(kt)\) gives the same two charge shifts. These are identities for specified representatives; they do not remove their connector currents. In particular lattice charges remain lattice charges throughout (18)--(21), with no restriction to \(0\le J\le N\). After another application of (16) in a reduced source, (13) still applies at every zero-power vertex. The recursion retains the full simple/normal data even when a shifted charge is zero or leaves the initial unit interval. An isolated surviving vertex has its actual scalar trace \(L_{n,\chi}[1]\), or the trace of its retained spectator, rather than being silently deleted. ## 5. A quantitative estimate in terms of actual reduced sources We give a bound on real outside colors \(z_b\in[-2,2]\); arbitrary fixed ordinary outside derivatives obey the same exponential estimate. The identities (16)--(22) themselves hold for unrestricted free outside variables. For \(h_*>0\), define \[  egin{split} x_{h_*}&=4-2\cosh h_*,\ p(h_*)&= rac2\pi\int_0^{\pi/2} \operatorname{asinh}\!\left(\sinh(h_*/2)\cot yight)\,dy,\ \lambda(h_*)&=\max\{p(h_*),h_*\},\ \gamma(h_*)&=\max\{p(h_*)+h_*/2,2h_*\}. \end{split} 	ag{23} \] The endpoint theorem proves \(p(h_*)	o0\), indeed \(p(h_*)=O(h_*\log(1/h_*))\). Its estimates imply, uniformly for \(0\le h,h'\le h_*\), \[  egin{split} \sup_{z\in[-2,2]}|K_N(2\cosh h,z)| &\le C_{h_*}N^{a_{h_*}}e^{N\lambda(h_*)},\ |K_N(2\cosh h,2\cosh h')| &\le C_{h_*}N^{a_{h_*}}e^{N\gamma(h_*)}. \end{split} 	ag{24} \] Fixed spectral derivatives on the real outside interval cost only additional powers of \(N\), by the ordinary polynomial Markov bound. No fixed-height exponential loss is dropped. A polynomial \(Q(z)\) of degree at most \(rD\), with real-interval sup norm \(M\), has Chebyshev coefficients satisfying \[ \sum_{k=0}^{rD}| eta_k|\le(2rD+1)M. 	ag{25} \] This follows from its ordinary cosine coefficient integrals on \([0,\pi]\), with the constant coefficient counted once. Therefore (19), with its entire shared product, satisfies \[ \sum_k| eta_{w,k}(\mathbf h)| \le C_{G,h_*}N^{a_{G,h_*}} e^{Nr_w\lambda(h_*)}. 	ag{26} \] At the exact height-zero endpoint this sharpens to \[ \sum_k| eta_{w,k}(\mathbf0)| \le (2r_wD+1)\{N+m(N-1)\}^{r_w} \le C_{r_w}N^{2r_w+1}\quad(r_w>0). 	ag{27} \] There is no exponential loss in (27). Let \(e_C\) be the number of edges with both endpoints in \(C\), and \(b_C\) the number with exactly one endpoint in \(C\), including edges to original outside vertices. For real powers and real charges put \[  egin{split} \varepsilon_C(\mathbf H;\mathbf n_C, oldsymbol\chi_C) ={}&e_C\gamma(h_*)+b_C\lambda(h_*)\ &+\sum_{v\in C} (|n_v|/2+|1-\chi_v|-1)_+H_v,\qquad h_*=\max_{v\in C}H_v. \end{split} 	ag{28} \] For fixed graph and bounded real power/charge boxes, \(\varepsilon_C	o0\) as all \(H_v	o0\). Let \(\mathcal Q_{C,N}\) be the finite set of shifted surviving charges in (20): in each coordinate with \(r_w>0\) the shift has the form \(\pm k/N\), \(0\le k\le r_wD\), and the other coordinates are unchanged. Define the actual reduced-source supremum \[ \mathcal M_{C,N} =\sup_{\mathbf h\in\prod[0,H_v]} \max_{ oldsymbol\chi'\in\mathcal Q_{C,N}} |Z_{G',N}^{A_{C,\mathbf h}} (\mathbf n_Y, oldsymbol\chi';\mathbf z_B)|. 	ag{29} \] When the outside variables vary in a real compact set, take the same supremum there. For a desired fixed outside derivative, include the finitely many derivatives of the reduced source up to that order in (29). **Theorem 3 (unconditional current reduction bound).** For fixed positive heights and bounded real powers and charges, \[ |I_{C,N}| \le C_{G,\mathbf H}N^{a_{G,\mathbf H}} e^{N\varepsilon_C(\mathbf H;\mathbf n_C, oldsymbol\chi_C)} \mathcal M_{C,N}. 	ag{30} \] The same statement holds for every fixed mixed ordinary outside derivative with the preceding convention in (29). **Proof.** The norm of the symmetric shift in (20), relative to the finite supremum in (29), is at most one. Apply (26) at each survivor. Its exponent counts the cut edges from \(C\) to \(Y\) once. The second product in \(D_{C,N}\) contributes the same \(\lambda\) cost on the remaining cut edges, while its first product contributes \(\gamma\) on the \(e_C\) internal removed edges. Apply (14) and bound its exponent on \(0\le h_v\le H_v\) by the positive part in (28). The finite integration volumes and all prefactors are absorbed in the stated polynomial. For outside derivatives use the ordinary product rule in (18); the differentiated cut kernels have the same rate by (24), and the required surviving-source derivatives were retained in (29). This proves (30). \(\square\) This is a bound by actual charged reduced sources, not a bound by the absolute norm of their unfilled spectators. If \(A_N\) is nonfactorized, its exact restriction \(A_{C,\mathbf h}\) remains inside those sources. The constants in (30) may depend on fixed positive heights; no uniform claim is made when heights shrink with \(N\). The asserted small-height limit concerns the explicit rate \(\varepsilon_C\). There is a useful shrinking-height regime with a stronger estimate. It uses the exact endpoint root disk rather than substituting \(h_*=O(N^{-1})\) into constants that were proved only at fixed height. **Corollary 4 (microscopic heights).** Fix \(0<\alpha_0<\pi\), and take \[ H_v=\alpha_v/N,\qquad 0<\alpha_v\le\alpha_0. 	ag{30a} \] Let \(q_C=\#\{w\in Y:r_w>0\}\). Uniformly for bounded real powers and charges, at every level, \[ |I_{C,N}| \le C_{G,\alpha_0}N^{\,2(e_C+b_C)+q_C} \mathcal M_{C,N}^{m mic}. 	ag{30b} \] Here \(\mathcal M_{C,N}^{m mic}\) is precisely (29), on the height box (30a). Constants also depend on the fixed real parameter bounds. For a fixed outside multi-derivative of order \(|
u|\), the exponent of \(N\) in (30b) may be increased by \(2|
u|\), with the required reduced-source derivatives included as in (29). No exponential factor occurs in this bound. **Proof.** For all sufficiently large \(N\), uniformly in (30a), \[ 2\cosh h-2\le 2-c_0,\qquad 0\le h\le\alpha_0/N. 	ag{30c} \] Indeed \(\cosh(\alpha_0/N)+\cos(\pi/N) =2-(\pi^2-\alpha_0^2)/(2N^2)+O_{\alpha_0}(N^{-4})<2\). The exact root disk in the endpoint theorem consequently gives \(|F_{j,N}(2\cosh h)|\le1\). Its cosine interpolation then bounds the low kernel by \(N\) on the real other color. With that other color also equal to \(2\cosh h'\), the bound is at most \(N e^{J h'}\le N e^{\alpha_0/2}\). The full radical estimate gives \[  egin{split} \sup_{z\in[-2,2]}|K_N(2\cosh h,z)|&\le C_{\alpha_0}N^2,\ |K_N(2\cosh h,2\cosh h')|&\le C_{\alpha_0}N^2 \qquad(0\le h,h'\le\alpha_0/N). \end{split} 	ag{30d} \] Only finitely many levels were excluded in proving (30c). Their compact polynomial evaluations can be absorbed into the same constant in (30d); no root-disk assertion at those levels is needed. Apply (25) to each whole shared product. For \(r_w>0\), \[ \sum_k| eta_{w,k}(\mathbf h)| \le C_{G,\alpha_0}N^{2r_w+1}. 	ag{30e} \] Each other removed edge in \(D_{C,N}\) costs \(C N^2\) by (30d). Finally (14), \(\sinh(\alpha_0/N)\le C_{\alpha_0}/N\), and the bounded real parameter boxes give \[ \int_0^{\alpha_v/N}|ho_{N,n_v,\chi_v}(h)|\,dh\le C \quad(0<\alpha_v\le\alpha_0). 	ag{30f} \] The powers \(N^2\), \(N^{-1}\) from \(\sinh h\), and \(N^{-1}\) from the integration length cancel. Multiplying (30e), (30d), and (30f) in (18)--(21) proves (30b). Ordinary outside derivatives of the cut kernels cost \(N^2\) per derivative by Markov on the whole real color interval; the other differentiated factors stay in (29). This proves the derivative statement. \(\square\) The macroscopic charge shifts in (20) remain in (30b). The improved height scale removes an exponential operator cost; it does not replace the shifted reduced sources by their unit-charge value. ## 6. The charge convolution is not local The shift interval in (20) cannot in general be replaced by an \(o(1)\) charge interval. This is visible in a coefficient of the literal original endpoint kernel, rather than in a chosen spectator. For one cut incidence at height zero write \[ B_N(z)=K_N(2,z)=\sum_{k=0}^{D} eta_kT_k(-z/2). 	ag{31} \] The original sine products satisfy \(S_D=N\) and \[ \prod_{a=0}^{N-1}2\sin rac{(2a+1)\pi}{2N}=2. \] Removing the last factor from this product gives \[ e_D(2)= rac{\eta}{N^2\sin^2(\pi/(2N))}. 	ag{32} \] Only the \(e_D(2)e_D(z)\) term contributes to the leading coefficient of \(B_N\). Since the leading coefficients of \(e_D(z)\) and \(T_D(-z/2)\) are respectively \(\eta/N^2\) and \(\eta/2\), \[  eta_D=  rac{2\eta}{N^4\sin^2(\pi/(2N))}. 	ag{33} \] At unit charge, (22) therefore includes the two extreme reduced-source charges \[ \chi=1/N,\qquad \chi=2-1/N, 	ag{34} \] each with the exact coefficient \[  rac{\eta}{N^4\sin^2(\pi/(2N))} \sim rac{4\eta}{\pi^2N^2}. 	ag{35} \] Thus these shifts have polynomial, not exponential, suppression. Neither (33) nor (35) asserts that one such contribution dominates; the coherent sum can cancel them. At the current level the height-zero density itself vanishes, and no single integration endpoint is being assigned positive measure. The assertion is the nonlocality of the exact endpoint operator being integrated. The classical saturated-face energy identity retains the surviving charges and imposes a compatibility condition involving the removed powers and charges. The coupons in (17) do not impose that condition: at height zero \(B_N(c_j)=K_N(c_j,2)>0\) at every distinct physical node, so \(B_N\) is a unit in the full physical algebra. Its physical support is not a projector onto a compatible angle fiber. Consequently neither (30) nor the polynomial endpoint theorem identifies the shifted reduced-source maximum with the classical same-charge face action. The next analytic task is to control this actual coherent convolution, including its current weights, or prove the needed reduced-source rate bound on its genuine shifted range. ## 7. Coverage and direct-source readback The prior one-step Gaussian Ward deletion and its decorated matching coupons concern a different translated source current. The present finite inclusion–exclusion identity starts instead from the complete full-\(\pi\) rectangle (7). It retains its entire vertical weight, all internal removed edges and all shared boundary products. It does not invoke square-zero deletion of an off-grid kernel. All three complete direct sources were read, their used implications checked, and their hashes verified: * [Exact complete trace contour](research_exact_complete_trace_contour.md), SHA256 a63c66e8078457fa84e8044dc876beca36126348e816de9c6997d2a2610474e8: original derivative trace, crossing carrier, full rectangle orientation and its exact double-pole vertical kernel. * [Finite polarized charge source](research_polarized_charge_heat_source.md), SHA256 860801dedc3f1093d58c0413f580599512bd2566c00f4a94d0ebf99636343db1: original full-Hermite cosine data, canonical real-power extension and scalar carrier, and the one-sided coupons used in (22)'s variant. * [Coherent endpoint kernel reduction](research_full_period_endpoint_kernel_reduction.md), SHA256 a1d67ac803c0160bbfdacaa96a6fde9dc1ffae06fc39eb94f0416dcf2ecef76e: exact original kernel normalization, full ordinary endpoint/mixed derivative bounds, and both-parity small-height estimate with the full radical retained. Only written mathematics, source reads and hashes were used. No mathematical program, numerical experiment, test or compilation was run. Adopted notes and public manuscripts are unchanged.

title: Coherent full-period endpoint bounds for the original edge kernel
text: # Coherent full-period endpoint bounds for the original edge kernel Private research note, 16 November 2026. Written proof only; frozen manuscripts and previously adopted notes are unchanged. The original kernel at the angular endpoint \(t=\pi\), hence spectral color \(w=2\), has polynomial bounds in the other real color, including all fixed mixed spectral derivatives. The proof sums the alternating low Newton sector by exact physical-row interpolation and retains the entire high radical. It therefore applies to the original first-normal closing, not just to its value part. A separate continuation estimate has exponential rate tending to zero as both angular heights tend to zero. No full-source lower bound or contour deformation is asserted. ## 1. Original data and direct sources Put \[ N\ge2,\quad D=N-1,\quad m=\lfloor N/2\rfloor,\quad J=\lfloor(N-1)/2\rfloor=D-m,\quad \theta=\pi/N, \qquad \eta=(-1)^D, \] \[ s_k=2\sin(k\theta),\quad S_k=\prod_{a=1}^k s_a,\quad S_0=1, \qquad c_j=2\cos((2j+1)\theta), \] \[ e_k(z)=S_k^{-2}\prod_{a=0}^{k-1}(c_a-z),\qquad K_N(w,z)=\sum_{k=0}^{D}e_k(w)e_k(z). \tag{1} \] The distinct physical nodes are \(c_0,\ldots,c_J\). They are double except for \(c_J=-2\) at odd levels, where this last node is simple. All statements below concern these ordinary polynomials before any physical quotient is taken. The directly used sources, read in full at the displayed versions, are: * [Actual matching-edge root location](actual_matching_edge_racah_root_location.md), SHA256 f84b82d7924a0c92ca803bc4834bcb0f18f63cedebf2bd072d41d0545a9f5793. Its exact polynomial (1), Jacobi realization and positive matrix shift prove that every nonconstant folded row has all roots strictly above \(2\). * [Full high Newton radical](research_high_newton_radical_contraction.md), SHA256 1faa5d2e02edf0a1462cc43b243e0ab4403bf56e9f1af0befb6b492441d9dd03. Equations (17), (34)--(36) give the exact low/high split and the ordinary radical's real-period and complex-height bounds; (2), (10) give the original full-normal closing. * [Last physical-row transport](research_last_physical_row_riccati.md), SHA256 a6a79106b81b94f5d163022b056c9c6a51e0cdb4f602f090c9f3401436f87c7d. Theorem 1 and (23) bound the actual last row at each fixed real color below \(2\), at both parities. This source is used only in Section 5. The first source proves roots greater than \(2\), not merely greater than \(c_0\). That stronger conclusion is essential here. ## 2. Exact coherent low-sector interpolation Define the physical rows \(F_{j,N}(w)=K_N(c_j,w)\), \(0\le j\le J\). For \(k\le j\), the difference-of-cosines product gives \[ \prod_{a<k}(c_a-c_j)=\frac{S_{j+k}}{S_{j-k}},\qquad e_k(c_j)=\frac{S_{j+k}}{S_{j-k}S_k^2}. \] For \(k>j\), \(e_k(c_j)=0\). Consequently \[ F_{j,N}(w)=\sum_{k=0}^j \frac{S_{j+k}}{S_{j-k}S_k^4}\prod_{a<k}(c_a-w). \tag{2} \] This is literally the normalized polynomial in the root-location source, with the same spectral variable. In particular \(F_{0,N}=1\), \[ F_{j,N}(c_0)=1,\qquad F_{j,N}(w)=\prod_{\ell=1}^{j} \frac{r_{j,\ell}-w}{r_{j,\ell}-c_0},\qquad r_{j,\ell}>2. \tag{3} \] Thus, including \(j=0\), \[ 0<F_{j,N}(w)\le1\qquad(c_0\le w\le2). \tag{4} \] Write the exact ordinary split \[ K_N=K_N^{\rm low}+H_N^{\rm rad},\qquad K_N^{\rm low}(w,z)=\sum_{k=0}^{J}e_k(w)e_k(z),\qquad H_N^{\rm rad}(w,z)=\sum_{r=0}^{m-1}e_{D-r}(w)e_{D-r}(z). \tag{5} \] Every radical polynomial vanishes at every distinct physical node. If \(L_{j,N}\) are the cardinal polynomials of degree at most \(J\) on \(c_0,\ldots,c_J\), ordinary interpolation gives \[ K_N^{\rm low}(w,z)=\sum_{j=0}^{J}F_{j,N}(w)L_{j,N}(z). \tag{6} \] Equation (6) is an exact polynomial identity in both variables. Its derivatives are ordinary derivatives; no normal is discarded. Here is a uniform bound on this interpolation at both parities. Put \(\vartheta_\ell=(2\ell+1)\pi/N\), \(0\le\ell<N\). The numbers \(2\cos\vartheta_\ell\) fold onto the distinct physical nodes, twice each except for the odd node \(-2\), which occurs once. For a polynomial \[ P(z)=\sum_{k=0}^{J}a_kT_k(z/2),\qquad \max_{0\le j\le J}|P(c_j)|\le M, \] the finite exponential sum on these \(N\) angles gives \[ a_0=\frac1N\sum_{\ell=0}^{N-1}P(2\cos\vartheta_\ell),\qquad a_k=\frac2N\sum_{\ell=0}^{N-1} P(2\cos\vartheta_\ell)\cos(k\vartheta_\ell)\quad(k>0). \tag{7} \] Indeed every nonzero cosine frequency needed for orthogonality is less than \(N\), since \(2J<N\). Hence \(|a_0|\le M\), \[ |a_k|\le2M,\qquad \sup_{-2\le z\le2}|P(z)|\le(2J+1)M\le NM. \tag{8} \] This also proves the interpolation estimate without a separately assumed Lebesgue bound. In particular (4) and (6) imply \[ \sup_{c_0\le w\le2,\ -2\le z\le2} |K_N^{\rm low}(w,z)|\le N. \tag{9} \] ## 3. Full endpoint bounds, including mixed normals **Theorem 1.** For every pair of fixed nonnegative integers \(a,b\), there is \(C_{a,b}\), independent of \(N\), such that \[ \sup_{-2\le z\le2} |\partial_w^a\partial_z^b K_N(2,z)| \le C_{a,b}N^{2+2a+2b}. \tag{10} \] More precisely, the low sector in (10) is bounded by \[ C_{a,b}N^{1+2a+2b}, \tag{11} \] and the high sector by \(C_{a,b}N^{2+2a+2b}\). **Proof.** The same root product gives a bound on a shrinking complex disk, not just on a real interval. If \(|w-2|\le2-c_0\), then \(|r_{j,\ell}-w|\le r_{j,\ell}-c_0\), so \(|F_{j,N}(w)|\le1\). Cauchy's formula therefore gives \[ |F_{j,N}^{(a)}(2)|\le a!(2-c_0)^{-a}\le C_aN^{2a}, \tag{12} \] because \(2-c_0=4\sin^2(\pi/(2N))\ge4/N^2\). Apply (8) to \((\partial_w^aK_N^{\rm low})(2,z)\), whose physical values are \(F_{j,N}^{(a)}(2)\). The elementary polynomial Markov inequality on an interval of length \(L\) bounds the first derivative of a degree-\(d\) polynomial by \(2d^2/L\) times its sup norm. For complex polynomials the same bound follows by rotating the derivative at the point being estimated and taking the real part. Iteration bounds fixed higher derivatives by the corresponding power. Applying this on \([-2,2]\) in \(z\) proves (11). No lower bound on \(r_{j,\ell}-2\) is required. The full radical source proves \[ \sup_{w,z\in[-2,2]}|H_N^{\rm rad}(w,z)|\le m(N-1). \tag{13} \] Its degree in each variable is at most \(D\). Markov on each real interval therefore gives the high-sector bound. Add (11) to obtain (10). The cited radical proof is stated for \(N\ge3\); for \(N=2\), \[ e_0=1,\quad e_1(z)=-z/4,\quad K_2(w,z)=1+wz/16, \] which verifies all the assertions directly. \(\square\) Thus a physical first normal in the second color costs only a fixed power of \(N\); so does a first normal at the endpoint \(w=2\), or any fixed mixed derivative. This includes the odd simple node by evaluation. The estimate was obtained after the alternating low sum was contracted. Taking absolute values of its individual Newton summands is a different estimate and need not have this zero exponential rate. ## 4. Application to the prescribed full-normal trace Let \(A\) be an arbitrary ordinary spectator polynomial, or its class in \(\mathcal A_N=\mathbb C[z]/(2T_N(z/2)+2)\). Define its physical seminorm \[ \|A\|_{\rm H}= \max\left\{\max_{a<m}(|A(c_a)|+|A'(c_a)|), \ |A(-2)|\text{ if }N\text{ is odd}\right\}. \tag{14} \] The original closing is \[ \phi_N(f)=\eta\sum_{a=0}^{m-1} \{(4-c_a^2)f'(c_a)-c_af(c_a)\} +\mathbf1_{N\text{ odd}}f(-2). \tag{15} \] The double-node formula is the original source residue. At the odd simple node, \(P_N'(-2)=N^2\) and \(\eta=1\), which gives its displayed coefficient from \(\phi_N=\eta N^2[z^D]\operatorname{rem}_{P_N}\). Apply (10) to the product rule in (15). For every fixed \(a\), \[ \left|\phi_N\big((\partial_w^aK_N)(2,z)A(z)\big)\right| \le C_aN^{5+2a}\|A\|_{\rm H}. \tag{16} \] This is a bound for the literal original trace, including both its value and normal terms. It is coefficientwise in additional free variables, and their derivatives commute with the identity. For several independently traced endpoint incidences it can be iterated using the corresponding full mixed Hermite seminorm of the shared spectator. The spectator is retained: (16) does not estimate it or assert that its whole network contribution is small. ## 5. A uniform small-height continuation For \(r>0\) set \[ \rho_r=2\cosh r-2,\qquad x_r=2-\rho_r=4-2\cosh r<2, \] \[ \Psi(x)=\frac2\pi\int_0^{\pi/2} \operatorname{asinh}\!\left(\frac{\sqrt{2-x}}2\cot y\right)dy \quad(x<2). \tag{17} \] **Corollary 2.** For every fixed \(r>0\), there are \(C_r,A_r\) such that, for every \(N\ge2\), every \(|w-2|\le\rho_r\), and every complex angle \(u\), \[ |K_N^{\rm low}(w,-2\cos u)| \le C_rN^{A_r}e^{N\Psi(x_r)+J|\Im u|}. \tag{18} \] For the actual full-period endpoint displacement \(w=2\cosh h\), \(0\le h\le r\), this gives the full-kernel bound \[ |K_N(2\cosh h,-2\cos u)| \le C_rN^{A_r}e^{N[\Psi(x_r)+|\Im u|/2]} +m(N-1)e^{D[h+|\Im u|]}. \tag{19} \] In particular the upper exponential rate tends to zero as \(r\to0\) and \(|\Im u|\to0\). Constants in (18)--(19) may depend on fixed \(r\); uniformity as \(r\) shrinks with \(N\) is not asserted. At \(h=0\), the stronger polynomial endpoint theorem already applies. **Proof.** The exact root product (3) gives \[ |F_{j,N}(w)|\le F_{j,N}(2-|w-2|)\le F_{j,N}(x_r). \tag{20} \] For sufficiently large \(N\), \(x_r<c_0\). The actual row recurrence in the last-row source has positive coefficients and starts with \[ \frac{F_{j+1,N}(x_r)}{F_{j,N}(x_r)}>1. \] Indeed its displayed recurrence (2) inducts this inequality from its first ratio. Thus all the right sides of (20) are at most \(F_{J,N}(x_r)\). Theorem 1 of that source gives \[ F_{J,N}(x_r)\le C_rN^{A_r}e^{N\Psi(x_r)}. \tag{21} \] Here the omitted interval from \(J/N\) to \(1/2\) changes the exponent by \(O(N^{-1})\), at either parity. Only a fixed color below \(2\) is used. The finitely many remaining levels can be absorbed in the constants. Apply the exact coefficient formula (7) to the polynomial in (6). For a complex angle, \(|T_k(-\cos u)|=|\cos(ku)|\le e^{k|\Im u|}\). The sum of its at most \(J+1\) terms proves (18). The original radical bound (36) of its source, at \(t=\pi-ih\), is exactly the second term of (19). This proves the full statement without omitting the high normals. Finally \(\Psi(x_r)\to0\). For an explicit bound put \(c=\sinh(r/2)\) and assume \(0<c\le1\). Split the integral in (17) at \(y=c\), use \[ \operatorname{asinh}(c\cot y)\le\log(1+2c/y)\quad(0<y\le c), \qquad \operatorname{asinh}(c\cot y)\le c\cot y\quad(y\ge c). \] Since \(\sin c\ge2c/\pi\), direct integration yields \[ \Psi(x_r)\le\frac{2c}{\pi} \left(3\log3-2\log2+\log\frac{\pi}{2c}\right) =O(r\log(1/r)). \tag{22} \] This establishes the stated limiting rate. \(\square\) Fixed derivatives in \(w\) on a strictly smaller disk than the one in (18) follow by Cauchy's formula with the larger fixed \(r\). Fixed spectral derivatives in the other color follow by applying Markov before (7), at an additional polynomial cost. These observations do not enlarge the endpoint or small-height domain to a full semicircular boundary at fixed nonzero height. The coherent endpoint cancellation and (16) supply an actual boundary kernel estimate. They do not discard the Laurent primitive, angular vertical current, alias completion, or any other side term in a full relative contour identity. A filled-source asymptotic still requires those original terms to be combined and controlled.

title: A whole physical Gaussian packet for one original crossing
text: # A whole physical Gaussian packet for one original crossing 24 November 2026. Research proof. Earlier finals and manuscripts are unchanged. The original signed crossing, in the uniform physical head metric, has a Gaussian approximation in the Hilbert--Schmidt norm of its entire matrix. Every fixed number of correction terms is available. The estimate is uniform for small real exponential boundary tilts and retains the exact physical phase. It strengthens the weighted norm rate of [W]; it does not identify a geometric tilt or control a closed knot scalar. ## 1. The actual entry, phase, and boundary tilts Put \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\), \(d=N-1\), \(x=-q^{-1}\), \(\kappa=q^{d^2/2}\), and \[ F_j=(Q;Q)_j,\qquad s_j=\prod_{h=1}^j2\sin(\pi h/N),\qquad F_0=s_0=1. \tag{1} \] Fractional powers mean the displayed exponentials. Declare the actual balanced basis \(w_0,\ldots,w_d\) orthonormal, as in [P], and use the unnormalized matrix Hilbert--Schmidt norm on its physical pair. The checked positive crossing sends input \((a,b)\) to \((b+k,a-k)\), with \(0\le k\le a\), \(b+k\le d\). There is one summand for this entry. Set \(j=a-k\). Directly from [B, (2)] and its Cartan diagonal, its full coefficient is \[ R^+_{(b+k,j);(j+k,b)} =\kappa x^{-b-j}Q^{jb} \frac{F_{b+k}F_{j+k}}{F_kF_bF_j} =\chi_N(j,b,k)\frac{s_{b+k}s_{j+k}}{s_ks_bs_j}, \tag{2} \] \[ \chi_N(j,b,k)= \kappa x^{-b-j}Q^{jb}(-i)^k q^{\,k(b+j)+k(k+1)/2},\qquad |\chi_N|=1. \tag{3} \] Indeed \(F_h=(-i)^h q^{h(h+1)/2}s_h\); substitution proves (3). All other matrix entries are zero. No physical entry is a sum of terms whose phases have been replaced by magnitudes. For real \(\rho=(\rho_a,\rho_b,\rho_c,\rho_e)\), put \[ W_{\rm in}|a,b\rangle=e^{\rho_a a+\rho_b b}|a,b\rangle,\quad W_{\rm out}|c,e\rangle=e^{\rho_c c+\rho_e e}|c,e\rangle,\quad R^\pm_\rho=W_{\rm out}R^\pm W_{\rm in}^{-1}. \tag{4} \] Write \(z=(u,v,t)=(j,b,k)/N\), and define \[ \lambda_+(\rho)=(\rho_e-\rho_a,\rho_c-\rho_b,\rho_c-\rho_a). \tag{5} \] Thus the added logarithmic weight of (2) is exactly \(N\lambda_+\cdot z\). These are prescribed positive diagonal changes, not a new source. In a contraction their inverse interface factors must be retained. The original negative crossing satisfies the exact balanced identity \[ R^-=\mathsf P\,\overline{R^+}\,\mathsf P,\qquad R^-_\rho=\mathsf P\,\overline{R^+_{\rho^\leftrightarrow}}\,\mathsf P, \quad \rho^\leftrightarrow=(\rho_b,\rho_a,\rho_e,\rho_c). \tag{6} \] Here \(\mathsf P\) flips the two physical heads; this is not transpose. It also follows directly by conjugating the finite Euler coefficients in [B] and moving the Cartan diagonal. The negative variables are \((u,v,t)=(b-k,a,k)/N\), with output \((b-k,a+k)\), and \(\lambda_-(\rho)=\lambda_+(\rho^\leftrightarrow)\). ## 2. A fixed open chamber of unique interior maxima Set \[ h(s)=\int_0^s\log(2\sin\pi r)\,dr,\quad \mathcal D=\{u,v,t\ge0:\ u+t\le1,\ v+t\le1\}, \] \[ S(z)=h(u+t)+h(v+t)-h(u)-h(v)-h(t),\qquad S_\lambda=S+\lambda\cdot z . \tag{7} \] The actual grid has both upper sums at most \(1-1/N\). The endpoint-uniform estimate in [W], or the proof below, gives \(\log s_j=Nh(j/N)+O(\log N)\). At \(\lambda=0\), fixing \(0<t<1\) gives strictly concave functions of \(u\) and \(v\). Their unique maxima are \(u=v=(1-t)/2\), since \[ \partial_u^2 S =-\frac{\pi\sin\pi t}{\sin\pi u\sin\pi(u+t)}<0. \] The derivative of the reduced maximum is \(\log\cot(\pi t/2)\). Its endpoint values are zero. Hence the unique global maximum is \[ z_0=(1/4,1/4,1/2),\quad M_0=2G/\pi,\quad H_0=-S''(z_0) =\pi\begin{pmatrix}2&0&1\\0&2&1\\1&1&2\end{pmatrix}, \quad\det H_0=4\pi^3 , \tag{8} \] where \(G=\sum_{r\ge0}(-1)^r/(2r+1)^2\); [W] fixes this value. There is a fixed closed real ball \(\Lambda\) about zero, with nonempty interior, such that every \(S_\lambda\), \(\lambda\in\Lambda\), has a unique interior global maximizer \(z_\lambda\). Its Hessian \(H_\lambda=-S''(z_\lambda)\) is uniformly positive definite. Here is also a global justification: choose a small convex neighborhood of \(z_0\) on which \(-S''\) is positive definite. The complete compact complement has a strict loss at zero tilt. Small linear tilts preserve that loss, and the implicit-function theorem supplies the unique critical point inside the neighborhood. Shrink \(\Lambda\) once. All statements below are uniform on this fixed chamber. Put \(M_\lambda=S_\lambda(z_\lambda)\), and \[ a(z)=\left[ \frac{\sin\pi(u+t)\sin\pi(v+t)} {\sin\pi u\sin\pi v\sin\pi t}\right]^{1/2}, \qquad a_\lambda=a(z_\lambda)>0 . \tag{9} \] No geometric point or unknown closed value defines these quantities. The maximum and derivatives are those of the explicit three-variable real function (7). ## 3. The all-order whole-matrix statement There are explicitly specified real polynomials \(P_{\lambda,l}(y)\), analytic in \(\lambda\), with \(P_{\lambda,0}=1\) and \(\deg P_{\lambda,l}\le3l\), with the following property. For any fixed integer \(J\ge0\), define a matrix \(\mathcal G^+_{N,J,\rho}\) on the exact support (2) by \[ (\mathcal G^+_{N,J,\rho})_{(b+k,j);(j+k,b)} =\chi_N(j,b,k)\frac{a_\lambda e^{NM_\lambda}}{\sqrt{2N}}\, e^{-y^{\mathsf T}H_\lambda y/2} \sum_{l=0}^J N^{-l/2}P_{\lambda,l}(y), \quad y=\frac{(j,b,k)-Nz_\lambda}{\sqrt N}, \quad\lambda=\lambda_+(\rho). \tag{10} \] It is zero at every other entry. Define the negative model by the same flip-conjugation as (6). **Theorem.** For either sign, uniformly when its induced tilt belongs to \(\Lambda\), \[ \boxed{\quad \frac{\|R^\pm_\rho-\mathcal G^\pm_{N,J,\rho}\|_{\rm HS}} {\|R^\pm_\rho\|_{\rm HS}} \le C_J N^{-(J+1)/2}. \quad} \tag{11} \] In particular a sufficiently small fixed ball of four boundary weights works simultaneously for both signs, at all sufficiently large integer levels, without a parity restriction. Moreover \[ \|R^\pm_\rho\|_{\rm HS}^2 =\sqrt N\,\frac{\pi^{3/2}a_\lambda^2} {2\sqrt{\det H_\lambda}}\, e^{2NM_\lambda}(1+O(N^{-1})), \quad \lambda=\lambda_\pm(\rho). \tag{12} \] At zero tilt this is \(\sqrt N\,e^{4GN/\pi}/4\,(1+O(N^{-1}))\). We specify the correction polynomials and prove the global error. On a fixed compact subinterval of \(0<x<1\), the sine product has, for every fixed order, an expansion \[ s_n=\sqrt{2N\sin\pi x}\,e^{Nh(x)} \left(1+\sum_{r=1}^L N^{-r}b_r(x)+O_L(N^{-L-1})\right), \quad x=n/N . \tag{13} \] The coefficient functions are real analytic on interior intervals; the remainder bound is needed only on the actual grid. To obtain it, write \(\log(2\sin\pi x)=\log(2\pi x)+g(x)\), where \(g=\log(\sin\pi x/(\pi x))\) is smooth at zero. Apply the finite Euler--Maclaurin formula to \(\sum g(j/N)\) and the factorial form of the same formula to \(\log(n!)\), with its \(\tfrac12\log(2\pi)\) constant fixed by the Wallis product. Their leading terms combine to \(Nh(x)+\tfrac12\log(2N\sin\pi x)\). At each requested order, apply the formulas two orders farther: the integral remainder is bounded by the next power of \(N^{-1}\) times a fixed derivative bound. This proves the asserted grid remainder. Subtracting also \(\log(1-x)\) leaves a smooth function on the full interval and proves the weaker endpoint estimate used above. Consequently the positive amplitude in (2), including its tilt, is \[ \frac{a(z)}{\sqrt{2N}}e^{NS_\lambda(z)} \left(1+\sum_{r=1}^L N^{-r}c_r(z)+O_L(N^{-L-1})\right) \tag{14} \] uniformly on an interior neighborhood of all \(z_\lambda\). The \(c_r\) are fixed by the five products in (2), not fitted data. With a formal variable \(\eta\), define \(P_{\lambda,l}\) as the coefficient of \(\eta^l\) in \[ \frac{a(z_\lambda+\eta y)}{a_\lambda} \left(1+\sum_{r\ge1}\eta^{2r}c_r(z_\lambda+\eta y)\right) \exp\left\{\sum_{r\ge3}\frac{\eta^{r-2}}{r!} S^{(r)}(z_\lambda)[y^r]\right\}. \tag{15} \] Only finitely many derivatives enter each coefficient. Every monomial has degree at most three times its \(\eta\)-order, and \(P_{\lambda,l}(-y)=(-1)^lP_{\lambda,l}(y)\). For completeness, fix \(J\) and choose a small \(\beta>0\), for example \(\beta<1/(12(J+2))\). On \(|y|\le N^\beta\), Taylor's formula in (14)--(15), with \(L\) sufficiently large, bounds the entry error by \[ C_J\,\frac{e^{NM_\lambda}}{\sqrt N}\, N^{-(J+1)/2}(1+|y|^{C_J})e^{-c|y|^2}. \tag{16} \] The bound follows by keeping the exponential remainder: \(N|z-z_\lambda|^3\le C N^{-1/2}|y|^3=o(1)\) there. The omitted Taylor terms have the stated power of \(N^{-1/2}\) times a fixed polynomial. Positive definiteness absorbs their remaining exponential factors into the displayed Gaussian. The lattice spacing in \(y\) is \(N^{-1/2}\), so the sum of a fixed Gaussian polynomial is \(O(N^{3/2})\), uniformly in the shifted center. The squared error from (16) is therefore at most \(C_J\sqrt N e^{2NM_\lambda}N^{-J-1}\). On the rest of a fixed interior neighborhood, strict concavity gives the same Gaussian upper bound for (14), and for (10). The part \(|y|>N^\beta\) is smaller than every power of \(N^{-1}\). Outside that neighborhood the compact global loss and the endpoint-uniform \(O(\log N)\) estimate give at most a polynomial times \(e^{2N(M_\lambda-\gamma)}\) for the squared norm. The model has the same negligible tail by its Gaussian bound. A ball of \(O(\sqrt N)\) lattice indices about \(Nz_\lambda\) gives the uniform lower bound \(c\sqrt N e^{2NM_\lambda}\) for \(\|R^+_\rho\|_{\rm HS}^2\). These estimates prove (11) globally. To obtain (12), use \(J=1\). The term of order \(N^{-1/2}\) in the squared model is odd in \(y\), by (15). Gaussian-polynomial lattice sums differ from their continuum integrals by \(O(e^{-cN})\), uniformly in their shift: periodize the Gaussian on the mesh, compute its Fourier coefficients by the real Gaussian integral, and differentiate that formula for polynomial factors. Every nonzero dual lattice point has an \(e^{-cN|m|^2}\) factor. Extending our interior lattice to all of \(\mathbb Z^3\) costs only an exponential tail. The leading integral is \(\pi^{3/2}/\sqrt{\det H_\lambda}\). Together with \(N^3/(2N)\) and the Gaussian scale \(N^{-3/2}\) this gives (12). Equation (6) proves all negative-sign assertions. ## 4. Full packets, interfaces, and scope At zero tilt, [P] identifies the complete physical algebra \(\mathcal A_N=\mathbb C[\Omega]\) as an \(N\)-dimensional subspace of these pair matrices. Let \(\Pi_N\) be its physical orthogonal projection. Since \(R^\pm\in\mathcal A_N\), projection cannot increase the error in (11). Thus \(\Pi_N\mathcal G^\pm_{N,J,0}\) is an actual full-boundary approximation at the same rate. No value quotient or deletion of double-root normal directions occurs. For nonzero tilts the correct space is the exact linear image \(W_{\rm out}\mathcal A_NW_{\rm in}^{-1}\); its orthogonal projection has the same contraction property in the Hilbert--Schmidt norm of the gauged arrays. It need not be the original algebra or preserve multiplication. Undoing the gauges can cost exponentially in \(N\). Both incident interface factors, original caps and physical budgets must therefore be retained in a proposed network use. No free transfer of (11) to an untilted whole-component error or unchanged new budgets is claimed. The two Gaussian models are not asserted to be exact mutual inverses. [W] already proves the compact weighted norm rate and the unique flat maximum. [G, Section 4] already proves a full Hilbert--Schmidt Gaussian operator limit for the \(N\times N\) Newton-coordinate crossing. That coefficient-space metric differs from the uniform physical \(N^2\times N^2\) array here. The Newton row covariance in [N] and the coherent lower-donor kernels in [H] are further closest coverage. The present addition is the entire physical-matrix Gaussian expansion with arbitrary fixed-order Hilbert--Schmidt errors and its prefactor. No general novelty for lattice Laplace expansions is claimed. Small boundary tilts have not been matched to arbitrary geometric Conway data. Even a full-matrix relative error can exceed the original closing overlap. Neither a whole short-component propagation theorem nor a scalar geometric lower or finite-exception theorem follows. ## Complete inputs and coverage All six complete matching texts were read. Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used; no earlier final was edited. | Label | Complete text | SHA-256 | | --- | --- | --- | | B, input, 247 lines | [Balanced physical crossing](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/balanced_verma_coherent_braiding.md) | 0203bdd7dbb36a4f8deb1c310b3445608e53d10922049447da8eecec4f87d1c4 | | W, input, 244 lines | [Weighted crossing rate](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/weighted_crossing_source_gap.md) | a6a6411a780c904493db4fca3b5536f902aa5be8b6ef7cfb880a4f57509f436c | | P, input, 477 lines | [Uniform physical algebra](research_conway_uniform_physical_quartic.md) | 39895b430535f565d30133b46ef57f67589207bc83f40597ffe96e2ce79bbda8 | | N, coverage, 415 lines | [Newton row covariance](research_actual_newton_crossing_gaussian_covariance.md) | ce2b1b8efbbcffa8bafe0d0de4f7ce12febf193e433d8e3291f7d2a8c826fa3f | | H, coverage, 398 lines | [Physical hybrid lower kernel](research_physical_crossing_hybrid_lower_kernel.md) | 3025b561b9e30503de6eb2fe6ca265f04cfa730313c77c2156d3fc3b35f8926f | | G, coverage, 468 lines | [Newton full Gaussian operator limit](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_one_crossing_gaussian_window.md) | d5d8611da7158539ee73af5413ab2f59da50afe5d3d43dcf2631f4c28f373683 |

title: A joint physical Gaussian packet for a fixed crossing fan
text:
# A joint physical Gaussian packet for a fixed crossing fan 24 November 2026. Research proof. Earlier finals and manuscripts are unchanged. A fixed positive fan has one transfer path at each nonzero matrix entry. Its whole physical Hilbert--Schmidt norm and joint Gaussian packet can therefore be calculated before any closing. The result includes a nonzero coefficient between independently specified product Gaussian boundary vectors. It does not estimate the prescribed knot closing. The same bipyramid volume already occurs in the Fourier bridge coordinates of [B]; the new assertions concern the original physical fan matrix, its joint norm, and its prepared physical boundary vectors. ## 1. The exact fan, including its phase Fix an integer \(r\ge1\), independently of \(N\ge2\). Put \[ D=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\quad x_0=-q^{-1}, \quad \kappa=q^{D^2/2},\quad s_j=\prod_{h=1}^j2\sin(\pi h/N),\quad s_0=1. \] Use the uniform physical orthonormal head basis of [G]. All matrix norms below are unnormalized Hilbert--Schmidt norms unless specified. Let \(R_i^+\) act on heads \(i,i+1\), and set \[ \mathsf F_{r,N}=R_r^+\cdots R_1^+. 	ag{1} \] For input \((a,b_1,\ldots,b_r)\), write \(K_i=k_1+\cdots+k_i\), \[ d=a-K_r,\qquad j_i=a-K_i=d+\sum_{h>i}k_h. \] The output is \((b_1+k_1,\ldots,b_r+k_r,d)\). Its nonzero support is exactly \[ d,k_i,b_i\ge0,\qquad d+\sum_i k_i\le D,\qquad b_i+k_i\le D. 	ag{2} \] The input and output determine every \(k_i\), so there is no internal sum at one entry. The exact coefficient in [G, (2)--(3)] telescopes to \[ (\mathsf F_{r,N})_{m out,in} =\Xi_N(d, oldsymbol k, oldsymbol b)  rac{s_a}{s_d}\prod_{i=1}^r  rac{s_{b_i+k_i}}{s_{b_i}s_{k_i}}, \quad \Xi_N=\prod_{i=1}^r\chi_N(j_i,b_i,k_i), 	ag{3} \] \[ \chi_N(j,b,k)=\kappa x_0^{-j-b}Q^{jb}(-i)^k q^{k(j+b)+k(k+1)/2},\qquad |\Xi_N|=1. \] All powers mean the displayed exponentials. The Cartan scalar is \(\kappa^r\); it has not been removed. The integer coordinates \(n=(d, oldsymbol k, oldsymbol b)\) in (2) parametrize entries once, on a primitive lattice of dimension \(\ell=2r+1\). ## 2. The complete joint maximum Write \(z=(x, oldsymbol t, oldsymbol v)=n/N\), \(T=\sum_i t_i\), and \(\mathfrak a=x+T\). Define \[ h(u)=\int_0^u\log(2\sin\pi v)\,dv,\qquad S_r(z)=h(\mathfrak a)-h(x)+ \sum_i\{h(v_i+t_i)-h(v_i)-h(t_i)\}. 	ag{4} \] Its compact domain is \(x,t_i,v_i\ge0\), \(x+T\le1\), \(v_i+t_i\le1\). The uniform factorial bound of [G] gives the entry rate \(NS_r+O_r(\log N)\) on the entire finite support. For fixed \(0<t<1\), \(h(v+t)-h(v)-h(t)\) is strictly concave in \(v\in(0,1-t)\), since its second derivative is \(-\pi\sin(\pi t)/(\sin\pi v\sin\pi(v+t))<0\). Its maximum is at \(v=(1-t)/2\), and its value is \(-2h(t/2)\). Here reflection \(h(1-u)=-h(u)\) and \[ h(2u)=2h(u)-2h(1/2-u),\qquad 0\le u\le1/2, \] prove the value; the latter identity follows by differentiation and its zero value at \(u=0\). Continuity includes \(t=0,1\). For fixed \(\mathfrak a=a\) and \(T=K\), strict convexity of \(h\) on \([0,1/2]\) gives equal \(t_i=K/r\). Thus the remaining maximum is \[ \max_{0\le K\le a} \{h(a)-h(a-K)-2r h(K/(2r))\} =I_r(a):=h(a)-(2r+1)h(a/(2r+1)). 	ag{5} \] Indeed the derivative in \(K\) is \(\log[\sin\pi(a-K)/\sin(\pi K/(2r))]\). For \(0<K<a\le1\), the sum of the two sine arguments, divided by \(\pi\), is less than one. The sine-difference formula therefore makes its sign that of \(a-K-K/(2r)\). This proves the unique maximum \(K=2ra/(2r+1)\), with endpoint values obtained by continuity. Finally \(I_r'(a)=\log[\sin\pi a/\sin(\pi a/(2r+1))]\) changes sign only at the following point. Put \[ \delta= rac{\pi}{2r+2},\quad x_*={1\over2r+2},\quad t_{i,*}={1\over r+1},\quad v_{i,*}={r\over2r+2},\quad \mathfrak a_*={2r+1\over2r+2}. 	ag{6} \] This is the unique global maximum of \(S_r\), including its boundary, and \[ M_r=-(2r+2)h(1/(2r+2)). 	ag{7} \] Every maximizing transfer is strictly positive, so the possible nonuniqueness in the recipient optimization at \(t=0\) is irrelevant. For clarity, (7) is the previously occurring bipyramid value, not a new volume formula. With \(\Lambda(	heta)=-\int_0^	heta \log(2\sin u)\,du\), it is \(2\pi M_r=2(2r+2)\Lambda(\pi/(2r+2))\). Place \(n_0=2r+2\) equally spaced equatorial vertices on a circle of the ideal boundary sphere, with the two ideal apices at the poles. In the Klein ball, subdivision about their axis gives \(n_0\) ideal tetrahedra with angle triples \((2\pi/n_0,\pi/2-\pi/n_0,\pi/2-\pi/n_0)\). The ideal-tetrahedron Lobachevsky formula and its duplication identity give volume \(2\Lambda(\pi/n_0)\) for each. Thus \(2\pi M_r\) is the volume of the regular ideal \(n_0\)-gonal bipyramid. ## 3. Hessian, density, and the whole norm Set \(\alpha=\pi\cot\delta\), \( eta=\pi	an\delta\). In coordinate order \((x, oldsymbol t, oldsymbol v)\), \(H=-S_r''(z_*)\) has blocks \[ H_{xx}=2\alpha,\quad H_{x oldsymbol t}=\alpha oldsymbol1^{\mathsf T}, \quad H_{x oldsymbol v}=0,\quad H_{ oldsymbol t oldsymbol t} =\alpha oldsymbol1 oldsymbol1^{\mathsf T} +{\alpha+ eta\over2}I, \quad H_{ oldsymbol t oldsymbol v}= eta I, \quad H_{ oldsymbol v oldsymbol v}=2 eta I. 	ag{8} \] Eliminate the \(v\) block and then the \(x\) block. The remaining Schur block is \((\alpha/2)(I+ oldsymbol1 oldsymbol1^{\mathsf T})\). Consequently \(H>0\), and \[ \det H=2(r+1)\pi^{2r+1}\cot\delta. 	ag{9} \] The interior sine-factorial expansion in [G] gives the entry modulus \((2N)^{-r/2}A(z)e^{NS_r(z)}(1+O_r(N^{-1}))\), where \[ A(z)^2={\sin\pi\mathfrak a\over\sin\pi x} \prod_i{\sin\pi(v_i+t_i)\over\sin\pi v_i\sin\pi t_i}, \qquad A_*^2=\sin(2\delta)^{-r}. 	ag{10} \] **Norm theorem.** Through all sufficiently large integer levels, \[  oxed{\quad \|\mathsf F_{r,N}\|_{m HS}^2 =C_r\sqrt N\,e^{2NM_r}(1+O_r(N^{-1})),\qquad C_r={ (2\sin(2\delta))^{-r}\over \sqrt{2(r+1)\cot\delta}}. \quad} 	ag{11} \] The lattice density is \(N^\ell\), the squared density in (10) contributes \((2N)^{-r}\), and the Gaussian integral contributes \(N^{-\ell/2}\pi^{\ell/2}/\sqrt{\det H}\). Their product is \(\sqrt N\,2^{-r}\pi^{\ell/2}A_*^2/\sqrt{\det H}\), which is (11). The next section proves the uniform error and both parities. At \(r=1\), (11) is precisely [G]'s prefactor \(1/4\). ## 4. Full fixed-order packets and real boundary tilts For prescribed real input weights \((ho_0,\ldots,ho_r)\) and output weights \((\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_r,\sigma_0)\), use diagonal factors \(e^{ho_0a+\sumho_i b_i}\) and \(e^{\sum\sigma_i(b_i+k_i)+\sigma_0d}\), called \(W_{m in}\) and \(W_{m out}\). The gauged fan \(W_{m out}\mathsf F_{r,N}W_{m in}^{-1}\) adds exactly \[ \lambda_x=\sigma_0-ho_0,\qquad \lambda_{t_i}=\sigma_i-ho_0,\qquad \lambda_{v_i}=\sigma_i-ho_i 	ag{12} \] to the entropy as \(\lambda\cdot z\). This map is onto; a common shift of all boundary weights has no effect. Compactness and (8) give a fixed small closed tilt ball on which the global maximizer \(z_\lambda\) remains unique and interior, with uniformly positive \(H_\lambda=-S_r''(z_\lambda)\). Put \(M_\lambda=S_r(z_\lambda)+\lambda\cdot z_\lambda\), \(A_\lambda=A(z_\lambda)\). For every fixed \(J\ge0\), there are real polynomials \(P_{\lambda,l}(y)\), analytic in \(\lambda\), with \(P_{\lambda,0}=1\), degree at most \(3l\), and parity \(l\). On the exact support (2), define the model by \[ \mathcal G_{r,N,J,\lambda} =\Xi_N(n)(2N)^{-r/2}A_\lambda e^{NM_\lambda} e^{-y^{\mathsf T}H_\lambda y/2} \sum_{l=0}^J N^{-l/2}P_{\lambda,l}(y), \qquad y={n-Nz_\lambda\over\sqrt N}. 	ag{13} \] It is zero elsewhere. If \(\mathsf F_{r,N,\lambda}\) denotes the gauged array, then uniformly on that ball, \[ {\|\mathsf F_{r,N,\lambda}-\mathcal G_{r,N,J,\lambda}\|_{m HS} \over\|\mathsf F_{r,N,\lambda}\|_{m HS}} \le C_{r,J}N^{-(J+1)/2},\qquad \|\mathsf F_{r,N,\lambda}\|_{m HS}^2 ={2^{-r}\pi^{\ell/2}A_\lambda^2\over\sqrt{\det H_\lambda}} \sqrt N e^{2NM_\lambda}(1+O_r(N^{-1})). 	ag{14} \] Here is the quantitative argument, rather than a formal expansion. The all-order sine-product formula [G, (13)] applied to (3) gives the density (10) times \(1+\sum_{j\ge1}N^{-j}c_j(z)\), with analytic \(c_j\) and a uniform remainder at each fixed order. Define \(P_{\lambda,l}\) by extracting \(\eta^l\) from \[ {A(z_\lambda+\eta y)\over A_\lambda} \left(1+\sum_{j\ge1}\eta^{2j}c_j(z_\lambda+\eta y)ight) \exp\left\{\sum_{j\ge3}{\eta^{j-2}\over j!} S_r^{(j)}(z_\lambda)[y^j]ight\}. 	ag{15} \] Only finitely many derivatives enter. For a small fixed \(b<1/(12(J+2))\), Taylor remainders on \(|y|\le N^b\) bound the entry error by \(C e^{NM_\lambda}N^{-r/2-(J+1)/2}(1+|y|^C)e^{-c|y|^2}\). The exponent remainder \(O(N^{-1/2}|y|^3)\) is \(o(1)\) there; the retained remainder bound is a Gaussian polynomial, so summing its square costs only \(O(N^{\ell/2})\), without a power loss. The intermediate tail is smaller than every algebraic order by the negative local Hessian. The compact global gap and uniform endpoint factorial bound control all other entries exponentially. A fixed rescaled ball supplies the matching norm lower bound. This proves the first part of (14). For \(J=1\), its relative error is \(O(N^{-1})\); the order-\(N^{-1/2}\) squared correction is odd. Gaussian-polynomial mesh sums have exponentially small errors uniformly in their fractional centers, by periodization and the Gaussian Fourier integral as in [G]. This proves the second part of (14), including all parity and rounding shifts. ## 5. A degree-\(r\) optimizer for an entire donor-tilt chamber Multiply the input column with donor index \(a\) by \(e^{\eta a}\), where \(\eta\) is any fixed real number. This is (12)'s direction \(\lambda=\eta(1, oldsymbol1, oldsymbol0)\). Formula (5) reduces the whole maximization exactly to \(I_r(A)+\eta A\), \(0\le A\le1\). Put \(m=2r+1\). The function \(u\cot u\) strictly decreases on \((0,\pi)\): its derivative has numerator \(\sin u\cos u-u<0\). Consequently \[ I_r''(A)=\pi\cot(\pi A)-{\pi\over m}\cot(\pi A/m)<0,\quad I_r'(0+)=\log m,\quad I_r'(1-)=-\infty. 	ag{16} \] There is a unique interior maximizer \(A_\eta\) precisely when \(\eta>-\log m\). It solves \(\sin(\pi A_\eta)/\sin(\pi A_\eta/m)=e^{-\eta}\). For \(\eta\le-\log m\) the maximum is \(A=0\), with value zero; no interior Gaussian assertion is made there. Writing \(	heta=\pi A_\eta/m\), the interior optimizer is \(x=	heta/\pi\), \(t_i=2	heta/\pi\), \(v_i=1/2-	heta/\pi\), and is determined by the single polynomial \[ P_r(y)=e^{-\eta},\qquad P_r(y)=U_{2r}(\sqrt y) =4^r\prod_{j=1}^r\left(y-\cos^2{j\pi\over m}ight), \quad \cos^2(\pi/m)<y=\cos^2	heta<1. 	ag{17} \] Here \(U_0(z)=1,U_1(z)=2z\), and \(U_{j+1}(z)=2zU_j(z)-U_{j-1}(z)\), define the Chebyshev polynomials of the second kind. The sine identity for \(U_{2r}\) proves (17); its paired roots and leading coefficient give the product, and the recurrence proves integer coefficients. On the displayed interval every factor is positive and strictly increasing, so \(P_r\) increases from zero to \(m\). Its degree is \(r\), independently of \(N\). For example \(P_1=4y-1\), \(P_2=16y^2-12y+1\). This is the explicit fan norm optimizer, not a knot \(A\)-polynomial. For the full Hessian, put \(\alpha=\pi\cot	heta,\  eta=\pi	an	heta,\ \gamma=\pi\cot(m	heta)\). Its \(x,t\) block is \(\operatorname{diag}(\alpha,(\alpha+ eta)I/2) -\gamma oldsymbol1 oldsymbol1^{\mathsf T}\); the \(v\) block is \(2 eta I\) and its only cross block is \(H_{tv}= eta I\). Eliminating \(v\) leaves \(\operatorname{diag}(\alpha,\alpha I/2) -\gamma oldsymbol1 oldsymbol1^{\mathsf T}\). This is positive definite since \(\alpha-m\gamma>0\), by (16), and \[ \det H_\eta=\pi^{2r+1}\{\cot	heta-m\cot(m	heta)\},\qquad A(z_\eta)^2=e^{-\eta}\sin(2	heta)^{-r}. 	ag{18} \] The second formula follows from (10) and the stationary sine ratio. The determinant follows from the one rank-one Schur block. Thus, writing \(M_\eta=I_r(A_\eta)+\eta A_\eta\), \[ \|\mathsf F_{r,N,\eta}\|_{m HS}^2 =\sqrt N\,e^{2NM_\eta} {e^{-\eta}(2\sin2	heta)^{-r}\over \sqrt{\cot	heta-m\cot(m	heta)}}(1+O(N^{-1})). 	ag{19} \] The packet estimate (14) holds uniformly over every fixed compact subinterval of \(\eta>-\log m\), also allowing sufficiently small full boundary perturbations there. Indeed these maxima stay uniformly interior, (18) gives positive Hessians, and compactness preserves the global gap. The proof of (14) then applies unchanged. No geometric interpretation of this entire donor-tilt chamber is asserted. ## 6. An independently specified product boundary coefficient The following is an actual open coefficient, rather than an unknown boundary state supplied as input. Let \(L_{m in},L_{m out}\) be the fixed integer matrices sending \(n\) to the input and output lists in (3), and stack them as \(L\). This matrix has full column rank: its input list contains every \(b_i\), its output contains \(d\), and \(k_i=\mathrm{out}_i-b_i\). Set \(
u_{m in}=L_{m in}z_*\), \(
u_{m out}=L_{m out}z_*\); all these coordinates lie strictly between zero and one. Choose the real quadratic lift \(\Theta_N(n)\) of (3)'s phase using \(\arg\kappa=\pi D^2/(2N)\), \(\log x_0=i(\pi-\pi/N)\), and \(\arg(-i)=-\pi/2\). Thus \(e^{i\Theta_N(n)}=\Xi_N(n)\) at every integer state and \(C=N\Theta_N''\) is a fixed real symmetric matrix. Choose real per-head carriers satisfying \[ L_{m in}^{\mathsf T}	heta_{m in} -L_{m out}^{\mathsf T}	heta_{m out} =-
abla\Theta_N(Nz_*). 	ag{20} \] There is an explicit choice.
