If the right-hand gradient before its minus sign is \(g=(g_x, oldsymbol g_t, oldsymbol g_v)\), take \(	heta_{m in,0}=0,\ 	heta_{m out,0}=g_x,\ 	heta_{m out,i}=g_{t_i},\ 	heta_{m in,i}=g_{t_i}-g_{v_i}\). Every coefficient is known from \(r,N\), independently of a tangle or a closed source. For each coordinate \(
u,	heta\), define a unit head vector \[ \psi_{
u,	heta,N}(j) ={e^{-(j-N
u)^2/(2N)+i	heta(j-N
u)}\over Z_{
u,N}}, \qquad Z_{
u,N}^2=\sum_{j=0}^{D}e^{-(j-N
u)^2/N}. 	ag{21} \] Tensor these vectors with the indicated input/output data to form \(\Psi_{m in,N}\), \(\Psi_{m out,N}\). Then \[  oxed{\quad \langle\Psi_{m out,N},\mathsf F_{r,N}\Psi_{m in,N}angle =e^{NM_r+i\Theta_N(Nz_*)} {2^{(r+1)/2}\pi^{r/2}A_*\over \sqrt{\det(H+L^{\mathsf T}L-iC)}} (1+O_r(N^{-1/2})). \quad} 	ag{22} \] The square root is continued from \(C=0\) inside the accretive complex symmetric matrices, equivalently fixed by the Gaussian integral. Its denominator is nonzero, since the matrix has real part \(H+L^{\mathsf T}L>0\). To prove the formula, each normalizer in (21) is \((\pi N)^{1/4}(1+O(e^{-cN}))\), uniformly in its fractional center. The two tensor boundaries contribute \((\pi N)^{-(r+1)/2}\). Equation (20) cancels the exact phase gradient; the remaining phase is exactly \(\Theta_N(Nz_*)+y^{\mathsf T}Cy/2\). The Gaussian product supplies \(e^{-y^{\mathsf T}L^{\mathsf T}Ly/2}\). Insert (13) at order zero and use the Gaussian-polynomial error estimate just proved, now in the scalar sum. Its mesh contributes \(N^{\ell/2}\), its entry density \((2N)^{-r/2}\), and its integral \((2\pi)^{\ell/2}/\sqrt{\det(H+L^{\mathsf T}L-iC)}\). The powers of \(N\) cancel. The complex Gaussian mesh sum has the same convergence: its Fourier transform is Gaussian and the inverse matrix has positive real part. The same tail bounds apply with the additional Gaussian factors of modulus at most one. This proves (22) with a relative error, because its fixed leading constant is nonzero. It proves no assertion about prescribed knot boundary data. ## 7. Negative fans, interfaces, and the original closing There is a simple flat-metric negative version. In the same order put \(\mathsf F^-_{r,N}=R_r^-\cdots R_1^-\). Its input/output path is \((a, oldsymbol b)\mapsto (b_1-k_1,\ldots,b_r-k_r,a+K_r)\), with \(k_i\le b_i\) and \(a+K_r\le D\). Its modulus is \(s_{a+K_r}/s_a\prod_i s_{b_i}/(s_{b_i-k_i}s_{k_i})\). Complement every input and output index by \(j\mapsto D-j\). The reflection \(s_j s_{D-j}=N\) identifies this modulus exactly with (3)'s positive modulus on the complemented support. Keep the negative word's own product phase from [G, (6)]. This gives the same flat norm (11) and all-order packet estimate by an entry bijection; no unproved symmetry or inverse approximation is used. Formula (22) was stated only for the positive fan. The tilts in (12) are actual diagonal gauges. Undoing them can cost exponentially in \(N\); both incident interface factors, original pivots and normalization budgets must remain. These estimates do not identify the tilted maximum with arbitrary geometric Conway data. They describe one fixed fan, not a word with repeated arbitrary crossings, arbitrary signs, or an expression growing with \(N\). The arrays retain the literal full finite head spaces, without a semisimple value quotient. No uniform meridian- or quantum-normal derivative estimate is inferred from the root-level packet theorem. In particular the prepared vectors in (22) are not the original closing. For the usual first-head cut and pivotal tail traces of this braid, the tail support equations include \(b_i=b_{i+1}+k_{i+1}\) for \(i<r\), and \(b_r=d\). For \(r\ge2\) the flat maximum (6) does not satisfy them. Replacing the globally scalar knot cut by a trace-one probe does not remove these internal equations. No scalar geometric lower bound or finite-exception volume theorem follows from this open-fan result. ## Complete inputs and coverage All four complete matching texts were read. [G] supplies the actual entry and fixed-order factorial estimates; all fan optimizations, determinants, prefactors and product probes are derived above. [W] already proves the one-crossing physical weighted norm rate. [B] already has the same regular bipyramid value for a fused Fourier bridge, whose clocks are not termwise physical occupation indices. [D] already proves a nonzero finite factorial-donor coherent kernel on its stated lower-donor scale. Neither is replaced by or claimed to be the joint uniform-physical fan coefficient (22). | Label | Complete text | SHA-256 | | --- | --- | --- | | G, direct, 306 lines | [Whole physical crossing packet](research_full_physical_crossing_gaussian_packet.md) | 7f1b9932f88aa549bc55088b6f056f5a362548bc51c9fdd7c6b00469e725f531 | | W, coverage, 244 lines | [Weighted complete crossing](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/weighted_crossing_source_gap.md) | a6a6411a780c904493db4fca3b5536f902aa5be8b6ef7cfb880a4f57509f436c | | B, coverage, 301 lines | [Role frames and bridge angles](research_rivin_role_frames_and_bridge_angles.md) | 125155bcd008e24bf5714457d9c6d1788a152bc563380f859c80bfe8b997ccf8 | | D, coverage, 392 lines | [Finite donor coherent sum](research_reduced_euler_donor_coherent_sum.md) | ff35583f203ae7686de4ff7fb91fcb4d4d0190e4f8995bd89a871849bc91d7f4 | Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used. title: Full-Psi ray patterns on the actual crossing boundary

# Full-Psi ray patterns on the actual crossing boundary Private written proof, 17 November 2026. The entire negative-ray functional of the original scalar cycle has a finite, explicit replacement at each original crossing. We compute both signed replacement matrices and their literal nine-cell boundary arrays. This transports a supplied original exterior observation; it does not replace that observation by a fixed-zero cut or by scalarity. The single finite reciprocal wall of [W] is not substituted for a ray. ## 1. The original ray moments and their finite support Put \(N>2\) odd, \(d=N-1\), \(Q=e^{2\pi i/N}\), \(x=-e^{-\pi i/N}\), and \(p_a=(Q;Q)_a\). All residues in square brackets lie in \(0,\ldots,d\). The complete point has \(|x|=1\), \(x^N=1\). The finite moments in [F] are \[ v_{+,a}= rac{(-1)^aQ^{a(a-1)/2}}{p_a},\qquad v_{-,a}= rac{Q^a}{p_a}. 	ag{1} \] Keep the indicated logarithmic lip in the full function \(\Psi_\epsilon\), and define its signed ray coefficient by \[ j_{\epsilon,a}(R)= - rac{\epsilon(-1)^{N-a}}{2\pi i} \int_0^R\Psi_\epsilon(\log r+i\epsilon\pi) r^{N-a-1}\,dr,\qquad 0\le a<N. 	ag{2} \] The circle coefficient is \(v_{\epsilon,a}-j_{\epsilon,a}(R)\). Thus the circle plus (2), including its sign, is exactly (1). From [F,(5)], \[ |j_{\epsilon,a}(1)| \le  rac{\sqrt2}{2\pi(N-a)}. 	ag{3} \] No value at \(a=N\) is used. For an atom chosen as original, circle, or ray, write \(b_{\epsilon,a}\) for respectively \(v_{\epsilon,a}\), \(v_{\epsilon,a}-j_{\epsilon,a}\), or \(j_{\epsilon,a}\). The exact coefficient replacements in the ordered source are \[  egin{array}{c|c} 	ext{atom}&	ext{coefficient of order or head index }a\ \hline U_\pm&x^{-a}Q^{-a}b_{-,a}\ V_\pm&x^{-a}b_{+,a}\ F^{-1}&Q^{-a}b_{-,a}\ F&NQ^{d-a}b_{+,d-a}. \end{array} 	ag{4} \] In particular the reflected factorial uses the complementary moment index, its full \(N\), and its original \(Q\)-shift. One does not replace a factorial coefficient by \(j_{\epsilon,a}\) without these factors. The support assertion used here is the coefficient-independent one in [F, Sections 3 and 8]. It is true for arbitrary numerical atom coefficients and real nonnegative flows: every moment order is in \([0,d]\), both before and after the head-forest contraction. Consequently (4) applies to every circle/ray pattern of the original whole source. It is not an expansion on an independently chosen fixed head torus. ## 2. Every entry of the signed modified crossing Use the strict checked crossings of [E,(1)], with their common Cartan factors \(\kappa^{\pm1}\) retained externally: \[ M_+^0=C D U_+C^{-1},\quad M_-^0=C V_+D^{-1}C^{-1}, \quad C=F_2U_-F_1F_2^{-1},\quad C^{-1}=F_2F_1^{-1}V_-F_2^{-1}. 	ag{5} \] Here \[ D|a,bangle=d_b|a,bangle,\qquad d_b=(-1)^bQ^{b(b-1)/2}x^{-2b}. \] Its Gaussian realization in [F] is integrated with the original Gaussian measure; it gives this same diagonal for every coefficient replacement. At the complete point all \(d_b\) have modulus one. Number the nine moment atoms from right to left: \[  egin{array}{c|ccccccccc} 	ext{number}&1&2&3&4&5&6&7&8&9\ \hline 	ext{atom}&F_2^{-1}&V_-&F_1^{-1}&F_2& U_+\ (\!+\!),\,V_+\ (\!-\!)& F_2^{-1}&F_1&U_-&F_2 . \end{array} 	ag{6} \] Each may have its own choice in (4). Denote its resulting coefficient by \(h_j\). In a positive crossing \(D\) occurs after atom 5 and before atom 6; in a negative crossing \(D^{-1}\) occurs after atom 4 and before atom 5. For input \((a,b)\), output \((u,v)\), and transfer orders \(r,t,s\), put \[ A=a-r+t,\quad B=b+r-t,\quad s=A-u,\qquad g_+(r,t)=d_B,\quad g_-(r,t)=d_{b+r}^{-1}. 	ag{7} \] Then the replacement matrix is exactly \[  oxed{ egin{split} M^\sigma_{uv;ab} ={}&\delta_{u+v,a+b}\,h_9(v)h_1(b)\ &	imes\sum_{r,t} h_2(r)h_3(a-r)h_4(b+r)h_5(t)\, g_\sigma(r,t)h_6(B)h_7(A)h_8(A-u). \end{split}} 	ag{8} \] The ranges are the ordinary integer inequalities \[  egin{split} 0&\le r\le\min(a,d-b),\ 0&\le t\le\min(b+r,d-a+r),\ 0&\le A-u\le\min(A,d-B). \end{split} 	ag{9} \] All external indices lie in \(0,\ldots,d\). The delta in (8) is ordinary integer equality, not merely a congruence. To prove (8), atom 2 sends \((a,b)\) to \((a-r,b+r)\); atom 5 sends that pair to \((A,B)\); atom 8 sends it to \((A-s,B+s)\). The six diagonal factors have the six arguments shown in (8). Truncation of these three transfers gives (9). This proves the formula before any cancellation of coefficients. For the original choices it is (5); for any ray pattern it is its actual full-Psi moment replacement, including all endpoint orders. An immediate coefficient norm bound follows without analyzing cancellation. Each diagonal contributes its coefficient supremum, and each transfer contributes its coefficient \(\ell^1\) norm. The stronger uniform full-ray theorem [A] retains the \(a=d\) endpoint and proves \(c/N\le |j_{\epsilon,a}|\le C/N\), for every physical \(a\) and all sufficiently large \(N\). A ray transfer therefore has norm at most \(C\), a reciprocal factorial ray at most \(C/N\), and a reflected factorial ray at most \(C\). The transfer inverse has norm at most \(CN e^{C\sqrt N}\); the two diagonal inverse bounds are \(CN\) and \(C\). The unit multiples of the truncated shifts in (4) satisfy exactly the hypotheses \(\|T\|\le1,T^N=0\) of [A]. Choosing rays at all nine atoms consequently gives the actual invertible crossing reference \[  oxed{\|M^\sigma_{m ray}\|_2\le C N^{-3},\qquad \|(M^\sigma_{m ray})^{-1}\|_2 \le C N^6e^{C\sqrt N}.} 	ag{10} \] There are three factors of each type; multiplying them in the literal order (5) proves (10). This uses no lower bound for an observed matrix element. For a mixed pattern the product of its actual nine coefficient bounds remains valid; (10) is not asserted for every nonempty ray pattern. ## 3. Both literal Fourier adapters Let \(F_{ia}=N^{-1/2}Q^{ia}\), \(\mathcal F=F\otimes F\), \(D_x|aangle=x^a|aangle\), and let \(P\) flip two heads. The actual bridge proved in [W,(15)] is \[ R^o_M=Q\mathcal F(D_x^{-1}\otimes I)P M (I\otimes D_x)\mathcal F^{-1}. 	ag{11} \] This defines the positive planar replacement for every matrix \(M\); for \(M=M_+^0\) it is the original unbraided crossing. The canonical planar array is \[ R^+_M(i,j,k,l)=Q^{-k-l}(R^o_M)_{ij;kl}. 	ag{12} \] Every displayed adapter in (11) is unitary. In particular no factorial similarity has been suppressed. The negative convention must be derived separately. Put \[ U=\mathcal F^{-1}(D_x\otimes I)P . 	ag{13} \] Transposing (11) and using the actual braid convention \(B_{K,+}=P(R^o)^t\) gives \[ B_{K,+}=Q U(M_+^0)^tU^{-1},\qquad B_{K,-}=Q^{-1}U(M_-^0)^tU^{-1}. 	ag{14} \] The second equation follows by inversion of the first. By [Q, Section 1] the printed negative planar crossing has an additional factor \(Q\), and its cyclic labels are \((i,j,k,l)=(	ext{input}_2,	ext{output}_2, 	ext{output}_1,	ext{input}_1)\). Therefore its raw south-sector replacement is \[ R^-_M(i,j,k,l) =Q^{-j-k}(UM^tU^{-1})_{k,j;l,i}. 	ag{15} \] Its sector is \((0,0,0,1)\). Equations (14),(15) retain the inverse-crossing phase rather than assuming the printed negative matrix is the inverse. ## 4. A single finite entry on the nine-cell boundary Use the actual paired-face coordinates and their two lips: \[ k_m=\alpha_{m,-}-\alpha_{m,+}+h_m,\qquad f_m(k)=s_{0m}^{[k-1]}s_{m5}^{[-k]},\qquad \mathcal A_m(\alpha;i)=f_m(k_m)Q^{ik_m}. 	ag{16} \] Keep the scalar \(C_N(\mathbf s)\) of [C,(4)] unchanged. Write \(\phi_+=3(h_1-1)/2\). For sector \((0,0,0,1)\), [Q,(10)] gives \(d_\chi=1/2-3h_1/2\), so the full exponent in [C,(38)] is \(\phi_-=3(h_1-1)/2+d_\chi+1=0\). This is its retained normalization, not a newly chosen negative-crossing scalar. For a positive replacement set \[ u=[-k_1],\quad v=[-k_2],\quad a=[k_3-1],\quad b=[k_4-1]. \] The complete eight-face replacement array is \[  oxed{\mathcal E_+(M)_\alpha =C_NQ^{\phi_+}s_{05}^d\,N^2Qx^{b-u} \prod_{m=1}^4f_m(k_m)\,M_{v,u;a,b}.} 	ag{17} \] For a negative replacement set \[ \gamma=[-k_1],\quad\delta=[-k_4],\quad \alpha_0=[k_2-1],\quad eta=[k_3-1]. \] Then \[  oxed{\mathcal E_-(M)_\alpha =C_NQ^{\phi_-}s_{05}^d\,N^2x^{ eta-\delta} \prod_{m=1}^4f_m(k_m)\, M_{\gamma,\delta;\alpha_0, eta}.} 	ag{18} \] In (17),(18), substitute the explicit sum (8) for the matrix entry. This describes every boundary coefficient and its exact support. For example the positive support satisfies \([{-k_1}]+[{-k_2}]=[k_3-1]+[k_4-1]\), as ordinary integers. It implies \(\sum_mk_m=2\) modulo \(N\), but the integer equality and the path inequalities (9) are stronger. Here is the direct Fourier proof, including its normalizations. Substitute (11),(12) in \[ C_NQ^{\phi_+}s_{05}^d \sum_{i,j,k,l}R^+_M(i,j,k,l) \prod_m f_m(k_m)Q^{i_mk_m}. 	ag{19} \] The four finite sums force the four residues in (17). They contribute \(N^4\); the two two-head Fourier factors contribute \(N^{-2}\). The remaining diagonal is \(Qx^{b-u}\). For (15), expand \[ (UM^tU^{-1})_{k,j;l,i} =N^{-2}\sum_{h,g,h',g'} Q^{-kg-jh+g'l+h'i}x^{g-g'}M_{h',g';h,g}. \] The four sums now force \((h',g',h,g)=(\gamma,\delta,\alpha_0, eta)\); their remaining factor is precisely that in (18). This proves both identities without an inverse-crossing estimate. For the original matrix (19) is the literal nine-cell array by [C]. For a replacement it defines its specified all-boundary insertion through the same proved invertible port maps. No cyclic seam has been smoothed. In particular \[  rac{f_m(k+1)}{f_m(k)} = rac{s_{0m}}{s_{m5}} \left[1+\left( rac{s_{m5}^N}{s_{0m}^N}-1ight) \delta_{k0}ight]. 	ag{20} \] An arbitrary sector gauge is carried by the actual port translations of [W,(28)], and the full scalar of [C,(38)]. It cannot be imposed on (17) without those same translations. On fixed compact sets of injective real decorations, with real odd roots, \(|C_N|=N^{-2}\), and all other absolute factors in (17),(18) are bounded above and below independently of \(N\). Thus, for the unnormalized Euclidean norm on all eight face indices, \[ c_KN^2\|M\|_{m HS}\le \|\mathcal E_\sigma(M)\|_2 \le C_KN^2\|M\|_{m HS}. 	ag{21} \] Indeed the residue-to-matrix-index map is a bijection, and each four-residue choice has \(N^4\) face-pair lifts. Since \(\|M\|_{m HS}\le N\|M\|_2\), (10) gives the explicit all-ray array bound \(C_K\), for all sufficiently large levels. The opposite singular-value bound in (10) also gives \(\|\mathcal E_\sigma(M_{m ray})\|_2 \ge c_KN^{-3}e^{-C\sqrt N}\). These are replacement-array bounds, not bounds for a quotient by an exponentially small observed scalar. ## 5. The original relative functional and exterior row For an unintegrated ray coordinate \(t>0\), use the density \[ \omega_\epsilon(t)= - rac{\epsilon}{2\pi i} \Psi_\epsilon(\log t+i\epsilon\pi)(-t)^N\, rac{dt}{t} 	ag{22} \] and replace its moment coefficient in (4) by \((-t)^{-a}\). For a circle use its original circle density and \(t^{-a}\). The matrix (8) and arrays (17),(18) are then finite Laurent polynomials of degree at most \(d\) in each inverse moment variable. Their integrals against (22) give exactly the integrated formulas (2),(4),(8). The Gaussian variables retain their original measure. This exchange of contraction and integration is the actual one in [F], not a new convergence assumption. Its continuous-flow bound is \(\prod_{m rays}t^{-d}\) times a fixed polynomial in logarithms and \(\exp(C_{m word}N(1+\sum|\xi|))\). Since \(|\omega_\epsilon(t)|=\sqrt{1+t}\,t^{N-1}dt/(2\pi)\), the inner ends are integrable, including the original coupled caps. The Gaussian weight controls the displayed \(\xi\) factor. Therefore all finite contractions above commute with the original joint integral. Common radial cutoffs and the original lip/interval gluing are retained when taking relative boundaries. No period is assigned separately to a divergent component of an intersecting wall decomposition. The exterior is not changed to a favorable cut. For example, in the literal averaged braid presentation of [E,(4)], a whole-word matrix \(T\) has the specified observation \[ 
u_E(T)= rac1N \sum_{p,q=0}^d\sum_{\mathbf a\in\{0,\ldots,d\}^{b-1}} \left(\prod_{j=2}^b g_{a_j}ight) T_{(q,\mathbf a);(p,\mathbf a)},\qquad g_a=x^{1-N}Q^{-a}. 	ag{23} \] The same formula applies to every modified word. For the plat presentation the original cup/cap tensors in [F] remain in its exterior contraction. Equation (23) is not replaced by \(T_{00}\). Each local change of coordinates (11)--(19) transports that exterior by its inverse dual, with all pivots and Cartan factors still attached. Hence the transformed ray-pattern contraction is exactly the original pattern observation, even when it is zero. The inverse dual here can be printed without an unspecified choice of exterior. Suppose the selected crossing acts in positions \(i,i+1\), and write the original modified word as \(T=T_>(M\otimes I)T_<\), retaining its order. Use \((u,v;\mathbf s)\) for the \(b\)-head vector with \(u,v\) in those positions. Its actual exterior coefficient is \[ \eta_{uv;ab}= rac1N \sum_{p,q,\mathbf a,\mathbf s} \left(\prod_{j=2}^b g_{a_j}ight) (T_>)_{(q,\mathbf a);(u,v;\mathbf s)} (T_<)_{(a,b;\mathbf s);(p,\mathbf a)} . 	ag{23b} \] Thus \(
u_E(T)=\sum_{uvab}\eta_{uv;ab}M_{uv;ab}\) before any ray integration. The corresponding cup/cap contraction defines the same coefficient for the original plat source. No complex conjugation is used. Write (17) or (18) as \(\mathcal E_\sigma(M)_\alpha =e_{\sigma,\mathbf k}M_{o_\sigma(\mathbf k);i_\sigma(\mathbf k)}\), where the displayed scalar \(e_{\sigma,\mathbf k}\) includes \(C_N,s_{05}^d,N^2\), all phases, and all four \(f\)'s. It is nonzero on the stated regular domain. The literal eight-face exterior is \[ \widehat\eta_\alpha = rac{\eta_{o_\sigma(\mathbf k);i_\sigma(\mathbf k)}} {N^4 e_{\sigma,\mathbf k}},\qquad \sum_\alpha\widehat\eta_\alpha\mathcal E_\sigma(M)_\alpha =\sum_{uvab}\eta_{uv;ab}M_{uv;ab}. 	ag{23c} \] The factor \(N^{-4}\) averages exactly the four paired fibers. On the real compact sets in (21), \(\|\widehat\eta\|_2\) is between fixed multiples of \(N^{-2}\|\eta\|_{m HS}\). This does not bound \(\eta\) when the original remaining word has large coefficients. Equations (23b),(23c) specify the original observation on the new boundary, rather than assuming it agrees with a fixed cut. For this explicit braid covector one can bound the entire all-ray pattern. The trace norm of its first-head rank-one cut is one, and the remaining \(b-1\) pivotal factors have trace norms \(N\). Thus \(|
u_E(T)|\le N^{b-1}\|T\|_2\). If the fixed word has \(c\) crossings, (10) gives \[ |P_{m all\,ray}| \le |\chi_{ eta,N}|\,C_{m word}N^{b-1-3c}. 	ag{23a} \] Here \(\chi_{ eta,N}\) is exactly the external source line of [E,(5)], including each omitted \(\kappa^{\pm1}\) once. It has not been renormalized. This estimates one actual whole pattern; it supplies no relative estimate for its mixed companions. If this supplied exterior has already been expressed as an open physical array \(G\) with a specified covector \(
u\), [H] gives the explicit marked closing coupon \[ D_
u=\sum_{i,j}Q^{-i}
u_{ij}|i,jangle\langle i,j|, \qquad N^3 Z_
u(G)=\Delta_N
u(G). 	ag{24} \] It applies to the array produced here without scalarity. It does not identify the actual covector transported from (23) with \(E_{00}\otimes E_{00}\). Equations (17),(18),(23) already give a local source-preserving replacement with its original exterior; (24) records the exact closing once that exterior is supplied in the stated end coordinates. ## 6. The same ray chain through an actual beta elimination There is also a specified boundary coupon when one wants to leave the original nine-cell tensor in place and perform one of its internal finite moves. Fix the original signed matrix \(M_0\) from (5). Its inverse is the opposite signed matrix from that equation, with the external \(\kappa\) convention unchanged. At fixed moment coordinates put \[ D(t)_{o;o'}=\sum_{a,b=0}^d M(t)_{o;ab}(M_0^{-1})_{ab;o'} . 	ag{25} \] Every entry of both matrices on the right is given by (8), using the chosen pattern and the original opposite pattern respectively. The sum has only \(a+b=|o|=|o'|\), as ordinary integers. This is an explicit finite formula for the coupon, not an assumed bound for an inverse crossing. It has degree at most \(d\) in each inverse moment variable, because \(M_0^{-1}\) is independent of those variables. For the positive array write \(u=-k_1,v=-k_2\) and \(u'=-l_1,v'=-l_2\), with residues understood. On its two output paired-face spaces the full coupon is \[ \mathscr D^+_{\alpha; eta}(t) = rac{x^{u'-u}}{N^2}  rac{f_1(k_1)f_2(k_2)}{f_1(l_1)f_2(l_2)} D(t)_{v,u;v',u'} . 	ag{26} \] The other two ports have their specified identity on the paired image. For the negative array its output ports are 1 and 4: \[ \mathscr D^-_{\alpha; eta}(t) = rac{x^{\delta'-\delta}}{N^2}  rac{f_1(k_1)f_4(k_4)}{f_1(l_1)f_4(l_4)} D(t)_{\gamma,\delta;\gamma',\delta'} , 	ag{27} \] where \((\gamma,\delta)=(-k_1,-k_4)\) and \((\gamma',\delta')=(-l_1,-l_4)\). Each \(N^{-2}\) averages the \(N^2\) lifts of the two input differences. Hence (26),(27) act on the paired image and kill the specified complementary kernel. Direct substitution into (17),(18) gives \[ \mathscr D^\sigma(t)\mathcal E_\sigma(M_0) =\mathcal E_\sigma(M(t)). 	ag{28} \] This also proves the placement of every seam in these kernels. Any sector change transports (26),(27) with the same port translations; its nonconstant phase ratio must be retained. The direct replacement bound (21) does not imply a tame norm for (25), whose fixed inverse may have exponential norm. Move (26) to the exterior *bilinear* covector, obtaining \(
u_J(t)\). This includes the original covector, all other coupons, and their exact finite sums. Collapse only its paired fibers: \[ v_J(\mathbf k;t)= \sum_{\alpha:\,\alpha_{m,-}-\alpha_{m,+}+h_m=k_m} 
u_J(t;\alpha). 	ag{29} \] There are \(N^4\) summands in (29). No constancy of the exterior on a fiber is assumed. Here is the first actual beta move in full. Use the canonical nine-cell coordinates of [S,(14)--(17)] and rename its internal variable \(t\) as \(	au\) to distinguish it from ray coordinates. Put \[ K=u+v+1,\qquad L=1-k_1+s+z, \] \[ \Xi_0=u(1+	au)+v(1+s)+(1+	au)(1+s) +z-k_1+(3h_1-1)/2. 	ag{30} \] Then the original pattern observation \(\int\omega_J\sum_{\mathbf k}v_J(\mathbf k;t)B_0(\mathbf k)\) is exactly \[  egin{split} \int\omega_J\! \sum_{\substack{\mathbf k,u,v,	au,s,z\\sum k_m=2}} &v_J(\mathbf k;t)\,\mathfrak n\mathfrak f_{01235} Q^{\Xi_0} W_{1234}(u)W_{1245}(v)W_{2345}(	au) W_{0134}(s)W_{0145}(z)\ &\quad	imes  rac{\overline W_{0235}(K+L)} {\overline W_{0235}(K+L-k_2) \overline W_{1235}(K)\overline W_{0135}(L) \overline W_{0345}(k_4+	au+v+z)} . \end{split} 	ag{31} \] All finite indices in (31) are cyclic, and the support equation is modulo \(N\). Here \(\mathfrak n\) and \(\mathfrak f\) are the literal normalization factors of [S,(15)] and [C,(3)]; none has been absorbed into the co-source. The measure \(\omega_J\) is the product of the chosen original circle/ray measures and Gaussian factors, with its original source lines. For a direct proof apply [C,(9)] only to the actual \(r\)-sum \[ \sum_r Q^{Kr}  rac{W_{0123}(r)}{\overline W_{0125}(r+L)} =\mathfrak f_{01235}  rac{\overline W_{0235}(K+L)} {\overline W_{1235}(K)\overline W_{0135}(L)} . 	ag{32} \] The exterior (29) is independent of this internal \(r\). Deleting the \(rK\) term in [S,(17)] leaves exactly (30), and all its other factors give (31). In particular the two \(0235\) factors have arguments differing by \(k_2\); their ratio is retained. They cannot be canceled as opposite cells without an additional boundary condition. Equation (32) is independent of every ray coordinate. The coefficient degree bound preceding (25), and the original absolute bound in Section 5, therefore justify its passage under the actual integral, not just under a formal finite symbol. At common truncated endpoints it commutes with the relative boundary operation; the same absolute bound takes the inner cutoffs to zero. Original lip and cap-interval seams remain matched. Thus (31) is a source-preserving first beta move for the full ray pattern with its exterior observation, rather than a replacement of one internal \(W\)-factor by \(j_{\epsilon,r}\). For another sector the source is \(Q^{D_\chi(\mathbf k,\mathbf h)}B_0(\mathbf k)\), with \(D_\chi\) exactly [S,(17b)]. Include this factor once in the exterior row (29) before applying (31). The scalar already contained in (17),(18) is not included twice. This gives the same statement for either crossing sign and every transported sector, without a new choice of geometric branch. This calculation does not assign the resulting relative chain a nonzero geometric-thimble coefficient. It supplies a concrete analytic-current interface and retains its observation; it does not justify deleting mixed circle/ray patterns or their cuts. The face formulas have the complete fixed odd-level scope of their sources; they do not assert a generic-meridian or moving-root extension. ## Complete direct sources - [F] [Original full-Psi scalar flow cycle](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_full_psi_scalar_flow_cycle.md), SHA256 692b270aa44922b930a78b25f73626b17027533d62fbec389994b51dda25c7f8. - [E] [Literal Euler/Gaussian network](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_euler_gaussian_cauchy_network.md), SHA256 8ed7102043d69b442400748447dd91d1093ca1b678b6ae6acbdefaec1904317f. - [W] [Original finite wall on the nine-cell boundary](research_actual_reciprocal_wall_nine_cell_boundary.md), SHA256 4a668f917a502a2aba1d6f9f2b4c2e14ef7f8c4b1f17597cd1c73080911c5d3f. - [Q] [Braid cut and global sewing](research_braid_cut_and_global_nine_cell_sewing.md), SHA256 58503fba3cf834269943956429cc7ac6190499da5e40f57c82d8f13ef995b470. - [C] [Exact nine-cell crossing evaluation](research_nine_cell_canonical_crossing_evaluation.md), SHA256 332062e67d64ab4a0767637c0fdd96f186d62c430ad38042aef35ad857d8d7c9. - [S] [Literal nine-cell source and six sums](research_nine_tetrahedron_boundary_source_reduction.md), SHA256 5aeecb0c174f33baa1264bc34c7419d4ccae007e84f4410b3dcb47c6c81c554c. - [H] [Marked cap with a prescribed observation](research_marked_cap_for_arbitrary_open_observations.md), SHA256 607f38636e273742f34c86f7c9ead0bdadb5c9bbe1fb2d441c22181a09e058ab. - [A] [Uniform full-ray moments and finite inverse transport](research_uniform_full_dilogarithm_ray_transport.md), SHA256 5585095f56c1015cabab1409b181eabff4b4dc8fb003191881e97a38a9adf256. No mathematical program or numerical experiment was used.

title: A full-step tensor interface for repeated endpoint turns
text:
# A full-step tensor interface for repeated endpoint turns Private written proof, 16 November 2026. The full angular step preserves the original value-and-first-normal quotient. It therefore permits exact multiplication of already turned source channels, followed by a further original turn. This note gives explicit polynomial conversion formulas, a finite tensor construction, and the actual initial-data budget. It does not establish a regular highest-order coefficient after the final turn, or a growth bound for that final output. ## 1. Source and the quotient-safe full step Retain the original conventions \[ q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad c=q+q^{-1},\quad s=q-q^{-1},\quad \eta=(-1)^{N-1},\quad \kappa=q^{(N-1)^2/2}, \] \[ P_N(Z)=2T_N(Z/2)+2,\qquad \mathcal A_N=\mathbb C[Z]/(P_N), \qquad C f=Zf\pmod {P_N}. \] Here \(T_N\) is Chebyshev's polynomial; \(T\) is the original turn, \(Te_j=e_{N-1-j}\), where \[ e_j(Z)=S_j^{-2}\prod_{a<j}(c_a-Z),\quad c_a=q^{2a+1}+q^{-2a-1},\quad S_j=\prod_{h=1}^j2\sin(h\pi/N). \] The original kernel, trace and signed turns are \[ K_N(w,Z)=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}e_j(w)e_j(Z),\qquad \phi_N(e_i e_j)=\mathbf1_{i+j=N-1}, \] \[ J=TCT,\quad V_n=\kappa^nTR^{-n}T,\quad D_n=V_nCV_{-n},\quad U_	au=V_	au\quad(	au=\pm1). 	ag{1} \] All multiplications in \(\mathcal A_N\) retain its nilpotents. The free parameters are never quotiented. The target is \[ U_	au F,\qquad F=\operatorname{can}\left(Q_{m base}\prod_{i=1}^bV_{n_i}Q_iight), \quad Q_i=\operatorname{can}\prod_{\ell=1}^{r_i} K_N(2\cosh(\alpha_{i\ell}/N),Z). 	ag{2} \] The integers \(b,r_i,n_i\) are fixed; all parameters range over fixed bounded complex sets. A factor with \(n_i=0\) can be absorbed into \(Q_{m base}\), which is another original endpoint product; an empty product is \(1\). Omit every transformed empty factor using the exact identity \(V_n1=1\). Thus every transformed factor retained below has \(r_i\ge1\) and \(n_i
e0\). No transformed factor in (2) is replaced by an endpoint product. Introduce \[ \mathcal B_N=\mathbb C[v,v^{-1}]/((v^N+1)^2), \quad C=v+v^{-1},\quad W=v-v^{-1},\quad E f(v)=f(q^2v). 	ag{3} \] Since \[ v^NP_N(v+v^{-1})=(v^N+1)^2, \] there is an exact presentation \[ \mathcal B_N=\mathcal A_N[v]/(v^2-Cv+1) =\mathcal A_N\oplus W\mathcal A_N. 	ag{4} \] The last equality uses \(W=2v-C\), so it is a free module decomposition, including at the ramified points. Inversion \(\iota:v\mapsto v^{-1}\) fixes the first summand and negates the second. Its invariants are exactly \(\mathcal A_N\). At odd \(N\), the double angular root \(v=-1\) has only a constant invariant local part, agreeing with the simple spectral root \(C=-2\); its odd nilpotent belongs to the second summand. The shift \(E\) preserves the ideal in (3) and permutes its double-root jets. For \(N\ge3\), define on ordinary spectral polynomials \[ \mathsf S= rac{E+E^{-1}}2,\qquad 
abla= rac{E-E^{-1}}{W},\qquad \mathsf D= rac{
abla}{q^2-q^{-2}}. 	ag{5} \] The numerator defining \(
abla\) is anti-invariant and hence is ordinarily divisible by \(W\). This is not an inversion of \(W\) in \(\mathcal B_N\). In particular \[ 
abla P_N=0,\quad \mathsf S P_N=P_N,\quad 
abla(P_N f)=P_N
abla f,\quad \mathsf S(P_N f)=P_N\mathsf S f. 	ag{6} \] Thus all three operators descend to \(\mathcal A_N\). Their exact product rules are \[  egin{split} 
abla(fg)&=(
abla f)\mathsf Sg+\mathsf Sf\,
abla g,\ \mathsf S(fg)&=\mathsf Sf\,\mathsf Sg + rac{C^2-4}{4}
abla f\,
abla g . \end{split} 	ag{7} \] These identities follow by multiplying the two full shifts before taking their sum or difference. For an ordinary Laurent lift \(X\), its two components in (4) are \[ F_X=(X+\iota X)/2,\qquad G_X=(X-\iota X)/(2W). 	ag{8} \] Changing the lift by \(P_N(C)H(v)\) changes each component by a \(P_N\) multiple, because the odd part of \(H\) is divisible by \(W\). Formula (8) is therefore well-defined in the full quotient. At \(v=-1\), \(G_X\) retains the odd first angular jet; dividing only values there would lose it. An angular derivative is not a derivation of \(\mathcal B_N\): it can lower the multiplicity of its defining ideal. All normal equations below mean derivatives of ordinary residuals, evaluated at the physical roots. Equality in (3) guarantees both their values and first derivatives vanish. ## 2. Explicit polynomial conversion to the original operators The following identities eliminate the full-step operators without inverting a physical endpoint factor. Write \(Z=C=v+v^{-1}\) in coefficient calculations, and set \[ d=(Z-c)^3,\quad a=8-cZ-c^2,\quad b=(4-q^{-1}Z)(Z+c)-8q, \] \[ h=- rac{s}{2}(Z^2+cZ-8),\qquad p= rac{-sZ(Z^2+cZ-8)-a(Z^2-4)}4, \] \[ t=8(3-q^2-q^{-1}Z),\qquad r=d-cp-h(4-q^{-1}Z). 	ag{9} \] Then the exact polynomial operator identities are \[  oxed{ egin{split} d(C)
abla&=-b(C)J-q\,a(C)D_1+t(C)I,\ d(C)\mathsf S&=p(C)J+q\,h(C)D_1+r(C)I . \end{split}} 	ag{10} \] Every coefficient in (10) multiplies on the left. The identities hold first on ordinary polynomials and then in \(\mathcal A_N\). In particular they retain every first normal. Here is a direct verification from the original operator. Put \[ A(v)=- rac{(qv-1)^4}{q(v^2-1)(q^2v^2-1)},\qquad B(v)=A(v^{-1}),\qquad r_*=8/(Z+c). \] The physical formulas for \(J,D_1\) give \[  egin{split} J&=r_*-(A+B)\mathsf S-(A-B)W
abla/2,\ D_1&=r_*+q^{-1}(A/v+Bv)\mathsf S +q^{-1}(A/v-Bv)W
abla/2 . \end{split} 	ag{11} \] Their removable interpretation on polynomials is the original one. Direct common-denominator calculation gives \[ A+B= rac8{Z+c}-c,\qquad A/v+Bv=4-q^{-1}Z- rac{8q}{Z+c}, \] \[ (Z+c)W(A-B)=2h,\qquad (Z+c)W(A/v-Bv)/2=p . 	ag{12} \] Consequently (11) becomes \[ -a\mathsf S-h
abla=(Z+c)J-8I,\qquad b\mathsf S+p
abla=q(Z+c)D_1-8qI. 	ag{13} \] The determinant and scalar cancellation are \[ bh-ap=(Z-c)^3(Z+c),\qquad  rac{b+qa}{Z+c}=3-q^2-q^{-1}Z. 	ag{14} \] Cramer's rule in the rational coefficient field proves (10). The coefficient \(r\) can equivalently be obtained by applying the second identity to \(1\), using \(J1=c\) and \(D_11=4q^{-1}-q^{-2}Z\). Both sides of (10) are polynomial operators, so the identities extend across the coefficient poles in (11). No inverse of \(C-c\) has been used in \(\mathcal A_N\). It is a nonunit at the original double endpoint. In particular (10) must not be solved by dropping this factor there. As a normalization check, at the formal limit \(q=1\), away from \(Z=2\), the formulas read \[ 
abla= rac{ZJ+2D_1-8}{(Z-2)^2},\qquad \mathsf S=1+ rac{Z+2}{2(Z-2)}(J-2). 	ag{15} \] This limit is only a check on coefficients, not an inverse operator assertion at the parabolic value. ## 3. Finite actual input columns and their multiplication We specify which input equations are tensorized. For a nonzero \(n_i\), use the pinned endpoint-product system with \[ k_i=33r_i,\quad m_i=|n_i|,\quad M_i=k_i m_i+1,\quad \ell_i=r_i m_i. \] Its actual gauged channels \(W_i\), of length \(6^{r_i}\), and its original product component \(Y_i=V_{n_i}Q_i\) satisfy \[ \{d_i(D_{n_i})(J-c)I-s^2E_i(D_{n_i})\}W_i=0,\qquad (D_{n_i}-2)^{r_i}Y_i=(W_i)_* . 	ag{16} \] Here \(W_i\) already denotes the turned canonical gauged vector. Use the value column of shifts \[ X_i(v)=  ig(E^{-M_i}W_i,\ldots,E^{M_i-1}W_i;\ E^{-\ell_i}Y_i,\ldots,E^{\ell_i-1}Y_i ig). 	ag{17} \] Its rank \(2M_i6^{r_i}+2\ell_i\) is fixed independently of \(N\). The two nonzero rational extreme coefficients proved in the pinned source give rational forward and backward matrices \(M_{i,+}(v),M_{i,-}(v)\). Globally their meaning is the cleared identities \[ a_{i,+}(v)EX_i=B_{i,+}(v)X_i,\qquad a_{i,-}(v)E^{-1}X_i=B_{i,-}(v)X_i \quad\hbox{in }\mathcal B_N. 	ag{18} \] The scalar Laurent polynomials \(a_{i,\pm}\) and matrix Laurent polynomials \(B_{i,\pm}\) have bounded degrees for fixed input data; \(M_{i,\pm}=B_{i,\pm}/a_{i,\pm}\) is a rational calculation only. The source gives their explicit construction by solving the extreme row of (16), and the central forcing in recovery is retained in the same column. Ordinary residuals before solving are \(P_N\) multiples, so multiplying back all denominators gives (18) with full jets. Neither an endpoint inverse nor an off-grid homogeneous identity for a canonical polynomial is asserted. For the unturned product \(Q_{m base}\), the ordinary six-channel module gives a convenient exact input column. Apply its ordinary half shifts twice before canonical reduction. If its ordinary half-step matrices are \(H_\pm(v)\), the full-step matrices are \[ H_+(qv)H_+(v),\qquad H_-(q^{-1}v)H_-(v). 	ag{19} \] These are obtained from the module's displayed half-step mean and divided difference by \(H_\pm=\mathbf S\pm sW\mathbf D/2\), or their tensor versions. All ordinary source channels \(P_N,1\) stay in this calculation: a half step sends \(P_N\) to \(4-P_N\). Only after forming and clearing (19) is the result reduced to (18). This includes the removable forcing \(P_N(Z)/(Z-c)\); it is not set to zero before its denominator has been treated. The input product is a selected component of this unturned column. Tensor these actual columns, including the base column if present. Their entries are ordinary products in the same angular color, not products transported by \(T\). Define \[ X= igotimes_iX_i,\quad A_\pm=\prod_i a_{i,\pm},\quad B_\pm= igotimes_iB_{i,\pm},\quad M_\pm=B_\pm/A_\pm . 	ag{20} \] Then, exactly in the full angular quotient, \[ A_\pm E^{\pm1}X=B_\pm X. 	ag{21} \] This follows by multiplying (18) before taking any normal. The product \(F\) in (2) is a specified component of \(X\): choose the current product component at each factor. It is inversion-invariant. This retains shared parameters and their correlations; there is no coefficientwise absolute majorization. ## 4. Even descent and the next original turn Here are explicit finite matrices for descending (21). For a rational Laurent matrix \(H\), write \[ H_e=(H+\iota H)/2,\qquad H_o=(H-\iota H)/(2W). \] They are rational in \(C\). Set \[ U=M_++M_-,\quad V=M_+-M_-,\quad W_\pm=q^{\pm2}v-q^{\mp2}v^{-1}, \] \[ N_\pm=M_\pm/W_\pm,\qquad U_N=N_++N_-,\quad V_N=N_+-N_- . 	ag{22} \] For the actual descended column \(Z=(F_X,G_X)^{\mathsf T}\) from (8), the rational matrix calculations are \[  egin{split} \mathsf S F_X&=	frac12U_eF_X+	frac12W^2U_oG_X,& 
abla F_X&=V_oF_X+V_eG_X,\ \mathsf S G_X&=	frac12(U_N)_eF_X+	frac12W^2(U_N)_oG_X,& 
abla G_X&=(V_N)_oF_X+(V_N)_eG_X . \end{split} 	ag{23} \] For example \(E\iota X=\iota(E^{-1}X)\); inserting (21) into the sum and difference of \(X,\iota X\) proves the first line after clearing denominators. In the second, \(\iota W_+=-W_-\), which gives the same calculation with \(M_\pm\) replaced by \(N_\pm\). Choose a common nonzero polynomial \(\mathfrak a(C)\) clearing the four matrices in (23), with sufficient multiplicity to clear the explicit linear combinations of (21) and its reflected version used to derive them, before canceling any factor. One can use products of the Laurent denominators and their inversions, and also \(W_+W_-=C^2-(q^2+q^{-2})^2\); their invariant products are spectral polynomials. Further finite powers clear any rational odd parts in (22). All degrees remain bounded independently of \(N\). Denote the resulting polynomial matrices by \(S_0(C),N_0(C)\). Then \[ \mathfrak a(C)\mathsf S Z=S_0(C)Z,\qquad \mathfrak a(C)
abla Z=N_0(C)Z \quad\hbox{in }\mathcal A_N. 	ag{24} \] These are obtained by algebraic combinations of the cleared equations (21), not by localizing \(\mathcal B_N\) and forgetting its killed components. The actual definitions (8), (17), the original equations (16), and their source data are retained alongside (24). In particular (24) alone is not asserted to characterize the source at zeros of \(\mathfrak a\). Substitute (10) into \(d(C)\) times (24). This yields the explicit polynomial, ordered system \[  oxed{ egin{split} \{\mathfrak a(C)[p(C)J+qh(C)D_1+r(C)]-d(C)S_0(C)\}Z&=0,\ \{\mathfrak a(C)[-b(C)J-qa(C)D_1+t(C)]-d(C)N_0(C)\}Z&=0. \end{split}} 	ag{25} \] Applying the actual \(U_	au\) to every component gives these same ordered polynomial relations under \[ C\mapsto D_	au,\quad J\mapsto J,\quad D_1\mapsto D_{	au+1},\quad Z\mapsto U_	au Z. 	ag{26} \] This is exact conjugation by (1). The resulting physical difference orders and matrix sizes are bounded in terms of the fixed input data. The desired output in (2) is the specified \(F_X\) component of \(U_	au Z\). No rational coefficient is evaluated at a nonunit operator. Every ordinary residual in (24)--(26) is a \(P_N\) multiple. In the physical coordinate \(c_N(u)=2\cos(2\pi u+\pi/N)\), \[ P_N(c_N(u))=4\sin^2(\pi Nu). 	ag{27} \] Thus values and first \(u\)-derivatives of the residual vanish at the grid. Differentiating includes all coefficient derivatives. This supplies the original full normal equations, including all product-rule normals and the odd simple node. No half step is applied to an already reduced source. ## 5. Actual data retained at the interfaces Clearing a nonunit can create additional solutions. Equations (18), (24), or (25) are therefore necessary source equations, not license to choose new homogeneous endpoint data. The actual column definitions and forced recovery in (16) remain part of the construction. Endpoint values and first normals are the original source traces described below. They are not set to zero when a clearing coefficient vanishes. There is a useful uniform bound for the data before the final turn. Write \(\mathcal I_n\) for the finite terminal maximal characteristic integral in the pinned sources, and set \[ A_{m in}=\sum_{i=1}^b\mathcal I_{n_i}. 	ag{28} \] The first-turn initialization theorem proves, simultaneously for \(Y_i\) and every gauged \(W_i\), real canonical norm at most \(\exp[N\mathcal I_{n_i}+o(N)]\), uniformly on the fixed complex parameter sets. The unturned base channels have polynomial real norm. Full shifts on \(|v|=1\) keep the spectral argument in \([-2,2]\), so the tensor column has unit-circle norm at most \(\exp[NA_{m in}+o(N)]\). Its ordinary Laurent degree is \(O(N)\). The descent (8) costs only a polynomial: every Laurent coefficient is bounded by the unit-circle norm, and \(|\sin(kt)/\sin t|\le k\) bounds the odd quotient, including its endpoint limits. Summing the \(O(N)\) coefficients costs \(O(N^2)\). Canonical reduction of these ordinary spectral polynomials also costs polynomially, by Markov and full-Hermite reconstruction of their unchanged jets. Consequently \[ \max_
u\|Z_
u\|_{\mathbb R} \le \exp[NA_{m in}+o(N)]. 	ag{29} \] Uniformity on larger parameter disks gives all fixed parameter derivatives; Markov gives fixed spectral normals. Every channel is even in each microscopic \(\alpha_{i\ell}\). Descending to \(\alpha_{i\ell}^2\), the map \(\alpha_{i\ell}^2\mapsto N^2(w_{i\ell}-2)\) has a uniformly regular analytic inverse on bounded sets for large \(N\). Thus fixed derivatives in the original exterior \(w_{i\ell}\) cost only \(N^2\) per derivative and obey the same rate. For every fixed physical row \(j\), let \[ F_j(Z)=K_N(c_j,Z),\quad Q_j(Z)=\partial_wK_N(c_j,Z), \quad Q_*=\partial_wK_N(c_0,Z),\quad G_n=TR^{-n},\quad H_n=T(R^{-n}Q_*). \] The pinned fixed-row source identities give polynomials \(\alpha_{j,N}, eta_{j,N}\), of fixed degree and polynomial coefficient size, with \[ Q_j=\alpha_{j,N}(C)Q_*+ eta_{j,N}(C)1. \] For every component \(z=Z_
u\), the actual outer data are \[  egin{split} (U_	au z)(c_j) &=\kappa^	au\phi_N(F_j(J)G_	au\,z),\ (U_	au z)'(c_j) &=\kappa^	au\phi_N( [\alpha_{j,N}(J)H_	au+ eta_{j,N}(J)G_	au]z). \end{split} 	ag{30} \] Here \(H_	au\) is the true normal channel, not \(V_	au Q_*\). Since \(\mathcal I_{\pm1}=0\), the coherent trace bound, \(\|J\|\le34N^3\), and (29) prove \[ \max_{
u,\ 0\le j\le j_0}  ig(|(U_	au Z_
u)(c_j)|+ |(U_	au Z_
u)'(c_j)| ig) \le \exp[NA_{m in}+o(N)] 	ag{31} \] for every fixed \(j_0\). Every product and shared parameter stays inside the original traces. Formula (31) controls actual fixed windows; it does not prescribe data at other possible singular rows or prove global propagation. The construction concerns sufficiently large \(N\), as do the input companions. No shortest-level limit is inferred from (10). At \(N=2\), \(C^2=0\) and directly \[ V_n(a+bC)=(a-4inb)+bC . 	ag{32} \] Canonical multiplication followed by this formula retains the complete double-root data. It handles the finite exception without dividing \(q^2-q^{-2}\) or \(C-c\). ## 6. What the interface does not yet estimate On a regular compact chart the principal full-step matrices of the inputs can be tensorized: their eigenvalues multiply, with the source and recovery branches retained. Formula (23) converts the step symbols to their sum and difference, and (26) performs the actual turn automorphism. It does not replace the ordinary product by a transported product, or identify this correspondence with a positive angle sector. After (26), a coefficient such as \(\mathfrak a(D_	au)\) is an operator. The preceding clearing and descent do not prove that the highest physical shift coefficient of the combined system is invertible, uniformly or otherwise. Eliminating components can also expose terms of smaller asymptotic coefficient size but greater shift order. Such terms cannot be discarded from a transfer proof. The regular leading-order argument for one original endpoint product does not automatically persist under (20)--(26). The new result is therefore an exact finite interface with full normals and a proved source initialization budget, not a new general annihilator existence statement or an integrated growth theorem. A regular physical companion and its endpoint control are still needed before a maximal characteristic-growth upper bound can be asserted for (2). No selected coefficient, filled-action inequality, or general forest closure follows here. ## 7. Direct sources The following complete sources were read at the stated pins; the directly used identities and hashes were checked: * [Original finite-band operators](research_unit_turn_finite_band_branching_operator.md), SHA256 31d9f574c7dc3aaac07e4eb50c131b3328be46b3c2a2ef46f9dae7f0c4ddb9cb: original ordinary operator, signed conjugation and carriers, finite physical order, ideal preservation and actual trace anchors. * [Ordinary divided-difference product module](research_endpoint_product_divided_difference_module.md), SHA256 8a1b215aa6034365d4faa84130381d6a78a17383c03ecf6c6b48a77b6c4e3093: base input channels, ordinary half-step source aliases and their explicit matrices, polynomial gauge and forced recovery. * [Actual product companions and fixed-row data](research_turned_endpoint_product_characteristic_upper_bound.md), SHA256 5e594fa40c1ab70b72a0c1b85748182e33850675a45ed6ea42f2c20349831b2a: exact forward/backward extremes, unequal companion windows, canonical input bounds and full-normal fixed-row trace formulas. * [First-turn initialization and the improved input budget](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_first_turn_endpoint_product_initialization.md), SHA256 7d0871a7dcde94c1cc73f98495b9521a61478729ddd52c51570ffa95f1901105: simultaneous gauged-channel estimate and the upper budget \(\mathcal I_n\), with uniform complex parameters and normals. Only written mathematics and source-text/hash reads were used. No mathematical program, numerical experiment, test or build was run. Adopted notes and public manuscripts are unchanged.
