title: Exact contraction of the full high Newton radical
text:
# Exact contraction of the full high Newton radical Research note, 3 November 2026. The entire nilpotent high-index sector of the original edge kernel contracts to physical values with uniformly bounded coefficients. At both ends of an edge these coefficients give an explicit real positive-definite Gram matrix. Original crossing phases remain in the physical color sum, so this is an exact grouping and an upper bound, not a positivity assertion for the filled source. The coefficient identity below is the signed form of the divided differences already used in the [original low-color bound](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_original_low_color_bound.md), equations (5)--(6). Square-zero nilpotence is also recorded in the [arbitrary-power compiler](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_arbitrary_power_source_compilation.md), Proposition 2. The purpose here is their full high-index edge contraction, including a uniform bound through the last double node. This differs from the first-normal product-rule expansion in [the grouped Ward-current note](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_grouped_endpoint_current_matchings.md): a radical insertion consumes the local normal and leaves only the spectator's value. ## 1. The physical radical and its exact value functional Let \[ N\ge3,\quad D=N-1,\quad m=\lfloor N/2floor,\quad 	heta=\pi/N,\quad q=e^{i	heta},\quad \eta=(-1)^D, 	ag{1} \] and use the full physical algebra and its original closing functional \[ \mathcal A_N=\mathbb C[z]/(P_N(z)),\quad P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2,\qquad \phi_N(f)=\eta N^2[z^D]\operatorname{rem}_{P_N}f. 	ag{2} \] The original Newton data are \[ s_j=2\sin(j	heta),\quad S_j=\prod_{h=1}^j s_h,\quad S_0=1, \qquad c_a=2\cos((2a+1)	heta),\quad e_j(z)=S_j^{-2}\prod_{h<j}(c_h-z). 	ag{3} \] The double nodes are \(c_a\), \(0\le a<m\). When \(N=2m+1\) there is also the simple node \(c_m=-2\). The radical, meaning the kernel of evaluation at every distinct physical node, is exactly \[ \mathfrak r_N=\operatorname{span} \{e_{D-r}:0\le r<m\},\qquad \mathfrak r_N^2=0. 	ag{4} \] Indeed each displayed polynomial contains every distinct root among its factors. They are independent and their number is \(N-\#\{	ext{distinct roots}\}=m\). A product of two polynomials vanishing at every root is divisible by \(P_N\), whose root multiplicities are at most two. At odd levels \(e_m\) is deliberately excluded: it does not vanish at the simple node \(-2\). For \(0\le a\le r<m\) define \[ b_{ra}=(-1)^{r+a}  rac{s_{2a+1}S_r^2}{S_{r-a}S_{r+a+1}}, \qquad b_{ra}=0\quad(a>r). 	ag{5} \] All denominators are nonzero: \(r+a+1\le2m-1<N\). **Theorem 1.** For every \(f\in\mathcal A_N\), \[ \phi_N(e_{D-r}f) =\sum_{a=0}^r b_{ra}f(c_a). 	ag{6} \] For the original crossing \(R\), every signed integer \(n\), and \(\kappa=\exp(\pi iD^2/(2N))\), this gives \[ \phi_N(R^n e_{D-r}f) =\sum_{a=0}^r b_{ra}\,\kappa^n(-1)^{na}q^{na(a+1)}f(c_a). 	ag{7} \] These are coefficientwise identities with arbitrary ordinary free-boundary polynomials as coefficients. *Proof.* Write the canonical representative \(f=\sum_{j=0}^D f_j e_j\). The original Frobenius pairing is \(\phi_N(e_i e_j)=\delta_{i+j,D}\), so the left side of (6) is \(f_r\). The first \(r+1\) nodes are distinct; ordinary Newton interpolation gives \[ f_r=(-1)^rS_r^2\sum_{a=0}^r  rac{f(c_a)}{\prod_{0\le h\le r,\ h
e a}(c_a-c_h)}. 	ag{8} \] They decrease with \(a\), so the denominator has sign \((-1)^a\). The difference-of-cosines product has absolute value \(S_{r+a+1}S_{r-a}/s_{2a+1}\), proving (5)--(6). Finally the actual crossing values are \[ R(c_a)=\kappa(-1)^a q^{a(a+1)}. 	ag{9} \] Evaluation is an algebra homomorphism and these values are nonzero, so (9) applies to all signed powers, proving (7). \(\square\) Formula (6) does not discard the original first normals. The local physical residue at a double node is \[ \eta\{(4-c_a^2)h'(c_a)-c_a h(c_a)\}. 	ag{10} \] For \(h=e_{D-r}f\), the value term and the derivative of \(f\) vanish, and \[ \eta s_{2a+1}^2 e_{D-r}'(c_a)=b_{ra} \quad(a\le r), 	ag{11} \] with zero derivative for \(a>r\). The odd simple-node value is zero. Thus (6) is exactly the original surviving normal, expressed as an evaluation functional. Ordinary derivatives in every uncontracted free-boundary variable commute with this finite identity. ## 2. A uniform bound on the exact coefficients **Theorem 2.** At every integer level and every \(0\le a\le r<m\), \[ |b_{ra}|\le2,\qquad \sum_{a=0}^{m-1}b_{ra}=\delta_{r0}. 	ag{12} \] In particular, uniformly in the signed crossing power, \[ |\phi_N(R^n e_{D-r}f)| \le2\sum_{a=0}^r|f(c_a)| \le2(r+1)\max_{a\le r}|f(c_a)|. 	ag{13} \] *Proof.* Factor the factorial quotient as \[  rac{S_r^2}{S_{r-a}S_{r+a+1}} = rac1{s_{r+a+1}} \prod_{j=1}^a rac{s_{r-j+1}}{s_{r+j}} \le rac1{s_{r+a+1}}. 	ag{14} \] Each factor is at most one, since \[ \sin((r+j)	heta)-\sin((r-j+1)	heta) =2\cos((r+	frac12)	heta)\sin((j-	frac12)	heta)>0. 	ag{15} \] The restriction \(r<m\) is exactly what keeps the cosine positive. Set \(x=(a+1/2)	heta\), \(y=(r+1/2)	heta\). Then \(0<x\le y<\pi/2\), and \[  rac{s_{2a+1}}{s_{r+a+1}} = rac{\sin(2x)}{\sin(x+y)}\le2, 	ag{16} \] because \(\sin(x+y)\ge\cos x\sin y\ge\cos x\sin x\). Equations (14)--(16) prove the first bound in (12). Putting \(f=1\) in (6) gives its row sum, since \(\phi_N(e_{D-r})=\delta_{r0}\). Equation (9) has unit modulus, even if the integer \(n\) depends on \(N\); this proves (13). \(\square\) ## 3. The whole radical edge becomes a physical Gram matrix Separate the exact ordinary kernel as \[  egin{split} K_N(z,w)&=K_N^{m low}(z,w)+H_N^{m rad}(z,w),\ H_N^{m rad}(z,w)&=\sum_{r=0}^{m-1}e_{D-r}(z)e_{D-r}(w),\ K_N^{m low}(z,w)&=\sum_{j=0}^{D-m}e_j(z)e_j(w). \end{split} 	ag{17} \] At even levels the radical sector is every index \(j\ge N/2\). At odd levels it is \(j\ge(N+1)/2\); the middle polynomial stays in the low sector. Let \(\mathsf B=(b_{ra})_{0\le r,a<m}\), and set \[ W=\mathsf B^T\mathsf B,\qquad W_{ab}=\sum_{r=\max(a,b)}^{m-1}b_{ra}b_{rb}. 	ag{18} \] Then for arbitrary original spectators \(f,g\) and signed powers \(n,p\), \[  oxed{\quad (\phi_N\otimes\phi_N)  igl[R^n(z)R^p(w)H_N^{m rad}(z,w)f(z)g(w) igr] =\sum_{a,b=0}^{m-1}W_{ab}R(c_a)^nR(c_b)^p f(c_a)g(c_b). \quad} 	ag{19} \] The same identity holds with \(f(z)g(w)\) replaced by any joint spectator \(F(z,w;\mathbf u)\), by replacing its final product of values with \(F(c_a,c_b;\mathbf u)\). No independence assumption on outside variables is required. **Theorem 3.** The matrix \(W\) is real symmetric positive definite, and \[  egin{split} |W_{ab}|&\le4m,\qquad \sum_{a,b}|W_{ab}|\le4m^3,\ \operatorname{sign}(W_{ab})&=(-1)^{a+b},\qquad W\mathbf1=\mathbf e_0. \end{split} 	ag{20} \] Consequently (19) is bounded in absolute value by \(4m^3\max_{a,b}|F(c_a,c_b;\mathbf u)|\), uniformly over all signed integer powers. *Proof.* Apply (6) in each variable to prove (19). The real triangular matrix \(\mathsf B\) has strictly positive diagonal \(b_{rr}=S_r^2/S_{2r}\), so it is invertible and its Gram matrix is positive definite. The bounds follow from \(|b_{ra}|\le2\). Every summand in (18) has sign \((-1)^{a+b}\), and at least one is nonzero. Finally (12) says \(\mathsf B\mathbf1=\mathbf e_0\), while the first row of \(\mathsf B\) is \(\mathbf e_0^T\). Hence \(W\mathbf1=\mathsf B^T\mathbf e_0=\mathbf e_0\). \(\square\) Conjugating \(W\) by \(\operatorname{diag}((-1)^a)\) makes every entry positive. This does not make (19) positive: after that sign change the original crossing still supplies the chirp \(q^{na(a+1)}\), as well as \((-1)^{(n+1)a}\) and its fixed unit \(\kappa^n\). Even when odd powers cancel the checkerboard signs, the chirp generally remains. The formula preserves that coherent sum exactly. **Proposition 4.** This actual positive Gram matrix is exponentially ill-conditioned as \(N	o\infty\): \[ \lambda_{\min}(W)\le \exp\{-2GN/\pi+O(\log N)\},\qquad \lambda_{\max}(W)\ge1, 	ag{21} \] where \(G\) is Catalan's constant. In particular its condition number is at least \(\exp\{2GN/\pi-O(\log N)\}\). *Proof.* Choose \(r=\lfloor N/4floor<m\). The diagonal entry of \(\mathsf B^{-1}\) at \(r\) is \(1/b_{rr}\), so \[ \lambda_{\min}(W)=\sigma_{\min}(\mathsf B)^2 =\|\mathsf B^{-1}\|_2^{-2}\le b_{rr}^2 =\left( rac{S_r^2}{S_{2r}}ight)^2. 	ag{22} \] The uniform sine-factorial estimate \(\log S_j=N\mathcal J(j/N)+O(\log N)\), together with \(\mathcal J(1/4)=-G/(2\pi)\) and \(\mathcal J(1/2)=0\), evaluates the last expression as \(\exp\{-2GN/\pi+O(\log N)\}\). The values of these integrals follow directly from the Fourier series for \(\log(2\sin\pi x)\); see the [original sine-factorial profile](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_three_crossing_full_coefficient_profile.md). Finally \(W_{00}\ge b_{00}^2=1\), so the largest eigenvalue is at least one. \(\square\) Thus positive definiteness here supplies no uniform lower frame bound in the ordinary physical-value Euclidean norm. It cannot be used as an identity metric or as a spectral-gap lower bound for a specified source coefficient. All nilpotence assertions here concern the physical relation \(P_N\). They are not assertions about a scalar-smoothed algebra \(P_\sigma
e P_N\). Likewise, two radical factors multiply to zero at a contracted or canonically reduced vertex, but their ordinary product need not vanish in an unreduced free-boundary variable. The free-variable identities and their derivatives in (19) remain literal polynomial identities without imposing such a reduction. ## 4. Grouping all radical edges in a coupled source Let \(\Gamma=(V,E)\) be a fixed finite simple graph, and let \(I\subseteq V\) be the vertices at which the original trace is taken. Each such vertex has a signed crossing power \(n_v\). The variables at the other vertices remain ordinary boundary variables. Put \[ E_I=\{\{v,w\}\in E:v,w\in I\},\qquad Z_K=\left(\prod_{v\in I}\phi_N^{(z_v)}ight) \left[\prod_{v\in I}R(z_v)^{n_v} \prod_{\{v,w\}\in E}K_N(z_v,z_w)ight]. 	ag{23} \] Define \(Z_{m low}\) by replacing \(K_N\) with \(K_N^{m low}\) only on the edges in \(E_I\). Every edge incident to an uncontracted boundary keeps its original full kernel. Thus the nilpotence in (4) will only be used at a vertex where the original algebra relation is imposed. A matching \(M\subseteq E_I\) is a set of edges with no shared endpoint. Write \(S=V(M)\) for its set of endpoints. For a choice of physical colors \(\mathbf a=(a_v)_{v\in S}\), with \(0\le a_v<m\), set \[ C_S(\mathbf a)= \left(\prod_{v\in I\setminus S}\phi_N^{(z_v)}ight) \left[ \prod_{v\in I\setminus S}R(z_v)^{n_v} \left.\prod_{\{v,w\}\in E}K_N(z_v,z_w) ight|_{z_v=c_{a_v}\ (v\in S)} ight]. 	ag{24} \] In particular \(C_\varnothing=Z_K\). This is the original source with the vertices in \(S\) evaluated at physical colors, and with their crossing scalars kept outside the definition. All edges are still present. An edge crossing from \(S\) to its complement has factor \(K_N(c_{a_v},z_w)\); an edge within \(S\) has factor \(K_N(c_{a_v},c_{a_w})\). **Theorem 5.** The exact difference between the full and low sources is \[  egin{split} Z_K-Z_{m low} =\sum_{\substack{M\subseteq E_I\ {m matching}\M
e\varnothing}} (-1)^{|M|+1}\sum_{\mathbf a} \left[\prod_{\{v,w\}\in M}  rac{W_{a_va_w}}{K_N(c_{a_v},c_{a_w})}ight] \left[\prod_{v\in V(M)}R(c_{a_v})^{n_v}ight] C_{V(M)}(\mathbf a). \end{split} 	ag{25} \] Each matching contribution has the bound \[ \left|\sum_{\mathbf a} \left[\prod_{\{v,w\}\in M}  rac{W_{a_va_w}}{K_N(c_{a_v},c_{a_w})}ight] \left[\prod_{v\in V(M)}R(c_{a_v})^{n_v}ight] C_{V(M)}(\mathbf a)ight| \le (4m^3)^{|M|} \max_{\mathbf a}|C_{V(M)}(\mathbf a)|. 	ag{26} \] These statements hold at both level parities, with arbitrary boundary variables and all their fixed ordinary derivatives retained. *Proof.* Expand \(K_N^{m low}=K_N-H_N^{m rad}\) on the edges in \(E_I\). If two chosen radical edges meet at a vertex, every resulting term contains a product of two elements of \(\mathfrak r_N\) there. Its original trace is zero by (4). The only surviving subsets are therefore matchings. For a matching, apply (19) at its disjoint pairs of endpoints. The joint-spectator version of that identity is needed here: edges not in the matching may connect different pairs or meet the same remaining vertex. They all become their literal physical evaluations. In particular they are not removed. The factors on the matching edges themselves have been replaced by \(W\). Restoring their original \(K_N\) factors in order to use (24) accounts for the divisions in (25). These divisions are harmless. At a physical node \(c_a\), \[ e_j(c_a)>0\quad(0\le j\le a),\qquad e_j(c_a)=0\quad(j>a), \qquad K_N(c_a,c_b)\ge1. 	ag{27} \] The first statement follows because the first \(a+1\) distinct nodes decrease; the second follows from the factor \(c_a-z\) in every later Newton polynomial. The constant term \(e_0=1\) then proves the last inequality. Finally use \(|R(c_a)^{n_v}|=1\), \(|W_{ab}|\le4m\), and the \(m^{2|M|}\) possible color assignments to prove (26). All operations are finite and in selected variables, so boundary derivatives commute with the identity. \(\square\) For a fixed graph, the prefactors and the number of matchings in (26) have no exponential growth in \(N\). Consequently, if one independently proves \[ \max_{\mathbf a}|C_{V(M)}(\mathbf a)| \le \exp\{N\mu_M+o(N)\} 	ag{28} \] for every nonempty matching, then \[ |Z_K-Z_{m low}| \le \exp\{N\max_{M
e\varnothing}\mu_M+o(N)\}. 	ag{29} \] If the low source has a nonzero leading term of rate \(\mu\), and all these \(\mu_M\) are strictly smaller than \(\mu\), the full source has that same leading term. This implication is just the reverse triangle inequality after (29). Neither the needed bound (28) nor the required strict comparison is supplied by the matching formula. This is the relevance to the [power-three kernel obstruction](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_bare_kernel_power_three_obstruction.md). The high sector can be exponentially large at an off-grid complex geometric point before contraction. Its exact contribution after contraction is instead bounded by physical-color sources at polynomial cost. The next analytic estimate therefore concerns those sources, with their remaining traces and edge couplings. The [all-color normal bound](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_all_color_path_normal_bound.md) controls the first-normal determinant at each color, but explicitly leaves the coherent color sum unestimated. A positive local Gram matrix cannot replace that missing estimate. For odd powers on the matched vertices, the signs \((-1)^{a_v+a_w}\) in \(W\) cancel the crossing signs. Their matching weights become positive magnitudes times \[ \kappa^{\sum_{v\in V(M)}n_v} q^{\sum_{v\in V(M)}n_v a_v(a_v+1)}. 	ag{30} \] The displayed quadratic phases and the phases of \(C_S\) remain. For reflected conjugate data a Gram pairing can give a squared norm, but a general matching contribution is a bilinear sum, not a Hermitian quadratic form. ## 5. The single top mode and why removing it is insufficient The special term \(e_D(z)e_D(w)\) has an especially simple interpretation. Equations (6) and (9) at \(r=0\) give \[ \phi_N(R^n e_D f)=\kappa^n f(c_0),\qquad K_N(c_0,w)=1. 	ag{31} \] The first identity already appears in [the free-boundary crossing identity](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_current_free_aw_crossing_transport.md). Let \(Z^\circ_\Gamma\) use \(K_N-e_D\otimes e_D\) on its selected--selected edges and the original kernel elsewhere. Expansion as above now gives \[ Z_\Gamma= \sum_{M\subseteq E_I\ {m matching}} \kappa^{\sum_{v\in V(M)}n_v} Z^\circ_{\Gamma\setminus V(M)}. 	ag{32} \] Here the graph on the right loses the matched vertices and every edge incident to them, since all those edges evaluate to one. An isolated surviving selected vertex still carries its original factor \(\phi_N(R^{n_v})\). The deletion in (32) is an algebraic contraction, not an asserted topological move on the knot complement. This deletion rule is special to the single top mode. For the full radical, the physical evaluations in (24) must remain. Moreover, at the power-three point in the linked obstruction theorem, the next term \(e_{D-1}(z)e_{D-1}(w)\) differs from the top by a factor of order \(N^{-4}\), and has the same exponential rate. Removing any fixed number of top terms therefore does not restore the bare geometric expansion. The full radical contraction in (25) addresses the entire sector instead. ## 6. Finite-level checks The proofs above are for all integer levels. The separate script [check_high_newton_radical_contraction.py](../experiments/check_high_newton_radical_contraction.py) also checks the normalization by direct polynomial division: python3 experiments/check_high_newton_radical_contraction.py It checks the trace on every monomial basis element at levels 3 through 14, the square-zero products, and the coefficient bound. Direct Laurent expansion also checks the Fourier bound in Section 7 on every radical basis element at those levels. At levels 3 through 8 it compares a four-vertex path contraction with the physical-evaluation matching expansion, using complex polynomial vertex weights and retaining the edge between two disjoint matched pairs. The [saved numerical diagnostics](../repro/results/research-high-newton-radical.json) record 100-digit arithmetic and the residuals. These finite checks test the formulas; they do not replace the uniform arguments. ## 7. Fourier bounds for the original radical polynomials There is also a direct Fourier estimate before contraction. It uses the same exact physical normals as (11), rather than a replacement interpolant or a general polynomial derivative inequality. For \(0\le r<m\), write \[ h_r(t)=e_{D-r}(-2\cos t) =\sum_{j=-D}^{D}\widehat h_r(j)e^{-ijt}, \qquad \|\widehat h_r\|_1=\sum_j|\widehat h_r(j)|. 	ag{33} \] **Theorem 6.** Uniformly over the whole radical basis, \[ \|\widehat h_r\|_1 \le rac{2\sqrt{N-1}}{N\sin(\pi/N)} \le\sqrt{N-1}. 	ag{34} \] Consequently, for every integer \(k\ge0\), \[ \sup_{t\in\mathbb R}|\partial_t^k h_r(t)| \le D^k\sqrt{N-1}. 	ag{35} \] In angular variables set \(\widehat H_N^{m rad}(t,u) =H_N^{m rad}(-2\cos t,-2\cos u)\). For all integers \(k,\ell\ge0\) and all complex \(t,u\), \[ |\partial_t^k\partial_u^\ell\widehat H_N^{m rad}(t,u)| \le m(N-1)D^{k+\ell} e^{D(|\Im t|+|\Im u|)}. 	ag{36} \] In particular its real-period derivatives have polynomial bounds. **Proof.** Put \(z=e^{-it}\) and \[ P_r(z)=z^Dh_r(t). \] This is an ordinary polynomial of degree at most \(2D\). At the physical angles \(t_j=\pi(N-1-2j)/N\), the numbers \(z_j=e^{-it_j}\) are the \(N\) distinct roots of \(z^N=\eta\). Every radical polynomial vanishes at every physical spectral node, including the odd simple node. Hence \[ P_r(z)=(z^N-\eta)g_r(z),\qquad \deg g_r\le N-2. 	ag{37} \] Differentiating along the angular variable at a grid point gives \[ z_j^D h_r'(t_j)=-iN\eta\,g_r(z_j),\qquad |g_r(z_j)|= rac{|h_r'(t_j)|}{N}. 	ag{38} \] For a double node \(c_a\), set \(\vartheta_a=(2a+1)	heta\). At its two angular preimages, the chain rule and (11) give \[ |h_r'(t_j)| = rac{|b_{ra}|}{2\sin\vartheta_a} \le rac1{\sin	heta}. 	ag{39} \] Here \(b_{ra}=0\) for \(a>r\). All double-node angles lie between \(	heta\) and \(\pi-	heta\), so their sines are at least \(\sin	heta\). At the odd simple node the angular point is \(t=0\), and \(h_r'(0)=0\) by the chain rule. Thus (39) bounds every value in (38). Write \(g_r(z)=\sum_{a=0}^{N-2}d_a z^a\). The orthogonality of the \(N\) equally spaced physical points gives the exact discrete Parseval identity \[ \sum_{a=0}^{N-2}|d_a|^2 = rac1N\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}|g_r(z_j)|^2 \le rac1{N^2\sin^2	heta}. 	ag{40} \] For completeness, a cross term with distinct frequencies \(a,b\) contains \(N^{-1}\sum_jz_j^{a-b}=0\), because \(0<|a-b|<N\); diagonal terms have average one. Cauchy--Schwarz therefore bounds \(\sum_a|d_a|\le\sqrt{N-1}/(N\sin	heta)\). Multiplication by \(z^N-\eta\) in (37) at most doubles the coefficient norm, and multiplication by \(z^{-D}\) only shifts its frequencies. This proves the first bound in (34). Concavity of sine on \([0,\pi/2]\) gives \(\sin(\pi/N)\ge2/N\), proving the second. Each differentiation of (33) multiplies its coefficients by a frequency of magnitude at most \(D\). On a complex line, each exponential has modulus at most \(e^{D|\Im t|}\). This proves (35) and its corresponding complex-line bound. Finally \(\widehat H_N^{m rad}(t,u)=\sum_{r=0}^{m-1}h_r(t)h_r(u)\). Apply the single-factor bounds to this finite sum to obtain (36). \(\square\) The normalization in (39) uses the actual surviving spectral normal. Thus the Fourier estimate includes both parities and does not discard derivative data. It explains the distinction between the real physical estimates and the complex obstruction: the radical is polynomially bounded on the entire real period, but (36) allows exponential growth at a fixed nonzero height. No polynomial bound on a fixed complex strip, or lower bound for a coherent traced source, follows from (34).

# A hybrid spin-coherent lower chart for the actual Euler star Private written proof, 19 November 2026. The actual finite Euler star has a nonzero ordinary-binomial coherent kernel near its lower donor row. Physical recipients may range over any fixed compact set off incidence. Recipients in a factorial gauge are allowed near their lower coherent row. The latter caps are restored by exponentially small, relative, finite Cauchy tails. All donor slots and all physical recipient caps are exact throughout. This supplies a mixed chart for every resolved lower-donor configuration whose physical \(K,f\) are units, using a physical recipient when \(p
e0\) and a factorial recipient at \(p=0,A=1\). It does not put the rest of a closed period in this chart. All gauge interfaces, physical crossings, closing rows, and meridian derivatives remain. Complete directs G and C are pinned below. G supplies the literal star and its resolved rational correspondence. C supplies the finite-degree padding method; the different recurrence, its estimates and graph identification are proved here. ## 1. Finite operators and the hybrid kernel Put \(d=N-1, h=N^{-1}, c=2\pi i, Q=e^{ch}\), \[ x=-M e^{-ch/2},\qquad f_a=(Q;Q)_a,\qquad G_Fw_a=f_aw_a,\qquad 0\le a\le d. 	ag{1} \] The quantum root is fixed when \(M
e0\) varies. In G's physical basis, \[ Lw_a=w_{a-1},\quad Fw_a=(1-Q^{a+1})w_{a+1},\quad Kw_a=xQ^{-a}w_a, 	ag{2} \] with the missing bottom/top arrows. On \(r\ge2\) heads let \[ F_{m t}=\sum_{j=2}^r K_2^{-1}\cdots K_{j-1}^{-1}F_j, \qquad S=\sum_{n=0}^d rac{(x^{-1}L_1F_{m t})^n}{f_n}. 	ag{3} \] For \(S^{-1}\), the summand has the additional multiplier \[ (-1)^nQ^{n(n-1)/2}. 	ag{4} \] Choose a subset \(H\subset\{2,\ldots,r\}\). Conjugate both operators by \(G_F\) on the donor and on precisely the recipients in \(H\): \[ \widetilde S^{\pm}=G_H^{-1}S^{\pm1}G_H,\qquad G_H=G_{F,1}\prod_{i\in H}G_{F,i}. 	ag{5} \] The donor lowering arrow becomes \(1-Q^a\); a recipient in \(H\) has unit raising arrow except at its physical top. The other recipients keep (2). Cartans are unchanged. These are actual finite diagonal conjugations; the original source uses the inverse changes on its incident rows and columns. Use an evaluation row and ordinary binomial column on every head: \[ \mathcal K_N^\pm(z,w)= \sum_{\alpha, eta\in\{0,\ldots,d\}^r} z^\alpha(\widetilde S^\pm)_{\alpha eta} \prod_i inom d{ eta_i}w_i^{ eta_i}. 	ag{6} \] Write \(t=w_1, v=tz_1, v_i=z_iw_i, I_i=1+v_i\) for \(i\ge2\). We work near any fixed compact set of \(M,z_1,z_i,w_i\) on which \[ M
e0,\qquad I_i
e0, \qquad |v_i|\leho\quad(i\in H), 	ag{7} \] where, for example, \(0<ho<1/8\) is sufficient. No size restriction is imposed on the physical-recipient products \(v_i\), \(i
otin H\). All assertions are uniform on smaller compacts and sufficiently small fixed complex \(t\)-disks, independently of \(N\). First remove only the output caps on the \(H\) recipients. Their unit raising operators become multiplication by \(z_i\). This defines an auxiliary finite polynomial: each such output degree is at most \(2d\), since the total donor transfer is at most \(d\). Physical recipients retain their exact operator \[ F_i^{m out}=z_i(1-QT_i),\qquad T_i:z_i\longmapsto Qz_i. 	ag{8} \] In particular its apparent degree-\(N\) coefficient is exactly zero. Every transfer raises recipients. Consequently applying the physical output projections at the end is exactly the original hybrid kernel; no path which has crossed a top can return. ## 2. An exact donor-slot evolution For an artificial donor binomial degree \(0\le j\le d\), keep all recipient input degrees equal to \(d\). Let \[ \mathcal Z=x^{-1}F_{m t}^{m out},\qquad H_a^+(A)=\sum_{n=0}^a{a rack n}_Q A^n, \qquad H_a^-(A)=(A;Q)_a. 	ag{9} \] Then the auxiliary kernel is exactly \[ K_j^\pm=\sum_{a=0}^j inom ja(tz_1)^a H_a^\pm(\mathcal Z/z_1)\prod_{i=2}^r I_i^d. 	ag{10} \] The expression is polynomial, including at \(z_1=0\). Indeed the factorial donor arrow supplies \(f_a/f_{a-n}\), and division by \(f_n\) in (3) gives the finite Gaussian coefficient in (9). Formula (4) gives the finite Pochhammer polynomial. This proves (10), not just a principal symbol for it. Gaussian Pascal and the Pochhammer product give \[ H_{a+1}^+(A)=H_a^+(QA)+AH_a^+(A),\qquad H_{a+1}^-(A)=(1-Q^aA)H_a^-(A). \] Ordinary binomial Pascal therefore gives the two literal evolutions \[  egin{split} K_{j+1}^+&=K_j^++tz_1K_j^+(Qt,Q^{-1}z_1) +t\mathcal ZK_j^+,\ K_{j+1}^-&=(1+tz_1)K_j^- -t\mathcal ZK_j^-(Qt,z_1). \end{split} 	ag{11} \] All recipient arguments not displayed are unchanged. These identities also hold with the actual capped recipient operators. We use the uncapped \(H\) version first for the relative cap estimate below. Normalize \[ G_j^\pm=K_j^\pm/  igl[(1+v)^j\prod_{i=2}^r I_i^d igr]. 	ag{12} \] Thus \(G_0=1\) and \(G_j(t=0)=1\). For \(I\subset\{2,\ldots,r\}\), put \[ B_{I,h}=\prod_{i\in I} \left( rac{1+Qv_i}{1+v_i}ight)^{h^{-1}-1}. 	ag{13} \] This has a holomorphic germ at \(h=0\), using the logarithm of each ratio which is zero there. The germ is an analytic device for the coefficients, not an off-root finite-matrix assertion. Index terms by \(

In particular no unit-time clock orbit is required to stay off incidence. ## 3. Low-degree logarithms and the complete finite tail We give the analytic estimate, including its finite-tail recovery. Work on a buffered polydisk about a point of (7), then use a finite cover. Set \(V_j=h\log G_j\) as a formal series in \(t\), with zero constant coefficient. The exact recurrence is \[ V_{j+1}=V_j+h\mathcal F_h^\pm(	au,V_j), 	ag{17} \] where \[  egin{split} \mathcal F_h^+(	au,V)&=\log\left[1+ 	heta\left(e^{(e^{hY_0}-1)V/h}-1ight) + rac t{1+v}\sum_
u a_{

u}-1)V/h}ight],\ \mathcal F_h^-(	au,V)&=\log\left[1-  rac t{1+v}R_h(	au,v)\sum_

u,h} e^{(e^{h(cD+Y_
u)}-1)V/h}ight]. \end{split} 	ag{18} \] For the coefficient of \(t^n\), the multiplier of \([t^n]V_j\) in (17) is exactly one. All other terms use strictly lower activity degrees. The logarithms in (18) are their branches at one. Collapse absolute spatial Taylor coefficients to a positive variable \[ y,\qquad \mathcal L=C(1+y)^2\partial_y, \] increasing \(C\) to majorize all the finitely many vector fields in (14),(16), including their displacements at the center. Let \(\phi_s\) be its positive flow. For positive series \[ (e^{h\mathcal L}-1)U/h\preceq e^{h\mathcal L}\mathcal LU. 	ag{19} \] If activity coefficient \(k\) is bounded at \(\phi_{kh}(y)\), one additional clock shift or divided difference is bounded at \(\phi_{(k+1)h}(y)\), with at most \(Ck+\mathcal L\) applied to its majorant. A shifted coefficient in (18) contributes only to output degree at least \(k+1\). In products every shifted factor has this same property, so positivity moves every argument to the common \(\phi_{nh}(y)\) at output degree \(n\). This proves the padding rule term by term for the full exponentials and logarithm. The coefficients \(a_{
u,h},R_h\) and their fixed derivatives are uniformly bounded on buffered neighborhoods, for \(0\le	au\le1\) and small \(h\). Their absolute Taylor series and (18) are majorized by a positive analytic function of the form \[ \mathcal H(t,y,p,q)=  rac{C(y)t}{1-C(y)(t+p+q)},\qquad C(y)=C/(1-y/R),\quad p=DU,\quad q=\mathcal LU. 	ag{20} \] The term with \(	heta\) is included because \(	heta=O(t)\). Consider \(U_	au=\mathcal H(t,y,DU,\mathcal LU)\), \(U(0)=0\). This has an analytic solution on fixed small \(t,y\) disks through time two. To see this directly, write its right side as \[ H(t,y,p,q),\qquad p=DU,\quad q=U_y. \] The characteristic equations are \[ \dot t=-tH_p,\quad\dot y=-H_q,\quad \dot p=tH_t,\quad\dot q=H_y,\quad \dot U=H-pH_p-qH_q. 	ag{21} \] At \(t=0\) all momenta and \(U\) remain zero and the coordinates remain fixed. On a small polydisk their deviations for time two are bounded by \(C(|t|+|p|+|q|+|U|)\). Picard iteration and Gronwall keep them \(O(|t(0)|)\); the initial-to-final coordinate map is identity at \(t=0\) and hence invertible on a smaller polydisk. Differentiating the equations gives \(p=DU,q=U_y\). This constructs the analytic solution. Its Taylor coefficients are nonnegative, by positive coefficient Picard iteration and continuation. The positive time-\(h\) flow dominates one positive Euler step. Using (19),(20) in the exact coefficient recursion, induction therefore bounds \(V_j\) by \(U(2jh,t,\phi_{nh}(y))\) at activity degree \(n\). We use this only for \(n\le L=\lfloor\delta Nfloor\). Choose \(\delta>0\) so that all padding by \(nh\le\delta\) stays in the buffered incidence complement. Cauchy's estimate then gives \[ |[t^n]V_j|\le C_1R_1^{-n}, \quad 1\le n\le L,\quad 0\le j\le d. 	ag{22} \] All fixed spatial and meridian derivatives obey the same estimate on smaller buffered sets. Repeated background ratios in (13) telescope to the corresponding bounded small-arc displacement; the proof uses degree padding, not a bound on an unrestricted length-\(N\) clock path. The actual whole polynomial has a separate elementary bound \[ |G_j|\le e^{C_2N}. 	ag{23} \] Here and below a polynomial factor in \(N\) is absorbed in a slightly larger constant. Indeed \({a rack n}_Q\) is a sum of \( inom an\) unit phases, so its absolute value is at most that integer. In a fixed compact coordinate set, each term of the output tail operator has coefficient bounded independently of \(N\): a raw raising coefficient has modulus at most two, a gauged one is one, and the Cartan phases have modulus one apart from fixed powers of \[ |x|^{\pm1}. \] Thus its \(n\)-th power has coefficients bounded by \(C^n\), including the finitely many ordered choices. In (10), \(a\le j\le d\), input recipient binomial sums have total absolute coefficients \(2^{(r-1)d}\), and every output degree is at most \(2d\). Evaluation on a fixed compact and division by (12) cost at most another \(e^{CN}\). The inverse's multiplier (4) is a unit phase. This proves (23) for both signs and for every artificial slot number. No \(N^{CN}\) norm bound for a gauged raising operator is used. Let \(V_j^{[L]}\) be the Taylor polynomial through degree \(L\). On a circle \(|t|=R_2<R_1\), (22) bounds it by \(C_3R_2\). The functions \(G_j\) and \(\exp(V_j^{[L]}/h)\) have identical Taylor coefficients through degree \(L\). For \(|t|\le\eta R_2\), \[ |G_j-e^{V_j^{[L]}/h}| \le rac{2\eta^{L+1}}{1-\eta}e^{N(C_2+C_3R_2)}. 	ag{24} \] The comparison exponential has modulus at least \(e^{-C_3N\eta R_2}\). Choose \(\eta>0\) after all the constants so that its power in (24) pays this entire bound. Then \[ G_j=e^{V_j^{[L]}/h}(1+O(e^{-\gamma N})). 	ag{25} \] This proves zero-freeness of the actual auxiliary polynomial and recovers all its finite high activity degrees. ## 4. Explicit phase and unit transport Set \(t_i=v_i/(1+v_i)\). The limiting coefficients in (14) and their first corrections are \[ a_{

All characteristic velocities vanish at \(t=0\); the initial projection is identity. The branch is fixed by \(V(	au,0)=0\). For clarity the complete first correction is specified. Let \[  egin{split} F_{1,+}(V)=Z_+^{-1}\{&	frac12	heta e^{Y_0V}Y_0^2V +	frac t{1+v}\sum_

The linear characteristic solution is analytic and is zero at \(t=0\). To justify comparison, put \(W_j=V(jh)+hA(jh)\). Taylor expansion of (18),(26),(27) gives \[ W_{j+1}-W_j-h\mathcal F_h(jh,W_j)=O(h^3), 	ag{31} \] with an analytic residual \(O(t)\). The low-degree error obeys the same padding rule. The derivative of the right side of (18) has a positive majorant \(B_1(t,y)De+B_2(t,y)\mathcal Le\), with both \[ B_i(t,y)=O(t). \] Indeed every divided difference in (18) has its explicit activity factor. The positive linear flow with this right side and an analytic forcing \(B_0(t,y)=O(t)\) exists through time two by (21). Comparing the coefficient recursion with it bounds \([t^n](V_j-W_j)\) by \[ h^2 C R^{-n},\qquad n\le L. 	ag{32} \] The argument is the positive Euler-step induction used for (22), now with residual \(h^3B_0\). This pays discrete stability as well as consistency. Summing (32), using the analytic tails of \(V,A\), and then (25), proves \[ G_d^\pm=e^{NV^\pm(1)}a_\pm(1+O(N^{-1})),\qquad a_\pm=\exp\{A^\pm(1)-V_	au^\pm(1)\}

Restoring every hybrid cap For each \(i\in H\), mark its output variable by \(z_i\mapsto\xi_i z_i\). Choose \(R>1\) with \(Rho<1\) and \[ g=\log R-\log rac{1+Rho}{1-ho}>0. 	ag{34} \] For example \(R=2,ho<1/8\) works. Prove (33) on the compact union of all such marker circles, with the other physical recipient products unchanged. They all remain off incidence. The normalized phase and transport are respectively \(O(t)\) and a bounded unit there. For a nonempty subset \(J\subset H\), Cauchy's formula for the sum of coefficients of degree at least \(N\) in each corresponding marker gives the factor \[ R^{-N|J|}(1-R^{-1})^{-|J|}. 	ag{35} \] Compared with the unmarked kernel, the background factors cost at most \[ \left( rac{1+Rho}{1-ho}ight)^{d|J|}, \] and the ratio of the phase/transport factors costs at most \(C e^{CN|t|}\). The donor background is unchanged. Thus every such tail is \(O(e^{-gN|J|+CN|t|})\) relative to the unmarked auxiliary kernel. Shrink the donor disk after (34). Inclusion--exclusion of the finitely many output projections gives \[ \mathcal K_N^\pm/K_d^\pm=1+O(e^{-\gamma_1N}). 	ag{36} \] This is the original hybrid finite kernel by the monotonicity argument after (8). Unrelated physical recipient phases have not been replaced by absolute majorants in this relative comparison. Combining (12),(33),(36) proves the theorem: \[  oxed{\quad\mathcal K_N^\pm =(1+tz_1)^d\prod_{i=2}^rI_i^d\, e^{NV^\pm(1)}a_\pm(1+O(N^{-1})).\quad} 	ag{37} \] It is zero-free on the stated fixed open chart for all sufficiently large \(N\). The relative remainder is holomorphic and \(O(N^{-1})\) on a buffered chart. Cauchy therefore gives the same bound for all fixed derivatives in coherent variables and in the actual fixed-root meridian \(M\). In particular this is a genuine meridian family of (3),(5), not a derivative of a root-only identification of \(E(M)\). No complex-\(q\) zero-free domain is asserted. ## 6. The actual mixed principal graph and resolved lower row The full phase in (37) is \[ \mathfrak F_\pm=\log(1+tz_1)+\sum_{i=2}^r\log I_i+V^\pm(1). 	ag{38} \] Its full amplitude is \(a_\pm/[(1+tz_1)\prod I_i]\), so the literal identity endpoint remains \(I_i^{N-1}\). Define occupations \[ u_i=w_i\mathfrak F_{w_i},\quad u_i'=z_i\mathfrak F_{z_i},\quad A_i=e^{cu_i},\quad A_i'=e^{cu_i'}. 	ag{39} \] In a physical recipient chart the input/output coordinate dictionaries are \[ p_i=w_i(1-u_i)/u_i,\quad f_i=(1-A_i)/p_i; \qquad p_i'=z_i^{-1},\quad f_i'=z_i(1-A_i'). 	ag{40} \] For the donor and a factorial recipient they are \[ f_i=u_i/[w_i(1-u_i)],\quad p_i=(1-A_i)/f_i; \qquad f_i'=z_i,\quad p_i'=(1-A_i')/z_i. 	ag{41} \] The displayed ratios are taken by their analytic limits at a lower row. These formulas follow directly from the binomial coefficient ratio \( inom d{a-1}/ inom da=a/(N-a)\) and the literal arrows, or from the mixed symplectic form: in either chart \[ d\log A\wedge d\log p=c\,du\wedge d\log w, \quad d\log A'\wedge d\log p'=-c\,du'\wedge d\log z. \] We identify the graph by an exact donor contiguity. Gaussian Pascal applied to each donor coefficient, including its binomial ratio, gives at degree \(d\) \[  egin{split} \partial_tK_d^+&=(d-D) \{z_1K_d^+(Qt,Q^{-1}z_1)+x^{-1}F_{m t}^{m out}K_d^+\},\ \partial_tK_d^-&=(d-D) \{z_1K_d^--x^{-1}F_{m t}^{m out}K_d^-(Qt,z_1)\}. \end{split} 	ag{42} \] These hold for actual caps as well; for the auxiliary kernels (8) gives their ordinary shift form. The relative cap estimate permits the same principal equations for (37). Using (39)--(41) gives \[ f_1=z_1 A_1/A_1'+F_{m t}'/x_{m cl}\quad(+),\qquad f_1=z_1-A_1F_{m t}'/x_{m cl}\quad(-), 	ag{43} \] where \(x_{m cl}=-M\), and \[ F_{m t}'=\sum_{j=2}^r x_{m cl}^{-(j-2)} \left(\prod_{2\le i<j}A_i'ight)f_j'. \] For the first equation use \(f_1=\mathfrak F_t/(1-t\mathfrak F_t)\). The factor \(d-D\) in (42) gives its denominator; omitting it would give the wrong ordinary-binomial graph. G's rational positive star has \(C=1-p_1F_{m t}/x_{m cl}\), preserves the tail \(F\), and satisfies \(A_1/A_1'=C\) and \[ f_1=C f_1'+F_{m t}/x_{m cl}. \] Its inverse gives the second equation of (43). Thus the literal contiguity agrees with G on the regular resolved correspondence. At \(t=0\) the initial phase is exactly \[ \mathfrak F_\pm=\sum_{i=2}^r\log I_i.	ag{44} \] Near that row (43) is an analytic first-order equation for \(\mathfrak F_t\): every occurrence of that derivative on the other side through \(A_1\) or its denominator has a factor \(t\). Its implicit derivative at \(t=0\) is one. Hence successive Taylor coefficients in \(t\) determine its analytic solution uniquely. The mixed projection of G's map is regular there. With a nonzero donor \(f_1\), its input spin coordinate is \[ w_1= rac{\Log A_1/c}{f_1(1-\Log A_1/c)} =-p_1/c+O(p_1^2). 	ag{45} \] Recipients are unchanged at \(p_1=0\). At fixed nonzero output \(z_i\), the input changes are \(w_i=p_i u_i/(1-u_i)\) in (40), or \(w_i=u_i/[z_i(1-u_i)]\) in (41); their derivatives in \(u_i\) are units away from \(u_i=1\). All G's \(C,T_j\) equal one at this row. The inverse function theorem and G's symplectic identity therefore give its local mixed generating function, normalized by (44). It satisfies (43); uniqueness identifies it with (38). In particular the mixed Hessian at the row is triangular: its donor diagonal entry is one, its recipient entries are \(I_i^{-2}\), and its recipient-input/donor-output entries vanish. It is nondegenerate on a smaller chart. The result is an actual generating kernel, not only a nonzero scalar function. At completeness a resolved lower donor has \(p_1=0,A_1=1,f_1

These coordinate choices cover all such resolved lower-donor configurations. They do not reset an independently prescribed nonlower logarithmic mark at an endpoint, and they do not make a generic nonlower donor small. ## 7. Retained source scope Every statement concerns the literal finite star (3) with the hybrid conjugations (5) and ordinary binomial columns (6). Returning to a physical braid network retains each actual \(G_F^{\pm1}\) interface; no uniform conditioning for those separate factors is asserted. The original κ, diagonal generator, physical crossing, framing and pivotal/first-jet source factors are not part of (37) and remain explicit. A source-preserving presentation may place its star on a covered lower row, but that separate presentation theorem does not follow from this local estimate. The theorem does not construct the full coherent integration chain, control its complement or its closing row, interpolate occupation blocks, or prove a geometric contribution or closed invariant lower bound.
