The [grouped endpoint theorem](research_internal_pair_grouped_angular_connectors.md#4-group-with-the-whole-other-trace-before-taking-absolute-values) bounds its entire right side below \(M_{n,p}\), uniformly on the wire rectangle. In particular every folded vertical endpoint, omitted physical-angle term, and their intersections have been included before taking absolute values. It remains to integrate \(H_nH_p\). Replace its product horizontal rectangle by the coupled trace surfaces proved above and in Sections 13–14 of [the reflected-contour note](research_internal_pair_reflected_current_identity.md#13-a-coupled-angular-contour-on-the-right-wire-interval). The following list accounts for the full wire rectangle: | Wire piece | Estimate and exact contour | |---|---| | Upper side, \(\alpha_N\le\Re x\le1/4\) | Theorem 5: the sole maximum is the positive geometric critical point; the complement of any fixed small neighborhood has a gap. | | Lower side, \(\alpha_N\le\Re x\le1/4\) | Theorem 5: the entire surface has a gap, including the reflected copy of the geometric neighborhood. | | Both horizontal sides, \(1/4\le\Re x\le eta_N\) | Theorem 19 of the reflected-contour note: the moving-wall coupled surface has a gap. | | Left half-grid side | Theorem 5 and (58) of the real-pair note: small positive trace heights bound the entire side, including zero wire height. | | Right half-grid side | Theorem 21 of the reflected-contour note: joint variation of the wire and trace heights bounds the entire side. | The surface changes are exact relative-boundary deformations of a closed holomorphic two-form. All trace heights stay positive, and the outer angular boundary stays fixed. No physical trace pole is crossed. Factorial reflection zeros remain in the exact integrand; no artificial wall residue is removed. The surfaces can be chosen to agree at their interfaces. More generally the pointwise trace identities allow each wire piece to use its own representation of the same source, so no unestimated interface current is created. Each fixed surface has bounded parametrization derivatives. Its trace heights have a fixed positive lower bound. The exact wire factor is bounded on the upper side, has its retained exponential penalty on the lower side, and is bounded on both half-grid vertical sides, including their real points. Taking the minimum of the finitely many proved gaps gives a number \(\delta_{n,p}>0\) for the entire complement of the local geometric piece. Near that piece the coupled heights are exactly \(H_n,H_p\); the surface Jacobian is one. Its scalar and orientation are therefore exactly those of the local pair theorem. It occurs once, with coefficient one, in this exact contour decomposition. The wire factor is \(1+O(e^{-cN})\) there, since \(\Im x=Y>0\); it does not alter the local leading amplitude. The local theorem supplies \(C_{N,n}C_{N,p}N^{-3/2}\mathcal A(0,0)e^{N\mathcal S(0,0)}\). The other terms have total absolute bound \(CN^A e^{N(M_{n,p}-\delta_{n,p})}\). They cannot cancel this nonzero leading term. This proves (37) at complete colors. ### 7.3. Uniformity in the two ordinary boundary colors A value at one boundary point cannot justify this extension. We use three estimates for the actual finite functions. First, the [free-outside physical-defect theorem](research_free_boundary_half_charge_observation.md#4-uniform-physical-defects-and-exterior-pair-colors) is uniform over every physical node on a fixed ordinary color disk. Applied to the literal trace with the full outside kernel, it gives for every low shared index \[ |W_{n,j,N}(\zeta)| \le CN^A e^{N\{\Re\mathcal S_n(\zeta)+V_0(j/N)\}} . 	ag{42} \] Here \(\mathcal S_n\) is the one-vertex half-charge action, so \(\Re\mathcal S_n(-2)=\mu(n)\). It is not the pair action \(\mathcal S\) in (37). To see (42), use the exact normal-defect trace identity: every double-node weight is polynomially bounded, \(e_j(c_a)=0\) for \(a<j\), and \(0\le e_j(c_a)\le e_j(-2)\) for \(a\ge j\). At odd levels the top low index instead uses the full-node observation and its exact rank-one top-degree term, given by Theorem 2 and equation (24) of that same note. It has the same half-charge rate. No derivative is assigned to the odd simple node. The uniform defect and observation expansions also retain all ordinary outside derivatives. Continuity of these proved analytic actions preserves the removed-low-index gaps on a sufficiently small fixed bidisk. For the shared radical, its real outside-color norm is bounded by (40), uniformly through both real periods. The omitted sum is a polynomial of degree at most \(N-1\) in each outside color. The polynomial Bernstein bound therefore gives the rate \(2M_\infty+|\Im u|+|\Im v|\) on complex angular strips. Ordinary Markov inequalities before this extension, or Cauchy estimates on smaller disks, retain its fixed derivatives. Thus this error has a strict gap on a fixed small ordinary bidisk as well. Second, the whole-contour kernel bound in [Lemma 3 of the free-outside connector theorem](research_internal_pair_grouped_angular_connectors.md#5-free-outside-colors-original-normals-and-coupled-trace-surfaces) states \[ |K_N(t,u)|\le CN^A e^{N\{\Re\Psi(t)+|\Im u|\}} 	ag{43} \] on any of the compact trace domains above, with fixed ordinary derivatives. Its hypotheses are satisfied: the central and transition pieces lie in the full complete-kernel rectangle, and the outer pieces have sufficiently small heights at the fixed cut \(T<\pi\). All mapped colors lie strictly in \(\Re w<2\), and \(\Re\Psi(t)>|\Im t|\) with a fixed margin. This is a physical-row interpolation estimate for the full kernel, including its radical. It does not continue a complete-point asymptotic without a bound. Consequently each noncritical contour exponent increases by at most \(|\Im u|+|\Im v|\). Theorem 4 in that note likewise preserves the exact grouped endpoint estimate (41) on a fixed ordinary bidisk. Finally, near the unique critical point use the independently proved free-edge expansions and the local pair theorem. The critical point \(z(u,v)\) moves holomorphically. Deform the contour only in a fixed small neighborhood to pass through it, leaving the boundary of that neighborhood fixed. For a small enough ordinary bidisk this deformation stays inside the regular factorial and edge charts, and its collar retains the strict complete-point gap. The holomorphic three-form has no pole there. Thus the local deformation is exact, and its coefficient remains one. On the rest of the contour (43) and continuity of \(\Re\mathcal S(u,v)\) preserve a fixed gap relative to that moving action. The local expansion now proves (37) uniformly on the bidisk. Evenness in \(u,v\) makes its action, amplitude, and remainder holomorphic in \(\zeta,\omega\) through the complete colors. The amplitude remains nonzero after shrinking the bidisk. Cauchy's formula on smaller ordinary-color disks proves the derivative assertions for the normalized remainder. ### 7.4. The original marked volume At the critical wire, the stationary identity proved in [the unsummed edge calculation](research_unsummed_network_phase_coercivity.md#5-what-positive-geometry-does-imply-locally) is \[ b(x_*,t_*)+b(x_*,r_*)=\psi(t_*,r_*). 	ag{44} \] Its logarithmic lift and absolute constant are fixed by continuation from the complete positive edge. Hence \[ \mathcal S(0,0)= \psi(t_*,0)+\psi(t_*,r_*)+\psi(r_*,0) + rac{i(nt_*^2+pr_*^2)}{4\pi}-i(t_*+r_*). 	ag{45} \] The positive-pair variational theorem gives positive original edge shapes, the full primitive filling equations, and \(\Im t_*,\Im r_*<0\). The [marked completion theorem](research_positive_point_marked_completion.md#1-statement-and-conventions) therefore identifies their face assembly with the specified smooth partial filling, with its original carriers and primitive curves. The [pointwise volume identity](research_positive_edge_volume_identity.md#4-a-stationary-action-on-an-arbitrary-selected-region) gives \(2\pi\Re\mathcal S(0,0)=\operatorname{Vol}Y_{n,p}\); its outside correction vanishes because \(u=v=0\). Exactly three original edges occur, so no extra complete-edge constant is added. Since \(|C_{N,n}C_{N,p}|=1\) and \(\mathcal A(0,0)
e0\), taking the logarithm of (37) proves (38). The same source statement for the mirror pair \((-n,-p)\) follows by conjugation at real boundary colors and holomorphic continuation in the ordinary colors. Its absolute rate is unchanged. This conclusion still concerns the corresponding marked block. The next section supplies the whole-period bounds needed for the existing finite-kernel composition theorem. It does not treat every remaining short or mixed-sign internal pair. ## 8. Boundary decay and the hypotheses for further composition The nonzero expansion near the complete boundary does not by itself estimate a later boundary trace. For that purpose we also need an upper bound over the entire real boundary period. The already proved edge and half-charge estimates provide it on the complete contour used in Section 7. No critical point for a distant outside angle is needed. **Theorem 7.** Fix integers \(n,p\ge7\). There are constants \(c,B,h_*>0\) such that, for every pair of fixed ordinary derivative orders \(k,\ell\), suitable \(C_{k,\ell},A_{k,\ell}\) give \[  egin{split} &\left|\partial_\zeta^k\partial_\omega^\ell \mathcal P_{n,p,N}(u+is,v+it)ight|\ &\quad\le C_{k,\ell}N^{A_{k,\ell}} \exp N\{M_{n,p}-c(1-\cos u)-c(1-\cos v)+B(s^2+t^2)\}, \end{split} 	ag{46} \] for \(-\pi\le u,v\le\pi\), \(|s|,|t|\le h_*\), at both level parities. The derivatives act in the ordinary colors \(\zeta=-2\cos(u+is)\), \(\omega=-2\cos(v+it)\), including their ramified angular endpoints. *Proof.* Keep the complete-boundary contour from Section 7 fixed as the outside angles vary. On a small fixed neighborhood of its geometric critical point, both selected trace angles lie in the domain of the [whole-period free-edge bound](research_pair_free_boundary_kernel.md#7-whole-outside-period-decay-and-a-complex-strip). That theorem bounds the two actual outside kernels, with their ordinary derivatives, by \[ CN^A e^{N\{\Re\Psi(t_1)+\Re\Psi(t_2) -c_0(1-\cos u)-c_0(1-\cos v)+B_0(s^2+t^2)\}}. 	ag{47} \] All remaining factors are unchanged. The complete real phase on this neighborhood is at most \(M_{n,p}\), by the strict mixed-phase maximum. Its absolute integral therefore has the upper exponent required in (46). For the removed low indices use [Theorem 4 of the free-outside observation note](research_free_boundary_half_charge_observation.md#5-whole-outside-period-decay-with-a-complex-strip). It estimates every actual physical defect row and the odd rank-one top term over the whole outside period. The exact trace argument proving (42) now gives \[ |\partial_\zeta^k W_{n,j,N}(-2\cos(u+is))| \le CN^A e^{N\{\mu(n)+V_0(j/N) -c_n(1-\cos u)+B_ns^2\}} . 	ag{48} \] The analogous bound holds for \(p\). Thus the entire removed low-index sum retains its complete-point rate gap, together with the two angular losses and a quadratic strip cost. Uniformity in the row is essential here; a finite-order approximation to its entries is not substituted into the coherent trace. Every other complementary contour piece has a complete-point gap. Equation (43) bounds its full outside kernels for all real outside angles with additional cost at most \(|s|+|t|\). The grouped angular terms have exactly this property by Theorem 4 of the free-outside connector note. The shared radical has the same property by its real-square bound and the polynomial Bernstein estimate. Let \(\delta>0\) be a common gap for these finitely many types of errors, after removing the fixed geometric neighborhood. Choose \[ h_*\le\delta/8,\qquad c\le\min\{c_0,c_n,c_p,\delta/16\},\qquad B\ge\max\{B_0,B_n,B_p\}, 	ag{49} \] also respecting the strips in the cited theorems. Then \(|s|+|t|\le\delta/4\), while \(c\{(1-\cos u)+(1-\cos v)\}\le\delta/4\). The fixed gap pays both costs. Every complementary contribution therefore obeys (46), and so does the sum. The bounds used above already include fixed ordinary derivatives, before integration or summation; no division by an angular sine at an endpoint is involved. This proves the theorem. \(\square\) For completeness, the boundary Hessian needed in the finite-kernel composition theorem is \[ \mathcal S_{uu}(0,0)=- rac{\cos(t_*/2)}{2\pi},\qquad \mathcal S_{vv}(0,0)=- rac{\cos(r_*/2)}{2\pi},\qquad \mathcal S_{uv}(0,0)=0. 	ag{50} \] Indeed the edge phase is even in each outside angle, so \(\Phi_u(z;0,0)=\Phi_v(z;0,0)=0\) identically in the internal variables. Implicit stationary differentiation introduces no Schur correction to these second derivatives. The original complete-edge derivative is \(\psi_{uu}(t,0)=-\cos(t/2)/(2\pi)\); separate evenness gives the mixed zero. The positive geometric angles have \(\Re\cos(t_*/2),\Re\cos(r_*/2)>0\). Consequently a smaller fixed bidisk has a strictly negative real boundary Hessian. Conjugation gives the same conclusion for the mirror block. Equations (37), (46), and (50), together with degree at most \(N-1\) in each ordinary color, verify the analytic hypotheses of the finite two-boundary kernel theorem. Any prescribed finite collection of these blocks and their mirrors has common domains and constants, obtained by taking finite minima and maxima. Its separator threshold may depend on that collection. No bound uniform over the entire infinite collection of pairs has been proved by this finite-family argument. Arbitrary adjacent short words, unrestricted tangle assembly, and the cofinite-assignment theorem remain separate obligations. The finite computations used in this argument are limited to the rigorous \((7,7)\) action enclosure and exact rational comparisons. The [action certificate](../experiments/certify_pair_seven_action.py) proves the original logarithmic root and its positive edge domain; the [scalar checker](../experiments/check_real_pair_geometry_and_tail_gap.py) reproduces the comparison constants in Sections 6–8. Their saved records are [the interval certificate](../repro/results/research-pair-seven-action.json) and [the rational comparisons](../repro/results/research-real-pair-geometry-and-tail-gap.json). The contour identities, inequalities on whole regions, source decomposition, and volume identification are the written proofs; they are not conclusions drawn from numerical samples.

title: A complete-edge gap at every positive internal pair
text: # A complete-edge gap at every positive internal pair Research proof, 3 November 2026. Frozen manuscripts are unchanged. The coupled complete-end pair equations improve the height bound to \(H<107/100\). On the resulting angular box the complete-edge action exceeds the entire radical's growth by a fixed positive amount. Consequently the nonzero logarithmic asymptotic for the low complete-end kernel also holds for the full kernel, through both level parities, on a fixed complex neighborhood containing every selected angle of these pairs. The other outside endpoint remains complete. ## 1. The height bound uses the actual two incidences Fix integer powers \(n,p\ge3\), charges in \([0,1]^2\), and the positive geometric solution with one complete outside endpoint attached to each selected vertex. By the [pair angle theorem](research_internal_pair_angle_bound.md), every active selected angle \(t=a-iH\) satisfies \[ 0<a<\pi/2,\qquad H>0. \tag{1} \] The [cosine maximum principle](research_positive_path_real_wire_order.md) also gives \(|\cos(u/2)|<1\) at an active neighbor; a complete or zero-charge neighbor has cosine one. The two original principal returns at \(t\) are \[ r_0=\operatorname{asinh}(\tan(t/2)),\qquad r_1=\operatorname{asinh}(\tan(t/2)\cos(u/2)). \tag{2} \] Their positive real parts obey \(\Re r_0+\Re r_1=nH/2\). Since \[ |\tan(t/2)|^2 =\frac{\cosh H-\cos a}{\cosh H+\cos a}<1, \tag{3} \] and \(|\sinh(k+ig)|^2=\sinh^2 k+\sin^2g\), one has \(\Re r_1<\operatorname{asinh}1\). At fixed \(H\), the real part of \(r_0\) increases with \(a\): its derivative is \(\frac12\Re\sec(t/2)>0\), on the branch continued from completeness. At \(a=\pi/2\) its value is exactly \(\operatorname{asinh}\sqrt{\operatorname{sech}H}\). Therefore \[ \frac{3H}{2}\le\frac{nH}{2} <\operatorname{asinh}\sqrt{\operatorname{sech}H} +\operatorname{asinh}1 . \tag{4} \] **Proposition 1.** Every active height in this family satisfies \[ H<107/100. \tag{5} \] Indeed the right side of (4) decreases with \(H\). At \(h_0=107/100\), \[ \begin{split} \cosh(h_0)\sinh^2(18/25)&>1,\\ \sinh(441/500)&>1,\qquad 18/25+441/500=801/500<321/200=3h_0/2. \end{split} \tag{6} \] All three comparisons are exact. For the first two it suffices to retain the terms through degree six of the positive cosh series and through degree seven of the positive sinh series. Thus the right side of (4) is less than \(801/500\) if \(H\ge h_0\), a contradiction. Inactive angles are zero. ## 2. A uniform gap on the whole pair box Let \[ \mathcal R=\{a-iH:0\le a\le\pi/2,\ 0\le H\le107/100\}. \tag{7} \] Keep the original complete-end phase, with its complete constant: \[ \psi(t,0)=-4J(1/4+t/(4\pi))-4J(1/4-t/(4\pi)), \quad J'(z)=\Log(2\sin\pi z),\quad J(0)=0. \tag{8} \] All factorial arguments in (8) stay in their regular strips on a neighborhood of this rectangle. **Theorem 2.** Uniformly on \(\mathcal R\), \[ \Re\psi(a-iH,0)-H>1/500. \tag{9} \] *Proof.* Write \(r_0=k_0+ig_0\) for the first return in (2). The original branch gives \(\psi_t(t,0)=-r_0/\pi\), with \(k_0\ge0\) and \(-\pi/2<g_0\le0\). Hence \[ \partial_a\Re\psi=-k_0/\pi\le0,\qquad \partial_H(\Re\psi-H)=-g_0/\pi-1<-1/2. \tag{10} \] It suffices to check \(a=\pi/2,H=h_0\). At this real part the exact return formula is \[ g_0=-\arctan(\sqrt2\sinh(H/2)). \tag{11} \] Consequently \[ \begin{split} \Re\psi(\pi/2-iH,0)-H &=\psi(\pi/2,0)-H +\frac1\pi\int_0^H\arctan(\sqrt2\sinh(s/2))\,ds\\ &\ge\psi(\pi/2,0)-H +\frac{H^2/2-H^4/24}{\sqrt2\,\pi}. \end{split} \tag{12} \] For the last inequality use \(\sqrt2\sinh(s/2)\ge s/\sqrt2\) and \(\arctan x\ge x-x^3/3\) for \(x\ge0\). The latter follows by differentiation, since the derivative of its difference is \(x^4/(1+x^2)\). Here is a short rational lower bound for the remaining constant. The integrated Fourier series of \(\log(2\sin\pi z)\) gives \[ \psi(\pi/2,0)=\frac{2\sqrt2}{\pi} \sum_{j=0}^{\infty} \left\{\frac1{(8j+1)^2}+\frac1{(8j+3)^2} -\frac1{(8j+5)^2}-\frac1{(8j+7)^2}\right\}. \tag{13} \] For example, integrate the Abel-regularized cosine series and then use the absolute convergence of the resulting sine series. Each block displayed in (13) is positive. The first three blocks, with \(\sqrt2>707/500\) and \(\pi<22/7\), give \[ \psi(\pi/2,0)>239/250. \tag{14} \] For the integral correction use \(\sqrt2<99/70\) and \(\pi<22/7\). At \(H=h_0\), the excess of the resulting lower bound over \(1/500\) is exactly \[ \frac{239}{250}-\frac{107}{100} +\frac{h_0^2/2-h_0^4/24}{(99/70)(22/7)}-\frac1{500} =\frac{261699551}{522720000000}>0 . \tag{15} \] This proves (9). \(\square\) ## 3. The full complete-end kernel at both parities Let \(\mathcal K_N(t)\) be the original low complete-end factor, with indices \(0\le j\le N-1-\lfloor N/2\rfloor\). The [odd last-row theorem](research_last_physical_row_riccati.md) and [even low-index comparison](research_even_complete_low_kernel.md) give on a fixed complex neighborhood of \(\mathcal R\) \[ \mathcal K_N(t)=\exp\{N\psi(t,0)+e_N(t)\},\qquad |\partial_t^\ell e_N(t)|\le C_\ell\log N \tag{16} \] for every fixed \(\ell\), after shrinking that neighborhood for derivative estimates. This use is legitimate because \(\Re(-2\cos t)\le0\) on \(\mathcal R\). Write \(D_N(t)=K_N(t,0)-\mathcal K_N(t)\). The [original radical Fourier bound](research_high_newton_radical_contraction.md#7-fourier-bounds-for-the-original-radical-polynomials) gives, at both parities, \[ |D_N(t)|\le N^2e^{(N-1)|\Im t|}. \tag{17} \] At odd levels it is identically zero. This bound needs no restriction such as \(|\Im(-2\cos t)|>1\). **Corollary 3.** There is a fixed complex neighborhood \(\mathcal V\) of \(\mathcal R\) on which, through all sufficiently large integer levels, \[ \begin{split} K_N(t,0)&=\exp\{N\psi(t,0)+\widehat e_N(t)\}\ne0,\\ |\partial_t^\ell\widehat e_N(t)|&\le C_\ell\log N,\\ K_N(t,0)/\mathcal K_N(t)&=1+O(e^{-cN}) \end{split} \tag{18} \] for some \(c>0\), with the same exponential relative error for every fixed derivative on smaller neighborhoods. *Proof.* By compactness, (9) persists with a smaller positive gap for \(\Re\psi(t,0)-|\Im t|\) on a complex neighborhood of \(\mathcal R\). Equations (16)--(17) then bound \(|D_N/\mathcal K_N|\) by a polynomial times a strictly decaying exponential, uniformly there. For all large levels this ratio has modulus less than \(1/2\). Define \(\widehat e_N=e_N+\Log(1+D_N/\mathcal K_N)\) using the logarithm near zero. Cauchy's formula on smaller neighborhoods proves all derivative statements. \(\square\) The normal derivatives here are in the selected ordinary spectral variable \(w=-2\cos t\), on neighborhoods of its nonzero geometric selected angles. Since \(\sin t\ne0\) there, fixed \(w\)-derivatives follow from (18). The other boundary argument of the kernel remains exactly complete. This theorem does not analytically continue the estimates to a fixed nonzero neighborhood in that outside argument. In particular the [local internal-pair Gaussian theorem](research_internal_pair_local_gaussian.md) may use the full original complete-end kernels at both parities. The global low-wire and trace cycle still needs its own bounds. There is no contradiction with the even-level bare-kernel counterexamples at homogeneous longer-path angles with \(\Re t>\pi/2\), outside \(\mathcal R\). ## 4. Exact scalar check The [independent rational check](../experiments/check_internal_pair_complete_edge_gap.py) uses only positive Taylor partial sums and exact fractions. It checks the height comparisons, the three positive Fourier blocks, and the strict margin (15). Its [saved record](../repro/results/research-internal-pair-complete-edge-gap.json) retains script and proof hashes. ~~~sh python3 experiments/check_internal_pair_complete_edge_gap.py ~~~

title: Grouped angular connectors for every positive internal pair
text: # Grouped angular connectors for every positive internal pair Research proof, updated 4 November 2026. Frozen manuscripts are unchanged. The folded angular endpoint terms become uniformly smaller than the geometric rate when paired with the whole other trace. This uses its exact half-band source, not an independent asymptotic or a worst-case bound for each horizontal trace piece. The result holds at complete outside colors, through both level parities, with every original physical first normal retained. Section 5 extends the grouped estimate to free outside colors, using actual physical values and normals on the whole contour. This supplies an upper bound throughout the real outside period and a fixed complex neighborhood of completeness; it does not assert decay as a real outside angle moves away from completeness. ## 1. Exact decomposition of one original trace Fix a real wire interval \(I=[\alpha,\beta]\Subset(0,1/2)\) containing the retained indices of the [combined contour reduction](research_internal_pair_combined_contour_reduction.md). Use a slightly larger compact interval for estimates, so that all \(O(N^{-1})\) half-grid adjustments are included. Put \(D=N-1\), \(\eta=(-1)^D\), and \[ C_{N,n}=e^{\pi i nD^2/(4N)},\qquad W_{n,N}(x)=\phi_N[R^n\mathbf B_N(x)K_N(\,\cdot\,,0)] . \tag{1} \] The function \(W_{n,N}\) is the actual half-band source with frequencies \(-D/2,-D/2+1,\ldots,D/2\). For a midpoint angular cut \(T_N=T+O(N^{-1})<\pi\), \(e^{iNT_N}=-\eta\), let \(O_{n,N}\) be its original omitted physical residues. Every first normal remains with its root. Use the exact factorial representative \(B_N(x,t)\) in the retained trace, and define \[ g_{n,N}(x,t)= \sin t\,B_N(x,t)K_N(t,0)e^{inNt^2/(4\pi)} . \tag{2} \] It is odd in \(t\). Choose a positive endpoint height \(\epsilon_n\), and any permitted lower path \(\Gamma_n(x)\) from \(-T_N-i\epsilon_n\) to \(T_N-i\epsilon_n\). The exact folded trace identity gives \[ \begin{split} H_{n,N}(x) &=-\frac{N^2C_{N,n}}{\pi i} \int_{\Gamma_n(x)} \frac{g_{n,N}(x,t)e^{-iNt}} {(1-\eta e^{-iNt})^2}\,dt,\\ V_{n,N}(x) &=\frac{\eta N^2C_{N,n}}{\pi} \int_{-\epsilon_n}^{\epsilon_n} \frac{g_{n,N}(x,T_N+is)} {4\cosh^2(Ns/2)}\,ds,\\ W_{n,N}(x)&=H_{n,N}(x)+V_{n,N}(x)+O_{n,N}(x). \end{split} \tag{3} \] All scalars, charges, and folded endpoint signs in (3) are those of the [original exact trace](research_exact_complete_trace_contour.md#3-removing-outer-grid-points-before-contour-deformation). In particular the double-pole denominator retains the first normal; it has not been replaced by a single Fourier mode. The odd simple node remains in the retained trace. The exact identity holds pointwise in \(x\). The lower paths and their endpoint heights may therefore taper with \(x\), as proved in the [endpoint-taper lemma](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_internal_pair_endpoint_taper.md). The estimates below remain uniform if their positive endpoint heights stay below the chosen \(\epsilon_n\). ## 2. The exact factorial exponent at the angular endpoint Let \(\mathfrak b(x,t)\) be the original continuous factorial upper exponent, with both terms of each reciprocal reflection included. On every fixed compact wire strip, \[ \mathfrak b(x,\pi)=\pi|\Im x|. \tag{4} \] Indeed \(J(1-x)=-J(x)\), so \(b(x,\pi)=-J(-x)-J(x)\). For \(\Im x>0\), the argument \(-x\) uses the lower continuation \(J_-(-x)=-J(x)+i\pi x\), hence \(b(x,\pi)=-i\pi x\). For \(\Im x<0\), the upper continuation gives \(b(x,\pi)=i\pi x\). Their real boundary values agree when \(\Im x=0\). This normalization can also be seen directly, without dropping an endpoint zero: \[ B_N(x,\pi)=\frac{2\cos(\pi Nx)}N \left(\frac{G_N(Nx-1/2)}{G_N(Nx)}\right)^2 . \tag{5} \] Use \(G_N(z)G_N(N-1-z)=N\) and the exact reciprocal reflection to obtain (5). The cosine keeps both exponential terms. Its absolute upper exponent is exactly that in (4). Fix \(Y_0<\infty\). On \(\Re x\in I\), \(|\Im x|\le Y_0\), the factorial arguments at \(t=\pi\) stay away from their integer singularities, except for crossing the negative real cut. The real upper primitive is continuous across that cut and has bounded one-sided derivatives on this compact set. Therefore \[ \mathfrak b(x,T+is) \le\pi|\Im x|+\omega_I(\pi-T+|s|),\qquad \omega_I(\rho)\longrightarrow0 . \tag{6} \] One may take \(\omega_I(\rho)=C_I\rho\) for sufficiently small \(\rho\). The exact uniform factorial bound then gives \[ |B_N(x,T_N+is)|\le CN^A e^{N\{\pi|\Im x|+\omega_I(\pi-T+|s|+O(N^{-1}))\}}. \tag{7} \] This remains valid on the real cut and at every reciprocal factorial zero. It is an estimate of the actual interpolation inside the original trace, not just of its lattice values. ## 3. The complete outside factor on a short vertical segment Write \(\Psi(t)=\psi(t,0)\). For fixed \(T<\pi\), choose \(\epsilon>0\) small enough that the vertical segment \(T+i[-\epsilon,\epsilon]\) and a neighborhood of it satisfy \(\Re(-2\cos t)<2\). For \(T>\pi/2\), it suffices to choose \(2\epsilon<(\pi-T)/2\), with a strict margin for midpoint rounding. Indeed \(\cos(\pi-T)\cosh((\pi-T)/2)<1\). The actual low complete-end kernel has \(\exp\{N\Psi(t)+O(\log N)\}\) on this compact neighborhood, by the last-row and even low-kernel theorems. The complete radical obeys \(N^2e^{N|\Im t|}\). Thus the full kernel, through both parities, satisfies \[ |K_N(T_N+is,0)|\le CN^A e^{N\kappa(T,\epsilon)},\qquad \kappa(T,\epsilon)= \max\left\{\sup_{|s|\le2\epsilon}\Re\Psi(T+is),\,2\epsilon\right\} +o_{N\to\infty}(1). \tag{8} \] Here the slightly larger neighborhood absorbs rounding and fixed selected-variable derivatives; decrease \(\epsilon\) first if necessary. Since \(J\) is continuous at the endpoint arguments, \(\Psi(t)\to0\) as \(t\to\pi\) within this domain. Consequently \(\kappa(T,\epsilon)\) can be made arbitrarily small by first taking \(T\) close to \(\pi\), then choosing \(\epsilon\) sufficiently small. No bound on free outside-color derivatives is inferred from this complete-end estimate. **Lemma 1.** Given \(q>0\), choose \(T<\pi\) sufficiently close to \(\pi\). For every fixed integer \(n\), its positive endpoint height \(\epsilon_n\) can then be chosen so that \[ |V_{n,N}(x)|\le CN^A e^{N\{\pi|\Im x|+q\}}, \qquad \Re x\in I,\quad |\Im x|\le Y_0 . \tag{9} \] *Proof.* The vertical weight in (3) has modulus at most \(1/4\). The sine and fixed curve length are bounded. The original crossing Gaussian has modulus \[ \left|e^{inN(T_N+is)^2/(4\pi)}\right| \le \exp\{N|n|(T+o(1))|s|/(2\pi)\}. \tag{10} \] Combining (7)--(10), the exponent in excess of \(\pi|\Im x|\) tends to zero as \(T\to\pi\) and then \(\epsilon_n\to0\). The factor \(N^2C_{N,n}\) in (3) costs only a polynomial because \(|C_{N,n}|=1\). Choose these parameters with a strict margin below \(q\). This proves the assertion for all sufficiently large levels; the remaining finite levels are absorbed in the constant. \(\square\) ## 4. Group with the whole other trace before taking absolute values The [physical-tail and half-band theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_internal_pair_angular_tail_transport.md) gives, on the whole complex wire plane with bounded height, \[ \begin{split} |W_{n,N}(x)|&\le CN^A e^{N\{3M_\infty/2+\pi|\Im x|\}},\\ |O_{n,N}(x)|&\le CN^A e^{N\{m(T_0)+\Psi(T_0)+\pi|\Im x|\}} . \end{split} \tag{11} \] Here \(T_0<T_N\) is a fixed nearby lower cut and \(m(T_0)+\Psi(T_0)\to0\) as \(T_0\to\pi\). These bounds reconstruct each half-band function separately from its \(N\) original samples. They include high Newton indices, every physical first normal, and both parities. Choose \(T_0<T<\pi\) close enough to \(\pi\) and the endpoint heights in Lemma 1 so that both small exponents are below \(q<1/100\). Put \(D_n=V_n+O_n\). Then \[ |D_n(x)|\le CN^A e^{N\{\pi|\Im x|+q\}},\qquad |H_n(x)|\le CN^A e^{N\{3M_\infty/2+\pi|\Im x|\}}, \tag{12} \] where the second inequality follows from the exact identity \(H_n=W_n-D_n\). **Theorem 2.** On the retained wire strip at the actual geometric pair height \(Y=\Im x_*\), \[ |W_n(x)W_p(x)-H_n(x)H_p(x)| \le CN^A e^{N\{3M_\infty/2+2\pi|\Im x|+q\}} <CN^A e^{N(M_{n,p}-1/100)} \tag{13} \] for \(\Re x\in I\), \(|\Im x|\le Y\), after the choices above. *Proof.* Use the exact grouping \[ W_nW_p-H_nH_p=D_nW_p+H_nD_p . \tag{14} \] Thus every folded angular connector and every omitted physical-angle term is retained, including their intersections. Equations (11)--(12) give the first bound in (13). The actual wire-height theorem gives \(2\pi Y<3/4\). Together with \(M_\infty<7/6\), \(q<1/100\), and \(M_{n,p}\ge M_{3,3}>63/25\), this yields \[ \frac32M_\infty+2\pi Y+q <\frac74+\frac34+\frac1{100} =\frac{251}{100}<M_{n,p}-\frac1{100}. \tag{15} \] All these scalar and geometric inputs are proved in the physical-tail and wire-height note. \(\square\) For the retained-index Cauchy formula, the exact wire kernel is \(1/(1-e^{2\pi iNx})\). It is bounded on a fixed positive upper height, has the favorable factor \(e^{-2\pi N|\Im x|}\) on a lower height, and has modulus at most one on a half-index vertical side. Multiplication by that kernel and integration therefore preserve the strict gap (13), with only polynomial factors. The conclusion also holds for the wire graphs and pointwise trace tapers of the endpoint-collar construction, provided their heights stay within \([-Y,Y]\) and the angular endpoint heights stay below the chosen \(\epsilon_n,\epsilon_p\). After combining this theorem with the real-tail and endpoint-collar reductions, the unresolved contour consists of the two joint lower-trace integrals over the middle wire band, including its exact wire alias. The original first normals and all higher trace charges are still present in those integrals. No independent geometric asymptotic for \(W_n\) or \(W_p\) was assumed. The extension below replaces the complete-point inputs in (8) and (11) by estimates of the actual finite polynomials. It does not continue a relative error known only at the complete outside color. ## 5. Free outside colors, original normals, and coupled trace surfaces Write the two ordinary outside colors as \(\zeta=-2\cos u\) and \(\omega=-2\cos v\). All derivatives in \(\zeta,\omega\) below are ordinary polynomial derivatives, including at \(-2\); they are not angular derivatives divided by a vanishing sine. Let \(L_N(w,\zeta)\) be the literal low Newton kernel and let \(K_N-L_N\) be the full original radical. Replace \(K_N(t,0)\) in (1)--(3) by \(K_N(t,u)\), and denote the resulting exact functions by \(W_n(x;\zeta),H_n(x;\zeta),V_n(x;\zeta),O_n(x;\zeta)\). They retain the identity \(W_n=H_n+V_n+O_n\). Indeed the new factor remains even in the trace angle, so the original folding, double-pole weights, and odd-level simple endpoint are unchanged. **Lemma 3 (whole-contour upper bound).** Let \(\mathcal T\) be a compact set of trace angles whose color image is contained in \(\Re w<2\). Suppose, on a neighborhood of this compact set, \[ \Re\Psi(t)>|\Im t|+\delta,\qquad \delta>0. \tag{16} \] For every fixed ordinary outside derivative order \(k\), uniformly for \(t\in\mathcal T\), \(-\pi\le\Re u\le\pi\), and bounded \(|\Im u|\), \[ \left|\partial_\zeta^k K_N(-2\cos t,\zeta) \big|_{\zeta=-2\cos u}\right| \le C_kN^{A_k} e^{N\{\Re\Psi(t)+|\Im u|\}}. \tag{17} \] All fixed ordinary selected-color derivatives satisfy the same bound after shrinking the selected-color neighborhood and increasing the polynomial power. *Proof.* Equations (5) and (9) of the [free-outside observation theorem](research_free_boundary_half_charge_observation.md#1-a-whole-contour-bound-from-the-actual-physical-rows) give, respectively, the actual low-kernel and radical bounds \[ \begin{split} |\partial_\zeta^k L_N(-2\cos t,-2\cos u)| &\le C_kN^{A_k}e^{N\Re\Psi(t)+J_N|\Im u|},\\ |\partial_\zeta^k(K_N-L_N)(-2\cos t,-2\cos u)| &\le C_kN^{A_k}e^{D(|\Im t|+|\Im u|)}, \qquad J_N=\lfloor(N-1)/2\rfloor . \end{split} \tag{18} \] The first estimate follows from the original row recurrence, ordinary Chebyshev interpolation, and the polynomial Bernstein bound. The second is the original radical Fourier bound. Since \(J_N,D\le N\), (16) proves (17). The estimates hold on a fixed selected-color neighborhood inside \(\Re w<2\). Cauchy's formula on color circles of radius \(1/N\) costs only powers of \(N\); the change in \(\Re\Psi(w)\) on such circles is \(O(1/N)\). This proves the derivative assertion even when the angular coordinate is ramified at \(t=0\). \(\square\) Every fixed angular cut \(T<\pi\) admits sufficiently small positive heights for (16): \(\Psi(\tau)\ge\Psi(T)>0\) for \(|\tau|\le T\), and the color image remains in \(\Re w<2\) at small heights. The half-charge rectangle \(|\Re t|\le\pi/2,\ |\Im t|\le2/5\) has the same property by the proved complete-edge gap. Thus this lemma applies to whole retained contours, not merely near their stationary points. It is an upper bound; it does not assert a nonzero free-outside packet on an enlarged selected-color domain. **Theorem 4 (free-outside grouped connectors).** Fix the integer powers \(n,p\ge3\), the compact wire interval \(I\), and the actual pair height \(Y\). Given sufficiently small \(q>0\), choose the cuts and positive endpoint heights as in Lemma 1. Then, for each fixed \(k,\ell\ge0\), \[ \begin{split} &\left|\partial_\zeta^k\partial_\omega^\ell \{W_n(x;\zeta)W_p(x;\omega) -H_n(x;\zeta)H_p(x;\omega)\}\right|\\ &\qquad\le CN^A e^{N\{3M_\infty/2+2\pi|\Im x|+q+|\Im u|+|\Im v|\}}, \quad \zeta=-2\cos u,\quad\omega=-2\cos v , \end{split} \tag{19} \] uniformly for \(\Re x\in I,\ |\Im x|\le Y\), all real outside angles, and a fixed bounded strip in those angles. In particular there are fixed ordinary color disks about \(\zeta=\omega=-2\), independent of \(N\), on which the right side is at most \[ CN^A e^{N(M_{n,p}-3/200)}. \tag{20} \] The same strict estimate holds throughout the real outside period. Neither assertion includes a positive loss proportional to \(1-\cos u\) or \(1-\cos v\). *Proof of the endpoint estimate.* Fix \(T<\pi\) first, then choose the endpoint height sufficiently small for (16) on \(T+i[-2\epsilon_n,2\epsilon_n]\). The supremum of \(\Re\Psi\) on this segment tends to zero as \(T\to\pi\) and then \(\epsilon_n\to0\). Lemma 3, the exact factorial estimate (7), and the crossing estimate (10) therefore prove \[ |\partial_\zeta^k V_n(x;\zeta)| \le CN^A e^{N\{\pi|\Im x|+q+|\Im u|\}}. \tag{21} \] The fixed ordinary outside derivatives were estimated in (18) before the endpoint integral. No derivative estimate has been inferred from its complete-point value. *Proof for the whole source and omitted rows.* At a double physical node \(c_a\), put \(F_{a,N}(\zeta)=K_N(c_a,\zeta)\) and \(G_{a,N}(\zeta)=\partial_wK_N(c_a,\zeta)\). The exact physical-row bound (11) in the free-outside observation note states \[ |\partial_\zeta^k F_{a,N}(-2\cos u)| +|\partial_\zeta^k G_{a,N}(-2\cos u)| \le C_kN^{A_k}F_{a,N}(-2)e^{D|\Im u|}. \tag{22} \] At the odd simple node only the value term is used. Formula (22) includes the full kernel and its actual selected first normal, not only its low part. Apply the original Hermite trace to each literal sample \(x=j/N\). The crossing values and first normals have polynomial size for fixed \(n\). All-color Newton values and their required ordinary first normals have rate at most \(m(0)=M_\infty/2\), while \(F_{a,N}(-2)\) has rate at most \(M_\infty\). Thus every sample of \(\partial_\zeta^kW_n\) has rate at most \(3M_\infty/2+|\Im u|\). For omitted angular nodes \(|t_a|\ge T_0\), the actual [physical-tail theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_internal_pair_angular_tail_transport.md) instead gives rates \(m(T_0)\) for the Newton value and normal, and \(\Psi(T_0)\) for \(F_{a,N}(-2)\). The normal estimate is on the corresponding real color interval before restriction to nodes, so Markov differentiation preserves the exponent. Hence omitted samples have rate \(m(T_0)+\Psi(T_0)+|\Im u|\). For every outside derivative these remain exact half-band functions of \(x\). Reconstruct each function separately from its \(N\) samples. The cardinal bound adds \(\pi|\Im x|\) to its rate and only polynomial factors. Consequently \[ \begin{split} |\partial_\zeta^kW_n(x;\zeta)| &\le CN^A e^{N\{3M_\infty/2+\pi|\Im x|+|\Im u|\}},\\ |\partial_\zeta^kO_n(x;\zeta)| &\le CN^A e^{N\{m(T_0)+\Psi(T_0) +\pi|\Im x|+|\Im u|\}} . \end{split} \tag{23} \] All original first normals and both level parities have been retained in this construction. Take \(T_0,T\) close enough to \(\pi\) that the small exponent in (23) is below \(q\). Equations (21)--(23) give the analogues of (12), with the added \(|\Im u|\). The exact grouping (14), and Leibniz's rule for its fixed ordinary derivatives, prove (19). For (20), take \(q<1/400\) and choose the ordinary color disks small enough that their small angular lifts satisfy \(|\Im u|+|\Im v|<1/400\). Such disks exist because \(-2\cos u+2=u^2+O(u^4)\); the two small lifts differ only by sign and the actual functions are polynomials in the color. Using \(2\pi Y<3/4,\ M_\infty<7/6,\ M_{n,p}>63/25\), \[ \frac32M_\infty+2\pi Y+q+|\Im u|+|\Im v| <\frac74+\frac34+\frac1{200} =\frac{501}{200}<M_{n,p}-\frac3{200}. \tag{24} \] For all real \(u,v\) the imaginary costs vanish, so the same conclusion holds uniformly on the real outside period. The wire kernel and its half-grid vertical sides are treated exactly as after (15). \(\square\) The theorem is also compatible with a coupled lower-trace surface. For each fixed wire point, start with the product of the two constant-height lower segments, with endpoint heights \(\epsilon_n,\epsilon_p\). Replace it by a smooth graph \[ (\tau,\rho)\longmapsto (\tau-ih_n(\tau,\rho),\rho-ih_p(\tau,\rho)), \qquad -T_N\le\tau,\rho\le T_N , \tag{25} \] which agrees with that product on its entire boundary, has strictly positive heights, and stays in the regular domain of the finite factorial representatives. Suppose its homotopy to the product has these properties as well. The product of the two original lower-trace densities is a closed holomorphic two-form below the physical poles. Stokes' theorem relative to the fixed boundary therefore identifies its integral on (25) with \(H_nH_p\), with the literal scalar and pullback Jacobian retained. There is no additional boundary term from the interior coupling of the heights. Its existing folded endpoint curtains are exactly the ones already included in (19). This equality may be applied pointwise along the wire contour. Height derivatives in the wire direction disappear after wedging with \(dx\), or equivalently by the pointwise residue identity and Fubini. Thus (19)--(20) also control the difference between the original product and this coupled lower-trace integral. The statement does not bound that integral itself or prove a global pair coefficient. A whole-boundary decay estimate for the remaining main integral, required for further composition, remains separate from the upper bounds proved here.

title: Actual local Gaussian preparation for every positive internal pair
text:
# Actual local Gaussian preparation for every positive internal pair Research proof, 3 November 2026. Frozen manuscripts are unchanged. For every fixed pair of integer powers \(n,p\ge3\), the original mixed wire and trace density with its low-index complete outside edges has a nonzero Gaussian component at its geometric critical point, through both level parities. At odd levels those outside edges equal the full original kernels. Section 6 upgrades the local conclusion to the full original complete-end factors at both parities on the actual pair domain. Sections 1–6 obtain its norm and relative annihilation residual from the exact physical-row normalization. Section 7 uses the sharper edge packet to compute a fixed, nonzero leading amplitude and the precise power \(N^{-3/2}\). It also allows both outside colors to vary in fixed complex neighborhoods. Neither argument assumes an asymptotic for the filled pair. This is a local source theorem. It neither identifies the coefficient of this local contour in the whole original cycle nor bounds that cycle's complement. The free-boundary statement in Section 7 includes all fixed ordinary boundary derivatives, but still concerns only the localized contour. ## 1. The exact density and the geometric point Put \(D=N-1\), \(\eta=(-1)^D\), and \[ C_{N,k}=\exp\!\left( rac{\pi i kD^2}{4N}ight). 	ag{1} \] Use the original Newton kernel and full Frobenius trace. Write \(L_N^{m ind}=N-1-\lfloor N/2floor\), and retain the literal low-index complete-end factor \[ \mathcal K_N(t) =\sum_{j=0}^{L_N^{m ind}}e_j(-2\cos t)e_j(-2). \] At odd levels \(\mathcal K_N(t)=K_N(t,0)\) exactly: every removed radical polynomial vanishes at the simple physical node \(-2\). At even levels only the low-index sector is used. The source under consideration is \[ \mathcal P^{m low\,out}_{n,p,N} =\phi_N^{(t)}\phi_N^{(r)} [R(t)^nR(r)^p\mathcal K_N(t)K_N(t,r)\mathcal K_N(r)]. 	ag{2} \] In particular the two selected vertices have degree two, each with its literal complete outside edge. The original first normal at every double physical root remains in each trace. The [exact wire averaging theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_internal_wire_exact_circle_averaging.md) gives \[  egin{split} \mathcal P^{m low\,out}_{n,p,N} &=N\int_{iY}^{1+iY}W_{n,N}(x)W_{p,N}(x)\,dx,\ W_{k,N}(x)&=\phi_N[R^k\mathbf B_N(x)\mathcal K_N]. \end{split} 	ag{3} \] The half-band quotient-valued \(\mathbf B_N(x)\) retains all physical jets. Its exact factorial representative at those jets is \[ B_N(x,t)=  rac{N}{ G_N(N(1/2-x+t/(2\pi))-1/2) G_N(N(1/2-x-t/(2\pi))-1/2)G_N(Nx)^2}. 	ag{4} \] Here \(G_N\) is the original [canonical sine factorial](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/exact_factorial_interpolation_and_complex_contours.md). The numerator \(N\) follows from its exact reflection identity. Formula (4) is not asserted to equal the canonical polynomial at arbitrary angular points. Agreement of the full physical jets is the reason it is legitimate in the original residue trace. Write \(z=(x,t,r)\). In a regular lower-horizontal trace chart define the exact holomorphic density \[  egin{split} I_N(z)={}&B_N(x,t)B_N(x,r)\mathcal K_N(t)\mathcal K_N(r)\sin t\sin r\ &{}	imes  rac{\exp\{iN(nt^2+pr^2)/(4\pi)-iN(t+r)\}} {(1-\eta e^{-iNt})^2(1-\eta e^{-iNr})^2}. \end{split} 	ag{5} \] The [original trace formula](research_exact_complete_trace_contour.md) has lower-horizontal scalar \(iN^2C_{N,k}/\pi\) for each selected vertex. Thus the corresponding three-dimensional density, including the wire factor in (3), is \[ - rac{C_{N,n}C_{N,p}N^5}{\pi^2}\,I_N(z)\,dx\,dt\,dr. 	ag{6} \] No first normal or higher charge in the rational denominators has been discarded. Other trace segments, physical rows, and any interpolation-divisor currents are not represented by (5); their place in a global deformation is a separate problem. Use the original primitives \[  egin{split} J'(v)&=\Log(2\sin\pi v),\qquad J(0)=0,\ b(x,t)&=-J(1/2-x+t/(2\pi)) -J(1/2-x-t/(2\pi))-2J(x),\ \Phi(z)&=b(x,t)+b(x,r)+\psi(t,0)+\psi(r,0) + rac{i(nt^2+pr^2)}{4\pi}-i(t+r). \end{split} 	ag{7} \] The \(J\) branch is continued from \(0<v<1\) in \(0<\Re v<1\); the edge phase has its original complete constant. Let \(z_*=(x_*,t_*,r_*)\) be the positive geometric point of this internal pair at unit charges. Its existence is supplied by the [positive charge-cube theorem](research_positive_path_fractional_charge_cube.md). The [internal-pair angle bound](research_internal_pair_angle_bound.md) gives \[ 0<\Re t_*,\Re r_*<\pi/2,\qquad \Im t_*,\Im r_*<0. 	ag{8} \] The [actual wire-order theorem](research_positive_path_real_wire_order.md) places \(x_*\) and both sets of shifted arguments in the regular factorial strips and fixes the zero logarithmic lift of the wire equation. The unexponentiated filling equations then give \[ 
abla\Phi(z_*)=0,\qquad \mathcal H=-\Phi''(z_*),\qquad R=\Re\mathcal H>0. 	ag{9} \] Indeed the [mixed-phase concavity theorem without height ordering](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_mixed_phase_height_extension_and_wire_order.md) applies to the two complete-end-compensated terms in (7). Its real change of coordinates from \((x,s_1,s_2)\) to \((x,t,r)\), where \(s_i=1/2-t_i/(2\pi)\), preserves strict definiteness. Consequently there are a fixed real ball \(U\) about zero and \(c>0\) such that \[ \Re\{\Phi(z_*+v)-\Phi(z_*)\}\le-c|v|^2 \quad(v\in U\subset\mathbb R^3). 	ag{10} \] All these statements concern the actual coupled geometric point, not arbitrary independent endpoint parameters. ## 2. A nonzero source normalization from the last physical row Put \(w(t)=-2\cos t\), and let \(N\) tend to infinity through both parities. By (8), both \(w(t_*)\) and \(w(r_*)\) have negative real part. Choose a fixed complex neighborhood \(\mathcal U\) of \(z_*\) where their real parts stay below \(2-\gamma\), for some \(\gamma>0\), and every factorial argument stays in a compact subset of its regular strip. The [last-physical-row theorem](research_last_physical_row_riccati.md), Corollary 2, proves the odd-level assertion below. At even levels the [exact low-index comparison](research_even_complete_low_kernel.md), Theorem 1 and (21), proves the same assertion for the prescribed low factor: its ratio to the last physical row is \(1+O(N^{-1/2})\), with all fixed derivatives. Thus at both parities \[  egin{split} \mathcal K_N(t)&=\exp\{N\psi(t,0)+e_N(t)\},\ |\partial_t^\ell e_N(t)|&\le C_\ell\log N \qquad(\ell	ext{ fixed}), \end{split} 	ag{11} \] and likewise for \(r\). Its logarithm is fixed by the original row \(F_{0,N}=1\), through the sum of the right-half-plane ratio logarithms. It is not a principal logarithm chosen independently for the final polynomial. At even levels add the logarithm near zero of the last-row quotient \(1+O(N^{-1/2})\); this changes none of the bounds in (11). Define the exact nonzero scalar \[ Q_N=\exp\{e_N(t_*)+e_N(r_*)\} =\mathcal K_N(t_*)\mathcal K_N(r_*) e^{-N(\psi(t_*,0)+\psi(r_*,0))}. 	ag{12} \] Thus, after increasing a fixed constant \(C\), \[ N^{-C}\le |Q_N|\le N^C. 	ag{13} \] This normalization uses two independently estimated original low-index complete-end factors. It does not divide by the unknown filled pair (2). The canonical factorial expansion, with its half-integer shifts retained, gives uniformly on \(\mathcal U\) \[ B_N(x,t)=  rac{e^{Nb(x,t)}}{2N\sin(\pi x)} (1+O(N^{-1})). 	ag{14} \] Every fixed derivative of the relative error obeys the same bound on smaller neighborhoods. In fact \(G_N(Nv-1/2)=N^{1/2}e^{NJ(v)}(1+O(N^{-1}))\), while \(G_N(Nx)^2=2N\sin(\pi x)e^{2NJ(x)}(1+O(N^{-1}))\); substitution in (4) proves (14) with its precise factor. The heights in (8) are strictly positive. On a smaller \(\mathcal U\), both rational trace denominators in (5) are \(1+O(e^{-c_0N})\), including every fixed derivative after decreasing \(c_0>0\). Equations (11)--(14) therefore give \[ I_N(z)=N^{-2}a(z) \exp\{N\Phi(z)+e_N(t)+e_N(r)\} (1+O(N^{-1})), \qquad a(z)= rac{\sin t\sin r}{4\sin^2(\pi x)}. 	ag{15} \] In particular \(a_*=a(z_*)
e0\). All factors in this calculation come from the original finite density (5). ## 3. Local preparation and its observed Gaussian coefficient Choose \(\zeta\in C_c^\infty(U)\), equal to one near zero, with \(0\le\zeta\le1\). For \(\xi\in\mathbb R^3\), set \[ G_N(\xi)= \zeta(\xi/\sqrt N)\, N^2 Q_N^{-1}e^{-N\Phi(z_*)} I_N(z_*+\xi/\sqrt N), \qquad \mathscr D_{\mathcal H}=
abla_\xi+\mathcal H\xi . 	ag{16} \] The function is extended by zero outside the cutoff chart. All norms in the following theorem use real Lebesgue measure in \(\xi\). **Theorem 1.** For every fixed integer pair \(n,p\ge3\), along all sufficiently large integer levels, \[  egin{split} \|G_N-a_*e^{-\xi^T\mathcal H\xi/2}\|_{L^1} +\|G_N-a_*e^{-\xi^T\mathcal H\xi/2}\|_{L^2} &=O\!\left( rac{\log N}{\sqrt N}ight),\ \|\mathscr D_{\mathcal H}G_N\|_{L^2} &=O\!\left( rac{\log N}{\sqrt N}ight),\ \|G_N\|_{L^2} &=|a_*| rac{\pi^{3/4}}{(\det R)^{1/4}} +O\!\left( rac{\log N}{\sqrt N}ight). \end{split} 	ag{17} \] In particular the norm is bounded below by a positive constant, and the relative annihilation residual tends to zero. The same \(L^2\) error holds after multiplication by any fixed power of \(1+|\xi|\). *Proof.* On the cutoff chart (11) gives \[  egin{split} |e_N(t_*+\xi_t/\sqrt N)-e_N(t_*)| +|e_N(r_*+\xi_r/\sqrt N)-e_N(r_*)| &\le C rac{\log N}{\sqrt N}|\xi|,\  ig|
abla_\xi(e_N(t)+e_N(r)) ig| &\le C rac{\log N}{\sqrt N}. \end{split} 	ag{18} \] Together with (10), this bounds the normalized density by \(C e^{-c|\xi|^2/2}\), since \(-c|\xi|^2+C(\log N)|\xi|/\sqrt N\le -c|\xi|^2/2+C'(\log N)^2/N\). Taylor expansion at the full critical point gives \[  egin{split} N(\Phi(z_*+\xi/\sqrt N)-\Phi(z_*)) &=-	frac12\xi^T\mathcal H\xi +O(|\xi|^3/\sqrt N),\ \sqrt N\,
abla\Phi(z_*+\xi/\sqrt N)+\mathcal H\xi &=O(|\xi|^2/\sqrt N). \end{split} 	ag{19} \] The elementary integral formula for \(e^u-e^v\), applied with the negative quadratic bounds for the two real parts, now gives an integrable error bounded by \[ C rac{\log N}{\sqrt N} (1+|\xi|^3)e^{-c_1|\xi|^2} 	ag{20} \] after decreasing \(c_1>0\). The amplitude variation costs \(C|\xi|/\sqrt N\), and the relative error in (15) costs \(C/N\). Outside the cutoff the limiting Gaussian has an exponentially small tail. This proves both norm approximations and their fixed polynomially weighted versions. Differentiating (15) in the rescaled variables, equations (18)--(19) give the same kind of integrable bound for \(\mathscr D_{\mathcal H}G_N\). The derivative of the cutoff has the factor \(N^{-1/2}\); its support has \(|\xi|\ge c_2\sqrt N\), so its contribution is exponentially small. Finally \[ \|a_*e^{-\xi^T\mathcal H\xi/2}\|_{L^2} =|a_*|\pi^{3/4}(\det R)^{-1/4}>0. \] This proves (17). \(\square\) The [already proved oscillator inequality](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_shifted_gaussian_observation.md) therefore applies to an independently normalized actual source: if \(\Pi_{\mathcal H}\) projects onto its normalized Gaussian, \[ \|(I-\Pi_{\mathcal H})G_N\|_2^2 \le  rac{\|\mathscr D_{\mathcal H}G_N\|_2^2} {2\lambda_{\min}(R)} =O\!\left( rac{(\log N)^2}{N}ight). 	ag{21} \] The norm on the right has not been inferred from the unknown integral (2). This is the additional source input that a spectral gap alone could not supply. There is also an explicit nonzero local observation. The Gaussian branch of \(\sqrt{\det\mathcal H}\), continued through \(\Re\mathcal H>0\), gives \[ \int_{\mathbb R^3}G_N(\xi)\,d\xi = rac{(2\pi)^{3/2}a_*}{\sqrt{\det\mathcal H}} \left(1+O\!\left( rac{\log N}{\sqrt N}ight)ight). 	ag{22} \] This follows from the \(L^1\) estimate, not from an unbounded constant test functional on \(L^2\). For precision, define the localized contour piece with its actual scalar (6) by \[ \mathcal P_{n,p,N}^{m loc} =- rac{C_{N,n}C_{N,p}N^5}{\pi^2} \int_{\mathbb R^3}\zeta(v) I_N(z_*+v)\,dv. 	ag{23} \] It has the nonzero expansion \[ \mathcal P_{n,p,N}^{m loc} =- rac{C_{N,n}C_{N,p}(2\pi)^{3/2}}{\pi^2} N^{3/2}Q_N  rac{a_*}{\sqrt{\det\mathcal H}}\, e^{N\Phi(z_*)} \left(1+O\!\left( rac{\log N}{\sqrt N}ight)ight). 	ag{24} \] Consequently \[ N^{-C}e^{N\Re\Phi(z_*)} \le|\mathcal P_{n,p,N}^{m loc}| \le N^C e^{N\Re\Phi(z_*)} 	ag{25} \] for a fixed \(C\), after increasing the lower level threshold. At this stage the normalization \(Q_N\) is controlled only by (13). Section 7 supplies its sharper asymptotic and hence the precise \(N^{-3/2}\) power. ## 4. The omitted outside radical has a strict gap after the traces Let \(\mathcal P^{m full}_{n,p,N}\) denote (2) with the two outside factors replaced by their full original kernels. Write \[ D_N(t)=K_N(t,0)-\mathcal K_N(t). 	ag{26} \] This is the radical complete-end factor. It vanishes identically at odd levels, but need not vanish at even levels. **Proposition 2.** For each fixed integer \(n,p\ge3\), \[ \left|\mathcal P^{m full}_{n,p,N} -\mathcal P^{m low\,out}_{n,p,N}ight| \le CN^A e^{2NM_\infty}, \qquad M_\infty=4G/\pi . 	ag{27} \] Moreover \(M_{n,p}:=\Re\Phi(z_*)>2M_\infty+1/100\). Consequently the error in (27) is exponentially smaller than the nonzero local piece (24). *Proof.* The [radical Fourier theorem](research_high_newton_radical_contraction.md#7-fourier-bounds-for-the-original-radical-polynomials), equations (34)--(36), proves \[ \sup_{w\in[-2,2]}|D_N(w)|\le N^2. 	ag{28} \] Here \(D_N(w)\) denotes (26) in its ordinary spectral variable. Indeed every radical \(e_j\) has real interval norm at most \(\sqrt{N-1}\), and there are fewer than \(N\) terms in \(\sum_j e_j(w)e_j(-2)\). Markov's polynomial derivative inequality gives polynomial bounds for its ordinary first normal as well, including both endpoint colors. The [real Newton estimate](research_three_crossing_real_period_newton_bound.md), equations (5), (8), and (13), gives \[ \sup_{w_1,w_2\in[-2,2]}|K_N(w_1,w_2)| \le CN^A e^{NM_\infty}. \] The same statement, at polynomial additional cost, holds for each first normal and mixed first normal by applying Markov's inequality in each variable. Original fixed crossing powers, the original trace, and multiplication of a fixed number of physical value/normal arrays all cost only powers of \(N\); this is the full Hermite-norm bound in [the original finite estimates](../papers/circle-tree-volume/finite-bounds.tex). The exact difference in (27) is the sum of the terms with outside factors \(D_N(t)K_N(r,0)\) and \(K_N(t,0)D_N(r)\), minus the term with \(D_N(t)D_N(r)\), always retaining the middle full kernel and both original traces. The first two have at most two exponentially sized kernel factors; the last has at most one. The bounds just proved give (27). This is an estimate of the traced terms, not their value on an off-grid complex angular contour. On the selected wire, the original branch identity \(b(x_*,t_*)+b(x_*,r_*)=\psi(t_*,r_*)\) is fixed at completeness and continued through the regular chart of the wire-order theorem. Thus \(\Re\Phi(z_*)\) has precisely the original three-edge stationary normalization. The [complete-end pair energy gap](research_radical_path_sector_gap.md#6-a-uniform-estimate-for-every-positive-pair-of-powers-at-least-three), Theorem 5, equation (23), is \(M_{n,p}>2M_\infty+1/100\). Combine it with (13), (24), and (27). \(\square\) ## 5. Exact scope of the advance This theorem establishes local norm growth, Gaussian preparation, and a nonzero local observed coefficient from the actual finite low-outer-edge sector at every fixed positive integer internal pair, at both level parities and complete outside ends. At odd levels this is the full source before contour localization. It is stronger than a formal quadratic expansion of a proposed phase: the actual outer factors in (5) are controlled by their original pinned recurrence and, at even levels, the exact alternating interpolation identity, and their possible \(N\)-dependent phase and magnitude are retained. All traced normal directions and both full trace denominators remain present. The remaining step is global. Formula (23) defines a local horizontal piece; it does not assert that this piece occurs with coefficient one in a deformation of (3), or that the other currents and regions have lower action. The exact high-index, alias, and boundary terms of that deformation still need to be controlled. The statements of Sections 1–6 fix the outside variables complete, as in (2). Their extension to ordinary derivatives in both outside variables is proved in Section 7. At even levels the last physical row has not been mistaken for the complete endpoint: the low factor is obtained by the separate exact interpolation comparison. Proposition 2 controls the omitted radical outside-edge sectors after their original traces. It does not control the rest of the low-outer-edge cycle, so it cannot by itself turn the local term into a full-source lower bound. No new universal lower bound for the original closing coefficient, volume theorem, or finite-exception conclusion is asserted. ## 6. The full original local density at both parities There is now a stronger pair-specific conclusion than the low-sector argument alone. The [complete-edge gap theorem](research_internal_pair_complete_edge_gap.md) uses the actual pair equations to prove \[ 0<\Re t_*,\Re r_*<\pi/2,\qquad 0<-\Im t_*,-\Im r_*<107/100, \qquad \Re\psi(t,0)-|\Im t|>1/500 	ag{29} \] on the closed pair box (with the last inequality interpreted there). Its Corollary 3 then proves, on a fixed complex neighborhood containing both selected angles, \[  rac{K_N(t,0)}{\mathcal K_N(t)} =1+O(e^{-cN}) 	ag{30} \] through both level parities, with every fixed derivative on smaller neighborhoods. This comparison follows from the original radical Fourier bound and the independently proved nonzero low kernel. It does not estimate a radical polynomial by a geometric kernel outside this domain. Define \(I_N^{m full}\) by replacing both \(\mathcal K_N\) factors in (5) by their full original kernels \(K_N(t,0)\), \(K_N(r,0)\). Keep the same known scalar \(Q_N\) in (12). Then on the cutoff chart \[ I_N^{m full}/I_N=1+O(e^{-cN}). 	ag{31} \] After the normalization (16), this and its first derivatives have exponentially small \(L^1\), \(L^2\), and annihilation errors. The Gaussian bounds used in (20) control these norms uniformly. Consequently Theorem 1 and the nonzero local integral (24) hold unchanged for the full original local density at both parities. This conclusion uses two exactly complete outside arguments. The normal data at the traced vertices are retained; fixed ordinary derivatives in their selected spectral variables are allowed. Section 7 extends this conclusion to fixed complex neighborhoods in both outside colors. The coefficient of the local contour in the whole source and all complementary low-sector currents remain unresolved. ## 7. The explicit local packet with two free outside colors Let \(u,v\) be the outside angles, so their ordinary colors are \(-2\cos u,-2\cos v\). Replace the two outside factors in (5) by the full original kernels \(K_N(t,u),K_N(r,v)\), and denote the resulting exact local density by \(I_N(z;u,v)\). Its scalar remains exactly (6). In particular neither an outside trace nor an additional level-dependent normalization has been inserted. The [free-boundary edge theorem](research_pair_free_boundary_kernel.md), Theorem 1, applies at both selected angles. Its hypotheses hold by (8), (29), and the strict inequality \(|\cos(t_*/2)|,|\cos(r_*/2)|<1\) from the wire-order theorem. It supplies the nonzero holomorphic amplitudes \(a_e\) in \[ K_N(t,u)=N^{-3/2}a_e(t,u)e^{N\psi(t,u)}(1+O(N^{-1})), \qquad Q_N=N^{-3}a_e(t_*,0)a_e(r_*,0)(1+O(N^{-1})). 	ag{32} \] The second equality uses (12) and the exponentially small full-to-low comparison (30). Both statements hold through all levels, with all fixed derivatives of their normalized errors. Define \[  egin{split} \Phi(z;u,v)&=b(x,t)+b(x,r)+\psi(t,u)+\psi(r,v) + rac{i(nt^2+pr^2)}{4\pi}-i(t+r),\ A(z;u,v)&= rac{\sin t\sin r}{4\sin^2(\pi x)} a_e(t,u)a_e(r,v). \end{split} 	ag{33} \] The invertible Hessian in (9) and the holomorphic implicit-function theorem give a unique local critical point \(z=z(u,v)\) with \(z(0,0)=z_*\). After shrinking a fixed bidisk about zero, put \[ \mathcal S(u,v)=\Phi(z(u,v);u,v),\qquad \mathcal H(u,v)=-\Phi_{zz}(z(u,v);u,v),\qquad \Re\mathcal H(u,v)>0. 	ag{34} \] All amplitudes below are nonzero on a sufficiently small bidisk. The matrix square root is the Gaussian branch in the convex space of complex symmetric matrices with positive real part. Choose a real, even cutoff \(\zeta\), equal to one near zero, with support sufficiently small for the uniform quadratic bound on \(z(u,v)+\operatorname{supp}\zeta\). Define the localized source by (23), using \(I_N(z(u,v)+w;u,v)\) in place of the complete-end density there. This is a holomorphic family: the integration variable \(w\in\mathbb R^3\) and its cutoff are fixed, and only the center of the contour moves holomorphically. **Theorem 3.** For every fixed integer pair \(n,p\ge3\), this localized part of the original source has the expansion \[  egin{split} \mathcal P_{n,p,N}^{m loc}(u,v) &=C_{N,n}C_{N,p}N^{-3/2}\mathcal A(u,v) e^{N\mathcal S(u,v)}(1+O(N^{-1})),\ \mathcal A(u,v) &=- rac{(2\pi)^{3/2}}{\pi^2}  rac{\sin t\sin r}{4\sin^2(\pi x)}  rac{a_e(t,u)a_e(r,v)}{\sqrt{\det\mathcal H(u,v)}}  igg|_{(x,t,r)=z(u,v)}
e0 . \end{split} 	ag{35} \] The remainder has a holomorphic expansion to every fixed inverse-power order, uniformly on smaller bidisks. The statement includes both level parities and every fixed ordinary derivative in the outside colors near \(-2,-2\). *Proof.* Equations (14), (32), and the exponentially small trace denominator errors give, with holomorphic relative remainders, \[ I_N(z;u,v)=N^{-5}A(z;u,v)e^{N\Phi(z;u,v)}(1+O(N^{-1})). 	ag{36} \] The two Newton-factorial representatives contribute \(N^{-2}\), and the two already normalized outside kernels contribute \(N^{-3}\). Thus the original scalar \(N^5\) in (6) cancels the amplitude power in (36). Integration in the three stationary variables contributes \(N^{-3/2}\). Taylor expansion at \(z(u,v)\), with the uniform strict real quadratic bound from (34), proves the Gaussian integral and its stated coefficient. The terms of order \(N^{-1/2}\) in the rescaled expansion are odd polynomials times the even Gaussian. Their integrals vanish because the cutoff is even. The remaining relative error is \(O(N^{-1})\); the fixed-cutoff tails are exponentially small. Repeating this argument with the higher factorial and edge expansions proves every fixed inverse-power order. The scalar and orientation are precisely those of (6), including its minus sign. Both edge kernels and their phases are even in their outside angle. Uniqueness of the local critical point therefore makes \(z(u,v)\), \(\mathcal S\), \(\mathcal A\), and the normalized local remainder separately even. They descend holomorphically through \(-2\cos u=-2+u^2+O(u^4)\) and the corresponding expression for \(v\). Cauchy's formula on smaller ordinary-color bidisks proves the assertions about normals. \(\square\) This sharper source estimate also removes the logarithmic loss in the local almost-invariance statement. Set \[ \widetilde G_N(\xi;u,v)= \zeta(\xi/\sqrt N)N^5e^{-N\mathcal S(u,v)} I_N(z(u,v)+\xi/\sqrt N;u,v). 	ag{37} \] Uniformly on a smaller bidisk, the proof of Theorem 1 now gives \[  egin{split} \|\widetilde G_N-A_*e^{-\xi^T\mathcal H\xi/2}\|_{L^1\cap L^2} +\|(
abla_\xi+\mathcal H\xi)\widetilde G_N\|_2 &=O(N^{-1/2}),\ \|\widetilde G_N\|_2 &=|A_*|\pi^{3/4}(\det\Re\mathcal H)^{-1/4} +O(N^{-1/2}),\ A_*&=A(z(u,v);u,v). \end{split} 	ag{38} \] Here the \(L^1\cap L^2\) norm denotes the sum of the two norms. Fixed polynomial weights in \(\xi\) are allowed as before. The variation of \(A\) is now \(O(|\xi|/\sqrt N)\), rather than the \(O((\log N)|\xi|/\sqrt N)\) variation used in (18). The oscillator estimate consequently bounds the squared non-Gaussian part by \(O(N^{-1})\), with a norm bounded below independently of the unknown full pair integral. Theorem 3 identifies an actual local coefficient and its exact power of \(N\). It does not state the coefficient of this local piece in the original global integration cycle. To obtain a full-source asymptotic one must still deform that cycle with its original residues and show that its remaining pieces have smaller exponential rate. The new free outside neighborhood and ordinary normals do not replace that global estimate.

title: Reflected middle currents and their original moving-wall residues
text:
# Reflected middle currents and their original moving-wall residues Research proof, updated 4 November 2026. Frozen manuscripts are unchanged. Reflecting both negative factorial arguments reorganizes the exact middle integrand into terms with fewer wire or trace poles. The reorganization is legitimate, but its pieces acquire moving poles when extended out of that chamber. Their residues are nonzero and recover the original value-support rows. Thus the pieces without a wire denominator cannot simply be discarded by a wire Cauchy argument. The later sections estimate the original integrand without discarding those terms. Sections 13–14 give coupled angular contours and the right vertical wire side for every fixed positive pair of powers at least seven. Together with the left contour and endpoint estimates, these supply the [full two-boundary source theorem](research_internal_pair_combined_contour_reduction.md#7-the-full-source-for-every-fixed-pair-of-powers-at-least-seven). ## 1. Exact denominator cancellation, with the common scalar Put \[  egin{gathered} q_x=e^{-2\pi iNx},\quad q_t=e^{-iNt},\quad q_r=e^{-iNr}, \qquad D_t=1-\eta q_t,\quad D_r=1-\eta q_r,\ w_t= rac12-x- rac{t}{2\pi},\qquad w_r= rac12-x- rac{r}{2\pi},\qquad \eta=(-1)^{N-1}. \end{gathered} 	ag{1} \] The exact reciprocal reflection is \[  rac1{G_N(Nw_t-1/2)} =E_N(x,t)(1-\eta q_xq_t),\qquad E_N(x,t)= rac{e^{-i\pi Nw_t}}N G_N(-Nw_t-1/2). 	ag{2} \] It is a meromorphic identity; its product is regular wherever the original reciprocal factorial is regular. For the original interpolation define \[ C_N(x,t)=  rac{G_N(-Nw_t-1/2)} {G_N(N(1/2-x+t/(2\pi))-1/2)G_N(Nx)^2}. 	ag{3} \] Then \(B_N(x,t)=C_N(x,t)e^{-i\pi Nw_t} (1-\eta q_xq_t)\), and likewise for \(r\). Using the literal one-cell wire kernel \(1/(1-e^{2\pi iNx})=-q_x/(1-q_x)\), one obtains \[  egin{split} & rac{B_N(x,t)B_N(x,r)} {1-e^{2\pi iNx}}  rac{q_tq_r}{D_t^2D_r^2}\ &\quad=\eta C_N(x,t)C_N(x,r)e^{-iN(t+r)/2} \left\{  rac{1-q_x}{D_t^2D_r^2} + rac{q_x}{D_tD_r^2} + rac{q_x}{D_t^2D_r} + rac{q_x^2}{(1-q_x)D_tD_r} ight\}. \end{split} 	ag{4} \] Indeed \(1-\eta q_xq_t=(1-q_x)+q_xD_t\). The common reflection exponential contributes \((-1)^Nq_x^{-1}e^{iN(t+r)/2}\); together with the original wire and trace kernels this gives exactly the scalar and half-charge exponential in (4). The sine factors and original crossing Gaussians multiply both sides unchanged. In the chamber \(\Re w_t,\Re w_r<0\), the reflected numerator factorials in (3) have positive scaled real part. Formula (4) is consequently a useful exact grouping there. Extending an individual term across a chamber wall requires the residues described next. ## 2. The artificial poles recover actual value-support rows Write \(S_j=\prod_{\ell=1}^j2\sin(\pi\ell/N)\), \(S_0=1\). The canonical shift relation and \(G_N(0)=1\) give, for \(1\le k\le N\), \[ \operatorname*{Res}_{z=-k}G_N(z) = rac{(-1)^{k-1}N}{2\pi S_{k-1}} . 	ag{5} \] For \(k=1\), use \(G_N(z)=G_N(z+1)/(2\sin(\pi(z+1)/N))\). The remaining cases follow by the next \(k-1\) shifts; their nonzero sine product is \((-1)^{k-1}S_{k-1}\). For fixed \(x\), the factor \(E_N(x,t)\) in (2) therefore has simple poles at \[ t_k(x)=\pi-2\pi x- rac{(2k-1)\pi}{N}, \qquad w_t= rac{k-1/2}{N}, \qquad \operatorname*{Res}_{t=t_k(x)}E_N(x,t) =- rac{i}{N S_{k-1}} . 	ag{6} \] The sign includes \(d(-Nw_t-1/2)/dt=N/(2\pi)\) and \(e^{-i\pi(k-1/2)}=i(-1)^k\). At the same point, \[ 1-\eta q_xq_t=0,\qquad \partial_t(1-\eta q_xq_t)=iN . 	ag{7} \] Thus the product in (2) has the regular value \[ \lim_{t	o t_k(x)} E_N(x,t)(1-\eta q_xq_t)= rac1{S_{k-1}}, 	ag{8} \] exactly \(1/G_N(k-1)\). The moving poles are artifacts of splitting the reflection multiplier; the unsplit original factor has no pole there. At a genuine low wire sample \(x=j/N\), a moving pole in the nonnegative physical half-period has \[ t_k(j/N)=	au_a,\qquad j\le a=j+k-1\le\lfloor(N-1)/2floor . 	ag{9} \] These are precisely the original value-support rows among the distinct physical roots, not the below-triangle normal-only rows \(a<j\). Negative angles are paired by evenness and exchange the two shifted factorials; no assertion that the residue of the isolated factor \(E_N\) survives all the other factors on every duplicated grid row is needed. For example, when \(0\le j\le a\le\lfloor(N-1)/2floor\), the remaining factors in (2) and (8) recover \[ e_j(c_a) = rac{N}{S_{N-1-a-j}S_{a-j}S_j^2} = rac{S_{a+j}}{S_{a-j}S_j^2}>0 . 	ag{10} \] This is also the direct original Newton product. At \(j=0\) it equals the exact cap value one. The meromorphic identity (2) holds on a neighborhood of each canceled pole, so it retains its full ordinary jets, not just this value. Consequently the first three terms of (4), although lacking the original wire denominator, can have nonzero moving-wall residues through \(C_N(x,t)C_N(x,r)\). At a wall, \(D_t=1-q_x^{-1}\), and the two summands of \((1-q_x)+q_xD_t\) cancel; the complete expression cancels the artificial residues exactly. At intersections or at physical wire samples this cancellation must be performed together with the original trace poles. This gives a precise restriction on a prospective middle-band deformation. One may keep the reflected pieces inside their chamber, or extend them while retaining these wall currents. There is no justification for treating all such currents as deleted-edge errors: (9)--(10) identify their direct connection to the original value sector. The identity makes no global gap or nonzero closing-coefficient claim. There is an exact independent description of the support in (9). The ordinary value interpolant of a crossing times \(e_j\) factors as \(e_j\) times the crossing interpolant on the remaining distinct nodes \(a\ge j\). Its Cauchy denominator is therefore \(\prod_{a\ge j}(z-c_a)\); see the [source-exact normal-defect regrouping](research_trace_normal_defect_positive_form.md). These are the same nodes as (9). This identifies the common support, not an equality between an individual term of (4) and the whole normal-defect observation: their trace poles must still be recombined. ## 3. A favorable height direction in the upper reflected chamber The exact reflected expression also has a useful monotonicity direction. It concerns the original complete-end phase, including the crossing and unit-charge terms: \[ \mathcal F_n(x,t) =b(x,t)+\psi(t,0)+ rac{int^2}{4\pi}-it,\qquad \psi_t(t,0)=- rac1\pi\operatorname{arsinh}	an(t/2). 	ag{11} \] The branch is continued from the original positive factorial strip. In particular, when \(w_t\) has negative real part and positive imaginary part, \(J(w_t)\) is continued through the upper half-plane. It is not replaced by a fresh principal logarithm of a final product. **Proposition 1.** Suppose \[  egin{gathered} x=\xi+iY,\qquad 0<\xi< rac14,\qquad Y>0,\qquad n\ge3,\ t=	au-iH,\qquad \pi-2\pi\xi\le	au<\pi,\qquad H>2\pi Y. \end{gathered} 	ag{12} \] Then \[  rac{\partial}{\partial H}\Re\mathcal F_n(x,	au-iH) >  rac{(2n-1)	au}{4\pi}+ rac{\xi}{2}- rac34 \ \ge\  rac{n-3}{4}+(n-1)\left( rac14-\xiight)>0 . 	ag{13} \] The integrated inequality extends to \(H=2\pi Y\) by the one-sided continuous upper exponent, including the limiting factorial zero. Thus lowering the trace height within this chamber strictly decreases its upper phase. *Proof.* The logarithmic derivative inherited from the strip is \[ b_t(x,t)= rac1{2\pi} \{\Log\cos(\pi x+t/2)-\Log\cos(\pi x-t/2)\}. 	ag{14} \] For the numerator, the real part of its cosine argument belongs to \([\pi/2,\pi)\), and its imaginary part is \(\pi Y-H/2<0\). Its value is in the closed upper left quadrant, with argument \(
u\ge\pi/2\). For the denominator, the cosine argument has real part \(\pi\xi-	au/2\in(-\pi/2,0)\) and positive imaginary part. Its value is in the first quadrant. Its argument \(\delta\) satisfies \[ 0<\delta =\arctan\{	an(	au/2-\pi\xi)	anh(\pi Y+H/2)\} <	au/2-\pi\xi . 	ag{15} \] In this chamber \(0<
u-\delta<\pi\). These arguments agree with the continued sine-factor logarithms in (14): the negative shifted argument has been crossed above zero, and the other shifted argument stays in \(0<\Re w<1\). There is no logarithmic winding to add. Consequently \[ \Im b_t> rac14- rac{	au}{4\pi} + rac{\xi}{2}. 	ag{16} \] For \(0<	au<\pi\) and \(H>0\), \(	an(t/2)\) has positive real part and negative imaginary part. Its selected \(\operatorname{arsinh}\) likewise has positive real part and imaginary part in \((-\pi/2,0)\). Hence \(\Im\psi_t(t,0)>0\). Since \(\partial_H\Re\mathcal F_n=\Im(\mathcal F_n)_t\), the other two derivatives contribute \(n	au/(2\pi)-1\). Adding this to (16) proves the first bound in (13). Substituting the lower bound for \(	au\) proves the second. The primitives have continuous real limits as \(H\) decreases to \(2\pi Y\); at a zero this follows from the local \(w\log w\) behavior. Integrating (13) first on a closed subinterval of \(H>2\pi Y\), then taking the lower endpoint limit, proves the stated one-sided extension. \(\square\) For example, if \(\xi\le eta<1/4\) and \(H_2>H_1\ge2\pi Y\), the phase drop is at least \[ \Re\mathcal F_n(x,	au-iH_2) -\Re\mathcal F_n(x,	au-iH_1) \ge \left\{ rac{n-3}{4}+(n-1)(1/4- eta)ight\}(H_2-H_1). 	ag{17} \] It applies separately to either trace variable in the joint pair phase, without altering the other crossing. For its use as a finite-source upper estimate, keep the contour in a compact subset of (12) on which the actual complete-end low kernel is covered by \(\Re(-2\cos t)<2\). The [absolute physical-row theorem](research_last_physical_row_riccati.md) then supplies its upper phase \(\Re\psi(t,0)\), with only polynomial losses. The reciprocal-factorial upper bound retains both terms of (2), including their zeros at the one-sided boundary. The trace denominator is uniformly bounded after its original \(e^{-NH}\) penalty is extracted. Thus (17) is a comparison of the actual available upper exponents. It is not a ratio bound between finite densities: the lower-height density can vanish at a reciprocal-factorial zero. Full outside radicals are still handled after the original trace by the established source decomposition. Proposition 1 does not cover \(H<2\pi Y\), \(\xi\ge1/4\), or the passage between a reflected and a regular trace factor. Nor does it license discarding the wall residues in Section 2. It therefore supplies a favorable part of an adapted contour, not the missing whole middle-band bound. ## 4. Height descent without ordering the wire and trace heights The same argument gives a useful direction on the lower wire without any height-order condition. On the upper wire, a power of at least seven also removes that condition. These statements concern the original continuous factorial upper exponent; no separated reflection term or moving-wall residue is discarded. For \(\sigma\in\{+1,-1\}\), write \[  egin{split} x_\sigma&=\xi+\sigma iY,\qquad t=	au-iH,\ E_{n,\sigma}(\xi,	au,H;Y) &=\mathfrak b(x_\sigma,t)+\Re\Psi(t) + rac{n	au H}{2\pi}-H, \qquad \Psi(t)=\psi(t,0). \end{split} 	ag{18} \] Here \(\mathfrak b\) is the continuous upper exponent of the actual reciprocal factorials, including both reflection terms. Then \(0<A_-\le A_+\), and \((q+A_-)/(q+A_+)\) increases with \(q\). Consequently \[  egin{split} k_\xi^-&\ge rac12\log  rac{\sinh((L-h)/2)}{\sinh((L+h)/2)}\ &=- rac12\int_{(L-h)/2}^{(L+h)/2}\coth v\,dv \ge- rac h2\coth(L/4). \end{split} 	ag{79} \] The last inequality uses \((L-h)/2\ge L/4\) and the decrease of \(\coth v\) for \(v>0\). For \(	au\ge\pi/2\) and \(h\le1/7\), the same explicit bound used in Proposition 14 gives \(k_0\ge\operatorname{asinh}\sqrt{\operatorname{sech}h} >3/5\). Equations (76), (78), and (79) therefore imply \[ \partial_	au E_{n,-} < rac{h\{n+\coth(L/4)\}/2-3/5}{\pi} \le- rac1{10\pi}. 	ag{80} \] Integrating from the wall carries its gap along the entire positive reflected segment in (77). The other trace and the lower-wire penalty are unchanged. Decrease \(h\) further, if needed, so that the compact rectangle \(|\Re t|\le T\), \(0\le-\Im t\le h\) lies in \(\Re(-2\cos t)<2\), and so that \(h<\Psi(T)/2\). This is possible because \(T<\pi\) and \(\Psi(T)>0\). The actual low complete-kernel logarithmic theorem applies there. Imaginary convexity yields \(\Re\Psi(t)\ge\Psi(T)>2h\), so the full outside radical is exponentially smaller. This proves the required full-kernel normalization on the reflected segment. Along the wall connector and the other regular trace, use the previously proved full pair rectangle, together with its evenness and Schwarz reflection. The trace and wire heights have fixed positive lower bounds. Their exact denominators therefore have bounded residual factors after their original exponential weights are extracted. The uniform reciprocal-factorial upper estimate retains all reflection terms and zeros. Continuity of its real exponent permits a fixed tube about (77), with less than half the strict gap spent on enlarging the domain. Holomorphic Cauchy estimates on smaller tubes retain every stated ordinary normal. Finally Proposition 15 supplies the negative-angle pieces at the same heights, with an additional phase loss of at least \(h/2\). This proves the assertion. \(\square\) As in Proposition 14, fixed physical midpoint adjustments at the angular ends are \(O(N^{-1})\) and stay in the proved tubes.
