If \(T\) is chosen close enough to \(\pi\), decrease \(h\) also to meet the allowance in the grouped angular-connector theorem. The final folded endpoint current then obeys (65), paired with the **whole** other trace before taking absolute values. That grouping includes its physical first normals. Proposition 17 controls a connected lower-wire piece for every positive pair; it does not bound every complementary joint region or projected-source current, and it does not by itself prove a nonzero global pair coefficient. ## 13. A coupled angular contour on the right wire interval The preceding connected pieces can be replaced, on the right wire interval and for powers at least seven, by one contour covering all retained trace angles. Its two heights change together. This avoids introducing independent mixed-height rectangles, whose corners have not been bounded. Fix integers \(n,p\ge7\), and write \(H_1=H_n\), \(H_2=H_p\). The [proved large-power geometry](research_real_pair_geometry_and_tail_gap.md#7-a-global-comparison-for-real-trace-angles) gives \[ H_i<3/10,\qquad L=2\pi Y<2/15,\qquad M_{n,p}>163/50. 	ag{81} \] Use the original density \(\mathcal I_N\) and its complete upper exponent \(\mathcal E\) from (4) and (20) of the [right-horizontal bulk note](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_internal_pair_right_horizontal_bulk.md). In particular \(\mathcal E\) includes the lower-wire penalty, the unit trace charges, and both full complete-end kernels. **Lemma 18 (simultaneous height convexity).** Put \(T_\xi=\pi-2\pi\xi\), where \(1/4\le\xi\le2/5\). For either wire \(x=\xi+\sigma iY\), \(\sigma=\pm1\), and every \(|	au|,|ho|\le T_\xi\), the function \[ q(\lambda)= \mathcal E igl(x,	au-i\lambda H_1, ho-i\lambda H_2 igr) \quad(0\le\lambda\le1) 	ag{82} \] is convex. If at least one of \(|	au|,|ho|\) equals \(T_\xi\), it has a uniform strict gap below \(M_{n,p}\), over all these parameters. *Proof.* For one trace write \(t=	au-ih\) and \(a=\pi\xi\). Away from a factorial zero, direct differentiation gives \[  rac{\partial^2}{\partial h^2} \left\{\mathfrak b(x,t)+\Re\Psi(t) + rac{n	au h}{2\pi}-hight\} = rac{\Re	an(\pi x+t/2)+\Re	an(\pi x-t/2) +2\Re\sec(t/2)}{4\pi}. 	ag{83} \] The real parts of the two tangent arguments belong to \([0,\pi/2]\), because \(|	au|\le\pi-2a\) and \(a\ge\pi/4\). The formula \(\Re	an(u+iv)=\sin(2u)/(\cos(2u)+\cosh(2v))\) shows that both terms are nonnegative wherever defined. Also \(\Re\sec(t/2)>0\) for \(|	au|\le\pi/2\). Thus (83) is positive between any singular heights, for either sign of the wire. At a wall a shifted factorial can vanish when \(h=L\). The local term in its real primitive is \(-\Re(z\Log z)\), up to a continuously differentiable function, with \(z=\pm i(h-L)/(2\pi)\). Its contribution is \(|h-L|/4\). The height derivative therefore has an upward jump of \(1/2\), which preserves convexity. This is the continuous original upper primitive; no logarithmic lift is changed at the crossing. Combining the two one-trace functions proves the convexity of (82). The wire penalty is independent of \(\lambda\). At \(\lambda=1\), the closed-wall theorem supplies a uniform gap \(\delta_{m wall}>0\) for both wires and both trace signs. At \(\lambda=0\), at least one real angle is reflected, so the [global real-angle mixed bound](research_real_pair_geometry_and_tail_gap.md#7-a-global-comparison-for-real-trace-angles) gives \(q(0)<M_{n,p}-1/600\). Convexity implies \[ q(\lambda)\le (1-\lambda)q(0)+\lambda q(1) \le M_{n,p}-\min\{1/600,\delta_{m wall}\}. 	ag{84} \] Only the phase is evaluated at zero trace height. No finite trace-density bound at its real poles is asserted. \(\square\) **Theorem 19 (the full right angular surface).** Fix \(\pi/2<T<\pi\). Let \(T_N=T+O(N^{-1})\) be the original physical midpoint cut, so \(e^{iNT_N}=-\eta\). There exist \(\lambda_0>0\), \(\epsilon>0\), and \(\delta>0\), depending on the fixed pair and the cut, with the following property. For every \(x=\xi+\sigma iY\), \(1/4\le\xi\le2/5\), the joint lower-trace horizontal integral has an exact representation on the smooth surface \[ t=	au-i\lambda(	au,ho)H_1,\qquad r=ho-i\lambda(	au,ho)H_2,\qquad -T_N\le	au,ho\le T_N, 	ag{85} \] where \(\lambda_0\le\lambda\le1\). The scale equals one when both \(|	au|,|ho|\le T_\xi-\epsilon\), and equals \(\lambda_0\) whenever one of \(|	au|,|ho|\ge T_\xi+\epsilon\). On this entire surface the original density, including its pulled-back two-form Jacobian, is at most \[ C N^A e^{N(M_{n,p}-\delta)}. 	ag{86} \] The integral equals the original product of the two horizontal integrals at the constant small heights \(\lambda_0H_1,\lambda_0H_2\). Both parities and all original physical first normals are retained. Every fixed selected ordinary-color derivative has the same upper exponent. Here the differentiated colors are the traced colors \(t,r\); the two outside colors remain complete. *Proof.* The compact wall family in Lemma 18 has a strict phase gap, uniformly in \(\lambda\in[0,1]\). By continuity of the real factorial upper primitive, including its zeros, that gap persists on a fixed small angular neighborhood of the family. Choose \(\epsilon>0\) small enough for this neighborhood and so that \(T_\xi+\epsilon<T\) and \(T_\xi+\epsilon<2\pi/3\) throughout the wire interval. Independently, the global mixed bound at zero trace height has gap \(1/600\) on the compact set where at least one of the two real angles is beyond its wall and both angles have absolute value at most \(T+o(1)<\pi\). Uniform continuity, followed by the finite-source conclusion of that bound, permits a fixed small \(\lambda_0>0\) at which this whole set has a strict gap. Shrink \(\lambda_0\) as necessary for the full outside kernels, as detailed below. Choose a smooth even cutoff \(\chi_\xi(s)\in[0,1]\) equal to one for \(|s|\le T_\xi-\epsilon\), and zero for \(|s|\ge T_\xi+\epsilon\), with uniformly bounded derivatives on this fixed compact interval of \(\xi\). Take \(0<\chi_\xi(s)<1\) between those two cut locations. Set \[ \lambda(	au,ho) =\lambda_0+(1-\lambda_0)\chi_\xi(	au)\chi_\xi(ho). 	ag{87} \] If \(\lambda=1\), both angles are in the regular region at their original geometric heights, and the right-horizontal bulk theorem gives the gap. If \(\lambda=\lambda_0\), at least one angle is beyond \(T_\xi+\epsilon\); the small-height mixed bound applies. If \(\lambda_0<\lambda<1\), both angles have absolute value at most \(T_\xi+\epsilon\), and one is within \(\epsilon\) of its wall. The point lies in the fixed neighborhood of the wall family controlled by (84). These three cases give a uniform phase gap on (85). For clarity, these are bounds on the full finite density. The central and transition pieces have \(|\Re t|,|\Re r|<2\pi/3\) and heights at most \(3/10\), so Lemma 12 supplies the full complete-kernel normalization. On the outer small-height piece, choose \(\lambda_0\) so that the entire rectangle of real angles up to \(T+o(1)\) stays in \(\Re(-2\cos t)<2\) and \(\Re\Psi(t)>|\Im t|\), and similarly for \(r\). The actual low complete kernels have their proved phase there, and the full outside radicals are exponentially smaller. All selected trace heights are bounded below by the fixed positive numbers \(\lambda_0H_i\). The original trace denominators and the wire denominator consequently have their stated exponential weights with bounded residual factors. The uniform reciprocal-factorial upper bound keeps all its reflected terms and zeros. Smaller complex neighborhoods and Cauchy estimates give the stated normals. It remains to justify the source equality. Start with the product horizontal rectangle at the constant heights \(\lambda_0H_1,\lambda_0H_2\), and use the homotopy \[ \lambda_s=\lambda_0+s\{\lambda(	au,ho)-\lambda_0\}, \qquad 0\le s\le1. 	ag{88} \] All its trace heights are strictly positive. The exact two-form \(\mathcal I_N(x,t,r)\,dt\wedge dr\), with \(x\) fixed, is holomorphic throughout this homotopy. Its physical trace poles lie on the real angles; the reciprocal-factorial continuation introduces zeros rather than omitted poles. Since \(\lambda=\lambda_0\) on the entire outer boundary, the homotopy fixes that boundary pointwise. Stokes' theorem therefore gives equality of the two horizontal integrals, without discarding any wall, side, or first-normal residue. The pulled-back Jacobian is exactly \[  rac{dt\wedge dr}{d	au\wedge dho} =1-i\{H_1\partial_	au\lambda +H_2\partial_ho\lambda\}, 	ag{89} \] which has a uniform fixed bound. It preserves the phase estimate, proving (86). Midpoint changes of size \(O(N^{-1})\) stay in the same compact neighborhoods. \(\square\) Choose \(T\) sufficiently close to \(\pi\) and decrease \(\lambda_0\) also to satisfy the allowances of the [whole-other-trace connector theorem](research_internal_pair_grouped_angular_connectors.md#4-group-with-the-whole-other-trace-before-taking-absolute-values). The surface (85) is unchanged from the constant-height product on its outer boundary. Thus the original folded endpoint currents and omitted physical-angle terms have precisely their old grouping, including their intersections. Their established gap, together with (86), controls the original right-wire horizontal contribution for \(1/4\le\xi\le2/5\). This conclusion uses the exact paired source, not a rowwise approximation to a projected normal defect. It does not estimate the remaining wire interval or the wire-side currents needed to close a global contour. ## 14. The right vertical wire side The vertical side at the retained-index cut \(2/5\) admits the same coupled contour construction. Here the wire height and the two central trace heights first vary together. A second common scaling lowers the trace heights near the angular boundary. Small positive endpoint heights remove the singular zero-height limit from the actual finite source. Put \( eta=2/5\) and \(T_*=\pi/5\). For \(\sigma=\pm1\), \(0\le	heta\le1\), define the ideal central family \[ x_	heta= eta+\sigma i	heta Y,\qquad t_	heta=	au-i	heta H_1,\qquad r_	heta=ho-i	heta H_2,\qquad |	au|,|ho|\le T_* . 	ag{90} \] **Lemma 20.** The complete upper phase on (90) has a uniform strict gap below \(M_{n,p}\). The same is true on its angular boundary when the two trace heights are multiplied by any common \(\lambda\in[0,1]\), with the wire kept at \(x_	heta\). *Proof.* Write \(s_i=1/2-t_i/(2\pi)=b_i+iS_i\), where \( eta\le b_i\le1- eta\). In the strict regular interior, set \[ u_i=\Re\cot\pi(s_i+x),\quad v_i=\Re\cot\pi(s_i-x),\quad w=\Re\cot\pi x,\quad d_i=\Re\csc\pi s_i . 	ag{91} \] For every choice of the imaginary parts in (90), \[ u_i\le0,\quad v_i\ge0,\quad w,d_i>0 . 	ag{92} \] Indeed the real parts of \(s_i+x\) belong to \([4/5,1]\), those of \(s_i-x\) to \([0,1/5]\), and those of \(s_i\) to \([2/5,3/5]\). These sign statements are independent of the signs or order of the imaginary heights. The negative real Hessian contributed by \(b(x,t_i)+\Psi(t_i)\), in the coordinates \((\Re x,b_i)\), is exactly \[ \pi v_i  egin{pmatrix}1&-1\-1&1\end{pmatrix} -\pi u_i  egin{pmatrix}1&1\1&1\end{pmatrix} +2\pi\operatorname{diag}(w,d_i). 	ag{93} \] It is positive definite by (92). Add the two contributions on the shared wire coordinate. Holomorphy changes the sign of this Hessian when all imaginary coordinates vary on a line, so the real phase in (90) is convex in \(	heta\). The original crossing terms, unit charges and lower-wire penalty are affine in \(	heta\), and do not affect this convexity. For angles on a factorial wall, take the continuous limit from the strict regular interior. This also covers a vanishing shifted argument along part of the ideal family. At \(	heta=1\), the right-horizontal bulk theorem gives the gap for both wire signs and all displayed trace signs. At \(	heta=0\), real-angle monotonicity and the [real right-cut estimate](research_real_pair_geometry_and_tail_gap.md#8-two-useful-endpoint-cuts) give \[ \mathcal E( eta,	au,ho) \le 2V_0(2/5)+2M_\infty < rac{97}{30}<M_{n,p}- rac2{75}. 	ag{94} \] Convexity between these two endpoints proves the first assertion, uniformly on the compact central family. On its angular boundary, one trace has real part \(\pm T_*=\pm(\pi-2\pi eta)\). At the fixed wire \(x_	heta\), Lemma 18's one-trace calculation proves convexity when both trace heights are scaled by \(\lambda\). It applies to every wire height in \([-Y,Y]\), including zero, by continuity. The \(\lambda=1\) endpoint is already bounded by the first assertion. At \(\lambda=0\), the global mixed real-angle bound has gap \(1/600\). Their convex interpolation proves the second assertion. \(\square\) **Theorem 21 (the original right-side current).** Let \( eta_N= eta+O(N^{-1})\) be a physical half-grid cut, so \(N eta_N\in\mathbb Z+1/2\). The original vertical wire contribution on \[ x= eta_N+iy,\qquad -Y\le y\le Y, 	ag{95} \] has upper bound \(CN^A e^{N(M_{n,p}-\delta)}\) for some fixed \(\delta>0\). This includes the full paired trace, its folded endpoint currents and its omitted physical-angle terms, with the original first normals at both parities. The two outside colors are complete. *Proof.* Choose a fixed \(T<\pi\), sufficiently close to \(\pi\) for the whole-other-trace connector theorem. By Lemma 20 and uniform continuity, its central and angular-boundary gaps persist on fixed neighborhoods. The global mixed real-angle estimate controls the complement of the square \(|	au|,|ho|\le T_*\) at sufficiently small positive trace heights. Choose a smooth even cutoff \(\chi\) equal to one on \([-T_*+\epsilon,T_*-\epsilon]\), zero outside \((-T_*-\epsilon,T_*+\epsilon)\), and strictly between zero and one in the two transition intervals. Put \(\lambda(	au,ho)=\chi(	au)\chi(ho)\). Choose fixed small numbers \(0<\varepsilon_i<H_i\). For \(y=\sigma	heta Y\), use the actual trace heights \[ h_i(	heta,	au,ho) =\varepsilon_i+ \lambda(	au,ho)	heta(H_i-\varepsilon_i). 	ag{96} \] Their difference from the ideal heights \(\lambda	heta H_i\) is at most \(\varepsilon_i\). Thus all sufficiently small fixed choices of \(\varepsilon_i\) retain the compact phase gaps just proved. In the central region \(\lambda=1\) use (90); in the transition use the boundary part of Lemma 20; where \(\lambda=0\) use the small-height mixed bound. This covers all retained real trace angles \(-T_N\le	au,ho\le T_N\), with \(T_N=T+O(N^{-1})\) the original midpoint cut. The \(O(N^{-1})\) displacement from \( eta\) to \( eta_N\) also lies in these fixed neighborhoods. The complete kernels on the central and transition parts lie in the proved full pair rectangle, or a slightly larger neighborhood from Lemma 12. On the outer part choose \(\varepsilon_i\) small enough that their low-kernel normalization dominates the outside radical, exactly as in Theorem 19. All actual trace heights are at least the positive \(\varepsilon_i\). On (95), the literal wire factor has the exact bound \[ \left| rac1{1-e^{2\pi iNx}}ight| = rac1{1+e^{-2\pi Ny}} \le e^{-2\pi N(-y)_+}. 	ag{97} \] It therefore has the required upper exponent even at \(y=0\). The uniform factorial estimates and the full outside kernels now give the actual density bound on the whole surface. For every fixed \(x\), deform the constant product trace heights \((\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2)\) to (96). The outer angular boundary remains fixed, all heights stay positive, and the exact holomorphic two-form has no crossed physical poles. The fixed-boundary Stokes argument of Theorem 19 gives equality of the integrals. Its Jacobian has a fixed bound. Dependence of this contour on the wire position introduces no additional current: this is a pointwise exact trace identity before the wire integration; equivalently, the extra \(dx\) terms disappear in \(dx\wedge dt\wedge dr\). The resulting central double-horizontal contribution has the claimed gap. Finally take the \(\varepsilon_i\) within the allowances of the grouped angular-connector theorem. On the outer angular boundary they are constant. The exact grouping with the whole other trace therefore applies without change, retaining the endpoint-current intersections and all omitted physical residues. Its bound (65) has a strict gap for every \(|y|\le Y\). Adding these terms and integrating over the fixed length of (95) proves the assertion. \(\square\) One may take \(\varepsilon_i=\lambda_0H_i\), using the same small scale as in Theorem 19. At \(y=\pm Y\), the vertical-side surface then joins that theorem's right horizontal surface. This matching is convenient; the pointwise exact trace identities already justify either choice. The result closes this right wire side, without replacing the unresolved central wire integral by an absolute estimate.

title: The full singleton clock phase and its algebraic stationary equations
text: # The full singleton clock phase and its algebraic stationary equations Written proof, 14 November 2026. This note gives the complete quadratic phase of the original charged source when every crossing is retained as one event. It includes all understrand histories, all closure degrees, and the original scalar normalization. The clock variables can then be eliminated exactly by the finite binomial theorem, or rationally from the regular classical stationary equations. Its reduced primitive agrees exactly with the physical crossing action on a specified analytic branch. The exact phase derivatives have a local polar-angle interpretation with explicit history terms. The result is an explicit refinement of the existing integer feedback operator, not a positivity or selected-period theorem. In particular, the exact clock elimination returns the original physical crossing network, with its phase. No knot-complement face pairing is assumed. ## 1. Direct sources and conventions The proof uses these written sources at the following versions: * [Whole charged source](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_global_charged_bridge_flow.md), SHA-256 b444e487eab3ec0a56c40b22584837cefcbe374a137b0beeaa185116c2a81d8c: original source (1), closure (2), event polynomial (4)--(6), undertransport (7)--(8), alias-free coefficient (12), and grouped phases (17)--(19). * [Signed overbridge proof](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_signed_overbridge_unwinding.md), SHA-256 0a875f4feb3a1eecb8dbb77a5a7ec170ef95884746f5babd8b54659bc2e0078a: the four signed ports, complete normalizers (4a), and simultaneous contraction in Section 4. * [Exact clock feedback](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_clock_feedback_normal_form.md), SHA-256 f58a4dfd06615ecace95959e58474837f7eb50ef7f01a3c00d517d3938cb06bf: causal histories (1)--(5), exact Gaussian (9)--(11), and the earlier implicit stationary equations (15)--(16). * [Rivin frames and bridge angles](research_rivin_role_frames_and_bridge_angles.md), SHA-256 125155bcd008e24bf5714457d9c6d1788a152bc563380f859c80bfe8b997ccf8: the complete halfedge weight (12)--(14), simplex volume (15), and its positive cyclic-bipyramid chamber. * [Marked braid holonomy](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/marked_braid_holonomy.md), SHA-256 eff47c757d0e44bda0c396c094315b8e1fce11f1fc2d6445d636c6d2d3a46c4f: the actual physical canonical relation, its matrix factorization, and its cut marking in Sections 4--6. * [Crossing fundamental cycle](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/crossing_fundamental_cycle.md), SHA-256 0d7d7da0f5cf4fe0d16907e7e999d5ce7980f7ff39d437df167c99ca30205b0f: the already proved complete rational Bloch normalization, whose scope is distinguished from a primitive or quantum-period identity. No numerical audit or saved numerical result is used. Set \[ d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\quad x=-q^{-1}=q^d,\qquad S_a=\prod_{r=1}^a2\sin(\pi r/N),\quad S_0=1. \tag{1} \] Thus \(S_aS_{d-a}=N\). The signs \(\sigma_j\in\{1,-1\}\) below are the balanced **physical** crossing signs of the charged source. The external rivin-jones adapter reverses them; no external sign is silently substituted here. Write \(c\) for the number of crossings, \(b\) for the number of braid heads, \(w=\sum_j\sigma_j\), and retain the source's \(\kappa=q^{d^2/2}\) and exterior scalar \(\chi_N\). The whole original scalar is \[ K_N=\frac{\chi_N}{N} \operatorname{Tr}\bigl[(I\otimes g^{\otimes(b-1)})W\bigr], \qquad g_a=\eta Q^{-a},\quad \eta=x/x^N=q^{-d^2}. \tag{2} \] As proved in the charged-source note, the original marked-cut replacement in (2) is made only after assembling the complete integer-degree-preserving word. It is not made separately in the new clock sectors. ## 2. Singleton events and the actual flow domain Keep every crossing as a singleton over-event, and keep the \(b\) original closure events. This follows from the overbridge proof by selecting no over-over internal edges for contraction. Its rank-one crossing identities and regular propagated frames still apply. There are \(c+b\) directed anchor segments between successive events. Each segment contains only under encounters, possibly none. In particular, two consecutive over crossings do not acquire a new monotonicity condition between their independent clocks. At crossing \(j\), its two block lengths are \(d-h_j,h_j\). Expand the blocks and write their four halfedge charges in cyclic order as \[ (n_{j0},n_{j1},n_{j2},n_{j3}) =(d-u_j-v_j,\ u_j-h_j+v_j,\ h_j-v_j,\ v_j). \tag{3} \] Here \(u_j=n_{j1}+n_{j2}\), \(v_j=n_{j3}\), and \(h_j=n_{j2}+n_{j3}\). The row constraint is \(\sum_an_{ja}=d\). The first incidence meets the over-input anchor, the middle two meet the under-output anchor, and the last meets the over-output anchor. Consequently the anchor contributions depend on \(u_j,v_j\) but not on the split \(h_j\). At closure \(i\), let \(a_i\) be its transmitted degree. Its row has incidences \((d-a_i,a_i)\), attached to the closure input and output anchors. Let \(a_s\) denote the degree at the start of an anchor segment \(s\): it is \(v_j\) if the starting event is crossing \(j\), and \(a_i\) if it is closure \(i\). Let \(b_s\) be the degree at its end: it is \(u_j+v_j\) at a crossing input, and \(a_i\) at a closure input. The exact anchor equations are \[ a_s+\sum_{j\ {\rm under\ on}\ s}u_j=b_s \qquad\hbox{for every segment }s. \tag{4} \] They are equivalent to charge \(d\) at each anchor in the original coefficient. They include the zero-under segments. If \(j\) is an under encounter on \(s\), put \[ J_j=a_s+\sum_{\ell\ {\rm before}\ j\ {\rm on}\ s}u_\ell . \tag{5} \] This is an integer linear function of the physical flow variables, independent of all clocks. Equation (4), nonnegativity, and the event degree bounds imply \[ 0\le J_j,\quad J_j+u_j\le d,\qquad u_j,v_j\ge0,\quad u_j+v_j\le d. \tag{6} \] Conversely these are exactly conserved physical color paths: crossing \(j\) has over-input \(I_j=u_j+v_j\), over-output \(v_j\), under-input \(J_j\), under-output \(J_j+u_j\), and transfer \(u_j\). Following each segment proves this correspondence in both directions, including the actual closing degrees. For each such physical flow, the clock domain is the independent product \[ v_j\le h_j\le u_j+v_j. \tag{7} \] It is precisely the nonnegativity condition in (3). Equivalently, the full domain is the nonnegative integral transportation fiber having charge \(d\) at every event row and every anchor column. The two middle incidences of a singleton are distinct parallel incidences; combining them before recording their charges loses the clock coordinate. ## 3. The full phase, including every downstream history The singleton crossing factor is \(\Gamma_j=\kappa^{\sigma_j}(-1)^{h_j} q^{\sigma_jh_j(h_j+1)}\). Let the propagated over-input, under-output, and over-output port factors be \(q^p,q^s,q^r\), respectively. The two grouped block phases from the charged-source theorem are \[ w_0=q^{\sigma h+s-p},\qquad w_1=q^{-\sigma h+r-s}. \tag{8} \] After including both block prefactors and the event denominator at the input, the complete row coefficient is \[ \kappa^\sigma\,\frac{N}{S_{n_0}S_{n_1}S_{n_2}S_{n_3}}\, q^{\,Nh+\sigma h(u+1)+(s-p)u+(r-p)v}. \tag{9} \] For verification before collecting phases, its port contribution is \(p n_0+s(n_1+n_2)+r n_3-dp\), its block contribution is \(\sigma h(n_1-n_3)\), and its crossing contribution is \(Nh+\sigma h(h+1)\). Since \(h+n_1-n_3=u\), these give (9). The magnitude is \(S_{d-h}S_h/\prod_aS_{n_a}=N/\prod_aS_{n_a}\). An under encounter \(\ell\) changes the port exponent by \[ \delta_\ell=d\sigma_\ell-2\sigma_\ell h_\ell. \tag{10} \] Consider one whole anchor segment, in its actual physical order. The increment \(\delta_\ell\) contributes to the under-output port of \(\ell\), to all later under-output ports, and to the final event input. Its total coefficient in the port exponent is \[ \sum_{j\ {\rm at\ or\ after}\ \ell}u_j-b_s =-a_s-\sum_{j\ {\rm before}\ \ell}u_j=-J_\ell . \tag{11} \] The segment's initial port exponent has coefficient \(a_s+\sum_ju_j-b_s=0\). This proves, without discarding any prefix or closing adapter, that all the propagated port phases sum to \(-\sum_j\delta_jJ_j\). Closure \(i=1\) contributes no extra phase. Each \(i>1\) contributes its original \(\eta q^{-2a_i}\). Therefore define \[ \boxed{\displaystyle \Phi_N=\sum_{j=1}^c \bigl\{[N+\sigma_j(u_j+1+2J_j)]h_j-\sigma_jdJ_j\bigr\} -2\sum_{i=2}^ba_i .} \tag{12} \] This is the full variable-dependent phase. Let \(\mathcal T_N\) be the incidence fiber in Section 2, including its closure rows. The exact original-source identity is \[ \boxed{\displaystyle K_N=\frac{\chi_N}{N}\kappa^w\eta^{\,b-1}N^{c+b} \sum_{n\in\mathcal T_N} \frac{q^{\Phi_N(n)}}{\prod_eS_{n_e}} .} \tag{13} \] The product includes every crossing and closure incidence. Indeed each crossing gives (9), and \(1=N/(S_{a_i}S_{d-a_i})\) inserts each closure magnitude exactly. Equation (13) is the alias-free coefficient identity of the direct source, expanded with all its factors. Its normalization has not been inferred from a nonzero unknown scalar. There is a useful completely integral quadratic description. View \(h_j,u_j,J_j,a_i\) as the integer linear functionals in (3), (5), and the closure rows. Then \[ \Phi_N(n)=\frac12 n^{\mathsf T}\mathsf Hn +N A(n)+B(n), \tag{14} \] where \[ \begin{split} \mathsf H&=\sum_j\sigma_j [h_j\otimes(u_j+2J_j)+(u_j+2J_j)\otimes h_j],\\ A&=\sum_j(h_j-\sigma_jJ_j),\\ B&=\sum_j\sigma_j(h_j+J_j)-2\sum_{i=2}^ba_i . \end{split} \tag{15} \] The tensor notation denotes the matrix of products of covectors. Its diagonal is even. Thus (14) is an integer polynomial, with a matrix and two covectors fixed by the signed diagram and cut. This explicitly evaluates the feedback coupling from the older normal form; it does not replace it by its zero-feedback fiber. ## 4. Exact lattice differences and coherent clock elimination For any two admissible incidence states differing by an integral vector \(\ell\) in the row-and-anchor constraint kernel, \[ \frac{w_N(n+\ell)}{w_N(n)} =q^{\,(\mathsf Hn+NA+B)\cdot\ell+ \frac12\ell^{\mathsf T}\mathsf H\ell} \prod_e\frac{S_{n_e}}{S_{n_e+\ell_e}}, \qquad w_N(n)=\frac{q^{\Phi_N(n)}}{\prod_eS_{n_e}} . \tag{16} \] All factorials here are nonzero. Written in physical variables, the phase increment is explicitly \[ \begin{split} \Delta\Phi_N=\sum_j\{& [N+\sigma_j(u_j+1+2J_j)]\Delta h_j\\ &+\sigma_jh_j(\Delta u_j+2\Delta J_j) -\sigma_jd\Delta J_j\\ &+\sigma_j\Delta h_j(\Delta u_j+2\Delta J_j)\} -2\sum_{i=2}^b\Delta a_i . \end{split} \tag{17} \] This keeps the exact finite pivot contribution and all histories. No boundaryless recurrence for a restricted interior sum is inferred from (16). In particular, fixing the physical flow and increasing \(h_j\) by one gives the exact ratio \[ \frac{w_N(h_j+1)}{w_N(h_j)} =q^{C_j}\, \frac{\sin(\pi(u_j-h_j+v_j)/N)} {\sin(\pi(h_j-v_j+1)/N)},\qquad C_j=N+\sigma_j(u_j+1+2J_j). \tag{18} \] All clocks are independent at this fixed flow. The finite positive-sine binomial identity gives their full sums: \[ \sum_{h=v}^{u+v} \frac{q^{Ch}}{S_{h-v}S_{u-h+v}} =\frac{q^{Cv}}{S_u}(-q^{C+1-u};Q)_u =\frac{q^{Cv}}{S_u} \begin{cases} (Q^{J+1};Q)_u,&\sigma=1,\\ (Q^{-J-u};Q)_u,&\sigma=-1 . \end{cases} \tag{19} \] For completeness, the identity being used is \[ \sum_{r=0}^u\frac{S_u}{S_rS_{u-r}}t^r =\prod_{k=0}^{u-1}(1+q^{2k-u+1}t). \] It follows from the finite \(Q\)-binomial theorem, and is valid also at even or composite \(N\), since \(u\le d\). Both products in (19) are nonzero on (6), and have magnitude \(S_{J+u}/S_J\). Including the other two factorials, their complete row magnitude is \[ \frac{N}{S_{d-u-v}S_v}\frac{S_{J+u}}{S_JS_u} =\frac{S_{u+v}S_{J+u}}{S_vS_JS_u}. \tag{20} \] Their phases also agree with the literal physical matrix. For \(\sigma=1\), the signed-overbridge source gives its coefficient as \[ \kappa x^{-J-v}Q^{vJ} \frac{F_{J+u}F_{u+v}}{F_uF_JF_v}, \qquad F_a=(-i)^a q^{a(a+1)/2}S_a . \tag{21} \] The exponent from (19), including \(q^{-dJ}\), is \[ Cv-dJ-Nu/2+Ju+u(u+1)/2. \] The exponent from (21), apart from \(\kappa\), is \[ -d(J+v)+2vJ-Nu/2+u(J+v)+u(u+1)/2. \] Their difference is \(2Nv\), hence their \(q\)-powers coincide. For \(\sigma=-1\), the product in (19) has phase \(Nu/2-Ju-u(u+1)/2\), and \(C=N-u-1-2J\); its full exponent is the negative of the positive exponent modulo \(2N\). This is exactly the source's antiunitary flip in physical over/under order. Thus (19) reconstructs the original signed crossings with the same closure and source. This is a coherent elimination for every fixed braid, not a positive sector: the remaining physical flow sum has precisely the original crossing phases. Nonzero individual products in (19) are not a lower bound on that remaining sum. ## 5. Complete regular stationary equations Write the scaled physical variables as \(H_j=h_j/N\), \(U_j=u_j/N\), \(V_j=v_j/N\), \(A_i=a_i/N\), and again write \(J_j\) for the limiting scaled linear function (5). In this section \(x_e=n_e/N\) denotes a limiting incidence coordinate, so its event and anchor sums are one. For crossings, \[ (x_{j0},x_{j1},x_{j2},x_{j3}) =(1-U_j-V_j,\ U_j-H_j+V_j,\ H_j-V_j,\ V_j). \tag{22} \] On the real interior, the elementary sine-factorial integral gives the variable-dependent leading action \[ \mathcal S(x)=-\sum_e\mathcal J(x_e)+i\pi\phi(x), \quad \mathcal J(t)=\int_0^t\log(2\sin\pi s)\,ds,\qquad \phi=\frac12x^{\mathsf T}\mathsf Hx+A(x). \tag{23} \] The sum of the two closure terms is zero: \(\mathcal J(t)+\mathcal J(1-t)=0\). The variable-dependent closure phase in (12) is order one in the exponent, not order \(N\); it remains in (13), (16), and (17), although it does not enter \(\phi\). The factors \(\chi_N,\kappa^w,\eta^{b-1}\) are independent of the state variables and remain outside this action. On a complex regular chart choose logarithms of \(2\sin\pi x_e\) consistently and use their primitives to define (23). These are algebraic stationary equations for that action; no continuation of the original cycle or saddle dominance is being asserted. For an integral tangent vector \(\ell\), exponentiating the stationary equation gives \[ \boxed{\displaystyle \prod_e(2\sin\pi x_e)^{\ell_e} =(-1)^{A(\ell)} \prod_e t_e^{(\mathsf H\ell)_e}, \qquad t_e=e^{\pi i x_e}.} \tag{24} \] This follows by differentiating (23): \(-\sum_e\ell_e\log(2\sin\pi x_e) +i\pi(A+\mathsf Hx)\cdot\ell=0\), modulo the chosen integer Fourier branch. Since \(2\sin\pi x_e=(t_e-t_e^{-1})/i\), (24) is a finite Laurent algebraic system after clearing denominators. Event and anchor constraints give \(\prod_{e\ {\rm incident}}t_e=-1\); their additive lifts must also be retained. Exponentiation alone forgets logarithmic branches and does not prove that every algebraic solution is a critical point on the prescribed chart. There is a more explicit version showing every downstream term. For a segment \(s\), and for an under encounter \(j\) on it, put \[ D_s=\sum_{\ell\ {\rm under\ on}\ s}\sigma_\ell(2H_\ell-1), \qquad B_j=\sigma_jH_j+ \sum_{\ell\ {\rm after}\ j\ {\rm on}\ s(j)} \sigma_\ell(2H_\ell-1). \tag{25} \] Let \(s_{\rm in}(j),s_{\rm out}(j),s(j)\) be its over-input, over-output, and under anchor segments. Let \(Z_s\ne0\) be exponentials of the multipliers for (4), using the convention \(d\mathcal S=\sum_s\log Z_s\,d(a_s+\sum u-b_s)\). Then the stationary equations are \[ \begin{split} \frac{\sin\pi x_{j1}}{\sin\pi x_{j2}}\, e^{i\pi[1+\sigma_j(U_j+2J_j)]}&=1,\\ \frac{\sin\pi x_{j0}}{\sin\pi x_{j1}}\,e^{i\pi B_j} &=Z_{s(j)}/Z_{s_{\rm in}(j)},\\ \frac{\sin\pi x_{j0}\sin\pi x_{j2}} {\sin\pi x_{j1}\sin\pi x_{j3}}\,e^{i\pi D_{s_{\rm out}(j)}} &=Z_{s_{\rm out}(j)}/Z_{s_{\rm in}(j)},\\ e^{i\pi D_{s_{\rm out}(i)}}&= Z_{s_{\rm out}(i)}/Z_{s_{\rm in}(i)} \qquad\hbox{at closure }i . \end{split} \tag{26} \] All equations have their chosen logarithmic lifts. To verify the history terms, vary (12) at fixed clocks and use (5): each variation of a segment's initial degree enters every \(J_\ell\) on it, and \(\Delta u_j\) enters exactly the later \(J_\ell\). Thus the limiting phase derivatives are \(\partial_{U_j}\phi=B_j\), \(\partial_{V_j}\phi=D_{s_{\rm out}(j)}\), and \(\partial_{A_i}\phi=D_{s_{\rm out}(i)}\). Differentiating the four factorial primitives in (22) gives the sine ratios in (26). The first equation is the independent clock direction. This proves (26), including its last, closing equation. The clock equation admits a useful rational elimination. Set \[ R_j=H_j-V_j,\quad Z=e^{2\pi iU_j},\quad T=e^{2\pi iJ_j},\quad Y=e^{2\pi iR_j}. \] It is equivalent to \[ \frac{\sin\pi R_j}{\sin\pi(U_j-R_j)} =-e^{i\pi\sigma_j(U_j+2J_j)}. \] Using \(\sin\pi R/\sin\pi(U-R)=e^{\pi iU}(Y-1)/(Z-Y)\) gives, on the regular divisor complement, \[ \boxed{\displaystyle Y=\frac{1-ZT}{1-T}\quad(\sigma_j=1),\qquad Y=\frac{Z(1-T)}{1-ZT}\quad(\sigma_j=-1).} \tag{27} \] Thus every singleton clock can be eliminated algebraically before solving the remaining physical-flow equations. If \(1-T\), \(1-ZT\), or an original sine denominator vanishes, the undivided equations (24)--(26) must be used instead. Equation (27) neither deletes these boundary strata from the original finite sum nor establishes a nonzero saddle coefficient. ### The clock elimination recovers the physical differential There is a stronger relation than coincidence of one clock equation. For a single crossing write \[ \begin{split} L_\sigma(U,V,J,H) &=-\sum_{a=0}^3\mathcal J(x_a) +i\pi[H+\sigma H(U+2J)-\sigma J],\\ G_\sigma(U,V,J) &=\mathcal J(U+V)+\mathcal J(J+U) -\mathcal J(V)-\mathcal J(J)-\mathcal J(U) +i\pi\sigma\psi(U,V,J),\\ \psi&=-J-V+2VJ-U/2+U(J+V)+U^2/2 . \end{split} \tag{27a} \] Here \(x_a\) are (22). Formula (21) and its inverse show directly that \(G_\sigma\) is the leading action of the literal balanced physical crossing, apart from its retained state-independent \(\kappa^\sigma\). On the regular clock graph (27), \[ \boxed{\quad e^{\partial_U L_\sigma}=e^{\partial_U G_\sigma},\qquad e^{\partial_V L_\sigma}=e^{\partial_V G_\sigma},\qquad e^{\partial_J L_\sigma}=e^{\partial_J G_\sigma}. \quad} \tag{27b} \] The derivatives of \(L\) on the left are taken holding \(H\) fixed before restriction. Thus they are also the derivatives of its stationary reduction, after choosing the clock's logarithmic Fourier branch. Here is a direct verification that retains constants in the sine factors. Put \(s(t)=2\sin\pi t\) and \(R=H-V\). Equation (27) implies \[ e^{2\pi iR}= \begin{cases} e^{\pi iU}s(J+U)/s(J),&\sigma=1,\\ e^{\pi iU}s(J)/s(J+U),&\sigma=-1 . \end{cases} \tag{27c} \] The \(V\) identity follows from \[ e^{\partial_VL} =\frac{s(U+V)}{s(V)}\frac{s(R)}{s(U-R)} =\frac{s(U+V)}{s(V)} e^{i\pi\sigma(-1+2J+U)}. \] For \(J\), (27c) gives \[ e^{i\pi\sigma(2H-1)} =\frac{s(J+U)}{s(J)} e^{i\pi\sigma(-1+2V+U)}. \] For \(U\), the required identity is \[ \frac{e^{i\pi\sigma R}}{s(U-R)} =\frac{s(J+U)}{s(U)} e^{i\pi\sigma(-1/2+J+U)}. \tag{27d} \] To check it without a logarithmic convention, put \(z=e^{\pi iU}\), \(Z=z^2\), \(T=e^{2\pi iJ}\), and \(Y=e^{2\pi iR}\). Its left side is \(izY/(Z-Y)\) for the positive sign and \(iz/(Z-Y)\) for the negative sign. Substitution of the two rational values in (27) gives (27d). Multiplying by \(s(U+V)e^{i\pi\sigma V}\) proves the \(U\) identity in (27b). These three computations prove the lemma. The clock equation, after clearing its unit denominators, is linear in the full color variable \(Y\), with unit coefficient \(1-T\) or \(1-ZT\). In these color variables its localized scheme is therefore the graph of (27), including over nonreduced test rings. Any half-color cover in (24) and any chosen logarithmic lift are retained. Equations (27b) show that its remaining localized exponentiated stationary scheme is the physical one. The statement persists under arbitrary diagram composition because the physical variables \(I=U+V,J,k=U\) have the same conservation equations (4), and the same actual closure is retained. After choosing those same covers and lifts, the independent clock variables introduce no additional component on this regular chart. Equation (27b) alone concerns differentials with their lifts. On a connected logarithmic chart they agree modulo an integral \(2\pi i\) linear differential; after compatible lifts are chosen their primitives differ by a constant. The following calibration fixes that constant on a specified canonical chart without inferring it merely from derivatives. ### Exact primitive calibration on the physical strip Let \[ \mathcal D=\{(U,V,J)\in\mathbb R^3: U,V,J>0,\ U+V<1,\ U+J<1\}. \] This domain is connected. On the strip \(0<\operatorname{Re}z<1\), the real part of \(\sin\pi z\) is positive. Thus \(\log(2\sin\pi z)\) has its unambiguous principal analytic branch there. Choose its primitive \(\mathcal J\) agreeing with the real integral (23) on \((0,1)\). It obeys \(\mathcal J(1-z)=-\mathcal J(z)\) and conjugation symmetry. Define on \(\mathcal D\) \[ R_\sigma=\frac U2-\frac{\sigma i}{2\pi} \log\frac{s(J+U)}{s(J)},\qquad H_\sigma=V+R_\sigma,\qquad s(t)=2\sin\pi t. \tag{27e} \] The logarithm in (27e) is real. All four incidence arguments in \(L_\sigma\) lie in that strip, and (27c) shows that this is the actual regular clock graph. On this branch the clock derivative is exactly \[ \partial_H L_\sigma=\pi i(1+\sigma). \tag{27f} \] Indeed its exponential is one by the clock equation, so it is a continuous integer multiple of \(2\pi i\). At \(J=(1-U)/2\) the sine ratio in (27e) is one, \(R=U/2\), and the derivative is \(\pi i(1+\sigma)\). Connectedness proves (27f) throughout \(\mathcal D\). Define the stationary primitive with this precise Fourier character removed: \[ \mathscr L_\sigma(U,V,J)= L_\sigma(U,V,J,H_\sigma)-\pi i(1+\sigma)H_\sigma. \] Then \[ \boxed{\mathscr L_\sigma=G_\sigma \quad\hbox{on }\mathcal D.} \tag{27g} \] To prove the value, reflection and elementary collection of the quadratic phases give \[ \begin{split} \mathscr L_\sigma-G_\sigma ={}&-\mathcal J(U-R)-\mathcal J(R) -\mathcal J(J+U)+\mathcal J(J)+\mathcal J(U)\\ &+i\pi\sigma(R-U/2)(U+2J-1). \end{split} \tag{27h} \] This expression is real on \(\mathcal D\): \(U-R=\overline R\), the primitive respects conjugation, and \(R-U/2\) is purely imaginary. By (27f), differentiation of the stationary primitive gives precisely the fixed-\(H\) derivatives used in (27b). Consequently every real partial derivative of (27h) lies in \(2\pi i\mathbb Z\). It is also real, hence is zero. The difference is constant. Letting \(U\) decrease to zero at fixed \(J,V\) gives \(R\to0\), and the continuous endpoint value \(\mathcal J(0)=0\) makes (27h) tend to zero. This proves (27g), including its additive constant and both signs. The equality holds in a complex neighborhood with these branches, and continues along any common analytic path on which those same lifts are transported. A different unrecorded Fourier or logarithmic lift must not be substituted. Equation (27g) does not identify the original finite sum's contour with a clock saddle's descending cycle, or prove its coefficient nonzero. The eliminated clock also has an explicit nonzero Hessian: \[ \partial_H^2L_\sigma =-\pi\{\cot\pi(U-R)+\cot\pi R\} =-\frac{\pi\sin\pi U} {\sin\pi(U-R)\sin\pi R}. \tag{27i} \] The equality is the sine addition identity. On the regular chart used for the physical action all three sine factors are nonzero, so (27i) cannot vanish. On \(\mathcal D\), \(U-R=\overline R\) and \(0<U<1\); hence (27i) is strictly negative real. For an arbitrary fixed diagram, take independent coordinates \(z\) on its physical-flow constraints (4), keeping every clock \(H_j\) independent before elimination. The total corrected action is \[ \mathscr F(z,H)=\sum_j [L_{\sigma_j}(U_j(z),V_j(z),J_j(z),H_j) -\pi i(1+\sigma_j)H_j], \] with any retained physical boundary action added unchanged. At fixed \(z\) the clock Hessian \(D=\mathscr F_{HH}\) is diagonal, with entries (27i). On the regular clock graph, differentiating \(\mathscr F_H(z,H(z))=0\) gives \(H_z=-D^{-1}\mathscr F_{Hz}\). Thus the exact reduced primitive identity implies \[ {\rm Hess}_zG_{\rm physical} =\mathscr F_{zz} -\mathscr F_{zH}D^{-1}\mathscr F_{Hz}. \tag{27j} \] The physical action on the left includes that same boundary action. At a critical point the block determinant identity therefore gives \[ \det{\rm Hess}_{(z,H)}\mathscr F =\det D\ \det{\rm Hess}_zG_{\rm physical}. \tag{27k} \] If a framing or other gauge gives zero directions, first choose a specified local gauge slice and use its physical coordinates \(z\); the same argument applies. Without such a slice, the Schur identity still gives equality of the physical and full Hessian nullities because \(D\) is invertible. Clock elimination introduces no additional local Hessian degeneracy. This identifies a nonzero determinant factor; it does not show that the original contour has nonzero intersection with the saddle. The physical critical correspondence is already identified with meridian holonomy by Sections 4--6 of the marked braid source. There is a boundary convention to retain when using that certificate: our whole source (2) has periodic physical momentum at the first head, whereas the marked cut fixes its constant-vector momentum to one. On a connected regular knot chart, two physical momentum lifts of the same position data differ by one common nonzero scalar. Indeed the local generating relations fix all four momentum ratios at each crossing; shared wires propagate their common scalar through the connected diagram. Simultaneous rescaling of all momenta preserves the canonical relation by total-degree conservation. A periodic lift can therefore be normalized to have first-cut momentum one at both ends. This is the marked representative, not a replacement inferred merely from equality of scalars. Accordingly the existing marked holonomy certificate applies to this regular stationary correspondence with its stated momentum marking. Its separate crossing fundamental-cycle certificate fixes the physical complete Bloch--Wigner regulator. The canonical comparison (27g) fixes the local primitive constant on its stated branch. These classical identities still do not transport a relative contour or prove a nonzero coefficient of the geometric component. ## 6. Exact polar terms and the remaining geometric identification For a singleton use the exact finite sum-one angular coordinates \[ \bar x_{ja}=(n_{ja}+1/4)/N,\qquad \theta_{ja}=\pi(1-\bar x_{j,a-1}-\bar x_{ja}), \tag{28} \] with cyclic subscripts. On the positive cyclic-bipyramid chamber these are the polar-edge dihedral angles from the local geometry in the direct source. In particular \[ \theta_{j0}=\pi(u_j+1/2)/N,\quad \theta_{j1}=\pi(h_j+1/2)/N,\quad \theta_{j2}=\pi-\theta_{j0},\quad \theta_{j3}=\pi-\theta_{j1}. \tag{29} \] Treat (12) as its explicit polynomial in \(h,u,v,a\), with the prefix definition (5). Its exact derivatives are \[ \begin{split} \frac{\pi}{N}\partial_{h_j}\Phi_N &=\pi+\sigma_j\theta_{j0} +2\pi\sigma_jJ_j/N+\sigma_j\pi/(2N),\\ \frac{\pi}{N}\partial_{u_j}\Phi_N &=\sigma_j\theta_{j1}-\sigma_j\pi/(2N) +\sum_{\ell\ {\rm after}\ j\ {\rm on}\ s(j)} \sigma_\ell(\theta_{\ell1}-\theta_{\ell3}),\\ \frac{\pi}{N}\partial_{v_j}\Phi_N &=\sum_{\ell\ {\rm under\ on}\ s_{\rm out}(j)} \sigma_\ell(\theta_{\ell1}-\theta_{\ell3}),\\ \frac{\pi}{N}\partial_{a_i}\Phi_N &=\sum_{\ell\ {\rm under\ on}\ s_{\rm out}(i)} \sigma_\ell(\theta_{\ell1}-\theta_{\ell3}) -\frac{2\pi}{N}\mathbf1_{i>1}. \end{split} \tag{30} \] Indeed \((\pi/N)(2h_\ell-d)= \theta_{\ell1}-\theta_{\ell3}\) exactly. These formulas also distinguish ordinary polynomial derivatives from finite lattice differences: the latter have the additional quadratic term displayed in (16)--(17). Equation (30) identifies the local polar contributions and every history and pivot term. Keeping only an isolated \(\sigma h u\) term would omit the signed downstream sums and the \(2\sigma J\) term in the clock equation. Keeping only fixed-clock connection holonomies would omit that clock equation altogether. The differential comparison (27b) transports the regular critical correspondence to the established physical holonomy chart. It does not assert that these particular positive cyclic bipyramids themselves form the desired complement. Such a direct angle-cell identification would require face pairings respecting the cyclic order, signs and closure, matching their polar-edge classes to the signed combinations in (30). The old crossing fundamental cycle supplies a different, already proved classical certificate; it should not be confused with this unproved positive-cell identification. Neither certificate proves the original cycle's nonzero geometric intersection or a uniform complementary estimate. What is established here is more explicit than a phase existence statement: (12)--(15) specify the original diagram's integer quadratic phase, (16)--(19) retain its exact finite differences and coherent clock sums, (24)--(27) give its algebraic stationary system and rational clock elimination, (27b) identifies its physical differential, (27g) fixes its canonical reduced primitive, and (30) gives the precise polar and history terms.

title: Joint factorial lenses for the original finite source
text: # Joint factorial lenses for the original finite source Private written proof, 15 November 2026. The restored Newton network has an exact joint integral in its wire indices and angular variables. This note places that integral on lower angular lenses in a common holomorphic factorial domain. It also gives an explicit relative primitive for the difference between the factorial and finite-band polynomial representatives. Thus compact joint deformations with the specified coordinate faces fixed preserve the full original source. No edge kernel is replaced by a single asymptotic branch. The result does not establish the geometric coefficient or an exponential bound on the remainder of such a joint contour. ## 1. Original source and the common domain Fix \(N\ge2\), \(D=N-1\), \(\eta=(-1)^D\), and \[ P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2,\qquad \phi_N(f)=\eta N^2[z^D]\operatorname{rem}_{P_N}f . \tag{1} \] Use the original Newton polynomials \(e_j\), physical crossing \(R\), and kernels \[ K_T(z,w)=\sum_{j=0}^D e_j(z)e_j(w),\qquad K_I(z,w)=\sum_{j=0}^D e_j(z)e_{D-j}(w). \tag{2} \] Take any finite network compiled from these operations as in the pinned source compiler. Let \(V\) be its traced vertices and \(E\) its paired wire indices. Loops and repeated edges are permitted. Every wire index occurs in precisely two halfwire factors. Each halfwire uses either \(x_e\) or \(D/N-x_e\), according to its original direct or reversed index. Free spectral variables are ordinary polynomial variables and are not reduced. At a traced vertex \(v\), allow any fixed signed power \(R^{n_v}\) and the canonical full-Hermite coupon \(\mathcal C_{N,\chi_v}\) of the pinned lens theorem. Here \(\chi_v\) may be complex; its value at \(z=-2\cos t\) is represented by \(\cos(N(1-\chi_v)t)\), with its prescribed first normals. The original source is recovered when every \(\chi_v=1\). Any additional specified polynomial spectators are retained. Write \[ \begin{split} B_N(x,t)&=\frac{N}{ G_N(D/2-Nx+Nt/(2\pi))G_N(D/2-Nx-Nt/(2\pi))G_N(Nx)^2},\\ \widetilde B_N(x,z)&=\sum_{j=0}^D \frac{\sin(\pi N(x-j/N))}{N\sin(\pi(x-j/N))}\,e_j(z). \end{split} \tag{3} \] The removable values in the second line are used. Its frequencies in \(x\) are \(-D/2,-D/2+1,\ldots,D/2\). The full Hermite class of \(B_N(x,t)\), with \(z=-2\cos t\), equals that of \(\widetilde B_N(x,z)\). At \(x=j/N\), both equal \(e_j(z)\) as an ordinary polynomial identity. Put \[ a_N=\pi-\frac{\pi}{2N},\qquad I_N=[-1/(2N),\,1-1/(2N)] . \tag{4} \] Use \(\Re x_e\in I_N\) and \(|\Re t_v|\le a_N\). The compiler's direct divisor check applies simultaneously to both halfwire orientations: the two shifted factorial arguments in (3) have real parts in \[ [-N+1/4,\,N-1/4],\qquad \Re(Nx_e)\in[-1/2,N-1/2]. \tag{5} \] Consequently all factorial halfwires are holomorphic on a neighborhood of any compact subset of this product strip, at arbitrary fixed finite imaginary heights. The reflection \(x\mapsto D/N-x\) preserves \(I_N\). At a free spectral endpoint use \(\widetilde B_N(x,z)\), not \(B_N(x,t)\). This distinction preserves the entire boundary polynomial. At traced endpoints either representative is allowed. ## 2. A full-grid lens inside the factorial domain Set \[ W_N(t)=\frac{e^{-iNt}}{(1-\eta e^{-iNt})^2},\qquad C_{N,n}=q^{nD^2/4},\qquad q=e^{\pi i/N}. \tag{6} \] The physical grid is \(\tau_j=\pi-(2j+1)\pi/N\), \(0\le j\le D\). All these points lie strictly between \(-a_N\) and \(a_N\); neither endpoint is a pole of \(W_N\). Let \(A(t)\) be even and holomorphic on a vertical strip containing \([-a_N,a_N]\), and let \([A]\) denote its full spectral Hermite class. This class exists because an even function near \(t=0\) is holomorphic in \(z=-2\cos t\) there; elsewhere the physical angular-to-spectral map is unramified. If \(\Gamma\) runs from \(-a_N\) to \(a_N\), with interior in the lower half-plane and inside that strip, then \[ \boxed{\quad \phi_N(R^n\mathcal C_{N,\chi}[A]) =-\frac{N^2C_{N,n}}{\pi i} \int_\Gamma \sin t\,e^{inNt^2/(4\pi)} \cos(N(1-\chi)t)A(t)W_N(t)\,dt . \quad} \tag{7} \] Indeed the numerator other than \(W_N\) is odd, and \(W_N\) is even. Adjoin the reflected upper arc \(-\Gamma\) to form the positively oriented lens around the entire physical grid. The exact derivative-sampling residue calculation of the lens theorem gives (7), with the two reflected integrals equal. Only evenness and holomorphy of \(A\), and its physical values and first normals, are used. It need not be a polynomial. The odd-level simple spectral node at \(t=0\) has precisely its original contribution; no extra normal is imposed. Unlike the endpoints \(\pm\pi\), the present endpoints need not annihilate the sine factor. Short endpoint connectors are therefore generally \(O_N(\varepsilon)\), which still tends to zero at fixed \(N\). There is no endpoint residue or half-weight. No uniform large-\(N\) connector estimate is asserted. ## 3. The exact joint integral Fix horizontal wire intervals \(I_N+i h_e\) and lower angular arcs \(\Gamma_v:-a_N\to a_N\) as above. Let \(d=|E|+|V|\), and order the complex coordinates once and for all. Let \(F_{\rm car}\) be the product of all halfwire factors, using \(\widetilde B_N(x,-2\cos t)\) at traced endpoints and the same polynomial representative at every free endpoint. Retain the specified polynomial spectators in this product. Let \(F_{\rm fac}\) replace the traced halfwires by (3), with their actual direct or reversed arguments; the free endpoints remain polynomial. Both functions are even in every angular coordinate. Define the two top forms, with the same chosen coordinate order, by \[ \Omega_\bullet= F_\bullet(\mathbf x,\mathbf t;\mathbf u) \prod_{v\in V} \left\{\sin t_v\,W_N(t_v) e^{in_vNt_v^2/(4\pi)} \cos(N(1-\chi_v)t_v)\right\} \,d\mathbf x\,d\mathbf t , \qquad \bullet\in\{{\rm car},{\rm fac}\}. \tag{8} \] Here \(\mathbf u\) denotes all unreduced free spectral variables. For the product chain \(\mathcal L=\prod_e(I_N+i h_e)\times\prod_v\Gamma_v\), the exact compiled source is \[ \boxed{\quad Z_N(\mathbf u)= N^{|E|}\prod_{v\in V} \left(-\frac{N^2C_{N,n_v}}{\pi i}\right) \int_{\mathcal L}\Omega_{\rm fac} = N^{|E|}\prod_{v\in V} \left(-\frac{N^2C_{N,n_v}}{\pi i}\right) \int_{\mathcal L}\Omega_{\rm car}. \quad} \tag{9} \] For the cardinal representative, each paired index has integer frequencies in \([-D,D]\), so its original \(N\)-point sum is exactly \(N\) times the period integral. Apply (7) at every traced vertex. This proves the second expression in (9). The factorial expression follows either by equality of every full Hermite trace, or by the explicit relative identity below. All integrations are over compact chains, and all free-variable coefficients remain unchanged. Thus (9) also holds after any finite number of free-boundary derivatives. ## 4. The relative primitive of the representative correction The exact identity \[ \boxed{\quad P_N(-2\cos t)\,W_N(t)=(-1)^N \quad} \tag{10} \] follows by expanding \[ P_N(-2\cos t) =(-1)^N e^{iNt}(1-\eta e^{-iNt})^2 . \tag{11} \] It retains both parities and every repeated root. Telescope the replacement \(F_{\rm car}\to F_{\rm fac}\) one traced vertex at a time. The difference at vertex \(v\) is divisible by \(P_N(-2\cos t_v)\), so \[ F_{\rm fac}-F_{\rm car} =\sum_{v\in V}P_N(-2\cos t_v)A_v(\mathbf x,\mathbf t;\mathbf u), \tag{12} \] where each \(A_v\) is jointly holomorphic in the common product strip and even in every angular variable. To verify holomorphic division, at a paired angular root the full-Hermite identity gives value and first angular derivative zero, matching the double zero of \(P_N(-2\cos t)\). When \(N\) is odd, its simple spectral root \(-2\) pulls back to a double angular zero at \(t=0\); evenness and value equality give that same order. There are no further zeros of \(P_N\) inside the angular strip. The quotient consequently has no pole there, including at \(N=2\). After multiplying the \(v\)-th summand of (12) by the factors in (8), use (10). The resulting top-form coefficient is holomorphic in \(t_v\), odd in \(t_v\), and may retain only the original \(W_N(t_w)\) poles in the other variables. Write that coefficient as \(H_v\). Define its primitive by \[ Q_v(\mathbf x,\mathbf t;\mathbf u) =\int_{-a_N}^{t_v} H_v(\mathbf x,t_1,\ldots,\tau,\ldots;\mathbf u)\,d\tau . \tag{13} \] The integration in the \(v\)-th strip is path independent: its coefficient is holomorphic there, including at the physical nodes. It is holomorphic in all remaining variables off their original angular poles. Oddness gives \[ Q_v|_{t_v=-a_N}=Q_v|_{t_v=a_N}=0 . \tag{14} \] If \(t_v\) is coordinate number \(j(v)\), let \(\Theta_v=(-1)^{j(v)-1}Q_v\) times the ordered wedge of all coordinate differentials except \(dt_v\). Then \[ \boxed{\qquad \Omega_{\rm fac}-\Omega_{\rm car}=d\Theta,\qquad \Theta=\sum_v\Theta_v . \qquad} \tag{15} \] Every derivative of \(Q_v\) in another coordinate wedges with the already present differential and vanishes. This proves (15) directly, without an asymptotic argument. The pullback of \(\Theta\) vanishes on every prescribed coordinate face. On \(t_v=\pm a_N\), its own summand vanishes by (14); every other summand contains \(dt_v\). On a wire face \(x_e=-1/(2N)+ih_e\) or \(1-1/(2N)+ih_e\), every summand contains \(dx_e\). This is the precise relative boundary condition used here. ## 5. Joint deformation and its limits **Theorem.** Let \(\mathcal L'\) be obtained from \(\mathcal L\) by a compact piecewise smooth joint homotopy in the common product domain, avoiding the physical angular poles. Require throughout the homotopy that each angular endpoint face keeps its coordinate \(t_v=\pm a_N\), and each wire seam face keeps its original coordinate \(x_e=-1/(2N)+ih_e\) or \(1-1/(2N)+ih_e\). Other coordinates may vary on these faces. Then (9) holds with \(\mathcal L'\) in place of \(\mathcal L\), for either representative, and the two representatives give the same integral on \(\mathcal L'\). **Proof.** The forms (8) are closed holomorphic top forms away from their angular poles. On every side face of the homotopy the fixed coordinate has zero differential, so the corresponding top-form integral is zero. Stokes' theorem proves invariance. Equation (15) and the relative boundary condition prove equality of the two representatives on the deformed chain. All statements are coefficientwise in the free polynomial variables. \(\square\) This is a joint statement: angular and wire directions may move together in the interior. It does not assert that the factorial integrand is pointwise periodic. In fact its exact period defect is \[ B_N(x+1,t)-\eta B_N(x,t) =\frac{(-1)^N P_N(-2\cos t)} {4\sin^2(\pi Nx)}B_N(x,t). \tag{16} \] The equality is meromorphic, with removable values interpreted. In particular, a deformation of the wire seams depending on angular coordinates is not covered by the coordinate-fixed-face theorem. Its transgression must be retained or separately proved to vanish. The cardinal representative is pointwise periodic after paired halfwires are multiplied, but its geometric asymptotics cannot be borrowed from the factorial representative merely by discarding (15). For a supplied compact family of positive angular points, \(|\Re t_v|<\pi\) leaves a uniform margin, so these angular points lie within (4) for all sufficiently large \(N\). This statement supplies room for a deformation; it does not prove positivity along a charge path or a global steepest-descent cycle. The exact factors \(W_N\), both coupon exponentials, all first normals and the canonical signed crossing factors remain in (8). No Fourier alias is discarded. The remaining source problem is to choose and estimate a whole joint representative of this fixed relative class: one must prove that its geometric local piece has a nonzero net coefficient and that its remaining pieces have smaller rate. The present exact primitive does not provide that estimate. In particular, an arbitrary connecting chain in (9) has not been identified with a scalar Ward deletion, so a classical action gap for those specific deletions does not by itself bound this chain. ## Direct sources All four complete source texts and their directly used implications were read, with the following fixed versions. * [Full-grid lens](research_full_grid_lens_source_continuation.md), SHA256 d141e6e8c23572bb13484807a2359395a0371d6a3d699198826a105b6dad5649: exact derivative trace, reflection normalization, canonical signed Gaussian factors and complete coupon jets. * [Arbitrary-power source compiler](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_arbitrary_power_source_compilation.md), SHA256 55e2de84870cfd20dac5922791dbc2bed54909439dfbf4663f17c70a1089445f: literal kernels, free-boundary convention, and common joint factorial domain (13). * [Finite Fourier band](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_newton_interpolation_finite_fourier_band.md), SHA256 2e2d95184081ba6440b56268cb597624d97a5f1931e8c0df886fa754e6684304: exact full-Hermite equality of (3), entire cardinal interpolation and paired-index averaging. * [Internal circle averaging](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_internal_wire_exact_circle_averaging.md), SHA256 0efa85a43da064197f25422d86ef37688971f2dface55da9d5efef3ccb0d08ef: arbitrary-network assembly, reflected wires and the distinction between trace periodicity and pointwise factorial periodicity. Only written proofs, source-text reads and file hashes were used. No mathematical code, numerical evaluation, test or compilation was run. Frozen notes, manuscripts and public documents were unchanged.

title: Kashaev's paired-face boundary adapter and its cyclic carry
text:
# Kashaev's paired-face boundary adapter and its cyclic carry Let \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), and let \(Q\) be a primitive \(N\)-th root of unity. The function in Kashaev's equation (4.28) defines an explicit map from one crossing index to a pair of boundary-face indices. This note proves its quotient, inverse, norm and cyclic-carry properties directly from that function. Its finite algebra works at every level. The tetrahedral state in the cited paper is restricted to odd levels; no even-level extension of that state is asserted here. ## 1. The specified finite function Choose nonzero complex numbers \(A,B\) and roots \[ a^N=A,\qquad b^N=B,\qquad r=a/b. \] Residues \([k]\) always lie in \(\{0,\ldots,d\}\). Define \[ f(k)=a^{[k-1]}b^{[-k]},\qquad \Psi_{kj}=Q^{jk}f(k),\qquad 0\le j,k<N. 	ag{1} \] In the published notation, \(a=s_{0m}\), \(b=s_{m5}\), and \[ A=s(u_0)-s(u_m),\qquad B=s(u_m)-s(u_5). \] Thus (1) is exactly the function \(\psi^k_{m,j}\) of (4.28), with its modular powers retained. In particular \[ f(0)=a^d,\qquad f(k)=a^{k-1}b^{N-k}= rac{B}{a}r^k\quad(1\le k<N). 	ag{2} \] The value at zero is not obtained by extending the second expression without its cyclic carry. Let \(F_{kj}=N^{-1/2}Q^{jk}\). Orthogonality of the finite geometric sum gives \(F^*F=I\). With \(D_f=\operatorname{diag}(f(k))\), \[ \Psi=\sqrt N D_fF,\qquad (\Psi^{-1})_{jk}= rac{Q^{-jk}}{Nf(k)}. 	ag{3} \] These are invertible matrices for every stated \(N,A,B\), with no primality assumption. The star on \(F\) concerns the fixed root of unity only; no complex conjugation of \(A,B\) enters the inverse. ## 2. The paired-face quotient and its exact projector Fix a charge \(c\in\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z\). On a face pair write \(\alpha_-,\alpha_+\in\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z\), and put \[ k=\alpha_- -\alpha_+ +c. \] Define \(J_c:\mathbb C^N\longrightarrow\mathbb C^{N^2}\) by \[ (J_cv)(\alpha_-,\alpha_+)=v(\alpha_- -\alpha_+ +c). 	ag{4} \] Its image \(\mathcal H_c\) consists precisely of the arrays invariant under simultaneous translation of both face indices. This invariant subspace is independent of \(c\); the charge specifies its coordinate. Each value of \(k\) has exactly \(N\) preimages. Consequently \[ J_c^*J_c=NI,\qquad P_{m diag}= rac1N J_cJ_c^* = rac1N\sum_{t\in\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z}T_t, 	ag{5} \] where \((T_tw)(\alpha_-,\alpha_+)=w(\alpha_-+t,\alpha_++t)\). This proves both that the quotient has dimension \(N\) and that \(\iota_c=J_c/\sqrt N\) is an isometry onto its invariant realization. Explicitly, the quotient is \(\mathbb C^{N^2}/\operatorname{span}\{(T_t-I)w\}\); the averaging projector in (5) identifies it with \(\mathcal H_c\). The literal boundary adapter and a specified left inverse are \[ \mathcal A_c=J_c\Psi,\qquad \mathcal L_c=\Psi^{-1} rac{J_c^*}{N}. \] They satisfy \[ \mathcal L_c\mathcal A_c=I,\qquad \mathcal A_c\mathcal L_c=P_{m diag},\qquad \mathcal A_c=N\iota_cD_fF. 	ag{6} \] Thus the adapter is a rank-\(N\) map into the full face-pair space, and an isomorphism onto its diagonal-translation quotient. It is not an isomorphism onto all \(N^2\) boundary coordinates. Charge shifts permute the \(k\) coordinate and do not alter any singular value. ## 3. Exact singular values and uniform decoration bounds The singular values of \(\Psi\) are \(\sqrt N|f(k)|\); the nonzero singular values of \(\mathcal A_c\) are \(N|f(k)|\). Formula (2) gives \[ |f(0)|=|A|^{d/N},\qquad |f(k)|=|A|^{(k-1)/N}|B|^{(N-k)/N}\quad(k\ge1). \] All exponents are nonnegative and sum to \(d/N\). Both extreme values occur, at \(k=0\) and \(k=1\). Hence \[ \min_k|f(k)|=\min\{|A|,|B|\}^{d/N},\qquad \max_k|f(k)|=\max\{|A|,|B|\}^{d/N}, \] \[ \kappa_2(\Psi)=\kappa_2(\mathcal A_c) =\left( rac{\max\{|A|,|B|\}}{\min\{|A|,|B|\}}ight)^{d/N}. 	ag{7} \] In (7), the rectangular condition number uses its nonzero singular values. On a fixed compact set of nonzero \(A,B\), the normalized adapter \(\mathcal A_c/N=\iota_cD_fF\) and its inverse on the image have bounds independent of \(N\). No factorial diagonal gauge is being substituted for (1). These bounds retain every fixed-order decoration derivative. Work on a simply connected parameter neighborhood with holomorphic choices of \(\log A,\log B\); each root differs from their exponential roots by a constant root of unity. In (2), \(f(k)\) is then a constant phase times \(A^{u_k}B^{v_k}\), where \(u_k,v_k\in[0,1]\). For the inverse the two exponents lie in \([-1,0]\). Differentiation multiplies these powers by falling factorials of bounded real exponents and by fixed negative powers of \(A,B\). On every compact subset \(K\) of this neighborhood, for each fixed multi-index \(
u\), \[ \sup_K\|\partial^
u D_f\|+ \sup_K\|\partial^
u D_f^{-1}\|\le C_{K,
u}, 	ag{8} \] uniformly in \(N\) and in the constant root choices. Equations (3),(6) give the corresponding normalized operator bounds. Composition with the linear differences of vertex decorations gives the same result for those parameters. This does not differentiate the root \(Q\) off the root-of-unity locus or identify decoration derivatives with the original meridian or quantum-normal directions. ## 4. The cyclic seam and its complete monodromy Let \((Sv)(k)=v(k+1)\), with cyclic indices. Direct substitution in (2), including \(k=N-1\), gives \[ Sf-rf= rac{B-A}{b}\,\delta_0, \qquad  rac{f(k+1)}{f(k)} =r\left[1+\left( rac BA-1ight)\delta_{k0}ight]. 	ag{9} \] Equivalently, with \(E_0\) the zero-coordinate projector, \[ D_f^{-1}SD_f=r[I+(B/A-1)E_0]S. 	ag{10} \] This is a rank-one correction to the geometric progression, not an assertion that its norm is one. Its norm contribution is \(|r|\,|B/A-1|\), uniformly bounded on the compacts used in (8). The multiplier accumulated around the complete cyclic index is \[ r^N rac BA= rac AB rac BA=1. 	ag{11} \] Thus (10) has \(N\)-th power \(I\), as also follows by conjugating \(S^N=I\). With face charge \(c\), the seam is the actual locus \(\alpha_- -\alpha_+=-c\). Replacing (9) by a seam-free progression would change the monodromy unless \(A=B\). ## 5. Four legs and the full boundary normalization Take four nonzero pairs \(A_m=a_m^N,B_m=b_m^N\), charges \(c_m\), and a nonzero root \(s_{05}\). For an arbitrary four-index array \(R=(R_{j_1j_2j_3j_4})\), define its boundary array by the literal right-hand expression of the published (4.25): \[ \mathcal B_R( oldsymbol\alpha_-, oldsymbol\alpha_+) =s_{05}^{d}\sum_{j_1,\ldots,j_4}R_{j_1j_2j_3j_4} \prod_{m=1}^4\Psi^{(m)}_{\alpha_{m,-}-\alpha_{m,+}+c_m,j_m}. 	ag{12} \] No property of \(R\) is needed for the following exact identities: \[ \mathcal B_R=s_{05}^{d}N^4 \left( igotimes_{m=1}^4\iota_{c_m}D_{f_m}Fight)R, \] \[ R= rac1{s_{05}^{d}N^4} \left( igotimes_{m=1}^4F^*D_{f_m}^{-1}\iota_{c_m}^*ight) \mathcal B_R. 	ag{13} \] In particular the \(N^4\) factor is the four-leg paired-face normalization; it is not removed by using normalized Fourier matrices. The image projector is \( igotimes_mP_{m diag}\), and the map has rank \(N^4\). Its norm bounds are precisely \[ |s_{05}|^dN^4\prod_m\min_k|f_m(k)|\,\|R\|_2 \le\|\mathcal B_R\|_2 \le |s_{05}|^dN^4\prod_m\max_k|f_m(k)|\,\|R\|_2. 	ag{14} \] For published vertex decorations, \(A_m+B_m=s_{05}^N\) for every leg. When these differences range over fixed nonzero compacts, \(|s_{05}|^d=|s_{05}^N|^{d/N}\) and its fixed-order derivatives are uniformly bounded, as are its inverse and the normalized maps (13). The four-leg exponential scale is therefore unchanged under these specific fixed-decoration bounds. Original tensor contractions use their specified dual rows. If a column is sent to \(\mathcal A_cv\), its row \(\ell\) is transported to \(\ell\mathcal L_c\); then \(\ell\mathcal L_c\mathcal A_cv=\ell v\) exactly. The inverse uses \(f(k)^{-1}\), not \(\overline{f(k)}\). Replacing the transported row by a Hermitian adjoint changes the contraction in general. Positive singular-value estimates do not authorize that replacement. For an arbitrary row on the full face-pair space, only its restriction through \(P_{m diag}\) contributes on the adapter image. ## 6. Opposite-face sewing retains the original wire clock Use the same roots \(a,b\) on two paired-face adapters. Reverse the face order in the second adapter and impose the charge condition \(c+c'=1\) modulo \(N\). Their arguments are then \[ k=\alpha_- -\alpha_+ +c,\qquad k'=\alpha_+ -\alpha_- +c'=[1-k]. \] The exact complement identity is \[ f(k)f([1-k])=(ab)^d. 	ag{15} \] At \(k=0,1\), this is \(a^db^d=(ab)^d\). For \(2\le k<N\), the second residue is \(N+1-k\); the two exponents of \(a\) sum to \((k-1)+(N-k)=d\), and those of \(b\) sum to \((N-k)+(k-1)=d\). Thus (15) also includes both cyclic endpoints and \(N=2\). There are \(N\) face pairs with each argument \(k\). Bilinear contraction therefore gives, with \(Z_{jj'}=Q^j\delta_{jj'}\), \[  egin{split} &\sum_{\alpha_-,\alpha_+} \mathcal A_c(\alpha_-,\alpha_+;j) \mathcal A_{c'}(\alpha_+,\alpha_-;j')\ &\quad=N(ab)^d \sum_{k=0}^{N-1}Q^{jk+j'(1-k)} =N^2(ab)^dQ^j\delta_{jj'}. \end{split} 	ag{16} \] If the specified non-link edge factors are \(a^{-d}b^{-d}\), they cancel the decoration factor in (16), leaving \(N^2Z\). The factor \(Q^j\) is the wire factor appearing in the original planar source (3.6). It is not an identity pairing or a Hermitian square. The statement here requires exactly the roots, reversed face order and complementary charges just specified; it does not prove that a proposed global triangulation has those data. Even changing only the root branches retains an explicit wire operator. If the second adapter instead uses \(a'=Q^u a,\ b'=Q^v b\), then \[ f'(l)=Q^{(u-v)l-u}f(l). \] Repeating the same finite sum yields \[ \sum_{\alpha_-,\alpha_+} \mathcal A_c^{a,b}(\alpha_-,\alpha_+;j) \mathcal A_{c'}^{a',b'}(\alpha_+,\alpha_-;j') =N^2(ab)^dQ^{j-u}\delta_{j',\,j-u+v}. 	ag{17} \] Thus branch changes give a recorded phase and index translation; they cannot silently be replaced by the common-root formula. ## 7. The literal fixed cut and its one-face marginal The planar definition in the primary paper fixes both open-edge indices to zero in (3.2). Its rank-one cut operator in that index basis is \(E_{00}\). Transport this particular operator, with the inverse row from (6), to the paired-face space: \[ \mathcal E_c=\mathcal A_cE_{00}\mathcal L_c. \] For row index \((\alpha_-,\alpha_+)\), column index \((\alpha'_-,\alpha'_+)\), and their respective differences \(k,k'\), (3),(6) give \[ (\mathcal E_c)_{\alpha_-\alpha_+;\,\alpha'_-\alpha'_+} = rac{f(k)}{N^2 f(k')}. 	ag{18} \] Thus \(\mathcal E_c^2=\mathcal E_c\), its rank and trace are one, and \(P_{m diag}\mathcal E_c=\mathcal E_cP_{m diag}=\mathcal E_c\). These identities follow either from (6) or directly from (18). They retain the fixed-index cut; no change of the original planar index basis is made in identifying \(E_{00}\). Trace out the second face and call the resulting \(N\)-dimensional matrix \(M\). Put \[ t=A/B=r^N,\qquad h=[\alpha'-\alpha]. \] Then \[ M_{\alpha\alpha'} = rac1{N^2}\sum_{k=0}^{N-1} rac{f(k)}{f([k+h])} = rac{r^{-h}}{N^2} igl[(N-h)+ht igr]. 	ag{19} \] For \(h=0\), every summand is one. For \(1\le h<N\), the ratio is \(r^{-h}\) at \(N-h\) indices and \(tr^{-h}\) at the remaining \(h\). More explicitly, \(k=0\) and \(N-h<k<N\) give the latter value; \(1\le k\le N-h\) give the former, including the denominator endpoint \(k+h=N\). This proves (19) without dropping either seam endpoint. The charge has disappeared because \(k\) ranges over every residue. Tracing out the first face gives \(M^{\mathsf T}\), so the two marginals have the same spectrum. The Fourier vector with entries \(N^{-1/2}Q^{j\alpha}\) has eigenvalue \[ \lambda_j= rac1{N^2}\sum_{h=0}^{N-1} [(N-h)+ht]z_j^h,\qquad z_j=r^{-1}Q^j. 	ag{20} \] If \(t
e1\), then \(z_j^N=t^{-1}\) and \(z_j
e1\). Using the finite geometric sum and its derivative in (20) gives \[ \lambda_j=  rac{(t-1)^2z_j}{N^2t(1-z_j)^2}. 	ag{21} \] For example, the numerator before substitution is \[ N(1-z_j^N)(1-z_j) +(t-1) igl[z_j-Nz_j^N+(N-1)z_j^{N+1} igr], \] which becomes \((t-1)^2z_j/t\). All eigenvalues are nonzero when \(t
e1\), even though the two-face cut itself has rank one. Their sum is \(\operatorname{Tr}M=1\). If \(t=1\), (19) instead gives \(M_{\alpha\alpha'}=r^{-[\alpha'-\alpha]}/N\); this is the rank-one Fourier projector onto the unique character with \(Q^j=r\). There is a positive case of the actual fixed cut. Suppose \(|A|=|B|\), so \(|r|=1\). Then all \(|f(k)|\) are equal, and (18) is an orthogonal rank-one projector. Its marginal is consequently positive semidefinite. If also \(t=e^{i	heta}
e1\), write \(z_j=e^{i\varphi_j}\); (21) gives \[ \lambda_j= rac{\sin^2(	heta/2)} {N^2\sin^2(\varphi_j/2)},\qquad  rac{\sin^2(	heta/2)}{N^2}\le\lambda_j\le1. 	ag{22} \] The denominator is nonzero because \(z_j^N=t^{-1}
e1\). The lower bound uses \(\sin^2(\varphi_j/2)\le1\), and the upper bound follows from positivity and trace one. Hence for every positive semidefinite one-face operator \(H\), \[  rac{\sin^2(	heta/2)}{N^2}\operatorname{Tr}H \ \le\ \operatorname{Tr}(MH)\ \le\ \operatorname{Tr}H. 	ag{23} \] The same holds on the other face. The constant is uniform in \(N\) when \(t\) stays on a fixed compact subset of the unit circle excluding \(1\); no such positive lower bound is asserted at \(t=1\). Equation (23) concerns a positive operator on one face against this explicitly transported fixed cut. It is not a lower bound for arbitrary signed crossings, two-face operators, or the remaining contracted knot network. It also does not identify a different uniform-vector mark in another matrix basis with the planar \(E_{00}\) used here. ## 8. Tetrahedral and source scope Equations (1)--(23) prove a concrete boundary-module adapter and transport its literal fixed-index cut. They do not prove that the nine-tetrahedron state sum equals (12). The published identity (4.25) makes that additional assertion for its specified crossing tensor at odd \(N\). Its four paired boundary faces, tangle edges, vertex measures, charge sums and root phases must all be retained in any use of that assertion. In particular, (13) alone does not supply an adapter from an independently assigned five-cell or pointed tetrahedral state. The sewing statement (16) supplies the original local wire phase under its stated charge and edge-factor conditions. No identification with the original marked meridian, a free-vertex deletion, a globally charged triangulation, or a selected geometric period is inferred. The explicit seam in (9), the inverse dual row, and the factor \(s_{05}^dN^4\) are part of the boundary data for that comparison, rather than discarded normalizations. ## Direct definition R. M. Kashaev, *A Link Invariant from Quantum Dilogarithm*, [q-alg/9504020v1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/q-alg/9504020), especially (4.25)--(4.28), with the odd-level convention (4.1), the fixed-index cut (3.2), the wire phase (3.6), and the non-link edge factor (4.19)--(4.20). The sole imported mathematical datum is the displayed function (4.28); the boundary expression (12) is defined for arbitrary \(R\). The complete paper also specifies the original three-dimensional state and its restrictions, which are not substituted for a proof of the broader source comparisons excluded above. Local archived PDF: `research_archive/finite-source-identification-2026-11-01/md-kashaev-normalization-critical-audit/kashaev1995.pdf`. SHA256: `0baef40fa9934c9119af2c67252f8032e288c884da72eeaecf405bf91569cda9`. The archived and linked PDF bytes agree.

title: Riccati transport through the last physical row
text: # Riccati transport through the last physical row Research proof, 3 November 2026. Frozen manuscripts are unchanged. The absolute normalization of the physical Newton rows extends to their last row. At odd levels this last row is the complete color \(-2\). Consequently the complete-end kernel itself has the geometric exponential rate, with a nonzero holomorphic factor of polynomial size, on every compact subset of the free-color half-plane \(\Re w<2\). This result estimates the coherent finite polynomial. An individual Newton summand can have a larger exponential rate there. At even levels the last physical color is different from \(-2\), and the conclusion about the complete-end kernel requires a separate argument. ## 1. Original rows and the assertion Use the original rows \[ F_{j,N}(w)=K_N(c_j,w),\qquad c_j=2\cos((2j+1)\theta),\qquad \theta=\pi/N,\qquad J_N=\lfloor(N-1)/2\rfloor . \tag{1} \] In particular \(F_{0,N}=1\). For \(0\le r<J_N\), their exact recurrence is \[ \rho_{r+1}=1+d_r+q_r(1-\rho_r^{-1}),\qquad \rho_r=F_{r,N}/F_{r-1,N},\qquad d_r=(c_0-w)/A_r, \tag{2} \] where the term involving \(\rho_0\) is absent, and \[ A_r=\frac{s_{r+1}^4}{s_{2r+1}s_{2r+2}},\qquad q_r=\frac{C_r}{A_r},\qquad s_r=2\sin(r\theta). \tag{3} \] The original positive Jacobi realization proves that every row is nonzero for \(\Re w<c_0\), and \(\Re\rho_r>1\) there. These facts and the bulk estimates are proved in [the physical-row transport note](research_physical_row_riccati_transport.md). Set \[ \lambda(x,w)= \exp\!\left(2\operatorname{asinh} \left(\frac{\sqrt{2-w}}2\cot(\pi x)\right)\right), \qquad 0<x<1/2 . \tag{4} \] The square root has positive real part. Thus \(\Re\lambda>1\), and the logarithm in (4) is the one continued from real \(w<2\). **Theorem 1.** Fix \(\gamma>0\) and \(R<\infty\). Uniformly for \[ \Re w\le2-\gamma,\qquad |w|\le R, \tag{5} \] and all sufficiently large \(N\), \[ \boxed{\quad \sum_{r=1}^{J_N}\Log\rho_r(w) =N\int_0^{J_N/N}\Log\lambda(x,w)\,dx+O(\log N). \quad} \tag{6} \] Each ratio logarithm in (6) is its right-half-plane logarithm. This specifies the logarithm of the row rather than taking the principal logarithm of the final polynomial. Every fixed derivative in \(w\) of the error is also \(O(\log N)\) on compact subsets of \(\Re w<2\). The same estimate holds with any final row between \(\lfloor N/4\rfloor\) and \(J_N\). ## 2. An exact lower barrier near the last row Put \(r_0=\lfloor N/4\rfloor\), and define \[ Q_r=\frac{\cos(r\theta)}{\sin^3(r\theta)},\qquad h_r=N/2-r,\qquad u_r=\rho_r-1. \tag{7} \] All these \(Q_r\) are positive for \(r_0\le r\le J_N\). For the recurrence indices \(r_0\le r<J_N\), the exact coefficient identities are \[ q_r=\frac{Q_{r+1}}{Q_r},\qquad \frac{1/A_r}{Q_rQ_{r+1}} =B_r:=\frac{\sin^3(r\theta)\sin((2r+1)\theta)} {2\cos(r\theta)}. \tag{8} \] For all sufficiently large \(N\), \(r_0/N\ge1/5\). Since \[ \sin((2r+1)\theta) =\sin(r\theta)\cos((r+1)\theta) +\cos(r\theta)\sin((r+1)\theta), \] one has uniform bounds \[ b_0:=\tfrac12\sin^4(\pi/5)\le B_r\le1,\qquad Q_r\asymp h_r/N,\qquad |Q_{r+1}-Q_r|\le C/N. \tag{9} \] The \(B_r\), \(q_r\), and \(d_r\) statements use \(r<J_N\); the estimates for \(Q_r\) itself include \(r=J_N\). Here and below all constants can depend on (5), but not on the row or the level. There is \(c>0\) such that \[ \Re u_r\ge cQ_r \quad(r_0\le r\le J_N). \tag{10} \] To prove this, the bulk theorem initializes (10) at \(r_0\), after choosing \(c\) small enough. Indeed the limiting ratio at \(x=1/4\) has real part strictly greater than one, uniformly on (5). Decrease \(c\) further so that \(c^2\le\gamma b_0/2\).
