title: A local geometric period chart for the original knot state
text:
# A local geometric period chart for the original knot state Private written proof, 18 November 2026. For every hyperbolic knot and every fixed finite braid presenting it, the original reduced state has an exact finite residue-period presentation whose integrand has a nonzero local amplitude at a regular geometric principal critical point. Its corrected principal action has the hyperbolic volume. The representation uses the literal factorial crossing coefficients, rather than their additional coherent occupation transforms. This is a local statement about an exact presentation. It does not show that its original residue cycle has a nonzero component at that critical point. The centralizer direction, other source boundaries and equal-rate aliases are still present. The complete proof directs are **A**, the literal slit-chart amplitudes; **F**, the common framing and complex cut; and **V**, the actual critical-action volume calibration. Their pins appear below. The ordinary binomial and residue-kernel steps are proved here. ## 1. The exact lattice and its coordinates Fix a braid of a hyperbolic knot, with \(c\) signed crossings. Put \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(h=2\pi i/N\), and \(c_0=2\pi i\). Keep the original crossing scalars, tail pivots and prescribed zero framing. View its closed diagram as the directed crossing graph. It has \(2c\) wire arcs and \(c\) vertices. Integer occupation on its wires satisfies input sum equals output sum at each crossing. The graph is connected and Eulerian. Choose a spanning tree avoiding the cut edge, which is not a bridge. The \(m=c+1\) chord-wire occupations \[ k=(k_1,\ldots,k_m) 	ag{1} \] are integral coordinates for its entire circulation lattice. Indeed integer values on the chords determine the tree values uniquely by leaf elimination of the conservation equations. No finite-index sublattice or determinant factor is introduced. One of the chords is the cut edge. At each positive crossing the transfer is \(n=c_{m out}-b_{m in}\); at a negative crossing it is \(n=b_{m in}-c_{m out}\). Thus all wire and transfer indices are integral linear forms in (1). Let \(S_N\subset\mathbb Z^m\) be the original finite support: every wire index is between \(0\) and \(d\), with the actual signed crossing inequalities on \(n\). Nothing extends this support to a cube of independent occupations. Let \(W_N(k)\) be the original summand for the unnormalized diagonal partial trace \(C_N(M)_{aa}\), before the cut average. A trace-one diagonal probe therefore inserts its weight directly into \(W_N\). If one instead starts with the old \(1/N\) cut-averaged summand, the insertion is \(N\) times that weight. These are the same normalization; an extra \(1/N\) is not retained. ## 2. A frame in which every local length is admissible F supplies a regular complete geometric frame, arbitrarily near the midpoint frame, for which every required wire and transfer clock has modulus different from one. It repairs the wire logarithms by an integer spanning-tree flow while preserving the chosen cut logarithm. Choose its cut parameter \[ 	heta= rac{\zeta_{m cut}}{c_0},\qquad 	heta\ \hbox{near }1/2,\quad \Im	heta
e0. 	ag{2} \] Use F's exact complex-binomial cut \[  eta_{	heta,a}= inom da	heta^a(1-	heta)^{d-a}. \] Its weights sum to one. The actual scalar endomorphism identity therefore gives, exactly at every level, \[ K_N=\sum_{k\in S_N} eta_{	heta,a(k)}W_N(k) 	ag{3} \] in the original reduced zero-framed convention. All original external factors in that convention remain in \(W_N\). The marked-cut difference is F's explicit Ward commutator; (3) does not assert equality of arbitrary marked families. Set \(x_j=\zeta_j/c_0\) for the chosen chord logarithms. At the framed geometric point \(x_*\), every chord \(x_j\) is nonreal: its wire clock is off the unit circle. Every affine crossing factorial length is also nonreal, including both numerator and denominator lengths in A. There is consequently a fixed small polydisc \(U\) about \(x_*\) on which * every such length lies in a common compact subset of \(\mathcal D=\mathbb C\setminus((-\infty,0]\cup[1,\infty))\); * each chord imaginary part has a fixed nonzero sign and absolute value at least some \(\delta>0\); * the cut coordinate stays near \(	heta\), with its real part strictly between zero and one. The frame, \(	heta,U,\delta\) are fixed independently of \(N\). They may depend on the knot and diagram. The finite offsets involving \(d=N-1\) remain in the literal formulas. ## 3. The local amplitude includes the actual cut weight Interpolate the cut binomial by its ordinary Gamma ratio: \[ b_{N,	heta}(y)=  rac{\Gamma(N)} {\Gamma(y+1)\Gamma(N-y)} 	heta^y(1-	heta)^{N-1-y}. 	ag{4} \] The logarithms of \(	heta\) and \(1-	heta\) are the compatible ones near \(1/2\). This equals \( eta_{	heta,a}\) at every allowed integer cut occupation \(a\). Ordinary Gamma Stirling expansion, on the closed sectors about the positive real directions used in A, gives uniformly for \(z\) near \(	heta\) \[ b_{N,	heta}(Nz)= N^{-1/2}  rac{1-z}{(1-	heta)\sqrt{2\pi z(1-z)}} \exp\{N\,b_	heta(z)\}(1+O(N^{-1})), 	ag{5} \] \[ b_	heta(z)=-z\log z-(1-z)\log(1-z) +z\log	heta+(1-z)\log(1-	heta). \] To check the finite correction, use \( inom{N-1}{Nz}=(1-z) inom N{Nz}\) and factor \((1-	heta)^{-1}\) from the last power in (4). This proves the factor \((1-z)/(1-	heta)\) in (5). All logarithms and square roots are continued together. The amplitude is a holomorphic unit on a smaller compact neighborhood. Bounded affine index offsets only add the corresponding nonzero exponential of a logarithmic derivative, as in A's shift calculation. Interpolate each crossing in \(W_N\) by A's same marked quantum-factorial ratios. Its exact monomial is kept, including the common Cartan scalar. Each crossing then has a nonzero \(N^{-1/2}\) local amplitude on \(U\). Combining the \(c\) crossings and (5) gives the literal interpolated summand \[ I_N(Nx) =N^{-(c+1)/2}\,a(x)\, e^{N\phi_	heta(x)}(1+O(N^{-1})), \qquad a(x)
e0\quad(x\in U), 	ag{6} \] with the explicitly retained normalizing powers understood if an alternative external normalization is supplied. For the reduced diagonal partial-trace convention of Section 1 there is no further old cut-average factor. All exact monomial, pivot and framing exponentials are included in the specified principal action and its remaining unit amplitude. Their root phases have not been replaced by moduli. Equation (6) concerns the same interpolated lattice summand whose supported values occur in (3). It is not a theorem about the additional coherent crossing sums. A supplies the uniform error and every fixed holomorphic derivative on smaller compacts. ## 4. An exact period with a locally nonzero residue-kernel amplitude For each \(N\), let \(\Gamma_N\) be the oriented sum of small product circles about the points of \(S_N\). Choose them small enough to enclose no other integer or factorial poles. The interpolant is holomorphic at these supported points: every physical factorial length is between zero and \(N-1\), and common endpoint ratios mean the cancelled finite product. For an integer vector \(n\in\mathbb Z^m\), define \[ \Omega_{N,n}(z)= rac1{(2\pi i)^m} e^{-c_0n\cdot z}I_N(z) \prod_{j=1}^m\pi\cot(\pi z_j)\,dz_j . 	ag{7} \] At an integer state the new character is one, and each cotangent factor has residue one. Multivariable residues therefore prove the exact identity \[ \int_{\Gamma_N}\Omega_{N,n}=K_N. 	ag{8} \] All support and source data are the original ones. The character is part of a specified alternate interpolant, not an assertion that the two meromorphic forms agree off the integer lattice. The cotangent factors also have a nonzero uniform local amplitude in the chart \(U\). The elementary exponential formula for cotangent gives \[ \pi\cot(\pi N x_j)= -i\pi\,\operatorname{sgn}(\Im x_j) +O(e^{-2\pi\delta N}). 	ag{9} \] This is uniform with fixed derivatives after shrinking \(U\); polynomial differentiation factors are absorbed by a slightly smaller exponential constant. Thus the actual residue kernel, not just the factorial summand, is a holomorphic unit there for all sufficiently large \(N\). Scaling \(z=Nx\) in (7) gives a local density \[ \Omega_{N,n}(Nx)= N^{m-(c+1)/2}\,\widetilde a(x) e^{N(\phi_	heta(x)-c_0n\cdot x)} (1+O(N^{-1}))\,dx_1\cdots dx_m , \qquad \widetilde a(x)
e0. 	ag{10} \] The constant factors in (7), (9) are included in \(\widetilde a\). No pole or zero of the cotangent kernel has been suppressed near this point. ## 5. Critical action and volume Write the actual principal action as \[ S_	heta(\zeta)=S_0(\zeta)+g_	heta(u),\qquad \phi_	heta(x)=S_	heta(c_0x)/c_0,\qquad g_	heta(c_0z)=c_0 b_	heta(z). 	ag{11} \] Here \(S_0\) includes all original crossing, pivot and framing terms. A's reversed factorial products can express some dilogarithms with reciprocal arguments compared with V's five-shape notation. The inversion identity changes their Gaussian part by a real quadratic polynomial, an imaginary linear polynomial and a real constant; \(D(z^{-1})=-D(z)\) gives the same crossing regulator. Thus the bare-state logarithmic identity used below has the same normalization for this literal factorial phase. F proves that the geometric point is a regular exponentiated principal critical point, with \(u=c_0	heta\). On compatible logarithms let \[ \partial_{\zeta_j}S_	heta(\zeta_*)=c_0 n_j, \qquad n_j\in\mathbb Z. 	ag{12} \] Choose precisely this vector in (7). The exponent in (10) then has zero first derivative at \(x_*\). This is additive principal stationarity in an exact period presentation, not just an exponentiated equation. At this point \(g_	heta=g_	heta'=0\) on the matching sheets. V supplies the bare-state regulator identity \[ D( eta)=\Im S_0 -\sum_j\Re\zeta_j\,\Im\partial_{\zeta_j}S_0 	ag{13} \] at \(M=1\), and the degree-one crossing fundamental-chain comparison \(D( eta)=\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K)\). Consequently \[ \Im\left(S_	heta-c_0\sum_jn_j\zeta_jight)_{\zeta_*} =\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K). 	ag{14} \] The cut coordinate is included in this subtraction. Its real part need not be zero for the complex cut. Thus (10) has the calibrated geometric exponential rate. Compatible changes of entropy or dilogarithm sheets carry their corresponding integer character and retained real constant, as in V; they are not arbitrary shifts of the imaginary action. The original external modified-dimension factor, if supplied, remains its whole function. At \(M=1\) its specified value is a unit phase times \(1/N\); it changes the explicit power and phase, not (14). No meridian normal is deleted. ## 6. What the theorem does not say The point \(x_*\) need not lie on a contributing deformation of \(\Gamma_N\). The principal critical family retains its centralizer direction, so this is not an isolated Gaussian saddle theorem. Even the nonzero local density in (10) does not fix its relative-cycle coefficient. Changing the integer character changes the off-lattice integrand and its possible boundary behavior. Equation (8) is exact on the stated original small-circle cycle; it does not permit a subsequent unrecorded contour change. All other source boundaries, support walls, escaping decorations and equal-rate aliases still require their own comparison. No scalar lower bound or new volume-conjecture knot case is asserted. Where the underlying finite coefficients have their specified analytic parameter germs, the residue equality also preserves those germs. For genuine fixed-color quantum normals one uses the original path \(M=-q^N\), with \(d=N-1\) fixed, as in A. A fixed-\(M\) auxiliary array is not identified with a generic-\(q\) representation by scalarity alone. ## Complete proof-source pins * A: notes/research_literal_crossing_slit_chart_amplitude.md, SHA256 c3682b0f84000aad4c2f53235b9c93bbd86283905a75d6f07ac03b1a3c00bc4a. * F: notes/research_literal_factorial_common_slit_frame.md, SHA256 9764a2b77469c7fad402b9b8e609b304a79083bde18fb139031c06fd93650ca8. * V: notes/research_soft_cut_critical_action_volume.md, SHA256 10db12845523ab5700e870e5a896ac003a6c29c3892d4618ddf043d3a5891689. All three complete unchanged directs were read in the current author sequence, every used implication checked and all matching pins renewed. The binomial correction, coordinate count, exact residue character and cotangent amplitude are proved here. Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used. Frozen and public files are unchanged.

title: A quantitative volume gap for actual long-filled groups
text: # A quantitative volume gap for actual long-filled groups Research note, 18 November 2026. The full group relation of a Dehn filling forces every nearby centered primitive charge to be a nonzero integer. Consequently the geometric charge comparison applies to every other admitted representation of the filled group, without matching a Fourier label to that centered charge. This is a statement about classical representations, not source cycles. ## 1. Proof sources, normalization, and theorem The complete proof sources are: * **G**, [A uniform representation-volume gap along centered long cone paths](research_centered_long_cone_representation_volume_gap.md). * **F**, [A finite positive certificate supplies every sufficiently long filling branch](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/finite_geometric_certificate_uniform_filling_existence.md). Fix the marked complete hyperbolic core \(M\), its positive complete certificate, and its positively oriented primitive cusp bases \((\mu_i,\lambda_i)\), as in these sources. A fixed earlier short partial filling may already be part of \(M\). Fill a nonempty subset \(I\) along primitive slopes \[ \alpha_i=\mu_i^{a_i}\lambda_i^{b_i},\qquad \gcd(a_i,b_i)=1,\qquad \ell_i=(a_i^2+b_i^2)^{1/2}. \tag{1} \] Write \(M(\sigma)\) for the actual marked filling and \(\pi:\pi_1M\twoheadrightarrow\pi_1M(\sigma)\) for its quotient map. All remaining cusps, including every unfilled physical main cusp, are retained. An admitted representation in this note is \[ \rho:\pi_1M(\sigma)\longrightarrow\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb C) \tag{2} \] whose image on every remaining cusp is boundary-parabolic, with the trivial image allowed. Use the signed representation volume normalized by the same oriented fundamental class as G and F. Section 2 checks its equality with the normalized volume of the core pullback \(\widehat\rho=\rho\circ\pi\). The parabolic condition on the remaining cusps is substantive. It is what fixes their centered peripheral coordinates to zero near complete holonomy. No uniform gap over varying nonparabolic boundary conditions is asserted. If all cusps are filled, this condition is empty. **Theorem.** There are constants \(L_*,\delta,c_1>0\), depending only on the fixed marked core and certificate, such that for every primitive slope tuple with \(\ell_{\min}>L_*\), the filling \(M(\sigma)\) is the actual oriented hyperbolic filling supplied by F. Let \(\rho_{\mathrm{hyp},\sigma}\) be its oriented projective holonomy. Every admitted representation not conjugate to it satisfies \[ \operatorname{Vol}_{M(\sigma)}(\rho) \le \operatorname{Vol}(M(\sigma)) - \min\left\{\frac{\delta}{2}, \frac{3c_1}{\ell_{\max}^2}\right\}, \qquad \ell_{\max}=\max_{i\in I}\ell_i. \tag{3} \] One choice works for all subsets, signs and independently unequal long slope lengths. The comparison is between underlying projective conjugacy classes. Central lifts and different source decorations of the same projective representation are not separated by volume. ## 2. Pullback volume and cyclic filled peripheral images Primitivity in (1) implies \(\mathbb Z^2/\langle(a_i,b_i)\rangle\cong\mathbb Z\). Therefore the image of the \(i\)-th filled peripheral group under \(\widehat\rho\) is cyclic. In particular it is trivial, parabolic, or fixes both endpoints of an axis individually. There is no peripheral endpoint-interchanging group hidden in this assertion. Together with the admitted unfilled cusps, these are precisely the peripheral types used by the core volume comparison in G. Here is a map-level verification of the normalization under filling. On a filled solid torus, use coordinates \((d,t)\in D^2\times\mathbb R\) on its universal cover, with \(t\mapsto t+1\) representing the core generator \(g\). Choose a \(g\)-equivariant curve \(\gamma:\mathbb R\to\mathbb H^3\) and put \[ \mathcal D(d,t)=\gamma(t). \tag{4} \] For a loxodromic \(g\), take its axis with the appropriate translation speed. For an elliptic \(g\), take a constant point on its axis. For a parabolic \(g\), conjugate it to \(w\mapsto w+b\) and use \(\gamma(t)=(tb,1)\) in upper-half-space coordinates. For the identity take a constant curve. These maps are equivariant for the actual cyclic peripheral quotient and have differential rank at most one. Their volume integrals are zero. Prescribe the same maps on the bounding tori of a compact truncation of \(M\), independent of the meridional coordinate. An equivariant map on the remaining compact core with these boundary values exists by extending over a lifted finite cell decomposition: the target \(\mathbb H^3\) is contractible, and each cell extension is propagated equivariantly. Smooth it relative to the fixed collars. Keep identical admissible maps on all unfilled cusps in the two constructions. For the core volume, replace each solid torus by a cusp tail. In the axis case the tail can be kept in that same axis. In the parabolic case use \((tb,e^s)\), with the cusp-depth variable \(s\ge0\); its image lies in the vertical hyperbolic plane over the line \(\mathbb R b\). The trivial case uses a ray. Each such tail has rank at most two and zero three-volume, and matches (4) at its initial torus. These are the cyclic instances of the axis/parabolic cusp models defining the volume in G. Changing the axis-depth parametrization, or comparing the displayed parabolic tail with its conical ideal end, remains in the same axis or plane; the comparison homotopy has zero three-volume as well. The compact-core integrals and all unfilled ends are thus identical, and the added pieces contribute zero. With the retained orientation, \[ \operatorname{Vol}_{M(\sigma)}(\rho) =\operatorname{Vol}_M(\widehat\rho). \tag{5} \] This uses the full cyclic quotient at the filled tori. An equation for peripheral eigenvalues alone would not supply the solid-torus map. ## 3. The full slope relation forces a nonzero centered charge Use the fixed conjugacy-invariant complete-holonomy neighborhood \(\mathcal U\) from G, shrinking it if necessary as in its Section 4. Every admitted pullback in \(\mathcal U\), with any retained peripheral fixed flags, lies in the actual positive decorated gluing chart. Its centered similarity logarithms satisfy \[ V_i=U_i\tau_i(U),\qquad \Im\tau_i(U)\ge m>0. \tag{6} \] For unfilled cusps, boundary-parabolicity gives their centered \(U_i=V_i=0\). At a filled cusp the full projective matrix relation is \[ \widehat\rho(\alpha_i)=I. \tag{7} \] Taking its similarity multiplier on the retained fixed flag gives \[ a_iU_i+b_iV_i=2\pi i q_i,\qquad q_i\in\mathbb Z. \tag{8} \] Here \(U_i,V_i\) themselves remain centered; (8) is not obtained by choosing their deck translates. Suppose \(q_i=0\). The denominator estimate in F gives \[ |a_i+b_i\tau_i(U)|\ge c_0\ell_i>0. \tag{9} \] Equations (6), (8) imply \(U_i=V_i=0\). In the moving selected-flag affine frame, F supplies the actual commuting maps \[ \mu_i(w)=e^{U_i}w+B_i(U),\qquad \lambda_i(w)=e^{V_i}w+D_i(U),\qquad B_i(U)\ne0. \tag{10} \] Moreover, on \(U_i=0\), \[ D_i/B_i=\tau_i(U). \tag{11} \] For completeness, differentiate the exact commuting identity \((e^{U_i}-1)D_i=(e^{V_i}-1)B_i\) in the coordinate \(U_i\), holding all other coordinates fixed, and set \(U_i=0\). Since \(V_i=U_i\tau_i(U)\), this gives (11). The slope map when \(U_i=V_i=0\) is therefore the translation \[ w\longmapsto w+a_iB_i+b_iD_i =w+B_i(a_i+b_i\tau_i(U)). \tag{12} \] Its translation is nonzero by (9)--(10), so it is not the identity. This contradicts the full relation (7). We have proved \[ q_i\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\} \qquad(i\in I). \tag{13} \] If one starts with \(\mathrm{SL}_2\) data, projectivize while retaining its actual central signs. A slope matrix \(+I\) or \(-I\) both give (7); the nonidentity parabolic (12) gives neither. Thus the proof does not presume an odd-only or an even-only charge congruence. It also does not identify the integer \(q_i\) with a quantum Fourier label. The full group relation is what excludes zero. ## 4. The gap for all admitted filled-group representations Source G gives a fixed \(\delta>0\) such that every admitted core representation outside \(\mathcal U\) has volume at most \(\operatorname{Vol}(M)-\delta\). Its long-slope threshold can be chosen so that \[ \operatorname{Vol}(M(\sigma)) >\operatorname{Vol}(M)-\delta/2. \tag{14} \] By (5), a filled-group representation whose pullback is outside \(\mathcal U\) therefore has deficit greater than \(\delta/2\). For a pullback in \(\mathcal U\), (13) places all its centered charges in the nonzero integer set. G's neighborhood was chosen so that all these charges lie in its larger box \(|q_i|\le\rho_*\ell_i\). Its exact monotonicity estimate gives \[ \operatorname{Vol}(M(\sigma)) -\operatorname{Vol}_M(\widehat\rho) \ge c_1\sum_{i\in I}\frac{q_i^2-1}{\ell_i^2}, \qquad c_1=\frac{\pi^2m}{1+T^2}>0. \tag{15} \] If any \(|q_i|\ge2\), the right side is at least \(3c_1/\ell_{\max}^2\). If all \(|q_i|=1\), the independent flag-reversal and contraction argument in G identifies the underlying pullback representation with the unit-charge geometric one. Since \(\pi\) is surjective, a conjugacy of these pullbacks is also a conjugacy of the representations of \(\pi_1M(\sigma)\). Such a representation is the excluded \(\rho_{\mathrm{hyp},\sigma}\). Together with the outside-neighborhood case and (5), this proves (3). ## 5. Source scope The theorem removes a classical charge-matching premise for representations that already satisfy the actual filled-group relations. It does not prove that every source critical configuration satisfies those relations as matrices, or that its action has the required representation-volume normalization. A peripheral exponential equation alone still permits the nonidentity parabolic excluded in (12). Nor does the theorem compare distinct source lifts of geometric holonomy or determine their combined coefficient. Source boundary currents, escaping decorations, the original highest-cut relative cycle and its physical observation remain separate. No quantum lower bound or noncancellation statement is inferred. ## Frozen proof-source pins * G: research_centered_long_cone_representation_volume_gap.md, SHA256 5e68b3c689a8b85454ae256c3e298a412ddf9ff3ef52cfef5c836dace0da85d5. * F: finite_geometric_certificate_uniform_filling_existence.md, SHA256 f3f78212e1f42f501593412a71c21590f24f8838f4add8abeb2f12534ad2b39b.

title: The lowest physical block and the original cut pairing
text: # The lowest physical block and the original cut pairing Private written proof, 19 November 2026. Author-final for independent review. The operator dual to physical highest-block multiplication has a literal endpoint interpretation: it takes an intertwiner to its lowest diagonal block. This endpoint is another regular coordinate on the whole intertwiner space. The original cut pairing is therefore perfect in these coordinates, including at the complete meridian. The abstract perfect cut form is existing coverage in integral_projective_cut_duality.md. That result is not a premise below. The present proof identifies the finite duality operator and proves its invertibility directly, without projective-module or fusion arguments. Its sole complete direct is H, the physical highest-block reconstruction, pinned below. This is a bilinear statement. It supplies neither a positive inner product nor a lower bound for the closing of a specified knot word. ## 1. The two physical endpoints Use H's actual fixed-root family. Thus \[ N\ge2,\quad d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2, \quad M=e^\mu,\quad x=-M/q, \qquad f_a=\prod_{j=1}^a(1-Q^j). \tag{1} \] There are \(m=r+1\) heads. The remaining tensor is \(U\), with ordered total operators \(E,F,K\). The first head has \[ E_1w_a=e_aw_{a-1},\quad e_a=MQ^{-a}-M^{-1}\ (1\le a\le d), \qquad F_1w_a=(1-Q^{a+1})w_{a+1}, \quad K_1w_a=xQ^{-a}w_a, \tag{2} \] and the actual zero outward arrows. The total generators are \[ E_\Sigma=E_1K+E,\qquad F_\Sigma=F_1+K_1^{-1}F,\qquad K_\Sigma=K_1K. \tag{3} \] Put \[ \mathcal A=\{H\in\operatorname{End}(U):[K,H]=0\}, \qquad g=K^{1-N},\qquad \tau_0(H)=\operatorname{Tr}_U(gH). \tag{4} \] H proves that, whenever \(e_1\cdots e_d\ne0\), each \(H\in\mathcal A\) extends uniquely to an actual total intertwiner \(W_H\) with \((W_H)_{00}=H\). This includes \(M=1\) and every strict collar \(|\mu|<\eta/N\), \(\eta<\pi\). All spaces can alternatively be restricted to exact integer-degree preservation. The root-weight condition is not substituted for that restriction. Write \[ C_a(H)=(W_H)_{a0},\qquad U_a(H)=(W_H)_{0a}. \] The exact endpoint recurrences in H are \[ C_0(H)=H,\qquad C_{a+1}(H)=-e_{a+1}^{-1}K^{-1}[E,C_a(H)], \tag{5} \] \[ U_a(H)=\frac{x^{-a}}{f_a}\mathcal D_aH,\qquad \mathcal D_a=\prod_{j=0}^{a-1}(L_F-Q^jR_F). \tag{6} \] Here \(L_FT=FT\), \(R_FT=TF\); these two operators commute. Empty products are identities. The transported product is \[ H\star J=\sum_{a=0}^d U_a(H)C_a(J),\qquad W_{H\star J}=W_HW_J. \tag{7} \] The actual pointed source of \(W_H\) is \(\tau_0(H)\). Scalars included in a word remain in \(H\); a separately prescribed scalar line remains separately prescribed. ## 2. The explicit duality operator Define a finite linear operator on \(\mathcal A\) by \[ \mathscr L J= \sum_{a=0}^d\frac{x^{-a}}{f_a} \prod_{j=0}^{a-1}(Q^{-1}R_F-Q^jL_F)\,C_a(J). \tag{8} \] The factors act on the displayed \(C_a(J)\). Each summand has total root weight zero. The formula also preserves exact integer degree zero when that restriction is imposed. The weighted ordinary trace gives the exact identity \[ \boxed{\qquad \tau_0(H\star J)=\operatorname{Tr}_U(gH\mathscr L J). \qquad}\tag{9} \] Indeed \(gF=Q^{-1}Fg\). Moving one left or right multiplication under the ordinary finite trace shows \[ \operatorname{Tr}(g(FH)T) =\operatorname{Tr}(gH(Q^{-1}TF)),\qquad \operatorname{Tr}(g(HF)T)=\operatorname{Tr}(gH(FT)). \tag{10} \] Thus the bilinear adjoint of \(L_F-Q^jR_F\) is \(Q^{-1}R_F-Q^jL_F\). Their factors commute, so applying (10) to every factor of (6), and then (7), proves (9). No complex conjugation has been taken. ## 3. The duality operator is the lowest block In fact \[ \boxed{\qquad \mathscr L J=(W_J)_{dd}.\qquad}\tag{11} \] We verify this with the actual finite prefix operator, so all caps and root phases are visible. Put \[ c_j=(-1)^jQ^{j(j-1)/2},\qquad S=\sum_{j=0}^d\frac{x^{-j}L_1^jF^j}{f_j},\qquad S^{-1}=\sum_{j=0}^d\frac{c_jx^{-j}L_1^jF^j}{f_j}. \tag{12} \] H gives \(F_\Sigma=SF_1S^{-1}\), \(p_dS=p_d\), and \[ W_J=T_JS^{-1},\qquad T_Ji_b=f_b^{-1}F_\Sigma^b\sum_{a=0}^di_aC_a(J). \tag{13} \] For \(a\ge j\), expansion of \(p_dF_\Sigma^{d-j}i_a=p_dF_1^{d-j}S^{-1}i_a\) has precisely one surviving term, namely \[ p_dF_\Sigma^{d-j}i_a =\frac{c_{a-j}x^{-(a-j)}}{f_{a-j}} \frac{f_d}{f_j}F^{a-j}. \tag{14} \] For \(a<j\) it is zero. Substituting (12)--(14) in \(p_dW_Ji_d\) therefore gives \[ (W_J)_{dd}= \sum_{a=0}^d x^{-a}\sum_{j=0}^a \frac{c_jc_{a-j}f_d}{f_j^2f_{d-j}f_{a-j}} F^{a-j}C_a(J)F^j. \tag{15} \] The elementary root product identities are \[ f_d=N,\qquad f_{d-j}=\frac{f_d(-1)^jQ^{j(j+1)/2}}{f_j}. \tag{16} \] The first follows from \((t^N-1)/(t-1)\) at \(t=1\). For the second, separate the last \(j\) factors and use \(1-Q^{-k}=-Q^{-k}(1-Q^k)\). In particular \(c_jf_d/f_{d-j}=Q^{-j}f_j\). Thus (15) becomes \[ \sum_{a=0}^d x^{-a}\sum_{j=0}^a \frac{Q^{-j}c_{a-j}}{f_jf_{a-j}} F^{a-j}C_a(J)F^j. \tag{17} \] The ordinary commuting-variable quantum binomial expansion of \(\prod_{k=0}^{a-1}(Q^{-1}R_F-Q^kL_F)/f_a\) has exactly the coefficients in the inner sum of (17). This proves (11) for the whole fixed-root meridian family. ## 4. Invertibility from the opposite endpoint The lowest-block map is injective on the total intertwiner space. To see this, let \(W_{dd}=0\). The physical raising equation gives \[ (1-Q^a)W_{a-1,d} =x^{-1}\bigl(Q^dW_{ad}F-Q^aFW_{ad}\bigr), \qquad a=d,d-1,\ldots,1. \tag{18} \] All displayed denominators are nonzero, so the entire last column vanishes. The maps \[ E_\Sigma^bi_d:U\longrightarrow V_1\otimes U, \qquad 0\le b\le d, \tag{19} \] jointly form an invertible triangular coordinate system: their lowest first-head row is \(d-b\), with coefficient \((e_d\cdots e_{d-b+1})K^b\), an invertible operator. Commutation with \(E_\Sigma\) and the vanishing last column now give \(WE_\Sigma^bi_d=0\) for every \(b\); hence \(W=0\). The highest-block map already identifies the whole intertwiner space with \(\mathcal A\). The lowest-block map has the same target and is injective, so it is an isomorphism. Its matrices depend holomorphically on \(M\). Since its determinant is nonzero wherever \(e_1\cdots e_d\ne0\), its inverse is holomorphic on that same domain. The degree-zero argument is identical using H's exact integer-degree restriction. Together with (11), this proves that \(\mathscr L\) is an actual holomorphic linear automorphism at \(M=1\), not just an invertible principal symbol. Both directions have controlled finite-cap conditioning. Here is an explicit inverse construction, also proving the bound. Given \(J=W_{dd}\), solve (18) downward with \(D_d=J\), and set \(V_J=\sum i_aD_a\), \(F_{\rm top}=x^{-1}Q^dF\). The only possible residual of the raising equation is \(F_\Sigma V_J-V_JF_{\rm top}=i_0R\). Telescope its \(N\)-th powers, which vanish by H, and apply \(p_d\). Only the term with \(d\) first-head raisings survives, giving \(f_dR=0\). Thus the terminal row holds as well. Put \[ h_b=e_d e_{d-1}\cdots e_{d-b+1},\quad h_0=1, \qquad A=EK^{-1}, \qquad S_Ei_{d-b}=h_b^{-1}E_\Sigma^bi_dK^{-b}. \tag{19a} \] In reversed first-head indices its only nonzero blocks are \[ (S_E)_{b-j,b}=\frac{h_{b-j}}{h_b}{b\brack j}_Q Q^{j(j-1)/2}A^j,\qquad 0\le j\le b. \tag{19b} \] Indeed the summands \(E_1K\) and \(E\) of \(E_\Sigma\) \(Q\)-commute. Expand their \(b\)-th power with the tail \(E\)'s to the left and use \(E^jK^{-j}=Q^{j(j-1)/2}A^j\). The exact inverse is \[ (S_E^{-1})_{b-j,b}=\frac{h_{b-j}}{h_b}(-1)^j {b\brack j}_QA^j. \tag{19c} \] Multiplying the two finite triangular matrices reduces a block at distance \(n>0\) to a nonzero common factor times \(\sum_{j=0}^n(-1)^jQ^{j(j-1)/2}{n\brack j}_Q=(1;Q)_n=0\). At distance zero the product is the identity. No denominator \(1-Q^N\) occurs. Each \(D_a\) has weight \(KD_a=Q^{a-d}D_aK\), by (18). Define \[ T_Ei_{d-b}=h_b^{-1}E_\Sigma^bV_JK^{-b},\qquad W=T_ES_E^{-1}. \tag{19d} \] This agrees with extension along the basis (19): it commutes with \(E_\Sigma\), including its top row by \(E_\Sigma^N=0\), and with \(K_\Sigma\). The already verified column equation makes \([F_\Sigma,W]i_d=0\). Jacobi and Cartan commutation make that commutator commute with \(E_\Sigma\); (19) therefore makes it zero everywhere. Thus (19d) is the inverse endpoint reconstruction. Fix \(|\mu|\le\eta/N\), \(\eta<\pi\), at fixed width. H's prefix-product bounds also bound every reversed product \(h_b\) and its reciprocal by \(e^{CN}\): each is a ratio of two complete or prefix products. Downward recursion (18) costs at most a fixed constant per step divided by a reversed prefix of \(f_d\), hence \(\|V_J\|\le e^{CN}\|J\|\). In (19b)--(19c) use \(|{b\brack j}_Q|\le\binom bj\), bounded \(\|A\|\), and those product bounds. They give \(\|S_E^{\pm1}\|\le e^{CN}\). Equation (19d) then gives \(\|W\|\le e^{CN}\|J\|\). Together with H's forward bound this proves \[ \|\mathscr L\|+\|\mathscr L^{-1}\| \le e^{CN}. \tag{19e} \] Constants can be enlarged to absorb all polynomial factors in \(N\). True fixed-root meridian derivatives of either map cost at most \(C_jN^je^{CN}\) on smaller scaled collars, by Cauchy's formula. These are exponential bounds, not zero-exponential-rate estimates or positivity statements. ## 5. The original cut is a perfect bilinear pairing The ordinary form \[ (H,T)\longmapsto\operatorname{Tr}(gHT) \tag{20} \] is perfect on \(\mathcal A\). Indeed the actual Cartan is diagonal, so its commutant is a direct sum of full matrix algebras on its weight spaces. On each, \(g\) is a nonzero scalar. The ordinary matrix trace pairing on each block is perfect. The same reasoning works for the finer blocks of exact total occupation degree. Equations (9) and (11), and invertibility of the lowest-block map, therefore prove that \[ B(H,J)=\tau_0(H\star J) \tag{21} \] is perfect. It remains perfect over the holomorphic meridian germ and after specialization to \(M=1\). It is associative in the Frobenius sense, since associativity of \(\star\) gives \(B(H\star J,T)=B(H,J\star T)\). No separate symmetry theorem is needed for these conclusions. The conclusion is concrete: cut duality is realized by the opposite physical endpoint, with the original pivot and every finite coefficient retained. Nondegeneracy says a nonzero element has some nonzero pairing. It does not say that its prescribed pairing with the identity is nonzero. In particular it supplies no positive norm, no subexponential conditioning statement, and no surviving geometric contour coefficient for an actual knot word. ## Complete proof-source pin * H: notes/research_physical_highest_block_endpoint_coordinates.md, 453 lines, SHA256 deaadaa899cdb08aefbbcb1e1ca87a40f84a1ade608fceeeaba6426027bd9b1b. The matching final was read back in full, every used implication checked, and both pins renewed before freezing. Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used. title: Main-color preserving metrics in a bounded regularized source problem
text: # Main-color preserving metrics in a bounded regularized source problem 24 November 2026. Research note. Written proof. Main-color preserving gauges already suffice at the leading exponential scale for the actual all-main-color source. The earlier proof establishes an infimum over those gauges. Here that infimum is approximated inside an explicit finite metric window, including when individual color values vanish. The restricted regularized minimizer consequently has logarithmic metric radius \(O(N)\) and the same leading rate as the unrestricted problem. The proof retains the original closing in every color. This removes color mixing from that bounded variational formulation at the leading scale. It does not identify the remaining within-color metrics with geometric data or prove a volume lower bound. ## 1. The actual sectors and a known input bound Use the actual all-main-color compiler of [C, Section 5]. Fix a completed braid word whose prescribed marked closure is one knot, with its original zero-framing factors and partial pivotal trace. Let \(b\) be its fixed braid width; each proper edge in color \(j\) is the full operator space \(\operatorname{End}(V_{j,N}^{\otimes b})\). Compile multiplication of its signed crossing operators as a tree with \(m\ge2\) vertices, including the root readout. Select any set \(\mathcal J\subset\{1,\ldots,N\}\) containing \(1\), with \(2\le r:=|\mathcal J|\le N\). Keep those original color blocks and their original readouts. An internal edge is an orthogonal direct sum of these \(r\) physical color spaces. Every local tensor has blocks \(T_{v,j}\), \(j\in\mathcal J\), and a contraction pairs only equal color labels. The root output is exactly \[ Y_{\mathcal J,N}=(c_j)_{j\in\mathcal J},\qquad c_1=1, \qquad \|Y_{\mathcal J,N}\|\ge1,\qquad c_N=K_N. \tag{1} \] The last identity refers to the original complete-color readout, whether or not \(N\) was selected. Every selected physical space is retained in full, including its reducible structure. No nonvanishing of \(c_j\) for \(j>1\), or of \(K_N\), is assumed. Orient edges toward the root. Write \(a_{e,j}\) for the actual open subtree message in sector \(j\), before its parent is contracted. These proper messages are products of invertible signed physical crossings. They do not include the final closing. Fix a known \(B=B_N\ge2\) which bounds \[ \|T_{v,j}\|_{\rm HS},\quad \|T_{v,j}\|_{\rm HS}^{-1}, \quad \|a_{e,j}\|,\quad \|a_{e,j}\|^{-1} \quad\hbox{for every }v,e,j. \tag{2} \] Vector norms on the edge spaces are their physical Hilbert--Schmidt norms. Norms of maps between those spaces below are induced operator norms. Local tensor norms are coefficient Hilbert--Schmidt norms. For every fixed actual word, such a \(B_N\) satisfies \[ \log B_N=O(N),\qquad \log D_N=O(\log N),\qquad D_N:=\sum_e\dim H_e. \tag{3} \] Here \(D_N\) includes all selected colors. To verify the first assertion, [M, (10)--(12)] bounds both signed crossings and their inverses uniformly over the entire main-color orbit. The inverse of a fixed proper word is the reversed word of inverse crossings. Thus its operator norm and inverse operator norm are \(\exp(O(N))\); tensoring spectator identities adds polynomial factors. Its Hilbert--Schmidt norm has the same upper bound and is at least the reciprocal of its inverse operator norm. In every selected sector the multiplication and original readout blocks have nonzero unit-modulus coefficients and polynomial norms. Their reciprocal norms are therefore bounded too, even if that readout evaluates to \(c_j=0\). These observations prove (2)--(3) without any division by a closed color value. Fixed signed powers or fixed short word blocks may be contracted first. All constants can depend on that fixed presentation. The gauges below use the complete open messages, not their principal symbols. ## 2. A finite sector-preserving competitor For positive metrics \(H=(H_e)\), let \[ L_N(H)=\sum_v\log\|T_v\|_H,\qquad Z(H)=1+\sum_e\operatorname{tr}(H_e+H_e^{-1}). \tag{4} \] The pairing is bilinear: a gauge \(g_e\) acts on the child output and \(g_e^{-\mathsf T}\) on its parent input. In this section every gauge preserves the color sectors. Put \[ C_{\rm block} =\left(\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}|c_j|^{2/m}\right)^{m/2}. \tag{5} \] By [M, Section 5], this is the exact restricted product-norm infimum. In particular every sector-preserving metric satisfies \(L_N(H)\ge\log C_{\rm block}\). We prove a finite approximation with a quantitative metric bound. **Theorem.** For \(0<\eta\le1\), define \[ \begin{split} \delta&=\left(\frac{2\eta}{m(r+1)}\right)^{m/2},& t&=B^{m+1}/\delta,\\ \mathcal L&=\log B+(m-1)\log t\\ &=m^2\log B+ \frac{m(m-1)}2\log\frac{m(r+1)}{2\eta},\\ A_{\rm block}(B,D_N,\eta) &=\log(1+2D_N)+2(1+2m^2)\mathcal L . \end{split} \tag{6} \] There are finite positive block-diagonal metrics with \[ 0\le L_N(H)-\log C_{\rm block}\le\eta,\qquad \log Z(H)\le A_{\rm block}(B,D_N,\eta). \tag{7} \] Choose, independently on each edge and sector, a gauge sending \(a_{e,j}\) to a fixed first unit vector \(e_0\), with its norm and inverse norm at most \(B\). Rotate the unit direction first, then scale its first coordinate by \(\|a_{e,j}\|^{-1}\). All these gauges can be applied simultaneously: they cancel inside every contracted subtree. At a proper vertex the slice with all child indices zero is exactly \(e_0\) on its parent edge. At the root that slice is \(c_j\). In particular a proper output-excited entry with every child index zero vanishes exactly. Before further filtering, each sector tensor has norm at most \(B^{m+1}\). At an edge whose child has depth \(h\), with root depth zero, apply the additional child-side gauge \[ \operatorname{diag}(1,t^h,\ldots,t^h). \tag{8} \] An excited output at a proper vertex of depth \(h\), with \(k\ge1\) excited child indices, receives exponent \(h-k(h+1)\le-1\). An unexcited output with any excited child is also suppressed by at least \(t^{-1}\). The only remaining case, an excited output with no excited child, was zero already. The corresponding statement at the root is immediate. Thus the norm of the entire nonselected slice is at most \(\delta\). It is orthogonal in coefficient space to the unchanged selected slice. Let \(a_{v,j}>0\) now denote these finite gauged local sector norms, and set \(p_j=\prod_v a_{v,j}\). These are local tensor norms, distinct from the open messages \(a_{e,j}\). Orthogonality gives \[ a_{v,j}\le\sqrt{1+\delta^2}\quad(v\ne{\rm root}),\qquad a_{{\rm root},j}\le\sqrt{|c_j|^2+\delta^2}, \quad |c_j|\le p_j\le (1+\delta^2)^{(m-1)/2}\sqrt{|c_j|^2+\delta^2}. \tag{9} \] The lower product inequality is tree Cauchy in that sector. Every \(a_{v,j}\) is positive, even when \(c_j=0\), since its original block was nonzero and every applied gauge is invertible. The accumulated edge gauge and its inverse have norm at most \(e^{\mathcal L}\). Applying the inverse gauges to a local tensor and using (2) consequently also gives \[ |\log a_{v,j}|\le m\mathcal L. \tag{10} \] This lower bound is the step that makes finite scalar balancing uniform at the zero-output sectors. ## 3. Scalar balancing and the metric radius Within sector \(j\), prescribe the logarithmic vertex rescalings \[ \lambda_{v,j} =\frac1m\log p_j-\log a_{v,j}. \tag{11} \] Their sum is zero and \(|\lambda_{v,j}|\le2m\mathcal L\). For an edge, assign the scalar gauge whose logarithm is the sum of \(\lambda_{v,j}\) over the subtree below it. The incidence identity on a rooted tree makes the resulting logarithmic change at each vertex exactly \(\lambda_{v,j}\), including at the root. Each edge scalar and its inverse are bounded by \(\exp(2m^2\mathcal L)\). No scalar is defined from \(c_j^{-1}\). After balancing, every local norm in sector \(j\) equals \(p_j^{1/m}\). Hence the whole product is exactly \[ F_{\rm bal} =\left(\sum_jp_j^{2/m}\right)^{m/2}. \tag{12} \] Let \(S=\sum_j|c_j|^{2/m}\ge1\), using \(c_1=1\). Concavity and (9) give \[ \begin{split} \log F_{\rm bal}-\log C_{\rm block} &\le\frac{m-1}{2}\log(1+\delta^2) +\frac m2\log\left(1+\frac{r\delta^{2/m}}S\right)\\ &\le\frac{m(r+1)}2\delta^{2/m}=\eta . \end{split} \tag{13} \] Here \((x+\delta^2)^{1/m}\le x^{1/m}+\delta^{2/m}\), \(0<\delta\le1\), and \(\delta^2\le\delta^{2/m}\). This estimate includes every zero \(c_j\). The final full edge gauge and its inverse have norms at most \(\exp[(1+2m^2)\mathcal L]\). Its polar metric \(H_e=g_e^*g_e\) remains block diagonal. Removing the edge unitary factors preserves all local norms and the original source. Therefore \[ Z(H)\le(1+2D_N)\exp[2(1+2m^2)\mathcal L]. \tag{14} \] Equations (12)--(14) prove (7). ## 4. The restricted regularized minimum Keep exactly the regularizer of [R], and define \[ J_{N,\varepsilon}(H)=L_N(H)+\varepsilon\log Z(H), \qquad 0<\varepsilon\le1. \tag{15} \] Restrict all edge matrices to the positive block-diagonal cone. This cone is geodesically stable. The strict geodesic convexity and coercivity proof of [R] applies on it: \(L_N\ge\log C_{\rm block}\), and a bound on \(Z\) bounds every metric eigenvalue and reciprocal. Thus the restricted objective has a unique minimizer \(H^{\rm block}_{N,\varepsilon}\). Use the finite competitor (7) with \(\eta=\varepsilon\). The lower bound \(L_N\ge\log C_{\rm block}\) then proves \[ \boxed{\begin{split} \log Z(H^{\rm block}_{N,\varepsilon}) &\le1+A_{\rm block}(B,D_N,\varepsilon),\\ 0\le \min_{\rm block}J_{N,\varepsilon} -\log C_{\rm block} &\le\varepsilon[1+A_{\rm block}(B,D_N,\varepsilon)] . \end{split}} \tag{16} \] Each optimizing eigenvalue and its reciprocal are bounded by this \(Z\). For \(\varepsilon_N=N^{-2}\), (3) and (6) give \[ \sup_e\|\log H^{\rm block}_{e,N}\|_{\rm op}=O(N),\qquad \min_{\rm block}J_{N,\varepsilon_N} =\log C_{\rm block}+O(N^{-1}). \tag{17} \] Constants depend on the fixed actual tree and word, not on which individual color values happen to vanish. For the unrestricted positive cone, use the same objective (15). Since it contains the block cone, [C,M] give \[ \boxed{\quad 0\le\min_{\rm block}J_{N,\varepsilon_N} -\min_{\rm full}J_{N,\varepsilon_N} \le\frac{m-1}{2}\log r+O(N^{-1}) . \quad} \tag{18} \] Here the full cone is on the same selected-color compiler. Its minimum is at least \(\log\|Y_{\mathcal J,N}\|\), while \(\|Y_{\mathcal J,N}\|\le C_{\rm block} \le r^{(m-1)/2}\|Y_{\mathcal J,N}\|\) by [M, (17)]. Thus color mixing changes neither the leading variational rate nor the leading logarithmic output norm: \[ \frac{2\pi}{N}\min_{\rm block}J_{N,\varepsilon_N} -\frac{2\pi}{N}\log\|Y_{\mathcal J,N}\| \longrightarrow0. \tag{19} \] ## 5. Two actual colors suffice for a positive target rate In particular take the two original main colors \(\mathcal J=\{1,N\}\). Their selected output is exactly \[ Y_{\{1,N\},N}=(1,K_N),\qquad C_2=(1+|K_N|^{2/m})^{m/2},\qquad \sqrt{1+|K_N|^2}\le C_2 \le2^{(m-1)/2}\sqrt{1+|K_N|^2}. \tag{20} \] Equations (16)--(17) become \[ \min_{\rm block}J_{N,N^{-2}}=\log C_2+O(N^{-1}),\qquad \sup_e\|\log H^{\rm block}_{e,N}\|_{\rm op}=O(N). \tag{21} \] For every \(V>0\) this gives the exact target equivalence \[ \lim_N\frac{2\pi}{N}\min_{\rm block}J_{N,N^{-2}}=V \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \lim_N\frac{2\pi}{N}\log|K_N|=V . \tag{22} \] Indeed \(\log C_2\) differs from \(\max(0,\log|K_N|)\) by at most \((m/2)\log2\). A strictly positive limiting rate removes that maximum and implies eventual nonvanishing. This argument needs no estimate for the other ordinary-color remainder. Each internal edge here is two copies of the raw physical operator space \(\operatorname{End}(V_{j,N}^{\otimes b})\), of total dimension \(2N^{2b}\). These are two actual main-color sectors, with the original crossings and root readouts. They are not a newly appended constant coordinate. The orthogonally anchored Conway construction [A] already has output \((1,K_N)\) in a different, smaller boundary presentation. No new anchoring principle or improvement of its dimension is claimed. The new assertion is finite controlled-window near-attainment of the exact sector infimum and its regularized consequence. There is also a direct comparison with [A]'s fixed-degree quartic minimum \(Q_N\) for the same original Conway source. That theorem gives \(1+|K_N|^2\le Q_N\le(1+1/N)(1+|K_N|^2)\). With \(j_{2,N}=\min_{\rm block}J_{N,N^{-2}}\), equations (20)--(21) imply \[ -\tfrac12\log(1+1/N) \le j_{2,N}-\tfrac12\log Q_N \le\tfrac{m-1}{2}\log2+O(N^{-1}). \tag{23} \] This is a bounded additive difference of logarithmic values. It identifies neither minimizers nor pointwise objectives. For all \(N\) colors the output remains the one in [C], \(\|Y_{\{1,\ldots,N\},N}\|^2=|K_N|^2+R_N\), with its original polynomial ordinary-color remainder. No original source value changes when that larger selected set is used instead. ## 6. Scope of the reduction The new conclusion is a finite-window realization and regularized version of the sector infimum already proved in [M, Section 5]. The normalizing directions are exact open source packets, and the balancing scalars use actual finite local tensor norms. This is not a construction of those directions from a classical angle structure. The original cap stays at the root, and a zero complete-color value is permitted throughout. The restricted minimizer is not asserted to equal the full minimizer. Pinching an arbitrary gauge is not asserted to improve the objective. Restricted stationarity controls only the permitted block variations; it does not imply the full marginal balance of [C,R]. No within-color dimension reduction, principal-symbol limit, interchange of an infimum and a limit, or geometric noncancellation follows. All statements concern the raw multiplication tree of a fixed completed one-component knot. Proper packets are invertible word operators; arbitrary Conway packets or components containing internal partial traces need not have this property. Constants may depend on the fixed word, filling assignment and braid width. No uniformity in unbounded word length, or anchor for an unfilled auxiliary link, is asserted. There is no new volume identity or finite-exception theorem. ## Complete inputs and closest coverage | Label | Complete text | Lines | SHA-256 | | --- | --- | ---: | --- | | M | [Metric compactness and sector infima](research_regularized_source_metric_compactness.md) | 337 | fd8dae7561eff37089e8481b4eb8c8344acb56da86b502350292f6d2be9c8818 | | R | [Regularized actual-source problem](research_regularized_actual_source_capacity.md) | 377 | 0cea0d52182eb24b4610538f354dbe5158fa54aa6f9cf7f9fc280c72ab090ff8 | | C | [Actual all-main-color tree capacity](research_scalar_tree_full_gauge_capacity.md) | 466 | 2997b732aa73e063c66e81d6487a1d9927509609d61842c1dbb43d9345df1d6d | | A | [Earlier anchored Conway source](research_anchored_conway_positive_variational_period.md) | 392 | e83c35d16c79faa13ac6556db78b9b57da2a2371d3fc04c4673ecd74e1d336f7 | Only written mathematics, text reads and metadata operations were used. title: The main-color Fourier energy retains a coherent cap projection
text: # The main-color Fourier energy retains a coherent cap projection 20 November 2026. Research note; public manuscripts remain frozen. The main-color Plancherel norm has an exact realization by positive projectors on the original physical braid. Its cap projector is still coherent: the input and output indices of each traced head are paired in a maximally entangled vector. This note gives the actual identity, characterizes its allowed lower-bound test vectors, and computes what happens when a local output window is inserted. It proves no geometric lower bound or additional volume-conjecture case. ## 1. The original main-color orbit Fix a zero-framed knot presented as the closure of a braid on \(b\) strands. Its closure has one component. At level \(N\ge2\), put \[ q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\quad \alpha_j=j-1,\quad x_j=q^{j-1},\quad M_j=-q^j, \qquad 1\le j\le N. \] At every \(j\), use the original \(N\)-dimensional unrolled color \(V_{\alpha_j}\), including its reducible specializations. On its fixed basis \(e_a\), \(0\le a<N\), \[ K_je_a=x_jQ^{-a}e_a. \] Let \(W_j\) be the original checked braid operator on \(V_{\alpha_j}^{\otimes b}\), including all common Cartan factors and its scalar zero-framing correction. Cut the first strand. The original reduced source is the \((0,0)\) entry of its partial pivotal trace: \[ c_j=\left[\operatorname{Tr}_{\rm env} \{W_j(I\otimes g_j)\}\right]_{00},\qquad g_j=(K_j^{1-N})^{\otimes(b-1)}. \tag{1} \] This is the reduced tangle scalar with unknot value one, as specified in [the ADO source note](kashaev_ado_pointing.md), Section 1. It does not include the modified-dimension factor, whose ordinary-color specializations can have poles. The selected cut entry retains the reduced marked normalization; the pivotal trace closes only the other strands. In particular \[ c_N=K_N,\qquad c_j=C_j(q)\quad(1\le j<N). \tag{2} \] Here (2) is an actual source comparison, not a renaming of labels. For \(j<N\), the span of \(e_j,\ldots,e_{N-1}\) is invariant under \(E,F,K,H\). Both finite signed crossings and the pivot preserve it on each strand. Its quotient is the ordinary \(j\)-dimensional highest-weight color. In a partial trace of a one-component braid, a path contributing to the quotient cut cannot enter that invariant subspace and later leave it. Every contributing strand path therefore stays in the quotient. The pivotal and framing convention difference is \((-1)^{(j-1)(b-1-w)}=1\), since the writhe \(w\) of a braid with cyclic closure permutation satisfies \(w\equiv b-1\pmod2\). This proves the ordinary-color assertion in (2); the complete-color assertion is the retained original Kashaev normalization. The [ordinary-color Plancherel proof](ordinary_color_plancherel_bound_audit.md) also proves \[ E_N:=\sum_{j=1}^N|c_j|^2=|K_N|^2+R_N,\qquad 0\le R_N\le (N-1)(N/2)^{2b-2}. \tag{3} \] Briefly, in its positive path realization the ordinary color projector is orthogonal and has trace \([j]=\sin(\pi j/N)/\sin(\pi/N)\); the cabled braid is unitary. The unreduced colored trace is therefore bounded by \([j]^b\). Dividing by its nonzero dimension \([j]\) gives \(|C_j|\le[j]^{b-1}\le(N/2)^{b-1}\). The argument applies to the whole range \(j<N\). At \(j=N\), the dimension is zero and that positive quotient erases the complete sector; we do not use it there. ## 2. A common physical cap projector Write the traced environment as \(\mathbb C^D\), where \(D=N^{b-1}\), with multi-indices \(I=(i_2,\ldots,i_b)\). Its pivot has the exact form \[ (g_j)_I=\gamma_j(g_*)_I,\qquad \gamma_j=x_j^{(1-N)(b-1)},\qquad (g_*)_I=Q^{-\sum_{s=2}^b i_s}. \tag{4} \] Indeed \(Q^{(N-1)a}=Q^{-a}\). Both \(\gamma_j\) and every entry of \(g_*\) have modulus one. Move only the recorded scalar phase into \(\widetilde W_j=\gamma_jW_j\); no source factor is dropped. For an operator \(A\), fix the vectorization convention \[ \operatorname{vec}A =\sum_{a,a',I,J}A_{(a,I),(a',J)} e_a\otimes e_{a'}\otimes e_I\otimes e_J. \tag{5} \] The two first factors are the open output and input; the final factors are the environment output and input. All carry their usual positive coordinate inner products, so \(\|\operatorname{vec}A\|=\|A\|_{\rm HS}\), the Hilbert--Schmidt norm. Define unit vectors \[ h=\frac1{\sqrt D}\sum_I\overline{(g_*)_I}\,e_I\otimes e_I, \qquad r=e_0\otimes e_0\otimes h. \tag{6} \] The vector \(h\) is a product of the specified pivotal cap-pair vectors over the \(b-1\) traced heads. Its Schmidt rank across the whole environment output/input split is \(D\). Add one main-color register \(\mathbb C^N\), with basis \(|j\rangle\), and set \[ \mathsf w=\sum_{j=1}^N|j\rangle\otimes \operatorname{vec}\widetilde W_j, \qquad \Pi=I_{\rm color}\otimes|r\rangle\langle r|. \tag{7} \] This is a direct sum of different actual main-color braid operators, not a braid with independently chosen colors on its different strands. **Proposition 1.** The rank-\(N\) positive orthogonal projector in (7) satisfies \[ \sqrt D\,\Pi\mathsf w =\sum_{j=1}^Nc_j|j\rangle\otimes r, \qquad E_N=D\|\Pi\mathsf w\|^2. \tag{8} \] **Proof.** Equations (1), (4)--(6) give \[ \langle r,\operatorname{vec}\widetilde W_j\rangle =D^{-1/2}\sum_I(g_*)_I(\widetilde W_j)_{(0,I),(0,I)} =D^{-1/2}c_j. \] Project onto \(r\) in each orthogonal color block and sum their squared norms. This proves both identities. \(\square\) The unitary Fourier matrix \(\mathcal F_{kj}=N^{-1/2}Q^{-kj}\), \(0\le k<N\), acts only on the main-color register and commutes with \(\Pi\). Applying it to (8) gives exactly the main-color Plancherel norm. It does not remove the cap projector. Opening it instead gives the upper bound \(E_N\le D\sum_j\|W_j\|_{\rm HS}^2\). The single-color vectorized closure identity underlying (8) is already proved in [the weighted plat-energy note](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_weighted_fourier_plat_energy.md), Section 4; (4) supplies the common projector for the whole actual orbit. ## 3. Which lower-bound tests preserve this source? Every vector in \(\operatorname{ran}\Pi\) is uniquely \(\psi=\sum_j a_j|j\rangle\otimes r\). Cauchy gives \[ E_N\ge\frac{|\sum_j\overline a_jc_j|^2}{\sum_j|a_j|^2} \quad(a\ne0). \tag{9} \] For an arbitrary trial vector \(v\), the valid test is \(\Pi v\): \[ E_N\ge D\frac{|\langle\Pi v,\mathsf w\rangle|^2} {\|\Pi v\|^2} \quad(\Pi v\ne0). \tag{10} \] Replacing \(\Pi v\) by \(v\) in the numerator has no justification. Moreover, when \(\sum_j|a_j|^2=1\), (3) gives the exact separation \[ \left|\sum_j\overline a_jc_j-\overline a_NK_N\right| \le\sqrt{1-|a_N|^2}\,\sqrt{R_N}. \tag{11} \] Thus a test avoiding the complete main color has only polynomial size. A successful exponential lower bound from (9) is possible, but it must retain and estimate the original complete-color contribution. ## 4. Exact effect of localizing an environment output Let \(A\) be any operator on the environment output factor alone; extend it by identities on the other factors and call the extension \(\widehat A\). Maximal entanglement in (6) gives \[ \boxed{\qquad \Pi\widehat A\Pi=\frac{\operatorname{Tr}A}{D}\Pi. \qquad} \tag{12} \] To verify this, expand \(\langle h,(A\otimes I)h\rangle\). The input inner product sets the two indices equal, the pivot phases cancel, and the result is \(D^{-1}\sum_IA_{II}\). The remaining factors in (7) are unchanged. In particular a rank-\(s\) orthogonal output-window projector gives exactly \((s/D)\Pi\). Sandwiching such a window between the actual source projectors therefore rescales the same unknown source norm; it does not extract an independently localized contribution. There is a second useful support restriction. If \(0\le Q_0\le\Pi\), then \(\operatorname{ran}Q_0\subseteq\operatorname{ran}\Pi\). For \(z\in\ker\Pi\), positivity gives \(0\le\langle z,Q_0z\rangle\le0\), hence \(Q_0^{1/2}z=0\); taking orthogonal complements proves the claim. When \(D>1\), this range contains no nonzero vector whose environment output/input part is a single product vector: every nonzero color block has the full-Schmidt-rank environment vector \(h\). Consequently an independently product-localized positive projector cannot be placed below \(\Pi\) in operator order. These statements hold for all input tensors. They do not prove that a source-compatible entangled geometric test is impossible, or that such a test has small overlap with the actual \(\mathsf w\). They specify what must be constructed before positivity can give the desired lower bound without changing the original source. Finally, this is the orbit of the knot's main meridian: it changes every main-strand crossing representation and its pivot. Auxiliary crossing-circle colors instead change selected inserted circle coupons while the main representation stays fixed. Their Fourier or Hermite norms cannot be substituted for (8). Likewise a complete-main-color Conway Gram does not become an all-main-meridian compiler from (8). All ordinary and complete physical blocks in (7) must remain as stated. ## Complete direct-source pins All three direct texts were read completely. No mathematical program, test, build, or public-document edit was used. * [Original main-color source](kashaev_ado_pointing.md): `005ad157ebbf068b71eb80e2ceddc1aa9fccc460a54266756306e5cb54cf4c78`. * [Ordinary-color comparison and Plancherel remainder](ordinary_color_plancherel_bound_audit.md): `1c8b95921af8da7063d92af35cfcc15756b276fb9c85639fb2ffc3def1f922f0`. * [Original vectorized pivotal closure](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_weighted_fourier_plat_energy.md): `69757cb8ab3b857b690d9da8d3d7a46e4a42df4f0ab47a6bb85816aa9efc38b2`.

title: The literal closing cap with a prescribed observation
text:
# The literal closing cap with a prescribed observation Private written proof, 17 November 2026. The unmarked closing cap agrees with the original fixed cut on the scalar open knot operator. After a nonintertwining insertion the open operator need not be scalar. We give a marked cap which retains any specified linear observation of that operator. Its boundary entries and norm are explicit. No scalarity or cancellation is used for the inserted operator. ## 1. The already evaluated open source and cap Fix odd \(N>2\), \(q=e^{2\pi i/N}\), and the constructed braid source of [Q]. Write its two free physical indices as \(i,j\). Its boundary expansion, with both end-edge phases omitted from the physical array, has the form \[ B_G=K_{m open}\sum_{i,j=0}^{N-1} G(i,j)\mathcal A_a(i)\mathcal A_b(j), \qquad K_{m open}=N^{2c-1}\prod_{v=1}^c C_vq^{\phi_v}. 	ag{1} \] For the uninserted source \(G=O_\chi\). Formula (1) also defines its replacement by an arbitrary physical array \(G\); the resulting paired boundary tensor is unambiguous because the adapters have their specified inverses. Any actual insertion whose boundary array has been computed can be used for \(G\). This does not assert that two different insertion conventions give the same array. The actual two-tetrahedron cap of [Q, Section 5], with its neutral phase choice, has physical row \[ \ell_{m cap}(i,j)=N^{-2}q^i. 	ag{2} \] It includes its four newly interior vertices and all its edge weights. Consequently its unmarked closing is, for arbitrary \(G\), \[ Z_{m cap}(G)=N^{-2}K_{m open}\sum_{i,j}q^iG(i,j). 	ag{3} \] The passage from (3) to a fixed-zero observation in [Q] uses the particular identity \(O_\chi(i,j)=q^{-i}\delta_{ij}O_\chi(0,0)\). We do not apply that identity to a modified array \(G\). Put \[ \Delta_N=NK_{m open} =\prod_{v=1}^c N^2C_vq^{\phi_v}. 	ag{4} \] On the injective real decoration and compatible branches of [Q], \(|\Delta_N|=1\). These are the original retained crossing factors. ## 2. An exact cap for any covector Specify a complex array \(
u=(
u_{ij})\) and its bilinear observation \[

u_{ij}G(i,j). 	ag{5} \] There is no complex conjugation in (5). On the two physical end spaces insert the diagonal operator \[ D_
u=\sum_{i,j}q^{-i}
u_{ij} |i,jangle\langle i,j|. 	ag{6} \] This is an explicit boundary coupon; it need not be a Hopf morphism, a positive operator, or a product of two one-end operators. Multiplying the actual row (2) by (6) gives \(N^{-2}
u\). Thus the marked closed source \(Z_

u(G)|=|

u_{ij}=\delta_{i0}\delta_{j0}\). Then \[ D_
u=E_{00}\otimes E_{00}. 	ag{9} \] Both free indices are fixed, exactly as in the planar definition. For the uninserted scalar array only, \[ N^3Z_{\delta_{00}}(O_\chi) =N^2Z_{m cap}(O_\chi). 	ag{10} \] For a general inserted array their difference is explicitly \[ N^2Z_{m cap}(G)-N^3Z_{\delta_{00}}(G) =\Delta_N\left\{N^{-1}\sum_{i,j}q^iG(i,j)-G(0,0)ight\}. 	ag{11} \] Equation (11) is the closing discrepancy that an argument using unmarked scalarity would otherwise lose. An averaged observation from a different representation must be supplied as its actual covector \(
u\) in these end coordinates. Equality with a fixed-zero observation on scalar operators alone does not identify their values on nonintertwining insertions. Formula (6) retains either specified covector without making such an identification. ## 3. The actual face-pair insertion and its bounds Use the boundary adapters and inverse duals of [A], unchanged. For \(m=a,b\), write \[ k_m=\alpha_{m,-}-\alpha_{m,+}+h_m,\quad l_m= eta_{m,-}- eta_{m,+}+h_m,\quad f_m(k)=a_m^{[k-1]}b_m^{[-k]} . \] Their entries are \[ \mathcal A_m(\alpha;i)=f_m(k_m)q^{ik_m},\qquad \mathcal L_m(i; eta)= rac{q^{-il_m}}{N^2f_m(l_m)}. 	ag{12} \] Here residues lie in \(0,\ldots,N-1\), and \(a_m,b_m\) are the original nonzero pole-edge roots. The face realization of (6) is \[ \mathcal D_
u=(\mathcal A_a\otimes\mathcal A_b) D_

u)_{\alpha; eta} = rac{f_a(k_a)f_b(k_b)} {N^4f_a(l_a)f_b(l_b)} \sum_{i,j}
u_{ij} q^{i(k_a-l_a-1)+j(k_b-l_b)} . } 	ag{13} \] It acts on the two paired invariant images and kills their specified complementary kernels. The identities \(\mathcal L_m\mathcal A_m=I\) show that inserting (13) into (1) has exactly the effect of (6). Every cyclic seam and inverse \(f_m(l_m)^{-1}\) remains; no Hermitian adjoint is substituted. For (9), formula (13) is the product of the two literal fixed-cut face projectors in [A]. In the standard Euclidean physical norm, \[ \|D_

Thus the cap transport itself adds no exponential norm loss to a supplied covector. It does not bound the covector if its own coefficients grow exponentially. All formulas are exact at fixed odd level and preserve any further linear combinations of inserted arrays. Regular decoration derivatives retain the coupons, inverse rows, and scalar \(\Delta_N\); they do not introduce an off-root level or physical meridian family. This supplies the full marked closing observation once the open array and its covector are specified. It does not identify a negative-ray current with a particular insertion, transport an analytic integration cycle, or prove a geometric lower bound. ## Complete direct sources - [Q] [Braid cut and global sewing](research_braid_cut_and_global_nine_cell_sewing.md), SHA256 58503fba3cf834269943956429cc7ac6190499da5e40f57c82d8f13ef995b470. title: Marked factorial calculus and the original Gauss source normalization
text:
# Marked factorial calculus and the original Gauss source normalization Private written proof, 18 November 2026. The exact factorial ratio represents the actual finite Gauss operator on its prescribed physical logarithm germs, including endpoints, Casimir Jordan blocks, and the whole fixed-root meridian family. The marking matters. An individual integer logarithm shift can have a genuine radical meridian pole. A simultaneous shift of both logarithms is the scalar inverse cyclic Green multiplier, and changes the original sewn source if the other kernel is held fixed. This is an exact definition and normalization result. It removes an ambiguity in replacing a finite polynomial by a special-function expression. It supplies neither a coherent propagation estimate nor a contribution of a geometric relative cycle. ## 1. The actual norm relation and its physical logarithms Use the complete directs B, G, J, and U pinned below. Fix \[ N\ge2,\quad d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\quad c_0=2\pi i,\quad m\ge2,\quad r=m-1,\quad \mu=\Log M. 	ag{1} \] On G's actual remaining-head space let \(K,E,F,\Omega\) be its commuting Cartan--Casimir pair and balanced arrows: \[ \Omega=FE+qK+q^{-1}K^{-1},\qquad K(M)=M^rK_0,\qquad K_0^{2N}=I. 	ag{2} \] G proves the full matrix identity, including all Jordan blocks, \[ W_N(K,\Omega):=C_N(\Omega)+K^N+K^{-N}=F^NE^N=0, \quad C_N(z+z^{-1})=z^N+z^{-N}. 	ag{3} \] It also proves the literal factorization \[  egin{split} A_N&=H_d(M)K^d\,\mathcal S_N(u,v;c),& c&=M^{-2}Q,\ u+v&=\Omega/(qK),&uv&=1/(QK^2),\ T&=\mathcal B_m(W_	au^{-1})A_ND_{m top}\mathscr C_r(M), &J_{m op}&=D_N(MK)^{-1}T. \end{split}	ag{4} \] Here \(H_d=\prod_{j=1}^d(MQ^{-j}-M^{-1})\), \(D_N(z)=(z^N-z^{-N})/(z-z^{-1})\), and the routed factors and original scalars have exactly G's order. The notation \(\mathcal S_N(u,v;c)\) means its symmetric polynomial evaluation in \(K,\Omega\), not a choice of scalar Casimir eigenvalue. We write \(J_{m op}\) for J's opposite kernel to avoid confusing it with other scalar functions. Introduce roots \(u,v\) only as local scalar coordinates. Their symmetric powers satisfy the polynomial identity \[ (1-u^N)(1-v^N)=K^{-N}W_N(K,\Omega). 	ag{5} \] Indeed \(u^Nv^N=K^{-2N}\) and \(u^N+v^N=-K^{-N}C_N(\Omega)\), since \(q^N=-1\). At \(M=1\), every actual joint eigenvalue of \(K_0,\Omega(1)\) has \(u^Nv^N=1\) and \((1-u^N)(1-v^N)=0\); hence \(u^N=v^N=1\). Thus each unordered physical pair is \[ \{u,v\}=\{Q^l,Q^k\},\qquad 0\le l,k<N. 	ag{6} \] Only pairs actually present in the joint spectrum are used. The physical marking is the germ of the logarithms \[ u=e^{c_0x},\quad v=e^{c_0y},\qquad x(Q^l)=l/N,\quad y(Q^k)=k/N. 	ag{7} \] These are fixed-\(N\) germs. In particular the germ at \(u=1\) has \(x=0\), not \(x=1\). Swapping the two roots swaps their marked logarithms. ## 2. Exact endpoint germs and symmetric descent Let \(F_N\) denote B's exact marked factorial, and put \[  eta=-2N\mu/c_0,\qquad \mathfrak b_N(x,y;\mu)=  rac{F_N(N(x+y)+ eta)F_N( eta)} {F_N(Nx+ eta)F_N(Ny+ eta)}. 	ag{8} \] At every pair (6), this is holomorphic on a sufficiently small \((u,v,\mu)\)-neighborhood with the logarithms (7). The denominator arguments \(l+ eta,k+ eta\) are in the zero-free strip \(-1<\Re z<N\). The numerator is holomorphic also when \(l+k\ge N\), where it may vanish. Thus \(l=0\) or \(k=0\) presents no fixed-\(N\) obstruction. There is an elementary local divisibility proof that does not use an infinite strip contour at those endpoints. B's finite cardinal identity and the factorial shift give, identically in the other variable and in \(\mu\), \[  egin{split} \mathcal S_N(Q^l,v;c) &= rac{(cv;Q)_l}{(c;Q)_l} =\mathfrak b_N(l/N,y;\mu),\ \mathcal S_N(u,Q^k;c) &= rac{(cu;Q)_k}{(c;Q)_k} =\mathfrak b_N(x,k/N;\mu). \end{split}	ag{9} \] The equalities include \(l=0,k=0\). Expand the holomorphic difference at \((Q^l,Q^k)\). Its terms of degree zero in either variable vanish by (9), so it is divisible by \((u-Q^l)(v-Q^k)\). Since the other factors of \(1-u^N\) and \(1-v^N\) are units on the germ, there is a holomorphic function \(\mathfrak r_N\) such that \[  oxed{\quad \mathcal S_N(u,v;c)-\mathfrak b_N(x,y;\mu) =(1-u^N)(1-v^N)\mathfrak r_N(u,v;\mu). \quad}	ag{10} \] On B's fixed interior logarithmic patches this is also its exact paired strip current divided by the two Fermat factors. At endpoint germs, (9) proves (10) directly. Both the difference and its divisor are symmetric. The quotient is therefore symmetric on the union of the two swapped germs, first off the divisor and then by holomorphic continuation. For \(u
e v\), the unordered roots are local coordinates through their elementary symmetric functions. At \(u=v=u_0\), write \(u=u_0+a+t,\ v=u_0+a-t\). A symmetric holomorphic function has an even convergent power series in \(t\), hence is holomorphic in \(a,t^2\), which are holomorphic functions of \(u+v,uv\). This proves descent also at \[ u=v\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\Omega=\pm2. 	ag{11} \] No division by \(u-v\) is used for (10) or for this descent. For clarity, the actual local functional calculus is finite and unambiguous. On a fixed \(K_0\)-weight space, choose a small Riesz contour enclosing one root joint Casimir value and all the eigenvalues that split from it when \(M\) varies. Keep the contour away from the other root values. Its projector \(P(M)\) is analytic for sufficiently small fixed-\(N\) \(\mu\). The descended holomorphic functions are evaluated by their convergent Taylor series on the generalized eigenspaces, or equivalently by their Cauchy resolvents. This includes the nilpotent parts. Empty primary spaces contribute zero. Equations (3),(5),(10) now give the actual identity \[  oxed{\quad \mathcal S_N(K(M),\Omega(M);c)\,P(M) =\mathfrak b_N(K(M),\Omega(M);\mu)\,P(M). \quad}	ag{12} \] The notation on the right means the descended marked germ (8). The finitely many primary projectors sum to the identity, so these formulas prescribe the full actual Gauss matrix. On overlaps their values agree because each equals the original polynomial. This statement is not a claim that arbitrary logarithm decks give the same representative. The identity is analytic in the actual meridian family before differentiation. It therefore keeps every moving-matrix and projector normal. In particular a derivative of a function of \(\Omega(M)\) is its Fréchet derivative, with a term \[  rac1{2\pi i}\oint f(\zeta) (\zeta-\Omega)^{-1}\Omega' (\zeta-\Omega)^{-1}\,d\zeta, 	ag{13} \] as well as explicit parameter derivatives and any moving localizer. No commutation of \(\Omega'\) with \(\Omega\) is assumed. The vanishing in (12) is the identity \(W_N(M)=0\) of actual matrices and its derivatives, not substitution in a large-degree principal symbol. ## 3. Which channels are units, and which begin in the first normal The marking gives an exact local description stronger than scalar node values. On a fixed Cartan weight \(K(M)=M^r\kappa\), put \(n=l+k\). Since \(uv=1/(QK^2)\), the chosen logarithms satisfy \[ x+y=n/N-2r\mu/c_0. 	ag{14} \] Define the symmetric holomorphic operator unit \[ \mathfrak D_{lk}(M) =F_N(Nx+ eta)F_N(Ny+ eta) 	ag{15} \] on the localized space. Its scalar eigenvalue at the root is \(f_lf_k
e0\), where \(f_j=(Q;Q)_j\). All nilpotent parts are included in its inverse. Equations (8),(12),(14) give exactly \[  oxed{\quad \mathcal S_N(M)P(M)= F_N(n-2mN\mu/c_0)F_N(-2N\mu/c_0) \mathfrak D_{lk}(M)^{-1}P(M). \quad}	ag{16} \] If \(n<N\), the root restriction is the unit \(f_n\mathfrak D_{lk}(1)^{-1}\). It admits a local analytic logarithm on the primary block. If \(n\ge N\), the entire root restriction in (16) is zero, not merely its eigenvalues. This does not delete that channel: the exact factorial identity \(F_N(z+N)=(1-e^{c_0z})F_N(z)\) gives \(F_N'(N+j)=-c_0f_j\), and hence \[  oxed{\quad \left.\partial_\mu(\mathcal S_N(M)P(M))ight|_0 =2mN f_{n-N}\,\mathfrak D_{lk}(1)^{-1}P(1), \qquad n\ge N. \quad}	ag{17} \] This is nonzero if that primary space is nonzero. It is an exact operator statement, with no norm or original closed-source lower bound. The factor \(2mN\) includes the motion of the physical arguments; holding the Fourier arguments fixed would lose part of it. The analytic projector was retained in (16) before taking the derivative. These upper **primary channels** are distinct from U's upper Fourier coefficient sector. In U's two-tail degree-\(d\) example the physical primary labels satisfy \(l+k=d<N\), and the full Gauss root block is a unit, even though its prescribed upper Fourier normal has an exponentially large norm. Equation (17) neither removes nor bounds that Fourier sector separately. There is an exact common divisor, not only a first-normal formula. Put \[ \delta_m(M)=1-M^{-2mN}. 	ag{17a} \] For \(n=N+s\), the factorial \(N\)-shift gives \[ F_N(n-2mN\mu/c_0) =\delta_m(M)F_N(s-2mN\mu/c_0). 	ag{17b} \] The second factor is a holomorphic unit on the primary germ. Since \(H_d(1)=(-1)^dN
e0\), inclusion of the prefactor \(H_dK^d\) in (4) proves that each lower restriction of \(A_N\) is a holomorphic unit, while every upper restriction is \(\delta_m\) times a holomorphic unit. Each actual channel has vanishing order exactly zero or one. This factorization can be assembled at fixed \(N\). The Cartan weight projectors are constant, and within each weight the distinct root Casimir values have disjoint small Riesz contours. Group the whole cluster splitting from each root value; do not separate a colliding Jordan pair. The unordered pair (6), and hence \(n=l+k\), is uniquely determined by that joint root value. Therefore the sum \(P_{m up}(M)\) of the upper primary projectors is holomorphic near \(M=1\), after reducing the meridian neighborhood if needed. It commutes with \(A_N(M)\), and the complementary primary sum is \(I-P_{m up}\). Define \[ \mathfrak G_N =A_N(I-P_{m up})+\delta_m^{-1}A_NP_{m up}. 	ag{17c} \] Equation (17b) gives the holomorphic continuation of the second term. Each primary restriction of \(\mathfrak G_N\) is a unit, so \(\mathfrak G_N\) is a holomorphic invertible matrix and \[  oxed{\quad A_N=\mathfrak G_N igl[(I-P_{m up})+\delta_mP_{m up} igr]. \quad}	ag{17d} \] This is a reduced finite-dimensional primary resolution, not a lift of \(P_{m up}\) to an original total-intertwiner projector. Its contour widths and conditioning may depend on \(N\). All the routed factors on both sides of \(A_N\) in (4) remain attached to this factorization. On compact lower angle patches, B additionally gives the scalar logarithm \(N^{-1}\log\mathfrak b_N=\Phi+O((\log N)/N)\) and its scalar unit amplitude. This does not estimate the physical Riesz projector or its coherent kernel. At time zero a localized operator evolution has kernel \(P\), not the identity. Endpoint germs can shrink with \(N\), and the upper channels in (17) cannot be included in a holomorphic logarithm of the root matrix. ## 4. Exact logarithm decks and the cyclic Green scalar Now continue the marked factorial expression itself, keeping the scalar arguments \(u,v\) fixed while shifting a logarithm. Put \[ ho=M^{-2N},\qquad \alpha=u^N,\quad \zeta=v^N,\qquad k_N=\alpha\zeta=K^{-2N}. 	ag{18} \] The letter \(\zeta\) here denotes a power of \(v\), not a contour coordinate. From the factorial \(N\)-shift, \[  egin{split} \mathfrak b_N(x+1,y)&=	au_x\mathfrak b_N(x,y),& 	au_x&= rac{1-ho\alpha\zeta}{1-ho\alpha},\ \mathfrak b_N(x,y+1)&=	au_y\mathfrak b_N(x,y),& 	au_y&= rac{1-ho\alpha\zeta}{1-ho\zeta}. \end{split}	ag{19} \] These are meromorphic identities; omitted denominators are not declared units at \(M=1\). On the actual norm quotient, (5) says \(\alpha+\zeta=1+k_N\). Consequently \[ 	au_x= rac{1-ho\zeta}{1-ho},\qquad 	au_y= rac{1-ho\alpha}{1-ho},\qquad 	au_x	au_y= rac{1-ho k_N}{1-ho}. 	ag{20} \] For example multiply \(1-ho\alpha\) by \(1-ho\zeta\) to get \((1-ho)(1-ho k_N)\); this proves (20) generically and then meromorphically, including Jordan blocks. The individual formulas use an ordered nonramified root pair. Their product is symmetric and requires no such choice. Since \(K^{2N}=M^{2rN}I\), the simultaneous deck is the scalar \[  oxed{\quad d_{{m deck},N}(M)=	au_x	au_y = rac{1-M^{-2mN}}{1-M^{-2N}} =\sum_{a=0}^{m-1}M^{-2aN} =\mathcal R_N(M)^{-1}. \quad}	ag{21} \] Here \(\mathcal R_N\) is exactly G's finite cyclic transport multiplier, not a newly chosen normalizer. In particular \[ d_{{m deck},N}(1)=m,\qquad \left.\partial_\mu d_{{m deck},N}(e^\mu)ight|_0 =-Nm(m-1). 	ag{22} \] It is a holomorphic unit on a sufficiently small scaled meridian disk. This notation is distinct from \(D_N(M)/N\), which occurs in the turnover and other source frames. The individual decks can have genuine operator poles. At the root, on an ordered local cover, write \(\alpha(0)=I+R\). Equation (5) gives \(\zeta(0)=I-R\) and \(R^2=0\). Expanding (20) yields \[ \operatorname*{Res}_{\mu=0}	au_x =R/(2N),\qquad \operatorname*{Res}_{\mu=0}	au_y =-R/(2N). 	ag{23} \] On a double Casimir block with root value \(\lambda=z_0+z_0^{-1}\), \(\Delta=z_0-z_0^{-1}
e0\), choose \(u=(qKz)^{-1}\). For \(L=\Omega-\lambda I\), \(L^2=0\), the logarithmic derivative of \(u^N\) with respect to \(\Omega\) is \(-N/\Delta\). Thus \[ R=- rac N\Delta L,\qquad \operatorname*{Res}	au_x=- rac{L}{2\Delta},\qquad \operatorname*{Res}	au_y= rac{L}{2\Delta}. 	ag{24} \] These are nonzero when the Casimir block is genuinely Jordan. Such blocks occur in the actual source: U proves, for every even \(N=2p\), on the two-tail degree-\(d\) block with \(K=1\), that the nodes \(2\cos((2j+1)\pi/N)\), \(0\le j<p\), have actual columns \(v_j,v'_j\) with \((\Omega-\lambda_j)v'_j=v_j
e0\). Their \(\Delta\)'s are nonzero. Their physical pair has \(l+k=d<N\), so (16) is a root unit there; an individual shifted Gauss expression has a genuine pole on these blocks as well. The scalar branchwise limits \(m\) and \(1\) on the two split components therefore do not define a regular individual operator transition through a Jordan collision. At \(\Omega=\pm2\), the unordered functional identity in Section 2 remains valid, but an individual deck is not claimed to descend across the ramification. The simultaneous scalar (21) does descend. ## 5. The original closing source changes if a deck is dropped For the same actual braid word \(W\) and its reflected reduced word \(B_-\), J proves the sewn expression with its original cut, pivot, framing line, and finite coherent resolutions, \[ \Phi_0(W(M))=  rac{D_N(M)}{a_N(M)} \operatorname{Tr}\!\left( J_{m op}(M)B_-(M^{-1})J_{m op}(M^{-1})ight), 	ag{25} \] where \[ \gamma_N(M)=(-1)^dD_N(M)/N,\qquad a_N(M)=(-1)^dN\gamma_N(M)^m. 	ag{26} \] The full trace is analytically continued from its punctured meridian expression as prescribed by the original source. Make the simultaneous logarithm shift in the left Gauss factor of (4), on its marked primary germs, and hold every other factor, in particular the right reflected kernel in (25), fixed. Equations (20)--(21) give exactly \[ A_N^{m deck}=d_{{m deck},N}A_N,\qquad T^{m deck}=d_{{m deck},N}T,\qquad J_{m op}^{m deck}=d_{{m deck},N}J_{m op}. 	ag{27} \] These identities hold after summing the physical primary spaces, because the multiplier is the same scalar on every one.
