Therefore the modified sewn expression is \[  oxed{\quad \Phi_0^{m deck}(W(M)) =d_{{m deck},N}(M)\Phi_0(W(M)). \quad}	ag{28} \] In particular its root value is \(m\Phi_0(W(1))\), and its first \(\mu\)-normal is \[ m\,\partial_\mu\Phi_0(W)|_0 -Nm(m-1)\Phi_0(W(1)). 	ag{29} \] This is an equality of source expressions, not a claim that a given source value is nonzero. It shows precisely why an untracked deck choice is not a source-preserving normalization. The same scalar multiplication holds before integration in J's three-kernel compact period. All occupation caps, factorial duals, Cartan twists, and meridian finite parts remain. An inverse scalar on another leg could compensate it, but that would be an explicit additional source transformation, not omission of (21). For individual decks the nonscalar meromorphic transitions and their residues (23) must instead remain in their actual order. On a relative window with polar terms, the finite part uses the entire product with \(d_{{m deck},N}(M)\); it cannot in general be replaced by \(m\) times that window's finite part. ## 6. What is defined, and what is still not estimated The original finite polynomial is now exactly represented by the factorial germs with labels \(0,\ldots,d\), including every root endpoint and normal channel. This equality survives arbitrary ordered outer matrices and windows when the same primary resolution is retained. It does not identify a shifted logarithm germ with that same physical definition: (19)--(29) record the difference. This establishes the marked local functional calculus, its unit and first-normal channels, and the concrete deck effect on the original source. No estimate of the primary projectors, their Fréchet normals, or the resulting coherent kernel has been supplied. In particular an analytic scalar logarithm is not an actual near-identity coherent evolution, and scalar nonvanishing in B is not a matrix norm estimate. Transporting these marked germs along a geometric contour still requires the actual logarithm transitions, endpoint channels, and relative-window currents. No intersection coefficient or knot noncancellation conclusion is asserted. ## Complete proof directs * B: notes/research_balanced_gauss_global_cardinal_strip.md, SHA256 bde4e38cb64477d13a558000545e53fc81413f2fcfe82f80562ce3691d8a19ca. * G: notes/research_opposite_kernel_forced_cyclic_normalization.md, SHA256 42e6d6c3a5039859c241a2832de56301eff49d749db86d67868f3534c89aaaaa. * J: notes/research_opposite_polarization_source_kernel.md, SHA256 d52c6dd8e62f575a262fc7af460e258f7cb0e40b5a9c037ac46dd8d151002d44. * U: notes/research_actual_upper_gauss_carry_conditioning.md, SHA256 19d9942be54c4dcde7209b332d70ca3ce19b888b20d60480ae74f6ac1e9af4c3. The entire final and all four complete directs were read nontruncated in this author sequence; every used implication and all matching pins were checked. Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used. Frozen and public files were not edited.

title: A marked short corridor outside the three/four reduction
text: # A marked short corridor outside the three/four reduction Private written deduction, 10 November 2026. No mathematical numerical evaluation, test, import or compilation is used. The existing rational normal form is not reproved here. Its uniqueness gives an exact test for a prescribed coefficient alphabet, and already excludes a universal reduction to positive three/four paths by end twists and proper half-turns. The obstruction concerns that marked reduction, not the volume conjecture or the exponential rate of the unreduced source. The second distinction is analytic: the actual joining of two proved single-power kernels retains a turn. Omitting it merges their powers and changes the finite source. The existing concentrated boundary class is not closed under arbitrary turns, even on actual tangle sources. ## 1. A coefficient-alphabet test with both boundary frames fixed Use the physical crossing \(R\), turn \(T\), and affine pillowcase maps of [the marked move theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_marked_degree_two_tangle_moves.md): \[ \widetilde R^{\,n}(x,y)=(x+ny+n/2,y),\qquad \widetilde T(x,y)=(-y,x+1/2). \tag{1} \] Their linear parts are \[ A_n=\begin{pmatrix}1&n\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad S=\begin{pmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}. \tag{2} \] The symbols \(A_n\) in this section are two-dimensional integral matrices; the original quantum matrices will have a different symbol in Section 3. Let a fixed corridor have projective linear matrix \(G\). Choose its deck sign so that its lower-left entry is \(C>0\), and suppose \(C\ge2\). Integral twists on the left and right leave \(C\) and the two diagonal residues modulo \(C\) unchanged. The determinant-one condition makes both residues nonzero. There is consequently a unique normalization by these two end twists of the form \[ G_0=\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\C&D\end{pmatrix}, \qquad 0<A,D<C,\qquad B=(AD-1)/C. \tag{3} \] All physical half-turns retained in the marked normal form have identity linear part on the pillowcase, up to the deck sign. They do not change (3). Fix any alphabet \(\mathcal B\subseteq\{2,3,\ldots\}\). A replacement in this section must preserve the two outside frames and arbitrary outside tangles. It may add fixed integral end twists and the specified proper half-turn, but may not add an outside quarter-turn or a new long filling. **Proposition 1.** Such a uniform-negative replacement \[ R^r T R^{-b_1}T\cdots T R^{-b_k}T R^s H, \qquad b_j\in\mathcal B, \tag{4} \] exists if and only if the unique negative continued fraction of \(C/A\), with all coefficients at least two, has every coefficient in \(\mathcal B\). A uniform-positive replacement of the same form with \(R^{b_j}\) instead exists if and only if the corresponding continued fraction of \(C/(C-A)\) has every coefficient in \(\mathcal B\). *Proof.* The [definite corridor normal form](research_definite_rational_corridor_normal_form.md), Sections 2--3, proves that a negative word with all \(b_j\ge2\) has normalized ratio \[ C/A=[b_1,\ldots,b_k]_-. \tag{5} \] It also proves uniqueness by the ceiling Euclidean algorithm: the next coefficient is the ceiling of the current complete quotient, and its remainder determines the next quotient. Thus (5) is necessary. Conversely, the same theorem realizes that continued fraction with the unique full matrix (3), and then restores both end twists and the actual affine half-turn. This gives the marked identity for arbitrary attached tangles. For the positive statement, conjugate a negative-word matrix by \(\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)\). On projective linear parts this changes every negative crossing to a positive one and preserves the turn. If the negative normalized matrix is \(\left(\begin{smallmatrix}A'&B'\\C&D'\end{smallmatrix}\right)\), the positive matrix, after choosing lower-left entry \(C>0\), is \[ \begin{pmatrix}-A'&B'\\C&-D'\end{pmatrix}. \tag{6} \] Its normalized first diagonal residue is \(C-A'\). Consequently matching (3) requires \(A'=C-A\), and (5) becomes the second continued fraction in the proposition. The full affine correction is again the prescribed proper half-turn. This argument proves a boundary-map identity; it does not replace only one attachment by its mirror. \(\square\) This is a test for reductions of the specified marked corridor form. Special fixed attachments can have further stabilizers. The proposition does not exclude identities exploiting such an attachment or an unrelated finite-level quantum relation. ## 2. An explicit adjacent pair Consider the fixed corridor \[ W=T R^3 T R^5 T. \tag{7} \] Direct integer multiplication gives \[ S A_3 S A_5 S =\begin{pmatrix}-5&1\\14&-3\end{pmatrix},\qquad A_1(S A_3 S A_5 S)A_1 =\begin{pmatrix}9&7\\14&11\end{pmatrix}. \tag{8} \] Its two ratios in Proposition 1 are exactly \[ \frac{14}{9}=[2,3,2,2,2]_-, \qquad \frac{14}{5}=[3,5]_-. \tag{9} \] For the first equality the successive tails from the right are \(2,3/2,4/3,9/4,14/9\); the second is \(3-1/5\). Thus neither sign has a replacement whose coefficients all belong to \(\{3,4\}\), even allowing arbitrary length and fixed integral twists at both ends. Reversing the corridor reverses the continued-fraction lists and does not change this conclusion. Nor can (7) be replaced by one arbitrary nonzero-power kernel with only those end adapters. The necessary and sufficient test in [single-corridor compression](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_rational_corridor_compression.md), Proposition 1, requires the two normalized diagonal residues to be the same \(1\) or \(-1\) modulo \(C\). Here they are \(9,11\) modulo \(14\), neither \(1\) nor \(13\). The same obstruction excludes reducing (7) to a same-sign run of twos with only those end adapters: every such run has the marked one-vertex form proved by [the repeated-two reduction](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_repeated_two_crossing_chain_reduction.md), Proposition 2. Composing its end twists and proper rotation with the proposed adapters would give the excluded one-vertex form for (7). These are exact restrictions even under the stronger hypothetical assumption that every positive three/four path already had a complete boundary theorem. They do not assert that the pair \((3,5)\) has no other useful presentation or cannot be estimated directly. In particular (9) is itself a valid uniform-sign presentation; its new adjacent powers still require their actual coherent contraction. No added separator has been used to turn them into a covered long-separated family. ## 3. The turn in the exact finite composition Now return to the original full algebra and use the quantum notation \[ \mathcal A_N=\mathbb C[z]/(2T_N(z/2)+2),\quad D_N=N-1, \quad \phi_N(e_i e_j)=\delta_{i+j,D_N},\quad \mathsf J_{ij}=\delta_{i+j,D_N}. \tag{10} \] Let \(M\) be multiplication by the original crossing, including \(\kappa_N=\exp(\pi iD_N^2/(2N))\), and put \[ \mathsf A_n=\mathsf J M^n,\qquad v(w)=(e_0(w),\ldots,e_{D_N}(w))^T,\qquad P_n(w,z)=v(w)^T\mathsf A_n v(z). \tag{11} \] The identity \(M^T\mathsf J=\mathsf J M\) makes every \(\mathsf A_n\) symmetric. The full single-power theorem [for every nonzero degree-two filling](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_all_nonzero_degree_two_fillings.md) estimates precisely \(P_n\), with both free ordinary variables and their original normal data. Two different contractions of these same polynomials must be distinguished. Direct Frobenius gluing gives \[ \phi_z[P_a(w,z)P_b(z,u)] =v(w)^T\mathsf A_a\mathsf J\mathsf A_bv(u) =P_{a+b}(w,u). \tag{12} \] The last equality uses \(\mathsf A_a\mathsf J\mathsf A_b =\mathsf J M^a\mathsf J^2M^b=\mathsf A_{a+b}\). In contrast, the actual two-adjacent-vertex path is \[ Q_{a,b}(w,u)=v(w)^T\mathsf A_a\mathsf A_bv(u) =\phi_x\phi_y[ P_a(w,x)K_T(x,y)P_b(y,u)], \qquad K_T(x,y)=\sum_{j=0}^{D_N}e_j(x)e_j(y). \tag{13} \] Indeed the two pairings contribute \(\mathsf A_a\mathsf J I\mathsf J\mathsf A_b\). Equivalently, (13) is \(\phi_x[P_a(w,x)(\mathsf T_xP_b)(x,u)]\), where \(\mathsf T e_j=e_{D_N-j}\). There is no extra scalar in either identity: the original crossing factors already occur in \(M^a,M^b\). All products are taken before the full traces, so (12)--(13) retain both parities, every first normal at a double root, and the odd simple root. Thus replacing (13) by the easier single-trace composition (12) deletes the turn and changes the source to power \(a+b\). Single-power upper bounds do not make that deletion legitimate. The exact ordinary adapters and their potentially growing-order Fourier observations are also explicit in [the adjacent-kernel observation theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_mixed_two_adjacent_ordinary_observation_adapter.md), Sections 1--3. End crossing adapters are different: if a complete concentrated boundary theorem is already known, canonical multiplication by a fixed crossing preserves it under [boundary crossing preservation](research_boundary_crossing_packet_preservation.md). For a rational normal-form identity the exact quantum transformation is \[ \mathcal Q_N(W)=\kappa_N^\ell M^r[\mathsf J M^{-b_1}\mathsf J\cdots \mathsf J M^{-b_k}\mathsf J]M^s, \qquad \ell=\frac{e(W)-r-s+\sum_jb_j}{3}\in\mathbb Z. \tag{14} \] Here \(e(W)\) is the original signed crossing sum. The phase changes and unit scalars from the two canonical boundary multiplications are those in Sections 4--5 of the normal-form theorem. Formula (14) does not erase the separately specified physical half-turn. ## 4. Why the known analytic class cannot supply automatic turns There is already an actual-source obstruction, not merely a formal possibility. For every fixed \(|p|\ge2\), the terminal source \(H_{p,N}=\mathsf T(R^p)\) has the complete nonzero local packet and a strict whole-real angular gap. But \[ \mathsf T H_{p,N}=\operatorname{can}(R^p). \tag{15} \] At every physical angle \(\tau_j=\pi(D_N-2j)/N\), the latter has the exact value \[ \operatorname{can}(R^p)(-2\cos\tau_j) =\exp\!\left(\frac{\pi i pD_N^2}{4N} +\frac{ipN\tau_j^2}{4\pi}\right), \qquad |\operatorname{can}(R^p)(-2\cos\tau_j)|=1. \tag{16} \] As proved in Section 7 of boundary crossing preservation, a nonzero even local packet at the nodes tending to zero forces its real complete rate to be zero. At physical nodes tending to any fixed nonzero real angle, a strict angular bound at rate zero would then force the modulus to tend to zero, contradicting (16). This holds at both parities. Consequently a theorem asserting closure of the existing concentrated class under every short turn is false. This does not disprove a source-specific theorem for (13), whose geometric action and contributing cycle can change. The existing [finite-kernel composition theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_finite_two_boundary_kernel_closure.md) proves such preservation with a sufficiently long intervening power, and explicitly retains that hypothesis. ## 5. What remains for arbitrary partial fillings The exact [source compiler](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_arbitrary_power_source_compilation.md) does cover every finite Conway expression. At a branch it keeps the multiplication tensor \[ \mu_{ijr}=\phi_N(e_i e_j e_{D_N-r}), \tag{17} \] and every still-free ordinary boundary variable. The [internal-wire averaging theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_internal_wire_exact_circle_averaging.md) then integrates every paired index exactly, with factor \(N\) per internal wire. It retains full Hermite data and all signed powers. That identity removes internal-index alias errors in its stated representation; it does not remove the original angle traces or provide their calibrated competing-current bounds. Thus the obstruction is already present for the rational two-port example (7), before branching is considered. General arborescent components additionally retain (17) and more outside boundaries. The rational-corridor theorem does not replace those tensors by a two-boundary path. A useful sufficient next theorem is therefore a complete boundary estimate for the actual uniform-sign chains with arbitrary magnitudes at least two, stable under the particular turns in (13), or a direct estimate for the fixed short component after its actual surrounding contraction. The marked rational normal form would transfer such a theorem with its end crossings and scalar (14) retained. No such general analytic conclusion follows here, and no closed-knot or finite-exception statement is inferred. ## 6. Frozen direct source bindings All files below were read in the sections used above. The listed hashes bind the exact source statements, not new evaluations. | Source | SHA-256 | |---|---| | research_definite_rational_corridor_normal_form.md | 7d74cd2247aee1b87a1d225364c29df12469a9bd87d6680667cf48367475d147 | | research_rational_corridor_compression.md | 3feea5432842284b8c6fe20f1ea8c3cae2b10c174b8f707340a69183641f368c | | research_marked_degree_two_tangle_moves.md | 0951bded882c68d38fc6f1cede247f628f103102386940d63d5ed93d90b55158 | | research_repeated_two_crossing_chain_reduction.md | e56a85bae513ebaadb28bd0b50a752e892e3b29035e8b3d43a7ee33f9fb7a6d1 | | research_all_nonzero_degree_two_fillings.md | 7ac634d458e5805e95a7ce064d4e1fc513c96c0b758cfaee9f91fd46de10304c | | research_boundary_crossing_packet_preservation.md | a2f9cadf0fd6f23889ea7d20b469055fe33cb9df4d971668a2923666983cfec8 | | research_finite_two_boundary_kernel_closure.md | 759118c877a9657355d5c457bfc3d0b7a45cc2601a8b247f4e030c90770155cc | | research_arbitrary_power_source_compilation.md | 55e2de84870cfd20dac5922791dbc2bed54909439dfbf4663f17c70a1089445f | | research_internal_wire_exact_circle_averaging.md | 0efa85a43da064197f25422d86ef37688971f2dface55da9d5efef3ccb0d08ef | | research_mixed_two_adjacent_ordinary_observation_adapter.md | 9d6cd4139f53754c2fc4164e239f3f6c650fbc4631923416eeb7016179e53478 |

title: A matched spherical triangulation has the original general Morse source
text:
# A matched spherical triangulation has the original general Morse source 31 October 2026. This is a finite topology/source extension, not a volume asymptotic and not a claim that a new presentation has a prescribed flat-plat width. ## 1. Input, conclusion, and the local ordering Let \(\mathcal T\) be a finite connected triangular cellulation of the oriented sphere, with a perfect matching \(D\) of its cubic dual \(\Delta\). Assume every paired pair of triangles has a four-sided disk as its union, with four distinct white vertices. Equivalently, begin with a connected spherical quadrangulation \(\mathcal Q\), choose one embedded diagonal in each quadrilateral, and triangulate along those diagonals. Parallel edges produced by a choice of diagonals are not silently identified. They are allowed as cellulation data here. A positive geometric certificate, when needed, is a separate hypothesis. There are \(2R\) triangles, \(R\) matched pairs, and \(R+2\) white vertices. For each quadrilateral choose the oriented cyclic order \((x,b,y,c)\), with chosen diagonal \(xy\). The two triangles are \((x,b,y)\) and \((x,c,y)\). The local box frame is input middle \(b\), output middle \(c\), left outer \(x\), right outer \(y\). Reversing this frame later would require its actual duality adapter; no such unrecorded reversal is part of the construction. The construction below gives a genuine augmented link in \(S^3\), with \(R\) labeled twice-punctured crossing disks, whose original cut graph is \((\Delta,D)\). It has a general Morse diagram containing exactly these \(R\) recorded two-strand boxes and no other crossing. In the fixed frames, any full original coupons \(f_e(\Omega)R^{\epsilon_e}\) have exactly the homogeneous source \[ P(L)=\prod_{e=1}^R H_{f_eR^{\epsilon_e}} (L_{x_e},L_{b_e},L_{c_e},L_{y_e}). 	ag{1} \] For any MAIN edge between faces \(a,b\), the original raw one-mark contraction is exactly \[ I_N=[\prod_{f
e a,b}L_f^{N-1}]\,P ig|_{L_a=L_b=0}. 	ag{2} \] It is independent of the selected MAIN edge. The formula uses the original turns, reduced mark, all full crossing scalars, and complete root Hermite data. No level factor is suppressed. ## 2. Inverting the actual crossing-disk cut Embed the cubic dual \(\Delta\) on the sphere. Choose disjoint small regular-neighborhood disks around the matched edges and their endpoint vertices. Because \(D\) is a perfect matching, these disks are disjoint and meet the other edges in four boundary terminals each. Contracting each disk gives a connected plane four-valent graph \(G\), with \(R\) vertices and \(2R\) edges. At one disk label the four terminals cyclically \(0,1,2,3\) so that the two original matched vertices group terminals \((1,2)\) and \((3,0)\). These are the two shaded half-disk sectors. Draw the **physical untwisted main strands** with the other planar pairing \[ (0,1),\qquad(2,3). 	ag{3} \] These arcs are disjoint. Join the terminals outside the disks along the original nonmatching dual edges. The result is a finite union of embedded circles in the projection sphere. Each circle meets a box, because every piece came from the finite four-terminal construction. One must not identify these circles with the abstract cycles of \(\Delta\setminus D\): the latter uses the shaded grouping \((1,2),(3,0)\), whereas the physical strands use (3). In a disjoint three-ball neighborhood of each disk put the standard perpendicular crossing circle and its twice-punctured spanning disk, meeting exactly the two strands in (3). All its labels and its collar orientation are inherited from the chosen local box frame. This is an explicit link embedded in \(S^3\); no abstract three-manifold realization theorem is needed. Cut it along the projection sphere and open each original upper and lower half disk. The two shaded triangles at the box have the original labels \[ S_0=(O,C_1,C_2),\qquad S_1=(O,C_3,C_0). \] The untwisted within-copy gluing fixes \(O\) and sends \(C_1\mapsto C_0\), \(C_2\mapsto C_3\). Thus the cut is literally the inverse of sections 1–4 of [original matching-graph cut](../papers/marked-fillings/README.md). Its medial boundary graph is the medial graph of the supplied \(\Delta\), with every original white face and matching edge retained. The proof there that opening the disjoint half disks gives two balls is local and does not use a plat sweep; it therefore applies to this construction. Insert a recorded half twist \(\epsilon_e\in\{0,1,-1\}\) in a box when desired. Its original shaded maps are precisely the cross-copy maps in that same cut theorem. Both nonzero signs have the same terminal permutation but retain their different disk-framed peripheral paths. The external graph and the local polynomial frame are unchanged. ## 3. A knot parity pattern exists, without a bridge-width assertion Start with the untwisted physical circles of section 2. Form a finite graph whose vertices are these circles and whose edge at a box joins the two circles passing through that box (a loop is allowed). This graph is connected: otherwise the union of boxes and outside arcs, and therefore the connected four-valent graph \(G\), would split. Choose a spanning tree. Give its boxes odd parity and all other boxes even parity. Switching a tree box from (3) to the odd pairing \((0,2),(1,3)\) joins two distinct current circles into one. Process the tree edges in any order: after any subset, its connected tree components are exactly the merged circles, so the next edge still joins two different circles. Thus the final main link has one component. Each odd sign may independently be chosen \(+1\) or \(-1\). Filling box \(e\) with any integer power \(n_e\) of that parity preserves this one-component property. The original convention is \(n_e=\epsilon_e-2p_e\), where \(p_e\) is the integer full-twist filling coordinate in the recorded local disk framing. Arbitrarily large independent positive or negative powers of the chosen parity are available. This says nothing about minimal bridge number or a specified original flat width. ## 4. Producing the original finite Morse tensor network Choose a point outside the disks as infinity. In each disk use its given orientation-preserving parametrization to draw two vertical strands, with terminals \(1,2\) at the input and \(0,3\) at the output. The local quadrilateral is then exactly \((x,b,y,c)\) in section 1. The finitely many disjoint disks can be placed in such plane charts independently; this fixes, rather than transports or resets, their ordered four-leg frames. More explicitly, straighten each chosen disk parametrization in its own disjoint collar, and extend those collar changes to an orientation-preserving plane isotopy. The remaining outside arcs are then drawn between the resulting boundary endpoints. Thus the local vertical charts belong to one global plane drawing; no ribbon normal twist or permutation of a coupon's legs is introduced. Smooth the outside arcs and perturb their height functions away from the disks. There are finitely many ordinary nondegenerate maxima and minima, all at distinct heights after another small perturbation. No new crossing or ribbon twist is required. This is a general Morse diagram, with arbitrary cups/caps between recorded box heights. It need not be a plat with all cups below and all caps above the boxes. Evaluate it using exactly the original complete module \(V_d\), its regular self-duality \(J\), all four original turns, the original checked crossings and Casimir coupons, and one exposed original reduced cap. Upward/downward arcs carry the corresponding actual module or dual; their physical frames are related by \(J\), not by an independently reset diagonal insertion. Since the complete object is self-dual, these are the same original finite matrices in the ordered balanced head frames. This is the usual original ribbon tangle evaluation on the explicitly constructed diagram. There is no new normalization ambiguity. For fixed \(N\), the regular generic lift uses \(\widetilde g=(-1)^HK\), with \(J^{-t}J=\widetilde g\), which specializes literally to \(g=K^{1-N}\). Its two traces agree on every endomorphism in the tensor-generated integral-weight category. The full proof, including duals and regular root specialization, is in sections 2–3 of [all-MAIN mark and general Morse compiler](research_arbitrary_main_edge_mark_transport.md); it is independent of a flat layout. Its snakes prove invariance under the Morse interchanges just used. Its spherical trace exchange exposes any selected MAIN edge as a top cap while keeping every coupon disk fixed. The cut network is a regular generic intertwiner on \(V_d\) or its dual. Its \(K\) weights are distinct and its internal \(F\) arrows nonzero, so it is scalar. Its ordinary closure is \((-1)^d[N]_q\) times that scalar. Equality of closed spherical readings, followed by regular specialization, proves independence of the reduced marked scalar from the MAIN edge. No root quantum dimension is divided by zero. This argument works on any component because all the complete colors agree. ## 5. General Morse winding and the full original coefficient Here the all-MAIN compiler is repeated on the new diagram itself; there is no assumed old flat diagram whose coefficient is being transported. Choose the marked edge's adjacent face \(a\) as exterior and expose a top cap, with \(b\) its inside face. A connected four-valent graph has no bridge (the parity of degrees in either component would contradict one crossing edge), so these two faces are distinct. The finger move preserves their labels. Put \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\). In literal left-to-right head order \((i,j)\), both original left/right cups and both caps are \[ p_{ij}=Nq^{-d^2+di}\,1_{i+j=d},\qquad \ell_{ij}=N^{-1}q^{di}\,1_{i+j=d}. 	ag{4} \] The exposed original mark, after the whole-source conservation forces its two remaining heads to sum to \(d\), is \(m_{ij}=N^{-2}q^{dj}\). This is a consequence of the full source, not an early restriction of the unrestricted marked matrix. Its contraction with its original cup is exactly one. At every fixed coupon the original adapter is \[ N^{-1}H_e(x,b,c,y)/(bc)^{d/2}. 	ag{5} \] Let \(M_f\) count middle incidences at boxes and \(T_f\) count outside turns minus inside turns in face \(f\), temporarily including the ordinary cap that will be marked. Round each fixed local box in its actual frame. Each middle passage contributes \(+\pi\) to the boundary turning index and the two outer passages have net zero; inside turns contribute \(+\pi\) and outside turns \(-\pi\). The bounded face winding is \(+1\) and exterior winding \(-1\), counting repeated boundary occurrences. Therefore \[ M_f-T_f=2\ (f
e a),\qquad M_a-T_a=-2. 	ag{6} \] This is the face-boundary proof in section 6 of the all-MAIN theorem, which uses only the local boxes and Morse arcs, not their vertical ordering or a flat gap forest. All ordinary turns and (5) thus give \(L_a^d\prod_{f
e a}L_f^{-d}\). The exact mark/cap ratio is \(N^{-1}(L_b/L_a)^d\). If there are \(k'\) cups, there are \(k'\) caps; their complete powers of \(N\) give \(N^{k'}N^{-(k'-1)}N^{-2}=N^{-1}\). Their recorded \(q\)-constants cancel, just as in (4). The whole marked summand is consequently \[ N^{-R-1} rac{P(L)}{\prod_{f
e a,b}L_f^d}. 	ag{7} \] The integral conserved-head lattice is the original cycle lattice of the connected spherical graph. Bending edges does not change it. Integration across dual paths identifies it primitively with face potentials modulo their common constant. There are \(R+2\) faces, thus \(R+1\) independent grids after \(L_a=1\). For odd \(N\) use \(L_f=Q^{p_f}\). For even \(N\), the cochain which is one on MAIN edges and zero on matching edges is closed: each triangle has two MAIN edges. Since the sphere is simply connected it integrates to \(t_f\in\mathbb F_2\), with \(t_a=0,t_b=1\); use \(L_f=q^{t_f}Q^{p_f}\). The local full-polynomial adapter first imposes the canonical physical head support, killing all wrong unwrapped totals. Supported states and primitive grids then correspond exactly. Only coherent integrated face-log lifts are varied; no arbitrary individual head reset is used. The \(N^{R+1}\) grid count cancels (7). Nonnegative exponents of total degree \(dR\) leave only the alias \(n_a=n_b=0\), \(n_f=d\) otherwise: those \(R\) ordinary minimum degrees already exhaust the total. The even coset character is one there. This proves exactly (2), with no additional factor of \(N\). ## 6. Original signed filling powers and their whole spectral functional Replace the \(e\)-th box by its actual \(R^{n_e}\), where the signed integer \(n_e
e0\) is fixed before \(N\). The exact local identity \[ R^{n_e}=q^{n_ed^2/4} \exp\!\left( rac{n_e K(\Omega)}{2\hbar}ight), \quad \hbar=2\pi i/N,\quad K(z)=\operatorname{arccosh}(-z/2)^2, 	ag{8} \] retains all Hermite derivatives and every crossing scalar. It is the fixed-root identity of [exact original signed crossing powers](actual_direct_long_power_source.md). The explicit Gaussian/resolvent numerator functional is also recorded in [exact Gaussian/resolvent functional](actual_gaussian_resolvent_numerator_and_cap.md). Different boxes do not need to commute; their ordered tensor contraction is multilinear in the local matrices. Define the full spectral numerator using the newly constructed original source, \[ S_N( oldsymbol\sigma) =[\prod_{f
e a,b}L_f^d] \left.\prod_e H_{V_N(\sigma_e)}ight|_{L_a=L_b=0}. 	ag{9} \] Applying the original matrix Fourier/Hermite functional separately at each box gives exactly \[  egin{split} I_{N,\mathbf n}={}&q^{ rac{d^2}{4}\sum_e n_e}(-i)^R \sum_{ oldsymbol\ell\in(\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\})^R} \Bigl(\prod_e\ell_e\Bigr)(-1)^{(N+1)\sum_e\ell_e}\ &\ 	imes\int_{[-1/2,1/2]^R} \Bigl(\prod_e\sin(2\pi\delta_e)\Bigr) S_N(-2\cos(2\pi oldsymbol\delta))\ &\ 	imes\exp\!\left\{N\sum_e [\pi i n_e\delta_e^2+2\pi i\ell_e\delta_e]ight\} d oldsymbol\delta . \end{split}	ag{10} \] This is the same local source-independent finite functional as in section 1 of [original whole spectral period](general_localized_unit_charge_filling_period.md). Its charge-zero absence and whole-domain absolute summability hold before any geometric estimate. The proof uses the local matrix identity, the entire finite-degree numerator, and its original sine endpoint factors; it does not use a plat sweep. All side currents in a subsequent contour deformation would still have to be retained. The raw scalar in (10) is the actual original reduced ribbon contraction of the filled link constructed above. Its conversion to the specified zero-framed enhanced Kashaev convention is the original recorded framing/component character. At complete color its modulus is one; for a knot the enhanced component sign is one. If instead using the full one-cut modified convention, retain its additional \(i^{N+3}/N\). These exact distinctions are proved in [complete source normalization](actual_complete_augmented_source_normalization.md), using local crossing/duality identities and scalar cut maps; they do not depend on the bridge count. No extra quantum dimension, semicircle normalization, or exponential basis factor has appeared here. For the complete augmented link, the original local crossing-circle contraction is still its exact \(L_N\) coupon, with its one ordinary auxiliary trace and no extra modified dimension. Thus (1)–(2) apply to that source too. A geometric certificate identifies its two cut balls with the original right-angled polyhedron and gives the actual augmented exterior, as in section 2; a volume asymptotic requires its own verified analytic hypotheses. ## 7. Scope needed by a diagonal-choice argument This theorem constructs an actual source for **each** diagonal choice on the fixed quadrangulation. The constructed links for different choices need not be isotopic, their marked coefficient polytopes need not coincide, and no projected sector or physical operator is moved from one choice to another. The common quadrangulation supplies a common finite combinatorial indexing only. Every original target, half-index coset, retained half-twist and disk-framed signed filling coordinate has now been supplied for that choice. Consequently a proposed complete-capacity-maximizing choice can refer to a genuine original source rather than a formal entropy model. This does not by itself prove its global source estimate, local filling packet, nonzero period, hyperbolicity, or volume limit. Those hypotheses must be checked on the chosen diagram. In particular no old flat-plat gap forest or prescribed bridge width has been transported merely by constructing a general Morse source. ## scope All finite matrix ingredients are the original duality, homogeneous source, all-MAIN compiler, and local full-Hermite filling functional. No new numerical audit is asserted for this constructive proof. No global spectral comparison, filling asymptotic, prescribed plat width, or equality between sources from different diagonal choices is claimed.

title: Scalar compatibility of the actual microscopic endpoint in the physical bulk
text:
# Scalar compatibility of the actual microscopic endpoint in the physical bulk Private written proof, 16 November 2026. The actual value and first spectral normal of a microscopic endpoint kernel admit one polynomially bounded holomorphic scalar representative on every buffered physical bulk interval. The two source coefficients in the prior normal-defect transport are exponentially small. The argument combines its moderate separate channels with an exact alternating analytic expression for their difference; both parity subgrids are essential. Locally the scalar representative can be chosen to be an actual partial Newton sum. Its bounded complex neighborhood can be thin. No endpoint extension, whole-period representative, contour connector estimate, or filled-source rate follows. ## 1. Original data and the assertion Put \[ D=N-1,\quad \eta=(-1)^D,\quad 	heta=\pi/N,\quad m=\lfloor N/2floor,\quad J=\lfloor(N-1)/2floor,\quad k_0=\lceil N/2ceil=J+1, \] \[ c_j=2\cos((2j+1)	heta),\quad e_k(Z)=S_k^{-2}\prod_{a<k}(c_a-Z),\quad S_k=\prod_{a=1}^k2\sin(a	heta),\quad S_0=1, \] \[ K_N(w,Z)=\sum_{k=0}^{D}e_k(w)e_k(Z),\qquad w_N(\alpha)=2\cosh(\alpha/N),\qquad B_N(Z,\alpha)=K_N(w_N(\alpha),Z). 	ag{1} \] The distinct physical nodes are \(c_0,\ldots,c_J\). All are double roots of \(P_N(Z)=2T_N(Z/2)+2\), except the odd simple node \(c_J=-2\). Use the normalized index and its angular coordinates \[ x_j=j/N,\quad 
u_N(x)=2\pi x+\pi/N,\quad 	au_N(x)=\pi-
u_N(x),\quad c_N(x)=2\cos
u_N(x), \] \[ c_N'(x)=-4\pi\sin
u_N(x),\qquad F_j=B_N(c_j,\alpha),\quad G_j=\partial_ZB_N(c_j,\alpha). 	ag{2} \] Fix nested nondegenerate closed intervals \[ I_0\Subset\operatorname{int}I_1,\qquad I_1\Subset\operatorname{int}I_2,\qquad I_2\Subset(0,1/2). 	ag{3} \] All parameters are allowed in an arbitrary fixed bounded complex disk. Larger fixed disks and smaller spatial domains are used for derivative estimates. Call \(f_N(x,\alpha)\) admissible if it is holomorphic on a fixed neighborhood of \(I_2\) and a larger parameter disk, has a bound \(\lVert f_NVert\le CN^p\), and satisfies \[ f_N(x_j,\alpha)=F_j(\alpha) \quad(x_j\in I_2). 	ag{4} \] The two-channel source supplies such a family and, separately, a polynomially bounded holomorphic \(\mathcal G_N\) with \(\mathcal G_N(x_j,\alpha)=G_j(\alpha)\). Intersect its domain with that of any chosen admissible \(f_N\). **Theorem 1.** For every admissible \(f_N\), there are a fixed complex neighborhood \(U\) of \(I_0\) and constants \(C,P,c>0\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(N\), \[ d_N(x,\alpha):=c_N'(x)\mathcal G_N(x,\alpha)-\partial_xf_N(x,\alpha) =O_{m hol}(N^Pe^{-cN})\quad(x\in U). 	ag{5} \] Here and below fixed derivatives are bounded on smaller spatial and parameter domains. In particular the actual nodal defect \[ \Delta_{j,N}=c_N'(x_j)G_j-\partial_xf_N(x_j) 	ag{6} \] is exponentially small on \(I_0\). Both actual anchor coefficients of the two-mode normal-defect theorem are exponentially small. There is a polynomially bounded holomorphic scalar \(h_N\) on a fixed smaller bulk neighborhood, jointly holomorphic in \(\alpha\), such that at every physical node in \(I_0\) \[ h_N(x_j)=F_j,\qquad h_N'(x_j)=c_N'(x_j)G_j. 	ag{7} \] It differs from \(f_N\) by an exponentially small holomorphic function on that neighborhood. All assertions hold at both parities and uniformly on bounded complex parameter sets, including zeros of \(\cosh(\alpha/2)\). ## 2. A polynomially bounded distinct-root quotient Let \(L_N(Z,\alpha)\) be the ordinary degree-\(J\) interpolation of the \(F_j\)'s at all distinct physical nodes. It is exactly the low Newton part of \(B_N\). Indeed the remaining Newton polynomials vanish at all distinct nodes, and the degree-\(J\) interpolation is unique. The endpoint-product source proves, on every bounded complex parameter disk, \[ \sup_{Z\in[-2,2]}|L_N(Z,\alpha)|\le CN^p. 	ag{8} \] Its proof uses the actual physical row values and ordinary Chebyshev interpolation; it does not require the endpoint parameter to stay below its first imaginary zero. Write \(\mathcal P_N\) for the monic distinct-root polynomial. Its exact formulas are \[  egin{array}{ll} N=2m:&\mathcal P_N(Z)=2T_m(Z/2),\ N=2m+1:&\mathcal P_N(Z)=2T_{m+1}(Z/2)+2T_m(Z/2). \end{array} \] Consequently \[ \mathcal P_N(c_N(x))=-a_N(x)\sin(\pi Nx),\qquad a_N(x)=  egin{cases} 2,&N	ext{ even},\ 4\cos(\pi x+\pi/(2N)),&N	ext{ odd}. \end{cases} 	ag{9} \] On a sufficiently small fixed bulk neighborhood \(a_N\) is a uniform unit. Define \[ g_N(x,\alpha)=  rac{L_N(c_N(x),\alpha)-f_N(x,\alpha)} {\mathcal P_N(c_N(x))}. 	ag{10} \] All its apparent poles on a buffered bulk domain are removable: the sine zeros there are precisely \(x_j=j/N\), and (4) makes the numerator zero at each. Division is jointly holomorphic in the parameter. There are no additional zeros from \(a_N\). Here it is important that this quotient has polynomial norm, despite the ordinary interpolant's possible off-real growth. From (8), each Chebyshev coefficient of \(L_N\) has modulus at most twice its real norm. Thus, for \(x=X+iY\), \[ |L_N(c_N(x),\alpha)| \le CN^{p+1}e^{2\pi J|Y|},\qquad 2J<N. 	ag{11} \] Choose a rectangle enclosing a fixed neighborhood of \(I_1\), whose closure lies in the common analytic domain over \(I_2\). Its horizontal sides have fixed heights \(\pm h_0\). Move its vertical sides by \(O(N^{-1})\) so their real parts are \((j+1/2)/N\), retaining fixed buffers. On either vertical side, \[ |\sin(\pi Nx)|=\cosh(\pi NY)\ge	frac12e^{\pi N|Y|}; \] on either horizontal side it is at least \(\sinh(\pi Nh_0)\ge c_0e^{\pi Nh_0}\) for large \(N\). Equations (9)--(11), \(2J<N\), and the polynomial bound for \(f_N\) therefore bound \(g_N\) by a fixed power of \(N\) on the whole boundary. The maximum principle gives the same bound inside. Cauchy's formula gives polynomial bounds for its fixed derivatives on a fixed smaller rectangle. This argument is uniform in the larger parameter disk. At a grid point, differentiation of (10) now gives exactly \[ \partial_x[L_N(c_N(x))-f_N(x)]_{x=x_j} =-\pi N(-1)^j a_N(x_j)g_N(x_j). 	ag{12} \] ## 3. An exact analytic high normal on every local bulk chart We recall enough of the general-domain source to verify both its normalization and its applicability throughout the physical bulk. For \(0<\delta<1/2\), let \(L=\lfloor\delta Nfloor\) and \[ (A_\ell,B_\ell)=  egin{cases} ((\ell+	frac12)	heta,(\ell+1)	heta),&N	ext{ even},\ ((\ell+1)	heta,(\ell+	frac32)	heta),&N	ext{ odd}, \end{cases} \] \[ ho_{\ell,N}(\alpha,t)=  rac{[\cos^2A_\ell+\sinh^2(\alpha/(2N))] [\sin^2(t/2)-\sin^2A_\ell]}{\cos^4B_\ell}, \qquad \Gamma_N^\delta(\alpha,t) =T_{0,N}(\alpha,t)\sum_{\ell=0}^{L}\prod_{r<\ell}ho_{r,N}, 	ag{13} \] \[ T_{0,N}(\alpha,t)=  egin{cases} N^{-1}\cosh(\alpha/2)\sin t,&N	ext{ even},\[2pt] \displaystyle  rac{\cosh(\alpha/2)\cosh(\alpha/(2N))} {N\cos^4(	heta/2)}\sin t\sin(t/2),&N	ext{ odd}. \end{cases} 	ag{14} \] Let \(B_N^{m high}=B_N-L_N\). Its exact physical normal is \[ \eta(4-c_j^2)(B_N^{m high})'(c_j,\alpha) =\eta(-1)^j\gamma_{j,N}(\alpha). 	ag{15} \] For every fixed \(b<2\pi\delta\), the source proves, at all sufficiently large levels, \[ \Gamma_N^\delta(\alpha,	au_N(x_j)) =\gamma_{j,N}(\alpha)\qquad (0<	au_N(x_j)\le b). 	ag{16} \] This is exact for every complex \(\alpha\): a factor in the finite lowering product vanishes when its actual physical chain stops. It is not an asymptotic interpolation. Put \(a_\delta=\sin^2(\pi\delta)\). On every compact subset of \[ \mathcal D_\delta =\{t:|\sin^2(t/2)-a_\delta|<1-a_\delta\}, 	ag{17} \] all the ratios in (13) have modulus at most a common \(q<1\) for large \(N\), uniformly for bounded complex \(\alpha\). Thus \(\Gamma_N^\delta=O_{m hol}(N^{-1})\) there. No division by the base factors in (14) is needed. Every fixed physical bulk point admits both (16) and (17) on the same local chart. To see this, fix \(x_0\in(0,1/2)\), and put \(	au_0=\pi-2\pi x_0\), \(z_0=\sin^2(	au_0/2)<1\). Choose \(\delta\) so that \[ z_0<a_\delta<(1+z_0)/2. 	ag{18} \] Then \(\delta>	au_0/(2\pi)\), while \(|z_0-a_\delta|<1-a_\delta\). There is therefore a fixed complex neighborhood of \(	au_0\), compactly contained in (17), whose real angles lie in \(0<t<b<2\pi\delta\). A fixed local \(x\)-disk and all sufficiently large \(N\) satisfy these conditions under \(t=	au_N(x)\). The \(O(N^{-1})\) offset has been absorbed into fixed margins. A finite collection of such charts covers \(I_0\). In particular a cutoff larger than \(1/4\), when needed, causes no problem: its symbol domain need not contain zero, but it does contain the local angle in (18). This is the domain fact that allows the argument on arbitrary compact physical bulk intervals. Since \(4-c_j^2=4\sin^2
u_N(x_j)\), (2), (15), and (16) give \[ c_N'(x_j)(B_N^{m high})'(c_j) =(-1)^{j+1}  rac{\pi\Gamma_N^\delta(\alpha,	au_N(x_j))} {\sin
u_N(x_j)}. 	ag{19} \] Combining (12) and (19) proves the exact local identity \[ \Delta_{j,N}=(-1)^j\mathcal A_N^\delta(x_j,\alpha), \qquad \mathcal A_N^\delta(x,\alpha)= -\pi N a_N(x)g_N(x,\alpha) - rac{\pi\Gamma_N^\delta(\alpha,	au_N(x))} {\sin
u_N(x)}. 	ag{20} \] The function \(\mathcal A_N^\delta\) has polynomial norm on a fixed local chart. The factor \(\sin
u_N\) is a uniform unit there. Equation (20) retains the actual first spectral normal and its parity sign. ## 4. Two dense subgrids force the actual defect to be small We use the following elementary analytic observation. Suppose \(d_N\) and \(a_N^\circ\) are holomorphic on a fixed disk about a real point, have a polynomial norm bound, and \[ d_N(j/N)=(-1)^j a_N^\circ(j/N) 	ag{21} \] at every grid point in its central real interval. Then \(d_N-a_N^\circ\) vanishes on the even subgrid and \(d_N+a_N^\circ\) on the odd subgrid. For an explicit estimate, take a closed disk of radius \(R\) within the domain. The real interval of radius \(R/8\) contains at least \(RN/16\) nodes of each parity for large \(N\). For \(|z-x_0|\le R/8\) and a zero \(a\) in that same interval, the disk Blaschke factor is bounded by \[ \left| rac{R(z-a)}{R^2-\overline{(a-x_0)}(z-x_0)}ight| \le rac{16}{63}< rac13. 	ag{22} \] Dividing by all those factors and applying the maximum principle gives \(CN^P3^{-RN/16}\) for each of \(d_N\pm a_N^\circ\) on the smaller disk. Hence both \(d_N\) and \(a_N^\circ\) are exponentially small there. Fixed derivatives have the same type of estimate on a smaller disk by Cauchy's formula. The argument is uniform in holomorphic parameters when the original norm bounds are uniform on a larger parameter domain. Apply this observation to \(d_N\) from (5) and \(a_N^\circ=\mathcal A_N^\delta\) from (20). The separate normal interpolant gives \(d_N(x_j)=\Delta_{j,N}\), so (21) is exact. Both functions are polynomially bounded on a common fixed disk. The finite cover from Section 3 now gives a common positive exponential rate and a fixed complex neighborhood of \(I_0\). This proves (5)--(6), as well as exponential smallness of each local \(\mathcal A_N^\delta\). In particular no approximate oscillatory Fourier transform has been used. Here is the consequence for the prior two-mode transport in its exact normalization. At a bulk node let \[ D_j^f=  egin{pmatrix} \Delta_{j,N}\ N(\Delta_{j,N}-\Delta_{j-1,N}) \end{pmatrix}. 	ag{23} \] At an anchor in the interior of \(I_0\), both components are \(O(N^Pe^{-cN})\), increasing \(P\) if necessary. In the pinned transport theorem the actual source coefficients are \[ \mathbf a_N^f(\alpha) =\Phi(x_{*,N},\alpha)^{-1}D_{j_*}^f. 	ag{24} \] Its regular fundamental matrix has columns generated by \[  rac{\cos((\alpha/\pi)\log\sin\pi x)}{\sin\pi x}, \qquad  rac{\sin((\alpha/\pi)\log\sin\pi x)} {(\alpha/\pi)\sin\pi x}, 	ag{25} \] and their derivatives. The second expression has its removable logarithmic value at \(\alpha=0\). Its determinant is \(\pi\cos(\pi x)/\sin^3(\pi x)\), a bulk unit. Thus \(\Phi^{-1}\) is uniformly bounded on the fixed compact domains. Equation (24) proves exponential smallness of both actual coefficients, also at the coalescing parameter. These coefficients have not been selected or reset. ## 5. Explicit local scalars and a scalar on the full compact interval On a chart with its chosen \(\delta\), define \[ h_N^\delta(x,\alpha)=L_N(c_N(x),\alpha) - rac{\Gamma_N^\delta(\alpha,	au_N(x))} {N\sin
u_N(x)}\sin(\pi Nx). 	ag{26} \] At grid nodes its second term has value zero. Its derivative there is exactly the high-normal correction (19). Thus (26) matches both original channels on the chart without an approximation. Equations (9), (10), and (20) also give the exact identity \[ h_N^\delta-f_N = rac{\sin(\pi Nx)}{\pi N}\mathcal A_N^\delta. 	ag{27} \] The exponential estimate just proved beats the sine growth on a sufficiently thin fixed strip. Therefore (26) is polynomially bounded there and exponentially close to \(f_N\). There is also a literal polynomial interpretation. With \(L=\lfloor\delta Nfloor\) and large \(N\), \[ h_N^\delta(x,\alpha) =\sum_{k=0}^{k_0+L}e_k(w_N(\alpha))e_k(c_N(x)). 	ag{28} \] To check the constants, at even \(N=2m\), \(S_m^2=2N\), so \[ e_m(w)e_m(Z)= rac{\cosh(\alpha/2)}{2N^2}\mathcal P_N(Z). 	ag{29} \] At odd \(N=2m+1\), \(S_{m+1}^2=4N\cos^2(	heta/2)\), and \[ e_{m+1}(w)e_{m+1}(Z) = rac{\cosh(\alpha/2)\cosh(\alpha/(2N))} {4N^2\cos^4(	heta/2)}\mathcal P_N(Z). 	ag{30} \] These follow directly from the products in (1), the monic distinct-root formulas, and \(S_{N-1}=N\). For \(Z=-2\cos t\), the ratio of successive products beginning at \(k=k_0\) is precisely \(ho_{\ell,N}(\alpha,t)\). Indeed their numerator is \(16[\cos^2A_\ell+\sinh^2(\alpha/(2N))] [\sin^2(t/2)-\sin^2A_\ell]\) and their denominator is \(16\cos^4B_\ell\). Summing and using (9), (13)--(14) gives (28). The bound is on the thin local domain supplied by (27); it asserts nothing about this polynomial at a larger height. For one scalar covering all of \(I_0\), the exact repair in the pinned two-mode theorem can be used directly: \[ h_N(x,\alpha)=f_N(x,\alpha)+ \sum_{j:\,x_j\in I_0} \Delta_{j,N}(\alpha)(x-x_j)\operatorname{sinc}^2(Nx-j), \quad \operatorname{sinc}z= rac{\sin\pi z}{\pi z}. 	ag{31} \] Each term has zero value at every grid point, derivative \(\Delta_{j,N}\) at its own point, and a double zero at the others. This proves (7) exactly. There are \(O(N)\) terms and \(|\operatorname{sinc}^2(Nx-j)|\le e^{2\pi N|\Im x|}\). Thus the correction is at most \(CN^{P+1}e^{-cN+2\pi N|\Im x|}\). Choose a fixed strip height less than \(c/(4\pi)\) within the common domain. The correction is exponentially small and \(h_N\) has polynomial norm. This proves all scalar assertions of Theorem 1. On a sufficiently narrow bulk strip \(x\mapsto c_N(x)\) is one-to-one, with derivative bounded away from zero. Equality of two cosines requires \(x-y\in\mathbb Z\) or \(x+y+1/N\in\mathbb Z\); the first gives \(x=y\), and the second is excluded by the fixed buffers inside \((0,1/2)\). Its inverse converts (26) locally, or (31) on the compact interval, into a scalar spectral representative with exactly the original value and first normal. ## 6. Shared products and original trace placement For any fixed number of microscopic endpoint factors, take their scalar representatives on a common smaller domain and multiply them before tracing. Their product has polynomial norm and its value and first spectral normal agree exactly with those of the original shared product, by the ordinary product rule. All fixed derivatives in the separate bounded complex endpoint parameters are retained on smaller parameter sets. For example, with an arbitrary actual joint spectator \(A(Z)\), the original contribution of these bulk rows for one endpoint is \[ \eta\sum_{x_j\in I_0} \left[(4-c_j^2)\{G_jA(c_j)+F_jA'(c_j)\} -c_jF_jA(c_j)ight]. 	ag{32} \] Replacing \(F_j,G_j\) by the value and spectral derivative of the scalar representative leaves (32) exactly unchanged. A crossing, its carrier and first normal, all shared graph kernels, all other traces, and ordinary free boundary variables may remain in \(A\). The assertion is coefficientwise in those uncontracted variables; their growth is not bounded by the present theorem. Products at several traced vertices preserve the full mixed normals by repeated ordinary differentiation. No quotient reduction is imposed in a free variable. Only the covered bulk rows have been replaced. The odd simple node, both physical endpoint regions, external connectors, and all remaining source currents stay in the original expression. Polynomial local scalar size does not supply a filled-action estimate or prove a nonzero contribution. In particular there is no conflict with the lower bound for a full-period even Hermite representative: the domains and the required endpoint coverage are different. ## 7. Coverage and direct sources The prior two-channel theorem supplied moderate separate value and normal interpolants, while the two-mode theorem isolated their unknown true compatibility coefficients. The general radical-domain theorem supplied exact high normals with analytic control, but had not combined its locally varying cutoff with those two channels. The new step is (18)--(22): exact physical termination on a suitable chart at every bulk point, followed by the two dense parity subgrids. It proves smallness of the actual compatibility coefficients and gives the scalar representatives (26), (28), and (31). All four complete direct source texts were freshly read in this author sequence, and their used implications and hashes checked: * [General endpoint radical domain](research_endpoint_radical_general_domain.md), SHA256 600ae0d78f29946272ed54b600cb1f5fdf170965985a08d6e3d9201303722074: exact finite lowering amplitude, both normal signs, physical termination, and the complex contraction domain. * [Actual two-channel interpolation](research_microscopic_endpoint_two_channel_interpolation.md), SHA256 44f6db0f8afdf1205ab8b0935b95b8a4fd9fa16c6414be2467b8b40a123c0ffe: jointly holomorphic moderate interpolation of the actual values and normals, with bounded complex microscopic parameters. * [Two half-plane endpoint-product source](research_endpoint_two_half_plane_relative_source.md), SHA256 985fa3331379c3877734f28773d314b667ee87fa63314a5ef4513a3fe128d194: polynomial real norm of the ordinary low interpolation, original full-normal trace, and shared-product placement. * [True two-mode normal-defect transport](research_endpoint_normal_defect_two_mode_transport.md), SHA256 91620d1ea26793157843f78fff32c7d3eca62509799114a2d3069af8b96b47dc: actual anchor normalization, bounded regular fundamental matrix, and exact scalar Hermite repair. Only written mathematics, source-text reads, and file hashes were used. No mathematical program, numerical experiment, test, or build was run. Adopted notes and public manuscripts remain unchanged.

title: Moderate bulk interpolation of the actual endpoint value and normal channels
text:
# Moderate bulk interpolation of the actual endpoint value and normal channels Private written proof, 16 November 2026. A uniformly analytic matrix recurrence whose step is \(I+O(N^{-1})\) has an exact holomorphic interpolation on a fixed narrow strip, with the same polynomial size as its nodal data. A discrete Newton construction first gives bounded exact local interpolants. Their many common zeros make the overlap errors exponentially small. A Cauchy correction and a final sinc repair produce one exact global vector. For the original microscopic endpoint kernel, the physical value and common-index normal form such a four-component recurrence. The result therefore retains both channels without dividing by the value, which can vanish. It does **not** identify the interpolated normal with the derivative of the interpolated value. This distinction is essential for placing the result in the original trace. ## 1. An analytic near-identity recurrence Let \(I=[a,b]\), \(a<b\), and fix \(R>0\). Write \[ \Omega_R=\{z\in\mathbb C:\operatorname{dist}(z,I)<R\},\qquad h=N^{-1}. \] Suppose \(T_N\) is a \(d\)-by-\(d\) holomorphic matrix on a neighborhood of \(\overline{\Omega_R}\), and \[ \|T_N-I_d\|_{\Omega_R}\le A_0h. 	ag{1} \] Let vectors \(y_j\) be given at all grid points \(x_j=jh\) in the real interval \([a-R/2,b+R/2]\), with \[ y_{j+1}=T_N(x_j)y_j,\qquad \|y_j\|\le M_N 	ag{2} \] whenever the indicated indices are in this interval. Holomorphic parameters are permitted, with (1)--(2) uniform on a fixed larger parameter set. **Theorem 1.** There are \(r>0\), \(c>0\), \(C<\infty\), and \(N_0\), depending only on \(I,R,A_0,d\), such that for \(N\ge N_0\) there is a holomorphic vector \(Y_N\) on \[ \mathcal R_r=\{a-r<\Re z<b+r,\ |\Im z|<r\} \] with \[ Y_N(j/N)=y_j\quad(j/N\in I),\qquad \|Y_N\|_{\mathcal R_r}\le C M_N. 	ag{3} \] The construction preserves holomorphic dependence on the parameters. It consists of bounded exact local Newton polynomials, exponentially small overlap and gluing errors, and a final correction bounded by \(CM_Ne^{-cN}\) on this strip. Fixed derivatives have the same bound \(C_kM_N\) on smaller fixed strips and parameter sets. One polynomially bounded anchor in (2) suffices to obtain the stated bound for all its real nodes, after changing a constant. Indeed, for large \(N\), \(\|T_N\|\le1+A_0h\) and \(\|T_N^{-1}\|\le1+2A_0h\). There are \(O_I(N)\) steps in the fixed buffered interval. Forward and backward multiplication therefore cost a constant independent of \(N\). No eigenvector, logarithm of a scalar solution, or nonvanishing assumption is involved. ### Exact local Newton polynomials Here are constants and domains for a proof. Put \[ \delta=R/4,\qquad C_0=e(2/\delta+A_0), \] and fix \[ 0<\ell<\min\{R/64,\delta/4,1/(100C_0)\}. 	ag{4} \] We increase \(N_0\) whenever a displayed elementary grid condition is needed, in particular \(h\le\ell/16\). Local anchors are grid points in \([a-2\ell,b+2\ell]\), so their closed \(\delta\)-disks lie inside \(\Omega_R\). Define matrix functions \[ B_0(x)=I_d,\qquad B_{k+1}(x)= rac{B_k(x+h)T_N(x)-B_k(x)}h. 	ag{5} \] For every available string of nodes, induction on \(k\) gives \[ \Delta^k y_j=h^k B_k(x_j)y_j. 	ag{6} \] To estimate \(B_k\), use \(k\) nested disks about its anchor, each losing radius \(\delta/k\). If \(kh\le\delta/2\), a segment of length \(h\) still leaves Cauchy radius at least \(\delta/(2k)\). Since \[ B_{l+1}= rac{B_l(x+h)-B_l(x)}h +B_l(x+h) rac{T_N(x)-I_d}{h}, \] Cauchy's estimate at each step yields \[ \|B_k(x_j)\|\le(2k/\delta+A_0)^k \le C_0^k k!. 	ag{7} \] The final inequality uses \(k!\ge(k/e)^k\); the case \(k=0\) is read separately. The same nested-disk argument applies componentwise in a fixed matrix norm, or in an operator norm using the vector-valued Cauchy integral. Set \(L=\lfloor\ell/hfloor\). The Newton polynomial at the anchor \(x_j\) is \[ P_j(z)=\sum_{k=0}^{L}  inom{(z-x_j)/h}{k}\Delta^k y_j. 	ag{8} \] It matches the entire string \(y_j,\ldots,y_{j+L}\) exactly. Combining (6)--(7) with \[ h^k k!\left| inom{(z-x_j)/h}{k}ight| =\prod_{v=0}^{k-1}|z-x_j-vh| \le(|z-x_j|+\ell)^k \] gives \[ \|P_j(z)\|\le M_N\sum_{k=0}^{L} [C_0(|z-x_j|+\ell)]^k\le2M_N \quad(|z-x_j|\le8\ell). 	ag{9} \] Thus its degree grows with \(N\), but its norm on this fixed disk does not. Its initial bound uses no cancellation of large coefficients. ### Exponentially small overlaps Take successive anchors separated by \(J h\), where \(J=\lfloor L/2floor\). Start with the largest grid point not exceeding \(a-\ell\), and stop when the last block covers \(b+\ell\). There are a bounded number of blocks, independent of \(N\), all within the real buffered interval. The estimates \[ Lh\ge15\ell/16,\qquad 13\ell/32\le Jh\le\ell/2 	ag{10} \] hold under the preceding grid restriction. Adjacent polynomials have the common nodes from index \(j+J\) through \(j+L\). Their number \(K=L-J+1\) is at least \(\ell/(3h)\). Let \(o\) be the midpoint of this common interval. Every common node is within \(\ell/3\) of \(o\). Both polynomials are bounded by \(2M_N\) on the disk \(|z-o|\le6\ell\), since this disk lies inside their respective disks in (9). For clarity, the elementary zeros estimate used here is explicit. An analytic scalar \(f\), bounded by \(M\) on \(|z-o|\le R_1\), with zeros \(a_
u\) in that disk, satisfies \[ |f(z)|\le M\prod_
u \left| rac{R_1(z-a_
u)} {R_1^2-\overline{(a_
u-o)}(z-o)}ight|. 	ag{11} \] Divide by the displayed disk Blaschke factors and apply the maximum principle; their boundary moduli are one and the apparent poles at the zeros are removable. With \(R_1=6\ell\), \(|a_
u-o|\le\ell/3\), and \(|z-o|\le2\ell\), each factor is at most \(42/106<1/2\). Applied to every component of the difference, this gives \[ \|P_{j+J}-P_j\|_{|z-o|\le2\ell} \le C_d M_Ne^{-\kappa N},\qquad \kappa=\ell\log2/3. 	ag{12} \] All constants are uniform in the holomorphic parameters. ### Global gluing and exact nodal repair Use real smooth transition functions only in the intervals \(|\Re z-o|<\ell/8\). These intervals are disjoint by (10); they lie strictly inside the common-node intervals, whose half-length is at least \(15\ell/64\). Interpolate from one polynomial to the next with a fixed smooth function of \((\Re z-o)/\ell\). Outside transitions use the single appropriate polynomial. This defines a smooth vector \(F_N\) on \[ \mathcal R^{\,0} =\{a-\ell/4<\Re z<b+\ell/4,\ |\Im z|<\ell/2\}. \] The first and last blocks provide the indicated outer buffers. Only polynomials whose exact node block contains \(x_j\) are used at a real grid point \(x_j\in I\). Hence \[ F_N(x_j)=y_j,\qquad \|F_N\|\le CM_N,\qquad \| ar\partial F_N\|\le CM_Ne^{-\kappa N}. 	ag{13} \] The fixed factor \(1/\ell\) is included in \(C\). To check the last bound, in a transition the derivative is one half the real derivative of its cutoff times \(P_{j+J}-P_j\). These points lie in the disks of (12). Away from the transitions that derivative is zero. Choose a smooth cutoff supported in \(\mathcal R^{\,0}\) and equal to one on \[ \mathcal R^{\,1} =\{a-\ell/8<\Re z<b+\ell/8,\ |\Im z|<\ell/4\}. \] Extend its product with \( ar\partial F_N\) by zero, calling the result \(f_N\). Its plane Cauchy transform \[ u_N(z)= rac1\pi\int_{\mathbb C}  rac{f_N(\zeta)}{z-\zeta}\,dA(\zeta) 	ag{14} \] satisfies \( ar\partial u_N=f_N\). This is the Cauchy--Pompeiu identity for a smooth compactly supported density. The kernel is locally integrable and the support lies in a fixed bounded set, so \[ \|u_N\|_{\mathbb C} \le CM_Ne^{-\kappa N}. 	ag{15} \] Thus \(H_N=F_N-u_N\) is holomorphic on \(\mathcal R^{\,1}\), and its nodal error is precisely \(u_N(x_j)\). Use \(\operatorname{sinc}(z)=\sin(\pi z)/(\pi z)\), with value one at zero, and set \[ S_N(z)=\sum_{j:\,j/N\in I}u_N(j/N)\operatorname{sinc}(Nz-j), \qquad Y_N=H_N+S_N. 	ag{16} \] This finite sum repairs every node exactly. The integral identity \(\operatorname{sinc}(z)=\int_{-1/2}^{1/2}e^{2\pi izs}\,ds\) gives \[ |S_N(z)|\le CM_N N e^{-\kappa N+\pi N|\Im z|}. 	ag{17} \] Choose \[ r<\min\{\ell/8,\kappa/(4\pi)\}. 	ag{18} \] On \(\mathcal R_r\), (17) is at most \(CM_Ne^{-\kappa N/2}\), after enlarging a constant and \(N_0\). This proves (3). The correction (14) and (16) is exponentially small relative to \(M_N\); on each transition the local polynomials already differ by (12). All operations are linear in the vector data, and the cutoffs and integration contours do not depend on external parameters. The integrals therefore preserve their holomorphic dependence. Cauchy's formula on smaller fixed domains proves the derivative statement. This completes the proof of Theorem 1. This construction proves a bounded vector interpolation, not an exact off-grid solution of the original difference equation. Its remaining source interpretation must use the exact nodal identities. ## 2. The actual microscopic endpoint system Use the original data \[ 	heta=\pi/N,\quad D=N-1,\quad \eta=(-1)^D,\quad s_r=2\sin(r	heta),\quad S_j=\prod_{r=1}^j s_r,\quad S_0=1,\quad c(r)=2\cos((2r+1)	heta), \] \[ P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2,\qquad e_j(z)=S_j^{-2}\prod_{r<j}(c(r)-z),\qquad K_N(z,w)=\sum_{j=0}^{D}e_j(z)e_j(w). 	ag{19} \] Fix \(0<a<b<1/2\), \(I=[a,b]\), and any bounded complex parameter disk \(|\alpha|\le A\). Put \[ w_N(\alpha)=2\cosh(\alpha/N),\quad F_j(\alpha)=K_N(c(j),w_N(\alpha)),\quad G_j(\alpha)=\partial_zK_N(c(j),w_N(\alpha)). \] The parameter disk may be enlarged whenever fixed parameter derivatives are wanted. The original difference coefficients are \[ A_N(r)= rac{s_{r+1}^4}{s_{2r+1}s_{2r+2}},\qquad C_N(r)= rac{s_r^4}{s_{2r}s_{2r+1}},\qquad c'(r)=-4	heta\sin((2r+1)	heta). 	ag{20} \] The subscript distinguishes the coefficient \(A_N\) from the bound on \(\alpha\). The literal off-grid source identity is \[  egin{split} A_N(r)K_N(c(r+1),w) ={}&(c(0)+A_N(r)+C_N(r)-w)K_N(c(r),w)\ &-C_N(r)K_N(c(r-1),w) + rac{\eta P_N(w)}{N^2}e_D(c(r)). \end{split} 	ag{21} \] This is the full polynomial identity, before specialization or differentiation. At every bulk physical index \(j\ge1\) under consideration, \(e_D(c(j))=e_D'(c(j))=0\): the corresponding spectral root occurs twice in \(e_D\). Therefore the source in (21) and its common-index derivative both vanish there. They have not been discarded at \(j=0\) or away from the physical grid. Define, for \(x=r/N\), \[ q_N(x)=C_N(Nx)/A_N(Nx),\qquad d_N(x)= rac{c(0)-w_N(\alpha)}{A_N(Nx)},\qquad T_N(x)=  egin{pmatrix} 1+d_N(x)&q_N(x)/N\ Nd_N(x)&q_N(x) \end{pmatrix}. 	ag{22} \] The exact value vector and its scaled common-index normal are \[ X_j= inom{F_j}{N(F_j-F_{j-1})},\qquad U_j=c'(j)G_j,\qquad Y_j= inom{NU_j}{N^2(U_j-U_{j-1})}. 	ag{23} \] Equation (21) and its derivative give exactly \[ X_{j+1}=T_N(j/N)X_j,\qquad Y_{j+1}=T_N(j/N)Y_j+(\partial_xT_N)(j/N)X_j. 	ag{24} \] For the derivative equation, \(Y_j\) is \(N\) times the common-index derivative of the displayed off-grid value vector. The chain rule for \(T_N(r/N)\) supplies \(\partial_xT_N\), with no missing factor of \(N\). All terms involving the endpoint source vanish only for the bulk indices just specified. Consequently \(Z_j=(X_j,Y_j)^T\) obeys the exact four-component recurrence \[ Z_{j+1}=\mathbb T_N(j/N)Z_j,\qquad \mathbb T_N(x)=  egin{pmatrix}T_N(x)&0\ \partial_xT_N(x)&T_N(x)\end{pmatrix}. 	ag{25} \] Choose a fixed sufficiently small \(R>0\) such that the closure of \(\Omega_R\) stays away from \(0\) and \(1/2\), and from the zero sets of their sine and cosine denominators. On a slightly larger such domain, uniformly for bounded complex \(\alpha\), \[ A_N(Nx)=	an^2(\pi x)+O(N^{-1}),\quad q_N(x)=1+O(N^{-1}),\quad d_N(x)=O(N^{-2}). 	ag{26} \] Here \(c(0)-w_N(\alpha)=-(\pi^2+\alpha^2)N^{-2}+O(N^{-4})\); the limiting \(A_N\) is a unit. Direct holomorphic substitution in (20), followed by Cauchy estimates on the larger domain, proves (26) with all fixed \(x\)-derivatives. In particular \[ \mathbb T_N=I_4+O(N^{-1}) 	ag{27} \] uniformly and holomorphically. No scalar root of a characteristic equation or of \(F_j\) is used. ## 3. Polynomial initial size and exact two-channel interpolation The pinned endpoint-product theorem, with one factor, gives \[ \sup_{z\in[-2,2],\ |\alpha|\le A} |K_N(z,w_N(\alpha))|\le C_A N^{p_A}. 	ag{28} \] It holds on every bounded complex parameter disk, not only below the first endpoint zero. Its proof compares the physical values to one fixed low physical row and retains the whole high radical. Markov's inequality for the ordinary degree-\(D\) kernel gives \[ |G_j(\alpha)|\le C_A N^{p_A+2}. 	ag{29} \] Since \(|c'(j)|\le4\pi/N\), (23) yields the sufficient bound \[ \|Z_j\|\le C_A N^{p_A+3} 	ag{30} \] on the entire buffered bulk node interval. Differences in (23) are bounded by the sum of their two actual endpoint norms; no smoothness of the unknown interpolation is assumed. Apply Theorem 1 to (25). Denote its first and third components by \(\mathcal F_N(x,\alpha)\) and \(\mathcal U_N(x,\alpha)\). Shrinking its fixed strip if necessary, define \[ \mathcal G_N(x,\alpha)=  rac{\mathcal U_N(x,\alpha)}{N c'(Nx)} =- rac{\mathcal U_N(x,\alpha)} {4\pi\sin(2\pi x+\pi/N)}. 	ag{31} \] The denominator is bounded away from zero on this bulk strip. Thus for some fixed \(r>0,C,p\), at both parities and all sufficiently large \(N\), \[  oxed{\quad \mathcal F_N(j/N,\alpha)=F_j(\alpha),\qquad \mathcal G_N(j/N,\alpha)=G_j(\alpha),\qquad \|\mathcal F_N\|+\|\mathcal G_N\|\le CN^p \quad} 	ag{32} \] on \(\mathcal R_r\), uniformly for \(|\alpha|\le A\). Both interpolants are jointly holomorphic. All fixed index-strip and exterior-parameter derivatives have polynomial bounds on smaller fixed domains. The other two vector components interpolate the differences in (23) and remain available. This is a phase-free analytic interpolation of both **separate** physical channels: its norm has no extensive exponential rate. No scalar zero-freeness or separation of limiting modes is needed. Any \(N\)-dependent oscillation in the actual vector initial data is retained rather than normalized away. ## 4. Original trace placement and its precise limitation For any actual ordinary spectator \(f(z;\mathbf u)\), the contribution of the bulk rows \(J_I=\{j:j/N\in I\}\) to the original full trace is exactly \[ \eta\sum_{j\in J_I} \left[ (4-c(j)^2) \{G_j(\alpha)f(c(j);\mathbf u) +F_j(\alpha)\partial_z f(c(j);\mathbf u)\} -c(j)F_j(\alpha)f(c(j);\mathbf u) ight]. 	ag{33} \] Any original crossing \(R^n\), including its carrier and normal, can remain inside \(f\). Every other graph factor and remaining trace can remain jointly inside \(f\) as well. The replacements \(F_j\mapsto\mathcal F_N(j/N,\alpha)\) and \(G_j\mapsto\mathcal G_N(j/N,\alpha)\) leave (33) exactly unchanged. All ordinary exterior derivatives commute with these identities. For fixed shared endpoint products, their value and normal in (33) are respectively \[ \prod_i\mathcal F_N(x,\alpha_i),\qquad \sum_i\mathcal G_N(x,\alpha_i) \prod_{k
e i}\mathcal F_N(x,\alpha_k). 	ag{34} \] These have polynomial bounds on the common strip and reproduce the entire shared product rule. No quotient is imposed on a free outside variable, and no spectral normal of the spectator is removed. The theorem does not assert \[ \partial_x\mathcal F_N(x,\alpha) =N c'(Nx)\mathcal G_N(x,\alpha). 	ag{35} \] Interpolating the two components separately is sufficient for the two-channel sampling formula (33), but does not create a single scalar Hermite representative. Accordingly (32) alone does not justify replacing a scalar double-pole contour amplitude by \(\mathcal F_N\) and differentiating it. Such a replacement must retain the difference between the two sides of (35), with its actual current or normal contribution. The physical endpoints \(j/N=0,1/2\) are outside the fixed bulk hypothesis. The odd simple node is therefore not among (33); its separate original value remains untouched. Both even and odd bulk recurrences are covered by the same argument. No global periodicity, endpoint connector estimate, filled-action upper bound, or nonzero source coefficient follows from this result. In particular it does not contradict the full-period scalar Hermite obstruction. ## 5. Coverage and direct sources The original physical value recurrence and its differentiated source equation are archived. The endpoint polynomial bound is also prior. The added result is the analytic near-identity vector interpolation theorem, and its application to the actual coupled value/normal data, including all shared endpoint products. Both complete direct sources were read at the following versions, their directly used implications checked, and their hashes verified: * [All physical first normals](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_all_color_path_normal_bound.md), SHA256 08f8932c2cdee4c7afadbb4db3cd85480603f8adb4c936ce29a5517b2d4799c7: the original source difference equation, common-index differentiation, endpoint forcing, and full-normal conventions. * [Two half-plane endpoint-product representatives](research_endpoint_two_half_plane_relative_source.md), SHA256 985fa3331379c3877734f28773d314b667ee87fa63314a5ef4513a3fe128d194: the actual polynomial bound for every bounded complex microscopic parameter set and the original full-normal trace normalization. Only written mathematics, source-text reads, and file hashes were used. No mathematical program, numerical experiment, test, or build was run. Adopted files and public manuscripts remain unchanged.

title: The original crossing multiplier on the full microscopic boundary
text:
# The original crossing multiplier on the full microscopic boundary Private written proof, 23 November 2026. The canonical polynomial of each signed original crossing has an entire microscopic limit, with error \(O(N^{-1})\) and every fixed holomorphic derivative. Both Newton endpoints and an oscillating bulk term survive. The limit retains the true first spectral normal at every fixed physical index. Its crossed Frobenius kernel also converges explicitly. Canonical reduction remains essential: the two limiting multipliers are inverse only modulo the limiting physical polynomial. An explicit nonzero carry survives. These local results do not justify composing an arbitrary short component by pointwise multiplication or limiting kernel integrals. ## 1. Original signed crossings and the limiting functions Put \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), and \[ \kappa=e^{\pi i d^2/(2N)},\quad c_j=2\cos((2j+1)\pi/N),\quad s_m=2\sin(\pi m/N),\quad S_m=\prod_{r=1}^m s_r,\quad S_0=1, \] \[ P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2,\qquad e_m(z)=S_m^{-2}\prod_{j<m}(c_j-z),\qquad w_N(\alpha)=2\cosh(\alpha/N). 	ag{1} \] Here \(T_N\) is the ordinary Chebyshev polynomial. All canonical representatives have degree at most \(d\). The full repeated-root algebra is \(\mathbb C[z]/P_N\), with its original functional \(\phi_N(e_i e_j)=\delta_{i+j,d}\) and genuine turn \(\mathsf T e_i=e_{d-i}\). For \(\sigma\in\{+1,-1\}\), let \(R_N^\sigma(z)\) be the canonical polynomial of the original signed crossing, including its Cartan scalar. The exact full-Hermite alphabet [N] gives \[ r_{N,\sigma}(z):=\kappa^{-\sigma}R_N^\sigma(z) =\sum_{i=0}^{d}(-q)^{\sigma i}e_i(z),\qquad r_{N,+}r_{N,-}\equiv1\pmod {P_N}. 	ag{2} \] Define \(E_{i,N}(\alpha)=(-1)^i e_i(w_N(\alpha))\). Then exactly \[ r_{N,\sigma}(w_N(\alpha)) =\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}q^{\sigma i}E_{i,N}(\alpha). 	ag{3} \] Use the entire endpoint functions of [K]: \[ a=	frac12+ rac{i\alpha}{2\pi},\quad b=1-a,\quad c(\alpha)=\cosh(\alpha/2),\quad C(\alpha)=c(\alpha)/\pi, \] \[ \mathsf E_m(\alpha)= rac{(a)_m(b)_m}{(m!)^2},\qquad \mathsf H_m(\alpha)= rac{c(\alpha)^2} {\pi^2m^2\mathsf E_m(\alpha)} \quad(m\ge1),\qquad \mathsf E_0=1. 	ag{4} \] The second expression means its entire continuation: every zero of \(\mathsf E_m\) is simple and is a double zero of its numerator. **Theorem 1.** The series and functions \[ D(\alpha)=1+\sum_{m\ge1} [\mathsf E_m(\alpha)-\mathsf H_m(\alpha)],\qquad F_\sigma(\alpha)=D(\alpha)+\sigma i c(\alpha) 	ag{5} \] are entire and even. For every fixed \(A<\infty\) and integer \(k\ge0\), \[ \sup_{|\alpha|\le A} \left|\partial_\alpha^k [r_{N,\sigma}(w_N(\alpha))-F_\sigma(\alpha)]ight| \le C_{A,k}/N. 	ag{6} \] The limit is through both parities. On the real axis \(D\) is real and \[ |F_\sigma(\alpha)|^2=D(\alpha)^2+c(\alpha)^2 \ge c(\alpha)^2\ge1. 	ag{7} \] In particular the original microscopic crossing is uniformly nonzero on each bounded real parameter interval for all sufficiently large \(N\). The known unit scalar \(\kappa^\sigma\) has not been discarded from the original crossing; (6) states its normalization explicitly. ## 2. A common bulk unit for the two Newton ends Write \(\operatorname{sinc}z=\sin z/z\) and \(\operatorname{sinhc}z=\sinh z/z\), with removable values one. The exact product and complementary identities [K] are \[ E_{m,N}=\mathsf E_m U_{m,N},\qquad U_{m,N}=\prod_{r=0}^{m-1}  rac{\operatorname{sinhc}((\alpha+i(2r+1)\pi)/(2N)) \operatorname{sinhc}((\alpha-i(2r+1)\pi)/(2N))} {\operatorname{sinc}(\pi(r+1)/N)^2}, \] \[ E_{N-m,N}=\mathsf H_m \operatorname{sinc}(\pi m/N)^{-2}U_{m,N}^{-1}. 	ag{8} \] They hold through all apparent zeros. For \(1\le m\le N/2\), all displayed unit factors are nonzero on a fixed bounded \(\alpha\)-disk once \(N\) is sufficiently large. We prove the stronger comparison \[ V_{m,N}:=U_{m,N}\operatorname{sinc}(\pi m/N),\qquad V_{m,N}^{\ \pm1}=1+O_A(m/N^2). 	ag{9} \] Set \(\Delta=\pi/N\) and \(f(v)=\log\operatorname{sinc}v\) on a fixed neighborhood of \([0,\pi/2]\). At zero parameter, \[ \log U_{m,N}(0)+f(m\Delta) =\sum_{r=1}^m [2f((r-	frac12)\Delta)-f((r-1)\Delta)-f(r\Delta)] =O(m/N^2). 	ag{10} \] This is a telescoping identity followed by the bounded second derivative of \(f\). For the parameter dependence let \(g(z)=\log\operatorname{sinhc}z\), \(g(0)=0\), on a zero-free neighborhood of the imaginary segment from \(-i\pi/2\) to \(i\pi/2\). With \(v=(r+1/2)\Delta\), evenness of \(g\) gives \[ g(\alpha/(2N)+iv)+g(\alpha/(2N)-iv)-2g(iv) =O_A(N^{-2}). 	ag{11} \] Its first derivative in \(\alpha/(2N)\) vanishes at zero; its second derivative is uniformly bounded. Summing (11) and using (10) bounds \(\log V_{m,N}\) by \(C_A m/N^2\). Exponentiating both signs proves (9). No logarithm of \(\mathsf E_m\) was taken. ## 3. Summation with the oscillating bulk retained Uniformly on compact parameter disks, as \(m	o\infty\), \[ \mathsf E_m= rac C m (1-ab/m+O_A(m^{-2})),\qquad \mathsf H_m= rac C m (1+ab/m+O_A(m^{-2})). 	ag{12} \] Here is also a direct way to check the opposite first corrections. The Gamma product gives \(\mathsf E_m=C\Gamma(m+a)\Gamma(m+b)/\Gamma(m+1)^2\), using \(1/(\Gamma(a)\Gamma(b))=\sin(\pi a)/\pi=C\). The normalized ratio \(u_m=m\Gamma(m+a)\Gamma(m+b)/\Gamma(m+1)^2\) (equivalently \(m\mathsf E_m/C\), by removable continuation) tends to one and obeys \(u_{m+1}/u_m=1+ab/[m(m+1)]\). The normalization follows, for example, by scaling the beta integral for Gamma ratios and then shifting its parameters; it is uniform on fixed compact sets. For sufficiently large \(m\), take logarithms of its tail product: \(\log u_m=-\sum_{j\ge m}\log(1+ab/[j(j+1)]) =-ab/m+O_A(m^{-3})\). This proves the first expansion; the exact identity \(\mathsf H_m=C^2/(m^2\mathsf E_m)\) proves the second. The Gamma expressions extend through the finitely many exceptional parameter values, so the estimates are uniform there as well. Thus \[ \mathsf E_m-\mathsf H_m=O_A(m^{-2}),\qquad \mathsf E_m+\mathsf H_m=2C/m+O_A(m^{-3}). 	ag{13} \] The first bound proves normal convergence and entire evenness in (5). For the positive sign, pair indices \(m,N-m\) in (3). Set \(	au_m=\pi m/N\) and \(M=\lfloor(N-1)/2floor\). By (8)--(9), their exact sum is \[ 	au_m\cot	au_m (\mathsf E_m V_{m,N}-\mathsf H_m V_{m,N}^{-1}) +i	au_m(\mathsf E_m V_{m,N} +\mathsf H_m V_{m,N}^{-1}). 	ag{14} \] Replacing both \(V\)'s by one costs \(O_A(N^{-2})\) per pair, since \(\mathsf E_m,\mathsf H_m=O_A(1/m)\), and the two displayed weights are bounded. The real-weight error also costs \(O_A(N^{-2})\) per pair, because \(|	au\cot	au-1|\le C	au^2\) for \(0\le	au\le\pi/2\) and the difference in (13) is \(O_A(m^{-2})\). Its omitted infinite tail is \(O_A(1/N)\). The imaginary part of (14), after this replacement, sums to \(i\sum_{m=1}^M[2\pi C/N+O_A(1/(Nm^2))] =ic+O_A(N^{-1})\). The index zero contributes one. At even \(N\) the additional midpoint is \(iE_{N/2,N}=O_A(N^{-1})\), by (8)--(9) and (12); at odd \(N\) there is no unpaired index. This proves (6) for the positive sign and zero derivatives. The negative sign reverses the imaginary part in (14) with no other change. Applying the result on a larger parameter disk and Cauchy's formula proves every derivative in (6). The endpoint functions are real for real parameters, proving (7). ## 4. The original physical first normals For a fixed integer \(j\ge0\), put \(\alpha_j=i\pi(2j+1)\) and \(
u_j=(-1)^j q^{j(j+1)}\). At all sufficiently large levels this is a double physical node. The actual crossing data [W, equation (8)] give exactly \[ r_{N,\sigma}(w_N(\alpha_j))=
u_j^\sigma,\qquad \left.\partial_\alpha r_{N,\sigma}(w_N(\alpha)) ight|_{\alpha_j} =-\sigma rac{d-2j}{2N}
u_j^\sigma. 	ag{15} \] Consequently (6) retains, with their original sign, \[ F_\sigma(\alpha_j)=(-1)^j,\qquad F_\sigma'(\alpha_j)=- rac\sigma2(-1)^j,\qquad D(\alpha_j)=(-1)^j,\quad D'(\alpha_j)=0, \] \[  rac{r_{N,\sigma}'(c_j)}{N^2} = rac{\sigma i(-1)^j}{4\pi(2j+1)}+O_j(N^{-1}). 	ag{16} \] The last derivative is the ordinary fixed-root Casimir derivative; it follows from \(w_N'(\alpha_j)=2i\sin((2j+1)\pi/N)/N\). It is not a genuine-\(q\) normal or a changed-meridian derivative. The estimates concern fixed \(j\), not indices proportional to \(N\). ## 5. The surviving inverse-pair carry The exact inverse identity (2) defines an ordinary polynomial \[ Q_N(z)= rac{r_{N,+}(z)r_{N,-}(z)-1}{P_N(z)}. 	ag{17} \] Since \(P_N(w_N(\alpha))=4c(\alpha)^2=:P(\alpha)\) exactly, Theorem 1 implies \[ Q_N(w_N(\alpha))\longrightarrow Q_\infty(\alpha)= rac{D(\alpha)^2+c(\alpha)^2-1} {4c(\alpha)^2}, 	ag{18} \] with \(O_A(N^{-1})\) error and every fixed holomorphic derivative.
