Finally the numerator matrix in (14) is \(I+(w,-z)^T(w,-z)\), of norm at most three, while \(|s|^2>41/50>(9/10)^2\). Thus \(\|K\|_2<10/3\), proving the other assertions in (31). **Mixed currents.** Keep the exact trace rectangles and all their orientations. For a \(P\)-type vertical coordinate the proof of (19)--(21) in the power-dominated note gives \(\partial_{h_v}\mathcal E<-4/5\), while every other coordinate may be anywhere on its own wide rectangle. Lower each such height to \(-H_v\) in this pointwise upper estimate. This is not a change of the exact current; it bounds its integrand, retaining the \(-|h_v|\) penalty and its corner at zero. At the resulting point write \(t-t^*=a+ib\). Only \(D\)-type vertical coordinates can have \(b_v\ne0\). For them choose the side \(\operatorname{sgn}(n_v)T_N\), or \(+T_N\) at zero power. Then \[ \begin{array}{c|c|c} \text{vertical type}& |a_v|&b_v\\ \hline P&>3/5&0\\ D&>59/40&0\le b_v<1/20 \end{array} \qquad n_va_vb_v\ge0. \tag{33} \] The entire straight segment from the saddle to this point is in the wide rectangle. Using (31) in Taylor's formula, and the same degree-weighted \(A_2,B_2\) as in Section 3, gives \[ \begin{split} \mathcal E-M &\le\frac1{4\pi} \left[-\frac13A_2+\frac{10}{3}B_2+ \frac{20}{3}\sqrt{A_2B_2}\right] -\frac1{2\pi}\sum_vn_va_vb_v\\ &\le-\frac{A_2}{24\pi}+\frac{35B_2}{2\pi} -\frac1{2\pi}\sum_vn_va_vb_v. \end{split} \tag{34} \] The Young inequality here uses \((20/3)\sqrt{AB}\le A/6+(200/3)B\). The loss per \(D\)-vertical incidence is greater than \(1801/(38400\pi)>1/70\); the loss per already lowered \(P\)-vertical incidence is greater than \(3/(200\pi)>1/220\). Including the favorable height changes, every nonempty original vertical set \(S\) therefore satisfies \[ \mathcal E_S<M-\frac1{220}\sum_{v\in S}d_v -\frac45\sum_{v\in S\cap P}(h_v+H_v). \tag{35} \] This bound includes currents containing both vertex types. Loops use the same two-incidence quadratic-form pullback as in Section 3. No assertion of entrywise positivity or of a norm lower bound is used. For removed physical rows, (30) and the \(P\)-vertex action budget combine with the original centered loss to give \[ \operatorname{rate}(S)<M- \left(\frac{21}{200}-\frac3{40}\right) \sum_{v\in S}d_v =M-\frac3{100}\sum_{v\in S}d_v. \tag{36} \] Every partial-charge retained graph has the same hybrid bounds. First normals, including derivatives of loop factors, have the same finite product-rule bookkeeping as in Section 5. The odd simple node and all trace aliases are unchanged. The remaining source calculation is now exactly Section 6: strict horizontal concavity, the unit coefficient of the leading trace charge, nonzero sine and edge factors, and a nonzero Gaussian determinant give (4); (35)--(36) bound the rest of the actual source. All inequalities have strict margins. Small fixed complex outside angles stay in the larger incidence box, preserve the hybrid contraction, and are covered directly by the original complex centered-incidence estimates. Even descent and Cauchy's formula give the ordinary outside-color statement. The marked conclusion then follows from the same original slopes, positive completion and component tests as in Section 7. This proves Theorem 3. \(\square\)

title: Whole-boundary decay for the proved path and graph sources
text:
# Whole-boundary decay for the proved path and graph sources Research proof, 4 November 2026. Frozen manuscripts are unchanged. The full wide-kernel estimate upgrades the recently proved local outside packets to whole-period bounds and quadratic complex strips. The argument retains the original finite source and all its normals. It supplies boundary control for later composition; it does not by itself solve an arbitrary adjacent short component. ## 1. The original source and the covered classes Use the exact source, crossing powers, and marking conventions of one of the following proved theorems: * [The path theorem, Theorem 4](research_uniform_path_trace_assembly.md#7-the-source-theorem-at-powers-seven-and-eight): positive powers at least seven with the stipulated complete outside endpoint, or signed powers of absolute value at least eight. * [The branching theorem](research_degree_controlled_network_source.md): a fixed loopless same-index graph, allowing repeated edges, with \(|n_v|\ge\max(8,4d_v)\) at each selected vertex. * [The degree-power theorem](research_network_degree_power_source.md): a fixed same-index graph, allowing loops and repeated edges, with \(n_v^2+d_v^2\ge4096\) at each selected vertex. * [The hybrid theorem, Theorem 3](research_network_degree_power_source.md#8-mixing-the-degree-and-power-regimes-at-adjacent-vertices): a fixed same-index graph, allowing loops and repeated edges, in which each selected vertex independently satisfies either \(|n_v|\ge\max(8,4d_v)\) or \(\sqrt{n_v^2+d_v^2}\ge512\). The degrees are the actual incidence degrees, with loops counted twice. Each bullet is a separately proved source class. Only the last permits the displayed vertexwise combination. In particular the homogeneous degree-power threshold \(64\) is not substituted for the hybrid threshold \(512\). Let \(I\) be the nonempty selected set and let \(B\subseteq V\setminus I\) be any set of unselected vertices whose angles will be left free. Other unselected angles stay zero. Delete isolated outside vertices from \(B\), since the source is independent of their angles. With \(z_b=-2\cos u_b\), define the literal polynomial \[ F_N(\mathbf u)= \left(\prod_{v\in I}\phi_N^{(z_v)}R(z_v)^{n_v}ight) \prod_{\{v,w\}\in E}K_N(t_v,t_w), \quad t_b=u_b\ (b\in B),\quad t_b=0\ (b
otin I\cup B). 	ag{1} \] Products precede the selected traces. A loop occurs once as \(K_N(t_v,t_v)\). Unselected variables are not reduced in the Casimir quotient. Their actual degrees obey \[ \deg_{z_b}F_N\le d_b(N-1). 	ag{2} \] Let \(M\) be the proved selected stationary action with every outside angle complete. Put \[ \gamma= rac1{100},\qquad \mathcal U(\mathbf x)= \sum_{b\in B}d_b(1-\cos x_b). 	ag{3} \] **Theorem 1.** In each of the stated classes, for every fixed multi-index \(\alpha\) of ordinary outside-color derivatives, \[ \left|\partial_{\mathbf z}^{\alpha}F_N(\mathbf x)ight| \le C_\alpha N^{A_\alpha} e^{N[M-\gamma\mathcal U(\mathbf x)]}, \qquad \mathbf x\in[-\pi,\pi]^B . 	ag{4} \] There are \(c,B_0,h>0\) such that the same original functions satisfy \[ \left|\partial_{\mathbf z}^{\alpha} F_N(\mathbf x+i\mathbf y)ight| \le C'_\alpha N^{A'_\alpha} e^{N[M-c\mathcal U(\mathbf x)+B_0|\mathbf y|^2]}, \qquad |x_b|\le\pi,\quad |y_b|\le h. 	ag{5} \] The constants may depend on the fixed graph and powers, but not on the level. Both statements hold at both level parities. Near \(\mathbf u=0\), the nonzero holomorphic packet is exactly the one proved by the corresponding source theorem. ## 2. A loss for every free outside incidence Write \[ \mathcal W=\{t:|\Re t|\le\pi/2,\ |\Im t|\le3/10\}, \qquad \delta= rac{21}{200}. 	ag{6} \] The [wide edge theorem](research_bare_kernel_thin_rectangle.md#6-the-full-rectangle-through-real-angle-pi-over-two) and [wide phase Hessian](research_path_mixed_trace_currents.md#9-vertical-current-monotonicity-at-powers-of-at-least-seven) give, including every fixed ordinary derivative, \[ |K_N(t,u)|\le CN^A e^{N\Re\psi(t,u)},\qquad -\Re\psi''(t,u)\succeq rac1{20\pi}I, \qquad t,u\in\mathcal W . 	ag{7} \] All derivatives here and below act on the corresponding ordinary colors, not on an angle divided by a possibly vanishing sine. For fixed complex \(t\in\mathcal W\) and real \(|u|\le\pi/2\), separate evenness gives \(\psi_u(t,0)=0\). Twice integrating the \(uu\) entry of (7) yields \[ \Re\psi(t,u)\le\Re\psi(t,0)- rac{u^2}{40\pi} \le\Re\psi(t,0)-\gamma(1-\cos u). 	ag{8} \] Indeed \(1-\cos u\le u^2/2\) and \(\pi<5\). For real \(\pi/2\le|u|\le\pi\), the [centered incidence theorem](research_path_mixed_trace_currents.md#8-a-stronger-centered-loss-for-a-removed-incidence) gives exponent \(\Re\psi(t,0)-\delta\). Since \(2\gamma<\delta\), it implies the same outside loss. Thus a retained selected angle anywhere on its actual horizontal or vertical contour satisfies \[ |K_N(t,u)|\le CN^A e^{N[\Re\psi(t,0)-\gamma(1-\cos u)]}, \quad t\in\mathcal W,\quad u\in[-\pi,\pi]. 	ag{9} \] Both branches of this proof already include all fixed ordinary derivatives in either color. Suppose the selected neighbor is instead an original removed physical row, of real angle \(t\) with \(|t|\ge T_N\). The strict reserve in the centered theorem permits the physical midpoint cutoff \(T_N=\pi/2+O(N^{-1})\) below \(\pi/2\). If \(|u|\le\pi/2\), use the symmetric centered estimate \(\Re\psi(0,u)-\delta\), followed by (8) with \(t=0\). If \(|u|\ge\pi/2\), use its two-removed-endpoint bound \(M_\infty-2\delta\). Both give \[ |K_N(t,u)|\le CN^A e^{N[M_\infty-\delta-\gamma(1-\cos u)]}. 	ag{10} \] Thus the entire internal removal cost \(\delta\) survives, in addition to the outside loss. For an edge with two unselected endpoints, both angles can be free. If both have magnitude at most \(\pi/2\), integrate the full real Hessian in (7) from \((0,0)\): \(\psi(u,v)\le M_\infty-(u^2+v^2)/(40\pi)\). If only one is large, use the centered estimate and (8) for the other. If both are large, use the double-removed estimate. In every case, \[ |K_N(u,v)|\le CN^A e^{N[M_\infty-\gamma\{(1-\cos u)+(1-\cos v)\}]}. 	ag{11} \] This also applies on the diagonal of an outside loop; its two losses correspond to its two actual incidences. The same arguments apply to all ordinary derivatives. A loop's diagonal derivatives are finite sums of those mixed derivatives. ## 3. The original traces retain these losses Use exactly the complete-outside contours and removed-row subsets in the underlying source theorem. No new stationary point at a distant real outside color is assumed. For a retained boundary edge use (9), and for a removed boundary edge use (10). Edges with no selected endpoint use (11). Edges entirely inside the selected set keep their original estimates. After these replacements, the remaining exponent is precisely the complete-outside exponent of the proved source calculation, minus \(\gamma\mathcal U(\mathbf x)\). Every horizontal, mixed vertical, higher-charge, and removed-row estimate therefore retains that same loss. In particular each removed incidence still has its full \(\delta\) cost before the original partial-charge action budget is applied. All coefficients and orientations of the finite Hermite identities are unchanged. For negative powers their reflected vertical-side signs are retained, and the zero-power case uses its already proved mixed-current estimate. First normals differentiate a finite incident product; (9)--(11) and the interior bounds retain every such derivative at polynomial cost. Odd simple-node terms remain among the original physical rows. The number of terms and the orders of derivatives are fixed independently of \(N\). This proves (4), including its ordinary outside derivatives. ## 4. Why the complex strip has quadratic height growth Here polynomial continuation alone would give a linear height cost. Use both (4) and the proved local packet, as in the [two-boundary Laurent argument](research_uniform_path_trace_assembly.md#5-boundary-sources-and-kernels). We give the multivariable version with the literal degrees (2). For the undifferentiated source put \(D_b=d_b(N-1)\), and express it as a Laurent polynomial in \(q_b=e^{iu_b}\). The function \[ \left(\prod_{b\in B}q_b^{D_b}ight) F_N(\mathbf q)\, \exp\left[-N\gamma\sum_{b\in B}d_bq_bight] 	ag{12} \] is holomorphic on the closed unit polydisk. Its distinguished boundary norm is at most \(CN^A\exp N(M-\gamma\sum_bd_b)\), by (4). Apply the maximum principle one variable at a time. Separate evenness permits either sign of each height, so evaluation at \(|q_b|=e^{-|y_b|}\) gives the upper exponential rate \[ M-\gamma\sum_bd_b+ \gamma\sum_bd_be^{-|y_b|}\cos x_b+ \sum_bd_b|y_b|. 	ag{13} \] The same conclusion holds for every ordinary derivative, since it is again a separately even polynomial of degree at most (2) and has the real bound (4). Outside any fixed neighborhood of \(\mathbf x=0\), the quantity \(\mathcal U(\mathbf x)\) has a positive minimum. Choose \(h>0\) so small that the linear height terms in (13), including the change \(1-e^{-|y_b|}\), are absorbed into half that real loss. This gives (5) on this part of the real torus. On a fixed small polydisk about zero, use the proved source expansion \[ F_N(\mathbf u)=\varepsilon_N N^
u a(\mathbf u)e^{NW(\mathbf u)}(1+O(N^{-1})), \qquad a(\mathbf u)
e0,\quad \Re W(0)=M. 	ag{14} \] The phase, amplitude and normalized remainder are holomorphic. Taking pointwise exponential rates in (4) gives \(\Re W(\mathbf x)\le M-\gamma\mathcal U(\mathbf x)\). The branch is separately even, so \(
abla W(0)=0\) and \[ -\Re W''(0)\succeq \gamma\,\operatorname{diag}(d_b)>0. 	ag{15} \] Holomorphic Taylor expansion on a smaller neighborhood and Young's inequality for the mixed real-imaginary quadratic terms give \(\Re W(\mathbf x+i\mathbf y) \le M-c\mathcal U(\mathbf x)+B_0|\mathbf y|^2\). The bounded local amplitude proves (5) there. All fixed ordinary derivatives have the same exponential upper bound with polynomial cost: apply Cauchy's formula on ordinary-color circles of radius \(O(N^{-2})\) inside the packet domain. The phase is holomorphic in those colors, including the ramified complete angles, so the change of exponent is \(O(N^{-1})\). No nonvanishing derivative of the leading amplitude is assumed. This proves the theorem. ## 5. Consequence for marked corridor composition For a connected path whose only unselected vertex is one free endpoint, \(e=m\) and \(
u=0\). For a selected run between two unselected endpoints, \(e=m+1\) and \(
u=-3/2\), whether both ends are free or one is kept complete. Equations (4)--(5) and the unchanged nonzero local packet give exactly the boundary source and kernel hypotheses of the existing finite-library and long-turn composition theorems. A fixed finite collection has common constants after taking smaller neighborhoods and strips. This now applies at the positive-seven and signed-eight thresholds, with their original geometric and complete-end qualifications. The [exact corridor threshold criterion](research_affine_reduction_fibers_and_core_obligation.md#10-which-short-corridors-can-be-made-long-and-what-conjugation-preserves) can therefore be used at \(K=7\) for its positive complementary presentation with complete retained ends. For example, binary negative corridors with endpoint runs of twos of length at least five and internal runs of length at least four have an admissible marked two-boundary source. Their fixed end twists and proper rotations remain those of the exact tangle identity. The [canonical boundary-crossing theorem](research_boundary_crossing_packet_preservation.md) retains their chirp factors and full ordinary normals; it is applied after the whole-period estimate has been established, not to an arbitrary unproved short source. The graph assertions concern the literal source (1). At an outside vertex of degree greater than one, they do not assert that canonical reduction to degree less than \(N\) preserves the same global angular loss. Path endpoints have degree one and are already canonical, which is the scope of the immediate admissibility conclusion above. Knot and volume conclusions still use the underlying marked circle-tree realization and component tests. This boundary upgrade neither changes original assignment fibers nor resolves every fixed adjacent short word. The minimal exact checker [check_network_whole_boundary_decay.py](../experiments/check_network_whole_boundary_decay.py) verifies the two scalar loss comparisons, incidence degree accounting with loops, and the original powers of \(N\). Its [saved record](../repro/results/research-network-whole-boundary-decay.json) records the proof dependencies. It does not replace the contour, source, or Laurent arguments above.

title: Factorial chambers for the actual Newton gates
text:
# Factorial chambers for the actual Newton gates Private written proof, 15 November 2026. The canonical factorial already has uniform asymptotics on compact subsets of both open half-planes, without a restriction on the real part. Near a real noninteger argument outside its original strip, the missing factors are explicit level-dependent Fourier factors. Retaining them gives a local meromorphic normal form for every algebraically regular multiplication or signed-crossing gate. For any collection of nonconstant wrapped real-affine arguments, a common imaginary direction puts their Fourier factors and inverse factors in a pointed cone. Their joint constant Fourier coefficient is then exactly one, even if the affine forms are dependent. This concerns the distinguished sector of that specified chamber. A previously marked geometric action can differ by a Fourier character; its sector is not relabeled as the constant one. Nothing here computes the coefficient of the original integration cycle. ## 1. Exact periods and marked primitives The canonical sine factorial is the original function \[ G_N(z)=\left( rac{2\pi}{N}ight)^z\Gamma(z+1) \prod_{r\ge1}  rac{\Gamma(Nr+z+1)} {\Gamma(Nr-z)(Nr)^{2z+1}}. 	ag{1} \] Its positive-base powers use real logarithms. The source construction proves its nonvanishing on \(-1<\Re z<N\), its meromorphic continuation, and the exact identities \[ G_N(z+1)=2\sin rac{\pi(z+1)}N\,G_N(z),\qquad G_N(z)G_N(N-1-z)=N. 	ag{2} \] In particular, the complementary displacement is \(N-1\), not \(N\). For \(	au=+1\), on the upper half-plane put \[ J_+(\xi)= rac{i\pi}{2}\xi(1-\xi) + rac{i}{2\pi} \{\operatorname{Li}_2(e^{2\pi i\xi})-\pi^2/6\}; \qquad J_-(\xi)=\overline{J_+( ar\xi)}. 	ag{3} \] The dilogarithm in its defining half-plane is its convergent disk series. Both primitives agree with the original \(J\), real on \(0<\xi<1\), on their overlaps with \(0<\Re\xi<1\). Their continuations satisfy, for every integer \(k\), \[  egin{split} J_	au(\xi+k) &=J_	au(\xi)-	au\pi i \{k\xi+k(k-1)/2\},\ J_	au'(\xi+k)&=J_	au'(\xi)-	au\pi i k. \end{split} 	ag{4} \] These identities follow by differentiating (3) and fixing the constant there; the integer shifts leave its disk variable unchanged. The finite sine product in (2) gives \[ G_N(z+N)=-2\sin(\pi z)\,G_N(z). 	ag{5} \] Iterating in either direction, as meromorphic identities, gives \[ G_N(z+kN) =(-1)^{Nk(k-1)/2}[-2\sin(\pi z)]^kG_N(z), \qquad k\in\mathbb Z. 	ag{6} \] This formula retains its zeros and poles. For negative \(k\), the displayed power is a reciprocal; it is not replaced by a nonvanishing normalization. ## 2. A uniform normal form through a real chamber Fix an integer \(k\), a compact set in \(k<\Re\xi<k+1\), and a bounded complex offset \(a\). For \(	au=\pm1\), extend \(J_	au\) to this strip from its indicated half-plane, using (4) and the original primitive at \(\xi-k\). Define \[ \mathcal U_N(\xi,a)=  rac{G_N(N(\xi-k)+a)} {N^{1/2}\exp\{NJ(\xi-k)+(a+	frac12)J'(\xi-k)\}}. 	ag{7} \] For all sufficiently large \(N\), this is a nonzero holomorphic function on a fixed neighborhood of the compact set. The original uniform strip expansion proves \[ \mathcal U_N(\xi,a)=1+O_{m hol}(N^{-1}). 	ag{8} \] Every fixed derivative has this order on smaller compact sets, also with respect to bounded offsets on a fixed compact set. **Theorem 1.** With the same actual offset and either choice of \(	au\), the following identity is exact and meromorphic: \[  oxed{\quad G_N(N\xi+a)= N^{1/2}\exp\{NJ_	au(\xi)+(a+	frac12)J_	au'(\xi)\}  igl(1-e^{	au2\pi i(N\xi+a)} igr)^k \mathcal U_N(\xi,a). \quad} 	ag{9} \] Consequently (8) is a uniform asymptotic after the displayed Fourier divisor has been factored, including at its zeros and poles. The remainder is not differentiated by first dividing pointwise at a zero; it is the holomorphic function (7). **Proof.** Apply (6) with \(z=N(\xi-k)+a\). For either sign, \[ -2\sin\pi z =-	au i\,e^{-	au\pi i z} (1-e^{	au2\pi i z}). 	ag{10} \] The last factor is unchanged by adding \(kN\). Substitute (7) and use (4). The remaining constant is \[ (-1)^{Nk(k-1)/2} e^{	au\pi iNk(k-1)/2} (-	au i)^k e^{	au\pi i k/2}=1. 	ag{11} \] Indeed \(k(k-1)\) is even. Thus no parity scalar, square-root sign or offset phase is missing from (9). The uniform remainder claim is precisely the original strip estimate applied in (7). This proves the theorem. \(\square\) On a compact set with \(	au\Im\xi>0\), the Fourier factor in (9) is \(1+O(e^{-cN})\), with every fixed derivative after possibly decreasing \(c>0\). This recovers the archived half-plane asymptotic. If \(\Re\xi\) is an integer but \(\Im\xi
e0\), that half-plane theorem applies directly, without a real-chamber choice. At a real argument outside \((0,1)\), the factor in (9) cannot in general be dropped. Its zero or pole lattice is \(N\xi+a\in\mathbb Z\), with signed order \(k\). Nonvanishing of \(\sin(\pi\xi)\) excludes the macroscopic factorial wall, not this level-dependent lattice. Both signs give the same exact function, not different interpolations. Their agreement is also visible from \[ 1-e^{2\pi iz}=-e^{2\pi iz}(1-e^{-2\pi iz}) 	ag{12} \] together with (4). Exponentially small Fourier factors in one half-plane need not be small in the other one. ## 3. The literal multiplication and crossing factors For actual index variables \(I,J,R\), retain the canonical interpolation of the original multiplication coefficient: \[ \mu_N(I,J,R)=  rac{G_N(I+J)G_N(R)} {G_N(I)G_N(J)G_N(R-I)G_N(R-J)G_N(I+J-R)}. 	ag{13} \] On its original supported integer set this is the exact positive Newton multiplication table, including the original repeated-root algebra. Its seven scaled arguments and multiplicities are \[  egin{array}{c|rrrrrrr} \ell_j&x+y&z&x&y&z-x&z-y&x+y-z\ \hline 
u_j&1&1&-1&-1&-1&-1&-1 . \end{array} 	ag{14} \] If \(I=Nx+a_I,\ J=Ny+a_J,\ R=Nz+a_R\), their literal offsets are respectively \[ a_I+a_J,\ a_R,\ a_I,\ a_J,\ a_R-a_I,\ a_R-a_J,\ a_I+a_J-a_R. 	ag{15} \] No offset is rounded or removed. For a signed crossing \(\sigma=\pm1\), use the specified interpolation of the actual multiplication matrix, with output \(I\) and input \(J\): \[ (M_{\sigma,N})_{I,J} =\kappa_N^\sigma e^{\sigma\pi i I} e^{\sigma\pi i I(J+1)/N}  rac{G_N(I)}{G_N(J)G_N(I-J)},\qquad \kappa_N=e^{\pi i(N-1)^2/(2N)}. 	ag{16} \] The sign interpolation \(e^{\sigma\pi iI}\) is the original one used for this signed local phase. The boundary operator \(C_{\sigma,N}\) is the transpose of (16). The three factorial arguments are \(x,y,x-y\), of multiplicities \(1,-1,-1\), with offsets \(a_I,a_J,a_I-a_J\). The complete prefactor in (16) is retained exactly. At any point where all seven sines in (14), or all three crossing sines, are nonzero, choose a small fixed neighborhood. An argument with \(k_j<\Re\ell_j<k_j+1\) has the period chart (9), whether it is real or nonreal. A nonreal argument may instead use the archived half-plane expansion; this covers in particular its integer-real-part case. Every real argument uses its period chart. Multiplication of these exact factorizations gives \[  egin{split} \mu_N &=N^{-3/2} \exp\left\{N\sum_j
u_jJ_j(\ell_j) +\sum_j
u_j(a_j+	frac12)J_j'(\ell_j)ight\} \mathfrak W_N\,\mathfrak U_N,\ \mathfrak W_N &=\prod_{j\ {m period\ chart}}  igl(1-e^{	au_j2\pi i(N\ell_j+a_j)} igr)^{
u_jk_j}, \qquad \mathfrak U_N=1+O_{m hol}(N^{-1}). \end{split} 	ag{17} \] Here each \(J_j\) has the specified half-plane or chamber mark. The exact nonzero holomorphic unit \(\mathfrak U_N\) is the product of the exact normalized remainder factors; no equality is asserted with a truncated series. For a crossing, the same formula has \(N^{-1/2}\), its three arguments, and the full prefactor (16). This is a local normal form for the same meromorphic gate, including all its divisors. It is not a rectangular extension of its finite support. The existing factorial-divisor criterion shows that distinct affine zero hyperplanes need not cancel pole hyperplanes in (13). They remain present in (17). ## 4. Joint Fourier factors in a pointed cone Let \(\mathbf z\in\mathbb C^d\) be independent retained label coordinates, and let the wrapped arguments be real affine forms \[ \ell_j(\mathbf z)=\mathbf a_j\cdot \mathbf z+b_j,\qquad \mathbf a_j\in\mathbb Z^d\setminus\{0\}, \quad b_j\in\mathbb R. 	ag{18} \] The actual gate forms (14), and their original integer complementary identifications, have this form. Write \(h=\Im\mathbf z_*\) at the chart center. Choose a real \(v\) with \(\mathbf a_j\cdot v
e0\) for every form that is real there. For sufficiently small fixed \(\varepsilon>0\), the vector \(v_*=h+\varepsilon v\) has nonzero pairing with every \(\mathbf a_j\), and those pairings preserve the signs of all nonreal arguments. Set \[ 	au_j=\operatorname{sgn}(\mathbf a_j\cdot v_*), \qquad e_j=
u_jk_j. 	ag{19} \] Thus the choice keeps every nonreal canonical half-plane branch and chooses a coherent side at the real arguments. Along \(\mathbf z=\mathbf z_*+itv_*\), \(t>0\) fixed and small, every exponential in (17) has modulus less than one for all sufficiently large \(N\), also with the actual bounded offsets. If all arguments are real at the center, \(h\) is orthogonal to all their gradients and this reduces to a generic imaginary direction. **Theorem 2.** Expand every factor of \[ \mathfrak W_N(\mathbf z) =\prod_j (1-e^{	au_j2\pi i(N\ell_j(\mathbf z)+a_j)})^{e_j} 	ag{20} \] in its convergent binomial series on this common side. The expansion is locally normally convergent there. Its Fourier frequencies, in the variables \(e^{2\pi iNz_\alpha}\), lie in \[ \mathcal C=\left\{\sum_jr_j	au_j\mathbf a_j: r_j\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}ight\}. 	ag{21} \] Every nonzero term has strictly positive pairing with \(v_*\). The coefficient of frequency zero is exactly \(1\), for all levels and all actual offsets; this coefficient identity is algebraic, whereas convergence on the specified local chart holds for sufficiently large \(N\) as above. This includes negative \(e_j\) and arbitrary linear dependencies between the affine forms. **Proof.** For integer \(e\), the series \((1-u)^e=\sum_{r\ge0}(-1)^r inom er u^r\) is finite if \(e\ge0\) and absolutely convergent for \(|u|<1\) if \(e<0\). Its constant term is one. Each nonconstant choice contributes a frequency \(r	au_j\mathbf a_j\), whose pairing with \(v_*\) is \(r|\mathbf a_j\cdot v_*|>0\). Thus no nonzero tuple of choices can have total frequency zero. The tuple of all zero choices gives coefficient one. The finite product converges normally on smaller regions where all \(|u_j|<1\) uniformly. Frequency grouping is unambiguous: if \(\delta=\min_j|\mathbf a_j\cdot v_*|>0\), a fixed frequency \(\lambda\) can arise only from tuples with \(\sum_jr_j\le\lambda\cdot v_*/\delta\). There are finitely many such tuples. Affine constants and literal offsets change their scalar coefficients, not their frequencies or this argument. \(\square\) All seven forms in (14), and all three crossing forms, are nonconstant in the retained labels of the actual gate, so the theorem applies directly to each gate and to any collection before imposing further identifications. It also applies after actual affine wire identifications whenever the wrapped forms remain nonconstant and have real affine constants in the remaining coordinates: choose the pointing vector in that coordinate space. Any form that becomes constant instead is retained as its explicit scalar factor in (20); its zero cannot be excluded by this Fourier argument. In particular an exterior parameter is not silently varied to make such a form nonconstant. With fixed complex affine constants, the same cone proof applies if a common pointing vector for the prescribed signs exists; its existence is not inferred from \(h\) in that case. Theorem 2 concerns \(\mathfrak W_N\), not the Fourier expansion of the complete action, normalized remainder, or lattice kernel. It proves that the wall-transition factors do not cancel their specified zero-frequency sector. It does not say that all their other coefficients are nonzero. ## 5. Positive prefixes and the retained geometric mark The original positive-prefix theorem proves that all seven arguments of every proper multiplication gate and all three arguments of a signed crossing have nonzero sines at its specified positive primitive point. The construction leaves one incident factor for the final complementary pairing; it does not treat that final pairing as a strict multiplication gate. Consequently every gate in that algebraically regular resolution has a local factorial description (17): use a half-plane chart at a nonreal argument and a real-chamber chart otherwise. This fills the local analytic description without assuming that all arguments have real part between zero and one. It retains every \(N\)-dependent Fourier factor and does not assert a nonzero unfactored symbol at a real out-of-support argument. The exact complementary pairing and its \(N-1\) reversal stay unchanged. A geometric primitive already marked by continuation must also stay unchanged. Here is the branch bookkeeping explicitly. For a single argument, two continued primitives with the same original normalization can differ locally by \[ 2\pi i(w\xi-h),\qquad w,h\in\mathbb Z. 	ag{22} \] Indeed continuation of \(\log(2\sin\pi\xi)\) around its simple zero at an integer \(r\) adds \(2\pi i\); its primitive changes by \(2\pi i(\xi-r)\). Composing finitely many signed loops gives (22). A change of derivative branch also changes the offset prefactor by the exact constant \(\exp\{2\pi i(a+	frac12)w\}\). For several arguments, if the previously marked phase is \[ S_{m geom}(\mathbf z) =S_{m chamber}(\mathbf z) +2\pi i(\lambda\cdot\mathbf z+\gamma), 	ag{23} \] retain that character and its associated offset constants. This includes any Fourier character already present in the spectral--Newton adapter, such as its signed-crossing shift \(-2\pi i\sigma x\); it is not restricted to new factorial monodromy. Relative to \(e^{NS_{m geom}}\), the Fourier factor in (17) is multiplied by \(e^{-2\pi iN(\lambda\cdot\mathbf z+\gamma)}\). Thus the wall-factor coefficient associated to this geometric mark comes from its coefficient at frequency \(\lambda\), not automatically from frequency zero. Theorem 2 identifies it with the nonzero constant coefficient only when the character has the corresponding zero frequency; it does not remove a nonzero \(\lambda\). Even when that local branch agrees, the original finite support cycle, the other Fourier modes, endpoints, shared-wire contractions and first-normal closing terms remain. No intersection number or full geometric contribution is deduced from the factorial chamber or its unit remainder. ## Direct sources * [Exact factorial interpolation](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/exact_factorial_interpolation_and_complex_contours.md), SHA256 \(	exttt{1f34f65437dfe0bfb4062a7a74840beae1676353cf13bb8a86f8849a8a36bc72}\): the specified gamma product, reflection, strip asymptotics with complex offsets and the actual supported residue cycle. * [Uniform half-plane continuation](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_factorial_uniform_halfplane_continuation.md), SHA256 \(	exttt{0514ffe3e13a887eccd9099b306117ee86553f0731d976315e2607b3e33493fa}\): marked \(J_\pm\), arbitrary off-real compact charts and the exact one-period phase. * [Factorial divisor criterion](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_factorial_rectangle_divisor_criterion.md), SHA256 \(	exttt{462b8c22c73f73b12152bca96cf6636708dcf153c2cbc2751458454827b3ddf8}\): actual zero/pole orders and the limitation of joint rectangular extension for multiplication. * [Spectral--Newton adapters](research_newton_spectral_legendre_adapters.md), SHA256 \(	exttt{34c0e2e1114488c6ac82a5dffbdbd8a4a8d85e7fbba252de91833dc8d697e303}\): literal multiplication and signed-crossing coefficients, carrier, transpose, offsets and the retained local Fourier lift. * [Positive primitive prefixes](research_positive_primitive_prefix_regularity.md), SHA256 \(	exttt{a01b55a71d133aadff4aac0929e50de03e1059991d6874e81646c770eb5604a6}\): all gate sine exclusions for the stated proper-prefix resolution, without a prior factorial-chart or cycle conclusion. The arguments use written proofs and source-text reads only. No mathematical code, numerical evidence, tests or compilation are used.

title: Local spectral adapters for the original Newton gates
A polynomial Newton operator bound for the original turn-trace density
text: # A polynomial Newton operator bound for the original turn-trace density Written proof, 24 November 2026. Earlier finals and public manuscripts are unchanged. The original diagonal turn kernel provides a canonical weight for the full-primary compression of the genuine turn. Every selected compression is invertible, with inverse norm at most \(m(N+2)\) when \(m\) distinct Casimir nodes are retained. This holds for every cluster size and includes both directions at each double root. For the whole algebra it gives a polynomial operator bound for the original turn-trace density. Its known small nodal weights and indefinite signature remain; no positive scalar closing or geometric lower bound is inferred. ## 1. Original algebra, turn and density Fix \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), and \(\eta=(-1)^d\). Use the full original algebra and normalized Newton basis [A,T]: \[ {\cal A}_N=\mathbb C[z]/P_N(z),\qquad P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2, \qquad c_j=2\cos((2j+1)\pi/N), \] \[ S_0=1,\qquad S_r=\prod_{h=1}^r2\sin(\pi h/N),\qquad b_r(z)=S_r^{-2}\prod_{j<r}(c_j-z),\quad 0\le r\le d. \tag{1} \] Here \(T_N\) is Chebyshev of the first kind. Newton coefficients carry their usual positive Hermitian norm. The basis polynomials are real. All first normals at double roots remain independent. The original turn and cylindrical closing satisfy \[ {\cal T}b_r=b_{d-r},\quad {\cal T}^*={\cal T}={\cal T}^{-1}, \qquad \phi(f)=\eta N^2[z^d]\operatorname{rem}_{P_N}f, \qquad \phi(b_rb_s)=\delta_{r+s,d}. \tag{2} \] Thus \(\phi(fg)=f^{\mathsf T}{\cal T}g\) on coefficient vectors. The other original row is \(\lambda_0=\phi{\cal T}\). No ordinary cap is substituted for the prescribed mark. Write \(Z=M_z\). The Newton product recurrence gives \[ Zb_r=c_rb_r-4\sin^2(\pi(r+1)/N)b_{r+1}\quad(r<d), \qquad Zb_d=c_db_d,\qquad \|Z\|\le6. \tag{3} \] The faithful full minimal polynomial is \(P_N\). Define the literal diagonal kernel and its canonical quotient inverse: \[ {\cal B}_N(z)=\sum_{r=0}^d b_r(z)^2,\qquad \mathfrak b_N={\cal B}_N^{-1}\ \text{in }{\cal A}_N. \tag{4} \] Since \({\cal B}_N(x)\ge1\) on the real axis, it is a unit in the full repeated-root algebra. The inverse retains its prescribed first derivatives, not only its distinct-root values. The existing turn-trace theorem [T] proves the exact original-source identity \[ \phi(f)=\operatorname{Tr}({\cal D}_N M_f),\qquad {\cal D}_N={\cal T}M_{\mathfrak b_N}. \tag{5} \] The trace acts on the \(N\)-dimensional Newton algebra. All original framing and external factors remain attached to the original source when (5) is used. ## 2. Full-primary Newton frames and their source normalization The distinct double nodes are indexed by \(0\le i\le\lfloor(N-2)/2\rfloor\). There is one additional simple node \(-2\) at odd levels. Let \({\cal I}_i\) be its full primary ideal, of dimension two or one respectively. For a double node \(c=c_i\), put \[ a_i=\eta(4-c^2),\qquad \chi_i=\frac{c}{4-c^2},\qquad v_i=(b_r(c))_{r=0}^d,\quad w_i=(b_r'(c))_{r=0}^d, \] \[ A_i=\|v_i\|^2={\cal B}_N(c),\qquad \alpha_i=\frac{v_i^{\mathsf T}w_i}{A_i},\qquad \delta_i=\frac{\|w_i-\alpha_iv_i\|}{\sqrt{A_i}}. \tag{6} \] These are real Newton coordinate vectors and a real positive normal scale, not magnetic Clebsch columns in a physical pair degree. The local source coefficients can be checked directly. The Chebyshev equation is \[ (4-z^2)P_N''-zP_N'+N^2(P_N-2)=0. \] For \(Q_i=P_N/(z-c)^2\), this equation and its derivative give \[ Q_i(c)=\frac{N^2}{4-c^2},\qquad \frac{Q_i'(c)}{Q_i(c)}=\frac{c}{4-c^2}. \] The original residue \(\eta N^2\operatorname{Res}(h/P_N)\) at \(c\) is therefore \[ a_i h'(c)-\eta c\,h(c). \tag{7} \] At the odd simple node, \(P_N'(-2)=N^2\), so its residue is \(h(-2)\). Let \(p_i\) be the full primary idempotent and \(n_i=(z-c_i)p_i\). Testing (7) on an arbitrary original spectator, and using the nondegenerate pairing (2), proves \[ n_i=a_i{\cal T}v_i,\qquad p_i={\cal T}(-\eta c_i v_i+a_iw_i). \tag{8} \] These identities prove that the following frame spans the entire actual primary ideal: \[ E_i=\left(\frac{{\cal T}v_i}{\sqrt{A_i}}, \frac{{\cal T}(w_i-\alpha_iv_i)} {\sqrt{A_i}\delta_i}\right),\qquad E_i^{\mathsf T}E_i=I_2, \qquad ZE_i=E_i\begin{pmatrix}c_i&\delta_i^{-1}\\0&c_i\end{pmatrix}. \tag{9} \] In particular \(\delta_i>0\). The first vector is the nilpotent eigenvector direction; the second retains the generalized direction. The Jordan identity follows from \((Z-c_i)p_i=n_i\), not from differentiating a root-only equality. At the odd simple node define \(v_i=(b_r(-2))_r\), \(A_i=\|v_i\|^2\), and \(E_i={\cal T}v_i/\sqrt{A_i}\). Its primary idempotent is \({\cal T}v_i\). Distinct primary ideals have zero product, hence \[ E_i^{\mathsf T}{\cal T}E_j=0 \qquad(i\ne j). \tag{10} \] All frames are real, so their transpose here is also their Hermitian adjoint. This is full-primary Frobenius orthogonality, not Hermitian orthogonality between the primary ideals themselves. Two existing kernel estimates control the scales in (6). Writing \(K_N(z,w)=\sum_r b_r(z)b_r(w)\), one has \[ \delta_i^2= \left.\partial_z\partial_w\log K_N(z,w)\right|_{(c_i,c_i)}. \] The all-color first-normal theorem [H, Theorem 1] gives \[ \frac18\le\delta_i\le\gamma_i,\qquad \gamma_i=\frac{N-2i-1}{4\sin\theta_i},\qquad \theta_i=(2i+1)\pi/N. \tag{11} \] The lower bound follows separately from (3),(9): \(\delta_i^{-1}\le\|Z-c_i\|\le8\). The diagonal-kernel derivative bound [T, (12)] also gives \[ -N^2/8\le\alpha_i\le0,\qquad {\cal B}_N'(c_i)=2A_i\alpha_i. \tag{12} \] ## 3. Canonical weighted turn blocks Formula (7) applied to (8),(9) yields \[ E_i^{\mathsf T}{\cal T}E_i =\frac1{a_iA_i\delta_i} \begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&(\chi_i-2\alpha_i)/\delta_i\end{pmatrix}. \tag{13} \] The original diagonal kernel, including its first normal (12), acts by \[ M_{{\cal B}_N}E_i =E_i A_i\begin{pmatrix}1&2\alpha_i/\delta_i\\0&1\end{pmatrix}. \] Consequently its shear cancels exactly: \[ C_i:=E_i^{\mathsf T}{\cal T}M_{{\cal B}_N}E_i =\frac1{a_i\delta_i} \begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&\chi_i/\delta_i\end{pmatrix}, \qquad C_i^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}-a_i\chi_i&a_i\delta_i\\ a_i\delta_i&0\end{pmatrix}. \tag{14} \] This uses the canonical source kernel \({\cal B}_N\), not a scalar replacement of its jets. Omitting its derivative would leave the \(\alpha_i\) term in (13). Now \(a_i\chi_i=\eta c_i\), and (11) gives \[ |a_i\delta_i| \le4\sin^2\theta_i\,\gamma_i =(N-2i-1)\sin\theta_i\le N . \] Splitting the last matrix in (14) into its diagonal and off-diagonal parts proves the universal bound \[ \|C_i^{-1}\|\le N+2. \tag{15} \] At the odd simple node the same weighted block is exactly \(C_i=1\). Cross blocks in (14) vanish for distinct nodes, since multiplication by \({\cal B}_N\) preserves each full primary ideal. ## 4. Every selected compression and the global density bound Select any nonempty set \(J\) of \(m\) distinct nodes, keeping each full primary ideal. Set \[ {\cal I}_J=\bigoplus_{i\in J}{\cal I}_i,\quad V=(E_i)_{i\in J},\quad G=V^{\mathsf T}V>0,\quad C=\operatorname{diag}_{i\in J}(C_i). \] Primary decomposition proves that \(V\) has full column rank. Its individual blocks are orthonormal, so \(\|V\|^2\le m\), without a lower Gram bound. Let \(P_J=VG^{-1}V^{\mathsf T}\) be the Newton orthogonal projection onto this selected sum and define its measured weighted turn by \[ H_J=P_J{\cal T}M_{{\cal B}_N}|_{{\cal I}_J}. \tag{16} \] For every coefficient vector \(x\), \(H_J(Vx)=VG^{-1}Cx\). Hence the inverse on the selected sum is \[ H_J^{-1}=VC^{-1}V^{\mathsf T}|_{{\cal I}_J},\qquad \boxed{\quad \|H_J^{-1}\|\le m(N+2),\qquad \|H_Ju\|\ge\frac{\|u\|}{m(N+2)}.\quad} \tag{17} \] Multiplying both displayed maps on \(Vx\) verifies both inverse identities. This argument needs no sublinear restriction, no estimate on \(\|G^{-1}\|\), and no ambient spectral-projector bound. For all \(q_N=\lceil N/2\rceil\) distinct nodes, the selected sum is the whole algebra. Then \(P_J=I\), and \[ ({\cal T}M_{{\cal B}_N})^{-1} =M_{\mathfrak b_N}{\cal T} =V\operatorname{diag}(C_i^{-1})V^{\mathsf T}. \] The order of these factors matters. The original density in (5) is \({\cal D}_N={\cal T}({\cal T}M_{{\cal B}_N})^{-1}{\cal T}\), not the inverse itself. Since the turn is unitary, \[ \boxed{\quad \|M_{\mathfrak b_N}\|_{{\rm Newt}\to{\rm Newt}} =\|{\cal D}_N\| \le\lceil N/2\rceil(N+2). \quad} \tag{18} \] This is an operator estimate on the entire original Newton algebra, including arbitrary coherent inputs and every first normal. It strengthens the earlier pointwise and real-boundary estimates for \(\mathfrak b_N\); it does not bound its inverse polynomially. For a fixed number \(r\) of contracted algebra copies, [T, (9)] gives \(\phi^{\otimes r}(F)=\operatorname{Tr}({\cal D}_N^{\otimes r}M_F)\). Put \(C_N^{\rm dens}=\lceil N/2\rceil(N+2)\). For every operator error \(\Delta A\) on that full tensor algebra, with \(\|A\|_1=\operatorname{Tr}\sqrt{A^*A}\), one has \[ |\operatorname{Tr}({\cal D}_N^{\otimes r}\Delta A)| \le(C_N^{\rm dens})^r\|\Delta A\|_1 \le(C_N^{\rm dens})^rN^r\|\Delta A\|_{\rm op}. \tag{18a} \] This is polynomial absolute source error with the actual density retained in the leading trace, not a relative scalar estimate. ## 5. The original closing under the canonical half-density The original cylindrical row on each paired frame is exactly \[ \phi E_i=A_i^{-1/2}(1,-\alpha_i/\delta_i). \tag{19} \] Indeed \(\phi({\cal T}v_i)=b_0(c_i)=1\) and \(\phi({\cal T}w_i)=b_0'(c_i)=0\). At the odd simple node the row is \(A_i^{-1/2}\). Let \(s_N\) be the real Hermite unit with \(s_N^2={\cal B}_N\) and positive nodal values. Its full prescribed jets are \(s_N(c_i)=\sqrt{A_i}\) and \(s_N'(c_i)=\sqrt{A_i}\alpha_i\) at double nodes; at the simple node only its value is prescribed. This is the inverse of the positive-jet square root of \(\mathfrak b_N\) used in [T]. Thus \[ M_{s_N}E_i=E_i\sqrt{A_i} \begin{pmatrix}1&\alpha_i/\delta_i\\0&1\end{pmatrix}, \qquad \phi M_{s_N}E_i=(1,0). \tag{20} \] The simple block gives \(\phi M_{s_N}E_i=1\). This identifies the original row in a specified full-normal frame. Its kernel remains: (20) is not a scalar lower bound for an arbitrary incoming packet. The unweighted source is restored with \(M_{s_N}^{-1}\); neither its action factor nor the original mark has been removed. ## 6. Scope and complete sources The weight in (14)--(18) is the actual diagonal kernel from the original turn-trace source. A double block has negative determinant. Also \({\cal D}_N\) is real symmetric, invertible, and has trace \(\phi(1)=0\), hence is indefinite. The operator upper bound (18) does not turn its original trace pairing into a positive norm. The original nodal weights \(\mathfrak b_N(c_i)\) can still be exponentially small at central nodes, as [T] proves. No lower bound for the smallest singular value of \({\cal D}_N\), an arbitrary original closing, or geometric coefficient is inferred. Nor is inserting \(P_J\) into a closed source authorized by (17): its omitted component and subsequent exterior remain. Actual turns, pivots, crossing phases and prescribed source rows retain their original meanings. The closest physical middle-weight turn theorem [M] already gives an exact kernel and positive transported boundary Gram. Its flat physical coordinates and positive-metric transport are different from the full-primary Newton compression considered here. There is no new interpolation or abstract compression method claimed. The new estimates are (17)--(18) for the canonical original-source density, with the explicit normal and closing calibrations above. No new knot-volume or finite-exception theorem is proved.
