title: Exact evaluation of the nine-cell crossing array
text: # Exact evaluation of the nine-cell crossing array Private written proof, 17 November 2026. We evaluate the actual six-variable source of [S], with all boundary indices. It is the specified planar crossing tensor times one explicit nowhere-zero scalar and the recorded charge phase. For every injective real vertex decoration, with real odd roots, that scalar has modulus exactly \(N^{-2}\). Its phase is retained. Neither the printed nine-cell formula nor a pentagon assertion is a premise. ## 1. Source conventions and result Use [S] unchanged: \(N>2\) is odd, \(q\) is primitive, \(d=N-1\), and halves are modulo \(N\). For a sorted cell \(T=abcd\), put \[ \alpha_T=\frac{s_{ad}s_{bc}}{s_{ac}s_{bd}},\quad \beta_T=\frac{s_{ab}s_{cd}}{s_{ac}s_{bd}},\quad Z_T=s_{ac}s_{bd},\qquad \alpha_T^N+\beta_T^N=1. \tag{1} \] The six vertex decorations are distinct. All roots and normalization square roots remain on the same lifted regular domain. In the notation \(W_T,\overline W_T\) of [S,(1)], \[ \frac{\overline W_T(j+1)}{\overline W_T(j)} =\frac{\beta_T}{1-\alpha_Tq^j},\qquad \frac{W_T(j)}{\overline W_T(j+1)} =\frac{1-\alpha_T}{\beta_T}. \tag{2} \] For five increasing labels define the literal finite sum \[ \mathfrak f_{abcde} =f\left(\alpha_{abcd},\alpha_{abce}/q \,\middle|\,\beta_{abcd}/\beta_{abce}\right). \tag{3} \] Here \(f\) is exactly [B,(4)]. With \(\mathfrak n\) exactly [S,(15)], define \[ \begin{split} J={}&\mathfrak n\, \mathfrak f_{01235}\mathfrak f_{01345}\mathfrak f_{12345}N^3 \frac{1-\alpha_{1245}}{\beta_{1245}} \frac{1-\alpha_{2345}}{\beta_{2345}} \frac{1-\alpha_{0145}}{\beta_{0145}} \frac{\beta_{1345}}{1-\alpha_{1345}^{N}},\\ C_N(\mathbf s)={}&\frac{J}{N^2} \left(\frac{s_{34}}{s_{01}s_{02}s_{03}s_{35}s_{45}^{\,2}}\right)^d . \end{split} \tag{4} \] Then the recovered canonical array in [S,(18)] is \[ \boxed{\mathcal R^0_{\mathbf i} =C_N(\mathbf s)q^{\,3(h_1-1)/2} R(\mathbf i\mid1,0,0,0).} \tag{5} \] The \(R\) on the right is the specified planar finite weight. The scalar \(C_N\) is holomorphic and nowhere zero on the stated lifted regular domain. For distinct real vertex decorations, real odd roots \(s_{ij}\), and positive square roots of the real divided-difference brackets in [B], \[ |C_N(\mathbf s)|=N^{-2}. \tag{6} \] No ordering of the real decorations is required. ## 2. Exact cyclic beta convolution The cyclic summand \(a_j\) of \(f(x,y\mid z)\), with \(z^N=(1-x^N)/(1-y^N)\), obeys \((1-xq^{j+1})a_{j+1}=z(1-yq^{j+1})a_j\). Hence \[ (1-z)f(x,y\mid z)=(x-qyz)f(x,y\mid qz), \tag{7} \] \[ f(x,qy\mid z) =\frac{f(x,y\mid z)-qy f(x,y\mid qz)}{1-qy} =\frac{x-qy}{(1-qy)(x-qyz)}f(x,y\mid z). \tag{8} \] These are finite-sum identities and do not divide by \(f\). For any \(K,L\in\mathbb Z/N\), they imply \[ \boxed{\sum_r q^{Kr} \frac{W_{abcd}(r)}{\overline W_{abce}(r+L)} =\mathfrak f_{abcde} \frac{\overline W_{acde}(K+L)} {\overline W_{bcde}(K)\overline W_{abde}(L)}.} \tag{9} \] Indeed, set \(x=\alpha_{abcd}\), \(y=\alpha_{abce}/q\), and \(z=\beta_{abcd}/\beta_{abce}=\alpha_{bcde}\). The left side is \(\overline W_{abce}(L)^{-1}f(x,q^Ly\mid q^Kz)\). Its \(K,L\) steps from (7),(8) equal those of the right side, using \[ \alpha_{acde}=\alpha_{abce}z/x,\quad \alpha_{abde}=\alpha_{abce}/x,\quad \beta_{acde}/\beta_{bcde}=1/x,\quad \beta_{acde}/\beta_{abde}=1/\beta_{abce}. \tag{10} \] At \(K=L=0\) both are (3). Every step multiplier is a unit: its denominators reduce to nonzero roots and \(1-\alpha_Tq^j\), with \(1-\alpha_T^N=\beta_T^N\ne0\). Periodicity retains the cyclic seam. If \(\mathfrak f_{abcde}\) vanished, these unit steps would make the left side zero for all \(K\) at \(L=0\). Fourier inversion would annihilate its nonzero summand vector. Thus every scalar (3) is nonzero. ## 3. The actual six sums and their prefactor Retain \(k_i=m_i-p_i+h_i\), \(\sum k_i=2\), and put \[ H=(3h_1-1)/2,\quad a=[-k_1],\quad m=[-k_2],\quad C=[k_3-1]+1\in\{1,\ldots,N\},\quad B=m-C. \tag{11} \] Off \(\sum k_i=2\), the actual source is already zero. The capital \(C\) is an integer representative, not \(C_N\). Define \[ (qX;q)_r= \begin{cases} \prod_{j=1}^{r}(1-q^jX),&r\ge0,\\ \displaystyle\prod_{j=0}^{-r-1}(1-q^{-j}X)^{-1},&r<0. \end{cases} \tag{12} \] In [S,(16)], first sum \(r\) by (9) for \(01235\), with \(K=u+v+1,\ L=1-k_1+s+z\). The remaining \(0235\) ratio is exactly \[ \frac{\overline W_{0235}(K+L)} {\overline W_{0235}(K+L-k_2)} =\beta_{0235}^{-m} \prod_{j=0}^{m-1}(1-\alpha_{0235}q^{K+L+j}). \tag{13} \] Expand by degree \(\ell\), whose coefficient is \(\beta_{0235}^{-m}(-\alpha_{0235})^\ell q^{\ell(\ell-1)/2}{m\brack\ell}_q\). Then sum \(s\) by (9) for \(01345\) with \(K=v+t+1+\ell,\ L=z+1-k_1\), and sum \(u\) for \(12345\) with \(K=t+1+\ell,\ L=v+1\). The remaining \(1345\) ratio is \(\beta_{1345}/(1-\alpha_{1345}q^{v+t+1+\ell})\). Equation (2) leaves the three linear ratios in (4), and the polynomials \[ \begin{split} &\beta_{2345}^{-\ell}\prod_{j=1}^{\ell} (1-\alpha_{2345}q^{t+j}),\\ &\beta_{0145}^{-a}\prod_{j=1}^{a} (1-\alpha_{0145}q^{z+j}),\\ &\beta_{0345}^{-b_\ell}\prod_{j=0}^{b_\ell-1} (1-\alpha_{0345}q^{v+t+z+2-k_1+\ell+j}),\qquad b_\ell=[B-\ell]. \end{split} \tag{14} \] Their unexpanded phase is \[ q^{(1+\ell)v+t+(1+\ell)z+1-k_1+H+\ell(2-k_1)}. \tag{15} \] Call the degree of the last polynomial \(j\), and let \(r=[-1-\ell-j]\). The exact \(v\)-sum is \[ \sum_v\frac{q^{(1+\ell+j)v}} {1-\alpha_{1345}q^{v+t+1+\ell}} =\frac{N\alpha_{1345}^{r}}{1-\alpha_{1345}^N} q^{-(1+\ell+j)(t+1+\ell)}. \tag{16} \] The \(t\)-sum selects its polynomial's top degree \(\ell\), contributing \(N(-\alpha_{2345})^\ell q^{\ell(\ell+1)/2}\beta_{2345}^{-\ell}\). The \(z\)-sum selects degree \(r\le a\), or is zero, and contributes the third \(N\). The collected phase and signs are \[ q^{H-k_1}q^{-k_1\ell} (-1)^j q^{j(j-1)/2+(1-k_1)j} (-1)^r q^{r(r-1)/2+r}. \tag{17} \] The root identities \[ \alpha_{0235}\alpha_{2345}/\beta_{2345} =\alpha_{0345}/\beta_{0345},\qquad \alpha_{1345}\alpha_{0145}=\alpha_{0345} \tag{18} \] give the remaining factor \(\alpha_{0345}^{\ell+j+r}\beta_{0345}^{-\ell-b_\ell}\). The only ordinary totals congruent to \(d\) are \(d,2N-1\). Thus all three \(N\)'s and all endpoint contributions in (4) are retained. Define the rational function \[ F(X)=\sum_{\ell=0}^{m}{m\brack\ell}_q q^{a\ell} X^\ell(qX;q)_{a+m-C-\ell}. \tag{19} \] All its Gaussian binomial denominators have order below \(N\). Split \(F=L+U\) at \(\ell\le B\) and \(\ell>B\), with empty parts zero. The first is polynomial of degree at most \(a+B<2N-1\). For the second, the actual polynomial from (14) is \(1-X^N\) times the corresponding rational term. Using \(\beta_{0345}^N=1-\alpha_{0345}^N\), the precise result of (13)--(18) is \[ \begin{split} b(\mathbf k)={}& Jq^{H-k_1}\beta_{0235}^{-m}\beta_{0145}^{-a} \alpha_{0345}^d\beta_{0345}^{-B}\\ &{}\cdot\left([X^d]F+ \frac{\alpha_{0345}^N}{1-\alpha_{0345}^N}[X^{2N-1}]F\right). \end{split} \tag{20} \] This equality comes from the original six sums, not a substituted boundary representative. ## 4. Rational coefficient and exact triangular support The finite binomial convolution gives the exact factorization \[ F(X)=(qX;q)_{a-C} \sum_{r=0}^{m}{m\brack r}_q q^{ar} (q^{1-C};q)_r X^r. \tag{21} \] Indeed factor out \((qX;q)_{a-C}\) in (19), expand the remaining \((q^{a-C+1}X;q)_{m-\ell}\), and use \[ {m\brack\ell}_q{m-\ell\brack r-\ell}_q ={m\brack r}_q{r\brack\ell}_q. \] The coefficient of \(X^r\), apart from \({m\brack r}_q q^{ar}\), is exactly \[ \sum_{j=0}^{r}{r\brack j}_q(-1)^j q^{j(j-1)/2+(1-C)j}=(q^{1-C};q)_r. \tag{22} \] All used factorial orders are below \(N\). The polynomial in (21) has degree at most \(\min(m,C-1)\), because its displayed product vanishes for \(r\ge C\). Hence \(F\) has degree at infinity at most \(a-1\). If \(C\le a\), \(F\) is polynomial, so both coefficients in (20) vanish. If \(C>a\), its poles are simple and lie among \(1,q,\ldots,q^{C-a-1}\), and its polynomial part has degree at most \(a-1<d\). Partial fractions therefore give \[ [X^{2N-1}]F=[X^d]F=-[X^{-1}]_\infty F. \tag{23} \] Consequently, with \(c(\mathbf k)=[X^d]F\), (20) becomes \[ b(\mathbf k)=Jq^{H-k_1}\beta_{0235}^{-m}\beta_{0145}^{-a} \alpha_{0345}^d\beta_{0345}^{C-m-N}c(\mathbf k) \tag{24} \] when \(C>a\), and is zero otherwise. Put \(n=a+m-C\), \(h=C-a-1\), and \(M=m-h=n+1\). If \(M<0\), every summand is \(O(X^{-2})\) at infinity, so \(c=0\). If \(M\ge0\), only \(\ell\ge M\) contribute a \(1/X\) term and \[ -[X^{-1}]_\infty X^\ell(qX;q)_{n-\ell} =(-1)^{\ell-M}q^{(\ell-M)(\ell-M+1)/2}{\ell\brack M}_q. \tag{25} \] Indeed, expansion of the reciprocal product at infinity leaves the complete homogeneous coefficient \({\ell\brack M}_q\). Use \({m\brack\ell}_q{\ell\brack M}_q ={m\brack M}_q{m-M\brack\ell-M}_q\) and the finite binomial identity: \[ \boxed{c(\mathbf k)=q^{aM} \frac{p_m p_{C-1}}{p_Mp_hp_a},\qquad p_j=\prod_{r=1}^{j}(1-q^r).} \tag{26} \] All these indices lie in \(0,\ldots,d\). The exact nonzero support is \(C>a,\ M\ge0\); there are no undeclared cyclic carries. ## 5. Comparison with the specified planar weight Let \(\Phi(\mathbf k)=\sum_{\mathbf i} R(\mathbf i\mid1,0,0,0)q^{\sum i_jk_j}\). The literal composition of \(d\) in [S, Section 6] gives zero unless \(\sum k_i=2\). On that support the same direct substitution gives \[ \Phi=N^2q^{1-k_1}\sum_{z=0}^{d}q^{-z(k_1+k_2+z)} S_{d-z}(q^{-k_1-z})S_z(q^{1+z-k_3}),\quad S_j(X)=\frac{\prod_{r=1}^{j}(X-q^r)}{p_j}. \tag{27} \] The two factors restrict \(a\le z\le C-1\). When \(C>a\), put \(z=a+j\), \(h=C-a-1\), and \(M=m-h\). Substitute the products \(S\) and the exact reflection identity \(p_{d-r}p_r=N(-1)^r q^{r(r+1)/2}\). The remaining sum is \[ \frac{\Phi}{N^2q^{1-k_1}} =q^{aM}\frac{p_{C-1}}{p_a p_h} \sum_{j=0}^{h}{h\brack j}_q(-1)^j q^{j(j-1)/2+(M+1)j} =q^{aM}\frac{p_{C-1}}{p_a p_h}(q^{M+1};q)_h . \tag{28} \] This is the elementary finite binomial formula already proved in [S,(31)]. If \(M<0\), the product contains \(1-q^0\); otherwise it is \(p_m/p_M\), since \(M+h=m\le d\). Equations (26),(28), including every zero, prove \[ \Phi(\mathbf k)=N^2q^{1-k_1}c(\mathbf k). \tag{29} \] On this support set \(a_i=[-k_i]\). We have \(a_3=N-C\) and \(a_4=d-M\), the latter because \(k_4\equiv M+1\) and \(0\le M\le d\). Together with \(M=m-C+a+1\), this gives \(\sum_i a_i=2d\). Since \(f_i(k_i)=s_{0i}^{d-a_i}s_{i5}^{a_i}\), direct cancellation yields \[ \frac{\beta_{0235}^{-m}\beta_{0145}^{-a} \alpha_{0345}^d\beta_{0345}^{C-m-N}} {\prod_i f_i(k_i)} =\left(\frac{s_{05}s_{34}} {s_{01}s_{02}s_{03}s_{35}s_{45}^{\,2}}\right)^d . \tag{30} \] For example, \(\beta_{0145}=s_{01}s_{45}/(s_{04}s_{15})\), \(\beta_{0235}\beta_{0345}=s_{02}s_{45}/(s_{04}s_{25})\), and \(\beta_{0345}=s_{03}s_{45}/(s_{04}s_{35})\); the fourth exponent is fixed by \(\sum a_i=2d\). Equations (24),(29),(30) prove the all-boundary identity \[ b(\mathbf k)=C_N(\mathbf s)q^{3(h_1-1)/2}s_{05}^d \Phi(\mathbf k)\prod_i f_i(k_i). \tag{31} \] Both sides also vanish off their common support. The exact inverse adapter of [S] proves (5). Every factor in (4) is a unit by [B], (1), and the argument following (10). ## 6. Exact modulus for all distinct real decorations Now every vertex decoration is real and distinct, and every odd root is chosen real. Their order can be arbitrary. The function \(t^N\) is strictly increasing, so every divided-difference bracket \((U^N-V^N)/(N(U-V))\) in [B] is positive. Choose its square roots positive, consistently in each normalization. Conjugating a finite sum and replacing its cyclic index by its negative gives \[ f_q(x,y\mid z)^* =f_q(\bar y/q,\bar x/q\mid\bar z^{-1}). \tag{32} \] The summand is periodic, so this also holds for negative real \(z\). Applied to [B], it gives \(\bar\rho_T=\rho_T^*\) and \[ |\rho_T|^2=|\bar\rho_T|^2 =\frac{Z_T^d\beta_T^N}{N(1-\alpha_T)}. \tag{33} \] This is positive: \(d\) is even and \((1-\alpha_T^N)/(1-\alpha_T)>0\) for real \(\alpha_T\ne1\). Only within the following formula let \(A=abcd,B=abce,C=acde,D=bcde,E=abde\). The conjugate of (3) is its paired sum in [B,(11)]. That proved finite product and (10) give \[ |\mathfrak f_{abcde}|^2 =N\frac{(1-\alpha_A)(1-\alpha_B)(1-\alpha_C)\beta_D^N} {\beta_A^N(1-\alpha_D)(1-\alpha_E)}. \tag{34} \] This is a signed rational identity valid on every real component; no continuation across a collision is used. Multiply (33) for the nine cells and (34) for the three beta sums. Six linear factors cancel immediately. The other three are canceled by the squared linear ratios explicitly retained in (4). The powers of \(N\) are \(N^{-9}N^3N^6=1\). Using \[ \beta_{0125}\beta_{0235}\beta_{0345}=\beta_{0145},\qquad \beta_{1235}\beta_{1345}=\beta_{1245}, \tag{35} \] all remaining factors reduce to \[ |J|^2=\mathfrak e^{\,2}\! \left(\prod_{\text{nine }T}Z_T\right)^d \left(\frac{\beta_{1245}\beta_{2345}\beta_{0145}} {\beta_{1345}}\right)^{2d},\quad \mathfrak e=(s_{12}s_{23}s_{34}s_{14})^{-d}. \tag{36} \] This retains the original edge weights. Finally \[ \prod_{\text{nine }T}Z_T =(s_{02}s_{03}s_{04}s_{13}s_{14}s_{15}s_{24}s_{25}s_{35})^2, \] so substitution in (36) proves \[ |J|=\left|\frac{s_{01}s_{02}s_{03}s_{35}s_{45}^{\,2}}{s_{34}}\right|^d . \tag{37} \] Equation (6) now follows from (4), at every allowed odd level. This proves a modulus, not constancy of the holomorphic phase. ## 7. Charge and source scope For the full charge table of [S], its exact sector transport gives \[ \mathcal R^\chi_{\mathbf i} =C_N(\mathbf s)q^{3(h_1-1)/2+d_\chi+\zeta+w} R(\mathbf i\mid x,y,\zeta,w). \tag{38} \] Here \(d_\chi\) is exactly [S,(17b)], not a discarded charge gauge. All boundary indices and both sides of each paired face remain. The identities are holomorphic on the same lifted regular domain; fixed-order decoration derivatives retain \(C_N\) and its derivatives. Thus the previously unresolved array comparison is evaluated, with an explicit scalar whose modulus is known for arbitrary distinct real decorations. No globally canonical sector, new cut, or identity wire pairing is substituted. Global contractions must retain the original paired-face wire, charge, vertex, and edge factors. This proves no even-level tetrahedral extension, off-root quantum derivative, free-vertex source adapter, or selected geometric-period lower bound. The residual phase is not asserted to be constant or a root of unity. ## Complete direct sources - [S] [Literal nine-cell source reduction](research_nine_tetrahedron_boundary_source_reduction.md), SHA256 5aeecb0c174f33baa1264bc34c7419d4ccae007e84f4410b3dcb47c6c81c554c. The entire proof and its complete primary definition were read. - [B] [Literal charged tetrahedron inverse and bubble](research_literal_charged_tetrahedron_bubble.md), SHA256 1dfe35f26137572235b1c3af66dcf410e0af758836baddaa8dd6d958c0f61d9b. The entire proof was read; only its proved finite normalization identities are used. No mathematical program, numerical experiment, or knot example was used.

title: The literal nine-tetrahedron source and its paired-face quotient
text: # The literal nine-tetrahedron source and its paired-face quotient Private written proof, 17 November 2026. This records the complete incidence, a charge lift, and an exact six-variable reduction of the nine-cell crossing source specified in [K, Section 4]. In the explicit charge lift, for every crossing sector, the actual boundary tensor lies in the paired-face adapter image proved in [A]. Its inverse loses no boundary data. The recovered four-index tensor is **not yet identified** with Kashaev's crossing weight. Neither the printed identity (4.25) nor a closed contraction of it is a premise. An ordered-decoration limit also proves a normalization obstruction: with the explicit 1994 scalars used here, one actual boundary entry has leading coefficient \(q\), whereas the unit-coefficient printed crossing expression has \(N^2q\). This does not evaluate the recovered array globally. ## 1. Conventions and the nine cells Let \(N>2\) be odd, \(q\) a primitive \(N\)-th root, and let \(\epsilon=1/2\) in \(\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z\). All indices, charges, and exponents of \(q\) below are in that ring. Choose six distinct complex vertex decorations \(z_0,\ldots,z_5\), and compatible fixed roots \[ s_{ij}^{\,N}=z_i-z_j\qquad(i<j). \] Work on a lifted regular domain for those roots and the normalization square roots in [B]. For a sorted tetrahedron \(T=abcd\), put \[ X_T=s_{ad}s_{bc},\qquad Y_T=s_{ab}s_{cd},\qquad Z_T=s_{ac}s_{bd}. \] Then \(X_T^N+Y_T^N=Z_T^N\), and all three entries are nonzero. Write \[ W_T(n)=\prod_{j=1}^{[n]}\frac{Y_T}{Z_T-X_Tq^j}, \qquad \overline W_T(n)= \prod_{j=1}^{[n]}\frac{Y_T}{Z_T-(X_T/q)q^j}. \tag{1} \] These are nonzero periodic functions. The bar in this notation is a label and does not mean complex conjugation. The scalars \(\rho_T,\bar\rho_T\) are the literal finite normalizations of [B, (2),(5)], with \[ (P,Q,R,B,C,H)=(s_{ab},s_{bc},s_{cd},s_{ac},s_{bd},s_{ad}). \tag{2} \] In particular all normalization sums and their shared root choices remain present. The 1995 paper refers to the earlier paper for these scalar functions, without displaying a scalar-conversion formula there. Our normalization is the explicit one in (2); a different conversion must be stated and checked, rather than supplied by assuming its printed contraction. For the sorted tetrahedron let \(\alpha_i\) denote the face omitting local vertex \(i\). The local charges are written \((a,b,c)\) on the opposite pairs \[ ab|cd,\qquad ac|bd,\qquad ad|bc, \quad\text{with }a+b+c=\epsilon, \] where the letters in the pairs denote the vertices, not the charges. The parameters in the tensor are the first and third charges. To avoid an implicit matrix convention, define the positive and negative tensors directly from [K, (4.6),(4.7)]: \[ \begin{split} T_T(a,c)_{\alpha,\beta}^{\gamma,\delta} &=\rho_T\, q^{c(\gamma-\alpha)+\alpha\delta+ac/2+\alpha^2/2} W_T(\gamma-a-\alpha)\, \delta_{\beta,\gamma+\delta},\\ \bar T_T(a,c)_{\gamma,\delta}^{\alpha,\beta} &=\bar\rho_T\, q^{c(\gamma-\alpha)-\alpha\delta-ac/2-\alpha^2/2} \overline W_T(\gamma+a-\alpha)^{-1} \delta_{\beta,\gamma+\delta}. \end{split} \tag{3} \] For either orientation the four face slots are \((\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta)=(\alpha_3,\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\alpha_0)\). The nine ordered cells and their orientations are \[ \begin{array}{c|rrrrrrrrr} T&1234&1245&2345&0123&0134&0125&0235&0345&0145\\ \hline \operatorname{sign}(T)&+&+&+&+&+&-&-&-&+ \end{array}. \tag{4} \] Indeed, starting with positive \(1234\), the four first attachments are positive. Their remaining octahedral faces are filled by the last four cells with the signs in (4). This can also be checked by cancelling the oriented boundaries occurrence by occurrence. Here is every internal face pairing; the number in parentheses is the omitted local vertex: \[ \begin{array}{c|ll} 123&1234(3)&0123(0)\\ 124&1234(2)&1245(3)\\ 134&1234(1)&0134(0)\\ 234&1234(0)&2345(3)\\ 013&0123(2)&0134(3)\\ 245&1245(0)&2345(1)\\ 012&0123(3)&0125(3)\\ 125&1245(2)&0125(0)\\ 023&0123(1)&0235(3)\\ 235&2345(2)&0235(0)\\ 034&0134(1)&0345(3)\\ 345&2345(0)&0345(0)\\ 014&0134(2)&0145(3)\\ 145&1245(1)&0145(0) \end{array}. \tag{5} \] Each map preserves the displayed vertex labels. The four edges \(05\) belonging to the four last cells remain distinct. Write \(p_m=\alpha_m^+\) and \(m_m=\alpha_m^-\) for the two boundary faces \(0m5\). The actual boundary slots are \[ \begin{array}{c|cc} 0125&015=p_1&025=m_2\\ 0235&025=p_2&035=m_3\\ 0345&035=p_3&045=m_4\\ 0145&015=m_1&045=p_4 . \end{array} \tag{6} \] The sign here uses [K]'s right/left face convention: in a positive sorted tetrahedron faces \(3,1\) are right, and faces \(2,0\) are left. A right face has the negative sign in the oriented simplicial boundary. This explains the apparent reversal between (4) and (6). There are no interior vertices. The interior edges are \(12,13,14,23,24,34\); the specified tangle consists of \(13,24\). Consequently the only interior edge weights in [K, (4.19)] are \[ \mathfrak e=(s_{12}s_{23}s_{34}s_{14})^{-(N-1)}. \tag{7} \] There is no interior-vertex power of \(N\) in this crossing ball. These statements follow directly from (5),(6), rather than from an Euler-characteristic argument about a different cellulation. ## 2. An explicit charge lift Let the four distinct \(05\) charges, in collar order, be \((x,y,z,w)\), with \(x+y+z+w=1\). Let \(h_m\) be the total charge on the boundary edge \(m5\), with \(\sum_m h_m=2\). The following opposite-pair triples give an actual charge lift: \[ \begin{array}{c|ccc} 1234&0&\epsilon&0\\ 1245&0&\epsilon&0\\ 2345&1&\epsilon-1&0\\ 0123&-y&x+y-\epsilon&1-x\\ 0134&1-z&\epsilon-w&-x-y\\ 0125&y+z-h_1&h_1+w-\epsilon&x\\ 0235&1+z-h_1-h_2&h_1+h_2-y-z-\epsilon&y\\ 0345&h_4-1&1+\epsilon-h_4-z&z\\ 0145&0&\epsilon-w&w . \end{array} \tag{8} \] Every row sums to \(\epsilon\). The four non-link interior totals are one, and the two link totals are zero. For example the totals on \(13,24\) are respectively \[ \epsilon+(x+y-\epsilon)-x-y=0,\qquad \epsilon+0+(\epsilon-1)=0. \] On \(14\) the total is \(\epsilon+(\epsilon-w)+w=1\); the totals on \(12,23,34\) are respectively \(1-x+x,1-y+y,1-z+z\). Substitution also gives \[ c_{\rm tot}(m5)=h_m,\qquad c_{\rm tot}(0m)=1-h_m. \tag{9} \] Thus the boundary conditions used here are exactly specified. Conversely, the two sum conditions are necessary for any such charge assignment. Each of vertices \(1,\ldots,4\) occurs in six tetrahedra. Subtracting its three prescribed interior-edge totals from its total vertex charge \(6\epsilon=3\) gives \(c_{\rm tot}(0m)+c_{\rm tot}(m5)=1\). The sum of all nine tetrahedral edge-charge sums is nine. Subtracting the four non-link interior totals leaves boundary sum five, hence \(x+y+z+w=1\). Vertex \(5\) then gives \(\sum_mh_m+(x+y+z+w)=3\), or \(\sum_mh_m=2\). No division other than the legitimate odd-level \(1/2\) is used. For the rest of the finite reduction fix the canonical sector \[ (x,y,z,w)=(1,0,0,0), \tag{10} \] while retaining all four \(h_m\) and all eight boundary face indices. This is one local charge sector, not permission to choose all sectors canonically in a global diagram whose region totals are prescribed. ## 3. Eliminating every Kronecker symbol Give the internal faces the following names: \[ \begin{array}{c|rrrrrrrrrrrrrr} \text{face}&123&124&134&234&013&245&012&125&023&235&034&345&014&145\\ \hline \text{index}&A&B&C&D&E&F&G&H&I&J&K&L&M&V . \end{array} \tag{11} \] The letter \(V\) here is the index on face \(145\). The nine deltas in (3) say \[ \begin{gathered} C=B+D,\quad V=H+F,\quad F=J+L,\quad I=E+A,\quad K=M+C,\\ H=m_2-p_1,\quad J=m_3-p_2,\quad L=m_4-p_3,\quad V=p_4-m_1. \tag{12} \end{gathered} \] The last four determine \(H,J,L,V\); the first three then impose one boundary condition, \[ \sum_m(m_m-p_m)=0. \tag{13} \] When it holds, the six free internal indices are \(A,B,D,E,G,M\). Every eliminated sum contributes exactly one. In particular no factor \(N\) may be inserted for a redundant boundary delta. Set \[ k_m=m_m-p_m+h_m. \] Condition (13) is equivalent to \(\sum_m k_m=2\). Make the following invertible affine change of the six free indices: \[ u=B-A,\quad v=H-B,\quad t=J-1-D,\quad r=E-G,\quad s=M-1-E,\quad z=m_1-M. \tag{14} \] Here \(z\) is a finite summation index, not a vertex decoration. For example the inverse gives \[ B=H-v,\ A=H-v-u,\ D=J-1-t,\ M=m_1-z,\ E=m_1-1-z-s,\ G=m_1-1-z-s-r. \] Thus (14) is a bijection over every odd \(\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z\), including composite levels. Define the fully retained normalization \[ \mathfrak n=\mathfrak e\, \rho_{1234}\rho_{1245}\rho_{2345}\rho_{0123}\rho_{0134} \bar\rho_{0125}\bar\rho_{0235}\bar\rho_{0345}\rho_{0145}. \tag{15} \] Let \(\mathcal B(\mathbf m,\mathbf p)\) be the literal sum of the nine tensors (3), over all fourteen internal faces (5), multiplied by (7). Then it is zero unless \(\sum k_m=2\). On that support it is exactly \[ \begin{split} \mathcal B(\mathbf m,\mathbf p)=\mathfrak n \sum_{u,v,t,r,s,z} &q^{\,\Xi(u,v,t,r,s,z;\mathbf k,h_1)} W_{1234}(u)W_{1245}(v)W_{2345}(t)\\ {}\cdot& W_{0123}(r)W_{0134}(s)W_{0145}(z)\\ {}\cdot& \left[ \overline W_{0125}(1-k_1+r+s+z)\, \overline W_{0235}(2-k_1-k_2+u+v+s+z)\, \overline W_{0345}(k_4+t+v+z) \right]^{-1}, \end{split} \tag{16} \] where every sum runs independently over \(\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z\), and \[ \Xi=u(1+t+r)+v(1+r+s)+(1+t)(1+s)+z+r-k_1 +(3h_1-1)/2. \tag{17} \] All denominators in (16) are units on the specified regular domain. For completeness, the phase calculation is as follows. Before the deltas are substituted, the explicit non-Gaussian tensor phases sum to \[ AD+BF+DL+GA+EC-IJ-KL+MV-GH-M+E+p_1-G+(h_1-1)/2. \] The Gaussians inside the two-index \(w\)'s contribute \[ (A^2+B^2+D^2+E^2-I^2-K^2+M^2)/2 =-EA-MB-MD-BD. \] Use (12), then (14). The terms containing \(H,J\) cancel, and the result is precisely (17). The six numerator arguments become the six variables in (14). The three denominator arguments become the ones displayed in (16). This proves (16) from the literal source, without a tetrahedral move identity or an assumed crossing formula. ## 4. General sectors, the actual paired-face image, and its inverse The same calculation also transports the specified charge lift to every sector \(\chi=(x,y,\zeta,w)\), with \(x+y+\zeta+w=1\). Here \(\zeta\) is the third sector charge, distinguished from the summation variable \(z\). Let \(\mathcal B_\chi\) denote the source with the full table (8), and let \(\mathcal B_0\) denote (16). Then \[ \mathcal B_\chi(\mathbf m,\mathbf p) =q^{D_\chi(\mathbf k,\mathbf h)} \mathcal B_0(\mathbf m,\mathbf p), \tag{17a} \] where \[ \begin{split} D_\chi={}&(\zeta+w)k_1-y k_2+\zeta k_4+d_\chi,\\ d_\chi={}&\zeta-2y+w/2 -\tfrac32(\zeta+w)h_1+\tfrac32y h_2-\tfrac32\zeta h_4 . \end{split} \tag{17b} \] This is an exact charge-gauge formula for the particular table (8). To verify it, keep the variables (14) before translation. The two changed numerator arguments are \(r+y,s+\zeta\). The first and second denominator arguments acquire respectively \(y+\zeta\) and \(\zeta\); the third is unchanged. Thus the bijection \(r'=r+y,s'=s+\zeta\) restores exactly the canonical arguments. Collecting the changed \(c(\gamma-\alpha)\) and \(ac/2\) terms in (3), and subtracting the corresponding change in (17), leaves (17b). More explicitly, the change from the \(c(\gamma-\alpha)\) terms before translation is \[ yu+(y+\zeta)v+\zeta t +(\zeta+w)k_1-y k_2+\zeta k_4 +\zeta-(\zeta+w)h_1+y h_2-\zeta h_4. \] The remaining constant from the \(ac/2\) terms is \[ \zeta+w/2-y-\tfrac12(\zeta+w)h_1 +\tfrac12y h_2-\tfrac12\zeta h_4. \] The change of the canonical phase under \(r,s\mapsto r+y,s+\zeta\) is \(yu+(y+\zeta)v+\zeta t+\zeta+y\). Subtracting it proves (17a),(17b), including every constant. Equation (16) depends on the eight boundary indices only through the four \(k_m\). Therefore simultaneous translation of \(m_m,p_m\) leaves the actual tensor unchanged, independently for every leg. Equations (17a),(17b) prove the same conclusion for all sectors. This proves its membership in the fourfold diagonal-translation invariant image in [A]. It is a property of the calculated source, not merely of a proposed right-hand expression. Put \[ f_m(k)=s_{0m}^{[k-1]}s_{m5}^{[-k]}. \] Let \(b_\chi(\mathbf k)\) denote (16) multiplied by (17a), extended by zero off \(\sum k_m=2\). The inverse adapter yields the unique array \[ \mathcal R^\chi_{\mathbf i} =\frac1{s_{05}^{N-1}N^4} \sum_{\mathbf k\in(\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z)^4} b_\chi(\mathbf k)\prod_{m=1}^4\frac{q^{-i_mk_m}}{f_m(k_m)}. \tag{18} \] Finite Fourier inversion gives the exact all-boundary identity \[ \mathcal B_\chi(\mathbf m,\mathbf p) =s_{05}^{N-1}\sum_{\mathbf i}\mathcal R^\chi_{\mathbf i} \prod_{m=1}^4 q^{i_m k_m}f_m(k_m). \tag{19} \] Equation (19) defines and recovers the array (18); it does not identify it with the published \(R\). All boundary rows must be transported by the inverse from [A], rather than by a newly chosen Hermitian adjoint. The support already proved implies \[ \mathcal R^\chi_{i_1+\ell,\ldots,i_4+\ell} =q^{-2\ell}\mathcal R^\chi_{\mathbf i}. \tag{20} \] The literal planar definition [K, (2.8)] has the same covariance: its four difference arguments are unchanged and its explicit phase changes by \(q^{-2\ell}\). This is a verified consistency condition, not a uniqueness statement. The complete sector transport of the recovered array is also explicit: \[ \mathcal R^\chi_{\mathbf i} =q^{d_\chi} \mathcal R^0_{\,i_1-\zeta-w,\ i_2+y,\ i_3,\ i_4-\zeta}. \tag{20a} \] For comparison, direct substitution in the *specified* planar definition gives \[ R(i_1,i_2,i_3,i_4\mid x,y,\zeta,w) =q^{\zeta+w} R(i_1,i_2+1-x,i_3+\zeta+w,i_4+w\mid1,0,0,0). \tag{20b} \] The four finite-product arguments agree term by term; the displayed phase is the remaining explicit prefactor. Using (20), the shifts in (20a),(20b) agree up to a common translation. Thus a canonical identification, if proved with scalar \(C_N\), would give scalar \(C_Nq^{d_\chi+\zeta+w}\) in this particular charge lift. This records a calibration to check; it does not assume the canonical identification or discard the root phase. The construction is an equality of finite holomorphic functions on the same lifted regular domain. Fixed-order decoration derivatives retain (16)--(19), including the normalizations and inverse adapters. No off-root quantum deformation or original meridian-normal identification is implied. ## 5. The retained 1994/1995 charge phase and the open identity There is a literal convention difference which matters before a global comparison. In the operator convention of [B, (17)], take the lower indices of the uncharged \(\mathcal R_{\alpha,\beta}^{\gamma,\delta}\) as matrix rows. This is the convention in the action on the CG-index vector. Expanding the first line of that formula gives \[ T^{94}_{\alpha,\beta}{}^{\gamma,\delta} =\rho_T q^{c(\gamma-\alpha)+\alpha\delta-ac/2+\alpha^2/2} W_T(\gamma-a-\alpha)\delta_{\beta,\gamma+\delta}. \tag{21} \] Indeed \(Y^{-a}\) selects row \(\alpha+a\) with factor \(q^{-a\alpha-a^2/2}\), while the left \(Z^{-c}\) contributes \(q^{-c(\alpha+a)}\). The right clocks contribute \(q^{c\gamma-a\delta}\); the uncharged kernel contributes \(q^{(\alpha+a)\delta+(\alpha+a)^2/2}\). Together with \(q^{ac/2}\) these give (21). Thus the explicit 1995 definition (3) obeys \[ T^{95}(a,c)=q^{ac}T^{94}(a,c),\qquad \bar T^{95}(a,c)=q^{-ac}\bar T^{94}(a,c). \tag{22} \] The second equality follows by the same inverse/conjugate-index calculation; its phase is inverse. Complementary-charge inverse and bubble pairs in [B] consequently retain their exact scalar. For the canonical charge lift (8),(10), the signed sum of \(ac\) over the nine cells is \(h_1-1\). Therefore \[ \mathcal B^{95}=q^{h_1-1}\mathcal B^{94}. \tag{23} \] In particular the symmetric boundary choice \(h_m=1/2\), which satisfies both \(\sum h_m=2\) and complementary wire charges, has the recorded factor \(q^{-1/2}\). This factor is not suppressed. The remaining crossing equation is the evaluation of (18) as the specified planar tensor [K, (2.8)], with the precise chosen charge gauge and root phase. Neither the shared covariance (20), the existence of the inverse boundary adapter, nor the nonzero factors in (15) proves that evaluation. It requires an additional finite sum identity or a sufficient set of actual boundary intertwining relations with their support and initialization proved. This note does not assert pointwise nonvanishing of the recovered array, invertibility, triangular support, or equality to a quantum-group crossing. It makes no selected geometric-period or large-\(N\) asymptotic claim. ## 6. A complete normalization test at every allowed level Fix any odd \(N>2\). Take the admissible canonical data \[ (x,y,\zeta,w)=(1,0,0,0),\qquad \mathbf h=(1,0,0,1),\qquad \mathbf p=(0,0,0,0),\qquad \mathbf m=(0,1,0,-1). \tag{24} \] Thus \(\mathbf k=(1,1,0,0)\), and all boundary constraints hold. Let the real vertex decorations be \[ z_i=L^{5-i}\quad(0\le i\le5),\qquad L>1,\qquad L\longrightarrow\infty . \tag{25} \] Choose every \(s_{ij}\) positive, and choose the normalization square roots in [B] positive on this ordered real domain. All the data are regular for every \(L>1\). This is a limit with \(N\) fixed; no uniformity in \(N\) is asserted. For each sorted tetrahedron put \(\varepsilon_T=Y_T/Z_T\) and \(\xi_T=X_T/Z_T\). Both are positive, \(\varepsilon_T\to0\), and \(\xi_T=(1-\varepsilon_T^N)^{1/N}\to1\). Put \[ p_n=\prod_{j=1}^n(1-q^j),\qquad p_0=1. \] For \(1\le n<N\), the literal finite products (1) give \[ W_T(n)\sim\frac{\varepsilon_T^n}{p_n},\qquad \overline W_T(n)^{-1} \sim\frac{\varepsilon_T^{N-n}}{N}\,p_{n-1}. \tag{26} \] For the second formula, separate its \(j=0\) factor: \[ \overline W_T(n)^{-1} =\varepsilon_T^{-n}(1-\xi_T) \prod_{j=1}^{n-1}(1-\xi_Tq^j),\qquad 1-\xi_T=\frac{\varepsilon_T^N} {1+\xi_T+\cdots+\xi_T^{N-1}}. \] Both functions at \(n=0\) are exactly one. Thus both \(W_T\) and \(\overline W_T^{-1}\) converge to the zero-index delta, and no summand in (16) diverges. At the data (24), only \(u=v=t=r=s=z=0\) survives in the finite six-variable sum. Its three denominator arguments are zero and its phase (17) is \(q\). Consequently \[ \mathcal B/\mathfrak n\longrightarrow q. \tag{27} \] This step includes all finite endpoint residues. We also compute the full normalization, rather than discarding it. Put \(\Lambda_i=z_i^{1/N}\). For \(T=abcd\) with \(a<b<c<d\), the six roots in (2) satisfy \[ P\sim B\sim H\sim\Lambda_a,\qquad Q\sim C\sim\Lambda_b,\qquad R\sim\Lambda_c. \] The exact scalar formula in [B] therefore gives \[ \kappa_*^2= \frac{B^NQ^N(H-C)} {N^2(B-Q)(H-R)(C-R)} \sim\frac{(\Lambda_a\Lambda_b)^{N-1}}{N^2}. \tag{28} \] The two finite sums defining \(\rho_T,\bar\rho_T\) both have arguments tending to \((0,0\mid1)\). Every summand tends to one, so each sum tends to \(N\). With the specified positive square roots, \[ \rho_T\sim\bar\rho_T \sim(\Lambda_a\Lambda_b)^{(N-1)/2}. \tag{29} \] These formulas use the actual three-numerator/one-denominator square-root prefactor, not a norm estimate. In the nine cells the first two vertex labels have total multiplicities \((6,6,4,2)\) at vertices \(0,1,2,3\), respectively. Thus their scalar product contributes \(\Lambda_0^{3d}\Lambda_1^{3d}\Lambda_2^{2d}\Lambda_3^d\), where \(d=N-1\). The four edge weights (7) contribute \(\Lambda_1^{-2d}\Lambda_2^{-d}\Lambda_3^{-d}\). Writing \[ \mathfrak D=(s_{05}s_{15}s_{25}s_{03}s_{04})^d, \] we conclude \[ \mathfrak n\sim\Lambda_0^{3d}\Lambda_1^d\Lambda_2^d \sim\mathfrak D,\qquad \frac{\mathcal B}{\mathfrak D}\longrightarrow q. \tag{30} \] The coefficient of the proposed planar expression can be calculated independently from [K, (2.7),(2.8)]. Let \(\bar p_n=\prod_{j=1}^n(1-q^{-j})\) and define \[ S_n(X)=\sum_{j=0}^n\frac{X^j}{p_j\bar p_{n-j}}\qquad(0\le n<N). \] Direct coefficient comparison, including both endpoints, proves \[ (1-q^n)S_n(X)=(X-q^n)S_{n-1}(X),\qquad S_0=1. \] At coefficient \(X^j\), the two terms in the numerator are \((1-q^j)-q^n(1-q^{-(n-j)})=1-q^n\). Induction gives the exact finite formula \[ S_n(X)=\frac{\prod_{j=1}^n(X-q^j)}{p_n}. \tag{31} \] No binomial summation theorem is assumed. Consider the Fourier coefficient \[ \Phi_N=\sum_{i,j,k,l} R(i,j,k,l\mid1,0,0,0)\,q^{i+j}. \tag{32} \] For every supported term of the specified planar weight set \[ u=[j-i-1],\quad v=[i-l],\quad t=[l-k],\quad h=[k-j]. \] The two theta factors say \(u+t<N\) and \(v+h<N\). Their total is congruent to \(N-1\) and at most \(2N-2\); hence \(u+v+t+h=d\) as an ordinary integer. Conversely every such composition and one free \(j\) give one term, with \[ i=j-1-u,\qquad k=j+h,\qquad l=j+h+t \pmod N. \] Substitution in the literal weight, including its prefactor \(N\), gives after multiplication by \(q^{i+j}\) the phase \[ q^{-(t+h)-(t+h+1)(u+h)} \] and denominator \(p_u\bar p_v p_t\bar p_h\). The free \(j\)-sum therefore supplies a second factor \(N\). Set \(m=t+h\) and \(X=q^{-m-1}\). Equation (32) becomes exactly \[ \Phi_N=N^2\sum_{m=0}^{d} q^{-m}X^m S_{d-m}(X)S_m(X^{-1}). \tag{33} \] For \(m<d\), \(X=q^{d-m}\) is a root of the first polynomial in (31). For \(m=d\), \(X=1\), \(S_d(1)=1\), and \(q^{-d}=q\). Thus \[ \Phi_N=N^2q. \tag{34} \] At the boundary data (24), the four functions in [A] are \[ f_1(1)=s_{15}^d,\quad f_2(1)=s_{25}^d,\quad f_3(0)=s_{03}^d,\quad f_4(0)=s_{04}^d. \] Hence the right-hand crossing expression in [K, (4.25)], with unit coefficient and the specified planar \(R\), is exactly \(\mathfrak D\,N^2q\). Combining (30),(34) proves \[ \frac{\text{nine-cell tensor from (2),(3),(7)}} {\text{unit-coefficient planar crossing expression}} \longrightarrow \frac1{N^2}. \tag{35} \] There is no charged-convention phase in this test: \(h_1=1\) also makes (23) equal to one. Therefore the specified 1995 kernels together with the explicit 1994 scalar normalizations (2) cannot give the unit-coefficient crossing expression on the whole regular decoration domain. This is a normalization obstruction for that precise combination of definitions. The 1995 reference to earlier scalar functions does not itself specify every possible conversion; an unstated conversion must be made explicit and verified. No global theorem of either paper is refuted here. Equation (35) does not prove \(\mathcal R^\chi=N^{-2}R(\,\cdot\mid\chi)\) globally. It fixes a necessary scalar in the phase-free canonical test if an independently proved, decoration-independent scalar comparison exists. It also proves that the calculated tensor is not identically zero: for each fixed allowed \(N\) this boundary entry is nonzero for sufficiently large \(L\). No all-decoration nonvanishing, triangular support, or selected geometric coefficient follows. The size \(N^{-2}\) is subexponential in \(N\), but that observation does not supply the missing array or global source comparison. ## Complete direct sources - [K] R. M. Kashaev, *A Link Invariant from Quantum Dilogarithm*, [q-alg/9504020v1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/q-alg/9504020). Complete primary text read; only its finite definitions and specified incidence/charge/weight data are used. Local PDF: research_archive/finite-source-identification-2026-11-01/md-kashaev-normalization-critical-audit/kashaev1995.pdf, SHA256 0baef40fa9934c9119af2c67252f8032e288c884da72eeaecf405bf91569cda9. - [B] [Literal charged tetrahedron bubble](research_literal_charged_tetrahedron_bubble.md), SHA256 1dfe35f26137572235b1c3af66dcf410e0af758836baddaa8dd6d958c0f61d9b. - [A] [Paired-face boundary adapter](research_kashaev_paired_face_boundary_adapter.md), SHA256 c430fd2714acdc7588003e1c18c60453e1ebe123bd7c0155d20a0eef639ec8ed. The three complete direct texts were read and their used implications checked. No mathematical program, numerical experiment, published nine-tet contraction, or published global state-invariance theorem was used.

title: A convergent Fourier expansion on the translated state domains
text: # A convergent Fourier expansion on the translated state domains Private written proof, 18 November 2026. The exact oblique contour decomposition can be written as a sum over the integer Fourier charges, each occurring once with coefficient one, together with its retained relative boundary currents. On each translated top domain the factorial amplitude is uniformly nonzero on the entire domain. Charges sufficiently far out in their respective orthants have an arbitrarily small absolute exponential bound. The Fourier integrals are complex and can cancel. The result supplies neither a nonzero geometric integral nor cancellation bounds for the relative boundary currents. The complete proof sources are R, the exact oblique decomposition, and A, the literal factorial amplitude. Their pins appear below. ## 1. Keep the exact domains and boundary terms Use R's primitive cut-and-transfer coordinates in dimension \(m=c+1\), original literal interpolant \(I_N(z)\), and bulk real chain \(\Omega_N\). Let \(x^*\) be its geometric point, \(x^0\) its strict real interior point, and \(\epsilon_j=\operatorname{sgn}\operatorname{Im}x^*_j\). The positive vector \(a\) is R's generic height vector. For \(\sigma\in\{\pm1\}^m\), denote the translated top by \[ T_{\sigma,N}= \begin{cases} \Omega_N+N(x^*-x^0),&\sigma=\epsilon,\\ \Omega_N+iN\sigma a,&\sigma\ne\epsilon . \end{cases} \tag{1} \] Every top has the coordinate orientation inherited from \(\Omega_N\), before multiplication by \(c_\sigma=\prod_j(-\sigma_j)\). Fix the geometric correcting charge \(q\in\mathbb Z^m\), and put \[ J_N(z)=e^{-2\pi i q\cdot z}I_N(z),\qquad K_{\epsilon_j}(z_j)=\pi\cot(\pi z_j)-i\pi\epsilon_j . \] Write \(\mathcal B_N\) for the sum of the three retained boundary contributions in R's equation (24): the original boundary-band tori, the initial mixed rectangle current, and the signed translated side currents. This is their actual sum of integrals, not an estimated error. The exact identity is \[ K_N=\sum_\sigma\int_{T_{\sigma,N}} c_\sigma(2\pi i)^{-m}J_N(z) \prod_jK_{\epsilon_j}(z_j)\,dz+\mathcal B_N . \tag{2} \] All fixed framing, pivotal and external normalization lines in R remain unchanged. ## 2. Exact Fourier charges of the polarized kernels Set \[ d_\sigma=\frac{\epsilon-\sigma}{2}\in\mathbb Z^m, \qquad q_\sigma=q+d_\sigma . \tag{3} \] The elementary formula for cotangent proves the meromorphic identity \[ c_\sigma(2\pi i)^{-m}\prod_jK_{\epsilon_j}(z_j) =\frac{\exp(-2\pi i d_\sigma\cdot z)} {\prod_j(1-\exp(2\pi i\sigma_jz_j))}. \tag{4} \] For one coordinate, when \(\sigma=\epsilon\) its normalized factor is \(1/(1-e^{2\pi i\epsilon z})\). When \(\sigma=-\epsilon\), it is \(e^{-2\pi i\epsilon z}/(1-e^{-2\pi i\epsilon z})\). These are the four possible sign cases and prove (4), including the rectangle orientations. On each top, \(\sigma_j\operatorname{Im}z_j>0\) with a fixed lower bound proportional to \(N\). The denominator of (4) therefore has its absolutely and uniformly convergent geometric expansion. Consequently (2) becomes \[ K_N= \sum_{\sigma\in\{\pm1\}^m}\ \sum_{r\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^m} \int_{T_{\sigma,N}} I_N(z)\exp\{-2\pi i(q_\sigma-\sigma r)\cdot z\}\,dz +\mathcal B_N . \tag{5} \] Products such as \(\sigma r\) are coordinatewise. Uniform absolute convergence on the compact chain at each fixed \(N\) justifies termwise integration. The charges in (5) form a disjoint partition of \(\mathbb Z^m\). In one coordinate, the two sets are \[ \{q_j-\epsilon_jr:r\ge0\}, \qquad \{q_j+\epsilon_j(1+r):r\ge0\}. \tag{6} \] They partition the integers. Taking products proves the claim. Thus (5) is a genuine complete integer Fourier expansion, with a specified translated integration domain for each charge. It is not a collection of independent unknown lattice-period coefficients. The geometric charge \(q\) occurs at \(\sigma=\epsilon,\ r=0\), with coefficient exactly one. This statement concerns its explicit Fourier integral. It does not say that a local geometric steepest-descent cycle occurs in that integral with coefficient one. ## 3. Uniform amplitudes on the whole translated tops All normalized real domains \(\Omega_N/N\) lie in one fixed bounded set. On any chosen top, every normalized factorial length has a fixed nonzero imaginary part, independent of the real point of that domain. The same holds for the cut coordinate. Hence the union, over all sufficiently large \(N\), of the normalized tops has a compact neighborhood on which every such length lies in \[ \mathcal D=\mathbb C\setminus((-\infty,0]\cup[1,\infty)). \tag{7} \] There are only finitely many tops and factor forms. This gives simultaneous compact sets, with a separate neighborhood component when necessary. A supplies its uniform shifted factorial expansion on these compact sets. Its chosen branches are fixed on \(\mathcal D\). The cut binomial has the same global compact-domain expansion \[ \frac{\Gamma(N)\theta^{Ny}(1-\theta)^{N-1-Ny}} {\Gamma(Ny+1)\Gamma(N-Ny)} = N^{-1/2} \frac{1-y}{(1-\theta)\sqrt{2\pi y(1-y)}} e^{N b_\theta(y)}(1+O(N^{-1})). \tag{8} \] Here logarithms and square roots are continued from \(0<y<1\) on (7), and \[ b_\theta(y)=-y\log y-(1-y)\log(1-y) +y\log\theta+(1-y)\log(1-\theta). \] To prove (8) beyond the small midpoint neighborhood, apply ordinary Gamma Stirling to \(Ny\) and \(N(1-y)\). On every compact subset of (7), both arguments remain in fixed closed sectors away from the negative real axis. The remainder is uniform. The identity \(\binom{N-1}{Ny}=(1-y)\binom N{Ny}\) gives the displayed finite correction. None of its amplitude factors vanish on the compact sets under consideration. Multiplying (8), the \(c\) actual crossing expansions, and their retained monomial and pivotal factors proves \[ I_N(Nx)=N^{-(c+1)/2}A_0(x)e^{N\phi(x)} (1+O(N^{-1})), \qquad A_0(x)\ne0 . \tag{9} \] It holds uniformly on the entire normalized top domains and on fixed neighborhoods of them, with every fixed holomorphic derivative on smaller neighborhoods. The phase and units use the original marked factorial sections. As in R, any explicitly supplied alternative whole external normalization keeps its prescribed phase and polynomial power. In particular each signed top in (2) has uniform density \[ N^{m-(c+1)/2}A_0(x) e^{N(\phi(x)-2\pi i q_\sigma\cdot x)} (1+O(N^{-1}))\,dx . \tag{10} \] The remaining denominator in (4) is exponentially close to one there. Every signed top has leading normalized kernel coefficient \(+1\); its differing exponential penalty is part of the explicit integer-alias phase. ## 4. A uniform tail bound for the Fourier charges Choose \(v_*>0\) such that \(\sigma_j\operatorname{Im}z_j\ge Nv_*\) on every top and every coordinate. Put \[ C_{\sigma,N}= \int_{T_{\sigma,N}} |I_N(z)e^{-2\pi iq_\sigma\cdot z}|\,|dz|. \] Compactness and (9) give constants \(C,p,C_*>0\), depending on the fixed braid and selected frame, with \[ C_{\sigma,N}\le C N^p e^{C_*N}. \tag{11} \] All domains have only polynomial geometric volume. For \(\gamma=2\pi v_*\), a term of index \(r\) in (5) has absolute integral at most \(C_{\sigma,N}e^{-\gamma N|r|_1}\). Therefore \[ \sum_{|r|_1\ge R} \left|\int_{T_{\sigma,N}} I_N(z)e^{-2\pi i(q_\sigma-\sigma r)\cdot z}\,dz\right| \le C_{\sigma,N} \frac{e^{-\gamma NR/2}}{(1-e^{-\gamma N/2})^m}. \tag{12} \] For any fixed \(\Lambda>0\), choose a fixed integer \(R\) with \(\gamma R/2>C_*+\Lambda\). Summing (12) over the finitely many tops then gives \(O(e^{-\Lambda N})\), after absorbing the polynomial factor using the strict inequality. Thus only finitely many Fourier integrals are needed at any prescribed exponential accuracy. This is a finite-charge reduction, not a theorem of finitely many exceptional Dehn fillings. The finitely many remaining integrals still require their genuine contour analysis. Their coefficients being one does not make the integrals nonnegative. The geometric charge retains its centralizer direction. Nor has (12) estimated any term in \(\mathcal B_N\). Those distinctions are essential to the outstanding volume-conjecture lower bound. ## Complete proof-source pins * R: notes/research_actual_oblique_geometric_contour_decomposition.md, SHA256 9180de472bafb38c479d3e1aafac6c75c388d668371892f54219de658728034c. * A: notes/research_literal_crossing_slit_chart_amplitude.md, SHA256 c3682b0f84000aad4c2f53235b9c93bbd86283905a75d6f07ac03b1a3c00bc4a. The entire matching R was freshly read; the complete unchanged A read was explicitly retained from the active author sequence. Every used implication was checked and both matching hashes renewed. The Fourier partition, global binomial extension and tail bound are proved here by written calculations. No mathematical program, numerical test, build, or edit to frozen or public files was used.

title: The odd-level half-charge observation and its normal defect

# The odd-level half-charge observation and its normal defect Research proof, 4 November 2026. Frozen manuscripts are unchanged. The ordinary value interpolation at odd levels has a simple physical endpoint in addition to its double roots. Its angular Cauchy kernel is a sine kernel. The ramified angular pole at zero supplies exactly the original simple-node contribution. With this term retained, the same half-charge saddle as at even levels gives a nonzero observation and a locally dominant normal defect at every positive internal pair. This note uses the full distinct-node interpolation, not the different weighted odd space on which a positive crossing form was proved. The original trace's top-degree correction is retained in Section 3. ## 1. The full-node polynomial and exact angular contour Let \(N=2m+1\ge3\). The distinct physical roots are \[ c_a=2\cos((2a+1)\pi/N),\qquad 0\le a\le m, \qquad c_m=-2. 	ag{1} \] Write \[  egin{split} Q_{\mathrm d}(w)&=U_m(w/2)-U_{m-1}(w/2),\ Q_{\mathrm o}(w)&=(w+2)Q_{\mathrm d}(w),\qquad P_N(w)=(w+2)Q_{\mathrm d}(w)^2,\ Q_{\mathrm o}(-2\cos z)&=4(-1)^m\sin(z/2)\sin(Nz/2). \end{split} 	ag{2} \] Here \(U_{-1}=0\). These are monic polynomials in \(w\). The last identity follows from the elementary sine formula for \(U_j\) and holds as an entire identity in \(z\). Let \[  egin{split} \mathcal L_N(w)&=\sum_{j=0}^{m}e_j(w)e_j(-2)=K_N(w,-2),\ 	au_a&=\arccos(-c_a/2)=2\pi(m-a)/N,\qquad T_a=N	au_a^2/(4\pi),\qquad F_a=\mathcal L_N(c_a),\ \sigma_a^{\mathrm o}&= rac{N}{Q_{\mathrm o}'(c_a)},\qquad \mathcal O^{\mathrm o}_nF(w) =\sum_{a=0}^{m}  rac{\sigma_a^{\mathrm o}e^{inT_a}F_a}{w-c_a}. \end{split} 	ag{3} \] The equality of the low and full complete-end kernels at odd levels is the [exact simple-endpoint identity](research_last_physical_row_riccati.md). For \(a<m\) the Chebyshev differential equation gives \[ (4-c_a^2)Q_{\mathrm o}'(c_a)^2=N^2(c_a+2),\qquad |\sigma_a^{\mathrm o}|=\sqrt{2-c_a}\le2. 	ag{4} \] At the simple endpoint, \[ Q_{\mathrm o}'(-2)=Q_{\mathrm d}(-2)=(-1)^mN,\qquad \sigma_m^{\mathrm o}=(-1)^m . 	ag{5} \] For a real crossing time \(n\), set \[ h_{n,N}(w)= e^{inN\arccos(-w/2)^2/(4\pi)}\mathcal L_N(w). 	ag{6} \] The squared inverse cosine is continued on \(\mathbb C\setminus[2,\infty)\), holomorphically through \(w=-2\). Let \(\mathcal I^{\mathrm o}_{n,N}\) be its ordinary value interpolant of degree at most \(m\) at the nodes (1). Then \[ \mathcal O^{\mathrm o}_nF(w) =N rac{\mathcal I^{\mathrm o}_{n,N}(w)}{Q_{\mathrm o}(w)}, \qquad \mathscr D^{\mathrm o}_{n,N}(w) = rac{h_{n,N}(w)-\mathcal I^{\mathrm o}_{n,N}(w)} {Q_{\mathrm o}(w)} 	ag{7} \] are exact identities. The normal defect is holomorphic through every physical node. Choose midpoint cuts \(T_N=(2k_N+1)\pi/N\) tending to \(\pi/2\). Let \(\mathcal R_N\) be the positively oriented angular rectangle with real ends \(\pm T_N\) and imaginary heights \(\pm H_0\). For real \(w>2\), the retained physical observation is exactly \[  rac{N}{4\pi i}\oint_{\partial\mathcal R_N}  rac{(-1)^m\cos(z/2)\, e^{inNz^2/(4\pi)}\mathcal L_N(-2\cos z)} {(w+2\cos z)\sin(Nz/2)}\,dz . 	ag{8} \] It includes all nodes with \(	au_a<T_N\), including \(	au_m=0\). Indeed (8) is the change of variables \(v=-2\cos z\) in the Cauchy expression with denominator \(Q_{\mathrm o}(v)\). Every nonzero positive angle has two preimages. At zero the map is ramified, and \[ Q_{\mathrm o}(-2\cos z)=(-1)^mNz^2+O(z^4),\qquad dv=(2z+O(z^3))\,dz . \] The integrand before multiplication by \(N/(4\pi i)\) therefore has residue \(2(-1)^m h_{n,N}(-2)/(N(w+2))\). The resulting term is exactly \((-1)^m h_{n,N}(-2)/(w+2)\), as required by (5). Thus neither an endpoint factor of two nor a physical source term has been omitted. ## 2. The half-charge packet and the exterior residue Use the notation of the [even-level observation theorem](research_complete_source_pick_observation.md#5-a-nonzero-half-charge-observation): \[  egin{split} nt_0+2i\operatorname{asinh}	an(t_0/2)&=\pi,\qquad t_0=a_0-iH_0,\quad 0<a_0<\pi/3,\quad 0<H_0<2/5,\ S_n(z)&=\Psi(z)+inz^2/(4\pi)-iz/2,\qquad \mathcal S_n=S_n(t_0),\quad M_n=\Re\mathcal S_n,\ A_n&=\{\sec(t_0/2)-in\}/(2\pi). \end{split} 	ag{9} \] Here \(n\ge3\) is fixed and real, and the square root of \(A_n\) has positive real part. Define \[ b_n^{\mathrm o}(w) = rac{\sqrt{2\pi}}{\pi}  rac{\cos(t_0/2)a_e(t_0,0)} {(w+2\cos t_0)\sqrt{A_n}} . 	ag{10} \] **Theorem 1.** Uniformly for real \(w>2\), through odd levels, \[ \mathcal O^{\mathrm o}_nF(w) =(-1)^mN^{-1}b_n^{\mathrm o}(w)e^{N\mathcal S_n} (1+O(N^{-1})). 	ag{11} \] The coefficient is nonzero and comparable in modulus to \(1/(w+1)\). The same expansion holds locally in the crossing time and with fixed holomorphic parameter derivatives, on smaller neighborhoods. *Proof.* The angular integrand in (8) is odd, so its two horizontal sides add after reflection. On the lower side, \[  rac1{\sin(Nz/2)} = rac{2i\,e^{-iNz/2}}{1-e^{-iNz}} . \] Thus its exact principal integral is \[  rac{(-1)^mN}{\pi} \int_{-T_N-iH_0}^{T_N-iH_0}  rac{\cos(z/2)\mathcal L_N(-2\cos z) e^{inNz^2/(4\pi)-iNz/2}} {(w+2\cos z)(1-e^{-iNz})}\,dz . 	ag{12} \] The denominator differs from one exponentially on this segment. At a midpoint vertical side the sine denominator has modulus \(\cosh(Nh/2)\); its reciprocal is at most \(2e^{-N|h|/2}\). Consequently the horizontal and vertical upper exponents are exactly the ones already proved in the even-level theorem. For precision, \(\Re S_n(a-iH_0)\) is strictly concave for \(|a|\le\pi/2\), with unique maximum at \(a_0\). The lower right connector increases in height and is bounded by its smaller horizontal endpoint value. The lower left connector decreases in height and is bounded by \(\Psi(T_N)\). The upper sides are their reflected copies. All physical omitted values are at most the first omitted complete-kernel value by the actual positive row recurrence. Their rate is \(\Psi(\pi/2)\), and \[ \Psi(\pi/2)<M_n-7/80. 	ag{13} \] Their weights are bounded by (4), and \((w-c_a)^{-1}\le N^2/(w+1)\). Thus every omitted part has a fixed gap with a majorant integrable after squaring. No off-grid estimate near the physical color \(2\) is substituted. At \(t_0\), the original complete-edge packet is \(\mathcal L_N(-2\cos z)=N^{-3/2}a_e(z,0)e^{N\Psi(z)} (1+O(N^{-1}))\). The Gaussian integral in (12) contributes \(\sqrt{2\pi/N}/\sqrt{A_n}\), proving (10)–(11). The new factor \(\cos(t_0/2)\) is nonzero. All rational amplitudes, after multiplication by \(w+1\), and their derivatives are uniformly bounded with nonzero leading value for \(w>2\). Strict gaps persist in a small complex time neighborhood; Cauchy's formula proves the normalized derivative statements. \(\square\) Let \(\mathcal J^{\mathrm o}_{n,N}(w)\) denote (8), and \(\mathcal T^{\mathrm o}_{n,N}(w)\) the omitted physical sum. For a complex color \(w=-2\cos(a-iH)\), \(0<a<\pi/2\), the exact continuation, away from the rectangle boundary, is \[  egin{split} \mathcal J^{\mathrm o}_{n,N}(w) &=\mathcal O^{\mathrm o}_nF(w)-\mathcal T^{\mathrm o}_{n,N}(w) -N
u_N(w) rac{h_{n,N}(w)}{Q_{\mathrm o}(w)},\ \mathscr D^{\mathrm o}_{n,N}(w) &=(1-
u_N(w)) rac{h_{n,N}(w)}{Q_{\mathrm o}(w)} - rac{\mathcal J^{\mathrm o}_{n,N}(w) +\mathcal T^{\mathrm o}_{n,N}(w)}{N}. \end{split} 	ag{14} \] Here \(
u_N=1\) if both angular evaluation poles are enclosed, and zero otherwise. Each of the two additional angular poles has residue \(-h_{n,N}(w)/Q_{\mathrm o}(w)\) before the prefactor in the unsimplified Cauchy integrand, giving the displayed factor \(-N\). Thus the interior case cannot be obtained by ignoring this residue. **Corollary 2.** At an actual unit-charge positive internal pair of integer powers \(n,p\ge3\), on a fixed neighborhood of the angle \(t\) at its power-\(n\) vertex, one has \[  egin{split} \mathscr D^{\mathrm o}_{n,N}(-2\cos z) &= rac{h_{n,N}(-2\cos z)}{Q_{\mathrm o}(-2\cos z)} (1+O(N^{-1/2}e^{-\delta N}))\ &=i(-1)^mN^{-3/2}  rac{a_e(z,0)}{2\sin(z/2)}e^{NS_n(z)} (1+O(N^{-1}))
e0 \end{split} 	ag{15} \] for some \(\delta>0\), at all large odd levels. Every fixed ordinary spectral derivative has the corresponding differentiated holomorphic expansion on smaller neighborhoods. *Proof.* The [pair comparison theorem](research_pair_half_charge_action_gap.md) gives \(H(t)>H_0\) and \(\Re S_n(t)>M_n\). The color is therefore exterior to the rectangle. The contour proof of (11) applies uniformly on a fixed neighborhood of this color, because its Cauchy denominators stay away from zero on the contour and at the physical nodes. It gives \(\mathcal I^{\mathrm o}_{n,N}/Q_{\mathrm o} =O(N^{-2}e^{NM_n})\). Meanwhile (2) gives exactly, in the lower half-plane, \[  rac1{Q_{\mathrm o}(-2\cos z)} = rac{i(-1)^m e^{-iNz/2}} {2\sin(z/2)(1-e^{-iNz})}. 	ag{16} \] The direct complete-edge packet and the strict action gap prove (15). Cauchy's formula treats normalized remainders and ordinary color derivatives; \(\sin t
e0\) on the neighborhood. The original crossing carrier is restored by multiplying by \(C_{N,n}=\exp(\pi i n(N-1)^2/(4N))\). No carrier has been included twice. \(\square\) ## 3. The original odd trace still has its top-degree term The odd full-node normal defect must not be substituted for a weighted positive trace. Let \[ Q_{j,N}(w)=\prod_{a=j}^{m}(w-c_a),\qquad S_{j,N}=\prod_{r=1}^{j}2\sin(r\pi/N),\qquad \ell_{n,N}=[w^m]\mathcal I^{\mathrm o}_{n,N}(w). \] For any contour in the slit plane enclosing the remaining nodes, the exact original trace is \[  egin{split} \phi_N[R^n\mathcal L_Ne_j] ={}& rac{C_{N,n}N^2(-1)^j}{2\pi i S_{j,N}^2} \oint rac{(w+2)\mathscr D^{\mathrm o}_{n,N}(w)} {Q_{j,N}(w)}\,dw\ &\quad+ oldsymbol 1_{\{j=m\}}\, C_{N,n}N^2\ell_{n,N} rac{(-1)^m}{S_{m,N}^2}, \qquad 0\le j\le m . \end{split} 	ag{17} \] Indeed the original normal-defect formula gives \(\sum_{a<m}(4-c_a^2)Q_{\mathrm o}'(c_a) \mathscr D^{\mathrm o}_{n,N}(c_a)e_j(c_a)\), plus the product of the two leading coefficients times \(N^2\). Use (4) and \(e_j/Q_{\mathrm o}=(-1)^j/(S_{j,N}^2Q_{j,N})\) to obtain the contour term in (17). The factor \(w+2\) cancels the simple endpoint pole, exactly as the first-normal trace requires. The remaining rank-one term includes that original endpoint and the top-degree polynomial coefficient. For \(j=m\) the contour integrand is holomorphic, so this entire term is zero, not an approximation. Since \(S_{m,N}^2=N\), \[ \phi_N[R^n\mathcal L_Ne_m] =C_{N,n}(-1)^mN\,\ell_{n,N},\qquad N\ell_{n,N}=\lim_{w	o+\infty}w\mathcal O^{\mathrm o}_nF(w). 	ag{18} \] The uniform observation theorem gives its explicit nonzero half-charge asymptotic \[ \phi_N[R^n\mathcal L_Ne_m] =C_{N,n}N^{-1}b^{\mathrm o}_{n,\infty} e^{N\mathcal S_n}(1+O(N^{-1})), \quad b^{\mathrm o}_{n,\infty} = rac{\sqrt{2\pi}}{\pi}  rac{\cos(t_0/2)a_e(t_0,0)}{\sqrt{A_n}}
e0 . 	ag{19} \] The limit in (18) can be taken directly in the bounded rational amplitudes and finite sums of the contour proof. In particular a two-vertex product of these top-index terms has rate \(M_n+M_p<2M_\infty\). The strict inequality follows by integrating the positive height along each half-charge leaf from charge zero. This does not estimate the other shared indices. The identities and local packets above retain the actual odd simple node, all first normals, and the full top-degree correction. They do not establish a global signed internal-pair asymptotic or a positive energy identity for this unweighted odd observation. ## 4. Independent finite normalization checks The [focused checker](../experiments/check_odd_half_charge_observation.py) constructs the crossing and its signed powers by multiplication and division in the original Newton quotient. It compares those traces with (17), including the simple endpoint and the top coefficient. Separately, it integrates the sine contour and checks both exterior and interior evaluation colors with their exact residue correction. ~~~sh .venv/bin/python experiments/check_odd_half_charge_observation.py --precision 100 ~~~ The [saved record](../repro/results/research-odd-half-charge-observation.json) contains the script, direct dependency, and proof hashes. These finite checks test normalizations; no finite sample is used to prove the asymptotic or its nonzero coefficient.

title: A quantitative Schur lemma for the original head and its marked cut
text: # A quantitative Schur lemma for the original head and its marked cut 23 November 2026. Research note. The manuscripts and earlier final notes remain unchanged. The original complete head admits a polynomial quantitative Schur lemma. Two of its actual generators control the distance of an arbitrary matrix from a scalar matrix. Including the adjoint lowering generator gives a completely positive averaging flow with an explicit spectral gap. Applied to the original highest cut, this flow produces a positive, uniformly conditioned probe in time \(O(N^2\log N)\). This is a one-head theorem in the uniform physical metric. It does not identify a geometric packet or evaluate a knot invariant. In particular, it supplies no spectral estimate for a many-head coproduct system. ## 1. The actual generators and metric Fix \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), and \[ q=e^{\pi i/N},\qquad Q=q^2,\qquad x=-q^{-1}. \] Declare the physical head basis \(w_0,\ldots,w_d\) orthonormal. Use exactly the balanced complete-root matrices \[ \mathcal E w_a=(Q^{-a}-1)w_{a-1},\qquad Fw_a=(1-Q^{a+1})w_{a+1},\qquad Kw_a=xQ^{-a}w_a. \tag{1} \] The missing bottom and top arrows are zero. Here \(\mathcal E\) is the physical lowering operator called \(E\) in the uniform-physical source and \(\mathcal E\) in the Azumaya-head calculation. It is not the latter's rescaled unrestricted generator \(\mathcal E/(q-q^{-1})^2\). Directly, \[ K^*K=I,\qquad K\mathcal EK^{-1}=Q\mathcal E,\qquad F=-\mathcal E^*,\qquad \|\mathcal E\|_{\rm op},\|F\|_{\rm op}\le2. \tag{2} \] All matrix norms below are the unnormalized Hilbert--Schmidt norm \(\|A\|_2^2=\operatorname{Tr}(A^*A)\), unless marked as operator norms. Put \[ c(A)=\frac{\operatorname{Tr}A}{N},\qquad D(A)=\frac1N\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}K^jAK^{-j}. \tag{3} \] The trace in (3) is the ordinary matrix trace. The matrix \(D(A)\) is precisely the diagonal part of \(A\), and is its Hilbert--Schmidt orthogonal projection onto diagonal matrices. ## 2. Coercivity of the actual commutators **Theorem 1.** For every \(A\in\operatorname{End}(V_N)\), \[ \boxed{\quad \|A-c(A)I\|_2^2 \le\frac{3N^2}{8}\|[\mathcal E,A]\|_2^2 +\frac{N^2}{16}\|[K,A]\|_2^2. \quad} \tag{4} \] There is also the symmetric bound \[ \boxed{\quad \|A-c(A)I\|_2^2 \le\frac{N^2}{16} \left(3\|[\mathcal E,A]\|_2^2+ 3\|[F,A]\|_2^2+\|[K,A]\|_2^2\right). \quad} \tag{5} \] Both bounds hold at every level, with the original zero arrows. **Proof.** The eigenspaces of the unitary map \(A\mapsto KAK^{-1}\) are mutually orthogonal in Hilbert--Schmidt norm. They have eigenvalues \(Q^m\), \(m\in\mathbb Z/N\); its eigenvalue-one space consists exactly of diagonal matrices. Every other eigenvalue is at distance at least \(2\sin(\pi/N)\) from one. Multiplication by \(K^{-1}\) does not change the norm, so \[ \|A-D(A)\|_2^2 \le\frac{\|[K,A]\|_2^2}{4\sin^2(\pi/N)} \le\frac{N^2}{16}\|[K,A]\|_2^2. \tag{6} \] The final inequality uses \(\sin(\pi/N)\ge2/N\). Write \(D=D(A)=\operatorname{diag}(d_0,\ldots,d_d)\). The actual lowering arrows give \[ \|[\mathcal E,D]\|_2^2 =\sum_{j=1}^{d}4\sin^2(\pi j/N)|d_j-d_{j-1}|^2. \tag{7} \] This is the weighted path energy of the elementary-cap Laplacian. Its written Hardy estimate, Section 5 of [L], gives \[ \sum_{j=0}^d|d_j-c(A)|^2 \le\frac{3N^2}{8} \sum_{j=1}^{d}4\sin^2(\pi j/N)|d_j-d_{j-1}|^2. \tag{8} \] That estimate is for this actual path, including both endpoints, and holds also at \(N=2\). By (2), commutation with \(\mathcal E\) raises the \(K\)-conjugation grade by one. Consequently \[ [\mathcal E,D(A)] \quad\hbox{is an orthogonal grade projection of } [\mathcal E,A]. \tag{9} \] Thus its norm is at most the full defect norm. The corresponding statement holds for \(F\), with grade lowered by one. On a diagonal matrix, the two commutator norms are equal by (2), or directly by (7). Finally \(A-D(A)\) and \(D(A)-c(A)I\) are orthogonal. Adding (6) and (8), and using (9), proves (4). Alternatively average the equal diagonal estimates obtained from \(\mathcal E\) and \(F\) before adding (6). This proves (5). No nonunitary matrix-unit or fusion-frame change occurs. ## 3. A positive averaging flow For a matrix \(X\), let \(\operatorname{ad}_X(A)=[X,A]\). Its Hilbert--Schmidt adjoint is \(\operatorname{ad}_X^*=\operatorname{ad}_{X^*}\). Define \[ \mathscr L= \operatorname{ad}_{\mathcal E}^* \operatorname{ad}_{\mathcal E} +\operatorname{ad}_{F}^*\operatorname{ad}_{F} +\operatorname{ad}_{K}^*\operatorname{ad}_{K}. \tag{10} \] This is a self-adjoint nonnegative operator on the matrix space. Its energy is exactly the sum of the three squared Ward defects. Equation (5) implies \[ \ker\mathscr L=\mathbb CI,\qquad \mathscr L|_{(\mathbb CI)^\perp} \succeq\frac{16}{3N^2}I. \tag{11} \] Also \(\|\mathscr L\|_{\rm op}\le36\), since a commutator with \(X\) has Hilbert--Schmidt operator norm at most \(2\|X\|_{\rm op}\). The order of the lower gap cannot be improved to a larger order: for \(A=\operatorname{diag}(j-d/2)_{j=0}^d\), \[ \|A\|_2^2=\frac{N(N^2-1)}{12},\quad \|[\mathcal E,A]\|_2^2=\|[F,A]\|_2^2=2N,\quad [K,A]=0. \tag{12} \] Its Rayleigh quotient is \(48/(N^2-1)\). **Theorem 2.** For \(t\ge0\), the map \[ T_t=e^{-t\mathscr L} \tag{13} \] is completely positive, unital, trace preserving, and Hilbert--Schmidt self-adjoint. It satisfies \[ \boxed{\quad \|T_t(A)-c(A)I\|_2 \le e^{-16t/(3N^2)}\|A-c(A)I\|_2. \quad} \tag{14} \] **Proof.** Write \(\mathcal E=H+iJ\) and \(K=U+iV\), with all four displayed parts Hermitian. Since \(K\) is normal, \([U,V]=0\). Equation (2) gives the exact identity \[ \mathscr L =2\operatorname{ad}_H^2+2\operatorname{ad}_J^2 +\operatorname{ad}_U^2+\operatorname{ad}_V^2. \tag{15} \] For any Hermitian matrix \(B\) and \(s>0\), \[ e^{-s\operatorname{ad}_B^2}(A) =\frac1{\sqrt{4\pi s}}\int_{\mathbb R} e^{-u^2/(4s)}e^{iuB}Ae^{-iuB}\,du. \tag{16} \] Diagonalizing \(B\) proves (16) by the one-dimensional Gaussian Fourier integral. Its right side is an average of unitary conjugations, hence is completely positive, unital and trace preserving. Apply (16) separately to the four terms in (15), and take the finite-dimensional Lie product limit. The product limit follows by expanding each factor through first order: one step has error \(O(m^{-2})\), so \(m\) steps converge to the exponential of the sum. Here \(N\) is fixed for this identity; no uniform approximation by a finite number of steps is required. Complete positivity, unitality and trace preservation pass to the limit. Self-adjointness follows directly from (10), not from self-adjointness of a noncommuting finite product. Finally (11) and spectral decomposition prove (14). ## 4. Quantitative observation at the original cut Let \(P\) be any positive trace-one matrix in this same physical metric. Define the computable Ward bound \[ \Delta(A)^2=\frac{N^2}{16} \left(3\|[\mathcal E,A]\|_2^2+ 3\|[F,A]\|_2^2+\|[K,A]\|_2^2\right). \tag{17} \] By Theorem 1, \(\|A-c(A)I\|_2\le\Delta(A)\). Since \(\|P\|_2\le\operatorname{Tr}P=1\), \[ |\operatorname{Tr}(PA)-c(A)|\le\Delta(A),\qquad \|A\|_2^2=N|c(A)|^2+\|A-c(A)I\|_2^2. \tag{18} \] Thus, with \([u]_+=\max(u,0)\), \[ \boxed{\quad \left[\frac{\sqrt{[\|A\|_2^2-\Delta(A)^2]_+}}{\sqrt N} -\Delta(A)\right]_+ \le|\operatorname{Tr}(PA)| \le\frac{\|A\|_2}{\sqrt N}+\Delta(A). \quad} \tag{19} \] This uses no lower bound for an unknown overlap or denominator. For example, put \[ \mathfrak w(A)^2= \|[\mathcal E,A]\|_2^2+\|[F,A]\|_2^2+\|[K,A]\|_2^2. \] If \(A\ne0\), \(0\le\varepsilon\le1/4\), and \(\mathfrak w(A)\le\varepsilon N^{-3/2}\|A\|_2\), then \(\Delta(A)\le\varepsilon\|A\|_2/\sqrt N\), and (19) gives \[ (1-2\varepsilon)\frac{\|A\|_2}{\sqrt N} \le|\operatorname{Tr}(PA)| \le(1+\varepsilon)\frac{\|A\|_2}{\sqrt N}. \tag{20} \] For the lower bound use \(\sqrt{1-\varepsilon^2/N}\ge1-\varepsilon^2/N \ge1-\varepsilon\). In particular a relative Ward defect \(o(N^{-3/2})\) makes the ratio in (20) tend to one. The original highest cut is the rank-one orthogonal projector \(P_0=|w_0\rangle\langle w_0|\), with the actual tail pivots and framing factors kept in its one-cut operator. Consequently (18)--(20) apply to this prescribed observation. ## 5. A canonical softened cut and its source scope Set \[ \rho_t=T_t(P_0),\qquad t_N=\frac{3N^2}{16}\log(2N). \tag{21} \] Theorem 2 gives positivity, trace one, and \[ \|\rho_t-I/N\|_2 \le e^{-16t/(3N^2)}\sqrt{1-1/N}. \tag{22} \] Since operator norm is at most Hilbert--Schmidt norm, for every \(t\ge t_N\), \[ \boxed{\qquad \frac{I}{2N}\preceq\rho_t\preceq\frac{3I}{2N},\qquad \operatorname{cond}_2(\rho_t)\le3. \qquad} \tag{23} \] This is an explicit flow from the actual original probe, constructed from its actual head generators. It is particularly concrete on this probe: diagonal matrices stay diagonal. If \(\Delta_{\mathrm{path},N}\) denotes the weighted path Laplacian with edge weights \(p_j=4\sin^2(\pi(j+1)/N)\), \(0\le j<d\), direct multiplication in (10) gives \[ \mathscr L(\operatorname{diag}a) =2\operatorname{diag}(\Delta_{\mathrm{path},N}a), \qquad \rho_t=\operatorname{diag} (e^{-2t\Delta_{\mathrm{path},N}}\mathbf e_0). \] The matrix \(-2\Delta_{\mathrm{path},N}\) has nonnegative off-diagonal entries and zero row sums. Its exponential therefore preserves nonnegative vectors and their total sum: this follows also by shifting its diagonal to make the entire generator nonnegative and expanding the exponential series. Thus the softened cut is the probability distribution of a specified continuous-time walk on the path, starting at vertex zero. No cyclic endpoint edge has been introduced. For the fully assembled unmarked one-cut knot operator \(A_N=K_N I\), with its recorded external normalization included, \[ \operatorname{Tr}(\rho_t A_N)=K_N \qquad(t\ge0). \tag{24} \] The scalarity used here is the exact original-source scalarity recorded in [A, Section 4]. Its qualitative consequence that any trace-one probe gives the same unmarked knot scalar was already known. The new estimates are the actual-generator coercivity, the positive flow and its polynomial mixing time. For an arbitrary marked matrix, the source is not unchanged. The exact transported identity is instead \[ \operatorname{Tr}(P_0T_t(A))=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_t A). \tag{25} \] To check it, \(T_t\) preserves adjoints and is Hilbert--Schmidt self-adjoint, so it is self-adjoint also for the bilinear trace pairing. Equation (18) bounds the discrepancy from the cyclic mean when the Ward defects are controlled. Replacing the marked source by that mean without this control is not licensed. All averaging in (21)--(25) concerns the complete one-head operator after assembly. It does not replace internal cups, turns or Casimir derivative channels by scalar quotients. There is no assertion that this heat flow intertwines every crossing or that it may be inserted independently on all internal heads. In particular (11) is not a many-head coproduct gap. The full source still needs a geometric norm estimate and source-faithful control of any proposed geometric approximation. No such approximation, nonzero geometric period, or finite-exception volume theorem is supplied here. ## Complete inputs and coverage The three complete proof inputs were read at these versions. Theorem 1 uses the actual weighted path estimate of [L]; all new grading, heat-flow and observation calculations are written above. | Input | SHA-256 | |---|---| | [L: Elementary cap path Laplacian](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_elementary_cap_path_laplacian.md), 355 lines | 0e6ec0f5bfc4fa3e46184c405468144b1c99a41d2dda9fc6a78304e67e679d4f | | [A: Actual head and original cut](research_actual_head_azumaya_and_cut_descent.md), 327 lines | 1771973ccf96f03e90ec757c9988aa27263a3af02f02e5143a9d9e5445162ffa | | [Uniform physical source](research_conway_uniform_physical_quartic.md), 477 lines | 39895b430535f565d30133b46ef57f67589207bc83f40597ffe96e2ce79bbda8 | The complete 494-line original-almost-invariance note was read at 66f4c93efa35425444fbdf90728dcfd254496f3d17f48a7cf6310867fde2cc15, and the complete 216-line simultaneous-Ward diagnostic at b97f3f401a53b8ccef359666932b4616c83ac67b7e5ee980f6f9a2c49332b1ad. They concern different Newton-vector and many-head systems; their unresolved estimates are not inferred from this one-head result. No general novelty is claimed for Schur's lemma, Hilbert--Schmidt orthogonal projection, or completely positive heat semigroups. The quantitative assertions above concern the displayed original root head and its prescribed cut. Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used. No mathematical program, numerical experiment, build, git action, or earlier-final edit was performed.

title: A polynomial reference for one prescribed matrix-product leaf
text:
# A polynomial reference for one prescribed matrix-product leaf 24 November 2026. Research note. Written proof. Earlier finals and public manuscripts remain unchanged. A known leaf of the actual physical matrix-product compiler can be matched to its parent's full input density with an explicit polynomial change of reference. The other input and output have specified row/column-energy densities. These give a full-matrix logarithmic inequality on every finite metric window, without selecting a largest singular mode or using the unknown closed invariant. The construction is one-sided. It does not match the second input to an arbitrary subtree, or prove a geometric lower bound. ## 1. The actual matrix-product compiler Let \[ {\cal A}= igoplus_{
u=1}^{s}\operatorname{Mat}_D(\mathbb C), \qquad \|A\|^2=\sum_
u\operatorname{Tr}(A_
u^*A_
u), \qquad n=\dim{\cal A}=sD^2 . 	ag{1} \] Vector norms on \({\cal A}\) use this unnormalized physical Hilbert--Schmidt structure. Map norms labelled \({m op}\) are induced operator norms; tensor coefficient norms are labelled \({m HS}\). Componentwise multiplication is the linearized tensor \[ \mu:{\cal A}\otimes_2{\cal A}\longrightarrow{\cal A}, \qquad \mu(A\otimes B)_
u=A_
u B_
u . 	ag{2} \] For the actual all-main-color source of [C, Section 5], \(s=N\) and \(D=N^b\), where \(b\) is the fixed braid width. Its leaves are the original signed physical crossings, or specified nonzero blocked words. Its root takes the original partial pivotal trace and marked entry, including framing and external factors. The output and its positive norm remain \[ Y_N=(c_1,\ldots,c_N),\qquad \|Y_N\|^2=|K_N|^2+R_N,\qquad 0\le R_N\le(N-1)(N/2)^{2b-2}. 	ag{3} \] We do not replace this root by an identity trace. The full matrix spaces retain all physical channels and Jordan data. Fix a known nonzero leaf \(A=\alpha a\), where \(\alpha=\|A\|>0\) and \(\|a\|=1\). The number \(\alpha\) is computed from this prescribed leaf; it can be exponentially large. It is not the closed source and will not be discarded. Write \(L_a(B)=aB\). Matrix units in each color block give \[ C:=\mu\mu^*=D I_{\cal A},\qquad \operatorname{Tr}_1(\mu^*\mu) =\operatorname{Tr}_2(\mu^*\mu)=D I_{\cal A},\qquad X:=L_aL_a^*\preceq C,\qquad \operatorname{Tr}C=sD^3,\quad \operatorname{Tr}X=D . 	ag{4} \] For example \(\mu^*E_{ij}= \sum_k E_{ik}\otimes E_{kj}\); different color blocks do not interact. Also \(\|L_a\|_{m op}=\max_
u\|a_
u\|_{m op}\le1\). We first treat a leaf on the first input. For a leaf on the second input, use \(R_a(B)=Ba\) instead of \(L_a\), apply the reference on that second input, and exchange the logical input labels below. The same matrix-unit proof applies. No matrix factors are commuted. ## 2. An input reference which fixes the entire original leaf Put \[ P=|aangle\langle a|,\quad Q=I-P,\quad G_t=P+tQ,\qquad t\ge1,\qquad B_t=\mu(G_t^{-1}\otimes I). 	ag{5} \] Thus \(G_t a=a\), \(G_t A=A\), and \(\|G_t\|_{m op}\le t,\ \|G_t^{-1}\|_{m op}=1\), with equality in the first bound when \(n>1\). Use \(G_t\) on the selected leaf's output and its inverse on the first input of its parent. In coefficient tensor notation the latter is the inverse transpose on the dual leg. The complex bilinear contraction is exactly unchanged. This is a full bundled compiler-edge gauge. In general \(P\) mixes colors and matrix coordinates. It is not a physical-head gauge or an algebra automorphism. No output reference change is needed. Every original source row, phase and incident inverse remains. Since \(\mu(P\otimes I)=L_a(\langle a|\otimes I)\), (4) gives \[ Y_t:=B_tB_t^*=X+t^{-2}(C-X),\qquad Z_t:=\operatorname{Tr}Y_t =D\{1+t^{-2}(sD^2-1)\}. 	ag{6} \] In particular \(Y_t\succ0\); no normal channel is removed. Define densities on the output and on the two logical inputs by \[ ho_t= rac{Y_t}{Z_t},\qquad \omega_t= rac{B_t^*B_t}{Z_t},\qquad \omega_{1,t}=\operatorname{Tr}_2\omega_t,\quad \omega_{2,t}=\operatorname{Tr}_1\omega_t . 	ag{7} \] These are the actual normalized Hilbert--Schmidt marginals of \(B_t\), in the logical-input convention. Their transposes belong on the physical dual input half-edges, as in [O]. No independent ordered-density witness is being identified with an actual tensor marginal. ## 3. Three exact marginal formulas The canonical comparison states are \[ ho_0= rac{X}{D},\qquad \sigma_a= rac{L_a^*L_a}{D},\qquad \eta_t= rac{sD^2-1}{t^2+sD^2-1}. 	ag{8} \] Both comparison states have trace one. Write \(\epsilon=t^{-2}\) and \(Z=Z_t/D=1+(n-1)\epsilon\). All three actual marginals have the same explicit form: \[  oxed{\qquad \omega_{1,t}= rac{P+\epsilon(I-P)}{Z},\quad \omega_{2,t}= rac{\sigma_a+\epsilon(I-\sigma_a)}{Z},\quad ho_t= rac{ho_0+\epsilon(I-ho_0)}{Z}. \qquad} 	ag{9} \] For the first identity, trace \(B_t^*B_t\) over the second input and use (4), obtaining \(DG_t^{-2}\). For the second, cyclicity in the traced first factor moves the two copies of \(G_t^{-1}\) together. The \(P\) term is \(\operatorname{Tr}_1((P\otimes I)\mu^*\mu)=L_a^*L_a\); the identity term is \(DI\). This gives the middle formula. The last formula is (6). These partial-trace identities do not assume that \(G_t\) commutes with \(\mu^*\mu\). For \(n>1\), every density \(	au\) obeys \(0\preceq	au\preceq I\), so the expression in (9) equals \((1-\eta_t)	au+\eta_t(I-	au)/(n-1)\). The two densities in this convex combination are normalized positive states. Therefore, with \(\|T\|_1=\operatorname{Tr}\sqrt{T^*T}\), \[  oxed{\quad \|\omega_{1,t}-P\|_1=2\eta_t,\qquad \|\omega_{2,t}-\sigma_a\|_1\le2\eta_t,\qquad \|ho_t-ho_0\|_1\le2\eta_t . \quad} 	ag{10} \] The first equality uses the orthogonal supports of \(P\) and \(I-P\). For \(n=1\) all three states agree and \(\eta_t=0\). ## 4. A full-matrix logarithmic calibration For arbitrary positive metrics \(H_o,H_1,H_2\) on \({\cal A}\), write \(X_i=\log H_i\). Scalar spectral Jensen on the coefficient tensor of \(B_t\) gives \[  egin{split} \log\|H_o^{1/2}B_t(H_1^{-1/2}\otimes H_2^{-1/2})\|_{m HS} \ \ge\ & rac12\log Z_t+ rac12\operatorname{Tr}(ho_tX_o)\ &- rac12\operatorname{Tr}(\omega_{1,t}X_1) - rac12\operatorname{Tr}(\omega_{2,t}X_2). \end{split} 	ag{11} \] For clarity, after vectorization the three signed logarithms act on distinct tensor legs. Diagonalize them independently. The squared norm divided by \(Z_t\) is a positive average of exponentials of their summed eigenvalues. Jensen gives its mean exponent, which is exactly the marginal expression in (11). This is the identity-reference case of the tensor convexity proof in [C]; it requires no ordering or mutual commutativity of the metrics. Suppose now that \(\|X_o\|_{m op},\|X_1\|_{m op},\|X_2\|_{m op}\le R\).
