Equation (10), applied before bounding any matrix entries, gives \[  oxed{ egin{split} \log\|H_o^{1/2}B_t(H_1^{-1/2}\otimes H_2^{-1/2})\|_{m HS} \ \ge\ & rac12\log Z_t+ rac12\operatorname{Tr}(ho_0X_o)\ &- rac12\operatorname{Tr}(PX_1) - rac12\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma_aX_2)\ &-3R\eta_t . \end{split}} 	ag{12} \] Each of the three marginal replacements costs at most \(R\eta_t\). All comparison densities are specified from the actual local leaf. The unchanged leaf itself has, again by scalar spectral Jensen, \[ \log\|H_1^{1/2}A\| \ge\log\alpha+	frac12\operatorname{Tr}(PX_1). 	ag{13} \] Adding (12) and (13) cancels this incidence's metric term exactly. The known leaf normalization contributes \(\log\alpha\), while the parent contributes \(	frac12\log Z_t=	frac12\log D-	frac12\log(1-\eta_t)\). No possibly exponential physical leaf norm has been deleted. ## 5. Polynomial accuracy in the actual color dimensions In the actual source put \(s=N,\ D=N^b\). For any fixed integer \(J\ge1\), choose \[ t=\sqrt{s}\,D\,N^J . 	ag{14} \] Then \[ \eta_t\le N^{-2J},\qquad 2\eta_t=O(N^{-2J}),\qquad \log\|G_t\|_{m op}=(b+J+	frac12)\log N . 	ag{15} \] Thus (12) has loss \(O(RN^{-2J})\), and \(O(N^{1-2J})\) on any supplied window \(R=O(N)\). The theorem holds for every \(R\); it does not identify the anchored Newton window in [O] with a window on this larger matrix algebra. No new window theorem is asserted. A polynomial reference changes spectral bounds for positive metrics by only \(O(\log N)\) in their logarithmic radius, on the same compiler. One may perform this construction simultaneously on any set of prescribed-leaf edges with at most one selected input per parent. Each affected parent is exactly its own \(B_t\); no product output is gauged and the selected leaves remain fixed. For \(M\) selections, the sum of actual defects on those incidences is at most \(2M\eta_t\), and the reference costs \(O(M\log N)\) for fixed \(b,J\). The original output and root remain exact. Other edge defects are not controlled by this statement. ## 6. Scope and closest coverage The states \(ho_0,\sigma_a\) are the complete left/right multiplication energy states of the known leaf. They are not an arbitrarily chosen largest mode or an unknown internal output. The construction works for any specified nonzero crossing or blocked word leaf; it makes no claim that every tangle contraction is nonzero. It is a one-sided calibration. In fact \(\|\sigma_a\|_{m op}\le1/D\), so every unit vector \(h\) obeys \[ \|\sigma_a-|hangle\langle h|\|_1\ge2(1-1/D). 	ag{16} \] Test the trace-zero difference against \(|hangle\langle h|\). Thus a second actual pure leaf is not automatically matched. Compatibility of these mixed states through the remaining tree and the original closing is still a separate problem. No Gaussian description of the whole all-color tuple, metric undoing, geometric volume rate or finite-exception result is inferred. [C] already proves qualitative leaf elimination with singular limiting gauges and full tensor capacity. [O] already supplies full-matrix calibration families and a different anchored Newton leaf shear. [R] gives the actual positive main-color capacity with its original source. The addition here is the explicit finite matrix-product reference, exact defect, polynomial source-dimensional cost and the local logarithmic inequality (12). No general novelty for tensor Jensen or rank-one suppression is claimed. | Label | Complete text | Lines | SHA-256 | | --- | --- | ---: | --- | | C | [Actual full-gauge tree capacity](research_scalar_tree_full_gauge_capacity.md) | 466 | 2997b732aa73e063c66e81d6487a1d9927509609d61842c1dbb43d9345df1d6d | | O | [Ordered-density calibration](research_ordered_density_bilinear_calibration.md) | 320 | 928322373f35eee6692949953a91a592d9486b3507ffa439db5fbbc5729e516a | | R | [Regularized actual source capacity](research_regularized_actual_source_capacity.md) | 377 | 0cea0d52182eb24b4610538f354dbe5158fa54aa6f9cf7f9fc280c72ab090ff8 | All three complete matching texts were read. Only written mathematics, text reads and metadata operations were used. No mathematical program, numerical experiment, test, build, git operation or earlier-final edit was performed.

title: The opposite kernel's finite Gauss row and forced cyclic normalization
text: # The opposite kernel's finite Gauss row and forced cyclic normalization Private written proof, 18 November 2026. The actual opposite-polarization operator contains a finite balanced hypergeometric polynomial. Its clock contiguity has an explicit extreme-tail source. Going once around the finite clock solves the resulting forced recurrence. On the actual tensor module its assembled denominator is a uniformly bounded analytic unit on a scaled meridian collar. No individual clock denominator or endpoint source is removed. This identifies the literal normalization, including its meridian normals. The scalar polynomial away from the finite spectrum has an additional norm row, displayed below. Substituting a geometric scalar argument into the finite central relation would lose that row. No coherent phase, amplitude estimate, geometric occurrence, or vanishing relative-window defect is inferred. The two complete directs are J and R, pinned at the end. All finite summations, contiguities, and cyclic estimates used here are proved below. ## 1. An actual top-head factor of the opposite kernel Use J's conventions \[ N\ge2,\quad d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\quad m\ge2,\quad r=m-1,\quad x=-M/q,\quad f_n=(Q;Q)_n. \tag{1} \] The quantum root is fixed and the common meridian \(M\) varies near one. Thus \(f_d=N\). On the \(r\) remaining heads write \[ K=K_{\rm r},\quad E=E_{\rm r},\quad F=F_{\rm r},\qquad \Omega=FE+qK+q^{-1}K^{-1}. \] These are the actual ordered totals; \(E^N=F^N=0\). In particular \(K^{2N}=M^{2rN}I\). Put \[ H_n(M)=\prod_{j=1}^n(MQ^{-j}-M^{-1}),\qquad H_0=1. \tag{2} \] This \(H_n\) is a finite lowering product, not J's source normalization \(D_N(MK)\). Retain the actual maps \[ q_F=p_0S_m^{-1},\qquad S_m=\sum_{n=0}^d\frac{(x^{-1}L_1F)^n}{f_n},\qquad T=q_FE_\Sigma^d\mathscr C_m i_0,\qquad J=D_N(MK)^{-1}T. \tag{3} \] All scalar factors, the original cut, and the full balanced turnover \(\mathscr C_m\) have their meanings in J. Introduce the finite tail operator \[ A_N(M)=q_FE_\Sigma^d i_d, \qquad i_dv=w_d\otimes v. \tag{4} \] It is a literal factor of \(T\), not an independently chosen scalar interpolant. Here is the exact routing. Let \(\tau=R_1R_2\cdots R_r\), with the rightmost crossing acting first, and let \(\mathsf n\) be total remaining occupation. R's positive crossing is \(\kappa\mathsf P D\Theta\). When its second input is \(w_d\), every positive transfer vanishes because the recipient raising arrow is zero. Its remaining scalar is \(\kappa x^{-a-d}Q^{ad}\). Hence, with \(i_{{\rm last},d}\) inserting the last top head, \[ W_\tau i_{{\rm last},d}=i_dD_{\rm top},\qquad D_{\rm top}=\kappa^r x^{-rd}(x^{-1}Q^{-1})^{\mathsf n}. \tag{5} \] Also \(\mathscr C_m i_0=i_{{\rm last},d}\mathscr C_r\). The actual braid intertwines \(E_\Sigma\), and the quotient row \(q_FW=\mathcal B_m(W)q_F\) is R's exact row. Therefore \[ \boxed{\quad T=\mathcal B_m(W_\tau^{-1})\,A_N(M)\,D_{\rm top}\, \mathscr C_r(M). \quad}\tag{6} \] The order and every factor in (6) are retained. There is a useful direct normalization check. J's identity \(\mathscr C_m F_\Sigma(M^{-1})=E_\Sigma(M)\mathscr C_m\) and \(F_1^di_0=Ni_d\) give \[ T=Nq_F\mathscr C_m S_m(M^{-1})i_d. \tag{7} \] On the all-top remaining vector, \(S_m(M^{-1})\) fixes the full all-top vector. Turnover sends it to \(\gamma_N(M)^m\) times the all-bottom vector, where \(\gamma_N=(-1)^dD_N(M)/N\). The quotient fixes the latter. Thus the actual extreme entry is \[ T_{\boldsymbol0,\boldsymbol d}=N\gamma_N(M)^m,\qquad J_{\boldsymbol0,\boldsymbol d} =\frac{N\gamma_N(M)^m}{D_N(M^m\chi)},\quad \chi=(-q^{-1})^r. \tag{8} \] This is a fixed finite kernel datum. It does not assert a nonzero contraction with an exterior or a geometric cycle. ## 2. The finite polynomial and its transfer forcing The two terms in \(E_\Sigma=E_1K+E\) \(Q\)-commute. Order the degree-\(d\) binomial term as \(E^nE_1^{d-n}K^{d-n}\). At the root \[ {d\brack n}_Q=(-1)^nQ^{-n(n+1)/2}. \] The degree-\(n\) term of \(p_0S_m^{-1}\), on first occupation \(n\), has coefficient \((-1)^nQ^{n(n-1)/2}x^{-n}F^n/f_n\). The first lowering product from \(d\) to \(n\) is \(H_d/H_n\). Multiplication, in that order, proves \[ \boxed{\quad A_N(M;K,\Omega)= \sum_{n=0}^d \frac{Q^{-n}x^{-n}}{f_n}\frac{H_d}{H_n} F^nE^nK^{d-n}. \quad}\tag{9} \] The quotient \(H_d/H_n\) in this formula is its finite product from \(n+1\) to \(d\), so (9) is analytic near \(M=1\). The commutation relations give \[ F^nE^n=\prod_{j=0}^{n-1} (\Omega-qQ^jK-q^{-1}Q^{-j}K^{-1}). \tag{10} \] Thus \(A_N\) is a Laurent polynomial in \(K,M\) and a polynomial of degree \(d\) in the full commuting Casimir \(\Omega\). Its leading \(\Omega\)-coefficient is \[ \frac{Qx^{-d}}{N}. \tag{11} \] No scalar specialization of the tail Casimir was made. For scalar algebra only, put \(\Omega=z+z^{-1}\), and define \[ a=qKz,\quad b=qK/z,\quad c=M^{-2}Q,\quad t=M^{-2}K^{-2}=\frac{c}{ab}. \tag{12} \] Indeed \[ \Omega-qQ^jK-q^{-1}Q^{-j}K^{-1} =-q^{-1}Q^{-j}K^{-1}(1-aQ^j)(1-bQ^j), \] and \(H_n=M^nQ^{-n(n+1)/2}(c;Q)_n\). Substitution in (9) yields \[ A_N=H_dK^d\mathcal F_N(a,b;c;t),\qquad \mathcal F_N(a,b;c;s)= \sum_{n=0}^d\frac{(a;Q)_n(b;Q)_n}{f_n(c;Q)_n}s^n. \tag{13} \] The right side is a finite polynomial. The variable \(s\) in the second formula is independent; it is set equal to \(t\) only in the first formula. Let \(\mathcal Q_s f(s)=f(Qs)\). Comparison of consecutive coefficients, including the last coefficient, proves the exact row \[ \boxed{\begin{split} &\big[(1-\mathcal Q_s)(1-cQ^{-1}\mathcal Q_s) -s(1-a\mathcal Q_s)(1-b\mathcal Q_s)\big]\mathcal F_N\\ &\hspace{20mm} =-\frac{s^N(1-a^N)(1-b^N)}{N(c;Q)_d}, \qquad \mathcal F_N(0)=1. \end{split}}\tag{14} \] For degrees \(1,\ldots,d\), this is precisely the coefficient ratio in (13). At degree \(N\), the first bracket contributes zero because \(Q^N=1\); the last summand supplies the displayed forcing, using \(f_d=N\). Nothing beyond degree \(N\) occurs. This proves (14) without an infinite-series identity. Let \(C_N\) be the monic polynomial specified by \(C_N(z+z^{-1})=z^N+z^{-N}\), and set \[ \begin{split} \mathcal W_N(K,\Omega) &=\prod_{\ell=0}^d (\Omega-qQ^\ell K-q^{-1}Q^{-\ell}K^{-1})\\ &=C_N(\Omega)+K^N+K^{-N},\\ \mathcal V_N(K,\Omega) &=\prod_{\ell=1}^d (\Omega-qQ^\ell K-q^{-1}Q^{-\ell}K^{-1}). \end{split}\tag{15} \] The second equality follows by the roots and leading coefficient, first for generic \(K\) and then identically. The elementary recursion \(C_{j+1}(v)=vC_j(v)-C_{j-1}(v)\), \(C_0=2,C_1=v\), also defines these polynomials. Equations (10) and its reversed version give, on the actual tail, \[ \mathcal W_N=F^NE^N=0,\qquad \mathcal V_N=E^dF^d,\qquad (\Omega-qK-q^{-1}K^{-1})\mathcal V_N=0. \tag{16} \] Before that module specialization, \((1-a^N)(1-b^N)=K^N\mathcal W_N\). Thus (14) retains exactly the same off-spectrum norm row as (15). ## 3. Balanced contiguity, with its complete polynomial defect Write \[ \begin{split} D(K)&=(1-t/Q)(1-t/Q^2),\\ P(K,\Omega)&=1-M^{-2}q^{-1}K^{-1}\Omega +M^{-4}Q^{-1}K^{-2},\\ \alpha_N(M)&=\frac{(-1)^NqM^{-N-1}}{N}. \end{split}\tag{17} \] In \(A_N(M;QK,\Omega)\), only the Laurent variable \(K\) is replaced. This notation does not change the tail module or its meridian. The full polynomial identity is \[ \boxed{\begin{split} QD(K)A_N(QK,\Omega)-P(K,\Omega)A_N(K,\Omega) ={}&\frac{\alpha_N}{qK}\mathcal W_N(K,\Omega)\\ &+\alpha_N(1-t/Q)(1-K^{-2}/Q)\mathcal V_N(K,\Omega). \end{split}}\tag{18} \] All quantities in this identity include their \(M\) dependence. Here is a finite proof. For \(0\le l<N\), the elementary identity \[ \sum_{n=0}^l \frac{(Q^{-l};Q)_n(b;Q)_n}{f_n(c;Q)_n} (cQ^l/b)^n =\frac{(c/b;Q)_l}{(c;Q)_l} \tag{19} \] can be proved without importing a summation theorem. Multiply by \((c;Q)_l\), put \(y=c/b\), and rewrite the left side as \[ L_l(b,y)=\sum_{n=0}^l {l\brack n}_Q (-y)^nQ^{n(n-1)/2}(b;Q)_n(byQ^n;Q)_{l-n}. \] The Gaussian Pascal identity gives \[ L_{l+1}(b,y)=(1-byQ^l)L_l(b,y) -yQ^l(1-b)L_l(bQ,y). \] Starting with \(L_0=1\), induction gives \(L_l=(y;Q)_l\), proving (19). Only products of length less than \(N\) have been divided. For generic \(K,M\), evaluate at \(\Omega_l=qKQ^l+q^{-1}K^{-1}Q^{-l}\), \(0\le l<N\). Then \(a=Q^{-l}\), and (19) gives \[ \frac{A_N(K,\Omega_l)}{H_dK^d} =\frac{(tQ^{-l};Q)_l}{(c;Q)_l}. \tag{20} \] For \(l\ge1\), shifting \(K\) to \(QK\) replaces \(l\) by \(l-1\). The ratio in (20) is exactly \[ \frac{(1-cQ^{l-1})(1-tQ^{-l-1})} {(1-t/Q)(1-t/Q^2)} =\frac{P(K,\Omega_l)}{D(K)}. \tag{21} \] The prefactor \(K^d\) changes by \(Q^{-1}\). Consequently the left side of (18) vanishes at the \(d\) nodes \(l=1,\ldots,d\). At \(l=0\), the unshifted finite sum is one and the shifted terminating length is \(d\). The two root products give \[ \mathcal F_N(Q,Q^2K^2;c;t/Q^2) =\frac{(1-t^N)(1-c/Q)} {(1-t/Q^2)(1-c^N)}. \tag{22} \] Hence the left side of (18), at \(\Omega_0\), equals \[ H_dK^d P(K,\Omega_0)\frac{c^N-t^N}{1-c^N}. \tag{23} \] Here \[ \begin{split} H_d&=(-1)^dM^d\frac{1-M^{-2N}}{1-M^{-2}},\\ P(K,\Omega_0)&=(1-M^{-2})(1-t/Q),\\ \mathcal V_N(K,\Omega_0) &=Nq^dK^d\frac{1-K^{-2N}}{1-Q^{-1}K^{-2}}. \end{split} \tag{24} \] Equations (23)--(24) show that its quotient by \(\mathcal V_N\) at this node is \(\alpha_N(1-t/Q)(1-K^{-2}/Q)\). Finally (11) shows that the degree-\(N\) coefficient of the left side of (18) is \(\alpha_N/(qK)\). Subtract that multiple of the monic \(\mathcal W_N\); the remainder has degree at most \(d\), vanishes at the \(d\) nodes \(l=1,\ldots,d\), and has the value just computed at \(l=0\). This proves (18). The argument was on a generic set only to divide displayed factors and separate nodes. Polynomial/Laurent continuation proves the full identity, including all coincident nodes. On the actual tail module, (16) reduces (18) to \[ \boxed{\quad QD(K)A_N(QK)-P(K,\Omega)A_N(K) =\alpha_N(1-t/Q)(1-K^{-2}/Q)E^dF^d. \quad}\tag{25} \] The endpoint on the right is a specified finite operator. It has not been discarded as a homogeneous normalization. ## 4. The forced cyclic Green row on the full tail module For \(j=0,\ldots,N-1\), put \[ K_j=Q^jK,\quad t_j=M^{-2}K_j^{-2},\quad \mathscr A_j=A_N(M;K_j,\Omega),\quad \mathcal V_j=\mathcal V_N(K_j,\Omega), \] and, where the displayed denominators are invertible, define \[ \rho_j=\frac{P(K_j,\Omega)}{QD(K_j)},\qquad \eta_j=\frac{\alpha_N(1-t_j/Q)(1-K_j^{-2}/Q)} {QD(K_j)}\mathcal V_j. \tag{26} \] All these are commuting functions of the actual \(K,\Omega\). Since \(K_N=K\) and \(\mathcal W_N(K_j,\Omega)=0\), (25) is \[ \mathscr A_{j+1}=\rho_j\mathscr A_j+\eta_j,\qquad \mathscr A_N=\mathscr A_0. \tag{27} \] There is no assumption of diagonalizability of \(\Omega\). The full orbit can be multiplied exactly. With \(b_0=M^{-2N}\) and \(k=K^N\), one has \[ \begin{split} \prod_jD(K_j)&=(1-b_0k^{-2})^2,\\ \prod_jP(K_j,\Omega) &=(1+b_0k^{-1}z^N)(1+b_0k^{-1}z^{-N}) \quad(\Omega=z+z^{-1}). \end{split}\tag{28} \] The first formula is valid also for even \(N\). In that case the two half-orbit products are \((1+t^{N/2})^2\) and \((1-t^{N/2})^2\), whose product is \((1-t^N)^2\). The second formula follows by factoring \(P\) as \((1-M^{-2}q^{-1}K^{-1}z) (1-M^{-2}q^{-1}K^{-1}z^{-1})\) and using \(q^N=-1\). Before module specialization their difference is \[ \prod_jD(K_j)-\prod_jP(K_j,\Omega) =b_0(1-k^{-2})(1-b_0k^{-2}) -b_0k^{-1}\mathcal W_N(K,\Omega). \tag{29} \] Thus the off-spectrum row is still explicit. On the actual module, \(\mathcal W_N=0\), and (28) yields the scalar \[ \mathcal R_N(M):=\prod_{j=0}^{N-1}\rho_j =\frac{1-M^{-2N}}{1-M^{-2N}K^{-2N}} =\frac{1-M^{-2N}}{1-M^{-2mN}}. \tag{30} \] Iterating (27) and using periodicity now gives the exact row \[ \boxed{\quad \mathscr A_0=\frac{1}{1-\mathcal R_N(M)} \sum_{j=0}^{N-1} \left(\prod_{\ell=j+1}^{N-1}\rho_\ell\right)\eta_j. \quad}\tag{31} \] The empty product is one. This is an operator identity on the whole actual tail module, including its Casimir Jordan blocks. It initially holds on the generic meridian set of (26), and its continuation is the analytic finite polynomial (9). Individual \(D(K_j)\) inverses at completeness are not thereby declared defined; their cancellations occur in the full row. The assembled scalar inverse in (31) has uniform local control. For \(u=N\Log M\), \[ \mathcal R_N(M)=\mathcal R(u) =\frac{1-e^{-2u}}{1-e^{-2mu}},\qquad \mathcal R(0)=\frac1m. \tag{32} \] For fixed \(m\ge2\), choose \(\eta>0\) so that this removable function is analytic on \(|u|\le\eta\) and \(\lvert1-\mathcal R(u)\rvert\ge(m-1)/(2m)\). Then \[ |(1-\mathcal R(u))^{-1}|\le\frac{2m}{m-1}. \tag{33} \] Cauchy estimates on a smaller \(u\)-disk bound all fixed \(u\)-derivatives independently of \(N\). Since \(\partial_M u=N/M\), the corresponding fixed meridian derivatives are \(O(N^j)\). These bounds concern only the assembled scalar inverse. They do not bound the individual clock transports, the endpoint kernels, or the norm of \(A_N\). In particular (31) fixes the literal normalization from the forced rows, rather than estimating its size. ## 5. Actual kernel and relative-window consequences All matrices in (6), (9), and (31) are on J's original finite spaces. Applying its compact kernel \(K_B(\mathbf w,\mathbf z)=v(\mathbf w)B c(\mathbf z)\) therefore gives exact finite coherent identities and exact convolutions on the original compact resolutions. Every cap \(\prod_i(1+w_i z_i)^d\), Cartan factor, factorial dual, and meridian derivative remains. This does not replace an operator kernel by the scalar evaluation in (13). There is also an explicit relative row. For any two actual partial-resolution matrices \(P_{\mathcal C},P_{\mathcal D}\) from J, define \(\Delta_j=P_{\mathcal C}\mathscr A_j-\mathscr A_jP_{\mathcal D}\). Multiplying (27) on both sides, without commuting a window past a coefficient, gives \[ \Delta_{j+1} =\rho_j\Delta_j+[P_{\mathcal C},\rho_j]\mathscr A_j +P_{\mathcal C}\eta_j-\eta_jP_{\mathcal D}. \tag{34} \] Its periodic solution is the same ordered sum as (31), with \(\eta_j\) replaced by the three retained terms after \(\rho_j\Delta_j\) in (34). Thus the window comparison has both a coefficient commutator and an explicit extreme-tail source. J's boundary transgression applies to the two partial resolutions, with their complementary chains retained. No term in (34) is zero merely because the full trace is sewn. The finite formulas are holomorphic or meromorphic in the common meridian before taking their prescribed continuations. They may consequently be differentiated with all displayed normal terms. They are not ordinary quantum-parameter-normal identities obtained by differentiating the root equations. For clarity, the following distinction is essential. Equation (30) used the actual operator relation \(\mathcal W_N=0\). At a geometric scalar argument \((K,\Omega)\), even when \(\Omega=z+z^{-1}\) comes from a loxodromic representation, the polynomial \(\mathcal W_N\) in (15) need not vanish. Equations (14), (18), and (29) retain its complete contribution. Nor does the finite-node evaluation (20) define a preferred complex interpolation of its integer label \(l\). The canonical scalar continuation is the original polynomial (9). The result is an actual factorization of the opposite kernel, its explicit finite Gauss polynomial, and a forced cyclic normalization with a controlled assembled meridian denominator. The high-degree endpoint kernel and the relative row (34) remain to be estimated in a proposed geometric chart. No nonzero local amplitude, source-sector coefficient, or geometric relative-cycle transport follows from these identities. ## Complete proof directs * J: notes/research_opposite_polarization_source_kernel.md, SHA256 d52c6dd8e62f575a262fc7af460e258f7cb0e40b5a9c037ac46dd8d151002d44. * R: notes/research_actual_reduced_braid_source.md, SHA256 9a472ef27b08305a519ff1f24b6d2b909e63a0acbdc49b3a29e001c52a2f2243. Both complete directs were freshly read nontruncated in this active author sequence. Every used implication was checked. Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used. Frozen and public files were not changed.

title: The opposite source kernel sews by its actual Krein adjoint
text: # The opposite source kernel sews by its actual Krein adjoint Written research proof, 23 November 2026. The actual opposite-polarization kernel has an explicit adjoint after the prefix Krein descent. One frozen Cartan factor converts it into a single kernel whose reflected meridian value is its Krein adjoint. The original pointed source is consequently an exact adjoint sewing of that kernel with the actual reduced word. Every scalar, meridian pole and root finite part is retained. The form is indefinite. This is not a positive trace or a lower bound for the marked scalar. No geometric window or complementary current is removed by the adjoint identity. ## 1. Spaces, original operators and normalization Fix the original root and head count \[ N\ge2,\quad d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2, \quad m\ge2,\quad r=m-1,\quad x=-M/q . \tag{1} \] The quantum parameter stays fixed. Initially \(M>0\), on the real branch of \(\Log M\). Label the full physical space by \(V(M)\) and its remaining \(r\)-head space by \(U(M)\), retaining the same ordered occupation bases at every meridian. Their forms are \[ H_N|a\rangle=qQ^a|d-a\rangle,\qquad \mathscr H_b=H_N^{\otimes b},\qquad A^\sharp=\mathscr H_{\rm in}A^\dagger\mathscr H_{\rm out}. \tag{2} \] The last formula also defines the rectangular adjoint from the output back to the input. Both forms are Hermitian involutions, independent of \(M\). Use the prefix of [D], with its original zero endpoint: \[ S_M=e_Q(x^{-1}L_1F_{\rm r}(M)),\quad q_M=p_0S_M^{-1},\quad i_0v=|0\rangle\otimes v, \quad i_dv=|d\rangle\otimes v . \tag{3} \] Thus \(S_Mi_0=i_0\), \(q_Mi_0=I\), and [D] proves \(S_M^\sharp=S_M^{-1}\). Write \[ K_\Sigma(M)=M^mK_{\Sigma,0},\qquad K_{\rm r}(M)=M^rK_0,\qquad K_0^N=\varepsilon I, \quad\varepsilon=(-1)^{(N+1)r}. \tag{4} \] These are the actual total Cartans; \(K_0\) is the frozen remaining Cartan at completeness. In particular \(K_0^\sharp=K_0\). We retain [O]'s scaled lowering operator, denoted here by \(E\): \[ E|a\rangle=(MQ^{-a}-M^{-1})|a-1\rangle\quad(a>0), \qquad E|0\rangle=0 . \tag{5} \] On ordered heads \(E_\Sigma=E_1K_{\rm r}+E_{\rm r}\). This is \(q^{-1}\) times the head \(e_x\) convention used in the physical real-meridian proof; its adjoint is therefore \(E^\sharp=QE\), not \(E\). Directly, the two reflected \(H_N\) factors contribute \(Q\), and \(\overline{MQ^{-(d-a+1)}-M^{-1}}=MQ^{-a}-M^{-1}\). The zero bottom arrow matches the top zero of the adjoint. Hence \[ E_\Sigma^\sharp=QE_\Sigma,\qquad (E_\Sigma^d)^\sharp=Q^{-1}E_\Sigma^d, \quad K_{\Sigma,0}E_\Sigma K_{\Sigma,0}^{-1}=QE_\Sigma. \tag{6} \] The entire balanced turnover and its tensor reversal are those of [O]: \[ C_M|a\rangle=c_a(M)|d-a\rangle,\quad c_a(M)=\prod_{j=1}^a\frac{MQ^j-M^{-1}}{1-Q^j},\quad \mathscr C_M=C_M^{\otimes m}\mathsf J . \tag{7} \] Here \(\mathsf J\) reverses the original head order. In particular \(\mathscr C_M\) goes from the reflected full module to \(V(M)\). The actual opposite kernel is \[ T_M=q_ME_\Sigma(M)^d\mathscr C_Mi_0: U(M^{-1})\longrightarrow U(M). \tag{8} \] Every symbol in this definition is a specified finite original matrix. ## 2. The turnover and rectangular adjoints For positive real \(M\), each factor in (7) gives \(\overline{c_a(M)}=c_a(M^{-1})\). On one head the coefficient of \(C_M^\sharp\) on input \(a\) is \(q^2Q^{2a}\overline{c_a(M)}\). Since the frozen one-head Cartan is \(-q^{-1}Q^{-a}\), its inverse square has exactly that factor. Tensor reversal commutes with the total Cartan, so the complete identity is \[ \mathscr C_M^\sharp =\mathscr C_{M^{-1}}K_{\Sigma,0}^{-2}. \tag{9} \] No scalar \(M\)-power remains in this frozen-Cartan expression. From (2)--(3) the rectangular adjoints are exactly \[ i_0^\sharp=q^{-1}p_d,\qquad p_0^\sharp=qi_d,\qquad q_M^\sharp=qS_Mi_d . \tag{10} \] The first two follow from the entries \((H_N)_{0d}=q^{-1}\) and \((H_N)_{d0}=q\); the last uses prefix isometry. The finite top-row identities needed below are \[ p_dF_\Sigma(M)^d=Nq_M,\qquad S_Mi_d=F_\Sigma(M)^di_0/N,\qquad K_{\Sigma,0}^{-2}i_d=Q^{-1}i_dK_0^{-2}. \tag{11} \] Indeed \(F_\Sigma=S_MF_1S_M^{-1}\), \(p_dS_M=p_d\), and \(F_1^di_0=(Q;Q)_di_d=Ni_d\). These prove the first two formulas, with both factors \(N\) retained. For the last, the first-head top Cartan is \(-q\), whose inverse square is \(Q^{-1}\). All statements include the finite top and bottom rows. ## 3. The exact adjoint of the opposite kernel Use the shorthand \(\widehat M=M^{-1}\). Combining (6),(9),(10) first gives \[ T_M^\sharp=Q^{-1}p_d\mathscr C_{\widehat M} K_{\Sigma,0}^{-2}E_\Sigma(M)^dS_Mi_d. \tag{12} \] The factors \(q^{-1}\) and \(q\) from the rectangular adjoints have canceled; \(Q^{-1}\) is still present from \(E^d\). Moving \(K_{\Sigma,0}^{-2}\) through \(E_\Sigma^d\) contributes \(Q^{-2d}=Q^2\). It commutes with \(S_M\), and the last formula of (11) then contributes \(Q^{-1}\). Thus all three remaining phases cancel, leaving \[ T_M^\sharp=p_d\mathscr C_{\widehat M} E_\Sigma(M)^dS_Mi_dK_0^{-2}. \tag{13} \] The actual turnover in [O, (7)] exchanges the two totals: \(\mathscr C_{\widehat M}E_\Sigma(M)= F_\Sigma(\widehat M)\mathscr C_{\widehat M}\) and \(\mathscr C_{\widehat M}F_\Sigma(M)= E_\Sigma(\widehat M)\mathscr C_{\widehat M}\). Use these and the first two formulas of (11) in order: \[ \begin{split} T_M^\sharp &=Nq_{\widehat M}\mathscr C_{\widehat M}S_Mi_dK_0^{-2}\\ &=q_{\widehat M}\mathscr C_{\widehat M} F_\Sigma(M)^di_0K_0^{-2}\\ &=q_{\widehat M}E_\Sigma(\widehat M)^d \mathscr C_{\widehat M}i_0K_0^{-2} =T_{\widehat M}K_0^{-2}. \end{split} \tag{14} \] The factor \(N\) has canceled only against the specified \(1/N\) in the top section. Equation (14) holds for all positive real meridians and every original primitive level. ## 4. Source normalization gives one kernel and its adjoint Retain exactly [O]'s notation for the scalar normalization: \[ \begin{gathered} \mathcal D_N(z)=\frac{z^N-z^{-N}}{z-z^{-1}},\quad \gamma_N(M)=(-1)^d\mathcal D_N(M)/N,\quad a_N(M)=(-1)^dN\gamma_N(M)^m,\quad \mathcal H_M=\mathcal D_N(MK_{\rm r}(M)),\quad J_M=\mathcal H_M^{-1}T_M . \end{gathered} \tag{15} \] The Laurent-polynomial continuation defines \(\mathcal D_N\) at \(z=\pm1\). The actual finite identities of [O, (11),(13),(16),(19)] are \[ \begin{gathered} K_0T_M=T_MK_0^{-1},\quad \mathcal H_MT_M=T_M\mathcal H_{\widehat M},\quad T_MT_{\widehat M}=a_N(M)\mathcal H_M,\quad J_MJ_{\widehat M}=a_N(M)\mathcal H_M^{-1}. \end{gathered} \tag{16} \] Here inverses are generic meromorphic matrices; the complete source is continued before specializing a singular meridian. For positive real \(M\), \(\mathcal H_M^\sharp=\mathcal H_M\), since \(K_{\rm r}^\sharp=K_{\rm r}\) and \(\mathcal D_N\) has real Laurent coefficients. Equations (14),(16) therefore give \[ J_M^\sharp=J_{\widehat M}K_0^{-2}. \tag{17} \] For example, in this calculation \(T_{\widehat M}\mathcal H_M^{-1} =\mathcal H_{\widehat M}^{-1}T_{\widehat M}\); the diagonal factor cannot simply be commuted through \(T\). Define the typed kernel \[ A_M=J_MK_0^{-1}:U(\widehat M)\longrightarrow U(M). \tag{18} \] Its right Cartan acts on its reflected input. Since \(K_0J_M=J_MK_0^{-1}\) and \(K_0^\sharp=K_0\), we obtain \[ \boxed{\qquad A_M^\sharp=A_{\widehat M},\qquad A_MA_M^\sharp=a_N(M)\mathcal H_M^{-1}. \qquad} \tag{19} \] These are adjoints between the two actual tail modules, whose numerical forms are the same \(\mathscr H_r\). For the original reduced word \(B_\beta(M)\), [O, (21)] is \(\Phi_0(W_\beta(M))=\mathcal D_N(M) \operatorname{Tr}_{U(M)}(\mathcal H_M^{-1}B_\beta(M))\). Consequently (19) and cyclicity give the source-exact sewing \[ \boxed{\quad \Phi_0(W_\beta(M))=\frac{\mathcal D_N(M)}{a_N(M)} \operatorname{Tr}_{U(\widehat M)} (A_M^\sharp B_\beta(M)A_M). \quad} \tag{20} \] The outside trace is on the reflected tail. It is not an additional factor \(N\), a reset cap, or an unidentified opposite word. The density identity holds for any remaining matrix \(B\); identifying it with \(\Phi_0(W)\) uses the actual intertwiner and original source formula just stated. For real positive \(M\), the scalar in (20) is exactly \[ \frac{\mathcal D_N(M)}{a_N(M)} =\sigma\left(\frac{N}{\mathcal D_N(M)}\right)^{m-1}, \qquad\sigma=(-1)^{d(m+1)}. \tag{21} \] It is real; the sign is retained. An equivalent Hermitian congruence for the original trace density is \[ \mathcal D_N(M)\mathcal H_M^{-1}\mathscr H_r =\frac{\mathcal D_N(M)}{a_N(M)} A_M\mathscr H_rA_M^\dagger. \tag{22} \] This is an indefinite congruence, not a positive Gram factorization. ## 5. Root finite parts and scope For the meridian germ about completeness put \(M=e^u\). The holomorphic reflected adjoint means \(A^{\natural\sharp}(u)= \mathscr H_r\overline{A(\bar u)}^{\mathsf T}\mathscr H_r\), not a pointwise conjugation of an unrelated complex meridian. Polarization of (19) gives \(A^{\natural\sharp}(u)=A(-u)\). Thus (20) continues meromorphically with the literal product \(A(-u)B_\beta(e^u)A(u)\) and the even scalar (21). All root finite parts are taken after this whole product. The original source is analytic there; its individual kernel factors need not be. In particular [O] gives at most a simple pole. If \(A(u)=\sum_{j\ge-1}A_ju^j\), then exactly \[ A_j^\sharp=(-1)^jA_j,\qquad A_{-1}^2=0. \tag{23} \] The second statement follows because the right side of (19) has at most a simple pole, so the coefficient of \(u^{-2}\) in \(A(u)A(-u)\) vanishes. Neither residue nor its normal terms is discarded. For the ACTUAL unwindowed braid there is a stronger matrix cancellation. Put \(B_+(M)=B_\beta(M)\), and let \(B_-(M)\) be the word with reflected head labels of [O, (11)]. That exact intertwining and commutation of \(B_-\) with \(K_0\) give \(B_+(M)A_M=A_MB_-(\widehat M)\). Thus \[ A_{\widehat M}B_+(M)A_M =a_N(M)\mathcal H_{\widehat M}^{-1}B_-(\widehat M). \tag{24} \] The right side has at most a simple meridian pole as a MATRIX. Consequently \(A_{-1}B_\beta(1)A_{-1}=0\) as a matrix. This uses the actual word intertwining, before taking any trace. An arbitrary holomorphic middle insertion \(C(u)\), without that intertwining, can instead give a nonzero matrix coefficient \(-A_{-1}C(0)A_{-1}\) at \(u^{-2}\). Its complete unwindowed trace is zero by cyclicity and (23). A further outer window, or separate windows on the two kernel factors, need not retain that trace cancellation; their actual relative defects must be kept. The first-meridian-jet source remains the original one reconstructed in [O] and [D]. Quantum-parameter normals are different and are not differentiated in this proof. The gain is a genuine adjoint sewing of the original source, using a specified single kernel and its reflected meridian value. No assertion is made that a partial coherent resolution commutes with that kernel, that its relative-window defect vanishes, or that the actual geometric cycle is selected. The two tails retain all \(N^r\) physical coordinates and every root Jordan direction. All exterior rows, pivots, framing and modified-dimension factors retain their original positions and their own conjugate factors. No positive norm, two-eigenline noncancellation, or marked scalar lower bound follows from (20). ## Complete sources and coverage Both complete direct texts were read at the matching pins: | Source | SHA-256 | |---|---| | [D: Reduced prefix Krein descent](research_reduced_prefix_krein_descent.md), 310 lines | `5f0ab1e56d6a2877cec8d52e2f13efc355729caf48f3726b4cd8654a1c9b3abe` | | [O: Original opposite-polarization source kernel](research_opposite_polarization_source_kernel.md), 639 lines | `d52c6dd8e62f575a262fc7af460e258f7cb0e40b5a9c037ac46dd8d151002d44` | The complete [paired Bargmann/Krein proof](research_paired_bargmann_krein_sewing.md), 256 lines, SHA-256 `23f6029f059e6d63cb25dc0f9450052fc7aa541e9122afcef0a159416949da2f`, was checked for coverage. Its exact coefficient-form pairing does not identify the adjoint of the opposite source operator; that is proved here. Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used. This corrected proof supersedes the unadopted predecessor `research_opposite_krein_adjoint_source.md` at SHA-256 `4c24de63b6458337df54ebd705e44b36c479f6bd4c1c2bcede20f2270232abac`. That file and all earlier final files remain unchanged.

title: Opposite-polarization kernels and the original closing source
text:
# Opposite-polarization kernels and the original closing source Private written proof, 18 November 2026. The actual total lowering power, balanced turnover, and prefix quotient give a finite operator between the two polarizations. Its normalization is exactly the inverse-Jacobian coupon of the original pointed source. Two normalized kernels sew to that source, on the original compact coherent cycles. Their root Laurent coefficients recover the first meridian jet and give an explicit contracting homotopy on every nonself reciprocal physical-weight pair. This is also a relative-source construction: restricting a resolution to a subchain produces a specified operator defect and its boundary transgression. Neither the defect nor the complementary chains are discarded. No geometric contribution is selected by generic invertibility or by the contracting homotopy. The complete directs R, P, and Z are pinned below. They supply the actual quotient, balanced turnover, and original source normalization. The power product, normalized sewing, Laurent algebra, and relative kernel statements are proved here. ## 1. The literal map and its balanced scalar Fix \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\), and \(m\ge2\) heads at the common meridian \(M\) near one. The quantum parameter is fixed. Put \(r=m-1\), \(x=-M/q\), and \[ K_{m r}(M)=M^rK_0,\qquad K_0^N=\varepsilon I,\qquad \varepsilon=(-1)^{(N+1)r}. 	ag{1} \] The remaining occupation space is a fixed vector space \(U\). All reflected maps below use its same ordered basis. Use the actual ordered total matrices \(E_\Sigma,F_\Sigma,K_\Sigma\), where \(E\) is the scaled balanced lowering operator. On one head, \[ Fw_a=(1-Q^{a+1})w_{a+1},\qquad Ew_a=(MQ^{-a}-M^{-1})w_{a-1},\qquad Kw_a=xQ^{-a}w_a. 	ag{2} \] The missing extreme arrows are zero. In particular \(E^N=F^N=0\). The same identities hold for the totals: the two terms in \(E_1K_{m r}+E_{m r}\) \(Q\)-commute, and those in \(F_1+K_1^{-1}F_{m r}\) \(Q^{-1}\)-commute. The finite binomial formula at a primitive \(N\)-th root has zero intermediate coefficients in degree \(N\). Induction over the heads proves \[ E_\Sigma^N=F_\Sigma^N=0. 	ag{3} \] R's actual triangular matrix and quotient maps are \[ S(M)=\sum_{j=0}^{d}  rac{(x^{-1}L_1F_{m r})^j}{\prod_{a=1}^j(1-Q^a)},\qquad q_F(M)=p_0S(M)^{-1},\qquad i_F(M)=S(M)i_0=i_0. 	ag{4} \] They are holomorphic near one, \(q_Fi_F=I\), and \(\ker q_F=F_\Sigma V\). For a total intertwiner \(W\), \[ B(W)=q_FW i_F,\qquad q_FW=B(W)q_F. 	ag{5} \] The second identity follows either from the quotient or directly from R's expansion \(S^{-1}WS=\sum F_1^nB_n\). Retain the entire balanced turnover \[ C(M)w_a=c_a(M)w_{d-a},\qquad c_a(M)=\prod_{j=1}^a rac{MQ^j-M^{-1}}{1-Q^j},\qquad \mathscr C(M)=C(M)^{\otimes m}\mathsf J, 	ag{6} \] where \(\mathsf J\) reverses the factors. P proves, with the original Cartan and crossing scalars, \[ \mathscr C F_\Sigma(M^{-1})=E_\Sigma(M)\mathscr C,\quad \mathscr C E_\Sigma(M^{-1})=F_\Sigma(M)\mathscr C,\quad K_\Sigma(M)\mathscr C=\mathscr C K_\Sigma(M^{-1})^{-1}. 	ag{7} \] There is a scalar which must not be suppressed: \[ \mathscr C(M)\mathscr C(M^{-1})=\gamma_N(M)^mI,\qquad \gamma_N(M)=(-1)^d rac{D_N(M)}{N},\qquad D_N(z)= rac{z^N-z^{-N}}{z-z^{-1}}. 	ag{8} \] Indeed \(c_{d-a}(M)c_a(M^{-1})\) is independent of \(a\). Its consecutive ratio is one after replacing \(Q^{d-a}\) by \(Q^{-a-1}\). At \(a=0\), the root product \(\prod_{j=1}^d(1-Q^j)=N\) gives \(c_d(M)=\gamma_N(M)\). The Laurent-polynomial continuation defines \(D_N\) at \(z=\pm1\). Define the actual analytic matrix \[  oxed{\quad T(M)=q_F(M)E_\Sigma(M)^d\mathscr C(M)i_F(M^{-1}). \quad} 	ag{9} \] Equivalently the rightmost factor is \(S(M^{-1})i_0\). It descends from the reflected quotient: adding \(F_\Sigma(M^{-1})v\) to a representative gives zero after \(E_\Sigma^d\mathscr C\), by (3),(7). More explicitly it factors as \[ V(M^{-1})/F_\Sigma V(M^{-1}) \ \xrightarrow{\ \mathscr C\ }\ V(M)/E_\Sigma V(M) \ \xrightarrow{\ E_\Sigma^d\ }\ker E_\Sigma(M) \ \xrightarrow{\ q_F\ }\ V(M)/F_\Sigma V(M). 	ag{10} \] Every arrow here is an actual finite linear map. Let \( eta^{m rev}\) replace \(\sigma_i^{\pm1}\) by \(\sigma_{m-i}^{\pm1}\), without reversing word order. Write \(B_+(M)=B(W_ eta(M))\) and \(B_-(M)=B(W_{ eta^{m rev}}(M))\). P's whole-meridian turnover and (5),(7) imply \[ B_+(M)T(M)=T(M)B_-(M^{-1}),\qquad K_0T(M)=T(M)K_0^{-1}. 	ag{11} \] For the first identity, the difference between \(W_{ eta^{m rev}}i_F\) and \(i_FB_-\) lies in \(F_\Sigma V\) and is killed in (9). For the second use \(K_\Sigma E_\Sigma^d=Q^{-1}E_\Sigma^dK_\Sigma\), the quotient and section rows \(q_FK_\Sigma=xK_{m r}q_F\), \(K_\Sigma i_F=i_FxK_{m r}\), and \(x(M)x(M^{-1})=Q^{-1}\). The scalar first-head Cartan substitution is made only in these rows. The prescribed zero-framing line is reciprocal and stays in \(W\), as in P. Any additional external scalar remains explicit. Marks not satisfying the indicated intertwining and turnover retain their defect; (11) is not imposed on them. ## 2. Exact double composition and source normalization Put \[ H(M)=D_N(MK_{m r}(M)),\qquad a_N(M)=(-1)^dN\,\gamma_N(M)^m . 	ag{12} \] Then \[  oxed{\quad T(M)T(M^{-1})=a_N(M)H(M).\quad} 	ag{13} \] Here is a proof including the lowering product. With \(\Omega_\Sigma=F_\Sigma E_\Sigma+qK_\Sigma+ q^{-1}K_\Sigma^{-1}\), set \(v(k,\omega)=\omega-qk-q^{-1}k^{-1}\). The commutation relations give by induction \[ E_\Sigma^dF_\Sigma^d =\prod_{j=1}^{d}v(Q^{-j}K_\Sigma,\Omega_\Sigma). 	ag{14} \] Both \(K_\Sigma\) and \(\Omega_\Sigma\) descend to the \(F\) quotient. There their values are \[ K_\Sigma=-z/q,\qquad \Omega_\Sigma=-z-z^{-1}, \qquad z=MK_{m r}. \] Thus each factor in (14) becomes \((1-Q^j)(zQ^{-j}-z^{-1})\). The two finite products give \[ q_FE_\Sigma^dF_\Sigma^di_F=(-1)^dN D_N(MK_{m r}). 	ag{15} \] In composing (9), replace \(i_F(M^{-1})q_F(M^{-1})\) by \(I\): its difference has image in \(F_\Sigma(M^{-1})V\), which the left factor \(E_\Sigma^d\mathscr C\) annihilates. Equations (7),(8),(15) then give (13). The reflected identity follows too. From (11) and \(D_N(z^{-1})=D_N(z)\), \[ H(M)T(M)=T(M)H(M^{-1}). 	ag{16} \] On a sufficiently small punctured meridian disk all these \(H\)'s are invertible. Set \[  oxed{\quad J(M)=H(M)^{-1}T(M).\quad} 	ag{17} \] This is precisely source normalization, rather than an arbitrary normalizing scalar. Z's central coupon \(Z_N=U_{N-1}(-\Omega_\Sigma)^{-1}\) has \(q_FZ_N=H^{-1}q_F\): the first block row of its actual triangular matrix inverse proves this equality. Hence \[ J(M)=q_F(M)Z_N(M)E_\Sigma(M)^d\mathscr C(M)i_F(M^{-1}). 	ag{18} \] Its exact reflection law and generic inverse are \[ J(M)J(M^{-1})=a_N(M)H(M)^{-1},\qquad J(M)^{-1}=a_N(M)^{-1}T(M^{-1}). 	ag{19} \] In particular the failure of a reflection square to be \(I\) is the specified central source kernel. The poles of \(J\) at completeness have order at most one. On \(K_0=\chi\), put \(z=M^m\chi\). Then \[ H(M)^{-1} ig|_\chi = rac{M^m\chi-M^{-m}\chi^{-1}} {\varepsilon(M^{mN}-M^{-mN})}. 	ag{20} \] For \(\chi
e\chi^{-1}\) the denominator has a simple zero; for \(\chi=\pm1\) the quotient is removable. Since \(T\) is analytic, this proves the assertion without a bound on its norm. All these statements concern fixed-root meridian normals, not ordinary quantum-parameter normals. ## 3. Two kernels sew to the original pointed functional The exact original highest-cut and pivotal source is \[ \Phi_0(W)=\operatorname{Tr}_{V} ((P_0\otimes K_{m r}^{1-N})W) =D_N(M)\operatorname{Tr}_{U}(H(M)^{-1}B_+(M)), 	ag{21} \] by R and Z. Equations (11),(16),(19) give the stronger matrix identity \[ J(M)B_-(M^{-1})J(M^{-1}) =a_N(M)H(M)^{-1}B_+(M). 	ag{22} \] Consequently \[  oxed{\displaystyle \Phi_0(W_ eta(M))=  rac{D_N(M)}{a_N(M)} \operatorname{Tr}_{U}\! \left(J(M)B_-(M^{-1})J(M^{-1})ight). }	ag{23} \] All meromorphic expressions have the continuation prescribed by the original analytic left side. Even though the individual \(J\)'s can have simple poles, the sewn matrix in (22) has at most a simple pole. Its residue has zero trace. This cancellation uses exact composition; it is not a pointwise cancellation of an unintegrated product of coherent kernels. For arbitrary reduced matrices \(A_+,A_-\), the corresponding defect is explicit. Put \(\Delta=A_+T-TA_-\). Direct multiplication gives \[ J A_- J(M^{-1}) =a_NH^{-1}A_+-H^{-1}\Delta J(M^{-1}). 	ag{24} \] Thus neither inserted marks nor localized windows are made intertwiners by the normalization. Formula (24) is a matrix identity, independent of any source formula for a nonintertwining mark. ## 4. Root Laurent algebra and the first meridian jet Use \(u=\Log M\) and define \[ \sigma=(-1)^{d(m+1)},\qquad J(e^u)= rac{R}{u}+J_0+uJ_1+O(u^2). 	ag{25} \] Here \(R\) is the residue matrix, not a crossing. The scalar \(a_N(e^u)\) is even and \(a_N(1)=\sigma N\). Expansion of (20) gives \[ H(e^u)^{-1} = rac{K_0-K_0^{-1}}{2\varepsilon mN\,u} + rac{K_0+K_0^{-1}}{2\varepsilon N}+O(u). \] Comparing the three first coefficients in (19) proves \[  oxed{ egin{split} R^2&=0,\ [R,J_0]&= rac{\sigma}{2\varepsilon m}(K_0-K_0^{-1})=:D,\ J_0^2-RJ_1-J_1R&= rac{\sigma}{2\varepsilon}(K_0+K_0^{-1}). \end{split}}	ag{26} \] These are identities of the actual finite matrices. All coefficients of \(J\) reverse the \(K_0\) weights, by (11). On any nonself pair \(U_\chi\oplus U_{\chi^{-1}}\), \(D\) is invertible and \(DR=-RD\). Thus \[ h=J_0D^{-1},\qquad Rh+hR=I 	ag{27} \] on this pair. This is an explicit contracting homotopy for the square-zero residue. In particular \(\ker R=\operatorname{im}R\) there and its rank is half the pair dimension. On self weights \(R=0\), and the constant identity in (26) instead makes \(J_0\) invertible. No norm bound for this homotopy is asserted. In particular the differences \(\chi-\chi^{-1}\) can approach zero as \(N\) varies. Nor is (27) an unqualified equivariant contraction. If \(B_\pm(e^u)=B_{\pm,0}+uB_{\pm,1}+O(u^2)\), the actual intertwining equation \(J(e^u)B_-(e^{-u})=B_+(e^u)J(e^u)\) gives exactly \[ RB_{-,0}=B_{+,0}R,\qquad J_0B_{-,0}-B_{+,0}J_0=B_{+,1}R+RB_{-,1}. 	ag{27a} \] Its finite part therefore retains the first normal rows. The contraction does not make the source zero. To see exactly what remains, write \[ B_-(e^u)=B_0+uB_1+	frac12u^2B_2+O(u^3). \] Also \[  rac{D_N(e^u)}{a_N(e^u)} =\sigma\left( rac{N}{D_N(e^u)}ight)^{m-1} =\sigma+O(u^2). 	ag{28} \] The product in (22) has no coefficient of \(u^{-2}\). Its finite trace, calculated before suppressing any normals, is \[ \operatorname{Tr}\left[ B_0(J_0^2-RJ_1-J_1R)+B_1[R,J_0]ight]. 	ag{29} \] Indeed the apparent second-derivative term is \(-	frac12\operatorname{Tr}(RB_2R) =-	frac12\operatorname{Tr}(R^2B_2)=0\). The other terms follow by multiplying (25); cyclicity gives the displayed orders. Inserting (26) into (23),(28),(29) yields \[  oxed{\displaystyle \Phi_0(W_ eta(1))=  rac1{2\varepsilon}\operatorname{Tr}((K_0+K_0^{-1})B_0) + rac1{2\varepsilon m}\operatorname{Tr}((K_0-K_0^{-1})B_1). }	ag{30} \] This is the original first-jet closing row, now assembled from the two opposite-polarization kernels. Here \(B_0,B_1\) initially belong to the reversed word. The actual half-twist conjugates it to the original word and its reduced matrix commutes with \(K_0\); cyclic trace, including its differentiated commutator, therefore gives the same row for \(B_+\). Equation (29) uses the full trace. On relative windows, neither \(R^2=0\) with intervening windows nor the trace cancellation of the \(B_2\) term can be assumed. Those terms stay in the unassembled meromorphic kernel. ### Exact integer-degree pairs The actual map (9) has a stronger grading property than its Cartan-weight reversal. Let \(U_k\) be the remaining occupation space with total integer degree \(k\), \(0\le k\le rd\). The map \(i_F\) inserts first occupation zero, \(\mathscr C\) changes total degree \(k\) to \(md-k\), and \(E_\Sigma^d\) lowers it by \(d\). Every term of \(S\) and \(S^{-1}\) preserves total degree, and \(p_0\) extracts degree zero in the first head. Therefore, exactly, \[ T(M)U_k\subset U_{rd-k},\qquad J(M)U_k\subset U_{rd-k}. 	ag{30a} \] The diagonal normalization in (17) does not change this rule. Generic invertibility in (13),(19) makes each indicated block an isomorphism, with the reflected block as its inverse up to the specified diagonal scalar. For an actual braid word, \(B_ eta\) preserves the integer degree: each original crossing preserves the sum of its occupations, and the quotient (4) preserves degree too. Define its exact finite sector trace by \[ t_k^ eta(M)=\operatorname{Tr}_{U_k}B_ eta(M). \] Equation (11), applied to the isomorphisms (30a), gives \(t_k^ eta(M)=t_{rd-k}^{ eta^{m rev}}(M^{-1})\) generically. The reduced half twist is also an actual degree-preserving invertible braid operator, so it removes the word reversal within each integer sector. Holomorphic continuation then proves the whole-meridian identities \[  oxed{\quad t_k^ eta(M)=t_{rd-k}^ eta(M^{-1}),\qquad \mathcal F_ eta(v,M) =v^{rd}\mathcal F_ eta(v^{-1},M^{-1}),\quad \mathcal F_ eta(v,M)=\sum_{k=0}^{rd}v^k t_k^ eta(M). \quad}	ag{30b} \] The last equality is a finite polynomial identity, continued at \(v=0\); it does not interpolate the integer index \(k\). At \(M=1\) the sector values agree and their first meridian derivatives are opposite. For a self sector \(k=rd/2\), the first derivative vanishes. This also refines the scalar closing bookkeeping to integer degree pairs. Put \(\chi_k=x_0^rQ^{-k}\), \(x_0=-q^{-1}\). Since \(d=N-1\), \(\chi_{rd-k}=\chi_k^{-1}\). Formula (21) is exactly the sum of the meromorphic scalar terms \[ \phi_k(M)=  rac{D_N(M)(M^m\chi_k-M^{-m}\chi_k^{-1})} {\varepsilon(M^{mN}-M^{-mN})}\,t_k^ eta(M). 	ag{30c} \] For \(k
e rd-k\), (30b) cancels the possible residue of \(\phi_k+\phi_{rd-k}\) within this pair. Expansion at one gives \[  oxed{\quad (\phi_k+\phi_{rd-k})(1)=  rac{\chi_k+\chi_k^{-1}}{\varepsilon}t_k^ eta(1) + rac{\chi_k-\chi_k^{-1}}{\varepsilon m} (t_k^ eta)'(1). \quad}	ag{30d} \] This remains valid if the two distinct integer sectors happen to have self-reciprocal Cartan weight. A self integer sector has \(\chi_k^2=1\), is counted once, and contributes \(\chi_k t_k^ eta(1)/\varepsilon\). These are removable scalar contributions of the actual reduced trace and its capped integer sectors. An individual \(U_k\) projector has not been lifted to an analytic original total-intertwiner projector through the root: the Casimir localizers in P distinguish only the Cartan weights modulo \(N\), and retain their collisions. No such lift, geometric Morse projector, angular cycle coefficient, or complex-index continuation follows from the finite graded reciprocity. The relative-window defects below remain. ## 5. Exact compact coherent convolution This section uses the original binomial head metric, without a new Fourier or Gaussian gauge. Let \[ X=(\mathbb P^1	imes\mathbb P^1)\setminus\{1+wz=0\},\quad \Gamma=\{w=v,\ z= ar v\},\quad 
u=- rac{dw\wedge dz}{2\pi i(1+wz)^2}. \] For a head set \[ c(z)_a= inom da z^a,\qquad v(w)_a=w^a,\qquad \Pi(w,z)= rac{c(z)v(w)}{(1+wz)^d}. 	ag{31} \] This is the same coherent projector as Z. It is a global matrix-valued function on \(X\). On \(r\) heads use tensor products and write \(
u^{[r]}\) for the ordered product. The elementary beta moments give \[ N^r\int_{\Gamma^r}\Pi\,
u^{[r]}=I,\qquad K_A(\mathbf w,\mathbf z)=v(\mathbf w)A c(\mathbf z). 	ag{32} \] For one head the moment is \(\int_\Gamma w^a inom db z^b(1+wz)^{-d}
u =\delta_{ab}/N\); tensor multiplication proves (32). The identity kernel is exactly \(\prod_i(1+w_i z_i)^d\). Every head occupation remains \(0,\ldots,d\). For three copies \(x_l=(\mathbf w_l,\mathbf z_l)\) of \(X^r\), with \(l=0,1,2\), put \[ \mathcal K(M;x_0,x_1,x_2)=  rac{D_N(M)}{a_N(M)} K_{J(M)}(\mathbf w_0,\mathbf z_1) K_{B_-(M^{-1})}(\mathbf w_1,\mathbf z_2) K_{J(M^{-1})}(\mathbf w_2,\mathbf z_0) \prod_{l=0}^2\prod_{i=1}^r \left[- rac{dw_{l,i}\wedge dz_{l,i}} {2\pi i(1+w_{l,i}z_{l,i})^{N+1}}ight]. 	ag{33} \] Then (23),(32) prove the exact original source period \[  oxed{\quad \Phi_0(W_ eta(M))= N^{3r}\int_{(\Gamma^r)^3}\mathcal K(M). \quad}	ag{34} \] The cyclic order of the three kernels is fixed. Every original crossing, Cartan factor, prefix endpoint, and external source line remains in the matrices defining them. Further resolutions expand \(B_-\), \(S\), or \(E_\Sigma^d\) into a finite word without altering (34). There is no replacement of a cap by an infinite series or of the pointed source by a normalized trace. On the compact cycle the incidence denominators stay nonzero. At each fixed \(N,m\) the form has a Laurent expansion in \(u\) with a finite principal part, smooth on that cycle. Thus finite part and integration commute. The original value is the integral of its full finite part. Its individual negative coefficients and all relative normal terms are retained. Equation (29) follows only after the complete resolutions have performed their contractions. The same formulas apply to a whole actual Casimir pair: its reduced projector is \(P_\chi+P_{\chi^{-1}}\), which commutes with \(T,J\) and the actual reduced word. This exact physical pair resolution is distinct from a local geometric phase window. ## 6. Relative windows and their boundary comparison Let \(\mathcal C\) be a compact oriented real \(2r\)-chain in \(X^r\), possibly with boundary, on which the displayed forms are defined. Its actual partial resolution is the matrix \[ P_{\mathcal C}=N^r\int_{\mathcal C}\Pi\,
u^{[r]}. 	ag{35} \] It need not be an idempotent. A restriction of (34) to three such chains is exactly \[  rac{D_N(M)}{a_N(M)} \operatorname{Tr} igl( P_{\mathcal C_0}J(M)P_{\mathcal C_1}B_-(M^{-1}) P_{\mathcal C_2}J(M^{-1}) igr). 	ag{36} \] This statement retains the full finite cap and factorial dual; it does not replace a chain by a symbolic point. The precise opposite-polarization comparison of two windows is \[ \mathcal D_{\mathcal C,\mathcal D}(M) =P_{\mathcal C}T(M)-T(M)P_{\mathcal D}. 	ag{37} \] For the full compact resolutions it is zero. For \(A_+=P_{\mathcal C}B_+(M)\) and \(A_-=P_{\mathcal D}B_-(M^{-1})\), (11) gives \(\Delta=\mathcal D_{\mathcal C,\mathcal D}B_-(M^{-1})\); (24) is therefore its exact source-sewing correction. In particular an assertion that the two local windows are transported into each other has this concrete finite row to pay. There is also an explicit boundary transgression. Suppose a compact homotopy \(\mathcal H:[0,1]	imes\mathcal C	o X^r\) avoids the incidence divisor. Orient its side as \([0,1]	imes\partial\mathcal C\). The matrix-valued form \(\Pi
u^{[r]}\) is a holomorphic top form, hence closed. Stokes gives \[ P_{\mathcal C_1}-P_{\mathcal C_0} =N^r\int_{[0,1]	imes\partial\mathcal C} \mathcal H^*(\Pi
u^{[r]}). 	ag{38} \] The sign is positive because \(\partial([0,1]	imes\mathcal C)= \mathcal C_1-\mathcal C_0-[0,1]	imes\partial\mathcal C\). Changing both windows in (37) consequently changes its defect by the first boundary matrix times \(T\), minus \(T\) times the second boundary matrix. All these statements hold meromorphically in \(M\) and coefficientwise in its normals. A noncompact homotopy additionally requires its end chains and their estimates; none is supplied by compact Stokes. If \(\Gamma^r=\mathcal C+\mathcal C^{m comp}\) as chains, then \(P_{\mathcal C^{m comp}}=I-P_{\mathcal C}\) exactly. Expanding each full resolution in (34) retains every complementary product in (36). There is no implicit removal of the other seven products after choosing three windows. Relative products can have a double meridian pole and their finite parts can contain second derivatives: the closed cancellations in (22),(29) do not remove them separately. This is an actual integral correspondence with a specified relative defect. It is not yet a pointwise map or a homology isomorphism between selected geometric relative cycles. ## 7. The geometric loxodromic argument remains a separate continuation The factorization (10) explains exactly which polarization change is implemented at the finite source level. The first turnover takes \(F_\Sigma=0\) to \(E_\Sigma=0\) on controlled classical charts, as Z records. The subsequent \(E_\Sigma^{N-1}\) and quotient are retained operators, not a presumed classical coordinate change of those cycles. Their full kernels occur in (33). No uniform large-\(N\) symbol for them is asserted here. For a scalar argument \(z\) on a compact loxodromic branch \(|z|>1+\delta\), the normalization has the exact formula \[ D_N(z)^{-1}=(z-z^{-1})z^{-N}(1-z^{-2N})^{-1}. 	ag{39} \] The last factor is \(1+O((1+\delta)^{-2N})\), with fixed derivatives bounded by the corresponding polynomial powers of \(N\). Thus the character \(-N\Log z\) and the nonzero factor \(z-z^{-1}\) remain. The reciprocal branch uses the same \(D_N\). This is a scalar statement; it neither evaluates \(J\)'s coherent kernel at a geometric point nor turns it into a unit-amplitude transport. All physical root weights \(\chi\) in (20) lie on the unit circle. A loxodromic geometric total-product eigenvalue is not one of those physical eigenvalues at \(M=1\). Continuing a source phase or a relative cycle to that argument still needs its actual analytic comparison. In particular neither (27) nor compact source equality makes the window defect (37) zero. Acyclicity of the polar residue does not cancel the secondary first-normal source (30), and does not prove addition or nonvanishing of two geometric contributions. The result is the explicit opposite-polarization operator (9), its source normalization (18), compact paired period (34), root normal algebra (26)--(30), and relative boundary row (37)--(38). These leave the geometric occurrence and relative-cycle estimates as identifiable additional work. ## Complete proof directs * R: notes/research_actual_reduced_braid_source.md, SHA256 9a472ef27b08305a519ff1f24b6d2b909e63a0acbdc49b3a29e001c52a2f2243. * P: notes/research_reduced_casimir_pair_localizer.md, SHA256 e5307ed7e424ba181db9b73f8473342a094ed85caf0b521b4aa965bb78e3c4ea. * Z: notes/research_central_resolvent_compact_source_symmetry.md, SHA256 cad44400a6c2af18972d363d6e69e61c72eb60b7499c43fba9545fe45f93ff9a. title: Opposite cyclic sources and the canonical Gram of an original Morse cut
text:
# Opposite cyclic sources and the canonical Gram of an original Morse cut 24 November 2026. Research proof. Earlier finals and manuscripts are unchanged. A fixed original one-cut knot diagram admits a cyclic-source presentation through every odd-width Morse slice. Dual turns use opposite sources; the total cyclic power consequently stays constant when a pair is born or dies. In the canonical averaged Grams, normalized literal cups are isometries, normalized ordinary caps are contractions, and actual crossings transport between the differently labeled Grams without a metric-conversion factor. The whole cut matrix remains the original one. These assertions retain the complete physical spaces. An ordinary cap is not declared the adjoint of its cup: their ordinary bubble is zero. The result does not lower-bound the knot scalar or its geometric part. ## 1. Fixed diagram, actual head, and signed sources Fix \(N\ge2\), and write \[ d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\quad x=-q^{-1}, \quad\gamma=x^N=(-1)^{N+1}. 	ag{1} \] The physical basis \(w_0,\ldots,w_d\) is orthonormal. At complete color use the regular E-semicyclic chart of [B]: \[  egin{split} K w_a&=xQ^{-a}w_a,\ E_\mu w_a&=(Q^{-a}-1)w_{a-1}\quad(a>0),& E_\mu w_0&=\mu w_d,\ Fw_a&=(1-Q^{a+1})w_{a+1}\quad(a<d),& Fw_d&=0 . \end{split} 	ag{2} \] Here \(E_\mu\) is [B]'s scaled generator \(\mathcal E\). The coproducts are \[ \Delta E=E\otimes K+I\otimes E,\quad \Delta F=F\otimes I+K^{-1}\otimes F,\quad \Delta K=K\otimes K. 	ag{3} \] The corresponding antipodes are \(S(E)=-EK^{-1}\), \(S(F)=-KF\), \(S(K)=K^{-1}\). Fix an original oriented \(1	o1\) Morse presentation \(\mathscr D\) of a knot, using the standard actual turns of [P]. Keep its original signed crossing matrices, common Cartan scalars, pivotal convention, framing and assigned external normalization lines. All internal deaths below are ordinary caps. The distinguished original marking is applied only to the completed one-cut operator. Choose \(|\mu|=1/N\). On a slice with \(b\) ordered heads set \[ 
u_i=\gamma^{i-1}\mu_i,\qquad 
u_i\in\{\mu,-\mu\}, \qquad \sum_{i=1}^b
u_i=\mu . 	ag{4} \] The signs are the orientations of the sliced strands, with the surviving cut strand assigned \(+\mu\). Thus every width \(b\) is odd. At a birth insert two opposite \(
u\)'s; at a death remove them. At a crossing the two \(
u\) labels exchange positions. This gives consistent labels along the fixed oriented diagram. Indeed [B, (8)] at \(x^N=\gamma\) gives, for either crossing sign, \[ (\mu_i,\mu_{i+1})\longmapsto (\gamma\mu_{i+1},\gamma\mu_i); \qquad(
u_i,
u_{i+1})\longmapsto(
u_{i+1},
u_i). 	ag{5} \] Use the genuinely changing-source finite crossings of [B, (7)] and their inverses, rather than the unchanged nilpotent crossing matrix. Their coefficients contain the actual \(E_{\mu_i}\), and they intertwine the total generators between the stated source fibers. All sources have modulus \(1/N\), at both parities. ## 2. The literal dual turns at opposite centers For clarity, duality in this E-chart is checked directly. On the ordinary linear dual, with action \(ho(S(h))^{\mathsf T}\), put \[ J_Ew_a=x^a w_{d-a}^*,\qquad \mu^\vee=-\gamma\mu. 	ag{6} \] This is an isomorphism \(V_{\mu^\vee}	o V_\mu^*\). The reversed inverse \(K\)-weight is \(x^{-1}Q^{d-a}=xQ^{-a}\). For \(a>0\), the dual \(E\)-coefficient after the change (6) is \[ -Q^{-a}(Q^a-1)=Q^{-a}-1. 	ag{7} \] The wrap sends \(w_d^*\) to \(-x^{-1}\mu w_0^*\); comparison with \(J_Ew_d=x^d w_0^*\) gives \(\mu^\vee=-x^{-N}\mu=-\gamma\mu\). Similarly the transposed \(-KF\) coefficient becomes \(1-Q^{a+1}\); its top arrow vanishes. This verifies all generators. In particular the different F-semicyclic frame of [R] is not silently used as the balanced E-chart matrix. The actual cup and ordinary cap in these coordinates are [P, Section 1] \[ p_{a,b}=N x^{a-d}\,\mathbf1_{a+b=d},\qquad \ell_{a,b}= rac{x^a}{N}\,\mathbf1_{a+b=d}. 	ag{8} \] Their full \(N,1/N\) factors and pivot phases are retained. Both oriented extrema have these same numerical matrices in the identified complete balanced frames. Indeed \(c_a=x^a\) in (6) and \(g_a=x^{-d}Q^{-a}\) give \(c_a^{-1}g_{d-a}^{-1}=x^{a-d}\) for the right cup and \(c_{d-a}g_a=x^a\) for the right cap. These use \(x^2Q=1\); the double-dual ratio \(c_a/c_{d-a}=g_a\) retains the actual pivot. For adjacent sources \(\mu_1,\mu_2\), these are Hopf intertwiners from or to the trivial module exactly when \[ \mu_2=-\gamma\mu_1 . 	ag{9} \] This is precisely the opposite-\(
u\) rule in (4), at any insertion position. Here is a direct check that includes the cyclic wall. At zero wraps the familiar identities \(E_{m pair}p=F_{m pair}p=0\), \(K_{m pair}p=p\) follow from \(x^2=Q^{-1}\) and \(Q^N=1\). For example the two contributions to the \(F\)-output \((a+1,d-a)\) are proportional to \(1-Q^{a+1}\) and \(Q^{a+1}-1\). The only new \(E\)-output is \[ E_{m pair}p =N(\gamma\mu_1+\mu_2)\,w_d\otimes w_d. 	ag{10} \] For the cap, its zero-wrap \(E\)-coefficient on an input \(a+b=N\) is \[  rac{x^a}{N} \{Q^{-b}(Q^{-a}-1)+(Q^{-b}-1)\}=0. 	ag{11} \] Its \(F\)-coefficient on \(a+b=N-2\) is proportional to \(1-Q^N\). The only added cyclic cap coefficient is \(\ell E_{m pair}|_{(0,0)}=(\gamma\mu_1+\mu_2)/N\). Also \(\ell K_{m pair}=\ell\). This proves (9) and its necessity. The physical norms, snakes and ordinary bubble are exactly \[ \|p\|^2=N^3,\qquad \|\ell\|^2=N^{-1},\qquad (I\otimes\ell)(p\otimes I)=I =(\ell\otimes I)(I\otimes p),\qquad \ell p=0 . 	ag{12} \] For each snake the matched coefficients multiply to one. For the bubble, their sum is \(x^{-d}\sum_a x^{2a}=0\). Thus no positive adjoint-cap convention has been substituted. ## 3. One common cyclic normalization through every width For a labeled odd slice let \[ E_\Sigma=\sum_{i=1}^b E_{\mu_i}K_{i+1}\cdots K_b,\qquad K_\Sigma=\prod_{i=1}^b K_i . 	ag{13} \] The root product gives \(E_{\mu_i}^N=\gamma N\mu_i I\). The summands in (13) \(Q\)-commute, so their mixed \(N\)-th multinomial coefficients vanish. Consequently \[ E_\Sigma^N =\gamma^bN\sum_i
u_i I=\gamma N\mu I=:cI, \qquad |c|=1. 	ag{14} \] Choose once and for all \(e^N=c\), and on every such slice define \[ T_{ oldsymbol
u}=E_\Sigma/e,\qquad T_{ oldsymbol
u}^N=I . 	ag{15} \] Births, deaths and both signed crossings intertwine these \(T\)'s. For a turn inserted inside other heads this follows from (3): the pair acts on its cup by \(K_{m pair}=1,E_{m pair}=0\), and the cap obeys the corresponding row equations. The earlier and later head terms therefore pass through unchanged. Crossing intertwining is the actual changing-source statement of [B]. No intermediate tail is required to have nonzero central power. If the first normalized label is \(+\mu\), its remaining even tail has \(E_{m tail}^N=0\). If it is \(-\mu\), that power is \(2cI\). Crossings can exchange these situations. Formula (15) remains valid in either case; no inverse of the tail coproduct or fusion-wall specialization is used. ## 4. Source preservation for the completed original cut Let \(\mathcal A_\mu(\mathscr D)\) be this literal fixed-diagram operator, with all original external factors restored. Its entire one-head matrix satisfies \[ \mathcal A_\mu(\mathscr D) =\mathcal A_0(\mathscr D) =K_N(\mathscr D)\,I . 	ag{16} \] The first equality has a direct degree proof extending [B, Section 5]. Give \(w_a\) integer degree \(a\), without reducing totals modulo \(N\). A birth (8) adds \(d\); an ordinary death removes \(d\). In a positive crossing term \(E_{\mu_1}^kF_2^k\), every ordinary lowering cancels one raising. Each cyclic \(E\)-wrap instead changes the total degree by an additional \(+N\). The diagonal Cartan and checked flip preserve the total. The actual negative crossing uses the finite inverse Euler series in [B, Section 4], evaluated in its recovered source fiber. It also has only \(E^kF^k\) terms with \(0\le k<N\); \(F\) has no wrap. Hence every source-dependent wrap in either sign contributes \(+N\), never \(-N\). Products of source labels may have signs, but do not alter this integer-degree accounting. A \(1	o1\) presentation has equally many births and deaths. If a matrix-entry path has \(r\) wraps, its output minus input degree is therefore \(rN\). Both degrees lie in \(\{0,\ldots,d\}\), forcing \(r=0\). All surviving entries are exactly the original nilpotent entries. This proves the first equality in (16), without changing an intermediate cap or testing an arbitrary marked sector. For the second equality, the completed original unmarked one-cut operator intertwines \(E_0,K\). The \(K\)-weights are distinct, so it is diagonal; every ordinary \(E_0\)-arrow is nonzero, so the diagonal entries agree. Its scalar, with the prescribed framing and external normalization, is the original selected value \(K_N\). The original final marking is applied to this completed matrix. This argument concerns a fixed Morse presentation. It does not infer a local crossing-through-cup identity from Hopf intertwining, define a new semicyclic ribbon invariant, or move a cap through an arbitrary exterior. No such move is needed for (16). ## 5. Exact averaged-Gram transport with all physical channels For each labeled slice define the actual canonical Gram \[ J_{ oldsymbol
u} =\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}(T_{ oldsymbol
u}^k)^* T_{ oldsymbol
u}^k . 	ag{17} \] As in [C], \(J_{ oldsymbol
u}\succeq I\), \(T_{ oldsymbol
u}^*J_{ oldsymbol
u}T_{ oldsymbol
u} =J_{ oldsymbol
u}\), and it commutes with the physical unitary \(K_\Sigma\). These facts need only (15), not the all-equal fixed line used for the sharp asymptotic in [C]. If \(A\) is any actual rectangular intertwiner \(T_{m out}A=AT_{m in}\), then \[ \|A v\|_{J_{m out}}^2 =\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\|A T_{m in}^kv\|_{m ph}^2 \le\|A\|_{m ph}^2\|v\|_{J_{m in}}^2 . 	ag{18} \] Thus \(\|A\|_{J_{m out}\leftarrow J_{m in}}\le\|A\|_{m ph}\). For an invertible crossing the same statement applies to its actual inverse between the reversed fibers. This is a comparison in different inherited Grams, not a fixed-metric unitarity claim. Let \(C\) insert the literal cup and \(B\) apply the ordinary cap, with identity operators on all other heads. Equations (12), (15) give the stronger exact cup identity and cap bound \[ C^*J_{m out}C=N^3J_{m in},\qquad B^*J_{m out}B\preceq N^{-1}J_{m in}. 	ag{19} \] The first follows by putting \(C^*C=N^3I\) inside the sum (17). The second is (18) with \(\|B\|_{m ph}=N^{-1/2}\). Hence \(C_{m iso}=N^{-3/2}C\) is an isometry and \(B_{m ctr}=N^{1/2}B\) is a contraction. The cap is neither asserted coisometric nor the Gram adjoint of that cup. If the fixed presentation has \(h\) births and \(h\) deaths, replacing its turns by \(C_{m iso},B_{m ctr}\) yields a normalized word \(\widetilde{\mathcal A}_\mu\) with the exact restoration \[ \mathcal A_\mu=N^h\widetilde{\mathcal A}_\mu . 	ag{20} \] In particular a normalized snake equals \(I/N\), not \(I\). For example (18)--(20) give the source-preserving upper estimate \[ |K_N(\mathscr D)|\le |\chi_N|\,N^h \prod_{	ext{crossings }v}\|R_{v,\mu}\|_{m ph}, 	ag{21} \] when \(\chi_N\) collects exactly the separately retained original scalar lines. No new estimate on the crossing product is asserted. ## 6. Scope and closest coverage The construction supplies a single source-compatible positive-metric system for a fixed original cut through variable odd widths. It retains every physical tensor coordinate. No multiplicity or normal direction is removed by a quotient or an eigenvalue-only Casimir specialization, and no cap-tree projection is inserted in a neighboring crossing. [R] already constructs oriented source duality and explains its degenerate fusion character. [S] already controls the original marked density in its complete fixed-width graph Gram. [A] already gives coisometric ordinary-cap tree packets after their specific factorial gauges. The additional statement here is the opposite-center E-source assignment through the fixed original Morse diagram, its full one-cut preservation, and the exact cross-width identities (18)--(20) in the canonical averaged Grams. The norm of the completed matrix in (16) is of course \(|K_N|\) in its one-head Gram. This is the existing scalarity identity, not a separately growing positive energy. The zero bubble in (12) explicitly prevents treating ordinary closure as a positive norm. No geometric boundary packet, nonzero marked overlap, lower bound for \(K_N\), or finite-exception volume theorem follows from these facts. Nothing here supplies off-root or quantum-normal estimates. ## Complete inputs and coverage All six complete matching texts were read. Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used.
