title: A full-matrix inequality for bilinear composition
text: # A full-matrix inequality for bilinear composition 22 November 2026. Research note; the public manuscripts remain frozen. A surjective bilinear tensor admits explicit affine lower bounds in the logarithms of arbitrary positive input and output metrics. The density matrices in these bounds belong to a specified spectral family. They are independent dual witnesses, rather than the actual marginals of a tensor after a common choice of gauges. The proof applies to the original anchored Conway multiplication, including every Hermite channel. It supplies local inequalities for the bounded-window certificate, but does not construct matching geometric densities or evaluate their constants at the volume scale. ## 1. Ordered densities All spaces are finite-dimensional complex Hilbert spaces. A density matrix is positive semidefinite with trace one. Say that a density \(\rho\) is ordered with a Hermitian matrix \(K\) if they have a common orthonormal eigenbasis in which \[ K=\operatorname{diag}(k_i),\qquad \rho=\operatorname{diag}(w_i),\qquad (w_i-w_j)(k_i-k_j)\ge0\quad\hbox{for all }i,j. \tag{1} \] Thus \([\rho,K]=0\) is required. Repeated eigenvalues cause no ambiguity: diagonalize \(\rho\) within each eigenspace of \(K\). Examples are the normalized identity, a normalized projection onto the largest eigenvalues, and \(\rho=e^{\alpha K}/\operatorname{tr}(e^{\alpha K})\) for \(\alpha\ge0\). More generally, a nonnegative nondecreasing function of \(K\), normalized to trace one, is allowed. An arbitrary density need not satisfy (1). Within a tied eigenspace (1) need not make \(\rho\) a scalar function of \(K\). We write \(\operatorname{tr}\), \(\|\cdot\|_{\rm op}\), and \(\|\cdot\|_{\rm HS}\) for trace, operator norm, and Hilbert--Schmidt norm. All matrix logarithms below are those of strictly positive matrices. ## 2. Logarithms and compression Scalar integration in a spectral basis gives the norm-convergent identity \[ \log B=\int_0^\infty \bigl\{(1+t)^{-1}I-(B+tI)^{-1}\bigr\}\,dt. \tag{2} \] Inversion reverses positive-matrix order, as follows by conjugating with a positive square root. Consequently (2) proves that \(0<B\le C\) implies \(\log B\le\log C\). No order-preservation assertion about exponentiation is needed. Let \(V:\mathcal K\to\mathcal H\) be a coisometry: \(VV^*=I_{\mathcal H}\). For \(B>0\), a Schur complement gives \[ V(B+tI)^{-1}V^*\ \ge\ (VBV^*+tI)^{-1}\quad(t\ge0). \tag{3} \] Indeed decompose \(\mathcal K=\operatorname{ran}V^*\oplus\ker V\). The left side is the upper block of the inverse of \(B+tI\), namely \((B_{11}+tI-B_{12}(B_{22}+tI)^{-1}B_{21})^{-1}\). The subtracted Schur correction is positive, so this is at least \((B_{11}+tI)^{-1}\). If \(\ker V=0\), equality holds directly. Integrating (3) in (2), with the constant terms cancelled and \(VV^*=I\), proves \[ \log(VBV^*)\ge V(\log B)V^*. \tag{4} \] The differences in these integrals converge in norm. ## 3. A positive factor and an ordered density **Lemma 1.** Let \(D=e^K>0\), and let \(\rho\) satisfy (1). For every \(B>0\), \[ \boxed{\quad \operatorname{tr}\{\rho\log(DBD)\} \ge \operatorname{tr}(\rho\log B) +2\operatorname{tr}(\rho K). \quad} \tag{5} \] **Proof.** Put \(B_s=e^{sK}Be^{sK}\) and \(R_{s,t}=(B_s+tI)^{-1}\). Differentiating (2), \[ \frac d{ds}\operatorname{tr}(\rho\log B_s) =\int_0^\infty \operatorname{tr}\{\rho R_{s,t}(KB_s+B_sK)R_{s,t}\}\,dt. \tag{6} \] In the common eigenbasis in (1), use \(B_sR_{s,t}=I-tR_{s,t}\) and \[ \int_0^\infty(R_{s,t}-tR_{s,t}^2)\,dt=I. \] The latter follows by scalar integration on the spectrum of \(B_s\). Subtracting \(2\operatorname{tr}(\rho K)\) from (6) gives \[ \begin{split} \frac d{ds}\operatorname{tr}(\rho\log B_s) -2\operatorname{tr}(\rho K) &=2\int_0^\infty t\sum_{i,j}w_i(k_i-k_j) |(R_{s,t})_{ij}|^2\,dt\\ &=\int_0^\infty t\sum_{i,j}(w_i-w_j)(k_i-k_j) |(R_{s,t})_{ij}|^2\,dt \ \ge0. \tag{7} \end{split} \] The second equality exchanges \(i,j\) in half the sum and uses Hermitian symmetry. The differentiations are justified uniformly for \(s\in[0,1]\): the positive matrices \(B_s\) have common positive lower and finite upper spectral bounds. In the last integral only off-diagonal terms matter. Near infinity they have \((R_{s,t})_{ij}=O(t^{-2})\), whereas near zero the resolvent is bounded. Thus the integrand is integrable. Integrating (7) from zero to one proves (5). \(\square\) For an invertible polar decomposition \(A=UD\), this also gives a unary bound. Put \(c=\|H_o^{1/2}AH_i^{-1/2}\|_{\rm op}^2\). The inequality \(DU^*H_oUD\le cH_i\), logarithmic order, and (5) give \[ \log\|H_o^{1/2}AH_i^{-1/2}\|_{\rm HS} \ge \operatorname{tr}(\rho\log D) +\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}(U\rho U^*\log H_o) -\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}(\rho\log H_i). \tag{8} \] Here \(\rho\) is ordered with \(\log D\). The rectangular result below does not require inserting a separate unary gate. ## 4. The original surjective binary tensor Let \(A:\mathcal H_1\otimes\mathcal H_2\to\mathcal H_o\) be surjective. Define \[ D=(AA^*)^{1/2}>0,\qquad V=D^{-1}A,\qquad VV^*=I. \tag{9} \] Choose a density \(\rho\) ordered with \(\log D\), and put \[ \omega=V^*\rho V,\qquad \rho_1=\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal H_2}\omega,\qquad \rho_2=\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal H_1}\omega,\qquad \beta=\operatorname{tr}(\rho\log D). \tag{10} \] Since \(VV^*=I\), \(\omega,\rho_1,\rho_2\) are densities. The joint density \(\omega\) can be entangled; no product-density replacement is made. **Theorem 2.** For arbitrary positive \(H_o,H_1,H_2\), \[ \boxed{\quad \log\|H_o^{1/2}A(H_1^{-1/2}\otimes H_2^{-1/2})\|_{\rm HS} \ge \beta+\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}(\rho\log H_o) -\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}(\rho_1\log H_1) -\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}(\rho_2\log H_2). \quad} \tag{11} \] **Proof.** Write \(X_i=\log H_i\), \(X=X_1\otimes I+I\otimes X_2\), and set \[ T=Ve^{-X}V^*>0,\qquad c=\|H_o^{1/2}DVe^{-X/2}\|_{\rm op}^2>0. \] The definition of \(c\) gives \(H_o^{1/2}DTD H_o^{1/2}\le cI\). Conjugating and inverting gives \[ DH_oD\le cT^{-1}. \tag{12} \] Use logarithmic order in (12), then trace against \(\rho\). Lemma 1 on the left, and (4) applied to \(e^{-X}\) on the right, give \[ \operatorname{tr}(\rho\log H_o)+2\beta \le \log c-\operatorname{tr}(\rho\log T) \le \log c+\operatorname{tr}(\rho VXV^*). \tag{13} \] The last trace equals \(\operatorname{tr}(\rho_1X_1)+\operatorname{tr}(\rho_2X_2)\). Since \(\log\|\cdot\|_{\rm HS}\ge\tfrac12\log c\), rearrangement proves (11). \(\square\) The metric matrices need not commute. Only the fixed calibration density is restricted by (1). For bilinear tree contractions, the output half-edge density is \(\rho\), and the dual input half-edge densities are \(\rho_1^{\mathsf T},\rho_2^{\mathsf T}\). The parent tensor uses \(H_i^{-\mathsf T/2}\) on its dual index; \(\operatorname{tr}(\rho_i^{\mathsf T}X_i^{\mathsf T}) =\operatorname{tr}(\rho_iX_i)\). ## 5. The full anchored Conway product For each integer \(N\ge2\), use the complete Newton coefficient space \[ H_N=\mathbb C[z]/(2T_N(z/2)+2) \] where \(T_N\) is the Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind. Use the actual normalized Newton basis \(b_i\), with coefficient vectors \(e_i=b_i\), and its Euclidean Hermitian norm. It retains all value and first-normal channels at repeated Casimir roots. Its actual multiplication \(M\) has unit \(b_0\), hence is surjective. The anchored compiler uses \[ \widehat H_N=\mathbb C e_\star\oplus H_N,\qquad \widehat M((a,u),(b,v))=(ab,M(u,v)). \tag{14} \] This is surjective because \(\widehat M((a,u),(1,b_0))=(a,u)\). Thus (9)--(11) apply to the literal tensor without changing a crossing leaf, a quarter-turn, or the original marked closing row. All original framing and peripheral scalars remain prescribed. Its covariance satisfies \[ \widehat M\widehat M^*=\operatorname{diag}(1,MM^*)\ge I. \tag{15} \] Indeed \(M(e_i\otimes e_0)=e_i=M(e_0\otimes e_i)\) in the orthonormal Newton basis. These input columns are distinct except at \(i=0\); their contribution gives \(MM^*\ge2I-e_0e_0^*\ge I\). Consequently every allowed \(\beta\) in (10) is nonnegative here. The densities in (10) are independent dual data. They need not be the actual reduced densities of any one gauged tensor. For example the whitened map \(V\), after Hilbert--Schmidt normalization, has actual output density \(I/\dim\widehat H_N\); this does not require choosing that density in (10). No physical channel has been projected away. There is also an explicit source-dependent change of reference that requires no unknown internal packet. At a literal crossing leaf put \(a_\pm=(1,R^{\pm1})\) and use the anchored shear \[ S_\pm(a,u)=(a,u-aR^{\pm1}),\qquad S_\pm a_\pm=e_\star,\qquad \|S_\pm\|_{\rm op},\ \|S_\pm^{-1}\|_{\rm op}\le1+\sqrt N. \tag{16} \] The bound follows from the shear formula and the exact Newton norm \(\|R^{\pm1}\|=\sqrt N\). Apply \(S_\pm^{-1}\) on the adjacent parent input to preserve the complete contraction. Each affected local logarithmic Hilbert--Schmidt norm changes by at most \(O(\log N)\); the new parent map remains surjective, so Theorem 2 applies to it. This is a known complex nonunitary reference change, rather than a unitary rephasing. The bound \(D\ge I\) in (15) concerns the original untransformed product, and is not asserted after this change. The shear neither constructs globally matched densities nor proves an upper volume rate. ## 6. Use on a fixed tree For the exact anchored source \(Y_N=(1,K_N)\), the three complete sources below give regularized minimizing metrics satisfying \[ \|\log H_e^*\|_{\rm op}\le R_N=O(N),\qquad \|Y_N\|\le\prod_v\|T_{v,N}\|_{H^*}\le2\|Y_N\|. \tag{17} \] One can take \(R_N=L_N(I)/\varepsilon+\log Z(I)\), where \(L_N=\sum_v\log\|T_{v,N}\|_H\), \(Z=1+\sum_e\operatorname{tr}(H_e+H_e^{-1})\), and \(\varepsilon=1/(512m^2)\) for a fixed tree with \(m\ge2\) vertices. For completeness, regularized stationarity gives total actual marginal mismatch \(S\le2\varepsilon\). The capacity comparison is \(\|Y_N\|/\prod_v\|T_v\|_{H^*} \ge1-4m\sqrt S-5mS>1/2\) at this value of \(\varepsilon\). Also \(L_N(H^*)\ge\log\|Y_N\|\ge0\); comparison of \(L_N+\varepsilon\log Z\) at \(H^*\) and \(I\) gives \(\log Z(H^*)\le R_N\). Each eigenvalue of \(H_e^*\) and its reciprocal is at most \(Z(H^*)\), proving the other part of (17). Use (11) at products and valid literal leaf, turn, and closing lower bounds on this window. Let \(\delta_{e,N}\) be the trace-norm mismatch between the child density and the transposed parent density. Summing at \(H^*\) and bounding each residual trace gives \[ \log\|Y_N\|\ge \sum_v\beta_{v,N}-\frac{R_N}{2}\sum_e\delta_{e,N}-\log2. \tag{18} \] Thus total density error \(o(1)\) costs \(o(N)\) in this logarithmic certificate on a fixed tree. This is not a complex-source error bound. Theorem 2 supplies an explicit valid family at the original product. It does not prove that this restricted family contains geometric data matching the actual leaves and closing with small error, or that its constants sum to the hyperbolic-volume rate. Source-adapted preconditioning may be needed. A separate full-metric upper trial is also required. No exact entropy dual or new volume theorem is asserted. ## Sources and coverage The matrix inequalities are proved above. These three entire sources supply the physical compiler and the tree comparison in Section 6. | Source | SHA-256 | |---|---| | [Full gauge capacity](research_scalar_tree_full_gauge_capacity.md) | 2997b732aa73e063c66e81d6487a1d9927509609d61842c1dbb43d9345df1d6d | | [Regularized capacity](research_regularized_actual_source_capacity.md) | 0cea0d52182eb24b4610538f354dbe5158fa54aa6f9cf7f9fc280c72ab090ff8 | | [Anchored physical compiler](research_anchored_conway_positive_variational_period.md) | e83c35d16c79faa13ac6556db78b9b57da2a2371d3fc04c4673ecd74e1d336f7 | The co-ordering trace inequality underlying (7) is a standard monotone-pair inequality: see Yanagi--Furuichi--Kuriyama, [Lemma II.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/quant-ph/0501152v2), and Furuichi--Kuriyama--Yanagi, [Lemma 1.5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1001.1384), which credits Bourin and Fujii. The compression inequality (4) is the logarithmic case of operator Jensen; see Hansen--Pedersen, [Theorem 2.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0204049). These definitions and statements were checked for coverage. They are not proof premises here, and no novelty claim about those inequalities is made. No mathematical program, numerical test, build, or manuscript edit was used for this proof.

title: Ordinary-orbit quantum jets reconstruct the complete source
text: # Ordinary-orbit quantum jets reconstruct the complete source Private written proof, 17 November 2026. Fix the original reduced, zero-framed knot source. Its complete value at level N is an explicit linear combination of quantum-normal jets of genuine finite colors in the noncomplete residue classes modulo N. The maximum normal order depends only on a fixed braid presentation, and the sum of the absolute coefficient weights is polynomial in N. The construction uses an omitted-node Hermite residue row and the actual integral-color restriction of the same all-root Verma source. No complete-color value or normal is supplied on the right side. The resulting row is complex and signed. It gives neither a lower bound for that row nor a nonzero geometric coefficient. ## 1. Source, normal paths, and a uniform Laurent width Fix a b-strand braid beta of length ell and writhe w, with one closed component and zero-framing normalization. Put \[ c=b-1-w\in2\mathbb Z,\quad D=N-1,\quad q_0=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q_0=q_0^2,\qquad N\ge2. \tag{1} \] Let F_N(M) be its actual reduced ADO source in [V]. By [C, (21)] and the root comparison it is even in M. Write \[ F_N(M)=f_N(M^2),\quad Y=M^2,\qquad K_N=f_N(1). \tag{2} \] The symmetric Alexander polynomial is denoted by Delta, with Delta(1)=1. All integer colors C_L(q) below are the original reduced, zero-framed colors, with unknot value one. Here is a support bound from the literal finite source. The two canceled checked entries of [V, (1.1)--(1.2)] are \[ \begin{split} R^+_{v+n,u-n;\,u,v} &=x^{-u-v+n}Q^{(u-n)v}{u\brack n}_Q (x^{-2}Q^{u-n};Q)_n,\\ R^-_{v-n,u+n;\,u,v} &=x^{u+v-n}Q^{-uv}{v\brack n}_Q (x^2Q^{1-v};Q)_n . \end{split} \tag{3} \] At the finite root head all input and output indices are between 0 and D. In the positive entry n<=u, and its x powers are \(-u-v+n-2h\), 0<=h<=n, lying in [-3D,0]. In the negative entry n<=v, and its powers \(u+v-n+2h\) lie in [0,3D]. The Gaussian coefficients and root chirps have no x dependence. The finite head numerator P in [V, Section 3] retains the scalar x^c. Its exact ordinary-pivot to ADO-pivot comparison is \[ P_{N,\beta}(x;1)=x^{Nc}F_N(-q_0x). \tag{4} \] Consequently F_N(-q0 x), rather than P itself, retains the overall power \(x^{-(N-1)c}\). Every exponent of this actual reduced source therefore has absolute value at most \((3\ell+|c|)(N-1)\). Evenness and the marked substitution \(x=-q_0^{-1}M\) give \[ \operatorname{supp} f_N\subset[-AN,AN],\qquad A=\max\!\left(1,\left\lceil\frac{3\ell+|c|}{2}\right\rceil\right). \tag{5} \] The support interval is deliberately generous and valid at every N>=2. No degree estimate for a different knot invariant is used. The full ADO normalization, if required, is still exactly \[ \mathcal N_N(M) =i^{N+3}\frac{M^{N-1}}{S_N(M^2)}f_N(M^2),\qquad S_N(Y)=1+Y+\cdots+Y^{N-1}. \tag{6} \] Our target is the reduced complete value (2). Neither the phase, the monomial in (6), nor the distinction between the full and reduced sources is absorbed into an unspecified scalar. ## 2. The omitted-complete-node residue row Fix once and for all \[ H=4A+1. \tag{7} \] Then \(H(N-1)>2AN\) for every N>=2. Define \[ \omega_N(Y)= \frac{Y^{AN}f_N(Y)}{(Y-1)S_N(Y)^H}\,dY =\frac{Y^{AN}(Y-1)^{H-1}f_N(Y)} {(Y^N-1)^H}\,dY. \tag{8} \] The factor Y^{AN} clears all Laurent powers. Its numerator in the first expression has degree at most 2AN, whereas the denominator has degree \(1+H(N-1)\ge2AN+2\). Thus (8) has no pole at zero and has zero residue at infinity. Its residue at Y=1 is K_N/N^H. Every other pole lies at \(\zeta_L=Q_0^L\), \(1\le L<N\), and has order at most H. The residue theorem proves the exact source identity \[ K_N=-N^H\sum_{L=1}^{N-1} \operatorname{Res}_{Y=\zeta_L}\omega_N. \tag{9} \] Only the ordinary nodes occur on the right side. We make every coefficient in this Hermite row explicit. Set \[ \mathscr E_N=\frac1N Y\partial_Y,\qquad \Psi_{A,H,N}(t;\zeta)= e^{At}\zeta e^{t/N}(\zeta e^{t/N}-1)^{H-1} \left(\frac{t}{e^t-1}\right)^H,\qquad b_{h,N}(\zeta)=[t^h]\Psi_{A,H,N}(t;\zeta). \tag{10} \] The removable value at t=0 is retained. In the local coordinate \(Y=\zeta e^{t/N}\) one has \(\zeta^{AN}=1\), \(Y^N=e^t\), and \[ \omega_N=\frac1N t^{-H}\Psi_{A,H,N}(t;\zeta) f_N(\zeta e^{t/N})\,dt . \] Expanding the last factor by its actual Euler derivatives gives \[ K_N=-N^{H-1}\sum_{L=1}^{N-1}\sum_{a=0}^{H-1} \frac{b_{H-1-a,N}(\zeta_L)}{a!} (\mathscr E_N^a f_N)(\zeta_L). \tag{11} \] This formula includes all normals through H-1. There is a uniform coefficient bound with no root-spacing loss. For |t|=1, \[ \left|\frac{e^t-1}{t}-1\right| \le\sum_{j=2}^\infty\frac1{j!}=e-2<1. \] The last strict inequality follows, for example, by bounding the factorial tail geometrically. Cauchy's coefficient estimate gives \[ |b_{h,N}(\zeta)|\le B_{A,H}:= e^{A+1/2}(1+e^{1/2})^{H-1}(3-e)^{-H}, \quad |\zeta|=1,\quad N\ge2,\quad h\ge0. \tag{12} \] Thus the total absolute row weight in (11) is at most \(eB_{A,H}N^H\). In ordinary derivative coordinates, the coefficient of \(f_N^{(r)}(\zeta_L)\) is \(O_{A,H}(N^{H-1-r})\). Indeed induction gives \((Y\partial_Y)^a=\sum_{r=0}^a s_{a,r}Y^r\partial_Y^r\) with fixed integer coefficients; only a>=r contributes and each term in (11) contains N^{-a}. This also shows directly why nearby ordinary nodes cause no inverse-distance blowup in this row. ## 3. The exact high-color quantum-normal adapter Use the fixed root-normal coordinate \[ \delta=1-q^{2N},\qquad q(\delta)=q_0(1-\delta)^{1/(2N)}. \tag{13} \] The formal fixed-Y completion proved in [C, (25a)--(26)] satisfies \[ \mathcal W_N(\delta,Y)=\sum_{j\ge0}\delta^j W_{j,N}(Y), \qquad W_{0,N}(Y)=g_N(Y):=\frac{f_N(Y)}{\Delta(Y^N)}. \tag{14} \] Its coefficients are rational in Y, with poles only at zero, infinity, and the Alexander divisor. They are regular at every \(\zeta_L\). This statement concerns the specified formal completion, not an assumed convergent quantum series. For \(1\le L<N\), h>=0 and r>=0 put \[ J_{h,L,N}(r)=[\delta^h]C_{L+rN}(q(\delta)). \tag{15} \] The ANY-positive-color quotient in [C, Section 6] retains every intermediate index and the ordinary pivot before root restriction. Together with the natural meridian \(Y=q^2x^2\), it gives exactly \[ C_{L+rN}(q(\delta)) =\mathcal W_N\!\left( \delta,\zeta_L(1-\delta)^{r+L/N}\right). \tag{16} \] The equality is one of formal delta germs. Its evaluation of the auxiliary grading at one is legitimate: at the corresponding root x=q0^{L-1} up to sign, the deleted classical compression is nilpotent, so its determinant is identically one in the grading, as proved in [C, (23)]. There is no independently frozen root pivot or identification of fixed-Y normals with integral-color normals. Let \(E=Y\partial_Y\) and \(\eta=\log(1-\delta)\). Expanding the right side of (16) yields \[ \sum_{a,d\ge0}\delta^a \frac{(r+L/N)^d\eta^d}{d!} (E^dW_{a,N})(\zeta_L). \tag{17} \] At order h only a+d<=h occurs. Hence J_{h,L,N}(r) is a polynomial in r of degree at most h, for every r>=0. Its leading coefficient is \((-1)^h(E^h g_N)(\zeta_L)/h!\). The elementary h-th finite difference therefore gives \[ B_{h,L,N}:=\sum_{r=0}^h(-1)^r\binom hr J_{h,L,N}(r) =(E^h g_N)(\zeta_L). \tag{18} \] For h=0 this is the original ordinary-color value. The sign in (18) includes the leading coefficient of log(1-delta); no parity character remains in the squared-meridian coordinate. Retain the entire Alexander factor by defining \[ \alpha_s=\left.(Z\partial_Z)^s\Delta(Z)\right|_{Z=1}, \qquad \alpha_0=1. \] Since \(\zeta_L^N=1\), the ordinary product rule gives exactly \[ (\mathscr E_N^a f_N)(\zeta_L) =\sum_{h=0}^a\binom ah N^{-h}\alpha_{a-h}B_{h,L,N}. \tag{19} \] In particular neither the denominator in (14) nor its higher normal derivatives have been replaced just by Delta(1). ## 4. Explicit reconstruction from genuine finite-color jets Combining (11), (18), and (19) proves \[ K_N=\sum_{L=1}^{N-1}\sum_{h=0}^{H-1}\sum_{r=0}^h w_{L,h,r,N}J_{h,L,N}(r), \tag{20} \] where every weight is specified by \[ w_{L,h,r,N} =-(-1)^r\binom hr N^{H-1-h} \sum_{a=h}^{H-1} \frac{b_{H-1-a,N}(\zeta_L)}{a!} \binom ah\alpha_{a-h}. \tag{21} \] The source quantities on the right use only the colors \[ 1\le L<N,\qquad 0\le r\le h\le H-1,\qquad L+rN\le HN-1. \tag{22} \] No color is divisible by N. In particular no complete-color value or quantum normal is input to this reconstruction. For r>=1, these are genuine high colors in ordinary residue classes; they are not the bounded ordinary colors strictly below N. All row weights are polynomially controlled. Put \[ A_{\Delta,H}=\sum_{s=0}^{H-1}\frac{|\alpha_s|}{s!}. \] Using \(\binom ah/a!=1/(h!(a-h)!)\), (12) gives \[ |w_{L,h,r,N}| \le B_{A,H}A_{\Delta,H}\frac{\binom hr}{h!} N^{H-1-h}, \tag{23} \] and consequently \[ \begin{split} \sum_{L=1}^{N-1}\sum_{r=0}^h |w_{L,h,r,N}| &\le B_{A,H}A_{\Delta,H}\frac{2^h}{h!}N^{H-h},\\ \sum_{L,h,r}|w_{L,h,r,N}| &\le e^2B_{A,H}A_{\Delta,H}N^H. \tag{24} \end{split} \] The maximum derivative order H-1 is fixed with the presentation. The coefficient bounds hold at every N>=2 and for all its ordinary residue classes, without primality assumptions. Equations (20)--(24) are an exact original-source reconstruction with an explicit polynomially bounded row. They do not claim a polynomially conditioned inverse for all the supplied data, which contain redundancy, or a positive representation of the scalar. ## 5. What the existing positive norm does and does not provide For comparison, [P, Sections 1--3] already proves \[ f_N(\zeta_L)=C_L(q_0),\qquad |C_L(q_0)|\le D_N:=\sin(\pi/N)^{1-b} \le(N/2)^{b-1},\quad 1\le L<N. \tag{25} \] Its exact positive cyclic norm is \[ \mathcal H_N=\frac1N\sum_{Y^N=1}|f_N(Y)|^2 =\frac{|K_N|^2}{N} +\frac1N\sum_{L=1}^{N-1}|C_L(q_0)|^2. \tag{26} \] Thus a positive exponential estimate for that specified norm would control K_N, but such an estimate is not supplied by positivity. The h=0 portion of (20) has a polynomial bound by (24)--(25). Higher h involve the actual normal data (15). The ordinary-color positive trace bounds do not bound these transverse quantum jets or the high colors with r>=1. In particular (20) alone cannot turn those positive bounds into a lower bound for K_N: its weights are signed and complex, and the identities retain cancellation. The all-root coefficient upper estimates are also not a lower bound for this selected row. No analytic summation theorem is used in (16)--(20), because fixed-order restrictions are exact formal identities of the genuine finite sources. ## 6. Coverage, scope, and complete proof sources [P] already contains ordinary-node interpolation with S_N to the first power, the regular quotient, actual ordinary-color bounds, and the positive Fourier norm (26). Full-orbit Fourier/Hermite sampling and bounded meridian jets have also been studied in the existing notes. The present calculation specifically omits the complete node, chooses a fixed higher S_N power from the literal Laurent width, and replaces every required meridian normal by the finite differences of actual quantum-normal data in (18). Derivative recovery of nonsemisimple knot invariants and recovery of ADO data from the colored-Jones family have literature coverage: [Murakami, arXiv:1406.1287](https://arxiv.org/abs/1406.1287) states a derivative relation for logarithmic invariants, and [Willetts, arXiv:2003.09854](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.09854) states a unification determining root ADO data from the colored family. These are statement-level coverage only, not proof premises. No broad novelty is asserted for derivative recovery or Hermite interpolation. The complete proof directs are: | Label | Complete source | SHA256 | |---|---|---| | V | notes/frobenius_verma_period.md | b11489368e7ac1106c7a5e760154b0713dfbc7eaf9b76193438df57b48041a90 | | C | notes/research_all_root_verma_normal_rationality.md | 46e984e3ce5491ff82a18da6914d89a0e42393fd7e66877dc679190e69b125f6 | | P | notes/regularized_kashaev_period.md | d7efc1e6e2995a0bff7553553e044f8554e559e51cdf8515d8048e2f603b94fc | V supplies the literal entries, finite head source, and exact pivot/framing normalization (3)--(6). C supplies evenness, the canonical natural-meridian completion and its actual integral-color restrictions, including regularity at every ordinary orbit point. P supplies only the original ordinary-color identities and bounds and the positive-norm comparison in Section 5. The Laurent width, omitted-node residue, explicit coefficients, finite-difference adapter, and weight bounds are proved above by written arguments. No mathematical programs, tests, or numerical cases are used.

title: Almost-invariant original vectors and their marked observations
text: # Almost-invariant original vectors and their marked observations An almost-invariant vector can give a lower bound for a specified source if its observation at the original closing row is also controlled. The finite Newton representation makes that requirement quite explicit. It has genuine geometric Casimir quasimodes whose overlaps with both original cap directions are exponentially small. For the forced three-crossing operator there is an exact adjoint quasimode whose endpoint overlap loses precisely the entire gain from its small residual. There is also a natural self-adjoint form of the adjacent three-crossing problem. Its inertia is known exactly, and the closing scalar is an off-diagonal Green entry. Thus this change of form retains the original source without turning it into a positive norm. All statements below concern the full original finite algebra, including first normals at double roots. They do not contradict unitarity of the different ordinary-color representations. ## 1. Original operators and the unitarization obstruction Fix \(N\ge2\), \(D=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\). Use the original normalized Newton basis of \[ {\cal A}_N=\mathbb C[z]/(2T_N(z/2)+2). \] Write \(C\) for multiplication by \(z\), \(M\) for the original positive crossing, and \(J\) for index reversal. Their exact relations include \[ \begin{split} (Cv)_j&=c_jv_j-d_jv_{j-1},\\ c_j&=2\cos((2j+1)\pi/N),\qquad d_j=4\sin^2(\pi j/N),\\ J^2&=I,\qquad C^\dagger=JCJ,\qquad M^\dagger JM=J . \end{split} \tag{1} \] The missing lower-end term is zero. These are identities on the entire original quotient. The positive Newton inner product is the ordinary coefficient inner product. The two original cap observations are \[ e_0^\dagger\mathbf f=f(c_0),\qquad e_D^\dagger\mathbf f=\phi_N(f). \tag{2} \] Both rows have norm one. The first is the original turned cap, equivalently evaluation at the first physical Casimir node; the second is the unturned closing functional. The crossing is not unitary for a different positive inner product. At a double root \(c_j\), its restriction to the original two-dimensional local algebra is \[ M_j=\lambda_j(I+K_j),\qquad K_j^2=0,\quad K_j\ne0, \qquad |\lambda_j|=1 . \tag{3} \] For example, in the basis \(1,\epsilon\), with \(\epsilon=z-c_j\), its nonzero nilpotent entry is \[ \frac{R'(c_j)}{R(c_j)} =\frac{i(D-2j)}{4\sin((2j+1)\pi/N)} . \tag{4} \] The pair \(j=0,D\) is double and has nonzero entry at every \(N\ge2\). Formula (4), including its original normalization, is proved in [the arbitrary-power compilation](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_arbitrary_power_source_compilation.md), Section 6. If \(H>0\) satisfied \(M^\dagger HM=H\), then \(H^{1/2}MH^{-1/2}\) would be unitary and hence diagonalizable. This contradicts (3). The same argument excludes making \(C\) self-adjoint while retaining its double-root Jordan blocks. There is a more precise conclusion for an actual positive average of crossing transports. **Proposition 1.** Let \(G_1,\ldots,G_r\) be original invertible word matrices with \(|\det G_i|=1\), with positive weights summing to one. Suppose the list contains \(M\). The completely positive average \[ {\cal P}(\rho)=\sum_i p_iG_i\rho G_i^\dagger \tag{5} \] has no positive definite stationary trace metric: there is no \(H>0\) satisfying \({\cal P}^\dagger(H)=H\). In particular this applies to the symmetric average of \(M,M^{-1},J\). **Proof.** Put \(A_i=H^{-1/2}G_i^\dagger HG_iH^{-1/2}\). Each \(A_i>0\), \(\det A_i=1\), and \(\sum p_iA_i=I\). The arithmetic-geometric mean inequality for its eigenvalues gives \(\operatorname{tr}A_i\ge N\), with equality only at \(A_i=I\). Taking traces of the average forces equality for every \(i\). In particular \(M^\dagger HM=H\), which (3) excludes. \(\square\) This does not exclude a Perron rescaling, a degenerate stationary form, or a different source-adapted unitary operator. Such a change must retain its scaling and the original test row; (5) is not already a trace-preserving quantum channel in a faithful positive metric. Even the simplest symmetric crossing average retains the normal obstruction explicitly. On the invariant local plane (3), use any positive inner product and its adjoint. Its restriction to positive matrices is \[ \tfrac12\{M_j\rho M_j^\dagger+ M_j^{-1}\rho M_j^{-\dagger}\} =\rho+K_j\rho K_j^\dagger. \tag{6} \] The added map is nonzero and square-zero. Its \(m\)-th iterate is \(\rho+mK_j\rho K_j^\dagger\). Thus this actual positive average has a Jordan direction at eigenvalue one, rather than a mixing gap to a stationary projector. Passing to the semisimple quotient would remove precisely that original normal direction. ## 2. A geometric quasimode invisible to the original caps Fix \(k\ge2\), and let \[ \alpha_N=M^{2k}e_0,\qquad a_N=\alpha_N/\|\alpha_N\|_2. \tag{7} \] The reflected volume theorem and the fixed-insertion theorem give \[ \begin{split} \|(C-z_k)a_N\|_2&\longrightarrow0,\\ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\|\alpha_N\|_2 &=\frac{V_k}{4\pi}>0, \end{split} \tag{8} \] where \(z_k=-2\cos t_k\) is the actual geometric core value and \(V_k\) is the volume of the original closed reflected knot. See [the Casimir insertion theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_even_reflected_casimir_insertions.md) and [the reflected volume theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_reflected_even_kashaev_volume_theorem.md). **Theorem 2.** The actual geometric quasimodes (7) satisfy \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log|e_0^\dagger a_N| =-\frac{V_k}{4\pi}. \tag{9} \] For every fixed polynomial \(P\), \[ \limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N \log|e_D^\dagger P(C)a_N| \le-\frac{V_k}{4\pi}, \tag{10} \] where a zero value has logarithm \(-\infty\). The same upper bound holds at the first cap. **Proof.** The original crossing is lower triangular and \(M_{00}=\kappa\), \(|\kappa|=1\). Thus \[ e_0^\dagger\alpha_N=\kappa^{2k}. \tag{11} \] This and (8) prove (9). Moreover \[ e_0^\dagger P(C)\alpha_N=P(c_0)\kappa^{2k}, \tag{12} \] because the first row of \(C\) is \(c_0e_0^\dagger\). Fixed polynomials are bounded on \(c_0\in[-2,2]\). For the other cap retain the actual backward channel of [the even-run endpoint theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_even_run_backward_source_growth.md): \[ \alpha_{N,j}=\kappa^{2k}e_k^Tu_j,\qquad g_h=S_h^2u_{D-h},\qquad g_0=u_D,\quad g_h=H_{N-h}g_{h-1}. \tag{13} \] Here \(\|u_D\|=O_k(N^{3/2})\) is the proved original endpoint estimate, and \(\|H_j\|\le4\). For each fixed integer \(h\ge0\), \[ S_h^2\asymp_h N^{-2h},\qquad |\alpha_{N,D-h}|=O_{k,h}(N^{2h+3/2}). \tag{14} \] If \(m=\deg P\), the last row of \(P(C)\) uses only indices \(D-m,\ldots,D\), and its norm is bounded independently of \(N\) since \(\|C\|\le6\). Equations (13)--(14) therefore make \(e_D^\dagger P(C)\alpha_N\) polynomially bounded in \(N\). Divide by (8) to obtain (10). \(\square\) This is an original source vector and an original geometric approximate eigenvalue. The small overlaps are not obtained by choosing an artificial orthogonal test row. In particular any fixed collection of Casimir observations at the first cap has the exact observation Gram matrix \[ \sum_{\ell=0}^{m}(C^\dagger)^\ell e_0e_0^\dagger C^\ell =\left(\sum_{\ell=0}^{m}|c_0|^{2\ell}\right)e_0e_0^\dagger. \tag{15} \] It cannot provide full-space coercivity. The same example already exists on the doubled positive space. Put \(\rho_N=a_Na_N^\dagger\), and use the actual Casimir transport \[ {\cal C}_{z_k}(\rho) =|z_k|^{-2}C\rho C^\dagger. \tag{16} \] If \(\epsilon_N=\|(C-z_k)a_N\|\), then \[ \|{\cal C}_{z_k}(\rho_N)-\rho_N\|_1 \le\frac{2\epsilon_N}{|z_k|} +\frac{\epsilon_N^2}{|z_k|^2} \longrightarrow0. \tag{17} \] This follows by expanding the two rank-one products; \(\|xy^\dagger\|_1=\|x\|\|y\|\). Nevertheless \[ \operatorname{tr}(e_0e_0^\dagger\rho_N) =\exp\{-NV_k/(2\pi)+o(N)\}. \tag{18} \] Map (16) is completely positive; it has not been asserted to preserve trace or to possess a mixing gap. Doubling preserves positivity but does not repair the specified observation. ## 3. The exact adjoint test for a forced boundary source For an invertible original operator \(A_N\) and its specified source \[ A_Nf_N=\zeta_N e_D,\qquad |\zeta_N|=1, \tag{19} \] every trial vector \(v\) gives \[ \boxed{\quad \|f_N\|\ge \frac{|v_D|}{\|A_N^\dagger v\|}. \quad} \tag{20} \] Indeed \(\zeta_N\overline{v_D} =\langle A_N^\dagger v,f_N\rangle\). For normalized trials, an exponentially small adjoint residual is useful only after comparing its rate with that of \(v_D\). The original free polynomial is \(F_N(w)=\mathbf e(w)^Tf_N\), where \(\mathbf e(w)=(e_0(w),\ldots,e_D(w))^T\) is the full Newton evaluation column. If \[ A_N^\dagger v=\overline{\mathbf e(w)}+r_N, \] then the exact identity and its useful lower bound are \[ \begin{split} F_N(w)&=\zeta_N\overline{v_D}-\langle r_N,f_N\rangle,\\ |F_N(w)|&\ge |v_D|-\|r_N\|\,\|f_N\|. \end{split} \tag{21} \] Thus a dual approximate solution can prove the specified lower bound without positive unitarization. It must retain the actual endpoint observation and make the residual smaller than that observation after multiplication by a proved upper bound for \(\|f_N\|\). The following exact original operator shows why the residual alone is insufficient. Put \[ T=C-q\mathsf X,\qquad \mathsf X=\operatorname{diag}(Q^j),\qquad h_j=q^{j(j+2)}S_j^2. \tag{22} \] The exact three-crossing equation gives \[ Th=q^{-1}e_0,\qquad T^\dagger=JTJ. \tag{23} \] For \(v=Jh/\|h\|\), therefore, \[ \|T^\dagger v\|=\frac1{\|h\|},\qquad |v_D|=\frac1{\|h\|}. \tag{24} \] These are exponentially small: the uniform sine-factorial estimate, with \(\mathcal J(x)=\int_0^x\log(2\sin\pi s)\,ds\), gives \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\|h\| =2\max_{0\le x\le1}\mathcal J(x) =2\mathcal J(5/6)>0 . \tag{25} \] The bound (20) for the endpoint-forced equation \(Tx=e_D\) is exactly one. That is sharp: \[ x=q^{-1}e_D,\qquad \|x\|=1. \tag{26} \] Indeed \(T\) is lower bidiagonal and \(T_{DD}=q\). This does not replace the original adjacent-pair operator by \(T\); it demonstrates, within its actual original factor, the exact loss from the wrong endpoint overlap. ## 4. The natural self-adjoint form of the adjacent pair For the actual pendant \(JM^3JM^3e_0\), retain the exact factorization from [the boundary-current theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_three_crossing_boundary_current.md): \[ A_N=B S T S^{-1},\qquad S=JM^3J,\qquad A_Nf_N=\zeta_Ne_D,\qquad \det A_N=-(-1)^D. \tag{27} \] Here \(f_N=JM^3JM^3e_0\), \(\kappa=\exp(\pi iD^2/(2N))\), and \(\zeta_N=(-1)^D\kappa^2q^{-1}\). Here \(T\) is (22), and the original upper bidiagonal matrix \(B\) has \[ B_{jj}=-qQ^j,\qquad B_{j,j+1}=1-Q^{j+1}. \tag{28} \] All absent entries are zero. In particular \[ B^\dagger=JBJ,\qquad S^\dagger=JS^{-1}J . \tag{29} \] **Theorem 3.** The original matrix \[ H_N=A_NBJ \tag{30} \] is Hermitian and invertible, with inertia \[ (n_+,n_-,n_0) =(\lfloor N/2\rfloor,\lceil N/2\rceil,0). \tag{31} \] The unturned original closing scalar is exactly \[ \phi_N(F_N)=(f_N)_D =-\zeta_Nq^{-1}e_0^\dagger H_N^{-1}e_D. \tag{32} \] The full free-boundary source is \[ F_N(w)=\zeta_N\mathbf e(w)^T BJH_N^{-1}e_D . \tag{32a} \] **Proof.** Relations (23), (27), and (29) give the exact congruence \[ H_N=(BS)(TJ)(BS)^\dagger. \tag{33} \] Since \(T^\dagger=JTJ\), the middle matrix is Hermitian. It remains invertible if its strictly lower diagonal is multiplied by any \(\lambda\in[0,1]\): before multiplying by \(J\) the matrix is triangular, with unchanged nonzero diagonal \(q^{-1}Q^{-j}\). The relation \(T_\lambda^\dagger=JT_\lambda J\) also persists. Thus the inertia stays constant along this path. At \(\lambda=0\), paired indices \(j,D-j\) give Hermitian blocks with zero diagonal and conjugate off-diagonal entries of modulus one. Each has eigenvalues \(1,-1\). If \(N\) is odd, the unpaired central entry is \(q^{-1}Q^{-(N-1)/2}=q^{-N}=-1\). This proves the inertia of \(TJ\), and (33) gives the same inertia for \(H_N\). Finally \(A_N^{-1}=BJH_N^{-1}\), and the last row of \(B\) is \(-q^{-1}e_D^\dagger\). Applying this to (19) proves (32); applying the complete Newton evaluation row gives (32a). \(\square\) The Hermitian matrix in (30) is built from the original finite source operators. No geometric projector has been substituted. Its fixed inertia precludes a positive-energy interpretation of its inverse. Formula (32) is an off-diagonal Green entry; it can involve cancellations between positive and negative spectral subspaces. For this turned pendant, its particular unturned cap is already simple: \[ (f_N)_D=\kappa^3(M^3e_0)_D. \] This follows from the first row of \(M^3\). Its endpoint asymptotic is known. It must not be confused with the unresolved retained-boundary value \(F_N(-2)\), whose actual Green formula is (32a). That formula has a boundary-dependent left observation, not a matching positive quadratic observation. For the negative pendant, conjugate the original matrices and source, as in the boundary-current theorem. The congruence, inertia and conjugated closing identity hold with that same convention. ## 5. What remains to obtain a lower bound The rational geometric curve of the adjacent \((-3,-3)\) pendant is now identified with its original peripheral germ in [the geometric branch theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_three_crossing_pendant_geometric_branch.md). That identifies a candidate phase for a local adjoint construction. It does not supply an adjoint vector with exponentially accurate residual and a controlled overlap at row \(D\). The end rows, the repeated-root directions and the phase through the intervening indices still have to be matched. Equations (20)--(21) state a precise sufficient target. A local frozen-symbol root or a first-order bulk approximation does not yet verify it. The sharp counterexamples (9) and (24) show that the overlap condition cannot be omitted even for actual geometric or exponentially accurate original quasimodes. The reflected Stein equation remains a useful positive special case: its observation Gram matrix has the proved polynomial lower bound in [the original Stein-energy theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_reflected_laurent_stein_energy.md). There the source itself is the matching nonnegative observation sum. The retained adjacent-pair boundary value (32a) has a different observation, which that theorem does not estimate. ## 6. Focused finite replay [The original-matrix checker](../experiments/check_original_almost_invariance_observation.py) constructs \(A_N\) from its band entries and independently constructs the literal source from \(M,J\). At levels \(2,\ldots,10\), for both crossing signs, it compares the Hermitian congruence, inertia, endpoint equations, and the complete Green formula (32a), including first normals. The boundary tests include \(-2\), a nonreal point and the repeated physical node \(c_0\). It also checks the exact residual/overlap equality in (24) and the norm-one solution (26). [The saved 100-digit record](../repro/results/research-original-almost-invariance-observation.json) retains the script, note and original-matrix dependency hashes. An independent output can be selected with \(\texttt{--output}\). The finite eigenvalue checks are diagnostics; the all-level inertia is the nonsingular Hermitian-path proof in Theorem 3. No source-asymptotic rate or uniform spectral gap is inferred from these computations.

title: Exact original before, active and after transfer
status: Exact original four-state identity; both parities
text: # Exact original before, active and after transfer 31 October 2026. An exact source identity: no asymptotic branch is selected and no unused row is deleted. Put \(N\ge3\), \(d=N-1\), \(m=\lfloor N/2\rfloor\), \(M=m-1\), and \(\sigma=-2\cos(2\pi\delta)\). Define \[ c_r=2\cos\frac{(2r+1)\pi}{N},\qquad \alpha_r=c_r-\sigma,\qquad s_r=2\sin\frac{\pi r}{N}, \quad A=x+y,\quad P=xy, \] \[ \beta_r=s_r^2,\qquad \gamma_r=s_rs_{r-1}\alpha_{r-1},\qquad A_{\mathrm{rest}}^\alpha=\prod_{r=m}^{d}\alpha_r. \] At \(r=0,1\), set \(\gamma_r=0\); these are the original absent negative-row term and the factor \(s_0=0\). All products retain level \(N\). ## 1. The exact original polynomial The [original one-sided coefficient expansion](../papers/casimir-source-asymptotics/README.md) has the sign-adjusted form \[ (-1)^dH_{V,\mathrm{LEFT}} =A_{\mathrm{rest}}^\alpha \sum_{0\le i\le j\le M} b^i c^{d-j} \prod_{r<i}\alpha_r\prod_{j<r\le M}\alpha_r\,K_{i,j}, \tag{1} \] where \(K_{i,i}=1\), \(K_{i,i+1}=\beta_{i+1}A\), and \[ K_{i,j}=\beta_j A K_{i,j-1}+\gamma_jP K_{i,j-2}. \] The raw resolvent sign is independent of the endpoints. The path sign \((-1)^{j-i}\), followed by changing the \(d-j+i\) outside factors from \(\sigma-c_r\) to \(-\alpha_r\), gives exactly \((-1)^d\). Set \(B_{-1}=1\) and \(R_{-1}=R_{-2}=Z_{-1}=0\). For \(0\le r\le M\), let \[ \begin{aligned} B_r&=b\alpha_r B_{r-1},\\ R_r&=B_{r-1}+\beta_r A R_{r-1}+\gamma_r P R_{r-2},\\ Z_r&=R_r+c\alpha_rZ_{r-1}. \end{aligned}\tag{2} \] Induction, first on the last active step and then on the last inactive step, gives \[ B_r=\prod_{u=0}^{r}b\alpha_u,\qquad R_r=\sum_{i=0}^{r}b^i\prod_{u<i}\alpha_u\,K_{i,r}, \] \[ Z_r=\sum_{0\le i\le j\le r} b^ic^{r-j}\prod_{u<i}\alpha_u\prod_{j<u\le r}\alpha_u\,K_{i,j}. \] In particular the diagonal \(i=j\) is retained, and \[ \boxed{(-1)^dH_{V,\mathrm{LEFT}} =A_{\mathrm{rest}}^\alpha c^{d-M}Z_M.}\tag{3} \] For the full numerator, the original path expansion runs over \(0\le i\le j\le d\). Take \(M=d\) and the empty omitted-half product \(A_{\mathrm{rest}}^\alpha=1\). The same induction gives \((-1)^dH_V=Z_d\), with every unused diagonal factor still present. The half-grid scalar formula in §3 is specific to the half-row restriction. ## 2. Four literal states Equations (2) are the polynomial transfer \[ \begin{pmatrix}B_r\\R_r\\R_{r-1}\\Z_r\end{pmatrix} =T_r\begin{pmatrix}B_{r-1}\\R_{r-1}\\R_{r-2}\\Z_{r-1}\end{pmatrix}, \qquad T_r=\begin{pmatrix} b\alpha_r&0&0&0\\ 1&\beta_rA&\gamma_rP&0\\ 0&1&0&0\\ 1&\beta_rA&\gamma_rP&c\alpha_r \end{pmatrix}. \tag{4} \] The initial vector is \((1,0,0,0)^T\). The direct before-to-after entry \(1\) accounts for starting and ending at the same row. There is no denominator at the initial rows or a sampled spectral zero. The diagonal blocks are the before scalar \(b\alpha_r\), the original active companion \[ C_r=\begin{pmatrix}\beta_rA&\gamma_rP\\1&0\end{pmatrix}, \] and the after scalar \(c\alpha_r\). Reversing the block order makes (4) upper triangular. On a strict compact row and spectral chart its active eigenvalues have limits \[ \Lambda_\pm(t)=2s\left[As\pm \sqrt{s^2(x-y)^2+4xy\cos^2(\pi\delta)}\right], \qquad s=\sin(\pi t). \tag{5} \] For positive \(x,y\), \(0<t<1/2\), and \(0<\delta<1/2\), the positive root is separated from the other root. The latter can vanish at the pole and must not be inverted. On the post-pole side \(\alpha(t)<0\), the after scalar is negative for positive \(c\), so it is separated from \(\Lambda_+\) even where their moduli coincide. The phase change \(c\mapsto-c\) can restore resonance. This identifies a possible input to the [analytic switching theorem](research_analytic_switching_suppression.md). It alone does not prove suppression where a genuine eigenvalue crossing remains, and separation from the secondary eigenvalue must also be checked. ## 3. The omitted-half scalar stays exact For the product convention \(\alpha_r=c_r-\sigma\), \[ A_{\mathrm{rest}}^\alpha= \begin{cases} 2\cos(N\pi\delta),&N\text{ even},\\ -4\sin(\pi\delta)\sin(N\pi\delta),&N\text{ odd}. \end{cases}\tag{6} \] The exact product definition fixes the signs, which would differ in the alternative \(\sigma-c_r\) convention. The odd central factor is included. Neither scalar is assumed nonzero; its oscillatory modes stay in (3). RIGHT follows by the literal original row reflection and middle interchange. A full-source application must still retain the original shared targets, half-twist and framing characters, and Fourier endpoint currents. An absolute-switch maximum with no actual eigenvalue resonance is only a candidate for suppression: a boundary-branch gap and a uniform analytic gauge estimate are additional hypotheses. No global source bound is claimed. The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_research_original_four_state_transfer.py) and its [results](../experiments/research_original_four_state_transfer_results.json) check the finite transfer against the independent start/end expansion at both parities and the exact scalar modes: 10 levels, 49 spectral values, 196 transfer/path comparisons and 85 scalar-mode identities. The original matrix interface is inherited from the local numerator formula; these checks are not advertised as a new independent audit of the physical matrix.

title: The original pivotal source in the canonical coproduct Gram
text: # The original pivotal source in the canonical coproduct Gram 24 November 2026. Research proof. Earlier finals and manuscripts are unchanged. The complete cyclic-source coproduct has an explicit spectral graph frame. In that frame the original marked pivotal source is a specified resolvent of the remaining coproduct, followed by its original pivot. Its inherited graph Gram makes this density polynomially bounded, together with its inverse. Consequently the unchanged original co-source has polynomial dual norm in the sharp canonical coproduct Gram of [C]. No comparison between two unestimated metrics is used. The density is generally complex and has trace zero when there is a tail. These are source and norm identities, not positivity of the original scalar trace or a geometric noncancellation theorem. ## 1. Actual transported words and fixed root data Fix \(b\ge1\), independently of \(N\ge2\), and put \[ d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\quad \gamma=(-1)^{N+1},\quad x=-q^{-1},\qquad \alpha_a=Q^{-a}-1,\quad A_a=\prod_{h=1}^a\alpha_h,\quad A_0=1. \tag{1} \] The original physical head basis \(w_0,\ldots,w_d\) is orthonormal. Use [B]'s regular E-semicyclic complete-color chart and its fixed line: \[ E_iw_a=\alpha_aw_{a-1}\ (a>0),\quad E_iw_0=\mu_iw_d,\quad K_iw_a=xQ^{-a}w_a,\qquad |\mu|=1/N,\quad \mu_i=\gamma^{1-i}\mu . \tag{2} \] The actual coproduct, in the convention of [M], is \[ E_\Sigma=\sum_{i=1}^b E_iK_{i+1}\cdots K_b,\qquad K_\Sigma=\prod_{i=1}^bK_i,\qquad E_\Sigma^N=bcI,\quad c=\gamma^bN\mu,\quad |c|=1. \tag{3} \] The last identity is proved in [C] by the root quantum multinomial; it includes even and composite levels and every cyclic wrap. An actual braid word below means the genuinely transported operator \(W_\mu\) in [B], with every crossing's finite \(\mu\)-dependence and original common Cartan scalar retained. On the fixed line it commutes with \(E_\Sigma,K_\Sigma\). It is not the unchanged nilpotent-head matrix \(W_0\), which need not commute with (2). [B, Section 5] identifies the completed one-cut operator of \(W_\mu\) with the original one. Its pivot, framing, whole meridian line and assigned external dimension factors remain unchanged. Write the physical space as \(\mathcal V=\mathcal V_1\otimes\mathcal V_{\rm t}\). On the tail put \[ B=E_{\rm t}=\sum_{i=2}^bE_iK_{i+1}\cdots K_b,\quad K_{\rm t}=\prod_{i=2}^bK_i,\quad g_{\rm t}=K_{\rm t}^{\,1-N}. \tag{4} \] Thus \(E_\Sigma=E_1K_{\rm t}+B\), \(B^N=(b-1)cI\), and \(K_{\rm t}B=QB K_{\rm t}\). For \(b=1\), the tail is \(\mathbb C\), with \(B=0\) and \(K_{\rm t}=g_{\rm t}=I\). In the physical metric, \[ K_{\rm t}^N=\gamma^{b-1}I,\qquad g_{\rm t}=\gamma^{b-1}K_{\rm t},\qquad g_{\rm t}Bg_{\rm t}^{-1}=QB . \tag{5} \] Both \(K_{\rm t}\) and \(g_{\rm t}\) are unitary. The original marked pivotal functional from [R] is exactly \[ D_{\rm cut}=P_0\otimes g_{\rm t},\quad P_0=|w_0\rangle\langle w_0|,\qquad t_b(W_\mu)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathcal V}(D_{\rm cut}W_\mu). \tag{6} \] Any existing exterior scalar multiplies (6) as before. Nothing here changes an invariant or asserts an identity for arbitrary inserted exteriors that fail the stated intertwining conditions. ## 2. The source density and its quantitative statement Choose \(e^N=bc\), set \(T=E_\Sigma/e\), and let \(\lambda=eQ^j\), \(0\le j<N\). Define \[ \Pi_\lambda=\frac1N\sum_{k=0}^d\lambda^{-k}E_\Sigma^k,\quad Z=B/\lambda,\quad \mathcal P_a(Z)=(Z;Q)_a=\prod_{h=0}^{a-1}(I-Q^hZ). \tag{7} \] These are the actual spectral projectors and finite polynomials. Since \(Z^N=(b-1)I/b\), one has \(\mathcal P_N(Z)=I/b\), and \(I-Z\) is invertible. Let \(\pi_0:\mathcal V\to\mathcal V_{\rm t}\) extract first color zero, and \(\iota_0f=w_0\otimes f\). Define the specified graph map by \[ L_\lambda f=\sum_{a=0}^d w_a\otimes L_{\lambda,a}f,\qquad L_{\lambda,a}=\frac{\lambda^a}{A_a} K_{\rm t}^{-a}\mathcal P_a(Z). \tag{8} \] Its inherited physical Gram is explicitly \[ G_\lambda=L_\lambda^*L_\lambda =\sum_{a=0}^d w_a^{(\lambda)}\mathcal P_a(Z)^*\mathcal P_a(Z), \qquad w_a^{(\lambda)}=\frac{|\lambda|^{2a}}{s_a^2},\quad s_a=|A_a|=\prod_{h=1}^a2\sin(\pi h/N). \tag{9} \] Here \(s_0=1\), and the scalar weights \(w_a^{(\lambda)}\) are distinct from the physical vectors \(w_a\). Stars in (8)--(9) use the specified physical metrics. In particular \(G_\lambda\succeq I\). For an endomorphism \(F\) of the tail, write \(\|F\|_{G_\lambda}\) for its operator norm in this Gram. **Theorem.** The map \(L_\lambda\) is a bijection from the complete tail onto \(\ker(E_\Sigma-\lambda)\), with inverse \(\pi_0\). For \(W_\lambda=\pi_0W_\mu L_\lambda\), the original source is \[ t_b(W_\mu)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathcal V_{\rm t}} (R_\lambda W_\lambda),\qquad R_\lambda=\sum_{k=0}^d\lambda^{-k}B^k g_{\rm t} =\frac1b(I-Z)^{-1}g_{\rm t}. \tag{10} \] Put \(\rho_{b,N}=b^{-1+1/N}\). The inherited, rather than a freely substituted, graph Gram satisfies the two-sided inequality \[ \boxed{\quad \frac{\rho_{b,N}^2}{4}G_\lambda \preceq R_\lambda^*G_\lambda R_\lambda \preceq N^2\rho_{b,N}^2G_\lambda . \quad} \tag{11} \] Thus \(\|R_\lambda\|_{G_\lambda}\le N\rho_{b,N}\) and \(\|R_\lambda^{-1}\|_{G_\lambda}\le2/\rho_{b,N}\). For the canonical Gram of [C] and the actual invariant source set \[ J_{\rm av}=\sum_{k=0}^d(T^k)^*T^k,\qquad D_{\rm inv}=\frac1N\sum_{k=0}^d T^kD_{\rm cut}T^{-k}. \tag{12} \] The subscript inv means invariant, not inverse. Then \[ \boxed{\quad \|D_{\rm inv}\|_{J_{\rm av}}\le\rho_{b,N},\qquad \|D_{\rm inv}^{-1}\|_{J_{\rm av}}\le2N/\rho_{b,N}. \quad} \tag{13} \] Its operator condition number is at most \(2N\), independently of \(b\). This is the condition of the source operator, not the condition number of \(J_{\rm av}\) relative to the physical metric. With the unnormalized Hilbert--Schmidt norm in \(J_{\rm av}\), \[ \boxed{\quad |t_b(W_\mu)|\le \rho_{b,N}N^{b/2}\|W_\mu\|_{{\rm HS},J_{\rm av}}. \quad} \tag{14} \] All finite identities and inequalities hold at every \(N\ge2\). More generally their linear-algebraic statements apply to matrices commuting with both \(E_\Sigma,K_\Sigma\); the identification with the original knot source uses the actual transported word above. ## 3. The complete eigenspace is the specified graph For \(v=\sum_a w_a\otimes v_a\), its eigenvalue equation gives \[ \alpha_{a+1}K_{\rm t}v_{a+1}=(\lambda-B)v_a \quad(0\le a<d),\qquad \mu K_{\rm t}v_0=(\lambda-B)v_d. \tag{15} \] The first recurrence and \(BK_{\rm t}^{-1}=QK_{\rm t}^{-1}B\) give (8), starting from the arbitrary vector \(v_0=f\). The final equation also holds, including its wrap. Indeed \[ (\lambda-B)L_{\lambda,d} =\frac{K_{\rm t}^{-d}}{A_d} \prod_{h=0}^d(\lambda-Q^hB) =\frac{cK_{\rm t}^{-d}}{\gamma N} =\mu K_{\rm t}. \tag{16} \] Here \(A_d=\gamma N\), \(K_{\rm t}^{-d}=\gamma^{b-1}K_{\rm t}\), and \(\lambda^N-B^N=cI\). This proves the last equality with its exact sign, at both parities. Conversely (15) determines every component from \(v_0\), proving the bijection and its inverse. The map retains all \(N^{b-1}\) tail coordinates. It does not specialize a total or intermediate Casimir to its nodal values. Their full matrices, including any Jordan channels, remain in the induced word \(W_\lambda\). ## 4. Compressing the original marked pivotal source For \(0\le k<N\), the quantum multinomial for \(E_\Sigma^k\) has the exact zeroth-head block \[ \pi_0E_\Sigma^k\iota_0=B^k. \tag{17} \] An allocation using the first-head lowering operator \(u\) times can return first color zero only if \(u\equiv0\pmod N\). Its range \(0\le u\le k<N\) forces \(u=0\). Thus the pure tail term, with coefficient one, is the only surviving allocation. This argument includes every permitted cyclic wrap. Since \(D_{\rm cut}L_\lambda=\iota_0g_{\rm t}\), the compressed source on this eigenspace, in the graph coordinates, is exactly \[ \pi_0\Pi_\lambda D_{\rm cut}L_\lambda =\frac1N\sum_{k=0}^d\lambda^{-k}B^kg_{\rm t} =R_\lambda/N. \tag{18} \] The finite geometric sum uses \((I-Z)\sum_{k=0}^dZ^k=I-Z^N=I/b\), proving the resolvent in (10). It also fixes its forcing: \((I-Z)R_\lambda=g_{\rm t}/b\). No homogeneous solution or unknown knot value is chosen. The matrices \(W_\mu,D_{\rm cut}\) commute with \(K_\Sigma\). Conjugation by \(K_\Sigma\) cycles the spectral projectors, \(K_\Sigma\Pi_\lambda K_\Sigma^{-1}=\Pi_{\lambda/Q}\). Therefore all \(N\) sector traces \(\operatorname{Tr}(D_{\rm cut}W_\mu\Pi_\lambda)\) are equal. Summing them and using (18) proves (10), including its factor \(N\). The induced word is the entire restriction, not an intermediate projection: \(W_\mu L_\lambda=L_\lambda W_\lambda\). ## 5. Exact Gram compensation by a shifted finite Pochhammer The inherited Gram (9) follows directly from (8), since \(K_{\rm t}\) is physically unitary and \(|A_a|=s_a\). The relation \(g_{\rm t}Zg_{\rm t}^{-1}=QZ\) and \(\mathcal P_N(Z)=I/b\) give the exact ordered identities \[ R_\lambda=g_{\rm t}\mathcal P_d(Z),\qquad \mathcal P_a(Z)R_\lambda =b^{-1}g_{\rm t}\mathcal P_{a-1}(Z)\quad(1\le a\le d). \tag{19} \] For the first, use \((I-Z)^{-1}=b\mathcal P_d(QZ)\). For the second, cancel the first factor of \(\mathcal P_a(Z)\) against \(I-Z\), then move \(g_{\rm t}\) to the left. This order retains the original pivot and is essential. Taking squared norms in (19), with \(g_{\rm t}^*g_{\rm t}=I\), gives \[ R_\lambda^*G_\lambda R_\lambda =b^{-2}\sum_{a=1}^d w_a^{(\lambda)} \mathcal P_{a-1}(Z)^*\mathcal P_{a-1}(Z) +\mathcal P_d(Z)^*\mathcal P_d(Z). \tag{20} \] The zeroth term of (9) has weight one; it becomes the last term displayed here. Thus no endpoint term has been dropped. Compare the coefficient of each positive summand in (20) with (9). For \(0\le a<d\) the ratio is \[ \frac{w_{a+1}^{(\lambda)}}{b^2w_a^{(\lambda)}} =\frac{\rho_{b,N}^2}{|1-Q^{a+1}|^2}, \qquad \frac1{w_d^{(\lambda)}}=N^2\rho_{b,N}^2. \tag{21} \] The last identity uses \(s_d=N\) and \(|\lambda|=b^{1/N}\). The elementary bounds \(4/N\le|1-Q^\ell|\le2\), \(0<\ell<N\), place every ratio between \(\rho_{b,N}^2/4\) and \(N^2\rho_{b,N}^2\). For the lower sine bound, reflect \(\ell\) to \(\min(\ell,N-\ell)\) and use concavity \(\sin v\ge2v/\pi\) on \([0,\pi/2]\). Positivity of all summands proves (11). Invertibility follows already from (10); (11) then proves both operator norm bounds without a comparison to the tail's flat metric. ## 6. The unchanged whole source in the sharp canonical Gram By [C], the spectral sectors are orthogonal for \(J_{\rm av}\), and \[ J_{\rm av}=N\sum_\lambda\Pi_\lambda^*\Pi_\lambda,\qquad L_\lambda^*J_{\rm av}L_\lambda=NG_\lambda. \tag{22} \] The second identity uses \(\Pi_{\lambda'}L_\lambda=\delta_{\lambda',\lambda}L_\lambda\). Thus the graph metric used above is precisely the restriction of the known canonical Gram, up to its stated scalar \(N\). Finite cyclic averaging gives \(D_{\rm inv}=\sum_\lambda\Pi_\lambda D_{\rm cut}\Pi_\lambda\). Its block in each graph frame is \(R_\lambda/N\), by (18). Taking the maximum of the block norms in the orthogonal sum (22) proves (13) and the condition-number bound. If \(W_\mu\) commutes with \(T\), cyclicity of the ordinary trace gives \[ \operatorname{Tr}(D_{\rm cut}W_\mu) =\operatorname{Tr}(D_{\rm inv}W_\mu). \tag{23} \] In a \(J_{\rm av}\)-orthonormal basis the ordinary matrix trace is unchanged. Its Hilbert--Schmidt Cauchy inequality and \(\dim\mathcal V=N^b\) give \[ |\operatorname{Tr}(D_{\rm inv}W_\mu)| \le\|D_{\rm inv}\|_{{\rm HS},J_{\rm av}} \|W_\mu\|_{{\rm HS},J_{\rm av}} \le\rho_{b,N}N^{b/2}\|W_\mu\|_{{\rm HS},J_{\rm av}}, \tag{24} \] as claimed. An assigned external scalar line multiplies both sides. For \(b=1\) the formulas give \(R_\lambda=I\) on the scalar tail and \(D_{\rm inv}=I/N\); all assertions include this case. For \(b\ge2\), each tail contains a pivot of trace zero. Equation (10) with \(W_\mu=I\) and cyclic averaging therefore give \(\operatorname{Tr}R_\lambda=\operatorname{Tr}D_{\rm inv} =\operatorname{Tr}D_{\rm cut}=0\). The invariant density is invertible but not a positive trace density. The reflection obstruction [R] is therefore not contradicted. ## 7. Quantitative scope and closest coverage The sharp theorem [C] computes the exponential physical conditioning of \(J_{\rm av}\). The present proof adds polynomial original co-source control in that same Gram. Its compensation is the exact identity (20), including its final term, rather than permission to ignore the graph frame. Indeed \(G_\lambda\) need not be polynomially equivalent to the physical tail metric. [S] already factors genuine braided source charts into total and multiplicity operators, and [M] already gives complete multiplicity reductions with original caps and Jordan data. [P] constructs positive source Grams from specified terminal packets. The new assertion here is the explicit density (10) and the two-sided bounds (11)--(14) in the inherited canonical coproduct Gram, at arbitrary fixed width. Every actual fixed short-filled braid component can retain its genuine transported crossings in these identities; no sign or word-length condition has been introduced. They do not bound the resulting word energy by a geometric partition or compare it with hyperbolic volume. A trace may cancel even for an invertible, well-conditioned density. The norm bounds are at the complete roots; no uniform off-root derivative estimate is asserted. No positive scalar trace, nonzero geometric cycle coefficient, source relative precision, or finite-exception volume theorem follows here. ## Complete inputs and coverage All six complete matching texts were read. Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used. title: A positive matrix recursion for the original Conway source
text: # A positive matrix recursion for the original Conway source 22 November 2026. Research note. Frozen manuscripts and earlier final notes remain unchanged. The full Conway source has a positive representation which requires no minimization. At each proper vertex of its expression tree, add a small orthogonal error space. Contract the original maps and their adjoints, keeping their complete Gram matrices. The resulting scalar differs from the squared original invariant by a prescribed, uniformly bounded additive error. This construction uses the actual closing functional and the full repeated-root boundary algebra. It gives local positive-matrix lower and upper certificates. Their hyperbolic-volume rate is not evaluated here. ## 1. The normalized original tree Use the complete normalized compiler in the [convex source theorem](research_convex_normalized_conway_source.md). There is a fixed finite rooted expression tree. Its proper vertices are leaves, unary linear maps, or binary complex-bilinear maps. The root is the prescribed original complex-linear closing row. At level \(N\ge2\), each proper boundary space is the entire \[ H_N=\mathbb C[\zeta]/(2T_N(\zeta/2)+2)\cong\mathbb C^N, \tag{1} \] with its declared Newton coefficient Hermitian metric. Here \(T_N\) is the Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind. Value and derivative directions at repeated roots both remain in this space. All adjoints below are in this fixed metric. Let \(b_v=16\max(1,\|T_v\|_{\rm HS})\) be the known local budgets, including the root budget, and put \[ B_N=\prod_v b_v,\qquad \sigma=\frac1{16}. \tag{2} \] The coefficients of every local tensor \(T_v\) are prescribed by the original construction. In particular \(B_N\ge1\) is known without evaluating the closed invariant. After dividing each tensor by its own budget, write its leaf vector as \(a_v\), its unary map as \(A_v\), its bilinear map as \(M_v\), and its original closing row as \(L\). Each has norm at most \(\sigma\); for a bilinear map this means \[ \|M_v(u,w)\|\le\sigma\|u\|\,\|w\|. \tag{3} \] The normalized true packets, also denoted \(a_v\), obey \[ a_v=A_va_c\quad\hbox{or}\quad a_v=M_v(a_l,a_r),\qquad \|a_v\|\le\sigma,\qquad La_{\rm top}=K_N/B_N. \tag{4} \] At a leaf \(a_v\) is prescribed; at other vertices (4) defines it. The invariant \(K_N\) is the original reduced Kashaev invariant with the recorded marking, phases and framing normalization. It is not an input to the construction below. An expression is a literal tree: distinct child occurrences have disjoint sets of descendants. Repeated equal-looking subexpressions are kept as separate occurrences. For a bilinear map, the same letter \(M_v\) denotes its linearization from \(H_N\otimes H_N\) to \(H_N\). For Hermitian matrices, \(U\preceq V\) means that \(V-U\) is positive semidefinite. ## 2. The deterministic matrix recursion For any real \(\varepsilon>0\), define matrices from the leaves upward: \[ \begin{array}{ll} S_v=a_va_v^*+\varepsilon I, &v\ \hbox{a leaf},\\[2mm] S_v=A_vS_cA_v^*+\varepsilon I, &v\ \hbox{unary},\\[2mm] S_v=M_v(S_l\otimes S_r)M_v^*+\varepsilon I, &v\ \hbox{binary}. \end{array} \tag{5} \] All matrices in (5) are \(N\)-by-\(N\) and strictly positive definite. The binary operation is positive and order preserving in either matrix argument with the other held positive. Equivalently, one applies the positive linear map \(U\mapsto M_vUM_v^*\) to the tensor-product input. Joint linearity in the two matrices is not asserted. Retain the actual root row and set \[ F_N(\varepsilon)=B_N^2 L S_{\rm top}(\varepsilon)L^*. \tag{6} \] Equations (2), (5), and (6) prescribe this number entirely by local source data. No true internal packet from (4), except the prescribed leaf vectors, is needed to evaluate (5). **Theorem.** Fix \(0<\theta\le1\), and choose \[ \varepsilon_N=\frac{\theta}{N B_N^2}, \qquad P_N=1+F_N(\varepsilon_N). \tag{7} \] For every level and every such normalized tree, \[ \boxed{\qquad 0\le F_N(\varepsilon_N)-|K_N|^2\le\frac{\theta}{128}, \qquad 1+|K_N|^2\le P_N\le1+|K_N|^2+\frac{\theta}{128}. \qquad} \tag{8} \] The bounds include exact zeros. They hold for both level parities and composite levels because they use the full compiler, not a distinct-root quotient. ## 3. Orthogonality and the error bound Here is a finite Fourier interpretation and proof. At each proper vertex take an independent variable \(\omega_v\), uniform on \(\mathbb Z/(N+1)\). Let \(\chi_j(\omega)=\exp(2\pi i j\omega/(N+1))\), and choose an orthonormal basis \(e_1,\ldots,e_N\) of \(H_N\). Define \[ \xi_v=\sqrt{\varepsilon} \sum_{j=1}^N\chi_j(\omega_v)e_j. \tag{9} \] Character orthogonality gives \[ \mathbb E\xi_v=0,\qquad \mathbb E(\xi_v\xi_v^*)=\varepsilon I,\qquad \mathbb E\|\xi_v\|^2=N\varepsilon. \tag{10} \] Define random packets by the original maps: \[ X_v=a_v+\xi_v\quad\hbox{at a leaf},\qquad X_v=A_vX_c+\xi_v,\qquad X_v=M_v(X_l,X_r)+\xi_v. \tag{11} \] Child subtrees are independent, and the fresh error at their parent is independent of both. Induction therefore gives \[ \mathbb E X_v=a_v,\qquad \mathbb E(X_vX_v^*)=S_v. \tag{12} \] For the second identity at a binary vertex, use the exact equality \(\mathbb E[(X_lX_l^*)\otimes(X_rX_r^*)]=S_l\otimes S_r\). The adjoint in (5) conjugates the entire original map, including its phases. Its entries are not squared separately. Put \[ V_v=\mathbb E[(X_v-a_v)(X_v-a_v)^*]\succeq0,\qquad t_v=\operatorname{tr}V_v,\qquad h=N\varepsilon. \tag{13} \] Thus \(S_v=a_va_v^*+V_v\). At a binary vertex, writing \(\delta_c=X_c-a_c\), the three propagated fluctuations are \[ M_v(a_l,\delta_r),\quad M_v(\delta_l,a_r), \quad M_v(\delta_l,\delta_r). \tag{14} \] Their pairwise \(L^2\) inner products vanish: in each cross term one independent centered child fluctuation occurs only once. The fresh error is orthogonal to all three. In matrix form, \[ \begin{split} V_v={}&M_v\bigl(a_la_l^*\otimes V_r+ V_l\otimes a_ra_r^*+V_l\otimes V_r\bigr)M_v^* +\varepsilon I . \end{split} \tag{15} \] Using (3), (4), independence and (10) consequently gives \[ \begin{array}{ll} t_v=h,&v\ \hbox{a leaf},\\ t_v\le\sigma^2t_c+h,&v\ \hbox{unary},\\ t_v\le\sigma^4(t_l+t_r)+\sigma^2t_lt_r+h, &v\ \hbox{binary}. \end{array} \tag{16} \] If \(h\le1\), induction shows \(t_v\le2h\) at every vertex. For a unary vertex use \(1+2\sigma^2<2\). For a binary vertex, \[ \sigma^4(2h+2h)+\sigma^2(2h)^2+h =h(1+4\sigma^4+4\sigma^2h)<2h. \tag{17} \] These estimates do not accumulate a factor for the number of vertices. At the unchanged original closing, \[ F_N(\varepsilon)=|K_N|^2+B_N^2 L V_{\rm top}L^*,\qquad 0\le B_N^2 L V_{\rm top}L^* \le2\sigma^2B_N^2N\varepsilon. \tag{18} \] The choice (7) has \(h=\theta/B_N^2\le1\), and \(2\sigma^2=1/128\). This proves (8). The probability space in (9) is a proof device for a finite orthogonal expansion. Evaluation of (5) requires no random sampling, Gaussian integration or limiting operation. ## 4. A scalar polynomial of degree bounded by the number of leaves There is a second fixed-degree simplification. If the original tree has \(l\) leaf occurrences, then \[ F_N(\varepsilon)=|K_N|^2+ \sum_{j=1}^{l}c_{N,j}\varepsilon^j, \qquad c_{N,j}\ge0. \tag{19} \] Indeed each \(S_v(\varepsilon)\) is a matrix polynomial with positive semidefinite coefficient matrices. This holds at a leaf, is preserved by \(A_v S A_v^*\), and is preserved by tensoring the two polynomial matrices and applying \(M_v(\,\cdot\,)M_v^*\). Adding \(\varepsilon I\) preserves the assertion. The degree is at most one at a leaf, unchanged along a unary corridor, and at most the sum of the child degrees at a binary vertex. The constant coefficient is \(a_va_v^*\) by (4). Applying \(L\) proves (19). More explicitly, an antichain is a set of proper vertices no one of which is an ancestor of another. Let \(C_A\) be the original normalized scalar expression with the subtrees at the vertices of an antichain \(A\) replaced by free \(H_N\) inputs. All other subtrees and the original closing remain as prescribed. Then \[ F_N(\varepsilon)=|K_N|^2+ B_N^2\sum_{\substack{A\ne\varnothing\\A\ {\rm antichain}}} \varepsilon^{|A|}\|C_A\|_{\rm HS}^2. \tag{20} \] To see this, expand (11) using bilinearity. Choosing a fresh \(\xi_v\) replaces its entire subtree, so a surviving term uses an antichain of error vertices. Different antichains are orthogonal: an error variable present in just one term has mean zero. For the same antichain, (10) contracts the full coefficient tensor with its adjoint, giving its Hilbert--Schmidt norm. An antichain has at most \(l\) vertices, since their descendant leaf sets are disjoint. This also proves the degree bound. The nonnegative coefficients in (19) are squared norms of complete exterior contexts. Signed terms within a context are still assembled before taking its norm. Formula (19) does not make the original scalar state-sum coefficients nonnegative. ### Errors only at the original leaves The internal additions in (5) can also be omitted. Define \(\widetilde S_v=a_va_v^*+\varepsilon I\) at each original leaf, and propagate by \[ \widetilde S_v=A_v\widetilde S_cA_v^*,\qquad \widetilde S_v=M_v(\widetilde S_l\otimes\widetilde S_r)M_v^* \tag{20a} \] at internal vertices. These matrices are positive semidefinite; strict definiteness for an arbitrary unary map is not required. The same independent-error proof applies, with no fresh internal error. Now the covariance trace is at most \(h=N\varepsilon\le1\): it equals \(h\) at leaves, is at most \(\sigma^2h\) after a unary map, and at a binary map is at most \(\sigma^2(2\sigma^2h+h^2)\le h\). Consequently, at the same choice (7), \[ 0\le B_N^2 L\widetilde S_{\rm top}L^*-|K_N|^2 \le\frac{\theta}{256}. \tag{20b} \] Writing \(\mathcal B_E:H_N^{\otimes l}\to H_N\) for the normalized synthesis map of the original expression, the exact formula is simply \[ \widetilde S_{\rm top} =\mathcal B_E\! \left[\bigotimes_{\ell\ {\rm leaf}} (a_\ell a_\ell^*+\varepsilon I)\right] \mathcal B_E^* . \tag{20c} \] The nonconstant coefficients now correspond to subsets of leaves. Equation (20c) is the usual weighted synthesis covariance; the additional assertion here is its calibrated additive comparison with the same filled source. This version needs orthogonal error labels only at the original leaves. The all-vertex version gives a strict positive floor at every intermediate packet independently of the ranks of the maps. ## 5. Local matrix certificates One need not evaluate the exact messages to obtain rigorous bounds. Suppose positive semidefinite matrices \(Q_v^-\) satisfy the following local inequalities, with the same \(\varepsilon_N\): \[ \begin{array}{ll} Q_v^-\preceq a_va_v^*+\varepsilon_N I,&v\ \hbox{a leaf},\\ Q_v^-\preceq A_vQ_c^-A_v^*+\varepsilon_N I,&v\ \hbox{unary},\\ Q_v^-\preceq M_v(Q_l^-\otimes Q_r^-)M_v^*+\varepsilon_N I, &v\ \hbox{binary}. \end{array} \tag{21} \] Likewise let positive semidefinite \(Q_v^+\) satisfy the reversed inequalities. Then \[ Q_v^-\preceq S_v\preceq Q_v^+ \tag{22} \] by induction. The tensor-product step follows from \[ S_l\otimes S_r-Q_l^-\otimes Q_r^- =(S_l-Q_l^-)\otimes S_r+ Q_l^-\otimes(S_r-Q_r^-)\succeq0, \tag{23} \] and the analogous identity for the upper comparison. Combining (8), (18), and (22) gives \[ \boxed{\quad \max\!\left(0,B_N^2LQ_{\rm top}^-L^*-\frac{\theta}{128}\right) \le |K_N|^2\le B_N^2LQ_{\rm top}^+L^*. \quad} \tag{24} \] The matrices can have off-diagonal entries. Replacing them by their diagonals is not justified by these inequalities. For a hyperbolic knot complement of volume \(V>0\), one sufficient geometric target is a family of such messages for which, eventually, the two root observations are positive and \[ \liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac{\pi}{N} \log(B_N^2LQ_{\rm top}^-L^*)\ge V,\qquad \limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac{\pi}{N} \log(B_N^2LQ_{\rm top}^+L^*)\le V. \tag{25} \] The lower observation then grows exponentially; subtracting the fixed constant in (24) does not change its rate. The original volume identity follows by squeezing. No such geometric message family is constructed in this note. ## 6. Scope and sources At \(\varepsilon=0\), (5) is simply the exact rank-one contraction of the original source with its conjugate. The additional result is the explicit strictly positive regularization and its uniform unnormalized error bound. It avoids a variational solve but retains the full matrix size, precision requirements and coherent phases. The chosen \(\varepsilon_N\) can be exponentially small because the known budget \(B_N\) can grow exponentially. The two sides of (8) imply, for every \(V>0\), \[ \frac{\pi}{N}\log P_N\longrightarrow V \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \frac{2\pi}{N}\log|K_N|\longrightarrow V. \tag{26} \] Indeed \(P_N\) differs from \(1+|K_N|^2\) by a bounded additive quantity. A positive limiting rate implies eventual nonvanishing of \(K_N\). This is a finite-level comparison, not a proof of either limit. Every fixed short partial filling can be inserted into its actual leaf data, or contracted as a full open subtree before recompiling. The theorem therefore has no restriction on short words. The finite-exception program still needs (25), or the equivalent geometric rate of (5), for every required fixed short partial filling and sufficiently long remaining hyperbolic completions. Local saddle existence and strict angle-volume concavity alone do not supply the full-matrix inequalities (21). The sole direct proof source is the complete normalized compiler and its norm bounds: | Source | SHA-256 | |---|---| | [Normalized complete Conway source](research_convex_normalized_conway_source.md) | 6b89b4c6a67ef7a32cc41a5966c650f32de65d284ae7b70d94a71bddba21df3c | Second-moment contraction of a tensor with its conjugate and transfer operators are standard. For literature coverage, see [Schollwöck, sections 4.2.1–4.2.2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1008.3477). No estimate from that reference is used in this proof, and no novelty is claimed for those general operations. The statement here is the calibrated additive comparison with the original Conway source, together with its local matrix certificates. Only written mathematics, source reads and text operations were used. No mathematical program, numerical experiment, test, build, git operation or public-document edit was performed.

title: A free outside neighborhood for the actual pair-edge kernel
text: # A free outside neighborhood for the actual pair-edge kernel Research proof, 3 November 2026. Frozen manuscripts are unchanged. The complete-end logarithmic estimate can be strengthened to the full Gaussian edge packet, with a fixed small complex neighborhood in the outside color. The proof below uses the original finite Newton sum. Its contour is a ray in the tangent coordinate, rather than a horizontal line. All low-index endpoints, reciprocal-factorial terms, cotangent aliases, and the original radical are retained. ## 1. Domain and statement Write \(t=a-iH\), and put \[ C=\cos(t/2),\qquad A=C^2,\qquad \mathcal D=\{\,0<a<\pi/2,\ H>0,\ |C|<1\,\}. \tag{1} \] On this domain \(C\) is in the first quadrant, \(\Re A>1/2\), and \(0<\arg C<\pi/4\). Fix a compact subset \(\mathcal T\) of \(\mathcal D\cap\{H<107/100\}\). Every active angle of a fixed positive integer complete-end internal pair belongs to this domain, by the [real wire-order theorem](research_positive_path_real_wire_order.md) and the [pair complete-edge gap](research_internal_pair_complete_edge_gap.md). Use the original conventions \[ \begin{split} K_N(t,u)&=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}e_j(-2\cos t)e_j(-2\cos u),\\ L_N(t,u)&=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1-\lfloor N/2\rfloor} e_j(-2\cos t)e_j(-2\cos u),\\ b(y,t)&=-J(1/2-y+t/(2\pi))-J(1/2-y-t/(2\pi))-2J(y),\\ F(y;t,u)&=b(y,t)+b(y,u),\qquad J'(y)=\Log(2\sin\pi y). \end{split} \tag{2} \] The branches are continued from completeness without resetting a logarithm after crossing a factorial strip. **Theorem 1.** There are a complex neighborhood \(V\) of \(\mathcal T\) and \(\epsilon>0\) such that, uniformly for \(t\in V\), \(|u|<\epsilon\), through both level parities, \[ \begin{split} K_N(t,u)&=N^{-3/2}a_e(t,u)e^{N\psi(t,u)} (1+O(N^{-1})),\\ a_e(t,u)&=\frac{\sqrt{2\pi}} {4\sin^2(\pi y_*)\sqrt{-F_{yy}(y_*;t,u)}}\ne0 . \end{split} \tag{3} \] Here \(y_*\) is the selected wire saddle and \(\psi(t,u)=F(y_*;t,u)\) has the original complete constant. The Gaussian root is continued from positive real \(C\). The normalized error has a holomorphic expansion to every fixed inverse-power order, with all fixed parameter derivatives on smaller neighborhoods. Evenness in \(u\) gives the same assertion in a fixed ordinary outside-color neighborhood of \(-2\), including its normals. The same packet holds for \(L_N\), and \(K_N/L_N=1+O(e^{-cN})\). The theorem concerns an actual edge factor near the selected pair angles. It does not determine the coefficient of a joint trace cycle. ## 2. A strict single-maximum contour at the complete outside end Set \(u=0\) and \(z=\tan(\pi y)\). Direct differentiation of (2) gives \[ e^{F_y}=\frac{A-(1-A)z^2}{z^4}. \tag{4} \] Thus the finite critical equation factors as \((z^2-A)(z^2+1)=0\). The selected saddle is \(z=C\), or \(y_*=\pi^{-1}\arctan C\). Consider the oriented ray \[ z=Cr,\quad 0<r<\infty,\qquad y=\pi^{-1}\arctan(Cr). \tag{5} \] It is the graph \(y=x+ih(x)\), \(0<x<1/2\), where \[ h(x)=\frac1{2\pi} \operatorname{arsinh}\{\tan(\gamma)\sin(2\pi x)\}, \qquad \gamma=\arg C. \tag{6} \] Its endpoints are \(0\) and \(1/2\). **Lemma 2.** Along (5), \(\Re F\) strictly increases to \(r=1\) and strictly decreases thereafter. At the maximum, \[ F_r(1)=0,\qquad F_{rr}(1)=-\frac2{\pi C}, \qquad F_{yy}(y_*)=-\frac{2\pi(1+A)^2}{C^3}. \tag{7} \] *Proof.* On the ray let \[ R(r)=\frac{1-(1-A)r^2}{Ar^4},\qquad F_r=\frac{C}{\pi(1+Ar^2)}\Log R(r). \tag{8} \] For \(r<1\), \(R=r^{-4}\{r^2+(1-r^2)/A\}\) has negative argument and \(|R|>1\): its real part exceeds \(r^{-2}>1\). The tangent in (8) has positive real and imaginary parts because \(|A|r^2<1\). Hence \(\Re F_r>0\). For \(r>1\), \(R\) is in the upper half-plane and \(|R|<1\). Indeed, writing \(v=r^2>1\), the difference of squared moduli is \[ |A|^2v^4-|1-(1-A)v|^2 =(v-1)\{|A|^2(v^3+v^2)+(2\Re A-1)v+1\}>0. \tag{9} \] Until \(r=|A|^{-1/2}\) the tangent has nonnegative imaginary part, so \(\Re F_r<0\). For the remaining interval put \(v=r^{-2}\le s=|A|<1\). Now \[ R=v(A-1+v)/A,\qquad \frac{|\Im(C/(v+A))|}{\Re(C/(v+A))} =\tan\gamma\,\frac{s-v}{s+v}. \tag{10} \] Because \(2\Re A\ge1\), \(|A-1+v|\le|A|\); consequently \[ -\log|R|\ge-\log v\ge\frac{2(1-v)}{1+v},\qquad 0<\arg R<\pi-2\gamma . \tag{11} \] Also \((s-v)/(s+v)\le(1-v)/(1+v)\) and \(\tan\gamma(\pi-2\gamma)<2\) for \(0<\gamma<\pi/4\). For the latter inequality the expression is increasing on this interval, since \(\pi-2\gamma>\sin(2\gamma)\), and its endpoint value is \(\pi/2<2\). Equations (10)--(11) therefore show that the negative real-log term in (8) strictly exceeds its possible positive argument term. This proves \(\Re F_r<0\). The logarithm tends to zero at \(r=1\) from both sides. Differentiation there proves (7), including the zero logarithmic lift. \(\square\) The only possible numerator zero in the upper wire strip is \[ y_0=\frac12-\frac{t}{2\pi},\qquad \tan(\pi y_0)=\cot(t/2)=C/\sin(t/2). \tag{12} \] Since \(\sin(t/2)\) is in the fourth quadrant, its tangent coordinate has argument strictly greater than \(\gamma\). Thus \(y_0\) lies above the graph (6). In particular neither the ray nor the closed region between it and its reflection meets this zero. All continuations used in (8) are regular there.
