Equations (23)--(24) thus bound the central contribution by \[ C N^A e^{N[\Re\psi(0,z)+h^2-(1-\cos u)/20]}. \] Since \(h^2\le1/40000\) and \(1-\cos u\ge1-\cos(9/10)>1/3\), this is smaller than the bound (20). Here are uniform bounds for the other wire indices. The same midpoint argument used for real logarithmic zeros gives \[ |e_j(r+ih)|\le C N^A e^{N V_{r,h}(j/N)},\qquad V_{r,h}(y)\le V_r(y)+|h|. 	ag{26} \] To verify the second inequality directly, factor the numerator integrand as \[ 2\cos(2\pi x)+2\cos(r+ih) =4\cos(\pi x+(r+ih)/2)\cos(\pi x-(r+ih)/2). \] In each cosine, introducing the imaginary part increases its modulus. The increase in the logarithmic integral over a full period in \(x\) is \(|h|/2\) for each factor, by the elementary logarithmic mean of \(a+be^{2\pi ix}\). The increase over a partial interval is nonnegative and no larger than the sum \(|h|\). For the first inequality, omit the bounded number of mesh cells meeting a real cosine zero. On the remaining cells the logarithmic derivative has the same harmonic sum bound as for a real zero. In a removed cell, \(\log|\cos(a+ih/2)|\) has upper sampling error \(O(1)\), uniformly down to \(h=0\); an exact sampled zero only improves an upper bound. The total numerator error is uniform because, when \(|h|\le N^{-1}\), the sampled logarithm on such a cell is at most \(\log(C/N)\), while its integral average is at least \(-\log N-C\). When \(|h|>N^{-1}\), the variation across that cell is at most \(C/(N|h|)\le C\). The total numerator error is therefore \(O(\log N)\), uniformly in all the parameters in (19). The sine denominator has the established uniform error of the same order. This proves (26). On \(0<y<1/2-|r|/(2\pi)\), one has \(A_r''(y)\le V_0''(y)\le-4\pi\). The interval from (25) to either \(1/8\) or \(1/3\) lies in this range, because \(19/20<\pi/3\). Also \(A_r\) decreases on \([1/4,1/2]\), including across its logarithmic derivative singularity. Consequently \[ \sup_{y\in[0,1/2]\setminus(1/8,1/3)} A_r(y) \le\psi(0,r)-\delta,\qquad \delta= rac{9\pi}{800}. 	ag{27} \] At the lower endpoint the distance to the saddle exceeds \(3/40\); at the upper endpoint it is at least \(1/12\). These distances and the second-derivative bound give (27). For any real \(u\), \(V_u(y)\le V_0(y)\) on the lower half. Thus (26)--(27) bound its omitted part by \(C N^A e^{N[\psi(0,r)-\delta+|h|]}\). Since \(\delta-|h|>1/100\), this proves (20) for that part as well. On the upper half, both \(V_u\) and \(V_r\) are nonpositive, so (26) bounds the entire contribution by \(C N^A e^{N|h|}\). On the other hand \(\psi(0,r)>5/6\): use \(M_\infty>1\), \(|K|<2\), and integrate twice along the real interval of length less than one. This makes the upper half exponentially smaller than (20), finishing its proof. For (21), first retain the original wire \([1/5,3/10]\). The same real angular inequality used in (24), applied to both factors, bounds this part by \(C N^A e^{N[M_\infty-((1-\cos u)+(1-\cos v))/20]}\). The established full omitted-wire estimate has rate at most \(M_\infty-\pi/100\), uniformly on the real square. Since \(\gamma[(1-\cos u)+(1-\cos v)]\le4\gamma=1/50\), it satisfies (21) too. Finally apply the polynomial Markov inequality in each removed variable \(z=-2\cos u\) on the fixed interval \([-2\cos(9/10),2]\). The supremum bounds just proved are uniform in the remaining complex variable. Each derivative costs only \(C N^2\); applying it in both variables gives the mixed bound. Complex coefficients are allowed by rotating the derivative at the evaluation point and applying the real inequality to its real part. No endpoint or original first normal is excluded. \(\square\) ## 5. Every complementary-row subset has a local action budget Assume now \(n_v\ge64\). For \(S\subseteq I\), let \(\lambda_v=0\) on \(S\), and \(\lambda_v=1\) elsewhere. The [partial-charge theorem](research_positive_path_partial_charge_bounds.md) gives its stationary point with \(t_v=0\) exactly on \(S\), and \[ |t_v^*(\lambda)|\le  rac{2\pi}{n_v-2d_v/5}< rac1{10},\qquad H_v(\lambda)\le C_v< rac1{200}, \quad C_v= rac{14\pi d_v/5} {(n_v-2d_v/5)^2+(7d_v/5)^2}. 	ag{28} \] The same theorem bounds its real stationary action by \[ 0\le\mathcal M(\lambda)-\mathcal M(\mathbf1) \le rac12\sum_{v\in S}C_v < rac1{800}\sum_{v\in S}d_v . 	ag{29} \] For the last rational inequality drop the positive \((7d_v/5)^2\) term in the denominator, use \(n_v\ge64\), \(d_v\le2\), and \(C_v/(2d_v)\le35\pi/99856<1/800\). Expand the original finite trace according to the vertices whose physical angles lie outside \((-T_N,T_N)\). Fix a nonempty such set \(S\). Keep those original grid rows and their first normals. At every other vertex use (15), with the selected height from the partial-charge solution (28). Every remaining angle lies in \(\Omega\). On an edge between \(S\) and its complement, (20) replaces the edge's modulus by the phase \(\Re\psi(0,t_w)\) and an angular loss at its removed endpoint. On an edge inside \(S\), (21) gives \(\psi(0,0)\) and a loss at both endpoints. The last assertion of Lemma 2 preserves these estimates for every derivative contributed by the original removed rows. Crossing values have modulus one at those rows; their first normals and the finite trace factors cost only fixed powers of \(N\). Thus, after these bounds, the remaining phase is exactly the original phase with the vertices in \(S\) fixed at zero. The surviving components are paths with the same degrees, now including their zero-angle boundary incidences. Theorem 1 applies component by component to every retained mixed current. In particular their integrals have upper rate at most \(\mathcal M(\lambda)\). The total loss from the removed endpoints is at least \[ \gamma(1-\cos(9/10))\sum_{v\in S}d_v > rac1{600}\sum_{v\in S}d_v . 	ag{30} \] Combining (29)--(30) proves a gap greater than \[  rac1{2400}\sum_{v\in S}d_v 	ag{31} \] below the full selected action. This is independent of the number of other selected vertices. The finitely many grid sums and contour subsets have only polynomial costs for each fixed path. The full thin-box kernel theorem proves the required uniform upper bound on the surviving thin contours, \[ |K_N(t,u)|\le C N^A e^{N\Re\psi(t,u)},\qquad |\Re t|,|\Re u|\le1,\quad |\Im t|,|\Im u|\le1/200. 	ag{32} \] It does not require (18) on the larger-height box. Thus (31) controls every complementary-row subset of the original whole trace. The same kernel theorem gives its uniform nonzero local expansion at the selected saddle, so Section 3 supplies the surviving nonzero Gaussian term. This uses a single uniform kernel theorem and the local action budgets above for every fixed path length. ## 6. Signed retained currents, including a scalar closure Corollary 3 of [the partial-charge theorem](research_positive_path_partial_charge_bounds.md) constructs the original positive geometric solution for any selected set of a nontrivial circle path, including all auxiliary vertices, when \(|n_v|\ge8\). It retains every original carrier and primitive filling coefficient. For the current estimate we use the more conservative threshold \(|n_v|\ge64\). Put \(\sigma_v=\operatorname{sgn}(n_v)\). At the selected unit-charge point, \[ \operatorname{sgn}(	heta_v)=\sigma_v,\qquad |	heta_v|<1/10,\qquad 0<H_v<1/200. 	ag{33} \] For a current subset \(S\), use the unchanged lower horizontal segment at every vertex outside \(S\), and the vertical segment \[ t_v=\sigma_vT+ih_v,\qquad -H_v\le h_v\le H_v,\qquad T=19/20 	ag{34} \] at every vertex in \(S\). **Corollary 3.** For these domains the exponential upper functional (7) satisfies \[ \mathcal E_S\le\mathcal M-|S|/400 	ag{35} \] for every nonempty subset \(S\), with no restriction on the signs or relative magnitudes of the powers. No complete outside endpoint is required. The exact term for this domain retains the additional scalar \[ \prod_{v\in S}\sigma_v 	ag{36} \] from the choice of vertical sides. The proved thin-box kernel estimate (32) and its nonzero local expansion give the stated quantum comparison for the original retained trace. **Proof.** First check the exact change of side. With the odd function \(g(t)\) used in (15), and the even function \(c(h)=1/(4\cosh^2(Nh/2))\), one has \[ \int_{-H}^{H}g(-T+ih)c(h)\,dh =-\int_{-H}^{H}g(T-ih)c(h)\,dh =-\int_{-H}^{H}g(T+ih)c(h)\,dh . 	ag{37} \] The last equality changes \(h\) to \(-h\), including its integration limits. Thus replacing the positive vertical side by the negative one contributes exactly the factor \(-1\). Applying this independently at the vertices proves (36). The spectator remains even in each variable after other integrations, because each original edge kernel has that property. All shared normal data therefore remain those of the exact Hermite identity. The horizontal segment is still below the real axis, and its principal Fourier charge is still \(+1\). In particular the charge term remains \(-it_v\) for both signs of \(n_v\); it is not changed when a vertical side is reflected. The reflected vertical domain still contains the full symmetric height interval, so \(-|h_v|\le h_v\) proves \(\mathcal E_S\le\Re\Phi\) exactly as before. Write \(t-t^*=a+ib\). On a vertical coordinate, \[ a_v=\sigma_v(T-|	heta_v|),\qquad b_v=h_v+H_v\in[0,2H_v], \] and consequently \[ |a_v|>17/20,\qquad n_va_v=|n_v||a_v|>64(17/20),\qquad 0\le b_v<1/100. 	ag{38} \] All segments from \(t^*\) to the current domain remain in \(\mathcal B^I\). The weighted Taylor calculation (10)--(13) uses absolute norms for its mixed term and so does not require \(a_v>0\). Its last term is still favorable, since \(n_va_v>0\). In particular \(n_va_v>21d_vb_v\), and therefore the \(B_2\) term in (13) is absorbed. We obtain \[ \Re\Phi(t)-\mathcal M <- rac1{40\pi}\sum_{v\in S}d_v(17/20)^2 <-|S|/400. 	ag{39} \] This proves (35). The strict reserve also absorbs midpoint replacements \(T_N=T+O(N^{-1})\) for all sufficiently large levels, with the same constant \(1/400\). The partial-charge theorem and marked completion identify this critical point and its absolute volume even when all auxiliary vertices are selected. Its principal horizontal Gaussian determinant is nonzero by the same Hessian bound. Every height in the current domain is less than \(1/200\) in modulus, so (32) is the kernel bound needed for the retained finite trace; the larger-height assumption (18) is unnecessary here. The proved local kernel expansion supplies its nonzero Gaussian coefficient. \(\square\) The signs in (36) do not affect the upper bound, but they are part of the exact finite formula. This corollary concerns the retained trace currents. The complementary real grid rows obey the separate comparison in Sections 4--5, also in the all-selected scalar case. Those bounds use only the moduli of crossing values and their polynomially bounded first normals. The signed partial-charge theorem gives the same height and action budgets with \(|n_v|\) in their denominators. Hence that outer-row comparison applies unchanged to these independently signed powers. ## 7. The retained external angle has a whole-period bound Suppose one original outside endpoint is left free, with angle \(u\), while the other outside endpoints remain complete. Let \(F_N(u)\) be the corresponding original path source, with every selected power satisfying \(|n_v|\ge64\), and let \(\mathcal M\) denote its selected action at \(u=0\). Use the proved thin-box kernel bound (32) and the signed current domains of Section 6. Then \[ |F_N(u)|\le C N^A e^{N[\mathcal M-(1-\cos u)/200]}, \qquad -\pi\le u\le\pi . 	ag{40} \] The constants and polynomial powers may depend on the fixed path and its fixed crossing powers. For \(|u|\le19/20\), evenness at the free endpoint and (4) give, for every retained neighboring angle \(t\), \[ \Re\psi(t,u)\le \Re\psi(t,0)- rac{u^2}{20\pi}. 	ag{41} \] This follows by integrating the \(uu\) entry of the negative real Hessian twice along the real \(u\)-segment. Its first derivative at zero is exactly zero, also for complex \(t\). Thus the principal phase and every mixed current acquire the same external loss. If the neighboring vertex is one of the removed real rows, Lemma 2 first replaces the edge by \(\psi(0,u)\); (41), with \(t=0\), then gives that same loss. The estimates of Sections 5 and 6 therefore retain it term by term. For \(9/10\le|u|\le\pi\), use (20) when its neighboring vertex is retained. The centered phase is precisely the phase of the edge with its outside endpoint complete, and the extra loss is \((1-\cos u)/200\). If the neighboring vertex is also removed, (21) retains both angular losses, so the internal-row budget (30) is unchanged. This proves the same estimate in the outer range. The ranges overlap, and \(u^2/(20\pi)\ge(1-\cos u)/200\), proving (40). The uniform holomorphic kernel expansion has nonzero amplitude on the thin box. Therefore the full source has a nonzero holomorphic packet on a neighborhood of \(u=0\). The stationary point persists by the invertible complex Hessian; its amplitude is the product of the original edge amplitudes and the nonzero \(\sin t_v^*\) factors, divided by the continued Gaussian determinant. The strict current and complementary-row gaps persist on a smaller complex neighborhood, by polynomial continuation and the uniform kernel estimates. Finally the canonical source has degree at most \(N-1\) in \(-2\cos u\). The exact Laurent-polynomial maximum principle applied to (40), together with its local holomorphic packet, gives a quadratic thin-strip bound \[ |F_N(x+iy)|\le C_1N^{A_1} e^{N[\mathcal M-c(1-\cos x)+B y^2]} \quad(|x|\le\pi,\ |y|\le h), 	ag{42} \] for some \(c,B,h>0\). The proof is the harmonic-majorant and local Taylor argument in [the Newton note, Lemma 8](research_three_crossing_real_period_newton_bound.md). No new observation or positive replacement state is used. These are proved analytic estimates for the original source. Its marking and geometric volume identification are the separate inputs used when assembling a knot volume theorem. ## 8. A stronger centered loss for a removed incidence The next estimate concerns one full original edge. Its selected angle may range across the full width \(\pi/2\) at height \(3/10\). It requires the other real angle to be at least \(\pi/2\). It supplies a source estimate for a complementary-row argument; it does not extend the retained path contour theorem to powers seven. Write \(\mathcal K_N(w,v)=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}e_j(w)e_j(v)\), so that \(K_N(u,z)=\mathcal K_N(-2\cos u,-2\cos z)\), and keep the original normalization \(\Psi(z)=\psi(0,z)\). **Lemma 4.** For every fixed pair of nonnegative integers \(k,\ell\), there are constants \(C,A\) such that, at both level parities, \[ \left| \partial_w^k\partial_v^\ell\mathcal K_N(w,v)  ig|_{w=-2\cos u,\ v=-2\cos z} ight| \le CN^A\exp N\left\{\Re\Psi(z)- rac{21}{200}ight\}, \quad  rac{\pi}{2}\le |u|\le\pi,\quad |\Re z|\le rac{\pi}{2},\quad |\Im z|\le rac3{10}. 	ag{43} \] The derivatives are ordinary spectral derivatives, including at \(w=2\) and \(v=-2\). *The exact low-index entropy.* Put \(J_N=\lfloor(N-1)/2floor\). Evenness and conjugation allow writing \(z=r+iH\), with \(0\le r\le\pi/2\) and \(0\le H\le3/10\). Keep the selected angle in its modulus entropy: \[  egin{split} B_z(x)&=\int_0^x\log|2\cos(2\pi s)+2\cos z|\,ds-2J(x),\ F_{r,H}(x)&=V_{\pi/2}(x)+B_z(x),\ |e_j(-2\cos u)e_j(-2\cos z)| &\le CN^A e^{NF_{r,H}(j/N)},\qquad 0\le j\le J_N. \end{split} 	ag{44} \] The real-angle monotonicity of [the original Newton entropy](research_three_crossing_real_period_newton_bound.md) gives the removed-angle comparison. Its midpoint proof applies also to the two complex shifted cosine factors of the selected polynomial. Away from the bounded number of cells closest to a real zero, the logarithmic derivative is bounded by a constant over that real distance, uniformly in the imaginary shift. On those cells, rescaling the modulus of a complex linear factor bounds the upper midpoint error uniformly, including a zero sample. Summation costs \(O(\log N)\). This proves (44) uniformly through both low-index endpoints and all shifted zeros. In particular it uses the literal polynomials, without division by a vanishing value. Set \(c=\cos(r+iH)\), \(C=\cosh H<21/20\), and \(q=\cos(2\pi x)\). Since \(\Re c\ge0\), for \(q>0\) the ratio \(q|q+c|/(1-q)^2\) is strictly increasing in \(q\). Its logarithm is \(F'_{r,H}\). It has a unique critical value \(q_*\), and \[  egin{split} F'_{r,H}(x)&=\log rac{|q|\,|q+c|}{(1-q)^2},\ 1= rac{q_*|q_*+c|}{(1-q_*)^2} &\le rac{q_*(q_*+C)}{(1-q_*)^2}, \qquad q_*\ge rac1{C+2}> rac{20}{61}> \cos rac{2\pi}{5}. \end{split} 	ag{45} \] For \(q=-v<0\), \(0<v<1\), the ratio is at most \(v(C+v)/(1+v)^2<1\). Thus the reflected half has no competing maximum. The logarithmic zeros are integrable. The unique global maximum of (44) lies at \(0<x_*<1/5\). On \(0\le x\le1/5\) all selected factorial arguments are in their regular strips. Therefore \(B_z(x)=\Re b(x,z)\), with the original branch. Since \(q>0\) on this interval, \[  egin{split} \partial_H^2 B_{r+iH}(x) &= rac{\sin(2\pi x)}{2\pi} \Re rac1{q+\cos(r+iH)} \le rac{	an(2\pi x)}{2\pi}< rac12,\ B_{r+iH}(x)&\le V_r(x)+ rac{H^2}{4},\ E(r,H):=\max_{0\le x\le1/2}F_{r,H}(x) &\le E(r,0)+ rac9{400}. \end{split} 	ag{46} \] Here \(\partial_H B_{r+iH}|_{H=0}=0\). The final numerical inequality follows from \(	an^2(2\pi/5)=5+2\sqrt5<19/2<(31/10)^2<\pi^2\). No factorial estimate near the reflected zero was used in this second-derivative argument: (45) first located the maximum in the regular interval. *Centering at the actual complete-edge action.* At \(H=0\), the critical coordinate is \(q_*=1/(2+\cos r)\). The [calibrated stationary edge identity](research_unsummed_network_phase_coercivity.md#5-what-positive-geometry-does-imply-locally) gives, with its original complete constant, \[  egin{split} E(r,0)&=\psi(\pi/2,r),\ \Psi(r)-\psi(\pi/2,r) &= rac1\pi\int_0^{\pi/2} \operatorname{asinh}\{	an(a/2)\cos(r/2)\}\,da\ &\ge d_*:=  rac1\pi\int_0^{\pi/2} \operatorname{asinh}\{	an(a/2)/\sqrt2\}\,da. \end{split} 	ag{47} \] This is a phase identity, not an assumed kernel asymptotic. The bound \(\operatorname{asinh}s\ge s-s^3/6\) gives an elementary exact lower bound: \[ d_*\ge rac{13\log2-1}{12\pi\sqrt2} > rac{1127}{7920}. 	ag{48} \] For the integral use \(\int_0^{\pi/4}	an a\,da=(\log2)/2\) and \(\int_0^{\pi/4}	an^3a\,da=(1-\log2)/2\). For the strict rational inequality use \(\log2=2\operatorname{atanh}(1/3)>2/3\), \(\pi<22/7\), and \(\sqrt2<10/7\). The selected color box lies in \(\Re(-2\cos z)<2\). Since \(\Psi''(z)=-\sec(z/2)/(2\pi)\) and \(\Re\sec(z/2)>0\) there, imaginary convexity gives \(\Re\Psi(r+iH)\ge\Psi(r)\). Combining (46)--(48), \[ \Re\Psi(z)-E(r,H)>  rac{1127}{7920}- rac9{400} = rac{593}{4950} = rac{21}{200}+ rac{293}{19800}. 	ag{49} \] *Restoring the full radical.* Each original radical \(e_j\), \(j>J_N\), has real interval norm at most \(\sqrt{N-1}\), by the [full original radical bound](research_high_newton_radical_contraction.md#7-fourier-bounds-for-the-original-radical-polynomials). Bernstein continuation in the selected angle costs \(e^{(N-1)H}\); the removed angle stays real. Hence their sum is at most \(CN^Ae^{NH}\). For a coarse uniform lower bound on the selected phase, \(\operatorname{asinh}	an(a/2)\le a/\sqrt2\) on \(0\le a\le\pi/2\), by differentiation. Consequently \[  egin{split} \Re\Psi(z)&\ge\Psi(\pi/2) \ge M_\infty- rac{\pi}{8\sqrt2} > rac{29}{25}- rac{55}{196} = rac{4309}{4900} > rac3{10}+ rac{21}{200}. \end{split} 	ag{50} \] The lower bound \(M_\infty>29/25\) follows from the first six alternating terms of the Catalan series and \(\pi<22/7\). Thus every original index is retained in (43), at both parities. *Ordinary derivatives.* The low-index and radical estimates hold on the entire real removed-color interval \(0\le w\le2\), for every selected angle in the displayed box. Ordinary Markov inequalities retain all \(w\)-derivatives at polynomial cost, including both endpoints. The modulus entropy and its compact maximum are continuous in the selected angle, also when its factorial zeros move through the real integration interval. The strict reserve in (49)--(50) therefore persists on a slightly enlarged selected-angle neighborhood. Cauchy's formula on ordinary selected-color circles of radius \(O(N^{-2})\) then costs only powers of \(N\). Their angular lifts move by \(O(N^{-1})\), including the quadratic ramification at \(-2\). This proves all the stated mixed ordinary derivatives. \(\square\) **Corollary (two removed endpoints).** At both parities and for all fixed ordinary derivatives, \[ \left| \partial_w^k\partial_v^\ell\mathcal K_N(w,v)  ig|_{w=-2\cos u,\ v=-2\cos z} ight| \le CN^A e^{N(M_\infty-2(21/200))}, \qquad \pi/2\le|u|,|z|\le\pi. 	ag{51} \] Indeed the original real Newton bounds give low-index exponent at most \(2m(\pi/2)=\psi(\pi/2,\pi/2)\). Integrating the two real edge derivatives along the sides \((0,0)	o(\pi/2,0)	o(\pi/2,\pi/2)\) gives \(M_\infty-\psi(\pi/2,\pi/2)\ge2d_*>2(21/200)\). The full radical has polynomial norm on both real intervals. Markov's inequality in each ordinary color proves the derivative statement, including the endpoints. This establishes an actual loss per removed incidence even when both ends of an edge are removed. These are cancellation-free upper bounds for the original edge. No corresponding lower bound, nonzero distant-color coefficient, or whole-path contour theorem is inferred. The focused exact checker [check_path_large_angle_incidence.py](../experiments/check_path_large_angle_incidence.py) verifies the rational comparisons and the entropy-maximizer and integral identities in this section. Its [saved record](../repro/results/research-path-large-angle-incidence.json) records the proof and dependency hashes. It contains no finite-level pattern extrapolation and no test of an unproved path assembly. ## 9. Vertical-current monotonicity at powers of at least seven The threshold twenty in Section 2 comes from its Taylor estimate, not from a change in the actual trace currents. A direct height derivative gives a stronger phase comparison. The full finite-kernel input is identified separately at the end of this section. Use the positive path charge family with a stipulated complete outside endpoint. At unit charges, the [path geometry bound](research_unsummed_network_phase_coercivity.md#6-a-common-central-domain-for-positive-paths-of-power-at-least-seven) gives, for every integer power \(n_v\ge7\), \[ 0<a_v<19/20,\qquad 0<H_v<3/10. 	ag{52} \] Write \(t_v^*=a_v-iH_v\), and retain the original phase \(\Phi\) and action \(\mathcal M\) from (1)--(2). For any common cutoff \(99/100\le T\le\pi/2\), define the mixed rectangle and its exponent exactly by (6)--(7). **Lemma 5 (the wider phase rectangle).** On \[ |\Re t|,|\Re u|\le\pi/2, \qquad |\Im t|,|\Im u|\le3/10, 	ag{53} \] the original continued edge phase is holomorphic on a neighborhood of the rectangle, and \[ \Re K(t,u)\succeq rac1{10}I. 	ag{54} \] *Proof.* Set \(w=	an(t/2)\), \(v=	an(u/2)\). On (53), \(|w|,|v|\le1\) and \(|\Im w|,|\Im v|<3/10\). The latter follows directly from \(\cos(\Re t)\ge0\) and \[ |\Im	an(t/2)| = rac{\sinh|\Im t|}{\cos(\Re t)+\cosh(\Im t)} \le	anh|\Im t|. \] Consequently the branch \(s=\sqrt{1+w^2+v^2}\) has positive real part throughout the rectangle. None of the factors \(s\pm w,s\pm v\) vanish, since their paired products are \(1+v^2,1+w^2\), respectively. Continuing the logarithms from the complete point gives the original edge branch on this simply connected domain. Put \(X=(\Re w,\Re v)\), \(Y=(\Im w,\Im v)\) and \(\alpha=\Re s\). The [exact edge criterion](research_edge_hessian_and_phase_response.md#2-an-exact-positivity-criterion) gives \[  egin{split} \alpha^2-\{\Im(w\overline v)\}^2 &\ge(1-|Y|^2)(1+|X|^2)+(X\cdot Y)^2>41/50,\ \alpha(|s|^2+1)&\le4\sqrt3<7. \end{split} 	ag{55} \] Its determinant-over-trace estimate therefore bounds the smaller eigenvalue of \(\Re K\) below by \(41/350>1/10\). This proves (54). \(\square\) **Theorem 6 (all mixed-current subsets).** For every nonempty \(S\subseteq I\), every cutoff in the stated interval and every point of (6), \[ \mathcal E_S(\mathbf t) \le\mathcal M- rac{|S|}{80000} - rac1{40}\sum_{v\in S}(h_v+H_v). 	ag{56} \] The estimate is uniform in path length and in the individual powers \(n_v\ge7\). *Proof.* Hold all coordinates except a vertical one fixed, and write \(t_v=T+ih\). Its exact exponent derivative, away from the harmless cusp at \(h=0\), is \[ \partial_h\mathcal E_S = rac1\pi\sum_{w\sim v}\Im r_{vw} - rac{n_vT}{2\pi}-\operatorname{sign}h, \qquad r_{vw}=\operatorname{asinh} \{	an((T+ih)/2)\cos(t_w/2)\}. 	ag{57} \] This uses the original derivative \(\psi_t=-r/\pi\), and retains the folded vertical trace penalty \(-|h|\). Other coordinates may themselves lie anywhere on their vertical segments; their heights need not have the same sign. We record the branch and numerical bounds in (57). If \(C=\cos(t_w/2)\), then \[ \Re C>7/10,\qquad |\Im C|<4/35,\qquad \Re	an((T+ih)/2)>16/41,\qquad |\Im	an((T+ih)/2)|<3/10. 	ag{58} \] For the first two inequalities use \(\cos(\pi/4)>7/10\), \(\sin(\pi/4)<5/7\), and \(\sinh(3/20)<4/25\). For the third use \(\sin T\ge\sin(99/100)>4/5\) and \(\cos T+\cosh h<41/20\). Thus the argument of asinh in (57) has strictly positive real part. Its original branch has \(\Re r>0\) and \(-\pi/2<\Im r<\pi/2\) on all these segments. When \(h\le0\), the imaginary part of the tangent is nonpositive, and its real part is at most one. Hence a positive imaginary return \(g=\Im r\) satisfies \[ \sin g= rac{\Im\{	an((T+ih)/2)C\}}{\cosh(\Re r)} < rac4{35},\qquad g< rac{25}{24} rac4{35}= rac5{42}. 	ag{59} \] The same upper bound holds if \(g\le0\). There are at most two incidences. Using \(\pi<22/7\), (57) gives \[ \partial_h\mathcal E_S <1- rac{693/100-10/21}{2\pi} <- rac{353}{13200}<- rac1{40},\qquad h<0. 	ag{60} \] For \(h>0\), the simpler bound \(g<\pi/2\) gives \(\partial_h\mathcal E_S<-n_vT/(2\pi)<-1/40\). Both one-sided bounds hold at zero. Integrating each vertical height from \(-H_v\) to its actual value proves that its exponent is no larger than its bottom horizontal value minus \((h_v+H_v)/40\). At the resulting bottom point all imaginary coordinates equal those of the geometric saddle. Lemma 5, summed over the actual edges, and Taylor's formula at that saddle give \[ \Re\Phi(\mathbf r-i\mathbf H) \le\mathcal M- rac1{40\pi} \sum_v d_v(r_v-a_v)^2. 	ag{61} \] For each \(v\in S\), \(r_v=T\) and \(T-a_v>1/25\). Therefore its contribution to the loss is greater than \(1/(25000\pi)>1/80000\). Combining these losses with (60) proves (56). \(\square\) These are precisely the phases of the original mixed Hermite currents in (15), at both level parities. Choose the largest midpoint cut \(T_N\le T\), where \(T\in(99/100,\pi/2]\) is fixed. Then \(T_N	o T\) and the cut lies in the theorem's interval for all sufficiently large levels. Thus no rounding limit changes its positive gap. The full [wide-kernel theorem](research_bare_kernel_thin_rectangle.md#6-the-full-rectangle-through-real-angle-pi-over-two) now gives the uniform finite-kernel bound on all of (53), including its original normal directions. Consequently (56) bounds the actual mixed quantum currents with cutoff \(T=\pi/2\). Lemma 4 covers every retained complex endpoint on that same rectangle and gives the matching removed-row loss. The [full path assembly](research_uniform_path_trace_assembly.md#7-the-source-theorem-at-powers-seven-and-eight) combines these source bounds with the local action budget and the original nonzero Gaussian coefficient. The phase estimate (56) alone is not being substituted for those finite-source steps. The exact scalar checks for (55), (58)--(61) are included in [check_positive_path_seven_geometry.py](../experiments/check_positive_path_seven_geometry.py), with their current proof dependencies in its [saved record](../repro/results/research-positive-path-seven-geometry.json).

title: A contour-polarized heat family with an actual small-charge initializer
text:
# A contour-polarized heat family with an actual small-charge initializer Private written proof, 16 November 2026. Expand the original finite source by its removed physical-row subsets before choosing contour heights. Freeze for each subset the heights used in its small-charge estimate. Splitting only the retained lower horizontal cosine then gives exact polarized entire families. Their sign average is the original charged source, and every polarization has the original unit-charge endpoint. The all-plus family has a proved nonzero complex initializer and exact signed heat evolution. These families depend on the prescribed polynomial source and frozen contours. They are different from the finite Hermite coupons \(Q_{N,\pm}\). No polarized finite-coupon initializer is inferred. Nor does the construction supply the angle-label coverage or global action-relative bounds needed to reach arbitrary unit-charge targets. ## 1. Fixed operators with the original trace normalization Let \(N\ge2\), \(D=N-1\), \(\eta=(-1)^D\), and \[ 	au_j= rac{\pi(D-2j)}N,\qquad C_{N,n}=e^{\pi i nD^2/(4N)},\qquad W_N(t)= rac{e^{-iNt}}{(1-\eta e^{-iNt})^2}. 	ag{1} \] For an even holomorphic spectator \(A(t)\), write \[ g_n[A](t)=\sin t\,A(t)e^{inNt^2/(4\pi)}. 	ag{2} \] The carrier-removed original trace with the full-Hermite cosine coupon is \[ \mathcal L_{n,\chi}[A] =\eta\sum_{j=0}^{D} \left.\partial_t\{ g_n[A](t)\cos(N(1-\chi)t)\}ight|_{t=	au_j}. 	ag{3} \] It equals \(C_{N,n}^{-1}\phi_N(R_n[A]\mathcal C_{N,\chi})\). The odd simple node is the single value contribution at \(t=0\); all other terms combine in pairs to give the original first normals. The same direct formula holds at \(N=2\). Choose a positive midpoint \(a_N\le\pi\) with \(e^{iNa_N}=-\eta\). For all sufficiently large \(N\), choose the largest such midpoint not exceeding \(19/20\), as in the small-charge proof. The finite number of remaining levels can use \(a_N=\pi\). Define the literal outer-row operator \[ \mathcal O_{n,\chi}[A] =\eta\sum_{|	au_j|\ge a_N} \left.\partial_t\{ g_n[A](t)\cos(N(1-\chi)t)\}ight|_{t=	au_j}. 	ag{4} \] No value or first normal in this sum is dropped. For a fixed \(h>0\) and \(\sigma\in\{+,-\}\), set \[ \mathcal H_{\sigma,n,\chi}^{h}[A] =- rac{N^2}{\pi i} \int_{-a_N-ih}^{a_N-ih} g_n[A](t)e^{\sigma iN(1-\chi)t}W_N(t)\,dt, \qquad \mathcal H_{\cos}^{h}= rac{\mathcal H_+^{h}+ \mathcal H_-^{h}}2. 	ag{5} \] For a chosen side \(\epsilon\in\{+1,-1\}\), the unchanged cosine vertical current is \[ \mathcal V_{n,\chi}^{h,\epsilon}[A] = rac{\epsilon\eta N^2}{\pi} \int_{-h}^{h}  rac{g_n[A](\epsilon a_N+iv) \cos(N(1-\chi)(\epsilon a_N+iv))} {4\cosh^2(Nv/2)}\,dv. 	ag{6} \] The factor \(\epsilon\) retains the orientation: replacing the positive side by the negative side changes the unprefactored integral by a minus sign. The exact retained-trace identity is \[ \mathcal L_{n,\chi} =\mathcal O_{n,\chi} +\mathcal H_{\cos,n,\chi}^{h} +\mathcal V_{n,\chi}^{h,\epsilon}. 	ag{7} \] It uses evenness of the spectator and cosine, not charge integrality. The identity follows from the double-pole residue formula, with the two horizontal sides combined by reflection. Every contour and its endpoints in (4)--(7) will be fixed independently of the evolving power and charge parameters. ## 2. Expand the removed subsets before freezing heights Fix a finite original same-index graph with selected set \(I\), \(m=|I|\ge1\), and degrees \(d_v\ge1\) at selected vertices, counting loop incidences. Retain its original polynomial kernel product \(F_N(\mathbf t;\mathbf u)\), even in each selected angle. The outside angles \(u_w\) label spectral variables \(z_w=-2\cos u_w\); their ordinary polynomial dependence is retained. For the initializer only, set those outside angles to zero, exactly as in the small-charge source theorem. Fix base real powers \(\mathbf b\) and a base charge vector \[  oldsymbol\xi\in(1/4000,1/2000)^I. 	ag{8} \] For each subset \(S\subseteq I\), set the angles in \(S\) to zero and take the small critical point of the remaining graph at charges \(\xi_v\), \(v
otin S\). All original incidences remain, now including the new complete ends. Let its positive heights be \(h_v^S\), \(v
otin S\). For \(S=I\) no heights are needed. Freeze all these numbers. Also freeze \(\epsilon_v=\operatorname{sgn}b_v\) when \(b_v
e0\), and \(\epsilon_v=1\) when \(b_v=0\). Put \[ H_* =\max_{S,v
otin S}h_v^S>0. 	ag{9} \] The small-charge estimates give \(H_*<63/20000\). All choices in (8)--(9) are part of the definition of the family, not parameters silently adjusted during heat evolution. For a sign vector \( oldsymbol\sigma\in\{+,-\}^I\), define \[ \mathfrak Z_{N, oldsymbol\sigma}(\mathbf n, oldsymbol\chi;\mathbf u) =\sum_{S\subseteq I} \left[\prod_{v\in S}\mathcal O_{v,n_v,\chi_v} \prod_{v
otin S}  igl(\mathcal H_{\sigma_v,n_v,\chi_v}^{h_v^S} +\mathcal V_{n_v,\chi_v}^{h_v^S,\epsilon_v} igr) ight]F_N. 	ag{10} \] These are carrier-removed families. Operators in separate coordinates commute. The spectator remains even in each not-yet-contracted coordinate, since the original kernels are even there. Thus (7) can be applied independently after the outer subsets have been expanded. It gives the exact identities \[ 2^{-m}\sum_{ oldsymbol\sigma}\mathfrak Z_{N, oldsymbol\sigma} =\widetilde Z_N(\mathbf n, oldsymbol\chi;\mathbf u), \qquad \mathfrak Z_{N, oldsymbol\sigma}(\mathbf n,\mathbf1;\mathbf u) =\widetilde Z_N(\mathbf n,\mathbf1;\mathbf u). 	ag{11} \] For signs belonging to removed vertices the summand in (10) is independent of that sign; their multiplicity is exactly the one needed for the first equality. At charge one both horizontal exponentials equal one, giving the second equality term by term. Multiplication by \(\prod_v C_{N,n_v}\) restores the original crossing carriers. At integer powers the endpoint is the prescribed original scalar, with both parities and all normals retained. Charge reflection \(\chi_v\mapsto2-\chi_v\) exchanges the sign \(\sigma_v\), leaving every vertical and removed-row operator unchanged. The individual families need not be even about charge one. Away from that endpoint they generally do not factor through the finite spectral quotient: changing a polynomial representative or the frozen heights can change (10). No such change is made here. ## 3. Exact heat evolution and the full-source growth bound Each integrand in (4)--(6) obeys \[ \partial_{n_v} =- rac{i}{4\pi N}\partial_{\chi_v}^2 	ag{12} \] when applied to its Gaussian times its cosine or exponential. In (4), the physical angular derivative commutes with this identity. All finite sums and fixed compact contour integrals commute with the parameter derivatives. Consequently (10) is entire in powers and charges and satisfies (12) in every coordinate. No integration by parts or missing moving-endpoint term is involved. For fixed real powers in a bounded box and free boundaries in a fixed compact set, there are constants \(A,p,C\) such that \[ |\mathfrak Z_{N, oldsymbol\sigma}(\mathbf n, oldsymbol\chi;\mathbf u)| \le A N^p\prod_v(1+|\chi_v|) \exp N\left\{C+\sum_v  igl[\pi|\Im\chi_v|+H_*|1-\Re\chi_v| igr]ight\}. 	ag{13} \] Every angular argument used in (10) has \(|\Re t|\le\pi\) and \(|\Im t|\le H_*\). Its charge exponential is therefore bounded by the corresponding factor in (13); cosine is their mean. Physical normals add polynomial factors and \(1+|\chi_v|\). The original Newton polynomial envelopes on this fixed angular compact give \(N^p e^{CN}\) for the kernels and their fixed mixed normals, as in the local heat theorem. The horizontal \(W_N\) factors are bounded at the fixed positive heights; the vertical denominators in (6) are bounded by one. The finitely many patterns and finite small levels can be absorbed in the constants. This proves (13), also with any fixed number of ordinary free-boundary derivatives. For \(\delta\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}\) and \(v_\delta=e^{-i\operatorname{sgn}(\delta)\pi/4}\), the exact heat formula is \[ \mathfrak Z_N(\mathbf n+\delta\mathbf e_v, oldsymbol\chi) =\sqrt{ rac N{|\delta|}} \int_{\mathbb R}e^{-\pi Nr^2/|\delta|} \mathfrak Z_N(\mathbf n,  oldsymbol\chi+v_\delta r\mathbf e_v)\,dr. 	ag{14} \] Complete the square on each charge exponential before the compact angular integrations. It multiplies that integrand by \(e^{i\delta Nt_v^2/(4\pi)}\). The same identity holds for cosine and after the physical angular derivatives. Bound (13), with the Gaussian quadratic decay, justifies Fubini and all derivatives. It also permits any finite translation of the entire charge line. Thus (14) retains every original current. It does not rely on an incorrect finite-dimensional charge-space claim for (10). ## 4. A genuine holomorphic initializer for the all-plus family Throughout this section the outside angles are specialized to zero, so their spectral variables equal \(-2\). The initializer below is not asserted for arbitrary free-boundary values. Let \(\Phi_{\mathbf b, oldsymbol\chi}\), its small critical point, and \(A_\Gamma( oldsymbol\chi)
e0\) have exactly the original normalization in the small-charge theorem, with carriers removed. If \(e\) is the number of kernel edges in that theorem, then on a fixed complex neighborhood \(U\) of the base point (8), \[  oxed{\quad \mathfrak Z_{N,\mathbf+}(\mathbf b, oldsymbol\chi) =2^m N^{3(m-e)/2} A_\Gamma( oldsymbol\chi) e^{N\Phi_{\mathbf b, oldsymbol\chi}(\mathbf t^*)} (1+O_{m hol}(N^{-1})).\quad} 	ag{15} \] The amplitude is a holomorphic unit after shrinking \(U\), and there is an expansion to every fixed inverse-power order. Through both level parities, every other sign vector obeys, on a possibly smaller \(U\), \[ |\mathfrak Z_{N, oldsymbol\sigma}(\mathbf b, oldsymbol\chi)| \le A N^p e^{N(\Re\Phi_{\mathbf b, oldsymbol\chi}(\mathbf t^*)-\gamma)} \quad( oldsymbol\sigma
e\mathbf+) 	ag{16} \] for some \(\gamma>0\). Here is the source estimate, including the role of the frozen heights. At the real base point, a summand with \(S
e\varnothing\) uses precisely the reduced heights required by the original outer-row proof. Its centered kernel bound retains the losses at every removed incidence and every mixed physical normal. Replacing a remaining horizontal cosine by either exponential does not increase its exponential majorant: at height \(-h\) the plus choice gives charge \(\chi\), and the minus choice gives the larger decaying charge \(2-\chi\). Thus the archived outer-row gap applies to that summand. Likewise every summand with a vertical coordinate has the original mixed-current gap, with the side factor in (6) retained. For \(S=\varnothing\) and no vertical coordinate, \[ W_N(t)e^{iN(1-\chi)t} = rac{e^{-iN\chi t}}{(1-\eta e^{-iNt})^2},\qquad  rac{e^{-iN(1-\chi)t}}{e^{iN(1-\chi)t}} =e^{-2iN(1-\chi)t}. 	ag{17} \] On the fixed lower horizontals at the base point, the second factor has modulus \(e^{-2N(1-\xi_v)h_v^\varnothing}\). Every height is positive. Hence any minus sign gives a strict gap, while all plus signs give exactly the original selected phase and Gaussian density. The only normalization change is the absence of the cosine's factor \(1/2\) at each vertex, proving the factor \(2^m\) in (15). This argument is valid at real nonlattice charges: the exact coupon identities use the same even entire functions and full Hermite data, and all quoted estimates use real charge inequalities rather than integrality of \(N\chi\). Real powers are handled by the canonical crossing extension in the local heat theorem. Its physical values have unit modulus and its normals have polynomial cost. To obtain the complex neighborhood, keep every contour in (10) fixed. A change \(|\delta\chi_v|\le\varepsilon\) changes each of the preceding absolute exponential bounds by at most \(e^{C_1N\varepsilon}\), uniformly over all the compact contour pieces and physical angles. The physical derivatives add only polynomial factors; explicitly their coupon bounds are \(e^{\pi N|\Im\chi|}\) and \(N|1-\chi|e^{\pi N|\Im\chi|}\). Choose \(\varepsilon\) below the finitely many strict gap margins divided by the resulting constants. The continued action changes by \(O(\varepsilon)\), so the gaps remain uniform relative to it. This is an exponential estimate, not pointwise continuity in \(N\). The all-plus saddle moves holomorphically inside the same pole-free thin rectangle. Its local contour can be displaced through that saddle, keeping the ends fixed and the connecting pieces in the existing strict-gap region. The original holomorphic kernel symbols, sine factors and Gaussian determinant stay nonzero. Their standard Taylor expansion gives (15) with uniform holomorphic errors and all fixed orders. The same gap perturbation gives (16). ## 5. What local heat transport now does, and what it does not do Equations (13)--(15) supply an actual initialized family to which the quantitative local heat proof applies. Its growth function is now \(C+\pi|\Im\chi|+H_*|1-\Re\chi|\) in one coordinate. Along a Gaussian line, its extra linear cost is at most \((\pi+H_*)|r|\). Replacing the constant \(\pi\) by \(\pi+H_*\) in that proof's linear tail bound gives the same sufficient small-step theorem, with its excess constant also replaced by the supremum of \(C+\pi|\Im\zeta|+H_*|1-\Re\zeta|-\Re S(\zeta)\) on the certified initial domain. In particular the characteristic, new action and density remain \[ \chi=\zeta+ rac{i\delta}{2\pi}S'(\zeta),\qquad S_\delta=S(\zeta)+ rac{i\delta}{4\pi}S'(\zeta)^2, \qquad a_\delta= rac{a(\zeta)} {\sqrt{1+i\delta S''(\zeta)/(2\pi)}}, 	ag{18} \] with the square root continued from one and with the actual eroded-domain and tail requirements of that theorem. The frozen family is not redefined after a step. Rechoosing its heights would require retaining its exact height-change currents. Iteration still carries the same initially certified classical angle labels; the present construction does not prove that they cover a prescribed arbitrary short filling at unit charge. Nor does (13) replace the whole-source growth by the geometric action. The remaining problem is coverage and a certified chain of action-relative tail bounds for this now initialized family. It is no longer an internal charge-reflection obstruction, since the all-plus family is not itself even about charge one. ## Direct sources and versions The complete final proof and all directly used source implications were read before freezing, retaining earlier full source readbacks only at unchanged hashes. - [Exact complete trace contour](research_exact_complete_trace_contour.md), `a63c66e8078457fa84e8044dc876beca36126348e816de9c6997d2a2610474e8`: double-pole derivative sampling, removed rows and the oriented horizontal/vertical identity. - [Small-charge source](research_small_charge_path_source.md), `c6d0ce2a4ecf1412aa3752cb8a94c6933bb47acab5d96d879c6f1b17b2db2a90`: reduced small saddles, full same-index graph kernel bounds, all mixed-current/removed-row gaps, and the original amplitude. - [Local charged-source heat propagation](research_charged_source_local_heat_propagation.md), `a924922b515aecdedef0c3877d69f0e50da030b9a111220f712a3f6d1bdb926e`: real-power and complex-charge proof extensions, finite exponential envelopes, quantitative local heat estimate and its domain scope. - [Entire charged-source heat reduction](research_entire_charged_source_heat_reduction.md), `33213425be9cac699860a48b23830399c82cd89bea3140cc776274aafe115fba`: canonical crossing carrier, full normal data and Gaussian heat normalization. The finite-space assertion there is not imported for the contour families (10).

title: A hybrid lower-donor kernel for the full physical crossing
Physical highest-block coordinates for the whole intertwiner
text: # Physical highest-block coordinates for the whole intertwiner Private written proof, 19 November 2026. The physical highest block on one head is a pole-free coordinate on the entire actual intertwiner space near the complete meridian. Both endpoint columns and rows, and then every finite matrix block, are recovered from that one remaining-head operator. Unlike the constant coefficient after the prefix change of frame, this coordinate does not require inverting a resonant remaining Cartan eigenvalue. The seed is an arbitrary Cartan-preserving operator, not a scalar vacuum value. Its freedom is essential. The theorem supplies an exact finite reconstruction, a coupled low-degree norm envelope, whole-cap bounds, and true meridian derivatives. It does not supply an analytic phase or a nonzero closing coefficient for an unspecified seed. The sole complete direct is C, pinned below. We use its finite prefix operator and actual generator relations. All endpoint reconstruction, nilpotence, terminal compatibility and estimates are proved here. ## 1. Actual heads and the endpoint coordinate Fix \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), and \(Q=q^2\). Keep \(q\) fixed and put \(M=e^\mu\), \(x=-M/q\). On one head, \[ Kw_a=xQ^{-a}w_a,\qquad Fw_a=(1-Q^{a+1})w_{a+1},\qquad Ew_a=e_aw_{a-1},\quad e_a=MQ^{-a}-M^{-1}. \tag{1} \] The lowering formula is used only for \(1\le a\le d\). The outward arrows \(Ew_0,Fw_d\) are zero. In endpoint equations below, \(e_0=e_N=0\) means these forced arrows, not evaluation of the scalar expression in (1) at an omitted index. Set \(f_a=\prod_{j=1}^a(1-Q^j)\), with \(f_0=1\). There are \(m=r+1\) heads. Write \(U\) for the last \(r\) heads and \(E,K,F\) for their ordered total generators; for \(r=0\) use \(U=\mathbb C\), \(E=F=0\), \(K=1\). The total operators are \[ E_\Sigma=E_1K+E,\qquad F_\Sigma=F_1+K_1^{-1}F,\qquad K_\Sigma=K_1K. \tag{2} \] All products in (2) keep their tensor-head order. Let \(i_a:U\to V_1\otimes U\) and \(p_a:V_1\otimes U\to U\) be the actual inclusion and projection at first-head occupation \(a\). For an operator \(W\), write \(W_{ab}=p_aWi_b\). Define \[ \mathcal A_U=\{H\in\operatorname{End}(U):[K,H]=0\},\qquad \mathcal C_V=\{W:[E_\Sigma,W]=[F_\Sigma,W]=[K_\Sigma,W]=0\}. \tag{3} \] Since \(K(M)=M^rK(1)\), the vector space \(\mathcal A_U\) is independent of \(M\). We also allow its exact integer-degree-preserving subspace; integer degree is not identified modulo \(N\). Whenever \[ e_1e_2\cdots e_d\ne0, \tag{4} \] the map \[ \boxed{\quad\mathcal C_V\longrightarrow\mathcal A_U, \qquad W\longmapsto H=W_{00}\quad} \tag{5} \] is a linear isomorphism. It is not asserted to preserve products. Its inverse is holomorphic wherever (4) holds. In particular it is holomorphic at \(M=1\), and throughout every scaled collar \[ M=e^{u/N},\qquad |u|<\eta<\pi. \tag{6} \] The same assertion holds with exact integer-degree preservation imposed on both sides. It applies to an actual physical braid endomorphism with its end colors matched; its literal crossing and framing scalars remain part of \(W\) and therefore of \(H\). ## 2. The finite endpoint equations Taking first-head blocks of the two intertwining equations gives \[ \boxed{\quad e_{a+1}K W_{a+1,b} =e_bW_{a,b-1}K-[E,W_{ab}], \quad} \tag{7} \] \[ \boxed{\quad (1-Q^{b+1})W_{a,b+1} =(1-Q^a)W_{a-1,b} +x^{-1}(Q^aFW_{ab}-Q^bW_{ab}F). \quad} \tag{8} \] Use zero blocks outside \(0\le a,b\le d\). Equation (7) includes the final \(a=d\) compatibility row; (8) includes the final \(b=d\) compatibility row. No inverse is taken in either omitted row. Cartan commutation says exactly \[ KW_{ab}=Q^{a-b}W_{ab}K. \tag{9} \] In particular, the first column \(C_a=W_{a0}\) is obtained by \[ C_0=H,\qquad C_{a+1}=-e_{a+1}^{-1}K^{-1}[E,C_a] \quad(0\le a<d). \tag{10} \] The first row can independently be computed by \[ W_{00}=H,\qquad W_{0,b+1}=\frac{x^{-1}}{1-Q^{b+1}} (FW_{0b}-Q^bW_{0b}F). \tag{11} \] Thus both physical endpoint families are determined, with their actual relative orders. They are not replaced by a common scalar. There are useful closed finite formulas. Let \(L_E,R_E\) denote left and right multiplication by \(E\), and similarly for \(F\). They commute with each other when they act on opposite sides. The relation \(EK^{-1}=QK^{-1}E\) gives \[ C_a=\frac{(-1)^aK^{-a}}{e_1\cdots e_a} \prod_{j=0}^{a-1}(Q^jL_E-R_E)H, \qquad W_{0b}=\frac{x^{-b}}{f_b} \prod_{j=0}^{b-1}(L_F-Q^jR_F)H. \tag{12} \] The \(K^{-a}\) in the first expression acts on the left, after the displayed product. Formula (12) follows by induction from (10)--(11), and retains the two distinct endpoint polarizations. ## 3. Existence and every terminal row We first verify the nilpotence used to close the reconstruction. The summands \(E_i\prod_{j>i}K_j\) of an ordered total \(E\) pairwise \(Q\)-commute. The summands \((\prod_{j<i}K_j^{-1})F_i\) of a total \(F\) pairwise \(Q^{-1}\)-commute. At a primitive root the intermediate \(N\)-th quantum binomial coefficients vanish: their numerator contains \(1-Q^N\), and their denominators only contain \(1-Q^j\), \(0<j<N\). Expanding first for an indeterminate quantum parameter and then evaluating proves the finite identity. Induction on the number of summands, and the forced head caps, therefore give \[ E_\Sigma^N=F_\Sigma^N=E^N=F^N=0. \tag{13} \] This is at fixed \(q_N\) for every meridian in question, with no ordinary-color quantum-normal specialization. Given any \(H\in\mathcal A_U\), construct \(C_a\) by (10), and put \(V_H=\sum_{a=0}^di_aC_a:U\to V_1\otimes U\). The weight relation \(KC_a=Q^aC_aK\) follows inductively. Equation (10) gives \[ E_\Sigma V_H-V_HE=i_dR, \qquad R=[E,C_d]. \tag{14} \] The apparent last row vanishes automatically. Indeed telescope the \(N\)-th powers in (13): \[ 0=E_\Sigma^NV_H-V_HE^N =\sum_{j=0}^dE_\Sigma^j i_dR E^{d-j}. \tag{15} \] Apply \(p_0\). Fewer than \(d\) factors of \(E_\Sigma\) cannot lower the first head from \(d\) to zero. For \(j=d\), every factor must use its first-head lowering summand, whose product is \((e_1\cdots e_d)K^d\). Thus \[ (e_1\cdots e_d)K^dR=0. \tag{16} \] Condition (4) and invertibility of \(K\) imply \(R=0\). C's exact finite prefix change of frame is \[ S=\sum_{j=0}^d\frac{(x^{-1}L_1F)^j}{f_j},\qquad S^{-1}=\sum_{j=0}^d \frac{(-1)^jQ^{j(j-1)/2}(x^{-1}L_1F)^j}{f_j}, \quad L_1w_a=w_{a-1},\quad L_1w_0=0. \tag{17} \] It satisfies \(S^{-1}F_\Sigma S=F_1\), commutes with the total Cartan, and \(Si_0=i_0\). Consequently \[ Si_b=f_b^{-1}F_\Sigma^bi_0. \tag{18} \] Define a finite operator \(T_H\), and then \(W_H\), by \[ T_H i_b=f_b^{-1}F_\Sigma^bV_H\quad(0\le b\le d), \qquad W_H=T_HS^{-1}. \tag{19} \] Equation (13) includes the top \(F\) row, so (19) commutes with \(F_\Sigma\). Its weights give \([K_\Sigma,W_H]=0\), and its physical first column is \(V_H\). The actual root relation \([E_\Sigma,F_\Sigma]=(q-q^{-1})(K_\Sigma-K_\Sigma^{-1})\) then implies that \([E_\Sigma,W_H]\) commutes with \(F_\Sigma\). By (14)--(16) it vanishes on \(i_0U\). The vectors in (18) span the whole space, so it vanishes everywhere. This proves existence and both terminal equations in (7)--(8). Conversely (7) determines the first column of any intertwiner from \(H\); commutation with \(F_\Sigma\) and (18) then determines the whole operator by (19). This proves uniqueness and (5). Each operation in (10),(17),(19) preserves the exact total integer degree when \(H\) has degree zero, which proves the integer version. Only \(e_1,\ldots,e_d\), \(f_1,\ldots,f_d\), and units \(K,x\) are divided by. Their asserted nonvanishing proves holomorphicity. ## 4. Actual collar bounds and coupled low degrees Give every occupation basis its standard Euclidean norm. Fix the number of heads and \(0<\eta<\pi\). All constants below may depend on those choices, but not on \(N\), \(u\), or the seed. For \(|u|\le\eta\), (1) gives the exact expression \[ e_j=-2i e^{-\pi i j/N} \sin\big((\pi j+iu)/N\big). \tag{20} \] Since the real part of its sine argument lies strictly between zero and \(\pi\), the elementary inequalities \(|\sin(s+it)|\ge|\sin s|\) and \(\sin s\ge(2/\pi)\min(s,\pi-s)\) yield \[ |e_j|\ge \frac{4(\pi-\eta)}{\pi} \frac{\min(j,N-j)}{N},\qquad 1\le j<N. \tag{21} \] All \(e_j\) also have a uniform upper bound. The analogous bounds for \(1-Q^j\), and an elementary factorial estimate, imply \[ e^{-cN}\le |e_1\cdots e_a|\le e^{cN},\qquad e^{-cN}\le |f_a|\le e^{cN}\quad(0\le a<N). \tag{22} \] These estimates control all prefix products, not just the full product. For an explicit lower-bound argument, replace each factor by a constant times \(\min(j,N-j)/N\), with that constant at most one. Every partial product of these numbers is at least their full product, and \(n!\ge(n/e)^n\) bounds the latter below by \(e^{-cN}\). The actual fixed-width operators \(E,F,E_\Sigma,F_\Sigma,K^{\pm1}\) have uniformly bounded norm on this collar. Moreover \(\|K^{\pm a}\|\le e^{r\eta}\) for \(a\le d\). Formula (12) therefore bounds every \(C_a\) by \(e^{cN}\|H\|\). Formula (17) bounds \(S^{\pm1}\) by \(e^{cN}\). Finally (19), (22), and the finite number of blocks give \[ \boxed{\qquad \|H\|\le\|W_H\|\le e^{cN}\|H\|. \qquad}\tag{23} \] Polynomial factors in \(N\) have been absorbed into \(e^{cN}\). In particular there is no estimate of the form \(N^{cN}\) hidden in the reconstruction. There is a more informative coupled endpoint estimate. Choose a fixed \(0<\delta<1/2\). For \(a\le\delta N\), (21) gives \[ \|W_{a0}\|\le\frac{(cN)^a}{a!}\|H\|. \tag{24} \] For \(a+b+1\le\delta N\), (8) gives, with a larger fixed \(c\), \[ (b+1)\|W_{a,b+1}\| \le c a\|W_{a-1,b}\|+cN\|W_{ab}\|. \tag{25} \] Here \(|1-Q^a|\le 2\pi a/N\), whereas \(|1-Q^{b+1}|\ge4(b+1)/N\). The two \(F\) terms have bounded coefficients, including the exact \(x^{-1}\). For nonnegative formal variables \(s,t\), define \[ \mathcal M_N(s,t)=\frac1{1-cst} \exp\left(cN\left[t+\frac{s}{1-cst}\right]\right). \tag{26} \] It has nonnegative coefficients and satisfies \[ \partial_t\mathcal M_N =cs^2\partial_s\mathcal M_N+cs\mathcal M_N+cN\mathcal M_N, \qquad \mathcal M_N(s,0)=e^{cNs}. \tag{27} \] Equations (24)--(25), by induction on \(b\), show that \[ \|W_{ab}\|\le\|H\|[s^at^b]\mathcal M_N(s,t) \quad(a+b\le\delta N). \tag{28} \] All terms used in this induction stay within the displayed low band. Thus this is a coupled two-endpoint estimate, not two unrelated one-sided bounds. For the whole finite operator-valued endpoint polynomial in the ordinary physical first-head coordinates \(\mathcal W_H(s,t)=\sum_{a,b=0}^dW_{ab}s^at^b\), the remaining cap is also controlled. Equation (23) gives, for \(0<\rho<1\), \[ \left\|\sum_{a+b>\delta N}W_{ab}s^at^b\right\| \le N^2e^{cN}\rho^{\lfloor\delta N\rfloor+1}\|H\|, \qquad |s|,|t|\le\rho. \tag{29} \] After the fixed cap constant is known, shrinking \(\rho\) makes (29) at most \(e^{-\gamma N}\|H\|\), for any prescribed fixed \(\gamma>0\). The low part is bounded by \(\mathcal M_N(|s|,|t|)\|H\|\). This pays the complete cap in an actual endpoint norm estimate; it does not turn an upper bound relative to \(\|H\|\) into a lower bound for a scalar contraction. An additional factorial or ordinary-binomial endpoint gauge changes these coefficient bounds; its analytic effect is not included in the envelope (26). ## 5. True meridian jets and the original closing Let \(H(\mu)\) be holomorphic with values in the fixed space \(\mathcal A_U\). Its extension in (19) is the literal fixed- \(q_N\) meridian family. No quantum parameter is differentiated. For \(0<\eta<\eta'<\pi\), Cauchy's formula and (23) imply, for each fixed integer \(j\ge0\), provided the seed is holomorphic on a neighborhood of the closed larger collar, \[ \sup_{|\mu|\le\eta/N}\|\partial_\mu^jW_H(\mu)\| \le j!\left(\frac{N}{\eta'-\eta}\right)^j e^{cN} \sup_{|\mu|\le\eta'/N}\|H(\mu)\|. \tag{30} \] The same argument differentiates (28)--(29) on smaller collars. All first-head coefficients, tail coproducts, and changes of frame are differentiated. For example differentiating (10) gives \[ e_aK\dot C_a=-[E,\dot C_{a-1}]-[\dot E,C_{a-1}] -(\dot e_a+r e_a)KC_a, \qquad \dot e_a=MQ^{-a}+M^{-1}. \tag{31} \] Dots denote \(\partial_\mu\), and \(\dot K=rK\). The omitted lowering arrows remain identically zero and therefore have zero derivative. The full row normal is obtained by differentiating (8), including \(\partial_\mu x^{-1}=-x^{-1}\) and the actual \(\dot F\). Thus the root value and first normal of both endpoint families are fixed by \(H(0),\dot H(0)\), with no deleted resonance or terminal current. The original highest-cut pivotal source is particularly direct in these coordinates: \[ \boxed{\quad \Phi_0(W)=\operatorname{Tr}_{V_1\otimes U} ((P_0\otimes K^{1-N})W) =\operatorname{Tr}_U(K^{1-N}H). \quad}\tag{32} \] There is no new pivot on the opened head and no reset of a transformed source. Its true first meridian derivative is \[ \dot\Phi_0(W)=\operatorname{Tr}_U \big(K^{1-N}\dot H+r(1-N)K^{1-N}H\big). \tag{33} \] Any separately prescribed exterior scalar multiplies (32), with its own derivative in (33). Scalars already included in the actual word remain in \(H\). No nonzero assertion about this finite trace follows from (23), nor from invertibility of an actual word. ## 6. Exact composition and the remaining seed The coordinate (5) has an explicit transported product. Define \(U_a(H)=W_H{}_{0a}\) and \(V_a(H)=W_H{}_{a0}\) by (12). Then \[ \boxed{\qquad H_1\star H_2=\sum_{a=0}^d U_a(H_1)V_a(H_2),\qquad W_{H_1\star H_2}=W_{H_1}W_{H_2}. \qquad}\tag{34} \] This is the literal first-head matrix multiplication, with no reset of intermediate rows. It is associative by (5), has identity \(I_U\), and retains all finite transfer indices. The original closing of a product is therefore exactly \[ \Phi_0(W_{H_L}\cdots W_{H_1}) =\tau(H_L\star\cdots\star H_1),\qquad \tau(H)=\operatorname{Tr}_U(K^{1-N}H). \tag{35} \] Differentiating this finite product differentiates \(U_a,V_a\), the seeds, and the pivot, as in (30)--(33). Formula (35) supplies no positivity or nonvanishing for an invertible product. For comparison only, C's transformed constant term is \(B_0=p_0S^{-1}Wi_0\). The exact relation to the present seed is \[ B_0=\sum_{a=0}^d \frac{(-1)^aQ^{a(a-1)/2}x^{-a}}{f_a}\,F^aC_a. \tag{36} \] It is holomorphic at the complete point. Generically, where all \(b_n=MKQ^{-n}-M^{-1}K^{-1}\) are invertible, C reconstructs the whole operator from \(B_0\). Thus (36) is then an invertible linear change between two copies of \(\mathcal A_U\): injectivity follows from C's recursion and surjectivity from finite equal dimensions and (5). The \(B_0\) chart is also multiplicative there, because it is the constant coefficient of the \(F_1\)-Toeplitz normal form. The physical \(H\) chart need not be multiplicative. At \(M=1\), (36) can be singular, as C's explicit source coupon shows; the physical chart (5) stays nonsingular. This distinction addresses the actual endpoint reconstruction problem but does not eliminate its seed. Every operator in \(\mathcal A_U\) really is allowed by the homogeneous total intertwiner equations. In particular those equations alone cannot specify the remaining-head phase, its zeros, or its prescribed pivotal trace. The physical \(H\) generally does not commute with the remaining \(E,F\), so (5) cannot simply be iterated on \(H\) to erase another head. The initialized Gauss-type analytic propagation would additionally need actual estimates for this coupled remaining-head seed, or a separate source-specific identity fixing it. Equations (23)--(30) are genuine finite transport bounds, but do not provide a uniform analytic logarithm or a nonzero amplitude for an arbitrary seed. No geometric relative-cycle coefficient, full angular-period lower bound, or finite-exception conclusion is inferred. ## Complete direct-source pin * C: notes/research_prefix_commutant_and_pointed_normal_functional.md, SHA256 b4fb801a1482316aebb4799f1d0b80d5b43ced39138d903c04cfde811ca166b0. Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used; frozen and public files were unchanged.

title: A uniform packet for the physical normal-defect rows
text:
# A uniform packet for the physical normal-defect rows Research proof, 4 November 2026. Frozen manuscripts are unchanged. The half-charge observation determines the actual interpolation-normal defect at every physical row, not only at complex geometric colors. Rows outside the shifted contour require an exact cancellation of two Cauchy poles. The remaining regular part has a smaller exponential rate, by the original first-normal bound and polynomial collocation estimates. This gives one uniform source packet at both parities. The result concerns the specified complete-end source. It does not justify applying an exponentially ill-conditioned shared-index transform to a relative \(O(N^{-1})\) row error. ## 1. Unified notation and statement For even \(N=2m\), use \[ Q_N(w)=2T_m(w/2),\qquad \mathcal L_N(w)=\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}e_j(w)e_j(-2). \] For odd \(N=2m+1\), use \[ Q_N(w)=(w+2)\{U_m(w/2)-U_{m-1}(w/2)\},\qquad \mathcal L_N(w)=K_N(w,-2). \] In both cases \(Q_N\) is the monic polynomial of all distinct physical roots \(c_a\), and \(\epsilon_N=(-1)^m\). Set \[  egin{split} h_{n,N}(w)&= e^{inN\arccos(-w/2)^2/(4\pi)}\mathcal L_N(w),\ I_{n,N}&=	ext{the ordinary interpolant of \(h_{n,N}(c_a)\) at all distinct physical roots},\ D_{n,N}(w)&= rac{h_{n,N}(w)-I_{n,N}(w)}{Q_N(w)} . \end{split} 	ag{1} \] The analytic branch of the squared inverse cosine is the one fixed on \(\mathbb C\setminus[2,\infty)\). At every double root, \[ h'_{n,N}(c_a)-I'_{n,N}(c_a)=Q_N'(c_a)D_{n,N}(c_a) 	ag{2} \] is the actual first-normal difference. At the odd simple root there is no original first normal; \(D_{n,N}(-2)\) is a value of the holomorphic function (1). The odd trace uses its separate top-degree term, as in the [exact odd trace formula](research_odd_half_charge_observation.md#3-the-original-odd-trace-still-has-its-top-degree-term). Let \(t_0=a_0-iH_0\) be the half-charge saddle at fixed real \(n\ge3\), and write \[  egin{split} nt_0+2i\operatorname{asinh}	an(t_0/2)&=\pi,\ S_n(t)&=\Psi(t)+int^2/(4\pi)-it/2,\quad \mathcal S_n=S_n(t_0),\quad M_n=\Re\mathcal S_n,\ A_n&=\{\sec(t_0/2)-in\}/(2\pi),\ b_n^{m e}(w)&= rac{\sqrt{2\pi}}{\pi i}  rac{\sin t_0\,a_e(t_0,0)} {(w+2\cos t_0)\sqrt{A_n}},\ b_n^{m o}(w)&= rac{\sqrt{2\pi}}{\pi}  rac{\cos(t_0/2)a_e(t_0,0)} {(w+2\cos t_0)\sqrt{A_n}}. \end{split} 	ag{3} \] These are exactly the coefficients of the proved [even](research_complete_source_pick_observation.md#5-a-nonzero-half-charge-observation) and [odd](research_odd_half_charge_observation.md#2-the-half-charge-packet-and-the-exterior-residue) observations, with their original normalization. **Theorem 1.** Uniformly over all distinct physical roots, as \(N\) tends to infinity through its stated parity, \[  oxed{\quad D_{n,N}(c_a) =-\epsilon_N N^{-2}b_n^{m e/o}(c_a)e^{N\mathcal S_n} (1+O(N^{-1})). \quad} 	ag{4} \] The error constant may depend on the fixed crossing time. Both rational coefficients in (3) are bounded above and away from zero on the whole real interval \([-2,2]\). Thus all these defect values are nonzero for sufficiently large levels. ## 2. The source tail, including its actual first normals Choose the parity-appropriate midpoint cuts \(T_N	o\pi/2\) used in the observation proofs. Split the nodes into the inside set \(	au_a<T_N\) and the outside set \(	au_a>T_N\), where \(	au_a=\arccos(-c_a/2)\). Let \(I^{m tail}_{n,N}\) interpolate \(h_{n,N}(c_a)\) at the outside nodes and zero at all inside nodes. The omitted Cauchy sum is exactly \[ \mathcal T_{n,N}(w) =N\, rac{I^{m tail}_{n,N}(w)}{Q_N(w)}. 	ag{5} \] The positive physical-row recurrence and its endpoint normalization give, uniformly over the outside nodes, \[ |\mathcal L_N(c_a)|\le CN^A e^{N\Psi(\pi/2)}. 	ag{6} \] Indeed the complete values decrease with increasing \(	au_a\); the first omitted row lies at \(\pi/2+O(N^{-1})\). Its absolute logarithmic asymptotic has this rate. The same exponential bound holds for the actual first derivative of \(\mathcal L_N\) at the outside nodes. These nodes are double at both parities. The [all-color first-normal bound, Lemma 5](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_all_color_path_normal_bound.md#5-the-complete-normal-determinant-at-every-color-assignment) gives \[ |\partial_zK_N(c_a,-2)|\le N^{11}K_N(c_a,-2). \] At odd levels \(\mathcal L_N=K_N(\,\cdot\,,-2)\). At even levels their radical difference has polynomial real interval norm and polynomial first ordinary derivative, by the [radical Fourier bound](research_high_newton_radical_contraction.md#7-fourier-bounds-for-the-original-radical-polynomials) and the ordinary Markov inequality. Since every physical complete value is at least one, that polynomial correction is absorbed in (6). The crossing's logarithmic derivative at a double root is \(inN	au_a/(4\pi\sin	au_a)=O_n(N^2)\). Consequently \[ \max_{m outside} \{|h_{n,N}(c_a)|+|h'_{n,N}(c_a)|\} \le CN^A e^{N\Psi(\pi/2)}. 	ag{7} \] This is an estimate of the original first normals, not a derivative of a value-only asymptotic. Ordinary collocation on these nodes costs only powers of \(N\). In fact \(\sigma_a=N/Q_N'(c_a)\) obeys \[ 2/N\le|\sigma_a|\le2,\qquad |c_a-c_b|\ge4/N^2\quad(a
e b), 	ag{8} \] with the odd simple weight of modulus one included. The first inequalities follow from the explicit Chebyshev weights; the second follows from the sine difference formula for the physical nodes. The cardinal differentiation matrix has off-diagonal entries \[  rac{Q_N'(c_a)} {Q_N'(c_b)(c_a-c_b)} \] and diagonal entries \(\sum_{b
e a}(c_a-c_b)^{-1}\). It therefore has infinity norm at most \(CN^4\). By (7), \[ \max_a |(I^{m tail}_{n,N})'(c_a)| \le CN^A e^{N\Psi(\pi/2)} . 	ag{9} \] Also \(1/|Q_N'(c_a)|\le2/N\). ## 3. Exact cancellation and a uniform contour packet Let \(\mathcal J_{n,N}(w)\) be the exact shifted cosine or sine contour, without its omitted physical rows. At an inside physical node the interior residue identity gives \[ D_{n,N}(c_a) =- rac{\mathcal J_{n,N}(c_a)+\mathcal T_{n,N}(c_a)}{N}. 	ag{10} \] The tail sum has no pole there. Its node gaps (8), weights bounded by two, and (7) bound it by \(CN^A e^{N\Psi(\pi/2)}\). At an outside node use the exterior identity and (5) before taking the limit: \[ D_{n,N}(w) = rac{h_{n,N}(w)-I^{m tail}_{n,N}(w)}{Q_N(w)} - rac{\mathcal J_{n,N}(w)}N . \] The numerator vanishes at that node. Hence the exact regular value is \[ D_{n,N}(c_a) = rac{h'_{n,N}(c_a)-(I^{m tail}_{n,N})'(c_a)} {Q_N'(c_a)} - rac{\mathcal J_{n,N}(c_a)}N . 	ag{11} \] Equations (7)–(9) bound the first term by \(CN^A e^{N\Psi(\pi/2)}\). Thus the same conclusion holds at every node: \[ D_{n,N}(c_a) =- rac{\mathcal J_{n,N}(c_a)}N +O(N^A e^{N\Psi(\pi/2)}). 	ag{12} \] The contour proof of the observation packet is uniform at all these real evaluation colors. Here is the point requiring care. On the two horizontal sides, \(-2\cos z\) is a compact curve disjoint from \([-2,2]\), so the Cauchy denominator is uniformly bounded away from zero. On each midpoint vertical side, \[ |-2\cos	au_a+2\cos(T_N+iv)|\ge c/N \qquad(|v|\le H_0) 	ag{13} \] for all physical nodes and all sufficiently large levels. To see this, for \(|v|\ge1/N\) use \(2|\sin T_N\sinh v|\ge c/N\). For \(|v|<1/N\), the physical angles are at least \(\pi/N\) from the midpoint \(T_N\), and \(T_N=\pi/2+O(N^{-1})\). Their real cosine separation is at least \(c/N\), whereas the perturbation \(\cos T_N(\cosh v-1)\) is \(O(N^{-3})\). This proves (13). Thus near the vertical cut the Cauchy factor costs only a power of \(N\). The vertical and noncritical horizontal parts already have a fixed exponential gap. At the saddle itself \(c_a+2\cos t_0\) is uniformly separated from zero for \(c_a\in[-2,2]\), because \(\Im\cos t_0
e0\). The usual local expansion is consequently uniform over the full physical interval: \[ \mathcal J_{n,N}(c_a) =\epsilon_N N^{-1}b_n^{m e/o}(c_a)e^{N\mathcal S_n} (1+O(N^{-1})). 	ag{14} \] The source tail satisfies \(\Psi(\pi/2)<M_n-7/80\), by the proved half-charge comparison. Substituting (14) in (12) and absorbing the polynomially weighted exponential error proves (4). The odd endpoint \(c_m=-2\) lies in the inside set, so it uses (10) and its exact ramified residue. No nonexistent odd physical first normal was used in (7) or (11). ## 4. What can be transported from this estimate Equation (4) gives a nonzero source coefficient for every actual physical normal-defect row, with one common exponential phase and the explicit rational observation profile. It can be used inside identities that retain the whole original finite source. It does not license replacing the rows by their leading terms inside an arbitrary oscillatory shared-index sum. Such a sum can magnify the \(O(N^{-1})\) row error exponentially relative to its signed value. The exact Cauchy or reduced-node expression must be retained until the relevant collective contour has been controlled. Likewise the odd top-degree trace term remains the one displayed in the linked odd-level note. ## 5. A fixed complex neighborhood of the retained real interval The physical-row estimate has a holomorphic extension away from the spectral endpoint \(2\). This matters for the reduced-node Cauchy formula: its contour can be kept a fixed distance from the nodes. The extension still uses the literal low complete-end source in (1). It does not assert an estimate for the full even off-grid kernel. **Theorem 2.** Fix real \(n\ge3\) and \(0<\delta<4\). There is an open neighborhood \(\mathcal U\) of \([-2,2-\delta]\), independent of the level, on which \[ D_{n,N}(w)=-\epsilon_NN^{-2}b_n^{m e/o}(w)e^{N\mathcal S_n} (1+O(N^{-1})). 	ag{15} \] The error is uniform on a fixed smaller neighborhood, including every fixed ordinary spectral derivative in the differentiated holomorphic sense. In particular the actual defect is nonzero there for all sufficiently large levels of the stated parity. *Proof.* Put \(T_\delta=\arccos(-1+\delta/2)<\pi\), and choose \[ \max(T_\delta,\pi/2)<T<\pi. 	ag{16} \] Let \(T_{0,N}	o\pi/2\) and \(T_N	o T\) be physical midpoint cuts of the appropriate parity. Use the original half-charge contour of height \(H_0\) for \(|\Re t|\le T_{0,N}\). At each of its two real ends join vertically to a smaller positive height \(\varepsilon\), then continue at that height to \(\pm T_N\). Close by the vertical sides at \(\pm T_N\), and use the reflected upper boundary. This is one closed, symmetric angular contour. The two vertical joins at \(\pm T_{0,N}\) are retained parts of the old midpoint sides, not discarded deformation terms. We choose \(\varepsilon\) small enough to prove a strict gap on every added piece. The actual complete-end low polynomial satisfies \[ \mathcal L_N(-2\cos t) =\exp\{N\Psi(t)+O(\log N)\} 	ag{17} \] on compact subsets of \(\Re(-2\cos t)<2\), at both parities. This is the [even low-kernel theorem](research_even_complete_low_kernel.md#5-consequence-for-the-geometric-exponential-rate) and the [odd last-row theorem](research_last_physical_row_riccati.md#5-the-actual-complete-end-kernel-at-odd-levels), with their actual logarithmic normalization. Since \(T<\pi\), the outer pieces lie in such a compact subset for sufficiently small \(\varepsilon\). On the real interval, \(\Psi\) is even and strictly decreasing on \((0,\pi)\), because \(\Psi'(a)=-\operatorname{asinh}(	an(a/2))/\pi<0\). Write \(g=M_n-\Psi(\pi/2)>7/80\). Uniform continuity on the fixed outer interval permits \(\varepsilon>0\) so small that \[ \Re\Psi(a+ih)+ rac{n|a h|}{2\pi} \le \Psi(\pi/2)+g/3<M_n \quad \left\{ egin{array}{l} \pi/2-o(1)\le|a|\le T+o(1),\ |h|\le\varepsilon. \end{array}ight. 	ag{18} \] The \(o(1)\) allowances here are just the midpoint errors \(O(N^{-1})\); choose a fixed margin first, then take large \(N\). The exact cosine or sine denominator has size at most \(C e^{-N|h|/2}\) after inversion on the horizontal pieces and on the outer midpoint sides. Thus (18) bounds all these pieces, even after dropping that favorable exponential factor. On the two joins at \(\pm T_{0,N}\), the already proved half-charge connector bounds apply to every height between \(\varepsilon\) and \(H_0\). Their fixed gap is unchanged. The image of the fixed limiting symmetric angular boundary under \(t\mapsto-2\cos t\) encloses \([-2,2-\delta]\) and is separated from it. Choose \(\mathcal U\) with compact closure strictly inside that image, separated from the boundary and from the omitted real physical nodes \(	au_a>T_N\). Choose these separations with a positive fixed margin. The midpoint adjustments then leave \(\mathcal U\) inside every sufficiently large level's contour, with the same separation bounds. All angular Cauchy denominators are then uniformly bounded, with their fixed \(w\)-derivatives. The saddle color \(-2\cos t_0\) lies on the boundary, so \(b_n^{m e/o}\) has no pole or zero on this smaller neighborhood. Let \(\mathcal J^{m tap}_{n,N}(w)\) be the exact observation integral on this tapered contour, with the original parity scalar, and let \(\mathcal T^{m tap}_{n,N}(w)\) be its omitted physical Cauchy sum. Every target color is inside, so the exact interior residue identity gives \[ D_{n,N}(w)=- rac{ \mathcal J^{m tap}_{n,N}(w) +\mathcal T^{m tap}_{n,N}(w)}{N}. 	ag{19} \] At the physical nodes this identity is interpreted by its removable continuation. It retains the odd simple-node residue exactly. The same positive physical-row monotonicity used in (6), now at \(T_N\), bounds the omitted sum by \(N^A e^{N\Psi(T)}\), uniformly on \(\mathcal U\). The denominators are separated there, and \(\Psi(T)<\Psi(\pi/2)\). The central horizontal pieces and their nonzero saddle are the original ones. All added pieces, joins and omitted rows have the strict gaps just proved. Therefore the local Gaussian computation, including the two equal angular copies and the parity scalar, gives \[ \mathcal J^{m tap}_{n,N}(w) =\epsilon_NN^{-1}b_n^{m e/o}(w)e^{N\mathcal S_n} (1+O(N^{-1})) 	ag{20} \] uniformly on \(\mathcal U\). Equations (19)–(20) prove (15). The functions and normalized remainder are holomorphic; Cauchy's formula on smaller neighborhoods proves the derivative statement. No physical value or first normal has been replaced before taking the exact observation. \(\square\) Here is an explicit consequence for the even reduced-node transform. It estimates the whole source, without substituting a finite asymptotic expansion into an increasing-order divided difference. Fix \(0<\alpha<1/2\), and choose a fixed positively oriented contour \(\Gamma\subset\mathcal U\) around the real interval containing all \(c_a\) with \(a\ge\alpha N\), for large \(N\). Such a choice is possible by taking \(0<\delta<2-2\cos(2\pi\alpha)\) in Theorem 2. The contour can be chosen at a fixed positive distance from this interval. For \(x\in[\alpha,1/2]\), set \[ J(x)=\int_0^x\log(2\sin\pi r)\,dr,\qquad V_x(z)=\int_x^{1/2}\log|z-2\cos(2\pi r)|\,dr. 	ag{21} \] Then, uniformly for \(\alpha N\le j<N/2\), the original trace in the [reduced-node formula](research_complete_source_pick_observation.md#complex-colors-and-the-exact-normal-defect) satisfies \[ \left|\phi_N[R^n\mathcal L_Ne_j]ight| \le C N^A\exp\!\left\{ N\left[M_n-2J(j/N)-\min_{z\in\Gamma}V_{j/N}(z)ight] ight\}. 	ag{22} \] Indeed \(|D_{n,N}|\le C N^{-2}e^{NM_n}\) on \(\Gamma\), while the exact trace has prefactor \(N^2/S_j^2\) and denominator \(Q_{j,N}\). Uniform midpoint summation on this separated contour gives \(\log|Q_{j,N}(z)|=NV_{j/N}(z)+O(1)\), and the original sine factorial gives \(\log S_j=NJ(j/N)+O(\log N)\). These are upper bounds applied to the exact contour, proving (22). The potential in (22) is explicit, but no comparison of its minimum with the pair's geometric rate is asserted here. In particular, holomorphic control on a fixed contour does not by itself make the relative \(O(N^{-1})\) error small after an order-\(N\) divided difference. The grouped block currents remain part of the original pair calculation. The exact vanishing moments give a familiar polynomial-approximation version of (22), but that version does not reach the pair rate. Here is a quantitative comparison that fixes its scope. Let \(N=4k+2\), \(j=k\). Then \(c_j=0\), the retained nodes lie in \([-2,0]\), and their divided difference has order \(k\). For a Bernstein ellipse of parameter \(ho>1\) around this interval, suppose the whole actual defect obeys \(\sup|D_{3,N}|\le N^A e^{NM_3}\) there. Standard Chebyshev truncation gives a degree-\((k-1)\) polynomial with error at most \(C N^A e^{NM_3}ho^{-k}\). Explicitly, apply Cauchy's coefficient estimate to \(D_{3,N}(-1+(z+z^{-1})/2)\) on \(|z|=ho\): its Chebyshev coefficients obey \(|a_\ell|\le2\sup_{E_ho}|D_{3,N}|ho^{-\ell}\), and summing the geometric tail proves this error bound. The divided difference annihilates that polynomial exactly. Since \[ \sum_{a=j}^{m-1} rac{|e_j(c_a)|}{|Q_N'(c_a)|} \le e_j(-2),\qquad  rac1N\log e_j(-2)\longrightarrow M_\infty/2, 	ag{23} \] the resulting squared-coefficient upper-rate expression is \[ E(ho)=2M_3+M_\infty-	frac12\logho. 	ag{24} \] The first inequality uses \(0\le e_j(c_a)\le e_j(-2)\), \(|1/Q_N'(c_a)|\le2/N\), and at most \(N/2\) nodes. The limit is the original sine-product integral at \(j/N	o1/4\). Thus this is an upper bound for the actual source, obtained from the whole analytic remainder. It is not a new estimate independent of the contour principle in (22). A flat envelope at rate \(M_3\) cannot be used on an ellipse containing the half-charge color \(w_0=-2\cos t_0\). To see this, put \(t_h=t_0-ih\) for small fixed \(h>0\). The exact exterior defect identity in the [observation theorem](research_complete_source_pick_observation.md#complex-colors-and-the-exact-normal-defect) and the actual local complete-edge packet give \[  egin{split} \Re S_3(t_h)&=M_3+	frac12\Re A_3\,h^2+O(h^3)>M_3,\ D_{3,N}(-2\cos t_h)&= h_{3,N}(-2\cos t_h)/Q_N(-2\cos t_h) \,(1+O(e^{-c_hN})). \end{split} 	ag{25} \] Here \(S_3'(t_0)=0\), \(S_3''(t_0)=-A_3\), and \(\Re A_3>0\). The interpolation term has rate \(M_3\), whereas the displayed direct term is nonzero and has the strictly larger rate. If a fixed ellipse contains \(w_0\) in its interior, it contains these colors for sufficiently small \(h\). Provided the ellipse is a domain of holomorphy of the original defect, the maximum-modulus principle therefore rules out the flat polynomial-times-\(e^{NM_3}\) boundary bound. An ellipse crossing the original branch cut is already inadmissible for the same analytic approximation argument. The half-charge bounds \(0<\Re t_0<\pi/3\) and \(0<-\Im t_0<2/5\) place \(w_0\) strictly inside the \(ho=3\) ellipse about \([-2,0]\). In fact \[ |\Re(w_0+1)|<6/5,\qquad |\Im w_0|<3/4, \qquad \left( rac{6/5}{5/3}ight)^2+ \left( rac{3/4}{4/3}ight)^2 = rac{133569}{160000}<1. 	ag{26} \] These constants require no numerical saddle calculation. The Taylor series gives \(37/25<e^{2/5}<1007/675<3/2\); hence \(\cosh(2/5)<11/10\) and \(\sinh(2/5)<5/12\). Together with \(\sqrt3<7/4\), these prove (26). The ellipse has center \(-1\) and semiaxes \(5/3,4/3\). Consequently any radius justified by this flat envelope has \(ho<3\). Finally the [proved rational source bounds](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_pair_regular_support_cells.md#5-a-termwise-absolute-bound-fails-for-the-actual-short-pair) give \(M_3>21/20\), \(M_\infty>23/20\), and \(\log3<6/5\). Therefore every such instance of (24) satisfies \[ E(ho)> rac{13}{4}- rac12\log3 > rac{53}{20}> rac{13}{5}>\mathcal M_{3,3}, 	ag{27} \] where \(\mathcal M_{3,3}\) is the already proved full pair rate. Reaching even its coarser upper bound \(13/5\) through (24) would require \(\logho>13/10\), contrary to \(\logho<6/5\). This is an insufficiency of this particular upper-bound expression, not a lower bound on the original coefficient.
