Only the finite coefficient laws are independent; every shared edge and all coherent sums remain inside the descendant source. In particular internal \(U\)-edges remain the factors in (13), and no normal at a surviving vertex is removed. For complete outside colors every factor outside the expectation is positive. If \(d_v\) is the original degree of \(v\), then \[ D_U(\mathbf a)\prod_wM_w \le\prod_{v\in U}M_{a_v,N}^{d_v}. 	ag{15} \] Indeed a cut or outside incidence contributes precisely \(M_{a_v,N}\). An internal \(U\)-edge obeys \(0<K_N(c_a,c_b)\le\min(M_{a,N},M_{b,N}) \le M_{a,N}M_{b,N}\), by (2) and (10). Counting both original endpoints proves (15). With \(d_U=\sum_{v\in U}d_v\), (11) yields \[ D_U\prod_wM_w\le N^{d_U}e^{Nd_Uh(\varepsilon)} \quad\hbox{if all }a_v\le\varepsilon N. 	ag{16} \] The charge shifts in (14) satisfy \[ |K_w|/N\le A_w/N\le d\,\varepsilon,\qquad d=\max_{v\in S}d_v. 	ag{17} \] At unit readout one can say more without an estimate. The exact full-Hermite identity \(\mathcal C_{N,1+u}=\mathcal C_{N,1-u}\) implies that (14) is unchanged if \(1-K_w/N\) is replaced by \(1-|K_w|/N\) in each descendant coordinate. Thus only below-unit lattice charges in \([1-d\varepsilon,1]\) are used. ## 4. A usable endpoint-window lemma Consider the omitted-row source of the adopted outer-row theorem. At each \(v\in U\) its exact weight is \(\Omega_{v,a_v}\), allowing a fixed number of shared microscopic endpoint coupons with \(|\alpha|\le A<\pi\). All the other original factors are as in (14). In particular \[ |\Omega_{v,a_v}|\le C N^{3/2}. 	ag{18} \] Start with unit charge at every traced vertex, and retain the original integer powers. Restrict the exact row sum to \(0\le a_v\le\varepsilon N\), also respecting its original tail support. Call that restricted contribution \(T_{U,N}^\varepsilon\). **Endpoint-window lemma.** Suppose there are \(r_0,\Delta>0\), a reference rate \(M\), and constants \(C,p\) such that the actual descendant sources in (14) satisfy \[ \left|Z_{G',N}^{A_{N,\mathbf a}} (\mathbf n_Y, oldsymbol\chi)ight| \le C N^p e^{N(M-\Delta)} \quad	ext{for }\chi_w\in(1+N^{-1}\mathbb Z)\cap[1-r_0,1], 	ag{19} \] uniformly over all physical parameters \(\mathbf a\) in the indicated window and all retained insertions. Then, whenever \(d\varepsilon\le r_0\), \[ |T_{U,N}^\varepsilon| \le C' N^{p+d_U+(5/2)|U|} e^{N[M-\Delta+d_Uh(\varepsilon)]}. 	ag{20} \] In particular a fixed sufficiently small \(\varepsilon>0\) preserves half the supplied margin: \[ d_Uh(\varepsilon)\le\Delta/2 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad |T_{U,N}^\varepsilon|\le C' N^{p'} e^{N(M-\Delta/2)}. 	ag{21} \] The same choice can serve the finitely many evaluated subsets of a fixed graph, if (19) holds uniformly for them. *Proof.* Apply the exact unit-charge reflection after (17). Equation (14) then evaluates the source only at the lattice charge window in (19). The expectation has total mass one, so (19) bounds it without replacing the descendant by a physical norm. Apply (16), multiply by (18), and sum at most \(N^{|U|}\) physical assignments. The original evaluated crossing values have modulus one at real, in particular integer, powers. This proves (20); \(h(\varepsilon)	o0\) proves (21). \(\square\) This is a stability input for an induction whose descendant estimates are already available uniformly in charge. It does not infer (19) from a bound known only at \( oldsymbol\chi=\mathbf1\), from classical action concavity, or from a nonzero boundary state. Other endpoint windows and vertical currents remain. ## 5. The retained integer phase and the limit of absolute estimates The original crossing convention is \[ R_n(c_a)=C_{N,n}\exp\{inN	au_a^2/(4\pi)\},\qquad C_{N,n}=\exp\{\pi inD^2/(4N)\},\quad 	au_a=\pi- rac{2\pi(a+1/2)}N. 	ag{22} \] Combining its value with the exact tail character gives \[ (-1)^aR_n(c_a) =\kappa_{N,n} \exp\{i\pi(1-n)a+i\pi n(a+1/2)^2/N\},\qquad \kappa_{N,n}=C_{N,n}e^{i\pi n(N-2)/4}. 	ag{23} \] The scalar has modulus one for real \(n\). For odd integer \(n\) the linear character is one; for even integer \(n\) it is \((-1)^a\). The quadratic phase remains in both cases. For a shared product, each summand of its exact weight retains this character; its other physical row factors are unchanged. No integer-only identity has been differentiated in \(n\). The coefficient cost cannot generally be made subexponential on a fixed macroscopic endpoint window by using the Gaussian tail penalty alone. Here is an actual-kernel verification. Fix \(0<\delta<1/2\), take \(\alpha=0\), \(L=\lfloor\delta Nfloor\), and let \(a_N/N	o x\in(0,1/2-\delta)\). The exact tail products in the outer-row source have a common sign and give \[ \lim_{N	o\infty} rac1N\log|\omega_{a_N,N,L}(0)| =-J_\delta(x),\qquad J_\delta(x)= -\int_0^\delta \log\left(1- rac{\sin^2(\pi x)}{\cos^2(\pi u)}ight)du. 	ag{24} \] To prove the limit, the first retained product has length \(L+1\). Its logarithm divided by \(N\) converges to the displayed integral: all factors on that interval are strictly positive and bounded away from zero. Through physical termination, every subsequent ratio is at most some \(q_x<1\) for all large \(N\), because its limit is \((\cos^2(\pi x)-v)/(1-v)\le\cos^2(\pi x)<1\). Its denominators stay away from zero since \(x>0\). Thus the whole tail is between its first positive term and a constant times that term. The nonzero base factor contributes only \(O(\log N)\) to its logarithm. This proves (24) at both parities. Expansion at \(x=0\), uniformly on the fixed \(u\)-interval, yields \[ J_\delta(x)=\pi	an(\pi\delta)x^2+O(x^4). 	ag{25} \] In contrast, the positive \(k=a\) term of the actual row (2) gives \[ \liminf_{N	o\infty} rac1N\log M_{a_N,N}\ge m(x), \] \[ m(x)= \int_0^{2x}\log(2\sin\pi u)\,du -4\int_0^x\log(2\sin\pi u)\,du +\int_0^x\log(4\cos^2\pi u)\,du. 	ag{26} \] These Riemann-sum limits follow by separating the integrable \(\log u\) singularity at zero; its factorial sum has \(O(\log N)\) error. The cosine product uses its literal midpoint arguments. In particular \[ m(x)=2x\log(1/x)+O(x). 	ag{27} \] Equations (25)--(27) show that, for sufficiently small fixed \(x>0\), \[ \liminf_{N	o\infty}N^{-1} \log igl(|\omega_{a_N,N,L}(0)|F_{a_N,N}(-2) igr)>0. 	ag{28} \] The second factor is a literal complete outside incidence, not an arbitrary test polynomial. Thus this positive coefficient expansion is not a uniformly subexponential absolute contraction to an undeformed deleted rate on fixed macroscopic windows. Equation (28) does not rule out coherent cancellation in the row sum, a sufficiently large supplied action gap, or every possible filled-action estimate. The small-window lemma explicitly shows how a positive margin can absorb the cost. The original phase (23) and paired vertical currents remain relevant beyond that argument. ## 6. Coverage and direct sources The following earlier constructions were checked for overlap: [the complete-source Pick observation](research_complete_source_pick_observation.md) treats a Cauchy observation of the complete row; [the entropy Fourier embedding](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_entropy_circle_fourier_embedding.md) represents a classical entropy defect; [the shared-cycle Fourier compiler](actual_matching_graph_shared_cycle_fourier_compiler.md) uses positive magnetic-polynomial coefficients with matching flows and the original cycle characters. They are different objects from (3)--(6). General charge convolution itself is already in the full-period current source below. The present additional input is the positive physical-row law, its support and coefficient-mass control, and the resulting endpoint-window stability estimate. These coverage pointers are not additional proof dependencies. The complete direct sources were read at the following versions, their used implications checked, and hashes verified: * [Coherent endpoint kernel reduction](research_full_period_endpoint_kernel_reduction.md), SHA256 a1d67ac803c0160bbfdacaa96a6fde9dc1ffae06fc39eb94f0416dcf2ecef76e: exact physical-row formula, roots above \(2\), and original ordinary-polynomial/normal conventions. * [Actual outer-row decay](research_endpoint_outer_row_decay.md), SHA256 85e708606a44cbbbc45a82db0685fcb1d35215c89470ccdc7408790305e55e30: exact tail products, parity character, shared endpoint weights, and their coefficientwise full-source placement. * [Full-period current charge convolution](research_full_period_current_charge_convolution.md), SHA256 3f74b9824ecbf0b71a79b17959c7208f650103f95932192cfba87c7a7aa05595: original charge/crossing conventions and full-Hermite cosine multiplication inside arbitrary shared surviving traces. Only written mathematics, text reads and hashes were used. No mathematical program, numerical experiment, test or compilation was run. Adopted notes and public manuscripts are unchanged.

title: Comparing the two endpoint roles on common positive charts
text: # Comparing the two endpoint roles on common positive charts Private written proof, 16 November 2026. The regular continuation theorem constructs a source-normalized mode by treating either nonzero endpoint as the degree variable. Here the two constructions are compared on a common domain. Exact joint physical data give an exponentially small normalized difference on a two-variable real seed neighborhood. Holomorphic propagation then compares them on every compact subset of a connected common domain where both action bounds hold. The shared seed and common phase are hypotheses. This result does not identify arbitrary off-grid representatives merely because their physical jets agree. It neither constructs a global glued scalar nor removes window interfaces, endpoint packets or exterior currents. ## 1. The two constructions and the shared seed Put \[ h=N^{-1},\quad X_j=(j+\tfrac12)h,\quad Y_k=(k+\tfrac12)h,\qquad C(X)=2\cos(2\pi X),\qquad t(X)=\pi-2\pi X . \tag{1} \] Take one representative from the pinned regular continuation theorem with the first endpoint as degree variable, and one with the roles interchanged. In common centered coordinates write them as \[ A_N(X,Y)=\mathcal F_{N,1}^{\sigma_1}(X,t(Y)),\qquad B_N(X,Y)=\mathcal F_{N,2}^{\sigma_2}(Y,t(X)). \tag{2} \] The choices of anchors, first-degree windows and designated signs may differ. Every representative is the actual normalized construction with its exact one-sided repair; it is not a raw Sears cutoff. Require two fixed intervals \[ I_X,I_Y\Subset(0,1/2) \tag{3} \] and fixed complex neighborhoods \(U_X,U_Y\) of the respective intervals, with buffers, such that: 1. \(I_X\) lies in the matched first window of \(A_N\), and \(I_Y\) lies in the matched first window of the transposed construction \(B_N\). These intervals have positive length, independent of \(N\). 2. Both constructions are holomorphic on a neighborhood of \(\overline{U_X}\times\overline{U_Y}\). In particular the local second-parameter domain for \(A_N\) contains \(t(U_Y)\), and that for \(B_N\) contains \(t(U_X)\). 3. Their continued phases agree there with the original symmetric phase \[ \Psi(X,Y)=\psi(t(X),t(Y)). \tag{4} \] Both phase-normalized representatives have uniform \(e^{o(N)}\) bounds on this buffered seed product. The third condition holds on sufficiently thin real seed products when the two regular constructions use the same original phase: each designated-half estimate also supplies a fixed thin opposite collar. The intervals in (3) must nevertheless be shared as stated. A local second-parameter chart need not contain any other physical row. At every joint seed node, the exact full-jet identities give \[ \partial_X^a\partial_Y^b A_N(X_j,Y_k) =\partial_X^a\partial_Y^b B_N(X_j,Y_k) =\left.\partial_X^a\partial_Y^b K_N(C(X),C(Y))\right|_{(X_j,Y_k)}, \qquad 0\le a,b\le1. \tag{5} \] Here \(X_j\in I_X,Y_k\in I_Y\). These are double physical spectral rows for all sufficiently large \(N\). To verify (5), the first construction has the exact holomorphic identities \[ A_N(X_j,Y)=F_j(C(Y)),\qquad \partial_XA_N(X_j,Y)=C'(X_j)\widehat G_j(C(Y)). \tag{6} \] The source normal \(\widehat G_j\) has the value and first spectral normal of the original \(G_j\) at every physical second row. Differentiate (6) in \(Y\) and use this identity. The transposed construction gives the same four entries by symmetry of the original kernel. In particular the mixed entry is \[ C'(X_j)C'(Y_k)\, \partial_z\partial_wK_N(c_j,c_k). \tag{7} \] No assertion that a first normal follows from values alone is used. The equality also survives multiplication by any common holomorphic spectator, with its full mixed product rule. ## 2. Two successive dense-grid estimates We record the analytic estimate used at each stage. Let \(f_N\) be holomorphic on a fixed complex neighborhood of a real interval, bounded there by \(e^{o(N)}\). Suppose on its centered nodes \[ |f_N(X_j)|\le e^{-\kappa N} \tag{8} \] for a fixed \(\kappa>0\). Then \(f_N=O(e^{-\kappa' N})\) on a smaller open neighborhood of a shorter interior interval, for some \(\kappa'>0\). All statements are uniform in any buffered holomorphic parameters. For clarity, subtract the finite cardinal correction \[ q_N(X)=\sum_j f_N(X_j) \operatorname{sinc}(N(X-X_j)). \tag{9} \] On a sufficiently thin fixed neighborhood, \[ |q_N(X)|\le CN e^{-\kappa N+\pi N|\Im X|} \le e^{-\kappa N/2}. \tag{10} \] Thus \(f_N-q_N\) has exact zeros at every selected node and is still bounded by \(e^{o(N)}\). Take a disk inside that thin neighborhood and \(cN\) nodes in a smaller concentric disk. The corresponding disk Blaschke factors have modulus at most a fixed \(\vartheta<1\) on a still smaller disk. Dividing out these factors and using the maximum principle gives \[ |f_N-q_N|\le e^{o(N)}\vartheta^{cN}. \tag{11} \] Finite covering and buffered Cauchy estimates prove the assertion, including all fixed derivatives. For exact nodal zeros omit (9). This is the dense-zero argument of the pinned normal theorem, with its approximate-zero step made explicit. Set \[ D_N(X,Y)=e^{-N\Psi(X,Y)}(A_N-B_N). \tag{12} \] It is holomorphic and bounded by \(e^{o(N)}\) on the seed product. Fix a physical \(Y_k\in I_Y\). Equation (5) gives exact zeros \(D_N(X_j,Y_k)=0\) for \(X_j\in I_X\). The exact-zero case of (11), uniformly in \(k\), gives a fixed open \(U_X'\Subset U_X\) and \(c_1>0\) such that \[ \sup_{X\in U_X'}|D_N(X,Y_k)| \le e^{-c_1N}. \tag{13} \] Now fix \(X\in U_X'\) and regard \(D_N(X,Y)\) as a holomorphic function of \(Y\). Its values at the second grid are exponentially small by (13), although they need not be zero. Apply (9)--(11) in \(Y\), using \(X\) as a uniform holomorphic parameter. On a fixed smaller product, \[ |D_N(X,Y)|\le C e^{-c_2N}. \tag{14} \] All fixed mixed derivatives obey this estimate after further fixed buffers. This proves a two-complex-variable seed estimate; an estimate merely on the real product would not suffice for the propagation below. Only the value entries in (5) are needed for (14). The remaining entries establish that the compared constructions still represent the original full physical source. No independent jet has been discarded to obtain the analytic comparison. ## 3. Propagation on a connected common domain **Theorem.** In addition to the shared seed conditions, let \(\mathcal W\subset\mathbb C^2\) be a connected open common domain containing the seed product and a target compact set. Require a single holomorphic phase \(\Psi\) on \(\mathcal W\), equal to (4) on the seed, and assume that \(A_N,B_N\) are holomorphic there with \[ \sup_K\bigl(|e^{-N\Psi}A_N|+|e^{-N\Psi}B_N|\bigr) \le e^{o_K(N)} \quad\text{for every }K\Subset\mathcal W. \tag{15} \] For the one-sided representatives this means that the common domain stays in their designated half-domains and permitted opposite collars, or elsewhere where (15) has separately been proved. Then for every \(K\Subset\mathcal W\) there is \(c_K>0\) such that \[ \sup_K\left| \partial_X^a\partial_Y^b \bigl[e^{-N\Psi}(A_N-B_N)\bigr]\right| \le C_{K,a,b}e^{-c_KN} \tag{16} \] for every fixed \(a,b\). The exponent may be decreased when derivatives are taken. **Proof.** Equation (14) supplies one open seed ball. Cover compact paths from that ball to \(K\) by finitely many buffered Euclidean balls in \(\mathcal W\). The three-balls estimate for a holomorphic function is the usual three-circles estimate on each complex line through the center: a bound on an inner ball and a bound on an outer ball give the interpolated bound on an intermediate ball. Thus an inner \(e^{-cN}\) bound and the \(e^{o(N)}\) outer bound from (15) give an \(e^{-c'N}\) intermediate bound, with \(c'>0\). Choose the next center in the known smaller ball and repeat. A finite chain reaches each compact target neighborhood; compactness gives a finite collection of chains. Every step multiplies the positive exponential constant by a fixed positive number, while its \(o(N)\) term stays negligible. Buffered Cauchy estimates prove (16). \(\square\) The statement is uniform for buffered holomorphic exterior parameter families when the domains, phase, source identities and bounds above are uniform. Their fixed derivatives follow by Cauchy on the larger parameter compacts. The same conclusion holds for the two unrepaired baselines under the same common-domain bounds. Their actual nodal value errors from the regular continuation theorem are exponentially small relative to the physical rows. On a buffered real bulk seed the normalized physical rows have \(e^{o(N)}\) size. Hence the first stage uses the approximate-zero argument (9)--(11), rather than the exact-zero case; the rest of the proof is unchanged. ## 4. Scope for source transport The theorem compares two actual endpoint-role constructions. It allows different anchors and different matched windows, provided the fixed shared seed intervals in (3) remain. It cannot be applied when the local second domains omit the other seed window, when the target component is disconnected from the seed, or when the continued phases differ by an unrecorded branch or constant. On any overlap satisfying the theorem, a common holomorphic spectator multiplies (16) by its actual bound. Thus an interface primitive or contour integral still needs that bound and its original orientation; the theorem does not declare its integral zero. In particular the exact window identity in the continuation source uses \(\Phi^\sharp_{N,I}\), the finite residue expression with \(\widehat G_j\). Its difference from the original free-endpoint window trace is \(P_N(w)\) times a holomorphic function. Equality with the original follows only after the prescribed complete second trace, with all spectator normals. The present overlap estimate does not change that scope. No first-angle evenness of the one-sided repairs is asserted. No full-lens substitution, whole-grid interpolation, simultaneous fold construction, global Cousin gluing or global current bound follows from (16). All unmatched rows, angular endpoint packets, opposite-side closures and exterior currents remain in the original problem. ## Direct sources and author scope Both complete direct texts and their used implications were read at: * [Regular positive continuation](research_physical_row_regular_positive_continuation.md), SHA256 3a7d81d55f60396c2e3058d5ebe967ae625ff47c4b527b4e102e37fa8f28d644: actual repaired and baseline modes, full-normal window identities, common phase and designated-half bounds, and the precise \(\Phi^\sharp\) versus original trace distinction. * [Actual slit normal connection](research_physical_row_slit_normal_connection.md), SHA256 a5084adb4ff25cb08020e5f9485bd1aaea5b49468c6ab0af311ebc1c0c504d99: actual normal representatives and original mixed-jet equality, normalized bulk bounds, dense zeros and analytic propagation. Only written mathematics, source reads and metadata hashes were used. No mathematical program, numerical evaluation, test or compilation was run. Adopted notes and public manuscripts were unchanged.

title: Full physical-row products and strictly signed normal support
text: # Full physical-row products and strictly signed normal support Private written proof, 17 November 2026. The missing normal sector in an ordinary product of physical rows has a particularly simple support and sign. Its coefficient at the double node \(c_\ell\) is \((-1)^{N-1}\) times a strictly positive quantity exactly when \(j+k+\ell\ge N-1\). That quantity is a symmetric triple trace with an explicit positive sine-factorial sum. This holds for every physical pair \(j,k\), including products above the value-row degree range. The positive Newton multiplication table and the general confluent coordinate formula are prior results. We use them to obtain this strict support statement and explicit coefficients; we do not present coordinate inversion as a new theorem. The value coefficients retain a separate alternating derivative tail. No scalar lower bound after crossing phases is inferred. ## 1. Original basis and the finite reciprocal calculation Set \[ N\ge2,\quad D=N-1,\quad J=\lfloor D/2\rfloor,\quad \theta=\pi/N,\quad q=e^{i\theta},\quad \eta=(-1)^D, \quad\kappa=q^{D^2/2}, \] \[ s_r=2\sin(r\theta),\quad S_r=\prod_{a=1}^r s_a,\quad S_0=1, \quad c_j=2\cos((2j+1)\theta), \] \[ P_N(Z)=2T_N(Z/2)+2,\quad e_r(Z)=S_r^{-2}\prod_{a<r}(c_a-Z),\qquad \phi(f)=\eta N^2[Z^D]\operatorname{rem}_{P_N}f . \tag{1} \] Use the original turn \(Te_r=e_{D-r}\) in \(\mathcal A_N=\mathbb C[Z]/(P_N)\). The physical rows and normal rows are \[ F_j(Z)=K_N(c_j,Z),\quad 0\le j\le J,\qquad G_\ell(Z)=\partial_wK_N(c_\ell,Z),\quad \ell\in\mathcal D_N, \] \[ K_N(w,Z)=\sum_{r=0}^D e_r(w)e_r(Z),\qquad \mathcal D_N=\{0,\ldots,\lfloor N/2\rfloor-1\}. \tag{2} \] At odd \(N\) the additional simple node has index \(*=J\) and value \(c_*=-2\). The full basis is \(\{F_j\}_{j=0}^J\cup\{G_\ell\}_{\ell\in\mathcal D_N}\). There is no \(G_*\). Write \[ f_{j,a}=e_a(c_j) =\frac{S_{j+a}}{S_{j-a}S_a^2}>0 \quad(0\le a\le j),\qquad f_{j,a}=0\quad(a>j). \tag{3} \] The exact formula follows from \(c_r-c_j=s_{j+r+1}s_{j-r}\). All factorial indices in (3) are below \(N\). The archived positive Newton table is \[ e_a e_b=\sum_{r=\max(a,b)}^{a+b}\mu_{ab,r}e_r,\qquad \mu_{ab,r}= \frac{S_{a+b}S_r} {S_aS_bS_{r-a}S_{r-b}S_{a+b-r}}>0 \quad(a+b\le D). \tag{4} \] If \(a+b\ge N\), the product is zero in the full algebra. Both assertions retain all repeated-root normals. Fix any \(0\le j,k\le J\), and put \(s=j+k\le D\). For \(0\le r\le s\), define the explicit positive sum \[ u_r= \sum_{\substack{0\le a\le j,\ 0\le b\le k\\ \max(a,b)\le r\le a+b}} f_{j,a}f_{k,b}\, \frac{S_{a+b}S_r} {S_aS_bS_{r-a}S_{r-b}S_{a+b-r}}, \qquad u_r=0\quad(r>s). \tag{5} \] Every \(u_r\) in \(0\le r\le s\) is strictly positive: choose \(a+b=r\) with \(a\le j,b\le k\). Thus, exactly as ordinary polynomials, \[ F_jF_k=\sum_{r=0}^{s}u_re_r,\qquad T(F_jF_k)=\sum_{m=0}^D h_me_m,\qquad h_m=u_{D-m}. \tag{6} \] In particular \[ h_m>0\ \Longleftrightarrow\ D-j-k\le m\le D. \tag{7} \] This is a finite factorial calculation followed by coefficient reversal under the original turn. No triangular basis solve or generic-root specialization is required. ## 2. The normal coefficients and their exact threshold Expand uniquely in the full basis: \[ F_jF_k=\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal D_N} (A_{jk;\ell}F_\ell+B_{jk;\ell}G_\ell) +\mathbf1_{N\ {\rm odd}}A_{jk;*}F_* . \tag{8} \] Put \(\Delta_\ell=4-c_\ell^2>0\) at a double node. The prior confluent Gram formula gives, for any canonical \(f\), \[ B_\ell(f)=\eta\Delta_\ell(Tf)(c_\ell),\qquad A_\ell(f)=\eta\{\Delta_\ell(Tf)'(c_\ell)-c_\ell(Tf)(c_\ell)\}, \] \[ A_*(f)=(Tf)(-2). \tag{9} \] These are full original values and spectral first normals. **Theorem 1.** Define \[ \Gamma_{jk\ell}=\sum_{m=0}^{\ell}h_m f_{\ell,m}. \tag{10} \] It is symmetric in its three physical indices and satisfies \[ \Gamma_{jk\ell}=\phi(F_jF_kF_\ell),\qquad \Gamma_{jk\ell}>0\ \Longleftrightarrow\ j+k+\ell\ge D; \tag{11} \] it is zero otherwise. For every double node, \[ \boxed{\quad B_{jk;\ell}=\eta\Delta_\ell\Gamma_{jk\ell}.\quad} \tag{12} \] At the odd simple node, \[ A_{jk;*}=\Gamma_{jk*}>0 \ \Longleftrightarrow\ j+k\ge J . \tag{13} \] Equations (3), (5), and (10) are an explicit finite positive sine-factorial sum for \(\Gamma\). On its first nonzero boundary, \[ j+k+\ell=D \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \Gamma_{jk\ell}=\frac{N^2}{H_jH_kH_\ell},\qquad H_a=\frac{S_a^4}{S_{2a}} . \tag{14} \] **Proof.** Evaluation of (6) at \(c_\ell\) gives (10). The exact reproducing identity \((Tf)(c_\ell)=\phi(F_\ell f)\) proves the triple-trace identity and symmetry. Equations (3) and (7) show that the sum is nonempty precisely when \(D-j-k\le\ell\); all its nonzero terms are positive. Apply (9) to obtain (12) and (13). For (14), the ordinary product has degree exactly \(D\); there is no reduction. Its leading coefficient is \((-1)^{j+k+\ell}/(H_jH_kH_\ell)\), because \((-1)^aH_aF_a\) is monic. Formula (1) and \(\eta(-1)^D=1\) give (14). \(\square\) Consequently the missing normal coefficients are not arbitrary signed data. They all have sign \(\eta\) on a precisely known terminal interval of double-node indices. At even levels this interval is nonempty exactly when \(j+k\ge J+1\). At odd levels it is nonempty exactly when \(j+k\ge J+1\) as well. This agrees with the exact degree obstruction to an \(F\)-only expansion above \(J\). The simple coefficient also proves that the low-degree alternating rule cannot be extended unchanged to all value coefficients. At odd \(N\ge5\), choose physical indices with \(j+k=J+1\). Equation (13) gives \(A_{jk;*}>0\), whereas the extrapolated sign \((-1)^{j+k-J}\) would be negative. No claim about the remaining \(A\)-signs is needed. ## 3. Every value coefficient, with its derivative tail retained For a double node \(\ell\), the derivative of each Newton polynomial is explicitly \[ e_m'(c_\ell)= \begin{cases} -f_{\ell,m}\displaystyle\sum_{a=0}^{m-1} \frac1{c_a-c_\ell},&0\le m\le\ell,\\[2mm] (-1)^{m-\ell} \displaystyle\frac{S_{\ell+m}S_{m-\ell-1}} {s_{2\ell+1}S_m^2}, &\ell<m\le D-\ell,\\[2mm] 0,&m>D-\ell . \end{cases} \tag{15} \] The empty sum at \(m=0\) is zero. There are no zero denominators in (15). Its middle line has the displayed strictly alternating signs; the last line is a double-root zero, not a value-only simplification. To prove the middle line, differentiate the unique factor \(c_\ell-Z\) in \(e_m\). The remaining factors split as \[ \prod_{\substack{0\le a<m\\a\ne\ell}} s_{\ell+a+1} =\frac{S_{\ell+m}}{S_\ell s_{2\ell+1}},\qquad \prod_{\substack{0\le a<m\\a\ne\ell}} s_{\ell-a} =(-1)^{m-\ell-1}S_\ell S_{m-\ell-1}. \] For \(m>D-\ell\), both occurrences of \(c_\ell\) are present, so the derivative vanishes. The first line is ordinary logarithmic differentiation away from zeros. Combining (9), (10), and (15) gives every remaining coefficient: \[ \boxed{\quad A_{jk;\ell} =\eta\left\{\Delta_\ell\sum_{m=0}^Dh_m e_m'(c_\ell) -c_\ell\Gamma_{jk\ell}\right\}. \quad} \tag{16} \] Equivalently, with \(L=D-j-k\), it is the finite formula \[ \begin{split} A_{jk;\ell}={}&-\eta\sum_{m=L}^{\ell} h_m f_{\ell,m} \left(c_\ell+\Delta_\ell \sum_{a=0}^{m-1}\frac1{c_a-c_\ell}\right)\\ &+\eta\Delta_\ell \sum_{m=\max(L,\ell+1)}^{D-\ell} (-1)^{m-\ell}h_m \frac{S_{\ell+m}S_{m-\ell-1}} {s_{2\ell+1}S_m^2}. \end{split} \tag{17} \] An inverted summation range is empty. These formulas retain all tail signs, without assigning a universal sign to their sum. Together with (5), (12), and (13), they compute the whole expansion (8) at both parities and every \(N\ge2\). For example, \(N=2\) has \(j=k=\ell=0\); (15)--(17) give \(A_{00;0}=1,B_{00;0}=0\), as required. ## 4. Exact turns, canonical collisions, and closing scope Let \[ \lambda_{n,\ell}=(-1)^{n\ell}q^{-n\ell(\ell+1)},\qquad \alpha_\ell=\frac{R'(c_\ell)}{R(c_\ell)} =\frac{i(D-2\ell)}{4\sin((2\ell+1)\theta)} . \tag{18} \] The original signed turn \(V_n=\kappa^nTR^{-n}T\) acts on (8), for every \(n\in\mathbb Z\), by \[ (A_{jk;\ell},B_{jk;\ell}) \longmapsto \lambda_{n,\ell} (A_{jk;\ell}-n\alpha_\ell B_{jk;\ell},B_{jk;\ell}), \tag{19} \] with only the scalar factor on the odd simple coefficient. Thus the normal coefficients have the definite amplitudes (12) and the original quadratic phases, while their Jordan contribution to the value coefficients is also retained. The same support mechanism extends to any finite product \(P=\operatorname{can}\prod_{i=1}^rF_{j_i}\). Put \(s=\sum_i j_i\). Repeated use of (4), including its zero rule when two Newton indices sum to at least \(N\), gives \[ P=\sum_{a=0}^{\min(D,s)}u_a e_a,\qquad u_a>0. \tag{20} \] For strictness at a prescribed \(a\le\min(D,s)\), choose input indices \(a_i\le j_i\) summing to \(a\), and choose the top output at every multiplication. Each partial sum is at most \(D\), so this path survives with positive weight. No other term is negative. Outputs above \(s\) cannot occur. This proves (20) even when the ordinary degree exceeds \(D\). The canonical zero rule is an identity modulo the full \(P_N\), so all paired normals survive this argument. Replacing \(h_m\) by \(u_{D-m}\) in (9), (15), and (16) therefore gives the same all-channel formula for \(P\), with \[ \operatorname{sign}B_\ell(P)=\eta \quad\hbox{exactly when }s+\ell\ge D . \tag{21} \] The bare original closing has the exact elementary consequence \[ \phi(P)=u_D>0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad s\ge D. \tag{22} \] This is a positivity statement for the specified product without inserted multiplication crossings. It is also unchanged by one outer \(V_n\), since \(\lambda_{n,0}=1\) and the closing extracts only the normal coefficient at zero. For a pair \(j,k\), it is nonzero only at odd levels with \(j=k=J\), where it equals one by the odd simple Gram block. Thus the newly present normal sector at other nodes does not by itself yield a bare closing. After a multiplication crossing, the actual observation is the coherent sum from the confluent closing source, involving all \(A_\ell-(n+\sigma)\alpha_\ell B_\ell\) and their quadratic phases. Neither positivity in (12) nor (22) establishes noncancellation of that sum, an asymptotic lower bound, or a general fixed-short-filling theorem. ## Complete direct sources All three complete direct texts were read and their used implications checked at these pins: * [Positive Newton multiplication](../papers/newton-calculus/README.md), SHA256 543b5be6035ecec349ce8e78ee47085345ceefe4fc51e5f2005b802d999805bb: the prior positive factorial table, full canonical zero rule, and physical-row Newton coefficients. * [Alternating physical-row linearization](research_physical_row_alternating_linearization.md), SHA256 326c55623da9155b6f5a0be4ab3e3b2584bdf7c568cd288d1e69569473c36342: row degrees, monic factorial normalization, and full normal basis. * [Confluent row closing](research_confluent_row_closing_and_positive_quotient.md), SHA256 daf5760f74dbd9d9c9646a1a18b95cdffc1f42ebc3cbcfc0a1b9f79b2ad77251: the prior coordinate formula, original Jordan phases, and prescribed bare and crossed observations. Only written proof, source reads, and metadata hashes were used. No mathematical programs, tests, numerics, or builds were run. Adopted notes and public manuscripts were not edited.

title: Actual physical-row windows on regular positive continuation charts
text:
# Actual physical-row windows on regular positive continuation charts Private written proof, 16 November 2026. The full-slit physical-row theorem fixes the actual value and first-normal normalization on a real bulk window. Here that normalization gives a moderate scalar mode on a buffered complex degree chart, even where the selected characteristic root ceases to dominate in modulus. The proof constructs the mode there; it does not propagate an exponentially small source error through an uncontrolled growing solution. An exact one-sided Hermite repair preserves the original window data without a loss proportional to the designated complex height. The positive product-domain theorem supplies such charts near every positive pair whose first angle is nonzero. Connected overlaps with a common physical seed have exponentially small normalized differences. All original exterior window currents remain. No whole-grid kernel or bound on a raw Sears cutoff transition is asserted. ## 1. Actual data and regular charts Put \(h=N^{-1}\), \(	heta=\pi/N\), and use the centered degree coordinate \[ X_j=(j+	frac12)h,\qquad C(X)=2\cos(2\pi X),\qquad t=\pi-2\pi X,\qquad w(u)=-2\cos u . 	ag{1} \] Thus \(C(X_j)=c_j\), with the original \(c_j=2\cos((2j+1)	heta)\). Retain the original physical row and its independent first normal, \[ F_j(w)=K_N(c_j,w),\qquad G_j(w)=\partial_zK_N(c_j,w). 	ag{2} \] On the second spectral slit \(\Omega=\mathbb C\setminus[2,\infty)\), the pinned normal theorem gives the pole-free representative \[ \widehat G_j(w)=  rac{c'(0)F_j(w)\widetilde Q_N(w)+R_j(w)}{c'(j)}, \qquad c'(j)=-4	heta\sin((2j+1)	heta). 	ag{3} \] Here \(R_j\) is the original common-shift Jacobi determinant derivative, with \(c_0=2\cos	heta\) held fixed. At every physical second endpoint, (3) has the value and required first normal of \(G_j\). Consequently its use below is exact under subsequent original traces in that endpoint, with all spectators and mixed normals retained. It is not a replacement of an arbitrary free-boundary polynomial. Choose real intervals \[ I\Subset J\Subset(0,1/2) 	ag{4} \] with additional fixed real buffers on both sides. Let \(V\) be a bounded simply connected angular parameter domain containing a real interval; use a slightly larger domain and compact buffers whenever estimates are made. Require \(V\Subset\{|\Re u|<\pi\}\), so that \(w(V)\) lies in the spectral slit. Domains can be chosen symmetric in \(u\). For the first degree use bounded simply connected domains \[ \overline{\mathcal D_1}\subset\mathcal D_2,\qquad \overline{\mathcal D_2}\subset\mathcal D_3, 	ag{5} \] with positive buffer distances, containing the enlarged real interval in (4). Paths from a real base point to points of these domains have uniformly bounded length. Finite buffered tubes about a simple path and a real interval suffice. Require that their closures avoid \(X=0,1/2\) and the other zeros of \(\sin(2\pi X)\). On a neighborhood of the buffered product set define \[ a=	an(t/2)=\cot(\pi X),\qquad b=	an(u/2),\qquad q_*^2=1+a^2+b^2, 	ag{6} \] on the original branch, and put \[ \lambda= rac{q_*+a}{q_*-a},\qquad \lambda+\lambda^{-1}=2+ rac{4a^2}{1+b^2}. 	ag{7} \] The regular-chart requirements are that \(q_*,q_*+a,q_*-a\) are units and that \[ |1-\lambda^{-2}|\ge c>0 . 	ag{8} \] The logarithm of \(\lambda\) is the continuation of the physical real-degree branch. It is single valued on these product domains. For real \(X\in J\), the same branch has \(|\lambda|>1\), uniformly on compact second-parameter sets. No such modulus inequality is required at a nonreal first degree. Let \[ \Psi(X,u)=\psi(\pi-2\pi X,u) 	ag{9} \] be the original edge action on this continuation, with its real calibration. It obeys \[ \partial_X\Psi=\operatorname{Log}\lambda. 	ag{10} \] Equivalently, fix its value at a real degree from the actual slit-row profile and integrate (10). This fixes the constant, not just the derivative. The two descriptions agree on real degree and hence on the connected continuation chart. **Theorem 1.** On every such chart there is a holomorphic unit \(\mathcal A_N(X,u)\), anchored at an actual physical row \(X_*=X_{j_*}\in J\), for which \[ \mathcal A_N(X_*,u)=F_{j_*}(w(u)). 	ag{11} \] On compact buffered subsets of \(\mathcal D_1	imes V\), \[ \log\mathcal A_N-N\Psi=o(N) 	ag{12} \] with compatible logarithms. On the physical window \(X_j\in I\), \[  egin{split} \mathcal A_N(X_j,u)/F_j(w(u))-1&=O(e^{-\kappa N}),\  rac{\partial_X\mathcal A_N(X_j,u) -C'(X_j)\widehat G_j(w(u))} {F_j(w(u))}&=O(e^{-\kappa N}) \end{split} 	ag{13} \] for some fixed \(\kappa>0\). All assertions are uniform on the fixed second-parameter compact, including every fixed exterior derivative. On second-parameter compacts with \(\Re w<2\), the \(o(N)\) in (12) is \(O(\log N)\). There are holomorphic representatives \(\mathcal F_N^\sigma\), \(\sigma=\pm1\), with the exact window identities \[ \mathcal F_N^\sigma(X_j,u)=F_j(w(u)),\qquad \partial_X\mathcal F_N^\sigma(X_j,u) =C'(X_j)\widehat G_j(w(u)), 	ag{14} \] and \[ e^{-N\Psi}(\mathcal F_N^\sigma-\mathcal A_N) =O(e^{-\kappa_1N}) \quad	ext{on }\mathcal D_1\cap\{\sigma\Im X\ge0\}. 	ag{15} \] The estimate holds on every fixed compact part of that half-domain, with no restriction on its fixed height beyond membership in the chart. There is also a fixed sufficiently thin opposite collar. Fixed derivatives cost only polynomial factors, absorbed by decreasing \(\kappa_1\). In particular the representatives have the own-action upper bound \(\exp\{N\Re\Psi+o(N)\}\). At physical second endpoints (14) includes all original required mixed jets. At its odd simple node only the value is prescribed. This theorem concerns the bulk window (4), not the whole first grid. ## 2. Constructing a mode without off-real modulus ordering In centered coordinates the exact coefficients are \[ A_h(X)=  rac{[2\sin(\pi X+\pi h/2)]^4} {4\sin(2\pi X)\sin(2\pi X+\pi h)},\qquad C_h(X)=  rac{[2\sin(\pi X-\pi h/2)]^4} {4\sin(2\pi X-\pi h)\sin(2\pi X)} . 	ag{16} \] They are the original \(A(j),C(j)\) at \(X=X_j\). The exact physical ratio \(ho_j=F_j/F_{j-1}\) satisfies \[ ho_{j+1}=f_h(X_j,u,ho_j),\qquad f_h(X,u,z)=a_h(X,u)-b_h(X)z^{-1}, 	ag{17} \] where \[ a_h=1+(c_0-w(u))/A_h+C_h/A_h,\qquad b_h=C_h/A_h . 	ag{18} \] On the buffered domains these coefficients, their inverses where used, and their fixed derivatives are uniformly bounded. They have holomorphic expansions at \(h=0\), with \[ b_0=1,\qquad a_0=2+(2-w(u))\cot^2(\pi X). 	ag{19} \] Thus \(\lambda=f_0(X,u,\lambda)\). We construct \(\mathcal R_N=\lambda+r_N\) such that \[ \mathcal R_N(X+h,u)-f_h(X,u,\mathcal R_N(X,u)) =O(e^{-cN}),\qquad r_N=O(h). 	ag{20} \] Write \(L=1-\lambda^{-2}\), and define \[ \mathcal N(r)=(\lambda+r)-f_0(X,u,\lambda+r)-Lr. 	ag{21} \] It is \(O(r^2)\), with Lipschitz constant \(O(h)\) on \(|r|\le C_0h\). The shifted equation is equivalent to \[  egin{split} Lr={}&[f_h-f_0](X,u,\lambda+r) -[\lambda(X+h,u)-\lambda(X,u)]\ &-[r(X+h,u)-r(X,u)]-\mathcal N(r). \end{split} 	ag{22} \] This is an exact fixed-point equation, not a formal expansion. Its constant term is \(O(h)\). On domains eroded by \(\delta\ge2h\), Cauchy's estimate bounds its Lipschitz constant, after multiplication by \(L^{-1}\), by \[ C(h+h/\delta). 	ag{23} \] All constants are uniform in the buffered exterior parameter. Choose \(\delta=Mh\), with \(M\) a sufficiently large fixed number. The map in (22), divided by \(L\), preserves a ball \(\|r\|\le C_0h\) and contracts successive differences by at most \(1/2\) between successive eroded domains. Starting from zero, perform \(K\ge c_0/h\) iterations within a fixed part of the available domain reserve. The last difference and the residual of (22) are \(O(e^{-c_1/h})\). Reserve a further fixed buffer for derivatives. This proves (20), with all fixed derivatives. The construction is holomorphic in \(u\); evenness in \(u\), when present in the parameter domain, is preserved at every iteration. This is the scalar version of the nested-domain analytic graph construction in the pinned continuation theorem. Its use here rests on the explicit inverse \(L^{-1}\), not on a stable off-real eigenvalue or on diagonalizing a varying matrix and ignoring the coupling terms. ## 3. Real source comparison and the anchored primitive On a sufficiently thin complex neighborhood of the enlarged real interval, the actual slit ratio theorem gives \[ ho_j=\lambda(X_j,u)+O(h),\qquad |\partial_zf_h(X,u,z)|\le\vartheta<1 	ag{24} \] for \(z\) in the relevant neighborhoods of \(\lambda\). The centered shift changes the pinned limiting argument by \(h/2\), which is \(O(h)\); it changes no contraction assertion. Let \(\mathcal R_N^{\,0}\) be the centered version of the ratio interpolant in the pinned slit-normal theorem. Both it and (20) are \(\lambda+O(h)\), both have exponentially small shifted residual, and both are defined through a fixed earlier real buffer. Iterating their difference along the common real-direction shifts on this thin complex neighborhood gives \[ \mathcal R_N-\mathcal R_N^{\,0}=O(e^{-c_2N}) 	ag{25} \] on a smaller real tube, uniformly in the parameter. The initial difference is \(O(h)\); its contribution is \(\vartheta^{cN}O(h)\). The residuals sum to an exponential error. This is the only use of attraction. It takes place in the actual real-degree region where (24) is proved. The unit \(\mathcal R_N\) has a holomorphic logarithm \(\ell_N\) on the product chart, continued from \(\operatorname{Log}\lambda\), and \(\ell_N-\operatorname{Log}\lambda=O(h)\). Use the same actual anchor \(X_*\) for the two mode constructions. Define the finite Euler--Maclaurin primitive \[  egin{split} L_N(X,u)={}&h^{-1}\int_{X_*}^{X}\ell_N(s,u)\,ds +	frac12[\ell_N(X,u)-\ell_N(X_*,u)]\ &+\sum_{
u=1}^{p_N-1}  rac{B_{2
u}h^{2
u-1}}{(2
u)!} [\partial_X^{2
u-1}\ell_N(X,u) -\partial_X^{2
u-1}\ell_N(X_*,u)],\ \mathcal A_N(X,u)={}&F_{j_*}(w(u))e^{L_N(X,u)}, \qquad p_N=\lfloor cNfloor . \end{split} 	ag{26} \] Choose \(c>0\) sufficiently small relative to the fixed analytic buffer radius. The factorial Cauchy and Bernoulli estimates in the pinned interpolation proof give \[ L_N(X+h,u)-L_N(X,u) =\ell_N(X+h,u)+O(e^{-c_3N}). 	ag{27} \] This estimate applies to complex \(X\): the remainder is estimated on the segment \([X,X+h]\) and its fixed complex neighborhood. The higher endpoint terms in (26) have total size \(O(h)\). The path-length bound and (10) consequently give \[ L_N(X,u)=N[\Psi(X,u)-\Psi(X_*,u)]+O(1). 	ag{28} \] At the actual anchor the slit-row theorem gives \[ \log F_{j_*}(w(u)) =N\Psi(X_*,u)+o(N). 	ag{29} \] Its original profile uses \(j_*h=X_*-h/2\). The replacement by \(X_*\) in (29) costs \(O(1)\) in the logarithm on the fixed bulk and parameter compacts. The stronger half-plane source estimate has \(O(\log N)\) in (29). Equations (28)--(29) prove (12). On the thin real tube, (25) and the same anchored construction compare \(\mathcal A_N\) to the actual normalized mode in the pinned slit-normal theorem with exponential relative accuracy. Instantiate that earlier construction with the same truncation order \(p_N\), chosen small enough for both sets of buffers. For the terms of order growing with \(N\) in (26), Cauchy's factorial bounds apply to (25) on a reserved larger tube; choose the truncation constant smaller if needed. Their sum is still exponentially small. The source's value and derivative conclusions therefore give (13), including its actual independent normal anchor. This proof does not assume that a normal is determined by values alone. For comparison with the new Sears formula, its exact identity is \[ \left.\partial_\alpha \sum_{k=0}^{j}T_k(\alpha, eta)ight|_{\alpha=j} =c'(0)F_j(c( eta))\widetilde Q_N(c( eta)) +R_j(c( eta)). 	ag{30} \] It is precisely the normal used in (3). Thus the present mode has the actual local Sears full-jet normalization. Equation (30) does not identify this mode with the Sears cutoff sum away from the physical rows. The latter's exact finite flux and diagonal divisor have not been set to zero. ## 4. Exact repair at arbitrary designated height Set \(v_N=e^{-N\Psi}\mathcal A_N\). At the nodes in \(I\) define \[  egin{split} d_j(u)&=e^{-N\Psi(X_j,u)}F_j(w(u))-v_N(X_j,u),\ b_j(u)&=e^{-N\Psi(X_j,u)} [C'(X_j)\widehat G_j(w(u)) -N\Psi_X(X_j,u)F_j(w(u))] -\partial_Xv_N(X_j,u). \end{split} 	ag{31} \] Equations (12)--(13) imply \(d_j,b_j=O(e^{-\kappa N+o(N)})\). Decrease \(\kappa\) once; these are uniform exponentially small holomorphic parameter functions with all fixed derivatives. For \(\sigma=\pm1\), put \[  egin{split} \mathcal E_N^\sigma(X,u) =\sum_{X_j\in I} ig[d_j(u) +(b_j(u)-\sigma2\pi iN d_j(u))(X-X_j) ig]\, e^{\sigma2\pi iN(X-X_j)} \operatorname{sinc}^2(N(X-X_j)),\ \mathcal F_N^\sigma =e^{N\Psi}(v_N+\mathcal E_N^\sigma). \end{split} 	ag{32} \] The value and derivative of the \(j\)-th summand at its own node are \(d_j,b_j\); every other summand has a double zero there. This proves (14) as identities of holomorphic functions of \(u\). The kernel on the second line of the summand in (32) has Fourier support \([0,2N]\) for \(\sigma=1\), and \([-2N,0]\) for \(\sigma=-1\), with total absolute coefficient mass one. Its modulus is at most one in the designated half-plane, and each fixed \(X\)-derivative costs a power of \(N\). There are \(O(N)\) terms, and \(X\) remains in a bounded set. This proves (15). In the opposite half-plane the kernel is bounded by \(e^{4\pi N|\Im X|}\), giving the stated fixed thin collar. The repair need not be even in the first angular variable. It is used in the closed window-contour identity below; no full-lens replacement is inferred from angular parity. If the second parameter domain is symmetric, the construction and repair are even in \(u\). They therefore descend holomorphically through its spectral fold \(w=-2\). Fixed spectral derivatives there are obtained by holomorphic even descent and buffered Cauchy estimates, not division by \(\sin u\). The action upper bound follows directly from (12) and (15). The common baseline also retains an exponentially accurate normalized scalar recurrence: (20),(27) give it for \(\mathcal A_N\), and finite shifts of the repaired normalized errors remain exponentially small in the designated half-domain. This does not make the raw finite Sears boundary small. ## 5. Positive reachability and coherent overlaps The regular-domain hypotheses above are available at actual positive configurations, not only on a small rectangle about real angles. Fix a positive pair \((t_*,u_*)\), in the original \(|\Re t|,|\Re u|<\pi\) strips, with \(t_*
e0\). The pinned product-domain theorem supplies simply connected symmetric angular domains containing the full real intervals and the target, on whose product \[ q_*^2
otin(-\infty,0],\qquad \Re q_*>0. 	ag{33} \] Their tangent-coordinate domains are star shaped. Moreover \[ (q_*+a)(q_*-a)=1+b^2
e0,\qquad 1-\lambda^{-2}= rac{4q_*a}{(q_*+a)^2}. 	ag{34} \] Thus the only loss of (8) in these domains is \(a=0\), namely \(t=0\). Nonreal points with \(|\lambda|=1\) are not exceptions. Connect a small positive real \(t\)-interval to \(t_*\) by a simple compact path in the first angular domain avoiding zero. Such a path exists: the real spine and the radial target arm belong to the open tangent domain, and a small arc around zero joins them. A thin bounded simply connected neighborhood of this path and the real interval has closure avoiding zero and the angular endpoints. Nested neighborhoods and the change (1) give (5), its bounded path lengths and the coefficient margins in (16). Choose a bounded buffered second-parameter neighborhood containing the desired compact target set and a real interval inside the second product domain. Equations (33)--(34) supply all the remaining uniform units and logarithms. This construction is locally uniform in the target pair and uses domains fixed before \(N\). The phase in (9) is the original branch on this path, since it agrees at the real seed and its derivative is (10). No additive phase is selected from an off-grid factorial endpoint. If \(t_*=0\) but \(u_*
e0\), one can interchange the roles for a local construction. This observation does not make a single first-degree chart cross its fold. The simultaneous complete point and a whole first-grid fold neighborhood require their existing separate constructions. There is a useful quantitative overlap statement for two charts using the same first-degree coordinate. Suppose their constructions have a connected buffered common domain, the same continued phase, and a common real seed window containing \(cN\) physical nodes. Suppose the compact target overlap is connected to that window through this common domain where both normalized representatives have the bounds just proved. Then \[ e^{-N\Psi}(\mathcal F_{N,1}-\mathcal F_{N,2}) =O(e^{-\kappa_{12}N}) 	ag{35} \] on that compact overlap, with fixed derivatives. To prove this, the normalized difference has exact zeros at every common physical node and has norm \(e^{o(N)}\) on a fixed real tube. The disk Blaschke estimate used in the pinned normal theorem therefore gives \(e^{-cN+o(N)}\) on a smaller open seed set. A finite chain of buffered three-circles estimates propagates this to the specified compact overlap. The \(o(N)\) upper exponents remain negligible at each of finitely many steps. Work uniformly on a slightly larger exterior parameter compact and then use Cauchy for its derivatives. The same argument applies to the baselines using their exponentially small nodal errors. This statement requires the connected common domain and its shared seed, or an already compared open subset. It does not control a disconnected overlap, continuation around an unrecorded branch, or an arbitrary raw cutoff transition merely because its physical jets vanish. It is a controlled transport of the constructed normalized modes. Comparison of the two constructions obtained by interchanging the endpoint roles requires its own joint seed and overlap argument; it is not included in (35). ## 6. The original window currents and the remaining obligation Let \(\eta=(-1)^{N-1}\) and \[ D_h(X)=(\pi/h)^2\sec^2(\pi X/h). 	ag{36} \] Take midpoint vertical boundaries surrounding the selected centered nodes and a window contour contained in the supplied domains. Let \(P_N^{m sp}\) be the entire original remaining spectator, with all shared variables and crossings, and set \[ g_\sigma(X)=\sin(2\pi X)\, \mathcal F_N^\sigma(X,u)P_N^{m sp}(C(X);\ldots). 	ag{37} \] Write \(P_j^{m sp}=P_N^{m sp}(c_j;\ldots)\) and \(P_{Z,j}^{m sp}=\partial_ZP_N^{m sp}(c_j;\ldots)\), with every other shared variable held fixed. Define the finite residue expression \[ \Phi_{N,I}^{\sharp}(w;\ldots) =\eta\sum_{X_j\in I} \left\{(4-c_j^2) [\widehat G_j(w)P_j^{m sp} +F_j(w)P_{Z,j}^{m sp}] -c_jF_j(w)P_j^{m sp}ight\}. 	ag{37a} \] The closed two-half residue identity gives, exactly on \(V\), \[ \Phi_{N,I}^{\sharp}(w(u);\ldots) =- rac{\eta}{2\pi^2i} \left\{\int_{E_-}D_hg_-\,dX+\int_{E_+}D_hg_+\,dX +\int_{a_N}^{b_N}D_h(g_+-g_-)\,dXight\}. 	ag{38} \] Here \(E_-\) goes down the left side, across the lower horizontal and up the right side; \(E_+\) goes up the right side, across the upper horizontal and down the left side. Every vertical half-side is retained. The representatives need not be even in the first angle: (38) is the closed positive-window residue identity, not a parity argument replacing an open full lens. The actual original window trace is the same finite expression with \(G_j\) in place of \(\widehat G_j\). Since (3) retains every physical second-endpoint jet, holomorphic division on the slit gives \[ \Phi_{N,I}^{\sharp}(w;\ldots) -\phi_{N,I} ig(K_N(Z,w)P_N^{m sp}(Z;\ldots) ig) =P_N(w)\,\mathcal B_{N,I}(w;\ldots), 	ag{38a} \] where \(\mathcal B_{N,I}\) is holomorphic on that slit, with all other original variables retained. The spectator derivative in (37a) is part of the identity. Equation (38a) preserves every required mixed physical datum in the second endpoint, and proves equality after its subsequent complete original trace, including any further spectator and its normal product rule. Thus the later complete second trace is taken on the globally defined finite residue expression (37a), or on a covering which retains every other second row. A single local \(V\)-contour is not a whole-second-grid representative. Equation (38) itself does not assert a free off-grid equality with the original normal polynomial. The baseline cancels in the real interface. The elementary identity for \(D_h(\mathcal E_N^+-\mathcal E_N^-)\) in the pinned one-sided source theorem has removable singularities at the physical nodes. It gives, on the real window, \[ |D_h(g_+-g_-)| \le C e^{N\Re\Psi-\kappa_2N} |\sin(2\pi X)P_N^{m sp}(C(X);\ldots)|. 	ag{39} \] Polynomial factors are absorbed by decreasing \(\kappa_2>0\). The actual spectator is still present. This rate is not a comparison with an unspecified parent action. Likewise (35) controls seams between the constructed representatives only with the indicated phase and connected-overlap hypotheses. It does not delete the original exterior sides in (38), the rows outside \(I\), a first-degree fold packet, or the finite Sears flux if that raw representation is used elsewhere. No claim is made that the positive geometric contour pays the remaining currents, or that its local contribution survives their sum. Those are the next whole-source estimates. ## Direct sources and author scope The complete direct texts and their used implications were read at: * [Actual slit normal connection](research_physical_row_slit_normal_connection.md), SHA256 a5084adb4ff25cb08020e5f9485bd1aaea5b49468c6ab0af311ebc1c0c504d99: actual ratios, full-normal anchor, finite analytic primitive and real-source comparison, slit bounds and dense-grid smallness. * [Common baseline and one-sided repair](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_terminal_one_sided_characteristic_continuation.md), SHA256 1316cfb9ed7fec208a8aa8308ea7015c7cf32534a8662500892f9a62b5e9b475: nested-domain analytic iteration, exact one-sided Hermite kernels, removable real interface and full original window normalization. * [Positive product domains](research_positive_wire_product_contour.md), SHA256 5646f2d6b2a8dfa2d8c49662d17f19f3743fc4efcaf3c3685c6a899975a4c230: original discriminant and fixed product domains containing real seeds and positive targets, with all branches retained. * [Exact Sears full normals](research_finite_sears_full_normal_source.md), SHA256 07f9db823f7eee2e5d6b48ecdb8c82875d60915b9c0211d6f375b4b318fc271c: exact local degree derivative and mixed-jet normalization, and the finite flux and diagonal divisor that remain in a raw cutoff. Only written mathematics, source reads and metadata hashes were used. No mathematical program, numerical evaluation, test or compilation was run. Adopted notes and public manuscripts were unchanged.

title: Riccati transport for the original physical edge rows
text: # Riccati transport for the original physical edge rows Research note, 3 November 2026. Frozen manuscripts are unchanged. The original physical-row recurrence has a useful contraction that survives complex free colors. It gives a uniform exponential asymptotic for ratios of actual kernel values, with a bounded nonzero transport factor. The phase is the original edge-phase difference. Only the free-color endpoint is complex in this statement; the other endpoint remains on the physical grid. The argument uses the exact positive-real ratios from [the Jacobi boundary problem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_physical_jacobi_charge_boundary.md). It does not infer nonzero transport from a separation of two formal characteristic roots. ## 1. The original recurrence and its contracting domain For \(N\ge3\), put \[ \theta=\pi/N,\quad c_j=2\cos((2j+1)\theta),\quad J_N=\lfloor(N-1)/2\rfloor,\qquad F_{j,N}(w)=K_N(c_j,w). \tag{1} \] Here \(K_N\) is the original finite Newton kernel. We keep its normalization \(F_{0,N}=1\). For \(0\le r<J_N\), \[ \begin{split} A_{r,N}&=\frac{[2\sin((r+1)\theta)]^4} {4\sin((2r+1)\theta)\sin((2r+2)\theta)},\\ C_{r,N}&=\frac{[2\sin(r\theta)]^4} {4\sin(2r\theta)\sin((2r+1)\theta)}, \qquad C_{0,N}=0 . \end{split} \tag{2} \] The value equation is exactly \[ A_{r,N}F_{r+1,N} =(c_0+A_{r,N}+C_{r,N}-w)F_{r,N}-C_{r,N}F_{r-1,N}. \tag{3} \] All coefficients used in (3) are finite. The coalescing middle row at even levels is not treated as an ordinary row beyond this range. On \(\Re w<c_0\), the actual ratios \(\rho_{r,N}=F_{r,N}/F_{r-1,N}\) satisfy \[ \Re\rho_{r+1,N}\ge1+\frac{c_0-\Re w}{A_{r,N}}>1. \tag{4} \] This follows inductively from \[ \rho_{r+1,N}=\mathscr R_{r,N,w}(\rho_{r,N}),\qquad \mathscr R_{r,N,w}(z)=1+d_{r,N}+q_{r,N}(1-z^{-1}), \quad d_{r,N}=\frac{c_0-w}{A_{r,N}},\quad q_{r,N}=\frac{C_{r,N}}{A_{r,N}}, \tag{5} \] with \(\rho_{1,N}=1+(c_0-w)/A_{0,N}\). Indeed \(\Re z\ge1\) implies \(\Re(z^{-1})\le1\). In particular no physical value \(F_{r,N}\) vanishes in this half-plane. There is a stronger elementary coefficient fact: \[ q_{r,N}= \left(\frac{\sin(r\theta)}{\sin((r+1)\theta)}\right)^3 \frac{\cos((r+1)\theta)}{\cos(r\theta)} \in(0,1)\quad(r>0). \tag{6} \] Both factors are positive and less than one in the ordinary range. Also \(q_{0,N}=0\). Therefore, on any half-plane \(\Re z\ge1+\kappa\), \(\kappa>0\), \[ |\mathscr R_{r,N,w}(z)-\mathscr R_{r,N,w}(\zeta)| \le(1+\kappa)^{-2}|z-\zeta| \quad(\Re z,\Re\zeta\ge1+\kappa). \tag{7} \] This contraction is the reason a second solution cannot cancel the growing component of the normalized physical value solution in the result below. ## 2. Uniform attraction to the limiting root Fix \[ 0<\varepsilon<1/4,\qquad \gamma>0,\qquad R<\infty, \qquad \mathcal W_{\gamma,R} =\{w\in\mathbb C:\Re w\le2-\gamma,\ |w|\le R\}. \tag{8} \] Empty free-color sets can simply be omitted. For \(0<x<1/2\), define \[ p(x,w)=2+(2-w)\cot^2(\pi x),\qquad \lambda(x,w)=\frac{p(x,w)+\sqrt{p(x,w)^2-4}}2. \tag{9} \] The square root is positive for real \(p>2\), continued through \(\Re p>2\). This is a single-valued analytic branch: \(p^2-4\) does not meet the nonpositive real axis there. The chosen root satisfies \[ |\lambda|>1,\qquad \Re\lambda\ge1+(2-\Re w)\cot^2(\pi x)>1. \tag{10} \] To see the first assertion, continue from real \(p>2\). A root could cross the unit circle only if \(p=\lambda+\lambda^{-1}\) belonged to \([-2,2]\). Then \(\Re p=\Re\lambda(1+|\lambda|^{-2})>2\) gives \(\Re\lambda>1\). Finally \(\lambda=2+(2-w)\cot^2(\pi x)-\lambda^{-1}\) gives the displayed lower bound. We use the principal logarithm of this right-half-plane root. **Theorem 1.** There are \(N_0\) and \(C\), depending only on \(\varepsilon,\gamma,R\), such that for \(N\ge N_0\), \(w\in\mathcal W_{\gamma,R}\), and every physical row \(\varepsilon\le j/N\le1/2-\varepsilon\), \[ |\rho_{j,N}(w)-\lambda(j/N,w)|\le C/N. \tag{11} \] For each fixed nonnegative integer \(\ell\), the same estimate holds after \(\ell\) derivatives in \(w\), with a constant \(C_\ell\). *Proof.* Work first on the larger real row interval \[ I_0=[\varepsilon/4,\ 1/2-\varepsilon/2]. \tag{12} \] The sine denominators in (2), expressed in terms of \(x=r/N\), are bounded away from zero there. Taylor's formula, uniformly for \(w\in\mathcal W_{\gamma,R}\), therefore gives \[ \begin{split} A_{r,N}&=\tan^2(\pi r/N)+O(N^{-1}),\\ q_{r,N}&=1+O(N^{-1}),\\ d_{r,N}&=(2-w)\cot^2(\pi r/N)+O(N^{-1}). \end{split} \tag{13} \] The limiting function \(\lambda(x,w)\) and its first \(x\)-derivative are uniformly bounded on this compact parameter set. For large \(N\), \(c_0-\Re w\ge\gamma/2\). Equations (4), (10), and the uniform upper bound on \(A\) give a common \(\kappa>0\) such that \[ \Re\rho_{r,N}\ge1+\kappa,\qquad \Re\lambda(r/N,w)\ge1+\kappa \tag{14} \] whenever \(r/N\in I_0\) and the preceding row also lies in \(I_0\). Let \(a=(1+\kappa)^{-2}<1\). The exact limiting fixed-point equation, (13), and the bounded \(x\)-derivative imply \[ \left|\mathscr R_{r,N,w}(\lambda(r/N,w)) -\lambda((r+1)/N,w)\right|\le C_1/N. \tag{15} \] Thus, with \(e_r=|\rho_{r,N}-\lambda(r/N,w)|\), \[ e_{r+1}\le a e_r+C_1/N. \tag{16} \] Start at \(r_0=\lceil\varepsilon N/2\rceil\). The original initial solution gives a uniformly bounded \(e_{r_0}\); it is not an assumed preparation condition. In fact the preceding actual ratio has modulus at least one, so (5) and (6) give \[ |\rho_{r_0,N}|\le3+|d_{r_0-1,N}|, \tag{17} \] and the right side is bounded on \(I_0\). Iterating (16) gives \[ e_r\le C_2 a^{r-r_0}+\frac{C_1}{N(1-a)} . \tag{18} \] Every row in the stated interval has \(r-r_0\ge\varepsilon N/2-1\). This proves (11). For derivatives, repeat the argument on the larger free-color set \(\mathcal W_{\gamma/2,R+1}\). A fixed small complex disk around every point of \(\mathcal W_{\gamma,R}\) lies in that set. Both the actual ratios and the chosen root are holomorphic there. Cauchy's formula applied to (11) proves every fixed derivative estimate. \(\square\) ## 3. The logarithmic error and the nonzero transport factor On \(\Re w<c_0\), define the logarithm of the actual normalized ratio by \[ L_{i,j,N}(w)= \sum_{r=i+1}^{j}\operatorname{Log}\rho_{r,N}(w), \qquad \exp L_{i,j,N}=F_{j,N}/F_{i,N}. \tag{19} \] This is the holomorphic branch that is real on the real free-color interval. It need not equal the principal logarithm of the final quotient after its argument has wound around zero. **Corollary 2.** Under the hypotheses of Theorem 1, uniformly for \(\varepsilon\le i/N\le j/N\le1/2-\varepsilon\), \[ \left|L_{i,j,N}(w) -N\int_{i/N}^{j/N}\operatorname{Log}\lambda(x,w)\,dx\right| \le C\frac{j-i}{N}. \tag{20} \] The error is holomorphic and obeys the same bound, with a new constant, after every fixed number of free-color derivatives. Consequently the actual ratio has the form \[ \frac{F_{j,N}(w)}{F_{i,N}(w)} =B_{i,j,N}(w) \exp\left(N\int_{i/N}^{j/N} \operatorname{Log}\lambda(x,w)\,dx\right), \qquad e^{-C}\le|B_{i,j,N}(w)|\le e^C . \tag{21} \] The factor \(B_{i,j,N}\) is holomorphic and nonzero. *Proof.* On the common half-plane in (14), the logarithm is Lipschitz with constant \((1+\kappa)^{-1}\). Summing (11) therefore changes (19) by at most \(C(j-i)/N\) when each ratio is replaced by \(\lambda(r/N,w)\). The bounded \(x\)-derivative of \(\operatorname{Log}\lambda\) gives the same bound for the error of the right-endpoint Riemann sum. This proves (20). The derivative assertion again follows by applying the argument on a larger free-color set and using Cauchy's formula. Exponentiating the actual holomorphic error gives (21). \(\square\) This is a bounded-factor asymptotic. It does not assert that \(B_{i,j,N}\) converges, or that it equals \(1+O(N^{-1})\). The nonzero factor in (21) has been obtained from the normalized original solution, rather than inserted as an unspecified branch coefficient. ## 4. Agreement with the original edge phase The relation to the geometric return is explicit. For \(\Re w<2\), take the square root of \(2-w\) with positive real part. Then \[ \operatorname{Log}\lambda(x,w) =2\operatorname{arsinh} \left(\frac{\sqrt{2-w}}2\cot(\pi x)\right). \tag{22} \] The argument of the square root has absolute value less than \(\pi/4\). The indicated inverse hyperbolic sine has imaginary part in \((-\pi/4,\pi/4)\), so the logarithm in (22) is the same one used in (19)--(21). Squaring \(\sqrt{1+z^2}+z\), where \(z=\sqrt{2-w}\cot(\pi x)/2\), verifies its characteristic equation and proves (22). If \(w=-2\cos u\) and \(\cos(u/2)=\sqrt{2-w}/2\), the [original edge return](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_terminal_powers_three_and_above.md#1-the-phase-and-its-selected-leaf-solution) satisfies \[ \psi_t(t,u)=-\frac1\pi\operatorname{arsinh} (\tan(t/2)\cos(u/2)). \tag{23} \] It follows from (22)--(23) that \[ \int_a^b\operatorname{Log}\lambda(x,w)\,dx =\psi(\pi-2\pi b,u)-\psi(\pi-2\pi a,u). \tag{24} \] An additive normalization of \(\psi\) cancels here. The branches are continued from the complete real edge; no exponentiated characteristic is used to choose a new logarithmic lift. The actual physical angle is \(\tau_j=\pi-(2j+1)\pi/N\). Replacing \(j/N\) by \((j+1/2)/N\) at both endpoints of the integral changes the error in (20) by at most \(C(j-i)/N\). Thus \[ \frac{K_N(c_j,w)}{K_N(c_i,w)} =\widetilde B_{i,j,N}(w) e^{\,N\{\psi(\tau_j,u)-\psi(\tau_i,u)\}}, \qquad e^{-C}\le|\widetilde B_{i,j,N}(w)|\le e^C. \tag{25} \] Indeed the change of integral is the integral, over a shift of size \(1/(2N)\), of the difference of its two endpoint integrands. Their Lipschitz bound gives the stated estimate. For the positive path charge cube, the [geometric half-plane theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_geometric_spectral_half_plane.md) gives \(\Re w<7/4\) and \(|w|<7/2\). Hence a single choice \(\gamma=1/4,\ R=7/2\) covers every geometric free color, independently of the fixed path and its powers. The other endpoint in (25) remains an actual physical row. This result neither continues that row to a complex angle nor estimates the original signed Fourier sum over rows. ## 5. Why the determinant formula does not replace the contraction The existing Jacobi representation gives the exact Stieltjes formula \[ F_{j,N}(w)= \frac{\det(\mathcal J_j-wI)}{\prod_{r<j}A_{r,N}}, \qquad -\partial_w\log F_{j,N}(w) =\operatorname{Tr}(\mathcal J_j-wI)^{-1}. \tag{26} \] It proves zero-freeness and bounds free-color derivatives. By itself it does not compare neighboring row sizes at the required precision. The Riccati map is the exact Schur-complement recursion for these determinants. Its contraction (7) supplies the quantitative attraction and the bounded logarithmic error, without a separate assumption about spectral-measure convergence. ## 6. Absolute normalization from the original first row The normalization \(F_{0,N}=1\) also determines the exponential rate without a reference row in the interior. Fix \(0<\alpha<1/2\) and the same free-color set (8). Write \(\lambda_r=\lambda(r/N,w)\). **Theorem 3.** Uniformly for \(1\le j\le\alpha N\) and \(w\in\mathcal W_{\gamma,R}\), for all sufficiently large \(N\), \[ \left|\log F_{j,N}(w) -N\int_0^{j/N}\operatorname{Log}\lambda(x,w)\,dx\right| \le C\log(j+1). \tag{27} \] Here \(\log F_{j,N}=\sum_{r=1}^j\operatorname{Log}\rho_{r,N}\) is the actual normalized holomorphic logarithm. The integral converges at zero. Every fixed free-color derivative of the error has the same logarithmic bound. In particular \[ (j+1)^{-C}\le \left|F_{j,N}(w) \exp\left(-N\int_0^{j/N}\operatorname{Log}\lambda(x,w)\,dx\right) \right|\le(j+1)^C . \tag{28} \] *Proof.* The endpoint coefficient has the exact form \[ A_{r-1,N} =\tan^2(r\theta) \frac{\sin(2r\theta)}{\sin((2r-1)\theta)}. \tag{29} \] For \(1\le r\le\alpha N\), the sine ratio is bounded above and below by positive constants depending only on \(\alpha\). For example, putting \(m_\alpha=\sin(2\pi\alpha)/(2\pi\alpha)>0\), these bounds can be taken as \(m_\alpha\) and \(2\). Use that \(\sin x/x\) decreases on \((0,\pi)\) for the upper bound and \(\sin x\ge m_\alpha x\) for the lower. Moreover \[ \left|\frac{\sin((2r-1)\theta)}{\sin(2r\theta)}-1\right| \le\frac{1}{2m_\alpha r}. \tag{30} \] These estimates and (4) give uniform comparability \[ c(1+\cot^2(r\theta)) \le|\rho_{r,N}|,\ |\lambda_r| \le C(1+\cot^2(r\theta)). \tag{31} \] For the upper bound on \(\rho\), use \(|\rho_{r,N}|\le3+|(c_0-w)/A_{r-1,N}|\). For its lower bound use (4) and \(c_0-\Re w\ge\gamma/2\). For \(\lambda\), use (10) and \(|\lambda|\le|p|+1\). Both real parts also lie in one common half-plane \(\Re z\ge1+\kappa\), with \(\kappa>0\), throughout this range. We next bound the local relative defect down to the first row. Equations (6) and (29)--(30) give, for \(r\ge1\), \[ \begin{split} |q_{r,N}-1|&\le C/(r+1),\\ \left|d_{r,N}-(2-w)\cot^2((r+1)\theta)\right| &\le \frac{C}{r+1}|(2-w)\cot^2((r+1)\theta)|. \end{split} \tag{32} \] For the first estimate, the difference of two consecutive sines is at most \(\theta\), their denominator is at least a fixed multiple of \((r+1)\theta\), and \(\cos(r\theta)\) is bounded away from zero. Apply these facts to the two ratios in (6). For the second estimate use (30) with \(r+1\) in place of \(r\), and \((c_0-w)/(2-w)=1+O(N^{-2})\). The limiting root has a controlled logarithmic variation at the endpoint: \[ |\partial_x\operatorname{Log}\lambda(x,w)| \le\left|\frac{\partial_x[(2-w)\cot^2(\pi x)]} {(2-w)\cot^2(\pi x)}\right| =\frac{2\pi}{\sin(\pi x)\cos(\pi x)} \le\frac{C_\alpha}{x}. \tag{33} \] Indeed its exact derivative has denominator \(\sqrt{d(d+4)}\), with \(d=(2-w)\cot^2(\pi x)\); \(\Re d>0\) implies \(|d+4|\ge|d|\). Thus \(|\lambda_r/\lambda_{r+1}-1|\le C/r\). Combining this with (32) and the fixed-point equation for \(\lambda_{r+1}\) yields \[ \frac{|\mathscr R_{r,N,w}(\lambda_r)-\lambda_{r+1}|} {|\lambda_{r+1}|}\le C/r. \tag{34} \] For completeness, split the numerator by inserting \(\mathscr R_{r,N,w}(\lambda_{r+1})\). The first difference is \(q_{r,N}(\lambda_r-\lambda_{r+1})/ (\lambda_r\lambda_{r+1})\), up to sign. The second is the difference in \(d\) from (32) plus \((q_{r,N}-1)(1-\lambda_{r+1}^{-1})\). Also \(|d|\le4|\lambda_{r+1}|\), since \(d=\lambda_{r+1}+\lambda_{r+1}^{-1}-2\). This proves (34) without an unbounded absolute coefficient estimate. Let \(e_r=|\rho_{r,N}-\lambda_r|/|\lambda_r|\). The exact difference of two Riccati maps now gives \[ e_{r+1} \le\frac{q_{r,N}}{|\rho_{r,N}\lambda_{r+1}|}e_r+C/r \le a e_r+C/r,\qquad a=(1+\kappa)^{-2}<1. \tag{35} \] The factor \(\lambda_r\) cancels in this relative estimate. Equation (31) bounds \(e_1\) uniformly for the original first row. Iteration gives \(e_r\le C/r\): in the convolution \(\sum_{k<r}a^{r-1-k}/k\), terms with \(k\ge r/2\) are bounded by \(2/[r(1-a)]\), and the remaining terms by \(a^{r/2-1}(1+\log r)\). The initial term is exponentially smaller. For large \(r\), \(e_r\le1/2\) implies \(|\operatorname{Log}\rho_{r,N}-\operatorname{Log}\lambda_r| \le2e_r\). The finitely many smaller rows have the same bound \(C/r\), after enlarging \(C\), by (31) and the right-half-plane arguments of both factors. Therefore their total logarithmic difference is \(O(\log(j+1))\). Finally the elementary root expansion at \(x=0\) is \[ \operatorname{Log}\lambda(x,w) =\operatorname{Log}(2-w)-2\log(\pi x)+O(x^2), \tag{36} \] uniformly with every fixed free-color derivative; the \(x\)-derivative of the remainder is \(O(x)\). After adding \(2\log x\), the remaining function has a bounded first derivative on \([0,\alpha]\), so its Riemann-sum error is bounded. For the singular part, the error is \(2(j\log j-j-\log(j!))=O(\log(j+1))\); the elementary integral bounds for \(\log x\) suffice. This proves (27). Cauchy's formula on the enlarged free-color set used in Theorem 1 gives the derivative claim, and exponentiation gives (28). \(\square\) The integral in (27) is the absolute original edge phase. The normalization at its degenerate boundary is \(\psi(\pi,u)=0\). One can check this directly: the [symmetric return formula](research_edge_hessian_and_phase_response.md#1-branches-and-the-exact-edge-matrix) \(\psi_u(t,u)=-\pi^{-1}\operatorname{arsinh} (\tan(u/2)\cos(t/2))\) tends to zero at \(t=\pi\), so that boundary value is independent of \(u\). At \(u=0\), \(\int_0^\pi\operatorname{arsinh}(\tan(t/2))\,dt=4G\), where \(G=-\int_0^{\pi/4}\log(\tan s)\,ds\) is Catalan's constant. This cancels \(\psi(0,0)=4G/\pi\). The branch continues from the complete edge with this normalization. Thus, on each compact physical-row interval from Theorem 1, (27) also gives \[ \log K_N(c_j,w) =N\psi(\tau_j,u)+O(\log N), \qquad w=-2\cos u. \tag{37} \] The half-offset changes the exponent by \(O(1)\) on this interior interval. In particular the polynomial lower factor in (28) is anchored at the exact value \(F_{0,N}=1\); it contains no unknown reference-row amplitude. This remains a theorem about physical rows with complex free color, not a complex-row interpolation or a lower bound for their signed trace. ## 7. Finite reproduction Run ~~~sh python3 experiments/check_physical_row_riccati_transport.py \ --precision 140 \ --output repro/results/research-physical-row-riccati-transport.json ~~~ The [checker](../experiments/check_physical_row_riccati_transport.py) evaluates the original rows by the terminating Newton sum, independently of the recurrence used in the proof. The [saved record](../repro/results/research-physical-row-riccati-transport.json) covers 16 complete or complex free-color cases at levels \(32,64,128,256\). It checks 720 exact row recurrences, 600 bulk contraction inequalities, and 704 endpoint relative-contraction inequalities. It also checks the continued-log product and the return-phase identity with the physical half-offset. The scaled ratio and logarithmic errors in that record are reported as diagnostics. They are not used as a proof of a uniform asymptotic estimate; that estimate follows from the contraction and endpoint arguments above.

title: Actual first-normal normalization of the physical row interpolant
text:
# Actual first-normal normalization of the physical row interpolant Private written proof, 16 November 2026. The analytic interpolation of physical row values has a scalar first-normal normalization, determined by the original source. On every compact spectral slit chart that normalization is exponentially accurate. Its proof uses the common-shift Jacobi derivative, exact kernel symmetry at the physical grid, and analytic propagation of smallness. It does not assume a source coefficient from a formal characteristic equation. The degree variable remains in a fixed bulk interval. The result continues the second spectral variable through arbitrary compact subsets of its slit plane; it does not continue the first degree variable to an arbitrary height. An exact scalar full-jet interpolant on a thin degree strip follows, with the original row action. Equality at its bulk subgrid is not equality in the whole original trace. ## 1. Source, normalization and statement Put \(h=N^{-1}\), \(	heta=\pi/N\), and \[ c(r)=2\cos((2r+1)	heta),\qquad c_j=c(j),\qquad C_N(x)=c(Nx)=2\cos(2\pi x+	heta). 	ag{1} \] Use the original kernel \(K_N\), physical rows and normals \[ F_j(w)=K_N(c_j,w),\qquad G_j(w)=\partial_zK_N(c_j,w), \qquad \Omega=\mathbb C\setminus[2,\infty). 	ag{2} \] Here \(P_N(w)=2T_N(w/2)+2\) and \(s_1=2\sin	heta\). The first normal \(G_j\) is prescribed only at double nodes. All rows in a fixed compact degree interval inside \((0,1/2)\) are double nodes for sufficiently large \(N\). We retain the actual common-shift Jacobi polynomials \[ F_j^{(\varepsilon)}(w)=  rac{\det(\mathcal J_j(\varepsilon)-wI)} {\prod_{r<j}A(r+\varepsilon)},\qquad R_j(w)=\left.\partial_\varepsilon F_j^{(\varepsilon)}(w)ight|_0, \qquad D_j(w)=R_j(w)/F_j(w). 	ag{3} \] Here \[ A(r)= rac{[2\sin((r+1)	heta)]^4} {4\sin((2r+1)	heta)\sin((2r+2)	heta)},\quad C(r)= rac{[2\sin(r	heta)]^4} {4\sin(2r	heta)\sin((2r+1)	heta)},\quad C(0)=0. 	ag{4} \] The diagonal of \(\mathcal J_j(\varepsilon)\) is \(c_0+A(r+\varepsilon)+C(r+\varepsilon)\); its off-diagonal is \(-\sqrt{A(r+\varepsilon)C(r+1+\varepsilon)}\). In particular \(c_0\) is held fixed during this common shift. The definitions at the left endpoint have their removable values. Let \(\widetilde Q_N(w)\) be precisely the even logarithmic-factorial representative of \(Q_0=G_0\) in the pinned residue theorem. Its spectral descent is holomorphic on \(\Omega\). The pole-free source normal is \[ \widehat G_j(w)=  rac{F_j(w)}{c'(j)} \{c'(0)\widetilde Q_N(w)+D_j(w)\},\qquad c'(j)=-4	heta\sin((2j+1)	heta). 	ag{5} \] This preserves the value and required first \(w\)-normal of \(G_j\) at every physical second endpoint. It may replace \(G_j\) inside a subsequent original trace, with all mixed normals and spectators. It is not an equality of free off-grid polynomials. For clarity the source term behind (5) is \[  egin{split} c'(j)G_j(w)={}&c'(0)F_j(w)Q_0(w)+R_j(w)\ &+ rac{c'(0)P_N(w)}{N^2s_1^2} F_j(w)[(\mathcal J_j-wI)^{-1}]_{00}. \end{split} 	ag{6} \] The last factor multiplied by \(F_j\) is a polynomial cofactor. It is removed only in the full physical-jet class, and the replacement of \(Q_0\) is the specified one in (5). Fix \[ 0<a<b<1/2,\qquad \mathcal K\Subset\Omega. 	ag{7} \] Every construction below uses one slightly larger degree interval and a bounded simply connected slit neighborhood of \(\mathcal K\), with fixed buffers. The neighborhood also contains a fixed real interval inside \((-2,2)\). These choices precede \(N\). Constants and positive exponential rates can depend on those choices. Write \[ \lambda(x,w)+\lambda(x,w)^{-1} =2+(2-w)\cot^2(\pi x),\qquad \Psi(x,w)=\int_0^x\operatorname{Log}\lambda(s,w)\,ds . 	ag{8} \] For real \(0<x<1/2\), select the root \(|\lambda|>1\), positive for \(w<2\), and its real-normalized logarithm. The integral converges at zero. Extend \(x\) only to a sufficiently thin complex neighborhood of the enlarged bulk interval. **Theorem 1.** There is a holomorphic unit \(A_N(x,w)\) on such a degree neighborhood times a neighborhood of \(\mathcal K\), and an actual anchor \(j_*=j_*(N)\), \(x_*=j_*h\), in the interior of the degree interval, such that \[ A_N(x_*,w)=F_{j_*}(w). 	ag{9} \] Uniformly for \(j/N\in[a,b]\), \(w\in\mathcal K\), and every fixed number of \(w\)-derivatives, \[  egin{split} A_N(jh,w)/F_j(w)-1&=O(e^{-\kappa N}),\  rac{\partial_xA_N(jh,w)-C_N'(jh)\widehat G_j(w)} {F_j(w)}&=O(e^{-\kappa N}). \end{split} 	ag{10} \] The rate can be decreased when taking derivatives. The actual scalar connection coefficient is \[  oxed{\quad a_N(w)=c'(0)\widetilde Q_N(w)+D_{j_*}(w) -h\,\partial_x\log A_N(x_*,w). \quad} 	ag{11} \] It satisfies \[ \partial_w^k a_N(w)=O_k(e^{-\kappa_{\mathcal K}N}) \quad(w\in\mathcal K) 	ag{12} \] for every fixed \(k\). Thus no unspecified initial normal remains in (10). On the degree neighborhood, \[ N^{-1}\log A_N(x,w)=\Psi(x,w)+o(1) 	ag{13} \] locally uniformly, with the original normalized logarithm. On compact subsets of \(\Re w<2\), the error in \(\log A_N-N\Psi\) is \(O(\log N)\). On a general slit compact only \(o(N)\), or an arbitrary fixed exponential tolerance, is asserted. ## 2. Uniform nonzero ratios on the whole slit The exact value recurrence is \[ ho_{j+1}=\mathscr R_{N,jh,w}(ho_j),\qquad ho_j=F_j/F_{j-1},\qquad \mathscr R_{N,x,w}(z) =1+ rac{c_0-w}{A(Nx)} + rac{C(Nx)}{A(Nx)}(1-z^{-1}). 	ag{14} \] Both a lower and an upper bound on \(ho_j\) are needed. Bounds on determinant values alone would not suffice. Fix a bulk upper endpoint \(b_0<1/2\). All entries of \(\mathcal J_j\), for \(j\le b_0N\), are bounded uniformly in \(N\). This follows directly from (4): away from zero it is a compact sine-ratio bound; for small \(r/N\), cancel the common powers using the uniform comparison \(\sin y\asymp y\). The off-diagonal bound follows from the same bounds for \(A,C\). The source root-location theorem gives \(\mathcal J_j>2I\). Consequently its spectrum lies in one fixed interval \([2,L]\). The last resolvent entry is the Stieltjes transform of a probability measure on that interval: \[ m_j(w)=[(\mathcal J_j-wI)^{-1}]_{j-1,j-1} =\int_{[2,L]} rac{d\mu_j(s)}{s-w} = rac{F_{j-1}(w)}{A(j-1)F_j(w)}. 	ag{15} \] On every compact subset of \(\Omega\), these transforms are uniformly bounded above and away from zero. To prove the latter, for a fixed \(w\in\Omega\) the arguments of \(\{(s-w)^{-1}:2\le s\le L\}\) lie in an open sector of width less than \(\pi\). Rotate its bisector to the positive real axis. The real part then has a positive lower bound, uniform in \(s\), and remains so on a neighborhood of \(w\). A finite cover of the compact set proves the assertion for every probability measure \(\mu_j\). On a bulk interval \(A(j-1)\) is also bounded above and below. Equation (15) proves \[ 0<c\le|ho_j(w)|\le C<\infty 	ag{16} \] on every fixed slit compact. It also proves holomorphy there. Larger compact neighborhoods and Cauchy's formula give uniform fixed derivative bounds. The half-plane ratio theorem retained in the pinned interpolation source gives \(ho_j-\lambda(jh,w)=O(h)\) when \(\Re w<2\).
