It follows that \[ ho_j(w)-\lambda(jh,w)\longrightarrow0 	ag{17} \] uniformly on every bulk interval times every slit compact. Indeed otherwise take \(N_\ell	o\infty\) and \(j_\ell/N_\ell	o x\) witnessing failure. By (16), the holomorphic ratios have convergent subsequences on all slit compacts. On the half-plane each limit is \(\lambda(x,w)\); the identity theorem gives that limit on the connected slit. This contradicts the alleged failure. For real \(x\in(0,1/2)\), the quantity on the right of (8) cannot lie in \([-2,2]\) for \(w\in\Omega\). Thus the selected root has \(|\lambda|>1\) throughout the slit. On fixed bulk and slit compacts its modulus is at least \(1+\delta\). Small disks around that root and a small complex thickening in \(x\) give a uniform contraction factor \[ |\partial_z\mathscr R_{N,x,w}|\le\vartheta<1. 	ag{18} \] The limiting-root defect is \(O(h)\), uniformly and holomorphically. Use (17) at a fixed earlier bulk buffer and iterate \(e_{j+1}\le\vartheta e_j+Ch\). This proves the full-slit improvement \[ ho_j-\lambda(jh,w)=O(h). 	ag{19} \] All fixed exterior derivatives follow on smaller compacts. ## 3. The analytic value mode and its shifted residual The proof in the pinned degree-interpolation source now applies on the slit compacts just established. Its use of \(\Re\lambda>1\) was to obtain contraction and a unit logarithm; (18) and simple connectedness provide these here. For completeness specify the construction and the residuals which will be differentiated. Choose a fixed small \(\sigma>0\) within a left degree buffer and put \(m=\lfloor\sigma Nfloor\). Start at \(\lambda(x-mh,w)\), apply the \(m\) maps in (14) at \(x-mh,\ldots,x-h\), and call the result \(\mathcal R_N(x,w)\). Then on buffered complex neighborhoods \[ \mathcal R_N=\lambda+O(h),\qquad \mathcal R_N(jh,w)-ho_j(w)=O(e^{-\kappa_0N}), 	ag{20} \] and \[ \mathcal R_N(x+h,w) -\mathscr R_{N,x,w}(\mathcal R_N(x,w)) =O(e^{-\kappa_0N}). 	ag{21} \] For (21), compare the two starting values after aligning their last \(m\) maps; their difference is \(O(h)\), and the common maps contract it by \(\vartheta^m\). Equations (20)--(21) hold on larger fixed neighborhoods before Cauchy differentiation. Let \(\ell_N=\operatorname{Log}\mathcal R_N\), on the branch continued from real \(w<2\). Use the anchored Euler--Maclaurin primitive \[  egin{split} L_N(x,w)={}&h^{-1}\int_{x_*}^x\ell_N(s,w)\,ds +	frac12[\ell_N(x,w)-\ell_N(x_*,w)]\ &+\sum_{
u=1}^{p_N-1}  rac{B_{2
u}h^{2
u-1}}{(2
u)!} [\partial_x^{2
u-1}\ell_N(x,w) -\partial_x^{2
u-1}\ell_N(x_*,w)],\ A_N(x,w)={}&F_{j_*}(w)e^{L_N(x,w)},\qquad p_N=\lfloor cNfloor . \end{split} 	ag{22} \] Here \(c>0\) is small relative to the fixed analytic radius. The anchored integrals can run in either direction in the degree rectangle. The factorial Cauchy bounds and Bernoulli bounds in the pinned proof give exponential remainders, uniformly also on a smaller complex neighborhood. In particular \[  egin{split} L_N(x+h,w)-L_N(x,w) &=\ell_N(x+h,w)+O(e^{-\kappa_1N}),\ A_N(jh,w)/F_j(w)&=1+O(e^{-\kappa_1N}). \end{split} 	ag{23} \] The first identity can equivalently be checked by applying the Euler--Maclaurin remainder to the single complex segment \([x,x+h]\); its Cauchy estimates are uniform in \(x\). All fixed derivatives of these residuals are exponential after shrinking buffers. The correction terms in (22) beyond the half-endpoint term are \(O(h)\), and \(\ell_N=\operatorname{Log}\lambda+O(h)\). Thus \[ \log A_N(x,w)-\log A_N(y,w) =N[\Psi(x,w)-\Psi(y,w)]+O(1). 	ag{24} \] At the actual anchor, the all-row slit theorem supplies \(\log F_{j_*}=N\Psi(x_*,w)+o(N)\), with \(O(\log N)\) on half-plane compacts. This proves (13), its locally uniform lower bound as well as its upper bound, and its derivative versions. Also \(h\partial_x\log A_N=O(1)\) on fixed smaller neighborhoods. ## 4. Common-shift differentiation and the actual constant Let \[ ho_j^{(\varepsilon)} =F_j^{(\varepsilon)}/F_{j-1}^{(\varepsilon)},\qquad u_j=\left.\partial_\varepsilonho_j^{(\varepsilon)}ight|_0. 	ag{25} \] The exact determinant recurrence in (3) gives \[ ho_{j+1}^{(\varepsilon)} =\mathscr R_{N,jh+h\varepsilon,w} (ho_j^{(\varepsilon)}). 	ag{26} \] There is no derivative of \(c_0\) in this equation. Differentiating it gives every common-shift forcing term: \[ u_{j+1}= eta_j u_j+h f_j,\qquad  eta_j= rac{C(j)}{A(j)ho_j^2},\qquad f_j=\left.\partial_x\mathscr R_{N,x,w}(z) ight|_{x=jh,z=ho_j}. 	ag{27} \] Also, exactly, \[ D_j-D_{j-1}=u_j/ho_j. 	ag{28} \] The source determinant bound gives \(D_j=O(N^4)\) on slit compacts. By (16), \(u_j=ho_j(D_j-D_{j-1})\) is polynomially bounded at any starting bulk row. Differentiate (21) in \(x\) and multiply by \(h\). The result is the same affine equation as (27) for \(h\partial_x\mathcal R_N\), up to an exponential residual. Equations (20), (18) and bounded coefficient derivatives allow the two affine equations to be compared on a fixed earlier buffer. Any polynomial initial difference contracts exponentially. Therefore, throughout the inner bulk interval, \[ u_j-h\partial_x\mathcal R_N(jh,w) =O(e^{-\kappa_2N}). 	ag{29} \] This step retains the actual left-end derivative through its polynomial initial datum; it does not set that datum to zero. From (23), (28), and (29), \[  egin{split} &[D_{j+1}-h\partial_x\log A_N((j+1)h,w)]\ &\qquad-[D_j-h\partial_x\log A_N(jh,w)] =O(e^{-\kappa_2N}). \end{split} 	ag{30} \] Summing at most \(N\) steps, and reducing the rate, proves that this difference is its value at \(j_*\), up to an exponential error. Consequently \[  rac{c'(j)\widehat G_j(w)}{F_j(w)} -h\partial_x\log A_N(jh,w) =a_N(w)+O(e^{-\kappa_3N}). 	ag{31} \] The function \(a_N\) is exactly (11), not an unspecified constant of integration. It is holomorphic and polynomially bounded on every fixed buffered slit neighborhood, with all fixed derivatives: use \(D_{j_*}=O(N^4)\), the bound for \(\widetilde Q_N\) in the pinned source, and (22). ## 5. Dense physical symmetry determines the constant We use two elementary analytic observations. First, suppose holomorphic functions on a fixed rectangle are bounded by a fixed power of \(N\), and their values at the equally spaced nodes \(j/N\) of a fixed interior interval are \(O(e^{-\kappa N})\). On a smaller neighborhood of a shorter interior interval they and their fixed derivatives are \(O(e^{-\kappa' N})\), for some \(\kappa'>0\). Here is a proof that also handles approximate zeros. Subtract the finite cardinal sum of the nodal errors using \(\operatorname{sinc}(Nx-j)\). On a sufficiently thin fixed strip its size is at most \(CN^M e^{-\kappa N+\pi N|\Im x|}\), hence exponentially small. The remainder has exact zeros at all the nodes. Choose a fixed disk in the rectangle and a smaller concentric disk containing a positive fraction of those nodes. Factor the corresponding disk Blaschke factors. On a still smaller disk each factor has modulus at most a fixed number less than one, uniformly in the chosen nodes. The maximum principle then bounds the remainder by \(CN^M e^{-cN}\). A finite covering and Cauchy's formula prove the observation. Second, an exponentially small holomorphic family on one fixed open subset, polynomially bounded on a connected larger domain, is exponentially small on each compact subset of that domain. A finite chain of overlapping buffered disks and the three-circles inequality proves this: at each step the exponent is multiplied by a fixed positive number, while polynomial losses remain \(e^{o(N)}\). This assertion concerns compact paths; it has no uniform boundary or shrinking-buffer content. Choose a fixed physical second-row interval \(k/N\in[a_1,b_1]\) strictly inside \((0,1/2)\). Its spectral values lie in the real interval included in our slit neighborhood. For each such \(k\) compare, as functions of the complex degree \(x\), \[ A_N(x,c_k),\qquad F_k(C_N(x)). 	ag{32} \] At \(x=jh\), the exact source symmetry \(F_j(c_k)=F_k(c_j)\), together with (23), makes their difference exponentially small relative to \(F_j(c_k)\). Both functions in (32), divided by \(e^{N\Psi(x,c_k)}\), are polynomially bounded on a sufficiently thin fixed degree neighborhood, uniformly in \(k\). For the first this is (13) in a half-plane compact. For the second, apply the pinned half-plane row bound to \(F_k\) at \(C_N(x)\), which stays in a compact subset of \(\Re w<2\). The two phase functions differ by \(O(h)\) there: \[ \Psi(kh,C_N(x))-\Psi(x,c_k)=O(h). 	ag{33} \] To check (33), write \(\Psi\) as the original symmetric two-real-angle phase and then continue analytically to this thin neighborhood. The actual two angular arguments each differ from the corresponding unshifted one by \(	heta\). They stay in fixed bulk intervals, so their derivatives are bounded. Thus no endpoint estimate or omitted half-offset is being used. Apply the first analytic observation to the normalized difference in (32), on a degree disk around \(x_*\). It gives \[  rac{\partial_xA_N(x_*,c_k) -C_N'(x_*)F_k'(c_{j_*})} {F_{j_*}(c_k)} =O(e^{-\kappa_4N}). 	ag{34} \] Differentiating the normalizing exponential only introduces a polynomial factor, absorbed by a smaller rate. The exact source normal symmetry and the full-jet representative give \[ \widehat G_{j_*}(c_k) =G_{j_*}(c_k)=F_k'(c_{j_*}). 	ag{35} \] Using the exact anchor (9) in (11), equations (34)--(35) prove \[ a_N(c_k)=O(e^{-\kappa_5N}). 	ag{36} \] Apply the first observation again to \(a_N(C_N(y))\), on a fixed thin neighborhood of \([a_1,b_1]\). Its polynomial bound was proved after (31). Thus \(a_N\) is exponentially small on a fixed open spectral neighborhood. The second observation propagates this to every compact subset of the connected slit neighborhood, and hence to the originally prescribed \(\mathcal K\). Larger buffers followed by Cauchy's formula give all fixed spectral derivatives. This proves (12). Finally (31), (12), the value estimate (23), and \(C_N'(jh)=c'(j)/h\), with \(|c'(j)|\asymp h\) on the bulk, give the normal estimate (10). The factors from replacing \(A_N(jh,w)\) by \(F_j(w)\) are polynomial and are absorbed by reducing the positive exponential rate. Theorem 1 follows. ## 6. An exact scalar full-jet correction and its scope The approximate scalar can be corrected without prescribing a separate incompatible normal function. Put \(v_N=e^{-N\Psi}A_N\). At the physical degree nodes define \[  egin{split} d_j(w)&=e^{-N\Psi(jh,w)}F_j(w)-v_N(jh,w),\ b_j(w)&=e^{-N\Psi(jh,w)} [C_N'(jh)\widehat G_j(w)-N\Psi_x(jh,w)F_j(w)] -\partial_xv_N(jh,w). \end{split} 	ag{37} \] On general slit compacts, (10), (13) show these are \(O(e^{-\kappa N+o(N)})\); after reducing \(\kappa\) they are uniformly exponentially small. The same holds for fixed exterior derivatives. Define \[  egin{split} \mathfrak F_N(x,w)=e^{N\Psi(x,w)}  igg[v_N(x,w)+ \sum_{j:\,jh\in[a,b]} \{d_j(w)+b_j(w)(x-jh)\} \operatorname{sinc}^2(Nx-j) igg]. \end{split} 	ag{38} \] The cardinal functions in (38) have respectively value one and derivative zero, or value zero and derivative one, at their own node; both required jets vanish at every other node. Consequently \[ \mathfrak F_N(jh,w)=F_j(w),\qquad \partial_x\mathfrak F_N(jh,w) =C_N'(jh)\widehat G_j(w) 	ag{39} \] as identities of holomorphic functions of \(w\). All fixed \(w\)-derivatives of these identities are exact. Since \(|\operatorname{sinc}^2(Nx-j)|\le e^{2\pi N|\Im x|}\), the correction is exponentially small relative to the normalized action on a sufficiently thin fixed degree strip. Thus, for every \(\epsilon>0\), \[ |\mathfrak F_N(x,w)| \le C_\epsilon e^{N(\Re\Psi(x,w)+\epsilon)}. 	ag{40} \] On half-plane compacts one can replace the tolerance by a polynomial factor. Fixed derivatives obey the corresponding bound on buffered smaller domains. At a physical second endpoint, (39) contains the actual value, both independent first normals, and their mixed normal. At the odd simple second endpoint only its value is prescribed; the spectral formulas remain holomorphic through \(w=-2\). There is no degree-fold or degree-endpoint assertion. One may symmetrize (38) and its transposed construction on an overlapping thin two-degree bulk rectangle. The sampled full jets agree with the symmetric original kernel, so this preserves all four physical jets and the own-phase upper bound there. This observation does not extend the domain of either construction. The new part is the source-determined normal connection (11)--(12) throughout compact slit charts. The existing q-Hahn full-physical complex packet concerns a different ordinary column with an integer channel; it does not interpolate this channel or provide (12). The existing bare-kernel rectangle theorem already covers a larger central thin box with the actual whole kernel. No replacement for that theorem is claimed here. A compact positive second-color path lies in the slit, so (12) applies along its entirety. Continuing the first degree mode to a tall positive chart remains a separate problem. Its selected Riccati root may have modulus one there even while the two characteristic roots remain distinct. Neither the present real-degree contraction nor the thin correction (38) crosses that issue automatically. Finally (39) only covers the specified bulk subgrid. A full original trace must retain every other physical row, its endpoint packets and any contour seams. The replacement of \(G_j\) by (5) is valid before subsequent complete original traces, not by deleting the \(P_N\) term of (6) on an arbitrary open current. There is no whole-kernel positive-chart bound, global cycle transport, or filled-source estimate here. ## Direct sources Both complete texts and their used implications were read at the following versions: * [Exact analytic degree interpolation](research_physical_row_analytic_degree_interpolation.md), SHA256 f7d673e6633c0f46498a6c023512a3c64724d35c53ea168dabbd7f1e59f72d51: the exact physical Riccati recurrence and half-plane ratio input, exponential finite-iteration approximation, anchored growing-order Euler--Maclaurin primitive, and original phase. * [Complete physical residue packets](research_compact_positive_contour_residue_control.md), SHA256 cac1016d5f515510b95071a25c8d97345b334043492a6b430c4e924f87d82bb0: the actual common-shift determinant and endpoint-normal representative, full physical-jet identity, polynomial slit bounds, all-row action and symmetric real calibration. Only written mathematics, source-text reads and hashes were used. No mathematical program, numerical calculation, test or compilation was run. Frozen notes and public manuscripts are unchanged.

title: A common physical tensor Krein form for the original crossings
text: # A common physical tensor Krein form for the original crossings Written research proof, 22 November 2026. The original complete crossing preserves an explicit tensor product of one-head indefinite Hermitian forms. The same form works on overlapping adjacent pairs at arbitrary width. Its full change of coordinates to the prepared flags is proved entrywise, including every cyclic endpoint. The ordinary cup and cap are compatible with this form; the marked cap remains different. The form is indefinite. These identities give neither a positive whole-source norm nor a scalar noncancellation estimate. In particular, they do not identify the actual paired-face wire with a Hermitian pairing or remove any original pivot or marked boundary factor. ## 1. Original physical and flag conventions Use the complete balanced physical heads of [D,W,P,C], with \[ N\geq2,\quad d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2, \quad x=-q^{-1},\quad \lambda=x^{-1}=-q,\quad k=(-1)^d,\quad F_a=(Q;Q)_a . \tag{1} \] Physical indices lie in \(0,\ldots,d\); brackets mean cyclic reduction to this set. Thus \(F_d=N\), \(\lambda^2=Q\), and \(\lambda^N=k\). Every factorial denominator below has index at most \(d\). Write \(Z|r\rangle=Q^r|r\rangle\) and \(R_d|r\rangle=|d-r\rangle\). Define on one physical head \[ H_N=q^{-1}Z^{-1}R_d,\qquad H_N|r\rangle=qQ^r|d-r\rangle . \tag{2} \] Directly \(H_N^\dagger=H_N\) and \(H_N^2=I\). On two heads put \[ \mathcal K_N=-Nk(H_N\otimes H_N). \tag{3} \] It is Hermitian and \(\mathcal K_N^2=N^2I\). Let \(\widetilde{\mathcal B}\) be the source-fixed invertible flag frame of [D, (27)], with the wraps \(S_1^N=1,S_2^N=k\). Its coordinates are \(|m,s\rangle\). Put \(a=[-s]\). Expanding [D, (25),(27)] gives every physical coefficient: \[ \begin{split} \widetilde{\mathcal B}|m,s\rangle &=\sum_{h=0}^{a} A_{m,a,h}|[m+h],a-h\rangle,\\ A_{m,a,h} &=\frac{(-1)^h\lambda^{a-h} Q^{ma+h(h+1)/2}}{F_hF_{a-h}} . \end{split} \tag{4} \] Indeed the diagonal rescaling in [D] is \(\lambda^aQ^{ma}/F_a\), and \(\lambda^ax^h=\lambda^{a-h}\). This uses the complete physical space, of dimension \(N^2\). In these flag coordinates [D,W] give \[ \begin{gathered} v=Z_s,\qquad M=Z_m,\\ X|m,s\rangle=(1-Q^{-m})(1-Q^{1-s})|m-1,s-1\rangle, \qquad X^N=0 . \end{gathered} \tag{5} \] Here \(X\) is the physical nilpotent crossing argument of [W], not an additional boundary variable. Define the flag permutation and form \[ \mathcal R|m,s\rangle=|d-m,1-s\rangle,\qquad J=q\mathcal Rv^{-1}. \tag{6} \] All labels in (5),(6) are cyclic. Since \(\mathcal Rv\mathcal R=Qv^{-1}\), one has \(J^\dagger=J,J^2=I\), and \[ J_{ms;nt}=qQ^{-t}\delta_{m,d-n}\delta_{s,1-t}. \tag{7} \] ## 2. Full physical congruence The exact relation between the two forms is \[ \boxed{\quad \widetilde{\mathcal B}^{\dagger}\mathcal K_N \widetilde{\mathcal B}=J .\quad} \tag{8} \] We prove all matrix entries. For a left label \((m,s)\) and a right label \((n,t)\), put \(a=[-s],b=[-t]\), and \(R=a+b-d\). If \(R<0\), (4) and physical complementation in (3) give zero. Otherwise a possibly nonzero term must satisfy \[ h+g=R,\qquad m+n+R\equiv d\pmod N . \tag{9} \] Every \(g=0,\ldots,R\) is then valid, with \(h=R-g\): the bounds \(R\leq a,b\) follow from \(a,b\leq d\). If the second condition in (9) fails the whole entry is zero. For completeness, the only factorial identities needed are \[ \overline{F_u}=(-1)^uQ^{-u(u+1)/2}F_u,\qquad F_uF_{d-u}=N(-1)^uQ^{u(u+1)/2}. \tag{10} \] The second follows by reversing the last \(u\) factors of \(F_d\). In the entry under consideration, \((a-h)+(b-g)=d\), so (10) applies without a zero factorial. Also \[ \mathcal K_N|r,j\rangle =-NkQ^{r+j+1}|d-r,d-j\rangle . \tag{11} \] Insert (4) into (11), conjugating the left coefficient. Applying (10) to \(F_{a-h}F_{b-g}\) yields the following full entry: \[ -k\lambda^{d-2a}Q^{n+b+1-ma+nb+R} \sum_{g=0}^{R} \frac{(-1)^gQ^{g(g-1)/2}}{F_gF_{R-g}} . \tag{12} \] For example the power \(Q^{R-g}\) in this simplification comes from \(\lambda^{b-a+h-g}=\lambda^{d-2a}Q^{R-g}\); hence no wrap sign is being suppressed. The sum in (12) is \((1;Q)_R/F_R\), by the finite \(Q\)-binomial theorem. It vanishes for every \(R>0\). When \(R=0\), (9) implies literally \(b=d-a,n=d-m\). The exponent in front of the sum is \((n+1)(b+1)-ma\equiv0\pmod N\), and \[ -k\lambda^{d-2a}=q^{-1}Q^{-a}=qQ^b . \tag{13} \] This is exactly (7), since \(t=[-b]\) and \(s=[1-t]\). Thus (8) holds on every pair of basis vectors, including \(N=2\), even levels, and composite levels. Both forms in (8) are indefinite. When \(N\) is even their positive and negative indices are both \(N^2/2\). When \(N\) is odd, those indices are \((N^2-1)/2\) and \((N^2+1)/2\): directly (7) has trace \(-1\). In particular (8) is not a positive Gram identity. ## 3. The original crossing and marked full function Use the exact original stripped crossing factorization [W, (9)]: \[ \begin{gathered} W=\mathcal G\mathcal E_N(X),\qquad \mathcal E_N(X)=\sum_{h=0}^d X^h/F_h=P_N(X)^{-1},\\ P_N(X)=\sum_{h=0}^d(-1)^hQ^{h(h-1)/2}X^h/F_h,\qquad \mathcal G=\sum_{j=1}^N g_jE_j(v),\quad g_j=(-1)^{j-1}Q^{j(j-1)/2},\quad g_N=1 . \end{gathered} \tag{14} \] The full positive crossing is \(\kappa W\), and its negative is \(\kappa^{-1}W^{-1}\), with the original scalar retained. Equation (5) gives \(\mathcal RX\mathcal R=X^\dagger\), including the zero coefficients, and therefore \[ JXJ=QX^\dagger,\qquad \mathcal E_N(X)^\dagger=P_N(QX^\dagger) =JP_N(X)J . \tag{15} \] The middle identity follows from the first formula in (10). Reflection sends the marked label \(j\in\{1,\ldots,N\}\) to \(N+1-j\); the elementary equality \(g_{N+1-j}=g_j\) shows \([\mathcal G,J]=0\). Also \(\mathcal G^\dagger=\mathcal G^{-1}\). Equations (14),(15) consequently prove \[ W^\dagger=JW^{-1}J,\qquad W^\dagger JW=J \quad\text{in flag coordinates}. \tag{16} \] The marked physical-root full function of [P, (3),(12)] is \[ F_v=\phi_N\sum_{j=1}^N E_j(v)/F_{j-1},\qquad \phi_N=\sqrt N\exp\!\left\{i\pi\left[ \frac14-\frac{N+N^{-1}}{12}\right]\right\} . \tag{17} \] Here the \(j=N\) value is the specified top mark, not the zero at the bottom logarithmic mark. Formula (10) gives \(F_{j-1}F_{N-j}=Ng_j\), and \(|\phi_N|^2=N\). Thus the eigenvalues \(f_j=\phi_N/F_{j-1}\) satisfy \(\overline{f_j}f_{N+1-j}=1\). Hence, with no omitted scalar, \[ F_v^\dagger=JF_v^{-1}J,\qquad F_v^\dagger JF_v=J . \tag{18} \] ## 4. Cyclic root marks and physical tensor assembly For the determinant-normalized cyclic function of [D, (14)], denote its two orientations by \(\mathfrak d_Q,\mathfrak d_{Q^{-1}}\). Their anchored finite products imply \[ \mathfrak d_{Q^{-1}}(z)\mathfrak d_Q(Qz)=1 . \tag{19} \] Indeed each factor \(1-Q^rz\), including \(r=0\), has total exponent \(-d/N\) on the left, while the two central prefactors give \((1-z^N)^{d/N}\). Continue this identity with its marks. Put \(\mathcal C_t=\mathfrak d_Q(tv)\) on the nondegenerate marked cover. When \(t\) and \(\bar t\) use conjugate-compatible paths and roots from zero, (19) and the reflection of clock labels give \[ \mathcal C_t^\dagger=J\mathcal C_{\bar t}^{-1}J, \qquad \mathcal C_t^\dagger J\mathcal C_{\bar t}=J . \tag{20} \] For real \(t\) with a self-compatible mark this is a \(J\)-isometry. No unrelated choice of a norm root is licensed by (20); singular Fermat values are not evaluated by separating inverse factors. Conjugate the flat statements (16),(18),(20) by \(\widetilde{\mathcal B}\) and use (8). In original physical coordinates they read \[ \begin{gathered} W^\dagger(H_N\otimes H_N)W=H_N\otimes H_N,\\ F_v^\dagger(H_N\otimes H_N)F_v=H_N\otimes H_N,\\ \mathcal C_t^\dagger(H_N\otimes H_N)\mathcal C_{\bar t} =H_N\otimes H_N . \end{gathered} \tag{21} \] The scalar \(-Nk\) cancels. At completeness \(|\kappa|=1\), as fixed by the original crossing normalization [C, (15)]. Thus both full signed crossings satisfy the first identity in (21). For any width \(b\), set \(\mathscr H_b=H_N^{\otimes b}\). On every adjacent pair use its actual signed crossing \(R_i^{\pm1}\). Tensoring (21) with the untouched one-head forms proves \[ (R_i^{\pm1})^\dagger\mathscr H_bR_i^{\pm1} =\mathscr H_b,\qquad \mathcal W^\dagger\mathscr H_b\mathcal W=\mathscr H_b \tag{22} \] for every finite signed word \(\mathcal W\), including overlapping pairs. No common positive flag frame or transition-norm estimate is needed: \(H_N\) is the same physical one-head matrix on every wire. ## 5. Genuine ordinary turns and the retained marked closing The actual cup and ordinary cap [D,C] are \[ p=N\sum_{a=0}^d x^{a-d}|a,d-a\rangle,\qquad \ell_o|a,b\rangle=\frac{x^a}{N}\delta_{a+b,d} . \tag{23} \] The second formula uses \(x^{-a}Q^{-a}=x^a\). On degree \(a+b=d\), \(H_N\otimes H_N\) acts by the literal complementation \(|a,b\rangle\mapsto|d-a,d-b\rangle\), because the phase in (11) before its scalar is \(Q^{d+1}=1\). Conjugating the cup coefficients therefore proves, on the full space, \[ \boxed{\quad p^\dagger(H_N\otimes H_N)=N^2\ell_o, \qquad p^\dagger(H_N\otimes H_N)p=0 .\quad} \tag{24} \] Both rows vanish off degree \(d\); on that degree their coefficient is \(Nx^a\). The last equality is the original ordinary bubble \(\ell_op=0\). Equivalently \(p/N\) and \(N\ell_o\) are dagger compatible for this indefinite tensor form, with their actual order. The averaged marked row is instead \(\ell_m|a,b\rangle=x^b/N^2\), with \(\ell_mp=1\). Its exact flag row is \((\ell_m\widetilde{\mathcal B})_{ms}=Q^{-ms}/N^2\), while \(\widetilde{\mathcal B}^{-1}p=N^2|0,1\rangle\) [D, (29)]. It is not the ordinary row of (24). The original marked cap, pivots, peripheral and framing lines remain attached to every application; none is replaced by a Hermitian adjoint by definition. This establishes a common indefinite structure for the original crossings and ordinary turns at all levels. It does not make an arbitrary planar source a positive norm square, identify a paired-face seam, bound a general observed period below, or select a geometric integration cycle. The isotropic nonzero cup in (24) already prevents turning these identities into positive reflection by a change of basis. ## Complete proof sources and coverage - [D] [Retained Pachner ratio and physical flags](research_retained_pachner_ratio_physical_flags.md), 365 lines, SHA-256 `650d25db94060e306464ae00ef92ceb1e51ba4bec53da2c15ee67a89113be21a`. - [W] [Actual crossing flag Euler exchange](research_actual_crossing_flag_euler_exchange.md), 287 lines, SHA-256 `784a76132cf8116ec8afc5807e6bd98bb51178beb7f959b7ce3ab42e56eab6b5`. - [P] [Marked full-Phi flag pentagon](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_marked_full_phi_flag_pentagon.md), 328 lines, SHA-256 `3052cef4a1d666253562c13ceaf6a9bc472baf7691f23d13e33bb3f8d6e9888f`. - [C] [Actual Pascal coherent Gram](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_pascal_coherent_gram.md), 494 lines, SHA-256 `b6e6d697b4e21d30ca683f265b9c41170a0bee424d783169b2e0c70233dc889e`. [Reflection-compatible original cap metrics](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_reflection_marked_boundary_metric.md), 233 lines, SHA-256 `709bb3ae0ca888ded92de5d1e6dd6a570901330636b0c969063cd790c442f8f3`, and [the original reflection obstruction](original_reflection_gram_obstruction.md), 212 lines, SHA-256 `98263806bbbb5d69a9c595d0bba5e9a653063bc306c36f5b75bb482427e7ce85`, are coverage only. They distinguish reflected positive circle forms, genuine dual objects, and the failure of automatic positive source reflection. The new full physical congruence (8) and the common tensor identity (22) are consistent with those distinctions.

title: Uniform pressure and a nonzero amplitude for the original triple-row trace
text: # Uniform pressure and a nonzero amplitude for the original triple-row trace Private written proof, 17 November 2026. The positive original scalar \(\Gamma_{jk\ell}=\phi_N(F_jF_kF_\ell)\) has a uniform variational rate on its entire nonzero physical support. On compact subsets of strict macroscopic support, its exact normalization is \(N^{-3}\) times a positive analytic amplitude and its exponential action. The optimization is a strictly concave sum of nine ideal-tetrahedron actions. This controls the actual normal coefficients in the full \(F/G\) product basis. An inserted \(G\) row is a different derivative observable with a retained alternating tail; no estimate of that tail or of a subsequent signed closing is inferred by differentiating a continuous degree label. ## 1. Exact positive source and its symmetric sum Use \[ N\ge2,\quad D=N-1,\quad J_N=\lfloor D/2\rfloor,\quad \eta=(-1)^D,\quad s_r=2\sin(\pi r/N),\quad S_r=\prod_{a=1}^r s_a,\quad S_0=1, \] \[ c_j=2\cos((2j+1)\pi/N),\qquad e_r(Z)=S_r^{-2}\prod_{a<r}(c_a-Z), \] \[ P_N(Z)=2T_N(Z/2)+2,\quad \phi_N(f)=\eta N^2[Z^D]\operatorname{rem}_{P_N}f,\quad F_j(Z)=\sum_{a=0}^j f_{j,a}e_a(Z),\quad f_{j,a}=\frac{S_{j+a}}{S_{j-a}S_a^2}. \tag{1} \] All \(j,k,\ell\) below are physical indices in \(\{0,\ldots,J_N\}\). The full normal row at a double node is \(G_j(Z)=\partial_wK_N(c_j,Z)\), where \(K_N(w,Z)=\sum_{r=0}^D e_r(w)e_r(Z)\). At the odd simple node \(c_{J_N}=-2\) there is no normal row. The full-product source proves \[ \Gamma_{jk\ell}:=\phi_N(F_jF_kF_\ell)>0 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad j+k+\ell\ge D, \tag{2} \] and it is zero otherwise, with full canonical reduction and every repeated-root normal retained. Its positive sum can be made symmetric term by term. The original Newton multiplication and Frobenius pairing give \[ \phi_N(e_a e_b e_c) =\frac{S_{a+b}S_{a+c}S_{b+c}} {N S_aS_bS_cS_{a+b+c-D}} \quad(a+b+c\ge D,\quad a,b,c\le J_N), \tag{3} \] and zero below that threshold. Indeed it is the coefficient \(\mu_{ab,D-c}\) of the original product \(e_ae_b\). All pair sums are at most \(D\). Substitute its factorial formula and \(S_{D-r}=N/S_r\) to obtain (3). Thus, writing \(j_1=j,j_2=k,j_3=\ell\), \[ \boxed{\quad \Gamma_{\mathbf j} =\frac1N\! \sum_{\substack{0\le r_i\le j_i\\r_1+r_2+r_3\ge D}} \frac{\displaystyle \prod_i S_{j_i+r_i} \prod_{i<h}S_{r_i+r_h}} {\displaystyle \prod_i S_{j_i-r_i} \prod_i S_{r_i}^{\,3} S_{r_1+r_2+r_3-D}} . \quad} \tag{4} \] Every factorial index lies in \(0,\ldots,D\). No signed term has been replaced by its modulus. ## 2. The variational action on the whole physical support Set \[ \mathcal J(x)=\int_0^x\log(2\sin\pi u)\,du,\qquad0\le x\le1, \] \[ f(x,t)=\mathcal J(x+t)-\mathcal J(x-t)-2\mathcal J(t), \] \[ \mathfrak t(t_1,t_2,t_3)= \sum_{i<h}\mathcal J(t_i+t_h) -\sum_i\mathcal J(t_i) -\mathcal J(t_1+t_2+t_3-1). \tag{5} \] The continuous endpoint values are used. Define \[ \mathcal X=\{\mathbf x\in[0,1/2]^3:\ \sum_i x_i\ge1\}, \quad \mathcal P(\mathbf x)= \{\mathbf t:\ 0\le t_i\le x_i,\ \sum_i t_i\ge1\}, \] \[ \Phi(\mathbf x,\mathbf t) =\sum_i f(x_i,t_i)+\mathfrak t(\mathbf t),\qquad \mathcal G(\mathbf x) =\max_{\mathbf t\in\mathcal P(\mathbf x)} \Phi(\mathbf x,\mathbf t). \tag{6} \] All arguments of \(\mathcal J\) in (5) lie in \([0,1]\) on this compact feasible set. **Theorem 1.** Uniformly over every nonzero physical triple, at both level parities, \[ \boxed{\quad \log\Gamma_{\mathbf j} =N\mathcal G(j_1/D,j_2/D,j_3/D)+O(\log N). \quad} \tag{7} \] The constant is independent of the physical indices. The function \(\mathcal G\) is continuous and concave on \(\mathcal X\). Consequently every admissible sequence \(\mathbf j_N/D\to\mathbf x\in\mathcal X\) has limiting rate \(\mathcal G(\mathbf x)\). The exact zero region in (2) is excluded from (7). **Proof of the uniform estimate.** The uniform factorial bound is \[ \log S_r=N\mathcal J(r/N)+O(\log N) \quad(0\le r<N). \tag{8} \] Moreover \(\mathcal J\) has modulus of continuity \(O(\varepsilon(1+|\log\varepsilon|))\). For a summand of (4) put \(x_i=j_i/D\), \(t_i=r_i/D\). Replacing every factorial argument divided by \(N\) by its corresponding argument in (5) changes it by \(O(N^{-1})\). This includes \(r_1+r_2+r_3-D\). There is a fixed number of factors, so the logarithm of the summand is \[ N\Phi(\mathbf x,\mathbf t)+O(\log N) \tag{9} \] uniformly through all endpoints. There are at most \(N^3\) terms, giving the upper bound in (7). For the lower bound choose a maximizing \(\mathbf t\) and take \(r_i=\lceil Dt_i\rceil\). Since \(j_i\) are integers, \(r_i\le j_i\). Their sum is at least \(D\), so this is an actual supported term at both parities. Its distance from the maximizing state is \(O(N^{-1})\). The same modulus of continuity and (9) give the lower bound. Continuity of \(\mathcal G\) follows directly from continuity of \(\Phi\) and continuity of these feasible polytopes. For the latter point, if \(\mathbf x_n\to\mathbf x\) and \(\mathbf t\in\mathcal P(\mathbf x)\), first replace \(t_i\) by \(\min(t_i,x_{n,i})\). If their sum drops below one, restore the missing \(o(1)\) using the remaining box capacity; \(\sum_i x_{n,i}\ge1\) ensures enough capacity. This constructs feasible \(\mathbf t_n\to\mathbf t\). The reverse limiting assertion is compactness. Concavity is proved next. \(\square\) ## 3. Nine positive atoms and the unique strict optimizer For \(a+b+c=1\), let \[ V(a,b,c)=-\pi\{\mathcal J(a)+\mathcal J(b) +\mathcal J(c)\}. \tag{10} \] This is the usual ideal-tetrahedron action on the closed angle simplex. Its interior Hessian is negative definite; the elementary cotangent proof and its boundary derivatives are given in the variational source. Using \(\mathcal J(1-x)=-\mathcal J(x)\), one has exactly \[ \pi f(x,t) =V(x-t,t,1-x)+V(x,t,1-x-t). \tag{11} \] All angles are nonnegative on \(0\le t\le x\le1/2\). Also \(\mathfrak t(a,b,c)=m(a,b,1-c)\), where \(m\) is the original Newton product action. Its three-atom expression is \[ \begin{split} \pi\mathfrak t(a,b,c)={}&V(b,a,1-a-b)\\ &+V(1-c-a,1-c-b,a+b+2c-1)\\ &+V(2-a-b-2c,a+b+c-1,c). \end{split} \tag{12} \] These are exactly the three atoms of the original gate, with its output set to \(1-c\). They are nonnegative angles on the gate domain, which includes (6). Thus \(\Phi\) is a jointly concave nine-atom action. Maximization over the convex shared-label domain proves the concavity asserted in Theorem 1. Write \[ \mathcal X^\circ =\{\mathbf x:\ 0<x_i<1/2,\ \sum_i x_i>1\}. \tag{13} \] For every \(\mathbf x\) in (13), the maximum has \[ 0<t_i^*(\mathbf x)<x_i,\qquad \sum_i t_i^*(\mathbf x)>1. \tag{14} \] To prove this, choose a strict feasible state, which exists because \(\sum_i x_i>1\), and join any boundary state to it. A coordinate \(t_i=0\) is impossible on this polytope: the other two are bounded by numbers whose sum is less than one. If \(t_i=x_i\), the first atom of (11) is \(V(0,x_i,1-x_i)\), a nonvertex-flat atom. Its inward directional derivative is \(+\infty\). If \(\sum_i t_i=1\), the last atom of (12) is \(V(1-c,0,c)\), also nonvertex-flat. Every other atom has either finite or positive infinite inward derivative, never negative infinite derivative. This argument includes simultaneous intersections of these faces. No boundary point can maximize. Strictness and nondegeneracy can also be checked directly. For \(0<t<x<1/2\), \[ f_{xx}=\pi\{\cot\pi(x+t)-\cot\pi(x-t)\}<0, \] \[ \det\operatorname{Hess}_{(x,t)}f =\frac{4\pi^2\sin^2\pi x} {\sin\pi(x-t)\sin\pi(x+t)}>0 . \tag{15} \] Thus every row action has a negative definite joint Hessian. The gate Hessian is nonpositive, and is itself negative definite in the strict gate domain. Hence \(\Phi\) has negative definite Hessian in all six variables at (14). There is a unique maximizing state, analytic in \(\mathbf x\), and \[ \mathcal H(\mathbf x) =-\Phi_{\mathbf t\mathbf t}(\mathbf x,\mathbf t^*)>0. \tag{16} \] The profile is real analytic and strictly concave on (13), by the negative Schur complement of the full Hessian. In particular its actual derivative in the continuous degree parameter is \[ \partial_{x_i}\mathcal G(\mathbf x) =\log\frac{\sin\pi(x_i+t_i^*)} {\sin\pi(x_i-t_i^*)}. \tag{17} \] This is not identified with an original spectral first normal. ## 4. Uniform nonzero amplitude on strict macroscopic support For the amplitude use the exact parameters \(\mathbf x_N=(j_1/N,j_2/N,j_3/N)\). This differs from the convention in the uniform rate (7): the \(D=N-1\) shift must now be retained in the amplitude. For a strict state set \(d=t_1+t_2+t_3-1>0\) and \[ \mathcal R(\mathbf x,\mathbf t)= \frac{\displaystyle \prod_i\sin\pi(x_i+t_i) \prod_{i<h}\sin\pi(t_i+t_h)} {\displaystyle \prod_i\sin\pi(x_i-t_i) \prod_i\sin^3\pi t_i\ \sin\pi d}. \tag{18} \] All displayed factors are strictly positive. **Theorem 2.** For any compact \(K\subset\mathcal X^\circ\), uniformly over physical triples with \(\mathbf x_N\in K\), \[ \boxed{\quad \Gamma_{\mathbf j} =N^{-3}\mathcal A(\mathbf x_N) e^{N\mathcal G(\mathbf x_N)} \bigl(1+O_K(N^{-1})\bigr), \quad} \tag{19} \] where the positive real analytic amplitude is \[ \mathcal A(\mathbf x)= \frac{\pi^{3/2}}{8\sin(\pi d^*)}\, \frac{\sqrt{\mathcal R(\mathbf x,\mathbf t^*)}} {\sqrt{\det\mathcal H(\mathbf x)}}, \qquad d^*=\sum_i t_i^*-1. \tag{20} \] In particular it is bounded above and below by positive constants on \(K\). **Proof.** Strictness, uniqueness, and compactness provide uniform buffered neighborhoods of all the selected saddles. On them the bulk sine-factorial expansion is \[ S_{N\alpha+c} =\sqrt{2N\sin\pi\alpha}\ e^{N\mathcal J(\alpha)} (2\sin\pi\alpha)^c\bigl(1+O(N^{-1})\bigr), \tag{21} \] with uniform analytic derivatives on smaller bulk domains. This formula is used for integral factorial arguments; the canonical interpolation in the cited Laplace source also supplies the corresponding holomorphic summand. In (4) there are six numerator factorials and thirteen denominator factorials, counting multiplicities. There is also the displayed \(N^{-1}\). Only the final denominator has a nonzero offset: \[ r_1+r_2+r_3-D=Nd+1. \tag{22} \] Consequently each summand near the saddle equals \[ N^{-9/2}\mathfrak b(\mathbf x,\mathbf t) e^{N\Phi(\mathbf x,\mathbf t)} \bigl(1+O_K(N^{-1})\bigr),\qquad \mathfrak b= \frac{2^{-9/2}\sqrt{\mathcal R(\mathbf x,\mathbf t)}} {\sin\pi d}. \tag{23} \] The factor \(1/(2\sin\pi d)\) from (22) is essential. The whole complement of a sufficiently small saddle neighborhood has a uniform strict action gap. To apply this to the exact finite sum, its possible strip \(\sum_i r_i/N\in[1-N^{-1},1)\) can be moved into the limiting polytope by increasing coordinates by a total at most \(N^{-1}\), without leaving their upper box. The strict parameter margin supplies that capacity. The uniform factorial estimate and modulus of continuity then change the rate by only \(O(\log N)\). Thus all these terms, and every other nonsaddle term, are exponentially smaller than (19). The remaining lattice has three independent integer coordinates, with no congruence or parity restriction. The finite-window lattice Laplace lemma applies to (23), or equivalently follows by its midpoint cotangent contour proof with all endpoint and nonconstant-mode terms exponentially smaller. Its Gaussian factor is \[ N^{3/2}\frac{(2\pi)^{3/2}} {\sqrt{\det\mathcal H}}. \tag{24} \] Combining (23) and (24) yields \(N^{-3}\) and exactly (20). The relative error is \(O_K(N^{-1})\), uniformly over a finite cover of the compact parameter set. Both parities use the same primitive lattice and the same offset (22). \(\square\) ## 5. Actual normal coefficients and the remaining signed observable The result applies directly to the normal sector of the original full product. For a double node \(c_\ell\), the exact coefficient of \(G_\ell\) in \(F_jF_k\) is \[ B_{jk;\ell} =\eta(4-c_\ell^2)\Gamma_{jk\ell}. \tag{25} \] Therefore (7) controls its entire nonzero macroscopic rate, with only polynomial endpoint factors. On every strict compact of Theorem 2, its full asymptotic is \[ B_{jk;\ell} =\eta(4-c_\ell^2)N^{-3}\mathcal A(\mathbf x_N) e^{N\mathcal G(\mathbf x_N)} (1+O_K(N^{-1})). \tag{26} \] Here the factor \(4-c_\ell^2\) is left exact. At the odd simple node there is no normal coefficient; its value coefficient is the same exact triple trace. Theorem 1 covers that row, while the bulk amplitude theorem does not assert a uniform fold or support-boundary expansion. The inserted first normal \(\phi_N(G_jF_kF_\ell)\), with \(c_j\) double, is a separate observable. For precision, if \[ T(F_kF_\ell)=\sum_{m=0}^D h_m e_m,\qquad h_m\ge0, \tag{27} \] with the explicit factorial coefficients of the full-product source, then the original identity is \[ \phi_N(G_jF_kF_\ell) =\sum_{m=0}^D h_m e_m'(c_j). \tag{28} \] For \(m\le j\), logarithmic differentiation gives \[ e_m'(c_j)=-f_{j,m}\sum_{a=0}^{m-1}(c_a-c_j)^{-1}, \] with the empty sum zero. For \(j<m\le D-j\) they instead equal \[ e_m'(c_j)=(-1)^{m-j} \frac{S_{j+m}S_{m-j-1}}{s_{2j+1}S_m^2}. \tag{29} \] For \(m>D-j\) they vanish. The alternating tail (29) is retained; it is not present in the positive sum (4). No bound for it follows from Theorem 2 by differentiating (17). The same caution applies to mixed original first normals. Thus the new estimate gives the actual size and nonzero amplitude of the signed normal coefficient (25), not a positivity replacement for the complete \(F/G\) packet. Its subsequent \(V_n\) action retains the original phase and the value-channel shear \((A_\ell,B_\ell)\mapsto \lambda_{n,\ell}(A_\ell-n\alpha_\ell B_\ell,B_\ell)\). Here \(\lambda_{n,\ell}=(-1)^{n\ell}e^{-i\pi n\ell(\ell+1)/N}\) and \(\alpha_\ell=i(D-2\ell)/(4\sin((2\ell+1)\pi/N))\) are the original coefficients from the full-product source. The prescribed crossed closing still includes both channels and their coherent quadratic phases. No lower bound for that sum is asserted. The nine-atom expression provides a concrete positive variational problem with original integer labels. Identifying its external derivatives or internal stationary equations with a supplied parent triangulation requires its actual charge and gluing equations; no geometric volume equality is inferred from the atom decomposition alone. ## Complete direct sources All three complete texts were read and their used implications checked at the following pins: * [Full physical-row product support](research_physical_row_full_product_normal_support.md), SHA256 708d22248526c75b0d8b26cc9a07c63d8471b07d200b9e9947059ca8145b2efd: exact positive triple trace, all-index normal coefficients, and the retained original derivative tail. * [Primitive action and variation](../papers/newton-calculus/variation.tex), SHA256 0e92ea26937bff27b0b813d6289ae917113c2d567e843ec07f883b23d1124296: uniform factorial rate, the original three-atom gate, strict concavity, and boundary derivative facts. * [Uniform finite-window lattice Laplace proof](../papers/conway-asymptotics/README.md), SHA256 9bcd5f82e8de2be34e6a6428d9a6fb07049f06884f8febe111a4628719253cba: bulk factorial normalization with integer offsets and the uniform finite-lattice Gaussian amplitude. Only written mathematics, source-text reads, and metadata hashes were used. No programs, numerical evaluations, tests, builds, or compilations were run. Frozen notes and public manuscripts are unchanged.

title: Sector charges and the complete open planar array
text: # Sector charges and the complete open planar array Private written proof, 17 November 2026. We prove the charge-change formula for the full two-ended planar source, including both end colors. The input is Kashaev's explicit planar weight [K, (2.7),(2.8),(3.6)]. Neither its claimed invariance nor its asserted freedom in the sector charges is a proof premise. ## 1. Corners, end colors, and the source Let \(G\) be a connected finite plane graph with four half-edges at each crossing and two vertices of degree one. Both degree-one vertices meet the unbounded face. Loops, multiple edges and repeated occurrences of a region at a crossing are allowed. Each crossing specifies its overpassing pair of opposite half-edges. A *corner* is an occurrence of the sector between consecutive half-edges at a crossing. Thus four corners are retained even if the same face occupies two sectors. Fix \(N\ge2\) and a primitive \(N\)-th root \(q\). Every color and charge below belongs to \(\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z\). In counterclockwise order at a crossing, label the edge colors \(i,j,k,l\), with \(j,l\) on the overpassing strand, and let \(a,b,c,d\) label the following corners: \[ (i,j),\quad(j,k),\quad(k,l),\quad(l,i). \] Use the specified finite weight \[ R(i,j,k,l\mid a,b,c,d) =q^{a-k-j}W(j-i-a,\ i-l-d,\ l-k-c,\ k-j-b), \tag{1} \] where \(W\) is exactly [K, (2.7)], including its finite products, integer-residue representatives and two theta factors. It is enough here that its four arguments in (1) are retained exactly. A sector assignment is *admissible* if the four charges at every crossing sum to one, the charges on every bounded face sum to one, and every corner of the unbounded face has charge zero. Face sums count corner occurrences. For two fixed end-edge colors \(u,v\), put \[ F_a(u,v)=\sum_{\substack{\text{internal}\\\text{edge colors}}} \prod_{\text{crossings }t}R_t \prod_{\text{all edges }e}q^{j_e}. \tag{2} \] The two end edges also occur in the last product. This is the original fixed-end source when \(u=v=0\). When four distinct regions occur at every crossing, its charge conventions agree literally with [K, (3.1)--(3.6)]. With repeated regions, (1),(2) specify the occurrence-level convention explicitly, rather than identifying different corner charges by the name of their face. ## 2. A planar potential lemma Suppose corner values \(\delta_c\) sum to zero at each crossing and around each bounded face, and vanish at every unbounded-face corner. There are edge values \(x_e\) such that at each corner from a half-edge \(e\) to its next counterclockwise half-edge \(e'\), \[ \delta_c=x_{e'}-x_e. \tag{3} \] They can be chosen zero on both end edges. To prove this integrally, replace each crossing by a small circle. Its four incident half-edges meet that circle at four separate vertices; connect consecutive vertices by the four circle arcs. Keep the original graph edges between these circles and the two degree-one vertices. Give an original edge increment zero and an oriented circle arc increment \(\delta_c\), with sign reversed on the oppositely oriented arc. This is a connected plane graph. Its bounded faces are the small crossing disks and the original bounded regions, with the same corner occurrences. The assumed sums say that the increment around every bounded-face boundary is zero. The oriented boundaries of the bounded faces generate the integral cycle group of a connected plane graph. One direct proof takes any simple cycle and sums the faces inside it: interior edge occurrences cancel and its boundary remains. Split any closed edge walk at its repeated vertices into simple cycles, canceling immediate backtracks. Bridges contribute nothing. This proves the assertion for loops and repeated face boundaries as well. It uses only integer sums, so it remains valid after reduction modulo any \(N\). The increment therefore integrates along paths to a vertex potential, independent of the chosen path. Its value is the same at both ends of each original edge, giving \(x_e\), and its circle steps give (3). The outer boundary walk visits both degree-one vertices. Every increment along that walk is zero: original edges have zero increment and outer corners have \(\delta_c=0\). The two end values are equal. Subtract their common value to make both zero. Connectivity also shows that this normalized potential is unique. ## 3. Exact charge change, with its phase Let \(a\) and \(a'\) be admissible assignments. Their corner difference \(\delta=a'-a\) satisfies the potential lemma. Choose its normalized edge values \(x_e\), and replace every edge color by \(j'_e=j_e+x_e\). The end colors are unchanged. At one crossing, equation (3) says \[ a'-a=x_j-x_i,\quad b'-b=x_k-x_j,\quad c'-c=x_l-x_k,\quad d'-d=x_i-x_l . \] All four arguments of \(W\) in (1) are unchanged, as elements of \(\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z\). Consequently their integer residues and theta supports are unchanged as well. The explicit prefactor gives \[ R(i+x_i,j+x_j,k+x_k,l+x_l\mid a',b',c',d') =q^{-x_i-x_k}R(i,j,k,l\mid a,b,c,d). \tag{4} \] In particular this comparison loses no zero entry or endpoint residue. The color change is a bijection of the finite internal summation set. Each edge factor in (2) supplies \(q^{x_e}\). Multiplying (4) proves the identity of the entire open arrays \[ \boxed{F_{a'}(u,v)=q^{\Omega(x)}F_a(u,v),\qquad \Omega(x)=\sum_e x_e- \sum_{\text{crossings }t} (x_{\text{first under-half-edge}}+ x_{\text{second under-half-edge}}).} \tag{5} \] The second sum counts half-edge occurrences; a loop can contribute twice. This is an explicit unit independent of \(u,v\) and of the summation colors. No primality, oddness or division modulo \(N\) is required. Thus an admissible sector assignment may be changed with both end colors fixed, while retaining the single root phase in (5). The conclusion concerns the whole open array, so it also retains a specified closing functional once that functional is applied to the same end coordinates. It does not identify a different cap functional, prove scalarity of the open array, establish a geometric contribution, or supply a large-level lower bound. ## Complete direct source - [K] R. M. Kashaev, *A Link Invariant from Quantum Dilogarithm*, [q-alg/9504020v1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/q-alg/9504020). Only the finite planar definitions are used. The complete ten-page primary text was read. Local PDF: research_archive/finite-source-identification-2026-11-01/md-kashaev-normalization-critical-audit/kashaev1995.pdf, SHA256 0baef40fa9934c9119af2c67252f8032e288c884da72eeaecf405bf91569cda9. The complete text extraction has SHA256 24932c5d5eab93684888a6149518d710ed7ad48fe3674522c8adaa38a0b62cb1. No mathematical programs or numerical experiments were used.

title: Finite charge polarizations retaining the original Hermite trace
text: # Finite charge polarizations retaining the original Hermite trace Private written proof, 16 November 2026. The canonical positive physical angles define a square root of the full-Hermite squared-angle class. Its two algebra exponentials split the original cosine coupon exactly. Each polarized family has the same signed heat evolution and recovers the original source at unit charge. Its charge reflection exchanges the two families instead of forcing either family to have zero first derivative there. This is a finite-source construction. A polarized initializer is not inferred from the already proved cosine initializer. The earlier one-sided angular representative changes representatives modulo the angular Hermite ideal; the polarization here instead changes the charge coupon in the original spectral algebra. These are different operations. ## 1. The positive-angle class and its exponentials Use the original data of the entire charged-source heat theorem: \[ D=N-1,\qquad \eta=(-1)^D,\qquad N\ge2,\qquad \mathcal A_N=\mathbb C[z]/(P_N(z)),\qquad P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2, \] \[ \phi_N(f)=\eta N^2[z^D]\operatorname{rem}_{P_N}f. \tag{1} \] The distinct double nodes have positive angular lifts \[ c_a=-2\cos\tau_a, \qquad \tau_a=\frac{\pi(D-2a)}N>0, \qquad 0\le a<\lfloor N/2\rfloor. \tag{2} \] At odd levels the remaining node \(-2\) is simple. Define the unique class \(L_N\in\mathcal A_N\) by \[ L_N(c_a)=\tau_a,\qquad L_N'(c_a)=\frac1{2\sin\tau_a},\qquad L_N(-2)=0\quad(N\text{ odd}). \tag{3} \] This is a choice of full finite jets, not an assertion that a single inverse cosine is holomorphic across \(-2\). If \(\mathscr T_N\) is the squared-angle class in the heat theorem, then \[ L_N^2=\mathscr T_N. \tag{4} \] Indeed its double-node values are \(\tau_a^2\), its derivatives are \(\tau_a/\sin\tau_a\), and its odd simple value is zero. These are all the defining data of \(\mathscr T_N\). For \(\sigma\in\{+1,-1\}\), put \[ Q_{N,\sigma}(\chi) =\exp_{\mathcal A_N}\bigl(\sigma iN(1-\chi)L_N\bigr). \tag{5} \] Its complete data are \[ \begin{split} Q_{N,\sigma}(\chi)(c_a) &=e^{\sigma iN(1-\chi)\tau_a},\\ Q_{N,\sigma}(\chi)'(c_a) &=\frac{\sigma iN(1-\chi)}{2\sin\tau_a} e^{\sigma iN(1-\chi)\tau_a}, \end{split} \qquad Q_{N,\sigma}(\chi)(-2)=1\quad(N\text{ odd}). \tag{6} \] Thus all coefficients are entire in \(\chi\), and each coupon is an algebra unit at every finite charge. The original entire cosine coupon \(\mathcal C_{N,\chi}\) satisfies the exact identities \[ \frac{Q_{N,+}(\chi)+Q_{N,-}(\chi)}2=\mathcal C_{N,\chi}, \qquad Q_{N,\sigma}(1)=1, \qquad Q_{N,\sigma}(2-\chi)=Q_{N,-\sigma}(\chi). \tag{7} \] The last reflection is a reflection of the charge. Each polynomial \(Q_{N,\sigma}(-2\cos t)\) is individually even in \(t\); angular reflection does not exchange the two fixed spectral classes. Differentiation in charge gives, in the full algebra, \[ \partial_\chi Q_{N,\sigma} =-\sigma iN L_N Q_{N,\sigma},\qquad \partial_\chi^2 Q_{N,\sigma} =-N^2\mathscr T_NQ_{N,\sigma}. \tag{8} \] In particular (8) keeps the first normals, rather than just the semisimple values. At \(\chi=0\) the values in (6) are \(\eta\), but the double-node normals are generally nonzero. The polarized zero-charge coupon is therefore not silently identified with \(\eta\,1\). ## 2. Faithful one-sided charge observations and heat transport Write \(y=1-\chi\), \(\lambda_a=N\tau_a=\pi(D-2a)\), and let \[ \mathcal E_{N,\sigma} =\operatorname{span}\{e^{\sigma i\lambda_a y}, y e^{\sigma i\lambda_a y}\}_a +\operatorname{span}\{1\}\quad(N\text{ odd}), \tag{9} \] where the last summand is absent at even levels. Then \[ f\longmapsto\phi_N(fQ_{N,\sigma}(\chi)) \quad\hbox{is an isomorphism}\quad \mathcal A_N\longrightarrow\mathcal E_{N,\sigma}. \tag{10} \] To see this directly, the original trace formula gives \[ \phi_N(fQ_{N,\sigma}) =\sum_a\{A_a(f)+\sigma i B_a(f)y\} e^{\sigma i\lambda_a y} +\mathbf1_{N\text{ odd}}f(-2), \tag{11} \] \[ A_a(f)=\eta\{4\sin^2\tau_a f'(c_a)-c_af(c_a)\}, \qquad B_a(f)=2\eta N\sin\tau_a f(c_a). \tag{12} \] The distinct nonzero frequencies and their first polynomial factors are linearly independent, as is the optional constant. The coefficient of \(y\) first recovers \(f(c_a)\), and the constant at that frequency then recovers \(f'(c_a)\). Thus the dimension is exactly \(N\). Let \(F_N\) be any original compiled numerator, with all kernels, spectators and ordinary free boundaries retained. Distinct crossing positions remain in their distinct contracted algebra copies. Define \[ Z_{N,\boldsymbol\sigma}(\mathbf n,\boldsymbol\chi) =\phi_N^{\otimes m}\!\left[ F_N\prod_v R_{n_v}Q_{N,\sigma_v}(\chi_v)\right], \qquad \widetilde Z_{N,\boldsymbol\sigma} =\left(\prod_v C_{N,n_v}^{-1}\right)Z_{N,\boldsymbol\sigma}, \tag{13} \] \[ C_{N,n}=e^{\pi i nD^2/(4N)},\qquad R_n=C_{N,n}\exp_{\mathcal A_N} \left(\frac{inN\mathscr T_N}{4\pi}\right). \tag{14} \] For arbitrary fixed signed real powers, and also as entire identities in the powers, \[ \partial_{n_v}\widetilde Z_{N,\boldsymbol\sigma} =-\frac{i}{4\pi N}\partial_{\chi_v}^2 \widetilde Z_{N,\boldsymbol\sigma}. \tag{15} \] This follows from (8) and (14) inside the original trace. The constant-coefficient equations preserve (9), so their solution is unique in the tensor product of those finite spaces. For a nonzero real step \(\delta\), set \(v_\delta=e^{-i\operatorname{sgn}(\delta)\pi/4}\). The exact solution in that coordinate is \[ \widetilde Z_{N,\boldsymbol\sigma} (\mathbf n+\delta\mathbf e_v,\boldsymbol\chi) =\sqrt{\frac N{|\delta|}} \int_{\mathbb R}e^{-\pi Nr^2/|\delta|} \widetilde Z_{N,\boldsymbol\sigma} (\mathbf n,\boldsymbol\chi+v_\delta r\mathbf e_v)\,dr. \tag{16} \] The Gaussian computation on \(e^{\lambda\chi}\) and its \(\lambda\)-derivative proves (16), including every normal block. The corresponding oriented charge line may be translated by any finite complex amount, exactly as in the original heat theorem. The Gaussian beats the linear exponential type of (9), so all these integrals converge absolutely. Tensorization and ordinary free-boundary derivatives commute with the identities. For the fixed same-index graph sources covered by the local heat theorem, the same physical-data argument gives \[ |\widetilde Z_{N,\boldsymbol\sigma}(\mathbf n,\boldsymbol\chi)| \le A N^p\prod_v(1+|\chi_v|) \exp N\left(C+\pi\sum_v|\Im\chi_v|\right). \tag{17} \] Here powers range over a bounded real box and free boundaries over a fixed compact set. Indeed the values in (6) have modulus at most \(e^{\pi D|\Im\chi|}\); their normals add only a polynomial factor, since the smallest nonzero physical sine is bounded below by a constant times \(N^{-1}\). The original kernel and mixed-normal envelopes are otherwise unchanged. No filled-action estimate is substituted for the constant \(C\). Consequently the proved local heat estimate applies to (13) whenever an actual uniform holomorphic nonzero initializer for this polarized source is supplied. Equations (15)--(17) alone do not supply it. ## 3. Exact endpoint recovery and the Fourier projection The symmetrization and endpoint recovery are literal source identities: \[ Z_N(\mathbf n,\boldsymbol\chi) =2^{-m}\sum_{\boldsymbol\sigma\in\{+,-\}^m} Z_{N,\boldsymbol\sigma}(\mathbf n,\boldsymbol\chi), \qquad Z_{N,\boldsymbol\sigma}(\mathbf n,\mathbf1) =Z_N(\mathbf n,\mathbf1). \tag{18} \] Reflecting one charge exchanges the corresponding signs. If a polarized source has a uniquely specified holomorphic asymptotic branch \(e^{NS_+(\chi)}a_+(\chi)\), its reflected branch is marked by \(S_-(\chi)=S_+(2-\chi)\), \(a_-(\chi)=a_+(2-\chi)\). At unit charge their actions and coefficients agree with those marks. The factor \(1/2\) in their average then preserves the coefficient; it does not create cancellation. Integer \(2\pi i\) action shifts give the same exponential at integer levels but must not be inserted without their marks. This assertion presupposes the actual branch expansion; it is not its existence proof. Unlike the cosine family, an individual family (13) is not forced by charge reflection to have zero first derivative at unit charge. From (8) that derivative is exactly the original trace with insertion \(-\sigma iN L_N\). Thus the elementary single-branch symmetry obstruction is removed, while the prescribed endpoint scalar remains the same. There is an exact way to obtain (13) from the whole cosine charge function. In one variable let \(\Pi_+\), \(\Pi_-\), \(\Pi_0\) retain respectively its generalized Fourier frequencies \(+\lambda_a\), \(-\lambda_a\), and zero as a function of \(y=1-\chi\). Then \[ \phi_N(fQ_{N,\sigma}) =(2\Pi_\sigma+\Pi_0)\phi_N(f\mathcal C_{N,\chi}). \tag{19} \] This follows by expanding the sine and cosine, including their linear-in-\(y\) normal factors. At odd levels the constant must be retained once, not doubled. The analogous operators in distinct charges commute. Projection (19) is a projection of the whole charge function. It can be encoded on its finite space by a differential polynomial whose order grows with \(N\), or by a one-sided Fourier projection. It is not a fixed-order differentiation of a local asymptotic expansion. The existing cosine initializer therefore does not automatically give a polarized initializer. ## 4. The correct angular realization For one traced variable let \(A(t)\) be an even holomorphic spectator on neighborhoods of all physical angular nodes. Keep the canonical crossing representative and set \[ W_N(t)=\frac{e^{-iNt}}{(1-\eta e^{-iNt})^2},\qquad h_n(t)=\sin t\,A(t)e^{inNt^2/(4\pi)}. \tag{20} \] Let \(\gamma_+\) be the union of small positively oriented circles around precisely the positive physical angles \(\tau_a\). Then \[ \phi_N(R_n[A]Q_{N,\sigma}) =-\frac{N^2 C_{N,n}}{\pi i} \int_{\gamma_+}h_n(t)e^{\sigma iN(1-\chi)t}W_N(t)\,dt +\mathbf1_{N\text{ odd}}C_{N,n}A(0). \tag{21} \] Near a physical angle, \(W_N(t)\) has double principal part \(-\eta/[N^2(t-\tau_a)^2]\) and no simple-pole term. Its residue in (21) therefore gives twice \(\eta\) times the derivative of \(h_n(t)e^{\sigma iN(1-\chi)t}\), exactly the double-node value and normal in the original trace. The remaining odd simple term is exactly the last term displayed. Equivalently it is obtained by adding one half of a small full angular circle around zero. Its residue uses only the constant term of the exponential; no spurious spectral derivative is prescribed there. When the spectator is holomorphic on a symmetric lens neighborhood, a literal exponential on the full symmetric closed lens is different. With the original angular double-cover factor \(1/2\), its reflected positive and negative preimages average the two exponential jets. It consequently gives \(\phi_N(R_n[A]\mathcal C_{N,\chi})\), not (21). A literal exponential on only a lower open arc defines yet another entire period. Its average with the opposite exponential is the original lower-lens cosine period, and each agrees with that period at \(\chi=1\), but it retains separate open-arc connector data. Neither identification erases those connectors. Formula (21) gives the concrete remaining initializer problem: the positive-half-grid cycle, its central connector and its outer connectors must be estimated with the entire original spectator and all normals. A nonzero initializer on a fixed complex charge domain would then activate (16) and the already proved quantitative local heat theorem, with its actual domain and tail conditions. No such new half-grid estimate, arbitrary-filling propagation, or geometric cycle coefficient is asserted here. ## Direct sources and versions All directly used source implications were read in full, with earlier complete readbacks retained only at unchanged hashes. The complete final proof above was reread before freezing. - [Entire charged-source heat reduction](research_entire_charged_source_heat_reduction.md), `33213425be9cac699860a48b23830399c82cd89bea3140cc776274aafe115fba`: original trace, squared-angle class, crossings, finite charge space, exact Gaussian heat transform and compiled-source placement. - [Local charged-source heat propagation](research_charged_source_local_heat_propagation.md), `a924922b515aecdedef0c3877d69f0e50da030b9a111220f712a3f6d1bdb926e`: full-normal global envelope and the conditional quantitative local propagation theorem, without importing its cosine initializer. - [Joint factorial lens relative source](research_joint_factorial_lens_relative_source.md), `a14ca148bd55b36b1eea9de8be8a63025532c3bbbb928482b0d7cb8edae56e54`: physical angular grid, double-cover normalization, odd simple node and full lower-lens source placement. - [One-sided Hermite projection](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_one_sided_hermite_projection.md), `efa82935ada9aa9e06dcbd5d20d5e05357859986896b0b73a93eb78a4bb81cf4`: prior angular-representative coverage, distinguished from the new spectral charge polarization.

title: Canonical polarized endpoints and the exact heat-readout quotient
text:
# Canonical polarized endpoints and the exact heat-readout quotient Private written proof, 16 November 2026. The canonical finite charge polarization and the initialized frozen-contour polarization need not have the same leading term away from unit charge. They nevertheless represent exactly the same original scalar after any signed heat evolution and final unit-charge readout. Their difference belongs to the precise kernel of all such readouts: the sum of charge parity sectors odd in at least one coordinate. For the original same-index kernel network with complete outside data, the canonical polarization has an explicit complete-action endpoint term in its contractive charge half-planes. This statement includes all physical normals and both parities, and does not require a charged high-sector estimate. The quotient identity explains how that term can coexist with a geometrically initialized contour representative. ## 1. Original families and charge parity Fix \(N\ge2\), \(D=N-1\), and \(\eta=(-1)^D\). Retain the original algebra and closing functional \[ P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2,\qquad \mathcal A_N=\mathbb C[z]/(P_N),\qquad \phi_N(f)=\eta N^2[z^D]\operatorname{rem}_{P_N}f . 	ag{1} \] The distinct double nodes are \(c_a=-2\cos	au_a\), with \[ 	au_a=\pi(D-2a)/N>0,\qquad 0\le a<\lfloor N/2floor. 	ag{2} \] At odd levels the remaining node \(-2\) is simple. The canonical positive-angle class \(L_N\) has values \(	au_a\), first normals \(1/(2\sin	au_a)\), and odd simple value zero. Put \(y_v=1-\chi_v\). For a fixed compiled numerator \(F_N\), including all kernels, spectators and ordinary outside variables, define the carrier-removed canonical source \[ \mathcal F_{ oldsymbol\sigma}(\mathbf n,\mathbf y) =\phi_N^{\otimes I}\left[ F_N\prod_{v\in I} \exp_{\mathcal A_N}\!\left( rac{in_vN}{4\pi}L_N^2ight) \exp_{\mathcal A_N}(\sigma_viNy_vL_N)ight]. 	ag{3} \] Multiplication by \(\prod_v\exp(\pi i n_vD^2/(4N))\) restores the literal original carriers. At integer powers and \(\mathbf y=0\), this is the prescribed original scalar. Let \(\mathcal G_{ oldsymbol\sigma}(\mathbf n,\mathbf y)\) be a pattern-adapted contour family with its original polynomial numerator, removed-row expansion, cuts, and entire table of positive heights fixed as in its pinned source. It is not redefined during heat transport. Both exact constructions obey \[ R_v\mathcal F_{ oldsymbol\sigma} =\mathcal F_{ oldsymbol\sigma^{(v)}},\qquad R_v\mathcal G_{ oldsymbol\sigma} =\mathcal G_{ oldsymbol\sigma^{(v)}}, \qquad R_v f(\mathbf y)=f(y_1,\ldots,-y_v,\ldots), 	ag{4} \] where \( oldsymbol\sigma^{(v)}\) flips the indicated sign. Their sign averages are the same original cosine source \(\mathcal C(\mathbf n,\mathbf y)\). Thus, with \[ E=\prod_{v\in I} rac{1+R_v}{2}, 	ag{5} \] one has the exact identities \[ E\mathcal F_{ oldsymbol\sigma} =E\mathcal G_{ oldsymbol\sigma}=\mathcal C . 	ag{6} \] These are identities of the full source, before specializing any ordinary outside variables or taking any asymptotic expansion. ## 2. The maximal kernel of independent heat readouts Let \(\mathscr H\) consist of entire functions of \(\mathbf y\) satisfying some bound \[ |f(\mathbf y)|\le C(1+|\mathbf y|)^M \exp(A\sum_v|y_v|). 	ag{7} \] Constants here may depend on the fixed level. The original canonical families and fixed-contour families belong to this class at every fixed base power. Their actual source bounds give (7), including ordinary outside derivatives on compact sets. For independent heat increments \( oldsymbol\delta\), put \[ \mathsf H_{ oldsymbol\delta} =\exp\left[- rac{i}{4\pi N} \sum_v\delta_v\partial_{y_v}^2ight], \qquad \Lambda_{ oldsymbol\delta}f =(\mathsf H_{ oldsymbol\delta}f)(\mathbf0). 	ag{8} \] The series converges locally uniformly in \(\mathbf y\) and all complex \( oldsymbol\delta\). Indeed Cauchy estimates with radii proportional to the derivative orders bound an order-\( oldsymbol
u\) derivative of (7) by a fixed exponential in \(| oldsymbol
u|\) times a polynomial in \(| oldsymbol
u|\), locally uniformly in \(\mathbf y\). The factorials in the exponential series then give convergence for every bounded set of heat parameters. **Theorem 1.** On \(\mathscr H\), \[  igcap_{ oldsymbol\delta}\ker\Lambda_{ oldsymbol\delta} =\ker E = igoplus_{\varnothing
e A\subseteq I}\operatorname{im}P_A, \qquad P_A=\prod_{v\in A} rac{1-R_v}{2} \prod_{v
otin A} rac{1+R_v}{2}. 	ag{9} \] For the intersection it suffices to use all independent real heat parameters in any nonempty open box, or a complex neighborhood. Using only integer powers is not asserted sufficient. **Proof.** Every \(\partial_{y_v}^2\) commutes with every reflection, and evaluation at zero equals evaluation after \(E\). Hence \(\Lambda_{ oldsymbol\delta}=\Lambda_{ oldsymbol\delta}E\). This proves one inclusion and heat stability of the kernel. Conversely, vanishing on a real open box implies vanishing of the entire heat-readout function. Its derivatives at \( oldsymbol\delta=0\) give \[ \left.\partial_{ oldsymbol\delta}^{ oldsymbol\alpha} \Lambda_{ oldsymbol\delta}fight|_0 =\left(- rac{i}{4\pi N}ight)^{| oldsymbol\alpha|} \partial_{\mathbf y}^{2 oldsymbol\alpha}f(0). 	ag{10} \] These are exactly all Taylor coefficients of the all-even function \(Ef\). Thus \(Ef=0\). The commuting reflection projectors sum to the identity and have disjoint images, proving the last equality. \(\square\) For nonzero real increments the same statement is an absolutely convergent Gaussian identity. In one coordinate, \[ \Lambda_\delta f =\sqrt{ rac N{|\delta|}}\int_{\mathbb R} e^{-\pi Nr^2/|\delta|} f\!\left(-e^{-i\,\operatorname{sgn}(\delta)\pi/4}right)\,dr. 	ag{11} \] The minus sign accounts for \(y=1-\chi\) and can equally be removed by \(r\mapsto-r\). Bound (7) justifies tensorization, Fubini and reflection of a complete integration line. A parity sector odd in one coordinate integrates to zero. When an increment is zero, evaluation at that coordinate gives the same conclusion. Equations (6)--(11), together with the exact heat identities of the two sources, give for every base power \(\mathbf b\) \[ \Lambda_{ oldsymbol\delta} \{\mathcal F_{ oldsymbol\sigma}(\mathbf b,\cdot) -\mathcal G_{ oldsymbol\sigma}(\mathbf b,\cdot)\}=0, \qquad \mathcal F_{ oldsymbol\sigma}(\mathbf b+ oldsymbol\delta,0) =\mathcal G_{ oldsymbol\sigma}(\mathbf b+ oldsymbol\delta,0). 	ag{12} \] All original outside derivatives and carriers can be restored. For the frozen contour representative its small-charge initializer is the actual proved one; (12) does not require reconstructing it inside the canonical finite charge space. There are two useful limitations. Membership in the ideal generated by the \(y_v\) is insufficient: for example a nonzero \(y_v^2\) term can contribute after heat evolution. The precise kernel is (9). Also cancellation in (11) uses the entire centered lines. A displaced or truncated local saddle piece need not annihilate an odd sector; its compensating pieces must remain in the exact heat integral. Finally \(E\) is injective on the canonical finite-\(Q\) image of a fixed full spectral algebra. Its image is the faithful original cosine observation, and the crossing factors in (3) are algebra units. Thus a nontrivial repair by (9) generally leaves that finite image. The contour family is a representative of the same heat-readout class in the larger entire function space, not a new finite coupon with silently changed normal data. ## 3. A local complete-kernel estimate with a global physical envelope For the remaining statements take the original same-index source on a fixed finite circle tree, with a nonempty selected set \(I\). Keep all \(e\) edges incident to \(I\), counted once, and fix every outside endpoint at its complete spectral value \(-2\). No further uncontracted exterior is included in this assertion. The selected set need not be connected, and no lower degree or charged geometric-positivity hypothesis is needed. Write \[ K_N(z,w)=\sum_{a=0}^{D}e_a(z)e_a(w),\qquad \mathcal K_N=K_N(-2,-2),\qquad M_\infty=4G/\pi . 	ag{13} \] The pinned local low-edge proof at complete angles gives \[ \mathcal K_N = rac14N^{-3/2}e^{NM_\infty}(1+O(N^{-1})). 	ag{14} \] Here is why it applies to the full kernel with the needed derivatives. The complete index maximum is \(x=1/4\), with second derivative \(-8\pi\) and density \(1/4\). Retain a small fixed index interval about this maximum and apply the original holomorphic index-contour expansion. Outside that interval the real complete low-index action has a fixed strict gap, including its endpoint limits. The low Laurent coefficients are nonnegative, so its full real angular supremum is bounded by its complete value. Polynomial continuation preserves the gap on a sufficiently small fixed complex angular polydisk. The full high radical kernel, with both arguments ordinary, satisfies the source bound \[ |\partial_t^r\partial_u^s K_N^{m high}(-2\cos t,-2\cos u)| \le m(N-1)D^{r+s}e^{D(|\Im t|+|\Im u|)},\qquad m=\lfloor N/2floor, 	ag{15} \] apart from the possible middle low index, which stays in the low sum. Shrinking the fixed polydisk makes (15) exponentially smaller than the complete low-edge term. Thus, on that polydisk, \[ K_N(-2\cos t,-2\cos u) =N^{-3/2}a(t,u)e^{N\psi(t,u)}(1+O_{m hol}(N^{-1})), \quad a(0,0)=1/4,\quad\psi(0,0)=M_\infty . 	ag{16} \] All factors are separately even in their angular arguments. Let \(f_{N,\mathbf n}(\mathbf t)\) be the graph kernel product multiplied by the carrier-removed Gaussian factors \(\exp(i n_vNt_v^2/(4\pi))\). For real powers in a fixed bounded box, (16) implies, uniformly near the origin, \[ f_{N,\mathbf n}(0)=\mathcal K_N^e,\qquad  rac{f_{N,\mathbf n}(\mathbf t)}{\mathcal K_N^e} =a_*(\mathbf t)e^{NW_*(\mathbf t)} (1+O_{m hol}(N^{-1})), \quad a_*(0)=1,\quad W_*(0)=0, 	ag{17} \] with \(W_*=O(|\mathbf t|^2)\). The amplitudes, actions and errors are separately even. The ratio in (17) is normalized exactly at zero; changing its displayed error by \(O(N^{-1})\) achieves this. There is also a global polynomial physical-jet envelope. At a physical node \(c_j\), \[ 0\le e_r(c_j)\le e_r(-2)\quad(r\le j),\qquad e_r(c_j)=0\quad(r>j). 	ag{18} \] The first inequality follows term by term from the positive Newton product. Consequently every physical kernel value is at most \(\mathcal K_N\). The pinned full-normal bounds give \[ |K_z(c_j,w)|\le N^{11}K_N(c_j,w),\qquad |K_{zw}(c_j,c_l)|\le(N^{16}+N^{22})K_N(c_j,c_l), 	ag{19} \] with the stated first-normal bound also valid at outside \(w=-2\). Leibniz expansion over the fixed graph therefore bounds every mixed normal needed by the tensor trace by \(CN^A\mathcal K_N^e\). Real crossing values have modulus one and their normals add only polynomial cost. Odd simple nodes require only evaluation. This is a bound for the actual full source, not for a replacement positive closing. ## 4. The canonical half-grid endpoint term For \(\sigma=\pm1\), define on \(\sigma\Im y>0\) \[  egin{aligned} \mathfrak e_{\sigma,\mathrm{even}}(y) &=-i\sigma\{\csc(\pi y)-\pi y\csc(\pi y)\cot(\pi y)\},\ \mathfrak e_{\sigma,\mathrm{odd}}(y) &= i\sigma\{\cot(\pi y)-\pi y\csc^2(\pi y)\}. \end{aligned} 	ag{20} \] Their apparent singularity at zero is removable, but the asymptotic domain below stays a fixed positive distance inside the half-plane. **Theorem 2.** Uniformly on compact sets of \(\{\mathbf y:\sigma_v\Im y_v>0\ 	ext{for every }v\}\), and for real powers in a fixed bounded box, \[  oxed{\quad \mathcal F_{ oldsymbol\sigma}(\mathbf n,\mathbf y) =\mathcal K_N^e \left\{\prod_{v\in I}\mathfrak e_{\sigma_v,\operatorname{parity}(N)} (y_v)+O_{m hol}(N^{-1})ight\}. \quad} 	ag{21} \] Equivalently its complete-action prefactor is \(4^{-e}N^{-3e/2}e^{NeM_\infty}\). The assertion includes every mixed physical normal in (3). **Proof.** The exact positive-node contribution of a one-variable spectator \(f\), after inserting the polarized coupon, is \[ 2\eta e^{\sigma iNy	au} \{\sin	au\,\partial_	au+\cos	au +\sigma iNy\sin	au\}f(	au). 	ag{22} \] This follows from \(4\sin^2	au\,f_z=2\sin	au\,f_	au\) and \(-c=2\cos	au\). At odd levels add \(f(0)\). The tensor product of these exact operators is (3). On the compact charge set let \(\sigma_v\Im y_v\ge b_0>0\). If at least one physical angle is at least a fixed small \(\delta>0\), (19) and the coupon exponential bound make its entire contribution \(O(N^A e^{-Nb_0\delta})\mathcal K_N^e\). There are only polynomially many physical assignments. This also handles configurations in which some other coordinates are odd simple nodes. For the remaining assignments put \(r_v=N	au_v\). Formula (17), its holomorphic derivative bounds, and separate evenness show that applying the operators in braces in (22) gives their constant- spectator answer with error bounded by \[  rac{C}{N}(1+\sum_vr_v)^B \exp\!\left( rac C N\sum_vr_v^2ight) \mathcal K_N^e . 	ag{23} \] This elementary bound follows either by Leibniz expansion of (17) or by differentiating in the \(r_v\): each differentiated phase has at least its corresponding factor \(r_v/N\), and \(N\sin(r_v/N)\) supplies at most \(r_v\). An undifferentiated exponential differs from one by at most its quadratic bound times that exponential. The holomorphic \(O(N^{-1})\) remainder and its fixed derivatives have the same bound. There are only finitely many derivatives in this calculation. Choose \(\delta\) smaller if necessary so that \(Cr_v^2/N\le b_0r_v/2\) on this region. Multiplication by the coupon exponential then makes the sum of (23) at most \[  rac{C'}N\mathcal K_N^e \sum_{\mathbf r}(1+\sum_vr_v)^B e^{-b_0\sum_vr_v/2} =O(N^{-1})\mathcal K_N^e . 	ag{24} \] The mesh of each \(r_v\) is the fixed mesh \(2\pi\), with its appropriate parity offset. Thus the bound is independent of \(N\). In the constant-spectator part, replacing \(\cos(r/N)\) by one and \(N\sin(r/N)\) by \(r\) costs at most \(C(r^2+r^3)/N^2\) before the same exponential weight. Its sum is \(O(N^{-2})\), also absorbed in (24). The same argument permits extending the constant-spectator sums to the whole positive half-grid, with exponential error. At even levels that half-grid is \(r=(2j+1)\pi\), \(j\ge0\); at odd levels it is \(r=2j\pi\), \(j\ge1\), together with the simple evaluation at zero. The convergent sums are \[ K_{\sigma,\mathrm{even}}(y) =2\sum_{j\ge0}e^{\sigma i(2j+1)\pi y} =i\sigma\csc(\pi y), \qquad K_{\sigma,\mathrm{odd}}(y) =1+2\sum_{j\ge1}e^{\sigma i2j\pi y} =i\sigma\cot(\pi y). 	ag{25} \] Equation (22) gives \(\eta(K+yK')\) at even levels and \(K+yK'\) at odd levels, where \(\eta=-1\) and \(+1\), respectively. These are (20). All tensor variables factor in the constant-spectator answer, proving (21). Cauchy estimates on slightly larger compact half-plane sets give the holomorphic derivative assertion. \(\square\) The coefficient is not identically zero. More concretely, for every \( eta>0\), at \(y=i\sigma eta\) it is \[ \mathfrak e_{\sigma,\mathrm{even}} =(\pi eta\coth(\pi eta)-1)\operatorname{csch}(\pi eta)>0, \qquad \mathfrak e_{\sigma,\mathrm{odd}} =\coth(\pi eta)-\pi eta\operatorname{csch}^2(\pi eta)>0. 	ag{26} \] The inequalities follow by differentiating \(z\cosh z-\sinh z\) and \(\sinh z\cosh z-z\) for \(z>0\). Thus on neighborhoods of these actual charge points the canonical polarized source has precisely the complete action \(eM_\infty\), for every bounded real power tuple. ## 5. Exact removal and the remaining estimate Every function in (20) is odd in \(y\). This is consistent with, but is not a substitute for, the exact parity theorem (9). The two signs' asymptotics are proved in opposite half-planes; they must not be added outside their domains to infer a cosine asymptotic. The original cosine cancellation is instead an exact identity (6), with all normal data retained. One may remove the difference \[ \mathcal D_{ oldsymbol\sigma} =\mathcal F_{ oldsymbol\sigma}-\mathcal G_{ oldsymbol\sigma} =\sum_{\varnothing
e A\subseteq I}P_A\mathcal D_{ oldsymbol\sigma} 	ag{27} \] before estimating a final heat readout. Equations (9)--(12) prove that this removal has exactly zero effect on the prescribed scalar, at every level and every signed real power tuple. There is no unestimated residual boundary term in that identity. In particular the already initialized frozen-contour family can be used directly as a representative of the canonical family's heat-readout class. Subtracting only the first asymptotic term in (21) would not prove this: it is a local half-plane expression and leaves errors with the same complete exponential rate. Likewise subtracting a finite Taylor jet of the angular spectator generally lowers only the polynomial endpoint order. The exact parity decomposition is the relevant operation, and it retains the original scalar by (12). The construction does not provide a new action-relative bound along an arbitrary heat path. The initialized contour representative still has its actual fixed growth envelope, shrinking certified domains, and possible large complementary contributions. A proposed geometric initializer for the canonical finite-\(Q\) family cannot ignore (21) whenever its asserted action is strictly below \(eM_\infty\). Passing to the exact quotient permits the contour representative; it does not by itself extend its proved coverage to arbitrary short fillings. ## Direct sources and readback The complete proof and the following complete source versions are read before freezing.
