Only written mathematics, text reads and hashes are used; no programs, tests or numerical calculations are run. * [Canonical finite polarization](research_polarized_charge_heat_source.md), SHA256 860801dedc3f1093d58c0413f580599512bd2566c00f4a94d0ebf99636343db1: all physical jets, trace formula, cosine projection, faithful observation and exact carrier-removed heat evolution. * [Pattern-adapted initialized family](research_pattern_adapted_polarized_heat_initializer.md), SHA256 a27c25dae7f3be3f1ef52fb369ecca822b0896a4b034450131e05b12423c2694: fixed actual source, reflection and sign-average identities, entire exponential-type bound, exact Gaussian heat and initializer. * [Regular low-edge source](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_regular_zero_subtree_low_source.md), SHA256 06e4b7c14e3a61616dea61642103e2d2803709fcd465ae9860258119db3299d1: holomorphic edge symbol, exact density, strict index maximum and polynomial continuation of the discarded low indices. * [Full high Newton radical](research_high_newton_radical_contraction.md), SHA256 1faa5d2e02edf0a1462cc43b243e0ab4403bf56e9f1af0befb6b492441d9dd03: full ordinary radical Fourier bound and derivative bound (15). * [Original physical normal envelope](research_charged_source_physical_pressure.md), SHA256 1e127c0842c0d6d5727a517cc66c39e73baa2846848c284d257c1ebe49679091: all physical first and mixed-normal bounds and their assembly with the real crossing factors and complete outside ends. The finite reconstruction theorem (research_finite_charge_quantitative_reconstruction.md, 5d13994e8b6d2dc3c54d1fcf15d1f9435efc2d26921046bca14b90d22e75bf23) already identifies canonical polarization as a projection of the whole cosine charge function. No claim of novelty is made for reflection projectors or elementary heat parity. The additions are the exact comparison with the initialized original contour family, the maximal readout-kernel statement in its actual growth class, and the controlled complete-action asymptotic of the canonical half-grid source.

title: Exact height currents and local recentering of the polarized source
text:
# Exact height currents and local recentering of the polarized source Private written proof, 16 November 2026. Changing a frozen height in the contour-polarized family produces an explicit original endpoint current. It contains a sine of the charge offset and vanishes at unit charge. Its exponential majorant is the same one used for the original vertical current. Consequently nearby height tables in the certified small-charge region define sources that are exponentially equivalent, including all asymptotic coefficients. This is a local source transport statement; it supplies no new global boundary estimate along an arbitrary charge path. ## 1. Exact one-coordinate current Use the carrier-removed operators of the pattern-adapted initializer. Let \[ \eta=(-1)^{N-1},\quad N\ge2,\quad e^{iNa}=-\eta,\quad 0<a\le\pi,\quad k=N(1-\chi),\quad K=- rac{N^2}{\pi i}, \] \[ g(t)=\sin t\,A(t)e^{inNt^2/(4\pi)},\qquad W_N(t)= rac{e^{-iNt}}{(1-\eta e^{-iNt})^2}. 	ag{1} \] The spectator \(A\) is even and holomorphic on the required angular rectangle. It is held fixed when differentiating height. Put \[ T_\sigma^h=\mathcal H_\sigma^h+\mathcal V_{\cos}^h, \qquad \sigma\in\{+1,-1\},\qquad h>0, 	ag{2} \] retaining either of the original signed vertical-side conventions. The exact identity \(\mathcal L=\mathcal O+\mathcal H_{\cos}^h+ \mathcal V_{\cos}^h\) makes the cosine sum independent of height. Therefore \[ \partial_hT_\sigma^h[A] =\partial_h(\mathcal H_\sigma^h-\mathcal H_{\cos}^h)[A]. 	ag{3} \] Since \(e^{\sigma ikt}-\cos(kt)=\sigma i\sin(kt)\), differentiation of the horizontal integral at fixed real cuts gives \[ \partial_hT_\sigma^h[A] =\sigma K\{g(a-ih)\sin(k(a-ih))W_N(a-ih) -g(-a-ih)\sin(k(-a-ih))W_N(-a-ih)\}. 	ag{4} \] Here the moving endpoints contribute the factor \(-i\). The function \(g(t)\sin(kt)W_N(t)\) is even, and the physical midpoint gives \[ W_N(a-ih)=W_N(a+ih)=- rac{\eta}{4\cosh^2(Nh/2)}. 	ag{5} \] Thus the exact current is \[  oxed{\quad J_\sigma^h[A]:=\partial_hT_\sigma^h[A] =- rac{\sigma\eta K}{4\cosh^2(Nh/2)} \{g(a-ih)\sin(k(a-ih))-g(a+ih)\sin(k(a+ih))\}. \quad} 	ag{6} \] One may replace \(a\) by \(\epsilon a\), \(\epsilon=\pm1\), if the right side is also multiplied by \(\epsilon\). This is exactly the original signed-side orientation, and permits the side chosen from the base crossing power in the initializer proof. For any two positive heights whose intervening rectangle is admissible, \[ T_\sigma^{h_1}-T_\sigma^{h_0} =\int_{h_0}^{h_1}J_\sigma^h\,dh. 	ag{7} \] This includes both endpoint values of the original spectator. No factorial representative is substituted at those endpoints. Equations (6)--(7) are entire in \(\chi,n\), and are divisible by \(1-\chi\) as entire functions. In particular changing this height has no effect at \(\chi=1\), with every physical and outside normal retained. ## 2. Patternwise assembly and a quantitative kernel bound Let \(\mathbf h=(h_v^S)_{S\subseteq I,\,v
otin S}\) be the height table in the pattern-adapted source, denoted here by \(\mathfrak Z_{N, oldsymbol\sigma}^{\mathbf h}\). With its prescribed polynomial numerator \(F_N\), \[ \partial_{h_v^S}\mathfrak Z_{N, oldsymbol\sigma}^{\mathbf h} =\left[\prod_{u\in S}\mathcal O_u \prod_{w
otin S\cup\{v\}}T_{\sigma_w}^{h_w^S} J_{\sigma_v}^{h_v^S}ight]F_N. 	ag{8} \] All outside arguments and all parameters of the operators are kept as in the source definition. In particular \(\mathcal O_u\) still includes its literal full physical angular derivative. Those derivatives commute with the finite integrals and endpoint evaluations in (8). The spectator remains even in the coordinate where (6) is used. Integrating (8) along the straight path between two admissible height tables, or telescoping one entry at a time, gives the exact full-source difference. Each summand has a factor \(1-\chi_v\) at its changed vertex. Thus the difference belongs to the entire ideal generated by those charge offsets; a product of all offsets is not asserted. Averaging the signs restores zero current, as it must for the original height-independent cosine source. The sine factor has a useful uniform bound. For \(t=\epsilon a\pm ih\), \[  rac{|\sin(N(1-\chi)t)|}{4\cosh^2(Nh/2)} \le \min\{1,N|1-\chi|\sqrt{a^2+h^2}\}\, e^{-N\{(1-|1-\Re\chi|)h-a|\Im\chi|\}}. 	ag{9} \] Indeed \(|\sin z|\le\min\{1,|z|\}e^{|\Im z|}\), and \(4\cosh^2(Nh/2)\ge e^{Nh}\). For real \(0\le\chi\le1\), (9) becomes \[  rac{|\sin(N(1-\chi)t)|}{4\cosh^2(Nh/2)} \le\min\{1,N|1-\chi|\sqrt{a^2+h^2}\}\,e^{-N\chi h}. 	ag{10} \] The exponential factor is precisely the original vertical-current majorant. Consequently \[ |J_\sigma^h[A]| \le rac{N^2}{\pi} \min\{1,N|1-\chi|\sqrt{a^2+h^2}\} e^{-N\{(1-|1-\Re\chi|)h-a|\Im\chi|\}}  igl(|g(a-ih)|+|g(a+ih)| igr). 	ag{11} \] The actual spectator and crossing growth on both sides remain in (11). Exact vanishing at \(\chi=1\) does not turn an \(O(N^{-1})\) approach to that charge into an exponential gain. ## 3. Local exponential equivalence and recentering Fix a same-index graph, base real powers \(\mathbf b\), complete outside angles, and a base small charge \( oldsymbol\xi\in(1/4000,1/2000)^I\), as in the adopted pattern-adapted initializer. Let \(\mathbf h^0\) be its table of reduced-saddle heights, and let \[ S( oldsymbol\chi) =\Phi_{\mathbf b, oldsymbol\chi}(\mathbf t^*( oldsymbol\chi)) 	ag{12} \] be its marked holomorphic action. There exist \(ho,\gamma>0\), a bounded complex neighborhood \(U\) of \( oldsymbol\xi\), and constants \(C,p\) such that any two real height tables \(\mathbf h,\widehat{\mathbf h}\) within \(ho\) of \(\mathbf h^0\) satisfy \[  oxed{\quad |\mathfrak Z_{N, oldsymbol\sigma}^{\mathbf h} (\mathbf b, oldsymbol\chi) -\mathfrak Z_{N, oldsymbol\sigma}^{\widehat{\mathbf h}} (\mathbf b, oldsymbol\chi)| \le C N^p\|\mathbf h-\widehat{\mathbf h}\|_1 e^{N(\Re S( oldsymbol\chi)-\gamma)} \quad( oldsymbol\chi\in U). \quad} 	ag{13} \] The bound holds through both parities and for every sign vector. The outside values in this assertion are the complete ones; no arbitrary-exterior gap is claimed. To prove it, first evaluate a derivative (8) at the base parameters and table. Expanding the remaining \(T\)'s into horizontals and verticals gives exactly the contour patterns in the small-charge proof, with at least one actual endpoint face. At the changed coordinate, (10) has the same pointwise exponential envelope as the old vertical density. If \(S
e\varnothing\), the original centered outer-row kernel bound and its mixed normals apply at the reduced heights \(h^S\). If \(S=\varnothing\), the current provides a nonempty vertical subset. The archived strict outer-row and mixed-current gaps therefore bound every term by \(C N^p e^{N(\Re S( oldsymbol\xi)-\gamma_0)}\), with \(\gamma_0>0\). A minus horizontal sign only improves its real small-charge envelope. Choose \(ho\) so all heights stay positive and below the original thin-rectangle bound \(1/200\). The retained angular domains are compact; the actual holomorphic kernel upper phases and the crossing quadratics change by \(O(ho)\). The centered outer-row bound has the same uniformity and retains its first normals. Shrinking \(ho\) preserves a fixed part of every strict gap along the full interpolation between the two height tables. A small complex charge change costs at most \(e^{C_1N\varepsilon}\) in each of (9) and the other coupon bounds, with only polynomial normal cost. Shrink \(U\) to keep this cost and the change of \(\Re S\) below the remaining gaps. This gives a uniform bound for (8). Its integral along the height-table segment proves (13). The normalized difference \(e^{-NS}\Delta\mathfrak Z_N\) is holomorphic in the charges. Cauchy estimates on smaller neighborhoods therefore retain the exponential gap for every fixed holomorphic derivative. In particular all-plus sources from these nearby tables have the same complete asymptotic expansion and the same nonzero coefficient \(2^m A_\Gamma\). The suppressed sign families remain suppressed. Since the reduced-saddle heights depend continuously on the real base charge, sufficiently close small-charge base points can recenter their height tables with this exact exponentially small correction on their common certified neighborhood. No claim in (13) follows from the sine factor alone. Extending this recentring along a general charge path requires an actual endpoint face estimate beyond the presently certified region. Positivity of a local classical Hessian is not substituted for that estimate. ## 4. Full-midpoint specialization and the off-lattice defect Set \(a=\pi\) and now require the literal spectral spectator \(A(t)=A^\sharp(-2\cos t)\), with its ordinary polynomial retained. Then, exactly, \[ A(\pi-ih)=A(\pi+ih)=A^\sharp(2\cosh h)=:A_h. 	ag{14} \] Evenness alone would not imply (14); no equality of raw factorial representatives is used. Put \[ E=e^{inN(\pi^2-h^2)/(4\pi)},\qquad b=nNh/2. \] The bracket in (6) is \[ 2A_h\sinh h\,E \{\cos(\pi k)\sinh(kh)\sinh b +i\sin(\pi k)\cosh(kh)\cosh b\}. 	ag{15} \] This follows from \(\sin(\pi\mp ih)=\pm i\sinh h\) and the Gaussian multipliers \(E e^{\pm b}\). Formula (6), with its original normalization, multiplies (15) by \(-\sigma\eta K/[4\cosh^2(Nh/2)]\). At zero power it simplifies to \[ J_{\sigma,0,\chi}^h[A] = rac{\sigma\eta N^2}{2\pi} A_h rac{\sinh h\cosh(kh)}{\cosh^2(Nh/2)}\sin(\pi k). 	ag{16} \] Thus every finite height difference vanishes when \(n=0\) and \(k=N(1-\chi)\in\mathbb Z\). This includes the physical charge lattice at both parities. The identity tensorizes in changed zero-power coordinates because the other operations leave an ordinary spectral polynomial spectator in that coordinate. There is a precise off-lattice failure. At such an integer \(k\), with the spectator held fixed in this charge coordinate, \[ \left.\partial_\chi J_{\sigma,0,\chi}^h[A]ight|_{k\in\mathbb Z} =- rac{\sigma\eta N^3}{2}(-1)^k A_h  rac{\sinh h\cosh(kh)}{\cosh^2(Nh/2)}. 	ag{17} \] For \(h>0\) this is nonzero whenever \(A_h
e0\). Hence lattice height independence is not height independence on a complex charge neighborhood. The spectator in (14)--(17) is still the full original source evaluated at \(2\cosh h\), not a deleted graph or a controlled geometric amplitude. ## Direct sources and versions The author reread the complete final proof and all directly used source implications. Earlier complete source reads were retained only at the unchanged versions below. - [Exact complete trace contour](research_exact_complete_trace_contour.md), `a63c66e8078457fa84e8044dc876beca36126348e816de9c6997d2a2610474e8`: original derivative sampling, midpoint kernel, side orientations and retained endpoint currents. - [Pattern-adapted polarized initializer](research_pattern_adapted_polarized_heat_initializer.md), `a27c25dae7f3be3f1ef52fb369ecca822b0896a4b034450131e05b12423c2694`: exact subset expansion, frozen height tables, original spectator placement and complex small-charge initializer. - [Small-charge source theorem](research_small_charge_path_source.md), `c6d0ce2a4ecf1412aa3752cb8a94c6933bb47acab5d96d879c6f1b17b2db2a90`: pointwise mixed-current and centered outer-row bounds, all physical normals and their strict gaps for the original same-index graphs.

title: Polynomial upper bounds for an initialized polarized source
text:
# Polynomial upper bounds for an initialized polarized source Private written proof, 22 November 2026. An action-relative complex upper bound may lose any fixed power of the level. An actual all-order initializer still propagates through that loss, provided its formal coefficients extend holomorphically. A finite jet of those coefficients suffices for a nonzero leading term at a fixed target. This is a source-specific use of elementary analytic continuation, not a new estimate for the original period. ## 1. Polynomial losses and a holomorphic initializer Let \(D\subset\mathbb C\) be connected and open, and let \(U\subset D\) be a nonempty open set. Suppose \(f_N\) is holomorphic on \(D\), with \(N\) tending to infinity through an unbounded subset of the positive integers. Assume: 1. For every compact \(K\Subset D\), there are constants \(C_K,B_K\) such that \[ \sup_K|f_N|\le C_KN^{B_K}. 	ag{1} \] 2. There are holomorphic functions \(a_j\) on \(D\), \(j\ge0\), and for every integer \(L\ge1\), \[ f_N-\sum_{j=0}^{L-1}a_jN^{-j}=O_{\mathrm{loc},U}(N^{-L}). 	ag{2} \] Then (2) holds locally uniformly on all of \(D\), at every order. It also holds after any fixed number of complex derivatives. Here and below all constants may depend on the chosen order. The polynomial exponent used to propagate a remainder will not depend on that order. **Proof.** Fix a compact target set \(K\Subset D\). Choose a closed disk in \(U\), finitely many paths in \(D\) joining that disk to a finite disk cover of \(K\), and a compact neighborhood of these paths. There is a common \(r>0\) and a finite collection of disk chains with successive centers at distance at most \(r\), whose disks of radius \(4r\) remain in that compact neighborhood. Their final disks of radius \(2r\) cover \(K\); the initial disk of radius \(r\) lies in \(U\). Let \(J\ge1\) bound the number of interpolation steps in every chain. For \[ R_{L,N}=f_N-\sum_{j=0}^{L-1}a_jN^{-j}, \] (1) and boundedness of the finitely many \(a_j\) on this fixed compact neighborhood give \[ |R_{L,N}|\le C_LN^B,\qquad B\ge0, 	ag{3} \] where \(B\) is independent of \(L\). The initial disk has bound \(O_L(N^{-L})\). For a holomorphic function with inner bound \(M_1\) on radius \(r\) and outer bound \(M_4\) on radius \(4r\), the maximum principle gives the radius-\(2r\) bound \[ M_2\le M_1^{1/2}M_4^{1/2}. 	ag{4} \] Indeed compare \(\log|R|\) on the intervening annulus with the harmonic function affine in \(\log|z-z_0|\) with those two boundary values. Zeros are handled by the usual subharmonic inequality, or by a positive regularization of the boundary bounds. The next radius-\(r\) disk lies in the preceding radius-\(2r\) disk. Iterating (4), and using (3) at every outer disk, therefore gives \[ \sup_K|R_{L,N}| \le C_{K,L}N^{-L	heta+B(1-	heta)},\qquad 	heta=2^{-J}>0. 	ag{5} \] Shorter chains obey the same weaker bound. The fixed finite cover makes \(J,B\) common to all of \(K\), independently of \(L\). For any desired order \(M\ge1\), choose \(L\ge M\) so that \(L	heta-B(1-	heta)\ge M\). Equation (5), followed by adding back the finite tail \(\sum_{j=M}^{L-1}a_jN^{-j}=O_K(N^{-M})\), proves the order-\(M\) assertion. Apply it on a slightly larger compact set and use the Cauchy integral formula to obtain derivatives. \(\square\) There is a useful finite version. If only \(a_0,\ldots,a_{L-1}\) extend to \(D\), and only their order-\(L\) seed estimate is supplied, the same proof gives order \(M\) wherever \[ L\ge M,\qquad L	heta-B(1-	heta)\ge M. 	ag{6} \] In particular a fixed integer \[ L\ge \max\{1,\,2^J(B+1)-B\} 	ag{7} \] suffices for \(f_N=a_0+O_K(N^{-1})\). This jet length depends on the domain, upper-bound exponent and disk chains, but not on \(N\). Nonvanishing at a target still requires \(a_0\) to be nonzero there. The upper hypothesis may instead be the local complex-area estimate \[ \int_K|f_N(z)|^2\,dA(z)\le C_KN^{2B_K} \quad(K\Subset D). 	ag{8} \] To recover (1), first enlarge \(K\) inside \(D\), then apply the holomorphic submean inequality on disks of a fixed buffered radius. This uses area on complex disks, not a bound only on their real axes. ## 2. The actual initialized contour representative Fix the finite same-index graph and selected vertices of the pattern-adapted source theorem. Write \(m=|I|\), let \(e\) be its number of incident kernel edges counted once, and keep outside angles equal to zero, hence outside spectral values equal to \(-2\). Fix real powers \(\mathbf b\) before taking \(N	o\infty\). Integral powers give the prescribed physical crossings. Choose one small positive diagonal base charge and freeze the entire table of heights, cuts and oriented currents prescribed in that theorem. For one complex charge set \[ \mathscr G_N(\chi) =\mathfrak Z_{N,\mathbf+}(\mathbf b,\chi\mathbf1;\mathbf0), \qquad  eta= rac{3(m-e)}2,\qquad \varepsilon_N=\prod_{v\in I} e^{\pi i b_v(N-1)^2/(4N)}. 	ag{9} \] The source theorem gives an entire function of \(\chi\). On a genuine fixed complex seed neighborhood it gives an expansion to every fixed order, whose leading coefficient is \(2^mA_\Gamma
e0\). The heights are not reselected as \(\chi\) changes. Let \(D\) be a connected charge domain containing that seed and the target \(1\). Suppose \(S\) is holomorphic on \(D\) and restricts to the initialized marked action. Define \[ f_N(\chi)=N^{- eta}e^{-NS(\chi)} \mathscr G_N(\chi). 	ag{10} \] If its initialized formal coefficients extend holomorphically to \(D\) and it has the local polynomial bounds (1) or (8), Section 1 propagates its full expansion. For a leading result only the finite jet (6)--(7) is needed. If its continued leading coefficient satisfies \(a_0(1)
e0\), the exact endpoint identity gives \[ Z_N^{\mathrm{original}} =\varepsilon_N\mathscr G_N(1) =\varepsilon_NN^ eta e^{NS(1)} \{a_0(1)+O(N^{-1})\}. 	ag{11} \] Here \(Z_N^{\mathrm{original}}\) is the original marked source in the pinned contour construction, with its full phases and normal data. Since the fixed powers are real, \(|\varepsilon_N|=1\). One may apply the analytic theorem separately to even and odd levels if their formal coefficients differ. The full-sequence leading rate then follows when both target leading coefficients are nonzero and the same marked action is used. A fixed, \(N\)-independent holomorphic charge curve through the seed and the target may replace the diagonal. Its image must retain the asserted initializer and action charts. This application holds the outside data at their complete values. The exact identities allow ordinary free outside variables, but the quoted initializer does not establish an open seed in those variables. No such boundary initializer is inferred here. The heat-readout quotient theorem permits the initialized representative in (9) in place of the canonical spectral polarization: their difference has exactly zero readout after every independent signed heat evolution. It does not supply (1), (8), formal-coefficient continuation or a target unit. In particular the cosine family and the canonical finite coupon cannot be substituted for \(\mathscr G_N\) away from unit charge. ## 3. A source-faithful quadratic upper trial There is a direct positive upper trial for this off-endpoint source, without claiming that an existing physical-algebra quartic compiles it. Keep its actual ordinary polynomial numerator \(F_N(\mathbf z)\) unreduced, with \(z_v=-2\cos t_v\). For the same-index kernel product, \[ \deg_{z_v}F_N\le D_v=d_v(N-1),\qquad f_N^{\mathrm{coef}}\in  igotimes_{v\in I}\mathbb C^{D_v+1}. 	ag{12} \] Here \(d_v\) counts original incidences, including two for a loop; the crossing Gaussians belong to the trace rows, not this numerator. The coefficient-space dimension is \(O_\Gamma(N^m)\). Define a row \(\ell_N(\chi)\) by applying the exact frozen operator in the pattern-adapted formula to each ordinary monomial: \[ \ell_N(\chi)= \sum_{S\subseteq I} igotimes_{v\in I}  egin{cases} \mathcal O_{v,b_v,\chi},&v\in S,\ \mathcal H_{+,b_v,\chi}^{h_v^S} +\mathcal V_{b_v,\chi}^{h_v^S,\epsilon_v},&v
otin S. \end{cases} \qquad \mathscr G_N(\chi)=\ell_N(\chi)f_N^{\mathrm{coef}}. 	ag{13} \] The tensor rows in (13) act on the monomial basis of (12). Their entries are the prescribed local physical-row sums, with their first normals, and fixed compact contour integrals. There is no reduction modulo \(P_N\) in (12)--(13). Such a reduction is generally invalid for this representative away from the endpoint. In the ordinary coefficient Euclidean metric put \[ r_N=\|\ell_N(\chi)\|^2,\quad \lambda_N=1+r_N,\qquad J_{N,\chi}(x)=\lambda_N\|x-f_N^{\mathrm{coef}}\|^2 +|\ell_N(\chi)x|^2. 	ag{14} \] Completion of the rank-one square gives, with \(G=\ell_Nf_N^{\mathrm{coef}}\), \[ x_* =f_N^{\mathrm{coef}}- rac{\ell_N^*G}{\lambda_N+r_N}, \qquad \min J_{N,\chi}= rac{|G|^2}{1+r_N/\lambda_N}, \qquad |\mathscr G_N(\chi)|^2\le2J_{N,\chi}(x). 	ag{15} \] The coefficient matrix is \(\lambda_NI+\ell_N^*\ell_N\), with condition number at most \((\lambda_N+r_N)/\lambda_N<2\). This is a generic least-squares calculation, not a new growth bound. The data \(f_N^{\mathrm{coef}},\ell_N\) are specified without inserting or dividing by the unknown closed source; their construction and the choice of a useful trial may nevertheless be costly. Consequently any supplied trials \(x_N(\chi)\) satisfying \[ \int_K 2N^{-2 eta}e^{-2N\Re S(\chi)} J_{N,\chi}(x_N(\chi))\,dA(\chi) \le C_KN^{2B_K}\quad(K\Subset D) 	ag{16} \] supply (8). The trials and \(\lambda_N\) need not be holomorphic; the actual source (10) is holomorphic. No estimate (16) is proved here. ## 4. What has been reduced The continuation criterion asks only for an action-relative complex upper estimate with an arbitrary fixed polynomial loss. It does not ask for a residual lower witness or exact asymptotic power in that upper estimate. The cost of the loss is a finite number of continued formal coefficients when only the leading term is wanted. The remaining inputs are substantial: a connected regular action domain to the actual target, the required formal jet on that domain, a nonzero target density, and the complex upper estimate itself. A real-charge upper estimate is insufficient for the proof. A zero of the continued leading coefficient does not yield (11) with a nonzero leading term. Exact source-null freedom alone proves none of these analytic inputs. For a knot-volume conclusion one must additionally retain the exact source-to-knot normalization and peripheral marking, and establish \(2\pi\Re S(1)=\operatorname{Vol}\). Known nonvanishing factors whose logarithmic modulus is \(o(N)\) do not change that rate; omitted source factors are not licensed. No new filling class or volume lower bound is established here. ## Direct sources and versions Both complete direct sources and the complete final proof are read before freezing. The continuation proof above imports no source asymptotic beyond the initializer explicitly stated in Section 2. - [Pattern-adapted initialized family](research_pattern_adapted_polarized_heat_initializer.md), a27c25dae7f3be3f1ef52fb369ecca822b0896a4b034450131e05b12423c2694: exact frozen polynomial source, all-order complex initializer, original carriers, full normals and literal endpoint identity. - [Exact heat-readout quotient](research_polarized_endpoint_heat_readout_quotient.md), 32acb79c4f1fff481671d8205454a91b6a1eaf5704b6582b2affb901270e8ede: comparison with the canonical polarization in the precise readout kernel, retaining complete heat currents rather than a saddle piece.

title: Polynomial Ward transport to the literal top source
text: # Polynomial Ward transport to the literal top source Private written proof, 19 November 2026. The original highest-cut pivotal source differs from a specified top matrix coefficient by an explicit two-head \(E\)-current. Its primitive has norm \(O(N)\) at the root and polynomial norm, including all fixed true meridian jets, on a scaled meridian disk. The operator exponent does not grow with the number of spectator heads. No inverse of the full commutator operator is used. The sole complete direct F supplies the actual finite head matrices, ordered coproduct, original pointed pivot, and meridian diagonal frame. The primitive, top coupon, source identity, and bounds below are proved inline. All norms below use the physical coefficient Euclidean metric: the displayed vectors \(w_a\) are orthonormal, with tensor-product metrics. No estimate in a different coherent or binomial metric is inferred. F's diagonal conditioning bounds are unchanged in this metric. ## 1. Finite matrices and the claimed source comparison Fix \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(m\ge2\), \[ q=e^{\pi i/N},\qquad Q=q^2,\qquad M=e^\mu,\qquad x=-M/q,\qquad x_0=-q^{-1}. \tag{1} \] The quantum root stays fixed. On \(V=\operatorname{span}\{w_0,\ldots,w_d\}\), write \(Jw_b=bw_b\), and use the actual arrows \[ E(M)w_b=(MQ^{-b}-M^{-1})w_{b-1}\quad(b>0),\quad E(M)w_0=0, \qquad K(M)w_b=xQ^{-b}w_b. \tag{2} \] In particular the missing bottom arrow is zero also off the root. Put \(Z=V^{\otimes(m-2)}\), and let \(K_Z,E_Z\) be its ordered Cartan and lowering coproduct. For \(m=2\), \(Z=\mathbb C\), \(K_Z=I\), and \(E_Z=0\). Then \[ E_{12}=E_1K_2+E_2,\qquad E_\Sigma=E_{12}K_Z+E_Z. \tag{3} \] Here and below tensor identities in coproduct formulas are implicit. Let \(P_0=|0\rangle\langle0|\), and set \[ \begin{split} O&=|0\rangle\langle d|\otimes|d\rangle\langle0|,\\ Q_{\rm pt}(M)&=P_0\otimes K_2(M)^{-d}\otimes K_Z(M)^{-d},\\ Q_{\rm top}(M)&=O\otimes K_Z(M)^{-d},\\ \Phi_M(C)&=\operatorname{Tr}(Q_{\rm pt}(M)C). \end{split}\tag{4} \] This is F's original highest-cut pivot. Any original crossing scalar, zero-framing factor, or prescribed mark remains inside \(C\), or is retained as an explicit outside scalar with its product rule. We will construct a holomorphic matrix \(\mathcal A(M)\) satisfying \[ [\mathcal A(M),E_\Sigma(M)]=Q_{\rm pt}(M)-Q_{\rm top}(M). \tag{5} \] It follows for every full matrix \(C\), with no intertwining hypothesis, that \[ \boxed{\quad \Phi_M(C)=\operatorname{Tr}(Q_{\rm top}C) +\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(\mathcal A[E_\Sigma,C]\bigr). \quad}\tag{6} \] Indeed \(\operatorname{Tr}([\mathcal A,E_\Sigma]C) =\operatorname{Tr}(\mathcal A(E_\Sigma C-CE_\Sigma))\). The top term is the literal coefficient \[ \operatorname{Tr}(Q_{\rm top}C) =\operatorname{Tr}_Z\!\left[ K_Z^{-d}\langle d,0|C|0,d\rangle\right]. \tag{7} \] No ribbon cut move or replacement of a marked source by an unmarked scalar trace is needed to obtain (6). ## 2. An explicit capped two-head primitive at the root Define the unit raising shift \(Rw_b=w_{b+1}\) for \(b<d\), \(Rw_d=0\). This \(R\) is not a braid crossing or the physical \(F\). Write \(E_0=E(1)\), \(K_0=K(1)\). For \(1\le n\le N\), \[ [R^n,E_0]=(1-Q^{-n})x_0^{-1}R^{n-1}K_0. \tag{8} \] Here is the cap check. In the interior the coefficient on \(w_b\) is \((Q^{-b}-1)-(Q^{-b-n}-1)=Q^{-b}(1-Q^{-n})\). At \(b=0\) the same identity uses the actual zero bottom arrow, \(Q^0-1=0\). At \(b+n=N\), it uses \(Q^{-N}-1=0\), which is only a root coefficient identity, not an added arrow. For \(b+n>N\) both products on the left and \(R^{n-1}w_b\) vanish. For \(n=N\) both sides vanish. Thus (8) includes every finite endpoint. For \(0\le a<d\), put \[ \lambda_a=\frac{x_0^{a-d}}{1-Q^{-a-1}},\qquad X_a=\lambda_aR^{a+1},\qquad \mathcal A_{12,0}=\sum_{a=0}^{d-1}|0\rangle\langle a|\otimes X_a. \tag{9} \] All denominators are nonzero. Set \(X_{-1}=X_d=0\) and \(e_a=Q^{-a}-1\). The only possibly nonzero first-head row of \([\mathcal A_{12,0},E_{12,0}]\) is row zero. Its column \(a\) is \[ [X_a,E_0]+e_aX_{a-1}K_0. \tag{10} \] For \(a=0\), (8) makes this \[ \lambda_0(1-Q^{-1})x_0^{-1}K_0 =x_0^{-N}K_0=K_0^{-d}, \tag{11} \] where \(K_0^N=x_0^NI\). For \(1\le a<d\), the coefficient of \(R^aK_0\) is zero because \[ \lambda_a(1-Q^{-a-1})x_0^{-1}=x_0^{a-d-1},\qquad e_a\lambda_{a-1}=-x_0^{a-d-1}. \tag{12} \] At \(a=d\), \(e_d=Q-1\), \(\lambda_{d-1}=x_0^{-1}/(1-Q)\), and \(R^dK_0=x_0|d\rangle\langle0|\). Consequently the top column of (10) is \(-|d\rangle\langle0|\). This proves exactly \[ [\mathcal A_{12,0},E_{12,0}] =P_0\otimes K_0^{-d}-O. \tag{13} \] The argument also applies when \(N=2\), when the middle range is empty. The matrix in (9) has integer occupation degree \(+1\): its first head changes by \(-a\), and its second by \(a+1\). Its range is \(|0\rangle\otimes\operatorname{span}\{w_1,\ldots,w_d\}\), of dimension \(d\); the \(a=0\) block already covers this range. Row-block Cauchy--Schwarz and \(\|R^j\|\le1\) give \[ \|\mathcal A_{12,0}\| \le\left(\sum_{j=1}^{N-1}|1-Q^{-j}|^{-2}\right)^{1/2} \le\frac N2. \tag{14} \] For the last bound, use \(|1-Q^j|\ge4\min(j,N-j)/N\) and \(\sum_{j=1}^{N-1}\min(j,N-j)^{-2}\le 2\sum_{j\ge1}j^{-2}\le4\), the latter following from the integral comparison \(\sum_{j\ge1}j^{-2}\le2\). Thus, for \(1\le p<\infty\), \[ \|\mathcal A_{12,0}\|_{S_p}\le d^{1/p}N/2. \tag{15} \] ## 3. The actual meridian extension and spectator tensor Use F's diagonal one-head frame \[ h_b(M)=M^{-b}\frac{(Q;Q)_b}{(M^{-2}Q;Q)_b},\qquad D_h(M)w_b=h_b(M)w_b, \tag{16} \] where \((z;Q)_b=\prod_{j=0}^{b-1}(1-zQ^j)\). Its consecutive ratio proves \(E(M)=D_hE_0D_h^{-1}\), including the forced bottom. The two-head lowering frame is \[ \mathcal D_{12}(M)=(D_h(M)M^{-J_1})\otimes D_h(M),\qquad E_{12}(M)=\mathcal D_{12}E_{12,0}\mathcal D_{12}^{-1}. \tag{17} \] The first-head \(M^{-J_1}\) supplies the factor \(M\) in \(K_2(M)\). This diagonal frame fixes \(P_0\otimes K_0^{-d}\), while \[ \mathcal D_{12}O\mathcal D_{12}^{-1}=M^dO, \tag{18} \] since its entries at \((0,d)\) and \((d,0)\) are respectively \(h_d\) and \(h_dM^{-d}\). Therefore \[ \mathcal A_{12}(M)=M^{-d}\mathcal D_{12}(M) \mathcal A_{12,0}\mathcal D_{12}(M)^{-1} \tag{19} \] satisfies \[ [\mathcal A_{12}(M),E_{12}(M)]=P_0\otimes K_2(M)^{-d}-O. \tag{20} \] This is a whole-\(M\) identity wherever the displayed frame is a unit, not a derivative of an off-root continuation of (8). For the spectator tensor, at the fixed quantum root, \(K_Z(M)^N=x^{N(m-2)}I\). Hence \(K_Z^{-N}\) is a scalar matrix and commutes with \(E_Z\). Define \[ \boxed{\quad \mathcal A(M)=\mathcal A_{12}(M)\otimes K_Z(M)^{-N}. \quad}\tag{21} \] Equations (3),(20) give \[ [\mathcal A,E_\Sigma] =[\mathcal A_{12},E_{12}]\otimes K_Z^{1-N} =Q_{\rm pt}-Q_{\rm top}, \tag{22} \] proving (5)--(7). No identity at an off-grid Cartan parameter is used. The degree of \(\mathcal A\) remains \(+1\). In particular, if \(C\) has degree zero, then \([E_\Sigma,C]\) has degree \(-1\), and its trace pairing with \(\mathcal A\) need not vanish. Degree averaging does not discard the current in (6). ## 4. Polynomial collar bounds with explicit dimension costs Fix \(0<\eta<\eta'<\pi\), with \(m\) fixed. F's complete whole-cap estimate gives, uniformly for \(0\le b<N\) and \(|N\mu|\le\eta'\), \[ (N+1)^{-C_{\eta'}}\le|h_b(e^\mu)|\le(N+1)^{C_{\eta'}}. \tag{23} \] The matrices and their inverses are holomorphic on this disk. The Cartan factors \(M^{-J_1}\) and \(M^{-d}\) in (19) have bounded modulus and inverse there. Thus one may take \(P_{\eta'}=1+4C_{\eta'}\), increasing constants when necessary, such that \[ \sup_{|N\mu|\le\eta'}\|\mathcal A_{12}(e^\mu)\| \le C_{\eta'}(N+1)^{P_{\eta'}}. \tag{24} \] The exponent is independent of \(m\). The spectator scalar has modulus at most \(e^{(m-2)\eta'}\); it affects only the constant. Cauchy estimates on the buffered scaled disk consequently imply \[ \sup_{|N\mu|\le\eta} \|\partial_\mu^k\mathcal A(e^\mu)\| \le C_{m,\eta,\eta',k}N^k(N+1)^{P_{\eta'}} \qquad(k\ge0\text{ fixed}). \tag{25} \] Every derivative has range in the same subspace \(|0\rangle\otimes\operatorname{span}\{w_1,\ldots,w_d\}\otimes Z\). Its rank is at most \(dN^{m-2}\). Therefore (25) gives \[ \|\partial_\mu^k\mathcal A\|_{S_p} \le (dN^{m-2})^{1/p} C_{m,\eta,\eta',k}N^k(N+1)^{P_{\eta'}}. \tag{26} \] At \(\mu=0\), the spectator scalar has modulus one, and the sharper root estimates are \[ \|\mathcal A_0\|\le N/2,\qquad \|\mathcal A_0\|_{S_p}\le(dN^{m-2})^{1/p}N/2, \qquad \|\mathcal A_0\|_1\le N^m/2. \tag{27} \] Also \(Q_{\rm top}\) has rank \(N^{m-2}\) and norm \(|M|^{-(m-2)d}\). These statements include the empty spectator case. There is no Laurent pole at \(\mu=0\) in either source coupon or in \(\mathcal A\). For an analytic marked matrix \(C(M)\), write \(Y=[E_\Sigma,C]\) and \(\Delta=\Phi_M(C)-\operatorname{Tr}(Q_{\rm top}C)\). Trace duality gives the actual current bounds \[ \begin{split} |\Delta|&\le C_{m,\eta'}(N+1)^{P_{\eta'}}\|Y\|_1,\\ |\Delta|&\le C_{m,\eta'}N^{m-1}(N+1)^{P_{\eta'}}\|Y\|,\\ |\Delta|&\le C_{m,\eta'}N^{(m-1)/2}(N+1)^{P_{\eta'}}\|Y\|_2. \end{split}\tag{28} \] At the root the respective factors may instead be taken as \(N/2\), \(N^m/2\), and \((N/2)(dN^{m-2})^{1/2}\). For fixed \(k\), the product rule and (25) give, on the smaller disk, \[ N^{-k}|\partial_\mu^k\Delta| \le C_{m,\eta,\eta',k}(N+1)^{P_{\eta'}} \sum_{\ell=0}^kN^{-\ell}\|\partial_\mu^\ell Y\|_1. \tag{29} \] The operator-norm version has the extra factor \(N^{m-1}\), and the Hilbert--Schmidt version the extra factor \(N^{(m-1)/2}\). All quantities are full finite matrices in the stated metric. An \(O(N^{-k})\) current can therefore suffice for an absolute error after paying the displayed powers; its order, scalar normalization, and the desired error scale must be checked. A small normalized coherent kernel is not by itself a bound for any norm in (28). For example, suppose at the root that \(L_N\ne0\), \(\operatorname{Tr}(Q_{{\rm top},0}C_N)=L_N(1+o(1))\), and the actual trace-norm current satisfies \[ \|[E_{\Sigma,0},C_N]\|_1\le\varepsilon_N|L_N|/N. \tag{29a} \] Then (27) proves \(\Phi_{M=1}(C_N)=L_N(1+o(1)+O(\varepsilon_N))\). In particular a bound \(|L_N|N^{-2}\) for this current contributes relative error \(O(N^{-1})\). The operator-norm version requires \(\|[E_{\Sigma,0},C_N]\|\le\varepsilon_N|L_N|N^{-m}\). Thus this comparison has polynomial, rather than exponential, norm loss. The assumed norm control is a substantial input; the statement does not assert it for a geometric localization or after a coherent contraction. An outside scalar multiplies both compared terms and retains its derivatives. ## 5. The true first normal and exact scope For explicit first jets, set \[ \Sigma_{a,N}=\sum_{j=1}^a\frac{Q^j}{1-Q^j},\qquad \mathcal H_{12}=-2J_1-J_2-2\Sigma_{J_1,N}-2\Sigma_{J_2,N}. \tag{30} \] F's exact derivative of (16) gives \(\left.\partial_\mu\mathcal D_{12}(e^\mu)\right|_0=\mathcal H_{12}\). Differentiating (19),(21) in the actual fixed-\(q\) family proves \[ \mathcal A_1= \bigl([\mathcal H_{12},\mathcal A_{12,0}] -(d+N(m-2))\mathcal A_{12,0}\bigr)\otimes K_{Z,0}^{-N}. \tag{31} \] Subscripts 0 and 1 denote value and \(\partial_\mu\) at zero. The two pivot derivatives are \(Q_{{\rm pt},1}=-d(m-1)Q_{{\rm pt},0}\) and \(Q_{{\rm top},1}=-d(m-2)Q_{{\rm top},0}\). Put \[ Y_0=[E_{\Sigma,0},C_0],\qquad Y_1=[E_{\Sigma,1},C_0]+[E_{\Sigma,0},C_1]. \tag{32} \] The complete first-normal source identity is \[ \begin{split} \operatorname{Tr}Q_{{\rm pt},0}(C_1-d(m-1)C_0) &=\operatorname{Tr}Q_{{\rm top},0}(C_1-d(m-2)C_0)\\ &\quad+\operatorname{Tr}(\mathcal A_1Y_0+\mathcal A_0Y_1). \end{split}\tag{33} \] Higher fixed jets use (6) directly. They require only the corresponding actual derivatives of \(C,E_\Sigma,\mathcal A\), with no extra Laurent coefficient. Any retained outside scalar is differentiated as well. If \(C(M)\) commutes with \(E_\Sigma(M)\) throughout the meridian family, all current terms vanish. Root-only commutation eliminates \(Y_0\) but does not eliminate \(Y_1\). Thus the top coefficient agrees with the original source on actual total intertwiners, and for arbitrary marked matrices its discrepancy is one explicit polynomially bounded Ward functional. This is a source comparison, not an assertion that a chosen geometric window has a small current. It neither constructs such a window nor supplies a geometric relative-cycle coefficient, a relative phase comparison, or a nonzero closed-source lower bound. The separate opposite- polarization return is not identified with this two-head primitive. No new volume-conjecture case follows from these identities alone. ## Complete proof direct and verification record * F: `notes/research_actual_meridian_source_frames.md`, 506 lines, SHA256 `6f58fba195ba5e8208e1d5180a1d684b933f9f5d50eb28efc56609580fe29976`. The complete direct was freshly read nontruncated in three covering chunks during this author sequence. All used identities and bounds were checked, including the original pivot and the actual bottom-zero meridian frame. The new two-head proof does not use an estimate for a general commutator inverse. Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used; no mathematical programs or numerical tests were run. Frozen and public sources were not edited. The entire final was freshly reread nontruncated after the last presentation corrections; its sole direct pin was renewed and matched.

title: The transverse Hessian of the actual soft-cut braid phase
text: # The transverse Hessian of the actual soft-cut braid phase Private written proof, 18 November 2026. Under an actual positive complete ideal gluing certificate, the geometric critical germ of the literal soft-cut braid phase is smooth of dimension one. In its independent occupation coordinates the Hessian has precisely the residual framing direction as kernel. The common momentum has already been quotiented in passing to those coordinates; it is not a further variable to remove from the phase. This applies to every fixed finite braid of a one-cusped hyperbolic knot exterior supplied with the stated certificate. Existence of such a positive triangulation for every hyperbolic knot is not assumed. The result is a local complex Hessian theorem. It does not compute the residual framing period or any physical cycle coefficient. The complete proof directs are M (the actual crossing/representation scheme), S (the soft-cut ideal), R (marked positive gluing rigidity), and F (the complex-cut and common slit frame), pinned below. The incidence-coordinate and gradient-scheme adapter is proved here. ## 1. The actual phase and the theorem Fix a finite braid of the knot with \(c\) crossings, counting both signs positively. Its closed crossing graph has \(c\) vertices and \(2c\) oriented wire arcs. Put \[ \Lambda=\ker(L:\mathbb Z^{2c}\longrightarrow\mathbb Z^c), \tag{1} \] where \(L\) has incoming coefficient \(+1\) and outgoing coefficient \(-1\). Each crossing has two incoming and two outgoing arcs. Loops are allowed. The graph is connected and has rank \(c-1\); therefore \(\Lambda\) is free of rank \(m=c+1\). Choosing a spanning tree makes its chord occupations an integral basis: the tree occupations are recovered uniquely by leaf elimination. The cut edge may be a chord, since the oriented knot is an Euler circuit and that edge is not an undirected bridge. Use unwrapped logarithmic occupations \(\zeta_e\), so the local wire space is the linear space \[ W=\ker(L:\mathbb C^{2c}\longrightarrow\mathbb C^c). \tag{2} \] Choose chord coordinates \(z_1,\ldots,z_m\) on \(W\). Every signed transfer is its original difference of wire positions. There is no additional independent transfer variable after this linear matching is imposed. Keep M's literal signed principal crossing expressions, all original pivots and framing, and a trace-one complex-binomial cut as in F. Write \(c_0=2\pi i\), \(u=\zeta_{\rm cut}\), and \[ \Phi_\theta=S_0+g_\theta(u)-c_0\sum_{j=1}^m n_jz_j, \tag{3} \] \[ g_\theta(u)=c_0\!\left[-t\log t-(1-t)\log(1-t) +t\log\theta+(1-t)\log(1-\theta)\right], \qquad t=u/c_0. \tag{4} \] The logs are the matching sheets near \(\theta=1/2\), with \(\theta\ne0,1\). The fixed integers \(n_j\) are the actual local Fourier correction which makes the derivative vanish at the chosen exponentiated critical point. It changes neither the finite lattice values nor the Hessian. At \(\theta=1/2\), this is S's real-binomial cut. F permits nearby complex \(\theta\) and supplies regular geometric slit frames there. Its exact cut current and exponential cost remain unchanged. Suppose the actual exterior has R's marked positive complete ideal gluing certificate. Fix its complete oriented holonomy, the original central lift, and the selected peripheral eigenflag, with the meridian eigenvalue fixed exactly to its complete value. Take a regular source chart as supplied by S/F and choose the compatible logarithmic lift in (3). Then, near the corresponding geometric point \(z_*\), \[ \operatorname{Crit}(\Phi_\theta) \text{ is smooth of dimension }1,\qquad \ker\Phi_\theta''(z_*)=T_{z_*}\operatorname{Crit}(\Phi_\theta). \tag{5} \] Consequently the \(m\)-variable Hessian has rank \(m-1=c\). The surviving tangent is the actual \(r\)-framing direction. The assertions hold on a sufficiently small neighborhood of any such chosen frame and cut parameter, not uniformly over all braids. ## 2. Crossing momenta and the exact incidence adapter At one positive crossing, write the input log positions \(a,b\) and the transfer \(n\); the output log positions are \(b+n,a-n\). At a negative crossing they are \(b-n,a+n\). These are linear coordinates on the three-dimensional conservation hyperplane. M's exact generating identities, in the factorial basis, say \[ dS_v=\sum_{\rm out}\pi_{v,e}\,d\zeta_e -\sum_{\rm in}\pi_{v,e}\,d\zeta_e, \qquad \pi_{v,e}=\log p_{v,e}, \tag{6} \] on that hyperplane, with the external meridian fixed. They are precisely the actual canonical crossing graph, for both signs. In particular M's explicit rational inverse proves the equality on local Artin algebras, where all chart denominators remain units. Multiplying every momentum at this crossing by one common scalar does not change (6). Conversely (6) determines its four log momenta up to that one common additive constant. The annihilator of the conservation hyperplane is the one-dimensional span of its defining linear form. Thus two coefficient lists in (6) differ exactly by the same addition to every \(\pi_{v,e}\). This is true over each local Artin algebra as well. No local momentum equation is lost: M's three derivative identities recover its three independent momentum ratios and its regular signed crossing correspondence. For clarity, one can implement the gluing entirely linearly. Extend each \(S_v\) holomorphically off its conservation hyperplane by a fixed linear retraction. Its four partial derivatives give one choice of the signed momenta in (6); any other choice adds a vertex constant \(\lambda_v\). On an arc from one crossing to the next, let \[ R_e=\pi_{{\rm out},e}-\pi_{{\rm in},e} +g_\theta'(u)\,1_{e={\rm cut}}. \tag{7} \] The retained pivotal linear terms can be included in this coefficient list. Their logarithmic multipliers are fixed integer turns; they do not alter the following linear argument or its Hessian. The compatible Fourier correction fixes the same local additive constants. More explicitly, extend the integer covector \(n\) from the chord basis to the wire space by using its coefficients on the chord edges and zero on the tree edges. Assign each resulting linear term to one incident crossing. Subtracting it from that local primitive changes its half-edge log momentum by an integer multiple of \(c_0\), so it does not change its exponentiated canonical graph. We use those local log branches in (7). This realizes the exact corrected derivative in (3), rather than silently dropping a nonzero lattice covector. The pivotal integer turns are treated in the same way. The differential of the total phase, restricted to \(W\), is the restriction of the covector \(R\). Adding the vertex constants changes \(R\) by \(-L^t\lambda\). The exact sequence \[ 0\longrightarrow\mathbb C \longrightarrow\mathbb C^c \mathop{\longrightarrow}^{L^t}\mathbb C^{2c} \longrightarrow W^*\longrightarrow0 \tag{8} \] therefore shows that constrained stationarity is equivalent to being able to set every \(R_e\) equal to zero by local momentum rescalings. Its kernel consists of the one global common rescaling. There is a fixed linear right inverse on \(\operatorname{im}L^t\), obtained by deleting one vertex row and using the same spanning tree. Thus all these constructions commute with extension to local Artin algebras; they are not merely tangent-space arguments. Exponentiated stationarity gives the same germ after its prescribed integer correction: near zero, \(e^w-1=w\) times a holomorphic unit. Local logs of all momenta and chart functions are available because they are units at the chosen point. Equation (8) proves an isomorphism of the actual gradient scheme in the \(m=c+1\) chord variables with the glued canonical-graph scheme modulo the single common momentum. This resolves the coordinate count. The enlarged graph keeps local momenta and their one global scale; the chord phase has already eliminated that scale. Removing another phase variable as a “common momentum quotient” would be incorrect. ## 3. The soft cut leaves exactly one framing parameter On every noncut arc (7) is ordinary momentum matching. On the cut it is \[ \frac{p_{\rm out}}{p_{\rm in}} =e^{-g_\theta'(u)} =\frac{1-\theta}{\theta}\frac{u}{c_0-u}. \tag{9} \] S's ordered-coproduct ideal calculation applies to precisely these internal rows. Closure on the other strands and the preserved total \(K,E,F\) force the cut \(K,e,f\) to close. On the stated unit chart this also forces \(p_{\rm out}=p_{\rm in}\). Hence the ideal of (9) is exactly \[ (u-c_0\theta). \tag{10} \] F proves the same assertion for the complex probe, without discarding its finite-source current. Conversely a full braid fixed point satisfying (10) obeys all these weighted rows. Quotient the one common momentum by setting the cut momentum to one. M's explicit formula then puts its selected eigenflag at \(1=(1,1)^t\), with the exact inverse eigenvalue convention. Its rational Gauss inverse and Hurwitz identities give an isomorphism, including on Artin test rings, with the selected-flag framed knot representation germ. These are actual braid-closure relations, not only equations for peripheral eigenvalues. For the one-cusped positive certificate, R identifies the decorated representation germ modulo simultaneous \(\operatorname{PGL}_2\) with a smooth one-dimensional germ whose coordinate is the marked meridian similarity log. Fixing that log exactly to zero makes this unframed germ a point, also on local Artin algebras. The fixed eigenvalue condition matters: an unspecified invariant flag of a parabolic can have an infinitesimal motion, which R explicitly excludes by retaining the exact eigencharacter. Complete holonomy is irreducible, and its knot meridians are noncentral parabolics with nonzero trace in the retained lift. A projective centralizer element, lifted to a matrix, conjugates each lifted meridian to itself up to sign. Its nonzero trace forces the sign to be plus. The meridians generate the group, so this matrix commutes with the entire irreducible representation and is scalar: a nonscalar commuting matrix would give a common invariant eigenline. The projective centralizer is therefore trivial. M consequently identifies the remaining framed germ with a smooth open part of the two-dimensional group \[ B_1=\operatorname{Stab}_{\operatorname{PGL}_2}(1). \tag{11} \] This statement uses both the Artin-scheme comparison and R's rigidity; no dimension count replaces either. Its explicit local coordinates are \[ F(r,s)=\begin{pmatrix}r&1-r\\s&-s\end{pmatrix},\qquad F^{-1}J_1F=\begin{pmatrix}1+s&-s\\s&1-s\end{pmatrix}, \quad A_{\rm cut}=(1+s)^{-1}. \tag{12} \] On the matching log sheet, \[ u=-\Log(1+s),\qquad du=-\frac{ds}{1+s}. \tag{13} \] Near the midpoint \(s=-2\), this differential is a unit in the \(s\)-direction. For a nearby complex \(\theta\), (10) is therefore precisely \[ s=e^{-c_0\theta}-1, \tag{14} \] leaving the free coordinate \(r\). The derivative remains a unit and \(s\ne0\) on this neighborhood. Thus the actual gradient scheme of Section 2 is smooth of dimension one. The common momentum is distinct from \(r\): the former diagonally changes the chosen eigenflag coordinate, whereas the latter conjugates the other holonomies by the stabilizer of the now fixed noncentral cut meridian. ## 4. Hessian and a transverse holomorphic normal form The defining ideal in chord coordinates is generated by the actual marked derivatives of \(\Phi_\theta\). Its Zariski tangent space is therefore the kernel of the Hessian, before any reducedness assumption. Section 3 proves that this scheme is reduced and smooth of dimension one. This proves (5), including exclusion of further infinitesimal null directions. The coordinate \(r\) gives its entire tangent, not a presumed redundant equation. There is a holomorphic Morse--Bott normal form, if desired without importing a stationary-phase assertion. Choose local coordinates \((r,y_1,\ldots,y_{m-1})\) flattening the smooth critical curve to \(y=0\). Its phase value is constant along that curve, since the full differential vanishes there. The Hessian on the normal \(y\)-space is invertible. Taylor's integral formula gives \[ \Phi_\theta(r,y)-\Phi_\theta(r,0) =\tfrac12 y^t A(r,y)y \tag{15} \] with \(A\) holomorphic, symmetric and invertible near the point. A constant complex congruence makes \(A\) equal to the identity at that point. On a smaller neighborhood its convergent matrix binomial square root is symmetric and holomorphic; setting \(Y=A(r,y)^{1/2}y\) is an invertible holomorphic coordinate change. Consequently \[ \Phi_\theta=\Phi_\theta(z_*)+ \tfrac12\sum_{j=1}^{m-1}Y_j^2. \tag{16} \] The free coordinate \(r\) remains. Rescaling to normalized occupation variables or multiplying the phase by the nonzero physical constant \(1/(2\pi i)\) does not change the corank. This applies to the full chord/transfer phase used in an oblique residue presentation; it is not a Hessian of an additional coherent occupation sum. ## 5. Scope and complete source pins The conditional “if the old framing kernel has dimension two” in S is now discharged for the stated positive-certificate braid source. The related two-framing result for a different augmented-plat source already appears in its critical-scheme coverage; it is not used as a substitute for Section 2 here. The positivity hypothesis concerns the supplied complete triangulation of the actual exterior. The local braid shapes need not themselves be positive. No positive triangulation is asserted for every knot. No real-contour negativity, finite-\(N\) gauge quotient, nonzero \(r\)-period, physical intersection number or scalar asymptotic follows from (16). All original cut, pivot, framing and support currents remain. * M: notes/marked_braid_holonomy.md, SHA256 eff47c757d0e44bda0c396c094315b8e1fce11f1fc2d6445d636c6d2d3a46c4f. * S: notes/research_soft_binomial_cut_stationary_source.md, SHA256 667cb1eb70b770552de05e6f95f518016852b2c0aecdc874c3dff167fccb3d8b. * R: notes/general_marked_multicusp_gluing_rigidity.md, SHA256 f882d2c7d1f723590391d3cc03dcd9bba7a12d13c2e006c6dea570e1b4af1b42. * F: notes/research_literal_factorial_common_slit_frame.md, SHA256 9764a2b77469c7fad402b9b8e609b304a79083bde18fb139031c06fd93650ca8. All four complete sources were read nontruncated in the active author sequence; unchanged complete reads were retained where applicable, their used implications checked and matching pins renewed. The incidence adapter and normal-form argument above are written proofs. No mathematical programs or tests were run, and frozen/public files are unchanged.

title: Relative homology and compact periods in a positive gluing chart
text:
# Relative homology and compact periods in a positive gluing chart Research proof, 23 November 2026. A supplied positive critical point determines the entire ordinary relative homology of its positive logarithmic chart above a sufficiently high sublevel. There is one compact Legendre disk, and its coefficient in any finite relative cycle is an explicit angle-projection degree. For a holomorphic growing period this gives its full leading term, including the retained density and this integer coefficient. This is a statement about finite chains in one fixed marked chart. It does not provide such a representative for an original quantum source, or identify its cut, lip or infinite boundary currents. ## 1. The marked potential and its radial minimum Let \(t\geq1\), \(\Theta=(0,\pi)^t\), and write \[ X=\{x=ho+i	heta:ho\in\mathbb R^t,\ 	heta\in\Theta\}, \qquad P=P^{\mathsf T}\in M_t(\mathbb R),\qquad u=a+ib. 	ag{1} \] Use the principal upper-half-plane branches in \[ S(x)=\sum_j\operatorname{Li}_2(e^{x_j}) +	frac12x^{\mathsf T}Px-u^{\mathsf T}x, \quad v(x)=-\operatorname{Log}(1-e^x),\quad h=\Im S. 	ag{2} \] Thus \(S_x=v(x)+Px-u\). Suppose a positive critical point \(x_*=ho_*+i	heta_*\in X\) is supplied. The fixed affine target, quad choices and all logarithmic windings are part of (2). In the gluing application [G] supplies exactly this potential after positive quad selection. No existence assertion is implicit in this hypothesis. Put \[  eta(	heta)=b-P	heta,\qquad \gamma(	heta)=\pi\mathbf1-	heta- eta(	heta),\qquad \mathcal P=\{	heta\in\Theta: eta>0,\ \gamma>0\}. 	ag{3} \] This is a convex open polytope. At the critical point \( eta_* =\Im v(x_*)\), and \(\gamma_* =\pi\mathbf1-	heta_*-\Im v(x_*)\); both are positive. Indeed \(z\) and \(z/(1-z)\) are in the upper half-plane, so the three indicated arguments are the angles of their positive triangle. In particular \(	heta_*\in\mathcal P\). Direct differentiation gives \[  egin{split} h(ho,	heta) &=\sum_j\Im\operatorname{Li}_2(e^{ho_j+i	heta_j}) -ho^{\mathsf T} eta-a^{\mathsf T}	heta,\ D&=\operatorname{diag}_j\Im v'(x_j)>0,\qquad \Im v'(x_j)= rac{\Im(e^{x_j})}{|1-e^{x_j}|^2},\ h_{hoho}&=D,\qquad h_{	heta	heta}=-D. \end{split} 	ag{4} \] For fixed \(	heta\in\mathcal P\), the derivative \(h_{ho_j}=\Im v(x_j)- eta_j\) increases from \(- eta_j\) to \(\gamma_j\) as \(ho_j\) runs from \(-\infty\) to \(+\infty\). Consequently its unique global radial minimum is \[ ho_{L,j}(	heta)=\log rac{\sin eta_j(	heta)} {\sin\gamma_j(	heta)}, \qquad x_L(	heta)=ho_L(	heta)+i	heta. 	ag{5} \] The formula follows from the sine rule, or by substitution in \(\operatorname{Arg}(1-e^{x_j})=- eta_j\). It is smooth on \(\mathcal P\), and \(ho_L(	heta_*)=ho_*\). For \(z_j=e^{x_{L,j}}\), the Bloch--Wigner identity yields \[ H(	heta):=h(x_L(	heta)) =\sum_j D_{\mathrm{BW}}(z_j)-a^{\mathsf T}	heta. 	ag{6} \] The real peripheral tilt in (6) is retained. The sum is a calibrated hyperbolic volume only in an application supplying that calibration; neither an imaginary additive constant nor this tilt is discarded. For completeness, let \(S_{xx}=K+iD\), with \(K=K^{\mathsf T}\) real. The real Hessian and its radial Schur complement are \[ \operatorname{Hess}h= egin{pmatrix}D&K\K&-D\end{pmatrix},\quad ho'_L=-D^{-1}K,\quad H''=-D-KD^{-1}K<0,\quad J_L:=x'_L=-D^{-1}K+iI=-D^{-1}\overline{S_{xx}}. 	ag{7} \] These formulas are the Legendre calculation of [L], equally valid for complex \(u\). The matrix \(J_L\) is invertible: a complex symmetric matrix with positive imaginary part has trivial kernel. Thus \(H\) is strictly concave, with its unique maximum \(h_*:=H(	heta_*)=h(x_*)\). ## 2. A cutoff retracts the whole pair Define the fixed-radius height \(f(	heta)=h(ho_*,	heta)\). It is strictly concave on all of \(\Theta\), stationary at \(	heta_*\), and extends continuously to \([0,\pi]^t\). Here the dilogarithms have their upper-side boundary values; their values remain continuous even when a boundary shape equals \(1\). Every other point of this closed cube has strictly smaller height. To see the boundary assertion, restrict to a segment from \(	heta_*\): its derivative starts at zero and is strictly decreasing at every interior point. Its endpoint limit is therefore strictly smaller than its value at the center. Choose levels \[ c_0<c<h_*,\qquad \{	heta\in\Theta:f(	heta)\geq c_0\} \Subset\mathcal P. 	ag{8} \] Such levels exist by compactness of the closed cube and \(	heta_*\in\mathcal P\). Choose a smooth cutoff \(0\leq\chi\leq1\) depending only on \(f\), equal to zero for \(f\leq c_0\) and to one for \(f\geq c\). Set \[ ho_0(	heta)=ho_*+\chi(	heta)(ho_L(	heta)-ho_*),\quad A_c=\{x\in X:h(x)\leq c\},\quad R_s(ho,	heta)=((1-s)ho+sho_0(	heta),	heta). 	ag{9} \] Outside \(\mathcal P\) define \(ho_0=ho_*\). This is a smooth global definition because the support of \(\chi\) is compact in \(\mathcal P\). The maps \(R_s\) strongly retract \(X\) onto its graph; we now verify that they preserve \(A_c\). If \(f(	heta)\geq c\), the target \(ho_0=ho_L\) is the global radial minimum. If \(f(	heta)<c\), radial convexity and \(H(	heta)\leq f(	heta)\) show \(h(ho_0,	heta)\leq f(	heta)<c\); outside \(\mathcal P\) this is the definition of \(ho_0\). Thus a starting point of \(A_c\) always has its target in \(A_c\). Radial convexity proves the same for the whole joining segment. This proves a strong deformation retraction of pairs, not just of two reference chains. Moreover, \[ h(ho_0(	heta),	heta)>c \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 	heta\in\Omega_c:=\{	heta\in\mathcal P:H(	heta)>c\}. 	ag{10} \] Indeed a high graph point must have \(f\geq c\), hence lies on the Legendre graph; conversely \(H>c\) implies \(f>c\) and \(\chi=1\). The graph pair is therefore \((\Theta,\Theta\setminus\Omega_c)\). Notice also that (9) preserves every sublevel \(h\leq d\) for \(d\geq c\). It need not decrease height monotonically below \(c\). Strict concavity makes \(\Omega_c\) convex and nonempty. Since \(H\leq f\), its closure lies compactly inside \(\mathcal P\). It is exactly \(K_c=\{H\geq c\}\): every level point can be approached along its segment to \(	heta_*\) from higher values. On \(H=c\), the gradient is nonzero, since the only stationary point is \(	heta_*\). Thus \(K_c\) is a smooth convex closed \(t\)-ball, and \(\partial K_c=\{H=c\}\). Clamp each ray from \(	heta_*\) to its intersection with \(\partial K_c\), leaving points of \(K_c\) fixed. Linear interpolation of the radial distance gives a strong deformation of \((\Theta,\Theta\setminus\Omega_c)\) onto \((K_c,\partial K_c)\). It stays in \(\Theta\) by convexity; a point outside \(\Omega_c\) remains outside until it reaches \(\partial K_c\). The radial intersection depends continuously and smoothly on direction, since \(K_c\) is smooth and contains \(	heta_*\) in its interior. Combining this clamp with (9) proves \[ (X,A_c)\simeq (K_c,\partial K_c),\qquad H_j(X,A_c;\mathbb Z)=  egin{cases}\mathbb Z,&j=t,\0,&j
e t.\end{cases} 	ag{11} \] The compact disk \(\Gamma_c=x_L(K_c)\), with its standard \(	heta\)-orientation, is a generator, and its boundary has height exactly \(c\). All homology here uses ordinary finite singular chains. In particular no noncompact end is filled by this calculation. ## 3. Its coefficient is an angle-projection degree For every \(ho\), radial minimality at \(	heta_*\) gives \(h(ho,	heta_*)\geq h_*>c\). Hence angle projection is a map of pairs \[ \pi:(X,A_c)\longrightarrow (\Theta,\Theta\setminus\{	heta_*\}),\qquad \pi(ho+i	heta)=	heta. 	ag{12} \] It sends \([\Gamma_c]\) to the positive local fundamental class at \(	heta_*\). Both groups in degree \(t\) are \(\mathbb Z\), so \(\pi_*\) is an isomorphism. Consequently every finite relative cycle \(\Gamma\) has the exact coefficient formula \[ [\Gamma]=k[\Gamma_c],\qquad k=\deg_{	heta_*}(\pi\Gamma)\in\mathbb Z. 	ag{13} \] This degree means the induced local relative homology class. For smooth transverse chains it is the signed count of intersections with \(\{	heta=	heta_*\}\), counting the sign of the angle projection on each oriented chain. This convention fixes the intersection orientation without an additional ambient sign. Since \(X\) is contractible and \(t\geq1\), every compact closed \(t\)-cycle in \(X\) has zero class in (11). A nonzero generator therefore needs a relative boundary in \(A_c\), or separately controlled ends followed by a justified truncation. An entire compact closed quantum cycle cannot simply be placed in this unpunctured chart and assigned degree one. ## 4. The resulting compact-period formula Let \(\Gamma\) be a finite piecewise-smooth relative \(t\)-cycle in \((X,A_c)\). The retractions above and finite-chain homology in the ball give compact piecewise-smooth chains \(B,R\) with \[ \Gamma-k\Gamma_c=\partial B+R,\qquad \operatorname{supp}R\subset A_c. 	ag{14} \] One can triangulate the compact homotopies and the ball filling to obtain these chains. The clamp is smooth on either side of its boundary, so this needs only piecewise-smooth chains. Equivalently use smooth approximation relative to the regular level \(h=c\). Suppose, on a neighborhood of these compact chains, the actual forms are holomorphic top forms \[ \omega_N=N^\mu e^{NS(x)/(2\pi i)}a_N(x)\,dx_1\cdots dx_t. 	ag{15} \] Assume \(a_N\) is polynomially bounded on that neighborhood, and \(a_N=a_0+O(N^{-1})\) uniformly holomorphically near \(x_*\), where \(a_0(x_*)
e0\). Holomorphic top forms are closed. Stokes and (14) give the exact identity and the bound \[ \int_\Gamma\omega_N =k\int_{\Gamma_c}\omega_N+\int_R\omega_N, \qquad \left|\int_R\omega_Night| \leq N^C e^{Nc/(2\pi)}. 	ag{16} \] The constant includes the finite volume of \(R\). No independent bound on a noncompact homotopy or on its ends is used. Write \(\varphi(	heta)=S(x_L(	heta))/(2\pi i)\). At the center \(\varphi'=0\) and \[ \mathcal H=-\varphi''(	heta_*),\qquad \Re\mathcal H=-H''(	heta_*)/(2\pi)>0,\qquad C_*=(2\pi)^{t/2}  rac{a_0(x_*)\det J_L(	heta_*)}{\sqrt{\det\mathcal H}}
e0. 	ag{17} \] The square root is the Gaussian branch on matrices with positive real part; the orientation is the stated \(	heta\)-orientation. Strict concavity gives a fixed height gap outside every small neighborhood of \(	heta_*\) in \(K_c\). Taylor expansion there, Gaussian rescaling and the positive real Hessian in (17) give \[ \int_\Gamma\omega_N =k\,C_* N^{\mu-t/2}e^{NS(x_*)/(2\pi i)}(1+O(N^{-1})) +O(N^C e^{Nc/(2\pi)}). 	ag{18} \] The local estimate uses the uniform holomorphic expansion of the amplitude; its derivative bounds follow on a smaller neighborhood by Cauchy estimates. Odd Gaussian terms integrate to zero, and the remaining Taylor error is \(O(N^{-1})\). The complement is exponentially smaller by the fixed height gap. Thus if \(k
e0\) the period has its retained nonzero leading constant. If \(k=0\), (16) instead gives the lower sublevel bound directly. ## 5. What this does and does not assemble [L] constructs the Legendre chain and controlled homotopies of specified reference chains. Here the cutoff controls the whole positive-chart pair and computes the coefficient of every finite relative chain by (13); (18) then assembles its compact period. The argument works for the tilted height in (6), without assuming purely imaginary peripheral targets or using a descent flow. It does not show that an original Kashaev cycle, with its actual amplitude and closing row, has a representative satisfying these hypotheses. Quantum divisors, cut banks, finite flat faces and noncompact ends may supply additional chains outside this pair. Their actual marks and boundary currents must be retained. Different logarithmic windings give different potentials, not additional classes silently identified by (11). No source degree, scalar lower bound for a knot, or finite-exception theorem follows without the corresponding original-source construction. ## Complete direct sources - [L] [Global Legendre contour](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/general_legendre_rivin_contour.md), 421 lines, SHA-256 `b51be11036b05fbccd586c2d0a4505559631870357cf128dd256dcc87e26970b`: the off-critical Legendre identity, Hessian and local period calculation. The whole-pair and projection-degree arguments are supplied above. - [G] [Positive gluing gradient bound](research_positive_gluing_gradient_escape_bound.md), 226 lines, SHA-256 `60de078745893f5f3bb2b9491a974cc31cfe99bf54000d99f77672c374d5c779`: the actual marked potential and positive quad convention. Its gradient-flow conclusion is not a premise of (9)--(18).

title: Positive edge geometry and global uniqueness of the filling equations
text:
# Positive edge geometry and global uniqueness of the filling equations Research note, 2 November 2026. The eight original tetrahedra of a circle-tree edge determine a domain on which its peripheral-period map is globally strictly monotone. This statement compares any two points of the domain; it does not require the segment between them to remain positive. Summing the comparison over the original graph proves uniqueness of a positive solution of the primitive filling equations, for arbitrary signed powers. Existence is a different question. The last section identifies what can obstruct continuation of the positive solution. Neither uniqueness nor existence by itself determines the coefficient of its cycle in the original quantum period. ## 1. The original shapes in rational coordinates Retain the notation of [the Hessian calculation](research_cone_chamber_accretivity.md): \[ a=	an(t/2),\qquad b=	an(u/2),\qquad q^2=1+a^2+b^2, \qquad q(0,0)=1. 	ag{1} \] The original meridian increments are \[ r_t=\operatorname{arsinh} igl(	an(t/2)\cos(u/2) igr), \qquad r_u=\operatorname{arsinh} igl(	an(u/2)\cos(t/2) igr). 	ag{2} \] They satisfy \(\psi_t=-r_t/\pi\) and \(\psi_u=-r_u/\pi\). All logarithms initially vanish at completeness. Their global positive branches will be specified below. The ordered cross-ratio calculation in Section 3 of [the adjacent-pair geometry note](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_adjacent_two_crossing_pair.md) gives the eight original shapes as \[ (A,B,-1/A,-1/B),\qquad(C,D,-1/C,-1/D). 	ag{3} \] The four distinct expressions have the following rational form: \[ A= rac{q+a}{b-i},\qquad C= rac{q-a}{b-i},\qquad B=- rac{q-b}{a+i},\qquad D=- rac{q+b}{a+i}. 	ag{4} \] To check the conventions, the original formulas are \(A=i e^{r_t}e^{-iu/2}\), \(C=i e^{-r_t}e^{-iu/2}\), \(B=i e^{it/2}e^{-r_u}\), and \(D=i e^{it/2}e^{r_u}\). The identities \(e^{r_t}=\cos(u/2)(q+a)\), \(e^{r_u}=\cos(t/2)(q+b)\), and \((q-a)(q+a)=1+b^2\) give (4). Every expression is \(i\) at completeness. Thus these are the original oriented tetrahedra, with the original two-octahedron subdivision. Throughout the proof a positive shape means a shape with strictly positive imaginary part. Since \(z\mapsto-1/z\) preserves the upper half-plane, positivity of (3) is equivalent to positivity of the four expressions in (4). ## 2. Positivity is an exact matrix inequality Put \[ L= egin{pmatrix}q+a&b\b&q-a\end{pmatrix}, \qquad \det L=1. 	ag{5} \] For a complex symmetric matrix, \(\Re L\) is both its entrywise real part and its Hermitian part. **Theorem 1.** At a regular configuration in (1)--(4), all eight original tetrahedra are positive if and only if \[ \Re L>0, \quad\hbox{equivalently}\quad \Re q>\sqrt{(\Re a)^2+(\Re b)^2}. 	ag{6} \] This is also equivalent to \(\Re[-2\pi\psi''(t,u)]>0\) on the branch continued from the positive complete configuration. **Proof.** Write \(r=q+a\) and \[ k=(\Re r)(\Im b)-(\Im r)(\Re b). \] The determinant identity in (5) gives \(q-a=(1+b^2)/r\). In particular \(C=(b+i)/r\). Direct division in (4) gives \[ \Im A= rac{\Re r-k}{|b-i|^2}, \qquad \Im C= rac{\Re r+k}{|r|^2}. 	ag{7} \] Also \[ \det(\Re L)=  rac{(\Re r)^2-k^2}{|r|^2}. 	ag{8} \] For completeness, write \(r=x+iy\), \(b=B+iD\). Then \[ |r|^2\left[x\,\Re rac{1+b^2}{r}-B^2ight] =x^2-(xD-yB)^2, \] which is (8). Equations (7)--(8) show that \(A,C\) are both positive exactly when the first diagonal entry of \(\Re L\) and its determinant are positive. This is equivalent to \(\Re L>0\). Applying the same calculation with \((a,b)\) replaced by \((-b,-a)\) gives \(B,D\). The real matrices in the two calculations have the same eigenvalues \[ \Re q\ \pm\sqrt{(\Re a)^2+(\Re b)^2}. \] Thus positivity of \(A,C\) also implies positivity of \(B,D\), and proves (6). To compare with the Hessian, write \(P=\Re q\), \(Q=\Im q\), \(X=(\Re a)^2+(\Re b)^2\), \(Y=(\Im a)^2+(\Im b)^2\), and \(Z=(\Re a)(\Im a)+(\Re b)(\Im b)\). The identity \(q^2=1+a^2+b^2\) gives \[ P^2-Q^2=1+X-Y,\qquad PQ=Z. \] Since \(\{\Im(a\overline b)\}^2=XY-Z^2\), it follows that \[ P^2-\{\Im(a\overline b)\}^2 =(P^2-X)(1+X+Q^2). 	ag{9} \] The determinant formula in Proposition 1 of the Hessian note therefore reads \[ \det\Re[-2\pi\psi''] = rac{(P^2-X)(1+X+Q^2)}{|q|^2}. 	ag{10} \] The corresponding trace is \(P(1+|q|^{-2})\). Consequently its real part is positive definite exactly when \(P>\sqrt X\), proving the last assertion. \(\square\) ## 3. Global coordinates: two disks and two strips The Cayley transform of (5) is \[ C_L=(L-I)(L+I)^{-1} = rac1{q+1} egin{pmatrix}a&b\b&-a\end{pmatrix}. 	ag{11} \] The notation \(C_L\) distinguishes this matrix from the tetrahedron shape \(C\). Direct multiplication gives \[ I-C_L^*C_L =4(L+I)^{-*}(\Re L)(L+I)^{-1}. 	ag{12} \] Set \[ \zeta= rac{a+ib}{q+1},\qquad \xi= rac{a-ib}{q+1}. 	ag{13} \] The two eigenvalues of \(C_L^*C_L\) are \(|\zeta|^2,|\xi|^2\): its equal diagonal entries are \((|a|^2+|b|^2)/|q+1|^2\), and the off-diagonal entry is \((\overline a b-\overline b a)/|q+1|^2\). Thus (6) is exactly \[ |\zeta|<1,\qquad|\xi|<1. 	ag{14} \] Conversely, any pair in these two disks gives \[ q= rac{1+\zeta\xi}{1-\zeta\xi},\qquad a= rac{\zeta+\xi}{1-\zeta\xi},\qquad b= rac{\zeta-\xi}{i(1-\zeta\xi)}. 	ag{15} \] The denominator never vanishes, and (12) proves positivity. This parametrizes the entire positive edge domain, not only a neighborhood of completeness. Now use the principal strip coordinates \[ P=\operatorname{artanh}\zeta,\qquad Q=\operatorname{artanh}\xi,\qquad |\Im P|,|\Im Q|< rac{\pi}{4}. 	ag{16} \] The function \(\operatorname{artanh} z= 	frac12\Log((1+z)/(1-z))\) maps the unit disk bijectively onto this horizontal strip. Define \[ f(P)=\arctan(	anh P). 	ag{17} \] Here the inverse tangent is the analytic branch at zero on the unit disk. It satisfies \[ f'(P)= rac1{\cosh(2P)},\qquad \Re f'(P)>0\quad (|\Im P|<\pi/4). 	ag{18} \] Indeed \(\Re\cosh(2P)=\cosh(2\Re P)\cos(2\Im P)>0\), and taking a reciprocal preserves the sign of the real part. The original angles and meridian increments are exactly \[  egin{aligned} t&=2\{f(P)+f(Q)\},& u&=-2i(P-Q),\ r_t&=P+Q,& r_u&=i\{f(Q)-f(P)\}. \end{aligned} 	ag{19} \] One can verify the angle identities before taking logarithms: \[ e^{it}=  rac{(1+i\zeta)(1+i\xi)} {(1-i\zeta)(1-i\xi)},\qquad e^{iu}=  rac{(1+\zeta)(1-\xi)} {(1-\zeta)(1+\xi)}. 	ag{20} \] All four one-variable factors in these quotients have analytic logarithms on the disks. They fix (19) without an integer ambiguity. Likewise \[ e^{2r_t}= rac{(1+\zeta)(1+\xi)} {(1-\zeta)(1-\xi)},\qquad e^{2r_u}= rac{(1-i\zeta)(1+i\xi)} {(1+i\zeta)(1-i\xi)} \] give the last two identities in (19). These are the branches continued from \(t=u=0\). They satisfy \[ |\Re t|,|\Re u|<\pi,\qquad |\Im r_t|,|\Im r_u|<\pi/2. 	ag{21} \] For example, \(|\Re f(P)|<\pi/4\) because \(f(P)=-i\operatorname{artanh}(i	anh P)\). This proves the first and the last bounds in (21); the other two follow directly from (16). The positive domain in the original \(t,u\) variables is not convex. The two configurations \[ (-4i\log3,0),\qquad (0,-4i\log3) 	ag{22} \] are positive: the nonzero tangent is \(-40i/41\) and \(q=9/41\). At their midpoint, however, \(a=b=-4i/5\) and \(q^2=-7/25\), so (6) is impossible. The strip coordinates, rather than a nonexistent convexity of the \(t,u\) domain, are essential in the following comparison. There is nevertheless a contraction to completeness in the tangent variables. Write \[ X=(\Re a)^2+(\Re b)^2,\quad Y=(\Im a)^2+(\Im b)^2,\quad Z=(\Re a)(\Im a)+(\Re b)(\Im b),\quad D_0^2=XY-Z^2. \] For \(X>0\), condition (6) is equivalent to \(D_0^2<X\). Indeed, writing \(q=P_0+iQ_0\), the identity \[ X-D_0^2=(P_0^2-X)(X+Q_0^2) \] proves the equivalence whenever the positive square root exists. Conversely, \(D_0^2<X\) rules out a nonpositive real value of \(q^2\): such a value would require \(Z=0\) and \(Y\ge1+X\), hence \(D_0^2=XY\ge X\). For \(X=0\), positivity is simply \(Y<1\). Under \((a,b)\mapsto(sa,sb)\), \(0<s\le1\), the first criterion becomes \(s^4D_0^2<s^2X\), and the second becomes \(s^2Y<1\). Both are preserved. Thus simultaneously scaling all original vertex tangents contracts the whole positive network domain to completeness; outside angles zero remain zero. Positive edges exclude the inverse-tangent cuts \(a\in i[1,\infty)\cup-i[1,\infty)\), and similarly for \(b\). For example, if \(\Re a=0\), \(|\Im a|\ge1\), and \(\Re b
e0\), then \(D_0^2\ge X\); if \(\Re b=0\), then \(Y\ge1\). The contraction therefore gives continuous principal angles \(t_v(s)=2\arctan(s	an(t_v/2))\). This fixes a common complete continuation of the positive edge branches on the entire network. The contraction is not generally a path of solutions of fixed filling equations or a path with prescribed cone charges. The original face chart has no further singularity hidden by the simplified shapes. Its coordinates are \[ E= rac{q+i}{q-i},\qquad R= rac{1+b^2}{q^2+1},\qquad R_1=1-R= rac{1+a^2}{q^2+1},\qquad Z_1= rac{q+b}{q-i}. \] On the positive domain, \(q\), \(q\pm i\), \(q\pm a\), and \(q\pm b\) are nonzero: the first follows from \(\Re q>0\), and the last two pairs have positive real parts by (6). The preceding exclusion of the inverse-tangent cuts also gives \(a\pm i,b\pm i
e0\). The additional apex denominators factor as \[ Z_1-R_1= rac{(q+b)(b+i)}{q^2+1},\qquad Z_1-E R_1= rac{(q+b)(b-i)}{(q-i)^2}. \] They are therefore nonzero, as are the corresponding expressions with the endpoints interchanged. Together with the positive shapes, these identities verify that the original ordered face formulas remain regular throughout this continuation. ## 4. Global strict monotonicity of the edge periods **Theorem 2.** Let \((t,u)\) and \((\widetilde t,\widetilde u)\) be any two positive edge configurations, with the canonical branches in (19). Use \(\delta\) to denote the difference of the corresponding quantities. Then \[ \Re\{\delta r_t\,\overline{\delta t} +\delta r_u\,\overline{\delta u}\}>0 	ag{23} \] unless the configurations are identical. **Proof.** For any two points \(P,\widetilde P\) in the convex strip (16), integration along their straight segment and (18) give \[ \Re\{(P-\widetilde P) \overline{f(P)-f(\widetilde P)}\} =|P-\widetilde P|^2 \int_0^1\Re f'(\widetilde P+s(P-\widetilde P))\,ds>0 	ag{24} \] when \(P
e\widetilde P\). The same holds for \(Q\). Substitution of (19) into the left-hand side of (23) gives the exact identity \[  egin{split} &\Re\{\delta r_t\,\overline{\delta t} +\delta r_u\,\overline{\delta u}\}\ &\hspace{8mm}=4\Re\{\delta P\,\overline{\delta f(P)} +\delta Q\,\overline{\delta f(Q)}\}. \end{split} 	ag{25} \] The mixed terms cancel in their real parts. The right side is strictly positive unless both strip coordinates agree. Equations (15) and (19) then show that the edge configurations agree. \(\square\) Thus the period map is globally strictly monotone even though its domain in the original angle coordinates is not convex. The infinitesimal version of (25) recovers the Hessian positivity in Theorem 1. ## 5. Arbitrary original signed filling powers Let \(S\) be any selected set of vertices of the original ordered circle tree. The argument also applies to any finite network of these same edge blocks with the same peripheral concatenation rules. Include each edge incident to \(S\) once, and fix the angles at its outside endpoints. Every selected vertex is assumed incident to at least one edge. Orient each edge only to specify which endpoint is called \(t\) in (19). At a selected vertex define \[ R_v(\mathbf t)=\sum_{e
i v}r_{v,e}(\mathbf t). 	ag{26} \] For the general-network extension this sum is over endpoint incidences: a loop at \(v\) contributes both its endpoint increments, and contributes two to \(d_v\). Original circle trees have no loops. The original primitive filling equations, with real powers \(n_v\) and real cone charges \(c_v\), are \[ R_v(\mathbf t)- rac{i n_v}{2}t_v =-\pi i c_v. 	ag{27} \] For the original integer surgery data, \(n_v=\eta_v-2p_v\), and \[ U_v=2R_v-i\eta_vt_v,\qquad V_v=2it_v,\qquad U_v+p_vV_v=-2\pi i c_v. 	ag{28} \] These are the full marked logarithmic periods, not merely their exponentials. **Theorem 3.** With the outside angles, powers, and charges fixed, equations (27) have at most one solution for which every original edge block is positive on the branches (19). Any such solution has nonsingular complex Jacobian. **Proof.** Suppose that two positive solutions exist. Apply (23) to each edge and sum. At an outside endpoint \(\delta t_v=0\), so its contribution vanishes. At selected vertices the resulting sum is \[ \Re\sum_{v\in S} \delta R_v\,\overline{\delta t_v}. 	ag{29} \] Subtracting (27) gives \(\delta R_v=i n_v\delta t_v/2\). Since \(n_v\) is real, every summand in (29) has zero real part. On the other hand, Theorem 2 makes the sum strictly positive if any edge configuration differs. Hence all edge configurations, and therefore all selected angles, agree. For the Jacobian, each edge derivative is \(H/2\), with positive definite real part by Theorem 1. Insert these matrices in the original vertex coordinates and sum. The real part is positive definite because each selected vertex is incident to an edge. Subtracting \(i\operatorname{diag}(n_v)/2\) leaves that real part unchanged. A complex matrix with positive definite Hermitian part has no nonzero kernel. \(\square\) The assertion permits adjacent selected vertices, arbitrarily many of them, and powers of either sign and any magnitude. It is a theorem about the actual primitive equations in this positive edge decomposition. It does not assert that every hyperbolic filling admits that decomposition with all its original tetrahedra positive. ## 6.
