In particular its normalized value and fixed derivatives have polynomial bounds on our complete bidisk. **Lemma 1.** With fixed buffers for the radii in (4), there is \(c>0\) such that \[ \partial_t^p\partial_u^q \left[H_N(t,u)-e^{-N\psi(t,u)} K_N(-2\cos t,-2\cos u)\right] =O_{p,q}(e^{-cN}) \tag{6} \] uniformly for \(|t|,|u|\le\rho_1\), for every fixed \(p,q\). **Proof.** On the two real seed grids the normalized difference has exponentially small values, because the baseline's actual line data are \(F_a\), and \(F_a(w)=K_N(c_a,w)\) exactly. Both functions in (6) are bounded by \(e^{o(N)}\) on the buffered complete bidisk, by (3) and (5). Apply the two successive dense-grid estimates of the pinned endpoint-role comparison. At the first stage subtract its exponentially small finite sinc correction and use the disk Blaschke product for the remaining exact zeros. Do the same in the second variable. The fixed angular spacing is \(2\pi/N\), rather than \(1/N\); the affine coordinate change (1) gives exactly the same estimate. This yields an exponentially small bound on an open seed product, with a positive exponent independent of \(N\). The common complete bidisk is connected and both normalized functions have the required bounds there. A finite chain of buffered complex balls propagates the estimate to its smaller closed bidisk. Buffered Cauchy estimates prove all fixed derivatives. This is a comparison of these two bounded functions, not uniqueness inferred from finitely many samples alone. \(\square\) For later use write \(\tau_a=\pi-(2a+1)\pi/N\ge0\). The all-row theorem gives, uniformly over every physical row, the upper bound with its own phase \[ |F_a(-2\cos u)|+|\widehat G_a(-2\cos u)| \le e^{N\Re\psi(\tau_a,u)+o(N)} \tag{7} \] on every fixed compact second-angle domain in the original strip. The normal term is used only at double rows. Fixed ordinary spectral derivatives satisfy the same estimate. On a compact with \(\Re(-2\cos u)<2\), the \(o(N)\) loss can be replaced by a fixed power of \(N\). The actual midpoint relation in that source is \(\Psi_{a/N}(-2\cos u)=\psi(\tau_a+\pi/N,u)\); its monotone upper comparison gives (7) with \(\tau_a\), including the fold. There is no replacement of the row action by its complete maximum. **Lemma 2.** Uniformly over every double physical row with \(0\le\tau_a\le\rho_0\), \[ e^{-N\psi(\tau_a,u)} [\widehat G_a(-2\cos u)-G_a(-2\cos u)] =O(e^{-cN}) \tag{8} \] on a fixed smaller complete disk in \(u\), with fixed buffered derivatives. The positive exponent is uniform in the row and in parity. **Proof.** Choose the disk in (8) with a larger buffer still inside \(|u|<R\), and keep \(\tau_a\le\rho_0<\rho_1\). This is a compact subset of \(\Re(-2\cos u)<2\). Formula (7), including its polynomial normal loss, bounds the first term after normalization. The ordinary first-color derivative assertion of (5) bounds the canonical \(G_a\) by the same phase with a polynomial loss, uniformly even as \(\tau_a\to0\). The normalized difference is holomorphic and polynomially bounded on this disk. At every physical second color it vanishes exactly. There are \(c_0N\) distinct such angular points in a fixed positive real subinterval of the disk. A disk Blaschke estimate gives exponential smallness on an open interior disk; finite buffered propagation reaches any smaller complete disk. All constants are uniform in \(a\), since the bounds and zero set are uniform. Cauchy estimates give the derivative statement. The difference and phase are even in \(u\), so ordinary spectral derivatives through \(u=0\) also follow on a smaller disk by even holomorphic descent. No equality off the physical grid was used. \(\square\) ## 3. Uniform fold-line data on the whole parameter domain Write \(\mathcal H_N(X,Y)=H_N(t(X),t(Y))\) and \(\Psi(X,Y)=\psi(t(X),t(Y))\). Use all centered angular nodes satisfying \[ |t(X_j)|<\rho_0 . \tag{9} \] For such a node set \[ a(j)=\min(j,N-1-j). \tag{10} \] Thus its color is the original distinct color \(c_{a(j)}\). In particular a reflected index is not inserted as a new high Jacobi degree into \(\widehat G\). Its angular derivative has the actual sign \(C'(1-X_a)=-C'(X_a)\). Define the normalized target line data \[ T_{j,0}(Y)=e^{-N\Psi(X_j,Y)}F_{a(j)}(C(Y)), \tag{11} \] and, at every double row, \[ T_{j,1}(Y)=e^{-N\Psi(X_j,Y)} \{C'(X_j)\widehat G_{a(j)}(C(Y)) -N\Psi_X(X_j,Y)F_{a(j)}(C(Y))\}. \tag{12} \] At the odd center \(X_j=1/2\) define \(T_{j,1}=0\). This is a convenient auxiliary angular completion: \(C'=0\) and \(\Psi_X=0\) there. Only \(T_{j,0}\) is prescribed by the original simple spectral node. In particular (12) does not define an additional spectral normal there. Define the second line data \(S_{k,0},S_{k,1}\) by interchanging the endpoints. **Theorem 3.** On every fixed smaller connected second-parameter domain, uniformly for all nodes (9), \[ T_{j,a}(Y)-\partial_X^a\mathcal H_N(X_j,Y) =O(e^{-cN}),\qquad a=0,1. \tag{13} \] The symmetric assertion holds for \(S_{k,b}\). All fixed parameter derivatives retain this bound after fixed buffers. **Proof.** First restrict the other parameter to a small complete disk. Lemma 1 gives the value estimate, because the canonical kernel's physical row is exactly \(F_{a(j)}\). At a double row it also compares the angular derivative of the baseline with the canonical derivative \(C'(X_j)G_{a(j)}\). Lemma 2 replaces that canonical normal by \(C'(X_j)\widehat G_{a(j)}\), with an exponential error. Derivatives of the normalizing exponential produce only fixed powers of \(N\). At the odd center the canonical angular derivative and \(\Psi_X\) are zero, so Lemma 1 gives the auxiliary derivative estimate as well. Reflection changes only the sign of \(C'\); the phase and colors are even. For fixed \(j\), regard each difference in (13) as a holomorphic function of the other angle. On every buffered parameter compact it is bounded by \(e^{o(N)}\), uniformly over all the rows (9). For the target terms this follows from (7), the fixed compact phase derivative, and \(|C'|\le4\pi\). For the baseline and its first derivative it follows from (3) and a fixed first-variable Cauchy buffer around the entire small real fold interval. Its normalized derivative is the derivative of \(H_N\) itself; the \(N\Psi_X\) term has already been included in (12). Starting with the uniform open-disk estimate just proved, use a finite chain of buffered disks in the connected second-parameter domain. At each step the three-circles estimate combines an exponential bound with a uniform \(e^{o(N)}\) outer bound, leaving a positive exponential exponent. The same finite chains work for every \(j\); their constants depend on the fixed domains, not on the moving physical row. This proves (13). Buffered Cauchy estimates give fixed derivatives. No canonical-kernel bound is used outside the small complete bidisk. \(\square\) At a double row, conversion of an angular derivative error to a spectral first-normal error costs only a polynomial. Indeed \[ |C'(X_j)|=4\pi|\sin(2\pi X_j)|\ge c/N \tag{14} \] for the fold-near double nodes. The odd center is excluded from this division. No evenness or spectral descent of the off-grid baseline is inferred from (14). ## 4. Exact two-line fold repair Choose centered mirror windows with midpoint boundaries \[ a_N=k_N/N\longrightarrow\tfrac12-\rho/(2\pi),\qquad b_N=1-a_N,\qquad 0<\rho<\rho_0, \tag{15} \] and similarly in \(Y\). Include every grid node strictly between the boundaries. All these nodes satisfy (9) for large \(N\). The chosen original real seed windows can be retained inside these windows by making their initial choice smaller if necessary. At a joint selected node the target functions have the exact compatibility \[ \partial_Y^b T_{j,a}(Y_k) =\partial_X^a S_{k,b}(X_j), \qquad 0\le a,b\le1. \tag{16} \] For two double rows this is the original four angular jets of \(e^{-N\Psi}K_N(C(X),C(Y))\), including both independent spectral normals and their mixed normal. If one row is the odd center, its angular derivative is zero. The transposed target functions are even at that center because they are functions of its spectral color and the even phase. Thus (16) also holds there. This is only angular compatibility at a simple spectral node. For clarity use the explicit one-sided cardinal pairs \[ L_j^\sigma(X)=e^{\sigma2\pi iN(X-X_j)} \operatorname{sinc}^2(N(X-X_j)), \quad V_{j,0}^\sigma=[1-\sigma2\pi iN(X-X_j)]L_j^\sigma, \quad V_{j,1}^\sigma=(X-X_j)L_j^\sigma. \tag{17} \] They have the required unit value/derivative jets at their own node and double zeros at all other centered nodes. Write \(W_{k,b}^\tau\) for the second-coordinate pairs. Set \[ d_{j,a}=T_{j,a}-\partial_X^a\mathcal H_N(X_j,Y),\qquad e_{k,b}=S_{k,b}-\partial_Y^b\mathcal H_N(X,Y_k), \] \[ c_{jk}^{ab}=\partial_Y^bd_{j,a}(Y_k) =\partial_X^ae_{k,b}(X_j), \tag{18} \] and define \[ \mathcal K_N^{\sigma,\tau}=e^{N\Psi}\left[ \mathcal H_N+\sum_{j,a}d_{j,a}V_{j,a}^\sigma +\sum_{k,b}e_{k,b}W_{k,b}^\tau -\sum_{j,k,a,b}c_{jk}^{ab}V_{j,a}^\sigma W_{k,b}^\tau \right]. \tag{19} \] All sums are over the selected mirror windows and \(a,b\in\{0,1\}\). The same subtraction as in the product gluing theorem cancels the second correction against the mixed correction on a first row, and conversely. Consequently (19) has exactly the targets (11)--(12) on both line families. In particular its unnormalized value is \(F_{a(j)}(C(Y))\); its angular derivative is \(C'(X_j)\widehat G_{a(j)}(C(Y))\) at double rows. At an odd center its value is the actual simple row and its imposed angular derivative is zero. The latter is not used as an independent spectral datum. The errors in (18) are exponentially small by Theorem 3. The cardinal pairs and fixed derivatives are polynomially bounded on bounded parts of their designated half-planes. There are only \(O(N^2)\) summands. Hence on the corresponding inner product compacts, \[ e^{-N\Psi}\mathcal K_N^{\sigma,\tau} =\mathcal H_N+O(e^{-c_1N}),\qquad |\mathcal K_N^{\sigma,\tau}| \le\exp\{N\Re\Psi+o(N)\}, \quad \sigma\Im X\ge0,\quad\tau\Im Y\ge0. \tag{20} \] Fixed sufficiently thin opposite collars and all fixed buffered angular derivatives are allowed. Their only extra cardinal cost is \(\exp(4\pi N[(-\sigma\Im X)_++(-\tau\Im Y)_+])\); choose the collars after the positive error exponent. These claims do not assert evenness of (19). ## 5. The closed mirror trace and its odd simple node Here is the exact multiplicity, separate from the analytic estimates. Let \(\mathcal A_N\) consist of the distinct double spectral rows whose two angular lifts lie in (15). For an original spectral spectator \(P(Z;\ldots)\), keep its value and derivative, all crossing carriers and all shared variables. Define \[ \begin{split} \Phi^\sharp_{N,\mathrm{fold}}(w;\ldots) ={}&\eta\sum_{a\in\mathcal A_N} \{(4-c_a^2)[\widehat G_a(w)P(c_a) +F_a(w)P_Z(c_a)]-c_aF_a(w)P(c_a)\}\\ &+\mathbf1_{\{N\ {\rm odd}\}}F_{J_N}(w)P(-2). \end{split} \tag{21} \] The last term is a single value. There is no normal at the odd simple node. The original fold trace has the same expression with \(G_a\) instead of \(\widehat G_a\). Put \(D_h(X)=(\pi N)^2\sec^2(\pi NX)\), fix the second representative sign \(\tau\), and let \[ g_\sigma(X)=\sin(2\pi X) \mathcal K_N^{\sigma,\tau}(X,Y)P(C(X);\ldots). \tag{22} \] Take closed lower and upper window halves with the original orientations: \(E_-\) goes down the left side, across the lower side and up the right; \(E_+\) goes up the right side, across the upper side and down the left. Then \[ \boxed{\quad \Phi^\sharp_{N,\mathrm{fold}}(w(Y);\ldots) =-\frac{\eta}{4\pi^2i} \left\{\int_{E_-}D_hg_-\,dX+\int_{E_+}D_hg_+\,dX +\int_{a_N}^{b_N}D_h(g_+-g_-)\,dX\right\}. \quad} \tag{23} \] The contours must remain in the domains where the representatives are defined. All vertical half-sides and the real interface are part of this identity. **Proof.** Each centered pole of \(D_h\) has principal part \((X-X_j)^{-2}\), so its residue against \(g\) is \(g'(X_j)\). At a double spectral row the actual angular jets give \[ g'(X_j)=-\pi\{(4-c_a^2) [\widehat G_a(w)P(c_a)+F_a(w)P_Z(c_a)] -c_aF_a(w)P(c_a)\}. \tag{24} \] Both reflected lifts give the same expression: the two factors \(\sin(2\pi X_j)\) and \(C'(X_j)\) change signs together. Multiplication of their residue sum by \(-\eta/(2\pi)\), the closed coefficient in (23), gives exactly the corresponding term of (21). At the odd center \(X_j=1/2\), \(\sin(2\pi X)=-2\pi(X-1/2)+O((X-1/2)^3)\). Its residue is therefore \(-2\pi F_{J_N}(w)P(-2)\), regardless of the finite angular derivative of the representative. Since \(\eta=1\) at odd level, (23) gives exactly the final term of (21). Equivalently, \(P_N(C(X))=4\cos^2(\pi NX)\), and \(C\) has degree two at this angular lift of the simple spectral node. The factor one-half in (23) is compulsory there. For two different half-plane representatives the real-interface term is the usual split of the closed residue contour. Their full angular jets agree at all selected nodes, so its singularities are removable. This proves (23) without a first-angle parity assumption. \(\square\) The difference between (21) and the original free-\(w\) fold trace is \(P_N(w)\) times a holomorphic slit function, by the exact full-jet property of \(\widehat G_a\). Thus equality with the original follows after its required subsequent complete second trace, including arbitrary original spectators and their normal products. At two selected fold windows, the exact mixed jets of (19) give the original double-window trace directly, with the same mirror factor in each variable. A local parameter chart is not itself a contour for every remaining second row: the full trace is taken on the global finite expression (21), or on a covering retaining those rows. ## 6. Scope and direct sources This extends the matched data from fixed bulk windows to a fixed neighborhood of the simultaneous complete fold, including every nearby even last normal and the odd simple value. It does not extend to the original positive-color endpoint \(t=\pm\pi\), identify an arbitrary free polynomial with (19), assert spectral descent of the repaired functions, or replace a whole open lens by an uneven representative. All shared products retain their actual mixed product rules. The common baseline cancels from differences of the designated representatives, but the original trace kernels, spectators, interfaces and exterior sides remain; no parent-action or scalar noncancellation conclusion is inferred. Complete direct source texts and used implications were read at: * [Positive product gluing](research_positive_product_window_gluing.md), SHA256 ace4f667038c494e2690a77496ce32e8bc8538535356b78600e8ad8ced8183d5: common normalized Cauchy baseline, exact bulk line errors, designated cardinal pairs and mixed repair, and precise sharp-trace scope. * [Endpoint-role comparison](research_physical_row_endpoint_role_overlap.md), SHA256 67478e66259712bc648c23241c3c3e93bc4342c54b2dbcea39be97ee7b83edec: approximate-zero dense-grid estimates and finite complex propagation. * [All-row full-normal control](research_compact_positive_contour_residue_control.md), SHA256 cac1016d5f515510b95071a25c8d97345b334043492a6b430c4e924f87d82bb0: exact pole-free normal, every physical mixed jet, own-row slit and half-plane bounds, midpoint calibration, and original simple-node trace. * [Full complete-disk kernel](research_bare_kernel_three_fifths_disk.md), SHA256 fe2479fb7436a061f6fd5dda9a59ab22f3c10a9e79d5105b1f95361053196d3f: actual full canonical kernel expansion and all fixed ordinary spectral derivatives on the three-fifths bidisk, including both folded parities. Only written mathematics, source reads and metadata hashes were used. No mathematical program, numerical computation, test or compilation was run. Adopted notes and public manuscripts were unchanged.

title: A common positive-product baseline and exact two-endpoint window repair
text: # A common positive-product baseline and exact two-endpoint window repair Private written proof, 16 November 2026. The regular row constructions can be assembled on a fixed positive product chart. A finite boundary Cauchy integral gives one holomorphic baseline with the original action bound. The endpoint-role comparison controls this projection, including its actual normal data on the chosen real windows. Two one-sided row repairs, with their common mixed-jet correction subtracted once, then preserve both row families exactly. The windows remain fixed bulk windows. The conclusion is an angular holomorphic representative with a designated-quadrant bound, not a whole-grid or full-lens replacement. All original exterior and interface currents retain their original spectator. ## 1. Fixed product domains and designated paths Fix a positive pair \((t_*,u_*)\) in the original strips \(\mathcal S=\{|\Re t|<\pi\}\). The pinned product-domain theorem provides symmetric simply connected domains \(V_t,V_u\subset\mathcal S\), containing the full real intervals and the target, on whose product \[ a=\tan(t/2),\quad b=\tan(u/2),\quad q_*^2=1+a^2+b^2\notin(-\infty,0],\quad \Re q_*>0. \tag{1} \] In tangent coordinates each domain is the union of a thin horizontal strip and a thin neighborhood of the segment joining the target tangent to its negative. Both pieces contain zero. Choose bounded smooth Jordan domains \[ \Omega_v^0\Subset\Omega_v^1\Subset\Omega_v^2 \Subset\Omega_v^3\Subset V_v,\qquad v=t,u, \tag{2} \] containing zero, the target coordinate and fixed small positive real seed intervals. They may be chosen symmetric, with star-shaped tangent images. To see this, take a compact radial set consisting of the required segments and small real intervals in the open star-shaped tangent domain. A smooth positive radial boundary lying between that compact set and the domain boundary gives a bounded star-shaped Jordan neighborhood. Repeat with buffers and apply \(2\arctan\). All choices precede \(N\). The original phase \(\psi(t,u)\) is single valued on this product. For precision its derivatives are \[ r_t=\tfrac12\Log\frac{q_*+a}{q_*-a},\quad r_u=\tfrac12\Log\frac{q_*+b}{q_*-b},\qquad \psi_t=-r_t/\pi,\quad\psi_u=-r_u/\pi . \tag{3} \] The logarithms have their original value at completeness. Their arguments are units since \((q_*+a)(q_*-a)=1+b^2\), and similarly for \(b\). The product is simply connected. Moreover \(\partial_u r_t=\partial_t r_u=-ab/(2q_*)\), so (3), with the original complete constant, defines the continued original phase. It agrees with every row phase at its real seed. **Lemma 1.** A nonzero point of either \(\Omega_v^2\) can be joined to its positive real seed interval by a compact path avoiding zero which stays in the sign of its imaginary part, apart from its real seed. If the target is real, either side may be chosen. Fixed buffered tubes supply the regular continuation domains, uniformly for the other endpoint throughout a fixed buffered parameter compact. **Proof.** Work in the star-shaped tangent domain. Follow its radial target segment from a sufficiently small nonzero point to the target. Join that small point to a positive real seed through a small arc about zero on the same side, followed by the real spine. This arc lies in a disk contained in the domain. For \(a=A+i\beta\), \[ \Im(2\arctan a) =\tfrac12\log\frac{A^2+(1+\beta)^2}{A^2+(1-\beta)^2}, \tag{4} \] which has the sign of \(\beta\). Thus the angular path has the claimed side. A thin tube about a simple version of this path is simply connected and avoids zero and the angular endpoints. On this tube the selected degree root is \[ \lambda_t=\frac{q_*+a}{q_*-a},\qquad 1-\lambda_t^{-2}=\frac{4q_*a}{(q_*+a)^2}. \tag{5} \] Every factor is a unit on the compact buffered product, because the first angle avoids zero. This proves the required uniform separation without imposing off-real modulus ordering. The same proof applies with the endpoints interchanged. \(\square\) First choose the buffered tube and construct its mode. Then shrink only the opposite-side collar to the width supplied by its positive repair exponent. This order is important: no fixed preselected collar is declared smaller than an exponent not yet constructed. The path itself stays on the designated side, and its real seed has a nonempty permitted collar. Compactness leaves an open neighborhood of each target in the resulting bounded domain. In particular, if both target angles are nonzero, the two endpoint roles have a common designated product domain with two real physical seed intervals. Use the same domains (1), choose the two paths of Lemma 1 independently, and include each path in the other construction's parameter domain. Their product is connected to the joint seed and has both normalized bounds. This verifies the hypotheses of the endpoint-role overlap theorem on compact subsets of that product. Merely having two separate continuation paths would not have supplied this common domain. ## 2. One finite boundary Cauchy projection Use centered degree coordinates \[ N\ge2,\quad\eta=(-1)^{N-1},\quad X=(\pi-t)/(2\pi),\quad Y=(\pi-u)/(2\pi),\quad X_j=(j+\tfrac12)/N,\quad Y_k=(k+\tfrac12)/N,\quad C(X)=2\cos(2\pi X),\quad c_j=C(X_j),\quad P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2. \tag{6} \] Fix bulk intervals \(I_X,I_Y\Subset(0,1/2)\), corresponding to the positive real seed intervals in (2). Every local construction below matches those same windows. All sufficiently large-level rows in them are double spectral nodes. Cover the compact curve \(\Gamma_t=\partial\Omega_t^1\) by finitely many first-degree continuation charts. Each chart uses Lemma 1, the same \(I_X\), and a second-parameter domain containing \(\overline{\Omega_u^3}\) with a buffer inside \(V_u\). The first-degree paths and their buffers lie in \(\Omega_t^2\). Let \(A_{i,N}(t,u)\) be its repaired representative and put \[ a_{i,N}=e^{-N\psi}A_{i,N}. \tag{7} \] On a neighborhood of its boundary arc times \(\overline{\Omega_u^3}\), this function is holomorphic and has norm \(e^{o(N)}\). Its sign is chosen for that boundary arc. Different arcs may require different signs; all arc neighborhoods use their actual permitted collars. Choose a fixed smooth partition of unity \(\chi_i\) on \(\Gamma_t\), subordinate to these arcs. Define \[ H_N(t,u)=\frac1{2\pi i}\int_{\Gamma_t} \frac{\sum_i\chi_i(\zeta)a_{i,N}(\zeta,u)} {\zeta-t}\,d\zeta . \tag{8} \] The integral is counterclockwise. It is holomorphic in \(\Omega_t^1\times\Omega_u^3\), and \[ \sup_{\Omega_t^0\times K_u}|H_N|\le e^{o(N)} \quad(K_u\Subset\Omega_u^3). \tag{9} \] Indeed the contour length and its distance from \(\Omega_t^0\) are fixed, its cover is finite, and its integrand is holomorphic in the exterior parameter. This gives a bounded projection explicitly; no quantitative sheaf or \(\bar\partial\) theorem is being assumed. Now take a second-degree chart \(B_{j,N}(t,u)\) whose degree path and buffers lie in \(\Omega_u^2\), and whose first-endpoint parameter domain contains \(\overline{\Omega_t^3}\) with a buffer inside \(V_t\). Write \(b_{j,N}=e^{-N\psi}B_{j,N}\). On each boundary arc, the common-domain construction of Lemma 1 and the endpoint-role theorem give \[ a_{i,N}-b_{j,N}=O(e^{-c_{ij}N}) \tag{10} \] uniformly on fixed compact parts of the chart. There are finitely many \(i\). Cauchy's formula for \(b_{j,N}\) in its full first-parameter domain and (8) therefore give \[ H_N-b_{j,N}=O(e^{-c_jN}) \quad\text{on }\Omega_t^0\times K_j , \tag{11} \] where \(K_j\) is any fixed compact subset of the second chart's designated degree domain. All fixed derivatives satisfy the same conclusion on smaller buffers. The domain choices in (2) are deliberately asymmetric in each use: degree paths stay inside the level-two domains, while the opposite parameter domains contain level three. Thus every cross-role comparison in (10) has the entire two-path product and joint seed. No later enlargement or connectedness of an intersection of two same-role paths is required. The baseline also compares with any first-degree chart \(A_N^0\) on a compact part of \(\Omega_t^0\), with its path in \(\Omega_t^2\) and parameter domain containing \(\overline{\Omega_u^3}\). First compare both with a fixed second-degree chart about the real interval \(I_Y\). Equation (11) and the endpoint-role theorem give an exponentially small normalized difference on that real seed neighborhood, uniformly in the compact first-degree set. Both \(H_N\) and \(e^{-N\psi}A_N^0\) have \(e^{o(N)}\) bounds as holomorphic functions of \(u\). Finite analytic propagation on the connected second parameter domain gives \[ H_N-e^{-N\psi}A_N^0=O(e^{-cN}) \tag{12} \] on every fixed smaller parameter compact, including \(u=0\). This comparison is made where the first-degree chart itself is regular. It does not continue that chart through its degree fold. In particular choose \(A_N^0\) near the entire real window \(I_X\), and use a second-degree chart near \(I_Y\) in (11). The baseline consequently has exponentially small errors in both actual row families, as holomorphic functions of the other endpoint. This is stronger than comparing only isolated joint nodal values. The Cauchy baseline is holomorphic even at \((t,u)=(0,0)\); no physical data at that fold have been inferred from this fact. ## 3. Exact row identities and the compatible mixed repair Write \(\mathcal H_N(X,Y)=H_N(t(X),t(Y))\) and \(\Psi(X,Y)=\psi(t(X),t(Y))\). Use the original \[ F_j(w)=K_N(c_j,w),\qquad G_j(w)=\partial_zK_N(c_j,w), \tag{13} \] and the pinned full-normal representative \(\widehat G_j\). Define the normalized first-row target functions \[ \begin{split} T_{j,0}(Y)&=e^{-N\Psi(X_j,Y)}F_j(C(Y)),\\ T_{j,1}(Y)&=e^{-N\Psi(X_j,Y)} \{C'(X_j)\widehat G_j(C(Y)) -N\Psi_X(X_j,Y)F_j(C(Y))\}. \end{split} \tag{14} \] Define \(S_{k,0}(X),S_{k,1}(X)\) by interchanging the endpoints. They are holomorphic on the full parameter neighborhoods in use. The actual mixed physical-jet identity proves, exactly, \[ \partial_Y^bT_{j,a}(Y_k)=\partial_X^aS_{k,b}(X_j), \qquad 0\le a,b\le1. \tag{15} \] This includes the derivatives of the normalizing exponential: both sides are the same \((a,b)\) jet of \(e^{-N\Psi}K_N(C(X),C(Y))\) at the physical pair. It uses the required first normal of \(\widehat G_j\), not just its value. Set \[ d_{j,a}(Y)=T_{j,a}(Y)-\partial_X^a\mathcal H_N(X_j,Y), \quad e_{k,b}(X)=S_{k,b}(X)-\partial_Y^b\mathcal H_N(X,Y_k). \tag{16} \] Equations (11)--(12), with fixed buffers, give \[ d_{j,a}=O(e^{-cN}),\qquad e_{k,b}=O(e^{-cN}) \tag{17} \] uniformly for all selected rows and on the respective full smaller parameter domains. The same holds for every fixed derivative. These estimates use the actual row-normal normalization of the regular source theorem. The original canonical kernel is not being bounded off-grid to prove (17). For \(\sigma=\pm1\), define \[ L_j^\sigma(X)=e^{\sigma2\pi iN(X-X_j)} \operatorname{sinc}^2(N(X-X_j)), \] \[ V_{j,0}^\sigma(X)=[1-\sigma2\pi iN(X-X_j)]L_j^\sigma(X), \qquad V_{j,1}^\sigma(X)=(X-X_j)L_j^\sigma(X). \tag{18} \] They satisfy \(\partial_X^aV_{j,b}^\sigma(X_\ell)=\delta_{j\ell}\delta_{ab}\) for \(0\le a,b\le1\). Use \(W_{k,b}^\tau(Y)\) for the same functions in the second coordinate. On bounded parts of \(\sigma\Im X\ge0\), each function and fixed derivative is polynomially bounded in \(N\). This follows from the Fourier support of \(L_j^\sigma\) and its coefficient mass one. The compatibility in (15) gives one joint error array \[ c_{jk}^{ab}=\partial_Y^bd_{j,a}(Y_k) =\partial_X^ae_{k,b}(X_j). \tag{19} \] Define the three finite corrections \[ \begin{split} E_X^\sigma&=\sum_{j,a}d_{j,a}(Y)V_{j,a}^\sigma(X),\\ E_Y^\tau&=\sum_{k,b}e_{k,b}(X)W_{k,b}^\tau(Y),\\ E_{XY}^{\sigma,\tau} &=\sum_{j,k,a,b}c_{jk}^{ab} V_{j,a}^\sigma(X)W_{k,b}^\tau(Y), \end{split} \tag{20} \] and the actual angular holomorphic representative \[ \boxed{\quad \mathcal K_N^{\sigma,\tau}(X,Y) =e^{N\Psi(X,Y)} [\mathcal H_N+E_X^\sigma+E_Y^\tau-E_{XY}^{\sigma,\tau}]. \quad} \tag{21} \] All four choices are holomorphic on the same inner product domain. **Theorem 2.** The representatives (21) obey both exact row families, as holomorphic identities in the other variable: \[ \begin{split} \mathcal K_N^{\sigma,\tau}(X_j,Y)&=F_j(C(Y)),& \partial_X\mathcal K_N^{\sigma,\tau}(X_j,Y) &=C'(X_j)\widehat G_j(C(Y)),\\ \mathcal K_N^{\sigma,\tau}(X,Y_k)&=F_k(C(X)),& \partial_Y\mathcal K_N^{\sigma,\tau}(X,Y_k) &=C'(Y_k)\widehat G_k(C(X)). \end{split} \tag{22} \] On compact subsets of their designated quadrants \(\sigma\Im X\ge0,\ \tau\Im Y\ge0\), \[ e^{-N\Psi}\mathcal K_N^{\sigma,\tau} =\mathcal H_N+O(e^{-c_1N}),\qquad |\mathcal K_N^{\sigma,\tau}| \le \exp\{N\Re\Psi+o(N)\}. \tag{23} \] The estimate includes fixed sufficiently thin opposite collars. Every fixed derivative has the corresponding buffered estimate. **Proof.** Taking an \(X\)-jet at \(X_j\) in (20), equation (19) gives exactly \[ \partial_X^aE_{XY}^{\sigma,\tau}(X_j,Y) =\partial_X^aE_Y^\tau(X_j,Y). \tag{24} \] Thus the second and mixed corrections cancel in that row, and \(\mathcal H_N+E_X^\sigma\) has precisely the two targets (14). Multiplication by \(e^{N\Psi}\) proves the first line of (22). The symmetric calculation proves its second line. This is why the mixed correction is subtracted once. There are \(O(N)\) terms in each single sum and \(O(N^2)\) in the double sum. Equations (17)--(19) and the polynomial cardinal bounds prove (23). On the opposite sides the only additional exponential factor is at most \[ \exp\{4\pi N[ (-\sigma\Im X)_++(-\tau\Im Y)_+]\}. \tag{25} \] Choose the collar widths after \(c\), with their sum sufficiently small. The remaining exponential rate stays positive. Buffered Cauchy estimates give fixed exterior and spatial derivatives. \(\square\) ## 4. Original source and current scope For a selected first window and any actual joint spectator \(P\), the closed window contour of (21) is exactly the finite residue expression \[ \Phi^\sharp_{N,I_X}(w) =\eta\sum_{X_j\in I_X} \{(4-c_j^2)[\widehat G_j(w)P(c_j) +F_j(w)P_Z(c_j)]-c_jF_j(w)P(c_j)\}. \tag{26} \] This follows from (22), with every other variable held fixed. The original window trace uses \(G_j\) instead. Their difference is \(P_N(w)\) times a holomorphic slit function, and equality with the original follows after the required subsequent complete second trace, including all spectators and normal products. The second-window statement is identical with the roles reversed. At a joint selected physical pair, (22) retains the value, both first normals and their mixed normal of the original kernel. Thus the double selected-window trace is exact. A local parameter domain need not contain the remaining second grid: a later full trace is taken on the global finite residue expression (26), or on a covering retaining all other rows. No arbitrary free-boundary polynomial has been replaced. The four representatives have one common baseline. Their normalized differences are exponentially small where the relevant designated bounds hold; the original trace kernels and the entire spectator must still multiply those differences. The usual removable one-sided real interface and every oriented exterior half-side remain in each closed-window formula. An exponential local saving does not by itself pay a larger spectator or parent action. The Cauchy baseline extends through both angular folds, but (22) matches only the chosen bulk rows. No new fold value or fold normal is asserted. Neither the baseline nor the exact repairs are asserted even in both angular variables, so no spectral descent at an unmatched fold or parity-based full-lens substitution is inferred. The original endpoint rows near \(\pm\pi\), all unmatched rows, and the full geometric cycle and coefficient remain separate. ## Direct sources and coverage The complete direct texts and their used implications were read at: * [Regular positive continuation](research_physical_row_regular_positive_continuation.md), SHA256 3a7d81d55f60396c2e3058d5ebe967ae625ff47c4b527b4e102e37fa8f28d644: actual row modes, independent normal anchor, designated-half repair and exact \(\Phi^\sharp\) trace type. * [Endpoint-role overlap](research_physical_row_endpoint_role_overlap.md), SHA256 67478e66259712bc648c23241c3c3e93bc4342c54b2dbcea39be97ee7b83edec: full mixed physical compatibility, shared-seed comparison and finite analytic propagation. * [Positive product domains](research_positive_wire_product_contour.md), SHA256 5646f2d6b2a8dfa2d8c49662d17f19f3743fc4efcaf3c3685c6a899975a4c230: tangent-domain construction, original discriminant branches and fixed product neighborhoods. The earlier two-channel interpolation note already uses a Cauchy correction followed by a finite sinc repair on a thin one-variable strip. Here the boundary projection is controlled by the actual opposite-endpoint source chart, and the two line families are repaired together by (19)--(24). No general bounded Cousin solver or global continuation of a raw finite factorial sum is used. Only written mathematics, source reads and metadata hashes were used. No mathematical program, numerical evaluation, test or compilation was run. Adopted notes and public manuscripts were unchanged.

title: Formal coefficients along the marked positive source component
text:
# Formal coefficients along the marked positive source component Private written proof, 22 November 2026. The geometric formal coefficients of the initialized contour source are finite rational Gaussian expressions. Their continuation needs less logarithmic data than the action. For any supplied positive unit-charge primitive target, the original positive tangent domain supplies a marked regular path and a one-complex-parameter neighborhood on which every coefficient continues. The leading coefficient is nonzero at the target. In this class the polynomial upper-bound criterion therefore has no additional formal-coefficient or leading-unit hypothesis to discharge. No global upper estimate, quantum-cycle coefficient, or new filling class is proved. A positive lift of an arbitrary short hyperbolic filling is not assumed to exist. ## 1. The full independent-variable formal calculation Fix a finite original same-index graph, with selected vertices \(I\), \(m=|I|\ge1\), and all edges incident to \(I\) retained. Write \(e\) for their number, counted once, and \(d=e+m\). Every selected vertex has at least one incidence. Loops count twice; repeated edges remain distinct. Outside angles are fixed at zero. Fix real powers \(n_v\) before \(N	o\infty\); integral powers are the actual physical ones. Retain independent original variables \(x_e,t_v\), and put \[ w_v=	an(t_v/2),\qquad q_e=\cot(\pi x_e),\qquad z_{e,v,\pm}=	frac12-x_e\pm t_v/(2\pi). 	ag{1} \] An outside endpoint has \(t_v=w_v=0\). The original incidence phase is \[ b_0(x,t)=-J(	frac12-x+t/(2\pi)) -J(	frac12-x-t/(2\pi))-2J(x),\qquad J'(z)=\Log(2\sin\pi z),\qquad J(1/2)=0. \] On its marked local branches the full phase is \[ \Phi_{ oldsymbol\chi}(x,t)= \sum_{(e,v)}b_0(x_e,t_v) +\sum_{v\in I}\left( rac{in_vt_v^2}{4\pi}-i\chi_vt_vight). 	ag{2} \] The incidence sum has two terms for every edge. At a full critical point the selected wire sheet satisfies \[ q_e^2=1+w_v^2+w_u^2\quad(e=vu). 	ag{3} \] All derivatives below are taken in the independent variables of (1) before imposing (3). In particular no fold wire is differentiated as an eliminated function of its endpoint angles. Let \(H=-\Phi''\) in those \(d\) independent variables, and put \(\Delta=\det H\). On a marked critical chart suppose \[ (1+w_v^2)(1+q_e^2)
e0,\qquad q_e+w_v
e0,\quad q_e-w_v
e0,\qquad \Delta
e0 	ag{4} \] for every relevant incidence. The conditions at an outside endpoint have their literal meaning. On (3), the incidence conditions follow from \(1+w_u^2
e0\). **Formal coefficient statement.** Continue the determinant root from the actual initialized germ. Every coefficient of its full stationary expansion is holomorphic on the resulting regular determinant-root cover. Its leading coefficient is \[ a_0=\left( rac{i}{\pi}ight)^m(2\pi)^{d/2}  rac{A(x,t)}{\sqrt{\Delta}},\qquad A(x,t)=\prod_{v\in I}\sin t_v \prod_e rac1{4\sin^2(\pi x_e)} =\prod_{v\in I} rac{2w_v}{1+w_v^2} \prod_e rac{1+q_e^2}{4}. 	ag{5} \] Where all selected \(w_v
e0\), each \(a_j/a_0\) is a rational function of \(q,w\), with constants depending on the fixed graph and powers. The coefficients \(a_j\) themselves have no pole forced by \(w_v=0\). Nor is \(q_e=0\) a forbidden divisor when (4) and \(\Delta
e0\) hold. This last assertion does not prove regularity of an unspecified fold. Here is a direct construction. The centered factorial expansion in the pinned source gives the incidence defects \[ C_{r,e,v}= - rac{B_{2r}(1/2) \{J^{(2r)}(z_{e,v,+})+J^{(2r)}(z_{e,v,-})\} +2B_{2r}J^{(2r)}(x_e)}{(2r)!}, \qquad C_r=\sum_{(e,v)}C_{r,e,v}. 	ag{6} \] It is an actual uniform all-order factorial expansion near the initializer. Away from that neighborhood (6) defines its formal coefficient continuation, not an asserted asymptotic for the exact factorial on arbitrary complex domains. For \(r\ge1\), \(J^{(2r)}(z)\) is a polynomial in \(\cot(\pi z)\), with fixed powers of \(\pi\). Moreover \[ \cot(\pi z_{e,v,+})= rac{1-q_ew_v}{q_e+w_v},\qquad \cot(\pi z_{e,v,-})= rac{1+q_ew_v}{q_e-w_v}. 	ag{7} \] Thus every \(C_r\) is rational under (4). The independent-variable derivations are \[ \partial_{x_e}=-\pi(1+q_e^2)\partial_{q_e},\qquad \partial_{t_v}=	frac12(1+w_v^2)\partial_{w_v}. 	ag{8} \] They preserve this field. Every derivative of \(\Phi\) of order at least two is rational as well: a second derivative removes each sine logarithm, the crossing term contributes only its fixed quadratic coefficient, and the charge term has no second derivative. For completeness, write \(h=N^{-1}\), let \(p=(x,t)\) be the critical point, and let \(\Phi_k(\xi)\) be the degree-\(k\) Taylor term of \(\Phi(p+\xi)\). Define the normalized Gaussian functional by \[ \mathcal W_H(e^{l^T\xi}) =e^{l^TH^{-1}l/2}. 	ag{9} \] The formal coefficients are exactly those of \[ \left( rac{i}{\pi}ight)^m rac{(2\pi)^{d/2}}{\sqrt{\Delta}}\, \mathcal W_H\!\left[ A(p+\sqrt h\,\xi) \exp\left\{\sum_{k\ge3}h^{k/2-1}\Phi_k(\xi) +\sum_{r\ge1}h^{2r-1}C_r(p+\sqrt h\,\xi)ight\}ight]. 	ag{10} \] Odd Gaussian moments vanish, so only integer powers of \(h\) remain. At each fixed order only finitely many Taylor terms and pairings occur. They use derivatives in (8), the rational phase derivatives, and entries of \(H^{-1}\). Formula (10) proves the assertion, including holomorphy at a selected \(w_v=0\): it never divides by \(A(p)\). Dividing afterward by the nonzero expression (5) gives the rational ratio statement. ## 2. Identification with the actual initialized coefficients The initial identification retains the original polynomial source. At each discrete index the canonical halfwire satisfies \[ B_N(j/N,t)=e_j(-2\cos t) 	ag{11} \] as an ordinary polynomial identity. Near its original interior wire saddle the two halfwires have the actual expansion \[ B_N(x,t_v)B_N(x,t_u) = rac{e^{N\{b_0(x,t_v)+b_0(x,t_u)\}}} {4N^2\sin^2(\pi x)} \exp\left\{\sum_{r\ge1}N^{-(2r-1)} (C_{r,e,v}+C_{r,e,u})ight\}. 	ag{12} \] The expansion is meant to any fixed order with its remainder, on the initial compact regular chart. The original local finite-sum argument encloses the retained indices with the cotangent residue kernel. Its constant mode has coefficient exactly \(+N\) times the wire integral; its nonconstant modes, endpoint connectors and omitted index tails have a strict exponential gap. This is the finite-sum calculation in the regular low-source proof. Only that local calculation is used here, not its zero-power subtree theorem: at completeness the wire is \(x=1/4\), all normalized factorial arguments are \(1/4\), and the wire second derivative is \(-8\pi\). They retain their regularity and strict local gaps near the actual small-charge seed. The all-order factorial expansion therefore applies to that same finite-index calculation. The actual small-charge theorem estimates the remaining original rows and all mixed angular currents. The pattern-adapted all-plus family retains these estimates and removes just the factor \(2^{-m}\) from the central horizontal cosine. Consequently its actual all-order seed coefficients come from (12) followed by the angular Gaussian expansion. Formal Gaussian integration in successive variable groups equals the full rule (10). One elementary verification is to test the quadratic Gaussian on \(e^{l^T\xi}\): completing the wire square gives the same inverse quadratic form and determinant as the block Schur formula. Expansion in \(l\) proves equality for every polynomial moment, hence at every fixed Taylor order. The powers are \(N^{2m}\) from the angular traces, \(N^{-e}\) from the paired halfwire factors and index prefactors, and \(N^{-d/2}\) from the full Gaussian. Their product is \(N^ eta\), where \[  eta= rac{3(m-e)}2. 	ag{13} \] This proves (5) with its actual constant and marks, not only up to a nonzero function. Both level parities have the same formal calculation; their exact rational trace denominators differ only in terms already exponentially small at the seed. No global factorial substitution for the off-endpoint contour family has been made. Its ordinary polynomial numerator, frozen heights, removed rows and vertical currents remain the prescribed ones. Only the known seed coefficients have been identified and continued. ## 3. The positive tangent domain and its original marks Let \(\mathcal P\) be the domain of selected tangent configurations \(w\), with outside tangents zero, at which every original edge is positive. Use the original inverse-tangent strip \[ \mathcal A=\mathbb C\setminus (i[1,\infty)\cup-i[1,\infty)),\qquad t_v=2\arctan w_v,\quad |\Re t_v|<\pi. 	ag{14} \] The positive-wire contraction lemma proves independent-coordinate contraction within \(\mathcal P\). In particular it is open, star shaped about zero, and contractible. Here \(\mathcal P\) means the actual positive-edge domain, not the larger product neighborhoods constructed elsewhere for contour reachability. On \(\mathcal P\), use the principal roots and original wire branches \[ q_e=\sqrt{1+w_v^2+w_u^2},\quad \Re q_e>0,\qquad x_e= rac1{2\pi i}\Log rac{q_e+i}{q_e-i},\quad x_e(0)=	frac14. 	ag{15} \] They have \(0<\Re x_e<1/2\). All \(1+w_v^2\), \(q_e\pm i\) and \(q_e\pm w_v\) are units, the last by \((q_e+w_v)(q_e-w_v)=1+w_u^2\). Contractibility therefore supplies the canonical return logarithms \[ r_{v,e}=	frac12\Log rac{q_e+w_v}{q_e-w_v},\qquad r_{v,e}(0)=0, \qquad \mathcal P_v(t)=\sum_{e
i v}r_{v,e}- rac{in_vt_v}{2}. 	ag{16} \] Every incidence and original power is retained. The unexponentiated wire equation is \(F_{e,x}=0\) on this graph. Its exponential equals one by (3), its initial value is zero, and its continued value is discrete and continuous on connected \(\mathcal P\); hence it stays zero. The angular derivatives of the original phase are \[ \Phi_{t_v}=-\mathcal P_v/\pi-i\chi_v. 	ag{17} \] These are the marked equations, not just their multipliers. The critical edge actions have derivatives \(-r_{v,e}/\pi\). Their closed holomorphic one-forms have unique primitives on the contractible domain, normalized at the original complete action. They give the same continued phase as (2), anchored there at \(eM_\infty\), with \(M_\infty\) the original complete edge action. No logarithm or action constant is reset. To check full regularity, let \(K_e\) be the original edge matrix. For these complex symmetric matrices, \(\Re\) denotes the Hermitian part. \[ K_e= rac1{q_e}  egin{pmatrix}1+w_v^2&-w_vw_u\ -w_vw_u&1+w_u^2\end{pmatrix}. 	ag{18} \] The positive-edge theorem gives \(\Re K_e>0\). With \(B_e\) the real incidence pullback to selected variations, including repeated entries for a loop, \[ \mathcal P_t= rac12\sum_eB_e^TK_eB_e - rac i2\operatorname{diag}(n_v). 	ag{19} \] Since the powers are real and every selected vertex is incident, \(\Re\mathcal P_t>0\). The wire Hessian block is diagonal with units \[ H_e= rac{2\pi q_e(1+q_e^2)^2} {(1+w_v^2)(1+w_u^2)}. 	ag{20} \] Its Schur complement in the full \(H\) is \(\mathcal P_t/\pi\), by (17). Thus \(\Delta
e0\) everywhere on \(\mathcal P\), including zero selected tangents. The seed determinant root extends uniquely over this contractible domain. Formula (10) therefore defines every \(a_j\) holomorphically on \(\mathcal P\). There is a global charge chart, not merely a local inverse. The positive-edge comparison, summed over all incidences, gives for any two distinct configurations in \(\mathcal P\) \[ \Re\sum_{v\in I}\delta\mathcal P_v\, \overline{\delta t_v}>0. \] The fixed real-power term has zero real contribution to this pairing. Hence \( oldsymbol\chi=i oldsymbol{\mathcal P}/\pi\) is injective, also for complex charges. Its Jacobian is invertible by (19), so it is a biholomorphism onto an open contractible complex charge domain \(\mathcal C_{\mathbf n}\). The critical action and all the \(a_j\) descend holomorphically to this domain, with their original marks. An independent vertex sign flip preserves \(\mathcal P\), changes only \(\chi_v\) to \(-\chi_v\), and leaves all other charges unchanged. This follows from (15)--(16) and the canonical zero logarithms. Injectivity then proves \(\chi_v=0\) if and only if \(w_v=0\). Thus (5) has precisely the coordinate charge hyperplanes as its zero set on \(\mathcal C_{\mathbf n}\); no vanishing order is asserted. Suppose a target in this domain satisfies the original unit-charge primitive equations \(\mathcal P_v=-\pi i\), with their canonical logs. Then every selected \(w_v
e0\). Indeed \(w_v=0\) gives \(t_v=0\) and every \(r_{v,e}=0\): the zero-coordinate slice contracts to completeness, where these zero logarithms are fixed. It would give \(\mathcal P_v=0\), a contradiction. Formula (5) proves that the target leading coefficient is a unit. Intermediate zeros of \(a_0\), for example at completeness, do not obstruct continuation of the formal coefficients. ## 4. A one-parameter marked full critical curve Choose the actual small positive-charge seed for these same fixed powers, and let \(w^*\) be any supplied target as just specified. Both points have all selected coordinates nonzero. Contract each along its radial arm into a sufficiently small product polydisk contained in \(\mathcal P\), stopping before zero. Connect the two contracted points coordinate by coordinate inside the corresponding punctured disks. The two radial arms and this connector give a compact continuous path in \(\mathcal P\cap(\mathbb C^*)^m\). Approximate it uniformly by a fixed Bernstein polynomial vector \(p(s)\) preserving its endpoints. Such approximation follows directly from uniform continuity: in the Bernstein average, the mass at distance at least \(\delta\) from \(s\) is at most \(1/(4M\delta^2)\), while the remaining oscillation is bounded by the path's continuity modulus at \(\delta\). Taking the fixed degree \(M\) large keeps the image inside \(\mathcal P\cap(\mathbb C^*)^m\), since the compact path has positive distance from its complement. This degree is unrelated to the level \(N\). By compactness a complex stadium \(D\) around \([0,1]\) can be chosen so that \(p(D)\subset\mathcal P\cap(\mathbb C^*)^m\). On it define \[ w(s)=p(s),\quad t(s)=2\arctan w(s),\qquad \chi_v(s)= rac{i}{\pi}\mathcal P_v(t(s)). 	ag{21} \] These independent complex charges equal the chosen small seed vector at \(s=0\) and \(\mathbf1\) at \(s=1\). Equations (15), (17), (21) give a full critical point of the original phase for every \(s\in D\). Let \(S(s)\) be its marked critical value. It is holomorphic, as are all coefficients \(a_j(p(s))\), and \(a_0(p(s))\) is a unit throughout \(D\). Its charge curve lies in the single global chart \(\mathcal C_{\mathbf n}\). The construction never requires a common real charge path or a path with fixed filling periods. Freeze the initialized contour family's heights, cuts and currents once at the seed. The actual family used along the curve is \[ \mathscr G_N(s)= \mathfrak Z_{N,\mathbf+}(\mathbf n, oldsymbol\chi(s);\mathbf0), \qquad \varepsilon_N=\prod_v e^{\pi in_v(N-1)^2/(4N)}. 	ag{22} \] It is holomorphic on \(D\), with the actual all-order initializer near \(s=0\), and it has the original endpoint \(Z_N^{m original}=\varepsilon_N\mathscr G_N(1)\). The formal coefficients just constructed are exactly the analytic continuations of that initializer. ## 5. The remaining upper estimate The adopted polynomial upper-bound criterion now applies if \[ \sup_K\left|N^{- eta}e^{-NS(s)}\mathscr G_N(s)ight| \le C_KN^{B_K}\qquad(K\Subset D), 	ag{23} \] or if its local complex-area \(L^2\) version holds. It gives the full asymptotic expansion throughout \(D\), and in particular \[ Z_N^{m original} =\varepsilon_NN^ eta e^{NS(1)} \{a_0(p(1))+O(N^{-1})\}. 	ag{24} \] Within this supplied positive-target class, the formal continuation, regular marked path and target leading unit required by that criterion have thus been constructed. Estimate (23) has not been proved. The source in it is the same frozen ordinary-polynomial contour representative, with every original current retained. No global one-phase asymptotic for individual exact factorials is inferred from their formal coefficients. No free cardinal end or reversed-index edge is assigned the phase (2). Outside data remain complete; a general incoming-boundary initializer is not supplied. Nor is a positive lift of every hyperbolic short filling established. For a knot conclusion the original source identification, peripheral marking and equality \(2\pi\Re S(1)=\operatorname{Vol}\) must still be retained or proved. There is no new volume lower bound here. ## Complete direct sources The proof uses the following complete matching source texts. All coefficients and marks are those of these versions. - Factorial amplitude, 380 lines: [research_two_square_factorial_amplitude.md](research_two_square_factorial_amplitude.md), 995c38d1cc6fcd5a1a1306601778ce6068b5f1d766364216e7cdd933f344290f. - Full independent phase, 411 lines: [research_unsummed_two_square_morse_lift.md](research_unsummed_two_square_morse_lift.md), 82ad7a75e6ab2857bbebb2f003f7e182ab1f26da1cf425f579106cdad11d15dd. - Original local finite index sum, 351 lines: [research_regular_zero_subtree_low_source.md](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_regular_zero_subtree_low_source.md), 06e4b7c14e3a61616dea61642103e2d2803709fcd465ae9860258119db3299d1. - Initialized actual contour family, 370 lines: [research_pattern_adapted_polarized_heat_initializer.md](research_pattern_adapted_polarized_heat_initializer.md), a27c25dae7f3be3f1ef52fb369ecca822b0896a4b034450131e05b12423c2694. - Positive tangent contractions and original wire marks, 531 lines: [research_positive_wire_product_contour.md](research_positive_wire_product_contour.md), 5646f2d6b2a8dfa2d8c49662d17f19f3743fc4efcaf3c3685c6a899975a4c230. - Original positive edge matrix, 678 lines: [research_positive_edge_global_monotonicity.md](research_positive_edge_global_monotonicity.md), da5129c7110190035eedb8249d4004dd06b5a7555e78d948234d8de50fa17500. - Polynomial-loss continuation criterion, 289 lines: [research_polarized_polynomial_upper_criterion.md](research_polarized_polynomial_upper_criterion.md), 1a7ca165e0bc3b6e115566859e2a780079389d3004e6915ff396eb7c9ca47d9a.

title: A real negative factorial argument at a positive primitive star
text: # A real negative factorial argument at a positive primitive star Private written proof, 15 November 2026. Positive primitive geometry does not force the canonical Newton factorial arguments into their original strip. For every integer central power \(n\ge5\), a sufficiently large fixed degree admits an original positive star whose two-leaf multiplication gate has a real argument \(x+y-z\) strictly between \(-1\) and \(0\). The outside angles are prescribed and noncomplete. This is not an exhibited knot exterior or a complete global filling. All leaves in the construction are identical. Consequently every binary multiplication tree in the resolution that leaves one factor for the final pairing and puts all crossings after the products contains this gate. No assertion is made about redistributing crossings among proper subproducts. ## 1. An exact positive star with its primitive period Fix \(n\in\mathbb Z\), \(n\ge5\), and put \[ \theta=\frac{2\pi}{n}\in(0,\pi/2),\qquad t=\theta-iH,\qquad a=\tan(t/2),\qquad r=\frac{nH}{2d},\qquad H>0. \tag{1} \] Here \(d\ge3\) will be a fixed integer. At each of the \(d\) outside endpoints choose \[ w=a\,\operatorname{csch}r,\qquad b=\sqrt{w^2-1}\quad(\Re b>0),\qquad q=a\coth r,\qquad u=2\arctan b. \tag{2} \] The inverse tangent is its canonical branch with \(|\Re u|<\pi\). In fact \(\Re a>0,\ \Im a<0\), so \(\Re w>0,\ \Im w<0\); the square root in (2) has positive real part and negative imaginary part. All these functions are regular near any fixed \(H>0\). These are positive configurations of the original edge block. To prove this directly, write \(w=X+iY\), \(X>0\). Then \[ (\Re\sqrt{w^2-1})^2 =\frac{|w^2-1|+X^2-Y^2-1}{2}<X^2, \tag{3} \] because \[ (|w|^2+1)^2-|w^2-1|^2=4X^2>0. \tag{4} \] Also \[ q^2=1+a^2+b^2,\qquad \Re q>0,\qquad (\Re q)^2-(\Re a)^2=(\Re w)^2>(\Re b)^2. \tag{5} \] The original positive-edge criterion \(\Re q>\sqrt{(\Re a)^2+(\Re b)^2}\) therefore holds strictly. It proves positivity of all eight original edge tetrahedra, with the canonical branches. In particular no new geometric edge model is being substituted. The return at the central endpoint is exactly \(r\). Indeed, \[ \frac{q+a}{q-a}=e^{2r}. \tag{6} \] The canonical return satisfies \(e^{2r_t}=(q+a)/(q-a)\) and \(|\Im r_t|<\pi/2\); since \(r>0\) is real, (6) fixes \(r_t=r\). Thus the full central marked period is \[ \sum_{e=1}^d r_e-\frac{int}{2} =dr-\frac{in(\theta-iH)}2 =-\pi i . \tag{7} \] This is the primitive equation with the literal integer power \(n\), not only its exponentiated version. Once \(H\) is chosen, all outside angles \(u\) in (2) are held fixed. They are noncomplete: \(b\ne0\), since \(w\) has nonzero imaginary part. No primitive equations are imposed at those outside endpoints. ## 2. The actual two-leaf prefix labels Allocate no crossing to the first products. The original prefix dictionary gives the two identical input labels and their output: \[ x=y=\frac1\pi\arctan\!\left(\frac{\tanh r}{a}\right), \qquad z=\frac1\pi\arctan\!\left(\frac{\tanh(2r)}{a}\right). \tag{8} \] For large \(d\), these are the analytic inverse-tangent branches near zero; no integer lift is reset. They correspond to the returns \(r,r,2r\), respectively. The two-leaf set is proper when \(d\ge3\). Their branch also agrees with continuation from positive real labels: for \(R>0\) and \(\Re a>0,\ \Im a\le0\), the argument \(\tanh R/a\) has positive real part, and the inverse tangent is analytic there with its value fixed on the positive real axis. This gives the stated lift without crossing either inverse-tangent pole. Write \[ \Delta_d(H)=2x-z,\qquad f(H)=\frac1a+\frac1{a^3}. \tag{9} \] Taylor expansion of the analytic functions at \(r=0\) gives, uniformly for \(H\) near any fixed positive value, \[ \frac1\pi\arctan\!\left(\frac{\tanh r}{a}\right) =\frac{r}{\pi a}-\frac{r^3}{3\pi} \left(\frac1a+\frac1{a^3}\right) +O(r^5), \qquad \Delta_d(H)=\frac{2r^3}{\pi}f(H)+O(r^5). \tag{10} \] The remainders and their fixed derivatives are uniform there. ## 3. A transverse real negative value Put \(c=\cos\theta>0\) and \(s=\sin\theta>0\). The exact expression \[ \frac1a=A+iB =\frac{s+i\sinh H}{\cosh H-c} \tag{11} \] has \(A,B>0\). Consequently \[ \begin{split} \Im f(H) &=B(1+3A^2-B^2)\\ &=\frac{2B\{2-c^2-c\cosh H\}} {(\cosh H-c)^2}. \end{split} \tag{12} \] It has exactly one positive zero, namely \[ H_0=\operatorname{arcosh}(2/c-c)>0. \tag{13} \] At that zero, \[ A=\frac{c}{2s},\qquad B^2=1+3A^2,\qquad \Re f(H_0)=-2A(1+4A^2)=-\frac{c}{s^3}<0, \tag{14} \] and differentiating (12) gives \[ \left.\frac{d}{dH}\Im f(H)\right|_{H_0} =-\frac{c^2(4-c^2)}{4s^4}<0. \tag{15} \] **Theorem.** For every fixed integer \(n\ge5\), and every sufficiently large fixed integer \(d\), there is \[ H_d=H_0+O_n(d^{-2}) \tag{16} \] for which the original positive primitive star (1)--(7) has \[ \boxed{\quad \Delta_d(H_d)\in(-1,0),\qquad \Delta_d(H_d)= -\frac{n^3H_0^3\cos\theta}{4\pi\sin^3\theta}\,d^{-3} +O_n(d^{-5}). \quad} \tag{17} \] **Proof.** Regard \(\delta=1/d\) temporarily as a real parameter, with \(r=nH\delta/2\). The quotient \[ F(\delta,H)=\frac{\pi\Delta_d(H)}{2r^3} \tag{18} \] has a removable extension at \(\delta=0\). It is real analytic in \((\delta,H)\) near \((0,H_0)\), and (10) gives \(F(\delta,H)=f(H)+O_n(\delta^2)\). By (12)--(15), the real equation \(\Im F(\delta,H)=0\) has a unique nearby real solution \(H(\delta)=H_0+O_n(\delta^2)\). This is the real implicit-function theorem with nonzero \(H\)-derivative (15). At that solution \(\Re F<0\) for small positive \(\delta\), by (14). Substituting \(r=nH(\delta)\delta/2\) and (14) in (10) proves (17). Now take \(\delta=1/d\) for every sufficiently large integer \(d\). The choices of \(n,d,H_d\) are fixed before any quantum level \(N\) tends to infinity. Positivity and the complete central period were already proved exactly in (5)--(7). \(\square\) All the other arguments of this multiplication gate remain nonreal with positive imaginary part. Indeed \(x\), \(z\), \(2x\), and \(z-x\) have respective leading terms \[ \frac r\pi(A+iB),\quad \frac{2r}\pi(A+iB),\quad \frac{2r}\pi(A+iB),\quad \frac r\pi(A+iB), \tag{19} \] with \(B(H_0)>0\). The only real argument among its seven factorial arguments is the negative \(\Delta_d(H_d)\). It is noninteger, so this does not contradict the proper-prefix sine exclusions. ## 4. Source and resolution scope The original gate is \[ \mu_N(Nx,Ny,Nz)= \frac{G_N(N(x+y))G_N(Nz)} {G_N(Nx)G_N(Ny)G_N(N(z-x))G_N(N(z-y)) G_N(N(x+y-z))}. \tag{20} \] Its last argument at (17) belongs to the real chamber \((-1,0)\), with denominator multiplicity \(-1\). The exact factorial chamber formula therefore retains the factor \[ 1-e^{\tau2\pi iN\Delta_d(H_d)} \tag{21} \] for either indicated continuation side \(\tau=\pm1\), together with the corresponding marked action and nonzero local remainder. This factor is not an asymptotically constant unit on a neighborhood of that real point. Equation (17) by itself does not assert that it vanishes at that fixed point for any particular level. For the leave-one-factor resolution with all crossing layers after the products, the \(d-1\) multiplication inputs are identical copies of (8). Every full binary tree with at least two leaves has an internal vertex whose two children are leaves: take a deepest internal vertex. Hence every such binary parenthesization contains exactly the two-leaf gate analyzed above. Reassociation within this specified resolution does not remove it. Redistributing crossings before products changes the prefix returns and is not covered by this assertion. The example concerns an original positive edge star with a primitive central filling and prescribed noncomplete outside angles. It does not exhibit an actual knot exterior realizing those angles, or a globally filled knot. It rules out inferring the original factorial strip solely from positive primitive geometry, even in this simple boundary problem. The chamber formula retains the relevant Fourier factor; no obstruction to a complete corrected contour proof or to the volume identity is inferred. ## Direct sources * [Positive edge geometry](research_positive_edge_global_monotonicity.md), SHA256 \(\texttt{da5129c7110190035eedb8249d4004dd06b5a7555e78d948234d8de50fa17500}\): original eight-shape positivity criterion, canonical returns and branches, and the full marked primitive equation. * [Positive primitive prefixes](research_positive_primitive_prefix_regularity.md), SHA256 \(\texttt{a01b55a71d133aadff4aac0929e50de03e1059991d6874e81646c770eb5604a6}\): exact prefix label dictionary and the specified leave-one algebraic resolution. * [Newton factorial chamber atlas](research_newton_factorial_chamber_atlas.md), SHA256 \(\texttt{34d6e0e4e82a98bf8e6063558ecafdedb0a58d6229fbe462e7e4bfff48f4db4c}\): literal gate factorials and the retained real-chamber multiplier. All arguments are written analytic and algebraic proofs. No mathematical code, numerical evaluation, tests or compilation are used.

title: Positive Ward measure and the coherent Cauchy tail of an original turn
text: # Positive Ward measure and the coherent Cauchy tail of an original turn Private written proof, 17 November 2026. The source-exact Ward representative has a positive Stieltjes density on its actual spectral cut. The double physical rows are exactly orthogonal for the resulting finite-moment measure. This identifies the jump of a general turned source by an exact Plancherel formula. More particularly, the difference between its canonical polynomial and its Ward representative is one Cauchy transform. Orthogonality turns its estimate into a sum of inverse physical rows. The estimate applies to every actual input, including a product of received sources followed by any original integer multiplication crossing. No input first normal is estimated or discarded in this step. This controls the coherent null correction, not the Ward representative itself or a subsequent prescribed scalar. ## 1. Original source and one global Ward pair Put \[ N\ge2,\quad D=N-1,\quad m=\lfloor N/2\rfloor,\quad \theta=\pi/N,\quad \eta=(-1)^D, \] \[ c_j=2\cos((2j+1)\theta),\qquad P_N(C)=2T_N(C/2)+2,\qquad \mathcal A_N=\mathbb C[C]/(P_N). \tag{1} \] The double indices are \(0\le j<m\). At odd \(N=2m+1\), the remaining simple node is \(c_*=-2\). Write \(\theta_j=(2j+1)\theta\) and \(a_j=4-c_j^2\). The original Newton data are \[ s_r=2\sin(r\theta),\quad S_r=\prod_{b=1}^r s_b,\quad e_r(C)=S_r^{-2}\prod_{a<r}(c_a-C),\quad K_N(w,C)=\sum_{r=0}^{D}e_r(w)e_r(C), \] with empty products equal to one. The original normalization is \[ \phi_N(f)=\eta N^2[C^D]\operatorname{rem}_{P_N}f,\qquad Te_r=e_{D-r}, \] \[ F_j(C)=K_N(c_j,C),\qquad G_j(C)=\partial_wK_N(c_j,C). \tag{2} \] There is no \(G_*\). The pinned confluent source proves \[ TF_j=\delta_j=\frac{P_N(C)}{\eta N^2(C-c_j)},\quad \phi_N(\delta_j f)=f(c_j),\quad \phi_N(G_jF_k)=\frac{\eta}{a_j}\delta_{jk}, \tag{3} \] for double \(j,k\), and \(T\) is a bilinear Frobenius isometry and an involution. Let \(\Omega=\mathbb C\setminus[2,\infty)\). The original even Ward representative of \(G_0\) is denoted by \(\widetilde Q_N\). With \(C=-2\cos t\) and \(|\Re t|<\pi\), it is \[ \widetilde Q_N(C)=- \frac{g_N'(D/2-t/(2\theta))-g_N'(0)} {2\theta\sin\theta}, \] \[ g_N'(z)=\frac{\pi}{N^2} \sum_{r=0}^{D}(z-r)\cot\frac{\pi(z-r)}N . \tag{4} \] Evenness permits spectral descent through \(C=-2\). This gives one holomorphic function on \(\Omega\), real on \((-\infty,2)\), with \(\widetilde Q_N(c_0)=0\). It has the full physical Hermite data of \(G_0\). For \(j\ge1\) in the double range, retain the original common-shift determinant and its derivative \[ F_j^\epsilon(C)= \frac{\det(\mathcal J_j(\epsilon)-CI)} {\prod_{r<j} A(r+\epsilon)},\qquad R_j(C)=\partial_\epsilon F_j^\epsilon(C)|_{\epsilon=0}, \qquad R_0=0, \] \[ c'(j)=-4\theta\sin\theta_j,\qquad \widehat G_j(C)= \frac{c'(0)F_j(C)\widetilde Q_N(C)+R_j(C)}{c'(j)} . \tag{5} \] Here \(c_0\) is fixed during the common shift. The complete normal-source theorem proves that \(\widehat G_j\) has the original value and first inner normal of \(G_j\) at every double physical node, and its value at the odd simple node. For \(j=0\), (5) means \(\widehat G_0=\widetilde Q_N\). At \(N=2\) this is the only normal row, so no nontrivial common-shift determinant is needed. For an arbitrary actual \(A\in\mathcal A_N\), put \[ H_A=\operatorname{can}(TA). \] Expanding its original input trace gives the exact ordinary polynomial formula \[ H_A(C)=\eta\sum_{j<m} \{a_jA(c_j)G_j(C)+(a_jA'(c_j)-c_jA(c_j))F_j(C)\} +\mathbf1_{\mathrm{odd}}A(-2)F_*(C). \tag{6} \] Replace only \(G_j\) by (5), and define \[ \widehat H_A=Y_A+\widetilde Q_N L_A, \qquad L_A=4\eta\sin\theta\sum_{j<m}\sin\theta_j A(c_j)F_j, \tag{7} \] \[ Y_A=\eta\sum_{j<m} \left\{\frac{a_jA(c_j)}{c'(j)}R_j +(a_jA'(c_j)-c_jA(c_j))F_j\right\} +\mathbf1_{\mathrm{odd}}A(-2)F_* . \tag{8} \] Thus \(\widehat H_A\) is source-equivalent to \(H_A\) with all physical normals retained. Their difference divided by \(P_N\) is holomorphic on \(\Omega\), including the physical nodes. The polynomial degrees satisfy \[ \deg L_A\le m-1,\qquad \deg Y_A\le \begin{cases}m-1,&N=2m,\\m,&N=2m+1.\end{cases} \tag{9} \] The formulas hold with arbitrary ordinary free spectator coefficients and may be differentiated in those coefficients. ## 2. The positive cut measure For \(x>2\), set \(h(x)=\operatorname{arcosh}(x/2)>0\) and \[ \rho_N(x)=\frac{N}{4\pi\sin\theta} \tanh\frac{Nh(x)}2,\qquad d\mu_N(x)=\frac{N^2\rho_N(x)}{P_N(x)}\,dx. \tag{10} \] This is a positive measure on \((2,\infty)\): \[ P_N(2\cosh h)=e^{Nh}(1+e^{-Nh})^2>0. \] Its moments through degree \(N-2\) are finite. Indeed \(\rho_N(x)=O_N(\sqrt{x-2})\) at \(2\), while at infinity \[ \rho_N(x)=b_N+O_N(x^{-N}),\qquad b_N=\frac{N}{4\pi\sin\theta},\qquad P_N(x)\sim x^N. \tag{11} \] The moment of degree \(N-1\) diverges logarithmically. **Theorem 1.** On the entire slit plane, \[ \boxed{\quad \widetilde Q_N(C)=\int_2^\infty \rho_N(x) \left(\frac1{x-C}-\frac1{x-c_0}\right)dx . \quad} \tag{12} \] In particular \(\widetilde Q_N\) has positive imaginary part in the upper half-plane. For every polynomial \(f\) with \(\deg f\le N-2\), \[ \boxed{\quad \phi_N(G_0f)=\eta\int_2^\infty f\,d\mu_N.\quad} \tag{13} \] **Proof.** The pinned Ward monodromy gives the exact upper-minus-lower spectral jump \[ \widetilde Q_{N,+}(2\cosh h) -\widetilde Q_{N,-}(2\cosh h) =\frac{iN}{2\sin\theta}\tanh(Nh/2) =2\pi i\rho_N(2\cosh h). \tag{14} \] The integral in (12) converges normally on compact slit sets. It has that same jump and vanishes at \(c_0\). At \(2\), both functions are bounded. For the integral this follows from the local square-root behavior of its density; for the Ward function it follows from (4) at \(t=\pm\pi\). For completeness the normalization at infinity does not leave an unproved entire term. Use the branch with \(|\Re t|\le\pi\), \(\Im t>0\) at large \(|C|\). The finite cotangent sum in (4) gives \[ g_N'(D/2-t/(2\theta)) =-it/2+O_N((1+|t|)e^{-\Im t}). \tag{15} \] Here \(\cot z=i+O(e^{2\Im z})\) in the lower half-plane, and the centered finite sum of its linear factors is exact. Since \(\log(-C)=-it+o(1)\) on this slit branch, \(\widetilde Q_N(C)=-b_N\log(-C)+O_N(1)\). The integral in (12) has \(O_N(1+\log|C|)\) growth: split its density as \(b_N+(\rho_N-b_N)\), use \[ \int_2^\infty \left(\frac1{x-C}-\frac1{x-c_0}\right)dx =\log\frac{2-c_0}{2-C}, \] and the integrable \(O_N(x^{-N})\) tail in (11). Its derivative is \(O_N(x^{-N-1})\) at infinity. Thus the same bound holds up to either large cut bank: split the tail integral into \(x<R/2\), \(R/2<x<3R/2\), and \(x>3R/2\), and subtract its value at \(x=R\) in the middle interval. The subtracted numerator is bounded by \(O_N(R^{-N-1}|x-R|)\); the constant part has an explicit logarithmic integral. These estimates also bound the limiting principal values. The difference therefore extends through the cut and its endpoint to an entire function of logarithmic growth. Cauchy's derivative estimate makes it constant, and its value at \(c_0\) is zero. This proves (12). The positive imaginary part follows directly from the integrand, because the subtraction is real. Apply a whole keyhole contour to \(\widetilde Q_N(C)f(C)/P_N(C)\). Its outer integral tends to zero: the integrand is \(O_N(\log R/R^2)\) when \(\deg f\le N-2\). The cap at \(2\) tends to zero as well. The physical residues equal those of \(G_0f/P_N\), including the double-node residues. With the upper bank oriented from \(2\) to infinity, (14) gives \[ \sum_{\text{physical poles}}\operatorname{Res} \frac{\widetilde Q_N f}{P_N} =\int_2^\infty \frac{\rho_N f}{P_N}\,dx. \tag{16} \] Multiplication by \(\eta N^2\) is the original closing, which proves (13). No normal or endpoint pole has been replaced by a distinct-value trace. \(\square\) ## 3. Exact physical-row orthogonality and jump Plancherel **Theorem 2.** For the entire double-index range, \[ \boxed{\quad \int_2^\infty F_j(x)F_k(x)\,d\mu_N(x) =\frac{\delta_{jk}}{4\sin\theta\sin\theta_j}. \quad} \tag{17} \] Consequently \[ \boxed{\quad \int_2^\infty |L_A(x)|^2\,d\mu_N(x) =4\sin\theta\sum_{j<m}\sin\theta_j|A(c_j)|^2. \quad} \tag{18} \] Every \(F_j\) in (17) has simple roots in \((2,\infty)\). The degree-zero row has no roots. **Proof.** Use the whole keyhole for \(\widehat G_j(C)F_k(C)/P_N(C)\). Its numerator has growth at most \(O_N(C^{j+k}\log C)\), where \(j+k\le N-2\). Thus the outer circle vanishes just as in (16). Its jump is \[ 2\pi i\rho_N(C)\frac{c'(0)}{c'(j)}F_j(C)F_k(C). \] Source equivalence and (3) yield \[ \frac{\eta}{a_j}\delta_{jk} =\eta\frac{c'(0)}{c'(j)} \int F_jF_k\,d\mu_N. \tag{19} \] Since \(a_j=4\sin^2\theta_j\) and \(c'(0)/c'(j)=\sin\theta/\sin\theta_j\), this is (17). All moments used are finite, also at \(N=2\). Real coefficients and expansion of (7) give (18). The rows \(F_0,\ldots,F_{j-1}\) span all polynomials of degree below \(j\). Thus \(F_j\) is orthogonal to that whole space for a strictly positive measure on \((2,\infty)\). The usual sign-change proof is elementary here: multiply \(F_j\) by the product of its roots where its sign changes in this interval. If there were fewer than \(j\) such roots, the resulting nonzero polynomial would have one sign on the support, but zero integral by orthogonality. This contradiction proves the root assertion, including simplicity. \(\square\) At odd \(N=2m+1\), the simple row \(F_*\) has degree \(m\). Its squared norm for \(\mu_N\) diverges logarithmically; it is deliberately absent from (17)--(18). Its actual simple physical value is retained in \(Y_A\). For \(N=2\), the family in (17) is just \(F_0=1\); the formulas give \(\mu_N((2,\infty))=1/4\). In general the mass is \(1/(4\sin^2\theta)\). One exact closing interpretation of (18) is worth keeping. If \(\deg B\le m-1\), the same whole contour gives \[ \phi_N((TA)B)=\eta\int_2^\infty L_A(x)B(x)\,d\mu_N(x). \tag{20} \] The degree bound ensures that \(Y_AB/P_N\) and \(\widetilde Q_NL_AB/P_N\) have vanishing outer circles at both parities. Thus this is the original closing in its stated range, not a newly selected positive observation. ## 4. The coherent null tail and its inverse-row estimate **Theorem 3.** For every actual \(A\in\mathcal A_N\), \[ \boxed{\quad \frac{\widehat H_A(C)-H_A(C)}{P_N(C)} =\frac1{N^2}\int_2^\infty \frac{L_A(x)}{x-C}\,d\mu_N(x). \quad} \tag{21} \] The left side is interpreted by holomorphic continuation at the physical nodes. On \(\Omega\), writing \(d(C)=\operatorname{dist}(C,[2,\infty))>0\), one has \[ \boxed{\quad \left|\frac{\widehat H_A(C)-H_A(C)}{P_N(C)}\right| \le\frac1{N^2d(C)} \sum_{j<m}\frac{|A(c_j)|}{|F_j(C)|}. \quad} \tag{22} \] There is no input-normal term or odd-simple-value term in this exact tail. **Proof.** Set \(f=(\widehat H_A-H_A)/P_N\). The full source equivalence removes all physical poles. The function is bounded at \(2\), has jump \[ f_+-f_-=2\pi i\,\frac{\rho_N L_A}{P_N}, \] and tends to zero at infinity. More precisely (9) and \(\deg H_A\le N-1\) give \(f=O_N(1/C)\), with a smaller logarithmic contribution. Its jump density is integrable at both ends of the cut. The keyhole Cauchy formula for \(f(z)/(z-C)\) therefore has no outer-circle or endpoint term and gives (21). This proves its plus sign with the same upper-minus-lower convention as (14). For a double row put \[ S_j(C)=\int_2^\infty\frac{F_j(x)}{x-C}\,d\mu_N(x). \] The polynomial \((F_j(x)-F_j(C))/(x-C)\) has degree below \(j\). Orthogonality consequently gives the exact identity \[ F_j(C)S_j(C) =\int_2^\infty\frac{F_j(x)^2}{x-C}\,d\mu_N(x). \tag{23} \] There is no zero of \(F_j(C)\) off the cut. Positivity of the squared integrand's measure and (17) now imply \[ |S_j(C)|\le \frac1{4\sin\theta\sin\theta_j\,d(C)\,|F_j(C)|}. \tag{24} \] Insert (7) into (21) and use (24). The normalization factors cancel exactly, giving (22). \(\square\) The estimate is for a coherent Cauchy tail. It does not estimate \(Y_A\) and \(\widetilde Q_NL_A\) separately. In particular (18) is compatible with those two channels having large compensating values away from the grid. There is also uniform control of fixed output derivatives. For every compact \(K\Subset\Omega\) and fixed \(r\ge0\), \[ \left|\partial_C^r \frac{\widehat H_A-H_A}{P_N}(C)\right| \le C_{K,r}N^{r-2} \sum_{j<m}\frac{|A(c_j)|}{|F_j(C)|}, \qquad C\in K. \tag{25} \] Indeed all roots of \(F_j\) lie on the cut and \(j<N\). On a disk of radius \(d(C)/(4N)\), each root factor changes by a ratio between \(1-1/(4N)\) and \(1+1/(4N)\). Hence \(F_j\) changes by bounded factors, uniformly in \(j,N\). Apply (22) there and Cauchy's estimate. Derivatives in any free spectator parameter instead replace \(A(c_j)\) by its corresponding derivative, by the exact linearity of (21). ## 5. Original composition and the retained closing Let \(H_1,\ldots,H_s\in\mathcal A_N\) be any actual received sources, with their full canonical jets, and let \(p\in\mathbb Z\). Use the original input \[ A=\operatorname{can}\left(R^p\prod_{a=1}^sH_a\right). \tag{26} \] Every original physical crossing value has modulus one. Therefore Theorem 3 gives directly \[ \left|\frac{\widehat H_A-T(R^p\prod_aH_a)}{P_N}(C)\right| \le\frac1{N^2d(C)} \sum_{j<m}\frac{\prod_a|H_a(c_j)|}{|F_j(C)|}. \tag{27} \] Here the turned expression means its canonical polynomial. This estimate holds for every integer \(p\); no derivative of the crossing is omitted from \(Y_A\). Products and canonical reduction preserve the values used on the right. All original normal data remain in the exact representative (7)--(8) and its source equivalence. For clarity, for arbitrary \(A,B\in\mathcal A_N\), the full two-source Frobenius pairing also has an exact cut formula. Put \[ Q_{\mathrm R}(x)=\frac{\widetilde Q_{N,+}(x) +\widetilde Q_{N,-}(x)}2. \] Schwarz reflection makes this real. The whole keyhole gives \[ \begin{split} \phi_N((TA)(TB))={}& \mathbf1_{\mathrm{odd}}A(-2)B(-2)\\ &+\eta\int_2^\infty \{Y_AL_B+L_AY_B+2Q_{\mathrm R}L_AL_B\}\,d\mu_N . \end{split} \tag{28} \] Every cut term converges. At even levels the outer circle vanishes. At odd \(N=2m+1\), only the product of the leading \(Y\) coefficients contributes. Indeed \(F_*=K_N(-2,C)\) has leading coefficient \((-1)^m/N\): \(e_m(-2)=1\) because \(c_a+2=s_{m-a}^2\) for \(a<m\), and \(S_m^2=N\). Thus the outer coefficient is \(A(-2)B(-2)/N^2\), giving the displayed simple term. The jump of the product is precisely the integrand in (28) times \(2\pi i\rho_N\), which fixes its sign. The cut pairing on \((Y,L)\) has matrix \[ \begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&2Q_{\mathrm R}\end{pmatrix} \] and determinant \(-1\). It therefore retains the indefinite original Frobenius closing, rather than turning that closing into the positive jump norm (18). No conclusion here bounds \(\widehat H_A\) on a parent contour, pays the right side of (27) by a prescribed joint action, or proves a nonzero coefficient after another shared trace. Those remain distinct source estimates. ## 6. Complete direct sources All three entire direct texts were read and their used implications checked at these pins: * [Odd Ward logarithmic factorial](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_odd_ward_logarithmic_factorial.md), SHA256 63ae4693846f00a9b843b98b423959964a8ccb3a72dc8ee0fc1ac36b69f3d4b8: finite cotangent formula, even full-jet representative, its normalization, poles and angular monodromy. * [Coherent full-normal physical products](research_physical_products_full_normal_coherent_contour.md), SHA256 2f150a6d5a901521637f67c6db8fac96c6c6a14a0b23546e8383d1565189d574: exact common-shift normal representative, polynomial remainder, upper-minus-lower Ward cut and original contour orientation. * [Confluent row closing](research_confluent_row_closing_and_positive_quotient.md), SHA256 daf5760f74dbd9d9c9646a1a18b95cdffc1f42ebc3cbcfc0a1b9f79b2ad77251: full original trace, reproducing rows, degrees, Frobenius pairing, signed crossing values and normals. Only written mathematics, source-text reads and metadata hashes were used. No mathematical program, numerical experiment, test, build or compilation was run. Frozen source notes and public manuscripts are unchanged.

title: A product domain and exact wire contour through a positive source point
text:
# A product domain and exact wire contour through a positive source point Private written proof, 16 November 2026. Fix a positive configuration of the original same-index circle-tree edge geometry. There is a product of angular domains, independent of the level, which contains every full real angular interval and this configuration, and on which all stationary wire branches are single valued, even and holomorphic. The domains narrow near the angular endpoints; fixed-depth rectangular domains generally cannot do this. The reciprocal factorial divisor theorem then gives an exact original source contour through this entire stationary graph. Its wire endpoints stay fixed, so no moving-wire seam current is introduced. A coherent local Morse segment can be included. This is a reachability theorem for a representative of the whole source, not an estimate on its connectors or a proof of a surviving geometric coefficient. ## 1. The original stationary relation Let a finite graph have angular variables \(t_v\), with \[ \mathcal S=\{t:|\Re t|<\pi\},\qquad a_v=	an(t_v/2),\qquad \mathcal A=\mathbb C\setminus  igl(i[1,\infty)\cup-i[1,\infty) igr). 	ag{1} \] The maps \(t\mapsto	an(t/2)\) and \(a\mapsto2\arctan a\) are inverse biholomorphisms between these domains. The inverse is the branch through zero. Loops and repeated edges are allowed. Fixed outside angular parameters may be included in the geometric statements and then held fixed. Every variable used in the positive whole-phase Morse conclusion is assumed incident to at least one edge. For a same-index edge \(e=vw\), the original unsummed phase is \[ F_e(x;t,u)=b(x,t)+b(x,u),\qquad b(x,t)=-J(1/2-x+t/(2\pi))-J(1/2-x-t/(2\pi))-2J(x), \quad J'(z)=\Log(2\sin\pi z). 	ag{2} \] Branches in (2) are the continued original ones. The pinned unsummed-source calculation gives \[ q_e^2=1+a_v^2+a_w^2,\qquad \cot(\pi x_e^*)=q_e,\qquad H_e=-F_{e,xx}(x_e^*) = rac{2\pi q_e(1+q_e^2)^2} {(1+a_v^2)(1+a_w^2)}. 	ag{3} \] Fix a configuration \(a_v^*\in\mathcal A\) at which every original edge is positive. The exact positive-edge criterion is \[ \Re q_e> \sqrt{(\Re a_v^*)^2+(\Re a_w^*)^2}, \qquad q_e(0,0)=1. 	ag{4} \] No filling equation is needed until a geometric critical point of the whole phase is specified. In the source application below, the traced target angles have negative imaginary parts. ## 2. Independent tangent contractions and a product neighborhood **Lemma 1.** If an original edge is positive at \((a,b)\), it remains positive at \((\lambda a,\mu b)\) for all \[ 0\le\lambda,\mu\le1. 	ag{5} \] **Proof.** Write \(a=A+i\alpha\), \(b=B+i eta\), and \[ X=A^2+B^2,\qquad Y=\alpha^2+ eta^2, \qquad C=A eta-B\alpha. 	ag{6} \] The pinned positive-edge theorem proves that, for \(X>0\), (4) is equivalent to \(C^2<X\); this inequality also excludes a nonpositive real value of \(1+a^2+b^2\). For \(X=0\), the criterion is \(Y<1\).
