If \(X>0\) and \(\lambda\mu>0\), \[ \lambda^2\mu^2 C^2 <\lambda^2\mu^2(A^2+B^2) \le\lambda^2A^2+\mu^2B^2. 	ag{7} \] If \(X=0\), independent contractions decrease \(Y\). When one contraction is zero, the remaining endpoint belongs to \(\mathcal A\). The one-complete-end edge is positive there: if its tangent has nonzero real part, \(C=0<X\); if it is purely imaginary, membership in \(\mathcal A\) gives modulus less than one. Both zero endpoints give the complete point. This proves every case. \(\square\) This is an independent-coordinate strengthening of the archived simultaneous contraction. It is not a path of solutions of fixed primitive filling equations. Set \[ K_v=\mathbb R\ \cup\ [-a_v^*,a_v^*]. 	ag{8} \] The second set is the straight complex line segment. It lies in \(\mathcal A\). Sign changes do not change the positivity criterion in (6), so Lemma 1 applies to any pair of points in the two finite segments. **Theorem 2.** There are symmetric star-shaped open sets \(U_v\subset\mathcal A\), containing \(K_v\), such that for every edge and every \((a,b)\in U_v	imes U_w\), \[ 1+a^2+b^2
otin(-\infty,0]. 	ag{9} \] Consequently the angular domains \[ V_v=2\arctan U_v\subset\mathcal S 	ag{10} \] are symmetric and simply connected, contain \((-\pi,\pi)\) and \(t_v^*\), and have bounded imaginary parts. On their product all the functions in (3) have globally defined branches satisfying \[ \Re q_e>0,\qquad 0<\Re x_e^*<	frac12, \qquad H_e
e0. 	ag{11} \] They are even in each independent endpoint angle. The branches agree with the original positive branches at the target. All these domains are chosen before \(N\). **Proof.** On segment times segment, (9) follows from Lemma 1. If \(a\) is real and \(b\in\mathcal A\), a nonpositive real value of \(1+a^2+b^2\) would require \(b^2\) real. For real \(b\) the sum is positive. For purely imaginary \(b\), its modulus is less than one, and the sum is again positive. Thus (9) holds on \(K_v	imes K_w\). Here is a neighborhood construction which also treats the unbounded real tails. For small \(\epsilon>0\), let \[ U_v=\{a:|\Im a|<\epsilon\} \ \cup\ \{a:\operatorname{dist}(a,[-a_v^*,a_v^*]) <\epsilon\}. 	ag{12} \] Each of the two sets is convex and contains zero, so the union is star shaped and symmetric. Choose \(\epsilon<1/4\) and smaller than the positive distance of all the finite segments from the inverse-tangent cuts. Then \(U_v\subset\mathcal A\). The second set in (12) is uniformly bounded, say by \(M\), after an initial choice of \(\epsilon\le1/4\). If both arguments lie in the horizontal strips, then \[ \Re(1+a^2+b^2) \ge1-2\epsilon^2+(\Re a)^2+(\Re b)^2>0. 	ag{13} \] If one argument lies in a bounded segment neighborhood and the other in a horizontal-strip tail with \(|\Re a|>R\), choose \(R^2>M^2+2\). The same real-part calculation gives positivity. The remaining pairs lie in a fixed compact set. Their limiting skeleton pairs satisfy (9), so their discriminants have positive distance from the closed nonpositive real ray. Decreasing \(\epsilon\) once more proves (9) for all these pairs. There are finitely many edges, so one common choice works. The principal square root now gives \(\Re q_e>0\) throughout. The map \[ x(q)= rac{1}{2\pi i}\Log rac{q+i}{q-i},\qquad x(1)=1/4, 	ag{14} \] is the inverse of \(\cot\pi x\) from the right half-plane to \(0<\Re x<1/2\), with the logarithm specified by this normalization. It supplies \(x_e^*\). The factors \(q_e\), \(q_e\pm i\), and \(1+a_v^2\) do not vanish, proving the last assertion in (11). The discriminant and its principal root are even in the endpoint angles; uniqueness of (14) proves the same for \(x_e^*\) and \(H_e\). Independent contraction to zero identifies the branches at the positive target. Finally, the inverse tangent has bounded imaginary part on the horizontal strip in (12), because \(\epsilon<1\), and on the bounded segment neighborhood away from its cuts. Thus each \(V_v\) has bounded imaginary part. Its simple connectedness and symmetry follow from (1) and (12). \(\square\) The product domains need not consist entirely of positive edge configurations. Equation (9), rather than positivity everywhere, is what is proved on their mixed real-axis/segment neighborhoods. ## 3. Exact factorial admissibility Use \(D=N-1\), \(N\ge2\), and the actual interpolation \[ B_N(x,t)= rac{N}{ G_N(D/2-Nx+Nt/(2\pi)) G_N(D/2-Nx-Nt/(2\pi))G_N(Nx)^2}. 	ag{15} \] The pinned divisor theorem, derived from the original gamma product, states \[ \operatorname{ord}_{z=k}G_N(z)=\lfloor k/Nfloor, \qquad k\in\mathbb Z, 	ag{16} \] and there are no other zeros or poles. In particular \(1/G_N\) is holomorphic on \(\Re z<N\). Its zeros at \(z=-r\), \(r\ge1\), have order \(\lceil r/Nceil\). This is an existing exact divisor result, not a new choice of factorial interpolation. **Lemma 3.** Put \[ b_N=-1/(2N),\qquad I_N=[b_N,b_N+1]. 	ag{17} \] For every compact subset of \[ \Re x\in I_N,\qquad |\Re t|<\pi, 	ag{18} \] both \(B_N(x,t)\) and \(B_N(D/N-x,t)\) are holomorphic on a neighborhood, with no restriction on the finite imaginary heights. **Proof.** The unshifted argument obeys \(\Re(Nx)\le N-1/2<N\). For either shifted argument, \[ \Re(D/2-Nx\pm Nt/(2\pi)) \le N/2+N|\Re t|/(2\pi)<N. 	ag{19} \] Equation (16) proves the assertion. Reflection \(x\mapsto D/N-x\) preserves \(I_N\), proving the other orientation. Strictness of the bounds on a compact set supplies the asserted open neighborhood. \(\square\) In particular the entire graph in Theorem 2 is pole-free for the exact factorials. Their values can be zero. Negative real factorial arguments and the exact zeros in (16) are not removed from the source, and no nonvanishing Stirling amplitude is inferred across them. The statement concerns holomorphy of the reciprocal factorials, not a globally nonvanishing logarithm of \(B_N\). ## 4. A representative of the original whole source First take a closed network whose traced vertices and paired wires are those of the pinned joint-lens theorem. At each vertex retain its fixed signed power \(R^{n_v}\), its original full-Hermite coupon and any specified polynomial spectator. Direct and reversed halfwires use exactly their original arguments. The geometric stationary assignment in Theorem 2 is asserted for the same-index edges of (2); a reversed kernel is not silently assigned that phase. Set \[ a_N=\pi- rac{\pi}{2N},\qquad \eta=(-1)^D,\qquad W_N(t)= rac{e^{-iNt}}{(1-\eta e^{-iNt})^2},\qquad C_{N,n}=e^{\pi i nD^2/(4N)}. 	ag{20} \] Choose full lower angular arcs \(\Gamma_{v,N}\subset V_v\) from \(-a_N\) to \(a_N\), passing through \(t_v^*\) when \(\Im t_v^*<0\). They can be chosen with horizontal tangent at the target. Such arcs exist: in tangent coordinates the neighborhood (12) contains the full real interval and the lower radial arm to \(a_v^*\). Two nearby sides of that arm, joined to the real spine, give a simple lower arc; a small local adjustment passes through the target with the stipulated tangent. Apply the biholomorphism (1), and make that last tangent adjustment in the open angular domain. The endpoints remain fixed. The arc may extend beyond their real coordinates but remains in \(\mathcal S\). Together with its reflected upper arc, each lower arc encloses exactly the original physical angular grid, once. There are no additional grid poles in \(\mathcal S\). Thus the full-grid lens identity of the pinned source remains valid on these arcs. The odd-level simple spectral node and every double-node normal have their original contributions. Fix real wire heights \(h_e\) and write \[ A_{e,N}=b_N+ih_e,\qquad B_{e,N}=b_N+1+ih_e. 	ag{21} \] For an edge assigned its stationary graph, use the broken path \[ \mathcal L_{e,N}(\mathbf t): A_{e,N}\longrightarrow x_e^*(\mathbf t) \longrightarrow B_{e,N}. 	ag{22} \] Both segments lie in \(\Re x\in I_N\), by (11), and depend holomorphically and evenly on their angular variables. Keep any other wire on its original horizontal interval. Parameterize each path on \([0,1]\), with its midpoint at \(1/2\). **Theorem 4.** Replacing every selected wire interval by (22) in the joint factorial-lens integral preserves the entire original source. In particular, for unit coupons the exact traced-network scalar is \[ Z_N=\mathfrak c_N \int_{\prod_v\Gamma_{v,N}} \int_{\prod_e\mathcal L_{e,N}(\mathbf t)} \Omega_{{m fac},N},\qquad \mathfrak c_N=N^{|E|}\prod_{v\in V}  rac{-N^2C_{N,n_v}}{\pi i}. 	ag{23} \] Here \(\Omega_{{m fac},N}\) is exactly the pinned joint top form, with its fixed coordinate order. It contains every actual halfwire factor (15), all polynomial spectators, and \(\prod_v\sin t_v\,W_N(t_v)e^{in_vNt_v^2/(4\pi)}\). For a nonunit coupon its original cosine factor is retained. Any pre-existing external framing normalization is unchanged. **Proof.** The original horizontal joint integral is exact by the pinned lens theorem. Lemma 3 extends its holomorphic factorial domain from the closed substrip used there to all of (18). For fixed wire values the factorial and polynomial spectators are even and holomorphic on \(\mathcal S\), so its residue proof applies to the full lower arcs just constructed. The original physical values and first normals, and the ordinary free boundary polynomials when present, have not changed. Now fix a tuple of angular points on these arcs. Interpolate pointwise between the horizontal path \(b_N+r+ih_e\) and (22). The real part remains in the convex interval \(I_N\), and the two endpoints stay at (21). Lemma 3 makes this a compact pole-free homotopy. Cauchy's theorem therefore preserves that wire integral. Apply the argument successively to every wire and then integrate the angular variables. All chains are compact at this fixed level. In the pullback of the joint top form, angular derivatives of a wire path wedge to zero against the retained full angular volume form, so this fiberwise calculation is exactly the stated joint integral. Thus no moving seam current occurs. The result also agrees with the fixed-face relative-source identity: both wire endpoint faces remain fixed throughout. Broken paths are piecewise smooth chains; no embedding assumption on an intermediate wire path is needed. This proves (23). \(\square\) The result also holds as an identity in ordinary free boundary polynomials when those ends retain the cardinal representative, as required by the original compiler. It does not identify the asymptotic phase of that free polynomial with a factorial phase. Accordingly the stationary interpretation of a wire with such a free end requires its own boundary-phase input; the exact contour identity itself does not. ## 5. Coherent Morse segments and their limitation For a compact angular product in Theorem 2, the holomorphic unit \(H_e\) has a coherent square root, fixed by the original positive value at completeness. A parameter Morse construction can be made uniformly on a neighborhood of this compact product. For precision put \(A=\cos^2(t/2)\), \(B=\cos^2(u/2)\), \(z(x)=\sin^2\pi x\). Near \(x=x_e^*\), use the logarithm equal to zero there in \[ F_{e,x}(x)=\Log rac{(A-z(x))(B-z(x))}{z(x)^2}. 	ag{24} \] All factors are units on the graph: besides \(\sin\pi x_e^*
e0\), the two differences equal \(A^2/(A+B)\) and \(B^2/(A+B)\). Integrating (24) from \(x_e^*\) defines the original phase difference \(F_e(x)-F_e(x_e^*)\), without resetting its critical constant. Division by \((x-x_e^*)^2\), followed by the coherent square root and the inverse function theorem, gives \[ x=X_e(\xi;\mathbf t),\qquad X_e(0;\mathbf t)=x_e^*, \quad F_e(X_e(\xi);\mathbf t) =F_e(x_e^*;\mathbf t)-\xi^2/2. 	ag{25} \] The maps are even in each angular variable. Compactness gives a common \(ho_N>0\) such that \(X_e(\xi;\mathbf t)\) is defined for \(|\xi|\leho_N\) on a neighborhood of all the angular paths and stays strictly inside the wire strip. Replace (22) by \[ A_{e,N}\longrightarrow X_e(-ho_N;\mathbf t),\qquad \xi\in[-ho_N,ho_N]\longmapsto X_e(\xi;\mathbf t), \qquad X_e(ho_N;\mathbf t)\longrightarrow B_{e,N}. 	ag{26} \] The two connectors are straight. The same convex-strip homotopy proves (23) for this path. At a positive whole-phase critical point, horizontal angular tangents together with the real \(\xi_e\) directions give precisely the adapted local contour of the pinned unsummed-source theorem. The radius \(ho_N\) may shrink as the full angular paths approach their moving endpoints. A separate fixed compact neighborhood of the target has a fixed positive phase-Morse radius, because its phase and Hessian do not depend on \(N\). No assertion is made that this larger radius works over the whole product of full lenses, or that its actual factorial amplitude is uniformly nonzero. In particular, (26) is a literal segment in a representative of the full finite source. Its two connectors, all other angular portions, all exact factorial zeros and the complete Hermite trace kernels remain in (23). There is no estimate showing that these terms are smaller than its geometric local contribution, or that their coherent sum cannot cancel that contribution. ## 6. Why a rectangular stationary graph is generally unavailable The pinched product construction cannot be replaced by an arbitrary fixed-depth full-width rectangle. For an edge with two independent angles, set \(t=s-ih\), \(u=-s-ih\). Direct trigonometry gives \[ 1+	an^2(t/2)+	an^2(u/2) = rac{4-(\cosh h-\cos s)^2}{(\cosh h+\cos s)^2}. 	ag{27} \] For \(0<h<2\operatorname{arsinh}1\), this vanishes at \(s=\arccos(\cosh h-2)\in(0,\pi)\). The discriminant has nonzero derivative in either independent angular coordinate, since \(\partial_t q^2=a(1+a^2)
e0\) there. A local holomorphic square root is impossible. Circling this divisor exchanges \(q\) with \(-q\), hence \(x\) with \(1-x\) near the merging stationary value \(x=1/2\). More exactly, a rectangle with real half-width \(a_N\) and height \(T\) contains such a point whenever \[ T>h_N:=\operatorname{arcosh}(2+\cos a_N) =2\operatorname{arsinh}\!\left(\sin rac{\pi}{4N}ight). 	ag{28} \] Thus every fixed \(T>0\) fails for all sufficiently large \(N\). The construction of Theorem 2 avoids this divisor by narrowing the angular neighborhoods near \(\pm\pi\). It concerns the actual stationary relation, not a singularity of the finite cardinal source, which remains holomorphic. No fold-transport coefficient is inferred from the algebraic exchange of its two stationary branches. ## Direct sources and author readback - [Positive edge geometry](research_positive_edge_global_monotonicity.md): the exact positivity criterion, tangent characterization, original branches and the archived simultaneous contraction. Complete read retained at SHA256 `da5129c7110190035eedb8249d4004dd06b5a7555e78d948234d8de50fa17500`. - [Unsummed original phase](research_unsummed_network_phase_coercivity.md): (1)--(4), (25)--(30), same-index scope, stationary equation, Hessian and local adapted contour. Complete text reread at SHA256 `b5441bb508d3ffad3274e38dda2d6aeb099d08ae2ab043a0d12c25234e4a1e1e`. - [Exact factorial divisor](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_factorial_rectangle_divisor_criterion.md): Section 1, the specified canonical factorial and its entire divisor. Complete text read at SHA256 `462b8c22c73f73b12152bca96cf6636708dcf153c2cbc2751458454827b3ddf8`. - [Joint full-Hermite lens source](research_joint_factorial_lens_relative_source.md): the exact top form and prefactor, free-boundary convention, full physical normals and relative primitive for fixed coordinate faces. Complete author read retained and used implications reread at SHA256 `a14ca148bd55b36b1eea9de8be8a63025532c3bbbb928482b0d7cb8edae56e54`. All work here is written mathematics. No mathematical program, numerical computation or test was run. The final complete proof and all directly used source implications were reread before freezing.

title: Prefix commutants and the original pointed normal functional
text: # Prefix commutants and the original pointed normal functional Private written proof, 18 November 2026. The actual total-prefix change of coordinates reduces an intertwiner to a polynomial in one nilpotent raising operator. The remaining lowering equation is an explicit finite recursion. The original highest-cut, pivotal source retains every coefficient of that polynomial; it does not in general factor through its constant coefficient at the complete root. There is nevertheless a constructive reduction through the **whole meridian germ** of that constant coefficient. It is a universal meromorphic trace functional whose value on an actual analytic intertwiner is removable. Its pole order is at most \(N-1\), so a meridian jet of order at most \(N-1\) suffices. No minimal-depth or uniform norm assertion is made. A universal two-head Casimir coupon detects the distinction. Its constant coefficient vanishes at the root, whereas its original pivotal partial trace is \(N I\). It is square-zero, and adding any multiple of it to the identity gives an invertible intertwiner with the same constant coefficient and a varying pointed source. This is an obstruction inside the actual intertwiner/coupon algebra, not a counterexample about a knot or the image of the braid group. The complete directs are P, the actual relative prefix transition, and M, the original pivotal and cut conventions. All additional algebra and source evaluations are proved below. ## 1. The exact root commutant Fix \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), and \(Q=q^2\). The quantum parameter stays fixed in Sections 1--5. Meridian parameters remain unspecialized near their complete values. On each actual balanced head, \[ K_iw_a=x_iQ^{-a}w_a,\qquad x_i=-M_i/q, \quad F_iw_a=(1-Q^{a+1})w_{a+1}\quad(a<d), \tag{1} \] with \(F_iw_d=0\), and \[ \mathcal E_iw_a=(M_iQ^{-a}-M_i^{-1})w_{a-1}\quad(a>0), \qquad \mathcal E_iw_0=0. \tag{2} \] Put \(f_a=\prod_{j=1}^a(1-Q^j)\), \(f_0=1\); all \(f_a\), \(a<N\), are units. Split a total prefix of \(m\) heads into its first head and its remaining ordered tensor product. Write \(K_{\rm r},F_{\rm r}, \mathcal E_{\rm r}\) for the actual remaining coproducts. For \(m=1\), use \(K_{\rm r}=I\) and \(F_{\rm r}=\mathcal E_{\rm r}=0\). P gives the exact finite operator \[ S=\sum_{j=0}^{d}\frac{(x_1^{-1}L_1F_{\rm r})^j}{f_j}, \qquad L_1w_a=w_{a-1},\quad L_1w_0=0, \tag{3} \] with its finite inverse and original source transport. At the root, \[ S^{-1}F_\Sigma S=F_1,\qquad [S,K_\Sigma]=0, \quad K_\Sigma=K_1K_{\rm r}. \tag{4} \] The transformed lowering operator is \[ E':=S^{-1}\mathcal E_\Sigma S =I\otimes\mathcal E_{\rm r}+L_1b_A,\qquad b_a=M_1K_{\rm r}Q^{-a}-M_1^{-1}K_{\rm r}^{-1}. \tag{5} \] Here \(b_A\) is evaluated at the input first-head occupation \(a\); the second term is zero at \(a=0\). Let \(W\) be an endomorphism commuting with the actual total \(F_\Sigma,K_\Sigma,\mathcal E_\Sigma\). This includes an unmarked actual braid endomorphism with its colors matched at the two ends. It does not include arbitrary inserted marks without their Ward commutators. Define \(W'=S^{-1}WS\). Since \(F_1\) is one Jordan block with nonzero arrows below its last row, its full matrix commutant on the tensor product is \[ W'=\sum_{n=0}^{d}F_1^n\otimes B_n. \tag{6} \] For an elementary proof, define \(B_n\) by \[ W'(w_0\otimes v)=\sum_{n=0}^{d}f_nw_n\otimes B_nv. \tag{7} \] Commutation with \(F_1\) determines every other column from (7), giving (6) uniquely. Commutation with \(K_\Sigma\) is equivalent to \[ K_{\rm r}B_n=Q^nB_nK_{\rm r}. \tag{8} \] If \(W\) preserves total integer occupation, as the unmarked literal braid does, \(B_n\) has integer occupation degree \(-n\) on the remaining heads. Equation (8) alone only records its root weight. Set \[ D=M_1K_{\rm r}+M_1^{-1}K_{\rm r}^{-1}. \tag{9} \] The full remaining lowering condition is exactly \[ \boxed{\quad [\mathcal E_{\rm r},B_{n-1}] =-(1-Q^n)b_nB_n=[D,B_n]\quad(1\le n\le d), \qquad [\mathcal E_{\rm r},B_d]=0. \quad} \tag{10} \] Indeed the first-head \(w_{n-1}\) coefficient of \([E',W'](w_0\otimes v)\), divided by \(f_{n-1}\), is \[ [\mathcal E_{\rm r},B_{n-1}]+(1-Q^n)b_nB_n. \tag{11} \] The last coefficient is \(f_d[\mathcal E_{\rm r},B_d]\). The second equality in (10) follows from (8). These conditions are sufficient too: the root relation \([E',F_1]=(q-q^{-1})(K_\Sigma-K_\Sigma^{-1})\) and \([W',K_\Sigma]=[W',F_1]=0\) imply that \([E',W']\) commutes with \(F_1\). Its vanishing on \(w_0\otimes v\) then gives its vanishing on every column. The last equation of (10) is a genuine closing condition. It cannot be omitted by working only with the transformed Casimir. ## 2. The original pointed and pivotal source Write \(g_{\rm r}=K_{\rm r}^{\,1-N}\). In M's original braid closure convention the highest-cut source, before any additional unchanged scalar framing or peripheral line, is \[ \Phi_0(W)= \operatorname{Tr}\bigl((P_0\otimes g_{\rm r})W\bigr). \tag{12} \] All literal crossing scalars can equivalently be included in \(W\). No new pivot is inserted on the opened head. The original source in (12) is not its reset value in the \(S\) coordinates. Its exact expression is \[ \boxed{\quad \Phi_0(W)= \operatorname{Tr}_{\rm r}\left( g_{\rm r}\sum_{n=0}^{d}x_1^{-n}F_{\rm r}^{\,n}B_n \right). \quad} \tag{13} \] To prove it, \(S^{-1}(w_0\otimes v)=w_0\otimes v\). Apply (7), then (3). Only the \(j=n\) term of \(S\) returns the first head to zero. Its coefficient is \(x_1^{-n}F_{\rm r}^n/f_n\), cancelling the \(f_n\) in (7). The remaining trace is exactly (13), in the displayed order. For any other prescribed cut probe \(P\), the always valid source formula is instead \[ \Phi_P(W)= \operatorname{Tr}\left[ S^{-1}(P\otimes g_{\rm r})S \sum_{n=0}^{d}F_1^n\otimes B_n\right]. \tag{14} \] This includes the original soft diagonal probes. If the actual unmarked cut operator is scalar, M's exact source identity makes all trace-one probes equal; it does not authorize replacing the transformed probe in (14) by an untransformed one. Arbitrary marked words retain their nonzero Ward defects and are not silently put in the homogeneous commutant (6). ## 3. A nonzero source class in the kernel of the root constant term Take two actual complete heads, so \(M_1=M_2=1\), \(x_1=x_2=x=-q^{-1}\), and \(x^2=Q^{-1}\). In (6) take \[ B_0=\cdots=B_{d-1}=0,\qquad B_d=T_{0d}=|0\rangle\langle d|. \tag{15} \] Equation (8) holds since \(K_2T_{0d}=Q^dT_{0d}K_2\). Both \(\mathcal E_2T_{0d}\) and \(T_{0d}\mathcal E_2\) vanish. The only other condition in (10) is \[ b_dT_{0d}=(xQ^{-d}-x^{-1})T_{0d} =(Qx-x^{-1})T_{0d}=0. \tag{16} \] Thus \[ R_N=S(F_1^d\otimes T_{0d})S^{-1} \tag{17} \] is an actual total-degree-zero intertwiner, not just a matrix commuting with one generator. The whole retained source is computable. At the root, \[ f_d=N,\qquad f_{d-a}=\frac{N(-1)^aQ^{a(a+1)/2}}{f_a}. \tag{18} \] The first identity follows by evaluating \((t^N-1)/(t-1)=\prod_{j=1}^{d}(t-Q^j)\) at \(t=1\). To obtain the second, separate the last \(a\) factors of \(f_d\), use \(1-Q^{-j}=-Q^{-j}(1-Q^j)\), and solve for \(f_{d-a}\). Using (3) and its finite inverse from P gives \[ R_N=N|\psi\rangle\langle\phi|,\qquad |\psi\rangle=\sum_{a=0}^{d}x^{a-d}|a,d-a\rangle,\quad \langle\phi|=\sum_{a=0}^{d}x^{-a}Q^{-a}\langle a,d-a|. \tag{19} \] For example the coefficient of \(\langle a,d-a|\) in \(\langle0,d|S^{-1}\) is \((-1)^aQ^{a(a-1)/2}x^{-a}N/(f_af_{d-a})=x^{-a}Q^{-a}\). These are bilinear algebraic vectors and covectors, with no complex conjugation. Their pairing is \(x^{-d}\sum_aQ^{-a}=0\), so \[ R_N^2=0. \tag{20} \] Nevertheless its original pivotal partial trace is \[ \boxed{\quad \operatorname{Tr}_2\bigl((I\otimes K_2^{1-N})R_N\bigr)=N I. \quad} \tag{21} \] Indeed the support in (19) makes the partial trace diagonal. On its \(a\)-th diagonal the factor is \[ N x^{-d}Q^{-a}\cdot x^{-d}Q^{a+1} =N x^{-2d}Q=N. \tag{22} \] In particular \(\Phi_0(R_N)=N\), and every trace-one cut probe has the same value. Any fixed external scalar line multiplies this value unchanged; (21) is not an additional normalization factor for a knot invariant. The map from the commutant to its constant coefficient \(B_0\) is an algebra homomorphism. Its kernel is nilpotent of order at most \(N\), by positive \(F_1\)-degree. In particular \[ I+tR_N\text{ is invertible for every }t,\qquad B_0(I+tR_N)=I,\qquad \Phi_0(I+tR_N)=tN. \tag{23} \] Here \(\Phi_0(I)=x^{-d}\sum_aQ^{-a}=0\). Thus neither the root value \(B_0\) nor that value together with invertibility determines the prescribed source on the full actual intertwiner algebra. ## 4. An actual Casimir lift of the kernel coupon The coupon (17) extends through a whole root-quantum meridian family. Use the actual total Casimir \[ \Omega_\Sigma=F_\Sigma\mathcal E_\Sigma+ qK_\Sigma+q^{-1}K_\Sigma^{-1}. \tag{24} \] The root head relations, including their endpoint rows, imply that (24) commutes with all three total generators. This also follows directly by expanding each commutator with \([\mathcal E_\Sigma,F_\Sigma]=(q-q^{-1}) (K_\Sigma-K_\Sigma^{-1})\) and the two weight relations. At the two-head complete point, P's exact formula reads \[ S^{-1}\Omega_\Sigma S=F_1\mathcal E_2+ \operatorname{diag}(\lambda_b), \quad \lambda_b=q^{2b+1}+q^{-(2b+1)},\quad 0\le b\le d. \tag{25} \] The diagonal in (25) is on the second head. Define the monic degree-\(d\) polynomial \[ p_N(t)=\prod_{b=1}^{d}(t-\lambda_b). \tag{26} \] The only coincidences of the \(\lambda_b\) are \(\lambda_a=\lambda_b\) with \(a=b\) or \(a+b=d\). Indeed \(z+z^{-1}=w+w^{-1}\) implies \(z=w\) or \(zw=1\); apply this to \(z=qQ^a,w=qQ^b\). On a fixed total-occupation subspace, (25) is bidiagonal with tail index in a consecutive interval of \(0,\ldots,d\). Every proper such interval has characteristic polynomial dividing \(p_N\): the omitted occurrence \(\lambda_0\) is duplicated by \(\lambda_d\), and a proper interval cannot contain both endpoints. Cayley--Hamilton therefore kills each proper interval block. The same argument kills every entry of \(p_N\) on the full block except the longest off-diagonal: a polynomial entry between two ordered indices depends only on their intervening bidiagonal interval. For the longest entry, only the leading degree-\(d\) term can travel all \(d\) steps and its coefficient is one. Hence \[ p_N(S^{-1}\Omega_\Sigma S) =F_1^d\mathcal E_2^d =(-1)^dN(F_1^d\otimes T_{0d}), \tag{27} \] because \(\prod_{a=1}^{d}(Q^{-a}-1)=Q^{-d(d+1)/2}f_d=(-1)^dN\). Consequently \[ R_N=\frac{p_N(\Omega_\Sigma)}{(-1)^dN}. \tag{28} \] Keep \(q=q_N\) fixed and let the two meridians vary together near \(M=1\). The same polynomial of the actual matrix \(\Omega_\Sigma(M)\), with the coefficients (26) fixed, is an analytic intertwiner family specializing to (17). Its constant coefficient vanishes at \(M=1\), while its source does not. For each fixed \(t\), \(I+tR_N(M)\) is invertible on a sufficiently small meridian disk. Thus (23) is compatible with actual meridian-analytic coupons, not only with an isolated root fiber. No assertion that (28) is a literal braid word is needed or made. The conclusion is precisely that the homogeneous Ward equations and invertibility alone cannot give the proposed value-only source factorization. A stronger restriction on the image of actual knot words would be an additional input. ## 5. Constructive reconstruction from the whole meridian germ Return to \(m\) heads and vary their common meridian \(M\), still at fixed \(q_N\). Let \(W(M)\) be an analytic family of actual total intertwiners. All matrices in (3)--(10) are analytic near \(M=1\). Each \(b_n(M)\) is diagonal on the remaining-head occupation basis. If their total occupation is \(A_{\rm r}\), its diagonal entry is \[ (-q^{-1})^{m-1}M^mQ^{-A_{\rm r}-n} -(-q)^{m-1}M^{-m}Q^{A_{\rm r}}. \tag{29} \] It is not identically zero. Every zero at \(M=1\) is simple: the derivative there is \(2m\) times its first nonzero summand. There are only finitely many other zeros for fixed \(N,m\). Choose a punctured meridian disk excluding them. Then (10) recovers every coefficient uniquely: \[ B_n=\mathscr D_n(B_{n-1}),\qquad \mathscr D_n(B)= -\frac{b_n^{-1}[\mathcal E_{\rm r},B]}{1-Q^n}. \tag{30} \] Its \(n\)-fold composition has pole order at most \(n\) at \(M=1\). For an actual analytic intertwiner these apparent poles cancel. The top condition \([\mathcal E_{\rm r},B_d]=0\), the weight relations, and those cancellations remain restrictions on admissible \(B_0\); an arbitrary analytic matrix is not declared admissible. There is an explicit reduced source functional as well. For the ordinary matrix trace pairing, the adjoint of (30) is \[ \mathscr D_n^*(A) =\frac{[\mathcal E_{\rm r},A b_n^{-1}]}{1-Q^n}, \qquad \operatorname{Tr}(A\mathscr D_n(B)) =\operatorname{Tr}(\mathscr D_n^*(A)B). \tag{31} \] This follows by cyclically moving the single commutator; the position of \(b_n^{-1}\) in (31) is essential. Define the known meromorphic remaining-head matrix \[ \mathcal H_N(M)= \sum_{n=0}^{d}x_1^{-n} (\mathscr D_1^*\circ\cdots\circ\mathscr D_n^*) (g_{\rm r}F_{\rm r}^{\,n}), \tag{32} \] with \(n=0\) term \(g_{\rm r}\). Equations (13), (30), and (31) give exactly on the punctured disk \[ \Phi_0(W(M)) =\operatorname{Tr}_{\rm r} (\mathcal H_N(M)B_0(M)). \tag{33} \] The left side is the original analytic source, so (33) has its prescribed removable continuation. The pole order of \(\mathcal H_N\) is at most \(d\). Equivalently, \[ \Phi_0(W(1))= [t^0]\operatorname{Tr}_{\rm r} (\mathcal H_N(1+t)B_0(1+t)). \tag{34} \] Only the meridian jet of \(B_0\) through order at most \(d=N-1\) can enter (34). This is an upper bound, not a proof that depth \(N-1\) is necessary. Equations (17)--(28) only exclude depth zero as a universal replacement. No bound uniform in \(N\) for the coefficients of (34) is inferred. ## 6. An explicit scalar \(K\)-Casimir kernel The matrix \(\mathcal H_N\) in (32) has a more explicit universal form. Set \(K=K_{\rm r}\), \(F=F_{\rm r}\), \(E=\mathcal E_{\rm r}\), and retain the actual remaining-head Casimir \[ \Omega=FE+qK+q^{-1}K^{-1},\qquad u(k,\omega)=\omega-qk-q^{-1}k^{-1}. \tag{35} \] It commutes with \(K,F,E\) by the same root relations used in Section 4. No scalar Casimir value or simple spectrum is assumed. For an empty remaining tensor use \(K=I,F=E=0\) and \(\Omega=(q+q^{-1})I\). For every \(0\le n\le d\) define scalar rational functions \(a_{n,j}(k,\omega)\), \(0\le j\le n\), by \[ a_{n,n}(k,\omega)=Q^{-n}k^{1-N},\qquad b_j(k)=M_1kQ^{-j}-M_1^{-1}k^{-1}, \tag{36} \] and, descending from \(j=n\) to \(1\), by \[ \boxed{\quad a_{n,j-1}(k,\omega)=\frac1{1-Q^j} \left[ \frac{u(Q^{-j}k,\omega)a_{n,j}(k,\omega)}{b_j(k)} -\frac{u(k,\omega)a_{n,j}(Qk,\omega)}{b_j(Qk)} \right]. \quad} \tag{37} \] Then the actual universal matrix in (32) is exactly \[ \mathcal H_N(M)=\mathfrak h_N(K,\Omega;M_1),\qquad \mathfrak h_N(k,\omega;M_1) =\sum_{n=0}^{d}x_1^{-n}a_{n,0}(k,\omega). \tag{38} \] This is rational in the nonzero \(k\) and meridian, and polynomial of degree at most \(d\) in \(\omega\). Its evaluation uses the commuting matrices \(K,\Omega\), retaining every Casimir Jordan block. Here is a direct verification of all shifts and orders. The exact relations give \(FE=u(K,\Omega)\), \(EF=u(Q^{-1}K,\Omega)\), \(f(K)F^r=F^rf(Q^{-r}K)\), and \(f(K)E=Ef(QK)\). Consequently, for \(r\ge1\) and \(v=v(K,\Omega)\), \[ [E,F^rv] =F^{r-1}\{u(Q^{-r}K,\Omega)v(K,\Omega) -u(K,\Omega)v(QK,\Omega)\}. \tag{39} \] Also \(g_{\rm r}F^n=F^nQ^{-n}K^{1-N}\), since \(Q^N=1\). Apply (31) successively for \(j=n,n-1,\ldots,1\). In (39) put \(r=j\) and \(v=a_{n,j}/b_j\). This gives (37) and then (38), with precisely the adjoint order of (32). Every step adds at most one degree in \(\omega\). The denominators are only the displayed shifted \(b_j\)'s and the nonzero constants \(1-Q^j\). Their meridian zeros remain simple individually, so the pole bound in Section 5 is unchanged. There is an exact scalar contour form if desired. On the common meridian family put \(x_{\rm r}=(-M/q)^{m-1}\), \(k_a=x_{\rm r}Q^{-a}\), and \[ \Pi_a=\frac1N\sum_{\ell=0}^{d} (Q^aK/x_{\rm r})^\ell,\qquad 0\le a<N. \tag{40} \] These are the actual root weight projectors, including zero projectors for absent weights. They commute with \(\Omega\). For fixed \(N\), choose a small meridian circle \(|t|=\epsilon\) where all denominators are units, and a sufficiently large fixed circle \(|\zeta|=R\) enclosing the spectra of \(\Omega(1+t)\) for \(|t|\le\epsilon\). Polynomial functional calculus and (34) give, in the original source normalization, \[ \begin{aligned} \Phi_0(W(1)) =\frac1{(2\pi i)^2} \int_{|t|=\epsilon}\frac{dt}{t} \int_{|\zeta|=R}d\zeta\, \sum_{a=0}^{d} &\mathfrak h_N(k_a(1+t),\zeta;1+t)\\[-2pt] {}\cdot& \operatorname{Tr}_{\rm r} \left(\Pi_a(\zeta I-\Omega(1+t))^{-1}B_0(1+t)\right). \end{aligned} \tag{41} \] Both circles have positive orientation. There is no commutation of \(B_0\) with \(\Omega\) in this formula. The resolvent retains its full higher poles, and the meridian integral is the finite part already fixed by the actual source. These auxiliary finite contours do not assert a pushforward of a geometric framing cycle or an asymptotic bound. ## 7. Retained source scope and quantum normals The statements above use the actual root-quantum meridian family. They do not identify it with a fixed-\(N\) ordinary-color quantum normal path. On the whole \(q,M\) germ, P proves instead \[ S^{-1}F_\Sigma S=F_1+J_N,\qquad J_N=f_d^{-1}S^{-1}F_\Sigma^N(T_{0d}\otimes I). \tag{42} \] Its quantum normal generally survives. Thus a whole intertwiner commutes with \(F_1+J_N\), not automatically with \(F_1\). One must differentiate the unreduced matrices, the transformed probes (14), and (42), retaining all pivot, twist and boundary terms. Differentiating the root normal form (6) as if \(J_N=0\) on that germ is not licensed. The exact new conclusion is a meridian-jet reconstruction of the original pointed source, together with a calibrated resonant source class showing why the root constant term loses information. Neither conclusion determines the coefficient of that class in an original knot word, a geometric relative cycle, or a noncancelling asymptotic contribution. ## Complete direct-source pins * P: notes/research_relative_prefix_fourier_transition.md, SHA256 84c15158878a2c5eb4d6e3281149ae95d36fbd2e8333bf736940d62e66d21162. * M: notes/marked_braid_holonomy.md, SHA256 eff47c757d0e44bda0c396c094315b8e1fce11f1fc2d6445d636c6d2d3a46c4f. title: The actual prefix order and its first normal layer
text: # The actual prefix order and its first normal layer Private written proof, 19 November 2026. Author-final for independent review. The original cut pairing bounds the pole of the inverse prefix coordinate by one. Consequently the entire root intertwiner, not only its closing trace, is determined by the value and first meridian derivative of its actual reduced matrix. The part lost by the root reduction is a square-zero ideal. The admissible root reduced matrices form a self-annihilating subalgebra for the polar part of the original source pairing. These are statements about the actual finite source and its common-meridian germ. They do not give a positive pairing, an elliptic kernel, or a nonzero prescribed closing. The complete directs are L, the physical endpoint duality, and R, the actual prefix algebra and pointed source. All order and first-normal arguments are proved below. ## 1. The two coordinates and the original source Fix \[ N\ge2,\quad d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2, \quad m=r+1\ge2,\quad M=e^\mu,\quad x=-M/q. \tag{1} \] The quantum root is fixed. Let \(U\) be the remaining \(r\)-head occupation space, with its actual ordered totals \(E,F,K\). Put \[ K(M)=M^rK_0,\qquad K_0^N=\varepsilon I, \quad\varepsilon=(-1)^{(N+1)r},\qquad \mathcal A=\{H\in\operatorname{End}(U):[K_0,H]=0\}. \tag{2} \] This is a fixed direct sum of full matrix algebras. No occupation index or remaining matrix block is replaced by a scalar. L identifies every \(H\in\mathcal A\) with the unique actual total intertwiner \(W_H(M)\) having physical highest block \(H\). The identification and its inverse are holomorphic wherever the first head coefficients \[ e_a=MQ^{-a}-M^{-1},\qquad 1\le a\le d, \tag{3} \] are nonzero. This includes \(M=1\). Write \(\star_\mu\) for the transported product, so \(W_{H\star_\mu J}=W_HW_J\). L's opposite physical endpoint is the holomorphic linear unit \[ \mathscr L_\mu H=(W_H)_{dd}. \tag{4} \] With \(g_\mu=K(M)^{1-N}\), its exact source identity is \[ \operatorname{Tr}(g_\mu(H\star_\mu J)) =\operatorname{Tr}(g_\mu H\mathscr L_\mu J). \tag{5} \] Both \(\mathscr L_\mu\) and its inverse are regular at zero. Keep R's literal finite prefix and quotient: \[ S(M)=\sum_{a=0}^d\frac{(x^{-1}L_1F)^a}{f_a},\qquad f_a=\prod_{j=1}^a(1-Q^j),\qquad \mathscr B_\mu H=p_0S(M)^{-1}W_H(M)i_0. \tag{6} \] Thus \(\mathscr B_\mu\) is a holomorphic linear map on \(\mathcal A\), with every original prefix coefficient and cap. It satisfies \[ \mathscr B_\mu(H\star_\mu J) =(\mathscr B_\mu H)(\mathscr B_\mu J), \qquad\mathscr B_\mu I=I. \tag{7} \] It is not presumed invertible at \(\mu=0\). For clarity its finite construction can also be read directly from L. If \(C_a(H)=(W_H)_{a0}\), then \[ C_0=H,\quad C_{a+1}=-e_{a+1}^{-1}K^{-1}[E,C_a],\qquad \mathscr B_\mu H= \sum_{a=0}^d\frac{(-1)^aQ^{a(a-1)/2}x^{-a}}{f_a}F^aC_a(H). \tag{8} \] Only the nonzero first-head arrows and \(f_1,\ldots,f_d\) are divided by in this formula. Set \[ D_\mu=\frac{D_N(M)}{D_N(MK(M))},\qquad D_N(z)=\frac{z^N-z^{-N}}{z-z^{-1}}. \tag{9} \] The Laurent-polynomial convention for \(D_N\) is retained. R proves the exact original highest-cut and pivotal source \[ \operatorname{Tr}(g_\mu H) =\operatorname{Tr}(D_\mu\mathscr B_\mu H). \tag{10} \] The right side is first interpreted generically and then by its prescribed continuation. Since \(D_\mu\) is a function of \(K_0\), it is central in \(\mathcal A\). ## 2. A simple pole for the entire inverse coordinate Use the ordinary bilinear trace pairing on \(\mathcal A\). For a linear map \(T\), define its transpose by \[ \operatorname{Tr}(A\,T H) =\operatorname{Tr}((T^*A)H). \tag{11} \] There is no complex conjugation. This trace pairing is perfect on each Cartan matrix block, so \(T^*\) is uniquely defined. Put \(\mathcal G_\mu X=Xg_\mu\) and \(\mathsf D_\mu X=D_\mu X\). Equations (5), (7), and (10), applied to the actual product, give \[ \boxed{\qquad \mathcal G_\mu\mathscr L_\mu =\mathscr B_\mu^*\mathsf D_\mu\mathscr B_\mu. \qquad}\tag{12} \] Indeed the source of \(W_HW_J\) is both \(\operatorname{Tr}(g_\mu H\mathscr L_\mu J)\) and \(\operatorname{Tr}(D_\mu(\mathscr B_\mu H)(\mathscr B_\mu J))\). Move the latter's central \(D_\mu\) and take the transpose in (11). Equality for every \(H\) proves (12), including its order. On a punctured sufficiently small meridian disk the scalar on each Cartan block in (9) is a unit. The left side of (12) is invertible. Thus \(\mathscr B_\mu\) is injective, and hence bijective in the same finite dimension. In particular generic surjectivity does not require a separate recursive Cartan inversion. Equation (12) then gives the explicit inverse \[ \boxed{\qquad \mathscr B_\mu^{-1} =\mathscr L_\mu^{-1}\mathcal G_\mu^{-1} \mathscr B_\mu^*\mathsf D_\mu. \qquad}\tag{13} \] The source matrix has the exact expansion \[ \begin{split} D_\mu&=\frac{d_{-1}}\mu+d_0+O(\mu),\\ d_{-1}&=\frac{K_0-K_0^{-1}}{2\varepsilon m},\qquad d_0=\frac{K_0+K_0^{-1}}{2\varepsilon}. \end{split}\tag{14} \] To check it, replace its denominator by \(\varepsilon(e^{mN\mu}-e^{-mN\mu})\) and its numerator by \(D_N(e^\mu)(e^{m\mu}K_0-e^{-m\mu}K_0^{-1})\), using (2). All other factors in (13) are holomorphic at zero. Consequently \[ \boxed{\quad\mathscr C_\mu:=\mu\mathscr B_\mu^{-1} \text{ is holomorphic at }\mu=0.\quad} \tag{15} \] This is an operator statement for the full inverse coordinate, not just a cancellation after one closing trace. ## 3. Exact admissibility and whole-intertwiner first jets Let \(\mathcal O\) be the ring of holomorphic germs in the fixed parameter \(\mu=\Log M\), and set \[ \mathcal A_{\mathcal O}=\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal O, \qquad\mathcal I=\mathscr B(\mathcal A_{\mathcal O}), \qquad V=\operatorname{im}\mathscr B_0\subset\mathcal A. \tag{16} \] It follows from (15) that \[ \mu\mathcal A_{\mathcal O}\subset\mathcal I \subset\mathcal A_{\mathcal O}. \tag{17} \] For the left inclusion, \(\mu Z=\mathscr B(\mathscr C Z)\). Write \[ \mathscr B_\mu^{-1}=\frac{\mathscr R}{\mu}+\mathscr Q+O(\mu), \qquad\mathscr B_\mu=\mathscr B_0+\mu\mathscr B_1+O(\mu^2). \tag{18} \] Multiplying in both orders gives \[ \mathscr R\mathscr B_0=\mathscr B_0\mathscr R=0, \quad\mathscr B_0\mathscr Q+\mathscr B_1\mathscr R=I, \quad\mathscr Q\mathscr B_0+\mathscr R\mathscr B_1=I. \tag{19} \] In particular \[ \ker\mathscr R=V. \tag{20} \] One inclusion follows from the first identity; if \(\mathscr R Z=0\), the second gives \(Z=\mathscr B_0\mathscr Q Z\). Hence the exact image order is \[ \boxed{\qquad \mathcal I=\{Z\in\mathcal A_{\mathcal O}:Z(0)\in V\} =V\otimes\mathcal O+\mu\mathcal A_{\mathcal O}. \qquad}\tag{21} \] Equivalently, an analytic proposed reduced matrix is the prefix of an analytic actual intertwiner if and only if \(\mathscr RZ(0)=0\). Indeed (18) has only that possible pole. There are no successive higher-order divisibility conditions. The condition remains a full matrix condition on the extensive remaining-head seed. There is a corresponding physical co-source for an arbitrary analytic Cartan-preserving reduced mark \(Z(\mu)\): \[ \Xi_Z=\mathscr L_\mu\mathscr B_\mu^{-1}Z =\bigl(\mathscr B_\mu^*(D_\mu Z)\bigr)g_\mu^{-1}, \qquad \operatorname{Tr}(D_\mu(\mathscr B_\mu H)Z) =\operatorname{Tr}(g_\mu H\Xi_Z). \tag{21a} \] Its residue is exactly \(\mathscr L_0\mathscr RZ(0)\). It is holomorphic if and only if \(Z(0)\in V\). Thus (21a) transports an actual reduced marked closing to the opposite physical endpoint, but does not declare an arbitrary local window admissible. If \(Z=Z_0+\mu Z_1+\cdots\), its unrestricted finite part is \[ \mathscr L_0(\mathscr RZ_1+\mathscr QZ_0) +\mathscr L_1\mathscr RZ_0, \qquad\mathscr L_1=\partial_\mu\mathscr L|_0. \tag{21b} \] Both moving-mark and moving-endpoint normal terms remain. For such an actual reduced family write \(Z(\mu)=Z_0+\mu Z_1+O(\mu^2)\). Its entire physical root seed is \[ \boxed{\qquad H(0)=\mathscr RZ_1+\mathscr QZ_0.\qquad}\tag{22} \] Applying L's finite highest-block reconstruction then recovers every block of \(W_H(0)\). Thus the first meridian jet of the actual reduced matrix determines the whole root intertwiner. This does not mean its first normal needs no further data: \(H'(0)\) generally uses \(Z''(0)\) as well. Higher fixed jets follow by the ordinary product rule in \(H=\mathscr C Z/\mu\). No quantum parameter or forced outward arrow is differentiated. ## 4. The lost root ideal is square-zero The map \(\mathscr B\) is an algebra isomorphism from the physical intertwiner order, expressed with \(\star_\mu\), to \(\mathcal I\). After specializing it identifies the whole root intertwiner algebra with \(\mathcal I/\mu\mathcal I\). Reduction to the ordinary root matrix has kernel \[ \mathcal K=\mu\mathcal A_{\mathcal O}/\mu\mathcal I, \qquad 0\longrightarrow\mathcal K\longrightarrow \mathcal I/\mu\mathcal I\longrightarrow V\longrightarrow0. \tag{23} \] Every factor in the numerator of \(\mathcal K^2\) has one \(\mu\); (17) gives \(\mu^2\mathcal A_{\mathcal O}\subset\mu\mathcal I\). Therefore \[ \boxed{\quad\mathcal K^2=0.\quad}\tag{24} \] In physical coordinates this is the kernel of \(\mathscr B_0\) with the actual product \(\star_0\), not ordinary multiplication of the highest blocks. Its unit kernel is consequently additive: \((1+k)(1+l)=1+k+l\), \((1+k)^{-1}=1-k\) for \(k,l\in\mathcal K\). There is also an explicit splitting in the fixed prefix coordinates. By (21), constant matrices in \(V\) belong to \(\mathcal I\). The data of a class modulo \(\mu\mathcal I\) are exactly \[ (Z_0,[Z_1])\in V\oplus(\mathcal A/V). \tag{25} \] The multiplication is \[ (b,[c])(b',[c'])=(bb',[bc'+cb']). \tag{26} \] It is well-defined because \(V\) is a subalgebra, by (7). This is a split square-zero extension with its literal bimodule; it does not erase that bimodule or its possible source value. ## 5. The polar pairing and reciprocal blocks Define the symmetric bilinear, possibly degenerate form \[ \beta(A,B)=\operatorname{Tr}(d_{-1}AB). \tag{27} \] Its central coefficient is exactly the residue of the original source. Taking the residue of (13) gives \[ \mathscr R=\mathscr L_0^{-1}\mathcal G_0^{-1} \mathscr B_0^*\mathsf d_{-1}, \qquad\mathsf d_{-1}X=d_{-1}X. \tag{28} \] The first two factors are units. Thus \(\ker\mathscr R\) is the annihilator of \(\operatorname{im}\mathscr B_0\) for (27). Combining this with (20) proves the source-specific identity \[ \boxed{\quad V=V^{\perp_\beta}.\quad}\tag{29} \] In particular \(V\) contains the radical of \(\beta\). Here is the exact pair decomposition, without a new spectral projector premise. The actual total Casimir \(\Omega_\Sigma=F_\Sigma E_\Sigma+qK_\Sigma+q^{-1}K_\Sigma^{-1}\) commutes with all total generators. R's relations \(S^{-1}F_\Sigma S=F_1\), \([S,K_\Sigma]=0\), \(Si_0=i_0\), and \(p_0F_1=0\) give \[ \mathcal B_m(\Omega_\Sigma) =-MK-M^{-1}K^{-1}. \tag{30} \] At the root two actual weights \(\chi,\psi\) have the same number \(-\chi-\chi^{-1}\) exactly when \(\psi=\chi\) or \(\psi=\chi^{-1}\). Polynomial interpolation on these distinct numbers puts every inversion-pair projector \(P_{\mathfrak o}\) in \(V\), using the actual polynomial intertwiner \(p_{\mathfrak o}(\Omega_\Sigma)\). It is unnecessary to assert that this full polynomial coupon is itself a projector. The matrices \(P_{\mathfrak o}\) are central in \(\mathcal A\), so \(V\) decomposes over these pairs. Each physical Cartan weight space has dimension \(n=N^{r-1}\): choose \(r-1\) occupations freely and the last is uniquely fixed modulo \(N\). On a nonself pair, \[ \mathcal A_{\mathfrak o} =\operatorname{End}(U_\chi)\oplus\operatorname{End}(U_{\chi^{-1}}), \quad \beta((A,B),(C,D)) =\frac{\chi-\chi^{-1}}{2\varepsilon m} \operatorname{Tr}(AC-BD). \tag{31} \] This form is nondegenerate. Equation (29) therefore gives \(\dim V_{\mathfrak o}=n^2\), half the displayed space. It also identifies \(\mathcal A_{\mathfrak o}/V_{\mathfrak o}\) with \(V_{\mathfrak o}^*\) by (27). For a self weight \(\chi=\pm1\), the entire block is in the radical and hence in \(V\): no root matrix is lost there. These are bilinear statements, not Hermitian orthogonality or a positive resolution. A half-dimensional subalgebra need not be the graph of an isomorphism between the two matrix blocks. The source in the root coordinates (25) is exactly \[ \boxed{\qquad \tau_0(b,[c])=\operatorname{Tr}(d_0b)+\operatorname{Tr}(d_{-1}c). \qquad}\tag{32} \] The residue vanishes because \(I\in V\) and (29) gives \(\beta(b,I)=0\). Changing \(c\) by an element of \(V\) leaves (32) unchanged for the same reason. Thus the normal layer is retained as a genuine part of the original cut, even when the ordinary reduced root matrix misses it. Formula (32) has exactly the original factors \(2\varepsilon\) and \(m\), not a freely chosen normalization of the paired sheets. ## 6. Finite conditioning, true normals, and scope The construction is entirely finite and keeps every head cap. It also gives an exponential, rather than superexponential, bound for the regularized inverse. Fix the width and \(0<\eta<\pi/m\), and set \(\mu=u/N\), \(|u|\le\eta\). L bounds highest reconstruction, \(\mathscr L^{\pm1}\), and the finite prefix coefficients by \(e^{CN}\). In particular (6),(8) give \(\|\mathscr B\|\le e^{CN}\). One may use the Hilbert--Schmidt norm on each Cartan matrix block to take the transpose in (11); passage to occupation operator norm costs only a polynomial in \(N\) at fixed width. Also \(g^{\pm1}\) are bounded on this collar. The explicit expression used in (14) gives \(\|\mu D_\mu\|\le C\) there, with its removable value at zero: \(D_N(e^{u/N})=O(N)\) and \(\sinh(m u)/u\) is bounded away from zero on the smaller disk. Equation (13) consequently proves \[ \|\mathscr C_\mu\|\le e^{CN}. \tag{33} \] On nested collars, every fixed \(j\)-th \(\mu\) derivative of \(\mathscr C\) costs at most \(C_jN^je^{CN}\), by Cauchy's formula. These bounds include the actual meridian dependence of the prefix, totals, pivot, and endpoint maps. They are not zero-exponential-rate estimates for a geometric kernel. All crossing and zero-framing scalars included in an actual word remain in its physical seed and reduced matrix. A separately prescribed scalar remains outside (10), with its own product-rule derivatives. Nothing here differentiates the quantum root or resets a missing endpoint arrow. The result gives a single residue condition for analytic source admissibility, a first-jet reconstruction of the whole root operator, and the exact square-zero normal layer of its reduction. It does not estimate the extensive remaining seed of a particular braid. The reciprocal blocks in (31) are whole physical Cartan blocks, not selected geometric eigenflags. No local phase, geometric window transport, positive pairing, or nonzero prescribed closing is inferred from (29) or from perfect cut duality. ## Complete direct-source pins * L: notes/research_lowest_physical_block_cut_pairing.md, 327 lines, SHA256 be1d3960c0144b69308879d710076b5037e3253ac2ea4b0f788f28616c47d90f. * R: notes/research_actual_reduced_braid_source.md, 330 lines, SHA256 9a472ef27b08305a519ff1f24b6d2b909e63a0acbdc49b3a29e001c52a2f2243. Both complete directs were freshly whole-read nontruncated in the active author sequence.
