# Nonvanishing of actual inverse rows and signed q-Hahn node blocks Written proof, 24 November 2026. Replaces [the first author-final](research_q_hahn_inverse_row_nonvanishing_v2.md); only index terminology is changed. The complete inverse Clebsch frame contains a coherent subtraction of the derivative column and a multiple of its ordinary partner. The calibrated normal amplitude makes this subtraction nonzero on real strict physical compacts and fixed complex magnetic collars. Both original inverse rows then have the ordinary exponential action with their known Christoffel--Darboux measure retained. The same imaginary-part gap controls both terms of a signed mixed double-node Jordan contribution, uniformly over every physical auxiliary color, including its exact color zeros. The pair degree remains an original physical integer. No continuation of the finite-dimensional inverse measure in that degree is asserted. No scalar closing or full contracted coupon lower bound follows. ## 1. Exact columns, measures, and inverse rows Let \(N\ge3\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\), \(x=q^d\). Take physical integer degrees and an actual double pair \[ 0\le j<l,\qquad j+l=d,\qquad s=l-j,\qquad l\le t\le d. 	ag{1} \] Write \(c_m=q^{2m+1}+q^{-2m-1}\) and \(
u_j=(-1)^j q^{j(j+1)}\). Let \(C_j(t,u)\) be the original column, normalized by \(C_j(t,0)=1\), and retain its actual generic derivative normal \[ w_j(t,u)= rac{D C_j(q;t,u)-D C_l(q;t,u)} {-2N\Delta_j},\qquad \Delta_j=q^{2j+1}-q^{-2j-1}. 	ag{2} \] Here the two \(C_m(\zeta;t,u)\) use the original highest weight \(d\), \(D=\zeta\partial_\zeta\) is evaluated at \(\zeta=q\), and \(N,t,u\) are fixed during that derivative. For complex \(u\), use the same finite source and logarithmic lift as [N]. Thus this is a specified magnetic continuation of the actual rows. Define the real-rooted polynomial and its deleted double factor by \[ P_t(Z)=\prod_{m=0}^{t}(Z-c_m),\qquad Q_{t,j}(Z)= rac{P_t(Z)}{(Z-c_j)^2}. 	ag{3} \] Set \(S_t=\prod_{r=1}^{t}2\sin(\pi r/N)\), \(S_0=1\), and \[ B_t=(-1)^t S_t^2,\qquad \sigma_{t,j}= rac{x^t
u_j Q_{t,j}(c_j)}{B_t},\qquad \eta_{t,j}=ho_j+ rac{Q_{t,j}'(c_j)}{Q_{t,j}(c_j)},\quad ho_j=- rac{s}{2\Delta_j}. 	ag{4} \] In particular \(\sigma_{t,j}
e0\). These are the original complex measures, including their phases. For the complete frame \(V_t\), with double columns ordered as \((C_j,w_j)\), [H,M] give exactly the bilinear Gram and inverse \[  egin{pmatrix}C_j^T C_j&C_j^T w_j\ w_j^T C_j&w_j^T w_j\end{pmatrix} =\sigma_{t,j} egin{pmatrix}0&1\1&\eta_{t,j}\end{pmatrix}, \qquad V_t^{-1}=(V_t^TV_t)^{-1}V_t^T . 	ag{5} \] Thus the two actual inverse row entries, at a physical magnetic index \(u\), are \[  oxed{\quad L^{m val}_{t,j}(u)=\sigma_{t,j}^{-1} [w_j(t,u)-\eta_{t,j}C_j(t,u)],\qquad L^{m nor}_{t,j}(u)=\sigma_{t,j}^{-1}C_j(t,u). \quad} 	ag{6} \] The first extracts the coefficient of the value column, the second that of the normal column. There is no Hermitian conjugation in (5) or (6). At noninteger \(u\), equation (6) defines the literal continuation of those finite source expressions. The measures are still those of the physical integer block \(t\). ## 2. Statement on a complex magnetic collar Let \[ {\cal P}=\{(	au,
u)\in\mathbb C^2: 	frac12<\Re	au<1,\quad0<\Re
u<\Re	au\},\qquad {\cal P}_{\mathbb R}={\cal P}\cap\mathbb R^2 . 	ag{7} \] For every compact \(S\Subset{\cal P}_{\mathbb R}\), there is a fixed compact complex neighborhood \(K\Subset{\cal P}\) of \(S\), constants \(\delta,c,C>0\), and \(N_0\), such that the following hold for \(N\ge N_0\). Take (1), \(s\le\delta N\), \(u\in\mathbb C\), and \((t/N,u/N)\in K\). Then \[  oxed{\quad cN\, rac{|C_j(t,u)|}{|\sigma_{t,j}|} \le |L^{m val}_{t,j}(u)| \le CN^3\, rac{|C_j(t,u)|}{|\sigma_{t,j}|}, \qquad |L^{m nor}_{t,j}(u)|=  rac{|C_j(t,u)|}{|\sigma_{t,j}|}. \quad} 	ag{8} \] There is also a relative asymptotic formula retaining the exact shear: \[ L^{m val}_{t,j}(u) = rac{C_j(t,u)}{\sigma_{t,j}} [N{\cal F}_{\xi}(t/N,u/N)-\eta_{t,j}](1+o(1)), \qquad \xi=j/N, 	ag{9} \] \[ |N{\cal F}_{\xi}-\eta_{t,j}|\ge cN . 	ag{10} \] Here \({\cal F}_\xi\) is the source primitive in [N]. The relative error is uniform in these physical degree blocks and has all fixed holomorphic \(
u\) derivatives on smaller collars. In particular \[  rac1N\left(\log|L^{m val}_{t,j}(u)| -\log|C_j(t,u)/\sigma_{t,j}|ight) =O(\log N/N). 	ag{11} \] The normal dual row has the exact comparison in (8). The ordinary column's nonzero amplitude from [N] can be substituted in (9), without changing the retained inverse measure or its phase. The pair degree \(t\) is a physical integer in every assertion. Only the magnetic coordinate \(u\) varies in its fixed complex collar. ## 3. The exact imaginary part of the inverse shear The polynomial \(P_t\) in (3) has real coefficients and real roots. Deleting both occurrences of \(c_j\) leaves \(Q_{t,j}(c_j)
e0\). Consequently its logarithmic derivative in (4) is real. The other term is fixed by the original endpoint normal: \[ ho_j=- rac{s}{2\Delta_j} = rac{i s}{4\sin(\pi s/N)},\qquad  oxed{\quad  rac{\Im\eta_{t,j}}N = rac{s}{4N\sin(\pi s/N)}\ge rac1{4\pi}. \quad} 	ag{12} \] For its normalization, the original generic endpoint in [G] is \(C_m(\zeta;t,t)=(-1)^m \zeta^{dt-2Nm+m^2+m}\). The two endpoint exponents differ by \(Ns\). Dividing their derivative difference by the actual gap in (2) gives precisely \(ho_j\). Also \(2j+1=N-s\), so \(\Delta_j=2i\sin(\pi s/N)\), with the sign in (12). The final inequality uses \(\sin a\le a\). No real part of \(\eta_{t,j}\) is discarded. We will also use the existing uniform upper bound \[ |\eta_{t,j}|\le CN^3 . 	ag{13} \] For completeness, every distinct node difference factors as \(|c_j-c_m|=|1-Q^{j-m}|\,|1-Q^{j+m+1}|\ge16/N^2\). The logarithmic derivative of \(Q_{t,j}\) is a sum of fewer than \(N\) such reciprocals, counted with multiplicity. The remaining \(ho_j\) is \(O(N^2)\). This proves (13), including all parities. ## 4. A strict gap for the calibrated column normal We verify the real-domain inequality needed here. In the folded coefficient of [N], set \[ c=\cos(\pi	au),\quad \sigma=e^{\pi i	au},\quad z=e^{\pi i(	au-2
u)},\quad W=1-2cz,\quad {\cal F}_0= rac{\sqrt W+i\sigma}{8\pi c}. 	ag{14} \] For real \((	au,
u)\in{\cal P}_{\mathbb R}\), put \(b=-c\in(0,1)\) and \(	heta=\pi(	au-2
u)\). Then \(|	heta|<\pi	au<\pi\), and \(a=\cos	heta>-b\). Along this real slice \(W=1+2be^{i	heta}\) avoids the negative real axis; its source square root has positive real part. If \(v=\Im\sqrt W\), then \[ v^2= rac{\sqrt{1+4b^2+4ba}-1-2ba}{2}<b^2. 	ag{15} \] Indeed \(1+2ba+2b^2>1\), and its square minus \(1+4b^2+4ba\) equals \(4b^2(a+b)^2>0\). It follows that \[ 0<\Im{\cal F}_0 = rac{1-v/b}{8\pi}< rac1{4\pi}. 	ag{16} \] On the given compact \(S\), the upper inequality has a positive margin. Choose a small complex collar \(K\Subset{\cal P}\) so that the same strict upper margin, slightly decreased, holds for \(\Im{\cal F}_0\) there. The source primitives \({\cal F}_\xi\) in [N] depend continuously on the real parameter \(\xi\) through \(1/2\), uniformly on \(K\). Take \(\delta\) small enough to obtain the fixed-window amplitude of [N] on a buffered version of this collar, and also \[ \sup_K\Im{\cal F}_\xi\le rac1{4\pi}-2c 	ag{17} \] for the resulting actual \(\xi=j/N\). The calibrated amplitude gives \[ R_{N,j}=w_j/C_j=N{\cal F}_\xi+o(N),\qquad \sup_K\Im(R_{N,j}/N)\le rac1{4\pi}-c 	ag{18} \] for large \(N\), with every fixed magnetic derivative. Equations (12),(17),(18) imply \[ |R_{N,j}-\eta_{t,j}|\ge cN,\qquad |N{\cal F}_\xi-\eta_{t,j}|\ge cN . 	ag{19} \] This uses the actual coherent subtraction, not a lower bound for its two terms taken separately. The argument applies in the complex magnetic collar because its measure and shear still come from the real physical integer block. ## 5. Relative inverse-row amplitude Since \({\cal F}_\xi\) is bounded on this collar, [N] also gives \(|R_{N,j}|\le CN\). Equations (13),(19) prove (8). For the stronger formula, use the exact factorization \[ R_{N,j}-\eta_{t,j} =(N{\cal F}_\xi-\eta_{t,j}) \left(1+ rac{R_{N,j}-N{\cal F}_\xi} {N{\cal F}_\xi-\eta_{t,j}}ight). 	ag{20} \] The numerator in the fraction is \(o(N)\), uniformly with magnetic derivatives; its denominator is at least \(cN\). At each physical \(t\), the shear is independent of \(u\). The quotient is analytic on the collar, so buffered Cauchy estimates prove (9) with all stated relative derivatives. The remaining inverse normal row is exactly the second formula in (6). The bounds in (8) immediately give (11). The original measure can be kept quantitatively visible: \[ |\sigma_{t,j}|=  rac{N S_{t-j}S_{t+j-d}} {S_t^2\,|1-Q^{2j+1}|^2}. 	ag{21} \] All factorial indices are physical integers below \(N\). Its complex phase remains the one in (4). Neither this measure nor \(Q_{t,j}'/Q_{t,j}\) has been replaced by an asymptotic surrogate. ## 6. Both crossing signs and every physical auxiliary color Let \(1\le n\le N\) be an actual integer color. The original mixed compiler [M] has \[ L_n=l_n(\Omega),\qquad l_n(Z)=(-1)^{n-1}\mathsf U_{n-1}(Z/2), 	ag{22} \] where \(\mathsf U_r\) is the Chebyshev polynomial of the second kind. Write \(\kappa=q^{d^2/2}\); the original signed pair crossing \(\mathscr R^\epsilon\), \(\epsilon\in\{+1,-1\}\), retains \(\mathscr R(c_j)=\kappa
u_j\) and its logarithmic derivative \(ho_j\). At physical magnetic indices \(u,v\), the sum of both terms of the double-node contribution to \(\mathscr R^\epsilon L_n\) is exactly \[ {\cal D}_{t,j}^{\epsilon,n}(u,v) = rac{\kappa^\epsilon
u_j^\epsilon}{\sigma_{t,j}}\, C_j(t,u)C_j(t,v)\,{\cal A}_{t,j}^{\epsilon,n}(u,v), 	ag{23} \] \[ {\cal A}_{t,j}^{\epsilon,n} =l_n'(c_j)+l_n(c_j) [R_{N,j}(t/N,u/N)+R_{N,j}(t/N,v/N) +\epsilonho_j-\eta_{t,j}]. 	ag{24} \] Here the prime on \(l_n\) is its polynomial spectral derivative. Equation (23) is bilinear, with no conjugated column. It follows from the exact Jordan function \(\left( egin{smallmatrix}A(c)&A'(c)\0&A(c)\end{smallmatrix}ight)\) and the full inverse block (5); it is [M, equation (7)]. All Cartan, crossing, color, and measure phases shown there remain. The complex magnetic kernel used below is specified by continuing these same finite column expressions, with \(t,n\) and all measure factors still physical. For any compact real family of triples \[ 	frac12<	au<1,\qquad 0<
u<	au,\qquad0<\omega<	au, 	ag{25} \] apply the preceding construction to the union of its two \((	au,
u)\) and \((	au,\omega)\) projections. On a sufficiently small fixed complex magnetic collar, with \(	au=t/N\) still physical and real, shrink \(\delta\) so that \[ c\le\Im(R_{N,j}/N)\le rac1{4\pi}-c,\qquad c\le\Im{\cal F}_\xi\le rac1{4\pi}-c 	ag{26} \] at both indices. This follows from both strict inequalities in (16), continuity, and [N], just as in (17)--(18). Let \(q_{t,j}=Q_{t,j}'(c_j)/Q_{t,j}(c_j)\in\mathbb R\). For \(l_n(c_j)
e0\), both \(l_n(c_j)\) and \(l_n'(c_j)\) are real. Using \(\eta_{t,j}=ho_j+q_{t,j}\), the imaginary part of \({\cal A}/l_n(c_j)\) is the imaginary part of \[  egin{cases} R(t/N,u/N)+R(t/N,v/N),&\epsilon=+1,\ R(t/N,u/N)+R(t/N,v/N)-2ho_j,&\epsilon=-1 . \end{cases} 	ag{27} \] It is at least \(2cN\) in the first case and at most \(-2cN\) in the second, by (12),(26). Exactly the same bounds hold if each \(R\) is replaced by \(N{\cal F}_\xi\). These bounds are uniform through all integer-color cases. Put \(	heta_j=(2j+1)\pi/N\in(0,\pi)\). The exact color formula is \(l_n(c_j)=(-1)^{n-1}\sin(n	heta_j)/\sin	heta_j\). If this value is nonzero, the numerator is a nonzero root-lattice sine, so \[ |l_n(c_j)|\ge\sin(\pi/N)\ge2/N. 	ag{28} \] If it is zero, direct polynomial differentiation gives instead \[ |l_n'(c_j)|= rac{n}{2\sin^2	heta_j}\ge rac12 . 	ag{29} \] Thus both the exact coefficient and its specified leading version \[ {\cal A}^{m lead} =l_n'(c_j)+l_n(c_j) [N({\cal F}_\xi(t/N,u/N)+{\cal F}_\xi(t/N,v/N)) +\epsilonho_j-\eta_{t,j}] 	ag{30} \] are bounded below in modulus by a positive constant, uniformly in all \(1\le n\le N\) and both signs. Their upper bound is \(CN^4\): [M] gives \(|l_n|\le N\), \(|l_n'|\le N(N^2-1)/6\), while \(R=O(N)\), \(ho_j=O(N^2)\), and \(\eta_{t,j}=O(N^3)\). For nonzero \(l_n(c_j)\), the error in replacing the exact coefficient by (30) is \(|l_n|o(N)\), while its denominator has modulus at least \(2cN|l_n|\). When \(l_n(c_j)=0\), that error is identically zero. Consequently, uniformly over all colors and both signs, \[ {\cal D}_{t,j}^{\epsilon,n}(u,v) = rac{\kappa^\epsilon
u_j^\epsilon}{\sigma_{t,j}}\, C_j(t,u)C_j(t,v)\,{\cal A}^{m lead}(1+o(1)). 	ag{31} \] Every fixed magnetic derivative of the relative error tends to zero on smaller collars. In particular the exponential action of this individual double-node contribution is the sum of its two ordinary-column actions minus the retained measure action. The factor \({\cal A}^{m lead}\) costs only \(O(\log N)\) in the logarithm. At complete color \(n=N\), the zero case is kept exactly, rather than dividing by the vanishing value. The hypothesis \(\epsilon\in\{+1,-1\}\) is essential to this proof. For \(\epsilon=0\) the imaginary combination would subtract only one \(ho_j\), and may cancel. No assertion is made in that case. ## 7. Scope and complete inputs The complete frame still includes every other double block and every unpaired simple block, including the odd self-paired node when present. No additional normal is assigned to a simple block; its inverse row remains its original inverse simple measure times its ordinary column. The result estimates selected double-block rows, not a quotient obtained by removing the other channels. [H,M] already supply the exact full inverse and local coupon formulas. [O] already supplies strict real half-prefix action and spectral derivatives. The added conclusion here is the nonzero complex magnetic packet for the actual dual value-row subtraction and for an individual signed double-node contribution, at every color. It is not a new sector estimate or a general assertion about positivity of the inverse frame. There is no noninteger-\(t\) version of \(P_t\), \(\sigma_{t,j}\), or its inverse Gram being asserted. Subsequent turns, wire sums, source restrictions, caps and exterior factors remain literal. Nonzero inverse entries and individual node contributions do not prevent cancellation in the sum over nodes, a complete sewn coupon, or the original scalar. Nor do they bound the complete tangential error of a geometric trial for the quartic minimum. No knot-volume or finite-exception conclusion is claimed. # The full physical q-Hahn value and normal form a Gaussian–Hermite pair Written proof, 24 November 2026. The original ordinary column and its actual confluent partner have a nondegenerate two-column Hermitian Gram after an explicit centering and scaling. The ordinary column is Gaussian in its full physical magnetic norm. Orthogonal projection removes the scalar part of the normal and leaves its first Hermite mode. Both conclusions include every physical magnetic coordinate, rather than a truncated window. The result concerns one complete double channel at a real physical degree separated from the two degree endpoints. It does not turn the original bilinear gluing into a positive pairing. The proof also computes the entrywise value-column Gram across a larger channel window, retaining the original center phases. ## 1. Original columns, physical norm and the statement Put \(q_0=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(d=N-1\), and take actual integers \[ 0\le j<l,\qquad j+l=d,\qquad s=l-j,\qquad l\le t\le d. 	ag{1} \] The physical magnetic indices are \(u=0,\ldots,t\). Write \(	au=t/N\), \(\xi=j/N\), and \(u_0=t/2\), which may be half-integral. For \(q=q_0e^\epsilon\) use the marked logarithm \(\log q=\pi i/N+\epsilon\), and set \[ Q=q^2,\quad B=Q^{-N},\quad x=q^d,\quad T=Q^t,\quad U=Q^u, \] \[ C_m(q;t,u)=x^u\sum_{k=0}^m  rac{(Q^{-m};Q)_k(B^2Q^{m+1};Q)_k(U^{-1};Q)_kQ^k} {(BQ;Q)_k(T^{-1};Q)_k(Q;Q)_k},\quad (a;Q)_k=\prod_{r=0}^{k-1}(1-aQ^r). 	ag{2} \] The physical vectors in \(\mathbb C^{t+1}\) are \[ C_u=C_j(q_0;t,u),\qquad w_u= rac{D C_j(q_0;t,u)-D C_l(q_0;t,u)}{-2N\Delta_j}, \quad D=q\partial_q,\quad \Delta_j=q_0^{2j+1}-q_0^{-2j-1}. 	ag{3} \] The derivative fixes \(N,t,u\). It retains the large generic partner, all original scalar factors, and the actual eigenvalue-gap derivative. Let \(\widehat C(u)\) denote the same finite continuation in (2). Use the physical Hermitian product \(\langle v,zangle=\sum_{u=0}^t\overline{v_u}z_u\), and define \[ \alpha_N= rac{\langle C,wangle}{\|C\|^2},\qquad w^\perp=w-\alpha_N C,\qquad X_u= rac{u-u_0}{\sqrt N}. 	ag{4} \] This is a change of basis in the actual value–normal plane. It is not a quotient deleting the normal. Fix a real compact interval \(I\Subset(1/2,1)\). There is a fixed \(\delta_I>0\) such that the following estimates hold uniformly for \(	au\in I\) and the pairs (1) with \(1\le s\le\delta_I N\), at all sufficiently large levels. All constants below may depend on \(I\). Use the following coefficients: \[  egin{gathered} b=\sin(\pi\xi),\quad c=\cos(\pi	au),\quad \varpi=\sqrt{1-2c+\cos^2(\pi\xi)},\ \lambda= rac{2\pi b}{\varpi},\qquad p=2\arctan(\varpi/b),\qquad a= rac{i}{4b\varpi},\qquad \gamma= rac{|a|^2}{2\lambda} = rac1{64\pi b^3\varpi}. \end{gathered} 	ag{5} \] In particular \(\lambda,\gamma\) stay between positive constants. The full physical column measure has Gaussian moments: \[  rac{\|C\|^2}{|\widehat C(u_0)|^2\sqrt N} =\sqrt{ rac{\pi}{\lambda}}+O(N^{-1/2}),\qquad  rac{\sum_u X_u^2|C_u|^2}{\|C\|^2} = rac1{2\lambda}+O(N^{-1/2}). 	ag{6} \] The corresponding convergence holds for every fixed polynomial moment. Its first moment is exactly zero. For the actual normal, \[ \alpha_N=R_N(	au,	au/2)+O(1),\qquad \left\|w^\perp-a(u-u_0)Cight\|\le C_I\|C\|, \quad R_N(	au,
u)=w(N
u)/C(N
u). 	ag{7} \] Consequently \[  oxed{\quad  rac{\|w^\perp\|^2}{N\|C\|^2} =\gamma+O(N^{-1/2}),\qquad \det\operatorname{Gram}(C,w) =N\gamma\|C\|^4(1+O(N^{-1/2})). \quad} 	ag{8} \] Thus the Gram of \[  rac1{\|C\|} \left(C, rac{w^\perp}{\sqrt{N\gamma}}ight) 	ag{9} \] is \(\operatorname{diag}(1,1+O(N^{-1/2}))\). This retains both actual columns and their full physical supports. ## 2. An exact Gaussian upper tail on the entire physical support The magnetic polynomial [M] supplies the source-exact factorization \[ \widehat C(u)=x^u U^{-j}G_t(U),\qquad G_t(q_0^t z)=c_t B_h(z)A_n(z), \quad h=d-t,\quad n=t+j-d, 	ag{10} \] where \(c_t
e0\), all coefficients of \(A_n\) are positive, and \[ B_h(z)=\prod_{r=0}^{h-1} (1+q_0^{h-1-2r}z). \] Only the coefficient positivity is needed here; the stronger negative-root statement in [M] is not required for this estimate. For a physical \(u\), set \(	heta=2\pi(u-u_0)/N\), so \(U=q_0^t e^{i	heta}\). All prefactors outside \(B_h A_n\) in (10) have modulus one apart from the same constant \(c_t\), also at \(u_0\). Positivity gives \(|A_n(e^{i	heta})|\le A_n(1)\). Pair the factors of \(B_h\) with phases \( eta,- eta\). Since \(|	heta|\le\pi t/N\), \(| eta|\le\pi(h-1)/N\), their sum is strictly less than \(\pi\). The normalized pair modulus is \[  rac{\cos((	heta+ eta)/2)\cos((	heta- eta)/2)} {\cos^2( eta/2)} =1- rac{\sin^2(	heta/2)}{\cos^2( eta/2)} \le\cos^2(	heta/2). 	ag{11} \] It is nonnegative on this domain. If \(h\) is odd the remaining central factor has ratio \(\cos(	heta/2)>0\). Therefore, including the cases \(h=0,1\), \[  rac{|C_u|}{|\widehat C(u_0)|} \le \cos(	heta/2)^h \le \exp(-h	heta^2/8). 	ag{12} \] For \(	au\in I\), \(h\ge c_I N\) at large levels. Hence \(|C_u/\widehat C(u_0)|\le e^{-c_I X_u^2}\) on every physical index. This global bound uses neither an independent maximization nor a replacement of the original oscillatory column by positive coefficients. The exact physical reflection [G] also gives \[ C_{t-u}=C_t\overline{C_u},\qquad |C_t|=1. 	ag{13} \] Thus \(|C_{t-u}|=|C_u|\), and the physical probability measure in (6) has mean \(u_0\) exactly, including half-integral centers. ## 3. The full ordinary Gaussian On a fixed complex neighborhood of the center curve, [P] gives \[ \widehat C(N
u)=N^{-1/2}{\cal B}_\xi(	au,
u) e^{N\Phi_\xi(	au,
u)}(1+O(N^{-1})), 	ag{14} \] with a nonzero holomorphic amplitude and all fixed relative-error derivatives. The actual \(\xi=j/N\) stays in both coefficient functions. Its selected magnetic multiplier is \[ e^{\Phi_
u} = rac{(bz+i\sqrt{1-2cz+\cos^2(\pi\xi)z^2})^2} {1-2cz+z^2},\qquad z=e^{\pi i(	au-2
u)}. \] At the real center \(z=1\), direct differentiation gives \[ \Phi_
u=ip,\qquad \Phi_{
u
u}=-\lambda. 	ag{15} \] For example \(z\partial_z\log(e^{\Phi_
u})=-ib/\varpi\) there; multiplication by \(-2\pi i\) gives the second identity. The source logarithm chooses \(0<p<\pi\). Taylor expansion of (14), divided by its value at \(u_0\), yields on \(|X_u|\le N^{1/12}\) \[ C_u=\widehat C(u_0)e^{ip(u-u_0)}e^{-\lambda X_u^2/2} \left[1+O\!\left(N^{-1/2}(1+|X_u|^3)ight)ight]. 	ag{16} \] The remainder with its Gaussian factor is bounded by \(C N^{-1/2}(1+|X_u|^3)e^{-c X_u^2}\), after decreasing \(c>0\). This follows from bounded third derivatives on a fixed neighborhood; the cubic exponent is \(O(N^{-1/2}|X_u|^3)\), uniformly small on this window. The amplitude ratio has the same type of bound. Outside it, (12) gives an exponentially small tail even after multiplication by any fixed power of \(N\) or \(X_u\). Gaussian Riemann sums of spacing \(N^{-1/2}\) now prove (6) and all fixed moment statements. Their error is \(O(N^{-1/2})\): for each Gaussian times a fixed polynomial, compare the integral on each cell with its center value and integrate the absolute derivative. The far ends of the finite physical support cost \(e^{-cN}\). ## 4. Orthogonalization exposes the actual normal mode On a fixed buffered neighborhood of the center, [N, equation (30)] proves, for some positive fixed \(\delta_I\), \[ \partial_
u R_N=N\,\partial_
u{\cal F}_\xi+O(1),\qquad \partial_
u{\cal F}_\xi = rac{iz}{4b\sqrt{1-2cz+\cos^2(\pi\xi)z^2}}. 	ag{17} \] All fixed derivatives have the same bounded remainder after buffering. In particular its center value is \(a\) in (5). Integrating (17) and Taylor expanding its explicit coefficient gives, whenever \(|u-u_0|\le\eta_I N\), \[ R_N(	au,u/N)-R_N(	au,	au/2) =a(u-u_0) +O_I\!\left( rac{|u-u_0|}{N} + rac{(u-u_0)^2}{N}ight). 	ag{18} \] No estimate of the unknown magnetic-constant component of \(R_N\) is used to obtain this formula. There is no uncontrolled normal tail. On the whole physical grid, [G] proves \(|R_N|\le C_I N^4\). At the center [N] proves \(|R_N|\le C_I N\). Equations (12) and (6) therefore make the contribution of \(|u-u_0|>\eta_I N\) exponentially small in every norm or mean used below. On the central range the error in (18) is bounded by \(C_I(1+X_u^2)\), whose fixed moments are bounded by section 3. Exact symmetry (13) cancels the mean of its linear term. Averaging (18) against \(|C_u|^2/\|C\|^2\) proves the first part of (7). Subtract that mean; the same moment estimates prove its second part. Combining with the second moment in (6) proves (8). For an explicit full-profile formulation, use cells of length \(N^{-1/2}\) centered at \(X_u\), set a vector to zero off its physical cells, and define the isometry \[ ({\cal E}_{N,p}v)(x) =N^{1/4}e^{-ip(u-u_0)}v_u \quad\hbox{on the cell centered at }X_u. 	ag{19} \] The phase removal is discrete and constant on each cell. Let \(g_\lambda(x)=(\lambda/\pi)^{1/4}e^{-\lambda x^2/2}\), and let \(\omega_N=\widehat C(u_0)/|\widehat C(u_0)|\). Equations (7),(16) and the Gaussian cell estimate give \[  egin{split} \left\|{\cal E}_{N,p}  rac{\overline\omega_N C}{\|C\|}-g_\lambdaight\|_{L^2} &\le C_I N^{-1/2},\ \left\|{\cal E}_{N,p}  rac{\overline\omega_N w^\perp}{\sqrt{N\gamma}\|C\|} -i\sqrt{2\lambda}\,xg_\lambdaight\|_{L^2} &\le C_I N^{-1/2}. \end{split} 	ag{20} \] These are the zeroth and first normalized Gaussian–Hermite modes, with the actual normal's factor \(i\) retained. The uncentered Gram has the exact form \[  rac{\operatorname{Gram}(C,w)}{\|C\|^2} = egin{pmatrix} 1&\alpha_N\ \overline{\alpha_N}&|\alpha_N|^2+\|w^\perp\|^2/\|C\|^2 \end{pmatrix}. 	ag{21} \] The full calibration [N] gives \(\alpha_N/N={\cal F}_\xi(	au,	au/2)+o(1)\), a uniformly nonzero quantity after decreasing \(\delta_I\). Thus its two eigenvalues have orders \(N^2\) and \(N^{-1}\), respectively. Its condition number has order \(N^3\); the two-column frame condition has order \(N^{3/2}\). Centering and scaling in (9) explicitly removes this polynomial distortion. ## 5. The value Gram across nearby channels Fix \(R>0\), the same physical degree \(t/N=	au\in I\), and allow all complete pairs (1) with \(s\le R N^{3/4}\). This concerns only ordinary columns and follows from [P,M]; no normal estimate is being extended to a new degree domain. Put \[  egin{gathered} r_j=s^2/N^{3/2},\quad \varpi_0=\sqrt{1-2\cos(\pi	au)},\quad \lambda_0=2\pi/\varpi_0,\quad p_0=2\arctan\varpi_0,\quad  eta_0=\pi^2/(4\varpi_0),\ \psi_j=\overline{\omega_j}\,C_j/\|C_j\|,\qquad \omega_j=\exp\{i\pi[d(t-j)+j^2]/(2N)\}. \end{gathered} 	ag{22} \] The phase \(\omega_j\) is the exact center phase in [M], not a freely chosen relative channel character. Use the common discrete carrier isometry \({\cal E}_{N,p_0}\). Uniformly over this family, \[ \|{\cal E}_{N,p_0}\psi_j-g_{r_j}\|_{L^2} \le C_{I,R}N^{-1/2},\qquad g_r(x)=\left( rac{\lambda_0}{\pi}ight)^{1/4} e^{-\lambda_0x^2/2+i eta_0rx}. 	ag{23} \] Indeed set \(D_\xi=\cos^2(\pi\xi)\). At the center, \(\partial_{D_\xi}p=1/(b\varpi)\). Since \(\xi=1/2-(s+1)/(2N)\), Taylor expansion gives \[ \sqrt N(p-p_0)= eta_0 r_j+O_{I,R}(N^{-1/2}),\qquad \lambda-\lambda_0=O_{I,R}(N^{-1/2}). 	ag{24} \] The omitted \(2s+1\) in \((s+1)^2\) contributes \(O(N^{-3/4})\); the quadratic remainder in \(D_\xi\) contributes \(O(N^{-1/2})\). Use (16), (12) and the same moment bounds to obtain (23). Gaussian integration consequently gives the source-specific entrywise Gram formula \[  oxed{\quad \langle\psi_j,\psi_kangle =\exp\!\left[- rac{\pi^3(r_j-r_k)^2}{128\varpi_0}ight] +O_{I,R}(N^{-1/2}). \quad} 	ag{25} \] For \(s\le M\sqrt N\), all these phase-normalized unit columns are \(O_{I,M}(N^{-1/2})\) from the same full Gaussian. In particular they are not a uniformly separated orthogonal channel frame on that window. An entrywise error for a growing family does not give a lower bound for its smallest Gram eigenvalue. ## 6. The exact adjoint carrier has a tame doubled pairing There is also an exact gluing consequence for these particular full physical packets. Set \(q=q_0\), \[  egin{gathered} c_j=q^{2j+1}+q^{-2j-1},\quad P_t(Z)=\prod_{m=0}^t(Z-c_m),\quad Q_{t,j}(Z)=P_t(Z)/(Z-c_j)^2,\ B_t=(-1)^t\left(\prod_{r=1}^t2\sin(\pi r/N)ight)^2,\quad 
u_j=(-1)^j q^{j(j+1)},\ \sigma_{t,j}=x^t
u_j Q_{t,j}(c_j)/B_t,\qquad \eta_{t,j}=- rac{s}{2\Delta_j} + rac{Q_{t,j}'(c_j)}{Q_{t,j}(c_j)} . \end{gathered} 	ag{26} \] The complete actual Hermite identity [H] is \[ C^{\mathsf T}C=0,\qquad C^{\mathsf T}w=\sigma_{t,j},\qquad w^{\mathsf T}w=\sigma_{t,j}\eta_{t,j},\qquad |\eta_{t,j}|\le C N^3 . 	ag{27} \] Transpose here has no conjugation. All phases in \(\sigma_{t,j}\) are retained. Put \(d_N=\|w^\perp\|/\|C\|\), \(e_0=C/\|C\|\), \(e_1=w^\perp/(\|C\|d_N)\), and \({\cal U}=(e_0,e_1)\). These two vectors are exactly Hermitian orthonormal. Formula (27) gives their exact bilinear Gram \[ {\cal B}={\cal U}^{\mathsf T}{\cal U} = rac{\sigma_{t,j}}{\|C\|^2d_N}  egin{pmatrix} 0&1\1&(\eta_{t,j}-2\alpha_N)/d_N \end{pmatrix}. 	ag{28} \] The native energy in [E] is precisely \(E_{t,j}=\|C\|^2/|\sigma_{t,j}|\). It has \(\log E_{t,j}=N e(	au,\xi)+O(\log N)\), uniformly near the fold on our real degree compact. Its folded profile is positive throughout \(1/2\le	au\le1\), starting at \(v_8/(2\pi)>0\) and increasing. Continuity in \(\xi\) therefore allows a further fixed decrease of \(\delta_I\) so that \(e(	au,\xi)\ge c_I>0\). Use (8), \(\alpha_N=O_I(N)\), and (27) in (28). For some \(a_I>0\), \[ \|{\cal B}\|\le C_I e^{-a_I N}. 	ag{29} \] Thus pairing two copies of this same carrier bilinearly is exponentially small, despite its positive Hermitian Gram. Retain instead both this actual carrier and its complex conjugate: \({\cal D}=({\cal U},\overline{\cal U})\). Exact matrix identities give \[ {\cal D}^*{\cal D} = egin{pmatrix}I&\overline{\cal B}\{\cal B}&I\end{pmatrix}, \qquad {\cal D}^{\mathsf T}{\cal D} = egin{pmatrix}{\cal B}&I\I&\overline{\cal B}\end{pmatrix}. 	ag{30} \] Their respective limits are \(I_4\) and the two-by-two block swap, with exponentially small errors. In particular the doubled physical frame and this bilinear pairing have bounded condition numbers for large levels. No original normal direction was removed to get this. Its operator type matters. The original physical Casimir block \(\Omega_t\) is complex symmetric, and \[ \Omega_t{\cal U} ={\cal U} egin{pmatrix}c_j&d_N^{-1}\0&c_j\end{pmatrix}, \qquad \Omega_t^*\overline{\cal U} =\overline{\cal U}  egin{pmatrix}c_j&d_N^{-1}\0&c_j\end{pmatrix}. 	ag{31} \] The conjugate vectors are an actual adjoint-Casimir carrier, not additional eigenchannels of \(\Omega_t\). Formula (30) is an exact adapter when those two stated boundary types are paired. It does not assert that an arbitrary original crossing, turn, cap or partial filling produces the adjoint carrier on the other side. ## 7. What the Gram does and does not change The magnetic energy calculation [E] already gives exact Fourier norm comparisons and its original center action. A separate initialized-meridian-row calculation in the research ledger constructs fixed-order Gaussian jet Grams for a different source. Here the vectors are the ordinary and actual generic-confluent q-Hahn columns (3), and (12) controls their complete physical tails. Their particular normal direction and the cross-channel scale in (25) are computed from these original source equations. The Hermitian Gram above is not the bilinear complete Christoffel–Darboux gluing matrix. Original inverse rows, its measure and phase, the marked closing, turns, and external normalizations must be transported through any basis change. No cap is asserted to be the Hermitian adjoint of a cup. The statement also excludes the physical endpoint \(t=N-1\) as a uniform degree family and excludes the isolated simple channel. This supplies full-packet norm and transverse-normal information. It does not estimate the sum over distinct Casimir nodes, match geometric packets across an arbitrary short component, or prove a nonzero original scalar after closing. No new knot-volume case or finite-exception theorem follows without those further estimates. title: Source-normalized transport of the actual q-Hahn partner near the fold

# Source-normalized transport of the actual q-Hahn partner near the fold Written proof, 24 November 2026. The original generic q-Hahn columns have scalar normalizers which vanish near the channel fold. Keeping those normalizers inside the degree recurrence cancels the large coefficients at every nonresonant row. Only finitely many resonant rows retain a polynomial cost. This gives a relative upper bound with a linear scaled-channel exponent, on every fixed compact of the full strict physical tube. The normal is the original difference of two generic highest-weight \(N-1\) derivatives. No root-only derivative, interpolated normal, or complex continuation of the integer channel is substituted. ## 1. Exact source and statement Let \(N\ge3\), \(d=N-1\), \(q_0=e^{\pi i/N}\), and choose integers \[ 0\le j<l,\qquad j+l=d,\qquad s=l-j. 	ag{1} \] For \(q=q_0e^\epsilon\), keep \(N,t,u\) fixed when differentiating, and put \[ Q=q^2,\quad B=Q^{-N},\quad A=B^{-1},\quad x=q^d,\quad t=N	au,\quad u=N
u,\quad T=Q^t,\quad \sigma=q^t,\quad X=Q^{-u}. 	ag{2} \] All powers use \(\log q=\pi i/N+\epsilon\). Write \((a;Q)_k=\prod_{r=0}^{k-1}(1-aQ^r)\). The actual generic column is \[ C_m(q;t,u)=x^u F_m(Q,B;X,T),\qquad F_m=\sum_{k=0}^m  rac{(Q^{-m};Q)_k(B^2Q^{m+1};Q)_k(X;Q)_kQ^k} {(BQ;Q)_k(T^{-1};Q)_k(Q;Q)_k}. 	ag{3} \] The variable \(B\) can temporarily be independent in rational identities. Its value in the original source is always \(Q^{-N}\). This is the finite generic source of [S] and [C], rather than a deformation of its root specialization chosen afterward. The paired normal, with its original Casimir gap and sign, is \[ w_{j,l}(t,u)=  rac{D C_j(q_0;t,u)-D C_l(q_0;t,u)}{-2N\Delta_j}, \qquad \Delta_j=q_0^{2j+1}-q_0^{-2j-1},\qquad D=q\partial_q. 	ag{4} \] In particular the large generic partner in (4) is retained. Let \[ {\cal P}=\{(	au,
u)\in\mathbb C^2: 	frac12<\Re	au<1,\quad 0<\Re
u<\Re	au\}. 	ag{5} \] For every compact \(K\Subset{\cal P}\), there are constants \(\eta_K>0\), \(C_K\ge1\), and \(N_K\) such that, for all \(N\ge N_K\) and all actual pairs (1) with \(1\le s\le\eta_KN\), \[  oxed{\quad \left| rac{w_{j,l}(N	au,N
u)} {C_j(q_0;N	au,N
u)}ight| \le C_K N^{100} C_K^s,\qquad (	au,
u)\in K . \quad} 	ag{6} \] The denominator is nonzero, and both numerator and denominator are holomorphic on a neighborhood of \(K\), for these sufficiently large levels. Constants are uniform over all admissible integer pairs; their parity restriction is exactly \(j+l=N-1\). Consequently every window \(s=o(N)\) has subexponential relative cost. For a fixed \(0<\delta\le\eta_K\), the corresponding upper exponential cost is at most \(\delta\log C_K\), which tends to zero with \(\delta\). These are upper bounds, not a leading normal amplitude. ## 2. The monic recurrence and its source normalization Put \[ D_m(T)=\prod_{r=0}^{m-1}(T-Q^r),\qquad \kappa_m= rac{(B^2Q^{m+1};Q)_m}{(BQ;Q)_m},\qquad z=\sigma Q^{-u}. 	ag{7} \] For generic parameters define the monic polynomial \(R_m\) by \[ R_m(z)= rac{D_m(\sigma^2)}{\sigma^m\kappa_m} F_m(Q,B;z/\sigma,\sigma^2). \quad	ext{Thus}\quad C_m=x^u a^{m src}_m R_m(z),\qquad a^{m src}_m= rac{\sigma^m\kappa_m}{D_m(T)}. 	ag{8} \] The exact leading coefficient and finite degree recurrence in [S,N] give \[ R_{n+1}=(z+\alpha_n)R_n+ eta_nR_{n-1},\qquad R_0=1,\quad R_1=z+\alpha_0. 	ag{9} \] For clarity, their rational coefficients are specified completely by \[  egin{split} \Lambda_n&=AQ^{-n}+BQ^{n+1},\ b_n&= rac{(1+A)+Q\sigma^2(1+B) -Q^{-n}(Q\sigma^2+A)-Q^n(BQ\sigma^2+1)}{\sigma},\ d_n&=Q^{1-n}+Q^n-1-Q,\ \mathfrak u_n&= rac{b_n}{\Lambda_n-\Lambda_{n-1}}\quad(n\ge1),\ \mathfrak v_n&= rac{b_{n-1}\mathfrak u_n+d_n} {\Lambda_n-\Lambda_{n-2}}\quad(n\ge2),\ \alpha_n&=\mathfrak u_{n+1}-\mathfrak u_n,\qquad  eta_n=\mathfrak v_{n+1}-\mathfrak v_n-\alpha_n\mathfrak u_n, \end{split} 	ag{10} \] where \(\mathfrak u_0=\mathfrak v_0=\mathfrak v_1=0\). These are rational identities for every integer degree, including degrees beyond the small channel. One way to justify that range, as in [N], is to fix the recurrence index and clear denominators. The residual is a finite Laurent polynomial in \(B,Q,\sigma,z\), independent of the source size. Its vanishing at \(B=Q^{-N}\) for all sufficiently large source sizes separates its finite \(Q\)-exponent supports and forces the rational identity. A small-channel slice count at the present fixed \(N\) is not being applied to its large partner. The exact consecutive scalar ratio simplifies to \[ ho_n:= rac{\kappa_{n+1}}{\kappa_n} = rac{(1-B^2Q^{2n+1})(1-B^2Q^{2n+2})} {(1-B^2Q^{n+1})(1-BQ^{n+1})}. 	ag{11} \] This follows directly by canceling the ranges \(n+1,\ldots,2n\) and \(n+2,\ldots,2n+2\) in the two finite products. Set \[ a_n= rac{\sigmaho_n}{T-Q^n} = rac{a^{m src}_{n+1}}{a^{m src}_n}. 	ag{12} \] Multiplying (9) by its actual scalar gives the recurrence used here: \[  oxed{\quad C_{n+1}=a_n(z+\alpha_n)C_n +a_na_{n-1} eta_n C_{n-1}. \quad} 	ag{13} \] The common factor \(x^u\) cancels between consecutive degrees. Equation (13) is first used off the root, where all its monic factors are defined. It does not assert that those individual monic factors extend holomorphically across the fold. ## 3. Initial control on a genuine generic circle Fix a slightly larger compact neighborhood of \(K\) inside \({\cal P}\), and choose \[ 0<\eta_K<\min\left(	frac14,\inf_K(\Re	au-	frac12)ight). 	ag{14} \] Decrease it for that neighborhood if necessary. For \(s\le\eta_KN\), all indices from \(j-1\) to \(l+1\) lie near \(N/2\). Every extra divisor \(T=Q^r\), \(j\le r<l\), is then uniformly separated from this neighborhood. Its real scaled index is less than \(1/2+\eta_K/2\), whereas \(\Re	au\) stays farther to the right. The original small-column divisors are separated as well. Use the circle \[ |\epsilon|=\varrho_N=c_KN^{-8}. 	ag{15} \] The original generic determinant construction in [S] and its full-physical extension [P, section 6] give, on the entire disk, \[ \left| rac{C_j(q;t,u)}{C_j(q_0;t,u)}ight|\le C_K, \qquad \left| rac{R_{j-1}(z(q))}{R_j(z(q))}ight|\le C_K. 	ag{16} \] Here is the relevant distinction in the enlarged domain. The root determinant has a uniformly bounded inverse by the rotated positive-half-plane realization in [P]. For each adjacent pair one freezes the larger of its two root entries and sets the other generic entry to retain the exact product \(- eta_n(q)\). That frozen entry is uniformly bounded below. Freezing one specified upper entry everywhere would fail at its possible zeros. The generic perturbation is \(O_K(N^7|\epsilon|)\). The last inverse cofactor is precisely \(R_{j-1}/R_j\). This proves the two controls used in (16), with all original scalar factors restored. It also proves that \(C_j(q_0)
e0\) on \(K\). The initial consecutive actual columns have a modest additional cost. Since \(2j\le N-2\), neither numerator factor of \(ho_{j-1}\) in (11), with indices \(2j-1,2j\), vanishes at the root. Each has modulus at least \(c/N\). Its denominator factors lie near index \(N/2\) and are uniformly separated from zero. The bounded, nonzero factor \(\sigma/(T-Q^{j-1})\) therefore gives \[ |a_{j-1}^{-1}|\le C_KN^2,\qquad \left| rac{C_{j-1}(q;t,u)}{C_j(q_0;t,u)}ight| \le C_KN^2 	ag{17} \] on (15). These estimates persist on the disk, since the change in \(a_{j-1}\) is \(O_K(N|\epsilon|)\), much smaller than \(N^{-2}\). Only sufficiently large \(N\) is needed; then \(j\ge1\). ## 4. Uniform nonresonant transfers For a recurrence row \(j\le n<l\), write \[ q_n^{m dist}=1+|2n-N|,\qquad {\cal B}_N=\{n:|2n-N|\le4\}. 	ag{18} \] There are at most five bad rows in \({\cal B}_N\). Outside this set, all required root gaps for (10), including those with index \(n+1\), are nonzero. At the root put \(	heta=\pi/N\) and \(c=-\cos((t+1)	heta)\). The exact coefficients reduce to \[ \alpha_n= rac{c}{\cos(n	heta)\cos((n+1)	heta)},\qquad  eta_n=  rac{\sin^2(n	heta)[\cos^2(n	heta)-c^2]} {\cos^2(n	heta)\sin((2n-1)	heta)\sin((2n+1)	heta)}. 	ag{19} \] Although first derived on the small side in [S], these root formulas hold at every nonresonant degree. Fixing \(n\), they are rational identities in \(q,\sigma\) at \(B=1\): their cleared residual vanishes for all sufficiently large primitive source roots, and identically in \(\sigma\). The distinct \(q_0\) accumulate at \(1\), so that Laurent-polynomial residual is zero. This argument extends the identity, not an estimate through a pole. For example the diagonal formula follows directly at \(B=1\) from \(\mathfrak u_n=-(1+Q\sigma^2)(1-Q^n)/ [\sigma(1-Q)(1+Q^n)]\), fixing its sign. For \(n
otin{\cal B}_N\), the trigonometric distances in (19) give \[ |\alpha_n(0)|\le C_K(N/q_n^{m dist})^2,\qquad | eta_n(0)|\le C_K(N/q_n^{m dist})^4. 	ag{20} \] In contrast, the two numerator factors of (11) vanish quadratically in the scaled distance from the fold. Since its denominator factors are units near index \(N/2\), both neighboring actual scalar ratios obey \[ |a_n(0)|+|a_{n-1}(0)| \le C_K(q_n^{m dist}/N)^2. 	ag{21} \] The shift from \(n\) to \(n-1\) is harmless outside the bad set. We need these bounds on the actual circle, not only at its center. The only spectral differences in (10) factor as \[  egin{split} \Lambda_m-\Lambda_{m-1} &=(1-Q)AQ^{-m}(1-B^2Q^{2m}),\ \Lambda_m-\Lambda_{m-2} &=(1-Q^2)AQ^{-m}(1-B^2Q^{2m-1}). \end{split} 	ag{22} \] At nonbad rows all the differences required for \(\mathfrak u_n,\mathfrak v_n,\mathfrak u_{n+1},\mathfrak v_{n+1}\) have modulus at least \(c/N^2\), persisting on a small \(N^{-3}\) disk. The elementary coefficients in (10) are \(O_K(1)\) and their \(\epsilon\)-derivatives are \(O_K(N)\). The quotient rule gives \(\mathfrak u'=O_K(N^5)\), \(\mathfrak v'=O_K(N^7)\), and hence \(\alpha_n'=O_K(N^5)\), \( eta_n'=O_K(N^7)\). Thus their changes on (15) are \(O_K(N^{-3})\) and \(O_K(N^{-1})\). These are absorbed in (20), since \(q_n^{m dist}\le N\). Likewise \(a_n'=O_K(N)\) directly from (11),(12), so the change \(O_K(N^{-7})\) is absorbed in (21). Combining these retained source ratios with (20) yields \[ |a_n(z+\alpha_n)|+ |a_na_{n-1} eta_n|\le C_K,\qquad n
otin{\cal B}_N, 	ag{23} \] on the circle. This is the cancellation lost by propagating only the monic recurrence and subsequently bounding its normalizers. ## 5. The finite resonant cost and the actual normal At a bad row the last factor of a resonant difference (22) is \(1-Q^{-N}=1-e^{-2N\epsilon}\). On (15) it has modulus at least \(cN\varrho_N\). Its first factor has size at least \(c/N\). All other required gaps remain at least \(c/N^2\). Therefore every gap is at least \(c_K\varrho_N\) on the circle, just as in [N]. The exact formulas (10) then give \[ |\alpha_n|\le C_K\varrho_N^{-1},\qquad | eta_n|\le C_K\varrho_N^{-2}. 	ag{24} \] The scalar ratios \(a_n,a_{n-1}\) themselves are uniformly bounded there, including bad rows: the denominators in (11),(12) are units and all their numerators are bounded. A bad two-component transfer in (13) consequently costs at most \(C_KN^{16}\). Starting with (16),(17), propagate the actual recurrence (13) through exactly \(s\) rows. There are at most five bad transfers, so \[ \left| rac{C_l(q;t,u)}{C_j(q_0;t,u)}ight| \le C_K N^{82} C_K^s \qquad (|\epsilon|=\varrho_N). 	ag{25} \] No product of singular monic factors is differentiated. The full finite formula (3) is holomorphic inside the circle: its factorial indices are less than \(N\), and its \(T\) divisors are separated by (14). All apparent monic poles have therefore already canceled in the original source. Cauchy's formula applied to these full columns, with \(t,u,N\) fixed, now gives \[ \left| rac{D C_l(q_0)}{C_j(q_0)}ight| \le C_KN^{90}C_K^s,\qquad \left| rac{D C_j(q_0)}{C_j(q_0)}ight|\le C_KN^8. 	ag{26} \] Finally the actual gap in (4) satisfies \(2N|\Delta_j|=4N\sin(\pi s/N)\ge8s\ge8\). Equations (4),(26) prove (6), with room in the exponent \(100\). ## 6. Consequences, scope, and complete inputs Taking logarithms of (6) gives \[ \log|w_{j,l}/C_j| \le100\log N+(s+1)\log C_K. 	ag{27} \] Thus all \(s=o(N)\), rather than only \(s\log N=o(N)\), have subexponential relative upper cost on the same fixed magnetic compact. Uniformly for \(s\le\delta N\), its upper exponential cost is at most \(\delta\log C_K+o(1)\). At a fixed positive \(\delta\), this still permits exponential cost; subexponential cost there is not asserted. The original scalar ratios remove the nonresonant fold-distance cost. The old near-fold estimate [N] and its enlargement in [P] paid \(N^{16}\) at every intervening row. The improvement here comes from the exact actual-source recurrence (13). The normalizer zeros are used before taking absolute values, with finitely many resonances kept explicit. This does not replace the generic derivative in (4) by a derivative of a root collision identity. The result concerns actual integer channels and fixed complex magnetic compacts. It does not continue the channel to a complex parameter, prove a nonzero leading normal amplitude, or control the complete q-Hahn coupon after its remaining factors and contractions. It does not place a short-filled geometric saddle in this corridor or establish its coefficient in the original closed source. No volume or finite-exception conclusion follows here. title: Unipotent transport of the actual q-Hahn normal near the fold
text:
# Unipotent transport of the actual q-Hahn normal near the fold Written proof, 24 November 2026. The actual q-Hahn source has an exact constant column at magnetic input zero. This supplies a value/difference form of its channel recurrence. After a real rescaling of the difference, the nonresonant transfers are close to the identity in operator norm. Their accumulated cost is quadratic in the scaled channel separation. All columns and normal derivatives below retain the original generic highest-weight \(N-1\) source. The result is a relative upper bound for its paired normal, not a nonzero leading amplitude or a closed-source lower bound. ## 1. The source, the normal, and the bound Let \(N\ge3\), \(d=N-1\), \(q_0=e^{\pi i/N}\), and take actual integers \[ 0\le j<l,\qquad j+l=d,\qquad s=l-j. 	ag{1} \] Set \(q=q_0e^\epsilon\), with \(\log q=\pi i/N+\epsilon\), and write \[ Q=q^2,\quad B=Q^{-N},\quad x=q^d,\quad t=N	au,\quad u=N
u,\quad T=Q^t,\quad \sigma=q^t,\quad X=Q^{-u},\quad z=\sigma Q^{-u}. 	ag{2} \] The exact finite generic column is \[ C_m(q;t,u)=x^u\sum_{k=0}^m  rac{(Q^{-m};Q)_k(B^2Q^{m+1};Q)_k(X;Q)_kQ^k} {(BQ;Q)_k(T^{-1};Q)_k(Q;Q)_k}, \quad (a;Q)_k=\prod_{r=0}^{k-1}(1-aQ^r). 	ag{3} \] The original normal and its actual Casimir divisor are \[ w_{j,l}(t,u)= rac{D C_j(q_0;t,u)-D C_l(q_0;t,u)} {-2N\Delta_j},\qquad D=q\partial_q,\qquad \Delta_j=q_0^{2j+1}-q_0^{-2j-1}. 	ag{4} \] The derivative keeps \(N,t,u\) fixed and hence follows the actual family \(B=Q^{-N}\), including the large partner. Let \[ {\cal P}=\{(	au,
u)\in\mathbb C^2: 	frac12<\Re	au<1,\quad 0<\Re
u<\Re	au\}. 	ag{5} \] **Theorem.** For every compact \(K\Subset{\cal P}\), there are \(C_K\ge1\), \(A_K\ge0\), \(\eta_K>0\), and \(N_K\) such that \[  oxed{\quad \left| rac{w_{j,l}(N	au,N
u)} {C_j(q_0;N	au,N
u)}ight| \le C_K N^{A_K} \exp\!\left(C_K rac{s^2}{N}ight) \quad} 	ag{6} \] for \(N\ge N_K\), \(1\le s\le\eta_KN\), and \((	au,
u)\in K\). The columns and normal are holomorphic near \(K\) at these levels, and the denominator is nonzero. In particular \(s\le M\sqrt N\), with fixed \(M\), has polynomial relative cost. Every \(s=o(N)\) still has subexponential upper cost. At a fixed \(0<\delta\le\eta_K\), the upper exponential cost for \(s\le\delta N\) is at most \(C_K\delta^2\). This last statement allows exponential growth at each fixed positive \(\delta\). ## 2. Exact recurrence and the constant source anchor Keep the monic recurrence and its exact normalization from [F]: \[ C_m=x^u rac{\sigma^m\kappa_m}{D_m(T)}R_m(z),\quad D_m(T)=\prod_{r=0}^{m-1}(T-Q^r),\quad \kappa_m= rac{(B^2Q^{m+1};Q)_m}{(BQ;Q)_m}, 	ag{7} \] \[ R_{n+1}=(z+\alpha_n)R_n+ eta_nR_{n-1}. 	ag{8} \] The rational formulas and their full integer-degree justification are given in [F, equations (9)--(10)], with the original proofs in [S,N]. The actual consecutive scalar ratio is \[ ho_n= rac{\kappa_{n+1}}{\kappa_n} = rac{(1-B^2Q^{2n+1})(1-B^2Q^{2n+2})} {(1-B^2Q^{n+1})(1-BQ^{n+1})},\qquad a_n= rac{\sigmaho_n}{T-Q^n}. 	ag{9} \] Thus the exact actual-column recurrence on the generic circle is \[ C_{n+1}=a_n(z+\alpha_n)C_n+ a_na_{n-1} eta_nC_{n-1}. 	ag{10} \] These coefficients depend on \(q,t\); their only magnetic dependence in (10) is the displayed \(z\). There is an additional exact normalization in (3): \[ C_m(q;t,0)=1\quad\hbox{for every }m. 	ag{11} \] Indeed \(X=1\) makes every summand with \(k\ge1\) vanish, and \(x^0=1\). Substitution in (10), where now \(z=\sigma\), gives \[ a_n(\sigma+\alpha_n)+a_na_{n-1} eta_n=1. 	ag{12} \] This is a generic rational identity, prior to taking the root. Define \[ \delta C_n=C_n-C_{n-1},\qquad \varepsilon_n=a_n(z-\sigma),\qquad b_n=a_n(\sigma+\alpha_n)-1=-a_na_{n-1} eta_n. 	ag{13} \] The value and its difference therefore obey exactly \[ \delta C_{n+1}=\varepsilon_n C_n+b_n\delta C_n,\qquad C_{n+1}=(1+\varepsilon_n)C_n+b_n\delta C_n. 	ag{14} \] No root collision identity has been differentiated to obtain this system. In particular (11) is not an assumed normalization of an independent solution. ## 3. The source-specific unipotent estimate Choose \(\eta_K\) and a slightly larger compact neighborhood as in [F], with \[ 0<\eta_K<\min\left(	frac14,\inf_K(\Re	au-	frac12)ight). 	ag{15} \] All estimates below are on the genuine generic circle \(|\epsilon|=\varrho_N=c_KN^{-8}\). For every integer \(n\), put \[ r_n=1+|2n-N|,\qquad {\cal B}_N=\{n:|2n-N|\le4\}. 	ag{16} \] Among the used rows \(j\le n<l\), at most five are bad. At every other used row [F] proves, on that circle, \[ |a_n|+|a_{n-1}|\le C_K(r_n/N)^2,\quad |\alpha_n|\le C_K(N/r_n)^2,\quad | eta_n|\le C_K(N/r_n)^4. 	ag{17} \] It follows immediately that \(|\varepsilon_n|\le C_K(r_n/N)^2\). The decisive improvement is the estimate for \(b_n-1\). At the root \(B=1\), set \(y=Q_0^n\). The exact diagonal coefficient is \[ \alpha_n= - rac{2(1+Q_0T)y}{\sigma(1+y)(1+Q_0y)}. 	ag{18} \] This is the root formula of [S,F] at every nonresonant degree. Combining it with (9), and canceling \(1-Q_0^2y^2\), gives \[ a_n\alpha_n= - rac{2(1+Q_0T)y(1-Q_0y^2)} {(T-y)(1-Q_0y)(1+y)}. 	ag{19} \] All denominators other than \(1+y\) stay uniformly separated from zero in this near-fold range. Also \(|1+y|\asymp r_n/N\) at a nonbad row. In (19), replace \(Q_0\) by \(1\) while holding \(y,T\) fixed. The result is \(-2(1+T)y/(T-y)\). Its difference from \(2\) is \[ - rac{2T(1+y)}{T-y}=O_K(r_n/N). 	ag{20} \] The error in this replacement is \(O_K(1/r_n)\): \(|Q_0-1|=O(N^{-1})\), and the only small denominator is \(1+y\). Explicitly, \(1-Q_0y^2=(1-y^2)+(1-Q_0)y^2\); all remaining factors and their differences have uniformly bounded denominators. Since \(a_n\sigma=O_K((r_n/N)^2)\), equations (13),(19)--(20) give the root estimate \[ |b_n(0)-1| \le C_K(r_n/N+1/r_n). 	ag{21} \] This estimate persists on the actual generic circle. We use the generic quotient estimates, not a derivative of (18). At a nonbad row they give \[ a_n'=O_K(N),\qquad \alpha_n=O_K(N^2),\qquad \alpha_n'=O_K(N^5),\qquad \sigma'=O_K(N) 	ag{22} \] on the small disk; primes mean \(\partial_\epsilon\). The factors \(a_n,\sigma\) are bounded there. Differentiating the generic expression \(b_n=a_n(\sigma+\alpha_n)-1\) now gives \(b_n'=O_K(N^5)\). Its change on the \(N^{-8}\) circle is \(O_K(N^{-3})\), absorbed in (21). We have consequently proved the uniform nonbad estimates \[ |\varepsilon_n|\le C_K(r_n/N)^2,\qquad |b_n-1|\le C_K(r_n/N+1/r_n). 	ag{23} \] The real scale \(r_n\) records the degree's distance to the fold; it does not change the complex magnetic variables. ## 4. A bounded value/difference frame For every \(j\le n\le l\), define \[ h_n= rac{r_n}{N}+ rac1{r_n},\qquad Y_n= egin{pmatrix}C_n\ \delta C_n/h_n\end{pmatrix}. 	ag{24} \] These weights are positive and \(h_n\ge2/\sqrt N\). Throughout the near-fold interval they are bounded above by a fixed constant. The neighboring ratios satisfy \[ \max\left( rac{h_n}{h_{n+1}},  rac{h_{n+1}}{h_n}ight)\le1+ rac{C}{r_n}. 	ag{25} \] To check this directly, \(|r_{n+1}-r_n|\le2\), and their ratio is between \(1/3\) and \(3\). For \(h(r)=r/N+1/r\), \(|\partial_r\log h(r)|\le1/r\). Integrating on an interval of length at most two proves the individual bounds for \(r_n\ge3\); the finitely many values \(r_n=1,2\) satisfy them after increasing the absolute constant. In this frame (14) becomes the exact matrix equation \[ Y_{n+1}=  egin{pmatrix} 1+\varepsilon_n&b_nh_n\ \varepsilon_n/h_{n+1}&b_nh_n/h_{n+1} \end{pmatrix}Y_n . 	ag{26} \] At a nonbad row its induced maximum norm is at most \[ 1+C_Kh_n. 	ag{27} \] Indeed the first absolute row sum is at most \(1+|\varepsilon_n|+(1+C_Kh_n)h_n\). For the second row, (23),(25) give \[ |\varepsilon_n|/h_{n+1}\le C_K r_n/N,\qquad |b_n|h_n/h_{n+1}\le(1+C_Kh_n)(1+C/r_n). 	ag{28} \] Use \(r_n/N\le h_n\), \(1/r_n\le h_n\), and the uniform upper bound for \(h_n\). Both row sums are then bounded by (27). This argument allows arbitrary complex phases. At a bad row \(r_n\le5\) and \(r_{n+1}\le7\), so both frame changes are uniformly bounded. The original actual-column transfer from [F] costs at most \(C_KN^{16}\) on the circle. The same safe bound therefore holds in (26), with at most five such factors. The full accumulated nonbad cost is controlled by \[ \sum_{n=j}^{l-1}h_n \le C rac{s^2}{N}+C igl(1+\log(s+2) igr). 	ag{29} \] For the first sum use \(r_n\le s+2\), so \(\sum r_n/N\le s(s+2)/N\le3s^2/N\). For the second, each positive integer value of \(r_n\) occurs at most twice; hence \(\sum1/r_n\le2\sum_{m=1}^{s+2}1/m\). This proves (29), with no loss proportional to \(s\). ## 5. Initial field, full-source Cauchy estimate, and scope The full-physical determinant and its last inverse cofactor give the initial bounds from [F, equations (16)--(17)]: \[ |C_j(q)/C_j(q_0)|\le C_K,\qquad |C_{j-1}(q)/C_j(q_0)|\le C_KN^2. 	ag{30} \] They use the actual scalar ratio, whose initial inverse is \(O_K(N^2)\), and the full-physical larger-entry freezing from [P]. Thus \(h_j^{-1}\le\sqrt N/2\) implies \(\|Y_j/C_j(q_0)\|_\infty\le C_KN^3\). Multiplying (26), using the at most five bad rows and (27),(29), gives constants \(a_K,C_K\) such that \[ |C_l(q)/C_j(q_0)| \le C_KN^{a_K}\exp(C_Ks^2/N) \quad (|\epsilon|=\varrho_N). 	ag{31} \] The compact-dependent polynomial power includes the harmonic factor \((s+2)^{C_K}\) in (29), besides the explicit initial and bad-row powers. A universal numerical exponent is not asserted. Apply Cauchy's formula to the full finite columns (3). They are holomorphic throughout this disk: factorial indices are less than \(N\), and (15) keeps all \(T\) divisors separated. The singular monic factors have already canceled in that finite source. The derivatives therefore cost only the additional factor \(\varrho_N^{-1}=O_K(N^8)\). Finally \(2N|\Delta_j|=4N\sin(\pi s/N)\ge8s\ge8\). Together with the corresponding small-column derivative bound, this proves (6), with a larger compact-dependent \(A_K\). The previous source-normalized estimate [F] bounded each regular transfer by a fixed constant. The exact source anchor (11), the explicit root formula (19), and the weighted difference frame instead retain its near-unipotent form. This is why the scaled cost improves from linear to quadratic. The closest flux rescaling in [V] concerns a different source: a positive anchored four-coherent scalar on its physical half-grid. It proves a terminal fold value and does not estimate this generic q-Hahn derivative. Here no positivity of the column or of a flux is assumed, and both generic partner derivatives remain in (4). The theorem retains actual integer channels and both level parities. It does not provide a complex-channel interpolation, a nonzero normal amplitude, a bound for the complete contracted coupon, or a contributing original geometric cycle. In particular polynomial cost on the Gaussian channel scale does not prove that the needed short-filled geometric configuration lies there, or that its original cap projection is nonzero. No knot-volume lower bound or finite-exception theorem is claimed. title: Quantitative reconstruction from the actual cyclotomic source jets
text:
# Quantitative reconstruction from the actual cyclotomic source jets Private written proof, 23 November 2026. The exact bounded-jet Mellin theorem has a quantitative version for every specified actual arithmetic operator in that theorem. Its loss is at most \(e^{CN^2}\). When the leading coefficient is a product of nonconstant clock binomials, the loss improves to \(N^Ae^{CN}\). Both bounds include singular steps and preserve the original prefix, affine source, pole lattice and residue. The extra factor hypothesis is not proved for every Conway operator. No geometric approximate section is constructed, and no volume identity or arbitrary-short-filling theorem follows. ## 1. Actual source and the optional factor hypothesis Use the complete \(Q\)-only conventions of [M]: \[ P=\sum_{j=0}^{d}a_j(Q,Y)T^j,\qquad TY=QYT,\qquad \sum_{j=0}^{d}a_j(Q,Q^m)C_{m+j}(Q)=0,\quad m\ge1. 	ag{1} \] Here \(d\ge1\), the \(C_r\) are the actual reduced color periods, and the fixed \(a_j\) are Laurent polynomials over a fixed number field after one recorded denominator clearing. Retain their actual source and normalization. Let \(A_Q,D,s\) be the \(Q\)-span, \(Y\)-span, and number of collected monomials of \(a_d\). For the general bound take \(B=D(s-1)\), \(k=B+1\), and \(n_0\ge d+A_Q+1\) as in [M]. Larger fixed jet orders are allowed. For the sharper bound suppose additionally that \[ a_d(Q,Y)=cQ^uY^v \prod_{t=1}^{p}(1-Q^{a_t}Y^{b_t})^{m_t}, \quad c
e0,\quad b_t
e0,\quad m_t\ge1, 	ag{2} \] with all exponents integral and fixed. Empty products are allowed. Put \[ M=\sum_t m_t,\qquad B_0=\sum_t m_t|b_t|. 	ag{3} \] In this case it suffices to use any fixed \(k\ge B_0+1\). Increase \(n_0\) so \(a_t+b_t(r-d)
e0\) whenever \(r\ge n_0\). There are only finitely many excluded integer trajectories. The original formal section and source are \[ Z(Q,X)=\sum_{r\ge n_0}C_r(Q)X^r,\qquad P^MZ=\mathcal B, \] \[ P^M=\sum_{j,\ell}a_{j,\ell}(Q)Q^{-\ell j}X^{-j}S^\ell, \qquad Sf(X)=f(QX). 	ag{4} \] The source \(\mathcal B\) is fixed by the actual \(d\)-color prefix. No quantum normal of that prefix is reset. Write \(Q_N=e^{2\pi i/N}\), \(Z_N=Z(Q_N,\cdot)\), and \[ p_{<,N}(X)=\sum_{r=1}^{n_0-1}C_r(Q_N)X^r. \] The exact original cyclotomic lattice and closing in [M] are \[ (1-X^N)(Z_N+p_{<,N})\in X\mathbb C[X],\quad\deg\le N, \qquad K_N=\operatorname{Res}_{X=\infty}Z_N\, rac{dX}{X}. 	ag{5} \] This retains the polynomial part at infinity as well as finite poles. ## 2. Scaled jets and the quantitative statement Use \(Q=Q_N(1+\zeta/N)\), and let \(R_h=\mathbb C[\zeta]/\zeta^h\). For \(v=\sum_{j<h}v_j\zeta^j\), set \(\|v\|_h=\sum_{j<h}|v_j|\). This norm is submultiplicative and decreases under truncation. These are actual quantum jets, with a specified change of scale. Let \(W_N\) be a rational section in \(X^{n_0}\mathbb C[[X]]\) satisfying the same pole/prefix lattice \[ (1-X^N)(W_N+p_{<,N})\in X\mathbb C[X],\qquad\deg\le N. 	ag{6} \] Suppose coefficients \(w_r(\zeta)\in R_k\), \(n_0\le r\le N\), lift its root coefficients and retain the actual \(d\)-color prefix through order \(k-1\). Set \(w_r=0\) for \(r<n_0\). Assume \[ \left\|[X^m]\left(P^M\sum_{r=n_0}^{N}w_rX^r-\mathcal Bight) ight\|_k\le\delta_N,\qquad n_0-d\le m\le N-d. 	ag{7} \] All coefficients and \(\mathcal B\) in (7) are evaluated at the displayed scaled \(Q\); its Fourier ordering remains (4). Let \(\mathcal E_N\) be the maximum of the two quantities \[ \max_{n_0\le r\le N}|[X^r](W_N-Z_N)|,\qquad \left|\operatorname{Res}_{\infty}W_N rac{dX}{X}-K_Night|. \] **Theorem.** Constants depending only on the fixed operator, prefix and jet order satisfy, for all sufficiently large \(N\), \[  oxed{\quad \mathcal E_N\le C_1e^{C_2N^2}\delta_N.\quad} 	ag{8a} \] Under (2) there is the sharper bound \[  oxed{\quad \mathcal E_N\le C_1N^Ae^{C_2N}\delta_N,\quad A=1+kMB_0.\quad} 	ag{8b} \] Exact defect zero recovers uniqueness. Sections 3--5 prove the refinement; Section 6 gives the general arithmetic bound. ## 3. The full-orbit denominator estimate Fix integers \(a,b\) with \(b
e0\), and put \(g=\gcd(|b|,N)\). As \(r\) runs through \(0,\ldots,N-1\), its phase coset occurs \(g\) times. Factoring \(z^{N/g}-1\) proves \[ \prod_{\substack{0\le r<N\Q_N^{a+br}
e1}} |1-Q_N^{a+br}|=  egin{cases} (N/g)^g,&g\mid a,\ |1-e^{2\pi ia/g}|^g,&g
mid a. \end{cases} 	ag{9} \] In the first case use the derivative at the omitted root one. Since \(g\) belongs to the finite divisor set of \(|b|\), (9) is at least a constant \(c_{a,b}>0\), independent of \(N\). Every factor is at most two. Hence every subset of the nonzero orbit factors, including any consecutive propagation segment, obeys \[ \prod_{r\in I}|1-Q_N^{a+br}|\ge c_{a,b}2^{-N}. 	ag{10} \] The same lower bound holds for products of their minima with one: apply (10) to just the factors below one. For \(h_r(\zeta)=a_d(Q,Q^{r-d})\), each vanishing binomial has order one. Its integer exponent \(E=a_t+b_t(r-d)\) is nonzero by the choice of \(n_0\). The total order lost through \(r=N\) is \[ \sum_{r=n_0}^{N}\mu_r\le B_0,\qquad \mu_r=\operatorname{ord}_{\zeta=0}h_r. 	ag{11} \] Indeed the congruence \(a_t+b_t(r-d)\equiv0\pmod N\) has at most \(\gcd(|b_t|,N)\le|b_t|\) solutions in a window of length at most \(N\). ## 4. Regular and singular jet inverses Every coefficient \(a_j(Q,Q^m)\), \(n_0-d\le m\le N-d\), has uniformly bounded \(R_k\) norm. To see this termwise, its substituted monomials have exponent \(E=O(N)\), and \[ [\zeta^\ell](1+\zeta/N)^E= inom E\ell N^{-\ell} 	ag{12} \] is uniformly bounded for every fixed \(\ell<k\), also for negative integer \(E\). Fixed Laurent coefficients and their finite sums therefore have one common bound. If \(\mu_r=0\), the finite geometric inverse in \(R_k\) gives \[ \|h_r^{-1}\|_k\le C\max(1,|h_r(0)|^{-k}). 	ag{13} \] Its proof writes \(h_r=h_r(0)+v\), \(v\in\zeta R_k\), and sums \(h_r(0)^{-1}\sum_{\ell=0}^{k-1}(-v/h_r(0))^\ell\). The uniform coefficient bound proves (13). By (2), (10), and the unit moduli of the monomials, the product of the right sides of (13) over all regular steps is at most \(e^{CN}\). This uses the complete orbit product, not a worst pivot bound per step. At a singular step factor \(h_r=\zeta^{\mu_r}u_r\). A vanishing factor has first scaled coefficient \(-E/N\); because \(E\) is a nonzero multiple of \(N\), its modulus is at least one. Every nonvanishing root factor has modulus at least \(2\sin(\pi/N)\ge4/N\). Thus \[ |u_r(0)|\ge c'N^{-M},\qquad \|u_r\|_{k-\mu_r}\le C,\qquad \|u_r^{-1}\|_{k-\mu_r}\le C N^{kM}. 	ag{14} \] The quotient coefficients are bounded by (12), shifted by the fixed vanishing order. Only \(B_0\) steps can be singular. ## 5. Propagation with exactly the available precision Subtract the actual truncated jets and write their errors as \(e_r\). The exact Fourier ordering in (4) cancels the shift offset, giving \[ \sum_{j=0}^{d}a_j(Q,Q^{r-d})e_{r-d+j}=ho_{r-d}, \qquad \|ho_{r-d}\|_k\le\delta_N. 	ag{15} \] All initial prefix errors vanish. Put \(M_r=\sum_{t=n_0}^{r}\mu_t\), \(h(r)=k-M_r\ge1\). At step \(r\), retain earlier errors only through precision \(k-M_{r-1}\). These coefficients are already known: earlier steps retained at least that precision. At a regular step use (13). At a singular step the right side, after subtracting earlier terms, is divisible by \(\zeta^{\mu_r}\) modulo the available precision, since it equals \(h_re_r\). Drop those first \(\mu_r\) zero coefficients and use (14). This determines and bounds \(e_r\) in \(R_{h(r)}\). No unavailable higher error jet is used or divided at zero. The coefficient bounds (12), fixed memory \(d\), and triangle inequality now give a discrete forced estimate: its amplification is bounded by the product of fixed regular-step constants, the regular inverse factors (13), and the singular factors (14). There are at most \(N\) forcing terms. By (10)--(14) this is \[ \max_{r\le N}\|e_r\|_{h(r)} \le C N^{1+kMB_0}e^{CN}\delta_N . 	ag{16} \] For precision, take at each step the maximum of all earlier retained error norms; it is bounded by \(L_r(E+\delta_N)\), where \(L_r\ge1\) is a fixed constant times the applicable inverse bound. Iterating gives \(N\delta_N\prod_r L_r\), proving (16). Finally \(H=(1-X^N)(W_N-Z_N)\) has degree at most \(N\). Its coefficients through degree \(N\) are exactly \(e_r(0)\), since both sections start in degree \(n_0>0\). At infinity its quotient has constant term \(-e_N(0)\). Thus its residue against \(dX/X\) is \(e_N(0)\), proving (8b). ## 6. The general arithmetic bound Drop (2), and use \(B=D(s-1)\), \(k\ge B+1\). Multiply the whole equation and its source by one fixed nonzero integer so all Laurent coefficients are algebraic integers in a fixed number field \(K\). Constants absorb this recorded rescaling. This is possible by clearing the finitely many algebraic denominators. Put \(h=[K:\mathbb Q]\). At a regular step the pivot \(\lambda=a_d(Q_N,Q_N^{r-d})
e0\) is an algebraic integer in \(K(Q_N)\), whose degree is at most \(h\varphi(N)\le hN\). All of its conjugates have modulus at most one fixed \(H\ge1\): an embedding sends roots of unity to roots of unity, and the finitely many coefficient conjugates have a fixed sum-of-moduli bound. The field norm of a nonzero algebraic integer is a nonzero integer. Its modulus is at least one. Bounding all factors except the specified embedding by \(H\) therefore proves \[ |\lambda|\ge H^{-hN}. 	ag{17} \] The integer-norm assertion can also be seen from the monic integral minimal polynomial: its nonzero constant term is the signed product of its conjugates. Passing to the larger field only raises that integer product to a positive integral power. The zero-step budget is the exact one in [M]. Because \(r-d>A_Q\), the trajectory polynomial \(a_d(Q,Q^{r-d})\) is nonzero identically. Its order \(\mu_r\) at \(Q_N\) is at most \(s-1\), by the logarithmic-derivative Vandermonde argument. For all large \(N\), \(a_d(Q_N,Y)\) is not identically zero. Its \(Y\)-span is \(D\) and the visited \(Q_N^{r-d}\) are distinct. Hence at most \(D\) indices vanish, and \(\sum_r\mu_r\le B\). At such an index write the first nonzero scaled coefficient as \[  eta_{\mu_r}=N^{-\mu_r} \sum_{a,b}c_{a,b}Q_N^{a+b(r-d)}  inom{a+b(r-d)}{\mu_r}. 	ag{18} \] The sum \(N^{\mu_r} eta_{\mu_r}\) is a nonzero algebraic integer. Each of its conjugates is bounded by \(CN^{\mu_r}\), since generalized binomial coefficients of integral exponents are integers and the exponents are \(O(N)\). The same norm argument yields \[ | eta_{\mu_r}|\ge N^{-\mu_r}(CN^{\mu_r})^{-hN} \ge \exp[-C'N\log(N+1)]. 	ag{19} \] The uniformly bounded scaled coefficients (12) and the inverse proof (13) now bound each regular inverse by \(e^{CN}\), and each singular unit inverse by \(e^{CN\log(N+1)}\). The precision argument (15) is unchanged, with \(B\) replacing \(B_0\). There are at most \(N\) regular steps and at most \(D\) singular steps. Their product and the \(N\) forcing terms are bounded by \(C_1e^{C_2N^2}\). The exact residue argument after (16) proves (8a). ## 7. Necessity of the refinement hypothesis and scope Factors independent of \(Y\) cannot be admitted silently. For the actual unknot colors \(C_r=1\), the all-level annihilator \[ P=[((1-Q)T-1)(T-1)]=hT^2-(1+h)T+1,\qquad h=1-Q, \] has jet budget one in [M]. Put \(h_N=1-Q_N\). Fix \(r_0\ge n_0+2\) and set \(e_r=0\) below \(r_0\), \(e_r=h_N^{N-r}\) through \(N\). Its only finite-window defects are \(\pm h_N^{N-r_0+1}\); its last coefficient is one. Adding \((\sum_{r=r_0}^Ne_rX^r)/(1-X^N)\) preserves the exact prefix and pole lattice but changes the residue by one. The defect is \(\exp(-N\log N+O(N))\). Thus (8b) is false for general factorizations allowing \(b=0\). This is a test of a nonminimal actual annihilator, not a knot counterexample. The general bound uses no binomial or classical-end hypothesis. It applies to the specified arithmetic actual recurrence and source of [M]. The finite-array elimination [F] does not prove (2) for every knot, and primitive/Weyl symmetry does not eliminate the classical end losses in [E]. No broad Conway factorization is asserted. A geometric comparison must still produce (6)--(7) with its actual source and sufficiently small defect. No such comparison is supplied. All three complete matching texts were read; only written proofs and text/hash operations were used.
