# Real-meridian transport and one form for every meridian jet Written research proof, 23 November 2026. The original complete-head Hermitian form extends to the actual root meridian family on positive real meridians. The full original mixed-color crossing, including its unrolled Cartan diagonal, preserves it. Holomorphic polarization then gives all meridian derivative identities at once. A finite packet of meridian jets has an explicit nondegenerate Hermitian form preserved by the truncated original word. The forms are indefinite. The result removes repeated meridian-jet adjoint calculations; it does not bound a marked closing below, reduce the physical dimension to a fixed number, or concern derivatives of the quantum parameter away from its root. ## 1. The actual root meridian family Fix \[ N\geq2,\quad d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2, \quad F_h=(Q;Q)_h . 	ag{1} \] The quantum parameter stays fixed throughout. On each original balanced head use the physical basis \(|aangle\), \(0\leq a\leq d\), and \[  egin{gathered} x=-q^{-1}M,\qquad \alpha(M)=d+ rac{N}{\pi i}\Log M,\qquad q^{\alpha(M)}=x,\ K_x|aangle=xQ^{-a}|aangle,\qquad \mathsf h_\alpha|aangle=(\alpha-2a)|aangle,\ f|aangle=(1-Q^{a+1})|a+1angle\quad(a<d),\qquad f|dangle=0,\ e_x|aangle=(x^{-1}-QxQ^{-a})|a-1angle\quad(a>0), \qquad e_x|0angle=0 . \end{gathered} 	ag{2} \] These are the original matrices of [A,E]; the zero endpoint in \(e_x\) is part of the module. It is not replaced by a cyclic arrow. The branch \(\Log M\) is real for \(M>0\), continued from that branch when a complex meridian germ is used. In particular \(\alpha(1)=d\). Define the same one-head physical form at every meridian: \[ Z|aangle=Q^a|aangle,\qquad R_d|aangle=|d-aangle, \qquad H_N=q^{-1}Z^{-1}R_d . 	ag{3} \] Thus \(H_N|aangle=qQ^a|d-aangle\), \(H_N^\dagger=H_N\), and \(H_N^2=I\). Write \(A^\sharp=H_NA^\dagger H_N\) on one head, and use the corresponding tensor form on several heads. For positive real \(M\), \( ar x=Qx\) and \( ar\alpha=2d-\alpha\). Direct substitution in (2) proves \[ K_x^\sharp=K_x,\qquad e_x^\sharp=e_x,\qquad f^\sharp=Q^{-1}f,\qquad \mathsf h_\alpha^\sharp=-\mathsf h_\alpha . 	ag{4} \] For example, on input \(a>0\), the coefficient of \(H_Ne_x^\dagger H_N\) is \(Q[Q^{-1}x^{-1}-xQ^{-a}]=x^{-1}-QxQ^{-a}\). On input \(a=0\), the actual top zero of \(e_x^\dagger\) gives zero. Similarly the coefficient for \(H_Nf^\dagger H_N\) is \(Q^{-1}(1-Q^{a+1})\), including its top zero. For \(\mathsf h_\alpha\), reflection of \(a\) gives \( ar\alpha-2(d-a)=-\alpha+2a\). These identities are compatible with the actual coproducts \[ \Delta e=e_1K_2+e_2,\qquad \Delta f=f_1+K_1^{-1}f_2,\qquad \Delta K=K_1K_2,\qquad \Delta\mathsf h=\mathsf h_1+\mathsf h_2 . 	ag{5} \] For instance \((\Delta e)^\sharp=\Delta e\) and \((\Delta f)^\sharp=Q^{-1}\Delta f\). Distinct tensor factors commute in these calculations. No positive real form is asserted: the nonzero nilpotent \(e_x\) is self-adjoint for an indefinite form. ## 2. Full original crossings, with their unrolled diagonal Use the actual finite preflip factorization of [A, Section 2], with the original unstripped universal Cartan normalization explicit in [C, (5)] and retained as in [E]: \[  egin{gathered} R_0(M_1,M_2)=D_{12}P_N(e_{x_1}f_2),\qquad D_{12}=q^{\mathsf h_{\alpha_1}\mathsf h_{\alpha_2}/2},\ D_{12}|a,bangle =\exp\!\left\{ rac{\pi i}{2N} (\alpha_1-2a)(\alpha_2-2b)ight\}|a,bangle,\ P_N(Y)=\sum_{h=0}^d  rac{(-1)^hQ^{h(h-1)/2}}{F_h}Y^h . \end{gathered} 	ag{6} \] Indeed \(e=qho^2E\), with \(ho=q-q^{-1}\), and \(F_h=(-1)^hq^{h(h+1)/2}ho^h[h]_q!\). Substitution converts the original universal coefficient in [C, (5)] exactly into that of \(P_N(e_{x_1}f_2)\); it introduces no additional scalar. Its checked version is \(\check R(M_1,M_2)=\mathsf P R_0(M_1,M_2)\), where \(\mathsf P\) is the literal flip from input colors \((M_1,M_2)\) to output colors \((M_2,M_1)\). In particular the highest entry \(\kappa=q^{\alpha_1\alpha_2/2}\) has not been removed. Away from completeness this separate scalar need not have modulus one. The nilpotent argument \(Y=e_{x_1}f_2\) satisfies \(Y^N=0\). From (4), \(Y^\sharp=Q^{-1}Y\). The elementary factorial conjugation and finite Euler inverse are \[ \overline{F_h}=(-1)^hQ^{-h(h+1)/2}F_h,\qquad P_N(Y)^{-1}=\sum_{h=0}^dY^h/F_h . 	ag{7} \] The inverse follows coefficientwise below degree \(N\) from the finite \(Q\)-binomial identity; larger powers vanish. Hence \[ P_N(Y)^\sharp=\sum_{h=0}^dY^h/F_h=P_N(Y)^{-1}. 	ag{8} \] No factor \(F_N\) occurs. For the original full Cartan factor, (4) gives \((\mathsf h_{\alpha_1}\mathsf h_{\alpha_2})^\sharp =\mathsf h_{\alpha_1}\mathsf h_{\alpha_2}\). Conjugating the coefficient \(\pi i/(2N)\) in (6) therefore proves \[ D_{12}^\sharp=D_{12}^{-1},\qquad R_0^\sharp=P_N(Y)^{-1}D_{12}^{-1}=R_0^{-1}. 	ag{9} \] This uses the full unrolled diagonal, not an absolute-value estimate on \(\kappa\). Since the flip is an isometry between the two identical tensor forms, the checked crossing satisfies \[  oxed{\quad \check R(M_1,M_2)^\dagger(H_N\otimes H_N) \check R(M_1,M_2)=H_N\otimes H_N \quad(M_1,M_2>0).\quad} 	ag{10} \] Its genuinely typed negative crossing is the corresponding inverse. When a negative crossing starts with unequal colors \((M_1,M_2)\), that inverse is taken from the positive map with input colors \((M_2,M_1)\). No exchange of these source and target orders is implicit. For a signed colored word \(\mathcal W_\omega( oldsymbol M)\) of width \(b\), label meridians on the initial strands and carry them through its actual crossing permutation. Put \(\mathscr H_b=H_N^{\otimes b}\). Successive applications of (10), including overlapping adjacent pairs, give \[ \mathcal W_\omega( oldsymbol M)^\dagger\mathscr H_b \mathcal W_\omega( oldsymbol M)=\mathscr H_b, \qquad  oldsymbol M\in(0,\infty)^b . 	ag{11} \] Every original crossing scalar is included. The number of crossings, their signs and both level parities cause no exception. ## 3. Polarization and all derivative Wronskians Choose a positive real meridian tuple \( oldsymbol M^0\), and use the logarithmic coordinates \(M_i=M_i^0e^{t_i}\) on a small conjugation-invariant polydisc. Let \(W(t)=\mathcal W_\omega( oldsymbol M^0e^t)\). It is the actual holomorphic matrix germ with its original unrolled branches. Define the holomorphic reflected transpose \[ W^
atural(t)=\overline{W( ar t)}^{\mathsf T}. 	ag{12} \] Equation (11) holds on its real slice. The identity theorem, applied one coordinate at a time to that real open box, therefore yields \[  oxed{\qquad W^
atural(t)\mathscr H_bW(t)=\mathscr H_b. \qquad} 	ag{13} \] This is an identity of full meridian germs. Reflection conjugates the continued logarithmic branches; unrelated windings are not identified. For a multi-index \(\alpha\), put \(D_i=M_i\partial_{M_i}\) and \(D^\alpha=\prod_iD_i^{\alpha_i}\). Differentiating (13) at the positive real tuple gives every mixed meridian derivative identity in one formula: \[  oxed{\quad \sum_{ eta\leq\alpha} inom{\alpha}{ eta} (D^ eta\mathcal W_\omega( oldsymbol M^0))^\dagger \mathscr H_b D^{\alpha- eta}\mathcal W_\omega( oldsymbol M^0) = egin{cases}\mathscr H_b,&\alpha=0,\0,&\alpha
e0. \end{cases}\quad} 	ag{14} \] Equivalently one may replace every \(D^\gamma\mathcal W_\omega( oldsymbol M^0)\) by \(\partial_t^\gamma W(0)\). The first-order identity is the usual vanishing of \(W^\dagger\mathscr H_bD_iW+(D_iW)^\dagger\mathscr H_bW\). Higher identities retain all mixed derivative cross terms. They are exact at every finite order, not asymptotic estimates. The same germ identity also retains actual two-fiber transports. Where the specified continued logarithmic lifts are defined, put \(T_\delta(t)=W(t+\delta)W(t)^{-1}\). Substituting (13) at the two arguments, in the displayed order, gives \[ T_{ ar\delta}( ar t)^\dagger\mathscr H_bT_\delta(t) =\mathscr H_b . 	ag{14a} \] For a meridian shift \(M\mapsto q^jM\), \(\delta=j\pi i/N\), so the paired shift is \(-\delta\). This is the original uncontracted transport of [E, (9a)], with its logarithmic lifts retained. It does not say that one such imaginary-shift matrix is an isometry by itself, or identify a closed quantum-A companion with this full matrix. ## 4. An explicit nondegenerate form on finite meridian jets Fix nonnegative truncation orders \(r_1,\ldots,r_b\) and set \[ A_{ oldsymbol r}=\mathbb C[t_1,\ldots,t_b]/ (t_1^{r_1+1},\ldots,t_b^{r_b+1}). 	ag{15} \] Its involution conjugates coefficients and fixes the formal variables. For physical jet packets \(u,v\in A_{ oldsymbol r}\otimes\mathbb C^{N^b}\), define \[ [u,v]_{ oldsymbol r} =[t_1^{r_1}\cdots t_b^{r_b}] u(t)^*\mathscr H_bv(t). 	ag{16} \] Here the star on a formal vector means coefficientwise conjugate transpose with the same formal variables, not substitution of \( ar t\). The matrix of (16) is explicitly \[ J_{r_1}^{m jet}\otimes\cdots\otimes J_{r_b}^{m jet} \otimes\mathscr H_b, \qquad (J_r^{m jet})_{ij}=\delta_{i+j,r},\quad0\leq i,j\leq r. 	ag{17} \] Thus it is Hermitian and nondegenerate. Every chosen derivative coefficient and every physical head coordinate remains present; no additional radical quotient is taken. Its matrix squares to the identity, so all its singular values are one. This is a statement about this indefinite coefficient pairing, not a positive norm estimate or a condition-number bound for a word. Let \(W_{ oldsymbol r}\) be multiplication by the Taylor polynomial of \(W(t)\) in this jet algebra. Equation (13) implies its exact truncated coefficient identity, and hence \[ [W_{ oldsymbol r}u,W_{ oldsymbol r}v]_{ oldsymbol r} =[u,v]_{ oldsymbol r}. 	ag{18} \] Indeed substitute \(W(t)u(t),W(t)v(t)\) into (16), use (13), and extract the top coefficient. Terms killed by (15) cannot affect it. The jet map is invertible since its constant coefficient is invertible. For one parameter and first jets its matrix is \(\left( egin{smallmatrix}W_0&0\W_1&W_0\end{smallmatrix}ight)\), and its form is \(\left( egin{smallmatrix}0&\mathscr H_b\\mathscr H_b&0\end{smallmatrix}ight)\). Thus (18) simultaneously contains the zeroth- and first-order identities. ## 5. Original boundary observations and scope The adjoint used here is not an unrecorded change of Hopf dual or of head order. The original antipodes remain \(\mathscr S(K)=K^{-1}\), \(\mathscr S(e)=-eK^{-1}\), \(\mathscr S(f)=-Kf\), with their original left/right placements. For example, a genuine linear dual reverses the weights and has \[ \alpha^\vee=2d-\alpha,\qquad x^\vee=Q^{-1}x^{-1},\qquad M^\vee=M^{-1}. 	ag{19} \] This follows from the reversed spectrum of \(-\mathsf h_\alpha\). It is different from the anti-linear reflection used in (12). No linear dual color is silently replaced by the same meridian. For any prescribed original meridian-dependent source \(p(t)\) and row \(\Lambda(t)\), its scalar and all its retained jets are still the coefficients of \(\Lambda(t)W(t)p(t)\). The original marked cap, ordinary turns, pivots, modified dimension and framing/peripheral lines are kept in these boundary data. Equations (13)--(18) do not replace \(\Lambda\) by the adjoint of \(p\). At the complete point the ordinary cup is isotropic for the tensor form, whereas the original marked cup/cap pairing is one; directly use [A, (18)] and \(\sum_{a=0}^dQ^a=0\) for the former. These are distinct observations. No original closing or pivot is declared to be a metric isometry. This gives one exact orthogonality calculation for all meridian jet orders and arbitrary signed overlapping words. It avoids constructing and checking a separate derivative pairing at each order. The jet dimension is still \(N^b\prod_i(r_i+1)\). Neither fixed jet order nor the fixed degree of an auxiliary variational formulation makes the physical boundary dimension independent of \(N\). There is no positive jet norm, general marked scalar lower bound, geometric principal-symbol nonvanishing theorem, or estimate for derivative order growing with \(N\) here. In particular the parameter \(q\) was never varied: moving-\(q\) normal jets are not meridian jets, and [E, Section 7] explicitly warns against identifying them. ## Complete proof sources - [A] [Actual shared quantum flags and their charged exchange](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_shared_quantum_flags_and_charged_exchange.md), 459 lines, SHA-256 `dcab795cc141e2e1db726998cf7b1141dd03c681eaae9076387f90581f53a7d9`. - [E] [Actual crossing Euler completion and weight source](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_crossing_euler_completion_and_weight_source.md), 350 lines, SHA-256 `e3a82ec13787d64a20694c0281337dfd3a5ea1f23ddad800073ed60a82477d89`. - [C] [Original full half-Cartan and head dilation](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_half_clock_source_dilation.md), 249 lines, SHA-256 `5f76e05c3130ef482d315681feaca8ecf98c4cc367623ffa72a19316a7706a3f`. The complete-color [physical tensor-form proof](research_physical_tensor_krein_crossing_form.md), 286 lines, SHA-256 `610b5ac7d889429163ec230e9d644d174d38382733dbad57826fce66cec8e348`, is coverage only. The proof here works directly with the actual generic-meridian matrices and full unrolled diagonal, without using its complete-only flag frame or dropping the original Cartan line.

title: Real filling powers and a uniform bound for the outer shared indices
text: # Real filling powers and a uniform bound for the outer shared indices Research proof, 4 November 2026. Frozen manuscripts are unchanged. The angle bound for a positive internal pair was previously proved only at integer powers. This matters when comparing two actions by differentiating with respect to a filling power. We first fill that gap for the geometric problem. We then use the actual physical normal-defect estimate to bound the outer shared indices in the finite quantum sum. The estimate holds for every fixed positive integer pair of powers at least three, through both level parities. The two outside endpoints remain complete throughout. Nothing here asserts a nonzero coefficient for the remaining middle integral. ## 1. The continuous geometric family Give two adjacent selected vertices real powers \(n,p\ge3\), unit charges, and one complete outside endpoint at each vertex. The [real-power variational theorem](research_radical_path_sector_gap.md#6-a-uniform-estimate-for-every-positive-pair-of-powers-at-least-three) gives the unique positive interior solution. Its angles depend smoothly on the powers: the minimum is interior and its constrained Hessian is positive definite. Write one angle as \(t=a-iH\). The selected branches have \(0<a<\pi\), \(H>0\), and the original period equation is \[ nt+2i\{r_0(t)+r_1(t,u)\}=2\pi, \quad r_0(t)=\operatorname{asinh}\tan(t/2),\quad r_1(t,u)=\operatorname{asinh}\{\tan(t/2)\cos(u/2)\}. \tag{1} \] Each return has positive real part and imaginary part between \(-\pi/2\) and \(\pi/2\). The equation is logarithmic, with its branch fixed by the positive geometry. **Theorem 1.** For every real \(n,p\ge3\), both selected angles obey \[ 0<a<\pi/2,\qquad 0<H<107/100. \tag{2} \] We prove this by excluding a first angle with real part \(\pi/2\). The starting pair \((3,3)\) has the strict angle bound by the [integer-pair theorem](research_internal_pair_angle_bound.md). Join it to any prescribed real pair by a straight segment of powers. The positive solution exists along the whole segment. At a proposed first boundary point, both real angles are at most \(\pi/2\). Two elementary estimates supply a height bound at that boundary without assuming the angle theorem that we are proving. First, the cosine maximum principle holds for real powers. If an active vertex maximized \(C=|\cos(t/2)|\ge1\), every neighbor would have cosine modulus at most \(C\), including its complete neighbor. Every incident return would then satisfy \[ \Re r\le\operatorname{asinh}|\sin(t/2)| \le\operatorname{asinh}\{\sqrt2\sinh(H/2)\}<3H/4. \tag{3} \] Here \(C\ge1\) implies \(|\sin(t/2)|^2\le2\sinh^2(H/2)\). The last inequality follows from \(\sinh(3H/4)>(3/2)\sinh(H/2)>\sqrt2\sinh(H/2)\). The sum of at most two returns would be less than \(3H/2\), contrary to its required value \(nH/2\). Thus both active cosine moduli are strictly less than one. This argument uses no integrality. Second, as long as \(a\le\pi/2\), \(|\tan(t/2)|\le1\). The internal return has real part less than \(\operatorname{asinh}1\), and the complete return increases with \(a\) at fixed height. Its value at \(a=\pi/2\) is \[ k_0(H)=\operatorname{asinh}\sqrt{\operatorname{sech}H}. \] Consequently \[ 3H/2<k_0(H)+\operatorname{asinh}1. \tag{4} \] The right side decreases with \(H\). The exact Taylor comparisons in [Proposition 1 of the complete-edge note](research_internal_pair_complete_edge_gap.md#1-the-height-bound-uses-the-actual-two-incidences) give, at \(H=107/100\), \[ k_0(H)<18/25,\qquad \operatorname{asinh}1<441/500, \qquad 18/25+441/500<3H/2. \] Thus \(H<107/100<23/20\) at the proposed first boundary. ## 2. A first-quadrant barrier for continuous powers At \(a=\pi/2\), put \[ \begin{split} \omega(H)&=\arctan(\sinh H),& \beta(H)&=\arctan\{\sqrt2\sinh(H/2)\},\\ k_q(H)&=qH/2-k_0(H),& g_q(H)&=q\pi/4-\pi+\beta(H),& C_q(H)&=e^{i\omega}\sinh(k_q+ig_q). \end{split} \tag{5} \] The comparison power \(q\) is real. At the actual boundary \(q=n\), the complete return is \(k_0-i\beta\), so the internal return is exactly \(k_n+ig_n\). The other vertex still has real angle at most \(\pi/2\). Consequently \[ C_n=\cos(u/2)\ \hbox{lies in the first quadrant},\qquad \Re C_n^2\ge1/2. \tag{6} \] Here and below, \(\Re C^2\) means the real part of the complex square, not the square of its real part. The exact identity is \[ \Re C_q^2=\frac12\left[ \cos(2\omega)\{\cosh(2k_q)\cos(2g_q)-1\} -\sin(2\omega)\sinh(2k_q)\sin(2g_q)\right]. \tag{7} \] The coefficients of the two trigonometric terms differ. In particular, they cannot be combined into \(\cosh(2k_q)\cos(2g_q+2\omega)\). **Lemma 2.** Fix \(0<H<23/20\). Along any first-quadrant part of the curve \(q\mapsto C_q(H)\) with \(k_q>0\) and \(-\pi/2<g_q<\pi/2\), an intersection with \(\Re C_q^2=1/2\) has strictly negative derivative: \[ \left.\frac{d}{dq}\Re C_q^2\right|_{\Re C_q^2=1/2}<0. \tag{8} \] *Proof.* Write \(k=k_q\), \(g=g_q\), and \(E=e^{i\omega}\cosh(k+ig)\). In the first quadrant, \(k>0\), \(-\pi/2<g<\pi/2\), and \[ E=\tanh k\,C+\frac{e^{i\omega}\cos g}{\cosh k} \quad\hbox{also lies in the first quadrant},\qquad E^2=C^2+e^{2i\omega}. \tag{9} \] Direct differentiation gives \[ \frac{d}{dq}\Re C^2 =\Re\{(H+i\pi/2)CE\}. \tag{10} \] At \(\Re C^2=1/2\), write \(C^2=1/2+iY\), \(Y>0\). If \(1/2+\cos(2\omega)\le0\), then \(\arg E\ge\pi/4\). Since \(H<\pi/2\), (10) is strictly negative. Otherwise the real part of \(E^2\) is positive, and \[ \arg(CE)\ge\frac12\arg\{1/2+e^{2i\omega}\} >\arctan(2H/\pi). \] For the last strict inequality it is enough, after substituting \(\tan\omega=\sinh H\), to prove \[ \sinh H\,(\pi^2-4H^2)>H\pi(3-\sinh^2H). \tag{11} \] The factor \(\pi^2-4H^2\) is positive. The elementary lower bounds \(\sinh H/H>1+H^2/6\) and \(\sinh^2H>H^2+H^4/3\) show that the left side of (11), divided by \(H\), minus its right side divided by \(H\), is greater than \[ \pi(\pi-3)+(\pi^2/6+\pi-4)H^2 +(\pi-2)H^4/3>0. \] All three coefficients are positive because \(\pi>3\). This proves (11), hence (8). The argument also applies to the positive real boundary of the quadrant, where \(Y=0\). \(\square\) There is at most one relevant first-quadrant interval in \(q\). Indeed, for \(k\ge0\) and \(-\pi/2<g<\pi/2\), membership is equivalent to \[ -\arctan(\sinh H\tanh k)<g <\arctan(\tanh k/\sinh H). \tag{12} \] Along increasing \(q\), the lower boundary decreases while \(g\) increases at rate \(\pi/4\). The upper boundary increases at rate at most \(H/(2\sinh H)<1/2<\pi/4\). Thus the curve cannot leave this quadrant and subsequently return before the actual point in (6). The range of \(g\) between any of the starting points below and the actual point is contained in \((-\pi/2,\pi/2)\). It remains to prove that this interval starts with \(\Re C^2<1/2\). Put \[ H_c=\frac23\operatorname{asinh}\sqrt2<\frac45. \tag{13} \] The [exact power-three calculation](research_internal_pair_angle_bound.md#3-a-vertex-of-power-three-cannot-reach-the-boundary) gives \[ \begin{split} C_3(H)&=2\sinh H-\frac{\cosh(3H/2)}{\sqrt2} +i\left\{\frac{\sinh(3H/2)}{\sqrt2}-1\right\},\\ \frac12-\Re C_3(H)^2 &=4X^5-4X^4+8X^3-8X^2+X+1>0,\qquad X=\sqrt2\sinh(H/2)<1. \end{split} \tag{14} \] The polynomial identity is unchanged by the correction in (7); its two rational Bernstein tables prove positivity on \([0,1]\). For \(H\ge H_c\), one has \(k_3>0\), \(-\pi/4<g_3<0\), and \(\Im C_3\ge0\). Its real part is positive directly from \(C_3=e^{i\omega}\sinh(k_3+ig_3)\). Thus the curve starts, at \(q=3\), in the first quadrant or on its positive real boundary, with \(\Re C_3^2<1/2\). Lemma 2 and (12) prohibit a later upward crossing to (6). For \(H<H_c\), consider the entry on the positive real axis. Its nonnegative return \(k=k_{\rm ent}(H)\), when it exists, satisfies \[ k=2H-\frac{2H}{\pi} \{\beta(H)+\arctan(\sinh H\tanh k)\}-k_0(H). \tag{15} \] The right side strictly decreases with \(k\). If it is negative at \(k=0\), then at the first feasible value \(k_q=0\) one has \(g_q>0\); the upper inequality in (12) already fails and continues to fail. Such an \(H\) has no actual point (6). Otherwise there is one nonnegative entry root. This root increases with \(H\) while \(H\le H_c\). Here are explicit bounds for the differentiation, to keep this assertion independent of a numerical graph. For \(H\le4/5\), \[ \begin{gathered} \cosh H<7/5,\quad k_0(H)>3/4,\quad k_{\rm ent}<17/20,\quad \beta'(H)<3/4,\\ \beta(H)+\omega(H)<\pi/2,\qquad \pi>25/8. \end{gathered} \tag{16} \] The bound for \(k_0\) follows from \((7/5)(24/29)^2<1\) and \(\sinh(3/4)\le24/29\). The bound for the entry follows immediately from (15). Also \(\beta'=\cosh(H/2)/(\sqrt2\cosh H)<3/4\). For the angle sum use \[ \sinh H\,\sqrt2\sinh(H/2) <(60/67)(3/2)(30/73)<1, \] where the two hyperbolic-sine bounds are geometric majorants of their positive Taylor series. At a fixed \(k\le17/20\), the partial derivative in \(H\) of the right side of (15) is therefore greater than \[ 1-\frac{64}{125}\left\{\frac34+\frac75\frac{17}{20}\right\} =\frac{21}{3125}>0. \tag{17} \] In deriving this bound the term \(-k_0'(H)\) is positive and may be dropped. The implicit derivative is positive since the right side of (15) decreases with \(k\). Its value at \(k=0\) also increases with \(H\), so the entry roots form one interval, ending at \(H_c\), rather than separate branches. At the positive real entry, \[ \Re C_{\rm ent}^2= \frac{\sinh^2 k_{\rm ent}\cosh^2 k_{\rm ent}} {\sinh^2 k_{\rm ent}+\operatorname{sech}^2H}. \tag{18} \] This expression increases with both \(k_{\rm ent}\) and \(H\). At \(H=H_c\) the entry is exactly \(C_3(H_c)\), whose square is less than \(1/2\) by (14). Hence every earlier nonnegative entry has square less than \(1/2\). Lemma 2 again prohibits an upward crossing to (6). Both height ranges exclude the proposed first angle boundary. The argument in (4) then supplies the height bound throughout the real-power family. This proves Theorem 1. ## 3. Comparing the pair action with the two half-charge actions Let \(\mathcal M(n,p)\) be the original stationary action's real part for this complete-ended pair. Let \(\mu(n)\) be the real half-charge action of the complete leaf, denoted \(M_n\) in the [observation theorem](research_complete_source_pick_observation.md#5-a-nonzero-half-charge-observation). Its angle is \(t_0=a_0-iH_0\), and \[ nt_0+2i\operatorname{asinh}\tan(t_0/2)=\pi, \qquad \mu(n)=\Re\{\Psi(t_0)+int_0^2/(4\pi)-it_0/2\}. \tag{19} \] Here \(\Psi(t)=\psi(t,0)\) has its original constant \(\Psi(0)=M_\infty=4G/\pi\), where \(G\) is Catalan's constant. The proof of the [pair-to-half-charge position comparison](research_pair_half_charge_action_gap.md) uses only the positive returns, \(n\ge3\), and the rectangle (2). Theorem 1 has now established those hypotheses for real powers. Thus at the vertex of power \(n\), \[ a>a_0>0,\qquad H>H_0>0. \tag{20} \] In particular this extension does not differentiate through an interval on which the original integer angle proof was unavailable. At a stationary point all derivatives in the geometric variables vanish. Differentiating the explicit filling term \(int^2/(4\pi)\) therefore gives \[ \partial_n\mathcal M(n,p)=\frac{aH}{2\pi},\qquad \mu'(n)=\frac{a_0H_0}{2\pi}. \tag{21} \] The same formula holds at the other vertex. These are derivatives of the calibrated stationary actions, with no additive constant changed as the powers vary. Consequently \[ \mathcal G(n,p):=\mathcal M(n,p)-\mu(n)-\mu(p) \quad\hbox{is strictly increasing in each real power}, \qquad \mathcal G(n,p)\ge\mathcal G(3,3). \tag{22} \] We need a rational lower bound for this difference. The previously certified geometric half-action gives \(\mathcal M(3,3)>63/25\); see [the triangular-normal comparison](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_pair_triangular_normal_region.md#3-the-two-first-normal-factors-are-below-the-geometric-rate). The half-charge action admits the following upper bound without a numerical integration. On its power-three charge path \(0\le\chi\le1/2\), one has \(a<\pi/3\), \(H<2/5\). Throughout that rectangle, \[ \frac{49}{50}<\Re\sec((a-iH)/2)<\frac76. \tag{23} \] For the lower bound use \(\Re\sec\ge\operatorname{sech}(H/2)\) and \(\cosh(1/5)\le305/299<50/49\). For the upper bound use \(\Re\sec\le\sec(a/2)\le2/\sqrt3<7/6\). Integrating \(r_0'(t)=\sec(t/2)/2\) along horizontal and vertical segments gives \[ k\ge49a/100,\qquad |g|\le7H/12. \] The two period equations \(k=3H/2\) and \(3a+2|g|=2\pi\chi\) imply \[ H\ge\frac{588\pi}{3043}\chi,\qquad \mu(3)=M_\infty-\int_0^{1/2}H(\chi)\,d\chi \le M_\infty-\frac{147\pi}{6086}<\frac{219}{200}. \tag{24} \] The last comparison uses the proved rational estimate \(M_\infty<7/6\), \(\pi>3\), and \(7/6-441/6086=9989/9129<219/200\). Combining (22) and (24) yields the uniform classical comparison \[ \boxed{\quad\mathcal G(n,p)>33/100 \qquad(n,p\ge3).\quad} \tag{25} \] ## 4. The original low coefficients and the discarded indices We now return to fixed integer powers \(n,p\ge3\). At level \(N\), put \(L=\lfloor(N-1)/2\rfloor\), and retain the literal low complete-end polynomial \(\mathcal L_N(w)=\sum_{j=0}^{L}e_j(w)e_j(-2)\). For odd levels this already equals the full complete-end kernel. Define the actual traced coefficients \[ W_{n,j,N}=\phi_N[R^n\mathcal L_Ne_j],\qquad 0\le j\le L. \tag{26} \] All first normals are included in \(\phi_N\). The [uniform physical-defect packet](research_physical_normal_defect_packet.md) gives \(|D_{n,N}(c_a)|\le CN^A e^{N\mu(n)}\) at every physical row, through both parities. Its rational leading coefficient has no singularity on the physical interval. Apply the exact normal-defect trace formula to (26). All its node weights have polynomial size in \(N\), and \[ 0\le e_j(c_a)\le e_j(-2)\quad(a\ge j),\qquad e_j(c_a)=0\quad(a<j). \] The uniform sine-factorial bound gives \[ e_j(-2)\le CN^A e^{NV_0(j/N)},\qquad V_0(x)=-2J(1/2-x)-2J(x),\quad J(x)=\int_0^x\log(2\sin\pi s)\,ds. \tag{27} \] Thus, uniformly over every retained low index, \[ |W_{n,j,N}|\le CN^A e^{N\{\mu(n)+V_0(j/N)\}}. \tag{28} \] At odd levels the top index \(j=L\) has no contour term. Its separate exact rank-one term has the half-charge packet proved in [the odd observation note](research_odd_half_charge_observation.md#3-the-original-odd-trace-still-has-its-top-degree-term). That packet also satisfies (28). No simple endpoint has been assigned a nonexistent first normal. The profile \(V_0\) is symmetric about \(1/4\), increases up to that point, and decreases afterwards. At \(\beta=12/25\), with \(\delta=1/2-\beta=1/50\), \[ \begin{split} V_0(\beta) &=-2\int_0^\delta\log\tan(\pi s)\,ds\\ &\le\frac1{25}\{1+\log(50/\pi)\}<\frac{31}{200}. \end{split} \tag{29} \] Here \(\tan(\pi s)\ge\pi s\). The last strict comparison uses \(\pi>3\) and \(e^{23/8}>50/3\); the latter already follows from the first seven positive exponential Taylor terms. The same bound holds when \(x\le1/50\) or \(x\ge12/25\). **Theorem 3.** For every fixed integer \(n,p\ge3\), define \[ \mathcal T_N=\{0\le j\le L:j/N\le1/50 \ \hbox{or}\ j/N\ge12/25\}. \] There are constants \(C,A\), depending on the fixed powers, such that at both parities \[ \boxed{\quad \sum_{j\in\mathcal T_N}|W_{n,j,N}W_{p,j,N}| \le CN^A e^{N\{\mathcal M(n,p)-1/50\}}. \quad} \tag{30} \] *Proof.* There are at most \(N\) terms. Equations (28)–(29) give the rate \(\mu(n)+\mu(p)+31/100\). By (25) this is strictly less than \(\mathcal M(n,p)-1/50\). Absorb the number of terms and all fixed finite levels in the polynomial factor. The argument bounds the sum of absolute values, so no unproved cancellation between the discarded indices is used. \(\square\) The theorem is a bound after taking the two original traces. It does not give the same bound for a bare internal kernel on a fixed complex-angle contour. In particular it does not remove the endpoint obstruction to a full bare-kernel packet. The previously proved radical-sector estimates also permit replacement of the three full edge kernels by their low parts in the complete-ended pair: that error has rate at most \(2M_\infty<7/3\), whereas \(\mathcal M(n,p)\ge\mathcal M(3,3)>63/25\). Together with (30), this reduces the full original pair to the retained range \[ 1/50<j/N<12/25 \tag{31} \] with an error below \(\mathcal M(n,p)-1/50\). The remaining joint cycle over this middle range still has to be controlled. The estimate neither replaces that cycle by a single bare edge saddle nor proves its global noncancellation. ## 5. Uniform geometry when both powers are at least seven The real period equation does not permit assuming that every imaginary return is negative. In particular the internal return at one vertex can have positive imaginary part when its neighbor has a different power. The following bootstrap allows that sign and gives bounds uniform over all real \(n,p\ge7\). **Theorem 4.** In the complete-ended unit-charge pair of Section 1, if \(n,p\ge7\), then both selected angles \(t_i=a_i-iH_i\) and the original internal wire \(x=\xi+iY\) satisfy \[ 0<a_i<\frac{19}{20},\qquad 0<H_i<\frac3{10},\qquad 0<2\pi Y<\frac14. \tag{32} \] *Proof.* The proved pair angle bound gives \(a_i<\pi/2\). The cosine maximum principle gives \(|\cos(t_i/2)|<1\); its proof uses only positive real returns, degree two, and real powers at least three, so it applies to the real-power family here. Consequently \(|\tan(t_i/2)|<1\), and each of the two original return arguments at a vertex has modulus less than one. From their imaginary period equation, \[ \frac{nH}{2}=\Re r_0+\Re r_1<2\operatorname{asinh}1, \qquad H<\frac{4\operatorname{asinh}1}{7}<\frac{18}{35}. \tag{33} \] The last inequality uses \(\operatorname{asinh}1<9/10\), which follows from the first three positive terms of \(\sinh(9/10)\). Write \(C=\cos(u/2)\) for the neighbor cosine. Its real part is positive, and \[ 0<\Im C<\frac57\sinh(9/35)<\frac15. \] Here \(\sin(a_u/2)<1/\sqrt2<5/7\). Also \(\Im\tan(t/2)<0\) and \(\Re\tan(t/2)\le\tan(a/2)\). Thus \(\Im\{\tan(t/2)C\}\le\tan(a/2)/5<1/5\). If \(r_1=k_1+ig_1\) has \(g_1>0\), then \(\sin g_1=\Im(\tan(t/2)C)/\cosh k_1\). For \(0\le z\le1/5\), \(\arcsin z\le z/\sqrt{1-z^2}<(25/24)z\). It follows, also when \(g_1\le0\), that \(g_1\le(5/24)\tan(a/2)\). The complete return has \(g_0<0\). The real period therefore gives \[ \begin{split} na&=2\pi+2g_0+2g_1 <2\pi+\frac5{12}\tan(a/2) \le2\pi+\frac5{6\pi}a <2\pi+\frac4{15}a,\\ a&<\frac{2\pi}{n-4/15} \le\frac{30\pi}{101}<\frac{660}{707}<\frac{19}{20}, \qquad \cos a>\frac{29}{50}. \end{split} \tag{34} \] The chord bound for the convex function \(\tan\) on \([0,\pi/4]\) proves \(\tan(a/2)\le2a/\pi\). We used \(25/8<\pi<22/7\); the alternating cosine series through degree six at \(19/20\) proves the last lower bound. Two short height improvements now suffice. Since \(\cosh(18/35)<8/7\), equations (33)–(34) give \[ |\tan(t/2)|^2 =\frac{\cosh H-\cos a}{\cosh H+\cos a} <\frac{8/7-29/50}{8/7+29/50} =\frac{197}{603}<\sinh^2(14/25). \tag{35} \] Both real returns are at most \(\operatorname{asinh}|\tan(t/2)|\), because the neighbor cosine has modulus less than one. Hence \(H<(4/7)(14/25)=8/25\). The estimate \(\cosh(8/25)<53/50\) then gives \[ |\tan(t/2)|^2 <\frac{53/50-29/50}{53/50+29/50} =\frac{12}{41}<\sinh^2(21/40), \qquad H<\frac47\frac{21}{40}=\frac3{10}. \tag{36} \] The two sinh comparisons already follow from \(\sinh z>z+z^3/6\). The cosh bounds follow from \(\cosh z\le1+z^2/[2(1-z^2/12)]\). For the wire, put \(A=\cos^2(t_n/2)\) and \(B=\cos^2(t_p/2)\). The preceding estimates imply \[ \begin{split} |A-1|, |B-1| &<r:=\left(\frac{19}{40}\right)^2 +\left(\frac{3/20}{1-(3/20)^2/6}\right)^2\\ &=\frac{252350449}{1016334400}<\frac14. \end{split} \tag{37} \] Indeed \(|1-A|=|\sin(t_n/2)|^2 =\sin^2(a_n/2)+\sinh^2(H_n/2)\), and similarly for \(B\). The positive sinh series is bounded by \(z/(1-z^2/6)\). The disk \(D(1,r)\) is closed under the harmonic mean. To see this, inversion maps it to the convex disk with center \(1/(1-r^2)\) and radius \(r/(1-r^2)\). Averaging two points in that disk and inverting again returns to \(D(1,r)\). Thus the original wire parameter obeys \[ k=\frac{AB}{A+B}\in D(1/2,r/2),\qquad \cosh(2\pi Y)=|k|+|1-k|\le\sqrt{1+r^2}, \qquad 2\pi Y\le\operatorname{asinh}r<\frac14. \tag{38} \] The focal-distance bound follows by Cauchy–Schwarz: \(|k|^2+|1-k|^2=1/2+2|k-1/2|^2\le(1+r^2)/2\). The selected wire branch has \(Y>0\), as proved by its original geometric continuation. This proves (32). \(\square\) **Corollary.** The selected internal wire also satisfies \(1/5<\xi<1/4\). *Proof.* The disk in (38) gives \(\Re k>3/8\). The original wire order supplies \(0<\xi<1/4\), and therefore \[ 0<\cos(2\pi\xi)\cosh(2\pi Y)=1-2\Re k<\frac14. \] It follows that \(\cos(2\pi\xi)<1/4<\cos(2\pi/5)=(\sqrt5-1)/4\). Strict decrease of the cosine on this interval proves the lower bound. \(\square\) The thresholds in the mixed-phase concavity theorem consequently have a common fixed margin. For \(\alpha(s)=\arccos(\operatorname{sech}(2\pi s))/(2\pi)\), the identity \(\arccos(\operatorname{sech}z)=\arctan(\sinh z)\) and its derivative \(\operatorname{sech}z<1\) give \[ \alpha(Y)<\frac1{8\pi}<\frac1{25},\qquad \alpha(H_i/(2\pi))<\frac3{20\pi}<\frac1{20} <\frac3{50}. \tag{39} \] These are geometric domain bounds. They do not, by themselves, estimate the contour connectors or prove a nonzero coefficient in the finite source. ## 6. An original-action lower bound for powers at least seven The action monotonicity also turns one rigorously enclosed positive point into a uniform bound on a whole power quadrant. The calibration here uses the original unexponentiated periods and all three edges. It supplies a geometric comparison constant, not a new quantum coefficient. **Theorem 5.** For every real \(n,p\ge7\), \[ \mathcal M(n,p)>\frac{163}{50}. \tag{40} \] *Proof.* At \(n=p=7\) the original equations are \[ \begin{split} 7t+2i\{\operatorname{asinh}\tan(t/2) +\operatorname{asinh}(\tan(t/2)\cos(u/2))\}&=2\pi,\\ 7u+2i\{\operatorname{asinh}\tan(u/2) +\operatorname{asinh}(\tan(u/2)\cos(t/2))\}&=2\pi. \end{split} \tag{41} \] The [focused outward certificate](../experiments/certify_pair_seven_action.py) first finds an approximate symmetric solution, then proves the existence of a solution to (41) by a rectangular interval contraction in both complex variables. The recorded box has radius \(2^{-100}\) in each real coordinate. A fixed inverse of its central Jacobian gives a self-map strictly inside the box, with complex maximum-norm derivative bound less than \(8\cdot10^{-31}\). This is an existence proof for the original logarithmic equations; the numerical candidate is not used as an exact root. The symmetric box and uniqueness also imply \(t=u\). Every return argument lies in the right half-plane throughout the box. On each of the original edges \((t,0),(t,u),(u,0)\), the checker certifies the positive-domain inequality \(\Re q>\sqrt{(\Re a)^2+(\Re b)^2}\), with margin greater than \(1/2\), where \(a=\tan(t_{\rm left}/2)\), \(b=\tan(t_{\rm right}/2)\), and \(q=\sqrt{1+a^2+b^2}\). It also checks that the four distinct original shape expressions have positive imaginary parts and that \(\cosh r=q\cos(t_{\rm neighbor}/2)\) has the selected positive real-part sign. Thus this root belongs to the original positive variational domain and is the selected pair solution. Positivity of the returns alone is not substituted for positivity of the original edges. For the action put \[ \begin{split} A&=\cos^2(t/2),\qquad B=\cos^2(u/2),\qquad x=\pi^{-1}\arctan\sqrt{\frac{AB}{A+B-AB}},\\ J(z)&=\frac{\operatorname{Li}_2(1) -\operatorname{Li}_2(e^{2\pi iz})}{2\pi i} +\frac{i\pi}{2}z(1-z),\\ b(x,t)&=-J(1/2-x+t/(2\pi))-J(1/2-x-t/(2\pi))-2J(x),\\ \Psi(t)&=-4J(1/4+t/(4\pi))-4J(1/4-t/(4\pi)),\\ \mathcal S_{77} &=b(x,t)+b(x,u)+\Psi(t)+\Psi(u) +\frac{7i(t^2+u^2)}{4\pi}-i(t+u). \end{split} \tag{42} \] The square root is in the first quadrant and the arctangent is its selected continuation, giving \(1/5<\Re x<1/4\) and \(\Im x>0\). Every argument of \(J\) stays in \(0<\Re z<1\), where its displayed formula is holomorphic: the exponential avoids the principal dilogarithm cut \([1,\infty)\). Differentiating gives \(J'(z)=\Log(2\sin\pi z)\) on the original strip, and its limit at zero is zero. This fixes the constant and branch of the [original mixed phase](research_mixed_wire_phase_concavity.md). In particular \(\Psi(0)=M_\infty\); no additive real constant is chosen at the certified point. Outward complex-ball evaluation on the entire root box proves \[ 3.2624704255<\Re\mathcal S_{77}<3.2624704256 . \tag{43} \] The checker additionally encloses the original wire and angular gradient lifts and verifies their agreement with the selected return branches. The root, branch inequalities, action enclosure, and source hashes are in the [saved certificate](../repro/results/research-pair-seven-action.json). Thus \(\mathcal M(7,7)>163/50\). Finally the already proved derivatives \(\partial_n\mathcal M=aH/(2\pi)>0\) and \(\partial_p\mathcal M=a'H'/(2\pi)>0\) on the real positive pair family extend the bound to every \(n,p\ge7\), proving (40). \(\square\) Run the checker with: ~~~sh python3 experiments/certify_pair_seven_action.py ~~~ It uses rigorous Arb balls for every successful comparison, including the dilogarithms. The contour contraction and the positive-domain identification above are the proof of the root's status; no scan of numerical solutions or inferred quantum asymptotic is used. ## 7. A global comparison for real trace angles The preceding action bound is useful only when the other portions of the finite sum can be compared with it. We now make that comparison when at least one real trace angle is beyond its factorial wall. The wire may already have its full geometric imaginary part. The final conclusion is an upper bound on these portions of the source, not a proof that they join to a complete admissible contour. First, the same geometry gives a sharper wire-height estimate: \[ L:=2\pi Y<\frac2{15} \qquad(n,p\ge7). \tag{44} \] Here is a rational proof. Equation (34) gives \(a<660/707<15/16\). The alternating sine and cosine series give \(\sin a<81/100\) and \(\cos a>59/100\). For \(A=\cos^2(t_n/2)\), and likewise for \(B=\cos^2(t_p/2)\), the already proved \(H_i<3/10\) and \(|\cos(t_i/2)|<1\) imply \[ \ell:=\frac{159}{200}<\Re A,\Re B<1,\qquad 0<\Im A,\Im B<b_0:=\frac{243}{1970}. \tag{45} \] Indeed \(\Re A=(1+\cos a\cosh H)/2\), while \(\Im A=\sin a\sinh H/2\) and \(\sinh(3/10)<60/197\). For \(k=AB/(A+B)\), direct multiplication gives \[ \begin{split} \Im k &=\frac{\Im B\,|A|^2+\Im A\,|B|^2}{|A+B|^2}\\ &<b_0\left\{\frac12+ \frac{(1-\ell)^2+b_0^2}{8\ell^2}\right\}. \end{split} \tag{46} \] We used \(|A|^2+|B|^2=(|A+B|^2+|A-B|^2)/2\), \(|A-B|^2<(1-\ell)^2+b_0^2\), and \(|A+B|^2>4\ell^2\). The original identity \(k=\sin^2(\pi x_*)\) and \(1/5<\Re x_*<1/4\) give \[ \sinh L =\frac{2\Im k}{\sin(2\pi\Re x_*)} <\frac{108361228815}{816082404766}<\frac2{15}. \tag{47} \] For the denominator use \(\sin(2\pi/5)>19/20\), which follows from \(\sin^2(2\pi/5)=(5+\sqrt5)/8\) and \(\sqrt5>111/50\). Since \(L<\sinh L\), this proves (44). Let \(V_\tau(\xi)=\mathfrak b(\xi,\tau)\) be the real Newton profile, with the continuous factorial upper exponent \(\mathfrak b\) defined in [the uniform factorial bound](research_uniform_factorial_and_boundary_decay.md#3-the-exact-newton-interpolation). For real \(\tau\), its change with wire height satisfies \[ 0\le \mathfrak b(\xi+iy,\tau)-V_\tau(\xi) \le\pi|y|,\qquad 0<\xi<1/2,\quad |\tau|\le\pi. \tag{48} \] To prove this, first suppose \(y>0\) and \(|\tau|<\pi\). Put \(z=\pi(\xi+iy)\). Differentiation in \(x\) uses the individual continued logarithms \[ b_x=\Log\cos(z+\tau/2)+\Log\cos(z-\tau/2)-2\Log\sin z. \tag{49} \] Their exponential is \(\cos^2(\tau/2)\csc^2z-1\), which lies strictly in the lower half-plane: \(\Im(\sin^2z)>0\). At \(\tau=0\), the imaginary part of (49) is \(2\arg\cot z\in(-\pi,0)\). Varying the real angle keeps its exponential in that same half-plane, so the continued logarithm has imaginary part in \((-\pi,0)\) throughout. Therefore \(0<\partial_y\mathfrak b<\pi\). Integration from zero proves (48) for positive \(y\). Conjugation gives negative \(y\), and continuity includes the factorial wall and the angular endpoints. This proof fixes the logarithmic lift before using the quotient; it does not reset the branch at a reflected factorial argument. For \(0<\xi<1/2\), define \[ \begin{split} C(\xi)&=J(2\xi)-2J(\xi)+\Psi(\pi-2\pi\xi),\\ B(\xi)&=C(\xi)+V_0(\xi)+M_\infty. \end{split} \tag{50} \] If \(|\tau|\ge\pi-2\pi\xi\) and \(|\rho|\le\pi\), the real-angle monotonicity of \(V_\tau\) and \(\Psi\) gives \[ V_\tau(\xi)+\Psi(\tau)+V_\rho(\xi)+\Psi(\rho) \le B(\xi). \tag{51} \] The derivative of \(V_\tau\) is an integrable logarithm at its wall; its sign remains negative on both sides. Thus this comparison applies on the whole interval \(0<\xi<1/2\). **Theorem 6.** The maximum in (51) has the bound \[ B(\xi)\le B(1/3) =M_\infty-18J(1/3) <\frac{57641}{18500}<\frac{25}{8}. \tag{52} \] Consequently, for every fixed integer pair \(n,p\ge7\), the complete upper phase with real trace angles and \(|y|\le Y\) satisfies \[ \mathcal E_{n,p}(\xi+iy,\tau,\rho) <\frac{391}{120} <\mathcal M(n,p)-\frac1{600} \tag{53} \] whenever at least one of the two angles is beyond its wall. Here \(\mathcal E_{n,p}\) includes the original wire penalty from equation (22) of [the contour reduction](research_internal_pair_combined_contour_reduction.md#4-one-explicit-function-bounds-all-sixteen-pieces). *Proof.* Differentiating (50), with \(\Psi(\pi-2\pi\xi)=-4J((1-\xi)/2)-4J(\xi/2)\), gives \[ B'(\xi)=2\log\frac{2\cos^2(\pi\xi)}{1-\cos(\pi\xi)}. \tag{54} \] This derivative decreases strictly and vanishes only at \(\xi=1/3\). Reflection and duplication of \(J\) give \(J(2/3)=-J(1/3)\) and \(3J(1/3)=2J(1/6)\); substitution in (50) yields the equality in (52). For its rational bound, the absolutely convergent sine series gives \[ -J(1/3)=\frac{\sqrt3}{4\pi} \sum_{j\ge0}\left\{\frac1{(3j+1)^2}-\frac1{(3j+2)^2}\right\}. \tag{55} \] The summand decreases with \(j\). The terms starting at \(j=3\) therefore sum to at most \(21/12100+1/330<2/1000+1/300\). The first three terms plus this latter bound equal \(920357/1176000<157/200\). Use \(M_\infty<7/6\), \(\sqrt3<26/15\), and \(\pi>333/106\) to obtain \[ M_\infty-18J(1/3) <\frac76+\frac{18(26/15)}{4(333/106)}\,\frac{157}{200} =\frac{57641}{18500}<\frac{25}{8}. \tag{56} \] Finally apply (48) twice. The total wire correction is at most \(2\pi|y|\le L<2/15\); the lower-wire penalty can only decrease the exponent. The real crossing phases contribute zero at real trace angles. Since \(163/50-25/8-2/15=1/600\), (40) proves (53). \(\square\) For a fixed compact index interval \([\alpha,\beta]\subset(0,1/2)\) and a fixed angular cut \(T<\pi\), (53) gives a finite-source bound on sufficiently small positive trace heights, with gap \(1/1200\). Here the reflected region is specified by the real angles before those heights are introduced. Uniform continuity includes its factorial walls. The complete kernels have their proved low-kernel phase on the compact neighborhood, and decreasing the heights further gives \(\Re\Psi(t)>|\Im t|\), so their radicals have smaller rate. At fixed nonzero wire heights, or on half-grid vertical sides, the original wire denominator has its prescribed exponential weight and a bounded remaining factor. The trace denominators require positive heights. Thus the real-angle statement (53) is not being applied directly to a singular trace contour. The uniform factorial upper bound supplies the actual density estimate at both parities, and smaller holomorphic neighborhoods retain every fixed selected ordinary-color derivative. ## 8. Two useful endpoint cuts The full geometric wire rectangle can be used at the left cut. For \(0<\xi\le3/50\), \(|y|\le Y\), and real trace angles, the real-angle monotonicity gives \(\mathfrak b(\xi+iy,\tau)\le\Re b(\xi+iy,0)\). The function \(\Re b(\xi+iy,0)\) increases with \(\xi<1/4\): its derivative is \(2\log|\cot(\pi(\xi+iy))|>0\). Equation (48), applied at zero angle, therefore implies \[ \mathfrak b(\xi+iy,\tau) \le V_0(3/50)+\pi|y|,\qquad V_0(3/50)<\frac{33}{100}. \tag{57} \] For the last inequality integrate \(V_0'(x)=2\log\cot(\pi x)\le2\log(1/(\pi x))\) from zero. Use \(\pi>3\) and \(\log(50/9)<7/4\); the latter follows already from \(\sum_{k=0}^4(7/4)^k/k!=34193/6144>50/9\). The two factors and the complete phases have total rate \[ 2V_0(3/50)+2M_\infty+2\pi Y <\frac{33}{50}+\frac73+\frac14 =\frac{973}{300} <\mathcal M(n,p)-\frac1{60}. \tag{58} \] We have used the earlier \(2\pi Y<1/4\), which already suffices. As above, small positive trace heights preserve half the gap on any compact left interval \([\alpha,3/50]\). This includes half-grid vertical wire sides with \(|y|\le Y\). It retains the full complete kernels, both level parities, and fixed selected ordinary derivatives. There is a different estimate for the right endpoint, after the two original traces have been taken. In the notation (26), the half-charge action satisfies \(\mu(n)<M_\infty\). Equations (27)–(28) and the symmetry of \(V_0\) show \[ V_0(j/N)\le V_0(1/10)<\frac9{20} \quad\text{when }2/5\le j/N\le1/2. \tag{59} \] Indeed \(V_0(1/10)\le[1+\log(10/\pi)]/5\); \(\pi>3\) and \(\sum_{k=0}^4(5/4)^k/k!=7083/2048>10/3\) give the strict bound. Consequently \[ \sum_{2/5\le j/N\le L/N}|W_{n,j,N}W_{p,j,N}| \le CN^A e^{97N/30} <CN^A e^{N\{\mathcal M(n,p)-2/75\}} . \tag{60} \] The index \(L=\lfloor(N-1)/2\rfloor\) here is the one in Section 4, not the height notation used in Section 7. The odd simple endpoint is already included in (28). Replacing full edge kernels by their low parts has rate at most \(2M_\infty<7/3\), so it is smaller than the bound in (60). These facts justify choosing the right index cut at \(2/5+O(N^{-1})\) in the original source, with any slightly smaller gap if rounding is needed. This is an estimate after the traces; it does not assert the same bound on every vertical segment in a complex wire deformation. ## 9. Reproduction and proof scope The [exact scalar checker](../experiments/check_real_pair_geometry_and_tail_gap.py) verifies the rational comparisons used above and reads the saved \((3,3)\) action enclosure. It does not infer the geometric continuation, monotonicity, or quantum bound from samples; those arguments are the written proofs in Sections 1–5. ~~~sh python3 experiments/check_real_pair_geometry_and_tail_gap.py ~~~ The [saved record](../repro/results/research-real-pair-geometry-and-tail-gap.json) records the exact comparisons and the proof/input hashes. An earlier draft used the false identity \[ \Re\bigl[\{e^{i\omega}\sinh(k+ig)\}^2\bigr] =\tfrac12\{\cosh(2k)\cos(2g+2\omega)-\cos(2\omega)\}. \] The missing distinction between the \(\cosh(2k)\) and \(\sinh(2k)\) coefficients invalidated its asserted global derivative sign. Equation (7) is the corrected identity. The present proof instead uses a downward crossing at \(\Re C^2=1/2\) and an explicit bound at the quadrant entry; it makes no claim that the comparison is globally decreasing. The corresponding integer-angle argument was also repaired. The corrected geometric and finite-source implications have been independently checked. This correction changes the written proof; it does not replace a source estimate by a scalar test. The final scalar replay refreshes the proof/input hashes after those written corrections. No frozen pair-height certificate input is changed by this note.

title: Finite real-period image boundaries and their source contours

# Finite real-period image boundaries and their source contours Private written proof, 16 November 2026. The original positive period image already has an exact description by tilted minima of the compact angle energy. This note strengthens its finite-boundary conclusion: on every bounded real-period set, all angular heights, returns and square covectors are uniformly bounded. Every boundary approach therefore has finite sharp corner data. For a proper selected subset of a connected original tree, complete outside vertices also prevent vanishing half-angle observation factors. These statements do not make the inverse image a whole quantum contour. A general real family in that image meets genuine trace poles at infinitely many levels. That fact diagnoses a required detour problem, not an impossibility of transporting the original cycle. The component containing the geometric center is not assumed to contain this real family. ## 1. The fixed original tilted problem Fix a finite connected original ordered circle tree, a nonempty selected set \(S\), and all edges incident to \(S\), counted once. Let \(m\) be the number of included edges. Outside angles are complete: \(t_b=0\). Retain the original real signed powers \(n_v\), and a fixed charge vector \(c_v>0\). The original integral marking \(n_v=\eta_v-2p_v\), when present, is unchanged. Use the canonical positive branches and write \[ t_v=s_v+ih_v,\qquad r_{v,e}=k_{v,e}+ig_{v,e},\qquad P_v(t)=\sum_{e
i v}r_{v,e}- rac{i n_v}{2}t_v. 	ag{1} \] Every selected vertex has an incidence. The ambient angle body \(X\) has coordinates \(s_v\) and all endpoint incidence variables \(g\), with outside \(s_b=0\), and inequalities \[ |s_v|+2|g_{w,e}|<\pi,\qquad |s_w|+2|g_{v,e}|<\pi. 	ag{2} \] Its compact closure uses the weak inequalities. Put \[ ho_v=\sum_{e
i v}g_{v,e}-n_vs_v/2,\qquad \overline{\mathcal P}_c =\{z\in\overline X:ho_v(z)=-\pi c_v\}. 	ag{3} \] Assume a strictly feasible assignment \( ar z\in X\) with these rows is supplied. A positive original solution supplies one. For an oriented edge the two square coordinates are \[ A_P=s_v/4-g_{w,e}/2,\quad A_Q=s_v/4+g_{w,e}/2,\qquad y_P=g_{v,e}/2+s_w/4,\quad y_Q=g_{v,e}/2-s_w/4. 	ag{4} \] Let \(E_\square\) be the original square energy and \[ \mathcal E=4\sum_e(E_{P,e}+E_{Q,e}),\qquad E_{\max}=4mG_{m Cat},\qquad 0\le\mathcal E\le E_{\max}. 	ag{5} \] There is no outside imaginary-work term. Set \[ \alpha=\min_{	ext{square coordinates at } ar z} (\pi/4-|	ext{coordinate}|)>0. 	ag{6} \] For \(u\in\mathbb R^S\), let \[ z_u=\operatorname*{argmin}_{\overline{\mathcal P}_c} \{\mathcal E(z)-u\cdot s(z)\},\qquad \Xi_c=\{u:z_u\in X\}. 	ag{7} \] The pinned inverse-period theorem proves uniqueness and continuity of these closed minimizers. Its proof applies unchanged to the fixed rows (3): only their constant right sides change. It also identifies \(\Xi_c\) exactly with the real parameters for which the original positive equations \[ P(t)=u-\pi i c 	ag{8} \] have a solution. That solution is unique and analytic on \(\Xi_c\). No convexity or connectedness of \(\Xi_c\) is assumed. At an interior minimizer the exact ambient gradient is \[ d\mathcal E=u\cdot ds+\sum_{v\in S}h_v\,dho_v. 	ag{9} \] Indeed the incidence gradients match the imaginary angles, including zero at outside ends, while the real rows are \[ \sum_{e
i v}k_{v,e}+n_vh_v/2=u_v. 	ag{10} \] Equations (3), (10) are the two parts of (8). ## 2. Uniform finite-period bounds Fix \(R\ge0\), put \(c_{\max}=\max_v c_v\), and define \[  egin{aligned} H_R&= rac{E_{\max}+2\pi R}{\alpha},\ K_R&=\max\left\{2R+(2c_{\max}+1)H_R, \operatorname{arsinh} igl(\cosh(H_R/2) igr)ight\},\ L_R&=K_R/2+H_R/4 . \end{aligned} 	ag{11} \] **Theorem 1.** At every positive solution with \(u\in\Xi_c\), \(\|u\|_1\le R\), \[ \sum_{v\in S}|h_v|\le H_R,\qquad |k_{v,e}|\le K_R,\qquad |x_P|,|x_Q|,|B_P|,|B_Q|\le L_R. 	ag{12} \] Outside heights and returns are zero. The bounds are independent of the component of \(\Xi_c\). **Proof.** At the solution choose one incidence at each selected vertex. Starting at \( ar z\), change its chosen incidence by \(\alpha\operatorname{sgn}(h_v)\), and change no selected real angle. Denote the result by \(y\); use sign zero when \(h_v=0\). Each square coordinate changes by at most \(\alpha/2\). Opposite endpoint changes affect its \(A\) and \(y\) coordinates separately. Thus \(y\in X\), with square margin at least \(\alpha/2\), and \[ ho_v(y)-ho_v(z_u)=\alpha\operatorname{sgn}(h_v). 	ag{13} \] This is an ambient comparison; \(y\) need not lie in \(\overline{\mathcal P}_c\). The supporting inequality for \(\mathcal E\), (9), and \(|s_v( ar z)-s_v(z_u)|<2\pi\) give \[ \alpha\sum_v|h_v| \le\mathcal E(y)-\mathcal E(z_u) -u\cdot(s( ar z)-s(z_u)) \le E_{\max}+2\pi R. 	ag{14} \] This proves the first estimate without assuming any sign of \(h_v\). The original positive-prefix inequality is \[ \ell_{v,e}:=\Re(r_{v,e}\overline{t_v})>0 \quad	ext{when }t_v
e0 . 	ag{15} \] Here \(t_v=0\) is impossible: the canonical return identity \[ \sinh r_{v,e}=	an(t_v/2)\cos(t_w/2), \qquad |\Im r_{v,e}|<\pi/2 	ag{16} \] would make all its returns zero, contradicting \(c_v>0\) in (8). Pairing (8) with \(\overline{t_v}\) yields \[ 0<\sum_{e
i v}\ell_{v,e} =u_vs_v-\pi c_vh_v \le\pi|u_v|+\pi c_v|h_v|. 	ag{17} \] Since \(s_vk_{v,e}=\ell_{v,e}-h_vg_{v,e}\) and \(|g_{v,e}|<\pi/2\), for \(|s_v|\ge\pi/2\) we obtain \[ |k_{v,e}| \le2|u_v|+(2c_v+1)|h_v| \le2R+(2c_{\max}+1)H_R. 	ag{18} \] If \(|s_v|\le\pi/2\), direct trigonometry gives \[ |	an(t_v/2)|^2 = rac{\cosh h_v-\cos s_v}{\cosh h_v+\cos s_v}\le1,\qquad |\cos(t_w/2)|\le\cosh(H_R/2). 	ag{19} \] Use (16) and \(|\sinh(k+ig)|^2=\sinh^2k+\sin^2g\) to obtain the other bound defining \(K_R\). At a complete outside end, (16) gives its zero canonical return. Finally the original square identities are \[ x_P=k_{v,e}/2-h_w/4,\quad x_Q=k_{v,e}/2+h_w/4,\qquad B_P=h_v/4+k_{w,e}/2,\quad B_Q=h_v/4-k_{w,e}/2. 	ag{20} \] They give the last estimate. \(\square\) The four generating tetrahedron moduli and their negative reciprocals also remain in the fixed annulus \[ e^{-(K_R+H_R/2)}\le |Z|\le e^{K_R+H_R/2}, 	ag{21} \] by their original exponential formulas. This annulus does not exclude real shapes or the value one. ## 3. Every finite image-boundary approach **Corollary 2.** Suppose \(u_j\in\Xi_c\) tends to a finite \(u_*\). The primal assignments tend to the unique closed minimizer \(z_{u_*}\). Heights, returns and square covectors have a jointly convergent subsequence, with (12). If \(z_{u_*}\) is on the angle boundary, every noninterior square is a corner, and at each such square \[ (A,y)=(\varepsilon_A\pi/4,\varepsilon_y\pi/4),\qquad U=\varepsilon_Ax>0,\quad V=\varepsilon_yB>0,\qquad \sinh(2U)\sinh(2V)=1. 	ag{22} \] The original charge, real-period and matching rows pass to the limit without resetting their branches. **Proof.** Continuity in (7) gives the primal convergence; Theorem 1 and the bounded real coordinates give subsequential compactness of all remaining quantities. An open-side square would make one of \[ x=	frac12\operatorname{arsinh}(	an(2A)\cos(2y)),\qquad B=	frac12\operatorname{arsinh}(	an(2y)\cos(2A)) 	ag{23} \] diverge, contrary to (12). At a corner, pass to the exact identity \[ \sinh(2x)\sinh(2B)=\sin(2A)\sin(2y). 	ag{24} \] The signs of \(x,B\) are those of \(A,y\); bounded limits in (24) therefore give exactly (22). All period and matching rows are finite linear identities in these coordinates. \(\square\) This strengthens the finite-boundary statement in the earlier inverse-image theorem for complete outside data. It does not assert uniqueness of the reconstructed corner covectors when only the closed primal minimizer has been specified. **Corollary 3 (proper-selection observation units).** If \(S\) is proper in the connected original tree, then for each \(R\) there is \(\delta_R>0\) such that, at every solution covered by Theorem 1 and every selected vertex, \[ |\cos(t_v/2)|,\quad |\sin(t_v/2)|,\quad|\sin t_v|\ \ge\delta_R. 	ag{25} \] No nonzero lower bound on \(|h_v|\) is asserted. **Proof.** If the cosine bound failed, choose a sequence of solutions with that cosine tending to zero. Theorem 1 and the compact real-angle ranges give a joint subsequential limit. The limiting angle at this vertex is \(t_v=\pi\) or \(-\pi\). Use the division-free original identity \[ \sinh r_{v,e}\cos(t_v/2) =\sin(t_v/2)\cos(t_w/2). 	ag{26} \] Its bounded factors pass to the limit. Since the limiting sine is \(1\) or \(-1\), every neighbor has \(\cos(t_w/2)=0\). This propagates along the selected component to a complete outside neighbor, where the cosine equals one. Every selected component has such a neighbor because the original tree is connected and \(S\) is proper. This is a contradiction. If a half-angle sine tends to zero, its limiting angle must be \(t_v=0\). Equation (26) makes every incident \(\sinh r_{v,e}=0\). The closed range \(|\Im r_{v,e}|\le\pi/2\) forces \(r_{v,e}=0\). The limit of (8) would have imaginary part \(0=-\pi c_v\), again impossible. The only additional zeros of \(\sin t_v\) in the closed angular range are \(t_v=\pm\pi\), already excluded. Compactness and finiteness of the vertices prove uniformity. \(\square\) The tangent variables are consequently bounded, and the original relations \[ e^{\pm r_{v,e}}=\cos(t_w/2)(q_e\pm a_v) 	ag{27} \] bound \(q_e\pm a_v\) away from zero. These conclusions do **not** exclude \(q_e=\pm i\) at a general tilted corner. Thus they do not prove boundedness of \[ x_e= rac1{2\pi i}\log rac{q_e+i}{q_e-i}. 	ag{28} \] In particular the radial endpoint exclusion and two-square matching theorem cannot be imported into this tilted image. The estimates do not exclude finite tilted limits with \(\Re t_v=\pm\pi\) and \(\Im t_v
e0\). The remaining statement is compactness of angles, returns and square covectors, with (22), rather than properness of every face or stationary-wire chart. ## 4. A classical gap away from the center Suppose in addition that \(0\in\Xi_c\), so the original charged positive solution \(t^0\) is supplied. Retain the exact action \[ \Phi_c(t)=\sum_e\psi(t_v,t_w) + rac{i}{4\pi}\sum_{v\in S}n_vt_v^2 -i\sum_{v\in S}c_vt_v. 	ag{29} \] The original edge identity of the inverse-descent theorem gives, with \(M_\infty=\psi(0,0)=4G_{m Cat}/\pi\), on the entire positive inverse slice, \[ \Re\Phi_c(t(u)) =mM_\infty- rac{\mathcal E(z_u)}{\pi}. 	ag{30} \] Indeed summing \(\pi\Re\psi+4E_e-g_vh_v-g_wh_w=\pi M_\infty\) and using \(\sum g_v=n_vs_v/2-\pi c_v\) gives (30). This checks the charge normalization directly. For every \(0<r\le R<\infty\), \[ \Delta_{r,R} :=\min_{r\le\|u\|_1\le R} \{\mathcal E(z_u)-\mathcal E(z_0)\}>0. 	ag{31} \] To prove it, use continuity of the closed minimizers and compactness of the parameter annulus. Equality of energies would force \(z_u=z_0\), the unique minimum of \(\mathcal E\). Since \(z_0\) is interior, it could also minimize \(\mathcal E-u\cdot s\) only if \(u\cdot ds=0\) on every feasible tangent. The projection to selected \(s\) is surjective: change one incidence per selected vertex to restore its row. Hence \(u=0\), excluded in (31). Thus finite image-boundary approaches away from the center retain a strict calibrated classical action gap. At a regular single-square image boundary satisfying the already proved proper-selected-set Jacobian criterion, the inverse equations continue locally through the wall. The continued cells need not be positive, so the original convex argument does not control an unrestricted continuation beyond that neighborhood. At more general finite corners, (22) alone supplies no such continuation. No conclusion about the quantum source follows from the classical gap without its actual contour estimates. ## 5. The real slice and actual trace poles The full positive image is not generally confined to lower angular heights. This is an exact general statement: **Proposition 4.** Suppose \(n_v
e0\) and \(|n_v|>2c_v\) for every selected vertex. Then the real configuration \[ s_v= rac{2\pi c_v}{n_v},\qquad t_v=s_v, 	ag{32} \] with complete outside angles, lies on the positive inverse slice for the real parameter \(u_v=\sum_{e
i v}r_{v,e}(s)\). Near that parameter the heights \(h_v\), as functions of the real period coordinates, attain a neighborhood of zero. At unit charge, if all \(|n_v|\ge3\) are odd, every odd level \(N\) divisible by all \(|n_v|\) makes (32) an original angular grid point at every selected vertex. The literal unit-coupon factorial density has genuine trace double poles there. **Proof.** The angles in (32) lie in \((-\pi,\pi)\). All tangents \(a_v\) are real, and \(q_e=\sqrt{1+a_v^2+a_w^2}>\sqrt{a_v^2+a_w^2}\); thus every original edge is positive and its returns are real. The imaginary part of \(P_v\) is \(-n_vs_v/2=-\pi c_v\), proving (8). At this real point the complex period Jacobian is \[ J=A-iD,\qquad A=A^{\mathsf T}>0,\qquad D=\operatorname{diag}(n_v/2). 	ag{33} \] The real return matrix \(A\) is positive definite by original edge monotonicity. The inverse-period height derivative is the real symmetric matrix \[  rac{\partial h}{\partial u} =\Im(J^{-1})=J^{-*}D J^{-1}. 	ag{34} \] It is invertible since \(D\) is. The real inverse-function theorem proves the local height assertion. For the stated odd common-multiple levels, the integers \[ 2j_v+1=N- rac{2N}{n_v} 	ag{35} \] are positive, odd and less than \(2N\). Thus (32) equals \(	au_{j_v}=\pi-(2j_v+1)\pi/N\), the actual physical angular grid. The factor \[ W_N(t)= rac{e^{-iNt}}{(1-\eta e^{-iNt})^2}, \qquad \eta=(-1)^{N-1}, 	ag{36} \] has a double pole there. There is no cancellation of these poles by the literal local factorials. At the real stationary wire, \[  rac{\pi}{2}-\pi x_e=\arctan q_e>|s_v|/2, \qquad 0<	frac12-x_e\pm rac{s_v}{2\pi}<1. 	ag{37} \] Consequently every shifted factorial argument \(N(1/2-x_e\pm s_v/(2\pi))-1/2\) lies in \((-1,N)\), and \(Nx_e\in(0,N)\). All the original \(B_N\)'s are exact units. Also \(\sin s_v
e0\), the unit coupon is one, and the crossing Gaussian is a unit. This proves the last assertion about the specified density. \(\square\) Proposition 4 does not show that this real point belongs to the component of \(\Xi_c\) containing \(u=0\). Nor does the presence of poles forbid a valid cycle: it requires prescribed detours and retention of their residue or endpoint currents. On a compact regular phase chart, displacements of size \(O(1/N)\) change its exponential phase by only \(O(1)\); this observation is not an estimate for the entire original factorial network. Competing modes and the actual meromorphic factors still require their own coherent bounds. For the original source the allowed relative boundary remains the one in the joint-lens theorem: fixed angular endpoint faces and fixed wire seams, with free cardinal ends unchanged. A finite corner image is not one of those prescribed source faces merely because the classical positive cells degenerate there. The compactness and gap proved above therefore leave a precise global task: construct the connecting relative chain, including all necessary pole detours and wire faces, and control its complete source. No such homology or remainder statement is inferred in this note. A literal factorial density is deployed as the original source only under its traced-end convention or a separately proved boundary adapter. ## Direct sources and author readback * [Positive inverse-period descent](research_positive_period_inverse_descent.md), SHA256 b9b5c3d61c704700e9431315cf50591c921ebeb95becdf6a52877606bdbc4565: the exact tilted image, continuous unique minimizers, action calibration and already proved compact collars. Complete text read. * [Radial compactness and sharp corners](research_radial_charge_compactness_and_corners.md), SHA256 744d36368876f255df6e2b1f2ca15dd23e805d5d5a39b009f6983fec2c6243ec: original square identities, positive prefix pairing, ambient energy bound and sharp-corner argument. Complete text reread. * [Positive wire product domain](research_positive_wire_product_contour.md), SHA256 5646f2d6b2a8dfa2d8c49662d17f19f3743fc4efcaf3c3685c6a899975a4c230: real positive-edge criterion, original stationary wire and exact factorial unit strip. Complete read retained at the unchanged hash. * [Joint factorial-lens source](research_joint_factorial_lens_relative_source.md), SHA256 a14ca148bd55b36b1eea9de8be8a63025532c3bbbb928482b0d7cb8edae56e54: actual grid, trace poles, normalization, fixed relative faces and traced-versus-free endpoint convention. Complete read retained. * [Regular-corner period assembly](research_regular_corner_period_assembly.md), SHA256 7d551e90d04b7c45232074109581bf2a807569259f98ad81e00855bec7f51ce5: the limited local continuation statement used after (31).
