title: Reciprocal lowering flags and the actual root radical
text: # Reciprocal lowering flags and the actual root radical Private written proof, 19 November 2026. Author-final for independent review. The reciprocal Cartan-pair image of the actual prefix reduction is exactly the endomorphism algebra of a two-periodic exact lowering complex. This identifies its admissibility condition with explicit physical flags. Together with the original first-normal source order, it proves that the Jacobson radical of the entire actual root intertwiner algebra has cube zero, uniformly in the level and width. Only the units congruent to one modulo this radical form the resulting two-step nilpotent group. The complete directs are P, the first-jet source order, and C, the actual prefix Ward equations. The lowering-chain, division-free Ward, flag, and radical arguments are proved below. This is a statement about the full Cartan-preserving source algebra. Its integer-degree-preserving subalgebra is retained where a braid word requires it, but no separate classification of that subalgebra is asserted. ## 1. The actual pair and the image already determined by the source Fix \[ N\ge2,\quad d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2, \quad m=r+1\ge2, \qquad M=1,\quad x=-q^{-1}. \tag{1} \] Let \(U\) be the tensor of the remaining \(r\) physical heads, with actual totals \(E,F,K\). The total operators on all \(m\) heads are denoted by a subscript \(\Sigma\). Set \[ K^N=\varepsilon I,\qquad \varepsilon=(-1)^{(N+1)r}, \qquad \mathcal A=\operatorname{End}_K(U). \tag{2} \] Each actual weight space \(U_\chi\) has dimension \(D=N^{r-1}\). The weight set is closed under inversion. For an actual total intertwiner \(W\), C gives \[ W'=S^{-1}WS=\sum_{n=0}^{d}F_1^n\otimes B_n, \qquad KB_n=Q^nB_nK, \tag{3} \] and the literal transformed lowering operator \[ E'=S^{-1}E_\Sigma S=I\otimes E+L_1b_A, \qquad b_a=KQ^{-a}-K^{-1}. \tag{4} \] The second term vanishes at first occupation zero. All terms have the physical cap. In particular \([E',W']=0\). Let \(V\subset\mathcal A\) be the set of root matrices \(B_0\) arising from these actual intertwiners. P proves that every root intertwiner has an analytic meridian lift and identifies the full root algebra with \[ \mathcal T=V\oplus(\mathcal A/V),\qquad (b,[c])(b',[c'])=(bb',[bc'+cb']). \tag{5} \] Here the first and second components are the value and first \(\mu=\Log M\) coefficient of the actual reduced family. The normal-layer ideal in (5) is square-zero. For a nonself reciprocal pair \(\mathfrak o=\{\chi,\chi^{-1}\}\), P supplies its central projector in \(V\) and proves \[ \dim V_{\mathfrak o}=D^2,\qquad V_{\mathfrak o}=V_{\mathfrak o}^{\perp_\beta}, \quad \beta((X,Y),(X',Y'))=a_\chi\operatorname{Tr}(XX'-YY'), \quad a_\chi=\frac{\chi-\chi^{-1}}{2\varepsilon m}. \tag{6} \] On a self weight \(\chi=\pm1\), P proves that \(V\) is the entire matrix block and that its normal quotient is zero. Since \(\chi^{2N}=1\), for a nonself pair there is a unique \(s\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\) such that \(Q^s=\chi^2\). The two actual lowering maps of interest are \[ A=E^s:U_{\chi^{-1}}\longrightarrow U_\chi, \qquad B=E^{N-s}:U_\chi\longrightarrow U_{\chi^{-1}}. \tag{7} \] Their directions follow from \(KE=QEK\). No power of \(F\) or extra Cartan factor is included in (7). ## 2. Full physical lowering chains The operator \(E\) on \(U\) has only Jordan chains of length \(N\). This follows directly from the actual tensor structure. For one head, its coefficients \[ e_a=Q^{-a}-1,\quad 1\le a\le d, \tag{8} \] are nonzero, and its two outward arrows are zero. For more heads, split the first remaining head from the rest, writing \[ E=E_{\rm h}K_{\rm t}+E_{\rm t}. \tag{9} \] The two summands \(Q\)-commute. The finite quantum binomial identity at primitive \(Q\) therefore gives inductively \(E^N=E_{\rm h}^NK_{\rm t}^N+E_{\rm t}^N=0\). This uses the actual zero endpoint arrows. For \(0\le b\le d\), consider \[ E^b(w_d\otimes v),\qquad v\in U_{\rm t}. \tag{10} \] Their least first-head occupation is \(d-b\), with coefficient \((e_d\cdots e_{d-b+1})K_{\rm t}^b\). This is a unit. The joint map in (10) is consequently triangular and invertible. It provides \(N^{r-1}\) independent length-\(N\) chains, since applying \(E\) advances the displayed power and the next power after \(d\) is zero. Choosing \(v\) in a Cartan weight space makes each chain homogeneous. Each chain contains each of the \(N\) actual Cartan weights once. It follows on each chain, and hence on the actual weight spaces, that \[ AB=BA=0,\qquad \operatorname{im}A=\ker B, \qquad \operatorname{im}B=\ker A. \tag{11} \] Indeed the two weights in (7) occur at distinct positions in one linear chain. Exactly one of the two indicated forward paths stays inside that chain; the other crosses its zero endpoint. Write \(k=\operatorname{rank}A\), \(l=\operatorname{rank}B\). Then \(k+l=D\). For \(r\ge2\) these ranks are explicitly \[ k=(N-s)N^{r-2},\qquad l=sN^{r-2}. \tag{12} \] To count them, the starting weights of (10) are \(xQ^{-d}\kappa\), with \(\kappa\) a rest weight. Every rest weight occurs \(N^{r-2}\) times. Thus the position of \(\chi^{-1}\) is uniformly distributed among the \(N\) positions of these chains; exactly \(N-s\) positions permit \(s\) further steps. For \(r=1\), \(D=1\): if \(\chi^{-1}=xQ^{-a}\), then \(k=1\) precisely when \(a\ge s\); otherwise \(k=0\), and always \(l=1-k\). ## 3. The division-free Ward constraint We prove that the actual root image commutes with both arrows of (7). This step does not invert any resonant coefficient \(b_a\). Let \(i_n v=w_n\otimes v\), and restrict the full prefix space to total weight \(x\lambda\). Its \(n\)-th first-head component has tail weight \(Q^n\lambda\). For \(0\le n\le t<N\), direct expansion of (4) gives \[ p_0(E')^t i_n\big|_{U_{Q^n\lambda}} =c_{t,n}(\lambda)E^{t-n}, \quad c_{t,n}(\lambda)=Q^{n(n-1)/2}{t\brack n}_Q \prod_{j=t}^{t+n-1}(\lambda-Q^{-j}\lambda^{-1}). \tag{13} \] For \(n=0\) the coefficient is one, and for \(n>t\) the left side is zero. To verify the formula including all orders, separate the first step in (4). The term that keeps the first occupation and the term that lowers it give respectively \[ c_{t,n}(\lambda) =c_{t-1,n}(Q\lambda) +(\lambda-Q^{-n}\lambda^{-1})c_{t-1,n-1}(Q\lambda). \tag{14} \] The initial coefficient is \(c_{0,0}=1\). Substituting (13) in (14) reduces it to the two finite Pascal identities for \({t\brack n}_Q\). This proves (13) inductively. All Gaussian coefficients have index less than \(N\); no denominator \(1-Q^N\) occurs. If \(\lambda^2=Q^{-t}\), every coefficient in (13) with \(n\ge1\) vanishes because its product contains \(\lambda-Q^{-t}\lambda^{-1}\). Thus on this actual total weight space \[ p_0(E')^t=E^t p_0. \tag{15} \] Also \((E')^t i_0=i_0E^t\) without any weight restriction. Apply \(p_0\) to \((E')^tW'i_0=W'(E')^t i_0\), and use (3) and (15). It follows that \[ E^t B_0|_{U_\lambda}=B_0|_{U_{Q^t\lambda}}E^t. \tag{16} \] Take \((\lambda,t)=(\chi^{-1},s)\) and then \((\chi,N-s)\). For \((X,Y)=(B_0|_{U_\chi}, B_0|_{U_{\chi^{-1}}})\), this proves \[ XA=AY,\qquad YB=BX. \tag{17} \] Every intermediate physical first-head term was retained before the common factor made it zero. In particular (17) was not obtained by formally dividing C's scalar Ward recurrence at a root resonance. ## 4. Exact flag classification and the first-normal quotient Choose complements in the exact complex (11): \[ U_\chi=P\oplus Q_*,\qquad P=\operatorname{im}A=\ker B, \qquad U_{\chi^{-1}}=R_*\oplus T_*,\qquad R_*=\operatorname{im}B=\ker A. \tag{18} \] The dimensions are \((k,l)\) and \((l,k)\), respectively. Use \(A:T_*\to P\) and \(B:Q_*\to R_*\) to identify the complementary coordinates. Solving (17) now gives exactly \[ \boxed{\qquad X=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\0&d_*\end{pmatrix},\qquad Y=\begin{pmatrix}d_*&f\\0&a\end{pmatrix}. \qquad}\tag{19} \] Here \(a\in\operatorname{Mat}_k\), \(d_*\in\operatorname{Mat}_l\), \(b\in\operatorname{Mat}_{k\times l}\), and \(f\in\operatorname{Mat}_{l\times k}\) are arbitrary. For example \(XA=AY\) kills the lower-left block of \(X\) and identifies its \(a\) with the lower-right block of \(Y\); the other arrow does the complementary job. The algebra in (19) has dimension \(k^2+l^2+2kl=D^2\). Equation (17) includes \(V_{\mathfrak o}\) in this algebra, while P gives precisely that dimension in (6). Therefore \[ \boxed{\qquad V_{\mathfrak o}=\operatorname{End}(U_{\chi^{-1}} \mathop{\rightleftarrows}^{A}_{B}U_\chi). \qquad}\tag{20} \] The intrinsic statement is preservation of the two physical flags and compatibility with both arrows. The complements in (18) only display its matrix form. Its ideal \(J\) consisting of the two off-diagonal blocks \((b,f)\) satisfies \(J^2=0\), and \[ V_{\mathfrak o}/J =\operatorname{Mat}_k\oplus\operatorname{Mat}_l. \tag{21} \] A zero-size matrix factor is omitted. Thus \(J\) is its Jacobson radical: a nilpotent ideal is contained in that radical by the finite geometric-series inverse, and the displayed matrix quotient has zero radical. The latter is elementary: for a nonzero matrix \(T\), a suitable rank-one \(S\) makes \(I-ST\) singular, excluding \(T\) from the radical criterion. The same flags explicitly describe the quotient normal layer in (5). If a representative of \(\mathcal A_{\mathfrak o}/ V_{\mathfrak o}\) has blocks \((C,D_*)\) in (18), its class is determined by \[ C_{11}-(D_*)_{22},\quad C_{22}-(D_*)_{11},\quad C_{21},\quad(D_*)_{21}. \tag{22} \] The two upper-right blocks disappear in the quotient. Pairing with (19) is exactly \[ a_\chi\bigl[ \operatorname{Tr}_k((C_{11}-(D_*)_{22})a) +\operatorname{Tr}_l((C_{22}-(D_*)_{11})d_*) +\operatorname{Tr}_l(C_{21}b)-\operatorname{Tr}_k((D_*)_{21}f) \bigr]. \tag{23} \] Thus (6) identifies this quotient with \(V_{\mathfrak o}^*\), including its actual scalar \(a_\chi\). This is a bimodule identification. If \(\phi_c(v)=\beta(c,v)\), cyclicity and the central coefficient of \(\beta\) give \[ (b\phi_c)(v)=\phi_c(vb),\qquad (\phi_c b)(v)=\phi_c(bv), \tag{24} \] exactly the actions inherited from multiplication in \(\mathcal A/V\). It is not a Hermitian duality. ## 5. Cube-zero radical of the whole actual root algebra On a nonself pair, (5) and (24) identify the entire actual root factor with the trivial extension \[ T(V_{\mathfrak o})=V_{\mathfrak o}\oplus V_{\mathfrak o}^*, \qquad (b,\phi)(b',\phi')=(bb',b\phi'+\phi b'). \tag{25} \] Define \[ \mathfrak r_{\mathfrak o} =J\oplus V_{\mathfrak o}^*. \tag{26} \] This is an ideal. Its quotient is (21). Its cube is zero: a product containing two dual factors is zero, as is a product with two adjacent \(J\) factors. The only other possible three-factor product is \(j\phi j'\). For every \(v\in V\), \[ (j\phi j')(v)=\phi(j'vj)=0, \tag{27} \] because \(J\) is an ideal and \(J^2=0\). Hence \[ \mathfrak r_{\mathfrak o}^{3}=0. \tag{28} \] The nilpotent-ideal and matrix-quotient argument following (21) shows that (26) is the entire Jacobson radical, not merely a nilpotent subideal. The central pair projectors from P split (5): they are central in the ambient \(\mathcal A\) and therefore also in its quotient bimodule. Each self-Cartan factor has no normal quotient and is the full semisimple matrix algebra. Consequently, if \(\mathfrak R\) is the Jacobson radical of the actual full root intertwiner algebra on all \(m\) heads, then \[ \boxed{\quad\mathfrak R^3=0.\quad} \tag{29} \] The bound does not depend on \(N\) or \(m\). For one remaining head, every nonself pair has \(k=0\) or \(l=0\), so \(J=0\) and that factor's radical already has square zero. The assertion (29) concerns the full Cartan commutant. It does not claim that passing to an arbitrary subalgebra preserves this radical classification or these rank formulas. ## 6. Finite radical transport and the original source The radical unit group \(1+\mathfrak R\) has nilpotence class at most two. For \(X,Y\in\mathfrak R\), \[ (1+X)^{-1}=1-X+X^2, \quad (1+X)(1+Y)(1+X)^{-1}(1+Y)^{-1}=1+[X,Y], \tag{30} \] and the last commutator is central within \(1+\mathfrak R\). Equivalently, \[ e^X=1+X+\tfrac12X^2,\quad \log(1+X)=X-\tfrac12X^2,\quad \log(e^Xe^Y)=X+Y+\tfrac12[X,Y]. \tag{31} \] These follow by expansion and (29). For any element \(T\) of the actual root algebra, its conjugation is also exact at second order: \[ e^XTe^{-X}=T+[X,T]+\tfrac12[X,[X,T]]. \tag{32} \] Every omitted term has three radical factors, with ordinary algebra factors between them, and vanishes because \(\mathfrak R\) is an ideal and \(\mathfrak R^3=0\). The full unit group contains the nonnilpotent matrix groups of (21); it has not been declared nilpotent. All these coordinates keep the original source. P's exact formula for a root class \((b,[c])\) is \[ \Phi_0(b,[c])=\operatorname{Tr}(d_0b) +\operatorname{Tr}(d_{-1}c), \quad d_0=\frac{K+K^{-1}}{2\varepsilon},\qquad d_{-1}=\frac{K-K^{-1}}{2\varepsilon m}. \tag{33} \] On the pair in (19), this becomes \[ \frac{\chi+\chi^{-1}}{\varepsilon} (\operatorname{Tr}a+\operatorname{Tr}d_*) +a_\chi\bigl[ \operatorname{Tr}_k(C_{11}-(D_*)_{22}) +\operatorname{Tr}_l(C_{22}-(D_*)_{11})\bigr]. \tag{34} \] In particular the normal layer is not discarded by the flag classification. Crossings and framing scalars included in an actual word remain in its two jet coefficients; any prescribed outside scalar retains its own product-rule derivatives. The theorem gives explicit physical flags for admissibility and uniform algebraic nilpotence in the actual finite source. It does not estimate the condition numbers of the chosen flag complements, identify these Cartan pairs with selected geometric eigenflags, or prove positivity or nonvanishing of the closing of a prescribed braid. No geometric Regge or framing group is identified with the radical unit group. ## Complete direct-source pins * P: notes/research_prefix_first_jet_source_order.md, 434 lines, SHA256 ffdf484ab0222b99dc937b24ef940af91070609e4e85cf8675e20a500eb53ad5. * C: notes/research_prefix_commutant_and_pointed_normal_functional.md, 549 lines, SHA256 b4fb801a1482316aebb4799f1d0b80d5b43ced39138d903c04cfde811ca166b0. The complete matching P read from the immediately preceding formal review is retained fresh and unchanged in this author sequence. The complete C was freshly read nontruncated in covering chunks. The entire matching final was freshly read back nontruncated, every used implication checked, and all three pins renewed before freezing. Independent matching review and parent adoption remain separate. Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used. Frozen and public files were unchanged.

title: The original inverse-period collar over a convex real-angle domain

# The original inverse-period collar over a convex real-angle domain Private written proof, 16 November 2026. The compact inverse-period collar has a stronger description than its star-shaped real-period parametrization: it is the graph of the imaginary angles over a bounded convex domain of real angles. The convex function defining that domain is obtained by minimizing the original angle energy along its incidence fibers. This description retains the original signed powers, charges and complete peripheral branches. It also fixes the sign of a possible connector argument: moving vertically away from this graph increases the real action. Consequently the graph theorem does not itself complete the collar to the original quantum integration class. ## 1. Original coordinates and the closed fiber problem Fix a finite connected original ordered circle tree, a nonempty selected set \(S\), and all edges incident to \(S\), counted once. Let \(k=|S|\) and let \(m\) be the number of included edges. Every selected vertex has positive degree. Outside angles are complete: \(t_b=0\). Fix real powers \(n_v\) and positive real charges \(c_v\). In an integral filling the original convention is \(n_v=\eta_v-2p_v\); no carrier or slope is changed here. Use the complete positive branches and write \[ t_v=s_v+i h_v,\qquad r_{v,e}=k_{v,e}+i g_{v,e},\qquad P_v(t)=\sum_{e
i v}r_{v,e}- rac{i n_v}{2}t_v. 	ag{1} \] The affine angle coordinates consist of the selected \(s_v\) and all endpoint incidence variables \(g_{v,e}\), with \(s_b=0\) outside. Put \[ ho_v=\sum_{e
i v}g_{v,e}- rac{n_v}{2}s_v=-\pi c_v. 	ag{2} \] The open positive polytope \(\mathcal P_c\) is defined by these rows and the inequalities \[ |s_v|+2|g_{w,e}|<\pi,\qquad |s_w|+2|g_{v,e}|<\pi\qquad(e=vw). 	ag{3} \] Assume strict feasibility. Its compact closure is obtained by using weak inequalities. Indeed a segment from any weak assignment to a strict assignment is strict except at the weak endpoint. Interiors and boundaries of \(\mathcal P_c\) are relative to the affine space (2). For one edge the original square coordinates are \[  egin{aligned} A_P&=s_v/4-g_{w,e}/2,& A_Q&=s_v/4+g_{w,e}/2,\ y_P&=g_{v,e}/2+s_w/4,& y_Q&=g_{v,e}/2-s_w/4. \end{aligned} 	ag{4} \] The pinned variational theorem supplies the continuous convex energy \[ \mathcal E=4\sum_e(E_{P,e}+E_{Q,e}) 	ag{5} \] on \(\overline{\mathcal P}_c\). Its Hessian is positive definite on every nonzero affine tangent at an interior point. This follows from the positive square Hessians and the injectivity of (4). There is no outside imaginary-work term because the outside data are complete. The exact edge differential is \[ 4\,d(E_{P,e}+E_{Q,e}) =k_{v,e}\,ds_v+k_{w,e}\,ds_w +h_{v,e}\,dg_{v,e}+h_{w,e}\,dg_{w,e}. 	ag{6} \] Let \(\pi_s\) denote projection to the selected real angles and set \[ \overline D=\pi_s(\overline{\mathcal P}_c),\qquad e_c(s)=\min\{\mathcal E(s,g):(s,g)\in\overline{\mathcal P}_c\}. 	ag{7} \] Every fiber is nonempty and compact for \(s\in\overline D\), so the value in (7) is defined. At this stage the notation does not assert uniqueness or interiority of a closed fiber minimizer. The strict feasible real-angle base \(D=\pi_s(\mathcal P_c)\) is explicitly \[  oxed{\quad |s_v|<\pi,\qquad |n_vs_v-2\pi c_v|+ \sum_{e=(v,w)}|s_w|<\pi d_v\quad(v\in S).\quad} 	ag{8} \] Outside terms in the sum are zero; sums count incidences. This is the fixed-real-angle form of the existing feasibility criterion. For completeness, at fixed \(s\), each \(g_{v,e}\) independently varies in the interval \((-(\pi-|s_w|)/2,(\pi-|s_w|)/2)\). Their sum must equal \((n_vs_v-2\pi c_v)/2\), giving (8). Outside incidences have no sum constraint and can be chosen zero. Thus \(D\) is a bounded convex open polytope, and \(\overline D\) is its closure. The rows (2) are independent and their affine space projects surjectively onto the selected \(s\): an arbitrary change of \(s_v\) can be offset in one incidence at that vertex. The function \(e_c\) is convex on \(\overline D\). Choose minimizers in the two fibers and take their convex combination; convexity of \(\mathcal E\) gives the convexity inequality for (7). It is also lower semicontinuous: for any convergent sequence of base points, a subsequence of their compact fiber minimizers attaining the lower limit has a limiting feasible assignment. No global strict-convexity assertion at boundary fibers is needed. ## 2. The regular fiber locus is exactly the positive period slice Define \[ D_{\mathrm{reg}}= \{s\in D:	ext{a minimizer in (7) lies in }\mathcal P_c\}. 	ag{9} \] **Proposition 1.** The set \(D_{\mathrm{reg}}\) is open. Its fiber minimizer \(z(s)=(s,g(s))\) is unique and real analytic. Its endpoint imaginary angles match, giving a real analytic graph \[ t(s)=s+i h(s). 	ag{10} \] With \(u(s)=
abla e_c(s)\), this graph satisfies the original equations \[ P(t(s))=u(s)-\pi i c. 	ag{11} \] Conversely every positive solution of \(P(t)=u-\pi i c\) occurs exactly once on (10). Thus \(
abla e_c\) is a real analytic diffeomorphism from \(D_{\mathrm{reg}}\) onto the actual positive real-period image \(\Xi_c\). Neither of these sets is assumed connected or convex. **Proof.** An interior fiber critical point has positive Hessian on the homogeneous fiber tangent. It is the unique global fiber minimum, including against boundary points: its segment to any distinct feasible point is interior before the endpoint, and has strictly positive second derivative. The fiber stationarity equations have invertible Hessian, so the implicit-function theorem supplies an analytic interior critical point for all nearby \(s\). Its uniqueness as a global minimum proves the first assertions. Attach multipliers \(h_v\) to (2) while holding \(s\) fixed. By (6), incidence stationarity is precisely \[ h_{v,e}=h_v\quad(v\in S),\qquad h_{b,e}=0\quad(b
otin S). 	ag{12} \] The original square dictionary therefore reconstructs the matched positive point (10). Along this fiber-minimum graph, (2) and (6) give \[ de_c=\sum_{v\in S}\left( \sum_{e
i v}k_{v,e}+ rac{n_v}{2}h_vight)ds_v. 	ag{13} \] Combining (13) with (2) gives (11). Alternatively the ambient identity at this point is \(d\mathcal E=u\cdot ds+\sum_v h_v\,dho_v\). Consequently \(z(s)\) is the unique interior, hence global, minimum of \(\mathcal E-u(s)\cdot s\) on \(\overline{\mathcal P}_c\). This is the original tilted problem defining \(\Xi_c\). Conversely its interior minimizer minimizes its fixed-\(s\) fiber and satisfies (12), so it occurs on (10). Uniqueness of the tilted minimum gives injectivity. The period theorem supplies the analytic inverse \(u\mapsto t(u)\); its real part is the inverse of \(
abla e_c\). \(\square\) There is also a direct differential formula. Write the complex symmetric original Jacobian as \[ J= rac{\partial P}{\partial t}=A+iB, \qquad A=A^{\mathsf T}>0,\qquad B=B^{\mathsf T}. 	ag{14} \] Differentiating (11) in real \(s\) gives \[  oxed{\quad h_s=-A^{-1}B,\qquad 
abla^2e_c=A+B A^{-1}B = igl(\Re J^{-1} igr)^{-1}>0. \quad} 	ag{15} \] Indeed the imaginary part of \((A+iB)(I+i h_s)=u_s\) is \(B+A h_s=0\), and the real part gives the second formula. The matrix \(h_s\) need not be symmetric; the graph assertion does not identify \(h\) itself as the gradient of a function of \(s\). The reduced energy also has strict supporting inequalities between any two distinct regular points, even if a segment between their base points is not known to stay regular. Apply the strict supporting inequality of \(\mathcal E\) at the first interior minimizer to the second. The \(dho\) terms vanish, giving \[ e_c(s_2)>e_c(s_1)+
abla e_c(s_1)\cdot(s_2-s_1) \qquad(s_1
e s_2	ext{ in }D_{m reg}). 	ag{16} \] In particular the gradient is strictly monotone between those points. This does not replace the interior-minimizer requirement in (9) by strict linear feasibility alone. ## 3. Exact convex projection of every low-energy collar Assume now that the original charged positive solution at \(u=0\) is supplied. Write its angle assignment as \(z_0\), its real angles as \(s_0\), and \(E_0=\mathcal E(z_0)\). It is the unique global minimum of \(\mathcal E\). Put \[ \Delta=\min_{\partial\mathcal P_c}\mathcal E-E_0>0, \qquad 0<\delta<\Delta, \qquad D_\delta=\{s\in\overline D:e_c(s)<E_0+\delta\}. 	ag{17} \] **Theorem 2.** The set \(D_\delta\) is a bounded convex open domain with smooth boundary. Its closure is compactly contained in \(D_{\mathrm{reg}}\), and \[  egin{aligned} \overline{D_\delta} &=\{s:e_c(s)\le E_0+\delta\} =\pi_s\{z:\mathcal E(z)\le E_0+\delta\},\ 
abla e_c(D_\delta)&= \Omega_\delta:=\{u:\mathcal E(z_u)<E_0+\delta\},\ \Gamma_\delta:=t(\Omega_\delta) &=\{s+i h(s):s\in D_\delta\}. \end{aligned} 	ag{18} \] Here \(z_u\) is the unique closed tilted minimizer from the original inverse-period theorem. Thus (18) is the exact real-angle projection of that theorem's collar, with its same marking and its same energy level, not a substitute contour. **Proof.** The closed full sublevel \(K_\delta=\{z:\mathcal E(z)\le E_0+\delta\}\) is compact and lies in \(\mathcal P_c\). Whenever \(e_c(s)\le E_0+\delta\), every fiber minimizer lies in \(K_\delta\), so the fiber has its unique interior minimum. Thus the weak reduced sublevel is exactly \(\pi_s(K_\delta)\), is compact, and lies in the open set \(D_{\mathrm{reg}}\). Likewise the strict sublevel is the projection of the strict full sublevel. It is open by surjectivity of the affine projection, or by Proposition 1, and is convex by convexity of \(e_c\). It contains a neighborhood of \(s_0\). Its closure is the weak sublevel. To approximate a weak-level point, take its segment toward \(s_0\) and use convexity with \(e_c(s_0)=E_0<E_0+\delta\). Lower semicontinuity gives the opposite inclusion. On a neighborhood of the weak sublevel the function is analytic and has positive definite Hessian (15). Its gradient vanishes only at \(s_0\), by Proposition 1 and uniqueness at \(u=0\). The level \(E_0+\delta\) is therefore regular, proving smoothness of the boundary. For \(s\in D_\delta\), Proposition 1 identifies its fiber minimizer with \(z_{
abla e_c(s)}\), proving one inclusion in the second line of (18). Conversely any \(u\) in that line has an interior minimizer in \(K_\delta\); its real-angle projection lies in \(D_\delta\) and its gradient is \(u\). The third line now follows from the same inverse correspondence. \(\square\) In these coordinates the original calibrated action is particularly simple. Retain \[ \Phi_c(t)=\sum_{e=vw}\psi(t_v,t_w) + rac{i}{4\pi}\sum_{v\in S}n_vt_v^2 -i\sum_{v\in S}c_vt_v, \qquad (\Phi_c)_t=- rac{P+\pi i c}{\pi}. 	ag{19} \] The exact edge energy identity gives, on the graph, \[ \Re\Phi_c(s+i h(s))=mM_\infty- rac{e_c(s)}\pi, \qquad M_\infty=\psi(0,0). 	ag{20} \] This uses arbitrary fixed charges, as in the finite-period compactness theorem, not only unit charge. The right side is strictly concave on \(D_\delta\), has its unique maximum at \(s_0\), and has exactly the boundary loss \(\delta/\pi\). Compactness and (15) also give a constant \(\kappa_\delta>0\) such that \[ \Re\Phi_c(t^0)-\Re\Phi_c(s+i h(s)) \ge rac{\kappa_\delta}{2\pi}|s-s_0|^2 \qquad(s\in\overline{D_\delta}). 	ag{21} \] To see this, take the minimum eigenvalue of \(
abla^2e_c\) on the compact weak sublevel and integrate twice along the segment from \(s_0\), which stays in that convex sublevel. For a lower-half-plane center, sufficiently small \(\delta\) keeps the entire closed graph in that half-plane, since the full energy sublevels shrink to their unique minimizer. No height sign is asserted on the whole regular locus. ## 4. The exact height cost of a vertical connector Fix \(s\in D_{\mathrm{reg}}\). Suppose a real vector \(v\) is such that the entire segment \[ t_r=s+i(h(s)+r v),\qquad 0\le r\le1, 	ag{22} \] stays in the original positive domain with the fixed outside data and continued original logarithms. This segment hypothesis is additional: no global vertical convexity of that domain is used. At its initial point (11) gives \[ 
abla_h\Re\Phi_c= rac{\Im P+\pi c}{\pi}=0, \qquad 
abla_h^2\Re\Phi_c= rac{\Re J}{\pi}>0. 	ag{23} \] Twice integrating along (22) therefore gives the exact identity \[  oxed{\quad \Re\Phi_c(t_1)-\Re\Phi_c(t_0) = rac1\pi\int_0^1(1-r) v^{\mathsf T}\Re J(t_r)v\,dr. \quad} 	ag{24} \] The increase is strictly positive for \(v
e0\). In particular the graph is a strict minimum in the imaginary-angle directions, despite being a strict maximum along its real-angle graph near the geometric center. On a compact positive neighborhood with \(\Re J\le\Lambda I\), the cost in (24) is at most \(\Lambda|v|^2/(2\pi)\). For a point on \(\partial D_\delta\), a connector segment of this type consequently remains below the center's action by at least \[  rac{\delta-\Lambda|v|^2/2}{\pi} 	ag{25} \] when the numerator is positive. Such a common compact neighborhood and a sufficiently small uniform displacement exist around the closed graph. Formula (25) is a local budget for a short side connector. It does not assert that the displacement needed to reach the original endpoint faces or wire seams fits that budget, or that such a displacement remains in a positive chart. Compactness of finite real-period data does not change the sign in (24). There is nevertheless a valid local comparison with the constant geometric height \(h_0=h(s_0)\). On a sufficiently small compact convex real-angle neighborhood \(Q\) of \(s_0\), the graph, the constant-height slice and every segment between them stay positive. On that slice \(
abla_s^2\Re\Phi_c(s+i h_0)=-\Re J/\pi<0\), and its gradient vanishes at \(s_0\). Both endpoint chains therefore have their unique maximum at \(s_0\). Vertical convexity bounds the intervening prism by the larger endpoint action, giving a strict uniform gap on \(\partial Q\). This is the original period-coordinate application of the local Legendre-prism argument already recorded in [the general contour note, Section 5](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/general_legendre_rivin_contour.md). It is not a connection to the real-height rim or the full source faces. The real-height rim has a more definite limitation. Write \(\mathcal E(s,0)\) for the ambient energy at zero incidence angles; it need not satisfy the charged rows (2). At fixed \(s\in(-\pi,\pi)^S\), all real original angles give positive edges and real returns. Thus the zero-incidence assignment has zero incidence gradient and is the strict minimum of the ambient energy in its convex fixed-\(s\) incidence domain. The original edge energy identity consequently gives \[  egin{aligned} \Re\Phi_c(s)&=mM_\infty-\mathcal E(s,0)/\pi,\ \Re\Phi_c(s)-\Re\Phi_c(s+i h(s)) &=\{e_c(s)-\mathcal E(s,0)\}/\pi\ge0. \end{aligned} 	ag{26} \] Equality holds exactly when the graph's incidence assignment is zero, equivalently when \(h(s)=0\). Equivalently, all rows satisfy \(n_vs_v=2\pi c_v\): in that case the zero-incidence assignment is feasible and is the fiber minimum. The reality assertions here follow either directly from the square dictionary or from the canonical real positive-edge formulas. If \(h(s_0)
e0\), (26) gives \(\Re\Phi_c(s_0)>\Re\Phi_c(t^0)\). By continuity and the shrinking of \(K_\delta\) to \(z_0\), every sufficiently small projected collar has its entire real rim strictly above the target: \[ \Re\Phi_c(s)>\Re\Phi_c(t^0) \qquad(s\in\overline{D_\delta}). 	ag{27} \] Thus vertical sides all the way to \(h=0\) cannot be lower-action connectors for such collars, even if those sides happen to stay positive. This endpoint conclusion does not require their positivity. It is the fixed-real-angle energy excess already underlying [the physical-pressure theorem](research_charged_source_physical_pressure.md), applied here to the actual collar projection. It concerns the classical selected action, not the size of a signed trace remainder. ## 5. Exact remaining source task The construction supplies the explicit convex real-angle domain (8), its regular fiber-minimum locus, and the exact collar projection (18). It proves neither that every strictly feasible real angle is regular nor that the full inverse-period image has a prescribed topology. The closed fiber problem and the closed tilted problem are different; uniqueness of every tilted minimizer is not an assertion of uniqueness of every boundary fiber minimizer. For the original finite source, the relative boundary is still its angular endpoint faces and wire seams, with the retained full Hermite trace and free cardinal ends. The boundary of (18) is an interior energy level, not one of those prescribed source faces. The exact finite-period theorem also exhibits genuine trace poles on parts of the positive inverse slice; it does not place those parts in the component containing the center. Any deformation through such poles requires its actual residue/current terms. Small detours and a local action budget do not show that those terms have smaller complete source rate. Thus the result gives a canonical real-angle graph on which to try the global contour construction and an exact test of one possible connector's classical cost. It supplies no identification of the whole original relative class, no bound for the remaining joint factorial/wire source, and no nonzero quantum cycle coefficient. ## Direct sources and author readback * [Original convex variation](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_positive_filling_convex_variation.md), SHA256 `2777b2bcb149d64a79757ba64ccb16be5438cf37ce820ad50c5f532afd8fc6c0`: square energies and differential, original affine incidence rows, strict feasibility, convex extension and interior uniqueness. Complete source text read in this sequence. * [Original inverse-period descent](research_positive_period_inverse_descent.md), SHA256 `b9b5c3d61c704700e9431315cf50591c921ebeb95becdf6a52877606bdbc4565`: exact tilted image, accretive Jacobian, calibrated action, and the existing bounded star-shaped collars. Complete text reread. * [Finite real-period compactness](research_real_period_image_compactness.md), SHA256 `8ecdecc2c71e8a47a83fe60986ed618abaa926937920f376abebed779fb0c37e`: fixed-charge extension, bounded finite-period data and action calibration, and the precise original-source pole/relative-boundary limitations used in Section 5. Complete text reread. * [General Legendre contour](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/general_legendre_rivin_contour.md), SHA256 b51be11036b05fbccd586c2d0a4505559631870357cf128dd256dcc87e26970b: coverage for the already known local convexity/prism argument; no source realization is imported from that different positive triangulation chart. * [Physical charge pressure](research_charged_source_physical_pressure.md), SHA256 1e127c0842c0d6d5727a517cc66c39e73baa2846848c284d257c1ebe49679091: coverage for the same fixed-real-angle energy excess in (26). No positive-pressure estimate is identified with the original signed scalar. Only written proofs, source-text reads and metadata hashes were used. No mathematical program, numerical calculation, test or compilation was run. Frozen notes, manuscripts and public documents were unchanged.

title: Actual Casimir pair localization of the reduced closing source
text: # Actual Casimir pair localization of the reduced closing source Private written proof, 18 November 2026. The reciprocal Cartan pairs in the reduced first-jet formula have actual analytic central projectors on the original tensor module. Each pair cancels its own source residue. For a braid word the literal color turnover also reflects the two reduced block traces, including their meridian derivatives. These are finite source identities. The projectors retain the generalized Casimir eigenspaces at the root. They neither select a geometric state inside a multiplicity space nor prevent cancellation between different pairs. The complete directs are H, R and Y, pinned below. ## 1. The exact reduced blocks and the total Casimir Fix \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\). Use \(m\ge2\) actual heads with common meridian \(M\) near one, at this fixed \(q\). Write \(r=m-1\), \(x=-M/q\), \(x_0=-q^{-1}\), and \[ K_{\rm r}(M)=M^rK_0,\qquad \varepsilon=(-1)^{(N+1)r},\qquad K_0^N=\varepsilon I. \tag{1} \] Let \(\mathcal X\) be the \(N\) distinct eigenvalues of \(K_0\), with their constant occupation-space projectors \(P_\chi\) and spaces \(U_\chi\). Inversion preserves \(\mathcal X\). For an analytic family \(W(M)\) of total intertwiners, R gives the actual algebra map \[ B(W)=p_0S_m^{-1}W i_0,\qquad S_m^{-1}WS_m=\sum_{n=0}^{d}F_1^n\otimes B_n(W), \qquad [B(W),K_{\rm r}]=0. \tag{2} \] Set \[ t_\chi^W(M)=\operatorname{Tr}_{U_\chi}B(W(M)). \tag{3} \] The derivative of (3) always includes the dependence of the actual \(S_m(M)\). No cut or coupon is reset. Use the scaled lowering operator \(E\) in H. Thus \[ [E,F]=(q-q^{-1})(K-K^{-1}),\qquad \Omega=FE+qK+q^{-1}K^{-1}. \tag{4} \] The ordered total Casimir has the exact expression \[ \boxed{\quad S_m^{-1}\Omega_\Sigma S_m =F_1E_{\rm r}-(MK_{\rm r}+M^{-1}K_{\rm r}^{-1}). \quad} \tag{5} \] For completeness, H gives \(S_m^{-1}E_\Sigma S_m=E_{\rm r}+L_1b_A\), where \(b_a=MK_{\rm r}Q^{-a}-M^{-1}K_{\rm r}^{-1}\). The diagonal part of \(F_1L_1b_A\) on first occupation \(a\) is \((1-Q^a)b_a\). Adding \(q xQ^{-a}K_{\rm r}+q^{-1}x^{-1}Q^aK_{\rm r}^{-1}\) gives the negative diagonal term in (5), including the vacuum row. Consequently the spectrum of \(\Omega_\Sigma(M)\) is contained in \[ \lambda_\chi(M)=-M^m\chi-M^{-m}\chi^{-1}, \qquad \chi\in\mathcal X. \tag{6} \] Every value occurs: (5) is triangular in the first occupation, with the displayed diagonal on every row. For every polynomial \(p\), the algebra map in (2) gives \[ B(p(\Omega_\Sigma)W) =p(-MK_{\rm r}-M^{-1}K_{\rm r}^{-1})B(W). \tag{7} \] No remaining Casimir is specialized to a scalar. ## 2. Analytic paired projectors and their internal residue At \(M=1\), equality \(\lambda_\chi(1)=\lambda_\psi(1)\) is equivalent to \(\psi=\chi\) or \(\psi=\chi^{-1}\). Let \(\mathfrak o\) run over inversion orbits in \(\mathcal X\). Around the corresponding distinct number \(-\chi-\chi^{-1}\), choose disjoint small positively oriented circles \(\Gamma_{\mathfrak o}\). For \(M\) sufficiently close to one define \[ \mathcal Q_{\mathfrak o}(M) =\frac1{2\pi i}\int_{\Gamma_{\mathfrak o}} (zI-\Omega_\Sigma(M))^{-1}\,dz. \tag{8} \] All contours and neighborhoods here may depend on \(N,m\). The finite resolvent is holomorphic in \(M\) along them. Its elementary spectral integral is an idempotent, the projectors are disjoint and sum to \(I\), and they commute with all total generators and all total intertwiners. For example these assertions follow by integrating the resolvent identity; on a Jordan block the integral is \(I\) or zero according to whether its eigenvalue lies inside the contour. Thus no root Jordan directions have been removed. Triangularity in (5) applies also to the resolvent. Its constant diagonal block is \((z+MK_{\rm r}+M^{-1}K_{\rm r}^{-1})^{-1}\). It follows exactly that \[ B(\mathcal Q_{\mathfrak o})=P_{\mathfrak o} :=\sum_{\chi\in\mathfrak o}P_\chi,\qquad B(\mathcal Q_{\mathfrak o}W)=P_{\mathfrak o}B(W). \tag{9} \] In particular \(\mathcal Q_{\mathfrak o}W\) is an analytic actual intertwiner family, with its original highest cut and tail pivot. These projectors localize that source, not just an auxiliary scalar polynomial. H's exact residue equation, applied to (9), gives \[ \sum_{\chi\in\mathfrak o} (\chi-\chi^{-1})t_\chi^W(1)=0. \tag{10} \] For a two-element orbit this says \[ t_\chi^W(1)=t_{\chi^{-1}}^W(1). \tag{11} \] It holds for every analytic total intertwiner, without a braid or reflection assumption. A singleton orbit \(\chi=\pm1\) gives no additional constraint. There is also a purely polynomial proof of (10). Apply H's residue to \(p(\Omega_\Sigma)W\), using (7). The result is \[ \sum_{\chi\in\mathcal X} (\chi-\chi^{-1})p(-\chi-\chi^{-1})t_\chi^W(1)=0 \quad\text{for every }p. \tag{12} \] Interpolation on the distinct numbers indexed by \(\mathfrak o\) isolates one orbit. Formula (8) adds the actual holomorphic projector through the collision, which polynomial interpolation only at \(M=1\) would not by itself specify. ## 3. Literal turnover of the reduced braid traces For this section \(W=W_\beta\) is the actual unmarked same-color braid word, with its common crossing scalars. On one balanced head put \[ C(M)w_a=c_a(M)w_{d-a},\qquad c_a(M)=\prod_{j=1}^a\frac{MQ^j-M^{-1}}{1-Q^j}, \qquad c_0=1. \tag{13} \] The map goes from the head at \(M^{-1}\) to the head at \(M\) with its Chevalley action. It is holomorphic and invertible near one: \(c_a(1)=(-1)^a\). Directly from the literal arrows, \[ \begin{split} C(M)E(M^{-1})&=F(M)C(M),\\ C(M)F(M^{-1})&=E(M)C(M),\\ C(M)K(M^{-1})&=K(M)^{-1}C(M). \end{split} \tag{14} \] For instance the consecutive ratio in (13) is \((MQ^a-M^{-1})/(1-Q^a)\); substitution verifies both nonzero arrows. The forced extreme arrows also match. With the branch \(\alpha=d+\log M/\log q\), the weight operator is sent to its negative, since the reflected color has \(\alpha'=2d-\alpha\). The Chevalley map \(E\leftrightarrow F\), \(K\leftrightarrow K^{-1}\) reverses the coproduct order and fixes the Casimir (4). Let \(\mathsf J\) reverse the \(m\) tensor factors, and put \(\mathscr C(M)=C(M)^{\otimes m}\mathsf J\). The actual universal crossing in Y has its Cartan factor unchanged by changing both weight signs; its nilpotent term \(E^n\otimes F^n\) becomes \(F^n\otimes E^n\) with the same coefficient. Tensor reversal restores the checked crossing. This proves, for both signs, \[ \begin{split} \mathscr C(M)W_{\beta^{\rm rev}}(M^{-1}) \mathscr C(M)^{-1}&=W_\beta(M),\\ \mathscr C(M)\Omega_\Sigma(M^{-1}) \mathscr C(M)^{-1}&=\Omega_\Sigma(M), \end{split} \tag{15} \] where \(\beta^{\rm rev}\) replaces each \(\sigma_i^{\pm1}\) by \(\sigma_{m-i}^{\pm1}\), without reversing the order of the word. This is a finite matrix identity, not ordinary symmetric-power covariance. For explicit scalar bookkeeping, the full common crossing factor is \(q^{\alpha^2/2}\). The full Cartan operator is \(q^{H_1H_2/2}\), so (15) retains that factor rather than stripping it. The zero-framing twist \[ \theta(M)=q^{(\alpha^2-2d\alpha)/2} \tag{16} \] obeys \(\theta(M^{-1})=\theta(M)\). The original modified-dimension line \(\eta_N/D_N(M)\) is likewise reciprocal. Thus their prescribed external products introduce no missing multiplier in the stated unmarked turnover. Any other external line remains explicit. To extract reduced traces, first take generic \(M\) where the values (6) are distinct, and let \(\Pi_\chi(M)\) be the individual total-Casimir spectral projector. From (5) and (2), every first occupation diagonal block of \(S_m^{-1}\Pi_\chi W S_m\) is \(P_\chi B(W)\). Positive powers of \(F_1\) cannot return to that diagonal. Therefore \[ \operatorname{Tr}_{\rm full}(\Pi_\chi W) =N\,t_\chi^W(M). \tag{17} \] This auxiliary full trace computes a reduced block trace; it does not replace the highest-cut pivotal source by an ordinary trace. Since \(\lambda_{\chi^{-1}}(M^{-1})=\lambda_\chi(M)\), (15)--(17) imply \[ t_\chi^{W_\beta}(M) =t_{\chi^{-1}}^{W_{\beta^{\rm rev}}}(M^{-1}). \tag{18} \] The Artin half twist \(\Delta_m\) conjugates \(\sigma_i\) to \(\sigma_{m-i}\). Its usual triangular word verifies this using the braid relations. Hence \(\beta^{\rm rev}=\Delta_m\beta\Delta_m^{-1}\). R's algebra map sends this to conjugation by the invertible \(B(W_{\Delta_m})\), which commutes with each \(P_\chi\). The block traces are unchanged. All \(t_\chi\) are holomorphic through one, so (18) extends to the whole local germ and becomes \[ \boxed{\qquad t_\chi^{W_\beta}(M)=t_{\chi^{-1}}^{W_\beta}(M^{-1}). \qquad} \tag{19} \] In particular \[ t_\chi(1)=t_{\chi^{-1}}(1),\qquad t_\chi'(1)=-t_{\chi^{-1}}'(1). \tag{20} \] A singleton \(\chi=\pm1\) has \(t_\chi'(1)=0\). No root-only formula was differentiated: (19) is an equality of the actual fixed-\(q\) meridian germs. ## 4. The original closing row on one pair Define the actual localized source by \[ \Phi_{\mathfrak o}(M) =\Phi_0(\mathcal Q_{\mathfrak o}(M)W(M)). \tag{21} \] It sums exactly to the original source. H gives on a punctured meridian disk \[ \Phi_{\mathfrak o}(M) =\frac{D_N(M)} {\varepsilon(M^{mN}-M^{-mN})} \sum_{\chi\in\mathfrak o} (M^m\chi-M^{-m}\chi^{-1})t_\chi(M). \tag{22} \] Its removable value is the corresponding portion of H's first-jet row: \[ \Phi_{\mathfrak o}(1) =\frac1{2\varepsilon}\sum_{\chi\in\mathfrak o} (\chi+\chi^{-1})t_\chi(1) +\frac1{2\varepsilon m}\sum_{\chi\in\mathfrak o} (\chi-\chi^{-1})t_\chi'(1). \tag{23} \] For an actual braid and a two-element orbit, (20) reduces this to \[ \boxed{\quad \Phi_{\{\chi,\chi^{-1}\}}(1) =\frac{\chi+\chi^{-1}}{\varepsilon}t_\chi(1) +\frac{\chi-\chi^{-1}}{\varepsilon m}t_\chi'(1). \quad} \tag{24} \] A singleton is counted only once and contributes \(\chi t_\chi(1)/\varepsilon\). The exact normal coefficient and the derivative of the entire reduced word have both been retained. There is a useful elementary insertion consequence. If \(a(M)\) is a holomorphic scalar, then \[ \Phi_0(a\,\mathcal Q_{\mathfrak o}W)(1) =a(1)\Phi_{\mathfrak o}(1). \tag{25} \] In the first-jet calculation the extra term would be \(a'(1)\sum_{\chi\in\mathfrak o} (\chi-\chi^{-1})t_\chi(1)/(2\varepsilon m)\); it vanishes by the internal residue (10). This does not say that an arbitrary short tangle acts as a scalar on this multiplicity space. ## 5. Exact scope of the localization The weights group total occupations modulo \(N\). If \(k=\sum a_j\), then \(\chi_k=x_0^rQ^{-k}\); complementing every occupation gives \(\chi_{rd-k}=\chi_k^{-1}\). Nevertheless (19) is a trace identity on the whole \(U_\chi\), not an asserted equality separately for each integer degree \(k\). Nor does the actual turnover become simple occupation complementation after the triangular reduction. For inserted coupons, literal conjugation by \(\mathscr C(M)\) still gives their exact turnover, with its meridian dependence. To identify the result with the same unmarked braid in (19), those coupons would also need the corresponding covariance. Nonintertwining marks retain their original Ward defects and are not put into H's homogeneous first-jet formula by definition. The finite projectors in (8) need not be uniformly bounded as \(N\) grows. They retain whole generalized Casimir blocks, not a geometric line within them. All actual \(\chi\)'s lie on the unit circle; these identities alone do not continue a physical weight to an off-circle loxodromic eigenvalue. Even different internally regular pair contributions can cancel in their final sum. For instance the identity has \(t_\chi= \dim U_\chi\), derivative zero, and its complete pivotal source is zero. No positivity or nonzero geometric coefficient is inferred from (24). The result is an exact source-compatible finite localizer and an actual sector turnover, with the highest cut, pivotal line, root Jordan data and first meridian normal preserved. Quantum normals and ordinary-color closed jets still require their whole original adapters. ## Complete proof-source pins * H: notes/research_scalar_prefix_kernel_and_first_meridian_jet.md, SHA256 d7d82848a1b3f50709352905bafcc7ddfee36f41e434bf5de4663b4b6181dc9e. * R: notes/research_actual_reduced_braid_source.md, SHA256 9a472ef27b08305a519ff1f24b6d2b909e63a0acbdc49b3a29e001c52a2f2243. * Y: notes/actual_weyl_descent.md, SHA256 cf3add0dd88bcf413e04a595bfa52198b3d1a96c123ae6e356c994510f7093c4. title: The actual reduced first jet in one hybrid spin polarization
text:
# The actual reduced first jet in one hybrid spin polarization Private written proof, 19 November 2026. Both Cartan terms of the actual reduced pointed source have one and the same finite spin-coherent integrand. Their difference is carried by explicit rational scalar densities at one interface. This remains exact with arbitrary cyclic diagonal basis frames, including physical and factorial choices on different heads. The whole meridian pole, its specified integrated residue, and its first finite part are retained. The scalar first-normal density is a uniform unit on compact complex charts whose total spin occupation is nonreal. This supplies a source dual in the same polarization as hybrid spin kernels. It does not estimate the angular period or its geometric relative-cycle coefficient. The finite spin resolution is existing coverage in compact_coherent_source_period.md. The beta normalization and rotation used here are proved directly. The complete proof directs are R and G, pinned at the end. ## 1. Exact cyclic frames and the finite spin resolution Fix \(N\ge3\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\), \(m\ge2\), and \(r=m-1\). Put \[ x_0=-q^{-1},\qquad \varepsilon=(-1)^{(N+1)r}, \qquad M=e^\mu . 	ag{1} \] The quantum parameter is fixed when taking meridian derivatives. Let \(W(M)\) be the actual braid family, including its prescribed crossing and framing scalars, and let \[ B(M)=\mathcal B_m(W(M))=A_L(M)\cdots A_1(M), \qquad L\ge1 . 	ag{2} \] Use an identity factor for an empty word. R supplies the actual reduced generators and the source functional. Choose invertible diagonal frames \(D_\ell(M)\) on the remaining tensor, with \(D_L=D_0\), analytic on the meridian domain under discussion. They may depend on \(N\). Set \[ T_\ell=D_\ell^{-1}A_\ell D_{\ell-1}, \qquad T_L\cdots T_1=D_0^{-1}BD_0 . 	ag{3} \] Tensor products of \(G_F\) and identity frames are included. No condition-number estimate for these frames is part of the present theorem. For any finite matrix \(T\) on the \(r\) heads define \[ K_T(z,w)=\sum_{a,b\in\{0,\ldots,d\}^r} z^a T_{ab} inom db\,w^b , \qquad  inom db=\prod_{j=1}^r inom d{b_j}. 	ag{4} \] On one complex coordinate use the probability measure \[ d
u_N(u)= rac N\pi(1+|u|^2)^{-N-1}\,d^2u . 	ag{5} \] Angular integration and the beta integral give \[ \int u^a ar u^{\,b}\,d
u_N(u) = rac{\delta_{ab}}{ inom da}. 	ag{6} \] For \(a=b\), the radial integral is \(N\int_0^\infty v^a(1+v)^{-N-1}dv\). Integration by parts \(a\) times, followed by the elementary integral of \((1+v)^{-N-1+a}\), gives \(a!(N-1-a)!/(N-1)!\), proving (6) for every physical \(0\le a\le d\), including both endpoints. Consequently the exact identity kernel is \(\prod_j(1+z_jw_j)^d\), and (6) proves composition and trace by multiplication of finite sums. In particular define the one common closed integrand \[ \mathcal P_N(\mu;\mathbf u)= K_{T_L}(u_0, ar u_{L-1})\cdots K_{T_1}(u_1, ar u_0),\qquad d oldsymbol
u_N=\prod_{\ell=0}^{L-1} \prod_{j=1}^r d
u_N(u_{\ell,j}). 	ag{7} \] For \(L=1\) use the single diagonal kernel. Then \[ \int\mathcal P_N\,d oldsymbol
u_N =\operatorname{Tr}B . 	ag{8} \] The domains can be regarded as compact products of spheres. In the affine formula, each interface has degree at most \(d\) in \(u\) and in \( ar u\); its radial density is therefore \(O(v^{-2})\,dv\) at infinity. All integrals are absolutely convergent. There are no states outside the original finite box. If a frame moves with \(M\), differentiate the actual kernels (3). The frame connection terms cancel in the full integrated cyclic product, since its product is \(D_0^{-1}BD_0\). They are not discarded from a pointwise integrand or from a restricted integration window. ## 2. A beta rotation puts each Cartan in the density For \(s=Q\) or \(Q^{-1}\), put \[ R_s(v)= \left( rac{1+v}{1+s v}ight)^{N+1}. 	ag{9} \] On the original real sphere \(v=|u|^2\ge0\). Its denominator does not vanish for \(N\ge3\). The weighted beta moment is exactly \[ \int R_s(|u|^2)u^a ar u^{\,b}\,d
u_N(u) = rac{\delta_{ab}s^{-a-1}}{ inom da}. 	ag{10} \] Indeed the diagonal radial integral becomes \(N\int_0^\infty v^a(1+s v)^{-N-1}dv\). Make the substitution \(z=sv\). Its factor is \(s^{-a-1}\). The ray of \(z\) can be rotated back to the positive real ray: the intervening sector has angle \(2\pi/N<\pi\), and never contains the only pole \(z=-1\). On an outer circular arc of radius \(R>2\), its integral is \(O(R^{a-N})=O(R^{-1})\), even for \(a=d\). The inner arc is \(O(ho^{a+1})\). Both vanish. This proves (10) with its orientation and scalar, without an infinite occupation series. Insert these weights at the interface \(u_0\) only, and write \(v_j=|u_{0,j}|^2\). Define \[  egin{split} \mathcal A_N(v)&=x_0^{-r}\prod_{j=1}^rR_Q(v_j),\ \mathcal B_N(v)&=x_0^{r}\prod_{j=1}^rR_{Q^{-1}}(v_j). \end{split} 	ag{11} \] All other interfaces retain their original measure. The factors in (10) are \(Q^{-|a|-r}\) and \(Q^{|a|+r}\). Since \(x_0^2=Q^{-1}\), \[ x_0^{-r}Q^{-r}=x_0^r,\qquad x_0^rQ^r=x_0^{-r}. 	ag{12} \] Thus finite composition gives the exact identities \[  egin{split} \int\mathcal A_N\mathcal P_N\,d oldsymbol
u_N &=\operatorname{Tr}(K_0B(e^\mu)),\ \int\mathcal B_N\mathcal P_N\,d oldsymbol
u_N &=\operatorname{Tr}(K_0^{-1}B(e^\mu)). \end{split} 	ag{13} \] Here \(K_0\) is the complete remaining Cartan at \(M=1\), with eigenvalues \(x_0^rQ^{-|a|}\). It commutes with every diagonal \(D_0\), so no frame is left over in (13). The same literal integrand \(\mathcal P_N\) occurs in both lines. ## 3. The whole meridian and its true first jet The original source is \[ \Phi_N(\mu)=\operatorname{Tr}_{m full}  igl((P_0\otimes K_{m r}(e^\mu)^{1-N})W(e^\mu) igr). 	ag{14} \] R proves its meromorphic reduced expression \[ \Phi_N(\mu)=\operatorname{Tr}_{m r} \left( rac{D_N(e^\mu)} {D_N(e^\mu K_{m r}(e^\mu))}B(e^\mu)ight), \quad D_N(z)= rac{z^N-z^{-N}}{z-z^{-1}}. 	ag{15} \] The original finite left side is analytic at zero. The actual remaining Cartan is \(e^{r\mu}K_0\), and \(K_0^N=\varepsilon I\) on the finite tensor. This is a matrix statement on physical integer indices, not an off-grid clock substitution. Combining (13) with (15) gives \[  oxed{\quad \Phi_N(\mu)= \int\mathcal W_N(v,\mu)\mathcal P_N(\mu)\, d oldsymbol
u_N, \qquad \mathcal W_N=  rac{D_N(e^\mu) (e^{m\mu}\mathcal A_N-e^{-m\mu}\mathcal B_N)} {2\varepsilon\sinh(mN\mu)} . \quad} 	ag{16} \] It holds first away from the displayed poles and then by the original analytic continuation. The self-Cartan cases are included in this whole identity. Set \[ \mathfrak c_N= rac{\mathcal A_N+\mathcal B_N}{2\varepsilon}, \qquad \mathfrak d_N= rac{\mathcal A_N-\mathcal B_N}{2\varepsilon m}. 	ag{17} \] Since \(D_N(e^\mu)=\sinh(N\mu)/\sinh\mu\) is even and has value \(N\) at zero, \[ \mathcal W_N=\mathfrak d_N/\mu+ \mathfrak c_N+O(\mu). 	ag{18} \] The rational factors (9) are smooth on the original compact cycle. Finite matrices and compactness justify integration of this Laurent expansion and its fixed meridian derivatives. Analyticity of (14) yields the specified residue identity \[ \int\mathfrak d_N\mathcal P_N(0)\, d oldsymbol
u_N=0. 	ag{19} \] It is an integrated source identity, not a pointwise cancellation. On \(|\mu|<c/N\), \(0<c<\pi/m\), provided this collar lies in the chosen analytic word and frame domain, the density \[ \mathcal W_N(v,\mu)\mathcal P_N(\mu) -\mu^{-1}\mathfrak d_N(v)\mathcal P_N(0) 	ag{20} \] has a removable singularity at zero and no other meridian pole. By (19) its integral is still the original source. The finite part is exactly \[  oxed{\quad \Phi_N(0)=\int\left\{ \mathfrak c_N\mathcal P_N(0) +\mathfrak d_N\partial_\mu\mathcal P_N(0) ight\}d oldsymbol
u_N . \quad} 	ag{21} \] The derivative includes the whole actual reduced word, all scalars, and every moving-frame connection. At \(M=1\), it equals the \(M\) derivative. The frozen Cartan is not differentiated a second time; its required meridian dependence is already in \(e^{\pm m\mu}\) in (16). ## 4. The scalar normal is a unit at nonreal total spin moment Complexify the selected interface to independent \(z_j,w_j\), and put \[ v_j=z_jw_j,\qquad t_j= rac{v_j}{1+v_j}, \qquad T=\sum_{j=1}^r t_j,\qquad c_0=2\pi i . 	ag{22} \] Fix a compact affine chart with \(1+v_j
e0\). The \(t_j\)'s are bounded there. For sufficiently large \(N\), all \(1+Q^{\pm1}v_j\) are nonzero, and the logarithm near one gives, uniformly with all fixed holomorphic derivatives, \[  egin{split} \mathcal A_N&=(-1)^r e^{-c_0T}(1+O(N^{-1})),\ \mathcal B_N&=(-1)^r e^{c_0T}(1+O(N^{-1})),\ \mathfrak d_N &=- rac{i(-1)^r}{\varepsilon m} \sin(2\pi T)+O(N^{-1}). \end{split} 	ag{23} \] For example \(R_Q=(1+(Q-1)t)^{-N-1}\); expansion of this exact expression proves the first line, including the actual \(N+1\) and \(x_0^{-r}\). Their finite half shifts remain in (11), not in a reset amplitude. If \(|\Im T|\ge\delta>0\) on that compact set, then \[ |\sin(2\pi T)|\ge\sinh(2\pi\delta). 	ag{24} \] Equations (23)--(24) give a uniform positive lower bound on \(|\mathfrak d_N|\) for all sufficiently large \(N\). Its reciprocal and all fixed derivatives are uniformly bounded on smaller compact buffers. Thus it is an actual scalar normal unit on this complex spin chart, not merely a nonzero principal symbol. The common moment here is independent of the diagonal frames. Indeed their Cartan kernel is unchanged, and its exact normalized one-head symbol is \[ x_0\left( rac{1+Q^{-1}zw}{1+zw}ight)^d =-e^{-c_0t}(1+O(N^{-1})). 	ag{25} \] This identifies the corresponding principal clock without taking any off-grid \(N\)-th power of it. G's resolved total-lowering-zero map has \(K_\Sigma=x_{m cl}K_{m r}\). At a complete loxodromic geometric total, \(|K_{m r}|
e1\); on a spin chart actually matched to that map, \(K_{m r}=(-1)^r e^{-c_0T}\) therefore implies \(\Im T
e0\). The scalar unit applies whenever that chart matching and its nonincidence conditions have been supplied. It is not a new assertion of whole-word kernel coverage. ## 5. Scope of the exact adapter All formulas use one finite spin resolution and one cyclic list of actual frames. In particular hybrid choices of physical and factorial heads need no asymptotic passage through a Bargmann kernel to use (16) or (21). Every finite occupation cap is already present in (4). The rotated incidence divisors \(1+Q^{\pm1}z_jw_j=0\) of (11) remain part of the exact complex density. Although they avoid each fixed compact nonincident chart for large \(N\), their possible global contour currents are not discarded. The beta rotation proves the original cycle identity; it does not transport an arbitrary chosen geometric window through these divisors. Likewise (19) need not hold on an angular subchain. Its restricted pole coefficient and all frame-connection currents must then be retained. A separately prescribed scalar line multiplies the whole original expression, before its required finite part or derivative. No rate or nonvanishing is assigned to that line here. The conclusion is an exact common-spin source dual and a local scalar normal unit. Neither the angular pairing, its geometric coefficient, nor the full original-source lower bound is proved by this adapter. ## Complete proof-source pins * R: notes/research_actual_reduced_braid_source.md, 330 lines, SHA256 9a472ef27b08305a519ff1f24b6d2b909e63a0acbdc49b3a29e001c52a2f2243. * G: notes/research_actual_reduced_braid_critical_scheme.md, 564 lines, SHA256 ddddcd9bf75f35afdf3e5de0c03323acee2c66e624db36142c2344ef729a977a. Both complete directs were freshly read nontruncated in the active author sequence and retained unchanged. Every used implication was checked. title: A finite donor coherent sum for the reduced Euler star
text:
# A finite donor coherent sum for the reduced Euler star Private written proof, 18 November 2026. The actual lower-donor kernel can be summed over its integer donor index, using a specified finite factorial coherent vector. At the physical imaginary quantum parameter this gives a nonzero coherent Gaussian kernel on the \(O(\sqrt N)\) coherent scale. The linear characteristic may vanish. No interpolation in a complex donor occupation is used. The donor truncation has a superexponentially small relative error. The recipient projectors have such an error only under an explicit macroscopic upper margin. They remain exact outside that margin. A nonzero local matrix kernel is not a nonzero closed source coefficient. The sole complete proof direct is W, the exact Euler-star word kernel. All additional graph, generating-function, and tail arguments are proved here. ## 1. The specified finite coherent input Retain W's notation \[ d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\quad h=2\pi i/N,\quad x=-M/q,\quad f_a=(Q;Q)_a,\quad G_Fw_a=f_aw_a, 	ag{1} \] with \(N\ge2\), \(M
e0\), and \(r\ge2\) heads. Let \(\mathcal G=G_F^{\otimes r}\), and fix the actual integer recipient input \(b=(b_2,\ldots,b_r)\), \(0\le b_j\le d\). On the donor use the exact finite vector \[ \psi_N(\lambda) =G_F\sum_{a=0}^d rac{\lambda^a}{a!}w_a. 	ag{2} \] The recipient inputs in this same presentation are \(G_Fw_{b_j}\); if their original basis is used instead, the corresponding nonzero \(f_{b_j}\) factors must be retained. Let \(\Lambda_z\) evaluate normalized basis monomials \(w_{a_0}\otimes w_{a_2}\otimes\cdots\) at \(z_0^{a_0}\prod_{j=2}^rz_j^{a_j}\). The exact matrix kernel is \[ \Lambda_z\mathcal G^{-1}S_r^{\pm1} \left(\psi_N(\lambda)\otimes  igotimes_{j=2}^rG_Fw_{b_j}ight) =\left(\prod_{j=2}^rz_j^{b_j}ight) \mathcal C_{N,b}^\pm(\lambda,z). 	ag{3} \] Here W's word polynomial \(K_a^\pm\) gives \[ \mathcal C_{N,b}^\pm =P_b\sum_{a=0}^d rac{\lambda^a}{a!}K_a^\pm. 	ag{4} \] The exact operator \(P_b\) deletes a recipient monomial with transfer degree \(n_j>d-b_j\). The factor outside \(\mathcal C\) in (3) is not discarded. Differentiating (3) \(a\) times in \(\lambda\) at zero recovers the corresponding actual donor column, with its specified factorial basis factors. Thus (2)--(4) are a finite kernel presentation, not a replacement for the original cut or a choice of a new preferred source vector. ## 2. The word extension and its entire generating function For the ordered alphabet \(\mathcal J=\{0,2,\ldots,r\}\), put \[ c_0=z_0,\qquad c_j=x^{-(j-1)}Q^{\sum_{2\le i<j}b_i}z_j\quad(j
e0). 	ag{5} \] For the positive sign use \(c_j^+=c_j\). For the negative sign use \(c_0^-=c_0\), \(c_j^-=-c_j\) for \(j
e0\). The pair energies are \[ B_+(j,k)= oldsymbol1_{\{j>k\}},\qquad B_-(j,k)= oldsymbol1_{\{j>k\}} + oldsymbol1_{\{j
e0,\ k
e0\}}. 	ag{6} \] Each is a real integer between zero and two. W proves, for every physical \(0\le a\le d\), \[ K_a^\pm= \sum_{\ell\in\mathcal J^a}\prod_{i=1}^ac_{\ell_i}^\pm \exp\!\left(h\sum_{i<j}B_\pm(\ell_i,\ell_j)ight). 	ag{7} \] Use the right side to define auxiliary polynomials also for \(a>d\). These are bookkeeping polynomials, not extra physical head states or values of a factorial ratio at its root zero. We prove the analytic statement for one sign, writing \(c,B\). Set \[ C_0=\sum_j|c_j|,\qquad H=\sum_jc_j,\qquad A=\sum_{j,k}c_jc_kB(j,k). 	ag{8} \] At the physical imaginary \(h\), every exponential in (7) has modulus one. Hence \[ |K_a|\le C_0^a. 	ag{9} \] In particular \[ \mathcal E_h(\lambda;c) =\sum_{a=0}^\infty rac{\lambda^a}{a!}K_a 	ag{10} \] is entire in \(\lambda\). No condition \(H
e0\) is needed. We will compare the actual finite polynomial (4) to (10) with its exact tails retained. ## 3. A connected-graph identity with unit extra-edge factors For a fixed set of \(s\) ordered sites and fixed labels \(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_s\), write \[ u_{ij}=e^{hB(\ell_i,\ell_j)}-1,\qquad i<j,\qquad v=\max_{j,k}|e^{hB(j,k)}-1|\le2|h|. 	ag{11} \] Let \(w_s\) be the sum over all connected graphs on these sites of \(\prod_{\{i,j\}	ext{ edge}}u_{ij}\), followed by the finite label sum weighted by \(\prod_i c_{\ell_i}\). For \(s=1\), define \(w_1=H\). We need a bound that keeps the cancellations among extra edges. Root each connected graph at site \(1\), and let its levels be the graph distances from that root. For each other vertex select its smallest-labeled neighbor in the preceding level as parent. This gives a rooted tree \(T\). Define \(R(T)\) by adjoining to \(T\): * every edge between two vertices in the same level; * an edge between adjacent levels when its vertex in the preceding level has label at least that of the selected parent of the later-level vertex. Every graph producing \(T\) lies between \(T\) and \(R(T)\). Conversely every graph in that interval has exactly these levels and selected parents. Indeed an added edge changes level by at most one, so it cannot shorten a path to the root below the tree level; tree paths attain that level. The parent condition preserves the smallest preceding-level neighbor. These intervals therefore partition the connected graphs, without overlap. For arbitrary complex edge variables this proves the exact polynomial identity \[ \sum_{	ext{connected graphs }G}\prod_{e\in G}u_e =\sum_{	ext{rooted trees }T} \left(\prod_{e\in T}u_eight) \left(\prod_{e\in R(T)\setminus T}(1+u_e)ight). 	ag{12} \] There is no inequality or positivity assumption in (12). At imaginary \(h\), each extra-edge factor has modulus one. The number of rooted trees is at most \(s^{s-1}\), by assigning a parent to each non-root vertex. Taking absolute values only after (12), and then summing labels, gives \[ |w_s|\le C_0^s s^{s-1}v^{s-1} \qquad(s\ge2). 	ag{13} \] This is where the physical ray is used. Bounding each extra edge by \(1+|u_e|\) before summation would not give the convergent estimate needed below. ## 4. Exact exponential generating function and its logarithm Expand the pair factors in (7) into graphs and group every graph into its connected components. A component on an ordered subset \(S\) has weight \(w_{|S|}\). This assertion uses order: the increasing relabeling \(S	o\{1,\ldots,|S|\}\) preserves which endpoint of each pair comes first. The energies (6) are not replaced by symmetric label functions. If a partition has \(m_s\) components of size \(s\), the number of such partitions is \(a!/\prod_s((s!)^{m_s}m_s!)\). Consequently, as formal power series at \(\lambda=0\), \[ \sum_{a\ge0} rac{\lambda^a}{a!}K_a =\exp\left(\sum_{s\ge1}  rac{\lambda^s}{s!}w_sight). 	ag{14} \] This also proves the normalization of the singleton term: it is \(\lambda H\), not a scalar-normalized replacement. The connected series converges whenever \[ 	heta=e|\lambda|C_0v<1. 	ag{15} \] For example \(s^{s-1}/s!\le e^s\), obtained from the elementary integral lower bound for \(\log(s!)\), makes its absolute tail a geometric series. Both sides of (14) are analytic there and have identical Taylor series, so equality holds. In particular \(\mathcal E_h
e0\) on (15), and its holomorphic logarithm with value zero at \(\lambda=0\) is exactly the connected series. This conclusion holds even at \(H=0\). The two-site term is \[ w_2=\sum_{j,k}c_jc_k(e^{hB(j,k)}-1). 	ag{16} \] Taylor's formula along the imaginary segment gives \[ |w_2-hA|\le2C_0^2|h|^2. 	ag{17} \] For \(	heta\le1/2\), (13) bounds the remaining terms by \[ \sum_{s\ge3} rac{|\lambda|^s}{s!}|w_s| \le 2e^3|\lambda|^3C_0^3v^2. 	ag{18} \] Thus the exact connected logarithm satisfies \[  oxed{\quad \log\mathcal E_h =\lambda H+ rac{h\lambda^2}{2}A +O_{C_0} igl((|\lambda|^2+|\lambda|^3)|h|^2 igr). \quad} 	ag{19} \] For any fixed \(C\) and \(|\lambda|\le C\sqrt N\), (15) holds for all sufficiently large \(N\) on compact bounded coefficient sets, and \[ \mathcal E_h =\exp\left(\lambda H+ rac{h\lambda^2}{2}Aight) (1+O(N^{-1/2})). 	ag{20} \] All actual \(N\)-dependent coefficients in (5), including the half-shifts in \(x=-M/q\), remain in \(H,A\). No principal substitution has removed them. ## 5. Relative control of the finite donor and recipient tails Fix a compact coefficient neighborhood with \(C_0\le C_*\), and \(|\lambda|\le C\sqrt N\). Put \(D_*=|\lambda|C_*\). For an integer \(L\ge2D_*\), successive terms give \[ \sum_{a=L}^\infty rac{D_*^a}{a!} \le 2 rac{D_*^L}{L!} \le2\left( rac{eD_*}{L}ight)^L. 	ag{21} \] The factorial bound follows by integrating \(\log t\); no asymptotic factorial formula is needed. Let the finite unprojected donor polynomial be \[ \mathcal E_{N}^{m fin} =\sum_{a=0}^d rac{\lambda^a}{a!}K_a. 	ag{22} \] Equations (9),(21), with \(L=N\), show that its difference from (10) is at most \[ \exp\left(-	frac12N\log N+O(N)ight). 	ag{23} \] On the other hand the exponential on the right of (20) has modulus at least \(e^{-C_1\sqrt N-C_2}\), uniformly. Indeed \(|H|\le C_*\) and \(|A|\le2C_*^2\). Thus (23) is also a superexponentially small relative error. The finite unprojected donor kernel is nonzero for all sufficiently large \(N\), with the same estimate (20). For the recipient projector set \[ L_b=1+\min_{j\ge2}(d-b_j) =N-\max_{j\ge2}b_j. 	ag{24} \] A word deleted by \(P_b\) has at least \(L_b\) nonzero letters of some recipient type, hence has length at least \(L_b\). Taking absolute values of just those deleted monomials and using (9) bounds the change in (22) by the left side of (21) with \(L=L_b\). If the actual input satisfies \[ d-\max_{j\ge2}b_j\ge\eta N, \qquad \eta>0\ 	ext{fixed}, 	ag{25} \] this error is at most \[ \exp\left(-	frac\eta2N\log N+O(N)ight). 	ag{26} \] It is again superexponentially small relative to the nonzero factor in (20). Consequently the actual factored kernel (4), under (25), satisfies for either sign \[  oxed{\quad \mathcal C_{N,b}^\pm =\exp\left(\lambda H_\pm+  rac{h\lambda^2}{2}A_\pmight) (1+O(N^{-1/2})), \qquad |\lambda|\le C\sqrt N . \quad} 	ag{27} \] It is nonzero for all sufficiently large \(N\), including when \(H_\pm=0\). The full matrix kernel has the additional exact monomial in (3); its nonvanishing also requires that monomial to be nonzero. At \(\lambda=0\), the factored kernel is exactly one. All these bounds hold on slightly larger complex coefficient neighborhoods with the same bound \(C_*\). Cauchy estimates therefore give the same \(O(N^{-1/2})\) bound for every fixed derivative of the normalized error in the coherent variables and in \(M\) at fixed \(q\). This includes derivatives in the scaled donor variable \(	au=\lambda/\sqrt N\) on fixed compact sets. The integer occupations \(b_j\), and hence their projector thresholds, remain fixed when taking those derivatives. ## 6. What the coherent sum transports The donor index was summed with every coefficient of the specified finite vector (2). It was not analytically continued to a complex value. Formula (7) beyond \(a=d\) was used only to prove the tail estimate; it is not a new infinite head. The unitary extra-edge estimate in (12)--(13) uses imaginary \(h\). No zero-free neighborhood in a complex quantum parameter or shortcut for closed quantum normals follows. The actual meridian dependence in (1),(5) remains holomorphic and is included in the stated fixed-\(q\) derivative estimates. If the upper margin (25) fails, the exact formula (4) still holds, but this proof does not approximate its projected value by (20). In particular upper recipient sectors may change or cancel the kernel. The original source can require such sectors; they are not discarded by their absence from the estimate. Nor does (27) estimate a donor sector near \(a=d\) before the coherent sum. The original recipient clocks are \(Q^{b_j}\). Holomorphic coefficient parameters in (5) do not prove an interpolation in complex recipient occupations, or produce a physical integer sequence approaching arbitrary complex clocks. The resolved principal identification in W remains a separate statement about the correspondence. Finally every factorial basis change, neighboring operator, Cartan factor, pivot, scalar line and closing first-jet functional must remain in a full word. The map (3) retains them by transporting the source and dual along with the matrix. A local nonzero kernel, even one proved by an exact complex-weighted sum, does not imply noncancellation of their subsequent contraction or a geometric cycle coefficient. ## Coverage and complete proof source The graph interval partition is a standard cluster-expansion technique; the primary abstract of [Fernández--Procacci](https://arxiv.org/abs/math-ph/0605041) was checked for coverage of the Penrose tree identity. No external theorem is used in the proof above. The source-specific result is the exact Euler-star coherent sum with its original finite truncations and relative tails. * W: notes/research_reduced_euler_star_complex_word_kernel.md, SHA256 6baac1f8303d21be4a5c3f6c809795272dd51d3e0060e13843e0f25958902fdb.
