# The lower-donor Euler star as a complex word kernel Private written proof, 18 November 2026. After the actual factorial normalization, a full reduced Euler star is a finite word polynomial with an explicit inversion weight. Its inverse has one additional bounded pair interaction. On a compact chart where the ordinary linear characteristic is nonzero, an elementary connected-graph argument proves that both unprojected kernels are nonzero for a small normalized lower-donor interval. On the \(a=O(\sqrt N)\) scale it gives a relative quadratic-exponential approximation with error \(O(N^{-1/2})\), not an absolute multinomial majorant. The exact upper projectors remain. The result concerns the lower donor, not its opposite endpoint or a closed contraction. The sole complete proof direct is G, the actual reduced correspondence. All finite-word and analytic estimates are proved below. ## 1. The literal star and its capacity projectors Use \(r\ge2\) heads, donor occupation \(a\), recipient occupations \(b=(b_2,\ldots,b_r)\), and \[ d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\quad h=2\pi i/N,\quad x=-M/q,\quad f_k=\prod_{\ell=1}^k(1-Q^\ell),\quad f_0=1. 	ag{1} \] All indices initially lie in \(\{0,\ldots,d\}\), and \(M
e0\). Let \(\mathcal G=G_F^{\otimes r}\), \(G_Fw_k=f_kw_k\). G's exact positive \(S_r\) coefficient, after this conjugation, is \[  rac{f_a}{f_{a-n}\prod_{j=2}^rf_{n_j}}\, \prod_{j=2}^r x^{-(j-1)n_j}Q^{n_j\sum_{2\le i<j}b_i}, \qquad n=\sum_{j=2}^r n_j, 	ag{2} \] with \(0\le n\le a\) and \(b_j+n_j\le d\). For \(S_r^{-1}\), multiply (2) by \((-1)^nQ^{n(n-1)/2}\). No chirp is used in this note. The factorial basis has not been assumed uniformly conditioned. Identify the normalized basis with monomials in \(z_0,z_2,\ldots,z_r\), where \(0\) labels the donor. Put \[ c_0=z_0,\qquad c_j=x^{-(j-1)}Q^{\sum_{2\le i<j}b_i}z_j\quad(2\le j\le r). 	ag{3} \] Let \(\Pi_b\) delete monomials for which any recipient degree exceeds \(d\). There are polynomials \(K_a^\pm\) such that the exact finite kernels are \[ \mathcal G^{-1}S_r^{\pm1}\mathcal G \left(z_0^a\prod_{j=2}^rz_j^{b_j}ight) =\Pi_b\left[\left(\prod_{j=2}^rz_j^{b_j}ight)K_a^\pmight]. 	ag{4} \] The notation \(\Pi_b\) indicates its use on this displayed input-dependent polynomial, not a change of the upper wall. A sufficient condition for no truncation is \[ a+\max_{j\ge2}b_j\le d. 	ag{5} \] All intermediate masks are then satisfied as well: the donor decreases monotonically and each recipient only increases. Outside (5) the exact projector in (4) remains. ## 2. An exact word formula and a scalar difference recursion Order the alphabet \(\mathcal J=\{0,2,\ldots,r\}\) naturally. For a word \(\ell=(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_a)\), let \[ \operatorname{inv}(\ell)= \#\{i<j:\ell_i>\ell_j\},\qquad n(\ell)=\#\{i:\ell_i
e0\}. 	ag{6} \] Then the exact unprojected kernels are \[ K_a^+=\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal J^a} \prod_{i=1}^ac_{\ell_i}\, Q^{\operatorname{inv}(\ell)}, 	ag{7} \] \[ K_a^-=\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal J^a} (-1)^{n(\ell)}\prod_{i=1}^ac_{\ell_i}\, Q^{\operatorname{inv}(\ell)+n(\ell)(n(\ell)-1)/2}. 	ag{8} \] Both vacuum polynomials \(K_0^\pm\) are one. Here is a direct coefficient proof. For fixed letter counts \((n_0,n_2,\ldots,n_r)\) summing to \(a\), the inversion sum is \[ \sum_{	ext{words with these counts}}Q^{\operatorname{inv}} = rac{f_a}{\prod_j f_{n_j}}. 	ag{9} \] Indeed choosing the first letter \(j\) contributes \(Q^{\sum_{k<j}n_k}\). If the right side of (9) is inserted in that recursion, the required numerator identity is \[ \sum_j Q^{\sum_{k<j}n_k}(1-Q^{n_j})=1-Q^a. 	ag{10} \] It telescopes. Starting from the empty word proves (9), including zero counts. Equations (2), (7), and (8) follow with \(n_0=a-n\). For a uniform notation define \[ c_j^+=c_j,\qquad c_0^-=c_0,\quad c_j^-=-c_j\ (j
e0), \] \[ B_+(j,k)= oldsymbol1_{\{j>k\}},\qquad B_-(j,k)= oldsymbol1_{\{j>k\}} + oldsymbol1_{\{j
e0,\ k
e0\}} . 	ag{11} \] Both pair energies lie between zero and two. Let \(T_j^\pm\) replace every \(z_k\) by \(Q^{B_\pm(j,k)}z_k\), keeping the fixed input \(b\) unchanged. Choosing the first letter of a word proves the exact recursion \[ K_{a+1}^\pm =\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}c_j^\pm T_j^\pm K_a^\pm, \qquad K_0^\pm=1. 	ag{12} \] For example the positive \(j
e0\) term shifts \(z_0\) and the recipient variables with index less than \(j\) by \(Q\). Thus (12) is a scalar finite difference evolution in coherent variables. It is not an estimate obtained by replacing its complex coefficients by positive ones. ## 3. A zero-free estimate for complex normalized weights We prove a finite statement that applies to both signs. Let complex numbers \(p_j\) satisfy \[ \sum_jp_j=1,\qquad \sum_j|p_j|\le R,\qquad R\ge1, 	ag{13} \] and let \(B(j,k)\) be either pair energy in (11). With an auxiliary complex parameter \(\zeta\), define \[ Z_a(\zeta;p)= \sum_{\ell\in\mathcal J^a}\prod_i p_{\ell_i} \exp\!\left(\zeta\sum_{i<j}B(\ell_i,\ell_j)ight). 	ag{14} \] The \(p_j\)'s are held fixed when varying \(\zeta\). Put \[ \gamma= rac1{128e^4R^2}. 	ag{15} \] For \(a\ge2\), \(Z_a\) is nonzero on \(|\zeta|a\le\gamma\). It has the holomorphic logarithm normalized by \(\log Z_a(0;p)=0\), and \[ |\log Z_a(\zeta;p)|\le a\log2. 	ag{16} \] The same conclusions are immediate for \(a=0,1\), when \(Z_a=1\). We give the full zero-free proof. On an ordered subset \(\Lambda\subseteq\{1,\ldots,a\}\), write every pair factor as \[ e^{\zeta B(\ell_i,\ell_j)} =1+u_{ij}(\ell_i,\ell_j),\qquad |u_{ij}|\le v:=e^{2|\zeta|}-1. 	ag{17} \] Expanding the product gives a sum over graphs on \(\Lambda\). Group each graph into its connected components of size at least two; its isolated vertices contribute \(\sum p_j=1\). For a subset \(S\) of size \(s\ge2\), let \(w(S)\) be the sum over its connected graphs, followed by the finite label sum with weight \(\prod_{i\in S}p_{\ell_i}\). The result is exactly \[ Z_\Lambda=\sum_{\substack{\mathcal A	ext{ a family of}\ 	ext{pairwise disjoint }S\subseteq\Lambda,\ |S|\ge2}} \prod_{S\in\mathcal A}w(S). 	ag{18} \] This finite identity holds for complex weights. Every connected graph contains a spanning tree. With one vertex chosen as root, assigning a parent to every other vertex gives at most \(s^{s-1}\) rooted trees. This upper bound needs no tree-counting formula. Sum the possible extra graph edges after each tree. Together with (13), this gives \[ |w(S)|\le R^s s^{s-1}v^{s-1}(1+v)^{s(s-1)/2} \le R^s s^{s-1}v^{s-1}e^{vs^2/2}. 	ag{19} \] Overcounting graphs with several spanning trees is harmless. Under \(|\zeta|a\le\gamma\), one has \(v\le4|\zeta|\) and \(e^{vs^2/2}\le e^s\). Also \[  rac{s^{s-1}}{(s-1)!}\le e^s. 	ag{20} \] For (20), integrate \(\log t\) from \(1\) to \(s-1\) to bound \(\log((s-1)!)\) below, then use \((1+1/(s-1))^{s-1}\le e\). The case \(s=2\) is included. Consequently, for every vertex \(i\), \[  egin{split} \sum_{S
i i}|w(S)|2^{|S|-1} &\le \sum_{s=2}^a  inom{a-1}{s-1}R^ss^{s-1}(8|\zeta|)^{s-1}e^s\ &\le Re^2\sum_{s=2}^\infty (8a|\zeta|Re^2)^{s-1}< rac12 . \end{split} 	ag{21} \] The explicit constant (15) suffices: the last geometric ratio is at most \(1/(16Re^2)\), and its whole sum is less than \(1/2\). The same bound holds on every subset \(\Lambda\). We now induct on \(|\Lambda|\), proving both nonvanishing and \[ \left| rac{Z_\Lambda}{Z_{\Lambda\setminus\{i\}}}-1ight| \le rac12\quad(i\in\Lambda). 	ag{22} \] The empty and singleton cases are one. In (18), either \(i\) is isolated or belongs to its unique set \(S\). Hence \[  rac{Z_\Lambda}{Z_{\Lambda\setminus\{i\}}} =1+\sum_{\substack{S\subseteq\Lambda\i\in S,\ |S|\ge2}} w(S) rac{Z_{\Lambda\setminus S}} {Z_{\Lambda\setminus\{i\}}}. 	ag{23} \] Delete the other \(|S|-1\) vertices one at a time. The induction hypothesis bounds every inverse ratio by two, so the last quotient has modulus at most \(2^{|S|-1}\). Equation (21) proves (22), and its disk excludes zero. This induction proves the assertion for all subsets, not only for an initial segment of the ordered sites. Each ratio in (22) has the holomorphic logarithm of \(1+z\), \(|z|\le1/2\), of modulus at most \(\log2\). Multiply the ratios along any fixed sequence adding the vertices. Their logarithms sum to the logarithm normalized at \(\zeta=0\), proving (16). The construction is holomorphic also in the normalized weights on every neighborhood with the uniform bound (13). ## 4. The relative quadratic kernel Let \[ \mu=\sum_{j,k}p_jp_k B(j,k). 	ag{24} \] Differentiating the finite sum (14) at zero gives \((\log Z_a)'(0)= inom a2\mu\). Apply Cauchy's coefficient estimate to (16) on the disk of radius \(\gamma/a\). For \(|\zeta|a\le\gamma/2\), \[  oxed{\quad \log Z_a(\zeta;p) =\zeta inom a2\mu+O_R(a^3|\zeta|^2). \quad} 	ag{25} \] More explicitly the remainder is at most \(2(\log2)a^3|\zeta|^2/\gamma^2\). Indeed sum the geometric tail of the Taylor series from degree two. This proves a bound for the canonical logarithm, not a logarithm chosen separately at individual sample points. Apply this to the actual coefficients (3), with \[ H_\pm=\sum_j c_j^\pm,\qquad p_j^\pm=c_j^\pm/H_\pm. 	ag{26} \] Choose a compact coherent-variable and meridian neighborhood where \(H_\pm\) is a unit and \(\sum|p_j^\pm|\le R\) on a slightly larger neighborhood. Keep every \(N\)-dependent \(x=-M/q\) and \(Q\)-prefix factor in (3). Then exactly \[ K_a^\pm=H_\pm^a Z_a(h;p^\pm). 	ag{27} \] In particular the unprojected kernel is nonzero when \(a|h|\le\gamma\). Its normalized factor has the two-sided bound \(2^{-a}\le|Z_a|\le2^a\). For the lower-donor range \(0\le a\le C\sqrt N\), (25) gives \[ K_a^\pm =H_\pm^a \exp\!\left(h inom a2\mu_\pmight)  igl(1+O_{C,R}(N^{-1/2}) igr), 	ag{28} \] \[ \mu_+=\sum_{j>k}p_j^+p_k^+,\qquad \mu_-=\sum_{j>k}p_j^-p_k^- +\left(\sum_{j
e0}p_j^-ight)^2. 	ag{29} \] Every fixed coherent-variable and fixed-\(q\) meridian derivative of the normalized error in (28) has the same bound on the smaller compact set, by the holomorphy and uniform bounds just proved. The vacuum \(a=0\) remains one. In applying Cauchy in (25), \(\zeta\) was an auxiliary interaction variable while the actual \(p^\pm\) were held fixed. No \(N\)-dependent coefficient or half-shift has been differentiated away. Their full values remain in \(H_\pm,\mu_\pm\) in (28). ## 5. The physical characteristic at the resolved row At G's resolved row endpoint the donor has \(A_{m d}=1\), \(p_{m d}=0\), and physical \(f_{m d}
e0\). In the all-factorial polynomial model the unprojected physical lowering symbols on the outputs are \(z_0,z_2,\ldots,z_r\). G's \(S_r\) equations at \(p_{m d}=0\) give all partial \(T_j=1\), unchanged recipient clocks \(B_j\), and \[ f'_{m r,j}=f_{m r,j},\qquad f'_{m d}=f_{m d}-x_0^{-1}F_{m r}, \quad F_{m r}=\sum_{j=2}^r x_0^{-(j-2)}\left(\prod_{2\le i<j}B_iight) f_{m r,j}, \qquad x_0=-1. 	ag{30} \] One can obtain the donor equality without division by its vanishing flag: substitute \(A_{m d}=1-p_{m d}f_{m d}\) and \(C=1-p_{m d}F_{m r}/x_0\) in \(A'_{m d}=A_{m d}/C\), then take \(p_{m d}=0\). Thus the principal linear characteristic is exactly \[ H_+=f'_{m d}+x_0^{-1}F_{m r} =f_{m d}. 	ag{31} \] For the inverse, the sign changes and \[ H_-=f'_{m d}-x_0^{-1}F_{m r} =f_{m d}. 	ag{32} \] Consequently the physical input donor unit supplies the nonzero characteristic. This requires no assertion that each intermediate donor in a chosen factorization has nonzero \(f\). A compact neighborhood of that point has bounded \(R\). It supplies the parameter chart in (26); it does not supply a physical integer state at that point. ## 6. Capacity, normal, and source scope Equations (7)--(12) are exact finite polynomial identities. The actual kernel is still (4). Formula (28) is therefore an actual kernel estimate in the untruncated capacity region (5); elsewhere it is an estimate before the original upper projectors. Those projectors can change its value and cannot be estimated by the nonzero unprojected factor. The result is explicitly a lower-donor theorem. It does not apply when \(a\) is near \(d\). Even a two-head full-circle product retains a factor of the form \(1-u^N\), which can vanish or grow exponentially. No such factor is replaced by a unit here. The recipient clocks in the original integer source are \(B_j=Q^{b_j}\). Allowing their coefficients in (3) to vary holomorphically is useful for uniform estimates, but does not construct an exact interpolation in complex occupations. Neither does the auxiliary variable \(\zeta\) transport an original contour or a root carry. Fixed-\(q\) meridian derivatives in (28) are of the exact retained finite family; no closed ordinary-color quantum-normal identity is inferred. All factorial changes of basis, neighboring coupons, Cartan lines, pivots, scalar normalizations and final first-jet source functional must remain in a closed word. The original flow propagation may force additional boundary sectors outside (5). This theorem does not cancel them, prove an endpoint-to-interior source propagation, or infer noncancellation of a cyclic trace. It supplies the stated relative local kernel estimate only. ## Coverage and complete proof source Abstract polymer expansions and inductive zero-free arguments are established techniques: see the primary papers by [Kotecký--Preiss](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01211762) and [Scott--Sokal](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0309352). Their primary abstract pages were checked for coverage. No theorem or proof from them is a premise above. The specific content here is the actual finite Euler-star word, its inverse pair energy, and its source-calibrated lower-donor estimate. * G: notes/research_actual_reduced_braid_critical_scheme.md, SHA256 ddddcd9bf75f35afdf3e5de0c03323acee2c66e624db36142c2344ef729a977a. title: Krein adjoints descend through the actual prefix reduction
text: # Krein adjoints descend through the actual prefix reduction Written research proof, 23 November 2026. The actual triangular prefix change is an isometry for the fixed physical tensor Krein form on positive real meridians. Its constant-coefficient reduction preserves adjoints. Consequently the literal reduced braid matrices, including their boundary Euler generator and full Cartan scalar, preserve the same tensor form on the remaining heads. This is an algebraic descent through a star-stable nilpotent ideal, not restriction of the form to the first-head vacuum, which is isotropic. All statements are at the actual fixed quantum root, including even and composite levels. The form is indefinite. No marked scalar lower bound or identification of geometric eigenline contributions follows. ## 1. Actual matrices and the fixed tensor form Fix \[ N\ge2,\quad d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2, \quad F_n=(Q;Q)_n\quad(0\le n<N). \tag{1} \] Keep this quantum parameter fixed. The common meridian is \(M>0\), with \(x=-M/q\) and the real branch of \(\Log M\). Use the original balanced occupation basis \(|a\rangle\), \(0\le a\le d\), and the literal operators of [R]: \[ K|a\rangle=xQ^{-a}|a\rangle,\qquad F|a\rangle=(1-Q^{a+1})|a+1\rangle,\qquad L|a\rangle=|a-1\rangle. \tag{2} \] The raising arrow at \(a=d\) and the lowering arrow at \(a=0\) are zero. No cyclic completion is made. Put \[ H_N=q^{-1}Z^{-1}R_d,\quad Z|a\rangle=Q^a|a\rangle, \quad R_d|a\rangle=|d-a\rangle,\quad \mathscr H_b=H_N^{\otimes b}. \tag{3} \] Thus \(H_N|a\rangle=qQ^a|d-a\rangle\), \(H_N^\dagger=H_N\), and \(H_N^2=I\). For an operator on \(b\) heads write \(A^{\sharp_b}=\mathscr H_bA^\dagger\mathscr H_b\). When the number of heads is clear the subscript is omitted. The direct head identities are \[ K^\sharp=K,\qquad F^\sharp=Q^{-1}F,\qquad L^\sharp=QL,\qquad \bar x=Qx . \tag{4} \] The first two are [H, (4)]. For the third, on input \(a\ge1\), the coefficient of \(H_NL^\dagger H_N\) is \(q^2Q^{a+d-a+1}=Q\); at \(a=0\) the actual top zero of \(L^\dagger\) gives zero. Thus both endpoints satisfy (4). On \(m\ge2\) ordered heads let \(r=m-1\) and retain the actual remaining coproduct \[ F_{\rm r}=F_2+K_2^{-1}F_3+\cdots+ K_2^{-1}\cdots K_{m-1}^{-1}F_m, \quad F_\Sigma=F_1+K_1^{-1}F_{\rm r}. \tag{5} \] Distinct head factors commute. Consequently (4) gives \(F_{\rm r}^{\sharp_r}=Q^{-1}F_{\rm r}\) and \(F_\Sigma^{\sharp_m}=Q^{-1}F_\Sigma\), with every original finite arrow retained. ## 2. The prefix itself is an isometry [R, (2)] specifies the actual prefix and its transport: \[ Y=x^{-1}L_1F_{\rm r},\qquad S_m=e_Q(Y):=\sum_{n=0}^d\frac{Y^n}{F_n},\qquad S_m^{-1}F_\Sigma S_m=F_1. \tag{6} \] For one head use \(S_1=I\). Since \(L_1^N=0\), \(Y^N=0\). The transport identity in (6) is an identity of finite Laurent matrices in \(M\); its equality near one therefore holds at every nonzero \(M\), in particular on the positive real axis. The factors in its adjoint commute across the two tensor groups; (4)--(5) therefore imply exactly \[ Y^{\sharp_m}=\bar x^{-1}(Q^{-1}F_{\rm r})(QL_1) =Q^{-1}Y. \tag{7} \] Use the finite factorial conjugation and inverse from [H, (7)]: \[ \overline{F_n}=(-1)^nQ^{-n(n+1)/2}F_n,\qquad P_Q(Y)=\sum_{n=0}^d \frac{(-1)^nQ^{n(n-1)/2}Y^n}{F_n} =e_Q(Y)^{-1}. \tag{8} \] The inverse identity follows below degree \(N\) from the finite \(Q\)-binomial formula; higher powers vanish. In particular no denominator \(F_N\) occurs. Combining (7)--(8) gives \[ \boxed{\quad S_m^{\sharp_m}=P_Q(Y)=S_m^{-1},\qquad S_m^\dagger\mathscr H_mS_m=\mathscr H_m .\quad} \tag{9} \] There is no meridian-dependent metric or omitted diagonal scalar. ## 3. Constant coefficients preserve adjoints Let \(\mathcal C_\Sigma\) be the full matrix commutant of \(F_\Sigma\), at a fixed positive real \(M\). It is stable under \(\sharp_m\), since \(F_\Sigma^\sharp=Q^{-1}F_\Sigma\). After conjugating by \(S_m\), its elements have unique expansions \[ \widetilde W=S_m^{-1}WS_m =\sum_{n=0}^d F_1^n\otimes B_n(W). \tag{10} \] Indeed \(F_1\) is one nilpotent Jordan block: its nonzero arrows below the top are units. The column on \(|0\rangle\) determines all columns by commutation with \(F_1\), proving (10). This is the same commutant calculation used in [R, (3)]. Define \(\mathcal B_m(W)=B_0(W)\). This is the actual prefix map, not a different compression: for \(i_0v=|0\rangle\otimes v\), [R] gives \(S_mi_0=i_0\) and \(B_0=p_0S_m^{-1}Wi_0\). Positive \(F_1\)-degree cannot contribute to a constant coefficient, so \(\mathcal B_m\) is a unital algebra homomorphism. Moreover (9) yields \[ S_m^{-1}W^{\sharp_m}S_m=\widetilde W^{\sharp_m} =\sum_{n=0}^dQ^{-n}F_1^n\otimes B_n(W)^{\sharp_r}. \tag{11} \] Taking its constant coefficient proves the exact descent \[ \boxed{\quad \mathcal B_m(W^{\sharp_m}) =\mathcal B_m(W)^{\sharp_r}. \quad} \tag{12} \] Equivalently, the ideal of positive \(F_1\)-degree in (10) is star-stable and nilpotent, and its quotient carries the displayed tensor adjoint on the entire remaining matrix algebra. This calculation retains all coefficient matrices \(B_n\) before passing to that specified quotient. In particular, if an invertible actual total intertwiner satisfies \(W^{\sharp_m}W=I\), then \[ \boxed{\quad B(W)^\dagger\mathscr H_rB(W)=\mathscr H_r,\qquad B(W)^{-1}=\mathscr H_rB(W)^\dagger\mathscr H_r .\quad} \tag{13} \] Here and below \(B(W)=\mathcal B_m(W)\). This applies to the full original common-meridian signed braid words of [H], including overlapping adjacent crossings. The descent is not restriction to the vacuum section: \[ i_0^\dagger S_m^\dagger\mathscr H_mS_mi_0=0, \qquad i_0^\dagger S_m^\dagger\mathscr H_mS_mi_d =q^{-1}\mathscr H_r, \quad i_dv=|d\rangle\otimes v. \tag{14} \] These follow from (9) and the first-head anti-diagonal in (3). Thus the vacuum is isotropic, while its pairing with the opposite end is nondegenerate. The algebra quotient proof, rather than a nonexistent positive vacuum restriction, gives (13). ## 4. The literal reduced boundary generator checks its scalar For the original checked crossing [R, (7),(12)] gives \[ B(R_i)=R_{i-1}\ (i\ge2),\qquad B(R_1)=\kappa(M)S_rD_{\rm red},\qquad B(R_1^{-1})=\kappa(M)^{-1}D_{\rm red}^{-1}S_r^{-1}, \tag{15} \] where on the first remaining head \[ D_{\rm red}|a\rangle =\delta_a|a\rangle,\quad \delta_a=(-1)^aq^{a(a+1)}M^{-2a},\quad \alpha(M)=d+\frac{N}{\pi i}\Log M,\quad \kappa(M)=q^{\alpha(M)^2/2},\quad |\kappa(M)|=M^d. \tag{16} \] The last modulus follows by substituting real \(\Log M\) in the displayed unrolled exponent. For the diagonal, \[ \overline{\delta_{d-a}}\delta_a=M^{-2d},\qquad D_{\rm red}^{\sharp_r}D_{\rm red}=M^{-2d}I. \tag{17} \] In fact its phase is \((-1)^dq^{(2a-d)(d+1)}=1\). Equations (9),(16)--(17) prove (13) directly for the boundary generator. Dropping \(\kappa\) would leave the incorrect factor \(M^{-2d}\). Internal generators use [H]'s full physical crossing identity. The actual negative generators have the inverse order in (15), so products of arbitrary signs preserve \(\mathscr H_r\). The zero-framed normalized boundary generator is instead \(x^dS_rD_{\rm red}\), as in [R, (23)]. It is also an isometry because \(|x|=M\). Equivalently its retained twist \(\kappa x^{-d}\) has modulus one on positive real meridians. No external modified-dimension or other prescribed peripheral factor is thereby declared an isometry. ## 5. Meridian germs and the original pointed source Fix \(M_0>0\) and put \(M=M_0e^u\) on its continued logarithmic branch. Holomorphic polarization of (13), as in [H], gives for the full actual reduced braid germ \[ B^\natural(u)\mathscr H_rB(u)=\mathscr H_r, \qquad B^\natural(u)=\overline{B(\bar u)}^{\mathsf T}. \tag{18} \] Thus all fixed-order meridian Wronskians follow together: \[ \sum_{j=0}^n\binom nj B^{(j)}(0)^\dagger\mathscr H_rB^{(n-j)}(0) =\mathbf1_{n=0}\mathscr H_r. \tag{19} \] This includes the meridian dependence of the prefix itself. There is no differentiation in \(q\). In particular the original highest-cut pivotal observation stays exactly [R, (14)]. Write \(K_{\rm r}(M)=M^rK_0\), \(\varepsilon=(-1)^{(N+1)r}\), and \(\mathcal D_N(z)=(z^N-z^{-N})/(z-z^{-1})\) with its Laurent-polynomial continuation. Then \[ \Phi_0(W(M))= \frac{\mathcal D_N(M)}{\varepsilon(M^{mN}-M^{-mN})} \operatorname{Tr}\bigl[(M^mK_0-M^{-m}K_0^{-1})B(M)\bigr]. \tag{20} \] It is read meromorphically with the original removable continuation. For an analytic actual intertwiner, \(\mathcal D_N(1)=N\) forces \(\operatorname{Tr}((K_0-K_0^{-1})B(1))=0\). Differentiating its numerator and denominator before specialization therefore gives the unchanged first-meridian-jet row \[ \Phi_0(W(1))= \frac{\operatorname{Tr}((K_0+K_0^{-1})B(1))}{2\varepsilon} +\frac{\operatorname{Tr}((K_0-K_0^{-1})B'(1))}{2\varepsilon m}. \tag{21} \] Here the prime is \(\partial_M\), and the whole prefix dependence is included. External marking, framing and peripheral lines remain in their original positions. The source is not replaced by an \(\mathscr H_r\)-norm, an adjoint vacuum, or an ordinary trace. The same form also respects this actual source functional. At positive real \(M\), put \(C_N(M)=\mathcal D_N(M)\mathcal D_N(MK_{\rm r}(M))^{-1}\). Since \(K_{\rm r}^\sharp=K_{\rm r}\) and \(\mathcal D_N\) has real Laurent coefficients, \(C_N^\sharp=C_N\) wherever defined. For every remaining matrix \(B\), cyclic trace then gives \[ \overline{\operatorname{Tr}(C_NB)} =\operatorname{Tr}(C_NB^{\sharp_r}),\qquad \overline{\Phi_0(W(M))}=\Phi_0(W(M)^{-1}) \quad(W^{\sharp_m}W=I). \tag{22} \] The second equality uses the actual algebra map and (13). These identities continue as polarized meromorphic germs. For analytic original intertwiner families their removable values at one retain the complete first-jet row (21). An additional external scalar carries its own complex conjugate; it is not assumed unit. The functional in (22) is not asserted positive. ## 6. Scope and complete sources The new operation is the actual prefix star descent (9)--(13). It gives one common nondegenerate form for the complete reduced braid representation and its meridian germs. It does not remove any remaining head, root Jordan direction, or source coefficient. The physical dimension is still \(N^{m-1}\). No positive metric, geometric packet estimate, nonzero marked closing, comparison of off-circle geometric eigenlines, or general volume lower bound is asserted. Moving-\(q\) normal jets retain their separate original prefix adapters and are outside this fixed-root meridian proof. The current proof uses the generic-meridian head identities and full crossing of [H], rather than its complete-only flag-frame congruence. title: The actual reduced word as a closed finite Bargmann period
text: # The actual reduced word as a closed finite Bargmann period Private written proof, 18 November 2026. The Cartan first-meridian-jet formula has an exact closed Gaussian period built from the known reduced generators. Both sides of every interface are specified. The identity kernel is a finite exponential polynomial; its cutoff and all upper and lower projectors remain. A paired kernel estimate gives exponential control of the Gaussian ends using elementary bounds on the local matrices. This also places a lower, resolved row endpoint in finite complex Bargmann coordinates after the actual factorial gauge. It does not place that point on the original real cycle or prove that its contribution survives the closed pairing. The common meridian varies at fixed \(q_N\); ordinary-color quantum normals are not inferred. The complete proof directs are R, H, V, D and G, pinned below. The earlier compact coherent source and its two-mode realization were read for coverage. The one-mode normalization and estimates used here are proved directly. ## 1. Finite kernels, their dual, and the original first jet Put \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\), \(x=-M/q\). There are \(r=m-1\) remaining heads. Let \[ f_a=(Q;Q)_a,\qquad G_Fw_a=f_aw_a,\qquad \mathcal G=G_F^{\otimes r}. \tag{1} \] All these diagonal entries are nonzero. For the actual reduced word \(B(M)=\mathcal B_m(W(M))\) of R set \[ T(M)=\mathcal G^{-1}B(M)\mathcal G . \tag{2} \] The gauge depends on \(q\), not on \(M\). It commutes with the remaining Cartan. Consequently both \(B\) and its actual fixed-\(q\) meridian derivative can be replaced by \(T\) and \(T'\) in H's trace formula. For any matrix \(A\) on these finite heads define \[ \mathcal K_{A,N}(z,w) =\sum_{a,b\in\{0,\ldots,d\}^r} z^a A_{ab}\frac{(Nw)^b}{b!},\qquad d\mu_N(u)=\left(\frac N\pi\right)^r e^{-N|u|^2}\,d^{2r}u . \tag{3} \] The variables \(z,w\) are independent complex variables. The dual is exactly \((Nw)^b/b!\), not an unweighted evaluation row. Angular integration and integration by parts give \[ \int u^a\overline u^{\,b}\,d\mu_N(u) =\mathbf1_{a=b}\frac{a!}{N^{|a|}} . \tag{4} \] It follows by multiplying the finite sums that \[ \int\mathcal K_{A,N}(z,\overline u) \mathcal K_{B,N}(u,w)\,d\mu_N(u) =\mathcal K_{AB,N}(z,w),\qquad \int\mathcal K_{A,N}(u,\overline u)\,d\mu_N(u) =\operatorname{Tr}A . \tag{5} \] These are absolutely convergent integrals of finite polynomials against a Gaussian. No infinite head or occupation interpolation is involved. Write \[ x_0=-q^{-1},\qquad \varepsilon=(-1)^{(N+1)r},\qquad \mathcal I_\pm(M)= \int\mathcal K_{T(M),N}(Q^{\mp1}u,\overline u)\,d\mu_N(u). \tag{6} \] The simultaneous rotation acts on every remaining output coordinate. Since the actual complete Cartan has eigenvalue \(x_0^rQ^{-\sum a_j}\), (5) gives \[ \operatorname{Tr}(K_0^{\pm1}B(M)) =x_0^{\pm r}\mathcal I_\pm(M). \tag{7} \] H's original pointed/pivotal source is therefore \[ \boxed{\quad \Phi_0(W(1)) =\frac{x_0^r\mathcal I_+(1)+x_0^{-r}\mathcal I_-(1)} {2\varepsilon} +\frac{x_0^r\mathcal I_+'(1)-x_0^{-r}\mathcal I_-'(1)} {2\varepsilon m}. \quad} \tag{8} \] Its exact residue constraint is \[ x_0^r\mathcal I_+(1) -x_0^{-r}\mathcal I_-(1)=0 . \tag{9} \] The derivative in (8) is applied to the actual \(T(M)\). There is no derivative of a reset coupon or of the frozen complete Cartan in (7). Any separately prescribed external scalar multiplies the original source unchanged. For the empty remaining tensor, the integrals mean the corresponding scalar evaluations. ## 2. A closed integral of known local arrays Factor \(B=A_L\cdots A_1\) by R's literal reduced generators: physical signed crossings on the remaining heads, or \(\kappa S_rD\) and its inverse. Identity legs, finite pivots, and specified matrix insertions are included as their actual arrays. Put \(T_\ell=\mathcal G^{-1}A_\ell\mathcal G\). Then (6) is the explicit closed period \[ \mathcal I_\pm= \int \mathcal K_{T_L,N}(Q^{\mp1}u_0,\overline u_{L-1}) \mathcal K_{T_{L-1},N}(u_{L-1},\overline u_{L-2}) \cdots \mathcal K_{T_1,N}(u_1,\overline u_0) \prod_{\ell=0}^{L-1}d\mu_N(u_\ell). \tag{10} \] For \(L=1\) this means (6). Tensor identities give the identical formula for a partially factored network. The number of integration variables is fixed by the finite word, independently of \(N\). At fixed \(N\), the entire product is a finite polynomial times the product Gaussian, so Fubini and the meridian product rule are legitimate. More general local gauge choices are also exact, but their interfaces cannot be omitted. If \(\mathcal G_\ell\) is the chosen basis on the \(\ell\)-th interface, use \[ T_\ell=\mathcal G_\ell^{-1} A_\ell\mathcal G_{\ell-1}. \tag{11} \] For a closed chain take \(\mathcal G_L=\mathcal G_0\). A diagonal quadratic chirp \(J_a=Q^{a(a-1)/2}\), for example, must occur on both incident kernels in this manner. Such \(J\)'s and \(G_F\)'s commute with the Cartan insertion and are independent of the fixed-\(q\) meridian derivative. If a chosen gauge depends on \(M\), differentiate both sides of (11), including every interface term. The first-jet reduction (8) requires H's actual intertwining family. Formula (5) represents arbitrary marked matrices as well, but it does not promote a marked nonintertwiner to that family. Its original Ward/source defects must then be kept separately. ## 3. The finite cap and the donor kernel are both retained For one head put \(E_d(s)=\sum_{a=0}^d s^a/a!\). The identity kernel and the individual occupation projector are \[ \mathcal K_{I,N}(z,w)=E_d(Nzw),\qquad \mathcal K_{P_a,N}(z,w)=z^a(Nw)^a/a! . \tag{12} \] Thus all finite windows and their endpoints are literal sums of these kernels. In particular, the exact Cauchy representation \[ E_d(s)=\frac1{2\pi i}\oint_{|\zeta|=\rho} e^{s/\zeta}\frac{1-\zeta^N}{1-\zeta}\,\frac{d\zeta}{\zeta}, \qquad \rho>0,\quad \rho\ne1 , \tag{13} \] follows by multiplying its two finite/Taylor series. The quotient at \(\zeta=1\) is removable. Equation (13) retains its numerator \(1-\zeta^N\); it is not a replacement by an infinite exponential projector off the real cycle. The exact donor result D inserts in (10) without changing its dual. For a star on \(s\) heads let the donor be coordinate \(1\) and let \(b=(b_2,\ldots,b_s)\) be the actual integer recipient input. D supplies \[ \mathcal C^\pm_{N,b}(\lambda,z) =P_b\sum_{a=0}^d\frac{\lambda^a}{a!}K_a^\pm(z;b), \tag{14} \] where \(P_b\) is its exact recipient upper projector. Consequently the full kernel in (3) is exactly \[ \mathcal K_{\mathcal G^{-1}S_s^{\pm1}\mathcal G,N}(z,w) =\sum_{b_2,\ldots,b_s=0}^d \left(\prod_{j=2}^s\frac{(Nz_jw_j)^{b_j}}{b_j!}\right) \mathcal C^\pm_{N,b}(Nw_1,z). \tag{15} \] Both the external recipient monomial of D and its factorial dual are visible in (15). Any spectator identities are (12), and all neighboring Cartan or chirp matrices remain in (10)--(11). D's relative Gaussian estimate applies to each factored term of (15) when \(|Nw_1|=O(\sqrt N)\) and the actual integer recipients have its specified macroscopic upper margin. Outside that margin the exact \(P_b\) remains. Equation (15) does not interpolate the \(b_j\)'s to complex geometric occupations or discard their sum. ## 4. A paired bound and Gaussian end control The monomial metric underlying (4) is \[ H_a=a!/N^{|a|}. \tag{16} \] Write \(\|A\|_H\) for its operator norm and \(\Pi_N(z)=\prod_{j=1}^rE_d(N|z_j|^2)\). Evaluation and its exact dual, followed by Cauchy--Schwarz in this finite-dimensional metric, give \[ |\mathcal K_{A,N}(z,\overline w)| \le \|A\|_H\sqrt{\Pi_N(z)\Pi_N(w)} . \tag{17} \] This estimate pairs the two ends of the kernel. It is not a bound on a coherent column without its dual. In the closed product (10) every interface occurs once on each side. Since the Cartan rotation has modulus one, its absolute integrand is bounded by \[ \left(\prod_{\ell=1}^L\|T_\ell\|_H\right) \prod_{\ell=0}^{L-1}\Pi_N(u_\ell). \tag{18} \] The integral of each one-head projector is exactly \(N\). For \(R>1\), the one-head mass outside \(|u|^2\le R\) satisfies \[ \int_{|u|^2\ge R}E_d(N|u|^2)\,d\mu_N(u) \le N e^{-N I(R)},\qquad I(R)=R-1-\log R. \tag{19} \] To prove it, set \(s=N|u|^2\). For \(0<\theta<1\), \[ \frac1{a!}\int_{NR}^\infty e^{-s}s^a\,ds \le e^{-\theta NR}(1-\theta)^{-a-1}. \tag{20} \] This is the full gamma integral after multiplying by \(e^{\theta(s-NR)}\ge1\). Take \(\theta=1-R^{-1}\) and \(a+1\le N\), then sum the \(N\) terms. A union bound over the \(rL\) interface coordinates proves that the part of (10) with some \(|u_{\ell,j}|^2>R\) is bounded in absolute value by \[ rL\,N^{rL}e^{-NI(R)} \prod_{\ell=1}^L\|T_\ell\|_H . \tag{21} \] The same bound holds for a differentiated product, with the corresponding one differentiated norm in each term of its exact product rule. There is an elementary exponential bound on these local norms for every fixed word. At the root, reflection of the sine factors gives \[ |f_a f_{d-a}|=N,\qquad |f_a|\le2^d,\qquad |f_a|^{-1}\le2^d/N . \tag{22} \] Indeed the omitted factors in \(f_d=N\) have the same moduli as the first \(d-a\) factors. Also \[ e^{-N}\le a!/N^a\le1\quad(0\le a\le d). \tag{23} \] For the lower bound use \(\log(a!)\ge a\log a-a\); the sequence \(a!/N^a\) is decreasing through \(a=d\), and \((1-1/N)^{N-1}\ge e^{-1}\). Thus passing between the original occupation norm, the \(G_F\) gauge, and (16) costs only \(e^{C_rN}\). On \(|M-1|\le2\eta/N\), for sufficiently large \(N\), the finite arrows satisfy \(\|F\|_2\le2\), \(\|\mathcal E\|_2\le4\), and all fixed-width Cartan products and inverses have bounded norms. V's exact positive Euler series has coefficients \((-1)^nq^{n^2}/f_n\); its inverse has \(q^n/f_n\). Their \(n<N\) terms are therefore bounded using (22) and \(\|\mathcal E_1F_2\|_2\le8\). The finite sum has norm at most \(N C^N\). The remaining crossing Cartan and flip have bounded norms on this collar, apart from their specified common scalar. For a reduced star, \(\|F_{\rm tail}\|_2\) is bounded by a constant depending only on the fixed width and \(\eta\). Applying (22) to its series in (2) of R, and to its actual inverse, again gives \(N C^N\). The diagonal reduced \(D\) has bounded norm on this collar. The common crossing scalar is the original \(\kappa=q^{\alpha^2/2}\), with \(\alpha=N-1+\log M/\log q\). Thus \[ \frac{\kappa(M)}{\kappa(1)} =\exp\left((N-1)\log M+ \frac{(\log M)^2}{2\log q}\right), \tag{24} \] and \(|\kappa(1)|=1\). It and its inverse are bounded on the stated collar. The prescribed zero-framing powers have the same property. Any additional external scalar line is still retained explicitly, with its own domain. Combining these facts gives constants \(C,p\) for the unmarked reduced braid word, including its displayed pivots and interfaces, such that \[ \prod_\ell\|T_\ell(M)\|_H\le N^p e^{CN}. \tag{25} \] Fixed-degree occupation marks add their polynomial norms. Arbitrary extra matrix insertions retain their own norms; no bound for them is inferred from the unmarked word. Cauchy's formula on the larger meridian collar gives an additional \(O(N)\) for each fixed meridian derivative on the smaller collar. Consequently (21) makes the Gaussian ends smaller than \(N^{p'}e^{-\Lambda N}\), for any prescribed \(\Lambda>0\), by choosing one fixed large \(R\) with \(I(R)>C+\Lambda\). This is an actual global end estimate. It is not a volume bound on the compact part of the period. ## 5. Entire translation of the full cycle Complexify each interface to independent \(z,w\). The Gaussian measure is the restriction of \[ \left(\frac N{2\pi i}\right)^r e^{-Nz\cdot w}\bigwedge_{j=1}^r(dw_j\wedge dz_j) \tag{26} \] to \(z=u,w=\overline u\), with its original orientation. The closed integrand is entire in all these variables. For any fixed vectors \(\alpha_\ell,\beta_\ell\), the simultaneous translated cycle \[ z_\ell=u_\ell+\alpha_\ell,\qquad w_\ell=\overline u_\ell+\beta_\ell \tag{27} \] has exactly the same period. Here the ends have a paired estimate as well. Put \(F_N(v)=e^{-N|v|^2}E_d(N|v|^2)\). For one interface the exact identity is \[ e^{-N\operatorname{Re}(zw)} \sqrt{E_d(N|z|^2)E_d(N|w|^2)} =e^{N|\alpha-\overline\beta|^2/2} \sqrt{F_N(z)F_N(w)} . \tag{28} \] This follows from \(z-\overline w=\alpha-\overline\beta\). Cauchy--Schwarz in the measure \((N/\pi)d^2u\) and translation invariance of area bound its full integral by \(N e^{N|\alpha-\overline\beta|^2/2}\). If \(|\alpha|,|\beta|\le A\) and \(|u|^2>R\), both \(|z|\) and \(|w|\) exceed \(\sqrt R-A\). Equation (19) in the same Cauchy--Schwarz estimate therefore gives the tail bound \[ N e^{N|\alpha-\overline\beta|^2/2} e^{-NI((\sqrt R-A)^2)} \qquad(\sqrt R-A>1). \tag{29} \] Apply these estimates independently to every interface and use the finite union bound. The resulting full bound is \(N^{rL}\exp(\frac N2\sum|\alpha-\overline\beta|^2) \prod\|T_\ell\|_H\), with the additional tail factor from (29) for a large-coordinate event. It is uniform on the compact translation homotopy. Cutoff Stokes applied to the entire form now has vanishing end terms, since its cutoff error is bounded by these integrable tails. This proves (27). Together with (25) the same estimates give arbitrarily strong exponential end control after one sufficiently large fixed truncation, also for the exact first meridian derivatives. Replacing the finite \(E_d\) by the full exponential in (28) would remove this decay and is not done. A translation can pass through a specified finite complex point. This equality moves the whole cycle and retains every kernel. It does not show that the point is a stationary point of a uniform kernel phase, that its normal cycle occurs with nonzero coefficient, or that other parts have a smaller exponential rate. ## 6. The elementary resolved coordinate adapter There is a precise small-product region where the finite elementary kernels identify the classical coordinates. Put \(\tau=zw\) for one head. In the all-\(G_F\) basis, \[ \begin{split} \mathcal K_K&=xE_d(NQ^{-1}\tau),\\ \mathcal K_F&=zE_{d-1}(N\tau),\\ \mathcal K_L&=z^{-1}\bigl(E_d(N\tau)-E_d(NQ\tau)\bigr),\\ \mathcal K_{\mathcal E} &=z^{-1}\bigl( M E_d(NQ^{-1}\tau)+M^{-1}E_d(NQ\tau) -(M+M^{-1})E_d(N\tau)\bigr). \end{split} \tag{30} \] Here \(L\) is the original unilateral lowering shift. Apparent \(z^{-1}\)'s cancel in these polynomial kernels. The \(F\) formula retains its missing top arrow. For the last formula, its input coefficient is exactly \((1-Q^a)(MQ^{-a}-M^{-1})\). For \(|\tau|\le\rho<1\), the exponential tail is \[ |e^{N\tau}-E_d(N\tau)| \le\frac{(e\rho)^N}{1-\rho}. \tag{31} \] This follows from the first omitted term and its successive ratio at most \(\rho\), with \(N!\ge(N/e)^N\). After division by \(e^{N\tau}\) the bound is exponentially small whenever \(1+\log\rho+\rho<0\), for example \(\rho=1/8\). The same conclusion, with polynomial factors, holds for \(E_{d-1}\), fixed derivatives, and the \(Q^{\pm1}\) arguments on a smaller compact region. Dividing (30) by its exact identity kernel and then taking the physical principal limit on this region, with \(x_{\rm cl}=-M\), gives \[ A=e^{2\pi i zw},\quad f=z,\quad p=\frac{1-A}{z},\quad K=x_{\rm cl}/A,\quad e=(M/A-M^{-1})p . \tag{32} \] Thus this is the same physical factorial coordinate as G, with the gauge transported. Where defined, \[ d\log A\wedge d\log p=2\pi i\,dz\wedge dw . \tag{33} \] The term \(d\log(1-A)\) drops from that wedge. For a recorded lower logarithmic lift at a row endpoint, \(A=1,\ \log A=0,\ f\ne0\), the resolved point is \[ z=f,\qquad w=0 . \tag{34} \] Its G-coordinate \((A-1)/p\) is \(-z\), so the flag resolution is retained. This point is finite and lies in the cap-controlled local region of (31). It usually lies off the original real cycle \(w=\overline z\). More generally a chosen finite logarithm gives the algebraic assignment \(z=f,\ w=(\log A)/(2\pi i f)\) on G's all-\(f\)-unit geometric charts. It lies in the complexified finite kernel domain, but (31) need not hold there. In particular an upper logarithmic lift at clock one is not the lower point (34). No finite projector or Fourier sheet is reset to put it there. The full finite cap remains outside the stated small-product estimate. ## 7. What the closed pairing still requires Equation (15) inserts D's actual donor kernel into (10), but a relative estimate for that one factored kernel is not a relative estimate for the whole period. The neighboring dual, the integer recipient sum and its projectors remain. For any finite kernel error \(E\), the safe global contraction estimate is the corresponding bound (18) with \(\|E\|_H\) and the other local norms. Pointwise coherent column control does not automatically give that norm. The superexponential donor tails of D can outweigh exponential factors on a supplied bounded paired domain with the required recipient margin; this does not establish such a domain for the original whole cycle. The fixed global Gaussian tails (21) and their translated versions control only the ends of the exact representation. The compact part, its factorial caps, and its geometric intersection remain to be analyzed. In particular no positivity, geometric coefficient, or scalar lower bound follows. ## Complete proof-source pins * R: notes/research_actual_reduced_braid_source.md, SHA256 9a472ef27b08305a519ff1f24b6d2b909e63a0acbdc49b3a29e001c52a2f2243. * H: notes/research_scalar_prefix_kernel_and_first_meridian_jet.md, SHA256 d7d82848a1b3f50709352905bafcc7ddfee36f41e434bf5de4663b4b6181dc9e. * V: notes/balanced_verma_coherent_braiding.md, SHA256 0203bdd7dbb36a4f8deb1c310b3445608e53d10922049447da8eecec4f87d1c4. * D: notes/research_reduced_euler_donor_coherent_sum.md, SHA256 ff35583f203ae7686de4ff7fb91fcb4d4d0190e4f8995bd89a871849bc91d7f4. * G: notes/research_actual_reduced_braid_critical_scheme.md, SHA256 ddddcd9bf75f35afdf3e5de0c03323acee2c66e624db36142c2344ef729a977a. All five complete sources were freshly read nontruncated in the active author sequence and retained unchanged. Every used implication was checked. The kernels, pairings, end estimates and coordinate adapter above are written calculations. No mathematical programs were run; frozen and public files were not edited.

title: Reflection gives the sharp physical normal connection
text:
# Reflection gives the sharp physical normal connection Private written proof, 16 November 2026. The sine-factor approximate modes admit a regular divided-color frame through the middle fold. Exact reflection of that frame, together with the original recurrence, determines the derivative of the actual connection coefficients to the sharp truncation accuracy. Thus the same two-value normalization now approximates both physical values and first spectral normals at that rate. The result concerns the actual physical jets; it does not compare an unrelated off-grid baseline or estimate a filled current. ## 1. Parameters, modes and statement Put \(h=N^{-1}\), \(N\ge2\), and \[ s_z=2\sin(\pi hz),\quad c_z=2\cos(\pi h(2z+1)),\quad C_N(x)=2\cos(2\pi x+\pi h),\quad w=2\cosh(\alpha h),\quad P_N(C)=2T_N(C/2)+2. 	ag{1} \] Here \(T_N\) is the Chebyshev polynomial. The ordinary kernel is \[ K_N(w,C)=\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}e_k(w)e_k(C),\qquad e_k(C)= rac{\prod_{j<k}(c_j-C)}{\prod_{j=1}^k s_j^2}, \qquad u_N(x)=K_N(w,C_N(x)). 	ag{2} \] Fix a compact parameter rectangle \[ |\Re\alpha|\le A,\qquad |\Im\alpha|\le\pi-\epsilon, \quad 0<\epsilon<\pi, \qquad z_\pm=-	frac12\pm rac{i\alpha}{2\pi}. 	ag{3} \] Larger rectangles of the same kind are reserved for derivatives. This includes coalescence at zero. No continuation of the individual mode coefficients through their other index resonances is assumed. Fix \(x_0\in(0,1/2)\), and let \[ \delta= rac1\pi\arcsin rac{\sin(\pi x_0)}{\sqrt2}, \qquad m=\lfloor\delta Nfloor, \] \[ I_\delta(X)=\int_0^\delta \log rac{\sin^2(\pi X)-\sin^2(\pi v)} {\sin^2(\pi v)}\,dv, \qquad \delta<X<1-\delta. 	ag{4} \] Choose \(\delta<a<x_0<b<b_*<1/2\), sufficiently close to \(x_0\), with fixed larger buffers such that \(I_\delta(a)>0\). All intervals below have those buffers. In particular the symmetric extension around \([a,1-a]\) remains inside \((\delta,1-\delta)\) and has a positive minimum of \(I_\delta\). Use the specified Gamma-product factorial \[ G_N(t)=\left( rac{2\pi}{N}ight)^t\Gamma(t+1) \prod_{k\ge1} rac{\Gamma(Nk+t+1)} {\Gamma(Nk-t)(Nk)^{2t+1}}, \qquad -1<\Re t<N, 	ag{5} \] and the finite modes of the sharp truncation source: \[ F_z(x)=4^{-z} rac{G_N(Nx+z)}{G_N(Nx-z)},\qquad a_0(z)=1,\quad  rac{a_k(z)}{a_{k-1}(z)} = rac{s_{z-k+1}^4}{4(c_{z-k}-c_z)}, \] \[ U(z,x)=\sum_{k=0}^{m}a_k(z)F_{z-k}(x),\quad 
u=\alpha/\pi, \] \[ H_0(x)= rac{U(z_+,x)+U(z_-,x)}2,\qquad H_1(x)= rac{U(z_+,x)-U(z_-,x)}{2i
u}. 	ag{6} \] The last quotient has its removable value at zero. Define the divided-color state and mode frame by \[ \Delta_N(x)=C_N(x)-C_N(x-h) =-4\sin(2\pi x)\sin(\pi h), \] \[ \mathcal V_f(x)=  inom{f(x)}{[f(x)-f(x-h)]/\Delta_N(x)},\qquad \mathcal F_N(x)=  igl(\mathcal V_{H_0}(x),\mathcal V_{H_1}(x) igr). 	ag{7} \] The removable meaning at the fold is proved below. Choose a physical anchor \(x_{j_*}=j_*/N\in[b,b_*]\), and put \[ \mathbf a_* =\mathcal F_N(x_{j_*})^{-1}\mathcal V_{u_N}(x_{j_*}), \qquad V_N(x)=(H_0(x),H_1(x))\mathbf a_*. 	ag{8} \] This is exactly the two-value normalization: the two rows in (7) are obtained from the two values by an invertible change of basis at this anchor, which is separated from the fold. **Theorem.** For all large \(N\), (8) is defined and holomorphic in (3). Its coefficients are polynomially bounded in \(N\). For every fixed nonnegative parameter derivative order \(q\), there are \(C,p\), uniform on the specified windows, such that at every physical \(x_j=j/N\in[a,b]\), \[  oxed{\quad |\partial_\alpha^q(u_N(x_j)-V_N(x_j))| +|\partial_\alpha^q(u_N'(x_j)-V_N'(x_j))| \le CN^p e^{-NI_\delta(x_j)}. \quad} 	ag{9} \] Primes mean ordinary \(x\)-derivatives. Since \(C_N'\) is a uniform unit on this target bulk interval, (9) gives the same bound for the original first spectral normal, with \(V_N'(x_j)/C_N'(x_j)\) as its comparison. On every fixed-height buffered rectangle over \([a,b]\), \(V_N\) and its fixed derivatives are polynomially bounded, and its ordinary residual obeys \[ |\partial_x^r\partial_\alpha^q (\mathscr J_N-w)V_N(x)| \le CN^p e^{-NI_\delta(\Re x)}. 	ag{10} \] At \(x_j=x_0+O(N^{-1})\), the exponent in (9) is \[ I_\delta(x_j)=J_*(\pi-2\pi x_0)+O(N^{-1}). 	ag{11} \] Thus both physical jets have the sharp optimized rate at the target. ## 2. Exact reflection and extension of the mode estimates The normalized factorial has the exact reflection identity \[ G_N(t)G_N(N-1-t)=N. 	ag{12} \] For completeness, the canonical factorial source proves \[  rac{G_N'(t)}{G_N(t)} = rac{\pi}{N^2}\sum_{k=0}^{N-1} (t-k)\cot rac{\pi(t-k)}N. \] Its right side is unchanged under \(t\mapsto N-1-t\), by reversing \(k\). Hence the logarithmic derivative of the product in (12) vanishes. At \(t=0\), the normalization and the exact shift law give \(G_N(0)G_N(N-1)=N\). Meromorphic continuation proves (12) with no undetermined periodic multiplier. Let \(R_Nx=1-h-x\). Applying (12) to the numerator and denominator of each \(F_z\) gives \[ F_z(R_Nx)=F_z(x),\qquad H_l(R_Nx)=H_l(x),\qquad C_N(R_Nx)=C_N(x),\qquad u_N(R_Nx)=u_N(x). 	ag{13} \] The cutoff in (6) is identical for both modes and is fixed throughout the symmetric interval. Here are the estimates from the truncation proof on that extended interval. All factorial arguments remain in the zero-free strip: their scaled real parts lie between \(a-\delta+O(h)>0\) and \(1-a+\delta+O(h)<1\). For \(x=X+iY\), \(v\le\delta\), \[ |\sin\pi(X-v+iY)\sin\pi(X+v+iY)| \ge \sin^2(\pi X)-\sin^2(\pi v)>0. 	ag{14} \] This is the same product inequality as on the left half; it holds throughout \(\delta<X<1-\delta\). The exact summand ratio is \[  rac{a_kF_{z-k}}{a_{k-1}F_{z-k+1}} = rac{s_{z-k+1}^4} {s_ks_{2z+1-k}s_{Nx+z-k+1}s_{Nx-z+k}}. 	ag{15} \] The parameter margins in (3), (14), and the factorial estimate therefore give uniformly for \(0\le k\le m\) \[ |a_kF_{z-k}(x)| \le CN^p e^{-NI_{kh}(\Re x)}. 	ag{16} \] As a function of its upper endpoint, \(I_v(X)\) first increases and then decreases. Its values at zero and \(\delta\) are nonnegative on the chosen buffered interval. The proof of the source thus applies unchanged: the first summand ratio is \(O(h^2)\), the ratios for \(k\leho N\) are bounded by a fixed contraction after choosing small \(ho>0\), and the remaining terms have a uniform positive exponential saving. It follows, on any fixed-height rectangle in this symmetric strip, that \[ U(z,x)=F_z(x)+O_{m hol}(h^2),\qquad F_z(x)=\{\sin\pi(x+h/2)\}^{2z}(1+O_{m hol}(h^2)). 	ag{17} \] The ordinary telescoping identity is still \[ (\mathscr J_N-w)U(z,x) =- rac{a_m(z)s_{z-m}^4}{4}F_{z-m-1}(x). 	ag{18} \] Its final multiplier relative to the last term in (16) is bounded. Small disks of radius \(c/N\) preserve the smooth exponent, while Cauchy estimates in \(\alpha\) use a larger rectangle of type (3). Thus, writing \(r_l=(\mathscr J_N-w)H_l\), \[ |\partial_x^r\partial_\alpha^q r_l(x)| \le CN^p e^{-NI_\delta(\Re x)}. 	ag{19} \] The removable combination at \(\alpha=0\) has the same bounds. Finally, \(I_\delta(X)=I_\delta(1-X)\), and it increases on \(\delta<X<1/2\): differentiating its integrand gives \(\pi\sin(2\pi X)/(\sin^2(\pi X)-\sin^2(\pi v))>0\). Its minimum on \([x,1-x]\), for \(a\le x\le b_*\), is therefore \(I_\delta(x)\). ## 3. A uniform spectral frame through the fold Put \(\xi=x+h/2\). On a fixed complex neighborhood of the real spectral interval traversed by \([a,1-a]\), choose \[ L(C)=	frac12\log rac{2-C}{4},\qquad S_0(C)=e^{-L(C)}\cos(
u L(C)),\qquad S_1(C)=e^{-L(C)} rac{\sin(
u L(C))}{
u}. 	ag{20} \] The neighborhood avoids \(C=2\), and the logarithm is real on its real interval. The sine quotient is regular at zero. Equations (17) and (6) show \[ H_l(x)=S_l(C_N(x))+O_{m hol}(h^2). 	ag{21} \] This estimate descends uniformly in the spectral variable even at the fold \(\xi=1/2\). Here is the needed justification. By (13), its remainder is an even holomorphic function of \(y=\xi-1/2\) on a fixed disk. Its even power series, or the holomorphic local coordinate theorem, makes it a holomorphic function of \(y^2\). Since \(C_N(x)+2=4\sin^2(\pi y)\), the change from \(y^2\) to \(C+2\) is a local biholomorphism with uniform fixed disks. The descended remainder has norm \(O(h^2)\) there. Cauchy's formula on smaller spectral disks gives the same bound for all fixed spectral derivatives. Away from the fold, \(C_N'\) is a unit and ordinary inverse charts suffice. A finite cover gives a common spectral neighborhood of the full real interval, with these uniform bounds. No estimate was divided by a vanishing angular derivative. Accordingly each row quotient in (7) is the ordinary spectral divided difference of a holomorphic function. At \(x=1/2\), where \(C_N(x)=C_N(x-h)\), it equals its spectral derivative. In particular it has a holomorphic extension. Direct differentiation of (20) gives \[ S_0S_{1,C}-S_1S_{0,C}=- rac2{(2-C)^2}. 	ag{22} \] Since \(C_N(x)-C_N(x-h)=O(h)\), (21)--(22) imply \[ \det\mathcal F_N(x) =- rac2{(2-C_N(x))^2}+O(h). 	ag{23} \] It is a uniform unit on a fixed smaller neighborhood of \([a,1-a]\), including the fold and the parameter coalescence. Both the frame and its inverse, with every fixed derivative, are uniformly bounded there. The actual kernel is an ordinary polynomial in \(C\). The pinned endpoint-product estimate gives \(\|K_N(w,\cdot)\|_{[-2,2]}\le CN^p\) uniformly on larger bounded complex parameter sets. Markov's inequality gives polynomial bounds for its fixed spectral derivatives. Hence its divided-color state on this real interval is polynomially bounded, including coincident colors. It follows that \[ \mathbf a_N(x)=\mathcal F_N(x)^{-1}\mathcal V_{u_N}(x) \quad\hbox{satisfies}\quad \|\mathbf a_N(x)\|\le CN^p 	ag{24} \] on the real interval. The vector is holomorphic on the common neighborhood; no small off-real norm of the canonical kernel is used. ## 4. The exact regular recurrence and coefficient reflection Write the original operator as \[ \mathscr J_N f=(c_0+A_N+B_N)f-A_Nf(x+h)-B_Nf(x-h), \] \[ A_N= rac{s_{Nx+1}^4}{s_{2Nx+1}s_{2Nx+2}},\qquad B_N= rac{s_{Nx}^4}{s_{2Nx}s_{2Nx+1}}. \] Set \[ q_N^\sharp=\left( rac{\sin\pi x}{\sin\pi(x+h)}ight)^4, \quad b_N^\sharp= rac1{A_N\Delta_N(x+h)} =- rac{\sin(2\pi x+\pi h)} {16\sin(\pi h)\sin^4\pi(x+h)}, \] \[ T_N^\sharp=  egin{pmatrix} 1+(c_0-w)/A_N&q_N^\sharp\Delta_N(x+h)\ (c_0-w)b_N^\sharp&q_N^\sharp \end{pmatrix},\qquad \mathbf b_N= inom{1/A_N}{b_N^\sharp}. 	ag{25} \] Solving the ordinary equation for its forward value gives exactly \[ \mathcal V_f(x+h)=T_N^\sharp(x)\mathcal V_f(x) -\mathbf b_N(x)(\mathscr J_N-w)f(x). 	ag{26} \] Indeed \((B_N/A_N)\Delta_N(x)/\Delta_N(x+h)=q_N^\sharp\). All expressions in (25) are holomorphic through the fold. On the fixed neighborhood under consideration, \[ T_N^\sharp=I+O(h),\quad (T_N^\sharp)'=O(h),\qquad \|\mathbf b_N\|+\|\mathbf b_N'\|\le CN. 	ag{27} \] These follow from \(c_0-w=O(h^2)\), \(q_N^\sharp=1+O(h)\), and the explicit canceled formula for \(b_N^\sharp\). Thus the separate poles of the original angular coefficients create no singular transfer in this frame. Reflection of the frame is slightly shifted from reflection of the scalar. For every function in (13), \[ \mathcal V_f(1-x)=  egin{pmatrix}1&-\Delta_N(x)\0&1\end{pmatrix} \mathcal V_f(x). 	ag{28} \] The first value is \(f(x-h)\); the spectral divided difference is unchanged when its two arguments are exchanged. Formula (28) holds also at the fold by holomorphic continuation. Applying it to both the actual state and the mode frame proves the exact law \[ \mathbf a_N(1-x)=\mathbf a_N(x),\qquad \mathbf a_N'(1-x)=-\mathbf a_N'(x). 	ag{29} \] ## 5. The physical source fixes the derivative coefficient Let \(\mathbf r_N=(r_0,r_1)\) denote the row of mode residuals from (19), and let \(r_K=(\mathscr J_N-w)u_N\). The original ordinary source, with its sign retained, is \[ r_K(x)=- rac{P_N(w)P_N(C_N(x))}{N^4(C_N(x)-c_0)},\qquad P_N(C_N(x))=4\sin^2(\pi Nx). 	ag{30} \] The denominator is a unit throughout the real interval being used. At every physical point there, \[ r_K(x_j)=r_K'(x_j)=0. 	ag{31} \] This includes the odd middle point in its ordinary angular interpretation. No extra spectral normal at the odd simple root is prescribed. Using (26) for the actual state and both columns of the frame gives the exact coefficient equation \[ \mathbf a_N(x+h)=(I+M_N(x))\mathbf a_N(x)-\ell_N(x)r_K(x), \] \[ \ell_N=\mathcal F_N(x+h)^{-1}\mathbf b_N(x),\qquad M_N=\ell_N\mathbf r_N. 	ag{32} \] Uniform frame bounds, (19), and (27) imply \[ \|M_N(x)\|+\|M_N'(x)\| \le CN^p e^{-NI_\delta(x)} 	ag{33} \] on the real interval. Differentiating (32) before evaluation, then using both equalities in (31), yields at every such grid row \[ \mathbf a_{j+1}=(I+M_j)\mathbf a_j,\qquad \mathbf a_{j+1}'=(I+M_j)\mathbf a_j'+M_j'\mathbf a_j. 	ag{34} \] Thus the independent first normal is retained in its own exact equation. A values-only recurrence would not justify (34). Fix any physical \(x_j\in[a,b_*]\). Propagate (34) from \(j\) to \(N-j\). All rows lie in the symmetric buffered interval, and \(I_\delta(x_l)\ge I_\delta(x_j)\) along this run. There are at most \(N\) factors, and their errors are uniformly exponentially small. Consequently the exact products give \[ \mathbf a_{N-j}'=P_j\mathbf a_j'+Q_j\mathbf a_j,\qquad \|P_j-I\|+\|Q_j\|\le CN^p e^{-NI_\delta(x_j)}. 	ag{35} \] For example \(P_j\) is the product of \(I+M_l\), and \(Q_j\) is the finite sum with one factor \(M_l'\) and the ordinary products on either side. This proves (35) without any assumed bound on \(\mathbf a_j'\). By (29), its left side is \(-\mathbf a_j'\). The matrix \(I+P_j=2I+o(1)\) is uniformly invertible. Combining (24) and (35) therefore proves \[  oxed{\qquad \|\mathbf a_N'(x_j)\| \le CN^p e^{-NI_\delta(x_j)}. \qquad} 	ag{36} \] At the even coincident-color row, the frame itself is already regular; at the odd simple row only its ordinary canonical continuation was used. Neither case introduces a reset datum. For \(x_j\in[a,b]\), the first equation of (34), propagated to the right anchor in (8), similarly gives \[ \|\mathbf a_N(x_j)-\mathbf a_*\| \le CN^p e^{-NI_\delta(x_j)}. 	ag{37} \] Now \(u_N=(H_0,H_1)\mathbf a_N\) identically on the real neighborhood. Differentiate this identity and use (36)--(37), together with the bounded modes and their derivatives. This proves (9). Cauchy's formula on larger rectangles of type (3) gives its fixed parameter derivatives without changing the rate. The polynomial anchor bound and (19) prove (10); the sharp truncation identity in the source gives (11). All functions in (8)--(9) are even in \(\alpha\). On smaller parameter sets they descend holomorphically to \(\alpha^2\), and \(w_N-2\) is an analytic coordinate with derivative \(N^{-2}(1+O(N^{-2}))\) in that variable. Thus fixed original endpoint spectral derivatives cost only further powers of \(N\). The same estimates consequently retain fixed outside normals and finite products by the ordinary product rule. No division by a possibly zero kernel value is involved. ## 6. Scope and complete direct sources The scalar in (8) is the explicitly normalized approximate homogeneous basis combination, anchored by two actual physical values. The new estimate (36) supplies its previously retained normal mismatch. It gives a moderate representative with sharply small full physical-jet error; it does not make that error zero, remove an exterior or interface current, or estimate a scalar closing with arbitrary spectators. The construction does not compare this scalar to the old modified-differential-equation baseline on fractional grids. Such a comparison is unnecessary for (9), and no statement about the old Green boundary packet is inferred. Exact one-sided Hermite repair of the new physical-jet error remains a subsequent source operation with its own retained interface and sides. The following complete direct sources were read at unchanged pins, and their directly used implications checked: * [Sharp sine-factor approximate modes](research_endpoint_sine_factor_sharp_truncation.md), SHA256 c731b1ccc3ea05f65b1227bff048b4e8a32cf36832289a1ed6e390232cc210bd. * [Specified factorial and its logarithmic derivative](research_exact_cyclotomic_factorial.md), SHA256 0f989261f53747266ac62dba40ca7548138012b266521e98a03bd94b450c657b. * [Actual polynomial endpoint bounds](research_endpoint_two_half_plane_relative_source.md), SHA256 985fa3331379c3877734f28773d314b667ee87fa63314a5ef4513a3fe128d194. * [Original ordinary kernel source](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_edge_kernel_difference_and_endpoint_bound.md), SHA256 5d0d07d4d97d82cca66e0e0c3bf2cecad8e5f58ef8329178278b297cf0d6c5da. Only written mathematics and source-text/hash reads were used. No mathematical program, numerical experiment, test, build or compilation was run. Adopted notes and public manuscripts remain unchanged.

title: Primitive periods through regular square corners
text:
# Primitive periods through regular square corners Private written proof, 16 November 2026. A finite regular corner can flatten four of an original edge's eight tetrahedra without making the coupled primitive filling equations singular. In particular, for a proper selected set in a connected original graph, the Hermitian part of the complete selected period Jacobian remains positive definite when every edge is positive or has only one regular corner square. The conclusion holds for arbitrary real signed powers. This note proves the exact kernel transport when there is no fixed outside vertex, and extends the existing exact wire contour construction to these corners. All periods, face maps, wire kernels and logarithmic lifts are the original ones. A continuation of the analytic equations through a corner is not a positive-cell decomposition or a completed hyperbolic metric beyond it. No noncancellation assertion for the quantum source is made. ## 1. The original edge at a regular corner For an ordered edge with angular coordinates \((t,u)\), put \[ a=	an(t/2),\quad b=	an(u/2),\quad q^2=1+a^2+b^2, \qquad J_e= rac1{2q}  egin{pmatrix}1+a^2&-ab\-ab&1+b^2\end{pmatrix}. 	ag{1} \] Here \(J_e\) is the derivative of the two original meridian returns, not the Hessian of a substituted positive invariant. Its determinant is \(1/4\), and \(J_e=-\pi\psi_e''\), with the continued original edge phase \(\psi_e\). For a symmetric complex matrix, \(\Re J_e\) denotes its Hermitian part, equivalently its entrywise real part. Use the original disk and strip coordinates \[ \zeta= rac{a+ib}{q+1}=	anh P,\qquad \xi= rac{a-ib}{q+1}=	anh Q, \quad q= rac{1+\zeta\xi}{1-\zeta\xi},\quad a= rac{\zeta+\xi}{1-\zeta\xi},\quad b= rac{\zeta-\xi}{i(1-\zeta\xi)}. 	ag{2} \] A positive edge has \(|\zeta|,|\xi|<1\). A regular single-square corner has exactly one disk coordinate on the unit circle, away from \(\{1,-1,i,-i\}\), and the other strictly inside. The pinned corner classification proves that its face chart is regular: \(\Re q>0\), and all \(a\pm i,b\pm i,q\pm a,q\pm b,q\pm i\) are nonzero. Four original tetrahedra are flat with distinct vertices; the other four are positive. This excludes two-square corners and all ramified or infinite limits. **Lemma 1.** At a \(P\)-corner \(\zeta=e^{i	heta}\), \[ \Re J_e=\kappa_P  inom{\cos	heta}{-\sin	heta} (\cos	heta,-\sin	heta),\qquad \kappa_P= rac{1-|\xi|^4}{|1-\zeta^2\xi^2|^2}>0, 	ag{3} \] \[ k_P= inom{\sin	heta}{\cos	heta},\qquad J_e k_P= rac i2 inom{\cos	heta}{-\sin	heta}. 	ag{4} \] At a \(Q\)-corner \(\xi=e^{i\varphi}\), \[ \Re J_e=\kappa_Q  inom{\cos\varphi}{\sin\varphi} (\cos\varphi,\sin\varphi),\qquad \kappa_Q= rac{1-|\zeta|^4}{|1-\zeta^2\xi^2|^2}>0, 	ag{5} \] \[ k_Q= inom{-\sin\varphi}{\cos\varphi},\qquad J_e k_Q=- rac i2 inom{\cos\varphi}{\sin\varphi}. 	ag{6} \] In particular every corner kernel has two nonzero coordinates. **Proof.** Substitution in (1) gives \[ J_e= rac1{2(1-\zeta^2\xi^2)}  egin{pmatrix} (1+\zeta^2)(1+\xi^2)&i(\zeta^2-\xi^2)\ i(\zeta^2-\xi^2)&(1-\zeta^2)(1-\xi^2) \end{pmatrix}. 	ag{7} \] One can read its kernel and imaginary action without taking lengthy real parts. The original strip dictionary, with \(f(P)=\arctan	anh P\), is \[ t=2(f(P)+f(Q)),\quad u=-2i(P-Q),\quad r_t=P+Q,\quad r_u=i(f(Q)-f(P)). 	ag{8} \] Consequently the real energy of a complex variation is \[ \Re(\delta r_t\overline{\delta t} +\delta r_u\overline{\delta u}) =4\Re f'(P)|\delta P|^2+4\Re f'(Q)|\delta Q|^2. 	ag{9} \] At the \(P\)-corner, \(f'(P)=-i	an	heta\), while \(\Re f'(Q)>0\). The coordinate Jacobian in (8) has determinant \(4i(f'(P)+f'(Q))
e0\). Thus (9) is positive semidefinite of rank one. Set \(\delta Q=0\) and \(\delta P=i\cos	heta/2\); (8) gives (4). At the \(Q\)-corner set \(\delta P=0\) and \(\delta Q=-i\cos\varphi/2\), obtaining (6). The real kernel therefore determines the rank-one directions in (3) and (5). Their coefficients equal the trace, which is \[ \operatorname{tr}\Re J_e =	frac12\Re(q+q^{-1}) =\Re rac{1+\zeta^2\xi^2}{1-\zeta^2\xi^2}. 	ag{10} \] At the two respective walls this is exactly \(\kappa_P\) or \(\kappa_Q\). The excluded four disk points make every displayed sine and cosine nonzero. \(\square\) ## 2. The assembled kernel and the anchored theorem Let \(G\) be a finite graph with the original endpoint incidence, and let \(S\) be its selected vertices. Outside angular coordinates are fixed. Each selected vertex is incident to an edge. Keep all edges incident to \(S\), each once, with both occurrences of a loop. Assume every such edge is positive or a regular single-square corner. Write \(\iota_e w\) for its ordered endpoint vector, putting zero at an outside endpoint. The actual period and its derivative are \[ \mathcal P_v=\sum_{e
i v}r_{v,e}- rac{i n_vt_v}{2},\qquad J_S=D\mathcal P =\sum_e\iota_e^T J_e\iota_e- rac i2\operatorname{diag}(n_v), \quad n_v\in\mathbb R. 	ag{11} \] Form the graph of corner edges. Mark as pinned every outside vertex and every selected vertex incident to a positive edge. Orient each corner edge temporarily. Its nonzero real gain is \[ g_e=\cot	heta\quad(P	ext{-corner}),\qquad g_e=-\cot\varphi\quad(Q	ext{-corner}). 	ag{12} \] Reversing traversal replaces the gain by its reciprocal. **Theorem 2.** The real kernel of \(\Re J_S\) is exactly the space of assignments satisfying zero at all pins and \(w_{\mathrm{head}(e)}=g_e w_{\mathrm{tail}(e)}\) on every corner edge. Each connected corner component meeting a pin has zero kernel. An unpinned connected component has a one-dimensional kernel precisely when every oriented cycle has gain product one, and has zero kernel otherwise. Its nonzero kernel generator has no zero coordinate. These statements include parallel edges; a loop imposes \((1-g_e)w_v=0\). In particular, if \(G\) is connected and \(\varnothing
e S
e V(G)\), then \[ \Re J_S>0. 	ag{13} \] **Proof.** Every edge Hermitian form is nonnegative. A positive edge has zero form only when its full endpoint variation is zero. By Lemma 1 a corner has zero form exactly when its endpoint variation obeys (12). The filling term contributes no Hermitian part. Thus the kernel is exactly the stated simultaneous constraint space. Propagation from one vertex determines all values on a connected corner component. A pin forces them all to vanish. Otherwise the path values are consistent precisely when all cycle products are one, proving the dimension statement. For (13), extend a kernel assignment by zero outside \(S\). Along any original graph path, a positive edge makes both endpoint values zero, and a corner propagates a zero in either direction. Every selected vertex has a path to an outside vertex. Thus the whole assignment is zero. Positive semidefiniteness now gives positive definiteness. The same reasoning applies to complex vectors by complexification. \(\square\) When the fixed outside angles are zero, a boundary edge in fact cannot be a single-square corner: (2) gives \(\zeta=\xi\) if its second endpoint has \(b=0\). Under our alternatives that edge must therefore be positive. The pin proof does not require this extra observation and also allows other fixed regular angles. On a compact family with these hypotheses, fixed graph and selected set, continuity and (13) give a uniform constant \(\Re J_S\ge\gamma I\), \(\gamma>0\). This assertion excludes approach to two-square corners or any of the specified singular limits. No constant uniform over arbitrary graphs is claimed. ## 3. The exact imaginary obstruction when there is no anchor The gain criterion also determines when a null direction of the Hermitian part can be a null direction of the complex Jacobian. Let \(\mathcal K=\ker_{\mathbb R}\Re J_S\). Define a real skew matrix \(K\) on selected vertices by adding, for each oriented corner edge \(v	o w\), \[ K_{vw}=+1,\ K_{wv}=-1\quad(P	ext{-corner}),\qquad K_{vw}=-1,\ K_{wv}=+1\quad(Q	ext{-corner}). 	ag{14} \] Contributions are summed; the two entries of a loop cancel. The ordered edge chart fixes whether (14) is the P or Q case. **Proposition 3.** For \(w\in\mathcal K\), \[ J_Sw= rac i2(K-\operatorname{diag}n)w, 	ag{15} \] \[ \ker_{\mathbb C}J_S= \{w\in\mathcal K\otimes\mathbb C: (K-\operatorname{diag}n)w=0\}. 	ag{16} \] Consequently each unpinned gain-balanced component can be tested using its single real generator \(h\). A necessary condition for singularity on that component is \[ \sum_v n_vh_v^2=0. 	ag{17} \] If on each such component all powers have one weak sign and at least one is nonzero, \(J_S\) is nonsingular. **Proof.** Equations (4) and (6) give (15) edge by edge; positive edges vanish on \(\mathcal K\). If \(J_Sz=0\), then \(z^*(\Re J_S)z=0\), whence \(z\in\mathcal K\otimes\mathbb C\). Equation (15) proves (16). The residual matrix is real, so a complex kernel exists precisely when a real one exists. Distinct unpinned corner components do not couple in (15). On one such component a nonzero vector is a multiple of \(h\); multiply its residual equation by \(h^T\) and use \(h^TKh=0\) to obtain (17). All entries of \(h\) are nonzero, giving the sign conclusion. \(\square\) This last conclusion gives a nonsingular complex Jacobian. It does not give strict horizontal descent when \(\mathcal K
e0\). ## 4. Marked continuation and local descent Retain the original logarithms from a supplied positive germ up to the regular corner, and their local continuation there. The original face denominators and (1) are regular, so this continuation exists without resetting any logarithmic period. With cone charges \(c_v\), the original reduced phase is \[ F=\sum_e\psi_e(t_v,t_w) + rac i{4\pi}\sum_{v\in S}n_vt_v^2 -i\sum_{v\in S}c_vt_v, \qquad F'=-\mathcal P/\pi-ic, \qquad -F''=J_S/\pi. 	ag{18} \] At a supplied solution \(\mathcal P=-\pi ic\), Theorem 2 for a proper selected set gives a unique local holomorphic solution of the primitive equations as their parameters vary through the wall. In a sufficiently small convex neighborhood the Hermitian part remains positive definite, even on the side where some original tetrahedra have become negatively oriented. If \(\Re J_S\ge\gamma I\) there, then for real \(h\) in that neighborhood, \[ \Re F(t_*+h)\le\Re F(t_*)- rac\gamma{2\pi}|h|^2. 	ag{19} \] This follows by integrating (18) twice on the horizontal segment. The same positivity proves local injectivity of the period map by integrating its Jacobian along complex straight segments. The compact-family bound after Theorem 2 supplies uniform local coercivity; the usual finite subcover argument supplies local continuation neighborhoods on a compact family of marked solutions. For actual integral fillings, the original carrier \(\eta_v\) and coefficient \(p_v\) give \(n_v=\eta_v-2p_v\), and \[ U_v=2\sum_{e
i v}r_{v,e}-i\eta_vt_v,\qquad V_v=2it_v,\qquad U_v+p_vV_v=-2\pi ic_v. 	ag{20} \] Thus the continuation is of the marked primitive period, including the carrier. It is not merely an exponentiated slope equation. It does not assert that an arbitrary short hyperbolic filling reaches this configuration, or that the continued representation is discrete and faithful beyond it. ## 5. An exact wire contour through the regular corner The product-contour theorem has a useful extension at these same points. This statement uses the original same-index wire phase; reversed wires require their own retained phase dictionary. **Lemma 4.** If \((a,b)\) is a regular single-square corner, every proper independent contraction \((\lambda a,\mu b)\), \(0\le\lambda,\mu\le1\), is positive. The unchanged endpoint retains \(\Re q>0\). **Proof.** The canonical angles still obey \(|\Re t|,|\Re u|<\pi\), by (8). Thus \(a,b\in\mathcal A=\mathbb C\setminus(i[1,\infty)\cup-i[1,\infty))\). Write \(a=A+i\alpha,b=B+i eta\), and \(X=A^2+B^2,\ C=A eta-B\alpha\). The boundary of the positive-edge criterion at this regular point is \(C^2=X\). Here \(X>0\): otherwise both tangents are purely imaginary and the boundary would have \(q=0\), contrary to \(\Re q>0\). Moreover \(A,B
e0\). For example, if \(A=0\) and \(B
e0\), equality implies \(\alpha^2=1\), excluded by \(a\in\mathcal A\). For \(\lambda\mu>0\), \[ \lambda^2A^2+\mu^2B^2-\lambda^2\mu^2C^2 =\lambda^2(1-\mu^2)A^2+\mu^2(1-\lambda^2)B^2>0 	ag{21} \] unless \(\lambda=\mu=1\). The strict positive-edge criterion therefore holds at every such proper contraction. If one factor is zero, the other tangent stays in \(\mathcal A\); the complete-end edge is positive there. \(\square\) For a target graph made of positive edges and regular single-square corners, Lemma 4 and the existing positive contraction lemma show that every pair on the finite arms \([-a_v^*,a_v^*]	imes[-a_w^*,a_w^*]\) has discriminant \(1+a^2+b^2\) off \((-\infty,0]\). At unchanged corner pairs this follows from \(\Re q>0\); sign changes preserve the square. Pairs on \((\mathbb R\cup[-a_v^*,a_v^*])	imes (\mathbb R\cup[-a_w^*,a_w^*])\) have the same property: if one tangent is real, the other belongs to \(\mathcal A\), and a real nonpositive discriminant is impossible. The explicit compact-and-tail neighborhood proof in the pinned product-contour theorem now applies without change to this skeleton. Namely, take the union of a sufficiently thin horizontal strip and a sufficiently thin neighborhood of each finite arm. On real tails the real part of the discriminant is positive; on the remaining compact pairs its distance from the excluded ray is positive. These give symmetric star-shaped tangent domains and simply connected angular domains \(V_v\), chosen independently of \(N\), containing the full intervals \((-\pi,\pi)\) and the corner target. On their product, \[ \Re q_e>0,\qquad \cot(\pi x_e^*)=q_e, \quad 0<\Re x_e^*<	frac12, \qquad H_e= rac{2\pi q_e(1+q_e^2)^2} {(1+a_v^2)(1+a_w^2)}
e0. 	ag{22} \] The branches are even in each angle and agree with the original ones along the contraction to completeness. **Corollary 5.** Suppose the traced target angles have negative imaginary parts. The exact full-Hermite joint factorial-lens source has a representative whose fixed-endpoint wire paths pass through the stationary graph (22), including this regular corner. Every original coupon, normal, free boundary polynomial and framing factor is retained. No wire seam current is introduced. **Proof.** Put \(b_N=-1/(2N)\), \(N\ge2\). The pinned exact factorial theorem gives holomorphy of both direct and reflected halfwires on compact subsets of \(\Re x\in[b_N,b_N+1],\ |\Re t|<\pi\), without a bound on their finite imaginary heights. Choose full lower angular arcs in \(V_v\) through the targets and retain the exact lens trace. For each angular tuple replace the horizontal wire interval by \[ b_N+ih_e\longrightarrow x_e^*(t_v,t_w) \longrightarrow b_N+1+ih_e. 	ag{23} \] The real parts stay inside the same convex interval. Straight interpolation gives a compact holomorphic homotopy fixing both endpoints. Cauchy's theorem on each fiber, followed by the retained angular integrals, proves exact equality. Angular derivatives of the wire paths wedge to zero against the angular volume form. This is the proof of the pinned exact source theorem, with the extended product domain now justified by Lemma 4. In particular it retains the odd simple node and all double-node normals. \(\square\) At a marked primitive critical point covered by Theorem 2, these paths can include coherent local wire coordinates with \(F_e=\psi_e-\xi_e^2/2\), since \(H_e
e0\). Real \(\xi_e\) and horizontal selected angular coordinates give, by (18)--(19), a strictly descending local contour for the continued original selected phase. The square-root construction of those coordinates is exactly the one in the pinned unsummed-source proof. It remains valid at the corner because every factor in (22) is a unit. Small connectors join this local segment to (23) without moving its endpoints. This last stationary interpretation requires the same-index phase at each endpoint; the exact identity with a true free boundary polynomial does not identify its asymptotic phase with a factorial phase. Nor does holomorphy of the exact reciprocal factorials imply their nonvanishing. All factorial zeros, connectors, other angular sectors and coherent trace terms remain present. No estimate here shows they are smaller or prevents cancellation of the local term. ## Direct sources and scope of the extension The earlier positive-domain theorems establish strict positivity before a corner. The new assertions are the rank-one boundary identities, their exact graph kernel and skew-action tests, the automatic anchored coercivity, and the extension of the existing exact contour construction to regular single-square corners. - [Original positive edge periods](research_positive_edge_global_monotonicity.md): disk/strip dictionary, positive criterion, original returns and marked graph periods. Full proof read at SHA256 `da5129c7110190035eedb8249d4004dd06b5a7555e78d948234d8de50fa17500`. - [Original corner classification](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_square_corner_flat_geometry.md): Sections 1--3, regularity and the distinction from two-square corners. Full proof read at SHA256 `511c2c93d61482664cf62ed3b146c0af19ffbb149fa8772a4d1eb5ca7026eed0`. - [Original phase Hessian](research_cone_chamber_accretivity.md): (1)--(5), (12)--(15), (19)--(20), phase normalization, Hermitian interpretation and primitive carrier. Full proof read at SHA256 `7dd2888717147bd7e48c2d8a08c8ea9819c12329a9b2e83e02c40c27cf8da803`. - [Unsummed original phase](research_unsummed_network_phase_coercivity.md): (1)--(4), Section 5, same-index scope, stationary wire, Hessian and parameter Morse construction. Full text read at SHA256 `b5441bb508d3ffad3274e38dda2d6aeb099d08ae2ab043a0d12c25234e4a1e1e`. - [Exact product source contour](research_positive_wire_product_contour.md): Sections 1--5, skeleton construction, reciprocal-factorial holomorphy, exact full-Hermite source and fixed wire endpoints. Full proof read at SHA256 `5646f2d6b2a8dfa2d8c49662d17f19f3743fc4efcaf3c3685c6a899975a4c230`. All work is written mathematics; no mathematical program, numerical evaluation or test is used. The result is local analytic continuation and exact contour reachability at a specified regular corner. It does not prove existence of the corner solution, arbitrary-short-filling coverage, a positive retriangulation, or survival of its coefficient in the original finite source.

title: Phase exclusion for an original regular spectral window
status: Regular-window phase gap relative to the source envelope
text:
# Phase exclusion for an original regular spectral window 31 October 2026. The straddling-window theorem in §§1–6 estimates a literal start/end window, retaining every unused row, omitted-half mode and raw sign. Its conclusion is an exponential loss relative to that window’s positive envelope, not a bound by hyperbolic volume. Sections 7–8 give the full-row extension and shared-torus consequence. ## 1. Literal window and hypotheses Put \(d=N-1\), \(m=\lfloor N/2floor\), \(M=m-1\), \(	heta=\pi/N\), \(\sigma=-2\cos(2\pi\delta)\), and \[ \alpha_r=2\cos((2r+1)	heta)-\sigma,\qquad  eta_r=s_r^2,\quad \gamma_r=s_rs_{r-1}\alpha_{r-1}, \quad s_r=2\sin(r	heta),\qquad A_{\mathrm{rest}}^\alpha=\prod_{r=m}^{d}\alpha_r. \] The active companion and its tail are \[ C_r= egin{pmatrix} eta_r(x+y)&\gamma_rxy\1&0\end{pmatrix}, \qquad K_{i,j}=e_1^TC_j\cdots C_{i+1}e_1, \quad K_{i,i}=1.	ag{1} \] All face moduli \(x_0,y_0,b_0,c_0\) are strictly positive and range over a fixed compact set. The real spectral coordinate ranges over a compact subset of \((0,1/2)\). Write \[  egin{aligned} \alpha(t)&=4[\cos^2(\pi t)-\sin^2(\pi\delta)],\ \Lambda_+(t)&=2\sin(\pi t)\left[(x_0+y_0)\sin(\pi t) +\sqrt{\sin^2(\pi t)(x_0-y_0)^2+4x_0y_0\cos^2(\pi\delta)}ight],\ L_\delta(t)&=\Lambda_+(t)/|\alpha(t)|. \end{aligned} \] Assume the original positive weighted endpoint action \[ F(\mu,
u)=\mu\log b_0+(1-
u)\log c_0 +\int_{\mu}^{
u}\log L_\delta(t)\,dt, 	ag{2} \] has uniformly strict interior endpoint maxima \(\mu_*<t_c<
