u_*\), where \(t_c=1/2-\delta\). The logarithmic pole in (2) is integrable. Choose disjoint closed row windows \(I_\mu,I_
u\Subset(0,1/2)\), away from \(t_c\), whose maxima are uniformly interior. Work on one compact parameter chart with fixed windows; a finite collection covers a compact family. The action separates into a function of the start and a function of the stop. Strict maximality therefore gives a fixed loss at either boundary of either window, uniformly in the other endpoint. Shrink the windows further so that the middle modulus \(b_0|\alpha(t)|\), respectively \(c_0|\alpha(t)|\), stays strictly above the active secondary eigenvalue's modulus. This is possible: at the maximum it equals \(\Lambda_+\), while \(|\Lambda_-|<\Lambda_+\) uniformly on the compact chart. Let \(i\) and \(j\) run over all integers in \(NI_\mu\) and \(NI_
u\). The exact raw window is \[ W_N=(-1)^dA_{\mathrm{rest}}^\alpha\sum_{i,j} b^ic^{d-j}\prod_{r<i}\alpha_r\prod_{j<r\le M}\alpha_r K_{i,j}(x,y),	ag{3} \] where \(x=x_0e^{i\vartheta_x}\), and similarly for \(y,b,c\). Define \(E_N\) by taking the face moduli in each summand, the absolute values of both unused products and \(A_{\mathrm{rest}}^\alpha\), and the positive tail \(K_{i,j}(x_0,y_0)\). This is the original positive window envelope. No division by \(A_{\mathrm{rest}}^\alpha\) is used. For each \(\varepsilon>0\), there are uniform constants \(c,C>0\) and \(N_0\) such that \[  oxed{|W_N|\le Ce^{-cN}E_N}	ag{4} \] whenever the phase quadruple is at distance at least \(\varepsilon\), modulo \(2\pi\), from \[ \vartheta_x=\vartheta_y=\vartheta_b=\vartheta_c-\pi. 	ag{5} \] One can use the maximum of these three relative phase distances. If the omitted-half scalar is zero, both sides of (4) are zero exactly. ## 2. Every active subproduct has a positive comparison Set \[ \eta_r=1+ rac{\alpha_{r-1}}{s_rs_{r-1}},\qquad G_r= egin{pmatrix}1&- eta_ry\0& eta_ry\end{pmatrix}. \] On the present row range, \(G_r\) and its inverse are uniformly bounded. Direct multiplication gives the exact identity \[ G_rC_rG_{r-1}^{-1} = eta_r egin{pmatrix}x&\eta_rx\y&y\end{pmatrix}. 	ag{6} \] The real \(\eta_r\) are bounded above and below by positive constants. The absolute entries on the right of (6), at arbitrary outer phases, are exactly their positive-modulus entries. Products inherit this bound. Moreover, the two columns of a nonempty positive product are uniformly comparable: compare the columns in its rightmost factor, then multiply on the left by positive matrices. Since \(G_ue_1=e_1\) and \(e_1^TG_v^{-1}=(1,1)\), the positive \(K_{u,v}\) is the product of the \( eta\)'s times the first-column sum of the positive word product. Column comparability and bounded gauge endpoints consequently give, for every active subinterval, \[ \|C_v(x,y)\cdots C_{u+1}(x,y)\| \le C_0K_{u,v}(x_0,y_0).	ag{7} \] The empty product uses \(K_{u,u}=1\). This does not replace the signed companion recurrence by its entrywise absolute value. Split products can also be reassembled at bounded cost. For consecutive positive word products \(P_1,P_2\), column comparability gives \[ (\mathbf1^TP_2e_1)(\mathbf1^TP_1e_1) \le C_1\mathbf1^TP_2P_1e_1. \] The empty cases are immediate. Restoring the \( eta\) factors yields \[ K_{v,w}(x_0,y_0)K_{u,v}(x_0,y_0) \le C_1K_{u,w}(x_0,y_0),\qquad u\le v\le w. 	ag{8} \] This is used for a fixed number of consecutive pieces, not with a fixed loss multiplied over \(O(N)\) pieces. The [exact positive-word angular estimate](research_positive_eta_word_transfer.md) implies \[ |K_{i,j}(x,y)|\le e^{-c_1N}K_{i,j}(x_0,y_0)	ag{9} \] when the outer relative phase is separated from zero. Each selected interval has macroscopic length. Summing (9) termwise proves (4) in this case, retaining all scalar factors and their zeros. ## 3. The two restricted switches are literal finite matrices Write \(p_-\le i\le p_+\), \(q_-\le j\le q_+\) for the integer windows, with \(p_+<q_-\). On the start window use \[ T_r^{\mathrm{start}}=  egin{pmatrix}C_r&u\0&b\alpha_r\end{pmatrix}, \qquad u=e_1.	ag{10} \] Let \(U_N\) be its product's \(2\)-by-\(1\) off-diagonal block. On the stop window use \[ T_r^{\mathrm{stop}}=  egin{pmatrix}c\alpha_r&w_r\0&C_r\end{pmatrix}, \qquad w_r=e_1^TC_r=( eta_r(x+y),\gamma_rxy). 	ag{11} \] Let \(V_N\) be its product's \(1\)-by-\(2\) off-diagonal block. Then \[  egin{aligned} W_N={}&(-1)^d A_{\mathrm{rest}}^\alpha c^{d-M} \left(\prod_{q_+<r\le M}c\alpha_right) V_N(C_{q_--1}\cdots C_{p_++1})U_N \left(\prod_{r<p_-}b\alpha_right). \end{aligned}	ag{12} \] Empty products are identities. A start at \(i\) supplies the seed \(e_1\); a stop at \(j\) reads \(e_1^T\) after \(C_j\) acts. Thus its active factor is precisely (1). The disjoint windows exclude \(i=j\) because that path is outside their specified support. The [unrestricted four-state identity](research_original_one_sided_four_state_transfer.md) retains that diagonal path. Formula (12) introduces no pivot, factor of \(N\), or source renormalization. ## 4. A mismatched middle separates the whole active block It remains to consider small outer relative phase. Remove the common outer phase \(\vartheta_o=\vartheta_y\). At exactly equal outer phases, a constant unitary diagonal change of basis makes the active companion \(e^{i\vartheta_o}\) times its real companion. Both active eigenvalues have this common phase relative to their real, signed values. On the start window \(\alpha>0\), so the scalar phase is \(\vartheta_b\). A mismatch from \(\vartheta_o\) separates it from the Perron eigenvalue; the window's modulus condition separates it from the secondary eigenvalue for every phase. On the stop window \(\alpha<0\), the scalar phase is \(\vartheta_c+\pi\), and the same argument applies. If the quadruple stays away from (5), either (9) applies or at least one of these middle mismatches stays uniformly nonzero. Taking the outer-phase threshold sufficiently small preserves the full Sylvester separation. The exact coefficients are analytic in \(t\) and \(h=1/N\): \[  egin{aligned} \alpha_h(t)&=4\cos^2(\pi(t+h/2))-4\sin^2(\pi\delta),\  eta(t)&=4\sin^2(\pi t),\ \gamma_h(t)&=4\sin(\pi t)\sin(\pi(t-h))\alpha_h(t-h). \end{aligned}	ag{13} \] The uniform real separation extends to a fixed complex neighborhood of the relevant window. The bounded analytic Sylvester inverse there checks all hypotheses of the [analytic discrete-switch theorem](research_analytic_switching_suppression.md). There is no guessed interpolation of the discrete start or stop. Apply that theorem to (10) or (11), whichever has the mismatch. Its exact off-diagonal product consists of two pure endpoint terms and a sum with an exponentially small residual coupling. The scalar blocks remain \(b\alpha_r\) or \(c\alpha_r\). They do not occur in the same Sylvester equation, so no separation between them is required. ## 5. Both endpoints and the residual return to the original envelope Let \(T_{ij}\) be the positive summand of (3) without the common \(|A_{\mathrm{rest}}^\alpha|\). The compact positive-transfer Perron bounds and the unused-interval Riemann products give uniformly \[ \log T_{ij}=NF(i/N,j/N)+O(\log N),\qquad \sum_{i,j}T_{ij}=\exp\{NF(\mu_*,
u_*)+O(\log N)\}. 	ag{14} \] The unused intervals stay away from the pole. The active interval crosses it, but the positive word matrix remains regular. The identity \(\int_0^{1/2}\log|\alpha(t)|\,dt=0\) is used only to rewrite the already bounded products into (2); it creates no finite division at a sampled zero. Use (7) to bound complex active subproducts and (8) to reassemble a fixed number of pieces into the original unsplit \(K_{i,j}\). Bounded gauge vectors can replace the endpoint \(e_1\)'s at bounded cost. Each of the two pure gauge terms fixes the relevant switch at a window boundary, within one mesh step, while all other starts or stops and exterior factors remain unchanged. Strict maximality and separability of (2) therefore give \[ 	ext{each endpoint term} \le \operatorname{poly}(N) \exp\{N[F(\mu_*,
u_*)-\gamma]\},\qquad \gamma>0. 	ag{15} \] Both terms are kept. Neither is assumed absent. For a residual insertion, (7)–(8) and bounded one-row couplings compare its weight with a constant times the original positive summand at that row, up to one mesh shift. The unused \(\alpha\)'s on the two windows are bounded away from zero, so these shifts cost bounded factors. Only polynomially many locations are summed. Thus \[ 	ext{residual contribution} \le \operatorname{poly}(N)e^{-c_2N}\sum_{i,j}T_{ij}. 	ag{16} \] Together (14)–(16) prove (4). Multiply the common omitted-half scalar back exactly, including its zeros; no nonvanishing scalar amplitude is asserted. ## 6. Limits of the local conclusion The proof requires positive ordinary face moduli and strict regular endpoint maxima. It does not cover spectral caps, row-endpoint or pole-touching windows, or a maximum on its window boundary. One zero outer weight reduces the active recurrence to first order and admits a scalar version under the same strict-window assumptions, but that case is not used here. A protected middle needs a different start specification. Incompatible local phase requirements may permit (4) at one port of a shared torus. They do not by themselves compare the resulting envelope with complete volume or show that these windows cover the full source. ## 7. Full-row regular windows The polynomial identity extends to the full numerator by taking \(M=d\) and \(A_{\mathrm{rest}}^\alpha=1\) in (3) and (12). It is the same original path sum over \(0\le i\le j\le d\), with all outside diagonal factors retained. For \(2\le r\le d\), \[ \eta_r=  rac{\cos	heta+\cos(2\pi\delta)} {\cos	heta-\cos((2r-1)	heta)}>0 	ag{17} \] for all sufficiently large \(N\) on the fixed interior spectral chart. On compact row intervals inside \((0,1)\), it is uniformly positive and bounded. Hence (6)–(9) apply unchanged. The limiting formulas for \(\alpha,\Lambda_+\) and \(L_\delta\) also hold throughout \((0,1)\). Choose two disjoint fixed windows inside \((0,1)\), staying away from the two zeros \(1/2\pm\delta\) of \(\alpha\). Assume (2) has strict interior maxima in those windows, and shrink them to satisfy the same secondary-modulus separation. The proof of (4) is then unchanged, with alignment \[ \vartheta_x=\vartheta_y =\vartheta_b+\arg\alpha(\mu_*) =\vartheta_c+\arg\alpha(
u_*), \qquad \arg\alpha\in\{0,\pi\}. 	ag{18} \] The signs are constant on the selected windows for large \(N\). The rate differences in (14) are still given by (2), with the continuous normalization \(\int_0^1\log|\alpha(t)|\,dt=0\). No absolute rate formula for a possibly zero common scalar factor is needed. The before and after unused intervals may contain a pole when a full-row window lies beyond it. Such a factor is common to every selected term; factor it out exactly before applying the estimates. Only the varying parts on the two windows need the smooth Riemann-product bounds. More explicitly, factoring the products below the first window and above the second window leaves (12), whose variable scalar products stay in the pole-free windows. The active middle interval is controlled by (6). The boundary gaps are differences of (2), so any factored common scalar has no effect. Its zeros again make both sides zero. This proves the full-row version with no assumed nonzero sampled factors. It covers the usual regular sign pairs \((+,+)\), \((+,-)\), and \((-,+)\) when the corresponding strict-window hypotheses hold; no classification of all critical or boundary configurations is required. The [finite window audit](../experiments/audit_research_regular_spectral_window_phase_exclusion.py) and its [recorded output](../experiments/research_regular_spectral_window_phase_exclusion_results.json) check 402 exact half-row and full-row matrix/path identities, including sampled spectral zeros and zero outer weights. This checks the finite dictionary, not the analytical exponential estimate or a new physical-matrix interface. ## 8. An exact shared-torus consequence Fix the original incidence graph and protected-face specialization. Let \(J\) be a finite set of ports satisfying the full-row or half-row window theorem above, with all four incident weights positive. Other ports may have any certified absolute torus majorants \(M_{e,N}(L)\). Use one shared positive radius \(L_f\) for each ordinary face and the original coefficient target \(d\) there; protected variables remain zero. For each regular port impose (18) on its incident face phases. These are equations of the form \(\vartheta_f-\vartheta_g=0\) or \(\pi\). They have a simultaneous torus solution exactly when their signed incidence graph has even label sum around every cycle. Thus an inconsistent \(\mathbb F_2\) system has no torus solution. Compactness of the phase torus supplies \(\varepsilon>0\) such that at every phase point some port in \(J\) is at least \(\varepsilon\) from its alignment locus. Apply (4) at that port and the ordinary positive-envelope bound at all other selected ports. The original Cauchy coefficient formula gives \[ \left|[	ext{original targets}] \prod_{e\in J}W_{e,N}\prod_{e
otin J}P_{e,N}ight| \le Ce^{-cN}  rac{\displaystyle\prod_{e\in J}E_{e,N}(L) \prod_{e
otin J}M_{e,N}(L)} {\displaystyle\prod_{f	ext{ ordinary}}L_f^d}. 	ag{19} \] There is no independent choice of radii at each incidence and no alteration of the original target. The homogeneous common phase is harmless. Any external source characters must be retained separately in their original normalization. Formula (19) is an exponential improvement on the specified shared window envelope, uniform for a fixed diagram and compact regular parameters. It does not show that this envelope is at most \(e^{N\Phi_D}\), exclude consistent phase systems, or control the omitted irregular windows.

title: Fractional odd-cycle packing for the original regular-window source
status: Fractional odd-cycle loss; conditional shared-source rate
text:
# Fractional odd-cycle packing for the original regular-window source This regular cycle-packing lemma has local hypotheses. It gives neither a covering statement nor equality of volume and source rates. ## 1. Original face phases and certified local losses Keep one positive radius \(L_f\) and one phase \(\vartheta_f\) per original ordinary face, with the unchanged target exponent \(t_f(N)\). For the original homogeneous source this is \(d=N-1\). Protected variables are specialized to zero as in that source. Let \(J\) consist of selected original ports whose literal start/stop windows satisfy either the four-positive regular-window theorem or the [one-protected-outer theorem](research_protected_outer_window_phase_exclusion.md). In the latter case exactly one outer weight is zero and the other three incident weights are positive. Write \(W_{e,N}\) for the actual window polynomial and \(E_{e,N}(L)\) for its positive envelope. Every unused row, scalar zero and raw sign stays in these definitions. At other ports use certified phase-uniform majorants \(M_{e,N}(L)\) for their actual factors. Index the supported incidences at a port separately, even if they meet the same face. A protected zero incidence is omitted and has no phase variable. The required alignment has the form \[ \vartheta_{f(a)}=\varphi_e+\pi\epsilon_a\pmod{2\pi}, \qquad a	ext{ incident to }e,\quad \epsilon_a\in\mathbb F_2, 	ag{1} \] with a free common phase \(\varphi_e\). A straddling LEFT window has labels \((0,0,1,0)\) in the order \((x,b,c,y)\); full-row windows use the actual signs at their two endpoints. In a one-protected-outer window delete the zero incidence from this list; the remaining three labels are exactly those in its scalar-active theorem. Let \(|\cdot|_{\mathbb T}\) be circular distance modulo \(2\pi\), and set \[ d_e(\vartheta)=\min_{\varphi\in\mathbb T} \max_{a	ext{ at }e} |\vartheta_{f(a)}-\varphi-\pi\epsilon_a|_{\mathbb T}. 	ag{2} \] The minimum exists by compactness. This is precisely distance from the local alignment in the product supremum metric. To compare with the relative-phase version of the local theorem, fix one incidence \(a_0\) and put \[ D_e=\max_{a	ext{ at }e} |(\vartheta_{f(a)}-\pi\epsilon_a) -(\vartheta_{f(a_0)}-\pi\epsilon_{a_0})|_{\mathbb T}. \] The circular triangle inequality and the choice of \(a_0\) give \(d_e\le D_e\le2d_e\). Hence, for each fixed \(\eta>0\), the local theorem supplies \(c_e>0\), \(C_e\ge1\), and \(N_e\) such that \[  egin{aligned} |W_{e,N}|&\le C_e e^{-c_eN}E_{e,N}(L) &&	ext{if }d_e\ge\eta,\ |W_{e,N}|&\le E_{e,N}(L)&&	ext{for every phase}. \end{aligned}	ag{3} \] The second inequality is the original positive-envelope bound. A zero common scalar makes both sides zero exactly; no local value is divided out. ## 2. Odd cycles force a collection of mismatched ports Form the bipartite incidence multigraph with ordinary-face vertices, selected-port vertices, and the labeled incidences (1). Repeated edges remain distinct. A simple cycle here has no repeated vertices except its initial/final vertex; two distinct parallel edges are allowed to form a length-two cycle. Protected zero incidences are absent. Choose a nonempty finite collection \(\mathcal C\) of cycles for which the sum of the incidence labels is odd. Let \(r_{\max}\) be the largest number of port vertices on one of these cycles. Fix \[ \eta= rac{\pi}{4r_{\max}},\qquad B(\vartheta)=\{e\in J:d_e(\vartheta)\ge\eta\}. 	ag{4} \] Then \(B(\vartheta)\) meets every cycle in \(\mathcal C\). Indeed, choose a minimizing \(\varphi_e\) at each port on the cycle and subtract its two incidence equations. Upon summing around the cycle, the face phases telescope, while the odd label sum leaves \(\pi\) modulo \(2\pi\). Applying the circular triangle inequality gives \[ \pi\le2\sum_{e	ext{ on }C}d_e(\vartheta). 	ag{5} \] If every port of \(C\) were outside \(B\), the right side would be strictly below \(2r_{\max}\eta=\pi/2\), a contradiction. This uses only the original incidence multigraph; no white-sphere topology is needed. ## 3. Fractional cycle capacities give an additive loss Take every \(c_e\) in (3) at the same threshold (4). Define \[ \kappa_{\mathcal C}=\max_{\lambda_C\ge0} \left\{\sum_{C\in\mathcal C}\lambda_C: \sum_{C
i e}\lambda_C\le c_e 	ext{ for all }e\in Jight\}. 	ag{6} \] This finite linear program has a finite attained positive value. Every cycle contains a port, so its variable is bounded by that port's finite capacity. The feasible set is therefore compact. A sufficiently small positive weight on any single odd cycle proves positivity. For any feasible packing, (5) implies \[  egin{aligned} \sum_{e\in B(\vartheta)}c_e &\ge\sum_{C\in\mathcal C}\lambda_C |B(\vartheta)\cap C|\ &\ge\sum_{C\in\mathcal C}\lambda_C. \end{aligned}	ag{7} \] Consequently every phase point has total certified loss at least \(\kappa_{\mathcal C}\). For a port-disjoint collection one obtains the simple lower bound \[ \kappa_{\mathcal C}\ge \sum_{C\in\mathcal C}\min_{e\in C}c_e. 	ag{8} \] Overlapping cycles can improve the packing value; their phases are not assumed independent. The capacities are analytic inputs, not automatically known numerical constants. If a different cycle collection changes \(r_{\max}\), the threshold and its certified \(c_e\)'s must be checked again. Alternatively one may fix the smaller threshold \(\pi/(4|J|)\) once and then compare cycle collections using that common set of capacities. ## 4. The unchanged Cauchy coefficient At selected ports set \(P_{e,N}=W_{e,N}\). Multiply (3) over the bad ports, use the envelope bounds elsewhere, and then apply (7). Uniformly on the one original phase torus, for \(N\ge\max_eN_e\), \[ \left|\prod_eP_{e,N}ight| \le C e^{-\kappa_{\mathcal C}N} \prod_{e\in J}E_{e,N}(L) \prod_{e
otin J}M_{e,N}(L), \qquad C=\prod_{e\in J}C_e. 	ag{9} \] Use formal face variables \(z_f\), distinct from their radii \(L_f\). The original Cauchy formula gives \[  oxed{\displaystyle \left|\left[\prod_f z_f^{t_f(N)}ight]\prod_eP_{e,N}(z)ight| \le C e^{-\kappa_{\mathcal C}N}  rac{\prod_{e\in J}E_{e,N}(L) \prod_{e
otin J}M_{e,N}(L)} {\prod_fL_f^{t_f(N)}}.} 	ag{10} \] All protected specializations, source target exponents and scalar modes remain unchanged. There is one radius per original face, not one per incidence. Any external source character or prefactor retains its actual modulus separately; no such factor is silently discarded in (10). ## 5. A conditional strict source-rate certificate Let \[ B_L=\limsup_{N	o\infty} rac1N\log  rac{\prod_{e\in J}E_{e,N}(L) \prod_{e
otin J}M_{e,N}(L)} {\prod_fL_f^{t_f(N)}}, 	ag{11} \] with \(\log0=-\infty\). Then (10) bounds the actual window coefficient's normalized logarithmic limsup by \(B_L-\kappa_{\mathcal C}\). For a diagram with certified complete rate \(\Phi_D=\operatorname{Vol}(Y_D)/(2\pi)\), \[ B_L-\kappa_{\mathcal C}<\Phi_D,	ag{12} \] is a sufficient strict-rate certificate for this original window piece. It strengthens merely recording that some positive phase loss exists. It does not establish (12) without quantitative envelope and local-loss inputs. A polynomial-size family of pieces can be summed only with uniform estimates. Precisely, it suffices that the positive quotient for each piece \(p\) be at most \(\exp\{N(B_p+\omega_N)\}\), where \(\omega_N	o0\) uniformly, that the multiplicative constants have uniformly subexponential growth, that the bounds apply from one common level onward, and that \(B_p-\kappa_p\le\Phi_D-\varepsilon\) with one \(\varepsilon>0\). The polynomial number of pieces then costs only \(o(N)\) in the logarithm. Uncovered source configurations require their own estimates. No claim is made that compatible phase systems are negligible, that arbitrary boundary windows satisfy (3), or that the packing capacities overcome every diagram's envelope excess. This is a general fixed-graph criterion available at arbitrary fixed width, not universal diagram coverage or the volume conjecture.

title: A regularized convex problem for the actual main-color energy
text: # A regularized convex problem for the actual main-color energy 20 November 2026. Research note; the manuscripts and previous research finals remain unchanged. The full matrix balance required by the tree capacity theorem can always be obtained for the actual all-main-color source by minimizing one explicit regularized convex objective. The definition uses the original local tensors, their norms, and their original cap. It uses no unknown Kashaev value. The ordinary trivial main color supplies the lower bound needed for existence of a minimizer. The resulting unpenalized objective approximates the logarithm of the actual positive energy with an absolute error of order \(N^{-1}\). Thus a separate nonzero cycle coefficient is not an additional premise in this formulation. The remaining volume problem is to compare this positive variational value with the Casson--Rivin geometric value. That comparison is not proved here. ## 1. The prescribed tree and its positive objective Use the vector-valued tree compiler of [A positive variational formula for an actual source on a tree](research_scalar_tree_full_gauge_capacity.md), Section 5. At level \(N\ge2\), its output is \[ Y_N=(c_1,\ldots,c_N),\qquad \|Y_N\|^2=E_N=|K_N|^2+R_N, \qquad 0\le R_N\le(N-1)(N/2)^{2b-2}. \tag{1} \] Here \(b\) is the fixed braid width, \(c_j\) are the original reduced main-color values, and the prescribed partial pivotal trace and marked cut are part of the root tensor. In particular \(c_1=1\), so \[ \|Y_N\|\ge1. \tag{2} \] This is an unconditional ordinary-color anchor. It does not assert \(K_N\ne0\). Let the tree have \(m\ge2\) vertices. Its internal edge spaces are \(H_e\), of dimensions \(n_e\). They may be the full bundled operator spaces of that compiler; the theorem does not restrict gauges to individual physical wires. Write \(T_{v,N}\) for its actual local tensors. They are all nonzero, since a zero local tensor would make the output zero, contrary to (2). For positive Hermitian edge matrices \(H=(H_e)_e\), let \[ L_N(H)=\sum_v\log\|T_{v,N}\|_H, \qquad F_N(H)=e^{L_N(H)}. \tag{3} \] The local norms include \(H_e\) at one end and \(\overline H_e^{-1}\) at the other, precisely as in the direct source. That source proves \[ L_N(H)\ge\log\|Y_N\|\ge0, \qquad \inf_H L_N(H)=\log\|Y_N\|. \tag{4} \] It also proves geodesic convexity of \(L_N\). ## 2. An elementary coercive regularizer Define \[ Z(H)=1+\sum_e\operatorname{tr}(H_e+H_e^{-1}), \qquad \mathcal R(H)=\log Z(H), \qquad J_{N,\varepsilon}(H)=L_N(H)+\varepsilon\mathcal R(H), \quad\varepsilon>0. \tag{5} \] All coefficients in this objective are known from the original finite source. In particular its regularizer has no selected invariant in it. **Proposition 1.** The function \(J_{N,\varepsilon}\) is strictly geodesically convex and has a unique global minimizer in the product of the positive cones. **Proof.** Consider a simultaneous geodesic \(H_e(t)=P_e e^{tX_e}P_e\), with \(P_e>0\) and \(X_e=X_e^*\). After diagonalizing \(X_e\), both \[ \operatorname{tr}(P_e e^{tX_e}P_e),\qquad \operatorname{tr}(P_e^{-1}e^{-tX_e}P_e^{-1}) \] are finite sums of real exponentials with positive coefficients. The same is true of \(Z(H(t))\), including its constant term one. Its logarithm is convex by the variance formula for the second derivative of a logarithmic exponential sum. On a nonconstant geodesic, some \(X_e\) has a nonzero eigenvalue. Its exponential and the constant term one both have positive weights and distinct exponents. The variance is then strictly positive. Together with (4), this proves strict convexity. For existence, take a minimizing sequence with objective at most \(J_{N,\varepsilon}(I)+1\). By (4), its regularizer is bounded above. Thus \(Z\) is bounded. Every eigenvalue \(\lambda\) of every edge matrix satisfies a common bound on \(\lambda+\lambda^{-1}\). The matrices consequently lie in a compact set bounded away from the boundary of the positive cone. The finite tensor norms are continuous and nonzero there. A convergent subsequence attains the infimum. Two different minimizers would contradict strict convexity on the positive-matrix geodesic joining them. \(\square\) No effective numerical minimization is needed in what follows. ## 3. The minimizer is approximately balanced in the full matrix norm At a given metric, gauge by \(g_e=H_e^{1/2}\), normalize each local tensor, and let \(\rho_{v,e}\) denote its reduced density matrix on an incident leg. The original bilinear edge pairing prescribes the full mismatch \[ \Delta_e=\rho_{v,e}-\rho_{w,e}^{\mathsf T}, \qquad S(H)=\sum_e\|\Delta_e\|_1. \tag{6} \] No diagonal entries or first normal directions have been discarded. **Theorem 2.** Every global minimizer \(H^{(\varepsilon)}\) of (5) satisfies \[ \Delta_e=-\frac{2\varepsilon}{Z(H^{(\varepsilon)})} (H_e^{(\varepsilon)}-(H_e^{(\varepsilon)})^{-1}), \qquad S(H^{(\varepsilon)})\le2\varepsilon. \tag{7} \] The final bound is independent of all edge dimensions. **Proof.** Orient an edge so that \(g_e\) acts at \(v\) and its inverse transpose at \(w\). Vary it by \(g_e(s)=e^{sX}P\), where \(P=H_e^{1/2}\) and \(X=X^*\). The metric varies through \(H_e(s)=P e^{2sX}P\). The full norm derivative proved in the direct source is \[ \left.\frac{dL_N}{ds}\right|_0 =\operatorname{tr}(X\Delta_e). \tag{8} \] The two trace derivatives in (5) are elementary: \[ \left.\frac d{ds}\right|_0\operatorname{tr}H_e(s) =2\operatorname{tr}(XH_e),\qquad \left.\frac d{ds}\right|_0\operatorname{tr}H_e(s)^{-1} =-2\operatorname{tr}(XH_e^{-1}). \] Stationarity for every Hermitian \(X\) gives the matrix equality in (7). Since \(H_e\) and \(H_e^{-1}\) have common eigenvectors, \[ \|H_e-H_e^{-1}\|_1\le\operatorname{tr}(H_e+H_e^{-1}). \] Summing the first equality of (7) therefore gives \[ S(H^{(\varepsilon)}) \le\frac{2\varepsilon}{Z(H^{(\varepsilon)})} \sum_e\operatorname{tr}(H_e^{(\varepsilon)} +(H_e^{(\varepsilon)})^{-1}) <2\varepsilon. \] The weak inequality stated in (7) follows. \(\square\) ## 4. A regularized objective which preserves the full energy rate Set \[ \varepsilon_N=\frac1{m^2N^2},\qquad H_N\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{H>0}J_{N,\varepsilon_N}(H), \widehat F_N=F_N(H_N). \tag{9} \] This definition uses only original local tensors, their edge spaces, and the explicit numbers \(m,N\). It makes no assumption about the complete main color. **Corollary 3.** Whenever \(a_{N,m}=1-4\sqrt2/N-10/(mN^2)>0\), \[ \boxed{\qquad a_{N,m}\widehat F_N\le\sqrt{E_N}\le\widehat F_N. \qquad} \tag{10} \] For a fixed tree, in particular, \[ 0\le\log\widehat F_N-\tfrac12\log E_N=O(N^{-1}), \qquad \frac{2\pi}{N}\log\widehat F_N -\frac\pi N\log E_N=O(N^{-2}). \tag{11} \] **Proof.** Theorem 2 gives \(S(H_N)\le2/(m^2N^2)\). Insert this in the full-marginal tree estimate of the direct source, \[ \frac{\|Y_N\|}{F_N(H_N)}\ge[1-4m\sqrt{S(H_N)}-5mS(H_N)]_+. \] This is the first inequality in (10); tree Cauchy gives the second. Taking logarithms and using \(-\log a_{N,m}=O(N^{-1})\) proves (11). \(\square\) The quantity \(\widehat F_N\) is the **unpenalized** product of local norms, evaluated at a minimizer of the penalized problem. There is no assertion here that \(\varepsilon_N\mathcal R(H_N)=o(N)\). Substituting the minimum value of \(J_{N,\varepsilon_N}\) for \(\log\widehat F_N\) without controlling that penalty would be an additional step. There is a useful exact stability under blocking. Contract any connected subtree, with all its original phases and marked tensors, into one tensor. The resulting tree has exactly the same output \(Y_N\). Apply (9) separately to the two presentations, using their respective numbers of vertices. For every \(m\ge2\), \(a_{N,m}\ge a_N=1-4\sqrt2/N-5/N^2\). Thus, for \(N\ge8\), \[ \left|\log\widehat F_N^{\rm before} -\log\widehat F_N^{\rm after}\right| \le-\log a_N=O(N^{-1}). \tag{11a} \] Both logarithms lie in the same interval \([\log\|Y_N\|,\log\|Y_N\|-\log a_N]\), which proves this bound without an estimate for an intermediate source. If blocking leaves one tensor, its unpenalized norm is exactly \(\|Y_N\|\). The bound is independent of block complexity and edge dimensions. It applies in particular after exact contraction of any fixed short component. It does not identify that component's geometric asymptotic, or assert equality of the penalized objective values. ## 5. The optimizing matrices are algebraic at a fixed level There is also a finite-level algebraic statement, distinct from any bound as \(N\) grows. Suppose all local tensor entries are algebraic numbers and \(\varepsilon\) is positive rational. These assumptions hold for the original root-of-unity matrices and (9). Then every entry of the minimizing matrices is algebraic. To prove this, use real coordinates for the Hermitian matrices \(P_e=H_e^{1/2}\). Their real and imaginary entries form an open coordinate domain. Each squared local norm \(s_v=\|T_{v,N}\|_H^2\) and \(Z\) is a rational function in these coordinates with algebraic coefficients. They have no zero denominator and are positive in this domain. Consequently \[ dJ_{N,\varepsilon} =\tfrac12\sum_v\frac{ds_v}{s_v} +\varepsilon\frac{dZ}{Z} \tag{11b} \] is a vector of rational functions. Clearing nonzero denominators in its stationary equations gives polynomial equations with algebraic coefficients. At the minimum the Hessian is positive definite: along every nonzero tangent the second derivative of the regularizer is strictly positive, and the local norm objective is geodesically convex. Because the first derivative vanishes there, the ordinary coordinate Hessian has the same positive quadratic form. The Jacobian of the cleared stationary equations is therefore invertible. For completeness, a solution of polynomial equations in characteristic zero with invertible Jacobian has algebraic coordinates over their coefficient field. Otherwise its finitely generated coordinate field has a nonempty transcendence basis. Differentiation in one basis variable extends through its finite separable algebraic extension: differentiate each minimal polynomial and divide by its nonzero derivative. Applying this derivation to the stationary equations and using their invertible Jacobian makes the derivatives of every coordinate zero. That contradicts differentiation of the chosen transcendence basis variable. This proves the assertion. The size and degree of these algebraic points are not bounded here uniformly in \(N\). Algebraicity alone does not determine the limiting value of (3), and no such inference is used. ## 6. A regularized flow on the actual compiler edges The minimizing metrics can also be specified by a convergent flow. Keep \(N\) and \(\varepsilon>0\) fixed, and put \[ P_e=H_e^{1/2},\qquad G_e=\Delta_e+\frac{2\varepsilon}{Z(H)}(H_e-H_e^{-1}). \tag{11c} \] Starting at any positive metrics, solve \[ \dot H_e=-\tfrac12 P_eG_eP_e. \tag{11d} \] Everything on the right is computed from the original local tensors, the current edge metrics, and the one positive scalar \(Z\). In particular no value of \(K_N\) or selected geometric coefficient is used in this equation. The flow exists for all nonnegative time and converges to the unique minimizer of (5). Here is a direct verification. In the positive-matrix metric \(\langle U,V\rangle_H=\operatorname{tr}(H^{-1}UH^{-1}V)\), the derivative formulas above give gradient \(\tfrac12 P_eG_eP_e\). Thus \[ \frac{dJ_{N,\varepsilon}}{dt} =-\tfrac14\sum_e\operatorname{tr}(G_e^2). \tag{11e} \] The entire trajectory stays in a compact positive sublevel set, by Proposition 1's coercivity proof and (4). The smooth vector field is bounded there, so finite-dimensional local existence continues for all time. Equation (11e) and the lower bound on \(J\) show that the squared norm of \(G\) is integrable in time. It is uniformly continuous, since both the vector field and its derivatives are bounded on that compact set. It therefore tends to zero: otherwise disjoint intervals of uniformly positive length would give an infinite integral. Every accumulation point is consequently critical. Geodesic convexity makes each critical point a global minimum, and strict convexity makes that point unique. Compactness then gives convergence of the entire trajectory. This is a full matrix flow on the compiler edges, with its original source retained. It has not been identified with a classical flow of dihedral angles on an ideal triangulation. ## 7. What is now required for the finite-exception program For a fixed hyperbolic knot of complement volume \(V>0\), (1) and (10)--(11) give the equivalence \[ \lim_N\frac{2\pi}{N}\log|K_N|=V \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \lim_N\frac{2\pi}{N}\log\widehat F_N=V. \tag{12} \] The implication from energy to the original scalar uses the polynomial ordinary-color remainder, as proved in the direct source. It does not assume eventual nonvanishing of \(K_N\). Consequently the remaining task in this formulation is a quantum to classical variational comparison. One must determine the leading unpenalized objective at these actual full matrix minimizers and show that it is the hyperbolic volume. Classical angle balance by itself does not prove that comparison. The construction above does supply the full matrix balance, including the original source, but gives no description of the minimizing matrices by geometric shapes. Fix any short partial assignment. For each completion of the remaining integer coefficients that gives a one-component knot, apply the construction to that completed knot's original compiler. Its ordinary trivial main color again equals one, so existence and the estimates above apply to that completion. This makes no assertion about the source of an intermediate unfilled link or an open family of boundary variables, and requires no intermediate exterior to be hyperbolic. To obtain the proposed finite-exception theorem, the comparison in (12) must hold for all sufficiently long remaining fillings after each required fixed short partial assignment. The coefficients are fixed before the level tends to infinity. Infinite fibers representing a fixed hyperbolic core still require the same volume comparison for that core. This reformulation has removed an independent lower-bound hypothesis for the closing overlap. It has not proved (12)'s geometric limit, exchanged an uncontrolled infimum and limit, or added a new knot class with a proved volume identity. ## Direct proof source The complete direct source was read, including its zero-output proof, full marginal estimate, actual all-main-color compiler and limitations: * [A positive variational formula for an actual source on a tree](research_scalar_tree_full_gauge_capacity.md), SHA-256 `2997b732aa73e063c66e81d6487a1d9927509609d61842c1dbb43d9345df1d6d`. The coercive regularizer, its elementary convexity proof, the stationarity identity (7), and estimates (10)--(11) are proved above. Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used. No mathematical program, numerical test, build, git operation, frozen-file edit, or public-document change was performed.

title: Bounds on the regularized source metrics and their penalty
text: # Bounds on the regularized source metrics and their penalty 20 November 2026. Research note; previous finals and public manuscripts remain unchanged. The regularized source problem has a unique positive matrix minimizer. The earlier proof did not estimate its regularization penalty. Here we bound that penalty and the spectra of the optimizing metrics using only known input tensor norms and the ordinary trivial-color anchor. For a fixed original braid, the logarithms of the optimizing eigenvalues are of order at most the quantum level. The penalized minimum itself therefore has the same leading rate as the actual main-color energy. This is spectral control. It does not identify the optimizing eigenvectors or matrix symbols with a hyperbolic angle structure. That quantum to classical comparison remains necessary. ## 1. An explicit near-minimizer on an anchored tree Let a finite tree have \(m\ge2\) vertices, edge spaces of dimensions \(n_e\), and one vector output \(Y\). Use the bilinear contractions and full edge gauges of [the regularized source theorem](research_regularized_actual_source_capacity.md). Assume the known anchor \(\|Y\|\ge1\). Put \[ B=\prod_v\max(1,\|T_v\|),\qquad D=\sum_e n_e,\qquad A_m(B,D,\eta)=\log(1+2D) +(2+2m(m-1))\log B+(m-1)\log\frac m{2\eta}. \tag{1} \] Here \(0<\eta\le1\), the input norms are the original coordinate norms, and the output vertex is the root. In particular \(B\ge1\) and \(D\ge1\). **Theorem 1.** There are full edge metrics, specified by finite operations on the proper subtree messages, for which \[ 0\le L(H)-\log\|Y\|\le\eta,\qquad \log Z(H)\le A_m(B,D,\eta). \tag{2} \] No choice in the construction divides by the output \(Y\). **Proof.** Orient each edge toward the root, with its vector gauge acting on the child side. Reversing an earlier edge convention replaces \(H_e\) by \(\overline H_e^{-1}\), preserving both the local norms and \(Z\), so this choice changes no variational value. Let \(a_e\) be the ordinary contraction of the proper subtree below that edge. It is a vector on that edge. Tree Cauchy gives both \[ B^{-1}\le\|a_e\|\le B. \tag{3} \] The upper bound contracts the subtree. For the lower bound, leave \(a_e\) uncontracted and apply tree Cauchy to the rest: \(1\le\|Y\|\le B\|a_e\|\). In particular every such message is nonzero, using only the known anchor. Choose an edge gauge \(g_e\) sending \(a_e\) to the first unit vector \(e_0\), with \(\|g_e\|,\|g_e^{-1}\|\le B\). One construction first rotates \(a_e/\|a_e\|\) to \(e_0\), then scales its first coordinate by \(\|a_e\|^{-1}\). Applying all these gauges at once is consistent: gauges cancel inside a contracted subtree. Therefore each proper vertex tensor, when all its child indices are zero, is exactly \(e_0\) on its parent edge. The corresponding root slice is exactly \(Y\). All output-excited entries with zero child indices vanish. The gauged norm of any local tensor is at most \[ \|T_v\|B^{\deg(v)}\le B^m. \tag{4} \] Let the root have depth zero. At an edge whose child has depth \(r\), apply the further child-side gauge \(D_e(t)=\operatorname{diag}(1,t^r,\ldots,t^r)\), with \(t\ge1\). Its inverse transpose acts on the parent's input leg. An excited parent output at a vertex of depth \(r\), together with \(k\ge1\) excited child indices, receives exponent \(r-k(r+1)\le-1\). Without an excited output, any excited child also gives exponent at most \(-1\). The excluded case of an excited output and no excited child was already zero. Leaves remain \(e_0\). Thus every entry outside the zero-index slice is suppressed by at least \(t^{-1}\). These entries are orthogonal in the coordinate norm to the unchanged zero-index slice. Its norm is one at a proper vertex and \(\|Y\|\ge1\) at the root. By (4) and \(\log(1+x)\le x\), \[ L(H(t))-\log\|Y\| \le\frac{mB^{2m}}{2t^2}. \tag{5} \] The complete edge gauge \(g_e(t)=D_e(t)g_e\) has \[ \|g_e(t)\|\le Bt^{m-1},\qquad \|g_e(t)^{-1}\|\le B. \] Set \(H_e(t)=g_e(t)^*g_e(t)\). Removing the unitary factors of these gauges preserves all local norms, as in the direct source. The trace bound is \[ Z(H(t))\le1+2DB^2t^{2(m-1)} \le(1+2D)B^2t^{2(m-1)}. \tag{6} \] Take \(t=B^m\sqrt{m/(2\eta)}\ge1\). Equations (5)--(6) give (2), including exactly the constants in (1). \(\square\) ## 2. The penalty at the regularized minimum Let \(H^{(\varepsilon)}\) minimize \(J_\varepsilon=L+\varepsilon\log Z\), with \(0<\varepsilon\le1\). Apply Theorem 1 with \(\eta=\varepsilon\). Since \(L(H^{(\varepsilon)})\ge\log\|Y\|\), comparison with that explicit competitor proves \[ \boxed{\quad \log Z(H^{(\varepsilon)})\le1+A_m(B,D,\varepsilon), \qquad 0\le\min J_\varepsilon-\log\|Y\| \le\varepsilon[1+A_m(B,D,\varepsilon)]. \quad} \tag{7} \] In particular this is a bound for the actual penalty, rather than an assumption that it disappears. Every optimizing eigenvalue satisfies \[ e^{-1-A_m(B,D,\varepsilon)}\le \lambda(H_e^{(\varepsilon)}) \le e^{1+A_m(B,D,\varepsilon)}. \tag{8} \] Indeed each eigenvalue and its reciprocal are at most \(Z\). The bounds use no nonvanishing of a selected scalar coefficient. ## 3. Coarse uniform bounds for the actual input matrices For completeness the input growth needed below follows directly from the original finite matrices. Let \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\), \(\theta=\pi/N\), and \[ s_k=\prod_{r=1}^k2\sin(r\theta),\qquad 0\le k<N. \] The factorization of \((z^N-1)/(z-1)\) at \(z=1\) gives \(s_{N-1}=N\). Reflection of the sine factors then gives \[ s_ks_{N-1-k}=N,\qquad \frac1{s_k}\le\frac{2^{N-1-k}}N. \tag{9} \] No asymptotic factorial estimate is needed. At main color \(\alpha=j-1\), \(1\le j\le N\), the original unrolled module in [the ADO pointing note](kashaev_ado_pointing.md) has \[ E|a\rangle=[a]_q[\alpha-a+1]_q|a-1\rangle, \qquad F|a\rangle=|a+1\rangle, \qquad [r]_q=\frac{\sin(r\theta)}{\sin\theta}. \] Thus \(\|E^k\|\le(\sin\theta)^{-2k}\), and \(\|F^k\|\le1\). The finite universal crossing in [the original crossing definition](kashaev_crossing_and_period_lattice.md), equation (2.1), is a unitary Cartan factor followed by the nilpotent sum whose coefficient magnitudes are \(|q-q^{-1}|^k/[k]_q!\). Consequently its \(k\)-th summand has operator norm at most \[ \frac{(2\sin\theta)^k}{[k]_q!}(\sin\theta)^{-2k} =\frac{4^k}{s_k} \le\frac{2^{N-1+k}}N \le\frac{4^{N-1}}N. \tag{10} \] This estimate is uniform in the entire main-color orbit, including the reducible colors. The inverse nilpotent sum has coefficients \((-1)^kq^{-k(k-1)/2}(q-q^{-1})^k/[k]_q!\), of the same magnitudes. Multiplication with the positive sum gives coefficient zero in degree \(1\le n<N\) by the finite binomial identity \(\sum_{k=0}^n(-1)^kQ^{k(k-1)/2}{n\brack k}_Q=(1;Q)_n=0\). Degree \(N\) and above vanish by nilpotence. The inverse Cartan factor is unitary too. Each input pair has at most \(N\) possible transfer indices. Thus the physical \(N^2\)-dimensional crossing has at most \(N^3\) nonzero entries, each bounded by the last expression in (10). Both signed crossings consequently obey \[ \|R_\pm\|_{\rm HS}\le\sqrt N\,4^{N-1}. \tag{11} \] Checked permutations, original pivots, and the root-of-unity zero-framing scalars have unit modulus and add no exponential norm. For the all-main-color compiler of a fixed braid on \(b\) strands, tensoring with spectator identities and taking the direct sum over the \(N\) main colors gives crossing leaf norm at most \(N^{b/2}4^{N-1}\). Its componentwise matrix multiplication tensor has \(N^{3b+1}\) unit entries and norm \(N^{(3b+1)/2}\). Its original root readout has \(N\cdot N^{b-1}\) unit-modulus entries and norm \(N^{b/2}\). Therefore, for that fixed compiler, \[ \log B_N=O(N),\qquad \log D_N=O(\log N). \tag{12} \] Constants may depend on the fixed word and width. Fixed signed powers or fixed short pieces may be contracted first; submultiplicativity gives the same type of bound. No estimate uniform in an unbounded word length is asserted. ## 4. Spectral compactness and the full variational limit Take the actual regularized minimizer with \(\varepsilon_N=1/(m^2N^2)\). For a fixed completed knot assignment, the number \(m\) is fixed. Equations (7)--(12) yield \[ \log Z(H_N)=O(N),\qquad \sup_e\|N^{-1}\log H_{e,N}\|_{\rm op}=O(1), \qquad \varepsilon_N\log Z(H_N)=O(N^{-1}). \tag{13} \] Thus not only the unpenalized objective but also the entire penalized minimum recovers the actual energy at that precision: \[ 0\le\min_H J_{N,\varepsilon_N}(H) -\tfrac12\log E_N=O(N^{-1}). \tag{14} \] For any prescribed positive \(V\), this gives the equivalent target \[ \lim_N\frac{2\pi}{N}\log|K_N|=V \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \lim_N\frac{2\pi}{N}\min_HJ_{N,\varepsilon_N}(H)=V. \tag{15} \] The ordinary-color remainder remains the one in the direct source. No eventual nonvanishing of \(K_N\) is a premise. The bounded spectra in (13) do not provide compactness of the eigenvectors in a specified phase-space representation, convergence of matrix symbols, or the Casson--Rivin functional as a limiting objective. They also do not permit an unsupported interchange of an infimum and a limit. Those are the next substantive requirements for the geometric comparison in (15). For a fixed short partial assignment, all statements apply to each completed remaining integer assignment which gives a one-component knot. The anchor is not asserted for an unfilled auxiliary link. The algebraic and flow constructions now have controlled metric spectra on every such completed fixed source. A uniform description of their classical limits is still required to prove the requested finite-exception theorem. ## 5. Main-color preserving gauges suffice at the leading scale One exact restriction of the metric class is available. Suppose a tree is a direct sum of \(r\) sectors: every local tensor has blocks \(T_{v,j}\), and a contraction can pair only equal sector labels. The root output is the orthogonal direct sum of vectors \(Y_j\). Restrict the edge gauges to preserve the sectors, and denote the resulting product-norm infimum by \(\mathcal C_{\rm block}\). Then \[ \boxed{\quad \mathcal C_{\rm block} =\left(\sum_{j=1}^r\|Y_j\|^{2/m}\right)^{m/2}. \quad} \tag{16} \] Here is a proof including sectors with zero output. At any finite choice of sector gauges, let \(a_{v,j}\ge0\) be the local block norms. Tree Cauchy in each sector and generalized Hölder give \[ \prod_v\left(\sum_j a_{v,j}^2\right)^{1/2} \ge\left(\sum_j\left(\prod_va_{v,j}\right)^{2/m}\right)^{m/2} \ge\left(\sum_j\|Y_j\|^{2/m}\right)^{m/2}. \] Conversely, first consider sectors with all local blocks nonzero. The full tree capacity theorem, applied separately in each such sector, gives gauges with products \(p_j=\prod_va_{v,j}\) approaching \(\|Y_j\|\), including zero. Positive scalar edge gauges can make every vertex norm in sector \(j\) equal \(p_j^{1/m}\): the required logarithmic vertex rescalings sum to zero, and the incidence map of a tree maps onto the zero-sum vertex vectors. To verify that last statement, assign the required scalar at a leaf to its incident edge, remove the leaf, and repeat. These scalar gauges change neither the sector output nor its product of norms. The resulting whole product is \((\sum_j p_j^{2/m})^{m/2}\). If a sector has a zero local block, its output is zero. Scalar edge gauges can make all its nonzero vertex norms tend to zero too: prescribe their target logarithmic rescalings, let one zero vertex absorb the compensating sum, and again use the incidence map. The zero block remains zero. Thus such sectors contribute nothing in the limit. This proves (16) in every case without division by a zero output. If \(\mathcal C_{\rm full}=\|\bigoplus_jY_j\|\), the elementary finite-dimensional norm inequalities give \[ \mathcal C_{\rm full}\le\mathcal C_{\rm block} \le r^{(m-1)/2}\mathcal C_{\rm full}. \tag{17} \] For the actual all-main-color tree, \(r=N\) and \(Y_j=c_j\). For fixed \(m\), restricting the infimum to main-color preserving gauges therefore changes its logarithm by at most \((m-1)\log N/2\), which has zero volume rate. This is a statement about infima. It does not assert that the canonical regularized full-matrix minimizer is block diagonal, or that pinching an arbitrary individual gauge improves the objective. The exceptional complete color is still retained as its own sector. A continuous symbol in the main-color parameter cannot erase it: the adjacent ordinary colors and the complete color have different source behavior even when their limiting meridians coincide. ## Complete direct sources The complete texts below were read for the actual source, matrix definitions, and the earlier regularized minimizer. The quantitative normal form and its bounds (1)--(8), and the elementary matrix estimates above, are proved here. * [Regularized actual source](research_regularized_actual_source_capacity.md), SHA-256 `0cea0d52182eb24b4610538f354dbe5158fa54aa6f9cf7f9fc280c72ab090ff8`. * [Original unrolled main-color family](kashaev_ado_pointing.md), SHA-256 `005ad157ebbf068b71eb80e2ceddc1aa9fccc460a54266756306e5cb54cf4c78`. * [Finite universal crossing and original normalization](kashaev_crossing_and_period_lattice.md), SHA-256 `71e67223742fe905af47d0475435f3a13acc877695bd0cdc321798cf2e608037`. * [Full tree capacity](research_scalar_tree_full_gauge_capacity.md), SHA-256 `2997b732aa73e063c66e81d6487a1d9927509609d61842c1dbb43d9345df1d6d`. Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used. No mathematical program, numerical test, build, git operation, previous-final edit, or public-document change was performed.

title: A relative finite Fourier transition for a vanishing prefix minor
text: # A relative finite Fourier transition for a vanishing prefix minor Private written proof, 18 November 2026. The complementary entry at a simple classical prefix zero has an explicit finite-source transition. A triangular tensor-prefix operator, a diagonal factorial gauge and an actual finite Fourier matrix turn its ordered quantum lift into a nonzero diagonal clock **minus an explicit carry**. The carry has rank \(N^{m-1}\) on a prefix of \(m\) heads. It cannot be dropped: the original complementary entry is nilpotent, whereas the diagonal clock is invertible. The construction retains the original probes, finite projectors and all quantum/meridian normal terms. It also gives an exact partial inverse and a two-endpoint source-current identity. It is a relative prefix chart, not an invertible Bruhat factorization of the unchanged finite head or a calculation of its geometric period. The complete directs are E, the actual finite head; M, the classical marked prefix correspondence; and V, the whole finite Fourier source. The tensor-prefix splitting and the identities below are proved inline. ## 1. The classical complementary chart and its ordered finite lift In M's convention the retained classical prefix is \[ P_m=H_m\cdots H_1=B_-^{-1}B_+,\qquad B_-=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\-kf&k\end{pmatrix},\quad B_+=\begin{pmatrix}k&e\\0&1\end{pmatrix}. \tag{1} \] Thus \(P_{11}=k\) and \(P_{21}=fk\). Suppose \(P(r)\in SL_2\) is regular, \(a(r)=P_{11}(r)\) has a simple zero at \(r_*\), and write \[ P=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d_0\end{pmatrix}. \tag{2} \] Then \(b(r_*)c(r_*)=-1\), so \(c\) is a unit near that point. The complementary classical factorization is explicitly \[ W^{-1}P =\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\a&c\end{pmatrix}^{-1} \begin{pmatrix}c&d_0\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad W=\begin{pmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}. \tag{3} \] Indeed its lower-right entry is \((1-ad_0)/c=-b\). This chart is regular at \(a=0\). Its pivot is \(c=fk\), not the reciprocal of the old pivot. Use the original balanced heads \(w_0,\ldots,w_d\), where \(d=N-1\), \(Q=q^2\), \(x_i=-M_i/q\), with E's finite arrows \[ K_iw_a=x_iQ^{-a}w_a,\quad F_iw_a=(1-Q^{a+1})w_{a+1}\ (a<d),\quad F_iw_d=0. \tag{4} \] The corresponding lowering arrows are E's \(\mathcal E_i\); their two endpoint rows are unchanged. All statements take place on the actual fixed-\(N\) normal germ at \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(M_i=1\). In particular \[ f_a=\prod_{j=1}^a(1-Q^j),\quad 0\le a<N, \qquad f_0=1 \tag{5} \] are units. The letter \(f_a\) denotes a finite product, whereas \(f\) in (1) is a classical prefix field. For the first \(m\) ordered heads put \[ K_\Sigma=\prod_{i=1}^mK_i,\qquad F_\Sigma=F_1+K_1^{-1}F_2+\cdots+ K_1^{-1}\cdots K_{m-1}^{-1}F_m. \tag{6} \] Let \(\mathcal E_\Sigma\) be the correspondingly ordered sum \(\mathcal E_1K_2\cdots K_m+\cdots+\mathcal E_m\). Products of the literal triangular two-by-two matrices give \[ \widehat B_-= \begin{pmatrix}I&0\\-K_\Sigma F_\Sigma&K_\Sigma\end{pmatrix}, \qquad \widehat B_+= \begin{pmatrix}K_\Sigma&\mathcal E_\Sigma\\0&I\end{pmatrix}. \tag{7} \] Their exact ordered quotient is \[ \widehat P=\widehat B_-^{-1}\widehat B_+ =\begin{pmatrix} K_\Sigma&\mathcal E_\Sigma\\ F_\Sigma K_\Sigma&F_\Sigma\mathcal E_\Sigma+K_\Sigma^{-1} \end{pmatrix}. \tag{8} \] The order in the lower-left entry is important. Its commuting principal symbol is exactly the complementary entry \(c\) in (2). Set \[ C=F_\Sigma K_\Sigma. \tag{9} \] This is a specified insertion in the original tensor source. No exact quantum Hurwitz identity for (8) is asserted. At another braid level the insertion and its probes are transported by the literal braid word, not reset to an unprefixed coupon. ## 2. An exact triangular splitting of the prefix raising operator Write \(K_{\rm r}=K_2\cdots K_m\) and \[ F_{\rm r}=F_2+K_2^{-1}F_3+\cdots+ K_2^{-1}\cdots K_{m-1}^{-1}F_m. \tag{10} \] For \(m=1\), these mean \(K_{\rm r}=I,F_{\rm r}=0\). Let \(L_1w_a=w_{a-1}\) for \(a>0\), \(L_1w_0=0\), be the literal unilateral shift. Define \[ Z=x_1^{-1}L_1F_{\rm r},\qquad S=\sum_{j=0}^d\frac{Z^j}{f_j}. \tag{11} \] Since \(Z^N=0\), \(S\) is a finite unipotent matrix. Its exact inverse is \[ S^{-1}=\sum_{j=0}^d \frac{(-1)^jQ^{j(j-1)/2}Z^j}{f_j}. \tag{12} \] For a direct check, the scalar series \(\sum z^j/f_j\) satisfies \(A(Qz)=(1-z)A(z)\) modulo \(z^N\); the series in (12) has the reciprocal equation. Their product is one modulo \(z^N\). Substitute \(z=Z\). More concretely, for every vector \(v\) on the remaining heads, \[ S(w_a\otimes v) =\frac{F_\Sigma^a}{f_a}(w_0\otimes v), \qquad 0\le a<N. \tag{13} \] To prove this, put \(A=F_1\), \(B=K_1^{-1}F_{\rm r}\). The actual weight relation gives \(AB=Q^{-1}BA\). Induction therefore yields \[ (A+B)^a=\sum_{j=0}^a \frac{f_a}{f_jf_{a-j}}A^{a-j}B^j,\qquad a<N. \tag{14} \] Applied to \(w_0\otimes v\), its \(j\)-term divided by \(f_a\) is \(x_1^{-j}w_{a-j}\otimes F_{\rm r}^jv/f_j\), which is (11). The diagonal term is the identity and all other terms lower the first-head occupation. Every term preserves total integer occupation, so \[ [S,K_\Sigma]=0. \tag{15} \] This is an actual finite change of source coordinates. It is not declared to be an intertwining braid or a scalar-clock substitution. At the quantum root, \(F_\Sigma^N=0\). Indeed the intermediate Gaussian coefficients \({N\choose j}_Q\), \(0<j<N\), vanish, while \(F_1^N=0\) and, by induction on the number of heads, \((K_1^{-1}F_{\rm r})^N=0\). This uses primitivity of \(Q\), not primality or oddness of \(N\). Before root specialization the exact identity is instead \[ S^{-1}F_\Sigma S=F_1+J_N,\qquad J_N=\frac1{f_d}S^{-1}F_\Sigma^N(T_{0d}\otimes I), \quad T_{ab}=|a\rangle\langle b|. \tag{16} \] For \(a<d\), apply (13) on both sides of \(F_\Sigma S-SF_1\). For \(a=d\) the difference is \(F_\Sigma^N(w_0\otimes v)/f_d\). This proves (16) on every column. Thus \(J_N=0\) at the root but all its normal derivatives remain. Restricting later to the ordinary head path does not justify deleting this tensor-prefix term. ## 3. Partial inverse and the two retained endpoint projectors Define the finite one-head operator \[ L_Fw_a=(1-Q^a)^{-1}w_{a-1}\quad(a>0),\qquad L_Fw_0=0. \tag{17} \] It has \[ F_1L_F=I-P_0,\qquad L_FF_1=I-P_d, \quad P_a=T_{aa}\otimes I. \tag{18} \] All denominators are among the actual units (5). Set \[ C^\dagger=K_\Sigma^{-1}SL_FS^{-1},\qquad P_a^S=SP_aS^{-1}. \tag{19} \] At the root, (15)--(18) prove exactly \[ CC^\dagger=I-P_0^S,\qquad C^\dagger C=I-P_d^S. \tag{20} \] The defects have rank \(N^{m-1}\). In particular \(C^\dagger\) is not an inverse of \(C\). The nilpotent \(C\) cannot acquire a two-sided inverse under any finite Fourier similarity. The endpoint coupons themselves are explicit. Since \(SP_0=P_0\) and \(P_dS^{-1}=P_d\), (11)--(12) give \[ \begin{aligned} P_0^S&=P_0+\sum_{j=1}^d \frac{(-1)^jQ^{j(j-1)/2}x_1^{-j}}{f_j} T_{0j}\otimes F_{\rm r}^j,\\ P_d^S&=P_d+\sum_{j=1}^d \frac{x_1^{-j}}{f_j}T_{d-j,d}\otimes F_{\rm r}^j . \end{aligned} \tag{20a} \] They have total degree zero. Thus the difference from the original highest or lowest probe is a specified sum of coupled source insertions, not an unspecified boundary class. There is a useful complete normal version. Since \((T_{0d}\otimes I)L_F=0\), one has \(J_NL_F=0\). Consequently (20) becomes, before specialization, \[ CC^\dagger=I-P_0^S,\qquad C^\dagger C=I-P_d^S+\mathcal R_N, \tag{21} \] \[ \mathcal R_N= K_\Sigma^{-1}S L_FJ_NS^{-1}K_\Sigma. \tag{22} \] The whole row \(\mathcal R_N\), not only its zero root value, belongs to the source-normal identity. ## 4. A finite Fourier clock with its full carry The diagonal operator \[ G(w_a\otimes v) =f_a x_1^a Q^{-a(a-1)/2}\,w_a\otimes K_{\rm r}^{a}v \tag{23} \] is invertible on the same normal germ. Its consecutive ratio is \((1-Q^{a+1})x_1Q^{-a}K_{\rm r}\). Hence \[ G^{-1}(F_1K_\Sigma)G=U_1, \quad U_1w_a=w_{a+1}\ (a<d),\quad U_1w_d=0. \tag{24} \] This weights the complementary pivot itself, rather than only \(F_\Sigma\), by a source-compatible diagonal gauge. Choose an arbitrary nonzero evaluation radius \(\varrho\). It is distinct from the residual geometric framing coordinate \(r\). Put \(y_j=\varrho Q^j\) and \[ (V_\varrho)_{j,a}=N^{-1/2}y_j^a,\qquad (V_\varrho^{-1})_{a,j} =\sqrt N[X^a]\prod_{\ell\ne j} \frac{X-y_\ell}{y_j-y_\ell}. \tag{25} \] The node differences are units at the primitive root. This is the actual whole Vandermonde inverse, including away from \(Q^N=1\). Define \[ Y=\operatorname{diag}(y_j),\quad u_N=N^{-1/2}(y_j^N)_j,\quad v^t=e_d^tV_\varrho^{-1},\quad \mathcal A=(V_\varrho G^{-1})S^{-1}. \tag{26} \] The identity on the other prefix heads is understood. Evaluation of the missing last column of \(U_1\) gives \[ V_\varrho U_1V_\varrho^{-1}=Y-u_Nv^t. \tag{27} \] Combining (16), (24) and (27) gives the full finite transition \[ \boxed{\quad \mathcal A C\mathcal A^{-1}=Y-u_Nv^t+\mathcal D_N,\qquad \mathcal D_N=V_\varrho G^{-1}J_NK_\Sigma G V_\varrho^{-1}. \quad} \tag{28} \] Neither the carry nor the normal term has been discarded. The simultaneous Cartan operator is equally explicit. With \(B_1=\operatorname{diag}(Q^a)\) and \(\mathcal C_Q=V_\varrho B_1V_\varrho^{-1}\), \[ \mathcal A K_\Sigma\mathcal A^{-1} =x_1K_{\rm r}\mathcal C_Q^{-1},\qquad \mathcal A F_\Sigma\mathcal A^{-1} =(\mathcal A C\mathcal A^{-1}) (x_1K_{\rm r}\mathcal C_Q^{-1})^{-1}. \tag{28a} \] At the root \((\mathcal C_Qf)_j=f_{j+1}\), cyclically. Off root its last row is the full interpolation row at \(\varrho Q^N\). The entire transformed \(\mathcal E_\Sigma\) and its prefix Casimir are retained as matrices; no scalar Casimir channel is selected by (28a). More explicitly define the whole ordered matrix \[ \Omega_\Sigma=F_\Sigma\mathcal E_\Sigma+ qK_\Sigma+q^{-1}K_\Sigma^{-1}. \tag{28b} \] The exact weight equation \(K_\Sigma\mathcal E_\Sigma=Q\mathcal E_\Sigma K_\Sigma\) gives, without an inverse of \(C\), \[ C\mathcal E_\Sigma =Q(\Omega_\Sigma K_\Sigma-qK_\Sigma^2-q^{-1}I), \tag{28c} \] \[ \mathcal E_\Sigma =Q C^\dagger(\Omega_\Sigma K_\Sigma-qK_\Sigma^2-q^{-1}I) +P_d^S\mathcal E_\Sigma-\mathcal R_N\mathcal E_\Sigma . \tag{28d} \] The last line follows from (21). It displays the additional endpoint row and the generally nonscalar prefix Casimir needed when transporting all three generators. At the root there is a more explicit simultaneous formula before the diagonal/Fourier steps. Write \(\mathcal E_\Sigma=\mathcal E_1K_{\rm r}+\mathcal E_{\rm r}\) with its original ordered coproduct on the remaining heads. Then \[ \begin{aligned} S^{-1}\mathcal E_\Sigma S(w_a\otimes v) ={}&w_a\otimes\mathcal E_{\rm r}v\\ &+w_{a-1}\otimes (M_1K_{\rm r}Q^{-a}-M_1^{-1}K_{\rm r}^{-1})v \quad(a>0), \end{aligned} \tag{28e} \] and the second line is zero at \(a=0\). To prove this, the zeroth column is fixed because \(S,S^{-1}\) are the identity on \(w_0\otimes v\). The root head relations and their ordered coproduct give \[ [S^{-1}\mathcal E_\Sigma S,F_1] =\rho(K_\Sigma-K_\Sigma^{-1}),\qquad \rho=q-q^{-1}. \tag{28f} \] This determines each next column since \(1-Q^{a+1}\ne0\) for \(a<d\). The lower coefficients in (28e) solve the recurrence \[ (1-Q^{a+1})b_{a+1}-(1-Q^a)b_a =\rho(x_1K_{\rm r}Q^{-a}-x_1^{-1}K_{\rm r}^{-1}Q^a). \tag{28g} \] This verifies (28e), including the forced endpoint convention. Multiplication now gives the retained root Casimir matrix \[ S^{-1}\Omega_\Sigma S =F_1\otimes\mathcal E_{\rm r} -I\otimes(M_1K_{\rm r}+M_1^{-1}K_{\rm r}^{-1}). \tag{28h} \] In general it is not scalar. The formulas (28e)--(28h) are root identities; their quantum normals must be taken from the whole operators (16), (28b)--(28d), not by differentiating this root simplification. The root Fourier image is consequently explicit as well. Put \(\mathcal T=\mathcal C_Q^{-1}\). Then \[ \boxed{\quad \mathcal A\mathcal E_\Sigma\mathcal A^{-1} =\mathcal T\mathcal E_{\rm r} +Y^{-1}x_1Q(\mathcal T-I) (M_1K_{\rm r}^2\mathcal T-M_1^{-1}I). \quad} \tag{28i} \] Indeed \(G^{-1}\mathcal E_{\rm r}G=Q^{-a}\mathcal E_{\rm r}\) on the first occupation \(a\). Its lowering coefficient is \(x_1Q(Q^{-a}-1)(M_1K_{\rm r}^2Q^{-a}-M_1^{-1})\). The missing first-column correction in the Fourier transform of \(L_1\) annihilates this coefficient exactly at \(a=0\). This proves (28i), with the remaining-head operators and their ordering unchanged. It inverts \(Y\), not the actual nilpotent \(\mathcal A C\mathcal A^{-1}\). At the root set \(\lambda=\varrho^N\) and \(u_0=V_\varrho e_0=N^{-1/2}{\bf1}\). Then \[ u_N=\lambda u_0,\quad v_j=N^{-1/2}\varrho^{-d}Q^j,\quad \mathcal D_N=0,\qquad \mathcal A C\mathcal A^{-1}=Y-\lambda u_0v^t. \tag{29} \] Adding the omitted carry would replace the original unilateral shift by \(U_1+\lambda T_{0d}\), whose \(N\)-th power is \(\lambda I\). It changes the nilpotent central relation, so this completion is not an equality of the original source. For example the exact one-head determinant identities are \[ \det(tI-Y)=t^N-\lambda,\qquad \det(tI-Y+\lambda u_0v^t)=t^N. \tag{30} \] The carry's scalar resolvent coefficient is also explicit: \[ v^t(tI-Y)^{-1}u_0=\frac1{t^N-\lambda}. \tag{31} \] Expand at large \(t\); root orthogonality keeps precisely the powers \(t^{-N},t^{-2N},\ldots\), proving (31), hence its rational continuation. This is a calibration of the universal carry, not an evaluation against a knot-dependent source. In the standard root metric the normalized Fourier matrix gives \[ \|V_\varrho\|\|V_\varrho^{-1}\| =\max(|\varrho|,|\varrho|^{-1})^d,\qquad \|\lambda u_0v^t\|=|\varrho|. \tag{32} \] Indeed \(\|u_0\|=1\), \(\|v\|=|\varrho|^{-d}\). Thus small or large \(\varrho^N\) does not make the carry a small operator: its norm equals that of \(Y\). No compact-central-radius bound has been imported at a fixed nonunit \(\varrho\). The exact root change between two evaluation radii is \[ (V_{\varrho'}V_\varrho^{-1})_{j,k} =\frac1N\sum_{a=0}^d (\varrho'/\varrho)^aQ^{(j-k)a}. \tag{33} \] Equivalently its numerator is \(1-(\varrho'/\varrho)^N\), with the finite-sum removable values retained. The upper endpoint is \(d\), not an infinite Fourier tail. ## 5. Original source, projectors and a finite endpoint current Insert \(\mathcal A,\mathcal A^{-1}\) on the two sides of the actual prefix interface. Every original matrix \(W\), source vector, covector, pivot and occupation projector transforms by that same map. For example \(W'=\mathcal A W\mathcal A^{-1}\) and \(P'=\mathcal A P\mathcal A^{-1}\) satisfy \[ \operatorname{Tr}(P'W') =\operatorname{Tr}(PW). \tag{34} \] This applies to the literal highest or soft cut and arbitrary marked defects. The projectors \(P_a^S\) in (20) are not reset to the original \(P_a\). An occupation mask after the full transition is the full conjugate of that mask. Even on one head the Fourier kernel of an interval \(L\le a\le U\) is \[ \frac1N\sum_{a=L}^UQ^{(j-k)a}, \tag{35} \] with both endpoints. The \(S\)-conjugated coupled masks in (34) must be retained before making any simplification like (35). There is also an exact charge qualification. At the root the Fourier carry pulled back to the original prefix is \[ \lambda S G(T_{0d}\otimes I)G^{-1}S^{-1}. \tag{35a} \] It has total integer degree \(1-N\). Its bare trace pairing with a degree-zero unmarked word and diagonal cut/pivots is therefore zero. Products or charged probes can supply compensating degree; those actual coupons must remain. Nonzero rank of the carry matrix alone is not a nonzero source period. For a precise co-source identity put \(g=K_\Sigma^{1-N}\) and \(\gamma=Q^{N-1}\). Since \(K_\Sigma C=Q^{-1}CK_\Sigma\), \[ gC=\gamma Cg. \tag{36} \] For an arbitrary finite matrix \(B\), cyclicity and (21) give \[ \boxed{\begin{aligned} (1-\gamma)\operatorname{Tr}(gB) ={}&\operatorname{Tr}(gBP_0^S) -\gamma\operatorname{Tr}(gBP_d^S)\\ &+\gamma\operatorname{Tr}(gB\mathcal R_N) +\operatorname{Tr}(g[B,C]C^\dagger). \end{aligned}} \tag{37} \] Indeed \(\operatorname{Tr}(gBCC^\dagger) =\gamma\operatorname{Tr}(gBC^\dagger C) +\operatorname{Tr}(g[B,C]C^\dagger)\). Substitute (21). Any original full functional \(\operatorname{Tr}(P W)\) is covered by taking \(B=g^{-1}P W\), with all original other pivots, cut factors and scalar lines retained in that expression. At the root \(\gamma=Q^{-1}\), \(\mathcal R_N=0\). If in addition \([B,C]=0\), (37) reduces to the two-endpoint row. The original marked source is not assumed to satisfy this extra commutation. Equation (37) retains its actual defect. It does not turn either endpoint functional into a known nonzero scalar or supply a new multiplicative \(N\) normalization. All these identities are formed on the whole fixed-\(N\) germ. Differentiating a transformed matrix uses the forced connection \[ \partial_\alpha W' =\mathcal A(\partial_\alpha W)\mathcal A^{-1} +[(\partial_\alpha\mathcal A)\mathcal A^{-1},W']. \tag{38} \] The derivatives of \(S,G,V_\varrho,J_N,u_N,v\), the physical two head walls and the prescribed source are all included. If \(\varrho\) is parameter dependent, its derivatives are included too. The ordinary head path is imposed on this whole identity. It does not equate an ADO-pivot closed germ with the ordinary Jones germ without their pivot and twist comparison. ## 6. What is proved at the geometric prefix zero Equations (1)--(9) identify the exact classical complementary entry, and (11)--(29) give a finite integer/source transition for its ordered quantum lift. At a simple prefix zero the classical unit \(c\) may be used as an analytic choice of evaluation radius near a fixed Fourier label. This is a permitted parameter substitution in an exact matrix identity, not a proof that \(\mathcal A\) has a specified local stationary-phase amplitude. In particular the invertible classical Bruhat chart (3) does not justify inverting the nilpotent finite \(C\). Its exact substitute is the partial inverse (20), or the diagonal Fourier clock together with the carry and normal terms (28). The original source pairs the carry through its transported coefficient \(\lambda\operatorname{Tr}(P' u_0v^t W')\), with spectators and ordering retained. That coefficient is not fixed by (31). The quantum transform therefore supplies a relative chart and explicit missing rows, rather than an unevaluated assertion that all frames are equivalent. Its analytic matching to a regular geometric generating function, the pairing of the carry with the original source, and the resulting relative period remain to be proved. No contributing cycle or scalar lower bound is inferred from the classical regularity or finite invertibility of the change of basis itself. ## Complete direct-source pins * E: notes/research_actual_compressed_endpoint_euler_transition.md, SHA256 9c735f005fa94afe56931af5fc0cb77ee95849a9c4c89067290711135ad1ed16. * M: notes/marked_braid_holonomy.md, SHA256 eff47c757d0e44bda0c396c094315b8e1fce11f1fc2d6445d636c6d2d3a46c4f. * V: notes/actual_two_cut_fourier_polarization_and_cap.md, SHA256 81edcc80bb8eae878e5c02f212d4110ea7faae37b3315b5fca877b291a3acc14. The complete directs were read nontruncated in this active author sequence, with unchanged complete reads explicitly retained where applicable. The balanced full-Psi Fourier kernel, root holonomy braiding and Weyl-gluing notes were also read completely for coverage: their existing statements do not identify the present carry with a geometric prefix-zero period. All proofs here use written mathematics and text/hash operations only. No frozen or public source file was edited.

title: Repeated endpoint unit turns retain the terminal action
text: # Repeated endpoint unit turns retain the terminal action Private written proof, 16 November 2026. One unit turn of a full microscopic endpoint kernel has polynomial real norm. Repeating that operation does not preserve this bound: two turns of the same sign already have the positive exponential rate of the original two-crossing terminal message. This follows from an exact forced equation and a polynomial norm bound for its original difference operator. No new knot calculation is involved. ## 1. Exact repeated-turn forcing Use the original full algebra \[ \mathcal A_N=\mathbb C[Z]/(P_N),\quad P_N(Z)=2T_N(Z/2)+2,\quad D=N-1,\quad \theta=\pi/N,\quad \eta=(-1)^D,\quad \kappa=e^{i\pi D^2/(2N)}. \tag{1} \] Write \(q=e^{i\theta}\), \(S_j=\prod_{h=1}^j2\sin(h\theta)\), \(S_0=1\), \(c_j=2\cos((2j+1)\theta)\), and \(e_j(Z)=S_j^{-2}\prod_{a<j}(c_a-Z)\). The Newton basis, original crossing and turn satisfy \[ K_N(w,Z)=\sum_{j=0}^D e_j(w)e_j(Z),\quad Te_j=e_{D-j},\quad \phi_N(e_i e_j)=\mathbf1_{i+j=D}. \tag{2} \] All classes below have their canonical ordinary representatives of degree at most \(D\). Set \[ V_n=\kappa^n T R^{-n}T,\quad n\in\mathbb Z,\qquad G_{n,N}=T(R^{-n}),\quad F_{n,N,\alpha}=V_nK_N(w_N(\alpha),\cdot),\quad w_N(\alpha)=2\cosh(\alpha/N). \tag{3} \] Thus \(V_\sigma=U_\sigma\) for \(\sigma=\pm1\), and \[ V_nV_\ell=V_{n+\ell}. \tag{4} \] For example \(F_{2\sigma}=U_\sigma^2K_{w_N(\alpha)}\). Let \(C\) be multiplication by \(Z\), and let \(\mathcal L=TCT\). Multiplication by \(R^{-n}\) commutes with \(C\), so \(V_n\) commutes with \(\mathcal L\). The original reproducer gives \[ (w-\mathcal L)K_N(w,\cdot)=\frac{\eta P_N(w)}{N^2}e_D, \qquad V_ne_D=\kappa^nG_{n,N}. \tag{5} \] Therefore the exact full-normal identity is \[ \boxed{\quad (w_N(\alpha)-\mathcal L)F_{n,N,\alpha} =\frac{\eta P_N(w_N(\alpha))\kappa^n}{N^2}G_{n,N}. \quad} \tag{6} \] For one unit turn the right side contains \(G_{\sigma,N}=R^\sigma\). For two turns it contains the actual terminal polynomial \(T(R^{-2\sigma})\); it cannot be replaced by a unit crossing. ## 2. A real norm bound for the original difference operator Write \(\|p\|_{\mathbb R}=\sup_{[-2,2]}|p|\). The original off-grid difference formula, with \(t=(2r+1)\theta\), is \[ (\mathcal Lp)(2\cos t) =c_0 f(t)+ \frac{4\sin^4((t+\theta)/2)}{\sin t\sin(t+\theta)} [f(t)-f(t+2\theta)] \] \[ \hspace{38mm}+ \frac{4\sin^4((t-\theta)/2)}{\sin t\sin(t-\theta)} [f(t)-f(t-2\theta)], \qquad f(t)=p(2\cos t),\quad c_0=2\cos\theta. \tag{7} \] All apparent singularities in the combined expression are removable for degree at most \(D\). Expand \(f(t)=a_0+\sum_{k=1}^D a_k\cos kt\), and put \[ B(t)=\sin^4(t/2)\sum_{k=1}^D a_k\sin(k\theta) U_{k-1}(\cos t), \tag{8} \] where \(U_{k-1}(\cos t)=\sin(kt)/\sin t\) is the ordinary Chebyshev polynomial of the second kind. The two cosine differences in (7) give exactly \[ \boxed{\quad (\mathcal Lp)(2\cos t) =c_0 f(t)+8\,\frac{B(t+\theta)-B(t-\theta)}{\sin t}. \quad} \tag{9} \] Here \(B\) is an even trigonometric polynomial of degree at most \(D+1=N\). For a trigonometric polynomial, let \(\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm F,1}\) be the sum of the absolute values of its Fourier coefficients. The cosine integral formula and the finite Laurent expression for \(U_{k-1}\) give \[ |a_0|+\sum_{k=1}^D|a_k|\le(2D+1)\|p\|_{\mathbb R},\qquad \|U_{k-1}(\cos t)\|_{\mathrm F,1}=k,\qquad \|\sin^4(t/2)\|_{\mathrm F,1}=1. \tag{10} \] Consequently \[ \|B\|_{\mathrm F,1} \le D(2D+1)\|p\|_{\mathbb R}. \tag{11} \] If \(B=b_0+\sum_{m=1}^N b_m\cos mt\), then \[ \frac{B(t+\theta)-B(t-\theta)}{\sin t} =-2\sum_{m=1}^N b_m\sin(m\theta)U_{m-1}(\cos t). \tag{12} \] This is a polynomial identity also at \(t=0,\pi\), and the last term vanishes because \(\sin(N\theta)=0\). For real \(t\), \(|U_{m-1}(\cos t)|\le m\). Thus \[ \boxed{\qquad \|\mathcal Lp\|_{\mathbb R} \le34N^3\|p\|_{\mathbb R}. \qquad} \tag{13} \] This bound concerns the complete polynomial operator. Bounding its separate singular terms in (7) would not justify (13). Combining (6) and (13) proves, for every integer \(n\), every \(\alpha\in\mathbb C\), and every \(N\ge2\), \[ \boxed{\quad \|F_{n,N,\alpha}\|_{\mathbb R} \ge \frac{|P_N(w_N(\alpha))|} {N^2(|w_N(\alpha)|+34N^3)} \|G_{n,N}\|_{\mathbb R}. \quad} \tag{14} \] This is an unconditional finite-level comparison. At a zero of \(P_N(w_N(\alpha))\) it is simply vacuous. ## 3. A polynomial upper comparison for a fixed number of turns Fix \(n\in\mathbb Z\) and \(A<\infty\). The endpoint-side adapter extends exactly to this fixed power: \[ F_{n,N,\alpha}(Z) =\kappa^n[\operatorname{can}_w (R(w)^{-n}K_N(w,Z))]_{w=w_N(\alpha)}. \tag{15} \] Indeed Frobenius self-adjointness of multiplication gives the same transposed Newton matrix as for a single turn. The original physical values of \(R^{-n}\) have modulus one and their angular derivatives are bounded by \(|n|N/2\). The full-Hermite Fourier reconstruction and the endpoint normal \(Q_N=\partial_wK_N(c_0,\cdot)\), with \(\|Q_N\|_{\mathbb R}\le N^4/4\), therefore give polynomial initial value and first normal for (15), uniformly on \(|\alpha|\le A\). Apply the single-turn proof's forced propagation to (6), retaining \(G_{n,N}\) in its forcing. In its notation the regular physical rows have \[ 0\le q_j<1,\qquad A_j\ge16(j+1)^2/(\pi^2N^2),\qquad |(c_0-w_N(\alpha))/A_j|\le C_A/(j+1)^2. \tag{16} \] The balanced forward matrices have norm at most \(1+C_A/(j+1)\), so all their products are polynomial in \(N\). The value forcing is bounded by \[ C_A\|G_{n,N}\|_{\mathbb R}/(j+1)^2. \tag{17} \] For the differentiated equation, Markov bounds the spectral derivative of the ordinary degree-\(D\) polynomial \(G_{n,N}\) by \(C N^2\|G_{n,N}\|_{\mathbb R}\). All coefficient derivatives have polynomial bounds. The differentiated equation has the same homogeneous matrices, so its forcing and its propagated physical normals have a polynomial factor times \(1+\|G_{n,N}\|_{\mathbb R}\). Stable full-Hermite reconstruction then yields \[ \|F_{n,N,\alpha}\|_{\mathbb R} \le C_{A,n}N^{p_{A,n}} (1+\|G_{n,N}\|_{\mathbb R}). \tag{18} \] The regular-row endpoints and the odd simple node are exactly those of the single-turn proof; no coalescing next row is introduced. The harmless \(1\) can be absorbed. In fact \[ \phi_N(G_{n,N})=R^{-n}(c_0)=\kappa^{-n} \tag{19} \] has modulus one. The original full trace and Markov imply \(|\phi_N(p)|\le C N^3\|p\|_{\mathbb R}\), so \(\|G_{n,N}\|_{\mathbb R}\ge cN^{-3}\). For real \(|\alpha|\le A\), \[ P_N(w_N(\alpha))=4\cosh^2(\alpha/2)\ge4, \qquad |w_N(\alpha)|\le2\cosh(A/2). \tag{20} \] Equations (14),(18)--(20) therefore show \[ \boxed{\quad c_A N^{-5}\|G_{n,N}\|_{\mathbb R} \le\|F_{n,N,\alpha}\|_{\mathbb R} \le C_{A,n}N^{p_{A,n}}\|G_{n,N}\|_{\mathbb R}. \quad} \tag{21} \] Thus any existing exponential norm rate of the actual terminal polynomial \(T(R^{-n})\) is also the rate of this endpoint orbit. The claim holds uniformly for real microscopic parameters in a fixed compact interval. The lower comparison is not extended through the complex zeros in (20). ## 4. Two same-sign turns already have positive rate The original two-crossing terminal theorem, in the same normalization, proves \[ T(R^2)(-2)=\frac{e^{-i\pi/4}}2 e^{N(2G/\pi+i\pi/8)}(1+O(N^{-1})), \tag{22} \] where \(G=\sum_{j\ge0}(-1)^j/(2j+1)^2>0\) is Catalan's constant, and write \(M_\infty=4G/\pi\). The negative-power polynomial has conjugate coefficients. The theorem also bounds the entire real interval by \(C N^a e^{N\,2G/\pi}\). Consequently \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}N^{-1} \log\|T(R^{\pm2})\|_{\mathbb R}=2G/\pi. \tag{23} \] This is through all levels, with neither parity omitted. Combining with (21) gives \[ \boxed{\quad \lim_{N\to\infty}N^{-1} \log\|U_\sigma^2K_N(w_N(\alpha),\cdot)\|_{\mathbb R} =2G/\pi=M_\infty/2,\qquad \sigma=\pm1. \quad} \tag{24} \] The convergence is uniform for real \(|\alpha|\le A\). In particular, for all sufficiently large \(N\), \[ \|U_\sigma^2K_N(w_N(\alpha),\cdot)\|_{\mathbb R} \ge c_A N^{-5}e^{N\,2G/\pi}. \tag{25} \] The input and its first unit-turn image both have polynomial real norm. Their second same-sign turn has positive exponential norm. For the input this also follows directly from (18) at \(n=0\): \(G_{0,N}=e_D=\eta P_N/[N^2(Z-c_0)]\) has real norm at most one, by \(\|P_N'\|_{\mathbb R}\le N^2\). Hence the single-endpoint polynomial theorem cannot be iterated as a polynomial-norm closure rule, even without multiplying different endpoint factors. For clarity, the analytic input (22) was checked from its proof, not from its recorded experiments. The exact terminal expansion is \[ T(R^2)(Z)=N\sum_{k=0}^{N-1} \frac{i^kq^{k(k-1)/2}}{S_k}e_k(Z). \tag{26} \] The finite binomial identity gives (26) with the original carrier and full normals. At \(Z=-2\), its canonical-factorial phase is \[ F(x)=J(2x)-5J(x)+\frac{i\pi}{2}(x^2+x),\qquad J'(x)=\log(2\sin\pi x), \tag{27} \] with the selected saddle \[ e^{2\pi ix_*}=(1+2i)/5,\qquad F''(x_*)=\pi(-4+3i). \tag{28} \] On \(0<\Re x<1/2\), \(\Re F''<0\). The finite cotangent rectangle keeps both exponentially weighted vertical sides; reflection supplies the lower-horizontal gap. The unweighted upper connectors have strictly smaller endpoint values and convex vertical real part. The discarded low tails have continuous rate \(J(2x)-5J(x)\) tending to zero at both ends, while all high indices have polynomial complete norm. The exact factorial normalization gives the nonzero coefficient in (22). These are the proof steps establishing the needed terminal exponential rate.
