They require no theorem about an arbitrary descendant or its hyperbolicity. ## 5. Scope and source readback The norm in (24) is an ordinary real-interval polynomial norm. Further physical traces can cancel its large values; no lower bound for an arbitrary closed graph follows. The conclusion instead identifies the actual terminal action which a repeated source reduction must retain. It neither refutes an action-scale estimate nor proves one for arbitrary short components. Complex parameters where \(P_N(w_N(\alpha))=0\) are explicitly excluded from the lower-rate conclusion. The following complete direct sources were read at these pins: * [Single full endpoint under a unit turn](research_full_endpoint_unit_turn_polynomial_bound.md), SHA256 329ee59c992c359c42775f564f540ffeee7f142bf51b5132913bf4cf2a859d35: canonical forcing, both initial jets, forward physical-normal propagation, and stable full-Hermite reconstruction. * [Original polynomial difference operator](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_edge_kernel_difference_and_endpoint_bound.md), SHA256 5d0d07d4d97d82cca66e0e0c3bf2cecad8e5f58ef8329178278b297cf0d6c5da: exact operator and original endpoint forcing. * [Two-crossing terminal theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_two_crossing_terminal_filling.md), SHA256 7aedaded3efa3058a3250b2120cc4f41bcad1f7f20aff2e7f4dd4fab19aae9ed: exact finite identity, complete contour proof, nonzero germ, and real-interval upper bound. For the last source, its following analytic and algebraic inputs were also read completely, and the used proof implications checked: * [Original finite algebra](../papers/newton-calculus/finite.tex), SHA256 2db2d7e15df0210c32bace4c761bdabadbb5d67140473a61425dac4d1e382f8e: original crossing matrix, turn, and full closing normalization. * [Finite complete-normal bounds](../papers/circle-tree-volume/finite-bounds.tex), SHA256 e4cf66544703af6d9a78208deae971c4d9f4367ba4b2ad660694ee489ef67ea1: polynomial high-index bounds and real interval reconstruction. * [Canonical edge interpolation](../papers/circle-tree-volume/edge-packet.tex), SHA256 53eb6dbfbda3ca639db35911ed50947c29655840337f9d1f1ce909d435013dbb: exact factorial interpolant and its midpoint normalization. * [Factorial product and uniform complex Stirling proof](../papers/conway-asymptotics/factorial.tex), SHA256 fa05557505927ae81f005b90edbd3d0946288e7eacf2363f070d9753db632fe1: normalized product, zero-free strips, and summable complex remainder used on the terminal contour. Only written mathematics, text reads and file hashes were used. No mathematical program, numerical experiment, test or build was run. Existing private notes and public files were unchanged.

title: Exact finite-window conditioning near rational phase colors
text:
# Exact finite-window conditioning near rational phase colors Private written proof, 16 November 2026. For the complete finite-level repeated-turn equations, a fixed window near a rational phase has finitely many analytic coefficient germs in \(h=1/N\). A nonzero full-column minor gives polynomial conditioning on its leading-coefficient unit chart. This conclusion includes all physical first normals. It does not prove that such a minor exists for every active product, and it does not replace the boundary data required by a window with lower-rate data that have not been supplied. ## 1. A fixed actual window and its supplied data Use the original repeated-turn source \[ \mathcal Y_N=U_	au Z_N,\qquad 	au\in\{1,-1\}, \quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad C_N(u)=2\cos(2\pi u+\pi/N). 	ag{1} \] The column \(Z_N\), every cleared full-step row, and all retained source and recovery equations are those of the pinned full-step interface. All counts and signed powers are fixed. Microscopic parameters \( oldsymbol\alpha\) remain in a fixed bounded complex neighborhood; they are not independent physical colors being silently quotiented. Fix a reduced rational phase \[ 0<a/b<1/2,\qquad \gcd(a,b)=1,\qquad v_*=\exp(2\pi i a/b). 	ag{2} \] Let \[ j_N=\lfloor Na/bfloor . 	ag{3} \] Choose a fixed finite set of translated exact rows near \(j_N\). Include their value and first-\(u\)-normal equations. Specify a fixed finite list of unknown shifted components and their normals, forming a packet \(X_N\) of dimension \(d\). Every other shifted component appearing in the chosen rows must either be included in \(X_N\) or put in a separately specified supplied packet \(B_N\). Any genuine inhomogeneous source packet is denoted \(F_N\). Thus the actual finite equations have the form \[ \mathsf A_N X_N=F_N-\mathsf L_N B_N . 	ag{4} \] Rows containing additional unknowns cannot be used in (4) until those unknowns have been accounted for. Repeated occurrences of the same physical component are identified. The window is interior for sufficiently large \(N\), so all its spectral nodes are double and the \(u\)-normal and spectral normal differ by uniformly invertible factors. The choice of supplied packet is part of the assertion. For example, if a two-sided recovery uses a right boundary packet known only to have size \(e^{C N}\), (4) retains that size. It is not an initial-value transport bound at a smaller left boundary rate. ## 2. Exact residue classes and meromorphic coefficient germs **Lemma 1.** Split the levels into residue classes modulo a fixed multiple of \(b\). On each such class there is a fixed rational \(\delta\in(-1,1]\) such that every shifted physical angular color in the window is exactly \[ v_{j_N+k}=q^{2(j_N+k)+1} =v_*q^{\delta+2k},\qquad \delta=2\lfloor Na/bfloor+1-2Na/b . 	ag{5} \] After splitting further for any retained parity or rational carrier phases, every coefficient of \(\mathsf A_N,\mathsf L_N\) is the restriction of a meromorphic germ \[ \mathsf A(h, oldsymbol\alpha),\qquad \mathsf L(h, oldsymbol\alpha) 	ag{6} \] at \(h=0\), with at most a finite-order pole. On a fixed valid coefficient chart a common power \(h^s\), \(s\ge0\), makes these matrices holomorphic and bounded on a slightly smaller chart. *Proof.* If \(N\) increases by \(b\), the floor in (3) increases by \(a\), so \(\delta\) is unchanged. Formula (5) follows without approximation. The raw interface coefficients are obtained by finitely many rational operations, shifts and polynomial coefficient clearings from \[ q^{\pm1},\quad h,\quad v^{\pm1},\quad w_i=2\cosh(\alpha_i h),\quad P_N(w_i)=4\cosh^2(\alpha_i/2). 	ag{7} \] Removable scalar powers of \(h\) in their definitions are retained with their exact limits. Substitution of (5) makes (7) holomorphic in \(h, oldsymbol\alpha\) near \(h=0\). Any remaining coefficient denominator gives a meromorphic germ; on the stated coefficient chart its nonremovable part is a unit after a finite power of \(h\) is extracted. The numbers of operations and shifts are fixed. For the normal rows, ordinary differentiation at fixed \(N\) acts on the coefficient angular variable by \(2\pi i v\,\partial_v\). It preserves this meromorphic class. The ordinary residual is a multiple of \(P_N(C_N(u))\), so its value and first derivative do vanish at the grid; no off-grid homogeneous equation is used. The interface operator coefficients do not require a varying Gaussian carrier to be discarded. If a chosen row normalization retains \(\eta=(-1)^{N-1}\) or \[ \kappa=\exp\{\pi i(N-1)^2/(2N)\} =-i^N e^{\pi i h/2}, 	ag{8} \] enlarge the modulus to include \(4\). If physical crossing values at the moving center are explicitly included as coefficient factors, the additional carrier is \((-1)^{n(j_N+k)}q^{n(j_N+k)(j_N+k+1)}\). After (5), its phase is a rational multiple of \(\pi N\), a residue-class constant, and an analytic \(O(h)\) phase. A modulus divisible by \(4b^2\) suffices for these fixed integer powers. More generally choose a common multiple for every fixed rational phase actually retained. This finite refinement does not change the source or its modulus on physical levels. No meromorphic-germ assertion is made about \(X_N,B_N,F_N\) themselves. They remain the actual possibly exponentially large source packets. \(\square\) The coefficient-chart qualification is substantive. At a parameter where a proposed denominator loses its leading unit, re-clear the original rows or choose another valid coefficient chart before applying the lemma. Nonunit physical clearing factors are not canceled in the original algebra. ## 3. Nonzero actual minors give polynomial recovery **Theorem 2.** Fix one residue class and one coefficient chart from Lemma 1. Suppose \(h^s\mathsf A(h, oldsymbol\alpha)\) is holomorphic and bounded there, and some selection of \(d\) actual rows has determinant \[ \det \widehat{\mathsf A}_0(h, oldsymbol\alpha) =h^
u\{c( oldsymbol\alpha)+h r(h, oldsymbol\alpha)\}, \qquad 
u\ge0, \quad \widehat{\mathsf A}=h^s\mathsf A . 	ag{9} \] On a compact parameter set where \(|c( oldsymbol\alpha)|\ge c_*>0\), there is a left inverse of the full matrix \(\mathsf A_N\) with norm at most \(C N^K\), for a fixed \(K\). Consequently the original packet satisfies \[ \|X_N\|\le C N^{K'}  igl(\|F_N\|+\|B_N\| igr). 	ag{10} \] All quantities on the right are the supplied packets of (4). The constants and exponents are uniform on that fixed compact unit chart. *Proof.* After decreasing the \(h\)-disk, the expression in braces in (9) has modulus at least \(c_*/2\). The entries of the adjugate of \(\widehat{\mathsf A}_0\) are uniformly bounded, since its size is fixed. Its inverse is therefore \(O(h^{-
u})\). Select those rows of \(h^s\mathsf A X\), invert, and retain the factor \(h^s\) on the right. This defines a left inverse of the full matrix; one may take \(K=\max(0,
u-s)\). The remaining coefficient matrix \(\mathsf L_N\) is bounded by a fixed power of \(N\) by Lemma 1. Applying the left inverse to (4) proves (10). No equation or source channel has been dropped: the selected rows recover the packet, while the other actual rows remain its compatibility equations. \(\square\) For fixed parameters, this gives an exact eventual dichotomy. Either at least one full-column minor is a nonzero meromorphic germ, in which case the rank is full and the conditioning is polynomial for all sufficiently large levels in that residue class, or every such minor is the zero germ. In the latter case the chosen matrix is rank deficient for all sufficiently small \(h\) in its coefficient chart. This is rank of the specified finite window; it is not a statement that the entire global source problem has a free parameter. For varying parameters, a nonzero minor as a germ in \((h, oldsymbol\alpha)\) does not give uniform conditioning on an arbitrary compact set. The leading coefficient in (9) can vanish there, and parameters may approach its zero set very rapidly with \(N\). The unit-chart hypothesis must be verified or replaced by a separate stratified estimate. If the supplied data obey uniform bounds \[ \|F_N\|\le e^{N A_F+o(N)},\qquad \|B_N\|\le e^{N A_B+o(N)}, 	ag{11} \] then (10) gives only \[ \limsup_{N	o\infty}N^{-1}\log\|X_N\| \le\max(A_F,A_B) 	ag{12} \] along the residue class. Thus a right endpoint ceiling larger than the incoming rate remains larger in this result. All fixed parameter derivatives satisfy the same statement if the unit bound holds on a larger parameter neighborhood and the supplied source bounds hold there, by Cauchy's formula. The actual first physical normals are already entries of (4). ## 4. What must still be proved for the complete repeated-turn source The matrices in this note are formed from the full finite-\(N\) rows and their normal equations, with any original recovery and source constraints used in the window explicitly included. They are not formed from a principal scalar certificate. The rank-loss theorem gives the same warning at a single row: the first-normal block can determine a missing value without determining its normal, whereas further aligned rows can restore the full rank. For fixed active products, finitely many rational exceptional phases and finitely many residue classes therefore reduce local polynomial conditioning to exact nonvanishing assertions of the form (9), together with honestly supplied boundary packets. This note does not establish those assertions for every product or every minimal resonance core. Nor does it prescribe a fixed window that must work universally. An identity of all candidate minors may reflect a genuine remaining local channel, an unnecessarily large unknown packet, or extra solutions introduced by a nonunit clearing. It must be examined using the original source constraints. Conversely a nonzero minor may arise from small quantum terms even when the classical phase is exceptional. The arithmetic observation (5) does not decide either outcome. No rate for a general repeated-turn output, no disappearance of a clearing component, and no geometric gap is inferred. The conditioning statement is useful only after its exact rank and boundary-data premises are met. ## 5. Direct sources The complete direct source texts were read at the following pins, with the directly used formulas and hashes checked: * [Full-step repeated-turn tensor interface](research_full_step_repeated_turn_tensor_interface.md), SHA256 ef851eab40c8b2c44388a41d324e2fa41d4400f0f2118fe587405911e00e3398: exact polynomial row construction, rational coefficient field, source and recovery columns, full-normal residual interpretation and retained original carriers. * [Exact rank loss and the physical normal](research_simple_rank_loss_full_normal_transport.md), SHA256 307a26ca51fc9b0cc7bff689f52a873a49d7773406e67d243ec71021401e4694: the exact value-and-normal equations, complete aligned-row criterion and the distinction between local and global recovery. Only written mathematics and source-text/hash reads were used. No mathematical program, numerical experiment, test or build was run. Adopted notes and public manuscripts are unchanged.

title: The retained Pachner ratio in the original physical flag algebra
text: # The retained Pachner ratio in the original physical flag algebra Research note, 22 November 2026. The residual cyclic factorial in the first source-preserving nine-cell beta move has an explicit realization on the original two quantum-group heads. It is a commutator of the existing cyclic dilogarithm with a completed physical flag shift. The completion retains its missing corner, and the change of coordinates retains the full original exterior covector. The oscillator preparation used below is already proved in [P]. The new identification is with the two particular boundary clocks of [R, (31)]. It does not identify the other factors of that source with the nilpotent factors of the mixed pentagon. ## 1. The original heads and their prepared flags Fix \(N\geq2\), \(d=N-1\), and \[ q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\quad x=-q^{-1},\quad \lambda=x^{-1}=-q,\quad k=x^N=(-1)^d,\qquad F_a=(Q;Q)_a. \tag{1} \] In particular \(F_0=1\) and \(F_d=N\). Every index of a physical head lies in \(0,\ldots,d\); brackets denote reduction to this set. Write \(Z|a\rangle=Q^a|a\rangle\). Choose the auxiliary flag wraps \[ S_1|d\rangle=|0\rangle,\qquad S_2|d\rangle=k|0\rangle, \tag{2} \] with the ordinary raising arrows otherwise. Thus \(S_1^N=1\) and \(S_2^N=k\), including even \(N\). These auxiliary completions do not change the original nilpotent matrices. In the original balanced basis, \[ K|a\rangle=xQ^{-a}|a\rangle,\qquad e|a\rangle=\lambda(1-Q^{-a})|a-1\rangle\quad(a>0), \qquad e|0\rangle=0. \tag{3} \] The complete physical flags of [A] are \[ \Delta=Z_1(\lambda S_2-S_1),\qquad \gamma=-e_2K_1,\qquad v=Z_2^{-1}+S_1e_2. \tag{4} \] Their exact finite identities are \[ \begin{gathered} \Delta^N=\gamma^N=0,\quad v^N=1,\quad \Delta v=Qv\Delta,\quad v\gamma=Q\gamma v,\\ \Delta\gamma=\lambda(v-1),\qquad \gamma\Delta=\lambda(Q^{-1}v-1). \end{gathered} \tag{5} \] They retain the endpoint rows of the original crossing. In particular, the sign in (2) is required to obtain \(\Delta^N=0\). Let \(J_+|a\rangle=|a+1\rangle\) for \(a<d\), with \(J_+|d\rangle=0\), and put \[ P(A)=\sum_{h=0}^d\frac{(-1)^hQ^{h(h-1)/2}}{F_h}A^h, \qquad C=P(-S_1e_2Z_2). \tag{6} \] The argument is nilpotent, so \(C\) is invertible. The preparation identities of [P, (8)] are \[ C^{-1}vC=Z_2^{-1},\qquad C^{-1}\Delta C=K_1^{-1}J_{+,2},\qquad [C,\gamma]=0. \tag{7} \] These are identities of the complete \(N^2\)-dimensional physical space, rather than a quotient retaining only eigenvalues. The original cup and averaged marked cap are \[ p=N\sum_{a=0}^d x^{a-d}|a,d-a\rangle,\qquad \ell|a,b\rangle=x^b/N^2,\qquad \ell p=1. \tag{8} \] As proved in [P], \(\Delta p=0\), \(vp=Qp\), and \(p=N\lambda^d C|0,d\rangle\). ## 2. A cyclic completion with its actual corner Define \[ \Pi=E_1(v)=\frac1N\sum_{r=0}^dQ^{-r}v^r,\qquad c_*=[(-\lambda)^dF_d]^{-1},\qquad \Gamma=\gamma+c_*\Pi\Delta^d. \tag{9} \] Here \(\operatorname{im}\Pi=\ker\Delta\) has dimension \(N\), by (7). For \(h\in\ker\Delta\), (5) gives \[ \Delta\gamma^j h=-\lambda(1-Q^j)\gamma^{j-1}h, \qquad v\gamma^jh=Q^{j+1}\gamma^jh. \tag{10} \] The first formula is used for \(1\leq j\leq d\), and the second also holds for \(j=0\). Thus the maps \(h\mapsto\gamma^jh\), \(0\leq j\leq d\), are injective with distinct clock eigenvalues. Their images exhaust the physical space. The explicit coefficient-extraction maps are \[ L_j=[(-\lambda)^jF_j]^{-1}\Pi\Delta^j, \qquad L_j\gamma^rh=\delta_{jr}h. \tag{11} \] For \(j<r\), the projector kills the remaining nontrivial clock eigenvalue; for \(j>r\), a remaining \(\Delta\) kills \(h\). At \(j=r\), the product in (10) is \((-\lambda)^jF_j\). Consequently \(\Gamma\gamma^jh=\gamma^{j+1}h\) for \(j<d\), while \(\Gamma\gamma^dh=h\). In particular \[ \Gamma^N=1,\qquad v\Gamma=Q\Gamma v. \tag{12} \] The added rank-\(N\) term is essential. In the original prepared coordinates its entire matrix is printable: \[ C^{-1}\Gamma C=-e_2K_1+ c_*K_1^{-d}\otimes|d\rangle\langle0|_2. \tag{13} \] Indeed \(C^{-1}\Pi C=I\otimes|d\rangle\langle d|\), and \(C^{-1}\Delta^dC=K_1^{-d}\otimes|d\rangle\langle0|\). The last arrow in (13), multiplied by the \(d\) ordinary arrows, has coefficient one. No nilpotent operator has been inverted. ## 3. The cyclic factor and its finite commutator Let \(t\beta\ne0\), \(\beta^N=1-t^N\), on the marked root cover. Use the existing determinant-normalized function from [A, (22)], \[ \mathfrak d_N(z)=(1-z^N)^{d/(2N)} \prod_{j=1}^d(1-Q^jz)^{-j/N},\qquad \mathcal C_t=\mathfrak d_N(tv). \tag{14} \] All roots are continued together from the anchored chart at zero to the specified value of \(\beta\). On each clock eigenvalue its exact functional equation is \[ \frac{\mathfrak d_N(Qz)}{\mathfrak d_N(z)} =\frac{\beta}{1-z},\qquad z^N=t^N. \tag{15} \] These factors are units on the stated nondegenerate cover. Combining (12) and (15), including the cyclic arrow, gives \[ \mathcal C_t\Gamma^m\mathcal C_t^{-1} =\Gamma^m\frac{\beta^m}{(tv;Q)_m},\qquad R_m(tv):=\beta^{-m}(tv;Q)_m =\mathcal C_t\Gamma^{-m}\mathcal C_t^{-1}\Gamma^m. \tag{16} \] This holds for \(0\leq m\leq N\). At \(m=N\), both sides equal one because \((tv;Q)_N=1-t^N=\beta^N\). Thus (16) retains the complete periodic shift, unlike a verification on the nonzero nilpotent arrows alone. It uses precisely the cyclic factor in the mixed identity [A, (24)]; its common determinant normalization cancels in this commutator, while the relative root \(\beta\) remains fixed. ## 4. Matching the two boundary clocks of the actual source For the positive eight-face adapter [R, (17)], name its physical output indices \[ m=[-k_2],\qquad s=[-k_1]. \tag{17} \] Its physical matrix entry is \(M_{m,s;a,b}\). These are full colors, not meridian or quantum-parameter derivative indices. In [R, (30)], rename the four internal variables \(u,v,s,z\) as \(u_0,v_0,s_0,z_0\). Then \[ K=u_0+v_0+1,\quad L=1-k_1+s_0+z_0,\quad r_0=u_0+v_0+s_0+z_0+2, \qquad K+L=r_0+s\pmod N. \tag{18} \] For \(\alpha=\alpha_{0235}\) and \(\beta=\beta_{0235}\), the retained ratio of [R, (31)] and [E, (13)] is exactly the following, with the primitive root called \(q\) in [E] here identified with \(Q\): \[ \frac{\overline W_{0235}(K+L)} {\overline W_{0235}(K+L-k_2)} =R_m(\alpha Q^{r_0+s}). \tag{19} \] Here \(\alpha^N+\beta^N=1\). Fixing the internal \(r_0\) only fixes a scalar \(t=\alpha Q^{r_0}\); no internal variable is identified with a physical boundary index. Define the corresponding output coupon \[ \mathcal F_{r_0}|m,s\rangle =R_m(tQ^s)|m,s\rangle. \tag{20} \] It is defined on every two-head boundary coordinate, independently of any subsequent support restriction. Let \(\operatorname{Rev}_0|s\rangle=|[-s]\rangle\), and put \[ \mathcal B=C(I\otimes\operatorname{Rev}_0),\qquad M=\mathcal BZ_1\mathcal B^{-1}=CZ_1C^{-1}. \tag{21} \] Then \(\mathcal BZ_2\mathcal B^{-1}=v\). The operator \(M\) has \(M^N=1\) and commutes with \(\Delta,\gamma,v\): this follows from (7), since \(Z_1\) commutes with \(K_1^{-1}J_{+,2}\), with \(\gamma\), and with \(Z_2^{-1}\). It therefore commutes with \(\Gamma\) as well. Define its explicit projectors and a controlled shift by \[ P_m(M)=\frac1N\sum_{j=0}^dQ^{-mj}M^j,\qquad \mathcal U=\sum_{m=0}^dP_m(M)\Gamma^m,\qquad \mathcal U^{-1}=\sum_{m=0}^dP_m(M)\Gamma^{-m}. \tag{22} \] The projectors retain all \(N\) multiplicity coordinates. No choice of an eigenbasis or a smaller physical module is required. **Exact residual adapter.** For every boundary coordinate and every internal \(r_0\), \[ \boxed{\quad \mathcal B\mathcal F_{r_0}\mathcal B^{-1} =\mathcal C_t\mathcal U^{-1} \mathcal C_t^{-1}\mathcal U, \qquad t=\alpha Q^{r_0}.\quad} \tag{23} \] To prove this, conjugate the two commuting boundary clocks by \(\mathcal B\). The left side is \(\sum_mP_m(M)R_m(tv)\). Each projector commutes with \(\mathcal C_t\) and \(\Gamma\), so (16) gives exactly the right side. This proof establishes all matrix entries, including every wrap. ## 5. Original cap and arbitrary exterior The coordinate change has the following exact source data: \[ \mathcal B^{-1}p=N\lambda^d|0,1\rangle,\qquad (\ell\mathcal B)_{m,s}=\frac{x^aF_a}{N^2}, \quad a=[-s]. \tag{24} \] The first formula follows from (8). For the second, expand the finite preparation, with the wrap \(S_1^N=1\) fixed in (2), using \({a\brack h}_Q=F_a/(F_hF_{a-h})\): \[ C|m,a\rangle=\sum_{h=0}^a(-1)^hx^hQ^{h(h+1)/2} {a\brack h}_Q|[m+h],a-h\rangle. \tag{25} \] Pairing with \(\ell\) leaves \(x^a/N^2\) times \(\sum_h(-1)^hQ^{h(h+1)/2}{a\brack h}_Q=(Q;Q)_a\). Thus (24) retains the whole marked row. Its pairing with its displayed source column is one. With a different first wrap, (25) would carry the corresponding wrap powers; they have not been silently omitted. These are the original flag source expressed in the clock frame. They do **not** assert that the exterior of the nine-cell coupon is this special source. For an arbitrary actual exterior row \(\eta\) and remaining output tensor \(Y_{r_0}\), the correctly oriented equality is \[ \eta\mathcal F_{r_0}Y_{r_0} =(\eta\mathcal B^{-1}) (\mathcal C_t\mathcal U^{-1} \mathcal C_t^{-1}\mathcal U) (\mathcal BY_{r_0}). \tag{26} \] The row in [R, (23b),(23c)] is used literally in this formula. All paired-fiber sums, \(f_m\) factors, \(C_N\), Cartan factors, pivots, framing and peripheral lines stay in that row or in \(Y_{r_0}\). Equation (26) is bilinear; there is no Hermitian conjugation. It holds before the remaining finite sums. The identity applies to each circle/ray pattern before integration, so the source-preserving integrability statement of [R] carries it through the actual pattern integrals and their retained relative boundary components. ## 6. A source-fixed orthogonal coordinate frame There is a useful explicit rescaling of the same adapter. For \(a=[-s]\), set \[ H|m,s\rangle=\frac{\lambda^aQ^{ma}}{F_a}|m,s\rangle, \qquad \widetilde{\mathcal B}=\mathcal BH,\qquad \widetilde{\mathcal B}|m,s\rangle =\frac{\Delta^a|m,0\rangle}{F_a}. \tag{27} \] The last identity follows from (7), since \(C|m,0\rangle=|m,0\rangle\). The diagonal \(H\) commutes with both boundary clocks and with \(\mathcal F_{r_0}\). Replacing \(\mathcal B\) by \(\widetilde{\mathcal B}\) leaves the actual right side of (23) unchanged; the same replacement applies in (26). In these coordinates, with \(S_s\) the cyclic shift of the second coordinate and \(E_0\) its zero-coordinate projector, \[ \begin{gathered} v=Z_s,\quad M=Z_m,\quad \Gamma=\lambda S_sZ_s,\\ \Delta=S_s^{-1}(1-QZ_s^{-1}),\qquad \gamma=\lambda S_sZ_s(I-E_0). \end{gathered} \tag{28} \] For \(\Delta\), this follows directly from (27). For \(\gamma\), use \(\Delta\gamma=\lambda(v-1)\) and \(\gamma|m,0\rangle=0\). The added arrow of \(\Gamma\) has coefficient \((-\lambda)^{-d}=\lambda\). Its full cycle is \(\lambda^NQ^{N(N-1)/2}=1\), retaining the even-level sign. The original endpoint data become \[ \widetilde{\mathcal B}^{-1}p=N^2|0,1\rangle,\qquad (\ell\widetilde{\mathcal B})_{m,s}=Q^{-ms}/N^2. \tag{29} \] Hence, in the flat norm of these coordinates, \(v,M,\Gamma,\mathcal U\) are unitary, \(\|\Delta\|\leq2\), and \(\|\gamma\|=1\). The source column and full cap row have norms \(N^2\) and \(N^{-1}\). Equivalently this specifies the positive physical Gram \((\widetilde{\mathcal B}^{-1})^*\widetilde{\mathcal B}^{-1}\), fixed without reference to the exterior word. It is not asserted to have tame condition number in the original balanced norm. The cyclic factor \(\mathcal C_t\), and every transformed exterior coupon, retain their actual matrix entries and actions. ## 7. Scope The physical operator construction (1)--(29) is valid for all \(N\geq2\), even or composite. The existing literal nine-cell source occurrence (17)--(19) is proved in [R,E] for odd \(N>2\); nothing here extends that charged triangulation definition to even levels. The physical space throughout has dimension \(N^2\), including all original head coordinates and their original crossing endpoint data. This realizes the specific retained ratio as a coupon in the actual flag algebra. It does not show that the remaining \(W\)-factors in [R, (31)] are the neighboring \(P(a\Delta)\) factors in [A, (24)]. The negative adapter [R, (18)] uses a mixed input/output pair of boundary indices; (23) does not assert the same left-output endomorphism formula for it without a further typed dual transport. Nor does it justify cancelling adjacent commutators without checking their full shared frames and inverse-dual exterior. No further Pachner move, geometric source identification, whole-word norm bound or scalar noncancellation follows from (23) alone. At a singular Fermat wall, the relative expressions and their source lattices must be retained; separate inverse factors in (14)--(23) are not evaluated there. ## Complete direct sources All operator and source normalizations used above are fixed by these complete texts. The cyclic-function and oscillator methods are existing ones; the contribution is the source-specific all-boundary matching (18)--(23) and its literal exterior transport. - [A] [Actual shared quantum flags and their charged exchange](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_shared_quantum_flags_and_charged_exchange.md), 459 lines, SHA-256 `dcab795cc141e2e1db726998cf7b1141dd03c681eaae9076387f90581f53a7d9`. - [P] [The full dilogarithm resolves the actual charged flag pentagon at the root](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_marked_full_phi_flag_pentagon.md), 328 lines, SHA-256 `3052cef4a1d666253562c13ceaf6a9bc472baf7691f23d13e33bb3f8d6e9888f`. - [R] [Full-Psi ray crossings and the original nine-cell boundary](research_full_psi_ray_crossings_and_nine_cell_boundary.md), 588 lines, SHA-256 `495a2fde1ed1d7ca0707f060208121bddb2673be21ff3bcb9bac737420ac2d24`. - [E] [Canonical evaluation of the literal nine-cell crossing](research_nine_cell_canonical_crossing_evaluation.md), 424 lines, SHA-256 `332062e67d64ab4a0767637c0fdd96f186d62c430ad38042aef35ad857d8d7c9`.

title: The classical crossing relation in the external Rivin coordinates
text:
# The classical crossing relation in the external Rivin coordinates Private written deduction, 14 November 2026. The external formulas are those of `rivin-jones` at commit `e956fb919ac7d1bbc7cb3d3873fbac993feb94b7`, in `docs/MATHEMATICS.md` and `python/rivin_jones/r_matrix.py`. Their text was read; no code, numerical calculation, import, or test was executed. This gives the holomorphic generating function directly from those coefficients, an explicit rational crossing map, and its triangular matrix and Wirtinger interpretation. It keeps the actual highest-weight cut, quantum pivots, writhe factor and ordinary bends in view. The general critical-correspondence-to-representation theorem is already present in [the marked braid calculation](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/marked_braid_holonomy.md), Sections 4--6. The contribution here is its direct derivation and coordinate dictionary for the external matrices, not a new proof that a geometric critical component contributes to the original scalar. ## 1. A holomorphic primitive fixed by the actual coefficients Put \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\), and \(A_N=e^{-\pi i/(2N)}\). Let \(I,J\) be the overstrand and understrand inputs and \(k\) the transfer. The outputs on these two strands are \(I-k,J+k\), with \(0\le k\le\min(I,d-J)\). External positive input order is \((I,J)\) and negative input order is \((J,I)\). The literal coefficient is \[ R_\sigma(I,J;k)=A_N^{Q_\sigma(I,J,k)}  rac{S_I S_{J+k}}{S_{I-k}S_JS_k},\qquad S_a=\prod_{r=1}^a2\sin(\pi r/N),\quad S_0=1. 	ag{1} \] where \[  egin{split} Q_+&=(d-2I+2k)(d-2J-2k)+k(k-1)+Nk,\ Q_-&=-(d-2I)(d-2J)-k(k-1)-Nk. \end{split} 	ag{2} \] These identities, including their phases, were derived directly in [the role-frame calculation](research_rivin_role_frames_and_bridge_angles.md), Section 1. No positive boundary frame is applied in this section. On a simply connected neighborhood of a compact subinterval of \(0<z<1\), fix \[ \ell(z)=\Log(1-e^{2\pi iz})-\pi iz+ rac{\pi i}{2}, \qquad \mathcal J(z)=  rac{\operatorname{Li}_2(1)-\operatorname{Li}_2(e^{2\pi iz})}{2\pi i} + rac{\pi i}{2}(z-z^2). 	ag{3} \] The marks are the continuation for which \(\ell(z)=\log(2\sin\pi z)\) on that real interval and \(\mathcal J(0)=0\) by a one-sided limit. Then \(\mathcal J'=\ell\), and \(\mathcal J\) restricts to the real sine-factorial integral. Continue this marked primitive on logarithmic charts avoiding the integer divisors; no entire interpolation of the finite factorials is asserted. For \((u,v,t)=(I/N,J/N,k/N)\), define \[  egin{split} p_+&=(1-2u+2t)(1-2v-2t)+t^2+t,\ p_-&=-(1-2u)(1-2v)-t^2-t,\ \mathcal S_\sigma(u,v,t) &=\mathcal J(u)+\mathcal J(v+t)-\mathcal J(u-t) -\mathcal J(v)-\mathcal J(t)- rac{\pi i}{2}p_\sigma. \end{split} 	ag{4} \] The principal action is calibrated by the physical lattice: on every compact subset of \(0<t<u<1\), \(0<v<v+t<1\), the exact logarithm \(-\pi iQ_\sigma/(2N)\) of the monomial phase and the positive logarithms of the \(S\)'s give \[ \log R_\sigma=N\mathcal S_\sigma+O(\log N). 	ag{5} \] This uses the endpoint-uniform factorial estimate in [the crossing norm proof](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/weighted_crossing_source_gap.md), Section 2. In particular the leading phase in (4) is fixed by (2), not chosen by a stationary point. Equation (5) alone does not justify replacing a whole finite sum by an integral on an arbitrary complex cycle. The same action follows directly from exact contiguity. For example, \[  rac{R_\sigma(I+1,J;k)}{R_\sigma(I,J;k)} =A_N^{Q_\sigma(I+1,J,k)-Q_\sigma(I,J,k)}  rac{\sin(\pi(I+1)/N)}{\sin(\pi(I-k+1)/N)}, 	ag{6} \] and the \(k\)-ratio has sine factor \(2\sin(\pi(J+k+1)/N)\sin(\pi(I-k)/N)/\sin(\pi(k+1)/N)\). Their limits are \(e^{\partial_u\mathcal S_\sigma}\) and \(e^{\partial_t\mathcal S_\sigma}\). The \(J\)-ratio gives the third derivative. Thus the following rational equations are symbols of the actual difference ratios, rather than consequences of an arbitrary off-grid continuation. ### Exact primitive comparison with the physical and incidence actions The finite strand adapter fixes this comparison, including the constant. Write its scalar coefficient as \[ T_Ne_i=t_N(i)|d-iangle,\qquad t_N(i)=q^{-i(i-1)/2}. \] Equation (3) of [the local adapter](research_rivin_jones_local_crossing_adapter.md) identifies the external sign \(\sigma\) with physical sign \(-\sigma\), with no extra scalar. For either signed coefficient in the over/under notation of (1), its exact output/input scalar ratio is \[  rac{t_N(J+k)t_N(I-k)}{t_N(I)t_N(J)} =q^{k(I-J-k)}. 	ag{6a} \] The order of the two outputs does not affect this product. In physical roles the over-input, under-input and transfer are \((d-J,d-I,k)\). Thus the limiting physical coordinates used in [the joint clock action](research_joint_clock_phase_equations.md), equation (27a), are \[ (U,V,J_0)=(t,1-v-t,1-u), 	ag{6b} \] where \(V\) is the physical over-output and \(J_0\) the under-input. The real domain of (5) maps into \(U,V,J_0>0\), \(U+V<1\), \(U+J_0<1\). For clarity that physical action, with its state-independent Cartan factor kept separately, is \[  egin{split} G_	au(U,V,J_0) &=\mathcal J(U+V)+\mathcal J(J_0+U) -\mathcal J(V)-\mathcal J(J_0)-\mathcal J(U) +\pi i	au\psi(U,V,J_0),\ \psi(U,V,J_0) &=-J_0-V+2VJ_0-U/2+U(J_0+V)+U^2/2. \end{split} \] On these canonical real strips, and on their common marked analytic continuations, the primitive identity is exactly \[  oxed{\quad \mathcal S_\sigma(u,v,t)+\pi i\,t(u-v-t) =G_{-\sigma}(t,1-v-t,1-u)- rac{\sigma\pi i}{2}. \quad} 	ag{6c} \] Here \(\pi i\,t(u-v-t)\) is precisely the leading logarithm of (6a), while \(-\sigma\pi i/2\) is the leading logarithm of the physical factor \(\kappa^{-\sigma}\), \(\kappa=q^{d^2/2}\). No additive constant has been chosen from a critical point. To verify (6c) directly, the marked sine primitive satisfies \(\mathcal J(1-z)=-\mathcal J(z)\) on the strip. This follows from \(\ell(1-z)=\ell(z)\) and the endpoint value \(\mathcal J(1)=0\). Applying reflection to each term of \(G\) gives exactly the five sine-primitive terms of (4). Put \[ \psi_*=-u-v+2uv+t(u-v)+t/2-t^2/2 =\psi(t,1-v-t,1-u). \] The remaining quadratic identities are \[  rac{p_+}{2}-t(u-v-t)=\psi_*+ rac12, \qquad - rac{p_-}{2}+t(u-v-t)=\psi_*+ rac12. 	ag{6d} \] Expansion proves both, and hence (6c) for both signs with its displayed constant. The joint clock theorem, equations (27e)--(27g), proves that the corrected incidence primitive on its specified canonical clock graph is exactly \(G_	au\). Consequently (6c) completes the local primitive comparison from the external coefficients to the physical crossing and to the full incidence action. The finite boundary frame changes, the Cartan constants and the logarithmic/Fourier lifts remain part of that comparison. Neither this identity nor its analytic continuation identifies the original quantum cycle with a descending cycle. ## 2. Exponentiated derivatives and the rational crossing maps Write \(x=e^{\pi iu},y=e^{\pi iv},z=e^{\pi it}\), and let \(E_{\sigma,u}=e^{\partial_u\mathcal S_\sigma}\), with analogous notation for \(v,t\). Differentiation of (3)--(4) gives \[  egin{array}{c|cc} &\sigma=+&\sigma=-\ \hline E_{\sigma,u} &-\dfrac{1-x^2}{y^2z(z^2-x^2)} &-\dfrac{y^2z(1-x^2)}{z^2-x^2}\[6pt] E_{\sigma,v} &-\dfrac{z(1-y^2z^2)}{x^2(1-y^2)} &-\dfrac{x^2(1-y^2z^2)}{z(1-y^2)}\[6pt] E_{\sigma,t} &\dfrac{yz^2(1-y^2z^2)(z^2-x^2)}{x^3(1-z^2)} &-\dfrac{(1-y^2z^2)(z^2-x^2)}{xy(1-z^2)}. \end{array} 	ag{7} \] For instance \(e^{\ell(u)-\ell(u-t)} =z^{-1}(1-x^2)/(1-x^2/z^2)\); the quadratic phase in (4) supplies the rest of the first row. This also fixes the half-clock signs. Use the canonical convention that an action differential is output momentum times output variation minus input momentum times input variation. Conservation gives output positions \((u-t,v+t)\). Introducing the arbitrary exponential \(	au\) of its conormal multiplier, the four momentum exponentials satisfy \[ p_I= rac{	au}{E_uE_t},\quad p_J= rac{	au}{E_v},\quad p_{I'}= rac{	au}{E_t},\quad p_{J'}=	au. 	ag{8} \] Equivalently their three ratios are \(p_{I'}/p_I=E_u\), \(p_{J'}/p_J=E_v\), \(p_{J'}/p_{I'}=E_t\). These equations follow by differentiating with \(t=u-u'\) on \(u'+v'=u+v\); they retain the otherwise undetermined common momentum. Make the same momentum gauge on every strand: \[ X=x^2,\quad Y=y^2,\quad Z=z^2,\qquad a=p_I/x,\quad b=p_J/y. 	ag{9} \] It preserves the cotangent two-form, since subtracting \(\pi iu\) from \(\log p_I\) adds a function of the position alone. Eliminating \(	au,z\) in (7)--(8) gives the following rational formulas. For the external positive crossing, \[  egin{split} Z&=1- rac ab rac{(1-X)(1-Y)}Y,\ X'&=X/Z,\qquad Y'=YZ,\ a'&=- rac{a(1-X)}{Y(Z-X)},\qquad b'=- rac{b(1-YZ)}{X(1-Y)}. \end{split} 	ag{10} \] Here the output is in checked order \(((Y',b'),(X',a'))\). For the external negative crossing, written with the same over/under roles as in (1), \[  egin{split} Z^{-1}&=1- rac ab rac{(1-X)(1-Y)}X,\ X'&=X/Z,\qquad Y'=YZ,\ a'&=- rac{aYZ(1-X)}{Z-X},\qquad b'=- rac{bX(1-YZ)}{Z(1-Y)}. \end{split} 	ag{11} \] Its input is \(((Y,b),(X,a))\) and output is \(((X',a'),(Y',b'))\). All formulas concern the regular open set where their displayed factors and the shapes in (7) are nonzero. For completeness, the cancellation that solves for \(Z\) is \[  rac{p_I}{p_J}=  egin{cases} xy(1-z^2)/[(1-x^2)(1-y^2)],&+,\ (x^3/y)(1-z^{-2})/[(1-x^2)(1-y^2)],&-. \end{cases} \] Substitution of (9) gives (10)--(11). Their other formulas follow from \(a'/a=zE_u\) and \(b'/b=E_v/z\). They are inverse checked maps. Indeed after (10), \[  rac{a'}{b'}=  rac{X(1-Z)}{(Z-X)(1-YZ)}. \] Putting \((X/Z,YZ,a',b')\) into (11) gives \(Z_-=1/Z\). Its two momentum multipliers are respectively the reciprocals of those in (10), so it returns \((X,Y,a,b)\). This proves the inverse on the stated open chart. In particular fixed positive and negative powers and arbitrary fixed signed words have rational classical relations obtained by composition, with their singular loci retained. ## 3. Exact triangular factorization on a parabolic surface For one strand define \[ k=-X,\qquad e=(1-X)a,\qquad f= rac{1-X}{Xa}. \] Then \[ ef+k+k^{-1}=-2. 	ag{12} \] These are also the principal symbols of the external generators: with \(v=A_N^2=q^{-1}\) and \([r]_v=(v^r-v^{-r})/(v-v^{-1})\), the source module has \(K_v e_i=v^{d-2i}e_i\), \(E_v e_i=[N-i]_v e_{i-1}\), \(F_v e_i=[i+1]_v e_{i+1}\). On a local exponential state the symbols of \(K_v,(v-v^{-1})E_v,(v-v^{-1})F_v\) are precisely \((k,e,f)\). A lowering matrix reads the input state one index higher, which is the momentum factor \(p_I\); the raising matrix gives its inverse. The displayed external realization and coproducts are proved in [the regular bend note](research_rivin_jones_regular_bends_and_newton_turn.md), Section 1. Introduce \[ B_+(k,e)= egin{pmatrix}1&e\0&k\end{pmatrix},\qquad B_-(k,f)= egin{pmatrix}1&0\-f&k^{-1}\end{pmatrix}, \qquad M=k^{-1}B_-^{-1}B_+ = egin{pmatrix}k^{-1}&e/k\f&k+ef\end{pmatrix}. 	ag{13} \] Thus \(\det M=1\), \(\operatorname{tr}M=-2\). On \(X
e1\), it is noncentral; its image in \(\mathrm{PSL}_2\) is parabolic. Label input over/under strands by \(1,2\), and retain these role labels on \(1',2'\). Formula (10) gives \[ Z=1-e_1f_2,\quad k_1'=k_1/Z,\quad k_2'=k_2Z,\quad e_1'=e_1/(k_2Z),\quad f_2'=k_1f_2/Z. 	ag{14} \] It also satisfies the two full coproduct identities \[ e_2'k_1'+e_1'=e_1k_2+e_2,\qquad f_2'+(k_2')^{-1}f_1'=f_1+k_1^{-1}f_2. 	ag{15} \] Here is an elementary coefficient check of both, beyond trace matching. Put \(T=(a/b)(1-X)\), so \(Z=1-T(1-Y)/Y\) and \(1-YZ=(1-Y)(1+T)\). The first identity after cancellation of its nonzero factors is \[ Y(1-Y)(1+T)^2-T =[Y-T(1-Y)]\{(1-Y)-YT\}. \] For the second, use \(a(1-X)f_2=1-Z\); after clearing factors it is \[ (Z-X)^2-X^2(1-Z) =Z\{(1-X)^2-(1-Z)\}. \] Both are polynomial identities by expansion. This proves (15). Equations (14)--(15) yield three actual matrix factorizations: \[  egin{split} B_{+,1}B_{+,2}&=B_{+,2'}B_{+,1'},\ B_{-,1}B_{-,2}&=B_{-,2'}B_{-,1'},\ B_{+,1}B_{-,2}&=Z\,B_{-,2'}B_{+,1'}. \end{split} 	ag{16} \] The first two are (15) and conservation of \(k_1k_2\). The third can be checked entrywise: its left side is \(\left( egin{smallmatrix}Z&e_1/k_2\-k_1f_2&k_1/k_2\end{smallmatrix}ight)\); substitution of (14) gives exactly that matrix on the right. The scalar \(Z\) is essential with these unnormalized triangular matrices. ## 4. Explicit dressing gives the actual Wirtinger rule On a horizontal slice with \(b\) ordered heads put \[ H_i=B_{-,i+1}\cdots B_{-,b},\qquad \widehat M_i=H_i^{-1}M_iH_i. 	ag{17} \] An empty suffix is the identity. These are genuine determinant-one, trace-minus-two matrices, not just Casimir values. First take two heads. The mixed and lower identities in (16) imply \[ M_{1'}=B_{-,2}^{-1}M_1B_{-,2}. 	ag{18} \] Indeed substitute \(B_{-,1'}=B_{-,2'}^{-1}B_{-,1}B_{-,2}\) and \(B_{+,1'}=Z^{-1}B_{-,2'}^{-1}B_{+,1}B_{-,2}\) in (13); \(k_1'=k_1/Z\) cancels the extra scalar. Also the product of the dressed meridians is \[ \widehat M_1\widehat M_2 =(k_1k_2)^{-1}(B_{-,1}B_{-,2})^{-1}(B_{+,1}B_{+,2}), 	ag{19} \] which is preserved by (16). The checked output order is \((2',1')\). Thus (18) leaves the overstrand meridian unchanged, and (19) gives the complete positive rule \[ (A,B)\longmapsto(ABA^{-1},A). 	ag{20} \] The negative rule is its inverse, \((A,B)\mapsto(B,B^{-1}AB)\). For adjacent heads in a longer word, conjugate this calculation by the common suffix to their right. Suffixes of earlier heads contain the unchanged product \(B_{-,1}B_{-,2}\), so all spectator meridians are unchanged. This proves (20) for arbitrary signed braid words in their actual chronological operator order. The dressing has an explicit rational inverse. Given a tuple \((A_1,\ldots,A_b)\) with determinant one and trace minus two, work backwards from \(i=b\). Once the later \(B_-\)'s are known, set \[ M_i=H_iA_iH_i^{-1},\quad k_i=(M_i)_{11}^{-1},\quad e_i=k_i(M_i)_{12},\quad f_i=(M_i)_{21},\quad X_i=-k_i,\quad a_i=e_i/(1+k_i). 	ag{21} \] Require \((M_i)_{11}
e0,-1\) at each step. Determinant one gives \((M_i)_{22}=k_i+e_if_i\); trace minus two gives (12). The condition \(k_i
e-1\) then makes \(e_i,f_i,a_i\) nonzero. Equation (21) recovers (13) and defines the next \(B_{-,i}\). It is a rational inverse on this specified open set, rather than an argument by dimension count. A word uses the intersection with the corresponding regular sets at every intermediate stage. No claim that a particular representation belongs to that intersection is needed here. Consequently the rational crossing map is conjugate on this open set to the ordinary parabolic Wirtinger action. This statement also proves its braid relations there. It is consistent with, and substantially covered by, the earlier marked braid theorem; (21) and the suffix convention specify the present external coordinates independently. ## 5. Ordinary bends and fixed short compositions The external repository supplies no cup/cap API. Use exactly the regular self-dual extension in the cited bend note. At the root its cup and ordinary cap are supported on \(i+j=d\), and their adjacent coefficients satisfy \[ c_{i+1}/c_i=q^{2i+3},\qquad b_{i+1}/b_i=q^{-2i-1}. 	ag{22} \] These follow from that note's equation (6), using \([i+1]_q=[d-i]_q\). Their leading action derivatives have exponentials \(X\) and \(X^{-1}\), respectively. With the canonical input/output signs of (8), both bend relations in the chart (9) are \[ Y=X^{-1},\qquad b=-a. 	ag{23} \] For example the cup has \(p_I/p_J=X\). Its support has \(v	o1-u\), so \(y=-x^{-1}\); inserting (9) gives \(b=-a\). The same result for the cap uses the negative input derivative. The minus sign retains the original complementary-index lift; replacing it by \(+1\) would change the bend. Substitution in (13) shows \[ B_{+,1}B_{+,2}=B_{-,1}B_{-,2}=I. \] Hence its two dressed meridians multiply to the identity. The bends create or remove inverse oriented meridians, exactly as required by the tangle group. Their finite scalar and phase normalizations remain those of the regular bend theorem; (22)--(23) do not reset them. It follows that arbitrary fixed signed powers, stacking, ordinary turns and finite tangle compositions have a rational classical relation compatible with the actual oriented meridian words wherever the corresponding charts are regular. This includes inserting any fixed short signed tangle into an existing boundary relation. It is not a uniform asymptotic estimate for that tangle's prescribed observation, nor a theorem about its geometric coefficient. ## 6. The prescribed closing and the representation it yields The external source on \(b\) heads fixes the first input and output index to zero and closes the others with \(K_{m ext}\), then applies the prescribed writhe correction. In the present variables its exact diagonal weight is \[ (K_{m ext})_{ii}=-q\,Q^i=-qX. 	ag{24} \] At the literal pinned endpoint \(X=1\), the regular chart of (7)--(13) is singular. The pin is therefore not simply declared a regular periodic boundary point. For the **complete assembled braid intertwiner**, the prescribed cut equals its normalized first-head average. This is proved directly in [the cut-functional theorem](research_rivin_jones_prescribed_cut_and_hermite_recovery.md), Section 2: the tail quantum trace commutes with the first-head generators, and hence is scalar. Thus the exact external invariant is also \[  rac{q^{w(N^2-1)/2}}{N} \sum_{i_1,\ldots,i_b=0}^d \left(\prod_{r=2}^b[-qQ^{i_r}]ight) W_{ oldsymbol i, oldsymbol i}. 	ag{25} \] This equality uses no division by a vanishing quantum dimension. It is not permitted for an arbitrary inserted exterior that fails the intertwining hypothesis; that case retains the literal pin and its actual boundary data. Every pivot in (24) has a nonzero, bounded magnitude and bounded logarithm on any fixed compact complex chart in \(X
e0\). Its logarithm is order one, not order \(N\). Its exact lattice shift ratio is \(Q\), tending to one. Hence it remains an amplitude and finite shift mark in (25), but does not alter the leading exponentiated internal stationary equations. The exact framing factor is \[ q^{w(N^2-1)/2}= \exp(N\pi i w/2)\exp(-\pi i w/(2N)). 	ag{26} \] It contributes the leading constant \(\pi iw/2\) to the action; it has not been discarded merely because its internal derivatives are zero. At a regular full stationary point of (25), the sum of the local actions (4) has matching internal positions and momenta. Exponentiated stationarity includes the usual integer logarithmic branches; they are not a choice of a favorable saddle. Equations (8)--(11) therefore give a fixed point of the checked braid map on all heads. Conversely a fixed point in the specified regular chart supplies those exponentiated equations by the local generating relations. Under (17), this fixed locus is exactly the open part of \[ \{(A_1,\ldots,A_b):\det A_i=1,\ \operatorname{tr}A_i=-2,  eta(A_i)=A_i\ 	ext{for every }i\}. 	ag{27} \] The presentation obtained by placing one meridian on each braid strand, using (20) at crossings, and identifying the closing endpoints is the Wirtinger presentation of the braid closure. Therefore (27) gives actual parabolic representations of its group. Conversely any such representation whose tuple and intermediate stages lie in the explicit inverse-dressing chart (21) gives a fixed point and hence a regular exponentiated critical point. This is a converse on a stated open chart, not a claim about every representation or every boundary stratum. For a knot, a noncentral parabolic meridian has a parabolic centralizer in \(\mathrm{PSL}_2\); its commuting longitude consequently fixes the same ideal point. Thus these representations are boundary-parabolic. The trace-minus-two lift records the present convention. No preferred longitude eigenvalue, regulator constant, or quantum normal is inferred from that elementary centralizer statement. ## 7. What has and has not been transported The exact [external-to-Newton adapter](research_rivin_jones_local_crossing_adapter.md) reverses crossing signs at \(A_N\). All signs in this note are external signs. The adapter and its scalar lines must be applied when comparing the corresponding physical mirror word; the statement (20) does not silently change that convention. The full finite adapter and [split-incidence recovery](research_rivin_jones_split_boundary_source_equivalence.md) retain all Newton Hermite data. A principal classical symbol by itself does not estimate those normal coefficients. The earlier [positive-chart obstruction](research_rivin_jones_positive_chart_sewing_obstruction.md) concerns simultaneous strict upper-half-plane choices for particular raw Fourier shapes. The present maps live on complex rational charts; they assert neither positivity of those shapes nor an equality of a raw full-function density with the finite polynomial away from its sampling grid. There is no conflict with its two-crossing reciprocal shape relation or its retained seam character. This explicit character map does not by itself identify \(2\pi\operatorname{Re}\mathcal S_{\mathrm{total}}\) with hyperbolic volume in the chosen orientation. Here the action is normalized by \(\log R/N\), so its real part governs exponential magnitude. The earlier marked braid and [fundamental-cycle results](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/crossing_fundamental_cycle.md) address regulator comparisons in their recorded coordinates. Equation (6c), together with the joint clock theorem's calibrated primitive, now supplies the local marked-action comparison among the external, physical and incidence coordinates, with the exact adapter and all boundary/framing conventions retained. Transporting a chosen global branch must retain those same lifts and the already specified orientation; equality of group relations alone would not suffice. More decisively, neither a representation nor a regular critical point proves that the prescribed quantum cycle has a nonzero coefficient there. Global cycle transport, endpoint contributions, cancellation and the lower bound needed for arbitrary fixed short partial filling remain separate requirements. ## 8. Pinned written sources The direct local formulas and scope comparisons above were checked at these SHA-256 versions. The two external files are at the commit stated at the beginning. No saved numerical audit is a premise of this note. | Source | SHA-256 | | --- | --- | | External `docs/MATHEMATICS.md` | `0b7b0c0df2452d9691c807d0c3f556fe38ef3f284ebd0c0c227ae90d2af6ce5d` | | External `python/rivin_jones/r_matrix.py` | `b6c5b48a9094587faa2ea6a9467ff801d838cfb007974a0fcd22a6e11aabfa76` | | `research_rivin_role_frames_and_bridge_angles.md` | `125155bcd008e24bf5714457d9c6d1788a152bc563380f859c80bfe8b997ccf8` | | `weighted_crossing_source_gap.md` | `a6a6411a780c904493db4fca3b5536f902aa5be8b6ef7cfb880a4f57509f436c` | | `research_rivin_jones_regular_bends_and_newton_turn.md` | `ced2c87e74c255d68f367d553fb5b36da9432a90d59687823fa6401778b72af0` | | `research_rivin_jones_prescribed_cut_and_hermite_recovery.md` | `1b0e105ffb67b2b8552f5fddc5f0a3ac009e9795b33e27599ac4726ebd74079e` | | `marked_braid_holonomy.md` | `eff47c757d0e44bda0c396c094315b8e1fce11f1fc2d6445d636c6d2d3a46c4f` | | `crossing_fundamental_cycle.md` | `0d7d7da0f5cf4fe0d16907e7e999d5ce7980f7ff39d437df167c99ca30205b0f` | | `research_rivin_jones_local_crossing_adapter.md` | `c4a9a92ec22f31a035036642e0621ef9abe569646b2488dbac2d2add786500f0` | | `research_rivin_jones_split_boundary_source_equivalence.md` | `f5b481568c2cef411ab67e88de6f818288383c8e0f8d8e3f69272551e7d81a22` | | `research_rivin_jones_positive_chart_sewing_obstruction.md` | `7809489b46a1eb50accca9910428ca929fd98622734060e39b42e1e2070c7910` | | `research_joint_clock_phase_equations.md` | `71393aa353909dfa2dd19b078b1d3fccdf8561520aa071b7537e4bbfc50bb867` |

title: An exact local adapter from the division-free braid to the Newton algebra
The division-free braid formula and the partial-filling problem
text: # The division-free braid formula and the partial-filling problem Written comparison, 14 November 2026. The inspected external source is [rivin-jones, commit e956fb919ac7d1bbc7cb3d3873fbac993feb94b7](https://github.com/igorrivin/rivin-jones/tree/e956fb919ac7d1bbc7cb3d3873fbac993feb94b7). The mathematical specification, sparse crossing implementation and tensor contraction description were read. No code from that repository was imported, executed, or used for a numerical calculation. The useful contribution is a particularly explicit presentation of the reduced colored braid scalar. It does not itself prove a volume limit. The deductions below concern its displayed finite formulas. Identifying them with every marked free-boundary object in our construction is a separate task. ## 1. The exact reduced observation The [mathematical specification](https://github.com/igorrivin/rivin-jones/blob/e956fb919ac7d1bbc7cb3d3873fbac993feb94b7/docs/MATHEMATICS.md) uses representation dimension \(N\), \(n=N-1\), \(v=A^2\), and Jones parameter \(q=A^{-4}\). Its crossing entries are Laurent polynomials in \(A\): the symmetric Gaussian binomials are obtained by a polynomial recurrence, with no division by quantum factorials. For a braid with knot closure, one strand is cut and its input and output are fixed to the highest-weight state. The other strands are traced with their quantum weights, and the writhe correction is applied. Thus the displayed scalar has a well-defined specialization at nonzero roots of unity. It is not obtained by dividing two values that both specialize to zero. This is relevant to our prescribed closing functional. Any comparison must preserve that marked scalar, its framing and its boundary specializations. Scalar equality for closed knots alone does not identify an unreduced polynomial at several free boundaries or its normal derivatives. ## 2. Exact positive magnitudes and the remaining phase For an integer \(N\ge2\), take \[ A_N=e^{-\pi i/(2N)},\qquad S_m=\prod_{r=1}^{m}2\sin(\pi r/N),\qquad S_0=1. \] All \(S_m\) with \(0\le m<N\) are strictly positive. At this root the symmetric Gaussian binomial is \[ B(a,b)=\frac{S_a}{S_b S_{a-b}}\quad(0\le b\le a<N). \] Indeed the symmetric quantum integer becomes \(\sin(\pi m/N)/\sin(\pi/N)\); its factorial quotient gives the displayed expression. Equivalently this expression satisfies the finite Gaussian recurrence used in the implementation. For a positive crossing, the allowed transition is \[ (i,j)\longmapsto(j+k,i-k),\qquad 0\le k\le\min(i,n-j). \] Its coefficient is exactly \[ R_+(i,j,k)=A_N^{Q_+(i,j,k)} \frac{S_i S_{j+k}}{S_{i-k}S_j S_k}, \] where \[ Q_+=(n-2i+2k)(n-2j-2k)+k(k-1)+Nk. \] For a negative crossing the transition is \[ (i,j)\longmapsto(j-k,i+k),\qquad 0\le k\le\min(j,n-i), \] and its coefficient is \[ R_-(i,j,k)=A_N^{Q_-(i,j,k)} \frac{S_j S_{i+k}}{S_{j-k}S_i S_k}, \] where \[ Q_-=-(n-2i)(n-2j)-k(k-1)-Nk. \] To check the extra phase in the positive formula, each factor in the implementation's product is \[ A_N^{2(n-i+r)}-A_N^{-2(n-i+r)} =-2i\sin\frac{\pi(i+1-r)}N . \] The product is therefore \((-i)^kS_i/S_{i-k}\), and \((-i)^k=A_N^{Nk}\). In the negative formula the corresponding product combines with its printed \((-1)^k\) to give \(i^k S_j/S_{j-k}=A_N^{-Nk}S_j/S_{j-k}\). This proves both identities directly from the displayed coefficients. In particular every allowed local transition has nonzero coefficient at the matched root. There is no further local zero rule that removes the allowed transitions. Every crossing conserves \(i+j\). After the braid connections and highest-weight cut are imposed, the entire scalar is consequently a sum over integer points satisfying linear equalities and inequalities: \[ I_N=\sum_{\mathbf m\in\mathcal P_N\cap\mathbb Z^d} a_N(\mathbf m) \exp\!\left(-\frac{\pi i}{2N}Q_N(\mathbf m)\right), \qquad a_N(\mathbf m)>0. \] Here \(a_N\) is the product of the positive ratios above. The integer quadratic polynomial \(Q_N\) also contains the quantum trace and writhe phases. The braid is fixed; the bounds defining \(\mathcal P_N\) depend on \(N\). This is an explicit oscillatory sum. An estimate of its positive absolute sum is not a lower bound for \(I_N\). For example, in the charge-two block of \(R_+\), \(N\ge3\), the diagonal entries at \((i,j,k)=(1,1,0)\) and \((2,0,2)\) are both nonzero. Their phase exponents differ by \(2n\), so their phase ratio is \[ A_N^{2n}=-e^{\pi i/N}. \] It is not positive real. Diagonal similarity leaves diagonal entries unchanged, and multiplication by one common scalar leaves their ratio unchanged. Hence even this block cannot be made entrywise nonnegative by a diagonal phase change and a common scalar. This does not exclude a different, non-diagonal or boundary-dependent construction. ## 3. What can be transferred to the general research programme The [planned contraction implementation](https://github.com/igorrivin/rivin-jones/blob/e956fb919ac7d1bbc7cb3d3873fbac993feb94b7/docs/PLANNED_CONTRACTION.md) keeps the same weights while changing contraction order. Slicing fixes selected internal indices and sums every resulting slice. Backward support propagation excludes paths that cannot reach the prescribed output. Those are exact operations. They supply no estimate on cancellation among paths that remain. Our [arbitrary-power compiler](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_arbitrary_power_source_compilation.md) already contracts finite compositions of multiplication, turns and arbitrary fixed signed crossing powers, and retains their free ordinary boundary polynomials and normal data. Our [full scalar-flow construction](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_full_psi_scalar_flow_cycle.md), Section 3, already retains a bounded polytope from weight conservation. Conservation and exact regrouping are therefore not new missing theorems in the project. The useful comparison is more specific. Retain the boundary indices of an arbitrary short component in the division-free braid presentation, and prove the exact change from those coordinates to our Newton boundary polynomial, including the prescribed final observation and all repeated-root normals. Then retain the complete quadratic phase when deriving estimates. This could provide a simpler representation for a general composition proof and an independent check of the source. It has not yet supplied the required geometric coefficient. Two distinctions must be maintained in such an argument. Laurent regularity in \(A\) at fixed integer indices is not holomorphy in continued summation indices; rewriting the amplitudes as continued factorial ratios may introduce divisors again. Also the current external API computes closed knot scalars, whereas the partial-filling theorem needs boundary data before the final closure. The repository's finite-level enclosure routines and speed improvements are useful computational infrastructure. They do not bound the error to the large-\(N\) limit. They have not been used as proof inputs here.

title: Two local positive crossing charts cannot be sewn across a two-crossing twist
text:
# Two local positive crossing charts cannot be sewn across a two-crossing twist Private written deduction, 14 November 2026. No frozen manuscript, external code, numerical calculation, or test is used here. The exact Rivin-to-Newton adapter identifies an arbitrary signed block with its original physical block. It does not supply a new positive complex contour. In fact the existing exact physical Fourier kernel already gives nonzero local densities and a positive octahedral chart. Two source-specific calculations below show why applying that chart independently at every original crossing cannot prove general short filling. The obstruction occurs in the actual two-crossing block \(R_+^2\), before any arbitrary replacement exterior is chosen. ## 1. The actual local positive chart Use the exact four-function Fourier kernel from [the balanced crossing theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_balanced_fourier_crossing_kernel.md), including its original Cartan scalar, Gaussian, and logarithmic marks. For its input ports \(z_0,z_1\) and output ports \(z_6,z_7\), the classical shapes in its signed regulator are \[ u=-z_1/z_0,\qquad v=-z_6/z_7,\qquad w=z_7/z_1, \qquad D(u)+D(v)+D(w)-D(uvw). 	ag{1} \] The positive chart uses the four positively oriented shapes \(u,v,w,(uvw)^{-1}\). On its unit-angle locus their angles lie in \((0,\pi)\) and sum to \(2\pi\). Its kernel has the nonzero source-normalized density proved in the cited note. Now compose two positive crossings on the same adjacent heads, using the coherently propagated Fourier frames. Those frames make the interior adapters exactly the identity, as proved in [the propagated-frame theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/propagated_balanced_frames_and_boundary_source.md). The first crossing's output ports are literally the second crossing's input ports: \[ z'_0=z_6,\qquad z'_1=z_7. \] Consequently their shapes obey the exact algebraic relation \[ u'= rac1v. 	ag{2} \] **Lemma 1.** The product of these two local positive octahedral charts has empty intersection with the actual interior sewing equations. *Proof.* For every nonreal \(v\), \[ \operatorname{Im}(1/v) =- rac{\operatorname{Im}v}{|v|^2}. \] Thus \(\operatorname{Im}v>0\) and \(\operatorname{Im}u'>0\) cannot both hold under (2). \(\square\) This concerns the original signed shapes in (1). Cyclic positive quad rotations do not repair it: the maps \(z\), \(1/(1-z)\), and \(1-1/z\) each preserve the sign of the imaginary part. Declaring the reciprocal tetrahedron positive would change its orientation and its signed action unless an additional source identity is supplied. At finite level the full functions have their recorded \(q\)-shifts. These do not permit both crossings to lie in fixed compact subsets of their strict positive classical charts as \(N	o\infty\). The limiting relation remains (2). Any apparent repair confined to angles of order \(1/N\) approaches a degenerate boundary rather than a strict positive geometric chart. The lemma is independent of the external boundary parameters. In particular, requiring those parameters to arise from a positive hyperbolic geometric representation does not make these two original local charts compatible. It does not exclude a positive triangulation of the component after fusing or changing its internal decomposition. Such a change needs its own exact source comparison. ## 2. The same two-crossing block has a nontrivial sewn deck character There is a separate exact obstruction to treating the finite Fourier polynomial as the raw four-function continuation on a whole complex torus. Put \(s=(-1)^{N+1}\). Use logarithmic ports \((a,b;c,d)\) for the first crossing and \((c,d;e,f)\) for the second. Their central coordinates are \[ A=e^{Na},\ B=e^{Nb},\ C=e^{Nc},\ D=e^{Nd},\ E=e^{Ne},\ F=e^{Nf}. \] Write \(M_N(a,b,c,d)\) for the specific raw full-function continuation fixed in [the deck-character calculation](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/balanced_crossing_deck_characters.md), and set \[ \mathscr M_N=M_N(a,b,c,d)M_N(c,d,e,f). 	ag{3} \] No contour transformation is implicit in (3). The exact local full-turn characters needed here are \[ \mu_a= rac{sC(A-sB)}{B(A-C)},\quad \mu_b= rac{s(D-B)}{A-sB},\quad \mu_c= rac{s(A-C)}{D-sC},\quad \mu_d= rac{sB(D-sC)}{C(D-B)}. 	ag{4} \] The sewn characters in the two internal variables are their actual products. Cancellation of the displayed factors gives \[ 
u_c=- rac{sE(A-C)}{D(C-E)},\qquad 
u_d=- rac{sB(F-D)}{C(D-B)}. 	ag{5} \] These identities hold wherever the written ratios are regular and extend meromorphically across removable factors. The propagated two-crossing central frames have \[ C=sB,\quad D=sA,\quad E=A,\quad F=B. 	ag{6} \] Keep the external central values \(E=A,F=B\), but allow the internal ports to move. Then (5) simplifies to \[ 
u_c= rac{sA}{D},\qquad 
u_d= rac{sB}{C}. 	ag{7} \] Thus identity interior frame adapters do not make this raw continued product periodic away from the original balanced sampling multisection. ## 3. A microscopic movement already forces a same-order correction Choose regular nonzero \(A,B\) with \(B
e sA\), and fix a nonzero constant \(\lambda
e1\) sufficiently close to one to avoid the other displayed divisors. Starting at (6), move only \[ c\longmapsto c+ rac{\log\lambda}{N}. 	ag{8} \] This changes \(C\) to \(\lambda sB\), while \(D=sA\) remains. It is precisely the microscopic scale of a change between bounded Fourier-radius frames. Equations (7) now give \[ 
u_c=1,\qquad 
u_d=\lambda^{-1}. 	ag{9} \] The defect is independent of \(N\), including its parity. Let \(\mathscr P_N\) be the product of the actual two finite Fourier Laurent-polynomial crossing interpolants, with the same shared ports. It is fixed by the original finite matrices. In particular it is \(2\pi i\)-periodic in \(d\). It agrees with (3) on the original sampling grids, but no off-grid equality is assumed. Let \(p\) be the point after (8), and let \(p^+\) be the same point with \(d\) replaced by \(d+2\pi i\). **Lemma 2.** Wherever the raw product is regular, \[ \max igl\{ |\mathscr P_N(p)-\mathscr M_N(p)|, |\mathscr P_N(p^+)-\mathscr M_N(p^+)|  igr\} \ \ge\  rac{|1-\lambda^{-1}|}{2}|\mathscr M_N(p)|. 	ag{10} \] *Proof.* Periodicity gives \(\mathscr P_N(p^+)=\mathscr P_N(p)\), whereas the exact character (9) gives \(\mathscr M_N(p^+)=\lambda^{-1}\mathscr M_N(p)\). Subtract the two errors and apply the triangle inequality. \(\square\) In particular there is no relative \(o(1)\) identification of the actual finite polynomial with the raw full-function continuation on a domain containing both lips, even after a displacement of order \(1/N\). If the raw product has a given exponential rate along the chosen points, at least one correction in (10) has that rate or larger. This is a statement about density values. It does not give a lower bound for an integrated seam period, whose terms may themselves cancel. The exact one-port and paired-port interpolation theorems in [the physical port-polynomial note](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_fourier_port_polynomials_and_profiles.md) remain valid. Their fixed opposite grids and retained central factors are exactly what distinguish them from the simultaneous raw continuation ruled out by (10). ## 4. Consequence for the short-filling route These are two concrete gaps in a proposed universal argument from nonzero local Fourier kernels to a nonzero geometric coefficient. The original two-crossing twist cannot be placed in the product of the known strict positive local charts. Its raw continued Fourier product also needs a correction of nonnegligible relative size when microscopic frame movements are made across a full logarithmic cycle. Thus a general proof must do more than complete each crossing into its known nonzero full-function block, reflect the negative crossings, and apply positive-volume concavity. It must transform or fuse the actual block before imposing the positive chart, and preserve the finite boundary and seam source in that transformation. Neither lemma rules out such a transformation, or the original volume conjecture. They identify precisely why the new local matrix adapter alone does not provide it.

title: The external highest-weight cut and full Hermite boundary recovery
text: # The external highest-weight cut and full Hermite boundary recovery Private written comparison, 14 November 2026. The external `rivin-jones` formula fixes one highest-weight input and output and traces the remaining heads with its specified \(K\). This note transports that actual functional, rather than replacing it by an unmarked trace. It then recovers every coefficient of a canonical Newton boundary polynomial by explicit inserted versions of the same functional. The recovery includes the first derivatives at all double Casimir roots, at every level \(N\ge2\). The boundary polynomial recovered here has degree below \(N\) in each independent pair coordinate. Products of several free incidences at one vertex must be retained as ordinary polynomials after those incidences have been recovered separately. A single pair operator does not retain a multiple of \(P_N\). ## 1. Parameters, basis map, and the literal cut Use the external finite contraction at [rivin-jones commit e956fb919ac7d1bbc7cb3d3873fbac993feb94b7](https://github.com/igorrivin/rivin-jones/tree/e956fb919ac7d1bbc7cb3d3873fbac993feb94b7), specified in `docs/MATHEMATICS.md` and `python/rivin_jones/r_matrix.py`. The written source snapshot was read at `/private/tmp/rivin-jones-review-20261113`; no external code was executed. Put \[ d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad A_N=q^{-1/2},\quad t=A_N^2=q^{-1},\quad \eta=(-1)^d. \tag{1} \] The square root in (1) is the displayed exponential \(A_N=e^{-\pi i/(2N)}\). It is not an arbitrary square-root choice. In the external basis \(u_0,\ldots,u_d\), \[ K_{\rm ext}u_i=t^{d-2i}u_i. \] Let \(|0\rangle,\ldots,|d\rangle\) be the original balanced physical basis of the [finite Newton calculus](../papers/newton-calculus/finite.tex). The [exact local crossing adapter](research_rivin_jones_local_crossing_adapter.md) is \[ T u_i=q^{-i(i-1)/2}|d-i\rangle. \tag{2} \] Its local coefficient comparison gives \[ T K_{\rm ext}T^{-1}=K,\qquad (T\otimes T)R_{{\rm ext},\pm}(T\otimes T)^{-1}=R_{\mp}. \tag{3} \] Thus the physical braid word has every crossing sign reversed. There is no change of word order in (3). The first equality is also immediate from \(d-2(d-i)=-(d-2i)\). The monomial factors in (2) have modulus one and are retained in all uncontracted wires. For any operator \(X\) on \(b\) external heads, with no invariance assumption, define its prescribed external cut by \[ L_{{\rm ext},b}(X)= \operatorname{Tr}\left[ (P_0\otimes K_{\rm ext}^{\otimes(b-1)})X\right], \qquad P_0=u_0u_0^*. \tag{4} \] Here \(u_0^*\) is the coordinate dual row; no Hermitian pairing is being substituted for the original contraction. Formula (4) is exactly the sum over diagonal tail colors in the external source. If \[ Y=T^{\otimes b}X(T^{-1})^{\otimes b}, \] then cyclicity of the full matrix trace proves the unrestricted functional identity \[ L_{{\rm ext},b}(X)= \operatorname{Tr}\left[ (P_d\otimes K^{\otimes(b-1)})Y\right], \qquad P_d=|d\rangle\langle d|. \tag{5} \] Indeed \(TP_0T^{-1}=P_d\): the two nonzero scalar factors cancel. This proves the dual observation as well as the operator adapter. ## 2. When the lowest-head observation equals the original cut average Suppose \(Y\) commutes with the total physical \(E,F,K\). Treat the last \(b-1\) heads as one tail module, with generators \(E_B,F_B,K_B\), and put \[ C=\operatorname{Tr}_B(K_B Y). \tag{6} \] The coproducts are the original ones: \[ E_{1B}=E_1K_B+E_B,\qquad F_{1B}=F_1+K_1^{-1}F_B,\qquad K_{1B}=K_1K_B. \] Taking the unweighted partial trace of \([Y,E_1K_B+E_B]=0\) gives \([C,E_1]=0\), since the partial trace of \([Y,E_B]\) vanishes and a tail-only factor can be moved cyclically inside that partial trace. For the lowering equation, take the \(K_B\)-weighted partial trace. Conservation of \(K_1K_B\) gives \[ YK_1^{-1}=K_1^{-1}K_B^{-1}YK_B. \] It follows that \[ \operatorname{Tr}_B K_B[Y,K_1^{-1}F_B] =K_1^{-1}\operatorname{Tr}_B (YK_BF_B-K_BF_BY)=0. \] The other term gives \([C,F_1]=0\). Likewise \(C\) commutes with \(K_1\). The \(N\) eigenvalues of \(K_1\) are distinct, and all adjacent lowering coefficients are nonzero. Therefore \(C=cI\): first it is diagonal, and then commuting with the lowering arrows makes its diagonal entries equal. Let the original physical all-head cut average be \[ \Phi_b(Y)=\frac1N\operatorname{Tr} [(I\otimes g^{\otimes(b-1)})Y], \qquad g=\eta K. \tag{7} \] Equations (5)--(7) now give \[ L_{{\rm ext},b}(X)=\eta^{b-1}\Phi_b(Y). \tag{8} \] For \(b=1\), an invariant operator is already scalar and the same identity holds. No nonzero quantum dimension is divided out. Equation (5), rather than (8), remains the formula for arbitrary inserted exteriors that fail the intertwining condition. In particular, a highest or lowest coordinate projector must not be replaced by the normalized identity on such an exterior. This is the same distinction retained by the exact source formulas in [the complete multiplicity module](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_complete_source_multiplicity_module.md), Section 4: its scalar identity is proved on actual intertwiners, while its unrestricted marked contraction remains a matrix. ## 3. Exact framing of a closed knot braid Let \(w\) denote the writhe of an external \(b\)-strand word, and let \(Y\) be its physical sign-reversed word under (3). The external normalization multiplies (4) by \[ A_N^{-w d(d+2)}=q^{w d(d+2)/2}. \tag{9} \] The original physical enhancement with pivot \(g\) is \(\theta=\eta q^{d(d+2)/2}\). This follows directly from the first column of the actual Newton crossing matrix in [the source compiler](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_arbitrary_power_source_compilation.md), Section 1: the coefficient of \(e_k\) in \(R\) is \(\kappa(-1)^kq^k\), with \(\kappa=q^{d^2/2}\). Since \(\phi_N(e_k)=\delta_{k,d}\), \[ \phi_N(R)=\kappa\eta q^d =\eta q^{d(d+2)/2}. \] The inverse crossing has conjugate coefficients in the real Newton basis and gives the reciprocal enhancement. Replacing the physical pivot \(g=\eta K\) by \(K\) removes its factor \(\eta\), giving \(\alpha=q^{d(d+2)/2}\). Thus the pivot sign is checked in the same original polynomial source used below. If the braid closure is a knot, its permutation is a \(b\)-cycle. Each positive or negative braid generator is an odd permutation, so \(w\equiv b-1\pmod2\). The physical mirror word has writhe \(-w\). Its original zero-framing correction is therefore \[ \theta^{w}=\eta^{b-1}q^{w d(d+2)/2}. \tag{10} \] Combining (8)--(10) proves equality of the normalized external knot scalar with the normalized original physical scalar of that marked mirror word. This keeps the exact phase, not just its modulus. It makes no claim about a multi-component normalization not specified by the external source. ## 4. The full canonical pair boundary from prescribed inserted cuts Let \(\Omega\) be the original physical pair Casimir and define the explicit external operator \[ \Omega_{\rm ext}=(T\otimes T)^{-1}\Omega(T\otimes T). \tag{11} \] The full pair-commutant theorem of the finite Newton calculus gives \[ \mathcal A_N=\mathbb C[z]/(P_N),\qquad P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2,\qquad f\longmapsto f(\Omega_{\rm ext}) \tag{12} \] as an injective realization of the complete transported pair algebra. It includes the double-root nilpotents. For every canonical pair state \(X=f(\Omega_{\rm ext})\), write its unique polynomial as \[ f(z)=\sum_{i=0}^{d}a_i e_i(z),\qquad \deg f<N. \] The external cut \(L_{{\rm ext},2}\) will be denoted by \(L\). For every polynomial \(h\), equations (8) and Newton duality give \[ L\bigl(h(\Omega_{\rm ext})X\bigr)=\eta\phi_N(hf), \qquad \phi_N(e_i e_j)=\delta_{i+j,d}. \tag{13} \] Consequently the actual coefficient formula is \[ a_i=\eta L\bigl(e_{d-i}(\Omega_{\rm ext})X\bigr), \qquad 0\le i<N. \tag{14} \] This proves canonical boundary recovery from a specified module and its specified dual observations. It does not infer that boundary from the single scalar \(L(X)\). Every observation in (14) uses the same highest-head projector and external tail pivot as (4), with the displayed Casimir coupon inserted before that closing. For \(r\) independent pair-algebra factors the tensor formula is equally exact. If \[ X=\sum_{\mathbf i}a_{\mathbf i} \bigotimes_{j=1}^{r}e_{i_j}(\Omega_{{\rm ext},j}), \] then \[ a_{\mathbf i}=\eta^r L^{\otimes r} \left[\left(\bigotimes_{j=1}^{r} e_{d-i_j}(\Omega_{{\rm ext},j})\right)X\right]. \tag{15} \] The input space of (15) is the tensor product of the independent pair algebras. A general multihead braid intertwiner is not being declared a member of that smaller space merely from its total Hopf invariance. ## 5. Explicit reconstruction of every double-root normal For a double root \(c\) of \(P_N\), put \[ Q_c(z)=\frac{P_N(z)}{(z-c)^2},\qquad a_c=4-c^2\ne0. \] The original Chebyshev identities give \(Q_c(c)=N^2/a_c\) and \(Q_c'(c)/Q_c(c)=c/a_c\). Define canonical polynomials \[ E_c(z)=\frac{Q_c(z)}{N^2}\{a_c-c(z-c)\},\qquad V_c(z)=\frac{a_c}{N^2}(z-c)Q_c(z). \tag{16} \] At \(c\), their value/derivative pairs are respectively \((1,0)\) and \((0,1)\); at every other double root both pairs vanish. They also vanish at the possible simple root. Thus, in the full algebra, \[ E_c^2=E_c,\qquad E_cV_c=V_c,\qquad V_c^2=0. \tag{17} \] Distinct components annihilate one another. These identities follow from the stated jets and divisibility by \(P_N\) with its actual multiplicities. The original Hermite closing formula, combined with (13), is \[ L(f(\Omega_{\rm ext})) =\sum_{c\ { m double}} \{a_c f'(c)-c f(c)\} +\mathbf1_{N\ { m odd}}f(-2). \tag{18} \] There is no parity sign on the double terms: the factor \(\eta\) in (13) cancels the factor \(\eta\) in the physical Hermite trace. The odd-level simple term also has \(\eta=1\). Applying (18) to the two coupons (16) gives the explicit full-jet recovery formulas \[ \begin{split} f(c)&=\frac{L(V_c(\Omega_{\rm ext})X)}{a_c},\\ f'(c)&=\frac{L(E_c(\Omega_{\rm ext})X)+c f(c)}{a_c}. \end{split} \tag{19} \] At odd \(N\), let \[ E_{-2}(z)=\frac{P_N(z)}{N^2(z+2)}. \] Because \(P_N'(-2)=N^2\), this is the idempotent of the simple root, and \[ f(-2)=L(E_{-2}(\Omega_{\rm ext})X). \tag{20} \] Finally the recovered canonical polynomial is exactly \[ f(z)=\sum_{c\ { m double}} \{f(c)E_c(z)+f'(c)V_c(z)\} +\mathbf1_{N\ { m odd}}f(-2)E_{-2}(z). \tag{21} \] Both sides have degree below \(N\) and identical complete Hermite data, which proves (21). For example the nonzero element \(V_c\) has zero value at every spectral root, yet \(L(E_c(\Omega_{\rm ext})V_c(\Omega_{\rm ext}))=a_c\ne0\). This shows directly where an evaluation-only reconstruction would lose a genuine part of the external source. ## 6. Scope of the recovered boundary Equations (14), (19), and (20) recover all canonical pair data, including every first normal, from explicit finite contractions. They use Casimir coupons, not only crossing powers. At composite levels crossing eigenvalues can coincide at different Casimir nodes; recovery from crossing powers alone is not asserted. If a free vertex has several incident canonical boundary factors, its retained ordinary polynomial is their product before reduction. Its degree can exceed \(N-1\). Passing first to one pair matrix identifies this polynomial with its remainder modulo \(P_N\), and none of the observations above can undo that loss.
