The incidence factors, or their full independent coefficient tensor (15), must be retained before their free coordinates are identified. This is an exact requirement on the boundary representation, not an asymptotic estimate. The external scalar routine alone does not return the inserted observations (14). The equations specify the additional boundary contractions required for an exact mathematical correspondence; no claim of an implemented boundary API is made here. No volume asymptotic or geometric saddle selection is inferred from the finite correspondence. Only written mathematics is used. No numerical evaluation, test, import, compilation, public-document edit, or frozen-proof edit was performed.

title: Regular bends for the external braid representation and the Newton turn
text: # Regular bends for the external braid representation and the Newton turn Private research proof, 14 November 2026. Frozen manuscripts are unchanged. The external repository at commit `e956fb919ac7d1bbc7cb3d3873fbac993feb94b7` implements braid matrices and a prescribed reduced trace. It does not implement a cup, cap, or quarter-turn API. This note specifies a self-dual boundary extension of that braid representation and checks its bends explicitly. At the principal root its turn becomes the recorded full Newton reversal, with the original cup and cap scalars. No equality of unmarked closed scalars is used to identify open operators. ## 1. A regular external cup and cap Fix \(N\ge2\), put \(d=N-1\), and use \[ \zeta=A^{-2},\qquad v=A^2=\zeta^{-1},\qquad q=e^{\pi i/N},\qquad \rho_\zeta=\zeta-\zeta^{-1}. \tag{1} \] All parameter families below are taken near \(\zeta=q\). We use \([a]_\zeta=(\zeta^a-\zeta^{-a})/(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})\) and \([a]_\zeta!=\prod_{r=1}^a[r]_\zeta\), with \([0]_\zeta!=1\); the same convention applies to \(v\). The external divided-power basis \(e_0,\ldots,e_d\) has \[ K_v e_i=v^{d-2i}e_i,\qquad E_v e_i=[N-i]_v e_{i-1},\qquad F_v e_i=[i+1]_v e_{i+1}, \tag{2} \] with missing endpoint vectors zero. The coproduct is \[ \Delta E_v=E_v\otimes K_v+1\otimes E_v, \qquad \Delta F_v=F_v\otimes1+K_v^{-1}\otimes F_v. \tag{3} \] The external positive-crossing formula is the checked universal crossing in this basis: \(E_v^k\) supplies the product of \([N-i]_v,\ldots,[N-i+k-1]_v\), and \(F_v^k/[k]_v!\) supplies \({j+k\brack k}_v\). Thus (2) is a concrete realization of the coefficients used by the external code, not an independently chosen representation with the same dimension. Define \[ r_i(\zeta)=\frac{[i]_\zeta![d-i]_\zeta!}{[d]_\zeta!}, \qquad c_0(\zeta)=N\zeta^{d(d-1)/2}, \] and the two coefficient lists \[ \begin{split} c_i(\zeta)&=c_0(\zeta)(-1)^i v^{i(d-i-1)}r_i(\zeta),\\ b_i(\zeta)&=\frac{(-1)^d v^d}{c_0(\zeta)} (-1)^i v^{i(i-d-1)}r_i(\zeta)^{-1}. \end{split} \tag{4} \] The cup \(p_v\) and cap \(\ell_v\) are \[ p_v(1)=\sum_{i=0}^d c_i e_i\otimes e_{d-i}, \qquad \ell_v(e_i\otimes e_j)=b_i\mathbf1_{i+j=d}. \tag{5} \] Every factor \([a]_\zeta\), \(1\le a<N\), is nonzero at \(q\). Thus these are regular families, with no quantum-dimension denominator. **Lemma 1.** The maps (5) are invariant for (2)--(3), and both snake contractions equal the identity. **Proof.** The weight of every supported pair is zero. The raising equation for the cup and the lowering equation for the cap are, respectively, \[ \frac{c_{i+1}}{c_i} =-v^{d-2i-2}\frac{[i+1]_v}{[d-i]_v}, \qquad \frac{b_{i+1}}{b_i} =-v^{-d+2i}\frac{[d-i]_v}{[i+1]_v}. \tag{6} \] They follow immediately from (4), since \([a]_v=[a]_\zeta\). Substitution in the other two equations gives \(\Delta F_v p_v=0\) and \(\ell_v\Delta E_v=0\) as well. More explicitly, the coefficient at \(e_a\otimes e_{d+1-a}\) in the first is \([a]_v c_{a-1}+v^{-d+2a}[d+1-a]_v c_a=0\); the corresponding cap equation is \(v^{-d-2+2a}[d+1-a]_v b_{a-1}+[a]_v b_a=0\). For the snakes, \(r_i=r_{d-i}\) and direct multiplication give \[ c_i b_{d-i}=b_i c_{d-i}=1. \tag{7} \] Each contraction has exactly one surviving summand at a given input index, with coefficient (7). This proves both identities. \(\square\) The invariant cup line is one-dimensional: the nonzero adjacent coefficients in (6) determine it from \(c_0\). The cap is then fixed by the snakes. The choice of \(c_0\) in (4) specifies the normalization needed below. Replacing the cup and cap by reciprocal nonzero scalar multiples does not change their quarter-turn contraction. There is a convention worth keeping explicit. The all-primal loop is \[ \ell_v p_v=(-1)^d[N]_v. \tag{8} \] Indeed \(c_i b_i=(-1)^d v^{d-2i}\). This is the signed self-dual convention, not a claim that the external code's prescribed \(K_v\)-trace has acquired the factor \((-1)^d\). That trace and its marked cut must be transported separately. ## 2. The actual change of basis and its root value In the generic balanced module use \[ K|a\rangle=\zeta^{d-2a}|a\rangle,\quad \mathcal E|a\rangle=(\zeta^{-N}-\zeta^{N-2a})|a-1\rangle, \quad \mathcal F|a\rangle=(1-\zeta^{2a+2})|a+1\rangle. \tag{9} \] These are the regular highest-weight family in the Newton manuscript. Its explicit basis change from the ordinary basis \(u_a\) is \[ |a\rangle=\frac{\rho_\zeta^a}{(\zeta^2;\zeta^2)_a}u_a. \tag{10} \] Every denominator in (10) is nonzero near the selected root. The local crossing adapter uses the regular anti-diagonal matrix \[ T_\zeta e_i=t_i(\zeta)|d-i\rangle, \qquad t_i(\zeta)=\zeta^{-i(i-1)/2}. \tag{11} \] It respects the generator structure, not only the crossing matrix: direct substitution gives \[ \begin{split} T_\zeta K_vT_\zeta^{-1}&=K,\\ T_\zeta E_vT_\zeta^{-1} &=-\zeta^{-2}\rho_\zeta^{-1}\mathcal F K,\\ T_\zeta F_vT_\zeta^{-1} &=-\zeta^2\rho_\zeta^{-1}K^{-1}\mathcal E. \end{split} \tag{12} \] For example, the first raising coefficient on the left is \([a+1]_\zeta\zeta^{d-a-1}\). On the right use \(1-\zeta^{2a+2}=-\rho_\zeta\zeta^{a+1}[a+1]_\zeta\). The lowering identity follows from \(\zeta^{-N}-\zeta^{N-2a} =-\rho_\zeta\zeta^{-a}[N-a]_\zeta\). Also \[ \Delta(\mathcal F K)=\mathcal F K\otimes K+1\otimes\mathcal F K, \quad \Delta(K^{-1}\mathcal E)=K^{-1}\mathcal E\otimes1 +K^{-1}\otimes K^{-1}\mathcal E. \tag{13} \] Thus (12) respects the displayed coproducts. In particular, the transported cup and cap are actual invariant bends of (9). Put \(x=q^d\). At the root, factorial reflection gives \(r_i(q)=1\), since \([N-a]_q=[a]_q\). For a supported external pair \((i,d-i)\), multiply (4) by \(t_i(q)t_{d-i}(q)\). The result is \[ t_i t_{d-i}c_i=N(-q)^i=Nx^{-i}, \qquad \frac{b_i}{t_i t_{d-i}}=\frac{x^{d-i}}N, \tag{14} \] using \(x=-q^{-1}\). Consequently \[ (T_q\otimes T_q)p_v=p, \qquad \ell_v(T_q\otimes T_q)^{-1}=\ell, \tag{15} \] where the literal recorded balanced maps are \[ p_{ab}=Nx^{-b}\mathbf1_{a+b=d},\qquad \ell_{ab}=\frac{x^a}{N}\mathbf1_{a+b=d}. \tag{16} \] Equation (14) checks the scalar on every supported entry. No scalar is left unspecified in (15). ## 3. Quarter-turns and the full Newton algebra Define the external quarter-turn by the actual contraction \[ \mathcal T_v(B)= (I^{\otimes2}\otimes\ell_v)(I\otimes B\otimes I) (p_v\otimes I^{\otimes2}). \tag{17} \] Write \(T_{2,\zeta}=T_\zeta\otimes T_\zeta\). With the regular transported bends from Section 2, the corresponding balanced turn satisfies \[ T_{2,\zeta}\mathcal T_v(B)T_{2,\zeta}^{-1} =\mathcal T_{\mathrm{bal},\zeta} (T_{2,\zeta}BT_{2,\zeta}^{-1}). \tag{18} \] This follows by substituting the two tensors from (5) and (11) into (17). Every internal index has one factor \(t_i\) and its inverse; they cancel. The two factors at the cup and cap are precisely those in their transported coefficients. The four remaining boundary factors are the two outer matrices in (18). This is an entrywise finite tensor identity, without a semisimple decomposition. At \(\zeta=q\), (15) identifies the balanced turn in (18) with the exact turn in the Newton manuscript. Let \[ P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2,\quad e_r(z)=\frac{\prod_{j<r}(q^{2j+1}+q^{-2j-1}-z)} {\prod_{j=1}^r4\sin^2(\pi j/N)}, \qquad 0\le r<N, \] and \(\Omega_{\mathrm{ext}}=T_{2,q}^{-1}\Omega T_{2,q}\). The full commutant and Newton-turn propositions therefore give \[ \boxed{\quad \mathcal T_v\bigl(e_r(\Omega_{\mathrm{ext}})\bigr) =e_{d-r}(\Omega_{\mathrm{ext}}). \quad} \tag{19} \] The underlying matrix algebra is faithful to \(\mathbb C[z]/P_N(z)\). Its double-root blocks retain both \(f(c)\) and \(f'(c)\); hence (19) includes every Casimir first normal. It is stronger than equality at the distinct eigenvalues. Equations (4)--(13) and (17)--(18) are regular parameter identities, so they can be differentiated in \(\zeta\) to any fixed order while retaining the derivatives of \(T_\zeta,p_v,\ell_v\). Formula (19) is the root specialization. It does not license replacing the generic turn by constant reversal when taking parameter derivatives. For completeness, the original marked cap can also be retained entrywise at the root. If \(m_{ab}=x^b/N^2\), its transported row is \[ m^{\mathrm{ext}}_{ij} =\frac{t_i(q)t_j(q)x^{d-j}}{N^2}, \tag{20} \] without a condition \(i+j=d\). On the cup (5), its \(N\) surviving summands are each \(1/N\), so \(m^{\mathrm{ext}}p_v=1\). The marked row is not substituted for the ordinary cap in (17). Nor is a generic extension of this marked row being inferred from its root value; the external code's prescribed open trace has its separately specified generic family. ## 4. Sources and limits of the conclusion The external entry formula is in `python/rivin_jones/r_matrix.py` at the commit stated above, SHA256 `b6c5b48a9094587faa2ea6a9467ff801d838cfb007974a0fcd22a6e11aabfa76`. Its actual crossing comparison under (11), including the reversed crossing sign, is proved separately in `research_rivin_jones_local_crossing_adapter.md`. The physical pair algebra, generic balanced family, literal maps (16), and full Newton-turn proposition used in (19) are in Sections 1--2 of `papers/newton-calculus/finite.tex`, SHA256 `2db2d7e15df0210c32bace4c761bdabadbb5d67140473a61425dac4d1e382f8e`. The proof there uses physical block support and the unique outermost tridiagonal path, so the repeated-root coefficients are not inferred from a limit of eigenvalue-only identities. This result supplies a regular local boundary adapter for bends. It does not assert that the external repository already offers such a boundary API, that its prescribed cut trace can be replaced on an arbitrary exterior by a scalar average, or that a resulting quantum period has a nonzero geometric asymptotic coefficient.

title: Recovering a short component from its open matrix contraction
text: # Recovering a short component from its open matrix contraction Private research proof, 14 November 2026. The manuscripts remain frozen. The purpose of this note is to compare two exact descriptions of the same short component: the original Newton boundary polynomial and a contraction in the basis used by Rivin's braid matrices. A short component may contain any fixed signed crossing powers and any finite number of the original Conway operations. No lower bound on those powers is assumed. The comparison retains the open boundary, not just a closed invariant. At a free vertex several polynomial factors can meet. Their ordinary product can have degree at least \(N\), whereas a single pair Casimir remembers a polynomial only modulo \(P_N\). We therefore give each free incidence its own pair of matrix indices, recover those separate polynomials, and only then identify their variables. This order is essential. ## 1. The two pair descriptions Fix \(N\ge2\), and put \[ d=N-1,\qquad q=e^{\pi i/N},\qquad \eta=(-1)^d,\qquad A_N=e^{-\pi i/(2N)}. \tag{1} \] Let \(T_N\) denote the Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind. The original pair algebra and its normalized Newton basis are \[ \begin{split} \mathcal A_N&=\mathbb C[z]/(P_N(z)),& P_N(z)&=2T_N(z/2)+2,\\ e_i(z)&=\frac{\prod_{a=0}^{i-1}(c_a-z)}{S_i^2},& c_a&=q^{2a+1}+q^{-2a-1},& S_i&=\prod_{a=1}^i2\sin(\pi a/N), \end{split} \tag{2} \] where empty products are one. Every class has a unique representative of degree at most \(d\). The original trace \(\phi\), turn \(\mathsf T\), and positive crossing \(R\) satisfy \[ \phi(e_i e_j)=\delta_{i+j,d},\qquad \mathsf T e_i=e_{d-i},\qquad R\in\mathcal A_N^\times. \tag{3} \] In particular, all signed integer powers of \(R\) are defined. On the external \(N\)-dimensional space \(V_{\rm ext}\) use basis \(u_0,\ldots,u_d\), pivot \(K_{\rm ext}u_i=q^{-(d-2i)}u_i\), and positive braid matrix \(R_{\rm ext}\) at \(A=A_N\). These are the conventions of the external repository at commit e956fb919ac7d1bbc7cb3d3873fbac993feb94b7. The explicit comparison with the balanced physical basis is \[ T u_i=q^{-i(i-1)/2}|d-i\rangle,\qquad \Omega_{\rm ext}=(T\otimes T)^{-1}\Omega(T\otimes T). \tag{4} \] Here \(\Omega\) is the original physical pair Casimir. The local crossing and prescribed-cut lemmas prove that \[ \begin{split} \iota:\mathcal A_N&\longrightarrow \operatorname{End}(V_{\rm ext}\otimes V_{\rm ext}), &\iota(f)&=f(\Omega_{\rm ext}),\\ \iota(R)&=R_{\rm ext}^{-1},& L(\iota(f))&=\eta\phi(f), \end{split} \tag{5} \] and that \(\iota\) is injective. The functional in (5) is the literal prescribed external cut \[ L(X)=\operatorname{Tr}[(P_0\otimes K_{\rm ext})X], \qquad P_0=u_0u_0^*. \tag{6} \] The row \(u_0^*\) is the coordinate dual. In particular, (6) is a specified linear observation, not a positive norm. The sign reversal in (5) is part of the comparison. The pair algebra in (5) contains its nilpotents. A double root \(c\) of \(P_N\) gives the local factor \(\mathbb C[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)\), on which \[ f(\Omega_{\rm ext}) \ \longleftrightarrow\ f(c)+f'(c)\epsilon. \tag{7} \] Thus the representation is not being replaced by its distinct eigenvalues. ## 2. A partial source and its separate free incidences Let \(\Gamma=(V,E)\) be one of the original finite circle trees. Partition its vertices into the filled set \(S\) and the nonempty free set \(U\). At every \(v\in S\), fix an arbitrary integer \(n_v\). Write \[ K_T(z,w)=\sum_{i=0}^d e_i(z)e_i(w). \tag{8} \] The exact original partial source is the ordinary polynomial \[ B_N(\mathbf z_U)= \left(\bigotimes_{v\in S}\phi_v\right) \left[ \prod_{v\in S}R(z_v)^{n_v} \prod_{e=vw\in E}K_T(z_v,z_w) \right]. \tag{9} \] At filled vertices multiplication and \(\phi_v\) take place in \(\mathcal A_N\). At free vertices the products are ordinary polynomial products, with no reduction modulo \(P_N\). In particular \[ \deg_{z_u}B_N\le d\,\deg_\Gamma(u). \tag{10} \] Formula (9) is the original source-compilation identity. It includes all crossing scalars and all first derivatives in the trace. Let \[ H=\{(e,u): e\in E,\ u\in U,\ u\hbox{ is an endpoint of }e\} \tag{11} \] be the set of free incidences. An edge joining two free vertices contributes two members of \(H\). Give each \(h\in H\) an independent variable \(z_h\). For an endpoint \(v\) of an edge \(e\), set \[ a(e,v)= \begin{cases} v,&v\in S,\\ (e,v),&v\in U. \end{cases} \tag{12} \] Replace \(z_v\) in that edge factor by \(z_{a(e,v)}\), while keeping a single variable \(z_v\) at each filled vertex. The result after the filled traces is a polynomial \(C_N(\mathbf z_H)\), separately of degree at most \(d\) in every free-incidence variable. By direct substitution, \[ B_N(\mathbf z_U)= C_N\bigl(z_{(e,u)}=z_u\bigr). \tag{13} \] The substitution in (13) takes place in the ordinary polynomial ring. An isolated free vertex contributes only a constant and causes no difficulty. ## 3. The exact matrix contraction and its inverse Assign an independent copy of \(V_{\rm ext}^{\otimes2}\) to every member of \(S\sqcup H\). Let \(\Omega_a\) and \(R_{{\rm ext},a}\) denote the operators (4)--(5) on that copy. Define the edge operator \[ \mathcal K_{ab}=\sum_{i=0}^d e_i(\Omega_a)e_i(\Omega_b). \tag{14} \] It is a specified sum of Casimir insertions, namely the image of the original turn kernel. It is not being identified with a single external crossing. Form the open operator on the free pairs \[ X_{S,N}= \eta^{|S|} \left(\bigotimes_{v\in S}L_v\right) \left[ \prod_{v\in S}R_{{\rm ext},v}^{-n_v} \prod_{e=vw\in E}\mathcal K_{a(e,v),a(e,w)} \right]. \tag{15} \] Applying \(L_v\) here means contraction of just that pair's matrix indices, leaving all other indices open. All factors within a pair are polynomials in its Casimir, so the products in (15) are unambiguous. **Theorem 1 (boundary correspondence).** The operator (15) belongs to \(\bigotimes_{h\in H}\iota(\mathcal A_N)\), and \[ X_{S,N}=\iota^{\otimes H}(C_N). \tag{16} \] Every coefficient of \(C_N\) is recovered by the same prescribed cuts with explicit insertions. More precisely, write \[ C_N(\mathbf z_H)= \sum_{\mathbf j\in\{0,\ldots,d\}^{H}} c_{\mathbf j}\prod_{h\in H}e_{j_h}(z_h). \tag{17} \] Then \[ c_{\mathbf j}= \eta^{|H|}L^{\otimes H} \left[ \left(\prod_{h\in H}e_{d-j_h}(\Omega_h)\right)X_{S,N} \right]. \tag{18} \] Equations (13), (17), and (18) recover the entire ordinary boundary polynomial \(B_N\). They hold at every \(N\ge2\), for every choice of signed integers \(n_v\), without a long-twist hypothesis. **Proof.** Expand the finite edge sums in (9) before taking any trace. Each summand is a tensor product of elements of the filled pair algebras and canonical polynomials at the separate free incidences. Under the algebra homomorphism \(\iota\), the crossing factor becomes \(R_{\rm ext}^{-n_v}\), and the edge factors become (14). At each filled pair, (5) gives \(\phi_v=\eta L_v\iota\). Taking these finite contractions proves (16) and the claimed membership. No pair has been projected onto its distinct eigenspaces. Apply the right-hand side of (18) to the expansion of (16) obtained from (17). On each free pair, equations (3) and (5) give \[ \eta L\bigl(e_{d-j}(\Omega_{\rm ext}) e_i(\Omega_{\rm ext})\bigr) =\phi(e_{d-j}e_i)=\delta_{i,j}. \tag{19} \] The product of these equalities extracts precisely \(c_{\mathbf j}\). Finally, substituting the common variable at each free vertex gives (13), term by term in the ordinary polynomial ring. This proves the theorem. \(\square\) The same algebraic proof permits identity connections \[ K_I(z,w)=\sum_{i=0}^d e_i(z)e_{d-i}(w) \tag{20} \] in place of selected turn connections, and the corresponding operator substitutions in (14). Which connection occurs is fixed by the original Conway expression. More generally, the source compiler writes every finite original Conway expression using these kernels, multiplication, crossing powers, and \(\phi\). Equation (5) intertwines multiplication and crossing powers, and (19) intertwines the contractions. Induction on that expression therefore proves the same boundary comparison. If a free ordinary product has several factors, its incidences are kept separate until the last substitution, exactly as above. The separately proved cup and cap formulas provide the explicit external boundary extension for a physical turn. They give \(\mathcal T_{\rm ext}(e_i(\Omega_{\rm ext})) =e_{d-i}(\Omega_{\rm ext})\), with the original cup and cap normalizations. Thus (20) and (14) encode the actual identity and turn operations. This does not assert that the external repository already implements arbitrary open Conway tangles. ## 4. Derivatives and the eventual closing functional The reconstruction includes the repeated-root derivatives in every independent variable by (7). It also determines derivatives of any fixed order of the unreduced ordinary polynomial in (13). Indeed, ordinary polynomial differentiation gives, for \(k\ge0\), \[ \partial_{z_u}^{\,k}B_N= \left. \left(\sum_{h=(e,u)}\partial_{z_h}\right)^k C_N \right|_{z_{(e,v)}=z_v}. \tag{21} \] For an empty incidence set the right-hand side is zero when \(k>0\). The multinomial expansion in (21) includes every way of distributing the derivative among factors at \(u\). Derivatives at several free vertices follow by taking the product of these commuting differential operators. There is no ambiguity about subsequent filling. If the remaining signed powers are \(m_u\), apply the original remaining functional \[ \mathcal C_{\mathbf m}(B)= \left(\bigotimes_{u\in U}\phi_u\right) \left[\prod_{u\in U}R(z_u)^{m_u}\,B(\mathbf z_U)\right]. \tag{22} \] At this final step its arguments are passed to \(\mathcal A_N\), as required by the original trace. Since (13), (17), and (18) recover \(B_N\) as an ordinary polynomial, (22) is exactly the original completed source scalar. Any prescribed exterior functional applied to that polynomial likewise agrees. If the completed diagram is instead evaluated as a braid in the external convention, the separate cut lemma gives its exact comparison: the physical word has reversed crossing signs, and the pivot and writhe factors are those of that lemma. They are not absorbed into a positive amplitude. For an exterior that is not an intertwiner, the unrestricted highest-head matrix functional must be retained; its replacement by an averaged trace is not justified. ## 5. Why a single boundary matrix would have lost information At one free vertex the map from ordinary polynomials to a single pair operator has kernel \((P_N)\). The nonzero ordinary polynomial \(P_N(z)\) is sent to zero. Therefore a boundary product of degree at least \(N\) cannot in general be recovered from one pair operator, even if its values and first derivatives at all Casimir roots are known. Those data recover its class, not the whole ordinary polynomial. The separate-incidence construction avoids this loss because each of its variables has degree below \(N\). The tensor product of the faithful maps (5) is injective on that space, and (18) is its explicit inverse. The ordinary diagonal substitution is performed only after this inverse. For \(h=|H|\) free incidences there are \(N^h\) coefficients in (17). Thus the representation has polynomial dimension in \(N\) for each fixed component, with no restriction on its fixed powers. This dimension count is not a bound on the condition number of the reconstruction. ## 6. What this gives the noncancellation problem The boundary correspondence removes a concrete ambiguity: the external matrix presentation, its specified closing trace, and the original Newton boundary source now agree exactly, including the derivatives that would be lost by diagonalizing the pair Casimir. The theorem applies to arbitrary fixed short components in the original compositional calculus. It does not give a lower bound for the geometric contribution after closing. The coefficient observations in (18) form a separating family; the required volume identity uses one prescribed completed contraction. A nonzero vector can have zero value under that contraction. Also, although the single-head change of basis (4) is unitary in the coordinate norms, the Newton reconstruction and the inserted dual observations need not have uniformly bounded condition numbers. The next analytic statement must therefore control the original geometric observation of (15), with its phases and the original closing functional retained. Exact recoverability of the boundary is available for that statement; a nonzero geometric asymptotic coefficient is not yet a consequence. ## 7. Direct proof dependencies The original pair algebra, its faithful physical realization, dual Newton basis, and full turn are proved in [the finite Newton calculus](../papers/newton-calculus/finite.tex), SHA256 2db2d7e15df0210c32bace4c761bdabadbb5d67140473a61425dac4d1e382f8e. The source (9) and the extension to finite Conway expressions are proved in [the arbitrary-power source compiler](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_arbitrary_power_source_compilation.md), SHA256 55e2de84870cfd20dac5922791dbc2bed54909439dfbf4663f17c70a1089445f. The external representation and sign in (5) are proved in [the local crossing comparison](research_rivin_jones_local_crossing_adapter.md), SHA256 c4a9a92ec22f31a035036642e0621ef9abe569646b2488dbac2d2add786500f0. The prescribed cut and reconstruction used in (5), (18), and (22) are proved in [the cut and Hermite recovery note](research_rivin_jones_prescribed_cut_and_hermite_recovery.md), SHA256 1b0e105ffb67b2b8552f5fddc5f0a3ac009e9795b33e27599ac4726ebd74079e. The turn is realized by the explicit regular bends in [the boundary-extension note](research_rivin_jones_regular_bends_and_newton_turn.md). These are written algebraic identities; no numerical checks or external code execution are used here.

title: A supplementary normal-fiber calculation for the exact boundary bridge
text: # A supplementary normal-fiber calculation for the exact boundary bridge Private written calculation, 14 November 2026. This records one concrete consequence of the [prescribed-cut recovery](research_rivin_jones_prescribed_cut_and_hermite_recovery.md). It is not a new general lower-bound theorem. The [closing stability-radius theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_observed_closing_stability_radius.md) already gives the abstract obstruction under arbitrary linear constraints; the calculation here identifies the relevant fiber inside the unit group of the actual full Hermite algebra. Use \(\mathcal A_N=\mathbb C[z]/(P_N)\), \(P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2\), and its distinct double nodes \(c\). Put \(a_c=4-c^2\ne0\). The exact prescribed external cut is \[ L(f)=\sum_{c\ {\rm double}}\{a_cf'(c)-cf(c)\} +\mathbf1_{N\ {\rm odd}}f(-2). \] Here \(L(f)\) means the original highest-head cut of \(f(\Omega_{\rm ext})\), not an unmarked matrix trace. The canonical nilpotent coupons \(V_c\) of the cited recovery have jets \((0,1)\) at \(c\), zero jets elsewhere, and satisfy \[ V_cV_{c'}=0\quad\hbox{for all }c,c',\qquad fV_c=f(c)V_c,\qquad L(V_c)=a_c. \] Fix a unit \(f\in\mathcal A_N\). Its entire fiber with the same values at every distinct spectral node is \[ f_{\boldsymbol\tau}=f\left(1+\sum_c\tau_cV_c\right), \qquad \boldsymbol\tau\in\mathbb C^{\lfloor N/2\rfloor}. \] Indeed the radical consists of the span of these \(V_c\), and division by the unit \(f\) preserves it. Every displayed element is still a unit: the inverse of the parenthesis is \(1-\sum_c\tau_cV_c\). It has the same represented eigenvalues and determinant as \(f\), because the parenthesis is \(I+B\) with \(B^2=0\), commutes with \(f\), and has determinant one. For any finite collection of prescribed closing coupons \(h_r\), the exact observation vector is \[ L(h_rf_{\boldsymbol\tau}) =L(h_rf)+\sum_c a_ch_r(c)f(c)\tau_c. \] Its affine image therefore has dimension \(\operatorname{rank}(h_r(c))_{r,c}\), since every \(a_cf(c)\) is nonzero. In particular, for a single closing unit \(h\) and any double node \(c\), choosing \[ \tau_c=\frac{z_0-L(hf)}{a_ch(c)f(c)}, \qquad \tau_{c'}=0\ (c'\ne c) \] sets the prescribed observation equal to any \(z_0\in\mathbb C\), including zero, while preserving all spectral values and invertibility. This includes \(h=R^n\) for every fixed integer \(n\). These changed coupons are not asserted to satisfy the Ward equations, endpoint pointing, or fixed-expression constraints of an actual short tangle. The calculation thus blocks an inference from unit spectral data alone; it makes no assertion about the coefficient of a fixed hyperbolic knot source. The existing positive criteria remain the [source-adapted composition criterion](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_source_adapted_observation_composition.md), the [joint analytic sewing criterion](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_six_port_analytic_sewing_criterion.md), and [transport of the original top relative cycle](research_dominant_saddle_transport.md). The exact external/Newton bridge transports their maps and prescribed observations, but does not establish their source overlap, transverse joint saddle, nonzero original contour intersection, or total complementary-current gap for arbitrary fixed short components. No stronger lower-bound implication is claimed here. Only written mathematics is used. No numerical evaluation, test, import, compilation, public-document edit, or frozen-proof edit was performed.

title: Rivin crossing frames, exact seams, and fused bridge angle volumes
text: # Rivin crossing frames, exact seams, and fused bridge angle volumes Written derivation, 14 November 2026. The external matrices are those of [rivin-jones at e956fb919ac7d1bbc7cb3d3873fbac993feb94b7](https://github.com/igorrivin/rivin-jones/tree/e956fb919ac7d1bbc7cb3d3873fbac993feb94b7), `docs/MATHEMATICS.md` and `python/rivin_jones/r_matrix.py`. Only their displayed formulas were read; no code was executed or imported. Each literal signed crossing has a direct two-cell positive angle half-density after an explicit change of its four boundary frames. The frames depend on whether the strand passes over or under. Their seams are part of the exact arbitrary-word identity. The existing coherent overbridge contraction then gives a useful fused form: its complete factorial magnitude is one angle-simplex weight, including the clock factor that would otherwise be mistaken for a harmless phase. On an explicit positive chamber its action is the volume of an ideal bipyramid. None of these statements removes the actual phase or proves survival of the original geometric scalar. ## 1. Both literal crossing signs in one notation Put \[ d=N-1,\qquad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad A=e^{-\pi i/(2N)},\qquad S_a=\prod_{j=1}^a2\sin(\pi j/N),\quad S_0=1. \] Every displayed index lies between zero and \(d\). Write \(I\) for the overstrand input and \(J\) for the understrand input. Their outputs are \(I-k\) and \(J+k\), respectively, where \[ 0\le k\le\min(I,d-J). \tag{1} \] For the positive crossing these are the external input indices \((i,j)=(I,J)\); for the negative crossing they are \((i,j)=(J,I)\). The checked outputs are in the order specified in the external source. The exact coefficient for either sign is \[ R_\sigma(I,J;k)=A^{Q_\sigma(I,J,k)} \frac{S_I S_{J+k}}{S_{I-k}S_J S_k}, \tag{2} \] with \[ \begin{split} Q_+&=(d-2I+2k)(d-2J-2k)+k(k-1)+Nk,\\ Q_-&=-(d-2I)(d-2J)-k(k-1)-Nk. \end{split} \tag{3} \] Indeed the symmetric Gaussian binomial at this root is its positive sine-factorial quotient. The positive product in the external formula contributes \((-i)^kS_I/S_{I-k}=A^{Nk}S_I/S_{I-k}\); the negative product and its printed sign contribute \(i^kS_I/S_{I-k}=A^{-Nk}S_I/S_{I-k}\). This verifies (2)--(3), including both parity conventions. The exact external-to-physical adapter in [the local crossing theorem](research_rivin_jones_local_crossing_adapter.md) reverses crossing sign at this choice of \(A\). Equation (2) uses the external signs throughout; it does not silently relabel them physical. ## 2. A direct two-cell half-density Define positive port frames \[ g_\epsilon(a)=\left(\frac{S_a}{\sqrt N}\right)^{\epsilon/2}, \qquad \epsilon=+1\text{ on an overstrand},\quad \epsilon=-1\text{ on an understrand}. \tag{4} \] The output port keeps its strand's role at that crossing. Let \(\widehat R_\sigma=G_{\rm out}R_\sigma G_{\rm in}^{-1}\), with the tensor products of these diagonal frames in the actual port order. Put \[ w_N(a,b,c)=\frac1{S_aS_bS_c},\qquad a+b+c=d. \] Then the complete entry is exactly \[ \boxed{\quad \widehat R_\sigma(I,J;k)=A^{Q_\sigma(I,J,k)}N \sqrt{w_N(k,I-k,d-I)\,w_N(k,J,d-J-k)}. \quad} \tag{5} \] The square root is positive real; the full original phase is outside it. To prove (5), the squared frame ratio is \(S_{I-k}S_J/(S_I S_{J+k})\). Multiplying it by the squared magnitude in (2) gives \[ \frac{S_I}{S_kS_{I-k}}\frac{S_{J+k}}{S_kS_J}. \] Root reflection \(S_aS_{d-a}=N\) converts this expression to the square of the magnitude in (5). The frames are positive, so the phase in (3) is unchanged. The proof includes all zero-transfer and endpoint entries; no additional internal summation variable has been introduced. The two triples in (5) have a shared first entry. Conversely two nonnegative sum-\(d\) triples with a shared first entry determine exactly one admissible \((I,J,k)\). Thus this is an actual local charge correspondence, not independent angles assigned after a sum. For the limiting interior coordinates \((u,v,t)=(I/N,J/N,k/N)\), write \[ \begin{split} \mathcal V_1&=V(\pi t,\pi(u-t),\pi(1-u)),\\ \mathcal V_2&=V(\pi t,\pi v,\pi(1-v-t)),\qquad V(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)=\Lambda(\alpha)+\Lambda(\beta)+\Lambda(\gamma), \end{split} \] where \(\alpha+\beta+\gamma=\pi\) and \(\Lambda'(\theta)=-\log(2\sin\theta)\), \(\Lambda(0)=0\). The uniform sine-factorial estimate proved in [the complete crossing norm calculation](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/weighted_crossing_source_gap.md), Section 2, gives \[ \frac{2\pi}{N}\log|\widehat R_\sigma| =\mathcal V_1+\mathcal V_2+O(\log N/N). \tag{6} \] At finite level one can use the exact positive angles \(\pi(a+1/3)/N\) for each triple in (5); they sum to \(\pi\), and the same error estimate holds. The limiting action in (6) is strictly concave on \(0<t<u<1\), \(0<v<1-t\). For \(\gamma=\pi-\alpha-\beta\), the negative Hessian of \(V\) is \(\left(\begin{smallmatrix}\cot\alpha+\cot\gamma&\cot\gamma\\ \cot\gamma&\cot\beta+\cot\gamma\end{smallmatrix}\right)\). Its determinant is one and its first diagonal entry is \(\sin\beta/(\sin\alpha\sin\gamma)>0\). Hence each tetrahedral volume has negative definite Hessian on its angle plane. The joint affine map from \((u,v,t)\) to the two triples is injective. Therefore a nonzero variation cannot lie in both Hessian kernels. This uses two cells for a whole crossing, compared with the six cells from the three fusion factors in [the reassociation angle kernel](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_reassociation_angle_kernel.md), Section 6. The price is that (4) is a role-dependent port frame, whereas that earlier theorem uses one fixed physical frame. This price must be retained in the next section. ## 3. The exact seams and the complete source On an internal strand segment of color \(a\), let \(\epsilon\) be its role at the preceding output and \(\epsilon'\) its role at the next input. The required diagonal connector is \[ H_{\epsilon',\epsilon}(a) =g_{\epsilon'}(a)g_\epsilon(a)^{-1} =\left(\frac{S_a}{\sqrt N}\right)^{(\epsilon'-\epsilon)/2}. \tag{7} \] It is one for equal roles and is \(S_a/\sqrt N\) or its reciprocal for a role switch. These are generally exponential weights. For example, for consecutive complete operators, \[ R_m\cdots R_1 =G_{{\rm out},m}^{-1}\widehat R_m (G_{{\rm in},m}G_{{\rm out},m-1}^{-1})\widehat R_{m-1} \cdots\widehat R_1G_{{\rm in},1}. \tag{8} \] Spectator frames are simply transported along their unchanged wires. Equation (8) is an equality of full matrices and therefore holds in an arbitrary exterior. Every original source vector is multiplied by its input frame and every original output row by its inverse output frame. An ordinary turn is transported by that same tensor rule. In particular \(g_\epsilon(a)g_\epsilon(d-a)=1\); two equally framed complementary legs fix their ordinary cup or cap pointwise. Unequal frames have their explicit remaining factor and are not declared source-fixing. For the external closed-braid prescription the quantum trace is diagonal, so its weight commutes with (7); the closing connector stays in the traced matrix element. The original highest-weight pin remains the index zero. Its possible endpoint-frame ratio is a power of \(N\), because \(g_\epsilon(0)=N^{-\epsilon/4}\). The writhe correction is unchanged. Thus (8), including closing seams, computes the prescribed original scalar for every fixed signed braid word. The full boundary adapter and [split-incidence theorem](research_rivin_jones_split_boundary_source_equivalence.md) transport the same equality to the original tangle source; this does not replace a full pair module by its semisimple spectrum or discard its Hermite normals. The seam action is also explicit. With \(x=a/N\), uniformly in \(a\), \[ \frac{2\pi}{N}\log H_{\epsilon',\epsilon}(a) =-(\epsilon'-\epsilon)\Lambda(\pi x)+O(\log N/N). \tag{9} \] Consequently the whole physical-state expansion has the sum of the two-cell actions (6), plus all terms (9) and the transported source action. The phase is exactly the sum of (3), the original pivot phases and writhe phase. Positive frame changes have not altered it. Strict concavity of an isolated two-cell expression alone says nothing about the Hessian after the seam terms are restored. ## 4. Coherent bridge fusion absorbs the factorial bookkeeping There is a source-exact way to combine these weights, rather than discard the seams. First undo the displayed port frames algebraically in (8), then apply the finite Fourier transformations and exact signed overbridge contraction of [the bridge theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_signed_overbridge_unwinding.md) and [the whole charged-source theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_global_charged_bridge_flow.md). These are equalities of the original source. Their Fourier clocks are new summation coordinates; no termwise identification with the physical colors of (2) is asserted. For a bridge with \(m\ge1\) encounters, put \(r=m+1\) and use its monotone clocks \(d\ge h_1\ge\cdots\ge h_m\ge0\). Its block lengths are \[ L_0=d-h_1,\quad L_j=h_j-h_{j+1}\ (1\le j<m),\quad L_m=h_m, \qquad \sum_{j=0}^mL_j=d. \tag{10} \] The exact bridge numerator is \(\Gamma_e\) times \(r\) homogeneous root-interval blocks. All its phase factors are prescribed in the whole charged-source theorem, equations (4), (6), (8)--(9). In particular \[ |\Gamma_e|=\frac{S_{h_1}}{S_{h_m}\prod_{j<m}S_{h_j-h_{j+1}}} =\frac{N}{\prod_{j=0}^mS_{L_j}}. \tag{11} \] Expand each block with head charge \(t_j\), \(0\le t_j\le L_j\). Its coefficient magnitude is \(S_{L_j}/(S_{t_j}S_{L_j-t_j})\). Therefore the complete magnitude, including the clock factor, is \[ \boxed{\quad |\Gamma_e|\prod_{j=0}^m\frac{S_{L_j}}{S_{t_j}S_{L_j-t_j}} =\frac{N}{\prod_{j=0}^m S_{t_j}S_{L_j-t_j}}. \quad} \tag{12} \] This cancellation includes every zero-length block. It is valid for arbitrary sign patterns along the bridge. The phase in (12) has not disappeared. If a block is \(\prod_{a<L}(\alpha X-Q^a\beta Y)\), its head-charge coefficient is exactly \[ \alpha^L\frac{S_L}{S_tS_{L-t}} \bigl[-(\beta/\alpha)q^{L-1}\bigr]^t. \tag{13} \] At the complete source \(\alpha,\beta\) are specified unit phases. Thus the complete bridge phase is \(\Gamma_e/|\Gamma_e|\) times the product of (13)'s unit factors. Anchor charges, closure adapters and their pivots are still exactly those of the whole charged-source theorem. For any specified complete choice of block charges, (12)--(13) give its actual complex weight; when several choices produce the same monomial they must still be summed coherently. The cancellation of factorials is not cancellation of the phase character. Writing the \(2r\) halfedge charges as \(a_{j,0}=L_j-t_j\), \(a_{j,1}=t_j\), one has \(\sum a=d\). For \(x_a=a/N\), the limiting bridge action is \[ \mathcal B(x)=2\sum_{a=1}^{2r}\Lambda(\pi x_a), \qquad x_a>0,\quad\sum_a x_a=1. \tag{14} \] Indeed \((2\pi/N)\log\) of (12) equals (14) up to \(O_m(\log N/N)\), uniformly up to the closed simplex. The shift \(x_a=(a+1/(2r))/N\) makes the simplex equation exact at finite level with the same error. ## 5. Genuine local geometry and its precise limit The function (14) is strictly concave on its open simplex. An explicit tetrahedral decomposition proves this without an assumed global angle incidence. For \(n=2r\), \(s_j=x_1+\cdots+x_j\), \[ \sum_{a=1}^n\Lambda(\pi x_a) =\sum_{j=2}^{n-1}V(\pi s_{j-1},\pi x_j,\pi(1-s_j)). \tag{15} \] The equality telescopes using \(\Lambda(\pi-y)=-\Lambda(y)\). Every triple is positive. The map of simplex tangent spaces into all these triangle tangent spaces is injective: the first triangle fixes the variations of \(x_1,x_2\), then each next triangle fixes the next variation. Strict concavity of tetrahedral volume proves the assertion. On the smaller chamber \(x_a<1/2\) for every \(a\), (14) is literally the volume of a convex ideal cyclic \(n\)-gonal bipyramid. In the sphere at infinity put its two apices at \(0,\infty\), and its equatorial vertices successively on the unit circle with angle gaps \(2\pi x_a\). Every gap is less than \(\pi\), so the center belongs to the interior of the equatorial polygon. In the Klein ball the convex hull is the two pyramids on this polygon; the central axis and its successive equatorial edges subdivide it into nonoverlapping ideal tetrahedra. The tetrahedron at gap \(2\pi x_a\) has dihedral angle triple \[ (2\pi x_a,\ \pi/2-\pi x_a,\ \pi/2-\pi x_a). \] Its volume is \(2\Lambda(\pi x_a)\), by the Lobachevsky duplication identity, which also follows by differentiating both sides and fixing the value at zero. Summing proves (14)'s geometric assertion. Outside that chamber, (14)--(15) remain strictly concave positive-tetrahedron identities, but the central-axis bipyramid subdivision just described is not a positive subdivision and is not claimed as one. The actual anchor equations linearly couple the halfedge charges of different bridges. They have not here been identified with the edge and peripheral angle equations of the desired hyperbolic complement. Nor does a maximum of (14) remove the phase (13), select a complex critical point, or prove its nonzero coefficient under the prescribed closing. What is established is a direct literal-crossing angle half-density, its exact arbitrary-source seams, and their source-exact coherent fusion into an explicit geometric local volume functional. The earlier reciprocal raw-Psi chart obstruction does not apply to these coefficient identities; no replacement of that off-grid density or its relative cycle has been made.

title: Exponentially small root carries in an actual Euler coproduct
text: # Exponentially small root carries in an actual Euler coproduct Private written proof, 18 November 2026. The finite Euler polynomial of the actual total lowering operator factors, up to an exponentially small operator carry, into a reversed ordered product of the finite one-head coproduct factors. The agreement below total degree \(N\) is exact. The carry is bounded before any coherent evaluation and remains exponentially small after multiplication by either actual operator inverse. The estimates hold in the original binomial metric, including a genuine complex meridian collar and its fixed derivatives. On any fixed compact coherent chart away from incidence, shrinking the activity disk makes the carry beat the exact conditioning cost of coherent evaluation. This does not prove a nonzero phase for the individual factors or for their product. The complete directs C and J are pinned below. C supplies the finite logarithm estimate; J supplies the actual ordered coproduct and source conventions. The factorization, norm estimates, and coherent comparison are proved here. ## 1. Actual finite operators and the required order Fix \(r\ge1\) heads and \[ N\ge2,\quad d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\quad f_n=\prod_{j=1}^n(1-Q^j),\quad f_0=1. \tag{1} \] The quantum root remains fixed. Each head has the original metric \[ \|w_a\|^2=\binom da^{-1}. \tag{2} \] At common meridian \(M\ne0\), the actual matrices are \[ E(M)w_a=(MQ^{-a}-M^{-1})w_{a-1}\quad(a>0),\quad E(M)w_0=0, \qquad K(M)w_a=-M q^{-1}Q^{-a}w_a. \tag{3} \] All tensor metrics are products of (2). Define \[ X_i(M)=E_i(M)\prod_{j>i}K_j(M),\qquad X(M)=\sum_{i=1}^rX_i(M)=E_{\rm tot}(M). \tag{4} \] These are exactly J's ordered lowering coproduct terms, with all Cartan factors present. Since \(KE=QEK\), one has \[ X_iX_j=QX_jX_i\quad(i<j),\qquad X_i^N=0,\qquad X^N=0. \tag{5} \] For the last identity, the finite binomial formula has zero intermediate coefficients in degree \(N\): its numerator contains \(1-Q^N\), whereas its denominators in the intermediate terms contain only \(1-Q^j\), \(0<j<N\). Induction over the heads proves the assertion. These are whole-meridian finite-matrix identities. Write \[ E_N(t)=\sum_{n=0}^{d}\frac{t^n}{f_n},\qquad \mathcal G_N(t,M)=E_N(tX(M)),\qquad \mathcal P_N(t,M)=E_N(tX_r(M))\cdots E_N(tX_1(M)). \tag{6} \] The order in \(\mathcal P_N\) is decreasing head index. For \(n<N\), the finite binomial identity gives \[ \frac{X^n}{f_n} =\sum_{n_1+\cdots+n_r=n} \frac{X_r^{n_r}\cdots X_1^{n_1}} {f_{n_r}\cdots f_{n_1}}. \tag{7} \] One elementary proof for two terms with \(AB=QBA\) is to expand \((A+B)^n\) in the order \(B^bA^a\). Multiplication by \(A+B\) gives the finite Gaussian-binomial recurrence, with coefficient \(f_n/(f_af_b)\). All denominators are nonzero for \(n<N\). Iteration gives (7). Thus \[ \boxed{\quad \mathcal G_N=[\mathcal P_N]_{<N},\qquad \mathcal C_N:=\mathcal P_N-\mathcal G_N =\sum_{n=N}^{rd}P_{N,n}(M)t^n . \quad}\tag{8} \] For \(r=1\) this carry is zero. For more heads it is retained as the specified finite polynomial. No exact generic-parameter infinite-product factorization has been specialized through a root singularity. ## 2. Exact finite logarithms and both inverses Set \[ L_N(t)=\sum_{j=1}^{d}\frac{t^j}{j(1-Q^j)}. \tag{9} \] C proves directly from the coefficient recurrence that \(E_N\) is the degree-\(d\) Taylor polynomial of \(\exp L_N\). It follows, for every actual matrix \(Y\) with \(Y^N=0\), that \[ \boxed{\quad E_N(tY)=\exp L_N(tY),\qquad E_N(tY)^{-1}=\exp[-L_N(tY)] . \quad}\tag{10} \] These are exact matrix identities for every \(t\), not small-\(t\) asymptotics. Terms of degree at least \(N\) vanish because they contain \(Y^N\). In particular both matrices in (6) are invertible for all \(t\). The inverse of the product has the reversed factor order. There is an absolute \(C>0\) such that \[ \|L_N(tY)\|\le CN|t|\,\|Y\|, \qquad |t|\,\|Y\|\le1/4. \tag{11} \] For clarity this does not require a spectral norm equality. Bound the sum in (9) by \(\sum_j(|t|\|Y\|)^j/[j|1-Q^j|]\). The elementary sine inequality \[ |1-Q^j|\ge4\min(j,N-j)/N \] bounds the terms \(j\le N/2\) by \(N(|t|\|Y\|)^j/(4j^2)\). The upper half has a geometric factor \((|t|\|Y\|)^{N/2}\) and a harmonic sum, uniformly bounded by the right side of (11). This proves the estimate. Consequently \[ \|E_N(tY)\|,\ \|E_N(tY)^{-1}\| \le \exp(CN|t|\,\|Y\|). \tag{12} \] The inverse bound is essential to the relative carry estimate. ## 3. Original-metric bounds on a genuine meridian collar At \(M=1\), the weighted lowering coefficient in (3) has norm \[ 2\sin(\pi a/N)\sqrt{\frac{N-a}{a}} \le 2\pi\sqrt{\frac aN(1-a/N)}\le\pi. \tag{13} \] Here \(1\le a\le d\); the forced bottom arrow is zero. If \(Lw_a=w_{a-1}\) with its bottom zero, then \[ \|L\|=\sqrt d,\qquad E(M)=M E(1)+(M-M^{-1})L,\qquad \|K(M)\|=|M|. \tag{14} \] Thus no unscaled meridian disk with a uniform small-activity domain is being assumed. Fix \(\eta>0\) and use the actual complex collar \[ M=\exp(u/\sqrt N),\qquad |u|\le\eta. \tag{15} \] Equations (13)--(14) give \[ \|E(M)\|\le \pi e^\eta+2\eta e^\eta,\qquad \|X_i(M)\|\le B,\qquad \|X(M)\|\le rB, \tag{16} \] where \(B=B(r,\eta)\) is independent of \(N\). For example the first bound follows from \(|M-M^{-1}|\le2|u|e^{|u|/\sqrt N}/\sqrt N\); the remaining Cartan factors in (4) give a bounded factor \(e^{r\eta}\). Their exact values have not been dropped. The customary smaller collar \(M=\exp(v/N)\), with bounded \(v\), is contained in (15) for large \(N\). Choose \(R>0\) with \(RrB\le1/4\). Equations (12),(16) imply, for \(|t|\le R\), \[ \begin{split} \|\mathcal G_N(t,M)\|,\ \|\mathcal G_N(t,M)^{-1}\| &\le e^{A N|t|},\\ \|\mathcal P_N(t,M)\|,\ \|\mathcal P_N(t,M)^{-1}\| &\le e^{A N|t|}, \end{split}\tag{17} \] with \(A=CrB\), enlarged if needed. All matrices are holomorphic in \(t,u\) on a neighborhood of each smaller closed bidisk. ## 4. The retained carry is exponentially small On \(|t|=R\), (17) and the operator-valued Cauchy estimate give \[ \|P_{N,n}(M)\|\le e^{ANR}R^{-n}. \] Apply this only to the actual high-degree coefficients in (8). For \(0<\rho<1\) and \(|t|\le\rho R\), \[ \boxed{\quad \|\mathcal C_N(t,M)\| \le \frac{\rho^N}{1-\rho}e^{ANR}. \quad}\tag{18} \] Multiplication by either actual inverse in (17) gives the two-sided relative bounds \[ \boxed{\begin{split} \|\mathcal G_N^{-1}\mathcal P_N-I\|,\ \|\mathcal P_N\mathcal G_N^{-1}-I\| &\le \frac1{1-\rho} \exp\{N[\log\rho+AR(1+\rho)]\},\\ \|\mathcal P_N^{-1}\mathcal G_N-I\|,\ \|\mathcal G_N\mathcal P_N^{-1}-I\| &\le \frac1{1-\rho} \exp\{N[\log\rho+AR(1+\rho)]\}. \end{split}}\tag{19} \] No commuting of an inverse through the carry is used. In particular, fixing a sufficiently small \(R\) and \(\rho=1/2\) proves an exponentially small relative carry. More generally, for any prescribed \(\Lambda>0\), one can keep \(R\) fixed and choose \(\rho>0\) sufficiently small so that all four relative errors and the absolute error in (18) are \(O(e^{-\Lambda N})\). This gives a nonempty activity disk, whose size is allowed to depend on \(\Lambda,r,\eta\). It does not assert that a given geometric source point lies inside that disk. The same conclusions hold with all fixed \(t\)- and \(u\)-derivatives on smaller bidisks. To see this, first choose a slightly larger activity disk and a slightly larger collar on which the desired exponential rate holds, then apply Cauchy estimates to the exact holomorphic errors in (18)--(19). In the original meridian variable this gives, for each fixed \(j\), the corresponding bound with at most a factor \(O(N^{j/2})\) for \(\partial_M^j\). Indeed \(M\partial_M=\sqrt N\,\partial_u\), and \(M\) stays bounded away from zero. These are genuine meridian derivatives of the actual fixed-root matrices, not quantum-parameter derivatives of a root identity. ## 5. Coherent evaluation and its explicit conditioning Retain the exact original binomial kernels of J: \[ c(\mathbf z)=\bigotimes_i \sum_{a=0}^d\binom da z_i^aw_a,\qquad v(\mathbf w)=\bigotimes_i\sum_{a=0}^d w_i^aw_a^*,\qquad \sigma_N(B)= \frac{v(\mathbf w)B c(\mathbf z)} {\prod_i(1+w_i z_i)^d}. \tag{20} \] There is no change of metric or of the finite caps. For any matrix \(B\), Cauchy--Schwarz in (2) gives \[ |\sigma_N(B)| \le \|B\|\prod_i \left[ \frac{\sqrt{(1+|w_i|^2)(1+|z_i|^2)}}{|1+w_i z_i|} \right]^d. \tag{21} \] The bracket is projectively well defined and continuous off the incidence divisor. For each fixed compact \[ \mathcal K\Subset \bigl((\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1) \setminus\{1+wz=0\}\bigr)^r \] there is therefore a finite \(\kappa_{\mathcal K}\ge0\) with \[ \sup_{\mathcal K}|\sigma_N(B)| \le e^{\kappa_{\mathcal K}N}\|B\|. \tag{22} \] On the original real coherent cycle \(z_i=\bar w_i\) the brackets are exactly one. Given \(\mathcal K\) and \(\Lambda>0\), choose the activity disk in (18)--(19) with rate larger than \(\Lambda+\kappa_{\mathcal K}\). Then \[ \boxed{\quad \sup_{\mathcal K} |\sigma_N(\mathcal P_N-\mathcal G_N)| =O(e^{-\Lambda N}). \quad}\tag{23} \] The same holds for the normalized kernels of each relative operator error in (19). Every fixed coherent-coordinate derivative has the same conclusion on smaller charts: use (22) on slightly larger projective charts and apply Cauchy estimates to the holomorphic normalized kernel. The meridian-normal statement from §4 remains valid. This is an absolute comparison after the stated identity-cap normalization. It is not a relative scalar estimate obtained by dividing by \(\sigma_N(\mathcal G_N)\), which may vanish. In particular neither (19) nor (23) supplies a selected coherent phase or a nonzero amplitude for the product factors. A paired exterior remains an actual matrix or kernel; its norm or conditioning must be included before (18) is used inside the full source. ## 6. The fixed-denominator family and the original normal row The theorem estimates precisely the family in (6): \(E_N(tE_{\rm tot}(M))\), with the fixed denominators \(f_n\) and all meridian dependence in the actual operators. It retains the complete cap and uses no continuation of an occupation index. It does not replace a different coefficient family such as \[ \sum_{n=0}^d \frac{t^n E_{\rm tot}(M)^n}{(M^{-2}Q;Q)_n}. \tag{24} \] Although (24) agrees with \(\mathcal G_N\) at \(M=1\), its meridian derivative also differentiates the denominator. For example that extra coefficient at \(M=1\) is exactly \[ \left.\partial_M \frac{f_n}{(M^{-2}Q;Q)_n}\right|_{M=1} =-2\sum_{j=1}^n\frac{Q^j}{1-Q^j}. \tag{25} \] This finite normal insertion must be retained in any use of the theorem for such a contracted source. No bound or cancellation for its pairing with the quotient is supplied by silently replacing (24) by (6). Likewise no ordinary quantum-parameter normal follows by differentiating (5), (7), or (10) away from the root. The result is a controlled factorization of an actual finite coproduct factor, with its carry and coherent conditioning quantified. The quotient, turnover, all source coupons, and relative-window defects of J remain in the full period. ## Complete proof directs * C: notes/research_factorial_coupon_small_activity_saddle.md, SHA256 9ab9fef5bfab21872aa9c6ec72990e9695df24e5cfffddb02902aaced4e16465. * J: notes/research_opposite_polarization_source_kernel.md, SHA256 d52c6dd8e62f575a262fc7af460e258f7cb0e40b5a9c037ac46dd8d151002d44. Both complete directs were freshly read nontruncated in this active author sequence and retained unchanged. Every used implication was checked. Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used. Frozen and public files were not changed.

title: Research methods and their present roles
text: # Research methods and their present roles 25 November 2026. The [current status](research_finite_exceptions_progress.md) states the open finite-exception problem. The [papers](../papers/README.md) contain the established restricted volume theorems. The following methods have distinct roles. ## Exact finite sources and orthogonality The actual source includes a fixed closing functional and normal directions at repeated spectral roots. The [ordinary-color Parseval calculation](ordinary_color_plancherel_bound_audit.md) separates a remainder by exact orthogonality; it does not evaluate the resulting whole norm geometrically. The [two-dimensional Hermite source frame](actual_tame_c0_hermite_source_frame.md) and [cap-tree energy](actual_cap_tree_angle_energy.md) give positive forms that retain the marked observations. Their stated compatibility conditions matter: a direction invisible at one cut can become visible after another crossing. The [normalized source energy](research_convex_normalized_conway_source.md), [orthogonal linear elimination](research_conway_orthogonal_linear_elimination.md) and [finite-fiber comparison](research_conway_reciprocal_finite_fiber_lower_bound.md) give the general variational formulation. Its remaining minimum still needs a geometric exponential evaluation. ## Algebraic periods, recurrences and torsors The [torsor status](a_polynomial_torsor_status.md) separates finite operator identities, algebraic branches, recurrence solutions and volume limits. A classical curve alone does not select the original quantum solution. The source, closing and normalization must survive every change of presentation. The [initialized coideal period](research_coideal_normalized_marked_period.md) is a finite realization of this viewpoint. The [cyclic Hardy comparison](research_cyclic_atom_hardy_head_comparison.md) provides a function-theoretic approach to coefficient norms. Neither calculation identifies an arbitrary closed source with a contributing geometric period. ## Geometry and optimization The [marked-filling paper](../papers/marked-fillings/README.md) constructs the geometric data used by the volume arguments. The [strict Conway geometry](../papers/strict-conway-geometry/README.md) identifies their marked action with the absolute knot-complement volume. The geometric maximum and its rigidity do not by themselves prove survival of the original quantum contribution. The [Rivin presentation comparison](research_rivin_jones_partial_filling_assessment.md) retains the necessary boundary indices. The [cover laws](regge_period_covers_and_a_curves.md) and [filled-slope obstruction](research_filled_cover_slope_length_obstruction.md) explain why a cover requires a separate filling and quantum descent argument. ## Obstructions and other comparisons The illustrated [methods chapter](../book/chapters/methods.md) explains weighted Cauchy--Schwarz, Fourier analysis, positive coefficient bounds and stationary phase. Its counterexamples distinguish upper bounds from noncancellation. The [analytic transport examples](actual_local_analytic_transport_action_barrier.md) show why distinct instantaneous eigenvalues do not give a single-branch asymptotic. The [relative-homology criterion](research_dominant_saddle_transport.md) states sufficient additional conditions for persistence of a saddle. The [source and transport chapter](../book/chapters/mechanism.md) retains the Racah, magnetic Fourier, reflection-double and positive-sewing approaches with their local conclusions and unresolved global steps. Earlier parameter pilots and superseded proof notes are in the [pre-cleanup snapshot](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/tree/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes), without duplicate archive directories in the active tree.

title: Exponential real characteristic concentration of the actual edge source
text:
# Exponential real characteristic concentration of the actual edge source Private written proof, 23 November 2026. The exact same-index edge equation gives exponential, rather than only algebraic, concentration away from a fixed real symbol gap. For a graph with arbitrary coupled channel weights, the bound is \(CE N^2e^{-cN\delta^2}\) times its full Fourier energy. Normalized angular jets satisfy the same estimate as a complete vector. The proof iterates the adjoint equation on explicit Gaussian test functions. Only those known test functions are continued to fractional Weyl displacements. No continuation or asymptotic expression for the unknown source is used. All incidence variables remain separate until the original vertex and marked-closing operations are applied. ## 1. Exact source and the quantitative statement Use the complete source conventions of [A] and its complete original source direct [F]. Put \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\), and \[ B_k(z)= rac{q^{-k^2}(-qz;Q)_k(-q/z;Q)_k}{S_k^2}, \qquad S_k=\prod_{j=1}^k2\sin(\pi j/N),\quad 0\le k\le d. 	ag{1} \] In particular \(B_k(z)=e_k(-z-z^{-1})\), with the actual common Newton basis and no discarded endpoint channels. For a graph with \(E\ge1\) edges, keep two separate incidence variables per edge and any finite complex coefficient array: \[ F_N=\sum_{\mathbf k\in\{0,\ldots,d\}^E} \mu_{\mathbf k,N}\prod_{e=1}^E B_{k_e}(z_e)B_{k_e}(y_e). 	ag{2} \] The weights may be arbitrarily coupled and level-dependent; they must be independent of the incidence activities. This includes the actual edge insertion weights and their activity-independent normal weights where defined. Each individual Fourier exponent lies in \([-d,d]\). Let \(\mathscr D_j=z_j\partial_{z_j}\), with all incidence variables included. Let \(\mathcal A\) be a finite downward-closed set of multiindices containing zero, and put \[ p=\max_{\alpha\in\mathcal A}|\alpha|,\qquad u_\alpha=N^{-|\alpha|}\mathscr D^\alpha F_N . 	ag{3} \] The scalar case is \(\mathcal A=\{0\}\). The integer \(p\) is fixed; it is unrelated to the growing physical occupation degree. Use the exact Gaussian Fourier analysis \(\mathcal F_N\) of [A], equation (8) on all \(2E\) coordinates, with a fixed width \(\sigma>0\). At edge \(e\), write \(z=e^{i	heta_z}\), \(y=e^{i	heta_y}\), \(Y_z=e^{2\pi i\xi_z}\), \(Y_y=e^{2\pi i\xi_y}\), and set \[ p_{e,0}=  rac{(1+z)(1+y)}{zy} \{(z-y)(Y_zY_y-1)+(1-zy)(Y_z-Y_y)\}. 	ag{4} \] The prefactor, including its zeros at \(z=-1\) or \(y=-1\), is retained. Define \(\mathcal B_\delta=\{\max_e|p_{e,0}|\ge\delta\}\). There are positive constants \(C_{\sigma,p},c_{\sigma,p}\), independent of the coefficient array and the number of edges, such that \[  oxed{\quad \int_{\mathcal B_\delta} \sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal A}|\mathcal F_Nu_\alpha|^2d
u \le C_{\sigma,p} E N^2 e^{-c_{\sigma,p}N\delta^2} \sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal A}\|u_\alpha\|_2^2, \qquad 0<\delta\le1 . \quad} 	ag{5} \] The norm and measure are exactly the Laurent coefficient norm and full Gaussian-frame measure. For every fixed \(\delta>0\), the right side is also \(C_{\sigma,p,\delta}E e^{-c_{\sigma,p,\delta}N}\) times that energy. This is an off-characteristic estimate, not an exponentially small bound on the entire weighted second moment. ## 2. Exact equations and Weyl ordering For one incidence pair put \[  egin{gathered} a_z=1+qz,\quad b_z=1+q^{-1}/z,\quad T_zf(z)=f(Qz),\ A_z=a_zT_z-b_z,\quad D_z=b_zT_z-a_z,\quad P_N=A_zD_y-D_zA_y . \end{gathered} 	ag{6} \] The cleared product identity in [A], equation (4) gives \(A_zB_k=-Q^kD_zB_k\). Consequently \(P_{e,N}F_N=0\) for every edge of (2). Its exact normal order is \[ P_N=(a_zb_y-b_za_y)(T_zT_y-1) +(b_zb_y-a_za_y)(T_z-T_y). 	ag{7} \] Its exponent set and coefficient bounds are fixed independently of \(N\). All these are full Laurent identities, including all low and high channels. No finite output compression occurs. On the full Fourier lattice \(\ell^2(\mathbb Z^2)\), let \((Z^af)_m=f_{m-a}\) and \((T^bf)_m=Q^{b\cdot m}f_m\). Thus \(T^bZ^a=Q^{a\cdot b}Z^aT^b\). The symmetric Weyl operator is \[  egin{split} W_N(a,b)&=Q^{a\cdot b/2}Z^aT^b,\ (W_N(a,b)f)_m &=e^{2\pi ib\cdot(m-a/2)/N}f_{m-a},\ W_N(a,b)W_N(c,e) &=e^{\pi i(b\cdot c-a\cdot e)/N}W_N(a+c,b+e). \end{split} 	ag{8} \] Here \(Q^{a\cdot b/2}=e^{\pi ia\cdot b/N}\), and \(W_N(a,b)^\dagger=W_N(-a,-b)\). A normal coefficient \(c_{ab,N}\) becomes \(c_{ab,N}Q^{-a\cdot b/2}\) in this Weyl order. No ordering phase is silently discarded. We will use a Hilbert-valued version. Suppose \(\mathbb P_N=\sum_t C_{t,N}W_N(a_t,b_t)\) on \(\ell^2(\mathbb Z^2;\mathcal H)\), with a fixed finite set of bounded integer displacements and \(\sum_t\|C_{t,N}\|\le A\). The coefficient operators act only on \(\mathcal H\). Its Weyl symbol is \[ \mathfrak p_N(	heta,\xi) =\sum_t C_{t,N}e^{i(a_t\cdot	heta+2\pi b_t\cdot\xi)}. 	ag{9} \] Assume \(\|\mathfrak p_N-p_0I_{\mathcal H}\|\le A/N\), uniformly on this real phase space. For (7) this follows by \(q	o1\) and the ordering phase in (8), with exactly the scalar (4). Constants in the test-function estimates may depend on the fixed displacement set. For the edge operators and their prolongations that set is absolute and independent of the graph. ## 3. Analytic Gaussian tests on the full lattice For \(	heta\in\mathbb T^2\), \(\xi\in\mathbb R^2\), write \[ g_{	heta,\xi}(m)=c_N e^{-|m-N\xi|^2/(2\sigma N)}e^{-im\cdot	heta}, \qquad c_N=(N/(\pi\sigma))^{1/2}. 	ag{10} \] Then \(\mathcal F_Nf=\langle g_{	heta,\xi},fangle\) and the frame is an exact isometry, also for Hilbert-valued coefficients. Its individual test-vector norm is at most \(C_\sigma N\). These vectors need not be individually normalized. For the following calculation only, extend the known Gaussian (10) to an entire function of its argument. For complex vectors \(A,B\) define its centered displacement by \[ (\mathcal C_{	heta,\xi}(A,B)h)(z)= e^{-iA\cdot	heta-2\pi iB\cdot\xi} e^{2\pi iB\cdot(z-A/2)/N}h(z-A). 	ag{11} \] At integer \(A,B\), this is the centered version of (8) on the sampled Gaussian. No fractional shift of the source \(f\) is defined. For \(t=m-N\xi\), direct substitution gives \[ (\mathcal C(A,B)g)(m)=c_N e^{-im\cdot	heta} \exp\left\{- rac{(t-A)\cdot(t-A)}{2\sigma N} + rac{2\pi iB\cdot t}{N}- rac{\pi iA\cdot B}{N}ight\}. 	ag{12} \] All dependence on the real center cancels except in the translated lattice \(t=m-N\xi\). Completing the real square proves \[ \|\mathcal C(A,B)g\|_{\ell^2} \le C_\sigma N \exp\{C_\sigma(|A|^2+|B|^2)/N\}. 	ag{13} \] Indeed its squared modulus is a real translated Gaussian times an exponential bounded by \(e^{C_\sigma(|A|^2+|B|^2)/N}\). The uniform bound \(\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z^2}e^{-|m-c|^2/(\sigma N)}\le C_\sigma N\) follows by a sum--integral comparison in each coordinate. Together with \(c_N^2=O_\sigma(N)\) it gives (13). This proof is uniform over all real \(	heta,\xi\). For any ordered list of \(m\) bounded displacements, consider \(\prod_{j=1}^m\mathcal C(s_ja_j,s_jb_j)g\). The product law (8) extends algebraically to these complex parameters. Its scalar phase has logarithmic modulus at most \(Cm^2(1+r)^2/N\) when \(|s_j|\le1+r\), and both summed displacements have size at most \(Cm(1+r)\). Equation (13) therefore gives the uniform bound \[ \left\|\prod_{j=1}^m \mathcal C(s_ja_j,s_jb_j)gight\|_{\ell^2} \le C_\sigma N\exp\{C_\sigma m^2(1+r)^2/N\}. 	ag{14} \] The product is an entire Hilbert-space-valued function of the \(m\) parameters: its sampled entries are entire and the Gaussian bound is locally summable. This continuation concerns explicit test functions only. ## 4. High differences give an exponential estimate Suppose \(\mathbb P_N f=0\). At a phase point where \(|p_0|\ge\delta\) and \(A/N\le\delta/2\), the matrix symbol is invertible with \(\|\mathfrak p_N^{-1}\|\le2/\delta\). Keep this symbol fixed at that point and define \[ \mathbb Q=I-\mathbb P_N^\dagger(\mathfrak p_N^\dagger)^{-1}. 	ag{15} \] The inverse in (15) is on the right. Thus \(\mathbb Q^\dagger f=f\) even when the coefficient matrices do not commute. For any \(h\in\mathcal H\), \(\langle g\otimes h,fangle =\langle\mathbb Q^m(g\otimes h),fangle\). Put \(w_t=e^{i(a_t\cdot	heta+2\pi b_t\cdot\xi)}\). Exactly, \[ \mathbb Q=\sum_t D_t(I-V_t),\quad D_t=C_{t,N}^\dagger ar w_t(\mathfrak p_N^\dagger)^{-1}, \quad V_t=w_tW_N(-a_t,-b_t),\quad \sum_tD_t=I,\quad\sum_t\|D_t\|\le2A/\delta . 	ag{16} \] The matrices \(D_t\) commute with the physical displacements, not necessarily with one another. The analytic interpolation of \(V_t\) is \(\mathcal C(-sa_t,-sb_t)\), equal to \(I\) at \(s=0\). For each ordered word, the mixed fundamental theorem of calculus expresses \(\prod_{j=1}^m(I-V_{t_j})g\), up to its sign, as the integral over \([0,1]^m\) of the mixed derivative \(\partial_{s_1}\cdots\partial_{s_m}\prod_j \mathcal C(-s_ja_{t_j},-s_jb_{t_j})g\). Apply multivariate Cauchy at radius \(r>0\) in each variable to (14). Every variable is differentiated once, so there is no factor \(m!\). One obtains \[ \left\|\prod_{j=1}^m(I-V_{t_j})gight\| \le C_\sigma N r^{-m} e^{C_\sigma m^2(1+r)^2/N}. 	ag{17} \] The same estimate follows by scalar Cauchy after testing against each unit vector, so no finite-dimensional truncation is involved. Expand \(\mathbb Q^m\), bound the matrix words by the products of their norms, and sum using (16). With \(1\le m\le N\) and \(r=\sqrt{N/m}\), (17) gives \[ \|\mathbb Q^m(g\otimes h)\| \le C_\sigma N \left( rac{C_{\sigma,A}}{\delta}\sqrt{ rac mN}ight)^m e^{C_\sigma m^2/N}\|h\|. 	ag{18} \] Here \(m^2(1+\sqrt{N/m})^2/N\le C(m+m^2/N)\); the factor \(e^{Cm}\) has been included inside the parentheses. Choose a fixed sufficiently small \(\varepsilon>0\), depending only on the coefficient and displacement bounds and \(\sigma\), and put \(m=\lfloor\varepsilon N\delta^2floor\). When \(N\delta^2\) exceeds a sufficiently large fixed constant, the symbol inverse exists, \(m\ge\varepsilon N\delta^2/2\), and the parenthesized factor times \(e^{C_\sigma m/N}\) is below \(e^{-2}\). Equations (15)--(18), followed by supremum over \(\|h\|=1\), imply \[ \|\mathcal F_N f(	heta,\xi)\|_{\mathcal H} \le C_\sigma N e^{-c_{\sigma,A}N\delta^2}\|f\|_2 \quad	ext{on }\{|p_0|\ge\delta\}. 	ag{19} \] This estimate is uniform in the center. To integrate it, assume the Fourier support of \(f\) in these two coordinates is in \([-d,d]^2\). On \(|\xi|_\infty\le2\), the measure has finite volume, and (19) gives the desired \(CN^2e^{-cN\delta^2}\) bound. On its complement, angular Parseval and (10) give directly \[ \int_{\{|\xi|_\infty>2\}}\|\mathcal F_Nf\|_{\mathcal H}^2d
u \le C_\sigma e^{-c_\sigma N}\|f\|_2^2 . 	ag{20} \] For every supported index, at least one Gaussian coordinate is a distance \(N\) from its center on that region; splitting half its Gaussian exponent proves (20) by elementary integration. Since \(0<\delta\le1\), this tail is absorbed by the same bound. In the remaining regime of bounded \(N\delta^2\), isometry gives the bound after increasing its fixed constant. We have proved \[ \int_{\{|p_0|\ge\delta\}}\|\mathcal F_Nf\|_{\mathcal H}^2d
u \le C_{\sigma,A}N^2e^{-c_{\sigma,A}N\delta^2}\|f\|_2^2 	ag{21} \] for every exact null vector of the operator in (9). ## 5. Coupled channels and the full angular-jet vector First apply (21) to (2) and one edge. Regard all other Fourier coordinates as a Hilbert-valued coefficient. The coefficients of (7) are uniformly bounded, and (9) differs from (4) by \(O(N^{-1})\). The source Fourier support on that edge is in \([-d,d]^2\). Analysis in the other coordinates is an exact isometry and preserves the integrated partial-frame norm. The constants are therefore independent of the number of other coordinates and of their coupled channel weights. Taking the union of the \(E\) bad sets proves (5) in the scalar case. For the jets (3), the exact equations in [A], equation (17) are \[ P_{e,N}u_\alpha+ \sum_{ eta<\alpha} inom\alpha eta N^{-(|\alpha|-| eta|)} (\mathscr D^{\alpha- eta}P_{e,N})u_ eta=0 . 	ag{22} \] Coefficient derivatives only are meant in the second term. These are homogeneous equations for the whole prolonged vector, not separate homogeneous equations for its individual jets. To apply (21), group the jets by their multiindex outside edge \(e\). Within each group, the two remaining indices form a downward-closed set with at most \((p+1)^2\) members. The resulting block operator has \(P_{e,N}\) on its diagonal and fixed-degree off-diagonal entries of norm \(O_p(N^{-1})\). Its Weyl symbol is \[ p_{e,0}I+O_p(N^{-1}). 	ag{23} \] Its finite exponent set, coefficient sum, and error bound depend only on \(p\), not on the outside multiindex or the number of edges. Indeed a coefficient derivative outside the two edge coordinates is zero; all remaining binomial factors have order at most \(p\). The direct sum of these groups, with the other Fourier coordinates, can be used as the Hilbert coefficient space in (9). Apply (21) to this exact homogeneous block system, use isometry in the other coordinates, and take the union over edges. This proves the full assertion (5). No commutator forcing has been discarded. ## 6. A bound for the actual marked closing of the complementary piece For the fixed template and vertex rules of [F], the original marked closing is a known polynomially bounded linear functional on the finite canonical incidence space. We prove the needed norm comparison, rather than commuting a phase-space cutoff through that closing. Let \(\mathcal V_N\) be the space of separately even Laurent polynomials of band \([-d,d]\) in every one of the \(2E\) incidence variables. The source (2) belongs to this space. Keep a compact parameter disk \(|s|\le R<1\), the template's fixed signed crossing powers, its own relations \(P_{\sigma_v}\), and its original full marked functional \(\Lambda_{N,s}\). Then \[ |\Lambda_{N,s}(h)|\le C_{\mathrm{template},R}N^B \|h\|_2,\qquad h\in\mathcal V_N . 	ag{24} \] Here \(B\) depends on the fixed template and powers, not on \(h\) or any coefficient array in (2). Indeed \(\|h\|_{\mathrm{Fourier}\,1}\le(2d+1)^E\|h\|_2\). Group reciprocal monomial orbits using \(z^j+z^{-j}=2(-1)^j C_j(X)\), \(X=-z-z^{-1}\). Their Chebyshev coefficient sum equals their Fourier coefficient sum. Identifying the incidence variables at a vertex cannot increase that sum: \(2C_iC_j=C_{i+j}+C_{|i-j|}\). The actual fixed crossing polynomial \(p_v\) has polynomial Chebyshev coefficient sum by the complete normal-norm lemma in [F]. After multiplication, the vertex degree is at most \((d_v+1)d\). Reduction in its proper relation costs at most a fixed power of \(2\cosh(2\pi R)+1\), again by [F], so this is a template constant. Finally \(\phi_{\sigma_v}=\eta N^2[X^d]\) extracts \(N^2/2\) times the top Chebyshev coefficient. These bounds prove (24). The actual external framing and \(H_N(s)\) factors in [F] are uniformly bounded on the disk and remain included. All quotient reductions and repeated-root normal directions stay in this calculation. Fixed parameter derivatives obey the same type of bound by Cauchy on a slightly larger disk inside \(|s|<1\); no moving-quantum-parameter estimate is asserted. Let \(\Pi_N\) be the orthogonal projection onto \(\mathcal V_N\): first retain the full band, then average independently under \(z_j\leftrightarrow z_j^{-1}\). Those two projections commute. Use the full \(2E\)-dimensional exact frame and define \[ Q_\Omega=\Pi_N\mathcal F_N^\dagger \mathbf1_\Omega\mathcal F_N\Pi_N,\qquad F_{\mathrm{off}}=Q_{\mathcal B_\delta}F_N,\qquad F_{\mathrm{on}}=Q_{\mathcal B_\delta^c}F_N . 	ag{25} \] Each \(Q_\Omega\) is a positive contraction on \(\mathcal V_N\), and \[ F_N=F_{\mathrm{on}}+F_{\mathrm{off}},\qquad \|F_{\mathrm{off}}\|_2^2 \le\langle F_N,Q_{\mathcal B_\delta}F_Nangle =\int_{\mathcal B_\delta}|\mathcal F_NF_N|^2d
u . 	ag{26} \] The inequality follows from \(0\le Q\le I\), hence \(Q^2\le Q\). Applying (5) in its scalar case and then the actual functional (24) gives the source-exact decomposition and estimate \[  egin{gathered} \Lambda_{N,s}(F_N)= \Lambda_{N,s}(F_{\mathrm{on}}) +\Lambda_{N,s}(F_{\mathrm{off}}),\ |\Lambda_{N,s}(F_{\mathrm{off}})| \le C_{\mathrm{template},R,\sigma}\sqrt E\,N^{B+1} e^{-c_\sigma N\delta^2/2}\|F_N\|_2 . \end{gathered} 	ag{27} \] Every functional and scalar is the original one. The complementary source has been projected back to its full canonical polynomial space before applying that functional. No cutoff is commuted through a vertex, and no new cap replaces the marked closing. This assertion concerns the base source and its activity-independent insertion weights. An angular-jet closing must retain its own literal functional and parity; (25) is not a prescription to evenize an arbitrary differentiated closing. ## 7. Scope and complete sources The exponential bound applies to the real unitary phase space of the full free incidence variables. There is no alias identification, discarded channel endpoint, or artificial finite output compression. The full marked vertex operations and their normal coordinates remain the original closing \(\Lambda_N\) of [A], with its full phases, turns, reductions and scalars. The proved closing estimate is (27) for that specific compiler and its canonical incidence norm; a different compiler requires its actual adapter. This Fourier norm is not identified with the original ordinary-color Plancherel energy. The estimate is an exponential real complementary-region bound for the actual pre-gluing source class, with the source-relative marked remainder (27). The retained contribution still needs a nonzero coherent lower estimate, and the pre-gluing norm still needs its geometric rate. Neither (5) nor (27) selects a complex hyperbolic characteristic or a nonzero geometric-cycle coefficient, or proves a lower bound after arbitrary short fillings. Moving-quantum-parameter jets and conversions to Casimir normals at parabolic angles are not inferred from normalized angular jets. The complete proof inputs are [A], [the 302-line algebraic characteristic bound](research_same_index_edge_fourier_characteristic_bound.md), SHA256 2e5788e51a5586966b53f0eb5a864b83415c134a083de939fca141cc7ae434ee; and [F], the complete 227-line original source papers/circle-tree-asymptotics/finite-bounds.tex, e4cf66544703af6d9a78208deae971c4d9f4367ba4b2ad660694ee489ef67ea1. The adjoint iteration, complex test bound, and matrix extension needed here are all proved above. Complete comparison texts, retained at their matching pins, are papers/circle-tree-asymptotics/edge-packet.tex (268 lines), 53eb6dbfbda3ca639db35911ed50947c29655840337f9d1f1ce909d435013dbb; notes/research_gaussian_frame_newton_transport.md (335 lines), b6ed7fa19097323f76b0b22fb4fc7361b9d4e52c3f19d17c12d94c6fff623af9; notes/research_finite_gabor_pointed_source_sewing.md (455 lines), 8a954f9f2bec9e0fc8971b08ea0ca493f712d4e2ace6bb9fc2c1fcf705699c37; notes/actual_pointed_a_bulk_agmon_energy.md (199 lines), df1bccf577f5732dd7697bf2ae03901077d63b48f85820544dba10395391effd; and notes/actual_pointed_a_interval_observability.md (215 lines), 2e35ceb58d9488b7b383bbce4af123243270ddeff86570eff8ac20efb010b136. No general novelty claim for analytic coherent-state methods is made. Only written mathematics and source-text/hash operations were used.
