title: A Fourier characteristic bound for the actual same-index edge source
text:
# A Fourier characteristic bound for the actual same-index edge source Private written proof, 23 November 2026. The actual same-index edge kernels satisfy a homogeneous, fixed-degree quantum-torus equation on their entire Laurent polynomials. An exact Gaussian analysis frame turns that equation into a quantitative bound: outside its real characteristic set, the normalized Fourier energy is at most \(C/(N\delta^2)\). The estimate also holds before vertex gluing for arbitrary coupled channel coefficients on any fixed graph. All Laurent coefficients and endpoint channels are retained. The norm here is the Fourier coefficient norm in separate incidence activities. It is not identified with a marked cap norm or a closed knot invariant. ## 1. The literal edge family and its equation Fix \[ N\ge2,\quad d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\qquad S_k=\prod_{j=1}^k2\sin(\pi j/N),\quad S_0=1. 	ag{1} \] The actual common Newton basis in [F] is \(e_k(X)=S_k^{-2}\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}(2\cos((2j+1)\pi/N)-X)\). Consequently its complete angular Laurent representative is exactly \[ B_k(z):=e_k(-z-z^{-1}) = rac{q^{-k^2}(-qz;Q)_k(-q/z;Q)_k}{S_k^2}, \qquad 0\le k\le d. 	ag{2} \] Indeed each paired factor on the right is \(q^{-(2j+1)}(1+q^{2j+1}z)(1+q^{2j+1}/z) =2\cos((2j+1)\pi/N)+z+z^{-1}\). No denominator in (2) vanishes. Write \(T_zf(z)=f(Qz)\), and put \[ a_z=1+qz,\quad b_z=1+q^{-1}/z,\qquad A_z=a_zT_z-b_z,\quad D_z=b_zT_z-a_z. 	ag{3} \] The two shifted products in (2) give the cleared identity \[ (a_z+Q^kb_z)B_k(Qz)=(b_z+Q^ka_z)B_k(z), \qquad A_zB_k=-Q^kD_zB_k. 	ag{4} \] For example, before clearing, their quotient is \((1+qQ^kz)b_z/[a_z(1+q^{-1}Q^k/z)]\). The denominator times \(B_k(Qz)\) is cleared in (4), so the proof includes its zeros, \(k=0\), \(k=d\), and both level parities. For arbitrary complex numbers \(\mu_0,\ldots,\mu_d\), define \[ K_N(z,y)=\sum_{k=0}^d\mu_k B_k(z)B_k(y),\qquad P_N=A_zD_y-D_zA_y. 	ag{5} \] The two terms in \(P_N[B_k(z)B_k(y)]\) agree by (4). Thus \[ P_NK_N=0 	ag{6} \] as an identity of full Laurent polynomials. It holds for arbitrary activity-independent insertion weights, and with any channel cutoff implemented by zero coefficients. No channel shift or partial summation has produced an endpoint current. The physical coefficients in [F] include \(\gamma_e(s)H_N(s)/W_k(s)\), with their prescribed orientation scalars. They are independent of both angular activities and hence are examples of (5), at every parameter where they are defined. The same assertion applies to finite Laurent coefficients of those weights: it does not require their positivity or a bound on their size. There is also a coupled version. For a fixed graph with \(E\ge1\) edges, give every edge two separate incidence variables \(z_e,y_e\), and allow any complex coefficient array: \[ F_N(\mathbf z,\mathbf y)= \sum_{\mathbf k\in\{0,\ldots,d\}^E} \mu_{\mathbf k,N}\prod_{e=1}^E B_{k_e}(z_e)B_{k_e}(y_e). 	ag{7} \] The coefficients may couple every channel and depend on the level and all nonangular source parameters. With \(P_{e,N}\) acting only on its own incidence pair, (4) proves \(P_{e,N}F_N=0\) for every edge. No independence of the edge coefficients is assumed. Every individual Laurent exponent in (7) lies between \(-d\) and \(d\). ## 2. An exact full-lattice Gaussian frame For a dimension \(n\ge1\), identify Laurent Fourier coefficients with \(f\in\ell^2(\mathbb Z^n)\). Fix \(\sigma>0\), let \[  egin{split} c_{N,n}&=(N/(\pi\sigma))^{n/4},\ (\mathcal F_Nf)(	heta,\xi) &=c_{N,n}\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z^n} e^{-|m-N\xi|^2/(2\sigma N)}e^{im\cdot	heta}f_m,\ d
u&= rac{d	heta}{(2\pi)^n}\,d\xi, \quad	heta\in\mathbb T^n,\quad\xi\in\mathbb R^n. \end{split} 	ag{8} \] First define this on finitely supported vectors. Integration in \(	heta\) removes cross terms, and \[ c_{N,n}^2\int_{\mathbb R^n} e^{-|m-N\xi|^2/(\sigma N)}d\xi=1. \qquad \int|\mathcal F_Nf|^2d
u=\|f\|_2^2. 	ag{9} \] This extends \(\mathcal F_N\) isometrically to the full lattice. The centers range over all of \(\mathbb R^n\); they are not cut off at a finite Fourier support boundary. The frame principle is the same elementary resolution already used in [G], with a full lattice here rather than a finite Newton interval. Let \(Z_j\) mean multiplication by the \(j\)-th Laurent variable, so \((Z_jf)_m=f_{m-e_j}\), and let \((T_jf)_m=Q^{m_j}f_m\). Both are unitary on the full lattice. For integer vectors \(a,b\), set \(z^a=e^{ia\cdot	heta}\), \(Y^b=e^{2\pi ib\cdot\xi}\). The following errors have exact norms: \[  egin{split} \|\mathcal F_N Z^af-z^a\mathcal F_Nf\|_{L^2}^2 &=2(1-e^{-|a|^2/(4\sigma N)})\|f\|_2^2,\ \|\mathcal F_N T^bf-Y^b\mathcal F_Nf\|_{L^2}^2 &=2(1-e^{-\pi^2\sigma|b|^2/N})\|f\|_2^2. \end{split} 	ag{10} \] For the first identity, reindex \(m\mapsto m+a\) and integrate the squared difference of two translated real Gaussians. Their normalized overlap is \(e^{-|a|^2/(4\sigma N)}\). For the second, angular integration leaves \(|Q^{b\cdot m}-e^{2\pi ib\cdot\xi}|^2\) against the squared window. Its Gaussian characteristic function is \(e^{-\pi^2\sigma|b|^2/N}\). These computations are independent of the lattice index and prove (10) for all \(f\). For a normal-ordered, fixed-degree quantum-torus polynomial \(P_N=\sum_{a,b}c_{ab,N}Z^aT^b\), define \(p_N(	heta,\xi)=\sum_{a,b}c_{ab,N}z^aY^b\). Assume its finite exponent set and coefficient bounds are uniform. Applying (10) first to \(Z^aT^bf\), then to \(T^bf\), and summing gives \[ \|\mathcal F_N(P_Nf)-p_N\mathcal F_Nf\|_{L^2} \le C_{P,\sigma}N^{-1/2}\|f\|_2. 	ag{11} \] All noncommutative ordering phases stay in the coefficients \(c_{ab,N}\). The proof uses full shifted output vectors, without a finite compression. ## 3. The actual real characteristic bound For (5), its exact left-ordered expression and symbol are \[  egin{gathered} c_{1,N}=a_zb_y-b_za_y,\qquad c_{2,N}=b_zb_y-a_za_y,\ P_N=c_{1,N}(T_zT_y-1)+c_{2,N}(T_z-T_y),\ p_N=c_{1,N}(z,y)(Y_zY_y-1)+c_{2,N}(z,y)(Y_z-Y_y). \end{gathered} 	ag{12} \] On the frame phase space, \(|z|=|y|=|Y_z|=|Y_y|=1\). The coefficient bounds and exponent set are absolute, uniformly for every \(N\ge2\). As \(q	o1\), the symbol differs by \(O(N^{-1})\) uniformly from \[ p_0=  rac{(1+z)(1+y)}{zy} \{(z-y)(Y_zY_y-1)+(1-zy)(Y_z-Y_y)\}. 	ag{13} \] The prefactor in (13) is retained. In particular its zeros at \(z=-1\) or \(y=-1\) are part of this characteristic set. No division by that factor is used. Apply (11) to the exact null vector (6), and use (9) to replace \(p_N\) by \(p_0\). This proves, without a source hypothesis, \[ \int|p_0|^2|\mathcal F_NK_N|^2d
u \le rac{C_\sigma}{N}\|K_N\|_2^2, \quad \int_{\{|p_0|\ge\delta\}}|\mathcal F_NK_N|^2d
u \le rac{C_\sigma}{N\delta^2}\|K_N\|_2^2 \quad(\delta>0). 	ag{14} \] Here \(n=2\). The norm is exactly the full Laurent coefficient norm. The constant is independent of all coefficients \(\mu_k\). If the kernel is zero, the same inequalities hold trivially. For (7), use \(n=2E\), and let \(p_{e,0}\) be (13) on its edge coordinates. Tensoring the frame calculations, or applying (10) in those two coordinates only, gives \[ \int\sum_{e=1}^E|p_{e,0}|^2|\mathcal F_NF_N|^2d
u \le rac{C_\sigma E}{N}\|F_N\|_2^2. 	ag{15} \] In particular the mass on \(\{\max_e|p_{e,0}|\ge\delta\}\), outside the common \(\delta\)-characteristic neighborhood, is at most \(C_\sigma E/(N\delta^2)\) times the full mass. This holds for arbitrary entangled channel weights, not only products of independent edge kernels. ## 4. Normalized angular jets retain their forcing Let \(\mathscr D_j=z_j\partial_{z_j}\), including every incidence variable, and let \(\mathcal A\) be a fixed finite downward-closed set of multiindices containing zero. Define the actual jet vectors \[ u_\alpha=N^{-|\alpha|}\mathscr D^\alpha F_N, \qquad\alpha\in\mathcal A. 	ag{16} \] Since each Fourier exponent of (7) is in \([-d,d]\), \(\|u_\alpha\|_2\le\|F_N\|_2\). These derivatives do not automatically satisfy the homogeneous equation. The exact product rule, because every \(\mathscr D_j\) commutes with the shifts, is \[ P_{e,N}u_\alpha= -\sum_{ eta<\alpha} inom\alpha eta N^{-(|\alpha|-| eta|)} (\mathscr D^{\alpha- eta}P_{e,N})u_ eta. 	ag{17} \] Here \( eta<\alpha\) means componentwise inequality and inequality somewhere, and \(\mathscr D^\gamma P\) differentiates its coefficients only. Every resulting fixed-degree operator has uniformly bounded norm. Thus the right side of (17) is \(O(N^{-1})\) as an operator on the fixed direct sum of predecessor jets. Applying (11) to each jet, including that residual, proves \[  egin{split} \int\sum_e|p_{e,0}|^2 \sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal A}|\mathcal F_Nu_\alpha|^2d
u &\le rac{C_{\sigma,\mathcal A}E}{N} \sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal A}\|u_\alpha\|_2^2. \end{split} 	ag{18} \] Its off-characteristic version has the additional factor \(\delta^{-2}\). All jet coordinates and their commutator forcing remain. This is not an assertion about moving-quantum-parameter derivatives or an automatic conversion of angular derivatives to Casimir normals at parabolic angles. ## 5. What remains at the original gluing The fixed graph and arbitrary coefficient array in (7) give a broad pre-gluing source class, including physical insertions and retained low or high channel sums. The actual vertex operations in [F] still identify incidence activities, multiply by their prescribed crossing polynomials, reduce in their proper relations, and apply the original marked functionals. Those operations, with all their scalar factors, remain the original closing map \(\Lambda_N\); none is replaced by the positive Fourier norm above. In particular (15) does not commute a positive phase-space cutoff through \(\Lambda_N\), nor bound its effect on the complementary normal channels. No ordinary-color Plancherel energy is identified with this norm. The real variables in (8) describe a unitary torus phase space, not a complex hyperbolic critical chart. The estimates are polynomial concentration bounds, not exponential complementary gaps, a selected geometric cycle coefficient, or a scalar lower bound. They impose the explicit relation (13) on the full normalized source energy before those remaining operations. ## Complete inputs and coverage The sole complete original-source proof direct is [F], `papers/circle-tree-asymptotics/finite-bounds.tex` (227 lines), SHA256 `e4cf66544703af6d9a78208deae971c4d9f4367ba4b2ad660694ee489ef67ea1`. Its basis, edge weights, and full marked source are used above. All new finite identities and Gaussian estimates are proved inline. Complete comparison texts read are the companion `papers/circle-tree-asymptotics/edge-packet.tex` (268 lines), `53eb6dbfbda3ca639db35911ed50947c29655840337f9d1f1ce909d435013dbb`; [G], `notes/research_gaussian_frame_newton_transport.md` (335 lines), `b6ed7fa19097323f76b0b22fb4fc7361b9d4e52c3f19d17c12d94c6fff623af9`; `notes/research_finite_gabor_pointed_source_sewing.md` (455 lines), `8a954f9f2bec9e0fc8971b08ea0ca493f712d4e2ace6bb9fc2c1fcf705699c37`; `notes/actual_pointed_a_bulk_agmon_energy.md` (199 lines), `df1bccf577f5732dd7697bf2ae03901077d63b48f85820544dba10395391effd`; and `notes/actual_pointed_a_interval_observability.md` (215 lines), `2e35ceb58d9488b7b383bbce4af123243270ddeff86570eff8ac20efb010b136`. The Gaussian frame and off-characteristic method are standard; no novelty is claimed for that general calculus. The specific result here is its quantitative application to the exact edge source (5), the coupled source (7), and their retained angular jets. Only written mathematics and source-text/hash operations were used.

title: Saturated angular faces: reduced energy and matched signs
text:
# Saturated angular faces: reduced energy and matched signs Private written proof, 16 November 2026. The endpoint-face theorem already computes the energy of an original angular endpoint and characterizes its feasible deletion. This note assembles that result with the reduced-angle fiber problem and finite real-period compactness. The resulting identity is for the entire reduced energy on a compatible face, with arbitrary positive charges. At an actual finite-period limit, the sharp corner data give additional sign and incidence constraints. These specify the classical rate a genuine source reduction would have to produce. They do not identify an angular side current with a deleted quantum source. ## 1. The original charged face and its exact fiber Fix the original finite connected circle tree, a nonempty selected set \(S\), and all edges incident to \(S\), counted once. Outside angles are complete, and every selected vertex has positive original degree. Keep the original real powers \(n_v\) and positive real charges \(c_v\). In the integral filling convention \(n_v=\eta_v-2p_v\), neither the carrier nor the slope is changed. Write \[ t_v=s_v+i h_v,\qquad r_{v,e}=k_{v,e}+i g_{v,e},\qquad P_v=\sum_{e
i v}r_{v,e}-i n_vt_v/2. 	ag{1} \] The closed original angle body has \(|s_v|\leq\pi\), outside \(s_b=0\), and \[ |s_v|+2|g_{w,e}|\leq\pi,\qquad |s_w|+2|g_{v,e}|\leq\pi,\qquad \sum_{e
i v}g_{v,e}-n_vs_v/2=-\pi c_v\quad(v\in S). 	ag{2} \] Assume strict feasibility. Its energy and reduced energy are \[ \mathcal E_G=4\sum_e(E_{P,e}+E_{Q,e}),\qquad e_{G,c}(s)=\min_{g	ext{ satisfying }(2)}\mathcal E_G(s,g). 	ag{3} \] Only nonempty fibers are assigned a value. No uniqueness of a closed boundary fiber minimizer is asserted. Choose a nonempty set \(C\subseteq S\), signs \(\varepsilon_v=\pm1\), and set \(s_v=\varepsilon_v\pi\) on \(C\). Delete \(C\) and every incident edge; let \(r_C\) be the number of deleted edges, counted once. Write \(G'\) for the retained forest and \(c'=c|_{S\setminus C}\). Retain all surviving selected vertices, including isolated ones, with their original powers and rows. In particular, an isolated vertex must satisfy \[ n_ws_w=2\pi c_w,\qquad |s_w|\leq\pi. 	ag{4} \] It is not silently removed. The retained outside data remain complete. Define \(e_{G',c'}(s')\) by the same closed fiber minimization, with the sum over retained edges; this also covers a fiber with no edge variables if its remaining rows hold. **Proposition 1 (exact reduced face factorization).** The full fiber over \((\varepsilon\pi,s')\) is nonempty if and only if the retained fiber is nonempty and \[  oxed{\quad |\varepsilon_v n_v-2c_v| \leq L_v(s') :=\sum_{\substack{e=vw\w
otin C}} (1-|s_w|/\pi)\quad(v\in C). \quad} 	ag{5} \] For every such \(s'\), \[  oxed{\quad e_{G,c}(\varepsilon\pi,s') =r_C\pi M_\infty+e_{G',c'}(s'),\qquad M_\infty=4G_{m Cat}/\pi. \quad} 	ag{6} \] The surviving charge lifts in this identity are exactly \(c'\). Here \(G_{m Cat}=\sum_{\ell\geq0}(-1)^\ell/(2\ell+1)^2\). **Proof.** At an edge incident to \(v\in C\), (2) forces \(g_{w,e}=0\). Both incidences on an internal \(C\)-edge therefore vanish. Every restored incidence at a surviving vertex is zero, so its row is precisely its retained row, including (4). The remaining choices at a removed vertex are independent intervals \[ |g_{v,e}|\leq(\pi-|s_w|)/2\quad(w
otin C),\qquad \sum_{e=vw,\ w
otin C}g_{v,e} = rac{\pi}{2}(\varepsilon_v n_v-2c_v). 	ag{7} \] Their sum interval gives (5). Choices for different removed vertices are independent, even if they have a common surviving neighbor. Consequently the full fiber is exactly the product of the retained fiber and the interval-section polytopes (7). For clarity, the original square coordinates at an ordered edge are \[ A_P=s_v/4-g_{w,e}/2,\quad A_Q=s_v/4+g_{w,e}/2,\qquad y_P=g_{v,e}/2+s_w/4,\quad y_Q=g_{v,e}/2-s_w/4. 	ag{8} \] The archived endpoint-face computation gives the same value at every side and every corner: \[ E_\square|_{\partial[-\pi/4,\pi/4]^2} =G_{m Cat}/2=\pi M_\infty/8. 	ag{9} \] For example its normalization is \[ E_\square(\pi/4,0) = rac14\int_0^{\pi/2}\log(\sec u+	an u)\,du = rac12\int_{\pi/4}^{\pi/2}\log	an v\,dv =G_{m Cat}/2. 	ag{10} \] The side derivative is zero in the continuous boundary limit, and continuity joins the side values at all corners. Each deleted edge has both square factors on their boundaries by (8), hence contributes exactly \[ 4(E_{P,e}+E_{Q,e}) =4G_{m Cat}=\pi M_\infty. 	ag{11} \] Every retained square is unchanged. The energy is therefore the retained energy plus this constant on the entire product fiber. Taking minima proves (6). \(\square\) Proposition 1 is the charged reduced-fiber form of the existing endpoint-face theorem. The product proof does not require a matched complex limit or sharp corners. The same algebra remains valid for other specified real charges, including zero, whenever the displayed fibers are defined; it does not authorize changing a charge in the original finite source. ## 2. The uniform classical gap on this face Suppose additionally that the original positive solution at \(P=-\pi i c\) is supplied. Let \(z_0\) be its angle assignment, \(E_0=\mathcal E_G(z_0)\), and let \(m\) be the original number of edges. The reduced-angle theorem gives \[ \Delta_c=\min_{\partial\mathcal P_c}\mathcal E_G-E_0>0,\qquad M_G=mM_\infty-E_0/\pi. 	ag{12} \] The boundary is relative to the original affine charge rows. Because the original polytope has an interior point and every removed vertex has an incidence, every feasible face in Proposition 1 is on that boundary. Equations (6) and (12) give the uniform bound \[  oxed{\quad (m-r_C)M_\infty- rac{e_{G',c'}(s')}{\pi} \leq M_G-\Delta_c/\pi<M_G. \quad} 	ag{13} \] The same bound holds for any retained assignment in that fiber, since its energy is at least its fiber minimum. This is a definite positive gap depending only on the supplied original charged problem. It requires no condition \(|n_v|\geq2\). In place of that condition it requires the exact compatibility (5). If a retained assignment is a matched positive inverse-period point, its expression in (13) is its calibrated real charged action. Otherwise (13) is only its angle-energy value. Deleting the saturated vertices from a matched boundary point \(P=u-\pi i c\), as in Section 3 below, does not in general preserve the real periods: at a surviving vertex it removes the real returns \(k_{w,e}\). If the retained edges remain positive, the new period is \[ P'_w=\left(u_w-\sum_{\substack{e=wv\v\in C}}k_{w,e}ight) -\pi i c_w. 	ag{14} \] It need not have real part zero. For degenerate retained assignments no positive metric or stationary interpretation is assigned by (13). ## 3. Sharp finite-period saturation Now assume \(S\) is proper in the connected original tree, and take a bounded real-period sequence \(P(t^{(j)})=u^{(j)}-\pi i c\) of positive points tending to a finite image boundary. Pass to the joint finite limits supplied by the compactness theorem. Let \[ C=\{v\in S:|s_v|=\pi\},\qquad s_v=\varepsilon_v\pi, 	ag{15} \] and suppose \(C
e\varnothing\). This \(C\) includes all saturated vertices. Write \(d_0(v)\) for its number of edges from \(v\) to vertices outside \(C\), and \(d_{m in}(v)\) for its number of neighbors in \(C\). **Proposition 2 (matched corner signs).** Every cut neighbor \(w
otin C\) of \(C\) has \(s_w=0\). At a cut edge \(e=vw\), \[ g_{w,e}=0,\qquad g_{v,e}=	au_v\pi/2,\qquad \operatorname{sgn}k_{v,e}=\varepsilon_v,\qquad 	au_v=\operatorname{sgn}h_v\in\{-1,1\}. 	ag{16} \] Both incidences on internal \(C\)-edges are zero. Consequently \[  oxed{\quad \varepsilon_v n_v-2c_v=	au_v d_0(v).\quad} 	ag{17} \] In particular the capacity inequality (5) is saturated. **Proof.** The opposite incidence is zero by (2), so both \(A\)-coordinates in (8) equal \(\varepsilon_v\pi/4\). There are no open-side squares at a finite-period limit. Thus both \(y\)-coordinates are corners. Solving their two possible signs gives exactly \[ (s_w,g_{v,e})\in \{(0,\pi/2),(0,-\pi/2),(\pi,0),(-\pi,0)\}. 	ag{18} \] The last two alternatives put \(w\) in \(C\). At a sharp square corner the finite covectors satisfy \[ \operatorname{sgn}x=\operatorname{sgn}A,\qquad \operatorname{sgn}B=\operatorname{sgn}y,\qquad \sinh(2|x|)\sinh(2|B|)=1. 	ag{19} \] For a cut edge \(y_P=y_Q=g_{v,e}/2\). The original matching identities \[ k_{v,e}=x_P+x_Q,\qquad h_v=2(B_P+B_Q) 	ag{20} \] therefore give both signs in (16), strictly. The proper-selection observation bound also excludes \(h_v=0\) at every saturated vertex, including one with no cut edge: otherwise \(t_v=\pm\pi\) would make \(\cos(t_v/2)=0\). Thus \(	au_v\) is defined throughout \(C\). All cut incidences at a given vertex have the same sign. Summing the unchanged primitive row gives (17). \(\square\) At a cut neighbor \(s_w=0\) means \(t_w=i h_w\), not necessarily \(t_w=0\). Such a surviving selected vertex must not be relabeled as a complete outside vertex. If it becomes isolated after deletion, its unchanged row (4) and \(s_w=0\) force \(c_w=0\). Hence this cannot occur under the positive charges of the present theorem. For a separate zero-charge sector it is an actual remaining row obligation, not a license to discard the vertex or its finite trace. The limiting assignment minimizes its fixed-\(s\) fiber: it minimizes \(\mathcal E-u_*\cdot s\), whose second term is constant on that fiber. Proposition 1 therefore identifies its exact reduced energy with the deleted reduced energy. If (12) is available, (13) applies to this boundary value with the same charge lifts and gap. ## 4. The component sign and an arithmetic resonance restriction Retain the original edge root \(q_e\), rather than resetting its sign. The finite observation identities are \[ a_v=	an(t_v/2),\quad q_e^2=1+a_v^2+a_w^2,\qquad \cosh r_{v,e}=\cos(t_w/2)q_e. 	ag{21} \] At a cut edge, write \(a_v=i\coth(h_v/2)\) and \(a_w=i	anh(h_w/2)\). Thus \(q_e=iQ_e\), \(Q_e
e0\). Equations (16), (21), and \(\cos(t_w/2)=\cosh(h_w/2)>0\) give \[ \operatorname{sgn}Q_e=\varepsilon_v	au_v. 	ag{22} \] At an internal \(C\)-edge both tangent imaginary moduli exceed one, so \(|Q_e|>1\). Since \(g_{v,e}=g_{w,e}=0\), its two instances of (21), with \(\cos(t_v/2)=-i\varepsilon_v\sinh(h_v/2)\), give \[ \operatorname{sgn}Q_e =\varepsilon_v	au_v=\varepsilon_w	au_w. 	ag{23} \] Hence \(\sigma_C:=\varepsilon_v	au_v\) is constant on each connected component of \(C\). Internal edges never have \(q_e=\pm i\). Here is a consequence usable by a separate exact deck calculation. Fix \(v\in C\) and a nonempty set \(J_v\) of incident edges with \(q_e=\sigma_e i\), \(\sigma_e=\pm1\); put \(r_v=|J_v|\). They are cut edges, \(r_v\leq d_0(v)\), and every \(\sigma_e=\varepsilon_v	au_v\). Therefore \[ n_v+\sum_{e\in J_v}\sigma_e =\varepsilon_v\{2c_v+	au_v(d_0(v)+r_v)\}. 	ag{24} \] If a source calculation requires the left side to vanish, positivity of \(c_v\) forces precisely the necessary arithmetic conditions \[ 	au_v=-1,\qquad 2c_v=d_0(v)+r_v,\qquad n_v=\varepsilon_v r_v. 	ag{25} \] Moreover original strict feasibility implies \[ 2\pi c_v \leq |n_v||s_v^{m int}|+2\sum_{e
i v}|g_{v,e}^{m int}| <\pi(|n_v|+d_v) 	ag{26} \] at any supplied strictly feasible assignment. Substituting (25) and \(d_v=d_0(v)+d_{m in}(v)\) gives \[ d_{m in}(v)>0. 	ag{27} \] Thus an isolated saturated vertex cannot satisfy this resonance, even when only some of its incident wires have \(q=\pm i\). In particular all incidences cannot be escaping wires. At unit charge a remaining candidate has \(d_0(v)=r_v=1\), \(n_v=\varepsilon_v\), and at least one saturated neighbor. These are necessary conditions; no realization or global exclusion of the remaining candidates is claimed. Equation (24) is an arithmetic consequence of the original period rows, not by itself a finite-source deck identity. ## 5. What still requires the actual source The constant in (11), the exact reduced factorization (6), and the gap (13) are classical statements about the original angle problem. The archived one-step Ward current has its own exact physical-node support and retained coupons. A general angular side at \(t_v=\pm\pi+i h_v\), a wire-end residue, or a deck defect is not identified with that current by a shared limiting real angle. Their full Hermite normals, angular aliases, wire seams, and exterior contractions must still be retained. In particular, an energy comparison on a compatible deleted fiber does not bound the entire deleted quantum source or show that a given side current lands in that fiber. An unconstrained deleted forest may have other assignments failing (5). Nor does the sign restriction (25) imply that a nonresonant bulk term has a smaller whole-current rate. The result supplies an exact boundary rate and matching constraints for such a future reduction, without claiming an arbitrary-short-filling asymptotic or a nonzero cycle coefficient. ## Direct sources and author readback * [Endpoint-current angle face](research_endpoint_current_angle_face.md), SHA256 f84acb848b889a1553b467ba2d040884f7792a5ab0439eaada14a79216f363cc: original interval-section proof, exact square-boundary normalization, pointwise deleted-energy identity, and the distinction from actual finite current deployment. Complete source read in this sequence. * [Reduced-angle inverse-period graph](research_reduced_angle_inverse_period_graph.md), SHA256 9575d0231700e49e46ddea42c989921ce23adaafaa6e81b4f4b83c16f227f0af: closed fiber problem with arbitrary positive charges, strict feasibility, original calibrated action, and the fixed positive boundary gap. Complete source reread. * [Finite real-period compactness](research_real_period_image_compactness.md), SHA256 8ecdecc2c71e8a47a83fe60986ed618abaa926937920f376abebed779fb0c37e: finite matched sharp covectors, absence of open sides, retained matching identities and edge observations, and proper-selection observation units. Complete source reread. Only written mathematics, text reads and metadata hashes were used. No mathematical program, numerical calculation, test or compilation was run. Adopted notes, manuscripts and public documents were unchanged.

title: The scalar prefix kernel and the original first-meridian-jet source
text:
# The scalar prefix kernel and the original first-meridian-jet source Private written proof, 18 November 2026. The universal kernel in C loses its remaining-head Casimir dependence exactly. At a fixed primitive quantum root it is \[  oxed{\qquad \mathfrak h_N(k,\omega;M)= rac{D_N(M)}{D_N(Mk)},\qquad D_N(z)= rac{z^N-z^{-N}}{z-z^{-1}}. \qquad} 	ag{1} \] Here \(D_N\) is its Laurent-polynomial continuation at \(z=\pm1\), and (1) is a rational identity, not a prescription to evaluate an uncancelled denominator at a zero. For the actual common-meridian family, this gives an explicit first-jet formula for the original highest-cut, pivotal source. Its functional cost in the actual occupation basis is polynomial in \(N\) at fixed tensor width. Neither the constant coefficient nor its derivative is estimated here. The proof uses finite matrix paths, a finite product telescope, and polynomial interpolation; it imports no modified-trace theorem. The sole complete direct is C, pinned at the end. The moment argument and finite telescope were independently developed with Early; all calculations needed for the conclusion are included. ## 1. The universal kernel and its two-head realization Fix \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\). Keep \(q\) fixed throughout. A head with meridian \(M_i\) has \[ K_iw_a=x_iQ^{-a}w_a,\quad x_i=-M_i/q,\qquad F_iw_a=(1-Q^{a+1})w_{a+1},\qquad E_iw_a=(M_iQ^{-a}-M_i^{-1})w_{a-1}. 	ag{2} \] The outward endpoint arrows vanish. We write \(E_i\) for C's scaled lowering operator \(\mathcal E_i\). The head Casimir is \(\omega_i=q x_i+q^{-1}x_i^{-1}=-M_i-M_i^{-1}\). For an ordered tensor prefix, C gives the analytic triangular operator \(S\), preserving the total Cartan, such that \[ S^{-1}F_\Sigma S=F_1,\qquad S^{-1}E_\Sigma S=E_{m r}+L_1b_A,\qquad b_j=MK_{m r}Q^{-j}-M^{-1}K_{m r}^{-1}, 	ag{3} \] where \(M=M_1\). An actual total intertwiner \(W\) has \[ S^{-1}WS=\sum_{n=0}^dF_1^n\otimes B_n,\qquad [K_{m r},B_0]=0,\qquad B_n=- rac{b_n^{-1}[E_{m r},B_{n-1}]}{1-Q^n} 	ag{4} \] where these inverses exist. Its original pointed source is \[ \Phi_0(W)=\operatorname{Tr}((P_0\otimes K_{m r}^{1-N})W) =\operatorname{Tr}_{m r} \left(K_{m r}^{1-N}\sum_{n=0}^d x_1^{-n}F_{m r}^nB_night). 	ag{5} \] The cut and pivot in (5) are the original ones, with no additional pivot on the opened head. For reference, the scalar kernel of C is defined as follows: \[ u(k,\omega)=\omega-qk-q^{-1}k^{-1},\qquad b_j(k)=MkQ^{-j}-M^{-1}k^{-1},\qquad a_{n,n}(k,\omega)=Q^{-n}k^{1-N}, 	ag{6} \] \[ a_{n,j-1}(k,\omega)= rac1{1-Q^j} \left\{  rac{u(Q^{-j}k,\omega)a_{n,j}(k,\omega)}{b_j(k)} - rac{u(k,\omega)a_{n,j}(Qk,\omega)}{b_j(Qk)} ight\},\quad j=n,\ldots,1, 	ag{7} \] \[ \mathfrak h_N(k,\omega;M)=\sum_{n=0}^d x_1^{-n}a_{n,0}(k,\omega). 	ag{8} \] It is rational in \(k,M\) and polynomial of degree at most \(d\) in \(\omega\). With the full remaining Casimir \(\Omega_{m r}=F_{m r}E_{m r}+qK_{m r}+q^{-1}K_{m r}^{-1}\), the exact source functional is \[ \Phi_0(W)=\operatorname{Tr}_{m r}  ig(\mathfrak h_N(K_{m r},\Omega_{m r};M)B_0 ig). 	ag{9} \] We will use (9) on two heads with independent generic meridians. This does not require extending C's common-meridian pole claim. Indeed (3)--(5) hold with independent meridians, and the adjoint of the recursion in (4), for the ordinary trace pairing, is \[ A\longmapsto rac{[E_{m r},A b_j^{-1}]}{1-Q^j}. 	ag{10} \] Using \(FE=u(K,\Omega)\), \(EF=u(Q^{-1}K,\Omega)\), and the weight relations in this adjoint gives precisely (6)--(9). Thus (9) holds on the generic two-parameter set where the displayed denominators are nonzero. These are finite rational matrix identities in independent nonzero \(M_1,M_2\), so they extend algebraically beyond an initial neighborhood of one. No Borel continuation or source-cycle transport is used when an auxiliary second color is moved around its root orbit. ## 2. Closed first-head paths and the pivotal moments Take a second head whose highest Cartan value is an independent \(k_0
e0\), so \(M_2=-qk_0\) and \(\omega_2=qk_0+q^{-1}k_0^{-1}\). Write \(K=K_2\). The ordered coproducts are \[ F_\Sigma=F_1+K_1^{-1}F_2,\qquad E_\Sigma=E_1K_2+E_2,\qquad K_\Sigma=K_1K_2. \] Expanding the actual total Casimir and collecting only commuting head factors gives \[ \Omega_\Sigma =K_1^{-1}\omega_2+  ig(\omega_1-(q+q^{-1})K_1^{-1} ig)K +F_1E_2+K_1^{-1}E_1F_2K. 	ag{11} \] All endpoint rows remain those of (2). For every \(0\le p\le d\), the first-head highest block \(\langle0|\Omega_\Sigma^p|0angle\) is a polynomial in \(K\) of degrees \(0,\ldots,p\). Its coefficient of \(K^p\) is independent of \(\omega_2\) and \(k_0\). Here is a finite path proof, including the degree assertion. Set \(X=E_2\), \(Y=F_2K\). The tail letters satisfy \[ KX=QXK,\qquad KY=Q^{-1}YK, \] \[ XY=u(Q^{-1}K,\omega_2)K,\qquad YX=Q\,u(K,\omega_2)K. 	ag{12} \] Both products in (12) are polynomials in \(K\) of degrees zero through two, with their degree-two coefficient independent of \(\omega_2\). A nonzero first-head path from occupation zero back to zero has equally many upward and downward steps, say \(r\) of each. Its remaining \(p-2r\) steps are diagonal. Move their tail polynomials through \(X,Y\) by the weight relations. Every balanced word in \(X,Y\) has an adjacent opposite pair. Removing such pairs with (12) inductively gives a polynomial of degree at most \(2r\), with no negative powers. The diagonal factors add degree at most \(p-2r\). To reach degree \(p\), every factor must contribute its top degree, whose coefficient contains no \(\omega_2\). All first-head path coefficients depend only on \(M,q\). Forbidden paths are simply zero, so no endpoint correction is removed in this argument. Since the second-head eigenvalues are \(k_0Q^{-a}\), \[ \operatorname{Tr}(K^{1-N+j})=0\quad(0\le j<d),\qquad \operatorname{Tr}(K^{1-N+d})=N. 	ag{13} \] Consequently the original source moments satisfy \[ \Phi_0(\Omega_\Sigma^p)=0\quad(0\le p<d),\qquad \Phi_0(\Omega_\Sigma^d)=C_N(M), 	ag{14} \] where \(C_N(M)\) is independent of the second-head meridian. No positive or cyclic replacement of the original source was used: (13) is the literal pivotal trace of the highest block. ## 3. Lagrange coupons and the exact phase factor Put \[ k_a=k_0Q^{-a},\quad z_a=Mk_a,\quad \lambda_a=-z_a-z_a^{-1},\qquad 0\le a<N, \] \[ P(t)=\prod_{a=0}^d(t-\lambda_a). 	ag{15} \] Work first where these \(N\) values are distinct. Let \[ f_a(t)= rac{\prod_{b
e a}(t-\lambda_b)}{P'(\lambda_a)}. 	ag{16} \] The actual coupon \(W_a=f_a(\Omega_\Sigma)\) is an intertwiner. In the \(S\) coordinates the Casimir is \[ S^{-1}\Omega_\Sigma S =F_1E_2-I\otimes(MK+M^{-1}K^{-1}). 	ag{17} \] Therefore its constant coefficient is \(B_0=f_a(-MK-M^{-1}K^{-1})=|aangle\langle a|\). Equation (9), and separately the leading coefficient of (16) with (14), give \[ \mathfrak h_N(k_a,\omega_2;M) =\Phi_0(W_a)= rac{C_N(M)}{P'(\lambda_a)}. 	ag{18} \] The remaining-head projector has ordinary trace one; there is no additional factor \(N\) in (18). The derivative in (18) has a direct product evaluation. Since the \(z_b\)'s run around the roots with common \(N\)-th power, \[  egin{split} P'(\lambda_a) &=(-1)^d\prod_{b
e a}(z_a-z_b) \prod_{b
e a}(1-z_a^{-1}z_b^{-1})\ &=(-1)^d N z_a^{N-1}  rac{1-z_a^{-2N}}{1-z_a^{-2}} =(-1)^d N D_N(z_a). \end{split} 	ag{19} \] The calculation is initially on its generic domain and hence holds by rational continuation. It fixes the phase as well as the magnitude. ## 4. The finite telescope and polynomial interpolation Evaluate (7) at \(\omega_0=qk+q^{-1}k^{-1}\). Then \(u(k,\omega_0)=0\), so every second term in the downward recursion at that fixed \(k\) vanishes. Direct factorization gives \[  rac{u(Q^{-j}k,\omega_0)}{(1-Q^j)b_j(k)} =x_1\, rac{1-k^2Q^{1-j}}{1-M^2k^2Q^{-j}}. 	ag{20} \] Put \(r=Q^{-1}\), \(a=k^2\), \(b=M^2k^2r\), and use \((a;r)_n=\prod_{j=0}^{n-1}(1-ar^j)\). Equations (6)--(8) become \[ \mathfrak h_N(k,\omega_0;M) =k^{1-N}\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}r^n  rac{(a;r)_n}{(b;r)_n}. 	ag{21} \] This sum telescopes without an infinite-series identity. For \(T_n=(a;r)_n/(b;r)_n\) and \(U_n=(1-br^{n-1})T_n\), including \(U_0=1-b/r\), \[ U_{n+1}-U_n=r^n(b/r-a)T_n,\qquad T_N= rac{1-a^N}{1-b^N}. 	ag{22} \] As \(r^N=1\), \(U_N=(1-b/r)T_N\). Summing (22) and substituting the parameters in (21) gives \[ \mathfrak h_N(k,\omega_0;M) =k^{1-N} rac{(1-b/r)(T_N-1)}{b/r-a} = rac{D_N(M)}{D_N(Mk)}. 	ag{23} \] All intermediate divisions are made generically; the resulting identity is rational, including the removable parameter values. Apply (23) to (18) with \(a=0\), so \(k=k_0\), and use (19). It follows that \[ C_N(M)=(-1)^d N D_N(M). 	ag{24} \] Thus (18) proves the desired value for every weight of every generic second head. Finally fix independent generic \(k,M\). For each \(a\) choose the second-head highest value \(k_0=Q^a k\). Its weight \(a\) is \(k\), and its Casimir is \[ \omega_a=qQ^a k+q^{-1}Q^{-a}k^{-1}. 	ag{25} \] These \(N\) numbers are distinct for generic \(k\): equality for different labels requires a fixed exceptional value of \(k^2\). The polynomial in \(\omega\) in (8) has degree at most \(N-1\), and (18),(24) give the same claimed value at all \(N\) nodes (25). Polynomial interpolation proves (1) over the rational function field in \(k,M\), hence identically. There is no assumption about a scalar or semisimple remaining Casimir in this conclusion. Evaluating this rational-polynomial identity at the commuting matrices \(K_{m r},\Omega_{m r}\) retains all their weight multiplicities and Casimir Jordan blocks. ## 5. The common-meridian first-jet row Return to \(m\ge1\) actual heads with common meridian \(M\), and an analytic family \(W(M)\) of total intertwiners. Set \[ K_0=K_{m r}(1),\qquad K_{m r}(M)=M^{m-1}K_0,\qquad \varepsilon=(-1)^{(N+1)(m-1)}. 	ag{26} \] The empty remaining tensor has \(K_0=I\) and \(\varepsilon=1\). The actual root weights give \((MK_{m r})^N=\varepsilon M^{mN}I\). Combining (1) and (9) gives, on a punctured meridian disk, \[  oxed{\quad \Phi_0(W(M))=  rac{D_N(M)} {\varepsilon(M^{mN}-M^{-mN})} \operatorname{Tr}_{m r}  ig((MK_{m r}-M^{-1}K_{m r}^{-1})B_0(M) ig). \quad} 	ag{27} \] This is the original source, not a new normalization. Its left side is analytic. The denominator has a simple zero at one, where \(D_N(1)=N\), so admissibility forces the exact residue row \[ \operatorname{Tr}_{m r} ((K_0-K_0^{-1})B_0(1))=0. 	ag{28} \] The removable value of (27) is consequently \[  oxed{\quad \Phi_0(W(1))=  rac1{2\varepsilon} \operatorname{Tr}_{m r}((K_0+K_0^{-1})B_0(1)) + rac1{2\varepsilon m} \operatorname{Tr}_{m r}((K_0-K_0^{-1})B_0'(1)). \quad} 	ag{29} \] Indeed the derivative of the denominator in (27) is \(2\varepsilon mN\); differentiate its trace numerator using (26). Equation (28) removes every term involving the derivative of \(D_N\) or the regular part of the scalar prefactor. Both the sign \(\varepsilon\) and the factor \(m\) are retained. For \(m=1\), (29) reduces to the scalar value of \(B_0\), as it should. The derivative in (29) is that of the actual constant coefficient of \(S(M)^{-1}W(M)S(M)\). It includes the meridian dependence of the entire triangular transform. An arbitrary pair of matrices called \(B_0,B_0'\) need not satisfy (28) or the other exact intertwiner conditions in C. Equip the actual remaining occupation basis in (2) with its standard \(\ell^2\) norm. At the complete root \(K_0\) is diagonal unitary, and the remaining dimension is \(N^{m-1}\). The elementary bound \(|\operatorname{Tr}(AB)|\le N^{m-1}\|A\|\|B\|\) and \(\|K_0\pm K_0^{-1}\|\le2\) give \[  oxed{\quad |\Phi_0(W(1))| \le N^{m-1} ig(\|B_0(1)\|+m^{-1}\|B_0'(1)\| ig). \quad} 	ag{30} \] This controls the cost of the explicit functional in that original basis. It bounds neither these two source matrices nor the condition number of \(S\). Any separately prescribed external framing or peripheral scalar multiplies the original functional unchanged and must also be retained in its bound. ## 6. Source and normal scope The collapse (1) is a universal rational identity for C's kernel. Equations (27)--(30) apply to its actual analytic common-meridian intertwiner families at fixed \(q_N\). Inserted marks that fail to commute with the total generators retain their Ward defects; they are not declared homogeneous intertwiners to use this reconstruction. On a whole quantum-normal germ, C instead retains \(S^{-1}F_\Sigma S=F_1+J_N\), whose \(q\)-normal need not vanish. The whole source, cut, pivotal and framing adapters must be differentiated before any such specialization. The root-meridian identities above are not ordinary-color closed-source quantum-normal identities. No knot-word estimate, source noncancellation, framing-cycle pushforward, or nonzero geometric coefficient follows from (29) or (30). The new conclusion is the exact Casimir-free kernel and its explicitly controlled first-meridian-jet functional for the original pointed source. ## Complete direct-source pin * C: notes/research_prefix_commutant_and_pointed_normal_functional.md, SHA256 b4fb801a1482316aebb4799f1d0b80d5b43ced39138d903c04cfde811ca166b0.
