# A single spectral representative on short physical windows Private written proof, 16 November 2026. The common positive-product baseline has exponentially small errors in its actual physical value and normal data. On sufficiently short windows, ordinary spectral Hermite interpolation repairs those errors throughout the fixed complex product domain. Its exponential cost tends to zero with the number of rows divided by the level. This gives one separately even representative with the original action bound on both angular sides. Its closed window trace has no real repair interface. This does not remove exterior window sides. Adjacent choices have exponentially small normalized differences, whose actual shared spectators must still be included in any estimate of the seam. ## 1. The baseline and its spectral symmetry Fix a positive pair and the symmetric buffered product domains of the pinned product-gluing theorem. Work on a fixed smaller product, retaining a larger symmetric product for every estimate. All these choices precede the level \(N\). Write \[ z=-2\cos t,\qquad w=-2\cos u,\qquad \psi(t,u)=\psi(-t,u)=\psi(t,-u). 	ag{1} \] The phase is the original one, on its single branch from completeness. Let \(H_N(t,u)\) be the phase-normalized common baseline: \[ U_N=e^{N\psi}H_N,\qquad \sup_K|H_N|\le e^{o_K(N)} . 	ag{2} \] The bulk seed intervals are chosen inside the small complete disk, as in the pinned fold extension. Its complete-disk comparison gives \[ H_N-e^{-N\psi}K_N(-2\cos t,-2\cos u)=O(e^{-cN}) 	ag{3} \] on a fixed smaller complete bidisk, with all fixed buffered derivatives. Only in that bidisk is the canonical off-grid kernel used. **Lemma 1.** On every fixed smaller symmetric product compact, the separately even average \[ \overline H_N(t,u)= rac14 \sum_{\epsilon,\epsilon'\in\{1,-1\}} H_N(\epsilon t,\epsilon'u) 	ag{4} \] satisfies \(\overline H_N-H_N=O(e^{-c_KN})\), with fixed derivatives. It descends to a holomorphic function \(h_N(z,w)\) on the corresponding spectral product domain. The phase descends there to \(\Psi(z,w)\). **Proof.** Each reflection difference is exponentially small on the complete bidisk by (3), since the canonical kernel and phase are separately even. It is holomorphic and bounded by \(e^{o(N)}\) on every buffered compact of the common symmetric product by (2). The finite complex-ball propagation argument in the pinned fold extension therefore makes it exponentially small on any fixed smaller product compact. Averaging proves the first assertion. This is an estimate of the actual baseline's symmetry defect, not an assumed symmetry of a one-sided repair. Inside \(|\Re t|<\pi\), the fibers of \(-2\cos t\) are precisely the pairs \(t,-t\), except for their meeting at zero. The domains are symmetric. An even holomorphic function therefore descends; at zero its even Taylor series is holomorphic in \(z+2\). Apply this separately in both variables, also to the original even phase. Compact spectral subsets have buffered preimages in the angular domains, so spectral Cauchy estimates retain the stated bounds. \(\square\) Use the original physical nodes and relation \[ c_j=2\cos((2j+1)\pi/N),\quad 0\le j\le J_N=\lfloor(N-1)/2floor,\quad P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2,\quad \eta=(-1)^{N-1}. 	ag{5} \] A double node has multiplicity \(
u_j=2\). The last node at odd level is \(c_{J_N}=-2\) and has \(
u_{J_N}=1\). Let \[ F_j(w)=K_N(c_j,w),\qquad G_j(w)=\partial_zK_N(c_j,w) 	ag{6} \] and retain the pole-free representative \(\widehat G_j\) only at double nodes. It agrees with \(G_j\) in every required physical second-endpoint jet. There is no first spectral normal at the odd simple node. Choose fixed eligible real row intervals: either the bulk intervals of the product-baseline theorem or the fold neighborhoods of its pinned extension. On each such interval, those theorems and Lemma 1 give exponentially small normalized line errors, uniformly on a buffered compact in the other spectral variable. In spectral coordinates the targets are \[ T_{j,0}(w)=e^{-N\Psi(c_j,w)}F_j(w), 	ag{7} \] \[ T_{j,1}(w)=e^{-N\Psi(c_j,w)} \{\widehat G_j(w)-N\Psi_z(c_j,w)F_j(w)\}, \qquad 
u_j=2. 	ag{8} \] The errors \(T_{j,a}-\partial_z^a h_N(c_j,w)\), \(a<
u_j\), are \(O(e^{-cN})\). Define \(S_{k,b}(z)\) by exchanging the endpoints; their errors have the same conclusion after taking the smaller exponent. Every fixed derivative in the other spectral parameter is included. Conversion from angular normals near a double fold node costs at most a power of \(N\); the odd simple row is not divided by a vanishing angular derivative. The exponent \(c>0\), chosen to cover the finitely many value and first mixed errors used below, is fixed before selecting the short subwindows. ## 2. The quantitative finite spectral interpolation bound Let \(I_N=\{j_0,\ldots,j_0+m-1\}\) be consecutive distinct physical rows, and retain their original multiplicities. Put \[ Q_I(z)=\prod_{j\in I_N}(z-c_j)^{
u_j},\qquad q_j(z)= rac{Q_I(z)}{(z-c_j)^{
u_j}},\qquad \ell_j(z)= rac{q_j(z)}{q_j(c_j)}. 	ag{9} \] At a simple node define \(V_{j,0}=\ell_j\). At a double node define \[ V_{j,0}(z)= \{1-\ell_j'(c_j)(z-c_j)\}\ell_j(z),\qquad V_{j,1}(z)=(z-c_j)\ell_j(z). 	ag{10} \] These polynomials have degree less than \(\deg Q_I\) and satisfy \[ \partial_z^aV_{j,b}(c_k)=\delta_{jk}\delta_{ab}, \qquad a<
u_k,\quad b<
u_j . 	ag{11} \] Thus no additional derivative is imposed at a simple node. **Lemma 2.** On every fixed spectral compact, with fixed derivative order \(p\), the interpolation operator \[ \mathscr L_I d(z)= \sum_{j\in I_N}\sum_{a<
u_j}d_{j,a}V_{j,a}(z) 	ag{12} \] obeys \[ \|\partial_z^p\mathscr L_I d\| \le C_p N^{B_p} \exp\!\left\{C_Km\left(1+\log rac Nmight)ight\} \max_{j,a}|d_{j,a}|. 	ag{13} \] The constants are uniform over the location of the consecutive window, including windows meeting the fold. In particular, for \(m\le\delta N\), \(0<\delta<1/4\), its exponential cost is at most \[ \omega_K(\delta)N,\qquad \omega_K(\delta)=C_K\delta(1+|\log\delta|)\longrightarrow0. 	ag{14} \] **Proof.** For distinct physical indices \(j,k\), let \(d=|j-k|\). The exact cosine identity and their index range give \[ |c_j-c_k| =4\sin((j+k+1)\pi/N)\sin(d\pi/N) \ge4\sin^2(d\pi/N)\ge16d^2/N^2 . 	ag{15} \] Indeed \(d\le j+k+1\le N-d\) and \(d\le N/2\). For \(r=j-j_0\), it follows that \[ \prod_{\substack{k\in I_N\k
e j}}|c_j-c_k| \ge (16/N^2)^{m-1}\{r!(m-1-r)!\}^{\,2}. 	ag{16} \] Since all distances are at most four and each multiplicity is one or two, \[ |q_j(c_j)|\ge 4^{-(m-1)} \left(\prod_{k
e j}|c_j-c_k|ight)^2 . 	ag{17} \] On \(|z|\le R\), the numerator \(q_j(z)\) is bounded by \(\max(1,R+2)^{2(m-1)}\). Also \[ r!(m-1-r)!\ge (m-1)!/2^{m-1} \ge\{(m-1)/(2e)\}^{m-1}. 	ag{18} \] For \(m\ge2\), (16)--(18) bound \(\ell_j\) by \(\exp\{C_Rm(1+\log(N/m))\}\), after changing the constant. For \(m=1\), the cardinal polynomials are \(1\) and, when needed, \(z-c_j\), so the same conclusion holds directly. The remaining coefficient satisfies \[ |\ell_j'(c_j)| =\left|\sum_{k
e j} rac{
u_k}{c_j-c_k}ight| \le C N^2\sum_{d\ge1}d^{-2}\le C'N^2 . 	ag{19} \] Equations (10), (18)--(19), followed by the at most \(2m\) summands, give (13) for values. Cauchy on a fixed larger disk gives every fixed derivative with the same exponential rate. Finally \(x(1+\log(1/x))\) is increasing for \(0<x\le1\), so (14) follows. No separation assumption stronger than the actual grid has been used. \(\square\) ## 3. One exact representative on both sides Fix a buffered spectral product compact as in Section 1, enlarged within the same domains to contain the eligible real row intervals as well as the target. Let \(I_N\) and \(J_N'\) be consecutive subwindows of the eligible row intervals, with at most \(\delta_zN\) and \(\delta_wN\) distinct rows respectively. The window widths are fixed positive numbers, independent of \(N\), chosen only after the exponent \(c\) in Section 1. Require \[ \omega_z(\delta_z)+\omega_w(\delta_w)<c/4. 	ag{20} \] Use the interpolation bases (9)--(10) in each variable; write \(W_{k,b}(w)\) for the second basis. Set \[ d_{j,a}(w)=T_{j,a}(w)-\partial_z^ah_N(c_j,w),\qquad e_{k,b}(z)=S_{k,b}(z)-\partial_w^bh_N(z,c_k). 	ag{21} \] The actual full mixed physical jets give exactly \[ c_{jk}^{ab}:=\partial_w^bd_{j,a}(c_k) =\partial_z^ae_{k,b}(c_j), \quad a<
u_j,\ b<
u_k . 	ag{22} \] At a simple endpoint only the value index occurs. In particular (22) does not complete that endpoint by an artificial spectral normal. Define \[  egin{split} E_z(z,w)&=\sum_{j,a}d_{j,a}(w)V_{j,a}(z),\ E_w(z,w)&=\sum_{k,b}e_{k,b}(z)W_{k,b}(w),\ E_{zw}(z,w)&=\sum_{j,k,a,b}c_{jk}^{ab} V_{j,a}(z)W_{k,b}(w),\ \mathcal K_{I,J,N}(z,w) &=e^{N\Psi(z,w)} \{h_N(z,w)+E_z(z,w)+E_w(z,w)-E_{zw}(z,w)\}. \end{split} 	ag{23} \] Every coefficient function is defined on the buffered spectral parameter domain from Section 1; the polynomial bases introduce no extra poles. **Theorem 3.** On the entire fixed smaller spectral product compact, \[ e^{-N\Psi}\mathcal K_{I,J,N} =h_N+O(e^{-c'N}),\qquad |\mathcal K_{I,J,N}| \le \exp\{N\Re\Psi+o(N)\} 	ag{24} \] for some \(c'>0\), with all fixed buffered spectral derivatives of the normalized error. This holds on both angular sides, without a designated sign or a restriction to a thin opposite collar. Its exact line data are \[  egin{split} \mathcal K_{I,J,N}(c_j,w)&=F_j(w),& \partial_z\mathcal K_{I,J,N}(c_j,w)&=\widehat G_j(w) \quad(
u_j=2),\ \mathcal K_{I,J,N}(z,c_k)&=F_k(z),& \partial_w\mathcal K_{I,J,N}(z,c_k)&=\widehat G_k(z) \quad(
u_k=2). \end{split} 	ag{25} \] The angular pullback is separately even. **Proof.** The coefficients in (21)--(22) are \(O(e^{-cN})\), with the exponent fixed before (20). Lemma 2 controls \(E_z,E_w\); its two operator bounds control \(E_{zw}\). There are only polynomially many terms. Equation (20) leaves a positive exponential margin, proving (24), also on fixed derivative buffers. The baseline satisfies (2). At a first node, the first correction supplies its target error. By (11) and (22), the jets of \(E_w\) are exactly those of \(E_{zw}\) and cancel. The second-node argument is identical. Removing the normalizing exponential in (7)--(8) proves (25). These are identities as holomorphic functions of the other variable, not merely identities at isolated physical pairs. The spectral construction proves evenness. \(\square\) The small-window choice is essential to the argument: the exponential accuracy is established on a larger fixed row interval before its short subwindow is selected. No assertion makes that accuracy exponent independent of an interval simultaneously shrinking in its construction. For a fixed finite collection of such choices using the same \(h_N\), (24) also makes every normalized difference exponentially small on the common compact. The smallest of their finitely many positive exponents may be used. ## 4. Exact closed traces and the remaining boundary terms Let \(\gamma_I\) be a closed positive spectral contour enclosing just the selected first-window nodes, within the domain where (23) is defined. Keep an original spectral spectator \(P(z;\ldots)\), including all crossings, shared variables and its derivative. Then \[ \Phi^\sharp_{I,N}(w;\ldots) = rac{\eta N^2}{2\pi i} \int_{\gamma_I}  rac{P(z;\ldots)\mathcal K_{I,J,N}(z,w)}{P_N(z)}\,dz . 	ag{26} \] At a double node its contribution is exactly \[ \eta\{(4-c_j^2) [\widehat G_j(w)P(c_j)+F_j(w)P_z(c_j)] -c_jF_j(w)P(c_j)\}, 	ag{27} \] and an odd simple selected node contributes \(F_{J_N}(w)P(-2)\). These follow from the original relation: for a double node, \[ \left. rac{P_N(z)}{(z-c_j)^2}ight|_{z=c_j} = rac{N^2}{4-c_j^2},\qquad \left.\partial_z\log rac{P_N(z)}{(z-c_j)^2}ight|_{z=c_j} = rac{c_j}{4-c_j^2}, 	ag{28} \] whereas \(P_N'(-2)=N^2\) at odd level. For (28), evaluate \((4-z^2)P_N''-zP_N'+N^2(P_N-2)=0\) at a double root and differentiate it once. This gives \(P_N''(c_j)=2N^2/(4-c_j^2)\) and \(P_N'''(c_j)/P_N''(c_j)=3c_j/(4-c_j^2)\), which are exactly the two Taylor coefficients in (28). Thus (26) is the same sharp window expression as in the pinned sources. Its difference from the original free-\(w\) window trace is \(P_N(w)\) times a holomorphic slit function, and equality with the original follows after the required subsequent complete second trace, including every spectator normal. If both endpoints are traced on the selected windows, (22) gives the original double-window functional directly. No arbitrary unreduced free polynomial is replaced. For a centered mirror angular window, (26) equivalently has the prefactor \(-\eta/(4\pi^2i)\) against \[ D_h(X)\sin(2\pi X) P(C(X))\mathcal K_{I,J,N}(C(X),w)\,dX, \qquad D_h=(\pi N)^2\sec^2(\pi NX). 	ag{29} \] It uses the same function on the lower and upper halves. Consequently the real interface term is exactly zero. Both lifts of a double node and the single odd central value have the multiplicity proved in the fold source; no spectral normal is supplied at that center. This cancellation concerns the repair interface only. The closed contour still has all its exterior sides. If neighboring cells use different short-window representatives, their common side contains their actual difference. Equation (24) bounds that difference by \(\exp\{N\Re\Psi-c'N+o(N)\}\), but it must be multiplied by the entire original spectator, trace density, and any remaining factors. A larger real boundary action need not be paid by \(c'\). No seam is deleted without that further estimate. The selected windows may cover a supplied compact set of rows inside the eligible intervals by finitely many cells. This gives a finite family of compatible estimates; it does not assert one exact representative for the union with the same bound, a complete grid near \(t=\pm\pi\), or a controlled global filled cycle. In particular (25) prescribes only the selected short windows, not the full data of an entire periodic angular strip. ## Direct sources and author audit The proof uses these complete direct texts at their fixed versions: * [Common positive-product baseline](research_positive_product_window_gluing.md), SHA256 ace4f667038c494e2690a77496ce32e8bc8538535356b78600e8ad8ced8183d5: common bounded baseline, bulk line accuracy, exact mixed data, and the sharp-trace versus free-color distinction. * [Fold-window extension](research_positive_product_fold_window_extension.md), SHA256 3c37b5fbe1ec4c8d6ddc137fe22dcc43428c18f8a99203627bad7e5b64aead17: complete-disk comparison, uniform fold line accuracy and finite propagation, mirrored trace normalization and the odd simple value. The finite spectral interpolation estimate is proved directly here. Only written mathematics, source reads and metadata hashes are used. No mathematical program, numerical computation, test or compilation is run. Frozen notes and public manuscripts are unchanged.

title: Sublinear polynomial observations through fixed Conway words
text: # Sublinear polynomial observations through fixed Conway words Written research proof, 22 November 2026. For any fixed word of original signed crossings and turns, polynomial observations of sublinear Casimir degree retain the exponential norm rate of the transported coherent packet. Both the packet and the observation are transported. The input bidisc has a positive radius depending on the word, and the comparison is in the original Newton coefficient norm. The proof combines an exact generating-unit gauge identity with explicit finite-head extraction operators. No bound for the norm or condition number of the word is used. The transported packet can have a different rate from the untransported one. Its new rate and its original scalar closing are not evaluated here. ## 1. Original operations and the joint observation family Fix \[ N\ge2,\quad d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\quad s_j=2\sin(\pi j/N),\quad S_j=\prod_{r=1}^j s_r,\quad S_0=1, \] \[ c_j=qQ^j+q^{-1}Q^{-j},\quad c_0=q+q^{-1},\quad P_N(\zeta)=2T_N(\zeta/2)+2,\quad \mathcal H_N=\mathbb C[\zeta]/(P_N). \tag{1} \] Here \(T_N\) is the Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind. Give the original Newton basis \[ e_j(\zeta)=S_j^{-2}\prod_{r<j}(c_r-\zeta),\qquad 0\le j<N, \] its coefficient Euclidean norm. This retains the entire Hermite algebra, including its first spectral normals. It is not the uniform physical Hilbert--Schmidt metric. Let \(Z\) be multiplication by \(\zeta\), let \(J\) be the genuine turn, and write \(L=JZJ\). Their exact actions are \[ Ze_j=c_je_j-s_{j+1}^2e_{j+1},\quad Je_j=e_{d-j},\quad Le_j=c_je_j-s_j^2e_{j-1},\qquad \|Z\|,\|L\|\le6 . \tag{2} \] Missing end vectors are zero. The positive crossing is the original unit \(R\), with \(\kappa=q^{d^2/2}\), not a new phase surrogate. For each integer \(n\), put \[ L_n=R^{-n}LR^n. \tag{3} \] A fixed word \(W\) means a fixed finite product of \(J\)'s and integer powers of multiplication by \(R\). Its original scalar carriers remain included. Use the centered generating unit of the full-tensor theorem: \[ A_N(t,\zeta)=\sum_{a=0}^d p_a(\zeta)t^a,\qquad f_a=N^{-1/2}R\,p_a,\qquad \mathcal F_N(t)=N^{-1/2}R\,A_N(t,\zeta). \tag{4} \] Define the actual product packet \[ w_N(y,z)=\mathcal F_N(y)\mathcal F_N(z) =N^{-1}R^2A_N(y,\zeta)A_N(z,\zeta). \tag{5} \] It is a unit of the algebra when \(|y|,|z|<1\). Indeed the physical node products of \(A_N\) have all their zeros on \(|t|=1\), and nonzero values imply invertibility in each full local Artin factor. A common normalization of the two inputs does not change any ratio below. For a polynomial \(P\), the joint family is \(WP(Z)w_N\). It is not \(P(Z)Ww_N\). Write \(\|P\|_2\) for its ordinary monomial coefficient norm. ## 2. Uniformly bounded transported trace operators We first record explicitly the operator bounds needed below. The exact Newton matrix of \(L_1\) has entries \[ (L_1)_{jj}=4qQ^j-q(1+Q)Q^{2j},\qquad (L_1)_{j-1,j}=(L_1)_{j,j-1}=-(1-Q^j)^2. \tag{6} \] This is the full finite-band conjugation identity, including \(N=2\); it is obtained by conjugating its displayed tridiagonal matrix by the unitary \(J\). Thus \(\|L_1\|\le14\). There is also the divisor-free operator recurrence \[ L_{n+1}+qZL_n+q^2L_{n-1}=8qI \qquad(n\in\mathbb Z). \tag{7} \] Starting from \(L_0=L,L_1\), this bounds every fixed \(L_n\) uniformly in \(N\), in both directions. The exact conjugation identities are \[ JZJ=L,\quad JLJ=Z,\quad JL_1J=L_{-1},\qquad R^{-m}ZR^m=Z,\quad R^{-m}L_nR^m=L_{n+m}. \tag{8} \] All scalars in the original braid relation cancel in these conjugations. Equation (7) expresses each \(L_n\) as a noncommutative polynomial in \(Z,L,L_1\), with Laurent-polynomial coefficients in \(q\). Substitution in (8) therefore proves, for every fixed word and integer \(n\), \[ \|WZW^{-1}\|\le C_W,\qquad \|WL_nW^{-1}\|\le C_{W,n}, \tag{9} \] with constants independent of \(N\). The statement bounds these specified observables; it bounds neither \(W\) nor \(W^{-1}\). No positive adjoint relation for \(R\) is asserted. ## 3. Exact conjugation by a generating unit Let \(M_t\) be multiplication by \(A_N(t,\zeta)\), and put \(b_t(\zeta)=1+t\zeta+t^2\). For every \(|t|<1\) and integer \(n\), the exact full-algebra identity is \[ \boxed{\quad b_t(Z)M_tL_nM_t^{-1} =L_n-c_0tL_{n+1}+t^2L_{n+2}+8tI . \quad} \tag{10} \] We prove this with its original first normals and endpoint terms. Write \(\zeta(v)=v+v^{-1}\), and use the original rational difference coefficients \[ a(v)=-\frac{(qv-1)^3}{q(v^2-1)(qv+1)},\qquad \bar a(v)=a(v^{-1}),\qquad c_0+a(v)+\bar a(v)=\frac8{c_0+\zeta(v)}. \tag{11} \] The bar over \(a\) in this display means inversion of its argument, not coefficient conjugation. On spectral polynomials, \[ L_nf=(c_0+a+\bar a)f -a(v)(-qv)^n f(Qv) -\bar a(v)(-qv^{-1})^n f(Q^{-1}v). \tag{12} \] The combined expression is polynomial; its apparent poles have the original removable continuations. Its full quotient action is (3). For \(v_j=qQ^j\), \(0\le j<N\), the finite node products and their independently proved normals give, at each interior transition \(j<d\), the value and first lifted jet of \[ \frac{A_N(t,\zeta(Qv))}{A_N(t,\zeta(v))} =\frac{1+v^{-1}t}{1+Qvt}. \tag{13} \] For clarity, on the first half of the physical circle, \[ A_N(t,c_j)=D_j(t)^2B_j(t),\quad D_j(t)=\prod_{r=-j+1}^0(1+q^{-1}Q^rt),\quad B_j(t)=\prod_{r=j+2}^{N-j}(1+q^{-1}Q^rt), \] \[ \partial_\zeta A_N(t,c_j) =\frac{D_j(t)^2tB_j'(t)}{v_j-v_j^{-1}} . \tag{14} \] The normal is required only at double nodes. Multiplication by \(v_j-v_j^{-1}\) identifies the logarithmic \(v\)-derivative with \(tB_j'/B_j\). Removing the two end factors of \(B_j\) gives exactly the derivative of (13). The even middle pair has one \(B_j\) factor and reflected derivatives of opposite sign. The odd simple middle has \(B_j=1\) and lifted derivative zero. Inversion gives the second half. This proves the claimed interior jets without differentiating a discrete index interpolation. Set the cleared defect \[ F_t(v)=(1+Qvt)A_N(t,\zeta(Qv)) -(1+v^{-1}t)A_N(t,\zeta(v)). \tag{15} \] It has a double zero at each interior physical transition. At the forward seam \(v=q^{-1}\) no homogeneous first-normal extension of (13) is assumed. Instead \(a(v)\) has a cubic zero there. The backward seam \(v=q\) uses the cubic zero of \(\bar a(v)\). These zeros remove the seam defects and their first derivatives in (12). The coalescing coefficient poles need a separate check. For \(\iota(v)=Q^{-1}v^{-1}\), inversion symmetry of the actual polynomial gives the exact identity \[ F_t(\iota(v))=-F_t(v). \tag{16} \] At an even-level middle pole \(v=-q^{-1}\), this involution fixes \(v\). In the local logarithmic coordinate it changes the sign. The matched value and first jet in (13), together with (16), force a zero of order at least three. The simple pole of \(a\) therefore leaves a double zero, preserving the first spectral normal. The reflected pole is identical. At the odd physical fixed point \(v=-1\), the paired expression leaves a zero value; only that simple Casimir value is required. At \(N=2\), a seam and a middle pole coincide for different shifted terms; the cubic-zero and involution arguments apply to their respective terms. No exceptional level is omitted. We can now verify (10) after clearing \(M_t^{-1}\). Its forward shifted coefficient uses \[ b_t(\zeta)\frac{A_N(t,\zeta(v))} {A_N(t,\zeta(Qv))} =(1+vt)(1+Qvt). \tag{17} \] This equality has the full jets just justified when multiplied by the corresponding coefficient in (12). The factor on the right is \(1-c_0t(-qv)+t^2(-qv)^2\); hence it gives the three \(L\)'s on the right of (10). The backward term follows by inversion. Their diagonal coefficients differ by \[ [b_t(\zeta)-(1-c_0t+t^2)](c_0+a+\bar a)=8t. \] Thus the cleared difference has every original Hermite value and normal zero. Each combined side is polynomial, so it is divisible by \(P_N\), proving (10) in the entire quotient. Define the source-adapted operator \[ B_w=M_{w_N}L M_{w_N}^{-1}. \tag{18} \] Its scalar input normalization cancels. Since \(R^2LR^{-2}=L_{-2}\), applying (10) twice shows that \(b_y(Z)b_z(Z)B_w\) is a finite polynomial combination of \(L_{-2},\ldots,L_2,Z,I\), with coefficients polynomial in \(y,z,q,q^{-1}\). In particular all coefficients are bounded on compact input bidisks, independently of \(N\). For a fixed word, choose \(0<\rho_W<1\) so small that \[ \rho_W C_W+\rho_W^2\le\tfrac12 , \tag{19} \] where \(C_W\) bounds \(WZW^{-1}\) in (9). Then \(b_t(WZW^{-1})^{-1}\) has norm at most two for \(|t|\le\rho_W\), by its Neumann series. Conjugating the preceding cleared formula and using (9) gives \[ \boxed{\qquad \|WZW^{-1}\|+\|WB_wW^{-1}\|\le K_W, \qquad |y|,|z|\le\rho_W , \qquad} \tag{20} \] uniformly in \(N\). No norm of a generating unit or its inverse was estimated separately. ## 4. Polynomial extraction from the finite head The following construction is independent of the coherent inputs. Assume \(D\ge1\) and \(D\le N/32\), and put \(M=2D\). For \(0\le j\le M\), use the original kernel polynomial \[ K_j(\zeta)=\sum_{r=0}^j e_r(c_j)e_r(\zeta),\quad \ell_j=\frac{(-1)^jS_{2j}}{S_j^4},\quad g_j=K_j/\ell_j . \tag{21} \] Indeed \(e_r(c_j)=0\) for \(r>j\), and \(e_j(c_j)=S_{2j}/S_j^2\), so \(\ell_j\) is the leading coefficient. Thus \(g_j\) is monic of degree \(j\). The Newton recurrence immediately gives \(LK_j=c_jK_j\). The original physical kernel row gives the exact monic recurrence \[ \zeta g_j=g_{j+1}+\gamma_jg_j+\beta_jg_{j-1}, \quad \gamma_j=c_0+\frac{s_{j+1}^4}{s_{2j+1}s_{2j+2}} +\frac{s_j^4}{s_{2j}s_{2j+1}}, \] \[ \beta_j=\frac{s_j^8} {s_{2j-1}s_{2j}^2s_{2j+1}}>0. \tag{22} \] At \(j=0\) the last summands are zero and \(g_{-1}=0\). To see precisely why no kernel source was lost, the ordinary free-boundary equation for \(K_N(w,\zeta)\) has defect proportional to \(P_N(\zeta)e_d(w)\). At the physical row \(w=c_j\) used here, \(e_d(c_j)=0\) for \(j<d\). The remaining row coefficients are \[ a_j=\frac{s_{j+1}^4}{s_{2j+1}s_{2j+2}},\qquad b_j=\frac{s_j^4}{s_{2j}s_{2j+1}}, \] so \( \zeta K_j=(c_0+a_j+b_j)K_j-a_jK_{j+1}-b_jK_{j-1}\). Normalizing by \(\ell_j\) gives \(-a_j\ell_{j+1}/\ell_j=1\) and \(-b_j\ell_{j-1}/\ell_j=\beta_j\), proving (22). All rows used are strictly before the middle. The elementary sine bounds now imply uniform estimates \[ |\gamma_j|+\beta_j\le C,\qquad \beta_j\ge c(j/N)^4\quad(1\le j\le D),\qquad \|g_j\|_{\mathrm{coeff},1}\le C^j . \tag{23} \] The last assertion follows inductively from the monic recurrence. The indices in every denominator are at most \(4D+2<N/2\) in the range needed below, after harmlessly excluding finitely many initial levels. The constants are absolute. On polynomials of degree at most \(M\), \(L\) has the distinct eigenbasis \(g_0,\ldots,g_M\). Its exact filters are \[ F_j(L)=\prod_{\substack{0\le r\le M\\r\ne j}} \frac{L-c_r}{c_j-c_r}. \tag{24} \] Their scalar polynomial coefficient norm satisfies \[ \|F_j\|_{\mathrm{coeff},1} \le e^{CD}(N/D)^{4D}. \tag{25} \] Here are the needed uniform factorials. Since \(c_j-c_r=-s_{j+r+1}s_{j-r}\), \[ \prod_{r\ne j}|c_j-c_r| \ge(c/N^2)^M\frac{(M-j)!(M+j+1)!}{2j+1} \ge(c/N^2)^M\frac{(M!)^2}{2M+1}. \] The numerator coefficient norm in (24) is at most \(3^M\); \(M!\ge(M/e)^M\) proves (25). Expand a nonzero polynomial \(P\), of degree at most \(D\), as \(P=\sum_{j=0}^D a_jg_j\). Equation (23) gives an index \(j\) with \[ |a_j|\ge e^{-CD}\|P\|_2. \tag{26} \] The written operator order in the next identity is essential: \[ F_0(L)Z^jF_j(L)P(Z)1 =a_j\left(\prod_{r=1}^j\beta_r\right)1. \tag{27} \] The right filter first isolates \(a_jg_j\). In \(j\) steps of (22), the only path from index \(j\) to zero lowers at every step. Its coefficient is the displayed product. All intermediate degrees are at most \(2D=M\), so the final filter is exact. No high-degree quotient or uncontrolled complement enters this calculation. Moreover (23) and the factorial inequality imply \[ \left(\prod_{r=1}^j\beta_r\right)^{-1} \le e^{CD}(N/D)^{4D},\qquad 0\le j\le D . \tag{28} \] For \(j>0\), first bound this by \(e^{Cj}N^{4j}/(j!)^4\); then use the monotonicity of \(j\log(N/j)\) for \(j\le D\le N/32\). The empty product at \(j=0\) is one. Consequently there is an explicit noncommutative polynomial \(\mathscr A_{P,N}(Z,L)\) such that \[ \mathscr A_{P,N}(Z,L)P(Z)1=1,\qquad \deg\mathscr A_{P,N}\le5D,\qquad \|\mathscr A_{P,N}\|_{\mathrm{coeff},1} \le\frac{e^{CD}(N/D)^{12D}}{\|P\|_2}. \tag{29} \] It is exactly the left side of (27) divided by its nonzero scalar on the right. The three losses in (29) are the two filters, the inverse lower-path coefficient, and the factor in (26). They use only finite explicit source data. No singular-value decomposition or unspecified inverse is used. ## 5. The joint transported Gram bound Fix a word \(W\), and take \(\rho_W\) from (19). There are \(C_W<\infty\) and \(N_0\) such that, for \[ N\ge N_0,\quad 1\le D\le N/32,\quad |y|,|z|\le\rho_W,\quad \deg P\le D, \] the full original vectors obey \[ \boxed{\begin{aligned} &e^{-C_WD}(D/N)^{24D}\|P\|_2^2\,\|Ww_N\|^2\\ &\hspace{12mm}\le\|WP(Z)w_N\|^2 \le e^{C_WD}\|P\|_2^2\,\|Ww_N\|^2 . \end{aligned}} \tag{30} \] Constants do not depend on \(D,N,P,y,z\) in this range. For \(D=0\) both sides are exactly \(|P|^2\|Ww_N\|^2\). The zero polynomial is included trivially. For the lower bound conjugate (29) by the actual invertible operator \(\mathcal U=WM_{w_N}\). Since multiplication by \(w_N\) commutes with \(Z\), its two conjugated generators are \[ Z_{\mathcal U}=WZW^{-1},\qquad L_{\mathcal U}=WB_wW^{-1}. \tag{31} \] Their norms are bounded by (20). Thus the conjugated extraction operator has norm at most \(e^{C_WD}(N/D)^{12D}/\|P\|_2\). It maps \(WP(Z)w_N\) exactly to \(Ww_N\). Squaring the resulting inequality proves the lower bound. For the upper bound use \[ WP(Z)w_N=P(WZW^{-1})Ww_N \] and the uniform bound (9). The factor \(\sqrt{D+1}\) from coefficient Cauchy--Schwarz is absorbed in \(e^{C_WD}\). No condition number of \(\mathcal U\), \(W\), or \(M_{w_N}\) appears in this proof. In particular, if \(D_N=o(N)\) and \(P_N^{\rm obs}\) has degree at most \(D_N\) and coefficient norm one, then \[ \boxed{\qquad \frac1N\log \frac{\|WP_N^{\rm obs}(Z)w_N(y,z)\|^2}{\|Ww_N(y,z)\|^2} \longrightarrow0 \quad(|y|,|z|\le\rho_W). \qquad} \tag{32} \] The convergence is uniform on the displayed bidisc. Indeed \(D_N+D_N\log(N/D_N)=o(N)\). A nonzero scalar coefficient norm with logarithm \(o(N)\) may also be included by homogeneity. The denominator is the norm of the newly transported packet. Equation (32) does not say that it has the old packet's rate. For example \(w_N(0,0)=R^2/N\), while \(R^{-1}w_N(0,0)=R/N\) has squared Newton norm \(1/N\). The theorem compares observations of each such transported packet with that same packet, and is consistent with this change. ## 6. Original closing and complete proof sources Every operation in the argument is an identity on the full original algebra. The low polynomial head is used only to construct the extraction operator; its conjugate acts on the full transported packets. No physical normal or source direction has been declared invisible. The original marked row \(\ell_N\) may be applied unchanged. For example extraction gives the exact equality \[ \ell_N(Ww_N)= \ell_N\!\left[ \mathscr A_{P,N}(Z_{\mathcal U},L_{\mathcal U}) WP(Z)w_N\right]. \tag{33} \] It does not replace this row by a positive norm, or prove a lower bound for \(\ell_N(WP(Z)w_N)\). The action of the new packet and its specified scalar closing remain separate questions. The result concerns fixed linear words of crossings and genuine turns and a word-dependent small coherent input bidisc. It does not give a closed bounded lift through arbitrary branching subtrees. Nor does sublinear Casimir degree mean a bounded number of crossings or degree four of a variational objective. No new knot-volume identity or finite-exception theorem is asserted. All four complete matching proof sources were read: | Source | SHA-256 | |---|---| | [Full generating tensor, 482 lines](research_centered_fourier_full_tensor_source.md) | 8426410354feb509c2780e1207613899bda8ab5eb46ad22fd4ab008bf5841bf1 | | [Full crossing/AW transport, 1283 lines](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_current_free_aw_crossing_transport.md) | f81b9fc3edc2504c5250ad283bf0ceff191a1fc3a310c00fdb57602362f0bf4a | | [Finite-band conjugation, 730 lines](research_unit_turn_finite_band_branching_operator.md) | 31d9f574c7dc3aaac07e4eb50c131b3328be46b3c2a2ef46f9dae7f0c4ddb9cb | | [Full kernel difference source, 399 lines](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_edge_kernel_difference_and_endpoint_bound.md) | 5d0d07d4d97d82cca66e0e0c3bf2cecad8e5f58ef8329178278b297cf0d6c5da | The first supplies the exact generating unit and its physical value/normal products. The second supplies the full AW operators, their endpoint mechanism and exact word conjugation. The third supplies the verified tridiagonal base matrix in (6). The fourth supplies the original physical kernel row and its retained free source. The generating-unit gauge identity, uniform coefficient extraction and joint Gram bound are proved above. No general Hilbert--Schmidt equivalence, generic orthogonality measure, or unverified root-of-unity limit is imported. Only written mathematics and text operations were used; earlier finals and public manuscripts remain unchanged.

title: Exact rank loss and the remaining physical normal
text:
# Exact rank loss and the remaining physical normal Private written proof, 16 November 2026. At a simple rank loss of an actual finite-level leading coefficient, the first-normal equation recovers a missing next value. It generally leaves one next normal undetermined. This note identifies that channel, gives the exact criterion for additional rows to remove it, and shows that the original closing trace sees it. A classical exceptional color alone does not imply such a finite-level rank loss. ## 1. The actual equations at a physical row Use the original algebra and trace \[ P_N(Z)=2T_N(Z/2)+2,\qquad \mathcal A_N=\mathbb C[Z]/(P_N),\qquad \phi_N(f)=\eta N^2[Z^{N-1}]\operatorname{can}(f), \quad \eta=(-1)^{N-1}. 	ag{1} \] The distinct double nodes are \[ c_j=2\cos((2j+1)\pi/N),\qquad 0\le j<\lfloor N/2floor. \] When \(N\) is odd there is also the simple node \(-2\). Set \[ h=N^{-1},\qquad C_N(u)=2\cos(2\pi u+\pi/N). \] The full-step source equations in the first pinned source have ordinary residuals divisible by \(P_N\), before their physical evaluation. In this coordinate, \[ P_N(C_N(u))=4\sin^2(\pi Nu). 	ag{2} \] Consequently their values and first \(u\)-derivatives vanish at \(u=j/N\). These are derivatives of ordinary residuals, not a derivation of the physical quotient. Consider one such finite-order row, possibly with several components. Move all already specified values and normals to the right. Suppose the only unknown value packet is \(x=F(u_0+mh)\in\mathbb C^d\), and its unknown first-normal packet is \(y=F'(u_0+mh)\). The two equations are exactly \[ A x=b,\qquad A y+\dot A x=\dot b . 	ag{3} \] Here \(A\) is the full finite-\(N\) coefficient at \(u_0\), \(\dot A\) is its ordinary \(u\)-derivative, and \(\dot b\) includes every derivative of the coefficients and known shifted values on the right. A dot in (3) never means that the unknown packet is held constant when the ordinary source equation is differentiated. The level and all exterior parameters are fixed in this calculation. Equation (3) also applies to a larger future packet, with rectangular \(A\), after all its unknown shifted values are included. A row involving another unknown future value cannot be stacked as an equation for \(x\) alone by treating that extra value as known. ## 2. A simple square rank loss **Theorem 1.** Let \(A(u)\) be a holomorphic \(d\)-by-\(d\) matrix near \(u_0\). Suppose \[ \operatorname{rank}A(u_0)=d-1,\qquad \ker A(u_0)=\mathbb C r,\qquad \ker A(u_0)^{\mathsf T}=\mathbb C\ell^{\mathsf T}, \qquad \ell\dot A r
e0. 	ag{4} \] The vectors \(\ell,r\) are nonzero, and no conjugation is used in \(\ell\dot A r\). The system (3) is solvable if and only if \(\ell b=0\). When it is solvable, its value \(x\) is unique and its normal \(y\) has precisely one undetermined scalar: \[  egin{split} Ax_p&=b,\ x&=x_p+  rac{\ell(\dot b-\dot A x_p)}{\ell\dot A r}\,r,\ Ay_p&=\dot b-\dot A x,\qquad y=y_p+\zeta r,\quad \zeta\in\mathbb C. \end{split} 	ag{5} \] The condition in (4) is equivalent to a simple zero of \(\det A(u)\) at \(u_0\). *Proof.* The range of \(A\) is \(\ker\ell\), so the value equation is solvable precisely when \(\ell b=0\). Its solutions are \(x_p+zr\). The normal equation is solvable precisely when \(\ell(\dot b-\dot A x_p-z\dot A r)=0\). This uniquely gives the displayed \(z\); the solutions for \(y\) then differ by \(\ker A\). Changing \(x_p\) changes \(z\) by the opposite multiple, so \(x\) is independent of that choice. At a rank-\((d-1)\) matrix, its adjugate is a nonzero scalar multiple of \(r\ell\). Thus \((\det A)'=\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{adj}(A)\dot A)\) is a nonzero scalar multiple of \(\ell\dot A r\). This proves the last assertion. \(\square\) In the scalar case, \(A(u_0)=0\), \(\dot A(u_0)
e0\). The exact equations reduce to \[ b=0,\qquad x=\dot b/\dot A, 	ag{6} \] and leave \(y\) arbitrary. Thus first normals supply the missing value row; they do not themselves supply a full next-state transfer. The same fact has a local-algebra description. At a double spectral node \(c\), put \(\epsilon=Z-c\). In \(\mathbb C[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)\), multiplication by a coefficient with a simple zero is \[ (a_1\epsilon)(f_0+f_1\epsilon)=a_1f_0\epsilon . 	ag{7} \] It detects the value and kills the remaining normal component. This is an exact statement about the retained nilpotent, not about a reduced value-only quotient. ## 3. All aligned rows and their precise recovery criterion **Theorem 2.** Stack any collection of actual rows aligned on the same unknown value packet, obtaining \[ Bx=b,\qquad By+\dot Bx=\dot b , 	ag{8} \] where \(B:\mathbb C^d	o\mathbb C^p\). Assume that at least one solution exists, as it does for the original source with its actual previous data. Define \[ K=\ker B,\qquad \pi:\mathbb C^p\longrightarrow\operatorname{coker}B,\qquad H=\left.\pi\dot Bight|_K . 	ag{9} \] Then the possible differences of value packets are precisely \(\ker H\subseteq K\). For each fixed admissible value packet, the possible normals form a translate of \(K\). In particular: * the value is unique if and only if \(H\) is injective; * the full value-and-normal packet is unique if and only if \(B\) has full column rank. *Proof.* Subtract two solutions. The resulting equations are \[ B\,\delta x=0,\qquad B\,\delta y=-\dot B\,\delta x . 	ag{10} \] The second is solvable precisely when \(\pi\dot B\,\delta x=0\). Every \(\delta x\in\ker H\) therefore occurs, and its corresponding \(\delta y\)'s differ by \(K\). For \(\delta x=0\), every element of \(K\) is an allowed \(\delta y\), irrespective of \(H\). This proves both criteria. \(\square\) In Theorem 1, suppose further actual rows have coefficient matrix \(C\) on the same future value packet. Once its value has been fixed by (5), the additional normal equations determine \(\zeta\) if and only if \[ Cr
e0. 	ag{11} \] Indeed the stacked coefficient is \((A^{\mathsf T},C^{\mathsf T})^{\mathsf T}\), whose kernel is \(\mathbb Cr\cap\ker C\). More generally, independent normal constraints applied after the value is known remove the remaining normal exactly when their restriction to \(K\) is injective. All right sides must still be the original compatible source data. These are statements about the equations at this row. Later rows, other recovery equations, or the original global closing conditions may determine the remaining scalar even when (11) fails locally. Theorem 2 neither discards those equations nor asserts a free parameter in the globally defined source. ## 4. The original trace sees the remaining normal For every double node \(c\), including the sole node at \(N=2\), \[ P_N''(c)= rac{2N^2}{4-c^2}. 	ag{12} \] Define the ordinary polynomial of degree \(N-1\) \[ R_c(Z)= rac{2P_N(Z)}{P_N''(c)(Z-c)} = rac{(4-c^2)P_N(Z)}{N^2(Z-c)}. 	ag{13} \] Division in this formula is exact ordinary polynomial division. The value of \(R_c\) at every physical node is zero. Its derivative is one at \(c\) and zero at every other double node. At odd \(N\) its value at the simple node \(-2\) is also zero. These facts follow directly from the root multiplicities of \(P_N\). **Proposition 3.** For every original spectator \(g\in\mathcal A_N\), \[ \phi_N(R_c g)=\eta(4-c^2)g(c). 	ag{14} \] The identity holds coefficientwise with arbitrary ordinary exterior variables and their fixed derivatives retained. *Proof.* At the double node \(c\), the only nonzero jet of \(R_c g\) is its derivative \(g(c)\). All other physical jets vanish. Hence \(R_c g=g(c)R_c\) in the full algebra. The polynomial \(P_N\) is monic, so the leading coefficient in (13) is \((4-c^2)/N^2\). Apply (1). Formula (12), used above, also follows from the Chebyshev differential equation at a root with \(T_N(c/2)=-1\) and \(T_N'(c/2)=0\). \(\square\) Thus a spectral normal difference \(\zeta r\) in a vector channel can be represented by \(\zeta rR_c\). For a vector spectator \(g=(g_1,\ldots,g_d)\), its local contribution to the original closing is \[ \sum_{
u=1}^d\phi_N(\zeta r_
u R_cg_
u) =\eta(4-c^2)\zeta\sum_{
u=1}^dr_
u g_
u(c). 	ag{15} \] This need not vanish. For the scalar channel, \(g=1\) already detects it. Original crossing phases can remain inside \(g\); their physical values are not dropped. Formula (15) concerns vector components at one common physical color. For a future packet spanning several shifted colors, use the corresponding cardinal \(R_{c_a}\) at each distinct color and sum its separate contribution (14), with the appropriate component spectator. Repeated occurrences of the same physical color must satisfy their original identification; they are not independent normal coordinates. If the packet in (3) uses the \(u\)-normal instead, then \(C_N'(u_0+mh)
e0\) at a double node. The spectral normal in (15) is \(\zeta r/C_N'(u_0+mh)\). The conclusion is unchanged. There is no independent spectral normal in the quotient at the odd simple node. An angular first derivative there vanishes for an invariant spectral polynomial; it is not an additional free channel to which Theorem 1 should be applied. The cardinal in (13) proves visibility in the original algebra. It does not say that adding this cardinal to an actual source continues to solve every shifted row. That is the distinction between a local missing transfer datum and a global homogeneous solution. ## 5. Why a second differentiated equation is not available for free Let an ordinary residual of a cleared full-step row be \[ \mathscr R(u)=P_N(C_N(u))\,H_N(u), 	ag{16} \] with \(H_N\) holomorphic near the physical point. Formula (2) gives the exact next derivative \[ \mathscr R''(j/N)=8\pi^2N^2 H_N(j/N). 	ag{17} \] Thus only the value and first differentiated equations (3) are homogeneous at the grid. Passing to a second differentiated row would introduce the actual quotient residual \(H_N\). Setting the right side of (17) to zero would delete source data. Equivalently, the original double-root relation does not become a triple-root relation. Fixed exterior-parameter derivatives are different: they differentiate a \(P_N\) multiple without changing its physical root multiplicities. They may be retained in (3)--(17), with the usual product rules, wherever the coefficient/rank chart is defined. ## 6. Application and boundary of the conclusion The leading matrix in these statements is the actual finite-level coefficient after retaining every quantum shift and every source channel. A limiting characteristic phase color, even when it equals an exact physical node, does not by itself establish that this matrix is singular. Terms of smaller asymptotic size can repair the coefficient, or can have greater shift order and change the appropriate unknown packet. No such terms are omitted in (3). If an actual simple rank loss does occur, (5) gives its exact value repair and (11) gives the test for removing the residual normal with further aligned rows. Quantitative transfer also needs bounds for the inverse on the range of \(A\), for \((\ell\dot A r)^{-1}\), and, when used, for the extra restriction in (11). If these are polynomially conditioned, the determined data cost polynomially. No bound for the undetermined normal follows from that fact alone. In particular this note supplies neither propagation across every classical exceptional color nor a growth rate for a general composed source. The original traces and global source constraints remain available to control the identified datum. Local physical jets do not give an off-grid polynomial bound for a canonical polynomial of growing degree. ## 7. Direct sources and coverage The following complete source texts were read at matching pins: * [Full-step repeated-turn interface](research_full_step_repeated_turn_tensor_interface.md), SHA256 ef851eab40c8b2c44388a41d324e2fa41d4400f0f2118fe587405911e00e3398: exact cleared source equations, derivatives of ordinary residuals, retained recovery data, and the identity (2). * [Original physical radical contraction](research_high_newton_radical_contraction.md), SHA256 1faa5d2e02edf0a1462cc43b243e0ab4403bf56e9f1af0befb6b492441d9dd03: the original trace normalization, double-node residue, odd simple node, and joint-spectator scope. The elementary first-jet obstruction map (9) is proved here. The coverage search found earlier first-order kernel/cokernel lifting arguments, but no statement identifying this remaining physical-row normal together with its original-trace visibility and the complete stacked-row recovery criterion. Only written mathematics and source-text/hash reads were used. No mathematical program, numerical experiment, test, or build was run. Adopted notes and public manuscripts are unchanged.

title: A nonzero geometric source along one radial leg and its turn
text: # A nonzero geometric source along one radial leg and its turn 22 November 2026. Research note. Earlier final notes and public manuscripts remain unchanged. The original centered multiplication tensor has a uniformly growing geometric contribution when two parameters have modulus one and the third runs along a strict prism ray, including its zero endpoint. An exact reciprocal identity gives the corresponding original scalar observation after a genuine turn. The coefficient comes from the initialized source, rather than a choice of a formal saddle solution. These are statements about a universal three-boundary source. They do not assert that arbitrary open outputs remain in this family, or that an assembled knot period satisfies the volume identity. ## 1. The source and the result Use the full algebra, centered basis and original Frobenius functional of the [centered compiler](research_centered_fourier_conway_compiler.md). Thus \[ N\ge2,\quad d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad \kappa=q^{d^2/2},\qquad U_N(t)=\sum_{j=0}^d t^j f_j, \] Every power \(q^\alpha\) means \(e^{\pi i\alpha/N}\), including half-integer exponents. In these conventions \[ \mathcal C_N(x,y,z)=\phi(U_N(x)U_N(y)U_N(z)),\qquad \phi(f_i f_j)=\delta_{ij},\qquad Jf_j=f_{d-j}. \tag{1} \] The positive coefficient norm makes the entire centered basis orthonormal. All value and first-derivative coordinates at the repeated Casimir roots remain in this space. A strict prism shape means real numbers \[ a,b,c>0,\qquad a+b,a+c,b+c<1,\qquad a+b+c>1. \tag{2} \] For such a shape put \[ x_r=-r e^{-2\pi ia},\qquad y=-e^{-2\pi ib},\qquad z=-e^{-2\pi ic},\qquad 0\le r\le1. \tag{3} \] There is no requirement that the radial leg have the largest angle. Use the source's calibrated branches \[ \begin{split} \Psi(x,y,z)={}&-\frac{\pi}{12} +\frac1{2\pi}\bigl[ \operatorname{Li}_2(-x)+\operatorname{Li}_2(-y) +\operatorname{Li}_2(-z)+\operatorname{Li}_2(-xyz)\\ &\hspace{27mm} -\operatorname{Li}_2(xy)-\operatorname{Li}_2(xz) -\operatorname{Li}_2(yz)\bigr],\\ B(x,y,z)={}&[(1-xy)(1-xz)(1-yz)]^{-1/2}. \end{split} \tag{4} \] The dilogarithms start with their power series in the open unit disk and take continuous limits at the displayed strict angular boundary. The square root has the branch specified by the same source. None of its three factors vanishes on (2)--(3). Set \[ h(r)=-\operatorname{Im}\Psi(x_r,y,z),\qquad J_0(t)=\int_0^t\log(2\sin\pi u)\,du\quad(0\le t\le1). \tag{5} \] **Theorem.** Uniformly for shapes in a fixed compact subset of (2) and all \(0\le r\le1\), \[ \mathcal C_N(x_r,y,z)= \kappa e^{i\pi/4-\pi i/(2N)}B(x_r,y,z) e^{iN\Psi(x_r,y,z)}(1+O(N^{-1})). \tag{6} \] The height is strictly increasing on \(0<r<1\), and \[ h(r)\ge h(0)=J_0(b+c)-J_0(b)-J_0(c)>0. \tag{7} \] Consequently the original source is nonzero for every sufficiently large level, uniformly in this family. The statement includes both parities, composite levels and level-dependent approaches to \(r=0\). It concerns the actual finite polynomial in (1). ## 2. Positivity of the entire radial interval For \(0<t<1\), differentiating the Fourier series of the dilogarithm, or integrating its logarithmic derivative, gives \[ \operatorname{Im}\operatorname{Li}_2(e^{-2\pi it}) =2\pi J_0(t). \] Formula (4) at \(x=0\) therefore gives the equality in (7). To prove its strict sign, fix \(c\) and consider \(g(b)=J_0(b+c)-J_0(b)-J_0(c)\) on \(0<b<1-c\). The log-sine integral has \(J_0(1)=0\) and \(J_0(1-t)=-J_0(t)\). Thus \(g\) is zero at both endpoints. Moreover \[ g'(b)=\log\frac{\sin\pi(b+c)}{\sin\pi b} \] is positive before \(b=(1-c)/2\) and negative afterwards. This proves \(g(b)>0\) throughout the open interval. For monotonicity in \(r\), set \[ E=e^{-2\pi i(a+(b+c)/2)},\qquad s=2\cos\pi(b-c),\qquad t_0=2\cos\pi(b+c). \] The strict prism inequalities imply \[ \frac12<a+\frac{b+c}{2}<1,\qquad \operatorname{Im}E>0,\qquad s-t_0=4\sin\pi b\sin\pi c>0. \tag{8} \] Differentiating (4) along the ray gives \[ \frac{dh}{d\log r}=-\frac1{2\pi}\arg\mathcal R_r, \quad \mathcal R_r= \frac{(1-r e^{-2\pi i(a+b)})(1-r e^{-2\pi i(a+c)})} {(1-r e^{-2\pi ia})(1-r e^{-2\pi i(a+b+c)})} =\frac{1-rsE+r^2E^2}{1-rt_0E+r^2E^2}. \tag{9} \] Here the argument is continued from zero at \(r=0\); it is not a new choice of logarithmic lift. Direct multiplication gives \[ \operatorname{Im}\mathcal R_r =-\frac{r(s-t_0)(1-r^2)\operatorname{Im}E} {|1-rt_0E+r^2E^2|^2}<0 \qquad(0<r<1). \tag{10} \] Thus the continued argument stays in \((-\pi,0)\), proving strict monotonicity. Continuity includes \(r=0,1\). The lower bound in (7) is uniformly positive on shape compacts. ## 3. Taking the initialized source formula to the zero endpoint The [full prism-source theorem](research_centered_tensor_full_prism_source_transport.md) already proves (6) on every interval \(r_0\le r\le1\), provided the height is nonnegative. Its exact canceled formula is \[ \mathcal C_N=\mathcal G_N -\frac{\kappa}{N}D_N(x)D_N(y)D_N(z)\mathcal I_N, \qquad D_N(t)=1-(-1)^d t^N. \tag{11} \] Here \(\mathcal G_N\) is the specified nonzero seven-factor canonical Gamma quotient. We now check the constants as the one radius tends to zero; the theorem's stated restriction \(r_0>0\) is not silently dropped. Permute the contour roles so that its first angle is largest, as in the source proof. Its two remaining angles, say \(b',c'\), are less than \(1/2\). Every use of the canonical factorial estimates there is on a full vertical strip with real part in a fixed compact subinterval of \((0,1)\). Those estimates, including the relative error, are uniform for arbitrarily large imaginary parts. Sending one radius to zero only sends some nonnegative heights to infinity. Write \(\varrho_x,\varrho_y,\varrho_z\) for the permuted moduli, and \(\ell_j=-\log\varrho_j/(2\pi)\). Before taking the limit they are finite and nonnegative. On the vertical current parameter \(Y\in\mathbb R\), the shifted arguments are \[ a_Y=1-b'+i(Y+\ell_y),\quad b_Y=1-c'+i(Y+\ell_z),\quad c_0=1-b'-c'+i(\ell_y+\ell_z). \] The possible amplitude denominators in its current estimate are \(h_*(c_0),h_*(a_Y),h_*(b_Y)\), where \(h_*(w)^2=i(1-e^{2\pi iw})\). Their angles are respectively \(b'+c',b',c'\). For every \(v\ge0\) and \(0<\theta<1\), \[ |1-v e^{-2\pi i\theta}|\ge\sin(\pi\theta)(1+v). \tag{12} \] All reciprocal amplitude factors therefore stay bounded independently of these heights. The current rate proof uses only that the moduli are at most one: its comparison \(v_0\le\min(v_y,v_z)\) requires no positive lower radius, since \(v_y=\varrho_y e^{-2\pi Y}\), \(v_z=\varrho_z e^{-2\pi Y}\) and \(v_0=\varrho_y\varrho_z e^{-2\pi Y}\). Its Cauchy factor also has the bound (12), uniformly even when the Cauchy-leg radius is zero. Hence the same integrable current majorant gives \[ |\mathcal I_N|\le C N\left[ \int_{-\infty}^0 e^{\pi NY}\,dY+ \int_0^\infty e^{-\pi NY/2}\,dY\right]\le C', \] and consequently \[ |\mathcal I_N|\le C,\qquad |\mathcal C_N-\mathcal G_N|\le C/N \qquad(0<r\le1), \tag{13} \] with constants independent of the lower radius. The seven-factor quotient is symmetric in its angle/height linear forms. Write \(\mathfrak F_N\) for the source's canonical factorial \(F_N\), to distinguish it from the generating polynomial (1). For the original radial leg its zero-radius limit is \[ \mathcal G_N(0,y,z)=\frac{\kappa}{\sqrt N} \frac{\mathfrak F_N(N(1-b)-1/2) \mathfrak F_N(N(1-c)-1/2)} {\mathfrak F_N(N(1-b-c))}\ne0. \tag{14} \] Indeed exactly two numerator and two denominator arguments tend upwards to infinity. At fixed \(N\), their factorials tend to the same nonzero canonical upper constant, and cancel in matching pairs. The remaining three factors lie in the nonzero canonical strip. Continuity of the original polynomial and this explicit limit extend (13) to \(r=0\). The same full-strip estimates give \[ \mathcal G_N= \kappa e^{i\pi/4-\pi i/(2N)}B(x_r,y,z) e^{iN\Psi(x_r,y,z)}(1+O(N^{-1})) \tag{15} \] uniformly down to that endpoint: all positive heights are allowed, and the remaining amplitude factors stay bounded and nonzero. This is a continuous radial assertion, not holomorphy of the Gamma quotient at zero. The original source itself is polynomial. The height bound (7) and the nonzero bounded amplitude make (13) exponentially small relative to (15), uniformly on the family. This proves (6). It is essential to take the limit of (11). In the representation using the radial leg as the Cauchy leg, setting that parameter equal to zero in the uncanceled rectangle would lose the moving pole at infinity. Its nonzero contribution is exactly the limit (14). If the largest-angle permutation chooses another Cauchy leg, the diverging shifts occur in the factorial weight instead; the uniform estimates above cover that representation as well. ## 4. The original scalar observation after a turn The compiler's full coefficient relation is \(\overline{C_{ijk}}=C_{d-i,d-j,d-k}\). Reindexing its polynomial gives the exact identity \[ \mathcal C_N(x,y,z)=(xyz)^d \overline{\mathcal C_N(1/\bar x,1/\bar y,1/\bar z)}. \tag{16} \] For \(|y|=|z|=1\), define the reciprocal polynomial \[ \mathcal T_N(t;y,z)=t^d\mathcal C_N(1/t,y,z) =\phi\bigl[J(U_N(y)U_N(z))U_N(t)\bigr]. \tag{17} \] Both expressions have their polynomial interpretation at \(t=0\). Equations (16)--(17) give \[ \mathcal T_N(t;y,z)=(yz)^d \overline{\mathcal C_N(\bar t,y,z)}. \tag{18} \] Thus on the turned ray \(t_r=\overline{x_r}\), (6) yields \[ \mathcal T_N(t_r;y,z)=(yz)^d \overline{\kappa e^{i\pi/4-\pi i/(2N)} B(x_r,y,z)e^{iN\Psi(x_r,y,z)}}(1+O(N^{-1})). \tag{19} \] Its exponential rate is the same positive \(h(r)\). The carrier \((yz)^d\) and all phases in (19) are retained. In particular the turned coordinate is \(t_r=\bar x_r\); replacing it by \(x_r\) would change the strict-prism angular condition. For unit-normalized coherent inputs \(u_N(t)=U_N(t)/\sqrt{Z_N(t)}\), with \(Z_N(t)=\sum_{j=0}^d|t|^{2j}\), the actual scalar is \[ \phi\bigl[J(u_N(y)u_N(z))u_N(t)\bigr] =\frac{\mathcal T_N(t;y,z)}{N\sqrt{Z_N(t)}}. \tag{20} \] Here \(1\le Z_N(t_r)\le N\). The exact normalization is only polynomial and does not change the positive exponential rate. ## 5. Scope and complete proof sources This proves the presence and nonzero coefficient of the geometric contribution in two specified original scalar observations, uniformly along the full radial interval and at its signed-crossing endpoint. It is not merely a forward norm maximum or a formal critical equation. Reciprocity itself is already part of the tensor's exact algebra; the additional estimate is the growing single-leg interval through zero and its correctly oriented turned observation. The result supplies neither the whole output after the next arbitrary branching nor a compatible scalar observation for an arbitrary short component. Its two unit parameters are a different regime from the compact open bidisks in the cyclic vacuum-gap theorem. No uniform vacuum gap at this unit boundary is inferred here. No new knot-volume class or finite-exception theorem follows from (6) or (19) alone. The complete direct proof texts are: | Source | SHA-256 | |---|---| | [Initialized full prism source, 651 lines](research_centered_tensor_full_prism_source_transport.md) | eb43e287eca5933b70de3b6362a81f92d46bb2e121f0eb5716793c107adaef10 | | [Full centered compiler, 405 lines](research_centered_fourier_conway_compiler.md) | 0edbabe42280d70e4d5dcbcb55b188a3e773c14b99fbd212eb0fe8c5b176a413 | Both were read in full at the matching pins. The radial sign argument, uniform endpoint extension and correctly marked turned observation are proved above. Only written mathematics and text operations were used. No earlier final or public manuscript was edited.

The actual soft-binomial cut: cycle, action and midpoint critical scheme
text: # The actual soft-binomial cut: cycle, action and midpoint critical scheme Private written proof, 18 November 2026. The binomial cut has an exact finite-source cycle and a definite principal boundary action. The latter changes one cut-gluing equation. Conservation of the full classical coproduct then identifies its regular principal critical scheme with the braid fixed-point scheme at the midpoint. This scheme contains the complete geometric representation for every fixed finite braid of a hyperbolic knot. The residual geometric centralizer remains. The complete proof sources are S (the binomial cut), C (the compact finite coherent calculus), M (the literal braid/holonomy correspondence), and G (the regular midpoint frame). Their pins are below. The stationary statement concerns the principal logarithmic equations of the actual weighted occupation-state array on its regular charts. Its critical scheme uses the exponentiated rows, retaining their logarithmic sheets; it does not select an additive Fourier charge. It does not assert a uniform phase expansion for a growing full coherent kernel, a sum-to-integral deformation, or a thimble coefficient. ## 1. The full finite array and retained current Keep the actual braid word, crossing signs, tail pivots and framing. Put \(d=N-1\), \(c_0=2\pi i\), \(h=c_0/N\), \(Q=e^h\), \(q=e^{h/2}\), and \(M=-qx\). The letter \(u\) below denotes a logarithmic occupation, distinct from the quantum square root \(q\). Let \(C_N(M)\) be the one-cut endomorphism in M's factorial basis. Its literal state array with cut occupation \(a\), internal states \(\mathcal I_N(a)\), and full weights \(W_N\) gives \[ Z_N(M)=\sum_{a=0}^{d}\pi_{N,a} \sum_{\mathbf k\in\mathcal I_N(a)}W_N(a,\mathbf k;M), \qquad \pi_{N,a}=2^{-d}\binom da. \tag{1} \] The inner support, head and transfer inequalities, and every zero factor are unchanged. S proves the exact whole-meridian identity \[ Z_N=\operatorname{Tr}(P_N^{\rm cut}C_N)=F_N,\qquad P_N^{\rm cut}=\sum_a\pi_{N,a}T_a. \tag{2} \] For an arbitrary marked endomorphism \(C\), the comparison is instead \[ \operatorname{Tr}((P_N^{\rm cut}-T_0)C) =\operatorname{Tr}(B_N^{\rm cut}[C,\mathcal E]),\qquad B_N^{\rm cut}=-\sum_{r=0}^{d-1} \frac{\Pr(A>r)}{M Q^{-r-1}-M^{-1}}E_{r+1,r}. \tag{3} \] The marked word, its tail pivot, and all meridian derivatives are retained on the right. It is not declared zero for arbitrary marks. The displayed denominators are units on S's shrinking meridian disk. Both signed crossings conserve integer total occupation. Closing the other strands forces the cut input and output occupations to agree in every surviving term, also with diagonal occupation and transfer marks. Thus (1) has one cut occupation, not two independent endpoint positions. ## 2. An exact finite cycle and an exactly removable gauge angle Use C's kernels \[ K_A(w,z)=\sum_{i,j=0}^{d}w^iA_{ij}\binom{d}{j}z^j,\qquad \sigma_A=K_A/(1+wz)^d. \tag{4} \] C proves the exact compact sphere composition \[ K_{AB}(w,z)=\frac N\pi\int_{\mathbb C} \frac{K_A(w,\bar v)K_B(v,z)}{(1+|v|^2)^{N+1}}\,d^2v. \tag{5} \] The sphere is \(\Gamma=\{w=v,z=\bar v\}\), including infinity, with C's orientation. Insert (5) between all actual local matrices and its trace version on closed strands. All factors \(N\), pivots, head projectors, clocks and framing stay inside the finite network. S gives the cut functional \[ Z_N=\frac1{2\pi i}\oint_{|v|=1} \sigma_{C_N}(v,v^{-1})\,\frac{dv}{v}. \tag{6} \] Equations (5)--(6) specify the complete finite compact cycle: the cut latitude circle times the intermediate and closing spheres. Its resolution measures avoid their coherent pole divisors. Expanding the finite kernels, the angle and beta integrations in C recover exactly (1), including every support condition. This is a whole-array identity before stationarity. Set \(S_ce_a=c^{-a}e_a\). Integer conservation and the diagonal physical pivots imply \[ [R^\pm,S_c\otimes S_c]=0,\qquad [\text{pivot},S_c]=0,\qquad \sigma_{S_cAS_c^{-1}}(w,z)=\sigma_A(w/c,cz). \tag{7} \] Position-preserving marks obey the same rule. For \(|c|=1\), this rotation preserves each sphere and its measure. In (6), use \(c=v\) and rotate every intermediate coherent coordinate. The cut becomes \((1,1)\); all internal gauges cancel by (7). This is an exact change of variables, and the normalized angle integral is one. Equivalently, diagonality gives \[ \sigma_{C_N}(v,v^{-1}) =2^{-d}\sum_a\binom da(C_N)_{aa}=\sigma_{C_N}(1,1). \tag{8} \] For charged Ward insertions the circle and defect (3) remain. This angle is the common diagonal momentum gauge, not the geometric centralizer coordinate \(r\). No geometric-centralizer relative interval has been specified by (5)--(6). In S's alternative normal-residue presentation the full normal pole packet, south affine clutch and endpoint current remain. Equal density endpoint values do not erase its derivative current. ## 3. The principal binomial action from the exact coefficients The consecutive ratio is exactly \[ \frac{\pi_{N,a+1}}{\pi_{N,a}} =\frac{d-a}{a+1} =\frac{c_0-h-u}{u+h},\qquad u=ha. \tag{9} \] Near \(u=c_0/2\), choose logarithms by continuation from \(u/c_0\in(0,1)\), avoiding \(0,c_0\). Its principal logarithm and normalized primitive are \[ g'(u)=\log\frac{c_0-u}{u},\qquad g(u)=c_0\left[-\frac u{c_0}\log\frac u{c_0} -(1-u/c_0)\log(1-u/c_0)-\log2\right]. \tag{10} \] In particular \[ g(c_0/2)=g'(c_0/2)=0,\qquad g''(c_0/2)=-4/c_0\ne0. \tag{11} \] The constant in (10) is fixed by the original cut normalization. Indeed a maximal binomial probability lies between \(1/N\) and one, so its logarithm divided by \(N\) tends to zero. Summing the logarithms of (9) between that central occupation and any \(a_N/N\to t\in(0,1)\) gives, on compact subintervals, the Riemann integral \(\int_{1/2}^t\log((1-y)/y)\,dy\). Hence \(h\log\pi_{N,a_N}\to g(c_0t)\). The rational ratio fixes its holomorphic principal continuation on the stated logarithmic chart. No deformation of the finite state sum was used. The exact finite mean is \(d/2\), with coordinate \(c_0/2-h/2\). At even \(N\) the two maximal integer weights flank it. These finite shifts, parity and all normal corrections remain in (9); only the principal position is \(c_0/2\). ## 4. The modified cut row and the full localized critical ideal Work in a regular logarithmic chart of M's literal generating correspondence. Let \(S_0\) be its leading expression, including the original Cartan, pivotal and framing contributions. For either signed crossing M's identities read \[ dS_{\rm crossing} =\sum_{\rm out}\log p_{\rm out}\,d\log A_{\rm out} -\sum_{\rm in}\log p_{\rm in}\,d\log A_{\rm in} +\text{external-meridian terms}. \tag{12} \] For the positive transfer \(C\), the outputs are \(BC,A/C\). Consequently (12) gives M's derivatives \(S_a=\log(p_{{\rm out},2}/p_{{\rm in},1})\), \(S_b=\log(p_{{\rm out},1}/p_{{\rm in},2})\), and \(S_C=\log(p_{{\rm out},1}/p_{{\rm out},2})\). The negative crossing has the inverse identities. M first derives these identities in the old basis. Its exact factorial change adds the corresponding endpoint primitives to the generating expression and changes momentum to \(p_{\rm new}=(1-A)p_{\rm old}\). Thus (12) has the same canonical form in the factorial basis used in (1). From here on \(p\) means this new-basis momentum. The new principal expression is precisely \(S_0+g(u)\). All internal rows are unchanged. For the single matching cut position \(A=e^u\), cancellation in (12) gives \(\partial_uS_0=\log(p_{\rm out}/p_{\rm in})\), with its retained logarithm branches. Thus the changed exponentiated cut equation is \[ \boxed{\displaystyle \frac{p_{\rm out}}{p_{\rm in}} =e^{-g'(u)}=\frac{u}{c_0-u}.} \tag{13} \] The physical pivot on a closed strand is \(x^{1-N}Q^{a(N-1)}\). Its leading expression is \(c_0(\log A-\log x)\), so its exponentiated momentum multiplier is one. The writhe term depends on \(x\). These facts explain why they do not alter (13); they are not dropped from the source or its meridian derivatives. It is important to use the entire internal correspondence, not (13) alone. The ordered classical coproduct has \[ K_*=K_1K_{\rm tail},\qquad E_*=e_1K_{\rm tail}+E_{\rm tail},\qquad F_*=f_1+K_1^{-1}F_{\rm tail}. \tag{14} \] Both signed maps of M preserve these functions. Direct substitution in its positive rational map gives \(K_1'K_2'=K_1K_2\), \(e_1'K_2'+e_2'=e_1K_2+e_2\), and \(f_1'+(K_1')^{-1}f_2'=f_1+K_1^{-1}f_2\). Its negative map is the inverse, proving the same identities. Iteration gives (14) in the original tensor ordering. In the canonical-graph ring impose the internal stationary rows, including closure of the positions and momenta at tensor positions \(2,\ldots,b\). Their \(K,e,f\) close. Since \(K_{\rm tail}\) is a unit, (14) first gives \(K_1'=K_1\), then \(e_1'=e_1\), and finally \(f_1'=f_1\). Hence also \(A_1'=A_1\). On any chart where either \(1-A_1\) or \(1-x^2/A_1\) is a unit, the literal formulas \[ f_1=(1-A_1)/p_1,\qquad e_1=(1-x^2/A_1)p_1/x \tag{15} \] force \(p_1'=p_1\). The argument is an ideal calculation in the localized graph ring, not merely a statement about closed points. Its unit condition holds near \(A_1=-1,M=1\). Modulo those internal rows, (13) is equivalent to \(1-u/(c_0-u)=0\). As \(c_0-u\) is a unit, its ideal is exactly \((u-c_0/2)\). Conversely a full braid fixed point at \(u=c_0/2\) satisfies every internal row and (13). Therefore the localized principal stationary ideal equals the full braid fixed-point ideal plus \((u-c_0/2)\). This conclusion is on the chosen logarithmic sheet and unit chart. Endpoint/nonunit strata, for example the simultaneous vanishing at \(A=1,M=1\), are not included by this localization. The common momentum remains free. A local classical diagonal gauge may set \(p_1=p_1'=1\); this is a frame choice, not another equation forced by (13). M identifies the resulting scheme with the actual selected-flag knot representation scheme. G gives a regular complete geometric point for every fixed finite braid of a hyperbolic knot: \[ A_{\rm cut}=-1,\qquad p_{\rm in}=p_{\rm out}=1,\qquad \mu_{\rm cut}=\begin{pmatrix}-1&2\\-2&3\end{pmatrix}. \tag{16} \] Thus the actual weighted principal state presentation has this geometric stationary point, with nondegenerate local five-shape coordinates. This does not put it on a contributing deformation of the compact cycle (5)--(6). ## 5. Latitude calibration and the surviving centralizer C's exact clock symbols are \(R_\pm(T)=[1+(Q^{\pm1}-1)T]^d\), with \(T=wz/(1+wz)\). At \(T=1/2\), put \(c_N=\cos(\pi/N)^{N-1}\). Direct substitution in C's complete finite generator formulas gives \[ R_+=-q^{-1}c_N,\quad R_-=-q c_N,\quad \sigma_K=M c_N, \] \[ \sigma_{\mathcal E} =v^{-1}[-M q c_N-M^{-1}-(M-M^{-1})2^{-d}], \qquad \sigma_F=v(1+q c_N). \tag{17} \] The vacuum term is explicit. The root upper wall is zero only after its prescribed specialization; off-root normals must be taken in C's full formula before that specialization. As \(N\to\infty\), (17) gives the actual Gauss coordinates \[ A=-1,\qquad p=v^{-1},\qquad K=M,\quad e=-(M+M^{-1})p,\quad f=2/p. \tag{18} \] This calibrates the latitude and occupation at principal order. It is not equality of finite coordinate operators, or a uniform star-symbol theorem for an arbitrary growing full-word kernel. Section 4 used M's signed generating correspondence, not the latter. At completion and \(p=1\), the actual framing is \[ F(r,s)=\begin{pmatrix}r&1-r\\s&-s\end{pmatrix},\qquad F^{-1}J_1F=\begin{pmatrix}1+s&-s\\s&1-s\end{pmatrix}, \qquad A=(1+s)^{-1}. \tag{19} \] It is independent of \(r\). Left multiplication by \(J_b=\begin{pmatrix}1&b\\0&1\end{pmatrix}\) changes \(r\) to \(r+bs\), preserving \(s\). At the midpoint \(s=-2\), this is a nonzero additive centralizer direction. Common momentum instead conjugates (19) by \(\operatorname{diag}(p,1)\); it does not change \(r\). The latitude angle in (17) is this latter gauge. On the old framed geometric family, \(u=-\log(1+s)\), so \(du=-ds/(1+s)\) is independent of \(r\). At the midpoint \(g'=0\), the Hessian changes by \[ g''(c_0/2)\,du\otimes du. \tag{20} \] The \(r\) direction remains in the full kernel because it is tangent to the unchanged critical family with \(s=-2\). After fixing the common momentum, if the old Hessian has exactly its two framing null directions, (20) removes exactly the one on which \(du\ne0\). Indeed projection of the new null-vector equation to the old cokernel first forces \(du=0\), and then the vector is in the old kernel. The exact corank assertion uses that old transverse-regularity premise; survival of \(r\) does not. There is no identification of the latitude circle with an \(r\)-centralizer relative contour here. The former has the exact normalized gauge integral one in (8). A nonzero universal integral along the latter requires a separate relative source map, including (3), not concentration of (1) or a normal residue. ## 6. Scope and complete proof-source pins The finite cycle, literal principal boundary action and regular principal critical scheme are now fixed. The geometric midpoint is present without an alternating or long-twist hypothesis. All source walls, pivots, framing and marked currents remain. Analytic phase/amplitude control of the full coherent network, the geometric centralizer reduction, its relative cycle and a nonzero physical geometric coefficient remain unproved. * S: notes/research_binomial_cut_framing_density.md, SHA256 4bc6efc595fd6d59c0bc572d83495fb779cff230ff1cb9c14429a0b7c6a2a1b0. * C: notes/compact_coherent_source_period.md, SHA256 8c6c3277367a4aa6c69269da635139d5f881f3d3d0d894e04dd97028d76537e4. * M: notes/marked_braid_holonomy.md, SHA256 eff47c757d0e44bda0c396c094315b8e1fce11f1fc2d6445d636c6d2d3a46c4f. * G: notes/research_midpoint_geometric_braid_frame.md, SHA256 9b9756929ac16b9413744ab376ac74718ecbaac645ab0440e3e3a835349b8e30. All four complete sources were read nontruncated in the author sequence and their used implications checked.
