title: Every regular soft-cut critical action has its representation volume
text:
# Every regular soft-cut critical action has its representation volume Private written proof, 18 November 2026. The regular principal critical scheme of the actual binomial-cut state is already identified in S. This note calibrates every one of its boundary-parabolic critical actions, with the integer Fourier correction made before taking its imaginary part. The result applies to competing representations, not only the complete geometric one. Copies of the same projective holonomy have the same exponential rate and are not separated by this result. The complete proof directs are S, Q, C and G, pinned below. The general crossing-chain and logarithmic regulator arguments are already present in C and Q. Their extension beyond faithful representations is also explicit in the earlier coverage note actual_wall_critical_regulator.md, Section 5. The new adapter here is the soft-cut entropy and its integral characters. ## 1. The actual principal action and its lattice Fix the literal finite braid of an oriented hyperbolic knot \(K\), with all signs, tail pivots, writhe compensation and reduced normalization retained. Work at the physical root \[ h=2\pi i/N,\qquad c_0=2\pi i,\qquad M=1. 	ag{1} \] Use independent integral coordinates \(k_i\) on the incidence and occupation lattice of its finite array, and unwrapped logarithms \(\zeta_i=h k_i\). Integral affine offsets, if used in choosing coordinates, remain part of these original integer occupations. They are not discarded by taking cyclic residues. Write \(
u=\log M\) for the meridian logarithm. Q supplies the actual leading action \[ S_0(\zeta,
u)=G_0(\zeta,
u) +\sum_j\epsilon_j\operatorname{Li}_2(z_j), 	ag{2} \] where the shapes are monomials with modulus-one constants. The polynomial \(G_0\) is a real quadratic form plus a purely imaginary linear form and a real constant. It includes the Cartan, pivot, original framing and \(\operatorname{Li}_2(1)\) terms; it is not an unspecified primitive of the gluing equations. The logarithms and dilogarithms are continued compatibly. Let \(u\) be the cut logarithmic occupation, an integral affine linear function of the \(\zeta_i\). S proves that the soft action is \[ S_{m soft}=S_0+g(u),\qquad g(u)=c_0[-(u/c_0)\log(u/c_0) -(1-u/c_0)\log(1-u/c_0)-\log2]. 	ag{3} \] Its distinguished local sheet near \(u=c_0/2\) has \[ g(c_0/2)=g'(c_0/2)=0. 	ag{4} \] The finite mean is \((N-1)/2\), not \(N/2\); all its finite shifts and normal corrections remain in the exact source of S. Equation (3) is its principal coefficient action. In this note a regular critical point means a point in S's localized canonical graph, with the internal and soft cut rows imposed. S proves, as an equality of ideals, that these rows are the full braid fixed-point rows together with \[ u=c_0/2. 	ag{5} \] This uses the conserved full ordered \(K,E,F\) coproduct and the stated unit chart. It is not inferred from a peripheral eigenvalue equation alone. After a common classical momentum gauge the cut is \(A=-1,p=1\), with noncentral parabolic meridian. The corresponding projective representation is denoted \(ho\). ## 2. The Fourier correction preserves every finite summand At an exponentiated critical point, on its compatible logarithmic lift, write \[ \partial_{\zeta_i}S_{m soft}=c_0 n_i, \qquad n_i\in\mathbb Z. 	ag{6} \] The integers are locally constant on a continued critical chart. Define the corrected action \[ S_{m corr}=S_{m soft}-c_0\sum_i n_i\zeta_i. 	ag{7} \] At every original finite lattice state, \[ \exp((S_{m corr}-S_{m soft})/h) =\exp(-2\pi i\sum_i n_i k_i)=1. 	ag{8} \] Thus (7) is a permitted Fourier character of the same discrete source, with no new coefficient or endpoint factor. It does not specify a contour or select the charge of a contributing saddle. On an integral affine parametrization, its integer offsets give the same identity, including their retained level dependence. The entropy sheets can be checked explicitly. If the two logarithms in (3) change by \(c_0j_0,c_0j_1\), respectively, then \[ \Delta g=-c_0(j_0-j_1)u-c_0^2j_1,\qquad j_0,j_1\in\mathbb Z. 	ag{9} \] For the actual cut occupation \(u=ha\), \(c_0=Nh\), its exponential multiplier is \[ \exp(\Delta g/h) =\exp[-2\pi i((j_0-j_1)a+Nj_1)]=1. 	ag{10} \] At (5), \[ \Delta g=-	frac12c_0^2(j_0+j_1)\in\mathbb R,\qquad \Delta g'=-c_0(j_0-j_1). 	ag{11} \] The derivative change is absorbed in (6). These are genuine integer characters, not arbitrary complex shifts of the action. The real constant in (9) is retained. ## 3. Calibration of the imaginary critical value Let \( eta=\sum_j\epsilon_j[z_j]\) be the actual signed five-shape crossing sum. For compatible branches Q proves \[ D( eta)=\operatorname{Im}S_0 -\sum_i\operatorname{Re}\zeta_i\, \operatorname{Im}\partial_{\zeta_i}S_0 -\operatorname{Re}
u\, \operatorname{Im}\partial_
u S_0. 	ag{12} \] This identity is algebraic in the logarithmic differential data: \(\operatorname{Im}\operatorname{Li}_2(z) =D(z)-\log|z|\operatorname{Im}\log(1-z)\), while the imaginary part of a real quadratic polynomial with imaginary linear part is the real-coordinate pairing with its imaginary gradient. Compatible dilogarithm monodromy contributes its integer logarithms and a real constant, so the same identity persists. On the distinguished entropy sheet, (4)--(5) imply that \(\operatorname{Im}g=0\) and that every internal derivative of \(g\) vanishes. Since \(\operatorname{Re}
u=0\) at \(M=1\), substitution of (6)--(7) into (12) gives \[ \operatorname{Im}S_{m corr}=D( eta). 	ag{13} \] For another entropy sheet, (11) gives a real value of \(g\) at the same point. Its internal derivative changes by the integer covector already corrected in (7). Also \(\operatorname{Re}u=0\); hence the pairing of that derivative with the real internal coordinates is zero. Any retained affine offset in \(u\) is purely imaginary and has the same property. Thus (13) holds on every compatible entropy sheet. There is no freely adjustable imaginary constant in (13). The original Gaussian/framing constants in Q and the normalized binomial constant in (3) have already fixed it. The preferred longitude and its inverse eigenflag are the ones in Q; their spin signs have not been recentered. The same conclusion holds for the other complete central lift when carried with the full source conventions. One can either apply (12) with \(\operatorname{Re}\log M=0\), or twist a determinant-one representation by the knot's meridian sign character. Then \(x\) and each \(K_j\) change sign together, so \(A_j=x/K_j\), transfer ratios and \(x^2\) do not change. The crossing Bloch sum is unchanged. This is a comparison of retained classical lifts, not a deletion of quantum signs. If the full ADO normalization is used, its exact factor remains \[ d_N(M)=i^{N+3} rac{M^{N-1}}{1+M^2+\cdots+M^{2N-2}}. 	ag{14} \] At \(M=1\) it is \(i^{N+3}/N\), and at \(M=-1\) it is \(i^{N+3}(-1)^{N-1}/N\). These phases and powers must be kept, and their contribution to the scaled logarithmic modulus is \(-(2\pi/N)\log N\), tending to zero. No off-root normal or generic-meridian gauge is discarded. ## 4. The crossing regulator is the competing representation volume C states its final comparison for complete faithful holonomy. Its chain proof applies to every representation obtained above. Here are the ingredients needed to check that extension. At \(M=1\), the noncentral meridians are unipotent projectively. Their fixed flags and the actual Hurwitz words supply exactly C's region decorations. Its determinant identities, three five-term boundaries and signed four-tetrahedron crossing balls use unipotence, not faithfulness of \(ho\). The paired faces and original strand closures are the same abstract oriented relative fundamental cycle, with the degree-one cusp marking and preferred-writhe shear proved in C. The abstract group in that construction is the knot group, independent of whether its image under \(ho\) is faithful. Choose free auxiliary vertex flags generically. If developed vertices are forced to repeat, use the normalized alternating configuration complex: that tetrahedron is zero, and its repeated-vertex faces cancel in pairs. The five-term map therefore still identifies the signed crossing sum with the \(ho\)-developed fundamental chain. Equivalently one can subdivide and add generic free interior vertex types; their stars are balls and change no fundamental regulator. Continuity \(D(0)=D(1)=D(\infty)=0\) gives the same value for any normalized degenerate developed tetrahedra. The longitude commutes with the nonidentity unipotent meridian. Its projective centralizer consists of the unipotents fixing that flag, so the peripheral image is boundary-parabolic. The regulated idealized chain is consequently the signed representation-volume normalization used in C and G. We obtain \[ D( eta)=\operatorname{Vol}_{S^3\setminus K}(ho). 	ag{15} \] A trivial meridian would force a trivial knot representation by normal generation and give volume zero, but it is outside the noncentral unit midpoint chart used here. Combining (13) and (15) proves the actual-source calibration \[  oxed{\displaystyle \operatorname{Im}S_{m corr} =\operatorname{Vol}_{S^3\setminus K}(ho),\qquad  rac{2\pi}{N}\log|e^{S_{m corr}/h}| =\operatorname{Vol}_{S^3\setminus K}(ho).} 	ag{16} \] The second equality evaluates the exponential of the principal action. It is not an asymptotic assertion about the sum (1) in S. ## 5. What the actual filled-group gap now compares Fix a hyperbolic marked core and any earlier fixed short partial filling that is already part of that core, in G's scope. Fill the remaining designated cusps along sufficiently long primitive slopes \(\sigma_i=(a_i,b_i)\), and suppose the resulting physical exterior is the knot exterior under consideration. Use a literal braid of that actual filled knot in S, rather than an unfilled-parent source equipped only with peripheral eigenvalue equations. Every regular midpoint critical point of this full braid already gives a representation of its actual knot group, hence of the actual filled group. Its remaining main cusp is boundary-parabolic by Section 4. G therefore applies directly. For every such point whose underlying projective representation is not conjugate to the oriented filled geometric holonomy, \[ \operatorname{Im}S_{m corr} \le \operatorname{Vol}(M(\sigma)) -\min\left\{ rac{\delta}{2},  rac{3c_1}{\ell_{\max}^2}ight\}, \qquad \ell_{\max}=\max_i\sqrt{a_i^2+b_i^2}. 	ag{17} \] G's positive constants depend only on the fixed core and certificate. This is a uniform comparison of the regular principal critical rates of these actual full-word presentations. It needs no matching of a quantum Fourier label to a centered geometric slope charge: G uses the full filled-group relations of the representation. In contrast, a critical configuration of an unreduced parent partial-filling expression has not been shown by this argument to satisfy those full matrix relations. Applying (17) to such an expression still requires that source-to-group map and its action normalization. The equality of its final invariant with a knot invariant does not identify the separate critical configurations. ## 6. Equal-rate aliases and remaining source boundaries Different compatible logarithm or entropy sheets, central lifts, regular framing points, or retained flag descriptions of the same projective representation all have the same value in (16). Their corrected actions can have different real parts. The associated oscillatory phases, multiplicities and cycle coefficients have not been added or shown nonzero. In particular (17) does not separate copies of the geometric holonomy or prevent cancellation among them. The original compact source cycle of S is retained. Neither its nonstationary boundary contributions, its nonunit/support-wall strata, escaping decorations nor its centralizer relative current is controlled by (16)--(17). No integral upper bound, geometric intersection number, scalar lower bound or new volume-conjecture filling case is inferred. ## Complete proof-source pins * S: notes/research_soft_binomial_cut_stationary_source.md, SHA256 667cb1eb70b770552de05e6f95f518016852b2c0aecdc874c3dff167fccb3d8b. * Q: notes/quantum_longitude_and_regulator_action.md, SHA256 e8ac5dc6bab05be0dad3810311dc3a8b169ad810b898aa3db75582087dbe8aa7. * C: notes/crossing_fundamental_cycle.md, SHA256 0d7d7da0f5cf4fe0d16907e7e999d5ce7980f7ff39d437df167c99ca30205b0f. * G: notes/research_long_filled_group_representation_volume_gap.md, SHA256 977d61c32e9610dc5e3bd1750b50614c88473f28683ca5dcea5f23a8a88becc0. All four complete texts were read in the author sequence and their used implications checked. The general nonfaithful chain comparison already has the coverage described above; no novelty is claimed for it. The binomial character adapter and its application to the new principal critical scheme are explicit here. Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used; frozen and public files are unchanged.

title: The literal soft-cut Morse–Bott one-form
text: # The literal soft-cut Morse–Bott one-form Private written proof, 18 November 2026. The actual complex-binomial braid source has a nonzero leading one-form on its remaining complete geometric framing curve. With the original factorial and Gaussian square-root marks retained, that form is a representation-dependent constant times \(dr/s\). This is an amplitude calculation, including the finite \(N-1\) cut correction; it is not an inference from the principal centralizer vector field. The complete positive gluing certificate remains an explicit hypothesis. No relative framing period or physical cycle coefficient is calculated here. The older two-form/torsion comparison is used in its stated regularity range, and that range is checked below. ## 1. Source, coordinates, and the one-form being computed Let the fixed knot braid have \(b\) strands and \(c\) crossings, with \[ m=c+1,\qquad c_0=2\pi i,\qquad h=c_0/N. \tag{1} \] Use the actual integral chord coordinates and logarithmic occupations \(\zeta=c_0x\) of H and F. The unweighted logarithmic phase is \(S_0\), including the original pivotal and framing terms. Use the full correcting integer Fourier covector, including the cut entry. For a complex cut parameter \(\theta\) near \(1/2\), write \[ \Phi_\theta=S_0-c_0 n\cdot\zeta+g_\theta(u),\qquad g_\theta(u)=c_0 b_\theta(u/c_0), \tag{2} \] \[ b_\theta(t)=-t\log t-(1-t)\log(1-t) +t\log\theta+(1-t)\log(1-\theta). \] All logarithms are the compatible original ones. The geometric critical curve has \[ u=u_\theta=c_0\theta,\qquad s=s_\theta=e^{-c_0\theta}-1\ne0, \tag{3} \] and its remaining coordinate is \(r\). H proves that the Hessian in the actual \(m\) occupation coordinates has rank \(c\). These coordinates have already removed the common momentum; no further phase variable is quotiented here. Separate only the explicitly supplied occupation-independent factors of the literal source, such as its common Cartan scalars and any external modified-dimension line. Denote their unchanged product by \(E_N\). In equations (4) and (20), the phase is the phase of the quotient by \(E_N\): a constant exponential contained in \(E_N\) is not counted a second time in \(\Phi_\theta\). Equivalently one may restore that same constant term to the phase and remove its factor from \(E_N\). Neither convention changes any Hessian below. The line is never set to one or replaced by an unspecified normalization. In particular this convention does not retain an extra old cut average \(1/N\): the binomial weight multiplies the unnormalized diagonal partial-trace summand. In the variable-amplitude convention of D and Q, let \(a_{\rm lit}(\zeta)\) be the leading crossing/pivot amplitude of the actual factorial section A, after this separation. F gives \[ E_N^{-1}I_N(Nx)=N^{-m/2}a_{\rm lit}(c_0x) B_\theta(u/c_0)e^{\Phi_\theta(c_0x)/h}(1+O(N^{-1})), \tag{4} \] \[ B_\theta(t)=\frac{1-t}{(1-\theta)\sqrt{2\pi t(1-t)}}. \tag{5} \] The Fourier character in (4) is included in \(I_N\) for this formula. All fixed derivatives of the error are uniform on smaller regular slit charts. In F's complete Fourier expansion the selected integral has coefficient one; its relative boundary currents are unchanged. Choose local coordinates \((r,y_1,\ldots,y_c)\) with critical curve \(y=0\), and write \(d\zeta_1\wedge\cdots\wedge d\zeta_m=J(r,y)\,dr\wedge dy\). The logarithmic Gaussian one-form is, by definition, \[ \omega_\theta= \left. \frac{a_{\rm lit} B_\theta J} {\sqrt{\det(-\partial_y^2\Phi_\theta)}} \right|_{y=0}dr. \tag{6} \] The square root belongs to the transported normal Gaussian orientation line. Under a normal coordinate change the Hessian determinant gains the square of the normal Jacobian, so (6) is independent of that choice with its orientation line retained. Let \(\mathcal T_\beta\) be Q's actual holonomy torsion, with its specified ordered bases. Then the result is \[ \boxed{\quad \omega_\theta^2= i^{\,1-c}(-1)^b\frac{\mathcal T_\beta}{2} \left(\frac{dr}{s_\theta}\right)^2. \quad} \tag{7} \] The square does not choose a fresh sign. The actual factorial marks and one oriented normal Gaussian fix the nonzero constant in (6). ## 2. The fixed-trace regularity needed for the torsion comparison For completeness, the fixed-trace premise in Q follows here from H's exact fixed-eigencharacter rigidity; it is not inferred merely by differentiating the trace function at a parabolic. At a noncentral complete meridian \(\mu\), let its retained eigenvalue be \(\varepsilon=\pm1\). On every local Artin deformation with \(\operatorname{tr}\mu=2\varepsilon\) and \(\det\mu=1\), \[ \det(\mu-\varepsilon I)=0. \tag{8} \] A fixed nonzero entry of the original rank-one matrix \(\mu-\varepsilon I\) stays a unit. Eliminating with that entry shows that its kernel is a unique free rank-one direct summand. It is the exact eigenline for eigenvalue \(\varepsilon\), not an arbitrary invariant line with a nilpotently varying eigencharacter. Commuting peripheral matrices preserve this kernel. Thus the unaugmented fixed-trace deformation carries a canonical decoration of precisely the kind used in H's rigidity argument. H's positive-certificate comparison makes the decorated fixed-meridian quotient a point over these Artin rings. Conversely forgetting the canonical exact eigenline recovers the same fixed-trace deformation. Hence the kernel of the linearized braid fixed-point map consists exactly of simultaneous conjugation directions. In Q's notation the actual holonomy complex is therefore acyclic: \[ 0\longrightarrow\mathfrak{sl}_2\mathop{\longrightarrow}^{A}V \mathop{\longrightarrow}^{D=dF-I}V \mathop{\longrightarrow}^{M}\mathfrak{sl}_2\longrightarrow0. \tag{9} \] Here \(A\) is injective by irreducibility. Surjectivity of \(M\) can also be checked directly: an element annihilating the product differential under the trace pairing commutes successively with every meridian, and is zero. Rank-nullity then proves exactness. The torsion \(\mathcal T_\beta\) is nonzero and independent of the framing point. The latter follows either from Q's determinant ratio or from applying the same simultaneous conjugation to its two middle bases and the same adjoint map to its endpoint bases. Thus Q's comparison is applicable to this actual source. It is not an additional acyclicity assumption on an unrelated presentation. ## 3. The literal subprincipal crossing factors This step is needed because the chosen root-factorial section has a definite phase and \(N^{1/2}\) normalization. One must not insert only its leading dilogarithm into a torsion formula. At complete color put \(A=e^a,B=e^b,C=e^v\) for one crossing's two input log occupations and transfer. A proves that the squared single-factor amplitude is \(i(1-e^z)\). Its positive five-factor ratio therefore has squared amplitude \[ \frac1i\frac{(1-BC)(1-A)}{(1-B)(1-C)(1-A/C)}. \tag{10} \] After retaining its common Cartan scalar, the exact monomial in A contributes \(AB/C\) to that squared amplitude: the half-step in \(x=-q^{-1}\) gives \(AB\), and its last transfer factor gives \(C^{-1}\). Since \[ \frac{1-A}{1-A/C} =C\frac{1-1/A}{1-C/A}, \tag{11} \] the literal positive amplitude is \[ a_{{\rm lit},+}^2=i^{-1} AB\frac{(1-BC)(1-1/A)}{(1-B)(1-C)(1-C/A)} =i^{-1}a_+^2. \tag{12} \] For the negative crossing the exact monomial has squared subprincipal factor \(1/(AB)\): its \(q^n\) and last transfer half-step cancel. Applying (11) with \(B\) in place of \(A\) gives \[ a_{{\rm lit},-}^2=i^{-1} \frac C{AB}\frac{(1-AC)(1-1/B)} {(1-A)(1-C)(1-C/B)} =i^{-1}a_-^2. \tag{13} \] The quantities \(a_\pm\) are exactly D's balanced principal amplitudes, not amplitudes of a coherent transform. D proves their mixed-Hessian/momentum factorization, including both signs. Multiplying it through the actual word cancels internal momenta and retains the original pivotal multiplier. Consequently \[ a_{\rm lit}^2=i^{-c}a_\beta^2. \tag{14} \] The phases have the same Hessian. To check the reciprocal-factorial convention explicitly, the positive literal monomial has quadratic part \(ab-bv+\pi i(v-a-b)\). Inverting its reflected factorial pair adds \(av-v^2/2-\pi iv\), giving \(ab+(a-b)v-v^2/2-\pi i(a+b)\), the balanced phase. Negatively the corresponding two parts are \(-ab-bv+v^2/2+\pi i(a+b)\) and \(bv-v^2/2-\pi iv\), giving \(-ab+\pi i(a+b-v)\). The continued dilogarithm inversion identity follows by differentiation; its integration constant is independent of the occupations. Other compatible branch marks add their recorded affine Fourier characters and constants. They do not change the Hessian used here. No root phase is replaced by its modulus. ## 4. The unweighted two-form and the additional binomial Gaussian Before adding \(g_\theta\), the actual phase has its two framing directions. The incidence adapter in H applies with \(g=0\), and the same rigidity argument above gives precisely this smooth two-dimensional critical germ. Its complete-color coordinates are \[ F(r,s)=\begin{pmatrix}r&1-r\\s&-s\end{pmatrix},\qquad u=-\Log(1+s),\qquad \Omega_{\rm cut}=-\frac{dr\wedge ds}{s(1+s)} =\frac{dr\wedge du}{s}. \tag{15} \] Q proves, with the actual kernel/cokernel identification and original lattice cofactor, that its raw variable Gaussian two-form obeys \[ \Omega_{\rm raw}^2=(-1)^b\frac{\mathcal T_\beta}{2} \Omega_{\rm cut}^2. \tag{16} \] In particular this is the raw parity convention, not Q's separately parity-normalized square. Combining (14) and (16), the two-form from the literal factorial section is a marked constant times \(dr\wedge du/s\), with squared constant \(i^{-c}(-1)^b\mathcal T_\beta/2\). Choose \((r,u,y)\) as local coordinates before the binomial insertion, with \(y\) transverse to the two-dimensional critical surface and \(u\) the actual cut coordinate. The symmetric normal Hessian is invertible. Taylor expansion followed by its holomorphic symmetric matrix square root puts the unweighted phase into a quadratic normal form while keeping \(r,u\) fixed. Adding \(g_\theta(u)\) therefore adds one independent normal Gaussian. This proves the iterated Gaussian determinant formula here directly; no nonzero normal or tangential Jacobian is suppressed. The two needed scalar values are \[ B_\theta(\theta)^2=\frac1{2\pi\theta(1-\theta)},\qquad g_\theta''(u_\theta)=-\frac1{c_0\theta(1-\theta)}. \tag{17} \] Their quotient is \[ \frac{B_\theta(\theta)^2}{-g_\theta''(u_\theta)} =\frac{c_0}{2\pi}=i. \tag{18} \] The factor \((1-t)/(1-\theta)\) in (5) is the actual \(N-1\) correction; at this particular stationary value it is one. The calculation retains it before evaluation, including its derivatives. Equations (14), (16), and (18) prove (7). ## 5. Transport, original normalization, and retained currents On a connected marked chart, define \(C_\beta\) by \[ \omega_\theta=C_\beta\frac{dr}{s_\theta},\qquad C_\beta^2=i^{1-c}(-1)^b\mathcal T_\beta/2\ne0. \tag{19} \] Since the square is independent of \(r\), differentiating it proves \(\partial_r C_\beta=0\). Thus the leading actual one-form is invariant under \(s_\theta\partial_r\). Its constant remains on the original factorial/Gaussian orientation line; independently changing a square-root sign is not the same marked continuation. There are no additional finite-\(r\) poles on this regular source fiber. Boundary degenerations or a changing representation can still affect the torsion and its domain. For clarity, the original scalar normalization can be restored without choosing it from the torsion. The measure in a Fourier integral is \(N^m dx=c_0^{-m}N^m d\zeta\). Formal integration of only its \(c\) normal variables therefore has leading one-form \[ E_N N^{1/2}(2\pi)^{c/2}c_0^{c/2-m} e^{\Phi_\theta(\zeta_*)/h}\omega_\theta. \tag{20} \] All powers in (20) use the same normal orientation. A different explicit external normalization multiplies \(E_N\) by precisely that whole factor. It does not alter (19). Uniformity with a relative \(O(N^{-1})\) error on compact \(r\)-charts follows from A/F's derivative bounds and H's holomorphic normal form: on a small descending normal ball the Gaussian tail is exponentially small, odd Taylor terms integrate to zero, and the first remaining Taylor terms have order \(h\). This constructs a local normal integral, not a deformation of the original global chain to it. The weighted Ward source has not been replaced by an invariant trace. Put \(P_\theta\) equal to the actual binomial cut tensor the original pivots. For every one of its ordered weighted Ward terms, and every marked word \(O\), finite matrix cyclicity gives the exact identity \[ \operatorname{Tr}(P_\theta[X,A B]O) =\operatorname{Tr}([P_\theta,X]A B O) +\operatorname{Tr}(P_\theta A B[O,X]). \tag{21} \] Summing (21), with the actual weights and any prescribed factor \(1/h\), retains all cut, pivotal and marked-word currents. Nothing in (12)--(20) sets either term on its right to zero. The leading invariance in (19) was obtained from the actual subprincipal amplitude and determinant, not by discarding those currents. An additional observable with leading symbol \(o(r)\), when its same local expansion is justified, multiplies (19) by \(o(r)\); no invariance or absence of poles is asserted for arbitrary marks. Finally, on the affine fiber (19) has primitive \(C_\beta r/s_\theta\). Compact closed loops have zero leading period. A specified finite-endpoint relative chain would pair as \(C_\beta/s_\theta\) times its signed endpoint sum, but the original chain's transverse pushforward and any infinity regularization remain unproved here. The one-form does not supply their values. ## Complete proof-source pins * A: notes/research_literal_crossing_slit_chart_amplitude.md, SHA256 c3682b0f84000aad4c2f53235b9c93bbd86283905a75d6f07ac03b1a3c00bc4a. * D: notes/actual_cut_residue_and_principal_density.md, SHA256 31ae47377d3fff90f177020e18ab1394866facdf9b783aa7823b52d2cebd0bda. * Q: notes/quantum_source_bridge_extension.md, SHA256 c8f75699921a83cbc2c5cc533b7b8441cf185f9cd45b130b44ad453ea6d734fb. * H: notes/research_positive_certificate_braid_morse_bott.md, SHA256 6ef5423e542170ffe3b5464753613ae042341d9c2ee20a2fa94fd0d828738410. * F: notes/research_oblique_top_fourier_aliases.md, SHA256 9fa4d981c401c1b744fa12b1241f0404d7ba8da90d21f6b90f556ef6a065b584. title: An exact two-mode Gaussian source for the binomial cut
text: # An exact two-mode Gaussian source for the binomial cut Private written proof, 18 November 2026. The binomial cut has a finite Gaussian presentation at a bulk coherent occupation. Two oscillator modes with fixed total degree \(d=N-1\) realize the original finite head. Composition of the literal local kernels is exact, and the binomial closing is a fixed-radius latitude evaluation with a normalization bounded above and below by constants times \(\sqrt d\). This construction does not continue the old small-clock Borel germ to the bulk. It gives a finite-level integral before an asymptotic expansion, retains the full occupation projector, and transports finite matrix currents. It is not identified with the previous finite-\(R\) Borel coarea chain. The complete proof directs are C, the actual compact coherent source, and S, the binomial cut and normal-residue density. Their pins appear at the end. The Gaussian and factorial calculations needed here are proved directly. ## 1. The finite head in a two-mode Gaussian space Fix \(N\ge2\) and \(d=N-1\ge1\). Use the original head basis \(e_0,\ldots,e_d\), with all matrix entries in the conventions of C and S. On \(\mathbb C^2\), write \(Z=(Z_0,Z_1)\) and use \[ d\gamma(Z)=\pi^{-2}e^{-|Z_0|^2-|Z_1|^2}\,d^2Z_0\,d^2Z_1. \tag{1} \] Angular integration and one-dimensional integration by parts give \[ \int_{\mathbb C^2}Z^\alpha\overline Z^\beta\,d\gamma(Z) =\mathbf1_{\alpha=\beta}\alpha!. \tag{2} \] Indeed each radial factor is \(\int_0^\infty t^a e^{-t}dt=a!\), starting with the unit integral and integrating by parts \(a\) times. Embed the finite head as the homogeneous degree-\(d\) subspace by \[ e_j\longmapsto u_j(Z) =\frac{Z_1^jZ_0^{d-j}}{\sqrt{d!}}, \qquad 0\le j\le d. \tag{3} \] Then \[ \langle u_i,u_j\rangle_\gamma =\delta_{ij}\frac{j!(d-j)!}{d!} =\frac{\delta_{ij}}{\binom dj}. \tag{4} \] This is exactly C's coherent head metric. No claim that the literal braiding is unitary in this metric is made. For an arbitrary finite matrix \(A=(A_{ij})\), define its kernel \[ \mathcal K_A(Z,\overline W) =\sum_{i,j=0}^d A_{ij}\binom dj\, u_i(Z)\overline{u_j(W)} =\frac1{d!}\sum_{i,j=0}^d A_{ij}\binom dj Z_1^iZ_0^{d-i} \overline W_1^{\,j}\overline W_0^{\,d-j}. \tag{5} \] The binomial belongs to the input index. The kernel acts on the embedded basis by \[ \int\mathcal K_A(Z,\overline W)u_j(W)\,d\gamma(W) =\sum_iA_{ij}u_i(Z). \tag{6} \] Thus the map is injective and uses the literal finite matrix. ## 2. Exact local composition, trace and occupation projector Using (2)--(4) on the middle index proves \[ \boxed{\quad \int_{\mathbb C^2} \mathcal K_A(Z,\overline X)\mathcal K_B(X,\overline W) \,d\gamma(X)=\mathcal K_{AB}(Z,\overline W),\qquad \int\mathcal K_A(Z,\overline Z)\,d\gamma(Z)=\operatorname{Tr}A. \quad} \tag{7} \] All integrands here are finite polynomials times a Gaussian, so these are absolutely convergent integrals. Tensor products use one pair of modes for each physical head and product measures. Rectangular maps between tensor products use the same output monomials and dual input monomials; their composition proof is the identical index contraction. In particular the identity head has kernel \[ \Pi_d(Z,\overline W) =\frac{(Z_0\overline W_0+Z_1\overline W_1)^d}{d!} =[t^d]\exp\!\left(t(Z_0\overline W_0+Z_1\overline W_1)\right). \tag{8} \] It is the orthogonal projection onto total degree \(d\), rather than the identity on the full oscillator space. This can be checked on every monomial using (2): all total degrees other than \(d\) are annihilated. The coefficient in (8) can equivalently be retained as a Cauchy integral on any fixed small \(t\)-circle. Neither a degree tail nor a boundary coefficient is discarded. Both mode occupations are nonnegative. Their fixed sum is \(d\); hence the physical occupation \(j\) lies exactly in \(\{0,\ldots,d\}\). This is a coupled sector condition, not two independent approximations to a cutoff. To display the extreme physical walls explicitly, \[ \mathcal K_{T_0}(Z,\overline W) =\frac{(Z_0\overline W_0)^d}{d!},\qquad \mathcal K_{T_d}(Z,\overline W) =\frac{(Z_1\overline W_1)^d}{d!}. \tag{9} \] Any actual finite generator relation with lower or upper projector terms therefore has its exact kernel counterpart under (7). The finite pivots remain their actual matrices inside the same formula. The map does not replace them by an oscillator trace or a classical value. ## 3. The bulk latitude and its normalization For \(|v|=1\), set \[ Z_d(v)=\sqrt{d/2}\,(1,v),\qquad |Z_d(v)|^2=d. \tag{10} \] C's full coherent symbol at latitude \(T=1/2\) is \[ f_C(v,1/2)=2^{-d} \sum_{i,j=0}^d C_{ij}\binom dj\,v^{\,i-j}. \tag{11} \] Direct substitution in (5) gives \[ e^{-d}\mathcal K_C(Z_d(v),\overline{Z_d(v)}) =e^{-d}\frac{d^d}{d!}f_C(v,1/2). \tag{12} \] Put \[ A_d=\frac{e^d d!}{d^d}. \tag{13} \] The exact soft-cut identity is consequently \[ \boxed{\quad \operatorname{Tr}(P_N^{\rm cut}C) =\frac{A_d}{2\pi i} \oint_{|v|=1} e^{-d}\mathcal K_C(Z_d(v),\overline{Z_d(v)}) \frac{dv}{v},\qquad P_N^{\rm cut}=\sum_{j=0}^d2^{-d}\binom djT_j . \quad} \tag{14} \] On this contour \(\overline v=v^{-1}\); thus (14) is also a finite Laurent contour identity. Angular integration kills \(i\ne j\), with the original diagonal coefficients left intact. Each fixed angular point is a trace-one rank-one probe: \[ (\mathcal P_v)_{ab}=2^{-d}\binom da\,v^{\,b-a}, \qquad \mathcal P_v^2=\mathcal P_v,\quad \operatorname{Tr}\mathcal P_v=1. \tag{15} \] It is positive in the metric (4), and \(\operatorname{Tr}(\mathcal P_vC)=f_C(v,1/2)\). The average of these probes is exactly \(P_N^{\rm cut}\). This does not make an arbitrary closed word or marked current positive. S proves equality of (14) with the original unmarked scalar and supplies its exact marked-cut transgression. ## 4. Polynomial conditioning, proved without Stirling's formula The normalization (13) satisfies, for every integer \(d\ge1\), \[ e^{-1/2}\sqrt d\le A_d\le10\sqrt d. \tag{16} \] Here is a direct proof. The gamma integral from (2), followed by \(t=dx\), gives \[ A_d=d\int_0^\infty e^{-d\psi(x)}\,dx,\qquad \psi(x)=x-1-\log x. \tag{17} \] For \(1\le x\le1+d^{-1/2}\), one has \(\psi(x)\le(x-1)^2/2\), because \(\psi(1)=\psi'(1)=0\) and \(\psi''(x)=x^{-2}\le1\) there. This gives the lower bound in (16). On \([1/2,2]\), \(\psi''\ge1/4\), so \(\psi(x)\ge(x-1)^2/8\). This part of (17) is at most \(\sqrt{8\pi d}<6\sqrt d\). For \(x\ge2\), \(\psi'(x)\ge1/2\), so its part is at most \(2e^{-d\psi(2)}\le2\sqrt d\). Finally \(\psi\) decreases on \((0,1)\), and \(\psi(1/2)=\log2-1/2\ge1/6\). For completeness \(\log2\ge2/3\) follows by integrating the tangent-line lower bound \(1/x\ge4/3-4x/9\) on \([1,2]\). The remaining part is therefore at most \((d/2)e^{-d/6}\le\sqrt d\); the last inequality follows by maximizing \(\sqrt t\,e^{-t/6}/2\) for \(t>0\). Their sum is below the upper constant in (16). The proof includes \(d=1\). There is a useful exact probabilistic normalization check. Let \(J_0,J_1\) be independent Poisson variables of means \(d/2,d/2\). Then \[ \Pr(J_0+J_1=d)=e^{-d}\frac{d^d}{d!}=A_d^{-1},\qquad \Pr(J_1=j\mid J_0+J_1=d)=2^{-d}\binom dj. \tag{18} \] Both equations follow by the binomial theorem in the finite sum \(J_0+J_1=d\). Thus the bulk cut is an exact conditioning at the mean total occupation, with polynomial normalization. This statement concerns the cut probe. It does not change the coupled transfer variables or Poisson means inside an actual signed crossing. ## 5. A finite-word integral before asymptotic expansion Formula (14) need not be applied after computing the unknown whole cut matrix. Factor that matrix by its given finite diagram: literal signed crossings, turn maps, pivots, marks, and the remaining finite partial traces. Apply (5) to each of those known local arrays, and (7) to every contraction. For example, for a one-head ordered product \(C=A_m\cdots A_1\), \[ \begin{split} \operatorname{Tr}(P_N^{\rm cut}C) ={}&\frac{A_d e^{-d}}{2\pi i}\oint\frac{dv}{v} \int\mathcal K_{A_m}(Z_d(v),\overline X_{m-1})\\ &\quad\cdot \mathcal K_{A_{m-1}}(X_{m-1},\overline X_{m-2}) \cdots \mathcal K_{A_1}(X_1,\overline{Z_d(v)}) \prod_{\ell=1}^{m-1}d\gamma(X_\ell). \end{split} \tag{19} \] The case \(m=1\) means no internal integral. Multi-head words and the actual partially traced knot network use the tensor and rectangular versions of the same identity. Their number of Gaussian mode pairs depends on the fixed diagram, not on \(N\). All matrix coefficients are the original finite ones; no unknown scalar defines a kernel or its normalization. All inserted identity wires use (8). Thus the formula retains every physical input/output occupation restriction, including restrictions shared by two legs of one crossing. Reordering integrations is legitimate because at fixed \(N\) their integrands are finite polynomials against product Gaussian measures. The only new outer cut normalization is (13). The factor \(e^{-d}\) in (19) is the recorded Gaussian weight at its fixed boundary radius, not an omitted scalar. For comparison with the compact source, ordinary radial coordinates give \[ d\gamma(Z)=e^{-t}t\,dt\,d\sigma(u),\qquad Z=\sqrt t\,u,\quad |u|=1, \tag{20} \] where \(d\sigma\) is normalized measure on \(S^3\). Since the trace kernel is homogeneous of bidegree \((d,d)\), its radial integral is \((d+1)!/d!=N\). The residual angular integral, after the scalar \(U(1)\) phase is removed, is exactly C's compact coherent trace with its factor \(N\). This verifies that (19) is a Gaussian presentation of the existing finite source, rather than a different quantum model. ## 6. Currents and the boundary of the conclusion The injective map (5) and product identity (7) transport every finite matrix identity, including its marked defects. In particular, S's exact equation \[ \operatorname{Tr}((P_N^{\rm cut}-T_0)C) =\operatorname{Tr}(B_N^{\rm cut}[C,\mathcal E]) \tag{21} \] is still the equality of the corresponding Gaussian kernel contractions. Commutators are Gaussian-composed kernels, not pointwise products of coherent symbols. Lower and upper projector terms remain the kernels (9). Their possibly small values at one latitude do not bound their composition with a growing source. At every fixed \(N\), differentiation in meridian or marking parameters commutes with these identities on compact subsets where the literal coefficient matrices are holomorphic: the integrands remain finite polynomial Gaussian moments. Consequently all finite meridian normals and marked endpoint currents are retained. This assertion gives no uniform large-\(N\) estimate for the differentiated whole word. The coefficient degree and literal entries in (19) grow with the level. A uniform analytic phase, amplitude or Gevrey bound on the bulk fields has not been obtained by Gaussian composition alone. In particular the old highest-cut small-clock germ cannot be evaluated at a singular bulk parameter merely because (19) exists. No Borel cutoff \(R\) was introduced in this construction. The earlier highest-cut coarea formula has a different relative chain and explicit upper-\(R\) derivative currents. Identifying that family with (19), including those currents, would require an additional source-preserving map; none is claimed here. The present gain is an exact finite Gaussian and conditioned-Poisson realization of the bulk cut, with polynomial outer normalization and complete finite walls. It supplies neither geometric-cycle occurrence nor a volume-conjecture lower bound. ## Complete proof-source pins * C: notes/compact_coherent_source_period.md, SHA256 8c6c3277367a4aa6c69269da635139d5f881f3d3d0d894e04dd97028d76537e4. * S: notes/research_binomial_cut_framing_density.md, SHA256 4bc6efc595fd6d59c0bc572d83495fb779cff230ff1cb9c14429a0b7c6a2a1b0. C supplies the original basis, coherent metric and local source kernels with their exact composition and wall scope. S supplies the source-preserving binomial cut and full marked transgression. The two-mode embedding, Gaussian integral, projector, bulk normalization and finite-word adapter are proved above. Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used. Frozen sources and public files are unchanged.

title: An exact source repair for correlated coherent windows
text:
# An exact source repair for correlated coherent windows Private written proof, 19 November 2026. The original pointed source admits an exact correlated coherent cutoff after an exponentially small correction in one explicit coupon direction. A polynomially bounded projection onto the actual lowering commutant also gives a stronger Neumann repair at matrix level. Both amplitudes are close to the original matrix in the whole-operator norm budget. The source equalities are exact, even when that scalar is zero. The complete directs C, F, and X are pinned below. C supplies a literal root radical coupon and its pivotal partial trace; F supplies the actual meridian frame; X supplies the capped Euclidean off-matching estimate. The projection, its calibration, and the convergent source repair are proved here. The earlier raw averaged co-source lift was checked for coverage; it is not an input to these proofs. ## 1. Matrices, metric, and the original functional Fix an integer width \(m\ge2\), and let \[ N\ge2,\quad d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2, \quad M=e^\mu,\quad x=-M/q,\quad x_0=-q^{-1}. 	ag{1} \] The vectors \(w_0,\ldots,w_d\) are orthonormal in the physical coefficient Euclidean metric. Put \(V=\operatorname{span}\{w_0,\ldots,w_d\}\), \(\mathcal H_N=V^{\otimes m}\), \(D=N^m\), and \(J_jw_a=a w_a\) on head \(j\). All matrix norms use this metric. Write \(\|\cdot\|_2\) for the Hilbert--Schmidt norm, \(\|\cdot\|_1\) for trace norm, and \(\|\cdot\|_{m op}\) for operator norm. Superoperator norms below are induced by \(\|\cdot\|_2\) unless indicated otherwise. Retain the literal capped arrows \[ E(M)w_a=(MQ^{-a}-M^{-1})w_{a-1}\quad(a>0),\qquad E(M)w_0=0, \qquad K(M)w_a=xQ^{-a}w_a, \] \[ E_\Sigma(M)=\sum_{j=1}^m E_j(M)K_{j+1}(M)\cdots K_m(M), \qquad J_\Sigma=\sum_jJ_j. 	ag{2} \] Define the original highest-cut functional on every matrix by \[ Q_{m pt}(M)=|0angle\langle0|\otimes K_2(M)^{-d}\otimes\cdots\otimes K_m(M)^{-d}, \qquad \Phi_M(C)=\operatorname{Tr}(Q_{m pt}(M)C). 	ag{3} \] No pivot has been inserted on the opened first head. Original crossing, framing, or peripheral scalar factors remain in the matrix to which this functional is applied. In particular, with \(r=m-1\), \[ Q_{m pt}(M)=M^{-rd}Q_{m pt}(1). 	ag{4} \] Let \(\mathcal S_M=\ker\operatorname{ad}_{E_\Sigma(M)}\). This is a linear commutant inside \(\operatorname{End}(\mathcal H_N)\). We require only \(E_\Sigma(M)W(M)=W(M)E_\Sigma(M)\), as in X. Actual braid families satisfy this identity, but the construction does not depend on their word length or filling powers. Throughout the analytic statements choose buffered disks \(0<\eta<\eta'<\pi\), and suppose the families in question are holomorphic on a neighborhood of \(|N\mu|\le\eta'\). All true meridian derivatives keep \(q\) fixed. ## 2. A literal source-calibrating coupon C gives the following two-head root intertwiner, in the original coefficient basis: \[ R_N=N|\psiangle\langle\varphi|,\qquad |\psiangle=\sum_{a=0}^d x_0^{a-d}|a,d-aangle, \quad \langle\varphi|=\sum_{a=0}^d x_0^{-a}Q^{-a} \langle a,d-a|. 	ag{5} \] The covector here is algebraic, not the Hermitian adjoint of \(|\psiangle\). Its Euclidean functional norm, and the norm of \(\psi\), are both \(\sqrt N\). Consequently \[ R_N^2=0,\qquad \|R_N\|_{m op}=N^2,\qquad \operatorname{Tr}_2((I\otimes K_2(1)^{-d})R_N)=N I. 	ag{6} \] For the first identity use \(\langle\varphi|\psiangle=x_0^{-d}\sum_aQ^{-a}=0\). For the partial trace, the support in (5) makes it diagonal. The \(a\)-th entry is \(N x_0^{-d}Q^{-a}x_0^{-d}Q^{d(d-a)}=N\), using \(x_0^2=Q^{-1}\). Thus the calibration includes its actual pivot. Each adjacent embedding \(R_{j,j+1}\) commutes with the root total lowering arrow and preserves total integer degree. Indeed C proves local total \(E,K\) intertwining; the local \(E\) block in (2) commutes, as do the terms before it through the product of its two Cartans and the terms after it by disjoint support. Define, in the displayed order, \[ T_0=N^{-r}R_{12}R_{23}\cdots R_{m-1,m}. 	ag{7} \] Take the pivotal trace of the final head first. All preceding factors are independent of that head, and the last factor is precisely the one in (6). This removes it with multiplier \(N\). Repeat from right to left; the final first-head trace is \(\operatorname{Tr}|0angle\langle0|=1\). Hence \[ T_0\in\mathcal S_1,\quad [J_\Sigma,T_0]=0,\qquad \Phi_1(T_0)=1. 	ag{8} \] The chain has better norms than the product estimate. Since \(x_0^2=Q^{-1}\), the nonzero pair entry of \(R_N/N\) is \(x_0^{u+v-d}\), with output \((u,d-u)\) and input \((v,d-v)\). Successive contractions in (7) therefore give exactly \[ T_0|a_1,\ldots,a_{m-2},v,d-vangle =\sum_{u=0}^d x_0^{u+v-d} |u,d-u,a_1,\ldots,a_{m-2}angle, 	ag{8a} \] and zero if the last input pair does not sum to \(d\). At each intermediate pair the required occupation is forced, and its exponent cancels the preceding intermediate exponent. This proves (8a) for every width, including the empty list when \(m=2\). It is one rank-one pair matrix, tensored with an identity and followed by a tensor permutation. Thus \[ \|T_0\|_{m op}=N,\qquad \operatorname{rank}T_0=N^{m-2},\qquad \|T_0\|_2=N^{m/2}. 	ag{8b} \] This fixed coupon is known explicitly; it does not require dividing by the unknown source of a braid. It is not asserted to be a braid word or a positive matrix. Let \(P_E\) be the coefficient-Hilbert--Schmidt orthogonal projection onto \(\mathcal S_1\). Define \[ \mathcal P_1 C=P_EC+ [\Phi_1(C)-\Phi_1(P_EC)]T_0. 	ag{9} \] Its image is \(\mathcal S_1\), it is the identity there, and \(\Phi_1\mathcal P_1=\Phi_1\). It is therefore an exact source-preserving projection. Since \(\|\Phi_1\|_{2^*}=\|Q_{m pt}(1)\|_2=N^{r/2}\) and \(\|I-P_E\|_{2	o2}=1\), \[ \|\mathcal P_1\|_{2	o2} \le 1+N^{m-1/2}. 	ag{10} \] The same calibration gives the root functional bounds \[ N^{-m/2}\le\|\Phi_1|_{\mathcal S_1}\|_{2^*} \le N^{(m-1)/2}. 	ag{10a} \] The lower bound is obtained by evaluating on \(T_0/\|T_0\|_2\). It controls the functional on the whole commutant, not its value on a specified matrix or a selected geometric state. No spectral gap or inverse of \(\operatorname{ad}_E\) is used. The finite orthogonal projection exists independently of such a gap. Unitary degree conjugation preserves \(\mathcal S_1\), hence commutes with \(P_E\). The functional \(\Phi_1\) kills every nonzero integer degree and \(T_0\) has degree zero. Thus \(\mathcal P_1\) also commutes with degree conjugation and degree averaging. ## 3. The whole-meridian projection and its true jets Put \(f_a=\prod_{j=1}^a(1-Q^j)\), with \(f_0=1\), and set \[ h_a(M)=M^{-a} rac{f_a}{\prod_{j=1}^a(1-M^{-2}Q^j)}, \qquad D_h(M)w_a=h_a(M)w_a, \] \[ A(M)= igotimes_{j=1}^m[D_h(M)M^{-(m-j)J_j}], \qquad \mathcal G_M C=A(M)CA(M)^{-1}. 	ag{11} \] F proves, including the forced bottom zeros, \[ E_\Sigma(M)=A(M)E_\Sigma(1)A(M)^{-1}. 	ag{12} \] The same direct proves polynomial bounds for \(A^{\pm1}\) on the whole buffered scaled disk. Those estimates apply in the present metric: these matrices are diagonal, so their operator norms are the maxima of their entries in either diagonal head metric. Since \(A\) is diagonal it commutes with \(Q_{m pt}(1)\). Equations (3)--(4) give for every matrix \(C\), \[ \Phi_M(\mathcal G_MC)=M^{-rd}\Phi_1(C). 	ag{13} \] Define \[  oxed{\quad \mathcal P_M=\mathcal G_M\mathcal P_1\mathcal G_M^{-1}. \quad} 	ag{14} \] It is a holomorphic projection onto \(\mathcal S_M\), is the identity on that space, and preserves \(\Phi_M\) on every matrix. Equivalently, put \[ P_{E,M}=\mathcal G_MP_E\mathcal G_M^{-1},\qquad T_M=M^{rd}\mathcal G_MT_0. \] Then \(\Phi_M(T_M)=1\), and \[ \mathcal P_MC=P_{E,M}C+ [\Phi_M(C)-\Phi_M(P_{E,M}C)]T_M. 	ag{15} \] Off the root \(P_{E,M}\) need not be orthogonal. We assert only \(E_\Sigma(M)\)-commutation for \(T_M\); the frame (11) is not a simultaneous \(E,F\) trivialization. There exist constants \(C_\eta,b\), depending on the fixed width and larger collar, such that \[ \sup_{|N\mu|\le\eta'}\|\mathcal P_M\|_{2	o2} \le C_\eta N^b=:p_N. 	ag{16} \] Indeed (14) costs at most \((\|A\|_{m op}\|A^{-1}\|_{m op})^2\) times (10). For each fixed \(k\), Cauchy's formula on a further arbitrarily small collar buffer gives polynomial bounds with the factor \(N^k\) for \(\partial_\mu^k\mathcal P_M\) and \(\partial_\mu^kT_M\). All matrices remain at the fixed quantum root. For example, if \(\mathfrak a=\partial_\mu A|_0\), then \[ \partial_\mu\mathcal P_M|_0 =[\operatorname{ad}_{\mathfrak a},\mathcal P_1],\qquad \partial_\mu T_M|_0=rd\,T_0+[\mathfrak a,T_0]. 	ag{17} \] Thus neither the moving projection nor the pivot normal has been reset to its root value. Finite-dimensional Schatten norm comparison changes (16) only by the polynomial factor \(D^{|1/p-1/2|}\) for the induced \(S_p\)-norm. ## 4. The coherent cutoff is a positive superoperator Use the coefficient-Euclidean coherent vectors and probability measure \[ \psi_z=(1+|z|^2)^{-d/2}\sum_{a=0}^d\sqrt{ inom da}\,z^a w_a, \qquad d
u(z)= rac{d\Re z\,d\Im z}{\pi(1+|z|^2)^2}. 	ag{18} \] Tensor products are denoted by \(\psi_{\mathbf z}\), and \(d
u^{[m]}\) is the product measure. The exact resolution is \(N\int|\psi_zangle\langle\psi_z|d
u=I\). Consequently the map \[ (\mathscr SC)(\mathbf y,\mathbf z) =N^m\langle\psi_{\mathbf y},C\psi_{\mathbf z}angle 	ag{19} \] is an isometry from Hilbert--Schmidt matrices into the indicated \(L^2\) space: apply the resolution to both variables in its squared norm to obtain \(\operatorname{Tr}(C^*C)\). For completeness, choose precisely a window of X. On strict charts put \[ p(z)= rac{|z|^2}{1+|z|^2},\quad e(z)= rac z{|z|}(e^{-2\pi i p(z)}-1),\quad k(z)=-e^{-2\pi i p(z)},\quad \epsilon(\mathbf z)=\sum_j e(z_j)\prod_{\ell>j}k(z_\ell). \] Choose \(0\le\kappa\le1\) smoothly supported in a compact strict chart for both variables, \(\gamma>0\), and a smooth \(0\le\vartheta\le1\) which vanishes below \(\gamma^2\) and equals one above \(4\gamma^2\). Set \[ b=\kappa\vartheta(|\epsilon(\mathbf y)-\epsilon(\mathbf z)|^2), \qquad \chi=1-b. 	ag{20} \] The fixed cutoff keeps the entire real observable-matching locus and all occupation endpoints. It is independent of \(N,\mu,W\). Define multiplication operators \(M_\chi,M_b\) in the \(L^2\) space of (19), and the finite matrix superoperators \[ \mathcal L=\mathscr S^*M_\chi\mathscr S,\qquad \mathcal R=I-\mathcal L=\mathscr S^*M_b\mathscr S. 	ag{21} \] They are self-adjoint positive contractions on Hilbert--Schmidt space, because their quadratic forms lie between zero and \(\|C\|_2^2\). In particular \(\|\mathcal L\|_{2	o2},\|\mathcal R\|_{2	o2}\le1\). This is positivity of superoperators; it does not assert that \(\mathcal L(C)\) is a positive matrix or that \(\mathcal L^2=\mathcal L\). Their exact synthesis formula is \[ \mathcal L(C)=N^{2m}\iint\chi(\mathbf y,\mathbf z) |\psi_{\mathbf y}angle \langle\psi_{\mathbf y},C\psi_{\mathbf z}angle \langle\psi_{\mathbf z}|\,d
u^{[m]}(\mathbf y)d
u^{[m]}(\mathbf z). 	ag{22} \] X proves, for every \(C\in\mathcal S_M\), uniformly on the larger scaled disk, \[ \|\mathcal R(C)\|_1\le C_0N^{2m}e^{-cN}\|C\|_{m op}. \] Its proof uses the literal finite matrices and capped propagation; it applies pointwise to every member of this commutant. Therefore \[ \|\mathcal R|_{\mathcal S_M}\|_{2	o2} \le \varepsilon_N:=C_0N^{2m}e^{-cN}. 	ag{23} \] The constants depend on width, window, and collar, not on the word length or integer filling powers of an eventual \(W\). ## 5. A single-coupon exact source repair The simplest repair uses only the known coupon \(T_M\). Set \[ z_N(M)=\Phi_M(\mathcal L(T_M)) =1-\Phi_M(\mathcal R(T_M)). 	ag{23a} \] Both \(\|T_M\|_2\) and \(\|Q_{m pt}(M)\|_2\) are polynomially bounded on the larger collar. Since \(T_M\in\mathcal S_M\), (23) gives \(|z_N-1|\le C N^B e^{-cN}\), uniformly there. In particular \(z_N\) is a holomorphic unit, bounded away from zero, for all \(N\ge N_0\), with \(N_0\) independent of \(W\). For any holomorphic \(W_N(M)\in\mathcal S_M\), define \[ W_N^\sharp=W_N+  rac{\Phi_M(\mathcal R(W_N))}{z_N(M)}T_M, \qquad C_N^\sharp=\mathcal L(W_N^\sharp). 	ag{23b} \] Then \(W_N^\sharp\) is still an exact lowering intertwiner, and \[ \Phi_M(C_N^\sharp)=\Phi_M(W_N),\qquad \|W_N^\sharp-W_N\|_2+\|C_N^\sharp-W_N\|_2 \le C N^B e^{-cN}\|W_N\|_2. 	ag{23c} \] Indeed \(\Phi_M(\mathcal L W_N)=\Phi_M(W_N)-\Phi_M(\mathcal R W_N)\), and the added term contributes precisely \(\Phi_M(\mathcal R W_N)\). Cauchy--Schwarz, (23), and the polynomial coupon bounds prove the first norm estimate; the contraction of \(\mathcal L\) and (23) prove the second. Thus the original source has the exact formula \[  oxed{\quad \Phi_M(W_N)=N^{2m}\iint\chi(\mathbf y,\mathbf z) \langle\psi_{\mathbf y},W_N^\sharp(M)\psi_{\mathbf z}angle \langle\psi_{\mathbf z},Q_{m pt}(M)\psi_{\mathbf y}angle d
u^{[m]}(\mathbf y)d
u^{[m]}(\mathbf z). \quad}	ag{23d} \] This uses a known linear functional of the discarded matrix, not division by the source of \(W_N\). The correction has one fixed explicit matrix direction. Cauchy's formula gives all fixed true meridian jets of (23c) on the smaller collar, with \(N^k\) per derivative and the supremum of \(\|W_N\|_2\) on the larger collar. All derivatives of (23d), including its pivot, are exact identities. ## 6. A stronger matrix repair by a convergent series Put \(\mathcal K_M=\mathcal P_M\mathcal R\) and \(q_N=p_N\varepsilon_N\). Its range lies in \(\mathcal S_M\), and \[ \|\mathcal K_M|_{\mathcal S_M}\|_{2	o2}\le q_N. 	ag{24} \] There is an \(N_0\), independent of \(W\), such that \(q_N<1/2\) for \(N\ge N_0\). For such levels and every holomorphic actual \(W_N(M)\in\mathcal S_M\), define \[ V_N(M)=\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}\mathcal K_M^jW_N(M),\qquad C_N^{m ex}(M)=\mathcal L(V_N(M)). 	ag{25} \] The inverse in (25) is holomorphic without choosing bases in moving commutants. Indeed \(\|\mathcal K_M\|\le p_N\) on all matrices, and its range property gives \(\|\mathcal K_M^j\|\le q_N^{j-1}p_N\) for \(j\ge1\). Thus the full-space Neumann series converges uniformly on the collar to \((I-\mathcal K_M)^{-1}\). Its restriction preserves \(\mathcal S_M\), so \(V_N\) remains an exact lowering intertwiner. Equations (23)--(25) yield the quantitative bounds \[ \|V_N\|_2\le rac{\|W_N\|_2}{1-q_N},\qquad \|V_N-W_N\|_2\le rac{q_N}{1-q_N}\|W_N\|_2, \] \[ \|C_N^{m ex}-\mathcal L(W_N)\|_2 \le rac{q_N}{1-q_N}\|W_N\|_2, \qquad \|C_N^{m ex}-W_N\|_2 \le rac{q_N+\varepsilon_N}{1-q_N}\|W_N\|_2. 	ag{26} \] The contraction of \(\mathcal L\) proves the first estimate on its second line; the last follows from \(C_N^{m ex}-W_N=V_N-W_N-\mathcal R(V_N)\). More strongly, the actual matrix and source identities are \[  oxed{\qquad W_N=\mathcal P_M C_N^{m ex},\qquad \Phi_M(W_N)=\Phi_M(C_N^{m ex}).\qquad} 	ag{27} \] Indeed \(V_N-\mathcal P_M\mathcal R(V_N)=W_N\) and \(\mathcal P_MV_N=V_N\), proving the first identity; source preservation proves the second. Combining it with (22) gives the promised exact formula, with the original coupon in its actual order: \[  oxed{\quad \Phi_M(W_N)=N^{2m}\iint\chi(\mathbf y,\mathbf z) \langle\psi_{\mathbf y},V_N(M)\psi_{\mathbf z}angle \langle\psi_{\mathbf z},Q_{m pt}(M)\psi_{\mathbf y}angle d
u^{[m]}(\mathbf y)d
u^{[m]}(\mathbf z). \quad}	ag{28} \] There is no division by \(\Phi_M(W_N)\), a coherent entry, or a selected coefficient. This equality includes zero sources. For every fixed \(k\), Cauchy's formula on the collar buffer gives \[ N^{-k}\sup_{|N\mu|\le\eta}  igl(\|\partial_\mu^k(V_N-W_N)\|_2+ \|\partial_\mu^k(C_N^{m ex}-W_N)\|_2 igr) \le C_k N^B e^{-cN} \sup_{|N\mu|\le\eta'}\|W_N(e^\mu)\|_2. 	ag{29} \] The constants and \(B\) are independent of the word or its filling powers. Dimension comparison gives corresponding Schatten estimates with polynomial costs. Since \(E_\Sigma\) is uniformly bounded, \([E_\Sigma,C_N^{m ex}]=[E_\Sigma,C_N^{m ex}-W_N]\) has the same kind of exponentially small norm and true-jet bounds. The same reasoning applies to \(C_N^\sharp\) by (23c). These currents need not vanish identically. Every derivative of (27)--(28) is an exact source equality. In particular \(\partial_\mu^kQ_{m pt}=(-rd)^kQ_{m pt}\), and the first derivative of (28) contains both \(\partial_\mu V_N\) and \(-rd\,V_N\). Any separately retained scalar line must multiply every term before differentiation. No root-only formula is being differentiated in place of the actual family. ## 7. Degree preservation and what the repair does not select One may choose \(\kappa\) in (20) invariant under the simultaneous rotation of all \(\mathbf y,\mathbf z\). Since \(\epsilon(e^{i	heta}\mathbf z)=e^{i	heta}\epsilon(\mathbf z)\), the resulting \(\chi\) is invariant too. The identity \(\psi_{e^{i	heta}\mathbf z}=e^{i	heta J_\Sigma}\psi_{\mathbf z}\) and a change of variables in (22) then show that \(\mathcal L\) and \(\mathcal R\) commute with degree conjugation. Equations (9)--(14) show the same for \(\mathcal P_M\). Hence a degree-zero \(W_N\) has degree-zero \(W_N^\sharp,C_N^\sharp,V_N,C_N^{m ex}\), without changing the source or any meridian jet. The construction for a general fixed cutoff is valid without this additional degree conclusion. The cutoffs in (23d) and (28) are integral cutoffs. The coherent kernel of either repaired marked matrix is obtained by another overlap integral; it need not vanish where \(\chi=0\). Neither \(P_E\), the radical calibrator, nor \(\mathcal P_M\) is asserted to preserve a complex phase, a local canonical graph, or a relative integration cycle. They are not algebra maps or positive matrix projections. The scalar correction is substantive. At any fixed level, \(\Phi_M(I)=x^{-rd}(\sum_{a=0}^dQ^{-a})^r=0\), although \(I\in\mathcal S_M\). But \[ \Phi_M(\mathcal R(I))=N^{2m}\iint b(\mathbf y,\mathbf z) \langle\psi_{\mathbf y},\psi_{\mathbf z}angle \langle\psi_{\mathbf z},Q_{m pt}(M)\psi_{\mathbf y}angle\,d
u d
u 	ag{30} \] need not vanish. On a protected nonempty open set where the strict matching gap exceeds \(2\gamma\), the displayed integrand is a nonzero real-analytic function: its numerator is a product of nonzero coherent-overlap polynomials, including the vacuum factor on head one. Choose a point where it is nonzero and a sufficiently small nonnegative smooth bump there; after a fixed scalar rotation the integrand has positive real part on that bump. It is an allowed \(b\) of (20), and (30) is nonzero. The whole-meridian factor is exactly \(M^{-rd}\); degree averaging does not change this scalar. This fixed-level test shows that an uncorrected window need not preserve the source kernel. It is not a knot or geometric-cycle counterexample. Only the original functional \(\Phi_M\) is exactly repaired. Writing \(\Phi_{{m top},M}(C)=\operatorname{Tr}(Q_{m top}(M)C)\) for X's top coupon, one has equality with \(\Phi_M\) on \(\mathcal S_M\), but cannot replace \(Q_{m pt}\) by \(Q_{m top}\) in either exact integral merely because its amplitude intertwines: the marked matrix is its image under \(\mathcal L\). Its two source values may differ. Their difference still has an exponentially small whole-norm budget by (23c), (26), and the bounded coupons; it has not been set to zero. The amplitude in (28) is close to the original matrix only on the scale \(\|W_N\|_2\). This scale may be exponentially larger than an individual geometric contribution or the original closed scalar. The window retains the full real matching locus and all endpoints, including competing contributions. Exact source repair therefore does not establish geometric component selection, a nonzero relative cycle coefficient, or an asymptotic lower bound. Its gain is an exact source-preserving cutoff representation with a quantitatively small matrix repair and no assumed commutator spectral gap. ## Complete directs and author verification * C: [research_prefix_commutant_and_pointed_normal_functional.md](research_prefix_commutant_and_pointed_normal_functional.md), 549 lines, SHA256 \(	exttt{b4fb801a1482316aebb4799f1d0b80d5b43ced39138d903c04cfde811ca166b0}\). * F: [research_actual_meridian_source_frames.md](research_actual_meridian_source_frames.md), 506 lines, SHA256 \(	exttt{6f58fba195ba5e8208e1d5180a1d684b933f9f5d50eb28efc56609580fe29976}\). * X: [research_euclidean_correlated_intertwiner_localization.md](research_euclidean_correlated_intertwiner_localization.md), 417 lines, SHA256 \(	exttt{12296ab7a60c3e424dcce9faf030c0f3299c14af64dd548d38dc254df3bbfdb2}\). title: A source-selected conserved channel and physical Gaussian compression
text: # A source-selected conserved channel and physical Gaussian compression 24 November 2026. Research note. Written proof. The actual cups of an even plat select one conserved channel exactly. At its source-selected parameter the complete conserved spectrum remains simple at every level, with controlled projectors and a known nonzero normalization of zero volume rate. Inside the selected channel its orthogonalizing metric is exactly the original physical metric. There is also a quantitative estimate on the previously constructed physical source spaces: a short operator block supported on at most half the heads retains its entire Hilbert--Schmidt norm up to an explicit power of the level. Thus a proved whole-block Hilbert--Schmidt model gives a relative operator model on the actual source, without an inverse fusion Gram. The original closing remains. These results do not give a relative scalar error or the hyperbolic value of the fixed-degree minimum. ## 1. The original source and the spaces being restricted Put \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\), \(x=-q^{-1}\), and take \(b=2k\ge2\) physical heads. Use the orthonormal balanced basis of H and G. Its actual complete generators are \[ Ke_a=xQ^{-a}e_a,\quad Ee_a=(Q^{-a}-1)e_{a-1},\quad Fe_a=(1-Q^{a+1})e_{a+1}, \tag{1} \] with the two missing arrows zero. Here \(E\) is the scaled generator. Totals use \(\Delta E=E\otimes K+1\otimes E\), \(\Delta F=F\otimes1+K^{-1}\otimes F\), and \(\mathsf K=K_1\cdots K_b\). The literal ordinary cup, ordinary cap and marked cap are, by H and P, \[ p_{uv}=Nx^{-v}\delta_{u+v,d},\qquad \ell_{uv}=x^u\delta_{u+v,d}/N,\qquad m_{uv}=x^v/N^2. \tag{2} \] The last has no degree delta. Keep the actual order of the paired heads, and put \(u_0=p^{\otimes k}\). Let \(\ell_0\) be the tensor of the original \(k-1\) ordinary top caps and the one full marked cap. For the actual unmarked signed braid operator \(R\), the scalar is \[ \mathcal K_N=\chi_N\ell_0Ru_0. \tag{3} \] All original turns, dual identifications, pivots and normalizations are in these data; \(\chi_N\) is the unchanged external scalar. No bound for it is inferred in an unreduced convention. The standard complete dual identification makes these the common total operators (1), not an unauthorized permutation of physical wires. Let \(\mathcal H=V_N^{\otimes b}\), with its physical norm, and define \[ T=kd,\quad \mathcal H_T=\operatorname{span}\{|a\rangle:\sum a_i=T\}, \qquad \mathcal I=\mathcal H_T\cap\ker\mathsf E\cap\ker\mathsf F. \tag{4} \] This is H's full root invariant space. Let \(\mathcal S\subset\mathcal I\) be the saturated specialization of the generic invariant lattice in U. It can be smaller than \(\mathcal I\). U and D already prove that the original cup source and its regular braid orbit lie in \(\mathcal S\), with the literal closing retained. They also give stronger invariant-space dimension reductions than the conserved channel used next. ## 2. The parameter selected by the cups is spectrally regular Use C's conserved operators \[ B_c=\mathsf F-(\mathsf E-cI)\mathsf K^{-1},\qquad H_c=B_c-2I, \quad p_N(z)=2iT_N\!\left(\frac{z}{2\sqrt q}\right), \quad \sqrt q=e^{\pi i/(2N)}. \tag{5} \] Here \(T_N\) is Chebyshev of the first kind. The auxiliary parameter is now \(c=2\). It is distinct from the eigenvalue \(2\) being selected. C proves on the full head space \(p_N(B_c)=\gamma^bp_N(c)I\), \(\gamma=(-1)^{N+1}\), with exact companion form and minimal polynomial of degree \(N\). Since \(b\) is even, the minimal polynomial at this parameter is \(p_N(z)-p_N(2)\). Here are estimates at \(c=2\), outside C's exterior-parameter range. Set \[ \theta=\frac{\pi}{2N},\quad s=\sin\theta,\quad \alpha=\operatorname{arsinh}\sqrt s,\quad \beta=\arcsin\sqrt s,\quad w=e^{\alpha-i\beta}. \tag{6} \] Then \(w+w^{-1}=2/\sqrt q\) exactly: its half-sum has real part \(\sqrt{1+s}\sqrt{1-s}=\cos\theta\) and imaginary part \(-s\). Also \[ (2N)^{-1/2}\le\alpha\le\sqrt{\pi/(2N)},\quad N\alpha\ge1, \quad |w^N-w^{-N}|\ge(1-e^{-2})e^{\sqrt{N/2}}. \tag{7} \] Indeed \(N^{-1}\le\sin\theta\le\pi/(2N)\) and \(z/\sqrt2\le\operatorname{arsinh}z\le z\) for \(0\le z\le1\). The roots are \(\lambda_j=\sqrt q(wQ^j+w^{-1}Q^{-j})\), \(0\le j<N\), with \(\lambda_0=2\). For \(v_j=wQ^j\), Chebyshev differentiation gives \[ |p_N'(\lambda_j)| =N\frac{|w^N-w^{-N}|}{|v_j-v_j^{-1}|} \ge\frac{1-e^{-2}}{2\sqrt2}N e^{\sqrt{N/2}}. \tag{8} \] The denominator is at most \(2\cosh\alpha\le2\sqrt2\). Thus every root is simple, at every \(N\), without a parity or prime-level exception. C gives its full eigenspace rank \(N^{b-1}\). The Lagrange spectral projectors satisfy \[ \|\Pi_j\|\le \frac{(4b+2+2\sqrt2)^{N-1}} {[(1-e^{-2})/(2\sqrt2)]N e^{\sqrt{N/2}}},\qquad G_2=\sum_j\Pi_j^*\Pi_j,\quad N^{-1}I\le G_2\le e^{C_bN}I. \tag{9} \] Here \(\|B_2\|\le4b+2\), and each \(|\lambda_j|\le2\sqrt2\). The denominator in the projector product is \(|p_N'(\lambda_j)|\). There is no product-of-nearest-gaps \(N\log N\) loss. Write \(\mathcal E_2=\ker(B_2-2I)\). Its exact projector is \[ \Pi_2=\frac{r_N(B_2)}{p_N'(2)},\qquad r_N(z)=\frac{p_N(z)-p_N(2)}{z-2}. \tag{10} \] The subscript denotes the eigenvalue, and \(r_N\) is a polynomial; no inverse of \(B_2-2I\) occurs. All complex phases of the derivative are retained. Its modulus has the explicit calibration \[ |p_N'(2)|=\frac{N|w^N-w^{-N}|}{2\sqrt{2\sin\theta}},\qquad \log|p_N'(2)|=\sqrt{\pi N/2}+\tfrac32\log N+O(1). \tag{11} \] For the first formula use \(|w-w^{-1}|^2=8\sin\theta\). For the second use \(\alpha=\sqrt\theta+O(\theta^{3/2})\) and \(|w^N-w^{-N}|=e^{N\alpha}(1+O(e^{-2N\alpha}))\). In particular this known nonzero projector normalization has zero exponential rate after division of its logarithm by \(N\). ## 3. Exact source selection and the physical norm The ordinary cup obeys \(E_{12}p=F_{12}p=0\), \(K_{12}p=p\). These follow termwise from (1)--(2), including the zero arrows; H and P already establish them for the original turns. Tensoring gives \[ \mathsf E u_0=\mathsf F u_0=0,\quad\mathsf K u_0=u_0, \quad B_2u_0=2u_0,\quad \mathcal K_N=\chi_N\ell_0\Pi_2R\Pi_2u_0. \tag{12} \] Every actual unmarked signed crossing intertwines the totals. Thus no other coideal channel contributes to this source. This selection is not inferred from a preferred geometric eigenvalue. It is an exact consequence of the original incoming cups. In particular \(e^{rH_2/h}u_0=u_0\) and \(e^{rH_2/h}Ru_0=Ru_0\) for every finite \(r\), where \(h=2\pi i/N\). This removes a redundant finite gauge direction; it constructs no nontrivial relative geometric transport. The eigenvalue alone does not select the discrete-faithful critical branch. For \(v\in\mathcal E_2\), \(\Pi_2v=v\) and the other projectors kill it. Hence \(\langle G_2v,v\rangle=\|v\|^2\): the channel metric is exactly the original physical norm on that whole space. Moreover \[ \mathcal S\subset\mathcal I =\mathcal E_2\cap\mathcal H_T. \tag{13} \] Indeed \(\mathsf K=1\) on \(\mathcal H_T\), so \((B_2-2)v=\mathsf Fv-\mathsf Ev\) there. Its two terms have different integer degrees \(T+1,T-1\), even at \(N=2\), and must vanish separately. This does not identify \(\mathcal S\) with the larger root invariant space, or identify \(\Pi_2\) with an orthogonal projection onto their intersection. ## 4. A physical norm test for an entire short block Consider a contiguous block of \(1\le r\le k\) heads. Let \(A_N\) be a regular original integer-degree-preserving Hopf-intertwining endomorphism supported on this block, such as a fixed unmarked signed braid block. Its generic lift is required when using \(\mathcal S\). Let \(A_N^{\rm glob}\) include the spectator identities. For each \(\mathcal T\in\{\mathcal S,\mathcal I,\mathcal E_2\}\), \[ \boxed{\quad N^{-r/2}\|A_N\|_{\rm HS} \le\|A_N^{\rm glob}|_{\mathcal T}\|_{\rm op} \le\|A_N\|_{\rm op}. \quad} \tag{14} \] These are physical operator norms. Every indicated space is preserved. Here is an original-source witness for the lower bound. Let \(L,R\) be the outside head counts, \(L+R=2k-r\). Choose an integer \[ \max(0,r-R)\le a\le\min(r,L),\qquad a\equiv L\pmod2. \tag{15} \] Such an integer exists: if the interval contains consecutive integers both parities occur; if it is a singleton, \(2k-2r\) even forces the stated parity. Pair the first \(a\) block heads, nested in order, to the closest left outside heads. Pair the remaining block heads nested to the closest right outside heads. Fill the even leftover outside intervals by adjacent ordinary cups. This is a noncrossing matching made from actual cups, not a free physical permutation. Normalize this tensor to a unit vector \(v\). It has a regular generic cup lift, so \(v\in\mathcal S\). Every block head has its own outside partner. Since every cup coefficient has constant modulus, the block reduced density of \(v\) is exactly \(I/N^r\). Thus \(\|A_N^{\rm glob}v\|^2=\|A_N\|_{\rm HS}^2/N^r\), proving (14). All cup phases and normalizations were used before normalization. This applies to a whole supported short block, not merely one entry. Let \(Q_{\mathcal T}\) denote the physical orthogonal projector onto one of these spaces. A supplied whole-block model \(D_N\) gives \[ \|A_N^{\rm glob}|_{\mathcal T} -Q_{\mathcal T}D_N^{\rm glob}|_{\mathcal T}\|_{\rm op} \le\|A_N-D_N\|_{\rm HS}. \tag{16} \] Only the pair/block error is used; spectator identities have operator norm one. If \(A_N\ne0\), a relative Hilbert--Schmidt error \(\varepsilon_N\) therefore becomes a relative operator error at most \(N^{r/2}\varepsilon_N\). The model itself need not preserve the source before this orthogonal compression. A whole-block approximation must actually be proved; it is not supplied by (14). ## 5. The full physical crossing Gaussian on the source For \(b\ge4\), use (14) with \(r=2\) and either signed crossing. For every fixed integer \(J\ge0\), G's zero-tilt full physical model \(\mathcal G_{N,J}^{\pm}\), with all exact entry phases and support retained, obeys \[ \|R^{\pm}-\mathcal G_{N,J}^{\pm}\|_{\rm HS} \le C_JN^{-(J+1)/2}\|R^{\pm}\|_{\rm HS}. \tag{17} \] Consequently its source orthogonal compression has relative operator error at most \(C_JN^{-(J-1)/2}\), independently of the spectator width. One may instead first project the pair model orthogonally onto the full physical algebra \(\mathbb C[\Omega]\), as G proves. This contracts the error. The resulting polynomial \(f_N(\Omega)\) has a regular generic lift using the same coefficients and the generic Casimir. It therefore preserves all three source spaces, including \(\mathcal S\), without a subsequent global projection. No Casimir value quotient is used: its first-normal channels remain. There is no fusion-coordinate conditioning or spectator Hilbert--Schmidt factor in this relative operator estimate. In particular (14) and G give \[ \log\|R_i^{\pm}|_{\mathcal T}\|_{\rm op} =\frac{2G_{\rm Cat}}\pi N+O_b(\log N). \tag{18} \] Here \(G_{\rm Cat}=\sum_{a\ge0}(-1)^a/(2a+1)^2\) is Catalan's constant. This Gaussian assertion is at sufficiently large levels for each fixed order. At two heads the source remains exact but this two-head norm comparison is not asserted. The models are not declared exact inverses or a new braid representation. ## 6. The literal closing still has to observe the propagated vector There are simple polynomial bounds in the same physical metric: \[ \|u_0\|=N^{3k/2},\qquad N^{-3k/2}\le\|\ell_0|_{\mathcal T}\| \le N^{-(k+2)/2},\qquad \mathcal T=\mathcal S,\mathcal I. \tag{19} \] For the upper bound ordinary caps force degree \(d\) on their pairs. On the central degree \(kd\), the last marked pair then also has degree \(d\). Its restricted row has norm \(N^{-3/2}\), and the ordinary rows contribute \(N^{-(k-1)/2}\). This is P's permitted whole-degree restriction, not a replacement of an arbitrary marked cap. For the lower bound use the actual cyclic noncrossing cup matching \((1,2k),(2,3),(4,5),\ldots,(2k-2,2k-1)\). It has a regular generic lift, norm \(N^{3k/2}\), and its literal pairing with \(\ell_0\) is exactly one. Indeed all odd indices become one index \(a\), all even indices \(d-a\); the monomial powers in (2) cancel, and each of the \(N\) remaining summands is \(1/N\). This proves (19) on both source spaces. Thus the bare linear root row \(A\mapsto\ell_0Au_0\) on \(\operatorname{End}(\mathcal T)\) has Hilbert--Schmidt dual norm between \(1\) and \(N^{k-1}\). If \(\chi_N\) is included in that row, multiply both bounds by \(|\chi_N|\). H and D already supply stronger source restrictions and polynomial boundary estimates in their stated frames. The additions here are the source-selected spectrally regular coideal channel and the quantitative physical block/Gaussian norm test. They can supply known budgets to an existing fixed-degree compiler; no new capacity identity is needed. The remaining scalar is still exactly \(\chi_N\ell_0Ru_0\). A lower bound for a row norm gives no lower bound for its value on this particular propagated vector. Neither (16) nor an all-order local relative operator model gives a relative scalar error after an arbitrary word and closing. The geometric value and noncancellation after fixed short partial fillings remain unproved. Fixed polynomial degree bounds neither the growing source dimension nor this missing precision. All results here are complete-root values, not off-root normal jets. ## Complete sources and closest coverage | Label | Complete text | Lines | SHA256 | | --- | --- | ---: | --- | | C | [Conserved coideal channels](research_conserved_coideal_braid_channels.md) | 437 | b2a8c539742b4662ab8acbf4dc11c9bfa6acd27e895653ccfc47848278899fd4 | | H | [Complete original invariant module](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_complete_source_multiplicity_module.md) | 602 | 14cfb558f50c5b091cec9439692dfeb87129e31f38588cb1ebfd8e8547ac99a9 | | G | [Whole physical crossing Gaussian](research_full_physical_crossing_gaussian_packet.md) | 306 | 7f1b9932f88aa549bc55088b6f056f5a362548bc51c9fdd7c6b00469e725f531 | | U | [Saturated source and uniform confluence](research_uniform_fusion_confluence_source.md) | 439 | c39b8eaab1e1b4fcd1cdf7bc034a5a4419a33d40e058c2b6d6d06f8096414864 | | D | [Earlier divided source projection](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_all_width_divided_source_projection.md) | 204 | dc83b5e232a3d258f516a479d7257e85b9e5663a38e166f07c6ad9ae81004a68 | | P | [Original cup/cap Gram supports](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_plat_cup_cap_gram_support.md) | 229 | d780592fac1067eba868d2a8939ea1bf6a4191361d1c100eefe789833fe1451d | Only written mathematics, source reads and text/hash operations were used.
