title: A general convex action gap for split endpoint currents
text:
# A general convex action gap for split endpoint currents Private written proof, 15 November 2026. At an original positive primitive solution, every admitted deleted angle action associated with a nonzero endpoint current of a suitable even-factor Ward implementation is strictly smaller than the full action. The comparison does not require that the deleted assignment extend to the original unit-charge constraint face. Instead it uses the supporting affine function of the original angle energy on the whole angle body. Its charge correction has the favorable sign. This is a general geometric comparison for arbitrary signed powers and arbitrary vertex subsets in a fixed original circle tree. It also compares every nonzero integer charge of the deleted forest. The exact finite current is a scalar times that forest, with all original closures retained. A bound on the complete quantum forest still has to be proved before the geometric comparison becomes a bound on its whole current; no contour or geometric coefficient is inferred here. ## 1. The original angle body without the filling constraints Fix an original finite circle tree, a nonempty selected vertex set \(S\), and every edge incident to \(S\), counted once. Each selected vertex has positive original degree. Denote the number of these edges by \(e_G\). Fix the full outside angles \(t_b=s_b+i h_b\), the signed integer powers \(n_v\), and the original unit-charge equations \[ \sum_{e
i v}r_{v,e}- rac{i n_vt_v}{2}=-\pi i \qquad(v\in S). 	ag{1} \] Assume they have a positive solution on the canonical original edge branches. In physical filling notation \(n_v=\eta_v-2p_v\); neither the original marking \(\eta_v\) nor the slope \(p_v\) will be changed. Write \(t_v=s_v+i h_v\) and \(r_{v,e}=k_{v,e}+i g_{v,e}\). The variables of the real angle body are the selected \(s_v\)'s and all endpoint incidences \(g_{v,e}\), including incidences at fixed outside vertices. The outside \(s_b\)'s stay fixed. Define \(X\) by the strict inequalities \[ |s_v|+2|g_{w,e}|<\pi,\qquad |s_w|+2|g_{v,e}|<\pi \qquad(e=\{v,w\}), 	ag{2} \] and let \(\overline X\) use their weak versions. There are no filling constraints in the definition of \(X\). Since the positive solution belongs to \(X\), it is nonempty, and \(\overline X\) is its compact closure in the affine space with the outside \(s_b\)'s fixed. For an edge oriented from \(v\) to \(w\), use the original square coordinates \[ A_P=s_v/4-g_{w,e}/2,\quad A_Q=s_v/4+g_{w,e}/2,\qquad y_P=g_{v,e}/2+s_w/4,\quad y_Q=g_{v,e}/2-s_w/4. 	ag{3} \] The square energy is the normalized original function \[ dE_\square=x\,dA+B\,dy,\qquad E_\square(0,0)=0, \quad x=	frac12\operatorname{arsinh}(	an(2A)\cos(2y)),\quad B=	frac12\operatorname{arsinh}(	an(2y)\cos(2A)). 	ag{4} \] It is strictly convex on the open square and continuous on the closed square. Its simultaneous reflection satisfies \(E_\square(-A,-y)=E_\square(A,y)\), by (4) and normalization. The full energy, with the prescribed imaginary outside angles, is \[ \mathcal E(z)=4\sum_e(E_{\square,P,e}+E_{\square,Q,e}) -\sum_{b
otin S}h_b\sum_{e
i b}g_{b,e}. 	ag{5} \] The square-coordinate map is injective: all selected vertex angles are recoverable because every selected vertex has an incidence. Thus \(\mathcal E\) has positive definite Hessian on \(X\), and is continuous and convex on \(\overline X\). The outside work in (5) is linear and does not affect this Hessian. Let \(z_0\in X\) be the original solution. Put \[ ho_v(z)=\sum_{e
i v}g_{v,e}-n_vs_v/2,\qquad h_v^0=\operatorname{Im}t_v^0,\qquad H_v=-h_v^0. 	ag{6} \] The original edge differential and the real parts of (1) imply, as an identity on the full ambient tangent space, \[ d\mathcal E(z_0)=\sum_{v\in S}h_v^0\,dho_v,\qquad ho_v(z_0)=-\pi. 	ag{7} \] Indeed the selected \(ds_v\)-coefficient is \(\sum k_{v,e}=-n_vh_v^0/2\); each selected incidence has coefficient \(h_v^0\); and each outside incidence has coefficient \(h_{b,e}-h_b=0\). Thus (7) includes the outside boundary term. ### Lower-half placement Every \(H_v\) is strictly positive. This already follows from the proper-prefix theorem: each actual positive return obeys \(\operatorname{Re}(r_{v,e}\overline{t_v})>0\) when \(t_v
e0\), and pairing (1) with \(\overline{t_v}\) gives \(\sum_e\operatorname{Re}(r_{v,e}\overline{t_v})=-\pi h_v\). Here \(t_v=0\) would give zero returns and contradict (1). For a direct convex check, reflect \(s_v\) and all \(g_{v,e}\) at one selected vertex, leaving every other coordinate fixed. On an edge where it is the first endpoint, the two squares in (3) are exchanged and simultaneously negated. Where it is the second endpoint, they are exchanged. The outside work is unchanged. Thus this reflection preserves \(X\) and \(\mathcal E\). It is nontrivial at \(z_0\), since otherwise \(ho_v(z_0)=0\). Strict convexity and (7) give \[ 0=\mathcal E(\operatorname{ref}_v z_0)-\mathcal E(z_0) >d\mathcal E(z_0)(\operatorname{ref}_v z_0-z_0) =2\pi h_v^0. 	ag{8} \] No coordinatewise sign condition on \(s_v\), individual return imaginary parts, or the powers \(n_v\) is used. ## 2. A supporting gap that allows different charge rows Define the Bregman remainder at the original point by \[ D_0(z)=\mathcal E(z)-\mathcal E(z_0) -d\mathcal E(z_0)(z-z_0). 	ag{9} \] It is continuous on \(\overline X\), zero at \(z_0\), and strictly positive at every other point of \(\overline X\). For a boundary point this follows by restricting to the segment from \(z_0\): its interior lies in \(X\), and the second derivative in the nonzero segment direction is strictly positive there. Consequently \[ \delta_0=\min_{\partial X}D_0>0. 	ag{10} \] The boundary is relative to the ambient affine space with the outside \(s_b\)'s fixed. It is not the boundary of the unit-charge feasible polytope. If a weak angle assignment \(z\) has rows \(ho_v(z)=-\pi c_v\), then (7)--(9) give the exact formula \[  oxed{\quad \mathcal E(z)-\mathcal E(z_0) =D_0(z)+\pi\sum_{v\in S}H_v(c_v-1). \quad} 	ag{11} \] The \(c_v\)'s in this identity can be any real numbers. They are the row values of a comparison assignment. No Fourier alias, peripheral change, or source equality is asserted by changing them. In particular, if all \(c_v\ge1\), the supporting correction is nonnegative, and a boundary comparison has at least the gap \(\delta_0\). ## 3. Every deleted forest and every nonzero charge Let \(\varnothing
e C\subseteq S\) and suppose \[ |n_v|\ge2\qquad(v\in C). 	ag{12} \] Delete every edge incident to \(C\). Let \(r_C\) be the number of deleted edges. Retain all remaining outside data. Consider any weak angle assignment \(z'\) of the resulting forest satisfying \[ \sum_{\substack{e
i w\e\ {m survives}}}g_{w,e} -n_ws_w/2=-\pi c'_w,\qquad |c'_w|\ge1\quad(w\in S\setminus C). 	ag{13} \] Require \(|s_w|\le\pi\) also at isolated surviving selected vertices. Their empty-incidence rows in (13) remain in force. If the resulting assignment set is empty, there is no assignment to which the theorem applies. No positive critical point is assumed for \(z'\). Write \(\mathcal E_{m del}(z')\) for (5) on the surviving edges, with the same outside linear work, and define its angle action by \[ M_{m del}(z')=(e_G-r_C)M_\infty-\mathcal E_{m del}(z')/\pi, \qquad M_\infty=4G_{m Cat}/\pi. 	ag{14} \] The original calibrated action is \(M_G=e_GM_\infty-\mathcal E(z_0)/\pi\). **Theorem 1.** Under these hypotheses, \[  oxed{\quad M_G-M_{m del}(z') \ \ge\  rac{\delta_0}{\pi} +\sum_{v\in C}H_v\left( rac{|n_v|}{2}-1ight) +\sum_{w\in S\setminus C}H_w(|c'_w|-1) \ >0 . \quad} 	ag{15} \] The same \(\delta_0>0\) works for every nonempty \(C\) satisfying (12), every such charge vector, and every admitted weak assignment. There is no ratio condition on the powers and no degree restriction. **Proof.** If a surviving \(c'_w\) is negative, reflect its \(s_w\) and all its surviving incidences \(g_{w,e}\). The reflection preserves the weak inequalities, outside data and energy by the square argument above. It changes its row to \(-\pi|c'_w|\); every other row stays unchanged. Reflections at different selected vertices commute. Thus we may use an energy-equivalent assignment whose surviving charges are all \(|c'_w|\). Extend it to the original weak angle body by setting \[ s_v=\operatorname{sgn}(n_v)\pi\quad(v\in C),\qquad g_{a,e}=0 \quad\hbox{at both ends of every deleted edge}. 	ag{16} \] Every restored edge satisfies (2) weakly. Surviving rows are unchanged, while a removed row is exactly \[ ho_v=-\pi|n_v|/2. 	ag{17} \] This assignment \(\widetilde z\) need not belong to the original unit-charge polytope. It does belong to \(\partial X\), since a removed vertex had an original incident edge and \(|s_v|=\pi\). The comparison charges in (17) are at least one by (12). Each deleted edge has both of its square factors on the square boundary. The endpoint-face theorem gives the exact constant \[ E_\square ig|_{\partial[-\pi/4,\pi/4]^2} =G_{m Cat}/2=\pi M_\infty/8. 	ag{18} \] The outside incidence on every deleted edge is zero, so its outside work is zero as well. Therefore \[ \mathcal E(\widetilde z) =\mathcal E_{m del}(z')+r_C\pi M_\infty. 	ag{19} \] Combining (11), (17), and (19) yields the exact identity \[ M_G-M_{m del}(z') = rac{D_0(\widetilde z)}{\pi} +\sum_{v\in C}H_v\left( rac{|n_v|}{2}-1ight) +\sum_{w\in S\setminus C}H_w(|c'_w|-1). 	ag{20} \] Use (10) and \(H_v>0\) to obtain (15). \(\square\) ### Action normalization for charged positive points If \(z'\) comes from a positive solution with its original canonical logarithms and charges \(c'_w\), its charge action is \[ F_{\mathbf c'}(t) =\sum_{e\ {m survives}}\psi(t_v,t_w) + rac{i}{4\pi}\sum_{w\in S\setminus C}n_wt_w^2 -i\sum_{w\in S\setminus C}c'_wt_w. 	ag{21} \] Then \(\operatorname{Re}F_{\mathbf c'}=M_{m del}\) exactly. Indeed the pinned edge calibration is \[ \pi\operatorname{Re}\psi+4(E_P+E_Q) -g_vh_v-g_wh_w=\pi M_\infty. 	ag{22} \] After summing it, the charged row \(\sum g=n_ws_w/2-\pi c'_w\) cancels the real parts of the quadratic and linear terms in (21), exactly as at unit charge. Thus Theorem 1 compares the actual real classical action of every positive deleted charged solution, including every nonzero integer charge vector, to the original primitive action. For an isolated surviving selected vertex, a charged critical point must obey \(n_wt_w=2\pi c'_w\). With \(|c'_w|\ge1\), this requires \(n_w
e0\) and gives real \(t_w\), so its terms in (21) have zero real part. A weak isolated row without a critical interpretation is still covered as an angle assignment. No quantum estimate for an isolated trace is assumed. The linear higher-charge term in (15) is a classical comparison, not by itself an estimate of an infinite quantum charge sum. ### Uniformity under small changes of outside angles The gap is uniform on a compact continuous family of positive original unit-charge solutions with the same tree, selected set and powers. Indeed \(H_v>0\) has a positive family minimum. For the boundary remainders, consider pairs consisting of a family parameter and an assignment on the boundary of its ambient body \(X\). All angle coordinates are bounded. Along a convergent sequence of such pairs, one of the finitely many weak affine inequalities is active on a subsequence, and remains active at its limit. The limiting body has an interior positive point, so this is still its boundary. Hence the set of pairs is compact. The square energy, outside work and gradient at the continued original solution are continuous; \(D_0\) is strictly positive at every pair. Its family minimum is therefore positive as well. In particular, the original positive-period implicit-function theorem continues any fixed solution under sufficiently small complex changes of the prescribed outside angles. Restricting to a small closed neighborhood gives a compact family of positive solutions. Shrinking it if necessary, (15) holds uniformly with \(\delta_0/2\) and \(H_v/2\) from its center. This is applicable near complete outside angles whenever the fixed short component has the required original positive solution there. It supplies no contour transport for the outside quantum variables. ## 4. An auxiliary even split with no exceptional small-power current For each original integer \(n_v\), choose the auxiliary factor \[ \epsilon_v^*=  egin{cases} 0,&n_v\ {m even},\ \operatorname{sgn}(n_v),&n_v\ {m odd}, \end{cases} \qquad m_v^*=n_v-\epsilon_v^*\in2\mathbb Z. 	ag{23} \] This is an algebraic factorization of the same original \(R^{n_v}\). The auxiliary \(\epsilon_v^*\) is not a replacement for the physical marking \(\eta_v\); the original relation \(n_v=\eta_v-2p_v\) stays fixed. It is possible that the auxiliary factor differs from that marking, for example at a total power \(n_v=1\) with \(\eta_v=-1\). The operation then changes the chosen conjugated Ward operator, not the crossing power or peripheral curve. To verify its exact validity, use the full original algebra \[ \mathcal A_N=\mathbb C[z]/(2T_N(z/2)+2),\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad ho=q-q^{-1},\quad \kappa=q^{(N-1)^2/2},\quad \sigma=(-1)^N. 	ag{24} \] Let \(f_j\) represent \(r_N^j\), with \(R=\kappa r_N\). For every signed integer split \(n=m+\epsilon\) with \(m\) even, \(f_n=f_mf_\epsilon\), including all repeated-node normals. Conjugating the original even Ward identity by the unit \(f_\epsilon\) gives, for the original trace and every polynomial spectator \(A\), \[ \phi_N\!\left(f_n\mathcal D_{m,1}^{\epsilon}Aight) =\sigma mNho\,A(c_0),\qquad c_0=q+q^{-1}. 	ag{25} \] Its proof uses only this factorization and \(f_\epsilon\Xi_0=\Xi_0\), not an identification of \(\epsilon\) with the marking. Hence the adopted full-algebra theorem applies unchanged to (23). The original carrier is still \(\kappa^n\). For a simultaneous set \(C\) of these currents on the original circle tree, its exact source is \[ \mathcal J_{C,N}^* =\left(\prod_{v\in C}\kappa^{n_v}\sigma m_v^*Nhoight) Z_{G\setminus C,N}. 	ag{26} \] All surviving traces, outside variables, and their mixed normal data are retained. This follows from \(K_T(c_0,w)=1\) before any exterior trace; no independent-component factorization is assumed. The formula is for the original turn edges. An identity kernel or another exterior coupon must retain its actual endpoint evaluation. If \(n_v\in\{0,1,-1\}\), then \(m_v^*=0\), so every current containing that vertex is zero. Conversely \(m_v^*
e0\) implies \(|n_v|\ge2\). Thus **every nonzero scalar prefactor in (26) has a removed set covered by Theorem 1**. This holds at both parities for every \(N\ge2\). For fixed powers, \[ \left|\prod_{v\in C}\kappa^{n_v}\sigma m_v^*Nhoight| \le\prod_{v\in C}2\pi|m_v^*|, 	ag{27} \] so these exact prefactors introduce no exponential rate. The deleted source itself can of course vanish. For comparison, retaining the original \(\eta_v\) as the split factor can leave a nonzero even current at total \(n_v=\pm1\). One must not infer (12) from that different choice. Formula (23) is the precise auxiliary choice that removes this issue. ## 5. Consequence and the remaining contour problem No Conway reduction and no charge alias are needed for this geometric gap whenever the original positive primitive solution exists. The old endpoint-face condition remains exact for an extension *within the same unit-charge rows*. The present comparison uses a different boundary assignment only as a competitor in the ambient convex body, and keeps its affine charge correction explicitly. Thus it does not contradict or alter the original face criterion. For a complete contour induction this removes a particular geometric comparison problem: every nonzero chosen split current is exactly a deleted source whose admitted nonzero-charge positive action is uniformly below the full action. If the original, fully normalized deleted source has already been bounded by those actions with subexponential loss, (26)--(27) transfer that bound immediately to this current, with the strict margin (15). The outstanding statement is genuinely about the original source. One must show that the actual deformation produces currents of the controlled form (26), and bound each entire deleted source, including its nonpositive sectors, lattice modes, endpoint seams and exterior closing. A deleted forest can lack a positive critical point; no action or quantum bound is assigned to it by assumption. Nor does the present proof supply a positive original chart for an arbitrary hyperbolic short filling after Conway reductions. The relative-cycle coefficient of the original geometric block remains a separate obligation. The chosen half-factor has the canonical analytic unit from the even-source theorem. Replacing it by an unwrapped Gaussian across a logarithmic cut still incurs that theorem's exact rank-two seam. Those seam currents are not silently identified with (26). ## Direct sources and proof coverage All listed source proofs were read in full at the pinned versions. * [Original convex variation](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_positive_filling_convex_variation.md), SHA256 2777b2bcb149d64a79757ba64ccb16be5438cf37ce820ad50c5f532afd8fc6c0: original square energy, positive Hessian, continuous extension, full edge differential, arbitrary-charge rows and outside work. * [Proper-prefix regularity](research_positive_primitive_prefix_regularity.md), SHA256 a01b55a71d133aadff4aac0929e50de03e1059991d6874e81646c770eb5604a6: previously proved \(H_v>0\) from the actual positive returns. The reflection proof above independently checks the needed sign. * [Endpoint angle face](research_endpoint_current_angle_face.md), SHA256 f84acb848b889a1553b467ba2d040884f7792a5ab0439eaada14a79216f363cc: exact square-boundary energy, deleted-edge normalization, isolated-vertex scope and the distinct fixed-row face criterion. * [Original action calibration](research_positive_period_inverse_descent.md), SHA256 b9b5c3d61c704700e9431315cf50591c921ebeb95becdf6a52877606bdbc4565: full edge identity (22), original primitive action and its outside-angle normalization. * [Even-factor source reduction](research_even_twist_ward_source_reduction.md), SHA256 7cd055df1b070ecc8a5f4a4b62e821e37c616e1bbb935aa274939cf44e8e0b18: exact conjugated even Ward identity, all-subset scalar deletion, retained full Hermite data, canonical analytic factor and its seam. Only written reasoning, source-text reads and file hashes were used. No mathematical code, numerical evaluation, tests or compilation were run. No frozen note, public document or manuscript was edited.

title: Every positive-value non-CROSS sharp maximum has an elementary odd MAIN cycle
status: Every non-CROSS maximum port forces an odd MAIN four-cycle
text:
# Every positive-value non-CROSS sharp maximum has an elementary odd MAIN cycle 31 October 2026. This source/combinatorial theorem uses full-fiber activation and stationary classification. It does not construct a representation or prove an absolute exponential phase gap, and uses no cap collar. ## 1. Exact hypotheses inherited from the original maximum Work with the actual certified simple-white marked plat and its original ordinary face targets \(1\), protected pair \(u,v\), and triangle pairing across MATCHING edges. Every MAIN edge has two incident triangles belonging to different ports. Let \(q\) and the common positive ordinary weights \(L\) be the data supplied by [finite-multiplier and stationary classification](research_full_fiber_sharp_stationary_classification.md). In particular every ordinary incidence is positive, the supported port/ordinary-face graph is connected, and each port is one of: * strict CROSS at \(\delta=0\), whose incidence character is constant; * strict Green, with one negative half and overloaded ordinary middle \(o\), \(q_{e,o}>1/2\), and \[ L_o-L_p= rac{L_x+L_y}{\sin^2(\pi\delta)},\qquad 0<\delta<	frac12; 	ag{1} \] * a residual cap, with the two protected faces as one outer and the parent middle; its two ordinary incidences are outer \(a\) and overloaded middle \(o\), with \[ q_{e,a}=
u,\quad q_{e,o}=1-
u,\quad 0<
u<	frac12,\qquad L_o=L_a. 	ag{2} \] For a Green, the literal source character on its negative half is \(1\) at its overloaded middle and \(0\) at its outers; its other half has character \(0\). For a cap, the two supported ordinary characters differ by \(1\). This is the exact alternating monomer character, up to a constant row gauge. These statements are unchanged by original RIGHT reflection or outer exchange. No globally coherent signs are assumed. Here is a direct source derivation of the character table. In the [exact full-interval source](research_original_one_sided_four_state_transfer.md), write \(\alpha_r=c_r-\sigma\) and retain every unused prefix and suffix factor. On a strict LEFT straddling window the prefix is positive and the lower-half suffix has sign \((-1)^{M-j}\). The [positive word expansion](research_positive_eta_word_transfer.md) makes the coefficients of \(K_{i,j}\) nonnegative for every sufficiently large level at a fixed strict spectrum. Thus, after retaining the common raw sign and omitted-half scalar, the varying sign is \((-1)^j\). The original middle monomial is \(c^{d-j}\), so this is exactly the character \(c\mapsto-c\), up to a degree-independent row sign. The common scalar is not divided out; at a sampled zero the source is zero. At the complete endpoint the same unused factors and tail coefficients are nonnegative, up to the common raw sign, giving the constant CROSS character. Literal row reflection gives RIGHT. The [flat-cap formula](research_flat_cap_no_local_exponential_angular_gap.md) gives the remaining character directly, including its raw sign at both parities. No geometric collar is needed for this table. A supported four-cycle \(e-f-e'-g-e\) has sign sum \[ \varepsilon_{e,f}+\varepsilon_{e',f} +\varepsilon_{e',g}+\varepsilon_{e,g}\quad	ext{in }\mathbf F_2. 	ag{3} \] It is odd precisely when the two ports' edge differences on \(f,g\) differ. The test retains actual incidences and is invariant under all row gauges and common face signs. ## 2. Every strict Green gives an odd MAIN four-cycle At a strict Green choose an ordinary outer \(a\). Such an outer exists: the two protected faces form a MAIN pair, whereas the two outers form a MATCHING pair. Write \(o\) for the overloaded middle of the negative half. Both endpoints of the MAIN edge \(oa\) are ordinary. Equation (1) gives \[ L_o>L_p+L_x+L_y\ge L_a.	ag{4} \] Thus \(L_o>L_a\) also when the other outer or parent is protected. The original edge \(oa\) has a second triangle at a different port \(e'\). The chosen Green has edge-character difference \(1\). We show that the second triangle has edge-character difference \(0\). A positive Green half or a CROSS half has that difference \(0\). If it is a negative Green half with difference \(1\), its overloaded middle must be \(o\) or \(a\): a MAIN edge joins a port middle to an outer. The two possibilities are impossible: * overload at \(o\) would put two distinct loads greater than \(1/2\) on the same original demand-one face; * overload at \(a\) would require \(L_a>L_o\) by its own version of (4). If the second triangle belongs to a residual cap and has both ordinary endpoints \(o,a\), it is the cap's ordinary output edge. Equation (2) would require \(L_o=L_a\), also impossible. These exhaust the classified ports. Thus the actual radial four-cycle \(e-o-e'-a-e\) is odd. The conclusion needs only (1), the exact sign table, original MAIN typing and face demands. It does not use a Green collar or representation volume. ## 3. Residual caps also give an odd MAIN four-cycle at positive value At a cap \(e\) let \(o,a\) be its ordinary output pair. They have equal positive weights and opposite incidence characters. Their MAIN edge has its other triangle at \(e'\). A noncap triangle cannot have opposite characters on this edge: a negative Green would require one of the equal weights to exceed the other strictly, while positive and CROSS halves have equal characters. Therefore the cycle is odd unless \(e'\) is itself a cap on the same pair. The latter case is incompatible with a positive-value maximum. Both caps have all their supply on the same two ordinary faces. The second cap cannot overload \(o\), since \(e\) already supplies more than \(1/2\) there; it must overload \(a\). Write the two parameters as \(
u\) and \(
u'\). Face demands imply \[ 1-
u+
u'\le1,\qquad 
u+1-
u'\le1, \] so \(
u'=
u\) and both demands are saturated by these two rows. Ordinary incidence positivity excludes every other port from both faces. The two cap ports have no other ordinary incidence. They and the two faces form a whole connected component of the supported graph. Connectedness then forces the entire source to consist of these two caps, whose sharp entropy is zero. This contradicts the positive-value hypothesis, in particular a global maximum at or above \(\Phi_D>0\). There is an independent literal sphere check of the exceptional geometry. After locally naming the protected pair \(u,v\), the first cap triangles are \((u,v,a)\) and \((u,o,a)\), paired across \(ua\). If the other triangle on \(oa\) is another cap output, its protected vertex must be \(v\). Its input must then be \((u,v,o)\): choosing ordinary outer \(a\) would repeat the first input triangle. The four triangles are exactly the boundary of a tetrahedron on \(u,v,o,a\). Every edge is already incident to two of them, so connectedness of the triangulated sphere leaves no other triangle. This is not a claim that the tetrahedral source cannot exist; its all-cap action is simply zero. Thus every residual cap at the positive-value data in §1 has its own explicit odd MAIN four-cycle as well. ## 4. Consequence and exact remaining limitation At every unrestricted global maximum, or competing strict-NC maximum of value at least \(\Phi_D\) under the stationary theorem's hypotheses, each non-CROSS port has an elementary odd supported four-cycle. In particular there is no common solution \[ \varepsilon_{e,f}=\gamma_f+\kappa_e \] unless every port is complete CROSS. In the restricted non-CROSS problem, this statement requires at least one middle load strictly greater than \(1/2\); it makes no assertion about a seam-only constrained maximum. A phase-coherent maximum therefore belongs entirely to the original complete endpoint problem. Its value is at most \(\Phi_D\), and the endpoint unique-max theorem identifies equality when that comparison is used. A competing non-CROSS maximum of high value is necessarily phase-inconsistent. An odd cycle alone is NOT an absolute upper bound for the oscillatory source. On regular windows the cycle-packing theorem subtracts an explicit local phase loss from a positive envelope; comparing that result to \(\Phi_D\) remains necessary. Residual flat caps do not automatically satisfy a regular-window exponential angular gap. The [exact flat-cap calculation](research_flat_cap_no_local_exponential_angular_gap.md) exhibits this limitation. No full invariant or volume theorem is inferred. Dependencies are the [full-fiber boundary reduction](research_full_fiber_sharp_boundary_activation.md), [stationary classification](research_full_fiber_sharp_stationary_classification.md), [exact source expansion](research_original_one_sided_four_state_transfer.md), and [original MAIN/MATCHING dictionary](../papers/marked-fillings/README.md). The [flat-cap companion](research_flat_cap_no_local_exponential_angular_gap.md) retains its exact raw coefficient and phase.

title: Estimating a boundary derivative using the stationary equations
text: # Estimating a boundary derivative using the stationary equations Research deduction, 6 November 2026. The terminal comparison needs a bound for the boundary derivative of an action at its critical point. An enclosure of each critical coordinate separately can lose information: the coordinates satisfy the same system of stationary equations. Those equations may be subtracted from the observable before estimating its error. The resulting function has the same value on the critical set, and can have much smaller first derivatives in the uncertain coordinates. This note proves that elementary implication. It does not supply new numerical signs, a finite-source estimate, or a volume theorem. Its intended application uses the existing terminal reference families and saved bounds for their original logarithms. It does not assert a new principle of asymptotic rigidity. ## 1. An exact identity with an approximate reference point Let \(z\in\mathbb C^d\), \(b\in\mathbb C\), and write \(x=(z,b)\). Let \(F(x)\in\mathbb C^d\) and \(P(x)\in\mathbb C\) be holomorphic on a domain containing all line segments used below. The actual reference family satisfies \[ F(z(b),b)=0. \tag{1} \] Choose a coordinate \(a=z_k\). Suppose the existing enclosure has the form \[ b=b^0+\delta,\qquad z=z^0+u\delta+\zeta,\qquad |\delta|\le r,\quad |\zeta_j|\le\eta_j. \tag{2} \] The stored point \(x^0=(z^0,b^0)\) need not satisfy (1). Put \(U=(u,1)\), and let \(E_j\) be the coordinate vector for \(z_j\) in \(\mathbb C^{d+1}\). In particular \(h=x-x^0=U\delta+\sum_j E_j\zeta_j\). For any fixed complex row \(w\in\mathbb C^{1\times d}\) and scalar \(\lambda\in\mathbb C\), define \[ R(x)=P(x)-wF(x)-\lambda(a-a^0). \tag{3} \] Taylor's formula along the segment \(x^0+th\), with real \(0\le t\le1\), gives the exact identity on (1): \[ \begin{split} P(x)={}&P(x^0)-wF(x^0)+\lambda(a-a^0) +DR(x^0)U\,\delta +\sum_j DR(x^0)E_j\,\zeta_j\\ &+\int_0^1(1-t)D^2R(x^0+th)[h,h]\,dt. \end{split} \tag{4} \] All derivatives here are complex derivatives and all matrix products are ordinary products, without conjugation. The term \(-wF(x^0)\) must be retained. Replacing the approximate stored point by a critical point without paying its residual would invalidate (4). Suppose an interval for \(\Im(P(x^0)-wF(x^0))\) has midpoint \(p_0\) and radius \(\rho_0\). If \[ |DR(x^0)U|\le\mu,\qquad |DR(x^0)E_j|\le\mu_j, \] and the last integral in (4) has modulus at most \(B\), then \[ \left|\Im P(x)-p_0-\Im\{\lambda(a-a^0)\}\right| \le \rho_0+r\mu+\sum_j\eta_j\mu_j+B. \tag{5} \] This is a bound for the same actual reference family as (2). It does not restrict the independent target coordinates in a subsequent phase comparison. Once (5) is certified, the exact quadratic maximum in [the source-cell comparison](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_mixed_terminal_source_cell_joined_plane.md), Section 2, applies without any change to its original cells. ## 2. Eliminating the first-order coordinate errors There is an exact choice of \(w,\lambda\) that makes all the first derivatives in (4) vanish whenever the following nonsingularity conditions hold at \(x^0\). Let \[ H=D_zF(x^0),\qquad f=D_bF(x^0),\qquad v=-H^{-1}f, \tag{6} \] and suppose \(H\) is invertible and \(v_k\ne0\). Here \(v\) is defined by (6); it is not silently identified with an approximate stored predictor \(u\). Set \[ \lambda=\frac{P_b(x^0)+P_z(x^0)v}{v_k},\qquad w=(P_z(x^0)-\lambda e_k^{\mathsf T})H^{-1}. \tag{7} \] Then \(R_z(x^0)=0\) directly. Also \[ w f=-(P_z-\lambda e_k^{\mathsf T})v =-P_zv+\lambda v_k=P_b, \] so \(R_b(x^0)=0\). Thus \(DR(x^0)=0\), and both first-order error terms in (4) disappear. This argument is valid whether or not \(F(x^0)=0\). Equivalently, the map \(x\mapsto(F(x),a)\) has invertible derivative at \(x^0\). The nonzero entry \(v_k\) is the precise condition that \(a\) can serve as a local coordinate on any zero level of \(F\) meeting that inverse chart. If \(F(x^0)\ne0\), the inverse-function theorem alone does not assert that the chart meets \(F=0\). The actual family in (1)--(2) is a separate premise of the error estimate. No global inverse or new finite-source identity is asserted. For a rigorous saved-data calculation one need not compute the exact complex values in (7). One may choose exact Gaussian rational \(w,\lambda\), then enclose the residual derivatives in (5) using the saved analytic intervals. The estimate remains valid for every such choice. A proposed inverse or a small numerical residual is not itself a certificate; the interval bounds \(\mu,\mu_j\) must still be proved. No choice is prescribed or numerically tested in this note. ## 3. Combining logarithmic terms before bounding the remainder The intended stationary equations and observable are affine functions plus linear combinations of the same original logarithmic primitives. More generally, suppose \[ F(x)=F_{\rm aff}(x)+\sum_\ell c_\ell j(\ell_\ell(x)),\qquad P(x)=P_{\rm aff}(x)+\sum_\ell d_\ell j(\ell_\ell(x)), \tag{8} \] where \(c_\ell\in\mathbb C^d\), \(d_\ell\in\mathbb C\), each \(\ell_\ell\) is affine, and the indicated branches of \(j\) are holomorphic on the entire segment images. Zero coefficients may be inserted to put both formulas on the same list of arguments. Write \(L_\ell=D\ell_\ell\), and suppose saved bounds give \(|j''|\le m_\ell\) on these images. Then a valid value of \(B\) in (5) is \[ B=\frac12\sum_\ell |d_\ell-wc_\ell|\,m_\ell \left(r|L_\ell U| +\sum_j\eta_j|L_\ell E_j|\right)^2. \tag{9} \] Indeed the affine terms, including \(-\lambda(a-a^0)\), have zero second derivative. Each remaining term contributes \((d_\ell-wc_\ell)j''(\ell_\ell(x))\,(L_\ell h)^2\) to the integrand in (4). Its modulus has the bound in (9), and \(\int_0^1(1-t)\,dt=1/2\). The coefficients must be combined before taking absolute values to obtain this particular bound. Evaluating \(P\) and \(wF\) separately gives a valid but potentially larger bound. For the original notation \(g'(z)=j(z)+i\pi(1/2-z)\), one has \(g'''=j''\). Thus the already saved full primitive curvature bounds are of the order required in (9). Their original argument domains and logarithmic lifts still have to be checked for each use; the identity alone does not enlarge those domains. ## 4. The two existing terminal representations At an actual coupled terminal reference the shared stationary equation is \[ f_a=g'(a+s)+g'(a+t)-3g'(a)+2\pi it=0. \tag{10} \] Consequently the two expressions \[ P_O=\tfrac32g'(a)-g'(a+s),\qquad P_T=g'(a+t)-\tfrac32g'(a)+2\pi it \tag{11} \] represent the same boundary derivative, since \(P_T-P_O=f_a\). This identity is already present in the original terminal action and height-derivative formulas; see [the height-sign proof](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_mixed_terminal_height_tangent_sign.md) and [the plane allocation](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_mixed_terminal_reserved_plane_transfer.md). It is one particular subtraction of a stationary equation. The two expressions generally differ at the stored approximate point. Any Taylor estimate must use the chosen expression's own constant, derivative and remainder. The whole-affine terminal representation can be estimated using the smaller posterior error of \(t\), while (3)--(9) also permit combinations of several stationary equations. Whether either choice pays the five remaining phase comparisons is a separate quantitative question. No computation or successful sign is asserted here, and no frozen comparison record is changed.

title: What is fixed in a strict Conway filling family?
text: # What is fixed in a strict Conway filling family? 18 November 2026. Expository research note. This note spells out the definitions and quantifiers in the frozen statements. It proves no new volume identity and changes none of those statements. The phrase “fix an admissible strict Conway tangle construction, its crossing circles, and a half-twist pattern giving one knot” means: choose one finite recipe for assembling two-strand boxes; keep a separate label and crossing disk at every elementary box; check a finite strictness test; and choose the local even/odd strand connections so that the closed main strands form one circle. The integers subsequently varied add full twists inside those same disks. They do not change the recipe or its component pairing. ## 1. Ordered four-endpoint tangles A box is a three-ball containing a tangle whose four boundary endpoints are fixed and ordered. In the rectangular drawing they are \[ 0=\text{bottom left},\qquad 1=\text{bottom right},\qquad 2=\text{top right},\qquad 3=\text{top left}. \] The box may also contain closed components. Those components must be retained when boxes are assembled. Boundary order matters: an abstract isomorphism of tangles that changes the attaching points is not the specified operation. The literal operations, in the conventions of [G, §1], are as follows. * **Product \(FG\).** Place \(F\) below \(G\), join \(F_2\) to \(G_1\) and \(F_3\) to \(G_0\), and keep the exposed tuple \((F_0,F_1,G_2,G_3)\). This is an ordered stack. * **Turn \(T(F)\).** Rotate the entire box clockwise through a quarter turn, carrying its strands, disks, framings and marks. The new ordered tuple is \((F_1,F_2,F_3,F_0)\). * **Cylindrical closure \(C(F)\).** Join endpoints \(0\) to \(3\) and \(1\) to \(2\) by the prescribed empty outside arcs. Products can be reparenthesized by rescaling their stack collars. Their factors cannot simply be exchanged. Likewise, the physical half-turn \(T^2\) must not be erased merely because the corresponding operator on a particular finite source algebra squares to the identity. The distinctions between physical moves and algebraic source identities are explicit in [C, §4]. In particular, there is no rule \(T(FG)=T(F)T(G)\). Write \(R^n\) for the standard two-strand braid with \(n\in\mathbb Z\) signed half twists; \(R^0\) is the two through strands. The elementary filled leaf is \[ h_i(n_i)=T(R^{n_i}). \tag{1} \] An expression is a finite rooted construction tree built from these leaves, products and turns, and closed as \(C(FG)\). There are \(H\ge2\) separately labeled leaf occurrences. Each occurs once and has its own parameter \(n_i\). Two leaves with the same numerical twist are still two different boxes. This is a presentation of a Conway algebraic, or arborescent, tangle. It is not a claim that every presentation of every arborescent knot is strict, or that every hyperbolic knot has this presentation. ## 2. Crossing circles and the retained half twists Before filling a leaf, keep an auxiliary unknot \(c_i\) surrounding its two strands. It bounds the original crossing disk, punctured twice by the main strands. The disks lie in the separate leaf boxes and retain their original local framings. Turns move these disks along with their boxes. At leaf \(i\), retain \[ \epsilon_i\in\{0,1,-1\} \] half twists: none, one positive, or one negative. Remove the other full twists but keep \(c_i\). After stacking and closing, this gives an augmented link with \(H\) labeled auxiliary components and its main components. Denote its exterior by \(Y_\tau^\epsilon\). On the boundary torus of \(c_i\), \(\mu_i\) is the meridian of that auxiliary component. The disk longitude \(\lambda_i\) is its push-off in the original crossing-disk framing. They are a primitive ordered integral basis. They are not the meridian and preferred longitude of the final main knot. Use the orientations of [G, §1] and [M, §§6–7]. Filling the slope \[ \mu_i+p_i\lambda_i,\qquad p_i\in\mathbb Z, \tag{2} \] removes the crossing circle and inserts \(p_i\) full disk turns with the convention \[ n_i=\epsilon_i-2p_i. \tag{3} \] Thus one positive unit of this surgery coordinate subtracts two positive braid half twists. Equation (3) fixes the sign convention; one must not replace it by \(\epsilon_i+2p_i\) while retaining the same oriented peripheral basis. At \(p_i=0\), meridional filling restores just the retained \(\epsilon_i\) crossing. The surgery is performed in the original disk neighborhood. Its ambient manifold remains \(S^3\). The main cusp is not filled. If only some crossing circles are filled, the others remain actual components of the link exterior. Both \(+1\) and \(-1\) give odd endpoint pairing, but their signed half-twist markings are retained. A comparison of those two parents also changes the description of the primitive meridian; it is not an instruction to forget the sign. ## 3. Strictness: a finite real-variable test Strictness is a condition on the construction tree before choosing the large integer twists. Its variables are normalized source-state or angle variables, not the integers \(n_i\), the surgery coefficients \(p_i\), or the quantum level \(N\). Assign a real output variable to every open subexpression. Require: \[ \begin{aligned} &0<a_i<\tfrac12 &&\text{at every elementary leaf},\\ &y=1-x &&\text{across a turn},\\ &\max(x,y)<z<x+y<1 &&\text{at every retained product}. \end{aligned} \tag{4} \] At the final cylindrical root \(C(FG)\), remove its forced last product and require only that the two outputs be \(b\) and \(1-b\). Do not impose the strict product inequality on that removed gate. The construction is **strict** when these conditions have a solution. The exact compiler in [C, §2] replaces this feasibility problem by four possible open-output sets: \[ L=(0,\tfrac12),\qquad H=(\tfrac12,1),\qquad A=(0,1),\qquad \varnothing. \] Here \(H\) as a type label is unrelated to the number \(H\) of leaves. A leaf has type \(L\). A turn exchanges \(L,H\), preserves \(A\), and preserves emptiness. The product table is | Lower / upper type | \(L\) | \(H\) | \(A\) | |---|---|---|---| | \(L\) | \(A\) | \(H\) | \(A\) | | \(H\) | \(H\) | \(\varnothing\) | \(H\) | | \(A\) | \(A\) | \(H\) | \(A\) | An empty child makes its ancestors empty. The table is symmetric as a feasibility statement; this does not make the physical product commutative. At closure the permitted pairs are \[ AA,\quad AL,\quad AH,\quad LH \tag{5} \] and their reversals. This is exactly the condition that the two open output sets contain complementary points. For example, two \(L\) inputs can produce any \(z\in(0,1)\): choose equal inputs \(a\) with \(z/2<a<\min(z,1/2)\). Two \(H\) inputs cannot satisfy \(x+y<1\). These illustrate why the type test concerns genuine open intervals, rather than nonnegative boundary states. The geometric meaning is substantial. For a strict construction, the frozen marked-geometry theorem constructs the complete augmented-link metric from the original ideal cells. The strict state places the variational problem in its interior; the proved optimizer is unique and nondegenerate. The original disks and primitive cusp markings survive this construction [G, §1; M, §§1–7]. Strictness alone does not say that an arbitrary short filling is hyperbolic or satisfies the volume identity. Conversely, failure of the strict test for one presentation is not a counterexample to that identity, nor an assertion that its finite invariant vanishes. ## 4. The separate knot test, and a checked example Ignore over/under information just for the purpose of following components. The three possible pairings of four terminals are \[ I=(03)(12),\qquad U=(01)(23),\qquad X=(02)(13). \] An even leaf \(T(R^{2k})\) has pairing \(U\); an odd leaf \(T(R^{2k+1})\) has pairing \(X\). A turn exchanges \(I,U\) and fixes \(X\). Products use the actual attachment convention of §1: | Lower / upper pairing | \(I\) | \(U\) | \(X\) | |---|---|---|---| | \(I\) | \(I\) | \(U\) | \(X\) | | \(U\) | \(U\) | \(U\), plus an internal circle | \(U\) | | \(X\) | \(X\) | \(U\) | \(I\) | Every internal circle is recorded and kept. At the end, cylindrical closure adds the pairing \(I\): an output \(U\) or \(X\) gives one main component, whereas an output \(I\) gives two. An internal circle can never reconnect to an endpoint later. This is the full knot test, as used in [M, §7] and [V, §1]. Here is a small actual admissible construction: \[ \tau=C\bigl((h_1h_2)(h_3h_4)\bigr),\qquad \epsilon=(0,1,1,1). \tag{6} \] Both retained products have type \(LL\to A\); the closing pair is \(AA\). More explicitly, take every \(a_i=3/10\) and both retained outputs \(1/2\). Then \(3/10<1/2<3/5<1\), and the two closing outputs are complementary. This is a feasible strict state, not a claim about the maximizing state. For the component check, the lower child has pairing \(U\cdot X=U\); the upper child has \(X\cdot X=I\); their product has \(U\cdot I=U\). No \(U\cdot U\) product occurs, so no internal circle is created. Closing \(U\) by \(I\) traces the single cycle \[ 0\longrightarrow1\longrightarrow2 \longrightarrow3\longrightarrow0. \] Thus (6) gives one main knot for every integer tuple \[ (n_1,n_2,n_3,n_4) =(-2p_1,1-2p_2,1-2p_3,1-2p_4). \] Hyperbolicity and the volume conclusion are guaranteed by the cited theorem only in its stated long regime. Changing the example to four odd leaves gives \(I\cdot I=I\), hence two main components. Strictness and the knot test really are different tests. ## 5. What “admissible” adds In this discussion, “admissible” is shorthand for a specified bundle of data and checked hypotheses; it is not a further universal topological adjective. The bundle consists of: 1. A fixed finite literal expression with \(H\ge2\), the ordered attachments of §1, and distinct labeled leaf occurrences. 2. The original crossing circles, their disjoint leaf neighborhoods, crossing disks, peripheral bases, and signed half-twist markings. 3. A successful strictness test (4), equivalently the recursive table. 4. A half-twist pattern whose complete component traversal gives one main component, including the internal-circle check. For the scalar invariant one also fixes its single reduced cut and framing convention. The frozen statement uses unknot value one and the specified correction from blackboard to zero framing [V, §1]. These normalization data do not add a new topological restriction on the knot. There is no extra requirement that both closing children be completed boxes: the current strict theorem allows bare or turned elementary closing children. The older completed-root grammar remains the scope of a separate signed local expansion, as [V, §1] explicitly explains. The general strict theorem uses the pure source and imposes no strict-quarter leaf bound or signed-packet prerequisite. Nor does admissibility mean “already known to satisfy the desired volume identity”; the combinatorial tests precede that theorem. ## 6. The order of quantifiers in the frozen result Fix the data in §5. The frozen theorem [V, Theorem 1.1] supplies a finite threshold \(P_0=P_0(\tau,\epsilon)\) such that, for every **fixed** integer tuple \(\mathbf p\) satisfying \[ |p_i|>P_0\quad\text{for all }i, \tag{7} \] the resulting knot is hyperbolic and \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N}\log|K_N(K_{\epsilon,\mathbf p})| =\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K_{\epsilon,\mathbf p}). \tag{8} \] The limit runs through all sufficiently large integer levels, not only a prime or odd subsequence. The precise source theorem also gives a nonzero leading asymptotic, with its framing phases retained. The logical order is \[ \boxed{\ \text{fix the construction and pattern}\ ;\ \text{choose a long fixed tuple}\ ;\ N\longrightarrow\infty.\ } \tag{9} \] “Independently long” means no constraint on relative signs or ratios of the coordinates. It does not allow \(\mathbf p\) or the construction tree to grow with \(N\). A maximum over the finitely many retained patterns gives a single threshold for one fixed construction if desired; no threshold uniform over all constructions is asserted. Since \(n_i=\epsilon_i-2p_i\), the same condition can be stated using large absolute physical crossing powers, with a correspondingly adjusted bound and the fixed parity pattern. The geometric theorem also permits filling a subset of crossing circles by long slopes while leaving the others unfilled [G, §1]. That is a theorem near the complete augmented parent. It is not the assertion that one may first perform arbitrary short fillings and then invoke the same theorem on the new exterior. ## 7. The stronger arbitrary-partial-filling target Fix a proper subset \(I\subsetneq\{1,\ldots,H\}\) and any fixed integers \(a_i\), \(i\in I\), with no longness condition. Fill those circles first and keep the entire resulting source and its remaining boundary data. The target is a bound \[ B(\tau,\epsilon,I,\mathbf a) \] such that (8) holds for every fixed completion with \[ p_i=a_i\ (i\in I),\qquad |p_j|>B(\tau,\epsilon,I,\mathbf a) \ (j\notin I), \tag{10} \] whenever the final filled knot is hyperbolic. The threshold may depend on the already fixed short fillings. The statement must remain applicable after further partial fillings; when no free coordinate remains, the iteration stops. The intermediate exterior need not itself be hyperbolic. Discarding such an intermediate would change the target unless its relevant hyperbolic descendants were separately controlled [P, §§3–4, 8]. Condition (7) misses infinitely many assignments when \(H\ge2\): one coordinate can stay short while another becomes arbitrarily large. Those are untreated assignments, not counterexamples. Distinct assignments can also represent the same knot. Thus “all coordinates long,” “finitely many exceptional assignments for one template,” and “finitely many exceptional knot types” are different assertions. Recent general local source results concerning amplitudes, critical schemes, transverse normal forms or exact current identities do not change these quantifiers by themselves. To prove (10), they must be assembled into a theorem for the entire actual partially filled source, retaining its closing functional and boundary terms and proving the geometric contribution is nonzero. This note makes no such additional assembly claim. ## 8. Complete direct texts and author review The direct texts used here are listed below. The two paper main files are used for their explicit definitions and theorem statements; this expository note does not reprove their imported analytic or geometric theorems. Each listed file was read completely, including the older scope qualifications, and its SHA256 was renewed after review. * **G:** [Marked geometry, main file](../papers/strict-conway-geometry/main.tex), SHA256 d2cd70531797177de1c73264bcec8e0a38c00668878ab97f8c9499a50d80ca3f. * **C:** [Exact source composition with single-leaf attachments](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_conway_single_leaf_source_composition.md), SHA256 ba0d23a5e929f375018481e3f9d037e5ed5abe31694f0614af5cb879e0fef022. * **M:** [General masked marked filling](../papers/strict-conway-geometry/README.md), SHA256 881a265fd9356e6c531ca5db49f337aff3928fac0fe6113a1a03acde39b16ec3. * **V:** [Conway asymptotics, main file](../papers/conway-asymptotics/main.tex), SHA256 98d34dcfe31f89e5c7c7f904da93f375386e9a94a113972fb0a8e78e08b0ca7b. * **P:** [Finite exceptions and partial fillings](research_finite_exceptions_under_partial_fillings.md), SHA256 b9c7a1021de618c1f44ab4b645f98068bd5188f93e51928c1d5de5a55870c566. The example (6) was checked by the displayed endpoint traversal and strict-state inequalities on paper. No mathematical program, numerical experiment, or change to a frozen source was used.

title: Sublinear clusters of the actual physical Casimir frame
text:
# Sublinear clusters of the actual physical Casimir frame Written proof, 24 November 2026. Any sublinear number of distinct physical Casimir blocks has a subexponentially conditioned joint frame after each individual block is Hermitian orthonormalized. The selected blocks may be anywhere in the spectrum and need not be consecutive. Every actual first normal in a double block is retained. The estimate holds at every physical pair degree, including its recorded high-degree mirror. The interpolation estimate behind the proof is already present in [S]. The source conclusion here is a bound for arbitrary coefficients in a growing sum of actual physical invariant spaces. It is stronger than an entrywise overlap estimate. It is not an ambient spectral projection bound, and raw column norms and inverse measures remain. For near-fold blocks on a strict real degree compact, the positive energy estimate in [F] supplies a further conclusion. The whole orthonormalized cluster is exponentially isotropic for the original bilinear pairing, while its conjugate adjoint-Casimir cluster gives an asymptotically orthonormal doubled frame and a bilinear block swap. No arbitrary original exterior is asserted to produce that adjoint carrier or a nonzero marked closing. ## 1. The original blocks and their exact normalization Let \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), and \(Q=q^2\). First take an original physical pair degree \(0\le t\le d\), with physical basis \(|u,t-uangle\), \(0\le u\le t\), orthonormal. The actual Casimir matrix \(J_t\) is complex symmetric. Its entries, with \(U_u=Q^u\), \(T=Q^t\), are \[  egin{split} D_u&= rac{U_u}{T} [2(q^{-1}+qT)-(q+q^{-1})U_u],\ A_u&=(U_u-T)(1-QU_u)/T\quad(0\le u<t). \end{split} 	ag{1} \] Thus \(|D_u|\le6\), \(|A_u|\le4\), and the row and column sum bounds give \[ \|J_t\|\le14 . 	ag{2} \] All norms below are physical Euclidean or induced operator norms. For a high physical degree \(d<t'\le2d\), [H] identifies its root matrix with \(J_{2d-t'}\) by the recorded unitary index translation. Apply the following constructions through that map. This is a root-level transport of the actual columns; no new flat generic-\(q\) duality is assumed. The characteristic polynomial is the original \[ P_t(Z)=\prod_{r=0}^t(Z-c_r),\qquad c_r=q^{2r+1}+q^{-2r-1}. 	ag{3} \] Every distinct node has multiplicity one or two. A double is exactly \(j,l=d-j\) with \(j<l\le t\); the odd self-paired node is simple. At a simple node use its original normalized column \(C_i\). At a double node use the actual value and normal \((C_i,w_i)\). They satisfy \[ (J_t-c_i)C_i=0,\qquad (J_t-c_i)w_i=C_i . 	ag{4} \] The normal in (4) is the generic divided derivative with divisor \(-2N(q^{2j+1}-q^{-2j-1})\), as in [H,G]. It is not an independently chosen generalized eigenvector. The first component of \(C_i\) is one. For a double define \[ \alpha_i= rac{\langle C_i,w_iangle}{\|C_i\|^2},\quad d_i= rac{\|w_i-\alpha_iC_i\|}{\|C_i\|},\quad E_i=\left( rac{C_i}{\|C_i\|},  rac{w_i-\alpha_iC_i}{\|C_i\|d_i}ight). 	ag{5} \] The two columns are exactly Hermitian orthonormal. They are independent by (4), so \(d_i>0\). For a simple block set \(E_i=C_i/\|C_i\|\). Write \(
u_i=1\) or \(2\) for its actual block dimension. At a double the exact restriction is \[ J_tE_i=E_i  egin{pmatrix}c_i&d_i^{-1}\0&c_i\end{pmatrix}. 	ag{6} \] The source adapter in each double block has polynomial cost at every physical degree. Indeed (2),(4) give \(\|C_i\|\le16\|w_i-\alpha_iC_i\|\), while [G] gives \(\|w_i\|\le C N^6\|C_i\|\). Consequently \[  rac1{16}\le d_i\le C N^6,\qquad |\alpha_i|\le C N^6. 	ag{7} \] In particular, for the actual canonical columns normalized by their common value-column norm, \[ F_i:=\left( rac{C_i}{\|C_i\|}, rac{w_i}{\|C_i\|}ight) =E_iS_i,\qquad S_i= egin{pmatrix}1&\alpha_i\0&d_i\end{pmatrix},\qquad \|S_i\|+\|S_i^{-1}\|\le C N^6 . 	ag{8} \] For a simple block take \(F_i=E_i\) and \(S_i=1\). No bound removes the possibly exponential, explicitly known per-block scalar \(\|C_i\|\) from the raw source columns. ## 2. The whole selected-cluster estimate Select any \(m\ge1\) distinct nodes occurring in this one physical block, with every column of each selected simple or double block. The nodes need not form a consecutive window. Put \[ r=\sum_{i=1}^m
u_i,\qquad V=(E_1,\ldots,E_m),\qquad {\cal L}_{N,m}=m\log(eN/m)+\log N . 	ag{9} \] Here \(m\le N\), so the logarithm is positive. **Theorem 1.** There is an absolute constant \(C\) such that, at every physical degree and for every selected set, \[  oxed{\qquad e^{-C{\cal L}_{N,m}}I_r\ \le\ V^*V\ \le\ mI_r . \qquad} 	ag{10} \] The same exponential form, after increasing \(C\), holds for \(W=(F_1,\ldots,F_m)\) in place of \(V\), with an upper bound \(CmN^{12}I_r\). Thus both frames have \[ \log\operatorname{cond}_2(V^*V),\quad \log\operatorname{cond}_2(W^*W) \le C{\cal L}_{N,m}. 	ag{11} \] All coefficients in these inequalities are arbitrary. They are not restricted to slowly varying or fixed-dimensional channel families. For any sequence \(m_N=o(N)\), the frame and Gram condition numbers in (11) are \(\exp(o(N))\), uniformly over the selected nodes and physical degrees. ### Actual cosine separation and the factorial denominator Label the distinct nodes by their canonical indices \(0\le a\le\lfloor d/2floor\), and sort the selected indices as \(a_1<\cdots<a_m\). For \(a<b\), put \(k=b-a\). Then \(k\le a+b+1\le N-k\), and \(k\le N/2\), so \[  egin{split} |c_a-c_b| &=4\sin((a+b+1)\pi/N)\sin(k\pi/N)\ &\ge16 k^2/N^2. \end{split} 	ag{12} \] In particular \(|c_{a_i}-c_{a_k}|\ge16|i-k|^2/N^2\). For every selected index \(i\), this gives \[ \prod_{k
e i}|c_i-c_k| \ge(16/N^2)^{m-1}\{(i-1)!(m-i)!\}^2. 	ag{13} \] The notation \(c_i\) from now on refers to the selected ordered node. Since \((i-1)!(m-i)!\ge(m-1)!/2^{m-1}\), the lower bound keeps the factorial improvement when \(m\) grows. Replacing every gap separately by \(N^{-2}\) would lose this improvement. ### Exact Hermite filters on the selected union Use the full multiplicity of each selected block and define \[ q_i(Z)=\prod_{k
e i}(Z-c_k)^{
u_k},\qquad \ell_i(Z)=q_i(Z)/q_i(c_i), \] \[ h_i(Z)=  egin{cases} \ell_i(Z),&
u_i=1,\ [1-\ell_i'(c_i)(Z-c_i)]\ell_i(Z),&
u_i=2. \end{cases} 	ag{14} \] These are the selected value-cardinals of the Hermite interpolation bound in [S]. Their value at \(c_i\) is one, and their first derivative there is zero when that normal exists. At any other selected node they vanish to its full multiplicity. Therefore \[ h_i(J_t)E_k=\delta_{ik}E_k . 	ag{15} \] The derivative-zero condition in (14) retains the Jordan column; it does not replace a double block by its value line. For completeness, the quantitative interpolation argument is repeated here with the operator evaluated directly at the actual \(J_t\). Every gap is at most four. Since \(
u_k\in\{1,2\}\), \[ |q_i(c_i)|\ge4^{-(m-1)} \left(\prod_{k

e i}|i-k|^{-2}\le C'N^2. 	ag{17} \] For \(m\ge2\), equations (13),(16) and \((m-1)!\ge((m-1)/e)^{m-1}\) consequently prove \[ L_{N,m}:=\max_i\|h_i(J_t)\| \le\exp\{C[m\log(eN/m)+\log N]\}. 	ag{18} \] Indeed the numerator of \(q_i(J_t)\) costs at most \(16^{2(m-1)}\), the reciprocal denominator costs at most \((CN)^{4(m-1)}/((m-1)!)^4\), and (17) adds only a fixed power of \(N\). For \(m=1\), the filter is exactly one, so (18) holds as well. The proof of [S, Lemma 2] uses the same factorial mechanism for consecutive row windows. Inequality (12) shows directly why arbitrary selected indices have the same bound. No new general interpolation method is claimed. ### Recovery on the actual selected invariant sum For arbitrary coefficient packets \(a_i\in\mathbb C^{
u_i}\), put \(v=\sum_iE_i a_i\). By (15) and block orthonormality, \[ \|a_i\|=\|h_i(J_t)v\| \le L_{N,m}\|v\|. 	ag{19} \] Summing their squares gives \(\|v\|^2\ge(mL_{N,m}^2)^{-1}\sum_i\|a_i\|^2\). Conversely the triangle and Cauchy--Schwarz inequalities give \(\|v\|^2\le m\sum_i\|a_i\|^2\). Together with (18), these prove (10). Formula (8), applied to the block diagonal adapter, proves (11) for the source columns too. Finally, if \(m=o(N)\), \[  rac{{\cal L}_{N,m}}N = rac mN\log rac{eN}{m}+ rac{\log N}N\longrightarrow0, 	ag{20} \] which proves the asserted uniform subexponential cost. The uniform degree estimate also gives a full pair-boundary version. Physical total-degree blocks are mutually Hermitian orthogonal, so the direct sum of selected frames over all degrees has a direct-sum Gram. Its logarithmic conditioning costs at most \(C\max_t{\cal L}_{N,m_t}\), with no factor for the number of degrees; empty blocks are omitted. For a fixed number \(k\) of disjoint physical pairs, take the tensor product of these boundary frames. Its Gram is the tensor product of their Grams, so \[ \log\operatorname{cond}_2\operatorname{Gram}(V_{\partial}) \le C\sum_{a=1}^k\max_t{\cal L}_{N,m_{a,t}}. 	ag{20a} \] This is \(o(N)\) if, for each pair, \(\sup_t m_{a,t}=o(N)\). It controls arbitrary coherent coefficient tensors, not only separable inputs. Disjoint pairings are essential to this tensor statement: changing to an overlapping pairing still requires the actual recoupling map and its source estimate. The filters (14) are **not** the ambient spectral projectors. Their action on unselected blocks is not zero in general. Equation (19) applies to the selected invariant sum, not to an arbitrary original vector before its unselected part is controlled. At \(m=1\) the filter is the identity, even when the actual ambient projector onto that one block has exponential norm. This distinction prevents an inference about the cost of selecting a physical source sector. ## 3. A doubled adapter for a growing near-fold cluster Now fix a real compact \(I\Subset(1/2,1)\), take \(	au=t/N\in I\), and select only double blocks with \(s_i=l_i-j_i\le\delta_I N\), where \(\delta_I>0\) is small enough for [F]. The number \(m\) can grow. Use exactly (5), so the per-node frames agree with the actual centered physical frames of [F], not just with arbitrary bases of the same spaces. At each node [H,F] give the exact bilinear Gram \[ B_i:=E_i^{\mathsf T}E_i = rac{\sigma_i}{\|C_i\|^2d_i}  egin{pmatrix}0&1\1&(\eta_i-2\alpha_i)/d_i\end{pmatrix}, 	ag{21} \] with the original complex measure and shear retained. The positive native-energy exponent in [F] implies, uniformly in these blocks, \[ \|B_i\|\le C_I e^{-a_I N} 	ag{22} \] for some \(a_I>0\). This is precisely where the near-fold and strict-degree hypotheses enter; they were not needed for Theorem 1. Only the positive native-energy bound from [F] is required here: \(\|C_i\|^2/|\sigma_i|\ge e^{aN}/\operatorname{poly}(N)\), together with (7) and \(|\eta_i|\le CN^3\), already proves (22). Its sharper Gaussian variance is not logically needed for this cluster consequence. Distinct actual generalized eigenspaces are orthogonal for the bilinear transpose pairing because \(J_t^{\mathsf T}=J_t\). For example apply the same filter (15) on its two sides. Hence \[ E_i^{\mathsf T}E_k=0\quad(i
e k),\qquad V^{\mathsf T}V=\operatorname{diag}(B_i). 	ag{23} \] Let \(A=V^*V\) and orthonormalize the **whole** selected cluster: \[ U=VA^{-1/2},\qquad U^*U=I_{2m}. 	ag{24} \] Theorem 1 and (22),(23) show \[ \|U^{\mathsf T}U\| \le C_I\exp\{-a_I N+C_I{\cal L}_{N,m}\}. 	ag{25} \] Indeed transpose has the same operator norm, and the two factors of \(A^{-1/2}\) cost \(\lambda_{\min}(A)^{-1}\). For every \(m_N=o(N)\), the right side is \(\exp(-a_I N+o(N))\). This is an operator estimate for the whole growing cluster, not an entrywise approximation to its Gram. Retain its actual conjugate carrier and put \({\cal D}=(U,\overline U)\), \(B=U^{\mathsf T}U\). The exact doubled identities are \[ {\cal D}^*{\cal D}=  egin{pmatrix}I&\overline B\B&I\end{pmatrix},\qquad {\cal D}^{\mathsf T}{\cal D}=  egin{pmatrix}B&I\I&\overline B\end{pmatrix}. 	ag{26} \] For sublinear \(m\), their errors from \(I_{4m}\) and the block swap are \(\exp(-a_I N+o(N))\) in operator norm. Their singular values therefore lie between \(1-\varepsilon_N\) and \(1+\varepsilon_N\), with \(\varepsilon_N	o0\) exponentially. The doubled frame and its bilinear pairing have condition numbers tending to one. The selected range of \(U\) is \(J_t\)-invariant. Since the physical matrix is complex symmetric, \(J_t^*=\overline{J_t}\), so the range of \(\overline U\) is invariant under the adjoint Casimir. Whole-cluster orthonormalization can mix the selected nodes; no individual column of \(U\) is newly declared an eigenvector. The conjugates are an adjoint carrier, not extra eigenchannels of the original Casimir. Formula (26) applies only when those two stated boundary types are actually paired. ## 4. Source meaning and remaining gluing problem Theorem 1 controls arbitrary coherent coefficient vectors in any selected sublinear cluster. It requires neither a local Gaussian approximation nor separation between its selected nodes beyond the exact physical cosine spacing. The first-normal directions, simple endpoints, both level parities and all physical degrees remain. This does not remove the raw per-block value norms, the inverse Christoffel--Darboux measures, framing phases, pivots, or the original marked closing. Those known factors must be transported explicitly when source coefficients are expressed in this frame. A component outside the selected invariant sum is not bounded by (19). Neither the ambient spectral complement nor an arbitrary turn or short component is asserted to preserve the selected cluster. Likewise (26) supplies a stable pairing for an actual carrier and its adjoint conjugate. It does not show that an arbitrary original exterior supplies that adjoint carrier. The original ordinary cap can annihilate a selected cluster omitting its distinguished source channel, as [H] records. The marked row is not replaced by an ordinary cap or by a Hermitian norm. No lower bound for its projection onto this growing cluster is inferred. The closest prior estimate [S] is the same factorial Hermite bound for analytic spectral repair. The fixed-window result [R] instead gives polynomial recovery for a fixed number of analytic source rows on a nonzero-minor chart. It is not the unconditional growing-block statement (10). The new conclusions here concern their source application to the actual bounded physical Casimir and, using [F], the operator-level doubled adapter for a sublinear cluster. No original knot-volume lower bound or finite-exception theorem is claimed without the further source, exterior and closing estimates. ## Complete proof inputs and closest coverage All five complete texts were read at their matching versions. | Label | Complete text | SHA256 | | --- | --- | --- | | H | [Complete actual Hermite packet](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_complete_casimir_hermite_packet.md), 321 lines | a4e96738a3a093d963fe13cc03585085951fa8699a506ade4e2e7a47c17b3f4c | | G | [Physical-grid actual normal](actual_q_hahn_physical_partner_normal_bound.md), 232 lines | 0725b210bd16899260533cf7a1a7aa9602a7ed0b0e18baf4831efb7a968e07d3 | | S | [Short physical spectral-window repair](research_short_spectral_window_repair.md), 405 lines | 581ccd3ec9232a6aa1f42172fcff856f94a6d76efccc001bd411cf2243de2550 | | F | [Full physical Gaussian--Hermite Gram](research_q_hahn_physical_normal_gaussian_gram.md), 476 lines | c28e236e33674ae93644ac255465944ab11b58883d1851637a2319fa6696b2f4 | | R | [Fixed resonant physical-window conditioning](research_resonant_physical_window_conditioning.md), 267 lines | f1af212ec05ffdb79cc9b99ce03961622740d58622213e648918000e81e5fa07 | Only written mathematics, complete text reads, and metadata hashes were used.
