title: Newton evaluation on the real boundary period
A trace-class endpoint model for the actual cut Ward current
text: # A trace-class endpoint model for the actual cut Ward current Written proof, 24 November 2026. The original binomial cut has a controlled endpoint limit, including its entire rescaled Ward current and every fixed micro-meridian jet. The current, both products with the limiting unbounded lowering operator, and their commutator converge in trace norm at rate \(O(N^{-1})\). This is a statement about the actual boundary operators before pairing with an exterior; it is not a large-level estimate for the exterior or its geometric framing period. ## 1. The original finite source and the endpoint scaling Use the orthonormal factorial head basis of [I], with \[ N\ge2,\quad d=N-1,\quad Q_N=e^{2\pi i/N},\qquad M=e^{u/N},\quad \theta=\lambda/N,\quad |u|<\pi . \tag{1} \] The parameters \(u,\lambda\) are complex. For real \(\lambda\ge0\) and sufficiently large \(N\), the cut weights below are probabilities; elsewhere their formulas mean holomorphic coefficients. The original lowering matrix is \[ \mathcal E_N|a\rangle =\epsilon_{N,a-1}(u)|a-1\rangle\quad(1\le a<N),\qquad \mathcal E_N|0\rangle=0,\qquad \epsilon_{N,r}=e^{u/N}Q_N^{-r-1}-e^{-u/N}. \tag{2} \] No outward endpoint arrow is added. Embed this basis into \(\mathcal H=\ell^2(\mathbb N_0)\), and extend finite matrices by zero. Define the coefficients and tails by \[ p_{N,a}=\binom{N-1}{a}(\lambda/N)^a(1-\lambda/N)^{N-1-a} \quad(0\le a<N),\qquad p_{N,a}=0\quad(a\ge N), \] \[ T_{N,r}=\sum_{a>r}p_{N,a},\qquad P_N=\sum_{a\ge0}p_{N,a}|a\rangle\langle a|,\qquad P_0=|0\rangle\langle0|. \tag{3} \] The notation \(P_0\) always means this fixed vacuum projection. In particular \(T_{N,r}=0\) for \(r\ge N-1\), and \(\operatorname{Tr}P_N=1\). Put \[ D_N=N\mathcal E_N,\qquad B_N=-\sum_{r=0}^{N-2} \frac{T_{N,r}}{N\epsilon_{N,r}(u)} |r+1\rangle\langle r|. \tag{4} \] These are precisely [I,S]'s actual cut current and lowering matrix with opposite scalar rescalings. Every finite denominator is a unit on \(|u|<\pi\), as also proved below. Multiplication cancels each denominator exactly: \[ \begin{split} D_NB_N&=-\operatorname{diag}(T_{N,0},T_{N,1},\ldots),\\ B_ND_N&=-\operatorname{diag}(0,T_{N,0},T_{N,1},\ldots),\\ [D_N,B_N]&=P_N-P_0 . \end{split} \tag{5} \] Thus for every actual finite marked cut matrix \(C\), \[ \operatorname{Tr}((P_N-P_0)C) =\operatorname{Tr}(B_N[C,D_N]). \tag{6} \] All original crossings, tail pivots, marks and scalar lines remain in \(C\). For the original unmarked knot cut, [I] gives \(C_N(M)=F_N(M)I\), so either trace-one probe computes the same original scalar. Equation (6), rather than equality of arbitrary marked probes, is the source-preserving statement used here. The rescaling in (4) changes neither (5) nor (6). ## 2. The whole limiting operators Let \[ p_a(\lambda)=e^{-\lambda}\lambda^a/a!,\quad \tau_r(\lambda)=\sum_{a>r}p_a(\lambda),\quad P(\lambda)=\operatorname{diag}(p_0,p_1,\ldots), \] \[ B(u,\lambda)= \sum_{r\ge0}\frac{\tau_r(\lambda)} {2(\pi i(r+1)-u)} |r+1\rangle\langle r|. \tag{7} \] Every tail is entire in \(\lambda\). The series defines a trace-class operator, holomorphic for \(|u|<\pi\) and entire in \(\lambda\), in the trace-class norm. The limiting lowering operator is the closed weighted shift \[ D_u|0\rangle=0,\qquad D_u|a\rangle=(2u-2\pi ia)|a-1\rangle\quad(a\ge1), \] \[ \operatorname{Dom}D_u= \left\{v\in\mathcal H:\sum_{a\ge1}a^2|v_a|^2<\infty\right\}. \tag{8} \] The displayed domain is independent of \(u\) in the stated disk. Closedness follows directly by taking coordinates in a convergent graph sequence. The tail estimates below show that \(B\) maps \(\mathcal H\) into this domain. They also give \[ D_uB=-\operatorname{diag}(\tau_0,\tau_1,\ldots),\qquad BD_u=-\operatorname{diag}(0,\tau_0,\tau_1,\ldots). \tag{9} \] The second identity first holds on \(\operatorname{Dom}D_u\); its right side is its unique bounded extension to \(\mathcal H\). Both operators in (9) are trace class. In particular the commutator below means the difference of these specified trace-class products: \[ [D_u,B]=P(\lambda)-P_0 . \tag{10} \] There is no claim of operator-norm convergence of the unbounded generators themselves. **Theorem.** For every compact \(K\subset\{(u,\lambda)\in\mathbb C^2:|u|<\pi\}\), uniformly on \(K\), \[ \begin{split} &\|B_N-B\|_1+\|P_N-P\|_1\\ &\quad+\|D_NB_N-D_uB\|_1 +\|B_ND_N-BD_u\|_1\le C_K/N . \end{split} \tag{11} \] The same bound holds after any fixed mixed derivatives in \(u,\lambda\), with a constant depending on their orders and \(K\). The symbol \(\|\cdot\|_1\) is trace norm on the stated orthonormal head space. No comparison with a full knot-period norm is made. ## 3. A weighted coefficient estimate For \(\lambda\) in a fixed complex compact set, the generating functions are \[ G_N(z,\lambda)=\sum_a p_{N,a}z^a =(1+\lambda(z-1)/N)^{N-1},\qquad G(z,\lambda)=e^{\lambda(z-1)}. \tag{12} \] On \(|z|=2\), the Taylor expansion of the logarithm gives \((N-1)\log(1+\lambda(z-1)/N)=\lambda(z-1)+O_K(N^{-1})\). The error is uniform for all sufficiently large \(N\). Exponentiation and the coefficient Cauchy formula therefore give \[ |p_{N,a}-p_a|\le C_KN^{-1}2^{-a},\qquad |p_{N,a}|+|p_a|\le C_K2^{-a}\quad(a\ge0). \tag{13} \] The first estimate includes the zero-extended finite coefficients. Summing coefficients above \(r\) proves \[ |T_{N,r}-\tau_r|\le C_KN^{-1}2^{-r},\qquad |T_{N,r}|+|\tau_r|\le C_K2^{-r}. \tag{14} \] In particular all fixed polynomially weighted \(\ell^1\) versions of these errors are \(O_K(N^{-1})\). These estimates prove the trace-class assertions for \(P,B\), and also \(\sup_r(r+1)|B_{r+1,r}|<\infty\), which justifies the domain claim before (9). For clarity, a diagonal matrix has trace norm equal to the sum of the absolute values of its entries. A shift \(\sum b_r|r+1\rangle\langle r|\) has the same formula for its trace norm: its adjoint times itself is \(\operatorname{diag}(|b_r|^2)\). Thus these coefficient estimates control the entire operators, rather than each fixed index alone. ## 4. The original denominators and the current limit Write \(k=r+1\). The exact factorization is \[ N\epsilon_{N,k-1}(u) =2N e^{-\pi ik/N}\sinh((u-\pi ik)/N). \tag{15} \] Fix \(|u|\le R<\pi\). Since \(|\sinh(x+iy)|^2=\sinh^2x+\sin^2y\), and \(|\sin y|\ge(2/\pi)\operatorname{dist}(y,\pi\mathbb Z)\), it follows for \(1\le k<N\) that \[ |N\epsilon_{N,k-1}(u)| \ge c_R\min(k,N-k),\qquad |2(u-\pi ik)|\ge2(\pi-R)k . \tag{16} \] Indeed the sine argument lies strictly between \(-\pi\) and zero, and its distance from either endpoint is at least \((\pi-R)\min(k,N-k)/N\). This also proves the asserted absence of finite poles. For \(1\le k\le N/2\), Taylor's formula for the two entire factors in (15) gives \[ |N\epsilon_{N,k-1}(u)-2(u-\pi ik)| \le C_R k^2/N,\qquad \left|\frac1{N\epsilon_{N,k-1}(u)} -\frac1{2(u-\pi ik)}\right|\le C_R/N . \tag{17} \] For the first bound use \(|u-\pi ik|\le C_R k\): the exponential correction is \(O(k^2/N)\) and the hyperbolic-sine correction is \(O(k^3/N^2)\). Their arguments remain in a fixed compact set. Dividing by the two lower bounds (16) proves the second. On this lower half, the difference of the shift coefficients in \(B_N\) and \(B\) is consequently bounded by \[ C_R\,|T_{N,k-1}-\tau_{k-1}|/k +(C_R/N)|T_{N,k-1}|. \tag{18} \] Its sum is \(O_K(N^{-1})\) by (14). On \(N/2<k<N\), (16) and the exponential tails (14) bound the sum of both coefficient magnitudes by \(C_K2^{-N/2}\). The remaining infinite tail \(k\ge N\) is bounded the same way. This proves the first term of (11); (13) proves its second term. The exact diagonal products (5),(9) and (14) prove the other two. No upper-endpoint denominator was replaced by a low-index limit. All parameter-dependent trace-class series converge normally on compact sets in the stated domain. Prove (11) on a slightly larger compact polydisc about each point of \(K\), still inside \(|u|<\pi\). Applying the Cauchy integral formula to the coefficient errors and summing their absolute values proves every fixed derivative bound. Finite coverings handle a general compact \(K\). These are the actual scaled meridian derivatives: \(\partial_u=(M/N)\partial_M\), with the full Leibniz rule retained. They are not derivatives moving the root \(Q_N\). ## 5. Normalization and source scope For real \(\lambda\ge0\) at \(u=0\), all \(\tau_r\) are nonnegative, so there is an explicit trace norm: \[ \|B(0,\lambda)\|_1 =\frac1{2\pi}\sum_{a\ge1}p_a(\lambda) \sum_{k=1}^{a}\frac1k =\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^\lambda\frac{1-e^{-t}}t\,dt . \tag{19} \] At zero the integrand has its removable value one. To verify the last equality, differentiate the absolutely convergent Poisson series. If \(H_a=\sum_{k=1}^a1/k\), its derivative is \(\sum_a p_a(H_{a+1}-H_a) =\sum_a p_a/(a+1)=(1-e^{-\lambda})/\lambda\). The series vanishes at \(\lambda=0\). Equations (5)--(11) retain the full finite cut and its endpoint current. They also imply \(O_K(N^{-1})\) error when the four trace-class operators in (11) are paired with any uniformly operator-bounded family of tests. No such bound for an arbitrary growing knot exterior is supplied by this boundary theorem. Differentiating (6) retains derivatives of that exterior and every other original factor. ## 6. An exponentially accurate finite window with its boundary current There is a stronger approximation when the exact finite coefficients are retained. For \(2\le m\le N\), censor the cut law at \(m-1\): \[ \begin{split} P_N^{[m]}&=\sum_{a=0}^{m-2}p_{N,a}|a\rangle\langle a| +\left(\sum_{a\ge m-1}p_{N,a}\right)|m-1\rangle\langle m-1|,\\ B_N^{[m]}&=-\sum_{r=0}^{m-2} \frac{T_{N,r}}{N\epsilon_{N,r}}|r+1\rangle\langle r|. \end{split} \tag{20} \] Both are supported on indices \(0,\ldots,m-1\). The last mass is explicit, not discarded. Direct multiplication gives \[ [D_N,B_N^{[m]}]=P_N^{[m]}-P_0,\qquad \operatorname{Tr}P_N^{[m]}=1 . \tag{21} \] At real \(0\le\lambda/N\le1\) it is still a positive probe. For the original unmarked scalar, its evaluation is therefore unchanged exactly, at every \(m\); this fact is the old normalized-cut identity. Every marked comparison instead retains (21)'s exact defect. For \(m=1\), one may set \(P_N^{[1]}=P_0,B_N^{[1]}=0\). Uniformly on compact parameter sets as in (11), \[ \begin{split} &\|P_N-P_N^{[m]}\|_1+\|B_N-B_N^{[m]}\|_1\\ &\quad+\|D_N(B_N-B_N^{[m]})\|_1 +\|(B_N-B_N^{[m]})D_N\|_1 \le C_K(C_K/m)^m . \end{split} \tag{22} \] The same statement holds for every fixed parameter derivative. The limiting operators have the identical censored construction and estimate, with \(D_u\) and their already specified products. Here is a direct proof with no real-probability assumption. For \(|\lambda|\le L\), the original finite coefficients and their Poisson limits obey \[ |p_{N,a}|,\ |p_a| \le e^L L^a/a!. \] Use \(\binom{N-1}{a}\le N^a/a!\) and \(|1-\lambda/N|^{N-1-a}\le e^L\) for the finite bound. The probability error in (22) is at most \(2\sum_{a\ge m}|p_{N,a}|\). The current and both product errors are bounded, using (16), by \(C_K\sum_{r\ge m-1}|T_{N,r}| \le C_Ke^L\sum_{a\ge m}(a+1)L^a/a!\). For \(m>2L+2\), this last sum is bounded by a constant times \(mL^m/m!\). The elementary inequality \(m!\ge(m/e)^m\), obtained by integrating \(\log t\), proves (22) after increasing \(C_K\). The finitely many smaller \(m\) are absorbed in that constant. The same proof applies to the limit. Buffered Cauchy estimates give the derivative assertion. Consequently, for any fixed \(c>0\), the rank window \[ m_N=\lceil cN/\log N\rceil=o(N) \tag{23} \] has error at most \(e^{-cN+o(N)}\) in (22), uniformly on compact parameter sets and for every fixed jet. It is understood for sufficiently large \(N\), so \(2\le m_N\le N\). This exponential accuracy uses (20)'s exact finite-\(N\) coefficients. Replacing them by the limiting Poisson coefficients gives only (11)'s algebraic error. For a specified original marked cut matrix satisfying \(\|C_N\|\le e^{C_\Gamma N+O(\log N)}\), choose \(c>C_\Gamma+A\), with \(A>0\). Trace duality and (21) then give \[ \begin{split} |\operatorname{Tr}((P_N-P_N^{[m_N]})C_N)|&=O(e^{-AN}),\\ |\operatorname{Tr}((B_N-B_N^{[m_N]})[C_N,D_N])| &=O(e^{-AN}). \end{split} \tag{24} \] The second trace equals the first by the exact commutator identity, not by deleting a cutoff current. At the original complete root, this applies to fixed literal crossing/cup/cap diagrams with polynomially bounded marks and their standard framing/cut lines, or other explicitly bounded external factors of at most exponential growth. Indeed [P] gives \(\|R_N^{\pm1}\|_{\rm ph}\le20^{N-1}\) in the same orthonormal physical head basis. Its cups, ordinary caps, marked cap and pivots have polynomial norm, so a fixed finite tensor contraction has a bound of the required form. Fixed crossing powers may be expanded into their finitely many signed crossings. For a micro-meridian family of exteriors, (24) and its fixed jets require that exterior bound on the corresponding buffered compact parameter set; no uniform exterior estimate is inferred from (11). The full source can still have cancellations far below this absolute error, so (24) is not a scalar relative-error assertion. ## 7. Coverage and the boundary of the conclusion The scalar Poisson approximation is classical; see [Le Cam's primary paper](https://msp.org/pjm/1960/10-4/pjm-v10-n4-p11-s.pdf) for coverage. The independent generating-function proof here also handles compact complex \(\lambda\). [G] already supplies a bulk conditioned-Poisson Gaussian presentation of the finite cut. The additional statement here is trace-class convergence of the entire actual endpoint Ward current, its products with \(D_u\), and its fixed micro-meridian jets. This result neither evaluates \(F_N\) nor identifies the internal geometric centralizer chain. It does not project away Fourier aliases, replace the marked source by a positive trace, or suppress any source-current term. No geometric coefficient or volume lower bound is inferred from the endpoint model. ## Complete chosen texts All four complete matching texts were read. Their exact finite source conventions are retained; all limiting estimates are proved above. | Label | Complete text | SHA-256 | | --- | --- | --- | | I, direct | [Actual fixed-cut Ward source](research_fixed_interior_cut_source.md), 214 lines | 93b2887527e0b5c9cb93f4da77702c996f0524e0a93f0c0032909345efdbd1b2 | | S, direct | [Binomial cut and exact marked current](research_binomial_cut_framing_density.md), 364 lines | 4bc6efc595fd6d59c0bc572d83495fb779cff230ff1cb9c14429a0b7c6a2a1b0 | | P, direct for (24)'s complete-root application | [Uniform physical source costs](research_conway_uniform_physical_quartic.md), 477 lines | 39895b430535f565d30133b46ef57f67589207bc83f40597ffe96e2ce79bbda8 | | G, coverage | [Finite two-mode Gaussian and bulk Poisson source](research_soft_cut_two_mode_gaussian_source.md), 345 lines | 1f95717e33e0fdcfe6b1cd453a02b4e5e63d83ed578df761a5c8bdd07e990c19 | Only written mathematics, text reads and hashes were used. title: Combining the first normals before estimating the trace
text:
# Combining the first normals before estimating the trace Research proof, 3 November 2026. Frozen manuscripts are unchanged. Splitting a trace at the triangular support of a Newton polynomial separates terms that can cancel. There is an exact way to put them back together. Interpolate the values of the other factor at the distinct physical roots, and subtract the derivative of this interpolant from its actual first normal. The trace then involves only this normal difference and the nonzero values of the Newton polynomial. No first normal is discarded. At even levels the resulting crossing operator has a positive Hermitian form. Its positivity follows from an explicit integral representation of the original quadratic crossing phase. This gives a positive observation with a specified adjoint cap; it does not make the original same-sign pair contraction positive. ## 1. The interpolation identity at both parities Set \[ 	heta=\pi/N,\quad \eta=(-1)^{N-1},\quad L=\lfloor(N-1)/2floor,\quad c_a=2\cos((2a+1)	heta),\qquad 0\le a\le L. 	ag{1} \] These are the distinct physical roots of \(P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2\). All are double except \(c_L=-2\) when \(N\) is odd. Put \[ A_a=4-c_a^2,\qquad \ell_a(z)=\prod_{b
e a} rac{z-c_b}{c_a-c_b},\qquad D_{ab}=\ell_b'(c_a),\qquad \lambda_a=[z^L]\ell_a(z)=\prod_{b
e a}(c_a-c_b)^{-1}. 	ag{2} \] The value interpolant is \(I_Nh=\sum_a h(c_a)\ell_a\). This is not the full Hermite representative: the first normals of \(h\) are kept separately. At each double node define \[ d_a(h)=h'(c_a)-(I_Nh)'(c_a). 	ag{3} \] The functions \(h\) below need only have the indicated physical values and first normals. Their original trace is \[ \phi(h)=\eta\sum_{	ext{double }a} \{A_a h'(c_a)-c_a h(c_a)\} + oldsymbol 1_{\{N\ {m odd}\}}h(-2). 	ag{4} \] For a polynomial this is also \(\eta N^2[z^{N-1}]\operatorname{rem}_{P_N}h\). These are the full trace conventions of the [exact derivative-sampling formula](research_exact_complete_trace_contour.md). **Theorem 1.** For every polynomial \(p\) of degree at most \(L\), \[  oxed{\quad \phi(hp)=\eta\sum_{	ext{double }a}A_a d_a(h)p(c_a) + oldsymbol 1_{\{N\ {m odd}\}} N^2[z^L](I_Nh)\,[z^L]p . \quad} 	ag{5} \] In particular, with \[ e_j(z)=S_j^{-2}\prod_{b<j}(c_b-z),\qquad S_j=\prod_{b=1}^j2\sin(b	heta),\qquad 0\le j\le L, \] the sum in (5) contains only \(a\ge j\). At odd levels its additional term vanishes unless \(j=L\), when it equals \[ N^2 rac{(-1)^L}{S_L^2} \sum_a\lambda_a h(c_a). 	ag{6} \] This includes the odd simple endpoint without assigning a first normal to it. **Proof.** The function \(h-I_Nh\) vanishes at every distinct physical root. Thus in the trace of \((h-I_Nh)p\) only its first normal at the double roots survives, giving the sum in (5). For even \(N=2m\), the polynomial \((I_Nh)p\) has degree at most \(2m-2=N-2\), so its trace is zero. For odd \(N=2m+1\), its degree is at most \(2m=N-1\); its trace is exactly \(N^2\) times the product of the two leading coefficients. Finally \(e_j(c_a)=0\) for \(a<j\), and its leading coefficient in degree \(L\) is zero unless \(j=L\). \(\square\) For the pair source take \[ h=R^n\mathcal L_N,\qquad \mathcal L_N(z)=\sum_{k=0}^{L}e_k(z)e_k(-2). 	ag{7} \] Then (5) is an identity for the complete original coefficient \(W_{n,j}=\phi(R^n\mathcal L_Ne_j)\). It combines the [first-normal-only rows](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_pair_triangular_normal_region.md) with the other trace terms before taking absolute values. It does not estimate their separate sums. ## 2. An explicit commutator for the original crossing Let \(l\) be any polynomial of degree at most \(L\), and write \(F_a=l(c_a)\). The crossing values and normals are \[ r_a=C_{N,n}\exp(i\varphi(c_a)),\qquad C_{N,n}=\exp rac{\pi i n(N-1)^2}{4N},\qquad \varphi(z)= rac{nN}{4\pi}	au(z)^2,\quad 	au(z)=\arccos(-z/2). 	ag{8} \] At every double node \(R^n{}'(c_a)=i\varphi'(c_a)r_a\). Here \(n\) can be any real number for the stated Hermite data; integer \(n\) gives the original algebra power. The square \(	au(z)^2\) is analytic at \(z=-2\). Its derivative there is one, but the odd trace does not use that derivative. Writing \(R=\operatorname{diag}(r_a)\), the double-node normal difference is the corresponding component of \[ d(R^nl)=\{\operatorname{diag}(i\varphi'(c_a)r_a) +[R,D]\}F. 	ag{9} \] Indeed \(l'=DF\) on the nodes, while \((I_N(R^nl))'=DRF\). Formula (9) therefore uses the actual first normals of the crossing and of \(l\). For clarity, the full odd-level correction can be written without any reference to an omitted endpoint. If \(N\) is odd, then \[ \phi(R^nlp) =p_{m val}^{\,T}A \{\operatorname{diag}(i\varphi' r)+[R,D]\}F +N^2(\lambda^TRF)(\lambda^Tp_{m val}), 	ag{10} \] where \(A=\operatorname{diag}(A_a)\), so \(A_L=0\), and \(p_{m val}=(p(c_a))_a\). This is an exact odd-level formula, not an extension of the even-level positivity assertion below. ## 3. The even-level operator is positive Assume \(N=2m\), so \(L=m-1\). Put \[ \sigma_a=2(-1)^a\sin((2a+1)	heta),\qquad B=AD-	frac12\operatorname{diag}(c_a). 	ag{11} \] The Chebyshev cardinal derivatives give \[ B_{aa}=0,\qquad B_{ab}= rac{\sigma_a\sigma_b}{c_a-c_b}\quad(a
e b). 	ag{12} \] Thus \(B\) is real and skew-symmetric. One way to check the diagonal is to use the differential equation for \(T_m(z/2)\): at a root, \(D_{aa}=c_a/(2A_a)\). Off the diagonal the barycentric weights are a common multiple of \(\sigma_a\). Define \[ H_{n,N} =A\operatorname{diag}(\varphi'(c_a)) + rac{B-R^*BR}{i}. 	ag{13} \] Since \(|r_a|=1\), this is Hermitian. The original trace satisfies the exact identity \[  oxed{\qquad \phi(R^nlp)=i\eta\,p_{m val}^{\,T}R H_{n,N}F . \qquad} 	ag{14} \] Indeed multiplication of (9) by \(R^*A\) gives \(iH_{n,N}F\); the diagonal part of \(AD\) commutes with \(R\). Applying (5) proves (14). **Theorem 2.** For every even \(N\ge2\) and every real \(n>0\), the matrix \(H_{n,N}\) is positive definite. For \(n<0\) it is negative definite, and it is zero for \(n=0\). **Proof.** Its off-diagonal entries are \[ (H_{n,N})_{ab} =\sigma_a\sigma_b  rac{1-\exp(i(\varphi(c_b)-\varphi(c_a)))} {i(c_a-c_b)} . 	ag{15} \] The diagonal is \(\sigma_a^2\varphi'(c_a)\), which equals \(nN	au(c_a)\sin	au(c_a)/\pi\). Remove the unitary half-phase factors in (15). The resulting real symmetric matrix is \[ S_{ab}=\sigma_a\sigma_b  rac{2\sin((\varphi(c_a)-\varphi(c_b))/2)} {c_a-c_b},\qquad S_{aa}=\sigma_a^2\varphi'(c_a). 	ag{16} \] To verify its sign directly, the original phase has the divided-difference representation \[  rac{\varphi(x)-\varphi(y)}{x-y} = rac{nN}{2\pi}\int_2^\infty  rac{\operatorname{arcosh}(s/2)} {(s-x)(s-y)}\,ds,\qquad -2<x,y<2. 	ag{17} \] The diagonal is the continuous limit. For example, the analytic function \(	au(z)^2\) on \(\mathbb C\setminus[2,\infty)\) vanishes at \(-2\), grows like \(O(\log^2|z|)\), and has upper-cut imaginary part \(2\pi\operatorname{arcosh}(s/2)\). The Cauchy formula with one subtraction at \(-2\) gives \[ 	au(z)^2=2(z+2)\int_2^\infty  rac{\operatorname{arcosh}(s/2)}{(s+2)(s-z)}\,ds. 	ag{18} \] Taking the divided difference proves (17). The integral also gives \((	au^2)'(-2)=1\), fixing its normalization. The identity \(\int_{-1/2}^{1/2}e^{iu(\varphi(x)-\varphi(y))}\,du =2\sin((\varphi(x)-\varphi(y))/2)/(\varphi(x)-\varphi(y))\) now expresses the quadratic form of \(S\), up to replacing \(u\) by \(-u\), as \[ v^*Sv= rac{nN}{2\pi}\int_2^\infty \operatorname{arcosh}(s/2) \int_{-1/2}^{1/2} \left|\sum_a  rac{\sigma_a v_a e^{iu\varphi(c_a)}}{s-c_a} ight|^2du\,ds . 	ag{19} \] It is nonnegative for \(n>0\). If it is zero, continuity makes the displayed rational function zero for all \(s>2\) and all interior \(u\). Its residues at the distinct poles \(c_a\) are zero. Every \(\sigma_a
e0\), so \(v=0\). This proves positive definiteness. Negative \(n\) reverses the sign in (19), while changing only its unit phase factors. For \(n=0\), (13) is zero. \(\square\) Equivalently, \(\exp(i\varphi(z))\) is a Schur function in the upper half-plane: \(	au(z)\) has real part in \((0,\pi)\) and positive imaginary part there. The matrix in (15) is its boundary Pick kernel, with the explicit original-node weights. The integral proof above supplies the needed positivity without assuming a spectral property of a comparison model. ## 4. What this does and does not prove for the coefficient There is an actual positive observation. Choose the unique polynomial \(p\) of degree at most \(L\) with values \[ p(c_a)=r_a^{-1}\overline{F_a}. 	ag{20} \] Then at even levels, \[  rac{\phi(R^nlp)}{i\eta}=F^*H_{n,N}F>0 \quad(n>0,\ l
e0). 	ag{21} \] Thus the positive form comes from the original crossing and trace, with a precisely specified adjoint cap. Its smallest eigenvalue has not been bounded on the exponential scale in this note. For the original pair, \(l=\mathcal L_N\) and \(p=e_j\); the cap in (20) is not inserted. In particular, \[ W_{n,j}=i\eta\,e_j(c)^{\,T}R H_{n,N}F,\qquad \sum_{j=0}^{L}W_{n,j}W_{p,j} =-F^TH_{n,N}^{T}R_n K^{m low}_{m phys} R_pH_{p,N}F 	ag{22} \] at even levels, where \(K^{m low}_{m phys}(a,b)=\sum_{j=0}^{L}e_j(c_a)e_j(c_b)\). The two phases and the bilinear, rather than Hermitian, pairing are retained. Positivity of \(H_{n,N}\) does not alone give a lower bound for (22). At odd levels use (10), including its rank-one correction, before forming the pair contraction. At both parities (5) has removed the artificial boundary \(a=j-1\) from the value support of the trace. Estimating the resulting normal differences, or their coherent contraction, remains necessary. No bound for a separately split normal--normal or mixed region follows by taking absolute values in this identity. Reflection supplies a positive norm for a different original word: the exact reality relations give \(W_{-n,j}=\overline{W_{n,j}}\), so the reflected pair is \(\sum_j|W_{n,j}|^2\), whereas the same-sign pair is \(\sum_jW_{n,j}^2\). This distinction can matter exponentially. For the full original internal-pair vectors, the [proved long-power comparison](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_complete_boundary_coefficient_transport.md#7-exponentially-small-coherence-in-an-actual-long-power-family), Theorem 2, gives \[  rac{|w_n^Tw_n|}{\|w_n\|_2^2} =C_ne^{-N\Delta_n}(1+O(N^{-1})),\qquad \Delta_n= rac{16\pi^3}{n^6}+O(n^{-7})>0 \] for every sufficiently large fixed positive integer \(n\). This is a result about those full original vectors; it is not silently transferred to the low-index vector in (22). It rules out using reflection as a general norm-preserving substitute for the signed closing observation. The positive form in this note still requires its specified cap or a separate estimate of the actual cap's observation. ## 5. A positive weighted subspace at odd levels The full odd-level formula is (10). There is also an exact positive form on a smaller, explicitly weighted space; it does not replace (10). Let \(N=2m+1\ge3\), and let \(c_0,\ldots,c_{m-1}\) be its double roots. Write \[ P_N(z)=(z+2)Q_N(z)^2,\qquad Q_N(z)=\prod_{a=0}^{m-1}(z-c_a). 	ag{23} \] For this section, \(D^+\) is the cardinal differentiation matrix on these \(m\) nodes only. Define \[ A_a^+=(c_a+2)(4-c_a^2),\qquad v_a=4-2c_a^2-2c_a,\qquad \sigma_a^+= rac{N}{Q_N'(c_a)}. 	ag{24} \] The original weighted trace is \[ \phi_+(f):=\phi((z+2)f) =\sum_{a=0}^{m-1}\{A_a^+f'(c_a)+v_af(c_a)\}. 	ag{25} \] The simple endpoint contributes zero because of the actual factor \(z+2\), not because its trace value has been omitted. Put \[ B^+=A^+D^++	frac12\operatorname{diag}(v_a),\qquad H_{n,N}^+=A^+\operatorname{diag}(\varphi'(c_a)) + rac{B^+-R^*B^+R}{i}, 	ag{26} \] where \(R\) and \(\varphi\) are (8), restricted to the double nodes. **Theorem 3.** If \(l,p\) have degree at most \(m-1\), and \(F_a=l(c_a)\), then \[  oxed{\qquad \phi((z+2)R^nlp)=i\,p(c)^{T}R H_{n,N}^+F . \qquad} 	ag{27} \] For every real \(n>0\), \(H_{n,N}^+\) is positive definite; for \(n<0\) it is negative definite. In particular, choosing the unique \(p\) of degree at most \(m-1\) with \(p(c_a)=r_a^{-1}\overline{F_a}\) gives \[ \phi((z+2)R^nlp)/i=F^*H_{n,N}^+F>0 \quad(n>0,\ l
e0). 	ag{28} \] **Proof.** The Chebyshev differential equation, evaluated at a double root, gives \((4-c_a^2)P_N''(c_a)=2N^2\). Differentiating (23) twice gives \(P_N''(c_a)=2(c_a+2)Q_N'(c_a)^2\). Consequently \[ A_a^+=(\sigma_a^+)^2. 	ag{29} \] For any \(l,p\) of degree at most \(m-1\), the polynomial \((z+2)lp\) has degree at most \(2m-1=N-2\), so its original trace is zero. Expanding (25) for this product, whose two value vectors are arbitrary, proves \[ A^+D^++(D^+)^TA^++\operatorname{diag}(v_a)=0. 	ag{30} \] It follows that \(B^+\) is skew-symmetric. Its off-diagonal entry is \(\sigma_a^+\sigma_b^+/(c_a-c_b)\), by the cardinal derivative formula and (29). Interpolate \(R^nl\) on the double nodes by a polynomial of degree at most \(m-1\). Its product with \(p\) has zero weighted trace by the same degree argument. Subtracting this interpolant gives the weighted version of (9). Multiplying by \(R^*A^+\) yields \(iH_{n,N}^+F\), proving (27). The half-phase gauge of \(H_{n,N}^+\) has exactly the kernel (16), with \(\sigma_a\) replaced by \(\sigma_a^+\). All these weights are nonzero. The positive integral (19) therefore proves strict definiteness with the asserted sign. Finally (28) is the stated adjoint choice in (27). \(\square\) The extra factor and the degree restriction in (27) matter. The unrestricted low complete-end polynomial has degree \(m\) at odd levels, and the original pair is not replaced here by a weighted contraction. Its endpoint and top coefficient remain as in (10). ## 6. Exact transport through ordinary value observations The positive matrix is an observability Gramian for a specified unitary evolution. Both its energy and the original signed trace can be expressed using ordinary value interpolation. This removes the first normals from the representation without dropping their contribution. First let \(N=2m\) and retain the \(m\) even-level nodes. Put \[ T_a= rac{N}{4\pi}	au(c_a)^2,\qquad U_t=\operatorname{diag}(e^{itT_a}),\qquad Q(z)=\prod_{a=0}^{m-1}(z-c_a)=2T_m(z/2). 	ag{31} \] Thus the original crossing values are \(R_t=C_{N,t}U_t\). The scalar \(C_{N,t}\) is kept in the signed trace; it cancels in unitary conjugations. Define the positive matrix \[ G_{ab}=\sigma_a\sigma_b  rac{T_a-T_b}{c_a-c_b},\qquad G_{aa}=\sigma_a^2 T'(c_a). 	ag{32} \] Its positive integral representation is (17) with \(n=1\). For a physical value vector \(F\), let \(I_tF\) be the polynomial of degree at most \(m-1\) whose values are \[ (I_tF)(c_a)=e^{itT_a}F_a. 	ag{33} \] When \(F=p(c)\), write \(I_t(p)\) for this same polynomial. This specifies its exact representative. The interpolation does not assume that the crossing phase is a polynomial off the grid. For real \(s>2\) define the observation \[ (\mathcal O_tF)(s)=\sum_a  rac{\sigma_a e^{itT_a}F_a}{s-c_a} =N\, rac{(I_tF)(s)}{Q(s)}. 	ag{34} \] The equality follows from the Lagrange partial fractions and \(\sigma_a=N/Q'(c_a)\). **Theorem 4.** For every real \(n\ge0\), \[  oxed{\quad H_{n,N}=\int_0^n U_t^*G U_t\,dt,\qquad H_{n+p,N}=H_{n,N}+U_n^*H_{p,N}U_n\quad(p\ge0). \quad} 	ag{35} \] Consequently \[ F^*H_{n,N}F = rac{N}{2\pi}\int_0^n\int_2^\infty \operatorname{arcosh}(s/2) |(\mathcal O_tF)(s)|^2\,ds\,dt 	ag{36} \] is strictly increasing in \(n\) for \(F
e0\). For the specified complete-end source \(F_a=\mathcal L_N(c_a)\), this is the fully determined positive integral \[ F^*H_{n,N}F = rac{N^3}{2\pi}\int_0^n\int_2^\infty \operatorname{arcosh}(s/2) \left| rac{I_t(\mathcal L_N)(s)}{Q(s)}ight|^2 ds\,dt . 	ag{37} \] No source amplitude or overlap is inserted as a hypothesis. For the original signed trace, for any \(l,p\) of degree at most \(m-1\), one has instead the bilinear identity \[  oxed{\quad \phi(R^nlp)=  rac{i\eta C_{N,n}N^3}{2\pi} \int_0^n\int_2^\infty \operatorname{arcosh}(s/2)  rac{I_{n-t}(p)(s)\,I_t(l)(s)}{Q(s)^2}\,ds\,dt . \quad} 	ag{38} \] This includes \(l=\mathcal L_N\) and every original low Newton coefficient \(p=e_j\). There is no remaining first-normal term or separately omitted row below \(a=j\) in (38). **Proof.** Differentiating (15), with \(\varphi(c_a)=nT_a\), gives \[  rac{d}{dn}H_{n,N}=U_n^*G U_n, \qquad H_{0,N}=0. 	ag{39} \] The diagonal follows by the same differentiation. Integration proves the first equality in (35). Split its integral at \(n\) and use \(U_{n+t}=U_nU_t\) to obtain the second. The positive integral for \(G\) then proves (36); (34) gives (37). For each \(t\), \(I_tF\) is nonzero when \(F
e0\), so its positive weighted squared integral on \(s>2\) is strictly positive. All integrals converge: the rational observation is \(O(s^{-1})\) at infinity and has no pole on \([2,\infty)\). For the signed observation, multiply the first equality in (35) by \(U_n\), obtaining \[ U_nH_{n,N} =\int_0^n U_{n-t}G U_t\,dt . 	ag{40} \] Substitute this in (14), with \(R_n=C_{N,n}U_n\). The Gram representation of \(G\) turns the two vectors into their Cauchy sums (34). In this bilinear product no complex conjugation is introduced. This proves (38). \(\square\) There is an exact odd-level counterpart on the weighted space of Theorem 3. Use its \(m\) double nodes, \(Q=Q_N\) from (23), and \(\sigma^+=N/Q'\). Equations (31)--(37) then hold for \(H^+_{n,N}\), with inputs of degree at most \(m-1\). Equation (38) has \(\phi((z+2)R^nlp)\) on its left and \(\eta=1\) on its right. The proof is identical, including the factor \(N^3/(2\pi)\). The unrestricted odd source still uses (10). The two formulas (37) and (38) distinguish the remaining issue. The first integrates nonnegative quantities and has a monotone transport law. The second is the actual trace, and multiplies observations at the complementary times \(t\) and \(n-t\) without conjugation. A lower bound for that integral needs control of those observations together. Neither a lower bound for the positive energy alone nor the invertibility of the finite crossing form supplies it. There is a useful exact timescale for observing every channel. It is proportional to the level, not a fixed crossing power. **Corollary 5.** At even levels, \[ H_{N,N}=N\operatorname{diag}(G)\ \ge 2I,\qquad H_{n+N,N}=H_{n,N}+N\operatorname{diag}(G)\quad(n\ge0). 	ag{41} \] On the odd weighted space of Theorem 3, \[ H^+_{2N,N}=2N\operatorname{diag}(G^+) \ \ge rac{128}{N^2}I,\qquad H^+_{n+2N,N}=H^+_{n,N}+2N\operatorname{diag}(G^+). 	ag{42} \] Here \(G^+\) is (32) with the odd double nodes and weights \(\sigma^+\). **Proof.** At even levels, reverse the node order and write \[ 	au_b=(2b+1)\pi/N,\qquad T_b= rac{\pi(2b+1)^2}{4N},\qquad 0\le b<N/2. 	ag{43} \] The distinct differences \(T_b-T_c\) are nonzero integer multiples of \(2\pi/N\): the integer \((b-c)(b+c+1)\) is even. Thus integration over \(0\le t\le N\) in (35) kills every off-diagonal entry. The diagonal of \(G\) is \[ G_{aa}= rac{N}{\pi}	au_a\sin	au_a. 	ag{44} \] Both \(	au_a\) and \(\pi-	au_a\) are at least \(\pi/N\). The inequality \(\sin x\ge2\min(x,\pi-x)/\pi\) gives \(NG_{aa}\ge2\). The second equality in (41) follows from the cocycle because the resulting diagonal commutes with \(U_n\). At odd levels the double-node angles are \(	au_b=2\pi b/N\), \(1\le b\le(N-1)/2\). Their frequencies are \(T_b=\pi b^2/N\), so their distinct differences integrate to zero over \(0\le t\le2N\). Now \(G^+_{aa}=N(c_a+2)	au_a\sin	au_a/\pi\). The bounds \(c_a+2=4\sin^2(	au_a/2)\ge16/N^2\), \(	au_a\ge2\pi/N\), and \(\sin	au_a\ge2/N\) give \(2NG^+_{aa}\ge128/N^2\). The cocycle again proves the translated identity. \(\square\) This supplies a polynomially coercive observation of the original value space over the full crossing period, with its appropriate odd weighted interpretation. It does not supply the corresponding bound on a fixed time interval: the [small-eigenvalue theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_pick_form_small_eigenvalues.md) gives exponentially small directions for every fixed positive power as \(N\) grows. Taking \(n=N\) or \(n=2N\) changes the crossing power with the quantum level and therefore is not a volume-conjecture statement for a fixed knot. Nor does a positive energy replace the bilinear observation in (38). The averaging in (41) is the continuous crossing flow (35). At even levels \(R^N\) has scalar physical values, but its first normals need not vanish: after dividing by that scalar, it is \(1+r\) with \(r\) in the radical of the full double-root algebra and \(r^2=0\). The nonzero matrix \(H_{N,N}\) retains precisely this normal contribution. Finite-level nilpotence therefore coexists with the observation problem at fixed crossing power. ## 7. Reproduction Run \[ 	exttt{python3 experiments/check\_trace\_normal\_defect\_positive\_form.py}. \] The checker compares the original value-and-normal trace with (5), (9), (10), and (14) at both parities, including the top odd Newton index. It also checks the even cardinal identities and the normalized Gram kernel, the weighted odd trace (27), and the exact transport and interpolation identities (34)--(40), and the frequency and diagonal identities in (41)--(44). Its [saved record](../repro/results/research-trace-normal-defect-positive-form.json) records the source hashes. These finite checks supplement the proofs above; no numerical eigenvalue test is used as a proof of positivity.

title: The common original Jacobi characteristic of the triple-row pressure
text: # The common original Jacobi characteristic of the triple-row pressure Private written proof, 17 November 2026. The critical equations of the positive triple-row pressure reduce to one strictly monotone scalar equation. Its selected solution is the common characteristic of the original Jacobi operators, and it computes the leading coefficient of every fixed-degree polynomial inserted in the original closing trace. The source equations hold exactly, with their original forcing canceled by the full trace ideal. The characteristic and fixed-degree observations are asymptotic statements on strict physical support. They do not supply a stable continuation of external first normals or a lower bound after a crossing whose canonical polynomial degree grows with the level. ## 1. Original source and exact coupled equations Set \[ N\ge2,\quad D=N-1,\quad \eta=(-1)^D,\quad s_r=2\sin(\pi r/N),\quad S_r=\prod_{a=1}^rs_a, \] \[ c_r=2\cos((2r+1)\pi/N),\quad e_r(C)=S_r^{-2}\prod_{a<r}(c_a-C),\quad P_N(C)=2T_N(C/2)+2, \] \[ \phi(f)=\eta N^2[C^D]\operatorname{rem}_{P_N}f,\qquad K_N(w,C)=\sum_{r=0}^De_r(w)e_r(C),\qquad F_j(C)=K_N(c_j,C). \tag{1} \] Physical indices satisfy \(0\le j\le\lfloor D/2\rfloor\). The quotient and trace in (1) retain the double-node first normals and the odd simple node. For a polynomial \(q\), define the ordinary external polynomial \[ \Gamma_{q,N}(\mathbf w) =\phi_C\!\left(q(C)\prod_{i=1}^3K_N(w_i,C)\right), \qquad \Gamma_N=\Gamma_{1,N}. \tag{2} \] Only the class of \(q\) modulo \(P_N\) enters this expression. Write \(\mathscr J_N\) for the original ordinary operator. On the angular lift \(C_N(x)=2\cos(2\pi x+\pi/N)\), it is \[ \mathscr J_N f=(c_0+A_N+B_N)f -A_Nf(x+N^{-1})-B_Nf(x-N^{-1}), \] \[ A_N(x)=\frac{s_{Nx+1}^4}{s_{2Nx+1}s_{2Nx+2}}, \qquad B_N(x)=\frac{s_{Nx}^4}{s_{2Nx}s_{2Nx+1}}. \tag{3} \] Its ordinary polynomial action and kernel source are \[ \mathscr J_Ne_r=c_re_r-s_r^2e_{r-1},\qquad (C-\mathscr J_{N,w})K_N(w,C) =\frac{P_N(C)P_N(w)}{N^4(w-c_0)}. \tag{4} \] The last fraction in \(w\) is a polynomial. The convention \(e_{-1}=0\) is used in the first identity. Multiply the second identity by the other two kernels and by \(q(C)\), and apply the original trace in \(C\). Its right side is divisible by the full \(P_N(C)\), so it vanishes with all multiplicities. Consequently \[ \boxed{\qquad \mathscr J_{N,w_i}\Gamma_{q,N} =\Gamma_{Cq,N}\quad(i=1,2,3). \qquad} \tag{5} \] In particular \[ (\mathscr J_{N,w_i}-\mathscr J_{N,w_k})\Gamma_{q,N}=0, \qquad q(\mathscr J_{N,w_i})\Gamma_N=\Gamma_{q,N}. \tag{6} \] These are ordinary polynomial identities in the external variables, not equalities only at distinct physical values. They therefore retain every external derivative as well. The cancellation in (5) occurs under the original closed \(C\)-trace; no forcing has been deleted from a free kernel. At a regular physical bulk index, (5) reads \[ \begin{split} &(c_0+A_j+B_j)\Gamma_{\mathbf j} -A_j\Gamma_{\mathbf j+\mathbf e_i} -B_j\Gamma_{\mathbf j-\mathbf e_i}\\ &\hspace{35mm} =\phi\!\left(CF_{j_1}F_{j_2}F_{j_3}\right), \end{split} \tag{7} \] where \(j=j_i,\ A_j=A_N(j/N),\ B_j=B_N(j/N)\). The right side is the same for every \(i\). ## 2. One scalar equation selects the pressure branch Let \[ \mathcal X^\circ =\{\mathbf x:0<x_i<1/2,\ \sum_i x_i>1\}. \tag{8} \] Here \(x_i\) is a macroscopic degree fraction. The exact finite physical color remains \(c_{j_i}\) in (1). Use the pressure action from the first direct source: \[ \mathcal J(u)=\int_0^u\log(2\sin\pi v)\,dv, \qquad f(x,t)=\mathcal J(x+t)-\mathcal J(x-t)-2\mathcal J(t), \] \[ \Phi(\mathbf x,\mathbf t)= \sum_i f(x_i,t_i) +\sum_{i<k}\mathcal J(t_i+t_k)-\sum_i\mathcal J(t_i) -\mathcal J(t_1+t_2+t_3-1). \tag{9} \] Its unique maximum has \(0<t_i^*<x_i,\ \sum_i t_i^*>1\), and \(\mathcal G(\mathbf x)=\Phi(\mathbf x,\mathbf t^*)\). The Hessian in the internal variables is negative definite. Introduce different letters for their cotangents: \[ X_i=\cot(\pi x_i)>0,\qquad Y_i=\cot(\pi t_i^*)>X_i,\qquad S=\sum_{i<k}Y_iY_k. \tag{10} \] Since \(\sum_i t_i^*\in(1,3/2)\), \[ \sin\!\left(\pi\sum_i t_i^*\right) =\left(\prod_i\sin\pi t_i^*\right)(S-1)<0. \tag{11} \] Thus \(S<1\). The same identity for the \(x_i\) gives \(\sum_{i<k}X_iX_k<1\). The stationary equation in \(t_i\) is \[ \frac{\sin\pi(x_i+t_i)\sin\pi(x_i-t_i) \sin\pi(t_i+t_j)\sin\pi(t_i+t_k)} {\sin^3\pi t_i\, \sin\pi(t_1+t_2+t_3-1)}=1. \tag{12} \] All factors are positive on the selected real domain. In cotangents this becomes \[ (Y_i^2-X_i^2)(Y_i+Y_j)(Y_i+Y_k) =(1+X_i^2)(1-S). \tag{13} \] The elementary identity \((Y_i+Y_j)(Y_i+Y_k)=Y_i^2+S\) makes (13) much simpler: subtracting its right side and factoring gives \[ (1+Y_i^2)\{Y_i^2-X_i^2-(1-S)\}=0. \tag{14} \] Hence all three differences are equal. **Theorem 1.** The selected critical point is exactly \[ Y_i=\sqrt{X_i^2+L},\qquad t_i^*=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{arccot}\sqrt{X_i^2+L}, \tag{15} \] where \(L>0\) is the unique solution of \[ E(L,\mathbf X):= L+\sum_{i<k}\sqrt{X_i^2+L}\sqrt{X_k^2+L}-1=0. \tag{16} \] It satisfies \[ 0<L\le \frac{1-\sum_{i<k}X_iX_k}{4}\le\frac14, \qquad E_L=1+\frac12\sum_{i<k} \left(\frac{Y_i}{Y_k}+\frac{Y_k}{Y_i}\right) \ge4. \tag{17} \] The branch is real analytic on (8), uniformly nondegenerate on its compact subsets, and has a single compatible holomorphic germ near each such real point. **Proof.** The critical point just proved to exist satisfies (15)--(16), by (14). Conversely \(E(0,\mathbf X)<0\); the derivative in (17) is at least four and \(E\) tends to infinity. This proves unique existence and the upper bound in (17). For its solution \(Y_i>X_i>0\) and \(S=1-L<1\). Therefore \(0<t_i<x_i<1/2\), and (11) implies \(\sum_i t_i>1\). Thus (12) holds on the original feasible domain, and this is the pressure maximizer. Positivity of the square roots and \(E_L\ne0\) give the analytic assertions. On a compact subset, \(L\) and the square roots stay uniformly away from zero, so the same implicit-function argument has fixed local complex buffers. \(\square\) The choice of positive square roots and of the original real logarithms is part of this branch selection. Continuation to a distant complex point requires retaining those branches and avoiding their discriminants; (17) is not by itself a global complex continuation estimate. ## 3. The action gradient and the actual common source characteristic The envelope derivative of (9) is \[ p_i:=\partial_{x_i}\mathcal G =\log\frac{\sin\pi(x_i+t_i^*)}{\sin\pi(x_i-t_i^*)} =\log\frac{Y_i+X_i}{Y_i-X_i} =2\operatorname{arsinh}\frac{X_i}{\sqrt L}. \tag{18} \] Every equality uses the selected positive real branch. Define \[ \zeta(\mathbf x)=2-\frac4{L(\mathbf x)}. \tag{19} \] At a macroscopic bulk index, the coefficients in (3) obey \[ c_0=2+O(N^{-2}),\qquad A_j,\ B_j=\tan^2(\pi x_i)+O(N^{-1}) =X_i^{-2}+O(N^{-1}). \tag{20} \] The leading symbol of its physical recurrence is therefore \[ 2+\frac2{X_i^2} -\frac{e^{p_i}+e^{-p_i}}{X_i^2} =2-\frac4L=\zeta, \tag{21} \] independently of \(i\), because \(\sinh^2(p_i/2)=X_i^2/L\). This identity is realized by the actual source, not only by the stationary equations. The pressure theorem gives, uniformly on every \(K\Subset\mathcal X^\circ\), \[ \Gamma_{\mathbf j} =N^{-3}\mathcal A(\mathbf j/N) e^{N\mathcal G(\mathbf j/N)}(1+O_K(N^{-1})), \qquad \mathcal A>0. \tag{22} \] Its neighboring physical indices remain in a slightly larger strict compact for sufficiently large \(N\). Thus \[ \frac{\Gamma_{\mathbf j\pm\mathbf e_i}}{\Gamma_{\mathbf j}} =e^{\pm p_i(\mathbf j/N)}(1+O_K(N^{-1})). \tag{23} \] Substituting into the exact equation (7) proves \[ \boxed{\qquad \frac{\phi(CF_{j_1}F_{j_2}F_{j_3})} {\phi(F_{j_1}F_{j_2}F_{j_3})} =\zeta(\mathbf j/N)+O_K(N^{-1}). \qquad} \tag{24} \] The original trace in numerator and denominator includes all internal first normals. By (17), \(\zeta\le-14\), with strict inequality on (8). It lies outside the physical Casimir spectrum \(\{c_r\}\subset[-2,2]\). This is an asymptotic characteristic of a growing source packet and a ratio of an indefinite original observation. It is not an additional eigenvalue of the finite operator, nor is (5) being replaced by an exact eigenvector equation. ## 4. Fixed-degree inserted coupons have a calibrated coefficient **Theorem 2.** Fix an integer \(d\ge0\) and a compact \(K\Subset\mathcal X^\circ\). For any polynomial \(q(C)=\sum_{r=0}^dq_rC^r\), uniformly over physical triples with \(\mathbf j/N\in K\), \[ \frac{\phi(q(C)F_{j_1}F_{j_2}F_{j_3})}{\Gamma_{\mathbf j}} =q(\zeta(\mathbf j/N)) +O_{K,d}\!\left(N^{-1}\sum_{r=0}^d|q_r|\right). \tag{25} \] The coefficients may depend on \(N\); the displayed coefficient norm records that dependence. In particular, if they stay bounded and \(|q(\zeta)|\) has a positive lower bound on \(K\), uniform in \(N\), this original coupon has the nonzero leading coefficient \(q(\zeta)\) times (22). **Proof.** By (6) the numerator is exactly \(q(\mathscr J_{N,w_1})\Gamma_N\) at the physical triple. For a fixed \(r\), expand \(r\) successive applications of the three-term physical recurrence. It involves only the indices \(j_1-r,\ldots,j_1+r\); they all lie in the regular bulk for large \(N\). Each coefficient is bounded uniformly and changes by \(O(N^{-1})\) under these finitely many shifts. For every fixed integer \(v\), (22) likewise gives \[ \frac{\Gamma_{\mathbf j+v\mathbf e_1}}{\Gamma_{\mathbf j}} =e^{v p_1(\mathbf j/N)}(1+O_{K,d}(N^{-1})). \tag{26} \] Thus the finite recurrence expansion, including all its signs, is its constant-coefficient symbol to the \(r\)-th power, with absolute error \(O_{K,d}(N^{-1})\). By (21) that symbol is \(\zeta\). Linearity in the coefficients of \(q\) proves (25). No absolute replacement of the original trace has occurred. \(\square\) The number of steps must remain fixed here. A literal crossing \(R^n\), even for fixed nonzero \(n\), generally has canonical degree growing with \(N\); it is not covered by (25). The theorem also does not estimate external \(G_j\) insertions. Their activated Newton bands require a separate coherent comparison beyond the established fold window. ## Complete direct sources Both complete texts were read and their directly used implications checked at the following pins: * [Triple-row pressure](research_physical_triple_row_pressure.md), SHA256 df556243507231e0edb2ea5234163b29623b6d5751b9be987d8f4d967170db4e: the exact scalar, strict optimizer, its gradient and the uniform nonzero physical amplitude. * [Ordinary Jacobi source and period monodromy](research_unturned_endpoint_exact_period_monodromy.md), SHA256 d082d1ef103c7c200340e36c6a79442ee658bf2582549cd399acb0384391a7a1: the ordinary triangular operator, its original kernel forcing and full characteristic multiplicities. Only written mathematics, source-text reads and metadata hashes were used. No mathematical programs, numerical evaluations, tests, builds or compilations were run. Frozen notes and public manuscripts were not changed.

title: A quantum flag model for the true cup source
text: # A quantum flag model for the true cup source 24 November 2026. Written research proof. The complete physical cup source has a unitary matrix-coordinate model. In these coordinates every canonical based quantum meridian acts by an explicit polynomial difference operator. The clock degree rises by at most one per regular meridian entry, at every width and level. The original last-marked closing is exactly one specified cyclic Weyl coefficient of the actual word state, with its original phase and scale. This identifies a full source and its observation, not a conditional coideal eigenmode. A positive regular-boundary limit gives inverse-pair flag circles for the cup state. The original closing still selects its prescribed coefficient; neither that limit nor the polynomial module gives a lower bound for the coefficient after an arbitrary braid. ## 1. Physical tensors and a unitary source map Use the complete conventions of B and M below. Put \[ N\ge2,\quad d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\quad x=-q^{-1}. \] The physical basis \(e_0,\ldots,e_d\) is orthonormal. Retain \[ Ke_a=xQ^{-a}e_a,\quad Ee_a=(Q^{-a}-1)e_{a-1},\quad Fe_a=(1-Q^{a+1})e_{a+1},\qquad e=qE. \tag{1} \] The missing endpoint arrows are zero. The letter \(e\) is M's actual upper Gauss entry; its factor \(q\) is essential below. The original tensors are \[ \mathbf p_{ab}=Nx^{-b}\mathbf1_{a+b=d},\quad \ell_{ab}=x^a\mathbf1_{a+b=d}/N,\quad m_{ab}=x^b/N^2. \tag{2} \] At width \(2k\), write \[ u_0=\mathbf p^{\otimes k},\quad \ell_0=\ell^{\otimes(k-1)}\otimes m,\quad Z_N(R)=\ell_0Ru_0,\qquad K_N=\chi_N Z_N(R). \tag{3} \] Here \(R\) is an original signed unmarked braid word. It preserves integer degree and the cup source has degree \(kd\). All its crossing scalars and the external \(\chi_N\) remain. Let \(J e_a=e_{d-a}\) and \(U=J\operatorname{diag}(x^{-a})\). Thus \(U\) is unitary and \(\mathbf p=N\operatorname{vec}U\), with the first tensor index the matrix row. Put \(\psi=\mathbf p/N^{3/2}=\operatorname{vec}U/\sqrt N\). For one pair define \[ \mathscr C(X)=(X\otimes I)\psi,\qquad \langle\mathscr C(X),\mathscr C(Y)\rangle =N^{-1}\operatorname{Tr}(X^\dagger Y). \tag{4} \] Tensor these maps over the ordered pairs \((1,2),\ldots,(2k-1,2k)\). Their domain is \(\operatorname{End}(V_N^{\otimes k})\), with inner product \(\tau_k(X^\dagger Y)\), \(\tau_k=N^{-k}\operatorname{Tr}\). The resulting \(\mathscr C_k\) is unitary onto the entire physical \(2k\)-head space. In particular \[ \psi_0=u_0/N^{3k/2}=\mathscr C_k(I),\qquad X_R=\mathscr C_k^{-1}R\psi_0 . \tag{5} \] This defines the unique full word state \(X_R\) without its scalar value. No physical head is swapped. The matrix indices merely label the original odd heads and their ordered cup partners. The exact first-to-second transpose and its inverse are \[ \theta(A)=(U^{-1}AU)^{\mathsf T},\qquad S=\theta^{-1}, \qquad (A\otimes B)\mathscr C(X)=\mathscr C(AXS(B)). \tag{6} \] They are complex-linear antiautomorphisms, not Hermitian adjoints. The literal cup and ordered coproduct give \[ \begin{array}{c|ccc} &K&e&F\\ \hline \theta&K^{-1}&-K^{-1}e&-FK\\ S&K^{-1}&-eK^{-1}&-KF . \end{array} \tag{7} \] The orders in the two rows differ. Equations (4),(6) also follow directly from vectorization, fixing all phases in (7). ## 2. Actual regular meridians and cyclic Weyl coordinates Let \(v e_a=Q^{-a}e_a\), and let \(T e_a=e_{a-1\ ({\rm mod}\ N)}\). Then \[ v^N=T^N=I,\quad Tv=Q^{-1}vT,\quad K=-q^{-1}v,\quad e=q(Q^{-1}v-1)T,\quad F=(1-v^{-1})T^{-1}. \tag{8} \] These are exact physical matrices: the apparent cyclic wrap of \(e\) has coefficient \(Q^{-1}v_d-1=0\), and that of \(F\) has coefficient \(1-v_0^{-1}=0\). No endpoint arrow was restored. Use M's canonical ordered matrices \[ b_-=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\-KF&K\end{pmatrix},\quad b_+=\begin{pmatrix}K&e\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\quad G=b_-^{-1}b_+ =\begin{pmatrix}K&e\\FK&K^{-1}+Fe\end{pmatrix}. \tag{9} \] Their inverses are bounded physical matrices. M proves \[ G^2-cG+QI_2=0,\qquad G^{-1}=Q^{-1}(cI_2-G),\qquad c=-2q. \tag{10} \] Thus an inverse entry is a linear combination of regular entries and constants. In the Weyl coordinates, (9) is exactly \[ G=\begin{pmatrix} -q^{-1}v&q(Q^{-1}v-1)T\\ q(1-v)T^{-1}&q(v-2) \end{pmatrix}. \tag{11} \] In particular its lower-right entry has no \(v^{-1}\) term. Replacing \(e=qE\) by \(E\) would change this finite identity. For physical head \(j\), set \(P_{j-1}=b_{-,j-1}\cdots b_{-,1}\) and retain the actual based meridian \[ H_j=P_{j-1}^{-1}G_jP_{j-1}. \tag{12} \] At principal level the physical \(SL_2\) lift is \(-H_j\). M proves that these are the actual quantum Hurwitz observables of both signed crossings, with bounded polynomial inverses. We count each entry of \(H_j\) or \(H_j^{-1}\) as one regular entry. A regular word is an ordered product of such scalar operator entries, or a finite sum of them. No localization by a head Gauss entry is included in this definition. The \(N^{2k}\) matrices \[ W_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b} =\prod_{i=1}^k v_i^{a_i}T_i^{b_i}, \qquad 0\le a_i,b_i<N, \] are an orthonormal basis for \(\tau_k(X^\dagger Y)\). Hence \[ X=\sum_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}x_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b} W_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b},\qquad \tau_k(X)=x_{\mathbf0,\mathbf0},\quad \tau_k(X^\dagger X)=\sum|x_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}|^2 . \tag{13} \] Every reduction here is cyclic. Ordinary Laurent coefficients cannot replace these coefficients when exponents cross a multiple of \(N\). ## 3. The exact two-head flag module We give the full action on a single cup, not only its value on \(I\). Let \(X=f(v)T^m\), \(m\in\mathbb Z\), and put \[ M_m=Q^m,\qquad D_Qf(v)=\frac{f(Qv)-f(v)}v . \] The displayed quotient is a polynomial. The first based matrix is \(H_1=G_1\), and its entries act by left multiplication in (11). Write \(\mathcal H_{ab}(X)\) for the exact Choi action of the entry \((H_2)_{ab}\): \((H_2)_{ab}\mathscr C(X)=\mathscr C(\mathcal H_{ab}(X))\). Direct multiplication of \(H_2=b_{-,1}^{-1}G_2b_{-,1}\), followed by (6),(7), gives \[ \begin{split} \mathcal H_{11}(X)&=XK^{-1}+KF XeK^{-1},\\ \mathcal H_{12}(X)&=-KXeK^{-1},\\ \mathcal H_{22}(X)&=-FKXeK^{-1}+X(K+eF),\\ \mathcal H_{21}(X)&=FXK^{-1}-K^{-1}XF +FKFXeK^{-1}-FX(K+eF). \end{split} \tag{14} \] These are linear operators on the matrix source. They are not multiplication by four substituted scalar entries. For completeness their polynomial forms are \[ \mathcal H_{11}(fT^m) =q[(v-1-M_m)f(Qv)+M_mD_Qf(v)]T^m, \] \[ \mathcal H_{12}(fT^m)=-q(v-QM_m)f(v)T^{m+1},\qquad \mathcal H_{22}(X)=-Q\mathcal H_{11}(X)-2qX, \tag{15} \] and \[ \mathcal H_{21}(fT^m)=q\,\frac{\mathcal N_{m,f}(v)}{v^2}T^{m-1}, \] \[ \begin{split} \mathcal N_{m,f}(v)={}&(v-M_m)f(v)\\ &+(v-1)[2v-M_m(1+Q^{-1})]f(Qv)\\ &+Q(v-1)(v-Q^{-1})(v-M_m/Q)f(Q^2v). \end{split} \tag{16} \] There is no pole in (16). Its constant coefficient is zero. Its coefficient of \(v\) also vanishes separately for the constant and linear coefficients of \(f\). For example those two linear coefficient cancellations are \[ -2-M_m/Q-M_m+1+1+M_m+M_m/Q=0,\qquad M_m(1+Q)-M_m-QM_m=0. \] Thus \(v^2\) divides the numerator as a polynomial, at every level. Equations (15),(16) show that each entry raises clock polynomial degree by at most one. This holds before reducing \(v^N=1\). One check on the order is obtained by applying (14) to \(I\). If \(G_1=(g_{ab})\), the exact result is \[ H_2\psi= \begin{pmatrix} g_{22}&-Qg_{12}\\ -Qg_{21}&Qg_{11}-(Q-1)g_{22} \end{pmatrix}\psi . \tag{17} \] This tends to the classical inverse, but does not authorize replacing products by entrywise multiplication of (17). Their exact action is composition of the operators (14). ## 4. Completed pairs and arbitrary width For a completed pair retain the actual totals \(K_{\rm pair}=K_1K_2\) and \(F_{\rm pair}=F_1+K_1^{-1}F_2\). The same Choi calculation gives \[ K_{\rm pair}\mathscr C(fT^m)=M_m\mathscr C(fT^m), \] \[ F_{\rm pair}\mathscr C(fT^m) =\mathscr C\!\left( [f(Qv)-M_m^{-1}f(v)-D_Qf(v)]T^{m-1}\right). \tag{18} \] For the second identity, (6) first gives \(FX-K^{-1}XKF\); its two negative powers of \(v\) combine into \(-D_Qf\). Both maps preserve clock polynomial degree. So do \(K_{\rm pair}^{\pm1}\) and their ordered products with \(F_{\rm pair}\). The exact coproduct order is \[ b_{-,{\rm pair}}=b_{-,2}b_{-,1} =\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\-K_{\rm pair}F_{\rm pair}&K_{\rm pair}\end{pmatrix}, \qquad b_{-,{\rm pair}}^{-1} =\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\F_{\rm pair}&K_{\rm pair}^{-1}\end{pmatrix}. \tag{19} \] Consequently dressing a later meridian by any preceding completed cup pair preserves the clock degree of that preceding pair. This statement uses the full source action (18), including when the preceding pair has already been acted on by other entries. Tensor the polynomial modules in their original pair order. For an odd head of a pair, its own \(G\) acts by left multiplication; for an even head, its own based action is (14). Earlier completed pairs act through (19). An entry of a finite auxiliary matrix product is a sum of compositions of these stated maps. This proves \[ \boxed{\quad \mathscr C_k^{-1}W\psi_0 =\sum_{\mathbf m}f_{\mathbf m}(v_1,\ldots,v_k) T_1^{m_1}\cdots T_k^{m_k},\qquad \deg f_{\mathbf m}\le L \quad} \tag{20} \] for every regular word \(W\) of length at most \(L\). The degree is total clock polynomial degree. Inverse meridian entries obey the same bound by (10). The proof is induction: a prefix action preserves total degree and each own entry adds at most one. Linearity covers nonseparable coefficient polynomials. All calculations hold modulo the actual cyclic relations and include \(N=2\), composite levels, arbitrary shifts and empty prefixes. Polynomial division in (15),(16) was done before that reduction. No physical pair-Casimir nilpotent direction or complementary source coordinate is deleted. ## 5. The original marked scalar is one Frobenius coefficient Put \(p=k-1\) and let \(\mathcal P=\prod_{i=1}^p\mathcal Q_{2i}\), where \(\mathcal Qe_a=Q^ae_a\). On the total integer degree \(kd\) subspace, the literal row is exactly \[ \ell_0=(x^d/N^2)^p N^{-3}u_0^\dagger\mathcal P. \tag{21} \] Indeed an ordinary cap is \((x^d/N^2)\mathbf p^\dagger(I\otimes\mathcal Q)\). On pair degree \(d\), the last marked row is \(N^{-3}\mathbf p^\dagger\). The ordinary caps first fix the degrees of their own pairs; total degree then forces degree \(d\) on the last pair. This proves (21), including its phase and its necessary domain. It is not an equality of ambient rows. For any actual degree-preserving word \(R\), (5),(21) give \[ Z_N(R)=x^{dp}N^p\langle\psi_0,\mathcal P R\psi_0\rangle. \] The Choi clock identity is \(U\mathcal Q U^\dagger=Q^{-1}v\). Therefore the exact full-source period is \[ \boxed{\quad Z_N(R)=x^{dp}N^pQ^{-p}\, \tau_k(v_1\cdots v_p X_R) =x^{dp}N^pQ^{-p}\,x_{\boldsymbol\eta,\mathbf0}(R), \quad \boldsymbol\eta=(d,\ldots,d,0). \quad} \tag{22} \] Here \(x_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}(R)\) are the canonical cyclic Weyl coefficients (13) of the full \(X_R\). For \(k=1\) the product is empty and \(\boldsymbol\eta=0\). Equivalently the prefactor is \(N^px^{-dp}\), since \(x^{2d}=Q\). No coefficient in (22) has been normalized using its unknown value. The full coefficient chart and boundary budget satisfy \[ \sum_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}|x_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}(R)|^2 =\|R\psi_0\|_{\rm phys}^2,\qquad |Z_N(R)|\le N^p\left(\sum|x_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}(R)|^2\right)^{1/2}. \tag{23} \] The initial state is \(X_I=I\). The normalized cup has norm one and the extension (22)'s row has dual norm \(N^p\). Any true-source constraints are carried by the same unitary map; the whole matrix space is not asserted to be the saturated source. There is a precise selection cutoff for regular observations. If a degree-preserving \(W\) is a sum of regular words of length at most \(L\), (20),(22) imply \[ Z_N(W)\ne0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad L\ge(k-1)(N-1). \tag{24} \] Indeed every surviving term must supply exponent at least \(N-1\) in each of the first \(p\) clock variables before cyclic reduction. Their sum is at least \(p(N-1)\). Shift aliases cannot change this clock degree requirement. At \(k=1\) the assertion is vacuous. An actual crossing has level-dependent degree; (24) makes no claim that a fixed braid word is a bounded regular word. ## 6. A regular holomorphic flag-circle limit The true cup is a positive vector state. For its fixed holomorphic regular observations it has the following boundary representative, before its original closing is applied. For \(w\) on the unit circle put \[ G_0(w)=\begin{pmatrix}0&-w^{-1}\\w&-2\end{pmatrix}. \] It has determinant one, trace \(-2\), and a noncentral parabolic flag \([w^{-1}:1]\). For any fixed regular word \(W\), \[ \begin{split} \langle\psi_0,W(H_1,\ldots,H_{2k})\psi_0\rangle =\int_{\mathbb T^k} W(&G_0(w_1),G_0(w_1)^{-1},\ldots,\\ &G_0(w_k),G_0(w_k)^{-1}) \prod_{i=1}^k\frac{dw_i}{2\pi i w_i} +O_W(N^{-1}). \end{split} \tag{25} \] This includes inverse words by (10). Here is a direct proof from the actual module. For fixed word degree, all shifts and clock degrees are bounded independently of \(N\). For sufficiently large \(N\), normalized cyclic trace in (13) therefore becomes ordinary constant term in \(v_i,T_i\). The coefficient formulas (15),(16),(18) are regular Laurent polynomials in \(q\) after their proved divisions. Replacing \(q\) by one costs \(O_W(N^{-1})\). At \(q=1\) and \(v=0\), the first matrix in (11) is \(G_0(w)\), with \(T=w^{-1}\). The second-pair maps become multiplication by \(G_0(w)^{-1}\). A completed-pair \(K_{\rm pair}\) becomes one and \(F_{\rm pair}\) becomes zero, so preceding prefixes become identity. Finally constant term in \(T_i\) is the stated flag Haar integral. This proves (25) with all original based orders retained. Formula (25) concerns the holomorphic regular algebra, not its full closure under Hermitian adjoints. The flag curve is not asserted to represent that larger positive moment problem. Formula (22) also has its separate unitary clock insertion and growing selected exponent; neither may be removed to replace the original scalar by (25). The flag variables are relative boundary data, not independently declared global framing gauges or knot meridians chosen after sewing. ## 7. What this changes and what remains The coordinate map is unitary on the complete physical source. It retains the entire cup, every coherent input term, actual signed crossings, the original last mark, and the separate \(\chi_N\). It does not project to a selected coideal height or a value-only pair-Casimir quotient. The statements are at the fixed quantum root. Parameter normals require their original families; the cyclic Weyl identities are not differentiated as off-root identities. The exact maps (14)--(20) supply a canonical polynomial module for regular quantum holonomy observations. Equation (22) identifies the original scalar's precise coefficient in that same full source. A change to these fixed linear coordinates preserves the degree of a polynomial variational formulation; no convexity theorem for an anchored quartic is inferred. Degree four in auxiliary variational variables is not bounded degree in the regular physical meridian entries. The level-dependent crossing, its original Frobenius coefficient and all remaining coherent sewing must still be estimated. No volume lower bound, nonzero original scalar, or finite-exception theorem is proved here. ## Complete inputs and coverage Generic vectorization, maximally entangled cap marginals and their source-projection guard already occur in [the earlier cap-projection note](research_main_color_cap_projection_energy.md). No novelty for those facts or Weyl orthogonality is claimed. B supplies the physical cup, ordinary and marked caps, their integer degree conventions and original scalar. M supplies the actual ordered quantum meridians, polynomial inverse and signed Hurwitz transport. The additions are the typed polynomial module at every width and the exact original co-source coefficient in that full module. | Label | Complete text | Lines | SHA256 | | --- | --- | ---: | --- | | B | [Balanced original marked observations](research_coideal_balanced_marked_height_observations.md) | 467 | 214c462d38a4e1c8bbe64e998d21f259859909a89e8767fde5b234f6dbdde4a6 | | M | [Bounded actual quantum meridians](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_bounded_quantum_meridian_transport.md) | 215 | dac1e5656b4b1e6923b8be5efc0e0543428fc3a2829d1183053cc899aa1fe5c8 | Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used.
