# Uniform confluence depth for the original generic fusion source Written research proof, 22 November 2026. The generic fusion coordinates of the actual invariant source can be regularized using a number of quantum-parameter jets bounded by tensor width, independently of the level. An explicit Clebsch inclusion and Casimir-projector dual give the pole bound. Finite coefficient equations then recover the saturated root source without an unspecified large minor inverse. The saturated source and its divided-current characterization are already known in [S,D]. The new assertion is an effective uniform confluence budget for its actual generic fusion frames. This is not an analytic norm bound or an identification with a formal cyclic tetrahedron kernel. ## 1. The actual family and the statement Fix \(N\ge2\), \(d=N-1\), \(q_0=e^{\pi i/N}\), and an even number \(\ell\ge2\) of physical heads. Let \[ u=\zeta-q_0,\qquad \mathcal O=\mathbb C\{u\},\qquad \mathcal K=\operatorname{Frac}(\mathcal O),\qquad ho=\zeta-\zeta^{-1},\quad [j]= rac{\zeta^j-\zeta^{-j}}{ho},\quad [j]!=\prod_{r=1}^j[r]. 	ag{1} \] All half-integral Cartan powers use the fixed analytic logarithm of \(\zeta\) near \(q_0\). A pole bound \(J\) means that multiplying every matrix entry by \(u^J\) makes it regular. The neighborhood in \(u\) may depend on \(N\); no uniform analytic radius is asserted. Use the actual generic balanced leaf family of [S], and put \[ \mathcal M_{\mathcal O}=V_d(\zeta)^{\otimes\ell},\qquad \mathcal I_{\mathcal K} =\operatorname{Inv}_{\mathcal K} (\mathcal M_{\mathcal O}\otimes\mathcal K), \quad \Lambda=\mathcal I_{\mathcal K}\cap\mathcal M_{\mathcal O}. 	ag{2} \] The lattice is saturated, free of rank \(g=\dim_{\mathcal K}\mathcal I_{\mathcal K}\), and its root fiber \[ \mathcal V=\Lambda/u\Lambda \ \subset\ \mathcal M_{\mathcal O}/u\mathcal M_{\mathcal O} 	ag{3} \] is embedded in the original physical root tensor. These statements, and the fact that every original regular braid/cup source lies in this fiber, are established in [S,D]. The entire raw root invariant space may be larger than (3). **Theorem.** For every binary fusion tree \(T\) with the \(\ell\) leaves labelled \(d\) and root label zero, there are explicitly defined matrices \[ B_T:\mathcal K^g\longrightarrow \mathcal M_{\mathcal O}\otimes\mathcal K,\qquad L_T:\mathcal M_{\mathcal O}\otimes\mathcal K \longrightarrow\mathcal K^g \] such that \[ \operatorname{im}B_T=\mathcal I_{\mathcal K},\qquad L_TB_T=I,\qquad u^{J_\ell}B_T,\ u^{J_\ell}L_T 	ext{ have regular entries},\qquad J_\ell=(5\ell+4)(\ell-1). 	ag{4} \] Consequently the intrinsic fusion-coordinate lattice \(\Lambda_T=B_T^{-1}\Lambda\) satisfies \[ u^{J_\ell}\mathcal O^g \subset\Lambda_T \subset u^{-J_\ell}\mathcal O^g . 	ag{5} \] All confluence depths are therefore bounded in terms of width, independently of \(N\), including even and composite levels. More explicitly, set \(J=J_\ell\), \(C_T=u^JB_T\). The full physical source fiber is computed by the finite formula \[  oxed{\quad \mathcal V= \left\{[u^{2J}](C_Tz):  egin{array}{l} z\in(\mathcal O/u^{2J+1})^g,\ [u^k](C_Tz)=0\quad(0\le k<2J) \end{array}ight\}. \quad} 	ag{6} \] Thus the Laurent coefficients of \(B_T\) at orders \(-J,\ldots,J\) suffice. No jet of an unknown knot value enters. If \(W\) is any whole actual regular physical braid word, then \[ L_{T'}WB_T 	ext{ has pole order at most }2J . 	ag{7} \] The bound does not grow with the number of letters in the word. At the root its action on (3) is simply the restriction of the original \(W(q_0)\); no positive-order jet of \(W\) is needed for that root-value operation. ## 2. Generic modules and the actual balanced leaf gauge For a nonnegative integer color \(A\), use the divided-\(F\) basis \(v_j^{(A)}=F^jv_0^{(A)}/[j]!\), \(0\le j\le A\). The matrices are \[ Fv_j=[j+1]v_{j+1},\qquad Ev_j=[A-j+1]v_{j-1},\qquad Kv_j=\zeta^{A-2j}v_j , 	ag{8} \] with the missing endpoint arrows zero. These matrices have Laurent-polynomial entries for every color. Use \[ \Delta E=E\otimes K+I\otimes E,\qquad \Delta F=F\otimes I+K^{-1}\otimes F . 	ag{9} \] The normalized Casimir is \[ \Omega=ho^2FE+\zeta K+\zeta^{-1}K^{-1}. 	ag{10} \] It has eigenvalue \(\lambda_A=\zeta^{A+1}+\zeta^{-A-1}\) on a highest weight \(A\) module. For an actual leaf \(A=d\), define \[ s_a=(-ho)^{-a}\zeta^{-a(a+1)/2},\qquad w_a=s_av_a^{(d)} . 	ag{11} \] Direct substitution gives \[  egin{split} Fw_a&=(1-\zeta^{2a+2})w_{a+1},\ ho^2Ew_a&=\zeta^{-N} (1-\zeta^{2(N-a)})w_{a-1},\ Kw_a&=\zeta^d\zeta^{-2a}w_a. \end{split} 	ag{12} \] These are exactly [S]'s actual balanced generic matrices, including their zero endpoint arrows. Every \(s_a\) and its inverse is a DVR unit at \(q_0\), because \(ho(q_0)
e0\). The gauge and all its phases are retained on the physical source, operators and rows. Its possible large complex norm is not discarded or claimed bounded. ## 3. A literal Clebsch inclusion and an elementary generic decomposition Take colors \(A,B\) and \[ C=A+B-2k,\qquad 0\le k\le\min(A,B). \] There is a highest vector \[ h_C=\sum_{r=0}^k b_r\, v_r^{(A)}\otimes v_{k-r}^{(B)},\qquad b_0=1 . 	ag{13} \] The equation \(\Delta E\,h_C=0\) gives exactly \[  rac{b_{r+1}}{b_r} =-\zeta^{-B+2k-2r-2}  rac{[B-k+r+1]}{[A-r]}, \quad b_r=(-1)^r\zeta^{r(2k-B-r-1)}  rac{[B-k+r]![A-r]!}{[B-k]![A]!}. 	ag{14} \] This follows by comparing the coefficient of \(v_r^{(A)}\otimes v_{k-r-1}^{(B)}\). Define \[ \iota_{A,B}^{C}(v_j^{(C)}) = rac{(\Delta F)^j}{[j]!}h_C . 	ag{15} \] This is the prescribed inclusion, with all normalization phases fixed by (13)--(14). For completeness these inclusions give the entire generic pair tensor. The elementary commutator calculation gives \[ (\Delta E)(\Delta F)^j h_C =[j][C-j+1](\Delta F)^{j-1}h_C . 	ag{16} \] It proves nonvanishing through \(j=C\). If \(F^{C+1}h_C\) were nonzero, it would be a highest vector of negative weight \(-C-2\). Its subsequent \(F\)-string could not terminate: all the coefficients in (16), with that negative highest weight, are nonzero over \(\mathcal K\). This contradicts nilpotence of \(F\) on the finite tensor. Hence (15) is an intertwiner from the full \(V_C\). Its Casimir eigenvalue is \(\lambda_C\). The eigenvalues for the distinct allowed colors \(C\) are distinct over \(\mathcal K\). The images are therefore independent, and \[ \sum_{k=0}^{\min(A,B)}(A+B-2k+1)=(A+1)(B+1) 	ag{17} \] shows that they exhaust the tensor product. No semisimplicity theorem at the root has been used. ## 4. An exact projector dual with a bounded pole order Let \(\mathcal C(A,B)\) be the allowed color list in (13). On the generic pair put \[ P_C(\Omega)= \prod_{\substack{D\in\mathcal C(A,B)\D
e C}}  rac{\Omega-\lambda_DI}{\lambda_C-\lambda_D}. 	ag{18} \] This is a generic projector, not a root specialization of distinct Casimir values. Let \(\varepsilon_{0,k}\) extract the coefficient of \(v_0^{(A)}\otimes v_k^{(B)}\). On the pair degree \(k+j\), define \[ \pi_{A,B}^{C}(y)=  rac{[C-j]!}{[C]!}\, \varepsilon_{0,k}(\Delta E)^jP_C(\Omega)y\, v_j^{(C)} \quad(0\le j\le C); 	ag{19} \] on the other degrees define it to be zero. Since \[ E^jv_j^{(C)}= rac{[C]!}{[C-j]!}v_0^{(C)}, \qquad \varepsilon_{0,k}h_C=1 , \] the complete decomposition just proved gives \[ \pi_{A,B}^{C}\iota_{A,B}^{D}=\delta_{CD}I,\qquad \sum_C\iota_{A,B}^{C}\pi_{A,B}^{C}=I . 	ag{20} \] The dual is therefore literal and explicit. No unknown minor or favorable Hermitian form defines its normalization. Every positive integer quantum factorial satisfies \[ \operatorname{ord}_{u=0}[m]!=\lfloor m/Nfloor . 	ag{21} \] Indeed \([j]\) has a simple zero precisely when \(N\mid j\); its denominator \(ho\) is a unit. All colors in a tree with \(\ell\) leaves are at most \(\ell d<\ell N\). Equation (14) is a regular numerator divided by the product \([A][A-1]\cdots[A-r+1]\). Its pole order is at most \(\lfloor A/Nfloor\le\ell\). The descendant denominator \([j]!\) in (15) contributes at most \(\ell\). Thus every inclusion has pole bound \(2\ell\). For the projector dual, the exact factorization \[ \lambda_C-\lambda_D =\zeta^{-C-1}(1-\zeta^{C-D})(1-\zeta^{C+D+2}) 	ag{22} \] counts all possible vanishing denominators. The allowed \(D\)'s progress in steps of two over a list of length at most \(\ell N+1\). Each of the two congruences in (22) occurs at most \(\ell+2\) times. Each vanishing factor is simple; \(C-D
e0\) and \(C+D+2>0\). When both congruences hold they are counted twice. The whole denominator of (18) consequently has valuation at most \(2\ell+4\), in particular at most \(4\ell+4\). Its numerator is a product of regular matrices. The factorial ratio in (19) has pole order at most \(\lfloor C/Nfloor\le\ell\), and \((\Delta E)^j\) is regular. Every dual therefore has pole bound \(5\ell+4\). All estimates hold for each \(N\ge2\), with no prime-level or parity assumption. They are valuations, not estimates of the size of the nonzero factors. ## 5. Complete tree frames and whole physical words Compose (15) at the vertices of a binary tree, with root color zero and all admissible internal colors retained. Each root vector \(1\in V_0\) gives one invariant column. These columns form \(B_T\). Compose the duals (19) in the reverse order to obtain the rows of \(L_T\). Iterating (20) proves exactly that their columns form a basis of the generic invariant space and \(L_TB_T=I\). There are \(\ell-1\) internal vertices. A finite sum does not worsen a pole bound, while product bounds add. The local estimates therefore prove (4) with the stated \(J_\ell=(5\ell+4)(\ell-1)\). Conjugating the external leaves by the unit gauge (11) gives the same bounds in the actual physical coordinates. The lattice \(\Lambda\) is intrinsic, not chosen separately by a tree or word. If \(z\in\mathcal O^g\), then \(u^JB_Tz\) is regular and invariant, proving the first inclusion in (5). Conversely, if \(B_Tz=\psi\in\Lambda\), then \(z=L_T\psi\in u^{-J}\mathcal O^g\), proving the second. This bounds the elementary lattice exponents without inverting a determinant of growing size. Every whole original physical braid matrix \(W\) and its inverse are regular at \(q_0\): each individual physical crossing has finite summation indices below \(N\), hence only nonvanishing leaf factorial denominators. The actual cups and ordinary dualities are regular as in [S,M]. Regular generic polynomial circle coupons are included as well. Such maps preserve the generic invariant source and hence the saturated lattices. For an endomorphism word, \[ \operatorname{ord}_{u=0}(L_{T'}WB_T)\ge-2J 	ag{23} \] entrywise, no matter how many regular letters occur in \(W\). This is a bound on the whole product, not a sum of the apparent pole orders of sequential recoupling moves. Between the intrinsic lattices \(\Lambda_T,\Lambda_{T'}\), the generic change of tree is an isomorphism, with inverse the reverse change. In any actual lattice bases its matrix is unimodular over \(\mathcal O\). The generic coordinate matrices before this regularization need not be regular. Their root values must not be substituted for their complete confluence data. ## 6. The finite jet construction and the literal root closing Let \(C_T=u^JB_T\), a regular rectangular matrix. For any \(\psi\in\Lambda\), set \(x=L_T\psi\in u^{-J}\mathcal O^g\) and \(z=u^Jx\in\mathcal O^g\). Then \[ C_Tz=u^{2J}\psi. 	ag{24} \] Truncating \(z\) modulo \(u^{2J+1}\) does not change any coefficient in (6). Thus every root source vector occurs in its right side. Conversely, a polynomial representative \(z\) satisfying the equations in (6) gives \[ \psi=u^{-2J}C_Tz\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal O}. \] It is generically invariant, hence belongs to \(\Lambda\), and its root is the displayed coefficient in (6). This proves that finite formula in both directions. In particular the jet budget is \(2J\) for the regular matrix \(C_T\), or orders \(-J,\ldots,J\) for \(B_T\). Choose \(g\) independent root vectors from (6). Their integral lifts just constructed form a basis of \(\Lambda\): their reductions form a basis of the embedded fiber, so the assertion follows by the elementary local basis criterion over a DVR. This also gives regularized tree frames without choosing an unspecified generic minor. The number of matrix entries and source coordinates still grows with \(N\); only the required jet order is bounded independently of \(N\). For the original cup source \(b_N\), and any specified original root co-source row \(\lambda_N\), including the literal marked cap, the original scalar remains \[ \lambda_N W(q_0)b_N . 	ag{25} \] By [S,D], \(b_N\in\mathcal V\) and each regular original gate preserves that source. Formula (6) computes the same space in the actual physical tensor coordinates. One may therefore restrict each root gate to \(\mathcal V\) and restrict the very same row \(\lambda_N\), without changing (25). All cup, pivot, framing and external normalization factors remain in those specified data. No trace average or unmarked cap replaces them. For a root-value contraction this restriction needs only the actual \(W(q_0)\) and the frame jets in (6). There is no demand for positive-order jets of a long word merely because its fusion coordinates have poles. An independently prescribed quantum-normal source still requires its own differentiated word and cap data; these are not determined by \(W(q_0)\). ## Complete proof sources and scope All three complete texts were read at renewed matching pins: | Label | Complete source | SHA-256 | |---|---|---| | S | [Deformable original source, 327 lines](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_six_port_deformable_source_and_recoupling.md) | e29acfe75fb61cead48a08691037d6b81041bb5115b6578c9d2b563c8664c049 | | M | [Complete physical source module, 602 lines](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_complete_source_multiplicity_module.md) | 14cfb558f50c5b091cec9439692dfeb87129e31f38588cb1ebfd8e8547ac99a9 | | D | [All-width divided source filter, 204 lines](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_all_width_divided_source_projection.md) | dc83b5e232a3d258f516a479d7257e85b9e5663a38e166f07c6ad9ae81004a68 | The source lattice, its exact divided-current kernel, and its source-preserving orthogonal compression were already established in those notes. In particular this does not identify the larger raw root Hom space with the generic source. Generic Clebsch decompositions, recoupling, and DVR saturation are also established methods. The content here is the explicit dual and uniform pole budget, the finite-jet realization, and the whole-word bound with the original source retained. No eigenprojector is specialized separately: the entire frame confluence, including its Casimir Jordan normal coefficients on the original source, is retained. No analytic bound for the fusion matrices or their positive Grams follows from a bounded valuation. No equality with the earlier formal cyclic \(\Phi\), its projected pentagon, or a geometric critical module has been asserted. The familiar generic compatibility of actual frame changes is not a new pentagon theorem. The resulting sharp coherent word estimate, original scalar lower bound, and finite-exception theorem remain separate and unproved. Only written mathematics and text/hash inspection were used. No program, numerical experiment, test, build, git action, or earlier-final file edit was performed.

title: The geometric contribution for positive and signed circle paths
Uniform physical bounds for rational-word Casimir transport
text:
# Uniform physical bounds for rational-word Casimir transport Written proof, 24 November 2026. Every fixed original rational word transports the two pair-Casimir observables to operators with uniformly bounded norm in the original physical Hilbert--Schmidt metric. The bound is independent of the quantum level. Commutators of any fixed pair of these transported observables are \(O(N^{-1})\) in that same metric. The new estimate uses a finite cyclic-Weyl representation on the actual four-index arrays, with the physical endpoint factors retained. The exact Fricke identities and their rational-word transport are already proved in [B]. Their role here is to propagate a new uniform physical norm estimate, rather than to assert a new operator algebra. As a consequence, any sublinear selected family of full generalized eigenspaces of a transported Casimir has a subexponentially conditioned physical frame. No norm bound for the rational word or its inverse, and no lower bound for its original scalar closing, is inferred. An additional application compares low-degree polynomial observations of an actual transported coherent packet with that same packet in the physical metric. Its finite extraction method is already in [O]. ## 1. Original packet space and observables Let \(N\ge3\), \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\), \(x=q^d=-q^{-1}\), and \(c_0=q+q^{-1}\). Use the full original Hopf-box algebra and its physical metric from [P]: \[ \mathcal A_N=\mathbb C[\Omega]\simeq \mathbb C[Z]/P_N(Z),\qquad P_N(Z)=2T_N(Z/2)+2,\qquad \|B\|_{m ph}^2=\operatorname{Tr}(B^*B). 	ag{1} \] Here \(T_N\) is the Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind. The basis \(w_0,\ldots,w_d\) on each physical head is orthonormal. The physical quarter-turn is the genuine unscaled turn \(T\), not the swap of the two heads. For a complete physical Hopf box it is \[ (TB)_{a,b;c,e}=x^{a-e}B_{d-a,c;b,d-e}. 	ag{2} \] It preserves \(\mathcal A_N\), is unitary in (1), and satisfies \(T^2=I\). All original cup/cap and pivot factors in (2) remain. Write \(L_f(B)=fB\) for multiplication in the actual algebra, and set \[ X=L_\Omega,\qquad Y=TXT,\qquad \mathsf R=L_{R_N},\qquad \kappa=q^{d^2/2}. 	ag{3} \] Here \(R_N\) is the original positive crossing polynomial, including its Cartan scalar \(\kappa\). Its inverse is its full Hermite inverse, not an inverse defined only on distinct eigenvalues. In particular \(\mathsf R\) and \(T\) are invertible on the full space (1). A fixed rational word \(W_N\) is a fixed finite composition of \(T\) and \(\mathsf R^{\pm1}\). Fixed integer twist powers can equivalently be used as generators. The word and its integer powers are fixed before \(N\) varies. Any recorded scalar framing unit remains in the word; it cancels when an observable is conjugated. **Theorem 1.** Define \(Z\) in (15) below. For every fixed word \(W\), the actual transported operators \[ X_W=W_NXW_N^{-1},\quad Y_W=W_NYW_N^{-1},\quad Z_W=W_NZW_N^{-1} 	ag{4} \] satisfy \[ \max(\|X_W\|_{m ph},\|Y_W\|_{m ph},\|Z_W\|_{m ph}) \le C_W. 	ag{5} \] The norm is the operator norm on the packet space (1). For any two fixed words \(W,V\) and any \(A_W\in\{X_W,Y_W,Z_W\}\), \(B_V\in\{X_V,Y_V,Z_V\}\), \[ \|[A_W,B_V]\|_{m ph}\le C_{W,V}/N. 	ag{6} \] Constants may depend on the fixed words, but not on \(N\). No assertion in (5) bounds \(\|W_N\|\) or \(\|W_N^{-1}\|\). ## 2. Literal ambient formulas and the boundary wraps For the estimate, embed (1) in the full four-index Hilbert space \(\mathscr B_N=\operatorname{End}(V_N\otimes V_N)\). Write an array as \(B(a,b;c,e)\), with every index in \(\{0,\ldots,d\}\). The same expression (2) defines a unitary involution \(\widetilde T\) on this whole Hilbert space: its index permutation is an involution, and its two successive phases are \(x^{a-e}\) and \(x^{e-a}\). Its restriction to the original Hopf boxes is precisely \(T\). No different boundary invariant is defined by using this linear extension for a norm estimate. Let \(\widetilde X(B)=\Omega B\) and \(\widetilde Y=\widetilde T\widetilde X\widetilde T\). Direct substitution of the original balanced generators in [P] gives \[  egin{split} (\widetilde XB)(a,b;c,e)={}&D_X(a,b)B(a,b;c,e)\ &+A_+(a,b)B(a+1,b-1;c,e)\ &+A_-(a,b)B(a-1,b+1;c,e), \end{split} 	ag{7} \] where \[  egin{split} D_X(a,b)&=2q^{-1}Q^{-b}+2qQ^a-(q+q^{-1})Q^{a-b},\ A_+(a,b)&=Q^{-b}(1-Q^b)(1-Q^{a+1}),\ A_-(a,b)&=Q^{-b-1}(1-Q^{b+1})(1-Q^a). \end{split} 	ag{8} \] Only existing physical indices are used in (7). For example the \(A_+\) term is zero if \(a=d\) or \(b=0\), and the \(A_-\) term is zero if \(a=0\) or \(b=d\). These are exact root zeros. Conjugating (7) by the literal formula (2) gives \[  egin{split} (\widetilde YB)(a,b;c,e)={}&D_Y(a,c)B(a,b;c,e)\ &+B_-(a,c)B(a-1,b;c-1,e)\ &+B_+(a,c)B(a+1,b;c+1,e), \end{split} 	ag{9} \] with \[  egin{split} D_Y(a,c)&=2q^{-1}(Q^{-a}+Q^{-c}) -(q+q^{-1})Q^{-a-c-1},\ B_-(a,c)&=q^{-1}(1-Q^{-a})(1-Q^{-c}),\ B_+(a,c)&=q(1-Q^{-a-1})(1-Q^{-c-1}). \end{split} 	ag{10} \] For clarity, before simplification its lower-shift coefficient is \(xQ^{-c}(1-Q^c)(1-Q^{-a})\), and its upper-shift coefficient is \(x^{-1}Q^{-c-1}(1-Q^{c+1})(1-Q^{-a-1})\). These follow from the phases \(x\) and \(x^{-1}\) introduced by the two corresponding turns. They simplify to (10) using \(x=-q^{-1}\). The \(B_-\) term vanishes if \(a=0\) or \(c=0\), while the \(B_+\) term vanishes if \(a=d\) or \(c=d\). Therefore (7),(9) can now be read with all indices taken cyclically modulo \(N\): every newly introduced wrap term has coefficient zero. This check is needed even at even levels, where \(x^N=-1\). We have not assumed that the turn phase itself is an ordinary \(Q\)-clock. The exact zero factors remove its possible wrap discrepancy. ## 3. Finite cyclic-Weyl estimates in the physical metric On the cyclic array indices \(r=(a,b,c,e)\), define \[ (M_\alpha B)(r)=Q^{\alpha\cdot r}B(r),\qquad (S_vB)(r)=B(r+v mod N),\qquad \alpha,v\in\mathbb Z^4. 	ag{11} \] Both are unitary in the ambient physical Hilbert--Schmidt metric. Expanding the factors in (8),(10) expresses \(\widetilde X,\widetilde Y\) as fixed finite sums of monomials \(M_\alpha S_v\), with exponents bounded independently of \(N\) and uniformly bounded scalar coefficients. The exact multiplication rule is \[ (M_\alpha S_v)(M_ eta S_w) =Q^{ eta\cdot v}M_{\alpha+ eta}S_{v+w}. 	ag{12} \] Thus the commutator of two such monomials has norm at most \(| eta\cdot v-\alpha\cdot w|\,|Q-1|\). Summing the fixed number of terms proves \[ \|[\widetilde X,\widetilde Y]\| \le C|Q-1|\le C'/N. 	ag{13} \] Restriction gives the same estimate for the original \(X,Y\). Also [P] and unitarity of the turn give \[ \|X\|,\|Y\|\le18. 	ag{14} \] No exponentially conditioned change from Newton coordinates was used. For \(N\ge3\), put \(\Delta=q^2-q^{-2}\) and define the original Fricke-conjugated operator \[ Z= rac8{c_0}I+ rac{q^{-1}YX-qXY}{\Delta}. 	ag{15} \] This is not a new definition of a source transform: [B] proves that it equals the actual \(D_1\) on the full original Hermite algebra. Its apparent small denominator has a bounded physical numerator. Indeed \[ q^{-1}YX-qXY=q^{-1}[Y,X]+(q^{-1}-q)XY, 	ag{16} \] and \(c_0\ge1\), \(|\Delta|^{-1}\le N/4\) for \(N\ge3\). Equations (13),(14) already give a level-independent norm for \(Z\). We need a little more than its norm. The same quotient has a finite cyclic-Weyl extension of fixed complexity with bounded coefficients. Pair one term of \(\widetilde Y\widetilde X\) with its reversed term in \(\widetilde X\widetilde Y\). Apart from their common bounded scalar, the quotient coefficient is \[  rac{q^{-1}Q^a-qQ^b}{q^2-q^{-2}} = rac{q^2Q^b}{c_0}  rac{Q^{a-b-1}-1}{Q-1}, \qquad a,b\in\mathbb Z	ext{ fixed}. 	ag{17} \] The last ratio is a finite Laurent sum with at most \(|a-b-1|\) terms, or zero. Its coefficients have modulus one. This proves the assertion also when distinct monomial labels coincide modulo a small level. The scalar \(8/c_0\) is bounded. The extension is used only to estimate the actual restriction (15). More generally, any two fixed noncommutative polynomial expressions in \(X,Y,Z\), with fixed Laurent polynomials in \(q\) as scalar coefficients, admit such finite cyclic-Weyl extensions. Their physical norms are bounded, and their commutator is \(O(N^{-1})\) by (12). The fixed expressions may have different degrees; their constants are allowed to depend on those expressions. ## 4. Exact generator closure for every fixed rational word The required algebra identities are prior exact source results, not principal-symbol replacements. In the full Newton basis [A,B], let \(C=X\), \(J=Y\), and \[ V_n=\kappa^nT\mathsf R^{-n}T,\qquad D_n=V_nXV_{-n}. 	ag{18} \] The signed Fricke identities in [B] give \(D_1=Z\) and \(T D_{-1}T=Z\). Consequently \[ \mathsf RY\mathsf R^{-1}=Z. 	ag{19} \] The divisor-free recurrence [B, equation (17a)] is \[ qD_{n+2}+q^{-1}D_n+D_{n+1}Y=8I, \qquad n\in\mathbb Z. 	ag{20} \] Set \(G_n=T D_{-n}T=\mathsf R^nY\mathsf R^{-n}\). Conjugating (20), with its index reversed, gives \[ G_{n+2}=8qI-q^2G_n-qG_{n+1}X, \quad G_0=Y,\quad G_1=Z. 	ag{21} \] In particular define \(Z_-=8q^{-1}I-q^{-2}Z-q^{-1}YX\). The exact conjugation rules are \[  egin{array}{c|ccc} &X&Y&Z\ \hline \mathsf R(\cdot)\mathsf R^{-1} &X&Z&8qI-q^2Y-qZX\ \mathsf R^{-1}(\cdot)\mathsf R &X&Z_-&Y\ T(\cdot)T&Y&X&Z_- \end{array} 	ag{22} \] The order of every product is part of these identities. For the last entry, \(TZT=\mathsf R^{-1}Y\mathsf R=G_{-1}\) follows from \(Z=D_1\), and (21) gives precisely \(Z_-\). All crossing and turn normalizations are those in (3),(18). Repeated substitution in (22) writes every operator (4) as a fixed noncommutative polynomial in \(X,Y,Z\), with scalar coefficients that are Laurent polynomials in \(q\). Its degree and number of terms may depend on the fixed word. Section 3 therefore proves both (5) and (6). This is an exact root-level transport of the full operators, including every first-normal direction. The algebra identities in [B] already retain those normals and prove the divisor-free recursion. That note obtains \(\|D_n\|\le C_nN^{4|n|}\) in the ordinary canonical-polynomial real norm. The later [O, section 2] already proves uniform fixed-word observable bounds in the Newton coefficient norm. The estimate here is uniform in the original physical Hilbert--Schmidt operator norm, by the finite-Weyl realization. No equivalence between those packet metrics, and no transport of a Newton adjoint into this metric, is assumed. ## 5. Moving full-cluster frames There is a quantitative consequence for the actual transported invariant spaces. Fix a word \(W\), and put \(A_W=W_NXW_N^{-1}\) on \(\mathcal A_N\). Similarity preserves its full minimal polynomial \(P_N\). Its generalized eigenspaces are exactly \[ \mathcal S_{W,j}=W_N\mathcal A_{N,j}, 	ag{23} \] where \(\mathcal A_{N,j}\) is the original primary ideal. Their dimensions remain the original multiplicities one or two. Choose a physical Hilbert--Schmidt orthonormal basis \(E_{W,j}\) inside each selected full generalized eigenspace, and concatenate any \(m\) distinct nodes into \(E_W\). The derivative-zero cardinal proof in [C] applies without requiring that \(A_W\) be normal or complex symmetric. The cosine-node gaps are unchanged, and (5) gives \(\|A_W-c_jI\|\le C_W+2\). For clarity, use selected multiplicities \(
u_j\in\{1,2\}\) and \[ \ell_j(z)=\prod_{k
e j} \left( rac{z-c_k}{c_j-c_k}ight)^{
u_k}. 	ag{24} \] Take \(h_j=\ell_j\) at a simple node and \(h_j=(1-\ell_j'(c_j)(z-c_j))\ell_j\) at a double node. Then \(h_j(A_W)E_{W,k}=\delta_{jk}E_{W,k}\) exactly. The same factorial denominator as [C] yields \[ \|h_j(A_W)\| \le\exp\{C_W[m\log(eN/m)+\log N]\}. 	ag{25} \] This evaluates the actual operator factors and does not replace a nonnormal operator norm by the supremum on its scalar spectrum. Recover each coefficient block by \(h_j(A_W)\), sum their squared norms, and use the triangle inequality for the upper bound. Thus \[  oxed{\quad e^{-C_W\Lambda_{N,m}}I\le E_W^*E_W\le mI, \qquad \Lambda_{N,m}=m\log(eN/m)+\log N . \quad} 	ag{26} \] Every selected block is complete, including its actual transported normal direction. For any \(m_N=o(N)\), (26) controls arbitrary coherent coefficient vectors with subexponential cost. There is no assertion of a polynomial adapter from specified raw vectors \(W_Nv\) to these internally orthonormal blocks. In particular (26) does not normalize the actual source, bound its transport amplitude, or control the ambient spectral projection. The filters only recover blocks on the selected invariant sum; their values on unselected blocks have not been set to zero. ## 6. An actual coherent-source observation theorem Here the same physical bounds have a direct application to full source packets. We restate the generating unit and extraction identities from [O]; the new assertion is their consequence in the physical metric, not a new extraction method. For \(v_j=qQ^j\), define \[ \mathcal D_j(t)=\prod_{r=-j+1}^{0}(1+q^{-1}Q^rt),\qquad \mathcal B_j(t)=\prod_{r=j+2}^{N-j}(1+q^{-1}Q^rt). \] The actual centered generating unit \(A_N(t,\zeta)\), canonical of degree less than \(N\) in \(\zeta\), is specified by its full jets: \[  egin{split} A_N(t,c_j)&=\mathcal D_j(t)^2\mathcal B_j(t),\ \partial_\zeta A_N(t,c_j) &= rac{\mathcal D_j(t)^2t\,\partial_t\mathcal B_j(t)} {v_j-v_j^{-1}} \quad\hbox{at double nodes}. \end{split} 	ag{27} \] The canonical indices are \(0\le j\le\lfloor d/2floor\). At the odd simple middle only the value is prescribed. All products use the original empty-product convention. These are the actual generating-unit jets in [O], including their first-normal normalization. They determine \(A_N\) uniquely, with \(A_N(0,\zeta)=1\). In particular it is a unit for \(|t|<1\), since all its displayed node factors are nonzero there. Retain the original coherent source packet \[ \mathcal F_N(t)=N^{-1/2}R_N A_N(t,\zeta),\qquad w_N(y,z)=\mathcal F_N(y)\mathcal F_N(z) =N^{-1}R_N^2A_N(y,\zeta)A_N(z,\zeta). 	ag{28} \] Its scalar \(N^{-1}\) is not changed by our metric choice. Write \(M_t=L_{A_N(t)}\), \(M_w=L_{w_N(y,z)}\), and \(\mathcal L_n=\mathsf R^{-n}Y\mathsf R^n\). The norm-free full-Hermite gauge identity [O, equation (10)] is \[ b_t(X)M_t\mathcal L_nM_t^{-1} =\mathcal L_n-c_0t\mathcal L_{n+1} +t^2\mathcal L_{n+2}+8tI,\qquad b_t(X)=I+tX+t^2I. 	ag{29} \] That identity retains the seam zeros and the coalescing first normals before it is asserted in the quotient. It is not a relation in the distinct-root value quotient alone. Set \(B_w=M_wYM_w^{-1}\). Apply (29) twice and retain the exact \(R_N^2\) in (28). As [O] proves, \(b_y(X)b_z(X)B_w\) is a finite combination of \(X,I,\mathcal L_{-2},\ldots,\mathcal L_2\) with coefficients polynomial in \(y,z,q,q^{-1}\). Theorem 1 bounds their conjugates by any fixed \(W\) in the physical metric. Choose \(0<ho_W<1\) with \(ho_W C_W+ho_W^2\le1/2\). A Neumann series gives \(\|b_t(X_W)^{-1}\|\le2\) for \(|t|\leho_W\). Consequently \[ \|WXW^{-1}\|_{m ph}+ \|WB_wW^{-1}\|_{m ph}\le K_W, \qquad |y|,|z|\leho_W , 	ag{30} \] uniformly in \(N\). No separate norm bound for \(M_t\), \(M_w\), or their inverses is used. The other input is the exact finite-head extractor of [O]. For \(1\le D\le N/32\) and a nonzero polynomial \(P\) of degree at most \(D\), it constructs a noncommutative polynomial \(\mathscr A_{P,N}\) with \[ \mathscr A_{P,N}(X,Y)P(X)1=1,\quad \deg\mathscr A_{P,N}\le5D,\quad \|\mathscr A_{P,N}\|_{m coeff,1} \le rac{e^{CD}(N/D)^{12D}}{\|P\|_2}. 	ag{31} \] Here \(\|P\|_2\) is its ordinary monomial coefficient norm. To specify the extractor, [O] uses the monic source kernel rows \(g_j=K_j/\ell_j\), where \(K_j(\zeta)=\sum_{r=0}^j e_r(c_j)e_r(\zeta)\), \(e_r(\zeta)=S_r^{-2}\prod_{a<r}(c_a-\zeta)\), and \(\ell_j=(-1)^jS_{2j}/S_j^4\). Their lowering coefficients are \( eta_j=s_j^8/(s_{2j-1}s_{2j}^2s_{2j+1})>0\), with \(s_j=2\sin(\pi j/N)\), \(S_j=\prod_{r=1}^j s_r\). On the head \(g_0,\ldots,g_{2D}\), let \(F_j(Y)=\prod_{0\le r\le2D,\ r
e j}(Y-c_r)/(c_j-c_r)\). Expand \(P=\sum_{j\le D}a_jg_j\), choose the index supplied by [O], and take \[ \mathscr A_{P,N} = rac{F_0(Y)X^jF_j(Y)} {a_j\prod_{r=1}^j eta_r}. \] The sole descending path gives (31). The two factorially bounded filters and its descending coefficient give the exponent \(12D\). This is an identity in the full algebra; its proof in a finite polynomial head does not erase any physical normal after conjugation. **Theorem 2.** For every fixed word there are \(C_W,N_0\) such that, for \(N\ge N_0\), \(1\le D\le N/32\), \(\deg P\le D\), and \(|y|,|z|\leho_W\), \[  oxed{ egin{split} &e^{-C_WD}(D/N)^{24D}\|P\|_2^2\|Ww_N\|_{m ph}^2\ &\hspace{8mm}\le\|WP(X)w_N\|_{m ph}^2 \le e^{C_WD}\|P\|_2^2\|Ww_N\|_{m ph}^2 . \end{split}} 	ag{32} \] For \(D=0\), the exact identity is \(\|WP(X)w_N\|_{m ph}^2=|P|^2\|Ww_N\|_{m ph}^2\). The zero polynomial is included trivially. To prove the lower bound, conjugate (31) by the actual invertible \(\mathcal U=WM_w\). Its two generators become \(X_W\) and \(WB_wW^{-1}\), bounded by (30). Its coefficient sum and degree therefore bound the conjugated extractor by \(e^{C_WD}(N/D)^{12D}/\|P\|_2\). It maps \(WP(X)w_N\) exactly to \(Ww_N\). The resulting norm inequality, squared, proves the lower bound. The upper bound follows from \(WP(X)w_N=P(X_W)Ww_N\) and (5). The physical value \(\|1\|_{m ph}=N\) has not been set to one; it appears in neither ratio because extraction compares these same two transported packets. If \(D_N=o(N)\) and \(\|P_N^{m obs}\|_2=1\), (32) implies \[  rac1N\log  rac{\|WP_N^{m obs}(X)w_N(y,z)\|_{m ph}^2} {\|Ww_N(y,z)\|_{m ph}^2}\longrightarrow0 \qquad(|y|,|z|\leho_W) 	ag{33} \] uniformly on that bidisc. The unit \(w_N\) and invertible word make the denominator nonzero. The new physical rate of \(Ww_N\) is not computed here and need not equal its untransported rate. Nor does (33) bound the original marked scalar from below. There is also an exact specialization to the original empty packet. At \(y=z=0\), use (32) with the fixed word \(V=W\mathsf R^{-2}\). Since \(w_N(0,0)=N^{-1}R_N^2\) and \(P(X)\) commutes with \(\mathsf R\), its two packets become \(N^{-1}WP(X)1\) and \(N^{-1}W1\). Hence (32), and the sublinear-degree conclusion (33), hold with \(w_N\) replaced by \(1\), with constants depending on \(W\). ## 7. Source and geometric scope The construction always uses the genuine physical quarter-turn, the original positive crossing polynomial and its full inverse, and the complete algebra (1). It makes no replacement of the original marked cap, pivot, framing, or external normalization. Its four-index extension is a norm-estimating realization of these same operators, not a changed state sum. Uniformly bounded conjugated observables do not imply that \(W_N\) or its inverse has subexponential norm. They also do not imply a lower bound for a selected coefficient or for the original closing of \(W_N(1)\). No geometric canonical graph or contributing cycle is identified solely from the finite-Weyl symbols. An arbitrary Conway product of two independent child packets is not an invertible rational-word conjugacy. Its actual mixed forcing, described in [B], is not removed by (22). Turns or changes to overlapping pairings may move a chosen cluster, and its exterior and original closing still require their own source estimates. No new knot-volume lower bound or finite-exception theorem is claimed here. ## Complete inputs and closest coverage All five complete texts were read at their matching versions. | Label | Complete text | SHA256 | | --- | --- | --- | | P | [Uniform physical Conway source](research_conway_uniform_physical_quartic.md), 477 lines | 39895b430535f565d30133b46ef57f67589207bc83f40597ffe96e2ce79bbda8 | | B | [Exact finite-band unit-turn and branching operator](research_unit_turn_finite_band_branching_operator.md), 730 lines | 31d9f574c7dc3aaac07e4eb50c131b3328be46b3c2a2ef46f9dae7f0c4ddb9cb | | A | [Actual Newton turn and original signed alphabet](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_newton_turn_positive_gram.md), 434 lines | d8b21fa8db909120035e86e997a0e02cb84f8dce2dcf6fb244bb5c85c17e28a3 | | C | [Selected physical Casimir-cluster Gram](research_sublinear_physical_casimir_cluster_gram.md), 412 lines | 7cfecc06fdba21757a89abd8e33d630aaccf6a306de1fd6f4f35bbedce6dabdb | | O | [Coherent observations through fixed words](research_short_word_coherent_observation_transport.md), 509 lines | ff2fbaaa56c48bc6845bd58f964e10de66483df550a4b30005aed244ff0a0398 | Only written mathematics, complete text reads, and metadata hashes were used. title: Exact finite-band unit-turn conjugation and the branching forcing

# Exact finite-band unit-turn conjugation and the branching forcing Private written proof, 16 November 2026. Conjugating spectral multiplication by an original unit turn gives an explicit tridiagonal operator. A fixed number of turns therefore preserves a finite-band operator presentation, with polynomial operator cost for the conjugated multiplication itself. This is not a polynomial bound for the turn operator. The ordinary branching product has an additional mixed-difference forcing, retained below with its original full normal data. Its growth after turning remains uncontrolled by the present calculation. ## 1. Original operators and the conjugation formula Put \[ N\ge2,\quad D=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad \eta=(-1)^D,\quad \kappa=q^{D^2/2}, \] \[ s_j=2\sin(j\pi/N),\quad S_j=\prod_{h=1}^j s_h,\quad S_0=1, \qquad c_j=q^{2j+1}+q^{-2j-1}, \] \[ P_N(Z)=2T_N(Z/2)+2,\qquad e_j(Z)=S_j^{-2}\prod_{h<j}(c_h-Z),\qquad \mathcal A_N=\mathbb C[Z]/(P_N). 	ag{1} \] Here \(T_N\) in \(P_N\) is the usual Chebyshev polynomial. The physical turn is denoted \(T\), so \(Te_j=e_{D-j}\). The original kernel and Frobenius functional are \[ K_N(w,Z)=\sum_{j=0}^{D}e_j(w)e_j(Z),\qquad \phi_N(e_i e_j)=\mathbf1_{i+j=D}. \] Retain the original crossing \(R\), all its carriers, and \[ C f=Zf\pmod{P_N},\qquad J=TCT,\qquad U_\sigma=\kappa^\sigma TR^{-\sigma}T,\quad \sigma=\pm1. 	ag{2} \] Every algebra element below has its ordinary canonical representative of degree at most \(D\). In this basis, \[ Ce_j=c_je_j-s_{j+1}^2e_{j+1},\qquad Je_j=c_je_j-s_j^2e_{j-1}, 	ag{3} \] with out-of-range terms zero. In particular the raising term at \(j=D\) is zero in the full algebra. **Theorem 1.** For \(N\ge3\), \[  oxed{\quad U_\sigma C U_\sigma^{-1} = rac8{c_0}I+  rac{q^{-\sigma}JC-q^\sigma CJ} {q^{2\sigma}-q^{-2\sigma}} . \quad} 	ag{4} \] Its full Newton action, valid also at \(N=2\), is \[ U_\sigma C U_\sigma^{-1}e_j =q^{-2\sigma j}s_j^2e_{j-1} +d_{\sigma,j}e_j +q^{-2\sigma(j+1)}s_{j+1}^2e_{j+1}, \] \[ d_{\sigma,j} =4q^{-\sigma(2j+1)} -(q^{-\sigma}+q^{-3\sigma})q^{-4\sigma j}. 	ag{5} \] Thus (4) is an identity of the original nonsemisimple algebra's linear operators. It includes every physical first normal. ### Complete entry verification It suffices first to prove (5) for \(\sigma=1\). Write \(U=U_+\) and let \(D_+\) be the tridiagonal matrix in (5). The full triangular matrix from the exact unit-turn source is \[ U_{rj}=(-1)^j q^{-j(r+1)}  rac{S_j}{S_rS_{j-r}}\quad(0\le r\le j\le D), \qquad U_{rj}=0\quad(r>j). 	ag{6} \] We prove \(D_+U=UC\), including the ends of the matrix. For \(0\le r\le j<D\), the ratios used in that comparison are \[  rac{U_{r,j+1}}{U_{rj}} =-q^{-r-1} rac{s_{j+1}}{s_{j-r+1}},\qquad  rac{U_{r-1,j}}{U_{rj}} =q^j rac{s_r}{s_{j-r+1}},\qquad  rac{U_{r+1,j}}{U_{rj}} =q^{-j} rac{s_{j-r}}{s_{r+1}}. 	ag{7} \] The absent lower or upper ratios at \(r=0\) or \(r=j\) are interpreted by their displayed zero numerators. After clearing \(s_{j-r+1}\), the required identity is \[  egin{split} 0={}&(c_j-d_{+,r})s_{j-r+1} +q^{-r-1}s_{j+1}^3-q^{j-2r}s_r^3\ &-q^{-j-2r-2}s_{r+1}s_{j-r}s_{j-r+1}. \end{split} 	ag{8} \] Here is a direct Laurent verification. Substitute \(x=q^r,z=q^{j-r}\), and use \(s_\ell=(q^\ell-q^{-\ell})/i\). After multiplying (8) by \(i^3\), only powers \(z^3,z,z^{-1},z^{-3}\) remain. Their coefficients are, respectively, \[ 0,\qquad qd_{+,r}-4x^{-2}+(1+q^{-2})x^{-4}, \] \[ 4q^{-2}x^{-2}-q^{-1}d_{+,r} -(q^{-2}+q^{-4})x^{-4},\qquad 0. 	ag{9} \] Both middle coefficients vanish by (5). This verifies every entry in this range, rather than only the first off-diagonal. The entry \(r=j+1\) compares \(-s_{j+1}^2U_{j+1,j+1}\) with \(q^{-2j-2}s_{j+1}^2U_{jj}\); they agree directly by (6). Entries \(r>j+1\) are zero on both sides. For \(j=D,r>0\), the same cleared identity (8) applies with \(s_{j+1}=s_N=0\), while \(s_{N-r}
e0\). The only division excluded from that argument is \(r=0,j=D\). At this corner \(q^{-D}=-q\), \(s_D=s_1\), and \[  rac{U_{1D}}{U_{0D}}=q^{-D}. \] The right side divided by \(U_{0D}\) is therefore \[ d_{+,0}+q^{-D-2}s_1^2 =d_{+,0}-q^{-1}s_1^2=c_0, 	ag{10} \] as required. This proves \(D_+U=UC\) throughout the finite matrix. Since the diagonal entries of \(U\) are nonzero, (5) follows. To identify (4), compute \(q^{-1}JC-qCJ\) using (3). Its off-diagonal entries divided by \(q^2-q^{-2}\) are precisely those of (5). Its diagonal at \(j\) is \[ (q^{-1}-q)c_j^2+q^{-1}s_{j+1}^4-qs_j^4 =(q^2-q^{-2})d_{+,j}-8(q-q^{-1}). 	ag{11} \] Since \(q^2-q^{-2}=(q-q^{-1})c_0\), adding \(8I/c_0\) gives the claimed diagonal. Both denominators in (4) are nonzero for \(N\ge3\). Coefficient conjugation in the real Newton basis proves the negative-sign formula with exactly its displayed phases. For \(N=2\), formula (4) is undefined and is not used. In the ordered basis \((e_0,e_1)\), \[ U_\sigma= egin{pmatrix}1&i\sigma\0&1\end{pmatrix}, \qquad C= egin{pmatrix}0&0\-4&0\end{pmatrix}, \] \[ U_\sigma C U_\sigma^{-1} = egin{pmatrix}-4i\sigma&-4\-4&4i\sigma\end{pmatrix}. 	ag{12} \] This is also (5), with its zero end terms. The proof is complete. ### The cyclic identities, including the shortest level Put \(\mathsf X=C,\mathsf Y=J,\mathsf Z=D_+\), and \(\Delta=q^2-q^{-2}\). The three identities have a denominator-free form valid for every \(N\ge2\): \[  oxed{ egin{split} q\mathsf X\mathsf Y-q^{-1}\mathsf Y\mathsf X &=8(q-q^{-1})I-\Delta\mathsf Z,\ q\mathsf Y\mathsf Z-q^{-1}\mathsf Z\mathsf Y &=8(q-q^{-1})I-\Delta\mathsf X,\ q\mathsf Z\mathsf X-q^{-1}\mathsf X\mathsf Z &=8(q-q^{-1})I-\Delta\mathsf Y. \end{split}} 	ag{12a} \] For \(N\ge3\), the first is (4). Here is a full entry check of the second. In \(qJD_+-q^{-1}D_+J\), the shift \(+1\) coefficient is \(\Delta s_{j+1}^2\). The shift \(-2\) coefficient cancels exactly. The shift \(-1\) coefficient is \[ s_j^2\{\Delta q^{-4j}-qd_{+,j}+q^{-1}d_{+,j-1}\}=0. 	ag{12b} \] At \(j=0\) this is an absent term, so \(d_{+,-1}\) is not required. The diagonal coefficient is \[ (q-q^{-1})c_jd_{+,j} +q^{-2j-1}(s_j^4-s_{j+1}^4) =8(q-q^{-1})-\Delta c_j. 	ag{12c} \] Both equalities follow directly on substituting (5); for (12c), expand \(s_j^4=q^{4j}+q^{-4j} -4q^{2j}-4q^{-2j}+6\). Zero end factors \(s_0=s_N=0\) retain the same identities at the first and last columns. These are all possible bands, so the second relation follows. Since \(J=C^{\mathsf T}\) and \(D_+=D_+^{\mathsf T}\) in the Newton coordinates, transposition proves the third. At \(N=2\), the matrices in (12), together with \(J=C^{\mathsf T}\), give all three relations directly: \(\Delta=0\) and the scalar is \(16i\). Thus no division by \(c_0\) or \(\Delta\) is hidden at that level. Complex conjugation gives the corresponding signed presentation for \(D_-\). No classical curve or knot invariant is identified by these operator identities alone. ### The exact central relation The same operators satisfy the quantum cubic \[  oxed{ egin{split} &q\mathsf X\mathsf Y\mathsf Z +q^2\mathsf X^2+q^{-2}\mathsf Y^2+q^2\mathsf Z^2\ &\hspace{6mm}-8q\mathsf X-8q^{-1}\mathsf Y-8q\mathsf Z =(c_0^2-32)I . \end{split}} 	ag{12d} \] Here too \(N=2\) is included. For a full algebraic proof, denote the left side by \(\Omega\), and put \(k=8(q-q^{-1})\). Successive use of (12a), without division, gives \[  egin{split} q[\mathsf X\mathsf Y\mathsf Z,\mathsf X] &=k\mathsf X(\mathsf Y-\mathsf Z) +\Delta\mathsf X(\mathsf Z^2-\mathsf Y^2),\ q^{-2}[\mathsf Y^2,\mathsf X]+q^2[\mathsf Z^2,\mathsf X] &=\Delta\mathsf X(\mathsf Y^2-\mathsf Z^2) +kc_0(\mathsf Z-\mathsf Y),\ [-8q^{-1}\mathsf Y-8q\mathsf Z,\mathsf X] &=k\mathsf X(\mathsf Z-\mathsf Y) +8\Delta(\mathsf Y-\mathsf Z). \end{split} 	ag{12e} \] Since \(kc_0=8\Delta\), these identities prove \([\Omega,\mathsf X]=0\). They can be checked by moving each rightmost \(\mathsf X\) left using respectively the third and first equations of (12a); all terms are displayed in (12e), including the scalar terms. Likewise, \[ q(\mathsf Y\mathsf Z\mathsf X-\mathsf X\mathsf Y\mathsf Z) =k(\mathsf Y-\mathsf Z) +\Delta(\mathsf Z^2-\mathsf Y^2). 	ag{12f} \] Consequently the expression defining \(\Omega\) is unchanged under the cyclic substitution \((\mathsf X,\mathsf Y,\mathsf Z)\mapsto (\mathsf Y,\mathsf Z,\mathsf X)\). Thus it commutes with \(\mathsf Y\) and \(\mathsf Z\) as well. The eigenspace \(\ker(J-c_0)\) is \(\mathbb C e_0\). Indeed, the only diagonal occurrences of \(c_0\) in (3) are at \(j=0,D\). Every intermediate diagonal differs from \(c_0\), and all the upper links \(-s_j^2\), \(1\le j\le D\), are nonzero. Solving the triangular equations from the last row through the first forces every coefficient except that of \(e_0\) to vanish; this also applies directly when \(N=2\). Since \(\Omega\) commutes with \(J\), it sends \(e_0\) to a scalar multiple of \(e_0\). The vector \(e_0\) is cyclic for \(C\), because all its successive raising links in (3) are nonzero. Commutation with \(C\) now makes \(\Omega\) scalar on the whole algebra. To evaluate the scalar, put \(h=q-q^{-1}\) and \(d_0=3q^{-1}-q^{-3}\). The coefficient of \(e_0\) in \(\Omega e_0\) is \[ q c_0^2d_0+q^2d_0^2-8qd_0 +(q^2+q^{-2})c_0^2-8c_0^2-h^4=c_0^2-32. 	ag{12g} \] For example, the off-diagonal contributions from \(q\mathsf X\mathsf Y\mathsf Z+q^2\mathsf Z^2\) combine to \((-q^{-1}c_0+q^{-2})s_1^4=-h^4\); the remaining terms in (12g) are diagonal. Substitution of \(c_0=q+q^{-1}\) and \(d_0\) proves the last equality. This completes the all-level proof of (12d). ## 2. Fixed-turn bandwidth and operator presentation For \(n\in\mathbb Z\), use the original repeated-turn operators \[ V_n=\kappa^nTR^{-n}T,\qquad V_nV_\ell=V_{n+\ell},\qquad D_n=V_nCV_{-n}. 	ag{13} \] Crossing multiplication commutes with \(C\), so \(V_nJ=JV_n\). For \(N\ge3\), conjugating (4) therefore gives exactly \[ D_{n+\sigma} = rac8{c_0}I+  rac{q^{-\sigma}JD_n-q^\sigma D_nJ} {q^{2\sigma}-q^{-2\sigma}}, \qquad \sigma=\pm1. 	ag{14} \] Starting at \(D_0=C\), it follows that the Newton shifts in \(D_n\) are contained in \[ -|n|\le r-j\le1. 	ag{15} \] Indeed \(J\) has shifts \(-1,0\), so each commutator step adds at most one lower shift and no new upper shift. This is a fixed number of bands when \(n\) is fixed. For \(N=2\), direct multiplication gives the separate formula \[ V_n= egin{pmatrix}1&in\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad D_n= egin{pmatrix}-4in&-4n^2\-4&4in\end{pmatrix}. 	ag{16} \] There is a quantitative bound for this conjugated multiplication, although no corresponding bound is asserted for \(V_n\). Equip ordinary canonical polynomials with their real norm on \([-2,2]\), and operators with the induced norm. The repeated-turn source proves \(\|J\|\le34N^3\). Also \(\|C\|\le6\): if \(p\) has degree at most \(D\), its leading coefficient has modulus at most \(\|p\|_{\mathbb R}\) by its Chebyshev expansion, and \(\operatorname{can}(Zp)=Zp-[Z^D]p\,P_N\). Use \(\|P_N\|_{\mathbb R}\le4\). For \(N\ge3\), \(c_0\ge1\) and \(|q^2-q^{-2}|^{-1}\le N/4\). Equation (14) thus proves, for every fixed integer \(n\), \[ \|D_n\|\le C_nN^{4|n|}. 	ag{17} \] The finitely sized case (16) is absorbed in \(C_n\). This estimate does not bound the condition number of \(V_n\). There is also a divisor-free second-order recurrence: \[  oxed{ egin{split} qD_{n+2}+q^{-1}D_n+D_{n+1}J&=8I,\ q^{-1}D_{n+2}+qD_n+JD_{n+1}&=8I , \end{split}\qquad n\in\mathbb Z.} 	ag{17a} \] For \(N\ge3\), insert the second cyclic relation (12a) into (14) at \(n=1,\sigma=1\). It gives \[ D_2=8q^{-1}I-q^{-2}C-q^{-1}D_1J. 	ag{17b} \] The other ordering follows from the same cyclic relation. Conjugate both identities by \(V_n\), using \(V_nJ=JV_n\), to obtain (17a). At \(N=2\), substitution of (16) verifies both identities directly, for every integer \(n\). Thus (17a) has no exceptional denominator even at that level. A completely finite Chebyshev formula follows. Let \(U_\ell\) denote the ordinary Chebyshev polynomial of the second kind, with \(U_{-1}=0,U_0=1\), only in the following display. For \(m\ge1\), \[  egin{split} D_m={}&q^{1-m}D_1U_{m-1}(-J/2) -q^{-m}C U_{m-2}(-J/2)\ &+8q^{-m}\sum_{\ell=0}^{m-2} q^{\ell+1}U_{m-2-\ell}(-J/2). \end{split} 	ag{17c} \] The sum is empty at \(m=1\). Multiply the first equation in (17a) by \(q^{n+1}\) and set \(E_n=q^nD_n\); then \(E_{n+2}=-E_{n+1}J-E_n+8q^{n+1}I\). The displayed finite expression solves this recurrence with \(E_0=C,E_1=qD_1\), as direct substitution shows. All polynomials in \(J\) are on the indicated right side; no commutation with \(C\) or \(D_1\) was assumed. Negative \(m\) follow by coefficient conjugation. In particular every noncommutative polynomial operator relation has the exact transport rule \[ \mathscr P(C,J)f=g \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \mathscr P(D_n,J)V_nf=V_ng. 	ag{18} \] The order of the factors in \(\mathscr P\) is unchanged. If an identity originally has scalar rational coefficients, its scalar denominators must first be retained or cleared on the stated parameter domain; (18) does not authorize an inverse of a vanishing operator coefficient. Moreover \(V_n1=1\), since \(Te_0=e_D\), \(R^{-n}e_D=\kappa^{-n}e_D\), and \(Te_D=1\). For any fixed number of endpoint kernels this gives \[  oxed{\quad V_n\left(\prod_{i=1}^r K_N(w_i,C)\,1ight) =\left(\prod_{i=1}^r K_N(w_i,D_n)ight)1 . \quad} 	ag{19} \] The products on both sides are the exact canonical products. Their factors on the right commute because all are polynomials in the same \(D_n\). Formula (19) is a finite quantum-operator presentation; its degree-\(D\) kernel polynomials cannot be estimated by (17) termwise without potentially exponential cost. ## 3. The elementary commuting principal-symbol relation This section is a formal coefficient calculation, not an asymptotic estimate. For an interior Newton scale \(j/N=x\), write \(\lambda=e^{2\pi ix}\), and let \(	au\) denote the formal index-raising variable. Set \[ c=\lambda+\lambda^{-1},\qquad a=2-c. \] Taking the leading coefficients of (3),(5) as \(N\) increases, with shift variables commuting at this formal leading order, gives the Laurent symbols \[  egin{split} X&=c-a	au,\ Y&=c-a	au^{-1},\ Z&=4\lambda^{-1}-2\lambda^{-2} +\lambda^{-1}a(	au+	au^{-1}). \end{split} 	ag{19a} \] They satisfy the exact Laurent-polynomial identity \[  oxed{\quad X^2+Y^2+Z^2+XYZ-8(X+Y+Z)+28=0. \quad} 	ag{19b} \] Indeed, put \(S=X+Y-4\). Direct expansion of (19a) gives \[ XY-4=(\lambda+\lambda^{-1})S,\qquad Z-2=-S/\lambda. 	ag{19c} \] Consequently \(S^2+(Z-2)^2+(XY-4)(Z-2)=0\); expansion is (19b). The proof does not divide by \(S\), \(a\), or any of the differences in (19b), so it retains their degenerate values. The variables \(\lambda,	au\) are nonzero formal Laurent variables throughout. No knot peripheral polynomial, integration cycle, or source-growth conclusion is identified by this cubic. The scalar relation itself is already recorded, in equivalent form, in research_mixed_next_outer_paired_newton_characteristics.md §5 (28) and in papers/nonparabolic-tree-geometry/character.tex (C10) at boundary trace \(2\). Neither is needed for the self-contained calculation above. The operator lift (12d) and its exact turn and branching transport are the point here. ## 4. Exact ordinary branching and its mixed forcing We next make explicit what the one-factor forced equation misses at an ordinary branching vertex. Let \(r\ge1\), let \(w_1,\ldots,w_r\) be arbitrary complex numbers, and put \[ k_i(Z)=K_N(w_i,Z),\qquad P_r=\operatorname{can}\prod_{i=1}^r k_i,\qquad \lambda_r=\sum_{i=1}^r w_i-(r-1)c_0. 	ag{20} \] For an index variable \(x\), write \[ c(x)=2\cos((2x+1)\pi/N),\quad a(x)= rac{s_{x+1}^4}{s_{2x+1}s_{2x+2}},\quad b(x)= rac{s_x^4}{s_{2x}s_{2x+1}}, \] \[ k_i^0(x)=k_i(c(x)),\quad \Delta_\pm k_i(x)=k_i(c(x\pm1))-k_i(c(x)). 	ag{21} \] All apparent poles below are interpreted in the combined expression. The original difference operator is \[ \mathcal L f(c(x)) =c_0f(c(x))-a(x)\Delta_+f(x)-b(x)\Delta_-f(x). 	ag{22} \] Its action on canonical polynomials is \(J\). It also acts on ordinary polynomials of higher degree. Indeed the cosine-difference calculation in the repeated-turn source makes (22) polynomial; the same calculation applies to every finite cosine sum. Furthermore \[ P_N(c(x+1))=P_N(c(x))=P_N(c(x-1)) \] implies \(\mathcal L(P_Nh)=P_N\mathcal Lh\). Thus this ordinary action descends to the same full quotient. Define the mixed expression \[  egin{split} \mathcal M_r(x)={}& a(x)\sum_{\substack{I\subset\{1,\ldots,r\}\|I|\ge2}} \prod_{i\in I}\Delta_+k_i(x) \prod_{i
otin I}k_i^0(x)\ &+b(x)\sum_{\substack{I\subset\{1,\ldots,r\}\|I|\ge2}} \prod_{i\in I}\Delta_-k_i(x) \prod_{i
otin I}k_i^0(x). \end{split} 	ag{23} \] Although its separate displayed terms use the index chart, their sum is an ordinary polynomial in \(c(x)\). To see this without any pole assumption, expand the finite product differences in (22) and use the exact one-factor equations \[ (w_i-\mathcal L)k_i= rac{\eta P_N(w_i)}{N^2}e_D. 	ag{24} \] The result is the ordinary polynomial identity \[ (\lambda_r-\mathcal L)\prod_i k_i = rac{\eta e_D}{N^2} \sum_iP_N(w_i)\prod_{\ell
e i}k_\ell +\mathcal M_r. 	ag{25} \] It also proves the asserted removability of the paired expression in (23). Let \(M_r\) denote its canonical representative. The endpoint source simplifies exactly after canonical reduction: \[ e_Dk_i=e_D\quad\hbox{in }\mathcal A_N. 	ag{26} \] Indeed \(k_i(c_0)=1\), while \((Z-c_0)e_D=\eta P_N/N^2\). This argument preserves the first normal, rather than merely checking values at distinct roots. Equations (25)--(26) give \[  oxed{\quad (\lambda_r-J)P_r = rac{\eta}{N^2}\left(\sum_iP_N(w_i)ight)e_D+M_r. \quad} 	ag{27} \] For \(r=1\), \(M_1=0\), recovering the original equation. For \(r=2\), the extra term is the canonical polynomial represented by \(a\,\Delta_+k_1\Delta_+k_2+b\,\Delta_-k_1\Delta_-k_2\). Since \(V_nJ=JV_n\) and \(V_ne_D=\kappa^nT(R^{-n})\), the exact turned branching source is \[  oxed{\quad (\lambda_r-J)V_nP_r = rac{\eta\kappa^n}{N^2} \left(\sum_iP_N(w_i)ight)T(R^{-n})+V_nM_r . \quad} 	ag{28} \] Every shared endpoint parameter and coefficient remains inside this identity. It can be differentiated in those ordinary parameters or multiplied by the remaining original spectator before its trace is taken. No quotient is imposed on a free outside variable. For fixed \(r\), \(w_i=2\cosh(\alpha_i/N)\), and bounded complex \(\alpha_i\), one has \(\lambda_r-2=O(N^{-2})\). Thus the homogeneous part remains at the same microscopic spectral scale as the one-factor equation. However (28) retains \(V_nM_r\), not \(M_r\) before turning. A bound for the latter does not bound the former. The present note supplies neither a finite growing-channel estimate nor a comparison of this mixed source with the filled geometric action. In particular it does not iterate the one-factor polynomial bound or discard the terminal action already present in \(T(R^{-n})\). ## 5. An unconditional norm estimate retaining the combined forcing There is a quantitative way to state the remaining task without separating terms that may cancel. Fix \(\Lambda<\infty\). For every canonical polynomial \(F\) and every \(|\lambda-c_0|\le\Lambda/N^2\), put \(g=(\lambda-J)F\). There are constants \(C_\Lambda,p_\Lambda\) such that \[  egin{split} &\|g\|_{\mathbb R}+|F(c_0)|+|F'(c_0)| \le C_\Lambda N^3\|F\|_{\mathbb R},\ &\|F\|_{\mathbb R} \le C_\Lambda N^{p_\Lambda} \{\|g\|_{\mathbb R}+|F(c_0)|+|F'(c_0)|\}. \end{split} 	ag{29} \] Here and below the norm is on the whole ordinary interval \([-2,2]\). The first inequality follows from the \(J\) bound and ordinary Markov's inequality. For completeness, the second is the original forced row argument with arbitrary polynomial forcing. At the regular rows \(0\le j<\lfloor(N-1)/2floor\), put \(h_j=F(c_j)\), \(q_j=b(j)/a(j)\), and \(d_j=(c_0-\lambda)/a(j)\). Then exactly \[ h_{j+1}=(1+q_j+d_j)h_j-q_jh_{j-1} +g(c_j)/a(j). 	ag{30} \] The direct single-turn proof gives \(0\le q_j<1\), \(a(j)\ge16(j+1)^2/(\pi^2N^2)\). Thus the balanced state \((h_j,(j+1)(h_j-h_{j-1}))\) has forward step norm at most \(1+B_\Lambda/(j+1)\). All its forward products are polynomial in \(N\); its forcing is bounded by a polynomial times \(\|g\|_{\mathbb R}\). The first row starts from the displayed anchor \(F(c_0)\). Differentiate the ordinary index identity (30). The state of \(y_j=c'(j)F'(c_j)\) has the same homogeneous matrices, with additional forcing from coefficient derivatives and from \(g'(c_j)c'(j)\). The coefficient derivatives have polynomial bounds, and Markov bounds \(g'\) by \(CN^2\|g\|_{\mathbb R}\). Its initial data are controlled by \(F(c_0),F'(c_0)\); the removable coefficient has \(b(0)=b'(0)=0\). The same forward estimate reaches every double-root normal without using a singular next row. Division by \(|c'(j)|\ge8\pi/N^2\) costs only a polynomial. The odd simple value is already in the value propagation. At \(N=2\) the two initial anchors are the complete data. Finally the exact value/first-normal Fourier reconstruction in the single-turn source has polynomial conditioning on both parities. This proves (29) for every canonical \(F\), with no zero-free assumption and no inverse fundamental matrix. Here are the actual anchors for the branching source. Write \[ Q_N(Z)=\left.\partial_wK_N(w,Z)ight|_{w=c_0}, \qquad G_n=T(R^{-n}). \] Frobenius self-adjointness of \(T\) and the original kernel give \[  egin{split} \mathcal A_0(n,P)&:=(V_nP)(c_0) =\kappa^n\phi_N(G_nP),\ \mathcal A_1(n,P)&:=(V_nP)'(c_0) =\kappa^n\phi_N\!\left[ T(R^{-n}Q_N)Pight]. \end{split} 	ag{31} \] Indeed \((Tf)(c_0)=\phi_N(f)\) and \((Tf)'(c_0)=\phi_N(Q_Nf)\); transfer the remaining \(T\) across the original pairing. Formula (31) keeps every product and normal before closing. For bounded microscopic parameters in (20), apply (29) with \(F=V_nP_r\), \(\lambda=\lambda_r\), and the *combined* source \[ \mathcal G_{n,r} = rac{\eta\kappa^n}{N^2} \left(\sum_iP_N(w_i)ight)G_n+V_nM_r. 	ag{32} \] It follows unconditionally that \[  oxed{\quad \|V_nP_r\|_{\mathbb R} \ \asymp_{m poly(N)}\ \|\mathcal G_{n,r}\|_{\mathbb R} +|\mathcal A_0(n,P_r)|+|\mathcal A_1(n,P_r)|. \quad} 	ag{33} \] The notation means the two explicit polynomial inequalities of (29), with constants depending on the fixed microscopic parameter bound and the fixed number of factors. No triangle inequality separates the two terms in (32). For arbitrary \(n\), the normal anchor in (31) is \(T(R^{-n}Q_N)\); it is not \(V_nQ_N\). In particular its bound is not inferred by differentiating the repeated-turn kernel at the physical endpoint. Equation (33) locates the required source estimate in the actual combined forcing and its actual two anchors. It does not supply a filled-action bound for those quantities. The extra normal channel has a precise source interpretation. Differentiating (24) at the double endpoint \(w=c_0\) gives \[ (J-c_0)Q_N=1, 	ag{34} \] because \(K_N(c_0,Z)=1\) and \(P_N'(c_0)=0\). Write \(H_n=T(R^{-n}Q_N)\). From (13), \[ D_n=TR^{-n}JR^nT. \] Therefore \[ (D_n-c_0)G_n=0,\qquad (D_n-c_0)H_n=G_n. 	ag{35} \] The first uses \((J-c_0)1=0\), and the second is (34) with all original factors retained. In particular \[ \|H_n\|_{\mathbb R} \ge rac{\|G_n\|_{\mathbb R}}{\|D_n\|+|c_0|}. 	ag{36} \] This is a polynomial-loss lower comparison for fixed \(n\), by (17), not an upper comparison. The original normal anchor involves this actual Jordan companion; it cannot be discarded as a zero endpoint term. ## 6. Direct-source readbacks All three complete direct sources were read at their unchanged pins, with the directly used implications and hashes checked: * [Exact full unit-turn identities](research_full_endpoint_unit_turn_identities.md), SHA256 e2f69aaff28080b9dd9e11365ce18d68a9d738667917204714556681c50789e8: original full triangular matrix, signed crossing convention, endpoint reproducer, and canonical representative. * [Repeated turns and the original difference operator](research_repeated_endpoint_unit_turn_action_growth.md), SHA256 92a5b15719f594668f5514cfd2decfa9a9350a784321127323153fe353084a9a: repeated-turn composition, original difference formula and kernel forcing, polynomial \(J\) norm, and retained terminal action. * [Full single-endpoint propagation](research_full_endpoint_unit_turn_polynomial_bound.md), SHA256 329ee59c992c359c42775f564f540ffeee7f142bf51b5132913bf4cf2a859d35: regular-row coefficient bounds, differentiated forward propagation, and polynomial full-Hermite reconstruction at both parities. The all-entry conjugation and mixed branching identities are proved above. Only written mathematics, source-text reads and hashes were used. No mathematical program, numerical experiment, test or build was run. Adopted notes and public manuscripts are unchanged.

title: Coercivity of the network phase with its wire variables retained
text:
# Coercivity of the network phase with its wire variables retained Research proof, 3 November 2026. Frozen manuscripts are unchanged. The complete-end contribution used in the earlier [mixed-phase calculation](research_mixed_wire_phase_concavity.md) is absent at a general interior vertex. The appropriate object is therefore the Hessian of each original incidence, followed by the Hessian of their actual sum. This gives an arbitrary-graph concavity theorem on an explicit contour domain. Outside that domain there is an exact network test, and positive geometry still gives an adapted local contour. None of these phase statements chooses a coefficient in the original finite quantum cycle. ## 1. The original incidence matrix Let \(G\) be a finite graph. Every edge \(e\) has one retained wire variable \(x_e\). A selected vertex \(v\) has an angular variable \(t_v\), a real filling power \(n_v\), and the original unit charge. An outside vertex has a fixed angle \(u_v\). Count an edge at each of its endpoints. Throughout this note an edge has the same-index kernel \[ K_T(z,w)=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}e_j(z)e_j(w). \] This is the kernel on the original circle-tree paths. A general Conway network may also have \(K_I(z,w)=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}e_j(z)e_{N-1-j}(w)\); its reversed wire index has a different phase. The theorems below do not silently replace those edges by \(K_T\). Such a replacement would need a separate exact source reduction. For the specified same-index graph, the phase is \[ \Phi=\sum_{(e,v)}b(x_e,t_v) +\sum_{v\ {m selected}} \left( rac{in_vt_v^2}{4\pi}-it_vight), 	ag{1} \] where \(t_v=u_v\) at outside vertices, and \[ b(x,t)=-J(1/2-x+t/(2\pi)) -J(1/2-x-t/(2\pi))-2J(x),\qquad J'(z)=\Log(2\sin\pi z). 	ag{2} \] Fix its branches on a regular factorial chart. Put \[ s_v= rac12- rac{t_v}{2\pi}=b_v+iS_v,\qquad x_e=a_e+iY_e. 	ag{3} \] The scalar \(b_v\) is a real coordinate; \(b(x,t)\) always denotes the phase (2). Reflection of \(J\) gives \[ b(x,t)=J(s+x)-J(s-x)-2J(x). 	ag{4} \] For one incidence define \[ u=\Re\cot\pi(s+x),\qquad v=\Re\cot\pi(s-x),\qquad w=\Re\cot\pi x. 	ag{5} \] The negative Hessian of its real part in the real coordinates \((a,b)\), with heights fixed, is exactly \[ H_{m inc}=\pi  egin{pmatrix} v+2w-u&-v-u\ -v-u&v-u \end{pmatrix}. 	ag{6} \] In particular there is no complete-end term in its lower diagonal. The real part of each filling term in (1) is affine in \(b_v\) at fixed \(S_v\). It contributes nothing to this Hessian, for either sign of the real number \(n_v\). ## 2. A concavity domain for every incidence Define \[ \alpha(Y)= rac1{2\pi}\arccos(\operatorname{sech}(2\pi Y)) \quad(Y\ge0). 	ag{7} \] **Theorem 1.** Suppose \[ Y,S\ge0,\qquad \alpha(Y)<a<b\le rac12,\qquad b\ge rac14. 	ag{8} \] Then (6) is positive definite. There is no required ordering between \(Y\) and \(S\). **Proof.** Since \(0<a<b\le1/2\), the real parts of the three factorial arguments \(x,s-x,1-s-x\) lie in \((0,1)\), and \(v,w>0\). If \(a+b\ge1/2\), then \(u\le0\), and \[ \pi^{-1}H_{m inc} =v egin{pmatrix}1&-1\-1&1\end{pmatrix} +(-u) egin{pmatrix}1&1\1&1\end{pmatrix} +2w egin{pmatrix}1&0\0&0\end{pmatrix}>0. 	ag{9} \] It remains to consider \(a+b<1/2\), so \(u>0\). Here \(0<a<1/4\). Set \[ R=2\pi a,\quad T=2\pi b,\quad H=2\pi Y,\quad K=2\pi S. 	ag{10} \] Thus \(0<R<\pi/2\), \(\pi/2\le T<\pi-R\), and \(\cos R\cosh H<1\), by (7)--(8). The identity \[  rac1{\Re\cot\pi(r+ih)} = rac{\cosh(2\pi h)-\cos(2\pi r)} {\sin(2\pi r)} 	ag{11} \] applies to all three positive real parts in (5). Expanding the addition formulas gives \[  rac1u- rac1v- rac2w = rac{2\mathcal N} {\sin R\,\sin(T-R)\,\sin(T+R)}, 	ag{12} \] where \[  egin{split} \mathcal N={}& \cosh H(\sin^2R-\sin^2T)+\cos R\sin^2T\ &-\cos T\cosh K\cosh H\sin^2R +\sin R\sin T\cos R\sinh K\sinh H. \end{split} 	ag{13} \] The denominator in (12) is positive. The last two terms in (13) are nonnegative, because \(\cos T\le0\). Also \(\sin^2T>\sin^2R\), so \(\cosh H<1/\cos R\) gives \[ \cosh H(\sin^2R-\sin^2T)+\cos R\sin^2T > rac{\sin^2R\cos^2T}{\cos R}\ge0. 	ag{14} \] Consequently (12) is strictly positive. This implies \(v>u\) and \[ \det(\pi^{-1}H_{m inc}) =2wv\left(1- rac uv- rac{2u}wight)>0. 	ag{15} \] Both the lower diagonal and determinant are positive, proving the claim. The computation used \(\sinh H,\sinh K\ge0\), but never \(H\le K\) or \(K\le H\). \(\square\) Conjugation gives the same theorem when all heights in the incidence are nonpositive. A mixture of height signs is not covered by (8); the exact matrix (6) remains valid. There is also a larger simple subregion: the proof of (9) only requires \(0<a<b\le1/2\) and \(a+b\ge1/2\). On that subregion the heights can have arbitrary real values, and the condition \(\alpha(Y)<a\) is unnecessary. For a quantitative bound put \[ T_{m inc}=2(v+w-u),\qquad \Delta_{m inc}=2w(v-u)-4uv,\qquad m_{m inc}=\Delta_{m inc}/T_{m inc}>0. 	ag{16} \] The smaller eigenvalue of (6) is at least \(\pi m_{m inc}\), since the larger eigenvalue of \(\pi^{-1}H_{m inc}\) is at most its trace. ## 3. Assembly on a finite graph Fix \(Y_e,S_v\ge0\). Require (8) at each incidence, interpreting the coordinates of an outside vertex as fixed. In particular a complete outside vertex has \(b_v=1/2,S_v=0\) and is allowed. The common domain in the variable real coordinates is convex: its conditions are the linear inequalities \[ \alpha(Y_e)<a_e<b_v,\qquad  rac14\le b_v\le rac12. 	ag{17} \] We assume each variable occurs in at least one incidence. Constant parts of the graph may simply be omitted. **Theorem 2.** On (17), the real part of (1) is strictly concave, for arbitrary real powers \(n_v\) and any finite graph. On a compact convex subset \(Q\), let \[ m_Q=\min_{(e,v)}\inf_Qm_{e,v}>0. 	ag{18} \] If a holomorphic critical point \(z_*\) lies on this contour, then \[ \Re\Phi(z)\le\Re\Phi(z_*)- rac{\pi m_Q}{2} \left(\sum_e(a_e-a_{e,*})^2 +\sum_{v\ {m selected}}(b_v-b_{v,*})^2ight) 	ag{19} \] for \(z\in Q\). **Proof.** Extend each incidence matrix by zero in all other coordinates and sum. Its quadratic form is at least \(\pi m_Q[(\delta a_e)^2+(\delta b_v)^2]\); a fixed outside coordinate has \(\delta b_v=0\). Every variable is counted at least once, so the full negative Hessian dominates \(\pi m_Q I\). The filling terms have zero real Hessian. Integrating along the segment from the critical point gives (19). \(\square\) This is a phase theorem for graphs of arbitrary size. It does not assert that a geometric point for every filling power lies in (17). For example, the homogeneous positive degree-two power-three point has \(\Re t>\pi/2\), hence \(b<1/4\). Nor does a statement valid for every real \(n_v\) on this fixed contour say that the selected geometry of mixed signs has these same heights. ## 4. The exact network test outside this chamber The full matrix is also explicit without (8). At a regular point write, for every incidence, \[ A_{e,v}=v_{e,v}+2w_e-u_{e,v},\quad B_{e,v}=v_{e,v}-u_{e,v},\quad C_{e,v}=v_{e,v}+u_{e,v}. 	ag{20} \] Let \(A_e\) be the sum of \(A_{e,v}\) over both endpoints, including fixed endpoints, and let \(B_v=\sum_{e
i v}B_{e,v}\) for selected vertices. Form the edge-by-selected-vertex matrix \(C\) from \(C_{e,v}\), with zero entries for nonincidences. If an edge meets the same vertex twice, add its two entries. Then the full negative real Hessian is \[ H_G=\pi  egin{pmatrix} \operatorname{diag}(A_e)&-C\ -C^{\mathsf T}&\operatorname{diag}(B_v) \end{pmatrix}. 	ag{21} \] **Proposition 3.** The matrix (21) is positive definite if and only if \[ A_e>0\quad\hbox{for every edge},\qquad \operatorname{diag}(B_v) -C^{\mathsf T}\operatorname{diag}(A_e^{-1})C>0. 	ag{22} \] These are conditions on the real Hessian, not the holomorphic Schur complement obtained by eliminating stationary wires. **Proof.** Complete the square in the real wire variables. \(\square\) For example, a sufficient condition that avoids computing the eigenvalues of (21) is the existence of positive weights \(p_e,q_v\) such that \[  egin{split} A_e-\sum_v|C_{e,v}|q_v/p_e&>0,\ B_v-\sum_e|C_{e,v}|p_e/q_v&>0. \end{split} 	ag{23} \] The minimum of these margins, times \(\pi\), is a coercivity constant. Indeed apply \(2|XY|\le(q_v/p_e)X^2+(p_e/q_v)Y^2\) to each cross term. Equations (22)--(23) permit compensation between incidences; they do not require every individual incidence matrix to be positive. Thus a further general extension has a precise target: prove (22), or construct weights in (23), on a specified connected family of original contour domains. Positive geometry after wire elimination alone does not prove (22). There is an explicit regular positive edge where (22) fails. Take the exact angles \[ t= rac{21}{10}- rac{3i}{4},\qquad r= rac34- rac{3i}{20}. 	ag{24} \] At its stationary wire, all original factorial arguments have real parts in \((0,1)\), and all eight original tetrahedra have positive imaginary parts. Nevertheless the \(s_t,s_t\) entry of the unsummed negative real Hessian is less than \(-59/100\). The [exact-interval checker](../experiments/check_positive_edge_horizontal_hessian_obstruction.py) and [saved bounds](../repro/results/research-positive-edge-horizontal-hessian-obstruction.json) verify these strict inequalities, the original logarithmic stationary equation, and positivity of the reduced edge Hessian. This is a counterexample to an implication from positive edge geometry to fixed-horizontal concavity. It is not asserted to satisfy any integer unit-filling equation. ## 5. What positive geometry does imply locally There is a different local statement at every regular positive geometric configuration. For an edge with angles \(t,r\), put \[ a=	an(t/2),\qquad c=	an(r/2),\qquad q^2=1+a^2+c^2. 	ag{25} \] The original positive branch has \(\Re q>\sqrt{(\Re a)^2+(\Re c)^2}\), by the [positive-edge theorem](research_positive_edge_global_monotonicity.md). The stationary equation for \(F_e(x;t,r)=b(x,t)+b(x,r)\) gives \[ \cot(\pi x_e^*)=q. 	ag{26} \] To verify it, put \(z=\sin^2\pi x\). Exponentiating the stationary equation gives \[  rac{(\cos^2(t/2)-z)(\cos^2(r/2)-z)}{z^2}=1, \quad z= rac{\cos^2(t/2)\cos^2(r/2)} {\cos^2(t/2)+\cos^2(r/2)} = rac1{1+q^2}. 	ag{27} \] More explicitly, choose \(x_e^*=\pi^{-1}\arctan(1/q)\), continued from \(q=1\). The right-half-plane condition on \(q\) fixes this holomorphic branch. The wire factorial sines do not vanish on the regular positive component: their vanishing would require \(q=\pm a\) or \(q=\pm c\), excluded by the strict positive-edge inequality. Thus the exponentiated gradient equal to one in (27) has a continuous logarithmic lift, which remains zero from completeness. The same continuation fixes the critical value as \(\psi(t,r)\). Indeed its \(t\)-derivative is \[ - rac1{2\pi}\Log rac{\sin\pi(s_t+x_e^*)} {\sin\pi(s_t-x_e^*)} =- rac1{2\pi}\Log rac{q+a}{q-a} =\psi_t(t,r), \] with the original logarithms continued from zero; the other derivative is identical with the endpoints exchanged. The constants agree at completeness. These are identities of the continued holomorphic phase, not assertions that one asymptotic branch dominates the finite factorial source. Direct differentiation at the stationary wire gives \[ H_e=-F_{e,xx}(x_e^*;t,r) = rac{2\pi q(1+q^2)^2}{(1+a^2)(1+c^2)}
e0. 	ag{28} \] The nonvanishing follows from \(\Re q>0\) and regularity of the angle coordinates. Its real part need not be assumed positive. At a fixed positive point, the holomorphic Morse construction with parameters supplies a local coordinate \(\xi_e\), with \(\partial_x\xi_e=\sqrt{H_e}\) at the stationary point, such that \[ F_e(x;t,r)=\psi(t,r)- rac{\xi_e^2}{2}. 	ag{29} \] For clarity, this requires no choice of a new phase: divide \(2\{\psi(t,r)-F_e(x;t,r)\}\) by \((x-x_e^*(t,r))^2\). The quotient extends holomorphically and equals \(H_e
e0\) at the center. Choose its local square root and multiply it by \(x-x_e^*(t,r)\). The inverse-function theorem gives (29). The critical value uses the original complete-branch normalization of \(\psi\). **Proposition 4.** At any regular positive geometric critical point of a finite graph, there is a local contour retaining every wire on which the real phase has a strictly negative Hessian. The contour keeps the imaginary angular coordinates fixed and takes all the coordinates \(\xi_e\) in (29) real. **Proof.** Every wire has its own coordinate (29), so on this contour the phase is exactly \[ \sum_{e=vw}\psi(t_v,t_w) +\sum_{v\ {m selected}} \left( rac{in_vt_v^2}{4\pi}-it_vight) - rac12\sum_e\xi_e^2. 	ag{30} \] The positive-edge theorem gives \(\Re[-\psi''(t_v,t_w)]>0\) at each edge. Restrict fixed outside angles and sum these matrices over the graph. Every selected variable is incident to an edge, so the reduced negative real angular Hessian is positive definite. Filling terms again have zero real Hessian on the fixed-height angular contour. The wire block in (30) is the identity. Positivity persists on a sufficiently small neighborhood, giving a quadratic real-part gap. \(\square\) The coordinate changes in (29) have nonzero holomorphic Jacobians. Accordingly a nonzero original analytic amplitude remains nonzero under this local change of variables. This does not establish that the original finite integration cycle has a nonzero coefficient on this contour, nor that its other pieces are smaller. The distinction between (22) and (30) matters. The former tests a fixed horizontal contour for the unsummed phase. The latter changes the wire directions with the angular variables. A complex holomorphic Schur complement does not imply the real-matrix inequality (22). The adapted contour proves local coercivity without making that invalid inference. ## 6. A common central domain for positive paths of power at least seven The pair bootstrap extends to paths, but each interior vertex can have two returns with positive imaginary part. Keeping both of them gives the following uniform bounds. This section concerns the positive charge family already proved for paths with a stipulated complete outside endpoint. It does not extend that existence theorem to an all-selected path or a general graph. **Theorem 5 (path geometry).** Take the family in the [positive fractional-charge theorem](research_positive_path_fractional_charge_cube.md), with original degrees at most two, integer powers \(n_v\ge7\), and \(0\le\chi_v\le1\). At an active vertex write \(t_v=a_v-iH_v\). Then \[ 0<a_v< rac{2\pi\chi_v}{n_v-7/20} \le rac{40\pi}{133}< rac{19}{20}, \qquad 0<H_v< rac3{10}. 	ag{31} \] At every edge with at least one active endpoint the selected wire \(x_e=\xi_e+iY_e\) satisfies \[  rac15<\xi_e< rac14,\qquad 0<2\pi Y_e< rac14 . 	ag{32} \] An edge with two complete endpoints has \(x_e=1/4\). All constants are independent of the path length and of the individual powers in this range. *Proof.* The existing [phase maximum principle](research_geometric_phase_maximum_principle.md#3-a-local-angle-bound-in-terms-of-the-charge) gives \(a_v<40\pi\chi_v/(17n_v)<\pi/2\). The [cosine modulus maximum principle](research_positive_path_real_wire_order.md#1-inputs-and-a-cosine-maximum-principle) gives \(|\cos(t_v/2)|<1\), with value one at complete vertices. Hence \(|	an(t_v/2)|<1\). Write each original return as \[ r_{vw}=k_{vw}+ig_{vw} =\operatorname{asinh}\{	an(t_v/2)\cos(t_w/2)\}, \quad \sum_wk_{vw}= rac{n_vH_v}{2},\quad \sum_wg_{vw}= rac{n_va_v}{2}-\pi\chi_v . 	ag{33} \] Its branch has \(k_{vw}>0\) and \(|g_{vw}|<\pi/2\). Since \(\Re\operatorname{asinh}z\le\operatorname{asinh}|z|\), the degree bound implies \[ H_v< rac{4\operatorname{asinh}1}{7}< rac{18}{35}. 	ag{34} \] Here \(\operatorname{asinh}1<9/10\), as follows from the first three positive terms of \(\sinh(9/10)\). For \(C_w=\cos(t_w/2)\), the first angle bound and (34) give \(\Im C_w<(5/7)\sinh(9/35)<1/5\). Also \(\Re C_w>0\), \(\Im	an(t_v/2)<0\), and \(\Re	an(t_v/2)\le	an(a_v/2)\). If \(g_{vw}>0\), the identity \(\sin g_{vw} =\Im\{	an(t_v/2)C_w\}/\cosh k_{vw}\) and \(\arcsin z<(25/24)z\) for \(0<z\le1/5\) give \(g_{vw}\le(5/24)	an(a_v/2)\). This upper bound also holds when \(g_{vw}\le0\). There are at most two incidences, so the real period yields \[ n_va_v \le2\pi\chi_v+ rac56	an(a_v/2) \le2\pi\chi_v+ rac5{3\pi}a_v <2\pi\chi_v+ rac8{15}a_v . 	ag{35} \] We used the chord bound \(	an(a/2)\le2a/\pi\) on \(0\le a\le\pi/2\), and \(\pi>25/8\). Thus \(a_v<30\pi/97<660/679<1\) at every active vertex. This improves the neighbor estimate to \[ \Im C_w< rac12\sinh(9/35)< rac2{15},\qquad 	an(a_v/2)<	an(1/2)< rac47 . 	ag{36} \] For a complete neighbor the first inequality is immediate. The scalar sinh bound follows from \(\sinh z\le z/(1-z^2/6)\), and \(	an(1/2)<4/7\) follows from \(\sin(1/2)<1/2\), \(\cos(1/2)>7/8\). Therefore a positive imaginary return satisfies \[ g_{vw}\le\arcsin\!\left\{ rac2{15}	an(a_v/2)ight\} < rac{101}{750}	an(a_v/2). 	ag{37} \] Indeed the argument is less than \(8/105\), and \((101/100)^2\{1-(8/105)^2\}>1\) bounds the derivative of arcsine by \(101/100\) on this interval. Sum the two possible positive contributions again. Since \(404/(375\pi)<3232/9375<7/20\), \[ n_va_v <2\pi\chi_v+ rac{202}{375}	an(a_v/2) \le2\pi\chi_v+ rac{404}{375\pi}a_v <2\pi\chi_v+ rac7{20}a_v . 	ag{38} \] This proves the angle assertion in (31), using \(40\pi/133<880/931<19/20\). In particular \(\cos a_v>29/50\). The two height improvements from the pair bootstrap now apply incidence by incidence, without a complete neighbor assumption: \[  egin{split} |	an(t_v/2)|^2 &< rac{8/7-29/50}{8/7+29/50} = rac{197}{603}<\sinh^2(14/25), &&H_v< rac8{25},\ |	an(t_v/2)|^2 &< rac{53/50-29/50}{53/50+29/50} = rac{12}{41}<\sinh^2(21/40), &&H_v< rac3{10}. \end{split} 	ag{39} \] The first line uses \(\cosh(18/35)<8/7\); the second uses \(\cosh(8/25)<53/50\). Each real return is at most \(\operatorname{asinh}|	an(t_v/2)|\), because \(|C_w|\le1\). Equation (33) and degree at most two therefore give the height bounds displayed in (39). All these scalar comparisons follow from the positive hyperbolic series and the alternating cosine series. For an edge put \(A=\cos^2(t_v/2)\), \(B=\cos^2(t_w/2)\). The new bounds give \[ |A-1|,|B-1|<r,\qquad r=\left( rac{19}{40}ight)^2+ \left( rac{3/20}{1-(3/20)^2/6}ight)^2 = rac{252350449}{1016334400}< rac14 . 	ag{40} \] Inversion maps \(D(1,r)\) to a convex disk, so its harmonic mean stays in \(D(1,r)\). Thus \(k=AB/(A+B)=\sin^2(\pi x_e)\) belongs to \(D(1/2,r/2)\), and \[ \cosh(2\pi Y_e)=|k|+|1-k|\le\sqrt{1+r^2}, \qquad 2\pi Y_e<1/4 . 	ag{41} \] The existing wire-order theorem gives \(0<\xi_e<1/4\), \(Y_e>0\), on an edge incident to an active vertex.
