Since \(\Re k>3/8\), \(\cos(2\pi\xi_e)<1/4<\cos(2\pi/5)\). This proves (32). At two complete endpoints the selected wire is \(1/4\) directly. \(\square\) **Corollary 6 (a closed central phase domain).** At unit charges, retain the actual wire and trace heights from Theorem 5, and the real-coordinate box \[  rac15\le\Re x_e\le rac3{10},\qquad |\Re t_v|\le rac{2\pi}{5}. 	ag{42} \] In its open regular interior the unsummed original phase has a uniformly negative real Hessian, with its unique maximum at the geometric critical point. Its continuous upper phase has a strict gap on the boundary of this box. The same incidence positivity statement holds for arbitrary signs of the fixed heights, though the critical-point conclusion refers to the actual upper geometric heights. *Proof.* At a selected incidence \(3/10\le b_v\le7/10\). The real parts of \(s_v+x_e\) and \(s_v-x_e\) lie, respectively, in \([1/2,1]\) and \([0,1/2]\). Consequently \(u\le0\), \(v\ge0\), and \(w>0\) where the cotangents are finite, independently of height signs. Use the positive decomposition (9), which does not include a complete-end contribution. The numbers \(-u\) and \(v\) cannot both vanish on this box: the simultaneous real-coordinate endpoint possibilities would require \((a,b)=(1/4,1/4)\) or \((1/4,3/4)\), or \(a=0,1/2\), all outside (42). For an outside complete vertex \(b=1/2\), the same strict positivity applies to its variable wire coordinate. On a closed factorial wall a cotangent can diverge when its imaginary argument also vanishes. No finite Hessian value at such a corner is asserted. The diverging term is positive semidefinite in (9). Discard it locally; the other nonzero incidence term and \(w>0\) retain a positive lower bound. A finite cover of the compact box gives a uniform bound on its open regular interior. Sum the incidence matrices exactly as in Theorem 2. The geometric point lies strictly inside (42), by (31)–(32). Integrating the Hessian bound along segments from it gives a quadratic phase loss. The original real primitive \(J\) is continuous at zero and one, so passage to the closed factorial walls preserves the inequality. This proves the boundary gap. \(\square\) **Corollary 7 (the cost of completing selected vertices).** Retain the full original edge constants and let \(M(\chi)=\Re\Phi_\chi(t(\chi))\) be the stationary action on the family of Theorem 5. Define \[ U_{n,d}= rac{14\pi d/5} {(n-2d/5)^2+(7d/5)^2}. 	ag{43} \] For \(0\le\lambda\le\mu\le1\), componentwise, \[ 0\le M(\lambda)-M(\mu) \le rac12\sum_v U_{n_v,d_v}(\mu_v^2-\lambda_v^2) < rac1{10}\sum_vd_v(\mu_v^2-\lambda_v^2) 	ag{44} \] when at least one coordinate changes. In particular, replacing the unit charges on a set \(S\) by zero increases the stationary action by less than \(\sum_{v\in S}d_v/10\), independently of the other charges and the path length. *Proof.* Theorem 5 places the entire actual charge family in \(|\Re t|<1,|\Im t|<1/3\). The exact incidence calculation (16)--(19) of the [partial-charge note](research_positive_path_partial_charge_bounds.md#2-the-exact-return-map-is-a-contraction) therefore applies to this already constructed family, regardless of the threshold used there to construct it by contraction. With the removable quotient \(Q_v=\sum_{w\sim v}r_{vw}/t_v\), it gives \[ |Q_v-d_v/2|<d_v/5,\qquad t_v= rac{2\pi\chi_v}{n_v+2iQ_v},\qquad H_v\le U_{n_v,d_v}\chi_v. 	ag{45} \] For the last inequality, write \(Q_v=A+iB\). The expression \(4\pi\chi_v A/[(n_v-2B)^2+4A^2]\) increases in both \(A\) and \(B\) on \(3d_v/10<A<7d_v/10, |B|<d_v/5\), since \(n_v>9d_v/5\). Its upper corner is (43). Stationarity gives \(\partial_{\chi_v}M=-H_v\), so integration yields the non-strict bounds in (44). For each \(d=1,2\), \(U_{n,d}\) decreases with \(n\ge7\). At \(n=7\), the two denominators in (43) are respectively \(1138/25\) and \(1157/25\). Consequently \[  rac{U_{n,d}}{2d} \le rac{35\pi}{1138}< rac1{10}. 	ag{46} \] This proves the strict last bound whenever a coordinate changes. All equations keep a zero-charge vertex and its incident complete edge factors; no edge is deleted by this comparison. \(\square\) The centered finite-kernel loss \(21/200\) in [the large-angle incidence lemma](research_path_mixed_trace_currents.md#8-a-stronger-centered-loss-for-a-removed-incidence) therefore exceeds this action cost by more than \(1/200\) per affected incidence. This is a local numerical budget, not a complete source decomposition: every affected edge and every normal must still satisfy the relevant finite-kernel bound on the contours actually used. This is a geometric and phase result. It does not establish the coefficient of the central piece in the full finite source or control any discarded wire or angular sector. The incidence-only theorem in Sections 2–3 already provides concavity on a larger positive-angle domain; (42) is useful because it is a common signed-angle box containing every unit-charge saddle in Theorem 5. The full-path threshold \(64\) also uses a source estimate on the complement, not just a saddle location. Its proof compares each removed vertex with the stationary action after setting that vertex's charge to zero. A complete-rate bound for every untouched edge would accumulate an error with path length and does not make this comparison. The [wide finite-kernel theorem](research_bare_kernel_thin_rectangle.md#6-the-full-rectangle-through-real-angle-pi-over-two) and the centered incidence estimates now cover the entire retained angular contour and its remaining complex endpoints. The [full path-source theorem](research_uniform_path_trace_assembly.md#7-the-source-theorem-at-powers-seven-and-eight) combines them with (43)–(46). The geometric and phase results in this section remain distinct inputs to that source proof; they do not independently assign a coefficient to its cycle. The focused exact scalar checks are reproduced by \(	exttt{python3 experiments/check\_positive\_path\_seven\_geometry.py}\); the saved record is [research-positive-path-seven-geometry.json](../repro/results/research-positive-path-seven-geometry.json). The written maximum-principle and branch arguments, rather than a numerical path sample, prove the arbitrary-length scope.

title: The full wire–angle phase at a two-square fold
text:
# The full wire–angle phase at a two-square fold Private written proof, 16 November 2026. The original stationary wire can cease to be a holomorphic function of its endpoint angles when its square root vanishes. At the radial limits classified in the pinned two-square theorem, this does not make the full unsummed wire–angle phase degenerate. Its critical equations are locally equivalent, by explicit holomorphic units, to the regular lifted primitive system. The full holomorphic Hessian is therefore nonsingular, including at every admitted \(q_e=0\). This is a statement about the retained original phase and its local holomorphic germ. It neither assigns its coefficient in the finite source nor constructs a completed cone metric at the two-square limit. The phase of a reversed-index kernel or of a genuinely free cardinal boundary factor is not substituted by a same-index factorial phase. ## 1. The original phase and its marked germ Use the hypotheses and limiting data of [the two-square primitive lift](research_radial_two_square_primitive_lift.md): a finite connected original ordered circle tree, a nonempty proper selected set \(S\), complete outside angles, fixed integer original powers \(n_v=\eta_v-2p_v\), and a supplied positive unit-charge solution. A sequence of actual positive common-charge solutions has a finite corner limit at \(0<\chi_*<1\). All limiting selected angles have \[ t_v=s_v-iH_v,\qquad H_v>0,\qquad |s_v|<\pi. 	ag{1} \] Every included edge is positive, a regular single-square corner, or a two-square matching edge whose endpoints each have another positive edge. On a two-square edge \[ a=	an(t_v/2)=-iA,\quad b=	an(t_w/2)=-iB,\quad 0<A,B<1,\quad q=iQ,\quad Q^2=A^2+B^2-1\ge0, 	ag{2} \] so \(|Q|<\min(A,B)<1\). A fold has \(Q=0\). For each original same-index edge retain its wire coordinate \(x_e\) and the literal incidence phase \[ b_0(x,t)=-J(1/2-x+t/(2\pi)) -J(1/2-x-t/(2\pi))-2J(x),\qquad J'(z)=\Log(2\sin\pi z). 	ag{3} \] Here \(b_0\) denotes a phase, not the endpoint tangent \(b\). The full charged phase is \[ \Phi_c(\mathbf x,\mathbf t) =\sum_{e=vw}\{b_0(x_e,t_v)+b_0(x_e,t_w)\} +\sum_{v\in S} \left( rac{i n_vt_v^2}{4\pi}-ic_vt_vight). 	ag{4} \] Outside angles are fixed, so their derivatives are omitted. The base charge is \(c_v=\chi_*\). No wire is eliminated in (4). On the positive approach the original stationary wires satisfy \[ q_e=\cot(\pi x_e),\qquad q_e^2=1+a^2+b^2. 	ag{5} \] The inverse through \(q=1,x=1/4\) is \[ x(q)= rac{1}{2\pi i}\Log rac{q+i}{q-i},\qquad  rac{dx}{dq}=- rac1{\pi(1+q^2)}. 	ag{6} \] For a positive or single-square edge, \(\Re q>0\) and \(0<\Re x<1/2\). On a two-square edge its limit is \[ x(iQ)= rac12- rac{i}{\pi}\operatorname{artanh}Q. 	ag{7} \] Thus \(x=1/2\) at a fold. In all cases \(q^2+1
e0\), so (6) is a local holomorphic coordinate change even at a fold. Every sine appearing in (3) is nonzero at this stationary limit. Indeed \(\sin\pi x
e0\), and \[  egin{aligned} \sin\pi(1/2-x+t/(2\pi)) &=\sin\pi x\,\cos(t/2)(q+a),\ \sin\pi(1/2-x-t/(2\pi)) &=\sin\pi x\,\cos(t/2)(q-a). \end{aligned} 	ag{8} \] All factors on the right are units by (1)--(2) and the pinned classification of the other edges. Consequently the logarithmic derivatives in (3) extend to a small simply connected neighborhood in the full independent variables \((x_e,t_v)\). Their constants are those reached from the positive approach. In particular the marked lift has \[ F_{e,x}=0,\qquad b_{0,t}(x_e,t_v)=-r_{v,e}/\pi \quad\hbox{at the stationary limit},\qquad F_e=b_0(x,t)+b_0(x,u). 	ag{9} \] These are the original positive-source identities passed to the limit, not logarithms reset from their exponentials. One can equivalently determine the local germ by its holomorphic sine-log derivatives and (9), with the critical constant continued from the original phase. There is no branch-existence assertion hidden here. The finite sharp square limits have bounded strip coordinates, with limiting disk points away from \(1,-1,i,-i\). A sufficiently small product of disk neighborhoods meets the positive bidisk in a connected simply connected set. On that set the unit factors in (8) and their logarithms are the original ones. Their local extensions, including at \(q=0\), give precisely the germs just specified. ## 2. Exact equivalence of the critical equations Temporarily make \(q_e\) an independent variable for every edge, using (6) to change the wire coordinates. Write \[ f_e=q_e^2-1-a^2-b^2,\qquad d_e=(1+a^2)(1+b^2),\qquad \gamma_e= rac{1+q_e^2}{d_e}. 	ag{10} \] These denominators are units near the limiting point. For the holomorphic function germ \[ L(z)= rac{\Log(1+z)}z,\qquad L(0)=1, 	ag{11} \] use its local branch at zero. The exact exponentiated original wire equation is \[  egin{aligned} \exp F_{e,x} &= rac{(q_e^2-a^2)(q_e^2-b^2)} {(1+a^2)(1+b^2)}\ &=1+\gamma_e f_e. \end{aligned} 	ag{12} \] For the first equality, differentiate (3), multiply the two incidence sine ratios, and use \(\sin^2\pi x=1/(1+q^2)\). For the second, expand the numerator difference: \[ (q^2-a^2)(q^2-b^2)-(1+a^2)(1+b^2) =(1+q^2)(q^2-1-a^2-b^2). 	ag{13} \] The zero lift in (9), retained in the local neighborhood, therefore gives the unexponentiated identity \[ F_{e,x}=\gamma_e f_e L(\gamma_e f_e). 	ag{14} \] Define the off-constraint original logarithmic extension by \[ \widehat r_{v,e} =\log\{\cos(t_w/2)(q_e+a)\},\qquad \widehat r_{w,e} =\log\{\cos(t_v/2)(q_e+b)\}. 	ag{15} \] Its branches have the limiting original values. Set also \[ \widetilde r_{v,e}=	frac12\Log rac{q_e+a}{q_e-a}, \qquad b_{0,t}(x_e,t_v)=-\widetilde r_{v,e}/\pi, 	ag{16} \] with the same continued lift. The elementary factor identity \[ \cos^2(t_w/2)(q_e+a)(q_e-a) = rac{q_e^2-a^2}{1+b^2} =1+ rac{f_e}{1+b^2} 	ag{17} \] proves \[ \widehat r_{v,e}-\widetilde r_{v,e} = rac12\Log\left(1+ rac{f_e}{1+b^2}ight). 	ag{18} \] There is no additional logarithmic constant: both sides vanish on the continued stationary sheet. The analogous formula at \(w\) interchanges \(a,b\). Put \[ \widehat{\mathcal P}_v =\sum_{e
i v}\widehat r_{v,e}- rac{i n_vt_v}{2}, \qquad G_v=\widehat{\mathcal P}_v+\pi i c_v. 	ag{19} \] Let \(\widetilde\Phi_c(q,t)=\Phi_c(x(q),t)\). Its full gradient obeys the exact local identities \[  oxed{ egin{aligned} \partial_{q_e}\widetilde\Phi_c &=- rac{L(\gamma_e f_e)}{\pi d_e}\,f_e,\ \partial_{t_v}\widetilde\Phi_c &=- rac{G_v}{\pi} +\sum_{e=vw}  rac{L(f_e/(1+a_w^2))} {2\pi(1+a_w^2)}\,f_e . \end{aligned}} 	ag{20} \] The angular derivative is taken with the independent \(q_e\) fixed, equivalently with the corresponding \(x_e\) fixed. In particular, if the equation vector is ordered as \((f,G)\), then the full gradient is an invertible triangular holomorphic matrix times that vector. Its first diagonal entries are \(-L(\gamma_e f_e)/(\pi d_e)\); its selected angular diagonal is \(-I/\pi\). Hence the two generated local holomorphic ideals are equal: \[  ig\langle d\widetilde\Phi_c igangle = ig\langle(f_e)_e,(G_v)_{v\in S} igangle . 	ag{21} \] This is a local identity for the exact continued phase, rather than an analogy between two stationary equations. ## 3. Nonsingularity of the full Hessian **Theorem.** At the supplied radial corner limit, the full holomorphic Hessian of (4) in all retained wire variables and selected angular variables is nonsingular. The conclusion includes every fold edge \(q_e=0\). **Proof.** First consider the Jacobian of \((f,G)\) in all independent \((q,t)\). On a nonfold edge \(\partial f_e/\partial q_e=2q_e
e0\), so its constraint can be solved for the original local square root. Eliminating these constraints leaves exactly the lifted fold and primitive system of the pinned two-square theorem. That system has invertible Jacobian. The full constraint/primitive Jacobian is therefore invertible as well. At a critical point, differentiation of (20) multiplies this Jacobian by the invertible triangular matrix in (21). Terms differentiating that matrix vanish because \(f=G=0\). Thus \(\operatorname{Hess}_{(q,t)}\widetilde\Phi_c\) is invertible. The coordinate change (6) has invertible differential, and a critical Hessian transforms by congruence. This proves the assertion in the original \((x,t)\) coordinates. \(\square\) For an explicit local check, the wire-only negative second derivative is the familiar original expression \[ -F_{e,xx}=  rac{2\pi q_e(1+q_e^2)^2}{(1+a^2)(1+b^2)} \quad\hbox{when }f_e=0. 	ag{22} \] It vanishes at a fold. There, with the notation of (2) and \(A^2+B^2=1\), the mixed wire–angle row is instead \[ F_{e,x(t_v,t_w)} = rac{i}{AB}(B,A)
e0. 	ag{23} \] Indeed \(df_e=iAB(B\,dt_v+A\,dt_w)\), and (14) at the fold has coefficient \(1/(A^2B^2)\). The same vector is the real constraint normal used in the lifted primitive proof. The positive edges forced beside each two-square edge control the complementary angle directions. This is why the joint system stays regular even though the wire-only Hessian vanishes. More precisely, with the ordering in (21) and \(d=|E|+|S|\), at the critical point \[ \det\operatorname{Hess}_{(q,t)}\widetilde\Phi_c = rac{(-1)^d}{\pi^d\prod_e d_e} \det D_{(q,t)}(f,G). 	ag{24} \] Passing to \((x,t)\) multiplies this determinant by \(\prod_e\{\pi(1+q_e^2)\}^2\), a nonzero factor. No lower bound uniform over unspecified radial limits is inferred from this local determinant identity. The holomorphic Morse lemma consequently gives local coordinates \(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_d\), with nonzero Jacobian, in which \[ \Phi_c=\Phi_c(x_*,t_*)- rac12\sum_{j=1}^d\xi_j^2. 	ag{25} \] Real \(\xi\) give a strictly descending local real \(d\)-disk. These coordinates generally mix wire and angle variables. They do not assert concavity on the original horizontal product contour. They also do not repair the singular operation of eliminating the fold wire as a function of arbitrary endpoint angles. ## 4. Relation to the exact factorial source For \(N\ge2\), \(D=N-1\), the actual halfwire interpolation is \[ B_N(x,t)= rac{N}{ G_N(D/2-Nx+Nt/(2\pi)) G_N(D/2-Nx-Nt/(2\pi))G_N(Nx)^2}. 	ag{26} \] The exact divisor result used in the pinned product-contour theorem implies that \(B_N(x,t)\) and \(B_N(D/N-x,t)\) are holomorphic near every compact subset of \[ - rac1{2N}\le\Re x\le1- rac1{2N},\qquad |\Re t|<\pi, 	ag{27} \] at arbitrary finite imaginary heights. This uses the canonical factorial itself, not an asymptotic continuation of Stirling's formula. Every stationary wire considered here has \(0<\Re x_e\le1/2\), by (6)--(7). The selected angles have the strict margin (1), and outside angles equal zero. Since there are finitely many edges, a small fixed neighborhood of the target satisfies (27) for every \(N\ge2\). For example, choose all wire real parts between a fixed positive number and a number strictly below \(3/4\); the latter is the upper endpoint of (27) at \(N=2\). Thus the exact halfwire factors have no pole in that neighborhood, including at \(x=1/2\). Where the source is traced, the exact joint-lens form still contains \[ \prod_v \sin t_v\,  rac{e^{-iNt_v}}{(1-\eta e^{-iNt_v})^2}\, e^{i n_vNt_v^2/(4\pi)} \cos(N(1-c_v)t_v),\qquad \eta=(-1)^{N-1}, 	ag{28} \] with the actual factors \[ N^{|E|}\prod_v rac{-N^2 C_{N,n_v}}{\pi i}, \qquad C_{N,n}=e^{\pi i nD^2/(4N)}, 	ag{29} \] and every prescribed spectator. On selected lower angular neighborhoods \(H_v>0\), there is no physical trace pole. The primitive branch in (4) uses the charge-\(c_v\) exponential: it is the product of \(e^{-iNt_v}\) in (28) and \(	frac12 e^{iN(1-c_v)t_v}\) from the original cosine. The other cosine exponential and the denominator in (28) remain in the exact source. At \(c_v=1\) the two cosine terms coincide and their coefficients add to one. No branch or current is deleted by the phase calculation. The exact source equalities retain all first Hermite normals, the odd simple node, and the original closing functional. At a genuine free spectral boundary the compiler requires its ordinary cardinal polynomial representative instead of (26); its asymptotic phase has not been identified with (3). Likewise, a reversed-index kernel retains its different original phase. The Hessian theorem concerns the same-index phase (4) with its stated fixed outside angular parameters. Holomorphy in (27) does not imply that (26) is nonzero, that one continued factorial asymptotic branch dominates there, or that the descending disk (25) has nonzero coefficient in the prescribed relative cycle. Exact factorial zeros, branch frequencies, connectors and all angular sectors must still be retained. The established gain is the removal of a local full-phase degeneracy: a vanishing wire-only Hessian at these admitted folds is not a caustic of the complete stationary system. ## Direct sources All four complete source texts were read, their directly used identities checked, and their hashes verified. * [Two-square radial primitive lift](research_radial_two_square_primitive_lift.md), SHA256 21d9af750653621cc82bd73373a99a138210fc4cdb10407faabcb209505df9ad: the actual radial hypotheses, matching/pinning theorem, units, and nonsingular lifted constraint/primitive system. * [Unsummed original network phase](research_unsummed_network_phase_coercivity.md), SHA256 b5441bb508d3ffad3274e38dda2d6aeb099d08ae2ab043a0d12c25234e4a1e1e: (1)--(4) and Section 5, the same-index incidence phase, original zero logarithmic lift and angular derivative normalization. Its numerical examples and saved computations are not used. * [Exact product source contour](research_positive_wire_product_contour.md), SHA256 5646f2d6b2a8dfa2d8c49662d17f19f3743fc4efcaf3c3685c6a899975a4c230: inverse cotangent branch, literal factorial interpolation, full-strip holomorphy and distinction between phase and source nonvanishing. Its positive-domain stationary graph theorem is not extended across the fold by assertion. * [Joint factorial-lens source](research_joint_factorial_lens_relative_source.md), SHA256 a14ca148bd55b36b1eea9de8be8a63025532c3bbbb928482b0d7cb8edae56e54: exact charged top form and normalization, retained full Hermite data, free-boundary convention and relative-cycle limitations. Only written proofs, source-text reads and hashes were used. No mathematical computation program, numerical evaluation, test or compilation was run. The adopted two-square note and all other frozen sources, manuscripts and public documents were unchanged.

title: A common complex endpoint baseline with its original window currents
text: # A common complex endpoint baseline with its original window currents Private written proof, 16 November 2026. The unturned microscopic kernel has a common polynomially bounded analytic baseline on every buffered bounded subdomain of \(0<\Re x<1/2\). Exact representatives on the two half-domains retain both physical channels and differ from that baseline exponentially. Their real interface and every exterior current remain explicit. No extra complex characteristic-separation hypothesis is needed: the original balanced two-component step is already \(I+O(N^{-1})\). There is also a direct estimate for the entire positive-spectral-end window of a filled-leaf trace, including the derivative of the outgoing kernel. That window has arbitrarily small exponential cost. Neither result supplies the still-missing generic-parameter scalar seed for the filled leaf: the opposite endpoint and the coherent interface remain to be estimated at the terminal action. ## 1. Original data and the complex domain Put \(h=N^{-1}\), \(D=N-1\), \(\eta=(-1)^D\), and retain \[ c_N(x)=2\cos(2\pi x+\pi h),\qquad x_j=jh,\qquad c_j=c_N(x_j),\qquad w_N(\alpha)=2\cosh(\alpha h), \] \[ e_k(Z)=S_k^{-2}\prod_{a<k}(c_a-Z),\qquad S_k=\prod_{\ell=1}^k2\sin(\pi\ell/N),\qquad B_N(Z,\alpha)=K_N(w_N(\alpha),Z)=\sum_{k=0}^D e_k(w_N)e_k(Z). \tag{1} \] The trace is the original full Hermite functional: \[ \phi_N(f)=\eta\sum_{j<\lfloor N/2\rfloor} \{(4-c_j^2)f'(c_j)-c_jf(c_j)\} +\mathbf1_{N\ {\rm odd}}f(-2). \tag{2} \] All endpoint parameters below range over arbitrary fixed bounded complex disks. Larger disks are used for parameter derivatives. Fix a real compact interval \(I\Subset(0,1/2)\), with larger real buffers, and a bounded target rectangle whose closure lies in \[ \mathcal V=\{0<\Re x<1/2\}. \tag{3} \] Enlarge the rectangle, still inside \(\mathcal V\), to contain the real buffers and choose three nested rectangles with fixed positive separations. Every bounded compact subset of \(\mathcal V\), together with a chosen real base interval, admits this construction. Thus the statement below also applies to arbitrary such compact subdomains. The rectangles and all their margins are independent of \(N,\alpha\). **Theorem 1.** There is a jointly holomorphic baseline \(A_N^0(x,\alpha)\), polynomially bounded on the target rectangle, and constants \(C,p,\kappa>0\), such that on the buffered real window \[ \begin{split} \varepsilon_j&=B_N(c_j,\alpha)-A_N^0(x_j,\alpha),\\ \omega_j&=c_N'(x_j)\partial_ZB_N(c_j,\alpha) -\partial_xA_N^0(x_j,\alpha), \end{split} \qquad |\varepsilon_j|+|\omega_j|\le C N^p e^{-\kappa N}. \tag{4} \] There are exact scalar representatives \[ H_N^\sigma=A_N^0+C_N^\sigma,\qquad \sigma=\pm1, \tag{5} \] whose value and \(x\)-derivative equal the two original data in (4) at every node of the window. On every fixed compact part of the target rectangle with \(\sigma\Im x\ge0\), \[ |C_N^\sigma|\le C'e^{-\kappa_1N}. \tag{6} \] All fixed derivatives have the same form on smaller domains. The constants may depend on the target height and buffers, but the one-sided repair in (6) does not lose an exponential factor at that height. The baseline and representatives are not asserted to be periodic or to extend through the two real spectral endpoints. ## 2. The exact near-identity step and the common baseline Write \(s_r=2\sin(\pi r/N)\), and set \[ A_N(r)=\frac{s_{r+1}^4}{s_{2r+1}s_{2r+2}},\qquad C_N(r)=\frac{s_r^4}{s_{2r}s_{2r+1}}, \] \[ q_N(x)=\frac{C_N(Nx)}{A_N(Nx)},\qquad d_N(x)=\frac{c_0-w_N(\alpha)}{A_N(Nx)},\qquad T_N(x)= \begin{pmatrix}1+d_N&h q_N\\d_N/h&q_N\end{pmatrix}. \tag{7} \] For \(F_j=B_N(c_j,\alpha)\) the exact physical value state is \[ X_j=(F_j,h^{-1}(F_j-F_{j-1}))^t, \qquad X_{j+1}=T_N(x_j)X_j. \tag{8} \] This is the original kernel recurrence. Its ordinary endpoint source is retained; its value and first derivative vanish at the bulk nodes used in (8), as established in the two-channel source. On every buffered rectangle in (3), direct substitution gives \[ A_N(Nx)=\tan^2(\pi x)+O(h),\quad q_N=1+O(h),\quad d_N=O(h^2),\qquad T_N=I+hB_h,\quad \|B_h\|\le C. \tag{9} \] The assertions are holomorphic and uniform on larger bounded parameter disks. The sine and cosine zeros in the exact coefficients are real and approach the boundaries of (3); no denominator vanishes on these rectangles for large \(N\). Their limiting factors are units there. Cauchy's estimates give every fixed derivative. This verifies (9) at any fixed complex height in the strip, not only in the original thin interpolation tube. The full endpoint-product bound and Markov's inequality give \(\|X_j\|\le CN^p\) on the real buffers. We apply the bounded modified differential-equation construction from the one-sided continuation source directly to (9). Here is its estimate in the present setting. For a bounded analytic matrix \(A\), let \(\Phi_h(A;x)\) be its fundamental flow from \(x\) to \(x+h\), and put \[ Q_h(A)=\frac{\Phi_h(A)-I}{h}-A,\qquad \mathcal F_h(A)=B_h-Q_h(A). \tag{10} \] Between domains eroded by \(\delta\ge2h\), the flow integral and Cauchy's estimate imply, on a fixed bounded matrix ball, \[ \|Q_h(A)-Q_h(\widetilde A)\| \le C(h+h/\delta)\|A-\widetilde A\|. \tag{11} \] Indeed the two terms in \(Q_h\) are the average of \(A(x+s)-A(x)\) and the average of \(A(x+s)(\Phi_s(A)-I)\). Their differences cost respectively \(Ch/\delta\) and \(Ch\). Start at \(A^{(0)}=B_h\). A fixed initial shrink makes its first increment \(O(h)\). Thereafter choose \(\delta=Mh\) with fixed large \(M\), so (11) is at most \(1/2\). A fixed remaining buffer permits \(K\ge c/h\) iterations. They remain in the bounded ball and give a bounded analytic matrix \(A_h\) with \[ \Phi_h(A_h;x)-T_N(x)=O(e^{-c_1/h}). \tag{12} \] Reserve another fixed buffer for derivatives. This is a finite analytic iteration, with an estimated residual, not a formal series. Solve \(Y'=A_hY\) with \(Y(x_{j_*})=X_{j_*}\) at an actual interior row. Rectangular paths have bounded lengths, so both its fundamental matrix and inverse have bounds \(e^{CL}\). Hence \(Y\) has polynomial norm throughout the target rectangle. On the real buffer, \(\|T_N^{\pm1}\|\le1+Ch\); comparison of its steps with (12), in both directions, gives \[ Y(x_j)-X_j=O(N^p e^{-c_2N}). \tag{13} \] Take \(A_N^0\) to be the first component of \(Y\). The derivative assertion in (4) is not inferred from (8). Use the actual scalar Hermite representative supplied by the bulk compatibility theorem on a fixed thin real tube. It and \(A_N^0\) have polynomial analytic norms. Repair the exponentially small nodal differences in (13) temporarily with a finite sinc sum. On a sufficiently narrow buffered tube the repair, and its derivative, remain exponentially small. The repaired functions have \(cN\) common zeros in each local disk. The disk Blaschke estimate, followed by Cauchy's formula and a finite cover, makes their derivative difference exponentially small on an inner tube. Undoing the temporary repair proves the second equation of (4). This uses the proved normal compatibility of the actual unturned kernel. ## 3. Exact one-sided Hermite repair and the original interface Sum over the window's nodes and define \[ L_j^\sigma(x)=e^{\sigma2\pi i(x-x_j)/h} \operatorname{sinc}^2((x-x_j)/h), \] \[ C_N^\sigma(x)=\sum_j [\varepsilon_j+(\omega_j-\sigma2\pi i\varepsilon_j/h)(x-x_j)] L_j^\sigma(x). \tag{14} \] At its own node the summand has value \(\varepsilon_j\) and derivative \(\omega_j\); at every other node it has a double zero. The Fourier support of \(L_j^+\) is \([0,2/h]\), and of \(L_j^-\) is \([-2/h,0]\), with absolute coefficient mass one. Thus \(|L_j^\sigma|\le1\) on its designated half-plane. Formula (4), the \(O(N)\) summands, and the fixed bounded domain prove (6). Fixed derivatives add polynomial factors. On the opposite half-plane the cost is \(e^{4\pi|\Im x|/h}\), so only a sufficiently thin fixed opposite collar is asserted. Use the uncentered grid kernel \[ D_h(x)=(\pi/h)^2\csc^2(\pi x/h). \tag{15} \] Writing \(z=x-x_j\), \(k=2\pi i/h\), the exact cancellation is \[ D_h(C_N^+-C_N^-) =\sum_j\frac{[\varepsilon_j+(\omega_j-k\varepsilon_j)z]e^{kz} -[\varepsilon_j+(\omega_j+k\varepsilon_j)z]e^{-kz}}{z^2}. \tag{16} \] The apparent singularity at zero is removable, with value \(4\pi i\omega_j/h\). For real \(z\), separate \(|z|\le h\) and \(|z|\ge h\), using Taylor's formula in the first region. Each term is at most \(C(h^{-2}|\varepsilon_j|+h^{-1}|\omega_j|)\). Consequently \[ \sup_{\text{real window}}|D_h(C_N^+-C_N^-)| \le C e^{-\kappa_2N}. \tag{17} \] The constants \(\kappa_1,\kappa_2\) are positive, not freely adjustable. For a fixed shared product of microscopic kernels, multiply the baselines and, separately, the two exact representatives. The ordinary product rule preserves all first normals. A telescoping product difference and (16)--(17) give the same exponential real interface bound with a changed polynomial prefactor. All shared parameters remain shared. Let \(A_N(Z;\mathbf y)\) be the whole remaining actual spectator, with any other traces still unapplied. Include the original crossing through \[ \tau_N(x)=\pi-2\pi x-\pi h,\quad E_{N,n}(x)=\mathfrak c_{N,n}e^{inN\tau_N(x)^2/(4\pi)},\quad \mathfrak c_{N,n}=e^{\pi i nD^2/(4N)}. \tag{18} \] For a positive-row window \(j_0\le j\le j_1\), choose midpoint boundaries \(a_N=(j_0-\tfrac12)h\), \(b_N=(j_1+\tfrac12)h\) and exterior half-contours inside the target rectangle. Put \[ g_\sigma(x)=\sin(2\pi x+\pi h)\, H_N^\sigma(x)E_{N,n}(x)A_N(c_N(x);\mathbf y). \tag{19} \] For shared products replace \(H_N^\sigma\) by their product. Then the original restricted full trace is exactly \[ -\frac{\eta}{2\pi^2i}\left\{ \int_{E_-}D_hg_-\,dx+\int_{E_+}D_hg_+\,dx +\int_{a_N}^{b_N}D_h(g_+-g_-)\,dx\right\}. \tag{20} \] Here \(E_-\) runs down the left side, across the bottom, and up the right side; \(E_+\) runs up the right side, across the top, and down the left side. All vertical half-sides are included. To check normalization, if \(g=\sin(2\pi x+\pi h)f(c_N(x))\), then \(g'(x_j)=-\pi\{(4-c_j^2)f'(c_j)-c_jf(c_j)\}\). The residue of \(D_hg\) is \(g'(x_j)\). The interface sign follows by closing the upper half-contour with the real path from \(a_N\) to \(b_N\); the difference has no grid poles because its two jets vanish. This proves (20) with the original crossing normal. The interface in (20) is bounded pointwise by \[ C e^{-\kappa_2N} |\sin(2\pi x+\pi h)E_{N,n}(x)A_N(c_N(x);\mathbf y)|. \tag{21} \] No spectator is factored or replaced. On real rows the crossing has modulus one. On midpoint verticals and nonzero horizontal heights, \(D_h=O(N^2e^{-2\pi N|\Im x|})\); all its original aliases are retained. The exterior integrals are still present. For every fixed positive power \(m\ge2\), the selected terminal saddle satisfies \(0<\Re t_m<\pi\), \(\Im t_m<0\). For power \(-m\), use the reflected Fourier sector on this right angular chart: its saddle is \(t_{-m}=\overline{t_m}\), so \(\Im t_{-m}>0\). Equivalently, the source's reflection \(t\mapsto-\overline t\) is followed by the even angular reflection back to the right chart; the Fourier sector is reflected with it. Under \(t=\tau_N(x)\), both nearby fixed charts lie in (3) for large \(N\). The positive-power saddle uses \(H_N^+\), since \(\Im x>0\); the negative-power saddle uses \(H_N^-\), since \(\Im x<0\). Theorem 1 therefore supplies the unturned insertion there with no additional exponential amplitude cost. This removes a complex-baseline continuation obstacle; it does not estimate the other terms in (20) or assert a filled-leaf scalar seed. ## 4. The actual positive-endpoint window, with both kernel channels Let \(M_{a,N}=K_N(c_a,-2)\). The positive-row source proves \[ M_{a,N}\le(a+1)(C_0N/a)^{2a},\qquad C_0=\pi e^2/2, \qquad M_{a,N}\le N e^{N h_0(\varepsilon)} \quad(a\le\varepsilon N), \] \[ h_0(\varepsilon)=2\varepsilon\log(C_0/\varepsilon). \tag{22} \] The case \(a=0\) is read separately as \(M_{0,N}=1\). Write \(Q_{a,N}(Z)=\partial_1K_N(c_a,Z)\); it need not have the low degree of \(K_N(c_a,Z)\). For fixed \(0<\varepsilon<1/8\), uniformly for \(0\le a\le\varepsilon N\) and all sufficiently large \(N\), \[ \|K_N(c_a,\cdot)\|_{[-2,2]} +N^{-2}\|Q_{a,N}\|_{[-2,2]} \le C N^2 M_{a+1,N}. \tag{23} \] Indeed \(c_a-c_{a+1}=4\sin(2(a+1)\pi/N)\sin(\pi/N)\ge c/N^2\), with an absolute positive margin in this range. Choose an absolute \(\rho>0\) so the disk \(|w-c_a|\le\rho/N^2\) lies in \(|w-2|\le2-c_{a+1}\). The physical-row root product, whose roots are all above \(2\), gives \[ |K_N(w,c_j)|\le K_N(c_{a+1},c_j)\le M_{a+1,N}. \tag{24} \] The distinct-node low interpolant consequently has real norm at most \(NM_{a+1,N}\). The remaining high Newton factors each have real norm at most \(\sqrt{N-1}\). The disk just chosen lies in a Bernstein ellipse of parameter \(e^{C/N}\): its endpoint extension is \(O(N^{-2})\) and its minor semiaxis is \(O(N^{-1})\). Their values in that disk are therefore at most \(C\sqrt N\). The entire high sum has real norm \(O(N^2)\). This proves \(\sup_{|w-c_a|\le\rho/N^2}\|K_N(w,\cdot)\|\le CN^2M_{a+1,N}\); Cauchy's formula proves (23). The entire first normal, not just the derivative of the low physical row, is bounded here. Now fix any integer \(n\) and any fixed microscopic product \(B(Z)=\prod_i K_N(w_N(\alpha_i),Z)\). Let \(W_{N,\varepsilon}(Z)\) be the literal part of \(\phi_N[R^n B K_N(\cdot,Z)]\) with \(0\le a\le\varepsilon N\). Every term of (2) and its full product derivative is retained. The bound for \(B,B'\) is polynomial by the endpoint-product theorem and Markov. The original crossing values and first normals cost a polynomial, by (18) and \(dZ/d\tau=2\sin\tau\). Equations (22)--(23) thus give \[ \boxed{\quad \sup_{|\boldsymbol\alpha|\le A} |W_{N,\varepsilon}(-2\cos u)| \le C N^p \exp\{N[h_0(2\varepsilon)+|\Im u|]\}. \quad} \tag{25} \] For the real-output estimate, sum the \(O(N)\) rows after applying (23); \(a+1\le2\varepsilon N\) for large \(N\). The resulting ordinary output polynomial has degree at most \(D\). Its Chebyshev coefficient bound gives the displayed complex continuation, with a polynomial factor. In particular the continuation cost is \(|\Im u|\), not \(\varepsilon|\Im u|\): \(Q_{a,N}\) can still have degree \(D\). Fixed output and microscopic-parameter derivatives have the same form on smaller parameter sets, with polynomial losses. Since \(h_0(2\varepsilon)\to0\), this actual endpoint window is strictly below any fixed positive terminal action on a sufficiently small fixed output disk. It includes neither the opposite spectral endpoint nor a connecting integral. It is not a scalar seed by itself. ## 5. The remaining action budget and a real product-rate diagnostic The baseline theorem provides a positive \(\kappa_2\), but does not prove that it pays the whole terminal deficit. At real complete output the reference edge rate is \(M_\infty=4G/\pi\), whereas \(\mathcal I_2=2G/\pi\). An absolute real-interface estimate from (21) has reference budget \(M_\infty-\kappa_2\), so this route would require \(\kappa_2\ge M_\infty-\mathcal I_n\). The explicit two-subgrid estimate in the scalar-compatibility source supplies \(R\log3/16\) on a buffered \(x\)-disk of radius \(R<\min(x,1/2-x)\le1/4\), before subsequent losses. These displayed constants do not establish the required inequality: \[ \log3/64<\log2/4<2G/\pi=M_\infty-\mathcal I_2. \tag{26} \] For the middle inequality, integrate \(\log\cot s>\log2\) on \((0,\pi/8)\). This comparison does not upper-bound the true error exponent or prove growth of the actual interface. There is an exact real diagnostic from the central lowering products in the scalar source. Put \(z=\sin^2(t/2)\), \(0<t<\pi\), and \[ J_\delta(t)=-\int_0^\delta \log\left|\frac{z-\sin^2(\pi u)}{\cos^2(\pi u)}\right|du, \qquad 0<\delta<1/2. \tag{27} \] This is their logarithmic product rate. To check the statement on real angles, take nearest midpoint sequences \(t_N=t+O(N^{-1})\), at distance at least \(c/N\) from each product zero. Factor the numerator as \(\sin(t/2+\pi u)\sin(t/2-\pi u)\). Removing its possible logarithmic zero leaves smooth Riemann sums; the removed shifted factorial sum has \(O(\log N)\) error. The two parity offsets change that error only by \(O(\log N)\). The bounded microscopic parameter perturbation of the cosine factor contributes \(O(N^{-1})\) to the logarithm. Thus the finite products from the scalar source have logarithm \(-NJ_\delta(t)+O(\log N)\) along these midpoint sequences. At actual zeros they vanish; no nonzero rate is assigned there. For each \(t\), the unique maximum is obtained at \[ \sin^2(\pi\delta_*)=(1+z)/2,\qquad J_*(t):=J_{\delta_*}(t) =\frac1\pi\int_t^\pi\operatorname{asinh}(\sin(s/2))\,ds. \tag{28} \] Indeed the \(\delta\)-derivative in (27) changes sign precisely when the absolute ratio is one. Differentiation in \(t\), with the logarithmic singularity interpreted as its elementary principal value, gives \[ J_*'(t)=-\frac{\sin(t/2)\cos(t/2)}{\pi} \operatorname{PV}\int_0^{\pi\delta_*} \frac{dv}{\sin^2(t/2)-\sin^2v} =-\frac{\operatorname{asinh}(\sin(t/2))}{\pi}. \tag{29} \] For the last equality substitute \(y=\tan v\); the real antiderivative is an inverse hyperbolic cotangent at the upper endpoint. The boundary term is zero because its logarithm is zero. The limit \(J_*(\pi)=0\) fixes (28): away from \(u=1/2\) the logarithm in (27) tends uniformly to zero, and its remaining shrinking endpoint interval has an integrable logarithmic bound with integral tending to zero. Also \(\int_0^{\pi/2}\operatorname{asinh}(\sin v)\,dv=G\): differentiating the same integral with a parameter \(k\) multiplying \(\sin v\) gives \(\arctan k/k\), then integrate \(0\le k\le1\). Consequently \(J_*(0)=2G/\pi\). The calibrated edge derivative is \(\psi_t(t,0)=-\operatorname{asinh}(\tan(t/2))/\pi\). Hence \[ \psi(t,0)-J_*(t)\le\mathcal I_2, \tag{30} \] strictly for \(t>0\); near zero the difference is \(\mathcal I_2-t^4/(64\pi)+O(t^6)\). This compares an exact real central-product rate with the action. It is not an estimate for the baseline error, its real interface, or their coherent complex continuation. In particular (28)--(30) do not establish the missing generic-parameter filled-leaf seed. ## 6. Coverage and direct sources The thin scalar compatibility, one-sided cardinal repair, and modified differential equation are prior results. The additional assembly uses the actual unturned near-identity system on the whole buffered vertical strip, without a new characteristic separation premise, and supplies the full-normal estimate (25). The hypergeometric value-connection theorem supplies a real-bulk leading profile, not a controlled fixed-height alias remainder; it is not used as a substitute for the source current. The following complete sources were read at unchanged pins, with their used implications checked: * [Actual two-channel recurrence](research_microscopic_endpoint_two_channel_interpolation.md), SHA256 44f6db0f8afdf1205ab8b0935b95b8a4fd9fa16c6414be2467b8b40a123c0ffe. * [Actual unturned scalar compatibility](research_microscopic_endpoint_bulk_scalar_compatibility.md), SHA256 2b8713ed16b66f5faa004403ac1d032021eee0a6f8f38082481d002c672c0b2e. * [Bounded modified ODE and one-sided repair](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_terminal_one_sided_characteristic_continuation.md), SHA256 1316cfb9ed7fec208a8aa8308ea7015c7cf32534a8662500892f9a62b5e9b475. * [Full endpoint products and original trace](research_endpoint_two_half_plane_relative_source.md), SHA256 985fa3331379c3877734f28773d314b667ee87fa63314a5ef4513a3fe128d194. * [Positive-row coefficient mass](research_physical_row_charge_transport.md), SHA256 d09d5c669848f0389504cea613244570eca18be03f2b608a359773e423e97040. * [Original terminal action calibration](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_terminal_characteristic_action_calibration.md), SHA256 582c359817b69b0dd1094e49878d15917230e86f6e7831fe448ea4aacee8a1fd. Only written mathematics, source-text reads and hashes were used. No mathematical program, numerical experiment, test, build or compilation was run. Frozen notes and public manuscripts are unchanged.

title: Exact period monodromy of the unturned endpoint recurrence
text:
# Exact period monodromy of the unturned endpoint recurrence Private written proof, 16 November 2026. The ordinary unturned recurrence has an explicit two-dimensional monodromy over one full angular period. Its trace follows from the entire characteristic polynomial of a generic cyclic orbit, including the repeated physical eigenvalues. This supplies branch data for a possible homogeneous scalar continuation. It does not choose that continuation's actual source coefficients or bound them. ## 1. Ordinary recurrence and generic orbit Put \[ N\ge2,\quad h=N^{-1},\quad 	heta=\pi/N,\quad s_r=2\sin(r	heta),\quad c_r=2\cos((2r+1)	heta), \] \[ c_N(x)=2\cos(2\pi x+\pi h),\qquad P_N(w)=2T_N(w/2)+2=\prod_{j=0}^{N-1}(w-c_j). 	ag{1} \] The original ordinary difference operator is \[ \mathscr J_NF=(c_0+A_N+B_N)F-A_NF(x+h)-B_NF(x-h), \] \[ A_N(x)= rac{s_{Nx+1}^{\,4}}{s_{2Nx+1}s_{2Nx+2}}, \qquad B_N(x)= rac{s_{Nx}^{\,4}}{s_{2Nx}s_{2Nx+1}}. 	ag{2} \] These are meromorphic coefficient functions of \(x\), of period one. This is the ordinary operator, not a relation imposed only after canonical reduction. Initially fix \(x\) with \[ 2Nx
otin\mathbb Z. 	ag{3} \] Then every coefficient on the orbit \(x+lh\), \(l\in\mathbb Z\), is finite, and \(A_N,B_N\) there are nonzero. The \(N\) spectral points \(c_N(x+lh)\), \(0\le l<N\), are distinct. Indeed, equality of two cosine values would imply either equality of their indices modulo \(N\), or \(2Nx+l+k+1\in N\mathbb Z\), excluded by (3). For a scalar solution of \((\mathscr J_N-w)F=0\), use the state \[ Y_F(x)= inom{F(x)}{F(x-h)},\qquad Y_F(x+h)=T_N(x,w)Y_F(x), \] \[ T_N(x,w)=  egin{pmatrix} (c_0+A_N(x)+B_N(x)-w)/A_N(x)&-B_N(x)/A_N(x)\ 1&0 \end{pmatrix}. 	ag{4} \] Its period transfer is the ordered product \[ M_N(x,w)=T_N(x+(N-1)h,w)\cdots T_N(x,w). 	ag{5} \] In particular no inverse-period or opposite-power convention enters this definition. ## 2. The full twisted cyclic determinant Write \(A_l=A_N(x+lh)\), \(B_l=B_N(x+lh)\), and \[ a_N(x)=(-1)^N\prod_{l=0}^{N-1}A_l. 	ag{6} \] The sine products give the exact identities \[ \prod_{l=0}^{N-1} rac{B_l}{A_l}=1,\qquad a_N(x)=	an^2(\pi Nx). 	ag{7} \] For the first, the fourth powers in \(B_l/A_l=s_{Nx+l}^4s_{2Nx+2l+2}/ [s_{Nx+l+1}^4s_{2Nx+2l}]\) telescope over a period. For the second, put \(ho=Nx\). The numerator of the product of the \(A_l\) is \(16\sin^4(\piho)\). Its denominator is \[ \prod_{m=1}^{2N}s_{2ho+m} =(-1)^N\left(\prod_{m=1}^Ns_{2ho+m}ight)^2 =(-1)^N\,4\sin^2(2\piho). 	ag{8} \] Here \(\prod_{m=1}^N2\sin((z+m)\pi/N)=2\sin(\pi(z+1))\) was used before squaring. Equations (6)--(8) prove (7) at both parities. For \(\mu
e0\), let \(J_\mu(x)\) be the \(N\)-dimensional cyclic operator (2), with the boundary convention \[ F_{l+N}=\mu F_l. 	ag{9} \] Thus the forward term in row \(N-1\) carries \(\mu\), and the backward term in row zero carries \(\mu^{-1}\). **Lemma.** For every \(N\ge2\), on the generic set (3), \[  oxed{\quad \det(wI-J_\mu(x)) =P_N(w)+a_N(x)(2-\mu-\mu^{-1}). \quad} 	ag{10} \] *Proof.* First take \(\mu=1\). The original Newton polynomials \[ e_k(C)= rac{\prod_{r<k}(c_r-C)} {\prod_{r=1}^k s_r^2},\qquad 0\le k<N, \] form a basis of the polynomials of degree less than \(N\). The ordinary source identity gives \[ \mathscr J_N[e_k(c_N(x))] =c_k e_k(c_N(x))-s_k^2e_{k-1}(c_N(x)), 	ag{11} \] where the last term is zero at \(k=0\). Evaluation on the \(N\) distinct points in section 1 is invertible. Since these evaluated polynomials are period one in \(x\), it conjugates \(J_1(x)\) to the triangular matrix in (11). Consequently \[ \det(wI-J_1(x))=P_N(w). 	ag{12} \] This is a characteristic-polynomial identity. In particular every double eigenvalue and the odd simple eigenvalue has its original multiplicity; vanishing at the distinct physical roots alone would not prove (12). For \(N\ge3\), the determinant expansion has only two terms with uncanceled winding across the cyclic boundary. The all-forward permutation contributes \((-1)^{N-1}\mu\prod_lA_l=-a_N\mu\), and the all-backward permutation contributes \(-a_N\mu^{-1}\), using (7). Every other permutation has winding zero, so its boundary factors cancel. This follows also by decomposing a permutation into cycles: a nearest-neighbor cycle with nonzero winding must traverse all \(N\) vertices. Comparing with \(\mu=1\) proves (10). At \(N=2\), the two shifted neighbors occupy the same matrix entry. The off-diagonal entries of \(wI-J_\mu\) are \[ A_0+B_0\mu^{-1},\qquad B_1+A_1\mu. \] Their product has the \(\mu\)-dependent part \(A_0A_1\mu+B_0B_1\mu^{-1}\). Since \(a_N=A_0A_1=B_0B_1\), subtracting its value at \(\mu=1\) again gives (10). \(\square\) ## 3. Exact monodromy and its branch information **Theorem.** For every \(N\ge2\), the period transfer satisfies \[  oxed{\qquad \det M_N(x,w)=1,\qquad \operatorname{tr}M_N(x,w) =2+P_N(w)\cot^2(\pi Nx). \qquad} 	ag{13} \] The assertion initially holds under (3) and then as a meromorphic identity in \(x,w\). *Proof.* The determinant in (4) is \(B_N/A_N\), so (7) gives the first assertion. A nonzero state with period multiplier \(\mu\) exists exactly when either \(M_N-\mu I\) or \(wI-J_\mu\) is singular: the recurrence and the two boundary conditions (9) identify their kernels. Multiplying (10) by \(\mu\) gives \[ \mu\det(wI-J_\mu) =-a_N\left[ \mu^2-\left(2+ rac{P_N(w)}{a_N}ight)\mu+1ight]. 	ag{14} \] For generic \(w\), this quadratic has distinct roots; they are the two roots of the monic characteristic polynomial of \(M_N\). The two monic quadratics therefore agree. Polynomial continuation in \(w\) includes the repeated-root cases, and (7) gives (13). All quantities are meromorphic, which gives the stated continuation in \(x\). \(\square\) If a homogeneous scalar is continued so that its recurrence and all the required shifted values are defined, Cayley--Hamilton gives \[  oxed{\quad F(x+1)+F(x-1) =\{2+P_N(w)\cot^2(\pi Nx)\}F(x). \quad} 	ag{15} \] Indeed \(Y_F(x+1)=M_N(x,w)Y_F(x)\), and period one of the coefficients gives \(Y_F(x-1)=M_N(x,w)^{-1}Y_F(x)\). Equation (15) is not an assertion that a function originally given on a smaller rectangle already has such a continuation. For the actual microscopic parameter \(w=2\cosh(\alpha/N)\), \[ P_N(w)=4\cosh^2(\alpha/2). 	ag{16} \] On either horizontal line \(|\operatorname{Im}x|=H>0\), uniformly in \(\operatorname{Re}x\) and bounded complex \(\alpha\), \[ \operatorname{tr}M_N(x,w) =-2\cosh\alpha+O_H(e^{-2\pi NH}). 	ag{17} \] Thus its two multipliers tend, as an unordered pair with multiplicity, to \(-e^\alpha,-e^{-\alpha}\). On parameter sets avoiding their collisions, individual locally labeled multipliers have the same exponential error as (17). At a collision only the multiset convergence is asserted here. There is also an exact elementary obstruction to an overly restrictive choice of continuation. If \(P_N(w)
e0\), a solution which is period one in \(x\) on a full generic orbit must vanish: (15) would give \(P_N(w)\cot^2(\pi Nx)F(x)=0\). Equivalently \(J_1(x)-w\) is invertible by (12). Consequently a nonzero homogeneous continuation cannot be a globally single-valued function of \(e^{2\pi ix}\) extending regularly around that whole orbit. A local branch on a buffered half-strip is not excluded. The same distinction applies to a proposed root-of-unity hypergeometric or factorial formula. At \(P_N(w)=0\), the trace in (13) is exactly two. This does not imply that \(M_N=I\); a nontrivial Jordan part may remain. The actual matrix and its Jordan data must be retained; the trace identity does not justify a semisimple replacement. ## 4. Actual source and remaining estimate The ordinary full kernel is not a homogeneous solution at generic microscopic \(w\). The pinned original source gives \[ (w-\mathscr J_N)K_N(c_N(x),w) = rac{\eta P_N(w)}{N^2}e_{N-1}(c_N(x)) = rac{P_N(w)P_N(c_N(x))} {N^4(c_N(x)-c_0)},\qquad \eta=(-1)^{N-1}. 	ag{18} \] The removable interpretation in (18) is the original polynomial one. On a physical bulk window the right side and its first normal vanish, but it cannot be deleted off that grid. The sharp Green budget in the second pinned source retains both the baseline's ordinary defect and its actual right boundary packet on every fractional grid. Equation (13) fixes a necessary period-transfer invariant of any exact homogeneous replacement. It does not determine which linear combination or periodic coefficient functions match the kernel's physical jets. Nor does it bound such coefficients on a tall rectangle, establish the sharp \(J_\delta\) comparison, or estimate the complementary original currents. No actual source coefficient, nonvanishing term, or filled-action estimate is inferred from (13)--(17). ## 5. Coverage and complete direct sources The ordinary Askey--Wilson recurrence, its polynomial triangular action, and the retained full-kernel forcing are prior results. The additional calculation here is its exact twisted cyclic determinant and full-period transfer trace, with both parity multiplicities and the \(N=2\) case retained. The following complete source texts were read at the pinned versions, and every directly used implication was checked: * [Original ordinary recurrence and kernel source](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_edge_kernel_difference_and_endpoint_bound.md), SHA256 5d0d07d4d97d82cca66e0e0c3bf2cecad8e5f58ef8329178278b297cf0d6c5da. * [Sharp truncation forcing and retained Green boundary packet](research_partial_endpoint_green_boundary_budget.md), SHA256 a1bbfaa8f64abca96d2b97078a9d87fbc60877b4f4791612b1e8e2d822be286e. Only written mathematics and source-text/hash reads were used. No mathematical program, numerical experiment, test, build, or compilation was run. Frozen notes and public manuscripts are unchanged.

title: An actual upper Euler column with a controlled complex resolvent chart
text:
# An actual upper Euler column with a controlled complex resolvent chart Private written proof, 18 November 2026. A diagonal change on the donor alone turns the actual top column of the finite Euler star into a finite resolvent of the original recipient raising matrix. The recipients keep their binomial metric, compact coherent kernels, and endpoint arrows. On every fixed compact recipient chart away from incidence, sufficiently large donor coordinate gives an actual holomorphic kernel with nonzero amplitude and relative error \(O(N^{-1})\). Every donor input and dual factor is explicit. In the opposite kernel, full turnover moves the remaining inverse-factorial coupon to the last head; it does not disappear against the first-head quotient. The result estimates an actual source factor, not the complete opposite kernel or a geometric relative cycle. The sole complete direct J is pinned below. It supplies the actual finite prefix, turnover, and compact source conventions. The column identity, metric estimate, all-power bounds, and interfaces are proved here. ## 1. Donor-only gauges and the literal upper column Fix \[ N\ge2,\quad d=N-1,\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad Q=q^2,\quad f_a=(Q;Q)_a,\quad x=-M/q. 	ag{1} \] There are one donor and \(r\ge1\) recipient heads at common meridian \(M
e0\). The quantum root is fixed. With the actual ordered recipient total \(F_{m r}(M)\), the original star is \[ S(M)=\sum_{n=0}^d rac{x^{-n}L_1^nF_{m r}(M)^n}{f_n}, \qquad F_{m r}(M)^N=0. 	ag{2} \] The donor shift \(L_1w_a=w_{a-1}\) has its bottom zero, and every recipient raising arrow has its physical top zero. On the donor only define \[ G w_a=f_aw_a,\quad Yw_a=Q^{a(a+1)/2}w_a,\quad D=YG^{-1}, \qquad \widetilde S=(D\otimes I)S(D^{-1}\otimes I). 	ag{3} \] No recipient factorial gauge is used. All \(f_a\), \(a<N\), are nonzero; \(Y\) is unitary in every diagonal occupation metric. Reflecting the finite root product gives \[  rac{f_d}{f_{d-n}}=(-1)^nQ^{-n(n+1)/2}f_n,\quad  rac{Y_{d-n}}{Y_d}=Q^{n(n+1)/2},\quad f_d=N,\quad Y_d=(-1)^d . 	ag{4} \] For the first identity replace \(1-Q^{N-j}=-Q^{-j}(1-Q^j)\), \(1\le j\le n\). Consequently, with \(i_av=w_a\otimes v\), \[  oxed{\quad \widetilde S(M)i_d=\sum_{n=0}^d i_{d-n}(-x^{-1}F_{m r}(M))^n . \quad}	ag{5} \] This is a whole finite-matrix identity for every \(M
e0\). Let \(v(\zeta)w_a=\zeta^a\), and set \[ \mathcal U_N(\zeta,M)= \sum_{n=0}^d(-x^{-1}F_{m r}(M)/\zeta)^n . 	ag{6} \] Then \[ (v(\zeta)\otimes I)\widetilde S i_d=\zeta^d\mathcal U_N, \qquad  oxed{\quad\mathcal U_N=(I+x^{-1}F_{m r}(M)/\zeta)^{-1}\quad} 	ag{7} \] for \(\zeta
e0\). Multiplication of the finite sum leaves \(I-(-x^{-1}F_{m r}/\zeta)^N=I\). The column \(\zeta^d\mathcal U_N\) remains a polynomial at \(\zeta=0\). No nilpotent finite matrix has been replaced by a non-nilpotent scalar. For an arbitrary donor row \(\ell\), the exact source interface is \[  oxed{\quad (\ell\otimes I)S i_d= rac{(-1)^d}{N} (\ell GY^{-1}\otimes I)\widetilde S i_d . \quad}	ag{8} \] Thus the evaluation row of (7) corresponds to the original row \(v(\zeta)D\), with its stated input scalar. An arbitrary exterior row is not silently replaced by it. The negative star has a companion column without the chirp. The inverse of (2) has coefficient \((-1)^nQ^{n(n-1)/2}/f_n\) in degree \(n\) of \(x^{-1}L_1F_{m r}\). Multiplication proves this: the degree-\(n>0\) coefficient is \(f_n^{-1}\sum_j{n rack j}_Q(-1)^jQ^{j(j-1)/2} =f_n^{-1}(1;Q)_n=0\), by the finite binomial product. Using (4), its donor-only \(G^{-1}S^{-1}G\) column is therefore \[ (v(\zeta)\otimes I)G_1^{-1}S(M)^{-1}G_1i_d =\zeta^d(I-Q^{-1}x^{-1}F_{m r}(M)/\zeta)^{-1}. 	ag{8a} \] Its original-row interface is \(\ell S^{-1}i_d=N^{-1}(\ell G_1) (G_1^{-1}S^{-1}G_1)i_d\). The inverse is the exact finite nilpotent sum, with no endpoint removal. The estimates below apply to it after replacing \(x^{-1}/\zeta\) by \(-Q^{-1}x^{-1}/\zeta\). ## 2. Recipient norm control in the original metric Use the original head metric \[ \|w_a\|^2= inom da^{-1}. 	ag{9} \] This is the metric in which J's binomial column \(c(z)_a= inom daz^a\) is dual to evaluation on the real compact coherent sphere. The literal raising matrix is \(Fw_a=(1-Q^{a+1})w_{a+1}\), \(a<d\), and \(Fw_d=0\). Its weighted shift norm is the maximum of \[ 2\sin\!\left( rac{\pi(a+1)}Night) \sqrt{ rac{a+1}{N-1-a}}. 	ag{10} \] Writing \(s=(a+1)/N\) and using \(\sin(\pi s)\le\pi(1-s)\) bounds (10) by \(2\pi\sqrt{s(1-s)}\le\pi\). Also \(\|K^{\pm1}\|=|M|^{\pm1}\), so the actual coproduct gives \[ \|F_{m r}(M)\|\le\pi\sum_{j=0}^{r-1}|M|^{-j}. 	ag{11} \] On a donor domain where \[ ho:= rac{|x|^{-1}}{|\zeta|} \pi\sum_{j=0}^{r-1}|M|^{-j}<1, 	ag{12} \] one therefore has \[ \|\mathcal U_N\|\le(1-ho)^{-1},\qquad \|\mathcal U_N^{-1}\|\le1+ho. 	ag{13} \] These are estimates in the unchanged recipient metric. They hold uniformly on a fixed meridian disk bounded away from zero, with fixed derivatives on smaller disks. In particular they hold on \(M=e^{u/N}\), \(|u|\le\eta\), at fixed \(r,\eta\), with a fixed strict donor margin. They do not estimate \(G\) or \(G^{-1}\). ## 3. All finite powers on a complex coherent chart For the recipients retain J's compact kernels \[ K_B(\mathbf w,\mathbf z)=v(\mathbf w)B c(\mathbf z),\quad B_N=\prod_{i=1}^r(1+w_i z_i)^d,\quad \sigma_N(B)=K_B/B_N. 	ag{14} \] All caps are finite. The normalized kernel is defined on \[ X^r,\qquad X=(\mathbb P^1	imes\mathbb P^1)\setminus\{1+wz=0\}. 	ag{15} \] Put \[ 	heta_i= rac{w_i z_i}{1+w_i z_i},\qquad h= rac{2\pi i}{N},\qquad \eta_N(	heta)=e^{dh	heta}, \] \[ b_{N,r}(M;\mathbf w,\mathbf z) =\sum_{j=1}^r x^{-(j-1)}w_j (1-Q\eta_N(	heta_j))\prod_{i<j}\eta_N(	heta_i). 	ag{16} \] This is holomorphic on \(X^r\). In particular the apparent factor \(w_j\) at infinity is removable because \(Q\eta_N(1)=1\) and \(w_j(1-	heta_j)=w_j/(1+w_jz_j)\) is regular there. Keeping \(d=N-1\) and the displayed \(Q\) prevents a false projective pole. For each \(\mathcal K\Subset X^r\) and fixed compact meridian disk \(\mathcal M\) bounded away from zero, there is \(C>1\), independent of \(N\), such that, for every \(1\le n<N\), \[  oxed{ egin{split} |\sigma_N(F_{m r}(M)^n)|&\le C^n,\ |\sigma_N(F_{m r}(M)^n)-b_{N,r}(M)^n| &\le C^n n^2/N . \end{split}}	ag{17} \] Each fixed coordinate or meridian derivative has the same form on smaller charts, after increasing the constants. Here is a proof including the finite endpoints. On output polynomials let \(T_i p(\mathbf w)=p(w_1,\ldots,Qw_i,\ldots,w_r)\). The literal matrices act as \[ F_i=w_i(1-QT_i),\qquad K_i^{-1}=x^{-1}T_i, \] and hence \[ F_{m r}=\sum_{j=1}^r x^{-(j-1)}w_j(1-QT_j)\prod_{i<j}T_i. 	ag{18} \] In particular \(F_iw_i^d=0\). An \(n\)-fold expansion has at most \((2r)^n\) words. Moving coordinate multiplications to the left turns each into \[ c(M)Q^\ell\mathbf w^{\mathbf s}T^{\mathbf k},\qquad |\mathbf s|=n,\quad 0\le k_i\le n,\quad |\ell|\le C_r n^2. 	ag{19} \] The coefficient mass is at most \(C^n\) uniformly on \(\mathcal M\). Retain the basic factors \(Q\) from \(1-QT_j\). Replacing only the extra ordering phase by one changes its coefficient by at most \(C^n n^2/N\), since \(|Q^\ell-1|\le2\pi|\ell|/N\). The exact normalized kernel of the remaining monomial is \[ \mathbf w^{\mathbf s} \prod_i\left( rac{1+Q^{k_i}w_i z_i}{1+w_i z_i}ight)^d. 	ag{20} \] Individual terms may have apparent upper-degree parts, but their complete finite sum has exactly the endpoint cancellations in (18). No expanded term is interpreted as an unrestricted physical shift. On an affine compact set away from incidence, \[ \left|\left( rac{1+Q^k v}{1+v}ight)^dight|\le e^{Ck}, \qquad 0\le k<N. 	ag{21} \] This follows from \(|Q^k-1|\le2\pi k/N\) and \(|1+(Q^k-1)v/(1+v)|^d\le e^{Ck}\). For \(k\le\sqrt N\), expansion of the logarithm at one gives \[ \left( rac{1+Q^k v}{1+v}ight)^d =e^{dhk\,v/(1+v)} +O(k^2e^{Ck}/N). 	ag{22} \] The finitely many small levels are absorbed by the constant. For \(k>\sqrt N\), (21) and the corresponding exponential bound prove (22) with a larger constant, since \(k^2/N>1\). Multiplying over the fixed number of heads gives an error \(C^n n^2/N\) when the shifts in (20) are replaced by \(\eta_N(	heta_i)^{k_i}\). After that replacement and removal of the extra ordering phases, the word expansion is precisely the commutative \(n\)-th power of (16). Summing proves (17) on affine compacts. Both sides of the difference are holomorphic on \(X^r\). Around an infinite coordinate choose a small projective polydisk avoiding incidence, with distinguished boundary in finite old coordinates. The affine estimates on that boundary and the maximum principle extend them through the polydisk. A finite cover proves (17) on arbitrary \(\mathcal K\Subset X^r\). Doing this on slightly larger charts and a larger meridian disk and applying Cauchy estimates proves the fixed-derivative statement. Only the original finite caps and exact shift words were used. ## 4. A genuine complex local unit Enlarge \(C\) in (17) to bound \(|b_{N,r}|\) too. Choose a donor domain with fixed \(\varrho<1\) satisfying \[ \sup_{M\in\mathcal M}|x|^{-1}C/|\zeta|\le\varrho. 	ag{23} \] Summing the exact finite resolvent gives \[  oxed{\quad \sigma_N(\mathcal U_N(\zeta,M)) = rac{1}{1+x^{-1}b_{N,r}(M;\mathbf w,\mathbf z)/\zeta} +O(N^{-1}). \quad}	ag{24} \] Indeed the error in (17) sums to \(N^{-1}\sum_{n\ge1}n^2\varrho^n\); the missing commutative geometric tail is bounded by \(\varrho^N/(1-\varrho)\). The same conclusion holds with every fixed derivative on smaller domains by Cauchy estimates. The leading factor has modulus at least \((1+\varrho)^{-1}\). Thus the actual normalized kernel is nonzero for sufficiently large \(N\), uniformly on smaller compact domains. In local branches the actual transformed upper-column kernel is \[  oxed{\quad \zeta^d\prod_i(1+w_i z_i)^d \left[ rac{1}{1+x^{-1}b_{N,r}/\zeta}+O(N^{-1})ight]. \quad}	ag{25} \] This phase and unit amplitude belong to an actual finite kernel, not to an interpolation of a discrete spectral label. The estimate is uniform on a fixed complex \(M\)-disk. Fixed meridian derivatives retain every \(x(M)\) factor and obey the same error on smaller disks; restricting to \(M=e^{u/N}\) is legitimate. Ordinary quantum-parameter normals are not obtained by differentiating the root identity \(F_{m r}^N=0\). ## 5. The retained interface in the opposite source For J's actual opposite kernel on \(m=r+1\) heads, use \(E_\Sigma^d\mathscr C_m=\mathscr C_mF_\Sigma(M^{-1})^d\) and \(F_\Sigma(M^{-1})^di_0=NS_m(M^{-1})i_d\). These give the exact form \[ T(M)=Nq_F(M)\mathscr C_m(M)S_m(M^{-1})i_d. 	ag{26} \] The upper star is therefore at the reflected meridian. Equation (8) gives the exact pairing \[ T(M)=(-1)^d q_F(M)\mathscr C_m(M) (GY^{-1})_1\widetilde S_m(M^{-1})i_d. 	ag{27} \] Full turnover reverses the heads. Moving the donor diagonal through it puts the reflected diagonal on the last head, not the first. The finite reflection identity in (4) gives \[ f_{d-b}Q^{-(d-b)(d-b+1)/2} =N(-1)^{d+b}/f_b. 	ag{28} \] The balanced turnover coefficient cancels in this diagonal conjugation, so the identity is valid in the whole meridian family. Writing \(Z_m w_b=(-1)^bw_b\) on the last head, \[ \mathscr C_m(GY^{-1})_1 =N(-1)^dZ_mG_m^{-1}\mathscr C_m, \] and hence \[  oxed{\quad T(M)=Nq_F(M)Z_mG_m^{-1}\mathscr C_m(M) \widetilde S_m(M^{-1})i_d. \quad}	ag{29} \] This is the original-source interface. The recipients in (24) have no hidden factorial gauge, but the complete paired source retains the specified last-head inverse-\(G\) coupon. It does not commute freely through \(q_F=p_0S_m^{-1}\). Neither its size nor its coherent generating function is estimated by (24). Every factor in (26)--(29), including \(N\), full balanced turnover and the first-head quotient, remains in J's compact source convolution. Its normalization \(D_N(MK_{m r})^{-1}\), Laurent rows, and first-meridian-jet assembly remain unchanged. An arbitrary exterior is paired through (8), (27), or (29); it is not replaced by the special evaluation row in (7). The theorem supplies a controlled upper-column factor with exact source interfaces. It does not bound the residual inverse-\(G\) coupon or prove that the resolved loxodromic frame satisfies (23) in the full pairing. No geometric occurrence, relative-window transport, or lower bound for the closed source is inferred. ## Complete proof direct * J: notes/research_opposite_polarization_source_kernel.md, SHA256 d52c6dd8e62f575a262fc7af460e258f7cb0e40b5a9c037ac46dd8d151002d44. title: The weighted centralizer current is not a matrix gauge derivation
text: # The weighted centralizer current is not a matrix gauge derivation Private written proof, 18 November 2026. The actual weighted Ward current has the required classical centralizer field. It is nevertheless not an inner derivation of the finite tensor matrix algebra. A local matrix-algebra splitting therefore does not turn this existing current into a change of basis. This statement concerns the specified lift; it does not rule out a different lift with additional terms. The sole complete proof source is W, the actual weighted Ward lift, pinned below. All finite calculations needed for this conclusion are given here. ## 1. The current and its part vanishing on the identity Use \(N\ge2\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\), \(\rho=q-q^{-1}\), and \(h=2\pi i/N\). On \(b\ge1\) actual heads retain W's ordered coproducts \[ \mathsf K=K_1K_{\rm t},\qquad \mathsf E=\mathcal E_1K_{\rm t}+\mathcal E_{\rm t}, \qquad \mathsf F=F_1+K_1^{-1}F_{\rm t}. \tag{1} \] The subscript \({\rm t}\) denotes the remaining tensor heads. For \(b=1\), set \(K_{\rm t}=1\) and \(\mathcal E_{\rm t}=F_{\rm t}=0\). In W's exact order the coefficients needed here are \[ A_E=K_1F_1\mathsf K^{-1},\qquad A_F=\mathcal E_1 . \tag{2} \] Keep its entire third coefficient \(A_K\); its explicit value will not enter the test. Write \[ \mathcal D(B)=h^{-1}\sum_{\iota=E,F,K}[X_\iota,A_\iota B], \qquad (X_E,X_F,X_K)=(\mathsf E,\mathsf F,\mathsf K). \tag{3} \] Removing its multiplication term gives \[ \delta(B):=\mathcal D(B)-\mathcal D(1)B =h^{-1}\sum_\iota A_\iota[X_\iota,B]. \tag{4} \] Thus \(\delta(1)=0\), as any derivation would require. Its exact product defect, however, is \[ \delta(BC)-\delta(B)C-B\delta(C) =h^{-1}\sum_\iota[A_\iota,B][X_\iota,C]. \tag{5} \] This follows by expanding the two commutators in (4). The defect may not be dropped merely because the principal commuting symbols have a vector-field interpretation. ## 2. A diagonal test at the original root head Evaluate (4) on \(\mathsf K\). The weight relations give \[ [\mathsf E,\mathsf K]=(1-Q)\mathsf E\mathsf K,\qquad [\mathsf F,\mathsf K]=(1-Q^{-1})\mathsf F\mathsf K. \] Since \(\mathsf K^{-1}\mathsf E\mathsf K=Q^{-1}\mathsf E\), substitution in (2)--(4) yields \[ \delta(\mathsf K)=\frac{1-Q^{-1}}h \bigl(\mathcal E_1\mathsf F\mathsf K -K_1F_1\mathsf E\bigr). \tag{6} \] Expanding (1), commuting only different tensor heads, and using \([\mathcal E_1,F_1]=\rho(K_1-K_1^{-1})\), gives \[ \delta(\mathsf K)=\frac{1-Q^{-1}}h \left[ \rho(K_1^2-1)K_{\rm t} +\mathcal E_1F_{\rm t}K_{\rm t} -K_1F_1\mathcal E_{\rm t} \right]. \tag{7} \] All these are identities of the actual finite matrices. In particular their zero endpoint arrows remain unchanged. In the original tensor weight basis the last two terms in (7) have zero diagonal: they change the first-head index. At complete color \(M=1\), \[ K_1w_a=-q^{-1}Q^{-a}w_a, \] so \[ \operatorname{diag}\delta(\mathsf K) =\frac{(1-Q^{-1})\rho}h (K_1^2-1)K_{\rm t} \ne0 . \tag{8} \] Indeed on the first-head index \(a=0\), \(K_1^2=Q^{-1}\ne1\), while \(K_{\rm t}\) is invertible. This proves (8) for every \(N\ge2\) and every width \(b\ge1\). Here \(\operatorname{diag}\) means taking matrix diagonal entries in this specified basis, not an invariant trace. For any finite matrix \(H\), the diagonal of \([H,\mathsf K]\) is zero in the same basis. Consequently \(\delta\) cannot have the form \[ \delta(B)=[H,B]. \tag{9} \] It is not any derivation of the full matrix algebra either. For completeness, every complex-linear derivation \(D\) of \(\operatorname{Mat}_n(\mathbb C)\) is inner: in matrix units set \(H=\sum_i D(E_{i1})E_{1i}\). Applying the product rule to \(E_{kl}E_{i1}\), then multiplying by \(E_{1i}\) and summing, gives \([H,E_{kl}]=D(E_{kl})\). The matrix units span the algebra, proving the assertion. ## 3. Consequence for a framing descent W proves that (3), with its full multiplication term and marked cut/pivot boundary, quantizes the principal field \(s\partial_r\) on the stated geometric chart. That sourced identity remains valid. Equations (5)--(8) show precisely why one cannot reinterpret it as an inner splitting change of the finite matrix algebra. A proposed replacement by such a change must supply a different finite derivation and compare its entire current, including the difference from (3), with the original source. Subtracting \(\mathcal D(1)B\) alone does not suffice. No relative framing period, contour coefficient or volume-conjecture lower bound follows from this calculation. ## Complete proof source * W: notes/research_actual_weighted_ward_centralizer_lift.md, SHA256 e689364ab8e756ef51f8da43a7ea86d84086afd6bf57ffbe0af1a4f508c2648a. The entire unchanged source was read in the author sequence, every used implication checked, and its matching pin renewed. The exact test was independently derived from its finite matrices. Only written mathematics and text/hash operations were used. Frozen and public files are unchanged.

title: A whole-interval upper rate for the original terminal Jordan pair
text:
# A whole-interval upper rate for the original terminal Jordan pair Private written proof, 16 November 2026. Polynomial initialization at finitely many original physical rows, crude propagation through short endpoint intervals, and the compact-interior transfer theorem give a whole-real-interval upper rate for every fixed signed terminal power. Both the terminal eigenvector and its original normal companion are included. This is an upper bound only, and does not control ordinary branching products. ## 1. Statement and original normalization Retain \[ q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad D=N-1,\quad \eta=(-1)^D,\quad \kappa=q^{D^2/2},\quad c_j=2\cos((2j+1)\pi/N), \] \[ P_N(Z)=2T_N(Z/2)+2,\qquad \mathcal A_N=\mathbb C[Z]/(P_N). \] The operators \(T,R,C,J,V_n,D_n\), the kernel \(K_N\), and the Frobenius functional \(\phi_N\) have their original normalizations. In particular \[ Te_j=e_{D-j},\quad e_j(Z)=S_j^{-2}\prod_{r<j}(c_r-Z),\quad S_j=\prod_{r=1}^j2\sin(r\pi/N),\quad \phi_N(e_i e_j)=\mathbf1_{i+j=D}, \] \[ C f=Zf\pmod {P_N},\quad J=TCT,\quad V_n=\kappa^nTR^{-n}T,\quad D_n=V_nCV_{-n}, \] \[ Q_0(Z)=\partial_wK_N(c_0,Z),\qquad G_n=T(R^{-n}),\qquad H_n=T(R^{-n}Q_0). 	ag{1} \] Every norm below is the norm of the ordinary canonical polynomial on \([-2,2]\), denoted \(\|\cdot\|_{\mathbb R}\). For fixed \(n
e0\), let \(	au_{\ell,n}(u)\), \(1\le\ell\le |n|\), be the distinct physical shift roots of the original terminal characteristic, each still of algebraic multiplicity two. The physical coordinate is \[ u=j/N,\qquad x=2\cos(2\pi u),\qquad 0<u<1/2. \] Define \[ L_n(u)=\max_\ell\log|	au_{\ell,n}(u)|,\qquad \mathcal I_n=\int_0^{1/2}L_n(u)\,du. 	ag{2} \] The integral is improper. The modulus-order theorem proves that it is finite and nonnegative. For \(|n|=1\), \(L_n=0\). For \(|n|\ge2\), it equals the logarithm of one globally labeled growing modulus \(ho_{1,|n|}\). The definition by the maximum is sufficient here. Put \(\mathcal I_0=0\). **Theorem 1.** For every fixed integer \(n\), \[  oxed{\quad \limsup_{N	o\infty} rac1N \log ig(\|G_n\|_{\mathbb R}+\|H_n\|_{\mathbb R} ig) \le \mathcal I_n . \quad} 	ag{3} \] For fixed \(n
e0\) and every sufficiently small fixed \(\epsilon>0\), a quantitative form is \[  egin{split} \|G_n\|_{\mathbb R}+\|H_n\|_{\mathbb R} \le{}& C_{n,\epsilon}N^{p_{n,\epsilon}} \exp\left\{ N\int_\epsilon^{1/2-\epsilon}L_n(u)\,du +N C_n\epsilon\log(e/\epsilon) +C_{n,\epsilon}\sqrt Night\}. \end{split} 	ag{4} \] Here \(C_n\) is independent of \(\epsilon\); the other constants may depend on the fixed interior interval. The two signs have the same integral, by the original signed characteristic conjugation. ## 2. Polynomial data at every fixed initial row We first prove the actual source initialization rather than assuming small initial data for an abstract recurrence. For a fixed nonnegative integer \(j\), put \[ F_j(w)=K_N(c_j,w),\qquad Q_j(w)=\partial_ZK_N(Z,w)|_{Z=c_j}. 	ag{5} \] **Lemma 2.** For every fixed integer \(M\), there are constants \(C_M,p_M\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(N\), \[ \max_{0\le j\le M}  ig(\|F_j\|_{\mathbb R}+\|Q_j\|_{\mathbb R} ig) \le C_MN^{p_M}. 	ag{6} \] Consequently, for every fixed \(n,M\), all the actual values and first spectral normals of \(G_n,H_n\) at these rows are polynomially bounded. *Proof.* The original kernel gives \(F_0=1\), while the full normal source gives \[ \|Q_0\|_{\mathbb R}\le N^4/4. 	ag{7} \] We record a simple bound on the endpoint forcing as well. The elementary sine product is \(S_D=N\), obtained by evaluating \((z^N-1)/(z-1)\) at \(z=1\). Thus \[ e_D(Z)= rac{\eta P_N(Z)}{N^2(Z-c_0)},\qquad \|e_D\|_{\mathbb R}\le1. 	ag{8} \] For the inequality use \(P_N(c_0)=0\) and \(\|P_N'\|_{\mathbb R}\le N^2\), the latter following from \(P_N'=N U_{N-1}(Z/2)\) and \(\|U_{N-1}\|_{[-1,1]}\le N\). Ordinary Markov inequalities give polynomial bounds for each fixed derivative of \(e_D\). Write \(c(r)=2\cos((2r+1)\pi/N)\), and retain the exact ordinary kernel equation in its first variable, \[ (w-\widetilde J_Z)K_N(Z,w) = rac{\eta P_N(w)}{N^2}e_D(Z), 	ag{9} \] \[ (\widetilde J f)(c(r)) =(c_0+A(r)+B(r))f(c(r)) -A(r)f(c(r+1))-B(r)f(c(r-1)), \] \[ A(r)= rac{s_{r+1}^4}{s_{2r+1}s_{2r+2}},\qquad B(r)= rac{s_r^4}{s_{2r}s_{2r+1}},\qquad s_r=2\sin(r\pi/N). 	ag{10} \] The removable first-row values are \(B(0)=B'(0)=0\). For each fixed \(0\le j\le M\), \(A(j)^{-1}\), all the other coefficients needed here, and their first index derivatives have polynomial bounds in \(N\). This follows directly from their finite sine quotients: all their nonzero small-index sines have size comparable to \(N^{-1}\). The removable \(B\) is simplified first. The physical values \(e_D(c_j)\) vanish. Solving (9) at row \(j\) therefore propagates \(F_{j+1}\) from \(F_j,F_{j-1}\) with polynomial coefficients on the real \(w\) interval. At \(j=0\) the previous value is absent. Starting with \(F_0=1\), finitely many such steps prove the value assertion in (6). Differentiate the ordinary index equation (9) before evaluating at the physical row. The unknown normal is \[ Y_j(w)=c'(j)Q_j(w). 	ag{11} \] It obeys the same homogeneous second-order row equation, with forcing from coefficient derivatives and the derivative of the literal right side of (9). This forcing is polynomially bounded in real \(w\): \(\|P_N\|_{\mathbb R}\le4\), (8) controls \(e_D'\), and all already obtained \(F_j\) and coefficients are polynomial. The first row again has no previous unknown, because \(B(0)=B'(0)=0\). Its initial datum is \(c'(0)Q_0\), controlled by (7). Finitely many steps give polynomial \(Y_j\); division by \(|c'(j)|\), whose inverse is polynomial at each fixed row, proves (6). For large \(N\) all these fixed rows are double physical nodes, so no ramified last-node normal is involved. Here are the exact initial trace formulas: \[  egin{split} G_n(c_j)&=\phi_N(R^{-n}F_j),& G_n'(c_j)&=\phi_N(R^{-n}Q_j),\ H_n(c_j)&=\phi_N(R^{-n}Q_0F_j),& H_n'(c_j)&=\phi_N(R^{-n}Q_0Q_j). \end{split} 	ag{12} \] They follow from \((Tf)(Z)=\phi_N(f\,K_N(Z,\cdot))\), with all products and product-rule normals inside the original trace. For any fixed integer \(n\), the original physical jets of \(R^{-n}\) have values of modulus one and angular first derivative bounded by \(|n|N/2\). This follows from the original signed crossing jets and the product rule in the full algebra. Equations (6)--(7), Markov's inequality, and the product rule therefore bound the complete physical data of each product in (12) by a polynomial in \(N\). The stable full-Hermite Fourier reconstruction gives a polynomial real norm for its canonical representative. This operation is on the traced variable; no quotient is imposed on a free exterior variable. For clarity, the trace itself also has polynomial norm. For a canonical polynomial \(p\), \[ \phi_N(p)=\eta N^2[Z^D]p,\qquad |\phi_N(p)|\le N^2\|p\|_{\mathbb R}. 	ag{13} \] The equality follows from \(\phi_N(e_j)=\mathbf1_{j=D}\) and the leading coefficient \(\eta/N^2\) in (8). For the inequality, the top Chebyshev coefficient has modulus at most \(2\|p\|_{\mathbb R}\), and \(T_D(Z/2)\) has leading coefficient \(1/2\). Applying (13) to the canonical products in (12) completes the proof. \(\square\) ## 3. Coarse propagation through both endpoint strips Fix \(n=\sigma m
e0\), \(m=|n|\), and put \[ J_N=\lfloor(N-1)/2floor. 	ag{14} \] Use the exact \(8m\)-dimensional value/normal system of the bulk-transfer theorem, with coordinate \(c_N(u)=2\cos(2\pi u+\pi/N)\). Its state is \[ \mathbb X_j=(X_j^G,Y_j^G,X_j^H,Y_j^H)^{\mathsf T}, \] \[ X_j^F=(F(c_{j-m}),\ldots,F(c_{j+m-1}))^{\mathsf T}, \quad Y_j^F=(c_N'((j-m)/N)F'(c_{j-m}),\ldots, c_N'((j+m-1)/N)F'(c_{j+m-1}))^{\mathsf T}. 	ag{15} \] There is no collision between the row kernel notation \(F_j\) in (5) and the placeholder \(F=G_n,H_n\) in (15). The exact equation is \[ \mathbb X_{j+1}=\mathbb A_N(j/N)\mathbb X_j,\qquad \mathbb A_N=  egin{pmatrix} \mathsf A_N&0&0&0\ \mathsf A_N'&\mathsf A_N&0&0\ \mathsf B_N&0&\mathsf A_N&0\ \mathsf B_N'&\mathsf B_N&\mathsf A_N'&\mathsf A_N \end{pmatrix}. 	ag{16} \] Primes are scaled-coordinate derivatives. Here \(\mathsf A_N\) is the order-\(2m\) physical companion matrix for \(D_n-c_0\); \(\mathsf B_N\) contains the literal forcing of \(H_n\) by \(G_n\). Their exact definitions, including the forcing column, are (15)--(18) of the bulk-transfer source. **Lemma 3.** For all sufficiently large \(N\) and all integers \[ m\le j\le J_N-m, 	ag{17} \] put \[ d_j=\min\{j-m+1,\ J_N-m-j+1\}\ge1. 	ag{18} \] There are constants \(C_n,B_n\), independent of \(j,N\), such that \[ \|\mathbb A_N(j/N)\| \le C_n(N/d_j)^{B_n}. 	ag{19} \] The equation (16), including its angular-normal rows, remains exact through the last row \(j=J_N-m\). That last step generates the value at \(J_N\). *Proof.* The ordinary operator expansion in the bulk source constructs \(D_n\) by finitely many products of the physical \(J\) row and spectral multiplication. In a coefficient of its \(2m\)-order row, every occurrence of \(A(r),B(r)\) has \[ j-m+1\le r\le j+m-1. 	ag{20} \] This follows inductively from the right-ordered recurrence for \(D_n\): a term of order \(k\) shifts the final \(J\) row by at most \(k\), where \(k\le m-1\). Thus \(r\ge d_j\) and \(J_N-r\ge d_j\). In particular \(1\le r\le J_N-1\); no singular next row is used. Every sine in a denominator in (10) is bounded below in modulus by \(c\,d_j/N\), uniformly in (17). For example, \(N-(2r+2)\ge2d_j\) at even \(N\), and \(N-(2r+2)\ge2d_j-1\ge d_j\) at odd \(N\). The other denominator arguments have at least the same endpoint distance up to an absolute factor. Also \(\sin((r+1)\pi/N)\ge c\,d_j/N\). Consequently \(A(r),B(r)\), their scaled-coordinate derivatives, and \(A(r)^{-1}\) are bounded by fixed powers of \(N/d_j\). Explicitly one can use \[ |A(r)|+|B(r)|\le C(N/d_j)^2,\qquad |A(r)^{-1}|\le C(N/d_j)^4. 	ag{21} \] Differentiating any sine factor in the coordinate \(u=r/N\) costs only an absolute constant in its numerator, and one extra inverse sine if it occurs in a denominator. Thus the same type of bound holds for all fixed coefficient derivatives needed in (16). The exact forward extreme coefficient is \[ b_{n,m,N}(j/N) =q^{-\sigma(2j+m+1)} \prod_{\ell=0}^{m-1}A(j+\ell). 	ag{22} \] Its inverse is bounded by \(C_n(N/d_j)^{4m}\). All other row coefficients are fixed finite sums of the products just bounded. Dividing by (22), and differentiating this quotient once, proves (19) for the companion and all four blocks in (16). The power \(B_n\) need not be optimized. No factor \(N^{B_n}\) independent of \(d_j\) is introduced. The original ordinary residual is a \(P_N\) multiple, and \(P_N(c_N(u))=4\sin^2(\pi Nu)\). Its value and first \(u\) derivative therefore vanish at all physical rows used here. This proves the same exact nodal-normal equation even at the last output. At odd \(N\), that output is the simple node \(c_{J_N}=-2\); its angular derivative is zero. Its value is retained, and no spectral normal at that simple node is asserted. At even \(N\), the last output is the last double node.
