All coefficient rows remain at most \(J_N-1\) by (20). \(\square\) Take \(0<\epsilon<1/16\), and define \[ \ell_N=\lceil\epsilon Nceil,\qquad r_N=J_N-\lceil\epsilon Nceil. 	ag{23} \] For sufficiently large \(N\), \(\ell_N\ge m\) and \(r_N\le J_N-m\). The initial state \(\mathbb X_m\) consists only of the fixed rows \(0,\ldots,2m-1\), and is polynomial by Lemma 2. On the left strip \(m\le j<\ell_N\), the first distance in (18) is the smaller one. On the right strip \(r_N\le j\le J_N-m\), the second one is the smaller one. Products of (19) on either strip are consequently bounded by \[ C_n^K\prod_{r=1}^K(N/r)^{B_n} \le \exp\{C_n K\log(eN/K)\}, 	ag{24} \] where \(K\le\epsilon N+O_n(1)\). Use \(K!\ge(K/e)^K\). Increasing constants to include the fixed discrepancy, the bound is \[ \exp\{N C_n\epsilon\log(e/\epsilon)+O_n(\log N)\}. 	ag{25} \] Constants in (25) are independent of \(\epsilon\). The same estimate bounds every partial endpoint product, after taking the coarse factors in (19) to be at least one. ## 4. Joining the estimates and recovering the ordinary polynomial For fixed \(\epsilon\), all rows from \(\ell_N\) through \(r_N\) lie in a compact physical interior interval. The full coupled bulk theorem gives, for every intermediate state, a polynomial factor times \[ \exp\left\{ N\int_{\ell_N/N}^{r_N/N}L_n(u)\,du +C_{n,\epsilon}\sqrt Night\}. 	ag{26} \] Here it is legitimate to use the integral over the entire bulk interval when bounding any prefix: \(L_n\ge0\). The original \(H_n\) forcing and both first normals are inside this transfer estimate, not estimated separately. Moving either endpoint of the integral by \(O(N^{-1})\) changes its exponent by \(O_{n,\epsilon}(1)\). Combine the polynomial initial state, (25) on both sides, and (26). This bounds every value and every scaled angular normal of \(G_n,H_n\) at all distinct physical nodes by the right side of (4), with possibly different constants and polynomial power. There is no missing final row: the last matrix is \(\mathbb A_N((J_N-m)/N)\), whose output state reaches the node \(J_N\). The stable full-Hermite reconstruction gives for every canonical polynomial \(p\) \[ \|p\|_{\mathbb R} \le (2N-1)\max_{m physical}|p| +2\max_{m angular}|\partial_t p(-2\cos t)|. 	ag{27} \] With \(t=\pi-2\pi u-\pi/N\), the angular derivative equals \(-1/(2\pi)\) times the scaled derivative in (15). The paired physical lifts have the required opposite angular derivatives; the odd simple node has derivative zero. Thus all data in (27) have just been bounded. This proves (4) for the ordinary real norm, including the full normal information of the original source. If desired, division by \(|c_N'(j/N)|\ge8\pi/N\) at a double physical node, or ordinary Markov after (27), costs only a polynomial. For fixed \(\epsilon\), divide the logarithm of (4) by \(N\) and take the upper limit. Then let \(\epsilon\) decrease to zero. The term \(\epsilon\log(e/\epsilon)\) tends to zero, and the characteristic integral converges by the modulus-order theorem. This proves (3) for \(n
e0\). The order of the limits matters: no uniform bulk estimate on a shrinking interval was assumed. For \(n=0\), \(D_0=C\) and \((C-c_0)G_0=0\), \((C-c_0)H_0=G_0\). At every other double physical node both values and first normals vanish, and at the odd simple node both values vanish. The only remaining physical jets are the fixed endpoint jets controlled by (12), with \(n=0,j=0\). Equation (27) therefore gives a polynomial bound also in this case, proving (3) with \(\mathcal I_0=0\). ## 5. Both original anchors with a polynomially bounded spectator **Corollary 4.** Fix an integer \(n\), and let \(p_N\) be any sequence of canonical polynomials with \(\|p_N\|_{\mathbb R}\le C N^a\), for fixed \(C,a\). Retain the actual coherent anchors \[ \mathcal A_{0,N}=\kappa^n\phi_N(G_n p_N),\qquad \mathcal A_{1,N}=\kappa^n\phi_N(H_n p_N). 	ag{28} \] Then \[  oxed{\quad \limsup_{N	o\infty} rac1N \log(1+|\mathcal A_{0,N}|+|\mathcal A_{1,N}|) \le\mathcal I_n . \quad} 	ag{29} \] In particular this supplies an upper budget for both branching anchors whenever the surviving coupon has the stated polynomial ordinary real norm. *Proof.* For any two canonical polynomials \(F,p\), the physical values of their product are bounded by \(\|F\|_{\mathbb R}\|p\|_{\mathbb R}\). Markov's inequality and the full product rule bound its angular first derivatives by \(C N^2\|F\|_{\mathbb R}\|p\|_{\mathbb R}\). Applying (27) to the canonical representative of this product therefore gives, with a deliberately coarse power, \[ \|\operatorname{can}(Fp)\|_{\mathbb R} \le C N^3\|F\|_{\mathbb R}\|p\|_{\mathbb R}. 	ag{30} \] The first-normal terms are part of this estimate; values alone would not justify the canonical multiplication. Now (13), \(|\kappa^n|=1\), and (30) give the exact trace upper estimate \[ |\mathcal A_{0,N}|+|\mathcal A_{1,N}| \le C N^5\|p_N\|_{\mathbb R} (\|G_n\|_{\mathbb R}+\|H_n\|_{\mathbb R}). 	ag{31} \] Use Theorem 1 and \(\mathcal I_n\ge0\) to obtain (29). No signs or normal channels in the original traces were replaced; only their absolute size is bounded here. \(\square\) This corollary assumes the ordinary polynomial norm of the actual spectator. It does not prove such a bound for an arbitrary turned product, and does not estimate the mixed forcing after a turn. The second anchor uses \(H_n=T(R^{-n}Q_0)\) exactly; it is not obtained by substituting \(V_nQ_0\). No lower bound is asserted. ## 6. Scope and direct sources This theorem closes the physical endpoint initialization and whole-interval upper propagation for the specified terminal pair \(G_n,H_n\). It does not show that a maximal-modulus characteristic has nonzero coefficient in either polynomial. No lower bound or equality of rates follows. It does not compare \(\mathcal I_n\) with a filled geometric action, control an ordinary product after branching, or identify a relative-cycle coefficient. All original crossing phases and normal traces were retained in (12) and the exact system (16). The three complete direct sources were read at their unchanged pins, and their used implications and hashes checked: * [Exact terminal bulk transfer](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_terminal_twist_bulk_transfer_bound.md), SHA256 fca96865315f21dc9961be89061cc6c3a292b2b563e7ded756e86c3438ef5bde: signed extreme coefficients, canonical residual, exact value/normal system, and integrated maximum-root bound. * [Global terminal modulus ordering](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_terminal_twist_global_modulus_order.md), SHA256 79f26184f1ea0a4d45bb9961397175fc1fa6bad332482edd681a85156a6eae3a: nonnegative maximum logarithmic modulus, both signs, and integrability at both physical endpoints. * [Original full endpoint and normal propagation](research_full_endpoint_unit_turn_polynomial_bound.md), SHA256 329ee59c992c359c42775f564f540ffeee7f142bf51b5132913bf4cf2a859d35: original kernel equation, removable first row, \(Q_0\) real-norm bound, crossing full jets, and stable full-Hermite reconstruction including the odd simple node. The fixed-row initialization, endpoint-strip estimates, and limiting assembly are proved above. Only written mathematics, source text and hashes were used. No mathematical program, numerical experiment, test, or build was run. Frozen notes and public manuscripts are unchanged.

title: The zero-charge transition of the original low Newton source
text: # The zero-charge transition of the original low Newton source Private written proof, 16 November 2026. The original all-low zero-power source has a uniform nonzero formula down to the first nonzero lattice charge. Its endpoint prefactor is the product of the charges. This comes from the antisymmetric Fourier differences in the full Hermite trace, not from replacing those differences by Fourier coefficients. The proof also allows some charges to stay in the interior while others tend to zero. The archived regular low-source theorem gives the local edge symbol and the interior Gaussian. The additional points here are compact control on partially zero-charge faces, a fixed gap for higher aliases without a positive lower bound on the heights, and analytic division of the principal Fourier remainder. The interpolants used for the last step agree with the actual source only on its lattice; they do not assert an off-lattice cosine initializer. ## 1. Source, uniform formula, and endpoint coefficient Keep a fixed finite tree and a nonempty connected proper selected set \(S\), with every original selected degree \(d_v\ge3\). Every selected crossing power is zero. Include every incident edge once, and write \[ k=|S|,\qquad e=|E_S|,\qquad b=|\partial S|, \qquad p=\frac{3(b-1)}2,\qquad e=k-1+b. \tag{1} \] Every outside incidence remains an ordinary independent spectral variable \(z_w=-2\cos u_w\). No reduction is made there. Use the original Newton polynomials and full closing functional \[ e_a(z)=S_a^{-2}\prod_{j<a}(c_j-z),\quad S_a=\prod_{j=1}^a2\sin(\pi j/N),\quad c_j=2\cos((2j+1)\pi/N), \] \[ D=N-1,\quad \eta=(-1)^D,\quad P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2,\quad \phi_N(f)=\eta N^2[z^D]\operatorname{rem}_{P_N}f. \tag{2} \] All repeated-root first normals are retained. Put \[ K_N^{\rm low}(t,u)=\sum_{2a<N}e_a(-2\cos t)e_a(-2\cos u), \qquad F_N(\mathbf t;\mathbf u)=\prod_{vw\in E_S}K_N^{\rm low}(t_v,t_w). \tag{3} \] For \(\chi_v=J_v/N\), \(1\le J_v\le N\), the actual coupon is \(\mathcal C_{N,\chi_v}=T_{N-J_v}(-z_v/2)\). Define \[ Z_N^{\rm low}(\boldsymbol\chi;\mathbf u)= \left(\prod_{v\in S}\phi_N^{(v)}\right) \left[F_N\prod_{v\in S}\mathcal C_{N,\chi_v}\right]. \tag{4} \] Fix \(0<c_*<1\). Let \(\mathbf H(\boldsymbol\chi)\) minimize \[ M(\boldsymbol\chi)=\min_{\mathbf H\ge0} \left\{\sum_{vw\in E_S}V(H_v,H_w) -\sum_{v\in S}\chi_vH_v\right\},\qquad H_w=0 \quad(w\notin S), \tag{5} \] where, with continuous endpoint values, \[ J(x)=\int_0^x\log(2\sin\pi s)\,ds, \quad B(x,h)=\int_0^x\log(2\cos2\pi s+2\cosh h)\,ds-2J(x), \] \[ V(h,g)=\max_{0\le x\le1/2}\{B(x,h)+B(x,g)\}, \qquad V(0,0)=M_\infty=4G/\pi. \tag{6} \] All complete-edge constants in (5) are retained. **Theorem 1.** On the closed charge cube \([0,c_*]^S\), the minimizer in (5) is unique, all edges are regular, and the minimizing configuration has a uniform regular neighborhood. There are a fixed complex boundary polydisk \(U\) about \(\mathbf u=0\), a critical action \(W(\boldsymbol\chi,\mathbf u)\), and a nonvanishing coefficient \(\beta(\boldsymbol\chi,\mathbf u)\), locally holomorphic in charges across every face of that cube, such that \[ W(\boldsymbol\chi,\mathbf0)=M(\boldsymbol\chi),\qquad \beta(\boldsymbol\chi,\mathbf0)>0, \tag{7} \] and, uniformly at both parities and at every nonzero lattice tuple \(1\le J_v\le c_*N\), \[ \boxed{\quad Z_N^{\rm low}(\boldsymbol\chi;\mathbf u) =N^{-p}\left(\prod_v\chi_v\right) e^{NW(\boldsymbol\chi,\mathbf u)} \bigl(\beta(\boldsymbol\chi,\mathbf u)+O_{\rm hol}(N^{-1})\bigr). \quad} \tag{8} \] Here the error is holomorphic in the ordinary boundary variables, uniform on a slightly larger polydisk than the one on which fixed derivatives are taken. Thus (8) is a uniform relative estimate after shrinking \(U\), and includes every fixed ordinary spectral boundary derivative. No assertion is made that the error is the restriction of one common off-lattice charged-source remainder. At the completely zero charge corner, \[ \beta(\mathbf0,\mathbf0) =(2\pi)^k4^{-e}\prod_{v\in S}d_v^{-3/2}. \tag{9} \] Consequently, for each fixed \(C<\infty\), uniformly for \(1\le J_v\le C\sqrt N\), \[ Z_N^{\rm low}(\mathbf J/N;\mathbf0) =N^{-p-k}\left(\prod_vJ_v\right) (2\pi)^k4^{-e}\prod_vd_v^{-3/2} \exp\left\{NeM_\infty-\frac\pi N\sum_v\frac{J_v^2}{d_v}\right\} (1+O_C(N^{-1})). \tag{10} \] This is the central Gaussian transition, with its original trace normalization. In particular it includes every fixed positive integer tuple \(\mathbf J\). ## 2. Geometry on all partially zero faces The convex potential source proves continuity and convexity of \(V\), its regular positive Hessian, and \(V(h,g)\ge(h+g)/2\). Thus the functional in (5) is uniformly coercive on the closed cube: \[ \mathcal L_{\boldsymbol\chi}(\mathbf H) \ge\sum_v(d_v/2-\chi_v)H_v \ge(3/2-c_*)\sum_vH_v. \tag{11} \] If \(\chi_v=0\), a minimum has \(H_v=0\): every incident potential is strictly increasing in its own positive height, whereas there is no linear reward at that coordinate. The remaining positive coordinates separate into selected components with the zero-height vertices treated as complete ends. Their original degrees are unchanged. The charge-cube theorem applies to each such component. Its only exceptional saturated component requires two charges equal to one, which is excluded by \(c_*<1\). Therefore every edge is regular, including edges between two zero-height vertices. The minimizer is unique: the positive components have their unique minima, and the other heights have just been forced to zero. Uniform coercivity and uniqueness imply continuity on the closed cube by the convergent-subsequence argument for minimizers. Compactness now gives a uniform strict regularity margin and uniform interior wire indices \(0<x_e<1/2\). On this compact regular set the edge potential extends analytically and evenly in each signed height. Its Hessian is positive definite after assembly, including at zero heights. The analytic implicit function theorem therefore gives the continued minimizing branch near every charge vector on the closed cube. The branches agree on their real overlaps and hence on sufficiently small complex overlaps. Reflection of one charge changes the sign of its own height and leaves the other heights unchanged. In particular \[ H_v=0\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \chi_v=0, \qquad H_v/\chi_v\text{ extends to a positive analytic unit.} \tag{12} \] For the last assertion at a zero coordinate, the off-diagonal entries in its Hessian row vanish by separate evenness. Its positive diagonal entry gives \(\partial H_v/\partial\chi_v>0\). Let \(\psi(t,u)\) and \(a_e(t,u)\) be the actual regular low-edge phase and density, calibrated positively at imaginary angles as in the regular low-source theorem. Define \[ \mathcal F(\mathbf t;\boldsymbol\chi,\mathbf u) =\sum_e\psi(t_v,t_w)-i\sum_v\chi_vt_v. \tag{13} \] Its critical point \(\mathbf t(\boldsymbol\chi,\mathbf u)\) continues \(-i\mathbf H\); put \(W=\mathcal F(\mathbf t;\cdot)\) and \(K=-\mathcal F_{\mathbf t\mathbf t}\) there. The square root of \(\det K\) continues its positive value at real charges and complete outside angles. Separate evenness shows that \(W\) is even in a charge reflected across a zero face, and that \(\sin t_v/\chi_v\) extends holomorphically. The coefficient in (8) is \[ \beta(\boldsymbol\chi,\mathbf u) =\left(\frac{i}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\right)^k \frac{\displaystyle\prod_v\frac{\sin t_v}{\chi_v} \prod_e a_e(t_v,t_w)}{\sqrt{\det K}}. \tag{14} \] It is positive on the real closed charge cube at \(\mathbf u=0\). Compactness permits one common smaller \(U\) on which it is a unit. ## 3. Exact principal Fourier block and the other aliases Write \(F_N=\sum_{\mathbf r}a_{N,\mathbf r}e^{i\mathbf r\cdot\mathbf t}\). The coefficients are separately symmetric; at complete outside angles they are nonnegative. For real outside angles their absolute values have the coefficientwise majorant at complete outside angles. Define the tensor antisymmetric difference \[ \Delta_{\mathbf q}a_N =\sum_{\boldsymbol\epsilon\in\{-1,1\}^S} \left(\prod_v(-\epsilon_v)\right) a_{N,\mathbf q+\boldsymbol\epsilon}. \tag{15} \] The exact charged full-normal identity from the half-charge note is the tensor product of \[ \phi_N(f\mathcal C_{N,J/N}) =\frac{N^2}{2}\sum_{\ell\ge1}\ell\eta^{\ell+1} \left[ a_{(\ell-1)N+J-1}-a_{(\ell-1)N+J+1} +a_{(\ell+1)N-J-1}-a_{(\ell+1)N-J+1}\right]. \tag{16} \] It includes the original normal multiplier \(\ell N\), the odd simple node, and the parity signs. The principal block is exactly \[ \mathcal P_N(\boldsymbol\chi;\mathbf u) =(N^2/2)^k\Delta_{\mathbf J}a_N. \tag{17} \] Every other block has effective nonnegative charges \(\lambda_v=(\ell_v-1)+\chi_v\) or \(\lambda_v=(\ell_v+1)-\chi_v\). They satisfy \(\boldsymbol\lambda\ge\boldsymbol\chi\), with at least one excess at least \[ a_*:=\min(1,2-2c_*)>0. \tag{18} \] Only a bounded number of these blocks can occur: the Laurent degree at \(v\) is at most \(d_v(N-1)/2\), so their \(\ell_v\)'s are bounded in terms of the fixed original degrees, independently of \(N\). Here is a uniform bound even when some minimizing heights vanish. For any nonnegative \(\mathbf h\), coefficient positivity gives \[ |\Delta_{N\boldsymbol\lambda}a_N(\mathbf u)| \le\prod_v2\cosh h_v\, e^{-N\boldsymbol\lambda\cdot\mathbf h} F_N(-i\mathbf h;\mathbf0) \quad(\mathbf u\text{ real}). \tag{19} \] The uniform endpoint factorial estimate in the half-charge note gives \[ F_N(-i\mathbf h;\mathbf0) \le C N^A\exp\left(N\sum_eV(h_v,h_w)\right) \tag{20} \] on every bounded nonnegative height box, including height zero. Choose a coordinate \(v\) with \(\lambda_v-\chi_v\ge a_*\). The compact regularity from Section 2 allows a fixed \(\epsilon>0\) such that \(\mathbf H(\boldsymbol\chi)+\epsilon\mathbf e_v\) remains in a regular bounded neighborhood for all charges in the closed cube. If \(L\) bounds the height Hessians there, stationarity gives \[ \mathcal L_{\boldsymbol\chi}(\mathbf H+\epsilon\mathbf e_v) \le M(\boldsymbol\chi)+L\epsilon^2/2. \] Since all heights and all excess charges are nonnegative, \[ \mathcal L_{\boldsymbol\lambda}(\mathbf H+\epsilon\mathbf e_v) \le M(\boldsymbol\chi)+L\epsilon^2/2-a_*\epsilon \le M(\boldsymbol\chi)-\delta \tag{21} \] after fixing a sufficiently small \(\epsilon\), with \(\delta>0\). Equations (16)--(21) prove \[ |Z_N^{\rm low}-\mathcal P_N| \le C N^A e^{N(M(\boldsymbol\chi)-\delta)} \tag{22} \] on the real outside torus, uniformly on the whole nonzero lattice cube. Polynomial continuation preserves a smaller gap on a fixed complex boundary polydisk: each boundary degree is less than \(N\), so its cost is a polynomial times \(e^{N\sum|\Im u_e|}\). Continuity of \(W\) preserves the relative gap after that polydisk is shrunk. No small-height geometric-series denominator is used. ## 4. Fixed face contours and division of the vanishing amplitude Fix a base charge vector \(\boldsymbol\chi^0\) in the closed cube, and let \(A=\{v:\chi_v^0=0\}\). Keep the product contours \[ C_v^0=[-\pi,\pi]-iH_v(\boldsymbol\chi^0) \tag{23} \] fixed while varying the charges near that base. In particular the contours for \(v\in A\) are real. Define the holomorphic interpolant \[ \mathcal P_N^0(\boldsymbol\chi;\mathbf u) =\left(\frac{iN^2}{2\pi}\right)^k \int_{\prod C_v^0} \prod_v\sin t_v\,F_N(\mathbf t;\mathbf u) e^{-iN\boldsymbol\chi\cdot\mathbf t}\,d\mathbf t. \tag{24} \] At integer \(N\boldsymbol\chi\), separate periodicity and Cauchy's theorem give (17) exactly. Away from those integers it is the stated fixed-contour interpolation, not the original cosine trace. For each \(v\in A\), reflection of its real integration interval shows that \(\mathcal P_N^0\) is exactly odd in \(\chi_v\). For completeness, all estimates used to deform (24) are uniform through a zero height. At the base, every real wire maximum is strict and in \((0,1/2)\). Choose compact index intervals around the maximizing indices. The complement has a fixed index-phase gap by strict concavity and compactness, using (20). On the retained indices, the local exact factorial expansion is \[ e_a(-2\cos t)e_a(-2\cos u) =\frac{e^{NQ(x;t,u)}}{4N^2\sin^2\pi x}(1+O_{\rm hol}(N^{-1})), \quad Q=b(x,t)+b(x,u),\quad x=a/N, \tag{25} \] where \(b(x,t)=\int_0^x\log(2\cos2\pi s+2\cos t)\,ds-2J(x)\) uses the branch positive at the imaginary base angles. The exact index cotangent contour gives \[ K_{N,I_e}(t,u)=N^{-3/2}a_e(t,u)e^{N\psi(t,u)} (1+O_{\rm hol}(N^{-1})), \qquad a_e=\frac{\sqrt{2\pi}}{4\sin^2(\pi x_e)\sqrt{-Q_{xx}(x_e)}}. \tag{26} \] These are the actual symbols of the pinned regular low-source proof. Their factorial arguments have a fixed bulk margin even when either angle is zero. The real angular tail estimate also remains uniform for bounded heights including zero. For a compact index interval \(I\), the root-product proof gives \[ |e_a(-2\cos(\tau-ih))| \le C N^A e_a(-2\cosh h) e^{-cN(1-\cos\tau)}, \qquad a/N\in I,\quad 0\le h\le H_*. \tag{27} \] One can see the endpoint uniformity directly in that proof: compare the midpoint sum of \(\log|1+e^{h+is}|\) with its integral. Remove the mesh intervals nearest its possible zero at \(h=0\); the upper error there is \(O(\log N)\), and the remaining variation has the same bound uniformly in \(h\). At a vanishing product the upper bound is automatic. The integrated derivative inequality has the uniform positive coefficient \(\min_{x\in I}\sin(2\pi x)/(2\pi(\cosh H_*+1))\). Thus the only angular maximum at the base is \(\Re\mathbf t=0\), and the endpoints of every interval (23) have a fixed strict gap. For sufficiently small complex changes of charges and outside variables, deform only a small neighborhood of that maximum through its continued saddle. Endpoint connectors require only a small motion from the fixed base contours; their existing gaps persist. The discarded index and angular pieces also retain their gaps: on the fixed compact contours the change of the charge exponential costs at most \(e^{CN|\boldsymbol\chi-\boldsymbol\chi^0|}\), and ordinary boundary polynomial continuation has the analogous cost. No deformation from a real full circle to a distant height at a nonlattice charge is invoked. The selected angular Hessian is the negative of the positive height Hessian at the base. The analytic Gaussian calculation in (24)--(26) therefore gives, on a fixed complex neighborhood, \[ N^p e^{-NW}\mathcal P_N^0 =A_0(\boldsymbol\chi,\mathbf u)+R_N(\boldsymbol\chi,\mathbf u), \qquad |R_N|\le C/N, \tag{28} \] where \(A_0=(\prod_v\chi_v)\beta\) with (14). The power of \(N\) is \(2k-3e/2-k/2=-p\). This is an additive Gaussian expansion; it does not assume that the amplitude is nonzero at a zero charge. Both sides of (28) are odd in every \(\chi_v\), \(v\in A\): the integral has that exact parity, \(W\) is even, and \(A_0\) is odd. Hence \(R_N\) is divisible by \(\prod_{v\in A}\chi_v\). Cauchy's estimate on a slightly larger complex polydisk gives \[ \left|\frac{R_N}{\prod_{v\in A}\chi_v}\right|\le C'/N \tag{29} \] on a smaller one, including its coordinate hyperplanes. For example, divide successively using the integral of the first derivative on the segment from zero to the given coordinate. The coordinates not in \(A\) are bounded away from zero on this patch, so (29) yields division by their factors as well. This proves the required uniform relative principal estimate locally. A finite collection of these face-centered and interior patches covers the closed cube. Their interpolants need not agree away from the lattice; at its points each equals the same principal Fourier block. Taking the finite minimum of their boundary radii and the finite maximum of their error constants proves the uniform principal formula everywhere on the nonzero lattice cube. Finally \(\prod_v\chi_v\ge N^{-k}\), so the alias error (22), divided by that prefactor, is still exponentially smaller. This proves (8). Separate evenness in every outside angle holds for the exact source, the critical action, and all the displayed coefficients and errors. An even holomorphic function of \(u_e\) descends holomorphically to \(z_e=-2\cos u_e\) near \(-2\). Cauchy's estimate on a smaller spectral polydisk therefore proves the ordinary derivative assertion in Theorem 1, including the angular ramification at completeness. ## 5. The transition and its quantitative scope At \(\boldsymbol\chi=\mathbf0\), every height is zero, every wire maximum is \(x_e=1/4\), and direct differentiation of (25) gives \[ Q_{xx}=-8\pi,\quad a_e=1/4,\quad K=\operatorname{diag}(d_v/(2\pi)),\quad H_v/\chi_v=2\pi/d_v. \tag{30} \] Substitution in (14) proves (9). Since \(\partial_{\chi_v}M=-H_v\) and \(M\) is separately even, \[ M(\boldsymbol\chi)=eM_\infty -\pi\sum_v\chi_v^2/d_v+O(|\boldsymbol\chi|^4), \qquad \beta(\boldsymbol\chi,\mathbf0)=\beta(\mathbf0,\mathbf0) (1+O(|\boldsymbol\chi|^2)). \tag{31} \] Equations (8) and (31) give (10), including its uniform error on the stated \(\sqrt N\) scale. For mixed faces, (8) instead retains the exact action of the remaining interior charges and the analytic coefficient (14); no simultaneous smallness of those charges is needed. The nonzero lattice qualification is essential. At \(J_v=0\) the principal difference in that coordinate is exactly zero. Moreover \(\mathcal C_{N,0}=\eta\,1\) in the full physical algebra: its values are \(\eta\) and all double-node normals vanish. Thus the actual zero-charge trace in that coordinate is \(\eta\) times the uncharged trace, supplied by the remaining aliases. Formula (8) is not asserted at that exact endpoint for the full low source. On the whole nonzero lower half-charge block, combine (8) with the adopted uniform high-sector gap to obtain the same formula for the full original zero-power source, with unchanged coefficient and ordinary boundary derivatives. On larger charge sets this additional step requires the corresponding actual high-sector estimate; none is inferred from the low calculation alone. The quantitative error proved here is relative \(O(N^{-1})\), with the explicitly retained factor \(\prod\chi_v\). Repeating the local factorial and Gaussian expansions to any fixed order and the same odd division gives the corresponding fixed-order version whenever those fixed-order symbols are retained. No uniform optimal-truncation or exponentially accurate sampling theorem is claimed. In particular, this relative estimate alone does not meet an exponentially amplified finite-reconstruction error budget. Nor does it supply a common off-lattice complex-charge initializer, a heat-path coverage theorem, or a nonzero coefficient after arbitrary further fillings. ## Direct sources and author readback The complete proof and directly used implications are read before the final version is frozen. Only written mathematics, text reads, and file hashes are used; no mathematical programs or numerical tests are run. * [Charge-cube positivity](research_zero_power_charge_cube_positivity.md), SHA256 91b0a03a677c9139bbfd04f9ef6b06b23e6c3fab435c1a974a2d243189925faf: regular positive components and the unique exceptional unit corner. Section 2 above supplies the additional compact partially zero-face conclusion instead of assuming it from that source. * [Convex height potential](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_zero_power_subtree_convex_potential.md), SHA256 c0ab73c2869ed3db7a0152634cbf3a315c573eed2f5fc99e437dacadcceb8eb8: coercivity, regular edge Hessians, edge maxima and phase calibration. * [Regular low source](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_regular_zero_subtree_low_source.md), SHA256 06e4b7c14e3a61616dea61642103e2d2803709fcd465ae9860258119db3299d1: exact local edge density, cotangent comparison, angular decrease, original trace normalization and holomorphic Gaussian proof. * [Lower half-charge source](research_zero_power_half_charge_high_gap.md), SHA256 fb2ffd3cfe32848d490bc866c70fb96505760cbe48344981a97c5abce131a0cd: exact charged Fourier differences, uniform bounded-height factorial estimate, and the separate whole-grid high-sector gap.

title: Positive geometry on the zero-power charge cube
text:
# Positive geometry on the zero-power charge cube Private written proof, 16 November 2026. For a connected zero-power selected tree with original degrees at least three, the original positive primitive solution exists on the entire charge cube \(0<c_v\le1\), except at the upper corner of the selected trivalent pair. In particular a supplied positive unit-charge endpoint is joined to completeness by its positive radial charge branch. This sharpens the sufficient degree condition in the archived convex height potential. The zero-power knot family was already treated by the separate Newton and Conway constructions; no new quantum asymptotic or knot family is asserted here. ## 1. Original data and statement Let \(T\) be a finite original circle tree and let \(S
e\varnothing\) be a connected proper set of vertices. Write \(d_v\) for the degree of \(v\) in \(T\), including its edges to the outside. Include every edge incident to \(S\) once, put every outside angle equal to zero, and set every selected original crossing power equal to zero. Keep the original complete branches and primitive equations \[ \sum_{e=vw}r_{v,e}(\mathbf t)=-\pi i c_v,\qquad r_{v,e}=\operatorname{arsinh}  igl(	an(t_v/2)\cos(t_w/2) igr),\qquad 0<c_v\le1. 	ag{1} \] The sum uses the original incidences. Positivity means that all eight tetrahedra of each included original edge block have positive imaginary shapes on the branch from completeness, not positivity after replacing the subdivision. **Theorem 1.** Suppose \(d_v\ge3\) for every \(v\in S\). 1. For every charge vector in \((0,1]^S\), (1) has exactly one positive solution, except when \(S\) consists of two adjacent vertices of original degree three and both charges equal one. Every existing solution has \(t_v=-iH_v\), \(H_v>0\), and is locally holomorphic in the full complex charge vector. 2. The positive configurations depend continuously on the charges and stay in a compact subset of the original positive domain on every compact subset of the cube avoiding the exception. For each fixed charge vector \(\mathbf c^0\) at which the solution exists, the entire radial path \(\mathbf c=\lambda\mathbf c^0\), \(0\le\lambda\le1\), is positive and analytic, including its complete endpoint. 3. At the exceptional pair's upper corner the unique limiting heights are \[ H_v=H_w=2\operatorname{arsinh}1. 	ag{2} \] The internal edge has \(q=0\), its two selected return angles are \(-\pi/2\), and the four outside edges remain positive. There is no positive solution at that corner. Thus the exact unit-charge criterion for an arbitrary connected proper all-zero selected subtree is \[  oxed{\quad d_v\ge3	ext{ at every selected vertex, and } S	ext{ is not a selected trivalent pair}.\quad} 	ag{3} \] The pair has its other four original edges to complete outside vertices. There is no bound on the size of \(S\). ## 2. The charge-scaled height minimum Use the original height potential from the first pinned source: \[  egin{split} J(x)&=\int_0^x\log(2\sin\pi s)\,ds,\ B(x,h)&=\int_0^x\log(2\cos2\pi s+2\cosh h)\,ds-2J(x),\ V(h,g)&=\max_{0\le x\le1/2}\{B(x,h)+B(x,g)\}, \qquad h,g\ge0. \end{split} 	ag{4} \] Endpoint integrals have their continuous values. The maximizing index is unique. Write \(r=\sinh(h/2)\), \(s=\sinh(g/2)\). If \(rs<1\), the maximum is interior, and \[ \pi V_h(h,g)=\alpha(h,g) =\arcsin rac{r\sqrt{1+s^2}}{\sqrt{1+r^2}}. 	ag{5} \] If \(rs\ge1\), the maximum is \(x=1/2\), and \[ V(h,g)=(h+g)/2,\qquad \pi V_h=\pi/2. 	ag{6} \] The first derivatives match continuously at \(rs=1\). Call an edge regular when \(rs<1\), and saturated otherwise. An edge to a complete outside vertex is always regular. The source proves convexity of \(V\) on the nonnegative quadrant. At a regular edge its two-variable Hessian is positive definite; on an outside edge the remaining scalar Hessian is \[ V_{hh}(h,0)= rac1{2\pi\cosh(h/2)}>0. 	ag{7} \] At \(h=0\), with the other height finite, its one-sided height derivative is zero. Define \[ \mathcal L_{\mathbf c}(\mathbf H) =\sum_{vw\ {m included}}V(H_v,H_w)-\sum_{v\in S}c_vH_v, \qquad H_w=0\quad(w
otin S). 	ag{8} \] **Lemma 2.** For every \(\mathbf c\in(0,1]^S\), (8) has a unique minimizer on \([0,\infty)^S\). All its coordinates are finite and positive, every selected vertex meets a regular edge, and \[ \sum_{e
i v}\alpha_{v,e}=\pi c_v. 	ag{9} \] **Proof.** Choosing \(x=1/2\) in (4), where \(B(1/2,h)=h/2\), gives the uniform coercive bound \[ \mathcal L_{\mathbf c}(\mathbf H) \ge\sum_{v\in S}(d_v/2-c_v)H_v \ge rac12\sum_{v\in S}H_v. 	ag{10} \] Continuous sublevel sets are compact, so a minimum exists. At \(H_v=0\) its one-sided derivative is \(-c_v<0\). Hence every minimizing height is positive, and stationarity gives (9). If every incidence at \(v\) were saturated, its derivative sum would be \(d_v/2>c_v\), a contradiction. The regular edges therefore cover all selected vertices. Their Hessians, using (7) on outside edges, sum to a positive definite form: any nonzero vector has a nonzero selected coordinate and a regular edge incident to it. This partial sum is locally strongly convex near the minimizer, while the remaining edge potentials are convex. Two minima would make their connecting segment constant, contradicting this local strictness. \(\square\) The minimizer varies continuously on the charge cube, including at the exceptional upper corner. The bound (10) is uniform and its value is at most \(\mathcal L_{\mathbf c}(0)\), independent of \(\mathbf c\). Every convergent subsequence of minimizers is optimal at the limiting charge vector by continuity; uniqueness identifies its limit. ## 3. The saturated-edge inequality At positive height, every incidence satisfies \[ \alpha_{v,e}\ge\arctan r_v,\qquad r_v=\sinh(H_v/2)>0. 	ag{11} \] There is equality on a complete outside edge and strict inequality on every edge to a selected neighbor. For a regular edge this follows from (5); for a saturated edge it follows from \(\pi/2>\arctan r_v\). Suppose \(vw\) is saturated at the minimizer. Its own contribution at each endpoint is exactly \(\pi/2\). Apply (11) only to the remaining \(d_v-1\) and \(d_w-1\) incidences: \[ \arctan r_v\le rac{\pi(c_v-1/2)}{d_v-1}\le rac{\pi}{4}, \qquad \arctan r_w\le rac{\pi(c_w-1/2)}{d_w-1}\le rac{\pi}{4}. 	ag{12} \] If either charge is at most \(1/2\), the first inequality already contradicts its positive height. Otherwise the displayed upper bounds follow from \(d_v,d_w\ge3\) and \(c_v,c_w\le1\). But \(r_vr_w\ge1\) implies \[ \arctan r_v+\arctan r_w\ge\pi/2. 	ag{13} \] Every inequality in (12)--(13) must therefore be an equality. Consequently \[ d_v=d_w=3,\quad c_v=c_w=1,\quad r_v=r_w=1. 	ag{14} \] Neither vertex can have another selected neighbor, since that would make its incidence estimate strict. Connectedness makes \(S\) exactly this pair. Conversely, for this pair at charges \((1,1)\), \(r_v=r_w=1\) gives an internal contribution \(\pi/2\) and two outside contributions \(\pi/4\) at each vertex. It solves (9); convexity and Lemma 2 make it the unique minimum. This proves the full saturated-edge classification. The improvement over the archived sufficient degree condition is the use of a saturated edge's entire \(\pi/2\) contribution before estimating its remaining incidences. It is not an enumeration of short words. ## 4. Original geometry and continuation At an all-regular minimizer set \(t_v=-iH_v\), with outside heights zero. Put \[ A_v=	anh(H_v/2)= rac{r_v}{\sqrt{1+r_v^2}},\qquad a_v=	an(t_v/2)=-iA_v. 	ag{15} \] Then every original edge satisfies \[ q_e^2=1-A_v^2-A_w^2 = rac{1-r_v^2r_w^2}{(1+r_v^2)(1+r_w^2)}>0. 	ag{16} \] The second source's exact positivity criterion is \(\Re q>\sqrt{(\Re a_v)^2+(\Re a_w)^2}\). Thus the positive root in (16) gives the original eight positive shapes, with all original face denominators regular. Simultaneously multiplying the heights by \(0\le\lambda\le1\) keeps their hyperbolic-sine products below one. This fixes the complete branches, on which \[ r_{v,e}^{m orig} =-i\arcsin\!\left(	anh(H_v/2)\cosh(H_w/2)ight) =-i\alpha_{v,e}. 	ag{17} \] Equation (9) is exactly (1). This height contraction fixes the logarithmic marking; it is not identified with the radial charge solution path. The original global uniqueness theorem makes this solution unique among all complex positive configurations. Its complex period Jacobian has positive definite Hermitian part. The implicit-function theorem consequently gives a holomorphic solution near each charge vector with a regular minimizer. These branches agree by uniqueness. Together with continuity of the minimizer, this also gives the compact-uniform assertion. To exclude an unobserved positive solution at the exceptional corner, first note that every positive solution of (1) is purely imaginary. The reflection \(\mathbf t\mapsto-\overline{\mathbf t}\) preserves positivity: \(a_v\mapsto-\overline{a_v}\) and \(q_e\mapsto\overline{q_e}\) preserve the original criterion. Its canonical returns are \(-\overline{r_{v,e}^{m orig}}\), so it preserves (1). Global uniqueness fixes the reflected point. At a purely imaginary positive edge the imaginary return has the same sign as its endpoint's imaginary angle, because its argument is \(i	anh(\Im t_v/2)\cosh(\Im t_w/2)\) in \(i(-1,1)\). The negative row in (1) therefore makes every selected angle \(-iH_v\) with \(H_v>0\). Such a solution is all regular by (16) and stationary for (8), contradicting the unique saturated minimizer at the exceptional pair. No other positive solution exists there. At any minimizer, (9) and (11) also give \[ 0<H_v(\mathbf c)\le 2\operatorname{arsinh}	an\!\left( rac{\pi c_v}{d_v}ight). 	ag{18} \] On a simultaneous radial charge path to zero the heights therefore tend to zero. The original complete period Jacobian is \(	frac12\operatorname{diag}(d_v)\); its analytic solution agrees with these solutions by uniqueness. For a fixed nonexceptional endpoint, the compact radial segment, including zero, is thus contained in the positive domain. A radial path ending at the exceptional corner is positive for \(\lambda<1\), and its minimizer converges to (14). Equations (16)--(17) give (2), the internal \(q=0\), and the claimed return angles. For a singleton, no internal edge is present and the solution is explicit: \[ H(c)=2\operatorname{arsinh}	an(\pi c/d). 	ag{19} \] It exists through unit charge precisely when \(d>2\). At any positive zero-power unit solution the original canonical bound \(|\Im r_{v,e}^{m orig}|<\pi/2\) likewise forces \(d_v>2\) at every vertex. This proves the necessity in (3), and the theorem proves sufficiency. For disconnected selected sets the same classification applies separately to each selected component, since all outside angles remain zero. Compact uniformity above concerns compact subsets of the positive charge cube avoiding its exceptional point, or fixed simultaneous radial segments with regular endpoints. It is not uniformity on all partially zero-charge faces: a zero-charge vertex can become complete and change the effective selected components. ## 5. Scope and full direct-source readback This settles radial continuation for the all-zero class. It does not settle the same question for adjacent nonzero signed powers: their real angles need not vanish, and the nonnegative incidence estimate (11) is not supplied by their original equations. The theorem concerns the original positive subdivision and full marked primitive periods. The trivalent-pair failure does not assert nonhyperbolicity of its partially filled parent; the archived Newton/Conway treatment uses other coordinates. No charged quantum asymptotic, original-cycle coefficient, or arbitrary-short hyperbolic coverage follows here. Both complete direct sources were read and their used implications checked: * [Zero-power convex height potential](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_zero_power_subtree_convex_potential.md), SHA256 c0ab73c2869ed3db7a0152634cbf3a315c573eed2f5fc99e437dacadcceb8eb8: Sections 2--4 give \(V\), its all-regime derivatives, convexity, regular Hessians, and the original unit-charge minimum. The proof above supplies the charge cube and sharp classification. * [Original positive geometry and periods](research_positive_edge_global_monotonicity.md), SHA256 da5129c7110190035eedb8249d4004dd06b5a7555e78d948234d8de50fa17500: Sections 1--3 give the actual shapes and complete branches; Sections 5 and 7 give the original primitive equations, global uniqueness, positive Jacobian, and complete initializer. Only written derivation, source-text reads and file hashes were used. No mathematical code, tests, numerical experiments or compilation were run. Frozen notes and public manuscripts were not changed.

title: A full-source lattice initializer on the lower half-charge cube
text:
# A full-source lattice initializer on the lower half-charge cube Private written proof, 16 November 2026. The original zero-power source has a nonzero geometric asymptotic on every compact subset of the lattice charge cube \((0,1/2]^S\). The high Newton sectors have a uniform strict gap, including high boundary edges and both level parities. The proof contracts their actual radical normals first, and then bounds the remaining charged low source with its shared indices intact. It does not use positivity of the charged closing functional. The archived radical contraction and path comparison already identify physical cut sources. The additional estimate here uses the convex zero-power height minimum to bound their charge cost. The all-low Fourier proof is extended below only at actual lattice charges; no off-lattice complex-charge initializer is asserted. ## 1. Original source and the charge-dependent pressure Let \(T\) be a fixed finite tree, let \(S\) be a nonempty connected proper selected set, and suppose every selected original degree \(d_v\) is at least three. Let \(E_S\) contain every edge incident to \(S\), once. Write \(k=|S|\), \(e=|E_S|\), and \(b=|\partial S|\), so \(e=k-1+b\). All selected powers are zero. Outside variables remain ordinary polynomials; complete outside values are used to define the pressure. Put \(N\ge2\), \(D=N-1\), \(\eta=(-1)^D\), \(m=\lfloor N/2floor\), and \[ s_j=2\sin(\pi j/N),\quad S_j=\prod_{h=1}^j s_h,\quad c_a=2\cos((2a+1)\pi/N),\quad e_j(z)=S_j^{-2}\prod_{a<j}(c_a-z). 	ag{1} \] The original algebra and closing are \[ P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2,\qquad \phi_N(f)=\eta N^2[z^D]\operatorname{rem}_{P_N}f, \qquad K_N(z,w)=\sum_{j=0}^D e_j(z)e_j(w). 	ag{2} \] For integer \(1\le J_v\le N\), set \(\chi_v=J_v/N\) and retain the actual coupon \(\mathcal C_{N,\chi_v}=T_{N-J_v}(-z_v/2)\), with reduction only inside a traced variable. The source is \[ Z_N( oldsymbol\chi;\mathbf u)= \left(\prod_{v\in S}\phi_N^{(v)}ight) \left[\prod_{v\in S}\mathcal C_{N,\chi_v}(z_v) \prod_{vw\in E_S}K_N(z_v,z_w)ight], \qquad z_w=-2\cos u_w\quad(w
otin S). 	ag{3} \] Each original boundary incidence is kept separately before any ordinary identification of boundary variables. Let \(Z_N^{m low}\) replace every kernel by its sum over \(2j<N\). Use the original real edge potential \[  egin{split} J(x)&=\int_0^x\log(2\sin\pi t)\,dt,\ B(x,h)&=\int_0^x\log(2\cos2\pi t+2\cosh h)\,dt-2J(x),\ V(h,g)&=\max_{0\le x\le1/2}\{B(x,h)+B(x,g)\},\ M( oldsymbol\chi)&=\min_{\mathbf H\ge0} \left\{\sum_{vw\in E_S}V(H_v,H_w) -\sum_{v\in S}\chi_vH_vight\}, \qquad H_w=0\quad(w
otin S). \end{split} 	ag{4} \] In particular \(V(0,0)=M_\infty=4G/\pi\), with \(G\) Catalan's constant. The cube theorem supplies a unique regular positive minimum \(\mathbf H( oldsymbol\chi)\) throughout \((0,1)^S\), and \[ 0<H_v( oldsymbol\chi) \le2\operatorname{arsinh}	an(\pi\chi_v/d_v). 	ag{5} \] Its canonical critical action is \(M( oldsymbol\chi)\), with phase \(\sum_e\psi(t_v,t_w)-i\sum_v\chi_vt_v\) and \(t_v=-iH_v\). All edge constants are included in (4). For an internal edge define \(\gamma_{vw}=M_\infty-\chi_vH_v-\chi_wH_w\); for a boundary edge at \(v\) define \(\gamma_{vw}=M_\infty-\chi_vH_v\). **Theorem 1.** Let \(\mathcal K\subset(0,1]^S\) be compact and avoid the exceptional trivalent-pair corner of the cube theorem. Suppose \(\gamma_{vw}\ge\gamma>0\) on \(\mathcal K\) for every included edge. Then constants \(C,p\), uniform at both level parities, satisfy \[ \sup_{\mathbf u\in\mathbb R^{\partial S}} |Z_N( oldsymbol\chi;\mathbf u)-Z_N^{m low} ( oldsymbol\chi;\mathbf u)| \le CN^p e^{N(M( oldsymbol\chi)-\gamma)} \quad( oldsymbol\chi\in\mathcal K\cap N^{-1}\mathbb Z^S). 	ag{6} \] The hypotheses hold for every compact \(\mathcal K\subset(0,1/2]^S\), with \[ \gamma=M_\infty-\log3>31/990. 	ag{7} \] ## 2. The exact charged low trace and its uniform majorant If \(f(t)=\sum_r a_re^{irt}\) is an even Laurent polynomial, extend \(a_r\) by zero off its support. The original derivative-sampling formula, applied to \(f(t)\cos((N-J)t)\), gives exactly \[  egin{split} \phi_N(f\mathcal C_{N,J/N}) = rac{N^2}{2}\sum_{\ell\ge1}\ell\eta^{\ell+1}  ig[&a_{(\ell-1)N+J-1}-a_{(\ell-1)N+J+1}\ &+a_{(\ell+1)N-J-1}-a_{(\ell+1)N-J+1} ig]. \end{split} 	ag{8} \] The multiplier is \(\ell N\), not \(J\); hence every original repeated-root normal is retained. The identity tensorizes in the selected variables. If the Laurent coefficients are nonnegative, the same coefficient estimate as in the archived Fourier theorem yields \[ |\phi_N(f\mathcal C_{N,J/N})| \le N^2 f(-ih)  rac{2\cosh h\,e^{-Nh}\cosh((N-J)h)}{(1-e^{-Nh})^2}, \qquad h>0. 	ag{9} \] More generally (9) applies to a coefficientwise absolute majorant. In several variables its factors multiply, while \(f(-i\mathbf h)\) retains all shared edge indices. For heights in a fixed positive compact interval and charges in a compact subset of \((0,1)\), the exponential penalty in (9) is \(e^{-N\chi h}\), up to a fixed factor. No assignmentwise positivity of the charged trace is used. The actual low Newton factors have nonnegative Laurent coefficients. Their uniform product estimate is \[ \log\{e_j(-2\cosh h)e_j(-2\cosh g)\} =N\{B(j/N,h)+B(j/N,g)\}+O(\log N),\qquad 2j<N. 	ag{10} \] It holds uniformly for bounded nonnegative heights, including zero endpoints. One may check the uniformity directly: the numerator logarithm is monotone on \([0,1/2]\), and the last midpoint of any low product stays a distance at least \(1/(2N)\) from \(1/2\). Its argument is bounded below by a constant times \(N^{-2}\), uniformly for bounded \(h\ge0\). The midpoint sum/integral error is therefore \(O(\log N)\); the usual endpoint-aware sine-factorial estimate has the same uniform error. Thus (9), (10), and the polynomial number of assignments bound a charged low network at any chosen surviving heights by the exponential of its full expression in (4). This statement needs no regularity of its wire maxima. ## 3. Contracting every high pattern before taking absolute values The high polynomials are exactly \(e_{D-r}\), \(0\le r<m\). They form the square-zero radical in the full physical algebra. Hence a nonzero high-edge pattern \(A\subset E_S\) has at most one high edge at each selected vertex. Outside vertices are not reduced and impose no such restriction. Let \(T_A\subset S\) be the selected endpoints of \(A\). The original surviving normal is the exact divided difference \[ \phi_N(e_{D-r}f)=\sum_{a=0}^r b_{ra}f(c_a),\qquad b_{ra}=(-1)^{r+a}  rac{s_{2a+1}S_r^2}{S_{r-a}S_{r+a+1}},\qquad |b_{ra}|\le2. 	ag{11} \] Indeed the perfect pairing identifies the left side with the Newton coefficient \([e_r]\operatorname{rem}f\). The first \(r+1\) nodes are distinct, so ordinary divided differences give its coefficient as \((-1)^rS_r^2\sum_{a\le r}f(c_a)/\prod_{h
e a}(c_a-c_h)\). The denominator has sign \((-1)^a\) and magnitude \(S_{r+a+1}S_{r-a}/s_{2a+1}\), proving (11). The bound follows by writing the factorial ratio as \[  rac{S_r^2}{S_{r-a}S_{r+a+1}} = rac1{s_{r+a+1}} \prod_{j=1}^a rac{s_{r-j+1}}{s_{r+j}} \le rac1{s_{r+a+1}}, \qquad  rac{s_{2a+1}}{s_{r+a+1}}\le2. 	ag{12} \] The two sine inequalities use \(a\le r<m\). In (11) the high factor vanishes at every physical value. Thus the derivative of the spectator, including the derivative of its charge coupon, vanishes from the product rule. The high factor's own derivative is exactly (11). The odd simple-node contribution is zero. At a lattice charge the remaining coupon value has modulus at most one. No normal was discarded in obtaining this estimate. At a physical node, \[ 0\le e_j(c_a)\le e_j(-2)\quad(j\le a),\qquad e_j(c_a)=0\quad(j>a). 	ag{13} \] Consequently each untouched low kernel meeting a contracted vertex has a coefficientwise Laurent majorant obtained by making that vertex complete. If both ends are contracted, keep the full scalar \(K_N^{m low}(-2,-2)\). In particular an edge between distinct high pairs remains present, with its full complete-edge rate. For a high boundary edge its other factor is the original ordinary polynomial \(e_{D-r}(-2\cos u)\). The radical Fourier bound gives \[ \sup_{u\in\mathbb R}|e_{D-r}(-2\cos u)|\le\sqrt{N-1}. 	ag{14} \] This includes the even-level values and the odd-level vanishing at the complete simple node. It does not impose a quotient on an outside variable. Equations (11)--(14), summed over their polynomially many indices and physical colors, give a polynomial-cost coefficientwise majorant from the low network obtained as follows: delete only edges in \(A\); make vertices in \(T_A\) complete and untraced; keep every other edge and every remaining original trace and coupon. Apply (9) to this majorant; its charged scalar is not asserted nonnegative. Let its pressure be \[ M_A^{m cut}( oldsymbol\chi) =\min_{H_v\ge0,\ v\in S\setminus T_A} \left\{\sum_{vw\in E_S\setminus A}V(H_v,H_w) -\sum_{v\in S\setminus T_A}\chi_vH_vight\}, \quad H_v=0\ (v\in T_A	ext{ or outside}). 	ag{15} \] Every remaining traced vertex keeps its original incident edges: no edge of \(A\) meets it. Thus its degree has not silently dropped. Edges with no remaining traced endpoint contribute \(V(0,0)\). If no traced vertices remain, (15) is precisely the sum of those constants, with no nonexistent trace or saddle introduced. All these minima exist uniformly. Choosing \(x=1/2\) in \(V\) gives the coercive bound \(\sum_v(d_v/2-\chi_v)H_v\ge	frac12\sum_vH_v\) on surviving vertices, apart from harmless constant edges. Their minima therefore lie in a fixed compact height box. At a surviving height zero the one-sided derivative is \(-\chi_v<0\), since \(V_h(0,g)=0\). Continuity of this derivative for bounded \(g\) gives a uniform positive lower bound for every surviving minimizing height on \(\mathcal K\). This argument does not assume a regular cut minimum, or import an asymptotic for a whole cut source. Use these minimizing heights in the joint majorant (9). It proves directly, with the other edges and their shared labels retained, \[ \sup_{\mathbf u	ext{ real}}|Z_N^A( oldsymbol\chi;\mathbf u)| \le CN^p e^{N M_A^{m cut}( oldsymbol\chi)}. 	ag{16} \] ## 4. A charge cost for every matching, and the strict half-cube gap Extend (4) to charges in \([0,1]^S\) by the same minimum. It is a concave function of the charges, being an infimum of affine functions. Let \( oldsymbol\chi^A\) equal \( oldsymbol\chi\) off \(T_A\) and zero on \(T_A\). Since \(V\) is nondecreasing in each nonnegative height, a minimum at these zero charges can be taken with \(H_v=0\) on \(T_A\). Restoring exactly the deleted edges adds \(|A|M_\infty\). Therefore \[ M( oldsymbol\chi^A) =M_A^{m cut}( oldsymbol\chi)+|A|M_\infty. 	ag{17} \] Evaluating the variational problem at its original minimizer gives the supporting inequality directly: \[ M( oldsymbol\chi^A) \le M( oldsymbol\chi)+\sum_{v\in T_A}\chi_vH_v( oldsymbol\chi). 	ag{18} \] Thus \[ M( oldsymbol\chi)-M_A^{m cut}( oldsymbol\chi) \ge |A|M_\infty-\sum_{v\in T_A}\chi_vH_v =\sum_{vw\in A}\gamma_{vw}. 	ag{19} \] The equality uses the exact condition that selected endpoints of high edges do not repeat. It allows repeated untraced outside endpoints. Combining (16), (19), and the finitely many nonempty patterns proves (6). If \(0<\chi_v\le1/2\), (5) gives \[ H_v\le2\operatorname{arsinh}(1/\sqrt3)=\log3, \qquad \chi_vH_v\le	frac12\log3. 	ag{20} \] Every high edge has at most two selected ends, proving (7). An elementary strict numerical-free margin follows from \(G>1-1/9=8/9\), \(\pi<22/7\), and \[ \log3=2\sum_{j\ge0} rac{(1/2)^{2j+1}}{2j+1} <1+ rac1{12}+ rac1{60}= rac{11}{10}. 	ag{21} \] Consequently \(M_\infty-\log3>112/99-11/10=31/990\). This comparison uses the full coupled minimizer; it does not optimize the incident edges independently or discard a connecting low edge. **Corollary 2 (larger original degrees).** If every selected \(d_v\ge12\), the high estimate (6) holds on every compact \(\mathcal K\subset(0,1]^S\), including charges equal to one, with \[ \gamma=M_\infty-4\operatorname{arsinh}(2-\sqrt3)>4/99. 	ag{21a} \] In fact (5) bounds every \(\chi_vH_v\) by \(2\operatorname{arsinh}	an(\pi/12) =2\operatorname{arsinh}(2-\sqrt3)\). An internal edge has at most twice this cost, and a boundary edge has less. Finally \(\operatorname{arsinh}x<x\) for \(x>0\), and \(\sqrt3>19/11\), so the internal cost is less than \(12/11\). The lower bound \(M_\infty>112/99\) proves (21a). This is a high-sector estimate through the unit-charge face; it does not assert the separated-companion asymptotic below uniformly at that face. **Corollary 3 (the whole nonzero lattice block).** The constants \(C,p\) in (6) can be chosen independently of the charge vector throughout either of these finite blocks: * \(1\le J_v\le\lfloor N/2floor\) for all \(v\), with the gap (7); * \(1\le J_v\le N\) for all \(v\), if every \(d_v\ge12\), with the gap (21a). Only the high-sector estimate is asserted uniformly in these blocks. To prove it, all cut minima lie in a fixed box \(0\le H_v\le B\): coercivity and the value at zero permit \(B=2eM_\infty\). Choose \(h_0>0\) so \(	anh(h_0/2)\cosh(B/2)\le1/2\). If a surviving minimizing height satisfies \(H_v\le h_0\), every incident edge is regular at that endpoint and \[ \alpha_{v,e} =\arcsin\{	anh(H_v/2)\cosh(H_w/2)\} \le H_v\cosh(B/2). 	ag{21b} \] Use \(\arcsin x\le2x\) on \([0,1/2]\) and \(	anh(H_v/2)\le H_v/2\). The stationary row \(\sum_e\alpha_{v,e}=\pi\chi_v\) then gives \[ H_v\ge c\chi_v\ge c/N,\qquad c=\min\{h_0,\pi/(d_{\max}\cosh(B/2))\}>0. 	ag{21c} \] If \(H_v>h_0\), the same inequality holds because \(\chi_v\le1\). Thus the denominators in (9) are uniformly bounded away from zero. All numerator factors there are uniformly bounded after extracting \(e^{-N\chi_vH_v}\). The uniform version of (10), the polynomial physical contractions, and the finite pattern count now prove (16) with charge-independent constants. Inequality (19) and its two uniform edge-cost bounds finish the proof. Vertices of zeroed charge remain untraced and require no Fourier denominator. ## 5. The resulting nonzero original lattice-source asymptotic For completeness, the needed charge version of the archived all-low proof follows from its written estimates without assuming a complex charge initializer. On a compact \(\mathcal K\Subset(0,1)^S\), the cube theorem gives positive heights, strict wire maxima and compact uniformity. Formula (9) removes all low assignments outside small intervals around these maxima with a strict gap, exactly as the uncharged discarded-index argument, now with penalty \(-\chi_vH_v\). For lattice \(\chi_v=J_v/N\), the literal cosine is an even \(2\pi\)-periodic Laurent polynomial. Hence the original full trace equals the full lower-circle integral of that cosine times its spectator; its opposite vertical sides cancel. On this circle, write \(W_N(t)=e^{-iNt}/(1-\eta e^{-iNt})^2\). Then \[ W_N(t)\cos((N-J)t) =	frac12e^{-iJt}  rac{1+e^{-2i(N-J)t}}{(1-\eta e^{-iNt})^2}. 	ag{22} \] The second numerator term and every nonconstant denominator mode have a uniform exponential gap, since the heights and \(1-\chi\) have positive compact lower bounds. This retains the companion \(2N-J\), every higher alias, and the exact original normal weights. The selected term has phase \[ F_{ oldsymbol\chi}(\mathbf t,\mathbf u) =\sum_{vw\in E_S}\psi(t_v,t_w)-i\sum_{v\in S}\chi_vt_v. 	ag{23} \] The archived low edge expansion and its strict angular bound apply at these compactly regular imaginary points. The only angular maximum is \(\mathbf t=-i\mathbf H\); its negative Hessian is the positive definite height Hessian. Thus its Gaussian coefficient is nonzero. Each factor \(1/2\) in (22) remains in that coefficient. The index-cotangent connectors and all fixed boundary derivatives are controlled by the same compact strict gaps in the low-source proof. This proves, uniformly over the lattice charges in \(\mathcal K\), \[ Z_N^{m low}( oldsymbol\chi;\mathbf u) =N^{-3(b-1)/2}A( oldsymbol\chi,\mathbf u) e^{N W( oldsymbol\chi,\mathbf u)}(1+O(N^{-1})). 	ag{24} \] Here \(W=F_{ oldsymbol\chi}(\mathbf t^*( oldsymbol\chi,\mathbf u), \mathbf u)\), \(W( oldsymbol\chi,0)=M( oldsymbol\chi)\), and, with \(\mathcal L_{ oldsymbol\chi}\) denoting the height functional inside braces in (4) and \(a_e\) the original positive edge amplitudes, \[ A( oldsymbol\chi,0)=2^{-k}(2/\pi)^{k/2}  rac{\prod_v\sinh H_v\prod_e a_e(-iH_v,-iH_w)} {\sqrt{\det
abla^2_{\mathbf H}\mathcal L_{ oldsymbol\chi}}}>0. 	ag{25} \] The power of \(N\) and every scalar normalization are unchanged. Under Theorem 1, (24) holds for the original full source (3). Indeed (6) is exponentially smaller. Its real-boundary bound extends to a sufficiently small fixed complex boundary polydisk: every boundary angular degree is at most \(D\), so Fourier coefficient bounds cost only a polynomial times \(e^{D\sum|\Im u_e|}\). Shrink the polydisk to retain the gap relative to \(\Re W\). Cauchy estimates preserve every fixed ordinary boundary derivative. In particular the conclusion holds on every compact lower half-charge cube, at both parities, and gives an actual nonzero initializer there. The functions \(W,A\) have local holomorphic continuations in charges by the geometric implicit-function theorem, but (24) here is asserted only at the lattice charges. Off lattice the lower-circle replacement has an original vertical current; it cannot be omitted. This theorem also gives no uniform low-source Gaussian expansion as a charge tends to zero, no full unit-block reconstruction error, and no arbitrary-short filled-source conclusion. Charges outside the edge-cost criterion require a different estimate of the coherent high sectors. ## Direct sources and author readback The complete final proof and all four complete direct sources were read; their directly used implications and versions were checked. - [Zero-power charge-cube geometry](research_zero_power_charge_cube_positivity.md), `91b0a03a677c9139bbfd04f9ef6b06b23e6c3fab435c1a974a2d243189925faf`: the potential, compact regular minima, height bound and original marked positive branches. - [Original low Fourier bounds](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_zero_power_subtree_fourier_bound.md), `9c7e71319ba9f416f5ea510dee472e481894396d0c8a3cebf6ff9cce05816c58`: Laurent coefficients, derivative sampling, uniform product profiles, and original matching support. - [Regular low-source asymptotic](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_regular_zero_subtree_low_source.md), `06e4b7c14e3a61616dea61642103e2d2803709fcd465ae9860258119db3299d1`: local edge amplitude, strict angular and index gaps, Gaussian normalization, and boundary continuation. Equations (8), (22) above supply the additional lattice-charge calculation. - [Full high-radical contraction](research_high_newton_radical_contraction.md), `1faa5d2e02edf0a1462cc43b243e0ab4403bf56e9f1af0befb6b492441d9dd03`: complete normal contraction, bounded divided-difference coefficients, square-zero support and the whole-real-period radical bound. Only written proofs, source-text reads and hashes were used. No mathematical programs, tests, numerical experiments, or public-file changes were made.

title: A zero crossing power with at least three neighboring tangles
text: # A zero crossing power with at least three neighboring tangles Research proof, 2 November 2026. This note proves a whole-boundary asymptotic at every original vertex of degree \(d\ge3\) whose crossing power is zero. The degree is fixed before the quantum level tends to infinity. The argument uses the full Fourier circle. Its vertical endpoint currents vanish exactly at zero crossing power, which removes the need for an endpoint estimate on a short angular interval. The frozen manuscripts are unchanged. ## 1. The original polynomial and its selected action Use the complete Newton polynomials and trace \[ e_k(z)=S_k^{-2}\prod_{j=0}^{k-1} \{2\cos((2j+1)\pi/N)-z\},\qquad S_k=\prod_{j=1}^k2\sin(\pi j/N), \] \[ K_N(t,u)=\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}e_k(-2\cos t)e_k(-2\cos u), \qquad \mathcal D_{0,N}f=\phi_N(f). \] The original boundary polynomial of a degree-\(d\) zero-power vertex is \[ P_{d,0,N}(\mathbf u) =\mathcal D_{0,N}^{(t)} \left[\prod_{j=1}^d K_N(t,u_j)\right]. \tag{1} \] The trace includes every first normal derivative at a repeated root. No boundary is closed after taking this trace. In particular, (1) is a polynomial of degree at most \(N-1\) in each \(-2\cos u_j\). Let \(\psi\) be the original edge phase, with \[ \psi(0,0)=M_\infty=\frac{4G}{\pi},\qquad \psi_t(t,u)=-\frac1\pi\operatorname{arsinh} (\tan(t/2)\cos(u/2)). \] For \(d\ge3\), put \[ h_d=2\operatorname{arsinh}\tan\frac\pi d, \qquad t_d=-ih_d, \qquad x_d=\frac1\pi\arctan\cosh(h_d/2). \tag{2} \] Then \(d\psi_t(t_d,0)=i\). Near \(\mathbf u=0\), define \(t_d(\mathbf u)\) by \[ \sum_{j=1}^d\psi_t(t_d(\mathbf u),u_j)=i, \qquad t_d(0)=t_d, \] and set \[ G_d(\mathbf u)=\sum_{j=1}^d\psi(t_d(\mathbf u),u_j) -it_d(\mathbf u), \qquad M_d=G_d(0)=d\psi(-ih_d,0)-h_d. \tag{3} \] The branch is continued from the original complete geometry. Its existence and positive primitive cone deformation are proved in [the isolated-vertex geometry](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_isolated_internal_vertex_geometry.md). **Theorem.** For every fixed integer \(d\ge3\), there is a complex polydisk about zero on which \[ P_{d,0,N}(\mathbf u) =N^{-3(d-1)/2}A_d(\mathbf u)e^{NG_d(\mathbf u)} (1+O_d(N^{-1})), \tag{4} \] uniformly through all sufficiently large integer levels. The amplitude is holomorphic and nonzero, and the normalized error is holomorphic, with the same order for fixed derivatives on smaller polydisks. There are positive constants \(c,B,b,C\) and a finite constant \(A\) such that \[ |P_{d,0,N}(\mathbf x+i\mathbf y)| \le CN^A\exp N\left\{ M_d-c\sum_{j=1}^d(1-\cos x_j)+B\sum_{j=1}^d y_j^2 \right\} \tag{5} \] for \(|x_j|\le\pi\), \(|y_j|\le b\). The phase in (4) is exactly the marked geometric action (3), with no additional unit phase. Its boundary Hessian is \[ (G_d)_{u_iu_j}(0) =-\delta_{ij}\frac{\cosh(h_d/2)}{2\pi}. \tag{6} \] The theorem concerns the complete source, including its discarded wire indices, and both parities of the level. ## 2. Positive Laurent coefficients and angular decrease For every \(k\) with \(2k<N\), there is an exact Laurent identity \[ e_k(-2\cos t) =\frac{S_{2k}}{S_k^2} \sum_{r=-k}^{k} \frac{e^{irt}}{S_{k+r}S_{k-r}}. \tag{7} \] All its coefficients are positive. To prove it, put \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\), \(w=e^{it}\). Factoring each cosine numerator gives \[ e_k(-2\cos t) =\frac{w^{-k}}{S_k^2} \prod_{j=0}^{2k-1}(1+wq^{-2k+1}Q^j). \] Expand by the finite Gaussian-binomial identity. The coefficient of \(w^a\) in the product is \(q^{a(a-2k)}{2k\brack a}_Q\). The equality \({2k\brack a}_Q=q^{a(2k-a)}S_{2k}/(S_aS_{2k-a})\) cancels this phase and proves (7). All indices of the denominators are less than \(N\), so this specialization has no zero denominator. The finite Gaussian-binomial identity itself follows by induction on the number of factors, or by its usual two-term coefficient recurrence. Fix a compact interval \(I=[\alpha,\beta]\subset(0,1/2)\) and a positive height \(h\). For real \(|\tau|\le\pi\), the root product gives the sharper angular estimate \[ |e_k(-2\cos(\tau-ih))| \le C_{I,h}e_k(-2\cosh h) \exp\left[-N\frac{\sin(2\pi k/N)} {2\pi(\cosh h+1)}(1-\cos\tau)\right] \qquad(k/N\in I). \tag{8} \] Here is the real-variable proof, including the uniformity in the wire index. Define \[ f_h(s)=\log|1+e^{h+is}|, \qquad L_{x,h}(\tau)=\frac1{2\pi} \int_{-2\pi x}^{2\pi x}f_h(\tau+s)\,ds. \] The roots in the product above are precisely the midpoints of this interval with mesh \(2\pi/N\). Since \(h>0\), the periodic function \(f_h\) is smooth, with bounded second derivative. The midpoint rule therefore gives, uniformly in \(k/N\in I\) and real \(\tau\), \[ \log\frac{|e_k(-2\cos(\tau-ih))|}{e_k(-2\cosh h)} =N\{L_{k/N,h}(\tau)-L_{k/N,h}(0)\}+O_{I,h}(N^{-1}). \tag{9} \] Let \(a=2\pi x\in(0,\pi)\). For \(0\le\tau\le\pi\), \[ L_{x,h}'(\tau) =\frac1{4\pi}\log \frac{\cosh h+\cos(\tau+a)}{\cosh h+\cos(\tau-a)} \le-\frac{\sin a\sin\tau}{2\pi(\cosh h+1)}. \tag{10} \] Indeed the denominator minus the numerator is \(2\sin a\sin\tau\), and \(\log(A/B)\le-(B-A)/B\) for \(0<A\le B\); also \(B\le\cosh h+1\). Integrating (10), and using evenness for negative \(\tau\), proves (8). We also need the real-parent estimate \[ |e_k(-2\cos u)| \le CN^{A_0}e_k(-2) \exp\left[-N\frac{\sin(2\pi k/N)}{4\pi} (1-\cos u)\right] \quad(k/N\in I,\ |u|\le\pi). \tag{11} \] This is the height-zero version of the same potential inequality. The logarithmic zeros of \(f_0\) prevent a uniform smooth midpoint error, but its upper error is \(O(\log N)\): remove the at most two mesh intervals touching a zero, bound the variation on the remaining intervals, and integrate the removed logarithms. A product vanishing at a root already satisfies the upper bound. At \(u=0\), the compact wire interval stays away from those zeros and has the ordinary uniform bulk estimate. Equivalently, (11) follows directly from the real-wire case of the proved [Newton boundary-decrease lemma](research_uniform_factorial_and_boundary_decay.md). In (10) with \(h=0\), the logarithmic singularity is integrable and the derivative inequality holds off its isolated singular point. It therefore integrates to the same loss, with coefficient \(\sin a/(4\pi)\). ## 3. A strict gap for the omitted wire indices First suppose \(d\ge4\), and put \(\Delta_d=dM_\infty-M_d\). The [action-gap lemma](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_isolated_vertex_action_gap.md) proves \[ 0<\Delta_d<M_\infty\qquad(d\ge4). \] For clarity, this uses the explicit zero-power branch \(h_d(\lambda)=2\operatorname{arsinh}\tan(\pi\lambda/d)\). Its integrated action loss decreases strictly with \(d\), and the exact degree-three loss is \(M_\infty\). Thus \[ \eta_d:=M_d-(d-1)M_\infty=M_\infty-\Delta_d>0. \tag{12} \] Choose rational cutoffs \(0<\alpha<\beta<1/2\), sufficiently close to zero and one half, that \(x_d\in(\alpha,\beta)\) and \[ \sup_{x\in[0,\alpha]\cup[\beta,1/2]}2g(x)<\eta_d/2, \qquad g(x)=J(2x)-4J(x). \] Such cutoffs exist because \(g\) is continuous and zero at both endpoints. Retain exactly the wire indices \(k/N\in I=[\alpha,\beta]\) in every edge kernel. The complete Hermite norm estimate applies before the trace and gives, for all omitted assignments together, \[ |\text{omitted contribution}| \le CN^A\exp N(M_d-\eta_d/2), \tag{13} \] uniformly for all real parent angles. One omitted low wire has rate at most \(\eta_d/2\); a high wire has rate zero; and every other wire has rate at most \(M_\infty\). There are polynomially many assignments for fixed \(d\). This includes the first normal derivatives and does not presume positivity of multiplication in the quotient algebra. At \(d=3\), the coarse gap in (12) is zero, so a different argument is necessary. The [degree-three discarded-wire proof](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_degree_three_zero_wire_tails.md) establishes the following stronger statement: for every fixed interval \(I\subset(0,1/2)\) containing \(x_3=\arctan(2)/\pi\) in its interior, all omitted assignments together have a uniform real-boundary bound \[ |\text{omitted contribution}|\le CN^A e^{N(M_3-\delta_I)} \qquad\text{for some }\delta_I>0, \qquad M_3=2M_\infty. \tag{13a} \] Its two ingredients are exact finite identities. Two high indices give zero in the full quotient algebra. For a term with one high index, the positive Newton multiplication law couples its coefficient to the two low parent factors; their continuous joint rate is strictly below \(2M_\infty\) on its entire compact support. For an all-low triple, write the product of its three Newton polynomials as \(\sum_m a_me^{imt}\). All \(a_m\) are nonnegative, and the full trace is exactly \(N^2(a_{N-1}-a_{N+1})\). Positivity of the Newton multiplication then gives the upper bound \(N^2e^{-(N-1)h_3}\sum_ma_me^{mh_3}\). Strict concavity of the three resulting real wire phases supplies the gap whenever one index is outside \(I\). This retains the first normal derivatives and all real parent angles. The cited proof includes the uniform endpoint estimates and the compactness argument. Thus for every fixed \(d\ge3\) we have an interval \(I\) with \(x_d\) in its interior and a strict whole-source omitted-wire gap. These are the only properties of the discarded terms used below. ## 4. The local edge expansion at the deeper imaginary angle Let \(h=h_d\) and \(t_0=-ih\). The retained kernel is \[ K_{N,I}(t,u)=\sum_{k/N\in I}e_k(-2\cos t)e_k(-2\cos u). \] At \((t,u)=(t_0,0)\), both Newton factors are positive. Its canonical interpolating phase is \[ A(x;t,u)=b(x,t)+b(x,u), \qquad b(x,t)=\int_0^x\log(2\cos(2\pi v)+2\cos t)\,dv-2J(x). \] At \((t_0,0)\) the logarithms are real and the phase is strictly concave for \(0<x<1/2\), since \[ A_{xx}(x;t_0,0) =\sum_{v\in\{t_0,0\}} \left[-\frac{2\pi\sin(2\pi x)}{\cos(2\pi x)+\cos v} -2\pi\cot(\pi x)\right]<0. \tag{14} \] Its derivative tends to positive infinity at zero and negative infinity at one half. Its unique maximum is \(x=x_d\). The critical equation is the original one, \[ \cos(2\pi x)=\frac{1-\cos t\cos u}{2+\cos t+\cos u}, \] and therefore its holomorphic critical branch agrees with the original edge phase \(\psi(t,u)\), continued along \(t=-iy\), \(0\le y\le h\). The canonical factorial interpolation has no singularity near the real wire interval at this point. Its midpoint arguments have real parts \(1/2-x>0\), the unshifted wire arguments have real parts \(x>0\), and all of them stay in compact subsets of their regular strips after a sufficiently small complex perturbation of \(x,t,u\). Thus the same factorial expansion as in the exact edge theorem applies. Here are the contour details needed to extend that theorem beyond its previous small angle disk. Enclose the retained integers by the exact cotangent rectangle with half-grid vertical sides near \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\), and horizontal wire heights \(\pm\varepsilon\). At the real base point, (14) gives a fixed gap at both endpoints. Choose \(\varepsilon>0\) so small that these vertical sides and their connectors retain the gap. Along the horizontal sides, the excess above the stationary real phase is at most \(C\varepsilon^2\), because the base phase is real on its real interval. Take \(C\varepsilon^2<\pi\varepsilon\). The nonconstant cotangent modes then retain a gap, since their exact decay is \(e^{-2\pi N\varepsilon}\). Next choose the \((t,u)\) neighborhood sufficiently small. The strict endpoint gaps and the cotangent gap persist uniformly there, and the imaginary part of the critical wire coordinate is less than \(\varepsilon/10\). The constant cotangent terms give \(N\) times the real integral; translate it to the horizontal tangent through the critical wire point. The endpoint connectors still have the fixed gap. Strict negative real wire Hessian gives the uniform Gaussian expansion. The half-grid endpoints differ from \(\alpha,\beta\) by \(O(N^{-1})\), and the estimates hold on a fixed larger regular rectangle, so this change is included. Consequently, near \((t_0,0)\), \[ K_{N,I}(t,u) =N^{-3/2}a_e(t,u)e^{N\psi(t,u)}(1+O(N^{-1})), \tag{15} \] with a holomorphic relative error. The original amplitude remains \[ a_e(t,u)=\frac{\sqrt{2\pi}} {4\sin^2(\pi x(t,u))\sqrt{-A_{xx}(x(t,u);t,u)}}. \tag{16} \] The square root is positive at \((t_0,0)\). No factor in (16) vanishes there. This proves the local expansion for the actual finite wire sum, including its lattice corrections. ## 5. The endpoint current is identically zero For any even periodic polynomial \(f(t)=f^\sharp(-2\cos t)\), the exact complete trace at zero crossing power is \[ \mathcal D_{0,N}f =-\frac{N^2}{\pi i}\int_{-\pi-ih}^{\pi-ih} \sin t\,f(t)\frac{e^{-iNt}}{(1-\eta e^{-iNt})^2}\,dt, \qquad \eta=(-1)^{N-1}. \tag{17} \] This is the full-circle form of the [exact rational trace](research_exact_complete_trace_contour.md). Its displayed vertical current vanishes exactly here: at \(t=\pi+iv\), \[ \sin(\pi+iv)f(\pi+iv) =-i\sinh v\,f^\sharp(2\cosh v) \] is odd in \(v\), while \(1/(4\cosh^2(Nv/2))\) is even. Their integral on \([-h,h]\) is zero. Equivalently, the opposite vertical sides cancel by \(2\pi\)-periodicity. This argument is valid for any polynomial degree and retains the original normal derivatives. It applies to the entire retained product in (1), not just to its leading phase. ## 6. The full lower circle and its unique contribution Let \[ c_t=\min_{x\in I}\frac{\sin(2\pi x)}{2\pi(\cosh h+1)}>0, \qquad c_u=\min_{x\in I}\frac{\sin(2\pi x)}{4\pi}>0. \] Equations (8) and (11), summed over the positive base terms, give \[ |K_{N,I}(\tau-ih,u)| \le CN^A K_{N,I}(-ih,0) e^{-N\{c_t(1-\cos\tau)+c_u(1-\cos u)\}} \tag{18} \] for the whole real circles in \(\tau\) and \(u\). This bound is possible because the base wire summands at \((-ih,0)\) are positive. It does not assert positivity at general real parent angles. Apply (17) to \(f(t)=\prod_jK_{N,I}(t,u_j)\). On its lower circle, \[ \frac{e^{-iNt}}{(1-\eta e^{-iNt})^2} =e^{-iNt}(1+O(e^{-Nh})). \] The modulus of the first factor is \(e^{-Nh}\). By (15), \(K_{N,I}(-ih,0)^d\) has rate \(d\psi(-ih,0)\). Consequently (18) bounds the full trace integrand by a polynomial times \[ \exp N\left\{M_d-dc_t(1-\cos\tau) -c_u\sum_j(1-\cos u_j)\right\}. \tag{19} \] At complete parents the lower-circle parameter \(\tau=0\) is therefore the only possible maximum, with a strict gap on every closed region excluding it. The exact rational denominator places all higher Fourier charges below that same contribution by at least \(h\). No other contour piece remains to be estimated. Near \(\tau=0\), insert (15) for each kernel. The phase is \(\sum_j\psi(t,u_j)-it\), whose selected critical point is (3). At complete parents its second derivative is \[ d\psi_{tt}(-ih,0)=-\frac{d}{2\pi}\operatorname{sech}(h/2)<0. \] Uniform one-dimensional Gaussian expansion proves (4), with \[ A_d(\mathbf u) =i\sqrt{\frac2\pi}\, \frac{\sin t_d(\mathbf u) \prod_j a_e(t_d(\mathbf u),u_j)} {\sqrt{-\sum_j\psi_{tt}(t_d(\mathbf u),u_j)}}. \tag{20} \] At zero its value is explicitly positive: \[ A_d(0)= \frac{2\sinh h}{\sqrt{d\operatorname{sech}(h/2)}} a_e(-ih,0)^d>0. \] There is also a closed expression. Put \(k=\cosh(h/2)=\sec(\pi/d)\). At the real wire saddle, direct substitution in (14) gives \(A_{xx}=-2\pi(1+k^2)^2/k^3\), so (16) simplifies to \(a_e(-ih,0)=1/(4\sqrt k)\). Hence \[ A_d(0)=\frac{4^{1-d}}{\sqrt d}\tan\frac\pi d \left(\sec\frac\pi d\right)^{(3-d)/2}. \tag{21} \] The powers of \(N\) are \(N^2\) from the trace, \(N^{-3d/2}\) from the kernels, and \(N^{-1/2}\) from the last Gaussian. The resulting exponent is \(-3(d-1)/2\). The local expansion and exterior gaps continue on a sufficiently small complex parent polydisk. The omitted-wire bounds of Section 3 also retain their gap there by polynomial continuation. This completes the proof of the uniform holomorphic asymptotic for the whole source. ## 7. Global boundary bounds and geometric normalization Equation (19) proves a real-parent angular loss for the retained trace. The omitted contribution from Section 3 has a fixed gap independently of the real parents. Since \(\sum_j(1-\cos u_j)\le2d\), decreasing the angular constant absorbs that contribution as well. This proves (5) first for real parents. Separate evenness gives \(\partial t_d/\partial u_j(0)=0\). The stationary boundary Hessian is consequently the explicit parent Hessian of the edge phase, which is (6). The local holomorphic expansion therefore gives a quadratic bound on a small complex parent neighborhood. Away from that neighborhood, the real angular gap persists on a sufficiently thin complex strip by the polynomial Bernstein–Walsh estimate on a finite cover by products of real spectral intervals. Each boundary degree is at most \(N-1\). Combining those two estimates proves (5). The selected action is exactly (3): the physical trace has no crossing chirp and \(C_{N,0}=1\), and the unit-charge factor in (17) is \(e^{-iNt}\). The isolated-vertex geometric proof identifies this same stationary action along the original positive primitive cone path, starting with \(2d\) regular ideal octahedra. Its Schläfli derivative is \(2\pi\) times the real action derivative. Thus the complete partially filled star contributes volume \(2\pi M_d\), with its original peripheral curves and absolute normalization. No additional phase or additive volume constant occurs. Accordingly these degree-\(d\ge3\) zero-power vertices may be used as singleton selected components in the further-filling theorem of [the connected-cluster note](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/research_connected_short_filling_clusters.md#10-a-volume-theorem-after-further-long-fillings). The resulting statement still requires all remaining powers to be independently sufficiently long, unless their own joint boundary polynomials have also been established. ## 8. The degree-three value and the remaining scope The additional omitted-wire argument is essential at degree three; the elementary Hermite estimate alone has no strict gap there. With (13a), however, the same full-circle proof applies. The explicit normalization (21) and the action-gap identity give \[ M_3=2M_\infty,\qquad A_3(0)=\frac1{16},\qquad P_{3,0,N}(0,0,0) =\frac{e^{2NM_\infty}}{16N^3}(1+O(N^{-1})). \] The theorem proves the entire three-boundary polynomial near zero and its global boundary bound, not only this value at complete parents. It makes no assertion that the finite polynomial is exactly the square of an edge kernel. At degree two and zero power, the selected cone branch degenerates at unit charge; its exact algebraic and marked tangle reduction is a separate result. Connected sets of adjacent low-degree short fillings also require their joint boundary estimates. The present theorem supplies one zero-power vertex of any degree at least three, with every neighboring boundary left free.

title: Rivin optimization, a regularized angle flow, and the quantum source
text: # Rivin optimization, a regularized angle flow, and the quantum source Research note, 26 October 2026, following the user's suggestion to use Rivin's geometrization and flow viewpoint. The classical geometric problem has a precise convex formulation. We give an exact constrained flow and prove global convergence when the triangulation is complete and positive geometric. We then identify the additional lift needed for the actual quantum period, retaining a newly computed paired source-normalization identity. The volume conjecture is not proved. This is not a replacement positive quantum state or a claim that real convexity determines the original finite period.
