Current source frontier (27 October): [exact complete Fourier localization](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/universal_resonant_fourier_source_completion.md) places the original period entirely at the resonant row; regular finite Fourier rows vanish exactly. The [all-strand Euler/Cauchy theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/all_strand_euler_cauchy_cap.md) now expresses that original period as a specified finite coefficient or endpoint divided difference, with the whole word retained. Its [physical-clock equation](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_fusion_right_euler_clock.md) has a nilpotent apparent denominator. The [full peripheral boundary calculation](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/resonant_boundary_blowup_and_actual_peripheral_line.md) proves the required first pole cancellation and corrects a raw-prefix half-shift. Its Vandermonde inverse is retained before taking normal jets, with the exact forced connection, both endpoint carries and every original phase/peripheral factor. The first source keeps its full output row. Its raw partial array is Jtilde_(a,j)=sum_c T^V_(c,j;a,j), original period=(1/N)sum_(a,j)Jtilde_(a,j). At a root the inverse Fourier contributes 1/N inside Jtilde. Old physical b and its output offset are now summed internally; j is a genuine new external source coordinate. A double diagonal at the first cut would have removed that coordinate and is not the chosen source. The finite Fourier/alias theorem preserves all independent power characters on unwrapped current tails. The [geometric Fourier theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_fourier_polarized_geometric_normal_block.md) uses the original macroscopic open phase S_open+vt, not an unbounded extrapolation of bounded-band jets. The mixed Hessian along the old framing tangent is dLog p_e, so the enlarged transverse block is nondegenerate on the new chart. Complete discrete-faithful holonomy makes (A,p_e) birational on that framing torsor; generic old projection caustics disappear. The marked regulator action is unchanged. The [extended partial-support proof](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/partial_geometric_support_theorem.md) applies finite proper-coefficient linear algebra and least-moment repair to this SAME actual root partial family. Its constructed operator has a geometric A-factor before the final source sum. The auxiliary proper root lift and whole inverse Fourier normal germs are explicitly distinguished. Finally the [fixed-column source theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_one_index_fourier_source_and_ward_reduction.md) uses actual scalar root closure to remove the a average exactly: original period=sum_j Jtilde_(a_N,j). A generic rational phase gives a good interior sequence a_N and a nonzero phase-specialized partial operator on each marked residue class of levels. The actual whole Ward defect of this source change has a polynomially bounded primitive and is kept before differentiation; root equality is not falsely promoted to equality of all quantum-normal jets. The last selected source problem now has ONE exterior Fourier index. Its geometric survival and regulator norm still have to be proved. ## 38. A whole rigid source frame, a Möbius fiber, and an actual cancellation test There is now a literal algebraic answer for the finite boundary frame before jets. For the actual clock B and cyclic repair P, with Z=Q^N and e=e_0 e_0^t, BPB inverse P inverse=Q[I+(Z inverse-1)e], original source matrix=e sum_(r=0)^(N-1)P^r. The [rank-one moment/source proof](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_rank_one_multiplicative_moment_and_orbit_source.md) keeps its divided wall projector, the original orbit co-source and both actual endpoint deletions. The [aligned cyclic frame theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/flat_cyclic_source_frame_and_scalar_period.md) classifies this whole source-cyclic chart directly: its endpoint-corrected function/shift algebra is Mat_N. Its unmarked frame ambiguity is a line bundle, removed by a vector marking. The defect must be aligned with the actual source; rank one and flatness alone do not impose that alignment. The scalar of a closed actual word is separate from the rigid frame. The geometric fiber also has a simpler global function. Factor U-V=u(a,b) and put (c,d)=(a,b)V inverse. With the original prefix sign sigma, the ACTUAL momentum is p=sigma[c(1-r)-ds]/[ar+bs]. The [Möbius theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/mobius_fourier_framing_and_intrinsic_norm_pole.md) gives its inverse and identifies r=infinity with the intrinsic pole lambda=-sigma c/a, independent of the cut s. The whole principal density retains the norm 1-lambda^N. For the figure-eight prefix this pole has order six, and principal sampling is singular when six divides N even though the actual finite tensor is regular. The independent wall divisors 1-Q^N and 1-lambda^N therefore cannot be equated or canceled without their actual word/source map. Finally, the [actual zero-source Fourier current](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_fourier_source_cancellation.md) is not an abstract countermodel. For the original two-cut tensor, W=[(I tensor B)T(I tensor B inverse)-T]/(Q-1) has zero second partial trace WHOLE, preserves its index support, and at a root has raw partial array J_W,j=[J_(j+1)-J_j]/(Q_N-1). Its formal geometric block on the good-A chart is nonzero, with the same regulator action: the leading amplitude is the derivative of the actual Fourier amplitude. Nevertheless its final source sum is exactly zero. The cyclic difference D has a centered inverse of norm at most one on the zero-source subspace, and abs(sum_j J_j)=sqrt(N) dist(J,im D). Thus the last selected norm is a norm in an exact source/current quotient. Local geometric support and Rivin algebraicity do not determine that quotient class. The next required construction must carry the actual original class, its independent wall/norm divisors and the marked relative boundary to the regulator line. No selected nonvanishing or volume limit is inferred from frame rigidity or a nonzero formal block alone. ## 39. The pointed source has an explicit polynomial unfolding before jets The [pointed companion theorem](pointed_companion_source_and_polynomial_hilbert90.md) now gives a stronger positive result than local root smoothness. Retain the source v,ell and aligned moment equation Q inverse XYX inverse Y inverse=I+v w, Xv=v, ell v=1, ell Y=ell. On the source-orbit chart v,Yv,...,Y^(N-1)v is a basis. Relaxing only the fixed finite cyclic equation Y^N=I gives an explicit principal open affine (N-1)-space over the whole Q-unit base. Y is companion with last column t_i, sum t_i=1 and t_0 a unit. The lower moment rows determine X by a polynomial recurrence; the top row then uniquely determines w. This is a scheme classification over arbitrary commutative bases, not a statement about individual jets or only field-valued points. The source forces an exact polynomial factor and its retained dual data. Put chi(z)=det(zI-Y)=(z-1)chi_red(z), h(z)=z^N chi(1/z)=(1-z)h_red(z), G=h(L), L^N=0 the actual lowering shift. Then, without any quantum-gap division, X=G B G inverse, G inverse v=v, ell G=e_0^t h_red(L). Thus clock trivialization carries the residual spectral polynomial into the co-source instead of deleting it. The actual fixed head is the regular section chi=z^N-1 and G=I, with its original orbit row and all peripheral factors retained. There is also a finite source-moment rigidity test. The mixed moments m_j=ell X Y^jv, 1<=j<N, recover all t_i by explicit triangular equations over the ordinary finite-head localization. Their Jacobian is product_(m=1)^(N-1)(1-Q^m), exactly N at a primitive N-th root. The pure moments ell Y^jv=1 cannot recover this polynomial. The theorem therefore supplies an actual finite algebraic test for a proposed transport/source comparison. For the original finite repair P the test recovers ONLY z^N-1. A geometric A-factor cannot be assigned to that same operator by changing its name. The actual quantum meridian transport must first be constructed with its full word/source and then tested by its own mixed moments. Neither the polynomial gauge nor its determinant one supplies a growing-level norm bound. The regulator comparison and the selected volume norm remain unproved. The explicit chart, gauge, retained co-source and moment reconstruction are the general algebraic progress here. ## 40. Actual horizontal transport and a universal complete cut The [actual open meridian theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_open_meridian_horizontal_source_transport.md) now derives the port character q^(-ell nu) from the unwrapped crossing potential. An actual SECOND-wire scaled Vandermonde W_(j,b)=(M^ell Q^j)^b removes it. Its whole inverse, both normal connections, full peripheral ratio and every alias power are retained. Partial trace is invariant on ALL tensors, so this is an exact source/current map. On the unit meridian arc it is an isometry of the root cyclic source complex. Its remaining meridian operator is the literal longitude insertion, including its Green/current terms. An [actual inverse-pair cut normalization](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/universal_resonant_cut_and_actual_source.md) now gives a general geometric simplification. Choose the first initial meridian U with nonzero lower-left entry relative to J. The preceding upper meridians are J by discreteness. Inverse Hurwitz moves carry U to the first slot; inserting those moves followed by their inverses preserves the original braid period. Cutting between them gives the actual prefix V=I and ell=0. All added coefficient atoms have a proved common regular open; the inverse graph is a nondegenerate normal stabilization. Writing U=I+c[-beta;1] * (1,beta), t=r+beta s, the actual complete momentum and density are p=1-1/t, r=1/(1-p)-beta s, Omega_cut=-p/[s(1-p)^2] dlog A_cut wedge dlog p. Thus the principal framing pole is the single fixed resonance p=1 for every complete discrete-faithful knot representation in the stated regular geometric model. It is not a finite quantum pole: the actual array is regular. Near p=1-zeta/N the framing escapes as r=N/zeta-beta s. The full source/current completion in this escaping region, and the global selected geometric coefficient, remain unproved. No replacement of that completion by the sampled principal density is made. The [actual meridian/shell audit](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_meridian_companion_source_compatibility.md) and [Borel divided-cap period](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_borel_regular_fusion_and_divided_cap_period.md) also distinguish genuine source transport from the auxiliary companion chart. The latter's root-center normal is abelian-local; it is not the hyperbolic critical branch. The next comparison must retain the actual word while crossing to that branch and controlling the marked escaping source. The three central gates in [the critical-path audit](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/critical_path_to_original_volume_conjecture.md) are still open.

title: The whole meridian profile and its regular period are equivalent
text: # The whole meridian profile and its regular period are equivalent Research proof, 27 October 2026. The canonical actual polar subtraction gives a uniform comparison of the whole scaled meridian function and its regular period, including every fixed resonance center. The original full-state monomial supplies an even resonance factor exactly. Uniform division across its zeros is justified by a fixed boundary norm, not by pointwise division or a jet argument. The result is conditional only on the explicitly stated domination of the polynomial-size ordinary-color tail when normalized by the Kashaev value. It does not assert that this growth or a whole profile limit exists for a general hyperbolic knot. It also keeps the fixed-root meridian normal distinct from the moving-q integral-color normal. For the figure-eight knot, the [paired-factor theorem](../papers/moving-meridian-sources/README.md) now proves these limits for the actual finite sum: $g_N\to2\sinh(z/2)/z$ and $\rho_N\to1$, uniformly on complex compact sets with all fixed derivatives. It also computes the first correction from the preferred cusp shape. The general comparison below remains useful without asserting these limits for other knots. ## 1. Exact actual functions and the tail assumption used here Use the actual functions of [the regularized Kashaev period](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/regularized_kashaev_period.md): q_N=exp(pi*i/N), Q_N=q_N^2, Y=M^2, K_N=F_N(1), S_N(Y)=1+Y+...+Y^(N-1), F_N(Y)=S_N(Y)R_N(Y)+P_N(Y). (1) Here P_N is the unique polynomial of degree at most N-2 with `P_N(Q_N^j)=C_j(q_N)`, 1<=j<N, and R_N is Laurent polynomial. The ordinary-color theorem gives |C_j(q_N)|<=D_N, D_N<= (N/2)^(b-1), |[Y^r]P_N|<=2D_N, 0<=r<=N-2. (2) Work along any sequence with K_N nonzero and epsilon_N=N D_N/|K_N| ->0. (3) A positive exponential lower bound for |K_N| implies (3), but is stronger than needed here. Put c=2pi*i and use the entire scaled meridian coordinate M_N(z)=exp(z/(2N)), Y_N(z)=exp(z/N), U=Y_N(z)^N=exp(z). Define g_N(z)=F_N(Y_N(z))/K_N, pi_N(z)=P_N(Y_N(z))/K_N, r_N(z)=N R_N(Y_N(z))/K_N, rho_N(z)=M_N(z)^(N-1) r_N(z). (4) All these functions are entire in z. The retained monomial in rho_N is the original full-state normalization, not a newly chosen gauge. For any compact K in the z-plane and every nonnegative integer l, the coefficient formula (2) gives the direct bound sup_K |partial_z^l pi_N| <=2(N-1)D_N exp(max(0,sup_K Re z))/|K_N|. (5) Indeed each differentiated exponential contributes `(r/N)^l`, of modulus at most one. Thus the complete interpolation tail and all its fixed jets vanish locally uniformly under (3). No growing Vandermonde inverse or unproved q-normal estimate is involved. ## 2. The original full-state factor gives an exact even resonance function The symmetric geometric sum gives exactly H_N(z)=S_N(Y_N(z))/[N M_N(z)^(N-1)] =sinh(z/2)/[N sinh(z/(2N))]. (6) At apparent common zeros this is its entire continuation. It is even and H_N(0)=1. Hence (1) becomes the exact whole identity g_N=H_N rho_N+pi_N. (7) The uncentered geometric sum would instead tend to `(exp(z)-1)/z`. Its additional factor `exp(z/2)` is accounted for by the exact monomial in (4). Removing or ignoring that factor would give the wrong Weyl transformation for the regular coefficient. Put H(z)=2sinh(z/2)/z, H(0)=1. On every fixed disk, for all sufficiently large N, H_N(z)=H(z)B_N(z), B_N(z)=[z/(2N)]/sinh(z/(2N)), B_N=1+O_K(N^(-2)). (8) B_N is a holomorphic nonvanishing unit on that disk. Its poles are at the distant points cN times nonzero integers. Thus (8) is locally uniform, including all fixed zeros of H. Those zeros are exactly `z_k=ck`, nonzero integers k; they are simple. For N>|k| they are exact zeros of H_N as well. The full modified dimension from the actual state is d_N(M)=eta_N (M-M^(-1))/(M^N-M^(-N)), eta_N=i^(N+3). Therefore its complete Weyl-even scaled cocycle is exactly N d_N(M_N(z))/eta_N=1/H_N(z). (9) This retains both the actual phase eta_N and every finite root divisor. It is a whole meromorphic identity, not just its value at z=0. In particular the full normalized ADO profile is N calN_N(M_N(z))/(eta_N K_N) =g_N/H_N=rho_N+pi_N/H_N. (10) The last summand must be subtracted before claiming holomorphic uniformity at a resonance. A small nonzero residue still gives a pole. For example C_1=1 forces a nonzero pole at z=c at every finite level, even if its normalized residue tends to zero. There is also an exact actual half-source interpretation. The marked rational Weyl splitting beta_N from [the source Weyl-gluing theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/twisted_cotangent_source_and_weyl_gluing.md) satisfies beta_N(M)beta_N(M^(-1))=c_N(M)^(-1), c_N(M)=N M^(N-1)/S_N(M^2). Thus, at this scaled meridian, without any limit or growth assumption, c_N(M_N(z))=H_N(z)^(-1), beta_N(M_N(z))beta_N(M_N(-z))=H_N(z). (10a) The odd/even-level phase and its unpaired even-level factor remain the original ones in beta_N. Hence the resonance factor is already the exact norm of the actual marked half-source, not an externally imposed entire function. ### 2.1 It is also the character of the original finite compact source On the actual N-dimensional source let J e_j=j e_j and n=N-1. Then exactly H_N(z)=(1/N)Tr exp[z(J-n/2)/N]. (10b) This is the finite sum (6), with its original 1/N. The compact coherent symbol is explicitly exp[-nz/(2N)] [1+(exp(z/N)-1)T]^n. Its original compact-source period is (10b), by the proved coherent trace formula. Uniformly for z in compact sets and 0<=T<=1 this symbol tends to `exp[z(T-1/2)]`. Consequently H(z)=integral_0^1 exp[z(T-1/2)]dT. (10c) Thus the resonance factor is at once an actual source character, the exact Weyl norm (10a), and the inverse full peripheral cocycle (9). No index theorem or identification of different quantum theories is needed for these equalities. ## 3. Uniform division is valid through every resonance center Choose radii 0<r<R with R not equal to 2pi times a positive integer. Let m_R=min_(|z|=R)|H(z)|>0. For all sufficiently large N, (8) gives `min_(|z|=R)|H_N(z)|>=m_R/2`. Whenever u_N/H_N has its holomorphic continuation to the disk of radius R, the maximum principle gives the fixed division bound ||u_N/H_N||_(|z|<=r) <=(2/m_R)||u_N||_(|z|=R). (11) There is no loss of control at an interior resonance. Its removable quotient is holomorphic before applying the maximum principle. For our exact numerator `u_N=g_N-pi_N`, this condition holds because (7) supplies the entire quotient rho_N. This proves the following equivalence under (3): * g_N converges locally uniformly on C to a holomorphic g; * rho_N converges locally uniformly on C to a holomorphic rho. The same proof is local on any open domain, using finitely many small boundaries avoiding its resonance zeros. The limits are necessarily related by g=H rho, g(0)=rho(0)=1. (12) For the nontrivial implication, at each fixed z_k the exact numerator vanishes for all large N. Equations (5) and local uniform convergence give g(z_k)=0, so g/H has a holomorphic removable continuation. Put rho=g/H. The numerator of rho_N-rho=(g_N-g-pi_N-(H_N-H)rho)/H_N is exactly divisible. Equations (5), (8), and (11) prove local uniform convergence, including all resonance centers. They also give the explicit estimate ||rho_N-rho||_(D_r) <=(2/m_R)[||g_N-g||_(boundary D_R) +||pi_N||_(boundary D_R) +||H_N-H||_(boundary D_R)||rho||_(boundary D_R)]. (13) The forward implication follows directly from (7). The same norms show that local boundedness of the two families is equivalent. In particular the regularization neither manufactures nor loses an unspecified normal-family assumption. At the centers the removable value can be recorded explicitly: rho_N(z_k)=[g_N'(z_k)-pi_N'(z_k)]/H_N'(z_k), H_N'(z_k)=(-1)^k/[2iN sin(pi k/N)], H'(z_k)=(-1)^k/(ck). (14) Thus fixed resonance derivatives and the regular quotient obey the same convergence. Higher derivatives follow either from Cauchy's formula after (13) or by repeated division. ## 4. Weyl symmetry and the regular coefficient The actual [Weyl theorem](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_weyl_descent.md) gives `F_N(Y^(-1))=F_N(Y)`, hence g_N is exactly even. H_N is even as well. Equation (7) implies H_N(z)[rho_N(z)-rho_N(-z)]=pi_N(-z)-pi_N(z). The numerator is exactly divisible. Applying (11) and (5) proves, even without convergence of rho_N, rho_N(z)-rho_N(-z) ->0 locally uniformly. (15) Every profile rho in (12) is therefore even. It may still be algebraic: the example `rho=1, g=H` satisfies all these resonance, Weyl and normalization constraints. If rho is entire and algebraic over C(z), it is an even polynomial; these identities do not exclude such a regular coefficient. The required whole period factor is already nonalgebraic and supplies all the resonance zeros. By contrast the uncentered limit r satisfies `r(-z)=exp(z)r(z)`. A nonzero global r with this property cannot itself be algebraic. This is a normalization issue resolved by the original full-state monomial, not an obstruction to an algebraic centered coefficient. Also `rho_N(0)=N R_N(1)/K_N=1-P_N(1)/K_N ->1`. Thus R_N(1) is nonzero for all large N on the sequence (3), and using the intrinsic normalization M_N(z)^(N-1)R_N(Y_N(z))/R_N(1) gives the same local-uniform limits and the same equivalence. No division by an unproved nonzero period is made before (3). ### 4.1 Unnormalized odd jets need no growth assumption There is an unconditional consequence of the same exact identity. It is useful when a lower bound for the complete value is the question, so division by \(K_N\) would be premature. Define \[ \widehat R_N(z)=e^{(N-1)z/(2N)}R_N(e^{z/N}),\qquad \mathscr D_N=N^{-1}Y\partial_Y,\qquad \lambda_N=\frac{N-1}{2N}. \] The balanced function \(\widehat R_N\) has no normalization by the unknown complete value. The evenness of \(F_N(e^{z/N})\) and \(H_N\) gives exactly \[ H_N(z)\{\widehat R_N(z)-\widehat R_N(-z)\} =\frac{P_N(e^{-z/N})-P_N(e^{z/N})}{N}. \] For any fixed disk, choose a larger circular boundary avoiding the zeros of \(H\). The coefficient estimate (2) bounds the right side by a constant times \(D_N\) there. The entire quotient on the left already exists, so the removable-division estimate (11) proves \[ \sup_{|z|\le r}|\widehat R_N(z)-\widehat R_N(-z)|\le C_rD_N \] for every fixed \(r\) and all sufficiently large levels. In particular, for every fixed odd integer \(m\), Cauchy's formula gives \[ \widehat R_N^{(m)}(0) =\left.(\mathscr D_N+\lambda_N)^m R_N\right|_{Y=1} =O_m(D_N). \] Thus the odd derivatives of the balanced regular function are polynomially bounded even if \(K_N=0\). No lower-growth or normal-family premise is used. At first order the exact relation is especially simple: \[ \mathscr D_NR_N(1) =-\frac{N-1}{2N}R_N(1)-\frac{P_N'(1)}{N^2}, \qquad \frac{|P_N'(1)|}{N^2}\le D_N. \] The inequality follows by summing \(r|[Y^r]P_N|\le2rD_N\) for \(0\le r\le N-2\). Since \(1/4\le\lambda_N<1/2\) for \(N\ge2\), this identity gives two-sided bounds between the complete value and this first derivative, with only polynomial additive errors. More precisely, the difference between any two of \[ \frac1N\log(1+|K_N|),\qquad \frac1N\log(1+|R_N(1)|),\qquad \frac1N\log(1+|\mathscr D_NR_N(1)|) \] tends to zero. For the first comparison use \(K_N=NR_N(1)+P_N(1)\) and the polynomial bound on \(P_N(1)\). Consequently their limsup and liminf rates agree, separately. This is a comparison of observations, not a positive lower bound for any of them. For a fixed higher jet order, the binomial change of basis between \(\mathscr D_N^rR_N(1)\) and \(\widehat R_N^{(r)}(0)\) and its inverse have uniformly bounded coefficients. The full finite jet norm at the complete point therefore has the same positive exponential rates as its even balanced derivatives. Symmetry controls the odd derivatives; it does not bound those higher even derivatives by \(\widehat R_N(0)\). Nor does it identify jets at other root-orbit points with the complete-point jet. Those are still missing observations in applying the orbit-jet growth theorem. ## 5. Fixed-root and integral-color normal maps have the same U but different sources Compare the preceding path with the actual integral-color one qfrak_N(z)=exp(c/(2N)+z/(2N^2)), M=-qfrak_N(z)^N=exp(z/(2N)), Qfrak_N(z)^N=exp(z/N)=Y_N(z). (16) Thus M, Y and U=exp(z) agree exactly. The quantum parameter does not: q is fixed at q_N in (1)--(15), while it varies in (16). On the actual common module put delta=1-Q^N, w=M Q^(-N)-M^(-1). The two source paths are exactly fixed root: delta=0, w=M-M^(-1), integral color: delta=1-Y_N(z), w=0. (17) They are different legs of the two-wall geometry. The head-word excursion factor delta*w vanishes on both legs, but that does not identify their derivatives, pivots or selected contractions. The actual ordinary integral pivot/twist differs from the frozen root auxiliary source by the already computed route factor qfrak_N(z)^(Nn kappa_D) (Qfrak_N(z)^N)^(sum_closed j_a), kappa_D=writhe-b+1, n=N-1. Knot parity removes only its root value. In this normal coordinate the remaining whole insertion is exp{z[n kappa_D/(2N)+(sum_closed j_a)/N]}. (18) Its modulus and every fixed z derivative are bounded on compact z sets uniformly in N, since `0<=sum_closed j_a<=(b-1)n`. It remains a nonconstant source insertion. A bound on its individual weights does not control cancellations in a selected sum, so it cannot be deleted when comparing normalized profiles. There is also a q-normal contribution. For a specified auxiliary finite-word lift, the path derivative in (16) contains `q partial_q/(2N^2)` in addition to the fixed-root contribution `M partial_M/(2N)`, together with the actual source derivatives from (18). Neither (2) nor the polar bound (5) bounds that q-normal derivative of the selected quantum word. The integral-color sampling centers are accordingly different: z_(N,k)=-ckN/(N+k) ->-ck, C_N(qfrak_N(z_(N,k)))=C_k(q_(N+k)). (19) These are moving q-color resonances, whereas the fixed-root zeros in (14) are exactly ck at every sufficiently large level. Equations (16)--(19) specify the coordinate and source adapter needed for a comparison; they do not assert equality of the two selected profile functions. ## 6. Exact scope The tail bound, full-state cocycle, quotient norm and equivalence of whole/regular profile convergence are exact consequences of the actual regularized state. They hold through the resonance centers, and retain the marked monomial and full modified dimension. The independent [whole Gamma source comparison](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/whole_gamma_frame_profile.md) proves an actual function-level refinement, with no K_N growth assumption. If z=ca and Phi_a(T)=G(T)^(-a)/Gamma(1-a), G(T)=(exp(cT)-1)/c, its actual middle-index q-normal residual V_(N,L)(a) and the marked meridian half-source obey N^(-a)beta_N(M_N(ca)) ->Phi_(-a)(1/2), V_(N,L)(a)=u_N(a) beta_N(M_N(-c b)), b=a/(1+a/N), u_N(0)=1, u_N=1+O_K(1/N). (21) The unit is specified by nonvanishing J-products there and remains valid through resonance zeros. The reparametrization b aligns their finite moving and fixed zeros; it cannot be omitted in a unit comparison. Consequently Phi_a(T)Phi_(-a)(T)=H(ca). Thus (10a), (10b) and (21) match actual source functions and their norm, not only a formally similar entire function. These are scalar source-line comparisons. They do not identify the full selected knot modules, their regular period coefficients or the state profiles in (16). In particular the opposite and slightly reparametrized half-source coordinate in (21) is not the identical-M normal path used in (16). No positive volume growth, whole normal-family convergence, algebraicity of the regular coefficient, or equality of q-normal and meridian-normal sourced periods has been proved here. ## 7. Audit [audit_scaled_meridian_regular_profile.py](../experiments/audit_scaled_meridian_regular_profile.py) and its [results](../experiments/scaled_meridian_regular_profile_results.json) check the finite centered character, both marked half-source norms and full cocycle at 85-digit precision, including odd and even N=2 through 18. They check the interpolation coefficient and derivative bound for bounded nodal data, and removable quotient values at the exact positive and negative resonances. The quotient stress family is an explicitly declared universal Laurent-polynomial family satisfying the same interpolation divisibility; it is not asserted to be a knot invariant. The general-knot analytic proof is (5)--(14). A separate compact grid through N=128 checks the improved centered factor rate O(N^(-2)); no general-knot growth assumption is inferred from these audits.

title: From the selected source volume to hyperbolic volume
text: # From the selected source volume to hyperbolic volume 29 October 2026. The task here starts AFTER an original-source theorem has proved lim_N (2pi/N) log|K_N| = V_src. It is to prove that this particular V_src is the hyperbolic volume of the actual complement. The argument below isolates a finite classical certificate for that equality. It does not assume that the displayed quantum limit has been proved for arbitrary knots. The existing [filled-source proof](actual_long_pretzel_casson_rivin_equality.md) already supplies this certificate for its selected long-filling branch. The [independent tangent-space audit](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/source_angle_stationarity_critical_audit.md) checks the distinction between a source saddle and a critical point on the FULL angle domain. Sections 2--3 below give an elementary proof of the complete-cusp Casson--Rivin implication, including completeness. ## 1. The exact certificate Let T be an actual oriented ideal triangulation of a manifold with torus ends. Write theta for its three opposite-edge-pair angles in each tetrahedron. Let A impose the tetrahedral sums and E count the local edge occurrences at each global edge, with multiplicities. The positive angle domain is P={theta>0: A theta=pi*1, E theta=2pi*1}. Put V_T(theta)=sum_i Lambda(theta_i), Lambda(theta)=-integral_0^theta log(2sin t)dt. For a complete cusped complement the certificate consists of: 1. A specified theta_src in P, on the actual triangulation and with every tetrahedron positive. 2. The absolutely normalized equality V_src=V_T(theta_src). 3. Full constrained stationarity: grad V_T(theta_src) in rowspace(A,E). (1) Equivalently, one exhibits real vectors mu,eta such that for each tetrahedral opposite edge pair i=(e,e'), -log(2sin theta_src,i)=mu_t+eta_e+eta_e'. (2) The conclusion is V_src=max_(closure P) V_T=Vol(M). (3) Row dependencies cause no problem: (1) is precisely annihilation of ker(A,E). A constrained source saddle proves (1) only if all omitted angle directions have also been accounted for. Section 4 explains two ways to do this without requiring the source variables themselves to parametrize every angle variation. For a filled manifold replace P by the actual filled-slope angle slice, and retain its primitive angular lifts and its end-completion certificate; see section 5. Imposing the unfilled boundary conditions would compute a different volume. ## 2. Strict concavity proves the maximum, including the boundary For one tetrahedron put beta=pi-alpha-gamma. Its negative volume Hessian, in independent coordinates alpha,gamma, is H=[[cot alpha+cot beta, cot beta], [cot beta, cot gamma+cot beta]]. (4) The first diagonal entry is sin gamma/(sin alpha sin beta)>0 and det H=1. Thus H is positive definite throughout the positive simplex. The sum over tetrahedra is strictly concave on every affine slice. If theta_src is an interior stationary point, follow the straight segment to any distinct point theta of the closure. This segment is positive except possibly at its final endpoint. Its volume derivative starts at zero and its second derivative is strictly negative. The continuous extension of Lambda to [0,pi] therefore gives V_T(theta)<V_T(theta_src) for theta!=theta_src. (5) The feasible domain is convex; V_T is concave. The convex function is -V_T. Neither nonemptiness of P nor strict concavity alone guarantees that its maximum lies in its interior. Positivity of theta_src in the certificate supplies the needed interior point directly. ## 3. Why the complete-cusp critical point is a complete metric This proves the geometric implication rather than merely naming the maximum a volume. It uses (2), not a presumed complete representation. Assign one real number to each global edge: l_e=-2 eta_e. (6) An ideal tetrahedron admits horospherical decorations whose six signed truncated edge lengths are exactly these numbers. Here is the explicit compatibility check. For any decorated ideal tetrahedron, the three opposite-pair length sums have differences (l_e+l_e')-(l_f+l_f') =2log(sin theta_i/sin theta_j). (7) For example normalize its vertices to infinity,0,1,z. If the three finite horospheres have Euclidean diameters d_0,d_1,d_z and the horosphere at infinity has height H, the six lengths are l_(infinity,a)=log(H/d_a), l_(a,b)=log(|a-b|^2/(d_a d_b)). The opposite sums are a common constant plus respectively 2log|1-z|, 2log|z|, 0. The sine rule proves (7) in the corresponding angle order. Equation (2) shows that the target lengths (6) have exactly these differences. Conversely those two independent differences are the ONLY restrictions. Changing the four horospheres adds r_v+r_w to the length of edge vw. A six-vector delta is of this form precisely when delta_01+delta_23=delta_02+delta_13 =delta_03+delta_12. For instance r_0=(delta_01+delta_02-delta_12)/2 determines the other three, and the displayed conditions check the remaining edges. Thus each tetrahedron has the required decoration. Glue the ideal faces according to T. The unique face isometry with the prescribed vertex matching preserves its three horocycles: the signed lengths on the three sides agree. Indeed a change of the three horocycles preserving all three side lengths would have r_0+r_1=r_1+r_2=r_2+r_0=0, hence all r_i=0. These decorations therefore match across EVERY face. Around an edge there is no residual dilation, since the horospheres at its ends return to themselves. Its total positive dihedral angle is exactly 2pi by E theta=2pi. Thus the edge has an ordinary hyperbolic neighborhood, with neither a cone angle nor a translation defect. There are no finite vertices to check. First shrink the compatible horospheres, by one common factor for each cusp, until they cut actual triangular corners and the finitely many corner neighborhoods are disjoint. Their matched triangles then form a nonsingular Euclidean metric on each compact link torus. It is complete; its universal development is the whole Euclidean plane. These corner neighborhoods give full complete horoball ends. The remaining core is compact. Hence the glued metric is complete, of curvature -1 and finite volume, on the ACTUAL M. Its volume is the sum of its tetrahedral volumes, V_T(theta_src). This proves (3). To compare with a separately specified complete metric, one can also apply the two marked representation-volume inequalities in opposite directions, as in the existing [geometric equality proof](general_source_regulator_hyperbolic_equality.md). No universal existence theorem for positive ideal triangulations is used in this implication. An actual positive theta_src is an input. ## 4. Eliminating internal variables is legitimate when they are optimized There are two sufficient ways to verify the full stationarity in (1). **Reduced optimization.** Choose affine coordinates (y,x) on the allowed angle domain, with y internal and x the retained source variables. Suppose the internal solution y(x) is an interior critical point in EVERY y direction, and define W(x)=V_T(y(x),x). Strict concavity makes each such internal point the unique fiber maximum. Its internal Hessian is invertible, so the implicit function theorem gives a smooth local y(x). The chain rule gives dW=partial_x V_T, because partial_y V_T=0. A critical point of W is therefore a critical point of the full V_T. This justifies coherent elimination if the eliminated action has been proved to be THIS fiber maximum. Naming an arbitrary reduced source action W is insufficient. **Full gluing and the boundary pairing.** The route already used by the actual source is more intrinsic. With x_t=Log z_t, y_t=Log(1-z_t^(-1)), a direct sine-rule calculation gives dV_T(delta theta) =sum_t[Re x_t delta Im y_t-Re y_t delta Im x_t]. At a full complex edge-gluing solution, the edge/peripheral symplectic reduction yields, for EVERY edge-angle tangent, dV_T=(1/2)sum_i[Re V_i dIm U_i-Re U_i dIm V_i]. (8) Here U_i,V_i are the actual small logarithms of the squared peripheral eigenvalues, in the fixed oriented marking of our notes. Full edge gluing kills the internal directions; the remaining quotient consists of these boundary directions. At a complete point U_i=V_i=0, (8) proves stationarity on all of P. The [tangent-space audit](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/source_angle_stationarity_critical_audit.md) states the necessary full-rank edge/peripheral hypotheses and proves the analogous equivalence for arbitrary Lagrangian boundary slices. In particular this is stronger than differentiating volume merely along a family of already-glued representations. ## 5. The actual long-filling source passes the filled certificate For a filled cusp, take a primitive slope a_i mu_i+b_i lambda_i and its actual log equation a_i U_i+b_i V_i=2pi i epsilon_i, epsilon_i=+/-1. (9) The affine angle constraints fix a_i Im U_i+b_i Im V_i=2pi epsilon_i. The real part of (9) annihilates (8) on every tangent to that constraint. Retained cusps are complete. Thus a positive source point satisfying full complex edge gluing and (9) is stationary on the ENTIRE filled angle slice. Strict concavity again makes it the unique global maximum. For our selected source these inputs are established as follows: * The [literal port lift](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_pretzel_port_lift_and_geometric_anchor.md) is a representation of the actual augmented-link group, based at its explicitly constructed complete oriented geometry. The [direct positive ideal subdivision](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_pretzel_positive_ideal_angle_certificate.md) supplies a compatible ideal chart for these actual cells, with no general triangulation existence assumption. Transporting this fixed positive triangulation by its marked flags gives the positive source point for sufficiently long fixed fillings. * Its source equation is U_i+p_i V_i=-2pi i on the selected unit-charge branch. The [primitive-period proof](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_long_pretzel_primitive_filling_angle.md) fixes this as an actual period, not a congruence modulo 2pi i. * The [marked action calculation](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_pretzel_marked_regulator_and_filling_action.md) proves V_src,s(p)=V_T(theta_p), including the actual filling quadratic and the absolute complete-volume anchor. There is no unidentified boundary constant left in this equality. * The [geometric completion](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/actual_long_pretzel_geometric_filling_completion.md) proves that these primitive periods close to smooth solid tori, with complete retained ends. This rules out a cone metric or a multiple covering at the core. Consequently V_src,s(p)=max_(closure P_p) V_T =Vol(S^3 minus K_p). (10) The complete augmented value V_s instead belongs to the unfilled boundary problem. It cannot simply be substituted for V_src,s(p). The [improved whole-source bound](actual_pretzel_all_width_extension.md) gives the original quantum limit needed above for every fixed odd width s>=9 and independently sufficiently long fixed signed p_i. The same note records even widths s>=10 for the specified single-cut two-component link invariant. These are the current quantum scopes; the classical certificate itself has no pretzel-width restriction. For a new source, once its limit is proved, the next work is precisely to supply its positive angle point, full stationarity and absolutely normalized volume equality on the actual topology. No further asymptotic theorem is needed AFTER those certificates hold. The existence of an abstract source rate alone supplies none of them.

title: Whole algebraic comparisons and their cyclotomic jets
text: # Whole algebraic comparisons and their cyclotomic jets Research note, 27 October 2026. This follows the user's proposal that Rivin's optimizer and quantum restrictions should be treated as parts of a whole period object. It proves a finite reconstruction theorem for algebraic comparison maps, including a quantum-normal direction which the earlier root-only source base does not record. The argument is exponent separation, Vandermonde inversion and a finite-algebra norm. No published rigidity or arithmetic module theorem is assumed. This does not construct the missing comparison of the actual selected Kashaev period with the geometric regulator period. The volume conjecture remains unproved. In particular, the theorem below requires a fixed algebraic presentation or a bounded space of possible maps; it does not assert algebraicity of a quantum period from its classical saddle. ## 1. What is algebraic about the Rivin optimum Let X be the nondegenerate gluing variety of a positive complete ideal triangulation, with shapes z_j, marked meridian M and longitude L. Its equations are monomial equations in z_j and 1-z_j, with integer exponents and the recorded peripheral signs. They define an algebraic variety over Q after inverting the shape denominators. Use the normalized geometric component, with its selected complete lift. The [positive rigidity proof](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/geometric_rigidity_and_cyclic_source.md) shows that its marked-meridian Jacobian is invertible at the complete geometric point. Consequently: * the complete shapes are algebraic numbers; * the local shape branch is algebraic over Q(M), and hence over the function field of its marked A-curve; * after shrinking a suitable algebraic neighborhood and retaining the chosen place, the branch is an etale algebraic germ over M; * every nilpotent thickening of that chosen place has a unique shape lift once its meridian lift is specified. The last assertion follows directly by Newton lifting. At each square- zero extension the correction is the unique solution of J delta z=-r, where J is the invertible gluing Jacobian and r is the residual. Repeating this through powers of the nilpotent ideal proves existence and uniqueness, with no convergence assertion needed. The [Rivin calculation](rivin_flow_and_quantum_source.md) independently proves strict concavity and stationarity at this geometric point. Thus positivity selects the same branch among the algebraic solutions. At the complete lift M=+1 or -1; the specified longitude sign and fundamental-class mark are still retained. M and L are not independent parameters on this curve. These statements concern shapes. Their arguments, logarithms and dilogarithm periods are not thereby algebraic functions. For example, the algebraic Gaussian coefficient and the action exp(S/h) are distinct parts of the period. The already marked action has Im S_complete=Vol(X)/2, h_N=pi*i/N. This gives log|exp(S_complete/h_N)|=N Vol(X)/(2pi). Establishing its contribution to the actual selected finite period is the remaining quantum assertion. For coverage, [Futer--Gueritaud, 1004.0440](https://arxiv.org/abs/1004.0440) describes the Casson--Rivin angle polytope and its critical-point criterion. Our rigidity and concavity proofs are in the linked notes. ## 2. Retain both power coordinates before taking quantum jets Work over any characteristic-zero coefficient field k. Put B=Spec k[t,t^(-1),q^(+/-1),M^(+/-1),v^(+/-1),w^(+/-1)]. Here t=1/N on the N-th restriction, and the power graphs are Gamma_N: t=1/N, v=q^N, w=M^N. (2.1) The actual cyclotomic point on this graph is q=q_N=exp(pi*i/N), M=1, v=-1, w=1. (2.2) The other meridian lift is handled in the same way. The finite phase cover of [the source base](https://github.com/sashakolpakov/murakamis_dream/blob/19d5b911bc409486f0e72b51a876a6a2bc70ee02/notes/uniform_frobenius_source_base.md) can be retained component by component, using levels in its specified residue class modulo four. None of its phases is reset here. The exact meridian shift on B is sigma(q)=q, sigma(M)=qM, sigma(v)=v, sigma(w)=vw, sigma(t)=t. (2.3) It preserves every Gamma_N. The two relative logarithmic derivatives which preserve these graphs are D_q=q partial_q+t^(-1)v partial_v, D_M=M partial_M+t^(-1)w partial_w. (2.4) They commute and satisfy the exact identities D_M sigma=sigma D_M, D_q sigma=sigma(D_q+D_M). (2.5) These follow by checking the five coordinate generators and extending by the product rule. Their pullbacks to Gamma_N are exactly q d/dq and M d/dM. Equivalently, the power coordinates are marked horizontal sections of the algebraic relative equations t dlog v=dlog q, t dlog w=dlog M, (2.6) with t fixed. Equations (2.6) specify a connection; their horizontal sections need not be rational functions for nonintegral 1/t. Setting v=-1 recovers the earlier root-only action w->-w. That closed slice is not preserved by D_q: D_q(v+1)=-1/t on it. In particular, replacing q^N by -1 before differentiating destroys quantum-normal information. The root values of v+1 are zero at every level, while their first quantum derivatives are -N. This is a refinement of the old source base, not an assertion that an N-dimensional cyclic Weyl representation extends off its root. The actual whole q-germs must still be supplied by the specified color/quantum-period construction. ## 3. Finite cyclotomic jets detect a whole bounded presentation Write a Laurent polynomial on B in the form P=sum_(a,b,c,d) p_(a,b,c,d)(t) q^a v^b M^c w^d, deg_t p_(a,b,c,d)<=D. (3.1) A Laurent power of t can be cleared first. Let S be the number of distinct pairs (a,b), R the number of distinct pairs (c,d), A the span of the a exponents, and C the span of the c exponents. These are bounds of the fixed presentation, independent of N. **Finite reconstruction theorem.** Choose D+1 distinct positive integers N>max(A,C). At each chosen N, suppose (D_q^i D_M^j P)(1/N,q_N,1,-1,1)=0 for 0<=i<S, 0<=j<R. (3.2) Then P=0 on B. The same conclusion holds if these jets vanish for infinitely many sufficiently large N. The number of derivatives is independent of N. No lower bound on the algebraic degree of q_N is needed, and k need not be a number field. **Proof.** On Gamma_N the exponents are lambda_(a,b)=a+Nb, mu_(c,d)=c+Nd. The lambda values are pairwise distinct when N>A: equality with b!=b' would give N<=|a-a'|. The same argument separates the mu values when N>C. Fill missing pairs with zero coefficients and form the S by R matrix A_N of coefficients p_(a,b,c,d)(1/N). Let V_lambda and V_mu be the Vandermonde matrices with rows indexed by derivative order, and put W=diag(q_N^lambda). The rectangular jet matrix in (3.2) is exactly J_N=V_lambda W A_N V_mu^t. (3.3) All three outer factors are invertible: characteristic is zero, the exponent lists are distinct, and q_N!=0. Hence J_N=0 implies A_N=0. Every p coefficient vanishes at D+1 distinct values 1/N; its degree bound makes it identically zero. This proves the theorem. If the full meridian family rather than its M=1 jets is known, its distinct M exponents can be compared directly; the R meridian jets are then unnecessary. Sparse supports can also reduce the rectangular test, but (3.2) gives a simple uniform sufficient bound. The theorem applies to rational residuals by clearing their fixed denominators. At a pole one must specify the regularized whole map and lattice before testing, rather than separately evaluating a vanishing numerator and denominator. Increasing the allowable support increases the required jet bound. For example (v+1)^s defeats all quantum jets of order less than s, and a polynomial in t vanishing at the tested levels defeats an insufficient number of level tests. The same proof handles any fixed number of power coordinates, including q^(N^2) from Gaussian phases. Write v_j=q^(N^j), w_j=M^(N^j), and use D_q(v_j)=t^(-j)v_j, D_M(w_j)=t^(-j)w_j. Exponents are now fixed-degree integer polynomials in N. Distinct such polynomials have distinct values for all sufficiently large N. The same two Vandermonde matrices and interpolation in t apply, with a fixed bound on the excluded levels. This retains a whole chosen phase lift; a phase's values at the roots alone do not determine its quantum-normal derivatives. ## 4. The same detection works on a fixed algebraic shape cover Let A be a finite free integral algebra over a localization of the coordinate ring of B, with fraction field K. A fixed algebraic shape branch is of this form after suitable localization. Consider a regular element f of A. At each tested cyclotomic point, choose an etale place, so it lifts uniquely to its two-variable formal q,M neighborhood, as in Section 1. Take the norm n(f), the determinant of multiplication by f on A. It has a fixed rational presentation on B. If the chosen lift of f vanishes in the rectangular jet ring, then the same is true of n(f). Indeed that etale place splits off a rank-one factor after formal base change, and multiplication determinants factor as n(f)=f_selected * det(m_f on the complementary factor). The complementary determinant is regular. Apply Section 3 with support and degree bounds of the cleared norm. It follows that n(f)=0 identically. Since K is a field, the norm of a nonzero element cannot be zero, and hence f=0. For a finite algebra with several integral components, apply this argument on the marked component; one selected component does not test all the others. A rational f must first have its poles cleared in the prescribed lattice. A finite number of shifted algebraic expressions can be treated in their finite compositum. We do not assume that the classical shape cover itself admits a finite algebraic lift of every q-shift. Thus algebraic shape coefficients do not require an independent unbounded list of Taylor coefficients. Nilpotent restrictions are faithful tests of a fixed whole comparison once its presentation and chosen algebraic place have been supplied. ## 5. Consequence for a pointed quantum comparison Suppose two specified finite-rank quantum objects have algebraic coefficient matrices, with their actual sources, cuts and integral lattices. Suppose a proposed comparison C and proposed inverse E are given on a fixed algebraic presentation. The intertwining, inverse, source and cut identities have residuals such as C B_1-B_2 sigma(C), CE-I, EC-I, C s_1-s_2, ell_2 C-ell_1. (5.1) If differential period connections are part of the specified objects, their residuals must also be checked: D_i C+C Omega_(1,i)-Omega_(2,i) C, i=q,M. (5.2) The maps C and E must be regular as maps of the prescribed lattices on their marked charts. This condition retains the peripheral zero and pole factors; it is not inferred from nonzero fiber values. Each cleared residual in (5.1)--(5.2) has a fixed algebraic norm. The finite jet test with the resulting bounds therefore proves all these identities for the whole objects. This is a finite certificate criterion for an already constructed comparison, not an existence theorem for C or E. In particular, equality of all fixed-root connection restrictions would not test a term proportional to dq. The quantum-normal jets and D_q in (5.2) are what test that direction. A classical optimizer, or a levelwise Hilbert-90 trivialization without bounded presentation, does not supply (5.1)--(5.2). ### A bounded family of jet intertwiners also proves generic existence There is an existence consequence which does not require proposing C in advance. It has a substantial uniformity hypothesis, stated here. Let F=k(q,t,v), and fix a finite-dimensional F-space of matrix functions of M,w, with a fixed Laurent support and denominator. Use this as the space of possible comparisons. The matrix entries of the two objects, their sources and cuts have fixed algebraic presentations. Include the meridian differential equation if it is specified and its unknown coefficients are constant for D_M. For rational coefficient objects, expanding the difference, source, cut and meridian identities in this fixed space gives a finite affine linear system H(q,t,v) u=b(q,t,v). (5.3) All unknown coefficients u are in F; sigma fixes F. For algebraic coefficient objects, a system of the form (5.3) is an additional descent requirement: testing one algebraic place alone does not imply coefficientwise equality in a generic algebraic basis. The theorem here assumes the displayed finite system and jet solutions to it. Clear the fixed denominators of (5.3). The assertion concerns regular charts of the prescribed lattices, so the candidate map denominators are units on the test germs. Other boundary factors need their stated lattice charts first. Let r be the generic rank of H. Take bounds for the t degrees and q,v supports of every r-minor of H and every (r+1)-minor of [H|b]. Such bounds are finite and can be obtained before choosing a comparison. Use D+1 levels for their t-degree bound and B quantum jets for their support bound as in Section 3. Use enough meridian jets to recover the coefficients in (5.3). **Bounded-comparison existence theorem.** Suppose at all these levels there are solutions in the fixed comparison space to order B in the quantum parameter, satisfying the pointing identities to that order. Suppose their leading matrices are invertible as rational meridian matrices. Then there is a generically invertible comparison in that space over F satisfying all of (5.3) exactly. Here order B means equality modulo epsilon^B, where q=q_N(1+epsilon), v=-(1+epsilon)^N. B is the number of jets, so the orders tested are 0 through B-1. It is enough to take B at least the largest number of distinct q,v exponent pairs in the stated minors. The size of the bound depends on the fixed comparison space, not on N. Maps at different levels need not be interpolated or assumed coherent beforehand. **Proof.** A jet solution makes every (r+1)-minor of [H|b] vanish modulo epsilon^B. Indeed its last column is a linear combination of the H columns plus a remainder of order B, and every (r+1)-minor of H is identically zero. Section 3, now with no meridian variables, makes these augmented minors identically zero. Therefore (5.3) is generically consistent and has a rational affine family of solutions, computable by Gaussian elimination. Choose a nonzero r-minor Delta of H. At one of the tested levels its whole power-graph pullback is nonzero; otherwise reconstruction would give Delta=0. Its order k at q_N is at most S_Delta-1 by the same sparse Vandermonde argument. In particular k<B. At that level retain the free coordinates of a jet solution and solve the pivot equations exactly over the Laurent-series field in epsilon. The pivot inverse has pole order at most k, so the correction is O(epsilon^(B-k)). It preserves the leading matrix. The exact specialized affine solution family consequently contains an invertible matrix. Its determinant is thus not the zero polynomial in its free parameters. The generic rational affine family has the same property. Since F is infinite, free parameters can be chosen in F outside that determinant's proper zero locus. This gives the claimed invertible rational comparison. For r=0 the same argument first gives b=0; an invertible matrix in the proposed space can be chosen directly. The zero-size pivot has order zero. This is an existence theorem for the difference/meridian/pointing identities encoded in (5.3). A q-direction period-connection identity contains derivatives of the unknown coefficients and is not an affine algebraic system of this form. It must be established for the constructed comparison by (5.2), or by a separate flatness and uniqueness argument with its hypotheses proved. Nor does generic invertibility prove regularity of C and its inverse on every boundary chart. There is one useful sufficient condition for the q-connection check. Suppose the two supplied period connections and semilinear shifts obey nabla_M T=T nabla_M, nabla_q T=T(nabla_q+nabla_M), (5.4) and their marked sources satisfy nabla_q s_i=0. Suppose s_1 is cyclic for T_1. If C already intertwines T and nabla_M and sends s_1 to s_2, then it automatically intertwines nabla_q. Indeed E=nabla_(q,2) C-C nabla_(q,1) is linear over the coefficient field; (5.4) and the meridian identity give E T_1=T_2 E. Also E s_1=0. Hence E kills every T_1^j s_1, which span the module, and E=0. The same proof works if nabla_q s_i is a specified common expression in T_i,nabla_(M,i),s_i already respected by C. Existence of these connections, their compatibility and this source law are hypotheses; they are not inferred from an A-symbol. The unresolved knot-specific input is a bounded comparison space and its sufficiently deep source-preserving jet intertwiners. Classical etaleness alone does not provide them. If that input is proved, however, generic algebraic existence follows from the finite rank argument above; a comparison matrix need not be guessed from a list of knot examples. title: plot figure eight meridian profile
text:
Plot the exact finite figure-eight microscopic main-meridian profiles.

Run from any directory:
    python3 experiments/plot_figure_eight_meridian_profile.py

Dependencies: mpmath, numpy, matplotlib.

The data are computed at 80 decimal digits from the whole Laurent polynomial
    f_N(Y) = sum_{n=0}^{N-1} prod_{r=1}^n
             (Y + Y^{-1} - 2 cos(2*pi*r/N)).
No limiting profile is substituted for finite-level data.

The canonical interpolant has degree at most N-2 and takes the values
f_N(exp(2*pi*i*j/N)) for 1 <= j < N.  Its coefficients are recovered by
the finite Fourier formula with its last coefficient set to zero.
At nonzero resonances t=2*pi*k, rho_N(i*t) is evaluated by
    (g_N'(i*t) - pi_N'(i*t)) / H_N'(i*t).
At t=0 it is 1 - P_ord(1)/f_N(1).

The script writes only the four named outputs.  The JSON includes the finite
data, removable-value diagnostics, and a separate 120-digit recalculation at
selected points.  The figure illustrates convergence; it is not its proof.

title: Research library
text: Volume limits for knots built from tangles: Volume limits for ordered tangle trees, decorated planar diagrams, and unchanged matched spheres satisfying an explicit packing condition. Each construction keeps its own hypotheses. Varying the knot meridian: Finite tangle operations, source estimates and meridian profiles in their specified long-filling classes. Calculating the finite quantum evaluation: Exact finite crossing data, repeated-root derivatives and the original coherent contraction. Research notes on other source coordinates are distinguished from the proved filling estimates. Angle optimization and actual geometry: See how angle actions become cell volumes, how ordered gluing faces match, and how the original peripheral curves determine the filled knot complement. Peripheral data, quantum operators and torsors: The conditional classical-symbol theorem and the retained proposals for source, boundary and regulator coordinates. The sharp source and its stationary maxima: A global upper problem with original face targets, an explicit seam gap, and finite stationary classification. The whole seam period is negligible for long fillings; macroscopic noncentral cancellation remains open. Fourier, weighted Cauchy, and energy: Follow the whole original CROSS period, coefficient-energy criteria, and mixed supported-window phase bounds with weighted cycle losses. The remaining general volume comparison is kept separate. Cube experiments and general sewing: A test of correlated boundary labels and a shared geometric core. The retained positive cube sectors have narrower conclusions than a full knot-invariant theorem. Short fillings and the finite-exception problem: The proposed extension after fixing arbitrary short partial fillings, and the orthogonal variational formulation of the original source.
